sn: भिन्द्यात् सुदुर्भिदं व्यूहं यतमानोऽपि संयुगे। प्रतिज्ञाया गतः पारं हत्वा सैन्धवमर्जुनः॥
en: Arjuna fulfill his vow by killing the king of Sindhu? O hero, how could the son of Pandu, if Drona had not wished it.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: पश्य राधेय पृथ्वीशान् पृथिव्यां पातितान् बहून्। पार्थेन निहतान् संख्ये महेन्द्रोपमविक्रमान्॥
en: Penetrate through that impenetrable array in battle when the latter was trying (to resist him). Indeed Phalguna is exceedingly dear to the high-souled preceptor.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: अनिच्छतः कथं वीर द्रोणस्य युधि पाण्डवः। भिन्द्यात् सुदुर्भिदं व्यूह यतमानस्य शुष्मिणः॥
en: It is, on this account, that he allowed him to enter into the array) without offering any opposition to him. Behold my misery now; that tormentor of foes, Drona, first, promised protection to the king of Sindhu.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: दयित: फाल्गुनो नित्यमाचार्यस्य महात्मनः। ततोऽस्य दत्तवान् द्वारमयुद्धेनैव शत्रुहन्।॥ अभयं सिन्धुराजाय दत्त्वा द्रोणः परंतपः। प्रादात् किरीटिने द्वारं पश्य निर्गुणतां मयि॥
en: (But) The afterwards allowed Kiriti to enter into the array. If he had before given permission to the king of Sindhu to return home, this dreadful havoc would never have taken place in battle. Jayadratha was for returning home in order to save his life.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: यद्यदास्यदनुज्ञां वै पूर्वमेव गृहान् प्रति। प्रस्थातुं सिन्धुराजस्य नाभविष्यज्जनक्षयः॥ अद्य मे भ्रातरः क्षीणाश्चित्रसेनादयो रणे। भीमसेनं समासाद्य पश्यतां नो दुरात्मनाम्॥
en: But relaying upon the promise of protection made by Drona, insensate fool that I was, i stooped him. Today my brothers Chitrasena and others, have in the very sight of our wretched selves, been destroyed by Bhimasena.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: कर्ण उवाच आचार्य मा विगर्हस्व शक्तयासौ युध्यते द्विजः। यथाबलं यथोत्साहं त्यक्त्वा जीवितमात्मनः॥
en: Karna said Do not blame the preceptor. (For) the twiceborn one is fighting to the best of his prowess and energy and heedless of his life.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: यद्येनं समतिक्रम्य प्रविष्टः श्वेतवाहनः। नात्र सूक्ष्मोऽपि दोषः स्यादाचार्यस्य कथंचन॥
en: If Shetavahana entered (into the array) after having overcome him the preceptor cannot be found fault with in the least (for that).

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: कृती दक्षो युवा शूरः कृतास्रो लघुविक्रमः। दिव्यास्रयुक्तमास्थाय रथं वानरलक्षणम्॥
en: (Again, Arjuna) is accomplished, skillful, young, heroic, accomplished in arms and quick in movements. He was armed with celestial weapons and mounted on the ape-bannered car.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: कृष्णेन च गृहीताश्वमभेद्यकवचावृतः। गाण्डीवमजरं दिव्यं धनुरादाय वीर्यमान्॥
en: The steeds of which were guided by Krishna. And that puissant one was clad in impenetrable armour and wielding his celestial and undecaying bow Gandiva.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: प्रवर्षन् निशितान् बाणान् बाहुद्रविणदर्पितः। यदर्जुनोऽभ्ययाद् द्रोणमुपपन्नं हि तस्य तत्॥
en: As Arjuna, proud of the prowess of his arms, sent forth keen darts, it was no wonder that he over came Drona.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: आचार्यः स्थविरो राजशीघ्रयाने तथाक्षमः। बाहुव्यायामचेष्टायामशक्तस्तु नराधिप।॥
en: (On the other hand), Oking, the preceptor is old and incapable of quick movements and o lord of men, (he is) also unable to exercise his arms (for a long time).

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: तेनैवमभ्यतिक्रान्तः श्वेताश्वः कृष्णसारथिः। तस्य दोषं न पश्यामि द्रोणस्यानेन हेतुना॥
en: It was on this account, that Setasva with Krishna as his charioteer was able to overcome him. I cannot, therefore, find any fault in Drona. are

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: दैवमत्र परं स्मृतम्। अजय्यान् पाण्डवान् मन्ये द्रोणेनासविदा मृधे। तथा ह्येनमतिक्रम्य प्रविष्टः श्वेतवाहनः॥
en: In my opinion the Pandavas unconquerable in battle by Drona, (however) skilled in weapons (he may be) in as much as Shetavahena, surpassing him, entered (into our array).

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: दैवादिष्टेऽन्यथाभावो नमन्ये विद्यते क्वचित्। यतो नो युध्यमानानां परं शक्त्या सुयोधन॥
en: My belief is that what is ordained by fate undergoes no alteration, when, O Suyodhana, in spite of our fighting to the very best of our power.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: सैन्धवो निहतो युद्धे परं यत्नं कुर्वतां च त्वया सार्धं रणाजिरे॥
en: The king of Sindhu has been killed in battle. It seems that fate is supreme. Though we have been making vigorous exertions with you on the field of battle.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: हत्वास्माकं पौरुषं वै दैवं पश्चात् करोति नः। सततं चेष्टमानानां निकृत्या विक्रमेण च॥
en: (And though he have been) always trying (to achieve success) by means of prowess and deceit, fate makes all our efforts futile.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: दैवोपसृष्टः पुरुषो यत् कर्म कुरुते वचित्। कृतं कृतं हि तत्कर्म दैवेन विनिपात्यते॥
en: O king, whatever act, a person who is not favoured by fate, does, it is baffled by fate, in spite of all his exertions to accomplish it.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: यत् कर्तव्यं मनुष्येण व्यवसायवता सदा। तत् कार्यमविशङ्केन सिद्धिदैवे प्रतिष्ठिता॥
en: That, which a person having perseverance ought to do, should be performed by him in a fearless spirit, (though of course) success depends upon fate.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: निकृत्या वञ्चिताः पार्था विषयोगैश्च भारत। दग्धा जतुगृहे चापि द्यूतेन च पराजिताः॥
en: We beguiled the sons of Pritha by deceit as well as by administration of poison, O Bharata. They were (again) burnt in the lac house and defeated at dice.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: निरर्थकम्। राजनीतिं व्यपाश्रित्य प्रहिताश्चैव काननम्। यत्नेन च कृतं तत्तद् दैवेन विनिपातितम्॥
en: In pursuance of state policy they were exiled to the forest; though we did all these with the utmost care, they have been frustrated by fate.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: युध्यस्व यत्नमास्थाय दैवं कृत्वा यततस्तव तेषां च दैवं मार्गेण यास्यति॥
en: Hurling defiance at fate, fight with (utmost) care. Between yourself and themselves, fate will espouse the cause of the party that will make the best exertion.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: न तेषां मतिपूर्वं हि सुकृतं दृश्यते क्वचित्। दुष्कृतं तव वा वीर बुद्ध्या हीनं कुरूद्वह॥
en: (It does not seem) that they (i.e., the Pandavas) have done anything good by reason of superior intellect; nor (does it appear) O hero, O perpetuator of Kuru-race you have done anything wrong through want of understanding.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: दैवं प्रमाणं सर्वस्य सुकृतस्येतरस्य वा। अनन्यकर्म दैवं हि जागर्ति स्वपतामपि॥
en: It is fate that always bears testimony to our acts, whether good or evil. Fate which is (ever) bent on its purpose is wide awake even when everything else sleeps.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: बहूनि तव सैन्यानि योधाश्च बहवस्तव। न तथा पाण्डुपुत्राणामेवं युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: When the war began your soldiers and warriors were more numerous than those of the sons of Pandu.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: तैरल्पैर्बहवो यूयं क्षयं नीताः प्रहारिणः। शङ्के दैवस्य तत् कर्म पौरुषं येन नाशितम्॥
en: By their small force numerous warriors on your side have been destroyed. I fear it is the work of Destiny by which exertion has been baffled.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: संजय उवाच एवं सम्भाषमाणानां बहु तत् तज्जनाधिप। पाण्डवानामनीकानि समदृश्यन्त संयुगे॥
en: Sanjaya said When, (monarch, they were thus conversing about many other (subjects) the army of the Pandavas was seen on the field of battle.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: । ततः प्रववृते युद्धं व्यतिषक्तरथद्विपम्। तावकानां परैः सार्धं राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव॥
en: Then, O monarch there ensued a furious encounter, the result of our evil policy, in which the infantry, cars and elephants of your party encountered those of the other.

sn: संजय उवाच तदुदीर्णं गजानीकं बलं तव जनाधिप। पाण्डुसेनामतिक्रम्य योधयामास सर्वतः॥
en: Sanjaya said 0 monarch, that impetuous elephant squadron of yours fought everywhere getting the better of the Pandava army.

sn: पञ्चालाः कुरवश्चैव योधयन्तः परस्परम्। यमराष्ट्राय महते परलोकाय दीक्षिताः॥
en: The Panchalas and the Kauravas, determined to go to the next world, that is, the great region of Yama, fought with one another.

sn: शूराः शूरैः समागम्य शरतोमरशक्तिभिः। विव्यधुः समरेऽन्योन्यं निन्युश्चैव यमक्षयम्॥
en: Heroes encounter (rival) heroes smote one another with arrows, lances and darts and quickly sent one another of the region of Yama.

sn: रथिनां रथिभिः सार्धं रुधिरस्त्रावदारुणम्। प्रावर्तत महद् युद्धं निघ्नताभितरेतरम्॥
en: Car-warriors were engaged in terrible battle, cause a dreadful flow of blood against (rival) car-warriors and smote one another.

sn: वारणाश्च महाराज समासाद्य परस्परम्। विषाणैर्दारयामासुः सुसंक्रुद्धा मदोत्कटाः॥
en: Furious elephants mad with rage, O mighty monarch, advancing against one another, mangled one another with tusks.

sn: हयारोहान् हयारोहा: प्रासशक्तिपरश्वधैः। बिभिदुस्तुमुले युद्धे पार्थयन्तो महद् यशः॥
en: In that dreadful encounter horsemen solicitous of high renown, pierced (rival) horsemen with spears, darts and battle-axes.

sn: पत्तयश्च महाबाहो शतशः शस्त्रपाणयः। अन्योन्यमार्दयन् राजन् नित्यंयत्ताः पराक्रमे॥
en: O mighty-armed one, O tormentor of foes, hundreds of foot-soldiers armed with weapons rushed against one another with vigorous efforts.

sn: गोत्राणां नामधेयानां कुलानां चैव मारिष। श्रवणाद्धि विजानीमः पञ्चालान् कुरुभिः सह॥
en: And, O worshipful sire, (in that terrible encounter) we could only distinguish the Kurus from the Panchalas by the names of their (respective) clans and families which we heard them utter.

sn: तेऽन्योन्यं समरे योधाः शरशक्तिपरश्वधैः। प्रेषयन् परलोकाय विचरन्तो ह्यभीतवत्॥
en: The warrior moving about fearlessly on the field of battle sent one another to the next world by arrows, darts and battle-axes.

sn: शरा दश दिशो राजंस्तेषां मुक्ताः सहस्रशः। न भ्राजन्ते यथातत्त्वं भास्करेऽस्तंगतेऽपि च॥
en: The sun having gone down, the arrows, O king, shot by thousands by them, did no longer illuminate the ten points as before.

sn: तथा प्रयुध्यमानेषु पाण्डवेयेषु भारत। दुर्योधनो महाराज व्यवागाहत तद् बलम्॥
en: The Pandava army, 0 Bharata being thus engaged in battle Duryodhana penetrated into them, Oking.

sn: सैन्धवस्य वधेनैव भृशं दुःखसमन्वितः। मर्तव्यमिति संचिन्त्य प्राविशच द्विपद्वलम्॥
en: Afflicted with great sorrow at the destruction of the king of Sindhu and determined to sacrifice his life, he entered into the enemy's army.

sn: नादयन् रथघोषेण कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्। अभ्यवर्तत पुत्रस्ते पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्॥
en: Causing the earth to tremble and resound with the rattle of his car, your son rushed against the Pandava army.

sn: स संनिपातस्तुमुलस्तस्य तेषां च भारत। अभवत् सर्वसैन्यानामभावकरणो महान्॥
en: O Bharata, that dreadful clash between him and them caused a terrible slaughter of all the troops.

sn: यथा मध्यंदिने सूर्यं प्रतपन्तं गभस्तिभिः। तथा तव सुतं मध्ये प्रतपन्तं शराचिभिः॥
en: As the noon-day sun scorches (the world) with his rays, so, it seemed, that your son scorched (the Pandavas army) with flaming darts.

sn: न शेकुर्धातरं युद्धे पाण्डवाः समुदीक्षितुम्। पलायनकृतोत्साहा निरुत्साहा द्विषज्जये॥
en: In that battle the Pandavas could not even look at their brother (i.e., Duryodhana) and despairing of conquering their enemy, they tried to flee (from the field).

sn: पर्यधावन्त पञ्चाला वध्यमाना महात्मना। रुक्मपुखैः प्रसन्नाग्रैस्तव पुत्रेण धन्विना॥
en: The Panchalas, struck with gold-winged darts of blazing points, shot by your highsouled son armed with a bow, fled away.

sn: अर्घमानाः शरैस्तूर्णं न्यपतन् पाण्डुसैनिकाः। न तादृशं रणे कर्म कृतवन्तस्तु तावकाः॥
en: The Pandava soldiers smitten with sharpened darts fell (dead). Indeed the sons of Pandu could never perform such exploits in battle.

sn: यादृशं कृतवान् राजा पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते। पुत्रेण तव सा सेना पाण्डवी मथिता रणे॥
en: As were achieved by your royal son, O lord of earth. In that encountei the Pandava army was crushed by your son.

sn: नलिनी द्विरदेनेव समन्तात् फुल्लपङ्कजा। क्षीणतोयानिलार्काभ्यां हतत्विडिव पद्मिनी॥
en: As lotuses are torn and crushed by a tusker. As lotuses are shorn of their beauty in consequence of the water (over which they grow) being dried up by the sun and the wind.

sn: बभूव पाण्डवी सेना तव पुत्रस्य तेजसा। पाण्डुसेनां हतां दृष्ट्वा तव पुत्रेण भारत॥
en: The Pandava army became so by virtue of the prowess of your son. Seeing, O Bharata, that the Pandava army was being destroyed by your son.

sn: भीमसेनपुरोगास्तु पञ्चालाः समुपाद्रवन्। स भीमसेनं दशभिर्माद्रीपुत्रौ त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः॥
en: The Panchalas led by Bhimasena advanced (against him). He then (pierced) Bhimasena with ten, each of the two sons of Madri with three.

sn: विराटद्रुपदौ षड्भिः शतेन च शिखण्डिनम्। धृष्टद्युम्नं च सप्तत्या धर्मपुत्रं च सप्तभिः॥
en: Virata and Drupada each with six, Shikandi with hundred, Dhrishtadyumna with hundred, the son of Dharma with seven.

sn: केकयांश्चैव चेदींश्च बहुभिर्निशितैः शरैः। सात्वतं पञ्चभिर्विद्धवा द्रौपदेयांसिभिस्रिभिः॥
en: And the Kalkeyas and the Chedies with numerous keen darts. piercing Satvatta with five (arrows), each of the son of Draupadi with three.

sn: घटोत्कचं च समरे विद्ध्वा सिंह इवानदत्। शतशश्चापरान् योधान् सद्विपांश्च महारणे॥ शरैरवचकर्ताग्रैः क्रुद्धोऽन्तक इव प्रजाः। सा तेन पाण्डवी सेना वध्यमाना शिलीमुखैः॥
en: And piercing Ghatotkacha too in battle he roared like a lion. Like the wrathful destroyer slaying the created beings, he cut down hundreds of other warriors and the bodies of horses and elephants in that terrific encounter. When he was thus destroying his enemies, his great bow, plaited at the back with gold.

sn: तव पुत्रेण संग्रामे विदुद्राव नराधिप। तं तपन्तमिवादित्यं कुरुराज महाहवे॥ नाशकन् वीक्षितुं राजन् पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैनिकाः। ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा कुपितो राजसत्तम॥
en: o king! The soldiers in the army of Pandavas could not even put an eye on Duryodhana, the Kuru king who was glowing like a son in that great battle. O great king! King Yudhishthira then rushed fast with an intention to kill your son, the king of Kuru, Duryodhana in furious mood.

sn: अभ्यधावत् कुरुपति तव पुत्रं जिघांसया। तावुभौ युधि कौरव्यो समीयतुररिंदमौ॥ स्वार्थहेतोः पराक्रान्तौ दुर्योधनयुधिष्ठिरौ।
en: Duryodhana, the warrior of Kuru clan and Yudhishthira both suppressor to enemy attacked furiously on each other with fantastic exhibition of valour for their respective interests.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः क्रुद्धः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ विव्याध दशभिस्तूर्णं ध्वजं चिच्छेद चेषुणा।
en: Duryodhana furiated enough, put ten arrows having bent knot on bow and shot at Yudhishthira. He was badly injured. He then shot an arrow again and cut-off the flag fixed on Yudhishthira chariot.

sn: इन्द्रसेनं त्रिभिश्चैव ललाटे जनिवान् नृप॥ सारथिं दयितं राज्ञः पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः।
en: O king! He shot again three arrows at Indrasena, the loyal charioteer of Yudhishthira and injured his forehead.

sn: धनुश्च पुनरन्येन चकर्तास्य महारथः॥ चतुर्भिश्चतुरश्चैव बाणैर्विव्याध वाजिनः।
en: Duryodhana again shot an arrow which had cut-off the bow with Yudhishthira and penetrated his four horses by another four arrows he shot at them.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरः क्रुद्धो निमेषादिव कार्मुकम्॥ अन्यदादाय वेगेन कौरवं प्रत्यवारयत्।
en: King Yudhishthira furiated enormous, picked up immediately at an wink, another bow and prevented Duryodhana with a sharp blow.

sn: तस्य तान् निघ्नतः शत्रून् रुक्मपृष्ठं महद् धनुः॥ भल्लाभ्यां पाण्डवो ज्येष्ठसिधा चिच्छेद मारिष।
en: Revered king! Yudhishthira, the eldest Pandava splitted the huge bow, gold studded with Duryodhana up into three pieces by giving acute blows twice with Bhalla.

sn: विव्याध चैनं दशभिः सम्यगस्तैः शितैः शरैः॥ मर्म भित्त्वा तु ते सर्वे संलग्नाः क्षितिमाविशन्।
en: He concomitantly injured Duryodhana too with a shot of ten sharp arrows. These arrows penetrated the sensitive parts in Duryodhana's body, made their way from them and sank deep in the earth.

sn: ततः परिवृता योधाः परिवQर्युधिष्ठिरम्॥ वृत्रहत्यै यथा देवाः परिव्रवुः पुरंदरम्। ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा तव पुत्रस्य मारिष।
en: The warriors in Pandavas' army then returned again to battle as they once were fled away. They all took their position around Yudhishthira as all gods had gathered around Indra when the monster Vritra was killed.

sn: शरं च सूर्यरश्म्याभमत्युग्रमनिवारणम्॥ हा हतोऽसीति राजानमुक्त्वामुञ्चद् युधिष्ठिरः।
en: Omajesty! Yudhishthira, then shot a dreadful and target hitting arrow glowing like sun beams at your son, king Duryodhana with a declaration-"Oh! You are killed."

sn: स तेनाकर्णमुक्तेन विद्धो बाणेन कौरवः॥ निषसाद रथोपस्थे भृशं सम्मूढचेतनः।
en: Duryodhana, the king of Kuru clan immediately lost conscious and seated with a thud at the rear part of his chariot when that arrow injured him.

sn: ततः पाञ्चाल्यसेनानां भृशमासीद् रवो महान्॥ हतो राजेति राजेन्द्र मुदितानां समन्ततः।
en: Then a great and tumultuous uproar arose from among the Panchala soldiers. O king of kings, that great noise was this “the king is slain.”

sn: बाणशब्दरवश्चोग्रः शुश्रुवे तत्र मारिष॥ अथ द्रोणो द्रुतं तत्र प्रत्यदृश्यत संयुगे।
en: And, O Bharata, sharp whiz's of arrows were also heard there. Then Drona speedily appeared there in that battle.

sn: हृष्टो दुर्योधनश्चापि दृढमादाय कार्मुकम्॥ तिष्ठा तिष्ठेति राजानं ब्रुवन् पाण्डवमभ्ययात्।
en: Duryodhana too with (great) joy grasping his bow firmly and shouting to the king (Yudhishthira) 'wait', 'wait' rushed against the Pandavas.

sn: प्रत्युद्ययुस्तं त्वरिताः पञ्चाला जयगृद्धिनः॥ तान् द्रोणः प्रतिजग्राह परीप्सन् कुरुसत्तमम्।
en: The Panchalas too desirous of victory speedily followed the king. In order to save the foremost of the Kurus, Drona received them (i.e., their charge).

sn: चण्डवातोद्भुतान् मेघान् निघ्नन् रश्मिमुचो यथा॥ ततो राजन् महानासीत् संग्रामो भूरिवर्धनः। तावकानां परेषां च समेतानां युयुत्सया॥
en: And then destroyed them all like the possessor of rays destroying the clouds driven to and fro by a terrific hurricane. Then there took place, O king, a terrific battle causing great havoc between you and your enemy's assembled troops eager for fight.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यत् तदा प्राविशत् पाण्डूनाचार्यः कुपितो बली। उक्त्वा दुर्योधनं मन्दं मम शास्त्रातिगं सुतम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When the wrathful preceptor endued with prowess, having addressed my Duryodhana, who (even) acts in opposition to my commands, thus entered into the Pandava army.

sn: प्रविश्य विचरन्तं च रथे शूरमवस्थितम्। कथं द्रोणं महेष्वासं पाण्डवाः पर्यवारयन्।॥
en: How did the Pandavas oppose that mighty bowman, the heroic Drona, who having entered it (i.e., the hostile army) was moving about (the field of battle) stationed on his car.

sn: केऽरक्षन् दक्षिणं चक्रमाचार्यस्य महाहवे। के चोत्तरमरक्षन्त निघ्नत: शात्रवान् बहून्॥
en: (And) when the preceptor was engaged in the terrible slaughter of the enemy in that great battle, who did protect the right wheel (of his car) and who the left?

sn: के चास्य पृष्ठतोऽन्वासन् वीरा वीरस्य योधिनः। के पुरस्तादवर्तन्त रथिनस्तस्य शत्रवः॥
en: Who were the heroes that guarded the rear of that warrior engaged in fight? Who were the enemies that were stationed in front of that carwarrior?

sn: मन्ये तानस्पृशच्छीतमतिवेलमनार्तवम्। मन्ये ते समवेपन्त गावो वै शिशिरे यथा॥
en: It seems to me that the experienced an excessive cold chill ill-suited to the proper season or I think they shivered like cows exposed to frosts.

sn: यत्प्राविशन्महेष्वासः पञ्चालानपराजितः। नृत्यन् स रथमार्गेषु सर्वशस्रभृतां वरः॥
en: When that unvanquished and mighty wielder of bow and that foremost of the wielders of weapons, dancing on the track of his car, entered among the Panchalas.

sn: निर्दहन् सर्वसैन्यानि पञ्चालानां रथर्षभः। धूमकेतुरिव क्रुद्धः कथं मृत्युमुपेयिवान्॥
en: Consuming all the forces of the Panchalas like an angry comet, how did that foremost of the car-warriors, meet with death?

sn: संजय उवाच सायाह्ने सैन्धवं हत्वा राज्ञा पार्थः समेत्य च। सात्यक्श्चि महेष्वासो द्रोणमेवाभ्यधावताम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Having killed the king of Sindhu in the evening Partha saw the king (i.e. Yudhishthira) and then united with the great bowman Satyaki he advanced against Drona himself.

sn: तथा युधिष्ठिरस्तूर्णं भीमसेनश्च पाण्डवः। पृथक्कमूभ्यां संयत्तौ द्रोणमेवाभ्यधावताम्॥
en: Then Yudhishthira together with the Pandava Bhimasena joined by their separate squadrons soon rushed against Drona himself.

sn: तथैव नकुलो धीमान् सहदेवश्च दुर्जयः। धृष्टद्युम्नः सहानीको विराटश्च सकेकयः॥
en: Similarly, Nakula endued with intelligence and Sahadeva difficult of being conquered and Dhrishtadyumna with his army and Virata together with the Kekayas.

sn: मत्स्याः शाल्वाः ससेनाश्च द्रोणमेव ययुयुधि। दुपदश्च तथा राजा पञ्चालैरभिरक्षितः॥
en: And the Matsyas and the Shalvas with their own divisions advanced against Drona for battle. protected by the Panchalas, Drupada.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नपिता राजन् द्रोणमेवाभ्यवर्तत। द्रौपदेया महेष्वासा राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः॥
en: The father of Dhrishtadyumna, O king, marched against Drona. Those mighty wielders of bow viz., the (five) sons of Draupadi and the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha.

sn: ससैन्यास्ते न्यवर्तन्त द्रोणमेव महाद्युतिम्। प्रभद्रकाश्च पञ्चालाः षट्रसहस्राः प्रहारिणः॥
en: Followed by their own troops proceeded against the highly resplendent Drona. The Prabhadrakas and the Panchałas, numbering sixty thousand (efficient) smiters.

sn: द्रोणमेवाभ्यवर्तन्त पुरस्कृत्य शिखण्डिनम्। तथेतरे नरव्याघ्राः पाण्डवानां महारथाः॥
en: With Shikhandi at their head, marched against Drona. Similarly (numerous) other foremost of men and mighty car-warriors on the side of the Pandavas.

sn: सहिताः सन्यवर्तन्त द्रोणमेव द्विजर्षभम्। तेषु शुरेषु युद्धाय गतेषु भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of men, jointly proceeded against Drona. O best of the Bharatas, those warriors having proceeded for the fight.

sn: बभूव रजनी घोरा भीरूणां भयवर्धिनी। योधानामशिवा रौद्रा राजन्नन्तकगामिनी॥
en: The night became dark increasing the terror of the cowards. (And) that dismal (night) O king, proved destructive of (numerous) warriors.

sn: कुञ्जराश्वमनुष्याणां प्राणान्तकरणी तदा। तस्यां रजन्यां घोरायां नदन्त्यः सर्वतः शिवाः॥
en: And it then prove fatal to elephants horses and men. On that bitchy dark night jackals setting up (terrible) yells everywhere.

sn: न्यवेदयन् भयं घोरं सज्वालकवलैर्मुखैः। उलूकाश्चाप्यदृश्यन्त शंसन्तो विपुलं भयम्॥ विशेषतः कौरवाणां ध्वजिन्यामतिदारुणाः। ततः सैन्येषु राजेन्द्र शब्दः समभवन्महान्॥
en: And with their gaping mouths all ablaze indicated dreadful terror. Specially greatly terrible owls, screaming from the standards of the Kauravas, foreboded dreadful terror. Then, O king of kings, there arose a tumultuous uproar from among the troops.

sn: भेरीशब्देन महता मृदङ्गानां स्वनेन च। गजानां हितैश्चापि तुरङ्गाणां च हृषितैः॥
en: (Mingling) with the loud beat of drums and sound of cymbals, the grunt of elephants and the neigh of horses.

sn: खुरशब्दनिपातैश्च तुमुल: सर्वतोऽभवत्। ततः समभवद् युद्धं संध्यायामतिदारुणम्॥
en: And the noise of hoofs (that uproar) spread everywhere. Then there took place an awfully dreadful nocturnal battle.

sn: द्रोणस्य च महाराज संजयानां च सर्वशः। तमसा चावृते लोके न प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥ सैन्येन रजसा चैव समन्तादुत्थितेन ह। नरस्याश्वस्य नागस्य समसजत शोणितम्॥
en: Of great king, between Drona (on one hand) and all the Srinjayas (on the other). In consequence of the night being enveloped in darkness and of the dust raised by the soldiers nothing could be discerned. The blood of men, horses and elephant mingled together.

sn: नापश्यम रजो भौमं कश्मलेनाभिसंवृताः। रात्रौ वंशवनस्येव दह्यमानस्य पर्वते॥
en: Stupefied with unconsciousness as we were we did not see any dust on the earth. Like the (creaking sounds) of a burning bamboo forest on a mountain during a night.

sn: बभूव रजनीमुखे। घोरचटचटाशब्दः शस्राणां पततामभूत्। मृदङ्गानकनि दैर्झर्झरैः पटहैस्तथा॥
en: There arose a dreadful clanging noise of the clashing weapons. In consequence of the sounds of Mridangas, Anakas, Vallakis and Patahas.

sn: फेत्कारैर्हेषितैः शब्दैः सर्वमेवाकुलं बभौ। नैव स्वे न परे राजन् प्राज्ञायन्त तमोवृते॥
en: And of the thundering shouts, of the combatants and the neigh (of steeds), O lord, everything was in utter confusion. O king, on account of darkness gathering fast, friends could not be distinguished from foes.

sn: उन्मत्तमिव तत् सर्वं भौमं रजोऽथ राजेन्द्र शोणितेन प्रणाशितम्॥
en: And at that night every one became as if seized with madness. O king of kings, then the dust on earth (soon) disappeared on account of (the profuse) flow of blood.

sn: शातकौम्भैश्च कवचैर्भूषणैश्च तमोऽभ्यगात्। ततः सा भारती सेना मणिहेमविभूषिता॥
en: (Then), on account of the golden armours and the ornaments (worn by the warriors) the gloom was dispersed. Adorned with gems and gold the Bharata army then.

sn: द्यौरिवासीत् सनक्षत्रा रजन्यां भरतर्षभ। गोमायुबलसंघुष्टा शक्तिध्वजसमाकुला॥
en: Looked like the firmament studded with stars during the night, О foremost of the Bharatas. (That field of battie) with maces and standards lying scattered all over, resounding with the howls of the Jackals.

sn: वारणाभिरुता घोरा क्षवेडितोत्क्रुष्टनादिता। तत्राभवन्महाशब्दस्तुमुलो लोमहर्षणः॥
en: Grunts of elephants and ringing with the striking of arms and shouts (of the combatants) appeared dreadful. Then there arose a great and tumultuous uproar, causing the hair to stand on end.

sn: समावृण्वन् दिश: सर्वा महेन्द्राशनिनिःस्वनः। सा निशीथे महाराज सेनादृश्यत भारती॥ अङ्गदैः कुण्डलैर्निष्कैः शस्त्रैश्चैवावभासिता। तत्र नागा रथाश्चैव जाम्बूनदविभूषिताः॥
en: And filling all the points like the roar of Mahendra's thunder. (A.d) great king, at that night the Bharata army illuminated with the Angadas, ear-rings, cuirasses and with the weapons could be (clearly) seen. There (on the field of battle) elephants and cars decked with gold.

sn: निशायां प्रत्यदृश्यन्त मेघा इव सविद्युतः। ऋषिशक्तिगदाबाणमुसलप्रासपट्टिशाः॥
en: Looked like clouds with lightning playing upon them during the night. Swords, darts, maces, scimitars, clubs, lances and axes.

sn: सम्पतन्तो व्यदृश्यन्त भ्राजमाना इवाग्नयः। दुर्योधनपुरोवातां रथनागबलाहकाम्॥
en: Looked like blazing sparks of fire when they fell. Duryodhana was the precursory wind, cars and elephants were the clouds,

sn: वादित्रघोषस्तनितां चापविद्युद्ज्ञैर्वृताम्। द्रोणपाण्डवपर्जन्या खड्गशक्तिगदाशनिम्॥
en: Sounds of musical instruments were the thundering noise, bow and standards were the lightning flashes; Drona and the Pandavas were the clouds, swords, darts and maces were the thunder.

sn: शरधारास्रपवनां भृशं शीतोष्णसंकुलाम्। घोरां विस्मापनीयमुग्रां जीवितच्छिदमप्लवाम्॥
en: And shower, both very hot and cold, of arrows and of (other) weapons were the gusts of wind-of that dreadful, marvellous and fierce (army) which was fata) to life and from which escape and not at all possible.

sn: तां प्राविशन्नतिभयां सेनां युद्धचिकीर्षवः। तस्मिन् रात्रिमुखे घोरे महाशब्दनिनादिते॥
en: desirous of battle, warriors entered fearlessly into that host at that dreadful night resounding with numerous sounds.

sn: भीरूणां त्रासजनने शूराणां हर्षवर्धने। रात्रियुद्धे महाघोरे वर्तमाने सुदारुणे॥
en: And when that awfully terrible and fierce nocturnal battle was raging which struck terror into (the minds of) the cowards and increased the joy of the valiant.

sn: द्रोणमभ्यद्रवन् क्रुद्धाः सहिताः पाण्डुसृञ्जयाः। ये ये प्रमुखतो राजन्नावर्तन्त महारथाः॥
en: The Pandavas and the Srinjayas united together rushed furiously against Drona. (But) O king, all those who confronted that highsouied one.

sn: तान् सर्वान् विमुखांश्चके कांश्चिन्निन्ये यमक्षयम्। तानि नागसहस्राणि रथानामयुतानि च।॥
en: Were driven back and some were sent to the abode of Yama. Thousands of elephants, ten thousands of car-warriors.

sn: पदातिहयसंघानां प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च। द्रोणेनैकेन नाराचैर्निर्भिन्नानि निशामुखे॥
en: Millions of foot-soldiers and hundreds of millions of horses were pierced with shafts by Drona alone at that night.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तस्मिन् प्रविष्टे दुधेर्षे सृञ्जयानमितौजसि। अमृध्यमाणे संरब्धे का वोऽभूद् वै मतिस्तदा॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When, unable to bear (the destruction of the king of Sindhu), that one of unrivaled energy and difficult of being vanquished penetrated into the Srinjayas what became the state of) your mind? one

sn: दुर्योधनं तथा पुत्रमुक्त्वा शास्त्रातिगं मम। यत् प्राविशदमेयात्मा किं पार्थः प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: Having addressed my disobedient son Duryodhana thus, when that of immeasurable energy entered into the Pandava army) what did Partha do?

sn: निहते सैन्धवे वीरे भूरिश्रवसि चैव ह। : यदाभ्यगान्महातेजाः पञ्चालानपराजित॥
en: (You say that) on the slaughter of the heroic king of Sindhu as well as of Bhurisrava that unvanquished one (i.e., Drona) endued with great energy rushed against the Srinjayas.

sn: किममन्यत दुधेचे प्रविष्टे शत्रुतापने। दुर्योधनस्तु किं कृत्यं प्राप्तकालममन्यत॥
en: What did (Partha) think on that invincible scorcher of foes having so entered? What also did Duryodhana think as to the most proper step that he could adopt at that time?

sn: के च तं वरदं वीरमन्वयुर्द्विजसत्तमम्। के चास्य पृष्ठतोऽगच्छन् वीराः शूरस्य युध्यतः॥
en: Who were they that followed the heroic bestower of boons, the foremost of the twiceborn ones? Who, O charioteer, were the warriors that remained behind that fighting hero?

sn: के पुरस्तादवर्तन्त निघ्नतः शात्रवान् रणे। मन्येऽहं पाण्डवान् सर्वान् भारद्वाजशरार्दितान्॥
en: Who were they that fought in, his van when he was destroying the enemies? I think that afflicted with the darts of the of Bharadvaja, all the Pandavas.

sn: शिशिरे कम्पमाना वै कृशा गाव इव प्रभो। प्रविश्य स महेष्वासः पञ्चालानरिमर्दनः। कथं नु पुरुषव्याघ्रः पञ्चत्वमुपजग्मिवान्॥
en: Like lean cows shivering in cold. Having entered into the Panchalas how that mighty wielder of bow, that grinder of foes and foremost of men came by his end?

sn: सर्वेणु योधेषु च संगतेषु रात्रौ समेतेषु महारथेषु। संलोड्यमानेषु पृथग्बलेषु के वस्तदानीं मतिमन्त आसन्॥
en: When, on that night, all the soldiers joined together and (all) the mighty car-warriors, combined, were being separately crushed, (by ona), who, were the intelligent men among you, that were then present?

sn: हतांश्चैव विषक्तांश्च पराभूतांश्च शंससि। रथिनो विरथांश्चैव कृतान् युद्धेषु मामकान्॥
en: son (You say) that, in the encounter. my soldiers were (either) killed, Driven away or defeated and that my car-warriors were deprived of their cars in the encounter.

sn: तेषां संलोड्यमानानां पाण्डवैर्हतचेतसाम्। अन्धे तमसि मग्नानामभवत् का पतिस्तदा॥
en: Crushed and deprived of senses by the Pandavas and buried in blinding darkness (as they were), what was (the state of) their mind?

sn: प्रहृष्टांश्चाप्युदग्रांश्च संतुष्टांश्चैव पाण्डवान्। शंससीहाप्रहृष्टांश्च विभ्रष्टांश्चैव मामकान्॥
en: You say that the Pandavas were full of joy and elated (with success) and that my partisans were cheerless, heartless and struck with terror,

sn: कथमेषां तदा तत्र पार्थानामपलायिनाम्। प्रकाशमभवद् रात्रौ कथं कुरुषु संजय॥
en: How, O chariotecr, O Sanjaya or that (dark) night could you unretreating sons of Partha and the Kurus?

sn: संजय उवाच रात्रियुद्धे तदा राजन् वर्तमाने सुदारुणे। द्रोणमभ्यद्रवन् सर्वे पाण्डवाः सह सोमकैः ॥
en: Sanjaya said Oking, when that greatly furious nocturnal battle was going on, all the Pandavas together with the Somakas rushed against Drona.

sn: ततो द्रोण: केकयांश्च धृष्टद्युम्नस्य चात्मजान्। सम्प्रेषयत् प्रेतलोकं सर्वानिषुभिराशुगैः॥
en: But Drona, by means of his swift-going darts, sent the Kekayas and sons of Dhrishtadyumna to the region of the departed spirits.

sn: तस्य प्रमुखतो राजन् येऽवर्तन्त महारथाः। तान् सर्वान् प्रेषयामास पितृलोकं स भारत॥
en: And Drona sent all those mighty carwarriors, those lords of earth who confronted hiin to the region of Pitris, O king.

sn: प्रमनन्तं तदा वीरान् भारद्वाजं महारथम्। अभ्यवर्तत संक्रुद्धः शिबी राजा प्रतापवान्॥
en: Then the powerful king Sibi furiously advanced against the heroic son of Bharadvaja, was the mighty-car warrior Drona who engaged in crushing (the enemy).

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य पाण्डवानां महारथम्। विव्याध दशभिर्बाणैः सर्वपारशवैः शितैः॥
en: Secing the great car-warrior of the Pandavas advance, Drona pierced him with ten arrows made wholly of steel.

sn: तं शिविः प्रतिविव्याध त्रिंशता निशितैः शरैः। सारथिं चास्य भल्लेन स्मयमानो न्यपातयत्॥
en: Sibi (too) pierced him (i.e., Drona) in return by thirty shafts adorned with the plumes of the Kanka (bird) and struck down his charioteer with a smile by a broad-headed shafts.

sn: तस्य द्रोणो हयान् हत्वा सारथिं च महात्मनः। अथास्य सशिरस्त्राणं शिरः कायादपाहरत्॥
en: (On the other hand) Drona, having killed the horses as well as the charioteer of that highsouled one, severed his head, adorned with a diadem, from the body.

sn: ततोऽस्य सारथिं क्षिप्रमन्यं दुर्योधनोऽदिशत्। स तेन संगृहीताश्वः पुनरभ्यद्रवद् रिपून्॥
en: Duryodhana then quickly ordered charioteer (to guide Drona's car). The reins of the) horses being taken by him, he (i.c., Drona) again proceeded against his foes.

sn: कलिङ्गानामनीकेन कालिङ्गस्य सुतो रणे। पूर्वं पितृवघात् क्रुद्धो भीमसेनमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Accompanied by the Kalinga forces the son of the king of Kalinga, excited with wrath for the destruction of his father by Bhimasena, rushed towards him.

sn: स भीमं पञ्चभिर्विद्ध्वा पुनर्विव्याध सप्तभिः। विशोकं त्रिभिरानछेद् ध्वजमेकेन पत्रिणा॥
en: Having (first) pierced Bhima with five shafts and then again with seven, be struck Vishoka (Bhima's chariotcer) with three darts and his (i.e. Bhima's) standard with one.

sn: कलिङ्गानां तु तं शूरं क्रुद्धं क्रुद्धो वृकोदरः। रथाद् रथमभिद्रुत्य मुष्टिनाभिजघान ह॥
en: Vrikodara, then fired with rage, leaped from (his own) car to that of the heroic prince of a : Kalinga, who also was (very) angry and killed him with blows from his fists.

sn: तस्य मुष्टिहतस्याजौ पाण्डवेन बलीयसा। सर्वाण्यस्थीनि सहसा प्रापतन् वै पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: All the bones of that one (i.c., the Kalinga prince) thus boxed to death by the powerful Pandava, suddenly fell down on the ground separated from one another.

sn: तं कर्णो भ्रातरश्चास्य नामृष्यन्त परंतप। ते भीमसेनं नाराचैर्जघ्नुराशीविषोपमैः॥
en: Karna and all the brothers (of the Kalinga prince) could not bear that act of the part of Bhimasena. They (therefore) struck him with keen darts (as fierce) as poisonous snakes.

sn: ततः शत्रुरथं त्यक्त्वा भीमो ध्रुवरथं गतः। ध्रुवं चास्यन्तमनिशं मुष्टिना समपोथयत्॥
en: Bhima, then leaving the car of his enemy (i.e., dead Kalinga prince) made for the car of Dhruva and smashed Dhruva who was incessantly striking him, by a blow of his fist.

sn: स तथा पाण्डुपुत्रेण बलिनाभिहतोऽपतत्। तं निहत्य महाराज भीमसेनो महाबलः॥
en: Thus struck by the powerful son of Pandu, he fell down (from his car). The highly powerful Bhimasena, Oking, after slaying him.

sn: जयरातरथं प्राप्य मुहुः सिंह इवानदत्। जयरातमथाक्षिप्य नदन् सव्येन पाणिना॥
en: Got up to the car of Jayadratha and repeatedly sent forth leoninc roars. While roaring he hurled him down with his left hand.

sn: तलेन नाशयामास कर्णस्यैवाग्रतः स्थितः। कर्णस्तु पाण्डवे शक्तिं काञ्चनीं समवासृजत्॥
en: And he (then) killed him with a slap in the very presence of Karna himself. Karna then shot a golden dart at that Pandava.

sn: यतस्तामेव जग्राह प्रहसन् पाण्डुनन्दनः। कर्णायैव च दुर्धर्षश्चिक्षेपाजौ वृकोदरः॥
en: But the son of Pandu seized that (dart) with a smile. And in that encounter the invincible Vrikodara hurled that very dart of Karna.

sn: तामापतन्ती चिच्छेद शकुनिस्तैलपायिना। एतत् कृत्वा महत् कर्म रणेऽद्भुपराक्रमः॥
en: (Then) Shakuni cut-off that dart while it was coming (towards Karna) by a shaft saturated with oil. Having performed such great exploits in battle, that one of marvellous prowess.

sn: पुनः स्वरथमास्थाय दुद्राव तव वाहिनीम्। तमायान्तं जिघांसन्तं भीमं क्रुद्धमिवान्तकम्॥
en: Returned to his own car and (then) rushed against your troops. When Bhima desirous of staying (your troops), was (thus) advancing furiously like the (grim) destroyer himself.

sn: न्यवारयन् महाबाहुं तव पुत्रा विशाम्पते। महता शरवर्षेण च्छादयन्तो महारथाः॥
en: Your mighty armed-sons, those great carwarriors tried to check his career by enveloping him with mighty showers of arrows.

sn: दुर्मदस्य ततो भीमः प्रहसन्निव संयुगे। सारथिं च हयांश्चैव शर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्॥
en: Then Bhima, with a smile, sent the charioteer and the steeds of Durmada in that battle to the abode of Yama with his shafts.

sn: दुर्मदस्तु ततो यानं दुष्कर्णस्यावचक्रमे। तावेकरथमारूढौ भ्रातरौ परतापनौ॥
en: Durmada then got to the car of Duskarna. Those two brothers, the tormentors of foes, mounted on the same car.

sn: संग्रामशिरसो मध्ये भीमं द्वावप्यधावताम्। यथाम्बुपतिमित्रौ हि तारकं दैत्यसत्तमम्॥
en: Both rushed against Bhima in the van of the battle, as the lord of the water (i.e. Varuna) (had rushed against) Taraka, the foremost of the Daitayas (in days of yore).

sn: ततस्तु दुर्मदश्चैव दुष्कर्णश्च तवात्मजौ। रथमेकं समारुह्य भीमं बाणैरविध्यताम्॥
en: Then your sons Durmada and Duskarna ascending the same car pierced Bhima with arrows.

sn: ततः कर्णस्य मिषतो द्रौणे दुर्योधनस्य च। कृपस्य सोमदत्तस्य बाहीकस्य च पाण्डवः॥
en: Then in the very sight of Karna and Duryodhana and in that of Kripa, Somadatta and Balhika, the Pandava,

sn: दुर्मदस्य च वीरस्य दुष्कर्णस्य च तं रथम्। पादप्रहारेण धरां प्रावेशयदरिंदमः॥
en: That chastiser of foes, buried the car of the heroic Durmada and that of Duskarna into the earth with the stroke of his foot.

sn: ततः सुतौ ते बलिनौ शूरौ दुष्कर्णदुर्मदौ। मुष्टिनाऽऽहत्य संक्रुद्धो ममर्द च ननर्द च॥
en: Then striking furiously with the blows of his fits those two heroic and powerful sons of yours, Duskama and Durmada, he crushed them (therewith) and sent forth thundering shouts.

sn: ततो हाहाकृते सैन्ये दृष्ट्वा भीमं नृपाऽब्रुवन्। रुद्रोऽयं भीमरूपेण धार्तराष्ट्रेषु युध्यति॥
en: Then your troops began to wail aloud and the kings seeing Bhima, said. "He is Rudra himself who assuming the shape of a Bhima is fighting with the troops of Dhritarashtra.”

sn: एवमुक्त्वा पलायन्ते सर्वे भारत पार्थिवाः। विसंज्ञा वाहयन् वाहान् न च द्वौ सह धावतः॥
en: 0 Bharata, saying this, all the kings deprived, (as it were) of their senses and urging the animals (on which they rode), fled away (from the field) and no two then (so great was their terror) did run together.

sn: ततो बले भृशलुलिते निशामुखे। सुपूजितो नृपवृषभैर्वृकोदरः। महाबल: कमलविबुद्धलोचनो युधिष्ठिरं नृपतिमपूजयद् बली॥
en: The army (of the Kurus) being thus greatly crushed, in that night, the heroic and highly powerful Vrikodara, endued with full blown lotus-like eyes, being highly complemented by (many) foremost of kings, paid his regards to king Yudhishthira.

sn: ततो यमौ दुपदविराटकेकया युधिष्ठिरश्चापि परां मुदं ययुः। वृकोदरं भृशमनुपूजयंश्च ते यथान्धके प्रतिनिहते हरं सुराः॥
en: Then the twins (i.e., Nakula and Sahadeva), Drupada, Virata and the Kekayas as well as Yudhishthira experienced a great joy and paid high complements to Vrikodara as the celestials paid to Hara after the slaughter of Andhaka by him.

sn: ततः सुतास्ते वरुणात्मजोपमा रुषान्विताः सह गुरुणा महात्मना। वृकोदरं सरथपदातिकुञ्जरा युयुत्सवो भृशमभिपर्यवारयन्॥
en: Then your sons resembling those of Varuna filled with wrath and eager for battle led by (their) high-souled preceptor surrounded on all sides Vrikodara by cars foot-soldiers and clephants.

sn: ततोऽभवत् तिमिरघनैरिवावृते महाभये भयदमतीव दारुणम्। निशामुखे वृकबलगृध्रमोदनं महात्मनां नृपवर युद्धमद्भुतम्॥
en: Then, O best of kings, on that dreadful night enveloped with darkness thick as clouds, there took place, between those high-souled ones, an awe-inspiring and terrible battle delightful to wolves, crows and vultures.

sn: संजय उवाच प्रायोपविष्टे तु हते पुत्र सात्यकिना तदा। सोमदत्तो भृशं क्रुद्धः सात्यकिं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Enraged at the slaughter of his son, while he was sitting with the desire of dying without food, Somadatta said these words to Satyakiक्षत्रधर्म: पुरा दृष्टो यस्तु देवैर्महात्मभिः।

sn: तं त्वं सात्वत संत्यज्य दस्युधर्मे कथं रतः॥
en: Why, O Satvata, without observing the Kshatriya duties as formerly laid down by the gods, have you taken to the practices of robbers?

sn: पराङ्मुखाय दीनाय न्यस्तशस्त्राय सात्यके। क्षत्रधर्मरतः प्राज्ञः कथं नु प्रहरेद् रणे॥
en: How can a wise person, practising the Kshatriya duties, strike in battle one who runs away or is helpless or has laid aside his weapons or who begs (for his life)?

sn: द्वावेव किल वृष्णीनां तत्र ख्यातौ महारथौ। प्रद्युम्नश्च महाबाहुस्त्वं चैव युधि सात्वत॥
en: O Satvata, it is said that among the Vrishnis there are two principal and mighty car-warriors in battle, namely, the highly highly energetic Pradyumna and yourself.

sn: कथं प्रायोपविष्टाय पार्थेन छिन्नबाहवे। नृशंसं पतनीयं च तादृशं कृतवानसि॥
en: Why then did you practise such a cruelty and commit such an act, that would lead to your downfall, towards one that had sat in prayer and whose arms had been cut-off by Partha?

sn: कर्मणस्तस्य दुर्वृत्त फलं प्राप्नुहि संयुगे। अद्य च्छेत्स्यामि ते मूढ शिरो विक्रम्य पत्रिणा॥
en: 0 wicked one, suffer (now) the consequences of that act of yours in battle. Exerting my strength, O fool, I will today cutoff your head with arrows?

sn: शपे सात्वत पुत्राभ्यामिष्टेन सुकृतेन च। अनतीतामिमां रात्रिं यदि त्वां वीरमानिनम्॥ अरक्ष्यमाणं पार्थन जिष्णुना ससुतानुजम्। न हन्यां नरके घोरे पतेयं वृष्णिपांसन॥
en: O Satvata, I swear by my two sons, by what is dear to me and by the virtuous deeds, if before this night comes to a close I fail to destroy you, you that so much pride on your heroism, together with your sons and younger brothers, unless you are backed up by fishnu, the son of Pritha, then, O wretch of Vrishnis, may I fall into dreadful hell.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा सुसंक्रुद्धः सोमदत्तो महाबलः दध्मौ शङ्ख च तारेण सिंहनादं ननाद च॥
en: The highly powerful Somadatta, excited with wrath, having said thus, blew loudly (his) conch and sent forth roars like a lion.

sn: ततः कमलपत्राक्षः सिंहदंष्ट्रो दुरासदः। सात्यकि शसंक्रुद्धः सोमदत्तमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the greatly powerful Satyaki endued with eyes (beautiful) as lotus petals and possessed of leonine teeth greatly enraged thus addressed Somadatta.

sn: कौरवेय न मे त्रासः कथंचिदपि विद्यते। त्वया सार्धमथान्यैश्च युध्यतो हृदि कश्चन॥
en: "O descendant of the Kurus, I entertain not the least fear in my heart whether fighting with you or with others.

sn: यदि सर्वेण सैन्येन गुप्तो मां योधयिष्यसि। तथापि न व्यथा काचित् त्वयि स्यान्मम कौरव॥
en: I shall not experience the slightest pain, even if backed up by all your forces you fight with me, Oscion of the Kuru race.

sn: युद्धसारेण वाक्येन असतां सम्मतेन च। नाहं भीषयितुं शक्यः क्षत्रवृत्ते स्थितस्त्वया॥
en: Observant of the practices of the Kshatriyas as I am, I can to be terrified with words smelling of battle and insulting to the virtuous.

sn: यदि तेऽस्ति युयुत्साद्य मया सह नराधिप। निर्दयो निशितैर्बाणैः प्रहर प्रहरामि ते॥
en: If, O lord of men, you are desirous of fighting with me, strike me with sharpened arrows and I also will strike you (in return).

sn: हतो भूरिश्रवा वीरस्तव पुत्रो महारथः। शलश्चैव महाराज भ्रातृव्यसनकर्षितः॥
en: O king, your son, the mighty car-warrior Bhurisrava has been slain. Then the heroic Shala and Vrisena too have been destroyed.

sn: त्वां चाप्यद्य वधिष्यामि सह पुत्रं सबान्धवम्। तिष्ठेदानीं रणे यत्तः कौरवोऽसि महारथः॥
en: I will today destroy you also together with your sons and friends, you are a descendant of the Kuru race and are endued with great prowess. Now remain carefully in battle.

sn: यस्मिन् दानं दमः शौचमहिंसा ही तिः क्षमा। अनपायानि सर्वाणि नित्यं राज्ञि युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: King Yudhishthira is always characterised by charity, self-restraint, purity, absence of cruelty, modesty, intelligence and forgiveness and all (the virtuous) that do not perish.

sn: मृदङ्गकेतोस्तस्य त्वं तेजसा निहतः पुरा। सकर्णसौबलः संख्ये विनाशमुपयास्यसि॥
en: You, who have been already slain by the energy of that one who standard bears the mark of a drum, will be destroyed in battle together with Shakuni and Soubala.

sn: शपेऽहं कृष्णचरणैरिष्टापूर्तेन चैव ह। यदि त्वां ससतुं पापं न हन्यां युधि रोषितः॥
en: I swear today by Krishna's feet and all the meritorious acts that I had done before, that I will wrathfully kill you in battle together with your sons, with arrows.

sn: अपयास्यसि चेत्युक्त्वा रणं मुक्तो भविष्यसि। एवमाभाष्य चान्योन्यं क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनौ।॥
en: If, however, you run away (from the field), you may be freed (from me).' Thus addressing each other, with eyes reddened with rage.

sn: प्रवृत्तौ शरसम्पातं कर्तुं पुरुषसत्तमौ। ततो रथसहस्रेण नागानामयुतेन च।॥
en: Those two foremost of men began to discharge arrows (at each other, Then with a thousand cars and ten thousand cars and ten thousand horses.

sn: दुर्योधनः सोमदत्तः परिवार्य समन्ततः। शकुनिश्च सुसंक्रुद्धः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः॥
en: Duryodhana stood surrounding Somadatta. Shakuni, too excited with wrath and armed with all the weapons.

sn: पुत्रपौत्रैः परिवृतो भ्रातृभिश्चन्द्रविक्रमैः। स्यालस्तव महाबाहुर्वज्रसंहननो युवा॥
en: And surrounded by sons and grandsons and brother powerful as Indra himself (followed Duryodhana's example), Your youthful brother-in-low. O king, endued with a body hard as the thunderbolt.

sn: साग्रं शतसहस्रं तु हयानां तस्य धीमतः। सोमदत्तं महेष्वासं समन्तात् पर्यरक्षत॥
en: And gifted with wisdom and who had with him one hundred thousand steeds of best breed, completely hemmed in that mighty bowman Somadatta.

sn: रक्ष्यमाणश्च बलिभिश्छादयामास सात्यकिम्। तं छाद्यमानं विशिखैर्दृष्ट्वा संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Supported by those heroes, (Somadatta) covered Satyaki with arrows. Seeing him covered with straight arrows,

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नोऽभ्ययात् क्रुद्धः प्रगृह्य महतीं चमूम्। चण्डवाताभिसृष्टानामुदधीनामिव स्वनः॥
en: Dhristadyumna, followed by a large army, proceeded wrathfully (towards him). Like the roar of waters dashed into fury by a terrible hurricane.

sn: आसीद् राजन् वलौघानामन्योन्यमभिनिघ्नताम्। विव्याध सोमदत्तस्तु सात्वतं नवभिः शरैः॥
en: There arose, O king, a great tumult among the (two) forces striking each other. Somadatta then pierced Satvata with nine arrows.

sn: सात्यकिर्नवभिश्चैनमवधीत् कुरुपुङ्गवम्। सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता समरे दृढधन्विना॥
en: Satyaki too pierced that foremost of Kurus with nine shafts. Deeply wounded in battle by that powerful and firm wielder of bow.

sn: रथोपस्थं समासाद्य मुमोह गतचेतनः। तं विमूढं समालक्ष्य सारथिस्त्वरया युतः।॥
en: (Somadatta) leaned against the terrace of his car and (then) swooned away and was deprived of consciousness. Seeing that he was deprived of consciousness, his charioteer, in great hurry.

sn: अपोवाह रणाद् वीरं सोमदत्तं महारथम्। तं विसंज्ञं समालक्ष्य युयुधानशरार्दितम्॥
en: Carried away the heroic and mighty carwarrior Somadatta from (the field of) battle. Beholding him deprived of senses and afflicted with the arrows of Yuyudhana.

sn: अभ्यद्रवत् ततो द्रोणो यदुवीरजिघांसया। तमायान्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमाः॥
en: Drona desirous of slaying the heroic (Yadu rushed (at him). Seeing (i.e. Drona advance), Yudhishthira (putting himself) at the head (of his troops).

sn: परिवQर्महात्मानं परीप्सन्तो यदूत्तमम्। ततः प्रववृते युद्धं द्रोणस्य सह पाण्डवैः॥
en: With the desire of rescuing the high-souled perpetuator of the Yadu race surrounded him on all sides. Then there commenced a battle between Drona and the Pandavas,

sn: बलेरिव सुरैः पूर्वं त्रैलोक्यजयकाङ्क्षया। ततः सायकजालेन पाण्डवानीकमावृणोत्॥
en: Like that (which took place) in days of yore between Bali and the celestials (both) desirous of the conquest of the three worlds. Then covering the Pandava army with arrowy showers.

sn: भारद्वाजो महातेजा विव्याध च युधिष्ठिरम्। सात्यकिं दशभिर्बाणैविंशत्या पार्षतं शरैः॥
en: The highly-energetic son of Bharadvaja pierced Yudhishthira also. (Drona then struck) Satyaki with ten darts and the son of Prishata (i.e. Dhristadyumna) with twenty five darts.

sn: भीमसेनं च नवभिर्नकुलं पञ्चभिस्तथा। सहदेवं तथाष्टाभिः शतेन च शिखण्डिनम्॥
en: (And he pierced) Bhimasena with nine, Nakula with five, Sahadeva with eight and Shikhandi with one hundred arrows.

sn: द्रौपदेयान् महाबाहुः पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिः शरैः। विराटं मत्स्यमष्टाभिर्दुपदं दशभिः शरैः॥
en: That mighty armed one (then pierced) each of (the five) sons of Draupadi with five arrows, Virata the king of Matsyas with eight, Drupada with ten darts.

sn: युधामन्यु त्रिभिः षडभिरुत्तमौजसमाहवे। अन्यांश्च सैनिकान् विद्ध्वा युधिष्ठिरमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Yudhamanu with three and Uttamanja with six (arrows) in that battle. (Similarly) piercing many other soldiers (he) rushed against Yudhishthira.

sn: ते वध्यमाना द्रोणेन पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैनिकाः। प्राद्रवन् वै भयाद् राजन् सार्तनादा दिशो दश॥
en: (Thus) struck by Drona, the troops of the son of Pandu with loud wails fled away in terror in ten directions, O king.

sn: काल्यमानं तु तत् सैन्यं दृष्ट्वा फाल्गुनः। किंचिदागतसंरम्भो गुरुं पार्थोऽभ्ययाद् द्रुतम्॥
en: Seeing that are army was being slaughtered by Drona, Phalguna Partha, enraged a little, advanced speedily against his preceptor.

sn: दृष्ट्वा द्रोणं तु बीभत्सुमभिधावन्तमाहवे। संन्यवर्तत तत् सैन्यं पुनौधिष्ठिरं बलम्॥
en: O king, beholding that Drona too was advancing against Vibhatsu in that battle, the soldiers of Yudhishthira rallied again.

sn: ततो युद्धमभूद् भूयो भारद्वाजस्य पाण्डवैः। द्रोणस्तव सुतै राजन् सर्वतः परिवारितः॥
en: Then again commenced a battle between the sons of Bharadvaja and the Pandavas. Drona, O king, completely surrounded by your sons.

sn: व्यधमत् पाण्डुसैन्यानि तूलराशिमिवानलः। तं ज्वलन्तमिवादित्यं दीप्तानलसमद्युतिम्॥
en: Began to destroy the troops of the Pandavas, as fire (consumes) a heap of cotton. (He then) looked like the radiant sun and was endued with the resplendence of a blazing fire.

sn: राजन्ननिशमत्यन्तं दृष्ट्वा द्रोणं शरार्चिषम्। मण्डलीकृतधन्वानं तपन्तमिव भास्करम्॥
en: O king, seeing Drona incessantly discharge fierce arrows like sparks of fire from his bow drawn to a circle and like the scorching sun.

sn: दहन्तमहितान् सैन्ये नैनं कश्चिदवारयत्। यो यो हि प्रमुखे तस्य तस्थौ द्रोणस्य पुरुषः॥
en: Consume the evenings there was none among the arıny that could withstand him. Those persons who stood before Drona (in order to resist him).

sn: तस्य तस्य शिरश्छित्त्वा ययुोणशराः क्षितिम्। एवं सा पाण्डवी सेना वध्यमाना महात्मना॥
en: Had their heads cut-off by Drona with arrows which (then) entered into the earth. The army of the Pandavas thus slaughtered by that high-souled one.

sn: प्रदुद्राव पुनर्भीता पश्यतः सव्यसाचिनः। सम्प्रभग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा द्रोणेन निशि भारत॥
en: Again ran away in terror (even) in the very sight of Savyasachi. Seeing his lines broken by Drona at (that) night, O Bharata.

sn: गोविन्दमब्रवीज्जिष्णुर्गच्छ द्रोणरथं प्रति। ततो रजतगोक्षीरकुन्देन्दुसदृशप्रभान्॥ चोदयामास दाशार्हो हयान् द्रोणरथं प्रति। भीमसेनोऽपि तं दृष्ट्वा यान्तं द्रोणस्य फाल्गुनम्॥
en: Jishnu said to Govinda "proceed towards the car of Drona.” Then that Dasarha (chief) drove the horses, looking like silver or milk of cows or like the Kunda flower, towards the car of Drona. Sceing that Phalguna was proceeding towards Drona, Bhimasena too.

sn: स्वसारथिमुवाचेदं द्रोणानीकाय मा वह। सोऽपि तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा विशोकोऽवाहयद्धयान्॥ ४९
en: Ordered his own charioteer to take him towards Drona's troops. Visaka (the charioteer of Bhima), hearing those words of his (master) guided the steeds.

sn: पृष्ठतः सत्यसंधस्य जिष्णोर्भरतसत्तम। तौ दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ यत्तौ द्रोणानीकमभिद्रुतौ॥
en: Behind Jishnu of unerring aim, O foremost of the Bharatas. Seeing those two brothers resolutely rush towards Drona's division.

sn: पञ्चाला: सृञ्जया मत्स्याश्चेदिकारुषकोसलाः। अन्वगच्छन् महाराज केकयाश्च महारथाः॥
en: The Panchalas, the Srinjayas, the Matsyas, the Chedis, the Kauravas, the Kosalas and those mighty car-warriors, the Keykayas followed suit, O great king.

sn: ततो राजन्नभूद् घोरः संग्रामो लोमहर्षणः। बीभत्सुर्दक्षिणं पार्श्वमुत्तरं च वृकोदरः॥ महद्भ्यां रथवृन्दाभ्यां बल जगृहतुस्तव। तौ दृष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रौ भीमसेनधनंजयौ॥
en: Then, O king, ensued a dreadful encounter, making the hair stand erect. Vivastsu, then, attacked the right and Vrikodara the left flank of your army with innumerable cars. Seeing those two foremost of men, viz., Bhimasena and Dhananjaya, (proceed towards Drona's troops).

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नोऽभ्ययाद् राजन् सात्यकिश्च महाबलः। चण्डवाताभिपन्नानामुदधीनामिव स्वनः॥
en: Dhristadyumna as well as the highly powerful Satyaki rushed (at them) like the roar of waters dashed into fury by a terrible hurricane.

sn: आसीद् राजन् बलौघानां तदान्योन्यमभिघ्नताम्। सौमदत्तिवधात् क्रुद्धो दृष्ट्वा सात्यकिमाहवे॥
en: There arose a great tumult among the combatants striking each other. Seeing Satyaki in battle and enraged at the slaughter of the son of Somadatta,

sn: द्रौणिरभ्यद्रवद् राजन वधाय कृतनिश्चयः। तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य शैनेयस्य रथं प्रति॥
en: The son of Drona rushed furiously against Satvatta at the van of battle. (Seeing) him proceed towards the car of the grandson of Sini in battle.

sn: भैमसेनिः सुसंक्रुद्धः प्रत्यमित्रमवारयत्। कार्णायसं महाघोरमृक्षचर्मपरिच्छदम्॥ महान्तं रथमास्थाय त्रिंशन्नल्वान्तरान्तरम्। विक्षिप्तयन्त्रसंनाहं महामेघौघनिःस्वनम्॥
en: That gigantic Rakshasa, the of Bhimasena, possessed of enormous strength, rushed (at him) inounted on a huge and awfully dreadful car made of black iron covered with bear-skin, measuring thirty Nalvas in height and width, furnished with various machines and emitting thundering roars like those of a mighty (mass of) clouds.

sn: युक्तं गजनिभैहिर्न हयैर्नापि वारणैः। विक्षिप्तपक्षचरणविवृताक्षेण कूजता॥
en: (And it was) drawn by animals looking like elephants; but they were neither elephants nor horses. With its wings and feet outstretched son and with expanded eyes and emitting (terrible) shrieks.

sn: ध्वजेनोच्छ्रितदण्डेन गृध्रराजेन राजितम्। लोहितापताकं त अन्त्रमालाविभूषितम्॥
en: A prince of vultures sat on its towering standard. (That car) was adorned with red flags furnished with rows of bones.

sn: अष्टचक्रसमायुक्तमास्थाय विपुलं रथम्। शूलमुद्गरधारिण्या शैलपादपहस्तया।॥ रक्षसां घोररूपाणामक्षौहिण्या समावृतः। तमुद्यतमहाचापं निशम्य व्यथिता नृपाः॥
en: And with eight wheels. (And he) sat down on this car surrounding by one Akshauhini of terrible-looking Rakshasa armed with maces and clubs and carrying rocks an trees in their hands. The kings were (greatly) pained on seeing him (to advance) with upraised bow.

sn: युगान्तकालसमये दण्डहस्तमिवान्तकम्। ततस्तं गिरिशृङ्गाभ भीमरूपं भयावहम्॥
en: Look like the very destroyer himself, mace in hand, at the time of universal dissolution. (And he) resembled a mountain peak, was frightful to look at and dreadful.

sn: दंष्ट्राकरलोग्रमुखं शङ्कुकर्णं महाहनुम्। अर्ध्वकेशं विरूपाक्षं दीप्तास्यं निम्नितोदरम्॥
en: (He) had terrible teeth and a dreadful face, was possessed of arrow-like ears, high cheek bones, shooting hair, un-natural eyes, flaming mouth and a sunken belly.

sn: महाश्वभ्रगलद्वारं किरीटच्छन्नमूर्धजम्। त्रासनं सर्वभूतानां व्यात्ताननमिवान्तकम्॥
en: His oesophagus was deep as a yawning pit and his head was furnished with a coronet. He was dreadful to all creatures and his jaws were as wide as those of the Destroyer himself.

sn: वीक्ष्य दीप्तमिवायान्तं रिपुविक्षोभकारिणम्। तमुद्यतमहाचापं राक्षसेन्द्र घटोत्कचम्॥
en: Seeing Gatotkacha, the lord of the Rakshasas endued with splendour and capable of striking terror into foes, advance upraising his great bow.

sn: भयार्दिता प्रचुक्षोभ पुत्रस्य तव वाहिनी। वायुना क्षोभितावर्ता गङ्गेचोर्ध्वतरङ्गिणी॥
en: Your son's forces struck with panic became as much agitated as when the waves of Ganga (dashed into fury) by a tempest are agitated into whirlpools.

sn: घटोत्कचप्रयुक्तेन सिंहनादेन भीषिताः। प्रसुस्रवुर्गजा मूत्रं विव्यथुश्च नरा भृशम्॥
en: Struck with panic by the leonine roars sent forth by Ghatotkacha, the elephants began to pass urine and the kings were greatly distressed.

sn: ततोऽश्मवृष्टिरत्यर्थमासीत् तत्र समन्ततः। संध्याकालाधिकबलैः प्रयुक्ता राक्षसैः क्षितौ॥
en: Hurled by the Rakshasa who became more powerful on night-fall, there began to fall from all sides showers of stones on the ground.

sn: आयसानि च चक्राणि भुशुण्ड्यः प्रासतोमराः। पतन्त्यविरता: शूलाः शतघ्यः पट्टिशास्तथा॥
en: Showers of iron, wheels, Bhushundis, arrows, spears, Sataghness and axes also began to fall there incessantly.

sn: तदुग्रमतिरौद्रं च दृष्ट्वा युद्धं नराधिपाः। तनयास्तव कर्णश्च व्यथिताः प्राद्रवन् दिशः॥
en: Seeing that furious and terrible battle the kings, your sons and Karna too, being (greatly) distressed, ran away from the battle field).

sn: तत्रैकोऽस्रबलश्लाघी द्रौणिर्मानी च विव्यथे। व्यधमच शरैर्मायां घटोत्कचविनिर्मिताम्॥
en: There the haughty son, of Drona only proud of his prowess in weapons, stood without fear (and he) soon did away with the illusion created by Ghatotkacha.

sn: विहतायां तु मायायाममर्षी स घटोत्कचः। विससर्ज शरान् घोरांस्तेऽश्वत्थामानमाविशन्॥ भुजङ्गा इव वेगेन वल्मीकं क्रोधमूर्छिताः। ते शरा रुधिराक्ताङ्गा भित्त्वा शारद्वतीसुतम्॥
en: Enraged at the illusion being dispelled (by the son of Drona), Ghatotkacha began to discharge fierce arrows. Those (arrows) penetrated into (the body of) Asvatthama. As snakes insensible with rage furiously (enter into) an ant-hill, those arrows penetrating through (the body of) the son of Saradvata became covered with blood.

sn: विविशुर्धरणीं शीघ्रा रुक्मपुङ्खाः शिलाशिताः। अश्वत्थामा तु संक्रुद्धो लघुहस्तः प्रतापवान्॥
en: And then speedily entered into the earth like serpents (entering) an ant-hill. The lighthanded and powerful Ashvatthama too, excited with wrath.

sn: घटोत्कचमभिक्रुद्धं बिभेद दशभिः शरैः। घटोत्कचोऽतिविद्धस्तु द्रोणपुत्रेण मर्मसु॥
en: Furiously pierced Ghatotkacha with ten arrows. Deeply pierced in the vital parts by the son of Drona, Ghatotkacha.

sn: चक्रं शतसहस्रारमृगह्नाद् व्यथितो भृशम्। क्षुरान्तं बालसूर्याभं मणिवज्रविभूषितम्॥
en: Became greatly afflicted and then took up a wheel furnished with one hundred thousand spokes. (this wheel) the edge of which was sharp as that of a razor and which was as resplendent as the morning sun and was studded with gems and precious stones.

sn: अश्वत्थाम्न स चिक्षेप भैमसेनिर्जिघांसया। वेगेन महताऽऽगच्छद् विक्षिप्तं द्रौणिना शरैः॥
en: Was hurled by the son of Bhimasena at Ashvatthama with the desire of slaying (him). cut-off into fragments by the son of Drona with arrows as it coursed with great speed (towards him).

sn: अभाग्यस्येव संकल्पस्तन्मोघमपतद् भुवि। घटोत्कचस्ततस्तूर्णं दृष्ट्वा चक्रं निपातितम्॥
en: If fell down on the ground like the purposes of an unlucky person. Seeing his wheel cut down, Ghatotkacha speedily.

sn: द्रौणिं प्राच्छादयद् बाणैः स्वर्भानुरिव भास्करम्। घटोत्कचसुतः श्रीमान् भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमः॥
en: Covered the son of Drona with shafts as Sarbhanu (i.e. Rahu) swallows the creator of light (i.e. the sun). The resplendent son of Ghatotkacha resembling a mass of antimony.

sn: रुरोध द्रौणिमायान्तं प्रभञ्जनमिवाद्रिराट्। पौत्रेण भीमसेनस्य शरैरञ्जनपर्वणा॥
en: Arrested the advance of the son of Drona as the king of mountains (checks the career of) the wind. (Struck with arrows) by the heroic Anjanaparva, the grandson of Bhimasena.

sn: बभौ मेघेन धाराभिर्गिरिर्मेरुरिवावृतः। अश्वत्थामा त्वसम्भ्रान्तो रुद्रोपेन्द्रेन्द्रविक्रमः॥
en: (The son of Drona) looked like the mountain Meru drenched with (copious) showers of rain from the clouds. Ashvatthama also endued with a prowess equal to that of Rudra or Upendra, becoming highly enraged.

sn: ध्वजमेकेन बाणेन चिच्छेदाञ्जनपर्वणः। द्वाभ्यां तु रथयन्तारौ त्रिभिश्चास्य त्रिवेणुकम्॥
en: Cut off the standard of Anjanaparva with one arrow, his two charioteers with two and his Trivenduka with four (arrows).

sn: धनुरेकेन चिच्छेद चतुर्भिश्चतुरो हयान्। विरथस्योद्यतं हस्ताद्धेमबिन्दुभिरावितम्॥ विशिखेन सुतीक्ष्णेन खङ्गमस्य द्विधाकरोत्। गदा हेमाङ्गदा राजंस्तूर्णं हैडिम्बिसुनूना॥
en: With one (arrow) he cut-off his bow and with four his four steeds. Deprived of his car, as he (i.e. the son of Ghatotkach) took up a scimitar studded with golden stars, in his hand and flourished it, (Ashvatthama) severed it into two parts of by a keen dart. Then, O king, the grandson of Hidimva speedily (took up) a mace decked with gold;

sn: भ्राम्योत्क्षिप्ता शरैः साऽपि द्रौणिनाभ्याहताऽपतत्। ततोऽन्तरिक्षमुत्प्लुत्य कालमेघ इवोन्नदन्॥ ववर्षाञ्जनीपर्वा स दुमवर्ष नभस्तलात्। ततो मायाधरं द्रौणिर्घटोत्कचसुतं दिवि॥ मार्गणैरभिविव्याध घनं सूर्य इवांशुभिः। सोऽवतीर्य पुरस्तस्थौ रथे हेमविभूषिते॥
en: And whirling it, (he) hurled (that mace at Ashvatthama). But the son of Drona, striking it (with arrows) filled it (to the ground). Then, leaping up in the air and roaring like black clouds, Anjaniparva began to pour down son showers of trees from the firmament. Then the son of Drona began to pierce that one capable of (creating) illusions by means of shafts in the sky as the sun (pierces) the clouds with his rays. Seated on his car again decked with gold, when that one of great strength.

sn: महीगत इवात्युग्रः श्रीमानञ्जनपर्वतः। तमयस्मयवर्माणं द्रौणिर्भीमात्मजात्मजम्॥ जघानाञ्जनपर्वाणं महेश्वर इवान्धकम्। अथ दृष्ट्वा हतं पुत्रमश्वत्थाम्ना महाबलम्॥
en: Looking like a high and beautiful mountain of antimony, descended to the earth, the son of Drona slew th the of Bhima's son, Anjanaparva, clad in armour as Maheshvara (killed) the Asura) Andhaka in days of yore. Seeing his son of enormous strength killed Ashvatthama.

sn: द्रौणेः सकाशमभ्येत्य रोषात् प्रज्वलिताङ्गदः। प्राह वाक्यमसम्भ्रान्तो वीरं शारद्वतीसुतम्॥ दहन्तं पाण्डवानीकं वनमग्निमिवोच्छ्रितम्।
en: (Ghatotkacha), the ornaments of whose arms were falling down from rage, came up to the son of Drona who consuming the Pandava army like a raging forest-fire and fearlessly

sn: घटोत्कच उवाच तिष्ठ तिष्ठ न मे जीवन् द्रोणपुत्र गमिष्यसि॥ त्वामद्य निहनिष्यामि क्रौञ्चमग्निसुतो यथा।
en: Ghatotkacha said O son of Drona, 'wait, wait.' You will not escape alive from me. I will today destroy you as the son of Angi (i.e. Kartikeya) rived the (mountain) Krouncha.

sn: अश्वत्थामोवाच गच्छ वत्स सहान्यैस्त्वं युध्यस्वामरविक्रम॥ न हि पुत्रेण हैडिम्बे पिता न्याय्यः प्रबाधितुम्।
en: Ashvatthama said O son equal in prowess to a celestial, go and fight with others. O son of Hidimva, it is not proper for the father to fight with the son.

sn: कामं खलु न रोषो मे हैडिम्बे विद्यते त्वयि॥ किं तु रोषान्वितो जन्तुर्हन्यादात्मानमप्युता
en: O son of Hidimva, I am in no way angry with you in my mind. But when a creature is excited with rage, it may (then) kill its own self.

sn: संजय उवाच श्रुत्वैतत् क्रोधताम्राक्षः पुत्रशोकसमन्वितः॥ अश्वत्थामानमायस्तो भैमसेनिरभाषत।
en: Sanjaya said Hearing those words, the son of Bhimasena who was filled with grief for the loss of son and whose eyes became copper-coloured in rage, addressed Ashvatthama thusकिमहं कातरो द्रौणे पृथग्जन इवाहवे॥

sn: यन्मा भीषयसे वाग्भिरसदेतद् वचस्तव।
en: “What! Am I like a common individual, unable to fight, O son of Drona, that you are terrifying me with words? These words of yeurs are (highly) improper.

sn: भीमात् खलु समुत्पन्नः कुरूणां विपुले कुले॥ पाण्डवानामहं पुत्रः समरेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्।
en: I am born of Bhima in the great race of the Kurus and am the son of the Pandavas who never run away from battle.

sn: रक्षसामधिराजोऽहं दशग्रीवसमो बले॥ तिष्ठ तिष्ठ न मे जीवन् द्रोणपुत्र गमिष्यसि।
en: I am the Emperor of the Rakshasas and equal to the ten-necked (Ravana) in prowess. O son of Drona, wait, wait, you will never escape alive from me.

sn: युद्धश्रद्धामहं तेऽद्य विनेष्यामि रणाजिरे॥ इत्युक्तवा क्रोधताम्राक्षो राक्षसः सुमहाबलः।
en: I will, today, put an end to your desire for fight on the field of battie.” Saying thus, that highly powerful Rakshasas, with eyes (red) as copper in wrath.

sn: द्रौणिमभ्यद्रवत् क्रुद्धो गजेन्द्रमिव केसरी॥ रथाक्षमात्रैरिषुभिरभ्यवर्षद् घटोत्कचः।
en: Rushed furiously against the son of Drona as a lion (rushes against) the king of elephants. (Then) Ghatotkacha began to discharge showers of arrows of the measure of the Aksha of a car.

sn: रथिनामृषभं द्रौणिं धाराभिरिव तोयदः॥ शरवृष्टिं शरैौणिरप्राप्तां तां व्यशातयत्।
en: At that foremost of car-warriors, the son of Drona, as a cloud (sends down) showers of rain. (But) the son of Drona allayed that down pour of arrows by means of his (own) shafts, before they could reach him.

sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षे बाणानां संग्रामोऽन्य इवाभवत्॥ अथास्त्रसम्मर्दकृतैर्विस्फुलिङ्गगैस्तदा बभौ।
en: It, then, seemed, that another fight was raging in the firmament between the arrows. In consequence of the sparks emitted forth by the clash of weapons, it seemed.

sn: विभावरीमुखे व्योम खद्योतैरिव चित्रितम्॥ निशाम्य निहतां मायां द्रौणिना रणमानिना।
en: That the firmament was studded with glowworms during the night. Beholding his illusion destroyed by the son of Drona, proud (of his prowess) in battle.

sn: घटोत्कचस्ततो मायां ससर्जान्तर्हितः पुनः॥ सोऽभवद् गिरिरत्युचः शिखरैस्तरुसंकटैः।
en: Ghatotkacha then disappeared from view again and created (another) illusion (by virtue of this new illusion); he assumed the shape of a towering mountain abounding with peaks and trees.

sn: शूलप्रासासिमुसलजलप्रस्रवणो महान्॥ तमञ्जनगिरिप्रख्यं द्रौणिदृष्ट्वा महीधरम्।
en: And having a great fountain of water from which spears, lances, swords and heavy clubs, flowed incessantly. The son of Drona, beholding that mountain looking like a mass of antimony.

sn: प्रपतद्धिश्च बहुभिः शस्रसंधैर्न विव्यथे॥ ततो हसन्निव द्रौणिर्वज्रमस्रमुदैरयत्।
en: From which innumerable weapons were being rained down, was not at all afflicted. The son of Drona, then, as if with a smile, invoked into existence the weapon of Bajra.

sn: स तेनास्रेण शैलेन्द्रः क्षिप्तः क्षिप्रं व्यनश्यत॥ ततः स तोयदो भूत्वा नीलः सेन्द्रायुधो दिवि।
en: By means of that weapon he soon destroyed that prince of mountains. Then he (i.e., Ghatotkacha) wearing the shape of a blue cloud adorned with rain-bow in the firmament.

sn: अश्मवृष्टिभिरत्युग्रो द्रौणिमाच्छादयद् रणे॥ अथ संधाय वायव्यमस्रमसविदां वरः।
en: Covered the son of Drona with furious showers of stones in battle. Thereupon, aiming ihe Vayavya weapon, that foremost of those skilled in weapons (viz.,)

sn: व्यथमद् द्रोणतनयो नीलमेघं समुत्थितम्॥ स मार्गणगणैौणिर्दिशः प्रच्छाद्य सर्वशः।
en: The son Drona destroyed that rising blue cloud covering all points completely with numerous arrows, the son of Drona.

sn: शतं रथसहस्राणां जघान द्विपदां वरः॥ स दृष्ट्वा पुनरायान्तं रथेनायातकार्मुकम्। घटोत्कचमसम्भ्रान्तं राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृतम्॥ सिंहशार्दूलसदृशैर्मत्तद्विरदविक्रमैः
en: That foremost of two-legged creatures. destroyed one hundred thousand cars. He (then) saw Ghatotkach come again fearlessly on a car bending his bow and surrounded by a host of Rakshasas, resembling (in shape) lions and tigers, endued with the prowess of infuriated elephants.

sn: गजस्थैश्च रथस्थैश्च वाजिपृष्ठगतैरपि॥ विकृतास्यशिरोग्रीवैर्हिडिम्बानुचरैः सह।
en: Riding on elephants, cars and horses and possessed of unnatural, faces head and necks. Those followers of the son of Hidimva.

sn: पौलस्त्यैर्यातुधानैश्च तामसैश्चेन्द्रविक्रमैः॥ नानाशस्त्रधरैवीरैर्नानाकवचभूषणैः
en: Belonged to Pulasta and Yatudhana clans and like them, were (all) equal to Indra in prowess. (These Rakshasa) heroes wielded several (sorts of) armours.

sn: महाबलैर्भीमरवैः संरम्भोवृत्तलोचनैः॥ उपस्थितैस्ततो युद्धे राक्षसैयुद्धदुर्मदैः।
en: Were dreadful to look at, excited with wrath and their eyes were rolling in ire. Accompanied by those Rakshasas difficult of being vanquished. (Ghatotkacha) appeared on the field of battle.

sn: विषण्णमभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य पुत्रं ते द्रौणिरब्रवीत्॥ तिष्ठ दुर्योधनाद्य त्वं न कार्य; सम्भ्रमस्त्वया।
en: Seeing that your son grew (greatly) dispirited (at the sight of these Rakshasas; the son of Drona thus addressed him. "O Duryodhana, wait. You need not entertain any fear (of the Rakshasas).

sn: सहैभिर्धातृभिर्वीरैः पार्थिवैश्चेन्द्रविक्रमैः॥ निहनिष्याम्यमित्रांस्ते न तवास्ति पराजयः। सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि पर्याश्वासय वाहिनीम्॥
en: (Remain here) with your heroic brothers and with the kings equal in prowess to Indra himself. I will destroy your enemies. You will not meet with reverse; I tell you (this) truly. Now cheer up (your) army.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच न त्वेतदद्भुतं मन्ये यत् ते महदिदं मनः। अस्मासु च परा भक्तिस्तव गौतमिनन्दन॥
en: Duryodhana said I do not deem it (i.e., what you say) wonderful because you have a large mind and (because), O son of Goutama's daughter, you are devotedly attached to us.

sn: संजय उवाच अश्वत्थामानमुक्त्वैवं ततः सौबलमब्रवीत्। वृतं रथसहस्रेण हयानां रणशोभिनाम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus addressing Ashvatthama, he then said to the son of Subala-"(Arjuna) is surrounded by one hundred thousand cars, adorning the (field of) battle.

sn: षष्ट्या रथसहस्रैश्च प्रयाहि त्वं धनंजयम्। कर्णश्च वृषसेनश्च कृपो नीलस्तथैव च॥
en: Do you mark against Dhananjaya with one thousand cars, Karna, Vrisasena, Kripa as well as Nila. as

sn: उदीच्याः कृतवर्मा च पुरुमित्रः सुतापनः। दुःशासनो निकुम्भश्च कुण्डभेदी पराक्रमः॥
en: And the warriors of the North, Kritavarma, the sons of Purumitra, Dusasana, Nikumva, Kundavedi, Purukrama.

sn: पुरंजयो दृढरथः पताकी हेमकम्पनः। शल्यारुणीन्द्रसेनाश्च संजयो विजयो जयः॥
en: And Puranjaya, Dridaratha, Pataki, Hemapusyaka, Shalya, Aruni, Indrasena, Sanjaya, Vijaya, Jaya.

sn: कमलाक्षः परक्राथी जयवर्मा सुदर्शनः। एते त्वामनुयास्यन्ति पत्तीनामयुतानि षट्॥
en: And Kamalaksha, Parakrathi, Jayadharma, Sudarsana-(all) these will follow you together with sixty thousand infantry.

sn: जहि भीमं यमौ चोभौ धर्मराजं च मातुल। असुरानिव देवेन्द्रो जयाशा मे त्वयि स्थिता॥
en: Destroy, O uncle, Bhima, the twins (i.e., Nakula and Sahadeva) as well the Dharmaraj, as the Asuras. My hope of success lies in you.

sn: दारितान् द्रौणिनां बाणैर्भृशं विक्षतविग्रहान्। जहि मातुल कौन्तेयानसुरानिव पावकिः॥
en: (They) are already deeply wounded, their bodies are mangled with shafts by the son of Drona. O uncle, (now) destroy the sons of Kunti, as the son of Agni (i.e., Kartikeya) slew the Asuras.

sn: एवमुक्तौ ययौ शीघ्रं पुत्रेण तव सौबलः। पिप्रीषुस्ते सुतान् राजन् दिधक्षुश्चैव पाण्डवान्॥
en: Thus spoken to by your son, the son of Subala, desirous of doing your son good, marched quickly, O king, for the purpose of destroying the Pandavas.

sn: अथ प्रववृते युद्धं द्रौणिराक्षसयोर्मधे। विभावर्यां सुतुमलं शक्रप्रह्लादयोरिव॥
en: Then commenced on that night a dreadful encounter between the son of Drona and the Rakshasas (Ghatotkacha) like that (which had taken place in days of yore) between Shakra and Prahrada.

sn: ततो घटोत्कचो बाणैर्दशभिर्गौतमीसुतम्। जघानोरसि संक्रुद्धो विषाग्निप्रतिमैदृद्वैः॥
en: Then Ghatatkacha, excited with, anger struck the son of the daughter of Goutama on the chest with ten strong arrows (fierce) like the venom or the fire.

sn: स तैरभ्याहतो गाढं शरैर्भीमसुतेरितैः। चचाल रथमध्यस्थो वातोद्धत इव दुमः॥
en: Deeply wounded by those arrows sent by the son of Bhima, he (i.e., Ashvatthama), like a tree shaken by the tempest trembled on the terrace of his car.

sn: भूयश्चाञ्जलिकेनाथ मार्गणेन महाप्रभम्। द्रौणिहस्तस्थितं चापं चिच्छेदाशु घटोत्कचः॥
en: Again by means of a broad-headed shaft, Ghatotkacha soon cut-off that highly lustrous bow wielded by the son of Drona.

sn: ततोऽन्यद् द्रौणिरादाय धनुर्भारसहं महत्। ववर्ष विशिखांस्तीक्ष्णान् वारिधारा इवाम्बुदः।।१३१
en: Then taking up another strong bow capable of sustaining a great strain, the son of Drona poured showers of keen arrows as the clouds (pour down) showers of rain.

sn: ततः शारद्वतीपुत्रः प्रेषयामास भारत। सुवर्णपुलाञ्छत्रुघ्नान् खचरान् खचरं प्रति॥
en: Then, O Bharata, the son of Saradvati sent gold winged and sky-ranging destructive of foes against that ranger of the sky.

sn: तद् बाणैरर्दितं यूथं रक्षसां पीनवक्षसाम्। सिंहैरिव बभौ मत्तं गजानामाकुलं कुलम्॥
en: That great host of the broad-chested Rakshasas, sore oppressed with his arrows, looked like a herd of furious elephants attacked) by a lion.

sn: विधम्य राक्षसान् बाणैः साश्वसूतरथद्विपान्। ददाह भगवान् वह्निर्भूतानीव युगक्षये॥
en: Like the god Agni consuming the creatures at the end of a Yoga, he began to consume with his arrows the Rakshasas together with (their) horses, charioteers, cars and elephants. arrows

sn: स दग्ध्वाक्षौहिणी बाणैर्नैर्ऋतीं रुरुचे नृप। पुरेव त्रिपुरं दग्ध्वा दिवि देवो महेश्वरः॥
en: Consuming one Akshauhini of Rakshasa troops with his shafts, he shone like the divine Maheshvara in heaven when the latter had burnt down (the chief of) Tripura in days of yore.

sn: युगान्ते सर्वभूतानि दग्ध्वेव वसुरुल्वणः। रराज जयतां श्रेष्ठो द्रोणपुत्रस्तवाहितान्॥
en: Having consumed the hostile forces, the son of Drona, the forernost of victors, shone like the resplendent Agni burning all the creatures at the end of a Yuga.

sn: ततो घटोत्कचः क्रुद्धो रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्। द्रौणिं हतेति महती चोदयामास तां चमूम्॥
en: Then Ghatotkacha, greatly enraged ordered that vast army of Rakshasas capable of achieving terrible feats, to slay the son of Drona.

sn: घटोत्कचस्य तामाज्ञां प्रतिगृह्याथ राक्षसाः। दंष्ट्रोज्ज्वला महावक्त्रा घोररूपा भयानकाः॥
en: In obedience to that order of Ghatotkacha, the Rakshasas, possessed of blazing teeth, large faces and terrible features, capable of causing dread.

sn: ध्यात्तानना घोरजिह्वाः क्रोधतानेक्षणा भृशम्। सिंहनादेन महता नादयन्तो वसुन्धराम्॥
en: Having gaping mouths, long tongues and eyes burning in ire, causing the earth to tremble with great leonine roars.

sn: हन्तुमभ्यद्रवन् द्रौणिं नानाप्रहरणायुधाः। शक्तीः शतघ्नीः परिघानशनीः शूलपट्टिशान्॥ खङ्गान् गदा भिन्दिपालान् मुसलानि परश्वघान्। प्रासानसींस्तोमरांश्च कणपान् कम्पनाञ्छितान्॥ स्थूलान् भुशुण्ड्यश्मगदाःस्थूणान् कार्णायसांस्तथा। मुद्रांश्च महाघोरान् समरे शत्रुदारणान्॥
en: And wielding several (sorts of) weapons rushed to slay the son of Drona. These Rakshasas, of gigantic strength and with eyes reddened with wrath, began to shower upon the head of the son of Drona hundreds and thousands of awfully terrible darts, Sataghness, spiked maces, Asanis, lances, axes, scimitars, maces, Bhindipalas, heavy clubs, battle axes, spears, swords, lances, Kunapas, polished Kampanas, sthulas, Bhushundees, stones. vessels of treacle, sthunas made of black iron and clubs (all) destructive of foes.

sn: द्रौणिमूर्धन्यसंत्रस्ता राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः। चिक्षिपुः क्रोधताम्राक्षाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ तच्छस्रवर्षं सुमहद् द्रोणपुत्रस्य मूर्धनि। पतमानं समीक्ष्याथ योधास्ते व्यथिताभवन्॥
en: Seeing that dreadful shower of weapons was falling upon the head of the son of Drona your warriors were greatly distressed (at heart).

sn: द्रोणपुत्रस्तु विक्रान्तस्तद् वर्ष घोरमुच्छ्रितम्। शरैर्विध्वंसयामास वज्रकल्पैः शिलाशितैः॥
en: (But) Drona's son dauntlessly baffled that dreadful and impending shower of weapons by means of his own shafts, hard as the thunderbolt and sharpened on stones.

sn: ततोऽन्यैर्विशिखैस्तूर्णं स्वर्णपुखैर्महामनाः। निजघ्ने राक्षसान् द्रौणिर्दिव्यास्त्रप्रतिमन्त्रितैः॥
en: Then that high-minded son, of Drona, quickly destroyed the Rakshasas with other gold winged shafts inspired with the mantras of celestial weapons.

sn: तद्बाणैरर्दितं यूथं राक्षसां पीनवक्षसाम्। सिंहैरिव बभौ मत्तं गजानामाकुलं कुलम्॥
en: The broad chested Rakshasa army, crushed by his arrows, looked like a herd of furious elephants oppressed by lions.

sn: ते राक्षसाः सुसंक्रुद्धा द्रोणपुत्रेण ताडिताः। क्रुद्धाः स्म प्राद्रवन् द्रौणिं जिघांसन्तो महाबलाः॥१४८
en: Sore oppressed by the son of Drona those Rakshasas, endued with enormous strength, became mad with rage and angrily rushed against Drona's son in order to slay him.

sn: तत्राद्भुतमिमं द्रौणिर्दर्शयामास विक्रमम्। अशक्यं कर्तुमन्येन सर्वभूतेषु भारत॥
en: There, 0 Bharata, the son of Drona displayed such wonderful exploits as are incapable of being achieved by any other being among all the creatures.

sn: यदेको राक्षसी सेनां क्षणाद् द्रौणिर्महास्रवित्। ददाह ज्वलितैर्बाणै राक्षसेन्द्रस्य पश्यतः॥
en: In as much as single-handed the son of Drona, versed in great weapons, by means of blazing darts, burnt that Rakshasa ariny in a moment in the very presence of the Rakshasa king.

sn: स हत्वा राक्षसानीकं रराज द्रौणिराहवे। युगान्ते सर्वभूतानि संवर्तक इवानलः॥
en: The son of Drona, while (thus burning that Rakshasa host in battle shone like the Samvartaka fire (consuming) all the creatures at the end of a Yuga.

sn: तं दहन्तमनीकानि शरैराशीविषोपमैः। तेषु राजसहस्रेषु पाण्डवेयेषु भारत॥
en: While engaged in consuming the forces with arrows (fierce) as poisonous snakes, among those thousands of kings on the side of the Pandavas, OBharata.

sn: नैनं निरीक्षितुं कश्चिदशक्नोद् द्रौणिमाहवे। ऋते घटोत्कचाद् वीराद् राक्षसेन्द्रान्महाबलात्॥
en: None else could look at the son of Drona in that encounter except Ghatotkacha, the heroic and highly powerful king of the Rakshasas.

sn: स पुनर्भरतश्रेष्ठ क्रोधादुद्भान्तलोचनः। तलं तलेन संहत्य संदश्य दशनच्छदम्॥
en: O best of the Bharatas, again he (i.e., Ghatotkacha), with eyes rolling in rage, striking his palms and biting his lip.

sn: स्वं सूतमब्रवीत् क्रुद्धो द्रोणपुत्राय मां वह। स ययौ घोररुपेण सुपताकेन भास्वता॥ द्वैरथं द्रोणपुत्रेण पुनरष्यरिसूदनः। स विनद्य महानादं सिंहवद् भीमविक्रमः॥ चिक्षेपाविध्य संग्रामे द्रोणपुत्राय राक्षसः। अष्टघण्टां महाघोरामशनि देवनिर्मिताम्॥
en: Said angrily to his charioteer “Bear me towards the son of Drona.” Ascending that terrible looking (car) furnished with triumphal banners, that destroyer foes again marched against the son of Drona in order to engage in a single combat with him. Sending forth a thundering roar like that of a lion, that terriblypowerful Rakshasa, whirling a highly dreadful Asani of celestial make and furnished with eight bells, hurled it in that encounter at the son of Drona.

sn: तामवप्लुत्य जग्राह द्रौणिय॑स्य रथे धनुः। चिक्षेप चैनां तस्यैव स्यन्दनात् सोऽवपुप्लवे॥
en: Placing his bow on the car and jumping down, the son of Drona seized it and hurled it back at him (i.e. the Rakshasa, (Seeing that Asani proceed towards him) he leaped down from his car.

sn: साश्वसूतध्वजं यानं भस्म कृत्वा महाप्रभा। विवेश वसुधां भित्त्वा साशनिर्भृशदारुणा॥
en: That dreadful Asani of great luster having consumed to ashes the car together with the steeds, the driver and the standard, rived the earth and (then) penetrated into it.

sn: द्रौणेस्तत् कर्म दृष्ट्वा तु सर्वभूतान्यपूजयन्। यदवप्लत्य जग्राह घोरां शङ्करनिर्मिताम्॥
en: Seeing the son of Drona achieve that (wonderful) feat all the creatures adored (him) inasmuch as leaping down from his car he seized that (Asani) made by Sankara.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नरथं गत्वा भैमसेनिस्ततो मृप। धनुर्घोरं समादाय महदिन्द्रायुधोपमम्।
en: Then, O king, riding on the car of Dhritarashtra and taking up a dreadful bow like the formidable bow of Indra (himself), the son of Bhimasena.

sn: मुमोच निशितान् बाणान् पुनौणेर्महोरसि॥ मुमोचाशीविषोपमान्।
en: Began again to discharge sharpened arrows at the high-soulcd of Drona. Dhristadyumna also, nothing daunted, discharged (arrows) fierce as poisonous snakes.

sn: सुवर्णपुङ्खान् विशिखान् द्रोणपुत्रस्य वक्षसि॥ ततो मुमाच नाराचान् द्रौणिस्तांश्च सहस्रशः।
en: Furnished with gold wings and excellent at the chest of the son of Drona. Thereupon

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्त्वसम्भ्रान्तो
en: Drona's son hurled at them thousands of Narachas.

sn: तावप्यग्निशिखप्रख्यैर्जघ्नतुस्तस्य मार्गणान्॥ अतितीव्र महद् युद्धं तयोः पुरुषपिहयोः।
en: (But) those two (i.e., Dhristadyumna and the Rakshasa) cut-off with their own shafts, having the touch of fire, the arrows discharged by Drona's son). (Then an awfully terrible battle took place between those two best of men.

sn: योधानां प्रीतिजननं द्रौणेश्च भरतर्षभ॥ ततो रथसहस्रेण द्विरदानां शतैत्रिभिः।
en: And the son of Drona caused a great delight to the warriors, O best of the Bharatas. Then followed by one thousand cars, three hundred elephants.

sn: षड्भिर्वाजिसहस्रश्च भीमस्तं देशमागमत्॥ ततो भीमात्मजं रक्षो धृष्टद्युम्नं च सानुगम्। अयोधयत धर्मात्मा द्रौणिरक्लिष्टविक्रमः॥ तत्राद्भुततमं द्रौणिर्दर्शयामास विक्रमम्।
en: And six thousand steeds Bhimasena made his appearance at that spot (where the battle was raging). But the virtuous-souled son of Drona, possessed of excellent prowess, continued to fight with the heroic son of Bhimasena and Dhristadyumna together with his younger brothers; there the son of Drona achieved the most marvellous exploit.

sn: अशक्यं कर्तुमन्येन सर्वभूतेषु भारत॥ निमेषान्तरमात्रेण साश्वसूतरथद्विपाम्। अक्षौहिणी राक्षसानां शितैर्बाणैरशातयत्॥ मिषतो भीमसेनस्य हैडिम्बेः पार्षतस्य च।
