en: Incapable of being performed by any one among all the creatures. O Bharata, within the twinkling of an eyes, he destroyed by means of arrows one Akshauhini of the Rakshasa army together with horses, drivers, cars and elephants, in the very sight of Bhimasena, the son of Hidimva, the son of Prishatha.

sn: यमयोधर्मपुत्रस्य विजयस्याच्युतस्य च॥ प्रगाढमञ्जोगतिभिर्नाराचैरभिताडिताः।
en: The twins, the son of Dharma, Vijaya and Achyuta. Pierced deeply with the strightcoursing shafts.

sn: निपेतुर्द्विरदा भूमौ सशृङ्गा इव पर्वताः॥ निकृत्तैर्हस्तिहस्तैश्च विचलद्भिरितस्ततः।
en: The tuskers fell down on earth like mountains devoid of (their) peaks with the trunks of elephants chopped off (by arrows) that were still moving about here and there.

sn: रराज वसुधा कीर्णा विसर्पद्भिरिवोरगैः॥ क्षिप्तैः काञ्चनदण्डैश्च नृपच्छत्रैः क्षितिर्बभौ।
en: The earth being strewn it looked as beautiful as if strewn around with moving snakes; with golden staves cut (to pieces) and royal umbrellas (lying scattered all over the field of battle) the earth looked like.

sn: द्यौरिवोदितचन्द्रार्का ग्रहाकीर्णा युगक्षये॥ प्रवृद्धध्वजमण्डूकां भेरीविस्तीर्णकच्छपाम्।
en: The firmament studded with (many) suns, moons and planets at the end of a Yuga. Tell standards constituted the frogs, drums the large tortoises.

sn: छत्रहंसावलीजुष्टां फेनचामरमालिनीम्॥ कङ्कगृध्रमहाग्राहां नैकायुधझषाकुलाम्।
en: Huge elephants the stones, elephants and horses the sharks, cars the unstable and great banks, flags the beautiful trees.

sn: विस्तीर्णगजपाषाणां हताश्वमकराकुलाम्॥ रक्षक्षिप्तमहावप्रां पताकारुचिरदुमाम्।
en: Arrows the fishes, lances, darts and swords the frightful snakes, marrow and flesh the deep mire, headless bodies, the ratters;

sn: शरमीनां महारौद्रां प्रासशक्त्यष्टिडुण्डुभाम्॥ मजामांसमहापां कबन्धावर्जितोडुपाम्। केशशैवलकल्माषां भीरूणां कश्मलावहाम्॥ नागेन्द्रहययोधानां शरीरव्ययसम्भवाम्।
en: Profusion of hair (of men and animals) the moss, lamentations of warriors the roar and blood flowing from the wounds formed the waves of that impetuous river of blood formed numerous by the blood shedding from the bodies of huge elephants, horses and combatants and inspiring the coward with terror-which the son of Drona caused to flow there.

sn: शोणितीयमहाघोरां द्रौणिः प्रावर्तयन्नदीम्॥ योधार्तरवनि?षां क्षतजोर्मिसमाकुलाम्। श्वापदातिमहाघोरां यमराष्ट्रमहोदधिम्॥ निहत्य राक्षसान् बाणैौणिहँडिम्बिमार्दयत्।
en: (It looked) frightful with the (dead) bodies of foot soldiers and (it flowed towards) that great ocean, that is, the abode of Yama. Having destroyed the Rakshasa the son of Hidimva with shafts.

sn: पुनरप्यतिसंक्रुद्धः सवृकोदरपार्षतान्॥ स नाराच गणैः पार्थान् द्रौणिर्विद्ध्वा महाबलः।
en: Waxing worth again, Drona's son having pierced with numerous shafts those great carwarriors, the of Pritha including Vrikodara and the son of Prishata.

sn: जघान सुरथं नाम द्रुपदस्य सुतं विभुः॥ पुनः शत्रुजयं नाम द्रुपदस्यात्मजं रणे। बलानीकं जयानीकं जयाश्वं चाभिजनिवान्॥
en: Killed, O Lord, one of the sons of Drupada, Suratha by name. Then in that encounter he killed the younger brother of Suratha, Satrunjaya by name and also Balmika, Jayanika and Jaya. Then again, roaring like a lion, the son of Drona, by means of sharpened sons arrows.

sn: श्रुताह्वयं च राजानं द्रौणिनिन्ये यमक्षयम्। त्रिभिश्चान्यैः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः सुपुजैर्हेममालिनम्॥ जधान स पृषघ्रं च चन्द्रसेनं च मारिष। कुन्तिभोजसुतांश्चासौ दशभिर्दश जनिवान्॥ अश्वत्थामा सुसंक्रुद्धः संधायोग्रमजिह्मगम्। मुमोचाकर्णपूर्णेन धनुषा शरमुत्तमम्॥ यमदण्डोपमं घोरमुद्दिश्याशु घटोत्कचम्।
en: Slew Prishadhru and the proud Chandrasena. (Then) with ten (darts) he destroyed ten sons of Kuntibhoja with another three red-eyed arrow graced with beautiful wings he dispatched O king of kings, to the abode of Yama, Shtrutayush. (He then) sent the powerful Satrunjaya to the abode of Shakra. Ashvatthama, then, greatly enraged, fixed a terrible and uncrooked (arrows) (on his bowstring). (And) drawing the string up to his very ear, he soon discharged from his bow that excellent and formidable (arrow) looking like Yamadanda at Ghatotkacha.

sn: स भित्त्वा हृदयं तस्य राक्षसस्य महाशरः॥ विवेश वसुधां शीघ्रं सुपुङ्खः पृथिवीपते।
en: O Lord of earth, that great arrow furnished with beautiful wings, riving the heart of that Rakshasa, penetrated into the earth.

sn: तं हतं पतितं ज्ञात्वा धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः॥ द्रौणेः सकाशाद् राजेन्द्र व्यपनिन्ये रथोत्तमम्।
en: Seeing him fallen down and taking him for dead, the great car-warrior Dhristadyumna. placed him upon another car and bore him away from the presence of the son of Drona, O king kings.

sn: ततः पराङ्मुखनृपं सैन्यं यौधिष्ठिरं नृप॥ पराजित्य रणे वीरो द्रोणपुत्रो ननाद ह। पूजितः सर्वभूतेषु तव पुत्रैश्च भारत॥
en: Thus the car-warriors of Yudhishthira were driven back O king. Vanquishing his enemies, the heroic son of Drona uttered thundering shouts and he was adored by all men and by your sons, O lord.

sn: हतपतितैः क्षणदाचरैः समन्तात्। निधनमुपगतैर्मही कृताभूद् गिरिशिखरैरिव दुर्गमातिरौद्र॥
en: Scattered all over with the fallen bodies of the dead night-rangers struck down and mangled by hundreds of shafts, the earth looked dreadful and became impassable as if strewn with mountain-peaks.

sn: तं सिद्धगन्धर्वपिशाचसंघा नागाः सुपर्णाः पितरो वयांसि। मपूजयन्नप्सरसः सुराश्च॥
en: Then the Siddhas, the Gandharvas, the Pishachas, the Nagas, the birds, the Pitris, ravens, the Rakshas, the ghosts, the Apsaras and the celestials all joined in adoring the son of Drona. Then the Siddhas, the Gandharvas, the Pishachas, the Nagas, the birds, the Pitris, ravens, the Rakshas, the ghosts, the Apsaras and the celestials all joined in adoring the son of Drona.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: संजय उवाच दुपदस्यात्मजान् दृष्ट्वा कुन्तिभोजसुतांस्तथा। द्रोणपुत्रेण निहतान् राक्षसांश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing that the sons of Drupada and those of Kuntibhoja as well as thousands of Rakshasas were destroyed by the son of Drona.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिरो भीमसेनो धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः। युयुधानश्च संयत्ता युद्धायैव मनो दधुः॥
en: Yudhishthira, Bhimasena, Dhristadyumna, the son of Prishata and Yuyudhana (all) united together, re-engaged their attention to battle.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: सोमदत्तः पुनः क्रुद्धो दृष्ट्वा सात्यकिमाहवे। महता शरवर्षेणच्छादयामास भारत॥
en: Growing angry again at seeing Satyaki in battle, O Bharata, Somadatta covered him with mighty discharge of arrows.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः समभवद् युद्धमतीव भयवर्धनम्। त्वदीयानां परेषां च धोरं विजयकाक्षिणाम्॥
en: Then the battle that took place between your army and that of the enemy was dreadful and highly marvellous to look at, (in which) both parties were desirous of gaining the victory.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा समुपायान्तं रुक्मपुङ्खः शिलाशितैः। दशभिः सात्वतस्यार्थे भीमो विव्याध सायकैः॥
en: Bhima, for the purpose of (helping) Sattavat, pierced the Kaurava (Somadatta) with ten (arrows). Somadatta too struck that hero in return with a hundred (darts).

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: सोमदत्तोऽपि तं वीरं शतेन प्रत्यविध्यता सात्वतस्त्वभिसंक्रुद्धः पुत्राधिभिरभिप्लुतम्॥ वृद्ध वृद्धगुणैयुक्तं ययातिमिव नाहुषम्। विव्याध दशभिस्तीक्ष्णैः शरैर्वज्रनिपातनैः॥
en: (Then) Sattavat, furious with wrath, struck that old one smitten with grief for the slaughter of his son (by Satyaki) and who was, like Yayati, the son of Nahusha, possessed of every noble quality, with ten sharpened arrows having the force of the thunder. After piercing him (with these ten arrows) with great mighty he (i.e. Sayiaki) struck him again with seven (more).

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: शक्त्या चैनं विनिर्भिद्य पुनर्विव्याध सप्तभिः। ततस्तु सात्यकेरर्थे भीमसेनो नवं दृढम्॥ मुमोच परिघं घोरं सोमदत्तस्य मूर्धनि।
en: Bhimasena, also for the purpose of (helping) Satyaki, hurled a new and formidable Parigha at the head of Somadatta.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: सात्वतोऽप्यग्निसंकाशं मुमोच शरमुत्तमम्॥ सोमदत्तोरसि क्रुद्धः सुपत्रं निशितं युधि।
en: Sattvata too, in anger, discharged at the chest of Somadatta, in that encounter, a keen and excellent dart, furnished with beautiful wings and as (furious) as the fire itself.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: युगपत् पेततुरि घोरौ परिघमार्गणौ॥ शरीरे सोमदत्तस्य स पपात महारथः।
en: Both the formidable Parigha and the arrow, having at one and the same time, fallen upon the body of the heroic Somadatta, that mighty car-warrior fell down.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: व्यामोहिते तु तनये बाह्रीकस्तमुपाद्रवत्॥ विसृजञ्छरवर्षाणि कालवर्षीव तोयदः।
en: His son being deprived of consciousness, Valhika, discharging showers of arrows like the clouds (pouring) torrents of rain during (the rainy, season), rushed at him.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: भीमोऽथ सात्वतस्यार्थे वाह्नीकं नवभिः शरैः॥ प्रपीडयन् महात्मानं विव्याण रणमूर्धनि।
en: Then Bhima, for the sake of Satyaki, tormented and pierced, in that encounter, the high-souled Balhika with nine arrows.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: प्रातिपेयस्तु संक्रुद्धः शक्तिं भीमस्य वक्षसि॥ निचखान महाबाहुः पुरंदर इवाशनिम्।
en: Like Purandara hurling the thunder bolt, the mighty arrmed son of Partha. (i.e., Valhika), smitten with ire, struck Bhima on the chest with an arrow.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: स तथाभिहतो भीमश्चकम्पे च मुमोह च॥ प्राप्य चेतश्च बलवान् गदामस्मै ससर्ज ह।
en: Thus struck (by Valhika) Bhima trembled and (then) fell into a swoon. Then that powerful one, recovering his senses, hurled a mace at him.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: सा पाण्डवेन प्रहिता बाह्रीकस्य शिरोऽहरत्॥ स पपात हतः पृथ्व्यां वज्राहत इवाद्रिराट्।
en: That (mace) hurled by the Pandava (Bhimasena) smashed the head of Valhika. He (then) fell down dead on the earth like a tree struck by lightning.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: तस्मिन् विनिहते वीरे बाह्लीके पुरुषर्षभ॥ पुत्रास्तेऽभ्यर्दयन् भीमं दश दशरथेः समाः। नागदत्तो दृढरथो महाबाहुरयोभुजः॥ दृढः सुहस्तो विरजाः प्रमाथ्युग्रोऽनुयाय्यपि।
en: That foremost of men, the heroic Valhika being (thus) slain, your ten sons, viz., Nagadatta, Dhridaratha, Viravahu, Ayobhuja, Dridha, Suhasta, Viraja, Pramatha and Ugrayayin; (each of whom) resembled the son of Dasharatha (i.e. Rama) began to torment Bhima.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा चुक्रुधे भीमो जगृहे भारसाधनान्॥ एकमेकं समुद्दिश्य पातयामास मर्मसु।
en: Filled with ire on beholding them, Bhima, aiming at each of them one after the other, struck each of them in the vital parts with arrows capable of bearing much strain.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ते विद्धा व्यसव: पेतुः स्यन्दनेभ्यो हतौजसः॥ चण्डवातप्रभग्नास्तु पर्वताग्रान्महीरुहाः।
en: Pierced (with those arrows) they fell down from their cars deprived of life and energy as trees broken by a furious hurricane (fall down) from the mountain summits.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: नाराचैर्दशभिर्भीमस्तान् निहत्य तवात्मजान्॥ कर्णस्य दयितं पुत्रं वृषसेनमवाकिरत्।
en: Having destroyed those (ten) sons of your with ten arrows Bhima covered Vrishasena, the beloved son of Karna (with downpours of shafts).

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ततो वृकरथो नाम भ्राता कर्णस्य विश्रुतः॥ जधान भीमं नाराचैस्तमप्यभ्यद्रवद् बली।
en: Then the renowned brother of Karna, Vrikaratha by name, pierced Bhima with arrows. (But) that hero (i.e., Bhima) soon slew him.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः सप्त स्थान् वीरः स्यालानां तव भारत॥ निहत्य भीमौ नाराचैः शतचन्द्रमपोथयत्।
en: Then the heroic Bhima, having killed seven car-warriors among your brothers-in-law, with arrows, buried Satachandra into the earth (by main force), O Bharata.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: अमर्षयन्तो निहतं शतचन्द्रं महारथम्॥ शकुने_तरो वीरा गवाक्षः शरभो विभुः।
en: Unable to put up with the destruction of that great car-warrior Satachandra, the brothers of Shakuni viz., the heroic Gavaksha, Sarava, Vibhu (and two others).

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: सुभगो भानुदत्तश्च शूराः पञ्च महारथाः॥ अभिद्रुत्य शरैस्तीक्षणैर्भीमसेनमताडयन्।
en: Rushing against Bhimasena, oppressed him with keen darts. Afflicted with those shafts like a mountain with torrents of rain, he.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: स ताड्यमानो नाराचैर्वृष्टिवेगैरिवाचलः॥ जघान पञ्चभिर्बाणैः पञ्चैवातिरथान् बली।
en: Destroyed those five kings endued with great prowess, with five arrows. Those foremost of kings (who were present in that battle) seeing the destruction of those five heroes began to waver.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा निहतान् वीरान् विचेलुनृपसत्तमाः॥ ततो युधिष्ठिरः क्रुद्धस्तवानीकमशातयत्। मिषत: कुम्भयोनेस्तु पुत्राणां तव चानघ॥
en: Then Yudhishthira began angrily to crush borm (Drona) and in that of your sons, O sinless one.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: अम्बष्ठान् मालवाञ्छूरांस्रिगर्तान् स शिबीनापि। प्राहिणोन्मृत्युलोकाय क्रुद्धो युद्धे युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: (And) in that battle Yudhishthira sent to the region of Death, the Ambhastas, the Malavas, the heroic Trigartas and the Sivis.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: अभीषाहाञ्छूरसेनान् बाह्रीकान् सवसातिकान्। निकृत्य पृथिवीं राजा चक्रे शोणितकर्दमाम्॥
en: Chopping off the Abhishahas, the Surasenas, the Valhikas and the Vashatikas, he made the earth muddy with (their) flesh and blood.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: यौधेयान् मालवान् राजन् मद्रकाणां गणान् युधि। प्राहिणोन्मृत्युलोकाय शूरान् बाणैर्युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: (And), O king, in a moment he sent to the region of Yama, with a number of darts, the heroic Youdheyas, the Malavas and hosts of the Madrakas in battle.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: हताहरत गृह्णीत विध्यत व्यवकृन्तत। इत्यासीत् तुमुलः शब्दो युधिष्ठिररथं प्रति॥
en: Then a tumultuous uproar (such as) “Slay, seize, capture, pierce and cut to pieces”-arose in the direction of Yudhishthira's car.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: सैन्यानि द्रावयन्तं तं द्रोणो दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरम्। चोदितस्तव पुत्रेण सायकैरभ्यवाकिरत्॥
en: Seeing Yudhishthira afflict your troops Drona, urged on by your son surrounded him (i.e. Yudhishthira) with arrows.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: द्रोणस्तु परमक्रुद्धो वायव्यास्रेण पार्थिवम्। विव्याध सोऽपि तद् दिव्यमस्रमस्रेण जनिवान्॥
en: Drona also, exceedingly enraged, discharged at that Pandava the weapon presided over by Vayu. over by Vayu. But he (i.e., Yudhishthira) destroyed that celestial weapon with (another) weapon.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: तस्मिन् विनिहते चास्रे भारद्वाजो युधिष्ठिरे। वारुणं याम्यमाग्नेयं त्वाष्ट्र सावित्रमेव च॥ चिक्षेप परमाद्धो जिघांसुः पाण्डुनन्दनम्। क्षिप्तानि क्षिप्यमाणानि तानि चास्त्राणि धर्मजः॥ जघानास्त्रैर्महाबाहुः कुम्भयोनेरवित्रसन्। सत्यां चिकीर्षमाणस्तु प्रतिज्ञां कुम्भसम्भवः॥
en: That weapon being baffled by Yudhishthira, the son of Bharadvaja, in great rage, hurled at the Pandu the Varuna and Agneya,. The Teshra and the Savitra weapon, with desire of destroying him. All those weapons that were (either) hurled (or) being hurled by the Pot-born, were dauntlessly baffled by that mighty-armed and righteous one. Desirous of accomplishing his vow the Pat-born.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: प्रादुश्चक्रेऽस्रमैन्द्रं वै प्राजापत्यं च भारत। जिघांसुर्धर्ततनयं तव पुत्रहिते रतः॥
en: Devoted to the welfare of your son, called into existence the weapons presided over by Varuna or Prajapati, in order to slay the son of Dharma, O Bharata.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: पतिः कुरूणां गजसिंहगामी विशालवक्षाः पृथुलोहिताक्षः। प्रादुचकारास्रमहीनतेजा। माहेन्द्रमन्यत् स जघान तेन॥
en: (Then) the lord of the Kurus (i.e. Yudhishthira) walking like a lion or elephant endued with a broad chest and large red eyes and possessed of an energy not less (then that of Drona) called into existence the Mahendra weapon, by means of which he baffled the weapon of Drona.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: विहन्यमानेष्वस्त्रेषु द्रोणः क्रोधसमन्वितः। युधिष्ठिरवधं प्रेप्सुाह्यमस्रमुदैरयत्॥
en: All those weapons of his being baffled, Drona was filled with ire; and desirous of slaying Yudhishthira, he called into existence the weapon presided over by Brahma.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ततो नाज्ञासिषं किंचिद् घोरेण तमसाऽऽवृते। सर्वभूतानि च परं त्रासं जग्मुर्महीपते॥
en: Being enveloped in a dismal darkness, we could not, then, discern anything. And, O lord of the earth, all the creatures experienced a terrible horror.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ब्रह्मास्रमुद्यतं दृष्ट्वा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। ब्रह्मास्रेणैव राजेन्द्र तदत्रं प्रत्यवारयत्॥
en: Seeing that the Brahma weapon was uplifted, Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, baffled that weapon by means of Brahma weapon, O king of kings.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः सैनिकमुख्यास्ते प्रशशंसुर्नरर्षभौ। द्रोणपार्थो महेष्वासौ सर्वयुद्धविशारदौ॥
en: Then the principal warriors (of the two armies) praised those two most exalted of men, those two great bowmen, viz., Drona and the son of Pritha, who were conversant with all the (arts of) warfare.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः प्रमुच्य कौन्तेयं द्रोणो दुपदवाहिनीम्। व्यधमत् क्रोधताम्राक्षो वायव्यास्रेण भारत॥
en: Leaving the son of Kunti, Drona, then, whose eyes became as red as copper in rage, began to destroy, by means of weapons, the army of Drupada.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ते हन्यमाना द्रोणेन पञ्चालाः प्राद्रवन् भयात्। पश्यतो भीमसेनस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: The Panchalas, (thus) destroyed by Drona fled away in terror in the very presence of Bhimasena and in that of the high-souled Pritha.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः किरीटी भीमश्च सहसा संन्यवर्तताम्। महद्भयां रथवंशाभ्यां परिगृह्य बलं तदा॥
en: Then Kiriti and Bhima, rallying their own ariny, all on a sudden attacked, with a great car-force, your army.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: बीभत्सुदक्षिणं पार्श्वमुत्तरं च वृकोदरः। भारद्वाजं शरौघाभ्यां महद्भयामभ्यवर्षताम्॥
en: Vibhatsu attacking the right and Vrikodara the left flank (of your army), discharged at the son of Bharadvaja mighty downpours of shafts.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: केकयाः सृञ्जयाश्चैव पञ्चालाश्च महौजसः। अन्वगच्छन् महाराज मत्स्याश्च सह सात्वतैः॥
en: The Kakeyas, the Srinjayas and the highly energetic Panchalas, O great king, together with the Matsyas and the Sattvata followed suit.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः सा भारती सेवा वध्यमाना किरीटिना। तमसा निद्रया चैव पुनरेव व्यदीर्यत॥
en: Then the Bharata army, butchered by Kiriti and (overpowered) with sleep and darkness, dispersed again.

description: The battle between Drona and Yudhishthira
sn: द्रोणेन वार्यमाणास्ते स्वयं तव सुतेन च। नाशक्यन्त महाराज योधा वारयितुं तदा॥
en: Although, O great king, Drona himself and your son tried to rally them, yet they were not capable of reducing the warriors to order.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: संजय उवाच उदीर्यमाणं तद् दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवानां महद् बलम्। अविषह्यं च मन्वानः कर्णं दुर्योधनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Duryodhana, on beholding the vast army of the Pandavas-inflated with wrath and thinking it to be irresistible thus spoke to Karna.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: अयं स कालः सम्प्राप्तो मित्राणां मित्रवत्सल। त्रायस्व समरे कर्ण सर्वान् योधान् महारथान्॥
en: The time is now, O you that are devoted to your friends (to seek your assistance). O Karna, save in battle all my soldiers and car warriors.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: पञ्चालैर्मत्स्यकैकेयैः पाण्डवैश्च महारथैः। वृतान् समन्तात् संक्रुद्धैनिः श्वसद्भिरिवोरगैः॥
en: Who are not completely hemmed in by the wrathful Panchalas and the Keykeas and the Matsyas and by the mighty car-warriors of the Pandavas who are all listening like (angry) snakes.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: एते नदन्ति संहृष्टाः पाण्डवा जितकाशिनः। शक्रोपमाश्च बहवः पञ्चालानां स्थव्रजाः॥
en: These Pandavas, filled with ecstasy and desirous of victory and these numerous carwarriors of the Panchalas equal to Shakra in prowess, are (all) roaring.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: कर्ण उवाच परित्रातुमिह प्राप्तो यदि पार्थं पुरंदरः। तमप्याशु पराजित्य ततो हन्तास्मि पाण्डवम्॥
en: Karna said Even if Purandara himself comes here in person in order to deliver the son of Pritha, I will soon vanquish him and then slay the son of Pandu (i.e. Arjuna).

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि समाश्वसिहि भारत। हन्तास्मि पाडुतनयान् पञ्चालांश्च समागतान्॥
en: I swear this truly. Reassure your-self O Bharata. I will destroy the sons of Pandu together with all the assembled Panchalas.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: जयं ते प्रतिदास्यामि वासवस्येव पावकिः। प्रियं तव मया कार्यमिति जीवामि पार्थिव॥
en: I will secure to you victory as the son of Pavaka (i.e., Kartikeya) did to Vasava himself. In this battle which is now going on, I will do good offices to you.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: सर्वेषामेव पार्थानां फाल्गुनो बलवत्तरः। तस्यामोघां विमोक्ष्यामि शक्तिं शक्रविनिर्मिताम्॥
en: Among all the sons of Pritha. Phalguna is the most powerful. I will hurl at him the unfailing dart made by Shakra.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: तस्मिन् हते महेष्वासे भ्रातरस्तस्य मानद। तव वश्या भविष्यन्ति वनं यास्यन्ति वा पुनः॥
en: When the mighty-bowman will be slain, his brothers, O bestower of honours, will either come under your away or depart to the forest again.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: मयि जीवति कौरव्य विषादं मा कृथाः क्वचित्। अहं जेष्यामि समरे सहितान् सर्वपाण्डवान्॥
en: O lord of the Kauravas, since I am alive you need not give way to sorrow. I will, in battle, destroy all the Pandavas joined together.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: पञ्चालान् केकयांश्चैव वृष्णींश्चापि समागतान्। बाणौधैः शकलीकृत्य तव दास्यामि मेदिनीम्॥
en: The Panchalas, the Keykayas and the assembled Vrishnis. (And) cutting (them) off into pieces with arrows I will give the earth to you.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: संजय उवाच एवं ब्रुवाणं कण तु कृपः शारद्वतोऽब्रवीत्। स्मयन्निव महाबाहुः सूतपुत्रमिदं वचः॥
en: Sanjaya said When Karna was saying all this the mightyarmed Kripa, the son of Saradvata smilingly said these words to the charioteer's son.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: शोभनं शोभनं कर्ण सनाथः कुरुपुङ्गवः। त्वया नाथेन राधेय वचसा यदि सिध्यति॥
en: "Very well very well, O Karna. If words alone were to lead to success, then 0 son of Radha, with yourself as his supporter, this most exalted of the Kuru could be considered as sufficiently backed.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: बहुशः कत्थसे कर्ण कौरवस्य समीपतः। न तु ते विक्रमः कश्चिद् दृश्यते फलमेव वा॥
en: Frequently in the presence of the Kaurava (king) you boast (of your prowess). But neither your prowess nor the result of it has ever been witnessed.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: समागमः पाण्डुसुतैदृष्टस्ते बहुशो युधि। सर्वत्र निर्जितश्चासि पाण्डवैः सूतनन्दन॥
en: You have been, on several occasions, seen to engage in battle with the sons of Pandu. But, charioteer's son, you have, on all those occasions, been defeated by the Pandavas.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: ह्रियमाणे तदा कर्ण गन्धर्वैधृतराष्टजे। तदायुध्यन्त सैन्यानि त्वमेकोऽग्रेऽपलायिथाः॥
en: On the son of Dhritarashtra being taken prisoner by the Gandharvas, you yourself were the first to take to your heels although all the troops were fighting (to rescue the Kuru king).

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: विराटनगरे चापि समेताः सर्वकौरवाः। पार्थेन निर्जिता युद्धे त्वं च कर्ण सहानुजः॥
en: Again, in the city of Virata, all the assembled Kauravas as well as you, O Karna, together with your younger brother were (all) defeated by Part. a in battle.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: एकस्याप्यसमर्थस्त्वं फाल्गुनस्य रणाजिरे। कथमुत्सहसे जेतुं सकृष्णान् सर्वपाण्डवान्॥
en: You are, in battle, incapable of fighting with Phalguna alone. How can you, (therefore) hope to conquer all the Pandavas together with Krishna?

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: अब्रुवन् कर्ण युध्यस्व कत्थसे बहु सूतज। अनुक्त्वा विक्रमेद् यस्तु तद् वै सत्पुरुषव्रतम्॥
en: O Karna, O charioteer's son, you boast too much (of your prowess). Be engaged in fight. It is the duty of good (i.e. really brave) men to display their prowess without uttering (a single boastful word).

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: गर्जित्वा सूतपुत्र त्वं शारदाभ्रमिवाफलम्। निष्फलो दृश्यसे कर्ण तब राजा न बुध्यते॥
en: By roaring like the rainless autumnal clouds, O charioteer's son, O Karna, you show that you have no worth. But the king does not understand this.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: तावद् गर्जस्व राधेय यावत् पार्थं न पश्यसि। आरात् पार्थं हि ते दृष्ट्वा दुर्लभं गर्जितं पुनः॥
en: Continue, O son Radha, to roar so long as you do not behold Partha; (for) you will cease roaring when you will see Partha near.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: त्वमनासाद्य तान् बाणान् फाल्गुनस्य विगर्जसि। पार्थसायकविद्धस्य दुर्लभं गर्जितं तव॥
en: Continue to roar so long as you are out of the reach of Phalguna's arrows: (for) you will cease roaring when you will see Partha near.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: बाहुभिः क्षत्रियाः शूरा वाग्भिः शूरा द्विजातयः। धनुषा फाल्गुनः शूरः कर्णः शूरो मनोरथैः॥
en: It is by means of (the prowess of) their arms that the Kshyatras are heroes. The twice-born ones display their heroism by words. It is by means of this bow that Phalguna is a hero. But Karna is a hero by the wishes (he cherishes in his heart).

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: तोषितो येन रुद्रोऽपि क: पार्थं प्रतिघातयेत्। एवं संरुषिस्तेन तदा शारद्वतेन ह॥
en: Who can resist Partha that has gratified even Rudra himself?” Thus reviled by the son of Saradvat.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: कर्णः प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठः कृपं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्। शूरा गर्जन्ति सततं प्रावृषीव बलाहकाः॥
en: Karna, the foremost of smiters, spoke these words to Kripa. Heroes always roar like clouds during the rainy season.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: फलं चाशु प्रयच्छन्ति बोजमुप्तमृताविव। दोषमत्र न पश्यामि शूराणां रर्णमूर्धनि॥
en: And they yield an early harvest like sceds sown into the soil (at the proper time). I do not find any fault with the warriors on the field of battle.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: तत्तद् विकस्थमानानां भारं चोद्वहतां मृधे। यं भारं पुरुषो वोढं मनसा हि व्यवस्यति॥
en: Boasting in several ways of themselves who bear a (great) burden in war. That person, who resolves in his mind to bear a burden.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: दैवमस्य ध्रुवं तत्र साहाय्यायोपद्यते। व्यवसायद्वितीयोऽहं मनसा भारमुद्वहन्॥
en: Is surely helped by fate in carrying out his purposes, If resolving in my mind to bear a (great) burden.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: हत्वा पाण्डुसुतानाजौ सकृष्णान् सहसात्वतान्। गर्जामि यद्यहं विप्र तव किं तत्र नश्यति॥
en: That is (if wishing in my mind) to slay in battle the son of Pandu together with Krishna and Sattvata, I roar thus, what harm is there in it to you, O Brahmana?

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: वृथा शूरा न गर्जन्ति शारदा अव तोयदाः। सामर्थ्यमात्मनो ज्ञात्वा ततो गर्जन्ति पण्डिताः॥
en: Heroes do not roar in vain like the autumnal clouds. The wise, conscious of their ownstrength, indulge in roars.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: सोऽहमद्य रणे यत्तौ सहितौ कृष्णपाण्डवौ। उत्सहे मनसा जेतुं ततो गर्जामि गौतम॥
en: I am, too, resolved in my mind to conquer in battle today the Pandavas and Krishna joined together, by exerting my best. O son of Goutama, it is on this account, that I indulge in roars.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: पश्य त्वं गर्जितस्यास्य फलं ते विप्र सानुगान्। हत्वा पाण्डुसुतानाजी सहकृष्णान् ससात्वतान्॥ दुर्योधनाय दास्यामि पृथिवीं हतकण्टकाम्।
en: O Brahmana, witness the result of these roars of mine. Having slain in battle the sons of Pandu together with Krishna. Sattvata and (all their) followers I will deliver the (entire) earth with its thorns weeded out, to Duryodhana.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: मनोरथप्रलापा मे न ग्राह्यास्तव सूतज॥ सदा क्षिपसि वै कृष्णौ धर्मराजं च पाण्डवम्।
en: Kripa said Your intentions being like the ravings (of a mad man) cannot be acceptable to me, inasmuch as you always tale to me, inasmuch as you always speak depreciatingly of Krishna, Arjuna and Dharmaraj, the son of Pandu.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: ध्रुवस्तत्र जयः कर्ण यत्र युद्धविशारदौ॥ देवगन्धर्वयक्षाणां मनुष्योरगरक्षसाम्। दंशितानामपि रणे अजेयौ कृष्णपाण्डवौ॥ ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवाग दान्तो गुरुदैवतपूजकः। नित्यं धर्मरतश्चैव कृतास्रश्च विशेषतः॥ धृतिमांश्च कृतज्ञश्च धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः।
en: O Karna, victory on the part of that person is certain who has on his side Krishna and the Pandava (Arjuna) both skilled in warfare and incapable of being vanquished in battle by the celestials, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the mortals the Uragas and the birds (even if all these fight) with their on). Yudhishthira the son of Dharma is devoted to the Brahmanas, (always) speaks truth, is selfrestrained, worships the Pitris and the celestials, is devoted to truth and righteousness, well skilled in weapons, is possessed of intelligence and is grateful.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: भ्रातरश्चास्य बलिन: सर्वानेषु कृतश्रमाः॥ गुरुवृत्तिरताः प्राज्ञा धर्मनित्या यशस्विनः।
en: His brother (also) are powerful, well-skilled in all the weapons, devoted to the ministrations of their elders, wise, renowned and (they) always practice righteousness.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: सम्बन्धिनश्चेन्द्रवीर्याः स्वनुरक्ताः प्रहारिणः॥ धृष्टद्युम्न: शिखण्डी च दौर्मुखिर्जनमेजयः।
en: His relations and kinsmen too are powerful as Indra himself, are devotedly attached (to him) and (efficient) smiters. Dhristadyumna, Sikhandi and Janamejaya, the son of Durmuksha. armoirs are

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: चन्द्रसेनो रुद्रसेनः कीर्तिधर्मा ध्रुवो धरः॥ वसुचन्द्रो दामचन्द्रः सिंहचन्द्रः सुतेजनः।
en: And Chandrasena, Bhadrasena, Kirtivarma, Dhruva, Dhara, Vasuchandra, Damachandra, Singha-Chandra, sutejana.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: दुपदस्य तथा पुत्रा दुपदश्च महासवित्॥ येषामर्थाय संयत्तो मत्स्यराजः सहानुजः।
en: And the sons of Drupada and Drupada himself skilled in great weapons and the king of Matsya together with his younger brothers are exerting their utmost on their behalf.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: शतानीकः सूर्यदत्तः श्रुतानीकः श्रुतध्वजः॥ बलानीको जयानीको जयाश्वो रथवाहनः। चन्द्रोदयः समरथो विराटभ्रातरः शुभाः॥
en: And Gajaneeka, Srutaneeka, Veerabhadra, Sudrasana, Srutadhvaja, Valaneeka, Jayaneeka, Jarapreya and Vijaya, Labdhalaksha, Jayasva, Rathavahana, Chandradaya, Kamaratha, the auspicious brothers of Virata,

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: यमौ च द्रौपदेयाश्च राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः। येषामर्थाय युध्यन्ते न तेषां विद्यते क्षयः॥
en: And the twins, the (five) sons of Draupadi and the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha are fighting for their sake. They (therefore) cannot meet with destruction.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो गुणाः पाण्डुसुतस्य वै। कामं खलु जगत्सर्वं सदेवासुरमानुषम्॥ सयक्षराक्षसगणं सभूतभुजगद्विपम्। निःशेषमस्रवीर्येण कुर्वाते भीमफाल्गुनौ॥
en: These and innumerable numbers of other kinsmen and relations) are on the side of the son of Pandu. Indeed, Bhima and Phalguna, by ineans of the prowess of their weapons, can easily destroy the whole universe together with all the celestials, the Asuras, the human beings and the Rakshasas, (other) created beings, the serpents and the elephants.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: युधिष्ठिरश्च पृथिवीं निर्दहेद् घोरचक्षुषा। अप्रमेयबलः शौरिर्येषामर्थे च दंशितः॥ कथं तान् संयुगे कर्ण जेतुमुत्र हसे परान्। महानपनयस्त्वेष नित्यं हि तव सूतज!॥ यस्त्वमुत्सहसे योद्धं समरे शौरिणा सह।
en: Yudhishthira, also by means of his angry looks, can consume the (whole). O Karna, how can you hope to vanquish these enemies in battle, for whose sake Souri of unrivaled prowess has armed himself? It is indeed a great impudence on your part, OCharioteer's son, as you always dare confronting Souri in battle.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: संजय उवाच राधेयः प्रहसन् भरतर्षभ॥ एवमुक्तस्तु अब्रवीच तदा कर्णो गुरुं शारद्वतं कृपम्।
en: Sanjaya said Thus spoken to (by Kripa), Karna the son of Radha then replied smilingly to the preceptor Kripa, the son of Saradvat.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: सत्यमुक्तं त्वया ब्रह्मन् पाण्डवान् प्रति यद् वचः॥४९ एते चान्ये च बहवो गुणाः पाण्डुसुतेषु वै।
en: “O Brahmana, the words that you have (just) spoken about the Pandavas are true. Indeed the sons of Pandu are gifted with these and many other noble qualities.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: अजय्याश्च रणे पार्था देवैरपि सवासवैः॥ सदैत्ययक्षगनधर्वैः पिशाचोरगराक्षसैः।
en: The sons of Pritha are unconquerable in battle by the celestials together with Vasava (at their head), by the Yakshas, the Daityas and the Gandharvas (all) united together and by the Pishachas, the Urages and the Rakshasas.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: तथापि पार्थाजेष्यामि शत्तया वासवदत्तया॥ मम ह्यमोघा दत्तेयं शक्तिः शक्रेण वै द्विज।
en: Still I will vanquish the Parthas by means of the dart granted to me by Vasava. This unfailing dart was given to me, O twice-born one, by Shakra.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: एतया निहनिष्यामि सव्यसाचिनमाहवे॥ हते तु पाण्डवे कृष्णो भ्रातरश्चास्य सोदराः।
en: By means of this dart I will slay Savyasachi in battle. When this son of Pandu will be slain, Krishna, as will as his uterine brothers (i.e., Yudhishthira and Bhima).

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: अनर्जुना न शक्ष्यन्ति महीं भोक्तुं कथञ्चन॥ तेषु नष्टेषु सर्वेषु पृथिवीयं ससागरा।
en: Will not able to enjoy the earth without Arjuna. At the destruction of all these, this, earth together with her seas.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: अयत्नात् कौरवेन्द्रस्य वश स्थास्यति गौतम॥ सुनीतैरिह सर्वार्थाः सिध्यन्ते नात्र संशयः।
en: Will come under the sway of the lord the Kurus without any trouble (on his part), O son of Goutama. There is no doubt that in this world, a sound policy leads to success in everything.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: एतमर्थमहं ज्ञात्वा ततो गर्जामि गौतम॥ त्वं तु विप्रश्च वृद्धश्च अशक्तश्चापि संयुगे।
en: Well aware of this (to be certain) I give forth (these) roar. O Goutama, you are much advanced in years, a Brahmana and unskillful in battle.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: कृतस्नेहश्च पार्थेषु मोहान्मामवमन्यसे॥ यद्यैवं वक्ष्यसे भूयो ममाप्रियमिह द्विजा
en: It is on account of your affection towards the sons of Pritha that you insult me (thus). If, O twice-born one, you speak such disagreeable words to me, as these again.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: ततस्ते खड्गमुद्यम्य जिह्वां छेत्स्यामि दुर्मते॥ यचापि पाण्डवान् विप्र स्तोतुमिच्छसि संयुगे।
en: Then taking up my scimitar I will cut-off your tongue, O wretch. O Brahmana, you are desirous of praising the Pandavas, in battle.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: भीषयन् सर्वसैन्यानि कौरवेयाणि दुर्मते॥ अत्रापि शृणु मे वाक्यं रथावदब्रुवतो द्विजा
en: In order to strike terror into the hearts of) all the troops and the Kauravas, O evil-minded one, O son of Goutama, hear what I say on this point.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: दुर्योधनश्च द्रोणच शकुनिर्दुमुखो जयः॥ दुःशासनो वृषसेनो मद्रराजस्त्वमेव च।
en: Where Duryodhana, Drona, Shakuni, Durmukha, Jaya, Dusasana, Vrishasena, the king Madra and yourself.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: सोमदत्तश्च भूरिश्च तथा द्रौणिर्विविंशतिः॥ : तिष्ठेयुर्दशिता यत्र सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः।
en: And Somadatta, Bhuri, the son of Drona and Vivingsati-all well-skilled in warfare, remain (prepared for battle) with their armours on.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: जयेदेतान् नरः को नु शक्रतुल्यबलोऽप्यरिः॥ शूराश्च हि कृतास्त्राश्च बलिनः स्वर्गलिप्सवः।
en: Can any foe, be he as powerful as Shakra himself, vanquish all these (heroes) in battle? All these warriors that are heroes, efficient in weapons, endued with strength, desirous of attaining the hcaven.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: धर्मज्ञा युद्धकुशला हन्युर्युद्धे सुरानपि॥ एते स्थास्यन्ति संग्रामे पाण्डवानां वधार्थिनः।
en: Conversant with religion and well skilled in battle, would slay the very gods in battle. These will remain on the field of battle for the purpose of destroying the Pandavas.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: जयमाकाङ्क्षमाणा हि कौरवेयस्य दंशिताः॥ दैवायत्तमहं मन्ये जयं सुबलिनामपि।
en: With their armours on, for the Kaurava king, solicitous of victory I deem victory even with regard to those endued with great prowess to be dependent on fate.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: यत्र भीष्मो महाबाहुः शेते शरशताचितः॥ विकर्णश्चित्रसेनश्च बाह्रीकोऽथ जयद्रथः।
en: Since the mighty-armed Bhisma lies (on the field) struck by a hundred arrows, (and since) Vikarna, Chitrasena, Valhika, Jayadratha.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: भूरिश्रवा जयश्चैव जलसंधः सुदक्षिणः॥ शलश्च रथिनां श्रेष्ठो भगदत्तश्च वीर्यवान्।
en: And Bhurisrava, Jaya, Jalasandha, Sudakshina, Sala, the foremost of car-warriors, the puissant Bhagadatta.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: एते चान्ये च राजानो देवैरपि सुदुर्जयाः॥ निहताः समरे शूराः पाण्डवैर्बलवत्तराः।
en: These and numerous other heroes difficult of be being vanquished by the very gods and more powerful than the Pandavas themselveslie slain in battle.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: किमन्यद् दैवसंयोगान्मन्यसे पुरुषाधम॥ यांश्च तान् स्तौषि सततं दुर्योधनरिपून् द्विजा
en: To what do you, that are the basest of men, attribute all this except the hand of fate? O twice-born one, as to the enemies, Duryodhana whom you always extol.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: तेषामपि हताः शूराः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ क्षीयन्ते सर्वसैन्यानि कुरूणां पाण्डवैः सह।
en: Hundreds and thousands of warriors on their side also have been destroyed. The troops of both the Kurus and the Pandavas are diminishing.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: प्रभावं नात्र पश्यामि पाण्डवानां कथंचन॥ यस्तान् बलवतो नित्यं मन्यसे त्वं द्विजाधम
en: I do not see in it any prowess on the part of the Pandavas. Those whom you, you that are the basest of men, always deem powerful.

description: The colloquy between Kripa and Karna
sn: यतिष्येऽहं यथाशक्ति योद्धं तैः सह संयुगे। दुर्योधनहितार्थाय 'जयो दैवे प्रतिष्ठितः'॥
en: I will confront in battle putting forth my utmost prowess for the welfare of Duryodhana. As regards success, it is dependent on fate.

sn: संजय उवाच तथा परुषितं दृष्ट्वा सूतपुत्रेण मातुलम्। खङ्गमुद्यम्य वेगेन द्रौणिरभ्यपतद् द्रुतम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing his maternal uncle thus insulted by the charioteer's son, the son of Drona brandishing his scimitar ran furiously towards him.

sn: ततः परमसंक्रुद्धः सिंहो मत्तमिव द्विपम्। प्रेक्षतः कुरुराजस्य द्रौणिः कर्णं समभ्ययात्॥
en: Then, excited with a great rage, the son of Drona, like a lion (rushing at) an infuriate elephant, rushed against Karna, even in the Very presence of the Kuru king. are of very very wicked

sn: अश्वत्थामोवाच यदर्जुनगुणांस्तथ्यान् कीर्तयानं नराधम। शूरं द्वेषात् सुदुर्बुद्धे त्वं भर्ल्सयसि मातुलम्॥
en: Ashvatthama said O basest of men, in spite of his speaking of the qualities that Arjuna is really endowed with, you, that understanding, have insulted my heroic maternal uncle through (sheer) malice.

sn: विकत्थमानः शौर्येण सर्वलोकधनुर्धरम्। दर्पोत्सेधगृहीतोऽद्य न कश्चिद् गणयन् मृधे॥
en: Without reckoning any of the words of bowmen in battle, puffed up with pride as you are, you are boasting today of your manliness.

sn: व ते वीय क चास्त्राणि यत्त्वां निर्जित्य संयुगे। गाण्डीवधन्वा हतवान् प्रेक्षतस्ते जयद्रथम्॥
en: Where was your prowess and where your weapons, when defeating you in battle, the wielder of Gandiva killed Jayadratha in your very presence?

sn: येन साक्षान्महादेवो योधितः समरे पुरा। तमिच्छसि वृथा जेतुं सूताधम मनोरथैः॥
en: O wretch of a charioteer, you are in vain hoping in your mind to conquer him, who formerly fought with the very Mahadeva himself.

sn: यं हि कृष्णेन सहितं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्। जेतुं न शक्ताः सहिताः सेन्द्रा अपि सुरासुराः॥
en: Since the combined celestials and the Asuras headed by Indra are incapable of defeating that foremost of the wielders of weapons, having Krishna for his ally.

sn: लोकैकवीरमजितमर्जुनं सूत संयुगे। किं पुनस्त्वं सुदुर्बुद्धे सहैभिर्वसुधाधिपः॥
en: How can you, O Suta, backed up by these earthly kings, indulge in hopes of vanquishing in battle, the unconquerable Arjuna, the foremost of all the heroes in the world?

sn: कर्ण पश्य सुदुर्बुद्धे तिष्ठेदानी नराधमा एष तेऽद्य शिरः कायादुद्धरामि सुदुर्मते॥
en: Look, O Karna of wicked understanding, O vilest of men stay here now. I will presently cut-off your head from your body.

sn: संजय उवाच तमुद्यतं तु वेगेन राजा दुर्योधनः स्वयम्। न्यवारयन्महातेजाः कृपश्च द्विपदां वरः॥
en: Sanjaya said The highly-energetic king Duryodhana himself and that best of men, Kripa, prevented him (i.e., Ashvatthama) who was rushing furiously (at Karna).

sn: कर्ण उवाच शूरोऽयं समरश्लाघी दुर्मतिश्च द्विजाधमः। आसादयतु मद्वीर्यं मुञ्चेम कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Karna said Let this basest of Brahmanas, who (thinks that he) is a hero, boasts of his prowess in battle and is of wicked understanding, taste of my prowess. Do leave him, O best of the Kurus.

sn: अश्वत्थामोवाच तवैतत् क्षम्यतेऽस्माभिः सूतात्मज सुदुर्मते। दर्पमुस्क्तिमेतत् ते फाल्गुनो नाशयिष्यति॥
en: Ashvatthama said 0 charioteer's of wicked understanding, we forgive you of this (fault). Phalguna will destroy this swelling pride of yours.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अश्वत्थामन् प्रसीदस्व क्षन्तुमर्हसि मानद। कोपः खलु न कर्तव्यः सूतपुत्रं कथंचन॥
en: Duryodhana said O Ashvatthama, O bestower of honours, be gratified; do forgive (him). O siniess one, you should not be angry with the charioteer's son.

sn: त्वयि कर्णे कृपि द्रोणे मद्रराजेऽथ सौबले। महत् कार्यं समासक्तं प्रसीद द्विजसत्तम॥
en: To you and Karna and Kripa and Drona and the king of Madra and to the son of Subala, a heavy task is entrusted. O best of the twiceborn ones, be gratified.

sn: एते ह्यभिमुखाः सर्वे राधेयेन युयुत्सवः। आयान्ति पाण्डवा ब्रह्मन्नाह्वयन्तः समन्ततः॥
en: O Brahmana, all the Pandavas, desiring to fight with and shouting to the son of Radha (to give battle) are coming (against him) from all sides.

sn: संजय उवाच प्रसाद्यमानस्तु तनो राज्ञा द्रौणिर्महामनाः। प्रससाद महाराज क्रोधवेगसमन्वितः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus appeased by the king, the highminded son of Drona, O great king, who was filled with a furious rage subdued his anger.

sn: तत: कृपोऽप्युवाचेदमाचार्य:सुमहामनाः। सौम्यस्वभावाद् राजेन्द्र क्षिप्रमागतमार्दवः॥
en: Then the large-heated preceptor, whose mild disposition soon returned (to him) an account of his being (naturally) of a peaceful

sn: कृप उवाच तवैतत् क्षम्यतेऽस्माभिः सूतात्मज सुदुर्मते। दर्पमुत्सितमेतत् ते फाल्गुनो नाशयिष्यति॥
en: Kripa said 0 Charioteer's of very wicked understanding, you are pardoned by us of this (fault). But Phalguna will (soon) destroy your swelling pride. son

sn: संजय उवाच ततस्ते पाण्डवा राजन् पञ्चालाश्च यशस्विनः। आजग्मुः सहिताः कर्णं तर्जयन्तः समन्ततः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O king, the Pandavas and the renowned Panchalas, united together and sending forth thundering roars, poured in by thousands.

sn: कर्णोऽपि रथिनां श्रेष्ठश्चापमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्। कौरवाग्रयैः परिवृतः शक्रो देवगणैरिव॥ पर्यतिष्ठत तेजस्वी स्वबाहुबलमाश्रितः। ततः प्रववृते युद्धं कर्णस्य सह पाण्डवैः॥
en: The puissant and energetic Karna too taking up his bow and surrounding by the foremost of the Kauravas, like Shakra by the celestials, awaited (their charge) relying on the strength of his own arms. The battle, that then took place between Karna (on one side) and the Pandavas (on the other).

sn: भीषणं सुमहाराज सिंहनादविराजितम्। ततस्ते पाण्डवा राजन् पञ्चालाश्च यशस्विनः॥
en: Was hot and furious and ruining with thundering shouts, O great monarch. Then, O king, the Pandavas and and the renowned Panchalas.

sn: दृष्ट्वा कर्णं महाबाहुमुच्चैः शब्दमथानदन्। अयं कर्णः कुतः कर्णस्तिष्ठ कर्ण महारणे॥
en: Seeing Karna, possessed of mighty arms, sent forth loud shouts. (And the said)-"This is Karna! where is Karna! O Karna, stay in this great battle.

sn: युध्यस्व सहितोऽस्माभिर्दुरात्मन् पुरुषाधम। अन्ये तु दृष्ट्वा राधेयं क्रोधरक्तेक्षणाऽब्रुवन्॥
en: O wicked-souled one, O vilest of men, give us battle. Others, with eyes burning in ire on beholding Karna, said.

sn: हन्यतामयमुत्सिक्तः सूतपुत्रोऽल्पचेतनः। सर्वैः पार्थिवशार्दूलै नेनार्थोऽस्ति जीवता॥
en: This arrogant son of charioteer having but a little sense should be killed by all these foremost of kings. He has no need of life.

sn: अत्यन्तवैरी पार्थानां सततं पापपुरुषः। एष मूलमनर्थानां दुर्योधनमते स्थितः॥
en: This sinful person is always an inveterate enemy to the sons of Pritha, abides by the advice of Duryodhana and is the root of all these evils.

sn: नतैनमिति जल्पन्तः क्षत्रियाः समुपाद्रवन्। महता शरवर्षेण च्छादयन्तो महारथाः॥ वधार्थं सूतपुत्रस्य पाण्डवेयेन चोदिताः। तांस्तु सर्वांस्तथा दृष्ट्वा धावमानान् महारथान्॥
en: "Slay him!” Thus saying, mighty Kshatriya car-warriors, at the command of the son of Pandu, rushed to slay the charioteer's son, enveloping (all the points) with a heavy downpour of arrows. Seeing all those highly powerful sons of Pandu (rush towards him).

sn: न विव्यथे सूतपुत्रो न च त्रासमगच्छत। दृष्ट्वा संहारकल्पं तमुद्भूतं सैन्यसागरम्॥
en: The charioteer's son was neither pained nor struck with terror. Beholding that wonderful army, vast as a sea and looking like Death itself.

sn: पिप्रीषुस्तव पुत्राणां संग्रामेष्वपराजितः। सायकौघेन बलवान् क्षिप्रकारी महाबलः॥
en: That puissant, light-handed and highly powerful one, devoted to the good of your sons and never vanquished in battle, by means of showers of arrows.

sn: वारयामास तत् सैन्यं समन्ताद् भरतर्षभ। ततस्तु शरवर्षेण पार्थिवास्तमवारयन्॥
en: Began to check (the career of) that army on all sides, O most exalted of the Bharatas. Then the Pandavas also, discharging downpours of shafts checked, (him).

sn: धनूंषि ते विधुन्वानाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। अयोधयन्त राधेयं शक्रं दैत्यगणा इव॥
en: Shaking hundreds and thousands of bows, they battled with the son of Radha as the Daityas (fought with) Shakra in days of yore.

sn: शरवर्षं तु तत् कर्णः पार्थिवैः समुदीरितम्। शरवर्षेण महता समन्ताद् व्यकिरत् प्रभो॥
en: That downpour, of shafts discharged by the kings on all sides, was destroyed by the puissant Karna with a heavy shower of arrows.

sn: तद् युद्धमभवत् तेषां कृतप्रतिकृतैषिणाम्। यथा देवासुरे युद्धे शक्रस्य सह दानवैः॥
en: Then a marvellous battle, in which each party was desirous of warding off the blows of the other and which resembled the fight between Shakra and the Danavas in the war between the gods and the Asuras, took place between them. arrows

sn: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम सूतपुत्रस्य लाघवम्। यदेनं सर्वतो यत्ता नाप्नुवन्ति परे युधि॥
en: There we beheld of wonderful lighthandness of the charioteer's son : for, all the hostile forces, exerting their utmost, could not subdue him in that battle.

sn: निवार्य च शरौघांस्तान् पार्थिवानां महारथः। युगेष्वीपासु च्छत्रेषु ध्वजेषु च हयेषु च॥ आत्मनामाङ्कितान् घोरान् राधेयः प्राहिणोच्छरान्।
en: That mighty car-warrior, the son of Radha, checking those downpours of discharged by the (hostile) kings, shot at their yokes, umbrellas, cars and steeds, dreadful arrows, marked with his own name. Then, afflicted by Karna and not knowing what to do, those (hostile) kings.

sn: ततस्ते व्याकुलीभूताः राजानः कर्णपीडिताः॥ बभ्रमुस्तत्र तत्रैव गावः शीतार्दिता इव। हयानां वध्यमानानां गजानां रथिनां तथा॥ तत्र तत्राभ्यवेक्षाम संघान् कर्णेन ताडितान्। शिरोभिः पतितै राजन् बाहुभिश्च समन्ततः॥ आस्तीर्णा वसुधा सर्वा शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम्। हतैश्च हन्यमानैश्च निष्टनदिश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Wandered about there on the field of battle) like cows pained with cold. Innumerable horses, elephants and car-warriors afflicted by Karna were seen to drop dead there. The entire field was strewn on all sides with the fallen heads and arms of the unretreating warriors, O king, with the dead and the dying and the waiting (combatants) lying on all sides.

sn: बभूवायोधनं रौद्रं वैवस्वतपुरोपमम्। ततो दुर्योधनो राजा दृष्ट्वा कर्णस्य विक्रमम्॥
en: The field of battle looked like the region of the son of Vivasvata, O king. Then, 0 monarch, beholding the feats of Karna, Duryodhana.

sn: अश्वत्थामानमासाद्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह। युध्यतेऽसौ रणे कर्णो दंशितः सर्वपार्थिवैः॥
en: Approached Ashvatthama and then said these words-"Yonder Karna, with his armour on, is seen (fighting) with all the (hostile) kings.

sn: पश्यैतां द्रवती सेनां कर्णसायकपीडिताम्। कार्तिकेयेन विध्वस्तामासुरी पृतनामिव॥
en: Behold, the (enemy's) army, oppressed with the arrows of Karna, is, like the Asura force afflicted by Kartikeya, running away in all the directions).

sn: दृष्वैतां निर्जितां सेनां रणे कर्णेन धीमता। अभियात्येष बीभत्सुः सूतपुत्रजिघांसया॥
en: Witnessing the defeat of his army by the intelligent Karna, Vibhatsu, in order to slay the charioteer's son, is advancing (against him).

sn: तद् यथा प्रेक्षमाणानां सूतपुत्रं महारथम्। न हन्यात् पाण्डव: संख्ये तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम्॥
en: Adopt such measures that the son of Pandu may not kill that mighty car-warrior, i.e., the charioteer's son in battle in our very sight."

sn: ततो द्रौणिः कृपः शल्यो हार्दिक्यश्च महारथः। प्रत्युद्ययुस्तदा पार्थं सूतपुत्रपरीप्सया॥
en: (Hearing these words of the king), the son of Drona and Kripa and Shalya and that mighty car-warrior, the son of Hridika, advanced against Partha in order to protect the charioteer's son.

sn: आयान्तं वीक्ष्य कौन्तेयं शक्रं दैत्यचमूमिव। बीभत्सुरपि राजेन्द्र पञ्चालैरभिसंवृतः॥ प्रत्युद्ययौ तदा कर्णं यथा वृत्रं शतक्रतुः ।
en: Seeing that the son of Kunti was coming against them like Shakra against the Daitya force. Then, O king of kings Vibhatsu also surrounded by the Panchalas marched against Karna like Purandara (marching against) Vritra.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच संरब्धं फाल्गुनं दृष्ट्वा कालान्तकयमोपमम्॥ कर्णो वैकर्तनः सूत प्रत्यपद्यत् किमुत्तरम्।
en: Dhritarashtra said Seeing the wrathful Phalguna looking like Yama, the destroyer of time, what measures, O charioteer, did Karna, the son of Vikartana, adopt?

sn: यो ह्यस्पर्धत पार्थेन नित्यमेव महारथः॥ आशंसते च बीभत्सुं युद्धे जेतुं सुदारुणम्।
en: That mighty car-warrior (i.e. Karna) always challenged Partha and hoped that he has powerful enough to vanquish Vibhatsu.

sn: स तु त सहसा प्राप्तं नित्यमत्यन्तवैरिणम्॥ कर्णो वैकर्तनः सूत किमुत्तरमपद्यत।
en: Thus meeting all on a sudden his inveterate enemy, what measures, O charioteer, did Karna, the son of Vikartana adopt?

sn: संजय उवाच आयान्तं पाण्डवं दृष्ट्वा गजं प्रतिगजो यथा॥ असम्भ्रान्तो रणे कर्णः प्रत्युदीयाद् धनंजयम्।
en: Sanjaya said Seeing the son of Pandu (advance against) his rival elephant, Karna dauntlessly fell upon Dhananjaya.

sn: तमापतन्तं वेगेन वैकर्तनमजिह्मगैः॥ छादयामास पार्थोऽथ कर्णस्तु विजयं शरैः।
en: Partha then enveloped Karna who was thus furiously advancing against him, with straightcoursing arrows furnished with golden wings.

sn: स कर्ण शरजालेन च्छादयामास पाण्डवः॥ ततः कर्णः सुसंरब्धः शरैसिभिरविध्यत।
en: (And) the son of Pandu covered Karna with a dense shower of arrows. Then Karna greatly excited with rage pierced him with three darts,

sn: तस्य तल्लाघवं पार्थो नामृष्यत महाबलः॥ तस्मै बाणाशिलाधौतान् प्रसन्नाग्रानजिह्मगान्। प्राहिणोत् सूतपुत्राय त्रिशतं शत्रुतापनः॥ विव्याध चैन संरब्धो बाणेनैकेन वीर्यवान्। सव्ये भुजाग्रे बलवान् नाराचेन हसन्निव॥
en: The mighty car-warrior (Partha) witnessing this nimbleness on his part could not endure it. That scorcher of foes, then, shot thirty arrows sharpened on stone, having flaming points and coursing straight, at the charioteer's son. That puissant and mighty one, then, as if with a smile, pierced him angrily with another long arrow in the end of his left arms. From that hand of his which was (thus) pierced with (great) force, his bow fell down.

sn: तस्य विद्धस्य बाणेन कराच्चापं पपात ह। पुनरादाय तचापं निमेषार्धान्महाबलः॥ छादयामास बाणौघैः फाल्गुनं कृतहस्तवत्।
en: Taking up that bow within half the time of the twinking of an eye, that highly powerful one, with great nibleness of hand, covered Phalguna with downpours of arrows.

sn: शरवृष्टिं तु तां मुक्तां सूतपुत्रेण भारत॥ व्यधमच्छरवर्षेण सम्पन्निव धनंजयः।
en: The arrowy shower, sent forth by the charioteer's son, was baffled by Dhananjaya with discharges of arrows, as if with a smile, O Bharata.

sn: तौ परस्परमासाद्य शरवर्षेण पार्थिव॥ छादयेतां महेष्वासौ कृतप्रतिकृतैषिणौ।
en: Those two mighty wielders of bow desiring to baffle each other and coming up to catch each other enveloped each other with a (perfect) deluge of arrows.

sn: तदद्भुतं महद् युद्धं कर्णपाण्डवयोर्मधे॥ क्रुद्धयोर्वासिताहेतोर्वन्ययोर्गजयोरिव।
en: Then a marvellous encounter took place between Karna and the of Pandu resembling that between two wild elephants for the sake of a she-elephant in the time of her passion.

sn: ततः पार्थो महेष्वासो दृष्ट्वा कर्णस्य विक्रमम्॥ मुष्टिदेशे धनुस्तस्य चिच्छेद त्वरयान्वितः।
en: Then that mighty bowman Partha, witnessing the prowess of Karna, speedily cutoff that part of his bow at which it is grasped.

sn: अश्वांश्च चतुरो भल्लैरनयद् यमसादनम्॥ सारथेच शिरः कायादहरच्छत्रुतापनः।
en: (And) that scorcher of (his) foes (i.e. Dhananjaya) sent his horses to the abode of Yama with broad headed shafts and severed the head of his charioteer from the body. son

sn: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं हताश्वं हतसारथिम्॥ विव्याध सायकैः पार्थश्चतुर्भिः पाण्डुनन्दनः।
en: Then Partha, the son of Pandu pierced that one (i.e., Karna) deprived on his steeds and driver and whose bow was cut-off with four arrows.

sn: हताश्वात् तु रथात् तूर्णमवप्लुत्य नरर्षभः॥ आरुरोह रथं तूर्णं कृपस्य शरपीडितः।
en: Afflicted with arrows of Kripa that foremost of men jumped down from the car of which the steeds were slain, quickly got up to another car.

sn: स नुन्नोऽर्जुनबाणौघेराचितः शल्यको यथा॥ जीवितार्थमभिप्रेप्सुः कृपस्य रथमारुहत्।
en: Afflicted with (Arjuna's) darts, that most exalted of men hastily jumped down from his steedless car and got up to the car of Kripa.

sn: राधेयं निर्जितं दृष्ट्वा तावका भरतर्षभ।॥ धनंजयशरैर्नुन्नाः प्राद्रवन्त दिशो दश।
en: 0 best of the Bharatas, witnessing the defeat of the son of Radha, your Partisans, (already) mangled by the shafts of Dhananjaya ran away in ten directions.

sn: द्रवतस्तान् समालोक्य राजा दुर्योधनो नृप॥ निवर्तयामास तदा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह।
en: Beholding that they were running away King Duryodhana himself rallied them and spoke these words.

sn: अलं दुतेन वः शूरास्तिष्ठध्वं क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥ एष पार्थवधायाहं स्वयं गच्छामि संयुगे।
en: Heroes, do not take to flight! O best of the Kshatriyas, stay! I am myself going against Partha in order to slay him in battle.

sn: अहं पार्थान् हनिष्यामि सपञ्चालान् ससोमकान्॥ अद्य मे युध्यमानस्य सह गाण्डीवधन्वना।
en: I will myself destroy Partha together with the Panchalas assembled (under his banners). In the battle that I will today fight with the wielder of Gandiva.

sn: द्रक्ष्यन्ति विक्रमं पार्थाः कालस्येव युगक्षये॥ अद्य मदाणजालानि विमुक्तानि सहस्रशः।
en: The son of Pritha will behold my prowess resembling that of the destroyer at the end of a Yuga. Today the arrowy showers that I will discharge by thousands.

sn: द्रक्ष्यन्ति समरे योधाः शलभानामिवायतीः॥ अद्य बाणमयं वर्षं सृजतो मम धन्विनः।
en: in battle, will be seen by the sons of Pritha to resemble (thick) flights of locusts. Today, when wielding my bow, I will continue to rain down arrows.

sn: जीमूतस्येव धर्मान्ते द्रक्ष्यन्ति युधि सैनिकाः॥ जेष्याम्यद्य रणे पार्थं सायकैर्नतपर्वभिः।
en: My soldiers will behold me like a cloud discharging torrents of rain at the end of the summer. Today I will, by means of straight arrows, conquer the sons of Pritha.

sn: तिष्ठध्वं समरे शूरा भयं त्यजत फाल्गुनात्॥ न हि मद्वीर्यमासाद्य फाल्गुनः प्रसहिष्यति।
en: Brave warriors, stay in battle. Shake off your fear of Phalguni. Encountering my prowess, Phalguni will not be able to stand it.

sn: यथा वेलां समासाद्य सागरो मकरालयः॥ इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ राजा सैन्येन महता वृतः।
en: As the ocean, the abode of the Makaras reaching the point between the high and the low tide-marks, is unable to get beyond it. Saying this, the king, surrounded by a mighty army, marched.

sn: फाल्गुनं प्रति दुर्धर्षः क्रोधात् संरक्तलोचनः॥ तं प्रयान्तं महाबाहुं दृष्ट्वा शारद्वतस्तदा।
en: Furiously with his eyes reddened in wrath, against Phalguni. Seeing that mighty-armed one advance (against Arjuna), the son of Saradvatta (i.e. Kripa).

sn: अश्वत्थामानमासाद्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ एष राजा महाबाहुरमर्षी क्रोधमूर्छितः।
en: Approaching Ashvatthama said these words-"This mighty-armed king, under the influence of rage and insensible with ire.

sn: पतङ्गवृत्तिमास्थाय फाल्गुनं योद्भुमिच्छति॥ यावन्नः पश्यमानानां प्राणान् पार्थेन संगतः। । न जह्यात् पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तावद् वारय कौरवम्॥ यावत् फाल्गुनबाणानां गोचरं नाद्य गच्छति।
en: Resorting to the practices of the insects, (which heedless of danger rush into fire) is desiring to fight with Arjuna (heedless of his life). Prevent the Kaurava king (from doing this) before he sacrifices his life in our very sight by encountering Partha in battle. So long as he does not present himself within the range। of Kirit's shafts.

sn: कौरवः पार्थिवो वीरस्तावद् वारय संयुगे॥ यावत् पार्थशरै।रैर्निमुक्तोरगसंनिभैः। न भस्मीक्रियते राजा तावद् युद्धान्निवार्यताम्॥ अयुक्तमिव पश्यामि तिष्ठत्स्वस्मासु मानद।
en: The heroic Kaurava king can only remain alive in battle. Prevent the king (from taking this rash step) before he is burnt to ashes by the dreadful arrows of Partha looking like snakes that have just cast off their sloughs. It looks very improper, O giver of hunours, that when we are here.

sn: स्वयं युद्धाय यद् राजा पार्थं यात्यसहायवान् दुर्लभं जीवितं मन्ये कौरव्यस्य किरीटिना। युध्यमानस्य पार्थेन शार्दूलेनेव हस्तिनः॥ मातुलेनैवमुक्तस्तु द्रौणिः शस्त्रभृतां वरः।
en: The king will go in person to fight in battle like one having no support. I think it will be (as) greatly difficult for Kaurava king to escape with life while fighting with Kiriti in battle, as it is in the case of an elephant (fighting with) a tiger. Thus addressed by his maternal uncle, the son of Drona, who was the foremost of those that could wield weapons.

sn: दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यं त्वरितः समभाषत॥ मयि जीवति गान्धारे न युद्धं गन्तुमर्हसि।
en: Quickly approaching Duryodhana, said these words-"O son of Gandhari so long as I am alive, it is not proper for you to fight.

sn: मामनादृत्य कौरव्य तव नित्यं हितैषिणम्॥ न हि ते सम्भ्रमः कार्यः पार्थस्य विजयं प्रति। अहमावारयिष्यामि पार्थं तिष्ठ सुयोधन॥
en: Disregarding me who am always devoted to your welfare. O Kaurava king, you need at all be anxious for vanquishing Partha. I will myself check Partha. Stay (here), 0 Suyodhona.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच आचार्य: पाण्डुपुत्रान् वै पुत्रवत् परिरक्षति। त्वमप्युपेक्षां कुरुषे तेषु नित्यं द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Duryodhana said The protector protects the sons of Pandu as if they were his own children. You also never manage in right earnest with my enemies.

sn: मम वा मन्दभाग्यत्वान्मन्दस्ते विक्रमो युधि। धर्मराजप्रियार्थं वा द्रौपद्या वा न विद्म तत्॥
en: It is either owing to my ill luck or owing to your desire to do good to the Dharmaraj ihat your prowess diminishes in battle, though I do not know what is the true cause.

sn: धिगस्तु मम लुब्धस्य यत्कृते सर्ववान्धवाः। सुखार्हाः परमं दुःखं प्राप्नुवन्त्यपराजिताः॥
en: Fie on my avaricious self on whose account all the friends, solicitous of my welfare, are, being vanquished (in battle), now experiencing great misery.

sn: को हि शस्त्रविदां मुख्यो महेश्वरसमो युधि। शत्रु न क्षपयेच्छक्तो यो न स्याद् गौतमीसुतः॥
en: What person is there, O son of Goutama's daughter, who though capable yet would not destroy my enemies, besides you that are the foremost of those that wield weapons and are equal to Maheshvara himself in battle.

sn: अश्वत्थामन् प्रसीदख नाशयैतान् ममाहितान्। तवारगोचरे शक्ताः स्थातुं देवा न दानवाः॥
en: O Ashvatthama, be gratified. Destroy my enemies. Neither the celestials nor thc Danavas are capable of staying within the range of your weapons.

sn: पञ्चालान् सोमकांश्चैव जहि द्रौणे सहानुगान्। वयं शेषान् हनिष्यामस्त्वयैव परिरक्षिताः॥
en: O Drona's son, destroy the Panchalas as well as the Somakas together with all their followers. Protected by you we shall slay the rest.

sn: एते हि सोमका विप्र पञ्चालाश्च यशस्विनः। मम सैन्येषु संक्रुद्धा विचरन्ति दवाग्निवत्॥
en: Look, O Brahmana, the Somakas and the renowned Panchalas are ranging furiously amidst my troops like a forest fire.

sn: तान् वारय महाबाहो केकयांश्च नरोत्तम। पुरा कुर्वन्ति निःशेषं रक्ष्यमाणाः किरीटिना॥
en: O mighty-armed and most excellent of men, check the career of these and also of the Kaikayas, before, they, backed up as they are by Kiriti, destroy (all our forces).

sn: अश्वत्थामंस्त्वरायुक्तो याहि शीघ्रमरिंदमा आदौ वा यदि वा पश्चात् तवेदं कर्म मारिष॥
en: Ashvatthama, O chastiser of foes march (against them) speedily. Earlier or latter this take should be accomplished by you, O Brahmana.

sn: त्वमुत्पन्नो महाबाहो पञ्चालानां वधं प्रति। करिष्यसि जगत् सर्वमपाञ्चालं किलोद्यतः॥
en: As, O mighty-armed one, you have sprung into existence in order to slay the Panchalas, you will surely, exerting your utmost, make the earth devoid of the Panchalas.

sn: एवं सिद्धाऽब्रुवन् वाचो भविष्यति च तत् तथा। तस्मात्त्वं पुरुषव्याघ्र पञ्चालाञ्जहि सानुगान्॥
en: It will surely come to pass as the worshipful sages who have attained (ascetic) success have said this. Therefore O most valiant of men, destroy the Panchalas together with their followers.

sn: न तेऽस्रगोचरे शक्ताः स्थातुं देवाः सवासवाः। किमु पार्थाः सपाञ्चालाः सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Not to speak of the sons of Pritha together with the Panchalas, even the very celestials together with their allies cannot stand within the range of your weapon. I speak this truly.

sn: न त्वां समर्थाः संग्रामे पाण्डवाः सह सोमकैः। बलाद् योधयितुं वीर सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I will tell you truth, O hero, that the Pandavas together with the Somakas, are incapable of fighting with you, even though they put forth their (utmost energy).

sn: गच्छ गच्छ महाबाहो न नः कालात्ययो भवेत्। इयं हि द्रवते सेना पार्थसायकपीडिता॥
en: O mighty-armed one, go, go. Do not waste time. Your forces, afflicted with Parthas' shafts, are taking to flight.

sn: शक्तो ह्यसि महाबाहो दिव्येन स्वेन तेजसा। निग्रहे पाण्डुपुत्राणां पञ्चालानां च मानद॥
en: 0 mighty-armed one, O bestower of honours, you are (No doubt) capable, by virtue of your own celestial energy, of chastising the sons of Pandavas as well as the Panchalas.

sn: संजय उवाच दुर्योधनेनैवमुक्तो द्रौणिराहवदुर्मदः। चकारारिवधे यत्नमिन्द्रो दैत्यवधे यथा॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus addressed by Duryodhana, the son of Drona invincible in battle, tried to destroy the enemies like Indra the Daytas.

sn: प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुस्तव पुत्रमिदं वचः। सत्यमेतनमहाबाहो यथा वदसि कौरव॥
en: (And) that mighty-armed one said these words to your son. O Kaurava of mighty-arms, what you have said is indeed true.

sn: प्रिया हि पाण्डवा नित्यं मम चापि पितुश्च मे। तथैवावां प्रियौ तेषां न तु युद्धे कुरूद्वह॥
en: The sons of Pandu are always dear to me as well as to my father. Similarly, we too also dear to them. But this is otherwise in battle.

sn: शक्तितस्तात युध्यामस्त्यक्त्वा प्राणानभीतवत्। अहं कर्णश्च शल्यश्च कृपो हार्दिक्य एव च।
en: O affectionate one, putting forth our (utmost) strength engage in fight dauntlessly regardless of our very lives. Myself we Karna, Shalya, Kripa and the son of Hridika i.e., Kritavarma.

sn: निमेषात् पाण्डवीं सेनां क्षपयेम नृपोत्तम॥ ते चापि कौरवीं सेनां निमेषार्धात् कुरूद्वह। क्षपयेयुर्महाबाहो न स्याम यदि संयुगे॥ युध्यतां पाण्डवाञ्छक्त्या तेषां चास्मान् युयुत्सताम्।
en: Can destroy the army of the Pandavas, O most excellent of kings, in the twinkling of an eye. And O best of the Kurus, O mighty armed one, they too can destroy the army of the Kauravas within the twinkling of an eye, if we are not present in battle. We are fighting with Pandavas putting forth our utmost prowess and they too are battling with us to the best of their might.

sn: तेजस्तेजः समासाद्य प्रशमं याति भारत॥ अशक्या तरसा जेतुं पाण्डवानामनीकिनी।
en: (Therefore) one energy encountering the other is neutralising (each other). O Bharata. (We are) incapable of putting down the Pandava's army by force.

sn: जीवत्सु पाण्डुपुत्रेषु तद्धि सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥ आत्मार्थं युध्यमानास्ते समर्थाः पाण्डुनन्दनाः।
en: So long as the sons of Pandu are alive. What I tell you is true. The sons of Pandu are fighting for their own sake and they are very competent also.

sn: किमर्थं तव सैन्यानि न हनिष्यन्ति भारत॥ त्वं तु लुब्धतमो राजन् निकृतिज्ञश्च कौरव।
en: Why will not they, therefore, destroy your troops, O Bharata? O descendant of Kuru, O king, you are most avaricious, deceitful.

sn: सर्वाभिशङ्की मानी च ततोऽस्मानभिशङ्कसे॥ मन्ये त्वं कुत्सितो राजन् पापात्मा पापपुरुषः।
en: Self-conceited and suspicious of everybody, It is for this reason that you suspect ourselves too. O king, I deem you are a mean, wickedsouled and sinful person.

sn: अन्यानपि स नः क्षुद्र शङ्कसे पापभावितः॥ अहं तु यत्नमास्थाय त्वदर्थे त्यक्तजीवितः।
en: As you are mean and your thoughts are sinful you suspect ourselves and others.
(However) for your sake, regardless of my very life I will do my best.

sn: एष गच्छामि संग्रामं त्वत्कृते कुरुनन्दन॥ योत्स्येऽहं शत्रुभिः सार्धं जेष्यामि च वरान् वरान्।
en: O foremost of Kurus, I am now going to fight for your sake. I will engage with your foes and destroy a large number of your enemies.

sn: पञ्चालैः सह योत्स्यामि सोमकैः केकयैस्तथा॥ पाण्डवेयैश्च संग्रामे त्वप्रियार्थमरिंदमा
en: In order to do what is agreeable to you, O chastiser of foes, I will fight with the Panchalas, the Somakas as well as with the Kaikeyas and the Pandavas, in battle.

sn: अद्य मद्वाणनिर्दग्धाः पञ्चालाः सोमकास्तथा॥ सिंहेनेवादिता गावो विद्रविष्यन्ति सर्वशः।
en: Today the Chedis, the Panchalas and the Somakas, scorched with my darts, like cows afflicted by a lion, will fly on all sides.

sn: अद्य धर्मसुतो राजा दृष्ट्वा मम पराक्रमम्॥ अश्वत्थाममयं लोकं मंस्यते सह
en: Witnessing my prowess today, king (Yudhishthira), the son of Dharma, together with the Somakas, will deem the whole world full of Ashvatthamas.

sn: आगमिष्यति निर्वेद धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ दृष्ट्वा विनिहतान् संख्ये पञ्चालान् सोमकैः सह।
en: Beholding the destruction of the Panchalas as well well as of the Somakas in battle, Yudhishthira, the lord of Dharma, will experience a great pain.

sn: ये मां युद्धेऽभियोत्स्यन्ति तान् हनिष्यामि भारत॥ न हि ते वीर मोक्ष्यन्ते मद्वाह्वन्तरमागताः।
en: O Bharata, I will destroy all those that will confront me in battle. O hero, afflicted with the prowess of my arms no one shall escape.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुः पुत्रं दुर्योधनं तव॥ अभ्यवर्तत युद्धाय त्रासयन् सर्वधन्विनः।
en: Having thus addressed your Duryodhana, that one, possessed of mighty arms (i.e., Ashvatthama), distressing all bow men, proceeded to battle.

sn: सोमकैः।
en: son

sn: चिकीर्षुस्तव पुत्राणां प्रियं प्राणभृतां वरः॥ ततोऽब्रवीत् सकैकेयान् पञ्चालान् गौतमीसुतः।
en: (And) that foremost of those that bear life was desirous of doing what was agreeable to your sons. Then the son of Goutama's daughter said thus to the Panchalas together with the Kaikeyas.

sn: प्रहरध्वमितः सर्वे मम गात्रे महारथाः॥ स्थिरीभूताश्च युद्ध्यध्वंदर्शयन्तोऽस्रलाघवम्।
en: All of you, O mighty car-warriors, strike me in the body and displaying your dexterity in handling weapons engage in battle with calmness.

sn: एवमुक्तास्तु ते सर्वे शस्त्रवृष्टीरपातयन्।॥ द्रौणिं प्रति महाराज जलं जलधरा इव।
en: Thus addressed (by Ashvatthama), all of them, O great monarch, began to discharge showers of weapons upon the son of Drona as clouds pour down showers of rain.

sn: तान् निहत्य शरान्द्रौणिर्दश वीरानपोथयत्॥ प्रमुखे पाण्डुपुत्राणां धृष्टद्युम्नस्य च प्रभो।
en: having destroyed those (showers of weapons), the son of Drona, even in the very presence of the sons of Drona, even in the very presence of the sons of Pandu and in that of Dhristadyumna, slew ten (warriors) among them in battle,olord.

sn: ते हन्यमानाः समरे पञ्चालाः सोमकास्तथा॥ परित्यज्य रणे द्रौणिं व्यद्रवन्त दिशो दश।
en: Sore oppressed in battle, the Panchalas and the Somakas, abandoning the son of Drona, took to flight in ten directions.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा द्रवतः शूरान् पञ्चालान् सहसोमकान्॥२३ धृष्टद्युम्नो महाराज द्रौणिमभ्यद्रवद् रणे।
en: Witnessing the flight of those heroes that is, the Panchalas and the Somakas, Dhristadyumna, O great king, rushed against the son of Drona in that battle.

sn: ततः काञ्चनचित्राणां सजलाम्बुदनादिनाम्॥ वृतः शतेन शूराणां स्थानामनिवर्तिनाम्।
en: Then surrounded by one hundred heroic and unretreating car-warriors riding on cars adorned with gold and the rattle of which resembled the roar of clouds full of rain.

sn: पुत्रः पाञ्चालराजस्य धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः॥ द्रौणिमित्यब्रवीद् वाक्यं दृष्ट्वा योधान् निपतितान्।
en: That great car-warrior, Dhristadyumna, the son of the king of Panchala, beholding the carnage of his warriors, said these words to the son of Drona.

sn: आचार्यपुत्र दुर्बुद्धे किमन्यैर्निहतैस्तव॥ समागच्छ मया साधु यदि शूरोऽसि संयुगे।
en: O son of the preceptor, O you that are possessed of wicked understanding, why are you slaughtering the common soldiers? If you are (really) a hero, then fight with me in battle.

sn: अहं त्वां निहनिष्यामि तिष्ठेदानीं ममाग्रतः॥ ततस्तमाचार्यसुतं धृष्टद्युम्नः प्रतापवान्। मर्मभिद्भिः शरैस्तीक्ष्णोर्जघान भरतर्षभ।॥ ते तु पतीकृता द्रौणिं शरा विविशुराशुगाः। रुक्मपुङ्खाः प्रसन्नाग्राः सर्वकायावदारणाः॥ मध्वर्थिन इवोद्दामा भ्रमराः पुष्पितं दुमम्।
en: I will (surely) slay you. Now stay (here) and be quiet.” The puissant Dhristadyumna, the, struck the son of the preceptor with keen and highly dreadful arrows capable of piercing the vital parts. (And) those thick flights of arrows, moving swiftly, furnished with golden wings, having keen points and capable of riving all the parts of the body, pierced (through the body of the son of Drona like maddened black-bees seeking for honey-entering into a flowering tree.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो भृशं क्रुद्धः पदाक्रान्त इवोरगः॥ मानी द्रौणिरसम्भ्रान्तो बाणपाणिरभाषत।
en: The proud and dauntless son of Drona, (thus) deeply pierced (with Dhristdyumna's arrows) became as enraged as a serpent crushed by foot and (then), arrow in hand, thus said

sn: धृष्टद्युम्न स्थिरो भूत्वा मुहूर्त प्रतिपालय॥ यावत् त्वां निशितैर्बाणैः प्रेषयामि यमक्षयम्।
en: O Dhristadyumna, wait a moment quietly before I send "you to the abode of Yama with sharpened darts."

sn: द्रौणिरेवमथाभाष्य पार्षतं परवीरहा।॥ छादयामास बाणौघैः समन्ताल्लघुहस्तवत्।
en: having thus addressed the son of Prishata, the son of Drona, the slayer of hostile heroes, like one endued with great nimbleness of hand, covered him completely with deluges of arrows.

sn: स बाध्यमानः समरे द्रौणिना युद्धदुर्मदः॥ द्रौणिं पाञ्चालतनयो वाग्भिरार्जयत् तदा।
en: Thus covered (with arrows) in that battle by the son of Drona, the son of the Panchala king, invincible in battle, thundered forth these words to the son of Drona.

sn: न जानीघे प्रतिज्ञां मे विप्रोत्पत्तिं तथैव च॥ द्रोणं हत्वा किल मया हन्तव्यस्त्वं सुदुर्मते।
en: O Brahmana, you are neither aware of my promise nor of my of my origin. Of wicked understanding as you are, I will slay you after killing Drona.

sn: ततस्त्वाहं न हन्म्यद्य द्रोणे जीवति संयुगे॥ इमां तु रजनी प्राप्तामप्रभातां सुदुर्मते।
en: I will not therefore slay you today in battle, since Drona is alive. O man of greatly vicious understanding, at the expiration of this night, when the bright dawn will appear.

sn: निहत्य पितरं तेऽद्य ततस्त्वामपि संयुगे॥ नेष्यामि प्रेतलोकाय ह्येतन्मे मनसि स्थितम्।
en: I will (first) slay your father and then send yourself too, in battle, to the abode of the departed spirits, I chariot this (thought) in my mind.

sn: यस्ते पार्थेषु विद्वेषो या भक्तिः कौरवेषु च॥ तां दर्शय स्थिरो भूत्वा न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यसे।
en: Now assuming a quiet attitude show all your hatred towards the sons of Pritha and your devotion towards the Kauravas. You will not escape alive (from me).

sn: यो हि ब्राह्मण्यमुत्सृज्य क्षत्रधर्मरतो द्विजः॥ स वध्यः सर्वलोकस्य यथा त्वं पुरुषाधमः।
en: That twice-born one, who giving up the practices of the Brahmana, gives himself up to the practices of the Kshaytrias, deserves to be slain by all the Kshaytrias like you, O vilest of men."

sn: इत्युक्तः परुषं वाक्यं पार्षतेन द्विजोत्तमः॥ क्रोधपाहारयत् तीव्र तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्।
en: That foremost of the twice-born ones (i.e. Ashvatthama), thus addressed in harsh words by the son of Prishata, became terrible excited with wrath and said (to Dhristadyumna) “Wait, wait."

sn: निर्दहन्निव चक्षुर्त्या पार्षतं सोऽभ्यवेक्षत॥ छादयामास च शरैर्नि:श्वसन् पन्नगो यथा।
en: (And) as if to burn the son of Prishata with his eyes, he gazed at him. Heaving sighs like a snake he covered (Dhristadyumna with arrows) in that battle.

sn: स च्छाद्यमानः समरे द्रौणिना राजसत्तम॥ सर्वपाञ्चालसेनाभिः संवृतो रथसत्तमः।
en: Though) that foremost of car-warriors, the son of Prishata, who was surrounded by all the Panchala troops, was (thus) struck with arrows by the son of Drona in that battle,

sn: नाकम्पत महाबाहुः स्ववार्यं समपाश्रितः॥ सायकांश्चैव विविधानश्वत्थाग्नि मुमोच ह।
en: (Yet) that mighty-armed one did not tremble; (but) resorting to his own prowess discharged at Ashvatthama numerous arrows.

sn: तौ पुनः संन्यवर्तेतां प्राणधूतपणे रणे॥ निपीडयन्तौ बाणौधैः परस्परममर्षिणौ।
en: Those two (warriors), who resisted each other, baffled the arrowy showers of each other and could not tolerate each other, were engaged in the game of battle in which the wager was life itself.

sn: उत्सृजन्तौ महेष्वासौ शरवृष्टीः समन्ततः॥ द्रौणिपार्षतयोर्युद्धं घोररूपं भयानकम्। दृष्ट्वा सम्पूजयामासुः सिद्धचारणवातिकाः॥ शरौघैः पूरयन्तौ तावाकाशं च दिशस्तथा।
en: Those two mighty wielders of bow poured down showers of arrows on a sides. Beholding the fight between the son of Drona and that of one Prishata which was awe-inspiring and dreadful to look at, the Siddhas, the Charanas and the (other) sky-ranging creatures highly extolled them. Filling the firmament and (all) the directions with a downpour of arrows.

sn: अलक्ष्यौ समयुध्येतां महत् कृत्वा शरैस्तमः॥ नृत्यमानाविव रणे मण्डलीकृतकार्मुकौ।
en: And creating a great darkness with the shafts, they fought with another unobserved (by other combatants). As if dancing in battle and drawing their bows to circles.

sn: परस्परवधे यत्तौ सर्वभूतभयङ्करौ॥ अयुध्येतां महाबाहू चित्रं लघु च सुष्ठु च।
en: And bent on killing each other and filling all the creatures with consternation, those two mighty-armed (heroes) fought admirably and with (great nimbleness and dexterity).

sn: सम्पूज्यमानौ समरे योधमुख्यैः सहस्रशः॥ तौ प्रबुद्धौ रणे दृष्ट्वा वने वन्यौ गजाविव।
en: (And they) were highly adored by thousands of foremost of warriors in battle. Seeing them engaged in battle like two wild elephants (encountering each other) in the forest.

sn: उभयोः सेनयोर्हर्षस्तुमुलः समपद्यत॥ सिंहनादरवाश्चासन् दध्मुः शङ्खांश्च सैनिकाः।
en: Both the armies experienced a great delight. The soldiers emitted forth roars like lions and blew their conches.

sn: वादिवाण्यभ्यवाद्यन्त शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ तस्मिंस्तु तुमुले युद्धे भीरूणां भयवर्धने।
en: And sounded hundreds and thousands of musical instruments. And in that terrific battle enhancing the terror of the coward.

sn: मुहूर्तमपि तद् युद्धं समरूपं तदाभवत्॥ ततो द्रौणिर्महाराज पार्षतस्य महात्मनः। ध्वजं धनुस्तथा छत्रमुभौ च पाणिसारथी॥
en: The encounter (between the sons of Drona and Prishata) seemed to go on equally for a moment only. Then O mighty monarch, the son of Drona, cutting off the bow, the standard, the umbrellas, the two Parshni drivers, the charioteer and the four steeds of the highsouled son of Prishata in battle, rushed against him.

sn: पञ्चालांश्चैव तान् सर्वान् बाणैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ व्यद्रावयदमेयात्मा शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। ततस्तु विव्यथे सेना पाण्डवी भरतर्षभ॥ दृष्ट्वा द्रौणेर्महत् कर्म वासवस्येव संयुगे।
en: And that one, of immeasurable soul, began ! to afflict all those Panchalas in hundreds and thousands with his straight coursing arrows. Then the arıny of the Pandavas, beholding that brilliant exploit, resembling that of Vasava, achieved by the son of Drona in battle, became greatly dejected, the most exalted of the Bharatas.

sn: शतेन च शतं हत्वा पञ्चालानां महारथः॥ त्रिभिश्च निशितैर्बाणैर्हत्वा त्रीन् वै महारथान्।
en: Destroying one hundred mighty carwarriors of the Panchalas with a hundred arrows and slaying three foremost of (their) men with three sharpened arrows.

sn: द्रौणिर्दुपदपुत्रस्य फाल्गुनस्य च पश्यतः॥ नाशयामास पञ्चालान् भूयिष्ठं ये व्यवस्थिताः।
en: In the very presence of Phalguna and of the son of Drupada, the son of Drona slaughtered all those Panchalas who had confronted him.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः पञ्चालाः समरे सह संजयैः॥ अगच्छन् द्रौणिमुत्सृज्य विकीर्णरथध्वजाः।
en: Thus slaughtered in battle, the Panchalas together with the Srinjayas fled from the son of Drona, on their cars with their standards cut down.

sn: स जित्वा समरे शत्रून् द्रोणपुत्रो महारथः॥ ननाद सुमहानादं तपान्ते जलदो यथा।
en: Having defeated his enemies in battle, that mighty car-warrior, the son of Drona, began to send forth thundering roars like those of the clouds at the end of summer.

sn: स निहत्य बहूञ्छूरानश्वत्थामा व्यरोचत। युगान्ते सर्वभूतानि भस्म कृत्वेव पावकः॥
en: Having destroyed numerous heroes, Ashvatthama shone like the fire at the end of a Yuga after having consumed all the creatures.

sn: सम्पूज्यमानो युधि कौरवेयैनिर्जित्य संख्येऽरिगणान् सहस्रशः। व्यरोचत द्रोणसुतः प्रतापवान्। यथा सुरेन्द्रोऽरिगणान् निहत्य वै॥
en: Highly adored by the Kauravas after having vanquished thousands of enemies in battle, the puissant son of Drona shone like the lord of the celestials himself after the destruction of his foes.

sn: संजय उवाच ततो युधिष्ठिरश्चैव भीमसेनश्च पाण्डवः। द्रोणपुत्रं महाराज समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O great monarch, king Yudhishthira and Bhimasena the son of Pandu hemmed in the son of Drona on all sides.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा भारद्वाजेन संवृतः। अभ्ययात् पाण्डवान् संख्ये ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: King Duryodhana, then, accompanied by the son of Bharadvaja, advanced against the Pandavas in battle. Then commenced a fight.

sn: घोररूपं महाराज भीरूणां भयवर्धनम्। अम्बष्ठान् मालवान् वङ्गाञ्छिबींस्त्रगर्तकानपि॥
en: Terrible to look at, highly dreadful and increasing the terror of the cowards. Large numbers of the Ambhastas, the Malavas the Vangas, the Sivis and the Trigartas.

sn: प्राहिणोन्मृत्युलोकाय गणान् क्रुद्धो वृकोदरः। अमीषाहाञ्छूरसेनान् क्षत्रियान् युद्धदुर्मदान्॥ निकृत्य पृथिवीं चक्रे भीमः शोणितकर्दमाम्। यौधेयानद्रिजान् राजन् मद्रकान्मालवानपि॥
