en: Were wrathfully sent by Yudhishthira to the region of Death. Cutting off (into pieces) the Abhisahas, the Surasenas and (other) Kshatriyas invincible in battle Bhima made the earth muddy with blood. (And) O king the Yaudheyas, the mountaineers, the Madrakas and the Malavas.

sn: प्राहिणोन्मृत्युलोकाय किरीटी निशितैः शरैः। प्रगाढमञ्जोगतिभिर्नाराचैरभिताडिताः॥
en: Were sent by the diadem-decked Shetavahana to the domains of Death. Deeply pierced with straight-coursing arrows.

sn: निपेतुर्विरदा भूमौ द्विशृङ्गा इव पर्वताः। निकृत्तैर्हस्तिहस्तैश्च चेष्टमानैरितस्ततः॥
en: The tuskers dropped (dead) on the ground like mountain peaks, with the chopped-off trunks of elephants, still moving to and fro (in convulsions).

sn: रराज वसुधाऽऽकीर्णा विसर्पद्भिरिवोरगैः। क्षिप्तैः कनकचित्रैश्च नृपच्छत्रैः क्षितिर्वभौ॥
en: The earth, being strewn all over, seemed to be full of snakes, moving about, with the fallen royal umbrellas decked with gold.

sn: द्यौरिवादित्यचन्द्राधैर्ग्रहैः कीर्णा युगक्षये। हत प्रहरताभीता विध्यत व्यवकृन्तत॥
en: The field, being scattered all over looked (beautiful) like the firmament studded with (innumerable) suns, moons and stars at the end of a Yuga. "Slay, strike dauntlessly, pierce and cut to pieces."

sn: इत्यासीत् तुमुलः शब्दः शोणाश्वस्य रथं प्रति। द्रोणमस्तु परमक्रुद्धो वायव्यारेण संयुगे॥
en: These (and similar other) tumultuous uproars arose near the car of Shonasva (i.e. Drona). Getting terribly enraged, Drona also, by means of Vayaveya weapon, in that encounter.

sn: व्यधमत् तान् महावायुर्मेघानिव दुरत्ययः। ते हन्यमाना द्रोणेन पञ्चालाः प्राद्रवन् भयात्॥
en: Began, like a furious hurricane (chasing away) the clouds, to destroy his enemies. (Thus slaughter by Drona, the Panchalas fled away from terror.

sn: पश्यतो भीमसेनस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः। ततः किरीटी भीमश्च सहसा संन्यवर्तताम्॥
en: In the very presence of Bhimasena and of the high-souled Partha. (Then) that one who wore a coronet (i.e. Arjuna and Bhimasena, rallying (their troops) all on a sudden.

sn: महता रथवंशेन परिगृह्य बलं महत्। बीभत्सुदक्षिणं पार्श्वमुत्तरं तु वृकोदरः॥
en: Attacked the large army (of Drona) with a mighty car force. Vibhatsu attacking the right and Vrikodara the left flank (of Drona's army).

sn: भारद्वाजं शरौघाभ्यां महद्भ्यामभ्यवर्षताम्। तौ तथा संजयाश्चैव पञ्चालाश्च महौजसः॥
en: They rained upon the son of Bharadvaja two mighty downpours of arrows. Then the Srinjayas and those great car-warriors, the Panchalas.

sn: अन्वगच्छन् महाराज मत्स्यैश्च सह सोमकैः। तथैव तव पुत्रस्य रथोदाराः प्रहारिणः॥
en: And the Matsyas together with the Somakas followed. In like manner, (many) car-warriors, who wore (efficient) smiters on the side of your son.

sn: महत्या सेनया राजन् जग्मुर्दोणरथं प्रति। ततः सा भारतो सेना हन्यमाना किरीटिना॥
en: (Followed) by a vast army, O king, proceeded towards the car of Drona. Then that Bharata army slaughtered by Kiriti (i.e., Arjuna who wore a coronet).

sn: तमसा निद्रया चैव पुनरेव व्यदीर्यत। द्रोणेन वार्यमाणास्ते स्वयं तव सुतेन च॥
en: (Overcome) with sleep and bewildered by darkness began once more to disperse. In spite of (the endeavours of) Drona and your son himself to prevent (their fight),

sn: नाशक्यन्त महाराज योधा वारयितुं तदा। सा पाण्डुपुत्रस्य शरैदीर्यमाणा महाचमूः॥
en: They were unable to rally the combat ts, O mighty monarch. That vast army, slaughter with arrows by the son of Pandu.

sn: तमसा संवृते लोके व्यद्रवत् सर्वतोमुखी। उत्सृज्य शतशो वाहांस्तत्र केचिन्नराधिपाः। प्राद्रवन्त महाराज भयाविष्टाः समन्ततः॥
en: Took to flight in all directions when the world was enveloped in darkness. Hundreds of kings, leaving their conveyances, fled away, O great monarch, in terror, on all side.

sn: प्राद्रवन्त महाराज भयाविष्टाः समन्ततः॥
en: Took to flight in all directions when the world was enveloped in darkness. Hundreds of kings, leaving their conveyances, fled away, O great monarch, in terror, on all side.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: संजय उवाच सोमदत्तं तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य विधुन्वानं महद् धनुः। सात्यकिः प्राह यन्तारं सोमदत्ताय मां वह।।॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing Somadatta angrily shake his great bow, Satyaki said to his charioteer “Bear me towards Somadatta.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: न ह्यहत्वा रणे शत्रु सोमदत्तं महाबलम्। निवर्तिध्ये रणात् सूत सत्यमेतद् वचो मम॥
en: O charioteer, I will not return from battle today without killing my enemy-the vilest of the Kurus, the son of Valhika. These my words are true.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततः सम्प्रेषयद् यन्ता सैन्धवांस्तान् मनोजवान्। तुरङ्गमाञ्छववर्णान् सर्वशब्दातिगान् रणे॥
en: Thereupon, (his) charioteer drove to the battle those horses oi' Sindhu breed endowed with great fleetness, having the colour of the conch and capable of bearing all the weapons.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: तेऽवहन् युयुधानं तु मनोमारुतरंहसः। यथेन्द्रं हरयो राजन् पुरा दैत्यवधोद्यतम्॥
en: Those (steeds), fleet as the mind or the wind, carried Yuyudhana (to the field of battle) as the horses of Indra, O king, had, in days of yore, born him who was preparing to slay the Asuras.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य सात्वतं रभसं रणे। सोमदत्तो महाबाहुरसम्भ्रान्तो न्यवर्तत॥
en: Beholding Sattyata quickly proceed against him to battle, Somadatta, O mighty monarch, confronted him undauntedly.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: विमुञ्चञ्छरवर्षाणि पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्। छादयामास शैनयं जलदो भास्करं यथा॥
en: Discharging a shower of arrows as the clouds (pour down) torrents of rain, he (i.e., Somadatta) covered the grandson of Sini like the clouds (covering the sun)

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: असम्भ्रान्तश्च समरे सात्यकिः कुरुपुङ्गवम्। छादयामास बाणौधैः समन्ताद् भरतर्षभ॥
en: 0 best of the Bharatas, the dauntless Satyaki also completely covered that most exalted the Kurus with arrowy showers in that battle.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: सोमदत्तस्तु तं षष्ट्या विव्याघोरसि माधवम्। सात्यकिश्चापि तं राजन्नविध्यत् सायकैः शितैः॥
en: Somadatta also pierced the descendant of Madhu in the chest with sixty arrows. Satyaki, too, O king, pierced him with keen darts.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: तावन्योन्यं शरैः कृत्तौ व्यराजेतां नरर्षभौ। सुपुष्यौ पुष्पसमये पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥
en: Pierced by each other with each other's arrows, they looked like two blossoming Kinsuka trees in the following season.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्गौ कुरुवृष्णियशस्करौ। परस्परमवेक्षेतां दहन्ताविव लोचनैः॥
en: With their bodies covered all over with blood, those two renowned descendants of Kuru and Vrishni eyed at each other as it (desirous of) consuming each other with their glances.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: रथमण्डलमार्गेषु चरन्तावरिमर्दनौ। घोररूपौ हि तवास्तां वृष्टिमन्ताविवाम्बुदौ॥
en: Those two dreadful-looking grinder of foes ranging on their cars coursing in circles, looked like two clouds pouring (torrents of) rain.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: शरसम्भिन्नगात्रौ तु सर्वतः शकलीकृतौ। श्वाविधाविव राजेन्द्र दृश्यतां शरविक्षतौ॥
en: With their bodies pierced, mangled and wounded with shafts, they looked, O king of kings, like two hedge hogs.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: सुवर्णपुङ्खरिषुभिराचितौ तौ व्यराजताम्। खद्योतैरावृतौ राजन् प्रावृषीव वनस्पती॥
en: Pierced with shafts endued with golden wings, those two (heroes), O monarch, looked as (beautiful) two lords of the forest covered with glow-worms during the rainy season.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: सम्प्रदीपितसर्वाङ्गौ सायकैस्तैर्महारथौ। अदृश्येतां रणे क्रुद्धावुल्काभिरिव कुञ्जरौ॥
en: Their bodies looking resplendent with arrows (they were pierced with) those two great car-warriors appeared in that battle, like two furious elephants with their bodies covered all over with (blazing) meteors.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततो युधि महाराज सोमदत्तो महारथः। अर्धचन्द्रेण चिच्छेद माधवस्य महद् धनुः॥
en: Then, O great monarch, in that encounter, the mighty car-warrior Somadatta cut-off with cresent-shaped arrows the great bow of the descendant of Madhu.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: अथैनं पञ्चविंशत्या सायकानां समार्पयत्। त्वरमाणस्त्वरकाले पुनश्च दशभिः शरैः॥
en: (He) then pierced him with twenty five darts and at that time when speed was (urgently) necessary, he again speedily pierced him with ten (more) arrows.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय सात्यकिर्वेगवत्तरम्। पञ्चभिः सायकैस्तूर्णं सोमदत्तमविध्यत॥
en: Thereupon Satyaki, taking up a very strong bow, speedily pierced Somadatta with five arrows.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततोऽपरेण भल्लेन ध्वजं चिच्छेद काञ्चनम्। बाह्रीकस्य रणे राजन् सात्यकिः प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Then again, Oking, Satyaki, as if with a smile in that battle, cut down with another broad-headed shafts the golden standard of the son of Balhika.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: सोमदत्तस्त्वसम्भ्रान्तो दृष्ट्वा केतुं निपातितम्। शैनेयं पञ्चविंशत्या सायकानां समाचिनोत्॥
en: Seeing his standard cut down Somadatta fearlessly pierced the grandson of Sini with twenty-five arrows.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: सात्वतोऽपि रणे क्रुद्धः सोमदत्तस्य धन्विनः। धनुचिच्छेद भल्लेन क्षुरप्रेण शितेन ह॥
en: Filled with wrath, Satyaki also, in that engagement, cut-off with a keen and razorfaced shaft, the bow of the (great) bowman Somadatta.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: अथैनं रुक्मपुङ्खानां शतेन नतपर्वणाम्। आचिनोद वहुधा राजन भग्नदंष्ट्रमिव द्विपम्॥
en: He then, O great king, pierced him (i.e. Somadatta), who then looked like a snake with its fangs broken, with one hundred straightcoursing arrows furnished with golden wings.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय सोमदत्तो महारथः। सात्यकि छादयामास शरवृष्ट्या महाबलः॥
en: Thereupon the greatly puissant Somadatta, the great car-warrior, taking up another bow, covered Satyaki with downpours of shafts.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: सोमदत्तं तु संक्रुद्धो रणे विव्याध सात्यकः। सात्यकिं शरजालेन सोमदत्तोऽप्यपीड्यत्॥
en: Satyaki also, getting greatly excited with wrath, pierced Somadatta in that battle. Somadatta, on his part, afflicted Satyaki with showers of arrows.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: दशभिः सात्वतस्यार्थे भीमोऽहन् बाह्निकात्मजम्। सोमदत्तोऽप्यसम्भ्रान्तो भीममाईच्छितैः शरैः॥
en: Bhima also, for the sake of Sattvata, struck the son of Valhika with ten arrows. And the dauntless Somadatta also pierced Bhima with sharpened arrows.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततस्तु सात्वतस्यार्थे भीमसेनो नवं दृढम्। मुमोच परिघं घोरं सोमदत्तस्य वक्षसि॥
en: Thereupon Satyaki, excited with wrath, discharged at the chest of Somadaita. a new, strong and formidable Parigha furnished with a golden handle.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: तमापतन्तं वेगेन परिघं घोरदर्शनम्। द्विधा चिच्छेद समरे प्रहसन्निव कौरवः॥
en: (But the descendant of Kuru), as if with a smile, cut-off into two parts, in that engagement, that dreadful-looking Parigha so it was advancing against him.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: स पपात द्विधाछिन्न आयसः परिघो महान्। महीधरस्येव महच्छिखरं वज्रदारितम्॥
en: Thus severed into two parts, that great Parigha of iron, fell down (on the ground) like the great peak of a mountain riven by thunder.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततस्तु सात्यकी राजन् सोमदत्तस्य संयुगे। धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन हस्तावापं च पञ्चभिः॥
en: Then, in the engagement, o king, Satyaki cut-off the bow of Somadatta with one broadheaded arrows and with another five the leathern case that sheathed his fingers.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततश्चतुर्भिश्च शरैस्तूर्णं तांस्तुरगोत्तमान्। समीपं प्रेषयामास प्रेतराजस्य भारत॥
en: Then with four darts he speedily sent before the lord of the departed spirit the four excellent horses (of Somadatta).

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: सारथेश्च शिरः कायाद् भल्लेन नतपर्वणा। जहार नरशार्दूलः प्रहसञ्छिनिपुङ्गवः॥
en: And, O Bharata, that foremost of carwarriors, as if with a smile, cut-off, with a broad-headed and straight-coursing arrow, the head of his charioteer from the trunk.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततः शरं महाघोरं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्। मुमोच सात्वको राजन् स्वर्णपुङ्ख शिलाशितम्॥
en: He then discharged (at Somadatta himself) a highly dreadful arrow, blazing like the fire, furnished with golden wings, bathed in oil and sharpened on stone.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: स विमुक्तो बलवता शैनेयेन शरोत्तमः। घोरस्तस्योरसि विभो निपपाताशु भारत॥
en: Shot with great force by the grandson of Sini that excellent and formidable shaft, darted like a falcon, at the chest of Somadatta.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महाराज सात्वतेन महारथः। सोमदत्तो महाबाहुर्निपपात ममार च॥
en: The great car-warrior Somadatta, deeply pierced by the puissant Satvata, fell down (from his car) and died, O great king.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं तत्र सोमदत्तं महारथाः। नहता शरवर्षेण युयुधानमुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Seeing Somadatta slain there, your soldiers proceeded against Yuyudhana with a large number of cars. arrowS

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: छाद्यमानं शरैर्दृष्ट्वा युयुधानं युधिष्ठिरः। पाण्डवाश्च महाराज सह सर्वैः प्रभद्रकैः। महत्या सेनया साधु द्रोणानीकमुपाद्रवन्॥
en: The Pandavas also, O mighty monarch, accompanied by all the Prabhadrakas and by a large army, made a rush upon Drona's division.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरः क्रुद्धस्तावकानां महाबलम्। शरैर्विद्रावयामास भारद्वाजस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Then, Yudhishthira, filled with rage, began to crush the troops of the son of Bharadvaja with in the the very presence of Bharadvaja's son.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: सैन्यानि द्रावयन्तं तु द्रोणो दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरम्। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः॥
en: Seeing his troops troops put to rout by Yudhishthira, Drona, with eyes, blood-shot in wrath, furiously rushed against him.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततः सुनिशितैर्बाणैः पार्थ विव्याध सप्तभिः। युधिष्ठिरोऽपि संक्रुद्धः प्रतिविव्याध पञ्चभिः॥
en: Then, (Drona) pierced the son of Pritha with seven sharpened darts. Yudhishthira also, inflamed with rage, pierced him in return with five (arrows).

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महाबाहुः सृक्विणी परिसंलिहन्। युधिष्ठिरस्य चिच्छेद ध्वजं कार्मुकमेव च॥
en: That mighty bowman, being (thus) deeply pierced, for a moment licked the corners of his mouth and (then) cut-off the standard and also the bow of Yudhishthira.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: स च्छिन्नधन्वा त्वरितस्त्वराकाले नृपोत्तमः। अन्यदादत्त वेगेन कार्मुकं समरे दृढम्॥
en: Deprived of his bows, that excellent king took up another tough and strong bow, with great speed when speed was highly necessary.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततः शरसहस्रेण द्रोणं विव्याध पार्थिवः। साश्वसूतध्वजरथं तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Then with a thousand shafts, the son of Pandu pierced Drona together with his horses, charioteer, standard and car and this (feat on the part of Yudhishthira) seemed marvellous.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: ततो मुहूर्त व्यथित शरपातप्रपीडितः। निषसाद स्थोपस्थे द्रोणो भरतसत्तम॥
en: In consequence of the strokes of those darts, Drona, the foremost of the Brahmanas, being (greatly) pained, sank unconsciously for a moment on the terrace of his car.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञां मुहूर्ताद् द्विजसत्तमः। क्रोधेन महताऽऽविष्टो वायव्यास्रमवासृजत्॥
en: Then regaining his consciousness, heaving sighs like a snake and excited with a terrible wrath, he brought into existence the weapon presided over by Vayu.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: असम्भ्रान्तस्ततः पार्थो धनुराकृष्य वीर्यवान्। ततस्तदसमस्रेण स्तम्भयामास भारत॥
en: But the dauntless and puissant son of Pritha, in that fight taking up his bow, checked the career of that weapon with one of his own.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: चिच्छेद च धनुदीर्घ ब्राह्मणस्य च पाण्डवः। ततोऽन्यद् धनुरादत्त द्रोणः क्षत्रियमर्दनः॥
en: And the son of Pandu also cut-off the large bow of that Brahamana. Drona, the grinder of the Kshatriyas then, having taken up another bow.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: तदप्यस्य शितैर्भल्लैश्चिच्छेद कुरुपुङ्गवः। ततोऽब्रवीद् वासुदेवः कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: The best of the Kurus cut-off that also with keen and broad-headed shaft, Then Vasudeva, addressed Yudhishthira, the son of

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: युधिष्ठिर महाबाहो यत्त्वां वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु। उपारमख युद्धे त्वं द्रोणाद् भरतसत्तम॥
en: "O mighty armed Yudhishthira, hear wihat I tell you. O foremost of the Bharatas, do not fight with Drona.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: यतते हि सदा द्रोणो ग्रहणे तव संयुगे। युद्धमस्य त्वया सह॥
en: Drona has been all along trying to capture you in battle. I do not think it proper for you to fight with him.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: योऽस्य सृष्टो विनाशाय च एवैनं हनिष्यति। परिवर्त्य गुरुं याहि यत्र राजा सुयोधनः॥
en: a

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: नानुरूपमहं मन्ये
en: He, that has been created created for his destruction, will slay him. Leaving your preceptor go (to the spot) were king Suyodhana is (fighting).

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: राजा राज्ञा हि योद्धव्यो नाराज्ञा युद्धमिष्यते। तत्र त्वं गच्छ कौन्तेय हस्त्यश्वरथसंवृतः॥
en: Kings ought to fight with kings (only); and they should not desire to fight with those that are not kings. O son of Kunti, surrounded by elephants, horses and cars, go to that spot.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: यावन्तात्रेण च मया सहायेन धनंजयः। भीमश्च स्थशार्दूलो युध्यते कौरवैः सह॥
en: Where Dhananjaya and that most valiant of men, Bhima, with myself only to help them are fighting with (all) the Kauravas.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: वासुदेववचः श्रुत्वा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। मुहूर्तं चिन्तयित्वा तु ततो दारुणमाहवम्॥ प्रायाद् द्रुतममित्रनो यत्र भीमो व्यवस्थितः। विनिप्रंस्तावकान् योधान् व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः॥५३
en: Hearing these words of Vasudeva, the virtuous king Yudhishthira reflected for a moment and then proceeded towards the spot where the battle was raging hot and furious and where, Bhima, the slayer of his foes, taking up his station, was destroying your warriors like the (grim) Destroyer with gaping mouth.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: स्थघोषेण महता नादयन् वसुधातलम्। पर्जन्य इव धर्मान्ते नादयन् वै दिशो दश॥
en: Ringing the surface of the earth with the thundering rattle of his car like the roar of the clouds at the end of summer, that king of kings, Yudhishthira.

description: The slaughter of Somadatta at the nocturnal fight
sn: भीमस्य निघ्नतः शत्रून् पाणिं जग्राह पाण्डवः। द्रोणोऽपि पाण्डुपञ्चालान् व्यधमद् रजनीमुखे॥
en: The son of Pandu, took up his station at the flank of Bhima who was destroying the foes. Drona also began, at that nigiit, to destroy his enemies, the Panchalas.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: संजय उवाच वर्तमाने तथा युद्धे घोररूपे भयावहे। तमसा संवृते लोके रजसा च महीपते॥
en: Sanjaya said That terrible and awe-inspiring battle having taken place when the world was enveloped with darkness and dust, o lord of the earth.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: नापश्यन्त रणे योधाः परस्परमवस्थिताः। अनुमानेन संज्ञाभिर्युद्धं तद् ववृधे महत्॥
en: The warriors, who remained on the field of battle) could not distinguish one another. It was by conjecture and uttering their names that those foremost of the Kshatriyas fought with one another.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: नरनागाश्वमथनं परमं लोमहर्षणम्। द्रोणकर्णकृपा वीरा भीमपार्षतसात्यकाः॥
en: When that terrible destruction of men, horses, elephants and foot-soldiers was going on, those heroes viz., Drona, Karna, Kripa, Bhima, the son of Prishata and Satvata.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: अन्योन्यं क्षोभयामासुः सैन्यानि नृपसत्तम। वध्यमानानि सैन्यानि समन्तात् तैर्महारथैः॥
en: Began, O best of the Bharatas, to afflict each other and the troops. The soldiers, (thus) terribly slaughtered by those great car-warriors.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: तमसा संवृते चैव समन्ताद् विप्रदुद्रुवुः। ते सर्वतो विद्रवन्तो योधा विध्वस्तचेतनाः॥
en: And surrounded by that dense gloom, took to flight in all directions. And with their minds (greatly) agitated (with terror) they ran away on all sides.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: अहन्यन्त महाराज धावमानाश्च संयुगे। महारथसहस्राणि जघ्नुरन्योन्यमाहवे॥
en: And, Ogreat king, while flying away in all directions they were (pursued) and killed. In that engagement thousands of great carwarriors slaughter one another.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: अन्धे तमसि मूढानि पुत्रस्य तव मन्त्रिते। ततः सर्वाणि सैन्यानि सेनागोपाश्च भारत। व्यमुह्यन्त रणे तत्र तमसा संवृते सति॥
en: (And) in that blinding darkness, (the soldiers) lost their senses. (All this is no doubt due to the evil counsels of your son. And that (dismal) darkness prevailing all around, all the creatures, may the very foremost of the combatants themselves, O Bharata, were seized with terror and their senses forsook them, o Bharata in that battle.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तेषां संलोड्यमानानां पाण्डवैर्विहतौजसाम्। अन्धे तमसि मग्नानामासीत् किं वो मनस्तदा।॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When drowned in that blinding darkness you were agitated by the Pandavas and were deprived of your energy, what became the state of your minds?

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: कथं प्रकाशस्तेषां वा मम सैन्यस्य वा पुनः। बभूव लोके तमसा तथा संजय संवृते॥
en: When the world was thus enveloped with darkness, how, O Sanjaya, their and my armies were disclosed to view again!

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: संजय उवाच ततः सर्वाणि सैन्यानि हतशिष्टानि यानि वै। सेनागोप्तनथादिश्य पुनर्वृहमकल्पयत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then all the survivors of the slaughtered army (of the Kurus) were, in obedience to the order of their commanders, again drawn up in battle array.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: स्तथा द्रौणिः पार्श्वतः सौबलश्चा स्वयं तु सर्वाणि बलानि राजन् राजाभ्ययाद् गोपयन् वै निशायाम्॥
en: And Drona (took his station) at the van, Shalya at the rear and the sons of Drona and Subala (respectively placed themselves) at the right and left flanks (of that array). And king (Duryodhana) himself, O monarch, was, during that night, engaged in protecting all the troops.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: उवाच सर्वांश्च पदातिसङ्घान् दुर्योधनः पार्थिव सान्त्वपूर्वम्। उत्सृज्य सर्वे परमायुधानि गृह्णीत हस्तैललितान् प्रदीपान्॥
en: (And) consoling all the foot-soldiers and also the lords of the earth, Duryodhana said to them "leaving aside your great weapons, take in hand blazing lamps.”

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: ते चोदिताः पार्थिवसत्तमेन ततः प्रहृष्टाः जगृहुः प्रदीपान्। देवर्षिगन्धर्वसुरर्षिसङ्घा विद्याधराश्चाप्सरसां गणाच॥
en: In obedience to the command of that foremost of kings they gladly took (burning) lamps, in their hands. large numbers of celestials, sages, Gandharvas and Rishis and hosts of Vidyadharas, Apsaras.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: नागाः सयक्षोरगकिन्नराच हृष्टा दिविस्था जगृहुः प्रदीपान्। ऽदृश्यन्त दीपाः ससुगन्धितैलाः॥
en: Nagas, Yakshas, Uragas and Kinnaras, stationed in the firmament, cheerfully took up lamps. Lamps, filled with perfumed oil, were seen to fall from the lands of) the regents of the cardinal points.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: विशेषतो नारदपर्वताभ्यां सम्बोध्यमानाः कुरुपाण्डवार्थम्। सा भूय एव ध्वजिनी विभक्ता व्यरोचताग्निप्रभया निशायाम्॥
en: Specially Narada and Parvata sent down for the sake of the foremost of the Kurus many such lamps, dispelling the darkness. On that night, the army (of the Kurus) looked brilliant by virtue of the lustre of these) lamps.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: महाधनैराभरणैश्च दिव्यैः शस्त्रैश्च दीप्तैरपि सम्पतद्भिः। रथे रथे पञ्च विदीपकास्तु प्रदीपकास्तत्र गजे त्रयश्च॥
en: The precious ornaments (wom by the combatants) and of the blazing celestial weapons that were hurled (by the Kaurava army against their enemies). Five lamps were placed on each car and three on each maddened elephants.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: प्रत्यश्वमेकश्च महाप्रदीपः। कृतास्तु तैः पाण्डवैः कौरवेयैः। क्षणेन सर्वे विहिताः प्रदीपा व्यादीपयन्तो ध्वजिनीं तवाशु॥
en: Upon each horse (was placed) a huge lamp. It was in this way that the Kuru warriors were illuminated. The lamps, being thus placed in due order, very lighted up your army.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: सर्वास्तु सेना व्यतिसेव्यमानाः पदातिभिः पावकतैलहस्तैः। प्रकाश्यमाना ददृशुर्निशायां यथान्तरिक्षे जलदास्तडिद्भिः॥
en: Nay, all the troops thus disclosed to view by the foot-soldiers carrying oilified lamps in their hands, looked as brilliant as the clouds in the firmament during the night with flashes of lightning (plying amidst them).

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: प्रकाशितायां तु ततो ध्वजिन्यां द्रोणोऽग्निकल्पः प्रतपन् समन्तात्। रराज राजेन्द्र सुवर्णवर्मा मध्यं गतः सूर्य इवांशुमाली॥
en: When the army was thus lighted up, Drona, like the fire, scorching everything around, looked resplendent, O king of kings, with his golden armour on, like the mid-day sun of blazing rays.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: जाम्बूनदेष्वाभरणेषु चैव निष्केषु शुद्धेषु शरासनेषु। पीतेषु शस्त्रेषु च पावकस्य प्रतिप्रभास्तत्र तदा बभूवुः॥
en: The lustre of the lamps (falling upon the golden Ornaments) the bright cuirasses and bow and the will-tempered weapons, was reflected from them.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: गदाश्च शैक्याः परिघाश्च शुभ्रा रथेषु शक्त्यश्च विवर्तमानाः। प्रतिप्रभारश्मिभिराजमीढ पुनः पुनः संजनयन्ति दीपान्॥
en: The rays (of these lamps) falling upon maces entwined with strings, bright Parighas, cars and darts as they whirled along, created innumerable lamps.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: छत्राणि वालव्यजनानि खङ्गा दीप्ता महोल्काश्च तथैव राजन्। व्याघूर्णमानाश्च सुवर्णमाला व्यायच्छतां तत्र तदा विरेजुः॥
en: O king, umbrellas and yak-tails and scimitars and flaming brands and necklaces of gold as they were being whirled looked exceedingly brilliant.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: शस्त्रप्रभाभिश्च विराजमानं दीपप्रभाभिश्च तदा बलं तत्। भृशं प्रकाशं नृपते बभूव॥
en: And, O king, that army illuminated by the lustre of the weapons, by the splendour of those lamps and by the brilliancy of the ornaments, looked highly resplendent.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: पीतानि शस्राण्यसृगुक्षितानि वीरावधूतानि तनुच्छदानि। दीप्तां प्रभां प्राजनयन्त तत्र तपात्यये विद्युदिवान्तरिक्षे॥
en: Well-tempered and beautiful weapons dyed with blood and wielded by the warriors shed a blazing lustre like flashes of lightning in the firmament at the end of the hot season.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: रभिघ्नतां चापततां जवेन। वक्त्राण्यकाशन्त तदा नराणां वाय्वीरितानीव महाम्बुजानि॥
en: The faces, of the combatants who were trembling by the impetuosity of their speed and rushing furiously against their enemies striking them down, shone at that time like great lotuses shaken by the wind.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: महावने दारूमये प्रदीप्ते यथा प्रभा भास्करस्यापि नश्येत्। तथा तदाऽऽसीद् ध्वजिनी प्रदीप्ता महाभया भारत भीमरूपा॥
en: On that dreadful night that army blazed up (by the light of those lamps) looked as terrible as the splendour of the sun during the progress of the conflagration of a great forest teeming with trees.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: तत् सम्प्रदीप्तं बलमस्मदीयं निशम्य पार्थास्त्वरितास्तथैव। नचोदयंस्तेऽपि चक्रुः प्रदीपान्॥
en: Seeing our army (thus) lighted up, the sons of Pritha urging all their foot-soldiers through their entire army, acted in the same way (as we did).

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: गजे गजे सप्त कृताः प्रदीपा रथे रथे चैव दश प्रदीपाः। द्वावश्वपृष्ठे परिपार्श्वतोऽन्ये ध्वजेषु चान्ये जघनेषु चान्ये॥
en: (And they) placed seven lamps on each elephant, ten on each car, two on the back of every horse and many on the flank and rear and the standards.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: सेनासु सर्वासु च पार्श्वतोऽन्ये पश्चात् पुरस्ताच समन्ततश्च। मध्ये तथान्ये ज्वलिताग्निहस्ता व्यदीपयन् पाण्डुसुतस्य सेनाम्॥
en: (Innumerable) blazing lamps were placed on the flanks and the rear and the van of and within and all around the entire army. Thus were the two hosts lighted up.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: मध्ये तथान्ये ज्वलिताग्निहस्ताः सेनाद्वयेऽपि स्म नरा विचेरुः। सर्वेषु सैन्येषु पदातिसङ्घा विमिश्रिता हस्तिरथाश्ववृन्दैः॥
en: Through the entire army, the infantry became mixed up with throngs of elephants, cars and horses. And like them (i.e. the footsoldiers) several other persons, also taking flaming brands in their hands, lighted up the army of the son of Pandu.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: व्यदीपयंस्ते ध्वजिनीं प्रदीप्तां तथा बलं पाण्डवेयाभिगुप्तम्। तेन प्रदीप्तेन तथा प्रदीप्तं बलं तवासीद् बलवद् बलेन॥
en: By virtue of (the lustre of) those lamps that army became fiercely blazed up like a blazing fire made fiercely illuminated by the rays of the sun, the maker of day.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: भाः कुर्वता भानुमता ग्रहेण दिवाकरेणाग्निरिवाभिगुप्तः। तयोः प्रभाः पृथिवीमन्तरिक्षं सर्वा व्यतिक्रम्य दिशश्च वृद्धाः॥
en: The splendour of those two (armies) reaching beyond the earth, the firmament and all the cardinal points began to increase. By that light their army as well as yours became crearly disclosed to view.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: तेन प्रकाशेन भृशं प्रकाशं बभूव तेषां तव चैव सैन्यम्। तेन प्रकाशेन दिवं गतेन सम्बोधिता देवगणाश्च राजन्॥
en: All the celestials, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the gods, the Siddhas and the Apsaras, awakened by that light which reached the skies, appeared on the scene.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसंघाः समागमन्नप्सरसश्च सर्वाः। तद् देवगन्धर्वसमाकुलं च यक्षासुरेन्द्राप्सरसां गणैश्च॥
en: The field of battle, thronged with the celestials, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Siddhas, the Apsaras and the spirits of the dead combatants about to enter the celestials regions, appeared like a second heaven.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: रायोधनं दिव्यकल्पं बभूव। रथाश्वनागाकुलदीपदीप्तं संरब्धयोधं हतविदुताश्वम्॥
en: Crowded with cars, horses and elephants lighted up by these lamps and (teeming with) furious warriors and steeds slain or careering madly, that mighty host, consisting of men, horses and elephants drawn up in battle array, looked like the array of the celestials and the Asuras (in days of yore).

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: महद् बलं व्यूढरथाश्वनागं सुरासुव्यहूसमं बभूवा तच्छक्तिसंघाकुलचण्डवातं महारथानं गजवाजिघोषम्॥
en: That nocturnal battle between the god-like combatants raged furiously like a tempest. The rush of arrows formed its fierce winds, the mighty car-warriors and elephants its clouds, the shafts its showers and the blood (of the combatants and the animals) its torrent of rain.

description: The lighting up of the troops
sn: शस्त्रैघवर्षं रुधिराम्बुधारं निशि प्रवृत्तं रणदुर्दिनं तत्। तस्मिन् महाग्निप्रतिमो महात्मा संतापयन् पाण्डवान् विप्रमुख्यः॥ गभस्तिभिर्मध्यगमो यथार्को वर्षात्यये तद्वदभून्नरेन्द्र॥
en: In that encounter that foremost of the Brahmanas, he magnanimous (Drona) endued with the energy of a great fire began to afflict the Pandavas like the noon day sun, (scorching everything) at the end of the rainy season.

sn: संजय उवाच प्रकाशिते तदा लोके रजसा तमसाऽऽवृते। समाजग्मुरथो वीराः परस्परवधैषिणः॥
en: Sanjaya said The field of battle, which had been before buried in darkness and dust, being thus lighted up (by the lustre of those lamps, heroic combatants, desirous of slay-ingone another, encountered one another (in battle).

sn: ते समेत्य रणे राजज्छस्रप्रासासिधारिणः। परस्परमुदैक्षन्त परस्परकृतागसः॥
en: Taking up their lances, swords and (other) weapons and encountering one another, they looked wrathfully at one another in battle, o king.

sn: प्रदीपानां सहस्रैश्च दीप्यमानैः समन्ततः। रत्नाचितैः स्वर्णदण्डैर्गन्धतैलावसिञ्चितैः॥
en: With thousands of lamps shedding their lustre all around and placed upon golden steeds adorned with gems and fed with fragrant oil.

sn: देवगन्धर्वदीपाद्यैः प्रभाभिरधिकोज्वलैः। विरराज तदा भूमिहैद्यौरिव भारत॥
en: And with the lamps sent down by the celestials and the Gandharvas which were more lustrous and brilliant, the field of battle, O Bharata, looked as beautiful as the firmament studded with planets and stars.

sn: उल्काशतैः प्रज्वलितै रणभूमिळराजत। दह्यमानेव लोकानामभावे च वसुंधरा॥
en: The field of battle, lighted up by hundreds of blazing brands, looked resplendent. Indeed, the earth seemed to be on fire like what happens at the time of universal destruction.

sn: व्यदीप्यन्त दिशः सर्वाः प्रदीपैस्तैः समन्ततः। वर्षाप्रदोषे खद्योतैर्वृता वृक्षा इवाबभुः॥
en: All the points illuminated by the light of) those lamps all around, looked (beautiful) like trees teeming with glow-worms on an evening of the rainy season.

sn: असज्जन्त ततो वीरा वीरेष्वेव पृथक् पृथक्। नागा नागैः समाजग्मुस्तुरगा हयसादिभिः॥
en: The, O monarch, brave warriors engaged with brave warriors. Elephants encountered elephants, horsemen (encountered) horsemen.

sn: रथा रथवरैरेव समाजग्मुर्मुदा युताः। तस्मिन् रात्रिमुखे घोरे तव पुत्रस्य शासनात्॥
en: and car-warriors joyfully engaged with one another, during the dreadful night at the command of your son.

sn: चतुरङ्गस्य सैन्यस्य सम्पातश्च महानभूत्। ततोऽर्जुनो महाराज कौरवाणामनीकिनीम्॥ व्यधमत् त्वरया युक्तः क्षपयन् सर्वपार्थिवान्।
en: Terrific, (indeed) was the clash of the two armies, (each) consisting of four (kinds of) forces. Then, 0 great king, Arjuna, vanquishing all the kings (on your son's side), began quickly to destroy the army of the Kauravas.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तस्मिन् प्रविष्टे संरब्धे मम पुत्रस्य वाहिनीम्॥ अमृष्यमाणे दुर्धर्षे कथमासीन्मनो हि वः।
en: Dhritarastra said What, (O Sanjaya) became the state of your minds when, filled with rage, the invincible one (i.e. Arjuna) entered into my son's army?

sn: किमकुर्वत सन्यानि प्रविष्ट परपीडने॥ दुर्योधनश्च किं कृत्यं प्राप्तकालममन्यत।
en: What did (my) forces do then when that sorcher of foes penetrated into them? (And) what course, (best) suited to that occasion, did Duryodhana think to adopt?

sn: के चैनं समरे वीरं प्रत्युद्ययुररिंदमाः॥ द्रोणं च के व्यरक्षन्त प्रविष्टे श्वेतवाहने।
en: What chastisers of foes opposed (the career of) that hero? Who were they that protected Drona when Shetavahana entered into our army)?

sn: के रक्षन् दक्षिणं चक्र के च द्रोणस्य सव्यतः॥ के पृष्ठतश्चाप्यभवन् वीरा वीरान् विनिघ्नतः।
en: Who were they that protected the right and the left car-wheels of Drona? Who were those heroes that protected the rear of that hero when he was engaged in fighting?

sn: के पुरस्तादगच्छन्त निघ्नन्तः शात्रवान् रणे॥ यत् प्राविशन्महेष्वासः पञ्चालानपराजितः। नृत्यन्निव नरव्याघ्रो रथमार्गेषु वीर्यवान्॥ यो ददाह शरैर्दोणः पञ्चालानां रथव्रजान्।
en: Indeed, when that invincible, puissant and mighty bowman, endued with the valour of a tiger, penetrated into the midst of the Panchalas, dancing as it were along the track of his car and destroying his enemies in battle, who were they that came to his front? How did Drona who consumed large troops of cars of the Panchalas.

sn: धूमकेतुरिव क्रुद्धः कथं मृत्युमुपेयिवान्॥ अव्यग्रानेव हि परान् कथयस्यपराजितान्।
en: Like a wrathful meteor, meet with his death? You always describe my enemies as cool, unvanquished.

sn: हृष्टानुदीर्णान् संग्रामे न तथा सूत मामकान्॥ हतांश्चैव विदीर्णाश्च विप्रकीर्णाश्च शंससि। रथिनो विरथांश्चैव कृतान् युद्धेषु मामकान्॥
en: Cheerful and impetuous in battle. But, O Sanjaya, you do not speak so of my warriors. You speak of them as slain, pale and routed and of my car-warriors as (always) made carless in the battle?

sn: संजय उवाच द्रोणस्य मतमाज्ञाय योद्धुकामस्य तां निशाम्। दुर्योधनो महाराज वश्यान् भ्रातूनुवाच ह॥
en: Sanjaya said Aware of the intentions of Drona as desirous of fighting during that night, Duryodhana, O mighty monarch, addressed his obedient brothers.

sn: कर्णं च वृषसेनं च मद्रराजं च कौरव। दुर्धर्षं दीर्घबाहुं च ये च तेषां पदानुगाः॥
en: (Namely) Vikarna, Chitrasena, Suparsa, Durdharsha and Dirghabahu and all their followers sayingद्रोणं यत्ताः परक्रान्ताः सर्वे रक्षन्तु पृष्ठतः।

sn: हार्दिक्यो दक्षिणं चक्रं शल्यश्चैवोत्तरं तथा॥
en: O powerful (heroes), all of your carefully protect Drona from the rear. Let the son of Hridika (protect) his right car-wheel and Shalya the left.

sn: ये त्रिगर्तानां च शूरा हतशिष्टा महारथाः। तांश्चैव पुरतः सर्वान् पुत्रसते समचोदयत्॥
en: Then your son commanded all the survivors of the heroic Trigarta warriors to place themselves in the van (saying).

sn: आचार्यो हि सुसंयत्तो भृशं यत्ताश्च पाण्डवाः। तं रक्षत सुसंयत्ता निघ्नतं शात्रवान् रणे॥
en: The preceptor is of benevolent disposition and the Pandavas are trying their utmost (to slay him). United together you will protect him while he will be engaged in destroying his enemies in battle.

sn: द्रोणो हि बलवान् युद्धे क्षिप्रहस्तः प्रतापवान्। निर्जयेत् त्रिदशान् युद्धे किमु पार्थान् ससोमकान्॥२४
en: Drona is powerful in battle, is endued with nimbleness of hand and is puissant. Not to speak of Pandavas united with the Somakas, he is competent to vanquish even the very gods in battle.

sn: ते यूयं सहिताः सर्वे भृशं यत्ता महारथाः। द्रोणं रक्षत पाञ्चालाद् धृष्टद्युम्नान्महारथात्॥
en: United together and exerting your very best in (this) dreadful engagement, all of you protect Drona from that invincible and mighty car-warrior Dhristadyumna.

sn: पाण्डवीयेषु सैन्येषु न तं पश्याम कञ्चन। यो योधयेद् रणे द्रोणं धृष्टद्युम्नाहृते नृपः॥
en: I do not find any one among the warriors of the Pandavas except Dhristadyumna, that is capable of defeating Drona in battle.

sn: तस्मात् सर्वात्मना मन्ये भारद्वाजस्य रक्षणम्। सुगुप्तः पाण्डवान् हन्यात् संजयांश्च ससोमकान्॥
en: I therefore think we should apply our whole heart and soul to protection of the son of Bharadvaja. (If) protected (by us) he will gradually destroy the Somakas as well as the Srinjayas.

sn: संजयेष्वथ सर्वेषु निहतेषु चमूमुखे। धृष्टद्युम्नं रणे द्रौणिर्हनिष्यति न संशयः॥
en: When all the Srinjayas, (placed) in the van of the (Pandava) army will be destroyed, the son of Drona will undoubtedly slay Dhristadyumna in battle.

sn: तथार्जुनं च राधेयो हनिष्यति महारथः। भीमसेनमहं चापि युद्धे जेष्यामि दीक्षितः॥
en: Similarly the great car-warrior Karna will vanquish Arjuna in battle. (And) I will myself destroy Bhimasena and others clad in mail in battle.

sn: शेषांश्च पाण्डवान् योधाः प्रसभं हीनतेजसः। सोऽयं मम जयो व्यक्तो दीर्घकालं भविष्यति।
en: The remaining Pandavas, destitute of energy, will be easily subjugated by (my) warriors. My success, then, will last for a long time.

sn: तस्माद् रक्षत संग्रामे द्रोणमेव महारथम्॥ इत्युक्त्वा भरतश्रेष्ठ पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव।
en: Therefore protect (carefully) the mighty car-warrior Drona in battle." Thus addressing (his soldiers), your son Duryodhana, 0 foremost of the descendants of Bharata.

sn: व्यादिदेश तथा सैन्यं तस्मिंस्तमसि दारुणे॥ ततः प्रववृते युद्धं रात्रौ भरतसत्तम।
en: Then cominanded his army (to act in obedience to his orders) during that dreadfully dark night. Then, O most exalted of Bharatas, took place a battle.

sn: उभयोः सेनयो?रं परस्परजिगीषया॥ अर्जुनः कौरवं सैन्यमर्जुनं चापि कौरवाः। नानाशस्त्रसमावायैरन्योयं समपीडयन्॥ द्रौणिः पाञ्चालराजं च भारद्वाजश्च सुंजयान्। छादयांचक्रतुः संख्ये शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ पाण्डुपाञ्चालसैन्यानां कौरवाणां च भारत। आसीनिष्टानको घोरो निजतामितरेतरम्॥
en: Between the two armies, both desirous of victory, O king, Arjuna, (then), began to sorely assailed the army of the Kauravas and Arjuna, with numerous (sorts of) weapons. (And) in that engagement the son of Drona began to cover the Panchala king and the son of Bharadvaja, the Srinjayas, with straight arrows. (And) O Bharata, as the armies of the Pandavas and the Panchalas (on one side) and that of the Kauravas (on the other).

sn: नैवास्माभिस्तथा पूर्वैर्दृष्टपूर्वं तथाविधम्। श्रुतं वा यादृशं युद्धमासीद् रौद्रं भयानकम्॥
en: Fell to destroying one another there arose a dreadful uproar. Neither ourselves nor those who preceded us, had (previously) witnessed such a furious and dreadful battle as took place during that night.

sn: संजय उवाच वर्तमाने तदा रौद्रे रात्रियुद्धे विशाम्पते। सर्वभूतक्षयकरे धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ अब्रवीत् पाण्डवांश्चैव पञ्चालांश्चैव सोमकान्। अभिद्रवत् संयातं द्रोणमेव जिघांसया॥
en: Sanjaya said When, O lord of the earth, that terrific nocturnal battle, destructive of all the creatures, was raging, Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, spoke to the (other) Pandavas and the united Panchalas and Somakas, O monarch, for the destruction of men, cars and elephants, "make a rush upon Drona only in order to slay him."

sn: राज्ञस्ते वचनाद् राजन् पञ्चालाः सृञ्जयास्तथा। द्रोणमेवाभ्यवर्तन्त नदन्तो भैरवान् रवान्॥
en: In obedience to the commands of the king, the Panchalas as well as the Srinjayas O monarch, sending forth thundering roars, rushed against Drona alone.

sn: तं तु ते प्रतिगर्जन्तः प्रत्युद्यातास्त्वमर्षिताः। यथाशक्ति यथोत्साहं यथासत्त्वं च संयुगे॥
en: We two, on our part, roaring in return and filled with wrath, rushed against them, in battle, to the full measure of our prowess, enthusiasm and courage.

sn: कृतवर्मा तु हार्दिक्यो युधिष्ठिरमुपाद्रवत्। द्रोणं प्रति समायान्तं मत्तो मत्तमिव द्विपम्॥
en: Kritavarman, the son of Hridika, rushed against Yudhishthira as he was advancing against Drona like a mad elephant against its infuriate rival.

sn: शैनेयं शरवर्षाणि विकिरन्तं समन्ततः। अभ्ययात् कौरवो राजन् भूरिः संग्राममूर्धनि॥
en: (Similarly), O king, Bhuri, the crusher (of his foes) in battle who belonged to the Kuru party rushed against the grandson of Sini (as he came forward) scattering showers of arrows on all sides.

sn: सहदेवमथायान्तं द्रोणप्रेप्सुं महारथम्। कर्णो वैकर्तनो राजन् वारयामास पाण्डवम्॥
en: Again, O king, Karna, the son of Vikartana, checked that mighty car-warriors Sahadeva, the son of Pandu, as he, actuated with the desire of taking Drona, was advancing (against him).

sn: भीमसेनमथायान्तं व्यादितास्यमिवान्तकम्। स्वयं दुर्योधनो राजा प्रतीपं मृत्युमाव्रजत्॥
en: Duryodhana himself rushed against Bhimasena, the foremost of car-warriors, in that engagement, who was advancing on his car (against Drona) like the grim Destroyer.

sn: नकुलं च युधां श्रेष्ठं सर्वयुद्धविशारदम्। शकुनिः सौबलो राजन् वारयामास सत्वरः॥
en: Shakuni, the son of Subala, O king, quickly opposed Nakula, the best of warriors and skilled in every (sort of) battle.

sn: शिखण्डिनमथायान्तं रथेन रथिनां वरम्। कृपः शारद्वतो राजन् वारयामास संयुगे॥
en: Similarly, in that encounter, Kripa, the son of Saradvata, opposed Shikhandi, the foremost of car-warriors, (who was) advancing on his car, Oking.

sn: प्रतिविन्ध्यमथायान्तं मयूरसदृशैर्हयैः। दुःशासनो महाराज यत्तो यत्तमवारयत्॥
en: In like manner, . great monarch, Dushasana, with utmost exertions, checked Prativindhya, who was resolutely advancing (on his car drawn by) heroes, (beautiful) as peacocks.

sn: भैमसेनिमथायान्तं मायाशतविशारदम्। अश्वत्थामा महाराज राक्षसं प्रत्यषेधयत्॥
en: Similarly, O mighty monarch, Ashvatthama checked the career of the son of Bhimasena, viz., the Rakshasa (Ghatotkacha) skilled in a hundred sorts of illusions.

sn: द्रुपदं वृषसेनस्तु ससैन्यं सपदानुगम्। वारयामास समरे द्रोणप्रेप्सुं महारथम्॥
en: In that engagement Vrishasena resisted the highly puissant Drupada, (who) accompanied by his troops and retainers, (advanced forward) with the desire of slaying Drona.

sn: विराटं दुतमायान्तं द्रोणस्य निधनं प्रति। मद्रराजः सुसंक्रुद्धो वारयामास भारत॥
en: 0 Bharata, O great monarch, the king of Madra, inflamed with rage, opposed Virata who was advancing quickly for slaying Drona.

sn: शतानीकमथायान्तं नाकुलिं रभसं रणे। चित्रसेनो रुरोधाशु शरैर्दोणपरीप्सया॥
en: Similarly, in that encounter, Chitrasena, with showers of arrows, checked the impetuous Sataneeka the son of Nakula, as he was advancing for the purpose of taking the life of Drona.

sn: अर्जुनं च युधां श्रेष्ठं प्राद्रवन्तं महारथम्। अलम्बुषो महाराज राक्षसेन्द्रो न्यवारयत्॥
en: O great king, Alambusha, the lord of the Rakshasas, resisted the rapid career of the mighty car-warrior Arjuna, the foremost of warriors.

sn: तथा द्रोणं महेष्वासं निजतं शात्रवान् रणे। धृष्टद्युम्नोऽथ पाञ्चाल्यो हृष्टरूपमवारयत्॥
en: Then Dhristadyumna, the son of the Panchala king, gladly resisted the mighty bowman Drona (who was) destroying his enemies.

sn: तथान्यान् पाण्डुपुत्राणां समायातान् महारथान्। तावका रथिनो राजन् वारयामासुरोजसा॥
en: Similarly, o king, your car-warriors energetically opposed other great car-warriors of the sons of Pandu, who were advancing (Against Drona).

sn: गजारोहा गजैस्तूर्णं संनिपत्य महामृधे। योधयन्तश्च मृद्गन्तः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Hundreds and thousands of warriors, mounted on elephants, speedily encountering riders on elephants in that great engagement, began to fight with and crush one another.

sn: निशीथे तुरगा राजन् द्रावयन्तः परस्परम्। समदृश्यन्त वेगेन पक्षवन्तो यथाऽद्रयः॥
en: O king, at dead of night, horses, rushing furiously against one another, looked like mountains endued with wings.

sn: सादिनः सादिभिः सार्धं प्रासशक्त्यष्टिपाणयः। समागच्छन् महाराज विनदन्तः पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: O mighty monarch, taking up lances, darts and swords in their hands and sending forth loud shouts, horsemen closed with horsemen.

sn: नरास्तु बहवस्तत्र समाजग्मुः परस्परम्। गदाभिर्मुसलैश्चैव नानाशस्त्रैश्च संयुगे॥
en: There (on the field of battle) large numbers of men destroyed one another in heaps, by means of maces, short clubs and several other weapons.

sn: कृतवर्मा तु हार्दिक्यो धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। वारयामास संक्रुद्धो वेलेवोवृत्तमर्णवम्॥
en: Kritavarma, the son of Hridika, inflamed with rage, resisted Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, as the place between the high and the low tide-marks (resists) the ocean.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु हार्दिक्यं विद्ध्वा पञ्चभिराशुगैः। पुनर्विव्याध विंशत्या तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Yudhishthira, also piercing the son of Hridika with five darts and again piercing him with twenty (more), said-"wait, wait."

sn: कृतवर्मा तु संक्रुद्धो धर्मपुत्रस्य मारिष। धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन तं च विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: O worshipful sire, Kritavarma too, fired with rage, cut-off the bow of the Dharmaraja with a broad-headed dart and then pierced him with seven (arrows).

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय धर्मपुत्रो महारथः। हार्दिक्यं दशभिर्बाणैर्बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्॥
en: Then that mighty car-warrior, that is, the son of Dharma, taking up another bow, struck the son of Hridika on the arms and the chest with ten arrows.

sn: माधवस्तु रणे विद्धो धर्मपुत्रेण मारिष। प्राकम्पत च रोषेण सप्तभिश्चादयच्छरैः॥
en: Pierced in (that) battle by the son of Dharma, O worshipful sire, the descendant of Madhu (i.e. Kritavarma) trembled in ire and (then) afflicted (Yudhishthira) with seven arrows.

sn: तस्य पार्थो धनुश्छित्त्वा हस्तावापं निकृत्य च। प्राहिणोन्निशितान् बाणान् पञ्च राजञ्छिलाशितान्।। २८
en: The son of Pritha (however), cutting off his bow and armlet, shot at him, O king, five keen and broad-headed shafts sharpened on stone.

sn: ते तस्य कवचं भित्त्वा हेमचित्रं महाधनम्। प्राविशन् धरणी भित्त्वा वल्मीकमिव पन्नगाः॥
en: Penetrating through his precious armour ornamented with gold, those fierce shafts entered into the earth like snakes (entering into) ant-hill.

sn: अक्ष्णोनिमेषमात्रेण सोऽन्यदादाय कार्मुकम्। विव्याध पाण्डवं षष्ट्या सूतं च नवभिः शरैः॥
en: Taking up another bow in the twinkling of an eye, he pierced the son of Pandu with six and again with ten arrows.

sn: तस्य शक्तिममेयात्मा पाण्डवो भुजगोपमाम्। चिक्षेप भरतश्रेष्ठ रथे न्यस्य महद् धनुः॥
en: Then that Pandava, of immeasurable soul, placing his mighty bow on the car, hurled at him (i.e. Kritavarman) a dart (fierce) as a snake.

sn: सा हेमचित्रा महती पाण्डवेन प्रवेरिता। निर्भिद्य दक्षिणं बाहुं प्राविशद् धरणीतलम्॥
en: Hurled by the son of Pandu that formidable (dart) ornamented with gold, penetrating through the right arm (of Kritavarma) entered into the bottom of the earth.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु गृह्य पार्थः पुनर्धनुः। हार्दिक्यं छादयामास शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: In the meantime, the son of Pritha, taking up his mighty bow covered the son of Hridika with straight shafts.

sn: ततस्तु समरे शूरो वृष्णीनां प्रवरो रथी। व्यश्वसूतरथं चक्रे निमेषार्धाद् युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Then there (on the field of battle) that hero, that foremost car-warrior among the Vrishnis, within half the time of the twinkling of an eye, deprived Yudhishthira of his horse, driver and car.

sn: ततस्तु पाण्डवो ज्येष्ठः खङ्गं चर्म समाददे। तदस्य निशितैर्बाणैर्व्यधमन्माधवो रणे॥
en: Then the eldest son of Pandu took up a sword and shield. But the descendant of Madhu cut-off those two with sharpened and broad headed shafts in that battle.

sn: तोमरं तु ततो गृह्य स्वर्णदण्डं दुरासदम्। प्रेषयत् समरे तूर्णं हार्दिक्यस्य युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Thereupon, taking up a formidable lance furnished with a golden handle, (Yudhishthira) hurled it, quickly in that engagement, against the high-souled son of Hridika.

sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा धर्मराजभुजच्युतम्। द्विधा चिच्छेद हार्दिक्यः कृतहस्तः स्मयन्निव॥
en: (But) the light-handed son of Hridika, as if with a smile, cut-off into two parts, that (formidable lance), as it, hurled by the hand of Yudhishthira careered impetuously along.

sn: ततः शरशतेनाजौ धर्मपुत्रमवाकिरत्। कवचं चास्य संक्रुद्धः शरैस्तीक्ष्णौरदारयत्॥
en: Then, in that encounter, he covered the son of Dharma with hundreds of shafts; (and then), inflamed with ire he cut-off the armour of (Yudhishthira) with showers of arrows.

sn: हार्दिक्यशरसंछन्नं कवचं तन्महाधनम्। व्यशीयर्त रणे राजंस्ताराजालमिवाम्बरात्॥
en: Cut off into a hundred fragments with the arrows of the son of Hridika, (the armour of Yudhishthira) ornamented with gold, fell down, scattered in that battle, O monarch (from its body) like a cluster of stars (dropping from) the sky.

sn: स च्छिन्नधन्वा विरथः शीर्णवर्मा शरार्दितः। अपायासीद् रणात् तूर्णं धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: With his coat of mail cut-off, deprived of his car and afflicted with the arrows of Krigavarma, Yudhishthira the son of Dharma, quickly withdrew from (the field of) battle.

sn: कृतवर्मा तु निर्जित्य धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। पुनर्दोणस्य जुगुपे चक्रमेव महात्मनः॥
en: Having defeated Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, the mighty car-warrior Kritavarma again engaged himself in protecting the carwheels of Drona.

sn: संजय उवाच
en: was an

sn: भूरिस्तु समरे राजशैनेयं रथिनां वरम्। आपतन्तमपासेधत् प्रयाणादिव कुञ्जरम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Bhuri also, 0 monarch, in (that) engagement, checked the grandson of Sini who rushing along like elephant (descending) from a gradually sloping ground.

sn: अथैनं सात्यकिः क्रुद्धः पञ्चभिर्निशितैः शरैः। विव्याध हृदये तस्य प्रास्रवत् तस्य शोणितम्॥
en: Inflamed with wrath, Satyaki, then, pierced him in the heart with five sharpened arrows. (Thus struck) his blood began to flow.

sn: तथैव कौरवो युद्धे शैनेयं युद्धदुर्मदम्। दशभिर्निशितैस्तीक्ष्णैरविध्यत भुजान्तरे॥
en: Similarly, the descendant of Kuru (i.e. Bhurij, in (that) engagement, quickly pierced the grandson of Sini invincible in battle, in the chest, with ten darts.

sn: तावन्योन्यं महाराज ततक्षाते शरैर्भृशम्। क्रोधसंरक्तनयनौ क्रोधाद् विस्फार्य कार्मुके॥
en: (And), O great king, their eyes blood-shot in rage and drawing their bows powerfully, those two (heroes) began to mangle each other.

sn: तयोरासीन्महाराज शस्त्रवृष्टिः सुदारुणा। क्रुद्धयोः सायकमुचोर्यमान्तकनिकाशयोः॥
en: Inflamed with wrath and looking like Death (itself) or the sun, those two (warriors commenced (to shower upon each other) terrible downpours of shafts, 0 mighty monarch.

sn: तावन्योन्यं और राजन् संछाद्य समवस्थितौ। मुहूर्तं चैव तद् युद्धं समरूपमिवाभवत्॥
en: The battle, O great king, between those two (heroes), who, covering each other (with arrows) stood (face to face) in (that) encounter, went on equally for a moment only.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज शैनेयः प्रहसन्निव। धनुश्चिच्छेद समरे कौरव्यस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, the grandson of Sini, fired with rage, cut-off, as it were, with a smile, the bow of that high-souled descendant of Kuru, in (that) engagement.

sn: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं नवभिर्निशितैः शरैः। विव्याध हृदये तूर्णं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Then he quickly pierced that (warrior) whose bow was cut-off, in the chest, with nine sharpened arrows and said (to him) “wait, wait."

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता शत्रुणा शत्रुतापनः। धनुरन्यत् समादाय सात्वतं प्रत्यविध्यत॥
en: That scorcher of foes, (thus) deeply pierced by his powerful antagonist, took up another bow and pierced Satvata in return.

sn: स विद्ध्वा सात्वतं बाणैसिभिरेव विशाम्पते। धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन सुतीक्ष्णेन हसन्निव॥
en: O lord of the earth, having pierced Satvata with three arrows, he cut-off his bow, as it were, with a smile, by means of a very keen and broad-headed shaft.

sn: छिन्नधन्वा महाराज सात्यकिः क्रोधमूर्छितः। प्रजहार महावेगां शक्तिं तस्य महोरसि॥
en: Ogreat king, his bow being (thus) cut-off, Satyaki, insensible with wrath, hurled an impetuous dart at the broad chest of that (Kuru hero).

sn: स तु शक्त्या विभिन्नाङ्गो निपपात रथोत्तमात्। लोहिताङ्ग इवाकाशाद् दीप्तरश्मिर्यदृच्छया॥
en: His body being riven by that dart, he fell down from his excellent car like the blazing Mars (dropping down) from the firmament.

sn: तं तु दृष्ट्वा हतं शूरमश्वत्थामा महारथः। अभ्यधावत वेगेन शैनेयं प्रति संयुगे॥
en: The mighty car-warrior Ashvatthama witnessing the slaughter of that hero, rushed impetuously, O descendant of Bharata, against the grandson of Shini.

sn: तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाभाष्य शैनेयं स नराधिप। अभ्यवर्षच्छरौघेण मेरुं वृष्ट्या यथाम्बुदः॥
en: O lord of men, saying “wait, wait' to Satyaki, he (i.e. Ashvatthama), covered him with downpours of arrows, like the clouds covering the breast of the (mountain) Meru with (showers of) rain.

sn: तमापतन्तं संरब्धं शैनेयस्य रथं प्रति। घटोत्कचोऽब्रवीद् राजन् नादं मुक्त्वा महारथः॥
en: (Thereupon), the mighty car-warrior Ghatotkacha, sending forth a loud shout, said to him (i.e., Ashvatthama) who was rushing furiously towards the car of the grandson of Shini.

sn: तिष्ठ तिष्ठ न मे जीवन् द्रोणपुत्र गमिष्यसि। एष त्वां निहनिष्यामि महिषं षण्मुखो यथा॥
en: “Wait, wait. O son of Drona, you shall not escape alive. I will presently destroy you as the six-faced (Kartikeya) slew the (Asura) Mahisha in days of yore).

sn: युद्धश्रद्धामहं तेऽद्य विनेष्यामि रणाजिरे। इत्युक्त्वा क्रोधताम्राक्षो राक्षसः परवीरहा।॥
en: I will today put an end to your desire for fight on the field of battle.” Saying this, the Rakshasa (Ghatotkacha), the slayer of hostile warriors-with his eyes red like copper in wrath.

sn: द्रौणिमभ्यद्रवत् क्रुद्धो गजेन्द्रमिव केसरी। रथाक्षमात्रैरिषुभिरभ्यवर्षद् घटोत्कचः॥
en: And inflamed with rage, rushed against the son of Drona like lion (rushing against) a lord of elephants. Ghatotkacha (then), began to shower arrows, measuring the Aksha of a car, upon.

sn: रथिनामृषभं द्रौणिं धाराभिरिव तोयदः। शरवृष्टिं तु तां प्राप्तां शरैराशीविषोपमैः॥ शातयामास समरे तरसा द्रौणिरुत्स्मयन्। ततः शरशतैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मर्मभेदिभिराशुगैः॥
en: The son of Drona, the foremost of carwarriors as the clouds (pour down) showers of rain. The son of Drona, however, in that engagement, quickly baffled that arrowy down pour by means of shafts resembling poisonous snakes. Then with a hundred keen darts, capable of piercing the vital parts and coursing rapidly.

sn: समाचिनोद् राक्षसेन्द्रं घटोत्कचमरिंदमम्। स शरैराचितस्तेन राक्षसो रणमूर्धनि॥
en: (He) pierced the subduer of foes, that is Ghatotkacha, the lord of the Rakshasas. The Rakshasa, thus pierced with shafts by him on the field of battle.

sn: व्यकाशत महाराज श्वाविच्छललतो यथा। ततः क्रोधसमाविष्टो भैमसेनिः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Looked, 0 great monarch, like the porcupine with its quills standing erect. Thereupon, the puissant son of Bhimasena, excited with rage.

sn: शरैरवचकर्तोगौणिं वज्राशनिप्रभैः। क्षुरप्रैरर्धचन्दैश्च नाराचैःसशिलीमुखैः॥ वराहकर्णैर्नालीकैर्विकर्णैश्चाभ्यवीवृषत्। तां शस्रवृष्टिमतुलां वज्राशनिसमस्वनाम्॥ पतन्तीमुपरि क्रुद्धो द्रौणिरव्यथितेन्द्रियः। सुदुःसहां शरै।रैर्दिव्यासप्रतिमन्त्रितैः॥ व्यधमत् सुमहातेजा महाभ्राणीव मारुतः। ततोऽन्तरिक्षे बाणानां संग्रामोऽन्य इवाभवत्॥
en: Lacerated the son of Drona with fierce shafts emitting loud roar like those of the thunder. (and Ghatotkacha) showered (upon Drona's son) numerous sorts of weapons, some having leads like razors, some of the form of the crescent, some long and pointed, some with faces like the frogs, some resembling the bear's ear, some barbed and some of other species. The son of Drona, (however), without his senses being in the least affected, frustrated that formidable down pour of weans emitting loud roar like those of the thunder and which were being unremittingly hurled (upon, him), by means of (his own) dreadful shafts inspired with mantras peculiar to the celestial weapons, as, O mighty monarch, the wind (chases away) mighty masses of clouds. Then it appeared that another encounter was going on in the firmament between the arrows (shot by those two rival heroes).

sn: घोररूपो महाराज योधानां हर्षवर्धनः। ततोऽस्रसंघर्षकृतैर्विस्फुलिङ्गैः समन्ततः॥
en: Which (encounter) was of terrible aspect and which, O great king, enhanced the joy of the combatants with the sparks scattering all around generated by the clash of weapons hurled by those two (warriors).

sn: बभौ निशामुखे व्योम खद्योतैरिव संवृतम्। स मार्गेणगणैौणिर्दिशः प्रच्छाद्य सर्वतः॥
en: The firmament looked (as beautiful) as if adorned with glow-worms during the night. Covering all the directions with innumerable arrows, the son of Drona.

sn: प्रियार्थं तव पुत्राणां राक्षसं समवाकिरत्। ततः प्रववृते युद्धं द्रौणिराक्षसयोर्मधे॥
en: In order to do good to your sons, shrouded the Rakshasa (Ghatotkacha). Then, between the son of Drona and the Rakshas, again took place a battle.

sn: विगाढे रजनीमध्ये शक्रप्रह्लादयोरिव। ततो घटोत्कचो बाणैर्दशभिौणिमाहवे॥ जधानोरसि संक्रुद्धः कालज्वलनसंनिभैः। स तैरभ्यायतैर्विद्धो राक्षसेन महाबलः॥ चचाल समरे द्रौणिवार्तनुन्न इव दुमः। स मोहमनुसम्प्राप्तो ध्वजयष्टिं समाश्रितः॥
en: During that pitchy-dark night, like that (which had taken place) between Shakra and Prahada (in days of yore). Then, in that engagement, Ghatotkacha, inflamed with wrath, struck the son of Drona in the chest with ten arrows resembling the Yuga fire. The son of Drona, endued with great strength (thus) deeply pierced in that encounter by the Rakshasa, became (greatly) afflicted and trembled like a tree shaken by the wind. Leaning against his flag-staff (for support), he fell into a swoon.

sn: ततो हाहाकृतं सैन्यं तव सव जनाधिप। हतं स्म मेनिरे सर्वे तावकास्तं विशाम्पते॥
en: Thereupon all your forces, O lord of men, set up a loud wail. (And) all your partisans, O lord of the earth, thought him to be dead.

sn: तं तु दृष्ट्वा तथावस्थमश्वत्थामानमाहवे। पञ्चाला: संजयाश्चैव सिंहनादं प्रचक्रिरे॥
en: Seeing Ashvatthama in that state, the Panchalas as well as the Srinjayas, in that encounter, sent forth roars like lions.

sn: प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञामश्वत्थामा महाबलः। धनुः प्रपीड्य वामेन करेणामित्रकर्शनः॥
en: Regaining his consciousness, that grinder of foes, the mighty car-warriors Ashvatthama, drawing powerfully his bow with the left hand.

sn: मुमोचाकर्णपूर्णेन धनुषा शरमुत्तमम्। यमदण्डोपमं घोरमुद्दिश्याशु घटोत्कचम्॥
en: Shot quickly from his bow, the string of which was) stretched up to the very ear, an excellent arrow, formidable as the rod of Yama, which was aimed at Ghatotkacha.

sn: स भित्त्वा हृदयं तस्य राक्षसस्य शरोत्तमः। विवेश वसुधामुग्रः सपुङ्खः पृथिवीपते॥
en: Riving the heart of the Rakshasa that excellent and formidable arrows, adorned with graceful wings, penetrated, o king, into the earth.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महाराज रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्। राक्षसेन्द्रः! सुबलवान् द्रौणिना रणशलिना॥
en: O great monarch, the puissant lord of the Rakshasas, pierced home by the son of Drona, proud of (his feats in) battle, sat down on the terrace of his car.

sn: दृष्ट्वा विमूढं हैडिम्बं सारथिस्तु रणाजिरात्। द्रौणे: सकाशात् सम्भ्रान्तस्त्वपनिन्ये त्वरान्वितः॥
en: Seeing that the son of Hidimva had lost his consciousness, his charioteer, struck with fear, hastily removed him from the field of battle and from the presence of the son of Drona.

sn: तथा तु समरे विद्ध्वा राक्षसेन्द्रं घटोत्कचम्। ननाद सुमहानादं द्रोणपुत्रो महारथः॥
en: Having, in that engagement, thus pierced Ghatotkacha, the lord of the Rakshasas, that great car-warrior, the son of Drona sent forth a highly dreadful roar.

sn: पूजितस्तव पुत्रैश्च सर्वयोधैश्च भारत। वपुषातिप्रजज्वाल मध्याह्न इव भास्करः॥
en: O Bharata, adored by your sons and all the warriors, his body shone brilliantly like the noon-day sun.

sn: भीमसेनं तु युध्यन्तं भारद्वाजरथं प्रति। स्वयं दुर्योधनो राजा प्रत्यविध्यच्छितैः शरैः॥
en: King Duryodhana himself pierced with keen arrows Bhimasena who was fighting his way, through your army, towards the car of the son of Bharadvaja.

sn: तं भीमसेनो दशभिः शरैर्विव्याध मारिष। दुर्योधनोऽपि विंशत्या शराणां प्रत्यविध्यत॥
en: O Bharata, Bhimasena pierced him in return with nine darts. Duryodhana also pierced him with twenty arrows.

sn: तौ सायकैरवच्छिन्नावदृश्येतां रणाजिरे। मेघजालसमाच्छन्नौ नभसीवेन्दुभास्करौ॥ 1४४॥
en: Those two (horses), shrouded with arrows on the field of battle, looked like the sun and the moon covered with masses of clouds in the firmament.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनो राजा भीमं विव्याध पत्रिभिः। पञ्चभिर्भरतश्रेष्ठ तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Then king Duryodhana pierced Bhima, O foremost of the descendants of Bharata, with five arrows and said (to him) “Wait, wait.”

sn: तस्य भीमो धनुश्छित्त्वा ध्वजं च दशभिः शरैः। विव्याध कौरवश्रेष्ठं नवत्या नवपर्वणाम्॥
en: But Bhima, cutting off his bow and his standard with sharpened arrows, pierced the lord of the Kauravas with nine straight darts.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः क्रुद्धो धनुरन्यन्महत्तरम्। गृहीत्वा भरतश्रेष्ठो भीमसेनं शितै शरैः॥ अपीडयद् रणमुखे पश्यतां सर्वधन्विनाम्। तान् निहत्य शरान् भीमो दुर्योधन धनुश्च्युतान्॥
en: Thereupon, O best of the Bharatas, excited with rage, Duryodhana took up another bow of a battle quality and began to afflict Bhimasena (stationed) at the front (rank) of that battle with keen darts, in the very sight of all bowman. Bhima, (however) destroying those arrows shot from Duryodhana's bow.

sn: कौरवं पञ्चविंशत्या क्षुद्रकाणां समार्पयत्। दुर्योधनस्तु संक्रुद्धो भीमसेनस्य मारिष॥ क्षुरप्रेण धनुश्छित्त्वा दशभिः प्रत्यविध्यत। अथान्यद् धनुरादाय भीमसेनो महाबलः॥
en: Oppressed him with five and twenty short arrows. Duryodhana also, O worshipfui sire, inflamed with ire, cut-off his bow with razorshaped dart and then pierced him in return with ten (darts). Thereupon, the highly-powerful Bhimasena, taking up another bow.

sn: विव्याध नृपतिं तूर्णं सप्तभिर्निशितैः शरैः। तदप्यस्य धनुः क्षिप्रं चिच्छेद लघुहस्तवत्॥
en: Pierced quickly the king with seven sharpened arrows. But he (i.e. Duryodhana), displaying great nimbleness of hand, quickly cut-off that bow also.

sn: द्वितीयं च तृतीयं च चतुर्थं पञ्चम तथा। आत्तमात्तं महाराज भीमस्य धनुराच्छिनत्॥ तव पुत्रो महाराज जितकाशी मदोत्कटः। स तथा भिद्यमानेषु कार्मुकेषु पुनः पुनः॥
en: Similarly, O mighty monarch, he cut-off the second, the third, the fourth and the fifty bows taken up by Bhima. And O great king, your son, desirous of success and swelling with pride, cut-off another bow as soon as it was taken up by Bhima. His bows being thus again and again cut-off (by Duryodhana) he i.e. Bhima.

sn: शक्तिं चिक्षेप समरे सर्वपारशवीं शुभाम्। मृत्योरिव स्वसारं हि दीप्तां वह्निशिखामिव॥ सीमन्तमिव कुर्वन्ती नभसोऽग्निसमप्रभाम्। आप्राप्तामेव तां शक्तिं त्रिधा चिच्छेद कौरवः॥
en: In that engagement, hurled a formidable dart, made wholly of iron (at the Kaurava king).-The king of the Kurus, (however), cut into three fragments that dart, before it could reach him, that dart blazing like a flame of fire, looking (terrible) like the sister of Death herself and dividing the firmament with its fire like splendour into two parts like the trees of a woman parting the hair of her head.

sn: पश्यतः सर्वलोकस्य भीमस्य च महात्मनः। ततो भीमो महाराज गदां गुर्वी महाप्रभाम्॥ चिक्षेपाविध्य वेगेन दुर्योधनस्थं प्रति। ततः सा सहसा वाहांस्तव पुत्रस्य संयुगे॥ सारथिं च गदा गुर्वी ममर्दास्य रथं पुनः। पुत्रस्तु तव राजेन्द्र भीमाद् भीतः प्रणश्य च॥
en: In the very presence of all the world and before (the very eyes) of Bhima himself. Thereupon, O great king, Bhima, flourishing his heavy and blazing mace, hurled it with great impetuosity at the car of Duryodhana. Then, in that engagement that heavy mace, all on a sudden, crushed the charioteer, the horses and the car (of the king). O lord of kings, your son, then afraid of Bhima, took to flight.

sn: आरुरोह रथं चान्यं नन्दकस्य महात्मनः। ततो भीमो हतं मत्वा तव पुत्रं महारथम्॥
en: Mounted on another car belonging to the high-souled Naduka. Then Bhima, thinking Suyodhana to be dead amid (the darkness of) that night.

sn: सिंहनादं महच्चक्रे तर्जयन् निशि कौरवान्। तावकाः सैनिकाश्चापि मेनिरे निहतं नृपम्। । ततोऽतिचुक्रुशुः सर्वे ते हाहेति समन्ततः॥
en: Roared furiously like a lion challenging the Kauravas. Your partisans and soldiers also thought that the king was slain.

sn: तेषां तु निनदं श्रुत्वा त्रस्तानां सर्वयोधिनाम्। भीमसेनस्य नादं च श्रुत्वा राजन् महात्मनः॥
en: And all of them set up a loud wail all around. Hearing the lamentation of all the coinbatants struck with terror.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिर राजा हतं मत्वा सुयोधनम्। अभ्यवर्तत वेगेन यत्र पार्थो वृकोदरः॥
en: And hearing also the yells of the highsouled Bhima, O monarch, king Yudhishthira, also, considered Suyodhana to have been slain.

sn: पञ्चाला: केकया मत्स्याः संजयाश्च विशाम्पते। सर्वोद्योगेनाभिजग्मुर्दोणमेव युयुत्सया॥
en: And hastened with all speed to the place where Vrikodara, the son of Pritha was. Then, the Panchalas, the Srinjayas, the Matsyas as well as the Keykeyas.

sn: तत्रासीत् सुमहद् युद्धं द्रोणस्याथ परैः सह। घोरे तमसि मग्नानां निजतामितरेतरम्॥
en: Desirous of slaying Drona, rushed with all their mighty (against him). There also took place a highly dreadful encounter between Drona and his enemies. And the combatants, (of both sides) buried in pitchy darkness, began to slaughter one another.

sn: संजय उवाच सहदेवमथायान्तं द्रोणप्रेप्सु विशाम्पते। कर्णो वैकर्तनो युद्धे वारयामास भारत॥
en: Sanjaya said Karna, the son of Vikartana, O king, checked in battle the great car-warrior Shahadeva who was advancing with the desire of slaying Drona.

sn: सहदेवस्तु राधेयं विद्ध्वा नवभिराशुगैः। पुनर्विव्याध दशभिर्विशिखैनतपर्वभिः॥२॥
en: Shahadeva, also piercing the son of Radha with nine arrows, pierced him again in that encounter with nine straight (shafts).

sn: तं कर्णः प्रतिविव्याध शतेन नतपर्वणाम्। सज्यं चास्य धनुः शीघ्रं चिच्छेद लघुहस्तवत्॥
en: Karna (also) pierced him in return with a hundred straight arrows and then with great light-handedness quickly cut-off his stringed bow.

sn: ततोऽन्यद् धनुरादाय माद्रीपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। कर्णं विव्याध विंशत्या तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Thereupon the puissant son of Madri taking up another bow, pierced Karna with twenty shafts and this appeared wonderful.

sn: तस्य कर्णो हयान हत्वा शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। सारथिं चास्य भल्लेन द्रुतं निन्ये यमक्षयम्॥
en: (Then) Karna, having destroyed his horses with straight shafts, quickly sent his charioteer, with a broad-headed dart, to the abode of Yama.

sn: विस्थः सहदेवस्तु खङ्ग चर्म समाददे। तदप्यस्य शरैः कर्णो व्यधमत् प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Made carless (thus), Shahadeva then took up a scimitar and a shield. But (Karma) cut-off those (things) also with a smile.

sn: अथ गुर्वी महाघोरां हेमचित्रां महागदाम्। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो वैकर्तनरथं प्रति॥
en: Thereupon the highly-puissant Shahadeva, in that engagement, hurled a heavy and formidable mace ornamented with gold, at the car of the son of Vikartana.

sn: तामापतन्ती सहसा सहदेवप्रचोदिताम्। व्यष्टम्भयच्छरैः कर्णो भूमौ चैनामपातयत्॥
en: Karna, however, cut-off with shafts that mace which, hurled by the Shahadeva, was making for him with great force and caused it to fall on the ground.

sn: गदां विनिहतां दृष्ट्वा सहदेवस्त्वरान्वितः। शक्तिं चिक्षेप कर्णाय तामप्यस्याच्छिनच्छरैः॥
en: Seeing that his cut-off, Shahadeva, with great haste, hurled a dart at mace was Karna. But that too was cut-off with arrows (by Karna).

sn: ससम्भ्रमं ततस्तूर्णमवप्लुत्य रथोत्तमात्। सहदेवो महाराज दृष्ट्वा कर्णं व्यवस्थितम्॥
en: The son of Madri, then, speedily jumping down from his excellent car and burning with indignation, as it were, at the sight of Karna stationed (before him).

sn: रथचक्रं प्रगृह्याजौ मुमोचाधिरथिं प्रति। तदापतद् वै सहसा कालचक्रमिवोद्यतम्॥
en: And taking up a car-wheel, discharged it at the son of Adhiratha. That (wheel), which was careering impetuously (towards him), like the upraised wheel of Death.

sn: शरैरनेकसाहस्रैराच्छिनत् सूतनन्दनः। तस्मिस्तु निहते चक्रे सूतजेन महात्मना।॥
en: Was cut-off by the charioteer's son with many thousands arrows. The car-wheel being thus cut to pieces, Shahadeva then, O worshipful sire.

sn: ईषादण्डकयोक्त्रांश्च युगानि विविधानि च। हस्त्यङ्गानि तथाश्वांश्च मृतांश्च पुरुषान् बहून्॥ चिक्षेप कर्णमुद्दिश्य कर्णस्तान् व्यधमच्छरैः। स निरायुधमात्मानं ज्ञात्वा साद्रवतीसुतः॥
en: Aiming at Karna, hurled at him the shaft of his car, the harnesses of his steeds, the yokes of cars, the limbs of elephants and horses and also dead human bodies. (But) Karna destroyed all these with shafts. Well aware that he had no weapons (to fight with), the son of Madri, that is.

sn: वार्यमाणस्तु विशिखैः सहदेवो रणं जहौ। तमभिद्रुत्य राधेयो मुहूर्ताद् भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Shahadeva, resisted with arrows (by Karna) withdrew from the battle. The son of Radha, (however), pursuing (and overtaking) him quickly in a moment, O best of the Bharatas.

sn: अब्रवीत् प्रहसन् वाक्यं सहदेवं विशाम्पते। मा युध्यस्व रणेऽधीर विशिष्टै रथिभिः सह॥
en: Addressed these very cruel words with a smile, to Shahadeva-"O iro, do not engage in fight with superior car-warriors.

sn: सदृशैयुध्य माद्रेय वचो मे मा विशङ्किथाः। अथैनं धनुषोऽग्रेण तुदन भूयोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: O son of Madri, you ought to fight with your equals (only). Do not mistrust my words." Then touching him with the end of his bow, he

sn: एषोऽर्जुनो रणे तूर्णं युध्यते कुरुभिः सह। तत्र गच्छस्व माद्रेय गृहं वा यदि मन्यसे॥
en: Yonder Arjuna is fighting resolutely with the Kurus. O son of Madri, either go there or return home, which ever you like.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु तं कर्णो रथेन रथिनां वरः। प्रायात् पाञ्चालपाण्डूनां सैन्यानि प्रदहन्निव॥
en: Having addressed him thus, Karna, the foremost of car-warriors, advanced smilingly against the troops of the Panchala king.

sn: वधं प्राप्तं तु माद्रेयं नावधीत् समरेऽरिहा। कुन्त्याः स्मृत्वा वचो राजन् सत्यसंधो महायशाः।। २०
en: Remembering the words of Kunti, that mighty car-warrior and slayer of foes in battle, firm in truth, did not, O king, slay the son of Madri though he could do so.

sn: सहदेवस्ततो राजन् विमना: शरपीडितः। कर्णवाक्छरतप्तश्च जीवितानिरविद्यत॥
en: With his mind ill at ease, afflicted with darts and smitten with the words of Karna (poignant) as darts, Shahadeva lost all love for life.

sn: आरुरोह रथं चापि पाञ्चाल्यस्य महात्मनः। जनमेजयस्य समरे त्वरायुक्ते महारथः॥
en: (And) that great car-warrior in that battle, with great haste mounted the car of Janamejaya, the high-souled Panchalas.

sn: संजय उवाच विराटं सहसेनं तु द्रोणं वै द्रुतमागतम्। मद्रराजः शरौघेण च्छादयामास धन्विनम्॥
en: Sanjaya said The king of Madra, with a down-pours of arrow, covered on all sides Virata, who, accompanied by his division, was proceeding quickly for (the slaughter ot) Drona.

sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं समरे दृढधन्विनोः। यादृशं ह्यभवद् राजञ्जम्भवासवयोः पुरा॥
en: (And) between those two strong bowmen ensued a battle, Oking, like that which had taken place between Bali and Vasava in days of yore.

sn: मद्रराजो महाराज विराटं वाहिनीपतिम्। आजने त्वरितस्तूर्णं शतेन नतपर्वणाम्॥
en: The king of Madra, O great monarch, displaying great alacrity, quickly wounded Virata, the chief of a great force, with straight arrows.

sn: प्रतिविव्याध तं राजन् नवभिर्निशितैः शरैः। पुनश्चैनं त्रिसप्तत्या भूयश्चैव शतेन तु॥
en: King (Virata also) pierced him in returm with nine sharpened arrows, again with seventy-three and once more with a hundred.

sn: तस्य मद्राधिपो हत्वा चतुरो स्थवाजिनः। सूतं ध्वजं च समरे शराभ्यां संन्यपातयत्॥
en: The king of Madra, (also) destroying the four horses of his car, cut down with two shafts, in that engagement, the umbrella and the standard (of Virata).

sn: हताश्वात् तु रथात् तूर्णमवप्लुत्य महारथः। तस्थौ विस्फारयंश्चापं विमुञ्चश्च शिताञ्छरान्॥
en: That lord of the earth (i.e., Virata) jumping down from his car, the steeds of which were destroyed, stood, drawing his bow and shooting keen darts.

sn: शतानीकस्ततो दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरं हतवाहनम्। रथेनाभ्यपतत् तूर्णं सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Witnessing the destruction of his brother's steeds, Shatanika quickly came up (there), in the very sight of all the troops.

sn: शतानीकमथायान्तं मद्रराजो महामृधे। विशिखैर्बहुभिर्विद्ध्वा ततो निन्ये यमक्षयम्॥
en: That lord of the earth, that is, the king of Madra, having with numerous shafts pierced Shatanika who was advancing (against him), sent him to the abode of Yama.

sn: तस्मिस्तु निहते वीरे विराटो रथसत्तमः। ततो विस्फार्य नयने क्रोधाद् द्विगुणविक्रमः। मद्रराजरथं तूर्णं छादयामास पत्रिभिः॥
en: The heroic (Shatanika) being slain, Virata, the chief of a great force, (abandoning his steed-less car, ascended to that (of his brother). Then, his eyes rolling (in ire) and his strength doubled with indignation, (he) quickly covered the car of the king of Madra with arrows.

sn: ततो मद्राधिपः क्रुद्धः शरेणानतपर्वणा। आजधानोरसि दृढं विराटं वाहिनीपतिम्॥
en: Therefore the king of Madra, inflamed with wrath, struck Virata, the chief of a large force, furiously in the chest with a hundred straight arrows.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महाराज रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्। कश्मलं चाविशत् तीव्र विराटो भरतर्षभ॥
en: The mighty car-warrior Virata thus pierced home by the puissant (Shalya) sat down on the terrace of his car and soon fainted away.

sn: सारथिस्तमपोवाह समरे शरविक्षतम्। ततः सा महती सेना प्राद्रवन्निशि भारत॥
en: His charioteer then bore him (i.e. Virata) away who was mangled with arrows in battle. Then, O Bharata, during that night, that large army (of Virata) began to take to flight.

sn: वध्यमाना शरशतैः शल्येनाहवशोभिना। तां दृष्ट्वा विद्रुतां सेनां वासुदेवधनंजयौ॥
en: Slaughtered with hundreds of arrows by Shalya, that ornament of battle, witnessing the flight of that army, Vasudeva and Dhananjaya.

sn: प्रयातौ तत्र राजेन्द्र यत्र शल्यो व्यवस्थितः। तौ तु प्रत्युद्ययौ राजन् राक्षसेन्द्रो ह्यलम्बुषः॥
en: Came to that spot, O king of kings, where Shalya was. Against them both, O king, advanced Alambusha, the lord of the Rakshasas. wide open

sn: अष्टचक्रसमायुक्तमास्थाय प्रवरं रथम्। तुरङ्गममुखैर्युक्तं पिशाचै?रदर्शनैः॥
en: Riding on an excellent eight-wheeled car drawn by terrible-looking Pishachas having faced like those of cows.

sn: लोहितार्द्रपताकं तं रक्तमाल्यविभूषितम्। कार्णायसमयं घोरमृक्षचर्मसमावृतम्॥
en: That terrible car was furnished with bloodred banners, adorned with garlands made of black iron and covered with bear skins.

sn: रौद्रेण चित्रपक्षण विवृताक्षेण कूजता। ध्वजेनोच्छ्रितदण्डेन गृध्रराजेन राजता॥
en: And it was furnished with a tall standard on which sat a fierce vulture of spotted wings, having eyes wide open and shrieking incessantly.

sn: स बभौ राक्षसो राजन् भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमः। रुरोधार्जुनमायान्त प्रभञ्जनमिवाद्रिराट्॥
en: That Rakshasa, who, O monarch, looked like a loose heap of antimony, checked the Aadvancing Arjuna as the mountain Meru (resists) a hurricane.

sn: किरन् बाणगणान् राजशतशोऽर्जुनमूर्धनि। अतितीवं महद् युद्धं नरराक्षसयोस्तदा॥
en: By incessant discharges of arrows, O king, on the head of Arjuna. The battle that commenced between the man (i.e. Arjuna) and the Rakshasa was exceedingly hot and furious.

sn: द्रष्ट्णां प्रीतिजननं सर्वेषां तत्र भारता मृध्रकाकबलोलूककङ्कगोमायुहर्षणम्॥
en: Causing delight to all the lookers on there, O Bharata and filling the vultures and the crows and the ravens and the owls and the Kankas and the jackals with joy.

sn: तमर्जुनः शतेनैव पत्रिणां समताडयत्। नवभिश्च शितैर्बाणैर्ध्वजं चिच्छेद भारत।॥
en: Arjuna, (then), struck Alamvusa with his arrows and with ten keen darts cut down his standard.

sn: सारथिं च त्रिभिर्बाणैसिभिरेव त्रिवेणुकम्। धनुरेकेन चिच्छेद चतुर्भिश्चतुरो हयान्॥
en: (And) with three darts he cut-off his charioteer, with three more his Trivenu, with one his bow and with four his horses.

sn: पुनः सज्यं कृतं चापं तदप्यस्य द्विधाच्छिनत्। विरथस्योद्यतं खङ्गं शरेणास्य द्विधाकरोत्॥ अथैनं निशितैर्बाणैश्चतुर्भिर्भरतर्षभ।
en: (The Rakshasa) took up another stringed bow again but (Arjuna) cut it off in two fragments. Then O foremost of the Bharatas, with four sharpened arrows.

sn: पार्थोऽविध्यद् राक्षसेन्द्रं स विद्धः प्राद्रवद् भयात्।।२४ तं विजित्यार्जुनस्तूर्णं द्रोणान्तिकमुपाययौ।
en: The son of Pritha pierced the lord of the Rakshasas, who, thus pierced, took to flight in terror. Having defeated him, Arjuna quickly advanced towards Drona.

sn: किरशरगणान् राजन् नरवारणवाजिषु॥ वध्यमाना महाराज पाण्डवेन यशस्विना।
en: Discharging numerous arrows, O king, at men, elephants and horses. O mighty monarch, slaughtered by that renowned Pandava.

sn: सैनिका न्यपतन्नुर्व्या वातुनुन्ना इव दुमाः॥ तेषु तूत्साद्यमानेषु फाल्गुनेन महात्मना। सम्प्राद्रवद् बलं सर्वं पुत्राणां ते विशाम्पते॥
en: The soldiers fell down like trees levelled (on the ground) by a storm. Thus slaughtered by that renowned Pandava all the soldiers (of your son) ran away like a terror-stricken herd of deer.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: संजय उवाच शतानीकं शरैस्तूर्णं निर्दहन्तं चमू तवा चित्रसेनस्तव सुतो वारयामास भारत॥
en: Sanjaya said O Bharata, your son Chitrasena withstood Satnika, the of Nakula, who consuming your troops with keen arrows. son was

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: नाकुलिचित्रसेनं तु विद्ध्वा पञ्चभिराशुगैः। स तु तं प्रतिविव्याध दशभिर्निशितैः शरैः॥
en: The son of Nakula pierced Chitrasena, with five arrows. He (i.e. Citrasena) also pierced him i.e. in return with ten sharpened arrows.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: चित्रसेनो महाराज शतानीकं पुनर्युधि। नवभिर्निशितैर्बाणैराजधान स्तनान्तरे॥
en: Once again, in that engagement Chitrasena, ( mighty monarch, pierced Satanika in the chest with nine keen darts.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: नाकुलिस्तस्य विशिखैवर्म संनतपर्वभिः। गात्रात् संच्यावयामास तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: The son of Nakula, (also), with straight arrows cut-off his armour from his body and this feat seemed marvellous.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: सोऽपेतवर्मा पुत्रस्ते विरराज भृशं नृप। उत्सृज्य काले राजेन्द्र निर्मोकमिव पन्नगः॥
