en: His armour being cut-off, your son O monarch, O lord of kings, looked as beautiful as a snake with its slough cast off in proper time.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: ततोऽस्य निशितैर्बाणैर्ध्वजं चिच्छेद नाकुलिः। धनुश्चैव महाराज यतमानस्य संयुगे॥
en: The, O great king, the son of Nakula, cutoff, with sharpened arrows, the standard and the bow of that one i.e., Chitrasena who was exerting his utmost in that engagement.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: स च्छिन्नधन्वा समरे विवर्मा च महारथः। धनुरन्यन्महाराज जग्राहारिविदारणम्॥
en: That mighty car-warrior, deprived of his car and coat of mail and his bow cut-off, took up another very strong bow capable of piercing every foe.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: ततस्तूर्णं चित्रसेनो नाकुलिं नवभिः शरैः। विव्याध समरे क्रुद्धो भरतानां महारथः॥
en: Then Chitrasena, that great car-warrior among the Bharatas, quickly pierced the son of Nakula, in battle, with straight arrows.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: शतानीकोऽथ संक्रुद्धश्चित्रसेनस्य मारिष। जघान चतुरो वाहान् सारथिं च नरोत्तमः॥
en: son The highly powerful Satanika, then inflamed with wrath, destroyed the four horses and also the charioteer of Chitrasena O Bharata.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: अवप्लुत्य रथात् तस्माचित्रसेनो महारथः। नाकुलिं पञ्चविंशत्या शराणामार्दयद् बली॥
en: Jumping down from his car, the highlyrenowned Chitrasena, possessed of (great) strength, oppressed the son of Nakula with twenty-five arrows.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तस्य तत्कुर्वतः कर्म नकुलस्य सुतो रणे। अर्धचन्द्रेण चिच्छेद चापं रत्नविभूषितम्॥
en: When he (i.e. Chitrasena) was achieving this feat, the of Nakula, in that engagement, cut-off, with a cresent-shaped arrow, his shaft furnished with gold.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: स च्छिन्नधन्वा विरथो हताश्वो हतसारथिः। आरुरोहं रथं तूर्णं हार्दिक्यस्य महात्मनः॥
en: His bow cut-off and deprived of his car, steeds and charioteer, he (i.e. Chitrasena) quickly mounted on the car of the high-souled son of Hridika.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: दुपदं तु सहानीकं द्रोणप्रेप्सुं महारथम्। वृषसेनोऽभ्ययात् तूर्णं किरशरशतैस्तदा॥
en: Then, O great king, Vrishasena, covered that great car-warrior Drupada, who, followed by his army, was advancing against Drona.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: यज्ञसेनस्तु समरे कर्णपुत्रं महारथम्। षष्ट्या शराणां विव्याध बाह्वोरुरसि चानघ॥
en: Yajnasena also, O lord, pierced in that battle, that mighty car-warrior, the son of Karna, in the arm and the chest with six arrows.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: वृषसेनस्तु संक्रुद्धो यज्ञसेनं रथे स्थितम्। बहुभिः सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैराजघान स्तनान्तरे॥
en: Thereupon inflamed with wrath, Vrishasena soon struck Yajnasena, stationed on his car, in the centre of his chest with numerous arrows.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तावुभौ शरनुन्नाङ्गो शरकण्टकितौ रणे। व्यभ्राजेतां महाराज श्वाविधौ शललैरिव॥
en: O great king, those two heroes mangled with shafts and their bodies looking prickly with the darts sticking io them, looked beautiful like a couple of hedgehogs with their quills erect on their bodies, in that encounter.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: रुक्मपुजैः प्रसन्नाग्रैः शरैश्छिन्नतनुच्छदौ। रुधिरौघपरिकिनौ व्यभ्राजेतां महामृधे॥
en: Covered all over with blood flowing from the wounds caused by straight arrows furnished with golden wings and keen points, those two warriors in that great engagement, looked beautiful.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तपनीयनिभौ चित्रौ कल्पवृक्षाविवाद्धातौ। किंशुकाविव चोत्फुल्लौ व्यकाशेतां रणाजिरे॥
en: Like a pair of highly graceful and radiant Kalpa trees or a couple of Kinsuka trees rich with their burden of flowers.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: वृषसेनस्ततो राजन् दुपदं नवभिः शरैः। विद्ध्वा विव्याध सप्तत्या पुनरन्यैस्रिभित्रिभिः॥
en: Vrishasena them, o king, having pierced Drupada with nine arrows, pierced him again with seventy and once more with another three shafts.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: ततः शरसहस्राणि विमुञ्चन् विवभौ तदा। कर्णपुत्रो महाराज वर्षमाण इवाम्बुदः॥
en: Then, discharging thousands of arrows in that battle, the son of Karna, O mighty monarch, looked like cloud pouring torrents of rain.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: दुपदस्तु ततः क्रुद्धो वृषसेनस्य कार्मुकम्। द्विधा चिच्छेद भल्लेन पीतेन निशितेन च॥
en: Thereupon, Drupada, excited with wrath, cut-off the bow of Vrishasena into fragments by means of a sharpened and well-tempered broad-headed arrow.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय रुक्मबद्धं नवं दृढम्। तूणादाकृष्य विमलं भल्लं पीतं शितं दृढम्॥
en: He (then) taking up another new and strong bow, plaited with gold and taking out of his quiver a shinning, well-tempered, strong, keen and broad-headed dart.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: कार्मुके योजयित्वा तं दुपदं संनिरीक्ष्य च। आकर्णपूर्ण मुमुचे त्रासयन् सर्वसोमकान्॥
en: And adjusting it to the string and aiming at Drupada and drawing (his bow-string) up to the very ear, discharged it, striking terror into (the hearts of all the Somakas.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: हृदयं तस्य भित्त्वा च जगाम वसुधातलम्। कश्मलं प्राविशद् राजा वृषसेनशराहतः॥
en: (That dart) riving his heart penetrated into the earth. The king (Drupada), thus wounded by Vrishasena, with dart, fell into a swoon.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: सारथिस्तमपोवाह स्मरन् सारथिचेष्टितम्। तस्मिन् प्रभग्ने राजेन्द्र पञ्चालानां महारथे॥
en: Remembering the duty of (all) charioteers, his driver bore him away. O lord of kings, that great car-warrior among the Panchalas being (thus) defeated.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: ततस्तु दुपदानीकं शरैश्छिन्नतानुच्छदम्। सम्प्राद्रवत् तदा राजन् निशीथे भैरवे सति॥
en: All the warriors (on your side), on that frightful night, rushed against the army of Drupada having their coats of mail cut to pieces with arrows (of the enemy).

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: प्रदीपैर्हि परित्यक्तैर्व्वलद्भिस्तैः समन्ततः। व्यराजत मही राजन् वीताभ्रा द्यौरिव ग्रहैः॥
en: In virtue of the (lustre of the) lamps abandoned (by the combatants) and which were burning all around, the field shone resplendent like the cloud-less firmament studded with planets and stars.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तथाङ्गदैर्नियतितैर्व्यराजत वसुंधरा। प्रावृट्काले महाराज विद्युद्भिरिव तोयदः॥
en: Similarly, O great king, (strewn all over) with the fallen Angadas of the combatants, the field looked beautiful like a (mass of) clouds (enlivened) with flashes of lightning during the rainy season.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तत: कर्णसुतात् त्रस्ताः सोमका विप्रदुद्रवुः। यथेन्द्रभयवित्रस्ता दानवास्तारकामये॥
en: Then, seized with the fear of the son of Karna, (the Panchalas troops) ran away in all directions as the Danavas agitated with the fear of Indra (had fled away) in the battle between the gods and the Asuras.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तेनार्यमानाः समरे द्रवमाणाश्च सोमकाः। व्यराजन्त महाराज प्रदीपैरवभासिताः॥
en: Crushed in that battle by him (i.e. Vrishasena) the Panchalas together with the Somakas, illuminated by lamps, shone resplendent.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तांस्तु निर्जित्य समरे कर्णपुत्रोऽप्यरोचत। मध्यंदिनमनुप्राप्तो धर्मांशुरिव भारत॥
en: Having, O Bharata, defeated them in battle, the son of Karna, looked like the sun of scorching rays when he reaches the meridian.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तेषु राजसहस्रेषु तावकेषु परेषु च। एक एव ज्वलंस्तस्थौ वृषसेनः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Amongst the thousands of kings belonging to your party and that of your enemy, the puissant Vrishasena alone stood (on the field) like the blazing fire.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: स विजित्य रणे शूरान् सोमकानां महारथान्। जगाम त्वरितस्तत्र यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Having vanquished (innumerable) horses as well as those great car-warriors the Somakas, he (i.e. Vrishasena) hastened to the spot where king Yudhishthira was.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: प्रतिविन्ध्यमथ क्रुद्धं प्रदहन्तं रणे रिपून्। दुःशासनस्तव सुतः प्रत्यगच्छनमहारथः॥
en: Your son Dushasana stood against that mighty car-warrior, the advancing Prativindhya, consuming his enemies in battle.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तयोः समागमो राजंश्चित्ररूपो बभूव ह। व्यपेतजलद व्योम्नि बुधभास्करयोरिव॥
en: O king, the clash between looked as marvellous as that between Mercury and Venus in the cloudless sky.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: प्रतिविन्ध्यं तु समरे कुवार्णं कर्म दुष्करम्। दुःशासनसिभिर्बाणैर्ललाटे समविध्यत॥
en: In (that) battle, Prativindhya, who was achieving frightful feats, was pierced by Dushasana in the forehead with three arrows.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता तव पुत्रेण धन्विना। विरराज महाबाहुः सशृङ्ग इव पर्वतः॥
en: Pierced deeply by that powerful bcwman, that is, your son, Prativindhya, O mighty monarch, looked like a mountain furnished with a peak.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: दुःशासनं तु समरे प्रतिविन्धयो महारथः। नवभिः सायकैर्विद्धवा पुनर्विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: The great car-warrior Prativindhya (also), in (that) battle, having pierced Dushasana with nine arrows, pierced him again with seven.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तत्र भारते पुत्रस्ते कृतवान् कर्म दुष्करम्। प्रतिविध्यहयानुप्रैः पातयामास सायकैः॥
en: There, O Bharata, your son performed a difficult feat in as much as he struck down the steeds of Prativindhya with fierce shafts.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: सारथिं चास्य भल्लेन ध्वजं च सतपातयत्। रथं च तिलशो राजन् व्यधमत् तस्य धन्विनः॥
en: (He then), with a broad-headed shaft, O king, struck down the charioteer and the standard and cut-off into minute fragments the car of that bowman.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: पताकाश्च सतूणीरा रश्मीन् योक्त्राणि च प्रभो। चिच्छेद तिलश: क्रुद्धः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: (And), inflamed with rage (he) cut-off into very small fragments, with straight arrows, the flags, the quivers, the strings and the terraces, O lord, (of Prativindhya,s) car.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: विरथः स तु धर्मात्मा धनुष्पाणिरवस्थितः। अयोधयत् तव सुतं किरशरशतान् बहून्॥
en: Made carless, the virtuous-souled (Prativindhya) stood, bow in hand and fought with your son by discharging many hundreds of shafts.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: क्षुरप्रेण धनुस्तस्य चिच्छेद तनयस्तव। अथैनं दशभिर्बाणैश्छिन्नधन्वानमार्दयत्॥
en: Your son, then) with (great) nimbleness of hand cut-off his bow with a razor-shaped arrow and then smote that one whose bow was cutoff, with ten darts.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा विस्थं तत्र भ्रातरोऽस्य महारथाः। अन्ववर्तन्त वेगेन महत्या सेनया सह॥
en: Witnessing that (sad) plight that their brother was in, his brothers, who were great car-warriors, followed by a large army, rushed furiously to that place.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: आप्लुतः स ततो यानं सुतसोमस्य भास्वरम्। धनुर्गृह्य महाराज विव्याध तनयं तव॥
en: He then mounted the resplendent car of Sutasoma and O great king, taking up a bow, pierced your son.

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: ततस्तु तावकाः सर्वे परिवार्य सुतं तव। अभ्यवर्तन्त संग्रामे महत्या सेनया वृताः॥
en: Thereupon, all your warriors surrounding your son (in order to protect him) and followed by a great force, rushed (against the Pandavas).

description: The fight by Satnika and others
sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तव तेषां च भारत। निशीथे दारुणे काले यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनम्॥
en: Then, at that frightful hour of midnight, there commenced an encounter swelling (the population of) Yama's domains between your (army) and theirs.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: संजय उवाच नकुलं रभसं युद्धे निघ्नतं वाहिनी तव। अभ्ययात् सौबलः क्रुद्धस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said The son of Subala (i.e. Shakuni), excited with wrath, rushed against Nakula who was slaughtering your troops with (great) impetuosity in battle and said (to him) “Wait, wait."

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: कृतवैरौ तु तौ वीरावन्योन्यवधकाङ्क्षिणौ। शरैः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैरन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः॥
en: Those two heroes, between whom was excited a bitter enmity, desirous of slaying each other, struck each other with arrows discharged (from their bows) drawn to their fullest stretch.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: यथैव नकुलो राजन् शरवर्षाण्यमुञ्चत्। तथैव सोबलश्चापि शिक्षा संदर्शयन् युधि॥
en: In (that) battle, O king, the son of Subala displayed as much dexterity in discharging showers of arrows as Nakula (god).

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: तावुभौ समरे शूरौ शरकण्टकिनौ तदा। व्यराजेतां महाराज श्वाविधौ शललैरिव॥
en: With arrows stricking (to their bodies) like prickly thorms, they, O mighty monarch, looked, in (that) engagement, like a couple of porcupines with erect quills.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: रुक्मपुरजिह्माणैः शरैश्छिन्नतनुच्छदौ। रुधिरौघपरिक्किन्नौ व्यभ्राजेतां महामृधे॥
en: Their coats of mail cut-off with shafts having straight points and wings of gold and themselves covered all over with blood, (those two heroes) looked as beautiful as.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: तपनीयनिभौ चित्रौ कल्पवृक्षाविव दुमौ। किंशुकाविव चोत्फुल्ली प्रकाशेते रणाजिरे॥
en: A fair of beautiful Kalpa trees or a couple of handsome Kinsuka trees laden with flowers, on the field of battle.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: तावुभैः समरे शूरौ शरकण्टकिनौ तदः। व्यराजेता महाराज कण्टकैरिव शाल्मलीः॥
en: Then, O great king, both the heroes pierced with shafts (sticking to their bodies) looked beautiful like a couple of Salmali trees (covered) with prickly thorns.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: सुजिप्तां प्रेक्षमाणौ च राजन् विवृतलोचनौ। क्रोधसंरक्तनयनौ निर्दहन्तौ परस्परम्॥
en: O king, looking delightedly at each other with expanded eyes which became red in wrath, they seemed to consume each other (with their fiery glances).

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: श्यालस्तु तव संक्रुद्धो माद्रीपुत्रं हसन्निव। कर्णिनैकेन विव्याध हृदये निशितेन ह॥
en: Inflamed with wrath, your brother-in-law, pierced, as it were with a smile, the son of Madri in the chest with keen and barbed dart.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: नकुलस्तु भृशं विद्धः श्यालेन तव धन्विना। निषसाद रथोपस्थे कश्मलं चाविशन्महत्॥
en: Your brother-in-law wielder of bow, wounded Nakula extremely. He fell down on his chariot and filled with very grief.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: अत्यन्तवैरिणं दृप्तं दृष्ट्वा शत्रु तथागतम्। ननाद शकुनी राजंस्तपान्ते जलदो यथा॥
en: Beholding his bitter and haughty foe in that (pitiable) plight, Shakuni roared there like the clouds at the end of summer.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञां नकुलः पाण्डुनन्दनः। अभ्ययात् सौबलं भूयो व्यात्तानन इवान्तकः॥
en: Then, Nakula, the son of Pandu, recovering his senses once again rushed against the son of Subala like death itself with gaping mouth.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: संक्रुद्धः शकुनि षष्ट्या विव्याध भरतर्षभा पुनश्चैनं शतेनैव नाराचानां स्तनान्तरे॥
en: He, (then), O best of the Bharatas, wrathfully pierced Shakuni with six (arrows) and again with a hundred long shafts, in the centre of the chest.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: अथास्य सशरं चापं मुष्टिदेशेऽच्छिनत् तदा। ध्वजं च त्वरितं छित्त्वा रथाद् भूमावपातयत्॥
en: (He then cut-off) his bow with the arrow fixed (on the string) into two fragments, at the points at which it is grasped. (Then), quickly cutting off his standard, (he) caused it to fall from his car to the ground.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: विशिखेन च तीक्ष्णेन पीतेन निशितेन च। ऊरू निर्भिद्य चैकेन नकुलः पाण्डुनन्दनः॥
en: Nakula, the son of Pandu, (then), having pierced his thigh with a sharpened, will tempered and keen dart.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: श्येनं सपक्षं व्याधेन पातयामास तं तदा। सोऽतिविद्धो महाराज रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्॥
en: Caused him to fall down as a hunter (causes) a winged hawk to drop down. O great king, (thus) pierced deeply, he sark down on the terrace of his car.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: ध्वजयष्टिं परिक्तिश्य कामुकः कामिनी यथा। तं विसंज्ञं निपतितं दृष्ट्वा श्यालं तवानघ॥
en: Clasping the flag-staff, like a lustful person (embracing) his lady-love. O sinless one, seeing your brother-in-law lose his senses and drop down.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: अपोवाह रथेनाशु सारथिर्ध्वजिनीमुखात्। ततः संचुक्रुशुः पार्था ये च तेषां पदानुगाः॥
en: His charioteer quickly carried him away on his car from the van of battle. Then sons of Pritha and all those who followed them gave utterance to a loud roar.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: निर्जित्य च रणे शत्रु नकुलः शत्रुतापनः। अब्रवीत् सारथिं क्रुद्धो द्रोणानीकाय मां वह॥
en: On the defeat of his foe in battle, Nakula. the scorcher of foes, said to his charioteer "convey me towards Drona's division."

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा माद्रीपुत्रस्य सारथिः। प्रायात् तेन तदा राजन् यत्र द्रोणो व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Hearing those words of the son of Madri, his charioteer, conveyed him to the spot where, O king, Drona took his stand.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: शिखण्डिनं तु समरे द्रोणप्रेप्सुं विशाम्पते। कृपः शारद्वतो यत्तः प्रत्यगच्छत् सवेगितः॥
en: Kripa, the son of Saradvata, rushed with great impetuosity and resoluteness, against the highly-powerful Sikhandi who was advancing in order to slay Drona.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: गौतमं द्रुतमायान्तं द्रोणानीकमरिंदमम्। विव्याध नवभिर्भल्लैः शिखण्डी प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Sikhandi, the subduer of foes, pierced as it were with a smile the son of Goutama advancing furiously (again him) towards the vicinity of Drona, with nine arrows.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: तमाचार्यो महाराज विद्ध्वा पञ्चभिराशुगैः। पुनर्विव्याध विंशत्या पुत्राणां प्रियकृत् तव॥
en: The preceptor, devoted to the welfare of your sons, having, O great monarch, pierced him with five shafts, struck him again with twenty (more).

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: महद् युद्धं तयोरासीद् घोररूपं भयानकम्। यथा देवासुरे युद्धे शम्बरामरराजयोः॥
en: (Then), O lord of the earth, the encounter that ensued between them was as dreadful as that between the (Asura) Samvara and the lord of the immortals in the war between the celestials and the Asuras.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: शरजालावृतं व्योम चक्रतुस्तौ महारथौ। मेघाविव तपापाये वीरौ समरदुर्मदौ॥
en: Invincible in battle, those two heroic and great car-warrior covered the firmament with arrowy nets like the clouds (covering the sky) at the end of summer,

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: प्रकृत्या घोररूपं तदासीद् घोरतरं पुनः। रात्रिश्च भरतश्रेष्ठ योधानां युद्धशालिनाम्॥
en: That night which was naturally of a terrible aspect became more dreadful, o best of the Bharatas, to the combatants engaged in battle.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: कालरात्रिनिभा ह्यासीद् घोररूपा भयानका। शिखण्डी तु महाराज गौतमस्य महद् धनुः॥ अर्धचन्द्रेण चिच्छेद सज्यं सविशिखं तदा। तस्य क्रुद्धः कृपो राजशक्तिं चिक्षेप दारुणाम्॥
en: That awfully-dreadful night striking terror (into very heart) seemed to be the death-night (of all the combatants). Then, O great monarch, Shikandi cut-off the great bow of the son of Goutama with a crescent-shaped (dart) and poured down sharpened arrows (at him). Kripa, then, O monarch, excited with rage, hurled a formidable dart.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: स्वर्णदण्डामकुण्ठाग्रां कर्मारपरिमार्जिताम्। तामापतन्तीं चिच्छेद शिखण्डी बहुभिः शरैः॥
en: Furnished with a golden handle, having keen point and polished by a black-smith. (But) Shikhandin severed it, as it was making for him, with ten darts.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: साऽपतन्मेदिनी दीप्ता भासयन्ती महाप्रभा। अथान्यद् धनुरादाय गौतमो रथिनां वरः॥
en: That dart ornamented with gold, dropped down to the ground. Thereupon, the son of Goutama, that best of speakers, taking up a fresh bow.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: प्राच्छादयच्छितैर्बाणैर्महाराज शिखण्डिनम्। च च्छाद्यमानः समरे गौतमेन यशस्विना॥
en: Covered Shikhandin, Ogreat monarch, with sharpened arrows. (Thus) covered (with shafts) by the high-souled son of Goutama in that battle.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: न्यषीदत रथोपस्थे शिखण्डी रथिनां वरः। सीदन्तं चैनमालोक्य कृपः शारद्वतो युधि॥
en: Shikhandin, the foremost of car-warriors, sank down exhausted on the terrace of his car. Kripa, the son of Saradvata, seeing himself exhausted in that engagement.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: आजघ्ने बहुभिर्वाणैर्जिघांसन्निव भारत। विमुखं तु रणे दृष्ट्वा याज्ञसेनिं महारथम्॥
en: Struck him with numerous arrows, 0 Bharata, (actuated) with the desire of slaying him. Witnessing defeat of that great carwarrior, the son of Jajnasena in battle.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: पञ्चाला: सोमकाश्चैव परिव्रवुः समन्ततः। तथैव तव पुत्राश्च परिवर्द्धिजोत्तमम्॥
en: The Panchalas as well as the Somakas surrounded him on all sides (for rescuing him). In like manner, your sons also surrounded that excellent Brahmana.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: महत्या सेनया सार्धं ततो युद्धमवर्तत। स्थानां च रणे राजन्नन्योन्यमभिधावताम्॥
en: With a vast force. Then there took place a battle again, o king, between car-warriors engaged in striking one another.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: बभूव तुमुलः शब्दो मेघानां गर्जतामिव। द्रवतां सादिनां चैव गजानां च विशाम्पते। ३६॥
en: And O lord of the earth, O Bharata, there arose a tumultuous uproar, like the roar of the clouds, as the horse-man and elephants rushed against.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: अन्योन्यमभितो राजन् क्रूरमायोधनं बभौ। पत्तीनां द्रवतां चैव पादशब्देन मेदिनी॥
en: And slaughtered one another. The battle, the. 0 monarch, became terrific. In consequence of the tread of foot-soldiers rushing along, the earth.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: अकम्पत महाराज भयत्रस्तेव चाङ्गना। रथिनो रथमारुह्य प्रदुता वेगवत्तरम्॥
en: O great king, began to tremble like an affrighted lady. Ascending their cars, carwarriors rushed furiously against.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: अगृह्णन् बहवो राजशलभान् वायसा इव। तथा गजान् प्रभिन्नांश्च सम्प्रभिन्ना महागजाः॥ तस्मिन्नेव पदे यत्ता निगृह्णन्ति स्म भारत। सादी सादिनपासाद्य पत्तयश्च पदातिनम्॥
en: And, O king, attacked numerous (other carwarriors), as crows (attack) winged insects. In the same manner, elephants, with the juice trickling down their bodies, resolutely attacked great elephants (of the opposite side) with juice trickling down their bodies, O Bharata. Horsemen approaching horsemen and foot soldiers (approaching) foot soldiers.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: समासाद्य रणेऽन्योन्यं संरब्धा नातिचक्रमुः। धावतां द्रवतां चैव पुनरावर्ततामपि॥ बभूव तत्र सैन्यानां शब्दः सुविपुलो निशि। दीप्यमानाः प्रदीपाश्च रथवारणवाजिषु॥
en: In that battle, angrily encountered one another, without getting the better of one another. Terrific indeed as the sound caused by the rush, retreat and return of the combatants at dead of night. (Innumerable) blazing lamps placed upon cars, elephants and horses.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: अदृश्यन्त महाराज महोल्का इव खाच्च्युताः। सा निशा भरतश्रेष्ठ प्रदीपैरवभासिता॥
en: Looked, O great king, like large meteors drooping from the firmament. O foremost of the Bharatas, that night blazed up by those lamps.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: दिवसप्रतिमा राजन् बभूव रणमूर्धनि। आदित्येन यथा व्याप्तं तमो लोके प्रणश्यति॥
en: Looked as (bright as) day, O king, on the field of battle. As the sun dispels dense darkness hanging all over.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: तथा नष्टं तमो घोरं दीपैर्दीप्तरितस्ततः। द्योश्चैव पृथिवी चापि दिशश्च प्रदिशस्तथा॥
en: So that pitchy darkness pervading the field of battle was destroyed by those blazing lamps. The firmament, the earth, the cardinal and the minor points.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: रजसा तमसा व्याप्ता द्योतिताः प्रभया पुनः। अस्त्राणां कवचानां च मणीनां च महात्मनाम्॥
en: (Hitherto) buried in darkness and dust, again blazed with the lustre (of those lamps). The lustre of weapons, armours and gems belonging to the high-souled (combatants).

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: अन्तर्दधुः प्रभाः सर्वा दीपैस्तैरवभासिताः। तस्मिन् कोलाहले युद्धे वर्तमाने निशामुखे॥
en: Was cast into shade by the light of those blazing (lamps), when during that night, the battle was raging hot and furious.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: न किंचिद् विदुरात्मानमयमस्मीति भारत। अवधीत् समरे पुत्रं पिता भरतसत्तम्॥
en: No one of the combatants could distinguish the men of his party, O Bharata. (And) O best of the Bharatas, in (that) battle, father killed (his) son.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: पुत्रश्च पितरं मोहात् सखायं च सखा तथा। स्वस्नीयं मातुलश्चापि स्वस्रीयश्चापि मातुलम्॥
en: Son (his) father and kinsmen (killed kinsmen, friends (slew) friends and maternal uncles (killed) sister's sons, through ignorance.

description: The hand of hand nocturnal fight
sn: स्वे स्वान् परे परांश्चापि निजत्रुरितरेतरम्। निर्मर्यादमभूद् युद्धं रात्रौ भीरुभयानकम्॥
en: (And) O Bharata, warrior killed warriors of the same party and enemies killed their own O king, in that awful nocturnal engagement (the combatants) lost all regard for one another. men.

sn: संजय उवाच तस्मिन् सुतुमले युद्धे वर्तमाने भयावहे। धृष्टद्युम्नो महाराज द्रोणमेवाभ्यवर्तत॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O mighty monarch, when the battle raged hot and furious Dhristadyumna rushed against Drona.

sn: संदधानो धनुःश्रेष्ठं ज्यां विकर्षन् पुनः पुनः। अभ्यद्रवत द्रोणस्य रथं रुक्मविभूषितम्॥
en: Wielding his strong bow and twanging its string often and often, he rushed against Drona's chariot decked with golden trappings.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नमथायान्तं द्रोणस्यान्तचिकीर्षया। परिववर्महाराज पञ्चालाः पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: And as Dhristadyumna rushed against Drona, O mighty monarch, the Panchalas together with the Pandavas surrounded him, with a view to put an end to Drona's life.

sn: तथा परिवृतं दृष्व द्रोणमाचार्यसत्तमम्। पुत्रास्ते सर्वतो यत्ता ररक्षुर्दोणमाहवे॥
en: Then beholding that foremost of preceptors Drona, thus hemmed in on all sides, your sons, exerting their best, protected Drona in that battle.

sn: बलार्णवौ ततस्तौ तु समेयातां निशामुखे। वातोधूतौ क्षुब्धसत्त्वौ भैरवौ सागरविव॥
en: Then those two sea of troops encountering each other at the dead of night resembled two dreadful sees agitated by the tempest with all the creatures within them dreadfully terrified.

sn: ततो द्रोणं महाराज पाञ्चाल्यः पञ्चभिः शरैः। विव्याध हृदये तूर्णं सिंहनादं ननाद च॥
en: Thereafter, O king, the prince of the Panchalas quickly pierced Drona on the breast with five arrows and then uttered his war-cry.

sn: तं द्रोणः पञ्चविंशत्या विद्ध्वा भारत संयुगे। चिच्छेदान्येन भल्लेन धनुरस्य महास्वनम् ॥
en: Thereupon, O Bharata, Drona piercing him with twenty-five shafts, cut-off his lustrous bow with another broad-headed shaft.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु निर्विद्धो द्रोणेन भरतर्षभ। उत्ससर्ज धनुस्तूर्णं संदश्य दशनच्छदम्॥
en: Pierced sore by Drona, Dhristadyumna, O foremost of the Bharatas, threw quickly aside the (severed) bow and bit his lips (in anger).

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज धृष्टद्युम्नः प्रतापवान्। आददेऽन्यद् धनुःश्रेष्ठं द्रोणस्यान्तचिकीर्षया॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, excited to his highest pitch of fury, the puissant Dhristadyumna grasped another strong bow, desirous of accomplishing Drona's destruction.

sn: विकृष्य च धनुश्चित्रमाकर्णात् परवीरहा। द्रोणस्यान्तकरं घोरं व्यसृजत् सायकं ततः॥
en: That handsome warrior, the slayer of his foes, then drawing back the string of that bow to his cars, let go a dreadful shaft capable of achieving Drona's destruction.

sn: स विसृष्टो बलवता शरो घोरो महामृधे। भासयामास तत् सैन्यं दिवाकर इवोदितः॥
en: In that terrible battle that shaft, shot by his strong arm, flooded the Kuru troops with its lustre like the risen sun.

sn: तं तु दृष्ट्वा शरं घोरं देवगन्धर्वमानवाः। स्वस्त्यस्तु समरे राजन् द्रोणायेत्यब्रुवन् वचः॥
en: Beholding that dreadful shaft, o king, the Gods, the Danavas and the Gandharvas said these words viz., “May good betide Drona."

sn: तं तु सायकमायान्तमाचार्यस्य रथं प्रति। कर्णो द्वादशधा राजंश्चिच्छेद कृतहस्तवत्॥
en: Then as that shaft coursed towards the chariot of Drona, Oking Karna like one endued with great lightness of hands, cut it off into twelve fragments.

sn: च च्छिन्नो बहुधा राजन् सूतपुत्रेण धन्विना। निपपात शरस्तूर्णं निर्विषो भुजगो यथा॥
en: () king, that shaft of Dhristadyumna severed into numerous pieces, quickly fell down on the earth like, O sire, a snake without its poisonous fangs.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं ततः कर्णो विव्याध दशभिः शरै। पञ्चभिट्टैणपुत्रस्तुं स्वयं द्रोणस्तु सप्तभिः॥
en: In that battle, cutting off arrows with his own close-knotted shafts, Karna then began to pierce Dhristadyumna with sharp arrows.

sn: शल्यश्च दशभिर्बाणैत्रिभिर्दुःशासनस्तथा। दुर्योधनस्तु विंशत्या शकुनिश्चापि पञ्चभिः॥
en: Drona's son pierced Dhristadyumna with five, Drona himself with five, Shalya with nine and Dushasana with three Vallas.

sn: पाञ्चाल्यं त्वरयाविध्यन् सर्व एव महारथाः। स विद्धः सप्तभिवीरैर्दोणस्यार्थे महाहवे॥
en: Duryodhana pierced him with twenty and Shakuni with five arrows. Thus all the mighty car-warriors (of your army) quickly pierced the Panchala prince.

sn: सर्वानसम्भ्रमाद् राजन् प्रत्यविद्ध्यत् त्रिभित्रिभिः। द्रोणं द्रौणिं च कर्णं च विव्याध च तवात्मजम्॥
en: Dhristadyumna was then pierced by the seven heroes who strove to protect Drona in battle. He also in his turn, pierced each of them with three shafts.

sn: ते भिन्ना धन्विना तेन धृष्टद्युम्नं पुनर्मधे। विव्यधुः पञ्चभिस्तूर्णमेकैको रथिनां वरः॥
en: 0 mighty monarch, with the greatest quickness, Dhristadyumna then pierced Drona, Karna, Drona's son and your son, in that terrible battle.

sn: दुमसेनस्तु संक्रुद्धो राजन् विव्याध पत्रिणा। त्रिभिश्चान्यैःशरैस्तूर्णं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus pierced by that bowman, your warriors again unitedly pierced Dhristadyumna in that battle, uttering terrible war-cries.

sn: स तु तं प्रतिविव्याध त्रिभिस्तीक्ष्णैरजिह्मगैः। स्वर्णपुङ्खः शिलाधौतैः प्राणान्तकरणैर्युधि॥
en: Inflamed with fury, O king, Drumasena then pierced Dhristadyumna with an arrow and then again quickly piercing the latter with sharp shafts he said-"wait, wait."

sn: भल्लेनान्येन तु पुनः सुवर्णोज्ज्वलकुण्डलम्। निचकत शिरः कायाद् द्रुमसेनस्य वीर्यवान्॥
en: Dhristadyumna pierced him in return with three sharp straight-flying arrows, winged with golden feathers, whetted on stone and capable of destroying life.

sn: तच्छिरो न्यपतद् भूमौ संदष्टौष्ठपुटं रणे। महावातसमुद्भूतं पक्कं तालफलं यथा।॥
en: Next with another broad-headed shaft, he lopped off from Drumasena's trunk, his head graced with glimmering ear-rings of gold.

sn: तान् स विद्ध्वा पुनर्योधान् वीरः सुनिशितैः शरैः। राधेयस्याच्छिनद् भल्लैः कार्मुकं चित्रयोधिनः॥
en: arrows on That head with its lips bitten, then fell on the field like a ripe palm-fruit thrown down by i a raging tempest.

sn: न तु तन्ममृषे कर्णो धनुषश्छेदनं तथा। निकर्तनमिवात्युग्रं लाङ्गलस्य महाहरिः॥
en: Thereafter the heroic Dhristadyumna piercing his opponent warriors with wellshaprened shafts cut-off with broad-headed arrows, the bow of Radha's son versed in various modes of war-fare.

sn: सोऽन्यद् धनुः समादाय क्रोधरक्तेक्षणःश्वसन्। अभ्यद्रवच्छरौघैस्तं धृष्टद्युम्नं महाबलम्॥
en: But Karna did not brook that severance of his bow even as a fierce lion does not brook the chopping off of its tail.

sn: दृष्ट्वा कर्णं तु संरब्धं ते वीराः षड्रथर्षभाः। पाञ्चाल्यपुत्रं त्वरिता: परिवर्जिघांसया॥
en: Taking up another bow, with eyes red in rage and breathing fiercely, he poured a shower of the highly puissant Dhristadyumna.

sn: घण्णां योधप्रवीराणां तावकानां पुरस्कृतम्। मृत्योरास्यमनुप्राप्तं धृष्टद्युम्नममंस्महि॥
en: Then beholding Karna wrought up with rage, the other six heroic foremost car-warriors, quickly surrounded the son the Panchala king with a view to slay him in battle.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु दाशार्हो विकिरछरान्। धृष्टद्युम्नं पराक्रान्तं सात्यकिः प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: 0 lord, the troops then considered Dhristadyumna to be already within the jaws of Death, as he was then confronted by the six foremost car-warriors of your army.

sn: तमायान्तं महेष्वासं सात्यकिं युद्धदुर्मदम्। राधेयो दशभिर्बाणैः प्रत्यविध्यदजिह्मगैः॥
en: At this juncture, Satyaki that scion of the Dasarha race, advanced to the rescue of the puissant Dhristadyumna, shooting numerous arrows (in all directions).

sn: तं सात्यकिर्महाराज विव्याध दशभिः शरैः। पश्यतां सर्ववीराणां मा गास्तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Beholding that Satvata warrior indomitable in battle advance, Radha's son pierced him in battle, with ten shafts.

sn: स सात्यकेस्तु बलिनः कर्णस्य च महात्मनः। आसीत् समागमो राजन् बलिवासवयोरिव॥
en: Him, O mighty monarch, Satyaki pierced in return with ten shafts before the eyes of all the heroes present and said-'Fly not-stay.'

sn: त्रासयन् स्थघोषेण क्षत्रियान् क्षत्रियर्षभः। राजीवलोचनं कर्णं सात्यकिः प्रत्यविध्यत॥
en: 0 king, that encounter between the powerful Satyaki and the high-souled Karna looked like the encounter between Bali and Vasava.

sn: कम्पयन्निव घोषेण धनुषो वसुधां बली। सूतपुत्रो महाराज सात्यकि प्रत्ययोधयत्॥
en: That foremost of the Kshatriyas Satyaki, then pierced the lotus-eyed Karna terrifying the Kshatriya warriors with the clatter of his car.

sn: विपाठकर्णिनाराचैर्वत्सदन्तैः क्षुरैरपि। कर्णः शरशतैश्चापि शैनेयं प्रत्यविध्यत॥
en: On the other hand, O mighty monarch the puissant son of Suta fought on with Satyaki, causing the earth to tremble with the tremendous twang on his bow.

sn: तथैव युद्ध्यमानोऽपि वृष्णीनां प्रवरो युधि। अभ्यवर्षच्छरैः कर्णं तद् युद्धमभवत् समम्॥
en: Karna then pierced that scion of Sini's race with Vipatkarnis, Narachas, Vatsadantas, Kshuras and hundreds of other kings of arrows.

sn: तावकाश्च महाराज कर्णपुत्रश्च दंशितः। सात्यकि विव्यधुस्तूर्णं समन्तान्निशितैः शरैः॥
en: So also Yuyudhana that foremost of the Vrishni warriors, covered Karna with his shower of arrows. The combat was an equal one (in all respects).

sn: अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य तेषां कर्णस्य वा विभो। अविद्ध्यत् सात्यकिः क्रुद्धो वृषसेनं स्तनान्तरे॥
en: Placing Karna in front of them, your sons then, O ruler of men, began to pierce Satyaki simultaneously with sharp arrows.

sn: तेन बाणेन निर्विद्धो वृषसेनो विशाम्पते। न्यपतत् स रथे मूढो धनुरुत्सृज्य वीर्यवान्॥
en: Baffing their as well as Karna's weapons with those of his own, O lord, Satyaki quickly pierced Vrishasena on the centre of his chest.

sn: ततः कर्णो हतं मत्वा वृषसेनं महारथम्। पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तः सात्यकिं प्रत्यपीड्यत्॥
en: Pierced with the shaft of Satyaki, the highly effulgent and puissant Vrishasena fell down on his car, losing hold of his bow.

sn: पीड्यमानसतु कर्णेन युयुधानो महारथः। विव्याध बहुभिः कर्णं त्वरमाणः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Thereupon Karna taking Vrishasena the mighty car-warrior to be slain, was afflicted with grief on account of his son's death and began to afflict Satyaki.

sn: स कर्णं दशभिर्विद्ध्वा वृषसेनं च सप्तभिः। स हस्तावापधनुषी तयोश्चिच्छेद सात्वतः॥
en: The mighty car-warrior Yuyudhana then afflicted sore by Karna, forcibly pierced Karna with numerous shafts over and over again.

sn: तावन्ये धनुषी सज्ये कृत्वा शत्रुभयंकरे। युयुधानमविध्येतां समन्तान्निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Piercing Karna with ten and Vrishasena with five shafts, the Satvata hero then cut-off their bow as well as their gloves.

sn: वर्तमाने तु संग्रामे तस्मिन् वीवरक्षये। अतीव शुश्रुवे राजन् गाण्डीवस्य महास्वनः॥
en: Thereupon they both having strung another pair of bows dreadful to the foe, began simultaneously to pierce Yuyudhana with sharp arrows.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु स्थनिर्घोषं गाण्डीवस्य च निःश्वनम्। सूतपुत्रोऽब्रवीद् राजन् दुर्योधनमिदं वचः॥
en: When that dreadful destruction of heroes was progressing, O king, the terrible twang of the Gandiva bow was heard, arising above the din of battle.

sn: एष सर्वां चमूं हत्वा मुख्यांश्चैव नरर्षभान्। पौरवांश्च महेष्वासो विक्षिपनुत्तमं धनुः॥
en: Having heard the sound of the Gandiva and the clatter of (Arjuna's) car, Oking Suta's son addressing Duryodhana said these wordsपार्थो विजयते तत्र गाण्डीवनिनदो महान्।

sn: श्रूयते स्थघोषश्च वासवस्येव नर्दतः॥
en: This is the tremendous twang of the Gandiva bow, emitted by Arjuna, as he has slain our entire army, many foremost of men and numerous warriors of the Kurus.

sn: करोति पाण्डवो व्यक्तं कर्मोपयिकमात्मनः। एषा विदार्यते राजन् बहुधा भारती चमूः॥
en: The clatter of his chariot is also heard, like the rumble of roaring clouds. Evidently the son of Pandu is achieving feats worthy of himself.

sn: विप्रकीर्णान्यनेकानि न हि तिष्ठन्ति कर्हिचित्। वातेनेव समूद्धृतमभ्रजालं विदीर्यते॥
en: O mighty monarch, this son of Pritha will completely crush our mighty host. Many troops are already scattered and none stays on the field.

sn: सव्यसाचिनमासाद्य भिन्ना नौरिव सागरे। द्रवतां योधमुख्यानां गाण्डीवप्रेषितैः शरैः॥
en: Our host is being shattered like risen masses of clouds by the raging tempest; encountering Savyasachin in battle, it is being split like a bark on a (rough) șea.

sn: विद्धानां शतशो राजश्रूयते नि:स्वनो महान्। शृणु दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषमर्जुनस्य रथं प्रति॥
en: Hark, O king, the terrible wails of foremost warriors as they fly or fall in battle in consequence of shafts shot from the Gandiva bow.

sn: निशीथे राजशार्दूल स्तनयित्नोरिवाम्बरे। हाहाकाररवांश्चैव सिंहनादांश्च पुष्कलान्॥
en: Hark, O foremost of monarchs, the roar of drums near Arjuna's chariot, resembling the rumble of clouds at the dead of night.

sn: शृणु शब्दान् बहुविधानर्जुनस्य रथं प्रति। अयं मध्ये स्थितोऽस्माकं सात्यकिः सात्वतां वरः॥५३
en: Hear also, numerous sounds, cries of woe and alas and loud war-cries, near the chariot of Arjuna.

sn: इह चेल्लभ्यते लक्ष्यं कृत्स्नाञ्जेष्यामहे परान्। एष पाञ्चालराजस्य पुत्रो द्रोणेन संगतः॥
en: But here in our middle stays Satyaki the foremost of the Satvatas; if this object o our aim could be smitten down, we might obtain victory over our foes.

sn: सर्वतः संवृतो योधैः शूरैश्च रथसत्तमैः। सात्यकि यदि हन्याम धृष्टद्युम्नं च पार्षतम्॥
en: There the Panchala Prince surrounded on all sides by heroic and foremost of carwarriors, has engaged himself with Drona.

sn: असंशयं महाराज ध्रुवो नो विजयो भवेत्। सौभद्रवदिमौ वीरौ परिवार्य महारथौ॥
en: If we can slay Satyaki and Prisata's son Dhristadyumna, then, O mighty monarch, undoubtedly victory will be ours.

sn: प्रयतामो महाराज निहन्तुं वृष्णिपार्षतौ। सव्यसाची पुरोऽभ्येति द्रोणानीकाय भारत॥
en: Impaling these two heroic and mighty carwarriors, the descendants of the Vrishni and the Prishata race respectively, like the son of Subhadra, we will, O king strive to slay them.

sn: संसक्तं सात्यकिं ज्ञात्वा बहुभिः कुरुपुङ्गवैः। तत्र गच्छन्तु बहवः प्रवरा रथसत्तमाः॥
en: But yonder comes Savyasachin, O Bharata, towards this division of Drona knowing that Satyaki is here encountered by many foremost warriors of the Kurus.

sn: यावत् पार्थो न जानाति सात्यकि बहुभिर्वृतम्। ते त्वरध्वं तथा शूराः शराणां मोक्षणे भृशम्॥
en: Let now a detachment of mighty and foremost car-warriors intercept Pritha's son, so that he may not advance to the rescue of Satyaki now surrounded by many.

sn: तथा त्विह व्रजत्येष परलोकाय माधवः। तथा कुरु महाराज सुनीत्या सुप्रयुक्तया॥
en: Let those mighty heroes be quick in shooting their arrows, so that this scion of Madhu's race may be dispatch to the next world. a

sn: कर्णस्य मतमास्थाय पुत्रस्ते प्राह सौबलम्। यथेन्द्रः समरे राजन् प्राह विष्णुं यशस्विनम्॥
en: Knowing this to be the opinion O, Karna, your son addressed Subala's son even as the highly illustrious Indra addressed Vishnu, on the field of battle.

sn: वृतः सहस्रैर्दशभिर्गजानामनिवर्तिनाम्। रथैश्च दशसाहस्रेस्तूर्णं याहि धनंजयम्॥
en: "Supported by a host of ten thousand unretreating elephants and also by detachment of ten thousand car-warriors, do you proceed against Dhananjaya.

sn: दुःशासनो दुर्विषहः सुबाहुर्दुष्प्रधर्षणः। एते त्वामनुयास्यन्ति पत्तिभिर्बहुभिर्वृताः॥
en: Dushasana Durvishaha, Subahu and Durshpradharshana these supported by numerous of infantry will follow you.

sn: जहि कृष्णौ महाबाहो धर्मराजं च मातुल। नकुलं सहदेवं च भीमसेनं तथैव च॥
en: O my uncle, slay me those fierce bowmen, the two Krishnas the very virtuous king Yudhishthira and Nakula and Sahadeva and Pandu's son Bhimasena.

sn: देवानामिव देवेन्द्र जयाशा त्वयि मे स्थिता। नहि मातुल कौन्तेयानसुरानिव पावकिः॥
en: My hopes of victory rest on you as those of the gods rest on their lord Indra. O uncle, slay the sons of Kunti, even as Pabaka's son slew the Asuras."

sn: एवमुक्तो ययौ पार्थान् पुत्रेण तव सौबलः। महत्या सेनया सार्धं सह पुत्रैश्च ते विभो॥
en: Thus addressed and urged on by your son, he (Subala's son) covered in mail, proceeded against the sons of Pritha, being himself supported by your sons and a large army.

sn: प्रियार्थं तव पुत्राणां दिक्षधुः पाण्डुनन्दनान्। ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तावकानां परैः सह॥
en: In order to please your son he proceeded to battle, desirous of consuming the sons of Pandu. Then commenced a terrible battle between your warriors and the foe.

sn: प्रयाते सौबले राजन् पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्। बलेन महता युक्तः सूतपुत्रस्तु सात्वतम्॥ अभ्ययात् त्वरितो युद्धे किरशरशतान् बहून्। तथैव पार्थिवाः सर्वे सात्यकि पर्यवारयन्॥
en: When, O king, Subala's son had going against the (main) army of the Pandavas, the son of Suta supported by a mighty force, quickly rushed upon the Satvata hero in battle, shooting many hundreds of shafts. Your troops then gathering together encompassed Satyaki.

sn: भारद्वाजस्ततो गत्वा धृष्टद्युम्नरथं प्रति। महद् युद्धं तदाऽऽसीत् तु द्रोणस्य निशि भारत। धृष्टद्युम्नेन वीरेण पञ्चालैश्च सहाद्भुतम्॥
en: The son of Bharadvaja also advancing against Dhristadyumna's car commenced at that night, O foremost of Bharatas, a most terrible and wonderful battle with the heroic Dhristadyumna and the Panchalas.

sn: संजय उवाच ततस्ते प्राद्रवन् सर्वे त्वरिता युद्धदुर्मदाः। अमृष्यमाणाः संरब्धा युयुधानरथं प्रति॥
en: Sanjaya said Then all those royal warriors of your army all indomitable in battle, furiously rushed against Yuyudhana's chariot, unable to brook his feats.

sn: ते रथैः कल्पितै राजन् हेमरूप्यविभूषितैः। सादिभिश्च गजैश्चैव परिवठ्ठः समन्ततः॥
en: Those warriors then surrounded on all sides the Satvata hero, with duly-equipped chariots decked with gold and gems and with horsemen and elephants.

sn: अथैनं कोष्ठकीकृत्य सर्वतस्ते महारथाः। सिंहनादांस्ततश्चक्रुस्तर्जयन्ति स्म सात्यकिम्॥
en: Having thus impaled the Satvata hero, all those mighty warriors filled the directions of the compass with the echo of their war-cries.

sn: तेऽभ्यवर्षञ्छरैस्तीक्ष्णैः सात्यकिं सत्यविक्रमम्। त्वरमाणा महावीरा माधवस्य बधैषिणः॥
en: Then those mighty heroes, desirous of achieving the slaughter of that scion of Madhu's race, began to pour showers of sharp arrows on Satyaki of infallible prowess.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा पततस्तूर्णं शैनेयः परवीरहा। प्रत्यगृह्णान्महाबाहुः प्रमुञ्चन् विशिखान् बहून्॥
en: Beholding then those heroes make towards himself in fury, that slayer of hostile heroes, that mighty-armed grandson of Shini, received them with a copious discharge of arrows.

sn: तत्र वीरो महेष्वासः सात्यकियुद्धदुर्मदः। निचकर्त शिरांस्युग्रैः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Then that mighty bowman, the heroic Satyaki of indomitable prowess, began to lop off the heads of his foes with fierce shafts of depressed knots.

sn: हस्तिहस्तान् हयग्रीवा बाहूनापि च सायुधान्। क्षुरप्रैः शातयामास तावकानां स माधवः॥
en: That scion of Madhu's race then severed with his razor-edged arrows, the trunks of elephants, the necks of horses and the arms of warriors decked with brace-lets.

sn: पतितैश्चामरैश्चैव श्वेतच्छत्रैश्च भारत। बभूव धरणी पूर्णा नक्षत्रै?रिव प्रभो॥
en: The earth then over-strewn with shattered yak-tails and white umbrellas, looked, O king, as beautiful as the star-bespangled firmament,

sn: एतेषां युयुधानेन युध्यतां युधि भारत। बभूव तुमुलः शब्दः प्रेतानां क्रन्दतामिव॥
en: Thus when they were being thus slaughtered by Yuyudhana in battle, O Bharata, a tumultuous uproar was heard there like the yell or bewailing of ghosts.

sn: तेन शब्देन महता पूरिताभूद् वसुन्धरा। रात्रिः समभवचैव तीव्ररूपा भयावहा॥
en: With that terrible uproar the earth was filled and the night appeared to be more hideous and more frightful.

sn: दीर्यमाणं बलं दृष्ट्वा युयुधानशराहतम्। श्रुत्वा च विपुलं नादं निशीथे लोमहर्षणे॥
en: Beholding the army routed and afflicted by the arrows of Yuyudhana and hearing in that nightly darkness that tremendous and horripilating uproar.

sn: सुतस्तवाब्रवीद् राजन् सारथिं रथिनां वरः। यत्रैष शब्दस्तत्राश्वांश्चोदयेति पुनः पुनः॥
en: Your son that foremost of car-warrior, O king, addressing his charioteer thus repeatedly spoke-"Drive, drive the steeds to the spot whence this tumult is proceeding.”

sn: तेन संचोद्यमानस्तु ततस्तांस्तुरगोत्तमान्। सूत: संचोदयामास युयुधानस्थं प्रति॥ ततो दुर्योधनः क्रुद्धो दृढधन्वा जितक्कमः। शीघ्रहस्तश्चित्रयोधी युयुधानमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Then inspired by him that charioteer proceeded those excellent horses to the car of Yuyudhana. Then that resolute bowman that indefatigable warrior, king Duryodhana versed in various modes of warfare and endued with great lightness of hands, rushed upon Yuyudhana.

sn: ततः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैः शरैः शोणितभोजनैः। दुर्योधनं द्वादशभिर्माधवः प्रत्यविध्यत॥
en: Thereupon the scion of Madhu's race pierced Duryodhana with twelve shafts shot from a full-drawn bow and capable of drinking the blood and mangling the skin.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तेन तथा पूर्वमेवादितः शरैः। शैनेयं दशभिर्बाणैः प्रत्यविध्यदमर्पितः॥
en: Duryodhana then pierced as before with those arrows of Shini's grandsons, angrily pierced the latter with ten shafts in return.

sn: ततः समभवद् युद्धं तुमुलं भरतर्षभ। पञ्चालानां च सर्वेषां भरतानां च दारुणम्॥
en: Meanwhile the battle that was being fought between the Panchalas and your troops, presented a wonderful and harming aspect.

sn: शैनेयस्तु रणे क्रुद्धस्तव पुत्रं महारथम्। सायकानामशीत्या तु विव्याधोरसि भारत॥
en: O Bharata, then the grandson of Shini, worked up with rage, pierced your mighty son with a group of eighty shafts on the chest.

sn: ततोऽस्य वाहान् समरे शर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्। सारथिं च रथात् तूर्णं पातयामास पत्रिणा॥
en: Thereafter that slayer of foes dispatched to the abode of Death the horses of Duryodhana and he also felled quickly the charioteer of the latter.

sn: हताश्वे तु रथे तिष्ठन् पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते। मुमोच निशितान् बाणाशैनेयस्य रथं प्रति॥
en: O ruler of men, remaining in that steedless car, your son began to discharge sharp arrows towards the car of Shini's grandson.

sn: शरान् पञ्चाशतस्तांस्तु शैनेयः कृतहस्तवत्। चिच्छेद समरे राजन् प्रेषितांस्तनयेन ते॥
en: Then like one endued with great lightness of hands, Shinis' grandson, O king, cut-off the group of fifty arrows shot by your son in that battle.

sn: अथापरेण भल्लेन मुष्टिदेशे महद् धनुः। चिच्छेद तरसा युद्धे तव पुत्रस्य माधवः॥
en: The descendant of Madhu's race then cutoff the mighty bow of your son near the grasp, with broad-headed arrows shot with great force.

sn: विरथो विधनुष्कश्च सर्वलोकेश्वरः प्रभुः। आरुरोह रथं तूर्णं भास्वरं कृतवर्मणः॥
en: Deprived of his car and his bow, that lord, that ruler of all men, quickly ascended the resplendent car of Kritavarman.

sn: दुर्योधने परावृत्ते शैनेयस्तव वाहिनीम्। द्रावयामास विशिखैर्निशामध्ये विशाम्पते॥
en: When Duryodhana had been compelled to turn his face away from the battle, the grandson of Shini in that night began to crush your troops, O ruler of men.

sn: शकुनिश्चार्जुनं राजन् परिवार्य समन्ततः। रथैरनेकसाहस्रैर्गजैश्चापि सहस्रशः॥
en: O king, meanwhile Shakuni surrounding Arjuna on all sides with countless cars and thousands of elephants.

sn: तथा हयसहस्रैश्च नानाशस्त्रैरवाकिरत्। ते महास्त्राणि सर्वाणि विकिरन्तोऽर्जुनं प्रति॥
en: And an equal number of horses, began furiously to assault him. His troops then began to discharge many celestial weapons against Arjuna.

sn: अर्जुनं योधयन्ति स्म क्षत्रियाः कालचोदिताः। तान्यर्जुनः सहस्राणि रथवारणवाजिनाम्॥ प्रत्यवारयदायस्तः प्रकुर्वन् विपुलं क्षयम्। ततस्तु समरे शूरः शकुनिः सौबलस्तदा॥ विव्याध निशितैर्बाणैरर्जुनं प्रहसन्निव। पुनश्चैव शतेनास्य संरुरोध महारथम्॥
en: Those Kshatriyas then urged on by fate fought on with Arjuna. Arjuna however singlehandedly checked those thousands of chariots, elephants and horses and finally compelled them to turn back. Then Subala's son with eyes coppery in rage and excited to the highest pitch of fury, pierced with twenty shafts that slayer of foes namely the puissant Arjuna. Then again he impeded the course of Arjuna's mighty car with a group of hundred arrows.

sn: तमर्जुनस्तु विंशत्या विव्याध युधि भारत। अथेतरान् महेष्वासांसिभिस्रिभिरविध्यत॥
en: Him, O Bharata, Arjuna pierced in battle with a set of twenty shafts and other mighty bowmen of his division with three shafts each.

sn: निवार्य तान् बाणगणैर्युधि राजन् धनंजयः। जघान तावकान् योधान् वज्रपाणिरिवासुरान्॥
en: O monarch, baffling the countless shafts shot by his foes, Dhananjaya slew the warriors of your army with excellent shafts charged with the force of the thunder.

sn: भुजैश्छिन्नैर्महीपाल हस्तिहस्तोपमैर्मधे। समाकीर्णा मही भाति पञ्चास्यैरिव पन्नगैः॥
en: The earth then covered over with loppedoff arms and thousands of mangled bodies, appeared beautiful as if covered over with charming flowers.

sn: शिरोभिः सकिरीटैश्च सुनसैश्चारुकुण्डलैः। संदष्टौष्ठपुटैः क्रुद्धैस्तथैवोद्भूतलोचनैः॥ निष्कचूडामणिधरैः क्षत्रियाणां प्रियंवदैः। पङ्कजैरिव विन्यस्तैः पतितैर्विबभौ मही॥
en: Strewn over with heads of Kshatriyasheads that were decked with diadems and graced with handsome noses and beautiful earrings and nether lips bit in anger and wide open eyes, heads that were graced with collars and crowned with gems and which while life was in them spoke salutary words, the earth looked beautiful as if strewn with hillocks covered with Champaka flowers.

sn: कृत्वा तत् कर्म बीभत्सुरुग्रमुग्रपराक्रमः। विव्याध शकुनि भूयः पञ्चभिर्नतपर्वभिः॥
en: Then Vibhatsu on fierce energy having achieved that dreadful feat once more pierced Sakuni with five arrows of depressed knots.

sn: अताड्यदुलूकं च त्रिभिरेव तथा शरैः। उलूकस्तु तथा विद्धो वासुदेवमताड्यत्॥
en: He then angrily pierced Uluka in that battle with his arrows. Thus having pierced Uluka even before the very eyes of Subala's son, Arjuna.

sn: ननाद च महानादं पूरयन्निव मेदिनीम्। अर्जुनः शकुनेश्चापं सायकैरच्छिनद् रणे॥
en: Uttered a mighty roar that filled the earth with its echo. Thereafter that son of the foremost of celestials, cut-off the bow of Sakuni with his arrows.

sn: निन्ये च चतुरो वाहान् यमस्य सदनं प्रति। ततो रथादवप्लुत्य सौबलो भरतर्षभ॥
en: And dispatched the latter's four steeds to the kingdom of Death. Thereupon, O foremost of the Bharatas, jumping down from his chariot, the son of Subala.

sn: उलूकस्य रथं तूर्णमासरोह विशाम्पते। तावेकरथमारूढौ पितापुत्रौ महारथौ॥
en: Quickly ascended the car of Uluka. Then those two mighty car-warriors, sire and son, riding on the same chariot.

sn: पार्थं सिषिचतुर्बाणैर्गिरिं प्रेधाविवाम्बुभिः। तौ तु विद्ध्वा महाराज पाण्डवो निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Began to shower arrows on Pritha's son, like two risen clouds showering rain on the mountain-breast. Thereafter, . mighty monarch, Pandu's son piercing them both with shafts.

sn: विद्रावयंस्तव चमूं शतशो व्यधमच्छरैः। अनिलेन यथाभ्राणि विच्छिन्नानि समन्ततः॥
en: Began to crush your troops by hundreds and thousands. Just as masses of clouds are torn as under by a violent storm.

sn: विच्छिन्नानि तथा राजन् बलान्यासन् विशाम्पते। तद् बलं भरतश्रेष्ठ वव्यमानं तदा निशि॥
en: So, O ruler of men, your troops were then routed and dispersed by Arjuna. O foremost of the Bharatas, then the troops of your army carnaged during that night.

sn: प्रदुद्राव दिशः सर्वा वीक्षमाणं भयादितम्। उत्सृज्य वाहान् समरे चोदयन्तस्तथा परे॥
en: Fled in fear in all directions looking at one another; some left behind their horses, others urged them to the top of their speed.

sn: सम्भ्रान्ताः पर्यधावन्त तस्मिस्तमसि दारुणे। विजित्य समरे योधांस्तावकान् भरतर्षभ।॥
en: They then fled away in great fright in that darkness of night. O foremost of the Bharatas, defeating your troops in battle.

sn: दध्मतुर्मुदितौ शङ्खौ वासुदेवधनंजयौ। धृष्टद्युम्नो महाराज द्रोणं विद्ध्वा त्रिभिः शरैः॥
en: Vasudeva and Dhananjaya began to blow their conchs. Meanwhile Dhristadyumna, 0 king, piercing Drona with three shafts.

sn: चिच्छेद धनुषस्तूर्णं ज्यां शरेण शितेन ह। तन्निधाय धनुर्भूमौ द्रोणः क्षत्रियमर्दनः॥
en: Quickly cut-off the latter's bowstring with a short arrow; thereupon Drona that crusher of hostile Kshatriyas, throwing that bow down on the ground.

sn: आददेऽन्यद् धनुः शरू वेगवत् सारवत्तरम्। धृष्टद्युम्नं ततो द्रोणो विद्ध्वा सप्तभिराशुगैः॥
en: Took up another bow of greater force and toughness; then Drona piercing Dhistadyumna with seven swift-flying arrows.

sn: सारथिं पञ्चभिर्बाणै राजन् विव्याध संयुगे। तं निवार्य शरैस्तूर्णं धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः॥
en: Pierced the latter's charioteer, O foremost of the Bharatas, with five arrows. Then the mighty car-warrior Dhistadyumna checking Drona by means of his arrows.

sn: व्यधमत् कौरवीं सेनामासुरीं मघवानिव। वध्यमाने बले तस्निस्तव पुत्रस्य मारिष॥
en: Began to agitate the Kaurava host like Indra agitating the Asura host. O sire when the troops of your son were thus being carnaged.

sn: प्रावर्तत नदी घोरा शोणितौघतरङ्गिणी। उभयोः सेनयोर्मध्ये नराश्वद्विपवाहिनी॥
en: A dreadful river of boldly currents began to flow between the two armies, carrying with it slain men horses and elephants.

sn: यथा वैतरणी राजन् यमराजपुरं प्रति। द्रावयित्वा तु तत् सैनयं धृष्टद्युम्नः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Like, O monarch, the river Vaitarani carrying creatures to the abode of Death. Then the puissant Dhristadyumna completely routing that army of your son.

sn: अभ्यराजत तेजस्वी शक्रो देवगणेष्विवा अथ दध्मुर्महाशङ्खान् धृष्टद्युम्नशिखण्डिनौ॥
en: Shone resplendent like Shakra in the midst of the celestial hosts. Thereafter Dhristadyumna and Sikhandin blew their mighty conchs;

sn: यमौ च युयुधानश्च पाण्डवश्च वृकोदरः। जित्वा रथसहस्राणि तावकानां महारथाः।
en: So did also the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) and Yuyudhana, the Pandu's son Vrikodara. Having vanquished thousands of energetic kings of your army.

sn: सिंहनादरवांश्चक्रुः पाण्डवा जितकाशिनः॥ पश्यतस्तव पुत्रस्य कर्णस्य च रणोत्कटाः। तथा द्रोणस्य शूरस्य द्रौणेश्चैव विशाम्पते॥
en: The Pandavas ever attended with victory uttered dreadful war-cries, even before the eyes of your son and Karna and the heroic Drona and the son of Drona, O ruler of men.

sn: संजय उवाच विद्रुतं स्वबलं दृष्ट्वा वध्यमानं महात्मभिः। क्रोधेन महताऽऽविष्टः पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding his own army carnaged by highsouled warriors, your son, O ruler of men, was excited to the highest pitch of fury.

sn: अभ्येत्य सहसा कर्णं द्रोणं च जयतां वरम्। अमर्षवशमापन्नो वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then quickly approaching Karna and Drona that foremost of victorious heroes and burning with rage, he eloquent in speech, spoke these wordsभवद्भ्यामिह संग्रामः क्रुद्धाभ्यां सम्प्रवर्तितः।

sn: आहवे निहतं दृष्ट्वा सैन्धवं सव्यसाचिना॥
en: Beholding the ruler of the Sindhus slain in battle by Savyasachin, you two, filled with rage, caused this battle to go on.

sn: निहन्यमानां पाण्डूनां बलेन मम वाहिनीम्। भूत्वा तद्विजये शतावशक्ताविव पश्यतः॥
en: Though competent to slay the Pandava troops, still you are beholding the slaughter of my troops by them with great in-difference.

sn: यद्यहं भवतोस्त्याज्यो न वाच्योऽस्मि तदैव हि। आवां पाण्डुसुतान् संख्ये जेष्याव इति मानदौ॥ तदैवाहं वचः श्रुत्वा भवद्भ्यामनुसम्मतम्। नाकरिष्यमिदं पार्वैरं योधविनाशनम्॥
en: If you now abandon me, you should have told me of it in the beginning. We two shall vanquish the sons of Pandu in battle even these were the words, you said to me, o you givers of honor. Hearing those words of yours, I then allowed these proceedings. Otherwise I would never have provoked these hostilities with the Parthas-hostilities that are so destructive of heroic combatants.

sn: यदि नाहं परित्याज्यो भवद्भ्यां पुरुषर्षभौ। युध्यतामनुरूपेण विक्रमेण सुविक्रमौ॥
en: If, O foremost of men, I do not deserve to be forsaken by you, then do you fight according to the measure of your prowess, O you that are possessed of great prowess.

sn: वाक्प्रतोदेन तौ वीरौ प्रणुनौ तनयेन ते। प्रावर्तयेतां संग्रामं घट्टिताविव पन्नगौ॥
en: Thus pierced with the goad of speech by your son, those two heroes once more engaged in battle like two snakes poked with sticks.

sn: ततस्तौ रथिनां श्रेष्ठौ सर्वलोकधनुर्धरौ। शैनेयप्रमुखान् पार्थानभिदुदुवतू रणे॥
en: Then those two foremost of car-warriors, the best of all human bowmen, rushed against the Parthas headed by the grandson of Shini and others.

sn: तथैव सहिताः पार्थाः सर्वसैन्येन संवृताः। अभ्यवर्तन्त तौ वीरौ नर्दमानौ मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: Similarly the Parthas supported by their own troops, rushed upon those two heroes, who were roaring repeatedly.

sn: अथ द्रोणो महेष्वासो दशभिः शिनिपुङ्गवम्। अविध्यत् त्वरितं क्रुद्धः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः॥
en: Then the enraged Drona that best of all wielders of weapons, quickly pierced that foremost of the descendants of Shini with ten sharp arrows.

sn: कर्णश्च दशभिर्बाणैः पुत्रश्च तव सप्तभिः। दशभिर्वृषसेनश्च सौबलश्चापि सप्तभिः॥
en: Karna pierced him with ten shafts, your son with seven, Vrishasena with ten and Subala's son with seven arrows.

sn: एते कौरव संक्रन्दे शैनेयं पर्यवाकिरन्। दृष्ट्वा न समरे द्रोणं निघ्नन्तं पाण्डवी चमूम्॥
en: Those hosts of the Kurus together with those warriors, began to shower arrows on the grandson of Shini. Then beholding Drona slaughter the Pandava hosts.

sn: विव्यधुः सोमकास्तूर्णं समन्ताच्छरवृष्टिभिः। तत्र द्रोणोऽहरत् प्राणान् क्षत्रियानां विशाम्पते॥
en: The Somakas from all side began to pierce him with showers of arrows. Then Drona snatched out of the Kshatriyas their lives, O ruler of men.

sn: रश्मिभिर्भास्करो राजंस्तमांसीव समन्ततः। द्रोणेन वध्यमानानां पञ्चालानां विशाम्पते॥
en: Like the sun dispelling darkness with his rays. O ruler of men, when the Panchalas were being slaughtered by Drona.

sn: शुश्रुवे तुमुलः शब्दः क्रोशतामितरेतरम्। पुत्रानन्ये पितॄनन्ये भ्रातृनन्ये च मातुलान्॥
en: A dreadful sound was heard as they challenged one another aloud. Some leaving their sons, some their fathers, some their brothers and some their uncles.

sn: भागिनेयान् वयस्यांश्च तथा सम्बन्धिबान्धवान्। उत्सृज्योत्सृज्य गच्छन्ति त्वरिता जीवितेप्सवः॥
en: Some their nephews, their companions and their friends and some their relatives, fled in all quickness, desirous of saving their own lives.

sn: अपरे मोहिता मोहात् तमेवाभिमुखा ययुः। पाण्डवानां रणे योधाः परलोकं गताः परे॥
en: Others, on the other hand, were confounded that they rushed even towards Drona himself. Indeed many warriors of the Pandava host were then dispatched to the other world.

sn: सा तथा पाण्डवी सेना पीड्यमाना महात्मन। निशि सम्प्राद्रवद् राजन्नुत्सृज्योल्काः सहस्रशः॥
en: Thus afflicted by that high-souled warrior, the Pandava army began to fly in all directions in that night, throwing down their blazing flambeaus.

sn: पश्यतो भीमसेनस्य विजयस्याच्युतस्य च। यमयोधर्मपुत्रस्य पार्षतस्य च पश्यतः॥
en: Even before the very sight of Bhimsena and Achyuta and the twins and the virtuous Yudhishthira and the son of Prishata. some SO

sn: तमसा संवृते लोके न प्राज्ञायत किंचन। कौरवाणां प्रकाशेन दृश्यन्ते विद्रुताः परे॥
en: Then the troops were shrouded in darkness and nothing could be discerned. Only the flight of the foe could be determined through the light that the torches of the Kauravas shed.

sn: द्रवमाणं तु तत् सैन्यं द्रोणकर्णी महारथौ। जघ्नतुः पृष्ठतो राजन् किरन्तौ सायकान् बहून्॥
en: And as the army of the Pandavas was routed, the mighty warriors Karna and Drona, O king, pursued them from behind discharging numerous arrows.

sn: पञ्चालेषु प्रभग्नेषु क्षीयमाणेषु सर्वतः। जनार्दनो दीनमनाः प्रत्यभाषत फाल्गुनम्॥
en: When the Panchala ranks were broken down and reduced in number, Janaraddana cheerless at heart addressed Phalguna sayingद्रोणकर्णौ महेष्वासावेतौ पार्षतसात्यकी।

sn: पञ्चालांश्चैव सहितौ जघ्नतुः सायकै शम्॥
en: "Let Parsata and Satyaki supported by the Panchala troops rush against the mighty Drona and Karna, shooting as they proceed numerous arrows.

sn: एतयोः शरवर्षेण प्रभग्ना नो महारथाः। वार्यमाणापि कौन्तेय पृतना नावतिष्ठते॥
en: This mighty army of ours has been broken and routed by the showers of the enemies' shafts; and though checked in their flight, they could into again be sufficiently rallied.

sn: तां तु विद्रवतीं दृष्ट्वा ऊचतुः केशवार्जुनौ। मा विद्रवत वित्रस्ता भयं त्यजत पाण्डवाः॥
en: beholding their troops fly away Kesava and Arjuna then addressed them thus-'Do you not flight from fear! Discard all your fears, O Pandavas.

sn: तावावां सर्वसैन्यैश्च व्यूहैः सम्यगुदायुधैः। द्रोणं च सूतपुत्रं च प्रयतावः प्रबाधितुम्॥
en: Supported by all the troops and disposing them of in perfect order, we two with weapons upraised are even now dashing against Drona and Suta's son with a view to fight with them."

sn: एतौ हि बलिनौ शूरौ कृतास्रो जितकाशिनौ। उपेक्षितौ तव बलैर्नाशयेतां निशामिमाभ्॥
en: O Dhananjaya! Do whatever you consider matching with the specific circumstance and appropriate in respect of slaughtering Karna in the battle.

sn: तयोः संवदतोरेवं भीमकर्मा महाबलः। आयाद् वृकोदरः शीघ्रं पुनरावर्त्य वाहिनीम्॥
en: O majesty! Arjuna in response to the advice given by Yudhishthira said to Sri Krishna! O god! King Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti is frightened of the valour shown by Karna, the son of Radha today.

sn: वृकोदरमथायान्तं दृष्ट्वा तत्र जनार्दनः। पुनरेवाब्रवीद् राजन् हर्षयन्निव पाण्डवम्॥
en: Then Janaradana seeing Vrikodora advance, once more addressed Pandus' son Arjuna in these words as if for cheering him the while.

sn: एष भीमो रणश्लाघी वृतः सोमकपाण्डवैः। अभ्यवर्तत वेगेन द्रोणकर्णी महारथौ॥
en: Yonder does the proud Bhima supported by the Somakas and Pandavas rush furiously against Drona and Karna, those two fierce bow-men.

sn: एतेन सहितौ युद्ध्य पञ्चालैश्च महारथैः। आश्वासनार्थं सैन्यानां सर्वेषां पाण्डुनन्दन॥
en: Supported by these and by the mighty carwarrior of the Panchalas, do you proceed to the fight fore-assuring your troops, O delighter of Pandu.

sn: ततस्तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रावुभौ माधवपाण्डवौ। द्रोणकर्णी समासाद्य घिष्ठितौ रणमूर्धनि॥
en: Thereafter those two foremost of men, the son of Pandu and the scion of Madhu's race, encountering Drona and Karna, took up their station in the van of their army.

sn: संजय उवाच ततस्तत् पुनरावृत्तं युधिष्ठिरबलं महत्। ततो द्रोणश्च कर्णश्च परान् ममृदतुर्युधि॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon the mighty army of king Yudhishthira once more returned to the spot where Drona and Karna where crushing their enemies.

sn: स सम्प्रहारस्तुमुलो निशि प्रत्यभवन्महान्। यथा सागरयो राजश्चन्द्रोदयविवृद्धयोः॥
en: A tremendous clash was then produce on that part of the field, like to that, O monarch, which takes place when two oceans swelling under the influence of the moon dash against each other.

sn: तत उत्सृज्य पाणिभ्यां प्रदीपांस्तव वाहिनी। युयुधे पाण्डवैः सार्धमुन्मत्तवदसंकुला॥
en: Then your soldiers throwing aside the flambeaus, with both their hands fought furiously with the Pandavas, like so many mad people.

sn: रजसा तमसा चैव संवृते भृशदारुणे। केवलं नामगोत्रेण प्रायुध्यन्त जयैषिणः॥
en: When the field was thus covered with nocturnal darkness and dust, the combatants fought during that dreadful battle, guided only by the names they uttered (in their challenge.

sn: अश्रूयन्त हि नामानि श्राव्यमाणानि पार्थिवैः। प्रहरद्भिर्महाराज स्वयंवर इवाहवे॥
en: The names of contending kings as they challenged one another were then heard there, O king, like to what takes places during a Sayamvara,

sn: निःशब्दमासीत् सहसा पुनः शब्दो महानभूत्। क्रुद्धानां युध्यमानानां जीयतां जयतामपि॥
en: Sometimes as awful silence reigned over the field; next moment there was heard a tremendous din caused by enraged contending warriors and by the victorious and the vanquished.

sn: यत्र यत्र स्म दृश्यन्ते प्रदीपज्ञः कुरुसत्तमा तत्र तत्र स्म शूरास्ते निपतन्ति एतगवत्॥
en: Wherever the flambeaus were seen to blaze, thither the combatants rushed, like so many insects rushing upon a flame of light.

sn: तथा संयुध्यमानानां विगाढासीन्महानिशा। पाण्डवानां च राजेन्द्र कौरवाणां च सर्वशः॥
en: Thus when the Kouravas and the Pandavas were fighting with one another the dreadful night deepened into deadness, Bharata.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: संजय उवाच ततः कर्णो रणे दृष्ट्वा पार्षतं परवीरहा। आजधानोरसि शरैर्दशभिर्मर्मभेदिभिः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then that slayer of foes viz., Karna beholding Prisata's son in battle, pierced the him on the breast with ten arrows capable of penetrating to the vitals.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: प्रतिविव्याध तं तूर्णं धृष्टद्युम्नोऽपि मारिष। दशभिः सायकैर्हष्टस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: In return Dhristadyumna quickly pierced, in that battle, Karna, with five arrows and challenged him saying 'stay, stay.'

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: तावन्योन्यं शरैः संख्ये संछाद्य सुमहारथैः। पुनः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैर्विव्यधाते परस्परम्॥
en: In that dreadful battle, they both covering each other with their arrowy showers, pierced each other with shafts shot from fully-stretched bows.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: ततः पाञ्चालमुख्यस्य धृष्टद्युम्नस्य संयुगे। सारथिं चतुरश्वाश्वान् कर्णो विव्याध सायकैः॥
en: Thereafter Karna dispatched the four steeds and charioteer of Dhristadyumna that foremost of the Panchalas, to the dreary abode of Death.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: कार्मुकप्रवरं चापि प्रचिच्छेद शितैः शरैः। सारथिं चास्य भल्लेन रथनीडादपातयत् ॥
en: He cut-off with sharp arrows the latter's excellent bow and then with a bhalla felled his charioteer from the niche on the car.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु विरथो हताश्वो हतसारथिः। गृहीत्वा परिघं घोरं कर्णस्याश्वानपीपिषत्॥
en: The puissant Dhristadyumna deprived of the use of his car and having his charioteer and his horses slain, quickly jumped down on the ground armed with a terrible mace.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: विद्धश्च बहुभिस्तेन शरैराशीविषोपमैः। ततो युधिष्ठिरानीकं पद्भ्यामेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: Then through inangled with arrows of depressed knots shot by Karna, he still approached the former's chariot and slew the steeds thereof with the strokes of his mace.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: आरुरोह रथं चापि सहदेवस्य मारिष। प्रयातुकामः कर्णाय वारितो धर्मनूनुना॥
en: Then quickly wheeling back, that slayer of hostile heroes viz., Prisata's son, that foremost of all car-warriors, ascended the chariot of Dhananjaya.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: कर्णस्तु सुमहातेजाः सिंहनादविमिश्रितम्। धनुःशब्दं महचके दध्मौ तारेण चाम्बुजम्॥ दृष्टवा विनिर्जितं युद्धे पार्षतं ते महारथाः। अमर्षवशमापन्नाः पञ्चालाः सहसोमकाः॥
en: Then though desirous of encountering Karna once more, he was prevented from doing so by the son of Dharma. Then the highly puissant Karna created a loud din by means of his bow, which became mingled with his warcries. He then blew his conch furiously. Beholding Prisata's son vanquished in battle, those mighty car-warriors.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: सूतपुत्रवधार्थाय शस्त्राण्यादाय सर्वशः। प्रययुः कर्णमुद्दिश्य मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्॥
en: The Panchalas and the Somakas influenced by wrath, grasped their weapons with a view to compass the death of Suta's son.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: कर्णस्यापि रथे वाहानन्यान् सूतोऽभ्ययोजयत्। शङ्खवर्णान् महावेगान् सैन्धवान् साधुवाहिनः॥
en: They then rushed against Karna, making death their final goal. Meanwhile Karna's

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: लब्धलक्ष्यस्तु राधेयः पञ्चालानां महारथान्। अभ्यपीडयदायस्तः शरैर्मेघ इवाचलम्॥
en: Steeds that were of the hue of conch shells, endued with great fleetness, of the Sindhu breed and well-broken. Then the son of Radha getting the mighty warriors of the Panchalas within his range.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: सा पीड्यमाना कर्णेन पञ्चालानां महाचमूः। सम्प्राद्रवत् सुसंत्रस्ता सिंहेनेवार्दिता मृगी॥
en: Began to afflict them with his arrowy showers, like masses of clouds afflicting the mountain breast with torrents of rain. Afflicted sore by Karna, the division of the Panchalas.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: पतितास्तुगेभ्यश्च गजेभ्यश्च महीतले। रथेभ्यश्च नरास्तूर्णमदृश्यन्त ततस्ततः॥ धावमानस्य योधस्य क्षुरप्रैः स महामृधे। बाहू चिच्छेद वै कर्णः शिरश्चैव संकुण्डलम्॥ ऊरू चिच्छेद चान्यस्य गजस्थस्य विशाम्पते।
en: Panic-struck,. began to break and fly away like a herd of deer attacked by a lion. O ruler of earth, then warriors were seen to fall down on the ground from their steeds or elephants or chariots, on all sides. In that fierce battle Karna cut-off with razor-headed arrows the arms and heads decked with ear-ring of warriors that were flying away. O ruler of men, he cut-off the thighs of other warriors riding on elephants.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: वाजिपृष्ठगतस्यापि भूमिष्ठस्य च मारिष॥ नाज्ञासिषुर्धावमाना बहवश्च महारथाः।
en: Or on the backs of steeds or of those standing on the ground. O sire, many mighty car-warriors in the confusion of their flight perceived no.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: संछिन्नान्यात्मगात्राणि वाहनानि च संयुगे॥ ते वध्यमानाः समरे पञ्चालाः सृञ्जयैः सह।
en: Their own limbs cut-off or the injuries of their animals. The Panchalas and the Srinjayas then slaughtered with dreadful arrows.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: तृणप्रस्पन्दनाचापि सूतपुत्रं स्म मेनिरे॥ अपि स्वं समरे योधं धावमानं विचेतसम्। कर्णमेवाभ्यमन्यन्त ततो भीता द्रवन्ति ते॥ तान्यनीकानि भग्नानि द्रवमाणानि भारत।
en: Took even the motion of a straw for Karna. Greatly confounded; the combatants mistook their flying friends for Karna and then fled from them in great fright. Then, O Bharata, as those broken and routed divisions were flying away.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: अभ्यद्रवद् द्रुतं कर्णः पृष्ठतो विकिरञ्छरान्॥ अवेक्षमाणास्त्वन्योन्यं सुसम्मूढा विचेतसः।
en: Karna pursued them from behind shooting his arrows in all directions. Those warriors as they were madly flying, were carnaged by thousands, in that battle.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: नाशक्नुवन्नवस्थातुं काल्यमाना महात्मना॥ कर्णेनाभ्याहता राजन् पञ्चालाः परमेषुभिः।
en: Afflicted by that illustrious warrior Karna, they could not then stay on the field. O king, the Panchalas then mangled with excellent shafts by Karna.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: द्रोणेन च दिशः सर्वा वीक्षमाणाः प्रदुद्रवुः॥ ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा स्वसैन्यं प्रेक्ष्य विद्रुतम्।
en: As also by Drona, looked vacantly at the different quarters and then fled away. Thereupon king Yudhishthira, beholding his own army routed.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: अपयाने मनः कृत्वा फाल्गुनं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ पश्य कर्णं महेष्वासं धनुष्पाणिमवस्थितम्।
en: And considering a retreat to be addressed Arjuna thus;-'Behold the mighty car-warriors Karna standard yonder armed with his bow.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: निशीथे दारुणे काले तपन्तमिव भास्करम्॥ कर्णसायकनुन्नानां क्रोशतामेष निःस्वनः। अनिशं श्रूयते पार्थ त्वद्वन्धूनामनाथवत्॥ यथा विसृजतश्चास्य संदधानस्य चाशुगान्। पश्यामि नान्तरं पार्थ क्षपयिष्यति नो ध्रुवम्॥ यदत्रानन्तरं कार्य प्राप्तकालं च पश्यसि। कर्णस्य वधसंयुक्तं तत् कुरुष्व धनंजय॥ एवमुक्तो महाराज पार्थः कृष्णमथाब्रवीत्। भीतः कुन्तीसुतो राजा राधेयस्याद्य विक्रमात्॥ एवंगते प्राप्तकालं कर्णानीके पुनः पुनः।
en: Like a burning sun shining even during the hideous hour of night. The yells of your own partisans helplessly mangled by the shafts of Karna are being incessantly heard. Karna does shoot his arrows so skillfully that no interval can be noticed between his fixing the arrow on the string and letting it off. He will surely fighting thus, extirpate all our friends. Do that now, O Dhananjaya, for compassing the slaughter of Karna, which according to your judgment should be done and for which the hour may have come." Being thus spoken to, Arjuna addressing Krishna said

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: भवान् व्यवस्यतु क्षिप्रं द्रवते हि वरूथिनी॥ द्रोणसायकनुन्नानां भग्नानां मधुसूदन।
en: “The royal son Dharma has been frightened today at the prowess of Karna. As Karna's division is repeatedly worsting that of our own, do your quickly make some arrangement that will cope with the present dangerous situation. Behold, yonder are our troops flying away. O slayer of Madhu, broken and mangled with the shafts of Drona.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: कर्णेन त्रास्यमानानामवस्थानं न विद्यते॥ पश्यामि च तथा कर्णे विचरन्तमभीतवत्।
en: And frightened by Karna, they have no stay or support. I see that Karna is careering dauntlessly on the field.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: द्रवमाणान् रथोदारान् किरन्तं निशितैः शरैः॥ नैनं शक्ष्यामि संसोढुं चरन्तं रणमूर्धनि।
en: Crushing numerous illustrious car-warriors and covering them with his sharp shafts I cannot brook the sight of him careering in thick of the fight.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: प्रत्यक्षं वृष्णिशार्दूलं पाढम्पर्शमिवोरगः॥ स भवांस्तत्र यात्वाशु यत्र कर्णो महारथः। अहमेनं हनिष्यामि मां वैष मधुसूदन॥
en: Under my very nose, foremost of the Vrishnis, even as a snake cannot bear the tread of human feet. So, do you take me there where the mighty Karna is fighting. Oslayer of Madhu, either I will slay him or he shall slay me.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: वासुदेव उवाच पश्यामि कर्णं कौन्तेय देवराजमिवाहवे। विचरन्तं नरव्याघ्रमतिमानुषविक्रमम्॥
en: Vasudeva said I see, O son of Kunti, that foremost of men, of super-human prowess, viz.., Karna, careering at the head of battle like the king of the celestials himself.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: नैतस्यान्योऽस्ति संग्रामे प्रत्युद्याता धनंजय। ऋते त्वां पुरुषव्याघ्र राक्षसाद् वा घटोत्कचात्॥
en: O Dhananjaya, there is none, save yourself and the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha who can encounter him in battle, O foremost of men.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: न तु तावदहं मन्ये प्राप्तकालं तवानघ। समागमं महाबाहो सूतपुत्रेण संयुगे॥
en: O sinless one, I do not think that the hour has come when, O mighty armed one, you should meet the son of Suta in battle.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: दीप्यमाना महोल्केव तिष्ठत्यस्य हि वासवी। त्वदर्थं हि महाबाहो सूतपुत्रेण संयुगे॥
en: The resplendent Sakti, resembling a mighty meteor, obtained by him from Vasava is still in his possession, o mighty armed one, kept carefully to be used against yourself by this son Suta.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: रक्ष्यते शक्तिरेषा हि रौद्रं रूपं बिभर्ति च। घटोत्कचस्तु राधेयं प्रत्युद्यातु महाबलः॥
en: He preserves that Sakti; and therefore he has now assumed a terrible aspect. Ghatotkacha, is ever attached to your interests and is anxious for your welfare.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: स हि भीमेन बलिना जातः सुरपराक्रमः। तस्मिन्नस्राणि दिव्यानि राक्षसान्यासुराणि च॥ सततं चानुरक्तो वो हितैषी च घटोत्कचः। विजेष्यति रणे कर्णमिति मे नात्र संशयः॥
en: Therefore let the mighty Ghatotkacha charge the son of Radha. That one of prowess resembling that of an immortal, was begotten by Bhima and he is conversant with numerous celestial, Asuri and Rakshasa-weapons. I am sure, he will conquer Karna in battle.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: एवमुक्तो महाबाहुः पार्थः पुष्करलोचनः। आजुहावाथ तद् रक्षस्तचासीत् प्रादुरग्रतः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus spoken to the mighty-armed Partha possessed of eyes resembling lotus petals, summoned the Rakshasa. Thereupon the Rakshasa appeared before him.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: कवची सशरः खड्गी सधन्वा च विशाम्पते। अभिवाद्य ततः कृष्णं पाण्डवं च धनंजयम्।
en: Cased in armour and armed with bows arrows and a sword, O ruler of men. Then doing obeisance to Krishna and Pandu's son Dhananjaya.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: अब्रवीच तदा कृष्णमयमस्यनुशाधि माम्॥ ततस्तं मेघसंकाशं दीप्तास्यं दीप्तकुण्डलम्। अभ्यभाषत हैडिम्बि दाशार्हः प्रहसन्निव॥
en: He proudly said-"Here am I order me.” Thereupon the descendant of the Dasarha race Krishna, addressing Hidimva's son of the complexion of clouds, of effulgent countenance and fiery eyes smilingly said these words.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: श्रीवासुदेव उवाच घटोत्कच विजानीहि यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि पुत्रक। प्राप्तो विक्रमकालोऽयं तव नान्यस्य कस्यचित्॥
en: Vasudeva said Take my blessings, O Ghatotkacha, hear attentively what I now say to you. The hour for the display of your prowess and of no one else has now arrived.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: स भवान् मज्जमानानां बन्धूनां त्वं प्लवो भव। विविधानि तवास्राणि सन्ति माया च राक्षसी॥
en: Do you become the raft in this battle to the sinking Pandavas. You possess weapons of various kinds and the potent Rakshasi illusion.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: पश्य कर्णेन हैडिम्बे पाण्डवानामनीकिनी। काल्यमाना यथा गावः पालेन रणमूर्धनि॥
en: Behold, O son of Hidimba, the hosts of the Pandavas afflicted by Karna in battle like a herd of kine belaboured by the keeper.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: एष कर्णो महेष्वासो मतिमान् दृढविक्रमः। पाण्डवानामनीकेषु निहन्ति क्षत्रियर्षभान्॥
en: Yonder does the mighty bowman Karna of great intelligence and resolute prowess, burn the foremost of the Kshatriyas of the Pandava host.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: किरन्तः शरवर्षाणि महान्ति दृढधन्विनः। न शक्रुवन्त्यवस्थातुं पीड्यमानाः शरार्चिषा॥
en: Scorched with his fiery arrows the Pandava warrior cannot stand before that resolute bowman who is shooting numerous arrows.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: निशीथे सूतपुत्रेण शरवर्षेण पीडिताः। एते द्रवन्ति पञ्चालाः सिंहेनेवार्दिता मृगाः॥
en: Afflicted at the dead of night with showers of arrows shot by the son of Suta, yonder are the Panchalas flying away like a flock of deer attacked by the lion.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: एतस्यैवं प्रवृद्धस्य सूतपुत्रस्य संयुगे। निषेद्धा विद्यते नान्यस्त्वामृते भीमविक्रम॥
en: Save yourself, O you of dreadful prowess, no one else is none who can confront Suta's son in battle thus engaged.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: स त्वं कुरु महाबाहो कर्म युक्तमिहात्मनः। मातुलानां पितॄणां च तेजसोऽस्रबलस्य च॥
en: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, do you now perform what will be worthy of yourself, your maternal uncles, your sires and the measure of your energy and might.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: एतदर्थं हि हैडिम्बे पुत्रानिच्छन्ति मानवाः। कथं नस्तारयेद् दुःखात् स त्वं तारय बान्धवान्॥
en: It is for saving them from difficulties, that men desire to have sons; O son of Hidimba, do you therefore, rescue your fathers and friends.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: इच्छन्ति पितरः पुत्रान् स्वार्थ हेतोर्घटोत्कच। इहलोकात् परे लोके तारयिष्यन्ति ये हिताः॥
en: O Ghatotkacha, fathers desire to have sons, for furthering their own interests. And goc sons save their fathers here and hereafter.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: तव ह्यत्र बलं भीमं मायाश्च तव दुस्तराः। संग्रामे युध्यमानस्य सततं भीमनन्दन॥
