en: You are generous and your strength in battle is indeed terrible and matchless. While engaged in battle, there is none else equal to you.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: पाण्डवानां प्रभग्नानां कर्णेन निशि सायकैः। मजतां धार्तराष्ट्रेषु भव पारं परंतप॥
en: O afflicter of your foes, do you become the raft for the Pandavas when they are being routed in this hour of night by the shafts of Karna and when they are sinking in the ocean identified with the Dhartarashtra troops.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: रात्रौ हि राक्षसा भूयो भवन्त्यमितविक्रमाः। बलवन्तः सुदुर्धर्षाः शूरा विक्रान्तचारिणः॥
en: Moreover, at night the Rakshasas become possessed of immeasurable prowess; the Rakshasas are by nature powerful, indomitable, heroic and energetic in battle.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: जहि कर्णं महेष्वासं निशीथे मायया रणे। पार्था द्रोणं वधिष्यन्ति धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः॥
en: With the help of your illusions do you kill the fierce bowman Karna in this nocturnal fight. The of Pritha headed by Dhristadyumna will slay Drona in battle.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: संजय उवाच केशवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा बीभत्सुरपि राक्षसम्। अभ्यभाषत कौरव्य घटोत्कचमरिंदमम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing the words of Kesava, Vibhatsu also addressing that Rakshasa, that slayer of foes viz., Ghatotkacha said, O foremost of the Kurus, these words.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: घटोत्कच भवांश्चैव दीर्घबाहुश्च सात्यकिः। मतो मे सर्वसैन्येषु भीमसेनश्च पाण्डवः॥
en: 0 Ghatotkacha, yourself, the long-armed Satyaki and the Pandava Bhimasena, these, according to my opinion, are the foremost among all our troops.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: तद्भवान् यातु कर्णेन द्वैरथं युध्यतां निशि। सात्यकिः पृष्ठगोपस्ते भविष्यति महारथः॥
en: In this nocturnal fight do you therefore sons warrior Satyaki will become your protect or from behind.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: जहि कर्णं रणे शूरं सात्वतेन सहायवान्। यथेन्द्रस्तारकं पूर्वं स्कन्देन सह जनिवान्॥
en: Supported by the Satvata hero, do you slay the heroic Karna in battle, even as Indra supported by Skanda slew Taraka in days gone by.”

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: घटोत्कच उवाच अलमेवास्मि कर्णाय द्रोणायालं च भारत। अन्येषां क्षत्रियाणां च कृतास्राणां महात्मनाम्॥
en: Ghatotkacha said I am capable of encountering Karna and Drona, O Bharata and I am a match for all the other high-souled Kshatriyas accomplished in the use of weapons.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: अद्य दास्यामि संग्रामं सूतपुत्राय तं निशि। यं जनाः सम्प्रवक्ष्यन्ति यावद् भूमिर्धरिष्यति॥
en: This night, I shall fight such a fierce battle with the son of Suta, of which men will talk as long as the earth will exit.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: न चात्र शूरान् मोक्ष्यामि न भीतान्न कृताञ्जलीन्। सर्वानेव वधिष्यामि राक्षस धर्ममास्थितः॥
en: Following the Rakshasa mode, I shall not spare this time any body, either the brave or the coward or those that will with folded palms, solicit mercy. I shall slay all folded palms, solicit mercy. I shall slay all.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहु डिम्बिर्वरवीरहा। अभ्ययात् तुमुले कर्णं तव सैनयं विभीषयन्॥
en: Sanjaya said Having thus spoken, that slayer of hostile heroes namely the mighty-armed son of Hidimba, dashed against Karna, in that fierce fight, frightening your troops.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: तमापतन्तं संक्रुद्धं दीप्तास्यं दीप्तमूर्धजम्। प्रहसन् पुरुषव्याघ्रः प्रतिजग्राह सूतजः॥
en: Then that foremost of men that son of Suta smilingly received Ghatotkacha of blazing countenance and burning locks, as the latter was furiously falling upon him.

description: The charge of Ghatotkacha against Karna
sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं कर्णराक्षसयोर्मधे। गर्जतो राजशार्दूल शक्रप्रहादयोरिव॥
en: Then the battle between those two roaring heroes, viz., Karna and that Rakshasa, commenced resembling O foremost of kings that between Shakra and Pralhada in days gone by.

sn: संजय उवाच दृष्ट्वा घटोत्कचं राजन् सूतपुत्ररथं प्रति। आयान्तं तु तथा युक्तं जिबांसुं कर्णमाहवे॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O monarch, beholding the mightyarmed Ghatotkacha, rush against the car of Suta's son Karna, with a view to slaughter him,

sn: अब्रवीत् तत्र पुत्रस्ते दुःशासनमिदं वचः। एतद् रक्षो रणे तूर्णं दृष्ट्वा कर्णस्य विक्रमम्॥
en: Your Duryodhana addressing Dushasana said these works "Beholding Karna's prowess in battle, yonder does the Rakshasa

sn: अभियाति द्रुतं कर्णं तद् वारय महास्थम्। वृतः सैन्येन महता याहि यत्र महाबलः॥
en: Rush against that mighty car-warrior, Do you check the Rakshasa's progress; supported by mighty divisions do you go to the spot where the highly powerful.

sn: कर्णो वैकर्तनो युद्धे राक्षसेन युयुत्सति। रक्ष कर्णं रणे यत्तो वृतः सैन्येन मानद॥
en: Karna the son of Vikartana is fighting with the Rakshasa. O bestower of honor, putting forth your best energies in battle and supported by the troops do you protect Karna in battle.

sn: मा कर्ण राक्षसो घोरः प्रमादानाशयिष्यति। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राजञ्जटासुरसुतो बली॥
en: Let not the dreadful Rakshasa succeed, through our negligence, in slaying Karna. Meanwhile, O monarch, the highly puissant son of Jatasura.

sn: दुर्योधनमुपागम्य प्राह प्रहरतां वरः। दुर्योधन तवामित्रान् प्रख्यातान् युद्धदुमदान्॥ पाण्डवान् हन्तुमिच्छामि त्वयाऽऽज्ञप्तः सहानुगान्। जटासुरो मम पिता रक्षसां ग्रामणीः पुरा॥
en: That best of smiters, approaching Duryodhana said these words-"O Duryodhana, with your permission, do I intend to slay the Pandava brothers and their followers who are your inveterate enemies and who are regarded as indomitable in battle. My father was Jatasura that foremost of the Rakshasas, endued with great prowess.

sn: प्रयुज्य कर्म रक्षोघ्नं क्षुद्रैः पार्थेनिपातितः। तस्यापचितिमिच्छामि शत्रुशोणितपूजया। शत्रुमांसैश्च राजेन्द्र मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: In days gone by, through some Rakshasaslaying charms, the puny sons of Pritha slew him. I now desire to render satisfaction to his departed spirit by worshipping him with the blood of his foes.

sn: तमब्रवीत् ततो राजा प्रीयमाणः पुनः पुनः। द्रोणकर्णादिभिः सार्धं पर्याप्तोऽहं द्विषद्वधे॥
en: As also with their flesh. O foremost of kings, it behoves you to accord me your permission.” Thereupon king Duryodhana, highly gratified, repeatedly told these words to

sn: त्वं तु गच्छ मयाऽऽज्ञप्तो जहि युद्धे घटोत्कचम्। राक्षसं क्रूरकर्माणं रक्षोमानुषसम्भवम्॥
en: “Supported by Drona and Karna and others, I am competent enough to conquer my enemies. With my leave, do you go and slay the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha.

sn: पाण्डवानां हितं नित्यं हस्त्यश्वरथघातिनम्। वैहायसगतं युद्धे प्रेषयेर्यमसादनम्॥
en: That Rakshasa of fierce feats, born of men, ever devoted to the interests of the Pandavas and always slaying our elephants, horses and charioteer in battle.

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा महाकाय: समाहूय घटोत्कचम्। जाटासुरिभैंमसेनि नानाशस्त्रैरवाकिरत्॥
en: Staying himself all the while in the firmament, go dispatch him to Yama's (dreary) place.” Then that huge-bodied son of Jatasura saying “yea' to his words, challenged Ghatotkacha.

sn: अलम्बुषं च कर्णं च कुरुसैन्यं च दुस्तरम्। हैडिम्बिः प्रममाथैको महावातोऽमबुदानिव॥ ततो मायाबलं दृष्ट्वा रक्षस्तूर्णंमलम्बुषः। घटोत्कचं शरव्रातैर्नानालिङ्गैः समार्पयत्॥
en: Thereafter the son of Jatasura covered the son of Bhimasena with various kind of weapons. But the son of Hidimba, singlehanded, crushed Alambusha, Karna and the unfordable ocean of Kuru soldiers, like a furious tempest agitating the clouds. Thereafter the Rakshasa Alambusha seeing the potency of the illusion of Ghatotkacha.

sn: विद्ध्वा च बहुभिर्बाणैर्भमसेनि महाबलः। व्यद्रावयच्छरवातैः पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्॥
en: Quickly covered him with myriads of shafts. Piercing the son of Bhimasena with numerous arrows, Alambusha.

sn: तेन विद्राव्यमाणनि पाण्डुसैन्यानि भारत। निशीथे विप्रकीर्यन्ते वातनुन्ना घना इव॥
en: With his arrows, caused the Pandava armies to be routed. Routed by him the Pandavas troops, O Bharata.

sn: घटोत्कचशरैर्नुना तथैव तव वाहिनी। निशीथे प्राद्रवद् राजन्नुत्सृज्योल्काः सहस्रशः॥
en: Began to disperse in that night, like masses of clouds torn away by a furious gale. Similarly your troops mangled with the arrows of Ghatotkacha.

sn: अलम्बुषस्ततः क्रुद्धो भैमसेनि महामृधे। आजघ्ने दशभिर्बाणैस्तोत्रैरिव महाद्विपम्॥ तिलशस्तस्य संवाहं सूतं सर्वायुधानि च। घटोत्कचः प्रचिच्छेद प्रणदंश्चातिदारुणम्॥ ततः कर्णं शरवातैः कुरुनन्यान् सहस्रशः। अलम्बुषं चाभ्यवर्षन्मेघो मेरुमिवाचलम्॥ ततः संचुक्षुभे सैन्यं कुरूणां राक्षसार्दितम्। उपर्युपरि चान्योन्यं चतुरङ्गं ममर्द ह॥
en: Fled away in that night throwing, O monarch, all their flambeaus down. Thereafter wrought up with rage, Alambusha struck Bhima's son in that fierce battle, with numerous arrows, like a guide striking an elephant with the goad. Then Ghatotkacha cutoff into small fragments the chariot, the driver and the weapons of his opponent and laughed terrible. Then like clouds showering torrents of rain on the Meru mountain, Ghatotkacha poured showers of shafts of Karna, Alambusha and all the rest of Kurus. Afflicted by the Rakshasa, the Kuru troops became greatly agitated.

sn: जाटासुरिर्महाराज विरथो हतसारथिः। घटोत्कचं रणे क्रुद्धो मुष्टिनाभ्यहनद् दृढम्॥
en: The four kinds of forces of which your army consisted, began to press and crush one another. Then the son of Jatasura deprived of his car and driver.

sn: मुष्टिनाभ्याहतस्तेन प्रचचाल घटोत्कचः। क्षितिकम्पे यथा शैलः सवृक्षस्तृणगुल्मवान्॥
en: Wrathfully struck Ghatotkacha in that battle with his bare fists. Thus struck Ghatotkacha trembled.

sn: ततः स परिघाभेन द्विट्संघनेन बाहुना। जाटासुरिं भैमसेनिरवधीन्मुष्टिना भृशम्॥ तं प्रमथ्य ततः क्रुद्धस्तूर्णं हैडिम्बिराक्षिपत्। दोामिन्द्रध्वजाभाभ्यां निष्पिपेष च भूतले॥
en: Like a mountain with its trees, creepers and grass at the time of an earth-quake. Then the son of Bhimasena furious with rage, raising his own foe-slaying arm that resembled bludgeon, dealt a severe blow to Jatasura's son; thus furiously crushing him, the son of Hidimba quickly threw him down.

sn: जाटासुरिर्मोक्षयित्वा आत्मानं च घटोत्कचात्। पुनरुत्थाय वेगेन घटोत्कचमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: a And then seizing him by his two arms began to press him with great force against the earth. Then the son of Jatasura freeing himself from the grasp of Ghatotkacha.

sn: अलम्बुषोऽपि विक्षिप्य समुत्क्षिप्य च राक्षसम्। घटोत्कचं रणे रोषानिष्पिपेष च भूतले॥
en: Once more rose up quickly and rushed furiously upon the latter. Alambusha also, throwing down and dragging the Rakshasa.

sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं गर्जतोरतिकाययोः। घटोत्कचालम्बुषयोस्तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्॥ विशेषयन्तावन्योन्यं मायाभिरतिमायिनौ। युयुधाते महावीर्याविन्द्रवैरोचनाविव॥
en: Ghatotkacha, out of rage began to press him against the earth. Then between those two roaring heroes of huge proportion, namely Ghatotkacha and Alambusha, a battle raged that was extremely terrible and horripilating. Then those highly proud heroes, each desirous of getting advantage over the other by means of their illusive powers.

sn: पावकाम्बुनिधी भूत्वा पुनर्गरुडतक्षको। पुनर्मेघमहावातौ पुनर्वज्रमहाचलौ।॥
en: Fought on with great fury like the puissant Indra and the son of Virochana. Becoming fire and the ocean, again Garuda and Takshaka.

sn: पुनः कुञ्जरशार्दूलौ पुनः स्वर्भानुभास्करौ। एवं मायाशतसृजावन्योन्यवधकाङ्गिणौ॥
en: And once a cloud and a tempest and again thunder and a mighty mountain and an elephant and a tiger and Rahu and the sun.

sn: भृशं चित्रमयुध्येतामलम्बुषघटोत्कचौ। परिघैश्च गदाभिश्च प्रासमुद्गरपट्टिशैः॥ मुसलैः पर्वताग्रैश्च तावन्योन्यं विजनतुः।
en: They thus exhibited a hundred different kinds of illusions, desirous of compassing each other's destruction. Indeed Alambusha and Ghatotkacha fought most wonderfully, with bludgeons and maces and lances and mallets and battle axes and clubs and crests of mountains, they then struck each other.

sn: हयाभ्यां च गजाभ्यां च रथाभ्यां च पदातिभिः॥ युयुधाते महामायौ राक्षसप्रवरौ युधि।
en: Riding on the back of elephants or horses or on their chariots, those foremost of Rakshasas both possessed of potent illusive powers, fought with each other in that battle.

sn: ततो घटोत्कचो राजन्नलम्बुषवधेप्सया॥ उत्पपात भृशं क्रुद्धः श्येनवनिपपात च।
en: Thereafter, king Ghatotkacha, impelled by a desire for killing Alambusha and excited to the highest pitch of fury soared aloft and then came down even like a hawk.

sn: गृहीत्वा च महाकायं राक्षसेन्द्रमलम्बुषम्॥ उद्यम्य न्यवधीद् भूमौ मयं विष्णुरिवाहवे।
en: Then seizing that foremost of the Rakshasas, namely, the huge-bodied Alambusha, he raised him high and then dashed him against the earth, like Vishnu dashing Maya against the ground.

sn: ततो घटोत्कचः खङ्गमुद्धृत्याद्भुतदर्शनम्॥ रौद्रस्य काशिद्ध शिरो भीमं विकृतदर्शनम्। स्फुरतस्तस्य समरे नदतश्चातिभैरवम्॥ निचकर्त महाराज शत्रोरमितविक्रमः।
en: Then with a sword of beautiful appearance, Ghatotkacha of infinite prowess cut-off, 0 king, from the trunk of his fierce and mighty foe, his terrible head that was even then uttering Creadful roars and that looked frightful, O mighty monarch.

sn: शिरस्तच्चापि संगृह्य केशेषु रुधिरोक्षितम्॥ ययौ घटोत्कचस्तूर्णं दुर्योधनस्थं प्रति।
en: Then holding that blood-stained head by the hair, Ghatotkacha quickly proceeded towards the chariot of Duryodhana.

sn: अभ्येत्य च महाबाहुः स्मयमानः च राक्षसः॥ शिरो रथेऽस्य निक्षिप्य विकृताननमूधजम्।
en: Then the mighty-armed Rakshasa, approaching the car, smilingly threw that head with contorted aspect and dishevelied hair in that car of the king.

sn: प्राणदद् भैरवं नादं प्रावृषीव बलाहकः॥ अब्रवीच ततो राजन् दुर्योधनमिदं वचः।
en: Then like clouds during the rainy season, he uttered a tremendous roar; and then O king,

sn: एष ते निहतो बन्धुस्त्वया दृष्टोऽस्य विक्रमः॥ पुनर्देष्टासि कर्णस्य निष्ठामेतां तथाऽऽत्मनः।
en: Here is your friend slain whose prowess you have witnessed yourself. You are destined to see the death of Karna and that of your ownself.

sn: स्वधर्ममर्थं कामं च त्रितयं योऽभिवाञ्छति॥ रिक्तपाणिर्न पश्यत राजानं ब्राह्मणं स्त्रियम्।
en: There is a saying, O king, that no one, desirous of keeping his morality, profit and pleasure unprejudiced should never approach a king a Brahmana and a female with empty hands (i.e., without presents.)

sn: तिष्ठस्तव तावत् सुप्रीतो यावत् कर्ण वधाम्यहम्॥ एवमुक्त्वा ततः प्रायात् कर्णं प्रति नरेश्वर।
en: Do you live without any anxiety whatever up to the time I do not slay Karna." Having thus spoken, O foremost of men, he rushed against Karna.

sn: किरज्छरगणांस्तीक्ष्णान् रुषितो रणमूर्धनि॥ ततः समभवद् युद्धं घोररूपं भयानकम्। विस्मापनं महाराज नरराक्षसयोर्मधे॥
en: Scattering hundreds of sharp arrows and directing them at the head of Karna. Then, O mighty monarch, a battle of terrible aspect and great fierceness commenced between the human hero and the Rakshasa-battle that filled every heart with great admiration.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यत्तद् वैकर्तनः कर्णो राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः। निशीथे समसजेतां तद् युद्धमभवत् कथम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said How did that battle between Vikartarna's son Kama and the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha rage at that dead of night when they encountered each other?

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: कीदृशं चाभवद् रूपं तस्य घोरस्य रक्षसः। स्थश्च कीदृशस्तस्य हयाः सर्वायुधानि च॥
en: What appearance did that terrible Rakshasa then assume? How looked his car and his steeds and what was the nature of his weapons?

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: किंप्रमाणा हयास्तस्य रथकेतुर्धनुस्तथा। कीदृशं वर्म चैवास्य शिरस्त्राणं च कीदृशम्॥ पृष्टस्त्वमेतदाचक्ष्व कुशलो ह्यासि संजय।
en: What was the measure of his horses, his standard and his bow? What kind of armour and head-gear did he then wear? O Sanjaya, expert as you are in the art of narration, tell me all this as I am asking you about them.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: संजय उवाच लोहिताक्षो महाकायस्ताम्रास्यो निम्नितोदरः॥ ऊर्ध्वरोमा हरिश्मश्रुः शङ्कुकर्णो महाहनुः। आकर्णदारितास्यश्च तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रः करालवान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Ghatotkacha was of gigantic proportion; his eyes were crimson; the hue of his countenance was coppery; his belly was low and sunk. The hair on his body were erect, his head was green; his ears were straight like shafts; and his check bones were high.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: सुदीर्घताम्रजिह्वोष्ठो लम्बभूः स्थूलनासिकः। नीलाङ्गो लोहितग्रीवो गिरिवर्पा भयंकरः॥
en: His mouth was large, extending from ear to ear. His teeth were sharp and four of them were long and pointed. His tongue and his lips were long and of a coppery hue. His brows were long drawn. His nose was thick.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: महाकायो महाबाहुर्महाशी। महाबलः। विकृतः परुषस्पर्शो विकटोवृद्धपिण्डकः॥
en: His body was of blue complexion, his neck was red. Tall as a mountain he was frightful to look at; of huge stature huge arms and huge head, he possessed unequaled strength.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: स्थूलस्फिग्गूढनाभिश्च शिथिलोपचयो महान्। तथैव हस्ताभरणी महामायोऽङ्गदी तथा॥
en: His limbs were hard and ugly, the hair on his head was tied in a ugly shape upwards. His hips were spacious and his navel was deep. His proportion were gigantic although they were not so strong.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: उरसा धारयन् निष्कमग्निमालां यथाचलः। तस्य हेममयं चित्रं बहुरूपाङ्गशोभितम्॥
en: His arms were duly adorned and that one of potent illusive energy wore Angadas and a cuirass on his breast like a circle of fire on the breast of a mountain.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तोरणप्रतिमं शुभं किरीटं मूर्ध्यशोभित।
en: A bright and beautiful diadem made of gold adorned his head-diadem of which every part was proportionate and resplendent and which looked like an arch.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: कुण्डले बाल सूर्यामे मालां हेममयीं शुभाम्॥ घारयन् विपुलं कांस्यं कवचं च महाप्रभम्।
en: His ear-rings were effulgent like the morning sun and his garlands were of gold and exceedingly bright. His body was cased in a massive brazen armour of great effulgence.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: किंकिणीशतनिर्घोषं रक्तध्वजपताकिनम्॥ ऋक्षचौवनद्धाङ्गं नल्वमानं महारथम्।
en: His chariot of gigantic size and of the measure of a Nalva and covered with bear-skin was adorned with a hundred tinkling bells and from its standard fluttered numerous crimson banners.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: सर्वायुधवरोपेतमास्थितो ध्वजशालिनम्॥ अष्टचक्रसमायुक्तं मेघगम्भीरनिःस्वनम्।
en: It was well furnished with all sorts of weapons, offensive and defensive and was decked with a festoon of bannerets. It possessed eight wheels and its clatter resembled the deep rumble of rain-clouds.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: मत्तमातङ्गसंकाशा लोहिताक्षा विभीषणाः॥ कामवर्णजवा युक्ता बलवन्तः शतं हयाः।
en: The horses yoked thereto were stout mettled, of chequered complexion, fleet, of red eyed and like infuriate elephants.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: वहन्तो राक्षसं घोरं बालवन्तो जितश्रमाः॥ विपुलाभिः सटाभिस्ते ह्येवमाणा मुहुर्मुहुः।
en: Those indefatigable and spirited steeds bore the dreadful Rakshasa to battle, neighing and throwing back their thick mains repeatedly.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: राक्षसोऽस्य विरूपाक्षः सूतो दीप्तास्यकुण्डलः॥ रश्मिभिः सूर्यरश्म्याभैः संजग्राह हयान् रणे।
en: A Rakshasa of frightful eyes and decked with bright ear-rings and possessing a fierce mouth acted as his charioteer, checking the horses by the rains that were as bright as the rays of the sun.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: स तेन सहितस्तस्थावरुणेन यथा रविः॥ संसक्त इव चाभ्रेण यथाद्रिमहता महान्।
en: Accompanied by that charioteer he came like the sun accompanied by his charioteer Arjuna (dawn). Looking like a high mountain enveloped in cloudy masses.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: दिवःस्पृक् सुमहान् केतुः स्यन्दनेऽस्य समुच्छ्रितः।। १७ रक्तोत्तमाङ्गः क्रव्यादो गृध्रः परमभीषणः।
en: A huge standard, touching the very clouds was set upon his chariot. A dreadful vulture of crimson body and flash-eating was the device on his standards.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: वासवाशनिनिर्घोषं दृढज्यमतिविक्षिपन्॥ व्यक्तं किष्कुपरीणाहं द्वादशारत्निकार्मुकम्।
en: The Rakshasa then advanced, forcibly stretching his bow of which the twang resembled the rattle of Indra's thunder and the string was very though and which measured twelve Aranis in length and one in breadth

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: रथाक्षमात्रैरिषुभिः सर्वाः प्रच्छादयन् दिशः॥ तस्यां वीरापहारिण्यां निशायां कर्णमभ्ययात्।
en: Filling all the quarters of the heaven with arrows of the measures of the Aksha of a car, the Rakshasa assailed Karna in that night that witnessed the destruction of so many heroes.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तस्य विक्षिपतश्चापं रथे विष्टभ्य तिष्ठतः॥ अश्रूयत धनुघोंषो विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः।
en: Proudly seated on his car, as he stretched his bow, the twang that was heard resembled the rumble of the roaring thunder.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तेन वित्रास्यमानानि तव सैन्यानि भारत॥ समकम्पन्त सर्वाणि सिन्धोरिव महोर्मयः।
en: Frightened at that sound, your troops O Bharata, trembled like the surging billows of the sea.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य विरूपाक्षं विभीषणम्॥ उत्स्मयन्निव राधेयस्त्वरमाणोऽभ्यवारयत्।
en: Beholding that one of frightful eyes and dreadful aspect rush towards himself, the son of Radha quickly withstood him in all cheerfulness.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ततः कर्णोऽभ्ययादेनमस्यन्नस्यन्तमन्तिकात्॥ मातङ्ग इव मातङ्गं यूथर्षभमिवर्षभः।
en: Karna then advanced against the smiting Rakshasa smiting him in return from a near point, like an elephant rushing against another or a bull charging another.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: स संनिपातस्तुमुलस्तयोरासीद् विशाम्पते॥ कर्णराक्षसयो राजनिन्द्रशम्बरयोरिव।
en: Then the dreadful collision, o mighty monarch, that took place between Karna and the Rakshasa, resembled ( ruler of men that between Shakra and Samvara (in days gone by).

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तौ प्रगृह्य महावेगे धनुषी भीमनिःस्वने॥ प्राच्छादयतामन्योन्यं तक्षमाणौ महेषुभिः।
en: Each then grasping a fearful bow of loud twang began to wound and cover the other with mighty shafts.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ततः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैरिषुभिर्नतपर्वभिः॥ न्यवारयेतामन्योन्यं कांस्ये निर्भिद्य वर्मणी।
en: Then penetrating each other's brazen armours, they pierced each other with shafts of depressed knots, shot from bows drawn to the fullest stretch.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तौ नखैरिव शार्दूलौ दन्तैरिव महाद्विपौ॥ रथशक्तिभिरन्योन्यं विशिखैश्च ततक्षतुः।
en: Then like two tigers mangling each other with claws or two elephants with their tusks, they mangled each other with their lances and arrows and javelins.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: संछिन्दन्तौ च गात्राणि संदधानौ च सायकान्॥ दहन्तौ च शरोल्काभिर्दुष्प्रेक्ष्यौ च बभूवतुः।
en: Mangling each other's body, aiming their shafts at each other and burning each other with myriads of shafts, they could not be gazed at.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तौ तु विक्षतसर्वाङ्गौ रुधिरौघपरिप्लुतौ॥ व्यभ्राजेतां यथा वारि स्रवन्तौ गैरिकाचलौ।
en: Covered with arrow-wounds all over the body and steeped in torrents of blood, they both looked beautiful like two hills of red chalk with rivulets flowing down their sides.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तौ शराग्रविनुन्नाङ्गौ निर्भिन्दन्तौ परस्परम्॥ नाकम्पयेतामन्योन्यं यतमानौ महाद्युती।
en: Those two mighty car-warriors, though they were striving hard and each had his limbs torn open with points of shafts, could not make each other flinch or tremble.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तत् प्रवृत्तं निशायुद्धं चिरं सममिवाभवत्॥ प्राणयोर्दीव्यतो राजन् कर्णराक्षसयोर्मधे।
en: That nocturnal combat between Karna and the Rakshasa, with both regarded as a game having their lives for the stake, seemed for a long time to be a equal one.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तस्य संदधतस्तीक्ष्णञ्छरांश्चासक्तमस्यतः॥ धनुर्घोषण वित्रस्ताः स्वे परे च तदाभवन्।
en: As Ghatotkacha placed keen shafts on his string and as he let them off, his foes and friends alike became terrified with the twang of his bow.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: घटोत्कचं यदा कर्णो विशेषयति नो नृप॥ ततः प्रादुष्करोद् दिव्यमस्रमस्रविदां वरः।
en: Then, O king, Karna was unable to gain any advantage over Ghatotkacha. Thereafter that foremost of all persons versed in the use of weapons, invoked into existence a celestial weapon.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: कर्णेन संधितं दृष्ट्वा दिव्यमस्र घटोत्कचः॥ प्रादुश्चक्रे महामायां राक्षसी पाण्डुनन्दनः।
en: Thereupon the king of the Rakshasas beholding a celestial weapon aimed at him, by Karna, brought into use his Rakshasa illusion.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: शूलमुद्गरधारिण्या शैलपादपहस्तया॥ रक्षसां घोररूपाणां महत्या सेनया वृतः।
en: Instantly he was encircled by a numerous force of dreadful looking Rakshasas armed with lances and large rocks and stones and clubs.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तमुद्यतमहाचापं दृष्ट्वा ते व्यथिता नृपाः॥ भूतान्तकमिवायान्तं कालदण्डोग्रधारिणम्।
en: Beholding the Rakshasa come with an uplifted weapon like the Destroyer of beings armed with his fatal bludgeon, all the kings of your host were filled with terror.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: घटोत्कचप्रयुक्तेन सिंहनादेन भीषिताः॥ प्रसुवुर्गजा मूत्रं विव्यथुश्च नरा भृशम्।
en: Frightened at the war-cries uttered by Ghatotkacha the elephants discharged urine and men were sorely afflicted.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ततोऽश्मवृष्टिरत्युग्रा महत्यासीत् समन्ततः॥ अर्धरात्रेऽधिकबलैर्विमुक्ता रक्षसां बलैः।
en: Then a mighty shower of rocks and stones fell on all sides, being poured incessantly by the Rakshasas, who had acquired greater strength, in consequence of the hour being mid-night.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: आयसानि च चक्राणि भुशुण्ड्यः शक्तितोमराः॥ पतन्त्यविरलाः शूलाः शतघ्यः पट्टिशास्तथा।
en: Iron wheels, Bhusundis, javelins, lances and spears and Shataghnis and battle axes, then began to fall in torrents.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तदुग्रमतिरौद्रं च दृष्ट्वा युद्धं नराधिप।॥ पुत्राश्च तव योधाश्च व्यथिता विप्रदुद्रुवुः।
en: Then beholding that battle fierce to the extreme, your son and your warriors sorely afflicted (with terror) took to their heels.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तत्रैकोऽस्रबलश्लाघी कर्णो मानी च विव्यथे॥ व्यधमच शरैर्मायां तां घटोत्कचनिर्मिताम्। मायायां तु प्रहीणायाममर्षाच घटोत्कचः॥ विससर्ज शरान् घोरान् सूतपुत्रं च आविशन्।
en: The proud Karna alone, ever boastful of strength of his weapons, was not terrified and he continued to stay on the field, baffling with his arrows the illusions displayed by Ghatotkacha. Ghatotkacha then discharged dreadful arrows for compassing the death of Suta's son.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ततस्ते रुधिराभ्यक्ता भित्त्वा कर्ण महाहवे॥ विविशुर्धरणी बाणा: संक्रुद्धा इव पन्नगाः।
en: Then those arrows piercing through Karna and steeped in blood entered the earth like so many infuriate snakes.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: सूतपुत्रस्तु संक्रुद्धो लघुहस्तः प्रतापवान्॥ घटोत्कचमतिक्रम्य बिभेद दशभिः शरैः।
en: Thereupon the light-handed and puissant son of Suta excited to the highest pitch of fury, prevailing over Ghatotkacha, pierced him with ten shafts.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: घटोत्कचो विनिर्भिन्नः सूतपुत्रेण मर्मसु॥ चक्रं दिव्यं सहस्रारमगृह्णाद् व्यथितो भृशम्।
en: Pierced in his vital parts and extremely pained by the son of Suta, Ghatotkacha took up a discus of celestial make having a thousands pokes.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: क्षुरान्तं बालसूर्याभं मणिरत्नविभूषितम्॥ चिक्षेपाधिरथेः क्रुद्धो भैमसेनिर्जिघांसया।
en: Then the son of Bhima, desirous of slaying the son of Adhiratha, hurled at the latter that discus furnished with a razor-sharp edge, of the effulgence of the morning sun and decked with gems and jewels.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: प्रविद्धमतिवेगेन विक्षिप्तं कर्णसायकैः॥ अभाग्यस्येव संकल्पस्तन्मोघमपतद् भुवि।
en: That discus of great impetus and hurled with great force, was cut-off into fragments with the shafts of Karna and it fell down on the earth baffled in its object, like the hopes and purposes of an unfortunate man.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: घटोत्कचस्तु संक्रुद्धो दृष्ट्वा चक्रं निपातितम्॥ कर्णं प्राच्छादयद् बाणैः स्वार्भानुरव भास्करम्।
en: Beholding his discus thus baffled, Ghatotkacha was highly enraged and he then covered Karna with his arrows like Rahu covering the sun.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: सूतपुत्रस्त्वसम्भ्रान्तो रुद्रोपेन्द्रेन्द्रविक्रमः॥ घटोत्कचरथं तूर्णं छादयामास पत्रिभिः।
en: But the son of Suta Karna possessed prowess equal to that of Rudra or Upendra or Indra himself dauntlessly covered Ghatotkacha's chariot with his winged arrows.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: घटोत्कचने क्रुद्धेन गदा हेमाङ्गदा तदा॥ क्षिप्ताऽऽभ्राम्य शरैः सापि कर्णेनाभ्याहतापतत्।
en: Thereafter a gold-decked mace was whirled and hurled at Karna by Ghatotkacha. But the former cutting it off with his arrows felled it on the ground.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षमुत्पत्य कालमेघ इवोन्नदन्॥ प्रववर्ष महाकायो दुमवर्ष नभस्तलात्।
en: Then soaring into the sky and roaring like destructive clouds, the huge-bodied Rakshasa poured a veritable shower of trees from the skies.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ततो मायाविनं कर्णो भीमसेनसुतं दिवि॥ मार्गणैरभिविव्याध घनं सूर्य इवांशुभिः।
en: Then Karna pierced with his shafts the son of Bhimasena versed in illusion when he was ranging through the skies, like the sun piercing the clouds with his rays.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तस्य सर्वान् हयान् हत्वा संछिद्य शतधा रथम्॥ अभ्यवर्षच्छरैः कर्णः पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्।
en: Next cutting his car into fragments and slaying all his horses, Karna covered him with arrows, like a cloud charged with rain.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: न चास्यासीदनिर्भिनं गात्रे सोऽदृश्यत मुहूर्तेन श्वाविच्छललितो यथा।
en: There was not even space of two finger's breadth in the body of Ghatotkacha that was not pierced with Karna's shafts. Soon the Rakshasa appeared to be like a porcupine with its quills erect.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: न हयान्न रथं तस्य न ध्वजं न घटोत्कचम्॥ दृष्टवन्तः सम समरे शरौघैरभिसंवृतम्।
en: So completely was he covered with shafts that we could not in that battle, any longer see either Ghatotkacha's person or his horses or his car or standard.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: व्यङ्गुलमन्तरम्॥ स तु कर्णस्य तद् दिव्यमस्रमस्रेण शातयन्॥ मायायुद्धेन मायावी सूतपुत्रमयोधयत्।
en: Then the Rakshasa versed in illusion destroying by his own weapon the celestial weapon of Karna, began to fight with Suta's son, aided by his own illusive powers.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: सोऽयोधयत् तदा कर्णं माया लाघवेन च॥ अलक्ष्यमाणानि दिवि शरजालानि चापतन्।
en: Indeed he fought on with Karna, aided by his illusive powers and exhibiting his great agility. Then showers of shafts began to fall from invisible quarters in the skies.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: भैमसेनिर्महामायो मायया कुरुसत्तम्॥ विचचार महाकायो मोहयन्निव भारत।
en: Then Bhimasena's son possessed of potent powers of illusion, O best of the Kurus, assumed, by the help of those powers, a dreadful appearance and began to confound the Kouravas, O Bharata.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: स तु कृत्वा विरूपाणि वदनान्यशुभानि च॥ अग्रसत् सूतपुत्रस्य दिव्यान्यस्राणि मायया।
en: The puissant Rakshasa then assuming many terrible heads, began to swallow up the celestial weapons of Karna.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: पुनश्चापि महाकायः संछिन्नः शतधा रणे॥ गतसत्त्वो निरुत्साहः पतितः खाद्ध्यदृश्यत।
en: Soon again, the huge Rakshasas with hundred of wounds on his body seemed to lie cheerlessly and like one dead, on the field.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तं हतं मन्यमानाः स्म प्राणदन् कुरुपुङ्गवाः॥ अथ देहेर्नवैरन्यैर्दिक्षु सर्वास्वदृश्यता
en: The foremost of the Kouravas then considering Ghatotkacha to be dead uttered loud joyous shouts. Soon however, he was seen to assume new forms and roving in all direction.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: पुनश्चापि महाकायः शतशीर्षः शतोदरः॥ व्यदृश्यत महाबाहुर्मैनाक इव पर्वतः।
en: Next he was seen to assume a huge form with a hundred heads and hundred stomachs and looked like the Mainaka mountain.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रो भूत्वा च पुनरेव स राक्षसः॥ सागरोमिरिवोद्भूतस्तिर्यगूर्ध्वमवर्तत।
en: Once again he became small about the transversely or soared high like the surging billows of the ocean.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: वसुधां दारयित्वा च पुनरप्सु न्यमजत॥ अदृश्यत तदा तत्र पुनरुन्मज्जितोऽन्यतः।
en: Tearing through the earth, he dived again into the waters. Once seen here he was next seen rising on the surface at a different place.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: सोऽवतीर्य पुनस्तस्थौ रथे हेमपरिष्कृते॥ क्षितिं खं च दिशश्चैव माययाभ्येत्य दंशितः।
en: Then coming down from the welkin, he was seen standing, covered in mail, on a chariot adorned with gold, having wandered through earth and sky and all the points of the compass aided by his powers of illusion.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: गत्वा कर्णरथाभ्याशं व्यचरत् कुण्डलाननः॥ प्राह वाक्यमसम्भ्रान्तः सूतपुत्रं विशाम्पते।
en: Then going near the vicinity of Karna's chariot, Ghatotkacha with his his ear-rings moving, dauntlessly addressed the son of Suta, O king, in these words.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तिष्ठेदानी क्व मे जीवन सूतपुत्र गमिष्यसि॥ युद्धश्रद्धामहं तेऽद्य विनेष्यामि रणाजिरे।
en: Wait a little, O son of Suta, whither shall you go with your life, avoiding me? Today I shall remove your itching for fight on the field of battle.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: इत्युक्त्वा रोषाताम्राक्षं रक्षः क्रूरपराक्रमम्॥ उत्पपातान्तरिक्षं च जहास च सुविस्तरम्।
en: Having thus spoken, the Rakshasa of fierce prowess, with his eyes red in rage, soared into the sky and laughed a tremendous laugh.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: कर्णमभ्यहनच्चैव गजेन्द्रमिव केसरी॥ रथाक्षमात्रैरिषुभिरभ्यवर्षद् घटोत्कचः।
en: Then Ghatotkacha assailed Karna like a lion attacking an elephant; and he then covered with his showers of arrows of the measure of the Aksha of a car.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: रथिनामृषभं कर्णं धाराभिरिव तोयदः॥ शरवृष्टिं च तां कर्णो दूरात् प्राप्तामशातयत्।
en: That foremost car-warrior viz., Karna, like a could with showers of rain. But Karna repulsed that arrowy shower before it could reach him.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: दृष्ट्वा च विहतां मायां कर्णेन भरतर्षभ॥ घटोत्कचस्ततो मायां ससर्जन्तर्हितः पुनः।
en: Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, seeing his illusions nullified by Karna, Ghatotkacha once more put forth another illusion and rendered himself invisible.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: सोऽभवद् गिरिरत्युचः शिखरैस्तरुसंकटैः॥ शूलप्रासासिमुसलजलप्रस्रवणो महान्।
en: He then became a huge mountain with numerous peaks, covered with tall trees. From that mountain streams of lances, spears, swords and maces began to issue out incessantly.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तमञ्जनचयप्रख्यं कर्णो दृष्ट्वा महीधरम्॥ प्रपातैरायुधान्युग्राण्युद्वहन्तं न चुक्षुभे।
en: Beholding that mountain resembling a heap of antimony from which fierce weapons continuously flowed out, Karna was not at all daunted.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: स्मयन्निव ततः कर्णो दिव्यमस्रमुदैरयत्॥ ततः सोऽस्रेण शैलेन्द्रो विक्षिप्तौ वै न्यनश्यत।
en: Then smiling, Karna invoked into existence a celestial weapon. Then that foremost of mountains, cut and thrown off by that weapons of Karna, was completely destroyed.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ततः स तोयदो भूत्वा नील: सेन्द्रायुधो दिवि॥ अश्मवृष्टिभिरत्युग्रः सूतपुत्रमवाकिरत्।
en: Thereafter the Rakshasa becoming a blue cloud decked with the rain-bow began to cover the son of Suta with a fierce shower of stones.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: अथ संधाय वायव्यमस्रमस्रविदां वरः॥ व्यधमत् कालमेघं तं कर्णो वैकर्तनो वृषः।
en: Then that foremost of all persons versed in the use of weapons, viz., Karna, the son of Vikartana, discharging the Vayavya weapon destroyed that blue cloud.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: स मार्गणगणैः कर्णो दिशः प्रच्छाद्य सर्वशः॥ जघानास्रं महाराज घटोत्कचसमीरितम्।
en: Then, O king, covered the quarters of the compass with his arrows, Karna baffled the weapons shot by Ghatotkacha.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ततः प्रहस्य समरे भैमसेनिर्महाबलः॥ प्रादुश्चक्रे महामायां कर्णं प्रति महारथम्।
en: Then the highly puissant son of Bhimasena smiling the while invoked into existence an allpowerful illusion against that mighty carwarrior viz., Karna.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: स दृष्ट्वा पुनरायान्तं रथेन रथिनां वरम्॥ घटोत्कचमसम्भ्रान्तं राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृतम्।
en: Beholding then that foremost of carwarriors viz., Ghatotkacha, dauntlessly approach him surrounded by a large number of Rakshasa.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: सिंहशार्दूलसदृशैर्मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमैः॥ गजस्थैश्च रथस्थैश्च वाजिपृष्ठगतैस्तथा।
en: That resembled lion and tigers and infuriate powerful elephants, mounted on elephants, some on chariots and some on horses.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: नानाशस्रधरैोरै नाकवचभूषणैः॥ वृतं घटोत्कचं क्रूरैर्मरुद्भिरिव वासवम्।
en: All bearing various kinds of weapons and wearing diverse kinds of armour and ornaments indeed beholding Ghatotkacha surrounded by these fearful Rakshasas like Vasava by the Marutas.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: दृष्ट्वा कर्णो महेष्वासो योधयामास राक्षसम्॥ घटोत्कचस्ततः कर्णं विद्ध्वा पञ्चभिराशुगैः।
en: The mighty bowman Karna began to fight with him fiercely. Then Ghatotkacha piercing Karna with five arrows.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ननाद भैरवं नादं भीषयन् सर्वपार्थिवान्॥ भूयश्चाञ्जलिकेनाथ सम्मार्गणगणं महत्। कर्णहस्तस्थितं चापं चिच्छेदाशु घटोत्कचः॥ अथान्यद् धनुरादाय दृढं भारसहं महत्। विचकर्ष बलात् कर्ण इन्द्रायुधमिवोच्छ्रितम्॥
en: some

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ततः कर्णो महाराज प्रेषयामास सायकान्।
en: Uttered a tremendous war-cry, filling all the kings with terror. Once more with an Anjalika, Ghatotkacha quickly cut-off the bow of Karna held in his hands together with the arrows fitted thereon. Thereupon Karna taking up another mighty bow capable of bearing a greater strain and looking like the bow of Indra itself, began to stretch it forcibly; thereafter, O king, Karna sped arrows.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: सुवर्णपुलाञ्छत्रुघ्नान् खेचरान् राक्षसान् प्रति॥ तद् बाणैरर्दितं यूथं रक्षसां पीनवक्षसाम्।
en: Furnished with golden wings, capable of slaying foes and ranging through the welkin at those Rakshasas. Afflicted with those shafts that host of broad-chested Rakshasas.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: सिंहनेवादितं वन्यं गजानामाकुलं कुलम्॥ विघम्य राक्षसान् बाणैः साश्वसूतगजान् विभुः।
en: Appeared agitated like a host of wild elephants attacked by a lion. Burning with his arrows the Rakshasas and their horses, charioteer and elephant, O lord.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ददाह भगवान् वह्निर्भूतानीव युगक्षये॥ स हत्वा राक्षसी सेनां शुशुभे सूतनन्दनः।
en: The heroic Karna appeared like the god of fire burning down creatures at the end of a Yuga. Slaying that Rakshasa host, the son of Suta appeared beautiful.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: पुरेव त्रिपुरं दग्ध्वा दिवि देवा महेश्वरः॥ तेषु राजसहस्रेषु पाण्डवेयेषु मारिष।
en: Like the god Maheshvara after he had destroyed Tripura in the days of yore. Among the thousands of king belonging to the Pandavas, O sire.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: नैनं निरीक्षितुमपि कश्चिच्छक्नोति पार्थिवः॥ ऋते घटोत्कचाद् राजन् राक्षसेन्द्रान्महाबलात्। भीमवीर्यबलोपेतात् क्रुद्धाद वैवस्वतादिव॥ तस्य क्रुद्धस्य नेत्राभ्यां पावकः समजायत। महोल्काभ्यां यथा राजन् सार्चिषः स्नेहबिन्दवः॥ तलं तलेन संहत्य संदश्य दशनच्छदम्।
en: There was none who could then even look at Karna. O ruler of men, except the powerful Ghatotkacha, that foremost of Rakshasas who was possessed of terrible energy and mighty and who burning with wrath, then looked like the himself. Excited as he was with wrath flames of fire seemed to issue out of his eyes, like burning drops of oil from a pair of flambeaus; then striking his palms against each other and biting his nether lip.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: रथमास्थाय च पुनर्मायया निर्मितं तदा॥ युक्तं गजनिभैर्वाहैः पिशाचवदनैः खरैः।
en: The Rakshasa was seen to ride a car the creation of his own illusion to which were yoked asses looking like elephants and having the heads of Pisachas.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: स सूतमब्रवीत् क्रुद्धः सूतपुत्राय मां वह॥ स ययौ घोररूपेण रथेन रथिनां वरः। द्वैरथं सूतपुत्रेण पुनरेव विशाम्पते॥
en: Then excited with rages he addressed his charioteer saying, “Take me near the son of Suta.” Then that foremost of car-warriors riding on that chariot of fearful aspect.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: स चिक्षेप पुनः क्रुद्धः सूतपुत्राय राक्षसः। अष्टचक्रां महाघोरामशनि रुद्रनिर्मिताम्॥ द्वियोजनसमुत्सेधां योजनायामविस्तराम्। आयसीं निचितां शूलैः कदम्बमिव केसरैः॥
en: An Asani of dreadful appearance furnished with eight wheels and manufactured by Rudra himself. Placing his bow on his car and jumping down on the earth.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तामवप्लुत्य जग्राह कर्णो न्यस्य महद् धनुः। चिक्षेप चैनां तस्यैव स्यन्दनात् सोऽवपुप्लुवे॥ साश्वसूतध्वजं यानं भस्म कृत्वा महाप्रभा।
en: And hurled it back at Ghatotkacha. The latter however had jumped down from his car. Meanwhile that highly resplendent weapon burning down the Rakshasa's car with its charioteer, horses and standard.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: विवेश वसुधां भित्त्वा सुरास्तत्र विसिस्मियुः॥ कर्ण तु सर्वभूतानि पूजयामासुरञ्जसा।
en: Entered the earth, piercing through her bowels, thereby filling the gods with wonder. Then all creatures applauded Karna.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: यदवप्लुत्य जग्राह देवसृष्टां महाशनिम्॥ एवं कृत्वा रणे कर्ण आरुरोह रथं पुनः।
en: Inasmuch as he succeeded in grasping the Asani of celestial make, having jumped down from his car. Having achieved this feat, Karna again ascended his car.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: ततो मुमोच नाराचान् सूतपुत्रः परंतप॥ अशक्यं कर्तुमन्येन सर्वभूतेषु मानद। यदकार्षीत् तदा कर्णः संग्रामे भीमदर्शने॥ स हन्यमानो नाराचैर्धाराभिरिव पर्वतः।
en: Thereafter that afflicter of foes, namely the son of Suta began to shoot his arrows. O giver of honour what Karna then achieved in that battle of fierce aspect was incapable of being achieved by any other creatures. Then struck with his Narachas like a mountain by showers of rain.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: गन्धर्वनगराकारः पुनरन्तरधीयत॥ एवं स वै महाकायो मायया लाघवेन च। अस्राणि तानि दिव्यानि जघान रिपुसूदनः॥ निहन्यमानेष्वस्रेषु मायया तेन रक्षसा। असम्भ्रान्तस्तदा कर्णस्तद् रक्षः प्रत्ययुध्यत॥ निहन्यमानेष्वस्रेषु मायया तेन रक्षसा।
en: Ghatotkacha of aerial from once more disappeared from the view. Fighting in this way, the huge Rakshasa, the slayer of foes, destroyed the celestial weapons of Karna, by means of high agility and illusive powers. Thus although his weapons were destroyed by the illusive powers of that Rakshasa.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: असम्भ्रान्तस्तदा कर्णस्तद् रक्षः प्रत्ययुध्यत॥ ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज भैमसेनिर्महाबलः।
en: Karna dauntlessly fought on with him. Thereupon the highly puissant son of Bhima, O king, being worked up with rage.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: चकार बहुधाऽऽत्मानं भीषयाणो महारथान्॥ ततो दिग्भ्यः समापेतुः सिंहव्याघ्रतरक्षवः। अग्निजिह्वाश्च भुजगा विहगाश्चाप्ययोमुखाः॥ स कीर्यमाणो विशिखैः कर्णचापच्युतैः शरैः।
en: Multiplied himself many times thereby inspiring terror in to the hearts of mighty carwarriors. Thereafter from all the points of the compass lions, tigers, hyenas, fire-tongued snakes and iron-beaked rangers of the sky, began to issue out. Covered with the swiftlyflying arrows shot from Karna's bow.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: नागराडिव दुष्प्रेक्ष्यस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥ राक्षसाश्च पिशाचाश्च यातुधानास्तथैव च।
en: That gigantic Rakshasa looking like the prince of mountains, disappeared then and there. Then numerous Rakshasas, Pisachas, Yatudhanas and.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: शालावृकाश्च बहवो वृकाश्च विकृताननाः॥ ते कर्णं क्षपयिष्यन्तः सर्वतः समुपाद्रवन्।
en: Peaks of wolves and leopards of frightful aspects, rushed upon Karna for devouring him.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: अथैनं वाग्भिरुग्राभिस्रासयांचक्रिरे तदा॥ उद्यतैर्बहुभि।रैरायुधैः शोणितोक्षितैः।
en: These then tried to frighten Karna by their fierce yells. With many dreadful weapons ready for use and steeped in blood.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: तेषामनेकैरेकैकं कर्णो विव्याध सायकैः॥ प्रतिहत्य तु तां मायां दिव्येनास्त्रेण राक्षसीम्।
en: Karna pierced each of those monsters. Then with a celestial weapons baffling that illusion of the Rakshasa,

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: आजघान हयानस्य शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ ते भग्ना विक्षताङ्गाश्च भिन्नपृष्ठाश्च सायकैः।
en: He wounded the former's fierce steeds with arrows of depressed knots. Those steeds thus maimed and deprived of their limbs and with their backs lacerated with Karna's arrows.

description: The combat between Karna and Ghatotkacha
sn: वसुधामन्वपद्यन्त पश्यतस्तस्य रक्षसः॥ स भग्नमायो हैडिम्ब कर्णं वैकर्तनं तदा। एष ते विदधे मृत्युमित्युक्त्वान्तरधीयत॥
en: Fell down on the earth, even before the eyes of that Rakshasa. The son of Hidimba seeing his illusions baffled once more made himself invincible, speaking thus to Vikartana's son-"I will presently compass your slaughter."

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: संजय उवाच तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तमाने कर्णराक्षसयोर्मधे। अलायुधो राक्षसेन्द्रो वीर्यवानभ्यवर्तत॥
en: Sanjaya sajd When the battle between Karna and that Rakshasa had been thus progressing, Alayudha the prince of the Rakshasa, endued with great strength made his appearance of the field of battle.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: महत्या सेनया युक्तो दुर्योधनमुपागमत्। राक्षसानां विरूपाणां सहस्रः परिवारितः॥
en: Supported by a large division of troops and surrounded by thousands of Rakshasas of dreadful aspect, he approached Duryodhana.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: नानारूपधरैवीरैः पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन्। तस्य ज्ञातिर्हि विक्रान्तो ब्राह्मणादो बको हतः॥
en: Indeed surrounded by many heroic Rakshasas of diverse appearances, he came there recollecting the ancient quarrel with the Pandavas. His relative, the Brahmanadevouring Vaka had been slain (by Bhima).

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: किर्मीरश्च महातेजा हैडिम्बश्च सखा तदा। स दीर्घकालसध्युषितं पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन्॥
en: So also the highly puissant Krimira and his friend Hidimba. He waited for a long time, keeping alive the memory of his old enmity with the Pandavas.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: विज्ञायैतन्निशायुद्धं जिघांसुर्भीममाहवे। स मत्त इव मातङ्गः संक्रुद्धः इव चोरगः॥
en: Now informed of this nocturnal battle he came there desirous of compassing the death of Bhima. Then like an infuriate elephant or an enraged snake.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीद् युद्धलालसः। विदितं ते महाराज यथा भीमेन राक्षसाः॥ हिडिम्बबककिर्मीरा निहता मम बान्धवाः। परामर्शश्च कन्याया हिडिम्बायाः कृतः पुरा॥
en: That one longing to engage in the fight spoke these words addressing Duryodhana "O mighty monarch, you have heard how Bhima slew my relatives the Rakshasas Vaka, Krimira and Hidimba in battle. In days gone by, he ravished our daughter Hidimba.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: किमन्यद् राक्षसानन्यानस्मांश्च परिभूय ह। तमहं सगणं राजन् सवाजिरथकुञ्जरम्॥ हैडिम्बि च सहामात्यं हन्तुमभ्यागतः स्वयम्। अद्य कुन्तीसुतान् सर्वान् वासुदेवपुरोगमान्॥ हत्वा सम्भक्षयिष्यामि सर्वैरनुचरैः सह। निवारय बलं सर्वं वयं योत्स्याम पाण्डवान्॥
en: Utterly disregarding ourselves and other Rakshasas. What shall I say more, O king, I have now come of my own accord here to slay him with his followers and cars and steeds and elephants as also the son of Hidimba with all his counselors. Today slaying all the sons of Kunti, headed by the son of Vasudeva, I will eat them up in company with all my followers. Prevent all your troops from battle with the Pandavas; we will fight with them."

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: तस्यैतद् वचनं श्रुत्वा हृष्टो दुर्योधनस्तदा। प्रतिगृह्याब्रवीद् वाक्यं भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः॥
en: Having heard those words of his, king Duryodhana was filled with delight; and surrounded as he was with his brothers welcoming the Rakshasa, he addressed these words to him.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: त्वां पुरस्कृत्य सगर्ण वयं योत्स्यामहे परान्। न हि वैरान्तमनसः स्थास्यन्ति मम सैनिकाः॥
en: Placing you and your followers in our front, we shall fight with our enemies. My troops, impelled by the enmity they bear against the Pandavas cannot be restrained.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: एवमस्त्विति राजानमुक्त्वा राक्षसपुङ्गवः। अभ्ययात् त्वरितो भैमि सहितः पुरुषादकैः॥
en: "Then let it be so," replying thus to the king, that foremost of the Rakshasas, accompanied by his man-eating followers, dashed in fury against Bhimasena.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: दीप्यमानेन वपुषा रथेनादित्यवर्चसा। तादृशेनैव राजेन्द्र यादृशेन घटोत्कचः॥
en: His person was effulgent and his chariot burnt with the splendour of the solar disc. Indeed, O foremost of kings, he looked as beautiful as Ghatotkacha himself.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: तस्याप्यतुलनिर्घोषो बहुतोरणचित्रितः। ऋक्षचर्मावनद्धाङ्गो नल्वमात्रो महारथः॥
en: His spacious chariot also emitted unequalled clatter and was adorned with numerous arches and covered with bear-skins and measured a Nalva.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: तस्यापि तुरगाः शीघ्रा हस्तिकायाः खरखनाः। शतं युक्ता महाकाया मांसशोणितभोजनाः॥
en: His steeds were also fleet and prodigious like elephants and they brayed like asses. Living upon flesh and blood and of huge bodies, a full hundred of them were yoked to his car.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: तस्यापि स्थनिर्घोषो महामेघरवोपमः। तस्यापि सुमहचापं दृढज्यं कनकोजवलम्॥
en: The clatter of his car also resembled the rumble of mighty clouds. His bow was also tough and strong with a hard string,

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: तस्याप्यक्षसमा बाणा रुक्मपुङ्खाः शिलाशिताः। सोऽपि वीरो महाबाहुर्यथैव स घटोत्कचः॥
en: His arrows also were furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone and they resembled Akshas of cars. That hero also possessed might of arms like that of Ghatotkacha himself.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: तस्यापि गोमायुबलाभिगुप्तो बभूव केतुर्व्वलनार्कतुल्यः। स चापि रूपेण घटोत्कचस्य श्रीमत्तमो व्याकुलदीपितास्यः॥
en: His standard also perched upon by hosts of vultures and ravens looked like the sun or the fire; in beauty of person he excelled Ghatotkacha and his countenance was flushed with rage.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: दीप्ताङ्गदो दीप्तकिरीटमाली बद्धस्रगुष्णीषनिबद्धखङ्गः। गदी भुशुण्डी मुसली हली च शरासनी वारणतुल्यवर्णा॥
en: He wore resplendent Angadas and effulgent diadem and garlands. His headgear and sword and floral garlands were duly tied. He was armed with maces, Bhusundis, bludgeons, ploughs and bows and he was covered with a coat of mail tough and impenetrable like the skin of elephant.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: रथेन तेनानलवर्चसा तदा। विद्रावयन् पाण्डववाहिनीं ताम्। रराज संख्ये परिवर्तमानो विद्युन्माली मेघ इवान्तरिक्ष॥
en: Then crushing the Pandava divisions with that car of his of the effulgence of the fire and roving thither and thither he looked beautiful, like a mass of clouds in the welkin fringed with streaks of lighting.

description: The battle between Alayudha and the Pandavas
sn: ते चापि सर्वप्रवरा नरेन्द्रा महाबला वर्मिणश्चर्मिणश्चा हर्षान्विता युयुधस्तस्य राजन् समन्ततः पाण्डवयोधवीराः॥
en: The foremost royal fighters of the Pandava host also, endued with great shields fought on delightfully, o king, on all sides (in that battle with Alayudha).

sn: संजय उवाच तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य भीमकर्माणमाहवे। हर्षमाहारयांचक्रुः कुरवः सर्व एव ते॥
en: Sanjaya said Then beholding Alayudha of fierce deeds come to fight on their behalf, all the Kouravas, were exceedingly delighted.

sn: तथैव तव पुत्रास्ते दुर्योधनपुरोगमाः। अप्लवाः प्लवमासाद्य तर्तुकामा इवार्णवम्॥
en: So also your sons, headed by Duryodhana himself, were filled with joy like persons, desirous of crossing a sea, setting rafts, when there was no chance of getting it.

sn: पुनर्जातमिवात्मानं मन्वानाः पुरुषर्षभाः। अलायुधं राक्षसेन्द्रं स्वागतेनाभ्यपूजयन्॥
en: Having received Alayudha, that foremost prince of the Rakshasas, with a respectful welcome, the kings of your army considered themselves as born anew.

sn: तस्मस्त्वमानुषे युद्धे वर्तमाने महाभये। कर्णराक्षसयोनक्तं दारुणप्रतिदर्शने॥
en: Meanwhile as that nocturnal battle raged between Karna and the Rakshasa-battle that, though terrible and superhuman and fierce, was yet delightful to the eye.

sn: उपप्रेक्षन्त पञ्चालाः स्मयमानाः सराजकाः। तथैव तावका राजन् वीक्षमाणास्ततस्ततः॥
en: The Panchalas and other kings became passive spectators of it. At the same time, O king, your troops, though protected all over the field by their commanders.

sn: चुक्रुशुर्नेदमस्तीति द्रोणद्रौणिकृपादयः। तत् कर्म दृष्ट्वा सम्भ्रान्ता हैडिम्बस्य रणाजिरे॥
en: As also Drona and Drona's son and Kripa and others uttered loud wails, saying All is lost. Indeed beholding on the field those terrible feats of Hidimva's son.

sn: सर्वमाविग्नमभवद्धाहाभूतमचेतनम्। तव सैन्यं महाराज निराशं कर्णजीविते॥
en: All your fighters were filled with anxiety; and uttering shrieks of distress they almost lost their senses. All your troops then, O king, became hopeless of Karna's life.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य कर्णमार्तिं परां गतम्। अलायुधं राक्षसेन्द्रं समाहूयेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then Duryodhana, beholding Karna hard pressed, summoned that foremost of the Rakshasas Alayudha and addressed him in

sn: एष वैकर्तनः कर्णो हैडिम्बेन समागतः। कुरुते कर्म सुमहद् यदस्यौपयिकं मृधे॥
en: "Yonder is Vikartana's son Karna engaged in battle with the son of Hidimba. Behold he is achieving feats worthy of his valour and strength.

sn: पश्यैतान् पार्थिवान् शूरान् निहतान् भैमसेनिना। नानाशस्त्रैरभिहतान् पादपानिव दन्तिना॥
en: Behold there lie the royal heroic warriors slain and wounded with various weapons by the son of Bhimasena, like so many trees crushed by a huge tusked elephant.

sn: तवैष भागः समरे राजमध्ये मया कृतः। तवैवानुमते वीरं तं विक्रम्य निबर्हय॥
en: Amongst all my kindly allies, I have allotted this (Rakshasa Ghatotkacha), with your permission as your share in battle. O hero, do you bring him down displaying your prowess.

sn: पुरा वैकर्तनं कर्णमेष पापो घटोत्कचः। मायाबलं समाश्रित्य कर्षयत्यरिकर्शन॥
en: O slayer of foes, allow not this sinful Ghatotkacha), to crush Vikartana's son through his illusive powers before you despatch him."

sn: एवमुक्तः स राज्ञा तु राक्षसो भीमविक्रमः। तथेत्युक्त्वा महाबाहुर्घटोत्कचमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Thus spoken to by the king, that Rakshasa, of fierce prowess, replied to former saying "let it be so"; and then that mighty-armed one rushed against Ghatotkacha.

sn: ततः कर्ण समुत्सृज्य भैमसेनिरपि प्रभो। प्रत्यमित्रमुपायान्तमर्दयामास मार्गणैः॥
en: Thereupon, O lord, the son of Bhimasena also, bearing alone Karna for a while, began to afflict his advancing adversary with this shafts.

sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं क्रुद्धयो राक्षसेन्द्रयोः। मत्तयोर्वासिताहेतो िपयोरिव कानने॥
en: Then the battle, that commenced between those two enraged Rakshasa chiefs, resembled that between two infuriate elephants both desirous of consorting with the same sheelephant in her season in the woods.

sn: रक्षसा विप्रमुक्तस्तु कर्णोऽपि रथिनां वरः। अभ्यद्रवद् भीमसेनं रथेनादित्यवर्चसा॥
en: Meanwhile, left alone by the Rakshasa that foremost of car-warriors viz., Karna, rushed against Bhimasena, on his car of solar effulgence.

sn: तमायान्तमनादृत्य दृष्ट्वा ग्रस्तं घटोत्कचम्। अलायुधेन समरे सिंहेनेव गवां पतिम्॥
en: Then disregarding the rushing Karna and beholding Ghatotkacha hard pressed by Alayudha, like a bull engaged with a lion.

sn: रथेनादित्यवपुषा भीमः प्रहरतां वरः। किरञ्छरौघान् प्रययावलायुधरथं प्रति॥
en: That foremost of all smiters, viz., Bhimasena, rushed against the chariot of Alayudha, riding on his own car of solar effulgence and shooting showers of sharp arrows.

sn: तमायान्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य स तदालायुधः प्रभो। घटोत्कचं समुत्सृज्य भीमसेनं समाह्वयत्॥
en: Then, O lord, beholding Bhimasena approach, Alayudha, leaving Ghatotkacha alone rushed against the former.

sn: तं भीमः सहसाभ्येत्य राक्षसान्तकरः प्रभो। सगणं राक्षसेन्द्रं तं शरवरवाकिरत्॥
en: Then, O master, that slayer of Rakshasa Bhima, furiously encountering that foremost of Rakshasas, covered him and his followers with showers of arrows.

sn: तथैवालायुधो राजशिलाधौतैरजिह्मगैः। अभ्यवर्षत कौन्तेयं पुनः पुनररिंदप॥
en: Similarly, O king, that subduer of foes namely, Alayudha, cutting off Bhima's arrows with straight going shafts of his, repeatedly covered the latter with his arrows.

sn: तथा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे भीमसेनमुपाद्रवन्। नानाप्रहरणा भीमास्त्वत्सुतानां जयैषिणः॥
en: On the other hand all these Rakshasas, armed with various weapons and dreadfullooking, assailed Bhimasena from all sides desirous of securing victory to your sons.

sn: स ताड्यमानो बहुभिर्भीमसेनो महाबलः। पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिः सर्वांस्तानविध्यच्छितैः शरैः॥
en: Then the highly puissant Bhimasena, wounded by those numerous Rakshasas, pierced each of them in return with five sharp arrows.

sn: ते वध्यमाना भीमेन राक्षसाः क्रूरबुद्धयः। विनेदुस्तुमुलान्नादान् दुद्रुवुस्ते दिशो दश॥
en: Those Rakshasas, of cruel minds, when thus engaged with Bhima, began to utter loud roared and to run in all the ten directions of the compass.

sn: तांनास्यमानान् भीमेन दृष्ट्वा रक्षो महाबलम्। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन शरैश्चैनमवाकिरत्॥
en: The mighty Rakshasa, then beholding the troops belonging to him fly away from fear of Bhima, rushed furiously upon the latter and covered him with arrows.

sn: तं भीमसेनः समरे तीक्ष्णागैरक्षिणोञ्छरैः। अलायुधस्तु तानस्तान् भीमेन विशिखान् रणे॥ चिच्छेद कांश्चित् समरे त्वरया कांश्चिदग्रहीत्। सतं दृष्टवा राक्षसेन्द्रं भीमो भीमपराक्रमः॥
en: In that battle Bhimasena then shot at Alayudha many shafts of keen points. Thereupon Alayudha, in that battle, quickly put off or caught hold of several arrows shot by Bhimasena. Then Bhima of dreadful prowess, beholding that feat of the foremost of the Rakshasas.

sn: गदां चिक्षेप वेगेन वज्रपातोपमा तदा। तामापतन्ती वेगेन गदां ज्वालाकुलां ततः॥ गदया ताड्यामास सा गदा भीममाव्रजत्। स राक्षसेन्द्रं कौन्तेयः शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्॥
en: Hurled at him with great force a mace whose fall resembled the fall of thunder. With his own mace then Alayudha struck the burning mace of Bhima, where-upon the latter flew towards Bhima. Then the son of Kunti covered that foremost of the Rakshasas with a perfect shower of arrows.

sn: तानप्यस्याकरोन्मोघान् राक्षसो निशितैः शरैः। ते चापि राक्षसाः सर्वे रजन्यां भीमरूपिणः॥
en: The Rakshasa baffled even those arrows of Bhima with his own sharp arrows. Then all the Rakshasa troops of dreadful aspect.

sn: शासनाद् राक्षसेन्द्रस्य निजजू रथकुञ्जरान्। पञ्चालाः संजयाश्चैव वाजिनः परमद्विपः॥
en: At the command of their leader, slew all the elephants of the Pandava division. The Panchalas, the Srinjayas, the horses and the excellent elephants (of the Pandava host).

sn: न शान्ति लेभिरे तत्र राक्षसै शपीडिताः। तं तु दृष्ट्वा महाघोरं वर्तमानं महाहवम्॥
en: Then could find no security being afflicted severely by the Rakshasa. Beholding then the progress of that mighty and terrific battle.

sn: अब्रवीत् पुण्डरीकाक्षो धनंजयमिदं वचः। पश्य भीमं महाबाहुं राक्षसेन्द्रवशं गतम्॥
en: The foremost of all male beings addressing Dhananjaya said these words. Behold the mighty-armed Bhima succumb to the prince of the Rakshasas.

sn: पदमस्यानुगच्छ त्वं मा विचारय पाण्डव। धृष्टद्युम्नः शिखण्डी च युधामन्यूत्तमौजसौ॥
en: Do you rush to his rescue, O son of Pandu and do not hesitate. Let Dhristadyumna and Uttamanjas.

sn: सहितौ द्रौपदेयाश्च कर्णं यान्तु महारथाः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च युयुधानश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: Accompanied by the mighty car-warriors of Droupada's division, assail Karna. let Nakula, Şahadeva and the puissant Yuyudhana.

sn: इतरान् राक्षसान् घनन्तु शासनात् तव पाण्डव। त्वमपीमां महाबाहो चमू द्रोणपुरस्कृताम्॥ वारयस्व नरव्याघ्र महद्धि भयमागतम्। एवमुक्ते तु कृष्णेन यथोद्दिष्टा महारथाः॥
en: Exert themselves in slaughtering the other Rakshasas at your command o son of Pandu. O mighty-armed one, do you hold in check this division headed by Drona, in as much as a great panic has seized our troops now.” When Krishna had thus spoken, those foremost of car-warriors, as appointed.

sn: जग्मुर्वैकर्तनं कर्णं राक्षसांश्चैव तान् रणे। अथ पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैः शरैराशीविषोपमैः॥
en: Assailed Karna and the inferior Rakshasas. Then with shafts shot from full drawn bows and resembling snakes of virulent poison.

sn: धनुश्चिच्छेद भीमस्य राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्। हयांश्चास्य शितैर्बाणैः सारथिं च महाबलः॥
en: The highly puissant prince of the Rakshasas cut-off Bhima's bow. The again that mighty hero, with sharp arrows, slew Bhima's steeds and charioteer.

sn: जघान मिषतः संख्ये भीमसेनस्य राक्षसः। सोऽवतीर्य रथोपस्थाद्धताश्वो हतसारथिः॥
en: Even, O Bharata, before the very eyes of Bhima himself. Then deprived of his horses and charioteer Bhima, jumping down from his chariot.

sn: तस्मै गुर्वी गदां धोरां विनदन्नुत्ससर्ज ह। ततस्तां भीमनि?षामापतन्तीं महागदाम्॥
en: Hurled a heavy and dreadful mace at the Rakshasa, uttering a fierce roar. Then as that mighty mace a fierce roar was flying towards him.

sn: गदया राक्षसो घोरो निजघान ननाद च। तद् दृष्ट्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य घोरं कर्म भयावहम्॥
en: The fearful Rakshasa broke it down with his own mace and then uttered a terrible roar. The beholding that fearful and awe-inspiring feat achieved by the prince.

sn: भीमसेनः प्रहृष्टात्मा गदामाशु परामृशत्। तयोः समभवद् युद्धं तुमुलं नररक्षसोः॥
en: Bhima, filled with joy, grasped another fierce mace. Thereupon a terrible encounter raged between the Rakshasas and men.

sn: गदानिपातसंह्रादैर्भुवं कम्पयतोम॑शम्। गदाविमुक्तौ तौ भूयः समासाद्येतरेतरम्॥
en: Causing the earth to tremble repeatedly with the fall of their maces. Then again throwing aside their maces and bearing each other.

sn: मुष्टिभिर्वज्रसह्रादैरन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः। रथचक्रैर्युगैरक्षैरधिष्ठानैरुपस्करैः॥
en: They began to strike each other with their fists emitting a sound like that of the thunder, With car wheels and axle and Akshas and Adisthanas and Upskaras.

sn: यथासन्नमुपादाय निजघ्नतुरमर्षणौ। तौ विक्षरन्तौ रुधिरं समासाद्येतरेतरम्॥
en: Whatever things they could then get, with that they rushed furiously against one another shedding blood profusely and encounter each other.

sn: मत्ताविव महानागौ चकृषाते पुनः पुनः। तदपश्यद्धषीकेशः पाण्डवानां हिते रतः। स भीमसेनरक्षार्थं हैडिम्बि पर्यचोदयत्॥
en: They began to drag each other like two infuriate elephants. Then Hrishikesha, ever devoted to the welfare of the Pandavas, beholding the combat (between Bhima and Alayudha) urged Hidimva's son to the rescue of his father.

sn: संजय उवाच
en: son

sn: संदृश्य समरे भीमं रक्षसा ग्रस्तमन्तिकात्। वासुदेवोऽब्रवीद् राजन् घटोत्कचमिदं वचः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then beholding Bhima hard pressed in battle by the Rakshasa Vasudeva's approaching Ghatotkacha said these words to him.

sn: पश्य भीमं महाबाहो रक्षसा ग्रस्तमाहवे। पश्यतां सर्वसैन्यानां तव चैव महाद्युते॥
en: O mighty armed one, behold Bhima as if devoured by the Rakshasa in battle, before the eyes of all troops and before those of yours, O highly effulgent one.

sn: ॥ स कर्णं त्वं समुत्सृज्य राक्षसेन्द्रमलायुधम्। जहि क्षिप्रं महाबाहो पश्चात् कर्णं वधिष्यसि॥
en: Therefore for a time leaving alone Karna, do you quickly slay Alayudha that foremost of the Rakshasas, O mighty armed one, after which you shall slay Karna.”

sn: स वार्ष्णेयवचः श्रुत्वा कर्णमुत्सृज्य वीर्यवान्। युयुधे राक्षसेन्द्रेण वकभ्रावा घटोत्कचः॥
en: Then hearing the words of that one of Vrishni race and leaving Karna alone for a while, the highly puissant Ghatotkacha, that brother of Vaka, fought with that prince of the Rakshasas.

sn: तयोः सुतुमलं युद्धं बभूव निशि रक्षसोः। अलायुधस्य चैवाग्रं हैडिम्बेश्चापि भारत॥
en: In that night the battle, that raged between the Rakshasa Alayudha and the son of Hidimba, was fierce and confused to the extreme.

sn: अलायुधस्य योधांश्च राक्षसान् भीमदर्शनान्। वेगेनापततः शूरान् प्रगृहीतशरासनान्॥ आत्तायुधः सुसंक्रुद्धो युयुधानो महारथः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च चिच्छिदुर्निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Meanwhile the mighty car-warriors Yuyudhana, Nakula and Sahadeva began to pierce with keen shafts the warriors of Alayudha, viz., those grim looking heroic Rakshasas, who, wielding there bows, were rushing impetuously against them.

sn: सर्वांश्च समरे राजन् किरीटी क्षत्रियर्षभान्। परिचिक्षेप बीभत्सुः सर्वतः प्रकिरछरान्॥
en: The diadem-decked Vibhatsu, O monarch, in that battle, discharging arrows on all sides, began to overthrow many foremost of Kshatriyas.

sn: कर्णश्च समरे राजन् व्यद्रावयत् पार्थिवान्। धृष्टद्युम्निशिखण्ड्यादीन् पञ्चालानां महारथान्॥
en: Similarly, O king, Karna caused many kings of fly away-including Dhristadyumna, Shikhandin and other mighty car-warriors of the Panchalas.

sn: तान् वध्यमानान् दृष्ट्वाथ भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। अभ्ययात् त्वरित: कर्णं विशिखान् प्रकिरन् रणे॥
en: Beholding them thus slaughtered and wounded Bhimasena, of terrible prowess, quickly rushed against Karna shooting sharp arrows.

sn: ततस्तेऽप्याययुर्हत्वा राक्षसान् यत्र सूतजः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च सात्यकिश्च महारथः॥
en: Then those warriors, viz., Nakula, Sahadeva and the mighty car-warrior, Satyaki, also came to the spot where Suta's son was, having slain many Rakshasas.

sn: ते कर्णं योधयामासुः पञ्चाला द्रोणमेव तु। अलायुधस्तु संक्रुद्धो घटोत्कचमरिंदमम्। परिघेणातिकायेन ताड्यामास मूर्धनि॥ स तु तेन प्रहारेण भैमसेनिर्महाबलः।
en: These then fought with Karna and the Panchalas fought with Drona. Meanwhile. Alayudha, excited with rage, began to strike that subduer of enemies, viz., Ghatotkacha on the head with a huge bludgeon. In consequence of that stroke the highly puissant son of Bhima.

sn: ईषन्मूर्छितमात्मानमस्तम्भयत वीर्यवान्॥ ततो दीप्ताग्निसंकाशां शतघण्टामलंकृताम्। चिक्षेप तस्मै समरे गदां काञ्चन भूषिताम्॥ सा हयांश्च रथं चास्य सारथिं च महास्वना। चूर्णयामास वेगेन विसृष्टा भीमकर्मणा॥ स भग्नहयचक्राक्षाद् विशीर्णध्वजकूबरात्। उत्पपात रथात् तूर्णं मायामास्थाय राक्षसीम्॥ स समास्थाय मायां तु ववर्ष रुधिरं बहु।
en: Squatted down, overwhelmed with a partial swoon. Thereafter he hurled at Alayudha a mace, looking like a blazing flame of fire, decked with a hundred bells and adorned with gold. Hurled forcibly by that one of fierce achievements, that mace crushed into pieces the horses, the driver and the loudly rattling chariots of Alayudha. Then betaking to his illusive prowess the latter then jumped down from his car of which the horses, the wheels Akshas and standard and Kurara had all been shattered. Then through his illusive powers he showered a copious downpour of blood on the field.

sn: विद्युद्विभाजितं चासीत् तुमुलाभ्राकुलं नभः॥ ततो वज्रनिपाताश्च साशनिस्तनयित्नवः।
en: Then sky the appeared to be over-spread with darts, masses of clouds with flashes of lightning. A thunder storm then made its appearance accompanied by rumble of clouds and claps of thunder.

sn: महांश्चटचटाशब्दस्तत्रासीच महाहवे॥ तां प्रेक्ष्य महतीं मायां राक्षसो राक्षसस्य च।
en: Loud clapping sounds were also then heard in that combat. beholding that illusion created by the Rakshasa Alayudha, the cannibal Ghatotkacha.

sn: ऊर्ध्वमुत्पत्य हैडिम्बिस्तां मायां माययावधीत्॥ सोऽभिवीक्ष्य हतां मायां मायावी माययैव हि।
en: Soaring high, destroyed it by his own illusive power. Possessed of potent illusive powers Alayudha then seeing his own illusions nullified by those of his adversary.

sn: अश्मवर्षं सुतुमलं विससर्ज घटोत्कचे॥ अश्मवर्षं स तं घोरं शरवर्षेण वीर्यवान्। दिक्षु विध्वंसयामास तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥ ततो नानाप्रहरणैरन्योन्यमभिवर्षताम्।
en: Began to pour a heavy downpour of stones on Ghatotkacha. That terrible shower of stones, the brave Ghatotkacha baffled by means of a shower of arrows. They then poured on each other diverse weapons.

sn: आयसैः परिघैः शूलैर्गदामुसलमुद्गरैः॥ पिनाकैः करवालैश्च तोमरप्रासकम्पनैः। नाराचैर्निशितैर्भल्लैः शरैश्चकैः परश्वधैः। अयोगुडैर्भिन्दिपालैगोंशीर्षोलूखलैरपि॥
en: Such as iron bludgeons, lances, maces sharp clubs, mallets, tridents, sabres, spears, long and small, kampanas, keen shafts, both long and broad-headed and arrows and discuses and battle axes and Ayagudas and sharp arrows and weapons with heads like those of kine, Ulukhalas.

sn: उत्पाटितैर्महाशाखैर्विविधैर्जगतीसहैः। शंमीपीलुकदम्बैश्च चम्पकैश्चैव भारत॥ इनुदैर्बदरीभिश्च कोविदारैश्च पुष्पितैः। पलाशैश्चारिमेदैश्च प्लक्षन्यग्रोधपिप्पलैः॥ महद्भिः समरे तस्मिन्नन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः। विपुलैः पर्वतायैश्च नानाधातुभिराचितैः॥
en: And they then struck each other tearing up many kinds of large branched trees, such as Sami, Pilu, Karira, Champaka and O Bharata, Juguda, Vadari, blossoming Kovidara, Plaksha, Arimedhas, Palasha and the Camian, the Peepul, as also with numerous crests of mountains decked with various kinds of metals.

sn: तेषां शब्दो महानासीद् वज्राणां भिद्यतामिव। युद्धं समभवद् घोरं भैम्यलायुधयोर्नृप॥
en: The clash, produced by those trees and mountain crest, became as loud as the sound of the roaring thunder. Indeed the battle, that then raged between Alayudha and Bhima's son was, O monarch, fierce in the extreme.

sn: हरीन्द्रयोर्यथा राजन् वालिसुग्रीवयोः पुरा। तौ युद्धवा विविधैोरैरायुधैर्विशिखैस्तथा। प्रगृह्य च शितौ खगावन्योन्यमभिपेततुः॥ तावन्योन्यमभिद्रुत्य केशेषु सुमहाबलौ। भुजाभ्यां पर्यगृह्णीतां महाकायौ महाबलौ॥
en: Like that which took place in the days of yore between the two monkey chiefs Bali and Sugriva. They wounded each other with shafts and various other kinds of weapois as also with keen-edged swords. Then those two might Rakshasas, rushing against each other, caught hold of each other by the hair.

sn: तौ स्विन्नगात्रौ प्रस्वेदं सुनुवाते जनाधिप। रुधिरं च महाकायावतिवृष्टाविवाम्बुदौ॥
en: And those two huge warriors, covered with numerous wounds on their bodies and blood and perspiration trickling down, appeared beautiful like two mighty masses of clouds pouring rain.

sn: अथाभिपत्य वेगेन समुद्धाम्य च राक्षसम्। बलेनाक्षिप्य हैडिम्बिश्चकर्तास्य शिरो महत्॥
en: Then rushing with great violence and whirling the Rakshasa on high and dashing him down again, Hidimba's son cut-off the large head of his adversary.

sn: सोऽपहत्य शिरस्तस्य कुण्डलाभ्यां विभूषितम्। तदा सुतुमुल नादं ननाद सुमहाबलः॥
en: Then holding that had graced with a pair of ear-rings, the puissant Ghatotkacha uttered a terrific roar.

sn: हतं दृष्ट्वा महाकायं वकज्ञातिमरिंदमम्। पञ्चालाः पाण्डवाश्चैव सिंहनादान् विनेदिरे॥
en: Beholding the huge-bodied brother of Vaka, that subduer of foes, slain, the Panchalas and the Pandavas uttered tremendous warcries.

sn: ततो भेरीसहस्राणि शङ्खानामयुतानि च। अवादयन् पाण्डवेया राक्षसे निहते युधि॥
en: Thereupon on the fall of that Rakshasa the Pandava troops struck up thousands of drums and ten thousand conches.

sn: अतीव सा निशा तेषां बभूव विजयावहा। विद्योतमाना विबभौ समन्ताद् दीपमालिनी॥
en: That night then exclusively brought victory to the Pandavas; echoing with the sound of musical instruments and illumined with torches it then appeared highly beautiful.

sn: अलायुधस्य तु शिरो भैमसेनिर्महाबलः। दुर्योधनस्य प्रमुखे चिक्षेप गतचेतसः॥
en: Then the highly puissant son of Bhima threw that head of Alayudha at he face of Duryodhana who was then rendered insensible.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनो राजा दृष्ट्वा हतमलायुधम्। बभूव परमोद्विग्नः सह सैन्येन भारत॥
en: Thereupon Duryodhana, beholding the heroic Alayudha slain, became filled with great anxiety together with all his troops.

sn: तेन ह्यस्य प्रतिज्ञातं भीमसेनमहं युधि। हन्तेति स्वयमागम्य स्मरता वैरमुत्तमम्॥
en: Alayudha, having come to Duryodhana out of his own accord, recollecting his old enmity, has said to the latter, that he would slay Bhima.

sn: ध्रुवं स तेन हन्तव्य इत्यमन्यत पार्थिवः। जीवितं चिरकालं हि भ्रातृणां चाप्यमन्यत॥
en: The Kuru king had considered the slaughter of Bhima to be certain and had considered the length of the days of his brother also to be measured.

sn: स तं दृष्ट्वा विनिहतं भीमसेनात्मजेन वै। प्रतिज्ञा भीमसेनस्य पूर्णामेवाभ्यमन्यत॥
en: Then beholding that Alayudha (on whom all his hopes rested) slain by the son of Bhimasena, Duryodhana considered Bhima's vow (about the slaughter of himself and his brothers) to be already fulfilled.

sn: संजय उवाच निहत्यालायुधं रक्षः प्रहृष्टात्मा घटोत्कचः। ननाद विविधान् नादान् वाहिन्याः प्रमुखे तव॥
en: Sanjaya said Having slain the Rakshasa Alayudha Ghatotkacha was greatly delighted; and then standing at the very van of the troops he began to utter diverse kinds of roars.

sn: तस्य तं तुमुलं शब्दं श्रुत्वा कुञ्जरकम्पनम्। तावकानां महाराज भयमासीत् सुदारुणम्॥
en: Those loud roars of his, capable of his making an elephant tremble, entering into the car of troops, struck a great panic to their hearts, O mighty monarch.

sn: अलायुधविषक्तं तु भैमसेनि महाबलम्। दृष्ट्वा कर्णो महाबाहुः पञ्चालान् समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Meanwhile the mighty-armed Karna, beholding the highly puissant son of Bhima engaged with Alayudha, rushed against the Panchalas.

sn: दशभिर्दशभिर्बाणैर्वृष्टद्युम्नशिखण्डिनौ। दृढः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैर्बिभेद नतपर्वभिः॥
en: He proceeded against Dhristadyumna and Sikhandin, each with ten strong and straight shafts, shot from his bow drawn to its fullest stretch.

sn: ततः परमनाराचैर्युधामन्यूत्तमौजसौ। सात्यकिं च रथोदारं कम्पयामास मार्गणैः॥
en: Thereafter with a group of other arrows, consisting of Narachas, & c., the son of Suta caused Yudhamanyu, Uttamanjas and the mighty car-warrior Satyaki to tremble.

sn: तेषामप्यस्यतां संख्ये सर्वेषां सव्यदक्षिणम्। मण्डलान्येव चापानि व्यदृश्यन्त जनाधिप॥
en: The bows of all those warriors also, O king, engaged in shooting shafts right and left, were also seen incessantly to be deawn in a circle.

sn: तेषां ज्यातलनिर्घोषो रथनेमिस्वनश्च ह। मेघानामिव धर्मान्ते बभूव तुमुलो निशि॥
en: In that night the sound of their palms and the twang of their bow-strings and the clatter of their car-wheels were so loud as to resemble and rumble of cloud at the end of summer.

sn: ज्यानेमिघोषस्तनयित्नुमान् वै धनुस्तडिन्मण्डलकेतुशृङ्गः शरोघवर्षाकुलवृष्टिमांश्च संग्राममेघः च बभूव राजन्॥
en: Then, O monarch, that battle appeared to be a cloud of which the sound of car-clatter and bow-twang consisted the roar of thunder; the bows of warriors its flashes and showers of arrows it torrents of rain.

sn: तदद्भुतं शैल इवाप्रकम्पो वर्षं महाशैलसमानसारः। विध्वंसयामास रणे नरेन्द्र वैकर्तनः शत्रुगणावमर्दी॥
en: O foremost of kings, then Vikartana's son Karna, that crusher of his foes, immovable like a hill and equal to a hill in personal proportions, destroyed that wonderful shower of arrows.

sn: ततोऽतुलैर्वज्रनिपातकल्पैः शितैः शरैः काञ्चनचित्रपुङ्खः। शत्रून् व्यपोहत् समरे महात्मा वैकर्तनः पुत्रहिते रतस्ते॥
en: Then Vikartana's son, high-souled, ever devoted to the interests of your sons, began to slay his adversaries in that battle, with Tomaras, which, in their fall, resembled the thunder-bolt and also with sharp arrows furnished with variegated wings of gold.

sn: संछिन्नभिन्नध्वजिनश्च केचित् केचिच्छरैरर्दितभिन्नदेहाः। केचिद् विसूता विहयाश्च केचिद् वैकर्तनेनाशु कृता बभूवुः॥
en: Some (of the enemy's host) then had their standards broken and torn; some had their bodies torn and mangled with sharp arrows. Some were deprived of their charioteers, some of their horses and some were soon maimed by Vikartana's son.

sn: अविन्दमानास्त्वथ शर्म संख्ये यौधिष्ठिरं तं बलमभ्यपद्यन्। तान् प्रेक्ष्य भग्नान् विमुखोकृतांश्च घटोत्कचो रोषमतीव चक्रे॥
en: Getting no refuge, the Panchala host then fell back upon the division of Yudhishthira. Beholding these troops broken and compelled to turn away, Ghatotkacha then became excited to the highest pitch of fury.

sn: आस्थाय तं काञ्चनरत्नचित्रं रथोत्तमं सिंहवत् संननादा वैकर्तनं कर्णमुपेत्य चापि विव्याध वज्रप्रतिमैः पृषत्कैः॥
en: Then mounting on his excellent car adorned with gold and gems, he began to roar like a lion. Thereafter approaching Vikartana's son Karna he pierced him with arrows resembling the bolt of Heaven itself,

sn: तौ कर्णिनाराचशिलीमुखैश्च नालीकदण्डासनवत्सदन्तैः। वराहकर्णैः सविपाठशृङ्गैः क्षुरप्रवर्धेश्च विनेदतुः खम्॥
en: They both then covered the welkin with showers of barbed arrows, Narachas, Silimukhas, Nalikas, Dandas, Asanis. Vatsyadantas, Varahakarnas and broad-headed and razor-faced arrows and shafts pointed like horns.

sn: तद् बाणधारावृतमन्तरिक्षं तिर्यग्गताभिः समरे रराज। सुवर्णपुङ्खज्वलितप्रभाभि विचित्रपुष्पाभिरिव स्रजाभिः॥
en: The welkin then, shrouded with that arrowy shower, appeared in consequence of these gold-winged shafts of burning effulgence flying straight through it, as if hung with festoons of beautiful flowers.

sn: समाहितावप्रतिमप्रभावा वन्योन्यमाजघ्नतुरुत्तमास्त्रैः। तयोर्हि वीरोत्तमयोर्न कश्चिद् ददर्श तस्मिन् समरे विशेषम्॥
en: Of unequaled splendour, they both were each other's match and they then wounded each other with excellent weapons. None could then find any superiority of either of those two excellent heroes.

sn: अतीव तचित्रमतुल्यरूपं बभूव युद्धं रविभीमसून्चोः। समाकुलं शस्रनिपातघोरं दिवीव रावशुमतोः प्रमत्तम्॥
en: The battle, that was thus fought between the sons of Surya and Bhima and in which showers of arrows were discharged, looked highly charming and presented almost of unequaled aspect like what is seen in the fierce encounter between Rahu and the sun in the heavens.

sn: संजय उवाच घटोत्कचं यदा कर्णो न विशेषयते नृप। ततः प्रादुश्चकारोग्रमस्रमस्रविदां वरः॥
