en: Sanjaya said When, o king, Ghatotkacha, that foremost of all wielders of weapons, found that could get no advantage over Karna he invoked into existence an exceedingly fierce weapon.

sn: तेनास्रेणावधीत् तस्य रथं सहयसारथिम्। विस्थश्चापि हैडिम्बिः क्षिप्रमन्तरधीयत॥
en: Then with that weapon having at first slain Karna's steed, the Rakshasa next destroyed his driver. And then the son of Hidimba quickly rendered himself invisible even then and there,

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तस्मिन्नन्तर्हिते तूर्णं कूटयोधिनि राक्षसे मामकैः प्रतिपन्नं यत् तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When that Rakshasa, after fighting by underhand measures, had thus disappeared, O Sanjaya, describe to me what befell my troops then.

sn: संजय उवाच अन्तर्हितं राक्षसेन्द्रं विदित्वा सम्प्राक्रोशन् कुरवः सर्व एव। कथं नायं राक्षस: कूटयोधि हन्यात् कर्णं समरेऽदृश्यमानः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then beholding the Rakshasa disappear, all the Kurus then exclaimed aloud Saying-"Appearing next to view, the Rakshasa, fighting by underhand means, will certainly slay Karna.”

sn: ततः कर्णो लघुचित्रानयोधी सर्वा दिशः प्रावृणोद् बाणजालैः। न वै किञ्चत् प्रापतत् तत्र भूतं तमोभूते सायकैरन्तरिक्षे॥
en: Thereupon Karna, who was endued with extreme lightness in the use of diverse weapons, covered all the points of the compass with bis arrowy net-work. Then in consequence of the welkin being darkened by those showers of arrows, no creature could be seen distinguished.

sn: नैवाददानो न च संदधाना न चेषुधीः स्पृश्यमानः कराग्रैः। अदृश्यद् वै लाघवात् सूतपुत्रः सर्वं बाणैश्छादयानोऽन्तरिक्षम्॥
en: So great was the lightness of hand displayed by the son of Suta that nobody could then mark when the touched his quiver with his fingers, when he placed his arrows on the bowstring and when he aimed and let them off. The whole welkin was then darkened with his shafts.

sn: ततो मायां दारुणामन्तरिक्षे घोरा भीमा विहितां राक्षसेन। अपश्याम लोहिताभ्रप्रकाशा देदीप्यन्तीमग्निशिखामिवोग्राम्॥
en: Then a fierce and dreadful illusion was invoked into existence in the welkin by the Rakshasa. We then beheld in the sky what appeared to be amass of red cloud resembling the terrible flames of a raging fire.

sn: नुल्काश्चापि ज्वलिताः कौरवेन्द्र। घोषश्चास्याः प्रादुरासीत् सुघोरः सहस्रशो नदतां दुन्दुभीनाम्॥
en: O ruler of the Kurus, then from that cloud were seen to issue out flashes of lightning and burning flame-beams. Tremendous roars also issued therefrom, resembling the din of thousands of drums beaten simultaneously.

sn: ततः शराः प्रापतन् रुक्मपुङ्खाः शक्त्यष्टिप्रासमुसलान्यायुधानि। परश्वधास्तैलधौताश्च खगाः। प्रदीप्तानास्तोमराः पट्टिशाश्च॥
en: From it also fell many gold-winged shafts, spears, javelins, heavy clubs and such other weapons, as also battle-axes, swords cleansed with oil and axes of blazing edges and darts.

sn: मयूखिनः परिघा लोहबद्धा गदाश्चित्राः शितधाराश्च शूलाः। गुयॊ गदा हेमपट्टावनद्धाः शतघ्यश्च प्रादुरासन् समन्तात्॥
en: And spiked bludgeons pouring shinning rays, charming maces made of iron, long lances of keen points, heavy maces adorned with gold and entwined with strings and Shataghnis all around.

sn: महाशिलाश्चापतस्तत्र तव सहस्रशः साशनयश्च वज्राः। चक्राणि चानेकशतक्षुराणि प्रादुर्बभूवुर्खलनप्रभाणि॥
en: Large stones drooped from it and thousands of thunderbolts with loud clap and hundreds of wheels and razors of the effulgence of fire.

sn: तां शक्तिपाषाणपरश्वधानां प्रासासिवज्राशनिमुद्गराणाम्। वृष्टिं विशालां ज्वलितां पतन्तीं कर्णः शरौधैर्न शशाक हन्तुम्॥
en: Shooting countless arrows Karna then failed to destroy that thick and blazing shower of lances, swords, clubs, mallets, thunderbolts Asains and axes.

sn: शराहतानां पततां हयानां वज्राहतानां च तथा गजानाम्। शिलाहतानां च महारथानां महान् निनादः पततां बभूव॥
en: Then a tremendous uproar was caused there as horse fell struck with arrows, elephants came down being crushed with thunderbolts and car-warriors fell deprived of life by other weapons.

sn: र्घटोत्कचेनाभिहतं समन्तात्। दौर्योधनं वै बलमार्तरूप मावर्तमानं ददृशे भ्रमत् तत्॥
en: Afflicted all around with the fall of dreadful weapons of various kinds discharged by Ghatotkacha and army of Duryodhana, in great distress, were seen to move helplessly on the field of battle.

sn: हाहाकृतं सम्परिवर्तमान संलीयमानं च विषण्णरूपम्। ते त्वार्यभावात् पुरुषप्रवीराः पराङ्मुखा नो बभूवुस्तदानीम्॥
en: Cries of Alas and Oh then arose there; and the warriors with their cheerless expression indicted as if they were on the verge of ruin. But those foremost of men, inspired as they were with honorable sentiments, did not then leave the field with faces turned round.

sn: तां राक्षसी भीमरूपां सुघोरां वृष्टिं महाशस्रमयी पतन्तीम्। दृष्ट्वा बलौघांश्च निपात्यमानान् महद् भयं तव पुत्रान् विवेश॥
en: Then beholding that immensely terrible and awful shower of weapons invoked into existence by the illusive energy of the Rakshasa and seeing their own troops felled incessantly by it, your sons were seized with a great panic.

sn: शिवाश्च वैश्वानरदीप्तजिह्वाः सुभीमनादाः शतशा नदन्तीः। रक्षोगणान् नर्दतश्चापि वीक्ष्य नरेन्द्र योधा व्यथिता बभूवुः॥
en: Jackals having tongues like the leaping flames of fire began to utter fierce howls by hundreds; the Rakshasa also uttered fierce yells. Hearing these disagreeable sounds, O king, your troops were greatly afflicted.

sn: ते दीप्तजिह्वानलतीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रा विभीषणाः शैलनिकाशकायाः। नभोगताः शक्तिविषक्तहस्ता मेघा व्यमुञ्चन्निव वृष्टिमुग्राम्॥
en: Those fierce Rakshasas having fiery tongues, blazing countenances and sharp teeth and forms huge as mountains, car-reering through the sky with lances in grasp, appeared like clouds pouring torrents of rain.

sn: र्गदाभिरुग्रैः परिघैश्च दीप्तैः। वजैः पिनाकैरशनिप्रहारैः शतनिचक्रैर्मथिताश्च पेतुः॥ सैन्यं
en: Wounded and crushed with those dreadful arrows, spears, darts, maces, spiked bludgeons of great lustre, thunder-bolts, trident, Asanis, wheels and Shataghnis, the Kaurava troops began to fall down.

sn: शूला भुशुण्ड्योऽश्मगुडाः शतघ्न्यः स्थूणाश्च कार्णायसपट्टनद्धाः। तेऽवाकिरंस्तव पुत्रस्य ततो रौद्रं कश्मलं प्रादुरासीत्॥
en: The Rakshasas then went on pouring upon the warriors of your sons long spears and treacle and Shataghnis and Sthunas made of steel and covered with strings of jute and all the combatants became confounded.

sn: विकीर्णान्त्रा विहतैरुत्तमाङ्गैः सम्भग्नाङ्गाः शिश्यिरे तत्र शूराः। छिन्ना हयाः कुञ्जराश्चापि भग्नाः संचूर्णिताश्चैव रथाः शिलाभिः॥
en: heroic warriors with weapons broken or falling off from their gasp or deprived of heads or with maimed limbs, began to fall down on the field. Then steeds and elephants and chariots were also crushed to pieces by the shower of stones.

sn: एवं महच्छस्रवर्षं सृजन्त स्ते यातुधाना भुवि घोररूपाः। मायासृष्टास्तत्र घटोत्कचेन नामुञ्चन् वै याचमानं न भीतम्॥
en: Those Yatudhanas of terrible forms created by Ghatotkacha by the help of his illusive powers, pouring that thick shower of mighty weapons, spread neither those that were frightened nor those that begged for mercy.

sn: तस्मिन् घोरे कुरुवीरावमर्दे कालोत्सृष्टे क्षत्रियाणामभावे। ते वै भग्नाः सहसा व्यद्रवन्त प्राक्रोशन्तः कौरवाः सर्व एव॥
en: In the ruthless slaughter of Kuru heroes, brought on by Death himself, in that extermination ou Kshatriyas the Kaurava warriors suddenly broke and fled with speed,

sn: पलायध्वं कुरवो नैतदस्ति सेन्द्रा देवा घनन्ति नः पाण्डवार्थे। तथा तेषां मजतां भारतानां तस्मिन् द्वीपः सूतपुत्रो बभूव॥
en: "Fly, O Kouravas, all is lost. The gods with Indra at their head are slaying us for the sake of the Pandavas.” At that time there was nobody that could save the sinking Bharata troops."

sn: तस्मिन् संक्रन्दे तुमुले वर्तमाने सैन्ये भग्ने लीयमाने कुरूणाम्। अनीकानां प्रविभागेऽप्रकाशे नाज्ञायन्त कुरवो नेतरे च॥
en: During that terrible uproar and shout and carnage of the Kurus, the divisions loosing their distinguishing marks the parties could not be differentiated from one another.

sn: निर्मर्यादे विद्रवे घोररूपे सर्वा दिशः प्रेक्षमाणाः स्म शून्याः। तां शस्रवृष्टिमुरसा गाहमानं कर्णं स्मैकं तत्र राजन्नपश्यन्॥
en: In that dreadful fight in which nobody paid any regard for any one else, every side of the field, when looked at, appeared to be said, O monarch. Karna alone was then to be seen drowned in that downpour of arrows.

sn: ततो बाणैरावृणोदन्तरिक्षं दिव्यां मायां योधयन् राक्षसस्य। ह्रीमान् कुर्वन् दुष्करं चार्यकर्म नैवामुह्यत् संयुगे सूतपुत्रः॥
en: Then Karna covered the welkin with his shafts, striking agair..t that celestial illusion of the Rakshasas. The son of Suta, endowed with modesty and achieving the most difficult and praiseworthy feats, was not at all confounded in that battle.

sn: ततो भीताः समुदैक्षन्त कर्णं राजन् सर्वे सैन्धवा बालिकाश्चा असम्मोहं पूजयन्तोऽस्य संख्ये सम्पश्यन्तो विजयं राक्षसस्य॥
en: was O king, then all the Saindhavas and Valhikas looked in fear at Karna whose senses were not confounded in that fight. And they all applauded him whether they looked at the triumphs of the Rakshasa.

sn: तेनोत्सृष्टा चक्रयुक्ता शतघ्नी समं सर्वांश्चतुरोऽश्वाञ्जघान। ते जानुभिर्जगतीमन्वद्यन् गतासवो निर्दशनाक्षिजिह्वाः॥
en: Thereafter a Sataghni, furnished with wheels, discharged at Karna by Ghatotkacha and it detached at once the four steeds of Karna. These horses then fell down on their knees, deprived of life, teeth, eyes and tongues.

sn: दन्तर्मनाः कुरुषु प्राद्रवत्सु। दिव्ये चारो मायया वध्यमाने नैवामुह्यचिन्तयन् प्राप्तकलम्॥
en: Then descending from his horseless chariot and seeing the Kouravas fly away and beholding his own celestial weapons repulsed by the illusion of the Rakshasa, Karna, not at all confounded, turned his mind inwards and then began to reflect as to what he should do next.

sn: ततोऽब्रुवन् कुरवः सर्व एव कर्णं दृष्ट्वा घोररूपां च मायाम्। शक्त्या रक्षो जहि कर्णाद्य तूर्णं नश्यन्त्येते कुरवो धार्तराष्ट्राः॥
en: At that time all the Kouravas, beholding Karna and the terrible the terrible illusion of the Rakshasas, cried out saying-O Karna, slay the Rakshasa with your dart. The Kouravas and the Dhritarashtras are on the point of being exterminated.

sn: करिष्यत: किञ्च नो भीमपार्थों तपन्तमेनं जहि पापं निशीथे। यो नः संग्रामाद् घोररूपाद् विमुच्येत् स नः पार्थान् सबलान् योधयेत॥
en: What can Bhima or Arjuna do to us? Slay this wicked Rakshasa, who is consuming us all, at this dead of night. They, that will escape alive form this encounter, will fight with the Parthas tomorrow.

sn: तस्मादेनं राक्षसं घोररूपं शक्त्या जहि त्वं दत्तया वासवेन। मा कौरवाः सर्व एवेन्द्रकल्पा रात्रियुद्धे कर्ण नेशुः सयोधाः॥
en: Therefore slay this dreadful Rakshasa now with that dart given to you by Vasava. O Karna, let not these great warriors, the Kouravas these royal combatants that resemble Indra himself be all exterminated in this nightfight.

sn: स वध्यमानो रक्षसा वै निशीथे दृष्ट्वा राजस्रास्यमानं बलं च। महच्छ्रुत्वा निनदं कौरवाणां मतिं दधे शक्तिमोक्षाय कर्णः॥
en: Then Karna, seeing the Rakshasa alive at the middle of night and the Kuru army filled with fear and hearing also the loud wails of the latter, set his heart upon hurling his dart.

sn: स वै क्रुद्धः सिंह इवात्यमर्षी नामर्षयत् प्रतिघातं रणेऽसौ। शक्तिं श्रेष्ठां वैजयन्तीमसह्यां समाददे तस्य वधं चिकीर्षन्॥
en: Burning with wrath like an infuriate lion and unable to brook the assaults of the Rakshasa Karna took up that foremost of victory-giving and indomitable darts, desirous of achieving the destruction of Ghatotkacha.

sn: यासौ राजनिहिता वर्षपूगान् वधायाजौ सत्कृता फाल्गुनस्य। यां वै प्रादात् सूतपुत्राय शक्रः शक्तिं श्रेष्ठां कुण्डलाभ्यां निमाय॥
en: That dart. O monarch, which he had kent and worshipped through years for encompassing the slaughter of Pandu's son in battle, that excellent dart that Indra himself had given to Suta's son in exchange for the latter's ear-rings.

sn: तां वै शक्तिं लेलिहानां प्रदीप्तां पाशैर्युक्तामन्तकस्येव जिह्वाम्। मृत्योः स्वसारं ज्वलितामिवोल्का वैकर्तनः प्राहिणोद् राक्षसाय॥
en: That burning and dreadful dart entwined with strings and which seemed to long for blood, that terrible missile that looked like very tongue of death or his sister, that resplendent and fearful dart Vikartana's son now hurled at the Rakshasa.

sn: तामुत्तमां परकायावहन्त्री दृष्ट्वा शक्तिं बाहुसंस्थां ज्वलन्तीम्। भीतं रक्षो विप्रदुद्राव राजन् कृत्वाऽऽत्मानं विध्यतुल्यप्रमाणम्॥
en: Thereupon seeing that excellent and glittering weapon, capable of penetrating of Suta's son, the Rakshasa fled away in fear making his body prodigious like the foot of the Vindhya hills.

sn: दृष्ट्वा शक्तिं कर्णबाह्वन्तरस्थां नेदुर्भूतान्यन्तरिक्षे नरेन्द्र। ववुर्वातास्तुमुलाश्चापि राजन् सनिर्याता चाशनिर्गा जगाम॥
en: Then seeing that dart in the grasp of Karna all creatures, in the heavens, began to utter loud wails. Fearful winds began to blow and thunder with tremendous clap began to fall on the earth.

sn: सा तां मायां भस्म कृत्वा ज्वलन्ती भित्त्वा गाढं हृदयं राक्षसस्य। ऊर्ध्वं ययौ दीप्यमाना निशायां नक्षत्राणामन्तराण्याविवेश॥
en: Then that dart, destroying the blazing illusion and going through the breast of the Rakshasa, soared aloft and penetrated in the night into a stony constellation in the heavens.

sn: दिव्यैर्नागैर्मानुषै राक्षसैश्चा नदन् नादान् विविधान् भैरवांश्च प्राणानिष्टांस्त्याजितः शक्रशक्त्या॥
en: Thus having fought with various kinds of weapons with numerous heroic warriors and Rakshasa, Ghatotkacha, then uttering various dreadful roars, fell deprived of life with that dart of Indra.

sn: इदं चान्यचित्रमाश्चर्यरूपं चकारासौ कर्म शत्रुक्षयाया तस्मिन् काले शक्तिनिर्भिन्नमर्मा बभौ राजशैलमेघप्रकाशः॥
en: This is the most exceedingly wonderful feat that the Rakshasa achieved for the destruction of his foes viz., that at the time when his heart was penetrated by that dart he shone resplendent, O monarch, like a mightymountain or a mass of clouds.

sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षादपतद् गतासुः स राक्षसेन्द्रो भुवि भिन्नदेहः। अवाक्शिराः स्तब्धगात्रो विजिह्वो घटोत्कचो महदास्थाय रूपम्॥
en: Deprived of life, that foremost of the Rakshasas, fell down on the ground from welkin. His body was torn, deprived of speech, head and tongue Gatotkacha extended his body in a very large form.

sn: स तद् रूपं भैरवं भीमकर्मा भीमं कृत्वा भैमसेनिः पपात। हतोऽप्येवं तव सैन्येकदेश मपोथयत् स्वेन देहेन राजन्॥
en: Having assumed that terrible and dreadful figure, Bhimasena's son of frightful deeds fell down. When dying, O monarch, he fell upon a portion of your army and pressed those troops down by the weight of his own body.

sn: एतद् रक्षः स्वेन कायेण तूर्णं मतिप्रमाणेन विवर्धता च। रक्षौहिणीं तव तूर्णं जघान॥
en: Then falling down with force, the Rakshasa, with his huge and still increasing body, desirous of benefiting the Pandavas, slew a full Akshauhini of your troops, while he himself gave up his life.

sn: भैर्यः शङ्खा मुरजाश्चानकाच। दग्धां मायां निहतं राक्षसं च दृष्ट्वा हृष्टाः कौरवेयाः॥
en: Then a tremendous uproar composed of the war-cries of combatants, beasts, of conchs and sound of drums and cymbals arose there. The Kouravas, then beholding the Rakshasa slain and his illusion destroyed, uttered loud shouts of joy.

sn: ततः कर्णः कुरुभिः पूज्यमानो यथा शक्रो वृत्रवधे मरुद्भिः। अन्वारूढस्तव पुत्रस्य यानं हृष्टश्चापि प्राविशत् तत् स्वसैन्यम्॥
en: Then Karna, applauded by the Kurus, as Shakra had been by the Marutas upon the death of Vritra, ascended behind the car of your son and becoming, the object of every body's sight entered the Kuru host.

sn: संजय उवाच हैडिम्बि निहतं दृष्ट्वा विशीर्णमिव पर्वतम्।
en: Sanjaya said Beholding Hidimva's son slain and lying like a riven hill all the Pandavas began to shed copious tears of grief.

sn: वासुदेववस्तु हर्षेण महताभिपरिप्लुतः। ननाद सिंहनादं वै पर्यष्वजत फाल्गुनम्॥
en: But the son of Vasudeva, overwhelmed with delight, began to utter there loud war-cries thereby causing pain to the Pandavas.

sn: स विनद्य महानादमभीषून् संनियम्य च। ननर्त हर्षसंवीतो वातोद्भूत इव दुमः॥
en: Indeed uttering loud shouts he then embraced the son of Pandu. Thus uttering loud roars and drawing the reins of the steeds.

sn: तत: परिष्वज्य पुनः पार्थमास्फोट्य चासकृत्। रथोपस्थगतो धीमान् प्राणदत् पुनरच्युतः॥
en: He began to dance in joy, like a tree shaken by the tempest. Then embracing Partha once more and clapping his armp-its.

sn: प्रहृष्टमनसं ज्ञात्वा वासुदेवं महाबलः। अर्जुनोऽथाब्रवीद् राजन्नातिहृष्टमना इव॥
en: That undeteriorating god, endowed with great intelligence, once more uttered roud roars standing on the terrace of his car. Then beholding those sings of joy manifested by Kesava, Dhananjaya.

sn: अतिहर्षोऽयमस्थाने तवाद्य मधुसूदन। शोकस्थाने तु सम्प्राप्ते हैडिम्बस्य वधेन तु॥
en: O monarch, with a beast overwhelmed with grief, addressed the former saying-"O slayer of Madhu, you are showing delight at a time scarcely fit for it.

sn: विमुखानीह सैन्यानि हतं दृष्ट्वा घटोत्कचम्। वयं च भृशमुद्विग्ना हैडिम्बेस्तु निपातनात्॥
en: Indeed on an occasion for sorrow generated by the death of Hidimva's son our troops, beholding Ghatotkacha slain, are flying away.

sn: नैतत्कारणमल्पं हि भविष्यति जनार्दन। तदद्य शंस मे पृष्टः सत्यं सत्यवतां वर॥
en: We also are filled with great grief, at the death of Hidimva's son, O Janardana. The cause of your delight on such occasion must indeed by very serious.

sn: योतन्न रहस्यं ते वक्तुमर्हस्यरिंदम। धैर्यस्य वैकृतं ब्रूहि त्वमद्य मधुसूदन॥
en: O foremost of all truth-speaking men, therefore tell me today truly the cause of your joy. O subduer of foes, if it is not a secret, it behoves you to say it to me.

sn: समुद्रस्येव संशोषं मेरोरिव विसर्पणम्। तथैतदद्य मन्येऽहं तव कर्म जनार्दन॥
en: O Slayer of Madhu, tell me what has disturbed your patience today? O Jannaradana, I consider this fickleness of yours to be like the drying up of the ocean or the walking of the Meru mountain.

sn: श्रीवासुदेव उवाच अतिहर्षमिमं प्राप्तं शृणु मे त्वं धनंजय। अतीव मनसः सद्यः प्रसादकरमुत्तमम्॥
en: Vasudeva's son said Overwhelming is the delight that has filled me now. Hear it, O Dhananjaya. What I shall tell you will immediately dispel your sorrow impart joy on your beast.

sn: शक्तिं घटोत्कचेनेमां व्यंसयित्वा महाद्युते। कर्णं निहतमेवाजौ विद्धि सद्यो धनंजय॥
en: O you of great splendour, his sakti having been used against Ghatotkacha, regard Karna as already slain in battle.

sn: शक्तिहस्तं पुनः कर्णं को लोकेऽस्ति पुमानिह। य एनमभितस्तिष्ठेत् कार्तिकेयमिवाहवे।॥
en: No person could have confronted Karna, if like Kartikeya he would have stood in battle armed with that dart.

sn: दिष्ट्यापनीतकवचो दिष्ट्यापहृतकुण्डलः। दिष्ट्या सा व्यंसिता शक्तिरमोघास्य घटोत्कचे॥
en: It is through good fortune that his armour had been taken away, that his ear-rings, had been taken away from him; by good luck it is that his infallible dart also had been baffled by Ghatotkacha.

sn: यदि हि स्यात् सकवचस्तथैव स्यात् कुण्डलः। सामरानपि लोकांस्त्रीनेकः कर्णो जयेद् रणे॥
en: Covered in his natural coat of mail and decked with his natural ear-rings, Karna, having his senses under thorough control, could, single-handed, defeat the three worlds with the gods therein.

sn: वासवो वा कुबेरो वा वरुणो वा जलेश्वरः। यमो वा नोत्सहेत् कर्णं रणे प्रतिसमासितुम्॥
en: Neither Vasava, nor Kubera, nor Varuna, the lord of the waters, nor the god of Death, could venture to confront him.

sn: गाण्डीवमुद्यम्य भवांश्चक्रं चाहं सुदर्शनम्। न शक्तौ स्वो रणे जेतुं तथायुक्तं नरर्षभम्॥
en: If that foremost of men had his natural coat of mail and car-rings then neither yourself, wielding the Gandiva, nor myself uplifting the discus Sudarsana could have defeated him in battle.

sn: त्वद्धितार्थं तु शक्रेण मायापहृतकुण्डलः। विहीनकवचश्चायं कृतः परपुरंजयः॥
en: For your good, Karna was deprived of his ear-rings by Indra with the aid of illusion. In the same manner that subjugator of hostile troops was deprived of his armour.

sn: उत्कृत्य कवचं यस्मात् कुण्डले विमले च ते। प्रादाच्छकाय कर्णो वै तेन वैकर्तनः स्मृतः॥
en: As Karna had given his effulgent ear-rings and armour cutting them off from his body he is designated as Vikartana.

sn: आशीविष इव क्रुद्धो जुभितो मन्त्रतेजसा। तथाद्य भाति कर्णो मे शान्तज्वाल इवानलः॥
en: Karna now appears to me to be like an infuriate snake of virulent venom stupefied by the virtue of incantation or like a fire with its flames quenched.

sn: यदाप्रभृति कर्णाय शक्तिर्दत्ता महात्मना। वासवेन महाबाहो क्षिप्ता यासौ घटोत्कच॥ कुण्डलाभ्यां निमायाथ दिव्येन कवचेन च। तां प्राप्यामन्यत वृषः सततं त्वां हतं रणे॥
en: 0 mighty-armed one, since the time the illustrious Shakra gave that Sakti to Karna in exchange for the latter's earrings and armour-that Salkti, which has slain Ghatotkacha from that time, Vrisha having obtained it. had always regarded you as slain in battle.

sn: एवंगतोऽपि शक्योऽयं हन्तुं नान्येन केनचित्। ऋते त्वां पुरुषव्याघ्र शये सत्येन चानघ॥
en: But though deprived of that dart, I swear to you, O sinless one, that hero could not still be defeated by any one else save yourself.

sn: ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवादी च तपस्वी नियतव्रतः। रिपुष्वपि दयावांश्च तस्मात् कर्णो वृषः स्मृतः॥
en: Devoted to the Brahmanas, truthful, of ascetic practices and vow-observing and merciful on his foes, Karna is called Vrisha.

sn: युद्धशौण्डो महाबाहुर्नित्योद्यतशरासनः। केसरीव वने नर्दन् मातङ्ग इव यूथपान्॥
en: Delighting in battle, possessed of mighty arms, his bow ever ready for use, like a lion in the forest depriving leaders of elephantine heads of their pride.

sn: विमदान् रथशार्दूलान् कुरुते रणमूर्धनि। मध्यं गत इवादित्यो यो न शक्यो निरीक्षितुम्॥
en: Karna ever humiliates the pride of many mighty car-warriors and resembles the mid-day sun incapable of being looked at.

sn: त्वदीयैः पुरुषव्याघ्र योधमुख्यैर्महात्मभिः। शरजालसहस्रांशु शरदीव दिवाकरः॥
en: When fighting with all the high-souled and excellent warriors of your army, O foremost of men, Karna, discharging his showers of arrows, looks like the autumnal sun of myriad rays.

sn: तपान्ते जलदो यद्वच्छरधाराः क्षरन् मुहुः। दिव्यास्रजलदः कर्णः पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्॥
en: Just like clouds at the end of summer pouring torrents of rain, Karna, shooting incessantly showers of arrows, resembles a pouring cloud charged with celestial weapons.

sn: त्रिदशैरपि चास्यद्भिः शरवर्ष समन्ततः। अशक्यस्तदयं जेतुं स्रवद्भिर्मासशोणितम्॥
en: He is incapable of being vanquished in battle by the very gods shooting showers of arrow in all directions and discharging flesh and blood profusely.

sn: कवचेन विहीनश्च कुण्डलाभ्यां च पाण्डव। सोऽद्य मानुषतां प्राप्तो विमुक्तः शक्रदत्तया॥
en: Deprived of his armour and his two earrings, O son of Pandu and haring given up his Sakti given to him by Shakra, Karna today is nothing more then a mortal.

sn: एको हि योगोऽस्य भवेद् वधाय च्छिद्रे ह्येनं स्वप्रमत्तः प्रमत्तम्। कृच्छं प्राप्तं रथचक्रे विमग्ने हन्याः पूर्वं त्वं तु सज्ञां विचार्य॥
en: There will happen only one opportunity for his slaughter. When the wheels of his chariot will be sunk in the earth, availing yourself of that opportunity and exerting vigourously you should slay him, acting up to my hint.

sn: मप्येकवीरो बलभित् सवज्रः। जरासंघश्चेदिराजो महात्मा महाबाहुश्चैकलव्यो निषादः॥ एकैकशो निहताः सर्व एते योगैस्तैस्तैस्त्वद्धितार्थं मयैव। अथापरे निहता राक्षसेन्द्रा। हिडिम्बकिर्मीरवकप्रधानाः। अलायुधः परचक्रावमर्दी घटोत्कचचोग्रकर्मा तरस्वी॥
en: The conqueror of Bala that excellent hero, wielding his thunder, cannot slay the indomitable Karna when he stands armed with weapons. Indeed, O Arjuna, for your welfare, by the help of numerous machinations, I have destroyed, one after another Jarasandha, the high-souled ruler of the Chedis, the mighty armed Ekalavya of the Nishada tribe, other great Rakshasas having Hidimba, Krimira and Vaka for their leaders, as also Alayudha that crusher of hostile troops and Ghatotkacha that guider of enemies and of fearful feats.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच कथमस्मद्धितार्थं ते कैश्च योगैर्जनार्दन। जरासंघप्रभृतयो घातिताः पृथिवीश्वराः॥
en: Arjuna said How, O Janardana and by what measures were those lords of earth Jarasandha and others slain, for our welfare?

sn: श्रीवासुदेव उवाच जरासंघश्चेदिराजो नैषादिश्व महाबलः। यदि स्युर्न हताः पूर्वमिदानीं स्युर्भयंकराः॥
en: Vasudeva said Had not Jarasandha, the ruler of the Chedis and the highly puissant prince of the Nishadas been slain before, they would have become very terrible by this time.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तानवश्यं वृणुयाद् रथसत्तमान्। तेऽस्मासु नित्यविद्विष्टाः संश्रयेयुश्च कौरवान्॥
en: Duryodhana would then surely have invited those foremost of car-warriors to embrace his cause and they, ever hostile to us, must have chosen the Kaurava party.

sn: ते हि वीरा महेष्वासाः कृतास्रा दृढयोधिनः। धार्तराष्ट्रां चमूं कृत्स्नां रक्षेयुरमरा इव॥
en: They all were brave, fierce bowmen, accomplished in the use of weapons and firm in battle; and they would have then defended the Dhritarashtras like so many immortals.

sn: सूतपुत्रो जरासंघश्चेदिराजो निषादजः। सुयोधनं समाश्रित्य जयेयुः पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: The son of Suta, Jarasandha, the ruler of the Chedis and the prince of the Nishadas, these, united with Suyodhana, mighty have conquered the whole earth.

sn: योगैरपि हता यैस्ते तन्मे शृणु धनंजय। अजय्या हि विना योगैर्मधे ते दैवतैरपि॥
en: It was through my tactics that they were slain. Hear from me of those tactics. Indeed even the gods, without the employment of tactics, could not have defeated them in battle.

sn: एकैको हि पृथक् तेषां समस्तां सुरवाहिनीम्। योधयेत् समरे पार्थ लोकपालाभिरक्षिताम्॥
en: Each of them, individually, could have fought with entire army of the celestials, protected by the regents of the worlds themselves, O son of Pritha!

sn: जरासंधो हि रुषितो रौहिणेयप्रधर्षितः। अस्मद्वधार्थं चिक्षेप गदां वै सर्वघातिनीम्॥
en: Once on a time, afflicted by the son of Rohini, Jarasandha, excited to the highest pitch of fury, hurled at ourselves a mace capable of slaying at creatures.

sn: सीमन्तमिव कुर्वाणा नभसः पावकप्रभा। अदृश्यतापतन्ती सा शक्रमुक्ता यथाशनिः॥
en: Sparkling like the tongues of fire, that mace flew towards ourselves dividing the welkin like the line that parts the tresses of woman and with the impetuosity of the thunder hurled by Shakra.

sn: तामापतन्तीं दृष्टैव गदां रोहिणिनन्दनः। प्रतिघातार्थमस्रं वै स्थूणाकर्णमवासृजत्॥
en: Then beholding that mace course towards us, the son of Rohini, for repulsing that mace, hurled the weapon know as Sthanukarna.

sn: अस्रवेगप्रतिहता सा गदा प्रापतद् भुवि। दारयन्ती धरां देवीं कम्पयन्तीव पर्वतान्॥
en: Repulsed by the force of Baladeva's weapon, that mace fell on the earth riving her open and causing the mountains thereon to tremble.

sn: तत्र सा राक्षसी घोरा जरानाम्नी सुविक्रमा। संदधे सा हि संजातं जरासंधमरिंदमम्॥
en: There was a terrible Rakshasi, by name Jara, possessed of dreadful mighty. She, O monarch, had put together the different parts of Jarasandha's body and therefore was the latter so named.

sn: द्वाभ्यां जातो हि मातृभ्यामर्धदेहः पृथक् पृथक्। जरया संधितो यस्माजरासंधस्ततोऽभवत्॥
en: From two mothers, the two halves of his body come out separately. And in consequence of those two halves being united by that Rakshasi, he was called Jarasandha.

sn: सा तु भूमिं गता पार्थ हता ससुतबान्धवा। गदया तेन चास्त्रेण स्थूणाकर्णेन राक्षसी॥
en: That Rakshasi, that was then within bowels of the death, was slain with her sons and relatives, O son of Pritha, by means of that mace and that weapon Sthanuharana.

sn: विनाभूत: स गदया जरासंधो महामृधे। निहतो भीमसेनेन पश्यतस्ते धनंजय॥
en: Deprived of that mace of his Jarasandha was slain in a fierce encounter by Bhimasena even before your very eyes O Dhananjaya!

sn: यदि हि स्याद् गदापाणिर्जरासंधः प्रतापवान्। सेन्द्रा देवा न तं हन्तुं रणे शक्ता नरोत्तम॥
en: Had the puissant Jarasandha been then armed with his mace then, O foremost of men, even the celestials, with Indra at their head, could not have succeeded in slaying him in battle.

sn: त्वद्धितार्थं च नैषादिरङ्गुष्ठेन वियोजितः। द्रोणेनाचार्यकं कृत्वा छद्मना सत्यविक्रमः॥
en: For your good also was the mighty son of the Nishadhas, deprived, by a guileful means, of his thuinb, by Drona who assumed the position of his preceptor.

sn: स तु बद्धाङ्गुलित्राणो नैषादिर्दृढविक्रमः। अतिमानी वनचरो बभौ राम इवापरः॥
en: That prince of the Nishadas of resolute prowess with his finger-protectors tied round them, used to rove in the forest, swelling with his own pride, like a second Rama.

sn: एकलव्यं हि साङ्गुष्ठमशक्ता देवदानवाः। सराक्षसोरगाः पार्थ विजेतुं युधि कर्हिचित्॥
en: Retaining the use of his thumb Akalavya could not have been defeated in battle by the Danavas, the celestials, the Rakshasas and the serpents, all united together in battle.

sn: किमु मानुषमात्रेण शक्य:स्यात् प्रतिवीक्षितुम्। दृढमुष्टिः कृती नित्यमस्यमानो दिवानिशम्॥
en: Of firm grasp, accomplished in the use of weapons, incessantly shooting his weapons, he could not have been looked at by mere men?

sn: त्वद्धितार्थं तु स मया हतः संग्राममूर्धनि। चेदिराजश्च विक्रान्तः प्रत्यक्षं निहतस्तव॥
en: For your good, he was slain by me in the van of battle. The powerful ruler of the Chedis was also slain before your very eyes.

sn: स चाप्यशक्यः संग्रामे जेतुं सर्वसुरासुरैः। वधार्थं तस्य जातोऽहमन्येषां च सुरद्विषाम्॥
en: He also was incapable of being conquered in battle by the celestials and the Asuras. I suffered this birth only for slaughtering him and other such molesters of the gods.

sn: त्वत्सहायो नरव्याघ्र लोकानां हितकाम्यया। हिडिम्बवककिर्मीरा भीमसेनेन पातिताः॥
en: With your aid, in order to achieve the word's welfare, O foremost of men, Hidimba and Vaka and Krimitra had all been slain by Bhimasena.

sn: रावणेन समप्राणा ब्रह्मयज्ञविनाशनाः। हतस्तथैव मायावी हैडिम्बेनाप्यलायुधः॥
en: Also Alayudha, possessed of potent powers of illusion, has been slain by Hidimva's son. All other Rakshasas, brave like Karna and destroyers of the Brahma, sacrifice, have also been slain.

sn: हैडिम्बश्चाप्युपायेन शक्त्या कर्णेन घातितः। यदि ह्येनं नाहनिष्यत् कर्णः शक्त्या महामृधे॥
en: Through our tactics Karna used that Sakti of his in felling the son of Hidimba. If on the other hand, Karna had not slain this Rakshasa by his Sakti.

sn: मया वध्योऽभविष्यत् स भैमसेनिर्घटोत्कचः। मया न निहतः पूर्वमेष युष्पत्प्रियेप्सया॥
en: Then it would have been my (painful) duty to slay Bhimasena's son Ghatotkacha. It was only for pleasing you that I did not slay him before.

sn: एष हि ब्राह्मणद्वेषी यज्ञद्वेषी च राक्षसः। धर्मस्य लोप्ता पापात्मा तस्मादेष निपातितः॥
en: This Rakshasa was a contumner of the Brahmanas and a destroyer of sacrifices; this wicked-souled one inimical to the performance of sacrifices and therefore has he been slain thus.

sn: व्यंसिता चाप्युपायेन शक्रदत्ता मयानघ। ये हि धर्मस्य लोप्तारो वध्यास्ते मम पाण्डव॥
en: O sinless one, through our tactics the Sakti given to him by Shakra has been also rendered useless. O son of Pandu, those who destroy righteousness are all slayable by me. was

sn: कार्यः धर्मसंस्थापनार्थं हि प्रतिज्ञैषा ममाव्यया। ब्रह्म सत्यं दमः शौचं धर्मो ह्रीः श्रीकृतिः क्षमा॥ यत्र तत्र रमे नित्यमहं सत्येन ते शपे। न विषादस्त्वया कर्ण वैकर्तनं प्रति॥
en: This vow has been taken for establishing righteousness. Where there are the Vedas, truth, self-control, purity, righteousness, humility, prosperity, wisdom and forbearance, there I am also to be found. You need not now be at all anxious about the slaughter of Karna.

sn: उपदेक्ष्याम्युपायं ते येन ते प्रसहिष्यसि। सुयोधनं चापि रणे हनिष्यति वृकोदरः॥
en: I shall tell you the means through which you shall be able to slay Karna. Vrikodara also will slay Suyodhana in battle.

sn: तस्यापि च वधोपायं वक्ष्यामि तव पाण्डव। वर्धते तुमुलस्त्वेष शब्दः परचमूं प्रति॥
en: O son of Pandu, I shall also tell you the means by which that one's slaughter will be compassed. But now, the tumult of the hostile cry is increasing every moment.

sn: विद्रवन्ति च सैन्यानि त्वदीयानि दिशो दश। लब्धलक्ष्या हि कौरव्या विधमन्ति चमू तव। दहत्येष च वः सैन्यं द्रोणः प्रहरतां वरः॥
en: Your own troops also are flying away in all the ten directions of compass; the Kaurava warriors, having reached their aim, are now killing your troops. Yonder indeed does Drona, that foremost of smiters, consume our ranks.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच एकवीरवधे मोघा शक्तिः सूतात्मजे यदा। कस्मात् सर्वान् समुत्सृज्य स तां पार्थे न मुक्तवान्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said If Suta's son had possessed such a Sakti as was sure to slay one hero, why then excepting all others, did he not hurl it at Pritha's son Arjuna.

sn: तस्मिन् हते हता हि स्युः सर्वे पाण्डवसृञ्जयाः। एकवीरवधे कस्माद् युद्धे न जयमादधे॥
en: Had Arjuna been slain by that Sakti, then all the Srinjayas and Pandavas also would have be slain. Indeed, if Phalguna could have been slain, then victory certainly would have been ours.

sn: आहूतो न निवर्तेयमिति तस्य महाव्रतम्। स्वयं मार्गयितव्यः स सूतपुत्रेण फाल्गुनः॥
en: "Challenged, I would never turn back" even this was the vow taken by Arjuna. The son of Suta should therefore have summoned Arjuna in battle.

sn: ततो द्वैरथमानीय फाल्गुनं शक्रदत्तया। जघान न वृषः कस्मात् तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Tell me, O Sanjaya, why then Vrisha, summoning Arjuna to a single combat, did not slay the latter by means of the Sakti given him by Indra.

sn: नूनं बुद्धिविहीनश्चाप्यसहायश्च ते सुतः। शत्रुभिर्व्यसितः पापः कथं नु स जयेदरीन्॥
en: Surely my son is a fool and has not good counsellors also to guide him; that wretch is ever outwitted by the foe, how then can be hope to obtain victory over them?

sn: या ह्यस्य परमा शक्तिर्जयस्य च परायणम्। सा शक्तिर्वासुदेवेन व्यंसिता च घटोत्कचे॥
en: That Sakti which was such a powerful weapon and on which rested his hopes of victory, also even that Sakti had been made futile by Vasudeva's son through Ghatotkacha.

sn: कुणेर्यथा हस्तगतं ह्रियेत् फलं बलीयसा। तथा शक्तिरमोघा सा मोघीभूता घटोत्कचे॥
en: As a fruit is snatched away from the hands of a cripple with withered arms by a powerful man, even so had that mortal Sakti, of Karna, been made futile by Krishna, through Ghatotkacha.

sn: स्तयोरभावे श्वपचस्य लाभ:। मन्ये विद्वन् वासुदेवस्य तद्वद् युद्धे लाभः कर्णहैडिम्बयोवै॥
en: Just as in a battle between a boar and a dog, the huntsman is the party to forfeit when either is slain, so, I think, O intelligent one, Vasudeva's son is to be party benefitted in that battle between Karna and Hidimva's son.

sn: घटोत्कचो यदि हन्याद्धि कर्ण परोलाभः स भवेत् पाण्डवानाम्। वैकर्तनो वा यदि तं निहन्यात् तथापि कृत्यं शक्तिनाशात् कृतं स्यात्॥
en: "If Ghatotkacha slays Karna in battle the Pandavas will be greatly benefitted; on the other hand, if Karna slay Ghatotkacha in battle there will be a great gain to the Pandavas because then Karna's Sakti will be useless."

sn: इति प्राज्ञः प्रज्ञयैतद् विचिन्त्य घटोत्कचं सूतपुत्रेण युद्धे। अधातयद् वासुदेवो नृसिंहः प्रियं कुर्वन् पाण्डवानाहितं च॥
en: Thinking in this way and for doing what was agreeable to the Pandavas that foremost of men Vasudeva, endued with great wisdom, had caused Ghatotkacha to be slain by Karna in battle.

sn: संजय उवाच एतचिकीर्षित ज्ञात्वा कर्णस्य मधुसूदनः। नियोजयामास तदा द्वैरथे राक्षसेश्वरम्॥ घटोत्कचं महावीर्यं महाबुद्धिर्जनार्दनः। अमोघाया विघातार्थं राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव॥
en: Sanjaya said Knowing perfectly well what Karna desired to do, the slayer of Madhu, the mighty armed Janaradana, O monarch ordered the foremost of the Rakshasas, viz., Ghatotkacha of puissant might to engage in a duel with Karna for rendering, O king, the latter's death-dealing Sakti fruitless. All this, O monarch, is the outcome of your wicked policy.

sn: तदैव कृतकार्या हि वयं स्याम कुरूद्वह। न रक्षेद् यदि कृष्णस्तं पार्थं कर्णान्महारणात्॥
en: Operpetuator of Kuru's race, we could then have surely been successful had not Karna.

sn: साश्वध्वजरथः संख्ये धृतराष्ट्र पतेद् भुवि। विना जनार्दनं पार्थो योगानीमीश्वरं प्रभूम्॥
en: O Dhritarashtra, Partha, with his horse, charioteer and standard, would have been completely destroyed in battle, had he been deprived of the aid of Jannardana, that lord of all yoga prowess.

sn: तैस्तैरुपायैर्बहुभी रक्ष्यमाणः च पार्थिवा जयत्यभिमुखः शत्रून् पार्थः कृष्णेन पालितः॥
en: Protected with various means and always defended by Krishna, Partha ever defeats his foes, encountering them.

sn: स विशेषात् त्वमोघायाः कृष्णोऽरक्षत पाण्डवम्। हन्यात् क्षिप्रं हि कौन्तेयं शक्तिर्वृक्षमिवाशनिः॥
en: Indeed, it was Krishna that rescued Pritha's son from that death dealing Sakti otherwise that weapon would have quickly consumed the son of Kunti like the bolt of Heaven destroying a tree.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच विरोधी च कुमन्त्री च प्राज्ञमानी ममात्मजः। यस्यैव समतिक्रान्तो वधोपायो जयं प्रति॥
en: Dhritarashtra said My son in quarrelsome; his counsellors are so many fools. He is proud of his wisdom. He has thus overlooked the certain means that have given him victory.

sn: स वा कर्णो महाबुद्धिः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। न मुक्तवान् कथं सूत ताममोघां धनंजये। १८॥
en: Why, O Suta, did not Karna of high intelligence that foremost of all wielders of weapons discharge that fatal Sakti at Dhananjaya?

sn: तवापि समतिक्रान्तमेतद् गावल्गणे कथम्। एतमर्थं महाबुद्धे यत् त्वया नावबोधितः॥
en: Why, O Gavalgani's son, did you too forget this great object, since endued as you are with great intelligence, you did not remind Karna?

sn: संजय उवाच दुर्योधनस्य शकुनेर्मम दुःशासनस्य च। रात्रौ रात्रौ भवत्येषा नित्यमेव समर्थना॥
en: Sanjaya said Indeed, every night, O monarch, this used to form the subject of deliberation among Duryodhana, Sakuni, Dushasana and myself.

sn: श्वः सर्वसैन्यान्युत्सृज्य जहि कर्ण धनंजयम्। प्रेष्यवत् पाण्डुपञ्चालानुपभोक्ष्यामहे ततः॥
en: O Karna, leaving alone the rest of the warriors do you slay Dhananjaya. After that we shall lord over the Panchalas and the Pandavas as if they were mere slaves.

sn: अथवा निहते पार्थं पाण्डवान्यतमं ततः। स्थापयेद् यदि वार्ष्णेयस्तस्मात्कृष्णो हि हन्यताम्॥२२
en: Or it may be that upon the fall of Pritha's son, he, of Vrishni's race, will appoint another among the Pandavas to act as the leader of them. Therefore let Krishna be slain.

sn: कृष्णो हि मूलं पाण्डूनां पार्थः स्कन्ध इवोद्गतः। शाखा इवेतरे पार्थाः पञ्चालाः पत्रसंज्ञिताः॥
en: Krishna is the root of the Pandavas, Partha is their risen trunk. The other sons of Pritha and the Panchalas are like their branches and leaves respectively.

sn: कृष्णाश्रयाः कृष्णबलाः कृष्णनाथाश्च पाण्डवाः। कृष्णः परायणं चैषां ज्योतिषामिव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: The Pandavas have Krishna for their shelter, Krishna for their strength and Krishna for their leader. Krishna is their main support like the moon of the constellations.

sn: तस्मात् पर्णानि शाखाश्च स्कन्धं चोत्सृज्य सूतज। कृष्णं हि विद्धि पाण्डूनां मूलं सर्वत्र सर्वदा॥
en: Therefore, O son of Suta, leave alone the leaves, the branches and the trunk of the Pandava tree. Know Krishna to be its root, ever and every where.

sn: हन्याद् यदि हि दाशार्ह कर्णो यादवनन्दनम्। कृत्स्ना वसुमती राजन् वशे तस्य न संशयः॥
en: (Thus indeed did we then speak to Karna). Had he slain the scion of the Dasharha race, that delighter of the Yadavas and in that case, the whole earth, O monarch, would certainly have come under your sway.

sn: यदि हि स निहतः शयीत भूमौ यदुकुलपाण्डवनन्दनो महात्मा। ननु तव वसुधा नरेन्द्र सर्वा सगिरिसमुद्रवना वशं व्रजेत॥
en: If that illustrious delighter, of the Yadu race and of the Pandavas, had lain prostrate on the field being slain in battle then, O ruler of men, this earth certainly would have fallen under your sway together with all her mountains, forests and seas.

sn: सा तु बुद्धिः कृताप्येवं जाग्रति त्रिदशेश्वरे। अप्रमेये हृषीकेशे युद्धकालेऽप्यमुह्यत॥
en: We rose every morning with this resolution regarding that lord of the celestials, viz., Hrishikesha of infinite prowess. But at the time of battle we forgot our resolution.

sn: अर्जुनं चापि राधेयात् सदा रक्षति केशवः। न ह्येनमैच्छत् प्रमुखे सौतेः स्थापयितुं रणे॥
en: Keshava ever defends Kunti's son Arjuna. He never allowed Arjuna to expose himself before Suta's son in battle.

sn: अन्यांश्चस्मै रथोदारानुपास्थापयदच्युतः। अमोघां तां कथं शक्तिं मोघां कुर्यामिति प्रभो॥
en: That undeteriorating one even made other foremost of car-ivarriors confront Karna, thinking how that fatal Sakti of ours might be rendered futile by us, O master.

sn: यश्चैवं रक्षते पार्थं कर्णात् कृष्णो महामनाः। आत्मानं स कथं राजन् न रक्षेत् पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: When again the illustrious Krishna protected Pritha's son in this manner, why, O king, would not that foremost of kings protect his own self?

sn: परिचिन्त्य तु पश्यामि चक्रायुधमरिंदमम्। न सोऽस्ति त्रिषु लोकेषु यो जयेत जनार्दनम्॥
en: Upon mature thought, I see that there is no person in the three worlds who is able to defeat that subduer of foe viz., Janaraddana, that hero bearing the discus in hand.

sn: ततः कृष्णं महाबाहुं सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः। पप्रच्छ रथशार्दूल: कर्णं प्रति महारथः॥
en: Sanjaya said That foremost of car-warrior viz., Satyaki of prowess incapable of being baffled, asked

sn: अयं च प्रत्ययः कर्णे शक्तिशामितविक्रमा। किमर्थं सूतपुत्रेण न मुक्ता फाल्गुने तु सा॥
en: O Janardana, it had been Karna's firm resolve that he would hurl that dart of infinite energy at Phalguna. Why then did he not hurt if at him actually.

sn: श्रीवासुदेव उवाच दुःशासनश्च कर्णश्च शकुनिश्च ससैन्धवः। सततं मन्त्रयन्ति स्म दुर्योधनपुरोगमाः॥
en: Vasudeva said Dushasana, Karna, Sakuni the ruler of the Sindhus with Duryodhana at their head, had frequently held consultation about this subject.

sn: कर्ण कर्ण महेष्वास रणेऽमितपराक्रम। नान्यस्य शक्तिरेषा ते मोक्तव्या जयतां वर॥
en: They used to say to Karna, "Oh Karna, oh mighty bowman, O you of infinite prowess in battle, you should not hurl this Sakti at any one close, O foremost of all victorious combatants.

sn: ऋते महारथात् कर्ण कुन्तीपुत्राद् धनंजयात्। स हि तेषामतियशा देवानामिव वासवः॥
en: Except the mighty car-warrior Partha, that son of Kunti who had conquered the lord of wealth himself. Like Vasava among the Gods, he is the most illustrious among the Pandavas.

sn: तस्मिन् विनिहते पार्थे पाण्डवाः सृञ्जयैः सह। भविष्यन्ति गतात्मानः सुरा इव निरग्नयः॥
en: Upon his slaughter, the rest of the Pandavas and the Srinjayas will be heartless like the god deprived of the fire in his mouth."

sn: तथेति च प्रतिज्ञातं कर्णेन शिनिपुङ्गव। हृदि नित्यं च कर्णस्य वधो गाण्डीवधन्वनः॥
en: Karna having agreed, saying let it be so, O foremost of the Shinis, the slaughter of the wielder of the Gandiva bow was ever the ruling through in Karna's mind.

sn: अहमेव तु राधेयं मोहयामि युधां वर। ततो नावासृजच्छक्तिं पाण्डवे श्वेतवाहने॥
en: O foremost of warriors, it was I who confounded the son of Radha, in consequence whereof he did not hurl that Satki at the son of Pandu owning white steeds.

sn: फाल्गुनस्य हि सा मृत्युरिति चिन्तयतोऽनिशम्। न निद्रा न च मे हर्षो मनसोऽस्ति युधां वर॥
en: O foremost of warriors, as long as I did not succeed in nullifying that means of Arjuna's death, I enjoyed neither sleep nor joy.

sn: घटोत्कचे व्यंसितां तु दृष्ट्वा तां शिनिपुङ्गव। मृत्योरास्यान्तरान्मुक्तं पश्याम्यद्य धनंजयम्॥
en: Beholding that dart therefore rendered fruitless through Ghatotkacha, O foremost of the Shinis, I consider Phalguna to be almost saved from the jaws of Death.

sn: न पिता न च मे माता न यूयं भ्रातरस्तथा। न च प्राणास्तथा रक्ष्या यथा बीभत्सुराहवे॥
en: Neither my father nor my mother nor yourself, nor my brother, nor even my life, is so worthy of my protection as is Vibhatsu in battle.

sn: त्रैलोक्यराज्याद् यत् किंचिद् भवेदन्यत् सुदुलभम्। नेच्छेयं सात्वताहं तद् विना पार्थं धनंजयम्॥
en: If there by anything more precious that the sovereignty of the three worlds, even that I do not want to have at the cost of Dhananjaya the son of Pritha.

sn: अतः प्रहर्षः सुमहान् युयुधानाद्य मेऽभवत्। मृतं प्रत्यागतमिव दृष्ट्वा पार्थं धनंजयम्॥
en: Therefore, O Yuyudhana, a great joy has taken possession of myself today, in as much as I look upon Pritha's son as returned from the dead.

sn: अतश्च प्रहितो युद्धे मया कर्णाय राक्षसः। न ह्यन्यः समरे रात्रौ शक्तः कर्णं प्रबाधितुम्॥
en: For this reason also was the Rakshasa dispatched by me to meet Karna. No one else couid have checked the latter in this nocturnal fight.

sn: संजय उवाच इति सात्यकये प्राह तदा देवकिनन्दनः। धनंजयहिते युक्तस्तत्प्रिये सततं रतः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then the son of Devaki did thus speak to Satyaki, he who devoted to Dhananjaya's good and to what was agreeable to him. was ever couid have checked the latter in this nocturnal fight.

sn: संजय उवाच इति सात्यकये प्राह तदा देवकिनन्दनः। धनंजयहिते युक्तस्तत्प्रिये सततं रतः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then the son of Devaki did thus speak to Satyaki, he who devoted to Dhananjaya's good and to what was agreeable to him. was ever

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कर्णदुर्योधनादीनां शकुनेः सौबलस्य च। अपनीतं महत् तात तव चैव विशेषतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O sire, this act of Karna, Duryodhana, Sakuni the son of Subala and especially of yourself, has been very much against the dictates of policy.

sn: यदि जानीथ तां शक्तिमेकघ्नीं सततं रणे। अनिवार्यामसह्यां च देवैरपि सवासवैः॥
en: Indeed when you knew that Sakti was capable of slaying only one person and that it was incapable of being borne and repulsed even by the gods with Vasava at their head.

sn: सा किमर्थं तु कर्णेन प्रवृत्ते समरे पुरा। न देवकीसुते मुक्ता फाल्गुने वापि संजय॥
en: Why then, O Sanjaya, was it not hurled by Karna at the son of Devaki or at Phalguna while he was engaged with these in battle before.

sn: संजय उवाच संग्रामाद् विनिवृत्तानां सर्वेषां नो विशाम्पते। रात्रौ कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ मन्त्रोऽयं समजायत॥ प्रभातमात्रे श्वोभूते केशवाया नाय वा। शक्तिरेषा हि मोक्तव्या कर्ण कर्णेति नित्यशः॥
en: Sanjaya said Every day returning from the field of battle, O ruler of men, we used to hold consultation in the night and speak unto Karna, O foremost of the Kurus, in the following manner. O Karna, tomorrow this Sakti should be hurled at either Karna or Arjuna."

sn: ततः प्रभातसमये राजन् कर्णस्य दैवतैः। अन्येषां चैव योधानां सा बुद्धिर्नाश्यते पुनः॥
en: When however, the day dawned, 0 monarch, as fate would have it, Karna as well as all the other warriors forget all about that resolution.

sn: दैवमेव परं मन्ये यत् कर्णो हस्तसंस्थया। न जघान रणे पार्थं कृष्णं वा देवकीसुतम्॥
en: Indeed it is destiny that is supreme to all other forces, inasmuch as Karna did not slay cither Partha or Krishna with the dart that he had in his grasp.

sn: तस्य हस्तस्थिता शक्तिः कालरात्रिरिवोद्यता। दैवोपहतबुद्धित्वान्न तां कर्णो विमुक्तवान्॥ कृष्णे वा देवकीपुत्रे मोहितो देवमायया। पार्थे वा शक्रकल्पे वै वधार्थं वासवीं प्रभो॥
en: Indeed because his intelligence had been confounded by destiny itself that he did not, stupefied by the illusion of the Gods, hur) that death dealing lart given him by Vasava, though he held in his hand, at Krishna the son of Devaki it at Parthas of prowess equal to that of Indra, for their destruction.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच दैवेनोपहता यूयं स्वबुद्ध्या केशवस्य च। गता हि वासवी हत्वा तृणभूतं घटोत्कचम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said You are destroyed by Destiny, by your own understanding and by Kesava. The fatal dart of Vasava is lost having brought about the slaughter of Ghatotkacha who was insignificant as a straw.

sn: कर्णश्च मम पुत्राश्च सर्वे चान्ये च पार्थिवाः। तेन वै दुष्प्रणीतेन गता वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: as Karna and my sons as all the other kings, through his greatly impolitic act, have already gone to the abode of wealth.

sn: भूय एव तु मे शंस यथा युद्धमवर्तत। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च हैडिम्बे निहते तदा॥
en: Describe to me how the battle raged between the Kurus and the Pandavas after the fall of Hidimva's son.

sn: थे च तेऽभ्यद्रवन् द्रोणं व्यूढानीकः प्रहारिणः। सुंजयाः सह पञ्चास्तेऽप्यकुर्वन् कथं रणम्॥
en: How did the Panchalas and the Srinjayas, arranged in order and well-skilled in smiting, fight, having rushed upon Drona in battle.

sn: सौमदत्तेर्वधाद् द्रोणमायान्तं सैन्धवस्य च। अमर्षाजीवितं त्यक्त्वा गाहमानं वरुथिनीम्॥ जृम्भमाणमिव व्याघ्रं व्यात्ताननमिवान्तकम्। कथं प्रत्युद्ययुयॊणमस्यन्तं पाण्डुसृञ्जयाः॥
en: How indeed did Pandus and Srinjayas resist the striking Drona when he proceeding against them, penetrated into their host inflamed with wrath at the slaughter of Bhurisravas and Jayadratha, regardless of his very life and resembling a yawning tiger on the destroyer himself with mouth agape.

sn: आचार्यं ये च तेऽरक्षन् दुर्योधनपुरोगमाः। द्रौणिकर्णकृपास्तात ते वाकुर्वन् किमाहवे॥
en: What also did they do in battle, O sire, viz., Drona's son and Karna and Kripa and others headed by Duryodhana that protected the preceptor.

sn: भारद्वाजं जिघांसन्तौ सव्यसाचिवृकोदरौ। समार्च्छन् मामका युद्धे कथं संजय शंस मे॥
en: Describe to me, O Sanjaya, how my combatants in that battle covered with their arrows Dhananjaya and Vrikodara who were desirous of slaying the son of Bharadvaja.

sn: सिन्धुरावधेनेमे घटोत्कचवधेन ते। अमर्षिताः सुसंक्रुद्धा रणं चक्रुः कथं निशि॥
en: How indeed did those, worked up with anger at the death of the ruler of the Sindhus and those at the death of Ghatotkacha, each side unable to brook their loss, fight during that night.

sn: संजय उवाच हते घटोत्कचे राजन् कर्णेन निशि राक्षसे। प्रणदत्सु च हृष्टेषु तावकेषु युयुत्सुषु॥
en: Sanjaya said Upon the destruction, that night, O monarch of the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha by Karna, all your soldiers filled with delight uttered loud shouts.

sn: आपतत्सु च वेगेन वध्यमाने बलेऽपि च। विगाढायां रजन्यां च राजा दैन्यं परं गतः॥
en: In that dark hour of night they furiously assailed the Pandava troop and began to slaughter them. Seeing all this king Yudhishthira became highly depressed.

sn: अब्रवीच महाबाहुर्भीमसेनमिदं वचः। आवारय महाबाहो धार्तराष्ट्रस्य वाहिनीम्॥
en: O chastiser of foes, the mighty armed son of Pandu then addressed Bhima and thus spoke: "O you of might arms, check the (rushing) host of Dhritarashtra's son.

sn: हैडिम्बेश्चैव घातेन मोहो मामाविशन्महान्। एवं भीमं समादिश्य स्वरथे समुपाविशत्॥
en: Owing to the slaughter of Hidimva's son a great stupefaction is overwhelming me." Having commanded Bhima thus he sat down on the terrace of his car.

sn: अश्रुपूर्णमुखो राजा निःश्वसंश्च पुनः पुनः। कश्मलं प्राविशद् घोरं दृष्टवा कर्णस्य विक्रमम्॥
en: With fearful countenance and repeated sighs the monarch became highly depressed on seeing Karna's prowess.

sn: तं तथा व्यथितं दृष्ट्वा कृष्णो वचनमब्रवीत्। मा व्यथां कुरु कौन्तेय नैतत् त्वय्युपपद्यते॥ वैकुव्यं भरतश्रेष्ठ यथा प्राकृतपूरुषे। उत्तिष्ठ राजन् युद्ध्यस्व वह गुर्वी धुरं विभो॥
en: Seeing him so afflicted, Krishna said these words, “O son of Kunti. let not such gricf overtake you. This depression is not worthy of yourself, O chief of the Bharatas, as it is of an ordinary person; arise O monarch and fight and bear this heavy burden of grief.

sn: त्वयि वैकुव्यमापन्ने संशयो विजये भवेत्। श्रुत्वा कृष्णस्य वचनं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: If you are overtaken by depression victory becomes uncertain." Hearing these words of Krishna the very virtuous king Yudhishthira.

sn: विमृज्य नेत्रे पाणिभ्यां कृष्णं वचनमब्रवीत्। विदिता मे महाबाहो धर्माणां परमा गतिः॥
en: Wiping his eyes with his hands replied unto Krishna saying-O) you of mighty arms, the excellent path of duty is not unknown to you.

sn: ब्रह्महत्या फलं तस्य यैः कृतं नावबुध्यते। श्रस्माकं हि वनस्थानां हैडिम्बेन महात्मना॥
en: The dreadful consequences of Brahmanicide are his that forgets the services he gets at the hands of others. While we were living in the woods the illustrious son of Hidimba.

sn: बालेनापि सता तेन कृतं साह्यं जनार्दन। असहेतोर्गतं ज्ञात्वा पाण्डवं श्वेतवाहनम्॥
en: Although then a small boy only, did us many good turns, O Jannarddana. Being informed that Pandu's son Arjuna had gone to acquire weapons.

sn: असौ कृष्ण महेष्वासः काम्यके मामुपस्थितः। उषितश्च सहास्माभिर्यावन्नासीद् धनंजयः॥
en: O Krishna, this fierce bowman went to see me in the Kamyaka forest. he there lived with us until Dhananjaya came back.

sn: गन्धमादनयात्रायां दुर्गेभ्यश्च स्म तारिताः। पाञ्चाली च परिश्रान्ता पृष्ठेनोढा महात्मना॥
en: On the occasion of our journey to the Ghandhamadana, we crossed all difficulties with his help. He then carried the fatigued daughter of the Panchalas on his own back.

sn: आरम्भाच्चैव युद्धानां यदेष कृतवान् प्रभो। मदर्थे दुष्करं कर्म कृतं तेन महाहवे॥
en: O master, the feats he had achieved in battle, fully prove that he was learned in all

sn: मे
en: modes of warfare. That illustrious warrior did accomplish many difficult tasks for my sake only.

sn: स्वभावाद् या च मे प्रीतिः सहदेवे जनार्दन। सैव मे परमा प्रीती राक्षसेन्द्रे घटोत्कचे॥
en: O Janardana, the affection that I naturally bear for Sahadeva, even double that affection did I bear to that foremost of the Rakshasas Ghatotkacha.

sn: भक्तश्च महाबाहुः प्रियोऽस्याहं प्रियश्च मे। तेन विन्दामि वार्ष्णेय कश्मलं शोकतापितः॥
en: That mighty armed one was devoted to me; I love him and he also loved me dearly. For all these reasons, descendant of the Vrishni race, I am depressed being afflicted with grief caused by his slaughter.

sn: पश्य सैन्यानि वार्ष्णेय द्राव्यमाणानि कौरवैः। द्रोणकर्णी तु संयत्तौ पश्य युद्धे महारथौ॥
en: Behold, O scion of the Vrishni race, my troops routed by the Kouravas! Behold the two mighty car-warriors, Drona and Karna fight, yonder, to the best of their abilities.

sn: निशीथे पाण्डवं सैन्यमेतत् सैन्यप्रमर्दितम्। गजाभ्यामिव मत्ताभ्यां यथा नलवनं महत्॥
en: Lo! at this dead hour of night, the Pandava army is being crushed like a forest of reeds by two infuriate elephants in rut.

sn: अनादृत्य बलं बाह्वोर्भीमसेनस्य माधव। चित्रास्रतां च पार्थस्य विक्रमन्ति स्म कौरवः॥
en: Oscion of Madhu's race, the Kouravas are striving hard (for victory) setting at naught the might of Bhima's arm and the vast mastery of weapons of Arjuna.

sn: एष द्रोणश्च कर्णश्च राजा चैव सुयोधनः। निहत्य राक्षसं युद्धे हृष्टाः नर्दन्ति संयुगे॥
en: Yonder joyfully roars Drona and Karna and king Suyodhana himself having slain the Rakshasa in battle.

sn: कथं वास्मासु जीवत्सु त्वयि चैव जनार्दन। हैडिम्बिः प्राप्तवान् मृत्युं सूतपुत्रेण सङ्गतः॥
en: How is it, O Janardana, that Hidimva's son met with death in his encounter with Suta's son, although you and ourselves are still alive?

sn: कदर्थीकृत्य नः सर्वान् पश्यतः सव्यसाचिनः। निहतो राक्षस: कृष्ण भैमसेनिर्महाबलः॥
en: Putting ourselves to shame and under the very eyes of Savyasachin, O Krishna, Karna has slain the puissant son of Bhimasena.

sn: यदाभिमन्युनिहतो धार्तराष्टैर्दुरात्मभिः। नासीत् तत्र रणे कृष्ण सव्यसाची महारथः॥
en: O Krishna, when Abhimanyu was slain by the sinful Dhartarashtras the mighty carwarrior Savyasachin was not at hand.

sn: निरुद्धाश्च वयं सर्वे सैन्धवेन दुरात्मना। निमित्तमभवद् द्रोणः सपुत्रस्तत्र कर्मणि॥
en: We also were held in check by the highsouled ruler of the Sindhus ; in the perpetration of that deed, Drona and Drona's son became instrumental.

sn: उपदिष्टो वधोपायः कर्णस्य गुरुणा स्वयम्। व्यायच्छतश्च खड्ड्रेन द्विधा खङ्गं चकार ह॥
en: Karna was informed of the means of Abhimanyu's death by the preceptor himself. While Abhimanyu was fighting with his sword, it was Drona who cut-off that sword in twain.

sn: व्यसने वर्तमानस्य कृतवर्मा नृशंसवत्। अश्वाञ्जधान सहसा तथोभौ पाणिसारथी॥
en: Like one heartless, Kritavarman slew the four steeds and the two drivers of Abhimanyu when the latter was involved in a great predicament.

sn: तथेतरे महेष्वासः सौभद्रं युध्यपातयन्। अल्पे च कारणे कृष्ण हतो गाण्डीवधन्वना॥ सैन्धवो यादवश्रेष्ठ तच नातिप्रियं मम। यदि शत्रुवधो न्याय्यो भवेत् कर्तुं हि पाण्डवैः॥
en: Then other bowmen slaughtered and felled the son of Subhadra. For trifling offense only, O Krishna, the ruler of the Sindhus was slain by the wielder of the Gandiva bow. O foremost of Yadus, this act did not afforded me much delight. If at all it is just for the Pandavas to slaughter their foes.

sn: कर्णद्रोणौ रणे पूर्वं हन्तव्याविति मे मतिः। एतौ हि मूलं दुःखानामस्माकं पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Then, I think, Drona and Karna should have been slain ere now. O foremost of men, they are the cause of all our miseries.

sn: एतौ रणे समासाद्य समाश्वस्तः सुयोधनः। यत्र वध्यो भवेद् द्रोणः सूतपुत्रश्च सानुगः॥
en: Getting these two for his supporter in battle, Suyodhana has become confident of his success. Indeed it was Drona or the son of Suta, with his followers who deserved to be slain.

sn: तत्रावधीन्महाबाहुः सैन्धवं दूरवासिनम्। अवश्यं तु मया कार्य: सूतपुत्रस्य निग्रहः॥
en: The mighty armed Dhananjaya slew the king of the Sindhus, who indeed, was the remote cause of the slaughter of Abhimanyu. It is surely my imperative duty to crush the son of Suta.

sn: ततो यास्याम्यहं वीर स्वयं कर्णजिघांसया। भीमसेनो महाबाहुर्दोणानीकेन सङ्गतः॥
en: Therefore, O hero, I will fight for compassing the death of Suta's son. The mighty-armed Bhima has already engaged himself with the division of Drona."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ययौ तूर्णं त्वरमाणो युधिष्ठिरः। स विस्फार्य महचापं शङ्ख प्रध्यमाप्य भैरवम्॥
en: Having thus spoken, king Yudhishthira quickly advanced against Karna stretching his mighty bow and blowing his dreadful conch.

sn: ततो रथसहस्रेण गजानां च शतैसिभिः। वाजिभिः पञ्चसाहौः पञ्चालैः सप्रभद्रकैः॥
en: Then with one thousand cars, three hundred elephants, five thousand horses and the Panchalas and the Pravadrakas.

sn: वृतः शिखण्डी त्वरितो राजानं पृष्ठतोऽन्वयात्। ततो भेरी: समाजघ्नुः शङ्खान् दध्मुश्च दंशिताः॥
en: Sikhandin quickly followed the king from behind. Then the drums were beat and conchs blown by the.

sn: पञ्चालाः पाण्डवाश्चैव युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमाः। ततोऽब्रवीन्महाबाहुर्वासुदेवो धनंजयम्॥
en: Panchalas and Pandavas who proceeding in Yudhishthira's van. Thereupon were the mighty armed Vasudeva addressing Dhananjaya said

sn: एष प्रयाति त्वरितः क्रोधाविष्टो युधिष्ठिरः। जिघांसुः सूतपुत्रस्य तस्योपेक्षा न युज्यते॥
en: Lo! under the influence of anger does king Yudhishthira advance to battle, impelled by a desire for slaughtering Suta's son. It is not proper that you should thoroughly rely on him in this encounter.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशः शीघ्रमश्वानचोदयत्। दूरं प्रयान्तं राजानमन्वगच्छजनार्दनः॥
en: Having thus spoken, Hrishikesha urged the steeds to the best of their speed and he then followed behind the king, who had already advanced a long way.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा सहसा यान्तं सूतपुत्रजिघांसया। शोकोपहतसंकल्पं दह्यमानमिवाग्निना॥
en: At that moment, behoiding the very virtuous king Yudhishthira proceed with impetuosity for bringing about the slaughter of Suta's son, Vyasa approached him and said these words to him who was then burning with the fire of grief and whose reason was clouded by it.

sn: व्यास उवाच अभिगम्याब्रवीद् व्यासो धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। कर्णमासाद्य संग्रामे दिष्ट्या जीवति फाल्गुनः॥ सव्यसाचिवधाकांक्षी शक्तिं रक्षितवान् हि सः।
en: Vyasa said. Indeed, O king, it fortunate that Phalguna still lives, although he had several times encountered Karna in battle. It was for compassing the slaughter to Savyasachin, that Karna preserved his Sakti.

sn: न चागाद् द्वैरथं जिष्णुर्दिष्ट्या तेन महारणे॥ सृजेता स्पर्धिनावेतौ दिव्यान्यस्राणि सर्वशः।
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, it is indeed fortunate that till now Jishnu never engaged in any duel with Karna. In that case, each of them, challenging the other, would have discharged their celestial weapons on all sides.

sn: वध्यमानेषु चास्रेषु पीडितः सूतनन्दनः॥ वासवीं समरे शक्तिं ध्रुवं मुञ्चेद् युधिष्ठिर।
en: Then the weapons of Suta's son would have been destroyed by those of Arjuna. Then sorely distressed the former surely would have discharged the Sakti given him by Vasava at the latter, O Yudhishthira.

sn: ततो भवेत् ते व्यसनं घोरं भरतसत्तम॥ दिष्ट्या रक्षो हतं युद्धे सूतपुत्रेण मानद।
en: In that case, O foremost of the Bharata, a dreadful catastrophe would have overtaken you. O bestower of honor, it is indeed fortunate that the Rakshasas has been slain (with that Sakti) in battle.

sn: वासवीं कारणं कृत्वा कालेनोपहतो ह्यसौ॥ तवैव कारणाद् रक्षो निहतं तात संयुगे।
en: Death himself has slain the Rakshasa and the fatal Sakti of Vasava was only the instrument. O sire, it is for your good that he has been slain in battle.

sn: मा क्रुधो भरतश्रेष्ठ मा च शोके मनः कृथाः॥ प्राणिनामिह सर्वेषामेषा निष्ठा युधिष्ठिर।
en: Do not give way to wrath, ( foremost of the Bharatas and set not your heart on sorrow. O Yudhishthira, this is the finale of all animate beings in this world.

sn: भ्रातृभिः सहितः सर्वैः पार्थिवैश्च महात्मभिः॥ कौरवान् समरे राजन् प्रतियुध्यस्व भारत।
en: United with your brother and the other high souled rulers of earth do you, O descendant of the Bharatas, give battle to the Kouravas.

sn: पञ्चमे दिवसे तात पृथिवी ते भविष्यति॥ नित्यं च पुरुषव्याघ्र धर्ममेवानुचिन्तय।
en: On the fifty day, the carth will fall under your sway. O foremost of men, meditate on virtue.

sn: आनृशंस्यं तपो दानं क्षमां सत्यं च पाण्डव।॥ सेवेथाः परमप्रीतो यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः। इत्युक्त्वा पाण्डवं व्यासस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: With a delightful heart do you ever practise harmlessness, ascetic austerities, charity, forbearance and truth, O son of Pandu. Victory cver follows in the wake of righteousness." Having thus spoken to Pandu's son, Vyasa disappcared then and there, forbearance and truth, O son of Pandu. Victory cver follows in the wake of righteousness." Having thus spoken to Pandu's son, Vyasa disappcared then and there,

sn: संजय उवाच
en: son

sn: व्यासेनैवमथोक्तस्तु धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। स्वयं कर्णवधाद् वीरो निवृत्तो भरतर्षभ॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus spoken to by Vyasa the very virtuous king Yudhishthira, endued with heroism, desisted himself from slaughtering Karna, O foremost of the Bharatas.

sn: घटोत्कचे तु निहते सूतपुत्रेण तां निशाम्। दुःखामर्षवशं प्राप्तो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Upon the slaughter of Ghatotkacha during that night by Suta's Karna, king Yudhishthira was overwhelmed with grief and wrath.

sn: दृष्ट्वा भीमेन महतीं वार्यमाणां चमू तव। धृष्टद्युम्नमुवाचेदं कुम्भयोनि निवारय॥
en: Then beholding your vast host resisted by Bhima himself, he, addressing Dhistadyumna said, 'Hold the pot-born Drona in check.'

sn: त्वं हि द्रोणविनाशाय समुत्पन्नो हुताशनात्। सशरः कवची खड्गी धन्वी च परतापनः॥
en: O afflicter of your foes, it was for the express purpose of slaying Drona, that you Sprang out of fire, armed with a bow and arrows and a sword and cased in a coat of mail.

sn: अभिद्रव रणे हृष्टो मा च ते भीः कथंचन। जनमेजयः शिखण्डी च दौर्मुखिश्च यशोधरः॥
en: Cheerfully assail Drona in battle. You have nothing to be afraid of. Let also Janamejaya, Siklandin and Durmukha's son and Jasadhara,

sn: अभिद्रवन्तु संहष्टाः कुम्भयोनि समन्ततः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च द्रौपदेयाः प्रभद्रकाः॥
en: Wrathfully assail thc pot-born Drona from all sides. Nakula and Sahadeva, the son of Draupadi and the Pravadrakas.

sn: दुपदश्च विराटश्च पुत्रभ्रातृसमन्वितौ। सात्यकि: केकयाश्चैव पाण्डवश्च धनंजयः॥
en: And Drupada and Virata accompanied by their sons and brothers and Satyaki and the Kekayas, the Pandavas and Dhananjaya.

sn: अभिद्रवन्तु वेगेन कुम्भयोनिवधेप्सया। तथैव रथिनः सर्वे हस्त्यश्वं यच किञ्चन॥
en: Let, the inspired with the desire for achieving the slaughter of Bharadvaja's son, assail him from all sides. So also, let all the other car-warriors and clephant riders and horsemen.

sn: पदाताश्च रणे द्रोणं पातयन्तु महारथम्। तथाऽऽज्ञप्तास्तु ते सर्वे पाण्डवेन महात्मना॥
en: And foot soldiers strive to overthrow that mighty car-warrior Drona in battle.” Thus commanded by the illustrious son of Pandu (Yudhishthira).

sn: अभ्यद्रवन्त वेगेन कुम्भयोनिवधेप्सया। आगच्छतस्तान् सहसा सर्वोद्योगेन पाण्डवान्॥
en: Assailed the pot-born Drona with a view to defeat him. Then as the Pandavas rushed with great impetuosity and force.

sn: प्रतिजग्राह समरे द्रोणः शस्रभृतां वरः। ततो दुर्योधनो राजा सर्वोद्योगेन पाण्डवान्॥ अभ्यद्रवत् सुसंक्रुद्ध इच्छन् द्रोणस्य जीवितम्। ततः प्रववृते युद्धं आन्तवाहनसैनिकम्॥ पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च गर्जतामितरेतरम्। निद्रान्धास्ते महाराज परिश्रान्ताश्च संयुगे॥
en: Drona, that foremost of all wielders of weapons, received them (duly) in battle. Thereupon king Duryodhana. with all efforts, assailed the Pandavas excited as he was with rage and solicitous of protecting Drona's life. Then ensued the battle between the troops of the Kurus and the Pandavas whose animals were exhausted as they challenged one another furiously. Deprived of sleep and fatigued in battle, O mighty monarch.

sn: नाभ्यपद्यन्त समरे काञ्चिच्चेष्टां महारथाः। त्रियामा रजनी चैषा घोररूपा भयानका॥
en: The mighty car-warriors knew not what to do. That night consisting of three Yamas, hedious and dreadful.

sn: सहस्रयामप्रतिमा बभूव प्राणहारिणी। वध्यतां च तथा तेषां क्षतानां च विशेषतः॥
en: And destructive of many lives, appeared to them to consist of a thousand Yamas. While they were being thus slain and mangled by another.

sn: अर्धरात्रिः समाजज्ञे निद्रान्धानां विशेषतः। सर्वे ह्यासन् निरुत्साहाः क्षत्रिया दीनचेतसः॥
en: And while their eyes were being closed in sleep, mid-night set in. Then every one became depressed and their spirits became low.

sn: तव चैव परेषां च गताम्रा विगतेषवः। ते तदापारयन्तश्च ह्रीमन्तश्च विशेषतः॥
en: Your troops as well as those of the enemy had their supply of weapons exhausted by that time. Passing the time thus the combatants, of both the armies, endued with modesty and energy.

sn: स्वधर्ममनुपश्यन्तो न जहुः स्वामनीकिनीम्। अस्राण्यन्ये समुत्सृज्य निद्रान्धाः शेरते जनाः॥
en: And observant of the duties of their order, did not desert their divisions. Others again, oppressed with sleep, left their weapons aside and laid themselves down on the field.

sn: रथेष्वन्ये गजेष्वन्ये हयेष्वन्ये च भारत। निद्रान्धा नो बुबुधिरे काञ्चिच्चेष्टां नराधिप॥
en: Oppressed with sleep, some again laid themselves down on the back of elephants or on that of horses or on their chariots, O Bharata and O foremost of men, they were deprived of all moving powers.

sn: तानन्ये समरे योधाः प्रेषयन्तो यमक्षयम्। स्वप्नायमानांस्त्वपरे परानतिविचेतसः॥ आत्मानं समरे जघ्नुः स्वानेव च परानपि। नानावाचो विमुञ्चन्तो निद्रान्धास्ते महारणे॥
en: Other warriors, that were awake in that battle, dispatched these to Yama's abode; others again, deprived of their senses in sleep and dreaming, slew their own comrades as also their opponents, regarding every one as their foes. Indeed they fought on in that fierce battle uttering dreadful exclamations.

sn: अस्माकं च महाराज परेभ्यो बहवो जनाः। योद्धव्यमिति तिष्ठन्तो निद्रासंरक्तलोचनाः॥
en: Many again of your army, thinking that they should continue to fight with the foe, stood, O king, on the field of battle although their eyes were heavy with sleep.

sn: संसर्पन्तो रणे केचिन्निद्रान्धास्ते तथा परान्। जनुः शूरा रणे शूरांस्तस्मिस्तमसि दारुणे॥
en: Some heroic warriors, during that hour of darkness, though blind with sleep, yet gliding along the field, slew one another in that battle.

sn: हन्यमानमथात्मानं परेभ्यो बहवो जनाः। नाभ्यजानन्त समरे निद्रया मोहिता भृशम्॥
en: Many of the enemy, entirely confounded in sleep, were slain without being conscious of the strokes that put an end to their existence.

sn: तेषामेतादृशी चेष्टां विज्ञाय पुरुषर्षभः। उवाच वाक्यं बीभत्सुरुच्चैः संनादयन् दिशः॥
en: Then, O foremost of men, beholding this plight of the soldiers, Vibhatsu exclaiming to the top of his voice, said these words.

sn: श्रान्ता भवन्तो निद्रान्धाः सर्व एव सवाहनाः। तमसा च वृते सैनये रजसा बहुलेन च॥
en: "You all are fatigued and oppressed with drowsiness; and your animals also are so. Both the armes are enveloped with darkness and clouds of dust.

sn: ते यूयं यदि मन्यध्वमुपारमत सैनिकाः। निमीलयत चात्रैव रणभूमौ मुहूर्तकम्॥
en: O soldiers, if you like you may desist from the fight. Close your eyes, here on the field, only for a moment.

sn: ततो विनिद्रा विश्रान्ताश्चन्द्रमस्युदिते पुनः। संसाधयिष्यथान्योन्यं संग्रामं कुरुपाण्डवाः॥
en: Then when the moon arises ye Kurus and the Pandavas, having taken rest and shaken off your fatigue, you may again meet one another in battle for securing paradise."

sn: तद् वचः सर्वधर्मज्ञा धार्मिकस्य विशाम्पते। अरोचयन्त सैन्यानि तथा चान्योन्यमब्रुवन्॥
en: Hearing these word of the virtuous Arjuna, the pious warriors of the Kuru army agreed to follow up the former's suggestion and addressing one another.

sn: चुक्रुशुः कर्ण कर्णेति तथा दुर्योधनेति च। उपारमत पाण्डूनां विरता हि वरुथिनी॥
en: Loudly said "O Karna, (king, Duryodhana, desist from fighting. The Pandava host has ceased to strike us."

sn: तथा विक्रोशमानस्य फाल्गुनस्य ततस्ततः। उपारमत पाण्डूनां सेना तव च भारत॥
en: Then, () Bharata, when Arjuna loudly uttered those words the Pandavas and your troop desisted from the fight.

sn: तामस्य वाचं देवाश्च ऋषयश्च महात्मनः। सर्वसैन्यानि चाक्षुद्रां प्रहृष्टाः प्रत्यपूजयन्॥
en: Those generous words of the illustrious Arjuna were highly applauded by the Rishis, the celestials and the highly delighted soldiers.

sn: तत् सम्पूज्य वचोऽक्रूरं सर्वसैन्यानि भारत। मुहूर्तमखपन् राजश्रान्तानि भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then applauding those noble words of Arjuna, O Bharata, O foremost of men, the fatigued troop laid themselves down only for a moment.

sn: सा तु सम्प्राप्य विश्रामं ध्वजिनी तव भारत। सुखमाप्तवती वीरमर्जुनं प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: Then that army of yours, O Bharata, joyful at the prespect of sleep and rest, sincerely blessed Arjuna sayingत्वयि वेदास्तथास्राणि त्वयि बुद्धिपराक्रमौ।

sn: धर्मस्त्वयि महाबाहो दया भूतेषु चानघ॥
en: "In you there are the knowledge of the Vedas and the weapons. In you there are intelligence and might. In you there are virtue, compassion for all creatures, O mighty-armed and sinless one.

sn: यचाश्वस्तास्तवेच्छामः शर्म पार्थ तदस्तु ते। मनसश्च प्रियानर्थान् वीर क्षिप्रमवाप्नुहि॥
en: As we have been comforted by you, we wish you well, O Partha. May you reap prosperity soon and may you get, O brave hero, those objects and that are dear to your heart."

sn: इति ते तं नरव्याघ्र प्रशंसन्तो महारथाः। निद्रया समवाक्षिप्तास्तूष्णीमासन् विशाम्पते॥
en: Thus, O foremost of men, those mighty carwarriors, while praising Partha, thus were stupefied by sleep and soon became silent, O ruler of men.

sn: अश्वपृष्ठेषु चाप्यन्ये रथनीडेषु चापरे। गजस्कन्धगताश्चान्ये शेरते चापरे क्षितौ॥
en: Some laid themselves down on the back of horses, some on the elephants, some on the carterraces and some on the bare earth only.

sn: सायुधाः सगदाश्चैव सखगाः सपरश्वधाः। सप्रासकवचाश्चान्ये नराः सुप्ताः पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: Others soldiers, well-armed and with maces, swords, axes and lances in grasp and covered with coats of mail, laid themselves down separately.

sn: गजास्ते पन्नगाभोगैर्हस्तै रेणुगुण्ठितः। निद्राधा वसुधां चक्रुना॑णनिःश्वासशीतलाम्॥
en: Elephants, having trunks resembling the tapering bodies of serpents and adorned with the dust of the field, oppressed with sleep, began to make the carth's surface cool with breaths.

sn: सुप्ताः शुशुभिरे तत्र निःश्वसन्तो महीतले। विकीर्णा गिरयो यद्वन्निःश्वसद्भिर्महोरगैः॥
en: The elephants, as they breathed on the ground, appeared beautiful like mountains (scattered over the field of battle) on which mighty serpents hissed.

sn: समां च विषमां चक्रुः खुरागैर्विकृतां महीम्। हयाः काञ्चनयोक्त्रास्ते केसरालम्बिभिर्युगैः॥
en: Steeds, in trappings of gold and with manes flowing down their yokes, began to paw and make the ground uneven with their hoops.

sn: सुषुपुस्तत्र राजेन्द्र युक्ता वाहेषु सर्वशः। एवं हयाश्च नागाश्च योधाश्च भरतर्षभ। युद्धाद् विरम्य सुषुपुः श्रमेण महतान्विता॥
en: Thus O foremost of kings, every body slept there with the animal he rode. Steeds and clephants and soldiers, ( foremost of the Bharatas.

sn: तत् तथा निद्रया भग्नमबोधं प्रास्वपद् भृशम्। कुशलैः शिल्पिभिय॑स्तं पटे चित्रमिवाद्भुतम्॥
en: Exhausted with exertion, slept on the field desisting from the battle. That sleeping host, deprived of senses and plunged in sleep, appeared beautiful like a charming picture painted on canvas by a skillful artist.

sn: ते क्षत्रियाः कुण्डलिनो युवानः परस्परं सायकविक्षताङ्गाः। कुम्भेषु लीना: सुषुपुर्गजानां कुचेषु लग्ना इव कामिनीनाम्॥
en: Then those Kshatriyas all youthful and graced with earnings, mangled with one another's shaft-wounds, lying down on the back of clephants slept as if lying on the breasts of beautiful ladies.

sn: ततः कुमुदनाथेन कामिनीगण्डपाण्डुना। नेत्रानन्देन चन्द्रेण माहेन्द्री दिगलङ्कता॥
en: Then the moon, that delighter of the eye and lord of the lilies of hue white as the cheeks of a youthful damsel, rose beautifying the quarter presided over by Indra himself.

sn: दशशताक्षककुब्दरिनिःसृतः किरणकेसरभासुरपिञ्जरः। तिमिरवारणयूथविदारण: समुदियादुदयाचलकेसरी॥
en: Indeed like a lion of the Udaya mountain with beams constituting his manes of glittering yellow, he issued out of his cave in the cast, dispelling the palpable darkness of night, resembling a large herd of elephants.

sn: हरवृषोत्तमगात्रसमद्युतिः स्मरशरासनपूर्णसमप्रभः। नववधूस्मितचारुमनोहरः प्रविसृतः कुमुदाकरबान्धवः॥
en: That lover of all lilies, bright as the body of Mahadeva's excellent bull, full-arched and radiant the bow of cupid and delightful and charming as the smile on the lips of bashful bride shone in the sky.

sn: ततो मुहूर्ताद् भगवान् पुरस्ताच्छशलक्षणः। अरुणं दर्शयामास ग्रसन् ज्योतिः प्रभाः प्रभुः॥
en: Soon that Divine Lord having the hare for the emblem showed himself reddish, shedding brighter beams around.

sn: अरुणस्य तु तस्यानु जातरूपसमप्रभम्। रश्मिजालं महचन्द्रो मन्दं मन्दमवासृजत्॥
en: After this, the moon seemed to spread gradually a bright halo of far-reaching light that resembled the glamour of gold.

sn: उत्सारयन्तः प्रभया तमस्ते चन्द्ररश्मयः। पर्यगच्छञ्छनैः सर्वा दिशः खंच क्षिति तथा॥
en: Then the rays of that lustrous orb, dispelling the gloom of night gradually spread themselves on the earth, the welkin and the directions of the compass.

sn: ततो मुहूर्ताद भुवनं ज्योतिर्भूतमिवाभवत्। अप्रख्यमप्रकाशं च जगामाशु तमस्तथा॥
en: Then within a moment the world was flooded with a stream of light and the palpable cnvelop of gloom soon fled away.

sn: प्रतिप्रकाशिते लोके दिवाभूते निशाकरे। विचेसन विचेस्श्च राजन् नक्तञ्चरास्ततः॥
en: When the world was illumined almost to the light of day. O king, some of the nightrangers began to rove about whils: hers desisted from doing so.

sn: बोध्यमानं तु तत् सैन्यं राजंश्चन्द्रस्य रश्मिभिः । बुबुधे शतपत्राणां वनं सूर्यांशुभिर्यथा॥
en: Then, O king, all the troops were awakened by the beams of the moon like louses blown by the rays of the sun.

sn: यथा चन्द्रोदयोद्भूतः क्षुभितः सागरोऽभवत्। तथा चन्द्रोदयोद्भूतः स बभूव बलार्णवः॥
en: Just as the ocean swells in consequence of the rising of the moon so that ocean of troops swelled at the rising of the moon.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं पुनरेव विशाम्पते। लोके लोकविनाशाय परं लोकमभीप्सताम्॥
en: Thereupon, O ruler of men, once more the battle between men desirous of getting heaven raged, a battle that was destructive of the world of creatures.

sn: यथा चन्द्रोदयोद्भूतः क्षुभितः सागरोऽभवत्। तथा चन्द्रोदयोद्भूतः स बभूव बलार्णवः॥
en: Just as the ocean swells in consequence of the rising of the moon so that ocean of troops swelled at the rising of the moon.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं पुनरेव विशाम्पते। लोके लोकविनाशाय परं लोकमभीप्सताम्॥
en: Thereupon, O ruler of men, once more the battle between men desirous of getting heaven raged, a battle that was destructive of the world of creatures.

sn: संजय उवाच ततो दुर्योधनो द्रोणमभिगम्याब्रवीदिदम्। अमर्षवशमापन्नो जनयन् हर्षतेजसी॥
en: Sanjaya said Then king Duryodhana, under the influence of anger, approached Drona and addressing him said these word for inspiring him with delight and wrath simultaneously.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच न मर्षणीयाः संग्रामे विश्रमन्तः श्रमान्विताः। सपत्ना ग्लानमनसो लब्धलक्ष्या विशेषतः॥ :॥
en: Duryodhana said No quarter should have been granted to our enemies when they were depressed at heart and exhausted with fatigue and taking rest, especially as they are ever of sure aim.

sn: यत् तु मर्षितमस्माभिर्भवतः प्रियकाम्यया। त एते परिविश्रान्ताः पाण्डवा बलवत्तराः॥
en: That we showed them mercy was only from a desire for pleasing you. The fatigued Pandavas, however, have now (after taking rest) become stronger.

sn: सर्वथा परिहीनाः स्म तेजसा च बलेन च। भवता पाल्यमानास्ते विवर्धन्ते पुनः पुनः॥
en: We, on the other hand, are becoming reduced in mighty and in energy, while the Pandavas, spared by you, are again and again gaining strength.

sn: दिव्यान्यस्राणि सर्वाणि ब्राह्मदीनि च यानि ह। तानि सर्वाणि तिष्ठन्ति भवत्येव विशेषतः॥
en: All weapons of celestial workmanship and all Brahma weapons are known perfectly to you.

sn: न पाण्डवेया न वयं नान्ये लोके धनुर्धराः। युध्यमानस्य ते तुल्याः सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Neither the Pandavas, nor ourselves nor any other bowman of the world are equal to you in battle. This I tell you truly.

sn: ससुरासुरगन्धर्वानिमाँल्लोकान् द्विजोत्तम। सर्वात्रविद् भवान् हन्याद् दिव्यैरस्त्रैर्न संशयः॥
en: Conversant with all kinds of weapons O foremost of regenerate ones, you are competent enough to slay with your celestial weapons, the gods, the Asureas, the Gandharvas and all this world.

sn: स भवान् मर्षयत्येतांस्त्वत्तो भीतान् विशेषतः। शिष्यत्वं वा पुरस्कृत्य मम वा मन्दभाग्यताम्॥
en: The Pandavas are all afraid of you. Yet you always forgive them remembering perhaps that they are your disciples or owing to my unfortunate luck."

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुद्धर्षितो द्रोण: कोपितश्च सुतेन ते। समन्युरब्रवीद् राजन् दुर्योधनमिदं वचः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus reprimanded and incited by your son, Drona, O monarch, wrathfully addressed

sn: घटे दुर्योधनाहवे। अतः परं मया कार्यं क्षुद्रं विजयगृद्धिना॥ अनस्रविदयं सर्वो हन्तव्योऽस्रविदा जनः। यद् भवान् मन्यते चापि शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्॥
en: Although I am advanced in years, yet. ) Duryodhana, I am fighting in battle to the best

sn: स्थविरः सन् परं शक्त्या
en: of my abilities. All these men are versed in the use of weapons; I am however well-versed in thein. If from desire of victory, I slay these men, there can be no more impious act for me to do. However, what is in your heart, be it good or bad.

sn: तद् वै कर्तास्मि कौरव्य वचनात् तव नान्यथा। निहत्य सर्वपञ्चालान् युद्धे कृत्वा पराक्रमम्॥ विमोक्ष्ये कवचं राजन् सत्येनायुधमालमे। मन्यसे यच्च कौन्तेयमर्जुनं श्रान्तमाहवे॥
en: I shall accomplish, foremost of the Kurus, at your behest. It will not be other.vise. Putting forth my prowess in battle and slaying all the Panchalas I will put off my coat of mail, O monarch. I swear this to you for sooth. You think that Kunti's son Arjuna was exhausted in battle.

sn: तस्य वीर्यं महाबाहो शृणु सत्येन कौरव। तं न देवा न गन्धर्वा न यक्षा न च राक्षसाः॥ उत्सहन्ते रणे जेतुं कुपितं सव्यसाचिनम्। खाण्डवे येन भगवान् प्रत्युद्यातः सुरश्वरः॥
en: O mighty-armed Kaurava, listen to what I say regarding his prowess. If Savyasachin's anger is excited, neither the Gandharvas nor the Yakshas, nor the Rakshasas can venture to oppose him. On the occasion of the burning of the Khandava forest, he fought with the chief of the gods himself.

sn: सायकैर्वारितश्चापि वर्षमाणो महात्मना। यक्षा नागास्तथा दैत्या ये चान्ये बलगर्विताः॥
en: With his arrows, the high-souled Arjuna then worsted the pouring Indra. Yakshas and the Nagas and the Daityas and other creatures.

sn: निहताः पुरुषेन्द्रेणर तचापि विदितं तव। गन्धर्वा घोषयात्रायां चित्रसेनादयो जिताः॥
en: Proud of their strength, were then slain by that foremost of men. This also you know. On the occasion of the numbering of cattle, the Gandharvas, headed by Chitrasena and others, were defeated by him.

sn: यूयं तैह्रियमाणाश्च मोक्षिता दृढधन्वना। निवातकवचाश्चापि देवानां शत्रवस्तथा॥
en: You also were set free from the bondage to the Gandharvas by that resolute bowman. The Nivtakavachas and other enemies of the gods.

sn: सुरैरवध्याः संग्रामे तेन वीरेण निर्जिताः। दानवानां सहस्राणि हिरण्यपुरवासिनाम्॥
en: Unslayable by the gods themselves in battle, were also vanquished by that hero. Thousands of Danavas dallying in the golden city.

sn: विजिग्ये पुरुषव्याघ्रः स शक्यो मानुषैः कथम्। प्रत्यक्षं चैव ते सर्वं यथाबलमिदं तव॥
en: Were defeated by that foremost of men. How it is possible for other men to resist him in battle? You have also seen with your own eyes, O king, how this host of yours, though striving hard, is destroyed by the son of Pandu, O ruler of men!

sn: संजय उवाच क्षपितं पाण्डुपुत्रेण चेष्टतां नो विशाम्पते। तं तदाभिप्रशंसन्तमर्जुनं कुपितस्तदा॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon, your son, 0 king highly enraged, once more thus addressed Drona who had been praising Arjuna then.

sn: द्रोणं तव सुतो राजन् पुनरेवेदमब्रवीत्। अहं दुःशासनः कर्णः शकुनिर्मातुलश्च मे॥
en: Dividing this Bharata army in two, today, myself, Dushasana, Karna and my uncle Sakuni will slay Arjuna in battle.

sn: हनिष्यामोऽर्जुनं संख्ये द्विधा कृत्वाद्य भारतीम्। तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा भारद्वाजो हसन्निव॥
en: Hearing those words of his, the son of Bharadvaja, as if smiling, quickly turned round and said, “Good befall you!"

sn: अन्ववर्तत राजानं स्वस्ति तेऽस्त्विति चाब्रवीत्। को हि गाण्डीवधन्वानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा।॥
