en: What presumptuous Kshatriya would venture to destroy that foremost of the Kshatriyas viz., the wielder of the Gandiva bow, who never suffers and reduction and who ever burns in his own effulgence?

sn: अक्षयं क्षपयेत् कश्चित् क्षत्रियः क्षत्रियर्षभम्। तं न वित्तपतिर्नेन्द्रो न यमो न जलेश्वरः॥
en: When furnished with weapons, neither the Lord of wealth, nor Indra nor Yama, nor Varuna, nor the Asuras nor the Rakshasas, will be able to defeat him?

sn: नासुरोगरक्षांसि क्षपयेयुः सहायुधम्। मूढास्त्वेतानि भाषन्ते यानीमान्यात्थ भारत॥
en: What you have spoken, 0 Bharata, is worthy of a fool only. Who ever returns safely to his own home, after having encountered Arjuna in battle?

sn: युद्धे ह्यर्जुनमासाद्य स्वस्तिमान् को व्रजेद् गृहान्। त्वं तु सर्वाभिशङ्कित्वान्निष्ठुरः पापनिश्चयः॥
en: Suspicious of everybody, you are cruel and of sinful purposes. You rebuke even those who are engaged in doing you good.

sn: श्रेयसस्त्वद्धिते युक्तांस्तत्तद् वक्तुमिहेच्छसि। गच्छ त्वमपि कौन्तेयमात्मार्थे जहि मा चिरम्॥
en: Go yourself to resist the son of Kunti, at your own risk. You are well-born and a Kshatriya too; you are again desirous of battle.

sn: त्वमप्याशंसये योद्धं कुलजः क्षत्रियो ह्यसि। इमान् किं क्षत्रियान् सर्वान् घातयिष्यस्यनागसः॥
en: Why then do you cause the ruin of all these other un-offending Kshatriyas? You are the root of this hostility, so, do you yourself encounter Arjuna.

sn: त्वमस्य मूलं वैरस्य तस्मादासादयार्जुनम्। दुर्दूतदेवी गान्धारे प्रयात्वर्जुनमाहवे।
en: Here indeed is your sagacious uncle, ever devoted to the performance of the Kshatriya duties. O son of Ghandhari, let this one, addicted to deceitful gambling at dice, meet Arjuna in battle.

sn: एषोऽक्षकुशलो जिह्मो द्यूतकृत् कितव: शठः॥ देविता निकृतिप्रज्ञो युधि जेष्यति पाण्डवान्।
en: Expert in the game of dice, crooked, fond of gambling and wily and deceitful-this gamester addicted to deception will surely vanquish the Pandavas in battle!

sn: त्वया कथितमत्यर्थं कर्णेन सह हृष्टवत्॥ असकृच्छून्यवन्मोहाद् धृतराष्ट्रस्य शृण्वतः।
en: Accompanied by Karna and delightful you used to brag always, out of your foolishness, within Dhritarashtra's hearing, with these

sn: अहं च तात कर्णश्च भ्राता दुःशासनश्च मे॥ पाण्डुपुत्रान् हनिष्यामः सहिताः समरे त्रयः।
en: O Sire, myself, Karna and my brother Dussasan, united in battle, shall slay the sons of Pandu!

sn: इति ते कत्थमानस्य श्रुतं संसदि संसदि॥ अनुतिष्ठ प्रतिज्ञा तां सत्यवाग् भव तैः सह।
en: This brag of yours was heard in every assemblage of the court. Now with their help fulfill your vow and be true to your words.

sn: एष ते पाण्डवः शत्रुरविशङ्कोऽग्रतः स्थितः॥ क्षत्रधर्ममवेक्षस्व श्लाघ्यस्तव वधो जयात्।
en: Yonder stand your fierce enemies, the sons of Pandu, prepared to fight to the last. Do now what should be done by a Kshatriya. It is batter that you did other than suffer defeat.

sn: दत्तं भुक्तमधीतं च प्राप्तमैश्चर्यमीप्सितम्॥ कृतकृत्योऽनृणश्चासि मा भैयुध्यस्व पाण्डवम्।
en: You have been charitable and enjoyed edibles to your heart's content. You have acquired wealth to your heart's content, you have accomplished all that one should do. You are debtless. Be not afraid. Encounter the son of Pandu battle.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा समरे द्रोणो न्यवर्तत यतः परे। द्वैधीकृत्य ततः सेनां युद्धं समभवत् तदा॥
en: Having thus spoken Drona desisted from fighting. Then the Bharata troops were divided in twain and the battle commenced.

sn: संजय उवाच त्रिभागमात्रशेषायां रात्र्यां युद्धमवर्तत। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च संहृष्टानां विशाम्पते॥
en: Sanjaya said When three fourths of the night had passed away, O ruler of men, once more the battle, between the delighted Kurus and Pandavas, commenced.

sn: अथ चन्द्रपभां मुष्णन्नादित्यस्य पुरःसरः। अरुणोऽभ्युदयांचक्रे ताम्रीकुर्वन्निवाम्बरम्॥
en: Soon after Arjuna (the sun's charioteer) robbing the effulgence of the moon, appeared on the sky, spreading a coppery hue over it.

sn: प्राच्यां दिशि सहस्रांशोररुणेनारुणीकृतम्। तपनीयं यथा चक्रं भ्राजते रविमण्डलम्॥
en: The eastern quarter was soon rendered crimson by the myriad rays of the sun and the solar disc looked like a circle of gold.

sn: न्युत्सृज्य सर्वे कुरुपाण्डुयोधाः। दिवाकरस्याभिमुखं जपन्तः संध्यागताः प्राञ्जलयो बभूवुः॥
en: Thereupon all the warriors of the Kuru and Pandava hosts, descending from their chariots, steeds, elephants and vehicles borne by men, turned their faces towards the sun and with folded palms uttered the Sandhya (prayers of the first twilight).

sn: ततो द्वैधीकृते सैन्ये द्रोणः सोमकपाण्डवान्। अभ्यद्रवत् सपाञ्चालान् दुर्योधनपुरोगमः॥
en: The host of the Kauravas having been divided into two parts, Diona, having Duryodhana in front of him, advanced (supported by one of this divisions) against the Somakas, the Panchalas and the Pandavas.

sn: द्वैधीकृतान् कुरून् दृष्ट्वा माधवोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत्। सपत्नान् सव्यतः कृत्वा अपसव्यमिमं कुरु॥
en: Then beholding the Kuru army divided in twain, the scion of Madhu's race, Krishna addressing Arjuna said-"Keeping the other division of the enemy to your left, place Drona's division to your right.”

sn: स माधवमनुज्ञाय कुरुष्वेति धनंजयः। द्रोणकर्णी महेष्वासौ सव्यतः पर्यवर्तत॥
en: Obedient to the counsel of Madhava, regarding everything about the Kurus. Dhananjaya wheeled round so as to keep Drona and Karna, those two might bowmen, to his right.

sn: अभिप्रायं तु कृष्णस्य ज्ञात्वा परपुरंजयः। आजिशीर्षगतं पार्थं भीमसेनोऽभ्युवाच ह॥
en: Then seeing through the purposes of Krishna, that subduer of hostile cities viz., Bhimasena, addressing Arjuna then stationed at the van of the troop, said these words.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच अर्जुनार्जुन बीभत्सो शृणुष्वैतद् वचो मम। यदर्थं क्षत्रिया सूते तस्य कालोऽयमागतः॥
en: Bhimasena said Ho, Arjuna, Arjuna, O Vibhatsu, hear these words of mine! The hour, for the realisation of that object for which Kshatriya ladies bring forth their sons, has now arrived.

sn: अस्मिश्चेदागते काले श्रेयो न प्रतिपत्स्यसे। असम्भावितरूपस्त्वं सुनृशंसं करिष्यसि।॥
en: If at this opportune season you do not exert yourself to attain good, then you shall act meanly like a perfect wreath.

sn: सत्यश्रीधर्मयशसां वीर्यणानृण्यमाप्नुहि। भिन्ध्यनीकं युधां श्रेष्ठ अपसव्यमिमान् कुरु॥
en: With the assistance of mighty do you, today, pay off your debt to Prosperity and Fame! ( foremost of warriors, penetrate into this army and keep this to your right.

sn: संजय उवाच स सव्यसाची भीमेन चोदितः केशवेन च। कर्णद्रोणावतिक्रम्य समन्तात् पर्यवारयत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus urged on by Bhima and Kesava, Savyasachin, disregarding Kama and Drona, began to resist the foe on all sides.

sn: तमाजिशीर्षपायान्तं दहन्तं क्षत्रियर्षभान्। पराक्रान्तं पराक्रम्य ततः क्षत्रियपुङ्गवः॥
en: Then as that puissant one advanced at the head of battle, leaving the foremost of Kshatriyas, these last, putting forth all their prowess.

sn: नाशक्नुवन् वारयितुं वर्धमानमिवानलम्। अथ दुर्योधनः कर्णः शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः॥
en: Could not check him even as men cannot check the raging conflagration. Thereupon Duryodhana, Karna and Subala's son Sakuni.

sn: अभ्यवर्षञ्छरव्रातैः कुन्तीपुत्रं धनंजयम्। तेषामस्राणि सर्वेषामुत्तमास्त्रविदां वरः॥ कदर्थीकृत्य राजेन्द्र शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्। अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य लघुहस्तो जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Began to shower thousands of arrows on Kunti's son Arjuna. That foremost of all, versed in excellent weapons, baffling all the weapons hurled by his opponents, poured on them, O foremost of king's a veritable shower of arrows. Of controlled senses and endued with great lightness of hand, he repulsed the weapons shot at him by those of his own.

sn: सर्वानविध्यन्निशितैर्दशभिर्दशभिः शरैः। उद्भूता रजसो वृष्टिः शरवृष्टिस्तथैव च॥
en: Then he pierced each of his foes with ten sharp shafts. The welkin was shrouded in a cloud of dust and showers of arrows fell thick.

sn: तमश्च घोरं शब्दश्च तदा समभवन्महान्। न द्यौर्न भूमिर्न दिशः प्राज्ञायन्त तथागते॥
en: Impenetrable darkness set in and dreadful tumult prevailed on the field of battle. When such was the condition of things, neither the sky nor the earth, nor the points of the compass, were recognised.

sn: सैन्येन रजसा मूढां सर्वमनधमिवाभवत्। नैव ते न वयं राजन् प्राज्ञासिष्म परस्परम्॥
en: one a Confounded with the dust thc troops became blind. Neither the foe, O monarch, nor we could distinguish one another.

sn: उद्देशेन हि तेन स्म समयुध्यन्त पार्थिवाः। विरथा रथिनो राजन् समासाद्य परस्परम्॥ केशेषु समसज्जन्त कवचेषु भुजेषु च। हताश्वा हतसूताश्च निश्चेष्टा रथिनो हताः॥ जीवन्त इव तत्र स्म व्यदृश्यन्त भयार्दिताः। हतान् गजान् समाश्लिष्य पर्वतानिव वाजिनः॥ गतसत्त्वा व्यदृश्यन्त तथैव सह सादिभिः। ततस्त्वभ्यवसृत्यैव संग्रामादुत्तरां दिशम्॥
en: For this reason, the royal combatants fought on guided by conjecture and the challenges they uttered. Destitute of chariots, the carwarriors, O monarch, encountering another, lost all order and became confounded mass. Their horses slain the charioteer killed, many, becoming incapacitated, saved their lives and looked highly frightened. Staughtered steeds, with their riders slain, were seen to lie over elephants as if prostrate on mountain tops. Then Drona, inoving towards the northern quarter of the field.

sn: अतिष्ठदाहवे द्रोणो विधूमोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन्। तमाजिशीर्षादेकान्तमपक्रान्तं निशम्य तु॥
en: Stood like fire free from smoke. Then beholding him move away from the field (towards the North).

sn: समकम्पन्त सैन्यानि पाण्डवानां विशाम्पते। भ्राजमानं श्रिया युक्तं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा॥ द्रोणं दृष्ट्वा परे त्रेसुश्चेरुर्मम्लुश्च भारत। आह्वयन्तं परानीकं प्रभिन्नमिव वारणम्॥
en: O ruler of men, the Pandava troops began to tremble. Beholding Drona exceedingly handsome and attended with prosperity and burning in his own effulgence, the soldiers of the enemy were affrighted, depressed and routed, O Bharata.-Challenging the hostile host as he stood, like an infuriate elephant in rut.

sn: नैनमाशंसिरे जेतुं दानवा वासवं यथा। केचिदासन् निरुत्साहाः केचित् क्रुद्धा मनस्विनः॥
en: None ventured to conquer him even as the Danavas could not conquer Vasava. Some were depressed at heart and some intelligent warriors became inspired with rage.

sn: विस्मिताश्चाभवन् केचित् केचिदासन्नमर्षिताः। हस्तैर्हस्ताग्रमपरे प्रत्यपिंषन् नराधिपाः॥
en: Some were filled with wonder and some could not beer him. Some rubbed their hands.

sn: अपरे दशनैरोष्ठानदशन् क्रोधमूर्छिताः। व्याक्षिपन्नायुधान्यन्ये ममृदुश्चापरे भुजान्॥
en: Others, overwhelmed with rage, began to bite their lips, with their teeth. Others began to hurl missiles at him and others to rule their arins.

sn: अन्ये चान्वपतन् द्रोणं त्यक्तात्मानो महौजसः। पञ्चालास्तु विशेषेण द्रोणसायकपीडिताः॥
en: Other warriors, of controlled passions and great might, fell upon Drona. Specially the Panchalas, though afflicted with the shafts of Drona.

sn: समसज्जन्त राजेन्द्र समरे भृशवेदनाः। ततो विराटद्रुपदौ द्रोणं प्रययतू रणे॥
en: And suffering extreme pain, O king, fought on with Drona. Thereafter Virata and Drupada, both rushed against Drona in battle.

sn: तथा चरन्तं संग्रामे भृशं समरदुर्जयम्। द्रुपदस्य ततः पौत्रास्त्रय एव विशाम्पते॥
en: Who, invincible as he was in battle, was roving freely on the field. Then O ruler of men, the grandsons of Drupada, in three number.

sn: चेदयश्च महेष्वासा द्रोणमेवाभ्ययुर्युधि। तेषां दुपदपौत्राणां त्रयाणां निशितैः शरैः॥
en: And the Chedis, all fierce bowmen, assailed Drona in battle. Of those three grandsons of Drupada, with sharp arrows.

sn: त्रिभिट्टैणोऽहरत् प्राणांस्ते हता न्यपतन् भुवि। ततो द्रोणोऽजयद् युद्धे चेदिकैकेयसंजयान्॥
en: Three in number Drona robbed the vital breaths, whereupon they fell down dead on the ground. Thereafter Drona vanquished in battle, the Chedis the Kaikayas and the Srinjayas.

sn: मत्स्यांश्चैवाजयत् कृत्स्नान् भारद्वाजो महारथान्। ततस्तु दुपदः क्रोधाच्छरवर्षमवासृजत्॥
en: That mighty car-warrior the son of Bharadvaja then also conquered the Matsyas. Thereafter Drupada, worked up with rage, poured a shower of arrows.

sn: द्रोणं प्रति महाराज विराटश्चैव संयुगे। तं निहत्येषुवर्षं तु द्रोणः क्षत्रियमर्दनः॥
en: On Drona, O mighty monarch. Virata also did so in that battle. Then that crusher of foes, viz., Drona, destroying that shower of arrows.

sn: तौ शरैश्छादयामास विराटदुपदावुभौ। द्रोणेन च्छाद्यमानौ तु क्रुद्धौ संग्राममूर्धनि॥
en: Covered the two, Drupada and Virata with his own arrows. Thus covered by Drona and inflamed with wrath at the head of battle.

sn: द्रोणं शरैर्विव्यधतुः परमं क्रोधमास्थितौ। ततो द्रोणो महाराज क्रोधामर्षसमन्वितः॥
en: Those two heroes began to afflict Drona wrathfully in that battle. O mighty monarch, therefore, Drona filled with rage and fury.

sn: भल्लाभ्यां भृशतीक्ष्णाभ्यां चिच्छेद धनुषी तयोः। ततो विराटः कुपितः समरे तोमरान् दश॥
en: Cut off the bows cf them both with a couple of broad headed shafts of great sharpness. Thereupon, filled with rage, Virata hurled ten tomaras.

sn: दश चिक्षेप च शरान् द्रोणस्य वधकाङ्क्षया। शक्तिं च दुपदो घोरामायसी स्वर्णभूषिताम्॥ चिक्षेप भुजगेन्द्राभां क्रुद्धो द्रोणरथं प्रति। ततो भल्लैः सुनिशितैश्छित्त्वा तांस्तोमरान् दश॥
en: As also ten shafts at Drona, with a view to encompass his slaughter. Drupada also, equally enraged, hurled at the car of Drona, a dreadful dart made wholly of iron and decked with gold and effulgent like the body of a excellent snake. Then cutting off with a well-sharpened bhalla those tomaras.

sn: शक्तिं कनकवैदूर्यां द्रोणश्चिच्छेद सायकैः। ततो द्रोणः सुपीताभ्यां भल्लाभ्यामरिमर्दनः॥
en: Drona cut-off the dart adorned with gold and lapises shot at him with his own arrows. Then that crusher of foes., viz., Drona with a couple of well-tempered bhalla.

sn: दुपदं च विराटं च प्रेषयामास मृत्यवे। हते विराटे दुपदे केकयेषु तथैव च॥
en: Dispatched both Drupada and Virata to the region of Death. Upon the slaughter of Virata and Drupada and the Kaikayas also.

sn: तथैव चेदिमत्स्येषु पञ्चालेषु तथैव च। हतेषु त्रिषु वीरेषु दुपदस्य च नृप्पृषु॥
en: As also the Chedis and the Panchalas and the Matsyas and upon the slaughter of the three heroic grandsons of Drupada.

sn: द्रोणस्य कर्म तद् दृष्ट्वा कोपदुःखसमन्वितः। शशाप रथिनां मध्ये धृष्टद्युम्नो महामनाः॥
en: And beholding these cruel deeds accomplished by Drona, the high-souled Dhristadyumna, filled with rage and grief,

sn: इष्टापूर्तात् तथा क्षात्राद् ब्राह्मण्याच स नश्यतु। द्रोणो यस्याद्य मुच्येत यं वा द्रोणः पराभवेत्॥
en: "Let that man lose the merits of his Istha, Purth, Kshatra and Brahmanya, whom Drona shall escape or shall defeat in battle."

sn: इति तेषां प्रतिश्रुत्य मध्ये सर्वधनुष्मताम्। आयाद द्रोणं सहानीकः पाञ्चाल्यः परवीरहा॥
en: Thus having sworn in the midst of all bowmen, that slayer of foes, viz., the Panchala prince rushed upon Drona, supported by his own division.

sn: पञ्चालास्त्वेकतो द्रोणमभ्यघ्नन् पाण्डवैः सह। दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः॥
en: The Panchalas attacked Drona from one side whilst the Pandavas attacked him from the other. Then Duryodhana, Karna, Subala's son Sakuni.

sn: सोदर्याश्च यथामुख्यास्तेऽरक्षन् द्रोणमाहवे। रक्ष्यमाणं तथा द्रोणं सर्वैस्तैस्तु महारथैः॥ यतमानास्तु पञ्चाला न शेकुः प्रतिवीक्षितुम्। तत्राक्रुध्यद् भीमसेनो धृष्टद्युम्नस्य मारिष॥ स एनं वाग्भिरुग्राभिस्ततक्ष पुरुषर्षभः।
en: And his other principal uterine brothers began to protect Drona in battle. Then the Panchalas, though striving hard, could not even look at Drona who was then being thus protected in battle by those high-souled warriors. Thereupon, O sire, Bhimasena became enraged with Dhistadyumna and then addressed that foremost of men in these harsh words.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच दुपदस्य कुले जातः सर्वानेष्वस्रवित्तमः॥ कः क्षत्रियो मन्यमानः प्रेक्षतारिमवस्थितम्।
en: Bhimasena said What man is there who, being regarded as a Kshatriya and who being born in the Dynasty of Drupada and who being foremost of all men possessing knowledge of weapons, would only thus passively look at his foe, stationed before him?

sn: पितृपुत्रवधं प्राप्य पुमान् कः परिपालयेत्॥ विशेषतस्तु शपथं शपित्वा राजसंसदि।
en: What person, having seen his father and son slain by his foes and having also sworn such a terrible oath in the assemblage of kings, would thus suffer his foe to stand before him?

sn: एष वैश्वानर इव समिद्धः स्वेन तेजसा॥ शरचापेन्धनो द्रोणः क्षत्रं दहति तेजसा।
en: Yonder stands Drona like a fire swelling with its own energy; indeed with bow and arrows constituting fuel he is consuming all the Kshatriyas with his energy.

sn: शरचापेन्धनो द्रोणः क्षत्रं दहति तेजसा। पुरा करोति निःशेषां पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्॥ स्थिताः पश्यत मे कर्म द्रोणमेव व्रजाम्यहम्।
en: Soon will he completely destroy the Pandava army; stand here passively as spectators of the feat I am going to perform; I myself assail Drona.

sn: संजय उवाच इत्युक्त्वा प्राविशत् क्रुद्धो द्रोणानीकं वृकोदरः॥ शरैः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टै वयंस्तव वाहिनीम्।
en: Sanjaya said Having thus spoken, Vrikodara, worked up with rage, penetrated into Drona's division; and he then routed your troops with arrows shot from his bow drawn to the fullest stretch.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नोऽपि पाञ्चाल्यः प्रविश्य महतीं चमूम्॥ आससादरणे द्रोणं तदाऽऽसीत् तुमुलं महत्।
en: The Panchala price Dhristadyumna also, pushing into the heart your mighty troops, approached Drona; whereupon a confused and terrible encounter commenced.

sn: नैव नस्तादृशं युद्धं दृष्टपूर्वं न च श्रुतम्॥ यथा सूर्योदये राजन् समुत्पिञ्जोऽभवन्महान्।
en: We never saw nor heard of such a battle before as, O king, was fought during that hour of sun-rise.

sn: संसक्तान्येव चादृश्यन् रथवृन्दानि मारिष॥ हतानि च विकीर्णानि शरीराणि शरीरिणाम्।
en: () sire, the chariots were then entangled with one another; thousands of corpses of slain creatures were also seen lying on the field of battle.

sn: केचिदन्यत्र गच्छन्तः पथि चान्यैरुपद्रुताः॥ विमुखाः पृष्ठतश्चान्ये ताड्यन्ते पार्श्वतः परे।
en: Some, when going to other parts of the field, were assailed by their foe on the way. Some, in flying away, were wounded on their backs and others on their sides.

sn: तथा संसक्तयुद्धं तदभवद् भृशदारुणम्। अथ संध्यागतः सूर्यः क्षणेन समपद्यत॥
en: Thus then that general engagement raged furiously. Soon however the morning sun made its appearance of the sky,

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच ते तथैव महाराज दंशिता रणमूर्धनि। संध्यागतं सहस्रांशुमादित्यमुपतस्थिरे॥
en: Sanjaya said The warriors then, O monarch, clad as they were in coats of mail, worshipped the sun of thousand rays as he made its appearance on the morning sky.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: उदिते तु सहस्रांशौ तप्तकाञ्चनसप्रभे। प्रकाशितेषु लोकेषु पुनयुद्धमवर्तत॥
en: Upon the rise of the thousand-rayed sun of the effulgence of heated gold and upon the illumination of the world, battle raged anew.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: द्वन्द्वानि तत्र यान्यासन् संसक्तानि पुरोदयात्। तान्येवाभ्युदिते सूर्ये समसज्जन्त भारत॥
en: The same soldiers, that were engaged with one another before sun rise, once more fought with each other, OBharata, after the sun rise.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: स्थैर्हया हयैर्नागाः पादातैश्चापि कुञ्जराः। हयैर्हयाः समाजग्मुः पादाताश्च पदातिभिः॥
en: Horsemen fought with car-warriors and elephants with horsemen and foot-soldier with elephants and horsemen with horsemen and infantry with infantry.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: रथा रथैरिभैर्नागास्तथैव भरतर्षभ। संसक्ताश्च वियुक्ताक्ष योधाः संन्यपतन् रणे॥
en: Car-warriors with car-warriors elephants with elephants, horsemen with horse men O foremost of the Bharatas, Sometimes, in a body and sometimes individually, the warriors assailed one another in battle.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: ते रात्रौ कृतकर्माणः श्रान्ताः सूर्यस्य तेजसा। क्षत्पिपासापरीताङ्गा विसंज्ञा बहवोऽभवन्॥
en: Having fought hard during the previous night many combatants, worn out with toil and weak with hunger and thirst, lost their senses in a swoon.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: शङ्खभेरीमृदङ्गानां कुञ्जराणां च गर्जताम्। विस्फारितविकृष्टानां कार्मुकाणां च कूजताम्॥ शब्दः समभवद् राजन् दिविस्पृग् भरतर्षभ। द्रवतां च पदातीनां शस्त्राणां पततामपि॥
en: The noise, O foremost of the Bharata race, created by the blowing of conchs, the bear of drums, the roar of elephants and the twang of bows stretched with force, reached the very heavens, O monarch. The tumult, made also by running foot-soldiers and falling weapons.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: हयानां द्वेषतां चापि रथानां च निवर्तताम्। क्रोशतां गर्जतां चैव तदाऽऽसीत् तुमुलं महत्॥
en: And neighing steeds and rattling chariots and shouting and challenging warriors, became tremendous.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: विवृद्धस्तुमुलः शब्दो द्यामगच्छन्महांस्तदा। नानायुधनिकृत्तानां चेष्टतामातुरः स्वनः॥ भूमावश्रूयत महांस्तदाऽऽसीत् कृपणं महत्। पततां पात्यमानानां पत्त्यश्वरथदन्तिनाम्॥
en: That tremendous din, momentarily increasing, touched the very heavens. The moans and groans of pain, uttered by falling and fallen foot-soldiers and car-warriors and elephants, became exceedingly loud and pitiable as they were heard on the field.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: तेषु सर्वेष्वनीकेषु व्यतिषक्तेष्वनेकशः। स्वे परे स्वांश्च स्वान् परेषां परे परान्॥
en: When the divisions were inter-mingled and confused, both sides slew each other and also their own men.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: वीरबाहुविमृष्टाश्च योधेषु च गजेषु च। राशयः प्रत्यदृश्यन्त वाससां नेजनेष्विव॥
en: Swords, hurled by the hands of heroic warriors upon combatants and elephants, in large heaps, were seen on the field, like cloths on the washing ground.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: उद्यतप्रतिपिष्टानां खङ्गानां वीरबाहुभिः। स एव शब्दस्तद्रूपो वाससां निज्यतामिव॥
en: The whizz, of lifted and descending swords, wielded by the arms of heroes, resembled that of clothes thrashed for wash.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: अर्धासिभिस्तथा खड्नेस्तोमरैः सपरश्वधैः। निकृष्टयुद्धं संसक्तं महदासीत् सुदारुणम्॥
en: Then that general engagement, in which the warriors encountered one another with swords and scimitars and lances and battle, axes, became extremely terrible.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: गजाश्वकायप्रभवां नरदेहप्रवाहिनीम्। शस्रमत्स्यसुसम्पूर्णां मांसशोणितकर्दमाम्॥ आर्तनादस्वनवतीं पताकाशस्रफेनिलाम्। नदीं प्रावर्तयन् वीराः परलोकौघगामिनीम्॥
en: The brave warriors then caused a river to flow there towards the region of the departed; the blood of elephants and steeds and human beings constituted its currents. Weapons constituted the large number of blood and flesh. Wails of grief and pain constituted its murmuring sound. Banners and cloths constituted its foam.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: शरशक्त्यर्दिताः कान्ता रात्रिमूढाल्पचेतसः। विष्टभ्य सर्वगात्राणि व्यतिष्ठन् गजवाजिनः॥
en: Afflicted with shafts and arrows, tired with fatigue, worn out with exertion of the previous night and robbed of their strength, elephants and horses, stood on the field utterly incapable of moving their limbs.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: बाहुभिः कवचैश्चिवैः शिरोभिश्चारुकुण्डलैः। युद्धोपकरणैश्चान्यैस्तत्र तत्र चकाशिरे॥
en: Heroes, with pale countenances and with head graced with charming ear-rings and armed with the implements of war, appeared extremely resplendent.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: क्रव्यादसङ्घराकीर्णं मृतैरर्धमृतैरपि। नासीद् रथपथस्तत्र सर्वमायोधनं प्रति॥
en: On the field infested with carnivorous animals and obstructed with the dead and the dying there was no space for the cars to move.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: मज्जत्सु चक्रेषु रथान् सत्त्वमास्थाय वाजिनः। कथंचिदवहश्रान्ता वेपमानाः शरार्दिताः॥
en: The wheels of cars being thus entangled, the steeds, yoked thereto, with great effort dragged them although they were tired and trembling and afflicted with arrows.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: कुलसत्त्वबलोपेता वाजिनो वारणोपमाः। विह्वलं तूर्णमुद्भरान्तं सभयं भारतातुरम्॥ बलमासीत् तदा सर्वमृते द्रोणार्जुनावुभौ। तावेवास्तां निलयनं तावार्तायनमेव च॥
en: Those steeds moreover were of good breed and were endued with mettle and strength and resembled elephants in seize. Then the Bharata troops, resembling the ocean for its vastness, became affrighted and terrible agitated, save and exert Drona and Arjuna. They both then became the refuge and the protectors of the warriors of their respective sides.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: तावेवान्ये समासाद्य जग्मुर्वैवस्वतक्षयम्। आविग्नमभवत् सर्वं कौरवाणां महद् बलम्॥
en: Meeting them both their opponents went to regions of Death. Then the mighty host of the Kurus became greatly agitated.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: पञ्चालानां च संसक्तं न प्राज्ञायत किंचन। अन्तकाक्रीडसदृशं भीरूणां भयवर्धनम्॥ पृथिव्यां राजवंश्यानामुत्थिते महति क्षये। न तत्र कर्णं द्रोणं वा नार्जुनं न युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: And the Panchalas being intermingled with them, none could be distinguished. During the progress of that terrible carnage of the Kshatriyas on that field of battle, enhancing the fear of the cowards and resembling a crematorium, neither Karna, nor Drona, nor Arjuna, nor Yudhishthira.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: न भीमसेनं न यमौ न पाञ्चाल्यं न सात्यकिम्। न च दुःशासनं द्रौणिं न दुर्योधनसौबलो॥
en: Nor Bhimasena, nor the twins Nakula and Sahadeva, nor the Panchala prince, nor Satyaki nor Dushasana, Drona's son, Duryodhana, nor Subala's son.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: न कृपं मद्रराजं च कृतवर्माणमेव च। न चान्यान् नैव चात्मानं च क्षितिं न दिशस्तथा॥
en: Nor Kripa nor the ruler of the Madra, nor Kritavarman, nor others, nor my own self, nor the earth, nor the different quarters of heaven. nor nor nor

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: पश्याम राजन् संसक्तान् सैन्येन रजसाऽऽवृतान्। सम्भ्रान्ते तुमुले घोरे रजोमेघ समुत्थिते॥
en: Could be discerned, O king, in consequence of all of them being mingled with troops and covered by ciouds of dust. During the progress of that dreadful and fierce battle, when that dust-cloud arose.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: द्वितीयामिव सम्प्राप्ताममन्यन्त निशां तदा। न ज्ञायन्ते कौरवेया न पञ्चाला न पाण्डवाः॥
en: Every body thought that night had once more set in. Neither the Kouravas, nor the Panchalas, the Pandavas could be distinguished.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: न दिशो द्यौर्न चोर्वी च न समं विषमं तथा। हस्तसंस्पर्शमापन्नान् परानप्यथवा स्वकान्॥ न्यपातयंस्तदा युद्धे नराः स्म विजयैषिणः। उद्भूतत्वात् तु रजसः प्रसेकाच्छोणितस्य च॥ प्राशाम्यत रजो भौमं शीघ्रत्वादनिलस्य च। तत्र नागा हया योधा रथिनोऽथ पदातयः॥
en: Nor the quarters of heaven, nor the welkin, nor the earth, nor the undulations of land. The warriors, impelled by the thought of victory, slew friends and foes indiscriminately, in fact all whom they perceived by their touch. The dust that had arisen was very soon driven away by the winds that began to blow then and it wad quenched by the blood that shed profusely. Elephants, steeds, car-warriors and foot-soldiers.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: पारिजातवनानीव व्यरोचन् रुधिरोक्षिताः। ततो दुर्योधनः कर्णो द्रोणो दुःशासनस्तथा॥ पाण्डवैः समसज्जन्त चतुर्भिश्चतुरो रथाः। दुर्योधनः सह भ्रात्रा यमाभ्यां समसज्जत॥
en: Steeped in blood, appeared beautiful like the celestial forest of the Parijata flowers. Thereafter Duryodhana, Karna, Drona and Dushasana engaged in battle with four Pandava warriors. Duryodhana and his brothers encountered twins (Nakula and Sahadeva).

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: वृकोदरेण राधेयो भारद्वाजेन चार्जुनः। तद् घोरं महदाश्चर्यं सर्वे प्रेक्षन्त सर्वतः॥
en: Radha's son encountered Vrikodara and Arjuna engaged with the son of Bharadvaja. All the soldiers then began to look on those marvelous and terrible encountered from all sides.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: रथर्षभाणामुग्राणां संनिपातममानुषम्। रथमागैर्विचित्रैस्तैर्विचित्ररथसंकुलम्॥ अपश्यन् रथिनो युद्धं विचित्रं चित्रयोधिनाम्। यतमानाः पराक्रान्ताः परस्परजिगीषवः॥
en: The car-warriors of both sides, beheld that wonderful battle, that super-human engagement between those furious and excellent car-warriors all versed in the different modes of war, mounted on their respective chariots, that moved in various charming motions. Possessed of great prowess, exerting their best and each anxious to defeat the other.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: जीमूता इव धर्मान्ते शरव(रवाकिरन्। ते रथान् सूर्यसंकाशानास्थिताः पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: They then poured on each other showers of shafts, like clouds pouring rain at the end of summer. Those foremost of men, mounted on their cars of solar effulgence.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: अशोभन्त यथा मेघाः शारदाश्चलविद्युतः। योधास्ते तु महाराज क्रोधामर्षसमन्विताः॥
en: Appeared beautiful like vast masses of clouds in the autumnal sky. Then those warriors, O mighty-monarch, inspired with rage and thought of rivenge.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: स्पर्धिनश्च महेष्वासाः कृतयला धनुर्धराः। अभ्यगच्छंस्तथान्योन्यं मत्ता गजवृषा इव॥
en: All proud and mighty bowmen, putting forth their greatest effort, rushed upon one another, like infuriate leaders of the herds of elephants.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: न नूनं देहभेदोऽस्ति काले राजन्ननागते। यत्र सर्वे न युगपद् व्यशीर्यन्त महारथाः॥
en: Indeed, O king, corporeal creatures do not forsake their corpus, until the proper hour comes, inasmuch as, O monarch, all those mighty car-warriors, though fighting hard, were not slain all together.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: बाहुभिश्चरणैच्छिन्नै: शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः। कार्मुकैर्विशिखैः प्रासैः खङ्गैः परशुपट्टिशैः॥
en: With lopped-off arms and legs with heads graced with charming ear-rings, with bows and arrows and lances and swords and axes and Pattiscs.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: नालीकैः क्षुद्रनाराचैर्नखरैः शक्तितोमरैः। अन्यैश्च विविधाकारैधौतैः प्रहरणोत्तमैः॥
en: With Nalikas, Ksharvas, Narachas, nails, darts and Tomaras, with diverse other kinds of excellent weapons, of various shapes and well cleansed.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: विचित्रविविधकारैः शरीरावरणैरपि। विचित्रैश्च रथैर्भग्नैर्हतैश्च गजवाजिभिः॥
en: With wonderful cuirasses of different shapes, with charming chariots shattered, with slain horses and elephants.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: विचित्रैश्च नगराकारैर्हतयोधध्वजै रथैः। अमनुष्यैर्हयैस्रस्तैः कृष्यमाणैस्ततस्ततः॥
en: With brave combatants slain, with standless and warriorless chariots looking like large cities, with vehicles dragged hither and thither by affrighted steeds having none to restrain them.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: वातायमानैरसकृद्धतवीरैरलङ्कतैः। व्यजनैः कङ्कटैश्चैव ध्वजैश्च विनिपातितैः॥
en: In speed more then that of the wind, with countless warriors adorned with ornaments, with fans, with coats of mail, with overthrown standards.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: छत्रैराभरणैर्वस्त्रैर्माल्यैश्च ससुगन्धिभिः। हारैः किरीटैर्मुकुटैरुष्णीषैः किङ्किणीगणैः॥
en: With umbrellas, with ornaments, garments and perfumeries with chains and diadems and crowns and headgears and with tinkling bells.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: उरस्थैर्मणिभिनिष्कैश्चूडामणिभिरेव च। आसीदायोधनं तत्र नभस्तारागणैरिव॥
en: With jewels that had adorned the breast of heroes with Niskhas and with jewels that had decorated the crowns of combatants, the field of battle, strewn over, looked resplendent like the star-bespangled firmament.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: ततो दुर्योधनस्यासीन्नकुलेन समागमः। अमर्षितेन क्रुद्धस्य क्रुद्धेनामर्षितस्य च॥
en: Thereafter an encounter took place between Duryodhana and Nakula when both were filled with feelings of wrath and revenge.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: अपसव्यं चकाराथ माद्रीपुत्रस्तवात्मजम्। किरज्छरशतैर्हष्टस्तत्र नादो महानभूत्॥
en: Then the son of Madri, delightful shooting hundreds of shafts, kept your son on his right side. At this, loud sounds and applause arose there.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: अपसव्यं कृतं संख्ये भ्रातृव्येनात्यमर्षिणा। नामृष्यत तमप्याजौ प्रतिचक्रेऽपसव्यतः॥
en: Though placed on the right by his enraged cousin, your son, inflamed with rage, began to resist him from even from that disadvantageous position of his.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: पुत्रस्तव महाराज राजा दुर्योधनो द्रुतम्। ततः प्रतिचिकीर्षन्तमपसव्यं तु ते सुतम्॥
en: Your son the king Duryodhana then began to fight wonderfully. O mighty monarch. Then as your son endeavoured to counteract Nakula even from his sight.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: न्यवारयत तेजस्वी नकुलचित्रमार्गवित्। स सर्वतो निवार्यैनं शरजालेन पीडयन्॥
en: The latter (Nakula) endued with energy and versed in the diverse ccurses of a chariot, restrained your son. But your son again, resisting Nakula on all sides and afflicting him, with his arrowy showers.

description: The battle between Nakula and Duryodhana
sn: तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति नकुलो बभाषे तनयं तव। संस्मृत्य सर्वदुःखानि तव दुर्मन्त्रितं च तत्॥
en: Compelled Nakula to turn back. Your troops then applauded that feat of your son. Then Nakula, keeping alive the memory of the wrongs inflicted on them by your wicked counsel, addressed your son saying-Wait, wait.'

sn: संजय उवाच ततो दुःशासनः क्रुद्धः सहदेवमुपाद्रवत्। रथवेगेन तीव्रण कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Filled with rage, Dushasana then assailed Sahadeva causing the earth to quake with the fierce clash of his chariot.

sn: तस्यापतत एवाशु भल्लेनामित्रकर्शनः। माद्रीपुत्रः शिरो यन्तुः सशिरस्त्राणमच्छिनत्॥
en: While Dushasana was thus rushing at the son of Madri, that subduer of foes, quickly cutoff with a broad-headed shafts, the head, protected with helmet helmet of of the former's charioteer.

sn: नैनं दुःशासनः सूतं नापि कश्चन सैनिकः। कृत्तोत्तमाङ्गमाशुत्वात् सहदेवेन बुद्धवान्॥
en: Owing to the quickness with which the charioteer's head was cut-off, neither any one among the troops nor Dushasana himself perceived him to have been decapitated by Sahadeva.

sn: यदा त्वसंगृहीतत्वात् प्रयान्त्यश्वा यथासुखम्। ततो दुःशासनः सूतं बुबुधे गतचेतसम्॥
en: The reins being no longer held by any body, the horses ran at their free will. It was only then that Dushasana came to know that his driver had been slain.

sn: स हयान् संनिगृह्याजौ स्वयं हयविशारदः। युयुधे रथिनां श्रेष्ठो लघु चित्रं च सुष्ठु च॥
en: Himself an expert in managing steeds he restrained his horses; and that foremost of carwarriors then fought on lightly, beautifully and skillfully.

sn: तदस्यापूजयन् कर्म स्वे परे चापि संयुगे। हतसूतरथेनाजौ व्यचरद् यदभीतवत्॥
en: Then as he covered dauntlessly on the field that driverless car of his, his friends and foes alike applauded his feat. soon

sn: सहदेवस्तु तानश्वांस्तीक्ष्णैर्बाणैरवाकिरत्। पीड्यमानाः शरैश्चाशु प्रादूर्वन्ते ततस्ततः॥
en: Sahadeva, however, covered Dushasana steeds with sharp arrows and these, afflicted with those arrows, began to run away wildly.

sn: स रश्मिषु विषक्तत्वादुत्ससर्ज शरासनम्। धनुषा कर्म कुर्वस्तु रश्मींश्च पुनरुत्सृजत्॥
en: For holding the reins Dushasana once laid his bow aside, again, for using the bow the took up the reins. (Thus did he then fight).

sn: छिद्रेष्वेतेषु तं बाणैर्माद्रीपुत्रोऽभ्यवाकिरत्। परीप्यंस्त्वत्सुतं कर्णस्तदन्तरमवाप तत्॥
en: During these opportunities, the son of Madri pierced him with numerous arrows. Then desirous of rescuing your son Karna rushed between those two combatants.

sn: वृकोदरस्ततः कर्णं त्रिभिर्भल्लैः समाहितः। आकर्णपूर्णैरभ्यघ्नद् बाह्वोरुरसि चानदत्॥
en: Thereupon Vrikodara, with due caution, pierced Kara on the breast and the arms, with three broad-headed shafts shot from a fulldawn bow.

sn: स निवृत्तस्ततः कर्णः संघट्टित इवोरगः। भीममावारयामास विकिरन् निशिताञ्छरान्॥
en: Thereupon like a snake struck with a stick Karna wheeled back and covered Bhima by scattering sharp arrows by thousands.

sn: ततोऽभूत् तुमुलं युद्धे भीमराधेययोस्तदा। तौ वृषाविव नर्दन्तौ विवृत्तनयनावुभौ॥
en: Thereupon tremendous combat commenced between Bhima and the son of Radha. Both the combatants then roared like two bulls and their eyes rolled in fury.

sn: वेगेन महतान्योन्यं संरब्धावभिपेततुः। अभिसंश्लिष्टयोस्तत्र तयोराहवशौण्डयोः॥
en: Filled with rage and rushing at one another, they challenged one another furiously. Those two foremost of combatants, in consequence of their being too near each other.

sn: विच्छिन्नशरपातत्वाद् गदायुद्धमवर्तत।
en: a

sn: गदया भीमसेनस्तु कर्णस्य रथकूबरम्॥ विभेद शतधा राजंस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्। ततो भीमस्य राधेयो गदामाविध्य वीर्यवान्॥
en: To use bows and arrows, began to fight with their maces. Then Bhimasena succeeded in crushing Karna's car terraced with his mace; O king, that indeed looked wonderful. Then the puissant son of Radha grasping a mace.

sn: अवासृजद् रथे तां तु बिभेद गदया गदाम्। ततो भीमः पुनर्गुर्वी चिक्षेपाधिरथेर्गदाम्॥
en: Hurled it at Bhima's car. But the latter broke it down with a mace of his own. Thereafter once more Bhima threw with force a heavy mace at the son of Adhiratha.

sn: तां गदां बहुभिः कर्णः सुपुङ्खः सुप्रवेजितैः। प्रत्यविध्यत् पुनश्चान्यैः सा भीमं पुनराव्रजत्॥
en: Then Karna struck that mace with numerous shafts furnished with beautiful wings and duly sped and also with other shafts. The mace then was thrown back on Bhima.

sn: व्यालीव मन्त्राभिहता कर्णबाणैरभिद्रुता। तस्याः प्रतिनिपातेन भीमस्य विपुलो ध्वजः॥
en: Being repulsed by the arrows of Karna, like a snake charmed with incantations. At the rebound of that mace the mighty standard of Bhima.

sn: पपात सारथिश्चास्य मुमोह च गदाहतः। स कर्णं सायकानष्टौ व्यसृजत् क्रोधमूर्छितः॥
en: Broke and fell down and his charioteer, also struck with that mace, became insensible. Thereupon furious in rage, Bhima discharged eight shafts at Karna.

sn: तैस्तस्य निशितैस्तीक्ष्णैर्भीमसेनो महाबलः। चिच्छेद परवीरघ्नः प्रहसन्निव भारत॥ ध्वजं शरासनं चैव शरावापं च भारत। कर्णोऽप्यन्यद् धनुर्गृह्य हेमपृष्ठं दुरासदम्॥ ततः पुनस्तु राधेयो हयानस्य रथेषुभिः। ऋक्षवर्णाञ्जघानाशु तथोभौ पाणिसारथी॥
en: And his standard and bow and his leathern fence, O Bharata. The mighty Bhimasena, that slayer of hostile heroes, with the greatest heedfulness, cut-off with those sharp arrows, O Bharata, the standard, the bow and the leathern fence of Karna's chariot. Thereupon the son of Radha, grasping another tough and golddecked bow, sped a large number of shafts and therewith quickly dispatched Bhima's steed of the hue of bear and then his two flank protector.

sn: स विपन्नरथो भीमो नकुलस्याप्लुतो रथम्। हरिर्यथा गिरेः शृङ्गं समाक्रामदरिंदमः॥
en: When his chariot was thus rendered useless, hat subduer of foes, viz., Bhima, quickly jumped into the chariot of Nakula like a lion leaping upon a mountain chest.

sn: तथा द्रोणर्जुनौ चित्रमयुध्येतां महारथौ। आचार्यशिष्यौ राजेन्द्र कृतप्रहरणौ युधि॥
en: Meanwhile Drona and Arjuna those two most of car-warriors preceptor and pupil, both accomplished in the use of weapons, O monarch, fought on with each other in battle.

sn: लघुसंघानयोगाभ्यां रथयोश्च रणेन च। मोहयन्तौ मनुष्याणां चढूंषि च मनांसि च॥
en: Confounding the eyes and minds of men with the celerity with which they used their weapons and the sureness of their aims and the motions of their chariot.

sn: उपारमन्त ते सर्वे योधा भरतसत्तम। अदृष्टपूर्वं पश्यन्तस्तद् युद्धं गुरुशिष्ययोः॥
en: Beholding that battle between the preceptor and pupil, of which no equal was seen before, the other warriors desisted from fighting and began to tremble.

sn: विचित्रान् पृतनामध्ये रथमार्गानुदीर्य तौ। अन्योन्यमपसव्यं च कर्तुं वीरौ तदेषतुः।। :॥
en: Then those two heroes, displaying various motions of cars on the field of battle, tried to leave each other to their right.

sn: पराक्रमां तयोर्योधा ददृशुस्ते सुविस्मिताः। तयोः समभवद् युद्धं द्रोणपाण्डवयोर्महत्॥
en: Then seeing their prowess, the warriors were filled with delight. Thereafter a mighty battle raged between Drona and that son of Pandu.

sn: आमिषार्थे महाराज गगने श्येनयोरिव। यद् यचकार द्रोणस्तु कुन्तीपुत्रजिगीषया॥
en: Like that, O mighty monarch, between two hawks in the heavens for a piece of meat. Whatever efforts Drona made for conquering the son of Kunti.

sn: तत् तत् प्रतिजघानाशु प्रहसंस्तस्य पाण्डवः। यदा द्रोणो न शक्नोति पाण्डवं स्म विशेषितुम्॥
en: Were overcome by Arjuna who also strove vigorously. When Drona failed to obtain any advantage over the son of Pandu.

sn: ततः प्रादुश्चकारासमस्रमार्गविशारदः। ऐन्द्रं पाशुपतं त्वाष्ट्र वायव्यमथ वारुणम्॥
en: Then that foremost of all knowers of weapons, began to invoke into existence, Aindra, Pasupata, Sashtra, Vayavya and Varuna weapons.

sn: मुक्तं मुक्तं द्रोणचापात् तज्जघान धनंजयः। अस्त्राण्यस्त्रैर्यदा तस्य विधिवद्धन्ति पाण्डवः॥
en: But as soon as those weapons issued out of the bow of Drona, Dhananjaya destroyed them quickly. Then Pritha's son duly destroyed all those weapons with his own weapons.

sn: ततोऽस्त्रैः परमैर्दिव्यैर्दोणः पार्थमवाकिरत्। यद् यदलं स पार्थाय प्रयुङ्क्ते विजिगीषया॥
en: Thereafter Drona covered Pritha's son with excellent and celestial shafts. Whatever weapon then he shot at Partha, desirous of obtaining victory.

sn: तस्य तस्य विघाताय तत् तद्वि कुरुतेऽर्जुनः। य वध्यमानेष्वस्रेषु दिव्येष्वपि यथाविधि॥
en: Arjuna destroyed it by due measures. Upon the destruction even of his celestial weapons.

sn: अर्जुनेनार्जुनं द्रोणो मनसैवाभ्यपूजयत्। मेने-चात्मानमधिकं पृथिव्यामधि भारत॥ तेन शिष्येण सर्वेभ्यः शस्रविद्भयः परंतपः। वार्यमाणस्तु पार्थेन तथा मध्ये महात्मनाम्॥
en: By Arjuna, Drona applauded him in his mind. Then that afflicter of foes, viz., Drona,O Bharata, regarded himself to be superior to all knowers of weapon on earth in consequence of his having Arjuna for his pupil. Thus checked by Pritha's son in the midst of all those high souled warriors.

sn: यतमानोऽर्जुनं प्रीत्या प्रत्यवारयदुत्स्मयन्। ततोऽन्तरिक्षे देवाश्च गन्धर्वाश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: Drona, vigorously striving cheerfully resisted Arjuna (in his turn) being filled with wonder all the while. Then in the welkin, thousands of celestial and Gandharvas,

sn: ऋषयः सिद्धसंघाश्च व्यतिष्ठनत दिदृक्षया। तदप्सरोभिकीर्णं यक्षगन्धर्वसंकुलम्॥
en: And sages and hosts of Siddhas, were seen on all sides. Thronged with Apsaras and Yakshasas and Rakshasas.

sn: श्रीमदाकाशमभवद् भूयो मेघाकुलं यथा। तत्र स्मान्तर्हिता वाचो व्यचरन्त पुनः पुनः॥
en: The welkin once more appeared to be darkened by gathering masses of clouds. An incorporeal voice repeatedly spoke.

sn: द्रोणपार्थस्तवोपेता व्यश्रूयन्त नराधिप। विसृज्यमानेष्वस्रेषु ज्वालयत्सु दिशो दश॥
en: In praise of Drona and the high-souled son of Pandu. when in consequence of the weapons discharged by Drona and Pritha’ son, all the directions were illumined with their effulgence.

sn: अब्रुवंस्तत्र सिद्धाश्च ऋषयश्च समागताः। नैवेदं मानुषं युद्धं नासुरं न च राक्षसम्॥ न दैवं न च गान्धर्वे ब्राह्मं ध्रवमिदं परम्। विचित्रमिदमाश्चर्यं न नो दृष्टं न च श्रुतम्॥
en: The Siddhas and the sages present then said "This is neither a human, nor an Asura, nor a Rakshasa, nor a celestial, nor a Gandharva battle; certainly this is a high Brahma battle; this encounter is exceedingly charming and greatly wonderful. We have never seen nor heard of its like before.

sn: अति पाण्डवमाचार्यो द्रोणं चाप्यति पाण्डवः। नानयोरन्तरं शक्यं दुष्टमन्येन केनचित्॥
en: At times the preceptor obtained advantages over the son of Pandu and at times the latter again prevailed over the former. None then was able to mark any difference between them.

sn: यदि रुद्रो द्विधाकृत्य युध्येतात्मानमात्मना। तत्र शक्योपमा कर्तुमन्यत्र तु न विद्यते॥
en: If Rudra, dividing himself in twain, fights with himself, then an example may be obtained that may match it.

sn: ज्ञानमेकस्थमाचार्ये ज्ञानं योगश्च पाण्डवे। शौर्यमेकस्थमाचार्य बलं शौर्यं च पाण्डवे॥
en: In the preceptor there is the knowledge of science. The knowledge of sciences and the means to be applied are in the son of Pandu. Heroism exists in Drona whereas both heroism and mighty exist in the son of Pandu.

sn: नेमौ शक्यौ महेष्वासौ युद्धे क्षपयितुं परैः। इच्छमानौ पुनरिमौ हन्येतां सामरं जगत्॥
en: None of these two combatants could be resisted by the foe in battle. At their will they can destroy the universe with the gods themselves.

sn: इत्यब्रुवन् महाराज दृष्ट्वो तौ पुरुषर्षभौ। अन्तर्हितानि भूतानि प्रकाशानि च सर्वशः॥
en: Seeing those two foremost of men, O mighty monarch, the visible and invisible creatures said these words.

sn: ततो द्रोणो ब्राह्ममस्र प्रादुश्चक्रे महामतिः। संतापयन् रणे पार्थं भूतान्यन्तर्हितानि च॥
en: Thereafter, Drona of great intelligence, invoked into existence the Brahma weapon thereby afflicting Partha and the invisible creatures.

sn: ततश्चचाल पृथिवी सपर्वतवनदुमा। ववौ च विषमो वायुः सागराश्चापि चुक्षुभुः॥
en: Thereupon the earth, with its mountains, forests and trees, began to tremble. Conflicting winds began to blow and the oceans were agitated.

sn: ततस्रासो महानासीत् कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः। सर्वेषां चैव भूतानामुद्यतेऽने महात्मना॥
en: When that weapon was raised by highsouled Drona for use, the Kuru and the Pandava troops as also all the other creatures were stricken with panic.

sn: ततः पार्थोऽप्यसंम्भ्रान्तस्तदा प्रतिजनिवान्। ब्रह्मास्रेणैव राजेन्द्र ततः सर्वमशीशमत्॥
en: Thereupon, O foremost of kings, Pirthas' son, with the other Brahma weapons, destroyed that weapon of Drona and then all things were again pacified.

sn: यदा न गम्यते पारं तयोरन्यतरस्य वा। ततः संकुलयुद्धेन तद् युद्धं व्याकुलीकृतम्॥
en: At last when none of them was able to vanquish his opponent in a single combat, a ge engagement commenced between the two hosts, creating a terrible confusion on the field.

sn: नाज्ञायत तत: किंचित् पुनरेव विशाम्पते। प्रवृत्ते तुमुले युद्धे द्रोणपाण्डवयोर्मधे॥
en: During the progress of that terrible encounter between Drona and Pandu's son, O king, once nothing could be distinguished.

sn: शरजालैः समाकीर्णे मेघजालैरिवाम्बरे। नापतच ततः कश्चिदन्तरिक्षचरस्तदा॥
en: The firmament being covered with networks of arrows, as if with masses of clouds, no ranger of the air was then seen to course through it. more

sn: संजय उवाच तस्मिस्तथा वर्तमाने गजाश्वनरसंक्षये। दुःशासनो महाराज धृष्टद्युम्नमयोधयत्॥
en: Sanjaya said When that battle, destructive of men, horses and elephants, thus progressed, O mighty monarch, Dushasana fought with Dhristadyumna.

sn: स तु रुक्मरथासक्तो दुःशासनशरार्दितः। अमर्षात् तव पुत्रस्य शरैर्वाहानवाकिरत्॥
en: on The latter, then mounted on a golden chariot and afflicted with rage and began to cover the animals of your son with his own arrows.

sn: क्षणेन च रथस्तस्य सध्वजः सहसारथिः। नादृश्यत महाराज पार्षतस्य शरैश्चितः॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, covered with the arrows the car of Prisata's son; soon did the car of Dushasana, its standard and charioteer became invisible.

sn: दुःशासनस्तु राजेन्द्र पाञ्चाल्यस्य महात्मनः। नाशकत् प्रमुखे स्थातुं शरजालप्रपीडितः॥
en: Then, O foremost of kings, Dushasana, being afflicted with the arrows of Panchalas, could not stay before that illustrious warriors.

sn: स तु दुःशासनं बाणैविर्मुखीकृत्य पार्षतः। किरञ्छरसहस्राणि द्रोणमेवाभ्ययाद् रणे॥
en: Thus the son of Prisata, having repulsed Dushasana with his arrows, assailed Drona shooting thousands of shafts as he proceeded.

sn: अभ्यपद्यत हार्दिक्यः कृतवर्मा चनन्नतरम्। सोदर्याणां त्रयश्चैव त एनं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Then Hridika's son Kritavarman, with his three uterine brothers, encountered him and tried to resist him.

sn: तं यमौ पृष्ठतोऽन्वैतां रक्षन्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ। द्रोणायाभिमुखं यान्तं दीप्यमानमिवानलम्॥
en: The twins, Nakula and Sahadeva, those two foremost of men, then protected Dhristadyumna from behind as he rushed upon Drona like a blazing fire.

sn: सम्प्रहारमकुर्वस्ते सर्वे च सुमहारथाः। अमर्षिताः सत्त्ववन्तः कृत्वा मरणमग्रतः॥
en: Then all those mighty car-warriors, possessed of strength and inspired with wraih. fell to smite one another, keeping death in their view.

sn: शुद्धात्मानः शुद्धवृत्ता राजन् स्वर्गपुरस्कृताः। आर्य युद्धमकुर्वन्त परस्परजिगीषवः॥
en: Of pure souls and pure behavirous, o king, those warriors, keeping the hope of paradise before their mind's eye, fought on fairly, impelled by a desire for conquering one another.

sn: शुक्लाभिजनकर्माणो मतिमन्तो जनाधिप। धर्मयुद्धमयुध्यन्त प्रेप्सन्तो गतिमुत्तमाम्॥
en: Of stainless extraction and of spotless deeds and gifted with keen intelligence those rulers of men, keeping paradise in view, fought on fairly with one another.

sn: न तत्रासीदधर्मिष्ठमशस्तं युद्धमेव च। नात्र कर्णी न नालीको न लिप्तो न च बस्तिकः॥
en: In that battle there was nothing unfair or nothing against the rules of military science. In that battle, neither Kanies nor Nalikas, nor poisoned arrows nor Vastikas.

sn: न सूची कपिशो नैव न गवास्थिर्गजास्थिजः। इषुरासीन्न संश्लिष्टो न पूतिर्न च जिह्मगः॥
en: Nor Suchikopisas, nor those made of the bones of bulls and elephants, nor those having two heads, nor those having fusty beards, nor those that were not straight flying, were used by any body.

sn: ऋजून्येव विशुद्धानि सर्वे शस्त्राण्यधारयन्। सुयुद्धेन पराँल्लोकानीप्सन्तः कीर्तिमेव च॥
en: O king Arjuna! The son of Kunti did not assert the opinion but being it a trick, all other present there had preferred it. Only Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti could agree to the matter after a lengthy and tough discussion.

sn: तदाऽऽसीत् तुमुलं युद्धं सर्वदोषविवर्जितम्। चतुर्णा तव योधानां तैसिभिः पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: All then used straight and pure weapon and those three of the Pandava side, the battle, that occurred, was highly terrible, but free from all unfairness.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नसतु तान् दृष्ट्वा तव राजन् रथर्षभान्। यमाभ्यां वारितान् वीराज्छीघ्रास्रो द्रोणमभ्ययात्॥
en: Then Dhristadyumna, very quick in the use of weapons and beholding those brave and mighty car-warriors of your army, resisted by the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva), rushed upon Drona.

sn: निवारितास्तु ते वीरास्तयोः पुरुषसिंहयोः। समसज्जन्त चत्वारो वाताः पर्वतयोरिव॥
en: Resisted by those two foremost of men, those four brave warriors encountered the former like the winds assailing a pair of mountains.

sn: द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां यमौ सार्धं रथाभ्यां रथपुङ्गवौ। समासक्तौ ततो द्रोणं धृष्टद्युम्नोऽभ्यवर्तत॥
en: Each of the twins, both mighty car-warriors was engaged with a couple of opponents. Meanwhile Dhristadyumna poured showers of arrows on Drona.

sn: दृष्ट्वा द्रोणाय पाञ्चाल्यं व्रजन्तं युद्धदुर्मदम्। यमाभ्यां तांश्च संसक्तांस्तदन्तरमुपाद्रवत्॥ दुर्योधनो महाराज किरञ्छोणितभोजनान्। तं सात्यकिः शीघ्रतरं पुनरेवाभ्यवर्तत॥
en: Then seeing the indomitable prince of the Panchalas advance upon Drona and those warriors of his army engaged with the twins, Duryodhana, O king, rushed to that part of the field, discharging myriad's of blood-sucking arrows. Beholding thus Satyaki approach the Kuru king in great speed.

sn: तौ परस्परमासाद्य समीपे कुरुमाधवौ। हसमानौ नृशार्दूलावभीतौ समसज्जताम्॥
en: Those two foremost of men, the two scions of the Kuru and Madhu race respectively nearing each other, were filled with the desire for smiting down each other.

sn: बाल्यवृत्तानि सर्वाणि प्रीयमाणौ विचिन्त्य तौ। अन्योन्यं प्रेक्षमाणौ च स्मयमानौ पुनः पुनः॥
en: Recollecting their conduct towards each other in their early days and reflecting with pleasure on the same, they looked at each other and smiled repeatedly.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनो राजा सात्यकि समभाषत। प्रियं सखायं सततं गर्हयन् वृत्तमात्मनः॥
en: Then king Duryodhana, blaming his own conduct, addressed his ever dear friend Satyaki and said

sn: धिक् क्रोधं धिक् सखे लोभं धिडयोहं धिगमर्पितम्। धिगस्तु क्षात्रमाचारं धिगस्तु बलमौरसम्॥
en: Fie on wrath, ( friend and fie on vindictiveness, fie on Kshatriya urge and fie on might and prowess.

sn: यत्र मामभिसंधत्से त्वां चाहं शिनिपुङ्गव। त्वं हि प्राणैः प्रियतरो ममाहं च सदा तव॥
en: Inasmuch as you aim weapons at me and I am directing mine at you, O foremost of the descendants of Sins's race. In the days of childhood, you were dearer to me than my very life and I also was so to you.

sn: स्मरामि तानि सर्वाणि बाल्यवृत्तानि यानि नौ। तानि सर्वाणि जीर्णानि साम्प्रतं नो रणाजिरे॥
en: Alas! all those deeds of boyhood that I recollect of both yourself and mine, become as nothing on the field of battle.

sn: किमन्यत्रोधलोभाभ्यां युद्धमेवाद्य सात्वत। तं तथावादिनं तत्र सात्यकि: प्रत्यभाषत॥ प्रहसन् विशिखांस्तीक्ष्णानुद्यम्य परमास्रवित्। नाचार्यस्य निवेशनम्॥
en: Alas! impelled by rage and covetousness, we are here today for fighting with each other, O scion of the Satvata race. Then O king, Satyaki conversant in the use of great weapons, taking up some sharp arrows smilingly replied to king Duryodhana who was thus speaking to him, “This is no assembly, O prince, nor the house of our preceptor where in days gone by, we sported smiling together."

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच क्व सा क्रीडा गतास्माकं बाल्ये वै शिनिपुङ्गव॥ क्व च युद्धमिदं भूय: ‘कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः'।
en: Duryodhana said O foremost of Shini's race, where have those sports of our childhood vanished and alas, how has this battle come upon us. It appears that the influence of time is irresistible.

sn: किं नु नो विद्यते कृत्यं धनेन धनलिप्सया॥ यत्र युध्यामहे सर्वे धनलोभात् समागताः। नेयं सभा राजपुत्र
en: Urged though we are by a desire for wealth, what use have we of wealth that meeting each other, we now engage in battle, urged by avarice.

sn: संजय उवाच तं तथावादिनं तत्र राजानं माधवोऽब्रवीत्॥ एवंवृत्तं सदा क्षात्रं युध्यन्तीह गुरूनपि। यदि तेऽहं प्रियो राजन् जहि मां मा चिरं कृथाः॥
en: Sanjaya said Satyaki then replied unto king Duryodhana who had thus spoken – "That they have to fight even with their preceptors has always been the duty of Kshatriyas.

sn: त्वत्कृते सुकृताल्लोकान् गच्छेयं भरतर्षभ। या ते शक्तिर्बलं यच्च तत् क्षिप्रं मयि दर्शय॥ नेच्छामि तदहं द्रष्टुं मित्राणां व्यसनं महत्।
en: If I am indeed believed of you, O king, slay me without delay. O foremost of the Bharatas, them through your instrumentality I shall be launched upon the regions of the righteous. Bring into play, as soon as possible, all your might and prowess, against myself. This carnage of my friends, I do not wish to behold any longer.

sn: इत्येवं व्यक्तमाभाष्य प्रतिभाष्य च सात्यकिः॥ अभ्ययात् तूर्णमव्यग्रो दयां नाकुरुतात्मनि।
en: Having thus replied to king Duryodhana and said his say, O king, Satyaki dauntlessly and reckless of his life, rushed furiously upon Duryodhana.

sn: तमायान्तं महाबाहुं प्रत्यगृह्णात् तवात्मजः॥ शरैश्चावाकिरद् राजशैनेयं तनयस्तव।
en: Beholding hinthus advance your son received him. Indeed, O king, your son then poured upon him a veritable shower of arrows.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं कुरुमाधवसिंहयोः॥ अन्योन्यं क्रुद्धयो?रं यथा द्विरदसिंहयोः।
en: Then ensued a dreadful battle between those two foremost of Kuru's and Madhu's race, that resembled an encounter between a lion and an elephant.

sn: ततः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैः सात्वतं युद्धदुर्मदम्॥ दुर्योधनः प्रत्यविध्यत् कुपितो दशभिः शरैः।
en: Then filled with rage Duryodhana pierced the indomitable Satyaki with numerous keen arrows shot from the bow drawn to its fullest stretch.

sn: तं सात्यकिः प्रत्यविध्यत् तथैवावाकिरच्छरैः॥ पञ्चाशता पुनश्चाजौ त्रिंशता दशभिश्च ह।
en: Satyaki quickly pierced Duryodhana in return with fifty keen shafts in that battle and then with twenty and next with another ten shafts.

sn: सात्यकिं तु रणे राजन् प्रहसंस्तनयस्तव॥ आकर्णपूर्णैर्निशितैर्विव्याध त्रिंशता शरैः।
en: Then in that battle your son smilingly pierced Satyaki in return with thirty arrows shot from his bow-string drawn back to the ear.

sn: ततोऽस्य सशरं चापं क्षुरप्रेण द्विधाच्छिनत्॥ सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय लघुहस्तस्ततो दृढम्। सात्यकिळसृजचापि शरश्रेणी सुतस्य ते॥
en: Discharging then a Kshurapra (razorheaded arrow) he cut-off in two, Satyaki's bow with arrows fixed thereon ; Satyaki, thereupon with great lightness of hands, grasped a tougher bow and began to shoot a shower of shafts at your son. As those lines of arrows flew for bringing about Duryodhana's death.

sn: तामापतन्ती सहसा शरश्रेणी जिघांसया। चिच्छेद बहुधा राजा तत उचुक्रुशुर्जनाः॥ सात्यकिं च त्रिसप्तत्या पीडयामास वेगितः। स्वर्णपुङ्खः शिलाधौतैराकर्णापूर्णनिःसृतैः॥
en: The latter, O monarch, cut them into pierces, whereupon the troops uttered a loud shout. Then quickly he afflicted Satyaki with seventy three shafts, furnished with golden wings, whetted on stone and shot from a bow drawn to its fullest stretch. Then all these arrows and the bow with shafts thereupon.

sn: तस्य संदधतश्चेषू संहितेषु च कार्मुकम्। आच्छिनत् सात्यकिस्तूर्णं शरैश्चैवाष्यवीविधत्॥ स गाढविद्धो व्यथितः प्रत्यपायाद् रथान्तरे। दुर्योधनो महाराज दाशार्हशरपीडितः॥
en: Satyaki cut-off and covered Duryodhana with a fresh shower of arrows. Thus deeply pierced and afflicted with the shafts of that i scion of the Dasarha race, Duryodhana, O mighty monarch, took shelter in another car. Then recovering a little your son once more rushed upon Satyaki.

sn: समाश्वस्य तु पुत्रस्ते सात्यकिं पुनरभ्ययात्। विसृजन्निषुजालानि युयुधानरथं प्रति॥ तथैव सात्यकिर्बाणान् दुर्योधनस्थं प्रति। सततं विसृजन् राजंस्तत् संकुलमवर्तत॥
en: Shooting myriad's of arrows at the chariot of the latter. Similarly Satyaki discharged arrows at Duryodhana's car; whereupon, O king, the battle became extremely fierced. Then in consequence of those shafts thus discharged and in consequence of their falling on all sides.

sn: तत्रेषुभिः क्षिष्यमाणैः पतद्भिश्च शरीरिषु। अग्नेरिव महाकक्षे शब्दः समभवन्महान्॥ तयोः शरसहस्रश्च संछन्नं वसुधातलम्।
en: Loud clashing sounds there, resembling that produced by a raging conflagration consuming a large forest. The surface of the earth was then covered with those thousands of shafts shot by both of them.

sn: अगम्यरूपं च शरैराकाशं समपद्यत॥ तत्राप्यधिकमालक्ष्य माधवं रथसत्तमम्।
en: Clouded therewith, the sky sky became invisible. Then beholding that foremost of carwarriors, namely, him of Madhu's race, prevail over Duryodhana.

sn: क्षिप्रमभ्यपतत् कर्णः परीप्संस्तनयं तव॥ न तु तं मर्षयामास भीमसेनो महाबलः।
en: Karna quickly advanced to rescue your son. But the mighty Bhimasena did not allow him to arose do so.

sn: सोऽभ्ययात्त्वरितः कर्ण विसृजन् सायकान् बहून्॥ तस्य कर्ण: शितान् बाणान् प्रतिहत्य हसन्निव।
en: And he in his turn assailed Karna, quickly shooting numerous arrows. Thereupon Karna smilingly destroyed all those sharp arrows of Bhima.

sn: धनुः शरांश्च चिच्छेद सूतं चाभ्यहनच्छरैः॥ भीमसेनस्तु संक्रुद्धो गदामादाय पाण्डवः।
en: Cut off his bow and arrows and wounded his driver with numerous shafts. Thereupon Pandu's son Bhimasena, burning with rage, took up a mace.

sn: ध्वजं धनुश्च सूतं च सम्ममर्दाहवे रिपोः॥ रथचक्रं च कर्णस्य बभञ्ज स महाबलः।
en: And therewith crushed the bow, the standard and the charioteer of his opponent in that battle. That mighty hero also shattered one of the wheels of Karna's car.

sn: भग्नचक्रे रथेऽतिष्ठदकम्पः शैलराडिव॥ एकचक्रं रथं तस्य तमूहुः सुचिरं हयाः।
en: Then staying on his chariot of which one wheel was broken, Karna did not tremble (in fear) but was as firm as the prince of mountains. That chariot of his which had now only one wheel left was drawn by his horses.

sn: एकचक्रमिवार्कस्य रथं सप्त हया यथा॥ अमृष्यमाणः कर्णस्तु भीमसेनमयुध्यता
en: Like the single-wheeled car of the Sun borne by the seven celestial steeds. Then not tolerating the feats of Bhimasena Karna fought on which latter.

sn: विविधैरिषुजालैश्च नानाशस्त्रैश्च संयुगे॥ भीमसेनस्तु संक्रुद्धः सूतपुत्रमयोधयत्।
en: Using different groups of arrows and diverse kinds of other weapons. Bhimasena similarly worked up with rage, fought on with the son of Suta,

sn: तस्मिस्तथा वर्तगने क्रुद्धो धर्मसुतोऽब्रवीत्॥ पञ्चालानां नरव्याघ्रान् मत्स्यांश्च पुरुषर्षभान्।
en: When then the battle became thus confused and general, king Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, addressing the foremost of her es of the Panchalas and the Matsyas said

sn: ये नः प्राणाः शिरोये च ये नो योधा महारथाः॥ त एते धार्तराष्ट्रेषु विषक्ताः पुरुषर्षभाः।
en: are “They who are like our lives, they that are our heads, they that are our heads, they that are possessed of immense strength those foremost of men now all engaged with the Dhritarashtra hosts.

sn: किं तिष्ठत यथा मूढाः सर्वे विगतचेतसः॥ तत्र गच्छत यत्रैते युध्यन्ते मामका रथाः।
en: Why are you then standing as if stupefied and with you, senses confounded? Hie there where my warriors are valorously fighting.

sn: क्षात्रधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य सर्व एव गतज्वराः॥ जयन्तो वध्यमानाश्च गतिमिष्टां गमिष्यथ।
en: Keeping in view the duties of the Kshatriya order and dismissing your fears, engage in the battle; for then conquering or slain, you will obtain desirable ends.

sn: जित्वा वा बहुभिर्यज्ञैर्यजध्वं भूरिदक्षिणैः॥ हता वा देवसाद् भूत्वा लोकान् प्राप्स्यथ पुष्कलान्।
en: If you conquer you may celebrate numerous sacrifices, giving away profuse Dakshina to the Brahmanas : If on the other hand you are slain, then becoming equal to the gods, you will attain regions of blessedness.

sn: ते राज्ञा चोदिता वीरा योत्स्यमाना महारथाः॥ क्षात्रधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य त्वरिता द्रोणमभ्ययुः।
en: Urged on by the king in the above manner. Those brave and mighty car-warriors engaged on the field, quickly rushed upon Drona, keeping in view the duties of the Kshatriyas.

sn: पञ्चालास्त्वेकतो द्रोणमभ्यमन् निशितैः शरैः॥ भीमसेनपुरोगाश्चाप्येकतः पर्यवारयन्।
en: Then the Panchalas, from one side began to assail Drona with their arrows, whilst those headed by Bhima began to check him on the other said,

sn: आसंस्तु पाण्डुपुत्राणां त्रयो जिह्या महारथाः॥ यमौ च भीमसेनश्च प्राक्रोशंस्ते धनंजयम्।
en: Three of the mighty and war-like sons of Pandu were crooked-minded. They were the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) and Bhimasena. These then addressing Arjuna loudly said

sn: अभिद्रवार्जुन क्षिप्रं कुरून् द्रोणादपानुद॥ तत एनं हनिष्यन्ति पञ्चाला हतरक्षिणम्।
en: Rush, O Arjuna, upon the Kurus and separate them from Drona. Then the Panchalas will be able to slay him easily when he will be deprived on their protection.

sn: कौरवेयांस्ततः पार्थः सहसा समुपाद्रवत्॥ पञ्चालानेव तु द्रोणो धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमान्। ममर्दुस्तरसा वीराः पञ्चमेऽहनि भारत॥
en: Thereupon Pritha's son, all on a sudden attacked the Kaurava troops, while Drona too marched against the Panchala troops headed by Dhristadyumna. O Bharata, in that the fifth day of Drona's command, the brave combatants were slaughtered in quick succession.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: संजय उवाच पञ्चालानां ततो द्रोणोऽप्यकरोत् कदनं महत्। यथा क्रुद्धो रणे शक्रो दानवानां क्षयं पुरा॥
en: Sanjaya said Then Drona effected a fierce carnage in the ranks of the Panchala troops, like the enraged Shakra causing a great slaughter amongst the Danava troops in days gone by.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: द्रोणास्रेण महाराज वध्यमानाः परे युधि। नात्रसन्त रणे द्रोणात् सत्त्ववन्तो महारथः॥
en: O mighty monarch, the enemies of Drona all mighty car-warriors and possessed of great strength, though thus slaughtered by his arrows, did not shrink in fear from him.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: युध्यमाना महाराज पञ्चालाः संजयास्तथा। द्रोणमेवाभ्ययुयुद्धे योधयन्तो महारथाः॥
en: Then those mighty car-warriors, the Panchalas and the Srinjayas, engaged in that battle, O king, rushed upon Drona's self.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: तेषां तु च्छाद्यमानानां पञ्चालानां समन्ततः। अभवद् भैरवो नादो वध्यतां शरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Slaughtered with arrows and darts and trying to encompass Drona on all sides, the yells they uttered were terrible and loud.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: वध्यमानेषु संग्रामे पञ्चालेषु महात्मना। उदीर्यमाणे द्रोणारे पाण्डवान् भयमाविशत्॥
en: Then beholding the slaughter of the Panchalas by the high-souled Drona and seeing his weapons enshroud all sides, the Pandavas became frightened.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: दृष्ट्वाश्वनरयोधानां विपुलं च क्षयं युधि। पाण्डवेया महाराज नाशशंसुर्जयं तदा॥
en: Beholding the profuse destruction of horses and foot-soldiers in the battle, the Pandava troops, O king, became hopeless regarding their victory.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: कचिद् द्रोणो न नः सर्वान् क्षपयेत् परमास्रवित्। समिद्धः शिशिरापाये दहन कक्षमिवानलः॥
en: "Is not Drona that warrior well-versed in the use of cxcellent weapons going to consume us all, like a raging conflagration consuming a heap of straw at the expiration of the winter season?

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: न चैनं संयुगे कश्चित् समर्थः प्रतिवीक्षितुम्। न चैनमर्जुनो जातु प्रतियुध्येत धर्मवित्॥
en: None can now even look at him in battle. Knowing the rules of fair combat even Arjuna will not now fight with him." (Even thus did they talk with each other).

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: त्रस्तान् कुन्तीसुतान् दृष्ट्वा द्रोणसायकपीडितान्। मतिमाश्रेयसे युक्तः केशवोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then beholding the sons of Kunti dismayed and afflicted by the arrows of Drona the intelligent Kesava ever solicitous of the welfare

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: नैष युद्धे न संग्रामे जेतुं शक्यः कथञ्चन। सधनुर्धन्विनां श्रेष्ठो देवैरपि सवासवैः॥
en: This foremost of all wielders of bows and arrows in incapable of being vanquished in battle by any one, one excepting the gods with Vasava at their head.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: न्यस्तशस्त्रस्तु संग्रामे शक्यो हन्तुं भवेभिः। आस्थीयतां जये योगो धर्ममुत्सृज्य पाण्डवाः॥
en: When he lays aside his weapons in battle, he may be slain even by men. O you sons of Pandu, abandoning virtue, do you therefore now bctake yourself to contrivances for securing victory in battle.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: यथा वः संयुगे सर्वान् न हन्याद् रुक्मवाहनः। अश्वत्थाम्नि हते नैष युध्येदिति मतिर्मम॥
en: Before Drona drawn by horses of golden colours succeeds in slaying us all. I think, if Ashvatthaman be killed, he will desist from fighting.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: तं हतं संयुगे कश्चिदस्मै शंसतु मानवः। एतन्नारोचयद् राजन् कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः॥
en: Let some one among us therefore tell him that Ashvatthaman has been slain in the battle, But O king, Kunti's son Dhananjaya did not accept this advice of Krishna.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: अन्ये त्वरोचयन् सर्वे कृच्छ्रेण तु युधिष्ठिरः। ततो भीमो महाबाहुरनीके स्वे महागजम्॥ जघान गदया राजन्नश्वत्थामानमित्युत। परप्रमथनं घोरं मालवस्येन्द्रवर्मणः॥
en: Others approved of it. Yudhishthira accepted it with much reluctance. Then the mighty-armed Bhiina, O monarch, slew with his mace, a terrible prodigious and foecrushing elephant called Ashvatthaman belonging to Indravarman the ruler of the Malavas.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: भीमसेनस्तु सव्रीडमुपेत्य द्रोणमाहवे। अश्वत्थामा हत इति शब्दमुच्चैश्चकार ह॥
en: Then Bhimasena approaching Drona with a little bashfulness began to exclaim to the top of his voice “Ashvatthaman is slain."

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: अश्वत्थामेति हि गजः ख्यातो नाम्ना हतोऽभवत्। कृत्वा मनसि तं भीमो मिथ्या व्याहृतवांस्तदा॥
en: The elephant known by the name of Ashvatthaman having been slain, Bhima spoke of Ashvatthainan's death. Knowing the true fact in his mind, Bhima then spoke what was false.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: भीमसेनवचः श्रुत्वा द्रोणस्तत् परमाप्रियम्। मनसा सन्नगात्रोऽभूद् यथा सैकतमम्भसि॥
en: Drona having heard this very dis-agreeable words of Bhimasena and he having reflected upon them in his mind, his limbs as if began to dissolve like sand in water.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: शङ्कमानः स तन्मिथ्या वीर्यज्ञः स्वसुतस्य वै। हतः स इति च श्रुत्वा नैव धैर्यादकम्पत॥
en: But knowing fully the prowess of his own son, he soon came to regard that news as false and therefore hearing of his slaughter he did not become unmanned.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: स लब्ध्वा चेतनां द्रोणः क्षणेनैव समाश्वसत्। अनुचिन्त्यात्मनः पुत्रमविषयमरातिभिः॥ स पार्षतमभिद्रुत्य जिघांसुर्मृत्युमात्मनः। अवाकिरत् सहस्रेण तीक्ष्णानां कङ्कपत्रिणाम्॥
en: Soon recovering his senses he became comforted, as he recollected that son was incapable of being assailed by the enemy. Rushing upon the son of Parshata and impelled by a desire to slay that brave warrior who was destined to be his slayer, he covered the former with thousands of sharp arrows furnished with wings of the Kanka feather.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: तं विंशतिसहस्राणि पञ्चालानां नरर्षभाः। तथा चरन्तं संग्रामे सर्वतोऽवाकिर छरैः॥
en: Thereupon twenty thousand illustrious carwarriors of the Panchala clan, covered him, thus careering on the field, with numerous shafts from all sides.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: शरैस्तैरचितं द्रोणं नापश्याम महारथम्। भास्करं जलदै रुद्धं वर्षास्विव विशाम्पते॥
en: O ruler of men, covered as he then was with those arrows, we could not seen that mighty car-warrior Drona, even as men cannot seen the sun covered when it is with clouds during the rainy season.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: विधूय तान् बाणगणान् पञ्चालानां महारथः। प्रादुश्चक्रे ततो द्रोणो ब्राह्ममस्रं परंतपः॥ वधाय तेषां शूराणां पञ्चालानाममर्षितः। ततो व्यरोचत द्रोणो विनिघ्नन् सर्वसैनिकान्॥
en: Then blowing off all those arrows of the Panchalas and with a view to effect the death of these heroic Panchala warriors, the mighty car-warrior Drona, the afflicter of hostile troops, invoked into existence a Brahma weapon. At this time he looked resplendent like a blazing fire without a streak of smoke.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: शिरांस्यपातयचापि पञ्चालानां महामृधे। तथैव परिघाकारान् बाहून् कनकभूषणान्॥
en: He then cut-off, in that great battle, innumerable heads of Panchala warriors as also their mace-like arms wearing golden ornaments.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे भारद्वाजेन पार्थिवाः। मेदिन्यामन्वकीर्यन्त वातनुन्ना इव द्रुमाः॥
en: Thus slaughtered by the son of Bharadvaja the royal warriors the began to fall down on the earth, like so many trees up-rooted by the force of the tempest.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: कुञ्जराणां च पततां हयौघानां च भारत। अगम्यरूपा पृथिवी मांसशोणितकर्दमा।॥
en: Miry with the flesh and blood of all the elephants and horses fallen in the battle, O Bharata, the earth appeared to he impassable.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: हत्वा विंशतिसाहस्रान् पञ्चालानां रथव्रजान्। अतिष्ठदाहवे द्रोणो विधूमोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन्॥
en: Having slain twenty thousand car-warriors of the Panchalas, Drona stood on the battlefield like a blazing fire free from even a single curl of smoke.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: तथैव च पुनः क्रुद्धो भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्। वसुदानस्य भल्लेन शिरः कायादपाहरत्॥
en: Thereafter filled with rage, the puissant son of Bharadvaja, lopped off the head of Vasudana from his trunk, by means of a bhalla.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: पुनः पञ्चशतान् मत्स्यान् षट्सहस्रांश्च सुंजयान्। हस्तिनामयुतं हत्वा जघानाश्वायुतं पुनः॥
en: He then slew five hundred Matsyas, six thousand Srinjayas and then again ten thousand elephants and ten thousand steads.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: क्षत्रियाणामभावाय दृष्ट्वा द्रोणमवस्थितम्। ऋषयोऽभ्यागतास्तूर्णं हव्यवाहपुरोगमाः॥
en: Then beholding Drona stay on the field for the extermination of the Kshatriya race, the following Rishis headed by the God of Fire approached him.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: विश्वामित्रो जमदग्निर्भरद्वाजोऽथ गौतमः। वसिष्ठः कश्यपोऽत्रिश्च ब्रह्मलोकं निनीषवः॥ सिकताः पृश्नयो गर्गा वालखिल्या मरीचिपाः। भृगवोऽङ्गिरसश्चैव सूक्ष्माश्चान्ये महर्षयः॥
en: They were, Vishvamitra, Jamadagni, Bharadvaja, Goutama, Vasistha, Kasyapa and Atri, the Sikatas, the Prisnis, Garga, the Valikhilyas, the Marichipas, the Vrigus, the Angiras and other mighty sages of subtle forms; these all were desirous of taking Drona to the region of Brahma.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: त एनमब्रुवन् सर्वे द्रोणमाहवशोभिनम्। अधर्मतः कृतं युद्धं समयो निधनस्य ते॥
en: All these then addressed Drona, that ornament of battle, into these words-'You are fighting wrongly, the hour of your death has come.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: न्यस्यायुधं रणे द्रोण समीक्षास्मानवस्थितान्। नातः क्रूरतरं कर्म पुनः कर्तुमिहार्हसि॥
en: Cast away your weapons, O Drona and look at us standing before you. Hence-forward it behoves you not to perform cruel acts like these.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: वेदवेदाङ्गविदुषः सत्यधर्मरतस्य ते। ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेण तवैतन्नोपपद्यते॥
en: You are learned in the Vedas and their auxiliaries and devoted truth and righteousness specially you are a Brahman, so these acts do not become you.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: त्यजायुधममोघेषो तिष्ठ वर्त्मनि शाश्वते। परिपूर्णश्च कालस्ते वस्तुं लोकेऽद्य मानुषे॥
en: Lay aside your weapons, shake off the pale of error that hangs over you and betake yourself to the eternal path (of virtue). Today, the days of your earthly habitation have been numbered.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: ब्रह्मास्त्रेण त्वथा दग्धा अनस्त्रज्ञा नरा भुवि। यदेतदीदृशां विप्र कृतं कर्म न साधु तत्॥
en: You have today consumed with your Brahma weapon many men who are ignorant of the use of weapons. This act which you have done is not at all praise-worthy.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: न्यास्यायुधं रणे विप्र द्रोण मा त्वं चिरं कृथाः। मा पापिष्ठतरं कर्म करिष्यसि पुनर्द्विज॥
en: O Drona, quickly lay you weapons aside in this battle; do not hesitate O twice-born one, you should not perpetrate such sinful acts any longer.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: इति तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा भीमसेनवचश्च तत्। धृष्टद्युम्नं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य रणे स विमनाऽभवत्॥
en: Having heard these words of the sages, as also the words of Bhimasena and also beholding Dhristadyumna stand before him in battle, Drona was dejected at heart.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: संदिह्यमानो व्यथितः कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। अहतं वा हतं वेति पप्रच्छ सुतमात्मनः॥
en: Burning with grief and extremely pained, he then inquired of king Yudhishthira the son of Kunti whether his son was really slain or not.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: स्थिरा बुद्धिर्हि द्रोणस्य न पार्थो वक्ष्यतेऽनृतम्। त्रयाणामपि लोकानामैश्वर्यार्थे कथञ्चन॥
en: Drona knew it for certain, the Pritha's son would never tell a lie, not even for the sake of getting the earth of the three worlds.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: तस्मात् तं परिपप्रच्छ नान्यं कञ्चिद् द्विजर्षभः। तस्मिंस्तस्य हि सत्याशा बाल्यात् प्रभृति पाण्डय।।४४
en: For that reason, that foremost of the regenerate ones questioned Yudhishthira in exclusion of every body else. Since the days of the latter's boyhood, Drona had hoped to hear truth from him.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: ततो निष्पाण्डवामुर्वी करिष्यन्तं युधां पतिम्। द्रोणं ज्ञात्वा धर्मराजं गोविन्दो व्यथितोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Meanwhile, O king, Govinda knowing that Drona, that foremost of all combatants, could sweep away the Pandavas off the face of the carth, was very much dejected and then addressing Yudhishthira he said

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: यद्यदिवसं द्रोणो युध्यते मन्युमास्थितः। सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते सेना विनाशं समुपैष्यति॥
en: "If influenced by rage Drona fights only for half a day, then I tell you truly, your troops are sure to be destroyed.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: स भवांस्त्रातु नो द्रोणात् सत्याज्ज्यायोऽनृतं वचः। अनृतं जीवितस्यार्थे वदन्न स्पृश्यतेऽनृतैः॥
en: Save us from Drona; under the circumstances as the present falsehood is better than truth. Speaking falsehood for the sake of saving a life one does not become a sinner.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: तयोः संवदतोरेवं भीमसेनोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ श्रुत्वैवं तु महाराज वधोपायं महात्मनः।
en: When they both were thus speaking with each other, Bhimasena said-"As soon as, O king, I heard of the means by which the illustrious Drona might be slain.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: गाहमानस्य ते सेनां मालवस्येन्द्रवर्मणः॥ अश्वत्थामेति विख्यातो गजः शक्रगजोपमः। निहतो युधि विक्रम्य ततोऽहं द्रोणमब्रुवम्॥ अश्वत्थामा हतो ब्रह्मन्निवर्तस्वाहवादिति।
en: Putting forth my prowess in battle, I immediately slew a mighty elephant resembling that of Shakra, belonging to Indravarman, the Chief of the Malavas who were standing in your army. I then went to Drona and told him, 'Ashvatthaman has been slain, O Brahman; desist from fighting.'

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: नूनं नाश्रद्दधद् वाक्यमेष मे पुरुषर्षभः॥ स त्वं गोविन्दवाक्यानि मानयस्व जयैषिणः।
en: Indeed, O foremost of men, the preceptor Drona did not believe in the veracity of my assertion; desirous of victory as you are, accept the counsel of Govinda.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: द्रोणाय निहतं शंस राजशारद्वतीसुतम्॥ त्वयोक्तो नैव युध्येत जातु राजन् द्विजर्षभः।
en: O monarch, inform Drona that the son of Saradvat's daughter is dead. Thus spoken by you that foremost of the Brahmanas will cease to fight.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: सत्यवान् हि त्रिलोकेऽस्मिन् भवान् ख्यातो जनाधिय॥ तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा कृष्णवाक्यप्रचोदितः।
en: O ruler of men, you are well-known in the three words for your truthfulness." Having heard these words of Bhima and influenced by the counsel of Krishna.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: भावित्वाच महाराज वक्तुं समुपचक्रमे॥ तमतथ्यभये मग्नो जये सक्तो युधिष्ठिरः।
en: And owing to the inevitability of Fate, O king, Yudhishthira decided to say, what he was called upon to say. Afraid of speaking lies, but anxious to obtain victory, Yudhishthira.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: अव्यक्तमब्रवीद् राजन् हतः कुञ्जर इत्युत॥ तस्य पूर्वे रथः पृथ्व्याश्चतुरङ्गुलमुच्छ्रितः।
en: Clearly said that Ashvatthama was dead, adding indistinctly the word elephant after the name Ashvatthama. Ere now the chariot of Yudhishthira had remained at a height of four fingers' breadth from the earth's surface;

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: बभूवैवं च तेनोक्ते तस्य बाहाः स्पृशन्महीम्॥ युधिष्ठिरात् तु तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा द्रोणो महारथः।
en: After he had uttered that lie his steeds touched the earth. Hearing these words from the lips of Yudhishthira, Drona that mighty car-warrior.

description: The utterance of the untruth by Yudhishthira
sn: पुत्रव्यसनसंतप्तो निराशो जीवितेऽभवत्॥ आगस्कृतमिवात्मानं पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। ऋषिवाक्येन मन्वानः श्रुत्वा च निहतं सुतम्॥ विचेताः परमोद्विग्नो धृष्टद्युम्नमवेक्ष्य च। योद्धु नाशक्नुवद् राजन् यथापूर्वमरिदम्॥
en: Overwhelmed with grief on account of the supposed death of his son, gave way to despair. Hearing the words of the sages, great offender against the illustrious Pandavas. Now hearing that his son had been slain he became completely senseless and filled with anxiety at the sight of Dhristadyumna, O monarch, the chastiser of foes was not able to fight as before.

description: The battle between Drona and Dhristadyumna
sn: संजय उवाच दृष्ट्वा परमोद्विग्नं शोकोपहतचेतसम्। पाञ्चालराजस्य सुतो धृष्टद्युम्नः समाद्रवत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then beholding Drona, Drona, exceedingly anxious and depressed at heart in consequence of grief, the son of the Panchala king, viz., Dhristadyumna assailed him.

description: The battle between Drona and Dhristadyumna
sn: य इष्ट्वा मनुजेन्द्रेण दुपदेन महामखे। लब्धो द्रोणविनाशाय समिद्धाद्धव्यवाहनात्॥
