sn: धनंजय गुरुं श्रुत्वा तत्र नादं सुभीषणम्। क एप कौरवान् दीर्णानवस्थाप्य महारथः॥ निवर्तयति युद्धार्थं मृधे देवेश्वरो यथा।
en: I ask you who is this mighty car-warrior that rallying this terrible and agitated host like the lord of the celestials themselves, is leading it to the charge.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच उद्यम्यात्मानमुग्राय कर्मणे वीर्यमास्थिताः॥ धमन्ति कौरवाः शङ्खान् यस्य वीर्यं समाश्रिताः!
en: Arjuna said He depending upon whose prowess the Kauravas, having addressed themselves to the accomplishment of ficrce deeds, are blowing their conches and facing us with firmness.

sn: यत्र ते संशयो राजन् न्यस्तशस्रे गुरौ हते॥ धार्तराष्ट्रानवस्थाप्य क एष नदतीति हि।
en: He about whom you entertain doubts as to who he may be who, having rallied the troops of the son of Dhritarashtra, that had fled from the fall of the weaponless Drona, is now uttering terrible roars.

sn: ह्रीमन्तं तं महाबाहुं मत्तद्विरदगामिनम्॥ आख्यास्याम्युग्रकर्माणं कुरूणामभयंकरम्।
en: He who is possessed of bashfulness and mighty arms, who has the gait of an infuriate elephant, who possesses a face like that of tiger, who achieves fierce feats and gives assurances of safety to the Kurus,

sn: यस्मिञ्जाते ददौ द्रोणो गवां दशशतं धनम्॥ ब्राह्मणेभ्यो महाहेभ्यः सोऽश्वत्थामैष गर्जति।
en: He, upon whose birth Drona distributed a thousand kine among Brahmanas of highworth, he, Oking, is Ashvatthaman who is thus roaring.

sn: जातमात्रेण वीरेण येनोच्चैःश्रवसा यथा॥ द्वेषता कम्पिता भूमिर्लोकाश्च सकलास्रयः।
en: As soon as he was born that hero ncighed like Uchhaisravas and thereby caused the three words to tremble.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वान्तर्हितं भूतं नाम तस्याकरोत् तदा॥ अश्वत्थामेति सोऽौष शूरो नदति पाण्डव।
en: Having heard that sound, an invisible being, master, ascribed to him the Ashvatthman, (horse-voiced). That brave warrior, O son of Pandu, is roaring today.

sn: यो ह्यनाथ इवाक्रम्य पार्षतेन हतस्तथा॥ कर्मणा सुनृशंसेन तस्य नाथो व्यवस्थितः।
en: He, who has been slain like one helpless by the son of Prisata, by a cruel and deceitful means, yonder stands the protector of that one. name

sn: गुरुं ते यत्र पाञ्चाल्य: केशपक्षे परामृशत्॥ तन्न जातु क्षमेद् द्रौणिर्जानन् पौरुषमात्मनः।
en: The Panchala prince dragged my poor preceptor by the locks of his hair. Certainly Drona's son will not forgive that act of his, aware as he is of his own manliness and resources.

sn: उपचीर्णो गुरुर्मिथ्या भवता राज्यकारणात्॥ धर्मज्ञेन सता नाम सोऽधर्मः सुमहान् कृतः।
en: You also, O king, has spoken a lie to the preceptor, being driven to it by the desire for obtaining the kingdom. Conversant with the rules of morality and of pious nature, you have indeed perpetrated a great sin.

sn: चिरं स्थास्यति चाकीर्तिस्त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे॥ रामे वालिवधाद् यद्वदेवं द्रोणे निपातिते।
en: Like that hanging in Rama on consequence of his slaying Bali, the infamy hanging on you in consequence of the slaughter of Drona will be cternal in the three worlds with their mobile and immobile creations.

sn: सर्वधर्मोपपन्नोऽयं स मे शिष्यश्च पाण्डवः॥ नायं वदति मिथ्येति प्रत्ययं कृतवांस्त्वयि।
en: “The son of Pandu is accomplished in all virtues; moreover he is my disciple, he will never tell me a lic.' Thinking this Drona believed what you then said.

sn: स सत्यकञ्चुकं नाम प्रविष्टेन ततोऽनृतम्॥ आचार्य उक्तो भवता हत: कुञ्जर इत्युत।
en: You have spoken an uniruth veiled in the garb of truth, to the preceptor, adding the word cicphant thereto.

sn: ततः शस्रं समुत्सृज्य निर्ममो गतचेतनः॥ आसीत् सुविह्वलो राजन् यथा दृष्टस्त्वया विभुः।
en: Thereupon the Puissant Drona, laid his weapons aside and became indifferent to every carthly concern. He was senseless and as you have seen was overwhelmed with a swoon.

sn: स तु शोकसमाविष्टो विमुखः पुत्रवत्सलः॥ शाश्वतं धर्ममुत्सृज्य गुरुः शस्त्रेण घातितः।
en: It was then that his disciple, transgressing all morality, slew his preceptor, filled with do you you with affection for his son and unwilling to fight and possessed by grief.

sn: न्यस्तशस्रमधर्मेण घातयित्वा गुरुं भवान्॥ रक्षत्विदानीं सामात्यो यदि शक्तोऽसि पार्षतम्।
en: Having slain by a deceitful means your preceptor who had laid his weapons aside, now your counsellors, protect the son of Prishata, if indeed, you arc equal to the task.

sn: ग्रस्तमाचार्यपुत्रेण क्रुद्धेन हतबन्धुना॥ सर्वे वयं परित्रातुं न शक्ष्यामोऽद्य पार्षतम्।
en: Today all of us conjointly will not be able to protect the son of Prisata, who has been as it were devoured by the son of Drona, filled with fury on account of his sire's slaughter.

sn: सौहार्दै सर्वभूतेषु यः करोत्यतिमानुषः। सोऽद्य केशग्रहं श्रुत्वा पितुर्धक्ष्यति नो रणे॥
en: He, who ever treated all creatures with exceeding compassion, even he, hearing that his sire was dragged by the hair will today consume us in battle.

sn: विक्रोशमाने हि मयि भृशमाचार्यगृद्धिनि। अपाकीर्य स्वयं धर्मं शिष्येण निहतो गुरुः॥
en: Setting at naught all dictates of morality, the pupil has slaughtered his preceptor, although I exclaimed at the top of my voice, protesting that the preceptor should not be slain.

sn: यदा गतं वयो भूयः शिष्टमल्पतरं च नः। तस्येदानी विकारोऽयमधर्मोऽयं कृतो महान्॥
en: We have already passed away the greater part of our lives; the lease of life left to us is indeed very short; even that short period is blotted by his sinful act (perpetrated in the maturity of our years).

sn: पितेव नित्यं सौहार्दात् पितेव हि च धर्मतः। सोऽल्पकालस्य राजस्य कारणाद् घातितो गुरुः॥
en: Drona, in consequence of the affection he cherished for us, was indeed like our father. By the ordinances of the holy texts, he was also our father. Yet such a preceptor of ours has been slain by ourselves, for the sake of enjoying sovereignty for a short period.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रेण भीष्माय द्रोणाय च विशाम्पते। विसृष्टा पृथिवी सर्वा सह पुत्रैश्च तत्परैः॥
en: Dhritarashtra, O monarch, gave the earth to Bhishma and Drona and what was more, he entrusted them with the lives of his sons.

sn: सम्प्राप्य तादृशीं वृत्तिं सत्कृतः सततं परैः। अवृणीत सदा पुत्रान् मामेवाभ्यधिकं गुरुः॥
en: Though thus esteemed and endowed with such an honorarium by the foe, yet the preceptor looked upon us like his own son.

sn: अवेक्षमाणस्त्वां मां च न्यस्तास्त्रश्चाहवे हतः। न त्वेनं युध्यमानं वै हन्यादपि शतक्रतुः॥
en: The preceptor, incapable of suffering any reduction in strength and energy, was only slain in battle, when he believing in your words laid his weapons aside. While engaged in fight even Indra the performer of hundred sacrifices could not have defeated him.

sn: तस्याचार्यस्य वृद्धस्य द्रोहो नित्योपकारिणः। कृतो ह्यनार्चरस्माभी राज्यार्थे लुब्धवुद्धिभिः॥
en: Even such a preceptor, venerable in years and devoted to our welfare, has been injured by ourselves, who have betaken to mean conduct for securing sovereignty.

sn: अहो बत महत् पापं कृतं कर्म सुदारुणम्। यद् राज्यसुखलोभेन द्रोणोऽयं साधु घातितः :॥
en: Alas, alas, what a heinous sin and a ruthless act have we perpetrated, for, tempted by the desire for enjoying the pleasures of sovereignty, we have slain our venerable preceptor.

sn: पुत्रान् भ्रातॄन् पितॄन् दाराञ्जीवितं चैव वासविः। त्यजेत् सर्वं मम प्रेम्णा जानात्येवं हि मे गुरुः॥
en: My preceptor had all along been under the impression, that I, Vasava's son, son, could abandon all, my sires, brothers, sons, wives and even life itself, for his sake, in consequence of the affection I bear for him.

sn: स मया राज्यकामेन हन्यमानो झुपेक्षितः। तस्मादर्वाक्शिरा राजन् प्राप्तोऽस्मि नरकं प्रभो॥
en: And yet, alas, longing for sovereignty, I have neglected him when he was on the point of being slaughtered. For this act, O king, I have already been condemned to hell, being covered with great ignominy.

sn: ब्राह्मणं वृद्धमाचार्यं न्यस्तशस्त्रं महामुनिम्। घातयित्वाद्य राज्यार्थे मृतं श्रेयो न जीवितम्॥
en: It is better that I should die then live, inasmuch as I have today, out of a desire for obtaining sovereignty, suffered my old preceptor to be slain, who was a Brahmana and a great Muni and who moreover had laid his weapons aside at the time.

sn: संजय उवाच अर्जुनस्य वचः श्रुत्वा नोचुस्तत्र महारथाः। अप्रियं वा प्रियं वापि महाराज धनंजयम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing the words of Arjuna O mighty monarch, the mighty car-warriors of the Pandava host spoke neither agreeable or disagreeable words in reply to Dhananjaya.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाबाहुर्भीमसेनोऽभ्यभाषत। कुत्सयन्निव कौन्तेयमर्जुनं भरतर्षभ॥
en: But the mighty Bhimasena filled with wrath, spoke, O foremost of the Bharatas, these words for reproaching Kunti's son Arjuna.

sn: मुनिर्यथारण्यगतो भाषसे धर्मसहितम्। न्यस्तदण्डो यथा पार्थं ब्राह्मणः संशितव्रतः॥
en: 'You are preaching the rules of morality, like a Muni living in the woods or like a Brahmana of austere observances who has cutoff all connections with this world.

sn: क्षतत्राता क्षताज्जीवन क्षन्ता स्त्रीष्वपि साधुषु। क्षत्रियः क्षितिमाप्नोति क्षिप्रं धर्मं यशः श्रियः॥
en: Saving others from injuries, defending himself against wounds and injuries and showing forgiveness to women and the pious, a Kshatriya soon obtains the (rule of the) earth, as also religious merit, fame and prosperity.

sn: स भवान् क्षत्रियगुणैर्युक्तः सर्वैः कुलोद्वहः। अविपश्चिद् यथा वाचं व्याहरन् नाद्य शोभसे॥
en: Yourself endowed with all the desirable qualifications of a Kshatriya, O perpetuator of your race, it looks odd that you should speak like one ignorant of the duties of your order.

sn: पराक्रमस्ते कौन्तेय शक्रस्येव शचीपतेः। न चाति वर्तसे धर्मं वेलामिव महोदधिः॥
en: O son of Kunti, your prowess resembles that of Shakra the lord of Sachi. You never pass beyond the limits of morality even as the ocean never transgresses its banks.

sn: न पूजयेत् त्वां को न्वद्य यत् त्रयोतशवार्षिकम्। अमर्षं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा धर्ममेवाभिकाङ्क्षसे॥
en: What person is there, who will not applaud you, you who, having forgotten the animosity fanned and kept alive for the last thirteen years, are solicitous for observing the precepts of morality?

sn: दिष्ट्या तात मनस्तेऽद्य स्वधर्ममनुवर्तते। आनृशंस्ये च ते दिष्ट्या बुद्धिः सततमच्युत॥
en: Surely it is fortunate, O sire, that your heart today bends towards virtue. It is also fortune that your understanding today inclines towards showing compassion, you of undeteriorating fame.

sn: यत् तु धर्मप्रवृत्तस्य हृतं राज्यमधर्मतः। द्रौपदी च परामृष्टा सभामानीय शत्रुभिः॥
en: Although you are so cager to observe the dictates of righteousness, yet your kingdom was snatched away from you most unrighteously. Your wife Draupadi having been dragged into the open court, was insulted by your foe.

sn: वनं प्रवाजिताश्चास्म वल्कलाजिनवाससः। अनर्हमाणास्तं भावं त्रयोदश समा: परैः॥
en: We were exiled, with barks of trees or skins of animals for our cloth and cover. Through undeserving of such a wretched plight, yet we were compelled to wear out thirteen long years in that condition.

sn: एतान्यमर्षस्थानानि मर्षितानि मयानघ। ! क्षत्रधर्मप्रसक्तेन सर्वमेतदनुष्ठितम्॥
en: You, O sinless one, have overlooked all these crying causes that call for revenge. Devoted as you are to perform the duties of Kshatriyas, you have quietly tolerated all these.

sn: तमधर्ममपाकृष्टं स्मृत्वाद्य सहितस्त्वया। सानुबन्धान् हनिष्यामि क्षुद्रान् राज्यहरानहम्॥
en: Keeping alive the memory of all these wrongs inflicted on us, we have come here today with you, to avenge them. (But as you are so righteous) I myself will slay all these mean fellows who snatched away our kingdonm.

sn: त्वया हि कथितं पूर्वं युद्धाभ्यागता वयम्। घटामहे यथाशक्तिं त्वं तु नोऽद्य जुगुप्ससे॥
en: You had said before "Addressing ourselves in battle. we shall exert to the utmost of our abilities." But now you are reproaching us.

sn: स्वधर्मं नेच्छसे ज्ञातुं मिथ्यावचनमेव ते। भयार्दितानामस्माकं वाचा मर्माणि कृन्तसि॥
en: You are now seeking virtue. So you have falsified the words you had said before. Afflicted as we are with fear, you take this opportunity for cutting us to the quick with your harsh words.

sn: वपन् ब्रणे क्षारमिव क्षतानां शत्रुकर्शन। विदीर्यते मे हृदयं त्वया वाक्शल्यपीडितम्॥
en: Like one applying salt on the sores of wounded men, Ogrinder of your foes. Afflicted with your dagger-like words, my heart is on the point of bursting open.

sn: अधर्ममेनं विपुलं धार्मिकः सन् न बुद्ध्यसे। यत् त्वमात्मानमस्मांश्च प्रशस्यान् न प्रशंससि॥
en: Pious as you are, you do not know the nature of impiety, for you do not offer us applause though we are worthy of it.

sn: वासुदेवे स्थिते चापि द्रोणपुत्रं प्रशंससि। यः कलां षोडशी पूर्णां धनंजय न तेऽर्हति॥
en: When Vasudeva himself is here, praise you the son of Drona, who, ODhananjaya, is not a match for even a sixteenth part of yourself?

sn: स्वयमेवात्मानो दोषान् ब्रुवाणः किन्न लज्जसे। दारयेयं महीं क्रोधाद् विकिरेयं च पर्वतान्॥
en: Disclosing your own weakness, it is strange that you fell no shame! I can rend this earth open in rage and split the very mountains.

sn: आविध्यैतां बदां गुर्वी भीमां काञ्चनमालिनीम्। गिरिप्रकाशान् क्षितिजान् भञ्जयमनिलो यथा॥
en: Whirling that heavy and terrible mace of fierce aspect decked with garlands of gold. Like a violent tempest, I can break down trees resembling huge mountains.

sn: द्रावयेयं शरैश्चापि सेन्द्रान् देवान् समागतान्। सराक्षसगणान् पार्थ सासुरोरगमानवान्॥
en: I can with my arrows rout and crush the assembled host of the celestials led by Indra himself, O Partha, assisted though they be by the Rakshasas, thc Asuras, Snakes and human bcings.

sn: स त्वमेवंविधं जानन् भ्रातरं मां नरर्षभ। द्रोणपुत्राद् भयं कर्तुं नार्हस्यमितविक्रम॥
en: Knowing, O foremost of men, me your brother, to be such, you should not, O you of infinite prowess, entertain any fear from the son of Drona.

sn: अथवा तिष्ठ बीभत्सो सह सर्वैः सहोदरैः। अहमेनं गदापाणिर्जेष्याम्येको महाहवे॥
en: Cr, O Vibhatsu, stay here with all these foremost of men and behold me, alone and armed with the mace, conquer him in fierce battle.

sn: ततः पाञ्चालराजस्य पुत्रः पार्थमथाब्रवीत्। संक्रुद्धमिव नर्दन्तं हिरण्यकशिपुर्हरिम्॥
en: Like the Daitya king Hiranyakasipu addressing the roaring and enraged Hari, the son of the king of the Panchalas addressed

sn: धृष्टद्युम्न उवाच बीभत्सो विप्रकर्माणि विदितानि मनीषिणाम्। याजनाध्यापने दानं तथा यज्ञप्रतिग्रहौ॥
en: Dhristadyumna said O Vibhatsu, the intelligent sages of yore have prescribed these-viz., conducting sacrifices on behalf of others, teaching, charity, celebration of sacrifices and acceptance of gifts to be the duties of the Brahmanas.

sn: षष्ठमध्ययनं नाम तेषां कस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितः। हतो द्रोणो मया ह्येवं किं मां पार्थ विगर्हसे॥
en: The sixth duty is study. To which of these six was that Drona who has been slain by me devoted? Wherefore then do you reproach me, O son of Pritha?

sn: अपक्रान्तः स्वधर्माच क्षात्रधर्मं व्यपाश्रितः। अमानुषेण हन्त्यस्मानस्रेण क्षुद्रकर्मकृत्॥
en: Transgressing the duties of his own order and observing those of the Kshatriyas that perpetrator of wicked deeds used to slaughter us with his celestials weapons.

sn: तथा माया प्रयुञ्जानमसह्यं ब्राह्मणब्रुवम्। माययैव विहन्याद् यो न युक्तं पार्थ तत्र किम्॥
en: Professing himself to be Brahmana, he used to injure us deceitfully; he has now been slain by deceitful means; O son of Pritha, what is there wrong in this?

sn: तस्मिस्तथा मया शस्ते यदि द्रौणायनी रुषा। कुरुते भैरवं नादं तत्र किं मम हीयते॥
en: Upon the punishment of Drona, (which he richly deserved), if his son, out of anger, utier such loud roars, what do I lose by them?

sn: न चाद्भुतमिदं मन्ये यद द्रौणियुद्धसंज्ञया। घातयिष्यति कौरव्यान् परित्रातुमशक्नुवन्॥
en: There is nothing wonderful in the fact that Drona's son leading the Kauravas in battle, will cause their destruction, being himself unable to protect them.

sn: यच मां धार्मिको भूत्वा ब्रवीषि गुरुघातिनम्। तदर्थमहमुत्पन्नः पाञ्चाल्यस्य सुतोऽनलात्॥
en: Now you have turned a virtuous person and are accusing me with the slaughter of any preceptor. bu do you now know that it was for those that I was born as son of Panchaia kig en sprung out of fire.

sn: यस्य कार्य मकार्यं वा युध्यतः स्यात् समं रणे। तं कथं ब्राह्मणं ब्रूयाः क्षत्रियं वा धनंजय॥
en: How, O Dhananjaya, can you designate him a Brahmana or a Kshatriya, who when engaged in fight used to look upon fair and unfair acts with an equal eye?

sn: यो ह्यनस्रविदो हन्याद् ब्रह्मास्त्रैः क्रोधमूछितः। सर्वोपायैर्न स कथं वध्यः पुरुषसत्तम॥
en: He, who furious in rage, used to slay with his Brahma weapons even those who are unacquainted with the use of weapons, O foremost of men, why should he not be slain by us by every means in our power?

sn: विधर्मिणं धर्मविद्भिः प्रोक्तं तेषां विषोपमम्। जानन् धर्मार्थतत्त्वज्ञ किं मामर्जुन गर्हसे॥
en: One fallen off from the duties of his order, has been said, by the righteousness, to be equal to poison. Knowing this, you who are conversant with the precepts of morality, why do you blame me, O Arjuna.

sn: नृशंसः स मयाऽऽक्रम्य रथ एव निपातितः। तन्मामनिन्द्यं बीभत्सो किमर्थं नाभिनन्दसे॥
en: That ruthless warrior, being assailed by me, has been overthrown and slain by me. O Vibhatsu, why do you not then congratulate myself on whom actually no blame hangs?

sn: कालानलसमं पार्थ ज्वलनार्कविषोपमम्। भीमं द्रोणशिरश्छिन्नं न प्रशंससि मे कथम्॥
en: ) Partha, I have lopped off Drona's dreadful head, resembling the All-destroying Fire or the burning Sun or the most virulent poison. Why do you not then applaud an act that is worthy of applause?

sn: योऽसौ ममैव नान्यस्य वान्धवान् युधि जनिवान्। छित्त्वापि तस्य मूर्धानं नैवास्मि विगतज्वरः॥
en: He who used 10 slay my kinsmen exclusively in baitle and of no one else, lopping off his head, have I not been freed from a terrible fever (of revenge) that used to burn me without remission.

sn: तच्च मे कृन्तते मर्म यन्न तस्य शिरो मया। निषादविषये क्षिप्तं जयद्रथशिरो यथा।॥
en: This fact that I have not thrown his head, like that of Jayadratha, into the omissions of the Nisadhas, is corroding he core of my heart.

sn: अथावधश्च शूत्रणामधर्मः श्रूयतेऽर्जुन। क्षत्रियस्य हि धर्मोऽयं हन्याद्धन्येत वा पुनः॥
en: It has been heard, O Arjuna, that, without slaying one's enemies one incurs sin. The duty of a Kshatriya is to stay or to be slain.

sn: स शत्रुनिहतः संख्ये मया धर्मेण पाण्डव। यथा त्वया हतः शूरो भगदत्तः पित्तुः सखा॥
en: O son of Pandu, Drona was my enemy; and therefore it is righteous that I have slain him; and thus you have slain your father's friend, king Bhagadatta.

sn: पितामहं रणे हत्वा मन्यसे धर्ममात्मनः। मया शत्रौ हते कस्मात् पापे धर्मं न मन्यसे॥
en: When you slew your aged grandsire, you thought it your duty to do so. But when I have slain my wicked foe, why should it not be regarded as my duty?

sn: सम्बन्धावनतं पार्थ न मां त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि। स्वगात्रकृतसोपानं निष्ण्णमिव दन्तिनम्॥
en: It behoves you not to speak to me in this way-ine who can raise my hand against you in consequence of the relationship I bear to you and who am therefore like prostrate elephant with ladder against its body, for helping puny creatures to get on its back.

sn: क्षमामि ते सर्वमेव वाग्व्यतिक्रममर्जुन। द्रौपद्या द्रौपदेयानां कृते नान्येन हेतुना॥
en: I forgive your abusive language, O Arjuna, for the sake of Draupadi and her sons and not for any other cause.

sn: कुलक्रमागतं वैरं ममाचार्येण विश्रुतम्। तथा जानात्ययं लोको न यूयं पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥
en: It is well-known that the hostility I bore to the preceptor was bequeathed to me by my sire. Every one in the words knows it but you sons of Pandu feign to be ignorant of it.

sn: नानृती पाण्डवो ज्येष्ठो नाहं वाधार्मिकोर्जुन। शिष्यद्रोही हत: पापो युध्यस्व विजयस्तव॥
en: The eldest son of Pandu is not a liar nor am I a sinful wretch, 0 Arjuna. The wicked Drona used to injure his pupils. He has been slain by me. Now fight and victory will be yours. The eldest son of Pandu is not a liar nor am I a sinful wretch, 0 Arjuna. The wicked Drona used to injure his pupils. He has been slain by me. Now fight and victory will be yours.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच साङ्गा वेदा यथान्यायं येनाधीता महात्मना। यस्मिन् साक्षाद् धनुर्वेदो ह्रीनिषेवे प्रतिष्ठितः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Thai high-souled person who had duly studied the Vedas and their auxiliaries, he who had mastered this entire science of arms and who possessed modesty.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: यस्य प्रसादात् कुर्वन्ति कर्माणि पुरुषर्षभाः। अमानुषाणि संग्रामे देवैरसुकराणि च॥
en: That Drona son of mighty sage, who had been insulted by the low-minded, cruel and mcan Dhristadyumna the slayer of his preceptor.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: तस्पिन्नाक्रुश्यति द्रोणे समक्षं पापकर्मणा। नीचात्मना नृशंसेन क्षुद्रेण गुरुघातिना॥
en: That Drona through whose grace the foremost of men still achieve superhuman feats difficult of being achieved even by the gods and the Asuras.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: नामर्षं तत्र कुर्वन्ति धिक् क्षात्रं धिगमर्षिताम्। पार्थाः सर्वे च राजानः पृथिव्यां ये धनुर्धराः॥
en: When that Drona suffered such an insult at the hands of that most sinful Dhristadyumna under the very eyes of all the warriors present, was there no Kshatriya who was then inspired with wrath? Fie on the Kshatriya order and fie on wrath itself!

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: श्रुत्वा किमाहुः पाञ्चाल्यं तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय।
en: Tell me, O Sanjaya, what did the Parthas or the other kings of the earth, all illustrious warriors, say, having heard the words of the Panchala prince?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: संजय उवाच श्रुत्वा द्रुपदपुत्रस्य ता वाचः क्रूरकर्मणः॥ तूष्णीं बभूवू राजानः सर्व एव विशाम्पते।
en: Sanjaya said Hcaring those words of the ruthless son of Drupada, O king, all the rulers of the earth remained silent.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: अर्जुनस्तु कटाक्षेण जिह्यं विप्रेक्ष्य पार्षतम्॥ सबाष्यंमतिनिःश्वस्य धिग्धिगित्येव चाब्रवीत्।
en: But Arjuna only casting side glances at Prisata's son and sighing and shedding copious tears said 'fie, fie.'

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: युधिष्ठिरश्च भीमश्च यमौ कृष्णस्तथापरे॥ आसन् सुव्रीडिता राजन् सात्यकिस्त्वब्रवीदिदम्।
en: Yudhishthira and Bhima and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) and Krishna himself were overwhelmed with shame, o king. Then Satyaki spoke these words-

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: नेहास्ति पुरुषः कश्चिद् य इमं पापपूरुषम्। भाषमाणमकल्याणं शीघ्रं हन्यान्नराधमम्।
en: Is there nobody that will quickly dispatch this sinful, low and cursed wretch, even when he is thus speaking?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: एते त्वां पाण्डवाः सर्वे कुत्सयन्ति विकुत्सया॥ कर्मणा तेन पापेन श्वपाकं ब्राह्मण इव।
en: Like the Brahmanas blaming a Chandala, all these Pandavas are reproaching you for your having perpetrated his sinful act.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: एतत् कृत्वा महत् पापं निन्दितः सर्वसाधुभिः॥ न लज्जसे कथं वक्तुं समिति प्राप्य शोभनाम्।
en: Having perpetrated the most sinful act and condemned by the pious, do you not fell ashamed to open your lips in this august assemblage?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: कथं च शतधा जिह्वा न ते मूर्धा च वीर्यते॥ गुरुमाक्रोशतः क्षुद्र न चाधर्मेण पात्यसे।
en: O despicable wretch, why did not your tongue and your cursed head go off into thousand fragments, when you were on the point of slaying your preceptor? Why were you not smitten down by that sinful act?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: वाच्चस्त्वमसि पार्थश्च सर्वेश्चान्धकवृष्णिभिः॥ यत् कर्म कलुषं कृत्वा श्लाघसे जनसंसदि।
en: You richly merit the condemnation of the Parthas and all the Vrishnis and the Andhakas inasmuch as perpetrating this sinful act, you are boasting of it in the presence of this august assembly.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: अकार्यं तादृशं कृत्वा पुनरेव गुरुं क्षिपन्॥ वध्यस्त्वं न त्वयार्थोऽस्ति मुहूर्तमपि जीवता।
en: Having committed the most heinous act of sin, you further reveal you hatred for the preceptor. For this you deserve to be slain; there is no use in sparing your life even for a moment.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: कस्त्वेतद् व्यवसेदार्यस्त्वदन्यः पुरुषाधम॥ निगृह्य केशेषु वधं गुरोर्धर्मात्मनः सतः।
en: What other sinful wretch, except yourself, will dare cause the virtuous preceptor's death, holding him by his hoary locks?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: सप्तावरे तथा पूर्वे बान्धवास्ते निमज्जिताः॥ यशसा च परित्यक्तास्त्वां प्राप्य कुलपांसनम्।
en: Having obtained you-the disgrace to their race-for their descendant, seven generations before you and seven after, in your race, have sunk in hell, being deprived of their glory.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: उक्तवांश्चापि यत् पार्थे भीष्मं प्रति नरर्षभम्॥ तथान्तो विहितस्तेन स्वयमेव महात्मना।
en: You have accused Partha that foremost of men with the slaughter of Bhisma. But this latter illustrious personage has hiinself caused his own destruction.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: तस्यापि तव सोदर्यो निहन्ता पापकृत्तमः॥ नान्यः पाञ्चाल्यपुत्रेभ्यो विद्यते भुवि पापकृत्।
en: Indeed that vilest of wretches viz., your uterine brother Sikhandin, was the cause of Bhisma's death. Really there is no one more sinful on the face of the earth, than the sons of Panchala king

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: स चापि सृष्टः पित्रा ते भीष्मस्यान्तकरः किल॥ शिखण्डी रक्षितस्तेन स च मृत्युर्महात्मनः।
en: Your father had begotten Sikhandin for the slaughter of Bhishma. As regards Arjuna he only protected your brother when he caused the death of the high-souled Bhishma.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: पञ्चालाश्चलिता धर्मात् क्षुद्रा मित्रगुरुदुहः॥ त्वां प्राप्य सहसोदर्यं धिक्कृतं सर्वसाधुभिः।
en: The Panchalas have gone astray from the paths of rectitude and like despicable wretches they are injuring their friends and their preceptors, only for having obtained yourself and your brother, hated by the pious, among themselves.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: पुनश्चेदीदृशीं वाचं मत्समीपे वदिष्यसि॥ शिरस्ते पोथयिष्यामि गदया वज्रकल्पया।
en: If you again speak such words before re, I shall knock down your head with a mace resembling the bolt of heaven.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: त्वां च ब्रह्महणं दृष्ट्वा जनः सूर्यमवेक्षते॥ ब्रह्महत्या हि ते पापं प्रायश्चित्तार्थमात्मनः।
en: Stained as you are with the sin of Brahmanicide, people looking at you the slayer of a Brahmana, have to look at the Sun for purifying themselves.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: पाञ्चालक सुदुर्वृत्त ममेव गुरुमग्रतः॥ गुरोर्गुरुं च भूयोऽपि क्षिपन्नैव हि लजसे।
en: Ill-mannered wretch of Panchala, villifying my own preceptor in the first instance and then my preceptor's preceptor, why don't you feel ashamed?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: तिष्ठ तिष्ठ सहस्वैकं गदापातमिमं मम॥ तव चापि सहिष्येऽहं गदापाताननेकशः।
en: 'Wait, Wait.' Bear but this single stroke of my mace. I will bear many strokes of that of yours."

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: सात्वतेनैवमाक्षिप्तः पार्षतः परुषाक्षरम्॥ संरब्धं सात्यकिं प्राह संक्रुद्धः प्रहसन्निव।
en: Thus reproached by that scion of the Satvata race, Prisata's son inspired with wrath, addressed these harsh words to the enraged Satyaki.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: धृष्टद्युम्न उवाच श्रूयते श्रूयते चेति क्षम्यते चेति माधव॥ सदानार्योऽशुभः साधु पुरुषं क्षेप्तुमिच्छति।
en: Dhristadyumna said O you of Madhu's race, I have heard you speak. But I forgive you; yourself sinful and impious, you desire to throw odium on the righteous?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: क्षमा प्रशस्यते लोके न तु पापोऽर्हति क्षमाम्॥ क्षमावन्तं हि पापात्मा जितोऽयमिति मन्यते।
en: Forgiveness is a praise worthy virtue, buy sinful wretches do not deserve it. A wicked fellow regards him who shows forgiveness as powerless (lit : conquered).

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: स त्वं क्षुद्रसमाचारो नीचात्मा पापनिश्चयः॥ आकेशाग्रान्नखाग्राच्च वक्तव्यो वक्तुमिच्छसि।
en: Ill-behaved, of low mind and sinful resolutions, you are condemnable from the end of your hair to the tip of your toe. Yet do you desire to censure others?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: यः स भूरिश्रवााश्छिन्नभुजः प्रायगतस्त्वया॥ वार्यमाणेन हि हतस्ततः पापतरं नु किम्।
en: What act can be more unrighteous than that perpetrated by you when, repeatedly prevented, you slew Bhurisrava, whose arm was lopped off and who had betaken to the Praya Yoga?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: गाहमानो मया द्रोणो दिव्येनास्त्रेण संयुगे॥ विसृष्टशस्रो निहतः किं तत्र क्रूर दुष्कृतम्।
en: Arranging his troops in order Drona was fighting with his celestial weapons he laid aside his weapons and I slew him o crooked one, what is there improper in this?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: अयुध्यमानं यस्त्वाजौ तथा प्रायगतं मुनिम्॥ छिन्नबाहुं परैर्हन्यात् सात्यके स कथं वेदत्।
en: How can he, O Satyaki, censure such as act, who himself has slain his opponent, desisted from battle an opponent that was sitting in Praya Yoga and whose arm was cut-off by another.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: निहत्य त्वां पदा भूमौ च विकर्षति वीर्यवान्।॥ किं तदा न निहंस्येनं भूत्वा पुरुषसत्तमः।
en: That puissant opponent of yours, careered on the field having thrown you down with the stroke of his feet. Foremost if you were of all male beings why did you not then slay him?

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: त्वया पुनरनार्येण पूर्वं पार्थेन निर्जितः॥ यदा तदा हतः शूरः सौमदत्तिः प्रतापवान्।
en: When Partha had already vanquished him, it was only then that by an unfair means you slew the puissant son of Somadatta.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: यत्र यत्र तु पाण्डूनां द्रोणो द्रावयते चमूम्॥ किरछरसहस्राणि तत्र तत्र प्रयाम्यहम्।
en: In whatever quarter Drona had sought to rout the troops of the Pandavas, in that quarter I proceeded, shooting myriads of shafts.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: स त्वमेवंविधं कृत्वा कर्म चाण्डालवत् स्वयम्॥ वक्तुमर्हसि वक्तव्यः कस्मात् त्वं परुषाण्यथ।
en: Having yourself perpetrated an act worthy of a Chandala only, it is strange that you desire to censure me in such a vile language.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: कर्ता त्वं कर्मणो ह्यस्य नाहं वृष्णिकुलाधम॥ पापानां च त्वमावासः कर्मणां मा पुनर्वदा
en: You are the perpetrator of vile acts and not I, O vilest of the Vrishni race. You are the hotbed of sin. Do not again blame this deed of mine.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: जोषमास्ख न मां भूयो वक्तुमर्हस्यतः परम्॥ अधरोत्तरमेतद्धि यन्मां त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि।
en: Hold your tongue. It is improper that you shall move after this. I give you this reply from my own lips, you should not address me any longer.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: अथ वक्ष्यसि मां मौाद् भूयः परुषमीदृशम्॥ गमयिष्यामि बाणैस्त्वां युधि वैवस्वतक्षयम्।
en: If again, out of folly you speak such harsh words to me, I shall dispatch you to the abode of Death with my own arrows.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: न चैवं मूर्ख धर्मेण केवलेनैव शक्यते॥ तेषामपि ह्यधर्मेण चेष्टितं शृणु यादृशम्।
en: Once cannot overcome his foes, O fool, solely through fair means. Hear how our opponents also acted unfairly.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: वञ्चितः पाण्डवः पूर्वमधर्मेण युधिष्ठिरः॥ द्रौपदी च परिक्लिष्टा तथा धर्मेण सात्यके।
en: Pandu's eldest son Yudhishthira was a few years back cheated unfairly (out of his own kingdom) and O Satyaki, Draupadi was also most vilely insulted.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: प्रव्राजिता वनं सर्वे पाण्डवाः सह कृष्णया॥ सर्वस्वमपकृष्टं च तथाधर्मेण बालिश।
en: The Pandavas with Krishna their wife were also exiled to the woods and fool, all their possessions were robbed out of them by unrighteous means.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: अधर्मेणापकृष्टश्च मद्रराजः परेरितः॥ अधर्मेण तथा बाल: सौभद्रो विनिपातितः।
en: The king of the Madras was again weaned away from our side by an act of unrighteousness by the foe, unfairly also was the tender son of Subhadra slain.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: इतोऽप्यधर्मेण हतो भीष्मः परपुरंजयः॥ भूरिश्रवा ह्यधर्मेण त्वया धर्मविदा हतः।
en: Now for the Pandavas, the grand-father of the Kurus, Bhishma was slain by an act of unrighteousness. Bhurisrava was unfairly slain by your very justicel-oving self.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: एवं परैराचरितं पाण्डवेयैश्च संयुगे॥ रक्षमाणैर्जयं वीरैर्धर्मज्ञैरपि सात्वत।
en: Thus, O you of the Salvata race, the heroic Pandavas and the Kurus have both acted sinfully for victory in battle, although they are all conversant with the rules of morality.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: दुर्जेयः स परो धर्मस्तथाधर्मश्च दुर्विदः॥ युध्यस्व कौरवैः सार्धं मा गा पितृनिवेशनम्।
en: Thus morality is a mystery, as also immorality is difficult of being ascertained. Fight on with the Kauravas and do not return to the home of your fathers.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: संजय उवाच एवमादीनि वाक्यानि क्रूराणि परुषाणि च॥ श्रावितः सात्यकिः श्रीमानाकम्पित इवाभवत्।
en: Sanjaya said Addressed in such ruthless and harsh words, the handsome Satyaki trembled from hcad to foot.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा क्रोधताम्राक्षः सात्यकिस्त्वाददे गदाम्॥ विनिःश्वस्य यथा सर्पः प्रणिधाय रथे धनुः।
en: Hearing those words Satyaki with his eyes coppery in rage, laid his bow aside on the car and breathing like a snake he grasped his mace.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: ततोऽभिपत्य पाञ्चाल्यं संरम्भेणेदमब्रवीत्॥ न त्वां वक्ष्यामि परुषं हनिष्ये त्वां वधक्षमम्।
en: Then advancing furiously upon the Panchala prince he said-"I shall not waste my harsh words on you any longer, but I shall crush you, as you richly deserve to be slaughtered."

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा महाबलममर्षणम्॥ पाञ्चाल्यायाभिसंक्रुद्धमन्तकायान्तकोपमम्।
en: Beholding the puissant Satyaki rush, from wrath and desire for revenge, at the Panchala prince, like Death against a match of his.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: चोदितो वासुदेवेन भीमसेनो महाबलः॥ अवप्लुत्य रथात् तूर्णं बाहुभ्यां समवारयत्।
en: The mighty Bhima urged by Vasudeva, quickly jumped down from his chariot and caught hold of him by the arms.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: द्रवमाणं तथा क्रुद्धं सात्यकिं पाण्डवो बली॥ प्रस्पन्दमानमादाय जगाम बलिनं बलात्।
en: The puissant Satyaki, who was then furiously rushing (at Dhristadyumna) advanced a few steps, dragging after him the mighty son of Pandu, who was trying to withhold him.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: स्थित्वा विष्टभ्य चरणौ भीमेन शिनिपुङ्गवः॥ निगृहीतः पदे षष्ठे बलेन बलिनां वरः।
en: Then Bhima firmly planting his feet, succeeded in stopping that foremost of all beings endowed with strength viz., that illustrious scion or Shini's race.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: अवरुह्य रथात् तूर्णं ध्रियमाणं बलीयसा॥ उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा सहदेवो विशाम्पते।
en: Then, Oking, Sahadeva jumping down from his car, addressed Satyaki held in check by the strong arms of Bhima, in these soothing

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: अस्माकं पुरुषव्याघ्र मित्रमन्यन्न विद्यते॥ परमन्धकवृष्णिभ्यः पञ्चालेभ्यश्च मारिष।
en: O foremost of men, we possess not friends dearer to ourselves, then the Andhakas, the Vrishnis and the Panchalas, O descendant of Madhu's race.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: तथैवान्धकवृष्णीनां तथैव च विशेषतः॥ कृष्णस्य च तथास्मत्तो मित्रमन्यन्न विद्यते।
en: Similarly the Andhakas and the Vrishnis, specially Krishna among the latter, cannot have any friend dearer than ourselves.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: पञ्चालानां च वार्ष्णेय समुद्रान्तां विचिन्वताम्॥ नान्यदस्ति परं मित्रं यथा पाण्डववृष्णयः।
en: The Panchalas also, O scion of the Vrishni race, will not be able to find friends dearer to themselves than the Vrishnis and the Pandavas, even if they search the whole earth to the very boundaries of the seas.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: स भवानीदृशं मित्रं मन्यते च यथा भवान्॥ भवन्तश्च यथास्माकं भवतां च तथा वयम्।
en: You are a dear friend to this prince and even such is he to you. You are to us even as we are to you.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: स एवं सर्वधर्मज्ञ मित्रधर्ममनुस्मरन्॥ नियच्छ मन्यु पाञ्चाल्यात् प्रशाम्य शिनिपुङ्गवा
en: Versed in the rules of duty, restrain your anger having the prince of the Panchalas for its object, remembering the duties that you owe to you friends.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: पार्षतस्य क्षमं त्वं वै क्षमतां पार्वतश्च ते॥ वयं क्षमयिताश्च किमन्यत्र शमाद् भवेत्।
en: Forgive the son of Prisata, let him also forgive you. We will also practise forgiveness. What other virtue can be equal to forgiveness!

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: प्रशाम्यमाने शैनेय सहदेवेन मारिष॥ पाञ्चालराजस्य सुतः प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्।
en: When, O sire, Sahadeva was thus pacifying the grandson of Shini, the son of the Panchala king thus smilingly spoke:मुञ्चमुञ्च शिनेः पौत्रं भीम युद्धमदान्वितम्॥

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: आसादयतु मामेष धराधरमिवानिलः।
en: Bhima, let the grandson of Shini, so proud of his prowess in battle, he released. Let him encounter me like the wind encountering the mountains.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: यावदस्य शितैर्बाणैः संरम्भं विनयाम्यहम्॥ युद्धश्रद्धां च कौन्तेय जीवितं चास्य संयुगे।
en: I shall smother his wrath with my sharp arrows, as also his itching for battle; O son of Kunti, let me deprive him of his life in battle.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: किं नु शक्यं मया कर्तुं कार्यं यदिदमुद्यतम्॥ सुमहत् पाण्डुपुत्राणामायान्त्येते हि कौरवाः।
en: I am alone competent to achieve the mighty task the sons of Pandu have undertaken, heavy though it may be. Yonder come the Kauravas.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: अथवा फाल्गुनः सर्वान् वारयिष्यति संयुगे॥ अहमप्यस्य मूर्धानं पातयिष्यामि सायकैः।
en: Or Phalguna himself will hold all of them in check. Let me cut-off this one's head with my arrows.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: मन्यते छिन्नबाहुं मां भूरिश्रवसमाहवे॥ उत्सृजैनमहं चैनमेष वा मां हनिष्यति।
en: He takes me for Bhurisravas with his arm lopped off. Leave him, Either I will slay him or he shall slay me

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: शृण्वन् पाञ्चालवाक्यानि सात्यकिः सर्पवच्छसन्॥६५ भीमबाह्वन्तरे सक्तो विस्फुरत्यनिशं बली।
en: Hearing the words of the Panchala prince the mighty Satyaki breathing like a snake, began to swell even within the embrace of Bhima's arms.

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: तौ वृषाविव नर्दन्तौ बलिनौ बाहुशलिनौ॥ त्वरया वासुदेवश्च धर्मराजश्च मारिष।
en: When those strong-armed and mighty heroes were thus roaring at each other like two bulls, O sire, Vasudeva and the son of Dharma Yudhishthira,

description: The rage of Dhristadyumna and Satyaki
sn: यत्नेन महता वीरौ वारयामासतुस्ततः॥ निवार्य परमेष्वासौ कोपसंरक्तलोचनौ। युयुत्सूनपरान् संख्ये प्रतीयुः क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥
en: With great difficulty restrained those two heroes. Thus restraining those two mighty bowmen, whose eyes were red in rage, the foremost of the Kshatriyas advanced desirous of meeting the foe in battle.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: संजय उवाच
en: were

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: ततः स कदनं चक्रे रिपूणां द्रोणनन्दनः। युगान्ते सर्वभूतानां कालसृष्ट इवान्तकः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereafter the son of Drona began to crush his foes like the Destroyer at the end of the Yuga slaughtering all creatures.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: ध्वजदुमं शस्त्रशृङ्गं हतनागमहाशिलम्। अश्वकिंपुरुषाकीर्णं शरासनलतावृतम्॥ क्रव्यादपक्षिसंघुष्टं भूतयक्षगणाकुलम्। निहत्य शात्रवान् भल्लैः सोऽचिनोद् देहपर्वतम्॥
en: Slaying his foes with his broad-headed shafts, he caused a mountain by corpses, whose trees were constituted by standards, peaks by weapons, stones by slain elephants; which teemed with Kimpurusas formed by slain horses, which was covered with creepers constituted by bows, whose cranes constituted by flesh-cating animals, and which was full of birds formed by the ghosts.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: ततो वेगेन महता विनद्य स नरर्षभः। प्रतिज्ञां श्रावयामास पुनरेव तवात्मजम्॥
en: Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, once more exclaiming aloud with great force, Ashvatthaman made your son to hear his vow.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: यस्माद् युध्यन्तमाचार्य धर्मकञ्चुकमास्थितः। मुञ्च शस्रमिति प्राह कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: "Inasmuch as Kunti's son Yudhishthira, disguised in the garb of righteousness, has spoken to the fighting Preceptor, saying 'lay you weapons aside.'

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: तस्मात् सम्पश्यतस्तस्य द्रावयिष्यामि वाहिनीम्। विद्राव्य सर्वान् हन्तास्मि जाल्मं पाझाल्यमेव तु॥
en: For that reason I shall crush his army even before his very eyes. Shattering the ranks of the hostile aimy I will slay the sinful son of the Panchala king

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: सर्वानेतान् हनिष्यामि यदि योत्स्यन्ति मा रणे। सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि परिवर्तय वाहिनीम्॥
en: I will slay them all in battle if they only face me in battle. This I speak to you for sooth. Let the army be rallied and return to the charge.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा तव पुत्रसतु वाहिनीं पर्यवर्तयत्। सिंहनादेन महता व्यपोह्य सुमहद् भयम्॥
en: Hearing those words of Drona's son your son rallied the troops, having dispelled their fear by uttering a loud leonine shout.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: ततः समागमो राजन् कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः। पुनरेवाभवत् तीव्रः पूर्णसागरयोरिव॥
en: Thereupon O king, once more a terrible encounter took place between the armies of the Kurus and the Pandavas, resembling the dashing of two oceans at full tide.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: संरब्धा हि स्थिरीभूता द्रोणपुत्रेण कौरवाः। उदग्राः पाण्डुपञ्चाला द्रोणस्य निधनेन च॥
en: The Kouravas were rallied and incited with revenge by Drona's son, the Pandavas and Panchalas were also excited to fury by having slain the Preceptor Drona.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: तेषां परमहृष्टानां जयमात्मनि पश्यताम्। संरब्धानां महावेगः प्रादुरासीद् विशाम्पते॥
en: The violence of tie collision was indeed very great collision that then took place on the field of battle between those warriors all of whom were filled with joy and rage and inspired with hopes of victory.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: यथा शिलोच्चये शैलः सागरे सागरो यथा। प्रतिहन्येत राजेन्द्र तथाऽऽसन् कुरुपाण्डवाः॥
en: The collision between the Kurus and the Pandavas was like that between a mountain against a mountain or an ocean against an Ocean.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: ततः शङ्खसहस्राणि भेरीणामयुतानि च। अवादयन्त संहृष्टाः कुरुपाण्डवसैनिकाः॥
en: Then the Kuru and the Pandava troops filled with delight struck up ten thousand Bheris and blew a thousand conches.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: यथा निर्मथ्यमानस्य सागरस्य तु निःस्वनः। अभवत् तव सैन्यस्य सुमहानद्भुतोपमः॥
en: Like the deep roar of the ocean when it was churned, a tremendous din was then heard in those troops. son

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: प्रादुश्चक्रे ततो द्रौणिरस्त्रं नारायणं तदा। अभिसंधाय पाण्डूनां पञ्चालानां च वाहिनीम्॥
en: Thereafter Drona's invoked into existence the Narayana weapon and he aimed it at the armies of the Panchalas and the Pandavas.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: प्रादुरासंस्ततो बाणा दीप्ताग्राः खे सहस्रशः। पाण्डवान् क्षपयिष्यन्तो दीप्तास्याः पन्नगा इव॥
en: Then thousands of arrows with blazing tips appeared in the welkin looking like snakes of fiery mouth, that continued to agitate the Pandavas.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: दिशः खं च सैन्यं च समावृण्वन् महाहवे। मुहूर्ताद् भास्करस्येव लोके राजन् गभस्तयः॥
en: Those arrows, O king, like the rays of the Sun, in that terrible battle, covered all the quarters of heaven, the sky and the Pandava soldiers.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: तथापरे द्योतमाना ज्योतीषीवामलाम्बरे। प्रादुरासन् महाराज कार्णायसमया गुडाः॥
en: Then, O ruler of earth, countless iron balls appeared there like lustrous orbs in the cloudless firmament.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: चतुश्चक्रा द्विचक्राश्च शतघ्यो बहुला गदाः। चक्राणि च क्षुरान्तानि मण्डलानीव भास्वतः॥
en: Shataghnis of four or two wheels and a large number of maces and sharp-edged discs, effulgent like the sun also appeared there.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: शस्राकृतिभिराकीर्णमतीव पुरुषर्षभ। दृष्ट्वान्तरिक्षमाविग्नाः पाण्डुपाञ्चालसृञ्जयाः॥
en: Then beholding the firmament densely covered by those weapons, O foremost of the Bharatas, the Pandavas, the Sanjaya and the Panchalas became exceedingly anxious.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: यथा यथा ह्युयुध्यन्त पाण्डवानां महारथाः। तथा तथा तदस्रं वै व्यवर्धत जनाधिप॥
en: The weapon showed its exceeding strength in all those places, O ruler of men, where the great car-warriors of the Pandava hosts contended furiously.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: वध्यमानास्तदास्त्रेण तेन नारायणेन वै। दह्यमानानलेनेव सर्वतोऽभ्यर्दिता रणे॥
en: Slaughtered by the Narayana weapon, as if burnt down by a raging fire, the troops of the Pandavas were greatly distressed in battle.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: यथा हि शिशिरापाये दहेत् कक्षं हुताशनः। तथा तदस्रं पाण्डूनां ददाह ध्वजिनीं प्रभो॥
en: O lord, as fire consumes a heap of dry grass in summer, even so did that weapon begin to consume the army of the Pandavas.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: आपूयर्ममाणेनास्त्रेण सैन्ये क्षीयति च प्रभो। जगाम परमं त्रासं धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: The very virtuous king Yudhishthira was filled with fear, as his army became reduced in number and that weapon swelled in its fury.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: द्रवमाणं तु तत् सैन्यं दृष्ट्वा विगतचेतनम्। मध्यस्थतां च पार्थस्य धर्मपुत्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Then behoiding the army broken and deprived of its senses and seeing the indifference of Partha, the very virtuous king Yudhishthira thus spokeधृष्टद्युम्न पलायस्व सह पाञ्चालसेनया।

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: सात्यके त्वं च गच्छस्व वृष्ण्यन्धकवृतो गृहान्॥
en: “Fly, O you Dhristadyumna, taking with you all the Panchala divisions; you also, Satyaki, go away with all Vrishnis and the Andhkas.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: वासुदेवोऽपि धर्मात्मा करिष्यत्यात्मनः क्षमम्। श्रेयो ह्यपदिशत्येष लोकस्य किमुतात्मनः॥
en: The high-souled son of Vasudeva will look after his own safety. Indeed he is competent to protect all the worlds; what to speak of his own self; it is useless to give him advise.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: संग्रामस्तु न कर्तव्यः सर्वसैन्यान् ब्रवीमि वः। अहं हि सह सौदर्येः प्रवेक्ष्ये हव्यवाहनम्॥
en: Ye soldiers, I command you to desist from the battle. I with my uterine brothers, am going to enter into a burning fire. was

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: भीष्मद्रोणार्णवं तीर्खा संग्रामे भीरुदुस्तरे। विमजिष्यामि सलिले सगणो द्रौणिगोष्पदे॥
en: In this war so dreadful to the timid, having crossed the oceans represented by Bhima and Drona, I shall now sink in the water contained in the vestige of a calf-foot represented by the son of Drona.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: कामः सम्पद्यतामस्य बीभत्सोराशु मा प्रति। कल्याणवृत्तिराचार्यो मया युधि निपातितः॥
en: Let king Duryodhana today attain the fruition of his desires for I have slain the prcccptor who used to treat us so mercifully and like a friend.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: येन बालः स सौभद्रो युद्धानामविशारदः। समर्थैर्बहुभिः क्रूरैर्घातितो नाभिपालितः॥
en: Indeed this preceptor with the help of other cruel warriors, slew and did not spare the son of Subhadra of tender years, who unacquainted with the modes of warfare.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: येनामिब्रुवता प्रश्नं तथा कृष्णा सभां गता। उपेक्षिता सपुत्रेण दासभावं नियच्छती॥
en: This preceptor with his son remained indifferent, when Krishna, dragged into the open court and about to be made a slave, asked him to speak the truth in answer to her question.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: जिघांसुर्धार्तराष्ट्रश्च श्रान्तेष्वश्वेषु फाल्गुनम्। कवचेन तथा गुप्तो रक्षार्थं सैन्धवस्य च॥
en: This preceptor gave an impenetrable armour to Duryodhana, when all other warriors were worn out with fatigue, in order that the latter may slay Phalguna and effect the protection of Jayadratha.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: येन ब्रह्मास्रविदुषा पञ्चालाः सत्यजिन्मुखाः। कुर्वाणा मजये यत्न समूला विनिपातिताः॥
en: Indeed this preceptor with his Brahma weapon exterminated that whole Panchala division under Satyajit, who had been entering to bestow victory on me.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: येन प्रव्राज्यमानाच राज्याद् वयमधर्मतः। निवार्यमाणा नु वयं नानुयातास्तदैषिणः॥
en: Indeed this preceptor did not with-hold his permission though solicited to do so by our friends, when despoiled of our kingdom we were on the point of being exiled into the woods.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: योऽसावत्यन्तमस्मासु कुर्वाणः सौहृदं परम्। हतस्तदर्थे मरणं गमिष्यामि सबान्धवः॥
en: Alas, such a well-wishing friend of ours who did us many good turns has been slain by us. For his sake I shall with all my relatives embrace death."

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: एवं ब्रुवति कौन्तेये दाशार्हस्त्वरितस्ततः। निवार्य सैन्यं बाहुभ्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: When the son of Kunti was thus speaking, the scion of the Dasaratha race, Krishna, forbidding the troops with the waive of his

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: शीघ्रं न्यस्यत शस्त्राणि वाहेभ्यश्चावरोहत। एष योगोऽत्र विहितः प्रतिषेधे महात्मना॥
en: “Quickly throw aside your weapons and come down from your vehicles; even this is the means ordained by the high-souled Narayana, for baffling this weapon.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: द्विपाश्वस्यन्दनेभ्यश्च क्षितिं सर्वेऽवरोहत। एवमेतन्न वो हन्यादस्त्रं भूमौ निरायुधान्॥
en: All of you quickly alight from the elephants, horses and chariots in the ground. Thus when you stand in earth laying aside your arms this weapon will not slay you.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: यथा यथा हि युध्यन्ते योधा ह्यस्रमिदं प्रति। तथा तथा भवन्त्येते कौरवा बलवत्तराः॥
en: Whatever you shall contend in battle for checking the force of this weapon, in all those places the Kouravas will become more powerful than

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: निक्षेपस्यन्ति च शस्राणि वाहनेभ्योऽवरुह्य ये। तान्नैतदत्रं संग्रामे निहनिष्यति मानवान्॥
en: Those men, on the other hand, who will thrown down their weapons and alight form their vehicles, will not be slain by this weapon. yourselves.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: ये त्वेतत्प्रतियोत्स्यन्ति मनसापीह केचन। निहनिष्यति तान् सर्वान् रसातलगतानपि॥
en: Those who will even think of contending against this weapon will be slain by it, even if he takes shelter within the bowels of the earth."

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: ते वचस्तस्य तच्छ्रुत्वा वासुदेवस्य भारत। ईषुः सर्वे समुत्स्रष्टुं मनोभिः करणेन च॥
en: Hearing those words of Vasudeva, O Bharata, all the Pandava warriors laid their weapons aside and discarded all thoughts of battle from their mind.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: तत उत्स्स्रष्टुकामांस्तानस्राण्यालक्ष्य पाण्डवः। भीमसेनोऽब्रवीद् राजन्निदं संहर्षयन् वचः॥
en: But Bhimasena the son of Pandu, beholding the Pandavas about to abandon their weapons had thus spoken, O king, gladdening the hearts of all.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: न कथंचन शस्राणि मोक्तव्यानीह केनचित्। अहमावारयिष्यामि द्रोणपुत्रास्रमाशुगैः॥
en: None should throw his weapons aside. I shall check the weapon of Drona's son with my swift-flying arrows.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: गदयाप्यनया गुा हेमविग्रहया रणे। कालवत् प्रहरिष्यामि द्रौणेरस्त्रं विशातयन्॥
en: Or armed with this heavy mace adorned with gold I shall career on the field of battle like Death himself, quelling the weapons of Drona's son.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: न हि मे विक्रमे तुल्यः कश्चिदस्ति पुमानिह। यथैव सवितुस्तुल्यं ज्योतिरन्यन्न विद्यते॥
en: Just as no luminary is equal to the Sun in effulgence, so there is no man equal to me in prowess and strength.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: पश्यतेमौ हि मे बाहू नागराजकरोपमौ। समर्थौ पर्वतस्यापि शैशिरस्य निपातने॥
en: Look at my strong arms like the trunks of the foremost of elephants. They are capable of pulling down the crests of the Himavat mountain.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: नागायुतसमप्राणो ह्यहमेको नरेष्विह। शको यथाप्रतिद्वन्द्वो दिवि देवेषु विश्रुतः॥
en: Among men, I am I am the only person possessed of the strength of ten thousand elephants, Like Shakra among the gods in heaven, I am known to be matchless on earth.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: अद्य पश्यत मे वीर्यं बाह्वोः पीनांसयोर्युधि। ज्वलमानस्य दीप्तस्य द्रौणेरस्त्रस्य वारणे॥
en: Today you shall behold the strength of my arms and my expanded chest, when I shall exert in resisting the effulgent and burning weapon of Drona's son.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: यदि नारायणास्रस्य प्रतियोद्धा न विद्यते। अद्यैतत् प्रतियोत्स्यामि पश्यत्सु कुरुपाण्डुषु॥
en: If there is none who can venture to contend against the Narayana weapon, let then the Kurus and the Pandavas behold how I shall quell that weapon.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: अर्जुनार्जुन बीभत्सो न न्यस्यं गाण्डिवं त्वया। शशाङ्कस्येव ते पङ्को नैर्मल्यं पातयिष्यति॥
en: O Arjuna, O Arjuna, O Vibhatsu, it befits you not to lay aside your Gandiva-bow; then from yourself the halo of glory will be gone, like that of moon leaving it."

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: अर्जुन उवाच भीम नारायणस्त्रे मे गोषु च ब्राह्मणेषु च। एतेषु गाण्डिवं न्यस्यमेतद्धि व्रतमुत्तमम्॥
en: Arjuna said O Bhima, my great vow is that I shall not use the Gandiva-bow against Brahmanas the kine and the Narayana weapon and against these I shall lay it aside.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्तस्ततो भीमो द्रोणपुत्रमरिंदमम्। अभ्ययान्मेघघोषेण रथेनादित्यवर्चसा॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus spoken to, Bhima, that subduer of foes, rushed against Drona's son on a chariot whose clatter resembled the roll of thunder and whose effulgence out-vied that of the Sun.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: य एनमिषुजालेन लघुत्वाच्छीघ्रविक्रमः। निमेषमात्रेणासाद्य कुन्तीपुत्रोऽभ्यवाकिरत्॥
en: Endued with great activity and prowess, the son of Kunti possessed as he was of extreme lightness of hands, succeeded in covering Drona's son with a net-work of arrows, within the twinkling of the eye.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: ततो द्रौणिः प्रहस्यैनं द्रवन्तमभिभाष्य च। अवाकिरत् प्रदीप्ताग्रैः शरैस्तैरभिमन्त्रितैः॥
en: Thereupon Drona's son smilingly eyeing the rushing Bhima, challenged him and then covered him with arrows of keen points and inspired with Mantras.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: पन्नगैरिव दीप्तास्यैर्वमद्भिर्व्वलनं रणे। अवकीर्णोऽभवत् पार्थः स्फुलिङ्गैरिव काञ्चनैः॥
en: Then Pritha's son shrouded with those shafts, of blazing points like the mouths of snakes, capable of penetrating to the very vitals, looked as if covered with speaks of gold.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: तस्य रूपमभूद् राजन् भीमसेनस्य संयुगे। खद्योतैरावृतस्येव पर्वतस्य दिनक्षये॥
en: Then O king, the appearance of Bhimasena became like that of a mountain surrounded by the fire-flies at the close of day.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: तदस्रं द्रोणपुत्रस्य तस्मिन् प्रतिसमस्यति। अवर्धत महाराज यथाग्निरनिलोद्धतः॥
en: That weapon of Drona's son directed against Bhimasena, swelled in fury like a conflagration assisted by the wind.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: विवर्धमानमालक्ष्य तदा भीमविक्रमम्। पाण्डुसैन्यमृते भीमं समहद् भयमाविशत्॥
en: Beholding that weapon of great energy increasing in its fury, the troops of the Pandavas were filled with fear with the exception of Bhima.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: ततः शस्त्राणि ते सर्वे अवारोहन रथेभ्यश्च हस्त्यश्वेभ्यश्च सवशः॥
en: Thereupon laying aside their celestial weapons on the ground they alighted on all sides from their cars and their horses.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: तेषु निक्षिप्तशस्त्रेषु वाहनेभ्यश्च्युतेषु च। तदस्रवीर्यं विपुलं भीममूर्धन्यथापतत्॥ समुत्सृज्य महीतले।
en: Thus when they had thrown their weapons down and when they had alighted from their vehicles and horses, that weapon of immense energy flew towards the head of Bhima.

description: The laying aside of weapons by the Pandava troops
sn: हाहाकृतानि भूतानि पाण्डवाश्च विशेषतः। भीमसेनमपश्यन्त तेजसा संवृतं तथा॥
en: All creatures cried Oh and Alas and specially the Pandavas did so, at the sight of Bhimasena wrapt in the effulgence of that weapons.

sn: संजय उवाच भीमसेनं समाकीर्णं दृष्ट्वास्रेण धनंजयः। तेजसः प्रतिघातार्थं वारुणेन समावृणोत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding Bhimasena completely shrouded by that weapon, Dhananjaya for quenching the fire produced by it shot the Varuna weapon.

sn: नालक्षयत तत् कश्चिद् वारुणास्रेण संवृतम्। अर्जुनस्य लघुत्वाच संवृतत्वाच तेजसः॥
en: The lightness with which Arjuna shot the weapon and also the fiery energy of the Narayana weapon, rendered it impossible for any body to perceive that Bhima was also protected by the Varuna weapon.

sn: साश्वसूतरथो भीमो द्रोणपुत्रास्रसंवृतः। अग्नावग्निरिव न्यस्तो ज्वालामाली सुदुर्दशः॥
en: His steeds, charioteers and horses covered by the effulgence of the weapon of Drona's son, Bhima then was incapable of being looked at like a blazing fire within another blazing fire.

sn: यथा रात्रिक्षये राजन् ज्योतीष्यस्तागिरि प्रति। समापेतुस्तथा बाणा भीमसेनरथं प्रति॥
en: Just as at the close of night, all the luminaries fly towards the western hills, so also the shafts of Drona's son flew towards the car of Bhima.

sn: स हि भीमो रथश्चास्य हयाः सूतश्च मारिष। संवृता द्रोणपुत्रेण पावकान्तर्गताऽभवन्॥
en: Then thus shrouded with shafts by Drona's son, Bhima, his horses and charioteer, O sire, looked as if wrapt in the flames of a blazing fire.

sn: यथा दग्ध्वा जगत् कृत्स्नं समये सचराचरम्। गच्छेद् वह्निर्विभोरास्यं तथास्रं भीममावृणोत्॥
en: Just as at the hour of the universal annihilation the All-destroying. Fire having burnt down the mobile and immobile creation proceeds to enter the mouth of the Creator, so also that weapon Proceeded to enter the body of Bhima.

sn: सूर्यमग्निः प्रविष्टः स्याद् यथा चाग्निं दिवाकरः। तथा प्रविष्टं तत् तेजो न प्राज्ञायत पाण्डवः॥
en: Just as the fire penetrating into the Sun or the Sun penetrating into the fire, cannot be perceived by any body so also that weapon entering into Bhima's body could not be perceived.

sn: विकीर्णमस्रं तद् दृष्ट्वा तथा भीमरथं प्रति। उदीर्यमाणं द्रौणिं च निष्प्रतिद्वन्द्वमाहवे॥
en: Beholding then that weapon swelling in fury near Bhima's chariot and also Drona's son career unopposed on the field of battle.

sn: सर्वसैन्यं च पाण्डूनां न्यस्तशस्रमचेतनम्। युधिष्ठिरपुरोगांश्च विमुखांस्तान् महारथान्॥
en: And seeing that all the warriors of the Pandava army had laid their weapons aside and that all the mighty car-warriors headed by Yudhishthira had turned their faces away from the field.

sn: अर्जुनो वासुदेवश्च त्वरमाणौ महाद्युती। अवप्लुत्य रथाद् वीरौ भीममाद्रवतां ततः॥
en: Those two brave heroes of great effulgence viz., Arjuna and Vasudeva, then jumping down from their chariot, ran towards Bhima.

sn: ततस्तद् द्रोणपुत्रस्य तेजोऽस्रबलसम्भवम्। विगाह्य तौ सुबलिनौ माययाऽऽविशतां तथा॥
en: Those two puissant persons then plunging into the energy born of the might of Ashvatthaman's weapon, betook to their power of illusion.

sn: न्यस्तशस्त्रौ ततस्तौ तु नादहत् सोऽस्रजोऽनलः। वारुणास्रप्रयोगाच वीर्यवत्वाच कृष्णयोः॥
en: The fire of that weapon failed to burn them down in consequence of their having laid aside their weapons, as also in consequence of their great personal prowess and the energy of the Varuna weapon.

sn: ततश्चकृषतुर्भीमं सर्वशस्त्रायुधानि च। नारायणास्रशान्त्यर्थं नरनारायणौ बलात्॥
en: Then Nara and Narayana began forcibly to take off all weapons from Bhima and to drag him out of the fire of that weapon.

sn: आकृष्यमाणः कौन्तेयो नदत्येव महारवम्। वर्धते चैव तद् घोरं द्रौणेरस्त्रं सुदुर्जयम्॥
en: Thus dragged the puissant son of Kunti (Bhima) began to roar aloud, where-upon the invincible weapon of Drona's son also swelled in its fury.

sn: तमब्रवीद वासुदेवः किमिदं पाण्डुनन्दन। वार्यमाणोऽपि कौन्तेय यद् युद्धान्न निवर्तसे॥
en: Then the son of Vasudeva, addressing (Bhima) said-"O delighter of Pandu, what do you mean? Why don't you desist from fighting though repeatedly for bidden to do so.

sn: यदि युद्धेन जेयाः स्युरिमे कौरवनन्दनाः। वयमप्यव युध्येम तथा चेमे नरर्षभाः॥
en: Had it been possible now to vanquish the Kouravas in battle, then we as well as all these forest of men would have fought against them.

sn: रथेभ्यस्त्ववतीर्णाः स्म सर्व एव हि तावकाः। तस्मात् त्वमपि कौन्तेय रथात् तूर्णमपाक्रम॥
en: All your troops have alighted from their chariots, so you also, O son of Kunti, quickly come down from your chariot.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु तं कृष्णो रथाद् भूमिमवर्तयत्। निःश्वसन्तं यथा नागं क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनम्॥
en: Having thus spoken, Krishna dragged him down on the earth, him who was breathing like a snake with eyes coppery with rage.

sn: यदपकृष्टः स रथान्नयासितश्चायुधं भुवि। ततो नारायणास्रं तत् प्रशान्तं शत्रुतापनम्॥
en: When he was thus dragged down from the car, when he was thus compelled to lay his weapons aside, the Narayana weapon, capable of burning down the foe, became pacified.

sn: संजय उवाच तस्मिन् प्रशान्ते विधिना तेन तेजसि दुःसहे। बभूवुर्विमलाः सर्वा दिशः प्रदिश एव च॥
en: Sanjaya said When the unbearable energy of that weapon was pacified by this means, all the quarters, subsidiary and cardinal, became clear.

sn: प्रववुश्च शिवा वाताः प्रशान्ता मृगपक्षिणः। वाहनानि च हृष्टानि प्रशान्तेऽस्त्रे सुदुर्जये॥
en: Auspicious winds began to blow and animals and birds became quiet. The steeds and elephants as well as the warriors themselves became cheerful, O ruler of men.

sn: व्यपोढे च ततो घोरे तस्मिस्तेजसि भारत। बभौ भीमो निश्पाये धीमान् सूर्य इवोदितः॥
en: O Bharata, when that dreadful energy was thus stilled, the intelligent Bhima shone like the Sun at the close of night.

sn: हतशेषं बलं तत् तु पाण्डवानामतिष्ठत। अस्रव्युपरमासृष्टं तव पुत्रजिघांसया॥
en: Then the remnant of the Pandava troops, beholding the subsidence of the energy of that weapon, again stood ready in order to slay your sons.

sn: व्यवस्थिते बले तस्मिन्नने प्रतिहते तथा। दुर्योधनो महाराज द्रोणपुत्रमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: When the Pandava army was rallied and rearranged and when the Narayana weapon was thus counteracted, your son Duryodhana, O king, addressing Drona's son said these

sn: अश्वत्थामन् पुनः शीघ्रमस्त्रमेतत् प्रयोजय। अवस्थिता हि पञ्चालाः पुनरेते जयैषिणः॥
en: O Ashvatthaman, once more discharged that weapon quickly, for the Panchalas, desirous of victory, have again rallied.

sn: अश्वत्थामा तथोक्तस्तु तव पुत्रेण मारिष। सुदीनमभिनिःश्वस्य राजानमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus spoken to your son, Ashvatthaman, O sire, depressed and sighing heavily, replied to the king sayingनैतदावर्तते राजन्नत्रं द्विर्नोपपद्यते।

sn: आवृतं हि निवर्तेत प्रयोक्तारं न संशयः॥
en: That weapon never comes back, neither, O king, can it be used twice. If invoked back it will slay the person invoking it.

sn: एष चास्रप्रतीघातं वासुदेवः प्रयुक्तवान्। अन्यथा विहितः संख्ये वधः शत्रोर्जनाधिप॥
en: The son of Vasudeva counter acted the weapon by what means you have seen. For this, O ruler of men, the extermination of the foe has not been accomplished in battle.

sn: पराजयो वा मृत्युर्वा श्रेयान् मृत्युन निर्जयः। विजिताश्चारयो होते शस्रोत्सर्गान्मृतोपमाः॥
en: The worst in battle is either defeat or death. Death is better than defeat. The enemy compelled to lay aside their weapons are vanquished and more than dead.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच आचार्यपुत्र यद्येतद् द्विरस्त्रं न प्रयुज्यते। अन्यैर्गुरुघ्ना वध्यन्तामस्त्रैरस्त्रविदां वर॥
en: Duryodhana said O son of my preceptor, O you foremost of those versed in the science of weapons, if this weapon cannot be used twice, then slay those slayers of their preceptor with other mighty weapons.

sn: त्वयि शस्राणि दिव्यानि त्र्यम्बके चामितौजसि। इच्छतो न हि ते मुच्येत् संक्रुद्धो हि पुरंदरः॥
en: Like the three-eyed Mahadeva of infinite energy, you possess all the celestial weapons; even the enraged Indra cannot escape you alive if you wish it not.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तस्मिन्नने प्रतिहते द्रोणे चोपधिना हते। तथा दुर्योधनेनोक्तो द्रौणिः किमकरोत् पुनः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When Drona had been slain with underhand measures and when that weapon of his son had been baffled, what did Ashvatthman, urged on by Duryodhana do?

sn: दृष्ट्वा पार्थांश्च संग्रामे युद्धाय समुपस्थितान्। नारायणास्रनिर्मुक्तांश्चरतः पृतनामुखे॥
en: Beholding the Parthas, rally for the fight and freed from the influence of the Narayana weapon and career at the head of their divisions.

sn: संजय उवाच जानन् पितुः स निधनं सिंहलाङ्गुलकेतनः। सक्रोधो भयमुत्सृज्य सोऽभिदुद्रावे पार्षतम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Remembering the unfair slaughter of his sire, Drona's son, having the lion's tail as a device on his banner, casting off all fear and filled with fury rushed upon the son of Prisata.

sn: अभिद्रुत्य च विंशत्या क्षुद्रकाणां नरर्षभ। पञ्चभिश्चातिवेगेन विव्याध पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Thus assailing him, that foremost of men, at first pierced his enemy with twenty small arrows and then again with five others, with great force.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्ततो राजन् ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्। द्रोणपुत्रं त्रिषष्ट्या तुराजन् विव्याध पत्रिणाम्॥
en: Thereupon, O king, Dhristadyumna pierced Drona's son looking like a blazing fire, with four and sixty winged arrows.

sn: सारथिं चास्य विंशत्या स्वर्णपुङ्खः शिलाशितैः। हयांश्च चतुरोऽविध्यचतुर्भिनिशितैः शरैः॥
en: He pierced the latter's charioteer with twenty shafts furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone and the four horses with four very sharp arrows.

sn: विद्धवा विद्ध्वानदद् द्रौणिं कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्। आददे सर्वलोकस्य प्राणानिव महारणे॥
en: Repeatedly piercing the son of Drona and making the earth trembling with his roars, Dhristadyumna appeared to be engaged in taking away the lives of every body on the face of earth in that dreadful battle.

sn: पार्षतस्तु बली राजन् कृतास्रः कृतनिश्चयः। द्रौणिमेवाभिदुद्राव मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्॥
en: O king, the son of Prisata was endued with prowess and accomplished in weapons and of resolute purposes. He rushed upon the son of Drona making death to be the final goal.

sn: ततो बाणमयं वर्षं द्रोणपुत्रस्य मूर्धनि। अवासृजदमेयात्मा पाञ्चाल्यो रथिनां वरः॥
en: Then that foremost of car-warriors, that prince of the Panchalas, of unmeasurable depth of soul, poured a veritable shower of arrows on the head of Drona's son.

sn: तं द्रौणिः समरे क्रुद्धं छादयामास पत्रिभिः। विव्याध चैनं दशभिः पितुर्वधमनुस्मरन्। ४१॥
en: Thereupon Drona's covered that enraged hero with innumerable winged shafts and remembering the slaughter of his sire, pierced him with ten shafts.

sn: द्वाभ्यां च सुविसृष्टाभ्यां क्षाभ्यां ध्वजकार्मुके। छित्त्वा पाञ्चालराजस्य द्रौणिरन्यैः समार्दयत्॥
en: Cutting down the bow and the standard of the Panchala prince with two well-directed razor-headed arrows, the son of Drona began to afflict the former with numerous other shafts.

sn: व्यश्वसूतरथं चैनं द्रौणिश्चक्रे महाहवे। तस्य चानुचरान् सर्वान् क्रुद्धः प्राद्रावयच्छरैः॥
en: Drona's son deprived his opponent of his horses, chariot and driver; and he, worked up with rage, covered the latter's followers with myriads of arrows.

sn: ततः प्रदुद्रवे सैन्यं पाञ्चालानां विशाम्पते। सम्भ्रान्तरूपमार्तं च न परस्परमैक्षत॥
en: Thereupon, O ruler of men, the troops of the Panchalas broke and fled away; their appearance reflected fear and they were greatly distressed and mangled with shaft-cuts. son arrows

sn: दृष्ट्वातु विमुखान् योधान् धृष्टद्युम्नं च पीडितम्। शैनेयोऽचोदयत् तूर्णं रथं द्रौणिरथं प्रति॥
en: Then beholding the troops turning back and Dhristadyumna greatly afflicted, the graidson of Shini, directed his chariot to be driven in haste towards that of Drona's son.

sn: अष्टभिर्निशितैर्बाणैरश्वत्थामानमार्दयत्। विंशत्या पुनराहत्य नानारूपैरमर्षणः॥
en: With eight sharp afflicted Ashvatthman; they once more he pierced his revengeful adversary with another twenty shafts of diverse shape.

sn: विव्याध च तथा सूतं चतुर्भिश्चतुरो हयान्। धनुर्ध्वजं च संयत्तश्चिच्छेद कृतहस्तवत्॥
en: He pierced his opponent's driver and the four horses with four arrows; and then like one endued with great lightness of hand, he cut-off his bow and standard with well-armed shafts.

sn: स साश्वं व्यधमचापि रथं हेमपरिष्कृतम्। हृदि विव्याध समरे त्रिंशता सायकैभृशम्॥
en: He consumed the horses of his antagonist and shattered his car of golden effulgence; then he pierced the latter on the centre of his breast with twenty shafts.

sn: एवं स पीडितो राजन्नश्वत्थामा महाबलः। शरजालैः परिवृतः कर्तव्यं नान्वपद्यत॥
en: Thus afflicted and enshrouded in a network of arrows, the puissant Ashvatthaman, O king, knew not what to do.

sn: एवं गते गुरोः पुत्रे तव पुत्रो महारथः। कृपकर्णादिभिः सार्धं शरैः सात्वतमावृणोत्॥
en: When the preceptor's son was involved in such a perilous position, your son, that mighty car-warrior, supported by Kripa, Karna and others, began to cover that scion of the Satvata race with numerous arrows.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तु विंशत्या कृपः शारद्वतस्रिभिः। कृतवर्माथ दशभिः कर्णः पञ्चाशता शरैः॥
en: Then Duryodhana with twenty Saradvata's son Kripa with three, Kritavarman with ten, Karna with fifty.

sn: दुःशासनः शतेनैव वृषसेनश्च सप्तभिः। सात्यकि विव्यधुस्तूर्णं समन्तान्निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Dushasana with hundred and Vrishasena with seven sharp arrows pierced Satyaki quickly and form all sides.

sn: ततः स सात्यकी राजन् सर्वानेव महारथान्। विरथान् विमुखांश्चैव क्षणेनैवाकरोन्नृप॥
en: Thereupon, O king, the puissant Satyaki deprived all those mighty car-warriors of their cars and compelled them to turn away from the field of battle, within a moment's time.

sn: अश्वत्थामा तु सम्प्राप्य चेतनां भरतर्षभ। चिन्तयामास दुःखार्ता निःश्वसंश्च पुनः पुनः॥
en: Meanwhile Ashvatthaman having regained his senses, began, O foremost of the Bharatas, to reflect, distressed with grief and sighing repeatedly.

sn: अथो स्थान्तरं द्रौणिः समारुह्य परंतपः। सात्यकिं वारयामास किरशरशतान् बहून्॥
en: Thereafter that afflicter of foes, namely, Drona's son, riding on another car proceeded to oppose Satyaki and shot hundreds of arrows.

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य भारद्वाजसुतं रणे। विरथं विमुखं चैव पुनश्चक्रे महारथः॥
en: Then beholding that son of Bharadvaja's son once wore advance against him in battle, the mighty car-warrior Satyaki once more compelled him to turn away and deprived him of his car.

sn: ततस्ते पाण्डवा राजन् दृष्ट्वा सात्यकिविक्रमम्। शङ्खशब्दान् भृशं चक्रुः सिंहनादांश्च नेदिरे॥
en: Thereat the Pandavas beholding the prowess of Satyaki, O king, loudly blew their conches and uttered deafening war-cries.

sn: एवं तं विरथं कृत्वा सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः। जघान वृषसेनस्य त्रिसाहस्रान् महारथान्॥
en: Then Satyaki of infallible prowess, thus rendering Drona's son carless, slew the three thousand mighty car-warriors engaged in supporting Vrishasena.

sn: निजधान सः। अयुतं दन्तिनां साधु कृपस्य पञ्चायुतानि चाश्वानां शकुनेर्निजघान ह॥
en: He also slew ten thousand tusked elephants that accompanied Kripa, as also fifty thousand horses that constituted Skuni's division.

sn: ततो द्रौणिर्महाराज रथमारुह्य वीर्यवान्। सात्यकिं प्रतिसंक्रुद्धः प्रययौ तद्वधेप्सया॥
en: Then once more, O king, the valorous son of Drona, mounting on a fresh car and excited to the highest pitch of fury assailed Satyaki for slaughtering him.

sn: पुनस्तमागतं दृष्ट्वा शैनेयिा निशितैः शरैः। अदारयत् क्रूरतरैः पुन: पुनररिंदम॥
en: But the grandson of Shini that subduer of foes seeing him once more proceed against him, ruthlessly pierced him with numerous sharp arrows.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महेष्वासौ नानालिङ्गैरमर्षणः। युयुधानेन वै द्रौणिः प्रहसन् वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: But this time, though thus deeply pierced by Yuyudhana with of diverse descriptions, that mighty bowmen, that son of Drona, worked up with rage, addressing his

sn: शैनेयाभ्युपपत्तिं ते जानाम्याचार्यघातिनि। न चैनं त्रास्यसि मया ग्रस्तमात्मानमेव च॥
en: O grandson of Shini, I know the partiality you bear for the murderer of his preceptor (viz., Dhristadyumna), but you shall not succeed in saying him and your own self when assailed by me.

sn: शपेऽऽत्मनां शैनेय सत्येन तपसा तथा। अहत्वा सर्वपाञ्चालान् यदि शान्तिमहं लभे॥
en: By my truth and by my ascetic austerities, I swear before you, that I shall enjoy no rest without slaying the whole Panchalas race.

sn: यद् बलं पाण्डवेयानां वृष्णीनामपि यद् बलम्। क्रियतां सर्वमेवेह निहनिष्यामि सोमकान्॥
en: You may unite together the troops of the Pandavas as well as those of the Vrishnis, yet I will exterminate the Somakas inspite of all their endeavours. arrows

sn: एवमुक्त्वार्करश्म्याभं सुतीक्ष्णं तं शरोत्तमम्। व्यसृज्यत् सात्वते द्रौणिर्वज्रं वृत्रे यथा हरिः॥
en: Having thus spoken, Drona's son hurled at that scion of the Satvata race an excellent arrow of the effulgence of the solar rays, like Hari (Indra) hurling the thunder-bolt against Vritra.

sn: स तं निर्भिद्य तेनास्तः सायकः सशरावरम्। विवेश वसुधा भित्त्वा श्वसन् बिलमिवोरगः॥
en: That arrow hurled by him, penetrating through the armour and the body of Satyaki, entered the earth like a hissing serpent entering its hole.

sn: स भिन्नकवचः शूरस्तोत्रादित इव द्विपः। विमुच्य सशरं चायं भूरिव्रणपरिस्रवः॥
en: Then like an elephant afflicted with the goad-stroke, with his armour pierced through and shedding copious blood from the wound, that hero Satyaki left his bow and arrows.

sn: सीदन् रुधिरसिक्तश्च रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्। सूतेनापहृतस्तूर्णं द्रोणपुत्राद् रथान्तरम्॥
en: And steeped in blood and loosing strength he squatted down on the terrace of his car. His driver then quickly drove him away from the vicinity of Drona's son.

sn: अथान्येन सुपुढेन शरेणानतपर्वणा। आजधान भ्रुवोर्मध्ये धृष्टद्युम्नं परंतपः॥
en: Then that afflicter of his forces namely the son of Drona, pierced Dhristadyumna between his bows with another shaft of depressed knots furnished with beautiful wings.

sn: स पूर्वमतिविद्धश्च भृशं पश्चाच पीडितः। ससादाथ च पाञ्चाल्यो व्यपाश्रयत च ध्वजम्॥
en: The Panchala prince had ere this been much wounded and now deeply hierced, he lost all his strength and caught pold of his flag-staff for supporting him.

sn: तं नागमिव सिंहेन दृष्ट्वा राजशरादितम्। जवेनाभ्यद्रवञ्छूराः पञ्च पाण्डवतो रथाः॥
en: Then fierce heroic warriors of the Pandava army rushed quickly to the rescue of an Dhristadyumna, who then resembled elephant assailed and afflicted by an enraged lion.

sn: किरीटी भीमसेनश्च वृद्धक्षत्रश्च पौरवः। युवराजश्च चेदीनां मालवश्च सुदर्शनः॥
en: Those warriors were the diadem decked Arjuna, Bhimasena, Vrihat Kshatra of Puru's race, the youthful prince of the Chedis and Sudarsana the ruler of the Malavas.

sn: एते हाहाकृताः सर्वे प्रगृहीतशरासनाः। वीरं द्रौणायनिं वीराः सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Then all these brave warriors crying Oh and Alas and grasping their bows and arrows surrounded Drona's brave son on all sides.

sn: ते विंशतिपदे यत्ता गुरुपुत्रममर्षणम्। पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिर्बाणैरभ्यजन् सर्वतः समम्॥
en: Advancing twenty paces, each of these warriors shot with great care, five arrows at the revengeful son of Drona.

sn: आशीविषाभैर्विंशत्या पञ्चभिस्तु शितैः शरैः। चिच्छेद युगपद् द्रौणिः पञ्चविंशतिसायकान्॥
en: But Drona's son, almost at the same time cut-off those twenty-five arrows shot at him with twenty-five sharp arrows of his own, resembling snakes of virulent poison.

sn: सप्तभिस्तु शितैर्बाणैः पौरवं द्रौणिरादयत्। मालवं त्रिभिरेकेन पार्थं षड्भिर्वृकोदरम्॥
en: Then Drona's son afflicted the scion of the Puru race with seven sharp arrows, the Malava king with three, Partha with one and Vrikodara with six.

sn: ततस्ते विव्यधुः सर्वे द्रौणिं राजन् महारथाः। युगपच पृथक् चैव रुक्मपुत्रैः शिलाशितैः॥
en: Thereupon, O king, all those mighty carwarriors, simultaneously and separately began to pierce the son of Drona with gold-winged arrows whetted on stone.

sn: युवराजश्च विंशत्या द्रौणिं विव्याध पत्रिभिः। पार्थश्च पुनरष्टाभिस्तथा सर्वे त्रिभित्रिभिः॥
en: The youthful prince of the Chedis pierced Drona's son with twenty winged shafts, Partha with eight and all the rest with three arrows each.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनं षड्भिरथाजधान द्रौणायनिर्दशभिर्वासुदेवम्। भ्यां द्वाभ्यां मालवं पौरवं च॥
en: Thereupon the son of Drona pierced Arjuna with six and Vasudeva's son with ten and Bhima with five and the youthful Chedi prince with four and the ruler of the Purus and the Malavas with couple of shafts.

sn: भ्यां विद्ध्वा कार्मुकं च ध्वजं चा पुनः पार्थं शरवप्रेण विद्ध्वा द्रौणिोरं सिंहनादं ननाद॥
en: Piercing Bhima's charioteer with six and cutting off his bow and standard with two other arrows and once more piercing Partha with a shower of arrows, the son of Drona uttered a dreadful war-cry.

sn: तस्यास्यतस्तान् निशितान् पीतधारान् द्रौणे: शरान् पृष्ठतश्चाग्रतश्चा धरा वियद् द्यौः प्रदिशो दिशश्च च्छन्ना बाणैरभवन् घोररूपैः॥
en: Then as Drona's son shot his welltempered, well-sharpened arrows, the earth, the welkin, the firmament, the cardinal and subsidiary quarters, all in his front and rear became covered with arrows of dreadful look.

sn: आसन्नस्य स्वरथं तीव्रतेजाः। सुदर्शनस्येन्द्रकेतुप्रकाशौ। सिभिः शरैर्युगपत् संचकर्त॥
en: Possessed of fierce energy and matching Indra himself in prowess, Ashvatthaman with three arrows, almost at the same time cut-off the two arms, like Indra's poles and the head of Sudarsana, as the latter was seated on his car.

sn: स पौरवं रथशक्त्या निहत्य छित्त्वा रथं तिलशश्चास्य बाणैः। छित्त्वा च बाहू वरचन्दनाक्ती भल्लेन कायाच्छिर उच्चकर्त॥
en: Then piercing Paurava with a lance and cutting off his chariot into smaller fragments, by means of his shafts, Ashvatthaman severed the two sandal-smeared arms of his opponent; and then with a bhalla he severed his head from his trunk.

sn: युवानमिन्दीवरदामवर्णं चेदिप्रभुं युवराज प्रसह्या विद्ध्वा प्रादान्मृत्यवे साश्वसूतम्॥
