sn: तथा तु संचिन्तयतां तान् केशान् द्यूतकारितान्। दुःखेन क्षणदा राजन् जगामाब्दशतोपमा॥
en: Thus reflecting upon those miseries resulting from the gambling match, (which the Pandavas had become subject to), their night had passed away with great uneasiness, which (night), O king, seemed to be (so long as) a hundred years.

sn: ततः प्रभाते विमले स्थिता दिष्टस्य शासने। चक्रुरावश्यकं सर्वे विधिद्दष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: Thereupon at the break of day they, being obedient to the injunctions of ordinance, all performed the necessary ceremonies, prescribed by the established usage.

sn: कृत्वावश्यकार्याणि समाश्वस्य च भारत। योगमाज्ञापयामासुयुद्धाय च विनिर्ययुः॥ ते
en: Having finished all the necessary ceremonies and consoled themselves, they, O Bharata, ordered for the array of soldiers and then started for battle.

sn: कर्णं सेनापतिं कृत्वा कृतकौतुकमङ्गलाः। पूजायित्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठान् दधिपात्रघृताक्षतैः॥ गोभिरश्चैश्च निष्कैश्च वासोभिश्च महाधनैः। वन्धमाना जयाशीर्भिः सूतमागधवन्दिभिः॥
en: After having made Karna their generalissimo with the due performance of the most auspicious rites (by tying a thread round his wrist) and having adored the foremost of the regenerate persons by offerings of vessels of curds, clarified butter and vessels, filled with corn and other auspicious articles, as well as by presents of gold-coins, kine and gems, valuable cloths and immense wealth and also having been praised by the charioteers and panegyrists, born in the country of Magadha, (the Magadha-panegyrists are the mixed tribes born of a Kshatriya mother and a Brahmana father), with hymns about victory.

sn: तथैव पाण्डवा राजन् कृतपूर्वाह्निकक्रियाः। शिबिरान्निर्ययुस्तूर्णं युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयाः॥
en: O monarch, the Pandavas on the other hand, having similarly performed the morning ceremonies, came out of their tents; and O king, they were resolved upon the battle.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च परस्परजयैषिणाम्॥
en: Thereupon the formidable battle began, which caused the hair of the body stand erect, between the Kurus and the Pandavas, each party being desirous of vanquishing the other.

sn: तयोर्दी दिवसो युद्धं कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः। कर्णे सेनापतौ राजन् बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनम्॥
en: O monarch, the most formidable battle, betwcen the troops of the Kurus and those of the Pandavas, lasted only for two days during the leadership of Karna.

sn: ततः शत्रुक्ष्यं कृत्वा समुहान्तं रणे वृषः। पश्वतां धार्तराष्ट्राणां फाल्गुनेन निपातितः॥
en: Thereupon Vrisha (Karna), having brought about an immense slaughter of the opponents in battle, was himself slain by Falguna (Arjuna), whilst the sons of Dhartarashtra were observing it.

sn: ततस्तु संजयः सर्वे गत्वा नागपुरं द्रुतम्। आचष्ट धृतराष्ट्राय यद् वृत्तं कुरुजाङ्गले॥
en: Thereafter Sanjaya departed towards the city of Hastinapur and told all to Dhritarashtra, that had taken place at Kurujangala.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच आपगेयं हतं श्रुत्वा द्रोणं चापि महारथम्। आजगाम परामार्तिं वृद्धो राजाऽम्बिकासुतः॥
en: Janamejaya said Having heard that both Bhishma and the car-warrior Drona of indomitable courage were slain (in the battle), the old king (Dhritarashtra) the son of Ambika, was highly oppressed with sorrow.

sn: स श्रुत्वा निहतं कर्णं दुर्योधनहितैषिणम्। कथं द्विजवर प्राणानधारयत दुःखितः॥
en: Having heard of the death of Karna the benefactor of Duryodhana, how could he, O best of the regenerate persons, hold his life, much aggrieved as he was?

sn: यस्मिञ्जयाशां पुत्राणां सममन्यत पार्थिवाः। तस्मिन् हते स कौरव्यः कथं प्राणानधारयत्॥
en: How could that royal descendant of Kuru hold his life, after having heard of the fall of that hero, on whom he supposed the hope of his sons' victory to rest?

sn: दुर्मरं तदहं मन्ये नृणां कृच्छ्रेऽपि वर्तताम्। यत्र कर्णं हतं श्रुत्वा नात्यजजीवितं नृपः॥
en: I suppose that men, falling in the most distressful circumstances, find greatest difficulty in yielding up their lives; for, the king, even after hearing of the death of Karna, could not (possibly) forsake his life.

sn: तथा शान्तनवं वृद्धं ब्रह्मन् बाह्रीकमेव च। द्रोण च सोमदत्तं च भूरिश्रवसमेव च॥ तथैव चान्यान् सुहृदः पुत्रान् पौत्रांच पातितान्। श्रुत्वा यन्नाजहात् प्राणां स्तन्मन्ये दुष्करं द्विज॥
en: As, O twice-born one, having heard of the fall of the old son of Shantanu, of Balhika, of Drona, of Somadatta, of Bhurisravas, as well as of other friends, of his sons and grandsons, the king did not give up his life; so, I suppose, that to yield up one's life is, O regenerate person, highly difficult.

sn: एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व विस्तरेण महामुने। न हि तृप्यामि पूर्वेषां शृण्वानश्चरितं महत्॥
en: Relate to me all these in their entirety, as they had really taken place. I am not (at all) satisfied with (simply) hearing the mighty achievements of my forefathers.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच हते कर्णे महाराज निशि गावल्गणिस्तदा। दीनो ययौ नागपुरमश्वैर्वातसमैर्जवे॥
en: Vaishampayana said O great king, when Karna was slain, the son of Gavalgana, greatly mortified in heart, repaired that very night to the city of Nagpur, in the back of horses resembling the wind in swiftness.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: स हास्तिनपुरं गत्वा भृशमुद्विग्नचेतनः। जगाम धृतराष्ट्रस्य क्षयं प्रक्षीणबान्धवम्॥
en: He then arrived at the city of Hastinapur; and with a greatly anxious heart, repaired to the house of Dhritarashtra which had now been vacated by all its friends.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: स तमुवीक्ष्य राजानं कश्मलाभिहतौजसम्। ववन्दे प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा मूर्धा पादौ नृपस्य ह॥
en: He then beholding the king deprived of energy in consequence of his gloominess of mind, folded his hands; and indeed, worshipped the monarch's feet by bowing down his head.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: सम्पूज्य च यथान्यायं धृतराष्ट्रं महीपतिम्। हा कष्टमिति चोक्त्वा स ततो वचनमाददे॥
en: Having worshipped the ruler of the earth, Dhritarashtra, according to the just rites and having uttered-Alas! and woe!-he then

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: संजयोऽहं क्षितिपते कचिदास्ते सुखं भवान्। स्वदोषैरापदं प्राप्य कचिन्नाद्य विमुह्यति॥
en: O ruler of earth, I am Sanjaya! Are you not at ease? After having obtained distress by your own faults, are you not now deprived of all your senses?

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: हितान्युक्तानि विदुरद्रोणगाङ्गेयकेशवैः। अगृहीतान्यनुस्मृत्य कचिन्न कुरुषे व्यथाम्॥
en: The good advises, uttered (given) by Vidura, Drona, son of Ganga and Keshava, were not received by you. Do you not feel pain to remember them now?

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: रामनारदकण्वाद्यैर्हितमुक्त सभातले। न गृहीतमनुस्मृत्य कचिन्न कुरुषे व्यथाम्॥
en: Also do you not feel pain to remember the rejection of the good advises given to you by Rama, Narada, Kanva and others in the assembly (of kings)?

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: सुहृदस्त्वद्धिते युक्तान् भीष्मद्रोणमुखान् परैः। निहतान् युधि संस्मृत्य कचिन्न कुरुषे व्यथाम्॥
en: Remembering that your friends, Bhishma, Drona and others, who were ever occupied in contributing to your welfare, were slain by the enemies in battle, do you not feel pain?

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: तमेवंवादिनं राजा सूतपुत्रं कृताञ्जलिम्। सुदीर्घमथ निःश्वस्य दुःखात इदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sighing heavy and hot, the king, oppressed with grief, addressed in these words the son of Suta, who with folded hands, was telling him the above.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच आपगेये हते शूरे दिव्यास्त्रवति संजय। द्रोणे च परमेष्वासे भृशं मे व्यथितं मनः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, owing to the deaths of that heroic wielder of celestial weapons, the son of Ganga and the mighty bowman, Drona, my heart greatly aches.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: यो रथानाह सहस्राणि दंशितानां दशैव तु। अहन्यहनि तेजस्वी निजघ्ने वसुसम्भवः॥
en: That the mighty hero, who was the incarnation of the (eighth) Vasu, killed every day ten thousand car-warriors protected by armour.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: तं हतं यज्ञसेनस्य पुत्रेणेह शिखण्डिना। पाण्डवेयाभिगुप्तेन श्रुत्वा मे व्यथितं मनः॥
en: He (that mighty hero) was killed in the battle by the son of Yajnasena (namely) Shikhandin, who who was protected by the Pandavas. At this (occurrence) my heart greatly aches.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: भार्गवः प्रददौ यस्मै परमास्त्रं महाहवे। साक्षाद् रामेण यो बाल्ये धनुर्वेद उपाकृतः॥
en: The son of Bhrigu gave to that lofty-minded one (that hero, Bhishma) the knowledge of the best weapons. To him also, during the childhood, the science of the bow was taught by Rama himself.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: यस्य प्रसादात् कौन्तेया राजपुत्र महारथाः। महारथत्वं सम्प्राप्तास्तथान्ये वसुधाधिपाः॥
en: Through whose (Drona's) kindness, the sons of Kunti-the royal sons-the mighty carwarriors-as well as several other rulers of earth, attained the abilities of a Maharathi (one simultaneously fighting with ten thousand

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: तं द्रोण निहतं श्रुत्वा धृष्टद्युम्नेन संयुगे। सत्यसंधं महेष्वासं भृशं मे व्यथितं मनः॥
en: Hearing of that mighty bowman, Drona, who true his aim, slain by Dhrishtadyumna in battle, my heart greatly aches.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: ययोलेकि पुमानस्त्रे न समोऽस्ति चतुर्विधे। तौ द्रोणभीष्मौ श्रुत्वा तु हतौ मे व्यथितं मनः॥
en: Those two had not a peer in this world in ihe wielding of the four-fold weapons. Hearing that both Drona and Bhishma were slain in the battle, my mind is greatly pained. was to

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: त्रैलोक्ये यस्य चास्त्रेषु न पुमान् विद्यते समः। तं द्रोण निहतं श्रुत्वा किमकुर्वत मामकाः॥
en: In the three worlds there is no person, who is equal to him in the use of weapons. Hearing the death of this hero, Drona, what did my followers do?

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: संशप्तकानां च बले पाण्डवेन महात्मना। धनंजयेन विक्रम्य गमिते यमसादनम्॥
en: The army of the Samsaptakas was sent away to the region of Yama by Dhananjaya, the lofty-minded son of Pandu, through the exertion of his terrible prowess.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: नारायणास्त्रे च हते द्रोणपुत्रस्य धीमतः। विप्रदुतेष्वनीकेषु किमकुर्वत मामकाः॥
en: (After the above occurrence and also) after, the Narayana weapon of the most intelligent son of Drona had been destroyed, as also after the divisions of my army had fled away (from the battle-field), what did the troops of my side do?

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: विप्रदुतानहं मन्ये निमग्नाशोकसागरे। प्लवमानान् हते द्रोणे सन्ननौकानिवार्णवे॥
en: I think that, on the death of Drona, my troops, plunged deep into the ocean of grief, ran away (from the field of battle), even as the slip-wrecked mariners float on the ocean.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: दुर्योधन कर्णस्य भोजस्य कृतवर्मणः। मद्रराजस्य शल्यस्य द्रौणेश्चैव कृपस्य च ॥ मत्पुत्रस्य च शेषस्य तथाऽन्येषां च संजय। विप्रद्रुतेष्वनीकेषु मुखवर्णोऽभवत् कथम्॥
en: O Sanjaya, when my troops had run away (from the battle field), what had become the colour of the faces of Duryodhana, Karna, Kritavarman the ruler of the Bhojas, Shalya the king of the Madras, Ashvatthaman the son of Drona and Kripacharya, as well as of the remaining sons of mine and several other monarchs.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: एतत् सर्वं यथावृत्तं तथा गावल्गणे मप। आचक्ष्व पाण्डवेयानां मामकानां च विक्रमम्॥
en: O son of Gavalgana, relate to me all those in detail that had actually happened in battle as to the prowess shown by Pandavas as well as by the troops of my own side.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: संजय उवाच तवापराधाद् यद् वृत्तं कौरवेयेषु मारिष। तच्छ्रुत्वा मा व्यथां कार्षीर्दिष्टे न व्यथते बुधः॥
en: Sanjaya said O Lord of kings, you should not be pained to hear of what had taken place in respect to the Kauravas through your misconduct. For, the learned sage never feels any anguish at what is brought about by Fate.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: यस्मादभावी भावी वा भवेदर्थो नरं प्रति। अप्राप्तौ तस्य वा प्राप्तौ न कश्चिद् व्यथते बुधः॥
en: What is not likely to happen to man (being subject to Fate) may happen to him; or what is likely to take place may, again, happen to a person. Hence at the acquisition or nonacquisition of the purposes the learned sage should not at all grieve.

description: The parley between Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच न व्यथाभ्यधिका काचिद् विद्यतेमम संजय। दिष्टमेतत् पुरा मन्ये कथयस्व यथेच्छकम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, no great anguish does find place in me. For, I think that all this is (the unavoidable consequence of) superior destiny. So, do you describe according as you desire.

sn: संजय उवाच हते द्रोणे महेष्वासे तव पुत्रा महारथाः। बभूवुरस्वस्थमुखा विषण्णा गतचेतसः॥
en: Sanjaya said When that mighty bowman Drona, was slain, your sons, the great car-warriors, became pale-faced, gloomy and senseless.

sn: अवाङ्मुखाः शस्त्रभृतः सर्व अप्रेक्षमाणाःशोकार्ता नाभ्यभाषन् परस्परम्॥ एव विशाम्पते। तु
en: And O king, all those who were armed with the weapons, stood speechless; and highly oppressed with grief, they neither beheld nor spoke any words to one another.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा व्यथिताकारान् सैन्यानि तव भारत। ऊर्ध्वमेव निरैक्षन्त दुःखत्रस्यान्यनेकशः॥
en: descendant of the Bharata race, seeing them changed in countenance, on account of their being oppressed with sorrow, your troops, themselves being highly afflicted with grief and anxiety, looked upwards.

sn: शस्त्राण्येषां राजेन्द्र शोणिताक्तानि सर्वशः। प्राभ्रश्यन्त करोग्रेभ्यो दृष्ट्वा द्रोणं हतं युधि॥
en: Beholding the death of Drona in battle, O foremost of kings, the weapons of many of them, indeed besmeared with blood, dropped down from their hands.

sn: तानि बद्धान्यरिष्टानि लम्बमानानि भारत। अदृश्यन्त महाराज नक्षत्राणि यथा दिवि॥
en: O great monarch, O descendant of the Bharata race, several of those (weapons), still retained by the troops in the various parts of their bodies, were seen hanging, like the meteors of heaven (pending from above).

sn: तथा तु स्तिमितं दृष्ट्वा गतसत्त्वमवस्थितम्। बलं तव महाराज राजा दुर्योधनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: O great monarch, seeing your force (his own troops) thus eclipsed (by that of the Pandavas) and standing as if lifeless, king

sn: भवतां बाहुवीर्यं हि समाश्रित्य मया युधि। पाण्डवेयाः : समाहूता युद्धं चेदं प्रवर्तितम्॥
en: Depending upon the strength of your arms this war had been entered into and the descendants of Pandu had also been summoned to the battle by me.

sn: तदिदं निहते द्रोणे विषण्णमिव लक्ष्यते। युध्यमानाश्च समरे योधा वध्यन्ति सर्वशः॥
en: But you, however, look very cheerless (dispirited) now in the death of Drona. All the warriors engaged in battle are slain in battle.

sn: जयो वापि क्धो वापि युध्यमानस्य संयुगे। भवेत् किमत्र चित्रं वै युध्यध्वं सर्वतोमुखाः॥
en: Victory or death falls to the lot of one who is engaged in battle. What wonder then there is in this (the fall of Drona)? So do you fight with your faces in all directions.

sn: पश्यध्वं च महात्मानं कर्णं वैकर्तनं युधि। प्रचरन्तं महेष्वासं दिव्यैरस्त्रैर्महाबलम्॥
en: Do you behold that lofty-minded Karna, the son of Vikartana, that highly powerful and mighty bowman-that wielder of celestial weapons, who is roving about in the (field of) battle.

sn: यस्य वै युधि संत्रासात् कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः। निवर्तते सदा मन्दः सिहात् क्षुद्रमृगो यथा।॥
en: Through fear, indeed, Dhananjaya-that coward son of Kunti, always flies away from him in battle, even as the small deer (does) froni a lion.

sn: येन नागायुतप्राणो भीमसेनो महाबलः। मानुषेणैव युद्धेन तामवस्थां प्रवेशितः॥
en: It is by him that Bhimasena of mighty strength, endowed with the force of ten thousand elephants, was brought, through the tactics of warfare that are peculiar to man, into the same circumstance.

sn: येन दिव्यास्त्रविच्छूरो मायावी स घटोत्कचः। अमोघया रणे शक्त्या निहतो भैरवं नदन्॥
en: It is by him that Ghatotkacha, thai wielder of celestial weapon, that god, that enchanter, that one who made a tremendous roar, was slain in battle through the most indomitable power.

sn: तस्य दुर्वारवीर्यस्य सत्यसंधस्य धीमतः। बाह्वोर्द्रविणमक्षय्यमद्य द्रक्ष्यथ संयुगे॥
en: Do you behold today in battle the inexhaustible strength of arms of that intellectual one, who is of unsubdued energy and of fixed purpose.

sn: द्रोणपुक्षस्य विक्रान्तं राधेयस्यैव चोभयोः। पश्यन्तु पाण्डुपुत्रास्ते विष्णुवासवयोरिव॥
en: Do you behold today the prowess of both the son of Drona and the son of Radha who are high-souled, among the troops of the Pandus and the Panchalas.

sn: सर्व एव भवन्तश्च शक्ताः प्रत्येकशोऽपि वा। पाण्डुपुत्रान् रणे हन्तुं ससैन्यान् किमुसंहताः॥
en: All of you are, however, capable of slaying in battle the sons of Pandu with their troops even fighting singly. What then, when fighting together? Endowed with immense strength and acquainted with the use of weapons, do you behold today one another (engaged in battle).

sn: संजय उवाच वीर्यवन्तः कृतास्त्राश्च द्रक्ष्यथाद्य परस्परम्। एवमुक्त्वा ततः कर्णं चके सेनापति तदा। तव पुत्रो महावीर्यो भ्रातृभिः सहितोऽनघ॥
en: Sanjaya said O faultless one, having thus addressed, you son (Duryodhana) of mighty prowess, (after having consulted) with his brothers, afterwards made Karna the generallissimo (of the Kuru troops).

sn: सैनापत्यमथावाप्य कर्णो राजन् महारथः। सिंहनादं विनद्योचैः प्रायुध्यत रणोत्कटः॥
en: O king, after having obtained the generalship (of the Kuru army) the mighty carwarrior Karna, invincible in battle, engaged himself in battle, making a tremendous roar like a lion.

sn: स सृञ्जयानां सर्वेषां पञ्चालानां च मारिष। केकयानां विदेहानां चकार कदनं महत्॥
en: He caused a great slaughter among the Srinjayas, all the Panchalas, the Kekayas and the Videhas, in the sight of all.

sn: तस्येषुधाराः शतशः प्रादुरासञ्छरासनात्। अग्रे पुढेषु संसक्ता यथा भ्रमरपङ्क्तयः॥
en: Hundreds of arrows most fearfully issued from his bow, one closely following the wings of another like the lines of bees (flying away from the hive).

sn: स पीडयित्वा पञ्चालान् पाण्डवांश्च तरस्विनः। हत्वा सहस्रशो योधानर्जुनेन निपातितः॥२१
en: Having oppressed the Pandavas and the Panchalas, of immense activity and killed thousands of heroes, he, at last, was slain by Arjuna. Having oppressed the Pandavas and the Panchalas, of immense activity and killed thousands of heroes, he, at last, was slain by Arjuna.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा महाराज धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। शोकस्यान्तमपश्यन् वै हतं मेने सुयोधनम्॥ विह्वलः पतितो भूमौ नष्टचेता इव द्विपः।
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this (the above intelligence), the great king Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, experienced, indeed, the farthest limit of grief and considered Suyodhana slain (in the battle); and highly perturbed, he fell down upon the ground, like an elephant, that had lost all his senses.

sn: तस्मिन् निपतिते भूमौ विह्वले राजसत्तमे॥ आर्तनादो महानासीत् स्त्रीणां भरतसत्तम।
en: O the most excellent of the Bharata race, on the fall of the highly agitated and foremost of monarchs upon the ground, there was tremendous wailing of women.

sn: स शब्दः पृथिवी कृत्स्नां पूरयामास सर्वशः॥ शोकार्णवे महाघोरे निमग्ना भरतस्त्रियः। रुरुदुर्दुःखशोकार्ता भृशमुद्विग्नचेतसः॥
en: Which (the noise) filled the entire earth to all its points. The ladies of the house hold of Bharata, greatly burnt in grief and with hearts filled with great anxiety, bewailed most bitterly, plunged as they were in the very deep ocean of sorrow.

sn: राजानं च समासाद्य गान्धारी भरतर्षभ। निःसंज्ञा पतिता भूमौ सर्वाण्यन्तः पुराणि च ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race advancing towards the king, Gandhari, as well as all other ladies of the royal household, fell down upon the ground, all having lost their senses. a

sn: ततस्ताः संजयो राजन् समाश्वासयदातुराः। मुह्यमानाः सुबहुशो मुञ्चन्त्यो वारि नेत्रजम्॥
en: Thereupon, O monarch, Sanjaya consoled those ladies, who were highly oppressed with sorrow and deprived of their senses and who, again, were copiously shedding tears from their eyes.

sn: समाश्वस्ताः स्त्रियस्तास्तु वेपमाना मुहुर्मुहुः। कदल्य इव वातेन धूयमानाः समन्ततः॥
en: In spite of their being comforted (by Sanjaya), those ladies shivered every moment like the plantain tree constantly shaken by the wind.

sn: राजानं विदुस्थापि प्रज्ञाचक्षुषमीश्वरम्। आश्वासयामास तदा सिञ्चस्तोयेन कौरवम्॥
en: Thereupon Vidura, too, began to sprinkle water over the face of that descendant of Kuru and consoled that powerful monarch, who had eyes of wisdom.

sn: स लब्वा शनकैःसंज्ञां ताश्च दृष्टा स्त्रियो नृप। उन्मत्त इव राजेन्द्र स्थितस्तूष्णीं विशाम्पते॥
en: O Lord of carth, having gradually attained to consciousness and understanding the rniserable plight of those ladies, the monarch, like at senseless being, remained silent for sometime.

sn: ततो ध्यात्वा चिरं कालं निःश्वस्य च पुनः पुनः। स्वान् पुत्रान् गर्हयामास बहु मेने त्व पाण्डवान्॥
en: Thereupon he, reflecting (upon the matter) for a pretty long time and sighing heavily and incessantly, condemned his own sons but spoke highly of the Pandavas.

sn: गर्हयंश्चात्मनो बुद्धिं शकुनेः सौबलस्य च। ध्यात्वा तु सुचिरं कालं वेपमानो मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: Then having condemned his own reason as well as that of Shakuni the son of Subala and meditated (upon the matter) for a long while, the king trembled at every moment.

sn: संस्तभ्य च मनो भूयो राजा धैर्यसमन्वितः। पुनर्गावल्गर्णि सूतं पर्यपृच्छत संजयम्॥
en: The king had, again, restrained his mind and collected enough of patience. Then he asked his charioteer Sanjaya, the son of

sn: यत् त्वया कथितं वाक्यं श्रुतं संजय तन्मया। कच्चिद् दुर्योधनः सूत न गतो वै यमक्षयम्॥ जये निराशः पुत्रो मे सततं जयकामुकः। ब्रूहि संजय तत्त्वेन पुनरुक्तां कथामिमाम्॥
en: O Sanjaya, whatever words were uttered by you were all heard by me. O charioteer, has not my son Duryodhana gone to the region of Yama? Has my son, who is ever desirous of victory, grown desperate of success? O Sanjaya, do you repeat to me in detail truly what you have said already.

sn: एवमुक्तोऽब्रवीत् सूतो राजानं जनमेजय। हतो वैकर्तनो राजन् सह पुत्रैर्महारथः॥ भ्रातृभिश्च महेष्वासैः सूतपुत्रैस्तनुत्यजैः।
en: O Janamejaya, having been thus asked, the Suta addressed the king, saying-"O king, the son of Vikartan., that mighty car-warrior, was killed in battle along with his sons and brothers, as well as the other warrior sons of Suta, who were all great bowmen and who also were ready to give up their lives in battle.

sn: दुःशासनश्च निहतः पाण्डवेन यशस्विना। पीतं च रुधिरं कोपाद् भीमसेनेन संयुगे॥
en: Dusshasana, too, was slain in an encounter by Bhimasena, that famous son of Pandu, who had drunk his (Dusshasana's) blood out of anger.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इति श्रुत्वा महाराज धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। अब्रवीत् संजयं सूतं शोकसंविग्नमानसः॥
en: Vaishampayana said O great king, hearing this intelligence, Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, with a heart filled with great anxiety on account of sorrow, an

sn: दुष्प्रणीतेन मे तात पुत्रस्यादीर्घजीविनः। हतं वैकर्तनं श्रुत्वा शोको मर्माणि कृन्तति॥
en: “O son, on account of the dishonest policy of my son, who has no foresight of the distant future, the son of Vikartana was slain in battle. Hearing this, I find my vital parts all cut as under.

sn: तस्य मे संशयं छिन्धि दुःखपारं तितीर्षतः। कुरुणां सृञ्जयानां च के च जीवन्ति के मृताः॥
en: Do you now remove all by doubts, who are most willing to bridge over this ocean of sorrow, by relating to me, who amongst the Kurus and the Pandavas are yet alive and who are already dead.

sn: संजय उवाच हतः शान्तनवो राजन् दुराधर्षः प्रतापवान्। हत्त्वा पाण्डवयोधानामव॒दं दशभिर्दिनैः॥
en: Sanjaya said O monarch, after having killed innumerable number of the Sanjayas and the Panchalas, Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, of mighty strength and of indomitable courage, was slain after ten days (of the battle).

sn: तथा द्रोणो महेष्वासः पञ्चालानां रथव्रजान्। निहत्य युधि दुर्धर्षः पश्चाद् रुक्मरथो हतः॥
en: Again, after having killed the whole force of the Panchalas in battle, the mighty bowman Drona of indomitable courage, riding upon a car of gold, was slain afterwards.

sn: हतशेषस्य भीष्मेण द्रोणेन च महात्मना। अर्धं निहत्य सैन्यस्य कर्णो वैकर्तनो हतः॥
en: Having slain the half of the troops, that had survived the slaughter by the high-souled Bhishma and Drona, Karna, the son of Vikartana, was at last killed.

sn: विविंशतिर्महाराज राजपुत्रो महाबलः। आनर्तयोधाशतशो निहत्य निहतो रणे।॥
en: O great king, having killed hundreds of Anarta warriors, the royal son Vivinshati of mighty strength was himself slain in battle.

sn: तथा पुत्रो विकर्णस्ते क्षत्रव्रतमनुस्मरन्। क्षीणवाहायुधः शूरः स्थितोऽभिमुखतः परान्॥
en: Thereupon your heroic son Vikarna, having remembered the duties of a Kshatriya, stood in front of the enemies, without his weapons on and also without a conveyance.

sn: घोररूपान् परिक्केशान दुर्योधनकृतान् बहून्। प्रतिज्ञा स्मरता चैव भीमसेनेन पातितः॥
en: He was slain by Bhimasena, who had (at the time) recollected the most severe and innumerable wrongs inflicted upon him by Duryodhana and also the most solemn promise of his own.

sn: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्तयौ राजपुत्रौ महारथौ। कृत्वा त्वसुकरं कर्म गतौ वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Having performed the most striking exploits in battle, the two royal sons, Vindu and Anuvindu, of the country of Avanti, of mighty prowess, departed to the region of Death.

sn: सिधुराष्ट्रमुखानीह दश राष्ट्राणि यानिह। वशे तिष्ठन्ति वीरस्य यः स्थितस्तव शासने॥ अक्षौहिणीर्दशैकां च विनिर्जित्य शितैः शरैः। अर्जुनेन हतो राजन् महावीर्यो जयद्रथः॥
en: That heroic leader, under whose control ten kingdom remained, the foremost of which was the kingdom of Sindhu; and who, again, was under your subjection-that one Jayadratha, O monarch, of mighty prowess, was slain by Arjuna, after he had subdued eleven Akshauhinis by his sharp arrows.

sn: तथा दुर्योधनसुतस्तरस्वी युद्धदुर्मदः। वर्तमानः पितुः शास्त्रे सौभद्रेण निपातितः॥
en: So also the son of Duryodhana, of immense activity and incapable of being vanquished in battle and resting over obedient under the command of his father, was killed by the son of Subhadra.

sn: तथा दौःशासनिः शूरो बाहुशाली रणोत्कटः। द्रौपदेयेन सङ्गभ्य गमितो यमसादनम्॥
en: So again the heroic son of Dusshasana looking most terrible in battle and endowed with the mighty strength of arms, was sent away to the region of Yama by the son of Draupadi, who careered in battle showing forth his prowess.

sn: किरातानामधिपतिः सागरानूपवासिनाम्। देवराज्य धर्मात्मा प्रियो बहुमतः सखा॥ भगदत्तो महीपालः क्षत्रधर्मरतः सदा। धनंजयेन विक्रम्य गमितो यमसादनम्॥
en: The most virtuous king Bhagadatta, ever obedient to the duties of a Kshatriya, who was the paramount lord of the Kiratas-dwelling in the low-land countries on the sea-cost and who, again, was the most esteemed and intimate friend of the king of the celestials, was sent away to the region of Yama by Dhananjaya showing forth his prowess (in battle).

sn: तथा कौरवदायादो न्यस्तशस्त्रो महायशाः। हतो भूरिश्रवा राजशूरः सात्यकिना युधि॥
en: O monarch, similarly Bhurisravas, the heroic son of Somadatta, of great renown, the kinsman of the Kauravas, was slain in battle by Satyaki.

sn: श्रुतायुरपि चाम्बष्ठः क्षत्रियाणां धुरंधरः। चरन्नभीतवत् संख्ये निहतः सव्यसाचिना॥
en: Fearlessly roving about in the field of battle, the Ambastha chief Shrutayus, the most exalted of the Kshatriyas, was slain by Savyasachin.

sn: तव पुत्रः सदामर्षी कृतास्त्रो युद्धदुर्मदः। दुःशासनो महाराज भीमसेनेन पातितः॥
en: O great king, your ever wrathful son Dushasana, who is well acquainted with the science of weapons and who is incapable of being vanquished in battle, was slain by Bhimasena.

sn: यस्य राजन् गजानीकं बहु साहस्त्रमद्भुतम्। सुदक्षिणः स संग्रामे निहत: सव्यसाचिना॥
en: O monarch, that Sudakshina, who had under him several thousands of extra-ordinary warriors fighting on elephants, was slain in battle by Savyasachin.

sn: कोसलानामधिपतिर्हत्वा बहुमतान् परान्। सौभद्रेण हि विक्रम्य गमितो यमसादनम्॥
en: Having slain several hundreds of the enemies, the lord of the Kosalas was himself sent to the abode of Yama by the son of Subhadra showing forth his prowess in battle.

sn: बहुशो योधयित्वा तु भीमसेनं महारथम्। मद्राराजात्मजः शूरः परेषां भयवर्धनः। असिचर्मधरः श्रीमान् सौभद्रेण निपातितः॥
en: Having fought several times with that great car-warrior Bhimasena. The heroic younger brother of the king of Madras, inspiring greater terror in the enemies-that handsome wielder of sword and shield-was slain by the son of Subhadra.

sn: समः कर्णस्य समरे यः स कर्णस्य पश्यतः। वृषसेनो महातेजाः शीघ्रास्त्रो दृढविक्रमः॥ अभिमन्योर्वधं श्रुत्वा प्रतिज्ञामपि चात्मनः। धनंजयेन विक्रम्य गमितो यमसादनम्॥
en: The highly energetic Vrisasena of steady prowess and ready in managing the weapon-that peer of Karna in battle, was sent to the abode of Yama by Dhananjaya, who, remembering the death of his son and also his own solemn vow, showed forth his prowess in battle.

sn: नित्यं प्रसक्तवैरो यः पाण्डवैः पृथिवीपतिः। विश्राव्य वैरं पार्थेन श्रुतायुः स निपातितः॥
en: That Srutayus, O king of the earth, who always entertained animosity against the Pandavas, was reminded of that animosity, before he was slain by the son of Pritha.

sn: शल्यपुत्रस्तु विक्रान्तः सहदेवेन मारिष। हतो रुक्मरथो राजन् भ्राता मातुलजो युधि॥
en: O sire, O monarch, Rukmaratha the son of Shalya, of mighty prowess-that brother (of Shahadeva), being son of the latter's maternal uncle, was slain by Shahadeva in battle.

sn: राजा भगीरथो वृद्धो बृहत्क्षत्रश्च केकयः। पराक्रमन्तौ विक्रान्तौ निहतौ वीर्यवत्तरौ॥
en: Both the old king Bhagiratha and Brihatkshatra, the chief of the Kekayas, highly powerful, possessed of prowess and greater energy as they were, also killed in battle.

sn: भगदत्त सुतो राजन् कृतप्रज्ञो महाबलः। श्येनवचरता संख्ये नकुलेन निपातितः॥
en: O monarch, the highly powerful and wise son of Bhagadatta was slain by Nakula, who moved about in the field of) battle like a hawk.

sn: पितामहस्तव तथा बाह्लीकः सह बाह्निकैः। निहतो भीमसेन महाबलपराक्रमः॥
en: So also your grand father Balhika, endued with great strength and prowess, was slain by Bhimasena with all the Balhikas,

sn: जयत्सेनस्तथा राजञ्जारासंधिर्महाबलः। मागधो निहत: संख्ये सौभद्रेण महात्मना॥
en: Then again, O monarch, the Magadha prince Jayatsena, the most powerful son of Jarasandha, was slain in battle by the loftyminded son of Subhadra.

sn: पुत्रस्ते दुर्मुखो राजन् दुःसहश्च महारथः। गदया भीमसेनेन निहतौ शूरमानिनौ॥
en: Your son Durmukha and the other son the great car-warrior Dussaha, both of them are considered to be the most heroic, were slain in battle by Bhimasena by means of his mace.

sn: दुर्मर्षणो दुर्विषहो दुर्जयश्च महारथः। कृत्वा त्वसुकरं कर्म गता वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Having achieved the extraordinary exploits in battle. Durmarsana, Durvisaha and the great car-warrior Durjaya departed to the region of Death.

sn: उभौ कलिङ्गवृषको भ्रातरौ युद्धदुर्मदौ। कृत्वा चासुकरं कर्म गतौ वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Having achieved the extraordinary exploits in battle, both the brothers, Kalinga and Vrishabha, who are incapable of being vanquished in battle, departed to the abode of Death.

sn: सचिवो वृषवर्मा ते शूरः परमवीर्यवान्। भीमसेनेन विक्रम्य गमितो यमसादनम्॥
en: Your highly energetic minister, the Suta Vrisavarman, was sent to the abode of Death by Bhimasena, who displayed his superior prowess in battle.

sn: तथैव पौरवो राजा नागायुतबलो महान्। समरे पाण्डुपुत्रेण निहतः सव्यसाचिना॥
en: In the same way, the great king Paurava, possessing the power of the thousand clephants, was slain with all his attendants by Savyasachin, the son of Pandu.

sn: वसातयो महाराज द्विसासस्त्राः प्रहारिणः। शूरसेनाश्च विक्रान्ताः सर्वे युधि निपातिताः॥
en: O great monarch, the great smiters of foes, the two thousand Vashati troops, as well as all the Surashenas possessed of great prowess, were slain in battle.

sn: अभीषाहाः कवचिनः प्रहरन्तो रणोत्कटाः। शिवयश्च रथोदाराः कालिङ्गसहिता हताः॥
en: The Abhishaha troops, the mighty smiters of foes, who are all clad in armour and most fierce in battle, as also the powerful carwarriors, the Shivi soldiers, all were slain with the Kalingas.

sn: गोकुले नित्यसंवृद्धा युद्धे परमकोपनाः। तेऽपावृत्तकवीराश्च निहताः सव्य साचिना॥
en: So also those other heroes, gradually grown up in Gokula, who were most of furious in battle and had never turned their backs in the field, were slain by Savyasachin.

sn: श्रेणयो बहुसाहस्त्राः संशप्तकगणाश्च ये। ते सर्वे पार्थमासाद्य गता वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Having approached Partha, many thousands of the Sreni warriors, as well as the army of the Samsaptakas, all these departed to the abode of Death.

sn: स्यालौ तव महाराज राजानौ वृषकाचलौ। त्वदर्थमतिविक्रान्तौ निहतौ सव्यसाचिना॥
en: O powerful monarch, your brothers-in-law, the prince Vrishaka and Achala, displaying their inighty prowess in battle for your sake, were slain by Savyasachin.

sn: उग्रकर्मा महेष्वासो नामतः कर्मतस्तथा। शाल्वराजो महाबाहुर्भीमसेनेन पातितः॥
en: The Shalya king of mighty strength and active habits, who was a grcat bowman both in name and deeds, was slain in battle by Bhimasena.

sn: ओघवांश्च महाराज बृहन्तः सहितौ रणे। पराक्रमन्तौ मित्रार्थे गतौ वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: O powerful monarch, Aghovat and Vrihantha, both exerting themselves in battle and displaying their prowess for the sake of their friends, departed to the region of Death.

sn: तथैव रथिनां श्रेष्ठः क्षेम धूर्तिर्विशाम्पते। निहतो गदया राजन् भीमसेनेन संयुगे॥
en: So also, O ruler of earth, Kshemadhurti, that best of the car-warriors, was slain by Bhimasena in battle by means of his mace.

sn: तथा राजन् महेष्वासो जलसंधो महाबलः। सुमहत् कदनं कृत्वा हतः सात्यकिना रणे॥
en: Having wrought an immense slaughter, then the great bowman king Jalasandha of mighty strength was slain in battle by Satyaki.

sn: अलम्बुषो राक्षसेन्द्र खरबन्धुरयानवान्। घटोत्कचेन विक्रम्य गमितो यमसादनम्॥
en: Alambusha the lord of the Rakshasas who had a chariot drawn by arms, was sent to the abode of Yama by Ghatotkacha displaying his prowess in battle.

sn: राधेयः सूतपुत्रश्च भ्रातरश्च महारथाः। केकयाः सर्वशश्चापि निहताः सव्यसाचिना॥ मालवा मद्रकाश्चैव द्राविडाश्चोग्रकर्मिणः। यौधेयाश्च ललित्याश्च क्षुद्रकाश्चाप्युशीनराः॥ मावेल्लाकास्तुण्डिकेरा: सावित्रीपुत्रकाश्च ये। प्रोच्योदीच्याः प्रतीत्याश्च दाक्षिणात्याश्च मारिष॥ पत्तीनां निहताः संघा हयानां प्रयुतानि च। रथव्रजाश्च निहता हताश्च वरवारणाः॥
en: The sons of Radha, the descendants of Suta, the mighty car-warriors, who are brother to one another, the Kalikeyas, the Malavas, the Madrakas, the Dravidas who are most terrible in prowess, the Yodheyas, the Lalityas, the Kshudrikas, even the Usinaras. the Mavelyakas, the Tundikeras, the Sabitriputrakas, the men of the eastern, the northern, the western and the southern countries, all these, O sire, were slain by Savyasachin. A large body of foot-soldiers were slain, so also many millions of horses. And a large number of car-warriors were killed. Many elephants of large shape and superior kind fell in the battle.

sn: सध्वजाः सायुधाः शूराः सवर्माम्बरभूषणाः। कालेन महता यत्ताः सुशलैर्ये च वर्धिताः॥ ते हताः समरे राजन् पार्थेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा।
en: Furnished with standards and weapons, several heroes decked in ornaments, garments and armour, who were of superior conduct and parentage and possessed of perseverance, as well as other warriors, who, again, were of immeasurable strength and desirous of each other's fall, had, in course of great time, all been slain in battle by Partha, who is indefatigable in achievements.

sn: अन्ये तथाऽमितबलाः परस्परवधैषिणः॥ एते चान्ये च बहवो राजानः सगणा रणे। हताः सहस्रशो राजन् यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: These and several other kings were slain with their followers by thousands. O monarch, thus I have answered now what you asked me.

sn: एवमेष क्षयो वृत्तः कर्णार्जुनसमागमे। महेन्द्रेण यथा वृत्रो यथा रामेण रावणः॥ यथा कृष्णेन नरको मुस्श्च नरकारिणा। कार्तवीर्यश्च रामेण भार्गवेण यथा हतः॥ सज्ञातिबान्धवः शूर समरे युद्धदुर्मदः। रणे कृत्वा महद् युद्धं घोरं त्रैलोक्यमोहनम्॥ यथा स्कन्देन महिषो यथा रुद्रेण चान्धकः। तथाऽर्जुनेन सहतो द्वैरथे युद्धदुर्मदः॥ सामात्यबान्धवो राजन् कर्णः प्रहरतां वरः।
en: Thus this destruction was brought about, while Karna and Arjuna fought against each other, even as Vritra was slain by Mahendra or as Ravana by Rama or as Naraka and Mura were slain by Krishna in battle, or as Kartavirjya of mighty strength by Rama of the Bhrigu race. That hero (Kartavirya), who is incapable of being vanquished, had fallen with all his friends and relatives, after having fought a great and terrible battle, renowned in the three worlds. Mahisha was slain by Skanda, as Andhaka by Rudra; even as that hero invincible in battle, was slain by Arjuna in a single engagement of two cars.' O, king that great smiter of enemies Karna, who was the hope of victory of all the Dhartarashtras and the cause of that hostilities, (was slain) with all his counselors and friends.

sn: जयाशा धार्तराष्ट्राणां वैरस्य च मुखं यतः॥ तीर्णस्तत् पाण्डवो राजन् यत् पुरा नावबुध्यसे। उच्यमानो महाराज बन्धुभिर्हितकाटिभिः॥ तदिदं समनुप्राप्तं व्यसनं सुमहात्मययम्।
en: The awful ocean has now been crossed over by the sons of Pandu. O great king, although you were told by all your well-wishing friends all this, yet you could not realise before the nature of this calamity, which has not befallen you, bringing about a great slaughter (of your troops).

sn: पुत्राणां राज्यकामानां त्वया राजन् हितैषिणा॥ अहितान्येव चीर्णानि तेषां तत् फलमागतम्॥
en: O monarch, it is by you, who are desirous of doing good to your sons, that mischief's have been wrought upon them, most covetous of kingdom as they are. The consequence of those mischief have now come.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच आख्याता मामकास्तात निहता युधि पाण्डवैः। हताश्च पाण्डवेयानां मामकै—हि संजया॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O son, you have related which of my followers were slain in battle by the Pandavas. But now do you tell me, O Sanjaya, which of the Pandavas were slain by the warriors of my side.

sn: संजय उवाच कुन्तयो युधि विक्रान्ता महासत्त्वा महाबलाः। सानुबन्धाः सहामात्या गाङ्गेयेन निपातिताः॥
en: Sanjaya said All the descendants of Kunti, exerting themselves with prowess in battle and possessed of great spirit and strength, was slain by Bhishma in battle with all their kinsmen and counselors.

sn: नारायण बलभद्राः शूराश्च शतशोऽपरे। अनुरक्ताश्च वीरेण भीष्मेण युधि पातिताः॥
en: The Narayanas, the Vallavas, the Ramas and hundreds of others warriors, attached to the Pandavas in the field, were all slain by Bhishma in battle.

sn: समः किरीटिना संख्ये वीर्येण च बलेन च। सत्यजित् सत्यसंधेन द्रोणेन निहतो युधि॥
en: Satyajit, who was like Kiritin (Arjuna, decked in diadem) fighting in the field, both in prowess and strength, was slain in battle by Drona, who was of sure aim.

sn: पञ्चालानां महेष्वासाः सर्वे युद्धिविशारदाः। द्रोणेन सह संगम्य गता वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: All the mighty bowmen among the Pandavas, who were expert in battle, departed to the region of Death, after having fought with Drona.

sn: तथा विराटदुपदौ वृद्धौ सहसुतौ नृपौ। पराक्रमन्तौ मित्रार्थे द्रोणेन निहतौ रणे॥
en: So also, the old king Virata and Drupada, displaying their prowess in battle, were slain by Drona for sake of their ally, with all their sons.

sn: यो बाल एव समरे सम्मितः सव्यसाचिना। केशवेन च दुर्धर्षो बलदेवेन वा विभो॥ परेषां कदनं कृत्वा महास्थविशारदः। परिवार्य महामात्रैः षड्भिः परमकै रथैः॥ अशक्नुवद्भिर्बीभत्सुमभिमन्युनिपातितः।
en: O Lord that invincible hero, Abhimanyu, who, as a boy, was like Savyasachin, Keshava and Baladeva and who also was greatly skilled in battle, was surrounded by six of the most exalted of the car-warriors and slain by them, after having made an utter extermination of the enemies, when they (warriors) became incapable of withstanding Arjuna.

sn: कृतं तं विरथं वीरं क्षत्रधर्मे व्यवस्थितम्॥ दौःशासनिर्महाराज सौभद्रं हतवान् रणे।
en: O powerful monarch, the son of Dushasana, after having dispossessed the son of Subhadra of his car, who was still observing the duties of a Kshatriya slew him in battle.

sn: सपत्नानां निहन्तां च महत्या सेनया वृत्तः॥ अम्बष्ठस्य सुतः श्रीमान् मित्रहेतोः पराक्रमन्। आसाद्य लक्ष्मणं वीरं दुर्योधनसुतं रणे॥ सुमहत् कदनं कृत्वा गतो वैवस्वतक्षयम्।
en: The handsome slayer of Patachcharas, having been encompassed by a large force, exerted himself with great prowess for the sake of his ally; and along with Ambashtha, approached heroic Lakshmana the son of Duryodhana, in battle; and also having made an immense slaughter of the enemies, repaired to the abode of Death.

sn: बृहन्तः सुमहेष्वासः कृतास्त्रो युद्धदुर्मदः॥ दुःशासनेन विक्रम्य गमितो यमसादनम्।
en: Brihanta, that great bowman, who was well acquainted with the use of weapons and most invincible in battle, was sent to the region of Yama by Dushasana showing forth his prowess in the field.

sn: मणिमान् दण्डधारश्च राजानौ युद्धदुर्मदौ॥ पराक्रमन्तौ मित्रार्थे द्रोणेन युधि पातितौ।
en: The two princes, Manimat and Dandadhara, who were incapable of being vanquished in battle and also who exerted themselves with prowess, were, for the sake of their friends, slain by Drona.

sn: अंशुमान् भोजराजस्तु सहसैन्यै महारथः॥ भारद्वाजेन विक्रम्य गमितो यमसादनम्।
en: So also, the mighty car-warrior Ansuman, the king of the Bhojas, was dispatched to the abode of Death with his soldiers by the son of Bharadvaja, displaying his prowess in battle.

sn: सामुद्रश्चिसेनश्च सह पुत्रेण भारत॥ समुद्रसेनेन बलाद् गमितो यमसादनम्।
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, Chitrasena, dwelling in the sea-coast, was means forcibly sent with his son, to the region of Yama by Samudrasena.

sn: अनूपवासी नीलश्च व्याघ्रदत्तश्च वीर्यवान्॥ अश्वत्थाम्ना विकर्णेन गमितो यमसादनम्।
en: O powerful monarch, Neela, the dweller of Anupa and Vyaghradatta, endued with great prowess, both these were sent to the abode of Yama by Ashvatthaman.

sn: चित्रायुधश्चित्रयोधी कृत्वा च कदनं महत्॥ चित्रमार्गेण विक्रम्य विकर्णेन हतो मृधे।
en: After having wrought an immense carnage, the two heroes, Chitrayudha and Chitrayodhi, were slain in battle by Vikarna, who was well acquainted with the diverse of stratagems and displayed immense prowess (in the field),

sn: वृकोदरसमो युद्धे वृतः कैकेययोधिभिः॥ कैकेयेन च विकम्य भ्रात्रा भ्राता निपातितः।
en: Having been encompassed by the Kaikeya warriors, the king of the Kaikeyas, who was the peer of Vrikodara in battle, was slain by (his brother) Kaikeya showing forth his prowess in this encounter of brother against brother.

sn: जनमेजयो गदायोधी पर्वतीयः प्रतापवान्॥ दुर्मुखेन महाराज तव पुत्रेण पातितः।
en: O great monarch, that great wielder of mace, Janamejaya, the dweller of the hilly country, who was possessed of great energy, was slain by your son Durmukha.

sn: रोचमानो नरव्याघ्रौ रोचमानौ ग्रहाविव।॥ द्रोणेन युगपद् राजन् दिवं सम्प्रापितौ शरैः।
en: O monarch, the two most exalted of persons, the two brothers known by the name of Rochamana (the bright), like two bright planets, were caused by Drona with his shafts, to repair at the same time to heaven.

sn: नृपाश्च प्रतियुध्यन्तः पराक्रान्ता विशाम्पते॥ कृत्वा नसुकरं कर्म गता वैवस्वतक्षयम्।
en: O ruler of earth, several other monarchs, possessed of immense prowess, who were engaged in battle (on the side of the Pandavas), all repaired to the abode of Death, after having achieved the most terrible and difficult deeds.

sn: पुरुजित् कुन्ति भोजश्च मातुलौ सव्यसाचिनः॥ संग्रामनिर्जिताँल्लोकान् गमितौ द्रोणसायकैः।
en: Purujit and Kuntibhoja, the two maternal uncles of Savyasachin, were sent by the shafts of Drona to those regions that are attainable in battle.

sn: अभिभूः काशिराजश्च काशिकैर्बहुभिर्वृतः॥ वसुदानस्य पुत्रेण न्यासितो देहमाहवे।
en: Having been encompassed by a large number of the Kashis, Abhivus, the king of the Kashis, was caused to lay dawn his body (i.e. life) in battle by the son of Vasudana.

sn: अमितौजा युधामन्युरुत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान्॥ निहत्य शतशः शूरानस्मदीयैर्निपातिताः।
en: Having slaughtered hundreds of heroes, Amitaujah, Yudhamanyu and Uttamanjah endued with prowess, were all slain by our followers.

sn: मित्रवर्मा त पाञ्चाल्यः क्षत्रधर्मा च भारत॥ द्रोणेन परमेष्वासो गमितो यमसादनम्।
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, the Panchala prince, Mitravarman and Kshatradharman, those mightest bowmen, were sent to the abode of Yama by Drona.

sn: शिखण्डितनयो युद्धे क्षत्रदेवो युधां पतिः॥ लक्ष्मणेन हतो राजंस्तव पौत्रेण भारत।
en: O King! In that battle, O Bharata! the foremost of warriors, son of Shikhandi Khatradeva was slain by your grandson Lakshmana.

sn: सुचित्रश्चित्रवर्मा च पितापुत्रौ महारथौ॥ प्रचरन्तौ महावीरौ द्रोणेन निहतो रणे।
en: The two heroes, possessed of mighty strength, Suchitra and Chitravarman, who are related to each others as father and son, roving about in the field of battle, were slain by Drona.

sn: वार्धक्षेमिर्महाराज समुद्र इव पर्वणि॥ आयुध्क्षयमासाद्य प्रशान्तिं परमां गतः।
en: O great king, when all his weapons were exhausted, Vardhakshemi obtained in the end the superior kind of peace, even as the ocean at full tide becomes peaceful after its (superfluous) water has been drained up.

sn: सेनाबिन्दुसुतः श्रेष्ठः शास्त्रवान् प्रहरन् युधि॥ बाबिकेन महाराज कौरवेन्द्रेण पातितः।
en: O monarch, having destroyed innumerable enemies in battle, Senavindu, that foremost of the Kurus, was himself slain by Balhika the great Kaurava prince,

sn: धृष्टकेतुर्महाराज चेदीनां प्रवरो रथः॥ कृत्वा नसुकरं कर्म गतो वैवस्वतक्षयम्।
en: O powerful king, having achieved the most difficult feats, Dhristaketu that greatest carwarrior among the Chedis, departed to the abode of Death.

sn: तथा सत्यधृतिर्वीरः कृत्वा कदनमाहवे॥ पाण्डवार्थे पराक्रान्तो गमितो यमसादनम्।
en: So also, having wrought a carnage of the foes in battle for the sake of his ally, the Pandava army, heroic Satyadhriti, who was possessed of great energy, was sent to the region of Yama.

sn: सेनाबिन्दुः कुरुश्रेष्ठ कृत्वा कदनमाहवे॥ पुत्रस्तु शिशुपालस्य सुकेतुः पृथिवीपतिः। निहत्य शात्रवान् संख्ये द्रोणेन निहतो युधि॥
en: Having slaughtered the enemies in battle, the lord of the earth Suketu, the son of Sishupala, was slain by Drona in the field.

sn: तथा सत्यधृतिर्वीरो मदिराश्वश्च वीर्यवान्। सूर्यदत्तश्च विक्रान्तो निहतो द्रोणसायकैः॥
en: So also, Satyadhriti the chief of the Matshyas and powerful Madirashva and Suryadatta of mighty prowess, slaughtered by the shafts of Drona.

sn: श्रेणिमांश्च महाराज युध्यमानः पराक्रमी। कृत्वा नसुकरं कर्म गतो वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: O great king, having achieved the most terrible tasks Srenimat, who was engaged in battle and possessed of mighty prowess, had gone to the abode of Death. were

sn: तथैव युधि विक्रान्तो मागधः परमास्त्रवित्। भीष्मेण निहतो राजशेतेऽद्य परवीरहा।॥
en: So also, O king, having been slain by Bhishma, the Magadha prince, that slayer of heroes on the side of the foes, who displayed his prowess in battle and was highly acquainted with the use of weapons, is now lying (in the field).

sn: विराटपुत्रः शङ्खस्तु उत्तरश्च महारथः। कुर्वन्तौ सुमहत् कर्म गतौ वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Having achieved the tasks most difficult to perform, the sons of Virata, Sankha and Uttara of mighty strengths departed to the abode of Death.

sn: वसुदानश्च कदनं कुर्वाणोऽतीव संयुगे। भारद्वाजेन विक्रम्य गमितो यमसादनम्३८॥
en: Having made a great slaughter in battle, Vasudana was sent to the abode of Yama, by the son of Bharadvaja careering in battle with great prowess.

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवः पाण्डवानां महारथः। हता द्रोणेन विक्रम्य यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: These and several other mighty car-warriors among the Pandavas were slain by Drona displaying their prowess in battle. These are all that you had asked me.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच मामकस्यास्य सैन्यस्य हृतोत्सेकस्य संजय। अवशेषं न पश्यामि ककुदे मृदिते सति॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, when the most exalted of my heroes were slain, I do not see the survival of the rest of warriors on my side that had escaped the destruction.

sn: तौ हि वीरौ महेष्वासौ मदर्थे कुरुसत्तमौ। भीष्मद्रोणौ हतो श्रुत्वा नार्थो वै जीवितेऽसति॥
en: Having heard that those two mighty bowmen, the foremost of the Kurus, the heroic Bhishma and Drona, were slain for my sake, what necessity can I have for my life?

sn: न च मृष्यामि राधेयं हतमाहवशोभनम्। यस्य बाह्वोर्बलं तुल्यं कुञ्जराणां शतं शतम्॥
en: Also I cannot bear the fall of the son of Radha, who adorned the field of battle (by his presence) and whose strength of arms was equal to the power of ten thousand elephants.

sn: हतप्रवरसैन्यं मे यथा शंससि संजय। अहतानपि मे शंस येऽत्र जीवन्ति केचन॥
en: After the most heroic warriors on my side were slain in-battle, O Suta, the best of speakers, do you relate to me which of my army are still alive unhurt.

sn: एतेषु हि मृतेष्वद्य ये त्वया परिकीर्तिताः। येऽपि जीवन्ति ते सर्वे मृता इति मतिर्मम॥
en: The names of those, who are slain today, had been described by you. But my opinion is that those who are still alive are now perhaps dead.

sn: संजय उवाच यस्मिन् महास्त्राणि समर्पितानि चित्राणि शुभ्राणि चतुर्विधानित दिव्यानि राजन् विहितानि चैव द्रोणेन वीरे द्विजसत्तमेन॥
en: Sanjaya said O monarch, the hero-to whom were given the four kinds of brilliant and mighty weapons of innumerable shapes, as well as various other celestial weapons by Drona the best of the regenerate persons.

sn: महारथः कृतिमान् क्षिप्रहस्तो दृढायुधो दृढमुष्टिढेषुः। स वीर्यमान् द्रोणपुत्रस्तरस्वी व्यवस्थितो योद्धुकामस्त्वदर्थे ॥
en: That great car-warrior, the high-souled son of Drona's-who is most expert in military performances, light-handed, having steng weapons and the strongest fist among the boxers and capable of shooting surely from a distance, is still staying in the field most desirous of fighting for your sake.

sn: आनर्तवासी हृदिकात्मजोऽसौ महारथः सात्वतानां वरिष्ठः। स्वयं भोजः कृतवर्मा कृतास्त्रो व्यवस्थितो योद्धुकामस्त्वदर्थे। ८॥
en: That mighty car-warrior Kritavarman, that son of Hridika, the dweller of the country of Anarta, the most exalted of the Satvatas, that chief of the Bhojas himself is still staying in the field of battle, desirous of fighting for your sake, as he is well acquainted with the use of weapons.

sn: आर्यायनिः समरे दुष्प्रकम्प्यः सेनाग्रणीः प्रथमस्तावकानाम्। यः स्वस्त्रीयान् पाण्डवेयान् विसृज्य सत्यां वाचं स्वां चिकीर्षुस्तरस्वी॥ तेजोवधं सूतपुत्रस्य संख्ये प्रतिश्रुत्याजातशत्रोः पुरस्तात्। दुराधर्षः शक्रसमानवीर्यः शल्यः स्थितो योद्धुकामस्त्वदर्थे॥
en: Having forsaken the sons of his own sister, the Pandavas, with the desire of making good his words, that son of Artayana, who never trembles in battle, who is the head of all the warriors and the first of those on your side, who is possessed of immense activity and who has promised before Ajatasatru that he would destroy the energy of the son of Suta in battle, who is Shakra's peer in prowess, that hero Shalya is still staying in the field desirous of fighting for your sake.

sn: आजानेयैः सैन्धवैः पर्वतीयै नदीजकाम्बोजवनायुजैश्च। गान्धारराजः स्वबलेन युक्तो व्यवस्थितो योदुकामस्त्वदर्थे॥
en: Attended by an excellent force consisting of the Ajaneyas, the Saindhavas, the Highlanders, the dwellers of the river-basins, the Kambojas, the Vanayus and the Balhikas, the king of the Gandharas, is still staying in the field desirous of fighting for your sake.

sn: शारद्वतो गौतमश्चापि राजन् महाबाहुर्बहुचित्रास्त्रयोधी। धनुश्चित्रं सुमहद् भारसाहं व्यवस्थितो योद्धुकामः प्रगृह्य॥
en: O monarch, Gautama, the son of Sharadvata, of great strength and variously skilled in the use of innumerable weapons, is staying in the field desirous of fighting, upholding an extraordinary bow capable of bearing a pretty great strain.

sn: महारथः केकयराजपुत्रः सदश्वयुक्तं च पताकिनं च। रथं समारुह्य कुरुप्रवीर व्यवस्थितो योद्धुकामस्त्वदर्थे ॥
en: Riding in the front part of his car, yoked to beautiful horses and furnished with standards, the son of the king of Kekayas, that mighty bowman, that foremost of men, is standing on the field with the desire of fighting for your sake.

sn: तथा सुतस्ते ज्वलनार्कवर्णं रथं समास्थाय कुरुप्रवीरः। व्यवस्थितः पुरुमित्रो नरेन्द्र व्यभ्रे सूर्यो भ्राजमानो यथा खे॥
en: O lord of men, riding on a car resembling the Sun or the fire in splendour, similarly your son, Purumitra, that best hero amongst the Kurus, is careering on the field, even as the Sun, shining brightly wanders on the cloudless firmament.

sn: दुर्योधन नागकुलस्य मध्ये व्यवस्थितेः सिंह इवाबभासे। रथेन जाम्बूनदभूषणेन व्यवस्थितः समरे योत्स्यमानः॥
en: Riding on a car adorned with gold, Duryodhana of mighty prowess, in the midst of a force consisting on the elephants, is staying on the field with all his heroic soldiers, ready for battling.

sn: स राजमध्ये पुरुषप्रवीरो रराज जाम्बूनदचित्रवर्मा। पद्मप्रभो वह्निरिवाल्पधूमो मेघान्तरे सूर्य इव प्रकाशः॥
en: Putting on an armour decked in gold, that foremost of persons, possessing the splendour of a lotus, shone in the midst of kings, like the fire sending out little smoke, or like the Sun rising after he has emerged from the clouds.

sn: स्तवात्मजः सत्यसेनश्च वीरः। व्यवस्थितौ चित्रसेनेन सार्ध हृष्टात्मानौ समरे योद्धुकामौ॥
en: Similarly, your sons, Sushena furnished with the sword and shield and the war-like Satyasena are still waiting on the field of battle with joy and desirous of battling for your sake.

sn: हीनिषेवो भारत राजपुत्र उग्रायुधः क्षणभोजी सुदर्शः। जारासंधिः प्रथमश्चादृढश्च चित्रायुधः श्रुतवर्मा जयश्च॥ शलश्च सत्यव्रतदुःशलौ च व्यवस्थिताः सहसैन्या नराग्र्याः।
en: The modest princes of the Bharata race, namely Chitrayudha, Shrutavarman, Jaya, Shala, Satyavrata and Dusshala, who are all endued with mighty strength, are still staying in the field with the desire of battling.

sn: कैतव्यानामधिपः शूरमानी रणे रणे शत्रुहा राजपुत्रः॥ रथी हयी नागपत्तिप्रयायी व्यवस्थितो योधुकामस्त्वदर्थे।
en: The lord of the Kitavyas, that prince, that smiter of foes, who considers himself most heroic and who is careering in the field accompanied by both infantry and cavalry, as well as by the elephant force and cars, is still in the field with the desire of fighting for your sake.

sn: वीरः श्रुतायुश्च धृतायुधश्च चित्राङ्गदश्चित्रसेनश्च वीरः॥ व्यवस्थिता योधुकामा नराम्या: प्रहारिणो मानिनः सत्यसंधाः।
en: Those foremost of persons, those mighty smiters of enemies, considering themselves highly proud, the heroic Shrutayus, Shrutayudha, Chitrangada and Chitravarman, all of whom are of sure aim, are similarly staying in the field with the desire of battling.

sn: कर्णात्मजः सत्यसंधो महात्मा व्यवस्थितः समरे यो कामः॥ अथापरौ कर्णसुतौ वरास्त्री व्यवस्थितौ लघुहस्तौ नरेन्द्र। बलं महद् दुर्भिदमल्पधैर्यैः सम्माश्रितौ योत्स्यमानौ त्वदर्थे॥
en: Satyasandha, the lofty-minded son of Karna, is still on the field, desirous of battling. So also, O lord of men, two other sons of Karna, who are acquainted with the use of excellent weapons and are light-handed, are both staying on the field with the desire of battling for your sake, being accompanied by a large army incapable of being vanquished by a force of little prowess.

sn: एतैश्च मुख्यैरपरैश्च राजन् योधप्रवीरैरमितप्रभावैः। व्यवस्थितो नागकुलस्य मध्ये यथा महेन्द्रः कुरुराजो जयाय॥
en: O monarch, being surrounded by these and several other chiefs, who are all best of warriors and are endued with immeasurable prowess, the Kuru king is staying in the field, in the midst of an elephant force, with the object of winning victory; even as Indra (stands in the midst of the celestials).

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच आख्याता जीवमान येऽपरे सैन्या यथायथम्। इतीदमवगच्छामि व्यक्तमर्थाभिपत्तितः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said All have been related to me in detail viz. who having escaped from the enemies are alive. From this I clearly understand which side will win the victory; this may really be arrived at from facts.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ब्रुवत्रेव तदा धृतराष्टोऽम्बिकासुतः। हतप्रवीरं विध्वस्तं किचिच्छेषं स्वकं बलम्॥ श्रुत्वा व्यामोहमागच्छच्छोकव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः।
en: Vaishampayana said While Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, was thus addressing and also having heard that the most exalted of the heroic warriors on his side were slain and only a small portion of the whole army was alive, he was plunged deep in sorrow and his heart, too, was greatly agitated by grief.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच मुह्यमानोऽब्रवीच्चापि मुहूर्त तिष्ठ संजय॥ व्याकुलं मे मनस्तात श्रुत्वा सुमहदप्रियम्। मनो मुह्यति चाङ्गानि न च शक्नोमि धारितुम॥
en: Dnritarashtra said Thereafter, he (the king) became almost senseless and addressed (after having recovered his senses a little) Sanjaya, saying.-'Do you stop for a moment.' O son, having heard of this exceedingly evil intelligence, my mind becomes becomes greatly perplexed. My mind (brain) as well as the different limbs are growing paralyzed, which I am not able to uphold.

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। भ्रान्तचित्तस्ततः सोऽथ बभूव जगतीपतिः॥
en: Having uttered these words, Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, that lord of down (upon the ground).

sn: जनमेजय उवाच श्रुत्वा कर्णं हतं युद्धे पुत्रांश्चैव निपातितान्। नरेन्द्रः किंचिदाश्वस्तो द्विजश्रेष्ठ किमब्रवीत्॥
en: Janamejaya said O foremost of regenerate persons, being consoled a little, what did the lord of kings say, when he heard of the death of Karna, as well as the fall of his sons?

sn: प्राप्तवान् परम् दुखं पुत्रव्यसनजं महत्। तस्मिन् यदुक्तवान् काले तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः॥
en: He (the monarch) attained exceedingly great uneasiness in the mind) arising from the fault of his sons. Relate to me, as I ask you, what did he say at that time.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा कर्णस्य निधनमश्रद्धेयमिवाद्भुतम्। भूतसम्मोहनं भीमं मेहोः संसर्पणं यथा।॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard of the death of Karna, which, being extraordinary, was incredible, which stupefied the senses of all creatures, which was most dreadful and which was like the downfall of the mountain of Meru.

sn: चित्तमोहमिवायुक्त भार्गवस्य महामतेः। पराजयमिवेन्द्रस्य द्विषद्भयो भीमकर्मणः॥
en: And which (the fall of Karna), was as impossible as the dullness of the intellect of highly energetic Bhargava and which, again, was like the defeat of Indra of formidable deeds at the hands of the enemies.

sn: दिवः प्रपतनं भानोरुपया॑मिव महाद्युतेः। संशोषणमिवाचिन्त्यं समुद्रस्याक्षयाम्भसः॥
en: And which (the fall of Karna), also, was like the falling of the highly blazing Sun upon the earth from the heaven and which was as incomprehensible as the drying up of the ocean, whose waters are never exhausted.

sn: महीवियद्दिगम्बूनां सर्वनाशमिवाद्भुतम्। कर्मणोरिव वैफल्यमुभयोः पुण्यपापयोः॥
en: And which (the fall of Karna), again, was as extraordinary as the total destruction of the earth, the firmament, the different points of the horizon and the waters and also as the fruitlessness of both virtuous and vicious acts.

sn: संचिन्त्य निपुणं बुद्धया धृतराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः। नेदमस्तीति संचिन्त्य कर्णस्य समरे वधम्॥
en: And then having meditated most skillfully in the mind upon the slaying of Karna in battle in the similar manner and also having deeply thought upon this viz. that his army was no more.

sn: प्राणीनामेवमन्येषां स्यादपीति विनाशनम्। शोकाग्निना दह्यमानो धम्यमान इवाशये॥
en: And also having argued that the other creatures would be of the similar fate, Dhritarashtra, the lord of men, was burnt by the fire of grief and looked like a burning serpent.

sn: विस्त्रस्ताङ्ग श्वसन् दीनो हाहेत्युकत्वा सुदुःखित। विललाप महाराज धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः॥
en: With paralysed limbs, sighing long, looking helpless, uttering-woe and alas and highly oppressed with with sorrow, the great king Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, became to weep most bitterly.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच संजयाधिररथिवीर सिंहद्विरदविक्रमः। वृषभप्रतिमस्कन्धो वृषभाक्षगतिश्चरन्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, the war-like son of Adhiratha was possessed of the strength of a lion or an elephant; and his neck was like that of a bull; and his eyes, speed and voice were also like those of a bull.

sn: वृषभो वृषभस्येव यो युद्धे न निवर्तते। शत्रोरपि महेन्द्रस्य वज्रसंहननो युवा॥
en: That young man of limbs as strong as the thunderbolt never desisted from battle even with so great an enemy as Indra himself, even as a bull never desists from battle with another bull.

sn: यस्य ज्यातलशब्देन शरवृष्टिरवेण च। रथाश्वनरमातङ्गा नावतिष्ठन्ति संयुगे॥
en: At the sound of whose bowstring and at the roaring of whose arrowy showers, the men and horses (ihe infantry and the cavalry), the cars and elephants could not stand in the field of battle.

sn: यमाश्रित्य महाबाहुं विद्विषां जयकाङ्क्षया। दुर्योधनोऽकरोद् वैरं पाण्डुपुत्रैर्महारथैः॥
en: Having taken refuge under the mighty arms of that imperishable slayer of innumerable foes, Duryodhana made enemies of the sons of Pandu, those great car-warriors.

sn: स कथं रथिनां श्रेष्ठः कर्णः पार्थेन संयुगे। निहतः पुरुष व्याघ्रः प्रसह्यासह्यविक्रमः॥
en: How could Karna, that foremost of carwarriors, that powerful hero, that one of mighty prowess, was slain in battle by force by the son of Pritha?

sn: यो नामन्यत वै नित्यमच्युतं च धनंजयम्। न वृष्णीन् सहितान्यान् स्वबाहुबलदर्पितः॥
en: Placing confidence upon the strength of his own arms, he (Karna) always indeed did care neither for Achyuta, nor for Dhananjaya, nor for the whole of the Vrishni race nor for the other enemies.

sn: शार्ङ्गगाण्डीवधन्वानौ सहितावपराजितौ। अहं दिव्याद् रथादेकः पातयिष्यायमि संयुगे॥
en: 'In the field of battle, alone I shall hurl down at once both the wielder of Gandiva bow, who are unconquerable and are united together, from their celestial cars.'

sn: इति यः सततं मन्दमवोचल्लोभमोहितम्। दुर्योधनमवाचीनं राज्यकामुकमातुरम्॥
en: This (the above saying) he always uttered to Duryodhana, who was bad, darkened by avarice, foolish and desirous of kingdom and also who was highly afflicted.

sn: योऽजयत् सर्वकाम्बोजानावन्त्यान् केकयैः सह। गान्धारान् मद्रकान् मत्स्यास्त्रिगर्तास्तङ्गणाशकान्॥१८
en: That hero (Karna) had subdued the unusually powerful and invincible enemies namely the Gandharvas, the Madrakas, the Matsyas, the Trigartas, the Tanganas the Shashas.

sn: पञ्चारां विदेहांश्च कुलिन्दान् काशिकोसलान्। सुह्यानङ्गांश्च वङ्गांश्च निषादान् पुण्ड्रचीरकान्॥
en: And the Panchalas, the Videhas, the Kulindas, the Kashi-Kosalas, the Suhmas, the Angas, the Bangas, the Nishadhas, the Pundras, the Kichakas.

sn: वत्सान् कलिङ्गाहस्तरलानश्मकानृषिकानपि। जित्वैतान् समरे वीरश्चके वलिभृतः पुरा॥
en: And the Vatsyas, the Kalingas, the Taralas, the Ashmakas and the Rishikas. In the days of yore, he subjugated these (above-mentioned) heroes in battle and made then pay tribute (to us).

sn: शरवातैः सुनिशितैः सुतीक्ष्णैः कङ्कपत्रिभिः। दुर्योधनस्य वृद्ध्यर्थं राधेयो रथिनां वरः॥ दिव्यास्त्रविन्महातेजाः कर्णो वैकर्तनो वृषः। सेनागोपश्च स कथं शत्रुभिः परमास्त्रवित्॥ घातितः पाण्डवैः शूरैः समरे वीर्यशालिभिः।
en: By means of his sharpened and keen arrows, that were adorned with the Kanka feathers for the sake of Duryodhana's aggrandisement. That one (Karna) was still waiting in the field for winning victory (for Duryodhana). How was that protector of armies (on my side), that one well-versed in the use of weapons, viz. Vaikartana Karna was slain in battle by the foes, the heroic sons of Pandu, who were possessed of immense strength?

sn: वृषो महेन्द्रो देवेषु वृषः कर्णो नरेष्वपि॥ तृतीयमन्यं लोकेषु वृषं नैवानुशुश्रुम।
en: Indra is the foremost of the celestials even as Karna is the best amongst men. In this world we have not heard of a third one, who was the most exalted like them.

sn: उच्चैःश्रवा वरोऽश्वानां राज्ञां वैश्रवणो वरः॥ वरो महेन्द्रो देवानां कर्णः प्रहरतां वरः।
en: Uchchaishravas is the best of all horses, Vaishravana is the best of the Yakshas; and Indra is the foremost of the celestials; so also Karna is the best of all smiters.

sn: योजितः पार्थिवः शूरैः समथैवीर्यशालिभिः॥ दुर्योधनस्य वृद्ध्यर्थं कृत्स्त्रामुर्वीमथाजयत्।
en: Having been unsubdued by the heroic and mightest monarchs of immense prowess, he then subjugated the entire earth for the aggrandisement of Duryodhana.

sn: यं लब्ध्वा मागधो राजा सान्त्वमानोऽथ सौहदैः॥२६ अरौत्सीत् पार्थिवं क्षत्रमृते यादवकौरवान्।
en: Having obtained his (Karna's) alliance, by means of conciliating terms, by paying honours and wealth to him and also by speaking gloriously of him, the king of Magadha and opposed all the Kshatriyas of the world excepting the Kauravas and the Yadavas.

sn: तं श्रुत्वा निहतं कर्णं द्वैरथे सव्यसाचिना॥ शोकार्णवे निमग्नोऽहं भिन्ना नौरिव सागरे।
en: Having heard of the slaughter of that Karna by Savyasachin in a single combat I am plunged deep in the ocean of grief, even as a ship-wrecked one (is plunged) in the vast sea.

sn: तं वृषं निहतं श्रुत्वा द्वैरथे रथिनां वरम्॥ शोकार्णवे निमग्नोऽहमप्लवः सागरे यथा।
en: Having heard of the fall of that best of men, that foremost of car-warriors, in a single combat, I am lunged in the ocean of grief, even as a person without a boat (is plunged) in the sea.

sn: ईदृशैर्यद्यहं दुःखैन विनश्यामि संजय॥ वज्राद् दृढतरं मन्ये हृदयं मम दुर्भिदम्।
en: O Sanjaya, when having been afflicted with such a grief as this, I do not die, I suppose that my heart is harder than the thunderbolt and most impenetrable.

sn: ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिमित्राणामिमं श्रुत्वा पराभवम्॥ को मदन्यः पुमाँल्लोके न जह्यात् सूत जीवितम।
en: O Suta, having heard of this utter defeat of kinsmen, relatives and friends, what other person in this world except myself would not give up his life?

sn: विषमग्निं प्रपातं च पर्वतग्रादहं वृणे। न हि शक्ष्यामि दुःखानि सोढुं कष्टानि संजय॥
en: I desire (to swallow) poison, (to be burnt in) fire and the fall from the summit of a mountain; for I am indeed unable, O Sanjaya, to bear the grief and pain.

sn: संजय उवाच श्रिया कुलेन यशसा तपसा च श्रुतेन च। त्वामद्य सन्तो मन्यन्ते ययातिमिव नाहुषम्॥
en: Sanjaya said The sages consider you to be equal to Yayati, the son of Nahusha, in beauty, in lineage, in celebrity, in austerity and in the knowledge about the Shastras.

sn: श्रुते महर्षिप्रतिमः कृतकृत्योऽसि पार्थिव। पर्यवस्थापयात्मानं मा विषादे मनः कृथा॥
en: O monarch, you are equal to a great sage in learning; and you are highly successful in respect of all actions. So be you concentrated in self and let not your heart be plunged in sorrow.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच दैवमेव परं मन्ये धिक् पौरुषमनर्थकम्। यत्र शालप्रतीकाशः कर्णोऽहन्यत संयुगे॥
en: Dhritarashtra said I consider Destiny to be superior and human effort to be fruitless; for the reason that Karna, who was like a Sala tree, was slain in battle.

sn: हत्वा युधिष्ठिरानीकं पञ्चालानां रथव्रजान्। प्रताप्य शरवर्षेण दिश: सर्वा महारथः॥
en: Having slain the entire force of Yudhishthira as well as the car-warriors of the Panchala race and having afflicted, by the showers of arrows, the men in the different directions of the horizon.

sn: मोहयित्वा रणे पार्थान् वज्रहस्त इवासुरान्। स कथं निहतः शेते वायुरुग्ण इव द्रुमः॥
en: And also having rendered the Parthas senseless in battle, even as Indra with the thunderbolt in his hand, stupifying the Asuras, how has that great car-warrior (Karna) been slain in battle, who now lies dead (in the field) like a large tree up-rotted by the wind.

sn: शोकस्यान्तं न पश्यामि पारं जलनिधेरिव। चिन्ता मे वर्धतेऽतीव मुमूर्षा चापि जायते॥
en: I do not find the end of my so 'w like that of the overflowed ocean. My anxieties are growing more acute; and the desire for death has been growing in me.

sn: कर्णस्य निधनं श्रुत्वा विजयं फाल्गुनस्य च। अश्रद्धेयमहं मन्ये वधं कर्णस्य संजय॥
en: Having heard of the intelligence of the slaughter of Karna and the victory of Falguna. To me, O Sanjaya, the death of Karna, seems to be incredible.

sn: वज्रसारमयं नूनं हृदयं दुर्भिदं मम। यच्छ्रुत्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रं हतं कर्णं न दीर्यते॥
en: Really, my heart is pretty well hard and seems to be made up of the essence of the thunder-bolt, because it does not split up into thousand pieces on my hearing of the death of Karna.

sn: आयुनूनं सुदीर्घं मे विहित दैवतैः पुरा। यत्र कर्णं हतं श्रुत्वा जीवामीह सुदुःखितः॥
en: Indeed, my life was ordained before (my birth) to be pretty long by Destiny; since, when having heard of the slaughter of Karna, I am still alive, although I am highly afflicted with grief.

sn: घिग्जीवितमिदं चैव सुहृद्धीनश्च संजय। अद्य चाहं दशोमेतां गतः संजय गर्हिताम्॥
en: O Sanjaya, let there be shame to this my life, who am deprived of friends. Rebuked to iny life, I have been reduced today to this hateful condition.

sn: कृपणं वर्तयिष्यामि शोच्यः सर्वस्य मन्दधीः। अहमेव पुरा भूत्वा सर्वलोकस्य सत्कृतः॥ परिभूतः कथं सूत परैः शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्।
en: Foolish as I am and subject to universal pity, I shall (hereafter) have to lead a miserable life. O Suta, having at first been highly esteemed by all people, how shall I, being vanquished by the enemies, be able to hold my life?

sn: दुःखात् सुदुःखव्यसनं प्राप्तवानस्मि संजय॥ भीष्मद्रोणवधैनैव कर्णस्य च महात्मनः।
en: O Sanjaya, on the death of Bhishma, Drona and the lofty-minded Karna, I have attained to the greatest sorrow and calamity.

sn: नावशेष प्रपश्यामि सूतपुत्रे हते युधि॥ स हि पारो महानासीत् पुत्राणां मम संजय।
en: When the son of Suta was slain in battle, I do not see the end (viz. that any one on my side will escape the slaughter); since he, indeed, O Sanjaya, was the best means of crossing over (this ocean of hostilities) to my sons.

sn: युद्धे हि निहतः शूरो विसृजन् सायकान् बहून्॥ को हि मे जीवितेनार्थस्तमृते पुरुषर्षभम्।
en: While that hero was showering forth innumerable arrows, he was slain in battle. Without that foremost of persons what necessity have I for my life."

sn: रथादाधिरथिनं न्यपतत् सायकार्दितः॥ पर्वतस्येव शिखरं वज्रपाताद् विदारितम्।
en: Having been highly afflicted with the showers of arrows, the son of Adhiratha, indeed, fell down from his car, like the summit of a mountain, split up by the fall of the thunder-bolt.

sn: स शेते पृथिवीं नूनं शोभयन् रुधिरोक्षितः॥ मातङ्ग इव मत्तेन द्विपेन्द्रेण निपातितः
en: Surely having adorned the earth, he, besmeared with blood, sleeps in the ground, like an elephant killed by an infuriate lord of elephants.

sn: यो बलं धार्तराष्ट्राणां पाण्डवानां यतो भयम्॥ सोऽर्जुनेन हतः कर्णः प्रतिमानं धनुष्मताम्।
en: That Karna who had been the strength of all the Dhartarashtras and who had been the object of terror to the Pandavas and who, again, had been the type of the best of all bowmen, was slain by Arjuna.

sn: स हि वीरो महेष्वासो मित्राणामभयंकरः॥ शेते विनिहतो वीरो देवेन्द्रेण इवाचलः।
en: That heroic and mighty bowman, conferred fearlessness on my sons; and that warlike one, being in battle, lies on the ground like a mountain pierced by the lord of the celestials.

sn: पङ्गोरिवाध्वगमनं दरिद्रस्येव कामितम्॥ दुर्योधनस्य चाकूतं तृषितस्येव विपुषः।
en: The realisation of the end of Duryodhana is even like the walking of the lame and like the fulfillment of the desires of the poor and also like straying out of the water drops from the mouth of the thirsty.

sn: अन्यथा चिन्तितं कार्यमन्यथा तत् तु जायते॥ अहो नु बलवद् दैवं कालश्च दुरतिक्रमः।
en: Actions considered in one way turn out differently. Alas, Destiny is really powerful and Time is insuperable?

sn: पलायमानः कृपणे दीनात्मा दीनपौरुषः॥ कचिद् विनिहतः सूत पुत्रो दुःशासनो मम। कचिन्न दीनाचरितं कृतवांस्तात संयुगे॥ कचिन्न निहतः शूरो यथाऽन्ये क्षत्रियर्षभाः।
en: O Suta, how was my son Dushasana slain, while that one of low spirit, that wretched one of little prowess, was flying away from the battle? O son, O Suta, has he not acted in a cowardly manner? Was not that hero slain, even as the other Kshatriyas were slain?

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्य वचनं मा युध्यस्वेति सर्वदा॥ दुर्योधन नाभ्यगृह्णानमूढः पथ्यमिवौषधम्।
en: The stupid Duryodhana did not accept the constant advice of Yudhishthira viz. do not fight, which was like the wholesome drug.

sn: शरतल्पे शयानेन भीष्मेण सुमहात्मना॥ पानीयं याचितः पार्थः सोऽविध्यन्पेदिनीतलम्। जलस्य धारां जनितां दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुसुतेन च॥ अब्रवीत् स महाबाहुस्तात संशाम्य पाण्डवैः। प्रशमाद्धि भवेच्छान्तिर्मदन्तं युद्धमस्तु वः॥ भ्रातृभावेन पृथिवी भुक्ष्व पाण्डुसुतैः सह।
en: Being asked for water by Bhishma, lying on his arrowy bed, Partha of great fame pierced the surface of the earth. Having seen the torrent of water flowing from the surface of the earth caused by the son of Pandu, that mighty-armed hero addressed him saying-"O son, do you conclude peace with the Pandavas." Stop all hostilities and then there will be peace. Let your war be concluded with my death. Do you enjoy sovereignty over the earth in brotherly feelings with the sons of Pandu.

sn: अकुर्वन् वचनं तस्य नूनं शोचति पुत्रकः॥ तदिदं समनुप्राप्तं वचनं दीर्घदर्शनः।
en: am Having disregarded the advice of that one of long foresight, my son is surely repenting that advice of his is now realised into its effect..

sn: अहं तु निहतामात्यो हतपुत्रश्च संजय॥ द्यूततः कृच्छ्रमापन्नो लूनपक्ष इव द्विजः।
en: O Sanjaya, I, who deprived of counsellor and sons, have too, obtained great misery consequent upon the game at dice, like a bird shorn of its wings.

sn: यथा हि शकुनि गृह्य छित्वा पक्षौ च संजय॥ विसर्जयन्ति संहृष्टाः क्रीडमानाः कुमारकाः। लूनपक्षतया तस्य गमनं नोपपद्यते॥ तथाऽमहपि सम्प्राप्तो लूनपक्ष इव द्विजः।
en: O Sanjaya, even as the playful boys having caught a bird and torn off its wings most cheerfully let it go. And whose (the bird's) flight does not become possible in consequence of the loss of its wings; so I have become (motionless) like the bird deprived of its wings.

sn: क्षीणः सर्वार्थहीनश्च निर्घातिबन्धुवर्जितः। को दिशं प्रतिपत्स्यामि दीनः शत्रुवशं गतः॥
en: Now I am weak, destitute of all resources and deprived of all kinsmen and left my friends and also I am poor and possessed by my foes-To what point of the horizon shall I depart?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येवं धृतराष्ट्रोऽथ विलप्य बहु दुःखितः। प्रोवाच संजय भूयः शोकव्याकुलमानसः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Dhritarashtra wailed so deep, became impatient in vagary of agony and grief and again said Sanjaya the following words-

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच योऽजयत् सर्वकाम्बोजानम्बष्ठान् केकयैः सह। गान्धाराचं विदेहांश्च जित्वा कार्यार्थमाहवे॥ दुर्योधनस्य वृद्ध्यर्थं योऽजयत् पृथिवी प्रभुः। स जितः पाण्डवैः शूरैः समरे बाहुशालिभिः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Who subdued all the Kambojas an the Ambashthas along with the Kekayas and the Gandharas and the Videhas; and having defeated them in battle for the fulfillment of his wishes. That lord subdued the entire earth for the aggrandisement of Duryodhana. But he himself was subdued by the heroic Pandavas of immense capacity and mighty arms.

sn: तस्मिन् हते महेष्वासे कर्णे युधि किरीटिना। के वीराः पर्यतिष्ठन्त तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: When that mighty bowman Karna was slain in battle by the holder of Kiriti (Arjuna), what other heroes were still waiting in the field. Tell me this, O Sanjaya.

sn: कचिन्नैकः परित्यक्तः पाण्डवैर्निहतो रणे। उक्तं त्वया पुरा तात यथा वीरो निपातितः॥
en: Was he not alone and forlorn, while slain by the Pandavas in battle? O son, it was told by you beforehand how the heroes my side were slain.

sn: भीष्ममप्रतियुद्ध्यन्तं शिखण्डी सायकोत्तमैः। पातयामास समरे सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्॥
en: Shikhandin slew in battle, by means of the best of his darts, that great wielder of all weapons, Bhishma, who did not care for repelling the foes.

sn: तथा द्रौपदिना द्रोणो न्यस्यसर्वायुधो युधि। युक्तयोगो महेष्वासः शरैर्बहुभिराचितः॥ निहतः खङ्गमुद्यम्य धृष्टद्युम्नेन संजय। अन्तरेण हतावेतौ छलेन च विशेषतः॥
en: So also, O Sanjaya, by Dhristadyumna, the son of Drupada, lifting up his sword, was slain that mighty bowman Drona, practising severe asceticisin, who, being already pierced by innumerable weapons had put aside all his weapons in battle. I have, indeed, heard of this, viz. that these two, Bhishma and Drona, were slain at a disadvantage and especially by means of a stratagem.

sn: अश्रौषमहमेतद् वै भीष्मद्रोणौ निपातितौ। भीष्मद्रोणौ हि समरे न हन्याद् वज्रभृत् स्वयम्॥ न्यायेन युध्यमानौ हि तद् वै सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते।
en: Surely even the wielder of the thunderbolt (Indra) himself cannot slay in battle by just means both Bhishma and Drona, while contending in battle. Indeed, that I tell you truly.

sn: कर्णं त्वस्यन्तमस्त्राणि दिव्यानि च बहूनि च॥ कथमिन्द्रोपमं वीरं मृत्युर्युद्धे समस्पृशत्।
en: While Karna was engaged in throwing down his innumerable celestial weapons in battle, how could Death touch that hero who was like Indra himself?

sn: यस्य विद्युत्प्रभा शक्तिं दिव्यां कनकभूषणाम्॥ प्रायच्छद् द्विषतां हन्त्री कुण्डलाभ्यां पुरंदरः। यस्य सर्पमुखो दिव्यः शरः काञ्चनभूषणः॥ अशेत निहितः पत्री समरेष्वरिसूदनः। भीष्मद्रोणमुखान् वीरान् योऽवमन्ये महारथान्॥ जामदग्न्यान्महाघोरं ब्राह्ममस्त्रमशिक्षत। यश्च द्रोणमुखान् दृष्ट्वा विमुखानर्दिताशरैः॥ सौभद्रस्य महाबाहुर्व्यधमत् कार्मुकं शितैः। यश्च नागायुतप्राणं वज्ररंहसमच्यतुम्॥ विरथं सहसा कृत्वा भीमसेनमथाहसत्। सहदेवं च निर्जित्य शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ कृपया विरथं कृत्वा नाहनद् धर्मचिन्ता। यश्च मायासहस्राणि विकुर्वाणं जयैषिणम्॥ घटोत्कचं राक्षसेन्द्रं शक्रशक्त्या निजनिवान्। एतांश्च दिवसान् यस्य युद्धे भीतो धनंजयः॥ नागमद् द्वैरथं वीरः स कथं निहतो रणे।
en: Purandara awarded that here, in exchange for his ear-rings, that celestial dust that had the splendour of lightning and also that was decked in gold and capable of destroying the foes. Whose that heroes' celestial arrow, known by the name of Snakemouthed, that was decked in gold and besmeared with soft sandal and also that was capable of slaying the enemies, was always laid up in the quiver. Having disregarded the heroic great car-warriors with Bhishma and Drona at their head, that hero, O mighty monarch, learnt the use of the Brahma weapon from the son of Jamadagni. Having seen the great warriors, with Drona at their head, deeply pierced by the arrows and turning away from the battle, that mighty-armed one had severed to a the the bow of the son of Subhadra by means of his sharp arrows. Having deprived, all on sudden, Bhimasena of his car, who was of never-failing energy and had the speed of wind and the strength of ten thousand elephants, that (mighty-armed) one afterwards laughed at him. Having subdued Sahadeva by means of his sharp and straight arrows and also having deprived him of his car, he did not slay him out of kindness and feelings of virtue. He had slain, by means of his arrow given to him by Shakra, Ghatotkacha, the lord of Rakshasas, who had made a thousand illusions and who was most desirous of victory. How could that hero be slain in battle, with whom even Dhananjaya was afraid to engage in a single combat for several days.

sn: संशप्तकानां योधा ये आह्वयन्त सदान्यतः॥ एतान् हत्वा हनिष्यामि पश्चाद् वैकर्तन रणे। इति व्यपदिशन् पार्थो वर्जयन् सूतजं रणे॥ स कथं निहतो वीरः पार्थेन परवीरहा।
en: How Arjuna, the killer of chivalrous enemy in battle had killed the great warrior Karna who used to escape him in battle-field under pretext that-"I will slaughter Vaikartana Karna subsequent to kill the warriors who challenge me for battle toward another side?

sn: रथभङ्गो न चेत् तस्य धनुर्वा न व्यशीर्यत॥ न चेदस्त्राणि निर्णेशुः स कथं नहतः परैः।
en: When his car was not broken, nor his bow was cut-off, nor his weapons were exhausted, how could he (Karna), therefore, be slain by the enemies?

sn: को हि शक्तो रणे कर्णं विधुन्वानं महद् धनुः॥ विमुञ्चन्तं शरान् घोरान् दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि चाहवे। जेतुं पुरुषशार्दूलं शार्दूलमिव वेगिनम्॥
en: Who, indeed, was able to subdue Karna in battle, that foremost of persons, possessed of the speed of a tiger, while that mighty bowman was shaking his bow and shooting forth his terrible arrows and exhausting his celestial weapons in battle.

sn: ध्रुवं तस्य धनुश्छिन्नं रथो वापि महीं गतः। अस्त्राणि वा प्रणष्टानि यथा शंससि मे हतम्॥
en: Surely his bow-string was torn; his car was engulfed in the earth; and his weapons were all spent, because you tell me that he was slain.

sn: न ह्यन्यदपि पश्यामि कारणं तस्य नाशने। न हन्मि फाल्गुनं यावत् तावत् पादौ न धावये॥ इति यस्य महाघोरं व्रतमासीन्महात्मनः।
en: Indeed, I do not find any other cause of his slaughter. 'I will not have my feet washed, so long as I do not slay Falguna.' This was highly the terrible vow of the high-souled one.
