sn: यस्य भीतो रणे निद्रां धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥ त्रयोदश समा नित्यं नाभजत् पुरुषर्षभः। यस्य वीर्यवतो वीर्यमुपाश्रित्य महात्मनः॥ मम पुत्रः सभां भार्या पाण्डूनां नीतवान् बलात्। तत्रापि त सभामध्ये पाण्डवानां च पश्यताम्॥ दासभार्येति पाञ्चलीमब्रवीत् कुरुसंनिधौ। न सन्ति पतयः कृष्णे सर्वे षण्ढतिलैः समाः॥ उपतिष्ठस्व भर्तारमन्यं वा वरवर्णिनि। इत्येवं यः पुरा वाचो रूक्षाश्चाश्रवयन् रुषा॥ सभायां सूतजः कृष्णं स कथं निहतः परैः।
en: Being afraid of him, the foremost of person Yudhishthira, the royal impersonation of justice, could not enjoy sleep, while exiled in the forest, for a period of thirteen years. Relaying upon the prowess of that high-souled hero of great energy, my son forcibly dragged the wife of the Pandavas to the assembly-hall. There in the midst of that assembly, that one (Karna) called the Princess of Panchala, in the very sight of the Pandavas and also in the presence of all the Kuru's, the wife of slaves. 'O Krishna (Panchali), all your husbands are no more; and if they really exist, they are more like the sesamum seeds without the Kernel. So do you, O beautiful lady, choose another husband.' That person of the Suta race had made, anger, Krishna listen to these harsh expressions in the midst of the assembly. How was he slain by the enemies?

sn: यदि भीष्मो रणश्लाघी द्रोणो वा युधि दुर्मदः॥ न हनिष्यति कौन्तेयान् पक्षपातात् सुयोधन। पुनस्तात पाण्डवैः। सर्वानेव हनिष्यामि व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥ किं करिष्यति गाण्डीवमक्षय्यौ च महेषुधी। स्निग्धचन्दनदिग्धस्य मच्छरस्यभिधावतः॥ स नूनमृषभस्कन्धो ह्यर्जुनेन कथं हतः। यश्च गाण्डीवमुक्तानां स्पर्शमुग्रमचिन्तयन्॥ अपतिसि कृष्णेति ब्रुवन् पार्थानवैक्षत। यस्य नासीद् भयं पार्थैः सपुत्रैः सजनार्दनैः॥ स्वबाहुलमाश्रित्य मुहूर्तमपि संजय। तस्य नाहं वधं मन्ये देवैरपि सवासवैः॥ प्रतीपमभिधावद्भिः किं
en: That hero, having disregarded the severe touch of the shots from the Gandiva bow, addressed Krishna, saying,'Doubtless you have no husbands;' and he also cast his glance upon the sons of Pritha. Again, O Sanjaya, placing confidence upon the strength of his own arms, that hero had no fear even for a moment, aroused by the sons of Pritha accompanied as they were by their sons and Janardana himself. I do not consider that his slaughter can ever be brought about by all the celestials, rushing against him, headed by Vashava himself. Again, O son, how can it by the Pandavas?

sn: न हि ज्यां संस्पृशानस्य तलने वाऽपि गृह्णतः॥ पुमानाधिरथेः स्थातुं कश्चित् प्रमुखतोऽर्हति। अपि स्यान्मेदिनी हीना सोमसूर्यप्रभांशुभिः॥ न वधः पुरुषेन्द्रस्य संयुगेष्वपलायिनः।
en: While that son of Atiratha had touched the bow-string and put on his fences, surely there was no person, who could be bold enough to stand up in his front. Indeed, the earth might be deprived of the splendour of the Moon and the rays of the Sun; but the slaughter of the lord of men who did never turn away from the field could not be possible in battle.

sn: येन मन्दः सहायेन भ्रात्रा दुःशासनेन च॥ वासुदेवस्य दुर्बुद्धिः प्रत्याख्यानमरोचत। स नूनं वृषभस्कन्धं कर्णं दृष्ट्वा निपातितम्॥ दुःशासनं च निहत् मन्ये शोचति पुत्रकः।
en: Having been assisted by that hero as well as by his brother Dushasana, that my evil-souled and wicked-minded son had resolved upon to reject the proposals of Vasudeva himself. I consider that my son, having witnessed the fall of Karna of bull like shoulders and also having seen the slaughter of Dushasana, is surely lamenting.

sn: हतं वैकर्तनं श्रुत्वा द्वैरथे सव्यसाचिना॥ जयतः पाण्डवान् दृष्ट्वा किंस्विदं दुर्योधनऽब्रवीत्।
en: Having seen that the son of Vikartana was slain by Savyasachin in a single combat and that the Pandavas were victorious, what, indeed, did Duryodhana say?

sn: दुर्मर्षणं हतं दृष्ट्वा वृषसेनं च संयुगे॥ प्रभग्नं च बलं दृष्ट्वा वध्यमानं महारथैः। पराङ्मुखांश्च राज्ञस्तु पलायनपरायणान्॥ विद्रुतान् रथिनो दृष्ट्वा मन्ये शोचति पुत्रकः।
en: Having seen that both Durmarsana and Vrishasena were slain in battle and also having witnessed that his army being slaughtered by the mighty car-warriors, was dispersed and again, having seen that the kings (in his side), most unwilling to fight, were turning away from the field of battle and having beheld the great car-warriors already fled, I think my son is now surely lamenting.

sn: अनेयश्चाभिमानी च दुर्बुद्धिरजितेन्द्रियः॥ हतोत्साहं बलं दृष्ट्वा किंस्विद् दुर्योधनऽब्रवीत्।
en: What did that undaunted, proud and evil souled Duryodhana of uncontrolled passions say, after beholding his army grown pretty well dispirited?

sn: स्वयं वैरं महत् कृत्वा वार्यमाणः सुहृद्गणैः॥ प्रधने हतभूयिष्ठैः किंस्विद् दुर्योधनऽब्रवीत्।
en: Although having been forbidden by the friends, yet himself having created this fierce hostility, what did Duryodhana say, after beholding the slaughter of innumerable soldiers in battle?

sn: भ्रातरं निहतं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनेन संयुगे॥ रुधिरे पीयमाने च किंस्विद् दुर्योधनऽब्रवीत्।
en: Having seen that his brother was slain in battle and his blood was drunk by Bhimasena, what did Duryodhana say? w

sn: सह गान्धारराजेन सभायां यदभाषत्॥ कर्णोऽर्जुनं रणे हन्ता हते तस्मिन किमब्रवीत्।
en: He (my son) said in the midst of the assembly-hall with the king of the Gandharas that Karna would slay Arjuna in battle. But how having seen that hero slain, what did he (Duryodhana) say?

sn: द्यूतं कृत्वा पुरा हृष्टो वञ्चयित्वा च पाण्डवान्॥ शकुनिः सौबलस्तात हते कर्णे किमब्रवीत्।
en: O son, when Karna was slain, what did Shakuni, the son of Subala, having at first played at dice with a cheerful heart and deceived the son of Pandu, say?

sn: कृतवर्मा महेष्वासः सात्वतानां महारथः॥ हतं वैकर्तनं दृष्ट्वा हार्दिक्यः किमभाषत।
en: Beholding the son of Vikartana (slain in battle), what did that son of Hridika, Kritavarman, that mighty bowman, that great car-warrior amongst the Satvatas, say?

sn: ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्या यस्य शिक्षामुपासते॥ धनुर्वेद चिकीर्षन्तो द्रोणपुत्रस्य धीमतः। युवा रूपेण सम्पन्नो दर्शनीयो महायशाः॥ अश्वत्थामा हते कर्णे किमभाषत संजय।
en: O Sanjaya, Most willing to acquire a knowledge in archery, the Brahmanas, the Kshatriyas and the Vaishyas received instructions of that highly intellectual son of Drona. What did that youthful, that handsomelooking, that highly famous Ashvatthaman, endued with beauty, say, when he saw Karna slain in battle?

sn: आचार्यो यो धनुर्वेद गौतमो रथसत्तमः॥ कृपः शारद्वतस्तात हते कर्णे किमब्रवीत्।
en: What did that son of Sharadvata, Kripa of the Gautama race, that mighty, car-warrior, that teacher of archery, say when he saw Karna slain in battle?

sn: मद्रराजो महेष्वासः शल्यः समितिशोभनः॥ दृष्ट्वा विनिहतं कर्णं सारथ्ये रथिनां वरः। किमभाषत वीरोऽसौ मद्राणामधिपो बली॥
en: On beholding the slaughter of Karna, what did the king of Madras, that mighty bowman, that ornament of assemblies, Shalya of the Shauvira tribe, that foremost of charioteers engaged in driving away the car (of Karna), that leading chief of the Madra warriors, who was possessed of mighty strength, say?

sn: दृष्ट्वा विनिहतं सर्वे योधा वा रणदुर्जयाः। ये च केचन राजानः पृथिव्यां यो मागताः। वैकर्तनं हतं दृष्ट्वा कान्यभाषन्त संजय॥
en: And again, O Sanjaya, what did the other warriors, who with difficulty could be vanquished, as well as all the kings of the earth, who had come with the desire of fighting, say, when they beheld the slaughter of the son of Vikartana?

sn: द्रोणे तु निहते वीरे रथव्याने नरर्षभे। के वा मुखमनीकानामासन् संजय भागशः॥
en: When that hero, that foremost of the carwarriors, that best among men, Drona was slain (in battle), who, O Sanjaya, had been the leaders of the several divisions of the army in succession?

sn: मद्रराजः कथं शल्यो नियुक्तो रथिनां वरः। वैकर्तनस्य सारथ्ये तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: O Sanjaya, do you relate to me, how Shalya, the king of the Madras, that best among all the car-warriors, was engaged as the charioteer of the son of Vikartana?

sn: केऽरक्षनं दक्षिणं चक्रं सूतपुत्रस्य युध्यतः। वामं चक्रं ररक्षुर्वा के वा वीरस्य पृष्ठतः॥
en: While the son of Suta was fighting, who were the persons guarding his right wheel and those who protected his left and again, who were they that guarded his back.

sn: के क्षुद्राः प्राद्रवंस्ततः। कथं च वः समेतानां हतः कर्णो महारथः॥
en: What heroes did not forsake Karna and what mean-minded men flew away from him? While you had been present in the field, how could that mighty car-warrior be slain in battle?

sn: पाण्डवाश्च स्वयं शूराः प्रत्युदीयुर्महारथाः। सृजन्तः शरवर्षाणि वारिधारा इवाम्बुदाः॥ स च सर्पमुखो दिव्यो महेषुप्रवरस्तदा। के कर्णं न जहुः शूराः व्यर्थः कथं समभवत् तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: O Sanjaya, How could the heroic and great car-warriors oppose the Pandavas, who were pouring forth showers of arrows like the clouds pouring forth drops of water. Do you relate to me, how then could that celestial snakemouthed arrow, that best one of its kind, become of no avail?

sn: मामकस्यास्य सैन्यस्य हतोत्सेधस्य संजय। अवशेषं न पश्यामि ककुदे मृदिते सति॥
en: When the best of the leaders were slain, I do not see, O Sanjaya, that even some of the soldiers of my side, who had already lost their courage, will survive (the terrible slaughter).

sn: तौ हि वीरौ महेष्वासौ मदर्थे त्यक्तजीवितौ। भीष्मद्रोणौ हतौ श्रुत्वा को न्वर्थो जीवितेन मे॥
en: Indeed, those two heroes, the great bowmen, were ready to give up their lives for my sake. Hearing of their (Bhishma and Drona) death, what use have I of my life?

sn: पुनः पुनर्न मृष्यामि हतं कर्णं च पाण्डवैः। यस्य बाह्वोर्बलं तुल्यं कुञ्जराणां शतं शतैः॥
en: Again and again, I cannot bear that Karna should be slain by the Pandavas; for whose strength of arms is equal to that of ten thousand elephants.

sn: द्रोणे हते च यद् वृत्तं कौरवाणां परैः सह। संग्रामे नरवीराणां तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: O Sanjaya, relate to me in detail what had happened in the battle that raged between the mighty heroes among men, namely, the Kauravas and their enemies, when Drona was slain.

sn: यथा कर्णश्च कौन्तेयैः सह युद्धमयोजयत्। यथा च द्विषतां हन्ता रणे शान्तस्तदुच्यताम्॥
en: Relate to me also how the sons of Kunti conducted the battle with Karna and do you tell me, again, how that slayer of enemies became quiet (was slain) in battle.

sn: संजय उवाच हते द्रोणे महेष्वासे तस्मिन्नहनि भारत। कृते च मोघसंकल्पे द्रोणपुत्रे महारथे॥
en: Sanjaya said O Descendant of the Bharata race, when, in that day, the mighty bowman Drona was slain in battle and when again, the objects of that mighty car-warrior were unfulfilled;

sn: द्रवमाणे महाराज कौरवाणां बलार्णवे। व्यूह्य पार्थः स्वकं सैन्यमतिष्ठद् भ्रातृभिर्वृतः॥
en: And when, O great king, the army of the Kauravas, that was like the vast ocean, had fled away, the son of Pritha, having arranged his own troops properly waited in the field with all his brothers.

sn: तमवस्थितमाज्ञाय पुत्रस्ते भरतर्षभ। विद्रुतं स्वबलं दृष्ट्वा पौरुषेण न्यवारयत्॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, your son having seen him staying in the field and also having witnessed his own army flaying away form the battle, forbade them run away in the most encouraging terms.

sn: स्वमनीकमवस्थाप्य बाहुवीर्यमुपाश्रितः। युद्ध्वा च सुचिरं कालं पाण्डवैः सह भारत॥
en: Then with the confidence in the strength of his own arms, having arranged his own army in a regular position and O descendant of the Bharata race, having fought for a while with the Pandavas.

sn: लब्धलक्ष्यैः परैर्हष्टैक्यच्छद्भिश्चिरं तदा। संध्याकालं समासाद्य प्रत्याहारमकारयत्॥
en: Who had attained their objects and who were the most cheerful enemies and who, again, were engaged for pretty long time in battle, he, on the approach of the evening, caused the army of the enemies to withdraw,

sn: कृत्वावहारं सैन्यानां प्रविश्य शिबिरं स्वकम्। कुरवः सुहितं मन्त्रं मन्त्रयाञ्चक्रिरे मिथः॥
en: Thereupon having drawn the troops and entered into their own encampment, the sons of Kuru held a consultation among themselves for their own welfare.

sn: पर्यङ्केषु परार्येषु स्पास्तरणवत्सु च। वरासनेषूपविष्टाः सुखशय्यास्विवामराः॥
en: They had seated themselves in the most excellent seats and valuable conches furnished with beautiful coverlets, even as the celestials take their seats on the most pleasant bows.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा साम्ना परमवल्गुना। तानाभाष्य महेष्वासान् प्राप्तकालमभाषत।॥
en: Thereupon king Duryodhana addressed these mighty bowmen in the most agreeable and pleasant terms and spoke them in a way most suited to the time.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच मतं मतिमतां श्रेष्ठाः सर्वे प्रबूत मा चिरम्। एवं गते तु किं कार्यं किं च कार्यतरं नृपाः॥
en: Duryodhana said O monarchs, all of you are the best of the intellectual persons; do you at once give your individual opinions as to what is necessary or what is unnecessary under the present circumstances.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्ते नरेन्द्रेण नरसिंहा युयुत्सवः। चक्रुर्नानाविधाश्चेष्टाः सिंहासनगतास्तदा॥
en: Sanjaya said When these words had been uttered by the lord of men, then the foremost of princes, who had seated themselves on the throne and were most willing to fight, began to make various gestures (expressive of their heroism).

sn: तेषां निशाम्येगितानि युद्धे प्राणाञ्जुहूषताम्। समुद्वीक्ष्य मुखं राज्ञो बालार्कसमवर्चसम्॥ आचार्यपुत्रो मेधावी वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यमाददे।
en: Having understood the gestures of those, who were ready to sacrifice their lives in the battle and having beheld the face of the king, that had the splendour of the newly rising Sun. The highly intellectual son of Acharya, who

sn: रागो योगस्तथा दाक्ष्यं नयश्चेत्यर्थसाधकाः॥ उपाया: पण्डितैः प्रोक्तास्ते तु दैवमुपाश्रिताः।
en: 'Zeal, perseverance, as also skillfulness and diplomacy, these have been declared by the learned me to be the principal expedients of accomplishing ends, which, again, are wholly dependent upon Destiny.'

sn: लोकप्रवीरा येऽस्माकं देवकल्पा महारथः॥ नीतिमन्तस्तथा युक्ता दक्षा रक्ताक्ष ते हताः। न त्वेव कार्यं नैराश्यमस्माभिर्विजयं प्रति॥
en: Those foremost of men, the mighty carwarriors, on our side, who had been like the celestials and who were acquainted with the principles of government were all slain in battle. In spite of all these, there should be no disappointment as regards victory.

sn: सुनीतैरिह सर्वार्थैर्देवमप्यनुलोम्यते। ते वयं प्रवरं नृणां सर्वैगुणगणौर्युतम्॥ कर्णमेवाभिषेक्ष्यामः सैनापत्येन भारत। कर्ण सेनापति कृत्वा प्रमथिष्यामहे रिपून्॥
en: For, Destiny could be made favourable, if we can take recourse to the honest principles comprehensive of all the expedients. O descendant of the Bharata race, we shall, therefore, install Karna, that best of men, endowed with all the good qualities, as the commander of the army. Having made Karna the commander of our force, we shall be in a position to destroy all the enemies.

sn: एष ह्यतिबलः शूरः कृतास्त्रो युद्धदुर्मदः। वैवस्वत इवासह्यः शक्तो जेतुं रणे रिपून्॥
en: Because this hero, who is possessed of immense strength and who is acquainted with the use of weapons and who cannot easily be vanquished and who is like Death himself and who is irresistible, is capable of subduing the enemies in battle.

sn: एतदाचार्यतनयाच्छ्रुत्वा राजंस्तवात्मजः। आशा बहुमती चक्रे कर्णं प्रति स वै तदा॥
en: O king, having heard these (words) from the son of the preceptor, then your son had entertained great hopes in respect to Karna.

sn: हते भीष्मे च द्रोणे च कर्णो जेष्यति पाण्डवान्। तामाशां हृदये कृत्वा समाश्वस्य च भारत॥ ततो दुर्योधनः प्रीतः प्रियं श्रुत्वाऽस्य तद् वचः। प्रीतिसत्कार संयुक्तं तथ्यमात्महितं शुभम्॥ स्वं मनः समवस्थाप्य बाहुवीर्यमुपाश्रितः। दुर्योधनो महाराज राधेयमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: When both Bhishma and Drona have been slain, Karna will surely then defeat the Pandavas. O descendant of the Bharata race, having cherished this hope in his heart and also having comforted himself. Thereupon king Duryodhana was exceedingly gratified to hear his words, that were fraught with delight and reverence, that were also beneficial to himself and true and most pleasant. Then having secured the steadiness of his mind and relied upon the strength of his own arms, the most powerful king Duryodhana spoke these words to the son of Radha-.

sn: कर्ण जानामि ते वीर्यं सौहृदं परमं मयि। तथापि त्वां महाबाहो प्रवक्ष्यामि हितं वचः॥
en: O Karna, I know your strength, as well as great intimacy that you entertain for myself. In spite of all that, O mighty-armed one, I will tell you some words that are beneficial to yourself.

sn: श्रुत्वा यथेष्टं च कुरु वीर यत् तव रोचते। भवान् प्राज्ञतमो नित्यं मम चैव परा गतिः॥
en: O hero, you are the greatest sage are always my highest protection as well. Now, having heard my words, do whatever you desire, or whatever you like most.

sn: भीष्मद्रोणावतिरथौ हतौ सेनापति मम। सेनापतिर्भवानस्तु ताभ्यां द्रविणवत्तरः॥
en: My two great generalissimos, Bhishma and Drona, those car-warriors of the first class, have been already slain in battle. You are more powerful than either of them. Now should you be installed as the commander of my army.

sn: वृद्धौ च तौ महेष्वासौ सापेक्षौ च धनंजये। मानितौ च मया वीरौ राधेय वचनात् तव॥
en: Indeed, those two mighty bowmen were very old; and they were favourable disposed and you towards Dhananjaya. In despite thereof, O son of Radha, those two heroes were selected by me as the generalissimo of my army at your word.

sn: पितामहत्वं सम्प्रेक्ष्य पाण्डुपुत्रा महारणे। रक्षितास्तात भीष्मेण दिवसानि दशैव तु॥
en: Beholding their connection of grand-father with themselves, the sons of Pandu, O father, were saved in that formidable battle by Bhishma for ten consecutive days.

sn: न्यस्तशस्त्रे च भवति हतो भीष्मः पितामहः। शिखण्डिन पुरस्कृस्य फाल्गुनेन महाहवे॥
en: When you had laid aside your arms, Bhishma of mighty prowess was slain in battle by Falguna, who had placed Shikhandin in his front.

sn: हते तस्मिन् महेष्वासे शरतल्पगते तथा। त्वयोक्ते पुरुष व्याघ्र द्रोणो ह्यासीत् पुरः सरः॥
en: When that great bowman had fallen and lain down on the bed of arrows, it was them, O foremost of men, that Drona was appointed as the commander (of the army) at your request.

sn: तेनापि रक्षिताः पार्थाः शिष्यत्वादिति मे मतिः। स चापि निहतो वृद्धो धृष्टद्युम्नेन सत्वरम्॥
en: My opinion is, that by that hero, too, the sons of Pritha were saved (from the hand of Death) in consideration that the latter were the pupils of the former. But even that old man, again, was speedily slain (in battle) by Dhristadyumna.

sn: निहताभ्यां प्रधानाभ्यां ताभ्यानमितविक्रम। त्वत्समं समरे योधं नान्यं पश्यामि चिन्तयन्॥
en: Reflecting for a while, I do not see any other person, like yourself, of more immeasurable prowess than those two best of warriors, who are already slain in battle.

sn: भवानेव तु नः शक्तो विजयाय न संशयः। पूर्वं मध्ये च पश्चाच तथैव विहितं हितम्॥
en: At present you are able to obtain victory for ourselves. There is no doubt about it. In accordance therewith you have rendered good to us both before and after, as well as in the middle.

sn: स भवान् धुर्यवत् संख्ये धुरमुद्वोढुमहति। अभिषेचय सैनान्ये स्वयमात्मानमात्मना॥
en: You should, like the commander of the force, bear all the burden in battle. So, should you be installed as the general by yourself.

sn: देवतानां यथा स्कन्दः सेनानीः प्रभुरव्ययः। तथा भवानिमां सेनां धार्तराष्ट्रीं बिभर्तु वै॥
en: Therefore, do you maintain this force of Dhritarashtra, even as lord Skanda of eternal energy, the leader of the celestials, maintain the celestial force.

sn: जहि शत्रुगणान् सर्वान् महेन्द्रो दानवानिव। अवस्थितं रणे दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवास्त्वां महारथाः॥ द्रविष्यन्ति च पञ्चाला विष्णुं दृष्ट्वेव दानवाः। तस्मात् त्वं पुरुषव्याघ्र प्रकर्षैतां महाचमूम्॥
en: Do you slay all the foes, even as Mahendra slays the Danavas. When the most powerful car-warriors, the Pandavas, will see you waiting in the field of battle, they will surely fly away with all the Panchalas, even as the Danavas fly away, beholding Vishnu. Consequently, O foremost of men, do you command this mighty force.

sn: भवत्यवस्थिते यत्ते पाण्डवा मन्दचेतसः। द्रविष्यन्ति सहामात्याः पञ्चालाः सुंजयाश्च ह॥
en: When you will stay in the field, all those Pandavas of wicked soul with their allies, the Panchalas and the Srinjayas, all will run away from the field.

sn: यथा ह्यभ्युदितः सूर्यः प्रतपन् स्वेन तेजसा। व्यपोहति समस्तीव्र तथा शत्रून् प्रतापय॥
en: So, do you exterminate all the enemies, even as the risen Sun, burning by his own energy, destroys the awful darkness.

sn: संजय उवाच आशा बलवती राजन् पुत्रस्य तव याऽभवत्। हते भीष्मे च द्रोणे च कर्णो जेष्यति पाण्डवान्॥ तामाशां हृदये कृत्वा कर्णमेवं तदाब्रवीत्। सूतपुत्र न ते पार्थः स्थित्वाग्रे संयुयुत्सति॥
en: Sanjaya said That after the slaughter of both Bhishma and Drona, Karna would surely subdue the Pandavas, this hope, O king, of your son was found to be very great. Having entertained in the mind that strong hope, he then addressed Karna saying thus-"O son of Suta, the son of Pritha would never fight, staying before you (in the field)."

sn: कर्ण उवाच उक्तमेतन्मया पूर्वं गान्धारे तव संनिधौ। जेष्यामि पाण्डवान् सर्वान् सपुत्रान् सजनार्दनान्॥४०
en: Karna said O son of Gandhari, this was already told by me before you, namely that I would subdue all the Pandavas with their sons and with Janardana, too.

sn: सेनापतिर्भविष्यामि तवाहं नात्र संशयः। स्थिरो भव महाराज जितान् विद्धि च पाण्डवान्॥४१
en: I will be your generalissimo, there is not doubt about it. O powerful monarch, have peace. And do you think the Pandavas were already conquered.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्तो महाराज ततो दुर्योधनो नृपः। उत्तस्थौ राजभिः सार्धं देवैरिव शतक्रतुः॥
en: Sanjaya said O great monarch, on his being thus addressed, king Duryodhana stood up with all other monarchs, like Indra of one hundred sacrifices with the celestials, in order to pay respect to Karna.

sn: सेनापत्येन सत्कर्तुं कर्णं स्कन्दमिवामराः। ततोऽभिषिषिचुः कर्णं विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥ दुर्योधनमुखा राजन् राजानो विजयैषिणः।
en: As the commander of his force, even as the gods do to lord Skanda. Thereupon, monarch, all the kings, at the head of whom was Duryodhana, who were most desirous of victory, installed Karna (in the generalship of army), according to the rites ordained by Providence.

sn: शातकुम्भमयैः कुम्भैर्माहेयैश्चभिमन्त्रितैः॥ तोयपूर्णविषाणैश्च द्विपखङ्गमहर्षभैः। मणिमुक्तायुतैश्चान्यैः पुण्यगन्धस्तथौषधैः। औदुम्बरे सुखासीनमासने क्षौमसंवृत। शास्त्रदृष्टेन विधिना सम्भारैश्च सुसम्भृतैः॥ ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रिया वैश्यास्तथा शूद्राश्च सम्मताः। तुष्टुवुस्तं महात्मानमभिषिक्तं वरासने॥
en: By the offerings of gold and earthen vessels filled with water, sanctified with the holy expressions (the mantras) and of the tusks of elephants and the horns of rhinoceroses and well-constituted bulls and also by the offerings of other vessels overlaid with jewels and gems and of fragrant herbs. He (Karna) at this time seated himself at ease on a seat made of Udumbara wood and covered over with a piece of silken cloth. The Brahmanas, the Kshatriyas, the Vaishyas, as well as the Sudras of high social position began to praise that loftyminded one, who was installed, with the offerings of articles collected according to the rites enjoined by the Shastras, in that highest position.

sn: ततोऽभिषिक्ते राजेन्द्र निष्कर्गोभिर्धनेन च। वाचयामास विप्राय्यान् राधेयः परवीरहा॥
en: Thereupon, being thus installed, O lord of monarchs, the son of Radha, that slayer of the most war-like enemies, worshipped the foremost of the regenerate persons by the offerings of gold, kine and other wealth; and thereby caused them to say benedictions to him.

sn: जय पार्थान सगोविन्दान् सानुगांस्तान् महामृधे। इति तं वन्दिनः प्राहुर्द्विजाश्च पुरुषर्षभम्॥ जहि पार्थान् सपाञ्चालान् राधेय विजयाय नः। उद्यन्निव सदा भानुस्तमांस्युप्रैर्गभस्तिभिः॥
en: O foremost of men, the bards and the twiceborn persons uttered these words to him-"Do you subdue the sons of Pritha, with Govinda and with their principal attendants in that formidable battle. O son of Radha, do you slay the sons of Pritha, along with the Panchalas, that we may win victory, even as risen Sun always destroys the thick gloom by his terrible rays.

sn: न ह्यलं त्वद्विसृष्टानां शराणां वै सकेशवाः। उलूकाः सूर्यरश्मीनां ज्वलतामिव दर्शने॥
en: The faithless sons of Pandu with Keshava, cannot indeed bear with the sight of the arrows shot by you, even as it is most intolerable to look at the burning rays of the Sun.

sn: न हि पार्थाः सपाञ्चाला: स्थातुं शक्तास्तवाग्रतः। आत्तशस्त्रस्य समरे महेन्द्रस्येव दानवाः॥
en: Having put on all the weapons, the sons of Pritha, along with the Panchalas, will not be able to stay before you in the field, even as the Danavas are not able to stand before Indra (in battle).

sn: अभिषिक्तस्तु राधेयः प्रभया सोऽमितप्रभः। अत्यरिच्यत रूपेण दिवाकर इवापरः॥
en: Having been thus installed in the generalship, the son of Radha of unparalleled radiance surpassed all the beauty and splendour like a second Sun.

sn: सैनापत्ये तु राधेमभिषिच्य सुतस्तव। अमन्यत् तदाऽऽत्मानं कृतार्थं कालचोदितः॥
en: Having installed the son of Radha in the leadership (of the army), thereupon, your son, insisted upon by Death as it were, considered himself most successful.

sn: कर्णोऽपि राजन् सम्प्राप्य सैनापत्यमरिंदमः। योगामाज्ञापगमास सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति॥
en: O monarch, Karna, the subduer of enemies, having obtained this leadership, ordered for arranging the troops in battle-array towards the rising of the Sun.

sn: तव पुत्रैर्वृतः कर्णः शुशुभे तत्र भारत। देवैरिव यथा स्कन्दः संग्रामे तारकामये॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, Karna, having been surrounded by your sons in the battle, looked resplendent, even as the lord Skanda, encompassed by all the celestials, looked radiant in the battle, wherein the Asura Taraka, like an evil, was sought to be defeated.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच सैनापत्यं तु सम्प्राप्य कर्णो वैकर्तनस्तदा। तथोक्तश्च स्वयं राज्ञा स्निग्धं भ्रातृसमं वचः॥ योगमाज्ञाप्य सेनानामादित्येऽभ्युदिते तदा। अकरोत् किं महाप्राज्ञास्तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Having attained the generalship of the army and been addressed by the king himself in sweet and brotherly terms and thereupon having ordered the troops to be arranged in battle-array towards the rise of the Sun, relate to me, O Sanjaya, what did the highly intellectual son of Vikartana, Karna, do at that time.

sn: संजय उवाच कर्णस्य मतमाज्ञाय पुत्रास्ते भरतर्षभ। योगमाज्ञापयामासुर्नन्दितूर्यपुरःसरम्॥
en: Sanjaya said O foremost of the Bharata race, your sons, having understood the object of Karna, ordered for the arrangement of the troops, followed by a joyful music of various instruments.

sn: महत्यपररात्रे च तव सैन्यस्य मारिष। योगो योगेति सहसा प्रादुरासीन्महास्वनः॥
en: Towards the close of the night, O lord of earth, a loud noise arose from amongst your soldiers, saying 'array and array.'

sn: कल्पतां नागमुख्यानां रथानां च वरूथिनाम्। संनयतां नराणां च वाजिनां च विशाम्पते॥ क्रोशतां चैव योधानां त्वरितानां परस्परम्। बभूव तुमुलः शब्दो दिवस्पृक् सुमहांस्ततः॥
en: Thereupon, O lord of the world, there was a terrible uproar of the best of elephants and cars overlaid with beautiful coverlets, whilst they were being equipped and of the infantry crying out in joy, of the horses, whilst being harnessed and of the warriors, whilst moving to and fro, as as shouting to one another in mirth's. The uproar was so very great that it reached the very heavens.

sn: ततः श्वेतपताकेन बलाकावर्णवाजिना। हेमपृष्टेन धनुषा नागकक्षेण केतुना॥ तूणीरशतपूर्णेन सगदेन वरूथिना। शतध्वीकिंकिणीशक्तिशूलतोमरधारिणा॥ कार्मुकैरूपन्नेन विमलादित्यवर्चसा। रथेनाभिपताकेन सूतपुत्रोऽभ्यदृश्यत॥
en: Thereupon the son of Suta appeared on the field of battle, mounted upon a car furnished with innumerable flags and white standards, drawn by horses white cranes, ornamented with a flag bearing the design of an elephant's rope, filled with one hundred quivers and again, furnished with mace and wooden fence, supplied with the Shataghnis, rows of bells, shafts, lances and spears, loaded with several excellent bows and having had the splendour of the resplendent Sun and himself wielding a bow bound with gold.

sn: ध्मापयन् वारिजं राजन् हेमजालविभूषितम्। विधुन्वानो महचापं कार्तस्वरविभूषितम्॥
en: O monarch, (Karna then began) to blow his conch adorned with a net-work of gold and also to shake his terrible bow studded with gold.

sn: दृष्ट्वा कर्णे महेष्वासं रथस्थं रथिनां वरम्। भानुमन्तमिवोद्यन्तं तमो निनन् दुरासदम्॥
en: Having seen Karna, that mighty bowman, that foremost of car-warriors, who was seated on his car and also was like the risen Sun destroying the thick darkness and who also was unapproachable.

sn: न भीष्मव्यसनं केचिन्नापि द्रोणस्य मारिष। नान्येषां पुरुषव्याघ्र मेनिरे तत्र कौरवाः॥
en: None of the Kauravas, O sire, O foremost of persons, considered the fall of eithe, Bhishma, or Drona, or other warriors to be a loss at the time.

sn: ततस्तु त्वरयन् योधाशङ्खशब्देन मारिष। कर्णो निष्कर्षयामास कौरवाणां महद् बलम्॥
en: Thereupon, O sire Karna, having ordered the warriors to make haste by the sound of his conch, led the vast army of the Kauravas.

sn: व्यूहं व्यूह्य महेष्वासो मकरं शत्रुतापनः। प्रत्युद्ययौ तथा कर्णः पाण्डवान् विजिगीषया॥
en: Then Karna, that powerful bowman, that siniter of enemies, having arranged the troops in the from of a Makara, started against the Pandavas with the object of winning victory (over them).

sn: मकरस्य तु तुण्डे वै कर्णो राजन् व्यवस्थितः। नेत्राभ्यां शकुनिः शूर उलूकश्च महारथः॥
en: O king, Karna placed himself in the tip of the beak of that Makara; and the heroic Shakuni and the great car-warrior Uluka were stationed in both the eyes.

sn: द्रोणपुत्रस्तु शिरसि ग्रीवायां सर्वसोदरा। मध्ये दुर्योधनो राजा बलेन महता वृतः॥
en: The son of Drona was stationed in the head; and all the uterine brothers were in the neck. King Duryodhana was stationed in the middle, surrounded by a large force.

sn: वामपादे तु राजेन्द्र कृतवर्मा व्यवस्थितः। नारायणबलैर्युक्तो गोपालैर्युद्धदुर्मदैः॥
en: O lord of kings, Kritavarman was placed in the left foot, who was attended by the Narayana-army, namely the Gopalas, most difficult to be vanquished in battle.

sn: पादे तु दक्षिणे राजन् गौतमः सत्यविक्रमः। त्रिगतैः सुमहेष्वासैर्दाक्षिणात्यैश्च संवृतः॥
en: O king, the son of Gautama, possessed of the unbaffled prowess, was stationed in right foot, encompassed by the most powerful bowmen, the Trigartas and the troops from the south.

sn: अनुपादे तु यो वामस्तत्र शल्यो व्यवस्थितः। महत्या सेनया सार्धं मद्रदेशसमुत्थया॥
en: There Shalya was placed in left hind-foot accompanied by a vast army recruited from the country of the Madras.

sn: दक्षिणे तु महाराज सुषेणः सत्यसंगरः। वृतो रथसहस्रेण दन्तिनां च त्रिभिः शतै॥
en: O great king, Sushena of certain resolution was stationed in the right hind-foot, encompassed by a force of one thousand cars and three hundred elephants.

sn: पुच्छे ह्यास्तां महावीर्यो भ्रातरौ पार्थिवौ तदा। चित्रश्च चित्रसेनश्च महत्या सेनया वृतौ॥
en: Thereupon the two royal brothers, Chitra and Chitrasena, of iminense prowess having been accompanied by a vast army, stood in the tail (of the Makara).

sn: तथा प्रयाते राजेन्द्र कर्णे नरवरोत्तमे। धनंजयमभिप्रेक्ष्य धर्मराजोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: O lord of kings, when Karna, that best of person had started for battle, the king of righteousness (Yudhishthira) beheld Dhananjaya and addressed him sayingपश्य

sn: पार्थ यथा सेना धार्तराष्ट्रीह संयुगे। कर्णेन विहिता वीर गुप्ता वीरैर्महारथैः॥
en: "O heroic son of Pritha, behold grow the army of Dhritarashtra was arranged in battlearray by Karna and encompassed by the most heroic car-warriors.

sn: हतवीरतमा ह्येषा धार्तराष्ट्री महाचमूः। फल्गुशेषा महाबाहो तृणैस्तुल्या मता मम॥
en: Indeed, the best of the heroes amongst the vast army of Dhritarashtra were all slain before, O mighty armed one, only the feeble ones are alive, who are in my opinion as worthless as the straw. But in the whole force one mighty bowman, namely, the son of Suta, is shining brilliantly.

sn: एको ह्यत्र महेष्वासः सूतपुत्रो विराजते। सदेवासुरगन्धर्वैः सकिन्नरमहोरगैः॥ चराचरैस्त्रिभिलेकिर्योऽजय्यो रथिनां वरः। तं हत्वाद्य महाबाहो विजयस्तव फाल्गुन॥ उद्धृतश्च भवेच्छल्यो मम द्वादशवार्षिकः। एवं ज्ञात्वा महाबाहो व्यूहं व्यूह यथेच्छसि।॥
en: That foremost of car-warriors is incapable of being defeated by the three worlds, both mobile and immobile, along with the Gods, Asuras, the Gandharvas, the Kinnaras and the Nagas. O mighty-armed Phalguna, having slain to your him today, you will surely win victory and great thorn, pierced in my heart for twelve years, will now also be rooted out. Understanding this, O mighty armed one, do you arrange the troops in battle-array according desire.

sn: भ्रातुरेतद् वचः श्रुत्वा पाण्डवः श्वेतवाहनः। अर्धचन्द्रेण व्यूहेन प्रत्यव्यूहत तां चमूम्॥
en: Having heard the word of his brother, the Pandava (the third brother), conveyed by white horses, arranged his army in the form of the half moon against the face of the enemies' force.

sn: वामपार्वे तु तस्याथ भीमसेनो व्यवस्थितः। दक्षिणे च महेष्वासो धृष्टद्युम्नो व्यवस्थितः॥ मध्ये व्यूहस्य राजा तु पाण्डवश्च धनंजयः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च धर्मराजस्य पृष्ठतः॥
en: Thereupon Bhimasena was stationed in the left side of that (half-moon); and the mighty bowman, Dhristadyumna, was placed in the right. In the middle (of that half-moon arrangement) both the monarch and the Pandava Dhananjaya were stationed. But Nakula and Shahadeva were placed in the rear of the king of righteousness (Yudhishthira.)

sn: चक्ररक्षौ तु पाञ्चाल्यौ युधामन्युत्तमौजसौ। नार्जुनं जहतुयुद्धे पाल्यमानौ किरीटिना।३१॥
en: The two Panchala chiefs, Yudhamanyu and Uttamanjas, who were the guards of the wheels of the car (of Arjuna), did not forsake him in battle, as they were supported by the diademdecked one (Arjuna.)

sn: शेषा नृपतयो वीराः स्थिता व्यूहस्य दंशिताः। यथाभागं यथोत्साहं यथायत्नं च भारतः॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, the rest of the heroic princes, who were all clad in armour, stationed in the different positions of the array allotted to them according to their respective zeal earnestness.

sn: एवमेतन्महाव्यूहं व्यूह्य भारत पाण्डवाः। तावकाश्च महेष्वासा युद्धोयैव मनो दधुः॥
en: were i O descendant of the Bharata race, the Pandavas, as well as the mighty bowmen in। your side, having arranged their troops in the array of battle in the above manner, directed their mind towards the battle.

sn: दृष्ट्वा व्यूढां तव चमूं सूतपुत्रेण संयुगे। निहतान् पाण्डवान् मेनेधार्तराष्ट्रः सबान्धवः॥
en: Having witnessed your army arranged in battle by the son of Suta, the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana), with all his kinsmen, considered the Pandavas to be slain.

sn: तथैव पाण्डवी सेनां व्यूढां दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरः। धार्तराष्ट्रान् हतान् मेने सकर्णान् वै जनाधिपः॥
en: O lord of men, in the similar way, Yudhishthira, having observed the troops in the side of the Pandavas arranged in battle-array, considered the army of Dhritarashtra to be surely slain along with Karna himself.

sn: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकदुन्दुभिः। डिण्डिमाश्चाप्यहन्यन्त झर्झराश्च समन्ततः॥ सेनायोरुभयो राजन् प्रावाद्यन्त महास्वनाः। सिंहनादश्च संजज्ञे शूराणां जयगृद्धिनाम्॥
en: Thereupon conches, kettle-drums, tabours and drums of large size and cymbals and other instruments, such as Dindimas and Jharjharas were begun to be blown and struck on every side. O monarch, there was a loud sound of musical instruments amongst the soldiers on both the sides. There were terrible lion-roars of the heroes, who were most desirous of victory.

sn: हयहेषितशब्दाश्च वारणानां च बृंहताम्। रथनेमिस्वनाचोग्रा: सम्बभूवर्जुनाधिप॥
en: O lord of men, there arose the sound of snorting of the horses and the grunting of elephants. And also there was the terrible noise of the car-wheels.

sn: न द्रोणव्यसनं कश्चिजीनीते तत्र भारत। दृष्ट्वा कर्णं महेष्वासं मुखे व्यूहस्य दंशितम्॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, beholding that mighty bowinan, Karna, stationed at the front of the battle-array, none in the field amongst the Kaurava troops considered the death of Drona to be a loss.

sn: उभे सैन्ये महाराज प्रहृष्टनरसंकुले। योद्भुकामे स्थिते राजन् हन्तुमन्योन्यमोजसा॥
en: O mighty monarch, in both the armies there were men filled with chcerfulness, who were all desirous of battle. O king, they waited in the field with the object of slaying one another without delay.

sn: तत्र यत्तौ सुसंरब्धौ दृष्ट्वान्योन्यं व्यवस्थितौ। अनीकमध्ये राजेन्द्र चेरतुः कर्णपाण्डवौ॥
en: O foremost of kings, there in the field these two namely, Karna and the son of Pandu, who beholding each other were filled with firm resolution rushed to and fro in the midst of their armies.

sn: नृत्यमाने च ते सेने समेयातां परस्परम्। तेषां पक्षैः प्रपक्षेभ्यो निर्जग्मुस्ते युयुत्सवः॥
en: The two armies came face to face, meeting cach other, as if dancing (in great cheer). The heroes on both the sides, who were most desirous of battle, came forth accompanied by their respective divisions.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं नरवारणवाजिनाम्। रथानां च महाराज अन्योन्यमभिनिघ्नताम्॥
en: 'O nighty monarch, thus commenced the battle of men, elephants, horses and cars, who were all engaged in slaying one another.

sn: संजय उवाच ते सेनेऽन्योन्यमासाद्य प्रहष्टाश्चनरद्विपे। बृहत्यौ सम्प्रजह्वाते देवासुरमसप्रभे॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon the two vast armies, composed of horses, men and elephants, that were filled with cheer and also that had the brilliany of the celestial and Asura hosts, can. face to face and struck each other down.

sn: ततो नररथाश्वेभैः पतयशोग्रविक्रमाः। सम्प्रहारान् भृशं चक्रुर्देपाप्मसुनाशनान्॥
en: Then the men, the cars, the horses, the elephants, as well as the infantry, all possessed of formidable strength, continued to strike most fiercely, thereby destroying the bodies and the sins as well.

sn: पूर्णचन्द्रार्कपद्मानां कान्तिभिर्गन्धतः समैः। उत्तमा.सिंहानां नृसिंहास्तस्तरुर्महीम्॥
en: The lion-like men, began to scatter over the earth, the heads of lion-like men, which were equal in splendour to the full-moon and the sun and also which had resembled the lotuses in fragrance.

sn: अर्धचन्द्रैस्तथा भल्लैः क्षुरप्रैरसिपट्टिशैः। परश्वधैश्चाप्यकृन्तन्नुत्तमाङ्गानि युध्यताम्॥
en: They, again, began to sever the heads of the fighting warriors by means of the crescentshaped, broad-faced and razor-handed arrows, swords, axes, battle-axes and other weapons.

sn: व्यायतायतबाहूनां व्यायतातबाहुभिः। बाहवः पातिता रेजुर्धरण्यां सायुधाङ्गदा॥
en: The arms of men, possessed of long and stout arms, severed by men, possessed of long and stout arms, looked resplendent upon the ground, decorated as they were 'vith both weapons and bracelets.

sn: तैः स्फुरद्भिर्मही भाति रक्ताङ्गुलितलैस्तथा। गरुडाहितैरुप्रैः पञ्चास्यैरुरगैरिव॥
en: The earth shone most brightly with the halo of their (the warriors) red fingers and palms, even as it shines with the fierce and fiveheaded snakes upon itself slain by Garuda.

sn: द्विरदस्यन्दनाश्वेभ्यः पेतुर्वीरा द्विषद्धताः। विमानेभ्यो यथा क्षीणे पुण्ये स्वर्गसदस्तथा॥
en: Smitten by the enemies, the heroic warriors fell down from the elephants, the cars and horses, even as the dwellers of heaven fall down from the celestial balloons, when their virtues are entirely spent.

sn: गदाभिरन्ये गुर्वीभिः परिधैर्मुसलैरपि। पोथिताः शतश: पेतुर्वीरा वीरतरै द्विपैः॥
en: While other heroic warriors, having been smitten by heroes of greater prowess with heavy maces, spiked clubs and maces, fell in the battle by hundreds.

sn: स्था रथैर्विमथिता मत्ता मत्तैर्द्विपा द्विपैः। सादिनः सादिभिश्चैव तस्मिन् परमसंकुले॥
en: In that formidable battle, the cars were smitten by cars, the infuriate elephants were crushed by infuriate elephants and the horsemen were struck down by horse-men.

sn: रथैरा रथा नागैरश्वारोहाश्च पत्तिभिः। अश्वारोहैः पदाताश्च निहता युधि शेरते॥
en: The men smitten by the cars and the cars destroyed by elephants and the horsemen slain by the foot-soldiers and the infantry slain by the cavalry, are lying dead in the field.

sn: रथाश्वपत्तयो नागै रथाश्वेभाश्च पत्तिभिः। रथपत्तिद्विपाश्चाश्चै रथैश्चापि नरद्विपाः॥
en: And again, the cars, the horses and the infantry smitten by the elephants; and the cars, steeds and elephants slain by the infantry; and the cars, the infantry and the elephant-force destroyed by the horses, and also the men and elephants struck down by the cars, are lying dead in the battle.

sn: रथाश्चेभनराणां तु नराश्चेभरथैः कृतम्। पाणिपादैश्च शस्त्रैश्च रथैश्च कदनं महत्॥
en: A terrible slaughter of car-warriors, horsemen, the elephant-force and men was wrought by men steeds, elephants and cars, with the help of their hands and feet, weapons and cars.

sn: तथा तस्मिन् बले शूरैर्वध्यमाने हतेऽपि च। अस्मानभ्याययुः पार्था वृकोदरपुरोगमाः॥
en: While the army was being thus smitten and slain by the horses, the sons of Pritha with Vrikodara at their head proceeded against us.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्न: शिखण्डी च द्रौपदेयाः प्रभद्रकाः। सात्यकिश्चेकितानश्च द्राविडैः सैनिकैः सह।॥
en: So also Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandin, the sons of Draupadi, the Provadrakas and Shatyaki and Chekitana accompanied by the Dravida warriors (proceeded against us);

sn: वृता व्यूहेन महता पाण्ड्याश्चोलाः सकेरलाः। व्यूढोरस्का दीर्घभुजा: प्रांशवः पृथुलोचनाः॥
en: And also the Pandavas and the Cholas along with the Keralas (advanced against us), surrounded by a formidable array of soldiers, who were all possessed of strong chests, long arms, huge statures and very large eyes;

sn: आपीडिनो रक्तदन्ता मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमाः। नानाविरागवसना गन्धचूर्णावचूर्णिताः॥
en: And who, again, were adorned with various ornaments and were of red teeth and were endowed with the strength of mad elephants and were clothed in dresses of various colours and also were besmeared with scented powders;

sn: बद्धासयः पाशहस्ता वारप्रतिवारणा:। समानमृत्यवो राजन् नात्यजन्त परस्परम्॥
en: And O monarch, as they were possessed of swords and nooscs in their hands and endued with the power of with-standing the infuriate elephants and as they were equally determined to die, they (the warriors) did not forsake one another (in the field).

sn: कलापिनश्चापहस्ता दीर्घकेशाः प्रियंवदाः। पत्तयः सादिनश्चान्ये घोररूपराक्रमाः॥
en: The infantry, belonging to the Andhara race, commanded by Satyaki, were all possessed of quivers and bows in the hand, of long hairs and were very sweet in speech and endowed with fierce forms and mighty prowess.

sn: अथापरे पुनः शूराश्चेदिपश्चालकेकयाः। कारूषाः कोसलाः काच्या मागधाश्चपि दुद्रुवः॥
en: Thereupon the other heroic leaders, namely the Chedis, the Panchalas, the Kaikeyas, the Karushas, the Kosalas, the Kanchyas and the Magadhas advanced most rapidly.

sn: तेषां रथाश्वनागाश्च प्रवराचोग्रपत्तयः। नानावाद्यधरैर्हष्टा नृत्यन्ति च हसन्ति च॥
en: Their car-warriors, cavalry and elephantforce, that all belonged to the superior class, as well as the terrible-looking infantry, were highly gratified to hear the harmonious sound of several instruments and began to laugh.

sn: तस्य सैन्यस्य महतो महामात्रवरैर्वृतः। मध्ये वृकोदरोऽभ्यायात् त्वदीयान् नागधूर्गतः॥
en: In the midst of at vast army stood Vrikodara, encompassed by the foremost elephant-force and advanced against your troops, each riding on the neck of an elephant.

sn: स नागप्रवरोऽत्युग्रो विधिवत् कल्पितो बभौ। उदयाग्रादिभवनं यथाभ्युदितभास्करम्॥
en: That terrible-looking elephant, the best of his kind, shone with all the equipments befitting him, even as the mountain-abode on the top of the Udaya (mountain) looks resplendent with the rising Sun over it.

sn: तस्यायसं वर्म वरं वररत्नविभूषितम्। ताराव्याप्तस्य नभसः शारदस्य समत्विषम्॥
en: His best armour, made of iron and bedecked with the most precious gems, shone like the autumnal firmament besprinkled with innumerable stars.

sn: स तोमरव्यग्रकरश्चरूमौलिः स्वलंकृतः। शरन्मध्यंदिनार्काभस्तेजसा व्यदहद् रिपून॥
en: He (that Bhima), who had a lance in the hand stretched out and who was crowned with a handsome diadem and who was adorned with innumerable ornaments and who, again, had the brilliancy of the autumnal sun when at the meridian, began to burn the enemies by energy.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा द्विरदं दूरात् क्षेमधूर्तिपिस्थितः। आह्वयन्नभिदुद्राव प्रमनाः प्रपनस्तरम्॥
en: Seeing that elephant from a distance, Kshemadhurti, riding on an elephant and very much gratified in the heart, invited that one, who was much more cheerful than he, to battle and rushed against him (Bhima).

sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं द्विपयोरुग्ररूपयोः। यद्दच्छया द्रुमवतोर्महापर्वतयोरिव॥
en: Then there followed an encounter between the two elephants of formidable appearances according they desired, which (the clephants) were like the two gigantic mountains with trees at their tops. as

sn: संसक्तनागौ तौ वीरौ तोमरैरितरेतरम्। बलवत् सूर्यरश्म्याभौर्भित्त्वान्योन्यं विनेदतुः॥
en: Those two heroic warriors, whose elephants had thus been engaged in the encounter, forcibly pierced each other with their lances, that were resplendent like the rays of the sun and they roared most loudly.

sn: व्यपसृत्य तु नागाभ्यां मण्डलानि विचेरतुः। प्रगृह्य चोभौ धनुषी जनतुर्वै परस्परम्॥
en: Having receded back, they (the two heroes) roved about in circles dismounting from their elephants, and also having taken up their bows, really struck each other.

sn: क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितरवैर्बाणशब्दैस्तु सर्वतः। तौ जनं हर्षयन्तौ च सिंहनादं प्रचक्रतुः॥
en: They cheered the hearts of the people by their roaring sounds and the slaps of their armpits, as well as by the whistling sound of their arrows on all sides; and then they shouted aloud like lions.

sn: समुद्यतकराभ्यां तौ द्विपाभ्यां कृतिनावुभौ। वातोद्भूतपताकाभ्यां युयुधाते महाबलौ॥
en: Again mounting upon their elephants, that had their trunks raised up in the air and that were adorned with banners floating on the wind, both the heroes, perfectly accomplished and possessed of immense strength, went on combating.

sn: तावन्योन्यस्य धनुषी छित्त्वान्योन्यं विनेदतुः। शक्तितोमरवर्षेण प्रावृण्मेधाविवाम्बुभिः॥
en: Thereupon both of them, having cut-off each other's bow, roared and poured forth showers of arrows and lances upon each other, even as the two masses of clouds during the rainy season drop down rains.

sn: क्षेमधूर्तिस्तदा भीमं तोमरेण स्तनान्तरे। निर्बिभेदातिवेगेन षड्भिश्चाप्यपरैर्नदन्॥
en: Then having roared aloud Kshemadhurti pierced Bhima in the chest with great force by means of his lance, as well as by six other (lances).

sn: स भीमसेनः शुशुभे तोमरै रङ्गमाश्रितैः। क्रोधदीप्तवपुर्मेधैः सप्तसप्तिरिवांशुमान्॥
en: That Bhimasena, whose form looked bright with rage, shone with those lances adhering to his body like the resplendent Sun with the masses of clouds about him.

sn: ततो भास्करवर्णाभमञ्जोगतिमयस्मयम्। ससर्ज तोमरं भीमः प्रत्यमित्राय यत्नवान्॥
en: Thereupon, Bhima thrust at his enemy most carefully the lance, made of iron, that had the splendour of the colour of the solar rays and had a speed, direct and straight.

sn: ततः कुलूताधिपतिश्चापमानम्य सायकैः। दशभिस्तोमरं भित्वा षष्ट्या विव्याध पाण्डवम्॥
en: Thereupon having stretched out his bow, the lord of the Kulatas severed the lance by means of ten arrows and pierced the son of Pandu (Bhima) by sixty other shafts.

sn: अथ कार्मुकमादाय भीमो जलदनि:स्वनम्। रिपोरभ्यर्दयन्नागमुन्नदन् पाण्डवः शरैः॥
en: Then having taken up his bow having the twang like the roar of clouds, Bhima the son of Pandu, oppressed his enemy's elephant by arrows and uttered terrible shouts.

sn: स शरोघार्दितो नागो भीमसेनेन संयुगे। गृह्यमाणोऽपि नातिष्ठद् वातोद्भूत इवाम्बुदः॥
en: That elephant, being thus oppressed by the arrows of Bhimasena, did not stay in the field of battle, although repeatedly restrained, even as the cloud dispersed by the wind (run away from their positions).

sn: तमभ्यधावद् द्विरदं भीमो भीमस्य नागराट्। महावातेरितं मेघं वातोद्भूत इवाम्बुदः॥
en: The most formidable and royal elephant of Bhima rapidly followed that elephant of (Kshemadhurti), even as the wind-blown cloud pursues the cloud dispersed by the tempest.

sn: संनिवार्यात्मनो नागं क्षेमधूर्तिः प्रतापवान्। विध्याधाभिद्रुतं बाणैर्भीमसेनस्य कुञ्जरम्॥
en: Kshemadhurti of immense energy having checked his own elephant, pierced with his arrows the elephant of Bhimasena pursuing his own.

sn: ततः साधुविसृष्टेन क्षुरेणानतपर्वणा। छित्त्वा शरासनं शत्रो गमामित्रमार्दयत्॥
en: Thereupon, he (Kshemadhurti), having cutoff his enemy's bow by means of an arrow well-shot, razor-like and straight, highly oppressed that elephant belonging to his foe.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो रणे भीमं क्षेमधूर्तिः पराभिनत्। जघान चास्य द्विरदं नाराचैः सर्वमर्मसु॥
en: Then highly wrathful Kshemadhurti struck Bhima in the battle and killed the elephant by piercing all his vital parts with his arrows.

sn: स पपात महानागो भीमसेनस्य भारत। पुरा नागस्य पतनादवप्लुत्य स्थितो महीम्॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, thus the great prince of elephant, belonging to Bhimasena, fell down. Before the fall of his elephant, Bhiinasena dismounted from him and stood on the earth.

sn: तस्य भीमोऽपि द्विरदं गदया समपोथयत्। तस्मात् प्रमथितान्नागात् क्षेमधूर्तिमवप्लुतम्॥ उद्यतायुधमायान्तं गदयाऽहन् वृकोदरः। स पपात हतः सासिळसुस्तमभितो द्विपम्॥
en: Then he, too, struck down the elephant of his enemy by means of his mace. Then Vrikodara killed Kshemadhurti with his mace, who then had descended from his crushed elephant and had advanced against him with uplifted weapons. Having been thus killed, he, with a sword in the hand, fell down dead by the side of his elephant.

sn: वज्रप्रभग्नमचलं सिंहो वज्रहतो यथा। तं हतं नृपति दृष्ट्वा कुलूतानां यशस्करम्। प्रादवद् व्यथिता सेना त्वदीना भरतर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, even as a lion killed by thunder falls dead by the side of a hill broken down by thunder. having seen the most famous lord of the Kulatas killed, your troops, highly distressed, ran away from ihe field.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: संजय उवाच ततः कर्णो महेष्वासः पाण्डवानामानीकिनीम्। जघान समरे शूरः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then the mighty bowman, the heroic Karna, killed the troops of the Pandavas in battle with the straight arrows.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तथैव पाण्डवा राजंस्तव पुत्रस्य वाहिनीम्। कर्णस्य प्रमुखे क्रुद्धा निजध्नुस्ते महारथाः॥
en: O king, the mighty car-warriors, namely the Pandavas, had most wrathfully smitten the soldiers of your son in the same way in the very presence of Karna.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: कर्णोऽपिराजन् समरे व्यहनत् पाण्डवीं चमूम्। नाराचैरर्करशम्याभैः कर्मारपरिमार्जितैः॥
en: So also Karna, O monarch, began to smite the army belonging to the Pandavas in the field of battle with the arrows, that were bright like the rays of the sun and excellently polished by the black-smith.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तत्र भारत कर्णेन नाराचैस्ताडिता गजाः। नेदुः सेदुश्च मम्लुश्च बभ्रमुश्च दिशो दश॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, there (in the field of battle) the elephants highly afflicted by Karna with his straight arrows, roared most loudly, became weakened and senseless and ran away towards the ten points of the horizon.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: वध्यमाने बले तस्मिन् सूतपुत्रेण मारिष। नकुलोऽभ्यद्रवत तूर्ण सूतपुत्रं महारणे॥
en: O father, while that immense force was being killed by the son of Suta, Nakula proceeded against that mighty car-warrior, the son of the Suta with great rapidity.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: भीमसेनस्तथा द्रौणिं कुर्वाणं कर्म दुष्करम्। विन्दानुविन्दौ कैकेयौ सात्यकिः समवारयत्॥
en: Then Bhimasena checked the progress of Drona's son, who was achieving the most arduous tasks and Satyaki, that of the two Kaikeya princes, Vindu and Anuvindu.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: श्रुतकर्माणमायान्तं चित्रसेनो महीपतिः। प्रतिविध्यस्तथा चित्रं चित्रकेतनकार्मुकम्॥
en: The lord of the earth, Chitrasena, rushed towards Srutakarman, who was advancing against him; so also Prativindhya towards Chitra, who carried a standard of diverse colours and a beautiful bow.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: दुर्योधनस्तु राजानं धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। संशप्तकगणान् क्रुद्धो ह्यभ्यधावद् धनंजयः॥
en: Duryodhana, too, proceeded against the king Yudhishthira the son of Dhrama, while Dhananjaya rushed against the wrathful Samsaptakas.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: धृष्टधुम्नः कृपेणाथ तस्मिन् वीरवरक्षये। शिखण्डी कृतवर्माणं समासादयदच्युतम्॥
en: While that whole host of the foretnost heroes was being thus slain, Dhrishtadyumna rushed against Kripa; and that undecayable Shikhandin proceeded against Kritavarman.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: श्रुतकीर्तिस्तथा शल्यं माद्रीपुत्रः सुतं तव। दुःशासनं महाराज सहदेवः प्रतापवान्॥
en: O mighty monarch, so again, Shrutakirti closed with Shalya; and that son of Madri, Shahadeva of immense prowess, closed with your son, Dussashana.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: कैकेयौ सात्यकिं युद्धे शरवर्षेण भास्वता। सात्यकिः केकयौ चापि च्छादयामास भारत॥
en: In that great battle, the two Kaikeya princes covered Satyaki with a shower of arrows. Satyaki on the other hand covered the two Kaikeya princes (with a shower of brilliant arrows, O descendant of the Bharata race).

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तावेनं भ्रातरौ वीरौ जघ्नतुर्हदये भृशम्। विषाणाभ्यां यथा नागौ प्रतिनागं महावने॥
en: Those two heroic brothers deeply pierced this warrior (Satyaki) in the chest, even as two elephant strike another hostile elephant with their tusks in a dense forest.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: शरसम्भिन्नवर्माणौ तावुभौ भ्रातरौ रणे। सात्यकिं सत्यकर्माणं राजन् विव्यधतुः शरैः॥
en: O monarch, these two heroic brothers whose vital parts were deeply struck with the arrows, pierced Satyaki, who always performed appropriate deeds with their shafts,

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तौ सात्यकिर्महाराज प्रहसन् सर्वतोदिशः। छादयञ्छरवर्षेण वारयामास भारत॥
en: O powerful monarch, Satyaki on the other hand, having smiled and shrouded all the points of the horizon with a shower of arrows, closed with the two brothers, O descendant of the Bharata race.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: वार्यमाणौ ततस्तौ हि शैनेयशरवृष्टिभिः। शैनेयस्य रथं तूर्णं छादयामासतुः शरैः॥
en: Thereupon those two brothers, whose progress was checked by the shower of arrows of Sini's grandson, indeed, covered the car of Sini's grandson with lots of shafts.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तयोस्तु धनुषी चित्रे छित्त्वा शौरिर्महायशाः। अथ तौ सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैर्वारयामास संयुगे॥
en: Having severed the most beautiful bows of those two brothers, then the highly celebrated Shauri restrained the progress of them both in the battle with a shower of sharp arrows.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: अथान्ये धनुषी चित्रे प्रगृह्य च महाशरान्। सात्यकिं छादयन्तौ तौ चेरतुर्लघु सुष्ठु च॥
en: Then having grasped two other beautiful bows and most effective shafts, they two, too, shrounded Satyaki (with the arrows) and roved about in the field with immense activity and expertness.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: ताभ्यां मुक्ता महाबाणाः कङ्कबर्हिणवाससः। द्योतयन्तो दिशः सर्वाः सम्पेतुः स्वर्णभूषणाः॥
en: Those mighty arrows, shot by the two brothers, adorned with the feathers of the Kanka and the peacock and ornamented with gold, fell down (upon the foes), after having illumined all the points of the horizon.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: बाणान्धकारमभवत् तयो राजन् महामृधे। अन्योन्यस्य धनुश्चैव चिच्छिदुस्ते महारथाः॥
en: O monarch, there was a gloom in that formidable battle owing to the shower of arrows shot by both the parties. Then those great car-warriors severed each other's bows.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज सात्वतो युद्धदुर्मदः। धनुरन्त्यत् समादाय सज्यं कृत्वा च संयुगे।॥ क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन अनुविन्दशिरोऽहरत्।
en: Thereupon, O mighty monarch, wrathful Satvata, most invincible in the field, having taken up another bow and stretched its string properly, severed the head of Anuvinda with an arrow, sharp like the razor.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: अपतत् तच्छिरो राजन् कुण्डलोपचितं महत्॥ शम्बरस्य शिरो यद्वनिहतस्य महारणे। शोचयन् केकयान् सर्वाञ्जगामाशु वसुन्धराम्॥
en: O monarch, that mighty head, adorned with ear-rings, fell like the head of Shambara, slain in that dreadful battle (of old). This, having fallen upon the earth most rapidly, greatly aggrieved all the Kaikayas.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं शूरं भ्राता तस्य महारथः। सज्यमन्यद् धनुः कृत्वा शैनेयः पर्यवारयत्॥
en: Having seen that hero slain, his brother, that mighty car-warrior (Vinda), after having stretched out the string of another bow, restrained the course of Shini's grandson.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: स षष्ट्या सात्यकिं विद्धा स्वर्णपु? शिलाशितैः। ननाद बलवन्नादं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Having pierced Satyaki with sixty shafts, all sharpened on stone and adorned with the feathers of gold, he roared most loudly and said-wait, wait.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: सात्यकिं च ततस्तूर्णं केकयानां महारथः। शरैरनेकसाहस्त्रैर्बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्॥
en: The mighty car-warrior of the Kaikeya troops then pierced Satyaki in his arms and chest most rapidly with several thousands of arrows.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: स शरैः क्षतसर्वाङ्गः सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः। रराज समरे राजन् सपुष्प इव किंशुकः॥
en: O king, Satyaki, of true prowess, being thus wounded with the arrows in all his limbs, shone in the field of battle like a Kinshuka with flowers.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: सात्यकिः समे विद्धः कैकेयेन महात्मना। कैकेयं पञ्चविंशत्या विव्याध प्रहसत्रिव॥
en: In the battle, Satyaki, having been pierced by the lofty-minded Kaikeya, smilingly pierced back the Kaikeya chief with twenty-five shafts.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तावन्योन्यस्य समरे संछिद्य धनुषी शुभे। हत्वा च सारथी तूर्णं हयाश्च रथिनां वरौ॥
en: Thereupon those two best of car-warriors, having broken down each other's beautiful bows and also slain each other's drivers and horses.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: विरथावसियुद्धाया समाजग्मतुराहवे। शतचन्द्रचिते गृह्य चर्मणी सुभुजौ तथा॥
en: Both of them, having taken up shields, as if adorned with hundred moons and grasped the best of swords and possessed as they were with the handsome arms, looked resplendent in that great field of battie.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: व्यरोचेतां महारङ्गे निस्त्रिंशवरधारिणौ। यथा देवासुरे युद्धे जम्भशक्रौ महाबलौ॥ मण्डलानि ततस्तौ तु विचरन्तौ महारणे। अन्योन्यमभितस्तूर्णं समाजग्मतुराहवे॥
en: Like the most powerful ones, Jambha and Shakra, in the battle between the celestials and the Asuras. Thereupon both the warriors roved about in that dreadful field of battle in circles and speedily approached each other, engaged in combating, in the battle.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: अन्योयन्यस्य वधे चैव चक्रतुर्यनमुत्तमम्। कैकेयस्य द्विधा चर्म ततश्चिच्छेद सात्वतः॥ सात्यकेस्तु तथैवासौ चर्म चिच्छेद पार्थिवः।
en: Thus the two, again, made the best of their efforts in slaying each other. Then Satvata severed the shield of the Kaikeya chief into two pieces. So also this Vinda severed the shield of Satyaki into two pieces.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: चर्म च्छित्त्वा तु कैकेयस्तारागणशतैर्वृतम्॥ चचार मण्डलान्येव गतप्रत्यागतानि च।
en: The Kaikeya chief, indeed, having thus broken into pieces the shield, that was decked with hundred of stars, roved in circles in the field, sometimes advancing and sometimes receding back.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तं चरन्तं महारङ्गे निस्त्रिंशवरधारिणम्॥ अपहस्तेन चिच्छेद शैनेयस्त्वरयान्वितः।
en: Thereupon the grandson of Shini who was possessed with greatest activity severed him (his head) who having grasped the best of swords, careered in the broad field of battle, by a side-stroke.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: सवर्मा केकयो राजन् द्विधा छिन्नो महारणे॥ निपपात महेष्वासो वजाहत् इवाचलः।
en: O monarch, the Kaikeya prince, that mighty bowman, who was adorned with the shield, being thus cut-off into pieces in that dreadful battle, fell down like a hill broken down by a thunderbolt.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तं निहत्य रणे शूरः शैनेयो रथसत्तमः॥ युधामन्युरथं तूर्णमासरोह परंतपः।
en: That war-like grandson of Shini, that best of car-warriors, that scorcher of enemies, after having slain him (the Kaikeya chief) in battle, immediately ascended the car of Yudhamanyu.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: ततोऽन्यं रथमास्थाय विधिवत्कल्पितं पुनः। केकयानां महत् सैन्यं व्यधमत् सात्यकिः शरैः॥
en: Thereupon, again, having ascended another car, that furnished with its its due equipment's, Satyaki began to destroy the immense army of the Kaikeyas with his was arrows.

description: The slaying of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: सा वध्यामाना समरे केकयानां महाचमूः। तमुत्सृज्य रणे शत्रु प्रदुद्राव दिशो दश॥
en: That vast force of the Kaikeyas, being slaughtered in battle, left that enemy in the field and ran away in the ten different directions of the horizon.

sn: संजय उवाच श्रुतकर्मा ततो राजंश्चित्रसेनं महीपतिम्। आजध्ने समरे क्रुद्धः पश्चाशद्भिः शिलीमुखैः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon, O monarch, the wrathful Shrutakarman had slain down Chitrasena, the lord of the earth, in the battle, by means of fifty different arrows.

sn: अभिसारस्तु तं राजन् नवभिनतपर्वभिः। श्रुतकर्माणमाहत्य सूतं विव्याध पञ्चभिः॥
en: O king, Avishara, indeed, after having struck down that Shrutakarman with nine straight shafts, pierced his driver with five other arrows.

sn: श्रुतकर्मा ततः क्रुद्धश्चित्रसेनं चमूमुखे। नाराचेन सुतीक्ष्णेन मर्मदेशे समार्पयत्॥
en: Wrathful Shrutakarman, on the other hand, had struck down that Chitrasena, who was then standing at the head of his force, with a keen arrow in the most vital part of his body.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महाराज नाराचेन महात्मना। मूर्छामभिययौ वीरः कश्मलं चाविवेश ह॥
en: O great king, that hero, having been deeply pierced by the arrow by the lofty-minded warrior, attained the condition of senselessness and entered into the abode of great grief.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे चैनं श्रुतकीर्तिर्महायशाः। नवत्या जगतीपालं छादयामास पत्रिभिः॥
en: During this interval, the highly famous Shrutakirtin closed this ruler of the earth (his insensible foe) with ninety different shafts.

sn: प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञा चित्रसेनो महारथः। धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन तं च विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: Thereupon Chitrasena, that mighty bowman, having attained consciousness again, struck down his enemy's bow by a broodheaded shafts and also pierced him with seven arrows.

sn: सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय वेगघ्नं रुक्मभूषितम्। चित्ररूपधर चक्रे चित्रसेनं शरोर्मिभिः॥
en: Then he (Shrutakarman) took up another bow, that was capable of casting away fierce arrows and was adorned with gold, made Chitrasena, by piercing him with the torrents of shafts, wear a varied appearance. to

sn: स शरैश्चित्रितो राजा चित्रमाल्यधरो युवा। युवेव समरेऽशोभद्गोष्ठीमध्ये स्वलंकृतः॥
en: That youthful prince, wearing an wonderful appearance with the shafts and putting on handsome garlands, shone in the field of battle, like an youth, excellently decked with ornaments, in the midst of an assembly.

sn: श्रुतकर्माणमथ वै नाराचेन स्तनान्तरे। बिभेद तरसा शूरस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: O monarch, he, indeed, then pierced Shrutakarman in the chest with a keen shaft immediately; and afterwards uttered him-'wait and wait.'

sn: श्रुतकर्मापि समरे नाराचेन समर्पितः। सुस्त्राव रुधिरं तत्र गैरिकाई इवाचलः॥
en: There Shrutakarman, on the other hand, being thus pierced by the arrow in the field of battle, began to shed blood, even as a mountain lets the liquid red chalk flow down.

sn: ततः स रुधिराक्ताङ्गो रुधिरेण कृतच्छविः। रराज समरे वीरः सपुष्प इव किंशुकः॥
en: Thereupon that heroic one, whose limbs were washed in blood and who, again was stained with blood, shone in the field of battle like a Kinshuka covered over with flowers,

sn: श्रुतकर्मा ततो राजशत्रुणा समभिद्रुतः। शत्रुसंवारणं क्रुद्धो द्विधा चिच्छेद कार्मुकम्॥
en: At that time, O monarch, Shrutakarman, having been attacked by his antagonist (Chitrasena), became very wrathful and severed his bow, that was capable of resisting the enemies, into two pieces.

sn: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं नाराचानां शतैस्त्रिभिः। छादयन् समरे राजन् विव्याध च सुपत्रिभि॥
en: Then, again, O monarch, he (Shrutakarman) covered, with three hundred arrows, him, whose bow was already severed into two pieces and pierced him in the field excellent winged shafts.

sn: ततोऽपरेण भल्लेन तीक्ष्णेन निशितेन च। जहार सशिरस्त्राणं शिरस्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Thereupon he had severed the head of that high-souled one, that was adorned with an (iron) protection, with another broad-headed, pointed and sharp-headed arrow.

sn: तच्छिरो न्यपतद् भूमौ चित्रसेनस्य दीप्तिमत्। यद्दच्छया यथा चन्द्रश्चयुतः स्वर्गान्महीतलम्॥
en: That head of Chitrasena, which looked most resplendent, fell down upon the earth, even as the moon, out of her own will, falls upon the ground, being loosened from heaven.

sn: राजानं निहतं दृष्ट्वा तेऽभिसारं तु मारिष। अभ्यद्रवन्त वेगेन चित्रसेनस्य सैनिकाः॥
en: O sire, the troops of Chitrasena, having seen their king slain, marched with great rapidity against Avishara.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महेष्वासस्तत्सैन्यं प्राद्रवच्छरैः। अन्तकाले यथा क्रुद्धः सर्वभूतानि प्रेतराट्।॥
en: Thereupon that mighty bowman, who became very wrathful, rushed against those troops, shooting arrows upon them; even as, during the period of universal dissolution the king of the nether world (Yama), filled with wrath, rushes against all creatures.

sn: ते वध्यामानाः समरे तव पौत्रेव धन्विना। व्यद्रवन्त दिशस्तूर्णं दावदग्धा इव द्विपाः॥
en: Those warriors, having been slain by that bowman, your grandson, in the field of battle, most speedily ran away in all directions; even, the elephants, burnt by the forestconflagration, (run away from the forest).

sn: तास्तु विद्रवतो दृष्ट्वा निरुत्साहन द्विषजये। द्रावयन्निषुभिस्तीक्ष्णैः श्रुतवर्मा व्यरोचत॥
en: Having seen them flying away (from the battle) hopeless of conquering the enemies, Srutakarman, pursuing and shooting keen arrows upon them, looked most brilliant.

sn: प्रतिविन्ध्यस्यतश्चित्रं भित्वा पञ्चभिराशुगैः। सारथिं च त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा ध्वजमेकेषुणापि च ॥
en: Thereupon Prativindhya pierced Chitra with five rapid-going shafts and pierced the driver of his car with three others. Then he broke down his standard by a single arrow. as

sn: तं चित्रो नवभिल्लैर्बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्। स्वर्णपुङः प्रसन्नात्रैः कङ्कबर्हिणवाजितैः॥
en: Then he, (Chitra) pierced him by throwing at his arms and chest nine broad-handed shafts, that were adorned with the wings of gold and sharp points and ornamented with the feathers of the Kanka and peacock.

sn: प्रतिविन्थ्यो धनुश्छित्त्वा तस्य भारत सायकैः। फञ्चभिर्निशितैर्बाणैरथैनं स हि जनिवान्॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, Prativindhya, having severed his (enemy's) bow with keen arrows, slaughtered him with five well-sharpened shafts.

sn: ततः शक्ति महाराज स्वर्णघण्टां दुरासदाम्। प्राहिणोत् तव पौत्राय घोरामग्निशिखामिव॥
en: Thereupon, O great king, he (Chitra) threw at your grandson the shaft, called Shakti, which was decked with golden bells and which, again, was most irresistible and dreadful and which also, was like the flame of fire.

sn: तामापतन्तीं सहसा महोल्काप्रतिमां तदा। द्विधा चिच्छेद समरे प्रतिविन्ध्यो हसन्निव॥
en: Prativindhya, as if laughing, severed into two pieces that shaft, in the field of battle, falling upon him, which was like a great flashing meteor suddenly falling from the sky.

sn: सा पपात द्विधा छिन्न प्रतिविन्ध्यशरैः शितैः। युगान्ते सर्वभूतानि त्रासयन्ती यथाऽशनिः॥
en: That shaft which was cut-off into three pieces by the keen arrows of Prativindhya, fell down like the thunderbolt, during the period of expiration of the Yuga, thus inspiring great fear in all creatures.

sn: शक्तिं तां प्रहतां दृष्ट्वा चित्रो गृह्य महागदाम्। प्रतिविन्ध्याय चिक्षेम रुक्मजालविभूषिताम्॥
en: Having seen that arrows, called Shakti, severed into pieces, Chitra took up his powerful mace, that was adorned with a network of gold and threw it against Prativindhya.

sn: सा जघान हयांस्तस्य सारथिं च महारणे। रथं प्रमृद्य वेगेन धरणीमन्वपद्यत॥
en: That mace had smitten his (antagonist's) heroes and the driver of his car in that great battle and then, having smitten his car, fell impetuously upon the ground.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु रथादाप्लुत्य भारत। शक्तिं चिक्षेप चित्राय स्वर्णदण्डामलंकृताम्॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, he (Prativindhya), in the mean time, having descended from his car, threw at Chitra the arrow, called Shakti, that was furnished with golden balls and decked with several ornaments.

sn: तामापतन्ती जग्राह चित्रो राजन् महामनाः। ततस्तामेव चिक्षेप प्रतिविन्ध्याय पार्थिवः॥
en: The high-minded king Chitra caught hold of it (that shaft), whilst it was falling upon him; and thereafter, O descendant of Bharata race, he threw it back at Prativindhya.

sn: समासाद्य रणे शूरं प्रतिविन्ध्यं महाप्रभा। निर्भिद्य दक्षिणं बाहु निपपात महीतले। पतिताभासयचैव त देशमशनिर्यथ॥
en: That highly resplendent shaft, having pierced heroic Prativindhya in the field of battle and also having penetrated through his right arm, fell down upon the ground; and as it fell, it illuminated that whole region (the battlefield) by its splendour, even as the lightning, falling upon the carth, illumines the entire place, where it falls.

sn: प्रतिविन्ध्यस्ततो राजस्तोमरं हेमभूषितम्। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धश्चित्रस्य वधकाङ्क्षया।॥
en: Thereupon, O monarch, the most wrathful Prativindhya, most desirous of slaying Chitra, hurled at him a lance adorned with gold.

sn: स तस्य गात्रावरणं भित्वा हृदयमेव च। जगाम धरणी तूर्णं महोरग इवाशयम्॥
en: That lance, having pierced through his armour and chest, immediately fell down upon the earth; even as the gigantic serpent enters into its hole.

sn: स पपात तदा राजा तोमरेण समाहतः। प्रसार्य विपुलौ बाहू पीनौ परिघसंनिभौ॥
en: Then that king, having been smitten by the lance, fell upon the earth, stretching out his two long and massive arms, that resembled two iron clubs in splendour.

sn: चित्रं सम्प्रेक्ष्य निहतं तावका रणशोभिनः। अभ्यद्रवन्त वेगेन प्रतिविन्ध्यं समन्ततः॥
en: Having seen Chitra slain (in the battle), the troops on your side, who are all ornaments of battle, rushed from all sides with great impetuosity against Pritivindhya.

sn: सृजन्तौ विविधान् बाणशतघ्नीश्च सकिंकिणीः। तमवच्छादयामासुः सूर्यमभ्रगणा इव॥
en: Shooting several kinds of arms and the shaft called Shataghni, that was ornamented with the rows of bells (those troops) covered him all ever, even as the clouds cover the Sun.

sn: तान् विधम्य महाबाहुः शरजालेन संयुगे। व्यद्रावयत् तव चमूं वज्रहस्त इवासुरीम्॥
en: That mighty-armed one (Prativindhya), having struck those warriors with a net-work of arrows in the field of battle, over threw your force, Indra, who carried the thunderbolt in the hand, over-threw the Asura host.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे तावकाः पाण्डवैर्नृप। विप्राकीर्यन्त सहसा वातनुन्ना घना इव॥
en: Thus slain in the battle by the Pandavas, the troops on your side, O monarch, suddenly broke in all directions, even as the clouds, scattered by the wind, run away in all sides.

sn: विप्रदुते बले तस्मिन् वध्यमाने समन्ततः। द्रौणिरेकोऽभ्ययात् तूर्णं भीमसेनं महाबलम्॥
en: Amongst your whole force, that was immensely slain and (the rest) running away from the field, the son of Drona alone proceeded with great impetuosity against that highly powerful Bhimasena.

sn: ततः समागमो घोरो बभूव सहसा तयोः। यथा देवासुरे युद्धे वृत्रवासवयोरिव॥
en: Then there suddenly followed a dreadful conflict between these two parties; even as there took place an encounter between Vritra even and Vashava (Indra) in the battle between the celestials and the Asuras. and Vashava (Indra) in the battle between the celestials and the Asuras.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: संजय उवाच भीमसेनं ततो द्रोणी राजन् विव्याध पत्रिणा। परया त्वरया युक्तो दर्शयन्नस्त्रलाघवम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon, O king, the son of Drona, who was possessed of great alacrity and who showed easiness in the management of weapons, pierced Bhimasena with an arrow.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: अथैनं पुनराजने नवत्या निशितैः शरैः। सर्वमर्माणि सम्प्रेक्ष्य मर्मज्ञो लघुहस्तवत्॥
en: In the same way, he (the son of Drona), who was well acquainted with the different vital parts of the body and who, again, was very smart in the management of his arms, after having seen all the vital parts of his body, had struck him with ninety sharp-headed shafts.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: भीमसेनः समाकीरें द्रौणिना निशितैः शरैः। रराज समरे राजन् रश्मिवानिव भास्करः॥
en: O monarch. Bhimasenc, having been closed with a shower of keen arrows by the son of Drona, shone in the field of battle like the sun with all his rays.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: ततः शरसहस्रेण सुप्रयुक्तेन पाण्डवः। द्रोणपुत्रमवच्छाद्य सिंहनादममुञ्चत॥
en: Thereupon the Pandava, after having covered the son of Drona with one thousand arrows, well-aimed, sent forth a leonine roar.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: शरैः शरांस्ततो द्रौणि: संवार्य युधि पाण्डवम्। ललाटेऽभ्यानद् राजन् नाराचेन स्मयन्निव॥
en: Then, O monarch, the son of Drona, having checked the course of his (antagonist's) shafts by his own arrows in the field of battle, smilingly struck the son of Pandu in the forehead with a dart.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: ललाटस्थं ततो बाणं धारयामासं पाण्डवः। यथा शृङ्गं वने दृप्तः खङ्गो धारयते नृप॥
en: Thereafter, O king, the son of (Pandu), carried the shafts, that was struck in his forehead; even as the proud rhinoceros in the forest bears his horn.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: ततो द्रौणि रणे भीमो यतमानं पराक्रमी। त्रिभिर्विव्याध नाराचैर्ललाटे विस्मयन्निव॥
en: Then Bhima of immense prowess smilingly pierced the son of Drona, who attempted very hard in the battle, in the forehead with three shafts.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: ललाटस्थैस्ततौ बाणैर्ब्राह्मणोऽसौ व्यशोभत। प्रावृषीव यथा सिक्तस्त्रिशृङ्गः पर्वतोत्तमः॥
en: Then this twice-born person looked most resplendent with the arrows struck in his forehead; even as the best of mountains, being washed (with water) during the rainy season, looks resplendent with its three peaks.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: ततः शरशतैद्रौणिरर्दयामास पाण्डवम्। न चैनं कम्पयामास मातरिश्वेव पर्वतम्॥
en: Thus the son of Drona afflicted the son of Pandu with hundreds of arrows, but he could not shake him; even as the wind cannot shake the mountain.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: तथैव पाण्डवो युद्धे द्रौणि शरशतैः शितैः। नाकम्पयत् संहृष्टो वार्योघ इव पर्वतम्॥
en: In the same way, the son of Pandu, highly gratified, could not shake the son of Drona, in the field of battle, with hundreds of his sharphanded arrows; even as the torrents of rain cannot shake the mountain.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: तावन्योन्यं शरैोरैश्छादयानौ महारथौ। रथवर्यगतौ वीरौ शुशुभाते बलोत्कटौ।॥
en: Those two mighty car-warriors, the two heroic warriors of terrible prowess, having covered each other with their dreadful shafts, looked very handsome, sitting upon their cars.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: आदित्याविव संदीप्तौ लोकक्षयकरावुभौ। स्वरश्मिभिरिवान्योन्यं तापयन्तौ शरोत्तमैः॥
en: Both (the heroes) looked resplendent like two suns and were destructive of men on each other's side. Moreover both of them burnt each other by their own excellent arrows, that resembled their own rays.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: ततः प्रतिकृते यत्नं कुर्वाणौ तौ महारणे। कृतप्रतिकृते यत्तौ शरसङ्घरभीतवत्॥
en: Thereupon, in that dreadful battle, those two heroic warriors made their best attempts in counteracting each other's deeds; and with the torrents of shafts they most fearlessly made efforts in challenging each other.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: व्याघ्राविव च संग्रामे चेरतुस्तौ नरोत्तमौ। शरदंष्ट्रौ दुराधर्षों चापवक्त्रौ भयंकरौ॥
en: Those two foremost of persons, those invincible and fierce heroes, whose teeth were constituted by the shafts and whose mouths were formed by the bows, roved about in the field of battle like two terrible tigers.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: अभूतां तावदृश्यौ च शरजालैः समन्ततः। मेघजालैरिव च्छन्नौ गगने चन्द्रभास्करौ॥
en: Both of them became invisible on account of the torrents of shafts in all sides; even as both the sun and the moon in the firmament become invisible, when they are covered over by the net-work of clouds.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: चकाशेते मुहूर्तेन ततस्तावष्यरिंदमौ। विमुक्तावभ्रजालेन अङ्गारकबुधाविव॥
en: Then the two smiters of foes appeared for a very short while and shone forth like Mars and Mercury, when they become wholly released from the cover of clouds.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: अथ तत्रैव संग्रामे वर्तमाने सुदारुणे। अपसव्यं ततश्चक्रे द्रौणिस्तत्र वृकोदरम्॥
en: Then at that moment, in that dreadful battle, the son of Drona made Vrikodara in the field occupy his right position.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: किरज्छरशतैरुपैराभिरिव पर्वतम्। न तु तन्ममृषे भीमः शत्रोर्विजयलक्षणम्॥
en: And he showered forth hundreds of terrible shafts, even as the masses of clouds drop down torrents of rain upon a mountain. This, indeed, namely the indication of his antagonist's victory Bhimasena could not like to tolerate.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: प्रतिचक्रे ततो राजन् पाण्डवोऽप्यपसव्यतः। मण्डलानां विभोगेषु गतप्रत्यागतेषु च॥
en: Thereupon, O monarch, the son of Pandu baffled his enemy's efforts from the position on his (antagonist's) right side; and they advanced or withdrew according to the divisions of their circular situations.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: बभूव तुमुलं युद्धं तयोः पुरुषसिंहयोः। चरित्वा विविधान् मार्गान् मण्डलस्तथानमेव त॥
en: Thus there ensued a fierce battle between those two foremost of warriors, who roved about (in the field of battle) in several ways and circles.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: शरैः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैरन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः। अन्योन्यस्य वधे चैव चक्रतुर्यनमुत्तमम्॥
en: Both of them struck each other with the arrows shot from their bows stretched to their perfect length; and also they made the best efforts in slaying each other in the battle.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: ईषतुर्विरथ चैव कर्तुमन्योन्यमाहवे। ततो द्रौणिर्महास्त्रणि प्रादुश्चक्रे महारथः॥ तान्यस्त्रैरेव समरे प्रतिजघ्नेऽथ पाण्डवः।
en: Again, each of them wished to make the other carless in the field. Thereupon the son of Drona, that mighty car-warrior, imparted strength to the most powerful weapons, which, indeed the son of Pandu frustrated by the weapons of his own, in the battle.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: ततो घोरं महाराज अस्त्रयुद्धमवर्तत॥ ग्रहयुद्धं यथां घोरं प्रजासंहरणे ह्यभूत।
en: Then, O mighty king, there ensued a very dreadful battle of weapons, even as there had taken place a very terrible battle of the planets, during the time of destruction of creatures of the universe.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: ते बाणः समसज्जन्त मुक्तास्ताभ्यां तु भारत॥ द्यौतयन्तो दिशः सर्वास्तव सैन्यं समन्ततः।
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, those arrows, shot by both of them, struck one another, and thus illumined all the points of the i horizon, as well as the troops on your side, from all directions. even

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: बाणसङ्घवृत घोरमाकाशं समपद्यत॥ उल्कापातावृतं युद्धं प्रजानां संक्षये नृप।
en: O king, the firmament looked very fearful as it was wholly covered by the showers of arrows, it appears during the destruction of the creatures of the universe, when it is entirely shrouded by the fall of the meteors.

description: The encounter between Ashvatthaman and Bhima
sn: बाणभिघातात् संजज्ञे तत्र भारत पावकः॥ सविस्फुलिङ्गौदीप्तर्चिर्योऽदहद् वाहिनीद्वयम्।
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, there (in the field of battle) was produced a great fire by the counteraction of shafts from both the parties, which, viz. the fire was attended with sparks and blazing flames. It continued to burn both the hosts.
