en: Hearing of the great and immense fear of his brother (Yudhishthira), as also witnessing it, the Pandava readily addressed him thus-'O Hrishikesha, urge the horses.'

sn: ततः प्रायाद्हृषीकेशो रथेनाप्रतियोधिना। दारुणश्च पुनस्तत्र प्रादुरासीत् समागमः॥
en: Thereupon, Hrishikesha went (to the battle), ascending on an irresistible car. Then there raged a dreadful battle.

sn: ततः पुनः समाजग्मुरभीताः कुरुपाण्डवाः। भीमसेनमुखाः पार्थाः सूतपुत्रमुखा वयम्॥
en: Then once more both the Kurus and the Pandavas fearlessly came face to face (for an encounter). The sons of Pritha were headed by Bhimasena; and we were headed by the son Suta.

sn: ततः प्रववृत्ते भूयः संग्रामो राजसत्तम। कर्णस्य पाण्डवानां च यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनः॥
en: Thereupon, O best of monarchs, again the dreadful battle took place between Karna and Pandavas, which aggrandised the kingdom of Yama.

sn: धनूर्षि बाणान् परिघानसिपट्टिशतोमरान्। मुसलानि भुशुण्डीश्च सशत्तवृष्टिपरश्वधान्॥ गदाः प्रासाञ्छितान् कुन्तान् भिन्दिपालान् महाङ्कुशान्। प्रगृह्य क्षिप्रमापेतुः परस्परजिघांसया॥
en: Having taken up the bows, the arrows, the spiked maces and the swords, lances and the battle-axes and also the short clubs, the Vushandis, the Shakti-darts, the rapiers and the axes, as well as the iron maces, the spears, the white Kuntas, the short arrows and the hooks, the warriors most rapidly fell upon one another with the desire of killing them.

sn: बाणज्यातलशब्देन द्यां दिशः प्रदिशो वियत्। पृथिवी नेमिघोषेण नादयन्तोऽभ्ययुः परान्॥
en: Having filled the firmament, the ten different points of the horison as well as the other subsidiary subsidiary points points and and the upper atmosphere with the noise of arrows, the bowstring and the sound of palms and again, having made the entire earth echo with the noise of clatter car-wheels, the warriors proceeded against their antagonists.

sn: तेन शब्देन महता संहृष्टाक्रुराहवम्। वीरा वीरैर्महाघोरं कलहान्तं तितीर्षवः॥
en: Being gratified with that tremendous noise, the hero, who were most willing to cross over and reach the shore of that dreadful ocean of hostility, began to fight with numerous other horses.

sn: ज्यातलज्ञधनुःशब्दः कुञ्जराणां च बुंहताम्। पादातानां च पततां नृणां नादो महानभूत्॥
en: There was a great noise of the bowstrings, bows and lances and the loud roar of elephants; as also there were terrible shouts of the foot soldiers and men falling (upon the earth).

sn: तालशब्दांश्चविविधाञ्शूराणां चाभिगर्जताम्। श्रुत्वा तत्र भृशं त्रेसुः पेतुर्मम्लुश्च सैनिकाः॥
en: There, having heard the numerous kinds of arrow sounds and the terrible uproar of the heroic warriors, the combatants were deeply struck with terror, fell down and became very pale.

sn: तेषां निनदतां चैव शस्त्रवर्षं च मुश्चताम्। बहूनाधिरथिर्वीरः प्रममाथेषुभिः परान्॥
en: The warlike son of Adhiratha crushed, with innumerable arrows, large numbers of these enemies, who uttered loud roars and poured forth showers of weapons.

sn: पश्च पश्चालवीराणां रथान् दश च पञ्च च। शाश्वसूतध्वजान् कर्णः शरैर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्॥
en: Then Karna led to the abode of Death twenty car-warriors against the Panchala heroes, along with their horses, drivers and standards, by means of his innumerable arrows.

sn: योधमुख्या महावीर्याः पाण्डूनां कर्णमाहवे। शीघ्रास्त्रास्तूर्णमावृत्य परिवठ्ठः समन्ततः॥
en: Then, again, the best of the warriors of the vast Pandava force, who were all very powerful and who also were very sinart in the management of weapons, after having careered round, surrounded Karna from all sides in the field of battle.

sn: ततः कर्णो द्विषत्सेना शरवर्षेर्विलोडयन्। विजगाहाण्डजाकीर्णां पद्यिनामिव यूथयः॥
en: Thereupon Karna crushed the army belonging to the foes by means of showers of shafts; even as the leader of the elephants, plunging into a lake, crushes down the lotuses and swans, adorning the lake itself.

sn: द्विषन्मध्यमवस्कन्ध राधेयो धनुरुत्तमम्। विधुन्वान्ः शितैर्वाणैः शिरांस्युन्मथ्य पातयत्॥
en: The son of Radha, after having entered the hostile force and also having shaken his best of bonds had struck off their heads with his keen arrows and caused them to fall upon the carth.

sn: चर्मवर्माणि संछिन्नान्यपतन् भुवि देहिनाम्। विषेहुर्नास्य संस्पर्शं द्वितीयस्य पतत्रिणः॥
en: Being broken into pieces, the shields and coats of mail, belonging to the warriors, fell upon the earth; and none of them could bear the touch of a second arrow (to be shot by Karna).

sn: वर्मदेहासुमथनैर्धनुषः प्रत्युतैः शरै। मौळ तलवे न्यहनत् कशया वाजिनो यथा॥
en: He (Karna) struck the fences of the antagonists, that could be perceivable only by the bowstrings, by means of shafts shot from his bow, that were capable of crushing the coats of mail, the bodies and the lives of the combatants); even as one strikes the horses with the whip.

sn: पाण्डुसृञ्जयपञ्चालाशरगोचरमागतान्। ममर्द तरसा कर्णः सिंहो मृगगणानिव॥
en: Then Karna, with great speed, crushed down the Pandus, the Panchalas and the Srinjayas, who came with the reach of his arrows; even as the lion slays the whole lot of dear.

sn: ततः पाञ्चालराजश्च द्रौपदेयाश्च मारिष। यमौ च युयुधानश्च सहिताः कर्णमभ्ययुः॥
en: Thereupon, O sire, the king of the Panchalas, the sons of Draupadi, the twin brothers and Yuyudhana, who all gathered together, advanced against Karna.

sn: तेषु व्यायच्छमानेषु कुरुपाञ्चालपाण्डुषु। प्रियानसून् रणेत्यक्त्वा योधा जघ्नुः परस्परम्॥
en: Whilst the Kurus, the Panchalas and the Pandus were fighting with one another, the combatants, offering up their lives slaughtered one another in the field of battle.

sn: सुसंनद्धाः कवचिनः सशिरस्त्राणभूषणाः। गदाभिर्मुसलैश्चान्ये परिधैश्च महाबलाः॥ समभ्यधावन्त भृशं कालदण्डैरिवोद्यते। नर्दन्तश्चह्वयन्तश्च प्रवल्गन्तश्च मारिष॥
en: O sire, the mighty warriors, who were all protected with armours and coats of mail and who also were ornamented with the headgears, uplifting their maces, short clubs and spiked maces, that resembled the very uplifted rod of Death jumped, marched most rapidly and dreadfully against their antagonists.

sn: ततो निजघ्नुरन्योन्यं पेतुश्चान्योन्यताडिताः। वमन्तो रुधिरं गात्रैर्विमस्तिष्केक्षणायुधाः॥
en: Thereupon they (the combatants), being highly afflicted by one another and also being deprived of their brains, eyes and weapons, struck one another and fell down in the field of battle, when blood gushed out of their limbs.

sn: दन्तपूर्णैः सरुधिरैर्वक्त्रैर्दाडिमसंनिभैः। जीवन्त इव चाप्येके तस्थुः शस्त्रोपबृंहिताः॥
en: Some of the warriors, who were covered over with innumerable weapons, lay in the field of battle); and they were supposed to be alive with faces, that were as handsome as the pomegranates and also that were adorned with numerous teeth and smeared with blood.

sn: परश्वधैश्चाप्यवरे पट्टिशैरसिभिस्तथा। शक्तिभिर्भिन्दिपालैश्च नखरपासतोमरैः॥ ततक्षुश्चिच्छिदुश्चान्ये बिभिदुश्चिक्षिपुस्तथा। संचकर्तुश्च जघ्नुश्च क्रुद्धा रणमहार्णवे॥
en: With the battle-axes, short maces, swords, the arrows called Sakti, the Vindipalas and hooks, spears and lances, others, again, who were highly enraged either crushed, cut-off, pierced, furled down lopped off or slaughtered one another in that vast ocean of battle.

sn: पेतुरन्योन्यनिहता व्यसवो रुधिरोक्षिताः। क्षरन्तः सुरसं रक्तं प्रकृत्ताश्चन्दना इव।॥
en: Being slain by one another, they (the combatants) fell down dead and covered over with blood; even as the sandal trees, being felled, fall down shedding red and excellent juice.

sn: रथै रथा विनिहता हस्तिभिश्चापि हस्तिनः। नरैर्नरा हताः पेतुरश्वश्चाश्वैः सहस्रशः॥
en: Cars, being destroyed by cars and elephants, smitten down by elephants, smitten down by elephants and men, slaughtered by men and horses, fell (upon the earth) in thousands.

sn: ध्वजाः शिरांसि छत्राणि द्विपहस्ता नृणां भुजाः। क्षुरैर्भल्लार्धचन्द्रश्च च्छिन्ना: पेतुर्महीतले॥
en: The standards, heads, umbrellas, trunks of elephants and arms of men, being severed by the razor-like, broad headed and crescentshaped arrows, fell down upon the earth.

sn: नरांश्च नागान् सरथान् हयान् समृदुराहवे। अश्वरोहैर्हताः शूराश्छिन्नहस्ताश्च दन्तिनः॥
en: They (the combatants) had smiiten down in that battle, the men, elephants and horses yoked to the cars. cars. Many heroes, were slaughtered by horsemen; and the elephants had their trunks cut-off.

sn: सपताकाध्वजा: पेतुर्विशीर्णा इव पर्वताः। पत्तिभिश्च समाप्लुत्य द्विरदाः स्यन्दनास्तथा॥
en: The elephants and cars being smitten down by the foot-soldiers, their standards along with their banner fell down like the cloven mountains.

sn: हताश्च हन्यमानाश्च पतिताश्चैव सर्वशः। अश्वारोहाः सामासाद्य त्वरिताः पत्तिभिर्हताः॥
en: On all sides, some (of the warriors) were slaughtered and some were in course of being slaughtered and others, again, fell down. Then the horsemen after having encountered most actively with the foot-soldiers, were killed (by the foot-soldiers).

sn: सादिभिः पत्तिसंघाश्च निहता युधि शेरते। मृदितानीव पद्मानि प्रम्लाना इव च स्त्रजः॥
en: The throngs of foot-soldiers, being slain by the horsemen, were lying on the field of battle, resembling the crushed lotuses and faded floral wreaths.

sn: हतानां वदनान्यासन् गात्राणि च महाहवे। रूपाण्यत्यर्थकान्तानि द्विरदाश्वनृणां नृप। समुन्नानीव वस्त्राणि ययुर्दुर्दर्शतां पराम्॥
en: The faces and limbs of the slain rested on the field and O king, the most beautiful forms of the elephants, horses and men, that resembled the dirty cloths, presented an exceedingly gloomy site.

sn: संजय उवाच हस्तिभिस्तु महामात्रास्तव पुत्रेण चोदिताः। धृष्टद्युम्नं जिघांसन्तः क्रुद्धाः पार्षतमभ्ययुः॥
en: Sanjaya said Having been persuaded by your son, many elephant-warriors, riding upon their elephants and desiring to bring about his destruction, became highly enraged and marched against Dhristadyumna.

sn: प्राच्याश्च दाक्षिणात्याच प्रवरा गजयोधिनः। अङ्ग वङ्गाश्च पुण्ड्राश्च मागधास्ताम्रलिप्तकाः॥
en: Many foremost of clephant-warriors belonging to the tribes called the Easterners, the Southerners, the Angas, the Bangas, the Pundras, the Magadhas and the Tamaliptakas.

sn: मेकला: कोसला मद्रा दशार्णा निषधास्तथा। गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः कलिङ्गैः सह भारत॥
en: And O descendant of the Bharata race, also belonging to the Mekalas, the Koshalas, the Madras, the Dasharnas and the Nishadhas, who were all very skillful in fighting on the back of elephants and who again, were accompanied by the Kalingas.

sn: शरतोमरनाराचैर्वृष्टिमन्त इवाम्बुदाः। सिषिचुस्ते ततः सर्वे पाञ्चालबलमाहवे।॥
en: Began to pour forth showers of arrows, lances and broad-headed shafts, like the masses of clouds and also they all drenched the whole force of the Panchalas (with them) in that battle,

sn: तान् सम्मिमर्दिषून् नागान् पाष्णर्यंङ्गुष्ठाङ्कशै शम्। चोदितान् पार्षतो बाणैराचैरभ्यवीवृषत्॥
en: He (Dhristadyumna) then dropped down showers of arrows and broad-headed shafts upon those elephants, that crushed down the enemies and also that were urged forward by their being deeply struck in the sides with heels, toes and hooks.

sn: एकैकं दशभिः षड्भिरष्टाभिरपि भारत। द्विरदानभिविव्याध क्षिप्तैर्गिरिनिभाशरैः :॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, he (the Panchala chief) pierced every one of these elephants, that resembled mountains with ten, six or eight keen arrows.

sn: प्रच्छाद्यमानं द्विरदैर्मेधैरिव दिवाकरम्। प्रययुः पाण्डुपश्चाला नदन्तो निशितायुधाः॥
en: Both the Pandus and the Panchalas, uttering loud roars and being furnished with the sharp weapons, advanced towards him (the Panchala chief) who was then closed with by those elephants even as the sun is covered over with the masses of clouds.

sn: तान् नागानभिवर्षन्तो ज्यातन्त्रीतलनादितैः। वीरनृत्यं प्रनृत्यन्तः शूरतालप्रचोदितैः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च द्रौपदेयाः प्रभद्रकाः॥ सात्यकिश्च शिखण्डी च चेकितानश्च वीर्यवान्। समन्तात् सिषिचुर्वीरा मेघास्तोयैरिवाचलान्॥
en: Then they (the above warriors) continued to shower (their weapons) upon those elephants and having been excited by the sound of bowstrings and palms, as well as by the beatings (caused by the heroes), began to dance the dance worthy of the heroic warriors. Afterwards Nakula, Shahadeva, the sons of Draupadi, the Provadrakas, Satyaki, Shikhandin and the most powerful Chekitana, these heroes drenched (these elephants) from all sides (with their weapons); even as the clouds drench the mountains with the torrents of water.

sn: ते म्लेच्छः प्रेषिता नागा नरानश्वान् स्थानपि। हस्तैराक्षिप्य ममृदुः पश्चिाप्यतिमन्यवः॥
en: Being driven by the Mlechchas, these elephants, highly enraged, had cast down the men, the horses and cars, with their trunks and crushed them with their feet.

sn: बिभिदुश्च विषाणाप्रैः समाक्षिप्य च चिक्षिपुः। विषाणलग्नाश्चाप्यन्ये परिपेतुर्विभीषणः॥
en: Then they (the elephants) pierced them with the points of their tusks and having thrown them down shattered them. Others, again, being lifted up with their tusks, fell down upon the ground exciting great horror (in the spectators).

sn: प्रमुखे वर्तमानं तु द्विप मङ्गस्य सात्यकिः। नाराचेनोग्रवेगेन भित्वा मर्माण्यपातयत्॥
en: Thereupon Satyaki, after having pierced the elephant of the Vanga prince, that was standing before him, in the very vitals with a long arrows possessed of great impetuosity, hurled him down upon the ground).

sn: तस्यावर्जितकायस्य द्विरदादुत्पतिष्यतः। नाराचेनाहनद् वक्षः सात्यकिः सोऽपतद् भुवि॥
en: Again, Satyaki had struck the chest of him (the rider of that elephant), whose body was not yet touched and who also fell down from his elephant, with a long shaft. Thus struck, he (the rider) fell upon the ground.

sn: पुण्ड्रस्यापततो नागं चलन्तमिव पर्वतम्। सहदेवः प्रयत्नस्तैर्नाराचैरहनत् त्रिभिः॥
en: Shahadeva, on the other hand, had struck the elephant of falling Pundra, that was moving like a mountain, with three long arrows, which were most excellently directed.

sn: विपताकं वियन्तारं विवर्मध्वजजीवितम्। तं कृत्वा द्विरदं भूयं सहदेवोऽङ्गमभ्ययात्॥
en: Then Shahadeva, after having deprived that elephant of his banners, driver, armour, standard and life, again advanced against the ruler of the Angas.

sn: सहदेवं तु नकुलो वारयित्वाङ्गमार्दयत्। नाराचैर्यमदण्डाभैस्त्रिभिर्नागं शतेन तम्॥
en: But Nakula, having forbidden Shahadeva (from advancement), himself crushed the chief of the Angas with three long shafts resembling the very rods of Death in appearance, as well as his elephant with hundred others.

sn: दिवाकरकरप्रख्यानङ्गचिक्षेप तोमरान्। नकुलाय शतान्यष्टौ त्रिधैकैकं तु सोऽच्छिनत्॥
en: The ruler of the Angas, on the other hand, had directed eight hundred lances, that were as resplendent as the rays of the sun, towards Nakula, who, again, shattered each of them into three pieces.

sn: तथार्धचन्द्रेण शिरस्तस्य चिच्छेद पाण्डवः। स पपात हतो म्लेच्छस्तेनैव सह दन्तिना॥
en: So again, the son of Pandu severed the head (of his antagonist) with a crescent shaped arrow. That Mlechchha, being thus cut-off, fell down with his elephant.

sn: अथाङ्गपुत्रे निहते हस्तिशिक्षाविशारदे। अङ्गा क्रुद्धा महामात्रा नागैर्नकुलमभ्ययुः॥
en: Thereupon, when the princes powerful monarch, Satyaki on the other hand, having smiled and shrouded all the points of the horizon with a shower of arrows, closed with the two brothers, O descendant of the Bharata race. of the Angas, who was well versed in the knowledge of managing elephants, was thus slain, the highly enraged elephant-warriors of the Anga race, rushed against Nakula, riding upon their elephants.

sn: चलत्पताकैः सुमुखैहेमकक्षातनुच्छदैः। मिमर्दिषन्तस्त्वरिताः प्रदीप्तैरिव पर्वतैः॥
en: That were adorned with waving banners and also that were furnished with excellent mouths and that were decked with the housings made of gold and that were as resplendent as the blazing mountains; for, the warriors were most desirous of crushing him and all possessed of immense activity.

sn: मेकलोत्कलकालिङ्गा निषधास्ताम्रलिप्तकाः। शरतोमरवर्षाणि विमुञ्चन्तो जिघांसव॥
en: The Mekalas, Utkalas, the Kalingas, the Nishadhas, the Tamraliptakas, who were all very willing to slaughter him, continued to pour forth showers of arrows and lance (upon Nakula).

sn: तैश्छाद्यमानं नकुलं दिवाकरमिवाम्बुदैः। परिपेतुः सुसंरब्धा पाण्डुपञ्चालसोमकाः॥
en: Then the highly enraged Pandus, Panchalas and Somakas proceeded most rapidly to rescue Nakula, who was closed with by those warriors, even as the sun is covered over with the masses of clouds.

sn: ततस्तदभवद् युद्धं रथिनां हस्तिभिः सह। सृजतां शरवर्षाणि तोमरांश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: Thereupon, the battle raged between the car-warriors, who were shooting showers of shafts and hurling down thousands of lances, (at the antagonists) and the heroes fighting from the back of elephant.

sn: नागानां प्रास्फुटन् कुम्भा मर्माणि विविधानि च। दन्ताश्चैवातिविद्धानां नाराचैर्भूषणानि च॥
en: The frontal globes and several other vitals, the tusks and the equipments of the elephants, that were deeply pierced with long shafts, were all shattered.

sn: तेषामष्टौ महानागांश्चतुःषष्ट्या सुतेजनैः। सहदेवो जघानाशु तेऽपतन् सह सादिभिः॥
en: Thereupon Shahadeva had most rapidly slaughtered eight of the gigantic elephants with sixty-four arrows, possessed of great impetuosity. On that, they all fell down along with their riders.

sn: अञ्जोगतिभिरायम्य प्रयत्नाद् धनुरुत्तमम्। नाराचैरहनन्नागान् नकुलः कुलनन्दनः॥
en: Nakula also, who was the darling of his family, after having lifted up the foremost of his bow with great care, had slaughtered innumerable elephants with straight shafts.

sn: ततः पाञ्चालशैनेयौ द्रौपदेयाः प्रभद्रकाः। शिखण्डी च महानागान् सिषिचुः शरवृष्टिभिः॥२७
en: Thereupon the chief of the Panchalas, the grandson of Shini, the son of Draupadi, the Provodrakas and Shikhandin, poured forth showers of arrows upon those huge elephants.

sn: ते पाण्डुयोधाम्बुधरैः शत्रुद्विरदपर्वताः। बाणवर्हताः पेतुर्वज्रवरिवाचलाः॥
en: Having been killed with the torrents of shafts by such clouds as the Pandu warriors, those hills of elephants belonging to the foes, fell down; even as the mountains are struck down by the falling of thunders.

sn: एवं हत्वा तव गजांस्ते पाण्डुरथकुञ्जराः। द्रुतां सेनामवैक्षन्त भिन्नकूलामिवापगाम्॥
en: Having thus slaughtered your elephants, those foremost of car-warriors, belonging to the side of the Pandavas, looked at the army (on your side), that was running away from the field like a river, flowing down a shore other than where it took its rise.

sn: तां ते सेना समालोड्य पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैनिकाः। विक्षोभयित्वा च पुनः कर्णं समभिदुदुवुः॥
en: Those warriors, belonging to the side of the son of Pandu, after having first agitated that army and again having afflicted, proceeded most rapidly against Karna.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: संजय उवाच सहदेवं तथा क्रुद्धं दहन्तं तव वाहिनीम्। दुःशासनो महाराज भ्राता भ्रातरमभ्ययात्॥
en: Sanjaya said O great monarch, Dushasana rushed against Shahadeva, that is, brother against brother, who was highly enraged and blasted your army.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: तौ समेतौ महायुद्धे दृष्ट्वा तत्र महारथाः। सिंहनादरवांश्चक्रुर्वासांस्यादुधुवुश्च ह॥
en: In the field of battle, the mighty carwarriors, seeing those two thus engaged in a encounter, began to uiter shouts resembling the roars of lions and to wave their cloths.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: ततो भारत कुद्धेन तव पुत्रेण धन्विना। पाण्डुपुत्रस्त्रिभिर्बाणैर्वक्षस्यभिहतो बली॥
en: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, the most powerful son of Pandu was decply struck in the chest with three shafts by the bowman, your son, who was highly enraged.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: सहदेवस्तौ राजन् नाराचेन तवात्मजम्। विद्ध्वा विव्याध सप्तत्या सारथिं च त्रिभिः शरै॥
en: Then, O monarch, Shahadeva, after having first pierced your son, again struck him with seventy shafts, as well as his charioteer with threc others.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: दुःशासनस्ततश्चापं छित्वा राजन् महाहवे। सहदेवं त्रिसप्तत्या बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्॥
en: Thereupon, O king, Dushasana, after having severed his bow in that dreadful battle, struck Shahadeva with seventy-three arrows both in the arms and the chest.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: सहदेवस्तु संक्रुद्धः खड्गं गृह्य महाहवे। आविध्य प्रासृजत् तूर्णं तव पुत्ररथं प्रति॥
en: Then the highly enraged Shahadeva, after having taken up his sword and turned it round, had hurled it immediately towards the ear of your son in that fierce encounter.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: समार्गणगुणं चापं छित्वा तस्य महानसिः। निपपात ततो भूमौ च्युतः सर्प इवाम्बरात्॥
en: Thus having severed his (Dusasana's) bow along with its string and arrow, then that fearful sword fell down upon the earth, even as a snake falls down from heaven upon the ground.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: अधान्यद् धनुरादाय सहदेवः प्रतापवान्। दुःशासनाय चिक्षेप बाणमन्तकरं ततः॥
en: Thereupon Shahadeva, possessed of immerise prowess, having taken up another bow, hurled at Dushasana a shaft, capable of bringing about death.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: तमापतन्तं विशिखं यमदण्डोपमत्विषम्। खड्गेन शितधारेण द्विधा चिच्छेद कौरवः॥
en: Then the son of Kuru had severed into two fragments, with his keen-edged sword, that shaft, which was as resplendent as the very rod of Death himself, directed towards him.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: ततस्तं निशित खड्गमाविध्य युधि सत्वरः। धनुश्चान्यत् समादाय शरं जग्राह वीर्यवान्॥
en: Then having turned round that sharp-edged sword in the field of battle, the most powerful one took up another bow most rapidly and grasped an arrow.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा निस्त्रिंशं निशितैः शरैः। पातयामास समरे सहदेवो हसन्निव॥
en: On the other hand, Shahadeva, as if laughing, had suddenly thrown down that sword with keen arrows, that was directed towards him.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: ततो बाणांश्चतुःष्टिं तव पुत्रो महारणे। सहदेवरथं तूर्णं प्रेषयामास भारत॥
en: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, your son most rapidly directed sixty-four arrows against the car of Shahadeva, in that dreadful battle.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: ताञ्छरान् समरे राजन् वेगेनापततो बहून्। एकैकं पञ्चभिर्बाणैः सहदेवो न्यकृन्तत॥
en: Then Shahadeva, O monarch, cut-off every one of these innumerable arrows, that were falling with speed (upon him) with five shafts of his own in that battle.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: संनिवार्य महाबाणांस्तवं पुत्रेण प्रेषितान्। अथास्मै सुबहून् बाणान् प्रेषयामास संयुगे॥
en: Having thus restrained those powerful arrows, shot by your son, he (Shahadeva) sent away innumerable shafts against him (his antagonist) in that dreadful battle.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: तान् बाणांस्तव पुत्रोऽपि छित्त्वैकैकं त्रिभिः शरैः। ननाद सुमहानादं दारयाणो वसुन्धराम्॥
en: Your son, too, having severed every one of these arrows with three shafts of his own, sent out a great uproar; and thereby caused the whole earth echo with it.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: ततोदुःशासनो राजन् विद्ध्वा पाण्डुसुतं रणे। सारथिं नवभिर्बाणैर्माद्रेयस्य समार्पयत्॥
en: Thereupon, O monarch, Dushasana, having pierced the son of Pandu in that battle, had struck the charioteer of the Madraya chief with nine shafts.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: तत: क्रुद्धो महाराज सहदेवः प्रतापवान्। समाधत्त शरं घोरं मृत्युकालान्तकोपमम्॥
en: O mighty monarch, the most powerful Shahadeva, being highly enraged at this, fixed an arrow on his bow, that was as deadly as Death himself.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: विकृष्य बलवञ्चापं तव पुत्राय सोऽसृजत्। स तं निभिद्य वेगेन भित्त्वा च कवचं महत्॥ प्राविशद् धरणी राजन् वल्मीकमिव पन्नगः। ततः सम्मुमुहे राजस्तव पुत्रो महारथः॥
en: Then having stretched his bow with great force, he shot that arrow at your son. O monarch, that shaft, after having successively pierced with great force through his body and his strong armour, itself entered into the earth, even as the snakes enter into the ant-hill. Thereupon, O king, your son, that mighty carwarrior, became senseless.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: मूढ चैनं समालोक्य सारथिस्त्वरितो रथम्। अपोवाह भृशं त्रस्तो वध्यमानः शितैः शरैः॥
en: Having seen him thus senseless and himself being deeply struck with sharp arrows, his charioteer with great rapidity carried away the car.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: पराजित्य रणे तं तु कौरव्यं पाण्डुनन्दनः। दुर्योधनबलं दृष्ट्वा प्रममाथ समन्ततः॥
en: Having defeated that Kuru warrior in battle, the son of Pandu looked at the army of Duryodhana and crushed it on all sides.

description: The encounter between Shahadeva and Dushasana
sn: पिपीलिकपुटं राजन् यथा मृद्गन्नरो रुषा। तथा सा कौरवी सेना मृदिता तेन भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, O monarch, that force belonging to the Kurus was crushed by the son of Pandu, even as a swarm of ants is crushed to death by a man with great rage.

sn: संजय उवाच नकुलं रभसं युद्धे द्रावयन्तं वरूथिनीम्। कर्णो वैकर्तनो राजन् वारयामास वै रुषा॥
en: Sanjaya said O monarch, Karna the son of Vikartana, indeed, restrained with great rage Nakula, who was destroying and dispersing the army (belonging to the Kurus) in that battle.

sn: नकुलस्तु ततः कर्णं प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्। चिरस्य बत दृष्टोऽहं दैवतैः सौम्यचक्षुषा॥
en: Thereupon, Nakula smilingly uttered these words of Karna-'I am, after a long while and through the kindness of the celestials, seen by you.

sn: पश्य मां त्वं रणे पाप चक्षुर्विषयमागतम्। त्वं हि मूलमनर्थानां वैरस्य कलहस्य च॥
en: O wretched one, such as I am, you have become the object of my sight in this battle. Indeed, you are the root of all these evils, as well as of this hostility and warfare.

sn: त्वद्दोषात् कुरवः क्षीणाः समासाद्य परस्परम्। त्वामद्य समरे हत्वा कृतकृत्योऽस्मि विज्वरः॥
en: Through you faults the Kuru warriors, after having fought against one another had become thinned. Having slaughtered you today in the battle. I will consider myself as having performed my duties; and also I will be free from the fever (of my heart).

sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच नकुलं सूतनन्दनः। सदृशं राजपुत्रस्य धन्विनश्च विशेषतः॥
en: Being thus addressed, the son of Suta replied to Nakula in expressions worthy of the son of a king and of a bowman specialiy.

sn: प्रहरस्व च मे वीर पश्यामस्तव पौरुषम्। कर्म कृत्वा रणे शूर ततः कस्थितुमर्हसि॥
en: 'O brave warrior, strike me; we will behold your manliness. O hero, first having achieved some deed in the battle, then it behoves you to speak.

sn: अनुक्त्वा समरे तात शूरा युध्यन्ति शक्तित:। प्रयुध्यस्व मया शक्त्या हनिष्ये दर्पमेव ते॥
en: O sire, without speaking anything (highly of themselves) in the battle, the warriors fight to the best of their might. hence, do you fight with me to the best of your power. I will surely destroy your vanity.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा प्राहरत् तूर्णं पाण्डुपुत्राय सूतजः। विव्याध चैनं समरे त्रिसप्तत्या शिलीमुखैः॥
en: Having addressed him thus, the son of Suta struck the son of Pandu most rapidly and pierced him in the battle with seventy-three arrows.

sn: नकुलस्तु ततो विद्धः सूतपुत्रेण भारत। अशीत्याशीविषप्रख्यैः सूतपुत्रमविध्यत॥
en: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, Nakula, indeed, having been thus pierced by the son of Suta, pierced the Suta's son in return with eight shafts, that were as deadly as the snakes possessing virulent poison.

sn: तस्य कर्णो धनुश्छित्त्वास्वर्णपुङ्खः शिलाशितैः। त्रिंशता परमेष्वासः शरैः पाण्डवमर्दयत्॥
en: Then Karna, that most powerful bowman, after having severed his (enemy's) bow with numerous shafts, winged with gold and sharpened on stone, crushed the son of Pandu with thirty other arrows.

sn: ते तस्य कवच भित्वा पपुः शोणितमाहवे। आशीविषा यथा नागाभित्त्वा गां सलिलं पपुः॥
en: Those arrows, after having pierced through his armour, drank his blood in the battle; even as the snakes of virulent poison, after having penetrated the earth, drink the water.

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय हेमपृष्ठं दुरासदम्। कर्ण विव्याध सप्तत्या सारथिं च त्रिभिः शरैः॥
en: Then he (Nakula), taking up another bow, that was most formidable and adorned with gold on the back, penetrated Karna with twenty shafts and pierced his charioteer with three others.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज नकुलः परवीरहा। क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन कर्णस्य धनुराच्छिनत्॥
en: Thereupon, O mighty king, the highly enraged Nakula, that slayer of heroic foes, severed the bow of Karna with sharp razor-like arrows.

sn: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं सायकानां शतैस्त्रिभिः। आजघ्ने प्रहसन वीरः सर्वलोकमहारथम्॥
en: Thereupon that brave warrior (the son of Pandu) smilingly struck this one (Karna), the mightiest of all car-warriors, (Karma) whose bow severed with three hundred shafts.

sn: कर्णमभ्यर्दितं दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुपुत्रेण मारिष। विस्मयं परमं जम्मू रथिनः सह दैवतैः॥
en: O sire, seeing, Karna thus crushed by the son of Pandu, all the car-warriors, along with the celestials, obtained the highest condition of astonishment.

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय कर्णो वैकर्तनस्तदा। नकुलं पञ्चभिर्बाणैर्जत्रुदेशे समार्पयत्॥
en: Then Karna, the son of Vikartana, grasping another bow, had shot upon Nakula five shafts in the shoulder-joint.

sn: तत्रस्थैरथ तैर्बाणैर्माद्रीपुत्रो व्यरोचयत्। स्वरश्मिभिरिवादित्यो भुवने विसृजन् प्रभाम्॥
en: Thus the son of Madri blazed with those arrows sticking to that place (in his body); even as the sun, shedding lustre on the earth, looks resplendent with his own rays.

sn: नकुलस्तु ततः कर्णं विद्ध्वा सप्तभिराशुगैः। अथास्य धनुषः कोटि पुनश्चिच्छेद मारिष॥
en: Thereupon Nakula, indeed, after having penetrated Karna with seven impetuous arrows, once more severed one of the horns of his bow, O sire.

sn: सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय समरे वेगवत्तरम्। नकुलस्य ततो बाणैः सर्वतोऽवारयद् दिशः॥
en: Thereupon in the field of battle he (Karna), taking up another bow, that was possessed of greater strength, closed the different points of the compass, on every side of Nakula, with his arrows.

sn: संछाद्यमानः सहसा कर्णचापच्युतैः शरैः। चिच्छेद स शरांस्तूर्णं शरैरेव महारथः॥
en: That mighty car-warrior (Nakula), being thus suddenly closed with the arrows, shot from Karna's bow, rapidly struck down these shafts with the arrows of his own.

sn: ततो बाणमयं जालं विततं व्योम्नि दृश्यते। खद्योतानामिव वातैः संपतद्भिर्यथा नभः॥
en: Then that net-work of arrows, spread over the sky, looked like the firmament, covered over with innumerable fire-flies, that roved about it.

sn: तैविमुक्तैः शरशतैश्छादितं गगनं तदा। शलभानां यथा वातैस्तद्वदासीद् विशांमते॥
en: Then, O ruler of earth, the welkin, covered over as it was with the hundreds of arrows shot by both of them, looked even as it was covered over with the swarms of locusts,

sn: ते शरा हेमविकृताः सम्पतन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः। श्रेणीकृता व्यकाशन्त क्रौञ्चाः श्रेणीकृता इव॥
en: Those arrows, that were adorned with gold, having issued forth in continuous lines, looked most handsome like the cranes flying in continuous lines (through the sky).

sn: बाणजालावृत्ते व्योम्नि च्छादिते च दिवाकरे। न स्म सम्पतते भूम्यां किंचिदप्यन्तरिक्षगम्॥
en: When the firmament was thus closed with the net-work of arrows and the sun was covered over with them, none of the rovers of the sky descended upon the earth.

sn: निरुद्ध तत्र मार्गे च शरसंधैः समन्ततः। व्यरोचेतां महात्मानौ कालसूर्याविवोदितौ॥
en: While all the directions were thus closed with the shots of innumerable arrows from all sides, those two lofty-minded heroes blazed forth like two risen suns appearing at the time of universals dissolution,

sn: कर्णचापच्युतैर्बाणैर्वध्यमानास्तु सोमकाः अवालीयन्त राजेन्द्र वेदनार्ता भृशार्दिताः॥
en: O foremost of monarchs, having been highly oppressed with the pain and greatly crushed and slaughtered by these arrows shot from the bow of Karna, all the Somakas dicd.

sn: नकुलस्य तथा बाणैर्हन्यमाना चमूस्तव। व्यशीर्यत दिशो राजन् वातनुन्ना इवाम्बुदा॥
en: In the same way, O king, the army on your side, thus slain by the arrows of Nakuſa, dispersed on all sides; even as the masses of clouds are dispersed by the wind.

sn: ते सेने हन्यमाने तु ताभ्यां दिव्यैर्महाशरैः। शरपातमपाक्रम्य तस्थतुः प्रेक्षिके तदा॥
en: The two armies, being thus slaughtered by both the (above) warriors with divine arrows, possessed of great impetuosity, fled beyond the WW reach of falling shafts and stood even as they were spectators (of the battle).

sn: प्रोत्सारितजने तस्मिन् कर्णपाण्डवयोः शरैः। अविध्येतां महात्मानावन्योन्यं शरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Thus when both the armies were dispersed by the arrows of Karna and the son of Pandu, these two high-minded warriors pierced each other with showers of shafts.

sn: विदर्शयन्तौ दिव्यानि शस्त्राणि रणमूर्धनि। छादयन्तौ च सहसा परस्परवधैषिणौ।॥
en: Most willing to kill each other, both the warriors showed their celestial weapons in the battle-field and closed each other all on a sudden (with showers of arrows).

sn: नकुलेन शरा मुक्ताः कङ्कबहिणवाससः। सूतपुत्रमवच्छाद्य व्यतिष्ठन्त यथाम्बरे॥
en: The arrows that were furnished with the Kanka, the peacock feathers and garments, shot by Nakula, after having closed the son of Suta, appeared to stay on the sky.

sn: तथैव सूतपुत्रेण प्रेषिताः परमाहवे। पाण्डुपुत्रमवच्छाद्य व्यतिष्ठन्ताम्बरे शराः॥
en: In the same way, the arrows that were shut by the son of Suta in that fierce battle, after having closed the son of Pandu appeared to stay on the sky.

sn: शरवेश्मप्रविष्टौ तौ ददृशाते न कैश्चन। सूर्याचन्द्रमसौः राजञ्छाद्यमानौ घनैरिव॥
en: O monarch, both the warriors, having entered the chambers composed of arrows, could not be seen by any persons; even as both the sun and the moon, covered over with the masses of clouds, cannot be seen by any persons.

sn: तत: क्रुद्धो रणे कर्णः कृत्वा घोरतरं वपुः। पाण्डवं छादयामास समन्ताच्छरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Thereupon Karna, who was highly enraged, after having assumed a very terrible look in the field of battle, shrouded the son of Pandu with showers of shafts shot from all sides,

sn: सोऽतिच्छन्नो महाराज सूतपुत्रेण पाण्डवः। न चकार व्यथां राजन् भास्करो जलदैर्यथा।॥
en: O powerful monarch, the son Pandu, who was wholly shrouded by the son of Suta (with arrowy showers), did not feel any uneasiness; even as the sun (the giver of light), covered by the clouds, feels no pain.

sn: ततः प्रहस्याधिरथिः शरजालानि मारिष। प्रेषयामास समरे शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Thereupon, O sire, the son of Adhiratha, after smiling from a time, shot forth hundreds and thousands of shafts in the field of battle.

sn: एकच्छायमभूत् सर्व तस्य बाणैर्महात्मनः। अभ्रच्छायेव संजज्ञे सम्पतद्भिः शरोत्तमैः॥
en: There (upon the field of battle) all appeared to be one continuous shade by the shafts of that lofty-minded one (Karna) even as there formed a shade of clouds by the foremost of falling arrows.

sn: ततः कर्णो महाराज धनुश्छित्त्वा महात्मनः। सारथिं पातयामास रथनीडाद्धसन्निव॥
en: Then, O powerful monarch, Karna after having severed the bow of that high-souled one (Nakula), smilingly caused the fall of his charioteer from the car-nichi.

sn: ततोऽश्वांश्चतुस्चास्य चतुर्भिनिशितैश्र शरैः। यमस्य भवनं तूर्णं प्रेषयामास भारत॥
en: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, he (Karna) sent away the four horses of him (Nakula) to the abode of Death most rapidly by means of four sharp-edged arrows.

sn: अथास्यं त रथं दिव्यं तिलशो व्यधमच्छरैः। पताकां चक्ररक्षांश्च गदां खङ्गं च मारिष॥ शतचन्द्रं त तधर्म सर्वोपकरणानि च।
en: Then also he with innumerable arrows, cutoff into minute fragments his (antagonist's) celestial car, his standard, the protector of his car-wheels, his mace and sword and his shield, that was furnished with hundreds of moons, as well as his all other equipment's of war, O sire.

sn: हताश्वो विस्थाश्चैव विवर्मा च विशाम्पते॥ अवतीर्य रथातूर्णं परिघं गृह्य धिष्ठितः।
en: O ruler of earth, losing his horse and being deprived of his car and shield, he (Nakula) immediately alighted from his car and taking up his spiked club, stood (in the field of battle).

sn: तमुद्यतं महाघोरं परिघं तस्य सूतजः॥ व्यहनत् सायकै राजन् सुतीक्ष्णैर्भारसाधनैः।
en: O monarch, the son of Suta had struck down that dreadful mace, uplifted by him, with the keenest arrows, capable of bearing the greatest strain.

sn: व्यायुधं चैनमालक्ष्य शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ आर्पयद् बहुभिः कर्णो न चैनं समपीडयत्।
en: On seeing him (his antagonist) without any weapons, Karna afflicted him with numerous straight arrows; but he did not oppress him too severely.

sn: स हन्यमानः समरे कृतास्त्रेण बलीयसा॥ प्राद्रवत् सहसा राजन् नकुलो व्याकुलेन्द्रियः।
en: O monarch, Nakula of agitated senses, who was struck by that most powerful warrior, well versed in the science of arms in the battle, fled away all on a sudden.

sn: तमभिदुत्य राधेयः प्रहसन् वै पुनः पुनः॥ सज्यमस्य धनुः कण्ठे व्यवासृजत भारत।
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, the sons of Radha, indeed laughing, again and again and pursuing him (Nakula), placed the bow, that was furnished with string, around his neck.

sn: ततः स शुशुभे राजन् कण्ठासक्तमहाधनुः॥ परिवेषमनुप्राप्तो यथा स्याद् व्योम्नि चन्द्रमाः। यथैव चासितो मेघः शक्रचापेन शोभितः॥
en: Thereupon, O king, that strong bow placed round his neck, blazed forth, like the moon in the firmament, when he is surrounded by a halo of light or like the mass of black clouds adorned by the bow Indra.

sn: तमब्रवीत्ततः कर्णो व्यर्थं व्याहृतवानसि। वदेदानीं पुनर्हष्टो वध्यमानः पुनः पुनः॥ मा योत्सीः कुरुभिः सार्धे बलवद्भिश्च पाण्डव। सदृशैस्तात युध्यस्व व्रीडां मा कुरु पाण्डव॥ गृहं वा गच्छ माद्रेय यत्र वा कृष्णफाल्गुनौ। एवमुक्त्वा महाराज व्यसर्जयत् तं तदा॥
en: Then Karna addressed him thus-'whatever you speak is of no avail. Being delighted, do you utter those words once more, as you are struck over and over again. O son of Pandu, do you not fight with the mightiest of Kurus; O son, fight with those, that are your cquals. O son of Pandu, do not be ashamed of it. O son of Madri, go home, where are Krishna and Falguna.' O most powerful monarch, he then, having addressed him thus, dismissed him at that time.

sn: वधप्राप्तं तु तं शरो नाहनद् धर्मवित्तदा। स्मृत्वा कुन्त्यावचो राजंस्तत एनं व्यसर्जयत्॥
en: Thereupon that hero (Karna), who was well-versed in the code of morality and did not slaughter him (Nakula), who was almost within the reach of Death himself. Then, O monarch, resembling the words of Kunti, he (Karna) let hiin go.

sn: विसृष्टः पाण्डवो राजन् सूतपुत्रेण धन्विना। ब्रीडन्निव जगामाथ युधिष्ठिररथं प्रति॥
en: O king, the son of Pandu, being thus abandoned by that bowman, the son of Suta and feeling shame for it, went towards the car of Yudhishthira.

sn: आरुरोह रथं चापि सूतपुत्रप्रतापितः। निश्वसन् दुःखसंतप्तः कुम्थ्यस्थ इव पन्नगः॥
en: He then, being afflicted by the son of Suta, ascended the car (of his brother) and being oppressed with grief, sighed heavily like shake confided within a vessel.

sn: तं विजित्याथ कर्णोऽपि पञ्चालांस्त्वरितो ययौ। रथेनातिपताकेन चन्द्रवर्णहयेन त ॥
en: Then Karna, after having defeated him (Nakula), rushed most rapidly against the Panchalas, riding upon a car, that was furnished with innumerable standards and having the colour of the moon.

sn: तत्राक्रन्दो महानासीत् पाण्डवानां विशाम्पते। दृष्ट्वा सेनापति यान्तं पञ्चालानां रथव्रजान्॥
en: On seeing the commander of the (Kaurava) army rushing against the car-warriors of the Panchala force, there arose a dreadful uproar against the Pandavas, O ruler of earth.

sn: तत्राकरोन्महाराज कदनं सूतनन्दनः। मध्यं प्राप्ते दिनकरे चक्रवद् विचरन् प्रभुः॥
en: O most powerful monarch, that lord the son of Suta, circling round the field of battle, like a wheel, perpetuated an immense slaughter there at the time when the sun attained the meridian.

sn: भग्नचकै रथेः सांश्चिच्छिन्नध्वजपताकिभिः हताश्चैर्हतसूतैश्च भग्नाक्षैश्चैव मारिष॥ ह्रियमाणानपश्याम पञ्चालानां रथव्रजान्।
en: O sire, we saw numerous car-warriors of the Panchala army, who were carried away (from the field of battle) upon cars, some of which had their, wheels broken down and some of which had their banners and standards torn into pieces and some also had their horses and drivers slaughtered (in the battle) and some, again, were without their wheels,

sn: तत्र तत्र च सम्भ्रान्ता विचेरुरथकुञ्जराः॥ दावाग्निपरिदग्धाङ्गा यथैव स्युर्महावने।
en: Innumerable elephants, also wandered and run about in the different directions of the field of battle, some of which had their bodies wholly burnt by the forest-fire.

sn: भिन्नकुम्भारुधिरश्छिन्नहस्ताश्च वारणाः॥ छिन्नगात्रावराचैव च्छिन्नवालधयोऽपरे। छिन्नाभ्राणीव सम्पेतुर्हन्यमाना महात्मना॥
en: Innumerable elephants had their frontal globes severed and the bodies besmeared with blood and the trunks cut-off into fragments. Moreover, O sire, some other elephants, being slaughtered by that high souled one (Karna) fell down with their armour cut-off, or their tails curtailed, like the masses of clouds dispersed by the wind.

sn: अपरे त्रासिता नागा नाराचशरतोमरैः। तमेवाभिमुखं जग्मुः शलभा इव पावकम्॥
en: Again, other elephants, that were terrified by the shots of arrows and lances of sons of Radha, rushed with their faces towards him (the son of Radha); even as the insects rush towards the blazing fire.

sn: अपरे निष्टनन्तश्च व्यद्दश्यन्त महाद्विपाः। क्षरन्तः शोणितं गात्रैर्नगा इव जलस्त्रवाः॥
en: Other mighty elephants were looked to strike against one another. They also shed blood from their limbs, even as the mountains let flow streams of water from their summits.

sn: उरश्छदैर्वियुक्तांश्च वालबन्धैश्च वाजिनः। राजतैश्च तथा कांस्यैः सौवर्णेश्चैव भूषणैः॥ हीनांश्चाभरणैश्चैव खलीनैश्च विवर्जितान्। चामरैश्च कुथाभिश्चैव तूणीरैः पतितैरपि॥ निहतैः सादिभिश्चैव शूरैराहवशोभितैः। अपश्याम रणे भ्राम्यमाणान् हयोत्तमान्॥
en: There is the field of battle, we saw numerous best heroes roving about in all directions-the heroes that were deprived of their breast-plates and several kinds of ornaments, made of silver, brass and gold and also that were diverged of their trappings, bridle-bits yak-tails and saddle-cloths and again, that had their quivers, falling off (from their bodies) and whose brave riders, who formed the beauty of battle were all slain.

sn: प्रासैः खङ्गैश्च रहितानृष्टिभिश्चापि भारत। हयतादीनपश्याम कञ्चकोष्णीधारिणः॥ निहतान् वध्यमानांश्च वेपमानांश्च भारत। नानागावयवैीनास्तत्र तत्रैव भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, we saw numerous horsemen, furnished with armou and coronets, who, being penetrated by the swords, scimitars, lances and clubs, were either slain, or in course of being slaughtered or were trembling with terror and who, again were deprived of their various limbs, on all sides of the field of battle.

sn: रथान् हेमपरिष्करान् संयुक्तञ्जवनैर्हयैः। भ्राम्यमाणानपश्याम हतेषु रथिषु द्रुतम्॥
en: We behold the cars, that were adorned with gold and to which were yoked the heroes of greatest speed, dragged in the different directions of the field with great rapidity; while their riders were all slaughtered.

sn: भग्नाक्षकूबरान् कांश्चिद् भग्नचक्रांश्च भारत। विपताकध्वजांश्चान्यच्छिन्नेषादण्डबन्धुरान्॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, some of these cars had their axes and poles shattered into fragments; and some others had their wheels broken; and others, again had their banners and standards torn into pieces; and several others were deprived of their arrows.

sn: विहतान् रथिनस्तत्र धावमानांस्ततस्ततः। सूतपुत्रशरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्हन्यमानान् विशाम्पते॥ विशस्त्रांश्च तथैवान्यान् सशस्त्रांश्च हतान् बहून्।
en: O ruler of earth, there is the field of battle we saw numerous car-warriors rushing in all directions who were deprived of their cars and who also were afflicted by the arrows of the son of Suta and some of whom, again, were divested of their weapons, and innumerable Other car-warriors were seen slaughtered there still with their weapons on.

sn: तारकाजालसंछन्नान् वंरघण्टाविशोभितान्॥ नानावर्णविचित्राभिः पताकाभिरलंकृतान्। वारणाननुपश्याम धावमानान् समन्ततः॥
en: We saw numerous elephants running in all directions of the field of battle, that were adorned with innumerable stars and that were furnished with the most handsome bells and also that were ornamented with banners variegated with various colours.

sn: शिरांसि बाहूनूरूंश्च च्छिन्नानन्यांस्तथैव च। कर्णचापच्युतैर्बाणैरापश्याम समन्ततः॥
en: Moreover, we behold on all side of the field of battle, numerous heads, arms, chests and other parts of the body, that were severed by the arrows shot from the bow of Karna.

sn: महान् व्यतिकरो रौद्रो योधामान्वपद्यत। कर्णसायकनुन्नानां युध्यतां च शितैः शरैः॥
en: The most dreadful and distressing calamity had fallen upon all the warriors while they were fighting with the keen arrows and cut-off with the shafts of Karna.

sn: ते वध्यमाना समरे सूतपुत्रेण सृञ्जयाः। तमेवाभिमुखं यान्ति पतङ्गा इव पावकम्॥
en: The Srinjayas were slaughtered by the son of Suta in the field of battle and they rushed towards the force of Karna, even as the insects rash towards the fire.

sn: तं दहन्तमनीकानि तत्र तत्र महारथम्। क्षत्रिया वर्जयामासुर्युगान्तग्निमिवोल्बणम्॥
en: All the Kshatriyas (the warriors) abandoned that mighty car-warrior who was slaughtering the forces (belonging to the Pandavas) on all sides of the battle, even as they abandon the blazing fire, that appears at the universal dissolution.

sn: हतशेषास्तु ये वीराः पञ्चालानां महारथाः। तान् प्रभग्नान् दुतान् वीरः पृष्ठतो विकिरञ्छरैः॥ अभ्यधावत तेजस्वी विशीर्णकवचध्वजान्। तापयामास तान् बाणैः सूतपुत्रो महाबलः। मध्यंदिनमनुप्राप्तो भूतानीव तमोनुदः॥
en: That hero of immense prowess (Karna) pursued these powerful car-warriors belonging to the Panchala divisions, shooting dreadful arrows at them from behind, while they (these car-warriors), as they survived the slaughter, were broken and running away from the field and deprived of their armours and standards. The son of Suta, who was endowed with great strength, afflicted them with his arrows; even as the remover of darkness (the sun), having reached the meridian, afflicts all the creatures with his rays.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: संजय उवाच युयुत्सुं तव पुत्रस्य द्रावयन्तं बलं महत्। उलूको न्यपतत्तूर्णं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then Uluka rushed most rapidly against Yuyutsu, who was routing the vast force belonging to your son; and uttered to him those words-'do you wait, do you wait.'

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: युयुत्सुश्च ततो राजशितधारेण पत्रिण। उलूकं ताडयामास वज्रेणेव महाबलम्॥
en: Thereupon, O monarch, Yuyutsu afflicted Uluka with a sharp-edged arrow (supplied with wings), even as a huge mountain is struck with the thunderbolt.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: उलूकस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्तव पुत्रस्य संयुगे। क्षुरप्रेण धनुश्छित्त्वा ताडयामास कर्णिना॥
en: Thus Uluka, too, being highly enraged and cutting off the bow of your son with a razor like shaft, struck him with a barbed arrows in the field of battle.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं युयुत्सुर्वेगवत्तरम्। अन्यदादत्त सुमहचापं संरक्तलोचनः॥
en: Yuyutsu, whose eyes became red with anger, after having thrown aside that severed bow, grasped another, the most dreadful one, possessed of greater impetuosity.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: शाकुनिं तु ततः षष्ट्या विव्याध भरतर्षभ। सारथिं त्रिभिरानर्छनं च भूयो व्यविध्यत॥
en: Thereupon, O foremost of the Bharata race, he (Yuyutsu) penetrated Uluka with sixty arrows; and then struck down his driver with three; and he once more pierced him (Uluka).

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: उलूकस्तं तु विंशत्या विद्ध्वा स्वर्णविभूषितैः। अथास्य समरे क्रुद्धो ध्वजं चिच्छेद काञ्चनम्॥
en: Uluka, too, who became highly wrathful, after having pierced him (Yuyutsu) with twenty arrows, decked with gold, struck down his standards, that was made of gold, in the field of battle.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: सच्छिन्नयष्टिः सुमहाशीर्यमाणो महाध्वजः। पपात प्रमुखे राजन् युयुत्सोः काञ्चनध्वजः॥
en: O monarch, that huge and magnificent standard, that one made of gold, being torn off and shattered into fragments, dropped down in front of Yuyutsu.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: ध्वजमुन्मथितं दृष्ट्वा युयुत्सुः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः। उलूकं पञ्चभिर्बाणैराजधान स्तनान्तरे॥
en: Seeing his standards thus cut-off, Yuyutsu, who became senseless with rage, struck Uluka with five arrows in the chest.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: उलूकस्तस्य समरे तैलधौतेन मारिष। शिरश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन यन्तुर्भरतसत्तम॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, O sire, Uluka then severed the head of his foe, with a broad-headed arrows, dipped in oil, in the field of battle.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तच्छिन्नमपतद् भूमौ युयुत्सोः सारथेस्तदा। तारारूपं यथा चित्रं निपपात महीतले॥
en: The cut-off head of Yuyutsu fell on ground as if any excellent star is fallen from sky on the ground.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: जघान चतुरोऽश्वांश्च तं च विव्याध पञ्चभिः। सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता प्रत्यपायाद् रथान्तरम्॥
en: Then he (Uluka), slaughtered his four horses and pierced himself (Yuyutsu) with five shafts. He (Yuyutsu), being thus fierced by that powerful one (Uluka) went into another car.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तं निर्जित्य रणे राजन्नुलूकस्त्वरितो ययौ। पञ्चालान् सृञ्जयांश्चैव विनिघ्नन् निशितैः शरैः॥
en: O monarch, Uluka, after having defeated him (his antagonist) in the battle, hastened towards the Panchalas and the Srinjayas and slew them with the keen arrows.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: शतानीकं महाराज श्रुतकर्मा सुतस्तव। व्यश्वसूतरथं चक्रे निमेषार्धादसम्भ्रमः॥
en: O mighty monarch, your son, Srutakarman, deprived, without any fear, Shatanika of his horses, charioteer and car within half the time taken up by the twinkling on an eye.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: हताश्वे तु रथे तिष्ठञ्शतानीको महारथः। गदां चिक्षेप संक्रुद्धस्तव पुत्रस्य मारिष॥
en: O sire, that mighty car-warrior, Shatanika, waiting in a car, that was deprived of its horses and becoming very wrathful, had thrown a mace upon your son.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: सा कृत्वा स्यन्दनं भस्म हयांश्चैव ससारथीन्। पपात धरणी तूर्ण दारयन्तीव भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, that mace, after having reduced the car and the horses along with the riders themselves into dusts (belonging to your son), fell down upon the earth most rapidly and penetrated through it.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तावुभौ विरथौ वीरौ कुरुणां कीर्तिवर्धनौ। व्यपाक्रमेतां युद्धात्तु प्रेक्षमाणौ परस्परम्॥
en: Then those two brave warriors, who were divested of their cars and who also had contributed to the increase of the glory of the Kurus, really fled away from the battle, looking each other in the face.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: पुत्रस्तु तव सम्भ्रान्तो विविंशो रथामारुहत्। शतानीकोऽपि त्वरितः प्रतिविन्ध्यरथं गतः॥
en: Thereupon your son, who became highly terrified, ascended the ascended the car of Vivingsa. Shatanika, too, with rapidity, mounted upon the car of Prativindhya.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: सुतसोमं तु शकुनिर्विद्ध्वा तु निशितैः शरैः। नाकम्पयत संक्रुद्धो वार्योघ इव पर्वतम्॥
en: Shakuni, who became very angry after having pierced Sutasoma with excellently sharpened arrows, could not cause him to tremble (with fear); even as a torrent of rain cannot shake a mountain.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: सुतसोमस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा पितुरत्यन्तवैरिणम्। शरैरनेकसाहस्त्रैश्छादयामास भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, Sutasoma, too, after having seen the bitterest enemy of his father, closed him with several thousands of arrows.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: ताशराशकुनिस्तूर्णं चिच्छेदान्यैः पतित्रिभिः। लघ्वस्त्रश्चित्रयोधी च जितकाशी च संयुगे॥ निवार्य समरे चापि शरांस्तान् निशितैः शरैः। आजघान सुसंक्रुद्धः सुतसोमं त्रिभिः शरैः॥
en: Shakuni, too, on the other hand, who was of light arms and who was acquainted with all sorts of warfare and who, again, was most desirous of winning victory, severed all those shafts with other winged arrows of his own. Then he (Shakuni), who was greatly enraged, after having restrained these arrows with the keen arrows of his own in the field of battle, struck down Sutasoma with three other shafts.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तस्याश्वान् केतनं सूतं तिलशो व्यधमच्छरैः। स्यालस्तव महाराज तत उच्चुक्रुशुर्जनाः॥
en: Thereupon, O great king, your brother-inlaw cut of his (antagonist's) horses, standard and charioteer into minute pieces by numerous arrows. At this, the people sent forth a loud roar.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: हताश्वो विरथश्चैव छिन्नकेतुश्च मारिष। धन्वी धनुर्वरं गृह्य रथाद् भूमावतिष्ठत॥
en: O sire, after taken up another excellent bow, that great bowman who was now steedless and carless and whose standard and charioteer into minute pieces by numerous arrows. At this, the people sent forth a loud roar.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: व्यसृजत सायकांश्चैव स्वर्णपुङ्खशिलाशितान्। छादयामास समरे तव स्यालस्य त रथम्॥
en: He (Sutasoma) then directed the shafts, that were furnished with the golden wings and also that were whetted on stone; and afterwards severed the car of your brother-in-law (with those shafts) in the field of battle.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: शलभानामिव वाताशरवातान् महारथः। रथोपगान् समीक्ष्यैवं विव्यथे नैव सौबलः॥ प्रममाथ शरांस्तस्य शरवातैर्महायशाः।
en: That mighty car-warrior, the son of Subala did not at all feel pain to behold the fights of arrows, that were like the throngs of locusts, approaching towards his car. Rather that highly glorious one really restrained those arrows with numcrous arrows of his own.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तत्रातुष्यन्त योधाश्च सिद्धाश्चापि दिवि स्थिताः॥ सुतसोमस्य तत् कर्म दृष्ट्वा श्रद्धेयमद्भुतम्। रथस्यं शकुनि यस्तु पदाति: समयोधयत्॥
en: There (in the field of battle) the warriors, as well as the Siddhas resting in the firmament, became highly gratificd to witness that extraordinary and incredible deed of Sutasoma. For he (Sutasoma) was fighting on foot with Shakuni, who rested upon his car.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तस्य तीक्ष्णैर्महावेगैर्भल्लैः संनतपर्वभिः व्यहनत् कार्मुकं राजंस्तूणीरांश्चैव सर्वशः॥
en: O king, he (Shakuni) severed the bow, as well as all the quivers of him (Sutasoma) by means of his broad-headed arrows, that were excellently whetted and also that were endued with great impetuosity and again, that were very straight. was

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: स च्छिन्नधन्वा विरथः खङ्गमुद्यम्य चानदत्। वैदूर्योत्पलवर्णाभं दन्तिदन्तमयत्सरुम्॥
en: Then he (Sutasoma), who thus deprived of his car and bow, raised a loud roar, after raising his sword that had the splendour of a blue lotus-color and also that had a handle made of ivory.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: भ्राम्यमाणं ततस्तं तु विमलाम्बरवर्चसम्। कालदण्डोपमं मेने सुतसोमस्य धीमतः॥
en: That sword of highly intellectual Sutasoma, whirled round by him, he (Shakuni) considered to be as resplendent as the clear sky, like the very rod of Death himself.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: सोऽचरत् सहसा खड्गी मण्डलानि सहस्रशः। चतुर्दश महाराज शिक्षाबलसमन्वितः॥
en: O powerful monarch, that holder of sword, who was endued with great lore and prowess, suddenly roved about creating fourteen different kinds of circle (Manoeuvres) on all sides (of the battle).

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: भ्रान्तमुद्धान्तमाविद्धमाप्लुतं विप्लुतं सृतम्। सम्पातसमुदीर्णे च दर्शयामास संयुगे।॥
en: He then exhibited in the field of battle the different kinds of dexterities of motion, namely, wheeling and whirling at certain height and making side-thrusts, rushing forward and jumping on high and moving about rapidly and advancing upwards and forwards.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: सौबलस्तु ततस्तस्य शरांश्चिक्षेप वीर्यवान्। तानापतत एवाशु चिच्छेद परमासिना॥
en: Thereupon the son of Subala, who was possessed of immense prowess, shot innumerable arrows at him (his antagonist), who, again, immediately severed them by means of his sword, that were directed against him.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज सौबलः परवीरहा। प्राहिणेत् सुतसोमाय शरानिशीविषोपमान्॥
en: Thereupon, O mighty monarch, the son of Subala, who became very angry at this once more shot numerous arrows at Sutasoma, that resembled snakes of virulent poison.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: चिच्छेद तांस्तु खड्ड्रेन शिक्षया च बलेन च। दर्शयँल्लाघवं युद्धे तार्क्ष्यतुल्यपराक्रमः॥
en: That warrior (Sutasoma), who resembled Garuda in strength, after having exhibited the lightness of his arms in the battle, severed those arrows by his sword with the assistance of both his learning and strength.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तस्य संचरतो राजन् मण्डलावर्तने तदा। क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन खङ्गं चिच्छेद सुप्रभम्॥
en: O monarch, he (Shakuni) severed the sword, that was most excellent, of his foe, who then was careering in circles in the field, by means of his sharp razor-headed arrows.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: स च्छिन्नः सहसा भूमौ निपपात महानसिः। अर्धपस्य स्थितं हस्ते सुत्सरोस्तत्र भारत॥
en: That strong sword, being thus cut-off, dropped down upon the ground all on a sudden. But, O descendant of the Bharata race, the other half of the sword still rested in the hand of that Sutasoma.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: छिन्नमाज्ञाय निस्त्रिंशमवप्लुत्य पदानि षट्। प्राविध्यत ततः शेषं सुतसोमो महारथः॥
en: Knowing that his sword was thus severed, then that powerful car-warrior, Sutasoma, after having retreated six steps back, struck his antagonist with that half (he still held in his hand).

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तच्छित्त्वा सगुणं चापं रणे तस्य महात्मनः। पपात धरणी तूर्णे स्वर्णवज्रविभूषितम्॥
en: That half (of the sword), after having severed the bow, that was ornamented with gold and gems, along with the string, of that high souled one (Shakuni), immediately dropped down upon the ground.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: सुतसोमस्ततोऽगच्छुतकीर्तेर्महारथम् । सौबलोऽपि धनुर्गृह्य घोरमन्यत् सुदुर्जयम्॥ अभ्ययात् पाण्डवानीकं निघ्नशत्रुगणान् बहून्।
en: Thereupon Sutasoma proceeded to that strong car of Shrutakirti. The son of Subala, too after having grasped another bow, that was most dreadful and invincible, rushed against the army of the Pandavas, slaughtering innumerable enemies on the way.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तत्र नादो महानासीत् पाण्डवानां विशाम्पते॥ सौबलं समरे दृष्ट्वा विचरन्तमभीतवत्।
en: On the very sight of the son of Subala, who was wandering about of in the field of battle most fearlessly, there had taken place, O ruler of earth, great roar amongst the Pandava host.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: तान्यनीकानि दृप्तानि शस्त्रवन्ति महान्ति च॥ द्राव्यमाणान्यदृश्यन्त सौबलेन महात्मना।
en: Then it was seen that those divisions of the army, that were very proud, furnished with the weapons and very vast, were routed by that high-souled son of Subala.

description: The encounter between Shutasome and the son of Subala
sn: यथा दैत्यचमं राजन देवराजो ममर्द ह। तथैव पाण्डवीं सेनां सौबलेया व्यनाशयत्॥
en: O king, the son of Subala continued to slaughter the soldiers of the Pandavas force; even as the king, of the celestials crushed the army of the Daityas.

sn: संजय उवाच धृष्टधुम्नं कृपो राजन् वारयामास संयुगे। यथा दृष्ट्वा वने सिंह शरभो वारयेद युधि॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, Kripa restrained proud Dhristadyumna in the field of battle; even as a Sharva resists a proud lion in the forest, while fighting.

sn: निरुद्धः पार्षतस्तेन गौतमेन बलीयसा। पदात् पदं विचलितं नाशकत्तत्र भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, the son of Prishata, being thus resisted by the most powerful son of Gautama, was not able to move a step further there (in the battle).

sn: गौतमस्य रथं दृष्ट्वा धृष्टधुम्नरथं प्रति। वित्रेसुः सर्वभूतानि क्षयं प्राप्तं च मेनिरे॥
en: Witnessing the car of Gautama staying by the side of that of Dhrishtadyumna, all the creatures were greatly terrified and considered that destruction was to be attained by him (Dhristadyumna).

sn: तत्रावोचन विमनसो रथिन: सादिनस्तथा। द्रोणस्य निधनान्नूनं संक्रुद्धो द्विपदां वरः॥ शारद्वतो महातेजा दिव्यास्त्रविदुदारधीः। अपि स्वस्ति धृष्टधुम्नस्य गौतमात्॥
en: There all the car-warriors and horsemen, who become very inattentive (or gloomy), addressed thus-"This best of persons, the son of Sharadvata, who was possessed of immense prowess and who also was acquainted with the use of celestial weapons and who was, again very high-minded, is sorely filled with anger at the fall of Drona. Will there be escape of Dhrishtadyumna from the hands of Gautama?

sn: अपीयं वाहिनी कृत्स्त्रा मुच्येत महतो भयात्। अप्ययं ब्राह्मणः सर्वान्न नो हन्यात् समागतान्॥
en: Will this entire army be freed from that extreme fear? Will not this twice-born person slay us all, who have assembled here?

sn: यादृशं दृश्यते रूपन्तकप्रतिमं भृशम्। गमिष्यत्यद्य पदवी भारद्वाजस्य गौतमः॥
en: Gautama, who exactly appears even like the most dreadful Destroyer himself, will he not obtain today the appellation of the son of Bharadvaja?

sn: आचार्यः क्षिप्रहस्तश्च विजयी च. सदा युधि। अस्त्रवान् वीर्यसम्पन्नः क्रोधेन च समन्वितः॥
en: The preceptor (Gautama), who is lighthanded (in the use of weapons) and who is always victorious in battle and who is furnished with various kinds of weapons and who is possessed of immense prowess, is now filled with rage.

sn: पार्षतश्च महायुद्धे विमुखोऽद्याभिलक्ष्यते। इत्येवं विविधा वाचस्तावकानां परैः सह॥ व्यश्रूयन्त महराज तयोस्तत्र समागमे।
en: The son of Prishata, too, appears today to have withdrawn from the great battle.' O great king, this and several other speeches were heard to have delivered by the man on your side, as well as by the antagonists; while those two (warriors) assembled there to fight against each other.

sn: विनिःश्वस्य ततः क्रोधात् कृपः शारद्वतो नृप॥ पार्षतं चार्दयामास निश्चेष्टं सर्वमर्मसु।
en: Thereupon, O monarch, Kripa, the son of Sharadvata, sighing heavily with rage, struck the son of Prishata, who had lost all his efforts, in all his vital parts.

sn: स हन्यमानः समरे गौतमेन महात्मना॥ कर्तव्यं न स्म जानाति मोहेन महताऽऽवृतः।
en: Having been thus struck in the battle by the high-souled Gautama, he (Dhristadyumna) could not make out what should he do, encompassed as he was by great insensibility.

sn: तमब्रवीत्ततो यन्ता कचित् क्षेमं तु पार्षत॥ ईद्दशं व्यसनं युद्धे न ते दृष्टं मया क्वचित्।
en: Thereupon his charioteer uttered these words to him-'O son of Prishata, it is well with you, perhaps. Such a great calamity was never witnessed by me in the battle, overtaking you?

sn: दैवयोगात्तु ते बाणा नापतन् मर्मभेदिनः॥ प्रेषिता द्विजमुख्येन मर्माण्युद्दिश्य सर्वतः!
en: Those shafts, that were capable of piercing through the very vital part and that were shot by the foremost of the twice-born persons, aiming at all the vital parts, had not struck you through the favour of the celestials.

sn: व्यावर्तये रथं तूर्णं नदीवेगमिवार्णवात्॥ अवध्यं ब्राह्मणं मन्ये येन ते विक्रमो हतः।
en: I will have the car immediately turned back like the current of a river from the great ocean. I consider that the twice-born person is incapable of being slain, by whom you prowess was done away with.

sn: धृष्टधुम्नस्ततो राजशनकैरब्रवीद् वचः॥ मुह्यते मे मनस्तात गात्रस्वेदश्च जायते। वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च सारथे॥
en: Thereupon, O monarch, Dhristadyumna slowly said these words-'O sire, my mind is being stupefied; and there is perspiration in my limbs. I feel a sensation of trembling in my body; and also the hairs and standing erect upon it.

sn: वर्जयन् ब्राह्मणं युद्धे शनैर्याहि यतोऽर्जुनः। अर्जुनं भीमसेनं वा समरे प्राप्य सारथे॥ क्षेममद्य भवेदेवमेषा मे नैष्ठिकी मतिः।
en: After abandoning the twice-born person in the battle, possessed slowly where Arjuna stays. After having come to the presence of either Arjuna or Bhima in the field, O charioteer, I will surely attain prosperity today. This is my certain belief.

sn: ततः प्रायान्महाराज सारथिस्त्वरयन् हयान्॥ यतो भीम महेष्वासो युयुधे तव सैनिकैः।
en: Thereupon, O powerful king, the charioteer, after having driven the horses, advanced to the place, where that powerful bowman, Bhimasena, was battling with your soldiers.

sn: प्रद्रुतं च रथ दृष्ट्वा धृष्टधुम्नस्य मारिष॥ किरशतशतान्येव गौतमोऽनुययौ तदा।
en: O sire, Gautama, after witnessing that the car of Dhrishtadyumna was with-drawing from the field, then followed it, shooting hundreds of arrows at it.

sn: शङ्ख च पूरयामास मुहुर्मुहुररिंदमः॥ पार्षतं त्रासयामास महेन्द्रो नमुचिं यथा।
en: That chastiser of foes blew his conch over and over again, and then he routed the son of Prishata, even as Indra routed Namuchi (a Danava, in the battle of old).

sn: शिखण्डिनं तु समरे भीष्ममृत्यु दुरासदम्॥ हार्दिक्यो वारयामास स्मयन्निव मुहुर्मुहुः।
en: The son of Hridika, smiling over and over again, resisted Shikhandin, who was the cause of death of Bhishma and most invincible in the field of battle.

sn: शिखण्डी तु समासाद्य हृदिकानां महारथम्॥ पञ्चभिर्निशितैर्भल्लै त्रुदेशे समाहनत्।
en: Shikhandin, however, coming against the mightiest car-warrior of the Hridika race struck him with five sharp and broad-headed arrows at the shoulder-joint.

sn: पा कृतवर्मा तु संक्रुद्धो भित्वा षष्ट्या पतित्रिभिः॥ धनुरेकेन चिच्छेद हसन् राजन् महारथः।
en: O king, the mighty car-warrior, Kritavarman, indeed, being highly enraged, penetrated through his antagonist with sixty winged arrows and then, smiling for a time, severed his bow with one individual shaft.

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय द्रुपदस्यात्मजो बली॥ तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति संक्रुद्धो हार्दिक्यं प्रत्यभाषत।
en: Taking up another bow, the most powerful son of Drupada, being greatly enraged, replied to the son of Hridika saying, Wait, Wait.

sn: ततोऽस्य नवर्ति बाणान् रूक्मपुङ्खान् सुतेजनान्॥२५ प्रेषयापास राजेन्द्र तेऽस्याभ्रशयन्त वर्मणः।
en: O lord of kings, then he (Shikhandin) shot at his antagonist ninety arrows, that were furnished with the wings of gold and possessed of great force. But these arrows were shot back from his (Kritavarman's) armour.

sn: वितथांस्तान् समालक्ष्य पतितांश्च महीतले॥ क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन कार्मुकं चिच्छिदे भृशम्।
en: Beholding those arrows thus sent back and scattered over the ground, he (Shikhandin) severed his dreadful bow with a sharp, razorhanded shaft.

sn: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं भग्नशृङ्गमिवर्षभम्॥ अशीत्या मार्गणैः क्रुद्धो बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्।
en: Then having been filled with rage, he struck this one (the son of Hridika), who, with his severed bow, resembled a bull with his broken horns, with eighty different arrows both in the chest and arms.

sn: कृतवर्मा तु संक्रुद्धो मार्गणैः क्षतविक्षतः॥ ववाम रुधिरं गात्रैः कुम्भवक्त्रादिवोदकम्।
en: Kritavarman, too, who became very angry and who also was greatly wounded by those arrows, vomited blood from his various limbs, as a water-vessel sends forth water through its mouth.

sn: रुधिरेण परिक्किन्नः कृतवर्मा त्वराजत॥ वर्षेण केदिता राजन् यथा गैरिकपर्वतः।
en: even O king, Kritavarman, being thus smeared with blood, blazed forth like a red-chalk mountain streaked (by the streams of liquefied red-chalk) by a shower.

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय समार्गणगुणं प्रभुः॥ शिखण्डिनं बाणगणैः स्कन्धदेशे व्यताडयत्।
en: Then the lord (Kritavarman), taking up another bow that was furnished with its string and an arrow, afflicted Shikhandin with the foremost of shafts in the shoulder.

sn: स्कन्धदेशस्थितैर्बाणैः शिखण्डी तु व्यराजत॥ शाखाप्रशाखाविपुलः सुमहान् पादपो यथा।
en: Shikhandin, indeed, shone most brightly with these shafts, sticking on his shoulders; even as a large tree looks very pretty with its numerous branches and twigs.

sn: तावन्योन्यं भृशं विदध्वा रुधिरेण समुक्षितौ॥ अन्योन्याभिहतौ रेजतुर्वृषभाविव।
en: Both the warriors, who were smeared with blood, after having penetrated each other deeply, looked like two bulls, that wounded each other with their horns.

sn: अन्योन्यस्य वधे यत्नं कुर्वाणौ तौ महारथौ॥ रथाभ्यां चेरतुस्तत्र मण्डलानि सहस्रशः।
en: Those two most powerful car-warriors, who made efforts in slaying each other, whirled round upon their cars, thereby creating thousands of circle, there (in the battle).

sn: कृतवर्मा महाराज पार्षतं निशितैः शरैः॥ रणे विव्याध सप्तत्या स्वर्णपुङः शिलाशितैः।
en: O great king, Kritavarman pierced the son of Prishata in the battle with seventy sharp arrows, that were furnished with golden wings and also that were whetted on atone.

sn: ततोऽस्य समरे बाणं भोजः प्रहरतां वरः॥ जीवितान्तकरं घोरं व्यसृजत्त्वरयान्वितः।
en: Thereupon the prince of the Bhojas, that foremost of chastisers of foes, shot with great activity at his antagonist a dreadful arrow, that was capable of bringing about the destruction of life, in the field of battle.

sn: स तेनाभिहतो राजन् मूर्छामाशु समाविशत्॥ ध्वजयष्टिं च सहसा शिश्रिये कश्मलावृतः।
en: O monarch, he, being thus wounded by that arrow, fall into the condition of insensibility; and he, being so choked with stupefaction, suddenly supported himself by holding his flag-staff.

sn: अपोवाह रणातूर्णं सारथिनां वरम्॥ हार्दिक्यशरसंतप्तं निःश्वसन्तं पुनः पुनः।
en: Thus his charioteer immediately carried away from the field of battle that foremost of car-warriors, who was highly afflicted by the arrows of the son of Hridika and was sighing repeatedly.

sn: पराजिते ततः शूरे दुपदस्यात्मजे प्रभो। व्यद्रवत् पाण्डवी सेना वध्यमाना समन्ततः॥
en: Thereupon, O lord, when the war-like son of Drupada was defeated, the whole army of the Pandavas, being slain on all sides, retreated from the field of battle.

sn: संजय उवाच श्वेताश्वोऽथ महाराज व्यधमत्तावकं बलम्। यथा वायुः समासाद्य तूलराशिं समन्ततः॥
en: Sanjaya said O great king, Arjuna, riding upon a white horse, slaughtered the force of your side, even as the wind, coming before a heap of cotton, disperses it away.

sn: प्रत्युद्ययुस्त्रिगर्तास्तं शिबयः कौरवैः सह। शाल्वः संशप्तकाश्चैव नारायणबलं च तत्॥
en: The Trigartas, the Shibis along with the Kaurava force, the Shalyas, the army of the Samsaptakas and the force called the Narayana, all proceeded against him (Arjuna).

sn: सत्यसेनश्चन्द्रदेवो मित्रदेवः सुतंजयः। सौश्रुतिश्चित्रसेनश्च मित्रवर्मा च भारत॥
en: Then Satyasena, Chandradeva, Mitradeva, Shrutanjaya, Sausruti, Chitrasena and Mitravarman, descendant of the Bharata race.

sn: ते त्रिगर्तराजः समरे भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः। पुत्रैश्चैव महेष्वासै नाशस्त्रविशारदैः॥
en: And the prince of the Trigatas, who was attended on all sides in the battle by his brothers and sons, that were all very powerful bowmen and that were acquainted with the management of various kinds of weapons.

sn: सृजन्तः शरवातान् किरन्तोऽर्जुनमाहवे। अभ्यवर्तन्त सहसा वार्योधा इव सागरम्॥
en: All these scattered and shot innumerable arrows at Arjuna in the battle, even as the masses of clouds suddenly pour forth showers of rain, that approach towards the vast ocean.

sn: ते त्वर्जुनं समासाद्य योधाः शतसहस्रशः। अगच्छन् विलयं सर्वे तायं दृष्ट्वेव पन्नगाः॥
en: Those hundreds of thousands of warriors all met with destruction at their approaching towards Arjuna, even as the snakes are all destroyed by Garuda.

sn: ते हन्यमानाः समरे नाजहुः पाण्डवं रणे। हन्यमाना महाराज शलभा इव पावकम्॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, those warriors, who were being thus slaughtered in the battle, did not abandon the son of Pandu, even as the insects, being burnt by the blazing fire, do not leave it.

sn: सत्यसेनस्त्रिभिर्बाणैर्विव्याध युधि पाण्डवम्। मित्रदेवस्त्रिषष्ट्या तु चन्द्रदेनस्तु सप्तभिः॥
en: In the battle, Satyasena penetrated the son of Pandu with three arrows; and Mitradeva pierced him with sixty-three; while indeed, Chandradeva pierced him with seven arrows.

sn: मित्रवर्मा त्रिसप्तत्या सौश्रुतिश्चापि सप्तभिः। शत्रुजयस्तु विशत्या सुशर्मा नवभिः शरैः॥
en: Again, Mitravarman (pierced) him (Arjuna) with seventy-three shafts; Sausruti with seven; and Satrunjaya, with twenty; and Shusharma, with nine arrows.

sn: स विद्धो बहुभिः संख्ये प्रतिविव्याध तान् नृपान्। सौश्रुतिं सप्तभिरिद्ध्वा सत्यसेनं त्रिभिः शरै॥
en: He (Arjuna) been thus penetrated, in the battle by numerous heroes, pierced in return those kings-piercing Susruti with seven arrows and Satyasena, with three.

sn: शत्रुजयं च विंशत्या चन्द्रदेवं तथाऽष्टभिः। मित्रदेवं शतेनैव श्रुतसेनं त्रिभिः शरै॥ नवभिर्मित्रवर्माणं सुशर्माणं तथाऽष्टभिः।
en: And Satrunjaya, with twenty arrows and also Chandradeva, with eight and Mitradeva, with one hundred and Srutasena, with three. And again, pierced Mitravarman with nine and also Susharman with eight.

sn: शत्रुजय च राजनं हत्वा तत्र शिलाशितैः॥ सौश्रुतेः सशिरस्त्राणं शिरः कायादपाहरत्। त्वरितश्चन्द्रदेवं च शरैर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्॥
en: Then having slaughtered king Satrunjaya there (in the battle) with arrows, that were sharpened on stone, he (Arjuna) severed the head of Sushruti, that was ornamented with head-gear, from his body. He then with great activity sent Chandradeva to the abode of Death by shooting innumerable arrows at him.

sn: तथेतरान् महाराज यतमानान् महारथान्। पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिर्बाणैरेकैकं प्रत्यवारयत्॥
en: So also, O mighty monarch, he restrained cvery one of the other car-warriors, who were engaged in the contest, by means of five arrows shot at each.

sn: सत्यसेनस्तु संक्रुद्धस्तोमरं व्यसृजन्महत्। समुद्दिश्य रणे कृष्णं सिंहनादं ननाद च॥
en: Then Satyasena, indeed, being greatly enraged, directed his large lance, aiming at Krishna, in the battle; and sent fort a loud roar like that of a lion.

sn: स निर्भिद्य भुजं सव्यं माधवस्य महात्मनः। अयस्मयो हेमदण्डो जगान् धरणीं तदा॥
en: Then that lance, that was made of iron, with a golden rod, after having penetrated through the left arm of that lofty-minded Madhava, went into the earth.

sn: माधवस्य तु विद्धस्य तोमरेण महारणे। प्रतोदः प्रापतद्धस्ताद रश्मयश्च विशाम्पते॥
en: O lord of earth, the whip and reins of Madhava, who was pierced with lance in that dreadful battle, dropped down from his hands.

sn: वासुदेवं विभिन्नाङ्गं दृष्ट्वा पार्थो धनंजयः। क्रोधमाहरयत्तीव्र कृष्णं चेदमुवाच ह॥
en: Seeing Vasudeva thus pierced, Dhananjaya, the son of Pritha, collected all his fierce wrath;

sn: प्रापयाश्वान् महाबाहो सत्यसेनं प्रति प्रभो। यावदेनं शैरस्तीक्ष्णैर्नयामि यमसादनम्॥
en: “O mighty armed lord, drive the steeds towards Satyasena that I may send this one to the abode of Death by means of sharp arrows.

sn: प्रतोदं गृह्य सोऽन्यत्तु रश्मीनपि यथा पुरा। वाहयामास तानश्वान् सत्यसेनरथं प्रति॥
en: Then that highly famous one (Krishna) immediately taken up the whip as well as the reins, led those steeds (i.e. the car) towards the car of Satyasena.

sn: विष्वक्सेनं तु निर्भिन्नं दृष्ट्वा पार्थो धनंजयः। सत्यसेनं शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्वारयित्वा महारथः॥ ततः सुनिशितैर्भल्लै राज्ञस्तस्य महच्छिरः। कुण्डलोपचितं कायाश्चकर्त पृतनान्तरे॥
en: Beholding the lord of the universe thus pierced, that powerful car-warrior Dhananjaya, the son of Pritha, restrained the course of Satyasena by means of keen shafts. Thereupon, he (Dhananjaya) severed the huge head, that ornamented with ear-rings, of that monarch, who stood at the head of the army, from his body by means of whetted broadheaded arrows.

sn: तन्निकृत्य शितैर्बाणैर्मित्रवर्माणमाक्षिपत्। वत्सदन्तेन तीक्ष्णोन सारथिं चास्य मारिष॥
en: O sire, having thus severed his (Satyasena's) head, he then hurled down (slain) Chitravarman with numerous keen arrows, as well as his charioteer with a calf-toothed sharp shafts. was on

sn: ततः शरशतैर्भूयः संशप्तकगणान् बली। पातयामास संक्रुद्धः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Thereupon that powerful one, being filled with wrath, again caused the destruction of hundreds and thousands of the force of the Samsaptakas by means of hundreds of arrows.

sn: ततो रजतपुड्वेन राजशीर्षं महात्मनः। मित्रदेवस्य चिच्छेद क्षुरप्रेण महारथः॥
en: Then, again, O monarch, that powerful carwarrior severed the head of the high-souled Mitrasena with a razor-headed arrow, that was furnished with the wings of silver.

sn: सुशर्माणं सुसंक्रुद्धो जत्रुदेशे समाहनत्। तत: संशप्तकाः सर्वे परिवार्य धनंजयम्॥ शस्त्रौधैर्ममृदुः क्रुद्धा नादयन्तो दिशो दश।
en: Afterwards he, being greatly enraged, struck Susharman his shoulder-joint. Thereupon the entire army of the Samsaptakas, that became very wrathful, having surrounded Dhananjaya on all sides, crushed him with a shower of weapons and thereby caused the ten points of the horizon echo with their roars.

sn: अभ्यर्दितस्तु तैर्जिष्णुः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमः॥ ऐन्द्रमस्त्रममेयात्मा प्रादुश्चक्रे महारथः।
en: Having been thus oppressed by those weapons, that mighty car-warrior, Jishnu, who was possessed of prowess equal to that of Sakra (Indra) himself and who also had a soul immeasurable, took up his weapon, called Aindra.

sn: ततः शरसहस्राणि प्रादुरासन् विशाम्पते॥ ध्वजानां छिद्यमानानां कार्मुकाणां च मारिष। रथानां सपताकानां तूणीराणां युगैः सह।॥ अक्षाणामथ चक्राणां योक्त्राणां रश्मिभिः सह। कूबराणां वरूथाणां पृषत्कानां च संयुगे॥ अश्वानां पततां चापि प्रासनामृष्टिभिः सह। गदानां परिधाना च शक्तितोमरपट्टिशैः॥ शतघ्नींनां सचक्राणां भुजानां चोरुभिः सह। कण्ठसूत्रामदानां च केयूराणां च मारिष॥ हाराणामथ निष्काणां तनुत्राणां च भारत। छत्राणां व्यजनानां च शिरसां मुकुटैः सह॥ अश्रूयत महाशब्दस्तत्र तत्र विशम्पते।
en: Thereupon, O ruler of earth, thousands of arrows continuously issued forth therefore. O sire, of broken standards and bows, of cars along with their banners, of quivers and yokes. Also of axles and wheels, of traces along with the chords, of bottoms of cars, of wooden fences about the cars and innumerable shafts in the field of battle. And of falling horses and of spears along with the swords, of maces and spiked clubs, of Sakti-arrows, lances and axes. And of Shataghnis furnished with wheels, as well as of the arms along with the thighs, of wreaths and Angadas, of Keyuras and of garlands and cuirasses, of of armours, of umbrellas and fans, of heads adorned with coronets, of these a tremendous roar, O ruler of carth, was heard in all the directions of the field of battle.

sn: सकुण्डलानि स्वक्षीणि पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानि च॥ शिरांस्युामद्दश्यन्त ताराजालमिवाम्बरे।
en: Upon the field of battle, the heads (of severed warriors), that were ornamented with ear-rings and furnished with the eyes as resplendent as the full moon, were seen, even as the net-work of stars is seen in the firmament.

sn: सुस्त्रग्वीणि सुवासांसि चन्दनेनोक्षितानि च॥ शरीराणि व्यदृश्यन्त निहतानां महीतले।
en: The bodies of the slaughtered warriors, that were furnished with the most handsome floral wreaths and covered with the excellent garments and also that were pointed with the soft sandal, lay resplendent upon the ground.

sn: गन्धर्वनगराकारं घोरमायोधनं तदा॥ निहतै राजपुत्रेश्च क्षत्रियैश्च महाबलैः। हस्तिभिः पतितैश्चैव तुरङ्गैश्चाभवन्मही॥ अगम्यरूपा समरे विशीर्णैरिव पर्वतैः।
en: Then the dreadful field of battle resembled the clouded firmament filled with various vapoury forins and the earth being scattered over with the slaughtered princes and the Kshatriyas, possessed of great strength, as well as with the fallen elephants and horses, became as impassable in the battle as the ground strewn over with numerous hills.

sn: नासीचक्रपथस्तत्र पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः॥ निघ्नतः शात्रवान् भल्लैर्हरत्यश्वं चास्यतो महत्।
en: There was no way in the field of battle, that car-wheels of that high-souled son of Pandu could proceed, whilst he was slaughtering his antagonists and greatly smiting the elephants and horses by means of his broad-headed arrows.
