sn: स्वानुगा इव सीदन्ति रथचक्राणि मारिष॥ चरतस्तस्य संग्रामे तस्मॅिल्लोहितकर्दमे।
en: O sire, the car-wheels of that one, who was carcering in the battle, stopped, as if with terror, while they were moving in that bloody mire.

sn: सीदमानानि चक्राणि समूहुस्तुरगा भृशम्॥ श्रमेण महता युक्ता मनोमारुतरंहसः।
en: His horses, however, that were possessed of the speed of either the mind of or the wind, had with great labour drawn these wheels, that were lagging behind.

sn: वध्यमानं तु तत्सैन्यं पाण्डुपुत्रेण धन्विना॥ प्रायशो विमुखं सर्व नावतिष्ठत भारत।
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, that army, which was thus slain by the son of Pandu, that great bowman, almost wholly ran away (from the field of battle); and in fact, none remained (to fight with the foe).

sn: ताजित्वा समरे जिष्णुः संशप्तकगणान् बहून्॥ विरराज तदा पार्थो विधूमोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन्। ४३॥
en: Then Jishnu, the son of Pritha, having defeated that immense force of Samsaptakas in the field of battle, blazed forth like the burning fire without any smoke. the

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: संजय उवाच युधिष्ठिरं महाराज विसृजन्तं शरान् बहून्। स्वयं दुर्योधनो राजा प्रत्यगृह्णदभीतवत्॥
en: Sanjaya said O great monarch, the king Duryodhana himself received, without any fear, was Yudhishthira, who then shooting innumerable shafts (at his antagonists).

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: तमापतन्तं सहसां तव पुत्रं महारथम्। धर्मराजो द्रुतं विद्ध्वा तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Then Yudhishthira, the righteous, after having quickly penetrated your son, that mighty car-warrior, who was all on a sudden proceeding against him, addressed him, saying-wait, wait.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: स तु तं प्रतिविव्याध नवभिर्निशितैः शरैः। सारथिं चास्य भल्लेन भृशं क्रुद्धोऽभ्यताडयत्॥
en: Then he (Duryodhana), indeed, who became highly enraged, penetrated him (Yudhishthira) in return with nine whetted arrows and again, afflicted his charioteer most dreadfully by means of his broad-headed shafts.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजन् स्वर्णपुखञ्छिलीमुखान्। दुर्योधन चिक्षेप त्रयोदश शिलाशितान्॥
en: Thereupon king Yudhishthira shot at Duryodhana thirteen keen arrows, that were furnished with the wings made of gold, sharpened on a stone.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: चतुर्भिश्चतुरो वाहंस्तस्य हत्वा महारथः। पञ्चमेन शिरः कायात् सारथेश्च समाक्षियत्॥
en: Then that powerful car-warrior, having slaughtered his (Duryodhana's) four horses with four arrows, with the fifth severed the head of his charioteer from his body.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: षष्ठेन तु ध्वज राज्ञः सप्तमेन त कार्मुकम्। अष्टभेन तथा खङ्गं पातयामास भूतले॥
en: Thereafter he smote down the king's standard with the sixth arrows, his bow with the seventh and his sword with the eighth, upon the ground.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: पञ्चभिर्नृपतिं चापि धर्मराजोऽर्दयद् भृशम्। हताश्वात्तु रथात्तस्मादवप्लुत्य सुतस्तव॥ उत्तमं व्यसन प्राप्तो भूमावेवावतिष्ठत।
en: The most righteous king crushed most severely the Kuru monarch with five other arrows. At this, your son, descending from his car, that had its horses all slain, became subject to the greatest danger and stayed upon the field.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: तं तु कृच्छ्रगतं दृष्ट्वा कर्णद्रौणिकृपादयः॥ अभ्यवर्तन्त सहसा परीप्सन्तो नराधिपम्।
en: After beholding him thus fallen into imminent danger, Karna, the son of Drona, Kripa and other heroes all on a sudden proceeded towards him with the desire of saving that ruler of men.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: अथ पाण्डुसुताः सर्वे परिवार्य युधिष्ठिरम्॥ अन्वयुः समरे राजंस्ततो युद्धमवर्तत।
en: Thereupon, O monarch, all other sons of Pandu, collected round Yudhishthira and rushed forth at that battle, whereupon a great encounter took place.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: ततस्तूर्यसहस्राणि प्रावाद्यन्त महामृधे॥ ततः किलाकिलाशब्दः प्रादुरासन् महीपते।
en: Thereupon in that dreadful battle thousands of trumpets were beaten; and after this, O mighty lord earth, a mixed noise, consisting of numerous voices, arose there (in the battle).

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: यत्राभ्यगतच्छन् समरे पञ्चालाः कौरवैः सहा। ११॥ नरा नरैः समजाग्मुर्वारणा वरवारणैः। रथाश्च रथिभिः सार्धं हयाश्च हयसादिभिः॥
en: In that part of the battle, where the Panchalas encountered the Kaurava divisions, the inen came against the foremost of elephants. The car-warriors encountered the car-warriors and horsemen with horsemen.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: द्वन्द्वान्यासन् महाराज प्रेक्षणीयानि संयुगे। विविधान्यप्यचिन्त्यानि शस्त्रवन्त्युत्तमानि त॥
en: Thus, O great monarch, several kinds of unthought encounters took place between heroes armed with the best of weapons, which were most beautiful to look at upon the field.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: ते शराः समरे सर्वे चित्रं लघु च सुष्टु च। अयुध्यन्त महावेगाः परस्परवधैषिणः॥
en: Those heroic warriors, who were possessed of great force and who also were willing to kill one another, continued to battle most excellently and with great lightness of hands and skill.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: अन्योन्यं समरे जघ्नुर्योधव्रतमनुष्ठिताः। न हि ते समरं चक्रः पृष्ठतो वै कथञ्चन॥
en: Indeed, those heroes, strictly observed the vow of warriors and slaughtered each other in the battle; but they not at all fought from each other's back.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: मुहूर्तमेव तद् युद्धमासीन्मधुरदर्शनम्। तत उन्मत्तवद राजन् निर्मर्यादमवर्तत॥
en: But that battle looked only for a while most excellent. Thereupon, monarch, the encounter look a very mad turn, in which all became regardless of one another.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: रथी नागं समासाद्य दारयन् निशितैः शरैः। प्रेषयामास कालाय शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Then the car-warrior, rushing against the elephant, pierced him with sharp arrows and led him towards the abode of Death by means of his straight shafts.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: नागा हयान् समासाद्य विक्षिपन्तो बहून् रणे। दारयामासुरत्युग्रं तत्र तत्र तदा तदा॥
en: Thereafter the elephants coming before the horses, hurled a large number of them in the battle and deeply pierced them in the different directions of the field.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: हयारोहाश्च बहवः परिवार्य हयोत्तमान्। तलशब्दरवांश्चक्रुः सम्पतन्तस्ततस्ततः॥ धावमानांस्ततस्तांस्तु द्रवमाणान् महागजान्। पार्श्वतः पृष्ठतश्चैव निजघ्नुर्हयसादिनः॥
en: Then numerous horsemen, after having encompassed the best of horses created a very sweet noise with their palms and then fell down upon them. The horsemen, again, slaughtered those horses, that were running away from the field, as well as the mighty elephants, that also were roving in the battle, both from behind them and from the sides.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: विद्राव्य च बहूनश्वान् नागा राजन् मदोत्कटाः। विषाणैश्चापरे जघ्नुर्ममृदुश्चापरे भृशम्॥
en: O monarch, the most furious elephants, after having crushed large numbers of horses to run away from the field, slaughtered some of them with their tusks and crushed down others most severely.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: साश्वारोहांश्च तुरगान् विषाणैविव्यधू रुषा। अपरे चिक्षिपुर्वेगात् प्रगृह्यातिबलास्तदा॥
en: Thereupon some of the elephants pierced numerous horses along with their riders with great wrath; while others, again, that were possessed of extraordinary strength, seized them and dragged them down upon the ground with great force.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: पादतैराहता नागा विवरेषु समन्ततः। चक्रुरार्तस्वरं घोरं दुदुवुश्च दिशो दश॥
en: The elephants, struck from all sides in the different vital parts by the foot-soldiers, uttered very dreadful cries of pain and ran away towards the ten points of the compass.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: पदातीनां तु सहसा प्रदुतानां महाहवे। उत्सृज्याभरणं तूर्णमवप्लुत्य रणाजिरे॥ निमित्तं मन्यमानास्तु परिणाम्य महागजाः। जगृहुर्बिभिदुश्चैर चित्राण्याभरणानि॥
en: Many of the foot-soldiers, who were all on sudden running away in that dreadful battle, leaving behind their ornaments, immediately hemmed in upon the field. Then, indeed, the most powerful elephant-warriors, having considered the indications of victory, caused their elephants to take up those handsome ornaments and penetrate the fallen warriors with their tusks.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: तांस्तु तत्र प्रसक्तान् वै परिवार्य पदातयः। हस्तोरोहान् निजघ्नुस्ते महावेगा बलोत्कटाः॥
en: Then also the foot-soldiers, that were possessed of immense force and endued with extraordinary strength, after having encircled those riders of elephants, who wee engaged in the massacre there (in the battle), slaughtered them.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: अपरे हस्तिभिहैस्तैः खं विक्षिप्ता महाहवे। निपतन्तो विषाणौ शं विद्धाः सुशिक्षितैः॥
en: In that dreadful battle, others were hurled up into the atmosphere by the elephants with their trunks; and while falling down they were were deeply pierced by those well-trained beasts with the points of their tusks.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: अपरे सहसा गृह्य विषाणैरेव सूदिताः। सेनान्तरं समासाद्य केचित् तत्र महागजैः॥ क्षुण्णगात्रा महाराज विक्षिप्य च पुनः पुनः। अपरे व्यजनानीव विभ्राम्य निहता मृधे॥
en: Other foot-soldiers were deprived of their lives with the tusks of the elephants, that had suddenly seized them and some, again, O great monarch, who had been thrown into the midst of other soldiers, were cut-off into pieces by those huge elephants, after they had rolled them over and over again upon the ground. And others also, that were tossed in the air like the fans, were slaughtered in the battle.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: पुरःसराश्च नागानामपरेषां विशाम्पते। शरीराण्यतिविद्धानि तत्र तत्र रणाजिरे॥
en: O ruler of earth, those (of the foot-soldiers), who stood in front of other elephants, had their bodies deeply penetrated (by the elephants) on all sides of the field of battle.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: प्रतिमानेषु कुम्भेषु दन्तवेष्टेषु चापरे। निगृहीतां भृशं नागाः प्रासतोमरशक्तिभिः॥
en: Many other elephants were very severely struck in their cheeks, the frontal globs and the parts between their tusks with spears, lances and shafts, called Shakti.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: निगृह्य च गजाः केचित् पार्श्वस्थैर्भृशदारुणैः। रथाश्वसादिभिस्तत्र सम्भिन्ना न्यपतन् भुवि॥
en: Moreover some other elephants, that were fearfully wounded by the most formidable warriors, posted on their sides, as well as by the car-warriors and horse-men, being cut-off by them, fell down upon the ground.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: सहयाः सादिनस्तत्र तोमरेण महामृधे। भूमावमृद्गन वेगेन सचर्माणं पदातिनम्॥
en: There in that dreadful battle, nur.erous horsemen had all on a sudden struck down with great violence upon the field the foot-soldiers, that had their arrows on, by means of their lances.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: तथा सावरणान् कांश्चित्तत्र तत्र विशाम्पते। रथान् नागाः समासाद्य परिगृह्य च मारिष॥ व्याक्षिपन् सहसा तत्र घोररूपे भयानके। नाराचैर्निहताश्चापि गजाः पेतुर्महाबलाः॥ पर्वतस्येव शिखरं वज्ररुग्णं महीतले।
en: So also, O ruler of earth, O sire, the mighty elephants, having advanced before some of the car-warriors, that had their armours on and also having seized them well dragged them down most suddenly on all sides of that dreadful field of battle, that presented a very awful aspect. Many mightiest clephants, that were slaughtered with the shafts, fell down upon the ground even as the summits of a mountain drop down upon the surface of the earth, when broken down by thunder.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: योधा योधान् समासाद्य मुष्टिभिर्व्यहनन् युधि॥ केशेष्वन्योन्यमाक्षिप्य चिक्षिपुर्बिभिदुश्च ह।
en: In that battle, the warriors, battling with their combatants, struck them with their fists; and having dragged cach other with their hairs, hurled down and cut-off each other.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: उद्यम्य त भुजानन्ये निक्षिप्य च महीतले॥ पदा चोरः समाक्रम्य स्फुरतोऽपाहरच्छिरः।
en: Some other combatants, having stretched their arms, hurled down their antagonists upon the ground, placed their feet upon their breasts and with great pleasure severed their heads.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: पततश्चापरो राजन् विजहारासिना शिरः॥ जीवतश्च तथैवान्यः शस्त्रं काये न्यमज्जयत्।
en: Some one of the combatants, O great king, smote down with his feet the dead antagonist; while some other, O monarch, severed the head of a falling enemy by means of his scimitar; and while some other combatant, again, directed his weapon at the body of another, who was still living.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: मुष्टियुद्धं महचासीद् योधानां तत्र भारत॥ तथा केशग्रहश्चोगो बाहुयुद्धं च भैरवम्।
en: Thus, O descendant of the Bharata race, the inost dreadful encounters between heroes took place there, some striking one another with their fists, and some also fiercely seizing one another with their hairs; and some, again, wrestling with another with their arms most fearfully.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: समासक्तस्य चान्येन अविज्ञातस्तथाऽपरः॥ जहार समरे प्राणान् नानाशस्त्रैर नेकधा।
en: Under various circumstances, some one of the combatants deprived the lives of many in the battle, who were engaged with others and were quite unconscious of the slaughter by means of several sorts of weapons.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: संसक्तेषु च योधेषु वर्तमारे च संकुले॥ कबन्धान्युत्थितानि स्युःशतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
en: In that general encounter, while the warriors were engaged in the battle and continued to be mangled, hundreds and thousands of headless bodies of the fallen warriors) stood upon the field.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: शोणितैः सिच्यमानानि शस्त्राणि कवचानि च।॥ महारागनुरक्तानि वस्त्राणीव चकाशिरे।
en: Diverse kinds of weapons and armours, that were drenched in blood, blazed forth like pieces of cloth, that are dyed with deep red.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: एवमेतन्मद् युद्धं दारुणे शस्त्रसंकुलम्॥ उन्मत्तगङ्गाप्रतिमं शब्देनापूरयजगत्।
en: Thus this most dreadful and extraordinary battle, that was characterised by a confused din of diverse kinds of weapons, filled the entire universe with a noise even as the furious Ganges fills the earth with the roar of her currents.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: नैव स्वे न परे राजन् विज्ञायन्ते शरातुराः॥ योद्धव्यमिति युध्यन्ते रानानो जयगृद्धिनः।
en: O monarch, the combatants, being highly oppressed the shafts, could not make out their friends from the antagonists and the assembled princes, who were all very desirous of victory, continued to battle, considering (the fact), that they should fight.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: स्वान् स्वे जनुर्महाराज परांश्चैव समागतान्॥ उभयोः सेनयोर्वीरैर्व्याकुलं समपद्यत।
en: O great monarch, the warriors began to slaughter both the friends and foes, who had assembled in that dreadful battle; and the warriors, belonging to both the forces, were rendered restless by the heroes, who engaged them.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: रथैर्भग्नैर्महाराज वारणैश्च निपातितैः॥ हयैश्च पतितस्तत्र नरैश्च विनिपातितः। अगम्यरूपा पृथिवी क्षणेन समपद्यत॥
en: Within a very short time, the earth, that was covered with a mire consisting of flesh and blood and also by which the currents of blood flowed continuously, became, O lord of earth, impassable with the shattered cars and with the fallen elephants and the horses lying there about and also with men slaughtered (in the battle), O great monarch.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: क्षणेनासीन्महीपाल क्षतजौघप्रवर्तिनी। पञ्चालानहनत् कर्णस्त्रिगर्ताश्च धनंजयः॥
en: So Karna slaughtered the Panchala warriors and Dhananjaya slew the Kuru troops along with all their elephant forces.

description: The general encounter of several heroes
sn: भीमसेनः कुरून् राजन् हस्त्यनीकं च सर्वशः। एवमेष क्षयो वृत्तः कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः। अपराह्ने गते सूर्ये कासतां विपुलं यश॥
en: Thus the great destruction had taken place of all the forces of both the Kuru and Pandavas. Both the parties were most desirous of gaining fame, when the sun had passed the other side of meridian.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अतितीव्राणि दुःखानि दुःसहानि बहूनि च। त्वतोऽहं संजयश्रौषं पुत्राणां चैव संत्रयम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, I have heard from you of great and intolerable grief's of fierce character as well as of the destruction of my sons.

sn: यथा त्वां मे कथयसे तथा युद्धमवर्तत। न सन्ति सूत कौरव्या इति मे निश्चिता मतिः॥
en: O Suta (charioteer), from what you describe to me and also from how the battle was fought, my certain conclusion is that the Kauravas are not alive.

sn: दुर्योधनश्च विरथः कृतस्तत्र महारथः। धर्मपुत्रः कथं चक्रे तस्य वा नृपतिः कथम्॥
en: In that fair battle, Duryodhana was deprived of his car. How did the son of Dharma fight; and how also did that prince (Duryodhana)?

sn: अपराह्ने कथं युद्धमभवल्लोमहर्षणम्। तन्ममाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन कुशलो ह्यसि संजय॥
en: How did take place the battle, that made the hairs to stand on points, in the afternoon? O Sanjaya, relate to me all these in detail; for you are an expert in this

sn: संजय उवाच संसक्तेषु तु सैन्येषु वध्यमानेषु भागशः। रथमन्यं समास्थाय पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते॥ क्रोधेन महता युक्तः सविषो भुजगो यथा।
en: Sanjaya said While the soldiers on both sides were thus engaged in fighting in their respective divisions your son, king Duryodhana, O lord of earth, ascending upon another car and being filled with great wrath, like a snake possessing virulent poison, addressed his charioteer, saying-

sn: दुर्योधनः समालक्ष्य धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥ प्रोवाच सूतं त्वरितो याहि याहीति भारत। तत्र मां प्रापय क्षिप्रं सारथे यत्र पाण्डव॥ ध्रियमाणातपत्रेण राजा राजति दंशितः।
en: Do you proceed, do you proceed, quickly. After he, O descendant of the Bharata race, had beheld Yudhishthira, the king of righteousness, he said-"O charioteer, most speedily do you lead me to that place, where the royal son of Pandu, having been clad in armour, looks most resplendent with the umbrella held over his head."

sn: स सूतश्चोदितो राज्ञा राज्ञः स्यन्दनमुत्तमम्॥ युधिष्ठिरस्याभिमुखं प्रेषयामास संयुगे।
en: Then the charioteer, being thus urged by the king, led the foremost of cars belonging to the king to the presence of king Yudhishthira in the battle. were an

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरः क्रुद्धः प्रभिन्न इव कुञ्जरः॥ सारथिं चोदयामास याहि यत्र सुयोधनः।
en: Thereupon Yudhishthira, being filled with wrath and resembling an infuriate elephant, urged his charioteer, asking him to proceed to the place, where Suyodhana took his stand.

sn: तौ समाजग्मतुर्वीरो भ्रातरौ रथसत्तमौ॥ समेत्य च महावीरौ संरब्धौ युद्धदुर्मदौ। ववर्षतुर्महेष्वासौ शरैरन्योन्यमाहवे॥
en: Those two heroic warriors, who were brothers to each other and who were the best of car-warriors and who were possessed of immense prowess and who also invincible in battle, coming in contact with each other, engaged themselves in encounter. Moreover these two mighty bowmen began to strike each other with numerous shafts in that battle.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा धर्मशीलस्य मारिष। शिलाशितेन भल्लेन धनुश्चिच्छेद संयुगे॥
en: Thereupon, O sire, the king Duryodhana severed the bow of that righteous one (Yudhishthira) by means of a broad-headed arrows, sharpened on a stone, in the battle.

sn: तं नामृष्यत संक्रुद्धो ह्यवमानं युधिष्ठिरः। अपविध्य धनुश्छिन्नं क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः॥ अन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय धर्मपुत्रश्चमूमुखे। दुर्योधनस्य चिच्छेद ध्वजं कार्मुकमेव च॥
en: Yudhishthira, who became highly enraged, did not indeed, car that insult. Then the son of Dharma, whose eyes became red with wrath, throwing aside his severed bow and grasping another bow, stood at the head of his army and cut-off the standard and bow of Duryodhana.

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय प्राविध्यत युधिष्ठिरम्। तावन्योन्यं सुसंक्रुद्धौ शस्त्रवर्षाण्यमुञ्चताम्॥
en: Then, having taken up another bow, he (Duryodhana) pierced the son of Pandu in return. Those two heroic warriors, poured forth showers of arrows upon each other.

sn: सिंहाविव सुसंरब्धौ परस्परजिगीषया। जघ्नतुस्तौ रणेऽन्योन्यं नर्दमानौ वृषाविव॥
en: Who like two lions filled with great rage, were highly enraged and who also were most desirous of defeating each other in the battle, those two most powerful car-warriors smote down each other like two roaring bulls.

sn: अन्तरं मार्गमाणौ च चेरतुस्तौ महारथौ। ततः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैः शरैस्तौ तु कृतव्रणौ॥ विरेजतुर्महाराज किंशुकाविव पुष्पितौ।
en: In the battle, and also they wandered over the field, expecting to catch each other on their weak points. Thereupon the two heroes, who were wounded by the arrows shot from bows stretched to their fullest length, looked most handsome, O great monarch, resembling two flowering Kinshukas.

sn: ततो राजन् विमुञ्चन्तौ सिंहनादान् मुहुर्मुहुः॥ तलयोश्च तथा शब्दान् धनुषश्च महाहवे। शङ्खशब्दवरांश्चैव चक्रतुस्तौ नरेश्वरो॥
en: Then, O monarch, those two rulers of men uttered roars of a lion in order to terrify each other; as also they made sounds with their palms and with their bows; and again, sent forth the loudest sound with their conches in that dreadful battle.

sn: अन्योयं तौ महाराज पीडयांचाक्रतुर्भृशम्। ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा पुत्रं तव शरैस्त्रिभिः॥ आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो वज्रवेगैर्दुरासदैः।
en: O great king, those two oppressed each other very greatly. Thereupon king Yudhishthira, who became very angry, struck your son on the chest with arrows, that were very irresistible, having had the impetuosity of thunder.

sn: प्रतिविव्याध तं तूर्णं तव पुत्रो महीपतिः॥ पञ्चभिर्निशितैबाणैः स्वर्णपुकैः शिलाशित।
en: Your son, that ruler of earth, most quickly pierced him (Yudhishthira) in return with five keen arrows, that were equipt with the wings of gold and sharpened on a stone.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा शक्तिं चिक्षेप भारत॥ सर्वपारसवीं तीक्ष्णां महोल्काप्रतिमां तदा।
en: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, the king Duryodhana shot an arrows, called Sakti, that was capable of slaughtering all creatures and was sharp-edged and also that looked like a large, resplendent brand.

sn: तामापतन्ती सहसा धर्मराजः शितैः शरैः॥ त्रिभिश्चिच्छेद सहसा तं च विव्याध पञ्चभिः।
en: Then the king of righteousness (Yudhishthira) severed into three fragments that arrows, which coursed towards him suddenly by means of numerous sharp shafts; and again, he, all on a sudden, pierced the prince himself (Duryodhana) with five others.

sn: निपपात ततः साऽथ स्वर्णदण्डा महास्वना॥ निपतन्ती महोल्केव व्यराजच्छिखिसंनिभा।
en: Thereupon that arrow, which was furnished with a golden staff and that was capable of producing a lould whizz, dropped down (upon the ground); and its falling, like a great brand attended with the blazing flames, looked most resplendent.

sn: शक्तिं विनिहतां दृष्ट्वा पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते॥ नवभिर्निशितैर्भल्लैर्निजघान युधिष्ठिरम्।
en: O ruler of earth, your son, beholding that Shakti-arrow thus severed into pieces, struck Yudhishthira with nine whetted and sharppointed arrows.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता शत्रुणा शत्रुतापनः॥ दुर्योधन समुद्दिश्य बाणं जग्राह सत्वरः। समाधत्त च तं बाणं धनुर्मध्ये महाबलः॥
en: That scorcher of antagonists, being thus deeply penetrated by the most powerful enemy, quickly equipped himself and took up an arrow, aiming at Duryodhana.

sn: चिक्षेप च महाराज ततः क्रुद्धः पराक्रमी। स तु बाणः समासाद्य तव पुत्रं महारथम्॥ व्यामोहयत राजानं धरणीं च ददार ह।
en: O mighty monarch, thereupon that hero, possessed of immense strength and great powers, being greatly wrathful, put that arrow upon his bow-string and directed it (at his antagonist). Indeed, that arrow, approaching towards your son, that powerful car-warrior stupefied that prince and then went down the earth.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः क्रुद्धो गदामुद्यम्य वेगितः॥ विधित्सुः कलहस्यान्तं धर्मराजमुपाद्रवत्।
en: Thereupon Duryodhana, who was filled with wrath, most quickly raising his mace, afflicted the king of righteousness (Yudhishthira) with the desire of piercing him through, in order to put an end to all hostilities (between the Kurus Pandavas).

sn: तमुद्यतगदं दृष्ट्वा दण्डहस्तमिवान्तकम्॥ धर्मराजो महाशक्तिं प्राहिणोत् तव सूनवे। दीप्यमानां महावेगां महोल्का ज्वलितामिव॥
en: Beholding him thus raising his mace like Death himself armed with his rod, the king of righteousness (Yudhishthira) shot that mighty Shakti-arrow at your son, that blazed forth most brilliantly and was endued with great impetuosity and also that resembled a large and resplendent brand

sn: रथस्थः स तया विद्धो वर्म भित्त्वा स्तनान्तरे। भृशं संविग्नहृदयः पपात च मुमोह च॥
en: Then he (the Kuru prince), who stayed on his car, having been pierced on the chest by that arrow, first piercing his vitals and also having been greatly pained a heart, fell down and became senseless.

sn: पीमस्तमाह च ततः प्रतिज्ञामनुचिन्तयन्। नायं वध्यस्तव नृप इत्युक्तः स न्यवर्तत॥
en: Thereupon Bhima, recollecting his own vow, uttered these words 'O prince, (Yudhishthira), this one is not to be slaughtered by you.' Being thus addressed Yudhishthira abstained (from slaying him).

sn: ततस्त्वरितमागम्य कृतवर्मा तवात्मजम्। प्रत्यपद्यत राजानं निमग्नं व्यसनार्णवे॥
en: Thereupon Kritavarman, most quickly approaching towards your son, got near that prince, who was then drowned in the great ocean of calamity.

sn: गदामादाय भीमोऽपि हेमपट्टपरिष्कृताम्। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन कृतवर्माणमाहवे॥
en: Then Bhima, too, grasping his mace, that was equipt with gold and flaxen chords, proceeded with great violence against Kritavarman in that dreadful battle.

sn: एवं तदभवद् युद्धं त्वदीयानां परैः सह। अपराह्णे महाराज काङ्क्षतां विजयं युधि॥
en: O great king, thus took place the battle between the forces on your side and their antagonists, in that afternoon while the parties were most desirous of victory in the battle.

sn: संजय उवाच ततः कर्ण पुरस्कृत्य त्वदीया युद्धदुर्मदाः। पुनरावृत्य संग्रामं चक्रुर्देवासुरोपमम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon the troops on your side who were most invincible in battle, having placed Karna in the front part (of the army) and returning back, engaged in a battle that looked like the war between the celestials and the Asuras.

sn: द्विरदनरथाश्वशङ्खशब्दैः परिहृषिता विविधैश्च शस्त्रपातैः। द्विरदरथपदातिसादिसंघाः परिकुपिताभिमुखाः प्रजजिरे ते॥
en: Then the multitudes of elephant-warriors, the car-warriors, the foot-soldiers and the horsemen, who were roused by the sound of conches, as well as by the roars of elephants, men, cars and horses and filled with great rage, stood on the face of the antagonists and continued to slaughter them.

sn: रिषुभिरनेकविधैश्च सूदिताः। द्विरदरथहया महाहवे वरपुरुषैः पुरुषाश्च वाहनैः॥
en: In that fierce battle, numerous elephants, cars and horses, as well as slaughtered by the foremost of horses with their sharp battle axes, scimitars, axes and men were several sorts of shafts, as also with their conveyances.

sn: कमलदिनकरेन्दुसंनिभैः सितदशडनैः सुमुखाक्षिनासिकैः। रुचिरमुकुटकुण्डलैर्मही पुरुषशिरोभिरुपस्तृता बभौ॥
en: The earth looked most resplendent with the severed heads of persons scattered over her, that resembled either the lotus, or the sun, or the moon in splendour and also that were furnished with the white teeth, excellent faces, eyes and noses and that and ornamented with beautiful ear-rings, upon their ears.

sn: नखरभुशुण्डिगदाशतैर्हताः। द्विरदनरहयाः सहस्रशो रुधिरनदीप्रवहास्तदाभवन्॥
en: Thus thousands of elephants and men and horses were slaughtered by means of hundreds of spiked maces, short bludgeons, arrows, called Shakti and lances, as also by the hooks, Bhushandis and clubs which caused the torrents of a river of blood flow down.

sn: प्रहतरथनराश्वकुञ्जरं प्रतिभयदर्शनमुल्बणव्रणम्।ष तदहितहतमाबभौ बलं पितृपतिराष्ट्रमिव प्रजाक्षये॥
en: Then that entire body of slain car-warriors, men, horses and elephants, that were all slaughtered by the antagonists and thus were most terrific to look at, lying (upon the field) with their gaping wounds, seemed to be like the kingdom of the prince of the Dead at the time of the utter destruction of all creatures.

sn: स्तव च सुताः सुरसूनुसंनिभाः। अमितबलपुरः सरा रणे कुरुवृषभाः शिनिपुत्रमभ्ययुः॥
en: Thereupon, O god among men, your troops and your sons, those foremost of the Kuru race, who are like the sons of the celestials, having placed at the front of the battle the heroes of immeasurable prowess, all rushed against that descendant of the Shini race (Satyaki).

sn: तदतिरुधिरभीममावभौ पुरुषवराश्वरद्विपाकुलम्। लवणजलसमुद्धतस्वनं बलमसुरामरसैन्यसप्रभम्॥
en: Then that force, which was filled with men, the best of horses, cars and innumerable elephants and that sent forth an uproar resembling the roar of a vast ocean of salt and also that looked like the army of the Asuras or of the celestials and again, that was most terrifying to look at, looked most resplendent with extraordinary beauty.

sn: स्त्रिदशवरावरजोपमं युधि। दिनकरकिरणप्रभैः पृषत्कै रवितनयोऽभ्यहनच्छिनिप्रवीरम्॥
en: Thereupon the son of Ravi (Sun), who was like the chief of the celestials (Indra) in prowess, struck that best of the Shini race, who also resembled the younger brother of the Tridashas (celestials), by means of arrows, that had the splendour of the rays of the sun, in the field of battle.

sn: तमपि सरथवाजिसारथि शिनिवृषभो विविधैः शरैस्तवरना भुजगविषसमप्रभै रणे पुरुषवरं समवास्तृणोत् तदा॥
en: Thereafter that foremost one of the Shini race, with threat activity, wholly covered, in the field of battle, that chief among men, along with his car, horses and charioteer, with numerous arrows, that were as fierce as the virulent poison of the snake, in that dreadful field of battle.

sn: शिनिवृषभशरैर्निपीडितं तव सुहृदो वसुषेणमभ्ययुः। त्वरितमतिरथा रथर्षभं द्विरदरथाश्वपदातिभिः सह॥
en: Then the most expert car-warriors, who are your friends, being attended by their elephants, cars, horses and the foot-soldiers, with immense activity, rushed against Vasusena, that foremost of car-warriors, who was then highly oppressed with the shafts, shot by that chief of the Shini race.

sn: तदुदधिनिभमाद्रवद् बलं त्वरिततरैः समभिद्रुतं परैः। दुपदसुतमुखैस्तदाभवत् पुरुषरथाश्वगजक्षयो महान्॥
en: That army, which was like a vast ocean and dispersed in all directions, was wholly inade to run away from the battle by the Pandava heroes, headed by the sons of Drupada, with extraordinary quickness. On this occasion, a great slaughter of men, cars, horses and elephants took place.

sn: अथ पुरुषवौर कृताह्निको भवमभिपूज्य यथाविधि प्रभूम्। अरिवधकृतनिश्चयौ दुतं तव बलमर्जुनकेशवौ सृतौ॥
en: Thereupon those two best of all persons, Arjuna and Keshava, who were resolved upon slaughtering all their antagonists, after having finished the worship of lord Bhava, according to the ordained rites and also having performed their daily prayer ceremonies, with great rapidity proceeded against your force.

sn: जलदनिनदनि:स्वनं रथं पवनविधूतपताककेतनम्। सितहयमुपयान्तमन्तिकं कृतमनसो ददृशुस्तदाऽरयः॥
en: Then their antagonists, namely the Kuru warriors, highly gratified at heart, looked upon that car, that had its rattle resembling the uproar of the masses of clouds and also whose banners and standards were being by the air and to which again, beautiful white horses were yoked and moreover, that was proceeding towards them like the very Death himself.

sn: अथ विस्फार्य गाण्डीवं रथे नृत्यनिवार्जुन:। शरसम्बाधमकरोत् खं दिशः प्रदिशस्तथा॥
en: Thereupon Arjuna, after having stretched his bow, called Gandiva, as if dancing upon the car, spread showers of arrows all over the firmament and the different points of the horizon, as well as all the subsidiary points of the compass.

sn: रथान् विमानप्रतिमान् मजयन् सायुधध्वजान्। ससारथींस्तदा बाणैरभ्राणीवानिलोऽवधीत्॥
en: After this, he (the son of Pandu, Arjuna) smote down numerous cars, that resembled the celestial balloons and that were furnished with all their equipments and also that were adorned with the weapons and standards, along with the charioteers themselves, by means of diverse kinds of arrows even as the great tempest disperses the congregated masses of clouds.

sn: गजान् गजप्रयन्तुंश्च वैजयन्तायुधध्वजान्। सादिनोऽश्वांश्च पत्तीश्च शरैर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्॥
en: He then led, to the abode of Death by means of his numerous arrows, large numbers of elephants, along with their riders, that were equip with the most beautiful flags, weapons and standards, as also numerous horsemen and horses and many foot-soldiers.

sn: तमन्तकमिव क्रुद्धमनिवार्य महारथम्। दुर्योधनऽभ्ययादेको निनन् बाणैरजिह्मगैः॥
en: Thereupon Duryodhana, unattended by any body else, rushed against that most powerful car-warrior, who was like the very Death himself and who was filled with great wrath and who, again, was most invincible in battle, smiting him with his numerous straight arrows.

sn: तस्यार्जुनो धनुः सूतमश्वान् केतुं च सायकैः। हत्वा सप्तभिरेकेन छत्रं चिच्छेद पत्रिणा॥
en: Arjuna, on the other hand, after having destroyed his (antagonist's) bow, charioteer, horses and the standard by means of seven sharp shafts, severed his (foe's) umbrella by means of another winged arrow.

sn: नवमं च समाधाय व्यसृजत् प्राणघातिनम्। दुर्योधनायेषुवरं त द्रौणिः सप्ताच्छिनन्त्॥
en: Then he (Arjuna), finding an opening in his antagonist, shot the foremost of his arrows, that was powerful enough to take away the very life itself (of the person struck with it), at Duryodhana. This the son of Drona severed into seven fragments.

sn: ततो द्रौणिर्धनुश्छित्त्वा हत्वा चाश्वरथाशरैः। कृपस्यापि तदत्युग्रं धनुचिच्छेद पाण्डवः॥
en: Thereupon the son of Pandu, having first cut-off the bow of the son of Drona and slaughtered his horses, that were the best of their species, by means of his arrows, again, shattered that formidable bow belonging to Kripa.

sn: हार्दिक्यस्य धनुश्छित्त्वा ध्वजं चाश्वांस्तदावधीत्। दुःशासनस्येष्वसनं छित्त्वा राधेयमभ्ययात्॥
en: Then he (the son of Pandu), having severed into pieces the bow, owned by the son of Hridika, cut-off his standard and slaughtered his horses. Again, he, cutting off the bow of Dushasana, rushed against the son of Radha,

sn: अथ सात्यकिमुत्सृज्य त्वरन् कर्णोऽर्जुनं त्रिभिः। विद्ध्वा विव्याध विंशत्या कृष्णं पार्थं पुनः पुनः॥
en: Thereupon Karna, having abandoned Satyaki and penetrated Arjuna with three sharp shafts most activity, pierced Krishna with twenty other arrows; and again, penetrated the son of Pritha often and often.

sn: न ग्लानिरासीत् कर्णस्य क्षिपतः सायकान् बहून्। रणे विनिघ्नतः शत्रून् क्रुद्धस्येव शतक्रतोः॥
en: Karna, resembling Indra himself, when he is greatly filled with wrath, felt no fatigue while he was shooting large numbers of arrows in the field of battle, slaughtering the antagonists.

sn: अथ सात्यकिरागत्य कर्ण विद्ध्वाशितैः शरैः। नवत्या नवभिश्चोग्रैः शतेन पुनरार्पयत्॥
en: Thereupon Satyaki, having advanced to him, pierced Karna with ninety-nine sharpheaded and dreadful arrows and again, struck him with one hundred others.

sn: ततः प्रवीरा पार्थानां सर्वे कर्णमपीडयन्। युधामन्युः शिखण्डी च द्रौपदेयाः प्रभद्रकाः॥
en: Afterwards all the best heroes among the Parthas continued to oppress Karna greatly. Thus Yudhamanyu, Shikhandin, the sons of Draupadi, as well as all the Prabhadrakas.

sn: उत्तमौजा युयुत्सुश्च यमौ पार्घत एव च। चेदिकारूषमत्स्यानां केकयाना च यद् बलम्॥
en: And also Uttamanjas and Yuyutsu along with the twin brothers and the several divisions of the Chedis, the Karushas, the Matsyas and the Kaikeyas.

sn: चेकितानश्च बलवान् धर्मराजश्च सुव्रतः। एते रथाश्वद्विरदैः पत्तिभिश्चोग्रविक्रमः॥
en: And Chekitana, who was possessed of immense prowess and the king of righteousness (Yudhishthira), observing the most excellent vows, all these heroes, perfectly aggrandised them by their cars, horses and elephants, as well as by their foot-soldiers, possessing fierce strength.

sn: परिवार्य रणे कर्ण नानाशस्त्रैवाकिरन्। भाषन्तो वाग्भिस्याभिः सर्वे कर्णवधे घृताः॥
en: They all, having surrounded Karna on all sides, poured forth showers of numerous kinds of arrows upon him; and they, then having addressed him in a very harsh language, all deterinined to bring about the fall of Karna.

sn: तां शस्त्रवृष्टि बहुधा कर्णश्छित्त्वा शितैः शरैः। अपोवाहास्त्रवीर्येण द्रमं भक्त्वे मारुतः॥
en: Then Karna, having severed into several fragment that shower of weapons by means of his sharp-headed arrows, cast away his foes with the help of his prowess in the use of weapon even as the wind uproots the tree that stands in its way.

sn: रथिन: समहामात्रान् गजानश्वान् ससादिनः। पत्तिव्रातांश्च संक्रुद्धो निघ्नन् कर्णो व्यदृश्यत॥
en: Karna, who was highly enraged, was found to slaughter large numbers of car-warriors, elephants along with their riders, horses with men riding upon them, as well as throngs of foot-soldiers.

sn: तद् वध्यमानं पाण्डूनां बलं कर्णास्त्रतेजसा। विशस्त्रपत्रदेहासु प्राय आसीत् पराङ्मुखम्॥
en: Then the entire army of the Pandavas, being thus slain by the prowess of those weapons belonging to Karna and being deprived of wcapons and also having had their limbs torn and shattered, almost fled away from the field of battle.

sn: अथ कर्णास्त्रमस्त्रेण प्रतिहत्यार्जुन। दिशं खं चैव भूमिं च प्रावृणोच्छरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Thereupon Arjuna, smiling for a time and smiting down in return the weapons of Karna by means of the weapons of his own, shrouded the different points of the horizon, the entire firmament and the earth will the showers of arrows.

sn: मुसलानीव सम्पेतुः परिधा इव चिषवः। शतघ्य इव चाप्यन्ये वज्राण्युग्राणि चापरे॥
en: Some of the arrows, shot by Arjuna, dropped down upon the earth like the maces; and some, like the spiked clubs; and other fell like the Shataghnis; whereas several other shafts fell down upon the ground like the most dreadful thunderbolt.

sn: तैर्वध्यमानं तत् सैन्यं सपत्तश्वरथद्विपम्। निमीलिताक्षमत्यर्थं बभ्राम च ननाद च॥
en: That force, belonging to the Kauravas, that consisted of numerous foot-soldiers, horses, cars and elephants and that were being slaughtered with the above weapons, that seemed to shut up the eyes, roved about (in the field of battle) ceaselessly and roared most loudly.

sn: निष्कैवल्यं तदा युद्धं प्रापुरश्वनरद्विपाः। हन्यमानाः शरैरार्तास्तदा भीताः प्रदुद्रुवः॥
en: Thereupon the battle became most dreadful, as numerous horses, men and elephants were continually slaughtered. Then, again, a large number of them, highly afflicted with the arrows and struck with terror, fled away from the field of battle,

sn: त्वदीयानां तदा युद्धे संसक्तानां जयैषिणाम्। गिरिमस्तं समासाद्य प्रत्यपद्यत भानुमान्॥
en: Thus whilst the battle raged most fearfully amongst your troops, who most were enthusiastic with the desire of victory, the Sun, approaching the setting mountain, entered into it.

sn: तमसा च महाराज रजसा च विशेषतः न किंचत् प्रत्यपश्याम शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्॥
en: O great monarch, we could not behold anything in the field, either favourable or unfavourable, owing to the thick darkness and especially on account of the dust,

sn: ते त्रसन्तो महेष्वासा रात्रियुद्धस्य भारत। अपयानं ततश्चकुः सहिताः सर्वयोधिभिः॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, then the most powerful bowman (belonging to the Kuru army), being afraid of a battle that would take place in the night, made retreat from the field of battle, accompanied by all their combatants.

sn: कौरवेष्वपयातेषु तदा राजन् दिनक्षये। जयं सुमनसः प्राप्य पार्थाः स्वशिबिरं ययुः॥
en: Thereupon, O monarch, at the fall of night when the Kaurava divisions had all field away (from the field), the sons of Pritha, highly gratified to attain the victory, retired to their own cainps.

sn: वादित्रशब्दैर्विविधेः सिंहनादैः सगर्जितैः। परानुपहसन्तश्च स्तुवन्तश्चाच्युतार्जुनौ॥
en: And they (the Pandava troops) continued to mock at the antagonists by raising various sorts of sounds with all their musical instruments and also by sending froth leonine-roars and uproars; and moreover, they praised both Achyuta and Arjuna.

sn: कृतेऽवहारे तैवीरैः सैनिकाः सर्व एव ते। आशीर्वाचः पाण्डवेषु प्रायुञ्जन्त नरेश्वराः॥
en: Thus when that force of the Kauravas was routed by those heroic warriors, all the troops, as well as the lords of men, began to utter benedictions upon the Pandavas.

sn: ततः कृतेऽवहारे च परदृष्टास्तत्र पाण्डवाः। निशाया शिविरं गत्वा न्यवसन्त नरेश्वराः॥
en: Thereupon, when the hostile army had made their retreat from the field, the Pandava warriors as well as the lords of men, became highly gratified and having retired to their camps, passed the night most cheerfully.

sn: ततो रक्षः पिशाचाच श्वापदाश्चैव संघशः। जग्मुरायोधनं धोरं रुद्रस्याक्रीडासंनिभम्।॥
en: Thereafter large numbers of Rakshasas and Pisachas, as well as numerous other beasts, came to that dreadful field of battle, the looked like the sporting ground of Rudra himself.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच स्वेनच्छन्देन नः सर्वानवधीद् व्यक्तमर्जुनः। न ह्यस्य समरे मुच्येदन्तकोऽप्याततायिनः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said It is told that Arjuna slaughtered all belonging to your side, according as he wished. Really even if the very Destroyer himself had come to battle, the could not escape Arjuna, when he took up arms against him.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: पार्थश्चैकोऽहरद् भद्रामेकश्चाग्निमतर्पयत्। एकश्चमां महीं जित्वा चक्रे बलिभृतो नृपान्॥
en: Thereupon the son of Pritha, unassisted by anybody, ravished Vadra. And again, he, being solitary, gratified Agni. Then he, having subjugated this entire earth, compelled all the monarchs to pay him tribute.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: एको निवातकवचानहनद् दिव्यकार्मुकः। एकः किरातरूपेण स्थितं शर्वमयोधयत्॥
en: Moreover he, being unassisted, slaughtered the whole force of the Nivatakavachas. And also having taken up his celestial bow and without any help from other hands, he (Arjuna) battled against the God, Mahadeva, who stayed before him in the guise of a hunter.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: एको ह्यरक्षद् भरतानेको भवमतोषयत्। तेनैकेन जिताः सर्वे महीपा [ग्रतेजसा॥
en: Again, single-handed, he protected the entire race of the Bharatas; and similarly single-handed he gratified Vava. Also all the monarchs of the earth were defeated by him alone, who was possessed of fierce strength.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: न ते निन्द्याः प्रशस्यास्ते यत्ते चक्रुर्ब्रवीहि तत्। ततो दुर्योधनः सूत पश्चात् किमकरोत् तदा॥
en: They, that is the Kuru warriors, are not to be blamed; rather they should be praised for the reason of their having fought with such a great warrior. Then, O Suta, what did Duryodhana do afterwards? O Sanjaya, do you relate to me all these in detail.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच दीनस्वरा दूयमाना हताहतविध्वस्ता विवर्मायुधवाहनाः। मानिनः शत्रुनिर्जिताः॥ शिबिरस्थाः पुनर्मन्त्रं मन्त्रयन्ति स्म कौरवाः। भग्नदंष्ट्रा हतिविषाः पादाक्रान्ता इवोरगाः॥
en: Sanjaya said The Kaurava warriors, who now resembled the serpents deprived of their fangs and poison and trodden over by the feet and some of whom were struck and wounded and some, again, were deprived of their armours, weapons and proper conveyances and some of whom were thrown down and who all, again, uttered very plaintive voices and who were scorched by the fire of grief and who merely made a parade of their knowledge in arms and who were all defeated by the antagonists and who now repaired to their encampment, had been counselling with one another.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तानब्रवीत् ततः कर्ण क्रुद्धः सर्प इव श्वसन्। करं करेण निष्पीड्य प्रेक्षमाणस्तवात्मजम्॥
en: Thereupon Karna, who was filled with wrath and who sighed heavily like a serpent and who squeezed his hands and who looked at

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: यत्तो दृढश्च दक्षश्च धृतिमानर्जुनस्तदा। सम्बोधयति चाप्येनं यथाकालमधोक्षजः॥
en: 'The thing is that Arjuna is always very persevering, skillful and intelligent and again, when the first time (for any thing to be done) comes, the Eternal One (Vasudeva) awakes him to his duties.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: सहसास्त्रविसर्गेण वयं तेनाद्य वञ्चिताः। श्वस्तवहं तस्य संकल्प सर्वं हन्ता महीपते॥
en: Today we were all deceived by him (Arjuna) by the shower of weapons poured forth all on a sudden. But tomorrow, O ruler of earth, I will baffle all his attempts.'

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा सोऽनुजज्ञे नृपोत्तमान्। तेऽनुज्ञाता नृपा सर्वे स्वानि वेश्मानि भेजिरे॥
en: Having been thus addressed (by Karna) and saying-so be it, he (Duryodhana) commanded all the best of monarchs to dissolve. All these kings, being thus ordered, repaired to their respective abodes.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: सुखोषितास्तां रजनीं हृष्टा युद्धाय निर्ययुः। तेऽपश्यन् विहितं व्यूहं धर्मराजेन दुर्जयम्॥ प्रयत्नात् कुरुमुख्येन बृहस्पत्युशनोमते।
en: Having passed that night most happily, the (those monarchs), with ample gratification, proceeded out for battle (the following morning). They then saw a very invincible array of army, that was constituted by the King of Justice (Yudhishthira), who was the greatest of the whole Kuru race, with the greatest care and quite in accordance with the advices of both Brihaspati and Ushanas.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अथ प्रतीपकर्तारं प्रवीरं परवीरहा॥ सस्मार वृषभस्कन्धं कर्णं दुर्योधनस्तदा।
en: Thereupon Duryodhana, that smiter of enemies, called to his memory, Karna, who baffled the attempts of the his antagonists and who was the foremost of all heroic warriors and who was the slayer of his foes and who had the neck like that of a bull.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: पुरंदरसमं युद्धे मरुद्गणसमं बले॥ कार्तवीर्यसमं वीर्ये कर्ण राज्ञोऽगमन्मनः।
en: The king's (Duryodhana's) mind was now constantly directed towards Karna, who resembled Purandara in battle and who was like the Marutas in prowess and who also was equal to Kartavirya in prowess.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: सर्वेषां चैवसैन्यानां कर्णमेवागमन्मनः। सूतपुत्रं महेष्वासं बन्धुमात्यकिकेष्विव॥
en: As also the hearts of all the troops turned towards Karna, who was the son of the charioteer and who, again was a great bowman, even as the heart of a person always turns towards his friends, whilst he falls in some great danger.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ततो दुर्योधनः सूत पश्चात् किमकरोत्तदा। यद्धोऽगमन्मनो मन्दाः कर्णं वैकर्तनं प्रति॥ अप्यपश्यत राधेयं शीतात इव भास्करम्।
en: Dhritarashtra said Thus when the minds of all you were turned towards Karna the son of Vikartana, did the warriors on my side look at the son of Radha, even as persons, oppressed with cold, look at the sun?

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: कृतेऽवहारे सैन्यानां प्रवृत्ते च रणे पुनः॥ कथं वैकर्तनः कर्णस्तत्रायुध्यत संजय। कथं च पाण्डवाः सर्वे युयुधुस्तत्र सूतजम्॥
en: O Sanjaya, how did Karna, the son of Vikartana, fight there (in the field of battle), when my troops had first re-retreated and again engaged themselves in the battle. And how also did the sons of Pandu fight in the field with the son of Suta?

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: कर्णो ह्येको पहाबाहुर्हन्यात् पार्थान् सगुंजयान्। कर्णस्य भुजयोवीर्यं शक्रविष्णुसमं युधि॥ तस्य शस्त्राणि घोराणि विक्रमश्च महात्मनः। कर्णमाश्चित्य संग्रामे पत्तो दुर्योधनो नृपः॥
en: Indeed, Karna that mighty-armed warrior, would have slaughtered all the sons of Pritha along with the whole lot of the Srinjayas, although he was alone. In the field of battle, the strength of the arms of Karna was similar to the prowess of both Shakra and Vishnu; and the weapons, as well as the prowess of that loftyminded warrior were very fierce. Hoping to be under the protection of Karna, Karna, king Duryodhana was most eager for the battle.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधन ततो दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवेन भृशार्दितम्। पराक्रान्तान् पाण्डुसुतान् दृष्ट्वा चापि महारथः॥
en: Then what did that very powerful carwarrior do after seeing Duryodhana very highly oppressed by the son of Pandu and also after witnessing all the sons of Pandu to display their prowess in arms?

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: कर्णमाश्चित्य संग्रामे मन्दो दुर्योधनः पुनः। जेतुमुत्सहते पार्थान् सपुत्रान् सहकेशवान्॥
en: Relying upon Karna, the foolish prince Duryodhana, again, aspired to defeat the sons, of Pritha along with their sons, as well as Keshava in the field of battle.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अहो बत महद् दुःखं यत्र पाण्डुसुतान् रणे। नातरद् रभसः कर्णो दैवं नूनं परायणम्॥
en: Alas! this is a matter of great grief that in the field of battle Karna, possessed of immense strength, could not defeat the sons of Pandu! It is certain that Destiny holds the foremost position in all affairs.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अहो द्यूतस्य निष्ठेयं घोरा सम्प्रति वर्तते। अहो तीव्राणि दुःखानि दुर्योधनकृतान्यहम्॥ सोढा घोराणि बहुशः शल्यभूतानि संजय।
en: Alas! the most dreadful result of gaming at dice has now been visible. O Sanjaya, I now hear of the greatest sorrows, that had been brought about by foolish, Duryodhana and also that resemble a large number of deadly arrows!

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: सौबलं च तदा तात नीतिमानिति मन्यते॥ कर्णश्च रभसो नित्यं राजा तं चाप्यनुव्रतः।
en: O Sire, the son of Subala was considered to be possessed of great policy; as also Karna was always extremely attached to the prince (Duryodhana).

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: यदेवं वर्तमानेषु महायुद्धेषु संजय॥ अश्रौषं निहतान् पुत्रान् नित्यदेव विनिर्जितान्। न पाण्डवानां समरे कश्चिदस्ति निवारकः॥ स्त्रीमध्यमिव गाहन्ते दैवं तु बलवत्तरम्।
en: O Sanjaya, when such is the matter with the battle which is most dreadful I have often heard that my sons were being constantly defeated and slaughtered. There exists no one who can restrain the Pandavas in the battle; and they enter into my whole force, even as one penetrates into the midst of a throng of women. I is sure that Destiny is the must supreme.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच राजन् पूर्वनिमित्तानि धर्मिष्ठानि विचिन्तय॥ अतिक्रान्तं हि यत् कार्य पश्चाचिन्तयते नरः। तचास्य न भवेत् कार्य चिन्तया च विनश्यति॥
en: Sanjaya said O monarch, do you now reflect upon your past actions, that were most righteous (the game at dice and others of the kind). Man afterwards reflects upon all actions that had past away. But that however, one should not do. For, one is destroyed by that sort of reflection.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तदिदं तव कार्यं तु दूरप्राप्तं विजानता। न कृतं यत् त्वया पूर्व प्राप्ताप्राप्तविचारणम्॥
en: That act of yours has been far from bringing out the desired end. Although you are possessed of knowledge, yet you did not consider before hand the propreity and impropriety of you actions.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: उक्तोऽसि बहुधा राजन् मा युध्यस्वेति पाण्डवैः। गृह्णीषे न च तन्मोहाद् वचनं च विशाम्पते॥
en: O monarch, it was several times told to you, that you should not fight with the, Pandavas. But, O ruler of earth, that advice you did not accept out of foolishness.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: त्वया पापानि घोराणि समाचीर्णानि पाण्डुषु। त्वकृते वर्तते घोर: पार्थिवानां जनक्षयः॥
en: The most horrible deeds of sin had been perpetrated by you in respect to the Pandavas. And only for those acts of yours that this terrible destruction of kings takes place now.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तत्त्विदानीमतिक्रान्तं मा शुचो भरतर्षभ। शृणु सर्वं यथावृत्तं घोरं वैशसमुच्यते॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race all has now passed away, do not grieve for them. O you of evenlasting fame, do you now hear of all that had taken place, namely the details of that awful slaughter.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: प्रभातायां रजन्यां तु कर्णो राजानमभ्ययात्। समेत्य च महाबाहुदुर्योधनमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus when the night dawned, Karna went of the king. And having approached him that hero of very powerful arms then addressed Duryodhana.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: कर्ण उवाच अद्य राजन् समेष्यामि पाण्डवेन यशस्विना। निहनिष्यामि तं वीरं स वा मां निहनिष्यति॥
en: Karna said Today, O monarch, I will go forth for battle with the famous son of Pandu. Either I shall slay that hero or he will slay me.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: बहुत्वान्मम कार्याणां तथा पार्थस्य भारत। नाभूत् समागमो राजन् मम चैवार्जुनस्य च॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, O monarch, on account of the innumerable acts of both myself as well as of the son, O Pritha, that this encounter between me and Arjuna had taken place; else this would not have occurred.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: इदं तु मे यथा प्राज्ञं शृणु वाक्यं विशाम्पते। अनिहत्य रणे पार्थं नाहमेष्यामि भारत॥
en: O ruler of earth, do you listen to my speech, uttered in accordance with my wisdom. O descendant of the Bharata race, if I cannot slay the son of Pritha in battle, I will not return from the field.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: हतप्रवीरै सैन्येऽस्मिन् मयि चावस्थिते युधि। अभियास्यति मां पार्थं शक्रशक्तिविनाकृतम्॥
en: For the reason of this army on over said having had the best of its warriors all slaughtered, that I will myself stand in the field-the son of Pritha will proceed against me, who am deprived of the Sakti-arrow given to me by Shakra (Indra).

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: ततः श्रेयस्करं यच्च तन्निबोध जनेश्वर। आयुधानां च मे वीर्यं दिव्यानामर्जुनस्य च॥
en: O lord of men, then be you conscious of what proves beneficial to you. The strength of my celestial weapons is similar to the strength of Arjuna's weapons.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: कायस्य महतो भेदे लाघवे दूरपातने। सौष्ठवे चास्त्रपाते च सव्यसाची न मत्समः॥
en: As regards the baffling of attempts of the most powerful antagonists and as to the highness of arms and the range of arrows shot and in respect to skillfulness, as also in the management of weapons, Suvyasachin is never my peer.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: प्राणे शौर्येऽथ विज्ञाने विक्रमे चापि भारत। निमित्तज्ञानयोगे च सव्यसाची न मत्समः॥
en: Again, O descendant of the Bharata race, either in physical strength, or in heroism, or knowledge (in the management or arms), or in prowess or in hitting the mark Savyasachin is never my peer.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: सर्वायुधमहामानं विजयं नाम तद्धनुः। इन्द्रार्थं प्रियकामेन निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा॥
en: My bow, that was known by the name of Vijaya, was the most supreme of all weapons. It was made by Vishvakarman with the object of performing what was agreeable to Indra.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: येन दैत्यगणान् राजञ्जितवान् वै शतक्रतुः। यस्य घोषेण दैत्यानां व्यामुह्यन्तः दिशो दशः॥
en: O monarch, Shatakratu (Indra), indeed, subdued all the Daityas by means of that bow and again, at the twang of that bow, the whole body of the Dailyas supposed the ten points of the compass to be empty.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तद् भार्गवाय प्रायच्छच्छकः परमसम्मतम्। तद् दिव्य भार्गवो मह्यमददद् धनुरुत्तमम्॥
en: And formerly Shakra (Indra) gave away to the son of Bhrigu that excellently equipt and best of the celestial bows, which was highly respected by all; and afterwards the son of Bhrigu gave it to me.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तेन योत्स्ये महाबाहुमर्जुनं जयतां वरम्। यथेन्द्रं समरे सर्वान् दैतेयान् वै समागतान्॥
en: I will battle with that foremost one amongst the victorious warriors, the mighty-armed Arjuna, in the field; even as Indra fought with all the Daityas, who had assembled against him.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: धनुर्घोरं रामदत्तं गाण्डीवात् तद् विशिष्यते। त्रिस्सप्तकृत्वः पृथिवी धनुषा येन निर्जिता॥
en: That fierce bow, given away by Rama, is in every way superior to the Gandiva bow; with that bow the entire earth was conquered twenty-one times (by Bhargava).

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: धनुषो ह्यस्य कर्माणि दिव्यानि प्राह भार्गवः। तद् रामो ह्यददन्मह्यं तेन योत्स्यामि पाण्डवम्॥४७
en: The son of Bhrigu speaks of the celestial deeds of that formidable bow. As Rama has given it to me I will surely fight with the son of Pandu with that bow.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अद्य दुर्योधन त्वां नन्दयिष्ये सबान्धवम्। निहत्य समरे वीरमर्जुनं जयतां वरम्॥
en: Today, O Duryodhana, I will gratify your heart, along with that of your friends by slaughter in the field of battle the heroic Arjuna that foremost one amongst the victorious warriors.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: सपर्वतवनद्वीपा हतवीरा ससागरा। पुत्रपौत्रप्रतिष्ठा ते भविष्यत्यद्य पार्थिव॥
en: O lord of earth, the whole kingdom of earth, along with the oceans, the mountains, the forests and the islands, with all her heroes slaughtered, will be your own; and over which you will be established with your sons and grandsons.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: नाशक्यं विद्यते मेऽद्य त्वत्प्रियार्थं विशेषतः। सम्यग्धर्मानुरक्तस्य सिद्धिरात्मवतो यथा॥
en: There exists nothing that I cannot perform today, especially for gratifying you; even as success (ascetic) does surely exist in respect to a person, who is passionately attached to virtue and who also has controlled his soul.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: न हि मां समरे सोढुं संशक्तोऽग्नि तसर्यथा। अवश्यं तु मया वाच्यं येन हीनोऽस्मि फाल्गुनात्।।५१
en: There is no one, who, coming in contact with me, is able to bear me in the battle; even as the tree, coming in contact with the fire, is able to bear it. Indeed this must be told by me that is what respect with the fire, is able to bear it. Indeed this must be told by me that in what respect I am inferior to Phalguna (Arjuna).

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: ज्या तस्य धनुषो दिव्या तथाक्षय्ये महेषुधी। सारथिस्तस्य गोविन्दो मम तादृङ् न विद्यते॥
en: The string of his bow is celestial as also he (Arjuna) has got two inexhaustible quivers. His charioteer is Govinda. But I have got nothing like all these.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तस्य दिव्यं धनुः श्रेष्ठं गाण्डीवमजितं युधि। विजयं च महद्दिव्यं ममापि धनुरुत्तमम्॥
en: His Gandiva bow is celestial and one of the best; as also it is indestructible in battle, whereas my bow, called Vijaya, is also divine and formidable, as it is also the foremost of its kind.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तत्राहमधिकः पार्थाद् धनुषा तेन पार्थिवा येन चाप्यधिको वीरः पाण्डवस्तन्निबोध मे॥
en: Thus, O monarch, as regards the bow I am superior to the son of Pritha. But in what respect the son of Pandu (Arjuna), that heroic one, is superior to me, do you now listen to.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: रश्मिग्राहश्च दाशार्हः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः। अग्निदत्तश्च वै दिव्यो रथः काञ्चनभूषणः॥
en: That one, born in the Dasharha race, is the holder of the reins (of his horses), who is revered by all people; as also his car, that is ornamented with gold, is celestial and the gift of Agni (the god of fire).

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अच्छेद्यः सर्वतो वीर वाजिनश्च मनोजवाः। ध्वजच दिव्यो द्युतिमान् वानरो विस्मयंकरः॥
en: That hero is impenetrable in all his parts. His horses are possessed of the speed of the mind. His standard is also celestial, the most resplendent, bearing an Ape exciting the greatest wonder.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: कृष्णाश्च स्रष्टा जगतो रथं तमभिरक्षति। एतैर्द्रव्यैरहं हीनो योद्धुमिच्छामि पाण्डवम्॥
en: Moreover Krishna, who is the creator of the universe, most carefully guards that car. I am destitute of all these equipments, yet I wish to fight with the son of Pandu.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अयं तु सदृशः शौरेः शल्यः समितिशोभन:। सारथ्यं यदि मे कुर्याद् ध्रुवस्ते विजयो भवेत्॥
en: Indeed, this Shalya, who is the creator of the assemblies, resembles Shauri. Should be perform the duties of my charioteer, the victory will surely by yours.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तस्य मे सारथिः शल्यो भवत्वसुकरः परैः। नाराचान् गार्धपत्रांश्च शकटानि वहन्तु मे॥
en: Let Shalya, therefore, who is irresistible by the antagonists, act as my charioteer. And let the carts also convey my long shafts, as well as the arrows furnished with the feathers of vultures.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: रथाश्च मुख्या राजेन्द्र युक्ता वाजिभिरुत्तमैः। आयान्तु पश्चात् सततं मामेव भरतर्षभ॥
en: Let, O lord of kings, the best of horses by yoked to my excellent cars; and let them, O foremost of the Bharata race, follow me without exhaustion.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: एवमभ्यधिकः पार्थाद् भविष्यामि गुणैरहम्। शल्योऽप्यभ्यधिकः कृष्णादर्जुनादपि चाप्यहम्॥
en: Thus I will be superior to the son of Pritha in respect to these (the above mentioned) qualities. And thus, again, A Shalya is superior to Krishna; and I am superior to Arjuna.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: यथाश्चहृदयं वेद दाशार्हः परवीरहा। तथा शल्यो विजानीते हयज्ञानं महारथः॥
en: Even as that one, of the Dasharha race, who is the slayer of the hostile neroes, is thoroughly versed in knowledge about horses, so Shalya, that most powerful car-warriors, is also acquainted with the science of horses.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: बाहुवीर्यं समो नास्ति मद्रराजस्य कश्चन। तथाऽस्त्रे मत्समो नास्ति कश्चिदेव धनुर्धरः॥
en: In respect of the strength of arms there exist none who is equal to the prince of Madras.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तथा शल्यसमो नास्ति हयज्ञाने हि कश्चन। सोऽयमभ्यधिकः कृष्णाद् भविष्यति रथो मम॥
en: Even as there exists not a single bowman, who is peer in respect to the management of arms, so there is no one, who resembles Shalya as to the knowledge of horses.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: एवं कुते रथस्थोऽहं गुणैरभ्यधिकोऽर्जुनात्। भवे युधि जयेयं च फाल्गुनं कुरुसत्तम।॥
en: Thus my car, which is attended with all these surroundings, will indeed, be superior to that of the son of Pritha. Even the very celestials, accompanied by Vasava, will not be capable of proceeding against it (my car).

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: समुद्यातुं न शक्ष्यन्ति देवा अपि सवासवाः। एतत् कृतं महाराज त्वयेच्छामि परंतप॥
en: Thus having performed all these, when I take my stand upon the car, I should surely be superior to Arjuna in respect of these (the above mentioned) qualities, and also I should, O foremost of the Kuru race, subdue Phalguna.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: क्रियतामेष कामो मे मा वः कालोऽत्यगादयम्। एवं कृते कृतं सह्यं सर्वकामैर्भविष्यति॥
en: O mighty, O searcher of enemies, I desire that all this should be done by you. Also this my desire should be fulfilled by you; and the time in doing it should not pass away for nothing.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: ततो द्रक्ष्यसि संग्रामे यत् करिष्यामि भारत। सर्वथा पाण्डवान् संख्ये विजेष्ये वै समागतान्॥
en: Having performed all this, there will be enough help to me on all desirable points. Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, you will witness whatever I will achieve in the field of battle. By all means I will subdue all the assembled Pandavas in the field of battle.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: न हि मे समरे शक्ताः समुद्यातुं सुरासुराः। किमु पाण्डुसुता राजन् रणे मानुषयोनयः॥
en: Even the very celestials and the Asuras will not be able to proceed against me in the field. O monarch, what should I say of the sons of Pandu, who are of human origin and who will not be capable of withstanding me in the battle.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्तस्तव सुतः कर्णेनाहवशोभिना। सम्पूज्य सम्प्रहृष्टात्मा ततो राधेयमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon your son, having been thus addressed by Karna, who was the ornament of battle and also having adore the son of Radha, told him these words with a highly gratified heart.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच एवमेतत् करिष्यामि यथा त्वं कर्ण मन्यसे। सोपासङ्गा रथाः साश्वाः स्वनुयास्यन्ति संयुगे॥
en: Duryodhana said I will perform all this, that you, O Karna, desire. Numerous cars, furnished with the excellent quivers and yoked to the foremost of horses, will follow you in the field of battle.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: नाराचान् गार्धपत्रांश्च शकटानि वहन्तु ते। अनुयास्याम कर्ण त्वां सर्वे च पार्थिवाः॥
en: And let the long shafts and the arrows furnished with the wings of vultures, be conveyed to you in innumerable carts; and O Karna, all of us, namely the princes, wi follow you into the field.

description: The parley between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा महाराज तव पुत्रः प्रतापवान्। अभिगम्याब्रवीद् राजा मद्रराजमिदं वचः॥
en: Sanjaya said O mighty monarch, your son, who is possessed of immense prowess, after having thus addressed and also having advanced before the prince of Madras, spoke these words to that chief, O monarch.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: संजय उवाच पुत्रस्तव महाराज मद्रराजं महारथम्। विनयेनोपसंगम्य प्रणयाद् वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said O great king, your son, approaching the prince of Madras, that very powerful carwarrior, with enough of humility, spoke these words to him out of affection.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: सत्यव्रत महाभाग तापवर्धन। मद्रेश्वर रणे शूर परसैन्यभयंकर।॥
en: O you of truthful vows, O greatly fortunate one, O you who increase the sorrows of the antagonists, O lord of the Madras, O hero in battle, O you who instill terror in the hostile forces.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: श्रुतवानसि कर्णस्य ब्रुवतो वदतां वर। यथा नृपतिसिंहानां मध्ये त्वां वरये स्वयम्॥
en: O best of speakers, you have heard what Karna had said, namely that this hero (Karna) chooses you amongst all the foremost of princes.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: तत्त्वामप्रतिवीर्याद्य शत्रुपक्षक्षयावह। मद्रेश्वर प्रयाचेऽहं शिरसा विनयेन च॥
en: When such you are, O you of invincible prowess, O prince of the Madras, I solicit you today with enough of humility and bowing down my head in order to bring about the destruction of my enemies.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: तस्मात् पार्थविनाशार्थं हितार्थं मम चैव हि। सारथ्यं रथिनां श्रेष्ठ प्रणयात् कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: In consequence thereof, O best of carwarriors, it is necessary that you should serve me, out of affection, as my charioteer in order to bring about the death of the sun of Pritha, as also to render me a real good.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: त्वयि यन्तरि राधेयो विद्विषो मे विजेष्यते। अभीषूणां हि कर्णस्य ग्रहीतान्यो न विद्यते॥
en: Having had you for his charioteer, the son of Radha will surely vanquish my antagonists.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: ऋते हि त्वां महाभाग वासुदेवसमं युधि। स पाहि सर्वथा कर्णं यथा ब्रह्मा महेश्वरम्॥
en: Indeed, O greatly fortunate one, these exists on one, who can restrain the horses belonging to Karna, excepting yourself, who are cruel to Vasudeva in battle. So do you protect Karna by all means, even as Brahma protects Maheshvara.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: यथा च सर्वथाऽऽपत्सु वार्ष्णेयः पाति पाण्डवम्। तथा मद्रेश्वराद्य त्वं राधेयं प्रतिपालय॥
en: Even as that descendant of the Vrishni race protects the son of Pandu all means in all his difficulties, so, O chief of the Madras, do you support today the son of Radha.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपः कर्णो भवान् भोजश्च वीर्यवान्। शकुनिः सौबलो द्रौणिरहमेव च नो बलम्॥
en: Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Karna, yourself and the most energetic king of the Bhojas as well as Shakuni, the son of Subala, the son of Drona and myself too, all had formed our army.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: एवमेव कृतो भागो नवधा पृथिवीपते। न च भागोऽत्र भीष्मस्य द्रोणस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: O ruler of earth, thus nine divisions had : been made of the army, but no such division or allotted share does yet exist of either Bhishma or lofty-minded Drona.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: ताभ्यामतीत्य तौ भागौ निहता मम शत्रवः। वृद्धौ हि तौ महेष्वासौ छलेन निहतौ युधि॥
en: By those two (Bhishma and Drona), who had gone beyond their respective divisions, all my enemies were slain.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: कृत्वा नसुकरं कर्म गतौ स्वर्गमितोऽनघ। तथान्ये पुरुषव्याघ्राः परैर्विनिहता युधि॥
en: Those two foremost of persons, who were very old, were slaughtered by stratagem in the field. O sinless one, they repaired to heaven from here, after having performed the most arduous tasks; as also other foremost of men, having been slain by the enemies in battle, departed to paradise.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: अस्मदीयाश्च बहवः स्वर्गयोपगता रणे। त्यक्त्वा प्राणान् यथाशक्ति चेष्टां कृत्वा च पुष्कलाम्।।
en: So again numerous other heroes, all belonging to our army, after having achieved the most difficult attempts to the best of their prowess and as also other having abandoned their lives in the battle, at last departed to heaven.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: तदिदं हतभूयिष्ठं बलं मम नराधिप। पूर्वमष्यल्पकैः पार्थैर्हतं किमुत साम्प्रतम्॥
en: O lord of men, this our army the large part of which has been slain have already been massacred by the sons of Pritha, who were at first very few in number. What would be done now?

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: बलवन्तो महात्मानः कौन्तेयाः सत्यविक्रमाः। बलं शेषं न हन्युर्मे यथा तत् कुरु पार्थिव॥
en: The sons of Kunti are all possessed of immense strength; they are lofty-minded; and also they are endued with undaunted course. O lord of earth, now act up in such a way that they may not slaughter the rest of my army.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: हतवीरमिदं सैन्यं पाण्डवैः समरे विभो। कर्णो ोको महाबाहुरस्मत्प्रियहिते रतः॥
en: O lord, this my force has lost the most heroic warriors, who were all slain by the sons of Pandu in the field of battle.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: भवांश्च पुरुषव्याघ्र सर्वलोकमहारथः। शल्य कर्णोऽर्जुनेनाद्य योद्भुमिच्छति संयुगे॥
en: Indeed, Karna alone, that mighty-armed hero, is dear to us and attached to our good; as also, O foremost of persons you are, who are the mightiest car-warrior throughout the entire world.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: तस्मिञ्जयाशा विपुला मद्रराज नराधिप। तस्याभिषुग्रहवरो नान्योऽस्ति भुवि कश्चन॥
en: O Shalya, Karna desires to engage in battle today with Arjuna. But O chief of the people of Madras, I entertain very great hopes in that dreadful battle.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: पार्थस्य समरे कृष्णो यथाभीषुग्रहो वरः। तथा त्वमपि कर्णस्य रथेऽभीषुग्रहो भव॥
en: There does none exist in the whole world, who can act as the best holder of the reins of Karna's horses; even as Krishna makes the foremost holder of reins of Partha's horses in the field of battle, so, O monarch, should you be the holder of reins of the car belonging to Karna.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: तेन युक्तो रणे पार्थो रक्ष्यमाणश्च पार्थिव। यानि कर्माणि कुरुते प्रत्यक्षाणि तथैव तत्॥
en: O sire, having been attended by him (Krishna) and also well guarded in battle, whatever deeds that the son of Pritha performs, will all be consequently done before your eyes.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: पूर्व न समरे ह्येवमवधीदर्जुनो रिपून्। इदानीं विक्रमो ह्यस्य कृष्णेन सहितस्य च॥
en: Formerly Arjuna, indeed, never slaughtered his enemies in battle; but now, as he is always attended by Krishna, he shows forth such a prowess.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: कृष्णेन सहित: पार्थो धार्तराष्ट्री महाचमूम्। अहन्यहनि मद्रेश द्रावयन् दृश्यते युधि॥
en: And now, O lord of the Madras, it is witnessed that day after day the son of Pritha causes the vast army of Dhritarashtra to retreat, because he is ever attended by Krishna in the field of battle.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: भागोऽवशिष्टः कर्णस्य तव चैव महाद्युते। तं भागं सह कर्णेन युगपन्नाशयाद्य हि॥
en: O most resplendent one, the rest of the share given to Karna as well as to yourself still remains. Being accompanied by Karna, do you at once proceed to the field of battle.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: अरुणेन यथा सार्धं तमः सूर्यो व्यपोहतिः। तथा कर्णेन सहितो जहि पार्थं महाहवे॥
en: Even as the Sun, being attended by the Arjuna, disposes the darkness, so you, being united with Karna, slaughter the son of Pritha in this dreadful battle.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: उद्यन्तौ च यथा सूर्यो बालसूर्यसमप्रभौ। कर्णशल्यौ रणे दृष्ट्वा विद्रवन्तु महारथाः॥
en: Let the greatest car-warriors, belonging to the hostile force, run away from the field, after seeing in the battle both Karna and Shalya, who are like two risen suns and who also are possessed of the splendour of the rising sun.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: सूर्यारुणौ यथा दृष्ट्वा तमो नश्यति मारिष। तता नश्यन्तु कौन्तेयाः : सपञ्चाला: ससुंजयाः॥
en: As, O sire, the thick gloom is destroyed at the very view of both the Sun and Arjuna, even so let all the descendants of Kunti along with the Panchalas and the Srinjayas be destroyed (at the sight of Karna and Shalya in the battle).

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: रथिनां प्रवरः कर्णो यन्तॄणां प्रवरो भवान्। संयोगो युवयोलेकि नाभून्न च भविष्यति॥
en: Karna is superior to all the car-warriors, as also you are the foremost of all the charioteers; and there exists no one in the whole world, who is your peer in the field of battle.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: यथा सर्वास्ववस्थासु वार्ष्णेयः पाति पाण्डवम्। तथा भवान् परित्रातुं कर्ण वैकर्तनं रणे॥
en: Even as that descendant of the Vrishni race protects the son of Pandu in all his vicissitudes, so do you guard Karna the son of Vikartana, in the battle.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: त्वया सारथिना ह्येष अप्रधृष्यो भविष्यति। देवतानामपि रणे सशक्राणां महीपते। किं पुनः पाण्डवेयानां मा विशंकीर्वचो मम॥
en: O ruler of earth, when you are his charioteer, this hero (Karna) will surely be invincible even in the war with all the celestials, headed by Shakra (Indra); and what again, need be said with all the Pandavas. O, do not doubt my sayings!

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: संजय उवाच दुर्योधनः श्रुत्वा शल्यः क्रोधसमन्वितः। विशिखां भृकुटिं कृत्वा धुन्वन् हस्तौ पुनः पुनः॥३०
en: Sanjaya said Having heard the words of Duryodhana, Shalya, who became highly enraged and who was stretching his bow to its extent and who, again, was waving his two arms often and often,

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: क्रोधरक्ते महानेत्रे परिवृत्य महाभुजः। कुलैश्चर्यश्रुतबलैर्दृप्तः शल्योऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: And who, moreover, was rolling his two expensive eyes reddened with great rage and who himself was endued with the mighty arms and who also was greatly proud of the possession of his high-birth, properties, vast learning and physical capability, Shalya uttered these words.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: शल्य उवाच अवमन्यसि गान्धारे ध्रुवं च परिशङ्कसे। यन्मां ब्रवीषि विश्रब्धं सारथ्यं क्रियतामिति॥
en: Shalya said O son of Gandhari, you are offending me; and also surely you are suspecting my conduct, when you ask me without hesitation by saying-Do you act as my charioteer.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: अस्मतोऽभयधिकं कर्णं मन्यमानः प्रशंससि। न चाहं युधि राधेय गणये तुल्यमात्मनः॥
en: You praise Karna by considering that he is superior to ourselves. But I never reckon the son of Radha to be equal to myself in the field of battle.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: आदिश्यतामभ्यधिको ममांशः पृथिवीपते। तमहं समरे जित्वा गमिष्यामि यथागतम्॥
en: O ruler of earth, let a much greater share be permitted to me in the battle. Having slaughtered him in the field, who has come to contend with me, I will repair to the place where from I came.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: अथवाष्येक एवाहं योत्स्यामि कुरुनन्दन। पश्य वीर्य ममाद्यत्वं संग्रामे दहतो रिपून्।॥
en: O descendant of the Kuru race, if it be desirable, I will fight alone. Do you witness today my energy in the field of battle, whilst I will engage in scorching the enemies.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: न चापि कामान् कौरव्य निधाय हृदये पुमान्। अस्मद्विधः प्रवर्तेत मा मां त्वमभिशङ्किथाः॥
en: O descendant of the Kuru race, no person, who is like ourselves, ever engages himself in the execution of my duties, after having reflected in the heart such an insult. Do not doubt me (my prowess). In the battle, you should not at all attach such a great insult to me.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: युधि वाप्यवमानो मे न कर्तव्यः कथञ्चन। पश्य पीनौ मम भुजौ वज्रसंहननौ पमौ॥
en: See these two my mascular arms, that can smite down like thunder; as also do you behold my bow that is variegated with the excellent colors, as well as my shafts that are like snakes possessing virulent poison.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: धनुः पश्य च मे चित्रं शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान्। रथं पश्य च मे कृप्तं सदश्चैर्वातवेगितैः॥ गदां च पश्य गान्धारे हेमपट्टविभूषिताम्।
en: See again, my car, to which are yoked the most beautiful horses endued with the swiftness of the wind. And O son of Gandhari, see my mace, that is ornamented with gold and threads of hemp.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: दारयेयं महीं कृत्स्नां विकिरेयं च पर्वतान्॥ शोषयेयं समुद्रांश्च तेजसा स्वेन पार्थिव।
en: O lord of earth, when I am angry I can split up the very earth; and I can break as under the mountains, as also I can soak up even all the oceans by means of my own energy.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: तं मामेवंविधं राजन् समर्थमरिनिग्रह॥ कस्माद् युनसि सारथ्ये नीचस्याधिरथे रणे। ह्यभ्युगतं
en: Why do you, O king, being conscious of the fact that I am thus capable of striking down the enemies, employ me to the office of the charioteer in the field of battle to the son of Adhiratha, who is born of such low parentage.

description: Shalya'a acceptance of the charioteership of Karna
sn: न मामधुरि राजेन्द्र नियोक्तुं त्वमिहार्हसि॥ न हि पापीयसः श्रेयान् भूत्वा प्रेष्यत्वमुत्सहे।
en: O lord of kings, you should not appoint me to this menial service. Having been indeed, thus superior to him, I cannot dare obey the commands of that sinful person.
