sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले दैत्या ह्यासन् महाबलाः। तैस्तदा दर्पमोहाद्यैरबाध्यन्त दिवौकसः॥
en: During this time, all the Daityas had really become very powerful. By them who we darkened with pride and senselessness, all the dwellers of heaven were greatly oppressed.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: ततः सम्भूय विबूधास्तान् हन्तुं कृतनिश्चयाः। चक्रुः शत्रुवधे यत्नं न शेकुर्जेतुमेव तान्॥
en: Thereupon all the celestials, having united together, were determined upon to slaughter them; and also made attempts to bring about the destruction of these antagonists. But they, however, were incapable of vanquishing them.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: अभिगम्य ततो देवा महेश्वरमुमापतिम्। प्रासादयंस्तदा भक्त्या जहि शत्रुगणानिति॥
en: All gods then got vicinity to Maheshvara, the husband of Uma, obtained his grace with ter salute in keen devotion and submitted O sovereign god! Slaughter please, our enemies.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: प्रतिज्ञाय ततो देवो देवतानां रिपुक्षयम्। रामं भार्गवमाहूय सोऽभ्यभाषत् शङ्करः॥
en: Thereupon that god Shankara, after having promised all the celestials the destruction of their enemies and also having called Rama, that descendent of Bhrigu's race before him, addressed him in the following language.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: रिपून् भार्गव देवानां जहि सर्वान् समागतान्। लोकानां हितकामार्थं मत्प्रीत्यर्थं तथैव च ॥
en: O descendant of Bhrigu race, do you slaughter all the antagonists of the celestials, who have assembled here, out of desire for benefiting all the worlds, as also for the satisfaction of myself.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच त्र्यम्बकं वरदं प्रभुम्।
en: Being thus addressed, he (Bhargava) replied to that boon-giving and three-eyed Lord.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: राम उवाच का शक्तिर्मम देवेश अकृतास्त्रस्य संयुगे॥ निहन्तुं दानवान् सर्वान् कृतास्त्रान युद्धदुर्मदान्।
en: Rama said O Lord of the celestials, what might have I got, who am quite unfit for the management of all weapons, that I may slaughter all the Danavas, who are very well-acquainted with the use of weapons, as also who are most invincible in the field of battle.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: महेश्वर उवाच गच्छ त्वं मदनुज्ञातो निहनिष्यसि शात्रवान्॥ विजित्य च रिपून् सर्वान्गुणान् प्राप्यसि पुष्कलान्।
en: Maheshvara said Being commanded by me, do you start at once. You will slaughter these enemies. Having thus subdued all these enemies, you will surely gain innumerable excellent virtues.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: एतच्छुत्वा तु वचनं प्रतिगृह्य च सर्वशः॥ रामः कृतस्वस्त्ययनः प्रययौ दानवान् प्रति। अब्रवीद् देवशāस्तान् महादर्पबलान्वितान्॥
en: Hearing these words and also accepting them in all ways, Rama performed all the propitiatory ceremonies; as also he advanced against the Danavas. Then he addressed those enemies of the celestials, who were possessed of insensibility, pride and enormous strength,

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: मम युद्धं प्रयच्छध्वं दैत्या युद्धमदोत्कटाः। प्रेषिता देवदेवेन वो विजेतुं महासुराः॥
en: Most invincible in battle as you are, O Daityas, do you give me battle. I had been sent by the lord of the celestials to subdue the mighty Asuras.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: इत्युक्ता भार्गवेणाथ दैत्या युद्धं प्रचक्रमुः। स तान् निहत्य समरे दैत्यान् भार्गवनन्दनः॥ वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शः प्रहारैरेव भार्गवः। स दानवैः क्षततनुर्जामदग्न्यो द्विजोत्तमः॥
en: Having been thus addressed by that descendent of Bhrigu's race, all the Daityas began to fight with him (Bhargava). Then that descendant of Bhrigu's race, that delighter of the race of Bhrigu, after having slaughtered those Daityas in the field of battle by means of strokes, that were like the touches of the thunder belonging to Indra.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: संस्पृष्टः स्थाणुना सद्यो निर्वण: समजायत। प्रीतश्च भगवान देवः कर्मणा तेन तस्य वै॥
en: Was greatly wounded in the body by the Danavas. But thereafter that son of Jamadagni, that foremost of regenerate persons, being immediately touched by Sthanu, became wholly freed from these wounds.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: वरान् प्रादाद् बहुविधान् भार्गवाय महात्मने। उक्तश्च देवदेवन प्रीतियुक्तेन शूलिना॥
en: Thereupon the illustrious lord, being gratified by that deed of his, gave to that highsouled descendant of Bhrigu's race various kinds of boons.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: निपातात्तव शस्त्राणां शरीरे याभवद् रुजा। तया ते मानुषं कर्म व्यपोढं भृगुनन्दन॥ गृहाणास्त्राणि दिव्यानि मत्सकाशाद् यथेप्सितम्।
en: The wounds, caused upon your body by the falling of innumerable weapons testify to the u superhuman act performed by you. O delighter of Bhrigu's race, do you, therefore, accept these numerous celestial weapons from me, according to your desire.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच ततोऽस्त्राणि समस्तानि वरांश्च मनसेप्सितान्॥ लख्वा बहुविधान् रामः प्रणम्य शिरसा भवम्। अनुज्ञां प्राप्य देवेशाजगाम स महातपाः॥
en: Duryodhana said Thereupon, having obtained all the diverse kinds of weapons and boons desired in his heart, Rama performed the ceremony of bowing down his head to Shiva. Thus having received the command from the lord of the celestials, that great devotee went away.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: एवमेतत् पुरावृत्तं तदा कथितवानृषिः। भार्गवोऽपि ददौ धनुर्वेदं महात्मने। १५७॥ कर्णाय पुरुषव्याघ्र सुप्रीतेनान्तरात्मना।
en: This is the old story, which then; the Rishi narrated (to my father). O foremost of persons, the son of Bhrigu handed over all that knowledge of archery to the high-souled Karna, being gratified in his inner heart.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: वृजिनं हि भवेत् किचिंद् यदि कर्णस्य पार्थिव॥ १५८ नास्मै शस्त्राणि दिव्यानि प्रादास्यद् भृगुनन्दनः।
en: O ruler, of earth, if Karna had the slightest fault, in that case the descendant of Bhrigu's race would not have given him these celestial weapons.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: नापि सूतकुले जातं कर्ण पन्ये कथंचन॥ देवपुत्रमहं मन्ये क्षत्रियाणां कुलोद्भवम्। विसृष्टमवबोधार्थं कुलस्येति मतिर्मम॥
en: I do not think that Karna was ever born in the family of a charioteer. Rather I think that he is the son of a god, or he is come of the race of the Kshatriyas. My opinion is that he was abandoned (in his infancy), lest his race be ascertained.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: सर्वथा न ह्ययं शल्य कर्णः सूतकुलोद्भवः। सकुण्डलं सकवचं दीर्घबाहुं महारथम्॥ कथमादित्यसदृशं मृगी व्याघ्र जनिष्यति।
en: O Shalya, this one, namely Karna, is, indeed, by no means born of the family of a charioteer. This mighty car-warrior resembling the very Sun, is furnished with the (natural) ear-rings, armour and long arms; could is be possible that the she deer had given birth to a tiger.

description: The history of destruction of the triple city belonging to the Asuras
sn: यथा ह्यस्य भुजौ पीनौ नागराजकरोपमौ॥ वक्षः पश्य विशालं च सर्वशत्रुनिबर्हणम्। न त्वेष प्राकृतः कश्चित् कर्णो वैकर्तनो वृषः। महात्मा ह्येष राजेन्द्र रामशिष्यः प्रतापवान्॥
en: O monarch, Indeed, his two arms are very massive; and they are like the trunk of the prince of elephants. Do you behold his broad chest, which is powerful enough to resist all sorts of enemies. This Karna, the son of Vikartana, can never be an ordinary individual. O lord of kings, this high-souled disciple of Rama is really a very powerful warrior.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच एवं स भगवान् देवः सर्वलोकपितामहः। सारथ्यमकरोत् तत्र ब्रह्मा रुद्रोऽभवद् रथी।॥
en: Duryodhana said Thus that illustrious god, Brahman, that Grandsire of all the words, acted as the charioteer on that occasion; while Rudra acted as the car-warrior.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: रथिनोऽभ्यधिको वीर कर्तव्यो रथसारथिः। तस्मात्त्वं पुरुषव्याघ्र नियच्छ तुरगान् युधि॥
en: That hero, who is superior to the warrior on the car, should be made to act as the charioteer. You do, therefore, hold the reins of the horses in the field of battle, O foremost of persons.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: यथा देवगणैस्तत्र वृतो यत्नात् पितामहः। तथास्माभिर्भवान् यत्नात् कर्णादभ्यधिकोवृतः॥
en: Even as, on that occasion, the Grandsire was elected by all the celestials with great care, so you, who are superior to Karna, are selected with great care by us.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: यथा ददैवैर्महाराज ईश्वरादधिको वृतः। तथा भवानि क्षिप्रं रुद्रस्येव पितामहः॥ नियच्छ तुरगान् युद्धे राधेयस्य महायुते।
en: As he (Grandsire), O great monarch, was chosen as one superior to the lord (Shankara) by all the celestials, even so do you immediately restrain the horses of Rudra.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: शल्य उवाच मयाप्येतन्नरश्रेष्ठ बहुशोऽनरसिंहयोः॥ कथ्यमानं श्रुतं दिव्यमाख्यानमतिमानुषम्। यथा च चक्रे सारथ्यं भवस्य प्रपितामहः॥ यथासुराश्च निहता इषुणैकेन भारत।
en: Shalya said O best of persons, this celestial and most extraordinary history regarding those two foremost of immortals, narrated several times, was heard by me also. O descendant of the Bharata race, I have also heard how the great Grandsire acted as the charioteer of Bhava and how the Asuras were all slaughtered with a single arrow.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: कृष्णस्य चापि विदितं सर्वमेतत् पुरा ह्यभूत्॥ यथा पितामहो जज्ञे भगवान् सारथिस्तदा।
en: All this, namely how the Grandsire, that illustrious one, acted as the charioteer on that occasion, had fully been known to Krishna beforehand.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: अनागतमतिक्रान्तं वेद कृष्णोऽपि तत्त्वतः॥ एतदर्थं विदित्वापि सारथ्यमुपजग्मिवान्। स्वयं भूरिव रुद्रस्य कृष्णः पार्थस्य भारत॥
en: Again, Krishna knows very well in all their details what had already taken place and what will take place hereafter. O descendant of the Bharata race, knowing the import of all this, Krishna took up the charioteership of the son of Pritha, even as the Self-create One took up the charioteer-ship of Rudra.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: यदि हन्याच कौन्तेयं सूतपुत्रः कथंचन। दृष्ट्वा पार्थं हि निहतं योत्स्यति केशवः॥ शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिर्धक्ष्यते तव वाहिनीम्।
en: If it be possible that the son of charioteer (Karna) should ever slay the son of Kunti, beholding the son of Pritha slaughtered, Keshava himself will surely engage in battle. And that holder of the conch, the discus and the mace will destroy your whole race.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: न चापि तस्य क्रुद्धस्य वार्ष्णेयस्य महात्मनः॥ स्थास्यते प्रत्यनीकेषु कश्चिदत्र नृपस्तव।
en: There exists no king in our whole army, who will be able to stand in the front of that high-souled descendant of Vrishni's race, when he will be filled with wrath.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: संजय उवाच सं तथा भाषमाणं तु मद्रराजमरिंदमः॥ प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुदीनात्मा सुतस्तव।
en: Sanjaya said Your son, who was a chastiser of enemies and who was endued with mighty arms and who also had a very cheerful heart, now replied to the king of the Madra, who was speaking in such a tone.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: मावमंस्था महाबाहो कर्णं वैकर्तनं रणे॥ सर्वशस्त्रभृतां श्रेष्ठं सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगम्।
en: In the field of battle, O mighty-armed warrior, you do not under-mine the value of Karna, the son of Vikartana, who is most supreme of all that are versed in the management of arms and who, again, has crossed the great ocean of all Shastras.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: यस्य ज्यातलनर्घोष श्रुत्वा भयकरं महत्॥ पाण्डवेयानि सैन्यानि विद्रवन्ति दिशो दश।
en: Hearing the most tremendous and very high twang of his bow-string and the sound of his palms, even the troops of the Pandavas run away in different directions.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: प्रत्यक्षं ते महाबाहो यथा रात्रौ घटोत्कचः॥ मायाशतानि कुर्वाणो हतो मायापुरस्कृतः।
en: O mighty-armed heroes, you have witnessed it with your own Ghatotkacha, who dreamed innumerable dreams, was slain by (Karna) in that night with several other illusions before him. eyes and

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: न चातिष्ठतः बीभत्सुः प्रत्यनीके कथंचन॥ एतांश्च दिवसान् सर्वान् भयेन महता वृतः।
en: Having been encompassed with very great terrors during all these days, Vibhatsu could never stay in the ranks facing against him (Karna).

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: भीमसेनश्च बलवान् धनुष्कोट्याभिचोदितः॥ उक्तश्च संज्ञया राजन् मूढ औदरिको यथा।
en: Then, O monarch, the very powerful Bhimasena, who was hemmed in on all sides by the horns of the bow (belonging to Karna), was addressed in these terms namely fool and Glutton.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: माद्रीपुत्रौ तथा शूरौ येन जित्वा महारणे॥ कमप्यर्थं पुरस्कृत्य न हतौ युधि मारिष।
en: So also, O sire, the two war-like sons of Madri, having been first vanquished by him in that dreadful battle, were not slain by him in the field having some motive in view.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: येन वृष्णिप्रवीरस्तु सात्यकिः सात्वतां वरः॥ निर्जित्य समरे शूरो विरथश्च बलात् कृतः।
en: By him (Karna) also that most heroic warrior of the Vrishni race, that chief of the Satvata clan, Satyaki, who was a mighty warrior, was vanquished in the battle; as also he was deprived of his car.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: सृञ्जयाश्चेतरे सर्वे धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः॥ असकृन्निर्जिताः संख्ये स्मयमानेन संयुगे।
en: And several other heroes, namely all the Srinjayas, who headed by Dhrishtadyumna, often and often vanquished in the field by him, who felt the greatest ease in the battle.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: तं कथं पाण्डवा युद्धे विजेष्यन्ति महारथम्॥ यो हन्यात् समरे क्रुद्धो वज्रहस्तं पुरंदरम्।
en: How will it be possible then that the Pandavas will defeat that great car-warrior in the field of battle, who, when enraged, can slaughter even Purandara, that wielder of the thunderbolt, in battle.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: त्वं च सर्वास्त्रविद् वीरः सर्वाविद्यास्त्रपारगः॥ बाहुवीर्येण ते तुल्यः पृथिव्यां नास्ति कश्चन।
en: were Were O heroic warrior, you are well-versed in diverse kinds of weapons and you have crossed over the ocean of all branches of knowledge. And there exists none else in this world, who is equal to you in the strength of arms.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: त्वं शल्यभूतः शत्रूणामविषह्यः पराक्रमे॥ ततस्त्वमुच्यसे राजशल्य इत्यरिसूदन।
en: O monarch, you are made up of shafts; and you are invincible in respect to your antagonists in prowess. O slayer of enemies, you are, therefore, called Shalya (shaft).

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: तव बाहुबलं प्राप्य न शेकुः सर्वसात्वताः॥ तव बाहुबलाद् राजन् किं नु कृष्णो बलाधिकः।
en: All the warriors of the Satvata race are not able to stand, encountering the strength of your arms. O monarch, is the highly powerful Krishna superior to you in the strength of your arms?

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: यथा हि कृष्णेन बलं धार्यं वै फाल्गुने हते॥ तथा कर्णात्ययीभावे त्वया धार्यं महद् बलम्।
en: Even as, indeed, the whole force (belonging to the Pandavas) is supported by Krishna upon the fall of Phalguna, so should this vast army (of the Kurus) be supported by you upon the death of Karna.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: किमर्थं समरे सैन्यं वासुदेवो न्यवारयत्॥ किमर्थं च भवान् सैन्यं न हनिष्यति मारिष।
en: O sire, for what reason should Vasudeva restrain your forces in the field of battle; and for what reason also you will not slaughter the hostile ariny.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: त्वत्कृते पदवीं गन्तुमिच्छेयं युधि मारिष। सोदराणां च वीराणां सर्वेषां त महीक्षिताम्॥
en: Now, O sire, for your sake I wish to go in the way in this field of battle, that had already been trodden by my heroic brothers (slain), as well as by all the rulers of the earth.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: शल्य उवाच यन्मां ब्रवीषि गान्यारे अग्रे सैन्यस्य मानद। विशिष्टं देवकीपुत्रात् प्रीतिमानस्म्यहं त्वहि॥
en: Shalya said O son of Gandhari, O bestower of honors, when you describe me in the presence of your troops to be superior to the son of Devaki I am highly satisfied with you.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: एष सारथ्यमातिष्ठे राधेयस्य यशस्विनः। युध्यतः पाण्डवार्येण यथा त्वं वीर मन्यसे॥
en: O hero, even as you desire, so now I accept the charioteership of that highly illustrious son of Radha, while he will engage in fight with that foremost of the sons of Pandu.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: समयश्च हि मे वीर कश्चिद् वैकर्तनं प्रति। उत्सृजेयं यथाश्रद्धमहं वाचोऽस्य संनिधौ॥
en: But war-like one, I must have a condition in respect to the son of Vikartana, namely that I may be allowed to utter any words, I like, in his presence.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: संजय उवाच तथेति राजन् पुत्रस्ते सह कर्णेन मारिष। अब्रवीन्मद्रराजानं सर्वक्षत्रस्य संनिधौ।॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O monarch, O sire, your son, attended by Karna, addressed the king of the Madras, in the presence of all the Kshatriyas, saying-So be it.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: सारथ्यस्याभ्युपगमाच्छल्येनाश्वासितस्तदा। दुर्योधनस्तदा दृष्टः कर्णं तमभिषस्वजे॥
en: Having been thus assured by Shalya's accepting the office of charioteership (of Karna), Duryodhana, being highly gratified, embraced Karna.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: अब्रवीच पुनः कर्णं स्तूयमानः सुतस्तव। जहि पार्थान् रणे सर्वान् महेन्द्रो दानवानिव॥
en: Moreover your son, being greatly praised (by the bands around him), addressed Karna, saying-do you slaughter all the sons of Pritha in the field of battle, even as Mahendra (Indra) slaughtered all the Danavas in the battle-field.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: स शल्येनाभ्युपगते हयानां संनियच्छने। कर्णो हृष्टमना भूयो दुर्योधनमभाषत॥
en: When the drivership of his horses was accepted by Shalya, Karna became highly once gratified and more addressed Duryodhana, saying-

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: नातिहष्टमना ह्येष मद्रराजोऽभिभाषते। राजन् मधुरया वाचा पुनरेनं ब्रवीहि वै॥
en: Indeed, this king of the Madras does not say this in a cheerful spirit. Therefore, O monarch, do you request him once more (for the charioteership) in sweeter words.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: ततो राजा महाप्रज्ञः सर्वास्त्रकुशलो बली। दुर्योधनऽब्रवीच्छलयं मद्रराजं महीपतिम्॥ पूरयन्निव घोषेण मेघगम्भीरया गिरा।
en: Thereupon king Duryodhana, who was very learned and versed in all objects and who also was possessed of great strength, once more addressed that ruler of earth. Shalya, the chief of the Madras, in a voice as deep as the rumbling of the clouds, filling the whole region with the echo of his voice.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: शल्य कर्णोऽजुनेनाद्य योद्धव्यमिति मन्यते॥ तस्य त्वं पुरुषव्याघ्र नियच्छ तुरगान् युधि।
en: O Shalya, Karna thinks that he should fight with Arjuna today. So you, O foremost of men, restrain his horses in the field of battle.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: कर्णो हत्वेतरान् सर्वान् फाल्गुनं हन्तुमिच्छति॥ तस्याभीषुग्रहे राजन् प्रयाचे त्वां पुनः पुनः।
en: Karna is most willing to slaughter Phalguna (Arjuna), after having slain all the other heroes inferior to him. In consequence of this, O monarch, I repeatedly entreat you to hold the reins of his horses.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: पार्थस्य सचिवः कृष्णो यथाभीषुग्रहो वरः। तथा त्वमपि राधेयं सर्वतः परिपालया॥
en: Even as Krishna, that foremost one amongst all the charioteers, is the adviser of the son of Pritha, so you would support the son of Radha in all ways.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: संजय उवाच ततः शल्यः परिष्वज्य सुतं ते वाक्यमब्रवीत्। दुर्योधनममित्रघ्न प्रीतो मद्रधिपस्तदा॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon Shalya, that king of the Madras, being highly gratified, after having embraced your son, Duryodhana, that slayer of enemies, addressed him, saying.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: शल्य उवाच एवं चेन्मन्यसे राजन् गान्धारे प्रियदर्शन। तस्मात्ते यत् प्रियं किंचित् तत् सर्वं करवाण्यहम्।।
en: Shalya said O monarch, O son of Gandhari, O handsome-looking one, if you so desire, I will perform all that you consider to be dear to you.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: यत्रास्मि भरतश्रेष्ठ योग्यः कर्मणि कर्हिचित्। तत्र सर्वात्मना युक्तो वक्ष्ये कार्यं परंतप॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, for whatever acts I am competent, there I will engage myself with the whole of my heart; and I will bear the burden of all your acts.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: यत्तु कर्णमहं ब्रूयां हितकामः प्रियाप्रिये। मम तत् क्षमतां सर्व भवान् कर्णश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Whatever, either agreeable or disagreeable, I will order to Karna, who are willing to do you good, for all that you, as well as Karna, should excuse me in every way.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: कर्ण उवाच ईशानस्य यथा ब्रह्मा यथा पार्थस्य केशवः। तथा नित्यं हिते युक्तो मद्रराज भवस्व नः॥
en: Karna said Even as Brahma is to Ishana or a Keshava is to Ishana or as Keshava is to the son of Pritha, so you, O king of the Madras, should ever be engaged in rendering us good.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: शल्य उवाच आत्मनिन्दाऽऽत्मपूला च परनिन्दा परस्तवः। अनाचरितमार्याणां वृत्तमेतचतुर्विधम्॥
en: Shalya said The most respectable personages believe in these four different ways, which are enumerated thus-self-blame, or self-praise and speaking ill or well of others.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: यत् तु विद्वन् प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रत्ययार्थमहं तव। आत्मनः स्तवसंयुक्तं तन्निबोध यथातथम्॥
en: O wise one, whatever I will speak with a view to draw out your confidence, all that is full of self-praise. Be what it may, do you listen to it properly.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: अहं शक्रस्य सारथ्ये योग्यो मातलिवत् प्रभो। अप्रमादात् प्रयोगाच ज्ञानविद्याचिकित्सनैः॥
en: O illustrious one, I am, like Matali, competent to act as the charioteer of Indra and careful as I am, I am also versed in the management of horses, as, again, I am acquainted with all sorts of knowledge and learning, conscious of the means of avoiding all future dangers.

description: Shalya's accepting the charioteer ship of Karna
sn: ततः पार्थेन संग्रामे युध्यमानस्य तेऽनघ। वाहयिष्यानि तुरगान् विज्वरो भव सूतज॥
en: Then, O sinless one, I will drive your horses, while you will be engaged in battle with the son of Pritha, in the field. O son of a charioteer, be you free from all anxieties and troubles.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अयं ते कर्णं सारथ्यं मद्रराजः करिष्यति। कृष्णादभ्यधिको यन्ता देवेशस्येव मातलिः॥
en: Duryodhana said O Karna, this king of Madra, superior even to Krishna, will act as your driver, like Matali, the driver of the king of gods.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: यथा हरिहयैर्युक्तं संगृह्णाति स मातलिः। शल्यस्तथा तवाद्यायं संयन्ता स्थवाजिनाम्॥
en: As Matali manages his car drawn by the horse of Hari so will Shalya manage today your car and horses.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: योधे त्वयि रथस्ये च मद्रराजे च सारथौ। संख्ये पार्थनभिभविष्यति॥
en: With you as the warrior on that car and the king of Madra as the charioteer it will, forsooth, defeat the Parthas in battle.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: रथश्रेष्ठो ध्रुवं संजय उवाच ततो दुर्योधन भूयो मद्रराजं तरस्विनम्। उवाच राजन् संग्रामेऽध्युषिते पर्युपस्थिते॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon again in the morning Duryodhana addressed the active king of

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: कर्णस्य यच्छ संग्रामे मद्रराज हयोत्तमान्। त्वयाभिगुप्तो राधेयो विजेष्यति धनंजयम्॥
en: O king of Madra, manage in battle the excellent horses of Karna. Protected by you Karna will defeat Arjuna.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: इत्युक्तो रथमास्थाय तथेति प्राह भारत। शल्येऽभ्युपगते कर्णः सारथिं सुमनाऽब्रवीत्॥ त्वं सूत स्यादनं मह्यं कल्पयेत्यसकृत् त्वरन्।
en: Thus addressed he expressed his consent and got upon the chariot, O Bharata. When Shalya went there, Karna, in good spirits, addressed his driver saying, O charioteer, quickly equip this car for me.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ततो जैत्रं रथवरं गन्धर्वनगरोपमम्॥ विधिवत् कल्पितं भद्रं जयेत्युक्त्वा न्यवेदयत्।
en: Having duly equipped that victorious car the best of its kind, which resembled the city of Gandharvas Shalya presented it to Karna, saying-“May good betide you and may you come off victorious!”

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: तं रथं रथिनां श्रेष्ठः कर्णोऽभ्यर्च्य यथाविधि॥ सम्पादितं ब्रह्माविदा पूर्वमेव पुरोधसा। कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं यत्नादुपस्थाय च भास्करम्॥ समीपस्थं मद्रराजमारोह त्वमथाब्रवीत्।
en: Duly worshipping that car which had formerly been sanctified by a priest conversant with Brahma, going round it and worshipping the sun, Karna, the foremost of car-warriors, addressed the king of Madra, standing near him, saying-"get upon the chariot."

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ततः कर्णस्य दुर्घषं स्यन्दनप्रवरं महत्॥ आरुरोह महातेजाः शल्यः सिंह इवाचलम्।
en: Then like a lion ascending a hill the highly energetic Shalya got upon the strong built car of Karna.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ततः शल्याश्रित दृष्ट्वा कर्णः स्वं रथमुत्तमम्॥ अध्यतिष्ठद् यथाम्भोदं विद्युत्वन्तं दिवाकरः।
en: Beholding Shalya stationed there Karna got upon his most excellent car like the sun riding on a mass of clouds charged with lightning.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: तावेकरथमारूढावादत्याग्निसमत्विषौ॥ अभ्रजेतां यथा मेघ सूर्याग्नी सहितौ दिवि।
en: Seated on the same car those two horses. effulgent like the sun and fire, shone there like the sun and fire sitting together on a cloud in the sky.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: संस्तूयमानो तौ वीरौ तदास्तां द्युतिमत्तसौ॥ ऋत्विक्सदस्यैरिन्द्राग्नी स्तूयमानाविवाध्वरे।
en: Eulogised those two highly effulgent heroes shone like Indra and Agni (fire-god) adored with hymns in a sacrifice by Ritvikas and Sadasyas.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: स शल्यसंगृहीताश्वे रथे कर्णः स्थितो बभौ॥ धनुर्विस्फारयन् घोरं परिवेषीव भास्करः।
en: Shalya holding the reins of the horses Karna stood on that car stretching his dreadful bow like the sun enveloped with a circular light.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: आस्थितः स स्थश्रेष्ठं कर्णः शरगभस्तिमान्।॥ प्रबभौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ मन्दरस्थ इवांशुमान्।
en: Stationed on that best of cars Karna, the foremost of men, with the rays of his shafts, looked like the sun on the mount Mandara.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: तं रथस्थं महाबाहुं युद्धायामिततेजसम्॥ दुर्योधनस्तु राधेयमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। अकृतं द्रोणभीष्माभ्यां दुष्करं कर्म संयुगे॥ कुरुष्वाधिरथे वीर मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम्।
en: Duryodhana invited to battle that mighty armed son of Radha of incomparable energy stationed on the car saying-O hero, O carwarrior, do you perform in the presence of all bond men an action, hard of accomplishment which had not been performed even by Bhishma and Drona.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: मनोगतं मम ह्यासीद् भीष्मद्रोणौ महारथौ॥ अर्जुनं भीमसेनं च निहन्ताराविति ध्रुवम्।
en: I had always thought that those two mighty car-warriors Bhishma and Drona would kill, without any doubt, Bhima and Arjuna.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ताभ्यां यदकृतं वीर वीरकर्म महामृधे॥ तत् कर्म कुरु राधेय वज्रपाणिरिवापरः।
en: Like the second wielder of thunderbolt do you accomplish that heroic feat in the great battle which had not been performed by them.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: गृहाण धर्मराजं वा जहि वा त्वं धनंजयम्॥ भीमसेनं च राधेय माद्रीपुत्रौ यमावपि।
en: Either attack the pious Yudhishthira or kill Arjuna and Bhima, O son of Radha and the twin sons of Madri.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: जयश्च तेऽस्तु भद्रं ते प्रयाहि पुरुषर्षभ॥ पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैन्यानि कुरु सर्वाणि भस्मसात्।
en: Many blessings and victory attend you. Start for battle, O foremost of men, consume the arıny of the Pandavas.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ततस्तूर्यसहस्राणि भेरीणामयुतानि च॥ वाद्यमानान्यराजन्त मेघशब्दो यथा दिवि।
en: Ten thousands of trumpets and ten thousand drums simultaneously struck and produced a sound resembling the muttering of clouds in the sky.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: प्रतिगृह्य तु तद् वाक्यं रथस्थो रथसत्तमः॥ अभ्यभाषत राधेयः शल्यं युद्धविशारदम्। चोदयाश्वान महाबाहो यावद्धन्मि धनंजयम्॥ भीमसेनं यमौ चौभौ राजानं च युधिष्ठिरम्।
en: Accepting his words that foremost of carwarriors, the son of Radha stationed on the car, said to Shalya, an expert in fighting. Drive the horses on, O great heroes so that I may kill Arjuna, Bhima, the twins and Yudhishthira.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अद्य पश्यतु मे शल्य बाहुवीर्यं धनंजयः॥ अस्यतः कङ्कपत्राणां सहस्राणि शतानि च।
en: O Shalya, Arjuna will witness today the strength of my arms when I will discharge hundreds and thousands of Kanka feather were arrows.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अद्य क्षेप्स्याम्यहं शल्यं शरान् परमतेजनान्॥ पाण्डवानां विनाशाय दुर्योधनजयाय च।
en: I will shoot today, O Shalya, powerful arrows for destroying the Pandavas and securing victory for Duryodhana.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: शल्य उवाच सूतपुत्र कथं नु त्वं पाण्डवानवमन्यसे॥ सर्वास्त्रज्ञान महेष्वासान् सर्वानेव महाबलम्। अनुवर्तिनो महाभागानजय्यान् सत्यविक्रमान्॥
en: Shalya said O son of a charioteer, why do you make light of the sons of Pandu who are all very powerful, great bow men and experts in the use of other weapons. They never retreat from battle, fortunate, unconquerable and are of great prowess.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अपि संतनयेयुर्धे भयं साक्षाच्छतक्रतोः। यदा श्रोष्यसि निर्घोषं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः॥ राधेय गाण्डिवस्याजौ तदा नैवं वदिष्यसि।
en: They are capable of striking fear even into the heart of Indra himself. O son of Radha, when you will hear the twang of his Gandiva bow in battle like the peal of the thunder itself you will not give vent to such words.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: यदा द्रक्ष्यसि भीमेन कुञ्जरानीकमाहवे॥ विशीर्णदन्तं निहतं तदा नैवं वदिष्यसि।
en: When you will see Bhimsena killed elephants with their riders by serially splitting their teeth in the battle-field, your tongue will dcfinitely pause saying anything otherwise,

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: यदा द्रक्ष्यसि संग्रामे धर्मपुत्रं यमौ तथा॥ शितैः पृषत्कैः कुर्वाणानभ्रच्छायामिवाम्बरे। अस्यतः क्षिण्वतश्चारील्लँघुहस्तान् दुरासदान्। पार्थिवानपि चान्यास्त्वं तदा नैवं वदिष्यसि॥
en: When you will see Yudhishthira and the twins making a canopy with their sharpened shafts like that of clouds in the sky and other irrepressible kings all light-handed, shooting arrows reducing the number of their enemies you will not speak such words.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: संजय उवाच अनाद्दत्य तु तद् वाक्यं मद्रराजेन भाषितम्। याहीत्येवाब्रवीत् कर्णो मद्रराजं तरस्विनम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Disregarding the words spoken by the king of Madra Karna said to him who was greatly active-"go on". Sanjaya said Disregarding the words spoken by the king of Madra Karna said to him who was greatly active-"go on".

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: संजय उवाच दृष्ट्वा कर्ण महेष्वासं युयुत्सुं समवस्थितम्। चुक्रुशः कुरवः सर्वे हृष्टरूपाः समन्ततः॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding the great bowmen bowmen Karna stationed for battle all the Kurus began to utter loud cries of joy from all sides.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: ततो दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैर्भेरीणां निनदेन च। बाणशब्दैश्च विविधैर्गर्जितैश्च तरस्विनाम्॥ निर्ययुस्तावका युद्धे मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्।
en: Thereupon with the beatings of cymbals and drums, the sound of all sorts of weapons and the war-cries of the greatly active heroes all your soldiers proceeded to the battle-field, making death the final point of stoppage.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: प्रयाते तु ततः कर्णे योधेषु मुदितेषु च।॥ चचाल पृथिवी राजन् ववाश च सुविस्तरम्।
en: When Karna went all the soldiers, were filled with joy. The earth, O king, trembled and created a loud noise.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: निःसरन्तौ व्यद्दश्यन्त सूर्यात् सप्त महाग्रहाः॥ उल्कापाताश्च संजजुदिशां दाहास्तथैव च। शुष्काशन्यश्च सम्पेतुर्ववुर्वाताश्च भैरवाः॥
en: All the great planets including the sun seemed moving about. And the meteors were seen blazing up all the quarters. Cloudless thunders fell and fierce winds blew.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: मृगपक्षिगणाश्चैव पृतनां बहुशस्तव। अपसव्यं तदा चक्रुर्वेदयन्तो महाभयम्॥
en: A large number of animals and birds, kept to the right of your army and emitted noise foreboding a dreadful calamity.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: प्रथितस्य च कर्णस्य निपेतुस्तुरगा भुवि। अस्थिवर्षं च पतितमन्तरिक्षाद् भयानकम्॥
en: After the departure of Karna his horses trembled down on earth. And a dreadful shower of bones fell from the sky.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: जज्वलुश्चैव शस्त्राणि ध्वजाश्चैव चकम्पिरे। अश्रूणि च व्यमुञ्चन्त वाहनानि विशाम्पते॥
en: O king, their weapons were as if burning and the flags were trembling. And the horses shed tears.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: एते चान्ये च बहव उत्पातास्तत्र दारुणाः। समुत्येतुर्विनाशाय कौरवाणां सुदारुणाः॥
en: Those and other dreadful portends appeared there presaging the destruction of the Kauravas. Stupefied by Destiny they paid no attention of them.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: न च तान् गणयामासुः सर्वे दैवेन मोहिताः। प्रस्थितं सूतपुत्रं च जयेत्यूचुर्नराधिपाः। निर्जितान् पाण्डवाश्चैव मेनिरे तत्र कौरवाः॥
en: Seeing the departure of the charioteer's son all the king cried out victory. The Kauravas then thought that the Pandavas had been defeated.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: ततो रथस्थः परवीरहन्ता भीष्मद्रोणावस्तवीर्यो समीक्ष्य। समज्ज्वलन् भास्करपावकाभो वैकर्तनोऽसौ रथकुञ्जरो नृप॥
en: The king Vikartana, the subduer of hostile heroes and the foremost of car-warriors, stood on the car, thinking of the death of Bhishma and Drona. He shone there like the sun of fire.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: स शल्यमाभाष्य वाक्यं पार्थस्य कर्मातिशयं विचिन्त्य। मानेन दर्पण विदह्यमानः क्रोधेन दीप्यनिव निःश्वसंश्च॥
en: Thinking of the powerful feats of Arjuna, elated with self conceit and pride, worked up with anger and breathing hot and hard, said to Shalya-

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: नाहं महेन्द्रादपि वज्रपाणे: क्रुद्धाद् बिभेम्यायुधवान् रथस्थः। नतीव मां ह्यस्थिरता जहाति॥
en: When I am with my bow I do not fear even the angry Mahendra with thunder-bolt in his hand. Beholding Bhishma and other leading heroes lying on the battle field I do not feel the least anxiety.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: महेन्द्रविष्णुप्रतिमावनिन्दतौ रथाश्वनागप्रवरप्रमाथिनौ। स्ततो न मेऽप्यस्ति रणे साध्वसम्॥
en: Seeing the immaculate Bhishma and Drona equal to Indra and Vishnu, the grinders of the best of cars, elephants and horses and who are not to be killed by any, slain by the enemy I do not feel any fear in battle today.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: समीक्ष्य संख्येऽतिबलान् नराधिपान् ससूतमातङ्गरथान् परैर्हतान्। कथं न सर्वानहितान् रणेऽवधीद् महास्त्रविद् ब्राह्मणपुङ्गवो गुरुः॥
en: Well-versed in the use of powerful weapons and himself the foremost of Brahmanas why did not the preceptor kill in battle all the enemies who killed the most powerful of our hero with their drivers, elephants and chariots?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: स संस्मरन् द्रोणमहं महाहवे ब्रवीमि सत्यं कुरवो निबोधत। न वा मदन्यः प्रसहेद् रणेऽर्जुनं समागतं मृत्युमिवोग्ररूपिणम्॥
en: Listen to me, O Karna, I tell you the truth, thinking of this Drona in battle that there is none amongst you excepting myself who can withstand the advancing Arjuna the heroes who resembled the most dreadful Regent of Death.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: शिक्षाप्रमादश्च बलं धृतिश्च द्रोणे महास्त्राणि च संनतिश्च। स चेदगान्मृत्युवशं महात्मा सर्वानन्यानातुरानद्य मन्ये॥
en: In Drona were skill, practice, strength, patience, the greatest of weapons and policy. While that high-souled one has come by death I think all others, shorn of strength, on the point of death.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: नेह ध्रुवं किंचिदपि प्रचिन्तयन् विद्यां लोके कर्मणो नित्ययोगात्। सूर्योदये को हि विमुक्तसंशयो भावं कुर्वीताद्य गुरौ निपातिते॥
en: Even on reflection I do not find any thing perinanent in this world on account of the eternal connection of acts. When the preceptor himself is no more who can expect that he will surely live till even today's sun-rise.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: न नूनमस्त्राणि बलं पराक्रमः क्रियाः सुनीतं परमायुधानि वा। अलं मनुष्यस्य सुखाय वर्तितुं तथा हि युद्धे निहतः परैर्गुरुः॥
en: While preceptor has been slain in battle by the enemies, weapons, strength, prowess, actions and wise policy cannot forsooth conduce to the happiness of a man.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: हुताशनदित्यसमानतेजसं पराक्रमे विष्णुपुरन्दरोपमम्। नये बृहस्पत्युशनोः सदा समं न चैनमस्त्रं तदुपास्त दुःसहम्॥
en: In energy Drona equaled the sun or firc; in prowess he was like Vishnu or Indra, in policy he was like Vrihaspati or Ushanas; invincible though he was even weapons could not protect him.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: सम्प्राक्रुष्टे रुदितस्त्रीकुमारे पराभूते पौरुषे धार्तराष्ट्र। मया कृत्यमिति जानामि शल्य प्रयाहि तस्माद् द्विषतामनीकम्॥
en: Our women and children are weeping and bewailing, the manliness of the sons of Dhritarashtra has been defeated. I know therefore, O Shalya, that it is I who am to fight; proceed therefore against the array of our enemies.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: यत्र राजा पाण्डवः सत्यसंधो व्यवस्थितो भीमसेनार्जुनौ चा वासुदेवः सात्यकिः सृजायाश्च यमौ च कस्तान् विषहेन्मदन्यः॥
en: Save me who can withstand the army in the midst of which in the truthful Pandavas king Bhimasena, Arjuna, Vasudeva, Satyaki, Srinjaya and the twins.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: तस्मात् क्षिप्रं मद्रपते प्रयाहि रणे पञ्चालान् पाण्डवान् सृञ्जयांश्च। तान् वा हनिष्यामि समेत्य संख्ये यास्यामि वा द्रोणपथा यमाय॥
en: Therefore, O king of Madra, move on quickly in this battle towards the Panchalas, Pandavas and Srinjayas. Encountering them either I will kill them or will myself go to the abode of death by the road followed by Drona.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: न त्वेवाहं न गमिष्यामि मध्ये तेषां शूराणामिति मां शल्य विद्धि। मित्रद्रोहो मर्षणीयो न मेऽयं त्यक्त्वा प्राणाननुयास्यामि द्रोणम्॥
en: Do not think, O Shalya, that I will not enter into the heart of their army. I cannot tolerate such dissension's amongst the kith and kin. I will even follow Drona, renouncing my life.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: प्राज्ञस्य मूढस्य च जीवितान्ते नास्ति प्रमोक्षोऽन्तकसत्कृतस्य। अतो विद्वन्नभियास्यामि पार्थान् दिष्टं न शक्यं व्यतिवर्तितुं वै॥
en: A wise man or an ignorant person, none can escape death, when the lease of his life expires. Therefore, O learned one. I shall proceed against Partha. I cannot transgress my destiny.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: कल्याणवृत्तः सततं हि राजा वैचित्रवीर्यस्य सुतो ममासीत्। तस्यार्थसिद्ध्यर्थमहं त्यजामि प्रियान भोगान् दुस्त्यजं जीवितं च॥
en: O king, the son of Chitravirya's son always does me good. For the accomplishment of his object I will give up this dear life which it is very difficult to renounce.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: वैयाघ्रचर्माणमकूजनाक्षं हैमत्रिकोषं रजतत्रिवेणुम्। युक्तं प्रादान्मह्यमिमं हि रामः॥
en: Rama conferred upon me this best of cars covered with tiger-skins, with axle producing no sound, equipped with a golden seat, having trivenu made of silver and drawn by best of horses.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: धनूंषि चित्राणि निरीक्ष्य शल्य ध्वजान् गदाः सायकांचोग्ररूपान्। असिं च दीप्तं परमायुधं च शङ्ख च शुभं स्वनवन्तमुग्रम्॥
en: Behold, O Shalya, these beautiful bows, these, flags, these maces, these dreadful arrows, this shinning sword, this powerful weapon this white conch of dreadful and loud blare.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: पताकिनं वज्रनिपातनि:स्वनं सिताश्वयुक्तं शुभतूणशोभितम्। इमं समास्थाय रथं स्थर्षभं रणे हनिष्याम्यहमर्जुनं बलात्॥
en: Mounted upon this chariot with banners, its wheels producing a sound like that of a thunderbolt drawn by white horses and adorned with beautiful quivers I shall, with all my mighty, destroy that best of car-warriors, Arjuna.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: तं चेन्मृत्युः सर्वहरोऽभिरक्षेत् सदाप्रमत्तः समरे पाण्डुपुत्रम्। तं वा हनिष्यामि रणे समेत्य यास्यामि वा भीष्ममुखो यमाय॥
en: Even if death himself the destroyer of all, protects vigilantly the son of Pandu, in battle I will either kill him or go myself to the abode of death following Bhishma.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: यमवरुणकुबेरवासवा वा यदि युगपत्सगणा महाहवे। जुगुपिषव इहैत्य पाण्डवं किमु बहुना सह तैर्जयामि तम्॥
en: If Yama, Varuna, Kubera and Vasava with all their followers come here and unitedly protect the son of Pandu in battle, I will even then defeat himn with them all. What is the use of speaking more?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: संजय उवाच स्तदुत निशम्यवचः स मद्रराट्। अवहमदवपन्य वीर्यवान् प्रतिषिषिधे च जगाद चोत्तरम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing those words of Karna who was delighted at the prospect of the battle, the powerful king of Madras laughed him and said the following to check him.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: शल्य उवाच दतिरभसोऽप्यतिवाचमुक्तवान्। क्व च हि नरवरो धनंजयः क्व पनरहो पुरुषाधमो भवान्॥
en: Do not brag thus, do not brag thus, O Karna; you are so much transported with joy that you are speaking what you should not do. Who is that Dhananjaya, the best of men and who again are you the vilest of men?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: यदुसदनमुपेन्द्रपालितं त्रिधशमिवामरराजरक्षितम्। प्रसभमतिरिलोड्य को हरेत् पुरुषवरावरजामृतेऽर्जुनात्॥
en: Who else save him the foremost of men (Arjuna) could carry away by force the younger sister of Keshava, having made a confusion in the capital of Yadus that was protected by the younger brother of Indra and that resembled the celestial region protected by the king of gods.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: त्रिभुवनविभुमीश्वरं क इह पुमान भवमाह्वयेद् युधि। मृगवधकलहे ऋतेऽर्जुनात् सुरपतिवीर्यसमप्रभावतः॥
en: Who else save, Arjuna, powerful like the king of gods, could on the occasion of a quarrel brought about by the slaughter of an animal summon Bhaba, the lord of lords, the creator of the worlds, to battle?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: असुरसुरमहोरगान् नरान् गरुडपिशाचसयक्षराक्षसान्। इषुभिरजयदग्निगौरवात् स्वभिलषितं च हविर्ददौ जयः॥
en: To honor the god of fire Jaya, (Arjuna) vanquished the Asuras, gods, great snakes, men, birds, Pishacas, Yakshas and Rakshasas with his arrow and gave him the food he wanted.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: स्मरसि ननु यदा परैर्हतः स च धृतराष्ट्रसुतोऽपि मोक्षितः। दिनकरसदृशैः शरोत्तमैर्युधा कुरुषु बहून् विनिहत्य तानरीन्॥
en: Do you remember, O Karna, the occasion when killing the large nuinber of enemies with this arrows effulgent like the sun Arjuna liberated the son of Dhritarashtra himself among the Kurus?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: प्रथममपि पलायिते त्वयि प्रियकलहा धृतराष्ट्रसूनवः। स्मरसि ननु यदा प्रमोचिताः खचरगणानवजित्य पाण्डवैः॥
en: Do you remember the occasion when you yourself were the first to take to your heels and the Pandavas, having defeated the Gandharvas headed by Chitraratha, liberated the quarrelsome sons of Dhritarashtra?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: समुदितबलवाहनाः पुनः पुरुषवरेण जिताः स्थ गोग्रहे। सगुरुगुरुसुताः सभीष्मकाः किमु न जितः स तदा त्वयाऽर्जुनः॥
en: When Virata's kine were seized by them, the Kauravas, overwhelining in number both as regards men and animals and having the preceptor, the preceptor's son and Bhishma amongst them, were defeated by that foremost of men. Why did you not defeat Arjuna then?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: स्तव निधनाय सुयुद्धमद्य वै। यदि न रिपुभयात् पलायसे समरगतोऽद्य हतोऽसि सूतज॥
en: Another battle has presented itself today for your destruction. If you do not fly from the battle in fear of your enemies you will be killed, O charioteer's son, as soon as you will go to the battle.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: संजय उवाच इति बहु परुषं प्रभाषति प्रमनसि मद्रपती रिपुस्तवम्। भृशमभिरुषितः परंतपः कुरुपृतनापतिराह मद्रपम्॥
en: Sanjaya said When the king of Madra was thus, in all sincerity, addressing these harsh words to him and singing the glories of his enemy, that slayer of foes, the commander of the Kuru army, excited with anger, said.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: कर्ण उवाच भवतु भवतु कि विकत्यसे ननु मम तस्य हि युद्धमुद्यतम्। यदि स जयति मानिहाहवे तत इदमस्तु सुकस्थितं तव॥
en: Karna said Let it be so. Why do you praise Arjuna so much. A battle will soon take place between him and me. If he defeats me in battle then your praises will be considered as well said.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: संजय उवाच एवमस्त्विति मद्रेश उक्त्वा नोत्तरमुक्तवान्। याहि शल्येति चाप्येनं कर्णः प्राह युयुत्सया॥ स रथः प्रययौ शत्रूश्वेताश्वः शल्यसारथिः। निघ्नन्नमित्रान् समरे तमो घ्नन् सविता यथा॥
en: Sanjaya said The king of Madra said-'let it be so,' and gave no reply, when Karna desirous of fighting, said to Shalya 'go'. Then that carwarrior, having white horses and Shalya as his driver, dashed against his enemies killing a number of enemies in battle like the sun destroying darkness.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya on the eve of the battle
sn: ततः प्रायात् प्रीतिमान् वै रथेन वैया ण श्वेतयुजाथ कर्णः। स चालोक्य ध्वजिनी पाण्डवानां धनंजयं त्वरया पर्यपृच्छत्॥
en: Then in that car covered with tiger-skins and white horses yoked to it, Karna went on cheerfully. And seeing the armies of the Pandavas he immediately inquired after Arjuna.

sn: संजय उवाच प्रयाणे च ततः कर्णो हर्षयन् वाहिनीं तवा एकैकं समरे दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवान् पर्यपृच्छत॥
en: Sanjaya said After Karna, gladdening your army, had started for battle he addressed to every Pandava soldier he met with these harsh words.

sn: यो मामद्य महात्मानं दर्शयेच्छवेतवाहनम्। तस्मै दद्यामभिप्रेतं धनं यन्मनसेच्छति॥
en: I shall give him whatever riches he will want who will point out to me today the highsouled (Arjuna) of white horses.

sn: न चेत् तदभिमन्येत तस्मै दद्यामहं पुनः। शकटं रत्नसम्पूर्ण यो मे ब्रूयाद् धनंजयम्॥
en: I shall further more confer upon him, if he is not satisfied, a cart-load of jewels who will tell me where Dhananjaya is.

sn: न चेत्तदभिमन्येत पुरुषोऽर्जुनदर्शिवान्। शतं दद्यां गवां तस्मै नैत्यकं कांस्यदोहनम्॥
en: If the person who will point out Arjuna be not contented with it, I shall give him a hundred kine with an equal number of brass vessels for milching them.

sn: शतं ग्रामवरांश्चैव दद्यामर्जुनदर्शिने। तथा तस्मै पुनर्दद्यां श्वेतमस्वतरीरथम्॥ युक्तमञ्जनकेशीभिर्यो मे ब्रूयाद् धनंजयम्।
en: I will confer one hundred prosperous villages upon the man who will find out Arjuna for w. I will also give him who will point out Arjuna a number of damsels having long tresses and black eyes and a car drawn by white mules.

sn: न चेत् तदभिमन्येत पुरुषोऽर्जुनदर्शिवान्॥ अन्यं वास्मै पुनर्दद्यां सौवर्णं हस्तिषड्गवम्। तथाप्यस्मै पुनर्दद्यां स्त्रीणां शतमलंकृतम्॥ श्यामानां निष्ककण्ठीनां गीतवाद्यविपश्चिताम्।
en: If the person, who will point out Arjuna, be not contented with it I shall give him another best of cars made of gold and drawn by six bulls as large as elephants. I shall furthermore confer upon him one hundred well-adorned females wearing golden necklaces, fair and accomplished in singing and dancing.

sn: न चेत् तदभिमन्येत पुरुषोऽर्जुनदर्शिवान्॥ तस्मै दद्यां शतं नागाशतं ग्रामाञ्शतं रथान्। सुवर्णस्य च मुख्यस्य हयाग्र्याणां शतं शतान्॥ ऋद्धया गुणैः सुदान्तांश्च धुर्यवाहान् सुशिक्षितान्।
en: If the person, who will point out Arjuna, be not contented with it I shall give him a hundred clephants, a hundred villages, a hundred golden cars, ten thousand horses of most superior breed, fat, docile, gifted with other qualities, capable of dragging cars and well-trained.

sn: तथा सुवर्णशृङ्गीणां गोधेनूनां चतुःशतम्॥ दद्यां तस्मै सवत्सानां यो मे ब्रूयाद् धनंजयम्।
en: I shall also give the person who will point out Arjuna four hundred kine, each with golden horns and her calf.

sn: चैत तदभिमन्येत पुरुषोऽर्जुनदर्शिवान्।॥ अन्यदस्मै वरं दद्यां श्वेतान् पञ्चशतान् हयान्। हेमभाण्डपरिछन्नान् सुमृष्टमणिभूषणान्॥
en: If the person, who will find out Arjuna for me, be not satisfied with it i shall give him a more valuable present, namely five hundred horses-with gold trappings and jewelled ornaments.

sn: सुदान्तानपि चैवाहं दद्यामष्टादशापरान्। रथं च शुभ्रं सौवर्णं दद्यां तस्मै स्वलंकृतम्॥ युक्तं परमकाम्बोजैर्यो मे ब्रूयाद् धनंजयम्।
en: I shall also give him eighteen other tame horses. I shall give him, who will point out Arjuna to me, a golden car adorned with various ornaments and drawn by best Kamboja horses.

sn: न चेत् तदभिमन्येत पुरुषोऽर्जुनदर्शिवान्॥ अन्यदस्मै वरं दद्यां कुञ्जराणां शतानि षट्। काञ्चनैर्विविधैर्भाण्डैराच्छन्नान् हेममालिनः॥ उत्पन्नानपरान्तेषु विनीतान् हस्तिशिक्षकैः।
en: If the person showing Arjuna to me considers it again inchoate reward, I will give him some more precious wealth. I will offer him six hundred elephants decorated with different gold ornaments and garlands who have born in the western border of India and suffice training given by the expert Mahavatas.

sn: न चेत् तदभिमन्येत पुरुषोऽर्जुनदर्शिवान्॥ अन्यदस्मै वरं दद्यां वैश्यग्रामांश्चतुर्दश। सुरफीतान् धनसंयुक्तान् प्रत्यासन्नवनोदकान्। अकुतोभयान् सुसम्पन्नान् राजभोज्यांश्चतुर्दश॥
en: In case that person still considers it inchoate reward, I will give him another wealth more previous than the above. I will grant him ownership of fourteen prosperous and fertile villages equipped with facilities of water and forest in adjacent areas and where fear and discomfort any kind is not existed. These fourteen villages will prosperous and filled with kingly luxuries.

sn: दासीनां निष्ककण्ठीनां मागधीनां शतं तथा। प्रत्यग्रवयसां दद्यां यो मे ब्रूयाद् धनंजयम्॥
en: I will offer in gift on hundred young maids from Magadha state, well dressed and with gold garlands to the man who will tell me whereabouts of Arjuna.

sn: न चेत् तदभिमन्येन पुरुषोऽर्जुनदर्शिवान्। अन्यं तस्मै वरं दद्यां यमसौ कामयेत् स्वयम्॥ दद्यामहं यो मे
en: If the person producing Arjuna is yet consider it insufficient, I shall grace him with another thing for which he should ask himself.

sn: पुत्रदारान् विहारांश्च यदन्यद् वित्तमस्ति मे। तय तस्मै पुनर्दद्या यद् यच मनसेच्छति॥
en: I will give him all that wished by him and had in my possession whether wife, son, the garden and parks including clubs and whatever is with me in term of wealth and prosperity.

sn: हत्वा च सहितौ कृष्णौ तयोर्वित्तानि सर्वशः। तस्मै प्रबूयात् केशवार्जुनौ॥
en: I shall give him who will find out Keshava and Arjuna all the riches that will be left by them after slaying these two.

sn: एता वाचः सुबहुश: कर्ण उच्चारयन् युधि। दध्मौ सागरसम्भूतं सुखरं शङ्खमुत्तमम्॥
en: Having expressed himself thus in the battle Karna blew his excellent conch sea-born and making sweet blare.

sn: ता वाचः सूतपुत्रस्य तथा युक्ता निशम्य तु। दुर्योधनो महाराज संदृष्टः सानुगोऽभवत्।॥
en: Hearing the words of the charioteer's son, which seemed proper to him, the great king Duryodhana, with all his followers, became filled with delight.

sn: ततो दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषो मृदङ्गानां च सर्वशः। सिंहनादः सवादिनः कुञ्जराणां च निःस्वनः॥ प्रादुरासीत् तदा राजन् सैन्येषु पुरुषर्षभ। योधानां सम्प्रहृष्टानां तथा समभवत् स्वनः॥
en: Then there arose in the midst of the army, O king, O foremost, of men, the beat of cymbals and druirs, leonine roars of the elephants and the sounds of the various musical instruments as well as war-cries of the heroes filled with joy.

sn: तथा प्रहृष्टे सैन्ये तु प्लवमानं महारथम्। विकत्थमानं च तदा राधेयमरिकर्षणम्। मद्रराज प्रहस्येदं वचनं प्रत्यभाषत।॥
en: When the Kuru ariny was thus filled with joy the king of Madra said in derision the following words to the subduer of foes, the son of Radha, the powerful car-warrior who was thus bragging and about to plunge himself into that ocean of battle.

sn: शल्य उवाच मा सूतपुत्र दानेन सौवर्णं हस्तिषड्वम्। प्रयच्छ पुरुषायाद्य द्रक्ष्यसि त्वं धनंजयम्॥
en: Shalya said O son of a charioteer, give away to any man a golden car with six bulls as large as the elephants you will see Dhananjaya today.

sn: बाल्यदिह त्वं त्यजसि वसु वैश्रवणो यथा) अयत्नेनैव राधेय द्रष्टास्यद्य धनजयम्॥
en: Foolishly you are giving away your wealth as if you are Vaisravana, the king of riches. Without any trouble, O son of Radha, you will see Dhananjaya today.

sn: परान् सृजसि यद् वित्तं किंचित्त्वं बहु मूढवत्। अपात्रदाने ये दोषास्तान् मोहान्नावबुध्यसे॥
en: You are giving away your riches as if they are nothing like a highly ignorant man. You do not out of ignorance perceive the demerit attached to gifts made to unworthy persons.

sn: यत् त्वं प्रेरयसे वित्तं बहु तेन शक्यं बहुविधैर्यज्ञैर्यष्टुं सूतं यजस्व तैः॥
en: You may perform many Yajnas with the immense wealth that you are thus distributing. Therefore, O charioteer's son, do you perform Yajnas.

sn: यच प्रार्थयसे हन्तुं कृष्णौ मोहाद् वृथैव तत्। न हि शुश्रुम सम्मः क्रोष्ट्रा सिंहौ निपातितौ॥
en: But vain is the desire that you cherish out of folly, for destroying Krishna and Arjuna. We have never heard of a couple of lions overthrown by a fox.

sn: अप्रार्थितं प्रार्थयसे सुहृदो न हि सन्ति ते। ये त्वां निवारयन्त्याशु प्रपतन्तं हुताशने॥ खलु त्वया।
en: You seek what you should never do. You have no such friends as will prevent you form immediately falling into fire.

sn: कार्याकार्यं न जानीघे कालपक्वोऽस्यसंशयम्। बह्वबद्धमकर्णीयं को हि ब्रूयाजिजीविषुः॥
en: You are unable to distinguish between what you should do and should not. Forsooth, the lease of your life has run out. What man, desirous of living, would give vent to such incoherent words unworthy of being listened to.

sn: समुद्रतरणं दो• कण्ठे बद्ध्वा यथा शिलाम्। गिर्यग्राद् वा निपतनं ताद्दक् तव चिर्कीर्षितम्॥
en: This your attempt is like that of a person, who, having tied round his neck a heavy stone, wishes to cross the ocean with his two arms or like that of a man who wishes to leap down from the summit of a mountain.

sn: सहित: सर्वयोधैस्त्वं व्यूढानीकैः सुरक्षितः। धनंजयेन युध्यस्व श्रेयश्चेत् प्राप्तुमिच्छसि॥
en: If you wish to secure your well-being, fight with Dhananjaya from the division of your own army well protected and aided by your warriors.

sn: हितार्थं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य ब्रवीमि त्वां न हिंसया। श्रद्धस्वैवं मया प्रोक्तं यदि तेऽस्ति जिजीविषा॥
en: I tell you this for the well-being of Duryodhana and not out of any ill will for you. If you wish to preserve your life obey my words.

sn: कर्ण उवाच स्वबाहुवीर्यमाश्रित्य प्रार्थयाम्यर्जुनं रणे। त्वं तु मित्रमुखः शत्रुर्मा भीषयितुमिच्छसि॥
en: Karna said Depending on the strength of my own arms I wish to meet Arjuna in battle. You are an enemy with the look of a friend and wish to frighten me.

sn: न मामस्मादभिप्रायात् कश्चिदद्य निवतये । अपीन्द्रो वज्रमुद्यम्य किमु मर्त्यः कचन॥
en: No one will be able to make me change this resolution, not even Indra taking up his thunderbolt, what to speak of an insignificant mortal?

sn: संजय उवाच इति कर्णस्य वाक्यान्ते शल्यः प्राहोत्तरं वचः। चुकोपयिषुरत्यर्थं कर्ण मद्रेश्वरः पुनः॥
en: Sanjaya said After Karna had his say, Shalya the king of Madra, with a view to provoke him greatly, said in reply.

sn: यदा वै त्वां फाल्गुनवेगयुक्ता ज्याचोदिता हस्तवता विसृष्टाः। स्तदा तप्स्यर्जुनस्यानुयोगात्॥
en: When keen edged and Kanka feathered arrows, shot off his bow. by the powerful Phalguna with all his energy, will come upon you, you will repent for your encounter with that hero.

sn: यदा दिव्यं धनुरादाय पार्थः प्रतापयन् पृतनां सव्यमाची। स्तदा पश्चात् तप्स्यसे सूतपित्र॥
en: When Partha, otherwise called Savyasachin, taking up his celestial bow, will scorch the Kuru army and assail you greatly with his keen edged arrows then O charioteer's son, you will repent for your folly.

sn: बालश्चन्द्रं मातुरङ्के शयानो यथा कश्चित् प्रार्थयतेऽपहर्तुम्। तद्वन्मोहाद् द्योतमान रथस्थं सम्प्रार्थयस्यर्जुनं जेतुमद्य॥
en: Like a child, on mother's lap seeking to catch hold of the sun, you, out of your folly, wish to defect the effulgent Arjuna stationed on his car.

sn: त्रिशूलमाश्रित्य सुतीक्ष्णधारं सर्वाणि गात्राणि विघर्षसि त्वम्। सुतीक्ष्णधारोपमकर्मणा त्वं युयुत्ससे योऽर्जुनेनाद्य कर्ण॥
en: By desiring to fight, O Karna, today with Arjuna of illustrious feats, you have addressed yourself to rule your body against the keen edges of a trident.

sn: क्रुद्धं सिंह केसरिणं बृहन्तं बालो मूढः क्षुद्रमृगस्तरस्वी। समाह्वयेत् तद्वदेतत् तवाद्य समाह्वानं सूतपुत्रार्जुनस्य॥
en: O charioteer's son, your challenge of Arjuna is like that of an over active little deer against a huge angry lion.

sn: मा सूतपुत्रालय राजपुत्रं महावीर्यं केसरिणं यथैव। वने शृगाल: पिशितेन तृप्तो मा पार्थमासाद्य विनश्यसि त्वम्॥
en: O charioteer's son, do not challenge that highly energetic prince like a fox, gratified with meat, challenging a lion. Do not be slain by encountering Arjuna.

sn: ईषादन्तं महानागं प्रभिन्नकरटामुखम्। शशको ह्वयसे युद्ध कर्ण पार्थं धनंजयम्॥
en: O Karna, your challenge of Dhananjaya, the son of Pritha, is like that of a hare challenging a powerful elephant with tusks large as ploughshares and with temporal juice trickling out of its mouth and temples.

sn: विलस्थं कृष्णसर्प त्वं बाल्यात् काष्ठेन विध्यसि। महाविषं पूर्णकोपं यत् पार्थं योद्धुमिच्छसि॥
en: By wishing to fight with Partha you are, out of folly, striking with a piece of wood the black cobra of deadly venom furiously excited within its hole.

sn: सिंह केसरिणं क्रुद्धमतिक्रम्याभिनर्दसे। शृगाल इव मूढस्त्वं नृसिंह कर्ण पाण्डवम्॥
en: You are a fool to yell at Arjuna, the best of men, disregarding him like a jackal yelling at an excited lion.

sn: सुपर्णं पतगश्रेष्ठ वैनतेयं तरस्विनम्। भोगीवाह्वयसे पाते कर्ण पार्थं धनंजयम्॥
en: As a snake, for its own destruction, encounters the best of birds Garuda, highly active and of beautiful feathers, so do you O Karna, challenge Dhananjaya the son of Pritha.

sn: सर्वाम्भसां निधि भीमं मूर्तिमन्त झषायुतम्। चन्द्रोदये विवर्धन्तमप्लव: सन् तितीर्षसि॥
en: You wish to cross, without a raft at the rise of the moon, the ocean, the receptacle of all waters with dreadful huge waves and teeming with aquatic animals.

sn: ऋषभं दुन्दुभिग्रीवं तीक्ष्णशृङ्गं प्रहारिणम्। वत्स आह्वयसे युद्धे कर्ण पार्थं धनंजयम्॥
en: O Karna, your challenge of Dhananjaya is like that of a calf against a fearful bull of sharpened horns and with a neck thick as a drum.

sn: महामेघं महाघोरं दर्दुरः प्रतिनर्दसि। कामतोयप्रदं लोके नरपर्जन्यमर्जुनम्॥
en: Your roaring at Arjuna, the deity of clouds among men, like that of frog at a dreadful huge cloud discharging copious showers of rain.

sn: यथा च स्वगृहस्थः श्वा व्याघ्रं वनगतं भषेत्। तथा त्वं भषसे कर्ण नरव्याघ्रं धनंजयम्॥
en: Like a dog barking from within his master's house at a forest-ranging tiger you bark at Dhananjaya, the foremost of men.

sn: शृगालोऽपि वने कर्ण शशैः परिवृतो वसन्। मन्यते सिंहमात्मानं यावत् सिंह न पश्यति॥
en: While living in the forest in the midst of hares a jackal, O Karna, considers himself a lion till he actually sees the latter.

sn: तथा त्वमपि राधेय सिंहमात्मानमिच्छसि। अपश्यशत्रुदमनं नरव्याघ्र धनंजयम्॥
en: So do you, O son of Radha, consider yourself a lion for you do not see that subduer of foes, that foremost of men, Dhananjaya.

sn: व्यानं त्वं मन्यसेऽऽत्मानं यावत् कृष्णौ न पश्यसि। समास्थितावेकरथे सूर्याचन्द्रमसाविव॥
en: You consider yourself a lion for you have not seen Krishna and Arjuna stationed on the same car like the sun and moon.

sn: यावद् गाण्डीवघोषं त्वं न शृणोषि महाहवे। तावदेव त्वया कर्ण शक्यं वक्तुं यथेच्छसि॥
en: As long as you do not hear the twang of Gandiva in battle, so long you are able to do what you please.

sn: रथशब्दधनुः शब्दैर्नादयन्त दिशो दश। नर्दन्तमिव शार्दूलं दृष्ट्वा क्रोष्टा भविष्यसि॥
en: Beholding the ten quarters filled with the sound of his car and the twang of his bow and him roaring like a tiger you will become a jackal.

sn: नित्यमेव शृगालस्तवं नित्यं सिंहो धनंजयः। वीरप्रद्वेषणान्मूढ तस्मात् क्रोष्टेव लक्ष्यसे॥
en: You are always a jackal and Dhananjaya always a lion. On account of your envy and hatred for heroes, you appear a jackal.

sn: यथाखुःस्याद् विडालश्च व्याघ्रश्च बलाबले। यथा शृगाल: सिंहश्च यथा च शशकुञ्जरौ॥ यथानृतं च सत्यं च यथा चापि विषामृते। तथा त्वमपि पार्थश्च प्रख्यातावात्मकर्मभिः॥
en: As a mouse and a cat are to each other in strength, or a fox and a lion or a hare and an elephant, as falsehood and truth, ambrosia and poison so you and Partha are known to all by your respective deeds.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: संजय उवाच अधिक्षिप्तस्तु राधेय शल्येनामिततेजसा। शल्यमाह सुसंक्रुद्धो वाक्शल्यमवधारयन्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus reviled by Shalya of incomparable energy the son of Radha understanding the meaning of the word Shalya by his words said to him in areat anger.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: कर्ण उवाच गुणान् गुणवतां शल्य गुणवान् वेत्ति नागुणः। त्वं तु शल्य गुणैर्हीनः किं ज्ञास्यसि गुणागुणम्॥
en: Karna said O Shalya, the meritorious only appreciate the merits of those who possess them and not one who has none. You are destitute of all merits. How can you understand what is merit and what is demerit.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: अर्जुनस्य महास्त्राणि क्रोधं वीर्य धनुः शरान्। अहं शल्याभिजानाभि विक्रमं च महात्मनः॥
en: O Shalya, I know that powerful weapons of Arjuna, his anger, energy, bow, arrows and as well as the prowess of that high-souled one.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: तथा कृष्णस्य महात्म्यमृषभस्य महीक्षिताम्। यथाहं शल्य जानामि न त्वं जानासि तथा॥
en: O Shalya, you do not know, so well as I do, the greatness of Krishna, the foremost of kings.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: एवमेवात्मनो वीर्यमहं वीर्यं च पाण्डवे। जाननेवाह्वये युद्धे शल्य गाण्डीवधारिणम्॥
en: Knowing my own strength as well as that of Pandava I have challenged him in battle, O Shalya, I shall not fall into fire like an insect.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: अस्ति वाऽयमिषुः शल्य सुपुङ्खो रक्तभोजनः। एकतूणीशयः पत्री सुधौत: समलंकृतः॥
en: I have this arrow, O Shalya, keen edged, blood-drinking, occupying alone one quiver, furnished with wings, well-steeped in oil and well-adorned.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: शेते चन्दनचूर्णेषु पूजितो बहुलाः समाः। आहेयो विषवानुग्रो नराश्वद्विपसंघहा॥
en: It lies in sandal dust and is being adored by me from a long time. Having the shape and nature of a serpent it is poisonous and dreadful and capable of killing a great many men, horses and elephants.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: घोररूयो महारौद्रस्तनुत्रास्थिविदारणः। निर्भिन्द्यां येन रुष्टोऽमहपि मेरुं महागिरम्॥
en: Highly dreadful in form it can go through coats of mail and bones. When worked up with anger I can perforate with it even the huge Meru mountain.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: तमहं जातु नास्येयमन्यस्मिन् फाल्गुनाहते। कृष्णाद् वा देवकीपुत्रात् सत्यं चापि शृणुष्व मे॥
en: I will not discharge this arrow at any other person excepting Arjuna or Krishna, the son of Devaki. Listen, I tell you the truth.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: तेनाहमिषुणा शल्य वासुदेवधनंजयौ। योत्स्ये परमसंक्रुद्धस्तत् कर्म सदृशं मम॥
en: Worked up with anger, I shall with that arrow, O Shalya, fight Vasudeva and Dhananjaya. That will be a deed becoming me.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: सर्वेषां वृष्टिवीराणां कृष्णे लक्ष्मी: प्रतिष्ठिता। सर्वेषां पाण्डुपुत्राणां जयः पार्थे प्रतिष्ठितः॥ उभयं तु समासाद्य को निवर्तितुमर्हति।
en: Of all the heroes of the Vrishni race in Krishna only prosperity exists eternally. Of all the sons of Pandu, Partha is the one who comes off invariable victorious.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: तावेतौ पुरुषव्याधौ समेतो स्यन्दने स्थितौ॥ मामेकमभिसंयातौ सुजातं पश्य शल्य मे।
en: Those two foremost of men, seated on the same car, will encounter me single in battle, you will, O Shalya, witness today the nobility of my birth.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: पितृष्वसा मातुलजौ भ्रातरावपराजितौ॥ मणी सूत्र इव प्रोतौ द्रष्टासि निहतौ मया।
en: You will seen that (With one shaft) I will kill those two cousins, one of whom is the son of the aunt and the other the son of the maternal uncle-those two invincible warriors. They will took like two pearls strung together in the same string

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: अर्जुने गाण्डिवं कृष्णे चक्रं तार्थ्यकपिध्वजौ॥ भीरूणां त्रासजननं शल्य हर्षकरं मम।
en: The Gandiva of Arjuna, the discus of Krishna and their two banners having the emblems of a monkey and Garuda strike terror into the timid. But they are sources of delight to me.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: त्वं तु दुष्प्रकृतिर्मूढो महायुद्धेष्वकोविदः॥ भयावदीर्ण: संत्रासादबद्धं बहु भाषसे।
en: You are a fool, a bad character and do not know the mode of a true war-fare. Possessed by fear you are giving vent to these ravings.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: संन्तौषि तौ तु केनापि हेतुना त्वं कुदेशज॥ तौ हत्वा समरे हन्ता त्वामद्य सहबान्धवम्। पापदेशज दुर्बुद्धे क्षुद्र क्षत्रियपांसन॥
en: Born in a sinful country you are wicked, mean and a wrath of a Kshatriya or you are praising them for something which is not known to me. Having killed those two first I shall kill you today with all your relatives.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: सुहृद् भूत्वा रिपुः किं मा कृष्णाभ्यां भीषयिष्यसि तौ वा मामद्य हन्तारौ हनिष्ये वापि तावहम्॥
en: Being a friend why do you frighten me with (the praises of) those two Krishnas? Either they will kill me today or I will kill them both.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: नाहं विभेमि कृष्णाभ्यां विजानन्नात्मनो बलम्। वासुदेवसहस्रं वा फाल्गुनानां शतानि वा॥ अहमेको हनिष्यामि जोषमास्स्व कुदेशज।
en: I know my strength well and I do not fear the two Krishnas. I will kill single handed a thousand Vasudevas and hundreds of Phalgunas. Hold your tongue. O you born in a sinful country.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: स्त्रियो बालाश्च वृद्धाश्च प्रायः क्रीडागता जनाः॥ या गाथाः सम्प्रगायन्ति कुर्वतोऽध्ययनं यथा। ता गाथाः शृणु मे शल्य मद्रकेषु दुरात्मसु॥ ब्राह्मणैः कथिताः पूर्वं यथावद् राजसंनिधौ। श्रुत्वा चैकमना मूढ क्षम वा ब्रूहि चोत्तरम्॥
en: Hear from me, O Shalya, the sayings that have already passed into proverbs, that men young and old and women, persons while sporting utter as if they are their studies about the wicked Madrakas. the Brahmanas also recounted them formerly in the courts of kings. Hearing them, O fool, you may forgive or give a reply.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: मित्रध्रुङ्गभद्रको नित्यं यो नो द्वेष्टि स मद्रकः। मद्रके संगतं नास्ति क्षुद्रवाक्ये नराधमे॥
en: Madraka is always a hater of friends. He who hates us is a Madraka. There is no good feeling in a Madraka who is the vilest of men and gives vent to mean words.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: दुरात्मा मद्रको नित्यं नित्यमानृतिकोऽनृजुः। यावदन्त्यं हि दौरात्म्यं मद्रकेष्विति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: The Madraka is always wicked, untruthful and crooked. We have heard that the Madrakas are wicked till the hour of their death.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: पिता पुत्रश्च माता च श्वश्रूश्वशुरमातुलाः। जामाता दुहिता भ्राता नप्तान्ये तै च बान्धवाः॥ वयस्याभ्यागताश्चान्ये दासीदासं च संगतम्। पुम्भर्विमिश्रा नार्यश्च ज्ञाताज्ञाता: स्वयेच्छा॥ येषां गृहेष्वशिष्टानां सक्तुमत्स्याशिनां तता। पीत्वा सीधु सगोमांसं क्रन्दन्ति च हसन्ति च ॥ गायन्ति चाप्यबद्धानि प्रवर्तन्ते च कामतः। कामप्रलापिनोऽन्योन्यं तेषु धर्मः कथं भवेत्॥ मद्रकेष्ववलिप्तेषु प्रख्याताशुभकर्मसु।
en: Amongst them the father, the son, the mother, the mother-in-law, the father-in-law, the maternal uncle, the son-in-law, the daughter-in-law, the brother, the grandson, other relations and guests, slaves, male and female mingle together. Thus women freely mix with men, known and unknown, Dishonest as they are they live upon friend and powered corn and fish in their homes and laugh and cry being drunk; they also eat beef. They sing unconnected songs and move about lustfully. They indulge in free speeches amongst themselves. How can virtue find a room among them?

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: नापि वैरं न सौहार्द मद्रकेण समाचरेत्॥ मद्रके संगतं नास्ति मद्रको हि सदामलः।
en: No one should inake friends with a Madraka or enter into hostilities with him. There is no feeling of friendship in him. The Madraka is always impure.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: मद्रकेषु न संसृष्टं शौचं गान्धारकेषु च॥ राजयाजकयाज्ये च नष्टं दत्तं हरिभवेत्। शूद्रसंस्कारको विप्रो यथा याति पराभवम्॥ यथा ब्रह्मद्विषो नित्यं गच्छन्तीह पराभवम्। यथैव संगतं कृत्वा नरः पतति मद्रकैः॥ मद्रके संगतं नास्ति हतं वृश्चिक ते विषम्। आथर्वणेन मन्त्रेण यथा शान्तिः कृता मया।॥
en: Friendship is lost on a Madraka as purity in Gandharakas and as oblation offered in a sacrifice where the king is both the sacrificer and the priest. As a Brahmana performing the initiation ceremony of a Sudra meets with deterioration as one who hates a Brahmana, meets with deterioration so a person, forming alliance with a Madraka, is deteriorated. As there is no friendship in a Madraka, so is your poison is powerless, O Scorpion; with this Mantra of Atharvan I have duly performed the ceremony of peace.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: इति वृश्चिकदष्टस्य विषवेगहतस्य च। कुर्वन्ति भेषजं प्राज्ञाः सत्यं तचापि दृश्यते॥
en: It is seen that with these words the wise treat a person bitten by a scorpion and affected by its poison.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: एवं विद्वजोधमास्स्व शृणु चात्रोत्तरं वचः। वासांस्युत्सृज्य नृत्यानि स्त्रियो या मद्यमोहिताः॥३५ मैथुनेऽसंयताअपि यथाकामवराश्च ताः। तासां पुत्रः कथं धर्म मद्रको वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Thinking of this, O learned one, either hold your tongue or hear something more that I will say. (The Madraka) women, influenced by liquor, throw off their robes and dance; they do not observe control in intercourse and do whatever they like. Being the son of one of those women, how can you, O Madraka, dictate duties unto a man?

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: यास्तिष्ठन्त्यः प्रमेहन्ति यथैवोष्ट्रदशेरकाः। तासां विभ्रष्टधर्माणां निर्लज्जानां ततस्ततः॥ त्वं पुत्रस्तादृशीनां हि धर्मे वक्तुमिहेच्छसि।
en: Being the son of one of those women who live and answer calls of nature like camels and asses, sinful and shameless as they are, how can you wish to dictate the duties of men?

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: सुवीरकं याच्यमाना मद्रिका कर्षति स्फिचौ॥ अदातुकामा वचनमिदं वदति दारुणम्। मा मां सुवीरकं कश्चिद् याचतां दयितं मम॥ पुत्रं दद्यां पतिं दद्यां न तु दद्याहं सुवीरकम्।
en: When a Madraka woman is requested to give a little bit of vinegar she scratches her hips and reluctant to give it gives vent to harsh words-“Let no one ask of me vinegar which is so dear to me. I would give him my son, I would give him my husband but I would not part with my vinegar.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: गौर्यो बृहत्यो निहींका मद्रिकाः कम्बलावृताः॥ घस्मरा नष्टशौचाश्च प्राय इत्यनुशूश्रुम।
en: The Madraka maidens, I am informed, are generally shameless, have profuse hairs, are gluttonous and impure.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: एवमादि मयान्यैर्वा शक्यं वक्तुं भवेद् बाहु॥ आकेशाग्रान्नखाग्राच वक्तव्येषु कुकर्मसु।
en: These and such like many other things of their evil acts beginning with the tip of their hair to that of their nails I can recount.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: मद्रकाः सिन्धुसौवीराः धर्म विद्युः कथं त्वित्॥ पापदेशोद्भवा म्लेच्छा धर्माणामविचक्षणाः।
en: The Madrakas and Sindhu Souviras are born in a sinful country, are Melechas and innocent of duties. How can they know them?

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: एष मुख्यतमो धर्मः क्षत्रियस्येति नः श्रुतम्॥ यदाजौ निहतः शेते सद्भिः समभिपूजितः।
en: We have heard that this is the prime duty of the Kshatriyas that when slain in battle he would lie down on earth being spoken highly of by the pious.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: आयुधानां साम्पराये यन्मुच्येयमहं ततः॥ ममैष प्रथमः कल्पो निधने स्वर्गमिच्छतः।
en: This is my first resolution, desirous of heaven after my death as I am that I will lay down my life in this clash of arms.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: सोऽयं प्रियः सखा चास्मि धार्तराष्ट्रस्य धीमतः॥४५ तदर्थे हि मम प्राणा यच मे विद्यते वसु। व्यक्तं त्वमप्युपहितः पाण्डवैः पापदेशज॥ यथा चामित्रवत् सर्वं त्वमस्मासु प्रवर्तसे।
en: I am the dear friend of the intelligent son of Dhritarashtra. For him are my vital airs and the wealth that I possess. As for you, born as you are in a sinful country it is clear that you have been bribed by the Pandavas as because you behave towards us in everything like an enemy.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: कामं न खलु शक्योऽहं त्वद्विधानां शतैरपि॥ संग्रामाद् विमुखः कर्तुं धर्मज्ञ इव नास्तिकैः।
en: As a pious man is not to be easily pursuaded by atheists so I am not to be dissuaded from this battle by hundreds of persons like you.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: सारङ्ग इव धर्मातः काम विलप शुष्य च॥ नाहं भीषयितुं शक्यं क्षत्रवृत्ते व्यवस्थितः।
en: Like a deer perspiring, you may either bewail or pant; observant of the duties of a Kshatriya I am incapable of being frightened by you.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: तनुत्यजां नृसिंहानामाहवेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्॥ या गतिर्गुरुणा प्रोक्ता पुरा रामेण तां स्मरे।
en: I remember the end, described to me formerly by my preceptor Rama, which befell those foremost of men who laid down their lives and did not return from the field of battle.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: तेषां त्राणार्थमुद्यन्तं वधार्थं द्विषतामपि॥ विद्धि मामास्थितं वृत्तं पौरूरवसमुत्तमम्।
en: I am bent upon rescuing the Kauravas and killing my enemies; know that I am determined upon imitating the excellent conduct of Pururavas.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: न तद् भूतं प्रपश्यामि त्रिषु लोकेषु मद्रप॥ यो मामस्मादभिप्रायाद् वारयेदिति मे मतिः।
en: I do not, O king of Madraka, see a man in the three worlds who can shake this resolution of mine.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: एवं विद्वञ्जोषमास्स्व त्रासात् किं बहु भाषसे॥ मा त्वा हत्वा प्रदास्यामि क्रव्याद्भयो मद्रकाधम।
en: Do not speak more. Knowing this Why do you rove in such a way from fear? O wretch of a Madraka, I shall not kill you now and offer your dead body to the carnivorous animals,

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: मित्रप्रतीक्षया शल्य धृतराष्ट्रस्य चोभयोः॥ अपवादतितिक्षाभिस्त्रिभिरेतैर्हि जीवसि।
en: Out of regard for a friend, O Shalya, for the sake of Dhritarashtra's son and for avoiding blame-for these three reasons, you will live.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: पुनश्चेदीदृशं वाक्यं मद्रराज वदिष्यसि॥ शिरस्ते पातयिष्यामि गदया वज्रकल्पया।
en: O king of Madras, if you speak again in this strain I will crush down your head with my mace, as hard as the thunder.

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: श्रोतारस्तिवदमोह द्रष्टारो वा कुदेशज॥ कर्णवा जघ्नतुः कृष्णौ कर्णो वा निजघान तौ।
en: O you born in a sinful country, people will either see or hear today that either the two Krishnas have slain Karna or Karna has killed the two Krishnas."

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु राधेयः पुनरेव विशाम्पते । अब्रवीन्मद्रराजानं याहि याहीत्यसम्भ्रमम्॥
en: Saying this the son of Radha, O king, once more addressed the king of Madras, saying-"go on! go on."

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: श्रोतारस्तिवदमोह द्रष्टारो वा कुदेशज॥ कर्णवा जघ्नतुः कृष्णौ कर्णो वा निजघान तौ।
en: O you born in a sinful country, people will either see or hear today that either the two Krishnas have slain Karna or Karna has killed the two Krishnas."

description: The discourse of Karna and Shalya
sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु राधेयः पुनरेव विशाम्पते । अब्रवीन्मद्रराजानं याहि याहीत्यसम्भ्रमम्॥
