en: Saying this the son of Radha, O king, once more addressed the king of Madras, saying-"go on! go on."

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: संजय उवाच मारिषाधिरथेः श्रुत्वा वाचो युद्धाभिनन्दिनः। शल्योऽब्रवीत् पुनः कर्णं निदर्शनमिदं वचः॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing the words of the great car-warrior Karna who took delight in battle Shalya again said to hiin, citing an example.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: जातोऽहं यज्वनां वंशे संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्। राज्ञां मूर्धाभिषिक्तानां स्वयं धर्मपरायणः॥
en: I am born in a family the members of which performed sacrifices, never fled away from the field of battle and who were kings whose heads were sprinkled with the water of coronation. I am also devoted to virtue.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: यथैव मत्तो मद्येन त्वं तथा लक्ष्यसे वृष। तथाऽद्य त्वां प्रमाद्यन्तं चिकित्सेयं सुहत्तया॥
en: O Vrisha, you appear like an intoxicated man. For all that, out of friendship I will try to cure you of your mistakes.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: इमां काकोपमा कर्ण प्रोच्यमानां निबोध मे। श्रुत्वा यथेष्टं कुर्यास्त्वं निहीन कुलपांसन॥
en: Hear, O Karna, this allegory of a crow that I will relate. Hearing this, you may do whatever you like, O you shorn of intelligence and the wretch of your family.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: नाहमात्मनि कंचिद् वै किल्बिषं कर्ण संस्मरे। येन मां त्वं महाबाहो हन्तुमिच्छस्यनागसम्॥
en: O Karna, I do not remember a single sin in me for which you desire to kill me innocent as I am.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: अवश्यं तु मया वाच्यं बुद्ध्यता त्वद्धिताहितम्। विशेषतो रथस्थेन राज्ञश्चैव हितैषिणा॥
en: I must tell you what is good for you and what is bad. I know both and besides I am the driver of your car and wish good to the king Duryodhana.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: समं च विषमं चैव रथिनश्च बलाबलम्। श्रमः खेदश्च सततं हयानां रथिना सह॥ आयुधस्य परिज्ञानं रुतं च मृगपक्षिणाम्। भारश्चाप्यतिभारश्च शल्यानां च प्रतिक्रिया॥ अस्त्रयोगश्च युद्धं च निमित्तानि तथैव च। सर्वमेतन्मया ज्ञेयं रथस्यास्य कुटुम्बिना॥ अतस्त्वां कथये कर्ण निदर्शनमिदं पुनः।
en: (I know) what land is even and what is uneven-the strength and weakness of the carwarrior (of my chariot) the fatigue and perspiration of the horses along with the car-warrior; (I have) a knowledge of weapons, of the cries of birds and animals, of what would be heavy for the horses and what would be exceedingly heavy for them, of the taking out of the arrows, of the wounds, of the weapons counteracting each other of the diverse modes of fighting and of all kinds of omens and indications. I know all this who am so familiar with this car. I therefore describe to you this incident once more.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: वैश्यः किल समुद्रान्ते प्रभूतधनधान्यवान्॥ यज्वा दानपति: क्षान्तः स्फकर्मस्थोऽभवच्छुचिः। बहुपुत्रः प्रियापत्यः सर्वभूतानुकम्पकः॥ राज्ञो धर्मप्रधानस्य राष्ट्रे वसति निर्भयः।
en: There lived on the other side of the sea a Vaishya who rolled in wealth and corn. He performed yajnas, made liberal gifts, was quiet, observant of the duties of his own order and pure in habits and mind.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: पुत्राणां तस्य बालानां कुमाराणां यशस्विनाम्॥ काको बहूनामभवदुच्छिष्टकृतभोजनः।
en: He had a number of sons of whom he was fond and kind to all creatures. He lived without any fear in the kingdom of a pious king.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: तस्मै सदा प्रयच्छन्ति वैश्यपुत्राः कुमारकाः॥ मांसौदन दधि क्षीरं पायसं मधुसर्पिषी।
en: There was a crow who lived upon the leavings of the well-behaved children of the Vaishya. His children always gave the crow meat, curds, mild, pudding, honey and butter.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: स चोच्छिष्टभूतः काको वैश्यपुत्रैः कुमारकैः॥ सदृशान् पक्षिणादृप्तः श्रेयसञ्चाधिचिक्षिपे।
en: Thus fed with the leavings of the food by those sons of the Vaishya the crow became arrogant and began to think light of all birds who were equal to him or even superior.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: अथ हंसाः समुद्रान्ते कदाचिदतिपातिनः॥ गरुडस्य गतौ तुल्याश्चक्राङ्गा हृष्टचेतसः।
en: It so happened that once on a time several cheerful swans, quick-coursing, capable of going every where at will, equal to Garuda in fight and speed, came to that side of the ocean.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: कुमारकास्तदा हंसान् दृष्ट्वा काकमथाब्रुवन॥ भवानेव विशिष्टो हि पतत्रिभ्यो विहङ्गम्।
en: Seeing those swans the Vaishya boys said to the crow-"O ranger of the sky, you are superior to all winged creatures."

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: प्रतार्यमाणस्तैः सर्वैरल्पबुद्धिभिरण्डजः॥ तद्वचः सत्यमित्येव मौाद् दर्पाच मन्यते।
en: Thus imposed upon by the little-witted children, the bird, out of folly and arrogance, took their words as true.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: तान् सोऽभिपत्य जिज्ञासुः क एषां श्रेष्ठभागिति॥ उच्छिष्टदर्पितः काको बहूनां दूरपातिनाम्। तेषां यं प्रवरं मेने हंसानां दूरपातिनाम्॥ तमाह्वयत दुर्बुद्धिः पताव इति पक्षिणम्।
en: Proud of the leavings on which he fed the crow, approaching the swans who were capable of traversing a great distance, desired to enquire who amongst them was the leader. That foolish crow challenged him whom he considered as the leader amongst those swans capable of going to a great distance, saying-“Let us compete in fight."

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: तच्छुत्वा प्राहसन् हंसा ये तत्रासन् समागताः॥ भाषतो बहु काकस्य बलिनः पततां वराः। इदमूचुः स्म चक्राङ्गा वचः काकं विहङ्गमाः॥
en: Hearing the words of the arrogant crow, the swans, that had come there, the foremost of birds gifted with great strength, began to laugh. The swans, who were capable of coursing everywhere at will then, addressed the crow saying.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: हंसा ऊचुः वयं हंसाश्चरामेमां पृथिवीं मानसौकसः। पक्षिणां च वयं नित्यं दूरपातेन पूजिताः॥
en: The Swans said "We are swans and live in the Manasa lake. We range over the whole earth and amongst the winged creatures we are always spoken high for the length of the distances we traverse.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: कथं हंस नु बलिनं चक्राङ्गं दूरपातिनम्। काको भूत्वा निपतने समाह्वयसि दुर्मते॥ कथं त्वं पतिता काक साहस्माभिब्रवीहि तत्।
en: A crow as you are, how do you, O fool, challenge a mighty swan coursing every where at will and traversing over a great distance. Tell us, Ocrow, how you will fly with us."

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: अथ हंसवचो मूढः कुत्सयित्वा पुनः पुनः। प्रजगादोत्तरं काकः कत्थनो जातिलाघवात्॥
en: Finding fault repeatedly with the words of the swans, the vain crow, on account of the foolishness of its species, at last gave this answer.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: काक उवाच शतमेकं च पातानां पतिताऽस्मि न संशयः। शतयोजनमेकैकं विचित्रं विविधं तथा॥
en: The crow said Forsooth shall I fly displaying a hundred and one different kinds of motion. I shall show them traversing every hundred yojanas with each separate and beautiful motion.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: उड्डीनमवडीनं च प्रडीनं डीनमेव च। निडीनमथ संडीनं तिर्यगडीनगतानि च॥ विडीनं परिडीनं च पराडीनं सुडीनकम्। अभिडीनं महाडीनं निर्डीनमतिडीनकम्॥ अवडीनं प्रडीनं च सडीनं डीनडीनकम्। संडीनोड्डीनडीनं च पुनर्जीनविडीनकम्॥ सम्पातं समुदीषं च ततोऽन्यद् व्यतिरिक्तकम्। गतागतप्रतिगतं बह्वीश्च निकुलीनकाः॥
en: Rising up, swooping down, whirling around, going straight, proceeding gently, coursing aslant up and down, going still, wheeling around, going back, sowing high, darting forward, sowing higher up with greater velocity more, moving on gently-and going on in various ways.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: कर्तास्मि मिषतां वोऽद्य ततो द्रक्ष्यथ मे बलम्। तेषामन्यतमेनाहं पतिष्यामि विहायसम्॥ प्रादिशध्वं यथान्यायं केन हंसाः पताम्यहम्।
en: These various motions I shall display before you. You will see my strength. With one of these diverse kinds of motions I shall immediately soar into the sky. Tell me, O swans, by which of these motion shall I course through the sky.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: ते वै ध्रुवं विनिश्चित्य पतध्वं न मया सह॥ पातैरेभिः खलु खगाः पतितुं खे निराश्रये।
en: Settling your course you shall have to fly with me. Adopting all these motions you shall have to course with me through the sky having no support."

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: एवमुक्ते तु काकेन प्रहस्यैको विहंगमः॥ उवाच काकं राधेय वचनं तन्निबोध मे।
en: Having been thus addressed by the crow, O son of Radha, one of the swans said to him laughing. Hear from me (what he said).

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: हंस उवाच शतमेकं च पातानां त्वं काक पतिता ध्रुवम्॥ एकमेव तु यं पातं विदुः सर्वे विहंगमाः तमहं पतिता काक नान्यं जानामि कञ्चन॥ पत त्वमपि ताम्राक्ष येन पातेन मन्यसे।
en: The Swan said Forsooth O crow, you will course in hundred and different ways. I shall however fly in one kind of motion which all other birds know; for I do not know any other, O crow. As for yourself, O you of red eyes, you may fly in any kind of way you like.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: अथ काकाः प्रजहसुर्ये तत्रासन् समागताः॥ कथमेकेन पातेन हसः पातशतं जयेत्। एकेनैव शतस्यैष पातेनाभिभविष्यति॥ हंसस्य पतितं काको बलवानाशुविक्रमः।
en: Thereupon all the crows that had assembled there laughed saying "How will the swan with one kind of flight beat down a hundred flights? The powerful and the quick-coursing crow will beat down the swan with one flight.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: प्रपेततुः स्पर्धया च ततस्तौ हंसवायसौ॥ एकपाती च चक्राङ्गः काकः पातशतेन च। पेतिवानथ चक्राङ्ग पेतिवानथ वायसः॥
en: Then those two, the swan the crow, rose into the sky challenging each other-the swan coursing in one motion and the crow in a hundred different ways. The swan flew and the crow flew.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: विसिस्मापयिषुः पातैराचक्षाणोऽऽत्मनः क्रियाः। अथ काकस्य चित्राणि पतितानि मुहुर्मुहुः॥ दृष्ट्वा प्रमुदिताः काका विनेदुरधिकैः स्वरैः।
en: Making each other to wonder and speaking highly of their respective feats. Seeing the various kinds of motions at every moment the crows that were there were filled with delight and began to caw loudly.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: हंसांश्चावहसन्ति स्म प्रावदन्नप्रियाणि च॥ उत्पत्योत्पत्य च मुहुर्मुहूर्तमिति चेति च। वृक्षाग्रेभ्यः स्थलेभ्यश्च निपतन्त्युत्पतन्ति त॥ कुर्वाणा विविधान् रावानाशंसन्तो जयं तथा।
en: The swans also laughed aloud making many unpleasant remarks. They began to rise up and alight repeatedly. They came down and rose up from the tops of the trees and the surface of the earth; they began to emit cries bespeaking their respective victories.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: हंसस्तु मृदुनैकेन विक्रान्तुमुपचक्रमे॥ प्रत्यहीयत काकाच मुहूर्तमिव मारिष।
en: With one kind of gentle motion the swan began to roar up. For a moment, O Marisha, the crow seemed to have defeated him.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: अवमन्य च हंसांस्तानिदं वचनमब्रुवन्॥ योऽसावुत्पतितो हंसः सोऽसावेवं प्रहीयते।
en: Thereat disregarding the swans the crows said-"That swan amongst us who has soared high up is evidently defeated."

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: अथ हंसः स तच्छ्रुत्वा प्रापतत् पश्चिमां दिशम्॥ उपर्युपरि वेगेन सागरं मकरालयम्।
en: Hearing this the swan with great velocity began to move westwards towards the ocean abounding in Makaras.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: ततोभी: प्राविशत् काकं तदा तत्र विचेतसम्॥ द्वीपगुमानपश्यन्तं निपातार्थे श्रमान्वितम्।
en: Then the crow became afraid who was almost besides himself at not seeing any island or trees whereon to perch when tired.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: निपतेयं क्व नु श्रान्त इति तस्मिञ्जलार्णवे॥ अविषह्यः समुद्रो हि बहुसत्त्वगणालयः। महासत्त्वशतोद्भासी नभसोऽपि विशिष्यते॥
en: (He then thought) “where shall I alight on this vast ocean when tired?” Irrepressible is the deep the abode of numberless creatures. Inhabited by hundreds of monsters it is greater than the sky.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: गाम्भीर्याद्धि समुद्रस्य न विशेषं हि सूतज। दिगम्बराम्भसः कर्ण समुद्रस्था विदुर्जनाः॥ विदूरपातात् तोयस्य किं पुनः कर्ण वायसः।
en: you wretch, none can exceed the ocean in depth. O Karna, the men know that the waters of the ocean are equally boundless like the sky. What is crow to it considering its extent?

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: अथ हंसोऽप्यतिक्रम्य मुहूर्तमिति चेति च॥ अवेक्षमाणस्तं काकं नाशकद् व्यपसर्पितुम।
en: Doing a great distance in a moment the swan looked back at the crow and could not leave him behind.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: अतिक्रम्य च चक्राङ्गः काकं तं समुदैक्षत॥ यावद् गत्वा पतत्येष काको मामिति चिन्तयन्।
en: Having beaten down the crow the swan looked at him and waited thinking 'Let the crow come up.'

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: ततः काको भृषं श्रान्तो हंसमभ्यागमत्तदा॥ तं तथा हीयमानं तु हंसो दृष्ट्वाब्रवीदिदम्। उजिहीर्षुर्निमज्जन्त स्मरन् सत्पुरुषव्रतम्॥
en: Thereupon greatly exhausted the crow came up to the swan. Thereupon beholding him about to sink and with a view to rescue him the swan, remembering the good offices of the pious, said to him-

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: हंस उवाच बहूनि पतितानि त्वमाचक्षाणो मुहुर्मुहुः। पातस्य व्याहरंश्चेदं न नो गुह्यं प्रभाषसे॥
en: The Swan said “While speaking about flight you again and again mentioned about a goodly number of them. You should not mention this your flight which is a mystery to us.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: किं नाम पतितं काकः यत्त्व पतसि सामप्रतम्। जलं स्पृशसि पक्षाभ्यां तुण्डेन च पुनः पुनः॥
en: What is the name of this flight, O crow, which you have followed now? You repeatedly touch the waters with your wings and beak.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: प्रबूहि कतमे तत्र पाते वर्तसि वायस। एोहि काक शीघ्रं त्वमेष त्वां प्रतिपालये॥
en: Which amongst those many kinds of flight, O crow, that you are bow following? Come quickly, Ocrow, I am waiting for you.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: शल्य उवाच स पक्षाभ्यां स्पृशन्नार्तस्तुण्डेन च जलं तदा। दृष्टो हंसेन दुष्टात्मन्निदं हंस ततोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Shalya said O wicked one, greatly tired and touching the water with his wings and beak and seen by the swan the crow said to him.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: अपश्यन्नम्भसः पारं निपतंश्च श्रमान्वितः। पातवेगप्रमथितो हंसं काकोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Not beholding the limit of the ocean, fatigued and broken down with the exertion of flight the crow said to the swan.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: वयं काकाः कुतो नाम चरामः काकवाशिकाः। हंस प्राणैः प्रपद्ये त्वामुदकान्तं नयस्व माम्॥
en: “We are crows, we move about here and there crying caw, caw. O swan, I lay my life at your hands and seek refuge with you. Take me to the bank of the ocean.'

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: स पक्षाभ्यां स्पृशन्नार्तस्तुण्डेन च महार्णवे। काको दृढपरिश्रान्तः सहसा निपपात ह॥
en: Greatly tired and touching the ocean with his wings and beak the crow all on a sudden fell down.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: सागराम्भसि तं दृष्ट्वा पतितं दीनचेतसम्। प्रियमाणमिदं काकं हंसो वाक्यमुवाच ह॥
en: Beholding him thus fallen into the ocean with a sorry heart the swan addressed the crow

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: शतमेकं च पातानां पताम्यहमनुस्मर। श्लाघमानस्त्वमात्मानं काक भाषितवानसि॥
en: “O crow, how did you praise yourself. Remember, you said that you would course through the sky in a hundred different ways.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: स त्वमेकशतं पातं पतन्नभ्यधिको मया। कथमेवं परिश्रान्तः पतितोऽसि महार्णवे॥
en: You, who would fly in a hundred different ways, are superior to me; why are you then tired and fallen on the ocean?"

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: प्रत्युवाचः ततः काकः सीदमान उदं वचः। उपरिष्टं तदा हंसमभिवीक्ष्य प्रसादयन्॥
en: Overcome with weakness, the crow, rating his looks up at the swan and trying to please him said.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: काक उवाच उच्छिष्टदर्पितो हंस मन्येऽऽत्मानं सुपर्णवत्। अवमन्य बहूंचाहं काकानन्यांश्च पक्षिणः॥
en: The crow said "Rendered arrogant by feeding upon the leavings of others' food I thought myself as equal to Garuda and did not care for crows and other birds.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: प्राणहंस प्रपद्ये त्वां द्वीपान्तं प्रापयस्व माम्। यद्यहं स्वस्तिमान् हंस स्वं देशं प्राप्नुयां प्रभो॥
en: I now seek refure with you and place my life at your disposal. Oh, take me to the shore of some island.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: न कंचिदवमन्येऽहमापदो मां समुद्धर। तमेवं वादिनं दीनं विलपन्तमचेतनम्॥
en: If I, O swan, O lord, return safely to my country I will never disregard any body; Oh, save me from this calamity."

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: काक काकेति वाशन्तं निमज्जन्तं महार्णवे। कृपयाऽऽदाय हंसस्तं जलक्किन्नं सुदुर्दसम्॥ पद्धयामुक्षिप्य वेगेन पृष्ठमारोपयच्छनैः। आरोप्य पृष्ठं हंसस्तं काकं तूर्णं विचेतनम्॥
en: Without a word the swan took him up with his foot and placed him slowly on his back, who said so, was melancholy, weeping, deprived of his sense, was sinking in the ocean, was crying caw! caw, was drenched with water, hedeous to look at and trembling in fear.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: आजगाम पुनर्दीपं स्पर्धया पेततुर्यतः। संस्थाप्य तं चापि पुनः समाश्वास्य च खेचरम्॥
en: Having placed speedily the crow who was besides himself on his back he came to the island from which they had started challenging each other.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: गतो यथेप्सितं देश हंसो मन इवाशुगः। एवमुच्छिष्टपुष्टः स काको हंसपराजितः॥
en: Putting that ranger of the sky down (on the land) and comforting him the swan repaired quickly to his wished-for region with the mind.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: बलं वीर्यं महत्कर्ण त्यक्त्वा क्षान्तिमुपागतः। उच्छिष्टभोजन: काको यथा वैश्यकुले पुरा॥
en: Thus the crow, fed fat with the leavings, was defeated by the swan. Then casting off the pride of strength and prowess the crow, O Karna, led a peaceful and quiet life.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: एवं त्वमुच्छिष्टभृतो धार्तराष्ट्र संशयः। सदृशाश्रेयसश्चापि सर्वान् कर्णावमन्यसे॥
en: As that crow, fed upon the refuses of the food of the Vaishya children, did not care his equals and superiors, so do you, O Karna, fed by Dhritarashtra's sons, with the leavings of their food, disregard your equals and superiors.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: द्रोणद्रौणिकृपैर्गुप्तो भीष्मेणान्यैश्च कौरवैः। विराटनगरे पार्थमेकं किं नावधीस्तदा॥
en: Why did you not kill Partha at Virata's city when you were protected by Drona and his son Kripa, Bhishma and other Kaurava?

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: यत्र व्यस्ता: समत्सांश्च निर्जिताः स्थ किरीटिना। शृगाला इव सिंहेन क्व ते वीर्तमभूत् तदा॥
en: What became of your prowess there when defeated by Kiriti you all fled away like a pack of jackals?

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: भ्रातरं निहतं दृष्ट्वा समरे सव्यसाचिना। पश्यतां कुरुवीराणां प्रथमं त्वं पलायितः॥
en: Seeing your brother killed by Savya Sachin in the very presence of the Kuru heroes it was you who fled away first.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: तथा द्वैतवने कर्ण गन्धर्वेः समभिद्रुतः। कुरून् समयानुत्सृज्य प्रथमं त्वं पलायितः॥
en: When you were assailed by the Gandharvas in the Dvaita forest it was you who, leaving behind the Kurus, did run away from the forest.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: हत्वा जित्वा च गन्धर्वाचित्रसेनमुखान् रणे। कर्ण दुर्योधनं पार्थं सभार्यं सममोक्षयत्॥
en: Having defeated in battle the Gandharvas led by Chitrasena with a great slaughter it was Arjuna, O Karna, who rescued Duryodhana with his wife.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: पुनः प्रभाव पार्थस्य पौराणः केशवस्य च। कथितः कर्ण रामेण सभायां राजसंसदि॥
en: Rama himself, O Karna, before the assembly of the Kuru heroes spoke of the prowess of Arjuna and Kesava.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: सततं च त्वमश्रौषीर्वचनं द्रोणभीष्मयोः। अवध्यौ वदन्तः कृष्णौ संनिधौ च महीक्षिताम्॥
en: You have always heard Drona and Bhishma speaking before all the kings of the two Krishnas as being unslayable.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: कियत् तत् तत् प्रवक्ष्यामि येन येन धनंजयः। त्वत्तोऽतिरिक्तः सर्वेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो ब्राह्मणों यथा॥
en: I have told you only a bit about this that Dhananjaya is superior to you as a Brahmana is to all creatures.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: इदानीमेव द्रष्टासि प्रधाने स्यन्दने स्थितौ। पुत्रं च वसुदेवस्य कुन्तीपुत्रं च पाण्डवम्॥
en: You will soon see stationed on that best of cars the son of Vasudeva and the son of Kunti and Pandu.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: यथाश्रयत चक्राङ्गं वायसो बुद्धिमास्थितः। तथाश्रयस्व वार्ष्णेयं पाण्डवं च धनंजयम्॥
en: As the crow intelligently sought the protection of the swan so do you seek the shelter of the Vrishni hero (Krishna) and of Pandu's son Dhananjaya.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: यदा त्वं युधि विक्रान्तौ वासुदेवधनंजयौ। द्रष्टास्येकरथे कर्ण तदा नैवं वदिष्यसि॥
en: When you will see in battle the highly powerful Vasudeva and Dhananjaya stationed in the same car, you will not utter such words, OKarna.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: यदा शरशतैः पार्थो दर्प तव वधिष्यति। तदा त्वमन्तरं द्रष्टा आत्मनंश्चार्जुनस्य त॥
en: When Partha with hundreds of shafts break down you pride you will then see the difference between yourself and Dhananjaya.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: देवासुरमनुष्येषु प्रख्यातौ यौ नरोत्तमौ। तौ मावमंस्था मौात् त्वं खद्योत इव रोचनौ॥८५
en: Those two best of men are well-known among the gods, Asuras and men; you are a fire-fly, do not foolishly disregard those two bright luminaries.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ यद्वत् तद्वदर्जुनकेशवौ। प्राकाश्वेनाभिविख्यातौ त्वं तु खद्योतवन्नृषु॥
en: Like the sun and the moon Kesava and Arjuna are famous for their effulgence; you are but a fire-fly among men.

description: The story of the swan and crow
sn: एवं विद्वान् मावमंस्थाः सूतपुत्राच्युतार्जुनौ। नृसिंहो तो महात्मानौ जोषमास्स्व विकत्थने॥
en: O learned one, O son of a charioteer, do not make light of Arjuna and Achyuta; those two high-souled ones are best of men. Do not make such vaunts. O learned one, O son of a charioteer, do not make light of Arjuna and Achyuta; those two high-souled ones are best of men. Do not make such vaunts.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: संजय उवाच मद्राधिपस्याधिरथिर्महात्मा वचो निशम्याप्रियमप्रतीतः। उवाच शल्यं विदितं ममैतद् यथाविधावर्जुनवासुदेवौ॥
en: Sanjaya said Listening to those unpleasant words and not being convinced the high-souled car-warrior, the king of Madra, said to Shalya "I know well what Vasudeva and Arjuna are.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: शौरे रथं वाहयतोऽर्जुनस्य बलं महास्त्राणि च पाण्डवस्य। अहं विजानामि यथावदद्य परोक्षभूतं तव तत् तु शल्य॥
en: Even now I know well the skill of Shouri in the management of cars and the power and great weapons of Arjuna, the son of Pandu. But you have no practical knowledge of them, O Shalya.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: तौ चाप्यहं शस्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठौ व्यपेतभीर्योधयिष्यामि कृष्णौ। च्छापोऽद्य मां ब्राह्मणसत्तमाच॥
en: I shall fearlessly fight with those two Krishnas, the foremost of the wielders of weapons. The course of Rama, the foremost of Brahmanas, pains me greatly.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अवसं वै ब्राह्मणच्छद्मनाहं रामे पुरा दिव्यमस्त्रं चिकीर्षुः। तत्रापि मे देवराजेन विघ्नो हितार्थिना फाल्गुनस्यैव शल्य॥ कृतो विभेदेन ममोरुमेत्य प्रविश्य कीटस्य तनुं विरूपाम्। ममोरुमेत्य प्रबिभेद कीट: सुप्ते गुरौ तत्र शिरो निधाय॥
en: I lived formerly with Rama in the disguise of a Brahmana with a view to obtain the celestial weapons from him. At that time, O Shalya, the king of gods, wishing to do a good office by Phalguna, put in an impediment by approaching my thigh and piercing it in the form of a dreadful worm. When my preceptor slept placing his head on my thigh that worm began to bore it through.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ऊरुप्रभेदाच महान् बभूव शरीरतो मे घनशोणितौधः। गुरोभयाचापि न चेलिवानहं ततो विबुद्धो ददृशे स विप्रः॥
en: On account of this boring of my thigh a pool of thick blood gushed out of my body. For fear of my preceptor I did not move my limb. The Brahmana, on waking, saw it.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: स धैर्ययुक्तं प्रसमीक्ष्य मां वै न त्वं विप्रः कोऽसि सत्यं वदेति। दाख्यातवान् सूत इत्येव शल्य॥
en: O Shalya, Beholding my patience he said-"you are never a Brahmana. Tell me truly who you are." I then gave him the true information about myself and said that I was a Suta.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: स मां निशम्याथ महातपस्वी संशप्तवान् रोषपरीतचेताः। सूतोपधावाप्तमिदं तवास्त्रं न कर्मकाले प्रतिभास्यति त्वाम्॥
en: Hearing this the great ascetic, worked up with anger, imprecated a curse on me, saying-"On account of the deception O charioteer, by which you have got this weapon it will never come to your mind at the time of necessity.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: दब्राह्मणे ब्रह्म न हि ध्रुवं स्यात्। मस्मिन् संग्रामे तुमुलेऽतीव भीमे॥
en: When the hour of your death will arrive. Brahmastra can never live in one who is not a Brahmana. I have forgotten that great weapon in this fierce and dreadful encounter.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: योऽयं शल्य भरतेषूपपन्नः प्रकर्षणः सर्वहरोऽतिभीमः। सोऽभिमन्ये क्षत्रियाणां प्रवीरान् प्रतापिता बलवान् वै विमर्दः॥
en: O Shalya, that descendant of Bharatas who is highly dreadful, the destroyer of all the grinders of foes and powerful, will, me-thinks, grind many Kshatriya heroes.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: शल्योगधन्वानमहं वरिष्ठं तरस्विनं भीममसह्यवीर्यम्। सत्यप्रतिज्ञं युधि पाण्डवेयं धनंजय मृत्युमुखं नयिष्ये॥
en: Know however, O Shalya, I will kill in battle today that terrible bowman and the foremost of warriors, the son of Pandu, Dhananjaya, who is highly energetic and ascetic-a hero whose promises and always carried out.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अस्त्रं ततोऽन्यत् प्रतिपन्नमद्य येन क्षेप्स्ये समरे शत्रुपूगान्। प्रतापिनं बलवन्तं कृतास्त्रं तमुग्रधन्वानमिततौजसं च॥ क्रूरं शूरं रौद्रममित्रसाह धनंजयं संयुगेऽहं हनिष्ये।
en: I have at least that weapon with me with which I will be able to kill a goodly number of enemies. I will kill in battle, that grinder of weapons, that powerful heroes, the master of weapons, that dreadful bowman of incomparable energy, that ruthless and dreadful hero who can resist his enemies-(I mean) Dhananjaya.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अपां पतिर्वेगवानप्रमेयो निमज्जयिष्यन् बहुलाः प्रजांश्च॥ महावेगं संकृरुते समुद्रो वेला चैनं धरायत्यप्रमेयम्।
en: The limitless deep, the king of waters dashes on impetuously for overwhelming numberless creatures. The continent flow over holds and restrains him.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: प्रमुञ्चन्तं बाणसंघानमेयान् मर्मच्छिदो वीरहणः सुपत्रान्॥ कुन्तीपुत्रं यत्र योतस्यामि युद्धे ज्यां कर्षतामुत्तममद्य लोके।
en: I will today, in this world, withstand in fight the son of Kunti the foremost of archers while he will ceaselessly discharge his winged arrows capable of killing heroes and penetrating into every limb and none of which becomes futile.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: एवं बलेनातिबलं महास्त्रं समुद्रकल्पं सुदुरापमुग्रम्॥ शरोधिणं पार्थिवान् मञ्जयन्तं वेलेव पार्थमिषुभिः संसाहिष्ये।
en: Like the bank of an ocean restraining it I will withstand Partha that foremost strongest of the strong the great hero owning many weapons, resembling the ocean itself and having many dreadful and far-reaching arrows like unto the waves of the ocean while he will be engaged in assailing the kings.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अद्याहवे यस्य न तुल्यमन्यं मन्ये मनुष्यं धनुराददानम्॥ सुरासुरान् युधि वै यो जयेत तेनाद्य मे पश्य युद्धं सुघोरम्।
en: Witness my highly dreadful encounter with him today in baitle, who, methinks, has not equal amongst men, using bows and who vanquished the gods and demons in battle.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अतीव मानी पाण्डवो युद्धकामो ह्यमानुषैरष्यति मे महास्त्रैः॥ तस्यास्त्रमस्त्रैः प्रतिहत्य संख्ये बाणोत्तमैः पातयिश्यामि पार्थम्।
en: The Pandava is exceedingly haughty. Desirous of fighting he will approach me with superhuman and powerful weapons. Counteracting his weapons with mine in battle I will fell Partha with my excellent arrows.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: सहस्ररश्मिप्रतिमं ज्वलन्तं दिशश्च सर्वाः प्रतपन्तमुग्रम॥ तमोनुदं मेघ इवातिमात्रं धनंजयं छादयिष्यामि बाणैः।
en: He burns down his enemies like the sun of fiery rays and shines in his fame. As the clouds gather round the dispeller of darkness, so I shall cover Dhananjaya with my shafts,

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: वैश्वानरं धूमशिखं ज्वलन्तं तेजस्विनं लोकमिदं दहन्तम्॥ पर्जन्यभूतः शरवर्षेथाग्नि तथा पार्थं शमयिष्यामि युद्धे।
en: As the clouds with showers extinguish the powerful fire burning with smoking flames and as if consuming the whole worlds, so I will with showers of my arrows, put down the son of Kunti.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: आशीविषं दुर्धरमप्रमेयं सुतीक्ष्णदंष्ट्र ज्वलनप्रभावम्॥ क्रोधप्रदीप्तं त्वहितं महान्तं कुन्तीपुत्रं शमयिष्यामि भल्लैः।
en: With my darts I will put down the son of Kunti in battle who is like a dreadful and fierce snake of sharpened fang, who burns in effulgence and anger and consumes those who work him evil.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: प्रमाथिनं बलवन्तं प्रहारिणं प्रभञ्जनं मातारिश्वानमुग्रम्॥ युद्धे सहिष्ये हिमवानिवाचलो धनंजयं क्रुद्धममृष्यमाणम्।
en: As the Himalaya holds the powerful, crushing and all-striking wind-god so I will, without perturbation, withstand the angry and vindictive Dhananjaya.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: विशारदं रथमार्गेषु शक्तं धुर्यं नित्य समरेषु प्रवीरम्॥ लोके वरं सर्वधनुर्धराणां धनंजयं संयुगे संसहिष्ये।
en: I will withstand in battle Dhananjaya the foremost of all the archers in the world who knows well all the car-tracks, who is always in the van, competent and heroic in battle.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अद्याहवे यस्य न तुल्यमन्यं मन्ये मनुष्यं धनुराददानम्॥ सर्वामिमां यः पृथिवीं विजिग्ये तेन प्रयोद्धास्मि समेत्य संख्ये।
en: Today, I will encounter in battle the man, who, in my view, is non-pariel amongst the archers and who conquered the entire earth.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: यः सर्वभूतानि सदैवतानि प्रस्थेऽजयत् खाण्डवे सव्यसाची॥ को जीवितं रक्ष्यमाणो हि तेन युयुत्सेद् वै मानुषो मामृतेऽन्यः।
en: What man, save me, who wishes to keep his life, will fight with Savyasachin who defeated all creatures, including even the celestials in the country called Khandava.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: मानी कृतास्त्रः कृतहस्तयोगो दिव्यास्त्रविच्छ्वेतहयः प्रमाथी॥ च्छिरो हरिष्यामि शितैः पृषत्कैः।
en: He is proud, holds his weapons firmly, is light-handed, knows the use of celestial weapons, has white horses and is capable of smiting all. Today shall I with sharpened shafts sever the head of such a great warrior from his body.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: योत्स्याम्येनं शल्य धनंजयं वै मृत्युं पुरस्कृत्य रणे जयं वा॥ अन्यो हि न ह्येकरथेन मयों युध्येत यः पाण्डवमिन्द्रकल्पम्।
en: O Shalya, keeping either death or victory before me, I will fight with Dhananjaya today. There is none else but me who can fight on a single car with that Pandava resembling Death himself.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: तस्याहवे पौरुषं पाण्डवस्य ब्रूया हृष्टः समितौ क्षत्रियाणाम्॥ किं त्वं मूर्खः प्रसभं मूढचेता ममावोचः पौरुषं फाल्गुनस्या
en: I will myself with pleasure speak of the prowess of Pandava in battle before the assembly of the Kshatriyas. Why do you, a fool as you are, speak of the prowess of Phalguna to me?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अप्रियो यः पुरुषो निष्ठुरो हि क्षुद्रः क्षेप्ता क्षमिणंश्चाक्षमावान्॥ हन्यामहं तादृशानां शतानि क्षमाम्यहं क्षमया कालयोगात्।
en: The forgiving always forgive a mean and a cruel person who performs unpleasant deeds. I can slay a hundred like you, but I forgive you for my forgiving nature and the necessity of the time.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अवोचस्त्वं पाण्डवार्थेऽप्रियाणि प्रधर्षयन् मां मूढवत् पापकर्मन्॥ मय्यार्जवे जिामतिर्हतस्त्वं मित्रद्रोही साप्तपदं हि मैत्रम्।
en: You are the perpetrator of evil deeds. You have, like a fool, for the sake of the Pandavas, remonstrated with me and spoken many unpleasant things. You have said these to me who am innocent. Cursed you are, an injurer of friendship is seven paced.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: कालस्त्वयं प्रत्युपयाति दारुणो दुर्योधनो युद्धमुपागमद् यत्॥ स्तन्मन्यसे यत्र नैकान्त्यमस्ति।
en: The present moment, that has arrived, is really dreadful for Duryodhona has come to battle. I always wish to see his ends accomplished. But you are acting in such a vay that it appears you have no friendship for the Kuru king.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: मित्रं मिन्देन्दतेः प्रीयतेर्वा संत्रायतेर्मिनुतेर्मोदतेर्वा॥ ब्रवीमि ते सर्वमिदं ममास्ति तचापि सर्वं मम वेत्ति राजा।
en: He is a friend who gladdens his friend, pleases him, protects him, honors him and shares in his joy. I have got all these qualities; the king himself knows it.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: शत्रुः शदेः शासतेर्वा श्यतेर्वा शृणातेर्वा श्वसतेः सीदतेर्वा॥ उपसर्गाद् बहुधा सूदतेश्च प्रा येण सर्वं त्वयि तच मह्यम्।
en: Whereas he who destroys, remonstrates with, sharpens his weapons, makes us to sigh and cheerless and wrongs us in many ways is our enemy. All these marks are to be seen in you and you display them all against us.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: दुर्योधनर्थं तव च प्रियार्थं यशोऽर्थमात्मार्थमपीश्वरार्थम्॥ तस्मादहं पाण्डववासुदेवौ योत्स्ये यत्नात् कर्म तत् पश्य मेऽद्य।
en: For the sake of Duryodhana, for the sake of doing what is agreeable to you, for the sake of fame, for the sake of myself and the God, I will vigorously fight with Partha and Vasudeva. Behold today my feats.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अस्त्राणि पश्याद्य ममोत्तमानि ब्राह्माणि दिव्यान्यथ मानुषाणि॥ आसादयिष्याम्यहमुग्रवीर्य द्विपो द्विपं मत्तमिवातिमत्तः।
en: Behold today all my excellent weapons, Brahma, celestial and human, I will like today that highly powerful heroes like an infuriate elephants slaying another such.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अस्त्रं ब्राह्मं मनसा युध्यजेयं क्षेप्स्ये पायाप्रमेयं जयाय। तेनापि मे नैव मुच्येत युद्धे न चेत् पतेद् विषमेमेऽद्य चक्राम्॥
en: For my victory I will hurl today that highly powerful Brahma weapon at Partha will my mind alone. Arjuna will never be able to escape that weapon if only the wheels of my car do not sink in the earth in battle today.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: वैवस्वताद् दण्डहस्ताद्वरुणाद् वापि पाशिनः। सगदाद् वा धनपतेः सवज्राद् वापि वासवात्॥ अन्यस्मदपि कस्माचिदमित्रादाततायिनः। इति शल्य विजानीहि यथा नाहं विभेम्यतः।। तस्मान्न मे भयं पार्थान्नापि चैव जनार्दनात्॥
en: Know this, O Shalya, that I will not even fear Yama armed with his rod or Varuna armed with his noose, or Kubera armed with his mace, or Vasava armed with his thunder-bolt or any other cnemy who may come forward to kill me.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: सहं युद्धं हि मे ताभ्यां साम्पराये भविष्यति। तदाचिद् विजयस्यामस्त्रहेतोरटन्नृप॥
en: There I have no fear from Partha or Janardana. There shall take place an encounter between me and them both in the battle.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अज्ञानाद्धि क्षिपन् बाणान् घोररूपान् भयानकान्। होमधेन्वा वत्समस्य प्रमत्त इषुणाहनम्॥ चरन्तं विजने शल्य ततोऽनुव्याजहार माम्। यस्मात् त्वया प्रमत्तेन होमधेन्वा हतः सुतः॥
en: O king, while wandering about to set arrows my Vijaya bow I myself unconsciously killed with an arrows the calf of a Brahmana's Homa I began discharging dreadful shafts while it was roaming in the dense forest. The Brahmana then addressed me, saying-

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: श्वभ्रे ते पततां चक्रमिति मां ब्राह्मणोऽब्रवीत्। युध्यमानस्य संग्रामे प्राप्तस्यैकायनं भयम्॥
en: Since you have carelessly killed the offspring of my Homa cow, the wheel of your car will sink into the earth and at the time of war your heart will be possessed by fear.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: तस्माद् बिभेमि बलवद् ब्राह्मणव्याहतादहम्। एते हि सोमराजान ईश्वराः सुखदुःखयो॥ अदां तस्मै गोसहस्रं बलीवर्दाश्च षट्शतान्। प्रसादं न लभे शल्य ब्राह्मणान्मद्रकेश्वर॥
en: I always stand in great fear of these words of the Brahmana. The kings of the Lunar dynasty, the lords of people's happiness and on COW as misery, offered him a thousand kine and six hundred bovine bulls. Still with such a gift O Shalya, O king Madra, the Brahmana was not grated.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ईषादन्तान् सप्तशतान् दासीदासशतानि च। ददतो द्विजमुख्यो मे प्रसादं न चकार सः॥
en: I then offered him seven hundred elephants of huge tusks and many hundreds of male and female slaves. And still that best of Brahmanas was not satisfied.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: कृष्णानां श्वेतवत्सानां सहस्राणि चतुर्दश। आहरं न लभे तस्मात् प्रसाद द्विजसत्तमात्॥
en: Offering him then full fourteen thousand black kine each with a white calf I could not obtain the grace of that best of Brahmanas.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ऋद्धं गृहं सर्वकामैर्यच मे वसु किंचन। तत् सर्वमस्मै सत्कृत्य प्रयच्छामि न चेच्छति॥
en: Then I offered him a beautiful palace abounding in all objects of desire, in fact, whatever riches I had but still he refused to accept the gift.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्मा याचन्तमपराधं प्रयत्नतः। व्याहृतं यन्मया सूत तत् तथा न तदन्यथा॥
en: He then said to nie who had offered him and thus implored his forgiveness.” What I have said, O Suta, will surely take place. It can never be otherwise.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अनुतोक्तं प्रजां हन्यात् ततः पापमवाप्नुयाम्। तस्माद् धर्माभिरक्षार्थ नानृतं तक्तुमुत्सहे॥
en: False words will destroy creatures and the sin will come upon me. Therefore for preserving virtue I dare not speak an untruth.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: मा त्वं ब्रह्मगति हिंस्याः प्रायश्चित्तं कृतं त्वया। मद्वाक्यं नानृतं लोके कश्चित् कुर्यात् समानुहि॥
en: You shall not destroy the means of Brahmana's livelihood. There is none on earth who can falsify my words. Accept my words and this will be an atonement for your sin,

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: इत्येतत्ते मया प्रोक्तं क्षिप्तेनापि सुहृत्तया। जानामि त्वां विक्षिपन्तं जोषमास्स्वोत्तरं शृणु।॥
en: Although chastised by you still for your friendship I have spoken out all this to you. I know you who are chastising me thus. Be silent and hear what I will speak 11OW. know you who are chastising me thus. Be silent and hear what I will speak 11OW.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: संजय उवाच ततः पुनर्महाराज मद्रराजमरिंदमः। अभ्यभाषत राधेयः संनिवार्योत्तरं वचः। ॥
en: Sanjaya said Once more, O great king, thus silencing the king of Madras, the son of Radha, the chastiser of foes, said to him.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: यत् त्वं निदर्शनार्थं मां शल्य जल्पितवानसि। नाहं शक्यस्त्वया वाचा बिभीषयितुमाहवे॥
en: As a rejoinder to what you have said to me, O Shalya, by way of examples I tell you that I am not to be frightened by you in battle with your words.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: यदि मां देवताः सर्वा योधयेयुः सवासवाः। तथापि मे भयं न स्यात् किमु पार्थात् सकेशवात्॥
en: If all the gods with Vasava come to fight with me I will not fear them what to speak of my fear from Partha and Kesava.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: नाहं भीषयितुं शक्यो वामात्रेण कथंचन। अन्यं जानिहि यः शक्यस्त्वया भीषयितुं रणे।॥
en: I am not to be frightened by mere words. O Shalya, he, whom you will be able to frighten in battle, is some other person.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: नीचस्य बलमेतावत् पारुष्यं यत्त्वमात्थ माम्। अशक्तो मद्गुणान् वक्तुं वल्गसे बहु दुर्मते॥
en: You have addressed many unpleasant words to me. Therein lies the strength of a mean person, O you of wicked soul; you can speak of my merits and so you say many unpleasant words.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: न हि कर्णः समुद्भूतो भयार्थमिह मद्रका विक्रमार्थमहं जातो यशोऽर्थं च तथाऽऽत्मनः॥
en: Karna is not born for fear in battle, O Madraka. I am rather born to display my valour and achieve glory for my own self.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: सखिभावेन सौहार्दान्मित्रभावेन चैव हि। कारणैस्त्रिभिरेतैस्त्वं शल्य जीवसि साम्प्रतम्॥
en: Out of friendship for you, out of my affection and on account of your being an ally-for these three reasons, you still live, O Shalya.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: राशंश्च धार्तराष्ट्रस्य कार्यं सुमहदुद्यतम्। मयि तचाहितं शल्य तेन जीवसि मे क्षणम्॥
en: A great work is now to be done for the king Dhritarashtra. This work depends on me, O Shalya and therefore you live for a moment,

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: कृतंश्च समयः पूर्वं क्षन्यव्यं विप्रियं तव। ऋते शल्यसहस्रेण विजयेयमहं परान्। मित्रद्रोहस्तु पापीयानिति जीवसि साम्प्रतम्॥
en: I made this agreement with you formerly that I would forgive you for all your unpleasant words. This agreement I will observe and for this you still live. Without a thousand Shalyas I will vanquish my enemies. The injurer of a friend is sinful. It is for this you live for the present.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: शल्य उवाच परान् प्रति। ननु प्रलापाः कफ्ते यान् ब्रवीपि ऋते कर्णसहस्रेण शक्या जेतुं परे युधि॥
en: Shalya said These are but your ravings, O Karna that you give vent to with regard to your enemies. But I can without a thousand Karnas defeat my foe in battle.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: संजय उवाच तथा ब्रुवन्तं परुषं कर्णो मद्रधिपं तदा। परुषं द्विगुण भूयः प्रोवाचाप्रियदर्शनम्॥
en: Sanjaya said To the king of Madras, who was speaking such harsh words Karna, of unpleasant looks, spoke words again twice as harsh.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: कर्ण उवाच इदं तु ते त्वमेकाग्रः शृणु मद्रजनाधिप। शंनिधौ धृतराष्ट्रस्य प्रोच्यमानं मया श्रुतम्॥
en: Karna said O king of Madras, listen attentively to what I heard recited in the presence of Dhritarashtra.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: देशांश्च विविधांश्चित्रान् पूर्ववृत्तांश्च पार्थिवान्। ब्राह्मणः कथयन्ति स्म धृतराष्ट्रनिवेशने॥
en: In Dhritarashtra's house the Brahmanas used to describe many pleasant regions and the lives of many ancient kings.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: तत्र वृद्धः पुरावृत्ताः कथा कश्चिद् द्विजोत्तमः। वाहीकदेशं मद्रांश्च कुत्सयन् वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: One aged and leading Brahmana among them, while recounting the ancient historian, said thus blaring the Balhikas and Madrakas.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: बहिष्कृता हिमवता गङ्गया च बहिष्कृताः। शरस्वत्या यमुनया कुरक्षेत्रेण चापि ये॥ पञ्चानां सिन्धुषष्ठानां नदीनां येऽन्तराश्रिताः। तान् धर्मबाह्यानशुचीन वाहीकानपि वर्जयेत्॥
en: One should always avoid the impure and impious Balhikas who live away from Himavat and Ganga, Sarasvati, Yamuna and Kurukshetra and the Sindhu with its five tributaries.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: गोवर्धनो नाम वटः सुभद्रं नाम चत्वरम्। एतद् राजकुलद्वारमाकुमारात् स्मराम्यहम्॥
en: I remember from my youth that a slaughter ground for kine and the cellars for wine mark out the gates of the palaces of Balhika kings.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: कार्येणात्यर्थगूढेन वाहीकेषूषितं मया। तत एषां समाचारः संवासाद् विदितो मम॥
en: For some secret work I had to live with them. On account of this living I know them very well.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: शाकलं नाम नगरमापगा नाम निम्नगा। जर्त्तिका नाम वाहीकास्तेषां वृत्तं सुनिन्दतम्॥
en: There is a town of the name of Shakala, a river by the name of Apaga and a clan of the Balhikas known as Jarttikas. Their conduct is very reprehensible.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: धाना गौड्यासवं पीत्वा गोमांसं लशुनैः सह। अपूपमांसवाट्यानामाशिनः शीलवर्जिताः॥
en: They drink the liquor Ganda and eat friend barley with it. They also eat beef with garlics. They also take flour with meat and boiled rice that is bought of others. They are shorn of all good practices.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: गायन्त्यथ च नृत्यन्ति स्त्रियो मत्ता विवाससः। नगरागारवप्रेषु बहिर्माल्यानुलेपनाः॥ मत्तावगीतैर्विविधैः खरोष्ट्रनिनदोपमैः। अनावृता मैथुने ताः कामचाराश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Their women all drink and are nude and laugh and dance, outside the walls of the houses in cities, with garlands and unguents, singing under the influence of liquor various obscene songs like the bray of the ass or the bleat of lambs. They freely mix and intercourse with all. Inebrite they address one another with endearing terms.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: आहुरन्योन्यसूक्तानि प्रब्रुवाणा मदोत्कटाः। हे हते हे हतेत्येव स्वामिभर्तृहतेति च॥
en: The fallen Balhika women, unobservant of restrictions even on sacred days, dance and exclaim “Alas! our husband, our lord is dead!"

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: आक्रोशन्त्यः प्रनृत्यन्ति व्रात्याः पर्वस्वसंयता। तासां किलावलिप्तानां निवसन् कुरुजाङ्गले॥
en: One of those wicked Balhikas who lived amongst them and and for time in Kurujangala burst out with cheerless heart saying-

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: कश्चिद् वाहीकदुष्टानां नातिहष्टमना जगौ। सा नूनं बृहती गौरी सूक्ष्मकम्बलवासिनी॥
en: "Surely that big and fair (Balhika maiden) dressed in her blankets is thinking of me her Balhika lover, who am living in Kurujangala at the time of her going to bed.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: मामनुस्मरती शेते वाहीकं कुरुजाङ्गले। शतद्रुकामहं तीर्खा तां च रम्यामिरावतीम्॥ गत्वा स्वदेश द्रक्ष्यामि स्थूलशङ्खा शुभाः स्त्रियः। मनः शिलोजवलापाङ्गयो गौर्यस्त्रिककुदाञ्जनाः॥
en: some Crossing the Sutlej, the charming Iravati and coming to my own country when shall I look at those beautiful women with thick frontal bones, with shining circles of red arsenic on their foreheads, with tinges of red, black collyrium on their eyes and their beautiful forms dressed in blankets and skins and themselves uttering shrill cries?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: कम्बलजिनसंवीता क्रन्दन्त्यः प्रियदर्शनाः। मृदङ्गानकशङ्खानां मर्दलानां च निःस्वनैः॥
en: When shall I be happy in the company of those inebriate women amid the sound of drums and kettle-drums and conches sweet as the brays of asses and cries of camels and mules?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: खरोष्ट्राश्वतरैश्चैव मत्ता यास्यामहे सुखम्। शमीपीलुकरीराणां वनेषु सुखवमसु॥
en: When shall I be in the midst of those women who live on cakes of flour and meat and balls of barley and skimmed milk in the forest having pleasant paths of Shami, Pilu and Karira?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: अपूपान् सक्तुपिण्डांश्चं प्राश्नन्तो मथितान्वितान्। पथि सुप्रबला भूत्वा कदा सम्पततोऽध्वगान्॥ चेलापहारं कुर्वाणस्ताडयिष्याम भूयसः।
en: When shall I, surrounded by my countrymen, muster strong on the high roads, fall upon the passers by, carry away their robes and attires and beat them repeatedly?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: एवंशीलेषु व्रात्येषु वाहीकेषु दुरात्मसु॥ कश्चेतयानो निवसेनमुहूर्तमपि मानवः।
en: What man is there who will live willingly even for a moment in the midst of Bahikas who are so fallen, wicked and of fraudulent conduct?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ईदृशा ब्राह्मणेनोक्ता वाहीका मोघचारिणः॥ येषां षड्भागहर्ता त्वमुभयोः शुभपापयोः।
en: Thus did the Brahmanas describe the vile Balhikas, a sixty of whose merit and demerit, you possess, O Shalya.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: इत्युक्त्वा ब्राह्मणः साधुरुत्तरं पुनरुक्तवान्॥ वाहीकेष्वविनीतेषु प्रोत्यमानं निबोध तत्।
en: Having said this the pious Brahmana said some thing about the wicked Bahikas. Hear what I say.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: तत्र स्म राक्षसी गाति सदा कृष्णचतुर्दशीम्॥ नगरे शाकले स्फीते आहत्य निशि दुन्दुभि।
en: In the large and populous city of Shakala a Rakshasa woman used to sing on every fourteenth day of the dark half of the month in accompaniment with a drum.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: कदा वाहेयिका गाथा: पुनर्गास्यामि शाकले।॥ गव्यस्य तृप्ता मांसस्य पीत्वा गौडं सुरासवम्। गौरीभिः सह नारीभिहतीभिः स्वलंकृताः॥ पलाण्डुगंडूषयुतान् खादन्ती चैडकान् बहून्। वाराहं कौक्कुटं मांसं गव्यं गार्दभमौष्ट्रिकम्॥ ऐडं च ये न खादन्ति तेषां जन्म निरर्थकम्।
en: When shall I next sing the songs of the Bahikas in this town of Shakala having fed me full with beef and drunk the Gada liquor. Decked with ornaments when shall I with these huge women and maidens feed upon a large number of sheep, a quantity of pork and beef and the meat of fowls, asses and camels. In vain do they live who do not eat the sheep.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: इति गायन्ति ये मत्ताः सीधुना शाकलाश्च ये॥ सबालवृद्धाः क्रन्दनन्तस्तेषु धर्मः कथं भवेत्।
en: Thus O Shalya, the young and old inhabitants of Sakala, sing and cry under the influence of liquor. How can there by virtue among such people?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: इति शल्य विजानीहि हन्त भूयो ब्रवीमि ते॥ यदन्योऽप्युक्तवानस्मान् ब्राह्मणः कुरुसंसदि।
en: You should know this. I will now recount to you again what another Brahmana said to us in the Kuru court.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: पञ्च नद्यो वहन्त्येता यत्र पीलुवनान्युत॥ शतर्दुश्च विपासा च तृतीयैरावती तथा। चन्द्रभागा वितस्ता च सिन्धुषष्टा बहिर्गिरेः॥ आरट्टा नाम ते देशा नष्टधर्मा न तान् व्रजेत्।'
en: There where the forests of Pilus stand and the five rivers Shatadru, Vipasha, Iravati, Chandrabhaga and Vitasta and which have the Sindhu for their sixty flow there in those region is situated the Province called the Arattas distant from Himavat. The Province is shorn of virtue and religion. No one should there.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: व्रात्यानां दासमीयानां वाहीकानामयज्वनाम्॥ न देवाः प्रतिगृह्णन्ति पितरो ब्राह्मणास्तथा। तेषां प्रनष्टधर्माणां वाहीकानामिति श्रुतिः॥
en: The celestials, the ancestral manes and the Brahmanas never accept gifts from fallen persons, from those that are begotten by Sudras upon women of other castes and from Bahikas who never perform Yajnas and are greatly irreligious.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: ब्राह्मणेन तथा प्रोक्तं विदुषा साधुसंसदि। काष्ठकुण्डेषु वाहीका मृन्मयेषु च भुञ्जते॥ सक्तुमद्यावलिप्तेषु श्वावलीढेषु निघृणाः। आविकं चौष्टिकं चैव क्षीरं गार्दभमेव च॥ तद्विकारांश्च वाहीका: खादन्ति च पिबन्ति च।
en: This the learned Brahmana also said in the Kuru Court. The Balhikas, who have no feelings of revulsion, take their food in deep wooden vessels, earthen plates in vessels that have been licked by dogs and those that have been stained with pounded barely and other corn. They drink the milk of sheep, camels and asses and cat curds and other preparations of those various kinds of milk.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: पुत्रसंकरिणो जाल्माः सर्वान्नक्षीरभोजनाः॥ आरट्टा नाम वाहीका वर्जनीया विपश्चिता।
en: There is a number of bastards among those fallen people. There is no food or no milk that they do not take. The ignorant Aratta Bahikas should always be avoided.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: हन्त शल्य विजानीहि हन्त भूयो ब्रवीमि ते॥ यदन्योऽप्युक्तवान् मह्यं ब्राह्मणः कुरुसंसदि।
en: You should always know this, O Shalya. I will now speak to you what another Brahmana said in the Kuru court.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: युगन्धरे पयः पीत्वा प्रोष्य चाप्यच्युतस्थले॥ तद्वद् भूतिलये स्नात्वा कथं स्वर्ग गमिष्यति।
en: How can a man attain to the celestial region having drunk milk in the town called Yugandhara and lived in the place called Achyutastala and bathed in the spot called Bhutilaya.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: पञ्च नद्यो वहन्त्येता यत्र निःसृत्य पर्वतात्॥ आरट्टा नाम दीका न तेष्वार्योद्वयहं वसेत्।
en: No respectable man should live even for two days where the five rivers flow just after issuing from the mountains and where live Aratta Balhikas.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: बहिश्च नाम हीच विपाशानां पिशाचकौ॥ तयोरपत्यं वाहीका नैषा सृष्टिः प्रजापतेः। ते कथं विविधान् धर्मान् ज्ञास्यन्ते हीनयोनयः॥
en: There are two Pishachas in the river Vipasha named Bahi and Hika. The Bahikas are the offspring of those two Pishchas. They are not creatures created by God. Being of such a low birth how can they know the duties laid down in the scriptures?

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: कारस्करान्माहिषकान् कुरण्डान् केरलांस्तथा। कर्कोटकान् वीरकांश्च दुर्धर्माचं विवर्जयेत्॥
en: The Karaskaras, the Mahishkas, the Kurandas, the Keralas, the Karkotakas, the Virakas and other people who have no religion should always be avoided by men.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: इति तीर्थानुसारं राक्षसी काचिदब्रवीत्। एकरात्रशयी गेहे महोलूखलमेखला॥
en: A Rakshasa woman of huge hips, thus spoke to a Brahman, who once went to that country for bathing in a sacred water and passed a single night there.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: आरट्टा नाम ते देशा वाहीकं नाम तज्जलम्। ब्राह्मणापसदा यत्र तुल्यकालाः प्रजापतेः॥
en: This Province passes under the name of Arattas. And the people who live there are called Balhikas. The Brahmanas of the lowest order also live there from a very ancient time.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: वेदा न तेषां वेद्यंश्च यज्ञा यजनमेव च। व्रात्यानां दासमीयानामन्नं देवा न भुञ्जते॥
en: They are ignorant of the Vedas and void of knowledge. They do not perform Yajnas nor can help others in them. They are all fallen and many of them have been begotten by Sudras upon other caste girls; the gods never accept gifts from them.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: प्रस्थला मद्रगान्धारा आरट्टा नामतः खशाः। वसातिसिन्धुसौवीरा इति प्रायोऽतिकुत्सिताः॥
en: The Prasthalas, the Madras, the Gandharvas, the Arattas, Khasas, the Vasatis, the Sindhus and the Sauviras also follow these reprehensible practices. upon other caste girls; the gods never accept gifts from them.

description: The conversation between Karna and Shalya
sn: प्रस्थला मद्रगान्धारा आरट्टा नामतः खशाः। वसातिसिन्धुसौवीरा इति प्रायोऽतिकुत्सिताः॥
en: The Prasthalas, the Madras, the Gandharvas, the Arattas, Khasas, the Vasatis, the Sindhus and the Sauviras also follow these reprehensible practices.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: कर्ण उवाच हन्त शल्य विजानीहि हन्त भूयो ब्रवीमि ते। उच्यमानं मया सम्यक् त्वमेकाग्रमनाः शृणु।॥
en: Karna said You should know all this, O Shalya, I shall again speak. Hear attentively what I say.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: ब्राह्मणः किल नो गेहमध्यगच्छत् पुरातिथिः। आचारं तत्र सम्प्रेक्ष्य प्रीतो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Once on a time a Brahmana came to our houses as a guest. he was highly pleased with

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: मया हिमवतः शृङ्गमेकेनाध्युषितं चिरम्। दृष्टांश्च बहवो देशा नानाधर्मसमावृताः॥
en: I lived for a long time alone on a summit of the Himalaya mountain, since then I have seen various countries following various religions.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: न च केन च धर्मेण विरुध्यन्ते प्रजा इमाः। सर्व हि तेऽब्रुवन् धर्मं यदुक्तं वेदपारगैः॥
en: But I have never seen a country where all the people are irreligious, All the races I have met with recognise as religion what has been declared by persons conversant with the Vedas.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: अटता तु ततो देशान् नानाधर्मसमाकुलान्। आगच्छता महाराज वाहीकेषु निशामितम्॥
en: Wandering through various countries following diverse religions, I came at last O king, among the Vahikas. There I heard,

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: तत्र वै ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा ततो भवति क्षत्रियः। वैश्यः शूद्रश्च वाहीकस्ततो भवति नापितः॥
en: That one at first becomes a Brahmana and then becomes a Kshatriya, A Vahika after that will become a Vaishya, then a Sudra and then a barber.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: नापितंश्च ततो भूत्वा पुनर्भवति ब्राह्मणः। द्विजो भूत्वा च तत्रैव पुनर्दासोऽभिजायते॥
en: Having become a barber he will again become a Brahmana. Attaining again to the position of a Brahmana he will again become a slave.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: भवन्त्येककुले विप्राः प्रसृष्टा: कामचारिणः। गान्धारा मद्रकांश्चैव वाहीकांचाल्पचेतसः॥
en: One member of a family becomes a Brahmana, All others falling off from virtue act as they please. The Govharas, the Madrakas and the little-witted Vahikas are such.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: एतन्मया श्रुतं तत्र धर्मसंकरकारकम्। कृत्स्त्रामटित्वा पृथिवीं वाहीकेषु विपर्ययः॥
en: Having wandered over the entire earth I heard of these sinful practices and irregularities amongst the Vahikas.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: हन्त शल्य विजानीहि हन्त भूयो ब्रवीमे ते। यदप्यन्योऽबवीद् वाक्यं वाहीकानां च कुत्सितम्॥१०
en: You should know this, O Shalya; I will speak to you again these words blaming the Vahikas which another person said to me.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: सती पुरा हृता काचिदारट्टात् किल दस्युभिः। अधर्मतंश्योपयाता सा तानभ्यशपत् ततः॥
en: In the days of yore a chaste woman of the country of Aratta was abducted by robbers; they violated her, on which she imprecated a

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: बालां बन्धुमती यन्मामधर्मेणोपगच्छथ। तस्मानार्यो भविष्यन्ति बन्धक्यो वै कुलस्य च॥
en: As you have sinfully ravished a girl who has no husband all the women of your families will become unchaste.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: न चैवास्मात् प्रमोक्षध्वं घोरात् पापानराधमाः। तस्मात् तेषां भागहरा भागिनेया न सूनवः॥
en: You villains, you will never escape the consequences of this great iniquity. It is for this O Shalya, that the sisters sons of the Arattas become their heirs and not their own sons,

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: कुरवः सहपञ्चाला: शाल्वा मत्स्याः सनैमिषाः। कोसलाः काशपौण्ड्राश्च कालिङ्गा मागधास्तथा।॥ चेदयंश्च महाभागा धर्मं जानान्ति शाश्वतम्। नानादेशेषु सन्तंश्च प्रायो बाह्यलयादृते॥
en: Kauravas with the Panchalas, the Shalyas, the Matsyas, the Naimishas, the Koshalas, the Kashapaunctras, the Kalingas, the Maghadas and the Chedis, who are all blessed, are conversant with the eternal religion. Even the wicked of every country know what religion is; the Balhikas are however divested of piety.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: आ मत्स्येभ्यः कुरुपञ्चालदेश्या आ नैमिषाचेदयो ये विशिष्टाः। धर्म पुराणमुपजीवन्ति सन्तो मद्रादृते पाञ्चनदांश्च जिह्यान्॥
en: The Matsyas, the Kurus, the Panchalas, the Naimishas and all other respectable races know the eternal truths of religion. This cannot be said of the Madrakas and the wily people that live in the land of the five rivers.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: स्तूष्णीभूतो जडवच्छल्य भूयाः। त्वं तस्य गोप्ता च जनस्य राजा षड्भागहर्ता शुभदृष्कृतस्य॥
en: Knowing all these, O Shalya, O king, you should hold your tongue like one of base words in all matters connected with religion and virtue. You are the guardian and the king of this race and therefore partake of the tenth part of their virtue and sin.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: अथवा दुष्कृतस्य त्वं हर्ता तेषामरक्षिता। रक्षिता पुण्यभागाजा प्रजानां त्वं ह्यपुण्यभाक्॥
en: Or perhaps you pertake of the sixth portion of their sins only for you never protect them. A king who protects his people is only entitled to the sixth portion of their virtue. You are not a sharer of their virtue.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: पूज्यमाने पुरा धर्मे सर्वदेशेषु शाश्वते। धर्मं पाञ्चनदं दृष्ट्वा धिगित्याह पितामहः॥
en: In the days of yore when the eternal religion was held in reverence in all countries, the grand-father, marking the conduct of those living in the land of five rivers, denounced them.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: व्रात्यानां दासमीयानां कृतेऽप्यशुभकर्मणाम्। ब्रह्मणा निन्दिते धर्मे स त्वं लोके किमब्रवीः॥
en: When even in the golden age the Brahman had consumed those fallen men of evil deeds who were begotten by Sudra on others' wives who can put them to shame?

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: इति पाञ्चनदं धर्ममवमेने पितामहः। स्वधर्मस्थेषु वर्षेषु सोऽप्येतान् नाभ्यपूजयत्॥
en: Thus did the grand-father condemn the practices of the land of five rivers. When all the people observed the duties of their respective orders he had to find fault with those people.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: हन्त शल्य विजानीहि हन्त भूयो ब्रवीमि ते। कल्माषपादः सरसि निमजन् राक्षसोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: You should know all this, O Shalya, I will speak again to you. A Rakshasa by the name of Kamalashapada, while bathing in a tank said.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: क्षत्रिस्य मलं भक्ष्यं ब्राह्मणस्याश्रुतं मलम्। मलं पृथिव्यां वाहीकाः स्त्रीणां मद्रस्त्रियो मलम्॥२३
en: Begging is a Kshatriya's dirt, the nonobservance of vows is that of Brahmana. The Vahikas are the dirt of the earth and the Madra women are the dirt of the whole female sex.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: निमज्जमानमुद्धत्य कश्चिद् राजा निशाचरम्। अपृच्छत् तेन चाख्यातं प्रोक्तवांस्तन्निबोध मे॥
en: While going down the stream a king rescued the Rakshasa. Asked by the former the latter gave this answer. I will recite it to you, listen.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: मानुषाणां मलं म्लेच्छा म्लेच्छाना मौष्ट्रिका मलम्। शौण्डिकानां मलं घण्ढाः षण्ढानां राजयाजकाः॥२५
en: The Mlechas are the dirt of the humanity, the oil-men are the dirt of Mlechas; eunuchs are the dirt of oilmen. And they who appoint Kshatriyas as priests in their yagnas are the dirt of eunuchs.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: राजयाजकयाज्यानां मद्रकाणां च यन्मलम्। तद् भवेद् वै तव मलं यद्यस्मान विमुञ्चसि॥
en: The sin of those persons who appoint Kshatriyas as their priests as well as that of the Madrakas will visit you if you do not abandon me.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: इति रक्षोपसृष्टेषु विषवीर्यहतेषु च। राक्षसं भैषजं प्रोक्तं संसिद्धवचनोत्तरम्॥
en: This was declared by the Rakshasa as the Mantra that should be used as a remedy for curing a person possessed by a Rakshasa or one killed by poison.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: ब्राह्यं पञ्चालाः कौरवेयास्तु धर्म्य सत्यं मत्स्याः शूरसेनाश्च यज्ञम्। प्राच्या दासा वृषला दाक्षिणात्याः स्तेना वाहीका: संकरा वै सुराष्ट्राः॥
en: The Panchalas observe the duties laid down in the Vedas; the Kauravas observe truth; the Matsyas Surasena perform Yajnas; the people of the east follow the conduct of the Sudras. Those of the south are fallen; the Bahikas are thieves, the Saurashtras are bastards.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: कृतघ्नता परवित्तपहारो मद्यपानं गुरुदारावमर्दः। वावपारुष्यं गोवधो रात्रिचर्या बहिर्गेहं परवस्त्रोपभोगः॥
en: They are defiled by ingratitude, theft, drunkenness, adultery with the wives of their preceptors, harshness of speech, slaughter of kine, absence from house during night for bad purposes, the using of other people's ornaments. What sin is there that they cannot commit? Fie on Arathas and the people of the land of the five rivers.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: येषां धर्मस्तान् प्रति नास्त्यधर्मो ह्यारट्टानां पञ्चनदान धिगस्तु। आ पाञ्चाल्येभ्यः कुरवो नैमिषाश्च मत्स्याश्चैतेऽप्यथ जानन्ति धर्मम्। अथोदीच्याश्चाङ्गका मागधाश्च शिष्टान् धर्मानुपजीवन्ति वृद्धाः॥
en: The Panchalas, the Kauravas, the Naimishas, the Matsyas all these are conversant with religion. Even the old people of the North, the Angas and Magadhas follow the practice of the pious.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: प्राची दिशं श्रिता देवा जातवेदः पुरोगमाः। दक्षिणां पितरो गुप्तां यमेन शुभकर्मणा॥
en: Many gods, led by Agni, reside in the East. The ancestral manes live in the South presided our by Yama the just.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: प्रतीची वरुणः पाति पालयानः सुरान् बली। उदीची भगवान् सोमो ब्राह्मणैः सह रक्षति॥
en: The West is ruled over by the powerful Varuna, who is superior to all the gods there. The North is guarded by the Divine along with the Brahmanas.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: तथा रक्षः पिशाचाच हिमवन्तं नगोत्तमम्। गुह्यकाश्च महाराज पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्॥
en: The Rakshasas and Pichashas protect Himavat, the best of mountains. The Guhykas protect, O great king, the mount Gandhamadana. Forsooth does Vishnu otherwise called Janardana all creatures.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: ध्रुवः सर्वाणि भूतानि विष्णुः पाति जनार्दनः। इङ्गितज्ञाश्च मगधाः प्रेक्षितज्ञाश्च कोसलाः॥
en: The Magadhas are conversánt with hints, the Koshalas can understand what they see. The Kurus and Panchalas can understand halfexpressed words. The Shalyas cannot understand till the whole thing is expressed.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: अर्थोक्ताः कुरुपञ्चालाः शाल्वाः कृत्स्नानुशासनाः। पर्वतीयाच विषमा यथैव शिवयस्तथा॥
en: The mountaineers like Sivis are very dull. The Yavanas are omniscient, O king and the Suras and particularly so.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: सर्वज्ञा यवना राजशूश्चैव विशेषतः। म्लेच्छाः स्वसंज्ञानियता नानुक्तमितरे जनाः॥
en: The Mlechchas are steeped in their own fanciful creations-other inferior people cannot understand any thing. Bahikas never accept good counsels and Madrakas are none amongst protect them. You are such, O Shalya, you should not give me any reply.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: प्रतिरथास्तु वाहिका न च केचन मद्रकाः। स त्वमेतादृशः शल्य नोत्तरं वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Madras are called the dirt of all nations on earth so the Madra woman is called the dirt of the entire female sex.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: साधोः पानं गुरुतल्यावमर्दो भ्रूणहत्या परवित्तापहारः। येषां धर्मस्तान् प्रति नास्त्यधर्म आरट्टजान् पञ्चनदान् धिगस्तु॥
en: There is none more wretched than he whose duty consists in drinking wine, violating the bed of his preceptor, destroying the embryo by miscarriage and robbing other people of their riches. Oh fie on the Arthas and the people of the land of five rivers.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: एतज्ज्ञावा जोषमास्स्व प्रतीपं मा स्म वै कृथाः। मा त्वां पूर्वमहं हत्वा हनिष्ये केशवार्जुनौ॥
en: Knowing this, be silent. do not try to contradict me. Do not make me kill Keshava and Arjuna after having killed you first.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: शल्य उवाच आतुराणां परित्याग: स्वदारसुतविक्रयः। अङ्गे प्रवर्तते कर्ण येषामधिपतिर्भवान्॥
en: Shalya said To forsake the distressed and sell children with wives are the practices of Angas whose king you are, O Karna.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: रथातिरथसंख्यायां यत् त्वां भीष्मस्तदाब्रवीत्। तान् विदित्वाऽऽत्मनो दोषान् निर्मन्युभव मा क्रुधः॥४
en: Remembering your faults that were recited by Bhishma before the assembled car-warriors and mighty car-warriors drive away your anger and be not angry.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: सर्वत्र ब्राह्मणा सन्ति सन्ति सर्वत्र क्षत्रियाः। वैश्याः शूद्रास्तथा कर्ण स्त्रियः साध्व्यश्च सुव्रताः॥
en: In every country, O Karma, there are Brahmanas, the Kshatriyas, the Vaishyas, the Sudras and the chaste women observant of good vows.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: रमन्ते चोपहासने पुरुषाः पुरुषैः सह अन्योन्यमवतक्षन्तो देशे देशे समैथुनाः॥
en: In every country there are kings observant of their own religions and engaged in repressing the wicked. And in every country there are virtuous men.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: परवाच्येषु निपणः सर्वो भवति सर्वदा। आत्मवाच्यं न जानीते जानन्नपि च मुह्यति॥
en: There is in every country and every moment men who are experts in speaking of the faults of others. There is none who knows his own faults and knowing them becomes ashamed.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: सर्वत्र सन्ति राजानः स्वं स्वं धर्ममनुव्रताः। दुर्मनुष्यान् निगृह्णन्ति सन्ति सर्वत्र धार्मिका॥
en: In every country there are kings observant of their own religions and engaged in repressing the wicked. And in every country there are virtuous men.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: न कर्ण देशसामान्यात् सर्वः पापं निषेवते। यादृशाः स्वस्वभावेन देवा अपि न तादृशा॥
en: There is no country, O Karma, where every one is sinful. There are men in many countries who excel even the gods by their good conduct.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: संजय उवाच ततो दुर्योधन राजा कर्णशल्याववारयत्। सखिभावेन राधेयं शल्यं स्वाञ्जल्यकेन च॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon the king Duryodhana stopped Karna Shalya, addressing the son of Radha as a friend and requesting Shalya with joined hands.

description: The end of wordy war-fare between Karna and Shalya
sn: ततो निवारितः कर्णो धार्तराष्ट्रेण मारिष। कर्णोऽपिनोत्तरं प्राह शल्योऽप्यभिमुखः परान्। ततः प्रहस्य राधेयः पुनर्याहीत्यचोदयत्॥
en: Karna was pacified, Osire and did not speak anything more. Shalya, then advanced against his enemies. Thereupon smilingly Karna once more excited Shalya saying-"go on."

sn: संजय उवाच ततः परानीकसहं व्यूहमप्रतिमं कृतम्। समीक्ष्य कर्णः पार्थनां धृष्टद्युम्मभिरक्षितम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon beholding that unrivalled arrangement of the army of Partha protected by Dhristadyumna who was capable of resisting all hostile armies Karna.

sn: प्रययौ रथघोषेण सिंहनादरवेण च। वादित्राणां च निनदैः कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्॥
en: Proceeded sending up leonine shouts and making his chariot produce a loud rattle. He made the earth tremble with the loud din of musical instruments.

sn: वेपमान इव क्रोधाद् युद्धशौण्डः परंतपः। प्रतिव्यूह्य महातेजा यथावद् भरतर्षभ।॥
en: That chastiser of foes, irrepressible in battle, seemed to tremble in anger. Then arranging his own army in counter array, that hero of great energy, O best of Bharatas.

sn: व्यधमत् पाण्डवीं सेनामासुरीं मघवानिव। युधिष्ठिरं चाभ्यहनदपसव्यं चकार ह॥
en: Made a great havoc of the Pandava army like Indra killing the Asura army. Then wounding Yudhishthira with many arrows he placed the son of Pandu to his right.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कथं संजय राधेयः प्रत्यव्यूहत पाण्डवान्। धृष्टद्युम्नमुखान् सर्वान् भीमसेनाभिरक्षितान्॥ सर्वानेव महेष्वासानजय्यानमरैरपि। के च प्रपक्षौ पक्षौ वा मम सैन्यस्य संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said How did, O Sanjaya, the son of Radha arrange his army against the Pandavas led by Dhristadyumna and protected by Bhimasena-all those great bowmen invincible even to the very gods. Who stood, O Sanjaya, at the one wing and at the other of my army?

sn: प्रविभज्य यथान्यायं कथं वा समवस्थिताः। कथं पाण्डुसुताश्चापि प्रत्यव्यूहन्त मामकान्॥
en: Dividing themselves duly how were they stationed? How did also the sons of Pandu arrange their army against mine?

sn: कथं चैव महद् युद्धं प्रावर्तत सुदारुणम्। क्व च बूभत्सुरभवद् यत् कर्णोऽयाद् युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: And how did that great and dreadful battle began? Where was Vibhatsu when Karna proceeded against Yudhishthira?

sn: को हर्जुनस्य सान्निध्ये शक्तोऽभ्येतुं युधिष्ठिरम्। सर्वभूतानि यो ह्येकः खाण्डवे जितवान् पुरा। कस्तमन्यस्तु राधेयात् प्रतियुद्ध्येजिजीविषुः॥
en: Who could successfully assail Yudhishthira before Arjuna? Who else except the son of Radha, who wishes to keep his life, would fight with Arjuna who had defeated single-handed formerly all creatures at Khandava?

sn: संजय उवाच शृणु व्यूहस्य रचनामर्जुनश्च यथा गतः। परिवार्य नृपं स्वं संग्रामश्चाभवद् यथा॥
en: Sanjaya said Hear now of the arrangement of the army and how Arjuna came and how the battle was fought by both sides encircling their respective kings.

sn: कृपः शारद्वतो राजन् मागधाश्च तरस्विनः। सात्वतः कृतवर्मा च दक्षिणं पक्षमाश्रिताः॥
en: O king, Saradvata's son Kripa, the highly active Magadhas and Kritavarma of the Satvata race stood at the right wing.

sn: तेषां प्रपक्षे शकुनिरुलूकश्च महारथः। सादिभिर्विमलप्रासैस्तवानीकमरक्षताम्॥ गान्धारिभिरसम्भ्रान्तः पर्वतीयैश्च दुर्जयैः। शलभानामिव वातैः पिशाचैरिव दुर्दशैः॥
en: Standing at the right of these and accompanied by many dauntless Gandhara horse-men armed with bright lances and many invincible mountaineers numerous swarms of locusts and grim-visaged as the as the cars W Pishachas, Shakuni and the powerful carwarrior Uluka protected the Kuru army.

sn: चतुस्त्रिंशत्सहस्राणि रथानामनिवर्तिनाम्। संशप्तका युद्धशौण्डा वाम पार्श्वमपालयन्॥ समन्वितास्तव सुतैः कृष्णार्जुनजिघांसवः।
en: Thirty-four thousand of the Samsaptakas never to come back from the battle-field mad after fight, encircling your son and desirous of killing Krishna and Arjuna, protected the left side.

sn: तेषां प्रपक्षाः काम्बोजाः शकाश्च यवनैः सह॥ निदेशात् सूतपुत्रस्य सरथाः साश्वपत्तयः। आह्वयन्तोऽर्जुनं तस्थुः केशवं च महाबलम्॥
en: The Kambojas, the Sakas, the Yavanas, with their cars, horses and infantry stood on this left challenging Arjuna and the powerful Kesava.

sn: मध्ये सेनामुखे कर्णोऽप्यवातिष्ठत दंशितः। चित्रवर्माङ्गदः स्त्रग्वी पालयन् वाहिनीमुखम्॥
en: In the centre, stood Karna at the head of the army, clad in armour and a beautiful coat of mail and adorned with bracelets and garlands, for protecting it.

sn: रक्षमाणैः सुसंरब्धैः पुत्रैः शस्त्रभृतां वरः। वाहिनीं प्रमुख वीरः सम्प्रकर्षन्नशोभत॥ अभ्यवर्तन्महाबाहुः सूर्यवैश्वानरप्रभः।
en: Endued with the effulgence of the moon and fire, beautiful to look at and with twany eyes, protected by his greatly angry sons, that hero, the foremost of the wielders of weapons, shone at the head of his army drawing his bow.

sn: महाद्विपस्कन्धगत: पिङ्गाक्ष प्रियदर्शनः॥ दुःशासनो वृतः सैन्यैः स्थितौ व्यूहस्य पृष्ठतः।
en: The mighty-armed Dushasana, encircled by his soldiers, stood at the back of the army on a huge elephant and proceeded therefrom.

sn: तमन्वयान्महाराज स्वयं दुर्योधन नृपः॥ चित्रास्त्रैचित्रसंनाहै: सोदयैरभिरक्षितः। रक्ष्यमाणो महावीर्यैः सहितैर्मद्रकेकयैः॥ अशोभत महाराज देवैरिव शतक्रतुः।
en: Protected by the highly energetic Madrakas and Kekayas the king shone there like the performer of hundred sacrifices surrounded by the celestials. Then followed him, O emperor, the king Duryodhana himself protected by his own brothers, clad in beautiful mails and riding on beautiful horses.

sn: अश्वत्थामा कुरूणां च ये प्रवीरा महारथाः॥ नित्यमत्ताश्च मातङ्गाः शूरैर्लेच्छैः समान्विताः । अन्वयुस्तद् स्थानीकं क्षरन्त इव तोयदा॥
en: Ashvatthama and other leading car-warriors and many infuriate elephants shedding temporal juice, resembling a mass of clouds and driven by brave Mlechchas followed that car force.

sn: ते ध्वजैर्वैजयन्तीभिर्व्वलद्भिः परमायुधैः। सादिभिश्चास्थिता रेजुर्द्रमवन्त इवाचलाः॥
en: With Vaijayanti flags, shining weapons and riders they appeared like hills filled with trees.

sn: तेषां पदातिनागानां पादरक्षा सहस्रशः। पट्टिशासिधराः शूरा बभूवुरनिवर्तिनः॥
en: The rear of that elephant army was protected by thousands of horses with swords and Patticas never to return back from battle.

sn: सादिभिः स्यन्दनै गैरधिकं समलङ्कृतेः। स व्यूहराजो विबभौ देवासुरचमूपमः॥
en: Brilliantly adorned with cavalry, carwarriors and elephants that best of armies looked exceedingly picturesque like that of that of the gods or of the demons.

sn: बार्हस्पत्यः सुविहितो नायकेन विपश्चिता। नृत्यतीव महाव्यूहः परेषां भयमादधत्॥
en: That army arranged after the plan of Vrihaspati by its expert commander appeared to dance and strike terror into the hearts of the enemies.

sn: तस्य पक्षप्रपक्षेभ्यो निष्पतन्ति युयुत्सवः। पत्यश्वरतमातङ्गाः प्रावृषीव बलाहकाः॥
en: Like the continual clouds of the rainy season, the infantry, cavalry, car-warriors and elephants, desirous of battle, began to issue from all the wings.

sn: ततः सेनामुखे कर्णं दृष्ट्वा राजा युधिष्ठिरः। धनंजयममित्रघ्नमेकवीरमुवाच ह॥
en: Beholding Karna at the head of the army Yudhishthira addressed the following words to Dhananjaya, that slayer of foes, the one heroes in the battle.

sn: पश्यार्जुन महाव्यूहं कर्णेन विहितं रणे। युक्तं पक्षैः प्रपक्षैश्च परानीकं प्रकाशते॥
en: Behold, O Arjuna, the great army arranged by Karna. The enemy's army shines with all its wings.

sn: तदेतद् वै समालोक्य प्रत्यमित्रं महद् बलम्। यथा नाभिभवत्यस्मांस्तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम्॥
en: In the face of such a huge army you should take such precautions as we may not be defeated.

sn: एवमुक्तोऽर्जुनो राज्ञा प्राञ्जलिर्नुपमब्रवीत्। यथा भवानाह तथा तत् सर्वेन तदन्यथा।॥
en: Thus accosted by the king, Arjuna replied with joined hands “Every thing will be done as you say. Nothing will be otherwise."

sn: यस्त्वस्य विहितो घातस्तं करिष्यामि भारत। प्रधानवध एवास्य विनाशस्तं करोम्यहम्॥
en: I will bring about the destruction of the enemy, O Bharata. By killing the head of this encompass their destruction.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच तस्मात् त्वमेव राधेयं भीमसेनः सुयोधनम्। वृषसेनं च नकुलः सहदेवोऽपि सौबलम्॥ दुःशासनं शतानीको हार्दिक्यं शिनिपुङ्गवः। धृष्टद्युम्नो द्रोणसुतं स्वयं योत्स्याम्यहं कृपम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said Having this in view you yourself proceed against the son of Radha; let Bhimasena proceed against Suyodhana; Nakula against Vrihsena, Sahadeva against the son of Subala, Satanika against Dushasana the best of Sinis; Shalyaki against the son of Hridika and Pandya against the son of Drona. I myself will fight with Kripa. army, I will

sn: द्रौपदेया धार्तराष्ट्रशिष्टान् सह शिखण्डिना। ते ते च तांस्तानहितानस्माकं मन्तु मामकाः॥
en: Let the sons of Draupadi, with Shikhandin proceed against the remaining sons of Dhritarashtra. Let the other heroes proceed against the rest of our enemies.

sn: संजय उवाच इत्युको धर्मराजेन तथेत्युक्त्वा धनंजयः। व्यादिदेश स्वसैन्यानि स्वयं चागाचमूमुखम्॥
