en: Sanjaya said Thus addressed by the pious Yudhishthira, Dhananjaya said-'so be it' and ordered his army. He then himself proceeded to the head.

sn: अग्निर्वैश्वानरः पूर्वो ब्रह्मेद्धः सप्तितां गतः। तस्माद् यः प्रथमं जातस्तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: Keshava and Arjuna proceeded to battle on that prime car, for which the leader of the universe Agni who derives his effulgence from Brahman became the horses and

sn: ब्रह्मेशानेन्द्रवरुणान् क्रमशो योऽवहत् पुरा। तमाद्यं रथमास्थाय प्रयातौ केशवार्जुनो॥
en: Sri Krishna and Arjuna were marching forward to enemies for attack on an ancient chariot used by Brahma, Rudra, Indra and Varuna respectively for riding during ancient period.

sn: अथ तं रथमायान्तं दृष्ट्वात्यद्भुतदर्शनम्। उवाचाधिरथिं शल्यः पुनस्तं युद्धदुर्मदम्॥
en: Beholding that wonderful car advance Shalya once more addressed the following words to that highly energetic warrior the son of Adhiratha.

sn: अयं सरथ आयातः श्वेताश्वः कृष्णसारथिः। दुर्वारः सर्वसैन्यानां विपाकः कर्मणामिव॥ निघ्नन्नमित्रान् कौन्तैयो यं कर्ण परिपृच्छसि।
en: There comes the car drawn by white horses and having Krishna as its driver, the car which even all the soldiers cannot resist as the fruit follows the work. There comes the son of Kunti slaying all his foes along the way, he of whom you were inquiring.

sn: श्रूयते तुमुलः शब्दो यथा मेघस्वनो महान्॥ ध्रुवमेतौ महात्मनौ वासुदेवधनंजयौ।
en: Undoubtedly they are the great Vasudeva and Arjuna as a tremendous uproar deep as the muttering of clouds is being heard.

sn: एष रेणुः समुद्भूतो दिवमावृत्य तिष्ठति॥ चक्रनेमिप्रणुन्नेव कम्पते कर्ण मेदिनी।
en: A cloud of dust is overspreading the welkin like a canopy. The whole earth, O Arjuna, is shaking cut deep by the wheels of Arjuna's cars.

sn: प्रवात्येष महावायुरभितस्तव वाहिनीम्॥ क्रव्यादा व्याहरन्त्येते मृगाः क्रन्दन्ति भैरवम्।
en: Violent winds are raging on both the sides of the army. The carnivorous animals are yelling aloud and the animals are emitting dreadful cries.

sn: पश्य कर्ण महाघोरं भयदं लोमहर्षणम्॥ कबन्धं मेघसंकाशं भानुमावृत्य संस्थितम्।
en: Behold, O Arjuna, the dreadful and evil Ketu of vapoury form, capable of making hairs erect. It has appeared covering the sun.

sn: पश्य यूथैर्बहुविधैगाणां सर्वतोदिशम्॥ बलिभिर्दृप्तशार्दूलैरादित्योऽभिनिरीक्ष्यते।
en: Behold various sorts of animals in large numbers and many powerful wolves and tigers are looking at the sun.

sn: पश्य कङ्कांश्च गृध्राश्च समवेतान् सहस्रशः॥ स्थितानभिमुखान् घोरानन्योन्यमभिभाषतः।
en: Behold those terrible Kankas and vultures in thousands sitting with faces towards one another as if holding a conversation.

sn: रञ्जिताश्चामरा युक्तास्तव कर्ण महारथे॥ प्रवराः प्रज्वलन्त्येते ध्वजश्चैव प्रकम्पते।
en: O Karna, the coloured chowries attached to your huge car are waving roughly and your pennon is also trembling.

sn: सवेपथून् हयान् पश्य महाकायान् महाजवान्॥ प्लवमानान् दर्शनीयानाकाशे गरुडानिवा
en: See, your beautiful and large horses endued with great speed resembling the beautiful Garuda in the sky, are also trembling.

sn: ध्रुवमेषु निमित्तेषु भूमिमाश्रित्य पार्थिवाः॥ स्वप्स्यन्ति निहताः कर्ण शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
en: It is evident from these evil omens O Karna, that hundreds and thousands of kings, deprived of their lives, will sleep the eternal sleep in the field of battles.

sn: शङ्खानां तुमुलः शब्दः श्रूयते लोमहर्षणः॥ आनकानां च राधेय मृदङ्गानां च सर्वशः।
en: There is being heard the hair-stirring and loud sound of the conch. The sound of drums and cymbals, O son of Radha, is being also heard on all sides.

sn: बाणशब्दान् बहुविधान् नराश्वरगज वाजिनाम्॥ ज्यातलत्रेषुशब्दांश्च शृणु कर्ण महात्मनाम्।
en: The whizz of the various sorts of shafts and the noise of chariots, horses and men is also being heard. Listen, O Karna, to the twang of the bows of the various warriors.

sn: हेमरूप्यप्रसृष्टानां वाससां शिल्पिनिर्मिताः॥ नानावर्णा रथे भान्ति श्वसनेन प्रकम्पिताः।
en: Many flags of diverse colours and embroidered with gold, made by skillful artisans and shining on Arjuna's car shaken by the wind.

sn: सहेमचन्द्रतारार्काः पताकाः किङ्किणीयुताः॥ पश्य कर्णार्जुनस्यैताः सौदामन्य इवाम्बुदे।
en: See, O Karna, also the banners of Arjuna, adorned with rows of bells and golden moons and stars, like lightning on the clouds.

sn: ध्वजाः कणकणायन्ते वातेनाभिसमीरिताः॥ विभ्राजन्ति रथे कर्ण विमान दैवते यथा।
en: Those banners, producing a sound, are being shaken by the wind; the high-souled Panchalas with their cars decked with flags look like the gods on their cars.

sn: सपताका रथाश्चैते पञ्चालानां महात्मनाम्॥ पश्य कुन्तीसुतं वीरं बीभत्सुमपराजितम्। प्रधर्षयितुमायान्तं कपिप्रवरकेतनम्॥
en: Behold the heroic Vibhatsu, the son of Kunti, invincible in battle and having a flag with the emblem of a monkey, is coming forward to assail his enemies.

sn: एष ध्वजाये पार्थस्य प्रेक्षणीयः समन्ततः। दृश्यते वानरो भीमो द्विषतामघवर्धनः॥
en: On the top of Partha's banner a dreadful monkey is being seen capable of increasing the anger of the enemies.

sn: एतचक्रं गदा शाई शङ्खः कृष्णस्य धीमतः। अत्यर्थ भ्राजते कृष्णे कौस्तुभस्तु मणिस्ततः॥
en: These are the discus, club, Sranga bow and the conch of the intelligent Krishna. The Kaustava jewel appears beautiful (on the breast of) Krishna.

sn: एष शङ्खगदापाणिर्वासुदेवोऽतिवीर्यवान्। वाहयन्नेति तुरगान् पाण्डुरान् वातरंहसः॥
en: The highly energetic Vasudeva with club and Sranga bow in his hands is driving the yellow horses cndued with speed of the wind.

sn: एतत् कूजति गाण्डीवं विकृष्टं सव्यसाचिना। एते हस्तवता मुक्ता घ्नन्त्यमित्राशिताः शराः॥
en: This is the twang of the bow Gandiva drawn by Savyasachin. These sharpened arrows discharged off his hands will kill the enemies.

sn: विशालायतताम्राक्षैः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननैः। एषा भूः कीर्यते राज्ञां शिरोभिरपलायिनाम्॥
en: The earth is strewn with the heads of the kings who never come back from the battlefield, having expansive coppery eyes and faces like the full moon.

sn: एते सुपरिधाकाराः पुण्यगन्धानुलेपनाः। उद्यतायुधशौण्डानां पात्यन्ते सायुधा भुजाः॥
en: There are falling, the arms, resembling the spiked maces, with weapons and smeared with scents, of warriors taking delight in fight and contending with uplifted weapons.

sn: निरस्तनेत्रजिह्वाश्च वाजिनः सह सादिभिः। पतिताः पात्यमानाश्च क्षितौ क्षीणाश्च शेरते॥
en: Horses with eyes, tongues and entrails drawn out, with their riders and falling, fallen and lie dead on earth.

sn: एते पर्वतशृङ्गाणां तुल्यरूपा हता द्विपाः। संछिन्नभिन्नाः पार्थेन प्रपतन्त्यद्रयो यथा॥
en: Wounded, mangled and pierced by Partha, lifeless elephants, huge as mountain tops, are falling down like hills.

sn: गन्धर्वनगराकारा रथा हतनरेश्वराः। विमानानीव पुण्यानि स्वर्गिणी नियतन्त्यमी॥
en: The cars, resembling the cities of the Gandharvas, with the kings slain are falling down like the celestial cars, on the wane of the piety of the inhabitants of heaven.

sn: व्याकुलकृतमत्यर्थं पश्य सैन्यं किरीटिना। नानामृगसहस्राणां यूथं केसरिणा यथाय॥
en: Behold, the army has been greatly assailed by Kiritin as various animals are by a lion.

sn: जन्त्येते पार्थिवान् वीराः पाण्डवाः समभिद्रुताः। नागाश्वरथपत्योघांस्तावकान् समभिघ्नतः॥
en: Coming forward the heroic Pandavas are killing the kings, a good many elephants, horses, car-warriors and foot soldiers of your army engaged in battle.

sn: एष सूर्य इवाम्भोदैश्छन्नः पार्थो न दृश्यते। ध्वजायं दृश्यते त्वस्य ज्याशब्दश्चापि श्रूयते॥
en: Partha is not visible like the sun covered with clouds. The top of his car is being seen and the twang of his bow is being heard.

sn: अद्य द्रक्ष्यसि तं वीरं श्वेताश्चं कृष्णसारथिम्। निघ्नन्तं शात्रवान् संख्ये यं कर्ण परिपृच्छसि॥
en: You will see him today, O Karna, about whom you are inquiring-that hero, with white horses and Krishna as his driver engaged in killing the enemies in battle.

sn: अद्य तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ लोहिताक्षौ परंतपौ। वासुदेवार्जुनौ कर्ण द्रष्टास्येकरथे स्थतौ॥
en: You will see today, O Karna, stationed on the same car in battle those two foremnost of men with coppery eyes-the subduers of enemies-Krishna and Arjuna.

sn: सारथिर्यस्य वार्ष्णेयो गाण्डीवं यस्य कार्मुकम्। तं चेद्धन्तासि राधेन त्वं नो राजा भविष्यसि॥
en: O son of Radha, you will be our king if you can slay him today who has Krishna for his driver and Gandiva for his bow.

sn: एष संशप्तकाहूतस्तानेवाभिमुखो गतः। करोति कदनं चैषां संग्रामे द्विषतां बली॥
en: Challenged by Samsaptakas Partha proceeds against them; the powerful warrior is making a great havoc of his enemies in battle.

sn: इति ब्रुवाणं मद्रेश कर्णः प्राहातिमन्युना। पश्य संशप्तकैः क्रुद्धैः सर्वतः समभिद्रुतः॥
en: Thereupon Karna in anger said to the king of Madras who had spoken thus. "See Partha is being assailed on all sides by the Samsaptakas.

sn: एष सूर्य इवाम्भोदैश्छन्नः पार्थो न दृश्यते। एतदन्तोऽर्जुनः शल्य निमग्नो योधसागरे॥
en: Like the sun covered by cloud Partha is no longer visible. Plunged into the deep of warriors O Shalya, Partha is sure to die."

sn: शल्य उवाच वरुणं कोऽम्भसा हन्यादिन्धनेन च पावकम्। को वानिलं निगृह्णीयात् पिबेद्वा को महार्णवम्।।७६
en: Shalya said Who is there who can slay the god of water with water and fire with fuel? Who is there who can get hold of the wind or drink off the ocean?

sn: ईदृग्रुपमहं मन्ये पार्थस्य युधि विग्रहम्। न हि शक्योऽर्जुनो जेतुं युधि सेन्द्रैः सुरासरैः॥
en: Methinks, to assail Partha is just like this. Even the very gods and demons united together with Indra at their head cannot discomfit Arjuna in battle.

sn: अथवा परितोषस्ते वाचोक्त्वा सुमना भव। न स शक्यो युधा जेतुमन्यं कुरु मनोरथम्॥
en: Better satisfy yourself and make your mind comfortable by saying this. Partha is not to be conquered in battle. Better fulfill some other object you may have in view.

sn: बाहुभ्यामुद्धरेद् भूमि दहेत् क्रुद्धः इमा प्रजाः। पातयेत् त्रिदिवाद् देवान् योऽर्जुनं समरे जयेत्॥
en: He who will lift up the earth on his two arms, or consume all creatures with his wrath of hurl down the gods from heaven, may defeat Arjuna in battle.

sn: पश्य कुन्तीसुतं वीरं भीममकिष्टकारिणम्। प्रभासन्तं महाबाहु स्थितं मेरुमिवापरम्॥
en: Behold Bhima, the other heroic son of Kunti who is never worn out with fatigue, shining in his native lustre, mighty armed and is like the second Meru.

sn: अमर्षी नित्यसंरब्धश्चिर वैरमनुस्मरन्। एष भीमो जयेप्रेप्सुर्युधि तिष्ठति वीर्यवान्॥
en: With his anger always burning, bent on wrecking revenge the highly energetic Bhima stands there with a view to acquire victory, remembering all his wrongs.

sn: एष धर्मभृताः श्रेष्ठो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। तिष्ठत्यसुकरः संख्ये परैः परपुरञ्जयः॥
en: There stands the impartial king Yudhishthira, the foremost of the pious and the conqueror of enemies' cities. The enemies can never resist him in battle.

sn: एतौ च पुरुषव्याघ्रावश्विनाविव सोदरौ। नकुलः सहदेवश्च तिष्ठतो युधि दुर्जयौ॥
en: There stand the twins Nakula Sahadeva, the two Asvinis, the two foremost of men, invincible in battle.

sn: अमी स्थिता द्रौपदेयाः पञ्च पञ्चाचला इव। व्यवस्थिता योद्धुकामाः सर्वेऽर्जुनसमा युधि॥
en: There stand the five Vrishni heroes like five inountains desirous of lighting all equal to Arjuna in battle.

sn: एते दुपदपुत्राश्च धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः। स्फीताः सत्यजितो वीरास्तिष्ठन्ति परमौजसः॥
en: There stand the proud, beautiful heroic and highly energetic sons of Draupadi headed by Dhristadyumna.

sn: असाविन्द्र इवासह्यः सात्यकिः सात्वतां पुरः। युयुत्सुरुपयात्यस्मान् क्रुद्धान्तकसमः पुरः॥
en: There advances against us Satyaki, the foremost of the Satvatas, irresistible like Indra, with view to fight like Death himself in anger.

sn: इति संवदतोरेव तयोः पुरुषसिंहयोः। ते सेने समसज्जेतां गङ्गायमुनवद् भृशम्॥
en: While these two best of men were thus speaking to each other the two armies encountered in battle like the streams of Ganga and Yamuna. While these two best of men were thus speaking to each other the two armies encountered in battle like the streams of Ganga and Yamuna.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तथा व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु संसक्तेषु च संजय। संशप्तकान् कथं पार्थो गतः कर्णश्च पाण्डवान्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said While armies thus encountered each other, did Partha, O Sanjaya, assail the Samsaptakas and Karna the Pandavas.

sn: एतद् विस्तरशो युद्धं प्रब्रूहि कुशलो ह्यासि। न हि तृप्यामि वीराणां शृण्वानो विक्रमान् रणे॥
en: Skilled in narration as you are, recount at length the incidents of the battle to me. I am never satiated with listening to the accounts of the prowess of heroes.

sn: संजय उवाच तदास्थितमवज्ञाय प्रत्यमित्रबलं महत्। अव्यूहतार्जुनो व्यूहं पुत्रस्य तव दुर्नये॥
en: Sanjaya said Disregarding the huge hostile array arranged in that way Arjuna rayed his force in proper form on account of the evil policy of your son.

sn: तत् सादिनागकलिलं पदातिरथसंकुलम्। धृष्टद्युम्नमुखं व्यूहमशोभत महद् बलम्॥
en: The huge army of the Pandavas, abounding in infantry, cavalry, elephants and cars and led by Dhristadyumna, looked magnificent.

sn: पारावतसवर्णाश्वश्चन्द्रादित्यसमद्युतिः। पार्षतः प्रबभौ धन्वी कालो विग्रहवानिव॥
en: With his horses white as the pigeons and endued with the effulgence of the sun or the moon the son of Prishata, with bow in hand, shone like Death himself in body.

sn: पार्षतं जुगुपुः सर्वे द्रौपदेया युयुत्सवः। दिव्यवर्मायुधधराः शार्दूलसमविक्रमाः॥ सानुगा दीप्तवपुषश्चन्द्रं तारागणा इव।
en: The sons of Draupadi desirous of fighting stood by the side of the son of Prishata. They had celestial coats of mail and weapons and were powerful like tigers. They followed him like stars following the moon.

sn: अथ व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु प्रेक्ष्य संशप्तकान् रणे॥ क्रुद्धोऽर्जुनोऽभिदुद्राव व्याक्षिपन् गाण्डिवं धनुः।
en: Beholding he Samsaptakas in battle array, Arjuna, worked up with anger, rushed against them, drawing his Gandiva bow.

sn: अथ संशप्तकाः पार्थमभ्यधावन् वधैषिणः॥ विजये धृतसंकल्पा मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्।
en: With a view to kill Arjuna the Samsaptakas bent upon acquiring victory, advanced against him, making death their end.

sn: तन्नराश्वौधबहुलं मत्तनागरथाकुलम्॥ पत्तिमच्छूरवीरौधं दुतमर्जुनमार्दयत्।
en: Those brave warriors with men, horses, infuriate elephants and cars began quickly to assail Arjuna.

sn: स सम्प्रहारस्तुमुलस्तेषामासीत् किरीटिना॥ तस्यैव नः श्रुतो यादृनिवातकवचैः सह।
en: Furious was their encounter with Kiritin. It resembled that between Arjuna and Nivata Kavachas, as we have heard.

sn: रथानश्वान् ध्वजान नागान् पतीन् रणगतानपि॥ इघून धनूंषि खड्गाश्च चक्राणि च परश्वधान्। सायुधानुद्यतान् बाहून् विविधान्यायुधानि च॥ चिच्छेद द्विषतां पार्थः शिरांसि च सहस्रशः।
en: Thousands and thousands of cars, horses, flags, elephants, foot-soldiers engaged in fighting, arrows, bows, swords, discus, battle axes, uplifted arms holding weapons and heads of enemies were cut by Partha.

sn: तस्मिन् सैन्यमहावर्ते पातालतलसंनिभे॥ निमग्न त रथं मत्वा नेदुः संशप्तकास्नथा।
en: Considering his car drowned into that whirlpool of warriors resembling the bed of the was nether region the Samsaptakas sent up loud war-cries.

sn: स पुनस्तानरीन् हत्वा पुनरुत्तरतोऽत्वधीत्॥ दक्षिणेन च पश्चाच क्रुद्धो रुद्रः पशूनिव।
en: Slaying all his enemies in front Partha killed those that stood at a distance, then those that were on his right and back like Rudra himself killing in anger the entire animate creation.

sn: अथ पञ्चालचेदीनां संजयानां च मारिष॥ त्वदीयैः सह संग्राम आसीत् परमदारुणः!
en: And exceedingly dreadful the encounter of your army with the Panchalas, Chedis and Srinjayas.

sn: कृपश्च कृतवर्मा च शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः॥ हृष्टसेनाः सुसंरब्धा रथानीकप्रहारिणः। कोसलैः काश्यमत्स्यैश्च कारुषैः केकयैरपि॥ शूरसेनैः शूरवरैर्युयुधुर्युद्धदुर्मदाः।
en: Kripa, Kritavarma, Shakuni, the son of Subala, with cheerful soldiers, all greatly worked up with anger and capable of striking the car-warriors fought with Kosalas, the Kachis, Matsyas, Karushas, Kekayas and Surasenas all of whom were highly terrible in battle.

sn: तेषामन्तकरं युद्धं देहपाप्मासुनाशनम्॥ क्षत्रविट्शूद्रवीराणां धर्म्य स्वर्ग्य यशस्करम्।
en: That great battle, destructive of life, body and sins, brought on fame, virtue and heaven for all the Kshatriya, Vaishyas and Sudra heroes that engaged in it.

sn: दुर्योधनऽथ सहितो भ्रातृर्भिरतर्षभ॥ गुप्तः कुरुप्रवीरैश्च मद्राणां च महारथैः। पाण्डवैः सह पञ्चालैश्चैदिभिः सात्यकेन च॥ युध्यमानं रणे कुरुवीरो भ्यपालत्।
en: O best of Bharatas, meanwhile, the king Duryodhana, with all his brothers and Kuru heroes and many powerful Madraka carwarriors, protected Karna while he fought with the Pandavas, the Panchalas, the Chedis and Satyaki.

sn: कर्णोऽपि निशितैर्बाणैर्विनिहत्य महाचमूम्॥ प्रमृद्य च रथश्रेष्ठान् युधिष्ठिरमपीडयत्।
en: Destroying that huge army with his sharpened arrows and assailing many leading car-warriors Karna afflicted Yudhishthira.

sn: विवस्त्रायुधदेहासून कृत्वा शत्रून् सहस्रशः॥ युक्त्वा स्वर्गयशोभ्यां च स्वेभ्यो मुदमुदावहत्।
en: Sundering the armour, weapons and bodies of thousands of his enemies, killing them by thousands and sending them to heaven to earn fame Karna gave great delight to his friends.

sn: एवं मारिष संग्रामो नरवाजिगजक्षयः। कुरूणां सृञ्जयानां च देवासुरसमोऽभवत्॥
en: Thus, O father, the battle, putting the Kurus and Srinjayas resembled that between the gods and demons in the days of yore.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यत्तत् प्रविश्य पार्थानां सैन्यं कुर्वञ्जनक्षयम्। कर्णो राजानमभ्येत्य तन्माचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Tell me, O Sanjaya, how Karna, having caused a great carnage and entered into the midst of the Pandavas assailed the king Yudhishthira.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: के च प्रवीराः पार्थानां युधि कर्णमवारयन्। कांश्च प्रमथ्याधिरथियुधिष्ठिरमपीडयत्॥
en: What leading warriors amongst the Pandavas resisted Karna? Whom did Karna crush before he could assail Yudhishthira?

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: संजय उवाच धृष्टद्युम्नमुखान् पार्थान् दृष्ट्वा कर्णो व्यवस्थितान्। समभ्यधावत्त्वरितः पञ्चालाञ्छत्रुकर्षिणः॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing the followers of the Pandavas led by Dhristadyumna stationed for battle, Karna, the subduer of foes, rushed furiously against the Panchalas.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: तं तूर्णमभिधावन्तं पञ्चाला जितकाशिनः। प्रत्युद्ययुर्महात्मानं हंसा इव महार्णवम्॥
en: The Panchalas, desirous of victory, advanced against that high-souled one who came quickly as the swans go to the ocean.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः शङ्खसहस्राणां निःस्वनो हृदयङ्गम। प्रादुरासीदुभयतो भेरीशब्दश्च दारुणः॥
en: Then there arose from both the armies the sound of a thousand conches capable striking terror into hearts as well as that of bugles.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: नानाबाणनिपाताश्च द्विपाश्वरथनिःस्वनः। सिंहनादच वीराणामभवद् दारुणस्तदा॥
en: Then there arose the dreadful sound of warriors other musical instruments, the noise of the elephants, horses and cars and leonine shouts of the heroes.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: साद्रिद्रुमार्णवा भूमि: सवाताम्बुदमम्बरम्। सार्केन्दुग्रहनक्षत्रा द्यौश्च व्यक्तं विघूर्णितः॥
en: The entire earth with her mountains, trees and oceans, the sky enshrouded with clouds driven by the wind and the whole firmament with the sun and the moon, scemed to tremble.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: इति भूतानं तं शब्दं मेनिरे ते च विव्यथुः। यानि चाप्यल्पसत्त्वानि प्रायस्तानि मृतानि च॥
en: So dreadful appeared the noise to all creatures and they became all agitated. The weak amongst them fell dead.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: अथ कर्णो भृशं क्रुद्धः शीघ्रमस्त्रमुदीरयन्। जघान पाण्डवीं सेनामासुरीं मघवानिव॥
en: Then worked with great anger and invoking speedily his weapons Karna began to assail the Pandava host like Indra grinding the army of the demons.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: स पाण्डवबलं कर्णः प्रविश्य विसृजञ्छरान्। प्रभद्रकाणां प्रवरानहनत् सप्तसप्ततिम्॥
en: Entering into the midst of the Pandava army and discharging his arrows furnished with beautiful wings of that best of car-warriors (Karna) killed seventy-seven five Prabhadrakas.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः सुपुडैनिशितै स्थश्रेष्ठो रथेषुभिः। अवधीत् पञ्चविंशत्या पञ्चालान् पञ्चविंशतिम्॥
en: Karna, the best chariot warrior shot twenty five arrows having decent wings and beheaded twenty five Panchalas.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: सुवर्णपुढे राचैः परकायविदारणैः। चेदिकानवधीद वीरः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: With many gold feathered Narachas capable of piercing others bodies the hence killed hundred and thousands of the Chedis.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: तं तथा समरे कर्म कुर्वाणमतिमानुषम्। परिवर्महाराज पञ्चालानां रथव्रजाः॥
en: While he was performing those superhuman feats in battle a large number of Panchala cars surrounded him quickly on all sides, O king.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः संधाय विशिखान् पञ्च भारत दुःसहान्। पञ्चालानवधीत् पञ्च कर्णो वैकर्तनो वृषः॥
en: O Bharata, then setting five dreadful arrows Karna, the son of Vikartana, killed five Panchalas.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: भानुदेवं चित्रसेनं सेनाबिन्दुं च भारत। तपनं शूरसेन च पञ्चालानहनद् रणे॥
en: He killed in battle the Panchalas-Bhanudeva, Chitrasena, Senabindu, Tapana and Shurasena.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: पञ्चालेषु च शूरेषु वध्यमानेषु सायकैः। हाहाकारो महानासीत् पञ्चालानां महाहवे॥
en: The heroic Panchalas being thus killed with arrows there arose lamentations Alas! and Oh of the Panchalas in that great battle.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: परिवर्महाराज पञ्चालानां रथा दश। पुनरेव च तान् कर्णो जघानाशु पतत्रिभिः॥
en: Then ten car-warriors amongst Panchalas surrounded Karna whom all he quickly killed with arrows.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: चक्ररक्षौ तु कर्णस्य पुत्रौ मारिष दुर्जयौ। सुषेण: सत्यसेननश्च त्यक्त्वा प्राणानयुध्यताम्॥
en: Then the two protectors of Karna's carwheels, his two invincible sons, Sushena and Satyasena began to fight reckless of their lives.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: पृष्ठगोप्ता तु कर्णस्य ज्येष्ठः पुत्रो महारथः। वृषसेनः स्वयं कर्ण पृष्ठतः पर्यपालयत्॥
en: The powerful car-warrior Vrishasena, the eldest son of Karna, himself protected his father's rear.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नः सात्यकिश्च द्रौपदेया वृकोदरः। जनमेजयः शिखण्डी च प्रवीराश्च प्रभद्रकाः॥ चेदिकेकयपञ्चाला यमौ मत्स्याश्च दंशिताः। सम्भ्यधावन् राधेयं जिघांसन्तः प्रहारिणम्॥
en: Thereupon, Dhristadyumna, Satyaki, the five sons of Draupadi, Vrikodara, Janmejaya, Shikhandin and many leading warriors among Probhadrakas and many amongst the Chedis, the Kekayas and the Panchalas, the twins, the Matsyas, all clad in mail rushed upon Karna to kill him.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: त एनं विविधैः शस्त्रैः शरधाराभिरेव च। अभ्यवर्षन् विमर्दन्तं प्रावृषीभाम्बुदा गिरिम्॥
en: Showering upon him various kinds of weapons and arrows they began to assail him like the clouds striking the mountain breast during the rainy season.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: पितरं तु परीप्सन्तः कर्णपुत्राः प्रहारिणः। त्वदीयाश्चारे राजन् वीरा वीरानवारयन्॥
en: To rescue their father, the sons of Karna all of whom were sinless and many heroes of your army resisted them.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: सुषेणो भीमसेनस्य च्छित्त्वा भल्लेन कार्मुकम्। नाराचैः सप्तभिर्विद्ध्वा हृदि भीमं ननाद ह॥
en: Cutting off with a broad headed bow, that of Bhimasena, Sushena pierced him on the breast with seven Narachas and made a loud war-cry.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय सुदृढं भीमविक्रमः। सज्यं वृकोदरः कृत्वा सुषेणस्याच्छिनद् धनुः॥
en: Thereupon taking up another strong bow and setting it right in haste the highly powerful Vrikodara cut-off Sushena's bow.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: विव्याध चैन दशभिः क्रुद्धो नृत्यन्निवेषुभिः। कर्णं च तूर्णं विव्याधि त्रिसप्तत्या शितैः शरै॥
en: Worked up with anger and as if dancing on his car he quickly bored through Sushena with ten arrows and pierced Karna himself with seventy sharp arrows within the twinkling of an eye.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: भानुसेनं च दशभिः साश्वसूतायुधध्वजम्। पश्यतां सुहृदां मध्ये कर्णपुत्रमपातयत्।॥
en: Then with ten other arrows Bhima struck down Bhanusena, another son of Karna, with horses, drivers, arms and flags before the eyes of his friends.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: क्षुरप्रणुन्नं तत्तस्य शिरश्चन्द्रनिभाननम्। शुभदर्शनमेवासीन्नालभ्रष्टमिवाम्बुजम्॥
en: Sundered by a razor-headed shaft the beautiful head of the youth with a moon-like countenance appeared like a lotus plucked from its stalk.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: हत्वा कर्णसुतं भीमस्तावकान् पुनरार्दयत्। कृपहार्दिक्ययोश्छित्त्वा चापौ तावप्यथार्दयत्॥
en: Having killed Karna's son Bhima began to assail your army once more; sundering the bows of Kripa and Hridika's son he began to assail those two heroes.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: दुःशासनं त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा शकुनि षड्भिरायसैः। उलूकं च पतत्रिं च चकार विरथावुभौ॥
en: Striking Dushasana with ten iron arrows and Shakuni with six he deprived both Uluka and Patatri of their cars.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: सुषेणं च हतोऽसीति बुवन्नादत्त सायकम्। तमस्य कर्णश्चिच्छेद त्रिभिश्चैनमताडयत्॥
en: Then saying to Sushena "you are killed” Bhima took up another arrow. Karna cut it off and pierced Bhima himself with three arrows.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: अथान्यं परिजग्राह सुपर्वाणं सुतेजनम्। सुषेणायासृजद् भीमस्तमप्यस्याच्छिनद् वृषः॥
en: Bhimasena shot at Sushena another sharp edge and decent knot arrow but Karna cut-off the same in pieces too.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: पुनः कर्णस्त्रिसप्तत्या भीमसेनपथेषुभिः। पुत्रं परीप्सन् विव्याध क्रूरं क्रूरैर्जिघांसया॥
en: With a view to save his son and kill the ruthless Bhima Karna struck the former with seventy-three dreadful arrows.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: सुषेणस्तु धनुर्गृह्य भारसाधानमुक्तमम्। नकुलं पञ्चभिर्बाणैर्पाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्॥
en: Then taking up an excellent bow capable of bearing a great strain Sushena struck Nakula on the arms and the chest with five arrows.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: नकुलस्तं तु विंशत्या विद्ध्वा भारसहैईलैः। ननाद बलवन्नादं कर्णस्य भयमादधत्॥
en: Striking his antagonist with twenty strong arrows capable of bearing a strain Nakula too sent up a loud war-cry and struck terror unto Karna.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: तं सुषेणो महाराज विद्ध्वा दशभिराशुगैः। चिच्छेद च धनुः शीघ्र क्षुरप्रेण महारथः॥
en: Then striking Nakula with ten arrows, the powerful car-warrior Sushena, quickly cut-off his bow with a razor headed arrows.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय नकुलः क्रोधमूर्छितः। सुषेणं नवभिर्बाणैर्वारयामास संयुगे॥
en: Then Nakula, beside himself with anger, took up another bow and withstood Sushena with nine arrows.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: स तु बाणैर्दिशो राजन्नाच्छाद्य परवीरहा। आजघ्ने सारथिं चास्य सुषेणं च ततस्त्रिभिः॥ चिच्छेद चास्य सुदृढं धनुर्भल्लैस्त्रिभिस्त्रिधा।
en: Then, O king, covering all the quarters with arrows that subduer of hostile heroes killed Sushena's driver, striking Sushena himself with three arrows and then sundered into pieces his highly strong bow with three Bhallas.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय सुषेणः क्रोधमूर्छितः। आविध्यन्नकुलं षष्ट्या सहदेवं च सप्तभिः।
en: Then beside himself with anger Sushena took up another bow and pierced Nakula with sixty arrows and Sahadeva with seven.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: तद् युद्धं सुमहद् घोरमासीद् देवासुरोपमम्॥ निघ्नतां सायकैस्तूर्णमन्योन्यस्य वधं प्रति।
en: Then there took place a dreadful encounter between those heroes striking one another like that between the gods and demons.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: सात्यकिवृर्षसेनस्य सूतं हत्वा त्रिभिः शरैः॥ धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन जघानाश्वांश्च सप्तभिः। ध्वजमेकेषुणोन्मथ्य त्रिभिस्तं हृद्यताडयत्॥
en: Having killed Vrishasena's driver with three arrows Satyaki sundered his bow with a Bhalla and killed his horses with seven arrows. Then crushing down his standard with another arrow he struck Vrishasena himself on the breast with three arrows.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: अथावसन्नः स्वरथे मुहूर्तात् पुनरुत्थितः। स रणे युयुधानेन विसूताश्वरथध्वजः॥ कृतो जिघांसुः शैनेयं खड्गचर्मधृगभ्ययात्।
en: Deprived of his driver, horses, chariot and flags by Yuyudhana, thus struck Vrishasena became senseless on his car but stood up again within the twinkling of an eye. Vrishasena, armed with sword and shield, then rushed against him with a view to kill him.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: तस्य चापततः शीघ्र वृषसेनस्य सात्यकिः॥ वाराहकणैर्दशभिरविध्यदसिचर्मणी।
en: As his antagonist advanced against him Satyaki struck at his sword and shield len arrows with heads like a boar's ear.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: दुःशासनस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा विरथं व्यायुधं कृतम्॥ आरोप्य स्वरथं तूर्णमपोवाह रणातुरम्।
en: Seeing Vrishasena deprived of his car and weapons Dushasana placing him on his own car then speedily put him on another.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: अथान्यं रथमास्थाय वृषसेनो महारथः॥ द्रौपदेयांस्त्रिसप्तत्या युयुधानं च पञ्चभिः। भीमसेनं चतुःषष्टया सहदेवं च पञ्चभिः॥ नकुलं त्रिशता बाणैः शतानीकं च सप्तभिः। शिखण्डिनं च दशभिधर्मराजं शतेन च॥ एतांश्चान्यांश्च राजेन्द्र प्रवीराञ्जयगृद्धिनः। अभ्यर्दयन्महेष्वासः कर्णपुत्रो विशाम्पते॥ कर्णस्य युधि दुर्धर्षस्ततः पृष्ठमपालयत्।
en: Then riding on another car the powerful car-warrior Vrishasena pierced the five sons of Draupadi with seventy-three and Yuyudhana with five, Bhimasena with sixty four, Sahadeva with five, Nakula with thirty, Shatanika with seven, Shikhandin with ten and king Yudhishthira with a hundred arrows. O monarch, the great bowman, the son of Karna continually assailed with arrows those and many leading heroes all having victory in view. The invincible Vrishasena protected the rear of Karna in battle.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: दुःशासन च शैनेयो नवैर्नवभिरायसैः॥ विसूताश्वरथं कृत्वा ललाटे त्रिभिरार्पयत्।
en: Having deprived Dushasana of his driver, horses and car, with ninety nine iron arrows the grandson of Sini struck him then on his forehead with nine arrows.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: स त्वन्यं रथमास्थाय विधिवत् कल्पित पुनः॥ युयुधे पाण्डुभिः सार्धं कर्णस्याप्याययन् बलम्।
en: Then riding on another car properly equipped once more he began to fight with the, Pandavas from within the division of Karna.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्ततः कर्णमविध्यद् दशभिः शरैः॥ द्रौपदेयास्त्रिसप्तत्या युयुधान्स्तु सप्तभिः। भीमसेनश्शुतःषष्ट्या सहदेव सप्तभिः॥ नकुलस्त्रिंशता बाणैः शतानीकस्तु सप्तभि। शिखण्डी दशभिर्वीरो धर्मराजः शतेन तु॥
en: Then Dhristadyumna pierced Karna with ten arrows, the sons of Draupadi pierced him with sevenly three arrows and Satyaki with seven. Bhimasena pierced him with sixty four arrows and Sahadeva with seven. Nakula pierced him with thirty arrows and Shatanika with seven. The heroic Shikhandin pierced him with ten and king Yudhishthira with a hundred.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: एते चान्ये च राजेन्द्र प्रवीरा जयगृद्धिनः। अभ्यर्दयन् महेष्वासं सूतपुत्रं महामृधे॥
en: Worked up with the desire of victory those and other foremost of men began to assail that great men, Suta's son, in that terrible battle.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: तान् सूतपुत्रो विशिखैर्दशभिर्दशभिः शरैः। रथेश्चारुचरन् वीरः प्रत्यविध्यदरिंदमः॥
en: Moving about in his car the heroic son of the charioteer, the subduer of foes, pierced each of them with ten arrows.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: तत्रास्त्रवीर्यं कर्णस्य लाघवं च महात्मनः। अपश्याम महाभाग तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: There, O monarch, we witnessed the wonderful strength in the handling of weapons and the light-handedness of the high-souled Karna.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: न ह्याददानं ददृशुः संदधानं च सायकान्। विमुञ्चन्तं च संरम्भादपश्यन्त हतानरीन्॥
en: People could not mark when he took up his arrows, when he ained them and when he discharged them. They only saw his enemies slain by his anger.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: द्यौर्वियद्धर्दिशश्चैव प्रपूर्णानिशितैः शरै। अरुणाभ्रावृताकारं तस्मिन् देशे बभौ वियत्॥
en: The sky, the earth and the firmament were filled with his sharpened arrows. The firmament looked brilliant as if covered with clouds smitten with the rays of the sun.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: नृत्यन्निव हि राधेयश्चापहस्तः प्रतापवान्। यैर्विद्धः प्रत्यविद्धयत् तानेकैकं त्रिगुणैः शरै॥
en: The highly powerful son of Radha, with bow in his hand, as if dancing, pierced each of his antagonists with thrice as many shafts as each of them had struck him with.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: दशभिर्दशभिश्चैतान् पुनर्विद्ध्वा ननाद च। साश्वसूतरथच्छत्रांस्ततस्ते विवरं ददुः॥
en: Once more striking each of them and his horses, drivers, car and flag with ten arrows he sent up a loud war-cry. His antagonist then gave him a way.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: तान् प्रमथ्य महेष्वासन् राधेयः शरवृष्टिभिः। राजानीकमसम्बाधं प्राविशच्छत्रुकर्शनः॥
en: Having crushed those powerful bowmen with showers of arrows, the son of Radha, the subduer of foes, entered unopposed into the thick of the army led by the Pandava king.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: स रथंस्त्रिशतं हत्वा चेदीनामनिवर्तिनाम्। राधेयो निशितैर्बाणैस्ततोऽभ्याईद् युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Having broken down thirty chariots of the Chedis who never return from the battle-field the son of Radha pierced Yudhishthira with many sharp arrows.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततस्ते पाण्डवा राजशिखण्डी च ससात्यकिः। राधेयात् परिरक्षन्तो राजानं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: With a view to rescue the king from the son of Radha many Pandava warriors, with Shikhandin and Satyaki surrounded him.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: तथैव तावकाः सर्वे कर्ण दुर्वारणं रणे। यत्ताः शूरा महेष्वासाः पर्यरक्षन्त सर्वशः॥
en: So did the powerful and brave bowinen of your army firmly guard the irresistible Karna in that battle.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: नानावादित्रघोषाश्च प्रादुरासन् विशाम्पते। सिंहनादश्च संजज्ञे शूराणामभिगर्जताम्॥
en: O king, then there arose the sound of various musical instruments and the leonine roars of brave heroes rent the sky.

description: The fight between Karna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः पुनः समाजग्मुरभीताः कुरुपाण्डवाः। युधिष्ठिरमुखाः पार्थाः सूतपुत्रमुखा वयम्॥
en: The Kurus and Pandavas once undauntedly met with each other, the former led by Karna and the latter by Yudhishthira. more

sn: संजय उवाच विदार्य कर्णस्तां सेनां युधिष्ठिरमथाद्रवत्। रथहस्त्यश्वपत्तीनां सहस्रः परिवारितः॥
en: Sanjaya said Riving through that army Karna encountered the pious king surrounded by thousands of cars, elephants, horses and footsoldiers.

sn: नानायुधसहस्राणि प्रेरिततान्यरिभिर्वृषः। छित्वा बाणशतैरुगैस्तानविध्यदसम्भ्रमात्॥
en: Sundering with hundreds of dreadful shafts the thousands of arms discharged at him by his enemies Karna fearlessly went through the army.

sn: निचकर्त शिरांस्येषां बाहूनूरूंश्च सूतजः। ते हता वसुधां पेतुर्भग्नाश्चान्ये विदुद्रुवः॥
en: The charioteer's son sundered the heads, the arms and the things of his enemies who, deprived of life, fell down on earth. Others, finding their division dispersed, took to their heels.

sn: द्राविडास्तु निषादास्तु पुनः सात्यकिचोदिताः। अभ्यद्रवञ्जिघांसन्तः पत्तयः कर्णमाहवे॥
en: The Dravida, the Andhaka and the Nishada infantry, excited by Satyaki once more rushed upon Karna with a view to kill him in that battle.

sn: ते विबाहुशिरस्त्राणाः प्रहताः कर्णसायकैः। पेतुः पृथिव्यां युगपच्छिन्नं शालवनं यथा॥
en: Shorn of their arms and head-dresses and killed by Karna with his arrows they fell down all at once on earth like a forest of Sala trees cut down.

sn: एवं योधशतान्याजौ सहस्राण्ययुतानि चः। तानीयुर्महीं देहैर्यशसा पूरयन्दिशः॥
en: Deprived of life and filling the heaven and earth with their fame, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands of warriors fell down with their bodies on earth.

sn: अत वैकर्तनं कर्णं रणे क्रुद्धमिवान्तकम्। रुरुधुः पाण्डुपाञ्चाला व्यार्घि मन्त्रौषधैरिव॥
en: The Pandus and Panchalas obstructed Karna, the son of Vikartana who proceeded in anger to battle like the destroyer himself even as people seek to obstruct a disease with incantations and drugs.

sn: स तान् प्रमृद्याभ्यपतत् पुनरेव युधिष्ठिरम्। मन्त्रौषधिक्रियातीतो व्याधिरत्युल्बणौ यथा॥
en: Grinding all those combatants Karna once more rushed upon Yudhishthira like irresistible disease unchecked by incantations, drugs and rites.

sn: स राजगृद्धिभी रुदः पाण्डुपञ्चालाकेकयौः। नाशकत् तानतिक्रान्तुं मृत्युब्रह्मविदो यथा॥
en: Then obstructed by Pandus, Panchalas and Kekayas who were all desirous of rescuing the king he could not overcome them as Death cannot those conversant with Brahman.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरः कर्णमदूरस्थं निवारितम्। अब्रवीत् परवीरनं क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः॥
en: Thereupon beholding Karna, the slayer of hostile heroes, obstructed at a distance, an Yudhishthira, with eyes reddened with anger, said-

sn: कर्ण कर्ण वृथादृष्टे सूतपुत्र वचः शृणु। सदा स्पर्धसि संग्रामे फाल्गुनेन तरस्विना॥ तथास्मान् बाधसे नित्यं धार्तराष्ट्रमते स्थितः।
en: O Karna, O son of a charioteer, O you of vain seeing, hear my words, You always challenge in fight Phalguna of quick speed. Abiding by the counsel of the son of Dhritarashtra you always obstruct us.

sn: यद् बलं यच ते वीर्यं प्रद्वेषो यस्तु पाण्डषु॥ तत् सर्वं दर्शयस्वाद्य पौरुषं महदास्थितः। युद्धश्रद्धां च तेऽद्याहं विनेष्यामि महाहवे॥
en: You bring all your strength, energy and hatred to bear upon the Pandus. Do you display today all your great manliness. I will today give battle and destroy your desire for fight.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज कर्णं पाण्डुसुतस्तदा। सुवर्णपुबैर्दशभिर्विव्याधायस्मयैः शरैः॥
en: Having said this to Karna, the monarch, the son of Pandu, pierced him with ten arrows, made of iron and furnished with golden wings.

sn: तं सूतपुत्रो दशभिः प्रत्यविद्ध्यदरिंदमः। वत्सदन्तैर्महेष्वासः प्रहसन्निव भारत॥
en: Then that Suta's son, the subduer of foes and a great bowman, pierced him in return as if smiling, O Bharata, with ten arrows furnished with heads like the calf's tooth.

sn: सोऽवज्ञाय तु निर्विद्धः सूतपुत्रेण मारिष। प्रजज्वाल ततः क्रोधाद्धविषेव हुताशनः॥
en: Thus placed by Suta's son in contempt the mighty-armed heroes was worked up with anger like fire with oblation.

sn: ज्वालामालापरिक्षिप्तो राज्ञो देहो व्यदृश्यत। युगान्ते दग्धुकामस्य संवर्ताग्नेरिवापरः॥
en: The body of Yudhishthira surrounded by the flames of anger looked as if it was second Samvartaka fire intended to burn the whole universe, in course of the great devastation (Pralaya).

sn: ततो विस्फार्य सुमहचापं हेमपरिष्कृतम्। समाधत्त शितं बाणं गिरीणामपि दारणम्॥
en: Then stretching his huge bow made of gold he set sharp arrows capable of breaking down the mountains.

sn: ततः पूर्णायतोत्कृष्टं यमदण्डनिभं शरम्। मुमोच त्वरितो राजा सूतपुत्रजिघांसया॥
en: With a view to kill the Suta's son he drew his bow to its fullest stretch and discharged that fatal shaft as the rod of the destroyer himself.

sn: स तु वेगवता मुक्तो बाणो वज्राशनिस्वनः। विवेश सहसा कर्ण सव्ये पार्श्वे महारथम्॥
en: Discharged with great velocity and making a sound like that of a thunder bolt the arrow suddenly pierced the great car-warrior Karna on his left side.

sn: स तु तेन प्रहारेण पीडितः प्रमुमोह वै। स्त्रस्तगात्रो महाबाहुर्धनरुत्सृज्य स्यन्दने॥
en: Greatly assailed by the violence of that spike the powerful Karna, with weaked limbs, swooned away on his car his bow dropping from his hand.

sn: गतासुरिव निश्चेताः शल्यस्याभिमुखोऽपतत्। राजापि भूयो नाजघ्ने कर्ण पार्थहितेप्सया॥
en: He fell down unconscious in front of Shalya as if he was dead. King Yudhishthira did not attack again on Karna by keeping in mind the interest of Arjuna.

sn: ततो हाहाकृतं सर्व धार्तराष्ट्रबलं महत्। विवर्णमुखभूयिष्ठं कर्णं दृष्ट्वा तथागतम्॥
en: Seeing Karna in that state the huge army of Dhritarashtra's son exclaimed Oh! and alas! and the faces of all the warriors became pale.

sn: सिंहनादश्च संजज्ञे श्वेला: किलकिलास्तथा। पाण्डवानां महाराज दृष्ट्वा राज्ञः पराक्रमम्॥
en: O monarch, witnessing the power of their king the Pandava army sent up leonine roars and cries of joy.

sn: प्रतिलभ्य तु राधेयः संज्ञा नातिचिरादिव। दने राजविनाशाय मनः क्रूरपराक्रमः॥
en: Regaining his sense in no time the dreadful son of Radha made up his mind to kill Yudhishthira.

sn: स हेमविकृतं चापं विस्फार्य विजयं महत्। अवाकिरदमेयात्मा पाण्डवं निशितैः शरै॥
en: Drawing his dreadful bow made of gold, Vijaya, the valiant son of Suta, began to resist Pandu's son with his sharp arrows.

sn: ततः क्षुराध्यां पाञ्चाल्यौ चक्ररक्षौ महात्मनः। जघान चन्द्रदेवं च दण्डधारं च संयुगे॥
en: Then with two razor he killed in that battle Chandradeva and Dandadhara, the two Panchalas princes who guarded the wheels of the high-souled (Pandu king).

sn: तावुभौ धर्मराजस्य प्रवीरौ परिपार्श्वतः। स्थाभ्याशे चकाशेते चन्द्रस्येव पुनर्वसू॥
en: Each of those heroes stood by Yudhishthira shining like the constellation Punarvasu by the side of the moon.

sn: युधिष्ठिरं: पुन: कर्णमविद्धयतं त्रिंशता शरैः। सुषेणं सत्यसेनं च त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरताडयत्॥
en: Yudhishthira again struck Karna with thirty arrows. He pierced Sushena and Satyasena each with three arrows.

sn: शल्यं नवत्या विव्याध त्रिसप्तया च सूतजम्। तांस्तस्य गोप्तन् विव्याध त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरजिह्मगैः॥
en: He pierced Shalya with ninty and struk Karna with seventy-three arrows. He also struck every one of Karna's body guards with three straight arrows.

sn: ततः प्रहस्ताधिरथिर्विधुन्वानः स कार्मुकम्। भित्वा भल्लेन राजानं विद्ध्वा षष्टयाऽनदत्तदा॥
en: Then laughing and shaking his bow the son of Adhiratha wounded the king's body with a Bhalla, then pierce him with sixty arrows and then sent up a loud war-cry.

sn: तत: प्रवीराः पाण्डूनामभ्यधावन्नमर्षिताः। युधिष्ठिरं परीप्सन्तः कर्णमभ्यर्दयञ्छरैः॥
en: Then to rescue the king many leading Pandava warriors fell upon Karna in great anger and began to assail him with their arrows.

sn: सात्यकिश्चेकितानश्च युयुत्सुः पाण्डव एव च। धृष्टद्युम्नः शिखण्डी च द्रौपदेयाः प्रभद्रका॥ यमौ च भीमसेनश्च शिशुपालस्य चात्मजः। कारूषा मत्स्यशेषाश्च केकथाः काशिकोसलाः॥ एते च त्वरिता वीरा वसुषेणमताडयन्।
en: Satyaki, Chekitana, Yuyutshu, Shikhandin, the sons of Draupadi, the Prabhadrakas, the twins, Bhimasena, Shishupala, the Karushas, the Matsys, the Kaikeyas the Kashis and the Kosalas, all those valiant and highly active warriors assailed Vasushena.

sn: जनमेजयश्च पाञ्चाल्यः कर्णं विव्याध सायकैः॥ वाराहाकर्णनाराचैर्नालीकैर्निशितैः शरैः। वत्सदन्तैर्विपाठैश्च क्षुरप्रैश्चटकामुखैः॥ नानाप्रहरणैश्चोत्रै रथहस्तश्वसादिभिः। सर्वतोऽभ्यद्रवत् कर्णं परिवार्य जिघांसया॥
en: The Panchala prince Janamejaya then struck Karna with many arrows. Encircling Karna with a view to kill him they all rushed upon him with various arrows, such as boareared, Narachas, Nalika, Nishat, calf-toothed, Vipatha, razor shaped, with diverse other weapons chariots horses, elephants.

sn: स पाण्डवानां प्रवरैः सर्वतः समभिद्रुतः। उदीरयन् ब्राह्ममस्त्रं शरैरापूरयद् दिशः॥
en: Thus assailed on all sides by the leading Pandava warriors Karna invoked the assistance of the Brahma weapon and filled all the quarters with his arrows.

sn: ततः शरमहज्वालौ वीर्योष्मा कर्णपावकः। निर्दहन् पाण्डववनं वीरः पर्यचरद् रणे॥
en: Like burning fire having arrows for its scorching flame Karna fought on consuming that forest of Pandava troops.

sn: स संधाय महास्त्राणि महेष्वासा महामनाः। प्रहस्य पुरुषेन्द्रस्य शरैश्चिच्छेद कार्मुकम्॥
en: Aiming some powerful weapons and laughing the noble Karna, the great bowman, sundered the bow of that best of men, Yudhishthira.

sn: तत: संधाय नवति निमेषान्नतपर्वणाम्। बिभेद कवचं राज्ञो रणे कर्णः शितैः शरै॥
en: Thereupon aiming ninety straight arrows within the twinkling of an eye Karna cut-off, with those sharp arrows, the armour of his antagonist.

sn: तद् वर्म हेमविकृतं रत्नचित्रं बभौ पतत्। सविद्युदभ्रं सवितुः श्लिष्टं वातहतं यथा॥
en: Made of gold and set with jewels that armour looked beautiful as if it fell down like the cloud driven by the wind and smitten by the rays of the sun.

sn: तदङ्गात् पुरुषेन्द्रस्य भ्रष्टं वर्म व्यरोचत। रत्नलंकृत चित्रैर्व्यभ्रं निशि यथा नभः॥ छिन्नवर्मा शरैः पार्थो रुधिरेण समुक्षितः।
en: The armour, adorned with jewels fallen off the body of that foremost of men, appeared like the sky in the night bespangled with stars. Having his armour sundered with those arrows the son of Pritha covered with blood.

sn: ततः सर्वायसीं शक्तिं चिक्षेपाधिरथिं प्रति॥ तां ज्वलन्तीमिवाकाशे शरैश्चिच्छेद सप्तभिः। सा छिन्ना भूमिमगमन्महेष्वासस्य सायकैः॥
en: He hurled in anger at the son of Adhiratha a dart made of iron. He too cut of that (dart) shining in the sky with seven arrows; sundered with shafts by that great bowman it reached the earth.

sn: ततो बाह्वोर्ललाटे च हृदि चैव युधिष्ठिरः। चतुर्भिस्तोमरैः कर्णं ताडयित्वानदन्मुदा॥
en: Then striking Karna with four lances on his two arms, forehead and chest Yudhishthira again and again sent up loud shouts.

sn: उद्भिनरुधिरः कर्णः क्रुद्धः सर्प इव श्वसन्। ध्वजं चिच्छेद भल्लेन त्रिभिर्विव्याध पाण्डवम्॥ इषुधी चास्य चिच्छेद रथं च तिलशोऽच्छिनत्।
en: Then blood gushed out from Karna wounds. Then filled with anger breathing like a snake he cut-off his enemy's standard and struck Pandava with three Bhallas. He also cutoff his two quivers and car into pieces.

sn: कालवालास्तु ये पार्थं दन्तवर्णावहन् हयाः॥ तैर्युक्तं रथमास्थाय प्रायाद् राजा पराङमुखः।
en: Riding on the car drawn by horses white as teeth and having black hairs which used to bear Partha the king fled away from the battle-field.

sn: एवं पार्थोऽभ्युपायात् स निहतः पाणिंसारथिः॥ अशक्नुवन् प्रमुखतः स्थातुं कर्णस्य दुर्मनाः।
en: Unable to stand before Karna, thus did the son of Pritha, with his charioteer Parshin slain, cheerlessly fly away.

sn: अभिद्रुत्य तु राधेयः पाण्डुपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥ वज्रच्छत्रांकुशैर्मतस्यैर्ध्वजकूर्मम्बुजादिभिः। लक्षणैरुपपन्नेन पाण्डुना पाण्डुनन्दनम्॥ पवित्रीकर्तुमात्मानं स्कन्धे संस्पृश्य पाणिना। ग्रहीतुमिच्छन् स बलात् कुन्तीवाक्यं च सोऽस्मरत्॥
en: It seemed at the time when Karna, the son of Radha was chasing Yudhishthira as if he is intended to catch him forcibly so as to touch him on should with his fair colour hand having lucky marks as thunderbolt, umbrella, goad, fish, flag, tortoise and lotus etc. in order to attain purity. In the meantime, a memory of commitment he had made once before Kunti, chained his racing feet.

sn: तं शल्यः प्राह मा कर्ण गृहीथाः पार्थिवोत्तमम्। गृहीतमात्रो हत्वा त्वां मा करिष्यति भस्मसात्॥
en: King Shalya in the meantime made Karna alert by saying-"O Karna! Don't' touch king Yudhishthira at all nonetheless you should burn in the fire erupted due to anger within him. You touch may cause of death for you.

sn: अब्रवीत प्रहसन् राजन् कुत्सयन्निव पाण्डवम्। कथं नाम कुले जातः क्षत्रधर्मे व्यवस्थितः॥ प्रजह्यात् समरं भीतः प्राणान् रक्षन् महाहवे। न भवान् क्षत्रधर्मेषु कुशलो हीति मे मतिः॥
en: O king, said, smiling and censuring the son of Pandu-"In what family are you born? You are to observe the duties of a Kshatriya. Why do you leave the battle-field in haste, to save your life? Methinks, you do not know the duties of a Kshatriya.

sn: ब्राह्मे बले भवान् युक्तः स्वाध्याये यज्ञकर्मणि। मा स्म युद्ध्यस्व कौन्तेय मा स्म वीरान् समासदः॥
en: O son of Kunti, Endued with Brahma force, you are better fitted for the study of the Vedas and sacrificial rites.

sn: मा चैतानप्रियं ब्रूहि मा वै व्रज महारणम्। वक्तव्या मारिषान्से तु न वक्तव्यास्तु मादृशाः॥
en: Do not, O son of Kunti, fight again. Do not approach heroes and use harsh words towards them and do not go to great battles.”

sn: मादृशान् विद्वावन् युद्धे एतदन्यच्च लप्स्यसे। स्वगृहं गच्छ कौन्तेय यत्र तौ केशवार्जुनौ॥ न हि त्वां समरे राजन् हन्यात् कर्णः कथञ्चन।
en: This and another pains you would have to bear for inflicting harsh words upon the people like me. Hence, O son of Kunti, either go back to your home or march only in company of Sri Krishna and Arjuna. "O king! Karna will not slaughter you in battle-field."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततः पार्थ विसृज्य च महाबलः॥ न्यहनत् पाण्डवीं सेनां वज्रहस्त इवासुरीम्।
en: Having said this and left off the son of Pritha the highly powerful Karna began to slay Pandava like the holder of thunder-bolt, the army of Asuras.

sn: ततोऽपायाद् दुतं राजन् वीडन्निव नरेश्वरः॥ अथापयति राजानं मत्वान्वीयुस्तमच्युतम्। चेदिपाण्डवपञ्चालाः सात्यक्श्चि महारथः॥ द्रौपदेयास्तथा शूरा माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ।
en: Then the king Yudhishthira, O king, took to his heels quickly in great shame. Seeing the king take to his heels, the Chedis, the Pandavas, the Panchalas and the powerful carwarrior Satyaki, the heroic sons of Draupadi and the twin sons of Madri followed him of eternal glory.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरानीकं दृष्ट्वा पराङ्मुखम्॥ कुरुभिः सहिता वीरः प्रहृष्टः पृष्ठतोऽन्वगात्।
en: Thereupon beholding the retreat of the army of Yudhishthira the heroes pursued them in great delight.

sn: भेरीशङ्गमृदङ्गानां कार्मुकाणां च निःस्वनः॥ बभूव धार्तराष्ट्राणां सिंहनादरवस्तथा।
en: Then there arose the leonine shout of the sons of Dhritarashtra accompanied by the sound of bugles, conch, mridangas and the twang of bows.

sn: कर्ण: युधिष्ठिरस्तु कौरव्य रथमारुद्य सत्वरम्॥ श्रुतकीर्तेर्महाराज दृष्ट्वान् कर्णविक्रमम्।
en: O king, his horses become tired so getting upon quickly the car of Srutakirti, Yudhishthira began to witness the prowess of Karna.

sn: काल्यमानं बलं दृष्ट्वा धमराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥ स्वान् योधानब्रवीत् क्रुद्धो निघ्नतैतान् किमासत।
en: Then beholding his own army slain the pious king Yudhishthira said to his own warriors-"Kill them; why do you sit idle?"

sn: ततो राज्ञाभ्यनुज्ञाताः पाण्डवानां महारथः॥ भीमसेनमुखाः सर्वे पुत्रास्ते प्रत्युपाद्रवन्।
en: Thereupon obtaining the command of the king all the mighty car-warriors of the Pandavas headed by Bhimasena rushed upon your sons.

sn: अभवत् तुमुलः शब्दो योधानां तत्र भारत॥ रथहस्त्यश्वपत्तीनां शस्त्राणां च ततस्ततः।
en: O Bharata, then there arose a great tumult of the warriors, chariots, elephants, horses, infantry and weapons.

sn: उत्तिष्ठत प्रहरत प्रेताभिपततेति च॥ इति ब्रुवाणा ह्यन्योन्यं जघ्नुर्योधा महारणे।
en: “Rise, strike, face the foe" uttering those words the warriors killed one another in that great battle.

sn: अभ्रच्छायेव तन्नासीच्छरवृष्टिभिरम्बरे॥ समावृतैर्नरवरैर्निनद्भिरितरेतरम्।
en: On account of the showers of arrows discharged by them a shadow as that of clouds seemed to spread over the field abounding in the best of men killing those weaker then they.

sn: विपताकध्वच्छत्रा व्यश्वसूतायुधा रणे॥ व्यङ्गाङ्गावयवाः पेतुः क्षितौ क्षीणा:क्षितीश्वराः।
en: Deprived of their standards, flags, umbrellas, horses, drivers, weapons, armas and other limbs, the kings, weakened, fell down on earth.

sn: प्रवणादिव शैलानां शिखराणि द्विपोत्तमाः॥ सारोहा निहताः पेतुर्ववभिन्ना इवाद्रयः।
en: Resembling mountain summits, the best of elephants with their drivers slain, fell down like mountains clapped by thunderbolt.

sn: छिन्नभिन्नविपर्यस्तैर्वर्मालङ्कारभूषणैः॥ सारोहास्तुरगाः पेतुर्हरवीराः सहस्रशः।
en: With their armours and other equipments torn and shattered thousands of horses and warriors fell down.

sn: विप्रविद्धायुधाश्चैव द्विरदाश्वरथैर्हताः॥ प्रतिवीरैश्च सम्म पत्तिसंघाः सहस्रशः।
en: There fell in battle thousands of foot soldiers with their limbs wounded by weapons and deprived by hostile combatants of their elephants, horses and cars.

sn: विशालायतताम्राक्षैः पद्मेन्दुसदृशाननैः॥ शिरोभियुद्धशौण्डानां सर्वतः संवृत्ता मही। यथा भुवि तथा व्योम्नि नि:स्वनं शुश्रुवुर्जनाः॥ विमानैरप्सरः सङ्गैर्गीतवादिनि:स्वनैः।
en: The earth was covered all over with heads of heroes, dreadful in battle, with expansive coppery eyes and with faces resembling the lotus or the moon. People heard on the earth as well as in the sky noise proceeding, from the singing and music of the band of Apsaras going in celestial cars.

sn: हतानभिमुखान् वीरान् वीरैः शतसहस्रशः॥ आरोप्यारोप्य गच्छन्ति विमानेष्वप्सरोगणाः।
en: Having placed on their cars thousands of heroes slain in battle the Apsara went on.

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यं प्रत्यक्षं स्वर्गलिप्सया॥ प्रहष्टमनसः शूराः क्षिप्रं जघ्नुः परस्परम्।
en: Beholding that wonderful spectacle the heroes, desirous of attaining to heaven, quickly and delightedly killed one another.

sn: रथिनो रथिभिः सार्धं चित्र युयुधुराहवे॥ पत्तयः पत्तिभिर्नागा: सह नागैर्हयैर्हयाः।
en: In that battle the car-warriors fought wondrously with car-warriors, the infantry with infantry, the elephants with elephants and horses with horses.

sn: एवं प्रवृत्ते संग्रामे गजवादिनरक्षये॥ सैन्येन रजसा व्याप्ते स्वे स्वाञ्जघ्नुः परे परान्।
en: When the battle, destructive of elephants, horses and men, thus raged on the field was enshrouded with dust raised by the troops; the enemies then killed enemies and friends killed friends.

sn: कचाकचि युद्धमासीद् दन्तादन्ति नखानखि॥ मुष्टियुद्धं नियुद्धं च देहपाप्मासुनाशनम्।
en: Then there took place a skirmish destructive of life and sins-the warriors dragging one another by their locks, biting one another with their teeth, tearing one another with their nails and striking one another with their clenched fists and fighting with one another with bare arms.

sn: तथा वर्तति संग्रामे गजवाजिनरक्षये॥ नराश्वनागदेहेभ्यः प्रसृता लोहितापगा। गजाश्वनरदेहान् सा व्युवाह पतितान् बहून्॥
en: As that battle, destructive of elephants, horses and men, raged on fiercely a river of blood flew from the bodies of men, horses and elephants. That stream carried away many bodies of men, horses and elephants that fell there.

sn: नराश्वगजसम्बाधे नराश्वगजसादिनाम्। लोहितोदा महाघोरा मांसशोणितकर्दमा॥ नराश्वगजदेहानां सा वहन्ती भीरुभीषणा।
en: In that huge army abounding in men, horses and elephants, the river, formed by the blood of men, horses and elephants, became miry with flesh and that highly terrible river, striking terror into the timid, carried away the bodies of men, horses and elephants.

sn: तस्याः पारमपारं च व्रजन्ति विजयैषिणः॥ गाधेन चोप्लवन्तश्च निमज्योन्मज्य चापरे।
en: Some, desirous of victory, crossed it. Some plunged into its depths and some rose above its surface.

sn: तु लोहितदिग्धाङ्गा रक्तवर्मायुधाम्बराः॥ शस्त्रुस्तस्यां पपुश्चास्यां मम्लुश्च भरतर्षभ।
en: Their limbs, weapons and robes became all besmeared with blood. O foremost of Bharatas, some bathed in it, some drank its liquid.

sn: ते रथानश्वान् नरान नागानायुधाभरणानि च॥ वसनान्यथ वर्माणि वध्यमानान् हतानापि। भूमि खं द्यां दिशश्चैव प्रायः पश्याम लोहिताः॥
en: We saw the cars, horses, men, elephants, armours, ornaments, robes, coats of mail, earth, sky and heaven and all directions were all seen dyed in red colour.

sn: लोहित्य तु गन्धेन स्पर्शेन च रसेन च। रूपेण चातिरक्तेन शब्देन च विसर्पता॥ विषादः सुमहानासीत् प्राय: सैन्यस्य भारत।
en: With the smell, the touch, the taste, the exceedingly redness of the blood and its gushing sound almost of the warriors became very cheerless.

sn: तत् तु विप्रहतं सैन्यं भीमसेनमुखास्तदा॥ भूयः समाद्रवनं वीराः सात्यकिप्रमुखास्तदा।
en: The Pandava heroes headed by Bhimasena and Satyaki again attacked fiercely on Kaurava's army already destroyed in its considerable fraction.

sn: तेषामापततां वेगमविषह्यं निरीक्ष्य च॥ पुत्राणां ते महासैन्यमासीद् राजन् पराङ्मुखम्।
en: Beholding the irrepressible force of their attack, the army of your sons, O king, turned their back.

sn: तत् प्रकीर्णरथाश्वेभं नरवाजिसमाकुलम्॥ विध्वस्तवर्मकवचं प्रविद्धायुधकार्मुकम्। व्यद्रवत् तावकं सैन्यं लोड्यमानं समन्ततः। सिंहार्दितमिवारण्ये यथा गजकुलं तथा॥
en: With armours and coats of mail, displaced, weapons and bows loosened from their hands, your army, abounding in cars, horses, elephants and men, fled away in all directions, being agitated by the enemy as a herd of elephants in the forest is afflicted by lions.

sn: संजय उवाच न्यवर्तत॥ तानभिद्रवतो दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवांस्तावकं बलम्। दुर्योधन महाराज वारयामास सर्वशः॥ योधांश्च स्वबलं चैव समन्ताद् भरतर्षभ। क्रोशतस्तव पुत्रस्य न स्म राजन्
en: Sanjaya said Beholding the Pandava troops rush upon your army, O monarch, Duryodhana checked his soldiers on all sides, O best of Bharatas. Although your son O king, cried at the top of his voice still his flying troops refused to stop.

sn: ततः पक्षः प्रपक्षश्च शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। तदा सशस्त्राः कुरवो भीममभ्यद्रवन् रणे॥
en: Then one and the other wing of the army and Shakuni, the son of Subala and the Kauravas well-armed fell upon Bhima in battle.

sn: कर्णोऽपि दृष्ट्वा द्रवतो धार्तराष्ट्रान् सराजकान्। पद्रराजमुवाचेदं याहि भीमरथं प्रति॥
en: Beholding the army of Dhritarashtra, with all the kings flying Karna said to the king of Madras. "Proceed towards the car of Bhima."

sn: एवमुक्तश्च कर्णेन शल्यो मद्राधिपस्तदा। हंसवर्णान् हयान्ग्रयान् प्रैषीद् यत्र वृकोदरकः॥
en: Thus accosted by Karna, the king of Madras urged those best of horses of the color of swans to where Vrikodara was.

sn: ते प्रेरिता महाराज शल्येनाहवशोभिना। भीमसेनरथं प्राप्य समसज्जन्त वाजिनः॥
en: Thus urged by Shalya, the ornament of battle those horses, approaching the chariot of Bhimasena, mingled in battle.

sn: दृष्ट्वा कर्ण समायान्तं भीमः क्रोधसमन्वितः। मतिं चक्रे विनाशाय कर्णस्य भरतर्षभ॥
en: Seeing Karna approach Bhima too was filled with anger and made up his mind to kill him.

sn: सोऽब्रवीत् सात्यकिं वीरं धृष्टद्युम्नं च पार्षतम्। यूयं रक्षत राजानं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्॥ संशयान्महतो मुक्तं कथंचित प्रेक्षतो मम।
en: He then said to the heroic Satyaki and Dhristadyumna, the son of Prishata-"You two protect the pious king Yudhishthira. With great difficulty he escaped a perilous situation in my presence.

sn: अग्रतो मे कृता राजा छिन्नसर्वपरिच्छदः॥ दुर्योधन प्रीत्यर्थं राधेयेन दुरात्मना।
en: Before my very eyes the wicked son of Radha cut-off the king's armnour and robes for the gratification of Duryodhana.

sn: अन्तमद्य गमिष्यामि तस्य दुःखस्य पार्षतः॥ हन्तास्यद्य रणे कर्णं स वा मां निहनिष्यति। संग्रामेण सुघोरेण सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I shall go today to the end of that misery, O son of Prishata. I shall either slay today in battle Karna or he will kill me with a dreadful encounter. I tell you the truth.

sn: राजानमद्य भवतां न्यासभूतं ददानि वै। तस्य संरक्षणे सर्वे यतध्वं विगतज्वराः॥
en: Today I made over the king to you as a sacred trust; do you all, shaking off lethargy, address yourselves to protect him."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुः प्रायादाधिरथिं प्रति। सिंहनादेन महता सर्वाः संनादयन् दिशः॥
en: Having said these words and made all the quarters resound with a loud and leonine shout the mighty-armed Bhima proceeded towards Adhiratha's son.

sn: दृष्ट्वा त्वरितमायान्तं भीमं युद्धाभिनन्दिनम्। सूतपुत्रमथोवाच मद्राणामीश्वरो विभुः॥
en: Beholding Bhima, who takes delight in battle, advance quickly, the king of Madras said to the charioteer's son.

sn: शल्य उवाच पश्य कर्णं महाबाहुं संक्रुद्धं पाण्डुनन्दनम्। दीर्घकालार्जित क्रोधं मोक्तुकामं त्वयि ध्रुवम्॥
en: Shalya said Behold, O Karna, the large-armed son of Pandu, worked up with anger. Forsooth he wishes to discharge at you his anger, accumulated for a long time.

sn: ईदृशं नास्य रूपं मे दृष्ट पूर्व कदाचन। अभिमन्यौ हते कर्ण राक्षसे च घटोत्कचे॥
en: O Karna, this form of his, I had never seen before even on the destruction of Abhimanyu and the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha.

sn: त्रैलोक्यस्य समस्तस्य शक्ताः क्रुद्धो निवारणे। बिभूति सदृशं रूपं युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभम्॥
en: He bears such a form, burning like the fire of dissolution, as it appears that he, when angered, is capable of resisting the three worlds.

sn: संजय उवाच इति ब्रुवति राधेयं मद्राणामीश्वरे नृप। अभ्यवर्तत वै कर्णं क्रोधदीप्तो वृकोदरः॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, while the son of Radha thus said to the king of Madra, Vrikodara, burning with anger, approached Karna.

sn: अथागतं तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य भीमं युद्धाभिनन्दिम्। अब्रवीद् वचनं शल्यं राधेयं प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Beholding Bhima, who take delight in battle thus approach the son of Radha, as if smiling, said to Shalya.

sn: यदुक्तं वचनं मेऽद्य त्वया मद्रजनेश्वर। भीमसेनं प्रति विभो तत् सत्यं नात्र संशयः॥
en: O king of Madra, what you have said to me today regarding Bhimasena is all true; there is no doubt about it.

sn: एष शूरच वीरश्च क्रोधनश्च वृकोदरः। निरपेक्ष शरीरे च प्राणतश्च बलाधिकः॥
en: This Vrikodara is heroic, brave and wrathful. He does not care for any while protecting his body and is superior to all in vital strength.

sn: अज्ञातवासं वसता विराटनगरे तदा। द्रौपद्याः प्रियकामेन केवलं बाहुसंश्रयात्॥ तु गूढभावं समाश्रित्य कीचकः सगणो हतः।
en: While living secretly in the city of Virata, he depending merely on the strength of his own arms, slew secretly, to satisfy Draupadi, Kichaka with all his relations,

sn: सोऽद्य संग्रामशिरसि संनद्धः क्रोधमूर्छितः॥ किं करोद्यतदण्डेन मृत्युनापि व्रजेद् रणम्।
en: He today stands at the head of the battle, clad in mail and is beside himself with anger. he is ready to engage in battle with the destroyer armed with uplifted mace.

sn: चिरकालाभिलाषितो मामयं मनोरथः॥ अर्जुनं समरे हन्यां मां वा हन्याद् धनंजयः। स मे कदाचिदद्यैव भवेद् भीमसमागमात्॥
en: I have cherished this desire all through my life that either I shall kill Arjuna or Arjuna will kill me. That desire of mine may be fulfilled today on account of my encounter with Bhima.

sn: निहते भीमसेने वा यदि वा विस्थीकृते। अभियास्यति मां पार्थस्तन्मे साधु भविष्यति॥ अत्र यन्मन्यसे प्राप्तं तच्छीघ्रं सम्प्रधारया
en: If I kill Bhima or overpower him Partha may come against me. That will be good for me. Decide without any delay with you think proper for the moment.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं राधेयस्यामितौजसः॥ उवाच वचनं शल्यः सूतपुत्रं तथागतम्। अभियाहि महाबाहो भीमसेनं महाबलम्॥ निरस्य भीमसेनं तु ततः प्राप्स्यसि फाल्गुनम्।
en: Hearing these words of the highly energetic son of Radha Shalya replied-"O hero, proceed against the highly powerful Bhimasena. Having over-powered him you may then obtain Phalguna.

sn: यस्ते कामोऽभिलषितश्चिरात् प्रभृति हृद्गतः॥ स वै सम्पत्स्यते कर्ण सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते।
en: Your determination, you long-cherished desire, O Karna, will be accomplished today. I tell you the truth.

sn: एवमुक्ते ततः कर्णः शल्यं पुनरभाषतः॥ हन्ताऽहमर्जुन संख्ये मां वा हन्याद् धनंजयः। युद्धे मनः समाधाय याहि यत्र वृकोदरः॥
en: Thus accosted Karna once more said to Shalya. “Either I will kill Arjuna in battle or he will kill me. Giving your heart to battle, proceed where Vrikodara is."

sn: संजय उवाच ततः प्रायाद् रथेनाशु शल्यस्तत्र विशाम्पते। यत्र भीमो महेष्वासो व्यद्रावयत वाहिनीम्॥
en: Sanjay said Then, O king, Shalya quickly went on his car where that great bowman Bhima, was engaged in belabouring your army.

sn: ततस्तूर्यनिनादश्च भेरीणां च महास्वनः। उदितष्ठच राजेन्द्र कर्णभीमसमागमे॥
en: Then there arose, O king, the sound of trumpets and drums when Karna and Bhima met.

sn: भीमसेनोऽथ संक्रुद्धस्तस्य सैन्यं दुरासदम्। नाराचैर्विमलैस्तीक्ष्णैर्दिशः प्राद्रावयद् बली॥
en: Worked up with anger the powerful Bhimasena began to rout your army, whom it is so difficult to vanquish, with his sharp and polished arrows.

sn: स संनिपातस्तुमुलो घोररूपो विशाम्पते। आसीद् रौद्रो महाराज कर्णपाण्डवयोर्मधे॥
en: O monarch, that encounter between Bhima and Karna in battle became dreadful and the noise thereof was tremendous.

sn: ततो मुहूर्ताद् राजेन्द्र पाण्डवः कर्णमाद्रवत्। समापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य कर्णो वैकर्तनो वृषः॥ आजघान सुसंक्रुद्धो नाराचेन स्तनान्तरे। पुनश्चैनममेयात्मा शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्॥
en: Beholding Bhima approach towards him, Karna, otherwise called Vaikartana or Vrisha, filled with anger, struck him on the chest with an arrows. Once more the highly energetic Karna covered him with a shower of arrows. Thus struck by the charioteer's son Bhima two enshrouded him with Narachas.

sn: स विद्धः सूतपुत्रेण छादयामास पत्रिभिः। विव्याध निशितैः कर्णं नवभिनतपर्वभिः॥
en: With nine sharp and bent arrows he struck Karna who again cut-off his bow in twain with winged arrows.

sn: तस्य कर्णो धनुर्मध्ये द्विधा चिच्छेद पत्रिभिः। अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं प्रत्यविध्यत् स्तनान्तरे॥ नाराचेनं सुतीक्ष्णेन सर्वावरणभेदिना।
en: Sundering his bow he once more struck him on the chest with a highly keen arrow capable of cutting off all kinds of arms.

sn: सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय सूतपुत्रं वृकोदरः॥ राजन् मर्मसु मर्मज्ञो विव्याध निशितैः शरैः। ननाद बलवन्नादं कम्पयन्निव रोदसी॥
en: Then, O king, taking up another bow, Bhima, who knew where the vital parts are, pierced the son of the charioteer to the very vitals with sharpened arrows.

sn: तं कर्णः पञ्चविंशत्या नाराचेन समार्पयत्। मदोत्कटं वने दृप्तमुल्काभिरिव कुञ्जरम्॥
en: Then Karna struck him with twenty-five arrows like a hunter striking a proud and infuriate elephant in the forest with a number of blazing brands.

sn: ततः सायकभिन्नाङ्गः पाण्डवः क्रोधमूर्छितः। संरम्भाषताम्राक्षः सूतपुत्रवधेप्सया॥ स कार्मुके महावेगं भारतसाधनमुक्तमम्। गिरीणामपि भेत्तारं सायकं समयोजयत्॥
en: Thereupon with his limbs mangled by arrows, beside himself with anger and his eyes reddened with pride and ire the son of Pandu set on his bow a highly impetuous and excellent arrow capable of bearing a heavy strain and riving the mountains,

sn: विकृत्यबलवच्चापमाकर्णादतिमारुतिः। तं मुमोच महेष्वासः क्रुद्धः कर्णजिघांसया॥
en: Stretching with great force his bow to his cars the Maruti (Bhima), filled with anger all desirous of slaying Karna discharged it.

sn: स विसृष्टो बलवता बाणो वनाशनिस्वनः। अदारयद् रणे कर्णं वज्रवेगो यथाचलम्॥
en: Discharged by powerful Bhima, that arrow, making a sound like that of a thunderbolt, struck Karna in that battle like the thunderbolt itself clapping a mountain,

sn: स भीमसेनाभिहत:सूतपुत्रः कुरूद्वह। निषसाद रथोपस्थे विसंज्ञः पृतनापतिः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, thus struck by Bhimasena, the Commander Suta's son sat down senseless on the terrace of his car.

sn: ततो मद्राधिपो दृष्ट्वा विसंज्ञं सूतनन्दनम्। अपोवाह रथेनाजौ कर्णमाहवशोभिनम्॥
en: Beholding the Suta's son insensible the king of Madras carried him away on his car from the battle-field.

sn: ततः पराजिते कर्णे धातराष्ट्रीं महाचमूम्। व्यद्रावदयद् भीमसेनो यथेन्द्रो दानवान् पुरा॥
en: After Karna's defeat Bhima began to belabour the huge army of Dhritarashthra like Indra routing the Danavas.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच सुदुष्करमिदं कर्म कृतं भीमेन संजय। येन कर्णो महाबाहू रथोपस्थे निपातितः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Highly difficult was this feat performed by Bhima, O Sanjaya, by which the mighty-armed Karna was caused to lie down on his car.

sn: कर्णो ोको रणे हन्ता पाण्डवान् सृञ्जयैः सह। इति दुर्योधनः सूत प्राब्रवीन्मां मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: “There is Karna who alone will kill the Pandava along with Srinjayas.” This my son Duryodhana oftentimes said to me.

sn: पराजितं तु राधेयं दृष्ट्वा भीमेन संयुगे। ततः परं किमकरोत् पुत्रो दुर्योधनो मम॥
en: Beholding the son of Radha vanquished by Bhimasena in battle what did my son Duryodhana do afterwards?

sn: ते संजय उवाच विमुखं प्रेक्ष्य राधेय सूतपुत्रं महाहवे। पुत्रस्तव महाराज सोदर्यान् समभाषत॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing Karna's retreat in that great battle, your son, O king, said to his own brothers.

sn: शीघ्रं गच्छतं भद्रं वो राधेयं परिरक्षत। भीमसेनभयागाधे मजन्तं व्यसनार्णवे॥
en: May good betide you! Go quickly and rescue the son of Radha who is plunged into the fathomless calamity consequent upon the fear of Bhimasena.

sn: तु राज्ञा समादिष्टा भीमसेनं जिघांसवः। अभ्यवर्तन्त संक्रुद्धाः पतङ्गाः पावकं यथा॥
en: Thus commanded by the king those princes, worked up with anger and desirous of killing Bhimasena, proceeded towards him like a swarm of insects, towards a blazing fire.

sn: श्रुतर्वा दुर्धरः क्राथो विवित्सुर्विकटः समः। निषङ्गी कवची पाशी तथा नन्दोपनन्दकौ॥ दुष्प्रधर्षः सुबाहुश्च वातवेगसुवर्चसौ। धनुर्लाहो दुर्मदश्च जलसंधः शलः सहः॥ एते रथैः परिवृता वीर्यवन्तो महाबलाः। भीमसेनं समासाद्य समन्तान् पर्यवारयन्॥
en: They were Srutarvan, Durddhara Kratha, Vivitsu, Vikata, Soma, Nishangin, Kavachin, Pashin, Nava, Upanedaka Duspradharsha, Savahu, Vatavega, Suvarchas, Dhanurgraha, Durmada, Jalasandha, Shala and Saha. Encircled by large car-force, those highly energetic and powerful princes approached Bhimasena and surrounded him on all sides.

sn: व्यमुञ्चञ्छरवातान् नानालिङ्गान् समन्ततः। से तैरभ्यर्घमानस्तु भीमसेनो महाबलः॥ तेषामापततां क्षिप्रं सुतानां ते जनाधिप। रथैःपञ्चादशैः सार्ध पञ्चाशदहनद् रथान्॥
en: They discharged at himn from all sides showers of arrows of various sorts. Thus assailed by them, O king, the highly powerful Bhima soon killed fifty leading car-warriors and five hundred from amongst your sons who fell upon him.

sn: ते विवित्सोस्तु ततः क्रुद्धो भल्लेनापाहरच्छिरः। भीमसेनो महाराज तत् पपात हतं भुवि।॥ सकुण्डलशिरस्त्राणं पूर्णचन्द्रोपमं तथा।
en: Worked up with anger, Bhima, O king, with a Bhalla, cut-off the head of Vivitsu, adorned with ear-rings and a crown and a face resembling the full-moon. Thus cut-off the prince fell down on earth.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं शूरं भ्रातरः सर्वतः प्रभो॥ अभ्यद्रवन्त समरे भीमं भीमपराक्रमम्।
en: Beholding their heroic brother slain your other sons, from all sides, rushed upon the terribly powerful Bhima.

sn: ततोऽपराभ्यां भल्लाभ्यां पुत्रयोस्ते महाहवे॥ जहार समरे प्राणान् भीमो भीमपराक्रमः।
en: With two Bhallas Bhima killed two other sons of yours in that great battle.

sn: तौ धरामन्वपद्येतो वातरुग्णाविव दुमौ॥ विकटश्च सहयोभौ देवपुत्रोपमौ नृप।
en: Then Vikata and Saha, looking like two celestial youths, fell down on earth like a couple of trees uprooted by a tempest.

sn: ततस्तु त्वरितो भीमः क्राथं निन्ये यमक्षयम्॥ नाराचेन सुतीक्ष्णेन स हतो न्यपतद् भुवि।
en: Then in a moment Bhima dispatched Kratha to the abode of Yama with a long keen arrow. Deprived of life that prince fell down on earth.

sn: हाहाकारस्ततस्तीव्रः सम्बभूव जनेश्वर॥ वध्यमानेषु वीरेषु तव पुत्रेषु धान्विषु।
en: O king, when those your heroic sons, great bowmen, were being thus killed people began to send loud cried of lamentations.

sn: तेषां सुलुलिते सैन्ये पुनर्भीमो महाबलः॥ नन्दोपनन्दौ समरे प्रेषयद् यमसादनम्।
en: When your army was once more agitated Bhima sent Nanda and Upananda in that great battle to the abode of the Regent of death.

sn: ततस्ते प्राद्रवन् भीताःपुत्रास्ते विह्वलीकृताः॥ भीमसेनं रणे दृष्टा कालान्तकयमोपमम्।
en: Beholding Bhimasena in battle behave like the Destroyer himself at the end of Yuga your sons, worked up greatly with fear, took to their heels.

sn: पुत्रांस्ते निहतान् दृष्ट्वा सूतपुत्रः सुदुर्मनाः॥ हंसवर्णान् हयान् भूयः प्रेषयद् यत्र पाण्डवः।
en: Seeing those sons of yours thus slain Karna once more urged on his swan-like horses to where that son of Pandu was.

sn: ते प्रेषिता महाराज मद्रराजेन वाजिनः॥ भीमसेनरथं प्राप्य समसज्जन्त वेगिताः।
en: The horses, driven by the king of Madras, approached quickly the car of Bhimasena and entered into battle.

sn: स संनिपातस्तुमुलो घोररूपो विशाम्पते॥ आसीद् रौद्रो महाराज कर्णपाण्डवयोर्मधे।
en: The encounter, O king, that once more took place between Karna and Bhima, was highly dreadful and fierce and accompanied by a loud noise.

sn: दृष्ट्वा मम महाराज तौ समेतौ महारथौ॥ आसीद् बुद्धिः कथं युद्धमेतदद्य भविष्यति।
en: Seeing, O king, those two powerful carwarriors near each other I became curious to observe the course of fight.

sn: ततो भीम रणश्लाघी छादयामास पत्रिभिः॥ कर्णं रणे महाराज पुत्राणां तव पश्यताम्।
en: Then boasting of his power in battle, O king, Bhima covered Karna with Naracha in the presence of your sons.

sn: ततः कर्णो भृषं क्रुद्धो भीमं नवभिरायसैः॥ विव्याध परमास्त्रज्ञो भल्लैः संनतपर्वभिः।
en: Then Karna, a master of best weapons, worked up with anger, struck Karna with nine Bhallas purely made of iron.

sn: आहत: स महाबाहुर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः॥ आकर्णपूणैर्विशिखैःकर्ण विव्याध सप्तभिः।
en: Thus struck by Karna the highly powerful and mighty-armed Bhima struck his antagonist in return with seven arrows shot off his bowstring drawn to his ear.

sn: ततः कर्णो महाराज आशीविष इव श्वसन्॥ शरवर्षेण महता छादयामास पाण्डवम्।
en: Then sighing like a serpent of deadly venom, O king, Karna covered the son of Pandu with a thick shower of arrows.

sn: भीमोऽपि तं शरवातैश्छादयित्वा महारथम्॥ पश्यतां कौरवेयाणां विननद महाबलः।
en: Then covering the mighty car-warrior Karna with a shower of arrows in return before the very eyes of the Kauravas, Bhima sent up a loud war-cry.

sn: ततः कर्णो भृशं क्रुद्धोः दृढमादाय कार्मुकम्॥ भीमं विव्याध दशभिः कङ्कपत्रैः शिलाशितैः। कार्मुकं चास्य चिच्छेद भल्लेन निशितेन च॥
en: Then worked up with anger Karna grasped his bow very strongly and struck Bhima with ten Kanka-feathered arrows whetted on stone. With another sharp Bhalla he cut-off Bhima's bow.

sn: ततो भीमो महाबाहुर्हमपट्टविभूषितम्। परिघं घोरमादाय मृत्युदण्डमिवापरम्॥ कर्णस्य निधनाकाङ्क्षी चिक्षेपातिबलो नदन्।
en: Then taking up a dreadful Parigha adorned with gold resembling the rod of death the mighty-armed Bhima, with a view to kill Karna, hurled it at him making a great roar.

sn: तमापतन्तं परिघं वज्रशनिसमस्वनम्॥ चिच्छेद बहुधा कर्णः शरैराशीविषोपमैः।
en: Then the serpentine arrow Karna sundered into pieces Parigha that was about to fall making a sound like that of a thunderbolt.

sn: ततः कार्मुकमादाय भीमो दृढतरं तदा॥ छादयामास विशिखैः कर्णं परबलार्दनम्।
en: Then taking up a bow with grim grasp Bhima, the grinder of enemies, covered Karna with arrows.

sn: ततो युद्धमभूद् घोरं कर्णपाण्डवयोर्मधे॥ हरीन्द्रयोरिव मुहुःपरस्परवधैषिणोः।
en: Then there took place a dreadful encounter between Karna and Bhima desirous of discomfiting each other every moment like that between Hari and Indra.

sn: ततः कर्णो महाराज भीमसेनं त्रिभिः शरैः॥ आकर्णमूलं विव्याध दृढमायम्य कार्मुकम्।
en: Thereupon, O king, drawing firmly to his ear the bow Karna struck Bhima with three arrows.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महेष्वासः कर्णेनबलिनां वरः॥ घोरमादत्त विशिखं कर्णकायावदारणम्।
en: Then pierced by Karna the great bowman, the foremost of the strong, took up a dreadful arrow capable of piercing Karna's body.

sn: तस्य भित्वा तनुत्राणं भित्वा कायं च सायकः॥ प्राविशद् धरणी राजन् वल्मीकमिव पन्नगः।
en: Piercing his coat of mail and body, O king, that arrow entered into the earth like a snake entering into a noble-hill.

sn: स तेनातिप्रहारेण व्यथितो विह्वलनिवा। ३८॥ संचचाल रथे कर्णः क्षितिकम्पे यथाचलः।
en: Then with that heavy stroke Karna trembled on his car, as if bewildered like a mountain at the time of earth-quake.

sn: ततः कर्णो महाराज रोषामर्षसमन्वितः॥ पाण्डवं पञ्चविंशत्या नाराचानां समार्पयत्। आजघ्ने बहुभिर्बाणैर्ध्वजमेकेषुणाहनत्॥
en: Thereupon O great king, filled with anger and revenge Karna discharged twenty-five Narachas at Bhima. With one arrow he then cut-off Bhima's standard.

sn: सारर्थि चास्य भल्लेन प्रेषयामास मृत्यवे। छित्त्वा च कार्मुकं तूर्ण पाण्डवस्याशुपत्रिणा॥ ततो मुहूर्ताद् राजेन्द्र नातिकृच्छ्राद्धसन्निवा विरथं भीमकर्माणं भीमं कर्णश्चकार ह। ४२॥
en: With another Bhalla he dispatched Bhima's driver to the abode of Yama. Then quickly cutting off his bow with another winged arrow Karna deprived Bhima of dreadful feats of his car.

sn: विरथो भरतश्रेष्ठ प्रहसन्ननिलोपमः। गदां गृह्य महाबाहुरपतत् स्यन्दनोत्तमात्॥
en: O best of Bharatas, deprived of his car the mighty-armed Bhima, who resembled the Wind-god, took up a mace and jumped down from his excellent car.

sn: अवप्लुत्य च वेगेन तव सैन्यं विशाम्पते। व्यधमद् गदया भीमः शरन्मेधानिवानिलः॥
en: Jumping down furiously from his car Bhima began to kill your troops, O king, like the wind destroying the autumnal clouds.

sn: नागान् सप्तशतान् राजन्नीषादन्तान् प्रहारिणः। व्यधमत् सहसा भीमः क्रुद्धरूपः परंतपः॥
en: Suddenly the son ot Pandu, the consumer of enemies worked up with anger, dispersed seven hundred elephants with tusks as large as plough-shares and all skilled in smiting hostile soldiers.

sn: दन्तवेष्टेषु नेत्रेषु कुम्भेषु च कटेषु च। मर्मस्वपि च मर्मज्ञस्तान नागानवधीद् बली॥
en: The powerful hero, conversant with vital parts, killed all those elephants striking them on their temples, frontal globes eyes and in parts above the gums.

sn: ततस्ते प्राद्रवन् भीताः प्रतीपं प्रहिताः पुनः। महामात्रैस्तामवतुर्मेघा इव दिवाकरम्॥
en: Then filled with fear those animals ran away. But again urged on by their drivers they surrounded Bhimasena like the clouds covering the sun.

sn: तान् स सप्तशतान् नागान् सारोहायुधकेतनान्। भूमिष्टो गदया जने वज्रेणेन्द्रि इवाचलान्॥
en: Like Indra, striking down mountains with his thunderbolt Bhima, with his mace, struck down those seven hundred elephants with their riders, weapons and standards.

sn: ततः सुबलपुत्रस्य नागानतिबलान् पुनः। पोथयामास कौन्तेयो द्विपञ्चाशदरिंदमः॥
en: Then the son of Kunti, the subduer of foes, struck down fiftytwo highly powerful elephants belonging to the son of Subala.

sn: तथा रथशतंसाग्रं पत्तींश्च शतशोऽपरान्। न्यहनत् पाण्डवो युद्धे तापयंस्तव वाहिनीम्॥
en: Then scorching your army the Pandava killed, in battle, a hundred of cars and hundreds of powerful foot soldiers.

sn: प्रताप्यमानं सूर्येण भीमेन च महात्मना। तव सैन्यं संचुकोच चर्माग्नावाहितं यथा॥
en: Scorched by the sun and the high-souled Bhima your army began to shrink like a piece of leather spread over a fire.

sn: ते भीमभयसंत्रस्तावका भरतर्षभ। विहाय समरे भीमं दुद्रुवः दिशो दश॥
en: O foremost of Bharatas, filled with anxiety consequent upon the fear of Bhima, your troops avoided him and fled away in all directions.

sn: रथाः पञ्चशताश्चान्ये हादिनचर्मवर्मिणः। भीममभ्यद्रवन् जन्तः शरपूगैः समन्ततः॥
en: Then five hundred car-warriors, clad in excellent coats of mail, fell upon Bhima with loud shouts discharging a shower of arrows on all sides.

sn: तान् स पञ्चशतान् वीरान् सपताकध्वजायुधान्। पोथयामास गदया भीमो विष्णुरिवासुरान्॥
en: Like Vishnu killing the demons Bhima, with his mace, destroyed those valiant warriors with their drivers, cars, banners, standards and weapons.

sn: ततः शकुनिनिर्दिष्टाः सादिनः शूरसम्मताः। त्रिसाहस्त्राभ्ययुभीमं शक्त्यृष्टिप्रासपाणयः॥
en: Then three thousand cavalry led by Shakuni, held in esteem by all brave men and armed with darts, swords and lances, dashed on the great Bhima.

sn: प्रत्युट्रम्य जवे पशु साश्वारोहांस्तदारिहा। विविधान् विचरन् मार्गान् गदया समपोथयत्॥
en: Advancing impetuously towards them and coursing in various ways that slayer of foes killed them with his mace.

sn: तेषामासीन्महाञ्छब्दस्ताडितानां त सर्वशः। अश्मभिर्विध्यमानां नगानामिव भारत॥
en: While they were thus being assailed by Bhima loud sounds arose among them like those from among a herd of elephants struck with a large piece of rock.

sn: एवं सुबलपुत्रस्य त्रिसाहस्त्रान् हयोत्तमान्। हत्वान्यं रथमास्थाय क्रुद्धो राधेयमभ्ययात्॥
en: Having killed those three thousand excellent horses of Subala's son in that way he rode upon another car and worked up with anger proceeded against the son of Radha.

sn: कर्णोऽपि समरे राजन् धर्मपुत्रमरिंदमम्। स शैरश्छादयामास सारथिं चाप्यपातयत्॥
en: Karna too, O king, coveredwith arrows in battle Dharma's son, the subduer of foes and struck down his charioteer.

sn: ततः स प्रद्रुतं संख्ये रथं दृष्ट्वा महारथः। अन्वधावत् किरन् बाणैः कङ्कपत्रैरजिह्मगैः॥
en: Beholding him thus fly away quickly in battle the mighty car-warrior Karna pursued him shooting straight Kanka-feathered arrows.

sn: राजानमभिधावन्तं शरैरावृत्य रोदसी। क्रुद्धः प्रच्छादयामास शरजालेन मारुतिः॥
en: Covering the earth and sky with arrows, the son of the Wind-god (Bhima) covered him with a shower of arrows while he pursued the king.

sn: संनिवृत्तस्ततस्तूर्णं राधेयः शत्रुकर्शनः। भीमं प्रच्छादयामास समन्तनिशितैः शरैः॥
en: Then quickly returning, the son of Radha, the subduer of enemies, covered Bhima on all sides with sharpened arrows.

sn: भीमसेनरथव्यग्रं कर्ण भारत सात्यकिः। अभ्यर्दयदजमेयात्मा पाणिग्रहणकारणात्॥
en: Then placing himself on the side of Bhima's car, O Bharata, the highly energetic Satyaki began to afflict Karna who was in front of Bhima.

sn: अभ्यवर्तत कर्णस्तदितोऽपि शरैर्भृशम्। तावन्योन्यं समासाद्य वृषभौ सर्वधन्विनाम्॥ विसृजन्तौ शरान् दीप्तान् व्यभ्राजेता मनस्विनौ।
