en: Though greatly assailed by Satyaki Karna still approached Bhima; approaching each : other, those two best of archers, the two highly energetic heroes, appeared highly resplendent as they discharged arrows at each other.

sn: ताभ्यां वियति राजेन्द्र विततं भीमदर्शनम्॥ क्रौञ्चपृष्ठारुणं रौद्रं नाणजालं व्यदृश्यता
en: Spread by them, O king, in the sky those rows, shining as the backs of crane, looked exceedingly fierce and terrible.

sn: नैव सूर्यप्रभा राजन् न दिशः प्रदिशस्तथा॥ प्राज्ञासिष्म वयं ते वा शरैमुक्तैः सहस्रशः।
en: On account of those thousands of arrows, O king, neither the rays of the sun nor the cardinal quarters could be seen either by ourselves or by the enemy.

sn: मध्याह्ने तपतो राजन् भास्करस्य महाप्रभाः॥ हृताः सर्वाः शरौघैस्तैः कर्णपाण्डवयोस्तदा।
en: The fierceness of the sun's rays burring at midday was removed by those thick showers of arrows discharged by Karna and the son of Pandu.

sn: सौबलं कृतवर्माणं द्रौणिमाधिरथिं कुपम्॥ संसक्तान् पाण्डवैर्दृष्ट्वा निवृत्ताः कुरवः पुनः।
en: Beholding the son of Subala, Kritavarma, Drona's son, Adhiratha's son and Kripa fight with the Pandavas the Kauravas rallied and came back to the battle.

sn: तेषामापततां शब्दस्तीव्र आसीद् विशाम्पते॥ उवृत्तानां यथा वृष्ट्या सागराणां भयावहः।
en: O king, the army, dashing impetuously against the enemies, caused a tumult resembling the terrible noise made by many oceans swollen with rams.

sn: ते सेने भृशसंसक्ते दृष्ट्वान्योन्यं महाहवे॥ हर्षेण महता युक्ते परिगृह्य परस्परम्।
en: Furiously engaged in fight the two armies became filled with delight as the warriors saw and seized one another.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं मध्यं प्राप्ते दिवाकरे॥ तादृश न कदाचिद्धि दृष्टपूर्वं न च श्रुतम्।
en: When the sun was at its meridian they engaged in fight the like of which was never seen or heard of before.

sn: बलौद्यस्तु समासाद्य बलौघं सहसा रणे॥ उपासर्पत वेगेन वार्योघ इव सागरम्। आसीन्निनादः सुमहान् बाणौघानां परस्परम्॥ गर्जतां सागरौघाणां यथा स्यान्निःस्वनौ महान्।
en: One powerful division, meeting with another such, rushed upon it with impetuosity like a huge collection of water rushing towards the ocean. The din, caused by the two armies as they roared at each other, was loud and deep like that which is heard when several oceans mingle with one another.

sn: ते तु सेने समासाद्य वेगवत्यौ परस्परम्॥ एकीभावमनुप्राप्ते नद्याविव समागमे।
en: That the two furious armies, approaching one another, formed one mass like two furious rivers that run into each other.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं घोररूपं विशाम्पते॥ कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च लिप्सतां सुमहद् यशः।
en: Then a dreadful encounter took place between the Kurus and Pandavas who were actuated by the desire of gaining glory.

sn: शूराणां गर्जतां तत्र ह्यविच्छेदकृता गिरः॥ श्रूयन्ते विविधा राजन् नामान्युद्दिश्य भारत।
en: O descendant of Bharata, as those warriors called one another by name a regular confusion of voices was heard.

sn: यस्य यद्धि रणे व्यङ्गं पितृतो मातृतोऽपि वा॥ कर्मतः शीलतो वापि स तच्छ्रावयते युधि।
en: In that battle, his antagonist was made to hear by a hero whatever matter or ridicule he had of his father, mother, conduct of character.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा समरे शूरांस्तर्जमानान् परस्परम्॥ अभवन्मे मती राजन् नैषामस्तीति जीवितम्।
en: Beholding those heroes reviling one another in battle, O king, I thought that the lease of their life had run out.

sn: तेषां दृष्ट्वा तु क्रुद्धानां वपूष्यमिततेजसाम्॥ अभवन्मेभयं तीव्र कथमेतद् भविष्यति।
en: Beholding the bodies of those highly energetic and wrathful heroes my mind was possessed by great fear and I thought, "what will become of them?

sn: ततस्ते पाण्डवा राजन् कौरवाश्च महारथाः। ततक्षुः सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैर्निजन्तो हि परस्परम्॥
en: O king! Soon thereafter the great chariot riders in Pandava and Kauravas' army started causing injuries to each other by shooting acute arrows. O king! Soon thereafter the great chariot riders in Pandava and Kauravas' army started causing injuries to each other by shooting acute arrows.

sn: संजय उवाच क्षत्रियास्ते महाराज परस्परवधैषिणः। अन्योन्यं समरे जघ्नुः कृतवैरा: परस्परम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Desirous of slaying one another and cherishing hatred, the Kshatriyas, O monarch, killed one another in battle.

sn: रथौघाश्च हयौघाश्च नरौघाश्च समन्ततः। गजौघाश्च महाराज संसक्ताश्च परस्परम्॥
en: Cars, horses, men and elephants, O monarch, in large numbers, encountered one another on all sides.

sn: गदानां परिधाणां च कणपानां च क्षिप्यताम्। प्रासानां भिन्दिपालानां भुशुण्डीनां च सर्वशः॥ सम्पातं चानुपश्याम संग्रामे भृशदारुणे। शलभा इव सम्पेतुः समन्ताच्छरवृष्टयः॥
en: We saw the falling maces, Parighas, Kunapas, lances, and rockets discharged at one another in that terrible encounter. Dreadful showers of arrows shot through like locusts.

sn: नागान् नागा: समासाद्य व्यधमन्त परस्परम्। हया हयांश्च समरे रथिनो रशिनस्तथा॥ पत्तयः पत्तिसंघांश्च हयसंघांश्च पत्तयः। पत्तयो रथमातङ्गान् रथा हस्त्यश्वमेव च॥ नागाश्च समरे त्र्यङ्गं ममृदुः शीघ्रगा नृप।
en: Elephants struck elephants, horses routed horses and the car-warriors fought with carwarriors. There fought foot-soldiers with footsoldiers and the infantry with the cars and elephants and horsemen and elephants with the three other kinds of forces. They began to crush, O inonarch and grind one another. arrows

sn: वध्यतां तत्र शूराणां क्रोशतां च परस्परम्॥ घोरमायोधनं जज्ञे पशूनां वैशसं यथा।
en: On account of those combatants striking one another and shouting at the top of their voices, the battle-field became awful, resembling the slaughter ground of creatures.

sn: रुधिरेण समास्तीर्ण भाति भारत मेदिना॥ शक्रगोपगणाकीर्णा प्रावृषीव यथा धरा।
en: Covered with blood, the earth looked like a vast plain in the season of rains covered with red cochineal.

sn: यथा वा वाससी शुक्के महारञ्जनिञ्जिते॥ बिभृयाद् युवती श्यामा तद्वदासीद् वसुंधरा। मासंशोणितचित्रेव शातुकम्भमयीव च॥
en: The earth assumed, as it were, the form of youthful maiden of great beauty clad in white robes dyed with deep red. Variegated with flesh and blood the earth appeared as if decked with gold.

sn: भिन्नानां चोत्तमाङ्गानां बाहूनां चोरुभिः सह। कुण्डालानां प्रवृद्धानां भूषणानां च भारत॥ निष्काणामथ शूराणां शरीराणां च धन्विनाम्। चर्मणां सपताकानां संघास्तत्रापतन् भुवि॥
en: Large numbers of beads, cut-off from trunks and arms and thighs and ear-rings and other ornaments stripped off the bodies of the warriors, collars, cuirasses, bodies of brave bowmen, coats of mail and banners, lay scattered on the earth.

sn: गजा गजान् समासाद्य विषाणैरार्दयन् नृप। विषाणाभिहतास्तत्र भ्राजन्ते द्विरदास्तथा॥
en: O king, the elephants approaching other elephants tore one another with their tusks. Stuck with the tusks of assailing elephants they looked beautiful.

sn: रुधिरेणावसिक्ताङ्गा गैरिकप्रस्त्रवा इव। यथा भ्राजन्ति स्यन्दन्तः पर्वता धातुमण्डिताः॥
en: Bathed in blood those huge creatures looked resplendent like moving hills covered with metals and streams of liquid chalk.

sn: तोमरान् सादिभिर्मुक्तान् प्रतीपानास्थितान् बहून्। हस्तैर्विचेरुस्ते नागा बभञ्जुश्चापरे तथा॥
en: Many of them seized the lances hurled by horsemen whilst others broke and twisted them.

sn: नाराचैश्छिन्नवर्माणो भ्राजन्ति स्म गजोत्तमाः। हिमागमे यथा राजन् व्यभ्रा इव महीधराः॥
en: Many huge elephants, with their armours cut-off with arrows, looked like mountains divested of clouds at the approach of the winter.

sn: शरैः कनकपुडैश्च चित्रा रेजुर्गजोत्तमाः। उल्काभिः सम्प्रदीप्तायाः पर्वता इव भारत॥
en: Many leading elephants, struck with goldwinged arrows, looked beautiful, like mountains whose summits are lighted with torches.

sn: केचिदभ्याहता नागैर्नागा नगनिभोपमाः। विनेशुः समरे तस्मिन् पत्रवन्त इवाद्रयः॥
en: Struck by their antagonists some of those creatures, huge as hills, fell down in battle like winged mountains.

sn: अपरे प्राद्रवन् नागाः शल्यार्ता व्रणपीडिताः। प्रतिमानैश्च कुम्भैश्च पेतुरुवा॒ महाहवे॥
en: Others, afflicted with arrows and much pained by the wound, fell down on the earth in that dreadful encounter with their frontal globes or the parts between their tusks.

sn: विनेदुः सिंहवचान्ये नदन्तो भैरवान् रवान्। बभ्रमुर्बहवो राजंश्चक्रुशुश्चापरे गजाः॥
en: Others roared like lions. And many emitting terrible sounds ran hither and thither and many, O king, uttered cries of pain.

sn: हयाश्च निहता बाणैर्हेमभाण्डविभूषिताः। निषेदुश्चैव मम्लुश्च बभ्रमुश्च दिशो दश॥
en: Horses, adorned with golden trappings, kills by arrows, fell down or became weak or ran in all directions.

sn: अपरे कृष्यमाणाश्च विचेष्टन्तो महीतले। भावान् बहुविधांश्चक्रुस्ताडिताः शरतोमरैः॥
en: Others, wounded with arrows or dragged, fell down on the earth making diverse kinds of motion in agony.

sn: नरास्तु निहता भूमौ कूजन्तस्तत्र मारिष। दृष्ट्वा च बान्धवानन्ये पितॄनन्ये पितामहान्॥ धावमानान् परांश्चान्यान् दृष्टाऽन्ये तत्र भारत। गोत्रनामानि ख्यातानि शशंसुरितरेतरम्॥
en: Men also slain fell down on the earth uttering many cries. Many beholding their relatives, fathers, grand-fathers, while others, seeing their retreating enemies called one another by their own and their family names.

sn: तेषां छिन्ना महाराज भुजाः कनकभीषणाः। उद्वेष्टन्ते विचेष्टन्तेपतन्त चोत्पतन्ति च॥
en: Cut-off by enemies, the arms of many warriors adorned with golden ornaments fell down on the earth and writhed in agony.

sn: निपतन्ति तथैवान्ये स्फुरन्ति च सहस्रशः। वेगांश्चान्ये रणे चक्रुः पञ्चास्या इव पन्नगाः॥
en: Thousands of such arms fell down on the earth and sprang up and many seemed to dart forward like five-headed snakes.

sn: ते भुजा भोगिभोगाभाश्चन्दनाक्ता विशाम्पते। लोहितार्दा भृशं रेजुस्तपनयध्वजा इव॥
en: O king, those arms, resembling the bodies of serpents, pasted with gold and besmeared with blood, appeared like little mountains.

sn: वर्तमाने तथा घोरं संकुले सर्वतोदिशम्। अविज्ञाताः स्म युध्यन्ते विनिघ्नन्तः परस्परम्॥
en: When such a dreadful battle raged on all sides, people not know themselves killed one another.

sn: भौमेन रजसाऽऽकीर्णे शस्त्रसम्पातसंकुले। नैव स्वे न परे राजन् व्यज्ञायन्त तमोवृताः॥
en: When everything was covered with dust raised by the weapons, they, O king, could not recognise who were their own and who were their enemies.

sn: तथा तद्भवद् युद्धं घोररूपं भयानकम्। लोहितोदा महानद्यः प्रसस्रुस्तत्र चासकृत्॥
en: Then there took place a dreadful encounter and there flew a river of blood striking terror unto all.

sn: शीर्षपाषाणसंछन्नाः केशशैवलशाद्वलाः। अस्तिमीनसमाकीर्णा धनुःशरगदोडुपाः॥
en: It was filled with heads forming the rocks. The hairs of the warriors formed the floating weeds and mosses. Bones formed the fishes; and bows, arrows and maces formed the rafts by which to cross them.

sn: मांसशोणितपकिन्यो घोररूपाः सुदारुणाः। नदी:प्रवर्तयामत्सुः शोणितौघविवर्धिनीः॥
en: Flesh and blood formed their mire. Thus dreadful and terrible rivers, with currents swelled by blood, were formed there.

sn: भीरुवित्रासकारिण्यः शूराणां हर्षवर्धनाः। ता नद्यो घोररूपास्तु नयन्त्यो यमसादनम्॥
en: They struck terror unto the timid and increased the joy of the brave. Those awful rivers led to the abode of Yama.

sn: अवगाढान् मजयन्त्यः क्षत्रस्याजनयन् भयम्। क्रव्यादानां नरव्याघ्र नर्दतां तत्र तत्र ह॥ घोरमायोधनं जज्ञे प्रेतराजपुरोपमम्।
en: And many plunged into those rivers striking terror unto the Kshatriyas and dies. O best of men, on account of many carnivorous animals emitting yells on all sides the battle-field became terrible, like the territory of the Regent of the Dead.

sn: उत्थितान्यगणेयानि कबन्धानि समन्ततः॥ नृत्यन्ति वै भूतगणाः सुतृप्ता मांसशोणितैः। पीत्वा च शौणितं तत्र वसां पीत्वा च भारत॥
en: And innumerable, headless trunks rose on all sides. And many terrible creatures eating flesh and drinking blood and fat began to dance around.

sn: मेदोमजावसामत्तास्तृप्त मांसस्य चैव ह। धावमानाः स्म दृश्यन्ते काकगृघ्रबकास्तथा॥
en: And gratified with fat, marrow and flesh crows, vultures and cranes were seen to move about in delight.

sn: शूरास्तु समरे राजन् भयं त्यक्त्वा सुदुस्त्यजम्। योघव्रतसमाख्याताश्चक्रुः कर्माण्यभीतवत्॥
en: The heroes, however, O king, shaking off fear and observing the warrior's warrior's vow, fearlessly did their duty.

sn: शरशक्तिसमाकीर्णे क्रव्यादगणसंकुले। व्यचरन्त रणे शूराः ख्यापयन्तः स्वपौरुषम्॥
en: On that field where innumerable arrows and darts passed through the air and where various carnivorous animals in large number and the brave warriors armed moved about displaying their powers.

sn: अन्योन्यं श्रावयन्ति स्म नामगोत्राणि भारत। पितृनामानि च रणे गोत्रनामानि वा विभो॥ श्रावयाणाश्च बहवस्तत्र योद्धा विशाम्पते। अन्योन्यमवमृद्नन्तः शक्तितोमरपट्टिशैः॥
en: They called out one another by their own and family names. And many taking the names of their fathers and families began to assail one another with darts, lances and battle axes.

sn: वर्तमाने तथा युद्धे घोररूपे सुदारुणे। व्यषीदत् कौरवी सेना भिन्ना नौरिव सागरे॥
en: In that-onset the Kuru army became divested of its strength and unable to stand any longer like a ship foundered on the bosom of the ocean.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: संजय उवाच वर्तमाने तथा युद्धे क्षत्रियाणां निमञ्जने। गाण्डीवस्य महाघोषः श्रूयते युधि मारिष॥
en: Sanjaya said While that war, destructive of the Kshatriyas, raged on, the dreadful twang of the Gandiva bow was heard, O Sire.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: संशप्तकानां कदनमकरोद् यत्र पाण्डवः। कोसलानां तथा राजन् नारायणबलस्य च॥
en: O king, there the son of Pandu brought about the destruction of the Samsaptakas, the Kosalas and the army of Narayana.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: संशप्तकास्तु समरे शरवृष्टीः समन्ततः। अपातयन् पार्थमूर्ध्नि जयगृद्धाः प्रमन्यवः॥
en: The Samsaptakas too, desirous of acquiring victory and worked up with rage, made a downpour of their arrows from all sides on the head of Partha.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: ता वृष्टीः सहसा राजंस्तरसा धारयन् प्रभुः। व्यगाहत रणे पार्थो विनिनन् रथिनां वरान्॥
en: That shower of arrows, O king, the powerful Arjuna soon checked and plunging into battle destroyed many leading carwarriors.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: विगाह्य तद् स्थानीकं कङ्कपत्रैः शिलाशितैः। आससाद ततः पार्थः सुशर्माणं वरायुधम्॥
en: Having assailed the car-warriors with Kanka-feathered and sharp arrows, Partha approached the mighty car-warrior, Susharma.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: स तस्य शरवर्षाणि ववर्ष रथिनां वरः। तथा संशप्तकाश्चैव पार्थं बाणैः समार्पयन्॥
en: That foremost of car-Warriors made a downpour of arrows and the Samsaptakas too covered Partha with their shafts.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: सुशर्मा तु ततः पार्थं विद्ध्वा दशभिराशुगैः। जनार्दनं त्रिभिर्बाणैरहनद् दक्षिणे भुजे॥
en: Thereupon, Susharma having pierced Partha with ten quick-coursing arrows struck Janardana on his right arm with three arrows.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: ततोऽपरेण भल्लेन केतुं विव्याध मारिष। स वानरवरो राजन् विश्वकर्मकृतो महान्॥ ननाद सुमहानादं भीषयाणो जगर्ज च।
en: Then with another Bhalla he struck down his standard. That huge monkey, created by Vishvakarma, O king, being terrified emitted a tremendous roar.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: कपेस्तु निनदं श्रुत्वा संत्रस्ता तव वाहिनी॥ भयं विपुलमाधाय निश्चेष्टा समपद्यत।
en: Hearing the roar of the monkey, your army was agitated. And possessed by terrible fear they became inactive.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: तत: सा शुशुभे सेना निश्चेष्टावस्थिता नृप।॥ नानापुष्पसमाकीर्णं यथा चैत्ररथं वनम्।
en: Becoming inactive, O king, that army looked like the garden of Chitraratha filled with various flowers.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: प्रतिलभ्यं तत: संज्ञां योधास्ते कुरुसत्तम॥ अर्जुनं सिषिचुर्बाणैः पर्वतं जलदा इव।
en: Then regaining their consciousness, O foremost of Kurus, your soldiers made a downpour of arrows on Arjuna like clouds on a mountain.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: परिवब्रुस्ततः सर्वे पाण्डवस्य महारथम्॥ निगृह्य तं प्रचुक्रुशुर्वध्यामानां शितैः शरैः।
en: They, then, all surrounded the huge car of Pandava. And then assailing him with sharpened arrows they, desirous of killing him, began to emit terrific cries.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: ते हयान् रथचक्रे च रथेषां चापि मारिष॥ निग्रहीतुमुपाक्रामन् क्रोधाविष्टाः समन्ततः।
en: O king, then assailing with with great vehemence his horses, the wheels of his car and Ishadanda.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: निगृह्य तं रथं तस्य योधास्ते तु सहस्रशः॥ निगृह्य बलवत् सर्वे सिंहनादमथानदन्।
en: Thousand of soldiers seized his car and began to send up leonine roars.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: अपरे जगृहुश्चैव केशवस्य महाभुजौ॥ पार्थमन्ये महाराज रथस्थं जगृहुर्मुदा।
en: O sire, Some among them seized the long arins of Kesava and others seized Arjuna who was on his car.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: केशवस्तु ततो बाहू विधुन्वन् रणमूर्धनि॥ पातयामास तान् सर्वान् दुष्टहस्तीव हस्तिपान्।
en: Then shaking his arms on the field of battle Keshava struck down all of them like an elephant assailing other leading elephants.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: ततः क्रुद्धो रणे पार्थः संवृतस्तैर्महारथैः॥ निगृहीतं रथं दृष्ट्वा केशवं चाप्यभिद्रुतम्।
en: Surrounded by those mighty car-warriors and beholding his car assailed and thus Keshava attacked, Partha, boiling with rage, overthrew a large number of car-warriors and foot-soldiers.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: रथारूढांस्तु सुबहून् पदातींश्चाप्यपातयत्॥ आसन्नांश्च तथा योधान् शरैरासन्नयोधिभिः। छादयामास समरे केशवं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: He pushed down a number of infantry soldiers rode on his chariot while fighting, covered all Samsaptaka warriors stood nearby through volley of arrows useful for proxy war and said with vigour to lord Krishna in the battle-field.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: पश्य कृष्ण महाबाहो संशप्तकगणान् बहून्। कुर्वाणान् दारुणं कर्म वध्यमानान् सहस्रशः॥
en: “Behold, O Krishna, O you of long arms, those numberless Samsaptakas, bent upon a dreadful feat, are killed by thousands.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: रथबन्धमिमं घोरं पृथिव्यां नास्ति कश्चन। यः सहेत पुमाँल्लोके मदन्यो यदुपुङ्गव॥
en: O foremost of Yadus, there is none on earth, save myself who is capable of bearing such a close attack on his car."

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा बीभत्सुर्देवदत्तमथाधमत्। पाञ्चजन्यं च कृष्णोऽपि पूरयन्निव रोदसी॥
en: Having said this Vibhatsu blew his Devadatta conch and Krishna his Panchajanya filling the earth and sky with the blare.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: तं तु शङ्खस्वनं श्रुत्वा संशप्तकवरूथिनी। संचचाल महाराज वित्रस्ता चादवद् भृशम्॥
en: Hearing that sound the army of the Samsaptakas began to tremble and were filled with fear.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: पादबन्धं ततश्चक्रे पाण्डवः परवीरहा। नागमस्त्रं महाराज सम्प्रकीर्य मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: O monarch, then repeatedly invoking the Naga weapon, Paridava, the slayers of hostile horses, tied down their legs.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: ते बद्धाः पादबन्धेन पाण्डवेन महात्मना। निश्चेष्टाश्चाभवन् राजन्नश्मसारमया इव॥
en: When they were thus bound down by the high-souled son of Pandu, O king, they became inactive like horses and dogs.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: निश्चेष्टास्तुं ततो योधानबधीत् पाण्डुनन्दनः। यथेन्द्रः समरे दैत्यांस्तारकस्य वधे पुरा॥
en: Then the son of Pandu began to slay all those inactive warriors as Indra killed the Asuras in the days of yore in his encounter with Taraka.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे मुमुचुस्तं रथोत्तमम्। आयुधानि च सर्वाणि विस्त्रष्टुमुपचक्रमुः॥
en: They, thus being slaughtered in battle, began to leave the best of cars and throw off all their weapons.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: ते बद्धाःपादबधेन न शेकुश्चेष्टितुं नृप। ततस्तानवधीत् पार्थः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Having their legs bound down they could make no effort, O king. Then Partha slew them all with his straight arrows.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: सर्वयोधा हि समरे भुजगैर्वेष्टिताभवन्। यानुद्दिश्य रणे पार्थः पादबन्धं चकार ह॥
en: All those warriors, against whom Partha discharged his weapon of tying legs, were encircled by serpents in battle.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: ततः सुशर्मा राजेन्द्र गृहीतां वीक्ष्य वाहिनीम्। सौपर्णमस्त्रं त्वरित: प्रादुश्चके महारथः॥
en: Then beholding his army thus bound down, O king, the might car-warrior Susharma speedily invoked his Sauparna weapon.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: तत: सुपर्णाः सम्पेतुर्भक्षयन्तो भुजङ्गमान्। ते वै विदुद्रुवुर्नागा दृष्ट्वा तान् खचरानृप॥
en: Then numerous vultures began to come down and devour snakes. Then, O king, beholding those birds the serpents began to fly away.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: बभौ बलं तद्विमुक्तं पादबन्धाद् विशाम्पते। मेघवृन्दाद् यथा मुक्तो भास्करस्तापयन् प्रजाः॥
en: Freed from that foot-trapping weapon the Samsaptakas, O monarch, looked like the sun giving rays unto all creatures when freed from clouds.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: विप्रमुक्तास्तु ते योधाः फाल्गुनस्य रथं प्रति। ससृजुर्बाण संघाश्च शस्त्रसंघांश्च मारिष॥ विविधानि च शस्त्राणि प्रत्यविध्यन्त सर्वशः।
en: Thus freed, the warriors once more discharged their arrows and weapons at Arjuna's car. And all of them pierced Partha with numerous weapons

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: तां महास्त्रमयीं वृष्टिं संछिद्य शरवृष्टिभिः॥ न्यवधीच ततो योधान् वासविः परवीरहा।
en: Cutting off with his own arrows the brightly weapons showered on him, Vasava's son, the slayer of hostile heroes, began to kill those warriors.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: सुशर्मा तु ततो राजन् बाणेनानतपर्वणा॥ अर्जुनं हृदये विद्ध्वा विव्याधान्यैस्त्रिभिः शरैः।
en: Thereupon Susharma, O king, struck Arjuna to his very vitals with arrows and three weapons.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: स गाढविद्धो व्यथितो रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्॥ तत उचुक्रुशुः सर्वे हतः पार्थ इति स्म हो ततः शङ्खनिनादाश्च भेरीशब्दाश्च पुष्कलाः॥ नानावादिनानिनदाः सिंहनादाश्च जज्ञिरे।
en: Deeply wounded and felling great pain Arjuna sunk down on the terrace of his car. Then all the soldiers cried aloud Partha is killed. Then there arose the blare of conch, the profuse sound of bugles and many other musical instruments and the leonine roars of the warriors.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञां श्वेतचाश्वः कृष्णसारथिः॥ ऐन्द्रमस्त्रममेयात्मा प्रादुश्चक्ते त्वरान्वितः।
en: Then regaining his consciousness the highly energetic Arjuna of white steeds and with Krishna for his charioteer, quickly discharged the Aindra weapon.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: ततो बाणसहस्राणि समुत्पन्नानि मारिष॥ सर्वदिक्षु व्यदृश्यन्त निघ्नन्ति तव वाहिनीम्।
en: Thereupon, thousands of arrows were seen on all sides which killed the kings and elephants.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: हयान् रथांश्च समरे शस्त्रैः शतसहस्रशः॥ वध्यमाने ततः सैन्ये भयं सुमहदाविशत्। संशप्तकगणानां च गोपालानां च भारत॥
en: Thousands of horses and cars were also destroyed by those weapons. The army being thus slaughtered they were possessed by terrible fear. O descendant of Bharata, there was no man amongst the Samsaptakas and Gopalas who could withstand Arjuna.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: न हि तत्र पुमान् कश्चिद योऽर्जुनं प्रत्यविध्यत। पश्यतां तत्र वीराणामहन्यत बलं तव॥
en: There in the very presence of all the heroes Arjuna began to destroy your army.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: हन्यमानमपश्यंश्च निश्चेष्टं स्म पराक्रमे। अयुतं तत्र योधानां हत्वा पाण्डुसुतो रणे॥ व्यभ्राजत महाराज विधूमोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन्।
en: Beholding that slaughter all of them were petrified and could not display their prowess. Having killed ten thousand warriors in that battle the son of Pandu shone like the blazing fire without smoke.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: चतुर्दश सहस्राणि यानि शिष्टानि भारत॥ रथानामयुतं चैव त्रिसाहस्त्राश्च दन्तिनः।
en: O Bharata! there remained living as much as fourteen thousand infantry soldiers, ten thousand chariot riders and three thousand elephants with Samsaptakas (Kauravas) till then.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: तत: संशप्तका भूयः परिवर्धनंजयम्॥ मर्तव्यमिति निश्चित्य जयं वाप्यनिवर्तनम्।
en: Then the Samsaptakas surrounded Dhananjaya determined upon either gaining victory or meeting with death.

description: Destruction of Ten thousand Samsaptakas by Arjuna
sn: तत्र युद्धं महवासीत् तावकानां विशाम्पते। शूरेण बलिना सार्धं पाण्डवेन किरीटिना॥
en: Then there took place a dreadful encounter between your army, O king and the heroic, diadem-decked son of Pandu.

sn: संजय उवाच कृतवर्मा कृपो द्रौणिः सूतपुत्रश्च मारिष। उलूकः सौबलश्चैव राजा च सह सोदरैः॥ सीदमानां चमूं दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुपुत्रभयार्दिताम्। समुहुः स्म वेगेन भिन्नां नावमिवार्णवे॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding the Kuru army afflicted with the fear of Pandu's son sinking like a boat foundered in the ocean, Kritavarma, Kripa, Drona's son, Suta's son, Ulaka, Subala's son Shakuni and the king himself with his brother, came to their rescue.

sn: ततो युद्धमतीवासीन्मुहूर्तमिव भारत। भीरूणां त्रासजननं शूराणां हर्षवर्धनम्॥
en: Then there took place an encounter for the time being capable of striking terror unto the timid and increasing the delight of the heroes.

sn: कृपेण शरवर्षाणि प्रतिमुक्तानि संयुगे। सृञ्जयांश्छादयामासुः शलभानां व्रजा इव॥
en: The downpour of arrows made by Kripa in the battle covered the Srinjayas like a swarm of locusts.

sn: शिखण्डी च ततः क्रुद्धो गौतमं त्वरितो ययौ। ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि समन्ताद् द्विजपुङ्गवम्॥
en: Thereupon Shikhandin, worked up with anger, speedily approached the son of Gautaina and discharged a shower of arrows upon that best of men.

sn: कृपस्तु शरवर्षं तद् विनिहत्य महास्त्रवित्। शिखण्डिनं रणे क्रद्धो विव्याध दशभिः शरैः॥
en: And checking that downpour of arrows Kripa, conversant with the use of mighty weapons and filled with anger, struck in that encounter Shikhandin with ten arrows.

sn: ततः शिखण्डी कुपितः शरैः सप्तभिराहवे। कृपं विव्याध कुपितं कङ्कपत्रैरजिह्मगैः॥
en: Then Shikhandin, worked up with anger, pierced Kripa and seven straight Kankafeathered arrows.

sn: ततः कृपः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः सोऽतिविद्धो महारथः। व्यश्वसूतरथं चक्रे शिखण्डिनमथो द्विजः॥
en: Then the Brahmana Kripa, a mighty carwarrior, piercing heavily with sharp arrows, deprived Shikhandin of his horses, charioteer and car.

sn: हताश्चात् तु ततो यानादवप्लुत्य महारथः। खङ्गं चर्म तथा गृह्य सत्वं ब्राह्मणं ययौ॥
en: Then jumping down from the car, the heroes of which were slain, the mighty carwarrior speedily took up his sword and armour and approached the Brahmana.

sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। छादयामास समरे तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥ तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम शिलानां प्लवनं यथा। निश्चेष्टस्तद् रणे राजञ्छिखण्डी समतिष्ठत॥
en: Then he covered him suddenly who was approaching with straight arrows. This was indeed wonderful. We then, O king, beheld a wonderful spectacle like the flying of rocks. And Shikhandin remained inactive in that battle.

sn: कृपेणच्छादितं दृष्ट्वा नृपोत्तम शिखण्डिनम्। प्रत्युद्यायौ कृपं तूर्णं धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः॥
en: Beholding Shikhandin covered with arrows by Kripa, O foremost of kings, the mighty carwarrior Dhristadyumna speedily approached him.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं ततो यान्तं शारद्वतरथं प्रति। प्रतिजग्राह वेगेन कृतवर्मा महारथः॥
en: Thereupon the mighty car-warrior Kritavarma vehemently resisted Dhristadyumna who was advancing towards the son of Sharadvata.

sn: युधिष्ठिरमथायान्तं शारद्वतरथं प्रति। सपुत्रं सहसैन्यं च द्रौणपुत्रो न्यवारयत्॥
en: Drona's son then resisted Yudhishthira who was advancing with his own son and arms against the son of Sharadvata.

sn: नकुलं सहदेवं च त्वरमाणौ महारथौ। प्रतिजग्राह ते पुत्रः शरवर्षेण वारयन्॥
en: Your son then impeded with a downpour of arrows the approach of the two car-warriors Nakula and Sahadeva.

sn: भीमसेन करूषांश्च केकयान् सह संजयैः। कर्णो वैकर्तनो युद्धे वारयामास भारत॥
en: Karna, the son of Vikartana, O descendant of Bharata, then resisted in battle Bhimasena, Karushas, Kaikeyas and Srinjayas.

sn: शिखण्डिनस्ततौ बाणान् कृपः शारद्वतो युधि। प्राहिणोत् त्वरया युक्तो दिधक्षुरिव मारिष।॥
en: Then in the battle, O Sire, Kripa quickly hurled arrows at Shikhandin as to burn him down.

sn: ताञ्छरान् प्रेषितास्तेन समन्तात् स्वर्णभूषितान्। चिच्छदेन खङ्गमाविध्य भ्रामयंश्च पुनः पुनः॥
en: Whirling his sword repeatedly (Shikhandin) then with his sword cut-off all those golddecked arrows that were discharged at him.

sn: शतचन्द्रं च तचर्म गौतमस्तस्य भारत। व्यधमत् सायकैस्तूर्णं तत उचुक्रुशुर्जनाः॥
en: The son of Gautama then quickly cut-off with his arrows the shield of Prishata's son that was adorned with a hundred moons. At this his people made a loud uproar.

sn: स विचर्मा महाराज खङ्गपाणिरुपाद्रवत्। कृपस्य वशमापन्नो मृत्योरास्यमिवातुरः॥
en: Deprived of his shield, O monarch and brought under the influence of Kripa, he, with his sword, advanced like a sick man advancing towards death.

sn: शारद्वतशरैर्ग्रस्तं विश्यमानं महाबलः। चित्रकेतुसुतो राजन् सुकेतुस्त्वरितो ययौ॥
en: O king, Chitraketu's son Suketu quickly proceeded towards the highly powerful (Shikhandin) who was thus distressed and assailed by the son of Sharadvata.

sn: विकिरन् ब्राह्मणं युद्धे बहुभिर्निशितैः शरै। अभ्यापतदमेयात्मा गौतमस्य रथं प्रति॥
en: Having covered in battle the Brahmana with sharp arrows, that one of immeasurable energy, advanced towards the car of Gautama's son.

sn: दृष्ट्वा च युक्तं त युद्धे ब्राह्मणं चरितव्रतम्। अपयातस्तस्तूर्णं शिखण्डी राजसत्तम।॥
en: Beholding that Brahmana, observant of vows thus engaged in battle, Shikhandin, O king, quickly proceeded there.

sn: सुकेतुस्तु ततो राजन् गौतमं नवभिः शरैः। विद्ध्वा विव्याध सप्तत्या पुनश्चैनं त्रिभिः शरैः॥
en: O king, having pierced the son of Gautama with nine arrows Suketu once more pierced him with seventy and again with three.

sn: अथास्य सशरं चापं पुनश्चिच्छेद मारिष। सारथिं च शरेणास्य भृशं मर्मस्वताडयत्॥
en: He then cut-off his bow and arrows; then with another he pierced greatly his driver to the very vitals.

sn: गौतमस्तु ततः क्रुद्धो धनुर्गृह्य नवं दृढम्। सुकेतुं त्रिंशता बाणैः सर्वमर्मस्वताडयत्॥
en: Thereupon worked up with anger Gautama took up a fresh and strong bow and cut-off Suketu to the very vital part with thirty arrows.

sn: स विह्वलितसर्वाङ्गः प्रचचाल रथोत्तमे। भूमिकम्पे यथा वृक्षश्चचाल कम्पितो भृशम्॥
en: All his limbs were weakened and he shook on that best of cars as a tree trembles greatly during an earth quake.

sn: चलतस्तस्य कायात् तु शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम्। सोष्णीयं सशिरस्त्राणं क्षुरप्रेण त्वपातयद्॥
en: Then with a razor-sharpened arrow he sundered from body his head still trembling with shining ear-rings, crown and headprotector.

sn: तच्छिरंः प्रापतद् भूमौ श्येनाहतमिवामिषम्। ततोऽस्य कायो वसुधां पश्चात् प्रापतदच्युत॥
en: His head fell down on the earth like a piece of meant stolen away by a hawk, afterwards his body, O Eternal one, fell down on the earth.

sn: तस्मिन् हते महाराज त्रस्तास्तस्य पुरोगमाः। गौतमं हरे त्यक्त्वा दुदुवुस्ते दिशो दश॥
en: O Emperor, when he was slain, all his followers, leaving behind the son of Gautama in the battle-field fled, away in ten directions.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं तु समरे संनिवार्य महारथः। कृतवर्माब्रवीद्धृष्टस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति भारत॥
en: Encircling the highly powerful Dhristadyumna in the battle-field Kritavarma said to him-"Wait! wait!"

sn: तदभूत् तुमुलं युद्धं वृष्णिपार्षतयो रणे। आमिषार्थे यथा युद्धं श्येनयोः क्रुद्धयोप॥
en: Then there took place a terrible and wonderful encounter between the Vrishnis and Parsatas like that of two angry hawks, O king, for a piece of meat.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु समरे हार्दिक्य नवभिः शरैः। आजधानोरसि क्रुद्धः पीडयन् हृदिकात्मजम्॥
en: Worked up with anger, Dhristadyumna, in that battle, assailed Hridika's son violently and struck him on the chest with nine arrows.

sn: कृतवर्मा तु समरे पार्षतेन दृढाहतः। पार्षतं सरथं छादयामास सायकैः॥
en: Thus Assailed by a Parohata in battle Kritavarma covered him, his chariot and horses with arrows.

sn: सरथश्छादितो राजन् धृष्टद्युम्नो न दृश्यते। मेधैरिव परिच्छन्नो भास्करो जलधारिभिः॥
en: O king, thus covered along with his car Dhristadyumna became invisible like the sun enshrouded by clouds surcharged with water.

sn: विधूय तं बाणगणं शरैः कनकभूषणैः। व्यरोचत रणे राजन् धृष्टद्युम्नः कृतव्रणः॥
en: Withstanding him with gold feathered arrows, O king, Dhristadyumna appeared in battle with wounds.

sn: ततस्तु पार्षतः क्रुद्धः शस्त्रवृष्टिं सुदारुणाम्। कृतवर्माणमासाद्य व्यसृजत् पृतनापतिः॥
en: Obtaining Kritavarma, Parsata, the commander of the forces, worked up with anger, made a terrible downpour of arrows.

sn: तामापतन्तीं सहसा शस्त्रवृष्टिं सुदारुणाम्। शरैरनेकसाहस्त्रैर्हार्दिक्योऽवारयद् युधि॥
en: In that battle Hridika's son with many thousand arrows, all on a sudden, dispelled that highly dreadful shower of arrows that was about to fall on him.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तु वारितां युद्धे शस्त्रवृष्टिं दुरासदाम्। कृतवर्माणमासाद्य वारयामास पार्षतः॥
en: Beholding in that battle that fearful downpour of arrows thus dispelled by him Prishata's son, approaching Kritavarma, withstood him.

sn: सारथिं चास्य तरसा प्राहिणोद् यमसादनम्। भल्लेन शितधारेण स हतः प्रापतद् रथात्॥
en: With a sharpened spike he dispatched his charioteer to the abode of Death. Slain he fell down from the chariot.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु बलवाञ्जित्वा शत्रु महाबलम्। कौरवान् समरे तूर्णं वारयामास सायकैः॥
en: Having vanquished his highly powerful enemy, the mighty Dhristadyumna speedily withstood the Kauravas in battle with arrows.

sn: ततस्ते तावका योधा धृष्टद्युम्नमुपाद्रवन्। सिंहनादरवं कृत्वा ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: Thereupon emitting leonine roars your warriors ran towards Dhristadyumna and again an encounter took place.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: संजय उवाच द्रौणियुधिष्ठिरं दृष्ट्वा शैनेयेनाभिरक्षितम्। द्रौपदेयैस्तथा शूरैरभ्यवर्तत हृष्टवतः॥ किरन्निषुगणान् घोरान् स्वर्णपुङ्खाशिलाशितान्। दर्शयन् विविधान् मार्गान् शिक्षाश्च लघुहस्तवत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding Yudhishthira protected by Sini's son as well as by the war-like sons of Draupadi, the son of Drona, as if delighted, proceeded against him, scattering goldfeathered arrows, showing various ways of his light-handedness.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: ततः खं पूरयामास शरैर्दिव्यास्त्रमन्त्रितैः। युधिष्ठिरं च समरे परिवार्य महास्त्रवित्॥
en: Thereupon he filled the sky with arrows of the vigour of celestial weapons. That one, conversant with the use of weapons, withstood Yudhishthira in battle.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: द्रौणायनिशरच्छन्नं न प्राज्ञायत किञ्चन। बाणभूतमभूत् सर्वमायोधनशिरो महत्॥
en: When the sky was covered with the arrows of Drona's son nothing could be perceived. The space before the warriors was filled with arrows.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: बाणजालं दिविच्छन्नं स्वर्णजालविभूषितम्। शुशुभे भरतश्रेष्ठ वितानमिव धिष्ठितम्॥
en: The sky being covered with a net-work of golden arrows it appeared as if a canopy had been spread there.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: तेनच्छन्न नभो राजन् बाणजालेन भास्वता। अभ्रच्छायेव संजज्ञे बाणरुद्ध नभस्तले॥
en: O king, the sky being covered with a network of shining arrows a shadow appeared there like that of clouds.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: तत्राश्चर्यमपश्याम बाणभूते तथाविधे। न स्म सम्पतते भूतंकिंचिदेवान्तरिक्षगम्॥
en: When the sky was thus converted into one sheet of arrows it was a wonderful sight to look at. No creature could range in the sky at that time.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: सात्यकिर्यतमानस्तु धर्मराजश्च पाण्डवः। तथेतराणि सैन्यानि न स्म चक्रुः पराक्रमम्॥
en: Satyaki, although trying his very best, the pious son of Pandu and other warriors, could not display their prowess.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: लाघवं द्रोणपुत्रस्य दृष्ट्वा तत्र महारथाः। व्यस्मयन्त महाराज न चैनं प्रत्युदीक्षितुम्॥ शेकुस्ते सर्वराजानस्तपन्तमिव भास्करम्।
en: Beholding the light-handness of Drona's son, all the mighty car-warriors there, O king, were filled with wonder. All the kings could not look at him, as if shedding lustre of the sun.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: वध्यमाने ततः सैन्ये द्रौपदेया महारथाः॥ सात्यकिधर्मराजश्च पञ्चालाश्चाप संगताः। त्यक्त्वा मृत्युभयं घोरं द्रौणायनिमुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Thereupon, when their soldiers were being thus slaughtered, the mighty car-warriors, the son of Draupadi, Satyaki, the pious king Yudhishthira and the Panchalas, all united, giving up the dreadful fear of death, rushed towards the son of Drona.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: सात्यकिः सप्तविंशत्या द्रौणि विद्ध्वा शिलीमुखैः। पुनर्विव्याध नाराचैः सप्तभिः स्वर्णभूषितैः॥
en: Piercing the son of Drona with twenty seven arrows he again pierced him with seven gold-plated winged arrows.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: युधिष्ठिरस्त्रिसप्ततया प्रतिबिध्यश्च सप्तभिः। श्रुतकर्मा त्रिभिर्बाणैः श्रुतकीर्तिश्च सप्तभि॥ सुतसोमस्तु नवभिः शतानीकश्च सप्तभिः। अन्ये च बहवः शूरा विव्यधुस्तं समन्ततः॥
en: Yudhishthira struck him with seventy three arrows and Prativinda with seven, Shrutakarma cut him with three arrows and Shrutakirti with seven. Sutasoma struck him with nine arrows and Satanika with seven. And many other warrior struck him from all sides with a number of shafts.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: स तु क्रुद्धस्ततो राजन्नाशीविष इव श्वसन्। सात्यकिं पञ्चविंशत्या प्रत्यविध्यच्छिलीमुखैः॥
en: Thereupon worked up with rage, O king, he, sighing like a deadly serpent, struck Satyaki with twenty five sharpened arrows.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: श्रुतकीर्ति च नवभिः सुतसोमं च पञ्चभिः। अष्टभिः श्रुतकर्माणं प्रतिविध्यं त्रिभिः शरैः॥ शतानीकं च नवभिर्धर्मपुत्रं च पञ्चभिः। तथेतरांस्ततः : शूरान् द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यामताडयत्॥ श्रुतकीर्तेस्तथा चापं चिच्छेद निशितैः शरैः।
en: And he struck Srutakirti with nine arrows and Sutasoma with five; and Prativindhya with three arrows and Srutakarma with eight. And he. struck Raja Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, with five arrows and Satanika with nine. And then he struck other warriors with two shafts each and cut into pieces the bow of Srutakirti with very sharp pointed arrows.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय श्रुतिकीर्तिर्महारथः॥ द्रौणानि त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा विव्याधान्यैः शितैः शरैः।
en: After this Shrutakirti took up another fresh bow and at once struck Drona's son with three a arrows and began to shower on him numerous sharp-pointed arrows.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: ततो द्रौणिर्महाराज शरवर्षेण मारिष॥ छादयामास तत् सैन्यं समन्ताद् भरतर्षभ।
en: Then, O monarch, O great sire of the Bharata race, the son of Drona covered the Pandava army with showers of arrows.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: ततः पुनरमेयात्मा धर्मराजस्य कार्मुकम्॥ द्रौणिश्चिच्छेद विहसन् विव्याध च शरैस्त्रिभिः।
en: Just after this the highly spirited son of Drona, casting smiling look upon Yudhishthira, simultaneously cut-off his bow and struck him with three arrows.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: ततो धर्मसुतो राजन् प्रगृह्यान्यन्महद् धनुः॥ द्रौणिं विव्याधं सप्तत्या बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्।
en: Upon that, О king, the son of Dharma took up a very big bow and darted, one after another, seventy shafts, piercing the arms and breast of the son of Drona.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: सात्यकिस्तु ततः क्रुद्धो द्रौणेः प्रहरतो रणे॥ अर्धचन्द्रेण तीक्ष्णेन धनुश्छित्त्वानदद् भृशम्।
en: Then Satyaki, filled with anger, roared aloud and broke down in that very battle the bow of that terrible afflicter, Drona's son, with the same-circular and sharp arrow of his own.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: छिन्नधन्वा ततो द्रौणिः शक्त्या शक्तिमतां वरः॥ सारथिं पातयामास शैनेयस्य रथा द्रुतम्।
en: When his bow was thus cut-off that hero of heroes, Drona's son, with a dart quickly struck the driver of Satyaki's car down and unseated him from his chariot.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय द्रोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥ शैनेयं शरवर्षेणच्छादयामास भारत!
en: Then, O Bharata, the mighty son of Drona, taking up another bow, covered the son of Sini with quite a shower of arrows.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: तस्याश्वाः प्रदूताः संख्ये पतिते रथसारथौ॥ तत्र तत्रैव धावन्तः समदृश्यन्त भारत।
en: Thus, O Bharata, the driver was killed Satyaki's horses were seen to run riot in the battle-field.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: युधिष्ठिरपुरोगास्तु द्रौणिशस्त्रभृतां वरम्॥ अभ्यवर्षन्त वेगेन विसृजन्तः शिताञ्छरान्।
en: Then the Pandava army commanded by Raja Yudhishthira, rushed furiously towards Drona's son, the foremost of all the wielders of weapons and began to shower sharp shafts upon him.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: आगच्छमानांस्तान् दृष्ट्वा क्रुद्धरूपान् परंतपः॥ प्रहसन् प्रतिजग्राह द्रोणपुत्रो महारणे।
en: Seeing them thus coming upon him as so many incarnations of anger the great terror of foes, Drona's son, received them all in the terrible battle with a spiteful smile.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: ततः शरशतज्वाल: सेनाकक्षं महारथः॥ द्रौणिर्ददाह समरे कक्षमग्निर्यथा वने।
en: Then the great car-warrior, Drona's son, burnt down, as it were, the Pandava troops in the battle with the flames of his arrows, just as the forest fire burns the dry hays and straws.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: तद् बलं पाण्डुपुत्रस्य द्रोणपुत्रप्रतापितम्॥ चुक्षुभे भरतश्रेष्ठ तिमिनेव नदीमुखम्।
en: O foremost of Bharata's race, the Pandava army, thus provoked by the son of Drona, became exceedingly agitated as the water of a river is troubled by a whale.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: दृष्ट्वा चैव महाराज द्रोणपुत्रपराक्रम्॥ निहतान् मेनिरे सर्वान् पाण्डून द्रोणसुतेन् वै।
en: O Maharaj, seeing the bravery of Drona's son made the people think, as if the Pandava army already were killed.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु त्वरितो द्रोणशिष्यो महारथः॥ अब्रवीद् द्रोणपुत्राय रोषमर्षसमन्वितः।
en: Then the great car-warrior Yudhishthira being enraged and filled with revengeful spirit thus addressed the son of Drona in a

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: नैव नाम तव प्रीत व नाम कृतज्ञता॥ यतस्तवं पुरुषव्याघ्र मामेवाद्य जिघांससि।
en: O mightiest of men, neither have you any feeling nor do you cherish any sense of gratitude when today you are ready even to slay me.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: ब्राह्मणेन तपः कार्ये दानमध्ययनं तथा॥ क्षत्रियेण धनुर्नाम्यं स भवान् ब्राह्मणब्रुवः।
en: To study and to practise asceticism and charities and the duties of a Brahman and the Kshatriyas only are authorised to use the bow. So it seems that you are a Brahmin in name only.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: मिषतस्ते महाबाहो युधि जेष्यामि कौरवान्॥ कुरुष्व समरे कर्म ब्रह्मबन्धुरसि ध्रुवम्।
en: However, O you of mighty arms, I am determined upon killing the Kaurava army in the battle just before your eyes. Do your best. I call you a scum of the Brahman race.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: एवमुक्तो महाराज द्रोणपुत्रः स्मयन्निव॥ युक्तं तत्त्वं च संचिन्त्य नोत्तरं किंचिद्ब्रवीत्।
en: Thus addressed, O monarch, the son of Drona smiled bashfully and pondering over what was proper and meet could not give any reply.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: अनुक्त्वा च ततः किंचिच्छरवर्षेण पाण्डवम्॥ छादयामास समरे क्रुद्धोऽन्तक इव प्रजाः।
en: Getting thus terribly annoyed the son of Drona kept quiet for a while and then began to shower arrows upon the Pandavas like unto the Destroyer himself when bent upon destroying the entire creation.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: स च्छाद्यमानस्तु तदा द्रोणपुत्रेण मारिष॥ पार्थोऽययातः शीघ्रं वै विहाय महतीं चमूम्।
en: Thus covered, as it were, by the arrows of the son of Drona Pritha's son fled away from the field leaving his large army.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: अपयाते ततस्तस्मिन् धर्मपुत्रे युधिष्ठिरे॥ द्रोणपुत्रस्ततो राजन् प्रत्यगात् स महामनाः।
en: After Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, had thus fled from the field, O king, the highminded son of Drona also left the spot.

description: The retreating of Yudhishthira from the battle-field
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजंस्तत्यक्त्वा द्रौणिं महाहवे। प्रवयौ तावकं सौन्यं युक्तः क्रूराय कर्मणे॥
en: Yudhishthira then, O king, thus avoiding the son of Drona in the great battle, marched against your army being determined to wage a ruthless slaughter.

sn: संजय उवाच भीमसेन सपाञ्चाल्यं चेदिकेकयसंवृतम्। वैकर्तनःस्वयं रुद्ध्वा वारयामास सायकैः॥
en: Sanjaya said After this Vaikartana, himself resisting Bhimasena aided by the king of Panchala, Chedi and Kaikeya, showered numberless arrows upon him.

sn: ततस्तु चेदिकारूषान् सृञ्जयांश्च महारथान्। कर्णो जघान समरे भीमसेनस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Karna killed in the battle many strong carwarriors of the Chedis, Karushas and Srinjayas in the very presence of Bhimasena.

sn: भीमसेनस्ततः कर्ण विहाय रथसत्तमम्। प्रयसौ कौरवं सैन्य कक्षमग्निरिव ज्वलन्॥
en: Then Bhimasena leaving Karna, the most powerful car-warrior, rushed towards the Kaurava force like a blazing forest fire.

sn: सूतपुत्रोऽपि समरेपञ्चालन् केकयांस्तथा। सृञ्जयांश्च महेष्वासान् निजधान सहस्रशः॥
en: The Suta's son too began to slay by thousands the mighty bowmen of the Panchalas, the Kaikeyas and the Srinjayas.

sn: संशप्तकेषु पार्थश्च कौरवेषु वृकोदरः। पञ्चालेषु तथा कर्ण क्षयं चक्रुर्महारथाः॥
en: Indeed, the mighty car-warriors Karna, Partha and Vrikodera began to annihilate the Panchalas, Samasaptakas and Kauravas respectively.

sn: ते क्षत्रिया दह्यमानास्त्रिभिस्तैः पावकोपमैः। जग्मुर्विनाश समरे राजन् दुर्मत्रिते तव॥
en: For your bad policy, O king, all these Kshatriyas, burnt down, as it were, by those three heroes resembling three burning flames, got exterminated.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः क्रुद्धो नकुलं नवभिः शरैः। विव्याध भरतश्रेष्ठ चतुरश्चास्य वाजिनः॥
en: Thereupon, O foremost of the Bharatas, Duryodhana, being enraged, pierced Nakula and the four holes of his car with nine arrows.

sn: ततः पुनरमेयात्मा तव पुत्रो जनाधिप। क्षुरेण सहदेवस्य ध्वजं चिच्छेद काञ्चनम्॥
en: Then again, O lord of men, your highly energetic son cut down the golden standard of Shahadeva with a razor.

sn: नकुलस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्तव पुत्रं च सप्तभिः। जघान समरे राजन् सहदेवश्च पञ्चभिः॥
en: Nakula then, O king, being greatly enraged, struck you son with seventy three arrows and Sahadeva with five. Filled with anger he struck.

sn: तावुभो भरतश्रेष्ठौ ज्येष्ठौ सर्वधनुष्मताम्। विव्याधोरसि संक्रुद्धः पञ्चभिः पञ्चभि शरैः॥
en: Then both of those great warriors of the Bharata race and the foremost of bowmen, on the breast with five arrows each.

sn: ततोऽपराभ्यां भल्लाभ्यां धनुषी समकृन्तत। यमयोः सहसा राजन् विव्याध च त्रिसप्तभिः॥
en: Then he cut-off the bows of both of those two warriors with two of his broad-pointed arrows and suddenly, O king he pierced both of them with twenty-one arrows.

sn: तावन्ये धनुषी श्रेष्ठे शक्रचापनिभे शुभे। प्रगृह्य रेजतुः शूरौ देवपुत्रसौ युधि॥
en: Each of them, taking up two beautiful bows resembling those of Indra's looked very graceful like two celestial youths in the battlefield.

sn: ततस्तौ रभसौ युद्धे भ्रातरौ भ्रातरं युधि। शरैर्ववृषतुोरैर्महामेघो यथाऽचलम्॥
en: Then, O king, those two brothers, greatly active in battle, began to throw terrible shafts in ceaseless torrents upon their cousins like two great masses of thick clouds pouring their contents on the hills.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज तव पुत्रो महारथः। पाण्डुपुत्रौ महेष्वासौ वारयामास पत्रिभिः॥
en: Thereupon, O king, your son, the great carwarrior, being greatly enraged resisted those the rays twin sons of Pandu, the great bowmen, with numberless arrows.

sn: धनुर्मण्डलमेवास्य दृश्यते युधि भारत। सायकाश्चैव दृश्यते निश्चरन्तः समन्ततः॥ आच्छादयन् दिशः सर्वाः सूर्यस्येवांशवो यथा।
en: The bow of your son, O Bharata, was repeatedly drawn to a circle and the arrows were ceaselessly issued from it towards all directions covered with Duryodhana's arrows those sons of Pandu ceased to shine brightly as the sun and the moon lose their splendour when enveloped with a mass of dark clouds. Indeed, O king, those gold-winged arrows, sharpened on stone, covered all the sides like of the sun.

sn: बाणभूते ततस्तस्मिन् संछन्ने च नभस्तले॥ यमाभ्यो ददृशे रूपं कालान्तकयमोपमम्।
en: When the firinament was thus covered and the whole sky looked like a sheet of arrows the twin brothers appeared like the destroyer himself.

sn: पराक्रमं तु तं दृष्ट्वा तर सूनोर्महारथाः॥ मृत्योरुपान्तिकं प्राप्तौ मादीपुत्रौ स्म मेनिरे।
en: But, on the other hand, beholding the valour of your son all the car-warriors took the twin sons of Madri to be at the point of death.

sn: ततः सेनापती राजन् पाण्डवस्य महारथः॥ पार्षतःप्रयसौ तत्र यत्र राजा सुयोधनः।
en: Then, O king, the mighty car-warrior Parsata, the commander of the Pandava army, went towards the direction of Suyodhana (Duryodhana).

sn: माद्रीपुत्रौ ततः शूरौ व्यतिक्रम्य महारथौ।॥ धृष्टद्युम्नस्तव सुतं वारयामास सायकैः।
en: Violating the regimental order of those two great car-warriors, the two brave sons of Madri, Dhristadyumna began to oppose your son with his arrows.

sn: तमविध्यदमेयात्मा तव पुत्रो ह्यमर्षणः॥ पाञ्चाल्यं पञ्चविंशत्या प्रहसन पुरुषर्षभः।
en: Then that highly energetic hero, your son, the foremost of men, full of revengeful spirit and smiling scoffingły, struck the prince of the Panchalas with twenty-five arrows.

sn: ततः पुनरमेयात्मा तव पुत्रो ह्यमर्षणः॥ विद्ध्वा ननाद् पाञ्चाल्यं षष्ट्या पञ्चभिरेव च।
en: Again the most energetic son of yours, actuated by the eager desire of taking revenge, struck the Panchala prince once with sixty arrows and again with five and roared aloud.

sn: तथास्य सशरं चापं हस्तावापं च मारिष॥ क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन राजा चिच्छेद संयुगे।
en: Then the king, O sire, cut-off, in the fight, with his razor-shaped arrow his enemy's bow and the leathern fence with the arrows fixed thereon.

sn: तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं पाञ्चाल्यः शत्रुकर्शनः॥ अन्यदादत्त वेगेन धनुर्भारसहं नवम्।
en: Throwing away that broken bow, that oppressor of foes, the prince of Panchala, quickly took up a new and more elastic one.

sn: प्रज्वलन्निव वेगेन संरम्भाद रुधिरेक्षणः॥ अशोभत महेष्वासो धृष्टद्युम्नः कृतव्रणः।
en: Then that great bowman, Dhristadyumna, with blood-shot eyes, shone on his car like a burning flame.

sn: स पञ्चदश नाराचाश्वसतः पन्नगानिव॥ जिघांसुर्भरतश्रेष्ठं धृष्टद्युम्नो व्यपासृजत्।
en: Then, O chief of Bharatas, the hero Dhristadyumna, bent bent upon killing him, discharged fifteen sharp shafts, called Narachas, which looked like hissing serpents.

sn: ते वर्म हेमविकृतं भित्वा राज्ञः शिलाशिताः॥ विविशुर्वसुधां वेगात् कङ्कबर्हिणवाससः।
en: These shafts, set with the feathers of Kanka's (peacocks') and sharpened on stone, were discharged with such a force that cutting through the gold bedecked armour of the king, they ran through his body and entered into the earth.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महाराज पुत्रस्तेऽतिव्यराजत॥ वसन्तकाले सुमहान् प्रफुल्ल इव किंशुकः।
en: Being deeply wounded, O king, your son looked exceedingly grand like a Kinshuka tree full of flowers in the spring.

sn: सच्छिन्नवर्मा नाराचप्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः॥ धृष्टद्युम्नस्य भल्लेन क्रुद्धश्चिच्छेद कार्मुकम्।
en: His armour being thus cut through and himself being fatigued with the wounds and his feelings being awfully excited he cut-off Dhristadyumna's bow with a broad pointed arrow.

sn: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं त्वरमाणो महीपतिः॥ सायकैर्दशभी राजन् भ्रुवोर्मध्ये समार्पयत्।
en: Then, O lord of the earth, the king penetrated ten arrows into the forehead of his assailant whose bow had already been cut-off by him.

sn: तस्य तेऽशोभयन् वक्त्रं कर्मारपरिमार्जिताः॥ प्रफुल्लं पङ्कजं यद्वद् भ्रमरा मधुर्लिप्सवः।
en: These shafts, polished by the black-smith, looked on the face of Dhristadyumna like so many black bees on a full blown lily desirous of sucking the sweet honey.

sn: तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं धृष्टद्युम्ना महामनाः॥ अन्यदादत्त वेगेन धनुर्भल्लांश्च षोडशा
en: Throwing that broken bow aside Dhristadyumna quickly took up another bow and with it sixteen broad-pointed arrows.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनस्याश्चन् हत्वा सूतं च पश्चभिः॥ धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन जातरूपपरिष्कृतम्।
en: Then with five of these arrows he slew Duryodhana's four horses and his Suta charioteer and with another he cut-off his gilded bow.

sn: रथं सोपस्करं छत्रं शक्तिं खङ्गं गदां ध्वजम्॥ भल्लैचिच्छेद दशभिः पुत्रस्य तव पार्षतः।
en: And with remaining ten shafts the son of Prishata cut-off the royal umbrella, the spear, the sword, the mace, the car with Upaskara and the flag of your son.

sn: तपनीयाङ्गदं चित्रं नागं मणिमयं शुभम्॥ ध्वजं कुरुपतेच्छिन्नं ददृशुः सर्वपार्थिवाः।
en: Alas, all the chiefs saw the beautiful standard of the Kuru king, adorned with golden Angada and bearing the likeness of an elephant set with jewels, cut-off by Dhristadyumna.

sn: दुर्योधन तु विरथं छिन्नवर्मायुधं रणे॥ भ्रातरः पर्यरक्षन्त सोदरा भरतर्षभा
en: Then, O foremost of the Bharata's race, Duryodhana, thus deprived of all his weapons in the battle, was protected by his brothers.

sn: तमोरोप्य रथे राजन् दण्डधारो नराधिपमः॥ अपाहरदसम्भ्रान्तो धृष्टद्युम्नस्य पश्यतः।
en: In the very sight of Dhristadyumna. Dandadhara, taking the king upon his own car, quickly carried him away from the field.

sn: कर्णस्तु सात्यकि जित्वां राजगृद्धी महाबलः॥ द्रोणहन्तारमुग्रेषु ससारभिमुखो रणे।
en: In the meantime, the greatly powerful Karna, having killed Satyaki, proceeded straight on towards the slayer of Drona for the rescue of the Kuru king.

sn: तं पृष्ठतोऽभ्ययात् तूर्णं शैनेयो वितुदञ्छरैः॥ वारणं जघनोपान्ते विषाणाभ्यामिव द्विपः।
en: And the son of Sini speedily pursued him striking him with arrows as an elephant pursues his rival piercing him with his tusks on the rear.

sn: स भारत महानासीद् योधानां सुमहात्मनाम्॥ कर्णपार्षतयोर्मध्ये त्वदीयानां महारणः।
en: Thus, O king, the battle raged furiously amongst these sturdy heroes of both the armies and the spot, lying between Karna and the son of Prishata, grew simply terrifying.

sn: न पाण्डवानां नास्माकं योधः कश्चित् पराङ्मुखः॥४० प्रत्यदृश्यत् ततः कर्णः पञ्चालांस्त्वरितो ययौ।
en: Not a single combatant, of either party, turned his face from the field. Karna then rushed towards the Panchala with great speed.

sn: तस्मिन् क्षणे नरश्रेष्ठ गजवाजिजनक्षयः॥ प्रादुरीसादुभयतो राजन् मध्यगतेऽहनि।
en: Then, O best of men, countless men, horses and elephant of both parties fell just when the sun ascended the meridian.

sn: पञ्चालास्तु महाराज त्वरिता विजिगीषवः॥ ते सर्वेऽभ्यद्रवन कर्णं पतित्रिण इव दुमम्।
en: The Panchalas, O king, desirous of victory, rushed towards Karna as birds flock towards their nest.

sn: तांस्तथाधिरथि: क्रुद्धो यतमानान् मनस्विनः॥ विचिन्वन्निव बाणौथैः समासादयदग्रगान्। व्याघ्रकेतुं सुशर्माणं चित्रं चोग्रायुधं जयम्॥ शुक्वं च रोचमानं च सिंहसेनं च दुर्जयम्।
en: And the energetic son of Adhiratha began to oppose the Panchalas from the front with his sharp arrows marking specially their leaders, Vyaghraketu, Susharma, Chitra, Ugrayudha, Jaya, Shukla, Rochainan and the unconquerable Singhasena.

sn: ते वीरा रथमार्गेण परिवर्नरोत्तमम्॥ सृजन्त सायकान् क्रुद्धं कर्णमाहवशोभिनम्।
en: All those heroes, quickly driving their cars towards Karna-the glory of the battle field, encompassed him and began to shower their sharp shafts upon that infuriated hero, the foremost of men.

sn: युध्यमानांस्तु तान् दूरान्मनुजेन्द्र प्रतापवान्॥ अष्टभिरष्टौ राधेयोऽभ्यर्दयनिशितैः शरैः।
en: But all those eight heroes who had proceeded to combat that brave hero, the son of Radha, were sorely afflicted by him each with eight piercing arrows.

sn: अथापरान् महाराज सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥ जघान् बहुसाहस्रान् योधान् युद्धविशारदान्।
en: Thereupon, O king, the powerful son of charioteer killed thousands of other heroes-all skillful in the manoeuvre of war.

sn: जिष्णुं च जिष्णुकर्माणं देवापि भद्रमेव च।॥ दण्डं च राजन् समरे चित्रं चित्रायुधं हरिम्। सिंहकेतुं रोचमान् शलभं च महारथम्॥ निजधान सुसंक्रुद्धश्चेदीनां त महारथान्।
en: Worked up with anger Karna stuck in battle, Jishnu, Jishnukarman, Devapi, Bhadra, Danda, Chitra, Chitrayudha, Hari, Singhaketu, Rochamana, the great car-warriors Shalabha and many other Chedi heroes.

sn: तेषामाददतः प्राणानासीदाधिरथेवपुः॥ शोणिताभ्युक्षिताङ्गस्य रुद्रस्येवोर्जितं महत्।
en: When the son of Adhiratha was engaged in striking those heroes his body, besmeared with blood and swelled with pride and animation, looked like the gigantic form of Rudra himself.

sn: तत्र भारत कर्णेन मातङ्गास्ताडिताः शरैः॥ सर्वतोऽभ्यद्रवन् भीताः कुर्वन्तो महदाकुलम्।
en: Then, O Bharata, the elephants afflicted by Karna's arrows, bolted with fear and caused great commotion in the battle-field.

sn: निपेतुरुर्व्य समरे कर्णसायकताडिताः॥ कुर्वन्तो विविधान् नादान् वज्रनुन्ना इवाचलाः।
en: Others, oppressed by Karna's arrows, cried aloud in diverse voice and fell down as do the mountain peaks when struck down with thunder.

sn: गजवाजिनमनुष्यैश्च निपतद्भिः समन्ततः॥ रथैश्चाधिरथेर्मार्गे समास्तीर्यत मेदिनी।
en: The earth, along the trace of Karna's car, was fully strewn with broken cars and carcasses of elephants, horses and men.

sn: नैवं भीष्मो न च द्रोणो नान्ये युधि च तावकाः॥५४ चक्रुः स्म तादृशं सर्म यादृशं वै कृतं रणे।
en: Verily one of the warriors of your army may not even Bhishma or Drona, did ever achieve such an exploit, as was achieved by Karna in the battle.

sn: सूतपुत्रेण नागेषु हयेषु त रथेषु च॥ नरेषु च महाराज कृतं स्म कदनं महत्।
en: Suta's son, O most valiant of men, indeed made a havoc amongst the elephants and horses and destroyed the cars and men in countless numbers.

sn: मृगमध्ये यथा सिंहो दृश्यते निर्भयश्चरन्॥ पञ्चालानां तथा मध्ये कर्णोऽचरदभीतवत् ।
en: Like a lion roaming fearlessly among a herd of deer Karna too moved about fcarlessly amongst the Panchalas.

sn: यथा मृगगणांस्त्रस्तान सिंहो द्रावयते दिशः॥ पञ्चालानां रथवातान् कर्णो व्यद्रावयत् तथा।
en: As a lion drives away a herd of timid deer in all directions, so Karna dispelled the crowd of Panchala's cars to all directions.

sn: सिहास्यं च यथा प्राप्य न जीवन्ति मृगाः क्वचित्।। तथा कर्णमुप्राप्य न जिजीवुर्महारथाः।
en: And as a stag cam never escape from the black jaws of a lion so even those heroes, who happened to approach Karna, could not return with their lives.

sn: वैश्वानरं यथा प्राप्य प्रतिदह्यन्ति वै जनाः॥ कर्णाग्निना रणे तद्वद् दग्धा भारत सृञ्जयाः।
en: As men are sure to be burnt down if they approach a blazing fire so even the Srinjayas, O Bharata, were burnt by the flame of Karna when they approached it.

sn: कर्णेन चेदिकैकेयपाञ्चालेषु च भारत॥ विश्राव्य नाम निहता बहवः शूरसम्मताः।
en: Many proud and well-approved heroes of the Chedis and Panchalas were killed by Karna.

sn: मम चासीन्मती राजन् दृष्ट्वा कर्णस्य विक्रमम्॥ नैकोऽप्याधिरथेर्जीवन् पाञ्चाल्यो मोक्ष्यते युधि। पञ्चालान् व्यधमत् संख्ये सूतपुत्रः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Beholding the valour of Karna, O king, I was under the impression that not even a single soul of the Panchalas would escape from the son of Adhiratha in that battle. Indeed the Suta's son repeatedly routed the Panchalas in the battle.

sn: पञ्चालानथ निघ्नन्तं कर्णं दृष्ट्वा महारणे। अभ्यधावत् सुसंक्रुद्धो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Beholding the Panchalas thus slain by Karna in that terrible battle Dharma-Raja Yudhishthira wrathfully rushed towards him.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नश्च राधेयं द्रौपदेयाश्च मारिष परिवब्रुरमित्रघ्नं शतशश्चापरे जनाः॥
en: Dhristadyumna, the sons of Droupadi and hundreds of other heroes, O Sire, speedily encompassed the son of Radha, the slayer of foes.

sn: शिखण्डी सहदेवश्च नकुलो नाकुलिस्तथा। जनमेजयः शिरेर्नप्ता बहवश्च प्रभद्रकाः॥ एते पुरोगमा भूत्वा धृष्टद्युम्नस्य संयुगे। कर्णमस्यन्तमिध्वस्त्रैर्विचेरुरमितौजसः॥
en: And many other warriors of immeasurable strength as Sikhandin, Sahadeva, Nakula, his sons, the descendant of Sini and a good many of the Prabhadrakas advancing along with Dhristadyumna in their respective cars looked very grand when they all began to strike Karna with their shafts and many other weapons of different descriptions.

sn: तांस्तत्राधिरथिः संख्ये चेदिपाञ्चालपाण्डवान्। एको बहूनभ्यपतद् गरुत्मान् पन्नगानिव॥
en: But the son of Adhiratha, though singlehanded, fell ferociously upon all those Panchalas, Chedis and Pandavas in the encounter just as Garuda falls upon a number of snakes.

sn: तैः कर्णस्याभवद् युद्धं घोररूपं विशाम्पते। तादृग् याद्दक् पुरा वृत्तं देवानां दानवैः सह॥
en: The battle, O monarch, that was fought between Karna and those warriors, became as fierce as the great battle that, in the days of yore, occurred between the gods and Asuras.

sn: तान् समेतान् महेष्वासाशरवर्षांघवर्षिणः। एको व्यधमदाव्यग्रस्तमांसीव दिवाकरः॥
en: Like unto the rising sun dispelling darkness the single-handed Karna unhesitatingly encountered the united force of all those great warriors ceaselessly showering sharp shafts upon him.

sn: भीमसनस्तु संसक्ते राधेये पाण्डवैः सह। सर्वतोऽभ्यहनत् क्रुद्धो यमदण्डनिभैः शरैः॥ वाह्रीकान् केकयान् मत्स्यान् वासात्यान् मद्रसैन्धवान्। एक: संख्ये महेष्वासो योधयन् बह्वशोभत।
en: While Karna was thus engaged with the Pandavas, Bhimasena, extremely exercised with anger, began to wound the Kurus with his shafts each of which was as sure as the very rod of Yama. That great bowman, struggling alone with all those Balhikas, Kaikeyas, Matsyas, Vasatiyas, Madras and the Saindhavas, looked exceedingly grand.

sn: तत्र मर्मसु भीमेन नाराचैस्ताडिता गजाः॥ प्रपतन्तो हतारोहाः कम्पयन्ति स्म मेदिनाम्।
en: The earth itself began to tremble with the violence of the fall of the huge elephants struck fatally with the awful arrows of Bhimasena in the vital parts of their riders shot dead.

sn: वाजिनश्च हतारोहा: पत्तयश्च गतासवः॥ शेरते युधि निर्भिन्ना वमन्तो रुधिरं बहु।
en: Many horses also, with their riders slain and many of the infantries lay down dead pierced with arrows and vomiting blood and bleeding profusely.

sn: सहस्रशश्च रथिनः पातितः पतितायुधाः॥ ते क्षताः समदृश्यन्त भीमभीता गतासवः।
en: Thousands of car-warriors, deprived of their arms, lay senseless through the fear of Bhima and inany lay dead, their bodies mangled with wounds.

sn: रथिभिः सादिभिः सूतैः पादातैर्वाजिभिर्गजैः॥ भीमसेनशरैश्छिन्नराच्छन्ना वसुधामवत्।
en: Dead bodies of elephants and their drivers, horses and riders, cars and car-warriors and foot soldiers shot dead by Bhimasena, literally covered the battle-field.

sn: तत् स्तम्भितमिवातिष्ठद् भीमसेनभयादितम्॥ दुर्योधन बलं सर्वं निरुत्साहं कृतव्रणम्। निश्चेष्टं तुमुलं दीनं वभौ तस्मिन् महारणे॥
en: The army of Duryodhana, of Duryodhana, O king, melancholy, mainted and grieved through fear of Bhimasena, stood in utter confusion. That poor confounded host stood motionless in the field.

sn: प्रसन्नसलिले काले यथा स्यात् सागरो नृप। तद्वत् तव बलं तद् वै निश्चलं समवस्थितम॥
en: O king, the deep ocean remains quiet in a fair season stood motionless as deep ocean remains clam and quiet in a fair weather season. Your army, in that batile, became poorly and thoroughly insert.

sn: मन्युवीर्यबलोपेतं दर्पात् प्रत्यवरोपितम्। अभवत् तव पुत्रस्य तत् सैन्यं निष्प्रभं तदा॥
en: The army of your son, however powerful and energetic it might have been, lost all its glory and pride at that time.

sn: तद् बलं भरतश्रेष्ठ वध्यमानं परस्परम्। रुधिरौघपरिक्किन्नं रुधिरा, बभूव ह ॥ जगाम भरतेश्रेष्ठ वध्यमानं परस्परम्।
en: That army, O foremost of the Bharata, when fighting with one another looked as if bathed in blood and went on killing one another.

sn: सूतपुत्रो रणे क्रुद्धः पाण्डवानापनीकिनीम्॥ भीमसेनः कुरुश्चापि द्रावयन्तौ विरेजतुः।
en: Suta's son, filled with anger, routed the Pandava army while the enraged Bhimasena routed the Kurus. And both the heroes thus engaged looked exceedingly beautiful.

sn: वर्तमाने तथा रौद्रे संग्रामेऽद्भुतदर्शने॥ निहंत्य पृतनामध्ये संशप्तकगणान् बहून्। अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठो वासुदेवमताब्रवीत्॥
en: In that extremely fierce and awe-inspiring battle, Arjuna, that foremost of victorious heroes, having killed a large number of Samasaptakas in the very heart of their array,

sn: प्रभग्नं बलमेतद्धि योत्स्यमानं जनार्दन। एते द्रवन्ति सगणा: संशप्तकमहारथाः॥ अपारयन्तो मद्वाणान् सिंहशब्दं मृगा इव।
en: This array of these fighting warriors, O Janaradana, has been broken through. These great warriors of the Samasaptakas, unable to withstand my arrows, are running away with their men as a herd of deer at the roar of a lion.

sn: दीर्यते चमहत् सैन्यं सृञ्जयानां महारणे॥ हस्तिकक्षो ह्यसौ कृष्ण केतुः कर्णस्य धीमतः। दृश्यते राजसैन्यस्य मध्ये विचरतो मुदा॥
en: And even the vast force of the Srinjayas appears to give way in this great battle. There in the midst of Yudhishthira's division, the banner, of the highly intelligent Karna, bearing the device of an elephant is seen to move about with great activity.

sn: न च कर्णं रणे शक्ता जेतुमन्ये महारथाः। कर्ण वीर्यवन्तं पराक्रमे॥
en: O Janardana, You are well aware of Karna's energy and prowess. No other warrior of our army is capable of conquering Karna.

sn: जानीते हि भवान् तत्र याहि यतः कर्णो द्रावयत्येष नो बलम्। वर्जयित्वा रणे याहि सूतपुत्रं महारथम्॥ एतन्मे रोचते कृष्ण यथा वा तव रोचते।
en: Pray, proceed there where Karna is crushing down our force. Leaving all others proceed against that mighty car-warrior, the son of Suta, O Krishna, this is my suggestion; but please do what you think proper,

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य गोविन्दः प्रहसन्निव॥ अब्रवीदर्जुनं तूर्ण कौरवाञ्जहि पाण्डव।
en: Hearing these words of his, Govind smiled and addressing Arjuna said-"O son of Pandu, go on killing the Kauravas indiscriminately."

sn: ततस्तव महासैन्यं गोविन्दप्रेरिता हयाः॥ हंसवर्णाः प्रविविशुर्वहन्तः कृष्णपाण्डवौ।
en: Then those swan white horses, driven by Krishna, penetrated into your strong array bearing both Krishna and himself and the son of Pandu.

sn: केशवप्रेरितैरश्वैः श्वेतैः काञ्चनभूषणैः॥ प्रविशद्भिस्तव बलं चतुर्दिशमभिट्टात।
en: And your host gave way on all sides as those two white animals bedecked with golden trappings entered into its midst led by Keshava.

sn: मेघस्तनितनिर्हादः स रथो वानरध्वजः॥ चलत्पताकस्तां सेनां विमानं द्यामिवविशत्।
en: That ape bannered car hoisting its flags in the sky and roaring like thunder-bolt cloud forced its way into your array like a celestial car passing through the welkin.

sn: तौ विदार्य महासेनां प्रविष्टौ केशवार्जुनौ॥ क्रुद्धौ संरम्भरक्ताक्षौ व्यभ्राजेतां महाद्युती।
en: When cutting through the vast army, Keshava and Arjuna entered the arena with their eyes blooded with anger they looked exceedingly splendid and resplendent.

sn: युद्धशौण्डी समाहूतावागतौ तौ रणाध्वरम्॥ यज्वभिर्विधिनाहूतौ मखे देवाविवाश्विनौ।
en: Taking great delight in battle and accepting the challenge of the Kurus when those two heroes came to the field they looked like the w twin gods Ashvinis invoked with proper rites in a sacrifice by the priests.

sn: क्रुद्धौ तौ तु नरव्याघ्रौ वेगवन्तौ बभूवतुः॥ तलशब्देन रुषितौ यथा नागौ महावने।
en: Those two enraged heroes of tigerish fierceness grew extremely violent in their moments like two elephants excited at the claps of hunters in a deep forest.

sn: विगाह्य तु स्थानीकमश्वसंघांश्च फाल्गुनः॥ व्यचरत् पृतनामध्ये पाशहस्त इवान्तकः।
en: Penetrating into the midst of those cars and horses drawn in array Phalguna move about like the destroyer himself armed with his fatal noose.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा युधि विक्रान्तं सेनायां तव भारत॥ संशप्तकगणान् भूयः पुत्रस्ते समचूचुदत्।
en: Beholding him displaying such courage within his own army, O Bharata, your son tried once more to stir up the Samasaptakas against him.

sn: ततो रथसहस्रेण द्विरदानां त्रिभिः शतैः॥ चतुर्दशसहस्रेस्तु तुरगाणां महाहवे। द्वाभ्यां शतसहस्राभ्यं पदातीनां च धन्विनाम्॥ शूराणांबल्धलक्ष्याणां विदितानां समन्ततः। अभ्यवर्तन्त कौन्तेयं छादयन्तो महारथाः॥ शरवर्षेमहाराज सर्वतः पाण्डुनन्दनम्।
en: Thereupon with thousand cars, three hundred elephants, fourteen thousand horses and two hundred thousand valiant footsoldiers, all well practised in aiming and highly skillful in all the ways of war and well armed with bows, the leaders of the Samanaptakas rushed towards the son of Kunti and covered the Pandavas, O king, with showers of shafts from all sides.

sn: स च्छाद्यमानः समरे शरैः परबलार्दनः॥ दर्शयन् रौद्रमात्मानं पाशहस्त इवान्तकः। निघ्नन् संशप्तकान् पार्थः प्रेक्षणीयतरोऽभवत्॥
en: Covered with arrows Partha, that repressor of foes, in fight, looked exceedingly fearful like the destroyer himself with the noose in his hand, but he grew still more fierce and worth looking at when he began to kill the Samasaptakas.

sn: ततो विद्युत्प्रभैर्बाणैः कार्तस्वरविभूषितैः। निरन्तरमिवाकाशमासीच्छन्नं किरीटिना॥
en: Thereupon the sky became enveloped with the arrows mounted with gold and possessed of the lustre of the lightning that were being constantly discharged by Kiriti (Arjuna).

sn: किरीटिभुजनिर्मुक्तैः सम्पतद्भिर्महाशरैः। समाच्छन्नं बभौ सर्वं काद्रवेयैरिव प्रभो॥
en: Indeed those arrows, that were ceaselessly being discharged by Arjuna, falling on all sides looked, O lord, as if so many snakes were lying all around.

sn: रुक्मपुङ्खान् प्रसन्नाग्राञ्छरान् संनतपर्वणः। अवासृजदमेयात्मा दिक्षु सर्वासु पाण्डवः॥
en: The immeasurably energetic son of Pandu sent out his straight and sharp-pointed shafts towards all directions.

sn: मही वियद् दिशः सर्वाः समुद्रा गिरयोऽपि वा। स्फुटन्तीति जना जजुः पार्थस्य तलनिःस्वनात्।। १०५
en: Hearing the terrible sound of Parth's palms people thought that all the oceans, the whole earth, all the ten directions, the ethereal vault were going to burst out.

sn: हत्वा दशसहस्राणि पार्थिवानां महारथः। संशप्तकानां कौन्तेयः प्रत्यक्षं त्वरितोऽभ्ययात्॥
en: Having killed ten thousand of the chiefs, that great car-warrior the son of Kunti proceeded rapidly to the further end of the Samasaptakas array.

sn: प्रत्यक्षं च समासाद्य पार्थः काम्बोजरक्षितम्। प्रममाथ बलं बाणैर्दनवानिव वासवः॥
en: Approaching the wing which was being defended by Kamboja he began to harass the troops by his powerful arrows as Vasava had harassed the Danavas.

sn: प्रचिच्छेदाशु भल्लेन द्विषतामाततायिनाम्। शस्त्रं पाणिं तथा बाहुं तथापि च शिरांस्युत॥
en: With his broad-headed arrows he began to chop off quickly the heads, thighs and arms with weapon in the grasp of his rivals who were desirous of killing him.

sn: अङ्गाङ्गावयवैश्छिन्नायुधास्तेऽपतन भुवि। विष्वग्वाताभिसम्भग्ना बहुशाखा इव द्रुमाः॥
en: Deprived of all the limbs and weapons they began to fall down on earth like large trees of many big boughs hurled down by a hurricane.

sn: हस्त्यश्वरथपत्तीनां वातान् निनन्तमर्जुनम्। सुदक्षिणादवरजः शरवृष्ट्याभ्यवीवृषत्॥
en: The younger brother of Sudakshina, the king of Kamboja started shooting volley of arrows on Arjuna, the great warrior capable of killing numerous cluster of elephants, horses, chariots and infantry soldiers.

sn: तस्यास्यतोऽर्धचन्द्राभ्यां बाहू परिघसंनिभौ। पूर्णचन्द्राभवक्त्रं च क्षेरेणाभ्यहरच्छिरः॥
en: Arjuna then cut-off the two arms of his assailant with a pair of crescent-shaped arrows and then with razor-headed arrow he knocked down his head containing a face as beautiful as the full moon.

sn: स पपात ततो वाहात् सुलोहितपरिस्त्रवः। मनःशिलागिरेः शृङ्गं वज्रेणोवावदारितम्॥
en: His like extinguished, the body bathed in blood fell down from his car like the summit of Manashila mountain clapped down by a thunder-bolt.

sn: सुदक्षिणादवरजं काम्बोजं ददृशुर्हतम्। प्रांशु कमलपत्राक्षमत्यर्थं प्रियदर्शनम्॥ काञ्चनस्तम्भसदृशं भिन्नं हेमगिरिं यथा।
en: When this most beautiful and handsomelooking young man, the younger brother of Sudakshina and chief of the Kambojas whose beautiful and lovely eyes could be compared with the lotus-petals, lay down dead on the ground it appeared as if the summit of the golden Sumeru was tumbled down on earth.

sn: ततोऽभवत् पुनर्युद्धं घोरमत्यर्थमद्भुतम्॥ नानावस्थाश्च योधानां बभूवस्तत्र युद्धयताम्।
en: And the battle, that was fought after this, was exceedingly terrible and awe-inspiring and the fate of each of the fighting combatants changed repeatedly.

sn: एकेषुनिहतैरश्वैः काम्बोजैर्यवनैः शकैः॥ शोणिताक्तैस्तदा रक्तं सर्वमासीद् विशाम्पते।
en: All the heroes of the Kambojas, Yavanas and the Sakas were killed by one arrow each and their bleeding bodies, O king, gave the battle-field the look of a vast expanse of red.

sn: स्थताश्वसूतैश्च हतारोहैश्च वाजिभिः॥ द्विरदैश्च हतारोहमहामात्रैर्हतद्विपैः। अन्योन्येन महाराज कृतो घोरो जनक्षयः॥
en: The car-warriors were deprived of their steeds and drivers, elephants and horses lost their riders; many riders and drivers lost their horses and elephants; and thus fighting with one another, O king, a great loss of lives took place.

sn: तस्मिन् प्रपक्षे पक्षे च निहते सव्यसाचिना। अर्जुनं जयता श्रेष्ठं त्वरितो द्रौणिरभ्ययात्॥ विधुन्वानो महचापं कार्तस्वरविभूषितम्। आददानः शरान् घोरान् स्वरश्मीनिव भास्करः॥११९
en: When the wing and further wing of the Samasaptakas had been thus eradicated by Savyasachin (Arjuna) the son of Drona rapidly proceeded against him. Furnished with many terrible arrows and violently shaking his formidable bow Drona's son appeared in the battle-field as the sun appears in the horizon with his fierce rays.

sn: क्रोधामर्षविवृत्तास्यो लोहिताक्षो बभौ बली। अन्तकाले यथा क्रुद्धो मृत्युः किङ्करदण्डभृत्॥
en: Full of rage and revengeful spirit the mighty warrior, with his mouth wide open and blood red eyes, looked formidable like Death himself with his terrible mace before a dying person.

sn: ततः प्रासृजदुग्राणि शरवर्षाणि संघशः। तैर्विसृष्टैर्महाराज व्यद्रवत पाण्डवी चमूः॥
en: Then he began to shower sharp shafts on the armies of the Pandavas and rout them.

sn: स दृष्टैव तु दासार्ह स्यन्दनस्थं विशाम्पते। पुनः प्रासृजदुग्राणि शरवर्षाणि मारिष॥
en: Again, O king, as soon as he saw the Dasarha on the car he began to discharge his terrible shafts much more quickly.

sn: तैः पतद्भिर्महाराज द्रौणिमुक्तैः समन्ततः। संछादितौ रथस्थौ तावुभौ कृष्णधनंजयौ॥
en: And their dangerous arrows discharged by Drona's son, O king, falling on Krishna and Dhananjaya, entirely enshrouded both of them on their car.

sn: ततः शरशतैस्तीक्षणैरश्वत्थामा प्रतापवान्। निश्चैष्टौ तावुभौ युद्धे चक्रे माघवपाण्डवौ॥
en: And thus the violent Ashvatthama, with hundreds of keen arrows, put both Madhava and Pandu's son into utter confusion.

sn: हाहाकृतमभूत सर्व स्थावरं जङ्गम् तथा। चराचरस्य गोप्तारौ संछादितौ शरैः॥
en: Beholding those two guardians of the world, thus covered with arrows, the creation sent forth piteous cries of woe.

sn: सिद्धचारणसंघाश्च सम्पेतुस्ते समन्ततः। चिन्तयन्तो भवेदद्य लोकानां स्वस्तयपीति च॥
en: There hordes of Siddhas and Charanas poured in form every direction all solicitous of common weal for the day.

sn: न मया तादृशो राजन् दृष्टपूर्वः पराक्रमः। संग्रामे यादृशो द्रौणेः कृष्णौ संचादयिष्यतः॥
en: Never before, O monarch, did I witness such prodigies of valor like those displayed by Drouni when shrouding Krishna and Arjuna in the field.

sn: द्रौणेस्तु धनुषः शब्दमहितत्रासनं रणे। अश्रौषं बहुशो राजन् सिंहस्य निनदो यता॥
en: Often and often did I hear in that battle, O king, the din of Drouni's volleys, thundering roars of lion to the consternation of the enemy.

sn: ज्या चास्य चरतो युद्धे सव्यदक्षिणमस्यतः। विद्युतम्बुदमध्यस्था भ्राजमानेव साभवत्॥
en: Flinging his shots right and left as he moved round the field, the string of his bow shone like flashes of lightning sparkling amidst the cloudy heavens.

sn: स तथा क्षिप्रकारी च दृढहस्तश्च पाण्डवः। प्रमोहं परमं गत्वा प्रेक्ष्य तं द्रोणजं ततः॥ विक्रम विहतं मेन आत्मनः स महायशाः। तस्यास्य समरे राजन् वपुरासीत् सुदुद्देशम्॥
en: Inspite of the dexterity and inflexibility of his hand, the son of Pandu, beholding the son of Drona, at the time, was greatly bewildered. And he (Arjuna) bethought himself of being deprived of his own prowess by that august personage (Ashvatthaman), whose bearing in the field, O king, presented a dazzling sight for human eyes.

sn: द्रौणिपाण्डवयोरेवं वर्तमाने महारणे। वर्धमाने च राजेन्द्र द्रोणपुत्रे महाबले॥ हीयमाने च कौन्तेये कृष्णे रोषः समाविशत्।
en: In that deadly conflict between Drouni and the Pandava, O king of kings Krishna, seeing the powerful son of Drona get the better of the son of Kunti, became highly infuriated.

sn: स रोषान्निःश्वसन् राजन् निर्दहन्निव चक्षुषा॥ द्रौणि ह्यपश्यत् संग्रामे फाल्गुनं च मुहर्मुहुः।
en: With inflamed eyes and swelling breath, frequently he cast his eyes towards. Ashvatthama and Phalguna, devouring them, as it were, with the fury of his fire.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धोऽब्रवीत् कृष्णः पार्थ सप्रणयं तदा॥ अत्यद्भुतमिदं पार्थ तव पश्यामि संयुगे। अतिशेते हि यत्र त्वां द्रोणपुत्रोऽद्य भारत॥
en: The indignant Krishna then addressing Partha in an endearing tone and said-O Partha, what a strange part of, see, you play in the field? O son of Bharata, Drona's son overcoming you today in battle!

sn: कचिद् वीर्यं यथापूर्वं भुजयोर्वा बलं तव। कचित् ते गाण्डिवं हस्ते रथे तिष्ठसि चार्जुन॥
en: Have you the same strength of your arms as you had before? Do you still hold your Gandiva in hand? Are you seated in the warchariot?

sn: कचित् कुशालिनौ बाहू मुष्टिर्वा न व्यशीर्यत। उदीर्यमाणं हि रणे पश्यामि द्रौणिमाहवे॥
en: Has nay thing gone wrong with your arms? Has your fist sustained any injury, or how is it that I see you overwhelmed by Drouni in the field.

sn: गुरुपुत्र इति ह्येनं मानयन् भरतर्षभ। उपेक्षा कुरु मा पार्थ नायं काल उपेक्षितुम्॥
en: O glory of Bharata's race, esteeming your assailant as the son of your preceptor stop not, O Partha, this is not the time for forbearance.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु कृष्णेन गृह्य भल्लांश्चतुर्दश। त्वरमाणस्तवराकाले द्रौणेर्धनुरथाच्छिनत्॥ ध्वजं छत्रं पताकाश्च खङ्ग शक्तिं गदां तथा। जत्रुदेशे च सुभृशं वत्सदन्तैरताडयत्॥
en: Hearing those words Arjuna just on the nick of time seizing fourteen Bhallas (arrows, with crescent-shaped heads) darted them off, piercing right through his weapons, chariot, standard and umbrella and dismantling Ashvatthama of his equipment's, bows, darts and all. He (Arjuna), then assailing him (Ashvatthama) with calf-toothed arrows.

sn: स मूर्छा परमां गत्वा ध्वजयष्टिं समाश्रितः। तं विसंज्ञं महाराज शत्रुणा भृशपीडितम्॥ अपोवाह रणात् सूतो रक्षमाणो धनंजयात्।
en: Inflicted terrible wounds on his shoulderjoints fainting from which he sustained himself with his flag-staff. Seeing him thus stunned with the assaults of his enemy his charioteer, O monarch, for rescuing him from (the army of) Dhananjaya bore him away from the field.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले च विजयः शत्रुतापनः॥ व्यहनत् तावकं सैन्यं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। पश्यतस्तस्य वीरस्य तव पुत्रस्य भारत॥
en: O Bharata, In the meanwhile, that scorcher of enemy, Vijay, before the very eyes of your valiant son slaughtered your army by hundreds and thousands.

sn: एवमेष क्षयो वृत्तस्तावकानां परैः सह। क्रूरो विशसनो घोरो राजन् दुर्मत्रिते तव॥
en: Thus, O monarch, owing to your evil counsels such a ruthless slaughter with cruel onslaught of your champions was brought about as these knights presented arms to your foe.
