sn: संशप्तकांश्च कौन्तेयः कुरूंश्चापि वृकोदरः। वसुषेणश्च पञ्चालान् क्षणेन व्यधमद् रणे॥
en: Arjuna then in the twinkle of an eye beset the Samasaptakas, while Vrikodara attacked the Kurus and Karna attacked the Panchalas.

sn: वर्तमाने तथा रौद्रे राजन् वीरवरक्षये। उत्थितान्यगणेयानि कबन्धानि समन्ततः॥
en: O monarch, as the war raged furiously, destroying the lives of valiant soldiers and presenting a vast scene of carnage, there arose in the field innumerable headless trunks, still retaining vitality.

sn: युधिष्ठिरोऽपि संग्रामे प्रहारर्गाढवेदनः। क्रोशमात्रमपक्रम्य तस्थौ भरतसत्तमः॥
en: O the chief of the Bharata race, king Yudhishthira, sorely distressed with his wounds and writhing in agony, stayed in the time two miles off from the scene of action.

sn: संजय उवाच दुर्योधन कर्णमुपेत्य भरतर्षभ। अब्रवीन्मद्रराजं च तथैवान्यांश्च पार्थिवान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon, O Bharata chief, approaching Karna Duryodhana said to the Madra king as well as to other chiefs (present there).

sn: यदृच्छयैतत् सम्प्राप्तं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्। सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः कर्ण लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम्॥
en: O Karna! This opportunity to fight has automatically come in hands like an opened gate of heaven. Only lucky Kshatriyas can see such opportunity to fight.

sn: सदृशैः क्षत्रियैः शूरैः शूराणां युद्धतां युधि। इष्टं भवति राधेय तदिदं समुपस्थितम्॥
en: If the heroic Kshatriyas fight with their pairs in battle great benefit occurs to them, O son of Radha.

sn: हत्वा च पाण्डवान् युद्धे स्फीतामुर्वीमवात्स्यथ। निहता वा परैयुद्धे वीरलोकमवाप्स्यथ॥
en: Either having slain the Pandavas let them acquire the prosperous kingdom or being slain by the enemies let them repair to the region of heroes.

sn: दुर्योधनस्य तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं क्षत्रियर्षभाः। हृष्टा नादानुदक्रोशन् वादित्राणि च सर्वशः॥
en: Hearing those words of Duryodhana the Kshatriya chiefs shouted aloud and played on their musical instruments.

sn: ततः प्रमुदिते तस्मिन् दुर्योधन बले तदा। हर्षयंस्तावकान् योधान् द्रौणिर्वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon when Duryodhana's army were filled with joy, the son of Drona gladdening all your soldiers said-

sn: प्रत्यक्षं सर्वसैन्यानां भवतां चापि पश्यताम्। न्यस्तशस्त्रौ मम पिता धृष्टद्युम्नेन पातितः॥
en: Before the entire army and before you all, my father, when he had laid aside his arms, was killed by Dhristadyumna.

sn: स तेनाहममर्षेण मित्रार्थे चापि पार्थिवाः। सत्यं वः प्रतिजानामि तद् वाक्यं मे निबोधत॥
en: By that wrath and for the sake of my friend, I tell you, O king, what I promise-

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नमहत्वाहं न विमोक्ष्यामि दंशनम्। अनृतायां प्रतिज्ञायां नाहं स्वर्गमवाप्नुयाम्॥
en: Without slaying Dhristadyumna, I will not lay aside my arms. If this my promise proves futile, I will not go to heaven.

sn: अर्जुनो भीमसेनश्च योधो यो रक्षिता रणे। धृष्टद्युम्नस्य तं संख्ये निहनिष्यामि सायकैः॥
en: Forsooth, I will grind him who will come against me, be he Arjuna, Bhimasena or any body else.

sn: एवमुक्ते ततः सर्वा सहिता भारतीचमूः। अभ्यद्रवत कौन्तेयांस्तथा ते चापि पाण्डवाः॥
en: Thus addressed the entire Bharata army rushed against the sons of Kunti. The Pandavas also (came forward).

sn: स संनिपातो रथयूथपानां बभूव राजन्नतिभीमरूपः। जनक्षयः कालयुगान्तकल्पः प्रावर्तताग्ने कुरसृञ्जयानाम्॥
en: O Bharata king, the encounter of the leading car-warriors was highly wonderful. An onslaught of men like that at the end of a cycle took place before the Kurus and Srinjayas.

sn: ततः प्रवृत्ते युधि सम्प्रहारे भूतानि सर्वाणि सदैवतानि। दिदृक्षमाणानि नरप्रवीरान्॥
en: When that encounter took place many created beings along with the gods and nymphs came there to see the leading heroes.

sn: दिव्यैश्च रत्नैर्विविधैर्नराग्र्यान्। नवाकिरन्नप्सरसः प्रहृष्टाः॥
en: Delightedly the Apsaras showered, on those leading warriors, observant of the duties of their own order, celestial garlands, perfumeries and various jewels.

sn: समीराणस्तांश्च निषेव्य गन्धान् सिषेव सर्वानपि योधमुख्यान्। निषेव्यमाणास्तवनिलेन योधाः परस्परांना धरणी निपेतुः॥
en: The wind used to collect those perfumes and carry it to the great warriors for their pleasure. The warriors so served by wind laid on ground by killing one another.

sn: सा दिव्यमाल्यैरवकीर्यमाणा सुवर्णपुढेश्च शरैर्विचित्रैः। नक्षत्रसंधैरिव चित्रिता द्यौः क्षितिर्बभौ योधवरैर्विचित्रा॥
en: That battle-field covered with divine garlands, excellent arrows having gold studded wings attached and the great warriors fighting there got an excellent look as if it was sky with countless twinkling stars.

sn: र्वादित्रघोषैः समुदीर्यमाणः। ज्योघोषनेमिस्वननदचित्र: समाकुलः सोऽभवत् संप्रहारः॥
en: The appreciation coming down from sky, the sound from musical instruments plied in war, the twang of bows and thrashing sound from wheels of chariots used there made severe noise in the battle-field.

sn: र्वादित्रघोषैः समुदीर्यमाणः। ज्योघोषनेमिस्वननदचित्र: समाकुलः सोऽभवत् संप्रहारः॥
en: The appreciation coming down from sky, the sound from musical instruments plied in war, the twang of bows and thrashing sound from wheels of chariots used there made severe noise in the battle-field.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमेष महानासीत् संग्रामः पृथिवीक्षिताम्। क्रुद्धेऽर्जुने तथा कर्णे भीमसेने च पाण्डवे॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus a great encounter took place amongst all those warriors. Then Arjuna, Bhimasena and Karna were worked up with anger.

sn: द्रोणपुत्रं पराजित्य जित्वा चान्यान् महारथान्। अब्रवीदर्जुनो राजन् वासुदेवमिदं वचः॥
en: Having vanquished the son of Drona and other leading car-warriors Arjuna said to Vasudevaपश्य कृष्ण महाबाहो द्रवन्ती पाण्डवीं

sn: चमूम्॥ कर्ण पश्य च संग्रामे कालयन्तं महारथान्॥
en: See, O Krishna, the Pandava army is flying away. Karna is making a havoc on our great car-warriors.

sn: न च पश्यामि दाशार्ह धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। नापि केतुर्युधा श्रेष्ठ धर्मराजस्य दृश्यते॥
en: O Krishna, I do not see Dharma's son Yudhishthira; nor is his standard visible.

sn: त्रिभागश्चावशिष्टोऽयं दिवसस्य जनार्दन। न च मां धार्तराष्ट्रेषु कचिद युध्यति संयुगे॥
en: O Janardana, the third portion of the day still remains. None amongst the sons of Dhritarashtra comes to fight with me.

sn: तस्मात् त्वं मत्प्रियं कुर्वन् याहि यत्र युधिष्ठिरः। दृष्ट्वा कुशलिनं युद्धे धर्मपुत्रं सहानुजम्॥ पुनर्योद्धास्मि वार्ष्णेय शत्रुभिः सं संयुगे।
en: If you wish to do me a good turn proceed where Yudhishthira is engaged. If I see Dharma's son and his younger brother well, I will fight again with the enemies.

sn: ततः प्रायाद् रथेनाशु बीभत्सोर्वचनाद्धरिः॥ यतो युधिष्ठिरो राजा सृञ्जयाश्च महारथाः।
en: Thereupon at the request of Vibhatsu Hari speedily moved the course of his car where king Yudhishthira and the valiant Srinjayas were fighting to death.

sn: अयुध्यस्तावकैः सार्धं मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्॥ तत: संग्रामेभूमि तां वर्तमाने जनक्षये। अवेक्षमाणो गोविन्दः सव्यसाचिनमब्रवीत्।॥
en: Thereupon, seeing in the battle-field such a slaughter of valiant heroes Govinda said to Savyasachin-

sn: पश्य पार्थ महारौद्रो वर्तते भरतक्षयः। पृथिव्यां क्षत्रियाणां वै दुर्योधन महान्॥
en: See, O Partha, this great on slaught of the Kshatriyas for the sake of Duryodhana.

sn: पश्य भारत चापानि रुक्मपृष्ठानि धन्विनाम्। मृतानामपविद्धानि कलापांश्च महाधनान्॥
en: Look at the gold-backed bows of the Kshatriyas for the sake of Duryodhana.

sn: जातरूपमयैः पुढेः शरांश्चानतपर्वणः। तैलधौतांश्च नाराचान् निर्मुक्तान् पन्नगानिव॥
en: The arrows having bent knots and gold studded wings and Naracha cleaned in oil are appearing as if numerous snakes have come out from their sloughs,

sn: हस्तिदन्तत्सरून् खङ्गान् जातरूपरिष्कृतान्। वर्माणि चापविद्धानि रुक्मगर्भाणि भारत॥
en: O Bharata! gold studded swords with ivory handles and gold studded shields are also thrown carelessly on the ground here.

sn: सुवर्णविकृतान् प्रासाशक्तीः कनकभूषणाः। जाम्बूनमयैः पट्टैर्बद्धाश्च विपुला गदाः॥
en: Look! At these prasa, saktis and heavy gadas trimmed, studded and made of gold so laid-on the ground.

sn: जातरूपमयीश्चर्टीः पट्टिशान् हेमभूषणान्। दण्डैः कनकचित्रैश्च विप्रविद्धान् परश्वधान्॥
en: These Rishtis made of gold, Pattisha trimmed by gold and the axes with gold studded handles all thrown on the ground.

sn: अयःकुन्तांश्च पतितान् मुसलानि गुरूणि च। शतघ्नी: पश्य चित्राश्च विपुलान् परिघांस्तथा॥
en: The iron spears, heavy musala, excellent Shatghnis and huge Parigha scattered to and fro here.

sn: चक्राणि चापविद्धानि तोमरांश्च महारणे। नानाविधानि शस्त्राणि प्रगृह्य जयगृद्धिनः॥ जीवन्त इव दृश्यन्ते गततत्त्वासनस्विनः।
en: Look also at these discuses (cakras) and tomaras used in this great war. The warriors in sheer excitement for victory have lost their lives in course of attack with weapons still in their hands are appear as if still living.

sn: गदाविमथितैर्गात्रैर्मुसलैर्भिन्नमस्तकान्॥ गजवाजिरथक्षुण्णान् पश्य योधान् सहस्रशः।
en: Look that several thousand warriors whose bodies are splitted by hard blows from gadas, their heads cracked and crushed under the hoofs of horses and chariot wheels.

sn: मनुष्यहयनागानां शरशक्तवृष्टिपट्टिशैः॥ परिवैरायसैोरैरयस्कुन्तैः परश्वधैः। शरीरैर्बहुभिश्छिन्नैः शोणितौघपरिप्लुतैः॥ गतासुभिरमित्रघ्न संवृता रणभूमयः।
en: O enemy suppressor! A majority of the men, horses and elephants' bodies are shattered in pieces, soaked in blood, lost of life on account of sharp and hard blows they received from arrows, Shakti, Rishti, Pattisha, iron parigha, iron kunta of huge size and the axes and the battle-field is seen covered by these lifeless bodies.

sn: बाहुभिश्चन्दनादिग्धैः साङ्गदैर्हेमभूषितैः॥ सतलवैः सकेयूरै ति भारत मेदिना।
en: O Bharata! the battle-field is getting an excellent grandeur in presence of the cut-off arms of the warriors as these are smeared with sandal, decorated by Angadas and Keyuras, trimmed by gold and other ornaments will fine gloves.

sn: साङ्गुलित्रैर्भुजायैश्च विप्रविरिलंकृतैः॥ हस्तिहस्तोपमैश्छिन्नरूरुभिश्च तरस्विनाम्। बद्धचूडामणिवरैः शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः॥ पतितैर्ऋषभाक्षाणां विराजति वसुंधरा।
en: The arms ornamented with gloves of the chivalrous warriors having huge eyes as that of an ox are cut-off and fell down on the ground. The sturdy thighs/legs like that of elephants' trunk are fell splitted and their heads holding Cudamani and car-rings are also on ground separated from the trunk. All these have given an excellent look to the battle-field.

sn: कबन्धैः शोणितादिग्धैश्छिन्नगात्रशिरोधरैः॥ भूर्भाति भरतश्रेष्ठ शान्तार्चिभिरिवाग्निभिः।
en: O Bharata! the battle-field covered by the trunks of human bodies without head and different organs cut-off (viz. without other organs), appearing red on account of soaked in blood, appears as if embers without flames are scattered everywhere.

sn: रथांश्च बहुधा भग्नान् हेमकिङ्किणिनः शुभान्॥ वाजिनश्च हतान् पश्य निष्कीर्णान्त्राशराहतान्।
en: Look at the beautiful chariots splitted here in pieces in which tiny bells made of gold are fixed. The horses injured by arrows are fell dead there and their intestines have come out from belly.

sn: अनुकर्षानुपासंगान् पताका विविधध्वजान्॥ रथिनां च महाशङ्खान् पाण्डुरांश्च प्रकीर्णकान्।
en: There are scattered Anukarsha, Upasanga, Pataka, different type flags and huge size white conch of the charioteer-riders (Rathis).

sn: निरस्तजिह्वान् मातङ्गासयानान् पर्वतोपमान्॥ वैजयन्तीविचित्राश्च हतांश गजवाजिनः।
en: Numerous mountain like elephants with their tongues came out has slept for ever on the ground. The excellent Vaijayanti flags splitted and the horses as also elephants have been killed.

sn: वारणानां परिस्तोमांस्तथैवाजिनकम्बलान्॥ विपाटितविचित्रांश्च रूप्यचित्रान् कुथाङ्कुशान्। भिन्नाश्च बहुधा घण्टा महद्भिः पतितैर्गजैः॥
en: The excellent seats on elephants' back, the stag hide and blankets have been fell down in pieces (rugs). The picturised bed with the silver fibres, goad and a number of gongs splitted in pieces have fallen on earth with those huge elephants.

sn: वैदूर्यदण्डांश्च पतिताङ्कुशान भुषि। बद्धाः सादिभुजाग्रेषु सुवर्णविकृताः कशाः॥
en: A number of fantastic goads with handles made of Vaiduryamani have fallen on the ground. A number of whips made of gold are yet in the cut-off arms of the riders.

sn: विचित्रमणिचित्रांश्च जातरूपपरिष्कृतान्। अश्वास्तरपरिस्तोमान् राङ्कवान् पतितान् भुवि॥
en: A number of riding-seats gem-studded, trimmed by gold fibres, made of Ranka stag's hide are now on the ground.

sn: चूडामणीन् नरेन्द्राणां विचित्राः काञ्चनस्त्रजः। छत्राणि चापविद्धानि चामरव्यजनानि च॥
en: The gem-studded of kings, excellent garlands, umbrellas, chanvara and vyajana all thrown on the ground.

sn: चन्द्रनक्षत्रभासैश्च वदनैश्चारुकुण्डलैः। क्लृप्तश्मश्रुभिरत्यर्थ वीराणां समलंकृतैः॥ वदनैः पश्य संछन्नां महीं शोणितकर्दमाम्।
en: Look at the faces with beard and moustache, ornamented varied ways, gracious with ear-rings shining like and constellations now covering the battle-field and see that the mud of blood is freezed on them.

sn: सजीवांश्चापरान् पश्य कूजमानान् समन्ततः॥ उपास्यमानान् बहुशो न्यस्तशस्त्रैर्विशाम्पते। ज्ञातिभिः सहितांस्तत्र रोदमानैर्मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: O Arjuna, look at those other warriors. Still living but severely injured and yelling in pain all around. Their family members in crowd have seated near them, the have dropped their arms down and weeping frequently. crowns moon

sn: व्युतक्रान्तानपरान् योधांश्छादयित्वा तरस्विनः। पुनर्युद्धाय गच्छन्ति जयगृद्धाःप्रमन्यवः॥
en: The warriors now succumbed to injuries are being covered by the sheets of clothes and the warriors in their sheer excitement for victory are again marching ahead very fast to attack again on the enemy. They are filled with anger.

sn: अपरे तत्र तत्रैव परिधावन्ति मानवः। ज्ञातिभि:पतितैः शूरैर्याच्यमानास्ततोदकम्॥
en: Numerous other soldiers, running to and fro in search of water for their chivalrous family members now fell down on battled field due to injuries when they have asked for water.

sn: जलार्थं च गताः केचिन्निष्प्राण बहवोऽर्जुन। संनिवृत्ताश्च ते शूरास्तान् वै दृष्ट्वा विचेतसः॥ जलं त्यक्त्वा प्रधावन्ति क्रोशमानाः परस्परम्।
en: O Arjuna! A number of warriors went for fetching water for their relatives injured in the battle-field but but in the meantime, they succumbed to injuries. The warriors when returned with water and saw them dead, threw water pots on ground and rushing here and there in sheer grief and wailing bitterly for them.

sn: जलं पीत्वा मृतान् पश्य पिबतोऽन्यांश्च मारिष॥ परित्यज्य प्रियानन्ये बान्धवान् बान्धवप्रियाः। व्युत्क्रान्ता:समदृश्यन्त तत्र तत्र महारणे॥
en: O the great warrior Arjuna! Look at a few people who have dead after sipping few drops of water. A number of soldiers dear to their kith and kins are seen dead hither and thither in that great war leaving behind them wailing.

sn: तथापरान् नरश्रेष्ठ संदष्टौष्ठपुटान् पुनः। भृकुटीकुटिलैर्वक्त्रैः प्रेक्षमाणान् समन्ततः॥
en: O majesty! Look at the other warriors staring all around with chewing their lips within teeth and brows cured on their faces.

sn: एवं बुवंस्तदा कृष्णो ययौ यत्रयुधिष्ठिरः। अर्जुनश्चापि नृपतेदर्शनार्थं महारणे॥
en: God Sri Krishna and Arjuna moved towards the place where Yudhishthira was seated concomitant to chanting these matters as they were tempted to see the king there.

sn: याहि याहिति गोविन्दं मुहुर्मुहुरचोदयत्। तां युद्धभूमिं पार्थस्य दर्शयित्वा च माधवः॥ त्वरमाणस्ततः कृष्णः पार्थमाह शनैरिदम्। पश्य पाण्डव राजानमुपयातांश्च पार्थिवान्॥
en: Arjuna frequently was saying god Krishna to march ahead. God Krishna proceeded forward by duly introducing Arjuna with the battle-field in haste. He said to Arjuna in a slow voice-O son of Pandu! See that a number of kings have already accessed to the king.

sn: कर्ण पश्य महारङ्गे ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्। असौ भीमो महेष्वासः सनिवृत्तो रणं प्रति॥
en: Look, Karna is illuminating like a fire blazed on the great stage of the war and the great warrior Bhimasena has returned to the battle-field.

sn: तमेते विनिवर्तन्ते धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः। पाञ्चालसृञ्जयानां च पाण्डवानां च ये मुखम्॥
en: The Panchalas, Srinjayas and the eminent warriors of Pandavas including Dhrishtdyumna etc. are also returning for battle in company of Bhimasena.

sn: निवृत्तैश्च पुनः पार्थेर्भग्नं शत्रुबलं महत्। कौरवान् द्रवतो ह्येष कर्णो रोधयतेऽर्जुन॥
en: O Arjuna! See there, the Pandava warriors have loosened the steps of the huge army of enemies. This This Karna is preventing the Kauravas' warriors departing away from the battle-field.

sn: अन्तकप्रतिमो वेगे शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमः। असौ गच्छति कौरव्य द्रौणिः शस्त्रभूतां वरः॥
en: O son of Kuru! The best weaponist Ashvatthama is also marching towards them. He is forceful as Yamaraja and valorous as Indra, the king of gods.

sn: तमेव पुदुतं संख्ये धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः। अनुप्रयाति संग्रामे हतान् पश्य चसृञ्जयान्॥
en: The great chariot holder (Maharathi) Dhrishtadyumna is pursuing Ashvatthama who himself is also marching forward in battlefield. Look there! A number of Srinjaya warriors have been killed in the war.

sn: सर्वमाह सुदुर्धर्षो वासुदेवः किरीटिने। ततो राजन् महाघोरः प्रादुरासीन्महारणः॥
en: O king! God Krishna, the warrior very tough to conquer told Arjuna, the crown holder Arjuna all these things. There began then fierce battle among the warriors.

sn: सिंहनादरवाश्चैव प्रादुरासन् समागमे। उभयोः सेनयो राजन् मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्॥
en: O king! The battle thereafter ensued with a resolution to leave the field only on death in both armies and the warriors began challenging to each other in a loud voice.

sn: एवमेष क्षयो वृत्तः पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपते। तावकानां परेषांच राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव॥
en: Thus on account of your evil advice that terrible onslaught of your soldiers and enemies took place.

sn: संजय उवाच ततः पुनः समाजग्मुरभीताः कुरुसृञ्जयाः। युधिष्ठिरमुखाः पार्थाः सूतपुत्रमुखा वयम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then again the Kurus and Srinjayas undauntedly encountered one another. The sons of Pritha were headed by Yudhishthira and our army was headed by the charioteer's son.

sn: ततः प्रववृते भीमः संग्रामो लोमहर्षणः। कर्णस्य पाण्डवानां च यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनः॥
en: Then took place a dreadful and hair-stirring battle between Karna and the sons of Pandu which increased the territory of Yama.

sn: तस्मिन् प्रवृत्ते संग्रामे तुमुले शोणितोदके। संशप्तकेषु शूरेषु किंचिच्छिष्टेषु भारत॥ धृष्टद्युम्नो महाराज सहित: सर्वराजभिः । कर्णमेवभिदुद्राव पाण्डवाश्च महारथाः॥
en: After that dreadful battle, producing pools of blood, had taken place and when only a few of the brave Samsaptakas remained alive, Dhristadyumna, with all the kings and the mighty car-warrior Pandavas, rushed towards Karna.

sn: आगच्छमानास्तान् संख्ये प्रहृष्टान् विजयैषिणः। दधारैको रणे कर्णो जलौघानिव पर्वतः॥
en: As a mountain holds water so Karna alone received in battle those warriors filed with joy and longing for victory.

sn: समासाद्य तु ते कर्ण व्यशीर्यन्त महारथाः। यथाचलं समासाद्य वार्योधाः सर्वतोदिशम्॥
en: Encountering Karna those great carwarriors were scattered (by him) as a collection of water is dispersed on all sides while dashing against a huge mountain.

sn: तयोरासीन्महाराज संग्रामो लोमहर्षणः। धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु राधेयं शरेणान्तपर्वणा॥ ताडयामास समरे तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्।
en: O great king, then took place a hair stirring encounter between them. With arrows Dhristadyumna struck the son of Radha exclaiming-"Wait! Wait!”

sn: विजयं च धनुः श्रेष्ठं विधुन्वानो महारथः॥ पार्षतस्य धनुश्छित्त्वा शरांश्चाविषोपमान्। ताडयामास संक्रुद्धः पार्षतं नवभिः शरैः॥
en: Boiling with rage the great car-warrior Karna shook the best of his bows, Vijaya. Then cutting off his bow and arrows like unto deadly serpents he struck Dhristadyumna with nine shafts.

sn: ते वर्म हेमविकृतं भित्त्वा तस्य महात्मनः। शोणिताक्ता व्यराजन्त शक्रगोपा इवानघ॥
en: Cutting through the golden armour of that high-souled hero they were covered with blood and looked like so many lady birds.

sn: तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः। अथान्यद् धनुरादाय शरांश्चासीविषोपमान्॥ कर्णं विव्याध सप्तत्या शरैः संनतपर्वभिः।
en: Then throwing off his broken bow the great car-warrior Dhrishtadyumna took up a fresh one and shafts resembling venomous snakes and struck Karna with seventy arrows.

sn: तथैव राजन् कर्णोऽपि पार्षतं शत्रुतापनम्॥ छादयामास समरे शरैराशीविषोपमैः। द्रोणशत्रुर्महेष्वासो विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Likewise Karna too covered Prishata's son, the scorcher of his enemies with arrows resembling deadly deadly serpents. The great bowman, the enemy of Drona, struck (Karna) with sharpened arrows.

sn: तस्य कर्णो महाराज खरं कनकभूषणम्। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो मृत्युदण्डमिवापरम्॥
en: Karna discharged at him in anger a golden arrow like the very rod of Death.

sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा घोररूपं विशाम्पते। चिच्छेद शतधा राजशैनेयः कृतहस्तवत्॥
en: O king, the descendant of Sini, like an expert, sundered into seven pieces that dreadful arrow which was about to fall on him.

sn: दृष्ट्वा विनिहतं बाणं शरैः कर्णो विशाम्पते। सात्यकिं शरवर्षेण समन्तान् पर्यवारयत्॥
en: Seeing that arrow broken with his shafts, Karna, O king, covered Satyaki completely with a downpour of arrows.

sn: विव्याध चैनं समरे नाराचैस्तत्र सप्तभिः। तंप्रत्यविध्यच्छैनेयः शरैर्हेमपरिष्कृतैः॥
en: He pierced him with seven arrows. The grandson of Sini, in return, struck him with golden-feathered arrows.

sn: ततो युद्धं महाराज चक्षुःश्रोत्रभयानकम्। आसीद् घोरं च चित्रं च प्रेक्षणीयं समन्ततः॥
en: Then there took place an encounter wonderful and terrible striking terror to ears and eyes.

sn: सर्वेषां तत्र भूतानां लोमहर्षोऽभ्य तद् दृष्ट्वा समरे कर्म कर्णशैनेययोर्नृप।॥
en: Hairs on the body of all creatures present there stood erect on beholding in that battle the wonderful feats of Karna and of the grandson of Sini.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे द्रौणिरभ्ययात् सुमहाबलम्। पार्षतं शत्रुदमनं शत्रुवीर्यसुनाशनम्॥
en: In the meantime the highly powerful son of Drona approached Parshata, the subduer of his enemies and the destroyer of their prowess.

sn: अभ्यभाषतं संक्रुद्धो द्रौणि परपुरंजयः। तिष्ठ तिष्ठाय ब्रह्मघ्न न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यसे।॥
en: Drouni, the victor of hostile cities, said to him, in anger, "Wait, wait! O slayer of Brahmanas, you will not escape me today with your life.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा सुभृशं वीरं शीघ्रकृन्निशितैः शरैः। पार्षतं छादयामास घोररूपैः सुतेजनैः॥ यतमानं परं शक्तया यतमानो महारथः।
en: Saying this he covered the great hero, Parshata, with dreadful, dreadful, sharpened and powerful arrows although that car-warrior tried his level best to thwart them.

sn: यथा हि समरे द्रोणः पार्षतं वीक्ष्य मारिष।॥ तथा द्रौणिं रणे दृष्ट्वा पार्षतः परवीरहा। नातिहष्टमना भूत्वा मन्यते मृत्युमात्मनः॥
en: As Drona, while he was alive, became dispirited on seeing the son of Prishata and took him for his death, so the son of Prishata, on seeing Drona's son in battle, regarded him as his death.

sn: स ज्ञात्वा समरेऽऽत्मानं शस्त्रेणावध्यमेव तु। जवेनाभ्याययौ द्रौणि कालः कालमिव क्षयेया॥
en: They immediately marched forward and accessed to Ashvatthama in battle-field considering themselves undefeated by the weapons and it appeared as if the god of death has attacked on god of death (time) at the time of great devastation (Maha Pralaya).

sn: द्रौणिस्तु दृष्ट्वा राजेन्द्र धृष्टद्युम्नमवस्थितम्। क्रोधेन निःश्वसन् वीरः पार्षतं समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Seeing Dhristadyumna stand firm before him the heroic son of Drona, sighing in anger, rushed towards Parshata.

sn: तावन्योन्यं तु दृष्टैव संरम्भं जग्मतुः परम्। अथाब्रवीन्महाराज द्रोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥ धृष्टद्युम्नं समीपस्थं त्वरमाणो विशाम्पते।
en: O king, both are very angry to see each other. Then, O king, the powerful son of Drona quickly said to Dhristadyumna who stood before him.

sn: पाञ्चालापसदाद्य त्वां प्रेषयिष्यामि मृत्यवे॥ पापं हि यत् त्वया कर्म नता द्रोणंपुरा कृतम्। अद्यं त्वां तप्स्यते तद् वै यथा न कुशल तथा॥ अरक्ष्यमाणः पार्थेन यदि तिष्ठसि संयुगे। नापक्रामसि वा मूढ सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: O wretch of a Panchala, I will dispatch you today to the abode of Death. Verily you committed a great sin by killing Drona before. You will meet with an evil turn in extenuation of that iniquity if you stand in battle without being protected by Partha or if you do not beat a retreat. O fool, I tell you the truth.

sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच धृष्टद्युम्नः प्रतापवान्। प्रतिवाक्यं स एवासिर्मामको दास्यते तव॥ तेनैव ते पितुर्दत्तं यतमानस्य संयुगे।
en: Thus addressed the powerful Dhristadyumna replied-What, I said to your father, while trying his best in battle, will serve as a reply to your words.

sn: यदि तावन्मया द्रोणो निहतो ब्राह्मणब्रुवः॥ त्वामिदानीं कथं युद्धे न हनिष्यामि विक्रमात्।
en: If Drona, who was a Brahmana in name, could have been killed by me, why should I not, by my power, kill you today in battle.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज सेनापतिरमर्षणः॥ निशितेनातिबाणेन द्रौणिहं विव्याध पार्षतः।
en: Having said this, O king, the revengeful commander (of Pandava's army) Parshata struck Drona's son with sharpened arrows.

sn: ततो द्रौणिः संसंक्रुद्धः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ आच्छादयद् दिशो राजन् धृष्टद्युम्नस्य संयुगे।
en: Thereupon, worked up with anger Drona's son, O king, covered all sides of Dhristadyumna with arrows.

sn: नैवान्तरिक्षं न दिशो नापि योधाः समन्ततः॥ दृश्यन्ते वै महाराज शरैश्छन्नाः सहस्रशः।
en: Covered with thousands of shafts neither the sky, nor the quarters, nor the warriors around could be seen.

sn: तथैव पार्षतो राजन् द्रौणिमाहवशोभिनम्॥ शरैः संछादयामास सूतपुत्रस्य पश्यतः।
en: Before the very eyes of the charioteer's son, O king, Parshata covered Drona's son, the ornament of the battle field, with arrows.

sn: राधेयोऽपि महाराज पञ्चालान् सह पाण्डवैः॥ द्रौपदेयान् युधामन्यु सात्यकिं च महारथम्। एकः संवारयामास प्रेक्षणीयः समन्ततः॥
en: But the son of Radha alone, O king, visible on every side, withstood the Panchalas, Pandavas, the sons of Draupadi, Yudhamanyu and the great car-warrior Satyaki.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु समरे द्रौणिश्चिच्छेद कार्मुकम्। तदपास्य धनुौणिरन्यदादाय कार्मुकम्॥ वेगवान् समरे घोरे शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान्। स पार्षतस्य राजेन्द्र धनुः शक्तिं गदां ध्वजम्॥ हयान् सूतं रथं चैव निमेषाद् व्यधमच्छरैः।
en: Dhristadyumna, again in battle, cut-off the dreadful bow of Drona's son and his arrows resembling venomous serpents. He, again, O king, in a moment struck with arrows Parshata's bow, Sakti, club, standard, horses, charioteer and car,

sn: सच्छिन्नधन्वा विरतो हताश्वो हतसारथिः॥ खङ्गमादत्त विपुलं शतचन्द्रं च भानुमत्।
en: Having his bow and car broken and horses and charioteer slain, he took up a huge sword shining like a hundred moon.

sn: द्रौणिस्तदपि राजेन्द्र भल्लैः क्षिप्रं महारथः॥ चिच्छेद समरे वीरः क्षिप्रहस्तो दृढायुधः। रथादनवरूढस्य तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: O king, the great car-warrior, the heroic son of Drona, displaying light handedness and holding firm his weapon, quickly cut-off in battle with Bhallas, that weapon of his, before he could come down from the car. It was indeed wonderful.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं हि विरथं हताश्वं छिन्नकार्मुकम्। शरैश्च बहुधा विद्धमस्त्रैश्च शकलीकृतम्॥ नाशकद् भरतश्रेष्ठ यतमानो महारथः।
en: O foremost of Bharatas, that great carwarrior, although striving hard, could not kill Dhristadyumna, who had his bow and car broken and horses slain and was wounded with various arrows.

sn: तस्यान्तमिषुभी राजन् यदा द्रौणिर्न जग्मिरान्॥ अथ त्यक्त्वा धनुर्वीरः पार्षतं त्वरितोऽन्वगात्।
en: O king, when the son of Drona could not kill him with arrows, that hero, laying aside his bow, quickly followed Parshata.

sn: आसीदाल्पवतो वेदस्तस्य राजन् महात्मनः॥ गरुडस्येव पततो जिघृक्षोः पन्नगोत्तमम्।
en: The motion of that high-souled one as he rushed on resembled that of Garuda, swooping down for catching a snake.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु माधवोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत्॥ पश्य पार्थ यथा द्रौणिः पार्षतस्य वधं प्रति। यत्नं करोति विपुलं हन्याचैनं न संशयः॥
en: In the interval Madhava said to Arjuna-"See, O Partha, how Drona's son is proceeding quickly towards Parshata's car. Forsooth, he will kill the prince. There is no doubt.

sn: तं मोचय महाबाहो पार्षतं शत्रुकर्शन। द्रौणेरास्यमनुप्राप्तं मृत्योरास्यगतं यथा॥
en: O you of large arms, O subduer of enemies, rescue Prishata's son who is near the mouth of Drona's son as if he is within the jaws of Death."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज वासुदेवः प्रतापवान्। प्रेषयत् तुरगांस्तत्र यत्र द्रौणिर्व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Having said this, O king, the powerful son of Vasudeva drove the horses where Drona's son was staying

sn: ते हयाश्चन्द्रसंकाशाः केशवेन प्रचोदिताः। आपिबन्त इव व्योम जग्मुद्रौणिरथं प्रति॥
en: Urged on by the Keshava those horses, effulgent like the moon, ran towards the car of Drona's son as if devouring the very sky.

sn: दृष्ट्वाऽऽयातौ महावीर्याबुभौ कृष्णधनंजयौ। धृष्टद्युम्नवधे यत्रं चक्रे राजन् महाबलः॥
en: Seeing those two mighty heroes approach him, Ashvatthama set forth his exertions for killing Dhristadyumna soon.

sn: विकृष्यमाणं दृष्टैव दृष्टद्युम्नं नरेश्वर। शरांश्चिक्षेप वै पार्थो द्रौणि प्रति महाबलः॥
en: O king, seeing Dhristadyumna dragged by his enemy, the powerful son of Pritha discharged many arrows at the son of Drona.

sn: ते शरा हेमविकृता गाण्डीवप्रेषिता भृशम्। द्रौणिमासाद्य विविशुर्वल्मीकमिव फन्नगाः॥
en: Those golden shafts, shot off his Gandiva, approached the son of Drona and wounded him deep like serpents entering into an ant hill.

sn: स विद्धस्तैः शरैधीरैर्दोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। उत्सृज्य समरे राजन् पाञ्चाल्यममितौजसम्॥
en: Thus struck with dreadful shafts the powerful son of Drona left off the highly energetic Panchala Prince.

sn: रथामारुरुहे वीरो धनंजयशरार्दितः। प्रगृह्य च धनुः श्रेष्ठ पार्थ विव्याध सायकैः॥
en: Thus wounded by Dhananjaya with arrows the hero got on his chariot. And taking up his bow he began to strike Partha with innumerabie arrows.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरः सहदेवो जनाधिप। अपोवाह रथेनाजौ पार्षतं शत्रुतापनम्॥
en: In the interval O king, the heroic Sahadeva carried away on his chariot Parshata the scorcher of his enemies.

sn: अर्जुनोऽपि महाराज द्रौणिं विव्याध पत्रिभिः: तं द्रोणपुत्रः संक्रुद्धो बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्॥
en: Arjuna in return struck Drona's son with Winged arrows. Worked up Drona's son struck him on the arms and the chest.

sn: क्रोधितस्यु रणे पार्थो नाराचं कालसम्मितम्। द्रोणपुत्राय चिक्षेप कालदण्डमिवापरम्॥
en: with anger Filled with anger Partha discharged in that battle at Drona's son a Naracha like unto the very rod of Death.

sn: ब्राह्मणस्यांसदेशे स निपपात महाद्युतिः। स विह्वलो महाराज शरवेगेन संयुगे॥ निषसाद रथोपस्थे वैकुव्यं च परं ययौ।
en: O king, That highly effulgent arrow fell on Brahmana's shoulder, he was stupefied in the battle with the force of that arrow. He sat down exhausted on the car.

sn: ततः कर्णो महाराज व्याक्षिपद् विजयं धनुः॥ अर्जुनं समरे क्रुद्धः प्रेक्षमाणो मुहुमुर्हः। द्वैरथं चापि पार्थेन कामयानो महारणे॥
en: Then, O king, Karna took up his bow, Vijaya and filled with anger he again and again cast his looks on Arjuna desiring for a duel with him.

sn: विह्वलं तं तु वीक्ष्याथ द्रोणपुत्रं च सारथिः। अपोवाह रथेनाजौ त्वरमाणो रणाजिरात्॥
en: Seeing Drona's son senseless his charioteer quickly took him away on his car from the battle-field.

sn: अथोत्क्रुष्टं महाराज पञ्चालैर्जितकाशिभिः। मोक्षितं पार्षतं दृष्ट्वा द्रोणपुत्रं च पीडितम्॥
en: Seeing Prishata's son released and Drona's son wounded, the Panchalas, O king, jubilant over the victory, sent up loud war-cries.

sn: वादित्राणि च दिव्यानि प्रावाद्यन्त सहस्रशः। सिंहनादांश्च चक्रुस्ते दृष्ट्वा संख्ये तदद्भुतम्॥
en: Thousands of musical instruments of swell tune were struck. Seeing those wonderful feats the heroes sent up leonine shouts.

sn: एवं कृत्वाब्रवीत् पार्थो वासुदेव धनंजयः। याहि संशप्तकान् कृष्ण कार्यमेतत् परं मम॥
en: Subsequent to exhibit such valour, Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti said to Sri Krishna-"Sri Krishna! Move now towards Samsaptakas as it is my prime target this time.

sn: ततः प्रयातो दाशार्हः श्रुत्वा पाण्डवभाषितम्। रथेनातिपताकेन मनोमारुतरंहसा॥
en: Hearing those words of Arjuna Krishna drove his car adorned with many banners and fleet like the wind or the mind. Hearing those words of Arjuna Krishna drove his car adorned with many banners and fleet like the wind or the mind.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: संजय उवाच एतस्मिन्नन्तरे कृष्णः पार्थ वचनमब्रवीत्। दर्शयन्निव कौन्तेयं धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Sanjaya said In the meantime pointing out the righteous king Yudhishthira to Parthia, the son of Kunti, Krishna said-

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एष पाण्डव ते भ्राता धार्तराष्टैर्महाबलेः। जिघांसुभिर्महेष्वासैर्वृतं पार्थोऽनुसार्यते॥
en: Behold, O son of Pandu, your brother Yudhishthira pursued by the highly powerful sons of Dhritarashtra, all great bowmen desirous of killing him.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तं चानुयान्ति संरब्धा पञ्चाला युद्धदुर्मदाः। युधिष्ठिरं महात्मानं परीप्सन्तो महाबलाः॥
en: The powerful Panchalas, whom it is difficult to vanquish, are running after the great Yudhishthira for rescuing him.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एष दुर्योधनः पार्थ रथानीकेन दंशितः। राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य राजानमनुधावति॥ जिघांसु पुरुषव्याघ्र भ्रातृभिः सहितो बली। आशीविषसमस्पशैः सर्वयुद्धविशारदैः॥
en: Accoutred in coat of mail and accompanied by a large army Duryodhana, the king of the whole world, is pursuing the Pandava king, with a view to kill him, O foremost of men, assisted by his brothers, all expert in fighting whose very touch is like the deadly venom of serpents.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एते जिघृक्षवो यान्ति द्विपाश्वरथपत्तयः। युधिष्ठिरं धार्तराष्ट्रा नरोत्तममिवार्थिनः॥
en: Your army, riding on elephants, horses and cars and proceeding on foot are going to kill a Yudhishthira like poor men for possessing a costly gem.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पश्य सात्वत भीमाभ्यां निरुद्धाधिष्ठिताः पुनः। जिहीर्षवोऽमृतं दैत्याः शक्रग्निभ्यामिवासकृत्॥
en: See, obstructed by Satvata and Bhima, they have become motionless like unto the Dailyas desirous of pilfering ambrosia stupefied by Sakra and Agni.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एते बहुत्वात्त्वारिताः पुनर्गच्छन्ति पाण्डवम्। समुद्रमिव वार्योधाः प्रावृट्काले महारथाः॥
en: On account of their numerical vastness (the Kuru) car-warriors are proceeding quickly towards Yudhishthira like unto a collection of water running towards the ocean during the rainy season.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: नदन्तः सिंहनादांश्च धमन्तश्चापि वारिजान्। बलवन्तो महेष्वासा विधुन्वन्तो धनूंषि च॥
en: Blowing their conch-shell and shaking their bows those powerful bow-men are sending up leonine shouts.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: मृत्योर्मुखगतं मन्ये कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। हुतमग्नौ च कौन्तेयं दुर्योधनवशं गतम्॥
en: I regard Kunti's son Yudhishthira who has been brought under the influence of Duryodhana as within the mouth of Death or like an oblation of ghee in fire.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: यथाविधमनीकं तु धार्तराष्ट्रस्य पाण्डव। नास्य शक्रोऽपिमुच्येत सम्प्रातो बाणगोचरम्॥
en: Duryodhana's army is properly armed. Coming within the range of their arrows even Sakra cannot escape.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: दुर्योधनस्य वीरस्य शरौघाशीघ्रमस्यतः। संक्रुद्धस्यान्तकस्येव को वेगं संसहेद् रणे॥
en: Who in battle can bear the force of arrows shot by Duryodhana, who, when worked ups with anger, resembles Death himself.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: दुर्योधनस्य वीरस्य द्रौणे: शारद्वतस्य च। कर्णस्य चेषुवेगो वै पर्वतानपि शातयेत्॥
en: The force of Duryodhana's arrows, or of Drona's son's, or Kripa's, or Karna's, can shatter even the very mountains. was

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: कर्णेन च कृतो राजा विमुखः शत्रुतापनः। बलवाँल्लघुहस्तश्च कृती युद्धविशारदः॥
en: The powerful light-handed and successful king Yudhishthira, expert in fighting and the scorcher of his enemies, was compelled by Karna to retreat from the battle-field.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: राधेयः पाण्डवश्रेष्ठं शक्तः पीडयितुं रणे। सहितो धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रैः शूरैर्महाबलेः॥
en: Accompanied by the highly powerful and heroic sons of Dhritarashtra the son of Radha is capable of afflicting the Pandava chief in battle.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तस्यैभिर्युध्यमानस्य संग्रामे संयतात्मनः। अन्यैरपि च पार्थस्य कृतं कर्म महारथैः॥
en: While the self-controlled Partha fighting with them, other great car-warriors brought about his discomfiture.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: उपवासकृशो राजा भृशं भरतसत्तमः। ब्राह्मे बले स्थितो ह्येष न क्षात्रे हि बले विभुः॥
en: O foremost of Bharatas, the king is great emaciated with fasts. He is gifted with the force of a Brahmana, but he is not endued with Kshatriya prowess.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: कर्णेन चाभियुक्तोऽयं भूपतिः शत्रुतापनः। शंशयं समनुप्राप्तः पाण्डवो वै युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Afflicted by Karna the king Yudhishthira, the son Pandu, has been greatly imperiled.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न जीवित महाराजो मन्ये पार्थ युधिष्ठिरः। यद् भीमसेनः सहते सिंहनादममर्षणः॥ नदतां धार्तराष्ट्राणां पुन: सिहनादममर्षणः। धमता च महाशङ्खान् संग्रामे जितकाशिनाम्॥
en: I think, O Partha, the king, Yudhishthira has fallen, since the wrathful Bhimasena, the slayer of his enemies, is calmy bearing the leonine shouts repeatedly sent up by Dhritarashtra's sons desirous of achieving victory and blowing their conch-shells.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: युधिष्ठिरं पाण्डवेयं हतेति भरतर्षभ। शंचोदयत्यसौ कर्णो धार्तराष्ट्रान् महाबलान्॥ स्थूणाकर्णेन्द्रजालेन पार्थ पाशुपतेन च। प्रच्छादयन्ति राजानं शस्त्रजालैर्महारथाः॥
en: Indeed, O foremost of men, Pandu's son Yudhishthira is slain. See Karna is exciting the great car-warrior of Dhritarashtra's army. The powerful car-warriors are covering the son of Pritha with a down-pour of various weapons such as Indrajala, Sthunakarna and Pasupata.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: आतुरो हि कृतो राजा संनिषेव्यश्च भारत। यथैनमनुवर्तन्ते पञ्चालाः सह पाण्डवैः॥ त्वरमाणास्त्वराकाले सर्वशस्त्रभृता वराः। मज्जन्तमिव पाताले बलिनोऽप्युजिहीर्षवः॥
en: Forsooth, O Arjuna, the king is greatly wounded and weakened, since the Panchalas, the wielders of all sorts of weapons, accompanied with Pandavas, are following him hurriedly at a time when it is necessary to display speed like unto men rushing to rescue a man sinking under earth.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न केतुर्दृश्यते राज्ञः कर्णेन निहतः शरैः। पश्यतोर्यमयोः पार्थ सात्यकेश्च शिखण्डिनः॥ धृष्टद्युम्नस्य भीमस्य शतानीकस्य वा विभो। पञ्चालानां च सर्वेषां चेदीनां चैव भारत॥ एष कर्णो रणे पार्थ पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्। शरैविध्वंसयति वै नलिनीमिव कुञ्जरः॥
en: The king's standard is not to be seen. Most likely it has been struck down by Karna with his arrows. Before the very eyes of the twin brothers, Satyaki, Shikhandin, Dhristadyumna, Satanika, Panchalas and Chedis, Karna is killing the Pandava army like an elephant spoilating lotuses.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एते द्रवन्ति रथिनस्त्वदीयाः पाण्डुनन्दन। पश्य पश्य यथा पार्थ गच्छन्त्येते महारथाः॥
en: The car-warriors of your army, O son of Pandu, are flying away. See, O Partha, how they are taking to their heels.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एतं भारत मातङ्गा कर्णेनभिहताः शरैः। आर्तनादान विकुर्वाणा विद्रवन्ति दिशो दश॥
en: Struck by Karna in battle, O Arjuna the elephants are flying away in ten directions yelling cries of pain.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: रथानां द्रवते वृन्दमेतचैव समन्ततः। द्राव्यमाणं रणे पार्थ कर्णेनमित्रकर्षिणा॥
en: Pursued in battle by Karna, the grinder of his enemies the collection of cars is dispersed on all sides.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: हस्तिकक्ष्यां रणे पश्य चरन्तीं तत्र तत्र ह। व्यस्यं सूतपुत्रस्य केतुं केतुमतां वर॥
en: O foremost of those leading standards, see the standard the bearing the emblem of an elephant of charioteer's son is moving about all over (the field).

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: असौ धावति राधेयो भीमसेनरथं प्रति। किरशरशतान्येव विनिघ्नस्तवं वाहिनीम्॥
en: There the son of Radha runs after Bhimasena scattering hundreds of arrows and killing your soldiers.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एतान् पश्य च पञ्चालान् द्राव्यमाणान् महारथान्। शक्रेणेव यथा दैत्यान् हन्यमानान् महाहवे॥
en: There the powerful Panchala car-warriors are being dispersed (by him) like the Daityas slain by Sakra in the great battle.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एष कर्णो रणे जित्वा पञ्चालान् पाण्डुसृञ्जयान्। दिशो विप्रेक्षते सर्वास्त्वदर्थमिति मे मतिः॥
en: Having defeated the Panchalas, Pandavas and Srinjayas, Karna is casting his eyes on all sides, methinks, for finding you out.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पश्य पार्थ धनुः श्रेष्ठ विकर्षन् साधु शोभते। शत्रु जित्वा यथा शक्रो देवसंघैः समावृतः॥
en: See Partha, how beautiful he looks while drawing his best of bows as did shine Shakra in the midst of the celestials after having defeated his enemies.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एते नर्दन्ति कौरव्या दृष्ट्वा कर्णस्य विक्रमम्। त्रासयन्तो रणे पाण्डून् सृञ्जयांश्च समन्ततः॥
en: Witnessing Karna's power there the Kauravas are shouting and striking terror to the Pandavas and Srinjayas.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एष सर्वात्मना पाण्डूंस्त्रासयित्वा महारणे। अभिभाषित राधेयः सर्वसैन्यानि मानद॥
en: Having thus terrified the Pandavas in the great battle with all his force, the son of Radha, O giver of honor, addressing his army said-

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अभिद्रवत भद्रं वो दुतं द्रवत कौरवाः। यथा जीवन वः कश्चिन्मुच्येत युधि सृञ्जयः॥
en: “May you fare well, O Kauravas. Do you move on with such a force that no Srinjaya can escape from the battle-field with his life.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तथा कुरुत संयत्ता वयं यास्याम पृष्ठतः। एवमुक्त्वा गतो ह्येष पृष्ठतो विकिरञ्छरान्॥
en: Do so in a body. We will follow you." Saying this he followed them shooting his arrow.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पश्य कर्ण रणे श्वेतच्छत्रविराजितम्। उदयं पर्वतं यद्वच्छसाङ्केनाभिशोभितम्॥
en: See Partha, Karna is shining in the battlefield with a white umbrella like the Udaya (rising mountain) beautified with the moon.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पूर्णचन्द्रनिकाशेन मूर्ध्निच्छत्रेण भारत। ध्रियमाणेन समरे श्रीमच्छतशलाकिना॥ एष त्वां प्रेक्षते कर्णः सकटाक्षं विशाम्पते। उत्तमं जवमास्थाय ध्रुवमेष्यति संयुगे॥
en: With this umbrella of a hundred ribs resembling the full-moon held over his head he is casting his looks around for you. Forsooth, he will come here quickly.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पश्य होनं महाबाहो विधुन्वानं महद् धनुः। शरांश्चाशीविषाकारान् विसृजन्तं महारणे॥
en: See, O you of large arms, he is drawing a huge bow shooting, in the great battle, arrows resembling deadly serpents.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: असौ निवृत्तौ राधेयो दृष्ट्वा ते वानरध्वजम्। प्रार्थयन् समरे पार्थ त्वया सह परंतप॥
en: Seeing your banner bearing the emblem of a monkey the son of Radha is turning to this direction for seeking an encounter with you.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: वधाय चात्मनोऽभ्येति दीप्तास्यं शलभो यथा। कर्णमेकाकिनं दृष्ट्वा रथानीकेन भारत॥ रिरक्षिषुः सुसंवृत्तो धार्तराष्ट्रो निवर्तते।
en: O Partha and bringing on his destruction like an insect approaching a burning flame. This wrathful hero is engaged in the well-being of Dhritarashtra's son; that own W one of wicked understanding always seeks to injure you. Seeing Karna alone Dhritarashtra's son is turning with his car force to protect him.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सर्वैः सहैभिर्दुष्टात्मा वध्यतां च प्रयत्नतः॥ त्वया यशश्च राज्यं च सुखं चोत्तममिच्छता।
en: That wicked man with all his followers should be killed by you with all care if you wish to secure fame, kingdom and happiness.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अदीनयोर्विश्रुतयोर्युवयोर्योत्स्यमानयोः॥ देवासुरे पार्थ मृधे देवदानवयोरिव। पश्यन्तु कौरवाः सर्वे तव पार्थ पराक्रमम्॥
en: O Partha! All Kauravas will introduce with your valour when the battle is initiated with extremne vigour between you both warriors renowned in the world. It will be a fight the same as took place during long long ago between demons and gods.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: त्वां च दृष्ट्वातिसंरब्धं कर्णं च भरतर्षभ। असौ दुर्योधनः क्रुद्धो नोत्तरं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Seeing you greatly worked up with anger and Karna too Duryodhiana, although angered, will not be able to do anything.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: आत्मानं च कृतात्मानं समीक्ष्य भरतर्षभ। कृतागसं च राधेयं धर्मात्मनि युधिष्ठिरे। प्रतिपद्यस्व कौन्तेयं प्राप्तकालमनन्तरम्॥
en: O foremost of Bharatas, knowing yourself self-controlled and Karna cherishing animosity against the pious Yudhishthira, O son of Kunti, make use of this good opportunity.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: आर्यां युद्धे मति कृत्वा प्रत्येहि रथयूथपम्। पञ्च ह्येतानि मुख्यानि स्थानां रथसत्तम॥ शतान्यायान्ति समरे बलिनां तिग्मतेजसाम्। पञ्च नागसहस्राणि द्विगुणा वाजिनस्तथा॥ अभिसंहत्य कौन्तेयं पदातिप्रयुतानि च।
en: Making up your mind for battle encounter all the car-warriors. O foremost of car-warriors, five hundred most excellent, powerful and energetic, car-warriors, five thousand elephants, ten thousand horses and ten lakhs foot-soldiers, protecting one another coming against you in a battle-field. as are

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अन्यान्यरक्षितं वीर बलं त्वामभिवर्तते॥ द्रोणपुत्रं पुरस्कृत्य तच्छीघ्रं संनिषूदय।
en: O warrior! Kill immediately the army just ready to attack on you under circle of defence led by Ashvatthama, the son of Drona.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: निकृत्यैतद्रथानीकं बलिनं लोकविश्रुतम्॥ सूतपुत्रं महेष्वासं दर्शयात्मानमात्मना।
en: Of your own accord show yourself to the great bowman, the charioteer's son. Advance with great force, O foremost of Bharatas.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: उत्तमं जवमास्थाय प्रत्येहि भरतर्षभ।॥ असौ कर्णः सुसंरब्धः पञ्चालानभिधावति। केतुमस्य हि पश्यामि धृष्टद्युम्नरथं प्रति॥
en: Worked up up with anger there Karna advances against the Panchalas. I see his standard approaching the car of Dhristadyumna, forsooth.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: समुपैष्यति पञ्चालानिति मन्ये परंतप। आचक्षे च प्रियं पार्थ तवेदं भरतर्षभ॥ राजासौ कुशली श्रीमान् धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। असौ भीमो महाबाहुः संनिवृत्तश्चमूमुखे॥
en: He will root out the Panchalas. O Bharata chief, I will communicate to you a good intelligence, the virtuous king Yudhishthira is still alive. The mighty-armed Bhima has returned and is leading the army.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: वृतः सृञ्जयसैन्येन शैनेयेन च भारत। वध्यन्त एते समरे कौरवा निशितैः शरै॥ भीमसेनेन कौन्तेय पञ्चालैश्च महात्मभिः।
en: He is surrounded by the Srinjayas and Satyaki. There in battle the Kuru soldiers are being killed in battle with sharp arrows by Bhimasena and the high-souled Panchalas.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सेना हि धार्तराष्ट्रस्य विमुखा विक्षरवणा॥ विप्रधावति वेगेन भीमस्याभिहता शरैः।
en: Wounded with Bhima's arrows, Duryodhana's army, retreating and bathed in blood, are quickly flying away.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: विपन्नसस्येव मही रुधिरेण समुक्षिता॥ भारती भरतश्रेष्ठ सेना कृपणदर्शना।
en: Covered with blood the Bharata is looking poorly like the earth divested of crops.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: निवृत्तं पश्य कौन्तेय भीमसेनं युधां पतिम्॥ आशीविषमिव क्रुद्धं द्रावयन्तं वरूथिनीम्।
en: Behold, O son of Kunti, Bhimasena, the commander of your army, worked up with anger like a serpent, is assailing the (Kuru) troops.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पीतरक्तासितसितास्ताराचन्द्रार्कमण्डिताः॥ पताका विप्रकीर्यन्ते छत्राण्येतानि चार्जुन।
en: Look, O Arjuna, at the yellow, crimson, black and white banners painted with stars, moons and suns and innumerable umbrellas scattered all over the field.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सौवर्णा राजताश्चैव तैजसाश्च पृथग्विधाः॥ केतवोऽभिनिपात्यन्ते हस्त्यश्वं च प्रकीर्यते।
en: Standards, made of gold, silver and other metals, are lying about and there lie scattered slain horses.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: रथेभ्यः प्रपतन्त्येते रथिनो विगतासवः॥ नानावणैर्हता बाणैः पञ्चालैरपलायिभिः।
en: Car-warriors, deprived of their life, are dropping down from cars, killed by the unretreating Panchalas with variegated arrows.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: निर्मनुष्यान् गजानश्वान् रथांश्चैव धनंजय॥ समाद्रवन्ति पञ्चाला धार्तराष्ट्रांस्तरस्विनः। विमृद्नन्ति नरव्याघ्रा भीमसेनबलाश्रयात्॥
en: There the quick-coursing Panchalas, O Dhananjaya, are rushing against the elephants, horses and cars belonging the Dhritarashtra's party, divested of their riders. O foremost of men, O slayer of enemies, your warriors, giving up the love of their lives and invincible in battle, are, aided by Bhimasena's power, grinding the enemy's army.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: बलं परेषां दुर्धर्षास्त्यक्त्वा प्राणानरिंदम। एते नर्दन्ति पञ्चाला ध्मापयन्ति च वारिजान्॥
en: There the Panchalas are sending up loud war-cries and blowing their conchs as they are advancing against their enemies and grinding them with their arrows.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अभिद्रवन्ति च रणे मृदनन्तः सायकैः : परान्। पश्यस्वैषां च माहात्म्यं पञ्चाला हि पराक्रमात्॥ धार्तराष्ट्रान् विनिघ्नन्ति क्रुद्धाः सिंहा इव द्विपान्।
en: Look at their greatness. through their power the Panchalas are killing Dhritarashtra's soldiers as the angry lions kill the tigers.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: शस्त्रमाच्छिद्य शत्रूणां सायुधानां निरायुधाः॥ तेनैवैतानमोधास्त्रा निघ्नन्ति च नदन्ति च।
en: Themselves although without any arms they are carrying away the arms of the enemies (from their hands) and with them they are killing foes and making war-caries.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: शिरांस्येतानि पात्यन्ते शत्रूणां बाहवोऽपि च॥ रथनागहया वीरा यशस्याः सर्व एव च।
en: They are striking down the heads and arms of their enemies. Their car-warriors, elephantwarriors and cavalry are all heroic and praiseworthy.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सर्वतश्चाभिपन्नैषा धार्तराष्ट्री महाचमूः॥ पञ्चलैर्मानसादेत्य हंसर्गनेव वेगितैः।
en: Like quick-coursing swans leaving Manasa lake and running into the Ganges the Panchalas are rushing against the Kuru army and are assailing every part of the huge force of Duryodhana.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सुभृशं च पराक्रान्ताः पञ्चालानां निवारणे॥ कृपकर्णादयो वीरा ऋषभाणामिवर्षभाः।
en: Like bulls withstanding bulls, Kripa, Karna and other warriors with all their energy are resisting the Panchalas.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: भीमास्त्रेण सुनिर्भग्नान् धार्तराष्ट्रान् महारथान्॥ धृष्टद्युम्नमुखा वीरा घ्नन्ति शत्रून् सहस्रशः।
en: The heroes, headed by Dhristadyumna, are killing thousands of their enemies, the great car-warriors of Duryodhana's force, already sunk in the ocean of Bhima's weapons.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पञ्चालेष्वभिभूतेषु द्विषद्भिरपभीर्नदन्॥ शत्रुपक्षमवस्कन्ध शरानस्यति मारुतिः।
en: Beholding Panchalas overpowered by their energies Marut's son is covering the hostile force with arrows and with roars of lions.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: विषण्णभूयिष्ठतरा धार्तराष्ट्री महाचमूः॥ रथाश्चैते सुवित्रस्ता भीमसेनभयार्दिताः।
en: The major portion of the huge army of Duryodhana is stricken with fear. The cars and horses assailed with Bhima's fear have been scattered all over.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पश्य भीमेन नाराचैर्भिन्ना नागाः पतन्त्यमी॥ वज्रिवज्रहतानीव शिखराणि धराभृताम्।
en: See, these elephants, struck by Bhima with his Narachas, are dropping down like the summits of mountains clapped by Indra's thunder-bolt.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: भीमसेनस्य निर्विदा बाणैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ स्वान्यनीकानि मृदनन्तो द्रवन्त्येते महागजा:।
en: There the huge elephants, wounded by Bhima with his arrows, are flying away crushing their own army.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अभिजानीहि भीमस्य सिंहनादं सुदुःसहम्॥ नदतोऽर्जुनं संग्रामे वीरस्य जितकाशिनः।
en: Do you not recognise the leonine shouts of Bhima, O Arjuna, who, worked up with the desire of achieving victory, is roaring.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एष नैषादिरभ्येति द्विपमुख्येन पाण्डवम्॥ जिघांसुस्तोमरैः क्रुद्धो दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः।
en: There worked up with anger the Prince of Nishadas is advancing on his best of cars, like Death himself armed with his rod against the son of Pandu for killing him with his Tomara.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सतोमरावस्य भुजौ छिन्नौ भीमेन गर्जतः॥ तीक्ष्णैरग्निविप्रख्यैर्नाराचैर्दशभिर्हतः।
en: His two arms with Tomaras are cut-off by Bhima with ten sharpened Narachas effulgent like fire of the sun.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: हत्वैन पुनरायाति नागानन्यान् प्रहारिणः॥ पश्य नीलाम्बुदनिभान् महासात्रैरधिष्ठितान्। शक्तितोमरसंघातैविनिघ्नन्तं वृकोदरम्॥
en: Killing him he is proceeding against other elephants resembling a mass of dark blue clouds and driven by riders. They are striking Vrikodara with Saktis and Tomaras.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सप्तसप्त च नागांस्तान् वैजयन्तीश्च सध्वजाः। निहत्य निशितैर्बाणश्छिन्नाः पार्थाग्रजेन ते॥
en: Slaying those forty-nine elephants with sharp arrows Parthas' elder brother is striking down their victorious standards.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: दशभिर्दशाभिश्चैको नाराचैर्निहतो गजः। न चासौ धार्तराष्ट्राणां श्रूयते निनदस्तथा॥ पुरंदरसमे क्रुद्धे निवृत्ते भरतर्षभ।
en: The other elephants were killed each with ten Narachas. The war-cries of Dhritarashtra's soldiers are no longer audible since (Bhima), like Purandara himself, is engaged in battle.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अक्षौहिण्यस्तथा तिस्त्रो धार्तराष्ट्रस्य संहता। क्रुद्धेन भीमसेनेन नरसिंहने वारिताः॥
en: Three Akshauhini of Dhritarashtra's soldiers have been arranged and they all have been thwarted by angry Bhima, the foremost of men.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न शक्नुवन्ति वै पार्थ पार्थिवाः समुदीक्षितुम्। मध्यंदिनगतं सूर्य यथा दुर्बलचक्षुषः॥
en: As the people having weak eye-sight cannot see at sun in noon, the kings are unable to gaze directly at Bhimasena, the son of Kunti.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एते भीमस्य संत्रस्ता: सिंहस्येवेतरे मृगाः। शरैः संत्रासिताः संख्ये न लभन्ते सुखं क्वचित्।। ८८
en: As the stags feel anxiety with fear of lion, these Kauravas' soldiers are so frightened of the arrows shot by Bhimasena as they are anxious everywhere in the battle-field.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: संजय उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा महाबाहुर्वासुदेवाद् धनंजयः। भीमसेनेन तत् कर्मकृतं दृष्ट्वा सुदुष्करम्॥ अर्जुनो व्यधमच्छिष्टानहितान् निशितैः शरैः।
en: Sanjaya said Beholding that arduous task accomplished by Bhima Arjuna, with his sharp arrows, killed the remaining enemies.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे संशप्तकगणाः प्रभो॥ प्रभग्नाः समरे भीता दिशो दश महाबलाः। शक्रस्यातिथितां गत्वा विशोका ह्यभवंस्तदा॥
en: O sovereign! The mighty samsaptakas have run away to ten directions on account of their severe slaughter in battle-field and the departing as also loss of courage. A number of other warriors got immediate relief by joining Indra as his guest.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पार्थश्च पुरुषव्याघ्रः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। जघान् धार्तराष्ट्रस्य चतुर्विधबलां चमूम्॥
en: Lion heart Partha killed the Caturangini army (infantry, chariot-rider, horse-riders and elephant-riders) led by Duryodhana by shooting arrows with bent nodes. O sovereign! The mighty samsaptakas have run away to ten directions on account of their severe slaughter in battle-field and the departing as also loss of courage. A number of other warriors got immediate relief by joining Indra as his guest.

description: The conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पार्थश्च पुरुषव्याघ्रः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। जघान् धार्तराष्ट्रस्य चतुर्विधबलां चमूम्॥
en: Lion heart Partha killed the Caturangini army (infantry, chariot-rider, horse-riders and elephant-riders) led by Duryodhana by shooting arrows with bent nodes.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच निवृत्ते भीमसेने च पाण्डवे च युधिष्ठिरे। वध्यमाने बले चापि मामके पाण्डुसृञ्जयैः॥ द्रवमाणे बलौघे च निरानन्दे मुहुर्मुहुः। किमकुर्वन्त कुरवस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When Bhimasena and Pandu's Yudhishthira were fighting, when my soldiers were being killed by the Pandavas and Srinjayas, when my army was routed and dispirited tell me, O Sanjaya, what did the Kauravas do. son

sn: संजय उवाच दृष्ट्वा भीमं महाबाहुं सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। क्रोधरक्तेक्षणो राजन् भीमसेनमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing the mighty-armed Bhima the valiant Karna, with eyes, reddened in anger, rushed towards him.

sn: तावकं तु बलं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनात् पराङ्मुखम्। यत्नेन महता राजन् पर्यवस्थापयद् बली॥
en: Beholding your soldiers routed by Bhima the powerful Karna rallied them again with great exertion.

sn: व्यवस्थाप्य महाबाहुस्तव पुत्रस्य वाहिनीम्। प्रत्युद्ययौ तदा कर्णः पाण्डवान् युद्धदुर्मदान्॥ प्रत्युद्ययुस्तु राधेयं पाण्डवानां महारथाः। धुन्वानाः कार्मुकाण्याजौ विक्षिपन्तश्च सायकान्॥
en: Having collected your son's force the largearmed Karna advanced against the heroic Pandavas invincible in battle. Drawing their bows and discharging arrows the great carwarriors of the Pandavas advanced against the son of Radha.

sn: भीमसेनः शिनेनप्ता शिखण्डी जनमेजयः। धृष्टद्युम्नश्च बलवान् सर्वे चापि प्रभद्रकाः॥ जिघांसन्तो नरव्याघ्राः समन्तात् तव वाहिनीम्। अभ्यद्रवन्त संक्रुद्धाः समरे जितकाशिनः॥
en: Worked up with anger and desiring for victory Bhimasena, the grandson of Sini, Shikhandi Janamejaya, the powerful Dhristadyumna, all the Prabhadrakas and the Panchalas advanced furiously from all directions against your army.

sn: तथैव तावका राजन् पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्। अभ्यद्रवन्त त्वरिता जिघांसन्तो महारथाः॥
en: In the same way the powerful car-warriors of your host speedily advanced against the Pandava army desirous of killing them.

sn: रथनागाश्वकलिलं पत्तिध्वद समाकुलम्। बभूव पुरुषव्याघ्र सैन्यमद्भुतदर्शनम्॥
en: The hosts, abounding in cars, elephants, the cavalry and infantry, looked exceedingly wonderful.

sn: शिखण्डी च ययौ कर्ण धृष्टद्युम्नः सुतं तव। दुःशासनं महाराज महत्या सेनया वृत्तम्॥
en: Shikhandi rushed against Karna and Dhristadyumna, accompanied by a great force, proceeded against your son Dushasana.

sn: नकुलो वृषसेनं तु चित्रसेनं युधिष्ठिरः। उलूकं समरे राजन् सहदेवः समभ्ययात्॥
en: Nakula against Vrishasena and Yudhishthira advanced against Chitrasena; Sahadeva proceeded against Uluka in that battle. two ran

sn: सात्यकिः शकुनि चापि द्रौपदेयाश्च कौरवान्। अर्जुनं च रणे यत्तो द्रोणपुत्रो महारथः॥
en: Satyaki proceeded against Shakuni and the sons of Draupadi against other Kauravas. And the great car-warrior Drona's son proceeded against Arjuna in that battle.

sn: युधामन्युं महेष्वासं गौतमोऽभ्यपतद्रणे। कृतवर्मा च बलवानुत्तमौजसमाद्रवत्॥
en: Gautama encountered in battle the great bowman Yudhamanyu. And the powerful Kritavarma rushed against Uttamoujasa.

sn: भीमसेनः कुरून् सर्वान् पुत्रांश्च तव मारिष। सहानीकान् महाबाहुरेक एव न्यवारयत्॥
en: The large-armed Bhimasena alone withstood all your sons with their armies.

sn: शिखण्डी तु ततः कर्ण विचरन्तमभीतवत्। भीष्महन्ता महाराज वारयामास पत्रिभिः॥
en: Thereupon Shikhandi, the slayer of Bhishma, with winged arrows, obstructed Karna ranging fearlessly in the battle-field).

sn: प्रतिरुद्धस्ततः कर्णो रोषात् प्रस्फुरिताधरः। शिखण्डिनं त्रिभिर्बाणैभ्रुवोर्मध्येऽभ्यताडयत्॥
en: Thus obstructed and with his lips trembling in anger Karna struck Shikhandi on the forehead with three arrows.

sn: धारयंस्तु स तान् बाणाशिखण्डी बह्वशोभत। राजतः पर्वतो यद्वत् त्रिभिः शृङ्गैरिवोत्थितैः॥
en: Carrying three arrows Shikhandi shone there like a silver mountain with three elevated summits.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महेष्वासः सूतपुत्रेण संयुगे। कर्ण विव्याध समरे नवत्या निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Sorely wounded by Karna in that battle that great bowman struck him in return with ninety sharp arrows.

sn: तस्य कर्णो हयान् हत्वा सारथिं च त्रिभिः शरैः। उन्ममाथ ध्वजं चास्य क्षुरप्रेण महारथः॥
en: Having slain his horses and driver with three arrows the great car-warrior Karna struck down his standard with a razor-shaped arrow.

sn: हताश्वात्तु ततो यानादवप्लुत्य महारथः। शक्तिं चिक्षेप कर्णाय संक्रुद्ध शत्रुतापनः॥
en: Then jumping down from his horseless car that great car-warrior, the aggrandiser of his enemies, discharged a dart in anger at Karna.

sn: तां छित्वा समरे कर्णस्त्रिभिारत सायकैः। शिखण्डिनमथाविध्यन्नवभिर्निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Cutting it off in battle with three arrows Karna struck Shikhandi with nine sharp arrows.

sn: कर्णचापच्युतान् बाणान् वर्जयंस्तु नरोत्तमः। अपयातस्तस्तूर्णं शिखण्डी भृशविक्षतः॥
en: Avoiding arrows shot off Karna's bow Shikhandi, greatly wounded, quickly retreated from the field.

sn: ततः कर्णो महाराज पाण्डुसैन्यान्यशातयत्। तूलराशि समासाद्य यथा वायुर्महाबलः॥
en: O king, then Karna fell on the Pandava army as the violent wind disperses a pack of cotton.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नो महाराज तव पुत्रेण पीडितः। दुःशासनं त्रिभिर्बाणैः प्रत्यविध्यत स्तनान्तरे॥
en: Wounded by your son Dhristadyumna struck, in return, Dushasana on the breast with three arrows.

sn: तस्य दुःशासनो बाहुं सव्यं विव्याध मारिष। स तेन रुक्मपुड्वेन भल्लेनानतपर्वणा॥
en: Then Dushasana struck the left arm of his enemy with a sharp gold feathered, winged arrows.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु निर्विद्धः शरं घोरममर्षणः। दुःशासनाय संक्रुद्धः प्रेषयामास भारत॥
en: Thus wounded and filled with terrible rage Dhristadyumna shot arrows at Dushasana.

sn: आपतन्तं महावेगं धृष्टद्युम्नसमीरितम्। शरैश्चिच्छेद पुत्रस्ते त्रिभिरेव विशाम्पते॥
en: O king, with three arrows your son cut-off the shaft discharged by Dhristadyumna which was about to fall with great force.

sn: अथान्यैः सप्तदशभिर्भल्लैः कनकभूषणैः। धृष्टद्युम्नं मसासाद्य बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्॥
en: Then approaching Dhristadyumna he struck him on the breast and two arms with seventeen other gold winged arrows.

sn: ततः स पार्षतः क्रुद्धो धनुश्चिच्छेद मारिष। क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन तत उचुक्रुशुर्जनाः॥
en: Then worked up with anger Prisata's son cut-off his bow with a sharp razor shaped arrow at which all his people shouted out.

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय पुत्रस्ते प्रहसन्निव। धृष्टद्युमं शरव्रातः समन्तात् पर्यवारयत्॥
en: Your son, however, taking up another bow, smilingly covered Dhristadyumna with wounds of arrows.

sn: तव पुत्रस्य ते दृष्ट्वा विक्रमं सुमहात्मनः। व्यस्मयन्त रणे योधाः सिद्धाश्चाप्सरसां गणाः॥
en: Beholding the prowess of your high-souled son all the warriors in the field, Siddhas and Apsaras were filled surprise.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं न पश्याम घटमानं महाबलम्। दुःशासनेन संरुद्धं सिंहेनव महगजम्॥
en: We saw the highly powerful Dhristadyumna obstructed by Dushasana like a huge elephant checked by a lion.

sn: ततः सरथनागाश्वाः पञ्चालाः पाण्डुपूर्वज। सेनापतिं परीप्सन्तो रुरुधुस्तनयं तव॥
en: Then desirous of rescuing their generalissimo, O elder brother of Pandu, the Panchala car-warriors, elephants and horses surrounded your son.

sn: ततः प्रववृत्ते युद्धं तावकानां परैः सह। घोरं प्राणभृतां काले भीमरूपं परंतप॥
en: O slayer of enemies, then ensued a dreadful and destructive encounter between your people and your enemy's host.

sn: नकुलं वृषसेनस्तु भित्वा पञ्चभिरायसैः। पितुः समीपे तिष्ठन् वै त्रिभिरन्यैरविध्यत॥
en: Standing by his father's side Vrishasena struck Nakula with five iron arrows and again wounded with three others.

sn: नकुलस्तु ततः शूरो वृषसेनं हसन्निव। नाराचेन सुतीक्ष्णेन विव्याध हृदये भृशम्॥
en: The heroic Nakula however smiling struck Vrishasena on the breast with a sharp Naracha.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता शत्रुणा शत्रुकर्षण। शत्रु विव्याध विंशत्या स च तं पञ्चभिः शरैः॥
en: Thus wounded greatly by his powerful enemy that grinder of his enemies struck his adversary with twenty five arrows.

sn: ततः शरसहस्रेण तावुभौ पुरुर्षभौ। अन्योन्यमाच्छादयतामथोऽभज्यत वाहिनी॥
en: Those two foremost of men covered each other with thousands of arrows at which their respective battalions broke.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा प्रदुतां सेनां धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सूतजः। निवारयामास बलादनुसृत्य विशाम्पते॥
en: Seeing Duryodhana's soldiers quickly flying away Karna, O king, prevented them with force.

sn: निवृत्ते तु ततः कर्णे नकुलः कौरवान् ययौ। कर्णपुत्रस्तु सपरे हित्वा नकुलमेव तु॥ जुगोप चक्रं त्वरितो राधेयस्यैव मारिष।
en: After Karna's departure Nakula proceeded against the Kauravas. Avoiding Nakula in battle Karna's son quickly went to Karna, who was guarding the passage of his chariot.

sn: उलूकस्तु रणे क्रुद्धः सहदेवेन वारितः॥ तस्याश्वांश्चतुरो हत्वा सहदेवः प्रतापवान्। सारथिं प्रेषयामास यमस्य सूदनं प्रति॥
en: Angry Uluka was restrained by Sahadeva in battle. Having killed his four horse the powerful Sahadeva dispatched his charioteer to the abode of Yama.

sn: उलूकस्तु ततो यानादवप्लुत्य विशाम्पते। त्रिगर्तानां बलं तूर्णं जगाम पितृनन्दनः॥
en: Then leaping down from his car O king, Uluka, the joy of his sire, soon advanced against the host of Trigarttas.

sn: सात्यकिः शकुनि विद्ध्वा विंशत्या निशितैः शरैः। ध्वजं चिच्छेद भल्लेन सौबलस्य हसन्निव॥
en: Having pierced Shakuni with twenty sharp arrows Satyaki, as if smiling, struck down the standard of Subala's son with his dart.

sn: सौबलस्तस्य समरे क्रुद्धो राजन् प्रतापवान्। विदार्य कवचं भूयो ध्वजं चिच्छेद काञ्जनम्॥
en: O king, the powerful son of Subala too, worked up with anger, cutting off his coat of mail, again sundered his golden standard.

sn: तथैनं निशितैबाणैः सात्यकिःप्रत्यविध्यत। सारथिं च महाराज त्रिभिरेव समार्पयत्॥
en: Then Satyaki pierced him in return with sharpened arrows and also pierced his charioteer with three arrows.

sn: अथास्य वाहांस्त्वरितः शरैर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्। ततोऽवप्लुत्य सहसा शकुनिर्भरतर्षभ॥ आरुहोह रथं तूर्णमुलूकस्य महात्मनः।
en: Then quickly dispatched his horses to the abode of Yama with arrows. Then ( king, jumping down all on a sudden from his own car Shakuni quickly got on Uluka's car.

sn: अपोवाहाथ शीघ्रं स शैनेयाद् युद्धशालिनः॥ सात्यकिस्तु रणे राजस्तावकानामनीकिनीम्। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन ततोऽनीकमभज्यत॥
en: Then that hero, expert in fighting, soon took away Sini's grandson. Then O king, Satyaki, with great force, advanced against your army at which they were all routed.

sn: शैनेयशकसहंछन्नं तव सैन्यं विशाम्पते। भेजे दश दिशस्तूर्णं न्यपतच गतासुवत्॥
en: Covered with arrows shot by Sini's grandson your soldiers, O king, fled away in all directions and dropped down dead.

sn: भीमसेनं तव सुतो वारयामास संयुगे। तं तु भीमो मुहूर्तेन व्यश्वसूतरथध्वजम्॥ चक्रे लोकेश्वर तत्र तेनातुष्यन्त वै जनाः।
en: Your son obstructed Bhimasena in battle. Bhima however, in a moment, deprived him of his horses, charioteer, car and standards. His men, O king, were highly pleased.

sn: ततोऽपायानृपस्तत्र भीमसेनस्य गोचरात्॥ कुरुसैन्यं ततः सर्व भीमसेनमुपाद्रवत्। तत्र नादो महानासीद् भीमसेन जिघांसताम्॥
en: The king soon fled away from Bhimasena's view. Then the entire Kuru army rushed towards Bhimasena. And desirous of killing Bhima they set up a terrible shout.

sn: युधामन्युः कृपं विद्ध्वा धनुरस्याशु चिच्छिदे। अथान्यद् धनुरादाय कृपः शस्त्रभृतां वरः॥ युधामन्योर्ध्वजं सूतं छत्रं चापातयत् क्षितौ। ततोऽपायाद् रथेनैव युधामन्युर्महारथः॥
en: Having struck Kripa Yudhamanyu soon cut-off his bow. But Kripa, the foremost of the wielders of arms, taking up another bow struck down on earth Yudhamanyu's standard, charioteer and umbrella. the great car-warrior Yudhamanyu fled away on his car.

sn: उत्तमौजाश्च हार्दिक्यं भीमं भीमपराक्रमम्। छादयामास सहसा मेघो वृष्ट्येव पर्वतम्॥
en: Uttamouja soon covered Hirdika's son Bhima of dreadful prowess like showers covering a mountain.

sn: तद् युद्धमासीत् सुमहद् घोररूपं परंतप। यादृशं न मया युद्धं दृष्टपूर्व विशाम्पते॥
en: Then O slayer of enemies, that battle became highly dreadful the like of which had never been seen by me before, O king.

sn: कृतवर्मा ततो राजन्नुत्तमौजसमाहवे। हृदि विव्याध सहसा रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्॥
en: Then Kritavarma, in that battle, O king, all on a sudden struck Uttamouja on the breast at which the latter sank down on his car.

sn: सारथिस्तमपोवाह रथेन रथिनां वरम्। कुरुसैन्यं ततः सर्व भीमसेनमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: His charioteer however carried away that foremost of car-warriors. Then the Kuru army surrounded Bhimasena from all sides.

sn: दुःशासनः सौबलश्च गजानीकेन पाण्डवम्। महता परिवार्यैव क्षुद्रकैरभ्याताडयत्॥
en: With a huge elephant force Dushasana and Subala's son surrounded Pandu's son and began to assail him with small arrows.

sn: ततो भीमः शरशतैर्दुर्योधनममर्षणम्। विमुखीकृत्य तरसा गजानीकमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Thereupon making the angry Duryodhana retreat from the battle-field with a hundred arrows Bhima quickly advanced against the elephant force.

sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा गजानीकं वृकोदरः। दृष्टैव सुभृशं क्रुद्धो दिव्यमस्त्रमुदैरयत्॥
en: Beholding that elephant force advance against him all on a sudden Vrikodara, worked up greatly with anger, invited celestial weapons.

sn: गजैर्गजानभ्यहनद् वज्रणेन्द्र इवासुरान्। ततोऽन्तरिक्षं बाणैघैः शलभैरिव पादपम्॥ छादयामास समरे गजान् निघ्नन् वृकोदरः।
en: He then struck elephants with elephants as Indra assailed the Asuras. Killing the elephants in battle Vrikodara covered the sky with arrows as a swarm of insects cover a flame.

sn: ततः कुञ्जरयूथानि समेतानि सहस्रशः॥ व्यधमत् तरसा भीमो मेघसङ्घानिवानिलः।
en: As the wind scatters a collection of clouds so Bhima dispersed and killed those elephants collected there in thousands.

sn: सुवर्णजालापिहिता मणिजालैश्च कुञ्जराः॥ रेजुरभ्यधिकं संख्ये विद्युत्वन्त इवाम्बुदाः।
en: Covered with net-works of gold and gems the elephants looked greatly beautiful like clouds charged with lightning.

sn: ते वध्यमाना भीमेन गजा राजन् विदुद्रुवुः॥ केचिद् विभिन्नहृदयाः कुञ्जरा न्यपतन् भुवि।
en: Assailed by Bhima, O king, the elephants fled away on all sides. Some, cut to their hearts, fell down on earth.

sn: पतितैर्निपतद्भिश्च गजैर्हेमविभूषितैः॥ अशोभत मही तत्र विशीर्णैरिव पर्वतैः।
en: With elephants adorned with gold fallen there the earth appeared as if strewn with shattered mountains.

sn: दीप्ताभै रत्नवद्भिश्च पतितैर्गजयोधिभिः॥ रराज भूमिः पतितैः क्षीणपुण्यैरिव ग्रहैः।
en: With fallen elephant warriors, shining and adorned with jewels and the earth shone beautiful as if covered with planets dropped for the wane of virtue.

sn: ततो भिन्नकटा नागा भिन्नकुम्भकरास्तथा॥ दुद्रुवु शतशः संख्ये भीमसेनशराहताः।
en: With their temples, frontal globes and trunks maimed the elephants, struck by Bhimasena's arrows, fled away in hundreds in that battle.

sn: केचिद् वमन्तो रुधिरं भयार्ताः पर्वतोपमाः॥ व्यद्रवञ्छरविद्धागा धातुचित्रा इवाचलाः।
en: With their limbs wounded with arrows, stricken with fear and vomiting blood, some, huge like mountains, fled away like mountains adorned with metals.

sn: महाभुजगसंकाशौ चन्दनागुरुरूषितौ॥ अपश्यं भीमसेनस्य धनुर्विक्षिपतो भुजौ।
en: There they saw the two arms of Bhimasena, holding bows, pasted with sandal and Aguru and resembling two huge serpents.

sn: तस्य ज्यातलनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वाशनिसमस्वनम्॥ विमुञ्चन्तः शकृन्मूत्रं गजाः प्रादुद्रुवु शम्।
en: Hearing the twang of his bow resembling the sound of a thunder-bolt the elephants passed urine and excreta and fled away.

sn: भीमसेनस्य तत् कर्म राजन्नेकस्य धीमतः। निघ्नतः सर्वभूतानि रुद्रस्येव च निर्बभौ॥
en: That feat, of the intelligent Bhimasena who fought single-handed, resembled that of Rudra while destroying all creatures.

sn: संजय उवाच ततः श्वेताश्वसंयुक्ते नारायणसमाहिते। तिष्ठन् रथवरे श्रीमानर्जुनः समपद्यत॥
en: Sanjaya said Then on that best of cars drawn by white horses and driven by Narayana himself the beautiful Arjuna arrived there.

sn: तद् बलं नृपतिश्रेष्ठ तावकं विजयो रणे। व्यक्षोभयदुदीर्णाश्वं महोदधिमिवानिलः॥
en: As the wind agitates a great ocean so Vijaya overpowered your army, O foremost of kings, abounding in horse-men.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तव सुतः प्रमत्ते श्वेतवाहने। अभ्येत्य सहसा क्रुद्धः सैन्यार्धेनाभिसंवृतः॥ पर्यवारयदायान्तं युधिष्ठिरममर्षणम्। क्षुरप्राणां त्रिसप्तत्या ततोऽविध्यत पाण्डवम्॥
en: While (Arjuna) the rider of white horses was a little careless your son Duryodhana, worked up with anger and surrounded by his soldiers, came there all on sudden and encompassed the revengeful Yudhishthira. He then struck Yudhishthira with seventy-three razor-shaped arrows.

sn: अक्रुध्यत भृशं तत्र कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। स भल्लास्त्रिशतस्तूर्णं तव पुत्रे न्यवेशयत्॥
en: At that Kunti's son Yudhishthira was greatly worked up with anger. He quickly struck your son with thirty darts.

sn: ततोऽधावन्त कौरव्या जिघृक्षन्तो युधिष्ठिरम्। दुष्टभावान् पाराज्ज्ञात्वा समवेता महारथाः॥ आजग्मुस्तं परीप्सन्त:कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्।
en: Then the Kuru soldiers rushed against Yudhishthira for seized him. Then apprised of the evil intention of the enemies the great carwarriors came there in a body for rescuing Kunti's son Yudhishthira.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥ अक्षौहिण्या परिवृतास्तेऽभ्यधावन् युधिष्ठिरम्।
en: Encircled by an Akshauhini of soldiers Nakula, Sahadeva, Dhristadyumna and Parshata advanced towards Yudhishthira.

sn: भीमसेनश्च समरे मृदनंस्तव महारथान्॥ अभ्यधावदभिप्रेप्स राजानं शत्रुभिर्वृतम्।
en: Grinding the great car-warriors your army Bhimasena too went where Yudhishthira was surrounded by his enemies.

sn: तांस्तु सर्वान् महेष्वासान् कर्णो वैकर्तनो नृप॥ शरवर्षेण महता प्रत्यवारयदागतान्।
en: Making a downpour of arrows, O king, Vikartana's son Karna obstructed alone all those great bowmen.

sn: नकुलः सहदेवश्च शरौघान् विसृजन्तस्ते प्रेरयन्तश्च तोमरान्॥ न शेकुर्यनवन्तोऽपि राधेयं प्रतिवीक्षितुम्।
en: Although making a downpour of arrows, discharging Tomaras and exerting their very best they could not look at the son of Radha.

sn: तांश्च सर्वान् महेष्वासान् सर्वशस्त्रास्त्रपारगः॥ महता शरवर्षेण राधेयः प्रत्यवारयत्।
en: With a huge downpour of arrows the son of Radha who had mastered all sorts of weapons withstood all those great bow men.

sn: दुर्योधनं च विंशत्या शीघ्रमस्त्रमुदीरयन्॥ अविध्यत् तूर्णमभ्येत्य सहदेवः प्रतापवान्।
en: Taking up speedily his bow the nobleminded Sahadeva soon approached Duryodhana and struck him with twenty arrows.

sn: स विद्धः सहदेवेन रराजाचलसंनिभः॥ प्रभिन्न इव मातङ्गो रुधिरेण परिप्लुतः।
en: Struck by Sahadeva Duryodhana, huge like a mountain, covered with blood, appeared like a maimed elephant.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तव सुतं तत्र गाढविद्धं सुतेजनैः॥ अभ्यधावद् दृढं क्रुद्धो राधेयो रथिनां वरः।
en: Seeing you son sorely wounded with many powerful shafts Karna, the best of car-warriors, worth proceeded there.

sn: दुर्योधनं तथा दृष्ट्वा शीघ्रमस्त्रमुदैरयत्॥ तेन यौधिष्ठिरं सैन्यमवधीत् पार्षतं तथा।
en: Beholding Duryodhana in that condition and quickly getting ready his weapon he soon struck the sons of Yudhishthira and Prishata.

sn: ततो यौधिष्ठिरं सैन्यं वध्यमान महात्मना॥ सहसा प्राद्रवद राजन् सूतपुत्रशरार्दितम्।
en: Assailed with arrows by the great son of the charioteer Yudhishthira's soldiers all on a sudden fled away.

sn: विविधा विशिखास्तत्र सम्पतन्तः परस्परम्॥ फलैः पुत्रान् समाजग्मुः सूतपुत्रधनुच्युताः।
en: Various sorts of arrows fell there touching one another. Those, shot off the bow of Karna, touched the wings of others with their blades.

sn: अन्तरिक्षे शरौघाणां पततां च परस्परम्॥ संघर्षेण महाराज पावकः समजायत।
en: The arrows coming in contact with one another a conflagration was caused in the sky.

sn: ततो दश दिशः कर्णः शलभैरिव यायिभिः॥ अभ्यघ्नंस्तरसा राजशरैः परशरीरगैः।
en: With arrows capable of piercing the bodies of the enemies and advancing quickly Karna covered the ten quarters as if with a swarm of locusts.

sn: रक्तचन्दनसंदिग्धौ मणिहेमविभूषितौ॥ बाहू व्यत्यक्षिपत् कर्णः परमास्त्रं विदर्शयन्।
en: Beautiful bows shone in the arms of Karna of the colour of crimson sandal and adorned with gold and jewels.

sn: ततः सर्वा दिशो राजन् सायकैर्विप्रमोहयन्॥ अपीडयद् भृशं कर्णो धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्।
en: Then all the quarters were shrouded with arrows. And Karna greatly assailed the righteous king Yudhishthira.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ निशितैरिषुभिः कर्णं पञ्चाशद्भिः समार्पयत्।
en: Then worked up with anger Kunti's son king Yudhishthira struck Karna with fifty sharpened arrows.

sn: बाणान्धकारमभवत्तद् युद्धं घोरदर्शनम्॥ हाहाकारो महानासीत्तावकानां विशाम्पते। वध्यमाने तदा सैन्ये धर्मपुत्रेण मारिष॥
en: Darkened with arrows that army looked exceedingly dreadful. And your soldiers, O king, sent up piteous wails of pain.

sn: सायकेविधैस्तीक्ष्णैःकङ्कपत्रैः शिलाशितैः। भल्लैरनेकैर्विविधैः शक्त्यृष्टिमुसलैरपि॥ यत्र यत्र स धर्मात्मा दुष्टां दृष्टिं व्यसर्जयत्। तत्र तत्र व्यशीर्यन्त तावका भरतर्षभ॥
en: While they were being slain by Dharma's son with various sharp Kanka-feathered arrows whetted on stone, Bhallas, Saktis and clubs. Wherever the virtuous king extended his looks all the soldiers of your party were shattered.

sn: कर्णोऽपि भृशसंक्रुद्धो धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। नाराचैरर्धचन्द्रश्च वत्सदन्तैश्च संयुगे॥ अमर्षी क्रोधनश्चैव रोषप्रस्फुरिताननः। सायकैरप्रमेयात्मा युधिष्ठिरमभिद्रवत्॥
en: Then Karna, greatly worked up with anger, struck Yudhishthira with winged and calf-tooth shaped arrows. Revengeful, wrathful and having his lips trembling in anger the highly energetic Karna struck Yudhishthira with arrows.

sn: युधिष्ठिरश्चापि स तं स्वर्णपुडैः शितैः शरै। प्रहसन्निव तं कर्ण:कङ्कपत्रैः शिलाशितैः॥ उरस्यविध्यद् राजानं त्रिभिर्भल्लैश्च पाण्डवम्।
en: Yudhishthira too struck him with gold feathered and sharpened arrows. Karna, as if smiling, struck the Pandava king on the breast with three winged darts.

sn: स पीडितो भृशं तेन धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥ उपविश्य रथोपस्थे सूतं याहीत्यचोदयत्।
en: Thus greatly assailed by him the pious king Yudhishthira sat down on his car and ordered his charioteer to go.

sn: अक्रोशन्त ततः सर्वे धार्तराष्ट्राः सराजकाः॥ गृह्णीध्वमिति राजानमभ्यधावन्त सर्वशः।
en: Then all the soldiers of your army with their king sent up a loud war-cry saying-"seize him" and then they rushed towards the king.

sn: ततः शताः सप्तदश केकयानां प्रहारिणाम्॥ पञ्चालैः सहिता राजन् धार्तराष्ट्रान् न्यवारयन्।
en: Then seventeen hundred Kekaya warriors with Panchalas obstructed the soldiers of Duryodhana.

sn: तस्मिन सुतुमुले युद्धे वर्तमाने जनक्षये॥ दुर्योधनश्च भीमश्च समेयातां महाबलौ॥
en: When that dreadful and destructive battle raged on the highly powerful Duryodhana and Bhima fought with each other.

sn: संजय उवाच कर्णोपि शरजालेन केकयानां महारथान्। व्यधमत् परमेष्वासानग्रतः पर्यवस्थितान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Karna, with a net-work of arrows, struck the mighty car-warrior, the great bowman of the Kekaya race who all stood before him.

sn: तेषां प्रयतमानानां राधेयस्य निवारणे। रथान् पञ्चशतान् कर्णः प्राहिणोद् यमसादनम्॥
en: Five hundred heroes who withstood him in battle were killed by Karna.

sn: अविषह्यं ततो दृष्ट्वा राधेयं युधि योधिनः। भीमसेनमुपागच्छन् कर्णबाणप्रपीडिताः॥
en: Thereupon seeing the son of Radha irrepressible in battle all those warriors, assailed by Karna's shafts, approached Bhimasena.

sn: रथनीकं विदार्यैव शरजालैरनेकधा। कर्ण एकरथेनैव युधिष्ठिरमुपाद्रवत्॥ सेनानिवेशमार्छन्त मार्गणैः क्षतविक्षतम्। यमयोर्मध्यगं वीरं शनैर्यान्तं विचेतसम्॥
en: Dispersing that car-force with his arrows Karna, in a chariot, pursued the heroic Yudhishthira, who, then wounded with arrows and almost unconscious, slowly proceeding towards encampment between the twins.
