sn: समासाद्य तु राजानं दुर्योधनहितेप्सया। सूतपुत्रस्त्रिभिस्तीक्ष्णैर्विव्याध परमेषुभिः॥ तथैव राजा राधेयं प्रत्यविध्यत् स्तनान्तरे। शरैस्त्रिभिश्च यन्तारं चतुर्भिश्चतुरो हयान्॥
en: Approaching the king, the car-warrior's son, with a desire to do good to Duryodhana, struck him with three highly powerful sharpened arrow, his charioteer with three and his horses with four. was

sn: चक्ररक्षौ तु पार्थस्य माद्रीपुत्रौ परंतपौ। तावप्यधावतां कर्ण राजानं मा वधीरिति॥
en: The two sons of Madri protected the sides of Yudhishthira and then they ran towards Karna so that he might not kill the king.

sn: तौ पृथक् शरवर्षाभ्यां राधेयमभ्यवर्षताम्। नकुलः सहदेवश्च परमं यत्नमास्थितौ॥
en: Then the highly careful Nakula and Sahadeva severally covered Karna with a downpour of arrows.

sn: तथैव तौ प्रत्यविध्यत् सूतपुत्रःप्रतापवान्। भल्लाभ्यां शितधाराभ्यां महात्मानावरिंदमौ॥
en: Then his highly powerful son of the charioteer struck those high-souled and victorious heroes with sharpened darts.

sn: दन्तवर्णांस्तु राधेयो निजघान मनोजवान्। युधिष्ठिरस्य संग्रामे कालवालान् हयोत्तमान्॥
en: Then in the battle Radha's son killed Yudhishthira's most excellent horses white as the teeth, quick-coursing like the mind and having black tails.

sn: ततोऽपरेण भल्लेन शिरस्त्राणमपातयत्। कौन्तेयस्य महेष्वासः प्रहसन्निव सूतजः॥
en: The as if smiling the charioteer's son, a great bowman himself, struck down with another Bhalla the crown of the son of Kunti.

sn: तथैव नकुलस्यापि हयान् हत्वा प्रतापवान्। ईषां धनुश्च चिच्छेद माद्रीपुत्रस्य धीमतः॥
en: Having killed then Nakula's horses the powerful (Karna) sundered the bow and arrows of the intelligent son of Madri.

sn: तौ हताश्वौ हतरथौ पाण्डवौ भृशविक्षतौ। भ्रातरावारुरुहतुः सहदेवरथं तदा॥
en: Then those sons of Pandu, the two brothers (Yudhishthira and Nakula) greatly wounded, got upon Sahadeva's car after their horses and car had been destroyed.

sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा मातुलस्तत्र विरथौ परवीरहा। अभ्यभाषत राधेयं मद्रराजोऽनुकम्पया॥
en: Seeing them deprived of their cars, their maternal uncle, the king of Madra and slayer of inimical heroes, out of compassion said to Karna.

sn: योद्धव्यमद्य पार्थेन फाल्गुनेन त्वया सह। किमर्थ धर्मराजेन युध्यसे भृशरोषितः॥
en: "You are to fight today with Pandu's son, Phalguna. Why do you, irate, then fight with the pious king Yudhishthira?

sn: क्षीणशस्त्रास्त्रकवचः क्षीणबाणो विबाणधिः। श्रान्तसारथिवाहश्च च्छन्नोऽस्त्रैररिभिस्तथा।॥ पार्थमासाद्य राधेय उपहास्यो भविष्यसि।
en: With your weapons exhausted, the coat of mail mutilated, arrows reduced and without quiver, with your horses and charioteer worn out with fatigue and yourself wounded with shafts by the enemies, when you will encounter Partha, O son of Radha, you will be a butt of ridicule.

sn: एवमुक्तोऽपि कर्णस्तु मद्रराजेन संयुगे॥ तथैव कर्णः संरब्धो युधिष्ठिरमताडयत्। शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः पराविध्य माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ॥ प्रहस्य समरे कर्णश्चकार विमुखं शरैः।
en: Although accosted thus by the king of Madra in the battle-field, still Karna, worked up with anger, pursued Yudhishthira. Having wounded then greatly with sharpened arrows the sons begotten on Madri by Pandu, Karna smiling made (the king) turn his face with arrows in battle.

sn: ततः शल्यः प्रहस्येदं कर्ण पुनरुवाच ह॥ रथस्थमतिसंरब्धं युधिष्ठिरवधे धृतम्।
en: Thereupon, Shalya, smiling again said to Karna, who was on the car, worked up with anger and bent upon killing Yudhishthira.

sn: यदर्थ धार्तराष्टैण सततं मानितो भवान्॥ तं पार्थ जहि राधेय किं ते हत्वा युधिष्ठिरम्।
en: "O son of Radha, leaving aside Partha, for whom you are always honored by the son of Dhritarashtra, what will you reap by killing Yudhishthira?

sn: शङ्खयोर्ध्यायतोः शब्दः सुमहाने कृष्णयोः॥ श्रूयते चापघोषोऽयं प्रावृषीवाम्बुदस्य ह।
en: Here is the great blare of the conchs blown by the two Krishnas. And here is being heard the twang of his bow like the muttering of clouds in the rainy season.

sn: असौ निघ्नन् रथोदारानर्जुनः शरवृष्टिभिः॥ सर्वा ग्रसति नः सेनां कर्ण पश्यैनमाहवे।
en: Behold O Karna, having slain all our carwarriors in battle with a net work of arrows, Arjuna is devouring our entire army.

sn: पृष्ठरक्षौ च शूरस्य युधामन्युत्तमौजसौ॥ उत्तरं चास्य वै शूरश्चक्रं रक्षति सात्यकिः। धृष्टद्युम्नस्तथा चास्य चक्रं रक्षति दक्षिणम्॥
en: The rear of the hero is being protected Yudhamanyu and Uttamajasa. And Satyaki is protecting his wheel on the north. Dhristadyumna is guarding his wheel in the south.

sn: भीमसेनश्च वै राज्ञा धार्तराष्ट्रेण युध्यते। यथा न हन्यात्तं भीमः सर्वेषां नोऽद्य पश्यताम्॥ तथा राधेय क्रियतां राजा मुच्येत नो यथा।
en: Bhimasena is fighting with the king Duryodhana. Look to it today, O Karna, so that Bhima may not kill the king in our very presence and he may escape him.

sn: पश्यैनं भीमसेनेन ग्रस्तमाहवशोभिनम्॥ यदि त्वासाद्य मुच्येत विस्मयः सुमहान् भवेत्।
en: Behold he has been overpowered by Bhimasena, a beauty of the battle field. It will be a great wonder if you can release him.

sn: परित्राोनमभ्येत्य संशयं परमं गतम्॥ किं नु माद्रीसुतौ हत्वा राजानं च युधिष्ठिरम्।
en: Go there and rescue the king for he has been overtaken by a great danger. What will you gain by killing the two sons of Madra and the king Yudhishthira?

sn: इति शल्यवचः श्रुत्वा राधेयः पृथिवीपते॥ दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनं चैव भीमग्रस्तं महाहवे। राजगृद्धी भृशं चैव शल्यवाक्यप्रचोदितः॥ अजातशत्रुमुत्सृज्य माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ। तव पुत्रं परित्रातुमभ्यधावत वीर्यवान्।॥
en: Hearing the words of the king Shalya and seeing Duryodhana overpowered by Bhima in that great battle, Karna, worked up with the words of Shalya and anxious to save the king, left the king Yudhishthira who has no enemies and the two sons of Madri and hurried on for rescuing your son.

sn: मद्रराजप्रणुदितैरश्वैराकाशगैरिव। गते कर्णे तु कौन्तेयः पाण्डुपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ अपायाजवनैरश्वैः सहदेवश्च मारिष।
en: O king, After Karna's departure, Yudhishthira, begotten by Pandu of Kunti left the battle-field, born by the quick-coursing horses of Sahadeva.

sn: ताभ्यां स सहितस्तूर्णं वीडन्निव नरेश्वरः॥ प्राप्य सेनानिवेशं त मार्गणैः क्षतविक्षतः अवतीर्णो रथातूर्णमाविशच्छयनं शुभम्॥
en: Guarded by the twins the king quickly returned to his camp in shame. His body was covered with wounds of arrows. He got down from the car and sat on his best seat.

sn: अपनीतशल्यः सुभृशं हृच्छल्याभिनिपीडितः। सोऽब्रवीभ्रातरौ राजा माद्रीपुत्रौ महारथौ॥
en: The arrows were then taken out of his person and the king, filled with sorrow, said to his twin brothers the great car-warriors, the powerful sons of Madri.

sn: अनीकं भीमसेनस्य पाण्डवावाशु गच्छताम्। जीमूत इव नद॑स्तु युध्यते स वृकोदरः॥
en: O sons of Pandu! Both of you should join immediately the army where Bhimasena is stood. Bhimasena is fighting there with challenge as loud as the cloud.

sn: ततोऽन्यं रथमास्थाय नकुलो रथपुङ्गवः। सहदेवश्च तेजस्वी भ्रातरौ शत्रुकर्षणौ॥ तुरगैरर्य्यरहोभिर्यात्वा भीमस्य शुष्मिणौ। अनीकैः सहितौ तत्र भ्रातरौ समवस्थितौ॥
en: Nakula, the great chariot holder and valorous Sahadeva just then rode of their chariots and joined Bhimasena immediately. They began fighting after joining the army led by Bhimasena.

sn: संजय उवाच द्रौणिस्तु रथवंशेन महता परिवारितः। अपतत्सहसा राजन् यत्र पार्थो व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon surrounded be a mighty carforce Drona's son appeared, all on a sudden O king, where Pritha's son was.

sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा शूरः शौरिसहायवान्। दधार सहसा पार्थो वेलेव मकरालयम्॥
en: Like a bank containing ocean Pritha's heroic son, assisted by Shouri, all on a sudden, encountered him.

sn: ततःक्रुद्धो महाराज द्रोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। अर्जुनं वासुदेवं च छादयामास सायकैः॥
en: Thereupon filled with anger, O monarch, the highly powerful son of Drona covered Arjuna and Krishna with arrows.

sn: अवस्छन्नौ ततः कष्णै दृष्ट्वा तत्र महारथाः। विस्मयं परमं गत्वा प्रेक्षन्त कुरवस्तदा॥
en: Beholding those two Krishnas covered with arrows the mighty car-warriors of the Pandava and Kuru armies, filled with great wonder, looked at them.

sn: अर्जुनस्तु ततो दिव्यमस्त्रं चक्रे हसन्निव। तदस्त्रं वारयामास ब्राह्मणो युधि भारत॥
en: Thereupon as if smiling Arjuna created a celestial weapon while, ( descendant of Bharata, the Brahmana baffled in battle.

sn: यद् यद्धि व्याक्षिपद युद्धे पाण्डवोऽस्त्रजिघांसया। तत् तदस्त्रं महेष्वासो द्रोणपुत्रो व्यसातयत्॥
en: Whatever weapon that the Pandava discharged in battle for killing the son of Drona, the great bowman made useless.

sn: अस्त्रयुद्धे ततो राजन् वर्तमाने महाभये। अपश्याम रणे द्रौणि व्यात्ताननमिवान्तकम्॥
en: Then, O king, a great encounter of weapons took place in that great battle when we saw the son of Drona like Death himself with widening mouth.

sn: स दिशः प्रादिशश्चैव च्छादयित्वा ह्यजिह्यगैः। वासुदेवं त्रिभिर्बाणैरविध्यद् दक्षिणे भुजे॥
en: Having filled all the quarters and directions with straight arrow he sundered Krishna's right arm with three arrows.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनो हयान् हत्वा सर्वांस्तस्य महात्मनः। चकार समरे भूमि शोणितौघतरङ्गिणीम्ः॥
en: Thereupon killing all the horses of the highsouled one Arjuna created, in the battle-field, a dreadful stream of blood, carrying away all to the other region.

sn: सर्वलोकवहां रौद्रां परलोकवहां नदीम्। सस्थान् रथिनः सर्वान् पार्थचापच्युतैः शरैः॥ द्रौणेरपहतान् संख्ये ददृशुः स च तां तथा। प्रावर्तयन्महाघोरां नदी परवहां तदा॥
en: That dreadful blood river was flowing towards. The another world and swaying with its course all people there. All people present there saw all warriors holding chariots under lead of Ashvatthama beheaded with the arrows shot by Arjuna. Ashvatthama himself took notice of that scenario. He also had flown a river floating people to another world at that time under the sheer grip of anger.

sn: तयोस्तु व्याकुले युद्धे द्रौणेः पार्थस्य दारुणे। अमर्यादं योधयन्तः पर्यधावन्त पृष्ठतः॥
en: In that agitating and dreadful encounter between Drona's son and Partha the warriors rushed towards one another without any consideration whatever.

sn: रथैर्हताश्वसूतैश्च हतारोहैश्च वाजिभिः। द्विरदैश्च हतारोहैर्महामात्रैर्हतद्विपैः॥ पार्थेन समरे राजन् कृतो घोरो जनक्षयः। निहता रथिनः पेतुः पार्थचापच्युतैः शरैः॥
en: O king, the horses and charioteers of cars were killed the cavalry were destroyed and the riders of elephants were slain. Thus a dreadful slaughter of animals was carried on by Partha in that battle. Then the car-warriors fell down slain by arrows shot off Partha's bow.

sn: हयाश्च पर्यधावन्त मुक्तयोक्त्रास्ततस्ततः। तद् दृष्ट्वा कर्म पार्थस्य द्रौणिराहवशोभिनः॥ अर्जुनं जयतां श्रेष्ठं त्वरितोऽभ्येत्य वीर्यवान्। विधुन्बानो महचापं कार्तस्वरविभूषितम्॥ अवाकिरत्ततो द्रौणिः समन्तान्निशितैः शरैः।
en: And the horses, with their trappings destroyed ran about hither and thither. Witnessing these feats of Partha, beautifying the battle-field the powerful son of Drona speedily encountered that foremost of the victorious, quivered his his dreadful, gold bedecked bow and struck him on all sides with innumerable sharpened arrows.

sn: भूयोऽर्जुनं महाराज द्रौणिरायम्य पत्रिणा॥ वक्षोदेशेभृशं पार्थं ताडयामास निर्दयम्।
en: O monarch, Drouni again ruthlessly wounded Arjuna on the breast with a winged arrow.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो रणे तेन द्रोणपुत्रेण भारत॥ गाण्डीवधन्वा प्रसभं शरवर्षेरुदारधीः। संछाद्य समरे द्रौणिं चिच्छेदास्य च कार्मुकम्॥
en: O son of Bharata being greatly wounded in battle by that son of Drona he, with force, took up his Gandiva bow. Then the highly intelligent hero covered Drona's son with a downpour of arrows and cut-off his bowstring.

sn: स छिन्नधन्वा परिघं वज्रस्पर्शसमं युधि। आदाय चिक्षेप तदा द्रोणपुत्रः किरीटिने॥
en: Having his bow thus snapped Drona's son took up a sword, like unto a thunderbolt and hurled it at Arjuna.

sn: तमापतन्तं परिधं जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृतम्। चिच्छेद सहसा राजन् प्रहसन्निव पाण्डवः॥
en: O king, as if smiling. Arjuna all on a sudden cut-off that gold-gilded sword that was about to fall on him.

sn: स पपात तदा भूमौ निकृत्यः पार्थसायकैः। विकीर्ण: पर्वतो राजन् यथा वज्रेण ताडितः॥
en: Sundered by parts, arrows it fell down on earth like a mountain shattered by (Indra's) thunder-bolt.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज द्रोणपुत्रो महारथः। ऐन्द्रेण चास्त्रवेगेन बीभत्सुं समवाकिरत्॥
en: Thereupon irate, the mighty car-warrior son of Drona, covered fully Vibhatsu with weapons glinted him by Indra.

sn: तस्येन्द्रजप्लावततं समीक्ष्य पार्थो राजन् गाण्डिवमाददे सः। ऐन्द्रं जालं प्रत्यहरत् तरस्वी वरास्त्रमादाय महेन्द्रसृष्टम्॥
en: Beholding those weapons of Indra about to fall on him Partha took up his Gandiva and speedily baffled them with an arrow created for him by Vasava.

sn: विदार्य तज्जालमथेन्द्रमुक्तं पार्थस्ततो द्रौणिरथं क्षणेना प्रच्छादयामास ततोऽभ्युपेत्य द्रौणिस्तदा पार्थशराभिभूतः॥ विगाह्य तां पाण्डवबाणवृष्टिं शरैः परं नाम ततः प्रकाश्य। शतेन कृष्णं सहसाभ्यविद्ध्यत् त्रिभिः शतैरर्जुनं क्षुद्रकाणाम्॥
en: Then cutting off that net-work of Indra's weapon Partha soon covered the car of Drona's son. Assailed by Arjuna's arrows Drouni, encountering the former and cutting through the downpour of Pandava's arrows, called to his aid a powerful weapon and all on a sudden wounded Krishna with a hundred arrows and Arjuna with three hundred small arrows.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनः सायकानां शतेन गुरोः सुतं मर्मसु निर्बिभेद। मवाकिरत् पश्यतां तावकानाम्॥
en: Arjuna then pierced the sensitive organs of the son of preceptor (Ashvatthama) through expert use of his arrows and shot a volley of arrows in presence of your sons; on his horses, charioteers, bow and the string stretched on bow.

sn: स विद्ध्वा मर्मसु द्रौणि पाण्डवः परवीरहा। सारथिं चास्य भल्लेन रथनीडादपातयत्॥
en: Pandava, the slayer of inimical heroes, struck down his driver from his car with a dart.

sn: स संगृह्य स्वयं वाहान् कृष्णौ प्राच्छादयच्छरैः। तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम द्रौणेराशु पराक्रमम्॥ प्रायच्छत्तुरगान् यच्च फाल्गुनं चाप्ययोधयत्। यदस्य समरे राजन् सर्वे योधा अपूजयन्॥
en: Then himself taking up the reins of horses Drona's son covered Krishna and Arjuna with arrows. He saw a wonderful power in him then. He simultaneously drove his horses and fought with Phalguna. It was spoken highly of by all the warriors in battle, O king.

sn: तत: प्रहस्य बीभत्सुद्रौणपुत्रस्य संयुगे। क्षिप्रं रश्मीनताश्वानां क्षुरप्रैश्चिच्छिदे जयः॥
en: Then smiling a little, Vibhatsu also named Jaya speedily cut-off the rein of Drouni's horses in battle with a razor-like shaft.

sn: प्राद्रवतंस्तुरगास्ते तु शरवेगप्रपीडिताः। ततोऽभून्निनदो घोरस्तव सैन्यस्य भारत॥
en: Assailed with weapons the horses ran away on all sides. There then took place a great havoc of your soldiers.

sn: पाण्डवास्तु जयं लब्वा तव सैन्यं समाद्रवन्। समन्तान्निशितान् बाणान् विमुञ्चन्तो जयैषिणः॥
en: Having thus accomplished victory the Pandavas, desirous of achieving (further) success, pursued your soldiers, on all sides, making a discharge of arrows.

sn: पाण्डवैस्तु महाराज धार्तराष्ट्री महाचमूः। पुनः पुनरथो वीरैः संयुगे जितकाशिभिः॥
en: Your great army was again and again routed by the Pandava warriors desirous of victory.

sn: पश्यतां ते महाराज पुत्राणां चित्रयोधिनाम्। शकुनेः सौबलेयस्य कर्णस्य च विशाम्पते॥
en: Thereupon in the very presence of your sons, O king, conversant with diverse modes of war-fare, of Subala's son Shakuni and Karna.

sn: वार्यमाणा महासेना पुत्रैस्तव जनेश्वरः। न चातिष्ठत संग्रामे पीड्यमाना समन्ततः॥
en: Although prevented, O king, by your sons that great army assailed on all sides did not stop in the battle-field.

sn: ततो योधैर्महाराज पलायद्भिः समन्ततः। अभवद् व्याकुलं भीतं पुत्राणां ते महद् बलम्॥
en: The warriors taking to their heels on all sides in numbers a great confusion took place in the vast terror-stricken army of your son.

sn: तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति च तत: सूतपुत्रस्य जल्पतः। नावतिष्ठति सा सेना वध्यामाना महात्मभिः॥
en: Karna then exclaimed-"Wait wait". But your army, slain by many great warriors, did not wait in the battle-field.

sn: अथोत्क्रुष्टं महाराज पाण्डवैर्जितकाशिभिः। धार्तराष्ट्रबलं दृष्ट्वा विद्रुतं वै समन्ततः॥
en: Beholding the army of Duryodhana, thus routed on all sides, the Pandavas, filled with the desire of victory, sent up loud war-cries.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः कर्णमब्रवीत् प्रणयादिव। पश्य कर्णं महासेना पञ्चालैरर्दिता भृशम्॥ त्वयि तिष्ठति संत्रासात् पलायनपरायणा। एतज्ज्ञात्वा महाबाहो कुरु प्राप्तमरिंदम॥
en: Duryodhana then lovingly said Karna-"See, O Karna, how our army, greatly assailed by the Pandava, is flying on all sides, although you are present here. O repressor of foes, do what you think proper now.

sn: सहस्राणि च योधानां त्वामेव पुरुषोत्तम। क्रोशन्ति समरे वीर द्राव्यमाणानि पाण्डवैः॥
en: Routed by the Pandavas, thousands of our soldiers are calling after you only.

sn: एतच्छुत्वापि राधेयो दुर्योधनवचो महान्। मद्रराजमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Hearing those weighty words of Duryodhana, Karna, as if smiling, said to the Madra king.

sn: पश्य मे भुजयोर्वीर्यमस्त्राणं च जनेश्वर। अद्यहन्मि रणे सर्वान पञ्चालन् पाण्डुभिः सह।॥ वाहयाश्वान् नरव्याघ्र भद्रेणैव न संशयः।
en: Behold, O king, the strength of my arms and weapons. I will kill today in battle all the Panchalas and Pandavas. Drive my car, O best of men and every thing will be as I have said.”

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥ प्रगृह्य विजयं वीरो धनुः श्रेष्ठं पुरातनम्। सज्यं कृत्वा महाराज संगृह्य च पुनः पुनः॥ संनिवार्य च योधान् स सत्येन शपथेन च। प्रायोजयदमेयात्मा भार्गवास्त्रं महाबलः॥
en: Having said this, O monarch, the charioteer's son, highly powerful as he was, took up his old victorious bow Vijaya the best of its kind and rubbing again and again its string set it on the bow. Thereupon having assured his army and commanded them to wait in the battle-field, the powerful and highly energetic Karna set Bhargava weapons to his bow-string.

sn: ततो राजन् सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च। कोटिशश्च शरास्तीक्ष्ण निरगच्छन् महामृधे॥
en: There came out in a stream, O king, millions of sharp arrows in that mighty encounter.

sn: ज्वलितैस्तैः शरै।रैः कङ्कबहिणवाजितैः। संछन्ना पाण्डवी सेना न प्राज्ञायत किञ्चन॥
en: Covered fully with those shining and dreadful Kanka and peacock-feathered arrows the Pandava soldiers could see nothing in the battle-field.

sn: हाहाकारो महानासीत् पञ्चालानां विशाम्पते। पीडितानां बलवता भार्गवास्त्रेण संयुगे॥
en: Assailed by the powerful Bhargava weapon in that battle, O king, Panchalas set up loud lamentations.

sn: निपतद्भिर्गजै राजन्नश्चैश्चापि सहस्रशः। रथैश्चापि नरव्याघ्र नरैश्चैव समन्ततः॥ प्राकम्पत मही राजन् निहतैस्तैः समन्ततः। व्याकुलं सर्वमभवत् पाण्डवानां महद् बलम्॥
en: And O king, thousands of elephants, horses, cars and men falling on all sides, the earth began to shake. The great army of the Pandavas quivered from one end to the other.

sn: कर्णस्त्वेको युधां श्रेष्ठो विधूम इव पावकः। दहशत्रून् नरव्याघ्र शुशुभे स परंतपः॥
en: In the meantime while killing his enemies, that foremost of men the great warrior Karna, even destroying his foes, shone like smokeless fire.

sn: ते वध्यमानां कर्णेन पञ्चालाश्चेदिभिः सह। तत्र तत्र व्यमुह्यन्त वनदाहे यथा द्विपाः॥
en: Massacred then by Karna, the Panchalas and Chedis lost their consciousness in the battle-field like elephants when a forest fire rages on.

sn: चुक्रुशुश्च नरव्याघ्र यथा व्याघ्रा नरोत्तमाः। तेषा तु क्रोशतामासीद् भीतानां रणमूर्धनि॥ धावतां च ततो राजंस्त्रस्तानां च समन्ततः। आर्तनादो महांस्तत्र भूतानामिव सम्ल्वे॥
en: The leading warriors sent up war-cries roaring like tigers. Like animals at the hour of universal dissolution the soldiers, terrorstricken and running wildly about in the battlefield,set-up loud cries of lamentation.

sn: वध्यमानांस्तु तान् दृष्ट्वा सूतपुत्रेण मारिष। वित्रेसुः सर्वभूतानि तिर्यग्योनिगतान्यपि॥
en: Seeing them thus slaughtered by the charioteer's son, all creatures, beasts and birds, were terrorised.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे सूतपुत्रेण संजयाः। अर्जुनं वासुदेवं च क्रोशन्ति च मुहुर्महुः॥ प्रेतराजपुरे यद्वत प्रेतराजं विचेतसः।
en: As the spirits call upon the Regent of Death to save them, so the Srinjayas, massacred by Karna, repeatedly prayed to Arjuna and Vasudeva's son to save them.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु निनदं तेषां वध्यता कर्णसायकैः॥ अथाब्रवीद् वासुदेवं कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः। भार्गवास्त्रं महाघोरं दृष्ट्वा तत्र समीरितम्॥
en: Beholding there the discharge of the dreadful Bhargava weapon and hearing the cries of his men slaughtered by Karna, with arrows Kunti's son Dhananjaya said to Krishna. can

sn: पश्य कुष्ण महाबाहो भार्गवास्त्रस्य विक्रमम्। नैतदस्त्रं हि समरे शक्यं हन्तुं कथञ्चन॥
en: Beholding there the discharge of the dreadful Bhargava weapon. No one withstand it in battle.

sn: सूतपुत्रं च संरब्धं पश्य कृष्ण महारणे। अन्तकप्रतिमं वीर्ये कुर्वाणं कर्म दारुणम्॥
en: Behold again in this great encounter O Krishna, the great son of a charioteer, resembling Death himself in power and performing a dreadful feat.

sn: अभीक्ष्णं चोदयन्नश्वान् प्रेक्षते मां मुहुर्मुहुः। न च पश्यामि समरे कर्णं प्रति पलायितुम्॥
en: Repeatedly urging on his horses he is looking at me. I will not be able to tear me away from Karna in battle.

sn: जीवन् प्राप्नोति पुरुषः संख्ये जयपराजयौ। मृतस्य तु हृषीकेश भङ्ग एव कुतो जयः॥
en: If a man survives he either meets with success or defeat in battle. To one dead, O Hrishikesh, death itself is a victory.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु पार्थेन कृष्णो मतिमतां वरम्। धनंजयमुवाचेदं प्राप्तकालमरिंदमम्॥
en: Thus addressed by Partha, Krishna, the subduer of his enemies, said to Dhananjaya, the foremost of the wise, the following suitable to the occasion.

sn: कर्णेनहि दृढं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रः परिक्षितः। तं दृष्ट्वाऽऽश्वास्य च पुनः कर्णं पार्थ वधिष्यसि॥
en: The royal son of Kunti has been greatly wounded by Karna. Seeing him first you will afterwards kill Karna.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा पुनः प्रायाद् द्रष्टुमिच्छन् युधिष्ठिरम्। श्रमेण ग्राहयिष्यंश्च युद्धे कर्ण विशाम्पते॥
en: Then Janardana proceeded to Yudhishthira, thinking, O king, that Karna, in the meantime, would be worn our with fatigue in battle.

sn: ततो धनंजयो द्रष्टुं राजानं बाणपीडितम्। रथेन प्रययौ क्षिप्रं संग्रामात् केशवाज्ञया॥
en: see Himself too being desirous of seeing the king thus wounded with arrows, Dhananjaya, at the bidding of Keshava, left the battle and went on his car.

sn: गच्छन्नेव तु कौन्तेयो धर्मराजदिदृक्षया। सैन्यमालोकयामास नापश्यत् तत्रचाग्रजम्॥ युद्धं कृत्वा तु कौन्तेयो द्रोणपुत्रेण भारत। दुःसह वज्रिणा संख्ये पराजित्य गुरोः सुतम्॥
en: O Bharata! Arjuna, the son of Kunti subsequent to the bitter defeat he gave to the son of preceptor, (Ashvatthama) tough to face for Indra, the holder of thunderbolt, threw a cursory eye on the whole army while he was leaving from there to see Dharmaraja. However, he could not see his elder brother there.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: संजय उवाच द्रौणि पराजित्य ततोऽग्रधन्वा कृत्वा महद् दुष्करं शूरकर्म। आलोकयामास ततः स्वसैन्यं धनंजयः शत्रुभिरप्रधृष्यः॥
en: Sanjaya said Having vanquished Drona's son and performed a highly difficult and heroic task, Dhananjaya, ever irrepressible to his enemies, with a bow ready in his hands, eyed his own army.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: स युध्यमानान् पृतनामुखस्थान् शूरः शूरान् हर्षयन् सव्यसाची। पूर्वप्रहारैर्मथितान् प्रशंसन् स्थिरांश्चकारत्मरथाननीके॥
en: Cheering up the warriors that were still fighting at the heads of their respective detachments and speaking highly of their former successes Arjuna enjoined his carwarriors to be at their posts.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: अपश्यमानस्तु किरीटमाली युधिष्ठिरं भ्रातरमाजमीढम्। उवाच भीमं तरसाभ्युपेत्य राज्ञः प्रवृत्तिं त्विह कुत्र राजा॥
en: Not finding his brother Yudhishthira, a descendant of Ajamida, Arjuna quickly approached Bhima and inquired of the king's whereabouts, saying “Where is the king?"

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: भीमसेन उवाच अपयात इतो राजा धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। कर्मबाणाभितप्ताङ्गो यदि जीवेत् कथञ्चन्॥
en: Bhima said Wounded with Karna's arrows the pious king Yudhishthira had gone away from here. I doubt if he still survives.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: अर्जुन उवाच तस्माद् भवाशीघ्रमितः प्रयातु राज्ञः प्रवृत्यै कुरुसत्तमस्य। नूनं स विद्धोनऽतिभृशं पृषत्कैः कर्णेन राजा शिबिरं गतोऽसौ॥
en: Arjuna said For this very reason proceed you quickly from here and bring the news of the king, that foremost of Kurus. Forsooth, greatly wounded with Karna's arrows the king has gone to his camp.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: द्रोणेन विद्धोऽतिभृशं तरस्वी। तस्थौ स तत्रापि जयप्रतीक्षो द्रोणोऽपियावन्न हत: किलासीत्॥
en: Although struck greatly with sharpened arrows by Drona's son the king still waited in the battle-field, desirous of victory, until Drona was slain.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: स संशयं गमितः पाण्डवाग्र्यः संख्येऽद्य कर्णेन महानुभावः। ज्ञातुं प्रयाह्यासु तमद्य भीम स्थास्याम्यहं शत्रुगणान् निरुद्धय॥
en: The high-minded chief of Pandus, undoubtedly met with peril in battle through Karna. go quickly, Bhima and learn of his condition. I will wait here and oppose the enemy.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: भीमसेन उवाच त्वमेव जानाहिह महानुभाव राज्ञः प्रवृत्तिं भरतर्षभस्य। अहं हि यद्यर्जुन याम्यमित्रा वदन्ति मां भीत इति प्रवीराः॥
en: Bhima said O illustrious and leading descendant of Bharata, better go yourself and enquire after the king, If I go, O Arjuna, the leading warriors will explain that I am rightened in battle.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: ततोऽब्रवीदर्जुनो भीमसेनं संशप्तकाः प्रत्यनीकं स्थिता मे। मितोऽपयातुं रिपुसङ्घगोष्ठात्॥
en: Then Arjuna said to Bhimasena-"The Samsaptakas are before my army, without killing these my enemies I cannot leave the post."

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: अथाब्रवीदर्जुनं भीमसेनः स्ववीर्यमासाद्य कुरुप्रवीर। संशप्तकान् प्रतियोत्स्यामि संख्ये सर्वानहं याहि धनंजय त्वम्॥
en: Bhima replied then to Arjuna-"O foremost of Kurus, with the aid of my own power, I will encounter the Samsaptakas in battle, you better go yourself, O Dhananjaya.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: संजय उवाच तद् भीमसेनस्य वचो निशम्य सुदुष्करं भ्रातुरमित्रमध्ये। संशप्तकानीकमसामेकः सुदुष्करं धारयामीति पार्थः॥ उवाच नारायणमप्रमेय कपिध्वजः सत्यपराक्रमस्य। स्तदाहवे सत्यवतो महात्मा। द्रष्टुं कुरुश्रेष्ठमभिप्रयास्यन् प्रोवाच वृष्णिप्रवरं तदानीम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Arjuna reported the promise made by Bhimasena, his brother that he shall face the whole army of chivalrous Samsaptakas alone to Sri Krishna, the god incarnated of Narayana and descendant of Vrishni clan. It was really very tough to materialise. Hence, he immediately inclined to see Yudhishthira for consult. In the meantime, he said to lord Krishna-

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: अर्जुन उवाच चोदयाश्वान् हृषीकेश विहायैतद् बलार्णवम्। अजातशत्रु राजानं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि केशव॥
en: Arjuna said “Leave this ocean-like army, O Hrishikesha and drive the horses. I wish to see, OKeshava, the king who has no enemies."

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: संजय उवाच ततो हयान् सर्वदाशार्हमुख्यः प्रचोदयन् भीममुवाच चेदम्। नैतचित्रं तव कर्माद्य भीम यास्माम्यहं पार्थारिसंघान्॥
en: While he was about to drive the horses, the foremost of Dasharhas said to Bhima-"If it nothing wonder for you, O Bhima. Kill the enemies of Partha.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: ततो ययौ हृषीकेश यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः। शीघ्रच्छीघ्रतरं राजन् वीजिभिर्गरुडोपमैः॥
en: Thereupon Hrishikesha drove quickly where Yudhishthira was. Quickly was he borne there, O king, by the horses resembling Garuda himself.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: प्रत्यनीके व्यवस्थाप्य भीमसेनमरिंदमम्। संदिश्य चैतं राजेन्द्र युद्धं प्रति वृकोदरम्॥ ततस्तु गत्वा पुरुषप्रवीरौ राजानमासाद्य शयानमेकम्। रथादुभौ प्रत्यवरुद्य तस्माद् ववन्तुर्धर्मराजस्य पादौ॥
en: He had left there Bhimasena, the slayer of his enemies, O king, then driving in their car those two heroes approached the king who was lying alone on his bed. They got down from the car and saluted the feet of the righteous Yudhishthira.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा पुरुष व्याघ्रं क्षेमिणं पुरुर्षभम्। मुदाभ्युपगतौ कृष्णावश्विनाविव वासवम्॥ तावभ्यनन्दद् राजापि विवस्वानविनाविव। हते महासुरे जम्भे शक्रविष्णू यथा गुरुः॥
en: Seeing that foremost of men safe and sound the two Krishnas were filled with delight as the two Ashvins are on seeing Indra. As Vivasvan congratulated the two Asvinis, as Vrihaspati congratulated Indra and Vishnu after they had killed the powerful Asura Jambha so the king congratulated them both.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: मन्यमानो हतं कर्णं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। हर्षगद्गदया वाचा प्रीतः प्राह परंतपः॥
en: Thinking that Karna had been killed the virtuous king was delighted and he then addressed them thus, with his with his accents suppressed with joy.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: संजय उवाच अथोपयातौ पृथुलोहिताक्षौ शरचिताङ्गौ रुधिरप्रदिग्धौ। समीक्ष्य सेनाग्रनरप्रवीरौ युधिष्ठिरो वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥
en: Sanjaya said Sri Krishna and Arjuna, the fore-front fighter in battle, the eminent warrior, having huge and red eyes when approached closer, the arrows stuck in their all organs of body were seen. They soaked in blood. Yudhishthira, on seeing them, started talking in following manner-

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: महासत्त्वौ हि तौ दृष्ट्वा सहितौ केशवार्जुनौ। हतमाधिरथिं मेने संख्ये गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: Having seen the mightiest Sri Krishna and Arjuna came together, he was conformed in mind that Arjuna, the holder of Gandiva has were killed Karna, the son of charioteer in the battlefield.

description: The arrival of Krishna and Arjuna to Yudhishthira
sn: तावभ्यनन्दत् कौन्तयेः साम्ना परमवल्गुना। स्मितपूर्वममित्रघ्नं पूजयन् भरतर्षभ॥
en: O son of Kunti! Owing to all these facts, I am curious enough to listen from you in prolix, the episode of Karna's slaughter by you. So safely. Tell me all without missing minutest information.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच स्वागतं देवकीमातः स्वागतं ते धनंजय। प्रियं मे दर्शनं गाढं युवयोरच्युतार्जुनौ॥
en: Yudhishthira said Welcome to you, Devaki's son and Dhananjaya, highly agreeable to me is the pleasure of you too, O Arjuna, O Achyuta.

sn: अक्षताभ्यामरिष्टाभ्यां हतः कर्णो महारथः। आशीविषसमं युद्धे सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम्॥
en: Thought yourselves are not wounded by your enemies, you two, who are his enemies, have killed the mighty Karna.

sn: अग्रगं धार्तराष्ट्राणां सर्वेषां शर्म वर्म च। रक्षितं वृषसेन सुषेणेन च धन्विना॥
en: Who was like a deadly serpent in battle, an adept in all weapons, the leader of all the sons of Dhritarashtra, may the very warder of their armour and coats of mail;

sn: अनुज्ञातं महावीर्यं रामेणास्त्रे सुदुर्जयम्। अग्र्यं सर्वस्य लोकस्य रथिनं लोकविश्रुतम्॥
en: Who was protected by the great archers Vrishasena and Sushena; highly energetic, powerful and taught by Rama (himself) the use of arms;

sn: त्रातारं धार्तराष्ट्राणां गन्तारं वाहिनीमुखे। हन्तारं परसैन्यानाममित्रगणमर्दनम्॥
en: Who was the head of all the world and most celebrated car-warrior, who was the saviour of Dhritarashtra's sons and who led the van of the army;

sn: दुर्योधनसहिते युक्तमस्मदुःखाय चोद्यतम्। अप्रधृष्यं महायुद्धे देवैरपि सवासवैः॥
en: Who was the destroyer of others' armies and the oppressor of the enemies and was bent upon doing Duryodhana a good turn and afflicting us;

sn: अनलानिलयोस्तुल्यं तेजसा न बलेन च। पातालमिव गम्भीरं सुहृदां नन्दिवर्धनम्॥
en: Who was irrepressible even unto the gods headed by Vasava in a great battle and was like unto fire and wind in energy and strength;

sn: अन्तकं मम मित्राणां हत्वा कर्णं महामृधे। दिष्ट्या युवामनुप्राप्तौ जित्वासुरमिवामरौ॥
en: Who was unfathomable like the nether region and an increaser of the joy of friends, he was like Death incarnate to his enemies. By good luck, having slain that Karna in the great battle you come here like the immortals after vanquishing the demons.

sn: घोरं युद्धमदीनेन मया हृद्याच्युतार्जुनौ। कृतं तेनान्तकेनेव प्रजाः सर्वा जिघांसता॥
en: O Achyuta, O Arjuna, a great encounter took place today between myself setting forth my best energies and that hero who appeared like Death incarnate bent upon destroying all creatures.

sn: तेन केतुश्च मे छिन्नो हतौ च पार्णिसारथी। हतावाहस्तुश्चास्मि युयुधानस्य पश्यतः॥ धृष्टद्युम्नस्य यमयोर्वीरस्य च शिखण्डिनः। पश्यतां द्रौपदेयानां पञ्चालानां च सर्वशः॥
en: By him my standard was cut down, my two Parshni drivers were killed and I was made horseless and carless in the very presence of Yuyudhana, Dhristadyumna, the twins, the heroic Shikhandin the son of Drupada and all the Panchalas.

sn: एताञ्जित्वा महावीर्यः कर्णः शत्रुगणान् बहून्। जितवान् मां महाबाहो यतमानो महारणे॥
en: O you of mighty arms, having vanquished them all and many others of his enemies the highly powerful Karna, defeated me in that great battle although I tried my very best to withstand him.

sn: अभिसृत्य च मां युद्धे परुषाण्युक्तवान् बहु। तत्र तत्र युधां श्रेष्ठ परिभूय न संशयः॥
en: Forsooth pursuing me on all the sides and defeating all my allies in that battle that foremost of warriors addressed to me many harsh words.

sn: भीमसेनप्रभावात्तु यजीवामि धनंजय। बहुनात्र किमक्तेन नाहं तत् सोढुमुत्सहे॥
en: It is through Bhima's power that I do still survive, O Dhananjaya; what more need I say? The humiliation is indeed too much for me.

sn: त्रयोदशाहं वर्षाणि यस्माद् भीतो धनंजय। न स्म निद्रा लभे रात्रौ न चाहनि सुखं क्वचित्।। १५
en: O Dhananjaya, through fear of him, I have not slept in the night nor have I enjoyed comfort in the day for these thirteen years.

sn: तस्य द्वेषेण संयुक्तः परिदह्ये धनंजय। आत्मनो मरणे यातो वाध्रीणस इव द्विपः॥ तस्यायमगमत् कालश्चिन्तयानस्य मे चिरम्। कथं कर्णो मया शक्तो युद्धे क्षपयितुं भवेत्॥
en: O Dhananjaya, I am burning with hatred against him. Conscious of my days being numbered I avoided Karna, like the bird Vaddrinasa. I approached him as if bent on my own destruction. Awake or asleep I spent my days only in thinking how I would accomplish Karna's death.

sn: जाग्रत्स्वपुंश्च कौन्तेय कर्णमेव सदा ह्यहम्। पश्यामि तत्र तत्रैव कर्णभूतमिदं जगत्॥
en: Even while awake, O Arjuna, I see his illusion (of Karna) and it seems as if the whole universe is filled with Karna.

sn: यत्र यत्र हि गच्छामि कर्णाद् भीतो धनंजय। तत्र तत्र हि पश्यामि कर्णमेवाग्रतः स्थितम्॥
en: Wherever I go, O Dhananjaya, in fear of Karna, everywhere I see his image before me.

sn: सोऽहं तेनैव वीरेण समरेष्वपलायिना। सहयः सरथः पार्थ जित्वा जीवन् विसर्जितः॥
en: O Partha, with my horses and cars I was vanquished by Karna, who never retreats from the battle-field. He simply let me go with my life.

sn: को न मे जीवितेनार्थो राज्येनार्थो भवेत् पुनः। ममैवं विक्षतस्याद्य कर्णेनाहवशोभिना॥
en: Of what use is life and kingdom to me, since Karna, the beauty of the battle-field, has defied and ridiculed me.

sn: न प्राप्तपूर्वं यद् भीष्मात् कृपद्रोणाच संयुगे। तत् प्राप्तमद्य मे युद्धे सूतपुत्रान्महारथात्॥
en: I had never undergone such humiliation in battle even from Bhishma, Kripa, or Drona, as I have today at the hands of the son of Suta the mighty charioteer.

sn: स त्वां पृच्छामि कौन्तेय यथाद्य कुशलं तथा। तन्ममाचक्ष्व कात्स्नर्येन यथा कर्णो हतस्त्वया॥
en: Therefore it is that I ask you today, O son of Kunti, about your welfare. Relate to me in detail how you slew Karna today.

sn: शक्रतुल्यबलो युद्धे यमतुल्य: पराक्रमे। रामतुल्यस्तथास्त्रेण स कथं वै निषूदितः॥
en: He was in battle like Sakra himself and in prowess like Yama and like Rama in arins. How has he been killed then?

sn: महारथः समाख्यातः सर्वयुद्धविशारदः। धनुर्धराणां प्रवरः सर्वेषामेकपूरुषः॥
en: He was a mighty charioteer and wellknown for being an adept in all the forms of warfare, he was the foremost of archers and the leader of all.

sn: पूजितो धृतराष्ट्रेण सपुत्रेण महाबलः। त्वदर्थमेव राधेयः स कथं निहतस्त्वया॥
en: O prince, he was respected by Dhritarashtra himself as well as by his sons for you alone. How has then of Radha been killed by today?

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रो हि योधेषु सर्वेष्वेव सदार्जुन। तव मृत्युं रणे कर्णं मन्यते पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: O Arjuna, O foremost of men, in all the battles Karna was regarded by Dhritarashtra's sons as your death.

sn: स त्वया पुरुषव्याघ्र कथं युद्धे निषूदितः। तन्ममाचक्ष्व कौन्तेय यथा कर्णो हतस्त्वया॥
en: How have you then, O most powerful of men, killed him in battle? Describe to me, O son of Kunti, how Karna has been slain by you.

sn: युध्यमानस्य च शिरः पश्यतां सुहृदा हृतम्। त्वया पुरुषशार्दूल सिंहेनेव यथा रुरोः॥
en: How did you cut-off his head, O most mighty one, as a tiger pieces off the head of a Ruru deer, while he was fighting, even in presence of all his allies?

sn: यः पर्युपासीत् प्रदिशो दिशश्च त्वां सूतपुत्रः समरे परीप्सन्। दित्सुः कर्णः समरे हस्तिषगवं स हीदानी कङ्कपत्रैः सुतीक्ष्णैः॥ त्वया रणे निहतः सूतपुत्रः कचिच्छेते भूमितले दुरात्मा। प्रियुश्च मे परमो वै कृतोऽयं त्वया रणे सूतपुत्रं निहत्य॥
en: Does the wicked Karna lic today on the naked earth killed with your keen Kankafeathered arrows-Karna, the son of Suta, who used to search all the quarters for you and who had promised to give a car with six elephantine bulls to him who would point you out? Indeed by killing him in battle you have performed a work highly congenial to me.

sn: यः सर्वतः पर्यपतत्त्वदर्थे सदार्चितो गर्वितः सूतपुत्रः। स शूरमानी समरे समेत्य कचित्त्वया निहतः संयुगेऽसौ॥
en: How did you encounter and kill in battle that well-honored hero, that proud and haughty son of Suta who used to search you everywhere in the battle-field.

sn: रौक्मं वरं हस्तिगजाश्वयुक्तं रथं प्रदित्सुर्यः परेभ्यस्त्वदर्थे। सदा रणे स्पर्धते यः स पापः कचित्त्वया निहतस्तात युद्धे॥
en: Have you, O brother, really slain in battle the vicious scoundrel who was ever ready to challenge you and to give away to others a superb golden chariot along with bulls, steeds and elephants provided they could give him some clue to you?

sn: योऽसौ सदा शूरमदेन मत्तो विकत्थते संसदि कौरवाणाम्। प्रियोऽत्यर्थं तस्य सुयोधनस्य कञ्चित् सपापो निहतस्त्वसाध॥
en: Have you, indeed, slain that favourite of Suyodhana who, being elated with the pride of chivalry, ever used to indulge in selfglorification amidst the assembly of the Kurus?

sn: स्त्वप्रेषितैर्लोहिताङ्गैर्रिहहै। शेते स पापः सुविभिन्नगात्रः कच्चिद् भग्नौ धार्तराष्ट्रस्य बाहू॥
en: Does the scoundrel lie low on the battlefield today being mangled all over the body with long-ranging blood-besmeared shafts hurled by you from your bow. Could you break in twin the arms of Dhritarashtra's sons?

sn: योऽसौ सदा श्लाघते राजमध्ये दुर्योधनं हर्षयन् दर्पपूर्णः। अहं हन्ता फाल्गुनस्येति मोहात् कचिद्वचस्तस्य न वै तथा तत्॥
en: Could you baffle the foolish braggings he used to make amidst the assembly of kings simply to soothe Duryodhana, saying, I will kill Phalguna?

sn: नाहं पादौ धाविष्ये कदाचित् यावत् स्थितः पार्थ इत्यल्पबुद्धेः। व्रतं तस्यैत त् सर्वदा शक्रसूनो कच्चिन त्वया निहतः सोऽद्य कर्णः॥
en: Have you, O son of Indra, slain in today's battle the dull-headed Karna, the son Suta, who had taken an oath not to wash his feet till Partha breathed?

sn: योऽसौ कृष्णामब्रवीद् दुष्टबुद्धिः कर्णः सभायां कुरुवीरमध्ये। किं पाण्डवांस्त्वं न जहासि कृष्णे सुदुर्बलान् पतितान् हीनसत्त्वान्॥ योऽसौ कर्णः प्रत्यजानात्त्वदर्थे नाहं हत्वा सह कृष्णेन पार्थम्। इहोपयातेति स पापबुद्धिः कचिच्छेते शरसम्भिन्नगात्रः॥
en: That designing Karna who amidst the assembly of the Kuru chiefs had said to Krishna 'why don't you, O Krishna, desert the powerless, imbecile and degraded Pandavas'-that Karna who had vowed solemnly that he would not return from the field till he slew (both) Krishna and Partha-tell me does that vicious Karna lie today on the field with mangled limbs?

sn: कचित् संग्रामो विदतौ वै तवायं समागमे सृञ्जयकौरवाणाम्। यत्रावस्थामीदृशी प्रापितोऽहं कञ्चित् त्वया सोऽद्य हतो दुरात्मा॥
en: You do full well remember how hotly the battle raged when the Srinjayas and the Kaurava's faced each other-the encounter in which I was brought to such a sad plight. Did you come face to face with Karna and shoot him down?

sn: र्गाण्डीवमुक्तैर्विशिखैलद्धिः। सकुण्डलं भानुमदुत्तमाङ्गं कायात् प्रकृत्तं युधि सव्यसाचिन्॥
en: Have you today, O Savyasachin, severed that ear-ring bedecked splendid head of Karna off from his body with your fiery shafts discharged from the Gandiva.

sn: यत्तन्मया बाणसमर्पितेन ध्यातोऽसि कर्णस्य वधाय वीर। तन्मे त्वया कचिदमोघमद्य ध्यानं कृतं कर्णनिपातनेन॥
en: O valiant one, afflicted with Karna's shafts today how I thought of you (that you would slay him)! Have you put that thought of mine to action by slaying Karna?

sn: नः पुरा नुदीक्षते कर्णसमाश्रयेण। कचित् त्वया सोऽद्य समाश्रयोऽस्य भग्नः पराक्रम्य सुयोधनस्य॥
en: Being under the aegis of Karna the proud Suyodhana cared us not a jot. Have you by your might removed that aegis?

sn: यो षण्ढतिलानवोचत् सभामध्ये कौरवाणां समक्षम्। स दुर्मतिः कचिदुपेत्य संख्ये त्वया हतः सूतपुत्रो ह्यमर्षी॥
en: Did you encounter him in the field and settle with that wretched wight, the son of Suta, who had even before the assembly of the Kauravas likened us to sesame seeds devoid of Kernel;

sn: यः सूतपुत्रः प्रहसन् दुरात्मा पुराब्रवीनिर्जिता सौबलेन। मपीह कचित् स हतस्त्वयाद्य॥
en: That unrighteous son of Suta who had, grinning all the while, ordered Dusvashanta to drag out Jagyasena's daughter won by Subala's son (as a stake) at dice;

sn: यः शस्त्रभृच्छ्रेष्ठतमः पृथिव्यां पितामहं व्याक्षिपदल्पचेताः। संख्यायमानोऽर्धरथः स कचित् त्वया हतोऽद्याधिरथिर्महात्मन्॥
en: That dull-headed Karna who had upbraided the foremost warrior in the course of the tale of Rathas and Atirathas?

sn: अमर्षजं निकृतिमसीरणेरितं हृदिस्थितं ज्वलनमिमं सदा मम। हतोमया सोऽद्य समेत्य कर्ण इति ब्रुवन् प्रशमयसेऽद्य फाल्गुन॥
en: O Phalguna, that you have met with and slain that Karna in battle and thereby quench the flame of vindictiveness blazing within my heart being fanned by the wind of mortification. Assure me,

sn: ब्रवीहि मे दुर्लभमेतदद्य कथं त्वया निहतः सूतपुत्रः। अनुध्याये त्वां सततं प्रवीर वृत्रे हतेऽसौ भगवानिवेन्द्रः॥
en: Tell me, therefore, how you slew the son of Suta. O hero, I have so long been expecting you even as the divine Vishnu had awaited the arrival of Indra to bring him the news of Vritra's death.

sn: संजय उवाच तद् धर्मशीलस्य वचो निशम्य राज्ञः क्रुद्धस्यातिरथो महात्मा। उवाच दुर्धर्षमदीनसत्त्वं युधिष्ठिरं जिष्णुरनन्तवीर्यः॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing those words of the pious kirg, who was all anger, the great warrior Jishnu of indomitable energy said to the irrepressible and

sn: अर्जुन उवाच संशप्तकैर्युध्यमानस्य मेऽद्य सेनाग्रयायी कुरुसैन्येषु राजन्। आशीविषाभान् खगमान् प्रमुञ्चन् द्रौणिः पुरस्तात् सहसाभ्यतिष्ठत्॥
en: O king, while fighting with the Samsaptakas today, Drona's son, the leader of the Kuru army, all of a sudden came upon me discharging arrows that were like deadly serpents.

sn: दृष्ट्वा रथं मेघरवं ममैव समस्तसेना च रणेऽभ्यतिष्ठत्। तेषामहं पञ्च शतानि हत्वा ततो द्रौणिमगभं पार्थिवाग्र्य॥
en: Seeing my car rattling like a cloud, all the soldiers stood encircling it. Killing them all, who were full five hundred in number, I proceeded, O mightest of kings, against Drona's son.

sn: स मा समासाद्य नरेन्द्र यत्त: समभ्ययात् सिंहमिव द्विपेन्द्रः। अकार्षीच रथिनामुजिहीर्षां महाराज वध्यता कौरवाणाम्॥
en: Encountering me, O king, the hero rushed resolutely against me like a leader of elephants rushing upon a lion and intended to rescue the warriors who were being slain by me.

sn: ततो रणे भारत दुष्प्रकम्प्य आचार्यपुत्रः प्रवरः कुरूणाम्। जनार्दनं चैव विषाग्निकल्पैः॥
en: Later on in the battle, the invincible preceptor's son, the foremost of Kuru warriors, afflicted me and Janardana with arrows poignant like poison and fire.

sn: अष्टागवामष्ट शतानि बाणान् मया प्रयुद्धस्य वहन्ति तस्य। तांस्तेन सुक्तानहमस्य बाणैळनाशयं वायुरिवाभ्रजालम्॥
en: While he fought with me, eight carts each drawn by eight bullocks conveyed his hundreds of arrows. Like a wind dissipating clouds I baffled the arrows he showered upon me.

sn: नाकर्णपूर्णायतरिप्रमुक्तान्। स्तथा यथा प्रावृषि कालमेघः॥
en: Like a dark cloud discharging its watery contents in downpours he, drawing his bowstring to his very ears, showered upon me with skill and force thousands of other arrows.

sn: नैवाददानं न च संदधानं जानीमहे कतरेणास्यतीति। वामेन वा यदि वा दक्षिणेन स द्रोणपुत्रः समरे पर्यवर्तत्॥
en: So quickly did he move about in the battlefield that we could not discern from which side did he shoot his arrows, right or left, nor could we ascertain when he took up the arrows and when he discharged them.

sn: तस्याततं मण्डलमेव सज्यं प्रदृश्यते कार्मुकं द्रोणसूनोः। सोऽविध्यन्मां पञ्चभिर्दोणपुत्रः शितैः शरैः पञ्चभिर्वासुदेवम्॥
en: In fact, always we saw the bow of Drona's son drawn to a circle. At last he struck me with five sharp arrows and Vasudeva with another five.

sn: अहं हि तं त्रिंशता वज्रकल्पैः समार्दयं निमिषस्यान्तरेणा क्षणाच्छवावित्समरूपौ बभूव समादितो मद्विसृष्टैः पृषत्कैः॥
en: In a moment, however, I struck him with thirty thunder-bolt like arrows. Greatly wounded with the shafts discharged by me he ere long looked like a porcupine.

sn: स विक्षरन् रुधिरं सर्वगात्रे रथानीकं सूतसूनोर्विवेश। नसौ प्रपश्यन् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान्॥
en: All his limbs were covered with blood. Beholding is soldiers, the best of warriors, bathed in blood and overpowered by me, the son of Suta soon entered into the detachment of car-warriors.

sn: ततोऽभिभूतं युधि वीक्ष्य सैन्यं वित्रस्तयोधं दुतवाजिनागम्। पञ्चाशता रथमुख्यैः समेत्य कर्णस्त्वरन् मामुपायात् प्रमाथी॥
en: Beholding the soldiers terror-stricken and over-powered by me in battle and seeing the elephants and horses flying away, Karna at once marched against me with fifty car warriors. Killing them, however and avoiding Karna I have come here presently to see you.

sn: तान् सूदयित्वाहमपास्य कर्ण दुष्टुं भवन्तं त्वतयाभियातः। सर्वेपञ्चाला झुद्विजन्ते स्म कर्णं दृष्ट्वा गाव: केसरिणं यथैव॥
en: Seeing Karna, the Panchalas are all filled with fright even like the kine on seeing a lion. Like men entering into the gaping jaws of Death the Prabhadrakas, O king, have confronted Karna.

sn: मृत्योरास्यं व्यात्तमिवाभिपद्य प्रभद्रकाः कर्णमासाद्य राजन्। स्तदा कर्णः प्राहिणोन्मृतयुसद्म॥
en: Karna has already killed seventeen hundred of these car-warriors. The son of Suta did not lose heart till he came to our view.

sn: न चाप्यभूत् कान्तमनाः स राजन् यावन्नास्मान् दृष्ट्वान् सूतपुत्रः। मश्वतथाम्ना पूर्वतरं क्षतं च॥ मन्ये कालमपयानस्य राजन् क्रूरात् कर्णात् तेऽहमचितन्त्यकर्मन्।
en: You were first engaged with Ashvatthama and awfully wounded by him. Afterwards Karna saw you. I thought, O you of wonderful deeds, that coming away from the wanton Karna you were enjoying rest.

sn: मया कर्णस्यास्त्रमिदं पुरस्ताद् युद्धे दृष्टं पाण्डव चित्ररूपम्॥ न ह्यन्ययोद्धा विद्यते सृञ्जायानां महारथं योऽद्य सहेत कर्णम्।
en: O son of Pandu, I saw Karna's wonderful weapon being carried in front of the army. Methinks there is none amongst the Srinjayas who will be able to withstand the mighty carwarrior Karna.

sn: शैनेयो मे सात्यकिश्चक्ररक्षौ धृष्टद्युम्नश्चापि तथैव राजन्॥ युधामन्युश्चोत्तमौजाश्च शूरौ पृष्ठतो मां रक्षतां राजपुत्रौ।
en: O king, let Srini's grandson, Satyaki and Dhristadyumna guard my two wings. Let the heroic princes Yudhamanyu and Uttamaujas protect my rear.

sn: रथप्रवीरेण महानुभाव द्विषत्सैन्ये वर्तता दुस्तरेण॥ समेत्याहं सूतपुत्रेण संख्ये वृत्रेण वज्रीव नरेन्द्रमुख्या मस्मिन् संग्रामे यदि वै दृश्यतेऽद्य॥
en: O illustrious and most mighty king, as Shakra encountered Vitra, I shall today fight with Suta's son, that heroic and invincible carwarrior, if he can be found in this battle.

sn: आयाहि पश्याद्य युयुत्समानं मां सूतपुत्रस्य रणे जयाय। महोरगस्येव मुखं प्रपन्नाः प्रभद्रकाः कर्णमभिद्रवन्ति॥
en: Come and see us fight with each other in battle for victory. Like persons facing a powerful bull the Prabhadrakas are charging upon Karna.

sn: षट्साहना भारत राजपुत्राः स्वर्गाय लोकाय रणे निमग्नाः। कर्ण न चेदद्य निहन्मि राजन् सबान्धवं युध्यमानं प्रसह्य॥ प्रतिश्रुत्याकुर्वतो वै गतिर्या कष्टा याता तामहं राजसिंह।
en: Six thousands of kings are giving their lives for heaven. If however, O king, displaying all my strength I do not kill Karna with is allies in battle, I shall be doomed, O lion among kings to the curse which falls to the lot of one who promises a thing and does not redeem it.

sn: आमन्त्रये त्वां ब्रूहि जयं रणे मे पुरा भीमं धार्तराष्ट्रा ग्रसन्ते॥ सौति हनिष्यामि नरेन्द्रसिंह सैन्यं तथा शत्रुगणांश्च सर्वान्॥
en: I seek your blessing, O king, do say that victory will be mine' There the sons of Dhritarashtra are about to devour Bhima, I will slay Karna and his men and all our enemies.

sn: संजय उवाच श्रुत्वा कर्ण कल्पमुदारवीर्य क्रुद्धः पार्थः फाल्गुनस्यामितौजाः। धनंजयं वाक्यमुवाच चेदं युधिष्ठिरः कर्णशराभितप्तः॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing that Karna of great prowess was still alive and being angry with Phalguna, Yudhishthira, the Pritha's son of incomparable energy, who had been wounded by Karna with arrows, said to Dhananjayaविप्रद्रुता तात चमूसत्वदीया

sn: तिरस्कृता चाद्य यथा न साधु। भीतो भीमं त्यज्य चायास्तथा त्वं यन्नाशकः कर्णमथो निहन्तुम्॥
en: “Your army, my brother, must have been disgraced today and fled away, stricken with fear. And you have come here forsaking Bhima because you have not been able to kill Karna.

sn: स्नेहस्त्वया पार्थ कृतः पृथाया दर्भ समाविश्यः यथा न साधु। त्यक्त्वा रणे यदापायाः स भीम यन्नाशकः सूतपुत्रं निहन्तुम्॥
en: Shame it is, O Partha, that you did enter into Kunti's womb. It did not become you to leave behind Bhima in the battle-field because you could not slay Karna.

sn: यत् तद् वाक्यं द्वैतवने त्वयोक्तं कर्णं हन्तास्म्येकरथेन सत्यम्। त्यक्त्वा तं वै कथमद्यापयातः कर्णाद् भीतो भीमसेनं विहाय॥
en: You said to me, O Partha, in the Daita forest that you would kill Karna with no one on your car. Why have you then, afraid of Karna, come here avoiding him and leaving behind Bhima.

sn: इदं यदि द्वैतवनेऽप्यचक्षः कर्णं योद्धं न प्रशक्ष्ये नृपेति। वयं ततः प्राप्तकालं च सर्वे कृत्यान्युपैष्याम तथैव पार्थ॥
en: If you had said in the Daita forest 'O king, I won't be able to kill Karna, we would have in time, O Partha, made some befitting arrangements.

sn: मयि प्रतिश्रुत्य वदं हि तस्य न वै कृत तच तथैव वीर। आनीय नः शत्रुमध्यं स कस्मात् समुत्क्षिप्य स्थण्डिले प्रत्यपिष्ठा॥
en: Having promised to kill him, O hero, you have not kept your promise. Having launched us in the midst of our enemies why have you shattered us into pieces by wrecking us on a rock?

sn: अप्याशिष्म वयमर्जुन त्वयि यियासवो बहु कल्याणमिष्टम्। तन्नः सर्व विफलं राजपुत्र फलार्थिना विफल इवातिपुष्पः॥
en: O Arjuna, we showered many a blessing on you because we expected much good of you. But all our hopes, O prince, are frustrated, like that of a man expecting fruits from a tree and getting flowers instead.

sn: प्रच्छादितं बडिशमिवामिषेण संछादितं गरलमिवाशनेन। अनर्थकं मे दर्शितवानसि त्वं राज्यार्थिनो राज्यरूपं विनाशम्॥
en: Like a hook hidden in a fish, like poison mixed up with food, you did for nothing point out to our covetuous selves this destruction in the shape of kingdom.

sn: त्रयोदशेमा हि समाः सदा वयं त्वामन्वजीविष्म धनंजयाशया। काले वर्षं देवमिवोप्तबीजं तन्नः सर्वान् नरके त्वं न्यमजः॥
en: For these thirteen years, O Dhananjaya, we have been hoping and expecting much of you on even like the seeds sown earth in expectation of rains from gods in season.

sn: यत्तत् पृथां वागुवाचान्तरिक्षे सप्ताहजाते त्वयि मन्दबुद्धे। जातः पुत्रो वासवविक्रमोऽयं सर्वाशूराशात्रवाञ्जेष्यतीति॥ अयं जेता खाण्डवे देवसंघान् सर्वाणि भूयान्यपि चोत्तमौजाः। नयं कुरूपन् राजमध्ये निहत्या॥
en: O you of wicked sense, an invisible voice from the sky said to Pritha, on the seventh day from your birth; ‘This son born to you will be powerful like Vasava. He will vanquish all his powerful enemies. Gifted with a superior energy he will defeat at Khandava all the gods assisted by other creatures. He ill conquer the Madra, the Kalingas and the Kaikeyas. He will kill the Kurus in the midst of numbers of kings.

sn: अस्मात् परो नो भविता धनुर्धरो नैनं भूतं किंचन जातु जेता। इच्छन्नयं सर्वभूतानि कुर्याद् वशे वशी सर्वसमाप्तविद्यः॥
en: There will be no archer superior to him and none will be able to discomfort him. This boy, being the master of his own senses and adept in all the branches of knowledge, will subjugate all the living beings at his will.

sn: कान्त्या शशाङ्कस्य जवेन वायोः स्थैर्येण मेरोः क्षमया पृथिव्याः। सूर्यस्य भासा धनदस्य लक्ष्म्या शौर्येण शक्रस्य बलेन विष्णोः॥ तुल्यो महात्मा तव कुन्ति पुत्रो जातोऽदितेर्विष्णुरिवारिहन्ता। स्वेषां जयाय द्विषतां वधाय ख्यातोऽमितौजाः कुलतन्तुकर्ता॥
en: O Kunti, this magnanimous son of yours will be handsome like the Soma, swift like the Wind, patient like Sumeru, forbearing like the Earth, effulgent like Sun. wealthy like Kubera, valiant and powerful like Vishnu. This son of yours, even like Aditi's son Vishnu, the slayer of foes, has taken his being in order to bring victory to his kins and deal destruction to the enemies. This boy of indomitable valour will be far-famed and the founder of a dynasty.'

sn: इत्यन्तरिक्षे शतशृङ्गमूर्ध्नि तपस्विनां शृण्वतां वागुवाच। एवंविधं तच नाभूत तथा च देवापि नूनमनृतं वदन्ति॥
en: Even that celestial voice resounding in the skies reached the ears of the Maharsis living on the peaks of the Satasringa mountains. But now that voice comes to be untrue. It seems, therefore, that the gods too speak falsehood.

sn: तथा परेषामृषिसत्तमानां श्रुत्वा गिरः पूजयतां सदात्वाम्। न संनति प्रेमि सुयोधनस्य न त्वां जानाम्याधिस्थेर्भयार्तम्॥
en: The praises which the saintly beings used to lavish upon you, never made me expect Suyodhana's success nor even did I think that you will be paralised with the fear of Karna.

sn: पूर्व यदुक्तं हि सुयोधनेन न फाल्गुनः प्रमुखे स्थास्ययीति। कर्णस्य युद्धे हि महाबलस्य मौात् तु तन्नावबुद्धं मयाऽऽसीत्॥
en: "Duryodhana had already forecasted that "Arjuna will not able to stay before Karna, the great mighty warrior in battle." Owing to ignorance, I was not confirmed to my mind on such forecast.

sn: तेनाद्य तप्स्ये भृशमप्रमेयं यच्छत्रुवर्गे नरकं प्रविष्टः। तदैव वाच्योऽस्मि ननु त्वयाहं न योत्स्येऽहं सूतपुत्र कथंचित्॥ ततो नाहं सृञ्जयान् केकयांश्च समानयेयं सुहृदो रणाय।
en: "This is the reason, I am in such grievous state today. I am in hellish calamity because so badly trapped in the gigantic lobby of enemies. O Arjuna! You would have better to tell earlier that you will not involve yourself in battle against Karna, the son of charioteer." Had it made clear on your part, I would have not invited in the circumstance, Srinjayas, Kekayas and other several friends for support in battle.

sn: एवं गते किंच मयाद्य शक्यं कार्यं कर्तुं विग्रहे सूतजस्य॥ तथैव राज्ञश्च सुयोधनस्य ये वापि मां योद्धुकामाः समेताः।
en: When this is the situation today, what act can I perform in this battle against Karna, the son of a charioteer, king Duryodhana and other countless warriors who have gathered here for battle?

sn: धिगस्तु मजीवितमद्य कृष्ण योऽहं वशं सूतपुत्रस्य यातः॥ मध्ये कुरूणां सुहृदां च मध्ये ये चाप्यन्ये योद्धुकामाः समेताः।
en: O Sri Krishna! I am now enslaved / subjugated by Karna, the son of a charioteer in the presence of all Kauravas, friends and other all who have come and assembled here for participating in the battle. Shame to such life as I am living.

sn: यदि स्म जीवेत् स भवेनिहन्ता महारथानां प्रवरो रथोत्तमः। तवाभिमन्युस्तनयोऽद्य पार्थ न चास्मि गन्ता समरे पराभवम्॥ स्तथापि नाहं समरे पराङ्मुखः।
en: O Partha! Had Abhimanyu, the best chariot fighter still living, the enemies would have severely killed by him. So, gross humiliation would not have to born with were he lived. Had Ghatotkaca living I would have not shown back to battle-field.

sn: मम ह्यभाग्यानि पुरा कृतानि पापानि नूनं बलवन्ति युद्धे॥ तृणं च कृत्वा समरे भवन्तं ततोऽहमेवं निकृतो दुरात्मना। वैकर्तनेनैव तथा कृतोऽहं यथा ह्यशक्तः क्रियते ह्यबान्धवः॥
en: It seems with certainty that the debited account of sins committed earlier coupled with misfortune have gathered momentum to harass me at this juncture of life. Wicked Kara has humiliated me by treating you as brittle as a straw. Karna had behead with me as if I am without siblings and relations and a helpless man.

sn: आपद्गतं कश्चन यो विमोक्षेत् स बान्धवः स्नेहयुक्तः सुहृच। एवं पुराणा मुनयो वदन्ति धर्मः सदा सद्भिरनुष्टितश्च॥
en: Our ancient sages have stated that sibling is the man who defends the man from adversity befallen and he is real friend also. This is the everlasting deed (religion) observed by the gentlemen.

sn: त्वष्ट्रा कृतं वाहमकूजनाक्षं शुभं समास्थायं कपिध्वजं तम्। खङ्ग गृहीत्वा हेमपट्टानुबद्धं धनुश्चेदं गाण्डिवं तालमात्रम्॥ स केशवेनोहमानः कथं त्वं कर्णाद् भीतो व्यपयातोऽस्मि पार्थ।
en: You ride upon a car especially made by the celestial artisan (Visvakarma) himself, the axles of which move smoothly and without any noise. You have the standard of an ape, you hold a sword bedecked with gold and tied with silk and your bow Gandiva is as lengthy as the palm tree, even you have Kesava for your charioteer. Why then, O Partha, have you come back from the field of battle, for fear of Karna?

sn: धनुश्च तत् केशवाय प्रयच्छ यन्ता भविष्यस्त्वं रणे केशवस्य॥ तदाहनिष्यत् केशवः कर्णमुग्रं मरुत्पतिवृत्रमिवात्तवज्रः।
en: If you, O wretch, had even made over your bow to Kesava and contented yourself by being his charioteer, he would have slain that fearful Karna, as the lords of the Maruts (Shakra) slew with thunder the Asura known by the name of Vritra.

sn: श्चरन्तमुग्रं प्रतिबाधनाय॥ प्रयच्छान्यस्मै गाण्डिवमेदद्य त्वत्तो योऽस्त्रैरभ्यधिको वा नरेन्द्रः।
en: If you are unable to resist the fearful Karna in his march on the field today, then do make over this your Gandiva to any other king who is your superior in the use of weapons.

sn: अस्मान् नैवं पुत्रदारैर्विहीनान् सुखाद्धृष्टान् राज्यनाशाच भूयः॥ द्रष्टा लोकः पतिनानप्यगाधे पापैर्जुष्टे नरके पाण्डवेय।
en: The world will not then seen us bereft of family and children, deprived of our happiness and kingdom and sunk, O son of Pandu, into the fathomless abyss of the hell of torment.

sn: मासेऽपतिष्यः पञ्चमे त्वं सुकृच्छ्रे न वा गर्भे आभविष्यः पृथायाः॥ तत् ते श्रेयो राजपुत्राभविष्यन्न चेत् संग्रामदपयानं दुरात्मन्।
en: It would have been better had come out in the fifth months as an abortion, or better still, if you would not have taken your being in the womb of Kunti, than, O vile wretch, being born of a royal line, to show your back in the battle-field.

sn: मसंख्येयान् बाणगणांश्च धिक् ते। धिक् ते केतुं केसरिणः सुतस्य कृशानुदत्तं च रथं च धिक् ते॥
en: Fie to your Gandiva! Fie to the strength of your arms, fie to your numberless arrows, fie to your standard bearing the ensign of an ape on it and fie to your car presented to you by the god of fire!

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: संजय उवाच युधिष्ठिरणैवमुक्तः कौन्तेयः श्वेतवाहनः। असिं जग्राह संक्रुद्धो जिघांसुर्भरतर्षभम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing the words of Yudhishthira, Kownteya-the owner of white steeds-in a tempestuous mood took hold of his sword to slay that mightiest of the Bharata's race.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तस्य कोपं समुद्वीक्ष्य चित्तज्ञः केशवास्तदा। उवाच किमिदं पार्थ गृहीतः खङ्ग इत्युत॥
en: Kesava, the cogniser of human hearts, seeing his rage, inquired-"Why, O Partha, do you lay your hands on your sword?

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न हि पश्यामि योद्धव्यं त्वयां किञ्चिद् धनंजय। ते ग्रस्ता धार्तराष्ट्रा हि भीमसेनेन धीमता॥
en: Here, O Dhananjaya, I see no adversary to try the strength of your steel. Clever Bhimasena has already assailed the Dhartarashtras.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अपयातोऽसि कौन्तेयः राजा द्रष्टव्य इत्यापि। स राजा भवता दृष्टः कुशली च युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: O Kownteya, you have returned from the field, to seen king Yudhishthira and you have seen that he is keeping up well.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: स दृष्ट्वा नृपशार्दूलं शार्दूलसमविक्रमम्। हर्षकाले च सम्प्राप्त किमिदं मोहकारितम्॥
en: This is the time of rejoicing, as you have seen that best of kings whose prowess is like that of a tiger. Why should you then betray yourself thus?

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न तं पश्यामि कौन्तेय यस्ते वध्यो भविष्यति। प्रहर्तुमिच्छसे कस्मात् किं वा ते चित्तविभ्रमः॥
en: O son of Kunti, I do not find any one here whom you can slay. What makes you then to yearn for fight, or have you lost the balance of your mind?

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: कस्माद् भवान् महाखङ्गं परिगृह्णाति सत्वरः। तत् त्वां पृच्छामि कौन्तेयं किमिदं ते चिकीर्षितम्॥ परामृशसि यत् क्रुद्धः खङ्गमद्भुतविक्रम।
en: Why do you seize your mighty sword so suddenly, I enquire this of you. O Kaunteya, whence is this desire of your heart, or why do you fly to sword in such a sullen mood and with such a vigour?"

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु कृष्णेन प्रेक्षमाणो युधिष्ठिरम्॥ अर्जुन: प्राह गोविन्दं क्रुद्धः सर्प इव श्वसन।
en: Thus addressed by Krishna, Arjuna, looking towards Yudhishthira and whizzing like an angry snake, replied,

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अन्यस्मै देहि गाण्डीवमिति मां योऽभिचोदयेत्॥ भिन्द्यामहं तस्य शिर इत्युपांशुव्रत मम। तदुक्तं मम चानेन राज्ञामितपराक्रम॥ समक्षं तव गोविन्द न तत् क्षन्तुमिहोत्सहे। तस्मादेनं वधिष्यामि राजानं धर्मभीरुकम्॥
en: He who tells me-'Give your Gandiva to another,' I would cut his head off, such is my secret vow. Now that this king of immeasurable prowess has told me those words in your presence, O Govinda, I won't forgive him. I will, therefore, put to the sword this pious king.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: प्रतिज्ञा पालयिष्यामि हत्वैनं नरसत्तमम्। एतदर्थं मया खड्गो गृहीतो यदुनन्दन॥
en: I will redeem my vow by slaying this best of men. For this alone I have taken up the sword.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सोऽहं युधिष्ठिरं हत्वा सत्यस्यानृण्यतां गतः। विशोका विज्वरश्चापि भविष्यामि जनार्दन॥
en: O delighter of the Yadus; by slaying Yudhishthira I will thus adhere to truth thereby be free from grief and fever.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: किं वा त्वं मन्यसे प्राप्तमस्मिन् काल उपस्थिते। त्वमस्य जगतस्तात वेत्थ सर्वं गतागतम्॥ तत् तथा प्रकरिष्यामि यथा मां वक्ष्यते भवान्।
en: O Janaradana, what do you wish me to do under the present circumstances. O sire, you are well acquainted with all the past the future of this universe. I shall, therefore, do as you tell me.”

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: संजय उवाच घिग् धिगित्येव गोविन्दः पार्थमुक्तराब्रवीतः पुनः॥१५
en: Sanjaya said Saying "Fie, fie unto you, Partha,"

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच इदानीं पार्थ जानामि न वृद्धाः सेवितास्त्वया। काले न पुरुषव्याघ्र संरम्भं यद् भवानगात्॥
en: “Now I understand, O Partha, that you have never attended upon the old, since you, O mightiest of men, have been overcome with anger at a time quite out of season.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न हि धर्मविभागज्ञः कुर्यादेवं धनंजय। यथा त्वं पाण्डवाद्येह धर्मभीरुरपण्डितः॥
en: O Dhananjaya, those who are versed in the niceties of religion would never act in the way as you are doing today, O pious son of Pandu, on not being acquainted with them.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अकार्याणं क्रियाणां च संयोगं यः करोति वै। कार्याणामक्रियाणां च स पार्थ पुरुषाधमः॥
en: O Partha, he who does an act improper and heinous is the vilest of men.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अनुसृत्य तु ये धर्मं कथयेयुरुपस्थिताः। समासाविस्तरविदां न तेषां वेत्सि निश्चयम्॥
en: You know not the words of wisdom the learned men preach, after the rules of morality, to the pupils waiting up on them.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अनिश्चयज्ञो हि नरः कार्याकार्यविनिश्चये। अवशो मुह्यते पार्थ यथा त्वं मूढ एव तु॥
en: Persons ignorant of them become benumbed and befooled in discriminating between what ought to be done and what ought not, even as you, O Partha, have been nonplussed.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न हि कार्यमकार्यं वा सुखं ज्ञातु कथंचन। श्रुतेन ज्ञायते सर्व तच त्वं नावबुध्यसे॥
en: 'It is not easy to learn what ought to be done and what ought not. Of course everything can be learnt with the help of the scriptures. You are, however, a stranger to them.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अविज्ञानाद् भवान् यच्च धर्म रक्षति धर्मवित्। प्राणिनां त्वं वधं पार्थ धार्मिको नावबुध्यसे॥
en: Believing yourself to be conversant with morality, you are observing it in a way which but indicates your ignorance of it. You believe yourself to be virtuous but you know not, O Partha, that it is a sin to slay living beings.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: प्राणिनामवधस्तात सर्वज्यायान् मतो मम। अनृतां वा वदेद् वाचं न तु हिंस्यात् कथञ्चन॥
en: Methinks, keeping from doing any injury to any animal is a cardinal virtue. Even an untruth might behold but never an animal ought be slain.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: स कथं भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं राजान् धर्मकोविदम्। हन्याद् भवान् नरश्रेष्ठ प्राकृतोऽन्यः पुमानिव॥
en: O best of men, how could you then like an ordinary man wish to slay your eldest brother the king, who is well versed in morality.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अयुध्यमानस्य वधस्तथाशत्रोश्च मानदा। पराङ्मुखास्य द्रवतःशरणं चापि गच्छतः॥ कृताञ्जलेः प्रपन्नस्य प्रमत्तस्य तथैव च। न वधः पूज्यते सद्भिस्तच सर्व गुरौ तव॥
en: O Bharata, the slaying of a man who is not engaged in a fight, or is unwilling to fight, or takes to flight, or seeks your shelter, or joins his hands, or gives himself up to you, or is insane, be he even a foe, is never upheld by the righteous. And your superior is even all this.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: त्वया चैवं व्रतं पार्थ बालेनेव कृतं पुरा। तस्मादधर्मसंयुक्तं मौात् कर्म व्यवस्यसि॥
en: You had formerly taken the vow through childishness. And now through folly you are inclined to do an unrighteous act.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: स गुरुं पार्थ कस्मात् त्वं हन्तुकामोऽभिधावसि। असम्प्रघार्य धर्माणां गति सूक्ष्मा दुरत्ययाम्॥
en: Why, O Partha, do you rush upon your superior, intending to slay him, without determining (before-hand) the exceedingly fine course of virtue which is, certainly, not easily intelligible.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: इदं धर्मरहस्यं च तव वक्ष्यामि पाण्डव। यद् ब्रूयात् तव भीष्मो हि पाण्डवो वा युधिष्ठिरः॥२ विदुरो वा यथा क्षत्ता कुन्ती वापि यशस्विनी। तत् ते वक्ष्यामि तत्त्वेन निबोधैतद् धनंजय॥
en: O son of Pandu, this mystery of virtue I will now explain to you as it was explained by Bhishma, by the pious Yudhishthira, by Vidura or the so-called Kshatri and by Kunti of great renown. I will tell it you in all its detail; listen to it, O Dhananjaya.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सत्यस्य वचनं साधु न सत्याद् विद्यते परम्। तत्त्वेनैव सुदुर्जेयं पश्य सत्यमनुष्ठितम्॥
en: One who tells the truth is a pious person. Nothing is there higher than truth. It is, therefore, very difficult to understand the details of truth as observed in action.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: भवेत सत्यमवक्तव्यं वक्तव्यमनृतं भवेत्। यत्रानृतं भवेत् सत्यं चाप्यनृतं भवेत्॥
en: Truth becomes unutterable and untruth utterable, where untruth would pose as truth and truth as untruth.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: विवाहकाले रतिसम्प्रयोगे प्राणात्यये सर्वधनापहारे। विप्रस्य चार्थे ह्यनृतं वदेत पञ्चानृतान्याहुरपातकानि॥
en: At a marriage or in the enjoyment of lust, or when one's life is at stake, or when one's entire fortunes are about to be lost, or in the cause of a Brahmin untruth may be uttered. It is said that there is no sin in uttering these five sorts of falsehood.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सर्वस्वस्यापहारे तु वक्तव्यमनृतं भवेत्। तत्रानृतं भवेत् सत्यं चाप्यनृतं भवेत्॥ तादृशं पश्यते बालो यस्य सत्यमनुष्ठितम्।
en: Where one's entire fortunes are at stake untruth becomes utterable. On these occasions untruth becomes truth and truth untruth. He who is bent upon always practising truth alone is a fool and takes truth to be as it is.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: भवेत् सत्यमवक्तव्यं न वक्तव्यमनुष्ठितम्। सत्यानृते विनिश्चित्य ततो भवति धर्मवित्॥
en: Indeed it is not a very easy thing to become righteous. He who can distinguish between the niceties of truth and untruth can alone become conversant with morality.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: किमाश्चर्यं कृतप्रज्ञः पुरुषोऽपि सुदारुणः। सुमहत् प्राप्नुयात् पुण्यं बलाकोऽन्धवधादिव॥
en: What wonder is there then that a wise man by doing something awfully cruel may even acquire virtue, as Balaka did by killing a blind beast.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: किमाश्चर्यं पुनमूर्दो धर्मकामो ह्यपण्डितः। सुमहत् प्राप्नुयात् पापमापगास्विव कौशिकः॥
en: What wonder then that an ignorant and inexperienced person, intending to practise virtue, would commit grave vice like Kaushika on the river-bank."

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अर्जुन उवाच आचक्ष्व भगवन्नेतद् यथा विन्दाम्यहं तथा। बलाकस्यानुसम्बन्धं नदीनां कौशिकस्य च॥
en: Arjuna said Tell me of it, O holy one, in a way that I may learn it these stories about Balaka and Kaushika on the river-bank.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: वासुदेव उवाच पुराव्याधोऽभवत् कश्चिद् बलाको नाम भारत। यात्रार्थ पुत्रदारस्य मृगान् हन्ति न कामतः॥
en: Vasudeva said There was once a hunter, O Bharata, Balaka by name. He used to kill animals, not willfully but, in order to support his children and wife.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: वृद्धौ च मातापितरौ बिभर्त्यन्यांश्च संश्रितान्। स्वधर्मनिरतो नित्यं सत्यवागनसूयकः॥
en: Devoted to his tribal pursuits, always speaking the truth and devoid of malice, he used to maintain his aged mother and father and other dependents.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: स कदाचिन्सृगं लिप्सु भ्यविन्दन्मृगं क्वचित्। अपः पिबन्त ददृशे श्वपादं घ्राणचक्षुषम्॥
en: Once on a day, thought diligently searching for an animal, he could find none. At last he found a beast of prey, drinking water, which had lost its eyes but the loss was supplied by its keen sense of smell.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अदृष्टपूर्वमपि तत् सत्त्व तेन हतं तदा। अन्धे हते ततो व्योग्नः पुष्पवर्षं पपात च॥
en: Though he had not before seen a like of it, yet he killed it then and there. No sooner the blind beast had been killed, that there fell from the skies a shower of flowers.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अप्सरोगीतवादित्रैर्नादितं च मनोरमम्। विमानमगमत् स्वर्गन्मृगव्यधनिनीषया॥
en: A celestial car, filled with the songs and music of Apsaras, came down from heaven to fetch that hunter of animals.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तद् भूतं सर्वभूतानामभावाय किलार्जुन। तपस्तप्तवा वरं प्राप्तं कृतमन्धं स्वयम्भुवा॥
en: That beast having, successfully performed all the austerities of asceticism with a view to kill all the animals, had received that boon but was made blind instead by the Self-born.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तद्धत्वा सर्वभूतानामभावकृतनिश्चयम्। ततो बालकः स्वरगादेवं धर्मः सुदुर्विदः॥
en: Therefore Valaka, having killed the beast that was bent upon killing all the animals, went to heaven. Morality is, therefore, very difficult to be understood.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: कौशिकोऽप्यभवद् विप्रस्तपस्वी नो नदीनां संगमे ग्रामाददूरात स किलावसत्॥
en: There was an ascetic Brahmin named Kaushika not much read in the Scriptures. He used to reside at a confluence of rivers, not far away from a village.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सत्यं मया सदा वाच्यमिति तस्याभवद् व्रतम्। सत्यवादिति विख्यातः स तदाऽऽसीद् धनंजय॥
en: He had taken the vow that the would ever speak the truth.' Therefore, O Dhananjaya, he become famous as a truthful man.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अथ दस्युभयात् केचित् तदा तद् वनमाविशन। तत्रापि दस्यवः क्रुद्धास्तानमार्गन्त यत्नतः॥ बहुश्रुतः।
en: At a time certain persons, being afraid of robbers, entered the woods. Even there the robbers, filled with anger, doggedly haunted after them.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अथ कौशिकमभ्येत्य प्राहुस्ते सत्यवादिनम्। कतमेन पथा भगवन् बहवो जनाः॥ सत्येन पृष्टः प्रबूहि यदि तान् वेत्थ शंस नः।
en: They then approaching Kaushika the truthful, said-'O holy one, which way have a number of men passed a little while ago? Asked in the name of truth tell us if you have seen them.'

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: श पृष्टः कौशिकः सत्यं तानुवाच ह॥ बहुवृक्षलतागुल्ममेतद् वनमुपाश्रिताः। इति तान् ख्यापयामास तेभ्यस्तत्त्वं स कौशिकः॥५१
en: Being thus asked Kaushika told them the truth, that they had entered the wood thickly covered with trees, creepers and shrubs. O Partha, thus did Kaushika inform them.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: ततस्ते तान् समासाद्य क्रूरा जघ्नुरिति श्रुतिः। तेनाधर्मेण महता वाग्दुरुक्तेन कौशिकः॥ गतः स कष्टं नरकं सूक्ष्मधर्मेष्वकोविदः।
en: And the report goes that on this those wanton men got hold of those persons and put them to death. For the gave sin of uttering that truth, which should not have been uttered, Kaushika, unversed in the subtleties of religion, fell into a fearful hell.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: यथा चाल्पश्रुतो मूढो धर्माणामविभागवित्॥ वृद्धानपृष्ट्वा संदेह महच्छवभ्रमिवार्हति।
en: As a foolish man, ill-read in the scriptures, unacquainted with the details of morality, is fit to fall into an awful hell for not asking aged men to set his doubts at rest.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तत्र ते लक्षणोद्देशः कश्चिदेवं भविष्यति॥ दुष्करं परमं ज्ञानं तर्केणानुव्यवस्यति। श्रुतेधर्म इति वदन्ति बहवो जनाः॥
en: Your definition of morality must be then something like that. Some people attempt at attaining that high and difficult knowledge by the exercise of reasoning. Many persons maintain, on the other hand, that morality can be learned from the scriptures alone.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तत् ते न प्रत्यसूयामि चन स सर्व विधीयते। प्रभवार्थाय भूतानां धर्मप्रवचन कृतम्॥
en: I do not find fault with the latter, but then everything is not provided for there. The moral precepts have been made for the well-being of the creatures.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: यत् स्यादहिंसासंयुक्तं च धर्म इति निश्चयः। अहिंसाय भूतानां धर्मप्रवचनं कृतम्॥
en: All that is free from any motive of injury to any being is surely morality. For, indeed, the moral precepts have been made to free the creatures from all injuries.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: धारणाद् धर्ममित्याहुर्धर्मो धारयते प्रजाः। यत् स्याद् धारणसंयुक्तंस धर्म इति निश्चयः॥
en: Dharma (morality) is so-called because it protects all. Indeed, morality saves all creatures. Surely then that is morality which is capable of keeping off a creature from all injuries.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: येऽन्यायेन निहीर्षन्तो धर्ममिच्छन्ति कर्हिचित्। अकूजनेन मोक्षं वा नानुकूजेत् कथंचन॥
en: Those who try to stick to them logically, have scarcely a mind to acquire morality. If you can get rid of them without a word do no account have any intercourse with them.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अवश्यं कूजितव्ये वा शङ्करन्नप्यकूजतः। श्रेयस्तत्रानृतं वक्तुं तत् सत्यमविचारितम्॥
en: If he must be spoken to or if he takes offence on not being talked with, in that case better speak a falsehood; verily that untruth is truth.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: यः कार्येभ्यो व्रतं कृत्वा तस्य नानोपपादयेत। न तत्फलमवाप्नोति एवमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: He who, having taken a vow on some set purpose, cannot redeem the same by acts, attains not the rewards of that vow.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: प्राणात्यये विवाहे वा सर्वज्ञातिवधात्यये। नर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्ते वा न च प्रोक्तं मृषा भवेत्॥ अधर्म नात्र पश्यन्ति धर्मतत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः।
en: When one's life is endangered, at marriage, at the risk of destruction of one's kith and kin or in the course of business, all that is uttered will not be regarded as falsehood. To those who are well-versed in the real secrets of morality, there appear no immorality in all this.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: यः स्तेनैः सह सम्बन्धान्मुच्यते शपथैरपि॥ श्रेयस्तत्रानृतं वक्तुं तत् सत्यमविचारितम्।
en: There even, where one cuts off his connections with robbers after having taken an oath, it is better to swear falsely, for surely that falsehood would be truth.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न च तेभ्यो धनं देयं शक्ये सति कथंचन॥ पापेभ्यो हि धनं दत्तं दातारमपि पीडयेत्।
en: On no account should one's wealth he give to the robbers, if that could be helped. Wealth when give to the sinful afflicts even the donor.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तस्माद् धमार्थमनृत्तमुक्त्वा नानृतभाग् भवेत्॥ एष ते लक्षणोद्देशो मयोद्दिष्टो यथाविधि। यथाधर्मं यथाबुद्धि मयाद्य वै हितार्थिना॥ एतच्छ्रुत्वा ब्रूहि पार्थ यदि वध्यो युधिष्ठिरः।
en: Therefore, an untruth spoken in the cause of morality does not amount to a falsehood. I have now duly pointed out to you the distinctive feathers of morality. Having heard all these tell me, O Partha, if Yudhishthira deserves to be killed.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अर्जुन उवाच यश्चा ब्रूयान्महाप्राज्ञो यथा ब्रूयान्महामतिः॥ हितं चैव यथास्माकं तथैतद् वचनं तव।
en: Arjuna said "O Krishna! You have spoken as a man of great wisdom should say, as a man of great intelligence need say. Your words are even such as would do good to us.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: भवान् मातृसमोऽस्माकं तथा पितृसमोऽपि च॥ गतिश्च परमा कृष्ण त्वमेव च परायणम्।
en: You are like both a mother and a father to us. You, O Krishna, are our sanctuary; that is why your words are beneficial to us.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न हि ते त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यतेऽविदितं क्वचिन्॥ तस्माद् भवान् परम धर्मं वेद सर्व यथातथम्।
en: Nothing is there in the three worlds that is unknown to you. Therefore, you know the sublime morality with all its niceties.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अवध्यं पाण्डवं मन्ये धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥ अस्मिंस्तु मम संकल्पे ब्रूहि किंचिदनुग्रहम्। इदं वा परमत्रैव शृणु हृत्स्थं विविक्षितम्॥
en: I admit that the righteous Yudhishthira, son of Pandu, is unslayable. In this connection kindly tell me something in my favour. Hear me tell you of something else that lies in my heart.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: जानासि दासार्ह मम व्रतं त्वं यो मां ब्रूयात् कश्चन मानुषेषु। अन्यस्मै त्वं गाण्डिव देहि पार्थ त्वत्तोऽस्त्रैर्वा वीर्यतो वा विशिष्टः॥ हन्यामहं केशव तं प्रसह्य भीमो हन्यात् तूबरकेति चोक्तः। तन्मे राजा प्रोक्तवास्ते समक्षं धनुर्देहीत्यसकृद् वृष्णिवीर॥
en: You know, O Keshava, the best scion of the Dasharha race, that my vow is that whoever among men tells me 'make over, O Partha, your Gandiva to him who is superior to you in point of chivalry or in wielding armours' I will, with all my mighty, slay him. So Bhima also has taken a vow to slay the man who addresses him as 'one without the hirsute indications of manhood!' Just now the king has repeatedly told me in your presence “make over your bow.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तं हन्यां चेत् केशव जीवलोके स्थाता नाहं कालमप्यल्पमात्रम्। ध्यात्वा नूनं ह्येनसा चापि मुक्तो वधं राज्ञो भ्रष्टवीर्यो विचेताः॥
en: O Keshava, if I slay him, surely then the thought of having slain the king will immerse me in sin and make me loose my valour and mental faculties and thus cut short my days in this world.
