description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: यथा प्रतिज्ञा मम लोकबुद्धौ भवेत् सत्या धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठ। यथा जीवेत् पाण्डवोऽहं च कृष्ण तथा बुद्धि दातुमप्यर्हसि त्वम्॥
en: Therefore, O Krishna, the best of all the righteous inen, do give me such counsels as would uphold my well-known vow and leave both myself and the eldest son of Pandu alive."

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: वासुदेव उवाच राजा श्रान्तो विक्षतो दुःखितश्च कर्णेन संख्ये निशितैबार्णसंधैः। यश्चानिशं सूतपुत्रेण वीर शरैर्भृशं ताडितोऽयुध्यमानः॥
en: Vasudeva said-"O valiant one, the King Yudhishthira feels weary and aggrieved on being afflicted with arrows shot at him by Karna during the campaign; the more so as he was harassed with shaft-shots by the son of Suta even when he was retiring form the field.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अतस्त्वमेतेन सरोषमुक्तो दुःखाचितेनेदमयुक्तरूपम्। अकोपितो ह्येष यदि स्म संख्ये कर्णं न हन्यादिति चाब्रवीत् सः॥
en: Heavy at heart as he was at all this, he used such angry and improper expressions to you. Moreover, he addressed you in that tenor thinking that if he could provoke you, you would forthwith slay Karna in battle.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: जानाति तं पाण्डव एष चापि पापं लोके कर्णमसामन्यैः। ततस्त्वमुक्तो भृशरोषितेन राज्ञा समक्षं परुषाणि पार्थ॥
en: O Partha, the king believes that this immoral Karna is unbearable to everyone else on earth but you. It was this that enraged him so highly as to use such cruel words even in your face.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: नित्योद्युक्ते सततं चाप्रसह्ये कर्णे द्यूतं ह्यद्य रणे निबद्धम्। रेवं बुद्धिः पार्थिवे धर्मपुत्रे॥
en: King Yudhishthira, the righteous, is of opinion that today's battle is a play at dice in which the life of the ever-deviceful and everover bearing Karna has been laid as an wager. If he is slain, the Kauravas would necessarily meet with defeat.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: स्त्वया प्रतिज्ञार्जुन पालनीया। जीवनयं येन मृतो भवेद्धि तन्मे निबोघेह तवानुरूपम्॥
en: Therefore, O Arjuna, the son of Dharma deserves not death at your hands. At the same time your vow also must be kept good. Under the circumstances listen to the means that will make him apparently dead without the real loss of life.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: स्तदा स वै जीवति जीवलोके। यदाऽवमानं लभते महान्तं तदा जीवन्मृत इत्युच्यते सः॥
en: A man of honour lives in this material world so long as he receives the homage due to him, but when he is woefully dishonored, he is spoken of as one more dead than alive.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सम्मानितः पार्थिवोऽयं सदैव त्वयाच भीमेन तथा यमाभ्याम्। स्तस्यापमानं कलया प्रयुडक्ष्व॥
en: O Partha, this king has ever been honored by you, Bhima and the twins and by all the wise and chivalrous men to this world. You just offer some insult to that king.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: त्वमित्यत्रभवन्तं हि ब्रूहि पार्थ युधिष्ठिरम्। त्वमित्युक्तो हि निहतो गुरुर्भवति भारत॥
en: O Bharata, a superior on being addressed as 'you' dies (at heart). Therefore, you do addressed the much-respected Yudhishthira as 'you.'

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एवमाचर कौन्तेय धर्मराजे युधिष्ठिरे। अधर्मयुक्तं संयोग कुरुष्वैन कुरूद्वह॥
en: O the best of Kurus, O son of Kunti, do behave thus towards Yudhishthira the righteous and insult that honorable man by this censurable behaviour.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अथर्वाङ्गिरसी ह्येषा श्रुतीनामुत्तमा श्रुतिः। अविचार्यैव कार्येषा श्रेयस्कामैनरैः सदा॥
en: This is a Shruti given out by the Rishis Atharva and Angira, the best of all the Srutis; people who wish well should always follow this without any scruple.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अवधेन वधः प्रोक्तो यद् गुरुस्त्वमिति प्रभुः। तद् ब्रूहि त्वं यन्मयोक्तं धर्मराजस्य धर्मवित्॥
en: To address a venerable superior as 'You.' is to kill him without actually depriving him of his life. Therefore do you, who are versed in morality, address Yudhishthira the righteous, in the manner I have indicated.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: स्त्वत्तोऽयुक्तं वेत्स्यते चैवमेषः। ततोऽस्य पादावभिवाद्य पश्चात् समं ब्रूया: सान्त्वयित्वा च पार्थम्॥
en: On your acting thus the righteous Yudhishthira will verily feel that you have offered him a death-blow. Later on you will worship his feet and speak to him in befitting terms and thus pacify him.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: भ्राता प्राज्ञास्तव कोपं न जातु कुर्याद् राजा धर्ममवेक्ष्य चापि। मुक्तोऽनृताद् भ्रातवधाच पार्थ हृष्टः कर्णं त्वं जहि सूतपुत्रम्॥
en: O Partha, your intelligent brother Yudhishthira would never feel in the least angry with you. On being thus freed from impiety and fratricide you may cheerfully proceed against and slay Karna, the son of Suta.

sn: संजय उवाच इत्येवमुक्तस्तु जनार्दनेन पार्थः प्रशस्याथ सुहृदवचस्तत्। मनुक्तपूर्वं परुषं प्रसह्य॥ काले हि
en: Sanjaya said Being thus spoken to by Janardana, Pritha's son Arjuna highly approved of the friendly counsels and then addressing Yudhishthira, the righteous, in a sullen tone, spoke such harsh words as he had never before done.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच मा त्वं राजन् व्याहर व्याहरस्व यस्तिष्ठसे क्रोशमात्रे रणाद् वै। भीमस्तु मामर्हति गर्हणाय यो युध्यते सर्वलोकप्रवीरैः॥ शत्रून् परिपीड्य संख्ये हत्वा च शूरान् पृथिवीपतींस्तान्। रथप्रधानोत्तमनागमुख्यान् सादिप्रवेकानमितांश्च वीरान्॥ यः कुञ्जराणामधिकं सहस्रं हत्वा नदंस्तुमुलं सिंहनादम्। काम्बोजानामयुतं पर्वतीयान् मृगान् सिंहो विनिहत्येव चाजौ॥ सुदुष्करं कर्म करोति धीरः कर्तुं यथा नार्हसि त्वं कदाचित्। स्तया निहन्त्यश्वरथद्विपान् रणे॥ स्तथा रथाङ्गैर्धनुषा दहत्यरीन्। प्रमृद्य पद्भ्यामहितान् निहन्ति पुनस्तु दो• शतमन्युविक्रमः॥ महाबलौ वैश्रवणान्तकोपमः प्रसह्य हन्ता द्विषतामनीकिनाम्। स भीमसेनोऽर्हति गर्हणां मे न त्वं नित्यं रक्ष्यसे यः सुहृद्भिः॥
en: Arjuna said O king, you should upbraid me no more. You who are at a distance of about two miles from the battle-field, should not upbraid me for nothing. He who having, in fair fight, defeated the enemies and slain those chivalrous lords of Earth and their best and leading car-warriors, elephants, cavalry and innumerable combatants, has been fighting with the foremost of heroes; he, who having routed in fight more than a thousand elephants and ten thousand soldiers of the Kambojamountaineers has been yelling as a lion roars after having killed many a deer; that Bhima may upbraid me. The wonderful feats the hero Vrikodara has been achieving on jumping down from his chariot with mace in hand and the innumerable horses, cars and elephants he has been destroying, are such, the like of which you can never achieve. That hero, with the valour of Indra, has been, with the best of swords, splitting down riders with horses and elephants and has been consuming the enemies with arrows and the broken limbs of cars and spreading death all around with his feet and hands. Indeed, Bhimasena, mighty like Yama and Kubera, readily slays the hostile army. That Bhimasena may revile me and not you who are ever being protected by friends.

sn: महारथान् नागवनरान् हयांश्च पदातिमुख्यानपि च प्रमथ्य। एको भीमो धार्तराष्ट्रेषु मग्नः स मामुपालब्धुमरिंदमोऽर्हति॥
en: He, who has been diving single-handed deep into the surge of Duryodhana's soldiers, carrying by storm the foremost elephants, steeds, infantry and charioteers; that Bhimsena, the slayer of foes, may reprove me.

sn: कलिङ्गवङ्गनिषादमागधान् सदामदानीलवलाहकोपमान्। निहन्ति यः शत्रुगजाननेकान् स मामुपालब्धुमरिंदमोऽर्हति॥
en: He, who has been slaying, in numbers the ever-furious elephants of the hostile Anga, Banga, Kalinga, Nishada and Magadha, that look like masses of blue clouds; that Bhimasena, the chastiser of enemies, may find fault with me.

sn: स युक्तमास्थाय रथं हि काले धनुर्विधुन्वशरपूर्णमुष्टिः। सृजत्यसौ शरवर्षाणि वीरो महाहवे मेघ इवाम्बुधाराः॥
en: In the battle that valiant Brikodara being seated on a superbly-decked chariot has been holding in readiness handful of arrows and opportunely hurling them down in showers, like the clouds pouring torrents of rain.

sn: शतान्यष्टौ वारणानामवश्यं विशातितैः कुम्भकराग्रहस्तः। भीमेनाजौ निहतान्यद्य बाणैः स मां क्रूरं वक्तुमर्हत्यरिजः॥
en: I have seen that in today's battle Bhimasena has cut asunder with his arrows, the heads, bodies and proboscis of eight hundred elephants and thereby killed them therefore, that Brikodara, the slayer of foes, may use harsh words me.

sn: बलं तु वाचि द्विजसत्तमानां क्षात्रं बुधा बाहुबलं वदन्तिा त्वं वाग्बलो भारत निष्ठुरश्च त्वमेव मां वेत्य यथाबलोऽहम्॥
en: O Bharata, the learned men say that the strength of the foremost of Brahmanas lies in words and the main strength of the Kshatriyas is in their arms; but your strength lies in your words, moreover you are wanton. As for me, it is not unknown to you what stuff I am made of.

sn: यते हि नित्यं तव कर्तुमिष्टं दारैः सुतैर्जीवितेनात्मना च। एवं यन्मां वाग्विशिखेन हंसि त्वत्तः सुखं न वयं विद्म किंचित्॥
en: I am ever bent upon pandering to your inclinations with my wives, sons, life and soul; still that you has been torturing me with your pointed words, I am convinced that we cannot expect happiness at your hands.

sn: मां मावसंस्था द्रौपदीतल्पसंस्थो महारथान् प्रतिहन्मि त्वदर्थे। तेनातिशङ्की भारत निष्ठुरोऽसि त्वत्तः सुखं नाभिजानामि किंचित्॥
en: O Bharata, do you be trifling with me no longer, lying all the while on Draupadi's bed. it is for you that I have been slaying many a mighty car-warrior. Perhaps that has been making you fearless and wanton still. Indeed, I could never feel any happiness from you.

sn: स्त्व प्रियार्थं नरदेव युद्धे। वीरः शिखण्डी द्रौपदोऽसौ महात्मा मयाभिगुप्तेन हतश्च तेन॥
en: O God among men, the magnanimous Bhishma, true to his vows and only with a view to please you, has himself pointed out that the valiant and high-souled Shikhandin, the son of Drupada, would be the cause of his death; and when I had been shielding that Shikhandin in the battle-field he was slain by the latter.

sn: न चाभिनन्दामि तवाधिराज्यं यतस्त्वमक्षेष्वहिताय सक्तः। मस्माभिर्वा तर्तुमिच्छस्यरीस्त्वम्॥
en: I do not approve of your being restored to sovereignty, because you are addicted to the vice of gambling. Having thyself committed a sin, to which the low alone are addicted, you are now trying to get off from your foes through our aid.

sn: अक्षेपु दोषा बहवो विधर्माः श्रुतास्त्वया सहदेवोऽब्रवीद् यान्। स्तेन स्म सर्वे निरयं प्रपन्नाः॥
en: You had heard of the immorality and the numerous evils of playing at dice, dilated upon by Sahadeva. Yet you could not forego those evils practised by the wicked alone. It is but for this that we are steeped in distress.

sn: सुखं त्वत्तो नाभिजानीमकिंचिद् यतस्त्वमक्षैर्देवितुं संप्रवृतः। स्वयं कृत्वा व्यसनं पाण्डव त्वमस्मास्तीवाः श्रावयस्यद्य वाचः॥
en: Since you wert engrossed in gambling, we could derive no happiness from you. O Pandava, having caused all these mischief's thyself, you are now heaping all these reproaches on me.

sn: शेतेऽस्माभिनिहता शत्रुसेना छिन्नैर्गात्रैर्भूमितले नदन्ती। त्वया हि तत् कर्म कृत् नृशंसं यस्माद् दोष: कौरवाणां वधश्च॥
en: Lo, the hostile troops, slain by us are lying prostrate on earth with mangled limbs and are uttering the deepest groans. Indeed, it was you who didst those wrongs, for which the Kauravas have lost their lives.

sn: हता उदीच्या निहताः प्रतीच्या नष्टाः प्राच्या दाक्षिणात्या विशस्ताः। स्तेषां योधैरस्मदीयैश्च युद्धे॥
en: The mighty warriors of the Kurus and ourselves have performed wonderful feats of valour in the battle-field. The hostile troops from the North, the West, the East and the South have been slain to a man.

sn: स्त्वसम्भवं नो व्यसनं नरेन्द्र। मास्मान् क्रूरैर्वाक्प्रतोदैस्तुदंस्तवं भूयो राजन् कोपयेस्त्वल्पभाग्यः॥
en: O ruler of mankind, it was you who had played at dice and it was for you alone that our kingdom was lost and we have fallen on evil days. Therefore, O king, do not provoke us too much by casting cruel aspersions on us.

sn: संजय उवाच एता वाचः परुषाः सव्यसाची स्थिरप्रज्ञः श्रावयित्वा तु रुक्षाः। बभूवासौ विमना धर्मभीरुः कृत्वा प्राज्ञाः पातकं किंचिदेवम्॥
en: Sanjaya said The calm, virtuous and conscientious, Sabyasachin (Arjuna) having addressed to Yudhishthira such harsh and exceedingly cruel words and having thus slightly sinned became cheerless.

sn: तदानुतेपे सुरराजपुत्रो विनिःश्वसंश्चासिमथोद्वबह। तमाह कृष्णः किमिदं पुनर्भवान् विकोशमाकाशनिभं करोत्यसिम्॥
en: Then that son of Indra became repentant and sighing heavily unsheathed his sword. Seeing this, Krishna said-"Wait is this? Why do you draw your sword lustrous like the blue skies?

sn: स्तथा प्रवक्ष्याम्यहमर्थसिद्धये। इत्येमुक्तः पुरुषोत्तमेन सुदुःखितः केशवमर्जुनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: If you have anything to ask, be out with it. I will tell you how to gain your desired ends." Being thus spoken to by Keshava, the foremost of men, the remorse-stricken Dhananjaya repliedअहं हनिष्ये स्वशरीरमेव

sn: प्रसह्य येनाहितमाचरं वै। निशम्य तत् पार्थवचोऽब्रवीदिदं धनंजय धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठः॥
en: “I do mean to destroy my body that has thus sinned.” Hearing this from Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, Krishna the adorable of the righteous, said unto himराजानमेनं त्वमितीदमुक्त्वा

sn: किं कश्मलं प्राविशः पार्थ घोरम्। त्वं चात्मानं हन्तुमिच्छस्यरिघ्न नेदं सद्भिः सेवितं वै किरीटिन्॥
en: O slayer of foes, O Kiritin (Arjuna), why have you become so much crest-fallen on addressing the king as 'you.' You intend to kill yourself, but no honest man would approve of it.

sn: धर्मात्मानं भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठमद्य खड्ड्रेन चैनं यदि हन्या नृवीर। धर्माद् भीतस्तत् कथं नाम ते स्यात् किंचोत्तरं वाकरिष्यस्त्वमेव॥
en: O hero among men, what your state would have been had you, under a false religious zeal, slain your elder brother today?

sn: सूक्ष्मो धर्मो दुर्विदश्चापि पार्थ विशेषतोऽज्ञैः प्रोच्यमानं निबोध। हत्वाऽऽत्मानमात्मना प्राप्नुयास्त्वं वधाद् भ्रातुर्नरकं चातिघोरम्॥
en: O Partha, religion is very subtle and awfully unintelligible, the more so to the ignorant. Hear me tell you of it. Suicide is tantamount to fratricide and in either case condemnation to the same hell would have been inevitable.

sn: स्तथा हतात्मा भवितासि पार्थ। तथास्तु कृष्णेत्यभिनन्द्य तद्वचो धनंजयः प्राह धनुर्विनाम्य॥ युधिष्ठिरं धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठं शृणुष्व राजनिति शक्रसूनुः।
en: Therefore, O Partha, now recount to him your merits and valourous deeds and you shall thereby slay yourself.” Dhananjaya, the son of Sakra (Indra) hailed these words, saying-"Be it so." Then lowering his bow, he said unto Yudhishthira, the adored of the virtuous, "Hear me, O king.

sn: न मादृशोऽन्यो नरदेव विद्यते धनुर्धरो देवमृते पिनाकिनम्॥ अहं हि तेनानुमतो महात्मना क्षणेन हन्यां सचराचरं जगत्।
en: O ruler of men, excepting only the wielder of Pinaka, the foremost of the Gods, there is no skilled archer like me. On receiving the sanction of that illustrious deity, whose forehead is bedecked with the crescent moon, I can surely destroy in a moment this whole universe with all its organic and inorganic creation.

sn: मया हि राजन् सादिगीश्वरा दिशो विजित्य सर्वा भवतः कृता वशे॥ स राजसूयश्च समाप्तदक्षिणः सभा च दिव्या भवतो ममौजसा।
en: O king, it was I who had defeated all the nations and the chiefs of all the principalities in the world and brought them under your subjection. It was through my influence that your Rajasuya sacrifice had been brought to a happy close by gifts of Dakshina and by a meeting of celestials.

sn: पाणौ पृषत्का निशिता ममैव धनुश्च सज्यं विततं सबाणम्॥ पादौ च मे सरथौ सध्वजौ च न मादृशं युद्धगतं जयन्ति।
en: In my palms there are the signs of sharp swords and stringed bows and arrows and in my soles and the marks of cars and ensigns. That is why a man like me can never be defeated in battle.

sn: हता उदीच्या निहताः प्रतीच्याः प्राच्या निरस्ता दाक्षिणात्या विशस्ताः॥ संशप्तकानां किंचिदेवास्ति शिष्टं सर्वस्य सैन्यस्य हतं मयार्धम्। शेते मया निहता भारतीयं चमू राजन् देवचमूप्रकाशा॥
en: I have slain the enemies from the North, routed the foes from the West, driven off the hostile squadron from the East and exterminated the foes from the South. Indeed I have slain over half the hostile armies; there is left only a small portion of the most unflinching foes. O king, the army of Bharata, with the blazing effulgence of the celestial host, being slain by me are lying flat on the field.

sn: स्तस्माल्लोकानेष करोभि भस्मसात्। जैत्रं रथं भीममास्थाय कृष्ण यावः शीघ्रं सूतपुत्र निहन्तुम्॥
en: With weapons, I slay those alone that are skilled in the use of weapons, that is why I do not make a wholesale massacre of the entire hostile army. O Krishna, let us hasten to slay the son of Suta, riding upon my awe-inspiring and victorious chariot.

sn: राजा भवत्वद्य सुनिर्वृतोऽयं कर्णं रणे नाशयितासि बाणैः। इत्येवमुक्त्वा पुनराह पार्थो युधिष्ठिरं धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठम्॥
en: Today a king Yudhishthira will be pleased. I shall distroyed Karna by my arrows. Thus addressing Arjuna, again said to Yudhishthira, the foremost of man of duties.

sn: अद्यापुत्र सूतमाता भवित्री कुन्ती वाथो वा मया तेन वापि। सत्यं वदाम्यद्य न कर्णमाजी शरैरहत्वा कवचं विमोक्ष्ये॥
en: Today either dame Suta will be bereft of her son by me, or Kunti will be bereft of me by Karna. Verily do I tell you that I won't unlock my mail-cloak today without slaying Karna in battle with my arrows.

sn: संजय उवाच इत्येवमुक्त्वा पुनरेव पार्थो युधिष्ठिरं धर्मभृता वरिष्ठम्। विमुच्य शस्त्राणि धनुर्विसृज्य कोशे च खङ्ग विनिधाय तूर्णम्॥ स वीडया नम्रशिराः किरीटी युधिष्ठिरं प्राञ्जलिरभ्युवाच। प्रसीद राजन् क्षम यन्मयोक्तं काले भवान् वेत्सस्यति तन्नमस्ते॥
en: Sanjaya said Having again thus addressed Yudhishthira, the foremost of the righteous, the diademdecked. Arjuna readily laid aside his weapons and bow and thursted his sword into the scabbard, having thus appeased Yudhishthira he huge down his head in shame and with joined hands thus addressed him-"O king, I bow unto you, be pleased with me; you will understand in due course the gist of all that I have told you."

sn: प्रसाद्य राजानममित्रसाह स्थितोऽब्रवीचैव पुन: प्रवीरः। त्यावर्ततेऽसाध्वभियामि चैनम्॥
en: The valiant Arjuna, having thus appeased Yudhishthira, capable of bearing all enemies and having stood there awhile, said again, “It shall not be deferred, it must be done ere long. There is Karna coming towards me. I must proceed against him.

sn: याम्येष भीमं समरात् प्रमोक्तुं सर्वात्मना सूतपुत्रं च हन्तुम्। तव प्रियार्थं मम जीवितं हि ब्रवीमि सत्यं तदवेहि राजन्॥
en: I am going to extricate Bhimasena from the battle by all means and slay the son of Suta. My life is devoted to perform truth, know it for certain."

sn: इति प्रयास्यन्नुपदृह्य पादौ समुत्थितौ दीप्ततेजाः किरीटी। एतच्छ्रुत्वा पाण्डवो धर्मराजो भ्रातुर्वाक्यं परुषं फाल्गुनस्य॥ उत्थाय तस्माच्छयनादुवाच पार्थं ततो दुःखपरीतचेताः।
en: The diadem-decked Arjuna of blazing effulgence having said this and worshipped Yudhishthira by his feet, rose to proceed to the battle. After having heard these harsh words of Phalguna (Arjuna). Yudhishthira, the foremost of the righteous, with a heavy heart rose from the bed (on which he had been reclining) and said unto him.

sn: कृतं मया पार्थ यथा न साधु येन प्राप्त व्यसनं वः सुघोरम्॥ तस्माच्छिरश्छिन्धि ममेदमद्य कुलान्तकस्याधमपूरुषस्य। पापस्य पापाव्यसनान्वितस्य विमूढबुद्धेरलसस्य भीरोः॥
en: O Arjuna, the wicked deed that I have done has brought upon you this terrible calamity; do you, therefore, chop off today the head of this exterminator of the race, the worst of the family.

sn: वृद्धावमन्तुः परुषस्य चैव किं ते चिरं मे ह्यनुसृत्य रुक्षम्। गच्छाम्यहं वनमेवाद्य पापः सुखं भवान् वर्ततां मद्विहीनः॥
en: A wretch, sinner, dull-headed, idle, coward, insulator of the aged and wanton that I am, what is the good of your thus behaving towards me, after having addressed such rude words?

sn: योग्यो राजा भीमसेनो महात्मा कीबस्य वा मम किं राज्यकृत्यम्। न चापि शक्तः परुषाणि सोढुं पुनस्तवेमानि रुषान्वितस्य॥
en: A sinner that I am, I would repair to the woods this very day, relived of my company may you live in happiness. The magnanimous Bhimasena is worthy of the throne. An impotent that I am, what the use of my having the sovereignty?

sn: भीमोऽस्तु राजा मम जीवितेन न कार्यमद्यावमतस्य वीर। इत्येवमुक्त्वा सहसोत्पपात राजा ततस्तच्छयनं विहाय॥ इयेष निर्गन्तुमथो वनाय तं वासुदेवः प्रणतोभ्युवाच॥
en: I cannot any longer bear the harsh words you spoke being excited with anger. Therefore, let Bhimasena be the king. It is not worth my while to live after being thus insulted." Having expressed himself thus, the king Yudhishthira leaving that bed stood up suddenly and then expressed his intention of proceeding to the woods. Upon this Vasudeva bowing down, said unto him.

sn: राजन् विदितमेतद् वै यथा गाण्डीवधन्वनः। प्रतिज्ञा सत्यसंधस्य गाण्डीवं प्रति विश्रुता॥
en: O king! you know already the vow of the veracious wielder of the Gandiva, in respect of his Gandiva.

sn: ब्रूयाद् एवं गाण्डीवमन्यस्मै देयमित्युत। वध्योऽस्य स पुमाँल्लोके त्वया चोक्तोऽयमीदृशम्॥५०
en: Whoever in this world tells him, 'Give your Gandiva to anotehr,' would be slain by him. And even these words you addressed him just now.

sn: ततः सत्यां प्रतिज्ञां ता पार्थेन प्रतिरक्षता। मच्छन्दादवमानोऽयं कृतस्तव महीपते॥ गुरूणामवमानो हि वध इत्यभिधीयते।
en: O lord of the Earth! that is why Partha simply to keep up that solemn vow, under my instructions, addressed you with those insulting words. Because it is said, that insults to superiors are tantamount to death.

sn: तस्मात् त्वं वै महाबाहो मम पार्थस्य चोभयोः॥ व्यतिक्रममिमं राजन् सत्यसंरक्षणं प्रति।
en: Therefore, O long armed king! forgive us of the unmannerly behaviour of us both, Arjuna and myself.

sn: शरणं त्वां महाराज प्रपन्नौ स्व उभावपि॥ क्षन्तुमर्हसि मे राजन् प्रणतस्याभियाचतः।
en: O king! we both of us surrender ourselves to you. I beseech you, by all means vouchsafe us your pardon.

sn: राधेयस्याद्य पापस्य भूमि: पास्यति शोणितम्॥ सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि हतं विद्ध्यद्य सूतजम्। यस्येच्छसि वधं तस्य गतमप्यस्य जीवितम्॥
en: Today the earth shall soak the blood of that reprobate son of Radha; solemnly I swear before you that you may count upon Suta's son as slain today and know it for certain that whomever you like, he loses his life today.

sn: इति कृष्णवचः श्रुत्वा धर्मराजौ युधिष्ठिरः। ससम्भ्रमं हृषीकेशमुत्थाप्य प्रणतं तदा॥ कृताञ्जलिस्ततो वाक्यमुवाचानन्तरं वचः।
en: Upon this Yudhishthira, the foremost of the righteous, hastened to raise the prostrate Hrishikesha with due honor. Then, folding his hands together, he said unto him these opportune words-

sn: एवमेव यथाऽऽत्य त्वमस्त्येषोऽतिक्रमो मम॥ अनुनीतोऽस्मि गोविन्द तारितश्चास्मि माधव। मोचिता व्यसनाद् घोराद् वयमद्य त्वयाच्युत॥
en: It is just as you said, O Govinda! Let this transgression be in respect of me; there is no harm in that. O Madhava, O Achyuta! I am obliged, to and saved by you; you have rescued us today from a grave calamity.

sn: भवन्तं नाथमासाद्य ह्यावां व्यसनसागरात्। घोरादद्य समुत्तीर्णाबुभावज्ञानमोहितौ॥ त्वबुद्धिप्लवमासाद्य दुःखशोकार्णवाद् वयम्। समुत्तीर्णाः सहामात्याः सनाथाः स्म त्वयाच्युत।।६०
en: Both of us were steeped in ignorance today. It is only through your help that we have been rescued from an ocean of distress. O Achyuta! It is through having obtained your intelligence at your raft that this day we have safely passed over an ocean of grief and remorse. In fact, it is through you that we have been blessed with our relatives and allies.

sn: संजय उवाच धर्मराजस्य तच्छ्रुत्वा प्रीतियुक्तं वचस्ततः। पार्थं प्रोवाच धर्मात्मा गोविन्दो यदुनन्दनः॥
en: Sanjaya said O majesty! Govinda, the religious soul and dignity of Yadu clan began explaining something to Arjuna in response to the vivid statement made by Dharamaraja (Yudhishthira).

sn: इतिस्म कृष्णवचनात् प्रत्युचार्य युधिष्ठिरम्। भभूव विमनाः पार्थः किंचित् कृत्वेन पातकम्॥
en: Having addressed Yudhishthira in such an unbecoming manner and thus being guilty of an unrighteous conduct, Dhananjaya, the son of Pritha, became disconsolate beyond measure.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीद् वासुदेवः प्रहसन्निव पाण्डवम्। कथं नाम भवेदेतद् यदि त्वं पार्थ धर्मजम्॥ असिना तीक्ष्णधारेण हन्या धर्मे व्यवस्थितम्। त्वमित्युक्त्वाथ राजानमेवं कश्मलमाविशः॥
en: Vasudeva (then) in caustic tone addressing the son of Pandu said-"How, O Partha, would you have fared, had you mindful of (your) truthfulness, slain the son of Dharma with the keen edge of your steel. a

sn: हत्वा तु नृपति पार्थ अकरिष्यः किमुत्तरम्। एवं हि दुर्विदो धर्मो मन्दप्रज्ञैर्विशेषतः॥
en: By simply 'you think the king you are affected so much-what, would you have done, O Partha, had you actually fulfilled your promise. The law of policy are indeed too subtle for comprehension, especially to those of weak intellect.

sn: स भवान् धर्मभीरुत्वाद् ध्रुवमैष्यन्महत्तमः। नरकं घोररूपं च भ्रातुर्येष्ठस्य वै वधात्॥
en: For moral scruples you would surely have taken out the life of your eldest and would have thus committed a heinous sin and fallen into eternal perdition.

sn: स त्वं धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठं राजानं धर्मसंहितम्। प्रसादय कुरुश्रेष्ठमेतदत्र मतं मम॥
en: I adjure you, therefore, to assuage the sorrows of the pious king, the adored of the devout and the head of the Kurus.

sn: प्रसाद्य भक्त्या राजानं प्रीते चैव युधिष्ठिर। प्रयावस्त्वरितौ योद्धं सूतपुत्ररथं प्रति॥
en: Let us pacify king Yudhishthira with due obeisance and when he is reconciled let both of us march against the chariot of the son of Suta and fight him out.es

sn: हत्वा तु समरे कर्णं त्वमद्य निशितैः शरैः। विपुला प्रीतिमाधत्स्व धर्मपुत्रस्य मानद॥
en: O bestower of honors, secure the blessings of the son of Dharma, by shooting down Karna with the keen points of your arrows.

sn: एतदत्र महाबाहो प्राप्तकालं मतं मम। एवं कृते कृतं चैव तव कार्यं भविष्यति॥
en: O mighty-aimed one, in my opinion this is the best course you could follow at present. By acting thus you will gain you ends."

sn: ततोऽर्जुनो महाराज लज्जया वै समन्वितः। धर्मराजस्य चरणौ प्रपद्य शिरसा नतः॥ उवाच भरतश्रेष्ठं प्रसीदेति पुनः पुनः। क्षमस्व राजन् यत् प्रोक्तं धर्मकामेन भीरुणा॥
en: After this, O monarch, Arjuna became quite ashamed of himself; bending his head down he touched Yudhishthira's feet and repeatedly said unto that chief of the Bharatas, "O king, be appeased; forgive me for the impropriety of my language towards you; they were given expression to (as the only course left me) for maintaining truthfulness and avoiding sin.”

sn: दृष्ट्वा तु पतितं पद्भ्यां धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। धनंजयममित्रघ्नं रुदन्तं भरतर्षभ।॥ उत्थाय भ्रातरं राजा धर्मराजो धनंजयम्। समाश्लिष्य च सस्नेहं प्ररुरोद महीपतिः॥
en: O giant of the Bharata race, seeing Dhananjaya, the slayer of foes, thus fall at his feet with tears in his eyes, Yudhishthira, the lord of creation, the emblem of religion, rose up from his reclining position and with gushing eyes affectionately embraced him.

sn: रुदित्वा सुचिरं कालं भ्रातरौ सुमहाद्युती। कृतशौचौ महाराज प्रीतिमन्तौ बभूवतुः॥
en: Having thus indulged themselves for some time and assuaged their grief the two brothers of bright effulgence became reconciled to each other and were once again cheerful.

sn: तत अतिश्लिष्य तं प्रेम्णा मूर्ध्नि चाध्राय पाण्डवः। प्रीत्या परमया युक्तो विस्मयंञ्च पुनः पुनः॥ अब्रवीत् तं महेष्वासं धर्मराजे धनंजयम्।
en: Later on the son of Pandu, again giving Jaya a hug and taking the fragrance of his head, became supremely happy and praising his conduct, said-

sn: कर्णेन मे महाबाहो सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः॥ कवचं च ध्वजं चैव धनुः शक्तिर्हयाः शराः। शरैः कृत्ता महेष्वास यतमानस्य संयुगे॥
en: O mighty-wielder of bows, in spite of all my exertions in the battle-field, Karna with his shafts has, in the midst of the whole assembly, shattered my armours pinions, forces, arrows, bows and steeds.

sn: सोऽहं ज्ञात्वा रणे तस्य कर्म दृष्ट्वा च फाल्गुन। व्यवसीदामि दुःखेन न च मे जीवितं प्रियम्॥
en: O Phalguna, thinking of this and witnessing his conduct in the battle, I have been sorely aggrieved. Life has no longer any charm for Ime.

sn: न चेदद्य हि तं वीरं निहनिष्यसि संयुगे। प्राणानेव परित्यक्ष्ये जीवितार्थो हि को मम॥
en: If you do not overcome that indomitable hero in today's battle, then surely I will give up my life, what would be the use of bearing the burden of this body and carrying it on the earth any longer?

sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच विजयो भरतर्षभ। सत्येन ते शपे राजन् प्रसादेन तथैव च। भीमेन च नरश्रेष्ठ यमाभ्यां च महीपते॥ यथाद्य समरे कर्णं हनिष्यामि हतोऽपि वा। महीतले पतिष्यामि सत्येनायुधमालभे॥
en: O mighty scion of the Bharata race, upon hearing Yudhishthira thus express himself, Vijaya replied-"O foremost of kings, O lord of the earth, solemnly do I swear unto you that by your grace, by Bhima and the twins that this day either I shall slay Karna or myself kiss the earth being slain by him. I take this vow upon this weapon."

sn: एवमाभाष्य राजानमब्रवीन्माधवं वचः। अद्य कर्णं रणे कृष्ण सूदयिष्ये न संशयः॥ तव बुद्ध्या हि भद्रं ते वधस्तस्य दुरात्मनः।
en: Having delivered himself thus to the king he addressed the following words to Madhava-“Verily, O Krishna, I will slay Karna in today's battle. May you be blessed for it is only through your tactics that the wretch could be slain.”

sn: एवमुक्तोऽब्रवीत् पार्थ केशवो राजसत्तम॥ शक्तोऽसि भरतश्रेष्ठ हन्तुं कर्णं महाबलम्। एष चापि हि मे कामो नित्यमेव महारथ॥ कथं भवान् रणे कर्णं निहन्यादिति सत्तम।
en: O foremost of kings, upon Partha's uttering these words Keshava said unto him-"O mighty Bharata, you are well worthy of slaying Karna. Indeed, O best of men, O foremost of car-warriors, it has ever been upper most in my thoughts as to how you would succeed in slaying him.”

sn: भूयश्चोवाच मतिमान् माधवो धर्मनन्दनम्॥ युधिष्ठिरेमं बीभत्सुं त्वं सान्त्वयितुमर्हसि। अनुज्ञातु च कर्णस्य वधायाद्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: Then the ever-intelligent Madhava once more turned towards the son of Dharma and said-“O Yudhishthira it is met that you would console Vibhatsu and order him to slay the wretched Karna today.

sn: श्रुत्वा ह्यहमयं चैव त्वां कर्णशरपीडितम्। प्रवृत्ति ज्ञातुमायाताविहावां पाण्डुनन्दन॥
en: O son of Pandu, it is upon hearing that you were being afflicted with the arrows of Karna that we came to ascertain the plight you were in.

sn: दिष्ट्यासि राजन् न हतो दिष्ट्या न ग्रहणं गतः। परिसान्त्वय बीभत्सुं जयमाशाधि चानघ॥
en: O king, it was very fortunate that you were not slain or captured. O holy one, do now console your Vibhatsu and bless him that he may attain victory."

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एह्येहि पार्थ बीभत्सो मां परिष्वज पाण्डव। वक्तव्यमुक्तोऽस्मि हितं त्वया क्षान्तं च तन्मया॥
en: Yudhishthira said Come O Partha, O Vibhatsu, come and embrace me; O son of Pandu, you have addressed me in words befitting the position and for my good and I have forgive you for their expressions.

sn: अहं त्वामनुजानामि जहि कर्णं धनंजय। मन्युं च मा कृथाः पार्थ यन्मयोक्तोऽसि दारुणम्॥३१
en: O Dhananjaya you have my orders to go and slay Karna. Do not, O Partha, take offence with me for the vile expression I have made use of against you.

sn: संजय उवाच ततो धनंजयो राजशिरसा प्रणतस्तदा। पादौ जग्राह पाणिभ्यां भ्रातुर्येष्ठस्य मारिष॥
en: Sanjaya continued O king, thereupon Dhananjaya bent his head low and with his hands took hold of the feet of his eldest brother.

sn: तमुत्थाप्य ततो राजा परिष्वज्य च पीडितम्। मू[पाघ्राय चैवैनमिदं पुनरुवाच ह॥
en: The king them raising him clasped him to his bosom and smelling his head once more addressed him thus :

sn: धनंजय महाबाहो मानितोऽस्मि दृढं त्वाय। माहात्म्यं विजयं चैव भूयः प्राप्नुहि शाश्वतम्॥
en: O Dhananjaya of mighty arms, I feel highly honoured by you, do you attain once more the greatness and victory you ever deserve.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच अद्य तं पापकर्माण सानुबन्धं रणे शरैः। नयाम्यन्तं समासाद्य राधेयं बलगर्वितम्॥
en: Arjuna said Getting hold of that sinful son of Radha, who vaunts of his prowess, I shall in today's battle slay him along with his allies.

sn: येत त्वं पीडितो बाणैदृढमायम्य कार्मुकम्। तस्याद्य कर्मणः कर्णः फलमाप्स्यति दारुणम्॥
en: Karna, who had afflicted you with his arrows shot from a full-drawn bow, would reap the dire effects of his act, this day.

sn: अद्य त्वामनुपश्यति कर्ण हत्वा महीपते। सभाजयितुमाक्रन्दादिति सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: O ruler of the earth, I assure you that I will slay Karna today in dreadful battle and come back to bring unto you the happy tidings walking all the while in your steps.

sn: नाहत्वा विनिवर्तिष्ये कर्णमद्य रणाजिरात्। इति सत्येन ते पादौ स्पृशामि जगतीपते॥
en: O lord of the universe, I swear unto you by your feet that I shall not return from the terrible battle today without having slain Karna.

sn: संजय उवाच इति ब्रुवाणं सुमनाः किरीटिनं युधिष्ठिरः प्राह वचो बृहत्तरम्। यशोऽक्षयं जीवितमाप्सितं ते जयं सदा वीर्यमरिक्षयं तदा॥
en: Sanjaya said As the diadem-decked Arjuna was speaking in this strain, Yudhishthira cheerfully addressed to him these graver words-“Do you ever attain unfading fame, eternal life, ready consummation of hopes, perpetual victory, ceaseless energy and continual success over your enemies!

sn: प्रयाहि वृद्धिं च दिशन्तु देवता यथाहमिच्छामि तवास्तु तत् तथा। प्रयाहि शीघ्रं जहि कर्णमाहवे पुरंदरो वृत्रमिवात्मवृद्धये॥
en: May the gods grant you prosperity! May you realise all that I wish of you! At present go at once to the battle and kill Karna for selfelevation even as Purandara killed Vritra.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: संजय उवाच प्रसाद्य धर्मराजानं प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना. पार्थः प्रोवाच गोविन्दं सूतपुत्रवधोद्यतः॥
en: Sanjaya said On having satisfied Yudhishthira, Partha, bent upon slaying the son of Suta, cheerfully said unto Govinda:

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: कल्पतां मे रथो भूयो युज्यन्तां च हयोत्तमाः। आयुधानि च सर्वाणि सज्जन्तां मे महारथे।॥
en: Let my chariot be again got ready and let the best of steeds be harnessed thereto and let all sorts of arms be placed in that superb vehicle.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: उपावृत्ताश्च तुरगाः शिक्षिताश्चाश्वसादिभिः। रथोपकरणैः सजा उपायान्तु त्वरान्विताः॥ प्रयाहि शीघ्रं गोविन्द सूतपुत्रजिघांसया।
en: The horse, thoroughly trained by expert horsemen, have already refreshed themselves by rolling on the ground. Let them be forth with brought out and equipped in the trappings of the car. O Govinda, make headway, to take away the life of Suta's son.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: एवमुक्तो महाराज फाल्गुनेन महात्मना॥ उवाच दारुकं कृष्णः कुरुं सर्व यथाब्रवीत्। अर्जुनो भरतश्रेष्ठः श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥
en: O sovereign, on being thus addressed by the magnanimous Phalguna, Krishna said to Daruka-"Do all that has been said by Arjuna, the foremost of archers and the best scion of Bharata's race."

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: आज्ञाप्तस्त्वथ कृष्णेन दारुको राजसत्तम। योजयामास स रथं वैयाघ्र शत्रुतापनम्॥ सज्जं निवेदयामास पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः।
en: O best of kings, Daruka on being thus ordered by Krishna, equipped the chariot, covered with tiger-skins and ever awe-inspiring to the enemies. He then informed the magnanimous son of Pandu, that the chariot was ready.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: युक्तं तु तं रथं दृष्ट्वा दारुकेण महात्मना।॥ आपृच्छय धर्मराजानं ब्राह्मणान् स्वस्ति वाच्य च। सुमङ्गलस्वस्त्ययनमारुरोह रथोत्तमम्॥
en: Seeing the chariot equipped by the highsouled Daruka, Arjuna took leave of Yudhishthira and with the Brahmanas' blessings and performance of their many propitiatory rites, then proceeded to ascend his superb chariot.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तस्य राजा महाप्राज्ञो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। आशिषोऽयुक्त स ततः प्रायात् कर्ण रथं प्रति॥
en: On Yudhishthira, the righteous one and of great wisdom, having bestowed his benedictions Arjuna marched against Karna's chariot.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तमायान्तं प्रहेष्वासं दृष्ट्वा भूतानि भारत। निहतं मेनिरे कर्णं पाण्डवेन महात्मना॥
en: O Bharata, seeing that great archer start off for the field all the living beings believed Karna as already slain by the magnanimous Pandava.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: बभूवुर्विमला: सर्वा दिशो राजन् समन्ततः। चाषाक्ष शतपत्राश्च क्रौञ्चाश्चैव जनेश्वर॥ प्रदक्षिणमकुर्वन्त तदा वै पाण्डुनन्दनम्।
en: O king, the whole universe turned calm for the time being. O lord of men blue jays (the king-fishers), wood-packers, herons, began to hover round the son of Pandu.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: बहवः पक्षिणो राजन् पुन्नामानः शुभाः शिवाः॥१२ त्वरयन्तोऽर्जुनं युद्धे हृष्टरूपा ववाशिरे।
en: O king, a fight of birds, of beauty and good omen, called Pung, began to cackle merrily as if to urge Arjuna to hasten to the battle.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: कङ्का गृध्रा बकाः श्येना वायसाश्च विशाम्पते॥ अग्रतस्तस्य गच्छन्ति मांसहेतोभयानकाः।
en: While O monarch, the portentous Kankas, vultures, cranes, hawks and revens flew before him in anticipation of food.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: निमित्तानि च धन्यानि पाण्डवस्य शशंसिरे॥ विनाशमरिसैन्यानां कर्णस्य च वधं प्रति।
en: Besides these other auspicious auguries presaged the extinction of the hostile host and the doom of Karna.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: प्रयातस्याथ पार्थस्य महान् स्वेदो व्यजायत।॥ चिन्ता च विपुला जज्ञे कथं चेदं भविष्यति।
en: While on his way to the field Partha began to perspire copiously and became deeply thoughtful as to how he would gain his end.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: ततो गाण्डीवधन्वानमब्रवीन्मधुसूदनः॥ पार्थं तथा यान्तं चिन्तापरिगतं तदा।
en: Then finding Partha proceeding in such a thoughtful mood Vasudeva's son, the slayer of Madhu, said these words to the wielder of Gandiva.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: वासुदेव उवाच गाण्डीव धन्वन् संग्रामे ये त्वया धनुषा न तेषा मानुषो जेता त्वदन्य इह विद्यते।
en: Vasudeva said O Wielder of Gandiva, there is no man in this world, who could defeat those you have defeated with your bow in the battle-field.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: जिताः॥ दृष्टा हि बहवः शूराः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमाः॥ त्वां प्राप्य समरे शूरं ते गताः परमां गतिम्।
en: I have seen many a hero, valiant like Sakra, who have gone off to the highest regions having encountered you in the battle.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: को हि द्रोणं च भीष्मं च भगदत्तं च मारिष॥ विन्दानुविन्दावावन्तयौ काम्बोजं च सुदक्षिणम्। श्रुतायुषं महावीर्यमच्युतायुषमेव च। प्रत्युद्गम्य भवेत् क्षेमी यो न स्यात् त्वमिव प्रभो॥२०
en: O gifted one, who, that is not equal to you, could in battle withstand Drona and Bhishma and Bhagadatta and Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti and Sudakshina, the chief of the Kambojas and Shrutayudha of mighty prowess and Achyutayudha as well.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तव शस्त्राणि दिव्यानि लाघवं बलमेव च। असम्मोहश्च युद्धेषु विज्ञानस्य च संततिः॥ वेधः पातश्च लक्ष्येषु योगश्चैव तथार्जुन। भवान् देवान् सगन्धर्वान् हन्यात् सह चराचरान्॥२२
en: O Arjuna, you have heavenly weapons and dexterity of hand and energy; you are always clear-handed in the battle-field, well-versed in the science of war, unfailing in your aim and your ready-wit in emergencies and your martial manoeuvres are admirable. O Partha, you can vanquish the gods and Gandharvas together with the organic and inorganic creation.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: पृथिव्यां तु रणे पार्थ न योद्धा त्वत्समः पुमान्। धनुग्रार्हा हि ये केचित् क्षत्रिया युद्धदुर्मदाः॥ आ देवात् त्वत्समं तेषां न पश्यामि शृणोमि च।
en: There is no mortal warrior on earth who can be your rival in battle. There cannot be found any skilled archer like you, either among the invincible Kshatriyas or the gods.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: ब्रह्मणा च प्रजाः सृष्टा गाण्डीवं च महद् धनुः॥ येनं त्वं युध्यसे पार्थ तस्मान्नास्ति त्वया समः।
en: Brahma, the creator of all beings, has himself made that powerful bow Gandiva, O Parthas, which you fight with. And that is why no one can outstrip you in battle.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अवश्यं तु मया वाच्यं यत् पथ्यं तव पाण्डव॥ मावमंस्था महाबाहो कर्णमाहवशोभिनम्।
en: However, O son of Pandu, I shall tell you words that would conduce to your well-being. O strong-armed one, do not think lightly of Karna, who is a glory of the field.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: कर्णो हि बलवान् दृप्तः कृतास्त्रश्च महारथः॥ कृती च चित्रयोधी च देशकालस्य कोविदः।
en: Karna is valiant, proud, an adept in the use of weapons, an expert charioteer, skilled in the tactics of war, a veteran warrior and an able diplomatist.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन संक्षेपाच्छृणु पाण्डव॥ त्वत्समं त्वद्विशिष्टं वा कर्णं मन्ये महारथम्। परमं यत्नमास्थाय त्वया वध्यो महाहवे॥
en: O son of Pandu, to you I need not say much; hear me tell you of him in brief. I regard that mighty car-warrior Karna as being equal, if not superior, to you in prowess. Therefore exert utmost caution in slaying his in the great battle.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तेजसा वह्निसदृशो वायुवेगसमो जवे। अन्तकप्रतिमः क्रोधे सिंहसंहननो बली॥
en: He is valarous like Agni, swift like the speed of the wind, furious like the Destroyer, strong and powerful like the lion.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अष्टरनिर्महाबाहुयूंढोरस्कः सुदुर्जयः। अभिमानी च शूरश्च प्रवीरः प्रियदर्शनः॥
en: He is eight ratnis (i.e. about 168 inches) in height and of long arms. His chest is expanded and strong and he is almost invincible. He is, moreover, chivalrous and an eminent hero and of graceful figure.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सर्वयोधगुणैर्युक्तो मित्राणामभयंकरः। सततं पाण्डवद्वेषी धार्तराष्ट्रहिते रतः॥
en: He possesses all the necessary attributes of an warrior and is a dispeller of the fears of his friends, always hostile to the Pandavas and ever bent upon doing good turns to the sons of Dhritarashtra.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सर्वैविध्यो राधेयो देवैरपि सवासवैः। ऋते त्वामिति मे बुद्धिस्तदद्य जहि सूतजम्॥
en: Methinks that the son of Radha cannot be slain by any one, not even by the gods with Vasava himself at their head, excepting by you alone. Therefore, do you slay the son of Suta today.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: देवैरपि हि संयत्तैर्बिभ्रद्भिर्मासशोणितम्। अशक्यः स रथो जेतुं सर्वैरपि युयुत्सुभिः॥
en: No one made of flesh and blood, not all the warriors, nor even the gods would succeed in defeating that inighty car-warrior in fight, even if they combine together to do so.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: दुरातमानं पापवृत्तं नृशंसं दुष्टप्रज्ञं पाण्डवेयेषु नित्यम्। हीनस्वार्थ पाण्डवेयैर्विरोधे हत्वा कर्ण निश्चितार्थो भवाद्य॥
en: He is wicked, vicious and wanton and ever bears evil designs against the Pandavas. He has no self-interest in this quarrel with the Pandavas. Do you attain success today by slaying Karna in battle.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तं सूतपुत्रं रथिनां वरिष्ठं निष्कालिकं कालवशं नयाद्य। तं सूतपुत्रं रथिनां वरिष्ठं हत्वा प्रीति धर्मराजे कुरुष्व॥
en: The son of a charioteer (Karna), the best chariot fighter thinks himself beyond the reach of Yama. Enslave him to Yama today. Kill Karna, the son of a charioteer today for the pleasure of Dharamraja, Yudhishthira.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: जानामि ते पार्थ वीर्यं यथावद् दुर्वारणीयं च सुरासुरैश्च। नसौ दर्पात् सूतपुत्रो दुरात्मा॥
en: O Partha! I am known to your might and valour toughest to bring down even for gods and monsters both. Karna, the wicked son of a charioteer humiliated Pandavas always under sheer influence of his super ego.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: आत्मानं मन्यते वीरं येन पापः सुयोधनः। तमद्य मूलं पापानां जहि सौतिं धनंजय॥
en: O Dhananjaya, the sinful Suyodhana poses himself as a hero only counting upon Karna's valour. Do you today strike at the root of all evils by slaying down that son of Suta.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: खङ्गजिआँ धनुरास्यं शरदंष्ट्रं तरस्विनम्। दृप्तं पुरुषशार्दूलं जहि कर्ण धनंजय॥
en: O Dhananjaya, do slay that mighty Karna, who has the sword for his tongue, the bow for his mouth, the arrows for his teeth and who is moreover arrogant and energetic. Slaughter him.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अहं त्वामनुजानामि वीर्येण च बलेन च। जहि कर्ण रणे शूर मातङ्गमिव केसरी॥
en: I am fully aware of your chivalry and strength. Do, O hero, slay that Karna battle even as a lion kills an elephant.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Arjuna
sn: यस्य वीर्येण वीर्यं ते धार्तराष्ट्रोऽवमन्यते। तमद्य पार्थ संग्रामे कर्ण वैकर्तनं जहि॥
en: Do in today's battle kill that Vaikartana Karna, counting upon whose prowess the sons of Dhritarashtra over look your manly virtues.

sn: संजय उवाच ततः पुनरमेयात्मा केशवोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत्। कृतसंकल्पमायन्तं वधे कर्णस्य भारत॥
en: Sanjaya said O Bharata, then again did Kesava of magnanimous heart address the following words to Arjuna, who was proceeding resolutely to slay Karna.

sn: अद्य सप्तदशाहानि वर्तमानस्य भारत। विनाशस्यातिघोरस्य नरवारणवाजिनाम्॥
en: Today, O Bharata, is the seventeenth day of this horrible carnage of men, elephants and horses.

sn: भूत्वा हि विपुला सेना तावकानां परैः सह। अन्योन्यं समरं प्राप्य किंचिच्छेषा विशाम्पते॥
en: O sovereign, at first your own troops and those of the hostile party were a legion, but being engaged in fight there have been left but a small remnant.

sn: भूत्वा वै कौरवाः पार्थ प्रभूतगजवाजिनः। त्वां वै शत्रु समासाद्य विनष्टा रणमूर्धनि॥
en: Though the Kauravas had, at the outset, numerous steeds and elephants, yet they have been routed on the field as they had to face yourself as their foe.

sn: एते ते पृथिवीपालाः सृञ्जयाश्च समागताः। त्वां सभासाद्य दुर्धर्षं पाण्डवाश्च व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: These potentates and these united forces of the Srinjayas and these Pandavas have been successful in holding their ground, only because they have such an unflinching leader in you.

sn: पाञ्चालैः पाण्डववैर्मत्स्यैः कारूषैश्चेदिभिः सह। त्वया गुप्तैरमित्रनैः कृतः शत्रुगणक्षयः॥
en: O destroyer of foes, being under your protection, the Panchala, Pandava, Matsya, Karusa and Chedis hosts have been sweeping away the hostile army.

sn: को हि शक्तो रणे जेतुं कौरवांस्तात संयुगे। अन्यत्र पाण्डवान् युद्धे त्वया गुप्तान् महारथान्॥
en: O Sire, who else could have vanquished the combined army of the Kauravas had not the valiant Pandavas been fighting under your aegis?

sn: शक्तस्त्वं हि रणे जेतुं ससुरासुरमानुषान्। त्रील्लोकान् समरे युक्तान् किं पुनः कौरवं बलम्॥८
en: What need I speak of defeating the Kauravas? Single-handed you can vanquish in battle the Asuras, celestials and human beings of the three worlds put together.

sn: भगदत्तं च राजानं कोऽन्यः शक्तसत्वया बिना। जेतुं पुरुषशार्दूल योऽपि स्याद् वासवोपमः॥
en: O mighty one, who else, excepting yourself, could have conquered Bhagadatta in fight, even were he powerful like Vasava himself.

sn: तथेमा विपुलां सेनां गुप्ता पार्थ त्वयानघ। न शेकुः पार्थिवाः सर्वे चक्षुर्भिरपि वीक्षितुम्॥
en: O holy Partha, no mortal could even gaze upon this vast army, being as they were, under your protection.

sn: तथैव सततं पार्थ रक्षिताभ्यां त्वाय रणे। धृष्टद्युम्नशिखण्डिभ्यां भीष्मद्रोणौ निपातितौ॥
en: O Partha, Dhristadyumna and Shikhandi had succeeded in slaying Drona and Bhishma, only because you protected them in battle.

sn: को हि शक्तो रणे पार्थ भारतानां महारथौ। भीष्मद्रोणौ युधा जेतुं शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमौ॥
en: Or, O Partha, who else could have conquered in battle those most eminent warriors of the Bharata race-Drona and Bhishma, endued with the prowess of a Sakra.

sn: को हि शान्तनवं भीष्मं द्रोणं वैकर्तनं कृपम्। द्रौणिं च सौमदत्तिं च कृतवर्माणमेव च॥ सैन्धवं मद्रराजानं राजानं च सुयोधनम्। वीरान् कृतास्त्रान् समरे सर्वानेवानिवर्तिनः॥ अक्षौहिणीपतीनुग्रान संहतान् युद्धदुर्मदान्। त्वामृते पुरुषव्याघ्र जेतुं शक्तः पुमानिह॥
en: O most powerful one, who else but you could defeat those formidable leaders of Aksouhinis, those unflinching and invincible heroes, Bhishma-son of Shantanu, Drona, Vaikartana, Kripa and Drona's son and King Duryodhana himself, all united together and adepts in wielding arms.

sn: श्रेण्यश्च बहुलाः क्षीणाः प्रदीर्णाश्वरथद्विपाः। नानाजनपदाचोग्राः क्षत्रियाणमर्षिणाम्॥
en: Numerous detachments of (hostile) soldiers have been extirpated; their cars, horses and elephants have been cut down (by you), as also numbers of indignant and impetuous Kshatriyas hailing from various provinces.

sn: गोवासदासमीयानां वसातीनां च भारत। प्राच्यानां वाटधानानां भोजानां चाभिमानिनाम्॥ उदीर्णाश्वगजा सेना सर्वक्षत्रस्य भारत। त्वां समासाद्य निधनं गता भीमं च भारत॥
en: O Bharata (lo) the forces of the Gobasas, the Dasmiyas, Basatis, the Easterners, the Batadhanas and the sensitive Bhojas and of other Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, with their best horses and elephants, have all been slain confronting you and Bhima (in battle).

sn: उग्राश्च भीमकर्माणस्तुषारा यवनाः खशाः। दाभिसारा दरदाः शका माठरतङ्गणाः॥ आन्ध्रकाश्च पुलिन्दाश्च किराताश्चोग्रविक्रमाः। म्लेच्छाश्च पर्वतीयाश्च सागरानूपवासिनः॥ संरम्भिणो युद्धशौण्डा बलिनो दण्डपाणयः। एते सुयोधनस्यार्थे संरब्धाः कुरुभिः सह॥ न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुं त्वदन्येन परंतप।
en: The Tusharas, the Yavanas, the Khashas, the Darbabhisaras, the Daradas, the Shakas, the Ramathas, the Tanganas, the Andhraks, the Pulindas, all of fierce temperament and awful deeds and the Kiratas of formidable prowess and the Mlechhas, the mountain tribes and the people inhabiting the sea coasts, all of whom are very powerful unflinching in battle and wielders of maces, have gathered round the standard of the Kurus and been fighting hard for Suyodhana. And none else but you, O scorcher of foes, could defeat them in battle.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रमुदग्रं हि व्यूढं दृष्ट्वा महद् बलम्॥ यदि त्वां न भवेस्त्राता प्रतीयात् को नु मानवः।
en: If you had not come to the rescue who else could advance against the mighty troops of the Dhartarashtras arrayed in battle order?

sn: तत् सागरमिवोधुतं रजसा संवृत्तं बलम्॥ विदार्य पाण्डवैः क्रुद्धस्त्वया गुप्तैर्हतं बिभो।
en: O puissant one, the hostile troops shrouded with dust looked like a surging sea and the infuriated Pandavas, forcing their way amongst them, threw them over-board.

sn: मगधानामधिपतिर्जयत्सेनो महाबलः॥ अद्य सप्तैव चाहानि हतः संख्येऽभिमन्युना।
en: Ten mighty Jayatsena, the king of the Magadhas, was slain in battle by Abhimanyu these seven days past.

sn: ततो दशसहस्राणि गजानां भीमकर्मणाम्॥ जधान गदया भीमस्तस्य राज्ञः परिच्छदम्। ततोऽन्येभिहता नागा रथाश्च शतशो बलात्॥
en: Ten thousand powerful elephants, forming the king's retinue, were then struck down by Bhimasena with his mace. Later on hundreds of other elephants and charioteer fell through Bhima's powerful hands.

sn: तदेवं समरे पार्थ वर्तमाने महाभये। भीमसेनं समासाद्य त्वां च पाण्डव कौरवाः॥ सवाजिरथमातङ्गा मृत्युलोकमितो गताः।
en: Therefore, O Partha, in the course of this terrible battle the Kauravas, along with their steeds, cars and elephants, have fallen victims of Death no sooner they encountered Bhimasena and yourself.

sn: तथा सेनामुखे तत्र निहते पार्थ पाण्डवैः॥ भीष्मः प्रासृजदुग्राणि शरजालानि मारिष।
en: O Partha, the van of the Kaurava host on being slain by the Pandavas, Bhishma shot forth showers of deadly arrows.

sn: स चेदिकाशिपाञ्चालन करूषान् मत्स्यकेकयान्॥२९ शरैः प्रच्छाद्य निधनमनयत् परमास्त्रवित्।
en: Skilled in the use of celestial weapons he covered the Chedis, the Kashis, the Panchalas, the Karushas, the Matsyas and the Kaikeyas, with his arrows and slew them to a man.

sn: तस्य चापच्युतैर्बाणैः परदेहविदारणैः॥ पूर्णामाकाशमभवद् रुक्मपुङ्खैरजिह्मगैः।
en: The atmosphere became thick with goldfeathered, straight-shot deadly arrows, that were discharged from his bow.

sn: हन्याद् रथसहस्राणि एकैकेनैव मुष्टिना॥ लक्षं नरद्विपान् हत्वा समेतान् समहाबलान्।
en: Discharging flights of shafts at a time he struck down thousands of charioteers. He killed in all a hundred thousand powerful men and elephants.

sn: गत्या दशम्या ते गत्वा जनुर्वाजिरथद्विपान्॥ हित्वा नवगतीर्दुष्टाः स बाणनाहवेऽत्यजत्।
en: The shafts he shot during the battle did not take any of the nine wrong courses, but flying direct through the tenth (and the approved) course destroyed many steeds, cars and elephants.

sn: दिनानि दश भीष्मेण निघ्नता तावकं बलम्॥ शून्याः कृता रथोपस्था हताश्च गजवाजिनः।
en: Massacring the (Pandava) troops for ten days together, Bhishma rendered the terraces of many a car empty and slew numberless elephants and steeds.

sn: दर्शयित्वाऽऽत्मनो रूपं रुदोपेन्द्रसमं युधि॥ पाण्डवानामनीकानि प्रगृह्यसौ व्यशातयत्।
en: Assuming the form, of Rudra or that of Upendra in battle, he afflicted the Pandava detachment and played a havoc with them.

sn: विनिघ्नन् पृथिवीपालांश्चेदि पञ्चालकेकयान्॥ अदहत् पाण्डवी सेनां रथाश्वगजसंकुलाम्। मजन्तचमप्लवे मन्दमुजिहीर्षुः सुयोधनम्॥
en: The wicked Suyodhana, bereft of a cause was about to be drowned in the sea of misfortune and with the view of rescuing him Bhishma slaughtered the rulers of the Chedis, the Panchalas and the Kaikeyas and caused a great carnage amongst the Pandava army teeming with cars, steeds with elephants.

sn: तथा चरन्तं समरे तपन्तमिव भास्करम्। पदातिकोटिसाहस्त्राः प्रवरायुधपाणयः॥ न शेकुः संजया द्रष्टुं तथैवान्ये महीक्षितः। विचरन्तं तथा तं तु संग्रामे जितकाशिनम्॥ सर्वोद्यमेन महता पाण्डवा समभिद्रवत्।
en: As he careered in battle, resplendent like the Sun himself neither the innumerable infantry of the Srinjayas, all well armed, nor the other rulers of the earth were even able to look at him. Yet the Pandava troops with all their resources made a giant effort against the victorious Bhishma who was thus careering in the battle.

sn: स तु विद्राव्य समरे पाण्डवन् संजयानपि॥ एक एव रणे भीष्म एकवीरत्वमागतः।
en: Indeed he had achieved an unrivalled heroism in the field, having routed the Pandavas and the Srinjayas all single-handed in battle.

sn: तं शिखण्डी समासाद्य त्वया गुप्तो महाव्रतम्॥ जघान पुरुषव्याघ्रं शरैः संनतपूर्वभिः। स एष पतितः शेते शरतल्पे पितामहः॥ त्वां प्राप्य पुरुषव्याघ्र वृत्रः प्राप्येव वासवम्।
en: Being under your powerful protection Sikhandin encountered him and with his straight shafts slew that foremost of men. O mighty one, as the Asura Vritra courted his death obtaining Vasava for his foe, so having obtained you (as his foe) there lies on a bed of arrows that grandsire (wrapt in eternal sleep).

sn: द्रोणः पञ्चदिनान्युमो विधम्य रिपुवाहिनीम्॥ कृत्वा व्यूहमभेद्यं च पातयित्वा महारथान्। जयद्रथस्य समरे कृत्वा रक्षां महारथः॥ अन्तकप्रतिमश्चोग्रो रात्रियुद्धेऽदहत् प्रजाः।
en: The violent Drona having arranged his troops in an impenetrable array has slain the army of the enemies and many a mighty charioteer for five days together. That valiant charioteer having protected Jayadratha in battle committed a havoc amongst the hostile army during the nocturnal fight, like the fierce Destroyer himself.

sn: दग्ध्वा योधाञ्छरैर्वीरो भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्॥ धृष्टद्युम्नं समासाद्य स गतः परमां गतिम्।
en: Having with his arrows killed numerous warriors that valiant and chivalrous son of Bharadvaja, at last attained highest and on encountering Dhristadyumna.

sn: यदि वाद्य भवान् युद्धे सूतपुत्रमुखान् रथान्॥ नावारयिष्यः संग्रामे न स्म द्रोणो व्यनंक्ष्यत।
en: If you had not held at day Suta's son and other charioteers in the battle that day, then Drona would never have been slain.

sn: भवता तु बलं सर्व धार्तराष्ट्रस्य वारितम्॥ ततो द्रोणो हतो युद्धे पार्षतेन धनंजय।
en: O Dhananjaya, you kept engaged the entire Dhartarashtra forces and thus it was that the son of Prishata could slay Drona.

sn: एवं वा को रणे कुर्यात् त्वदन्यः क्षत्रियो युधि॥ यादृशं ते कृतं पार्थ जयद्रथवधं प्रति।
en: O Partha, who else among the Kshatriyas but you, could have achieved such feats (of as material strength), you did when overthrowing Jayadratha?

sn: निवार्य सेनां महतीं हत्वा शूरांश्च पार्थिवान्॥ निहतः सैन्धवो राजा त्वयास्त्रबलतेजसा।
en: Having thwarted the vast host and slain numerous valiant kings you, with the strength of your weapons, have slain the ruler of the Sindhus.

sn: आश्चर्य सिन्धुराजस्य वधं जानन्ति पार्थिवाः॥ अनाश्चर्यं हि तत् त्वत्तस्तवं हि पार्थं महारथः।
en: O Partha, to the mortals the slaughter of the ruler of the Sindhus seem to be exceedingly strange, but to you it is no wonder, as you are an eminent charioteer.

sn: त्वां हि प्राप्य रणे क्षत्रमेकाहादिति भारत॥ नश्यमानमहं युक्तं मन्येयमिति मे मतिः।
en: O Bharata, methinks, it would not appear impossible even if all the Kshatriyas were to be exterminated in the course of a day, with you for their adversary in the field.

sn: सेयं पार्थ चमूर्घोरा धार्तराष्ट्रस्य संयुगे॥ हतसर्वस्ववीरा हि भीष्मद्रोणौ यदा हतौ।
en: O Partha, now that Bhishma and Drona are slain, the fierce Dhritarashtra force may well be regarded to have lost all their heroes.

sn: शीर्णप्रवरयोधाऽद्य हतवाजिरथद्विपा॥ हीना सूर्येन्दुनक्षत्रैद्यौरिवाभाति भारती।
en: With their chef and foremost warriors slain, with their horses, chariots and elephants struck down, the Bharata army look like the welkin bereft of the Sun, the Moon and the Stars.

sn: विध्वस्ता हि रणे पार्थ सेनेयं भीमविक्रम॥ सेना शक्रस्येव पराक्रमैः।
en: O Partha, as the Asura hosts were routed by the prowess of Sakra in days of yore, so yonder host of terrible prowess have been vanquished by you.

sn: तेषां हतवशिष्टास्तु सन्ति पञ्च महारथाः॥ अश्वत्थामा कृतवर्मा कर्णो मद्राधिपः कृपः।
en: Besides the slain there are now left only five mighty charioteers, Ashvatthama, Kritavarma, Karna, Shalya-the ruler of Madra and Kripa.

sn: आसुरीव पुरा तांस्त्वमद्य नरव्याघ्र हत्वा पञ्च महारथान्॥ हतामित्रः प्रयच्छोर्वी राज्ञे सद्वीपपत्तनाम्।
en: O mightiest of men, by killing those five eminent charioteers today may you get rid of all foes and bestow this earth with all its islands, cities and seas to King Yudhishthira.

sn: साकाशजलपाताला सपर्वतमहावनाम्॥ प्राप्नोत्वमितवीर्यश्रीरद्य पार्थो वसुन्धराम्।
en: Let the Pritha's son of illimitable valour and fortune obtain today the entire Earth with the mountains and forests and water (on it), the firmament (above it) and the nether regions (below it).

sn: एतां पुरा विष्णुरिव हत्वा दैतेयदानवान्॥ प्रयच्छ मेदिना राज्ञे शक्रायैव हरिर्यथा।
en: As Vishnu, in days of yore, made a gift of the three worlds to Sakra after overthrowing the Daityas and the Danavas, so may you bestow the Earth on the king after slaying the Kauravas.

sn: अद्य मोदन्तु पञ्चाला निहतेष्वरिषु त्वया। विष्णुना निहतेष्वेव दानवेयुषु देवताः॥
en: On their enemies being slain, let the Panchalas rejoice today as did the celestials on the occasion of Vishnu's exterminating the Danavas.

sn: यदि वा द्विपदां श्रेष्ठ द्रोणं मानयतो गुरुम्। अश्वत्थाम्नि कृपा तेऽस्ति कृपे वाचार्यगौरवात्॥ अत्यन्तापचितान् बन्धून मानयन् मातृबान्धवान्। कृतवर्माणमासाद्य न नेष्यसि यमक्षयम्॥ भ्रातरं मातुरासाद्य शल्यं मद्रजनाधिपम्। यदि त्वमरविन्दाक्ष दयावान् न जिघांससि॥ इमं पापमति क्षुद्रमत्यन्तं पाण्डवान् प्रति। कर्णमद्य नरश्रेष्ठ जह्याः सुनिशितैः शरैः॥
en: If out of respect for that illustrious personage, your preceptor Drona, you feel sympathy for Ashvatthama, if again out of reverence due to a preceptor, you are kindly disposed towards Kripa. If out of high regard for your material relatives you do not dispatch Kritavarman today to the regions of Pluto in encountering him. If, O lotus-eyed one, encountering your mother's brother, Shalya, the king of Madras, out of mere compassion, you do not deign to strike him down. Do you, O mighty one, with your sharp shafts hasten to slay that wretched Karna today who, at heart, cherishes utmost hatred for the sons of Pandu.

sn: एतत् ते सुकृतं कर्म नात्र किंचन युज्यते। वयमप्यनूजानीमो नात्र दोषोऽस्ति कश्चन॥
en: It is your noblest duty; nor is there any impropriety in it; we all assent to it and there is no guilt in that.

sn: दहने यत् सपुत्राया दिशि मातुस्तवानघ। द्यूतार्थे यच युष्मासु प्रावर्तत सुयोधनः॥ तस्य सर्वस्य दुष्टात्मा कर्णो वै मूलमित्युत।
en: O sinless one, in that attempt to burn your mother with all her children during the night and the behaviour that Suyodhana bore towards you during the play at dice, that wretched Karna lay at the bottom of all.

sn: कर्णाद्धि मन्यते त्राणं नित्यमेव सुयोधनः॥ ततो मामपि संरब्धो निग्रहीतुं प्रचक्रमे।
en: Suyodhana has ever a firm conviction that it is Karna alone who will help him out (of this scrape). That is why he has been filled with rage and tries also to afflict me.

sn: स्थिरा बुद्धिनरेन्द्रस्य धार्तराष्ट्रस्य मानद॥ कर्णः पार्थान् रणे सर्वान् विजेष्यति न संशयः।
en: O giver of honours, it is the firm belief of the royal Dhartarashtras that Karna will, to a certainty, slay all the Parthas in battle.

sn: कर्णमाश्रित्य कौन्तेय धार्तराष्ट्रेण विग्रहः॥ रोचितो भवता सार्धं जानतापि बलं तव।
en: O son of Kunti, it is through having secured the aid of Karna that Dhritarashtra's son has ventured to fight with you, though he is full well aware of your prowess.

sn: कर्णो हि भाषते नित्यमहं पार्थान् समागतान्॥ वासुदेवं च दाशार्ह विजेष्यामि महारथम्।
en: Karna also often says that, “I will conquer the assembled Parthas and Vasudeva, that valiant charioteer of Dasharha's race. roars

sn: प्रोत्साहयन् दुरात्मानं धार्तराष्ट्र सुदुर्मतिम्॥ समिती गर्जते कर्णस्तमद्य जहि भारत।
en: O Bharata, that wicked Karna thus always in the court (of the Kurus) of Dhritarashtra. Do you, therefore, slay him today.

sn: यच युष्मासु पापं वै धार्तराष्ट्रः प्रयुक्तवान्॥ तत्र सर्वत्र दुष्टात्मा कर्णः पापमतिर्मुखम्।
en: It is the profane and malignant Karna who is mainly responsible for all the evils that have been done to you by Dhritarashtra's son.

sn: यच तद् धार्तराष्ट्रस्य क्रूरैः षड्भिर्महारथैः॥ अपश्यं निहतं वीरं सौभद्रमृषभेक्षणम्। द्रोणद्रौणिकृपान् वीरान् कर्षयन्तं नरर्षभान्॥ निर्मनुष्यांश्च मातङ्गान् विरथांश्च महारथान्। व्यश्वारोहांश्च तुरगान् पत्तीन् व्याधुजीविनः॥ कुर्वन्तमृषभस्कन्धं कुरुवृष्णियशस्करम्। विधमन्तमनीकानि व्यथयन्तं महारथान्॥ मनुष्यवाजिमातङ्गान् प्राहिण्वन्तं यमक्षयम्। शरैः सौभद्रमायान्तं दहन्तमिव वाहिनीम्॥ तन्मे दहति गात्राणि सखे सत्येन ते शपे। यत् तत्रापि च दुष्टात्मा कर्णोऽभ्यद्रुह्यत प्रभो॥ अशक्नुवंश्चाभिमन्योः कर्णः स्थातु रणेऽग्रतः। सौभद्रशरनिर्भिन्नो विसंज्ञः शोणितोक्षितः॥
en: I have seen the valiant son of Subhadra, of lustrous eyes, fall at the hands of six heartless charioteers belonging to the Dhritarasthra force. Harassing mighty heroes like Drona, Drona's son and Kripa and others, he divested elephants of their riders and mighty charioteers of their cars. Abhimanyu of mighty neck, the pride and the glory of both the Kurus and the Vrisnis, made also the steeds bereft of their riders and the infantry, their arms and life. Overthrowing the hostile files and harassing many powerful charioteers, he has packed off numbers of men and steeds and elephants to the gates of Pluto. O friend, by truth I swear unto you that I am burning at the thought that while Subhadra's son was thus advancing, striking down with his arrows the hostile force, even then, O lord Partha, the malevolent Karna, unable to withstand him in a face to face fight, had been engaged in acts of hostility to that heroic Abhimanyu. Mangled with the arrows of Subhadra's son, rendered senseless and bathed in blood.

sn: निःश्वसन क्रोधसंदीप्तो विमुखः सायकार्दितः। अपयान्कृतोत्साहो निराशश्चापि जीविते॥
en: Karna became highly enraged and drew heavy breaths, till at last covered with shafts he thought of turning away from the field. Heartily wished to bear a retreat, but finding no means of egress of doing so, giving up all the while his hopes of life.

sn: तस्थौ सुविह्वल: संख्ये प्रहारजनितश्रमः। अथ द्रोणस्य समरे तत्कालसदृशं तदा॥ श्रुत्वा कर्णो वचः क्रूरं ततश्चिच्छेद कार्मुकम्।
en: Exhausted and stupefied with the wounds received, he had to roam about in the field. At last hearing the opportune, though wanton, words of Drona in battle, Karna cut-off Abhimanyu's bow.

sn: ततश्छिन्नायुधं तेन रणे पञ्च महारथाः॥ तं चैव निकृतिप्रज्ञाः प्राहरञ्छरवृष्टिभिः।
en: On his bow being thus cut asunder in that battle, five mighty charioteers of blunt conscience slew him with showers of arrows.

sn: तस्मिन विनिहते वीरे सर्वेषां दुःखमाविशत्॥ प्राहसत् स तु दुष्टात्मा कर्णः स च सुयोधनः।
en: On the hero being thus slain all were touched at heart. Only that wicked-hearted Karna and Suyodhana laughed.

sn: यच कर्णोऽब्रवीत् कृष्णां सभायां परुषं वचः॥ प्रमुखे पाण्डवेयानां कुरुणां च नृशंसवत्।
en: (Verily you remember) the vile epithets that Karna so cruelly flung towards Krishna in the (Kuru) court before both the Kurus the Pandavas.

sn: विनष्टाः पाण्डवाः कृष्णे शाश्वतं नरकं गताः॥ पतिमन्यं पृथुश्रोणि वृणीष्व मृदुभाषिणि। एषा त्वं धृतराष्ट्रस्य दासीभूता निवेशनम्॥ प्रविशारालपक्ष्माक्षि न सन्ति पतयस्त्व। न पाण्डवाः प्रभवन्ति तव कृष्णे कथञ्चन॥
en: O Krishna, the Pandavas have been slain and are gone to eternal damnation; do you, therefore, O one of sweet voice and heavy posteriors, take to yourself another lord. Betake not to the service of Dhritarashtra as a maid, for, O lotus-eyed one, your husbands are no more (in the land of the living). O Krishna, this day forth the Pandavas will no longer have any control over you.

sn: दासभार्या च पाञ्चालि स्वयं दासी च शोभने। अद्य दुर्योधनो ह्येकः पृथिव्यां नृपतिः स्मृतः॥
en: O Princess of Panchala, you are now the wife of men that are servants and O beautiful one, yourself, a maid. Duryodhana alone is regarded as the ruler of this earth.

sn: सर्वे चास्य महीपाला योगक्षेममुपासते। पश्येदानीं यथा भद्रे विनष्टाः पाण्डवाः समम्॥ अन्योन्यं समुदीक्षन्ते धार्तराष्ट्रस्य तेजसा।
en: Today all the other lords are engaged in helping him towards the good government of his state. Lo, O amiable one, how all the Pandavas have equally fallen, under the prowess of Dhirtarasthtra's son and have now been staring at each other.

sn: व्यक्तं षण्ढतिला ह्येते निरये च निमज्जितः॥ प्रेष्यवचापि राजानमुपस्थास्यन्ति कौरवम्।
en: Verily these (men) are like sesame seeds without kernel and have fallen into purgatory and they will have to serve ere long that foremost of Kaurava Kings.

sn: इत्युक्तवानधर्मज्ञस्तदा परमदुर्मतिः॥ पापः पापवचः कर्णः शृण्वतस्त्व भारत।
en: O Bharata, these vile words were uttered by that sinful, debased, mischievous and unprincipled Karna at that time, in your hearing.

sn: अद्य पापास्य तद् वाक्यं सुवर्णविकृताः शराः।।९० शमयन्तु शिलाधौतास्त्वयास्ता जीवितच्छिदः।
en: Let your gold-plated and sharpened shafts, capable of dealing death to the living today assuage the sorrows caused by those words of effrontery.

sn: यानि चान्यानि दुष्टात्मा पापानि कृतवांस्त्वयि॥ तान्यद्य जीवितं चास्य शमयन्तु शरास्तव।
en: Let your shafts retaliate all the other mischief's done to you by that wicked one by slaying him.

sn: गाण्डीव प्रहितान् घोरानद्य गात्रैः स्पृशञ्छरान्॥ कर्णः स्मरतु दुष्टात्मा वचनं द्रोणभीष्मयोः।
en: Let the wicked Karna feel the pangs of those deadly shafts sped from the Gandiva and remember the words of Bhishma and Drona.

sn: सुवर्णपुङ्खा नाराचाः शत्रुघ्ना वैद्युतप्रभाः॥ त्वयास्तास्तस्य वर्माणि भित्वा पास्यन्ति शोणितम्।
en: Let the gold-feathered iron shafts, capable of dealing death to the enemies and emitting rays of lightning, sped by you go straight into the vital organs and drink his blood.

sn: उपास्त्वद्भुजनिर्मुक्ता मर्म भित्वा महाशराः॥ अद्य कर्णं महावेगा: प्रेषयन्तु यमक्षयम्।
en: Let the sharp and winged arrow of irresistible force shot by your arms touch Karna to the core and dispatch him off to the den of Pluto.

sn: अद्य हाहाकृता दीना विषण्णास्त्वच्छरार्दिताः॥ प्रपतन्तं रथात् कर्णं पश्यन्तु वसुधाधिपाः।
en: Let the lords of this hemisphere, seeing Karna fall today from off his chariot, covered with your shafts, despondent and heart-broken, indulge themselves in grief.

sn: अद्य शोणितसम्मग्नं शयानं पतितं भुवि॥ अपविद्धायुधं कर्ण दीनाः पश्यन्तु बान्धवाः।
en: Let his relations with distress witness today the (sad) spectacle of Karna's falling prostrate and lying down on the bosom of the Earth, weltered in blood and bereft of arms.

sn: हस्तिकक्षो महानस्य भल्लेनोन्मथितस्त्वया। प्रकम्पमानः पततु भूमावाधिरथेध्वजः॥
en: Let the huge standard of Adhiratha's son, bearing the ensign of the elephant's rope, totter to its fall from the shots of crescent-shaped arrows.

sn: त्वया शरशतैश्छिन्नं रथं हेमविभूषितम्। हतयोधाश्वमुत्सृज्य भीतः शल्यः पलायताम्॥
en: Let Shalya, alarmed with the scene of his golden chariot thus scattered to the winds and his charioteer and steeds taken off with numberless darts of your arrows, deserting his empty car, beat a hasty retreat (from the field).

sn: त्वं चेत् कर्णसुतं पार्थ सूतपुत्रस्य पश्यतः। प्रतिज्ञावारणार्थाय निहनिष्यसि सायकैः॥ हतं कर्णस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा प्रियं पुत्रं दुरात्मवान्। स्मरतां द्रोणभीष्माभ्यां वचः क्षत्तुश्च मानद॥
en: Partha! You honour always the meritorious people. In case, you kill Vrishasena, son of Karna before his eyes in order to keep your commitment, he will definitely remember the advice given him by Dronacharya, Bhishma and Vidura time to time under influence of agony caused by separation of his son (i.e. so killed by you).

sn: ततः सुयोधनो दृष्ट्वा हतमाधिरथिं त्वया। निराशो जीविते त्वद्य राज्ये चैव भवत्वरिः॥
en: And then let the enemy Suyodhana, witness in today Adhiratha's son thus fall a victim to your arms, despair of his life and his sovereignty.

sn: एते द्रवन्ति पञ्चाला वध्यमानाः शितैः शरैः। कर्णेन भरतश्रेष्ठ पाण्डवानुजिहीर्षवः॥
en: Look up yonder, O foremost of the line of Bharata, (and see how) the Panchalas are dropping off from the sharp points of Karna's arrows in their anxiety to rescue the Pandavas.

sn: पञ्चालान् द्रौपदेयांश्च धृष्टद्युम्न् शिखण्डिना। धृष्टद्युम्नतनूजांश्च शतानीकं च नाकुलिम्॥ नकुलं सहदेव च दुर्मुखं जनमेजयम्। सुधर्माणं सात्यकिं च विद्धि कर्णवशं गतान्॥
en: Know it for certain that the Panchalas, the sons of Draupadi, Dhristadyumna, Shikhandin and the sons of Dhristadyumna and Shatanika, the of Nakula (himself), Sahadeva, Durmukha, Janamejaya and Sudhurman and Satyaki, are held in subjection by Karna. son

sn: अभ्याहतानां कर्णेन पञ्चालानामसौ रणे। श्रूयते निनदो घोरस्त्वद्वन्धूनां परंतप॥
en: (From off the scene of action) the howling groans, O subduer of foes, of those allies of yours, the Panchalas-reach our ears, as they are assailed, in that dreadful engagement with the weapons of Karna.

sn: न त्वेव भीताः पञ्ज्ञालाः कथंचित् स्युः पराङ्मुखाः। न हि मृत्युं महेष्वासा गणयन्ति महारणे॥
en: The Panchalas are not the persons to get frightened, much less to show their back in the thick of the fray. In sanguinary battle these mighty wielders of bow do not at all care to stake their life.

sn: य एकः पाण्डवी सेनां शरौघैः समवेष्टयत्। तं समासाद्य पञ्चाला भीष्मं नासन् पराङ्मुखाः।।१०७ ते कथं कर्णमासाद्य विद्रवेयुर्महारथाः।
en: The Panchalas did not show their back even encountering redoubtable Bhishma, who, alone and unaided, hemmed in the Pandava forces with a thick cloud of shafts.

sn: यस्त्वेकः सर्वपञ्चालानहन्यहनि नाशयन्॥ कालवच्चरते वीरः पञ्चालानां रथव्रजे। तमप्यासाद्य समरे मित्रार्थे मित्रवत्सल॥ तथा ज्वलन्तमस्त्राग्निं गुरुं सर्वधनुष्मताम्। निर्दहन्तं च समरे दुर्धर्ष द्रोणमोजसा॥ ते नित्यमुदिता जेतुं मृधे शत्रूनरिंदम। न जात्वाधिस्थे ताः पञ्चालाः स्युः पराङ्मुखाः॥
en: O benevolent friend! Panchala always kept on fighting in support of Pandavas when they found Dronacharya came for battle irrespective of Drona's march fiercely like death god in the chariot-rode army of Panchala killing them severally, whose face glew in the light of friction in weapons, who was preceptor to all archers and disastrous for the army of enemy in battle-field viz.. they did not shown back to battle-field and put at stake their lives for the cause of Pandavas. O enemy suppressor Arjuna! It is the main characteristic of Panchala soldiers that they are always prepared to defeat the enemies. They cannot show back to battle-field under fright of Karna, the son of a charioteer.

sn: तेषामापततां शूरः पञ्चालानां तरस्विनाम्। आदत्तासूशरैः कर्णः पतङ्गानामिवानलः॥
en: Like the flaming fire consuming myriads of insects that irrepressible Karna with his shafts devoured these swift-armed. Panchalas as they approached him in battle array.

sn: एते द्रवन्ति पाञ्चाला द्राव्यन्ते योधिभिर्बुवम्। कर्णेन भरतश्रेष्ठ पश्य पश्य तथाकृतान्॥
en: O Bharata! See here, these Panchala warriors racing. Karna and other warriors are so making them to run so haphazard. Look there, they are trapped in a worst network.

sn: तांस्तथाभिमुखान् वीरान् मित्रार्थे त्यक्तजीवितान्। क्षयं नयति राधेयः पञ्चालाञ्छतशो रणे॥
en: Rallying round the banner of their allies as these valiant Panchalas, reckless of their life, marched against him the son of Radha took off their hordes by legions.

sn: तद् भारत महेष्वासानगाधे मजतोऽप्लवे। कर्णार्णवे प्लवो भूत्वा पञ्चालास्त्रातुमर्हसि॥
en: O Bharata, it now behoves you to steer these sturdy bowmen, the valiant Panchala forces, who are fast sinking in the ocean of Karna without a bark.

sn: अस्त्र हि रामात् कर्णेन भार्गवादृषिसत्तमात्। यदुपात्तं महाघोरं तस्य रूपमुदीर्यते॥
en: The weapon which Karna obtained from that foremost sage Rama, the son of Bhrigu, is blazing forth its appalling form.

sn: तापनं सर्वसैन्यानां घोररूपं सुदारुणम्। समावृत्य महासेनां ज्वलन्तं स्वेन तेजसा॥
en: The awful form of that weapon, spreading terror and consternation all round and encompassing the vast array of troops, is glistening with its own bright.

sn: एते चरन्ति संग्रामे कर्णचापच्युताः शराः। भ्रमराणामिव वातास्तापयन्ति स्म तावकान्॥
en: Those arrows flung from the bow-strings of Kamna, afflicting your hosts in battle, are hovering round like swarms of bees.

sn: एते द्रवन्ति पञ्चाला दिक्षु सर्वासु भारत। कर्णास्त्रं समरे प्राप्य दुर्निवार्यमनात्मभिः॥
en: Afflicting in battle with the shots of Karna, that is irresistible by persons of weak nerve, O Bharata, the Panchalas, are flying in all directions.

sn: एष भीमो दृढक्रोधो वृतः पार्थ समन्ततः। सृञ्जयैर्योध्यन् कर्णं पीड्यते निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Yonder, O Partha, foaming and frothing with rage yet unsatiated, fights Bhima with the Srinjaya forces around him and is getting afflicted with the sharp arrows of Karna.

sn: पाण्डवान् सृञ्जयांश्चैव पञ्चालांश्चैव भारता हन्यादुपेक्षितः कर्णो रोगो देहमिवागतः॥
en: O Bharata, if you remain indifferent towards Karna, he will cause a sad havoc of the Pandava, the Srinjaya and the Panchala forces, like the seizure of the ills, that flesh is heir to, makes the body succumb.

sn: नान्यं त्वत्तो हि पश्यामि योधं यौधिष्ठिरे बले। यः समासाद्य राधेयं स्वस्तिमानाव्रजेद् गृहम्॥
en: Amongst the vast array of the forces of Yudhishthira, I find not another general, save and beyond yourself, who is capable of returning from the field scatheless, after having encountered son of Radha in battle.

sn: तमद्य निशितैर्बाणैर्विनिहत्य नरर्षभ। यथाप्रतिज्ञं पार्थ त्वं कृत्वा कीर्तिमवाप्नुहि॥
en: O foremost of men, buckle on your armour, therefore, to pop off Karna with the keen shafts of your arrows and thus redeeming your pledge, redound your glory.

sn: त्वं हि शक्तो रणे जेतुं सकर्णानपि कौरवान्। नान्यो युधि युधां श्रेष्ठ सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Most assuredly I tell you, O warrior of warriors, you and you alone, are capable of worsting Karna in battle and defeating the whole bands of Kaurava army.

sn: एतत् कृत्वा महत् कर्म हत्वा कर्ण महारथम्। कृतार्थः सफलः पार्थ सुखी भव नरोत्तम॥
en: And accomplishing this proud feat, O Partha and achieving victory over the master car-warrior, Karna, may you, the best of men, gain your ends and be successful and happy.

sn: संजय उवाच स केशवस्य बीभत्सुः श्रुत्वा भारत भाषितम्। विशोकः सम्प्रहृष्टश्च क्षणेन समपद्यत॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing, O Bharata, these (reassuring) words of Keshava, Vibhatsu, instantly shaking off his sorrowful countenance, took heart again.

sn: ततो ज्यामभिमृज्याशु व्याक्षिपद् गाण्डिवं धनुः। दने कर्णविनाशाय केशवं चाभ्यभाषत॥
en: And grating his bowstring and stretching it at length, he took hold of his Gandiva with a view to make away with Karna and addressing Keshava, thus expressed himself.

sn: त्वया नाथेन गोविन्द ध्रुव एव जयो मम। प्रसन्नो यस्य मेऽद्य त्वं लोके भूतभविष्यकृत्॥
en: Since you-O Govinda, who, (fathoming the mysteries of fate) see through events, past and future, since you are so kindly disposed towards me, under your (able) generalship, I may well be certain of gaining the day.

sn: त्वत्सहायो ह्यहं कृष्ण त्रील्लोकान् वै समागतान्। प्रापयेयं परं लोकं किमु कर्णं महाहवे॥
en: O Krishna, with you at my elbow, bidding defiance to all the three worlds, marshalled in array, I can well launch them (on and all), into eternity, what speak you of Karna then.

sn: पश्यामि द्रवती सेनां पञ्चालानां जनार्दन। पश्यामि कर्णं समरे विचरन्तमभीतवत्॥
en: O Janardana, I witness how the Panchala hordes are beating their retreats (from the field) and I also seen how Karna with his lofty bearing domineering in the battle.

sn: भार्गवास्त्रं च पश्यामि ज्वलन्तं कृष्ण सर्वशः। सृष्टं कर्णेन वार्ष्णेय शक्रेणेव यथाशनिम्॥
en: The sight of the Bhargava weapon, let loose by Karna and floating on the air like the great thunder of Shakra, meets also my view,

sn: अयं खलु स संग्रामो यत्र कर्ण मया हतम्। कथयिष्यन्ति भूतानि यावद् भूमिर्धरिष्यति॥
en: But in today's battle I will give no quarter to Karna and all the world will proclaim the fact till as long as it will last.

sn: अद्य कृष्ण विकर्णा मे कर्णं नेष्यन्ति मृत्यवे। गाण्डीवमुक्ताः क्षिण्वन्तो मम हस्तप्रचोदिताः॥
en: Today, O Krishna, pointed arrows flung from Gandiva and sped by my arms, will sent Karna to his last account.

sn: अद्य राजा धृतराष्ट्रः स्वां बुद्धिमवमंस्यते। दुर्योधनमराजयाह यया राज्येऽभ्यषेचयत्॥
en: And king Dhritarashtra, today will hurl malediction on his evil genius under the inspiration of which he placed the diadem on the brow of Duryodhana, who was least deserving of sovereignty.

sn: अद्य राज्यात् सुखाश्चैव श्रियो राष्ट्रात् तथा पुरात्। पुत्रेभ्यश्च महाबाहो धृतराष्ट्रो विमोक्ष्यति॥
en: O large-arined one, today King Dhritarashtra will be deprived of his sovereignty and happiness, wealth and dominion, capital and sons.

sn: गुणवन्तं हि यो द्वेष्टि निर्गुण कुरुते प्रभुम्। स शोचति नृपः कृष्ण क्षिप्रमेवागते क्षये॥
en: O Sri Krishna! The king who keep envy within heart for meritorious and offers throne to wicked person, regrets on the consequences when these are ripen. He thus, suffers at last from agony.

sn: यथा च पुरुषः कश्चिच्छित्त्वा चाम्रवर्ण महत्। फलं दृष्ट्वा भृशं दुःखी भविष्यति जनार्दन। सूतपुत्रे हते त्वद्य निराशो भविता प्रभुः॥
en: O Janaradana! As a man regrets on the consequences for deforestation of mango trees when these arise subsequent to such evil act committed, king Duryodhana will become helpless on the death of Karna, the son of charioteer. arrows

sn: अद्य दुर्योधनो राज्याजीविताच निराशकः। भविष्यति हते कर्णे कृष्ण सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Most assuredly do I tell you, O Krishna, the Karna's doom being (thus) sealed today, Duryodhana, goaded to desperation will lose all hope of both his life and sovereignty.

sn: अद्य दृष्ट्वा मया कर्णं शरैर्विशकलीकृतम्। स्परता तव वाक्यानि शमं प्रति जनेश्वरः॥
en: As in days of yore, in the contest between the Devas and the Asuras, Indra rent in twain the body of the demon Vritra, so beholding the body of Karna, all cut into pieces with the inflicted through my hands, let Duryodhana today recall to mind the proposal you made, O Lordly Being, when suing for peace.

sn: अद्यसौ सौबलः कृष्ण ग्लहाजानातु वै शरान्। दुरोदरं च गाण्डीवं मण्डलं च रथं प्रति॥
en: Let the son of Subal realize today, O Krishna, that my arrows happen to be my dice, my Gandiva is my gaming board and my chariot, my chequered cloth.

sn: अद्य कुन्तीसुतस्याहं दृढ राज्ञः प्रजागरम्। व्यपनेष्यामि गोविन्द हत्वा कर्णं शितैः शरैः॥
en: O Govinda, striking today the death knell of Karna with keen shafts, I will remove the long lost sleep of the son of Kunti.

sn: अद्य कुन्तीसुतो राजा हते सूतसुते मया। सुप्रहृष्टमनाः प्रीतिश्चिरं सुखमवाप्स्यति॥
en: On my hastening the departure of Suta's son to the other world will raise the drooping spirit of the royal descendant of Kunti and he, taking life easily, will enjoy eternal happiness.

sn: अद्य चाहमनाधृष्यं केशवाप्रतिमं शरम्। उत्स्त्रक्ष्यामीह यः कर्णं जीविताद् भ्रंशयिष्यति॥
