en: O Keshava, I will fling today such an irresistible arrow, unique of its kind, that will surely make Karna shuffle off his mortal coil.

sn: यस्य चैतद् व्रतं मह्यं वधे किल दुरात्मनः। पादौ न धावये तावद् यावद्धन्यां न फाल्गुनम्॥ मृषा कृत्वा व्रतं तस्य पापस्य मधुसूदन। पातयिष्ये रथात् कायं शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: And such was the vow of that wretch of human beings about taking my life, that "until I put an end to the existence of Phalguna, I will not have my feet washed.” Giving a lie to the words of honor of that vile creature, O Madhusudan, I will, hitting him straight with my arrows, throw off his body from his car.

sn: योऽसौ रणे नरं नान्यं पृथिव्यामनुमन्यते। तस्याद्य सूतपुत्रस्य भूमिः पास्यति शोणितम्॥
en: The Earth today will drink the blood of that son of Suta, who, in battle, defies all mortals of this sphere.

sn: अपतिहसि कृष्णेति सूतपुत्रो यदब्रवीत्। धृतराष्ट्रमते कर्णः श्लाघमानः स्वकान् गुणान्॥ अनृतं तत् करिष्यन्ति मामका निशिताः शराः। आशीविषा इव क्रुद्धास्तस्य पास्यन्ति शोणितम्।। २३
en: In addressing Krishna, that Karna, the son of Suta, vaunting of his own superiority, with the approbation of Dhritarashtra, had indulged himself (in the expression), "O Krishna, you are now without a husband.” My sharpened arrows will falsify today that vile expression of his and like the foaming snake, surcharged with active poison, will feast on his blood.

sn: मया हस्तवता मुक्ता नाराचा वैद्युतत्विषः। गाण्डीवसृष्टा दास्यन्ति कर्णस्य परमां गतिम्॥
en: My cloth-yard shafts, dazzling with the splendour of lightning, let loose by my capacious arms and from off the strings of Gandiva, will lead Karna to his eternal goal.

sn: अद्य तप्स्यति राधेयः पाञ्चालीं यत्तदाब्रवीत्। सभामध्ये वचः क्रूरं कुत्सयन् पाण्डवान् प्रति॥
en: The contumely which the son of Radha gave expression to, in addressing the Princess of Panchala in the open court, vilifying the Pandavas, will today make him repent of his misdemeanour.

sn: ये वै षण्ढतिलास्तत्र भवितारोऽद्य ते तिला:। हते वैकर्तने कर्णे सूतपुत्रे दुरात्मनि॥
en: After the fall of the son of Suta the vicioussouled Karna, also called Vaikartan, those words that were at one time sesame seeds without grain, will turn out today to be the reverse.

sn: अहं वः पाण्डुपुत्रेभ्यस्त्रास्यामीति तदब्रवीत्। धृतराष्ट्रसुतान् कर्णः श्लाघमानोऽऽत्मनो गुणान्॥२७ अनृतं तत् करिष्यन्ति मामका निशिताः शराः। उद्योगः पाण्डुपुत्राणां समाप्तिमुपयास्यति॥
en: While addressing the sons of Dhritarashtra Karna let fall from his lips these words, full of sound and fury-"I will save you of the sons of Pandu," today my keen shafts will belie even those imperious words of his.

sn: हन्ताहंन पाण्डवान् सर्वान् सुपुत्रानिति योऽब्रवीत्। तमद्य कर्णं हन्तास्मि मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम्॥
en: In the presence of all the assembled archers, today, I will take the life out of that Karna, who dared to have said, “I will put all the Pandavas to death with their sons."

sn: यस्य वीर्यं समाश्रित्य धार्तराष्ट्रो महामनाः। अवामन्यत दुर्बुद्धिर्नित्यमस्मान् दुरात्मवान्॥ हत्वाहं कर्णमाजौ हि तोषयिष्यामि भ्रातरम्।
en: O Madhusudana, today, I will cause the slaughter of that Karna, the son of Radha, confident of whose prowess the haughty son of Dhritarashtra, full of wicked design and evil passion, slighted us all along.

sn: शरान् नानाविधान् मुक्त्वा त्रासयिष्यामि शात्रवान्। आकर्णमुक्तैरिषुभिर्यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनैः॥ भूमिशोभां करिष्यामि पतितै रथकुञ्जरैः।
en: I will satisfy my brother Yudhishthira by killing Karna today in the battle-field on whose power, Duryodhana is confident to the extent that he insults us since beginning. He is wicked, stubborn and shrewd and Karna was his blind supporter.

sn: तत्राहं वै महासंख्ये युद्धदुर्मदम्॥ अद्य कर्णमहं घोरं सूदयिष्यामि सायकैः।
en: I will frighten the soldiers of enemy through attack with different type of arrows. I will make the battle-field gracious with a pile of chariots and elephants collapsed/killed by the arrows enhancing the state of Yama shot from bow stretched up to the ear length.

sn: अद्य कर्णे हते कृष्ण धार्तराष्ट्राः सराजकाः॥ विद्ववन्तु दिशो भीताः सिंहजस्ता मृगा इव।
en: And as a deer, afraid of the lion, turns its tail, so, O Krishna, let all the Dhartarashtras, today, with the fall of Karna, beat a hasty retreat.

sn: अद्य दुर्योधन राजा आत्मानं चानुशोचताम्॥ हते कर्णे मया संख्ये सपुत्रे ससुहजने।
en: Let king Duryodhana also indulge himself in grief, today, as Karna falls a victim to my arms in company with all his sons and relations.

sn: अद्य कर्णं हतं दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रोऽत्यमर्षणः॥ जानातु मां रणे कृष्ण प्रवरं सर्वधन्विनाम्।
en: Seeing Karna meeting his death today through my arrows, O Krishna, let the savage son of Dhritarashtra acknowledge me to be the peerless archer in the field.

sn: सपुत्रपौत्रं सामात्यं सभृत्यं च निराशिषम्॥ अद्य राज्ये करिष्यामि धृतराष्ट्र जनेश्वरम्।
en: I will make king Dhritarashtra, with all his descendants, counsellors and followers, shelterless today.

sn: अद्य कर्णस्य चक्राङ्गाः क्रव्यदाश्च पृथग्विधाः॥ शरैश्छिन्नानि गात्राणि विहरिष्यन्ति केशव।
en: O Keshava, today, vulture and other birds of prey will roam about the body of Karna, cut into pieces with the shafts of my arrows.

sn: अद्य राधासुतस्याहं संग्रामे मधुसूदन॥ शिरश्छेत्स्यामि कर्णस्य मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम्।
en: O Madhusudana, today, I will in the presence of all the archers, marshaled in array, dissever the head of Karna of Radha's womb.

sn: अद्य तीक्ष्णैर्विपाठैश्च क्षुरेश्च मधुसूदन॥ रणे छेत्स्यामि गात्राणि राधेस्य दुरात्मनः।
en: With sharp-pointed Vipathas and other razor-edged arrows, today, I will pierce through the body of that wicked soul, Karna.

sn: अद्य राजा महत् कृच्छं संत्यक्ष्यति युधिष्ठिरः॥ संतापं मानसं वीरश्चिरसम्भृतमात्मनः।
en: The mighty king Yudhishthira will shake off today his great suffering due to his long cherished mental anguish.

sn: अद्य केशव राधेयमहं हत्वा सबान्धवम्॥ नन्दयिष्यामि राजानं धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्।
en: O Krishna, I will cheer up king Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, by slaying today the son of Radha with all his tribe.

sn: अद्याहमनुगान् कृष्ण कर्णस्य कृपणान् युधि॥ हन्ता ज्वलनसंकाशैः शरैः सर्पविषोपमैः।
en: O Krishna, with shafts blazing like fire, or resembling venomous serpents, today, I will devour all the sunken hosts of Karna.

sn: अद्याहं हेमकवचैराबद्धमणिकुण्डलैः॥ संस्तारिष्यामि गोविन्द वसुधां वसुधाधिपैः।
en: O Govinda, with shafts adorned with the feathers of vultures, I will deluge the earth, today, with the scattered bodies of potentates, all armoured with shields of gold.

sn: अद्याभिमन्योः शत्रूणां सर्वेषां मधुसूदन॥ प्रमथिष्यामि गात्राणि शिरांसि च शितैः शरैः।
en: O Madhusudana, with sharp-pointed arrows, I will, today, striking down all the enemies of Abhimanyu dissever their heads and disjoint their body.'

sn: अद्य निर्धार्तराष्ट्रां च भ्रात्रे दास्यामि मेदिनीम्॥ निरर्जुनां वा पृथिवीं केशवनुचरिष्यसि।
en: O Keshava, today, either I will, making the earth devoid of Dhartarashtras, make a gift of her unto my brothers, or you shall have to traverse this ground shorn of Arjuna.

sn: अद्याहमनृणः कृष्ण भविष्यामि धनुर्भृताम्॥ कोपस्य च कुरूणां च शराणां गाण्डिवस्य च।
en: O Krishna, I will acquit myself, today, of the obligations I owe to all the bowmen, to my avenging spirit, to the Kurus, to my shafts and to Gandiva.

sn: अद्य दुःशमहं मोक्ष्ये त्रयोदशसमार्जितम्॥ हत्वा कर्णं रणे कृष्ण शम्बरं मघवानिव।
en: And like Maghavat causing the slaughter of Shambara, I will O Krishna, killing Karna, today in battle, shake off the heavy affliction I have been cherishing these thirteen long years.

sn: अद्य कर्णे हते युद्धे सोमकानां महारथाः॥ कृतं कार्यं च मन्यन्तां मित्रकार्येप्सवो युधि।
en: With the fall of Karna in battle, today, let the mighty car-warriors of the line of Somakas, all anxious for the interests of their allies, rest assured of the issue of this, their engagement.

sn: न जाने च कथं प्रीतिः शैनेयस्याद्य माधव॥ भविष्यति हते कर्णे मयि चापि जयाधिके।
en: And O Madhava, I cannot conceive even of the great joy which the descendants of Sini will experience today, when Karna will be no more and after I have won the battle.

sn: अहं हत्वा रणे कर्णं पुत्रं चास्य महारथम्॥ प्रीतिं दास्यामि भीमस्य यमयोः सात्यकस्य च।
en: Slaying Karna in battle and his mighty carwarrior son, I will clear the hearts of Bhima and the Twins, as also of Satyaki.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नशिखण्डिभ्यां पञ्चालानां च माधव॥ अद्यानृण्यं गमिष्यामि हत्वा कर्ण महाहवे।
en: Taking away the life of Karna, today in great battle, O Madhava, I will free myself of the very many obligations I am under the Panchalas, as also under Dhristadyumna and Shikhandin.

sn: अद्य पश्यन्तु संग्रामे धनंजयमर्षणम्॥ युध्यन्तं कौरवान् संख्ये घातयन्तं च सूतजम्।
en: Let them all witness today the scene of the furious Dhananjaya, encountering all the Kaurava forces in the field, give a death-blow unto the son of Suta.

sn: भवत्सकाशे वक्ष्ये च पुनरेवात्मस्तवम्॥ धनुर्वेद मत्समो नास्ति लोके पराक्रमे वा मम कोऽस्ति तुल्यः। स्तथा क्रोधे सदृशोऽन्यो मेऽस्ति॥
en: Let me, once again, indulge myself in the luxury of singing my own praise in your presence. In all this wide world I have no rival in archery. And who is there to match me in prowess? Then again what soul is there that can equal me in mercy? While in fire and fury I yield to none.

sn: अहं धनुष्मान् ससुरासुरांश्च सर्वाणि भूतानि च सङ्गतानि। स्वबाहुवीर्याद् गमये पराभवं मत्पौरुषं विद्धि परं परेभ्यः॥
en: With the bow in my hand and with the strength of my capacious arms, I can outlive the Asuras, the celestials and all the other creatures grouped together, know it for certain, that my prowess surpasses to that of the most powerful.

sn: शरार्चिषा गाण्डिवेनाहपेकः सर्वान् कुरून् बाह्निकांश्चाभिहत्य। स्तथा दहेयं सगणान् प्रसा॥
en: And like a spark of fire in a heap of dried grass at the end of winder, I, too, alone, am well capable of setting fire to all the Kurus and the Balhikas, as also their followers with my flashing arrows flung from Gandiva.

sn: पाणौ पृषत्का लिखिता ममैते धनुश्च दिव्यं विततं सबाणम्। पादौ च मे सरथौ सध्वजौ च न मादृशं युद्धगतं जयन्ति॥
en: My palms bear the marks of these arrows and this superb and out-stretched bow with its string trimmed with arrow; the soles of my feet also bear the marks of a car and a standard; and so when a person (with all these marks on) goes to battle, he, least of all, can be triumphed over."

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वार्जुन एकवीरः क्षिप्रं रिपुनः क्षतजोपमाक्षः। भीमं मुमुक्षः समरे प्रयातः कर्णस्य कायाच शिरो जिहीर्घः॥
en: Saying this much to Achyuta that hero of heroes and destroyer of enemies, rushed to battle with a view to rescue Bhima and dissever Karna.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच समागमे पाण्डवसुंजयानां महाभये मामकानामगाधे। धनंजये तात रणाय याते कर्णेन तद् युद्धमथोऽत्र कीदृक्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When Dhananjaya, the infinite dread of my valiant chieftains, rejoined the Pandava and Srinjaya forces, O Sire, how fared the battle?

sn: संजय उवाच तेषामनीकानि बृहद्ध्वजानि रणे समृद्धानि समागतानि। गर्जन्ति भेरीनिनदोन्मुखानि नादैर्यथा मेघगणास्तपान्ते॥
en: Sanjaya said All the assembled troops marshaled in array, sounding their bugles and blowing this horns, like thick volumes of clouds at the end of summer, roared thunders.

sn: महागजाभ्राकुलमस्त्रतोयं वादित्रनेमीतलशब्दवच। हिरण्यचित्रायुधाविद्युतं च शरासिनाराचमहास्त्रधारम्॥ तद् भीमवेग रुधिरौघवाहि खड्गाकुलं क्षत्रियजीवघाति। अनार्तवं क्रूरमनिष्टवर्षं बभूव तत् संहरण प्रजानाम्॥
en: That grim visaged war, which followed the sanguinary contest of the Kshatriyas, all up in arins, for the extermination of their race and in which blood streamed forth in rushing currents, like the untimely falling off of a shower of evil, became the cause of destruction of all livingbeings. Huge elephants forming the cluster of wheels, clapping of hands constituting its thunder-bolts and weapons, trimmed with gold, making its lightning; and swords and arrows and cloth-yard shafts and other weapons of great velocity, becoming its drops.

sn: एकं रथं सम्परिवार्य मृत्यु नयन्त्यनेके च रथाः समेताः। स्तथा रथश्चापि रथाननेकान्॥
en: Many car-warriors, assembled together, assailing an opponent dispatched him off to the King of Terrors; while a supreme car-warrior, fighting the good fight with a single adversary, hastened his departure to the other world or another, assailing many in close contest, launched them all into eternity.

sn: रथं ससूतं सहयं च कञ्चित् कश्चिद्रथी मृत्युवशं निनाय। निनाय चाप्येकगजेन कश्चिद् रथान् बहून् मृत्युवशे तथाश्वान्॥
en: Then again some car-warrior in exchanging shots with his enemy made him die a violent death, together with steeds and charioteer, while another warrior riding on his elephant put to death many car-warriors and horsemen.

sn: रथान् ससूतान् सहयान् गजांश्च सर्वानरीन् मृत्युवशं शरौघैः। निन्ये हयांश्चैव तथा ससादीन् पदातिसङ्घांश्च तथैव पार्थः॥
en: Partha thus inflicting the enemy with a heavy downpour of shafts rent them asunder with all their cavalry and elephant soldiers, as also the rides and riders of their war-chariots.

sn: कृपः शिखण्डी च रणे समेतौ दुर्योधन सात्यकिरभ्यगच्छत्। श्रुतस्तथा द्रोणपुत्रेण सार्धं युधामन्युश्चित्रसेनेन सार्धम्॥
en: Kripacharya met Sikhandin in the field, while Satyaki encountered Duryodhana; and Srutasravas challenged Drona's son, while Yudhamauna took Chitrasena for his assailant.

sn: कर्णस्य पुत्रं तु रथी सुषेणं समागतं संजयश्चोत्तमौजाः। गान्धारराजं सहदेवः क्षुधार्ता महर्षभं सिंह इवाभ्यधावत्॥
en: And like a hungry lion hotly pursuing a stout bull, Uttamauja, the great car-warrior of Srinjayas, pounced upon Susena, the son of Karna,; while Sahadeva launched out against Shakuni, the King of the Gandharas.

sn: शतानीको नाकुलिः कर्णपुत्रं युवा युवानं वृषसेन शरौघैः। समार्पयत् कर्णपुत्रश्च शूरः पाञ्चालेयं शरवर्षैरनेकैः॥
en: Young Satanika, the son of Nakula, rushing headlong afflicted young Vrishasena with a showering torrent of his shafts and (he, too), the heroic son of Karna returned the charges of the son of the princess of Panchala in no stinted measure.

sn: न्माद्रीपुत्रो नकुलचित्रयोधी। पञ्चलानामधिपो याज्ञसेनिः सेनापतिः कर्णमार्छत् ससैन्यम्॥
en: Madri's son Nakula, the skillful adept of war tactics and the wonderful warrior of unique fame, assailed Kritavarman, while Yajnasena's son the king of the Panchalas rushed against general Karna with all his hosts.

sn: दुःशासनो भारत भारती च संशप्तकानां पृतना समृद्धा। भीमं रणे शस्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठं भीमं समार्छत्तमसह्यवेगम्१२॥
en: O Bharata, Dushasana, with the swelling hosts of the Samsaptakas and all the troops comprising the Bharata force, rode full tile against Bhima, the inflictor of woes in battle to all wielders of arms and the foremost of all warriors.

sn: कर्णात्मजं तत्र जघान वीरस्तथाच्छिनचोत्तमौजाः प्रसह्य। तस्योत्तमाङ्गं निपपात भूमौ निनादयद् गां निनदेन खं च॥
en: There the powerful Uttamaujas, putting forth all his mighty, struck down the son of Karna and his dissevered head fell down on the ground with a terrible shriek, which made the Earth and the sky resound its roars.

sn: सुषेणशीर्षं पतितं पृथिव्यां विलोक्य कर्णोऽथ तदार्तरूपः। क्रोधाद्धयांस्तस्य रथं ध्वजं च बाणैः सुधारैर्निशितैरकृन्तत्॥
en: Overwhelmed with grief at the (ghastly) sight of the severed head of Sushena thus rolling on the ground. Karna remained stupefied (for a while), but, his avenging spirit soon taking the better of him, he, soon, with sharp-pointed arrows cut to pieces the steeds, chariot and the standard of his son's adversary.

sn: स तूत्तमौजा निशितैः पृषत्कैविव्याध खङ्गेन च भास्वरेण। पाणि हयांश्चैव कृपस्य हत्वा शिखण्डिवाहं स ततोऽध्यरोहत्॥
en: Uttamaujas, in the interval, trucking home, with his keen shafts and the sharp edge of his steed, the steed and the side-guards of Kripa, quickly leapt into the chariot of Shikhandin.

sn: कृपं तु दृष्ट्वा विरथं रथस्थो नैच्छच्छरैस्ताडयितुं शिखण्डी। तं द्रौणिरावार्य रथं कृपस्य समुजहे पङ्कगतां यथा गाम्॥
en: Shikhandin, observing from his own chariot, (the sad predicament of) Kripa thus deprived of his conveyance, did not like to pursue him with his shafts; the son of Drona, in the meanwhile, covering the car of Kripa with that of his own, like a bull fallen in a ditch, rescued him.

sn: हिरण्यवर्मा निशितैः प्रुषत्केस्तवात्मजानामनिलात्मजो वै। अतापयत् सैन्यमतीव भीमः काले शुचौ मध्यगतो यथार्कः॥
en: Here, the son of the Wind-god, Bhima, covered with armor of gold, afflicting with his keen shafts, like the burning mid-day Sun of summer, scorched the while body of troops of your sons. Here, the son of the Wind-god, Bhima, covered with armor of gold, afflicting with his keen shafts, like the burning mid-day Sun of summer, scorched the while body of troops of your sons.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: संजय उवाच अथ त्विदानीं तुमले विमर्दे द्विषद्भिरको बहुभिः समावृतः। महारणे सारथिमित्युवाच भीमश्चमूं वाहय धार्तराष्ट्रीम्॥
en: Sanjaya said In the thick of that awe-inspiring fray, Bhima, fighting single-handed, against tremendous odds, addressed his charioteer and said-"drive towards the centre of the Dhartarashtra force."

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: त्वं सारथे याहि जवेन वाहैनृयाम्येतान् धार्तराष्ट्रान् यमाय। संचोदितो भीमसेनेन चैवं स सारथिः पुत्रबलं त्वदीयम्॥ प्रायात् ततः सत्वरमुग्रवेगो यतो भीमस्तद् बलं गन्मुमैच्छत। ततोऽपरे नागरथाश्वपत्तिभिः प्रत्युद्ययुस्तं कुरवः समन्तात्॥
en: Spur your horses, O charioteer and I will hasten the departure of all these Dhartarashtras to the region occupied by the King of Death." The charioteer, being thus desired by Bhimasena, drove, at a furious speed, towards the spot against the whole hosts of your sons and from whence Bhima wished to fight them out and then, from all sides, a large retinue of Kaurava force, consisting of elephant and carwarriors and cavalry and infantry, hemmed him in.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: भीमस्य वाहाण्यमुदारवेगं समन्ततो बाणगणैर्निजघ्नुः। ततः शरानापततो महात्मा चिच्छेद बाणैस्तपनीयपुखैः॥
en: And they all poured down their arrows on that best of chariots occupied by Bhima from every direction, whereupon the high-souled Bhima, with his own gold-feathered shafts, scattered to the winds, all those weapons hurled against him by his enemies.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: ते वै निपेतुस्तपनीयपुङ्खा द्विधा त्रिधा भीमशरैर्निकृताः। ततो राजन् नगरथाश्वयूनां भीमहतानां वरराजमध्ये॥ घोरो निनादः प्रबभौ नरेन्द्र वजाहतानामिव पर्वतानाम्। ते वध्यमानाश्च नरेन्द्रमुख्या निर्भिद्यन्तो भीमशरप्रवेकैः॥ भीमं समन्तात् समरेऽभ्यरोहन् वृक्षं शकुन्ता इव जातपक्षाः। ततोऽभियाते तव सैन्ये स भीमः प्रादुश्चके वेगमनन्तवेगः॥ भूतान्तकृत काल इवात्तदण्डः। तस्यातिवेगस्य रणेऽतिवेगं नाशक्नुवन् वारयितुं त्वदीयाः॥ व्यात्ताननस्यापततो यथैव कालस्य काले हरतः प्रजा वै। ततो बलं भारत भारतानां प्रदह्यमानं समरे महात्मना॥ भीतं दिशोऽकीर्यत भीमनुन्नं महानिलेनाभ्रगणा यथैव। ततो धीमान् सारथिमबभीद् बली स भीमसेनः पुनरेव हृष्टः॥ सूताभिजानीहि स्वकान् परान् वा रथान् ध्वजांश्चापततः समेतान्। न्मा सैन्यं स्वं छादयिष्ये पृषत्कैः॥
en: And those gold-winged arrows of his enemies, thus broken into tatters of two or three fragments by the shafts of Bhima, fell upon the ground. Then, O King, there arose one long loud cry of woe from amidst the throng of those valiant chiefs of the Kshatriya race, as they, with their mounts of elephants and steeds and their chariots and body infantry, got afflicted with the arrows thrust hard by Bhima, like thunders rolling in mountains. Those pride of the Kshatriya race, being thus assailed by Bhima, and his powerful shafts smiting them hip and thigh, flew at him (Bhima) from every side of the plain, like the new-fledged family of the feathered tribes thickening around a tree. And as your troops fell back upon him, Bhima, of infinite prowess and strength, repulsed them with the full display of all his might, like the mighty King of Terrors, dealing destruction, at the end of time, with his mace, unto the creation. And your hosts, in that battle, could not repel the fearful impetuosity of Bhima, himself the personation of fire and fury, like the great Destroyer himself rushing, at the end of the cycle, with wide-open mouth for the extermination of all living beings. O Bharata, the whole troops, comprising the Bharata force, thus ruthlessly torn as under in battle, by the noble-minded Bhima, dispersed from the field in a state of panic, like a strong gust of wind scattering thick clouds in a tempest. Then the powerful Bhimasena, endowed with great sagacity, addressing his charioteer once more, said unto him in full glee. "Just know, O Suta, whether do all those chariots, which are advancing towards us, belong to our party, or to that of the enemy. As I, with this battle raging, can make no distinction between the two, see that I do not besiege my own hosts with my shafts.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: अरीन् विशोकाभिनिरीक्ष्य सर्वतो मनस्तु चिन्ता प्रदुनोति मे भृशम्। राजाऽऽतुरो नागमद् यत् किरीटी बहूनि दुःखान्यभियातोऽस्मि सूत॥
en: I am greatly mortified, O Vishoka, to see around me these leaders of war in hostile array and also with the sight of their cars and the tops of their standards. The king lies wounded and the diadem-decked Arjuna is not yet come to take the field. All these, O Suta, are preying heavily on me.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: एतद् दुःखं सारथे धर्मराजो यन्मां हित्वा यातवाशत्रुमध्ये। नैनं जीवं नाद्य जानाम्यजीवं बीभत्सुं वा तन्ममाद्यातिदुःखम्॥
en: O charioteer, that the pious king Yudhishthira should have gone away from the field, leading me alone in the midst of the enemy, is in itself hear-rending. Then again I am quite in the dark as to his fate. Nor do I know whether Vibhatsu is still alive or not. All these add to my grief.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: सोऽहं द्विषत्सैन्यमुदग्रकल्पं विनाशयिष्ये परमप्रतीतः। एतत्रिहत्याजिमध्ये समेतं प्रीतो भविष्यामि सह त्वयाद्य॥
en: And though dejected and disspirited, I will play the hell with all these troops inspite of their strength. And thus making the vast army in hostile array pay the penalty in the wager of battle, let me rejoice with you today.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: सर्वांस्तूणान् सायकानामवेक्ष्य किं शिष्टं स्यात् सायकानां रथे मे। का वा जातिः किं प्रमाणं च तेषां ज्ञात्वा व्यक्तं तत् समाचक्ष्व सूत॥
en: O Suta, examine closely all the quivers of my arrows and see the numbers still left and then let me know decidedly the quantity and variety of each.”

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: विशोक उवाच षण्मार्गणानामयुतानि वीर क्षुराश्च भल्लाश्च तथायुताख्याः। नाराचानां द्वे सहस्रे च वीर त्रीण्येव च प्रदराणां स्म पार्थ॥
en: Vishoka said Being thus addressed, Vishoka replied-"O hero, you have full sixty thousand arrows still left, while your shafts, both razor-shaped and broad-pointed, number ten thousand each. O hero, you have still two thousand cloth-yard shafts, while the Pradaras, O Partha, number three thousand.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: अस्तायुधं पाण्डवेयावशिष्टं न यद् वहेच्छकटं षड्गवीयम्। एतद् विद्वन् मुञ्च सहस्रशोऽपि गदासिबाहुद्रविणं च तेऽस्ति॥ प्रासाश्च मुद्गरा शक्तयस्तोमराश्च मा भैषीस्त्वं सङ्ख्यादायुधानाम्॥
en: To speak candidly, O son of Pandu, the quantity that is still left is quite unmanageable even by half-a-dozen bullocks, if placed on carts. O skillful one, throw off your weapons in no measured number, for your maces, swords and scimitars, as also your lances darts and spears and other weapons of the arms, number thousands upon thousands. So be of good cheer and pray do not be misapprehensive of your weapons running short."

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: भीमसेन उवाच सूताद्यैनं पश्य भीमप्रयुक्तैः संछिन्दद्धिः पार्थिवानां सुवेगैः। छन्नं बाणैराहवं घोररूपं नष्टादित्यं मृत्युलोकेन तुल्यम्॥
en: Bhima said Mark, O Suta, in this day's fearful engagement the plains will present the aspect of the dismal regions, of Death, when the field will be shrouded with thick sets of my irresistible arrows, furiously let loose from off my bow, tearing into pieces the entire body of the trainbands of my enemy and making the Sun, as it were, disappear from view.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: अद्यैतद् वै विदितं पार्थिवानां भविष्यति ह्याकुमारं च सूत। निमग्नो वा समरे भीमसेन एकः कुरून् वा समरे व्यजैषीत्॥
en: Today, O Suta, it will be known to all the Kshatriyas, even unto the last generation, that either Bhimasena has given himself up in battle, or, singly, he has got the better of all the Kurus.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: सर्वे संख्ये कुरवो निष्पतन्तु मां वा लोकाः कीर्तयन्त्वाकुमारम्। सर्वानेकस्तानहं पातयिष्ये ते वा सर्वे भीमसेनं तुदन्तु॥
en: Today, either let the Kauravas fall in battle, or, let all the world sound my death knell. Alone, encountering them all, I will either overmatch them, or, let them, all combined, put an extinguisher upon Bhimasena.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: आशास्तारः कर्म चाप्युत्तमं ये तन्मे देवाः केवलं साधयन्तु। आयात्विहाद्यार्जुनः शस्त्रघाती शकस्तूर्णं यज्ञ इवोपहूतः॥
en: May the guardian angels, who further the course of all righteous action, shower down their blessing on me; and let Arjuna, the victor of enemies, come here speedily (to my relief), like the invoked Sakra appearing in the sacrificial ground.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: मेते कस्माद् विद्रवन्ते नरेन्द्राः। व्यक्तं धीमान् सव्यसाची नराग्र्यः सैन्यं ह्येतच्छादयात्याशु बाणैः॥
en: Look there and see the disbanded Bharata force! Why are all these chiefs taking to their flight. Surely it seems to me inevitable that Savyasachin, that best of human beings has been shrouding that force with a heavy downpour of his arrows.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: पश्य ध्वजांश्च द्रवतो विशोक नागान् हयान् पत्तिसंघांश्च संख्ये। रथान् विकीर्णाशरशक्तिताडितान् पश्यस्वैतान् रथिनश्चैव सूत॥
en: Look there, O Vishoka, (and see how) the mounted soldiers riding on their steeds or elephants and standard-bearers and footsoldiers and beating their retreat. Look, also, at these war-chariots, (and see how) they with their warriors on, are getting scattered by the darts, shafts and arrows, O Suta.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: आपूर्यते कौरवी चाप्यभीक्ष्णं सेना ह्यसौ सुभृशं हन्यमाना। प्रेस्ता शरैः काञ्चनबर्हिबाजैः॥
en: Charged with the gold-winged and peacock-feathered arrows of Dhananjaya and bursting like the bolts from the blue, those Kaurava forces, falling fast in numbers, as often swell the ranks of their file.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: एते द्रवन्ति स रथाश्वनागाः पदातिसङ्घातिमर्दयन्तः। सम्मुह्यमानाः कौरवाः सर्व एव द्रवन्ति नागा इव दाहभीताः२६॥ हाहाकृताश्चैव रणे विशोक मुञ्चन्ति नादान् विपुलान् गजेन्द्राः॥
en: Those steed yoked on war-chariots and elephants trampling down the vast array of foot-soldiers are fleeting away. In sooth, the whole host of the Kauravas, seized with consternation, are beating a hasty retreat, as do the terrified elephants in the midst of a flaming forest. The elephants are roaring furiously in the field and their savage cries, O Vishoka, make, one and all, utter cries of woe and alas!'

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: विशोक उवाच किं भीम नैनं त्वमिहाशृणोषि विस्फारितं गाण्डिवस्यातिघोरम्। क्रुद्धेन पार्थेन विकृष्यतोऽद्य कचिन्नेमौ तव की विनष्टौ॥
en: Vishoka said Can't you, O Bhima, hear the awful sound of the Gandiva? (or), have those ears of yours lost their sensibility from the effects of the thunder produced by Partha, while out stretching it with fire and fury?

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: सर्वे कामाः पाण्डव ते समृद्धाः कपिसी दृश्यते हस्तिसैन्ये। नीलाद घनाद् विद्युतमुचरन्तीं तथा पश्य विस्फुरन्ती धनुाम्॥
en: All your wishes, O son of Pandu, have been gratified, yonder is seen the standard of Ape (of Arjuna) wafting aloft. Look there the bowstring (of Gandiva) is emitting incessantly rays of light, like the flashes of lightning from amidst the blue regions of ethereal space.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: कपिसौ वीक्षते सर्वतो वै ध्वजाग्रमारुद्य धनंजयस्य। वित्रासयन् रिपुसघान् विमर्दे बिभेम्यस्मादात्मनैवाभिवीक्ष्य॥
en: That Ape wafting aloft from the standard of Dhananjaya, is seen to strike terror, all along the line of the enemy, (and to speak freely) even I myself am stricken with awe at that (august) sight.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: विभ्राजते चातिमात्रं किरीटं विचित्रमेतच्च धनंजयस्य। दिवाकराभो मणिरेष दिव्यो विभ्राजते चैव किरीटसंस्थः॥
en: There, the resplendent beauty of Dhananjaya's diadem is shedding its effulgence brightly and the bright luster of the gem-studded on it. Sparkling with the radiancy of the Sun, is looking much more resplendent.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: पार्श्वे भीमं पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशं पश्यस्व शङ्ख देवदत्त सुघोषम्। अभीषुहस्तस्य जनार्दनस्य विगाहमानस्य चमूं परेषाम्॥
en: Alongside him, behold, there, his conch Devadatta to thundering blare and resembling a white sheet of cloud. Behold there, Janaradana, reins in hand, making his way into the centre of the hostile divisions.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: रविप्रभं वज्रनाभं क्षुरान्तं पार्थे स्थितं पश्य जनार्दनस्य। चक्रं यशोवर्धनं केशवस्य सदार्चितं यदुभिः पश्य वीर॥
en: Behold, there, O hero, by the side of Janardana his discus, radiant like the Sun, nave like thunder and sharp like razor-that discus which enhances the fame of Keshava and which is always worshipped by the Yadus. son

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: महाद्विपानां सरलट्ठमोपमाः करा निकृत्ताः प्रपतन्त्यमी क्षुरैः। किरीटिना तेन पुनः ससादिनः शरैर्निकृत्ताः कुलिशैरिवाद्रयः॥
en: There, large trunks of huge elephants, resembling the lofty yew trees, dissevered by Kiritin are falling fast. There, also, huge elephants and their riders, pierced with shafts all through, are falling down like mountains riven with thunder.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: तथैव कृष्णस्य च पाञ्चजन्यं महार्हमेतं द्विजराजवर्णम्। कौन्तेय पश्योरसि कौस्तुभं च जाज्वल्यमानं विजया स्त्रजं च॥
en: Behold, there, O of Kunti, the Panchajanya (conch) of Krishna, resplendent like the moon, the Kaustabha, (pearl) dazzling on his breasts and his garland of victory.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: ध्रुवं रथाय्यः समुपैति पार्थो विद्रावयन् सैन्यमिदं परेषाम्। हयैर्महाहै रथिनां वरिष्ठः॥
en: There cannot be any mistake in the fact that Partha, the glory of car-warriors-the best and foremost of them, carried by those precious steeds of his, the best of their kind, and in color as white as the white clouds of the sky, with Krishna as their driver, is rushing in the field, routing the enemy all through.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: विदारितान् पश्य पतन्त्यमी यथा। तवानुजेनामरराज तेजसा महावनानीव सुपर्णवायुना॥
en: Behold there, your younger, resembling in energy the deity of the celestials, is piercing with his shafts those cars, steeds and bands of foot-soldiers and they are falling down as if a forest over-thrown by the tempest caused by the wings of Garuda.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: चतुःशतान् पश्य रथानिमान् हतान् सवाजिसूतान् समरे किरीटिना। महेषुभिः सप्तशतानि दन्तिनां पदातिसादींश्च रथाननेकशः॥
en: Behold, Kiritin, with his powerful shafts, to outstrip in battle four hundred car-warriors with their steeds and drivers and seven hundred elephants, as also numberless infantry and cavalry.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: अयं समभ्येति तवान्तिकं बली निघ्नन् कुरूंचित्र इव ग्रहोऽर्जुनः। समृद्धकामोऽसि हतास्तवाहिता बलं तवायुश्च चिराय वर्धताम्॥
en: Shedding his effulgence like the constellation of Chirta, the all-powered Arjuna, after having massacred the Kuru forces, is speeding towards you. All your wishes have been gratified-your enemies, thrown overboard. May your prowess and the span of your life continue to increase for ever and ever.

description: The conversation between Bhimasena and Vishoka
sn: भीमसेन उवाच ददानि ते ग्रामवरांश्चतुर्दश प्रियाख्याने सारथे सुप्रसन्नः। दासीशतं चापि रथांश्च विंशति यदर्जुनं वेदयसे विशोक॥
en: Bhima said For this welcome news, O charioteer, with unfeigned pleasure I grant you fourteen choice villages; and O Vishoka, as you bring me the tidings of Arjuna, I also present you a hundred female slaves and twenty chariots.

sn: संजय उवाच श्रुत्वा तु रथनिर्घोषं सिंहनादं च संयुगे। अर्जुनः प्राह गोविन्दं शीघ्र नोदय वाजिनः॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing the loud rattles of chariots and the lion like roars (of warriors) in the field, Arjuna, addressing Govinda, said, “Clap spurs to the chargers."

sn: अर्जुनस्य वचः श्रुत्वा गोविन्दोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत्। एष गच्छामि सुक्षिप्रं यत्र भीमो व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Hearing these words of Arjuna, Govinda replied him (thus)-"Off I go towards the spot where Bhima has taken his post.”

sn: तं यान्तमश्चैर्हिमशङ्खवणैः सुवर्णमुक्तामणिजालनद्धैः। जम्भं जिघासुं प्रगृहीतवज्रं जयाय देवेन्द्रमिवोगमन्युम्॥
en: Then, like the king of the celestials, proceeding in great wrath and with thunder in his arms, to strike down Jambha (the Asura), Jaya (Arjuna) rushed (in the field), to obtain victory, borne by horses white as snow or conchs and with housings laid with gold, pearls and gems.

sn: रथाश्वमातङ्गपदातिसंघा बाणस्वनैमिखुरस्वनैश्च। संनादयन्तो वसुधां दिशश्च क्रुद्धा नृसिंहा जयमभ्युदीयुः॥
en: Many warriors, (of the other side), representing lions in prowess all boiling with rage and followed by a large retinue him and making the Earth resound and rending the skies with the whizz of their arrows, the rattling sound of the wheels of their war-chariots and the noise of the tread of their horses' hoofs.

sn: तेषां च पार्थस्य च मारिषसीद् देहासुपापक्षपणं सुयुद्धम्। त्रैलोक्यहेतोरसुरैर्यथाऽऽसीद् देवस्य विष्णोर्जयतां वरस्य॥
en: Then, there ensued, O sire, a mortal conflict between them (the train-bands of the Kaurava forces) and Partha, a conflict carrying death and destruction in its train to body, life and sin alike, like the great battle between the Asuras and Vishnu, the greatest of all great conquerors, for the (sovereignty of the) three worlds.

sn: देकः प्रचिच्छेद किरीटमाली। क्षुरार्धचन्द्रैर्निशितैश्च भल्लैः शिरांसि तेषां बहुधा च बाहून्॥
en: Alone and unaided, the diadem-decked and garland-necked Arjuna, rent asunder all the powerful weapons flung (against him) by them (his adversaries) and struck off their heads and arms in many and varied forms, with his razoredged and crescent shaped shafts, as also with his broad-pointed arrows.

sn: नश्वान् रथान् पत्तिगणान् द्विपांश्च। ते पेतुरुवा॒ बहुधा विरूपा वातप्रणुन्नानि यथा वनानि॥
en: Umbrellas, banners, horses, chariots, elephants and foot soldiers, shattered and mutilated, fell down on the Earth, like a forest uprooted by a violent wind.

sn: सुवर्णजालावतता महागजाः सवैजयन्तीध्वजयोधकल्पिताः। श्चकाशिरे प्रज्वलिता यथाचलाः॥
en: Mighty elephants caparisoned with goldlaid trappings and equipped with banners of triumphs and adorned with riders (on their back), wore a majestic look and shed a lustur all round as they were encompassed with goldwinged shafts, like blazing mountains.

sn: विदार्थं नागाश्वरथान् धनंजयः शरोत्तमैर्वासववज्रसंनिभैः। द्रुतं ययौ कर्णजिघांसया तथा यथा मरुत्वान् बलभेदने पुरा॥
en: With excellent shafts piercing elephants, horses and war chariots and resembling thunder of Vasava, Dhananjaya winged his way to strike down Karna, like Indra, in days of yore, proceeding to rend in twain (the Asura) Bala.

sn: ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तव सैन्यमरिंदमः। प्रविवेश महाबाहुर्मकरः सागरं यथा॥
en: Then that mightiest of men, the terror of enemies, rushed headlong into the midst of your vast array as does the Makar while plunging into the deep sea.

sn: तं हृष्टास्तावका राजन् स्थपत्तिसमन्विताः। गजाश्वसादिबहुलाः पाण्डवं समुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Seeing Pandu's sun so advance, O king, your warriors, with a long line of cars and a retinue of elephant, horse and foot soldiers, pressed upon him.

sn: तेषामापततां पार्थमारावः सुमहानभूत्। सागरस्येव क्षुब्धस्य यथा स्यात् सलिलस्वनः॥
en: And while rushing against Partha, they raised a tumultuous cry like the roarings of the surging waves in a tempest.

sn: ते तु तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं व्याघ्रा इव महारथाः। अभ्यद्रवन्त संग्रामे त्यक्त्वा प्राणकृतं भयम्॥
en: Those great warriors, powerful like tigers, reckless of their life, rushed in battle to face that mighty man, careering like a tiger.

sn: तेषामापततां तत्र शरवर्षाणि मुञ्चताम्। अर्जुनो व्यधमत् सैन्यं महावातो घनामिव॥
en: With a heavy down-pour of arrows they advanced towards him, but Arjuna dispersed them like vapours before the gushing wind.

sn: तेऽर्जुन सहिता भूत्वा रथवंशैः प्रहारिणः। अभियाय महेष्वासा विव्यधुर्निशतैः शरैः॥
en: Those mighty warriors-all good shots and of unfailing aim-in a body and with a long line of war-chariots following them, advanced against Arjuna and began to pierce him with their sharp weapons.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनः सहस्राणि रथावारणवाजिनाम्। प्रेषयामास विशिखैर्यमस्य सदनं प्रति॥
en: Arjuna, then, (rendering asunder) with his arrows, chariots, elephants and horses by thousands, dispatched (them) off to the region of Pluto.

sn: ते वध्यमाना समरे पार्थचापच्युतैः शरैः। तत्र यत्र स्म लीयन्ते भये जाते महारथाः॥
en: Thus afflicted in action with shots flung from Arjuna's bow, those mighty car-warriors, terrified and panic-stricken, began gradually to melt away.

sn: तेषां चतुःशतान् वीरान् यतमानान् महारथान्। अर्जुनो निशितेर्बाणैरनयद् यमसादनम्॥
en: Among those great car-warriors four hundred valiantly kept the field; and Arjuna, with his keen shafts, sent them, one and all, to their last account.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे नानालिङ्गै शितैः शरैः। अर्जुनं समभित्यज्य दुद्रुवुर्वे दिशो दश॥
en: (And those that held the rear) afflicted, in that battle, with keen shafts and sharp arrows of all kinds, dispersed themselves in all directions-far away from Arjuna.

sn: तेषां शब्दो महानासीद् द्रवतां वाहिनीमुखे। महौघस्येव जलधेर्गिरिमासाद्य दीर्यतः॥
en: The shouting noise made at the van by the retreating army was as furious as the grumbling roars of the breakers of the surging seas when dashing against rocks.

sn: तां तु सेनां भृशं विद्ध्वा द्रावयित्वार्जुनः शरैः। प्रायादभिमुखः पार्थः सूतानीकं हि मारिष॥
en: Thus, with his arrows, dispersing the panicstricken army, O sire, Arjuna, the son of Pritha, advanced against the column commanded by the son of Suta.

sn: तस्य शब्दो महानासीत् परानभिमुखस्य वै। गरुडस्येव पततः पन्नगार्थे यथा पुर॥
en: The great noise made by Arjuna while advancing towards his enemies, was like that of Garuda, in days of yore, while swooping down upon snakes.

sn: तं तु शब्दमभिश्रुत्य भीमसेनो महाबलः। भभूव परमप्रीतः पार्थदर्शनलालसः॥
en: The mighty Bhimasena, anxious as he was to have a look of Partha, became highly gratified with that sound.

sn: श्रुत्वैव पार्थमायान्तं भीमसेनः प्रतापवान्। त्यक्त्वा प्राणान् महाराज सेनां तव ममर्द ह॥
en: Hearing that Partha is come, the redoubtable Bhimasena, O king, began to afflict your troops, fearless of his own life.

sn: स वायुवीर्यप्रतिमो वायुवेगसमो जवे। वायुवद् व्यचरद् भीमो वायुपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Bhima, the son of the Wind-god and himself possessing the prowess and impetuousity of the wind, that valiant Bhima began to career in that battle like that of the wind itself.

sn: तेनार्धमाना राजेन्द्र सेना तव विशाम्पते। व्यभ्रश्यत महाराज भिन्ना नौरिव सागरे॥
en: Your army, O king, being thus hard pressed by him, O ruler of the universe, began to roll and tumble like a shattered vessel in the high seas.

sn: तां तु सेनां तदा भीमो दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्। शरैरवचकतॊग्रैः प्रेषयिष्यन् यमक्षयम्॥
en: Bhima then, with his deadly weapons and with great dexterity of hands, waging a ruthless slaughter amongst that body of troops, dispatched them to the region of Pluto.

sn: तत्र भारत भीमस्य बलं दृष्ट्वाऽतिमानुषम्। व्यभ्रमन्त रणे योधाः कालस्येव युगक्षये॥
en: Your warriors, O Bharata, seeing the wonderful exploits of Bhima in that battle, careering like the King of Terrors at the end of time, became greatly agitated.

sn: तथादितान् भीमबलान् भीमसेनेन भारत। दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनो राजा इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ सैनिकांश्च महेष्वासान् योधांश्च भरतर्षभ। समादिशन् रणे सर्वान् हत भीममिति स्म ह॥
en: King Duryodhana, seeing his best soldiers, O Bharata, thus worsted by Bhimasena, gave vent to the following expression, addressing his whole hosts, generals and other great warriors, O best of the Bharata race, "All of you in a body engaged Bhima in action and fell him down (inasmuch as on him hinges the fate of the Pandavas).

sn: तस्मिन् हते हतं मन्ये पाण्डुसैन्यमशेषतः। प्रतिगृह्य च तामाज्ञां तव पुत्रहस्य पार्थिवाः॥ भीमं प्रच्छादयामासुः शरवर्षेः समन्ततः।
en: When he (Bhimasena) is felled, well may I count upon the Pandu forces as if already slain. Following the behest of your son, all the vassal chiefs (hitting) from all sides, covered Bhima with a thick shower of arrows.

sn: गजाश्च बहुला राजन् नराश्च जयगृद्धिनः॥ रथे स्थिताश्च राजेन्द्र परिवब्रुर्वृकोदरम्।
en: Hosts of elephants, O monarch and men, eager for victory, as also war-chariots and horses, O King of Kings, thickened around Vrikodara.

sn: स तैः परिवृतः शरैः राजन् समन्ततः॥ शुशुभे भरतश्रेष्ठो नक्षत्रैरिव चन्द्रमाः।
en: That chef of the Bharata race, endued with heroic qualities, being thus hemmed in by those brave bands of heroes, looked resplendent like the radiant Moon shedding its effulgence amidst myriads of glowing stars.

sn: परिवेषी यथा सोमः परिपूर्णो विराजते॥ स रराज तथा संख्ये दर्शनीयो नरोत्तमः। निर्विशेषो महाराज यथा हि विजयस्तथा।॥
en: O monarch, that foremost of men, was looking, during that fight, so beautiful, like the full Moon in the midst of his corona. He look like Arjuna. There is no difference between him and Arjuna.

sn: तस्य ते पार्थिवाः सर्वे शरवृष्टिं समासृजन्। क्रोधरक्तेक्षणाः शूरा हन्तुकामा वृकोदरम्॥
en: All those kings with eyes flamed with wrath and bent upon slaying Vrikodara, began to shower down their weapons upon him.

sn: तां विदार्य महासेनां शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। निश्चकाम रणाद् भीमो मत्स्यो जालादिवाम्भसि॥३७
en: As the fish frees itself from the net, so did Bhima cutting their shafts straight free himself from the pressure of the battle.

sn: हत्वा दशसहस्राणि गजानामनिवर्तिनाम्। नृणां शतसहस्रे द्वे द्वे शते चैव भारत॥ पञ्च चाश्वसहस्राणि रथानां शतमेव च। हत्वा प्रास्यन्दयद् भीमो नदी शोणितवाहिनीम्॥
en: O Bharata slaying ten thousand elephants that faced him, two lakhs two hundred men, hundred car-warriors and five thousand horses Bhima actually made a river of blood to flow there.

sn: शोणितोदां रथावर्ता हस्तिग्राहसमाकुलाम्। नरमीनाश्वनक्रान्तां केशशैबलशाद्वलाम्॥ संछिन्नभुजनागेन्द्रां बहुरत्नापहारिणीम्। ऊस्याहां मजपङ्का शीर्षोपलसमावृताम्॥ धनुष्काशां शरावापां गदापरिधकेतनाम्। हंसच्छत्रध्वजोपेतामुष्णीषवरफेनिलाम्॥ हारपद्माकरां चैव भूमिरेणूर्मिमालिनीम्। आर्यवृत्तवतां संख्ये सुतरां भीरुदुस्तराम्॥ योधग्राहवतीं संख्ये वहन्तीं यमसादनम्। क्षणेन पुरुषव्याघ्रः प्रावर्तयत निम्नगाम्॥ यथा वैतरणीमुग्रां दुस्तरामकृतात्मभिः। तथा दुस्तरणी घोरां भीरूणां भयवर्धिनीम्॥
en: In that carnage blood flowed like water and the war-cars forming its eddies, elephants, its alligators, horses and men, its sharks and fishes and the hair of animals, its herbs and moss, were all floating on it. Arms severed from bodies floated like snakes and precious stones were abundant in the bloody current; thighs and marrows formed its gavials and mud and human heads, its mountain. Iron bound bludgeous and maces were also floating there like snakes, and bows and arrows formed its rafts by means of which persons tried to cross that fearful and bloody stream, banners and umbrellas drifted on it like swans and costly head-dresses its foam. The dust rising from the earth were like the waves of the stream and jeweled necklaces were looking like so many lotuses; the brave could alone cross that stream while the faint hearted sunk within to navigate it. That gushing current, with hands of sturdy soldiers forming its alligators and crocodiles, streamed its course towards the realm of Death. (and) and that man with tiger-like ferocity made its course flew on. (And) as the Vaitarani is unnavigable by persons of fifth and inequity, even so was that awful stream of blood to men wanting in valour and intrepidity, making their heart quail with shudder.

sn: यतो यतः पाण्डवेयः प्रविष्टो रथसत्तमः। ततस्ततोऽघातयत योधाशतसहस्रशः॥
en: (And) there that son of Pandu, the best of car-warriors, rushed in, slaying hundred thousands of enemy.

sn: एवं दृष्ट्वा कृतं कर्म भीमसेनेन संयुगे। दुर्योधन महाराज शकुनि वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Duryodhana seeing Bhimasena thus career in battle, ( king said unto Shakuni the following words-

sn: जहि मातुलं संग्रामे भीमसेनं महाबलम्। अस्मिञ्जिते जितं मन्ये पाण्डवेयं महाबलम्॥
en: Overpower in the battle, O uncle, the allpowerful Bhimasena. The victory over the vast array of the Pandava forces hinges on his final overthrow.

sn: ततः प्रायान्महाराज सौबलेयः प्रतापवान्। रणाय महते युक्तो भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः॥ स समासाद्य संग्रामे भीमं भीमपराक्रमम्। वारयामास तं वीरो वेलेव मकरालयम्॥
en: Being thus desired, O king, the powerful son of Subala, the peer of great warriors marshaled in array, marched on-his brothers surrounding him. That hero, affronting the fiercely powerful Bhima in that battle, checked his intrepidity, as if a continent resisting the tides of an ocean.

sn: संन्यवर्तत तं भीमो वार्यमाण: शितैः शरैः। शकुनिस्तस्य राजेन्द्र वामपार्श्वे स्तनान्तरे॥ प्रेषयामास नाराचान् रुक्मपुङ्खाशिलाशितान्।
en: And despite he resistance of the keen shafts, (which the powerful son of Subala hurled against him,) Bhima approached him (in formidable array). Whereupon Shakuni, O king of kings, flung a number of cloth-yard shafts, bedecked with wings of gold and sharpened on stone and assailed Bhima at the seat of his heart.

sn: वर्म भित्वा तु ते घोराः पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः॥ न्यमञ्जन्त महाराज कङ्कबर्हिणवाससः।
en: Those fearful shafts, feathered with the plumes of Kankas and peacocks, O monarch, piercing the coat of mail of the high-souled son of Pandu, sunk deep into his vital parts.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो रणे भीमः शरं रुक्मविभूषितम्॥ प्रेषयामास स रुषा सौबलं प्रति भारत।
en: Being thus smitten in battle, O Bharata, Bhima, then flung, all of a sudden, a shaft laid with gold upon the son of Subala.

sn: तमायान्तं शरं घोरं शकुनिः शत्रुतापनः॥ चिच्छेद सप्तधा राजन् कृतहस्तो महाबलः।
en: And the powerful Shakuni, the inflictor of woes on his enemies and O king, skillful in the manipulation of hands, rent that fearful weapon in seven fragments as it was coursing its way towards him.

sn: तस्मिन् निपतिते भूमौ भीमः क्रुद्धो विशामप्ते॥ धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन सौबलस्य हसन्निव।
en: His weapon thus falling adrift on the ground, O king, Bhima, inflamed with rage, without any strain rent in twain with a broadpointed arrow the bow of the son of Subala.

sn: तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं सौबलेयः प्रतापवान्॥ अन्यदादाय वेगेन धनुर्भल्लांश्च षोडश।
en: Whereupon the mighty son of Subala, throwing away that bow, rendered useless, with the greatest alacrity seized a new one, as also sixteen broad-edged shafts.

sn: तैस्तस्य तु महाराज भल्लैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ द्वाभ्यां स सारथिं ह्या द् भीमं सप्तभिरेव च। ध्वजमेकेन चिच्छेद द्वाभ्यां छत्रं विशाम्पते॥ चतुर्भिश्चतुरो वाहान् विव्याध सुबलात्मजः।
en: And the son of Subala, O king, hit the chariot-driver with two and Bhima with seven; struck off the banner with one and the umbrella with two; and pierced, O lord of the universe, the four chargers with the remaining four chargers with the remaining four of those broad-headed shafts.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज भीमसेनः प्रतापवान्॥ शक्तिं चिक्षेप समरे रुक्मदण्डामयस्मयीम्।
en: Enraged at this, O king, the powerful Bhima, in that battle, threw down a weapon made of iron and the staff of which was decked with gold.

sn: सा भीमभुजनिर्मुक्ता नागजिह्वेव चञ्चला॥ निपपात रणे तूर्णं सौबलस्य महात्मनः।
en: That weapon, resembling in activity the tongue of a snake, being thus cast from the arms of Bhima came speedily down upon the chariot of the noble son of Subala.

sn: ततस्तामेव संगृह्य शक्तिं कनकभूषणाम्॥ भीमसेनाय चिक्षेप क्रुद्धरूपो विशाम्पते।
en: (And) he (the son of Subala) seized that weapon, adorned with gold and O lord of the universe, hurled it back against Bhimasena with a fierce countenance,

sn: सा निर्भिद्य भुजं सव्यं पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः॥ निपपात तदा भूमौ यथा विद्युन्नभश्च्युता।
en: That weapon, piercing through the left arm of the noble son of Pandu, fell down like flashes of lightning coursing on the ground.

sn: अथोत्क्रुष्टं महाराज धार्तराष्ट्रः समन्ततः॥ न तु तं ममृषे भीमः सिंहनादं तरस्विनाम्।
en: Then the Dhartarashtras began to rent the air from all sides with their loud out-crics, but, O king, Bhima could not brook the lion-like roars of the enemy, all of great intrepidity.

sn: अन्यद् गृह्य धनुः सज्यं त्वरमाणो महाबलः॥ मुहूर्तादिव राजेन्द्र च्छादयामास सायकैः। सौबलस्य बलं संख्ये त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मानं महाबलः॥६५
en: That extraordinarily powerful man (Bhima) taking hold of another bow fitted with string, almost in no time, O best of kings, covered the mighty son of Subala and his forces, who were fighting valiantly without caring the least for their lives, with showers of arrows.

sn: तस्याश्वांश्चतुरो हत्वा सूतं चैव विशाम्पते। ध्वजं चिच्छेद भल्लेन त्वरमाणः पराक्रमी॥
en: That mighty man (Bhimasena) with utmost intrepidity stricking off his (Shakuni's) four horses and then sending his charioteer to his eternal rest, O ruler of the universe, rent asunder his adversary's banner with a broadedged arrow.

sn: हताश्वं रथमुत्सृज्य त्वरमाणो नरोत्तमः। तस्थौ विस्फारयंश्चापं क्रोधरक्तेक्षणः श्वसन्॥
en: Speedily bounding out of that steedless chariot, Shakuni, the best of men, with eyes flaming with wrath and stretched bow, took his stand on the ground, breathing all the while heavy breaths.

sn: शरैश्च बहुधा राजन् भीममार्च्छत् समन्ततः। प्रतिहत्य तु वेगेन भीमसेनः प्रतापवान्॥ धनुश्चिच्छेद संक्रुद्धो विव्याध च शतैः शरैः।
en: And then, O king, he covered Bhima with numberless arrows from all sides. Then the mighty Bhima rending asunder Shakuni's arrows with great wrath hit him with a host of sharp arrows.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता शत्रुणा शत्रुकर्शनः॥ निपपात तदा भूमौ किंचित्प्राणो नराधिपः।
en: Being thus afflicted by his powerful assailant, that destroyer of enemies, O king, dropped down on the Earth almost dead.

sn: ततस्तं विह्वलं ज्ञात्वा पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते॥ अपोवाह रथेनाजी भीमसेनस्य पश्यतः।
en: Seeing him (Shakuni) in such a woeful plight, your son, O supreme ruler of the universe, putting him in his own chariot carried him off from the scene of action before the very face of Bhimasena.

sn: रथस्थे तु नरव्याने धार्तराष्ट्राः पराङ्मुखाः॥ प्रदुद्रुवुर्दिशो भीता भीमाजाते महाभये।
en: Seeing that foremost of men, Shakuni, thus knocked down and borne away on Duryodhana's chariot, the Imperial hosts began to beat a hasty retreat from the field and flew in all directions from the very fear of Bhimasena.

sn: सौबले निर्जिते राजन् भीमसेनेन धन्विना॥ भयेन महताऽऽविष्टः पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। अपायाजवनैरश्वैः सापेक्षो मातुलं प्रति॥
en: When the son of Subala was thus discomfited and defeated, O monarch, by that excellent archer (Bhimasena) your son Duryodhana, left the field in a state of trepidation and out of his concern for the life of his uncle Shakuni, urged his fiery chargers to a furious speed.

sn: पराङ्मुखं तु राजानं दृष्ट्वा सैन्यानि भारत। विप्रजग्मुः समुत्सृज्य द्वैरथानि समन्ततः॥
en: Seeing the king thus flee away from the battle, all his troops, O foremost of the line of Bharata, who were each engaged in fierce struggle with a hand-to-hand fight, began to disperse themselves in all directions.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा विद्रुतान् सर्वान् धार्तराष्ट्रान् पराङ्मुखान्। जवेनाभ्यापतद् भीमः किरशरशतान् बहून्॥
en: Observing the whole hosts of the Dhritarasthra force thus dispersing themselves in every direction, Bhima, with great impetuosity rushed against them and attacked them with innumerable arrows.

sn: ते वध्यमाना भीमेन धार्तराष्ट्राः पराङ्मुखाः। कर्णमासाद्य समरे स्थिता राजन् समन्ततः॥
en: Thus afflicted by Bhima, O monarch, the retreating bands of Dhritarashtra's army (all in a body moved towards Karna's flank).

sn: स हि तेषां महावीर्यो द्वीपोऽभूत सुमहाबलः। भिन्ननौका यथा राजन् द्वीपमासाद्य निर्वृताः॥ भवन्ति पुरुषव्याघ्र नाविकाः कालपर्यये। तथा कर्णं समासाद्य तावकाः पुरुषर्षभ॥ समाश्वस्ता: स्थिता राजन् सम्प्रहृष्टाः परस्परम्। समाजग्मुश्च युद्धाय मृत्यु कृत्वा निवर्तनम्॥
en: And coming thither and with them (General Karna) in their centre, they once more held there ground. As the ship-wrecked mariners become comforted in reaching in island, so your distressed army stood cheerfully on finding that mighty Karna. O foremost of the Bharata race, O inightiest of men, O lord of the universe, they then proceeded having death for their ultimate end.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ततो भग्नेषु सैन्येषु भीमसेनेन संयुगे। दुर्योधनऽब्रवीत् किं नु सौबलो वापि संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, what did Duryodhana and Subala's son say on finding our troops shattered in battle by Bhimasena?

sn: कर्णो वा जयतां श्रेष्ठो योधा वा मामका युधि। कृपो वा कृतवर्मा वा द्रौणिर्दुःशासनोऽपि वा॥
en: Or, what did that mighty conqueror-Karna, or Kripa, or Kritavarman, or Drona's son or Dushasana, or the other leaders of my army, say in that battle?

sn: अत्यद्भुतमहं मन्ये पाण्डवेयस्य विक्रमम्। यदेकः समरे सर्वान् योधयामास मामकान्॥
en: The powers of Pandu's son seem to me to be most extraordinary that he could fight single-handed against all the warriors of my army.

sn: यथाप्रतिज्ञं योधानां राधेयः कृतवानपि। कुरूणामथ सर्वेषां कर्णः शत्रुनिषूदनः॥ शर्म वर्म प्रतिष्ठा च जीविताशा च संजय।
en: O Sanjaya, did the son of Radha, that scorcher of foes, keep his vow and did he discharge himself accordingly towards the (hostile) troops? (In fact), he was the bestower of prosperity, the saviour, the refuge and the hopes of the Kurus.

sn: तत् प्रभग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा कौन्तेयेनामितौजसा॥ राधेयो वाप्याधिरथिः कर्णः किमकरोद् युधि। पुत्रा वा मम दुर्धर्षा राजानो वा महारथाः। एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व कुशलो ह्यसि संजय॥
en: How did Karna, the son of Adhiratha and Radha, behave in that battle, on finding our troops worsted and beaten by Kunti's son of illimitable prowess? And also what did my unconquerable sons and the other kings and mighty charioteers of our army do? Tell me of all these, O Sanjaya, because you are a skilled narrator.

sn: संजय उवाच अपराह्ने महाराज सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। जघान सोमकान् सर्वान् भीमसेनस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, the valiant son of Suta began to strike down the Somaka troops, in that afternoon, even on very face of Bhimasena.

sn: भीमोऽप्यतिबलं सैन्यं धार्तराष्ट्र व्यपोथयत् । अथ कर्णोऽब्रवीच्छल्यं पञ्चालान् प्रापयस्व माम्॥
en: The mighty Bhima also began to smite down the Dhritarasthra troops. Upon this Karna ordered (his driver) Shalya to make straight way for the Panchalas.

sn: द्राव्यमाणं बलं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनेन धीमता। यन्तारमब्रवीत कर्णः पञ्चालानेव मां वह॥
en: Karna, on observing that his army was being routed by the highly intelligent Bhimasena, asked his driver once more to drive on direct to the Panchalas.

sn: मद्रराजस्ततः शल्यः श्वेतानश्वान् महाजवान्। प्राहिणोचेदिपपञ्चालान् करूषांश्च महाबलः॥
en: On being thus spoken to, Shalya, the avenger of enemies and the king of Madras, urged those white horses, that could run fast like thought, in the direction of the Chedis, the Panchalas and the Karushas.

sn: प्रविश्य च महत् सैन्यं शल्य: परबलार्दनः। न्ययच्छत् तुरगान् हृष्टो यत्र यत्रैच्छरग्रणीः॥
en: On penetrating into that vast array, Shalya, the avenger of foes, took Karna to the very spot that foremost of warriors wished to be in.

sn: तं रथं मेघसंकाशं वैयाघ्नपरिवारणम्। संदृश्य पाण्डुपञ्चालस्त्रस्ता ह्यासन् विशाम्पते॥
en: O lord of the universe, the very sight of that chariot, dismal like the cloud and enveloped in tiger-skins, struck terror into the hearts of the Pandavas and the Panchalas.

sn: ततो रथस्य निनदः प्रादुरासीन्महारणे। पर्जन्यसमनिर्घोषः पर्वतस्येव दीर्यतः॥
en: Then the clatter of that chariot became audible in that fierce battle like the crash of a thunder or like the sound of a mountain splitting into pieces.

sn: ततः शरशतैस्तीक्ष्णैः कर्ण आकर्णनिःसृतः। जघान पाण्डबलं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Then Karna, drawing the bow-strings close to his ears, shot numberless sharp shafts, which destroyed the Pandava forces by hundreds and thousands.

sn: तं तथा समरे कर्म कुर्वाणमपराजितम्। परिवतुर्महेष्वासाः पाण्डवानां महारथाः॥
en: While the invincible Karna was performing these heroic feats numbers of valiant archers and mighty charioteer of the Pandavas came forth and surrounded him on all sides.

sn: तं शिखण्डी च भीमश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च द्रौपदेयाश्च सात्यकिः॥ परिवर्जिघांसन्तो राधेयं शरवृष्टिभिः।
en: In sooth, Shikhandin, Bhima, Dhristadyumna, Nakula and Sahadeva, as also the (five) sons of Draupadi pressed hard upon the son of Radha and began to shower down their weapons upon him, all kindled with the desire of hastening his departure to the other world.

sn: सात्यकिस्तु तदा कर्णं विंशत्या निशितैः शरैः॥ अताडयद् रणे शूरो जत्रुदेशे नरोत्तमः।
en: In that battle that foremost of men, the valiant Satyaki struck Karna with a score of sharp arrows hitting him on the shoulder-joint.

sn: शिखण्डी पञ्चविंशत्या धृष्टद्युम्नश्च सप्तभिः॥ द्रौपदेयाश्चातुःषष्ट्या सहदेवश्च सप्तभिः। नकुलश्च शतेनाजौ कर्ण विव्याध सायकैः॥
en: In that engagement Shikhandin afflicted him with twenty-five arrows, as did also Dhristadyumna with seven, the sons of Draupadi with sixty-four, Sahadeva with seven and Nakula with a hundred.

sn: भीमसेनस्तु राधेयं नवत्या नतपर्वणाम्। विव्याध समरे क्रुद्धो जत्रुदेशे महाबलः॥
en: The redoubtable Bhimasena, boiling with rage, assailed the son of Radha, in that battle, with ninty straight shafts and hit him (also) in the shoulder-joint.

sn: अथ प्रहस्याधिरथिर्व्याक्षिपद् धनुरुत्तमम्। मुमोच निशितान् बाणान् पीडन् सुमहाबलः॥
en: Then the son of Adhirath, endued with great strength, with an indignant smile, stretched out his superb bow and began to pour down heavy showers of keen edged arrows to the discomfiture of his enemies.

sn: तान् प्रत्यविध्यद् राधेयः पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिः शरैः। सात्यकेस्तु धनुश्छित्त्वा ध्वजं च भरतर्षभ॥ तं तथा नवर्भिर्बाणैराजघान स्तनान्तरे।
en: And the son of Radha assailed them in return, each with five arrows and rending in twain, O best of the line of Bharata, the bow and standard of Satyaki, sped nine arrows against him, hitting him in the centre of his chest.

sn: भीमसेनं ततः क्रुद्धोविव्याध त्रिंशता शरैः॥ सहदेवस्य भल्लेन ध्वज चिच्छेद मारिष। सारथिं च त्रिभिर्बाणैराजघान परंतपः॥ विरथान् द्रौपदेयांश्च चकार भरतर्षभ। अक्ष्णौनिमेषमात्रेण तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: And then, with great violence, struck Bhimasena with thirty shafts. That scorcher of foes, O sire, next struck off Sahadeva's standard with a flat-faced arrow and then pierced his charioteer with three others. He, O foremost of the Bharata race, almost in no time, deprived the (five) sons of Draupadi of their chariots and it seemed truly wonderful.

sn: विमुखीकृत्य तान् सर्वाशरैः संनपपर्वभिः। पञ्चालानहनच्छूरांश्चेदीनां त महारथान्॥
en: In fact, the straight dead shots of the mighty Karna, made those brave warriors retreat from the field; and he caused a havoc amongst the Panchalas and the powerful car-warriors of the Chedis.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे चेदिमत्स्स्या विशांपते। कर्णमेकमभिद्रुत्य शरसङ्घः समार्पयन्॥
en: The Chedis and Matsyas, O ruler of the universe, being thus worsted in that encounter, all pressed forward and made a supreme effort to fell down Karna and poured down a heavy shower of arrows upon him.

sn: ताञ्जघान शितैर्बाणैः सूतपुत्रो महारथः। ते वध्यमानाः समरे चेदिमत्या विशाम्पते॥ प्राद्रवन्त रणे भीताः सिंहनस्ता मृगा इव।
en: In that battle, the mighty son of Suta, alone and unaided, fought single-handed with his own prowess and kept all the great Pandava archers at bay, despite their utmost endeavour.

sn: एतदुत्यद्भुतं कर्म दृष्ट्वानस्मि भारत॥ यदेकः समरे शूरान् सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। यतमानान् परं शक्त्या योधयानांश्च धन्विनः॥ पाण्डवेयान् महाराज शरैर्वारितवान् रणे। तत्र भारत कर्णस्य लाघवेन महात्मनः॥ तुतुषुर्देवताः सर्वाः सिद्धाश्च सह चारणैः।
en: O descendant of king Bharata, I am an eyewitness of this extraordinary and wonderful feat and the gods themselves, the Siddhas and Charans were all highly pleased to see the lightness of the hands of the noble Karna.

sn: अपूजयन् महेष्वासा धार्तराष्ट्रा नरोत्तमम्॥ कर्णं रथवरश्रेष्ठं श्रेष्ठं सर्वधनुष्मताम्।
en: And O lordly being, all the great warriors of the Dhritarasthra force paid him their homage and worshipped him as the best of all bowmen.

sn: ततः कर्णो महाराज ददाह रिपुवाहिनीम्॥ कक्षमिद्धो यथा वह्निर्निदाधे ज्वलितो महान्।
en: And then, O monarch, as in summer the blazing conflagration burns heaps of hay into ashes, so did Karna consume his enemies' forces, as it were, with the fire of his weapons.

sn: ते वध्यामानाः कर्णेन पाण्डवेयास्ततस्ततः॥ प्राद्रवन्त रणे भीताः कर्ण दृष्ट्वा महारथम्।
en: Thus beaten by that foremost of carwarriors, Karna, the Pandava troops began to flee in all directions-afraid to face him in battle.

sn: तत्राक्रन्दो महानासीत् पञ्चालानां महारणे॥ वध्यतां सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैः कर्णचापवरच्युतैः।
en: Afflicted with the sharp shots coming out of Karna's bow in that battle the Panchalas sent forth bitter cries of woe.

sn: तेन शब्देन विवस्ता पाण्डवानां मराचमूः॥ कर्णमेकं रणे योधं मेनिरे तत्र शात्रवाः।
en: Bewildered at that tumultuous uproar, the vast army, comprising the Pandava force and belonging to the hostile party, regarded him as the hero of the field in that great battle.

sn: तत्राद्भुतं पुनश्चक्रे राधेयः शत्रुकर्शनः॥ यदेनं पाण्डवाः सर्वे न शेकुरभिवीक्षितुम्।
en: The son of Radha, that scorcher of his enemies, displayed once again such wonderful prowess that the Pandavas, all combined, dared not even to look at him.

sn: यथौघः पर्वतश्चेष्ठमासाद्याभिप्रदीर्यते॥ तथा तत् पाण्डवं सैन्यं कर्णमासाद्य दीर्यते।
en: And like a stream dividing itself when checked by a mountain, so did the Pandava forces break themselves opposed by Karna.

sn: कर्णोऽपि समरे राजन् विधूमोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन्॥ दहंस्तस्थौ महाबाहुः पाण्डवानां महाचमूम्।
en: In that battle, the mighty and strong-armed Karna, O king, burning the vast army of the Panchalas, stood out in relief like a blazing fire without smoke.

sn: शिरांसि च महाराज कर्णाश्चैव स कुण्डलान्॥ बाहूंश्च वीरो वीराणां चिच्छेद लधु चेषुभिः।
en: That strong-armed man with great lightness of hands, O monarch, began to strike off with his shafts, the arms and heads, as also the ears adorned with rings of many of his sturdy enemy.

sn: हस्तिदन्तत्सरून् खङ्गान् ध्वजाशक्तीर्हयान् गजान्॥४१ स्थांश्च विविधान् राजन् पताका व्यजनानि च। अक्षं च युगयोक्त्राणि चक्राणि विविधानि च॥ शरान्धकारे तु चिच्छेद बहुधा कर्णो योधव्रतमनुष्ठितः।
en: He went on, O king, cutting off horses, elephants, shafts, swords with hilts of ivory, fans and cars and wheels, axles and yokes, as also many other things in a mess, like a hero.

sn: तत्र भारत कर्णेन निहतैर्गजवाजिभिः४३।। अगम्यरूपा पृथिवी मांसशोणितकर्दमा।
en: Heaps of carcasses of elephants and horses, slain by Karna, O Bharata, were lying on the sides and the earth became slippery with their blood, while their dead bodies blocked the way and made it impassable.

sn: विषमं च समं चैव हतैरश्वपदातिभिः॥ रथैश्च कुञ्चरैश्चैव न प्राज्ञायत किञ्चन।
en: The earth became so covered over with dead bodies of horses, foot soldiers, elephants and with broken cars that it became impossible to distinguish the even land from the uneven.

sn: नापि स्वे न परे योधाः प्राज्ञायन्त परस्परम्॥ घोरे कर्णस्त्रे च विजृम्भिते।
en: The (atmosphere) became dark as pitch with the shower of arrows shot by Karna and nobody could know each other, or foes from friends.

sn: राधेयचापनिर्मुक्तैः शरैः काञ्चनभूषणैः॥ संछादिता महाराज पाण्डवानां महारथाः।
en: O monarch, the great car-warriors of the Pandavas, were covered with the gold-decked darts coming out of Karna's bow.

sn: ते पाण्डवेयाः समरे राधेयेन पुनः पुनः॥ अभज्यन्त महाराज यतमाना महारथाः।
en: O king, the son of Radha repeatedly broke the ranks of the powerful car-warriors of the Pandavas, though they tried their utmost to worst him in that fight.

sn: मृगसङ्घान यथा क्रुद्धः सिंहो द्रावयते वने॥ पञ्चालानां रयश्रेष्ठान् द्रावयशात्रवांस्तथा। कर्णस्तु समरे योधास्त्रासयन् सुमहायशाः॥ कालयामास तत् सैन्यं यथा पशुगणान् वृकः।
en: As in a wild the herds of deer are scared away before an angry lion or other animals seeing an wolf, so, in that battle, the foremost car-warriors of the Panchalas and other great car-warriors of the Pandavas were driven before Karna.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवी सेनां धार्तराष्ट्राः पराङ्मुखीम्॥ तत्राजग्मुर्महेष्वासा रुवन्तो भैरवान् रवान्।
en: As the Pandava troops turned their backs in battle the powerful Dhartarashtras followed them uttering loud shouts.

sn: दुर्योधन हि राजेन्द्र मुदा परमया युतः॥ वादयामास संहृष्टो नानावाद्यानि सर्वशः।
en: O king of kinds, Duryodhana being very glad ordered in great glee his war bands to discourse music throughout the whole range of his army.

sn: पञ्चालापि महेष्वासा भग्नास्तत्र नरोत्तमाः॥ न्यवर्तन्त यथा शूरं मृत्यु कृत्वा निवर्तनम्।
en: The great Panchala warriors, the best of men, all determined to die in that battle, returned bravely to the field.

sn: तान् निवृत्तान् रणे शूरान् राधेयः शत्रुतापनः :॥ अनेकशो महाराज बभञ्ज पुरुषर्षभः।
en: O king, those brave warriors were repeatedly broken down in that light by the son of Radha, the smiter of his enemies and powerful like a bull.

sn: तत्र भारत कर्णेन पञ्चाला विंशती रथाः॥ निहताः सायकैः क्रोधाचेदयश्च परः शताः।
en: O Bharata, twenty Panchala car-warriors and more than a hundred of the Chedis were sent to the other world by Karna's arrows.

sn: कृत्वा शून्यान् रथोपस्थान् वाजिपृष्ठांश्च भारत॥ निर्मनुष्यान् गजस्कन्धान् पादातांश्चैव विद्वतान्।
en: O descendant of Bharata, he (Karna) pulled down men from their seats in the cars' and from the backs of horses and elephants' and also scared away the infantry.

sn: आदित्य इव मध्याह्ने दुर्निरीक्ष्यः परंतपः॥ कालान्तकवपुः शूरः सूतपुत्रोऽभ्यराजत।
en: That brave warrior, the son of Suta, the siniter of his foes, like Pluto at the time of destruction looked brilliant as the sun in the meridian and nobody could set his eyes upon him.

sn: एवमेतन्महाराज नरवाजिरथद्विपान्॥ हत्वा तस्थौ महेष्वासः कर्णोऽरिगणसूदनः। यथा भूतगणान् हत्वा कालस्तिष्ठेन्महाबलः॥ तथा स सोमकान् हत्वा तस्थावेको महारथः।
en: O great monarch, after destroying hosts of elephants, horses, infantry and car-warriors, that powerful archer, the destroyer of his enemies, stood upon his chariot. The great carwarrior Karna after killing the Somakas stood like the mighty Pluto after destroying the elephants.

sn: तत्राद्भुतपपश्याम पञ्चालानां पराक्रमम्॥ वध्यमानापि यत् कर्ण नाजहू रणमूर्धनि।
en: The Panchalas also showed very great courage, for they never left the head of the battle-field, even when thus distressed by Karna.

sn: राजा दुःशासनश्चैव कृपः शारद्वतस्तथा॥ अश्वत्थामा कृतवर्मा शकुनिश्च महाबलः। न्यहनन् पाण्डवीं सेनां शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: And the king (Duryodhana), killed the Pandava forces by hundreds and thousands as did also Dushasana, Kripa, the son of Sharadvata, Ashvatthama, Kritavarman and Shakuni of great strength.

sn: कर्णपुत्रौ तु राजेन्द्र भ्रातरौ सत्यविक्रमौ। निजघ्नाते बलं क्रुद्धौ पाण्डवानामितस्ततः॥
en: The two sons of Karna too, aye those two brothers of unconquerable strength, O king of kings, boiling with rage, waged a ruthless slaughter among the Pandava hosts in many different places.

sn: तत्र युद्ध महचासीत् क्रूरं विशसनं महत् । तथैव पाण्डवाः शूरा धृष्टद्युम्नशिखण्डिनौ॥ द्रौपदेयाश्च संक्रुद्धा अभ्यघ्नंस्तावकं बलम्।
en: And the battle (that ensued then) was deadly in the extreme and the slaughter (which followed) was really very great. Then the Pandava warriors Dhristadyumna and Shikhandin, the five sons of Draupadi, fretting and foaming with rage, caused a terrible havoc among your troops.

sn: एवमेष क्षयो वृत्तः पाण्डवानां ततस्ततः। तावकानामपि रणे भीमं प्राप्य महाबलम्॥
en: And thus the losses which attended the Pandava forces in their several divisions, were equal to those of your own, when the allpowerful Bhima joined them (the Pandavas) in the field.

sn: संजय उवाच अर्जुनस्तु महाराज हत्वा सैन्यं चतुर्विधम्। सूतपुत्रं च संक्रुद्ध दृष्ट्वा चैव महारणे॥ शोणितोदां महीं कृत्वा सांसमजास्थिपङ्कलाम्। मनुष्य शीर्षपाषाणां हस्त्यश्वकृतरोधसम्॥ शूरस्थिचयसंकीर्णा काकगृध्रानुनादिताम्। छत्रहंसप्लवोपेता वीरवृक्षापहरिणीम्॥ हारपद्माकरवतीमुष्णीषवरफेनिलाम्। धनुःशरध्वजोपेतांन नरक्षुद्रकपालिनीम्॥ चर्मवर्मभ्रमोपेतां रथोडुपसामाकुलाम्। जयैषिणां च सुतरां भीरूणां च सुदुतराम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Arjuna in that great battle, after destroying the four divisions (of the army belonging to the enemy) and taking a glance of the enraged son of Suta, make a river of blood to flow there, a river that was filled with flesh, bones and marrow; elephants and horses formed the bed of that river; and human heads, like rocks and stones strewn on all sides, seemed to resound with the cries of crows and ravens, umbrellas floated like swans; and bodies of brave soldiers like so many trees drifted away by the current; necklaces were like lotuses in the stream; and head-dresses its foam, broken pieces of skulls floated about and bows and arrows were like fishes in it; armours and shields formed its eddies; chariots, with which it teemed, were like its rafts; and braver-hearted men could alone cross that bloody stream, while the fainthearted sunk within to navigate it.

sn: नदी प्रवर्तयित्वा च बीभत्सुः परवीरहा। वासुदेवमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Vibhatsu, the foremost of men and smiter of hostile warriors after making this bloody stream to flow, spoke the following words to Vasudeva.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच एष केतू रणे सूतपुत्रस्य दृश्यते। भीमसेनादयश्चैते योधयन्ति महारथम्॥
en: Arjuna said "O Krishna, I see the banner of Suta our troops, with Bhimasena at their head are fighting with that mighty car-warrior.

sn: एते द्रवन्ति पञ्चालाः कर्णवस्ता जनार्दन। एष दुर्योधनो राजा श्वेतच्छत्रेण धार्यता॥ कर्णेन भग्नान् पञ्चाला: द्रावयन् बहु शोभते।
en: O Janaradana, the Panchalas becoming afraid of Karna are melting away. Behold, king Duryodhana, along-side Karna is looking exceeding beautiful, with the white umbrella over the head, in his efforts to rout the Panchalas.

sn: कृपुश्च कृतवर्मा च द्रौणिश्चैव महारथः॥ एते रक्षान्ति राजानं सूतपूत्रेण रक्षिताः। अवध्यमानास्तेऽस्माभिर्घातयिष्यन्ति सोमकान्॥
en: Karna is protecting Kripacharya, Kritavarman and Ashvatthama, while those great warriors are protecting the king Duryodhana in their turn; and unless we resist them they will cause a massacre among the Somakas.

sn: एष शल्यो रथोपस्थे रश्मिसंचारकोविदः। सूतपुत्ररथं कृष्ण वाहयन् बहु शोभते॥
en: O Krishna, Shalya, a thorough master in the art of driving, is looking surpassingly beautiful, as he drives the chariot of Suta's son, seated on high seat of the car.

sn: तत्र मे बुद्धित्पन्ना वाहयात्र महारथम्। नाहत्वा समरे कर्णं निवर्तिष्ये कथञ्चन॥ राधेयो ह्यन्यथा पार्थान् सृञ्जयांश्च महारथान्। निःशेषान् समरे कुर्यात् पश्यता नो जनार्दन॥
en: It would be well to go over there, so lead my big chariot in that direction, I am not going to return without killing Karna in that fight. O Janaradana, the whole hosts of the Pandavas and the Srinjayas will all be destroyed before our very face, unless this son of Radha be killed.'

sn: ततः प्रायाद् रथेनाशु केशवस्तव वाहिनीम्। कर्णं प्रति महेष्वासं द्वैरथे सव्यसाचिना॥
en: Thus asked Keshava led the chariot through your army towards the great archer, Karna, with a view to bring about a dual fight between him and Savyasachin.

sn: प्रयातश्च महाबाहुः पाण्डवानुज्ञया हरिः। आश्वासयन् रथेनैव पाण्डुसैन्यानि सर्वशः॥
en: As urged by the son of Pandu the very driving of the car by the strong-armed Vasudeva gave assurance to the Pandava troops and cheered them up.

sn: रथघोषः स संग्रामे पाण्डवेयस्य सम्बभौ। वासवाशनितुल्यस्य मेघौघस्येव मारिष॥
en: In that fight the rattling noise of the wheels of the car of Pandu's son, sounded, O sire, like the rumbling of Vasava's thunder.

sn: महता रथघोषेण पाण्डवः सत्यविक्रमः। अभ्ययादप्रमेयात्मा निर्जयंस्तव वाहिनीम्॥
en: The of Pandu of unfathomable nobleness and the very personification of power, thus went on destroying your army as he proceeded onward with the loud rattling noise of his car.

sn: तमायान्तं समीक्ष्यैव श्वेताश्वं कृष्णसारथिम्। मद्रराजोऽब्रवीत् कर्णं केतुं दृष्ट्वा महात्मनश्च :॥
en: Looking at the standard, the white steeds and the black driver, (Krishna) of the noble Arjuna, Shalya, the king of Madra, addressing Karna, said son

sn: अयं स रथ आयाति श्वेताश्वः कृष्णसारथिः। निजन्नमित्रान् समरे यं कर्णं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: “You were inquiring about Arjuna; there comes he in that chariot drawn by white steeds and driven by the black charioteer (Krishna), destroying his enemies as he-makes his way forward.

sn: एष तिष्ठति कौन्तेयः संस्पृशन् गाण्डिवं धनुः। तं हनिष्यसि चेदद्य तन्नः श्रेयो भविष्यति॥
en: There stands the son of Kunti with the outstretched Gandiva in his hand; save us by killing him.

sn: धनुा चन्द्रचाराङ्का पताकाकिङ्किणीयुता। पश्य कर्णार्जुनस्यैषा सौदामन्यम्बरे यथा॥
en: O Karna! Look at this twang of Arjuna's bow and here is the flag marked with moon and stars small bells are hanging from it and these are showing like skylark.

sn: एष ध्वजाग्रे पार्थस्य प्रेक्षमाणः समन्ततः। दृश्यते वानरो भीमो वीराणां भयवर्धनः॥
en: At the top of the Arjuna's flag a dreadful monkey is seen. It is enhancing fear of Kaurava's warriors with its watch all around.

sn: एतचक्रं गदा शङ्खः शार्ङ्ग कृष्णसह्यच च प्रभो। दृश्यते पाण्डवरथे वाहयान्सय वाजिनः॥
en: Lord Sri Krishna's discus, gada, conch and sarnga bow are being seen here. He is driving the horses of Panduputra, Arjuna.

sn: एतत् कूजित गाण्डिवंन विसृष्ट सव्यसाचिना। एते हस्तवता मुक्ता मन्त्यमित्राशिताः शराः॥
en: This is twang sound coming from the stretched Gandiva of Savyasanchi (Arjuna). These arrows shot by Arjuna are very acute and killing ceaselessly the enemies.

sn: विशालायतताम्राक्षैः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननैः। एषा भूः कीर्यते राज्ञां शिरोभिरपलायिनाम्॥
en: This battle-field is being covered with the cut-off heads of the brave kings who seldom show their back to the battle-field. The eyes on those heads are huge and red and face is attractive as full moo.

sn: एते परिघसंकाशाः पुण्यगन्धानुलेपनाः। उद्धता रणशूराणां पात्यन्ते सायुधा भुजाः॥
en: These arms uplifted with arms and weapons by the chivalrous persons are continuously cutoff in the battle-field. These arms are as thick as Parigha and duly smeared with pure sandal wood.

sn: निरस्तजिह्वानेत्रान्ता वाजिनः सह सादिभिः। पतिताः पात्यमानाश्च क्षितौ क्षीणा विशेरते॥
en: These horses are being knocked down on the ground with several injuries inflicted by shots of arrows and their riders. Their tongues and eyes have come out owing to excessive pressure of wheels on of wheels on them. These are slumbering on the ground.

sn: एते पर्वतश्रृङ्घाणां तुल्या हैमवता गजाः। संछिन्नकुम्भाः पार्थेन प्रपतन्त्यद्रयो यथा।॥
en: The elephants from Himachala Pradesha seemed as if these are mountain ridges collapsing the same way on the ground.

sn: गन्धर्वनगराकारा रथा वा ते नरेश्वराः। विमानादिव पुण्यान्ते स्वर्गिणे निपतन्त्यमी॥
en: Arjuna has cut-off their trunks. These are huge chariot like Gandharva city and these beheaded kings are falling down from them, as the heaven dwellers fall from air-craft down when their account of noble deeds is squared up.

sn: व्याकुलीकृतमर्थ परसैन्य किरीटिना। नानामृगसहस्राणां यूथं केसरिणां यथा॥
en: Arjuna, the crown holder has made impatient to the army of enemy as a lion becomes cause for anxiety to several thousand stags.

sn: त्वामिभिप्रेप्सुरायाति कर्ण निनन् वरान् रथान्। असह्यमानो राधेय तं याहि प्रति भारत॥
en: O Karna, he is willing to try his strength with you in battle and being restless is slaying many of our picked warriors. Advance, O son of Radha, onward to meet that descendant of Bharata race.

sn: एषा विदीर्यते सेना धार्तराष्ट्री समन्ततः। अर्जुनस्य भयात् तूर्ण निघ्नतः शात्रवान् बहून्॥
en: Slaughtered in large large numbers, the Dhritarashtra troops have become afraid of and are giving way before him.

sn: वर्जयन् सर्वसैन्यानि त्वरते हि धनंजय। त्वदर्थमिति मन्येहं यथास्योदीर्यते वपुः॥
en: I believe, hastily he is coming towards you avoiding other warriors, his body is swelling with wrath.

sn: न ह्यवस्थास्यते पार्थो युयुत्सुः केनचित् सह। त्वामृते क्रोधदीप्तो हि पीडयमाने वृकोदरे॥
en: You have worsted Vrikodara and so Partha is burning with anger to meet you in battle and would not wait to fight out any other warrior save and beyond yourself.

sn: विरथं धर्मराज तु दृष्ट्वा सुदृढविक्षतम्। शिखण्डिनं सात्यकिं च धृष्टद्युमं च पार्षतम्॥ द्रौपदेयान् युधामन्युमुत्तमौजसमेव च। नकुलंन सहदेव च भ्रातरौ द्वौ समीक्ष्य च॥ सहसैकरथः पार्थस्त्वामभ्येति परंतपः। क्रोधरक्तेक्षणः क्रुद्धो जिघासुः सर्वपार्थिवान्॥
en: You have badly hurt the virtuous King Yudhishthira and deprived him of his chariot, you have placed Shikhandin, Satyaki, the sons of Draupadi, Yudhamanyu, Uttamaujas and his brothers Nakula and Sahadeva in woeful plights; Partha, the smiter of his enemies, in a sullen mood and blood-shot eyes, is advancing, in hot haste and with impetuosity, to wreak his vengeance on you. Eluding the grasp of other warriors he is hastily advancing towards us.

sn: त्वरितोऽभिपतत्यस्मांस्त्यक्तवा सैन्यान्यसंशयम्। त्वं कर्ण प्रतियाह्येनं नास्त्यन्यो हि धनुर्धरः॥
en: There is not doubt that they have attacked on us in precipitation galloping over the whole army all escaped. Hence, O Karna! March forward to face them because no other archer than you is able to tackle this assignment.

sn: न तं पश्यामि लोकेऽस्मिस्त्वत्तो ह्यन्यं धनुर्धरम्। अर्जुनं समरे क्रुद्धं यो वेलामिव धारयेत्॥
en: As a continent resists the fury of the surging sea, so you are the only archer in all the world who can resist Dhananjaya's rage.

sn: न चास्य रक्षां पश्यामि पार्श्वतो न च पृष्ठतः। एक एवाभियाति त्वां पश्य साफल्यमात्मनः॥
en: He is advancing all alone, there is none to guard him in the front or in the rear and well may you now count upon success following you.

sn: त्वं हि कृष्णौ रणे शक्तः संसाधयितुमाहवे। तवैव भारो राधेय प्रत्युद्याहि धनंजयम्॥
en: You are the only man who can cope with the Krishnas in battle, so make your march, O son of Radha; you alone are capable of it.

sn: समानो ह्यसि भीष्मेण द्रोणद्रौणिकृपेण च। शव्यसाचिनमायान्तं निवारय महारणे॥
en: You stand in the same footing with Bhishma, Drona, Drauni and Kripa; in prowess, so put a stop to the advance of Savyasachin in this great battle.

sn: लेलिहानं यथा सर्प गर्जन्तमृषभ यथा। वनस्थितं यथा व्याघ्र जहि कर्ण धनंजयम्॥
en: Dhananjaya is looking like a snake protruding his quivering tongue, or like a bull bellowing loudly in rage, or indeed, like a tiger of a forest; O Karna, put an end to him.

sn: एते द्रवन्ति समरे धार्तराष्ट्रा महारथाः। अर्जुनस्य भयात् तूर्णं निरपेक्षा जनाधिपाः॥
en: Not at all caring for the safety of others those chiefs, the principal warriors of Dhritarasthra army, are melting away, being afraid to face Arjuna.

sn: द्रवतामथ तेषां तु नान्योऽस्ति युधि मानवः। भयहा यो भवेद् वीरस्त्वामृते सूतनन्दन॥
en: O mighty warrior, O Suta's son, you are the only man in this field who can bring relief and assurance into the hearts of flying chiefs.

sn: एते त्वां कुरवः सर्वे द्वीपमासाद्य संयुगे। धिष्ठिताः पुरुषव्याघ्र त्वत्तः शरणकाङ्क्षिणः॥
en: As in a tempest the drowning sailor look forward anxiously for an island for their protection, so the whole Kaurava army is looking up to you, O foremost of men, as their saviour.

sn: तां धृतिं कुरु वैदेहाम्बष्ठ काम्बोजास्तथा नग्नजितस्त्वया। गान्धाराश्च यया धृत्या जिताः संख्ये सुदुर्जयाः। राधेय ततः प्रत्येहि पाण्डवम्॥ वासुदेवं च वार्ष्णेय प्रीयमाणं किरीटिना। प्रत्युद्याहि महाबाहो पौरुषे महति स्थितः॥
en: O son of Radha, you have worsted in battle the unconquerable Vaidehas, Abvasthas, Kambojas, Nagnajits and the Gandharas, now with the same energy and putting forth your best exertion and prowess, O mighty armed one, like a man, do you proceed onward and attack the son of Pandu, as also against Vasudeva, the descendant of Vrishni and who is always adorned by the crowned Arjuna.
