en: As the huge tree uprooted of a strong storm falls down on ground, the great chariot fighter Kratha, fell down from the chariot on ground when a hill national (warrior) shot a voiley of arrows from his elephant.

sn: वृको द्विपस्थं गिरिराजवासिनं भृशं शरैर्द्वादशभिः पारभिनत्। ततो वृकं साश्वरथं महाद्विपो दुतं चतुर्भिश्चरणैर्व्यपोथयत्॥
en: Vrika then injured severely with hard blows through twelve arrows he shot on that mountaineer king. That huge elephant of mountain king leapt on Vrika and crushed him unto death immediately under its four feet. This chariot and horses were also crushed simultaneously.

sn: स नागराजः सनियन्तृकोऽपतत् तथा हतो बभ्रुसुतेषुभिभक्रशम्। स चापि देवावृधसूनुरर्दितः पपात नुन्नः सहदेवसूनुना॥
en: Finally, that elephant also fell on the ground with is Mahadeva because of penetrated badly by son of Babhru with volley of arrows he shot. The son of Devavridha also fell down dead when son of Sahadeva had shot acute arrows on him.

sn: विषाणगात्राफरयोधपातिना गजेन हन्तुं शकुनि कुलिन्दजः। जगाम् वेगेन भृशार्दयंश्च तं ततोऽस्य गान्धारपतिः शिरोऽहरत्॥
en: The second son of Kulinda attacked on Shakuni by the elephant capable to knock down the great warriors through his teeth, body and trunk and severally injured him. Shakuni, the king of Gandharva then beaded him.

sn: ततः शतीनीकहता महागजा हता रथाः पत्तिगणाश्च तावकाः। स्तथागता गां विवशा विचूर्णिताः॥
en: Shatanika then attacked immediately on your army. As the snakes fall on the ground when penetrated by the Garuda's (eagle) wing, your huge elephants, horses, chariots and infantry fell down on the ground and splitted up in pieces.

sn: ततोऽभ्वविद्धयद् बहुभिः शितैः शरैः कलिङ्गपुत्रो नकुलात्मजं स्मयन्। ततोऽस्य कोपाद् विचकर्त नाकुलिः शिरः क्षुरेणाम्बुजसंनिभाननम्॥
en: The son of Kalinga king shot numerous acute arrows with smile on Shatanika, the son of Nakula and damaged his body severely. The son of Nakula furiated on hearing this and he beheaded the lotus like face with a blow he made by a Kshura.

sn: स्त्रिभिः शरैः कर्णसुतोऽर्जुनं त्रिभिः। जनार्दनं द्वादशभिश्च सायकैः॥
en: Vrishascna, the son of Karna then injured Shatanika v ith three arrows, made of iron. He then penetrated Arjuna with three, Bhimasena with another three, Nakula with seven and Sri Krishna with twelve arrows.

sn: तु तदस्य कर्मातिमनुष्यकर्मणः समीक्ष्य हृष्टाः कुरवोऽभ्यपूजयन्। पराक्रमज्ञास्तु धनंजयस्य ये हुतोऽयमग्नाविति ते मेनिरे॥
en: All Kauravas filled with ecstasy to see this phenomenal valour of Vrishasena and they started appreciating him again and again. However, the people known of Arjuna's valour, understood it definitely that this Vrishasena will become morsel of fire.

sn: ततः किरीटी परवीरघाती हताश्वमालोक्य नरप्रवीरः। णाद्रीसुतं नकुलं लोकमध्ये समीक्ष्य कृष्णं भृशविक्षतं च॥
en: Arjuna, the great warrior of this human world, capable to kill all enemies a attacked forcibly on Vrishasena who had killed the horses of Nakula, the son of Madri and made attack on injured Sri Krishna Vrishasena was stood before Karna at that time.

sn: समभ्यधावद् वृषसेनमाहवे स सूतजस्य प्रमुखे स्थितस्तदा। तमापतन्तं नरवीरमुग्रं महाहवे बाणसहस्रधारिणम्॥ अभ्यापतत् कर्णसुतो महारथं यथा महेन्द्रं नमुचिः पुरा तथा।
en: When Vrishasena, the son of Karna saw Arjuna, the great chariot fighter with a store of several thousand arrows in that great war, he rushed towards him with the same way as Namuci had made an attack on Indra, the king of gods.

sn: ततो द्रुतं चैकशरेण पार्थ शितेन विद्ध्वा युधि कर्णपुत्रः॥
en: The great warrior Vrishasena, son of Karna injured the son of Kunti in battle-field with sharp blow from an arrow and began challenging with loud voice.

sn: ननाद नादं सुमहानुभावो विद्ध्वेव शक्रं नमुचिः स वीरः। र्बाणैरविद्धयद् भुजमूले तु सव्ये॥
en: Vrishasena then re-attacked at the root of the Arjuna's left arm, injured again Krishna by shooting nine arrows and injured Arjuna, the son of Kunti again with ten arrows shot on him.

sn: तथैव कृष्णं नवभिः समादयत् पुनश्च पार्थं दशाभिर्जधान्। रभ्याहतः श्वेतहयः शरैस्तैः॥
en: Arjuna, the rider on white horses filled with slight anger as he was also injured by the arrows shot by Vrishasena. He then decided to kill the son of Karna.

sn: संरम्भमीषद्गमितो वधाय कर्णात्मजस्याथ मनः प्रदधे। ततः किरीटी रणमूर्ध्नि कोपात् कृत्वा त्रिशाखां भ्रकुटि ललाटे॥ मुमोच तूर्ण विशिखान् महात्मा वधे धतः कर्णसुतस्य संख्ये।
en: Arjuna, the crown holder started attacking with arrows on the course of battle with haste when decided to kill the son of Karna in the battle-field. His brows curved at three spots on account of fallen in sheer anger.

sn: आरक्तनेत्रोऽन्तकशत्रुहन्ता उवाच कर्ण भृशमुत्सस्मयंस्तदा॥ नहं रणे वृषसेन तमुग्रम्। सम्पश्यतः कर्ण तवाद्य संख्ये नयामि लोकं निशितैः पृषत्कैः॥
en: His eyes that time had turned slight red. He was capable to kill even the enemy dreadful like Yama. He addressed then Karna Duryodhana and Ashvatthama etc. all warriors present there-"O Karna! I will book the brave Vrishasena, so valorous in battle-field before your eyes."

sn: ऊरनं च तावाद्धि जना वदन्ति सर्वैर्भवद्भिर्मम सूनुर्हतोऽसहौ। एको रथो मद्विहीनस्तरस्वी अहं हनिष्ये भवता समक्षम्॥ महं हनिष्ये वृषकेनमुग्रम्। महं हनिष्येऽर्जुन आजिमध्ये॥
en: My valorous son, chariot fighter (Maharathi) Abhimanyu was all alone. I was not with him. You all had slaughtered him collectively. All people. state all had slaughtered him collectively. All people state that activity as unjustified but I will kill Vrishasena in the presence of you all. O great chariot fighters, save if you can, this son of Karna. I, Arjuna will first kill the great valorous Vrishasena in battle-field and my next step will be taken for Karna, the malign and fool son of a charioteer which will book him definitely for another world.

sn: तमद्य मूलं कलहस्य संख्ये दुर्योधनापाश्रयजातदर्पम्। त्वामद्य हन्तास्मि रणे प्रसा अस्यैव हन्ता युधि भीमसेनः॥ दुर्योधनस्याधमपूरुषस्य यस्यानयादेष महान् क्षयोऽभवत्।
en: O Karna! You only are the bone of contention. Your ego has spurt to climax on receipt of support from Duryodhana. I will kill you definitely by putting my life at stake in the battle-field. The sole cause for this massacre, Duryodhana will be killed by Bhimasena.

sn: स एवमुक्तवा विनिमृज्य चापं लक्ष्यं हि कृत्वा वृषसेनमाजौ॥
en: O king! Gentle Arjuna wiped his bow with these words and started making fierce attack with arrows on Vrishasena, the son of Karna by targeting him.

sn: ससर्ज बाणान् विशिखान् महात्मा वधाय् राजन् कर्णसुतस्य संख्ये। मर्मस्वशङ्कं प्रहसन किरीटी॥
en: Arjuna, the crown holder penetrated his sensitive organs by ten arrows shot on him. He then cut-off his bow with four sharp churas, two arms and the head also.

sn: चिच्छेद चास्येष्वसनं भुजौ च क्षुरैश्चतुर्भिनिशितैः शिस्चा स पार्थबाणाभिहतः पपात रथाद् विबाहुर्विशिरा धरायाम्॥
en: As the huge Shala tree laden with beautiful flowers is collapsed/fell down on ground from the mountain ridge due to strong waves of storm, Vrishsena without arm and head fell down on ground when injured worstly with arrows shot by Arjuna.

sn: सुपुष्पितो वृक्षवरोऽतिकायो वातेरितः शाल इवाद्रिश्रृङ्गात्। सम्प्रेक्ष बाणाभिहतं पतन्तं रथान् सुतं सूतज: क्षिप्रकारी॥
en: Karna, the son of a charioteer aggrieved when he saw his son falling down from chariot due to sharp blows made by Arjuna with his arrows. He marched fast towards Arjuna's chariot in a fury.

sn: रथं रथेनाशु जगाम् रोषात् किरीटिनः पुत्रवधाभितप्तः। तत समक्षं स्वसुतं विलोक्य कर्णो हतं श्वेतहयेन संख्ये। संरम्भमागम्य रपं महात्मा कृष्णार्जुनौ सहसैवाभ्यधावत्॥
en: The bold and egoist Karna filled with anger when he saw his son killed by Arjuna before his eyes and he suddenly made a fierce attack on Arjuna.

sn: संजय उवाच तमायान्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य वेलोवृत्तमिवार्णवम्। गर्जन्त सुमहाकायं दुर्निवारं सुरैरपि।॥ अर्जुनं प्राह दाशार्हः प्रहस्य पुरुर्षभः। अयं सरथ आयाति श्वेताश्वः शल्यसारथिः॥
en: Sanjaya said Vasudeva the foremost of men beholding the great bodied Karna whom the gods could not advancing with roars like the swelling ocean said to Arjuna with a smile. There comes the chariot (of Karna) with gray steeds and Shalya its driver.

sn: येन ते सह योद्धव्यं स्थिरो भव धनंजय। पश्य चैन समायुक्त रथं कर्णस्य पाण्डव॥ श्वेतराजिसमायुक्तं युक्तं राधासुतेन त।
en: O Dhananjaya! With the intention of meeting you in battle so wait with calmness. O son of Pandu, look how beautifully the car of Karna is adorned; the son of Radha is on it.

sn: नानापताकाकलिलं किङ्किणीजालमालिनम्॥ उह्यमानमिवाकाशे विमानं पाण्डुरैर्हयैः। ध्वज त पश्यं कर्णस्य नागकक्षं महात्मनः॥
en: It has four beautiful gray horses and it is also decked with various sorts of banners and net work of bells and how it is being borne as if in the skies by their pale horses. Look the high souled Karna's banner with the sign of elephant rope.

sn: आखण्डलधनुः प्रख्यमुल्लिशन्तमिवाम्बरम्। पश्य कर्ण समायान्तं धार्तराष्ट्रप्रियैषिणम्॥ शरधारा विमुञ्चन्तं धारासारमिवाम्बुदम्।
en: The banner like clouds and resembles the bow of Akhandal (Indra) which divides the sky and earth. See how Karna sends hosts of arrows like clouds pouring down rain as he is advancing fulfill the intention of Dhritarashtra's son.

sn: एष मद्रेश्वरो राजा रथाने पर्यवस्थितः॥ नियच्छति हयान्सय राधेयस्यामितौजसः।
en: The king of Madra (Shalya) is seated on the front of the car and guiding the horses of the powerful Radha's son.

sn: श्रृणु दुन्दुर्भिनिर्घोषं शङ्खशब्दं च दारुणम्॥ सिंहनादांश्च विविधाश्रेणु पाण्डव सर्वतः।
en: to Hear, O son of Pandu, the noise of their tumtums and the shrill note of their conchs and lion-like roars that are coming from all directions.

sn: अन्तर्धाय महाशब्दान् कर्णेनमिततेजसा॥ दोधूयमानस्य भृशं धनुषः शृणु निःस्वनम्।
en: Karna, of unfathomable prowess, has drawn his bow and its loud twang can be heard above all other sounds.

sn: एते दीर्यन्ति सगणाः पञ्चालानां महारथाः॥ दृष्ट्वा केसरिणं क्रुद्धं मृगा इव महावने।
en: As in a forest a wrathful lion scares away herd of deers so the mighty Panchala warriors are melting (before Karna).

sn: सर्वयत्नेन कौन्तेय हन्तुमर्हसि सूतजम्॥ न हि कर्णशरानन्य सोढुमुत्सहते नरः।
en: O son of Kunti, you are the only person who would venture to bear the brunt of his weapons, so you should take all possible measures to kill him.

sn: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वास्त्री लोकान् सतराचरांन्॥ त्वं हि जेतुं रणे शक्तस्तथैव विदितं मम।
en: I know well that you are capable to conquer in battle all the three worlds together with its mobile and immobile creations and the gods and Gandharvas.

sn: भीममुग्रं महात्मानं त्र्यक्षं शर्व कपर्दिनम्॥ न शक्ता द्रष्टमीशानं किं पुनर्योधित प्रभुम्। त्वया साक्षान्महादेव सर्वभूतशिवः शिवः॥ युद्धेनाराधितः स्थाणुर्देवाश्च वरदास्तव। तस्य पार्थ प्रसादेन देवदवस्य शूलिनः॥ जहि कर्णं महाबाहो नमुचिं वृत्रहा यथा। श्रेयस्तेऽस्तु सदा पार्थ युद्धे जयमवाप्नुहि॥
en: Nothing need be told about fighting; men cannot look towards the great god the three eyed and terrible Sarva, also called the Kaparddin. You have satisfied in battle that god of gods the Siva, deity Sthanu, the creator of the happiness of all creatures. O Partha, as Indra slew Namuchi so you will, O, you of powerful arms, by the kindness of the great god who is armed with trident, kill Karna and be victorious; and may it farewell with you.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच ध्रुवः एव जयः कृष्ण मम नास्त्यत्र संशयः। सर्वलोकगुरुर्यस्त्वं तुष्टोऽसि मधुसूदन॥
en: Arjuna said O Krishna, you are the destroyer of Madhu and master of all creation; and as you are kind to me my victory in this battle is sure.

sn: चोदयाश्वान् हृषीकेश रथं मम महारथ। नाहं त्वा समरे कर्णं निवर्तिष्यति फाल्गुनः॥
en: O Hrishikesa, a mighty warrior, urge on the horses and advance with my car. Phalgun will kill Karna.

sn: अद्य कर्णं हतं पश्य मच्छरैः शकलीकृतम्। मां रा द्रक्ष्यसि गोविन्द कर्णेन निहतं शरैः॥
en: O Govinda, today either I will slay Karna and hack him to pieces with my weapons or he will see me killed by his arrows.

sn: उपस्थितमिदं घोरं युद्धं त्रैलोक्यमोहनम् यजनाः कथयिष्यन्ति यावद् भूमिर्धरिष्यति॥
en: You will soon witness the fight that will bewilder the three worlds and it will be spoken of till the world ends.

sn: एवं ब्रुर्वस्तदा पार्थः कृष्णमक्लिष्टकारिणम्। प्रत्युद्ययौ रथेनाशु गजं प्रतिगजो यथा॥
en: Thus speaking to Krishna of inexhaustible energy, Partha advanced towards Karna like one elephant against another.

sn: पुनरप्याह तेजस्वी पार्थः कृष्णमरिंदमम्। चोदयाश्चन हृषीकेष कालोऽयमतिवर्तते॥
en: Partha of great prowess again told Krishna who was the scorcher of foes "O Hrishikesa, time flies, so spur on the steeds".

sn: एवमुक्तस्तदा तेन पाण्डवेन महात्मना। जयेन सम्पूज्य स पाण्डवं तदा। प्रचोदयामास हयान् मनोजवान् स पाण्डुपुत्रस्य रथो मनोजवः क्षणेन कर्णस्य रथागतोऽभवत्॥
en: Thus addressed by the noble son of Pandu Kesava who wishes him victory lashed the steeds which were swift as the mind and very quickly brought the car of Pandu's son before Karna's chariot. steeds which were swift as the mind and very quickly brought the car of Pandu's son before Karna's chariot.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: संजय उवाच वृषसेन हतं दृष्ट्वा शोकामर्षसमन्वितः। पुत्रशोकोद्भवं वारि नेत्राभ्यां समवासृजत्॥ रथेन कर्णस्तेस्वी जगामभिमुखो रिपुम्। युद्धायामर्षताम्राक्षः समाहूय धनंजयम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing his son Vrishasena thrus killed the energetic Karna shed tears with grief and wrath, his eyes red as copper and advanced to meet his enemy having defied Dhananjaya is fight.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तौ रथौ सीर्यसंकशौ वैयाघ्रपरिवारितौ। समेतो दद्दशुस्तत्र द्वाविरामै समुद्गतौ॥
en: Then those two cars covered with tiger skins and shinning with lustre looked like two suns facing each other.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: श्वेताश्वौ पुरुषौ दिव्यावास्थितावरिमर्दनौ। शुशुभाते महात्मानौ चन्द्रदित्यौ यथा दिवि॥
en: Those scorchers of their enemies, the mighty warriors, with white steeds attached to their cars, looked like the sun and moon of the skies in brilliancy.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा विस्मयं जग्मुः सर्वसैन्यानि मारिष। त्रैलोक्यविजये यत्ताविन्द्रवैरोचनाविव॥
en: When those two warriors, like Indra and the Bali (son of Birochan) prepared for fight as if to conquer the three words, all the creatures were struck with wonder.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: रथज्यातलनिर्हादैर्वाणसिंहरवैस्तथा। तौ रथावभिधावन्तौ समालोक्य महीक्षिताम्॥ ध्वजौ च दृष्ट्वा संसक्तो विस्मयः समपद्यतः। हस्तिकक्षं च कर्णस्य वानरं च किरीटिनः॥
en: All the rulers of earth were filled with admiration as those two warriors faced each other with their car wheels rattling their bows twanging and their arrows flying, with whizz, Partha with his ape banner flying and Karna with his banner marked with an elephant and roaring like a lion.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तौ रथौ सम्प्रसक्तौ तु दृष्ट्वा भारत पार्थिवाः। सिंहनादरवांश्चक्रुः साधुवादाश्च पुष्कलान्॥
en: O Bharata, all the kings began to give vent to lion-like roars (with excitement) seeing those two car warriors engaged with each other and praised them greatly.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: दृष्ट्वा च द्वैरथं ताभ्यां तत्र योधा सहस्रशः। चक्रर्बाहुस्वनांश्चैव तथा चैलावधूननम्॥
en: Thousands of fighters, seeing them thus engaged in duel fight, began to sound their arm-pits with the palm of their hands and shook their garments (in excitement).

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: आजघ्नुः कुरवस्तत्र वादित्राणि समन्ततः। कर्णं प्रहर्षयिष्यन्तः शङ्खान् दध्मुश्च सर्वशः॥
en: The Kauravas struck up their martial music and sounded their conchs to excite and please Karna.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तथैव पाण्डवाः सर्वे हर्षयन्तो धनंजयम्। तूर्यशङ्खनिनादेन दिशः सर्वा व्यनादयन्॥
en: The Pandavas also for rousing Dhananjaya caused all the sides to resound with the sound of their drums and conchs.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितोत्क्रुष्टैस्तुमुलं सर्वतोऽभवत्। बाहुशब्दैश्च शूराणां कर्णार्जुनसमागमे॥
en: In that contest between Karna and Arjuna fearful noise arose on account of the shouts and lion-like roars of warriors and for the striking of their palms over their arm-pits.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रौ रथस्थौ रथिनां वरौ। प्रगृहीतमहाचापौ शरशक्तिध्वजायुतौ॥ वर्मिणौ बद्धनिस्त्रिंशौ श्वेताश्वौ शङ्खशोभितौ। तूणीरवरसम्पन्नौ द्वावष्येतौ सुदर्शनौ॥ रक्तचन्दनदिग्धाङ्गौ समदौ गोवृषाविव। चापविद्युद्ध्वजोपेतौ शस्त्रसम्पत्तियोधिनौ॥ चामरव्यजनोपेतौ श्वेतच्छनोपशोभितौ। कृष्णशल्यरथोपेतौ तुल्यरूपौ महारथौ॥ सिंहस्कन्धौ दीर्घभुजौ रक्ताक्षौ हेममालिनौ। सिंहस्कन्धप्रतीकाशौ व्यूढोरस्कौ महाबलौ॥ अन्योन्यवधमिच्छन्तावन्योन्यजयकाङ्क्षिणौ। अन्योन्यमभिधावन्तौ गोष्ठे गोवृषभाविव। प्रभिन्नाविव मातङ्गौ सुसंहब्याविवाचलौ॥ आशीविषशिशुप्रख्यौ यमकालान्तकोपमौ। इन्द्रवृत्राविव क्रुद्धौ सूर्याचन्द्रसमप्रभौ॥ महाग्रहाविव क्रुद्धौ युगान्ताय समुत्थितौ। देवगर्भी देवबल देवतुल्यौ च रूपतः॥ यद्दच्छया समायातौ सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ यथा। बलिनौ समरे दृप्तौ नानाशस्त्रधरौ युधि॥ तौ दृष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रौ शार्दूलाविव धिष्ठितौ। बभूव परमो हर्षस्तावकानां विशाम्पते॥
en: All the persons gazed eagerly on those two best of car warriors and most powerful of men as they faced each other adorned with arrows and darts. Both of them were cased in armour and had sword hanging in their belts; they had grey steeds yoked to their cars and both of them had beautiful conchs; both of them were mighty car warriors, one had Shalya for his driver, the other had Krishna. Both had long arms and necks powerful like that of the lion; their eyes looked red with rage and they were decked with golden garlands; their bows seemed to send forth lightning flashes and they were possessed of choicest of weapons. They were being fanned with chowries and white umbrellas were held over their heads; and they were masters of best arrows and looked most beautiful. Both of them were like furious bulls; and they were both broad chested and had short necks like lion and were exceedingly strong. O monarch, summoning each other to coinbat they precipitated upon one another like two powerful bulls in a cowshed with the intention of slaying one another. As they fought they resembled two furious elephants, or angry mountains, or the little snakes of deadly poison or Yama the destroyer of the creation. Roused against each other like Indra and Vritra (Asura) they resembled the sun and the moon in brilliancy and looked like two planets approaching each other in order to burning the world to its end. They were both handsome as the gods and were of godlike prowess having sprung from heavenly fathers. O king, your army were filled with delight seeing those two brave warriors of tiger-like ferocity engaged in battle.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: संशयः सर्वभूतानां विजये समपद्यत। समेतौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ प्रेक्ष्य कर्णधनंजयौ॥
en: Beholding those foremost of men Karna and Dhananjaya engaged in combat, it could not be said as to who would be victorious in the end.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: उभौ वरायुधरावुभौ रणकृतश्रमौ। उभौ च बाहुशब्देन नादयन्तौ नभस्तलम्॥
en: They were both skilful in war and possessed of select weapons and they made the skies ring back with the noise of sounding their arm-pits.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: उभौ विश्रुतकर्माणै पौरुषेण बलेन च। उभौ च सदृशौ युद्धे शम्बारामरराजयोः॥
en: Both of them were famous for their courage and strength and they were skilful like the (Asura) and the king of gods in war.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: कार्तवीर्यसमौ चोभौ तथा दाशरथेः समौ। विष्णुवीर्यसमौ चौभौ तथा भवसमौ युधि॥
en: Both resembled Kartavirya or Dasaratha's son (Rama) in battle and looked like the god Vishnu himself in prowess or Bhava himself.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: उभौ श्वेतहयौ राजन् रथप्रवरवाहिनौ। सारथी प्रवरौ चैर तयोरास्तां महारणे॥
en: In that fight, O monarch, both of them had white horses and select chariots and the best of drivers.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: ततो दृष्ट्वा महाराज राजमानौ महारथौ। सिद्धतारणसंघाना विस्मयः समपद्यत॥
en: Those two warriors looked beautiful and brilliant on their cars and they were admired by all the Siddhas and Charanas that were present.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तव पुत्रास्ततः कर्ण सबला भरतर्षभ। परिवब्रुर्महात्मानं क्षिप्रमाहवसोभिनम्॥
en: O best of Bharata race, the Dhritarashtras, without losing time, surrounded the noble Karna, who was the best of warriors.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तथैव पाण्डवा हृष्टा धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः। परिवब्रुर्महात्मानं पार्थमप्रतिमं युधि॥
en: So Dhristadyumna, with all the Pandavas surrounded the noble Partha matchless in war.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तावकानां रणे कर्णो ग्लहो ह्यासीद विशाम्पते। तथैव पाण्डवेयानां ग्लहः पार्थोऽभवत् तदा॥
en: Your troops, O monarch, began to fight for Karna and the Pandavas in favor of Partha.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: त एव सभ्यास्तत्रासन् प्रेक्षकाश्चाभवन् स्म ते। तत्रैषा ग्लहमानानां ध्रुवौ जयपराजयौय॥
en: The troops of both the sides were eager witnesses of that great Yama of battle and defeat and victory of either party depended on them (Karna and Arjuna).

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: ताभ्यां द्यूतं समासक्तं विजयायेतराय च। अस्माकं पाण्डवानां च स्थितानां रणमूर्धनि॥
en: To decide the fate of the war they began that duel fight and our men and the Pandavas stood in front of the field see that fight.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तौ तु स्थितौ महाराज समरे युद्धशालिनौ। अन्योन्यं प्रतिसंरब्यावन्योन्यवधकाङ्क्षिणौ॥
en: O king, in that battle those two brave warriors well skilled in warfare, determined to kill each other.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: ताबुभौ प्रजिहीर्षस्ताविन्द्रवृत्राविव प्रभौ। भीमरूपधरावास्तां महाधूमाविव ग्रहौ॥
en: O master, they looked like two fearful comets when they engaged in that deadly fight.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षे साक्षेपा विवादा भरतर्षभ। मिथो भेदाश्च भूतानामासन् कर्णार्जुनान्तरे॥
en: O most powerful of the Bharata race, the inhabitants of the skies different in opinion and angry disputes were going on amongst them as to whether Karna or Arjuna would be victorious.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: व्यश्रूयन्त मिथो भिन्नाः सर्वलोकास्तु मारिष। देवदानवगन्धर्वाः पिशाचोरगराक्षसाः॥ प्रतिपक्षग्रहं चक्रुः कर्णार्जुनसमागमे।
en: Also the whole world was uncertain as to the issue of that fight. The gods, Danavas, the Gandharvas, the Pichachas, the Nagas, the Rakshasas differed in their opinions.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: द्यौरासीत् सूतपुत्रस्य पक्षे मातेव धिष्ठिता॥ भूमिर्धनंजयस्यासीन्मातेव जयकाडिक्षणी।
en: The heavens with all the stars sided Karna and the earth backed Partha as mother wishes her son well.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: गिरयः सागराश्चैव नद्यश्च सजलास्तथा॥ वृक्षाश्चौषधयश्चैव व्याश्रयन्त किरीटिनम्।
en: O foremost of men, all the mountains, rivers, seas, with trees, herbs and plants were for crowned Arjuna.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: असुरा यातुधानाश्च गुह्यकाश्च परंतप॥ ते कर्ण समपद्यन्त ह्रष्टरूपाः समन्ततः।
en: O smiter of enemies, the Asuras, the Yatudhanas, the Guhyakas and ravens and other birds who roam the skies also favoured Arjuna.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: मुनयश्चारणाः सिद्धा वैनतेया वयांसि च॥ रत्नानि निधयः सर्वे वेदाश्चाख्यानपञ्चमाः। सोपवेदोपनिषदः सरहस्याः ससंग्रहाः॥ वासुकिश्चित्ररेग्नश्च तक्षको मणिकस्तथा। सर्पाश्चैव तथा सर्रे काद्रवेयाश्च सान्वयाः॥ विषवन्तो महाराज नागाश्चार्जुनतोऽभवन्। ऐरावताः सौरभेया वैशालेयाश्च भोगिनः॥ एतेऽभवन्नर्जुनतः क्षुद्रसर्माश्च कर्णतः।
en: All the valuable jewels, the four Vedas, the Mahabharata, the Upavedas, the Upanishads with all their mysterious contents, the Vasuki and Chitrasena, the Takshaka and Upatakshaka, the mountains and the and all the descendants of the Kadru and their children with all the poisonous great snakes and Nagas were on Arjuna's side. Airavata with his children, the descendants of Saurabhai and Vaikati and the Bhojins all favoured Arjuna the smaller snakes sided Karna.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: ईहामृगा व्यालमृगा माङ्गल्याश्च मृगद्विजाः॥ पार्थस्य विजये सर्व एवाभिसंसृताः। राजन्
en: The wolves and deer of the wild and other animals and birds of good omen all sided Partha.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: वसवो मरुतः साध्या रुद्रा विश्वेऽश्विनौ तथा॥ अग्निरिन्द्रश्च सोमश्च पवनोऽथ दिशो दश। धनंजयस्य ते पक्षे आदित्याः कर्णतोऽभवन्॥ विशः शूद्राश्च सूताश्च ये च संकर जायतः। सर्वशस्ते महाराज राधेयमभजस्तदा॥
en: The Vasus, the Maruts, the Siddhas, the Rudras, the Visvadevas, the Asvins, the Agni, the Soma Indra, the Pavana and the ten sides were in favor of Dhananjaya but the Aditya sided Karna. O monarch, the Vaisyas, the Sudras, the Sutas and other half caste people were in favour of Radha's son.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: देवास्तु पितृभिः सार्ध सगणा: सपदानुगाः। यमो वैश्रवणश्चैव वरुणश्च यतोऽर्जुनः॥ ब्रह्य क्षत्रं च यज्ञाश्च दक्षिणाश्चार्जुनं श्रिताः।
en: The Pitris and the heavenly bodies with all their followers and staff, Yama and Vaicravam and Varuna were for Arjuna. The Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, the gifts (Dakshinas), the sacred sacrifices were in favor of Arjuna.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: प्रेताश्चैव पिशाचाश्च क्रव्यादाश्च मृगाण्डजाः॥ राक्षसाः सह यादोभिः श्वसृगालाश्च कर्णतः।
en: The Pretas, the Pichaches, animals and birds of prey, the Rakshasas, the sea monsters, the dogs and jackals were on Karna's side.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: देवब्रह्मनृपर्षीणां गणाः पाण्डवतोऽभवन्॥ तुम्बुरुप्रमुखा राजन् गन्धर्वाश्च यतोऽर्जुनः। प्राधेया सहमौनेया गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः॥
en: The different sets of Rajarshis were for the son of Pandu. O monarch, all the Gandharvas with Tumburu as their head were in Arjuna's favor.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: ईमामृगाः पक्षिगणा द्विपाश्वरथपत्तिभिः। उह्यमानास्तथा मेधैर्वायुना चत मनीषिणः॥ दिद्दक्षवः समाजग्मुः कर्णार्जुनसमागमम्।
en: The different tribes of Gandharvas and Apsaras and the descendants of Pradha and Mauni and many sages riding on wolves, deers, elephants, horses and cars and others on foot or riding on the clouds and the wind came to see that combat between Karna and Arjuna.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: देवदानवगन्धर्वा नागयक्षाः पतत्रिणः॥ महर्षयो वेदविदः पितरश्च स्वधाभुजः। तपोविद्यास्तथौषध्यो नानारूपबलान्विताः॥ अन्तरिक्षे महाराज विनदन्तोऽवतस्थिरे।
en: O monarch, the Gods, Danavas Yakshas, Nagas, the birds, the learned Rishis well versed in the Vedas, the Pitris who live upon Swadha, the Sciences and asceticism and herbs of heavenly qualities all came and with great noise took their position in the sky.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मार्षिभिः सार्ध प्रजापतिभिरेव च॥ भवश्चैव स्थितो याने दिव्ये तं देशमागमत्।
en: Brahma together with Bhava (Mahadeva) with all the Bramharishis and Monsters of creation driving in excellent cars also came to that place.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: समेतौ तौ महात्मानौ दृष्ट्वा कर्णधनंजयौ॥ अर्जुनो जयतां कर्णमिति शक्रोऽब्रवीत्तदा।
en: As those two noble warriors engaged in fight Shakra (Indra) himself wished that Arjuna might conquer Karna.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: जयतामर्जुनं कर्ण इति सूर्योऽभ्यभाषत॥ हत्वार्जुनं मम सुतः कर्णो जयतु संयुगे। हत्वा कर्णं जयत्वद्य मम पुत्रो धनंजयः॥
en: Surya wished that Karna might conquer Arjuna. One said my son Karna will gain victory and the other said my son Arjuna will be victorious.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: इति सूर्यस्यत चैवासीद् विवादो वासवस्य च। पक्षसंस्थितयोस्तत्र तयोर्विबुधसिंहयोः। द्वैपक्ष्यमासीद् देवानामसुराणां च भारत॥
en: Thus they of lion like-prowess disputed for each other taking different sides. Seeing those two noble warriors face each other in fight the Asuras took one side and the gods the other.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: समेतौ तौ महात्मानौ दृष्ट्वा कणूदनंजयौ। अकम्पन्त त्रयौ लोकाः सहदेववर्षितारणाः॥
en: The gods, the Rishis and all the creations of the three worlds began to shake with fear sceing that fight.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: सर्वे देवगणाश्चैव सर्वभूतानि यानि च। यतः पार्थस्ततो देवा यतः कर्णस्ततोऽसुराः॥
en: All the Gods favoured Partha and the Asuras Karna and all the creations felt an interest either for the Pandava warrior or the Kuru warrior.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: रथयूथपयोः पक्षौ कुरुपाण्डववीरयोः। दृष्ट्वा प्रजापतिं देवाः स्वयम्भुवमचोदयन्॥
en: Seeing (Brahma) the master of creation who had no father (self born) all the Gods requested him to make the issue of that fight between those two foremost of men to be equal,

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: कोऽनयोर्विजयी देव कुरुपाण्डवयोधयोः। समोऽस्तु विजयो देव एतयोर्नरसिंहयो॥
en: The whole creation will be destroyed if Karna and Arjuna continued this fight O, self born one; only speak the word that these two will be equally successful.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: कर्णार्जुनविवादेन सर्वं संशयितं जगत्। स्वयम्भो ब्रूहि नस्तथ्यमेतयोर्विजयं प्रभो॥ स्वयम्भो ब्रूहि तद्वाक्यं समोऽस्तु विजयोऽनयोः।
en: O sovereign! The entire universe fell in the trap of illusion when Karna and Arjuna fought against cach other. O Svayambhu! Tell us facts regarding their victory. Speak in a manner so as their equal victory is indicated.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तदुपश्रुत्य मघवा प्रणिपत्य पितामहम्॥ व्यज्ञापयत देवेशमिदं मतिमतां वरः।
en: Hearing this Brahma and Ishana said to the king of the celestials the noble Vijaya (Arjuna) will surely gain victory.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: पूर्व भगवता प्रोक्तं कृष्णयोर्विजयो ध्रुवः॥ तत् तथास्तु नमस्तेऽस्तु प्रसीद भगवन् मम।
en: O sacred one, you have said before that the two Krishnas are sure to gain victory, he then pleased and let that be the case now.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: ब्रह्येशानावथो वाक्यमूचस्त्रिदशेश्वरम्॥ विजयो ध्रुवमेवास्य विजयस्य महात्मनः। खाण्डवे येन हुतभुकतोषितः सव्यसाचिना॥ स्वर्ग त समनुप्राप्यं साहाय्यं शक्र ते कृतम्।
en: Then Brahma and Mahadev told Indra-Arjuna will surely gain victory. O Shakra, Savyasachin has pleased the eater of sacrifices (Agni) in Khandava forest and also helped him when he came to Heaven.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: कर्णश्च दानवः पक्ष अतः कार्यः पराजयः॥ एवं कृते भवेत् कार्य देवानामेव निश्चितम्। आत्मकार्यं च सर्वेषां गरीयस्त्रिदशेश्वर॥
en: Karna takes part with the Danavas and he deserves to be defeated so the intentions of the gods will be fulfilled. One should always he careful about his business

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: महात्मा फाल्गुनश्चापि सत्यधर्मरतः सदा। विजयस्तस्य नयतं जायते नात्र संशयः॥
en: O king of Heaven, as the noble minded Phalgun is truthful and virtuous undoubtedly he must always be the conqueror.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तोषितो भगवान् येन महात्मा वृषभध्वजः। कथं वा तस्य न जयो जायते शतलोचन॥
en: O you with hundred eyes, why will not he be victorious, who both pleased the noble and sacred God who has the bull marked on his banner.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: यस्य चक्रे स्वयं विष्णुः सारथ्यं जगतः प्रभुः। मनस्वी बलवाञ्शूरः कृतास्त्रोऽथ तपोधनः॥
en: Partha has the master of the world Vishnu himself as his driver besides he is a hero, is very powerful and is virtuous at the same time.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: बिभर्ति च महातेजा धनुर्वेदमशेषतः। पार्थः सर्वगुणेपेतो देवकार्यमिदं यतः॥
en: He is of active body, master of the science of weapons and has all qualities, and he should conquer because the Gods wish it to be so.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: किश्यन्ते पाण्डवा नित्यं वनवासदिभिर्भृशम्। सम्पन्नस्तपसा चैव पर्याप्तः पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Arjuna is always religion abiding and truthful. He will therefore, acquire victory definitely. Nothing like doubt can be raised in it.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: अतिक्रमेच माहात्म्याद् दिष्टमप्यर्थपर्ययम्। अतिक्रान्ते च लोकानामभावो नियतं भवेत्॥
en: By his great prowess Partha can overrule destiny itself whether it be in his favour or not; when he means he can destroy all creatures.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: न विद्यते व्यवस्थानं क्रुद्धयोः कृष्णयोः कचित्। स्रष्टारौ जगतश्चैव सततं पुरुषर्षभौ॥
en: When those two Krishnas are roused, they care not for anything and those two foremost of men are creators of real and unreal matters.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: नरनारायणावतौ पुराणावृषित्तमौ। अनियम्यौ नियन्तारावेतौ तस्मात् परंतपौ।॥
en: They are the ancient and good Rishis Nara and Narayana; they have no fear and they are smiters of all enemies and cannot be ruled by any one; they rule over all.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: नैतयोस्तु समः कश्चिद् दिवि वा मानुषेषु वा। अनुगम्यास्त्रयो लोकाः सह देवर्षिचारणैः॥ सर्वदेवगणाश्चापि सर्वभूतानि यानि च। अनयोस्तु प्रभावेण वर्तते निखिलं जगत्॥
en: Either in Heaven or earth there is none to equal them; they are above all the Heavenly Rishis and Charanas of the three worlds, all the Gods and creatures come after them; they are properly speaking the main stay of the whole world.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: कर्णो लोकानयं मुख्यानाप्नोतु पुरुषर्षभः। कर्णो वैकर्तनः शूरौ विजयस्त्वस्तु कृष्णयोः॥ वसूनां समलोकत्वं मरुतां वा समाप्नुयात्। सहितो द्रोणभीष्माभ्यां नाकलोकमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: Let Karna, the son of Vikartan, who is foremost of men and who is a brave warrior, attain the best region and let him be like the Vasus or Maruts; let him be adored in heaven with Bhishma and Drona, but let the two Krishnas be victorious.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: इत्युक्तो देवदेवाभ्यां सहस्राक्षोऽब्रवीद् वचः। आमन्त्र्य सर्वभूतानि ब्रोशानानुशासनम्॥
en: When those two greatest of Gods (Brahma and Ishana) said so the God with thousand eyes respectfully bowed to their words and himself said to other creatures.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: श्रुतं भवद्भिर्यत् प्रोक्तं भगवद्भ्यां जगद्धितम्। तत्तथा नान्यथा तद्धि तिष्ठध्वं विगतज्वराः॥
en: You hear what the two Gods say for the good of the whole world and it must surely be so and no otherwise; so rest assured.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: इति श्रुत्वेन्द्रवचनं सर्वभूतानि मारिष। विस्मितान्यभवन् राजन् पूजायांचक्रिरे तदा॥ व्यसृजंश्च सुगन्धीनि पुष्पवर्षाणि हर्षिताः। नानारूपाणि विबुधा देवतूर्याण्यवादयन्॥
en: O my lord king, hearing Indra say these words all creatures admired and praised that deity. The inhabitants of heaven then sounded their horns and showered many sorts of sweet scented flowers.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: दिदक्षवश्चाप्रतिमं द्वैरथं नरसिंहयोः। देवदानवगन्धर्वाः सर्व एवावतस्थिरे॥
en: And actually all the Gods, Danavas and Gandharvas waited anxiously to see that unrivaled duel between those two men of leonine prowess.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: रथौ तयोः श्वेतहयौ दिव्यौ युक्तौ महात्मनोः। यौ तौ कर्णार्जुनौ राजन् प्रहृष्टावभ्यतिष्ठताम्॥
en: O monarch, both the cars, ridden by Karna and Arjuna, had gray steeds loudly as they careered with beautiful banners on their tops.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: समागता लोकवीराः शंखान् दध्मुः पृथक् पृथक्। वासुदेवार्जुनौ वीरौ कर्णशल्यौ च भारत॥
en: Many brave warriors came near Vasudeva and Arjuna and also near Shalya and Karna and sounded their conchs.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तद् भीरुसंत्रासकर युद्धं समभवत्तदा। अन्योन्यस्पर्धिनोरुग्रं शक्रशम्बरयोरिव॥
en: Then began that fight which struck terror into the hearts of cowards and like Sakra and Samvara the warriors rushed fiercely against each other.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तयोर्ध्वजौ वीतमलौ शुशुभाते रथे स्थितौ। राहुकेतू यथाऽऽकाशे उदितौ जगतः क्षये॥
en: Like the planets Rahu and Ketu appearing in the sky at the time of the destruction of the whole world the banners of those two heroes looked very brilliant and beautiful.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: कर्णस्याशीविषनिभा रत्नसारमयी दृढा। पुरन्दरधनुःप्रख्या हस्तिकक्ष्या व्यराजत॥
en: The elephant's rope of Karna's standard which was very strong and decked with jewels and precious stones resembled a poisonous snake and the bow of Indra in beauty (as it fluttered).

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: कपिश्रेष्ठस्तु पार्थस्य व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः। दंष्ट्राभिर्भीषयन् भाभिर्दुर्निरीक्ष्यो रविर्यथा॥
en: The great ape of Partha, opening its fearful and broad jaws, struck terror in to the hearts of all and became difficult to look at like the son.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: युद्धाभिलाषुको भूत्वा ध्वजो गाण्डीवधन्वनः। कर्णध्वजमुपातिष्ठत् स्वस्थानाद् वेगवान् कपिः॥ उत्पपात महावेगः कक्ष्यामध्याहनत्तदा। नखैश्च दशनैश्चैव गरुडः पन्नगं यथा॥
en: The ape, on the banner of Gandiva, being willing to fight all on sudden, left his place, lept upon Karna's banner, like Gadura swooping down upon a snake and began to tear the elephant rope standard fiercely with its nails and teeth.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: सा किङ्किणीकाभरणा कालपाशोपमाऽऽयसा। अभ्यद्रवत सुसंरब्धा हस्तिकक्ष्याथ तं कपिम्॥
en: The elephant's rope, which was strong as iron and adorned with strings of small bells, which resembled the fatal noose (of Yama), becoming wrathful pressed against the ape.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: तयो?रतरे युद्धे द्वैरथे द्यूत आहिते। प्रकुर्वाते ध्वजौ युद्धं पूर्वं पूर्वतरं तदा॥ हया हयानभ्यहेषन् स्पर्धमानाः परस्परम्। अविध्यत् पुण्डरीकाक्षः शल्यं नयनसायकैः॥
en: Thus in that terrible duel between those two great warriors and which was the result of their match game in dice, their banners first fought with each other and the horses of the one neighed at the horses of the other, Keshava, whose eyes were like lotuses, looked towards Shalya with piercing glances who returned them in the like manner.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: शल्यश्च पुण्डीरकाक्षं तथैवाभिसमैक्षतः। तत्राजयद् वासुदेवः शल्यं नयनसायकैः॥
en: Similarly, Shalya look at Sri Krishna lotus eyed but victory, there was acquired by Sri Krishna. He defeated Shalya by a shot of eye as acute as arrow.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: कर्णं चाप्यजयद् दृष्टया कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः। अथाब्रवीत्.सूतपुत्रः शल्यमाभाष्य स स्तिमतम्॥१०१ यदि पार्थो रणे हन्यादद्य मामिह कर्हिचित्। किं करिष्यसि संग्रामे शल्य सत्यमथोच्यताम्॥
en: Dhananjaya the son of Kunti conquered Karna. Then Suta's son with a smile asked Shalya-"O friend, tell me the truth what would you do if I am killed today by Partha".

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: शल्य उवाच यदि कर्ण रणे हन्यादद्य त्वां श्वेतवाहनः। उभावेकरथेनाहं हन्यां माधवपाण्डवौ॥
en: Shalya said The king of Madras said-"O Karna, if you are today killed by this grey-horsed Arjuna I alone on a single car will put both Madhava and Phalguna to death."

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: संजय उवाच एवमेव तु गोििन्दमर्जुन: प्रत्यभाषत। तं प्रहस्याब्रवीत् कृष्णः सत्यं पार्थमिदं वचः॥
en: Sanjaya said Arjuna also asked Govinda the same question and Krishna spoke to Partha these words having deep meaning.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: पतेद् दिवाकरः स्थानाच्छुष्येदपि महोदधिः। शैत्यमग्निरियान त्वां हन्यात् कर्णो धनंजय॥
en: O Dhananjaya, the sun may come down and be displaced, the earth itself may be crushed with a thousand pieces, the fire may become cold but Karna will never kill you.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: यदि चैतत् कथञ्जित् स्यालोकपर्यासनं भवेत्। हन्यां कर्णं तथा शल्यं बाहुभ्यामेव संयुगे॥
en: But if it so happens you must know that revolution of the word is near and as for myself I will send both Shalya and Kama to the Pluto's den with my army:

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: इति कृष्णवचः श्रुत्वा प्रहसन् कपिकेतनः। अर्जुनः प्रत्युवाचेदं कृष्णमक्लिष्टकारिणम्॥
en: Arjuna, who was ape-bannered, hearing these words smiled and told Krishna whose prowess was inexhaustible.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: मम तावदपर्याप्तौ कर्णशल्यौ जनार्दन। सपताकध्वजं कर्णं सशल्यस्थावाजिनम्॥ सच्छत्रकवचं चैव सशक्तिसवकार्मुकम्। द्रष्टास्यद्य रणे कृष्ण शरैश्छिन्नमनेकधा॥
en: O Janardana, Shalya and Karna both together is no match to me and today O Krishna, you will see how I destroy Karna with Shalya, his banners, car, horses, his umbrella, his armour, his bows and arrows all together with my shafts in the battle.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: अद्यैव सरथं सावं सशक्तिकवचायुधम्। संचूणितमिवारण्ये पादपं दन्तिता यथा॥
en: As the elephant, with his tusks, rends into pieces a tree in a forest so I will this day crush him with armour, his car, horses, arrows and other weapons into atoms.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: अद्य राधेयभार्याणां वैधव्यं समुपस्थितम्। ध्रुवं स्वप्नेष्वनिष्टानि ताभिर्दृष्टानि माधव॥
en: O Madhava, the day of widowhood for the wives of Radha's son is very near and surely they must have dreamt of the coming evil last night.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: द्रष्टासि ध्रुवमद्यैव विधवाः कर्णयोषितः। न हि मे शाम्यते मन्युर्यदनेन पुरा कृतम्॥ कृष्णां सभागता दृष्टरा मूढेनादीर्धदर्शिना। अस्मांस्तथावहसता क्षिपता च पुनः पुनः॥
en: Surely you will today see Karna's wives will become widows. I cannot check my rage when I think of evils done to us by this (thoughtless) fool when Krishna was taken forcibly before the assembly and he used abusive language to us and laughed.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: अद्य द्रष्टासि गोविन्द कर्णमुन्मथितं मया। वारणेनेव मत्तेन पुष्पितं जगतीरुहम्॥
en: As the furious elephant destroys a tree with all its blossoms and flowers in anger so O Govinda, I will knock him down today.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: अद्य ता मधुरा वाचः श्रोतासि मधुसूदन। दिष्ट्या जयसि वार्ष्णेय इति कर्णे निपातिते॥
en: Today after Karna is no more, O Slayer of Madhu, you will hear those pleasant words, i.e. by good fortune, O you of Vrishni's race, you have conquered.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: अद्याभिमन्युजननीं प्रहृष्टः सान्त्वयिष्यसि। कुन्ती पितृष्वसारं च प्रहृष्टः सञ्जानार्दन॥
en: Today you shall be able to console the mother of Abhimanyu with a free conscience by pay back the debt of the enemies in their own coin and also joyfully soothe your maternal aunt Kunti.

description: Krishana and Arjuna meeting in dual battle
sn: अद्य बाष्पमुखी कृष्णां सान्त्वयिष्यसि माधव। बाग्भिश्चामृतकल्पाभिर्धर्मराजं च पाण्डवम्॥
en: O Madhava, today you shall be able to comfort Krishna, on whose faced drops to tears and always trickling down and to speak pleasant sweet words to King Yudhishthira the just.

sn: संजय उवाच र्गन्धर्वरक्षाऽप्सरसां च सर्वः। ब्रह्मर्षिराजर्षिसुपर्णजुष्टं बभौ वियद् विस्मयनीयरूपम्॥
en: Sanjaya said It was really a wonderful sight to see the skies covered with Gods, Nagas, Asuras, Yakshas and numbers of Gandharvas, Rakshashas, Apsaras, Royal and regenerate Rishis and birds of most beautiful plumage.

sn: दिवदगीतस्तुनृत्यहासैः। सर्वेऽन्तरिक्षं ददृशुर्मनुष्याः स्वस्थाश्च तद् विस्मयनीयरूपम्॥
en: All the human beings looked and admired the scene in the sky which was filled with the echoes of sons, music, laughter, sacred hymns, dance and many other sorts of beautiful sounds.

sn: ततः प्रहृष्टाः कुरुपाण्डुयोधा वादित्रशङ्खस्वनसिंहनादैः। विनादयन्तो वसुधां दिशश्च स्वनेन सर्वान द्विषतौ निजघ्नुः॥
en: Then the warriors on both the Kaurava and Pandava sides went on slaying each other's enemies making the world and the ten sides ring with martial music, notes of their conchs, loud houts and noise of their warfare.

sn: नराश्वमातङ्गरथैः समाकुलं शरासिशक्तृष्टिनिपातदुःसहम्। अभीरुजुष्टं हतदेहसंकुलं रणाजिरं लोहितमाबभौ तदा॥
en: The field of battle became brilliantly red with blood and adorned with men, horses, elephants, cars and weapons and became difficult for the throwing of swords, maces, darts and other weapons and was filled with dead bodies.

sn: बभूव युद्धं कुरूपाण्डवानां यथा सुराणामसुरैः सहाभवत्। तथा प्रवृत्ते तुमुले सुदारुणे धनंजयस्याधिरथेश्च सायकैः॥ दिशश्च सैन्यं च शितैरजिह्मगैः परस्परं प्रावृणुतां सुदंशितौ।
en: Looked like the fight that in the old days took place between the Gods and the Asuras. When Dhananjaya and Adhiratha's son had begun to defeat the warriors with their arrows, they, with keen shafts, almost covered all the sides.

sn: ततस्त्वदीयाश्च परे च सायकैः कृतेऽन्धकारे ददृशुर्न किंचन॥ स्ततोऽभवत् त्वद्भुतमेव सर्वतः।
en: Darkness fell over the atmosphere, with the shafts shot at in that battle and the warriors on either side could not see anything. And being afraid they took shelter of either of the carwarriors (Karna or Arjuna) like streaks of light going towards the sun or the moon.

sn: ततोऽस्त्रमस्त्रेण परस्परं तौ विधूय वाताविव पूर्वपश्चिमौ॥ घनान्धकारे वितते तमोनुदौ यथोदितौ तद्वदतीव रेजतुः।
en: The two brave warriors thwarted one another's weapons, like the East and West winds struggling with each other and looked brilliant like the sun or the moon after dispelling darkness.

sn: न चाभिसर्तव्यमिति प्रचोदिताः परे त्वदीयाश्च तथावतस्थिरे॥ महारथौ तौ परिवार्य सर्वतः सुरासुराः शम्बरवासवाविव।
en: They assuring their troops with the words "don't give way” were surrounded by their troops and their inimical forces like Vasava and Shambara by the Gods and the Asuras.

sn: मृदङ्गभेरीपणवानकस्वनैः ससिंहनादैर्नदतुर्नरोत्तमौ॥ विरेजतुस्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ तदा।
en: O Bharata, those two foremost of men were welcomed by the beating of drums and other instruments and uttered loud shouts and looked resplendent as the sun and the moon when surrounded by deep roaring clouds.

sn: महाधनुर्मण्डलमध्यगावुभौ सुवर्चसौ बाणसहस्रदीधिती॥ युगान्तसूर्याविव दुःसहौ रणे।
en: Both of them were armed with fearful bows drawn to the fullest extent like circles which looked like coronas, shot thousands of shafts which were like rays. In war they could not be borne and looked like two powerful suns risen for destroying the universe at the end of Yuga.

sn: बुभौ जिघांसु कृतिनौ परस्परम्॥ महेन्द्रजम्भाविव कर्णपाण्डवौ।
en: Both unconquerable, both destroyers of enemies and they were bent upon killing one another and showing great skill in war. Those two fighters namely Karna and the son of Pandu bravely assailed each other in that awful fight like Indra and Asura Jamba;

sn: ततो महास्त्राणि महाधनुर्धरौ विमुञ्चमानाविषुभिर्भयानकैः॥ नराश्वनागानमितान् निजघ्नतुः परस्परं चापि महारथी नृप।
en: O monarch, invoking the help of most powerful weapons those two redoubtable bowmen shot fearful arrows against each other. The foremost of men however shot hosts of elephants, horses and men and also struck one another.

sn: ततो विसस्त्रः पुनपर्दिता नरा नरोत्तमाभ्यां कुरुपाण्डवाश्रयः॥ सनागपत्तयश्वरथा दिशो दश तथा यथा सिंहहता वनौकसः।
en: And like the smaller animals when attacked by a lion the Kurus and Pandus together with their horses, elephants and car warriors fled on all directions being assailed by those two best of men.

sn: ततस्तु दुर्योधनभोजसौबलाः कृपेण शारद्वतसूनुना सह॥ महारथाः पञ्च धनंजयाच्युतौ शरैः शरीरार्तिकरैरताडयन्।
en: Then the five great car warriors viz. Duryodhana, the king of Bhojas, Subala's son Kripa and the son of Sharadvata attacked Dhananjaya and Keshava with deadly arrows.

sn: धनूषि तेषामिषुधीनध्वजान् हयान् रथांश्च सूतांश्च धनंजयः शरै॥ समं प्रमथ्याशु परान् समन्ततः शरोत्तमैदशभिश्च सूतजम्। अथाभ्यधावंस्त्वरिताः शतं रथाः शतं गजाश्चर्जुनमाततायिनः॥ शकास्तुषारा यवनाश्च सादिनः सहैष काम्बोजवरैर्जिघांसवः। वरायुधान् पाणिगतैः शरैः सह क्षुरैर्यकृन्तत् प्रपतन् शिरांसि च॥ हयांश्च नागांश्च रतांश्च युध्यतो धनंजयः शत्रुगणान् क्षितौ क्षिणोत्।
en: Dhananjaya with arrows cut-off at once elephants, horses, the bows and quivers, the cars with their drivers of those fighters and struck every one of them with good arrows and Suta's son with twelve shafts. Then one hundred chariots, one hundred elephants and Shaka, Tushara and Yavana cavalry together with some best of Kamboja warriors precipitated themselves upon Arjuna in order to slay him but he (Arjuna) very soon not only cut-off with razor-headed shafts all those weapons of his enemies but also their heads, their elephants, cars and horses. Dhananjaya locked down his enemies in battle.

sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षे सुरतूर्यनिःस्वनाः ससाधुवादा हृषितैः समीरिताः॥ निपेतुरप्युमपुष्पवृष्टयः सुगन्धिगन्धाः पवनेरिताः शुभाः।
en: Then the good Gods sounded their heavenly drums in praise of Arjuna. Then heaps of sweet scented flowers fell upon Arjuna.

sn: तदद्भुतं देवमनुष्यसाक्षिकं समीक्ष्य भूतानि विसिस्मियुस्तदा॥ तवात्मजः सूतसुतश्च न व्यथां न विस्मयं जग्मतुरे कनिश्चयौ।
en: O monarch, the Gods, men and all the creatures were struck with wonder at seeing this. Only your son and Suta's son, who were sorry in their minds, felt neither any joy nor admired the deed.

sn: अथाब्ररीद् द्रोणसुतस्तवात्मजं करं करेण प्रतिपीडय सान्त्वयन्॥ रलं विरोधेन धिगस्तु विग्रहम्। हतो गुरुर्ब्रह्यसमो महास्त्रवित् तथैव भीष्मप्रमुखा महारथाः॥
en: Then Drona's son taking Duryodhana by the hands entreatingly said to him O Duryodhana, be pacified; you need not prolong this quarrel; make peace with Pandavas; war is detestable. The preceptor (Drona) who was like Brahma and was master of most powerful weapons he and other foremost of men with Bhishma have been killed in this war.

sn: अहं त्ववध्यो म चापि मातुलः प्रशाधि राज्यं सह पाण्डवैश्चिरम्। धनंजयः शाम्यति वारितो मया जनार्दनो नैव विरोधमिच्छति॥
en: I and my maternal uncle cannot be killed; and if I request Dhananjaya he is averse to this quarrel. Reign as a joint monarch with the sons of Pandu over this kingdom far long.

sn: युधिष्ठरो भूतहिते रतः सदा वृकोदरपस्तद्वशगस्तथा यमौ। त्वया तु पाथैश्च कृते च संविदे प्रजाः शिवं प्राप्नुयुरिच्छया तव॥ व्रजन्तु शेषाः स्वपुराणि बान्धवा निवृत्तयुद्धाश्च भवन्तु सैनिकाः। न चेद् वचः श्रोष्यसि मे नराधिप ध्रुवं प्रतप्तासि हतोऽरिभियुधि॥
en: Yudhishthira always seeks the welfare of all creatures. Vrikodara and the twins (Nakul and Sahadeva) are always under Yudhishthira's order; and if you make peace it would appear that you make it only for the welfare of all parties. All the kings then will return to their respective homes and the troops will no longer fight with each other; if you do not hear my advice you will have to repent hereafter when you will be crushed by your enemies.

sn: इदं च दृष्टं जगता सहं त्वया कृतं यदेकेन किरीटमालिना। यथा न कुर्याद् बलभिन्न चान्तको न चापि धाता भगवान् न यक्षराट्॥
en: It will be hard for the slayer of Bala (Indra) or Yama or Prachetas or the famous king of Yakshas to perform the heroic feats that have been done by crown-headed Arjuna single handed. You yourself and the whole world have seen that.

sn: अतोऽपि भूयान् स्वगुणैर्धनंजयो न चातिवर्तिष्यति मे वचोऽखिलम्। तवानुयात्रां च सदा करिष्यति प्रसीद राजेन्द्र शमं त्वमाप्नुहि॥
en: Dhananjaya is possessed of immense qualities and will never disobey my words. He will be your ally i.e. respect you. O monarch, for the good of the world, be pacified.

sn: ममापि मानः परमः सदा त्वयि ब्रवीम्यतस्त्वां परमाच सौह्रदात्। निवारयिष्यामि च कर्णमप्यहं यदा भवान् सप्रणयो भविष्यति॥
en: I am your sincere friend and you always respect me and it is for that reason that I am speaking these words to you; and if you make up your mind for peace, I shall dissuade Karna.

sn: स्तथैव साम्ना च धनेन चार्दितम्। प्रतापतश्चोपनतं चतुर्विधं तदस्ति सर्वं तव पाण्डवेषु॥
en: The sages have said there are four kinds of friends, namely, those who are born friends, those that are made friends by good behaviour, those that are made so by wealth and those that are made friends by power and you have all these advantages and connections with the Pandavas.

sn: नसर्गतस्ते तव वीर बान्धवाः पुनश्च साम्ना समवाप्नुहि प्रभो। तवयि प्रसन्ने यदि मित्रतां गते हितं कृतं स्याज्जगतस्त्वयातुलम्॥
en: O you most powerful, the Pandavas are your friends by nature and make them your permanent friends by making peace. O king of kings, you both agree and make peace.

sn: स एवमुक्तः सुहृदा वचो हितं विचिन्त्य निःश्वस्य च दुमनाब्रवीत। न्ममापि विज्ञापयतो वचः शृणु॥
en: Duryodhana thought for a while when those words were spoken to him by his friends and with sorrowful heart heaving a deep sigh, said-"O friend, you have said your say, now hear what I have got to speak to that.

sn: निहत्य दुःशासनमुक्तवान् वचः प्रसह्य शार्दूलवदेष दुर्मतिः। वृकोदरस्तद्धृदये मम स्थितं न तत् परोक्षं भवतः कुतः शमः॥
en: The declaration made by this wicked Bhimasena just after he killed Duhshasana in tome like lion roar, is not concealed by you. It is still inflicting pain to my heart. Tell then, how an alliance can be made in such circumstance.

sn: न चापि कर्ण प्रसहेद् रणेऽर्जुनो महागिरि मेरुमिवोगमारुतः। न चाश्वसिष्यन्ति पृथात्मजा मयि प्रसह्य वैरं बहुशो विचिन्त्य॥
en: As the mighty of the storm is checked by the mountain of Meru so Arjuna won't be able to cope with Karna in battle and the sons of Partha cannot possibly have any confidence in me for the many acts of willful enmity I have done to them.

sn: दुपारमेत्यर्हसि वक्तुमच्युता स्तमेष कर्णः प्रसभं हनिष्यति॥
en: O you glorious man, O preceptor's son, it is not meet for you to dissuade Karna from fighting, for Phalguna is greatly tired today and Karna will kill him in no time.

sn: तमेवमुक्तवाप्यनुनीय चासकृत् तवात्मजः स्वाननुशास्ति सैनिकान्। विनिघ्नदाभिद्रवताहितान् मम स बाण हस्ताः किमु जोषमासत॥
en: Saying these words humbly again and again to Drona's son, your son commanded his army, saying-"Armed with shafts proceed against the enemies and kill them; why are you standing inactive?"

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: संजय उवाच तौ शङ्खभेरीनिनदे समृद्धे समीयतुः श्वेतहतौ नराग्रयौ। वैकर्तनः सूतपुत्रोऽर्जुनश्च दुर्मत्रिते तव पुत्रस्य राजन्॥
en: Sanjaya said When the blare of conchs and sound of bugles became very high in the battle-field, those two, Suta's son Vaikartana and Arjuna mounted on white horses, closed each other, O king, on account of the vile policy of your son.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: यथा गजौ हैमवतौ प्रभिन्नौ प्रवृद्धदन्ताविव वासितार्थे। तथा समाजग्मतुरुग्रवी? दनंजयश्चाधिरथिश्च वीरौ॥
en: Those two dreadful heroes Dhananjaya and Adhiratha's son encountered each other like two Himalayan elephants with full-grown tusks, madly fighting for a she-elephant.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: बलाहकेनेव महाबलाहको यद्दच्छया वा गिरिणा यथा गिरिः। तथा धनुातलनेमिनिस्वनैः समीयतुस्ताविषुवर्षवर्षिणौ॥
en: Those two warriors, with bows twanging loudly and sending forth hosts of shafts and the palms of their hands also producing great sounds when shooting them and their carwheels making rattling, encountered each other like the collision of two heavy masses of clouds or two mountains.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: प्रवृद्धश्रृङ्गमवीरुदेषधी प्रवृद्धनानाविधनिर्झरौकसौ। यथाचलौ वा चलितौ महाबलौ तथा महास्त्रैरितरेतरं हतः॥
en: Those two great warriors fell upon and struck one one another with many powerful weapons resembling two mountains of towering height having many trees, herbs and creepers upon them and inhabited by various animals, rushing against each other.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: स संनिपातस्तु तयोर्महानभूत् सुरेशवैरोचनयोर्यथा पुरा। शरैर्विनुन्नाङ्गनियन्तृवाहयोः सुदुःसहोऽन्यैः कटुशोणिततोदकः॥
en: The fight between those two great warriors became so terrible that it resembled the war between the king of heaven and the son of Virvahana in the days of old, it was impossible for other persons to bear up in such a fight and a river of blood flowed there, ghastly to look at; the limbs of both the warriors were badly cut in many places as also their drivers and horses.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: प्रभूतपद्मोत्पलमत्स्यतच्छपौ महाह्रदौ पक्षिगणैरिवावृतौ। सुसंनिकृष्टवनिलोद्धतौ यथा तथा रथौ तौ ध्वजिनौ समीयतुः॥
en: Those two cars, fitted with broad banners, when nearing each other, looked like two large lakes full of fishes and tortoises and many kinds of lotuses floating on it waters which was gently moved by the wind and resounding with the sweet voices of diverse kinds of birds.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: बुभौ महेन्द्रप्रतिमौ महारथौ। महेन्द्र वृत्राविव सम्प्रजघ्नतुः॥
en: Both of them, mighty as the God Indra, assailed one another with weapons powerful as Indra's thunder and fought also like Indra himself and (Asura) Vritra.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: सनागपत्यश्वरथे उभे बले विचित्रवर्माभरणाम्बरायुधे। चकम्पतुस्मयनीयरूपे वियद्गताश्चार्जुनकर्णसंयगु॥
en: Both are armies abounding in cars, horses, elephants, foot adorned with fine mail, vestments and weapons as also those that were in the skies (the gods) were all struck with terror in seeing that extraordinary fight between Karna and Arjuna.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: भुजाः सवस्त्रगुलयः समुच्छ्रिताः ससिंहनादैह्रतैर्दिद्दक्षुभिः। यदर्जुनो मत्त इव द्विपो द्विपं समभ्ययादाधिरथिं जिघांसया॥
en: When Arjuna precipitated himself upon the son of Adhiratha like one furious elephant rushing against another with the intention of killing him, others out of excitement and joy uttered lion-like roars and raised their cloths shaking them fingers.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: उदक्रोशन् सोमकास्तत्र पार्थ पुरःसराश्चर्जुन भिन्धि कर्णम्। छिन्धस्य मूर्धानमलं चिरेण श्रद्धां च राज्याद् धृतराष्ट्रसूनोः॥
en: The Somakas called loudly to Partha, “Go haste and slay Karna and by that put an end to the hope of Dhritarashtra's son for empire."

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: तथास्माकं बहवस्तत्र योधाः कर्ण तथा याहि याहीत्यवोचन। जार्जुनं कर्ण शरैः सुतीक्ष्णैः पुनर्वनं यान्तु चिराय पार्थाः॥
en: In the same way many of our warriors went to Karna and said "Kill Arjuna with your sharp arrows and let the sons of Pritha go again to the wilderness for good."

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ततः कर्णः प्रथमं तत्र पार्थ महेषुभिर्दशभिः प्रत्यविध्यत्। तं चार्जुनः प्रत्यविद्धयच्छिताग्रैः कक्षान्तरै दशभिः सम्प्रहस्य॥
en: Then Karna struck Arjuna with the powerful arrows and Arjuna also shot sharp arrows with great force against Karna's chest in return.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: स्ततक्षतुः सूतपुत्रोऽर्जुनश्च। परस्परं तौ बिभिदुर्विमर्दे सुभीममभ्यापततुश्च हृष्टौ॥
en: Thinking to take advantage of each other's weak points with buoyant spirits they repeatedly attacked each other with great fierceness and hacked and wounded one another with may good winged arrows, in that terrible fight.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ततोऽर्जुनः प्रासृजदुग्रधन्वा भुजाबुभौ गाण्डिवं चानुमृज्य। नाराजनालीकवराहकर्णान् क्षुरांस्तथा साञ्जलिकार्धचन्द्रान्॥
en: The fierce warrior Arjuna then rubbed his bow-string with his arm and sent hosts of cloth yard shafts and arrows called Nalikas i.e. shafts headed with boar's ears and razors and Angalikas i.e. half moon-shaped arrows.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ते सर्वतः समकीर्यन्त राजन् पार्थेषवः कर्णरथं विशन्तः। अवाङ्मुखा पक्षिगणा दिनान्ते विशन्ति केतार्थमिवाशु वृक्षम्॥
en: As at night-fall the birds for the purpose of resting during the night enter a tree, so O monarch, Partha's arrows after entering Karna's car with bent heads spread on all sides.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: यानर्जुनः सभृकुटीकटाक्षं कर्णाय राजन्नसृजन्जितारिः। तान् सायकैर्यसते सूतपुत्रः क्षिप्तान् क्षिप्तान् पाण्डवस्याशु संघान्॥
en: But O King, all those arrows and the successive ones, shot by Arjuna, that contracted brow, were all destroyed by Karna by his own shafts.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ततोऽस्त्रमाग्नेयममित्र साधनं मुमोच कर्णाय महेन्द्रसूनुः। भूम्यन्तरिक्षे च दिशोऽर्कमार्ग प्रावृत्य देहोऽस्य बभूव दीप्तः॥
en: The son of Indra (Arjuna) then sent against Karna such a brilliant and fiery weapon that it lighted up the whole world. The skies, the ten sides and also his own body and covered the very course of the sun with its brilliancy and was capable of killing all enemies.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: योधाश्च सर्वे ज्वलिताम्बरा भृशं प्रदुद्रुवुस्तत्र विदग्धवस्त्राः शब्दश्च घोरोऽतिबभूव तत्र यथा वने वेणुवनस्य दह्यतः॥
en: The dresses of warriors caught fire and they fled making great noise like that which is heard when a bamboo forest catches fire.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: तद् वीक्ष्य कर्णो ज्वलनास्त्रमुद्यतं स वारुणं तत्प्रशमार्थमाहवे। समुत्सृजन् सूतसुतः प्रतापवान् स तेन वह्निं शमयाम्बभूव॥
en: The Suta's son, the brave Karna, seeing now that fiery weapon was burning everything, shot the Varuna weapon and extinguished the fire.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: बलाहकौघश्च दिशस्तरस्वी चकार सर्वास्तिमिरेण संवृताः। ततो धरित्रीधरतुल्यरोधसः समन्ततो वै परिवार्य वारिणा॥
en: Huge masses of clouds instantly covered the sides with darkness; they resembled big mountains and poured heavy showers upon the earth.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: तैश्चातिवेगात् स तथाविधोऽपि नीतः शमं वाहिरतिप्रचण्डः। बलाहकैरेव दिगन्तराणि व्याप्तानि सर्वाणि यथा नभश्च॥
en: The earth and the skies were covered by the clouds and that awful conflagration was ! extinguished in no time.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: तथा च सर्वास्तिमिरेण वै दिशो मेधैर्वृता न प्रदृश्येत किंचित्। अथापोवाह्याभ्रसंघान समस्तान् वायव्यास्त्रेणापततः स कर्णात्॥ ततोऽप्यस्त्रं दयितं देवराज्ञाः प्रादुश्चक्रे वज्रमतिप्रभावम्। गाण्डीवं ज्यां विशिखांश्चानुमन्त्र्य धनंजयः शत्रुभिरप्रधृष्यः॥
en: All the sides being covered by those clouds became very dark and nothing could be seen, but Arjuna with the vary weapons dispersed those clouds. Then the invisible Dhananjaya, inspiring the Gandiva, its string and the shafts with mantras, invoked a favourite weapon of the king of Heaven and powerful like his thunder.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ततः क्षुरप्राञ्जलिकार्धचन्द्रा नालीकनाराचवराहकर्णाः। गाण्डीवः प्रादुरासन् सुतीक्ष्णाः सहस्रशो वज्रसमानवेगाः॥
en: Then many sharp arrows namely the Anjalikas, i.e. razor-headed shafts and crescent like and Nalikas and cloth-yard arrows and those adorned with the boar's ears all very powerful and sharp, came out in numbers from the Gandiva with force.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ते कर्णमासाद्य महाप्रभावाः सुतेजना गापत्राः सुवेगाः। गात्रेषु सर्वेषु हयेषु चापि शरासने युगचक्रे ध्वजे च॥ स्ता_त्रसका भूमिमिवोरगास्ते। शराचिताङ्गो रुधिरागात्रः कर्णस्तदा रोषविवृत्तनेत्रः॥
en: Those powerful and sharp arrows, adorned with feathers like vulture quickly piercing the body, car, horses, earth and wheels of Karna, entered into the earth even as the snakes enter when afraid of Garuda; and thus being struck on all sides and bathed in blood Karna in anger rolled his eyes.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: दृढज्यमानाभ्य समुद्रघोषं प्रादुश्चक्ते भार्गवास्त्रं महात्मा। श्छित्त्वा कर्णः पाण्डवस्येषुसंघान्॥ तस्यास्त्रमस्त्रेण निहत्य सोऽथ जघान संख्ये रथनागपत्तीन्। अमृष्यमाणश्च महेन्द्रकर्मा महारणे भार्गवास्त्रप्रतापात्॥
en: Then bending the strong stringed bow, the twang of which resembled the deep roar of the sea, he invoked the Bhargava weapon and cutoff all the shots coming out of the mouth of the Indra weapon (shot by Arjuna). He thus cut-off the weapons of his enemy, many of the cars, elephants and foot soldiers of the Pandava army by virtue of the Bhargava weapon, himself not being able to bear the prowess of Arjuna in that battle.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: पञ्चालानां प्रवरांश्चापि योधान् क्रोधाविष्टः सूतपुत्रस्तरस्वी। बाणैर्विर्याधाहवे सुप्रमुक्तैः शिलाशितै रुकमपुङ्खैः प्रसह्य॥
en: That best of men, Suta's son of great energy, smiling at the two Krishnas, struck the chief men among the Panchalas with aimed arrows.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: तत्पञ्चाला: सोमकाश्चापि राजन् कर्णेनाजौ पीडयामानाः शरौघैः। क्रोधाविष्टा विव्यधुस्तं समन्तात् तीक्ष्णैर्बाणैः सूतपुत्रं समेताः॥
en: O monarch, the Panchalas and the Somakas being thus attacked by Karna, fired up with anger and conjointly began to strike Suta's son with arrows from all sides.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: तान् सूतपुत्रो निजधान बाणैः पञ्चालानां रथनागाश्वसंघान्। पर्दयद् बाणगणैः प्रसह्य विद्ध्वा हर्षात् सङ्गरे सूतपुत्रः॥
en: Then Suta's son cut-off with his own arrows the shots of the Panchalas and distressed the cars, elephants and horses of the Panchalas.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ते भिन्नदेहा व्यसरो निपेतुः कर्णेषुभिर्भूमितले स्वनन्तः। क्रुद्धेन सिंहेन यथेभयूथा महावने भीमबलेन तद्वत्॥
en: Like powerful elephants when killed by a mighty and angry lion, they fell down dead on the earth with loud noise being struck by those shafts of Karna.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: पञ्चालानां प्रवरान् संनिहत्य प्रसह्य योधानखिलानदीनः। ततः स राजन् विरराज कर्णो यथाम्बरे भास्कर उग्ररश्मिः॥
en: Having thus slain the choicest warriors of the Panchalas, those strong and brave and proud warriors, Karna, O King, when shooting his shafts resembled a mass of clouds when pouring down showers.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: कर्णस्य मत्वा तु जयं त्वदीयाः परां मुदं सिंहनादांश्च चक्रुः। सर्वे ह्यमन्यन्त भृशाहतौ च कर्णेन कृष्णाविति कौरवेन्द्र॥
en: Then, O Head of the Kuru race, your warriors, thinking that Karna had gained the day and brought the two Krishnas under subjection, began to clap and gave vent to lionlike roars.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: तत् तादृशं प्रेक्ष्य महारथस्य कर्णस्य वीर्यं च परैरसह्यम। दृष्ट्वा च कर्णेन धनंजयस्य तथाऽऽजिमध्ये निहतं तदस्त्रम्॥ ततस्त्वमर्षी क्रोधसंदीप्तनेत्रो वातात्मजः पाणिना पाणिमाछेत्। ममर्षितो निःश्वसज्जातमन्युः॥
en: They saw the power of the great hero Karna, overpower the enemies and his weapon to baffle all those of Dhananjaya in that fight. The son of Wind God, the wrathful Bhimasena, with eyes kindling with rage, pressed his own hands and drawing heavy breaths and greatly excited addressed Arjuna, of never-failing aim.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: कथं न पापोऽयमपेतधर्मः सूतात्मजः समरेऽद्य प्रसह्य। पञ्चालानां योधमुख्याननेकान् निजनिवांस्तव जिष्णो समक्षम्॥
en: How is it that this most irreligious scoundrel could slay so many good Panchala warriors before your very face.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: पूर्व देवैरजितं कालकेयैः साक्षात् स्थाणोर्बाहुसंस्पर्शमेत्य। नथेषुभिर्दशभिः प्रागविद्धयत्॥
en: The very gods and Kalakeyas were not able to vanquish you before this; why, you fought with Sthanu himself hand to hand. O diademadorned Arjuna, how is it that Suta's son has been able to pierce your with ten long arrows that are used by car warriors.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: नाश्चर्यमेतत् प्रतिभाति मेऽद्या कृष्णापरिक्लेशमनुस्मर त्वं यथाब्रवीत षण्ढतिलान् स्म वाचः॥ रूक्षाः सुतीक्ष्णाश्च हि पापबुद्धिः सूतात्मजोऽयं गतभूर्दुरात्मा। संस्यमृत्य कर्ण तदिहाद्य पापं जह्यासु कर्ण युधि स्वायसाचिना॥
en: I wonder how Suta's son has been able to penetrate the arrows shot by you, O Savyasachin; remember the distasteful, sharp and cutting jokes, this bold and wretched Suta's son uttered towards us and called us sesamum seeds not having anything within them and think over the sorrows of Krishna and soon put an end to the life of this scoundrel in today's battle, for you should not be any more careless about killing this Karna.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: कस्मादुपेक्षा कुरुषे किरीटित्रुपेक्षितुं नायमिहाद्य कालः। सिं ददत् खाण्डवे पावकाय॥ तया धृत्या सूतपुत्रं जहि त्वमहं चैनं गदया पोथयिष्ये।
en: Do you remember how you hàve conquered all creatures and have satisfied the hunger of Agni in the Khandava and with that patience i.e. (resembling yourself) kill Suta's son. I will also knock him down with my mace.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: अथाब्रवीद वासुदेवोऽपि पार्थं दृष्ट्वा रथेषून प्रतिहन्यमानान्॥ अमीमृदत् सर्वपातेऽद्य कर्णो ह्यस्त्रैरस्त्रं किमिदं भो किरीटिन्। स वीर किं मुह्यसि नावधत्से नदन्त्येते कुरवः सम्प्रहृष्टाः॥
en: Then Vasudeva seeing that Partha's shafts were being frustrated by Kama, addressed him (Arjuna)-How is this O Kiritin, that your weapons are being baffled by Karna. O brave warrior, why are you looking like one confounded. Don't you see the Kauravas, behind Karna, are all uttering loud shouts of joy.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: कर्ण पुरस्कृत्य विदुर्हि सर्वे तवासस्त्रमस्त्रैर्विनिपात्यमानम्। यया धृत्या निहतं तामसास्त्रं युगे युगे राक्षसाश्चापि घोराः॥ दम्भोद्भवाश्चासुराश्चाहवेषु तया धृत्या जहि कर्णं त्वमद्य।
en: Beholding your weapons made useless by those of Karna. This day kill Karna with the same energy that you have shown Yuga after Yuga in killing persons possessed of dark weapons and fierce Rakshasas and the boonproud Asuras in battle.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: अनेन चास्य क्षुरनेमिनाद्य संछिन्धि मूर्धानमरेः प्रसा॥ मया विसृष्टेन सुदर्शनेन वज्रेण शक्रो नमुचेरिवारेः।
en: Concentrating all your might cut-off the head of your enemy with this Sudarshana of razor-like keen edge which I am giving to you, like Cakra who cut-off the head of Namuchi, his enemy with thunder.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: किरातारूपी भगवान् सुधृत्या त्वया महात्मा परितोषितोऽभूत्॥ तां त्वां पुनर्वीर धृतिं गृहीत्वा सहानुबन्धं जहि सूतपुत्रम्।
en: You have even satisfied the great god Mahadeva (in battle) when he was disguised as a hunter; recovering the same patience, O hero, kill this son of Suta and his followers.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ततो महीं सागरमेखलां त्वं सपत्तनां ग्रामवतीं समृद्धाम्॥ प्रयच्छ राज्ञे निहतारिसंघां यशश्च पार्थातुलमाप्नुहि त्वम्।
en: By that you will restore to this king Yudhishthira the sea-belted earth with its towns, villages and wealth and remove all his enemies from the face of the Earth and by that you will gain great fame.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: स एवमुक्तोऽतिबलो महात्मा चकार बुद्धिं हि वधाय सौतेः॥ स चोदितो भीमजनार्दनाभ्यां स्मृत्वा तथाऽऽत्मानमवेक्ष्य सर्वम्। इहात्मनश्चागमने विदित्वा प्रयोजनं केशवमित्युवाच॥
en: Thus roused by Bhima and Janardana Partha,. of great prowess, internally remembered himself and for what he had come to the world and addressed Keshava and said-

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: प्रादुष्करोम्येष महास्त्रमुग्रं शिवाय लोकस्य वधाय सौतेः। तन्मेऽनुजानातु भवान् सुराश्च ब्रह्मा भवो वेदविदश्च सर्वे॥
en: Now I will invoke a powerful and terrible weapon for the benefit of the world and slaughter of Suta's son; let me have your permission as also of Brahma's and Bhava's as well of all persons who have acquired the Brahmajnana.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: इत्युच्य देवं स तु सव्यसाची नमस्कृत्वा ब्रह्मणे सोऽमितात्मा। तदुत्तमं ब्राह्ममसह्यमस्त्रं प्रादुश्चक्रे मनसा यद् विधेयम्॥
en: Addressing these words of Keshava Savyaschain, of unfathomable soul, bowing to Brahma, then brought forth into action that unbearable and choice weapon called, Brahma which could only be used after great : concentration of the mind.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: तदस्य हत्वा विरराज कर्णो मुक्त्वा शरान् मेघ इवाम्बुधाराः। समीक्ष्य कर्णेन किरीटिनस्तु तथाऽऽजिमध्ये निहतं तदस्त्रम्॥ ततोऽमर्षी बलवान् क्रोधदीप्तो भीमोऽब्रवीदर्जुनं सत्यसंधम्।
en: But thwarting that weapon Karna looked handsome like the raining clouds and went on sending showers of shafts. In that fight seeing that weapon of Kiritin waisted by Karna the powerful and wrathful Bhimasena, firing up with anger, thus addressed Arjuna of never failing aimननु त्वाहुर्वेदितारं महास्त्रं

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ब्राह्म विधेयं परमं जनास्तत्॥ निति स्मोक्तोऽयोजयत् सव्यसाची। ततो दिशः प्रदिशश्चापि सर्वाः समावृणोत् सायकैर्भूरितेजाः॥ दिवाकरांशुप्रतिमै लद्भिः।
en: "O Savyasachin, you are master of the noble Brahma weapon, the great means of destroying enemies. Do you, O Savyasachin, shoot the same sort of weapon again and again.” And thus being asked by his brother, The arrows, coming out of the Savyasachin Gandiva, resembled terrible snakes or the sun's rays shoot another like the one he used before and by that the energetic Partha covered all the cardinal and subsidiary points of ten compass.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: सृष्टास्तु बाणा भरतर्षभेण शतं शतानीव सुवर्णपुङ्खाः॥ प्राच्छादयन् कर्णरथं क्षणेन युगान्तवयर्ककरप्रकाशाः।
en: O Bharata race, they were brilliant as the Yuga fire or the sun's rays ten thousand arrows in not time covered Karna's car.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ततश्च शूलानि परश्वधानि चक्राणि नाराचशतानि चैव॥ स्ततो ह्यहन्यन्त समन्ततोऽपि।
en: From that celestial weapons came forth hundreds of long darts, battle-axes and cloth yard shafts of fearful shape and killed many warriors.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: छिन्नं शिरः कस्यचिदाजिमध्ये पतात् योधस्य परस्य कायात्॥ वन्यः प्रणष्टः पतितं विलोक्य। अन्यस्य सासिनिपपात कृत्तो योधस्य बाहुः करिहस्ततुल्यः॥
en: In that battle-field of the opposite party by cutting off their heads. One fell to the ground out of fear seeing another fall; the third's arm, powerful and large as an elephant trunk, was cut down with the sword still held in clasp.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: अन्यस्त सव्यः सह वर्मणा च क्षुरप्रकृत्तः पतितो धरण्याम्। एवं समस्तानपि योधमुख्यान् विध्वंसयामास किरीटमाली॥ ौर्योधनं सैन्यमशेषमेव। वैकर्तनेनापि तथाऽऽजिमध्ये सहस्रशो बाणगणा विसृष्टाः॥
en: The left arm, of a fourth with the shield grasped being severed by razor-headed shaft, fell to the ground and thus Partha, who was adorned with crown and garlands, killed and wounded all the best warriors of Duryodhana's army by his awful and dreadful arrows; Vaikartana (Karna) also sped in return thousands of arrows in that fight.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ते घोषिणः पाण्डवमभ्युपेयुः पर्जन्यमुक्ता इव वारिधाराः। ततः स कृष्णं च किरीटिनं च वृकोदरं चाप्रतिमप्रभावः॥ त्रिभिस्त्रिभिर्भीमबलो निहत्य ननाद घोरं महता स्वेण।
en: Those arrows came down upon the son of Pandu with hissing noise like a downpour of rain from the clouds. Then Karna of great prowess having struck Bhimsena, Janardana and Arjuna of crowned head, with three shafts which gave vent to loud and fearful roars.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: स कर्णबाणाभिहतः किरीटी भीमं तथा प्रेक्ष्य जनार्दनं च॥ अमृष्यमाण पुनरेव पार्थः शरान् दशाष्टौ च समुद्वबर्ह।
en: Then the diadem-adorned (Arjuna) beholding Bhimsena and Janardana thus struck and himself being also pierced lost all patience and again shot eighteen shafts.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: स केतुमेकेन शरेण विद्ध्वा शल्यं चतुभिस्त्रिभिरेव कर्णम्॥ ततः स मुक्तैर्दशभिर्जघान सभापति काजच्नवर्मनद्धम्।
en: Piercing Susena with one, Shalya with four and Karna with three, he with the other ten slew Sabhapati (a Kanrada prince) who was cased in a golden armour.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: विवाजिसूतो विधनुर्विकेतुः॥ हतो रथाग्रादपतत् स रुग्णः परश्वधैः शाल इवावकृत्तः।
en: That prince fell down dead from the front of his car, bereft of his head, arms, his steeds and banner like a Shala tree hewed down with the axe.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: पुनश्च कर्णं त्रिभिरष्टभिश्च द्वाभ्यां चतुर्भिर्दशभिश्च विद्ध्वा॥ चतुःशतान् द्विरदान् सायुधान् वै हत्वा रथानष्टशताञ्जघान्।
en: Again striking Karna with three, eight, twelve, four and ten shafts he put four hundred armed elephants and eight hundred carwarriors to death.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: नष्टौ सहस्राणि च पत्तिवीरान्॥ मदृश्यमञ्जोगतिभिः प्रचक्रे।
en: He also killed one thousand horses with their riders and eight thousand powerful infantry with his fleet arrows. So covered Karna, his car, horses, driver and standard that they all became invisible.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: अथाक्रोशन् कुरवो वध्यमाना धनंजयेनाधिरथिं समन्तान्॥ मुञ्चाभिविद्धयर्जुनमाशु कर्ण बाणैः पुरा हन्ति कुरून् समग्रान्।
en: Then the Kauravas being thus distressed by Dananjay began to call loudly the son of Adhiratha from all sides and said-"Do you display your weapons and slay this son of Pandu or he will with his shafts put on end to the whole Kuru army."

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: स चोदितः सर्वयत्नेन को मुमोच बाणान् सुबहून भीक्ष्णम्॥ मर्मच्छिदः शोणितपासुदिग्धाः।
en: Thus requested, Karna began to try his utmost and sent hosts of blood thirsty arrows that were capable of piercing the very core of the heart and thereby killed many of the Pandavas and Panchalas.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: तावुत्तमौ सर्वधनुर्धराणां महाबलो सर्वसपत्नसाहौ॥ मन्योन्यमप्यस्त्रविदौ महास्त्रैः। ते
en: In this way those two choicest of archers, the two most powerful warriors who could face and bear against all enemies and who were masters of all sorts of weapons, fearful to look at, went on striking each other and others that were fighting against them with their mighty weapons.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: मन्त्रौष्टीभिर्निरुजौ विशल्यः॥ युधिष्ठिरस्तत्र सुवर्णवर्मा।
en: After the broken blades have been drawn out of his body and his wounds healed by mantras and herbs prescribed by best surgeons who were friendly to him King Yudhisthira, cased in armour of gold, came to the spot to see the fight between Karna and Arjuna.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: तथोफ्यातं युधि धर्मराज दृष्ट्वा मुदा सर्वभूतान्यन्दन्॥ राहोर्विमुक्तं विमलं समग्रं चन्द्रं यथैवाभ्युदितं तथैव।
en: Like the brilliant full moon coming out of Rahu's grasp all the creatures were greatly delighted to see the virtuous king Yudhishthira in the battle-field.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: दृष्ट्वा तु मुख्यावथ युध्यमानौ दिद्दक्षवः शूरवरावरिघ्नौ॥ कर्ण च पार्थ च विलोकयन्तः खस्था महीस्थाश्च जनावतस्थुः।
en: All the gods in heaven and persons of the earth, checking the animals they were riding upon, waited calmly to see the issue of the fight between those great heroes, Karna and Partha, who were the choicest of warriors and scorchers of enemies.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: स कार्मुकज्यातलसंनिपातः सुमुक्तबाणस्तुमुलो बभूव॥ र्धनंजयस्याधिस्थेश्च तत्र।
en: O monarch, both Dhananjaya and Adhiratha's son went on striking each other with well-aimed shafts which made a great whizzing noise; and also the sounds made by the bows, bowstrings and the palms of the hands of those two brave warriors rose very loud.

description: The dual battle between Karna and Arjuna
sn: ततो धनुा सहसातिकृष्टा सुघोषमच्छिद्यत पाण्डवस्य॥ तस्मिन क्षणे पाण्डवं सूतपुत्रः समाचिनोत् क्षुद्रकाणां शतेन।
