en: When the earth was thus covered with dust and all the quarters were enshrouded with darkness your soldiers, O king, fled away on all sides in dismay.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: सम्भज्यमाने सैन्ये तु कुरुराजो विशाम्पते॥ परानभिमुखांश्चैव सुतस्ते समुपाद्रवत्।
en: When his army was thus routed your son, the Kuru king, rushed against his enemies who were proceeding against him.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: ततो दुर्योधनः सर्वानाजुहावाथ पाण्डवान्॥ युद्धाय भरतश्रेष्ठ देवानिव पुरा बलिः।
en: Duryodhana then challenged all the Pandavas in battle as did the Asura Bali the celestials in days of yore.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: त एनमभिगर्जन्तः सहिताः समुपद्रवन्॥ नानाशस्त्रभृतः क्रुद्धा भर्त्ययन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः।
en: Thereat all the Pandava warriors rushed in a body upon Duryodhana, hurled various weapons and chastised him again and again.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: दुर्योधनोऽऽप्यसम्भ्रान्तस्तान् रणे निशितैः शरैः॥ तत्रावधीत्ततः क्रुद्धः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
en: Worked up with anger, however, Duryodhana killed his enemies, in hundreds and thousands with keen arrows.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: तत् सैन्यं पाण्डवेयानां योधयामास सर्वतः॥ तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम तव पुत्रस्य पौरुषम्।
en: Wonderful was the prowess your son exhibited on that occasion for alone and with none to help him he fought with all the Pandavas in a body.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: यदेकः सहितान् सर्वान् रणेऽयुध्यत पाण्डवान्॥ ततोऽपश्यन्महात्मा स स्वसैन्यं भृशदुःखितम्।
en: Duryodhana then saw that all his soldiers were assailed with wounds and about to flee but had not gone very far from the scene of action.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: ततोऽवस्थाप्य राजेन्द्र कृतबुद्धिस्तवात्मजः॥ हर्षयन्निव तान् योधानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
en: Rallying his soldiers and cheering them up your son, who was bent upon keeping his honor, said-

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: न तं देशं प्रपश्यामि यत्र याता भयार्दिताः॥ गतानां यत्र वै मोक्षः पाण्डवात् किं गतेन वः।
en: There is no spot on earth or on mountain, I see, where if you go the Pandavas will not kill you. What is the use of your flying away?

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: अल्पं च बलमेतेषां कृष्णौ च भृशविक्षतौ॥ अद्य सर्वान् हनिष्यामि ध्रुवोहि विजयो भवेत्।
en: The Pandava army is very small now. The two Krishnas have been assailed with wounds. If we all stand for battle we will surely win victory.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: विप्नयातांस्तु वो भिन्नान् पाण्डवः कृतकिल्बिषान्॥ अनुसृत्य वधिष्यन्ति श्रेयान् नः समरे वधः।
en: If we however fly away disconcerted the sinsul Pandavas will pursue us and kill us all. It is better therefore that we should die in battle.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: सुखं सांग्रामिको मृत्युः क्षत्रधर्मेण युध्यताम्॥ मृतो दुःखं न जानीते प्रेत्य चानन्तमश्नुते।
en: Happy is the death in the battle-field. Follow your Kshatriya duties and fight. The dead know no misery. They however enjoy eternal bliss hereafter.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: शृणुध्वं क्षत्रियाः सर्वे यावन्तः स्थ समागताः॥ तदा शूरं च भीरुं च मारयत्यन्तको यमः को नु मूढो न युध्येत मादृशः क्षत्रियव्रतः॥
en: Listen therefore, O Kshatriyas who have assembled here. While death does not spare a hero or a coward what foolish Kshatriya is there who would not fight?

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: द्विषतो भीमसेनस्य क्रुद्धस्य वशमेष्यथ। पितामहैराचरितं न धर्मं हातुमर्हथ॥
en: Will you place yourselves under the power of our enemy Bhima? It is not proper that you should neglect the duties followed by your fathers and grand-fathers.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: न ह्यधर्मोऽस्ति पापीयान् क्षत्रियस्य पलायनात्। न युद्धधर्माच्छ्रेयो हि पन्थाः स्वर्गस्य कौरवाः। अचिरेण हता लोकान् सद्यो योधाः समश्नुता॥
en: There is no sin greater to a Kshatriya than flight from the battle-field. There is no more blessed road to heaven than battle; killed in battle therefore, O Kshatriyas, enjoy heaven in no time.

description: Kuru soldiers fled away from battle-field
sn: संजय उवाच एवं ब्रुवति पुत्रे ते सैनिकां भृशविक्षताः। अनवेक्ष्यैव तद्वाक्यं प्राद्रवन् सर्वतो दिशः॥
en: Sanjaya said Though your son gave vent to those words the Kuru soldiers greatly wounded fled away on all sides caring not for his speech.

sn: संजय उवाच दृष्ट्वा तु सैन्यं परिवर्त्यमानं पुत्रेण ते मद्रपतिस्तदानीम्। संत्रस्तरूपः परिमूढचेता दुर्योधनं वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing your son busy about rallying your soldiers the king of Madras, beside himself with grief, said-

sn: शल्य उवाच रायोधनं वीरहतैः सुपूणम्। महीधराभैः पतितैश्च नागैः सकृत्यप्रभिन्नैः शरभिन्नदेहैः॥ सविह्वलद्भिश्च गतासुभिश्च प्रध्वस्तवर्मायुधचर्मखङ्गैः। विभिन्नपाषाणमहाद्रुमौषधैः॥ प्रविद्धघण्टाङ्कुशतोमरध्वजैः सहेमजालैः रुधिरौघसम्प्लुतैः। शरावभिन्नैः पतितैस्तुरङ्गमैः श्वसद्भिरातेश्र क्षतजं वमद्भिः॥ मही दशद्भिः कृपणं नदद्भिः। तथापविद्धैर्गजावाजियोधैः शरापरिद्धैरथ वीरसंधै।॥ मन्दासुभिश्चैव गतासुभिश्च नराश्वनागैश्च रथैश्च मर्दितैः। मन्दानशुभिश्चैव मही महाहवे नूनं यथा वैतरवणीव भाति॥
en: Shalya said Look at this dreadful scene of action, O hero, covered with numberless killed men, horses and elephants. Some places are covered with of huge mountain-like elephants, maimed and their vital parts wounded with shafts. the armours, weapons, shields and swords of the lifeless warriors, shields and swords of the lifeless warriors are lying on all sides. They resemble huge mountains clapped with thunder, with trees, rocks and herbs dropping drown from them on all sides. The bells, hooks, lances and standards with which these huge animals, were equipped have been scattered on the ground. The bodies, which were adorned with golden trappings, are now covered with blood. Some places are covered with the carcasses of killed horses, mangled with arrows, breathing hard in agony carcasses and vomiting blood. Some of them are crying in agony, some of them are biting the earth with rolling eyes and some are neighing pitecusly. A part of the battle-field is covered with elephant warriors and horsemen thrown off their animals and car-warriors forcibly knocked down from their cars. Some of them are already and others are on the points of death. Covered with the dead bodies of men, horses and elephants their trunks and limbs and broken cars, the Earth looks awful like the great Vaitarini.

sn: रुद्वेपमानैःपतितैः पृथिव्याम्। विशीर्णदन्तः क्षतजं वमद्धि स्फुद्भिराते करुणं नदद्भिः॥ निकृत्तचक्रेषुयुगैः सयोक्तृभिः प्रविद्धतूणीरपताककेतुभिः। महारथौळेर्जलदैरिवावृता॥
en: The Earth looks awful covered with elephants with shattered tusks, vomiting blood, crying piteously in anguish in the battle-field, deprived of their armourless drivers and the infantry that protected them, with their quivers, banners and standards broken down and having their bodies that were adorned with nets of gold, wounded deep with the arrows of the enemy.

sn: यशस्विभिर्नागरथाश्वयोधिभिः पदातिभिश्चाभिमुखैर्हतैः परैः। वृता प्रशान्तैरिव तावकैर्मही॥
en: Covered with the dead bodies of elephants warriors, horsemen and car-warriors of great repute and of foot soldiers killed while combating with one another, divested of armours, ornaments and weapons the Earth looked like the sky covered with clouds.

sn: स्वेक्ष्यमाणैः पतितैः सहस्रशः। नक्तं ग्रहैद्यौरमलप्रदीप्तैः॥
en: Strewn with the heads the bodies of thousands of heroes wounded with arrows, all deprived of consciousness but some drawing vitality slowing, the Earth appeared to have covered with extinguished fires.

sn: र्मही बभूवानुगतैरिवाग्निभिः। हतैः प्रवीरैः कुरुसृञ्जयानाम्॥
en: Covered with the dead bodies of Kuru and Srinjaya warriors wounded with arrows and killed by Karna and Arjuna the Earth appeared as if covered with shining planets dropped from the sky or looked like the sky bespangled with stars in the night.

sn: शरास्तु कर्णार्जुनबाहुमुक्ता विदार्य नागाश्वमनुष्यदेहान्। महोरगा वासमिवातिताम्नाः॥
en: Cutting through the bodies of elephants, horses and men and putting out their vitality the arrows discharged by Karna and Arjuna entered into the earth like serpents entering into their holes with bent heads.

sn: हतैर्मनुष्याश्वगजैश संख्ये शरापविद्धैश्च रथैनरेन्द्र। रगम्यरूपा वसुधा बभूव॥
en: The entire field was blackened with carcasses, corpses, broken cars and arrows shot by Partha and Karna.

sn: रथैर्वरेघून्मथितैः सुकल्पैः सयोधशस्त्रैश्च वरायुधैर्ध्वजैः। निकृत्तचक्राक्षयुगत्रिवेणुभिः॥ हतानुकर्विनिषङ्गबन्धनैः। प्रभग्निनीडैर्मणिहेमभूषितै स्तृता मही द्यौरिव शारदैर्घनैः॥ । पेतुश्च खङ्गा
en: Well equipt cars were crushed by their arrows along with the warriors, weapons and standards. Their wheels, joints, axles, yokes, Trivenus, Upaskaras, Amikarsanas, the seats of the drivers and the fixtures of quivers were all broken into pieces. Covered with all these the Earth looked like the sky covered with autumnal clouds.

sn: हतेश्वरे राजरथैः सुकल्पितैः। दे॒तं व्रजन्तो बहुधा विचूर्णिताः॥
en: Riderless cars were dragged by quickcoursing horses, men, elephants and horses fled away in no time. And the army was thus completely routed.

sn: सहेमपट्टाः परिधाः परश्वधाः शिताश्च शूला मुसलानि मुद्गराः। विमला विकोशा गदाश्च जाम्बूनदपट्टानद्धाः॥
en: The battle-field was strewn with maces, battle-axes, lances, clubs, mallets, unsheathed swords and maces covered with cloth of gold.

sn: चापानि रुक्माङ्गभूषणानि शराश्च कार्तस्वरचित्रपुङ्काः। ऋष्टयश्च पीता विमला विकोशाः प्रासाश्च दण्डै कनकावभासैः॥ श्छिन्नापविद्धाश्च स्रजो विचित्राः। कुथाः पताकाम्बरभूषणानि किरीटमाला मुकुटाश्च शुभ्राः॥ प्रकीर्णका विप्रकीर्णाश्च राजन् प्रवालमुक्तातरलाश्च हाराः। आपीडकेयूरवराङ्गदानि ग्रैवेयनिष्काः ससुवर्णसूत्राः॥ मण्युत्तमा वज्रसुवर्णमुक्ता रत्नानि चोचावचमङ्गलानि। गात्राणि चात्यन्तसुखोचितानि शिरासिं चेन्दुप्रतिमाननानि॥ देहाचं भोगाचं परिच्छादांश्च त्यक्तवा मनोज्ञानि सुखानि चैव। स्वधर्मनिष्ठां महसतीमवाप्य व्याप्याशु लोकान् यशसा गतास्ते॥
en: It was covered with gold decked bows, gold-winged arrows, bright and unsheathed swords of good metal, lances, scimitars shining like gold, umbrellas, fans conchs, armours, painted with beautiful flowers of gold, trappings of elephants, standards, car-fences, crowns, necklaces, yalk tails, garlands of corals and pearls, chaplets, ornaments for the wrist and upper arms, golden collars for the neck, various precious diamonds, jems and pearls, beautiful moon-like heads and bodies brought up in luxury. Leaving behind their mortal coils, luxurious pleasures and dresses, acquiring glory by proving faithful to the duties of their caste they have gone with giory to the region of bliss.

sn: निर्वत दुर्योधन यान्तु सैनिका व्रजस्व राजशिबिराय मानदा दिवाकरोऽप्येष विलम्बते प्रभो पुनस्त्वमेवात्र नरेन्द्र कारणम्॥
en: "Retreat Duryodhana. Let your troops retire. O king, run on to your camp. The sun is going down. Remember O king, that you are the root of all this.”

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा विरराम शल्यो दुर्योधनं शोकपरीतचेताः। मार्त विसंज्ञं भृशमश्रुनेत्रम्॥
en: Addressing these words to Duryodhana, Shalya, with an aggrieved heart, stopped. Duryodhana too, greatly moved and beside himself with sorrow, with tears running down his eyes, wept for the charioteer's son crying "O Karna, O Karna!"

sn: तं द्रोणपुत्रप्रमुखा नरेन्द्राः सर्वे समाश्वास्य मुहुः प्रयान्ति। निरीक्षमाणा मुहुरर्जुनस्य ध्वजं महान्तं यशसा ज्वलन्तम्॥
en: Consoling Duryodhana again and again all the kings headed by Drona's son returned to their camp looking repeatedly on Arjuna's standard that was resplendent with his glory.

sn: नराश्वमातङ्गशरीरजेन रक्तेन सिक्तां च तथैव भूमिम्। नारी प्रकाशामिव सर्वगम्याम्॥ प्रच्छन्नरूपां रुधिरेण राजन् रौद्रे मुहुर्तेऽतिविराजमाने। नैवावतस्थुः कुरवः समीक्ष्य प्रव्राजिता देवलोकाय सर्वे॥
en: Beholding the earth that was saturated with blood coming out of the bodies of men, elephants and horses as if she were a courtezan clad in sable garments and golden ornaments, the Kauravas, who were bent upon going to the other world and who could not be recognized on account of their faces being covered with blood, could not stand therein that critical moment.

sn: वधेन कर्णस्य तु दुःखितास्ते हा कर्ण हा कर्ण इति ब्रुवाणा। दुतं प्रयाताः शिबिराणि राजन् दिवाकरं रक्तमवेक्षमाणाः॥
en: Worked up with sorrow on account of Karna's destruction they all bewailed crying "Alas!" Then seeing the sun assume crimson colour they all returned to their camps.

sn: गाण्डीवमुक्तैस्तु सुवर्णपुजैः शिलाशितैः शोणितदिग्धवाजैः। शरैश्चिताङ्गो युधि भाति कर्णो हतोऽपि सन् सूर्य इवांशुमाली॥
en: Although killed and wounded with goldwinged arrows, whetted on stone and adorned with blood-dyed feathers, shot off the Gandiva, the heroic Karna lying on earth looked like the sun of bright rays.

sn: कर्णस्य देहं रुधिरावसिक्तं भक्तानुकम्पी भगवान् विवस्वान्। स्पृष्टवांशुभिर्लोहितरक्तरूपः सिष्णासुरभ्येति परं समुद्रम्॥
en: Having touched with his rays Karna's body bathed in blood and assumed a crimson appearance on account of grief sun, ever kind to his votaries, proceeded to the other ocean for bathing.

sn: इतीव संचिन्त्य सुरर्षिसंघाः सम्प्रस्थिता यान्ति यथा निकेतनम्। यथासुखं खं च महीतलं च॥
en: Thinking thus the host of gods and Rishis left the scene of action for their respective habitations. Other creatures also wended their way, as they liked, either for the celestial region or for the earth.

sn: तदद्भुतं प्राणभृतां भयंकर निशाम्य युद्धं कुरुवीरमुख्ययोः। धनंजयस्याधिरथेश्चः विस्मिताः प्रशंसमानाः प्रययुस्तदा जनाः॥
en: Having witnessed that wondrous encounter between Karna and Arjuna which struck terror unto all living creatures also the leading Kuru heroes stricken with wonder and speaking highly (of the feat) proceeded (to their quarters).

sn: शरशंकृत्तवर्माणं रुधिरोक्षितवाससम्। गतासुमपि राधेयं नैव लक्ष्मीविमुञ्चति॥
en: Although his coat of mail had been shattered with arrows, although he had been killed in that dreadful fight the beauty of his countenance did not forsake Radha's son even when dead.

sn: तप्तजाम्बूदनदनिभं ज्वलनार्कसमप्रभम्। जीवन्तमिव तं शूरं सर्वभूतानि मेनिरे॥
en: Every one saw that the body of the heroes resembled burning gold. It appeared to have been instinct with life and looked effulgent like the sun or fire.

sn: हतस्यापि महाराज सूतपुत्रस्य संयुगे। वित्रेसुः सर्वतो योधाः सिंहस्येवेतरे मृगाः॥
en: Seeing the charioteer's son lying dead on the field of battle all the warriors were stricken with fear like other animals at the sight of a lion.

sn: हतोऽपि पुरुषव्याघ्र जीववानिव लक्ष्यते। नाभवद् विकृतिः काचिद्धतस्यापि महात्मनः॥
en: Although dead that best of men seemed ready to issue commands. Nothing was changed in that great heroes dead.

sn: चारवेषधरं वीरं चारुमौलिशिरोधरम्। तन्मुखं सूतपुत्रस्य पूर्णचन्द्रसमद्युति॥
en: Wearing a beautiful apparel and possessing a charining neck Karna's face looked resplendent like the full moon.

sn: नानाभरणवान् राजस्तप्तजाम्बूनदाङ्गदः। हतो वैकर्तन: शेते पादपोऽडकुरवानिव॥
en: Bedecked with various ornaments and golden Angadas, Vaikartana, albeit slain, lay on earth like a huge tree embellished with branches and twigs.

sn: कनकोत्तमसंकाशो ज्वलन्निव विभावसुः। स शान्तः पुरुषव्याघ्र पार्थसायकावारिणा॥
en: There lay that best of men like a mass of pure gold or blazing fire extinguished with the water of Arjuna's arrows.

sn: यथा हि ज्वलनो दीप्तो जलमासाद्य शाम्यति। कर्णाग्निः समरे तद्वत् पार्थमेघेन शामितः॥
en: As a blazing fire is quenched by water so Karna fire was extinguished by the Partha-like cloud in that battle.

sn: आहृत्य च यशो दीप्तं सुयुद्धेनात्मनो भुवि। विसृज्य शरवर्षाणि प्रताप्त च दिशो दश॥ सुपः समरे कर्णः स शान्तः पार्थतेजसा।
en: Having made a downpour of arrows and burnt the ten cardinal points that best of men with his sons was destroyed by Partha. He left the world but took away with him his fame which he had won on earth by fair fight.

sn: प्रताप्य पाण्डवान् सर्वान् पञ्चालांश्चास्त्रतेजसा॥ वर्षित्य शरवर्षेण प्रताप्य रिपुवाहिनीम्। श्रीमानिव सहस्रांशुर्जगत् सर्वं प्रताप्य च॥ हतो वैकर्तनः कर्णः सपुत्रः सहवाहनः। अर्थिनां पक्षिसंघस्य कल्पवृक्षो निपातितः॥
en: Having scorched the Pandavas with the fire of his weapons, having made a down-pour of arrows and consumed the hostile armies and heated the world like the thousand rayed sun Vaikartana left the world with his sons and followers. Thus perished the hero who was an all-giving tree unto the bird-like suitors.

sn: ददानीत्येव योऽवोचन्न नास्तीत्यर्थितोर्थिभिः। सद्भिः सदा सत्यपुरुषः स हतो द्वैरथे वृषः॥
en: Begged by them he always said “I give" and never “I have not." The virtuous always knew him to be pious. Such was Vrisha who died in a dual combat.

sn: यस्य ब्राह्मणसात् सर्वं वित्तमासीन्महात्मनः। नादेयं ब्राह्मणेष्वासीद् यस्य स्वमपि जीवितम्॥ सदा स्त्रीणां प्रियो नित्यं दाता चैव महारथः। स वै पार्थास्त्रनिर्दग्धो गतः परमिकां गतिम्॥
en: His wealth was always given to the Brahmanas. There was nothing not even his life which he could not make over to the Brahmanas. He was a darling of women, generous and a great car-warrior. Such a highminded man met with death,

sn: यमाश्रित्याकरोद् वैरं पुत्रस्ते स गतो दिवम्। आदाय तव पुत्राणां जयाशां शर्म वर्म च॥
en: Thus repaired to the celestial region the hero depending upon whom your son made enemies taking with him the hope of success and joy of the Kauravas.

sn: जगाम चास्तं सविता दिवाकरः। ग्रहश्च तिर्यग् ज्वलनार्कवर्णः सोमस्य पुत्रोऽभ्युदियाय तिर्यक्॥
en: The rivers were calın when Karna fell. The sun set with pale colour. Burning like fire or the sun, Soma's son Mercury moved askance through the sky

sn: नभः पफालेव ननाद चोर्वी वबुश्च वाताः परुषाः सुघोराः। दिगो बभूवुर्खलिताः सधूमा महार्णवाः सस्वनुश्चक्षुभुश्च॥
en: The sky was cut into two pieces. The earth roared loudly. All the points of compass, covered with smoke, were as if set on fire. The oceans were agitated and roared terribly.

sn: सकाननाश्चद्रिचयाश्चकम्पिरे प्रविव्यथुर्भूतगणाश्च सर्वे। बृहस्पतिः सम्परिवार्य रोहिणी बभूव चन्द्रार्कसमो विशाम्पते॥
en: There shook the mountains with their forests and all the creatures were pained. Assailing the constellation Rohini the planet Jupiter looked like the moon or the sun.

sn: स्तमोवृता द्यौर्विचचाल भूमिः। पपात चोल्का ज्वलनप्रकाशा निशाचराश्चाप्यभवन् प्रहृष्टाः॥
en: At Karna's death all the minor points of compass were ablaze. The sky was enshrouded with darkness. The Earth shook. Burning meteors dropped. The Rakshasas and other night rangers were filled with joy.

sn: शशिप्रकाशाननमर्जुनो यदा क्षुरेण कर्णस्य शिरो न्यपातयत्। तदान्तरिक्षे सहसैव शब्दो बभूव हाहेति सुरैर्विमुक्तः॥
en: When with his razor-shaped arrows Arjuna cut-off Karna's head having a moon-like countenance all the denizens of heaven, sky and earth sent forth cries of Oh and Alas!

sn: सदेवगन्धर्वमनुष्यपूजितं निहत्य कर्ण रिपुमाहवेऽर्जुनः। रराज राजन् परमेण वर्चसा यथा पुरा वृत्रवधे शतक्रतुः॥
en: Having killed his enemy Karna, adored of the celestials, men and Gandharvas Arjuna shone in his energy like the thousand-eyed deity after the destruction of Vritra.

sn: ततो रथेनाम्बुदवृन्दनादिना शरन्नभोमध्यदिवाकरार्चिषा। तपाकिना भीमनिनादकेतुना हिमेन्दुशङ्खस्फटिकारभासिना॥ महेन्द्रवाहप्रितमेन तावुभौ महेन्द्रवीर्यप्रतिमानपौरुषौ। रलंकृतावप्रतिमेन रंहसा॥ नरोत्तमौ केशवपाण्डुनन्दनौ तदाहितावग्निदिवाकराविव। रणाजिरे वीतभयौ विरेजतुः समानयानाविव विष्णुवासवौ॥
en: Then mounting their chariot the rattle of which was like the muttering of clouds, whose bright colour was like the mid-day sun of autumn, which was decorated with flags and standards, which was white in colour like the snow, the moon, the conch or crystal, whose horses were like those of Indra, those two foremost of men Krishna and Arjuna, who were energetic like great Indra himself who were embellished with gold, pearls, gems, diamonds and corals and who were effulgent like fire or the sun, moved on the battle-field with great force like Vishnu and Indra seated on the same car.

sn: ततो धनुातलबाणनिःस्वनैः प्रसह्य कृत्वा च रिपून हतप्रभान्। संछादयित्वा तु कुरूशरोत्तमैः कपिध्वजः पक्षिवरध्वजश्च॥ हृष्टौ ततस्तावमितप्रभावी मनांस्यरीणामवदारयन्तौ। सुवर्णजालावततौ महास्वनौ हिमावदातौ परिगृह्य पाणिभिः। चुचुम्बतुः शङ्खवरौ नृणां वरौ वराननाभ्यां युगपच दध्मतुः॥
en: Divesting perforce the enemy of his splendour by the twang of the Gandiva bow and the striking of palms and destroying the Kurus with arrows the ape-bannered Arjuna and Garuda-bannered Krishna, gifted with measureless prowess, those two best of men joyfully took up, with their hands, their snow white conchs sending forth loud peals, adorned with gold and blew them simultaneously striking terror unto the hearts of their enemies.

sn: पाञ्चजन्यस्य निर्घोषो देवदत्तस्य चोभयोः। पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षं च दिशश्चैवान्वनादयत्॥
en: The sounds of Panchajanya and Devadatta filled the earth, the sky and heaven.

sn: वित्रस्ताश्चाभवन् सर्वे कौरवा राजसत्तम। शङ्खशब्देन तेनाथ माधवस्यार्जुनस्य च॥
en: At the blare of Madhava's conch as well as that of Arjuna's all the Kauravas, O king, were stricken with fear.

sn: तौ शङ्खशब्देन निनादयन्तौ वनानि शैलान् सरितो गुहाश्च। वित्रासयन्तौ तव पुत्रसेनां युधिष्ठिरं नन्दयतां वरिष्टौ॥
en: Resounding the woods, mountains, rivers and cardinal points with the blare of their conchs and filling up your soldiers with terror those two foremost of men gladdened Yudhishthira.

sn: ततः प्रयाता: कुरवो जवेन श्रुत्वैव शङ्खस्वनमीर्यमाणम्। विहाय मद्राधिपति पतिं च दुर्योधन भारत भारतानाम्॥
en: No sooner the Kauravas heard the blare of the conchs then they speedily left the battlefield leaving behind them the king of Madras and the Bharata chief Duryodhana.

sn: महाहवे तं बहु रोचमानं धनंजयं भूतगणा: समेताः। तदान्वमोदन्त जनार्दनं च दिवाकरावभ्युदितौ यथैव॥
en: Then all the creatures in a body congratulated Dhananjaya who was shining in the battle-field and Janardana, those two foremost of men who were like two risen suns.

sn: बुभौ व्यभाता समरेऽच्युतार्जुनौ। तमो निहत्याभ्युदितौ यथामलौ शशाङ्कसूर्यो दिवि रश्मिमालिनौ॥
en: Pierced with Karna's arrows those two repressors of foes shone like the bright moon of many rays and the sun after dispelling darkness.

sn: विहाय तान् बाणगणानथागतौ सुहृढतावप्रतिमानविक्रमौ। सुखं प्रविष्टौ शिबिरं स्वमीश्वरौ सदस्यनिन्द्याविव विष्णुवासवौ॥
en: Then leaving off those arrows those two great heroes of incomparable prowess, encircled by their well-wishers and friends, returned to their camp like the Lords Indra and Vishnu.

sn: महर्षिभिर्यक्षमहोरगैरपि। जयाभिवृद्ध्या परयाभिपूजितौ हते तु कर्णे परमाहवे तदा॥
en: After Karna had been killed in that dreadful encounter, the celestials, Gandharvas, men, Charanas, Rishis, Yakshas and Nagas respectfully offered adorations of Krishna and Arjuna and wished them success.

sn: यथानुरूपं प्रतिपूजिताबुभौ प्रशस्यमानौ स्वकृतैर्गुणौघैः। ननन्दतुस्तौ ससुहृद्गणौ तदा बलं नियम्येव सुरेशकेशवौ॥
en: Having received all their friends with due honor and been praised by them for their heroic deeds those heroes enjoyed in the company of their friends like the king of gods and Vishnu after the destruction of Bali.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: संजय उवाच हते वैकर्तने राजन् कुरवो भयपीडिताः। वीक्षमाणा दिशः सर्वाः पर्यापेतुः सहस्रशः॥
en: Sanjaya said On Karna being slain, all the Kauravas, stricken with fear, fled away in all directions looking vacantly.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: कर्णं तु निहतं दृष्ट्वा शत्रुभिः परमाहवे। भीता दिशो व्यकीर्यन्त तावकाः क्षतविक्षताः॥
en: Hearing that the heroic Karna had been killed by his enemy your soldiers, overcome with fear, fled away on all sides.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: ततोऽवहारं चक्रुस्ते योधाः सर्वे समन्ततः। निवार्यमाणाश्चोद्विग्नास्तावका भृशदुःखिताः॥
en: Your all warriors then suffering from anxiety and agony, had received a number of wounds on their bodies. Hence, they all scattered in all directions wherever, they got the way.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: तेषां तन्मतमाज्ञाय पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। अवहारं ततश्चक्रे शल्यस्यानुमते नृप।॥
en: Then the Kuru leaders anxiously desired to rally your troops and your son also tried to cheek their flight.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: कृतवर्मा रथैस्तूर्णं वृतो भारत तावकैः। नारायणावशेषैश्च शिबिरायैव दुद्रुवे॥
en: Encircled by the remaining portion of the Narayana troops Kritavarma speedily proceeded to his camp.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: गान्धाराणां सहस्रेण शकुनिः परिवारितः। हतमाधिरथिं दृष्ट्वा शिबिरायैव दुद्रुवे॥
en: Seeing Adhiratha's son killed Shakuni surrounded by a thousand Ghandharvas, quickly returned to his camp.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: कृपः शारद्वतो राजन् नागानीकेन भारत। महामेघनिभेनाशु शिबियैव दुहुवे॥
en: Encircled by a large elephant force resembling a mass of clouds Saradvata's son Kripa quickly went towards his camp.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: अश्वत्थामा ततः शूरो विनिःश्वस्य पुनः पुनः। पाण्डवानां जयं दृष्ट्वा शिबिरायैव दुगुरे॥
en: Sighing heavily at the success of the Pandavas, the brave Ashvatthama quickly went to his camp

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: संशप्तकावशिष्टेन बलेन महात वृतः। सुशार्मापि ययौ राजन् वीक्षमाणो भयार्दितः॥
en: Encircled by the remaining portion of the Samsaptakas which was still a large army, Susarma, looking at the terror-stricken' soldiers, went away.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: दुर्योधनोऽपि नृपतिर्हतसर्वस्वबान्धवः। ययौ शोकसमाविष्टश्चिन्तयन् विमना बहु॥
en: Deprived of everything and his heart heavily laden with sorrow and afflicted by painful thoughts king Duryodhana went away.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: छिन्नध्वजेन शल्यस्तु रथेन रथिनां वरः। प्रययौ शिबिरायैव वीक्षमाणो दिशो दश॥
en: Having his standard broken and looking on all sides, Shalya, the best of car-warriors, returned to his camp.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: ततोऽपरे सुबहवो भरतानां महारथाः। प्राद्रवन्त भयत्रस्ता ह्रियाविष्टा विचेतसः॥
en: Assailed with fear and shame and beside themselves with grief the remaining car warriors of the Bharata army, still a large number, fled aw.y.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: असृक् क्षरन्तः सोद्विग्ना रेपमानास्तथातुराः। कुरवो दुद्रुवः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा कर्ण निपातितम्॥
en: Seeing Karna slain all the Kuru soldiers, trembling and with their voice suppressed with tears, fled away precepituously in fear.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: प्रशंसन्तोऽर्जुनं केचित् वेपमानास्तथातुराः। व्यद्रवन्त दिशो भीताः कुरवः कुरुसत्तम॥
en: The great car-warriors of the Kuru army fled away in fear some praising Karna and other Arjuna.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: तेषां योधसहस्राणांन तावकानां महामृधे। नासीत्तत्र पुमान् कश्चिद् यो युद्धाय मनो दधे।॥
en: Amongst the many thousand warriors of your army there was not a single individual who had any desire for fighting.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: हते कर्णे महाराज निराशाः कुरवोऽभवन्। जीवितेष्वपि राज्येषु दारेषु च धनेषु च॥
en: Upon the destruction of Karna, O king, the Kurus gave up all hopes of their lives, kingdom, wives and riches.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: तान् समानीय पुत्रस्ते यत्नेन महता विभुः। निवेशाय मनो दघे दुःखशोकसमन्वितः॥
en: Worked up with sorrow your son decided to give them rest for the night.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: तस्याज्ञां शिरसा योधाः परिगृह्य विशाम्पते। विवर्णवदना राजन् न्यविशन्त महारथाः॥
en: Obeying his orders, O king, the great carwarriors, bending low their heads, left the battle-field depressed and with pale countenances.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: तान् समानीय पुत्रस्ते यत्नेन महता विभुः। निवेशाय मनो दघे दुःखशोकसमन्वितः॥
en: Worked up with sorrow your son decided to give them rest for the night.

description: Kuru soldiers returned to his camp
sn: तस्याज्ञां शिरसा योधाः परिगृह्य विशाम्पते। विवर्णवदना राजन् न्यविशन्त महारथाः॥
en: Obeying his orders, O king, the great carwarriors, bending low their heads, left the battle-field depressed and with pale countenances.

sn: संजय उवाच तथा निपतिते कर्णे परसैन्ये च विद्रुते। आश्लिष्य पार्थ दाशार्हो हर्षाद् वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said After the destruction of Karna and the flight of the Kuru soldiers Krishna, embracing Partha in delight, said-

sn: हतो वज्रभृता वृत्रस्त्वया कर्णो धनंजय। वृत्रकर्णवधं घो कथयिष्यन्ति मानवाः॥
en: Vritra was killed by the holder of thunderbolt and Karna has been killed by you. They will simultaneously talk of the destruction of Vritra and Karna.

sn: वज्रेण निहतो वृत्र: संयुगे भूरितेजसा। त्वया तु निहतः कर्णो धनुषा निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Vritra was killed by Indra with thunder and Karna has been killed by you with bow and keen arrows.

sn: तमिमं विक्रमं लोके प्रथितं ते यशस्करम्। निवेदयावः कौन्तेय कुरुराजस्य धीमतः॥
en: Proceed, O Kunti's son and describe to the righteous king Yudhishthira your power capable of earning fame for you and which is known in the worlds.

sn: वधं कर्णस्य संग्रामे दीर्घकालचिकीर्षितम्। निवेद्य धर्मराजाय त्वमानृण्यं गमिष्यसि॥
en: Having given an account of the death of Karna, for which you had been trying for many years, to the virtuous king Yudhishthira, you will be freed from your debt to him.

sn: वर्तमाने महायुद्धे तव कर्णस्य चोभयोः। द्रष्टुमायोधनं पूर्वमागतो धर्मनन्दनः॥
en: While you were fighting with Karna Dharma's son came here for witnessing the battle.

sn: भृशं तु गाढविद्धत्वान्नाशकत् स्थातुमाहवे। ततः स शिबिरं गत्वा स्थितवान् पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Wounded deep with arrows he could not stay in the battle-field and that best of men returned to his tent.

sn: तथेत्युक्तः केशवस्तु पार्थेन यदुपुङ्गवः। पर्यावर्तयदव्यग्रो रथं रथवरस्य तम्॥
en: Partha acquiesced in the request of the Yadu chief who them cheerfully turned his car.

sn: एवमुक्त्वार्जुनं कृष्णः सैनिकानिदमब्रवीत्। परानभिमुखा यत्तास्तिष्ठध्वं भद्रमस्तु वः॥
en: Having thus accosted Arjuna Krishna addressed the soldiers, saying-"Blessings unto you all. Stand, confronting the enemies carefully."

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं युधामन्युं माद्रीपुत्रौ वृकोदरम्। युयुधानं च गोविन्द इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: He then said to Dhristadyumna, Yudhamanyu, the twin sons of Madri, Vrikodara and Yuyudhana.

sn: यावदावेद्यते राज्ञे हतः कर्णोऽर्जुनेन वै। तावद्भवद्भिर्यत्तैस्तु भवितव्यं नराधिपैः॥
en: Stand you all here carefully, O kings, till we come back having communicated to the king the destruction of Karna by Arjuna.

sn: स तैः शूरैरनुज्ञातो ययौ राजनिवेशनम्। पार्थमादाय गोविन्दो ददर्श च युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Having been thus permitted by those warriors he started for the camp of the king. Govinda, then, with Partha, saw Yudhishthira.

sn: शयानं राजशार्दूलं काञ्चने शयनोत्तमे। अगृह्णीतां च मृदितौ चरणौ पार्थिवस्य तौ॥
en: Yudhishthira the best king was slumbering that time on the royal bed. Both of them accessed thereto and put his feet on their palms under the influence of sheer gaiety.

sn: तयोः प्रहर्षमालक्ष्य हर्षाश्रूण्यवर्तयत्। राधेयं निहतं मत्वा समुत्तस्थौ युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Seeing them cheerful and with great wounds on their person Yudhishthira thought that the son of Radha was dead and speedily got up from his seat.

sn: उवाच च महाबाहुः पुनः पुनररिंदमः। वासुदेवार्जुनो प्रेम्णा तावुभौ परिषस्वजे॥
en: Having got up from his seat that repressor of his enemies, the king of mighty arms, again and again locked Arjuna and Krishna in his loving embraces. Then he asked Krishna about particulars (of Karna's death).

sn: तत् तस्मै तद् यथावृत्तं वासुदेवः सहार्जुनः। कथयामास कर्णस्य निधनं यदुपुङ्गवः॥
en: Then the sweet-speeched son of Vasudeva, the scion of the Yadu race, described Karna's death exactly in every detail.

sn: ईषदुत्स्मयमानस्तु कृष्णो राजानमब्रवीत्। युधिष्ठिरं हतामित्रं कृताञ्जलिरथाच्युत॥
en: Joining his hands and addressing Yudhishthira, whose enemies had been killed, Krishna alias Achyuta, smilingly said-

sn: दिष्ट्या गाण्डीवधन्वा च पाण्डवश्च वृकोदरः। त्वं चापि कुशली राजन् माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ॥ मुक्ता वीरक्षयादस्मात् संग्रामाल्लोमहर्षणात्। क्षिप्रमुत्तरकालानि कुरु कार्याणि पाण्डव॥ हतो वैकर्तनो राजन् सूतपुत्रो महारथः। दिष्ट्या जयसि राजेन्द्र दिष्ट्या वर्धसि भारत॥
en: By good fortune, the holder of the Gandiva bow, Pandu's son Vrikodara yourself and the two sons of Madri are all safe from his herodestroying and hair-stirring battle. Do what should next be done, O son of Pandu. The powerful son of the charioteer alas! Vaikartana has been killed. By good luck, O king of kings, you have achieved victory and by good fortune, you have gained over others, O son of Pandu.

sn: यस्तु द्यूतजितां कृष्णां प्राहसत् पुरुषाधमः। तस्याद्य सूतपुत्रस्य भूमिः पिबति शोणितम्॥
en: The Earth is drinking today the blood of the charioteer's sun, the wretch of a man who had laughed at Draupadi won at the game of dice.

sn: शेतेऽसौ शरपूर्णाङ्गः शत्रुस्ते कुरुपुङ्गव। तं पश्य पुरुषव्याघ्र विभिन्नं बहुभिः शरैः॥
en: Wounded all over with arrows, your enemy, O foremost of Kurus, is lying prostrate on the naked Earth. Look at that best of men mangled with arrows.

sn: हतामित्रामिमामुर्वीमनुशाधि महाभुजा यत्तो भूत्वा सहास्माभिर्भुडक्ष्व भोगांश्च पुष्कलान्॥ २३
en: O Heroe, rule now vigilantly the earth shorn of your enemies and enjoy with us all pleasures of life.

sn: संजय उवाच इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य केशवस्य महात्मनः। धर्मपुत्रः प्रहृष्टात्मा दाशार्ह वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ दिष्ट्या दिष्टेतिराजेन्द्र वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह। नैतचित्रं महाबाहो त्वयि देवकीन्दन॥ त्वया सारथिना पार्थो यत्नवानहनच तम्। न तचित्रं महाबाहो युष्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम्॥
en: Hearing the words of the great Keshava Yudhisthira cheerfully adored him in return and repeatedly said-"Good luck! Good luck!" “It is no wonder, O mighty-armed son of Devaki, that having yourself for his charioteer Partha should perform those super-human feats"

sn: प्रगृह्य स कुरुश्रेष्ठ सागदं दक्षिणं भुजम्। उवाच धर्मभृत् पार्थ उभौ तौ केशवार्जुनौ॥
en: Then taking hold of Keshava's right arm bedecked with Angadas and addressing him

sn: नरनारायणौ देवौ कथितौ नारदेन मे। धर्मात्मानौ महात्मानौ पुराणावृषित्तमौ॥
en: Narada told me that you two are the two foremost of divine Rishis Nara and Narayana ever engaged in maintaining virtue.

sn: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा असकृचापि मेधावी कृष्णद्वैपायनो मम। कथामेतां महाभाग कथयामास तत्त्ववित्॥
en: The highly intelligent and blessed Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa has also recounted to me several times this divine history.

sn: तव कृष्ण प्रसादेन पाण्डवोऽयं धनंजयः। जिगायाभिमुखः शत्रून् न चासीद् विमुखः क्वचित्॥
en: By your help, O Krishna, this son of Pandu, Dhananjaya, has defeated his enemies, without ever retreating from the battle-field.

sn: जयश्चैव ध्रुवोऽस्माकं न त्वस्माकं पराजयः। यदा त्वं युधि पार्थस्य सारथ्यमुपजग्मिवान्॥
en: Since you have condescended to drive Partha's chariot we are sure to win victory and not defeat.

sn: भीष्मो द्रोणश्च कर्णश्च महात्माः गौतमः कृपः। ये च तेषां पदानुगाः॥ त्वबुद्ध्या निहते कर्णे हता गोविन्द सर्वथा।
en: O Govinda! I accept the fact that Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Kripacharya, the descendant of Gautama clan and all existing as also erstwhile existed, number of gallants have automatically slaughtered with application of the wit to which you applied for beheading Karma.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा धर्मराजस्तु रथं हेमविभूषितम्॥ श्वेतवर्णैर्हयैर्युक्तं कालवालैर्मनोजवैः। आस्थाय पुरुषव्याघ्रः स्वबलेनाभिसंवृत्तः॥ प्रययौ स महाबाहुर्रेष्टुमायोधनं तदा। कृष्णार्जुनाभ्यां वीराभ्यामनुमन्त्र्य ततः प्रियम्॥ आभाषमाणस्तौ वीराबुभौ माधवफाल्गुनौ। स ददर्श रणे कर्णं शयानं पुरुषर्षभम्॥
en: Having said this the impartial king Yudhisthira, that foremost of men, got upon his chariot. It was adorned with gold and drawn by horses having black and ivory white tails and quick-coursing like mind. And talking pleasantly with Krishna and Arjuna he started, surrounded by his troops for seeing the battleficld teeming with many incidents. While talking with those two heroes Madhava and a Phalguna the king saw Karna, the foremost of men, lying on the battle-field.

sn: यथा कदम्बकुसुमं केसरैः सर्वतो वृतम्। चितं शरशतैः कर्णं धर्मराजो ददर्श सः॥
en: The king saw Karna pierced all over with shafts like a Kadamba flower with straight filaments shooting up all over.

sn: गन्धतैलावसिक्ताभिः काञ्चनीभिः सहस्रशः। दीपिकाभिः कृतोद्योतं पश्यते वै वृतं तदा।॥
en: He saw Karna lighted up by a thousand of golden lamps filled with scented oil.

sn: संछिन्नभिन्नकवचं बाणैश्च विदलीकृतम्। सपुत्रं निहतं दृष्ट्वा कर्णं राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥ संजातप्रत्ययोऽतीव वीक्ष्य चैवं पुनः पुनः। प्रशशंस नरव्याघ्राबुभौ माधवपाण्डवौ॥
en: Having seen Karna and his son killed and wounded with arrows shot off the Gandiva Yudhisthira looked again and again at them before he could believe his eyes. He then praised Krishna and Arjuna saying-

sn: अद्य राजास्मि गोविन्द पृथिव्यां भ्रातृभिः सह। त्वया नाथेन वीरेण विदुषा परिपालितः॥
en: "Having got you, highly wise as you are, as may lord and protector, I, O Govinda, the king of earth with my brothers.

sn: हतं श्रुत्वा नरव्याघ्र राधेयमतिमानिनम्। निराशोऽद्य दुरात्मासौ धार्तराष्ट्रो भविष्यति॥ जीविते चैव राज्ये च हते राधात्मजे रणे। त्वत्प्रसादाद् वयं चैव कृतार्थाः पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Hearing of the destruction of the haughty son of Radha the wicked son of Dhritarashtra will give up all hopes of his life and kingdom. By your favour, O foremost of men, we have achieved our object.

sn: दिष्ट्या जयसि गोविन्द दिष्ट्या शत्रुर्निपातितः। दिष्ट्या गाण्डीवधन्वा च विजयी पाण्डुनन्दनः॥
en: By good luck, you have won victory, O Govinda. By good luck, the enemy has been killed and by good luck the holder of the Gandiva bow has been crowned with success.

sn: त्रयोदश समास्तीर्णा जागरेण सुदुःखिताः। स्वप्स्यामोऽद्य सुखं रात्रौ त्वत्प्रसादान्महाभुज॥
en: Thirteen years we have spent in misery and vigilance. By your favour we will now sleep peacefully in night."

sn: संजय उवाच एवं च बहुशो राजा प्रशशंस जनार्दनम्। अर्जुनं च कुरुश्रेष्ठं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Sanjaya said In this way the king praised Janardana and Arjuna repeatedly.

sn: दृष्ट्वा च निहतं कर्णं सपुत्रं पार्थसायकैः। पुनर्जातमिवात्मानं मेने च स महीपतिः॥
en: Seeing Karna and his son slain with arrows Yudhisthira considered himself as if born anew.

sn: समेत्य च महाराज कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। हर्षयन्ति स्म राजानं हर्षयुक्ता महारथाः॥
en: Overflowing with joy all the car-warriors of the Pandava army approached Yudhisthira and delighted him.

sn: नकुलः सहदेवश्च पाण्डवश्च वृकोदरः। सात्यकिश्च महाराज वृष्णीनां प्रवरो रथः॥ धृष्टद्युम्नः शिखण्डी च पाण्डुपाञ्चालसृञ्जयाः) पूजयन्ति स्म कौन्तेयं निहते सूतनन्दने॥
en: After the death of the charioteer's son, Nakula, Sahadeva, Bhima, the great Vrishni car-warrior Satyaki, Dhristadyumna, Shikhandi, Panchalas, Srinjayas and other Pandava warriors adored the son of Kunti.

sn: ते वर्धयित्वा नृपतिं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। जितकाशिनो लब्धलक्ष्या युद्धशौण्डा: प्रहारिणः॥ स्तुवन्तः स्तवयुक्ताभिर्वाग्भिः कृष्णौ परंतपौ। जग्मुः स्वशिबिरायैव मुदाः युक्ता महारथाः॥
en: First speaking highly of Pandu's son Yudhisthira, those heroes, who always took delight in battle, desirous of victory and of sureness of aim, eulogised the iwo Krishnas. These great car-warriors delightedly returned to their caimps.

sn: एवमेष क्षयो वृत्तः सुमहाँल्लोमहर्षणः। तव दुर्मन्त्रिते राजन् किमर्थमनुशोचसि॥
en: Thus took place the dreadful, hair-stirring onslaught on account of your vile policy. Whey do you grieve for it now.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वैतदप्रियं राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। पपात भूमौ निश्चेष्टश्छिन्नमूल इव द्रुमः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing that evil news the Kuru king Dhritarashtra fell down on a sudden on the ground from his seat.

sn: तथा सा पतिता देवी गान्धारी दीर्घदर्शिनी। शुशोच बहुलालापैः कर्णस्य निधनं युधि॥
en: The far-seeing queen Gandhari too fell down. And she bewailed for the destruction of Karna in battle.

sn: तां पर्यगृह्णाद् विदुरो नृपतिं संजयस्तथा। पर्याश्वासयतां चैव तावुभावेव भूमिपम्॥
en: Vidura and Sanjaya then raised up the king and Gandhari consoled him.

sn: तथैवोत्थापयामासुर्गान्धारी कुरुयोषितः। स दैवं परमं मत्वा भवितव्यं च पार्थिवः॥ परां पीडां समाश्रित्य नष्टचित्तो महातपाः। चिन्ताशोकपरीतात्मा न जज्ञे मोहपीडितः। स समाश्वासितो राजा तूष्णीमासीद् विचेतनः॥
en: The Kuru ladies also raised up Gandhari. Thinking destiny to be all powerful the royal Rishi lost his senses under the weight of grief. His heart pining with sorrow and anxiety the king did not swoon away again. And consoled by them he sat silent indulging in melancholy reveries.

sn: श्रवणमहिमा र्धनञ्जयस्याधिरथेश्च यः पठेत्। स सम्यगिष्टस्य मुखस्य यत् फलं तदाप्नुयात् संश्रवणाच भारत॥
en: He who reads the account of this great encounter between Karna and Partha, like unto a great sacrifice and he who hears it read, both reap the fruits of a great sacrifice duly performed.

sn: मखो हि विष्णुर्भगवान् सनातनो वदन्ति तचाग्न्यनिलेन्दुभानवः! अतोऽनसूयुः शृणुयात् पठेच यः स सर्वलोकानुचरः सुखी भवेत्॥
en: The learned hold that the eternal Vishnu, Agni, Vayu, Soma and Surya is sacrifice. He who will therefore here recital these Parvans will attain to every blissful regions.

sn: तां सर्वदा भक्तिमुपागता नरा: पठन्ति पुण्यां वरसंहितामिमाम्। धनेन धान्येन यशसा च मानुषा नन्दन्ति ते नात्र विचारणास्ति॥
en: Those who devoutly read his holy and best of Samhitas, rejoice acquiring riches, corns and glory.

sn: अतोऽनसूयुः शृणुयात् सदा तु वै नरः स सर्वाणि सुखानि चाप्नुयात्। विष्णुः स्वयंभूर्भगवान् भवश्च तुष्यन्ति ते तस्य नरोत्तमस्य॥
en: Every one should therefore hear it reverentially. He who does it enjoys happiness and Vishnu, Brahma and Siva are propitiated with him.

sn: वेदावाप्तिाह्मणस्येह दृष्टा रणे बलं क्षत्रियाणां जयो युधि। धनज्येष्ठाश्चापि भवन्स् िवैश्या: शूद्राऽऽरोग्यं प्राप्नुवन्तीह सर्वे॥
en: By reading it a Brahmana reaps the fruit of the Vedic studies, a Kshatriya obtains victory and strength in battle a Vaisya immense riches and Sudra health and immunity from ailments.

sn: तथैव विष्णुर्भगवान् सनातनः स चात्र देवः परिकीर्त्यते यतः। ततः स कामाँल्लभते सुखी नरो महामुनेस्तस्य वचोऽर्चितं यथा॥
en: The illustrious Vishnu has been glorified in this Parvan-therefore by reading or hearing it recited a man becomes happy and acquires all desired for objects. These words of the great Rishi Vyasa can never be false.

sn: कपिलानां सवत्सानां वर्षमेकं निरन्तरम्। यो दद्यात् सुकृतं तद्धि श्रवणात् कर्णपर्वणः॥
en: The merit acquired by listening to the recitation of this Parvan is tantamount to what is obtained by giving away good kine with calves incessantly for a year.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्।।
en: Having saluted the Narayana and Nara the foremost of male beings, as also the goddess of learning Sarasvati let us cry success.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: जनमेजय उवाच एवं निपातिते कर्णे समरे सव्यसाचिना। अल्पावशिष्टाः कुरवः किमकुर्वत वै द्विज॥
en: Janamejaya said On Karna being thus killed by Savyasachin what did the sinall remnant of the Kurt army do?

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: उदीर्यमाणं च बलं दृष्ट्वा राजा सुयोधनः। पाण्डवैः प्राप्तकालं च किं प्रापद्यत कौरवः॥
en: Seeing the (Pandava) army elated with energy how did the king Suyodhana act towards them befitting the occasion?

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तदाचक्ष्व द्विजोत्तम। न हि तृप्यामि पूर्वेषां शृण्वानश्चरितं महत्॥
en: Describe it, О foremost of the twice-born. I wish to hear it. I am never satiated with hearing of the great feats of my forefathers.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कर्णे हते राजन् धार्तराष्ट्रः सुयोधनः। भृशं शोकार्णवमग्नो निराशः सर्वतोऽभवत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said After the destruction of Karna, O king, Dhritarashtra's son Suyodhana was immersed in a sea of grief and beheld despair on all sides.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: हा कर्ण हा कर्ण इति शोचमानः पुनः पुनः। कृच्छ्रात् स्वशिबिरं प्राप्तो हतशेषैःनृपैः सह॥
en: Exclaiming repeatedly "Oh Karna ! Oh Karna! he with difficulty reached his camp with the remaining kings on his side.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: स समाश्वास्यमानोऽपि हेतुभिः शास्त्रनिश्चितैः। राजभि लभच्छर्म सूतपुत्रवधं स्मरन्॥
en: Although consoled by those chiefs with cogent arguments sanctioned by scriptures he could not enjoy peace of mind thinking of the death of the charioteer's son.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: स दैवं बलवन्मत्वा भवितव्यं च पार्थिवः। संग्रामे निश्चयं कृत्वा पुनर्युद्धाय निर्ययौ॥
en: Considering Destiny and Luck as allpowerful and determined upon fighting the king issued out again for battle.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: शल्यं सेनापतिं कृत्वा विधिवद् राजपुङ्गवः। रणाय निर्ययौ राजा हतशैषैर्नृपैः सह॥
en: Having appointed duly Shalya as the coihmander-in-chief, that foremost of kings, O king, went out for battle with the remaining chiefs.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: ततः सुतुमुलं युद्धं कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः। बभूव भरतश्रेष्ठ देवासुररणोपमम्॥
en: Thereupon, O foremost of Bharatas a terrible encounter took place between Kurus and Pandavas like that between the celestials and Asuras.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: ततः शल्यो महाराज कृत्वा कदनमाहवे। ससैन्योऽथ स मध्याह्ने धर्मराजेन घातितः॥
en: Then, O king, having made a great onslaught in battle, Shalya, having lost a large number of his of his force, killed by Yudhishthira at mid-day.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा हतबन्यू रणाजिरात्। अपसृत्य ह्रदं घोरं विवेश रिपुजाद् भयात्॥
en: Thereupon having his allies slain king Duryodhana fled from the battlefield and was entered into a dreadful lake in fear of his enemies.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: अथापराह्ने तस्याह्नः परिवार्य सुयोधनः। ह्रदादाहूय युद्धाय भीमसेनेन पतितः॥
en: Then on that afternoon causing the lake to be encircled by mighty warriors Bhimasena invited him for battle and killed him.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: तस्मिन् हते महेष्वासे हतशिष्टास्त्रयो रथाः। संरम्भान्निशि राजेन्द्र जघ्नुः पाञ्चालसोमकान्॥
en: After his destruction in that great battle three car warriors who were still alive, worked up with great anger, killed the Panchalas in night.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: ततः पूर्वाह्नसमये शिबिरादेत्य संजयः। प्रविवेश पुरीं दीनो दुःखशोकसमन्वितः॥
en: Having left the camb next morning Sanjaya went to the Kuru capital depressed and laden with grief.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: स प्रविश्य पुरीं सूतो भुजावुच्छ्रित्य दुखितः। वेपमानस्ततो राज्ञः प्रविवेश निकेतनम्॥
en: Having entered the city and raising up his arms in sorrows and trembling the charioteer entered the Palace of the king.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: रुरोद च नरव्याघ्रं हा राजनिति दुखितः। अहो बत विनष्टाः स्म निधनेन महात्मनः॥ विधिश्च बलवानत्र पौरुषं तु निरर्थकम्।
en: Overwhelmed with grief, O foremost of men, he cried aloud, saying "Alas! O king, ruin has overtaken us all by the death of the great king.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: शक्रतुल्यबलाः सर्वे यथावध्यन्त पाण्डवैः॥ दृष्ट्वैव च पुरे राजञ्जन: सर्वः स संजयम्।
en: Alas! Time is powerful! Difficult are his ways, since all our men powerful like Indra, have been killed by the Pandavas.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: केशेन महता युक्तं सर्वतो राजसत्तम॥ रुरोद च भृशोद्विग्नो हा राजनिति विस्वरम्।
en: Beholding Sanjaya return in that painful state all the people anxiously lamented.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: आकुमारं नरव्याघ्र तत्र तत्र समन्ततः॥ आर्तनादं ततश्चक्रे श्रुत्वा विनिहतं नृपम्।
en: Hearing of Duryodhana's death the entire city, O foremost of men, including even children bewailed from all sides.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: धावतश्चाप्यपश्यामस्तत्र तान् पुरुषर्षभान्॥ नष्टचित्तानिवोन्मत्ताशोकेन भृशपीडितान्।
en: Pressed down with sorrow and be wildered men and women were seen running about like mad people.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: तथा स विह्वलः सूतः प्रविश्य नृपतिक्षयम्॥ ददर्श नृपतिश्रेष्ठं प्रज्ञाचक्षुषमीश्वरम्।
en: Entering the Royal Palace Sanjaya saw that great and highly wise king.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: तथा चासीनमनघं समन्तात् परिवारितम्॥ स्नुषाभिर्भरतश्रेष्ठ गान्धार्या विदुरेण च। तथान्यैश्च सुहृद्धिश्च ज्ञातिभिश्च हितैषिभिः॥ तमेव चार्थं ध्यायन्तं कर्णस्य निधनं प्रति। रुदन्नेवाब्रवीद् वाक्यं राजानं जनमेजय॥ नातिहष्टमना: सूतो वाक्यसंदिग्धया गिरा। संजयोऽहं नरव्याघ्र नमस्ते भरतर्षभ॥
en: Beholding the innocent king, the illustrious scion of the Bharata race seated encircled by his daughters-in-law, Gandhari, Vidura and other well-wishing relatives and friends and engaged in thinking of the same subject Sanjaya, with an aggrieved heart and suppressed accents said: " I am Sanjaya,.O great king. I bow to you, O foremost of the Bharatas.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: मद्राधिपो हतः शल्यः शकुनिः सौबलस्तथा। उलूकः पुरुषव्याघ्र कैतव्यो दृढविक्रमः॥ संशप्तका हताः सर्वे काम्बोजाश्च शकैः सहा म्लेच्छाश्च पर्वतीयाश्च यवना विनिपातिताः॥
en: The Madra-king Shalya has been killed as also Subala's son Shakuni and Uluka, the heroic son of Shakuni. The Samsaptakas, the Kambojas, the Shakas, the Mlechchhas, the mountaineers and the Yavanas have all been killed.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: प्राच्या हता महाराज दाक्षिणात्याश्च सर्वशः। उदीच्याश्च हताः सर्वे प्रतीच्याच नरोत्तमाः॥
en: The Easterners, the Southerners, the Northerners and the Westerners, O king, have all been killed.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: राजानो राजपुत्राश्च सर्वे ते निहता नृप। दुर्योधनो हतो राजा यथोक्तं पाण्डवेन ह॥
en: All the kings and princes have been killed. The king Duryodhana too has been killed by Pandu's son (Bhima) as he had promised.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: भग्नसक्तो महाराज शेते पांसुषु रूषितः। धृष्टद्युम्नो महाराज शिखण्डी चापराजितः॥
en: With the thighs broken he is lying prostrate on earth bathed in blood. Dhristadyumna and the invincible Shikhandi have also been slain.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: उत्तमौजा युधामन्युस्तथा राजन् प्रभद्रकाः। पाञ्चालाश्च नरव्याघ्र चेदयश्च निषूदिताः॥
en: Uttamouja, Yudhamanyu, Prabhadrakas and those foremost of men the Panchalas and Chedis have all been killed.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: तव पुत्रा हताः सर्वे द्रौपदेयाश्च भारत। कर्णपुत्रो हतः शूरो वृषसेनः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Your sons as also the five sons of Draupadi have been killed. The valiant and powerful son of Karna, Vrishasena, has also been killed.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: नरा विनिहताः सर्वे गजाश्च विनिपातिताः। रथिनश्च नरव्याघ्र हयाश्च निहता युधि॥
en: All the men collected have been destroyed as also the elephants. All the car-warriors and horses have been slain in battle.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: किञ्चिच्छेषं च शिबिरं तावकानां कृतं प्रभो। पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च समासाद्य परस्परम्॥ प्राय: स्त्रीशेषमभवजगत् कालेन मोहितम्। सप्त पाण्डवतः शेषा धार्तराष्ट्रस्त्रयो रथाः॥
en: Very few are serving on your side, O king. On account of the conflict between the Kurus and Pandavas the Earth contains only women now. Amongst the Pandavas seven are alive! and amongst your people only three.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: ते चैव भ्रातरः पञ्च वासुदेवोऽथ सात्यकिः। कृपश्च कृतवर्मा च द्रौणिश्च जयतां वरः॥
en: They are the five Pandava brothers and Vasudeva and Satyaki and Kripa and Kritavarman and Drona's son, that foremost of victorious heroes.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: तथाप्येते महाराज रथिनो नृपसत्तम। अक्षौहिणीनां सर्वासां समेतानां जनेश्वर॥
en: These three car-warriors, are all that survive, O best of kings, of all the Akshauhinis collected on your side, O ruler of men!

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: एते शेषा महाराज सर्वेऽन्ये निधनं गताः। कालेन निहतं सर्वं जगद् वै भरतर्षभ॥ दुर्योधनं वै पुरतः कृत्वा वैरं च भारत।
en: These are only living O monarch, the rest have died. Making Duryodhana and his hostility towards the Pandavas the cause, the whole world, it seems has been destroyed, O foremost of Bharata's race, by Time!"

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छुत्वा वचः क्रूरं धृतराष्ट्रा जनेश्वरः॥ निपपात स राजेन्द्रो गतसत्त्वो महीतले।
en: Vaishampayana sajd Hearing these cruel words, Dhritarashtra, that ruler of men, fell down, senses, O monarch, on the Earth.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: तस्मिन् निपतिते भूमौ विदुरोऽपि महायशाः॥ निपपात महाराज शोकव्यसनकर्षितः।
en: As soon as the king fell down, the illustrious Vidura also, O king, afflicted with sorrow for the king's distress, fell down on Earth.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: गान्धारी च नृपश्रेष्ठ सर्वांश्च कुरुयोषितः॥ पतिताः सहसा भूमौ श्रुत्वा क्रूरं वचस्तदा।
en: Gandhari also, O best of kings and all the Kuru ladies, suddenly fell down on the ground, hearing those cruel words.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: नि:सज्ञं पतितं भूमौ तदासीद् राजमण्डलम्॥ प्रलापयुक्तं महति चित्रन्यस्तं पटे यथा।
en: All those royal persons remained lying on the ground, deprived of their consciousness and crying in delirium, like figures painted on a large piece of canvas.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: कृच्छ्रेण तु ततो राजा धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः॥ शनैरलभत प्राणान् पुत्रव्यसनकर्शितः।
en: Then king Dhritarashtra, that lord of Earth, afflicted with the misery of the death of his sons, slowly and with difficulty regained his life-breaths.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: लम्वा तु स नृपः संज्ञा वेपमानः सुदुःखितः॥ उदीक्ष्य च दिशः सर्वाः क्षत्तारं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। विद्वन् क्षत्तर्महाप्राज्ञ त्वं गतिर्भरतर्षभ॥ ममानाथस्य सुभृशं पुत्रैर्हीनस्य सर्वशः। एवमुक्त्वा ततो भूयो विसंज्ञो निपपात ह॥ तं तथा पतितं दृष्ट्वा बान्धवा येऽस्य केचन। शीतैस्ते सिषिचुस्तोयैर्विव्यजुर्व्यजनैरपि॥ स तु दीर्घेण कालेन प्रत्याश्वस्तो नराधिपः। तूष्णीं दध्यौ महीपाल: पुत्रव्यसनकर्शितः॥ निःश्वसञ्जिह्मग इव कुम्भक्षिप्तो विशाम्पते।
en: Having recovered his consciousness, the king, with trembling limbs and aggrieved heart, looked of all sides and said these words to Kshatta Vidura:-"O learned Kshatta, O you of great wisdom, O foremost of Bharata's race, you are now my refuge! I am lordless and all my sons are dead"-Having said so, he once more dropped down unconscious. Beholding him fallen, all his relatives, that were present there, sprinkled cold water over him and fanned him. Comforted after a long while, that king stricken with sorrow on account of the death of his sons, remained silent, sighing heavily, like a snake put into a pot.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: संजयोऽप्यरुदत् तत्र दृष्ट्वा राजानमातुरम्॥ तथा सर्वाः स्त्रियश्चैव गान्धारी च यशस्विनी। ततो दीर्पण कालेन विदुरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ धृतराष्ट्रो नरश्रेष्ठ मुह्यमानो मुहुर्मुहुः। गच्छन्तु योषितः सर्वा गान्धारी च यशस्विनी॥
en: Sanjaya also wept aloud, beholding the king so aggrieved. All the ladies too with famous Gandhari, did the same.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: तथेमे सुहृदः सर्वे भ्राम्यते मे मनो भृशम्। एवमुक्तस्ततः क्षत्ता ताः स्त्रियो भरतर्षभ॥ विसर्जयामास शनैर्वेपमानः पुनः पुनः।
en: After a long while, O best of men, Dhritarashtra, having repeatedly swooned, said to Vidura. "Let all the ladies retire, even the illustrious Gandhari and all these friends! My mind is greatly unsettled!"-Thus addressed, Vidura, repeatedly trembling, slowly sent away the ladies, O foremost of Bharata's race.

description: Duryodhana's grief after the death of Karna. Sanjaya described to Dhritarastra the battle. Dhritarastra falls senseless
sn: निश्चक्रमुस्ततः सर्वाः स्त्रियो भरतसत्तम।॥ सर्वे दृष्ट्वा राजानमातुरम्। सुहृदश्च तथा ततो नरपतिं तत्र लब्धसंज्ञं परंतप॥ अवैक्षत् संजयो दीनं रोदमानं भृशातुरम्। प्राञ्जलिर्निश्वसन्तं च तं नरेन्द्रं मुहुर्मुहुः। समाश्वासयत क्षत्ता वचसा मधुरेण च॥
en: All those ladies retired, O) chief of the Bharatas, as also all those friends, sceing the king deeply afflicted. Then Sanjaya cheerlessly looked at the king, O scorcher of foes, who, having recovered his senses, was weeping in great misery.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विसृष्टास्वथ नारीषु धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। विललाप महाराज दुःखाद् दुःखान्तरं गतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said After the ladies had been sent away, Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, sunk into grief greater than that which had afflicted him before, began, O monarch, to bewail.

sn: सधूममिव निःश्वस्य करौ धुन्वन् पुनः पुनः। विचिन्त्य च महाराज वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Exhaling smoky breaths and repeatedly shaking his arms and reflecting a little, O monarch, he said these words.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अहो बत महद् दुःखं यदहं पाण्डवान् रणे। क्षेमिणश्चाव्ययांश्चैव त्वत्त: सूत शृणोमि वै॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Alas, O Suta, painful is the news that I hear from you viz., that the Pandavas are all safe and have suffered no loss in battle!

sn: वज्रसारमयं नूनं हृदयं सुदृढं मम। यच्छुत्वा निहतान् पुत्रान् दीर्यते न सहस्रधा॥
en: Forsooth, my hard heart is made of the essence of thunder since it breaks not upon hearing of the fall of my sons!

sn: चिन्तयित्वा वयस्तेषां बालक्रीडां च संजय। हतान् पुत्रानशेषेण दीर्यते मे भृशं मनः॥
en: Thinking of their ages, O Sanjaya and of their sports in childhood and learning today that all of them have died, my heart seems to break into pieces!

sn: अनेत्रत्वाद् यदेतेषां न मे रूपनिदर्शनम्। पुत्रस्नेहकृता प्रीतिर्नित्यमेतेषु धारिता॥
en: Although owing to my blindness I never saw their forms, still I cherished a great love for them on account of the affection one feels for his children.

sn: बालभावमतिक्रम्य यौवनस्थांश्च तानहम्। मध्यप्राप्तांस्तथा श्रुत्वा हृष्ट आसं तदानघ॥
en: Hearing that they had passed out of childhood and entered the period of youth and then of early manhood, I became highly glad, Osinless one.

sn: तानद्य निहतान् श्रुत्वा हतैश्वर्यान् हतौजसः। न लभेयं क्वचिच्छान्तिं पुत्राधिभिरभिप्लुतः॥
en: Hearing today that they have been killed and divested of prosperity and energy, I do not enjoy peace of mind, being overwhelmed with grief on account of the calamity that has befallen them.

sn: एह्येहि पुत्र राजेन्द्र ममानाथस्य साम्प्रतम्। त्वया हीनो महाबाहो का नु यास्याम्यहं गतिम्॥
en: Come, come, O king of kings, to me that am without a lord now! Deprived of you, O mighty-armed one, what will be my condition?

sn: कथं त्वं पृथिवीपालांस्त्यक्त्वा तात समागतान्। शेषे विनिहतो भूमौ प्राकृतः कुनृपो यथा।॥
en: Why, O sire, leaving all the assembled kings do you lie on the nacked ground, deprived of life, like an ordinary and wretched king?

sn: गतिर्भूत्वा महाराज ज्ञातीनां सुहृदां तथा। अन्धं वृद्धं च मां वीर विहाय क्क नु यास्यसि॥
en: Having been, O monarch, the refuge of kinsmen and friends, where do you go now, O hero, leaving me that am blind and old?

sn: सा कृपा सा च ते प्रीतिः क्क सा राजन् सुमानिता। कथं विनिहतः पार्थैः संयुगेष्वपराजितः॥
en: Where now, O king, is that pity of yours, that love and that respectfulness? Invincible you were in battle, how, alas, have you been killed by the Parthas?

sn: को नु मामुत्थितं वीर तात तातेति वक्ष्यति। महाराजेति सततं लोकनाथेति तासकृत्॥ परिष्वज्य च मां कण्ठे स्नेहेन किन्नलोचनः। अनुशाधीति कौरव्य तत् साधु वद मे वचः॥
en: Who will now, after I will get up from bed at the proper hour, repeatedly address me in such loving and respectful words as-O father, O father-O great king-O Lord of the world!-and affectionately clasping my neck with tearful eyes, will ask for my orders, saying-Command me, you of Kuru's race!-address me, O son, in that sweet language once inore!

sn: ननु नामाहमश्रौषं वचनं तव पुत्रका भूयसी मम पृथ्वीयं यथा पार्थस्य नो तथा॥
en: O dear child, I heard even these words from your lips, viz.-This wide Earth is cqually ours with Pritha's son!

sn: भगदत्तः कृपः शल्य आवन्त्योऽथ जयद्रथः। भूरिश्रवाः सोमदत्तो महाराजश्च बाह्निकः॥ अश्वत्थामा च भोजश्च मागधश्च महाबलः। बृहद्वलश्च क्राथश्च शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः॥ म्लेच्छश्च शतसाहस्राः शकाश्च: यवनैःसह। सुदक्षिणश्च काम्बोजस्त्रिगलाधिपतिस्तथा॥ भीष्मः पितामहश्चैव भारद्वाजोऽथ गौतमः। श्रुतायुश्चायुतायुश्च शतायुश्चापि वीर्यवान्॥ जलसन्धोऽथार्थ्यशृङ्गी राक्षसश्चाप्यलायुधः। अलम्बुषो महाबाहुः सुबाहुश्च महारथः॥ एते चान्ये च बहवो राजानो राजसत्तम। मदर्थमुद्यताः सर्वे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च।२१।।
en: Bhagadatta and Kripa and Shalya and the two princes of Avanti and Jayadratha and Bhurishravas and Cala and Somadatta and Valhika and Ashvatthaman and the chief of the Bhojas and the mighty princes of Magadha and Vrihadvala and the ruler of the Kasis and Shakuni, the son son of Subala and many thousands of Mlechchhas and Shakas and Yavanas and Sudakshina the ruler of the Kambojas and the king of the Trigartas and the grandsire Bhishma and Bharadvaja's son and Gotama's son and Shrutayusha and Ayutayusha and Shatayusha of great power and Jalasandha and Rishyashringa's son and the Rakshasa Alayudha and the mighty-arined Alambusha and the great car-warrior Suvahu-these and many other kings, O best of monarchs, have taken up arms on my behalf and are ready to throw away their very lives in great battle!

sn: तेषां मध्ये स्थितो युद्धे भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः। योधयिष्याम्यहं पार्थान् पञ्चालांश्चैव सर्वशः॥ चेदींश्च नृपशार्दूल द्रौपदेयांश्च संयुगे। सात्यकिं कुन्तिभोजं च राक्षसं च घटोत्कचम्॥
en: Stationed on the field amidst these and encircled by my brothers, I will fight against all the Parthas and the Panchalas and the Chedis, O foremost to kings and the son of Draupadi and Satyaki and Kuntibhoja and the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha.

sn: एकोऽप्येषां महाराज समर्थः संनिवारणे। समरे पाण्डवेयानां संक्रुद्धो ह्यभिधावताम्॥
en: Even one amongst these, O king, worked up with anger, is able to resist in battle the Pandavas rushing towards him!

sn: किं पुनः सहिता वीराः कृतवैराश्च पाण्डवैः। अथवा सर्व एवैते पाण्डवस्यानुयायिभिः॥
en: What need I say then of all these heroes, every one of whom has wrongs to avenge on the Pandavas, when united together? All these, O monarch, will fight with the followers of the Pandavas and will kill them in battle.

sn: योत्स्यन्ते सह राजेन्द्र हनिष्यन्ति च तान् मृघे। कर्ण एको मया सार्धं निहनिष्यति पाण्डवान्॥
en: Karna alone, with myself, will kill the Pandavas. All the heroic kings will then live under my control.

sn: ततो नृपतयो वीराः स्थास्यन्ति मम शासने। यश्च तेषां पणेता वै वासुदेवो महाबलः ॥ न स संनह्यते राजनिति मामब्रवीद् वचः। तस्याथ वदतः सूत बहुशो मम संनिधौ।॥
en: Their leader, the mighty Vasudeva, will not, he has told me, take up arms for them, O king. In this way, O Suta, did Duryodhana often use to speak to me. Hearing what he said, I believed that the Pandavas would be killed in battle.

sn: शक्तितो हुनुपस्यामि निहतान् पाण्डवान् रणे। तेषां मध्ये स्थिता यत्र हन्यन्ते मम पुत्रकाः॥
en: While, my sons, stationed in the midst of those heroes and fighting vigorously in battle, have all been slain, what can it be but Destiny?

sn: व्यायच्छमानाः समरे किमन्यद् भागधेयतः। भीष्मश्च निहतो यत्र लोकनाथः प्रतापबान्॥
en: When that lord of the world, viz., the valiant Bhishma, having encountered Shikhandin, died like a lion, killed by a jackal, what can it be but Destiny?

sn: शिखण्डिनं समासाद्य मृगेन्द्र इव जम्बुकम्। द्रोणश्च ब्राह्मणो यत्र सर्वशस्त्रास्त्रपारगः॥
en: When the Brahmana Drona, the master of all offensive and defensive, weapons has been killed by the Pandavas in battle, what can it be but Destiny?

sn: निहतः पाण्डवैः संख्ये किमन्यद् भागधेयतः। कर्णश्च निहतं संख्ये दिव्यास्त्रज्ञो महाबलः॥
en: When Bhurishravas has been slain in battle, as also Somadatta and king Valhika, what can it be else Destiny?

sn: भूरिश्रवा हतो यत्र सोमदत्तश्च संयुगे। बाह्निकश्च महाराजः किमन्यद् भागधेयतः॥
en: When Bhagadatta, an expert in fighting from the back of elephants, has been killed and when Jayadratha has been slain, what can it be but Fate?

sn: भगदत्तो हतो यत्र गजयुद्धविशारदः। जयद्रथश्च निहतः किमन्यद् भादधेयतः॥ सुदक्षिणो हतो यत्र जलसन्धश्च पौरवः। श्रुतायुश्चायुतायुश्च किमन्यद् भागधेयतः॥
en: When Sudakshina has been slain and Jalasandha of Puru's race, as also Shrutayusha and Ayutayusha, what can it be but Destiny?

sn: महाबलस्तथा पाण्डयः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। निहतः पाण्डवैः संख्ये किमन्यद् भागधेयतः॥ बृहद्वलो हतो यत्र मागधश्च महाबलः। उग्रायुधश्च विक्रान्तः प्रतिमानं धनुष्मताम्॥ आवन्त्यो निहतो यत्र त्रैगर्तश्च जनाधिपः। संशप्तकाश्च निहताः किमन्यद् भागधेयतः॥
en: When Brihadvala has been slain and the powerful king of the Magadhas and the brave Ugrayudha, that model of all bowmen when the two princes of Avanti viz., Vinda and Avinda have been slain, and the king also of thc Trigartas, as also the numerous Samshaptakas, what can it be but Destiny?

sn: अलम्बुषो महाशूरो राक्षसश्चाप्यलायुधः। आर्थ्यशृङ्गिश्च निहत: किमन्यद् भागधेयतः॥
en: When king Alambusha and the Rakshasa Alayudha and Rishyashringa's on have been slain, what can it be but Destiny.

sn: नारायणा हता यत्र गोपाला युद्धदुर्मदाः। म्लेच्छाश्च बहुसाहस्रा: किमन्यद् भागधेयतः॥
en: When the Narayanas have been slain as also the Gopalas, ever invincible in battle and many thousands of Mlecchas, who can it be but Destiny.

sn: शकुनिः सौबलो यत्र कैतव्यश्च महाबलः। निहत: सबलो वीरः किमन्यद् भागधेयतः॥
en: When Shakuni the son of Subala and the powerful Uluka, called the gamester's son, at the head of his forces, have been slain, what can it be but Destiny?

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवः कृतास्त्रा युद्धदुर्मदाः। राजानो राजपुत्राश्च शूराः परिघबाहवः॥ निहता बहवो यत्र किमन्यद् भागधेयतः। यत्र शूरा महेष्वासाः कृतास्त्रा युद्धदुर्मदाः॥ बहवो निहता: सूत महेन्द्रसमविक्रमाः। नानादेशसमावृत्ताः क्षत्रिया यत्र संजय॥
en: When numerous great heroes, well-read in all sorts of offensive and defensive weapons and gifted with prowess equal to that of Indra himself, have been slain, ( Suta, when Kshatriyas coming from different kingdoms, O Sanjaya, have all been slain in battle, what can it be but Destiny?

sn: निहताः समरे सर्वे किमन्यद् भागधेयतः। पुत्राश्च मे विनिहताः पौत्राश्चैव महाबलाः॥ वयस्या भ्रातरश्चैव किमन्यद् भागधेयतः। भागधेयसमायुक्तो ध्रुवमुत्पद्यते नरः॥
en: My mighty, sons and grandsons have been slain, as also my friends and brothers, what can it be but Destiny? Truly man takes his birth, subject to Destiny.

sn: यस्तु भाग्यसमायुक्तः स शुभं प्राप्नुयान्नरः। अहं वियुक्तस्तैर्भाग्यैः पुत्रैश्चैवेह संजय॥ कथमद्य भविष्यामि वृद्धः शत्रुवशं गतः। नान्यदत्र परं मन्ये वनवासादृते प्रभो॥ सोऽहं वनं गमिष्यामि निर्बधुओतिसंक्षये।
en: A fortunate man always meets with good. I am bereft of good fortune and therefore, am deprived of my children, O Sanjaya. Old as I am, how shall I now submit to the sway of enemies? I do not think anything else but exile into the woods is good for me, O lord. Shorn of relatives and kinsmen as I am, I will go into the woods.

sn: न हि मेऽन्यद् भवेच्छेयो वनाभ्युपगमादृते॥ इमामवस्थां प्राप्तस्य लूनपक्षस्य संजय।
en: Nothing else save an exile into the woods can be better for me who am fallen into this plight and who am shorn of my sons, O Sanjaya.

sn: दुर्योधनो हतो यत्र शल्यश्च निहतो युधि॥ दुःशासनो विविंशश्च विकर्णश्च महाबलः। कथं हि भीमसेनस्य श्रोष्येऽहं शब्दमुत्तमम्॥ एकेन समरे येन हतं पुत्रशतं मम।
en: When Duryodhana has been slain, Shalya also has been slain in battle, when Dusshasana and Vivingsha and the mighty Vikarna have been slain, how shall I be able to bear the shouts of that Bhimasena who has alone killed a hundred sons of inine in battle?

sn: असकृद्वदतस्तस्य दुर्योधनवधेन च॥ दुःखशोकाभिसंतप्तो न श्रोष्ये परुषा गिरः।
en: He will frequently speak of the slaughter of Duryodhana in my ears. Burning with grief and sorrow, I shall not be able to withstand his cruel words!"

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं वृद्धश्च संतप्तः पार्थिवो हतबान्धवः॥ मुहुर्मुहुर्मुह्यमानः पुत्रादिभिरभिप्लुतः।
en: Vaishampayana said Even thus that king burning with grief and deprived of relatives and kinsmen, repeatedly swooned, overwhelmed with grief consequent on the death of his sons.

sn: विलप्य सुचिरं कालं धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः॥ दीर्घमुष्णं स निःश्वस्य चिन्तयित्वा पराभवम्।
en: Having wept for a long time, Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, sighted heavily thinking of his defeat.

sn: दुःखेन महता राजन् संतप्तो भरतर्षभः॥ पुनर्गावल्गणिं सूतं पर्यपृच्छद् यथातथम्।
en: Overwhelined with sorrow and burning with grief, that best of Bharata's race once more enquired of his charioteer Sanjaya, the son of Gavalgana, the details of the battle.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच भीष्मद्रौणौ हतौ श्रुत्वा सूतपुत्रं च घातितम्॥ सेनापति प्रणेतारं किमकुर्वत मामकाः।
en: Dhritarashtra said After Bhishma and Drona had been slain and the Suta's son also overthrown, whom did my warriors make their general?

sn: यं यं सेनाप्रणेतारं युधि कुर्वन्ति मामकाः॥ अचिरेणैव कालेन तं तं निघ्नन्ति पाण्डवाः।
en: The Pandavas are slaying quickly every one whom my warriors make their general in battle.

sn: रणमूर्ध्नि हतो भीष्मः पश्यतां वः किरीटिना॥ एवमेव हतो द्रोणः सर्वेषामेव पश्यताम्।
en: Bhishma was slain at the van of battle by the diadem-decked Arjuna in your presence. Even thus was Drona slain before you all.

sn: एवमेव हतः कर्णः सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥ स राजकानां सर्वेषां पश्यतां वः किरीटिना।
en: Even thus was the Suta's son, the valiant Karna, slain by Arjuna in the presence of all the kings.

sn: पूर्वमेवाहमुक्तो वै विदुरेण महात्मना॥ दुर्योधनापराधेन प्रजेयं विनशिष्यति।
en: Long before, the high-souled Vidura had told me that through the fault of Duryodhana, the people of the Earth would be rooted out.

sn: केचिन्न सम्यक् पश्यन्ति मूढाः सम्यगवेक्ष्य च। तदिदं मम मूढस्य तथाभूतं वचः स्म तत्॥
en: There are some fools that do not see things even though they cașt their eyes on them. Those words of Vidura have proved true in my case.

sn: यदब्रवीत् स धर्मात्मा विदुरो दीर्घदर्शिवान्। तत्तथा समनुप्राप्तं वचनं सत्यवादिनः॥
en: What the pious Vidura, conversant with the attributes of everything, then said, had proved true, for the words he uttered were nothing but the truth.

sn: दैवोपहतचित्तेन यन्मया न कृतं पुरा। अनयस्य फलं तस्य ब्रूहि गावल्गणे पुनः॥
en: Afflicted by fate, I did not then act according to those words. The fruits of that evil course have now appeared. Describe them to me, O son of Gavalgana, once more.

sn: को वा मुखमनीकानामासीत् कर्णे निपातिते। अर्जुनं वासुदेवं च को वा प्रत्युद्ययौ रथी॥
en: Who became the head of our army after Karna's fall? Who was that car-warrior who proceeded against Arjuna and Vasudeva?

sn: केऽरक्षन् दक्षिणं चक्रं मद्रराजस्य संयुगे। वामं च योद्धुकामस्य के वा वीरस्य पृष्ठतः॥
en: Who were they that protected the right wheel of the ruler of the Madras in battle? Who protected the left wheel of that hero when he went to battle? Who also protected his rear?

sn: कथं च वः समेतानां मद्रराजो महारथः। निहतः पाण्डवैः संख्ये पुत्रो वा मम संजय॥
en: How, when all of you were together, could the mighty king of the Madras, as also my son, be slain, O Sanjaya, by the Pandavas?

sn: ब्रूहि सर्वं यथातत्त्वं भरतानां महाक्षयम्। यथा च निहतः संख्ये पुत्रो दुर्योधनो मम॥
en: Describe particularly the great destruction of the Bharatas. Tell me how my son Duryodhana fell in battle!

sn: पञ्चालानां यथा सर्वे निहताः सपदानुगाः। धृष्टद्युम्नः शिखण्डी च द्रौपद्याः पञ्च चात्मजाः॥
en: Tell me how all the Panchalas with their followers and Dhrishtadyumna and Shiklandhin and the five sons of Draupadi, were killed.

sn: पाण्डवाश्च यथा मुक्तास्तथोभौ माधवौ युधि। कृपश्च कृतवर्मा च भारद्वाजस्य चात्मजः॥
en: Tell me how the (five) Pandavas and the two Satvatas (viz., Krishna and Satyaki) and Kripa and Kritavarman and Drona's son, have escaped with life.

sn: यद् यथा यादृशं चैव युद्धं वृत्तं च साम्प्रतम्। अखिलं श्रोतुमिच्छामि कुशलो ह्यसि संजय॥
en: I desire to hear everything about the battle and its nature. You are a skillful narrator. O Sanjaya, tell the everything!'

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: संजय उवाच शृणु राजन्नवहितो यथावृत्तो महान् क्षयः। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च समासाद्य परस्परम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Hear, O king, attentively how that great thousands of the Kurus and the Pandavas took place when they encountered each other.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: निहते सूतपुत्रे तु पाण्डवेन महात्मना। विद्रुतेषु च सैन्येष समानीतेषु चासकृत्॥ घोरे मनुष्यदेहानामाजौ नरवर क्षये। यत्तत् कर्णे हते पार्थः सिंहनादमथाकरोत्॥
en: After the Suta's son had been killed by the illustrious son of Pandu and after the troops had been repeatedly collected and had repeatedly been routed and after a terrible ensaught had taken place, O foremost of men in battle after Karna's death, Partha began to utter leonine shouts. At that time your sons were possessed by great fear.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: तदा तव सुतान् राजन् प्राविशत् समुहद् भयम्। न संधातुमनीकानि न चैवाथ पराक्रमे॥
en: Indeed, after Karna's death, there was no warrior in your army who could rally the troops or show his prowess.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: आसीद् बुद्धिर्हते कर्णे तव योधस्य कस्यचित्। वणिजो नावि भिन्नायामगाधे विप्लवा इव॥ अपारे पारमिच्छन्तो हते द्वीपे किरीटिना।
en: They then looked like ship-wrecked merchants on the vast sea without a raft to save themselves. When their protector was slain by the diadem-decked Arjuna, they were like persons on the vast sea desirous of reaching safely some shore.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: सूतपुत्रे हते राजन् वित्रस्ताः शरविक्षताः॥ अनाथा नाथमिच्छन्तो मृगाः सिंहार्दिता इव।
en: Indeed, O king, after the slaughter of the Suta's son, your troops, panic-stricken and mangled with arrows, were like helpless men like a herd of deer attacked by a hon.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: भग्नशृङ्गा इव वृषा: शीर्णदंष्ट्रा इवोरगाः॥ प्रत्युपायाम सायाह्ने निर्जिता सव्यसाचिना।
en: Defeated by Savyasachin, they retired in the evening, like bulls with broken horns or snakes shorn of their fangs.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: हतप्रवीरा स्विस्ता निकृत्ता निशितैः शरैः॥ सूतपुत्रे हते राजन् पुत्रास्ते प्राद्रवंस्ततः।
en: Their foremost of heroes slain, themselves thrown into confusion and cut with keen arrows, your sons, O king, upon the slaughter of the Suta's son, fled away in fear.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: विध्वस्तकवचाः सर्वे कांदिशीका विचेतसः॥ अन्योन्यमभिनिघ्नन्तो वीक्षमाणा भयाद् दिशः।
en: Deprived of weapons and coats of mail, all of them were bewildered and know not where to fly. Looking on all sides, many of them began to kill one another.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: मामेव नूनं बीभत्सुर्मामेव च वृकोदरः॥ अभियातीति मन्वाना: पेतुर्मम्लुश्च भारत। अश्वानन्ये गजानन्ये स्थानन्ये महारथाः॥ आरुह्य जवसम्पन्ना पादातान् प्रजहुर्भयात्।
en: Many fell down or became pale, thinking-It is ine whom Vibhatsu is pursuing!—It is me whoin Vrikodara is pursuing!-Some riding on quick horses, some on fleet cars and some on fleet elephants, many great car-warriors fled away from fear, leaving behind the footsoldiers.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: कुञ्जरैः स्यन्दना भग्नाः सादिनश्च महारथैः॥ पदातिसंघाश्चाश्वोधैः पलायद्भिर्भृशं हताः।
en: Cars were broken by elephants, horsemen were crushed by great car warriors and the foot were smashed and slain by bodies of horse, as they fled away from the field of action.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: व्यालतस्करसंकीर्णे सार्थहीना यथा वने॥ तथा त्वदीया निहते सूतपुत्रे तदाभवन्।
en: After the fall of the Suta's son, your troops became like straggling travellers in a forest abounding with robbers and beasts of prey.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: हतारोहास्तथा नागाश्छिन्नहस्तास्तथापरे॥ सर्वं पार्थमयं लोकमपश्यन् वै भयार्दिताः।
