en: Some elephants whose riders had been killed and others whose trunks had been cut off, stricken with fear, saw the entire universe full of Partha.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: तान् प्रेक्ष्य द्रवतः सर्वान् भीमसेनभयार्दितान्॥ दुर्योधनोऽथ स्वं सूतं हा हा कृत्वैवमब्रवीत्। नातिक्रमिष्यते पार्थो धनुष्पाणिमवस्थितम्॥ जघने युद्धमानं मां तूर्णमश्वान् प्रचोदय।
en: Beholding his troops flying away in fear of Bhimasena, Duryodhana, then, with cries of Oh and Alas, addressed his driver, saying-If I stand it the rear of the army, armed with my bow, Partha then will never be able to go beyond me. Drive quickly the horses, therefore.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: समरे युद्धमानं हि कौन्तेयं मां धनंजयः॥ नोत्सहेताप्यतिक्रान्तुं वेलामिव महार्णवः।
en: When I will display my courage in battle Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, will not dare go beyond ine like the ocean never venturing to transgress its banks,

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: अद्यार्जुनं सगोविन्दं मानिनं च वृकोदरम्॥ निहत्य शिष्टाशत्रूश्च कर्णस्यानृण्यमाप्नुयाम्। तच्छ्रुत्वा कुरुराजस्य शूरार्यसदृशं वचः॥ सूतो हेमपरिच्छन्नाशनैरश्वानचोदयत्।
en: Today, killing Arjuna with Govinda and the proud Vrikodara and the rest of my enemies. I will free myself from the debt I owe to Karna.”—Hearing these words of the Kuru king worthy of an honorable man, his driver slowly urged those horse adorned with trappings of gold.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: गजाश्वरथहीनास्तु पादाताश्चैव मारिष॥ पञ्चविंशतिसाहस्राः प्राद्रवशनकैरिव।
en: At the time many brave warriors, deprived of elephants and horscs and cars and five and twenty thousand foot, procecded slowly for battle.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: तान् भीमसेनः संक्रुद्धो धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥ बलेन चतुरङ्गेण परिक्षिप्याहनच्छरैः।
en: Then Bhimasena, worked up with wrath and Dhrishtadyumna the son of Prishata, encircling those soldiers with the help of four kinds of forces destroyed them with arrows.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: प्रत्ययुध्यंस्तु ते सर्वे भीमसेनं सपार्षतम्॥ पार्थपार्षतयोश्चान्ये जगृहुस्तत्र नामनी।
en: All of them fought vigorously with Bhima and Prishata's son. Many amongst them challenged the two Pandava herocs mentioning their naimes.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: अक्रुद्ध्यत रणे भीमस्तैर्मधे प्रत्यवस्थितैः॥ सोऽवतीर्य रथात्तूर्णं गदापाणिरयुध्यता
en: Surrounded by them in battle, Bhima became angry with them. Quickly getting down from his car, he began to fight, with his mace.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: न तान् रथस्थो भूमिष्ठान् धर्मापेक्षी वृकोदरः॥ योधयामास कौन्तेयो भुजवीर्यमुपाश्रितः।
en: Depending on the might of his own arms, Vrikodara, the son of Kunti, who was on his car, observing the rules of fair fight, did not fight with those focs who were struck down on earth.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: जातरूपपरिच्छन्नां प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्॥ न्यवधीत् तावकान् सर्वान् दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः।
en: Armed with his heavy mace made entirely of iron and adorned with gold and resembling the Destroyer himself at the end of Yuga, Bhima slew them all like Yama destroying crcatures with his club.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: पदातयो हि संरब्धास्त्यक्तजीवितबान्धवाः॥ भीममभ्यद्रवन् संख्ये पतङ्गा इव पावकम्।
en: These foot-soldiers, worked up with great anger, having lost their friends and kinsmen, were prepared to cast away their lives and rushed in that battle towards Bhima like insects towards a blazing fire.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: आसाद्य भीमसेनं ते संरब्धा युद्धदुर्मदाः॥ विनेदुः सहसा दृष्ट्वा भूतग्रामा इवान्तकम्।
en: Indeed those warriors, stricken with fear and invincible in battle, approaching Bhimasena, suddenly died like living creatures at the look of the Destroyer.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: श्येनवद् व्यचरद् भीमः खड्डेन गदया तथा॥ पञ्चविंशतिसाहस्रास्तावकानां व्यपोथयत्।
en: Armed with sword and mace, Bhima inoved on like a hawk and killed your twenty-five thousand warriors.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: हत्वा तत् पुरुषानीकं भीमः सत्यपराक्रमः॥ धृष्टद्युम्नं पुरस्कृस्य पुनस्तस्थौ महाबलः।
en: Having killed that brave division, the powerful Bhima, of invincible prowess, once more stood, with Dhrishtadyumna before him.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: धनंजयो स्थानीकमन्वपद्यत वीर्यवान्॥ माद्रीपुत्रो च शकुनि सात्यकिश्च महाबलः।
en: In the meantime the highly energetic Dhananjaya proceeded towards the car-division of the Kurus. The twin sons of Madri and the mighty car-warrior Satyaki, all strong, cheerfully rushed against Shakuni for slaying him.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: जवेनाभ्यपतन् हृष्टा नन्तो दौर्योधनं बलम्॥ तस्याश्ववाहान् सुवहूंस्ते निहत्य शितैः शरैः। तमन्वधावंस्त्वरितास्तत्र युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: Having slain with keen the numerous cavalry of Shakuni, those Pandava heroes quickly proceeded against Shakuni himself, whereupon a fierce encounter took place.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: ततो धनंजयो राजन् रथानीकमगाहत। विश्रुतं त्रिषु लोकेषु गाण्डीवं व्याक्षिपन् धनुः॥
en: Then Dhananjaya, O king, penetrated into the midst of the car-detachment of the Kauravas, expanding his bow Gandiva known over the three worlds.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: कृष्णसारथिमायन्तं दृष्ट्वा श्वेतहयं रथम्। अर्जुनं चापि योद्धारं त्वदीयाः प्राद्रवन् भयात्॥
en: Beholding that car having white horses yoked to it and Krishna for its driver coming arrows towards them, with Arjuna as the warrior on it, your troops fled away in fear.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: विप्रहीनरथाश्वाश्च शरैश्च परिवारिताः। पञ्चविंशतिसाहस्राः पार्थमार्छन् पदातयः॥
en: Deprived of cars and horses and struck with arrows from every side, five and twenty thousand foot-soldiers proceeded towards Partha and surrounded him.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: हत्वा तत् पुरुषानीकं पञ्चालानां महारथः। भीमसेनं पुरस्कृत्य नचिरात् प्रत्यदृश्यत॥
en: Then that mighty car-warriors amongst the Panchalas, viz., Dhrishtadyumna with Bhimasena at the head quickly killed them and gained victory.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: महाधनुर्धरः श्रीमानमित्रगणमर्दनः। पुत्रः पाञ्चालराजस्य धृष्टद्युम्नो महायशाः॥
en: The son of the Panchala king, viz., the celebrated Dhrishtadyumna, was a great bowman possessed of great beauty and a repressor of foes.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: पारावतसवर्णाश्वं कोविदारवरध्वजम्। धृष्टद्युम्नं रणे दृष्ट्वा त्वदीयाः प्राद्रवन् भयात्॥
en: Seeing Dhrishtadyumna to whose car were yoked steeds white as pigeons and whose standard was made of lofty Kovidara, your troops fled away in fear.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: गान्धारराजं शीघ्रास्त्रमनुसृत्य यशस्विनौ। अचिरात् प्रत्यदृश्येतां माद्रीपुत्रौ ससात्यकी॥
en: The celebrated sons of Madri, with Satyaki among them, followed by the Gandhara king who was quick in the use of weapons, soon appeared befoie us.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: चेकितानः शिखण्डी च द्रौपदेयाश्च मारिष । हत्वा त्वदीयं सुमहत् सैन्यं शङ्खानथाधमन्॥
en: Chekitana and Shikhandhin and the five sons of Draupadi, having killed a large number of your troops, blew their conchs.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: ते सर्वे तावकान् प्रेक्ष्य द्रवतो वै पराङ्मुखान्। अभ्यधावन्त निघ्नन्तो वृषाञ्जित्वा वृषा इव॥
en: Seeing all your troops flying away from the field, those Pandava heroes pursued and killed them like bulls pursuing defeated bulls.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: सेनावशेषं तं दृष्ट्वा तव पुत्रस्य पाण्डवः। अवस्थितं सव्यसाची चुक्रोध बलावन्नृप॥
en: Then the mighty Savyasachin, the son of Pandu, beholding the remaining portion of your army still fighting was filled with anger, O king.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: तत एनं शरै राजन् सहसा समवाकिरत्। रजसा चोद्गतेनाथ न स्म किंचन दृश्यते॥
en: Suddenly, O monarch, he covered the remnant of your army with arrows. The dust, however, that was then raised, covered the sky, for which we could not see anything.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: अन्धकारीकृते लोके शरीभूते महीतले। दिशः सर्वा महाराज तावकाः प्राद्रवन् भयात्॥
en: Darkness also spread over the place and the field of battle was covered with arrows. Your troops, O monarch, then fled away in fear on all sides.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: भज्यमानेषु सर्वेषु कुरुराजो विशाम्पते। परेषामात्मनश्चैव सैन्ये ते समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: When his army was thus broken, the Kuru king, O monarch, rushed against both friends and foes.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: ततो दुर्योधनः सर्वानाजुहावाथ पाण्डवान्। युद्धाय भरतश्रेष्ठ देवानिव पुरा बलिः॥
en: Then Duryodhana challenged all the Pandavas to battle, O chief of Bharata's race, like the Asura Vali in days of yore challenging all the celestials.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: त एनमभिगर्जन्तं सहिताः समुपाद्रवन्। नानाशस्त्रसृजः क्रुद्धा भर्त्सयन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: The Pandavas then, collected in a body and filled with rage, chastising him repeatedly and discharging various weapons, proceeded against Duryodhana.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: दुर्योधनोऽप्यसम्भ्रान्तस्तानरीन् व्यधमच्छरैः। तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम तव पुत्रस्य पौरुषम्॥ यदेनं पाण्डवाः सर्वे न शेकुरतिवर्तितुम्। नातिदूरापयातं च कृतबुद्धिः पलायने॥ दुर्योधनः स्वकं सैन्यमपश्यद् भृशविक्षतम्। ततोऽवस्थाप्य राजेन्द्र कृतबुद्धिस्तवात्मजः॥ हर्षयन्निव तान् योधास्ततो वचनमब्रवीत्। न तं देशं प्रपश्यामि पृथिव्यां पर्वतेषु च॥ यत्र यातान्न वो हन्युः पाण्डवाः किं सृतेन वः।
en: The latter, however, fearlessly struck his foes with arrows. The prowess of your sons was exceedingly wonderful, since all the Pandavas together were unable to overcome him. At this time Duryodhana saw his troops, exceedingly mangled with shafts and about to fiy away. Rallying them then, O monarch, your son, resolved on battle battle and desirous of gladdening them, addressed those warriors saying "I do not see a place on plain or mountain whither if you fly, the Pandavas will not kill you! What use then in flight?

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: स्वल्पं चैव बलं तेषां कृष्णौ च भृशविक्षतौ॥ यदि सर्वेऽत्र तिष्ठामो ध्रुवं नो विजयो भवेत्।
en: The Pandava army has now been reduced to a small number. The two Krishna have been greatly wounded. If all of us make a stand here, we are sure to gain victory.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: विप्रयातांस्तु वो भिन्नान् पाण्डवाः कृतकिल्विषान्।। ५३ अनुसृत्य हनिष्यन्ति श्रेयोः न समरे वधः।
en: If, however, you fly away, the Pandavas, pursuing you, will slay you all. Death in battle, therefore, conduces to our good.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: सुखः सांग्रामिको मृत्युः क्षत्रधर्मेण युध्यताम्॥ मृतो दुःखं न जानीते प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते।
en: Death in the field of battle while fighting according to Kshatriya custom, is welcome. Such death begets no grief. By meeting with such a death, a person enjoys eternal happiness in the other world.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: शृण्वन्तु क्षत्रिया: सर्वे यावन्तोऽत्र समागताः॥ द्विषतो भीमसेनस्य वशमेष्यथ विद्रुताः। पितामहैराचरितं न धर्मं हातुमर्हथ॥
en: Let all the Kshatriyas assembled here me. It were better that they should submit to the angry Bhimasena than that they should neglect the duties practiced by them from the days of their fore-fathers.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: नान्यत् कर्मास्ति पापीयः क्षत्रियस्य पलायनात्। न युद्धधर्माच्छेयान् हि पन्थाः स्वर्गस्य कौरवाः॥
en: There is no act more sinful for a Kshatriya than to fly away from the battle-field. You Kauravas, there is no greater path to heaven than the duty of battle.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: सुचिरेणार्जिताँल्लोकान् सद्यो युद्धात् समश्रुते। तस्य तद् वचनं राज्ञः पूजयित्वा महारथाः॥ पुनरेवामभ्यवर्तन्त क्षत्रियाः पाण्डवान् प्रति। पराजयममृष्यन्तः कृतचित्ताश्च विक्रमे॥
en: The warrior acquires in a day the blissful regions of the other world that take many long years for others to acquire."-Obeying those words of the king, Kshatriya car-warriors once more rushed against the Pandavas, unable to put up with their discomfiture and firinly resolved to display their prowess.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं पुनरेव सुदारुणम्। तावकानां परेषां च देवासुररणोपमम्॥
en: Then began a battle once more that was highly terrific, between your troops and the enemy, that resembled the one between the gods and demons.

description: Account of the field after Karna's death-the joy of the Pandavas and the depression of the Kurus. Duryodhana rallies his army
sn: युधिष्ठिरपुरोगांश्च सर्वसैन्येन पाण्डवान्। अन्वधावन्महाराज पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव॥
en: Your son Duryodhana then, O monarch, with all his troops, rushed against the Pandavas with Yudhishthira at the head.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: संजय उवाच पतितान् रथनीडांश्च रथांश्चापि महात्मनाम्। रणे च निहतान् नागान् दृष्ट्वा पत्तींश्च मारिष॥ आयोधनं चातिघोरं रुद्रस्याक्रीड संनिभम्। अप्रख्याति गतानां तु राज्ञां शतसहस्रशः॥ विमुखे तव पुत्रे तु शोकोपहतचेतसि। भृशोद्विग्नेषु सैन्येषु दुःखं पार्थस्य विक्रमम्॥ ध्यायमानेषु सैन्येषु दुःखं प्राप्तेषु भारत! बलानां मथ्यमानानां श्रुत्वा निनदमुत्तमम्॥ अभिज्ञानं नरेन्द्राणां विक्षतं प्रेक्ष्य संयुगे। कृपाविष्टः कृपो राजन् वयः शीलसमन्वितः॥ अब्रवीत् तत्र तेजस्वी सोऽभिसृत्य जनाधिपम्। दुर्योधनं मन्युवशाद् वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः॥ दुर्योधन निबोधेदं यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि कौरव। श्रुत्वा कुरु महाराज यदि ते रोचतेऽनघ॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding the boxes of cars as also the cars of great warriors and the elephants and footsoldiers, O king, killed in battle-seeing the field of battle appear dreadful like the sporting ground of Rudra-seeing the ignominious death obtained by hundreds and thousands of kings-seeing also the prowess of Partha after the retreat of your son with a sorrowful heart and when your troops, filled with anxiety and fallen into great distress, O Bharata, were deliberating about their next course, hearing also the loud lamentations of the Kaurava warriors that were being smitten and marking the displaced and disordered tokens of great kings, the energetic, old, eloquent and compassionate Kuru leader Kripa, approached king Duryodhana and angrily said to him:-"O Duryodhana, listen, O Bharata, to these words. Having them, O monarch, act according to them, O sinless one, if you like.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: न युद्धधर्माच्छेयान् वै पन्था राजेन्द्र विद्यते। यं समाश्रित्य युद्ध्यन्ते क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रियर्षभ॥
en: There is no path, O monarch, that is better than the duty of battle, Taking recourse to that path, Kshatriyas, O best of Kshatriyas, fight.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: पुत्रो भ्राता पिता चैव स्वस्रीयो मातुलस्तथा। सम्बन्धिबान्धवाश्चैव योद्ध्या वै क्षत्रजीविना॥
en: He who follows Kshatriya practices, fights with son, father, brother, sister son and maternal uncle and relatives and kinsmen.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: वधे चैव परो धर्मस्तथाधर्मः पलायने। ते स्म घोरां समापन्ना जीविका जीवितार्थिनः॥
en: If he is killed in battle, there is great merit in it. Similarly, there is great sin if he flies from the field. It is for this that the life of a Kshatriya is exceedingly hard.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: तदत्र प्रतिवक्ष्यामि किंचिदेव हितं वचः। हते भीष्मे च द्रोणे च कर्णे चैव महारथे॥ जयद्रथे च निहते तव भ्रातृषु चनाघ! लक्ष्मणे तव पुत्रे च किं शेषं पर्युपासते॥
en: I will say a few wholesome words to you about this. After the fall of Bhishma and Drona and the mighty car-warrior Karna, after the slaughter of Jayadratlia and your brothers, O sinless one and your son Lakshmana, what is there now for us to do?

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: येषु भारं समासाद्य राज्ये मतिमकुर्महि। ते संत्यज्य तनूर्याताः शूरा ब्रह्मविदां गतिम्॥
en: They, upon whom we had laid all burdens and been enjoying the kingdoin, have all repaired to regions of blessedness attainable by persons conversant with the knowledge of Brahma, casting off their bodies.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: वयं त्विह विना भूता गुणवद्भिर्महारथैः। कृपणं वर्तयिष्याम पातयिता नृपान् बहून्।१४।।
en: As regards ourselves, deprived of those great car-warriors of numerous accomplishments, we shall have to pass our time in sorrow, having caused many kings to die.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: सर्वैरथ च जीवद्भिभित्सुरापराजितः। कृष्णनेत्रो महाबाहुर्देवैरपि दुरासदः॥
en: When all those heroes were alive even then Vibhatsu could not be defeated. Having Krishna, for his cyes, that mighty armed hero is incapable of being defeated by the very gods!

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: इन्द्रकार्मुकतुल्याभमिन्द्रकेतुमिवोच्छ्रितम्। निरं केतुमासाद्य संचचाल महाचमूः॥
en: The vast Kaurava army, approaching his monkey-emblem standard that is high as Indra's pole set up in the spring and that is cffulgent as Indra's bow, has always shaken in fear.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: सिंहनादाच भीमस्य पाञ्चजन्यस्वेनन च। गाण्डीवस्य च निर्घोषात् सम्मुह्यन्ते मनांसि नः॥
en: At the leonine shouts of Bhimasena and the blare of Panchajanya and the twang of Gandiva, our hearts will be paralyzed.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: चरन्तीव महाविद्युन्मुष्णन्ती नयनप्रभाम्। अलातमिव चाविद्धं गाण्डीवं समदृश्यत॥
en: Moving like flashes of lighting and closing our eyes Arjuna's Gandiva is seen to resemble a circle of fire.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: जाम्बूनदविचित्रं च धूयमानं महद् धनुम्। दृश्यते दिक्षु सर्वासु विद्युदभ्रघनेष्विव॥
en: Adorned with pure gold, that bow, as it is shaken, looks like lightning moving about on all directions.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: श्वेताश्च वेगसम्पन्ना शशिकाशसमप्रभाः। पिबन्त इव चाकाशं रथे युक्तान्तु वाजिनः॥
en: Quick-coursing and white horses endued with the splendour of the Moon or the Kusha grass, that run as if devouring the skies, are yoked to his car.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: उह्यमानांश्च कृष्णेन वायुनेव बलाहकाः। जाम्बूनदविचित्राङ्गा वहन्ते चार्जुनं रणे॥
en: Urged on by Krishna, like masses of clouds driven by the wind and decked with golden trappings, they hear Arjuna to battle.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: तावकं तद् बलं राजनर्जुनोऽस्त्रविशारदः। गहनं शिशिरापाये ददाहाग्निरिवोल्बणः॥
en: That foremost of warriors, Arjuna, burnt that great force of yours like a rising fire consuming dry grass in the forest in the winter.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: गाहमानमनीकानि महेन्द्रसदृशप्रभम्। धनंजयमपश्याम चतुर्दष्ट्रमिव द्विपम्॥
en: Possessed of the splendour of Indra himself, while penetrating into our army we have seen Dhananjaya look like an elephant with four tusks.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: विक्षोभयन्तं सेनां ते त्रासयन्तं च पार्थिवान्। धनंजयमपश्याम नलिनीमिव कुञ्जरम्॥
en: While agitating your army and terrorizing the kings we have seen Dhananjaya resemble an elephant agitating a lake full of lotuses.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: त्रासयन्तं तथा योधान् धनुघोषेण पाण्डवम्। भूय एनमपश्याम सिंह मृगगणानिव॥
en: While terrifying all the warriors with the twang of his bow, we have again seen the son of Pandu resemble a lion striking terror to sinaller aniinals.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: सर्वलोकमहेष्वासौ वृषभौ सर्वधन्विनाम्। आमुक्तकवचौ कृष्णौ लोकमध्ये विचेरतुः॥
en: Those two foremost of bowinen in all the worlds, viz., the two Krishnas clad in mail, are looking highly beautiful.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: अद्य सप्तदशाहानि वर्तमानस्य भारत। संग्रामस्यातिघोरस्य वध्यतां चाभितो युधि॥ ते
en: Today is the seventeenth day of this dreadful battle, O Bharata, of those that are being killed in the midst of this fight.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: वायुनेव विधूतानि तव सैन्यानि सर्वतः। शरदम्भोदजालानि व्यशीर्यन्त समन्ततः॥
en: The diverse detachments of your army are routed and dispersed like autumnal clouds scattered by the wind.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: तां नावमिव पर्यस्ता वातधूतां महार्णवे। तव सेनां महाराज सव्यसाची व्यकम्पयत्॥
en: Savyasachin, O monarch, made your army tremble and reel like a boat exposed to danger by a storm on the bosom of the ocean.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: क्व नु ते सूतपुत्रोऽभूत् क्व न द्रोण: सहानुगः। अहं क्व च क्व चात्मा ते हादिक्यश्च तथा क्व नु॥
en: Where was the Suta's son, where was, I, where were you, where was Hridika's son, where your brother Dussasana accompanied by his brothers, when Jayadratha was slain?

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: दुःशासनश्च भ्राता भ्रातृभिः सहितः क्व नु। बाणगोचरसम्प्राप्तं प्रेक्ष्य चैव जयद्रथम्॥ सम्बन्धिनस्ते भ्रातूंश्च सहायान् मातुलांस्तथा। सर्वान् विक्रम्य मिषतो लोकमाक्रस्य मूर्धनि।॥ जयद्रथो हतो राजन्किं नु शेषमुपास्महे। को हीह स पुमानस्ति यो विजेष्यति पाण्डवम्॥
en: Upon holding Jayadratha and finding him within the range of his arrows, Arjuna, displaying his prowess upon all your kinsmen and brothers and allies and maternal uncles and placing his feet upon their heads, killed king Jayadratha before us all. What then is there for us to do now? Who is there among your troops now that would defeat the son of Pandu?

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: तस्य चास्त्राणि दिव्यानि विविधानि महात्मनः। गाण्डीवस्य न निर्घोषो धैर्याणि हरते हि नः॥
en: Thai high-souled warrior is a master of many sorts of celestial weapons. The twang, of Gandiva, deprives us of our energies.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: नष्टचन्द्रा यथा रात्रि: सेनेयं हतनायका। नागभग्नद्रुमा शुष्का नदीवाकुलतां गता॥
en: This army of yours that is now without a leader is like a night without the Moon or like a river that is dried up with all the trees on its banks broken by elephants.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: ध्वजिन्यां हतनेत्रायां यथेष्टं श्वेतवाहनः। चरिष्यति महाबाहुः कक्षेष्वग्निरिव ज्वलन्॥
en: The mighty-armed Arjuna of white horses will, at his pleasure, move about amidst your army having no commander, like a blazing fire amid a heap of grass.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: सात्यकेश्चैव यो वेगो भीमसेनस्य चोभयोः। दारयेच गिरीन् सर्वाशोषयेचैव सागरान्॥
en: The vigour of those two, viz., Satyaki and Bhimasena, would rend all the mountains or dry up all the oceans!

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: उवाच वाक्यं यद् भीमः सभामध्ये विशाम्पते। कृतं तत् सफलं तेन भूयश्चैव करिष्यति॥
en: The words that Bhima spoke in the midst of the assembly have all been nearly fulfilled by him, O monarch. That which remains unaccomplished will again be accomplished by him.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: प्रमुखस्थे तदा कर्णे बलं पाण्डवरक्षितम्। दुरासदं तदा गुप्तं व्यूढं गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: While Karna was fighting with the unconquerable ariny of the Pandavas, it was vigorously protected by the wilder of Gandiva.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: युष्माभिस्तानि चीर्णानि यान्यसाधूनि साधुषु। अकारणकृतान्येव तेषां वः फलमागतम्॥
en: You have done many misdeeds without any cause, by the righteous Pandavas. The fruits of those acts have now come.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: आत्मनोऽर्थे त्वया लोको यत्नतः सर्व आहृतः। स ते संशायितस्तात आत्मा वै भरतर्षभ॥
en: For Accomplishing your own object you had, with great care, mustered together a large force. That huge force as also yourself, O best of Bharatas, have fallen into great danger.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: रक्ष दुर्योधनात्मानमात्मा सर्वस्य भाजनम्। भिन्ने हि भाजने तात दिशो गच्छति तद्गतम्॥
en: Preserve your own self now, for self in the stay of everything. If the support is broken, O sire, everything attached thereto is scattered on every side.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: हीयमानेन वै सन्धिः पर्येष्टव्यः समेन वा। विग्रहो वर्धमानेन मतिरेषा बृहस्पतेः॥
en: He that is being weakened should seek peace by conciliation. He that is prosperous should make war. This is the policy taught by Brihaspati.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: ते वयं पाण्डुपुत्रेभ्यो हीना स्म बलशक्तितः। तदत्र पाण्डवैः सार्धं सन्धिं मन्ये क्षमं प्रभो॥
en: We are now inferior to the sons of Pandu as regards the strength of our army. Therefore, O lord, I think peace with the Pandavas is conducive to our good.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: न जानीते हि यः श्रेयः श्रेयसश्चावमन्यते। स क्षिप्रं भ्रश्यते राज्यान च श्रेयोऽनुविन्दते॥
en: He that does not know what is for his good or knowing disregards what is for his good, is soon deprived of his kingdom and never obtains any good.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: प्रणिपत्य हि राजानं राज्यं यदि लभेमहि। श्रेयः स्यान्न तु मौढ्येन राजन् गन्तुः पराभवम्॥
en: If by submission to king Yudhishthira we may still have the kingdom even that would be for our good and not O king, to suffer through folly defeat at the hand of the Pandavas.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: वैचित्रवीर्यवचनात् कृपाशीलो युधिष्ठिरः। विनियुञ्जीत राज्ये त्वां गोविन्दवचनेन त॥
en: Yudhishthira is merciful. At the request of Vichitravirya's son and of Govinda, he will allow you to be the king.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: यद् ब्रूयाद्धि हृषीकेशो राजानमपराजितम्। अर्जुनं भीमसेनं च सर्वे कुर्यरसंशयम्॥
en: Whatever Hrishikesha will say to the victorious king Yudhishthira and Arjuna and Bhimasena, all of them will, forsooth, obey.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: नातिक्रमिष्यते कृष्णो वचनं कौरवस्य तु। धृतराष्ट्रस्य मन्येऽहं नापि कृष्णस्य पाण्डवः॥
en: Krishna will not, I think, be able to disobey the words of Dhritarashtra of Kuru's race, nor will the son of Pandu be able to disregard those of Krishna.

description: Kripa asks Duryodhana to make peace
sn: एतत् क्षेममहं मन्ये न च पार्थेश्च विग्रहम्। न त्वां ब्रवीमि कार्पण्यान प्राणपरिरक्षणात्॥ पथ्यं राजन् ब्रवीमि त्वां तत्परासुः स्मरिष्यसि। इति वृद्धो विलप्यैतत् कृपः शारद्वतो वचः। दीर्घमुष्णं च निःश्वस्य शुशोच च मुमोह च॥
en: The end of hostilities with the sons of Pritha is what I consider to be for your good, I do not say this to you from any mean motives nor for saving my life. I say, king, that which I think beneficial. You will recollect these words when no the verge of death if you neglect them now. Old Kripa, the son of Sharadvata, weepingly said these words. Breathing hard breaths, he was beside himself with sorrow.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्तस्ततो राजा गौतमेन तपस्विना। निःश्वस्य दीर्घमुष्णं च तूष्णीमासीद् विशाम्पते॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus addressed by the famous son of Gotama, the king Duryodhana, breathing hard, remained silent, O king.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: ततो मुहूर्तं स ध्यात्वा धार्तराष्ट्रो महामनाः। कृपं शारद्वतं वाक्यमित्युवाच परंतपः॥
en: Having thought for a little while, the great son of Dhritarashtra, that scorcher of foes, then said these words to Sharadvat's son Kripa-

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: यत् किञ्चित् सुहृदा वाच्यं तत् सर्वं श्रावितो ह्यहम्। कृतं च भवता सर्वं प्राणान् संत्यज्य युध्यता॥
en: "You have said to me whatever a friend should say. You have also, whilst fighting, done everything for ine, without caring for your very life.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: गाहमानमनीकानि युध्यमानं महारथैः। पाण्डवैरतितेजोभिर्लोकस्त्वामनुदृष्टवान्॥
en: People have seen you enter into the midst of the Pandavas army and fight with the mighty and energetic car-warriors of the Pandavas.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: सुहृदां यदिदं वाक्यं भवता श्रावितो ह्यहम्। न मां प्रीणाति तत्सर्वं मुमूर्षोरिव भेषजम्॥
en: What a friend should say has been said by you. Your words, however, do not please me like medicine that pleases not the person who is no the verge of death.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: हेतुकारणसंयुक्तं हितं वचनमुत्तमम्। उच्यमानं महाबाहो न मे विप्राय रोचते॥
en: These beneficial and excellent words, pregnant with reason, which you, O mightyarmed one, have said, do not scem acceptable to me, O foremost of Brahmanas.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: राज्याद् विनिकृतोऽस्माभिः कथं सोऽस्मासु विश्वसेत्। अक्षयूते च नृपतिर्जितोऽस्माभिर्महाधनः॥
en: Deprived by us of his kingdom on a former occasion, why will the son of Pandu trust us? That great king was once defeated by us at dice. Why will we again believe my words?

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: स कथं मम वाक्यानि श्रद्दध्याद् भूय एव तु। तथा दौत्येन सम्प्राप्तः कृष्णः पार्थहिते रतः॥
en: So also, Krishna, ever engaged in the good of the Parthas, when he came to us as an emissary, was cheated by us. Our act was exceedingly unfair. Why then, will Hrishikesha trust my words?

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: प्रलब्धश्च हृषीकेशस्तच कर्माविचारितम्। स च मे वचनं ब्रह्मन् कथमेवाभिमन्यते॥
en: The princess Krishna, while standing in the midst of the assembly, wept piteously. Krishna will never forget that act of ours, nor, the deprivation of Yudhishthira by us of his kingdom.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: विललाप च यत् कृष्ण सभामध्ये समेयुषी। न तन्मर्षयते कृष्णो न राज्यहरणं तथा॥
en: Formerly it was heard by us that the two Krishnas are of the same mind and are firmly attached to each other. Today, O lord, we have seen it with our eyes.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: एकप्राणावुभौ कृष्णावन्योन्यमभिसंश्रितौ। पुरा यच्छ्रुतमेवासीदद्य पश्यामि तत् प्रभो॥ स्वस्रीयं निहतं श्रुत्वा दुःखं स्वपिति केशवः। कृतागसो वयं तस्य स मदर्थं कथं क्षमेत्॥
en: Having heard of the death of his sister's son, Keshava passes his nights in sorrow. We have offended him highly. Why will he forgive us then?

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: आभिमन्योर्विनाशेन न शर्म लभतेऽर्जुनः। स कथं मद्धिते यत्नं प्रकरिष्यति याचितः॥
en: Arjuna also, in consequence of Abhimanyu's death, has become very miserable. Even if requested, why will he try for iny good?

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: मध्यमः पाण्डवस्तीक्ष्णो भीमसेनो महाबलः। प्रतिज्ञातं च तेनोग्रं भज्येतापि न संनमेत्॥
en: The second son of Pandu, Bhimascna, is highly powerful. He has taken a terrible vow. He will break but not bend.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: उभौ तौ बद्धनिस्त्रिंशावुभौ चाबद्धकङ्कटौ। कृतवैराबुभौ वीरौ यमावपि यमोपमौ॥
en: The heroic twins, cherishing hostility against us, when clad in mail and armed with their swords, resemble a pair of Yamas.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: धृष्टद्युम्न: शिखण्डी च कृतवैरौ मया सहा तौ कथं मद्धिते यत्नं कुर्यातां द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna and Shikhandin have taken up their swords against me. Why will those two, O best of Brahmanas, try for my good?

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: दुःशासनेन यत् कृष्ण एकवस्त्रा रजस्वलाः। परिक्लिष्टा सभामध्ये सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Clad in onc piece of cloth and in her scason, the princess Krishna was treated cruelly by Dushasana in the midst of the assembly and before all.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: तथा विवसनां दीनां स्मरत्वद्यापि पाण्डवाः। न निवारयितुं शक्याः संग्रामात्ते परंतपाः॥
en: Those scorchers of focs, the Pandavas, who still remember the naked Draupadi greatly distressed, can never be dissuaded from batile.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: यदा च द्रौपदी क्लिष्टा मद्विनाशाय दुःखिता। स्थण्डिले नित्यदा शेते यावद् वैरस्य यातनम्।॥ उग्रं तेपे तपः कृष्णा भर्तृणामर्थसिद्धये।
en: Then again, Krishna, the daughter of Drupada, is, with great difficulty, practising the austerest of penances for my destruction and the success of her husbands and sleeps every day on the bare ground, intending to do so till the end of the hostilities is got at.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: निक्षिप्य मानं दर्प च वासुदेवसहोदरा॥ कृष्णायाः प्रेष्यवद् भूत्वा शुश्रूषां कुरुते सदा।
en: Casting off honour and pride, the sister of Vasudeva, Subhadra, is always serving Draupadi like a waiting woman.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: इति सर्वं समुन्नद्धं न निर्वाति कथञ्चन॥ अभिमन्योर्विनाशेन स संधेयः कथं मया।
en: Everything, therefore, is on fire. That fire can never be extinguished. Peace with them is impossible on account of the death of Abhimanyu.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: कथं च राजा भुक्त्वेमां पृथिवीं सागराम्बराम्॥ पाण्डवानां प्रसादेन भोक्ष्ये राज्यमहं कथम्।
en: Having reigned as the sovereign of this Earth bounded by the ocean, how shall I be able to enjoy, by the favor of the Pandavas, a kingdom in peace?

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: उपर्युपरि राज्ञां वै ज्वलित्वा भास्करो यथा॥ युधिष्ठिरं कथं पश्यादनुयास्यामि दासवत्।
en: Having spread rays like the sun upon the heads of all the kings, how shall I walk behind Yudhishthira as slave?

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: कथं भुक्त्वा स्वयं भोगान् दत्त्वा दायांश्च युप्कलान्॥ कृपणं वर्तयिष्यामि कृपणैः सह जीविकाम्।
en: Having enjoyed all luxuries and shown cat mercy, how shall I lead a miserable life now with wretched men as my companions?

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: नाभ्यसूयामि ते वाक्यमुक्तं स्निग्धं हितं त्वया॥ न तु सन्धिमहं मन्ये प्राप्तकालं कथञ्चन।
en: I do not disapprove those mild and wholesome words you have spoken. I, however do not think that this is the time for peace.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: सुनीतमनुपश्यामि सुयुद्धेन परंतप॥ नायं कीबयितुं कालः संयोद्धं काल एव नः।
en: A righteous fight is, O scorcher of foes, is regarded by me to be a good policy. This is not the time for acting like a eunuch. On the other hand, this is the time for fighting.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: इष्टं मे बुहभिर्यज्ञैर्दत्ता विप्रेषु दक्षिणाः॥ प्राप्ता: कामाः श्रुता वेदाः शत्रूणां मूर्ध्नि च स्थितम्।
en: I have celebrated many sacrifices. I have given away presents to Brahmanas. I have achieved all my wishes. I have listened to the recitation of the Vedas. I have saved the heads of my foes.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: भृत्या मे सुभृतास्तात दीनश्चाभ्युद्धतो जनः॥ नोत्सहेऽद्य द्विजश्रेष्ठ पाण्डवान् वक्तुमीदृशम्।
en: My servants have all been well cared for by me. I have relieved people in distress. I dare not, O foremost of men, speak such humble words to the Pandavas.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: जितानि परराष्ट्रानि स्वराष्ट्रमनुपालितम्॥ भुक्ताश्च विविधा भोगास्त्रिवर्ग: सेवितो मया। पितॄणां गतमानृण्यं क्षत्रधर्मस्य चोभयोः॥
en: I have conquered foreign kingdoms. I have properly guverned by own kingdom. I have enjoyed various luxuries. I have pursued religion, profit and desire. I have paid off my debt to the departed manes and to Kshatriya duty.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: न ध्रुवं सुखमस्तीति कुतो राष्ट्रं कुतो यशः। इह कीर्तिर्विधातव्या सा च युद्धेन नान्यथा॥
en: Indeed, there is no happiness on this earth. What becomes of kingdom and what of good name? Fame is all that one should acquire here. That fame can be acquired by battle and by no other means.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: गृहे यत् क्षत्रियस्यापि निधनं तद् विगर्हितम्। अधर्मः सुमहानेष यच्छय्यामरणं गृहे॥
en: The death a Kshatriya meets with at home is blamcable. Death on one's bed at home is highly sinful.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: अरण्ये यो विमुच्येत संग्रामे वा तनुं नरः। ऋतूनादृत्य महतो महिमानं स गच्छति॥
en: The man, who casts off his body in the forest or in battle after having performed sacrifices, attains great glory.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: कृपणं विलपन्ना” जरयाभिपरिप्लुतः। म्रियते रुद्रतां मध्ये ज्ञातीनां न स पूरुषः॥
en: He is no man who dies miserably crying in agony, afflicted by disease and decay in the midst of crying kinsmen.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: त्यक्त्वा तु विविधान् भोगान् प्राप्तानां परमां गतिम्। अपीदानीं सुयुद्धेन गच्छेयं यत्सलोकताम्॥ शूराणामार्यवृत्तानां संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्। धीमतां सत्यसंघानां सर्वेषां ऋतुयाजिनाम्॥ शस्त्रावभृथपूतानां ध्रुवं वासस्त्रिविष्टपे। मुदा नूनं प्रपश्यन्ति युद्धे ह्यप्सरसां गणाः॥ पश्यन्ति नूनं पितरः पूजितान् सुरसंसदि। अप्सरोभिः परिवृतान् मोदमानांस्त्रिविष्टपे॥
en: Abandoning various objects of enjoyment, I shall now, by a righteous battle, repair to the regions of Shakra, obtaining the companionship of those that have attained to the highest end. Forsooth, that is the habitation of pious heroes, who never retreat from battle, who are intelligence and devoted to truth and who celebrate sacrifices, who took bath in the current of weapons, they always reside in the heaven The various divisions of Apsaras, forsooth, look with joy at such heroes when engaged in battle. Forsooth, the Pitris behold them adored in the assembly of the gods and rejoicing in heaven, in the company of Apsaras.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: पन्थानममरैर्यान्तं शूरैश्चैवानिवर्तिभिः। अपि तत्संगतं मार्ग वयमध्यारुहेमहि॥ पितामहेन वृद्धेन तथाऽऽचार्येण धीमता। जयद्रथेन कर्णेन तथा दुःशासनेन च॥
en: We will now ascend the path that is trod by the celestials and by heroes who never retreat from battle, the path followed by our venerable grandfather, by the highly intelligent preceptor, by Jayadratha, by Karna and by Dushasana.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: घटमाना मदर्थेऽस्मिन् हताः शूरा जनाधिपाः। शेरते लोहिताक्ताङ्गा संग्रामे शरविक्षतः॥
en: Many brave kings, who tried their best for me in this battle, have been killed. Wounded with shafts and their limbs bathed in blood, they lie now on the nacked Earth.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: उत्तमास्त्रविदः शूरा यथोक्तक्रतुयाजिनः। त्यक्त्वा प्राणान् यथान्यायमिन्द्रसास्वधिष्ठिताः॥
en: Courageous and masters of weapons, those kings, who had performed sacrifices according to the scriptures, having given their lives in the discharge of their duties, have now become the inhabitants of Indra's region.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: तैः स्वयं रचितो मार्गो दुर्गमो हि पुनर्भवेत्। सम्पतद्भिर्महावेगैर्यास्यद्भिरिह सद्गतिम्॥
en: They have gone there. The road will once more become difficult on account of a number of heroes that will hurry along it for reaching that happy region.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: ये मदर्थे हता शूरास्तेषां कृतमनुस्मरन्। ऋणं तत् प्रतियुञ्जानो न राज्ये मन आदधे॥
en: Recollect with gratitude the deeds of those heroes that have died for me. I desire to satisfy my debt, instead of thinking of the kingdom.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: घातयित्वा वयस्यांश्च भ्रातृनथ पितामहान्। जीवितं यदि रक्षेयं लोको मां गर्हयेद् ध्रुवम्॥
en: If, having caused my friends and brothers and grandsires to be killed, I save my own life, people will undoubtedly blame me.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: कीदृशं च भवेद् राज्यं मम हीनस्य बन्धुभिः। सखिभिश्च विशेषेण प्रणिपत्य च पाण्डवम्॥
en: It will be useless for me to enjoy the kingdom, destitute of kinsmen and friends and well-wishers and submitting to the son of Pandu.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: सोऽहमेतादृशं कृत्वा जगतोऽस्य पराभवम्। सुयुद्धेन ततः स्वर्गं प्राप्स्यामि न तदन्यथा॥
en: I, who was the master of the universe, will now acquire heaven by fair fight. It will not be otherwise.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: एवं दुर्योधनेनोक्तं सर्वे सम्पूज्य तद्वचः। साधु साध्विति राजानं क्षत्रियाः सम्बभाषिरे॥
en: Thus addressed by Duryodhana, all the Kshatriyas praised that speech and cheered the king, saying-Well, Well!

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: पराजयमशोचन्तः कृतचित्ताश्च विक्रमे। सर्वे सुनिश्चिता योद्धमुदग्रमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: Without at all grieving for their defeat and firmly bent upon displaying their prowess, all of them, prepared for fight, became enthusiastic.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: ततो वाहान् समाश्वस्य सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः। ऊने द्वियोजने गत्वा प्रत्यतिष्ठन्त कौरवाः॥
en: Having given their horses to the syces, the Kauravas, delighting at the prospect of battle, lived (for the night) at a spot little less than two Yojanas in distance from the field.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: आकाशे विद्रुमे पुण्ये प्रस्थे हिमवतः शुभे। अरुणां सरस्वतीं प्राप्य पपुः सस्नुश्च ते जलम्॥ तव पुत्रकृतोत्साहाः पर्यवर्तन्त ते ततः।
en: Having reached the Sarasvati of red waters on the sacred and beautiful table-land at the foot of the Himalaya, they bathed in that water and satisfied their thirst with it. Excited by your son, they halted there.

description: Duryodhana's reply to Kripa and his unwillingness to make peace. His army takes rest
sn: पर्यवस्थाप्य चात्मानमन्योन्येन पुनस्तदा। सर्वे राजन् न्यवर्तन्त क्षत्रियाः कालचोदिताः॥
en: Once more rallying themselves, all the Kshatriyas, O king, urged by destiny waited there.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: संजय उवाच अथ हैमवते प्रस्थे स्थित्वा युद्धाभिनन्दिनः। सर्व एव महायोधास्तत्र तत्र समागताः॥
en: Sanjaya said On that table-land at the foot of the Himavat, those heroes, O king, joyous at the prospect of battle and assembled together, passed the night.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: शल्यश्च चित्रसेनश्च शकुनिश्च महारथः। अश्वत्थामा कृपश्चैव कृतवर्मा च सात्वतः॥ सुषेणोऽरिष्टसेनश्च धृतसेनश्च वीर्यवान्। जयत्सेनश्च राजानस्ते रात्रिमुषितास्ततः॥
en: Indeed, Shalya and Chitrasena and the powerful car warrior Shakuni and Ashvatthaman and Kripa and Kritavarman of the Satwata race and the energetic Sushena and Arishtasena and Dhritasena and Jayatsena and all those kings passed the night there.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: रणे कर्णे हते वीरे त्रासिता जितकाशिभिः। नालभशर्म ते पुत्रा हिमवन्तमृते गिरिम्॥
en: After the heroic Karna has been killed in battle, your sons, filled with fear by the Pandavas desirous of victory, did not obtain peace anywhere else than on the Himavat.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: तेऽब्रुवन् सहितास्तत्र राजानं शल्यसंनिधौ। कृतयत्ना रणे राजन् सम्पूज्य विधिवत्तदा॥
en: All of them then, O king, who were bent on fighting, duly worshipped the king and said to him, in the presence of Shalya, these words.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: कृत्वा सेनाप्रणेतारं परांस्त्वं योद्भुमर्हसि। येनाभिगुप्ता: संग्रामे जयेमासुहृदो वयम्॥
en: It becomes you to fight with the enemy, after having made some body the commander, protected by whom in battle we will defeat the enemies.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: ततो दुर्योधनः स्थित्वा रथे रथवरोत्तमम्। सर्वयुद्धविभावज्ञमन्तकप्रतिमं युधि॥
en: Then Duryodhana, without descending from his car, went to that foremost of carwarriors, that hero conversant with all the rules of battle, Ashvatthaman, who resembled the Destroyer himself in battle.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: स्वङ्गं प्रच्छन्नशिरसं कम्बुग्रीवं प्रियंवदम्। व्याकोशपद्मपत्राक्षं व्याघ्रास्यं मेरुगौरवम्॥ स्थाणोवृषस्य सदृशं स्कन्धनेत्रगतिस्वरैः। पुष्टश्लिष्टायतभुजं सुविस्तीर्णवरोरसम्॥ बले जवे च सदृशमरुणानुजवातयोः। आदित्यस्यार्चिषा तुल्यं बुद्ध्या चोशनसा समम्॥ कान्तिरूयमुखैश्वर्यस्त्रिभिश्चन्द्रमसा समम्। काञ्चनोपलसंघातैः सदृशं श्लिष्टसंधिकम्॥ सुवृत्तोरुकटीजङ्घ सुपादं स्वङ्गुलीनखम्। स्मृत्वा स्मृत्वैव तु गुणान् धात्रा यत्नाद् विनिर्मितम्।।
en: Having beautiful limbs, well-covered head, a neck adorned with three lines like those in a conch-shell, sweet speech, eyes resembling the petals of a full-blown lotus and tiger-like face, the dignity of Meru, resembling the full of Mahadeva in neck, eyes, tread and voice, having huge, inassive and well-joined arms, having broad and well-formed chest, equal unto Garuda in speed and might, effulgent like the Sun, intelligent like Ushanas himself, beautiful like the Moon, having a body that seemed to be made of a number of golden lotuses, well-made joints, well-formed thighs and waist and hips, beautiful feet, beautiful fingers and beautiful nails, he seemed to have been made by Brahma with great care after remembering one after another all the beautiful and good attributes of creation.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नं निपुणं श्रुतिसागरम्। जेतारं तरसारीणामजेयमरिभिर्बलात्॥
en: Gifted with auspicious marks and clever in every act, he was an ocean of learning. Speedily vanquishing his enemies, he was incapable of being forcibly defeated by foes.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: दशाङ्गं यश्चतुष्पादमिष्वस्त्रं वेद तत्त्वतः। साङ्गांस्तु चतुरो वेदान् सम्यगाख्यानपञ्चमान्॥
en: He knew, in full, the science of war consisting of four padas and ten Angas. He knew also thc four Vedas with all their branches and the Akhyanas as the fifth.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: आराध्य त्र्यम्बकं यत्नाद् व्रतैरुपैर्महातपाः। अयोनिजायामुत्पन्नो द्रोणेनायोनिजेन यः॥
en: Possessed of great ascetic merit, Drona, himself not born of woman, having worshipped the three-eyed deity with care and penances, beget him upon a wife not born of woman.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: तमप्रतिमकर्माणं रूपेणाप्रतिमं भुवि। पारगं सर्वविद्यानां गुणार्णवमनिन्दितम्॥ तमभ्येत्यात्मजस्तुभ्यमश्वत्थामानमब्रवीत्। यं पुरस्कृत्य सहिता युधि जेष्याम पाण्डवान्॥ गुरुपुत्रोऽद्य सर्वेषामस्माकं परमा गतिः। भवांस्तस्मान्नियोगात्ते कोऽस्तु सेनापतिर्मम॥
en: Approaching him of incomparable deeds, he who is unrivalled in beauty on earth, he who has mastered all branches of learning, that occan of qualities, the faultless Ashvatthaman, your son said to him these words-. "O preceptor's son, you are today our highest refuge? Tell us, therefore, who should be the commander of my army now, placing whom at our head, all of us, united together, may defeat the Pandavas?"

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: द्रौणिरुवाच अयं कुलेन रूपेण तेजसा यशसा श्रिया। सर्वैर्गुणैः समुदितः शल्यो नोऽस्तु चमूपतिः॥ युद्धाय च मति
en: (Thus addressed) the son of Drona replied-"Let Shalya become the commander of our army. In birth, in prowess, in energy, in fame, in beauty and in every other accomplishment, he is superior.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: भागिनेयान् निजांस्त्यक्त्वा कृतज्ञोऽस्मानुपागतः। महासेनो महाबाहुर्महासेन इवापरः॥
en: Out of gratitude, he has joined us, having abandoned the sons of his own sister. Having a large army of his own, that mighty-armed one is like the second celestial generalissimo.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: एनं सेनापतिं कृत्वा नृपतिं नृपसत्तम। शक्यः प्राप्तुं जयोऽस्माभिर्देवैः स्कन्दमिवाजितम्॥२१
en: Making that king the commander of our army, O best of kings, we will be able to gain victory, like the celestials after making the invincible Skanda their commander.”

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: तथोक्ते द्रोणपुत्रेण सर्व एव नराधिपाः। परिवार्य स्थिताः शल्यं जयशब्दांश्च चक्रिरे॥ चक्रुरावेशं च परं ययुः।
en: On Drona's son saying these words all the kings stood, surrounding Shalya and cried victory to him. Determined for fighting, the felt great joy.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: ततो दुर्योधनो भूमौ स्थित्वा रथवरे स्थितम्॥ उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा द्रोणभीष्मसमं रणे।
en: Then Duryodhana, come down from his car, folded his hands and addressing Shalya, equal to Drona and Bhishma in battle, who was on his car, said these words.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: अयं स कालः सम्प्राप्तो मित्राणां मित्रवत्सल॥ यत्र मित्रममित्रं वा परीक्षन्ते बुधा जनाः।
en: "O You attached to friends, that time has arrived when intelligent men examine persons in the guise of friends as to whether they are true friends or not.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: स भवानस्तु न शूरः प्रणेता वाहिनीमुखे॥ रणं याते च भवति पाण्डवा मन्दचेतसः। भविष्यन्ति सहामात्यः पञ्चालाश्च निरुद्यमा:॥
en: Brave as you are do you become our commander-in-chief. When you will go to battle, the Pandavas, with their friends, will lose heart and the Panchalas will be depressed."

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: दुर्योधनवचः श्रुत्वा शल्यो मद्राधिपस्तदा। उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञो राजन् राजसंनिधौ॥
en: Hearing the words of Duryodhana, Shalya, the king of Madra, foremost of orators, said following words before the kings, O king!

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: यत्तु मां मन्यसे राजन् कुरुराज करोमि तत्। त्वत्प्रियार्थं हि मे सर्वं प्राणा राज्यं धनानि च॥
en: Shalya answered-"I will, O king of the Kurus, do what you desire me to do. My life, my kingdom, my wealth and everything else are at your disposal."

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच सैनापत्येन वरये त्वामहं मातुलातुलम्। सोऽस्मान् पाहि युधां श्रेष्ठ स्कन्दो देवानिवाहवे॥
en: Duryodhana said I wish you to accept the general-ship of my army. O maternal uncle, O foremost of warriors, protect us, even as Skanda protected the celestials in battle.

description: Ashvatthaman asks Duryodhana to make Shalya the commander and Duryodhana requests him accordingly
sn: अभिषिच्यस्व राजेन्द्र देवानामिव पावकिः। जहि शत्रून् रणे वीर महेन्द्रो दानवानिव॥
en: O foremost of kings, install yourself in the command as Pavakas's son Kartikeya was placed in the command of the celestial army. O hero, kill our foes in battle like Indra the Danavas.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: संजय उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचो राज्ञो मद्रराजः प्रतापवान्। दुर्योधन तदा राजन् वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing those words of the Kuru king, the brave king (Shalya), O king, said these words to him

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: दुर्योधन महाबाहो शृणु वाक्यविदां वर। यावतौ मन्यसे कृष्णो रथस्थौ रथिनां वरौ॥ न मे तुल्याबुभावेतौ वाहुवीर्ये कथंचन।
en: "O mighty-armed Duryodhana, listen to me, O foremost of orators. You consider the two Krishnas, when on their car, as the foremost of car-warriors. They are not, however, jointly equal to me in the strength of arms.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: उद्यतां पृथिवी सर्वा ससुरासुरमानवाम्॥ योधयेयं रणमुखे संक्रुद्धः किमु पाण्डवान्।
en: What shall I say of the Pandavas? When enraged, I can fight, at the van of battle, with the whole world consisting of the celestials, Asuras and men.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: विजेष्यामि रणे पार्थन् सोमकांश्च समागतान्॥ अहं सेनाप्रणेता ते भविष्यामि न संशयः।
en: I will defeat the assembled Parthas and the Somakas in battle. Forsooth, I will become the leader of your army.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: तं च व्यूहं विधास्यामि न तरिष्यन्ति यं परे॥ इति सत्यं ब्रवीम्येष दुर्योधन न संशयः।
en: I will form such an array that our enemies will not be able to discomfit it. Truly do I say this to you, O Duryodhana."

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: एवमुक्तस्ततो राजा मद्राधिपतिमञ्जसा॥ अभ्यपिञ्चत सेनाया मध्ये भरतसत्तम। विधिना शास्त्रदृष्टेन किष्टरूपो विशाम्पते।॥
en: Thus addressed (by Shalya), king Duryodhana joyfully poured sanctificd water, O best of the Bharatas, on the king of the Madras, in the midst of his soldiers, according to the rites ordained in the scriptures. O king.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: अभिषिक्ते ततस्तस्मिन् सिंहनादो महानभूत्। तव सैन्येऽभ्यवाद्यन्त वादित्राणि च भारत॥
en: After Shalya has been appointed the commander, leonine shouts arose among your soldiers and various musical instruments also, O Bharata, were struck.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: हृष्टाश्चासंस्तथा योधा मद्रकाश्च महारथाः। तुष्टुवुश्चैव राजानं शल्यमाहवशोभिनम्॥ जय राजंश्चिरञ्जीव जहि शत्रून् समागतान्। तव बाहुबलं प्राप्य धार्तराष्ट्रा महाबलाः॥ निखिलाः पृथिवी सर्वा प्रशासन्तु हतद्विषः।
en: The Kaurava warriors and the powerful carwarriors among the Madrakas became very cheerful. And all of them praised the royal Shalya, that ornament of battle, saying "Victory to you, O king! May you live long. Kill all the foes! Having obtained the strength of your arms, let the sons of Dhritarashtra, gifted with great strength, rule the wide Earth without an enemy.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: त्वं हि शक्तो रणे जेतुं ससुरासुरमानवान्॥ मर्त्यधर्माण इह तु किमु सृञ्जयसोमकान्।
en: You are capable of vanquishing in battle the three worlds consisting of the gods and Asuras, what to speak of the Somakas and the Shrinjayas."

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: एवं सम्पूज्यमानस्तु मद्राणामधिपो बली॥ हर्ष प्राप तदा वीरो दुरापमकृतात्मभिः।
en: Thus eulogised the power king of the Madrakas was filled with great joy that is unattainable by uncultured persons.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: शल्य उवाच अद्य चाहं रणे सर्वान् पञ्चालान् सह पाण्डवैः॥ निहनिष्यामि वा राजन् स्वर्ग यास्यामि वा हतः।
en: Shalya said Today, O King, I will either kill all the Panchalas with the Pandavas in battle or killed by them go to heaven.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: अद्य पश्यन्तु मां लोका विचरन्तमभीतवत्॥ अद्य पाण्डुसुताः सर्वे वासुदेवः ससात्यकिः। पञ्चालाश्चेदयश्चैव द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः॥ धृष्टद्युम्नः शिखण्डी च सर्वे चापि प्रभद्रकाः। विक्रमं मम पश्यन्तु धनुषश्च महद् बलम्॥ लाघवं चास्त्रवीर्यं च भुजयोश्च बलं युधि।
en: Let the world behold me today moving about fearlessly in the field; let all the sons of Pandu and Vasudeva and Satyaki and the sons of Draupadi and Dhristadyumna, Shikhandhin and all the Prabhadrakas, witness my powers, the great power of my bow, my quickness, the energy of my weapons and the strength of my arms in battle.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: अद्य पश्यन्तु मे पार्थाः सिद्धाश्च सह चारणैः॥ यादृशं मे बलं बाह्वोः सम्पदस्त्रेषु या च मे।
en: Let the Parthas and all the Siddhas with the Charanas, witness today the strength of my arms and the precious weapons I possess.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: अद्य मे विक्रमं दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवानां महारथाः॥ प्रतीकारपरा भूत्वा चेष्टन्तां विविधाः क्रियाः।
en: Witness my prowess to-day let the mighty car-warriors of the Pandavas, desirous of counteracting it, adopt various measures.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: अद्य सैन्यानि पाण्डूनां द्रावयिष्ये समन्ततः॥ द्रोणभीष्मावति विभो सूतपुत्रं च संयुगे। विचरिष्ये रणे युध्यन् प्रियार्थं तव कौरव॥
en: Today I will disperse the troops of the Pandavas on all sides. Excelling Drona and Bhishma and the son of Suta, O lord, in battle, I will move about the field, O Kourava, for doing what pleases you.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: संजय उवाच अभिषिक्ते तथा शल्ये तव सैन्येषु मानद। न कर्णव्यसनं किंचिन्मेनिरे तत्र भारत॥
en: Sanjaya said After Shalya had been appointed to the command, O giver of honours, no one among your soldiers, O foremost of Bharata's race, any longer felt sorrow for Karna.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: हृष्टाः सुमनसश्चैव बभूवुस्तत्र सैनिकाः। मेनिरे निहतान् पार्थान् मद्रराजवशं गतान्॥
en: Indeed your soldiers were filled with delight. They considered the Parthas as already slain and brought under the control of the king of Madras.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: प्रहर्षं प्राप्य सेना त तावकी भरतर्षभ। तां रात्रिमुषिता सुप्ता हर्षचित्ता च साभवत्॥
en: Delighted your soldiers, O best of Bharata's race, slept that night happily and became very cheerful.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: सैन्यस्य तव तं शब्दं श्रुत्वा राजा युधिष्ठिरः। वार्ष्णेयमब्रवीद् वाक्यं सर्वक्षत्रस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Hearing the war-cries of your army king Yudhishthira, addressing the Vrishni heroes, said these words, before all the Kshatriyas.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: मद्रराजः कृतः शल्यो धार्तराष्ट्रेण माधव। सेनापतिर्महेष्वासः सर्वसैन्येषु पूजितः॥
en: "The ruler of he Madras, Shalya, that great bowman who is highly respected by all the warriors, has, O Madhava, been appointed the commander of his forces of Dhritarashtra's son.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: एतज्ज्ञात्वा यथाभूतं कुरु माधव यक्षमम्। भवान् नेता च गोप्ता च विधत्स्व यदनन्तरम्॥
en: Knowing this, do, O Madhava, that which is beneficial. You are our leader and protector. Do what should next be done."

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: तमब्रवीन्महाराज वासुदेवो जनाधिपम्। आर्तायनिमहं जाने यथातत्त्वेन भारत॥
en: Then Vasudeva, O monarch, said to that king-"I know Artayani, O Bharata, as truly illustrious, powerful and energetic.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: वीर्यवांश्च महातेजा महात्मा च विशेषतः। कृती च चित्रयोधी च संयुक्तो लाघवेन च॥
en: He is accomplished, conversant with all the modes of warfare and possesses great lightness of hand.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: यादृग् भीष्मस्तथा द्रोणो यादृक् कर्णश्च संयुगे। तादृशस्तद्विशिष्टो वा मद्रराजो मतो मम॥
en: I think that the ruler of Madras is in battle equal to Bhishma or Drona or Karna or perhaps superior to them.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: युद्ध्यमानस्य तस्याहं चिन्तयानश्च भारत। योद्धारं नाधिगच्छामि तुल्यरूपं जनाधिप॥
en: O Bharata! O King of kings! My mind in course of searching in depth for the cominander of army, is not able to see any other warrior capable as Shalya in war-craft.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: शिखण्ड्यर्जुनभीमानां सात्वतस्य च भारत। धृष्टद्युम्नस्य च तथा बलेनाभ्यधिको रणे॥
en: In battle, he is superior in power to Shikhandin and Arjuna and Bhima and Satyaki and Dhrishtadyumna, O Bharata.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: मद्रराजो महाराज सिंहद्विरदविक्रमः। विचरिष्यत्यभीः काले कालः क्रुद्धः प्रजास्विव॥
en: The king of the Madras, O king, gifted with tlie prowess of a lion or an elephant, will move about fearlessly in battle, like the Destroyer himself enraged amongst creatures at the time of the universal dissolution.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: तस्याद्य न प्रपश्यामि प्रतियोद्धारमाहवे। त्वामृते पुरुषव्याघ्र शार्दूलसमविक्रमम्॥
en: I do not find a match for him in battle except you, O best of men, who are possessed of prowess equal to that of a tiger.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: सदेवलोके कृत्स्नेऽस्मिन् नान्यस्त्वत्तः पुमान् भवेत्। मद्रराजं रणे क्रुद्ध यो हन्यात् कुरुनन्दन॥
en: Except you there is no other person either in heaven or in the whole of this world, who, O best of Kurus, would be able to kill the king of the Madras while worked up with anger in battle.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: अहन्यहनि युध्यन्तं क्षोभयन्तं बलं तव। तस्माजहि रणे शल्यं मघवानिव शम्बरम्॥
en: Daily in fight, he agitates your troops. For this, kill Shalya in battle, like Mahgavan slaying Shambara.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: अजेयश्चाप्यसौ वीरो धार्तराष्ट्रेण सत्कृतः। तवैव हि जयो नूनं हते मद्रेश्वरे युधि॥ तस्मिन् हते हतं सर्वं धार्तराष्ट्रबलं महत्।
en: Honoured by Dhritarashtra's son, that hero is invincible in battle. When the king of the Madras will be killed in battle, you will surely win victory. Upon his slaughter, Dhritarashtra's huge army will be slain.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: एतच्छुत्वा महाराज वचनं मम साम्प्रतम्॥ प्रत्युद्याहि रणे पार्थ मद्रराजं महारथम्।
en: Hearing, O king, these words of mind now, proceed, O Partha, against that great carwarrior, the king of the Madras.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: जहि चैनं महाबाहो वासवो नमुचिं यथा॥ न चैवात्र दया कार्या मातुलोऽयं ममेति वै। क्षत्रधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य जहि मद्रजनेश्वरम्॥
en: Kill that hero, O you of great arms, like Vasava slaying the Asura Namuchi. There is no need of showing any compassion here, thinking that he is your maternal uncle. Observing the duties of a Kshatriya, slay the king of the Madras.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: द्रोणभीष्मार्णवं ती। कर्णपातालसम्भवम्। मा निमजस्व सगणः शल्यमासाद्य गोष्पदम्॥
en: Having crossed the fathomless represented by Bhishma and Drona and Karna, do not sink, with your followers, in a pit dug by a cow's hoop represented by Shalya. ocean

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: यच ते तपसो वीर्यं यच क्षात्रं बलं तव। तद् दर्शय रणे सर्वं जहि चैनं महारथम्॥
en: Display in battle the whole of your ascetic power and Kshatriya energy. Slay that carwarrior."

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं केशवः परवीरहा। जगाम शिविरं सायं पूज्यमानोऽथ पाण्डवैः॥
en: Having said these words, Keshava, that slayer of hostile heroes, went to his tent in the evening adored by the Pandavas.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: केशवे तु तदा याते धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। विसृज्य सर्वान् भ्रातूंश्च पञ्चालानथ सोमकान्॥ सुष्वाप रजनीं तां तु विशल्य इव कुञ्जरः।
en: After Keshava had departed the righteous king Yudhishthira, sending away all his brothers and the Somakas, happily slept that night, like an elephant from whose body the darts have been plucked out.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: ते च सर्वे महेष्वासाः पञ्चालाः पाण्डवास्तथा॥ कर्णस्य निधने हृष्टाः सुषुपुस्तां निशां तदा।
en: All those great bowmen, viz., the Panchalas and the Pandavas, delighted at the fall of Karna, slept that night happily.

description: Shalya accepts the command of the army
sn: गतज्वरं महेष्वासं तीर्णपारं महारथम्॥ बभूव पाण्डवेयानां सैन्यं च मुदितं नृप। सूतपुत्रस्य निधने जयं लब्ध्वा च मारिष॥
en: With their anxiety gone the army of the Pandavas, abounding with great bowmen and mighty car-warriors, having reached the shore as it were, became very happy that night on account of the victory, O sire, it had won by the destruction of Karna.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: संजय उवाच व्यतीतायां रजन्यां तु राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। अब्रवीत् तावकान् सर्वान् संनह्यन्तां महारथाः॥
en: Sanjaya said After the termination of the night king Duryodhana addressed all your soldiers, saying-Arm, you mighty car-warriors!

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: राज्ञश्च मतमाज्ञाय समनात सा चमूः। अयोजयन् रथांस्तूर्णं पर्यधावंस्तथा परे॥
en: Hearing the orders of the king, the warriors began to put on their armours. Some began to yoke horses to their card quickly, others ran about hither and thither.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: अकल्प्यन्त च मातङ्गा समनह्यन्त पत्तयः। रथानास्तरणोपेतांश्चक्रुरन्ये सहस्रशः॥
en: The elephants were also got ready. The infantry began to arm themselves. Thousands of attendants began to spread carpets on the cars.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: वादित्राणां च निनदः प्रादुरासीद् विशाम्पते। आयोधनार्थं योधानां बलानां चाप्युदीर्यताम्॥
en: The sound of musical instruments, O king, arose there, for exciting the war-like spirit of the soldiers.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: ततो बलानि सर्वाणि हतशिष्टानि भारत। प्रस्थितानि व्यदृश्यन्त मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्॥
en: Then all the troops, stationed in their proper posts, were seen, O Bharata, to stand, clad in mail and determined to die.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: शल्यं सेनापतिं कृत्वा मद्रराजं महारथाः। प्रविभज्य बलं सर्वमनीकेषु व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Having made the king of the Madras their leader, the great car-warriors, of the Kauravas, made detachments of their soldiers.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: तत: सर्वे समागम्य पुत्रेण तव सैनिकाः। कृपश्च कृतवर्मा च द्रौणिः शल्योऽथ सौबलः॥ अन्ये च पार्थिवाः शेषाः समयं चक्रुरादृताः। न न एकेन योद्धव्यं कथञ्चिदपि पाण्डवैः॥
en: Then all warriors, with Kripa and Kritavarman and Drona's son and Shalya, Subala's son and the other kings that were yet। alive, met your son and settled, that none of them would individually fight with the Pandavas.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: यो ह्येकः पाण्डवैर्युध्येद् यो वा युध्यन्तमुत्सृजेत्। स पञ्चभिर्भवेद् युक्तः पातकैचोपपातकैः॥ (अद्याचार्यसुतो द्रौणिर्नैको युध्येत शत्रुभिः।) अन्योन्यं परिरक्षद्भिर्योद्धव्यं सहितैश्च ह।
en: And they said-"He who will fight alone with the Pandavas or he that will leave a comrade engaged in fight, will be visited by the five grave and all the minor sins.”—–And they said-"Do not fight Ashvatthama alone, son of Drona. All of us, unitedly will fight with the enemy.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: एवं ते समयं कृत्वा सर्वे तत्र महारथाः॥ मद्रराजं पुरस्कृत्य तूर्णमभ्यद्रवन् परान्।
en: Having made this contact those great carworriers placed the king of the Madras at their head and speedily ran against their foes.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: तथैव पाण्डवा राजन् व्यूह्य सैन्यं महारणे॥ अभ्ययुः कौरवान् राजन् योत्स्यमानाः समन्ततः।
en: Similarly, all the Pandavas, having arranged their soldiers in that great battle, proceeded against the Kauravas, O king, fighting with them.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: तद् बलं भरतश्रेष्ठ क्षुब्धार्णवसमस्वनम्॥ समुद्धतार्णवाकारमुद्भूतरथकुञ्जरम्।
en: Soon, O chief of the Bharatas, that army, whose noise resembled that of the agitated ocean and which seemed wondrous for its cars and elephants, shone like the deep with heaving billows.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच द्रोणस्य चैव भीष्मस्य राधेयस्य च में श्रुतम्॥ पातनं शंस मे भूयः शल्यस्याथ सुतस्य मे।
en: Dhritarashtra said I have heard the fall of Drona, of Bhishma and the son of Radha. Tell me now of the fall of Shalya and of my son.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: कथं रणे हतः शल्यो धर्मराजेन संजय॥ भीमेन च महाबाहुः पुत्रो दुर्योधनो मम।
en: How, O Sanjaya, was Shalya killed by the . righteous king Yudhishthira? And how was my son Duryodhana slain by the powerful Bhimasena?

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: संजय उवाच क्षयं मनुष्यदेहानां तथा नागाश्वसंक्षयम्॥ शृणु राजन् स्थिरो भूत्वा संग्रामं शंसतो मम।
en: Sanjaya said Hear, O king, patiently of the destruction of human beings, elephants and horses as I describe the battle.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: आशा बलवती राजन् पुत्राणां तेऽभवत्तदा॥ हते द्रोणे च भीष्मे च सूतपुत्रे च पातिते। शल्यः पार्थान् रणे सर्वान् निहनिष्यति मारिष॥
en: O king, your sons became very sanguine that, after Drona and Bhishma and the Suta's son had been killed, Shalya would kill all the sons of Pritha in battle.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: तामाशां हृदये कृत्वा समाश्वस्य च भारत। मद्रराजं च समरे समाश्रित्य महारथम्॥ नाथवन्तं तदाऽऽत्मानममन्यन्त सुतास्तव।
en: Cherishing that hope in his heart and being comforted, O Bharata, your son Duryodhana, relying in battle upon that great car-carrier, the ruler of the Madras, thought himself as having a protector.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: यदा कर्णे हते पार्थाः सिंहनादं प्रचक्रिरे॥ तदा तु तावकान् राजन्नाविवेश महद् भयम्।
en: When after Karna's fall the Pandavas roared a great fear, O king, possessed the hearts of your sons.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: तान् समाश्वास्य योधास्तु मद्रराजः प्रतापवान्॥ व्यूह्य व्यूहं महाराज सर्वतोभद्रमृद्धिमत्। प्रत्युद्ययौ रणे पार्थान् मद्रराजः प्रतापवान्॥ विधुन्वन् कार्मुकं चित्रं भारघ्नं वेगवत्तरम्।
en: Assuring him the valiant king of the Madras, having formed, O king, a grand array, proceeded against the Parthas in battle. And the brave king of the Madras possessed, shaking his beautiful and strong bow capable of shooting arrows with great force.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: रथप्रवरमास्थाय सैन्धवाश्वं महारथः॥ तस्य सूतो महाराज रथस्थोऽशोभयद् रथम्।
en: And that mighty car-warrior drove an excellent car having horses of the Sindhu breed yoked to it. Riding upon his car, his driver made the car resplendent.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: स तेन संवृतो वीरो रथेनामित्रकर्षणः॥ तस्थौ शूरो महाराज पुत्राणां ते भयप्रणुत्।
en: Protected by that car, that hero, that brave destroyer of foes, stood, O king dissipating the fears of your sons.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: प्रयाणे मद्रराजोऽभून्मुखः व्यूहस्य दंशितः॥ मद्रकैः सिहतौ वीरैः कर्णपुत्रैश्च दुर्जयैः।
en: The king of the Madras, clad in mail, proceeded at the head of the army accompanied by the brave Madrakas and the invincible sons of Karna.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: सव्येऽभूत् कृतवर्मा च त्रिगर्तेः परिवारितः॥ गौतमो दक्षिणे पार्श्व शकैश्च यवनैः सह।
en: On the left stood Kritavarman, surrounded by the Trigartas. On the right was (Kripa) with the Sakas and the Yavanas.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: अश्वत्थामा पृष्ठतोऽभूत् काम्बोजैः परिवारितः॥ दुर्योधनोऽभवन्मध्ये रक्षितः कुरुपुङ्गवैः।
en: In the rear was Ashvathaman surrounded by the Kambojas. In the centre was Duryodhana, protected by the best of Kuru warriors.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: हयानीकेन महता सौबलश्चापि संवृतः॥ प्रययौ सर्वसैन्येन कैतव्यश्च महारथः।
en: Surrounded by a large army of cavalry and other troops, Subala's son, Sakuni, as also the great car-warrior, Uluka, proceeded with others.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: पाण्डवाश्च महेष्वासा व्यूह्य सैन्यमरिन्दमाः॥ विधा भूता महाराज तव सैन्यमुपाद्रवन्।
en: The great bowmen amongst the Pandavas, those chastisers of foes, dividing themselves, O king, into three divisions, rushed against your troops.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नः शिखण्डी च सात्यकिश्च महारथः॥ शल्यस्य वाहिनी हन्तुमभिदुद्रुवुराहवे।
en: Dhrishtadyumna and Shikhandin and the great car-warrior Satyaki proceeded quickly against the army of Shalya.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा स्वेनानीकेन संवृतः॥ शल्यमेवाभिदुद्राव जिघांसुर्भरतर्षभः।
en: Then king Yudhishthira, accompanied by his soldiers, rushed against Shalya alone, with a view to kill him, O best of Bharata's race.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: हादिक्यं च महेष्वाससमर्जुनः शत्रुसैन्यहा॥ संशप्तकगणांश्चैव वेगितोऽभिविदुद्रुवे।
en: Arjuna, the slayer of foes, rushed against that great bowman, Kritavarman and the Samsaptakas.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: गौतमं भीमसेनो वै सोमकाश्च महारथाः॥ अभ्यद्रवन्त राजेन्द्र जिघांसन्तः परान् युधि।
en: Bhimasena and the great car-warriors among the Somakas rushed, O monarch, against Kripa, desirous of killing their enemies in battle.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
sn: माद्रीपुत्रौ तु शकुनिमुलूकं च महारथम्॥ ससैन्यौ सहसैन्यौ तावुपतस्थतुराहवे।
en: The two sons of Madri, accompanied by their soldiers, proceeded against Sakuni and the great car-warrior Uluka at the head of their forces.

description: The arrangement of Kuru troops under Shalya and the preparation of both parties for a first battle
