en: Taking rest for this one night, I shall in the morning join you and fight with the enemy. There is no doubt about it.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्तोऽब्रवीद् द्रौणी राजानं युद्धदुर्मदम्। उत्तिष्ठ राजन् भद्रं ते विजेष्यामो वयं परान्॥
en: Sanjaya continued Thus addressed, the son of Drona replied to the king, who was invincible in battle, saying-"Rise up, O king, may you fare well. We shall yet defeat the enemy.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: इष्टापूर्तेन दानेन सत्येन च जयेन च। शपे राजन् यथा ह्यद्य निहनिष्यामि सोमकान्॥
en: I swear by all my holy acts, by all the gifts I have made, by truth itself and by my meditations, O king, that I shall today kill the Somakas.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: मा स्म यज्ञकृतां प्रातिमाप्नुयां सज्जनोचिताम्। यदीमां रजनी व्युष्टां न हि हन्मि परान् रणे॥
en: Indeed I shall not enjoy the pleasure of performing sacrifices, a pleasure which is enjoyed by all pious men, if this night passes away without my killing Pandavas in battle.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: नाहत्वा सर्वपञ्चालान् विमोक्ष्ये कवचं विभो। इति सत्यं ब्रवीम्येतत्तन्मे शृणु जनाधिप॥ तेषु सम्भाषमाणेषु व्याधास्तं देशमाययुः। मांसभारपरिश्रान्ताः पानीयार्थं यद्दच्छया॥
en: Without killing all the Panchalas, I will not, O lord, loosen my armour. I tell you this truly. Believe me, O king” While they were thus conversing, a number of hunters arrived there. Worn out with the weight of meat they carried, they came there not deliberately but for satisfying their thirst.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ते हि नित्यं महाराज भीमसेनस्य लुब्धकाः। मांसभारानुपाजहुर्भक्त्या परमया विभो॥
en: Those hunters, O king, used, every day, to procure basketfuls of meat for Bhimasena, O king.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ते तत्र धिष्ठितास्तेषां सर्वं तद् वचनं रहः। दुर्योधनवचश्चैव शुश्रुवुः संगता मिथः॥
en: As they sat concealed on the banks of that lake, those men heard every word of that conversation that took place between "Duryodhana and those warriors.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: तेऽपि सर्वे महेष्वासा अयुद्धार्थिनि कौरवे। निर्बन्धं परमं चक्रुस्तदा वै युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः॥
en: Finding the Kuru king reluctant to fight, those great bowmen, themselves desirous of fighting, began to urge him greatly to accept their advice.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: तांस्तथा समुदीक्ष्याथ कौरवाणां महारथान्। अयुद्धमनसं चैव राजानं स्थितमम्भसि॥ तेषां श्रुत्वा च संवादं राजश्च सलिले सतः। व्याधाभ्यजानन् राजेन्द्र सलिलस्थं सुयोधनम्॥
en: Seeing those car-warriors of the Kaurava army and knowing that the king, reluctant to fight, was living within the waters and hearing that conversation between those heroes and their chief living within the depth of the lake, O king, they clearly understood that it was Duryodhana who was staying within the lake and was firm in his resolution.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ते पूर्वं पाण्डुपुत्रेण पृष्टा ह्यासन् सुतं तव। यदृच्छोपगतास्तत्र राजान् परिमार्गता॥
en: Sometime before, the son of Pandu, while searching for the king, had met those men and asked them the whereabouts of Duryodhana.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ततस्ते पाण्डुपुत्रस्य स्मृत्वा तद् भाषितं तदा। अन्योन्यमब्रुवन् राजन् मृगव्याधाः शनैरिव॥ दुर्योधनं ख्यापयामो धनं दास्यति पाण्डवः। अव्यक्तमिह नः ख्यातो ह्रदे दुर्योधनो नृपः॥
en: Recollecting the words that the son of Pandu had said those hunters, O king, whispered to one another-"We will point out Duryodhana (unto the Pandavas). The son of Pandu will then give us riches. It is clear that the famous king Duryodhana is here.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: तस्माद् गच्छामहे सर्वे यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः। आख्यातुं सलिले सुप्तं दुर्योधनममर्षणम्॥
en: Let us then go all of us where king Yudhishthira is, for telling him that the vindictive Duryodhana is living hidden within the waters of this lake.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: धृतराष्ट्रात्मजं तस्मै भीमसेनाय धीमते। शयानं सलिले सर्वे कथयामो धनु ते॥
en: Let us also, all of us, inform that great bowman, the intelligent Bhimasena, that the son of Dhritarashtra has hidden himself within the waters of this lake.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: स नो दास्यति सुप्रीतो धनानि बहुलान्युत। किं नो मांसेन शुष्केण परिक्लिष्टेन शोषिणा॥ एवमुक्त्वा तु ते व्याधाः सम्प्रहृष्टा धनार्थिनः। मांसभारानुपादाय प्रययुः शिबिरं प्रति॥
en: Pleased with us, he will give us immense riches. Why should we exhaust ourselves day after day, with procuring meat?" Having said these words, those hunters, filled with joy and longing for wealth, took up their baskets of meat and went towards the Pandava camp.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: पाण्डवापि महाराज लब्धलक्ष्याः प्रहारिणः। अपश्यमानाः समरे दुर्योधनमवस्थितम्॥
en: The Pandavas of pure aim and expert in fighting, O monarch, not seeing in battle Duryodhana who was then concealed, were taking rest in their camp.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: निकृतेस्तस्य पापस्य ते पारं गमनेप्सवः। चारान् सम्प्रेषयामासुः समन्तात् तद्रणाजिरे॥
en: Desirous of putting an end to that sinful man's evil policy, they had sent spies in all directions on the field of battle.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: आगम्य तु ततः सर्वे नष्टं दुर्योधनं नृपम्। न्यवेदयन्त सहिता धर्मराजस्य सैनिकाः॥
en: All the soldiers, however, that had been dispatched on that mission, returned to the camp together and informed the just king Yudhishthira that they could not find out the kind Duryodhana.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा चाराणां भरतर्षभ। चिन्तामभ्यगमत् तीव्र निःशश्वास च पार्थिवः॥
en: Hearing those words of the messengers who had come back. back. ( Bharata-chief, king Yudhishthira was stricken with great anxiety and began to sigh heavily.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: अत स्थितानां पाण्डूनां दीनानां भरतर्षभ। तस्माद् देशादपक्रम्य त्वरिता लुब्धका विभो॥ आजग्मुः शिबिरं हृष्टा दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनं नृपम्। वार्यमाणाः प्रविष्टाश्च भीमसेनस्य पश्यतः॥
en: While the Pandavas, O best of Bharata's race, were thus disappointed those hunters, O lord, came speedily from the banks of that lake and arrived at the camp filled with joy at having found out Duryodhana. Though forbidden, they still entered the camp, before the very presence of Bhimasena.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ते तु पाण्डवमासाद्य भीमसेनं महाबलम्। तस्मै तत् सर्वमाचख्युर्यद् वृत्तं यच वै श्रुतम्॥
en: Having approached that powerful son of Pandu, Bhimasena, they described everything to him about what they had seen and heard.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: श्रुत्वा विशाम्पते। ततो वृकोदरो राजन् दत्त्वा तेषां धनं बहु। धर्मराजाय तत् सर्वमाचचक्षे परंतपः॥
en: Then Vrikodara, that scorcher of foes, O king, giving them immense wealth, described everything to the righteous king Yudhishthira saying.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: असौ दुर्योधनो राजन् विज्ञातो मम लुब्धकैः। संस्तभ्य सलिलं शेते यस्यार्थे परितप्यसे॥
en: "Duryodhana, O king, has been found out by the hunters that supply me with meat. He, O king, for whom you are sorry, now lies within a lake whose waters have been turned solid by him."

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: तद् वचो भीमसेनस्य प्रियं अज्ञातशत्रुः कौन्तेयो हृष्टोऽभूत् सह सोदरैः॥
en: Hearing those pleasant words of Bhimasena, O king, Yudhishthira was, with all his brothers, filled with joy.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: तं च श्रुत्वा महेष्वासं प्रविष्टं सलिलह्रदे। क्षिप्रमेव ततोऽगच्छन् पुरस्कृत्य जनार्दनम्॥
en: Having learnt that the great bowman Duryodhana had entered into the waters of a lake, the king went there quickly with Janarddana at the head.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ततः किलकिलाशब्दः प्रादुरासीद् विशाम्पते। पाण्डवानां प्रहृष्टानां पञ्चालानां च सर्वशः॥
en: Then a tumult arose, O king, from among the Pandavas and the Panchalas all of whom were filled with joy.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: सिंहनादांस्ततश्चकुः श्वेडाश्च भरतर्षभ। त्वरिता क्षत्रिया राजञ्जग्मुद्वैपायनं ह्रदम्॥
en: The warriors sent forth leonine roars, O foremost of Bharata's race and cried loudly. All the Kshatriyas, O king, went quickly towards that lake called Dvaipayana.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ज्ञातः पापो धार्तराष्ट्रो दृष्टश्चेत्यसकृद्रणे। प्राक्रोशन् सोमकास्तत्र हृष्टरूपाः समन्ततः॥
en: The Somakas rejoiced all around and exclaimed-"The sinful son of Dhritarashtra has been discovered.”

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: तेषामाशु प्रयातानां स्थानां तत्र वेगिनाम्। बभूव तुमुलः शब्दो दिवस्पृक् पृथिवीपते॥
en: The noise made by the cars of those quickly-proceeding warriors became very loud, O king and touched the very sky.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: दुर्योधनं परीप्सन्तस्तत्र तत्र युधिष्ठिरम्। अन्वयुस्त्वरितास्ते वै राजानं श्रान्तवाहनाः॥
en: Although their animals were exhausted all of them still proceeded quickly behind king Yudhishthira who was determined upon finding out Duryodhana.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: अर्जुनो भीमसेनश्च माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ। धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पाञ्चाल्यः शिखण्डी चापराजितः॥ उत्तमौजा युधामन्युः सात्यकिश्च महारथः। पञ्चालानां च ये शिष्टा द्रौपदेयाश्च भारत॥ हयाश्च सर्वे नागाश्च शतशश्च पदातयः।
en: Arjuna and Bhimasena, the two sons of Madri by Pandu, the Panchala prince Dhrishtadyumna, the invincible Shikhandin, Uttamaujas, Yudhamanyu, the great carwarrior Satyaki, the five sons of Draupadi and those amongst the Panchalas, O king, that were yet alive and all the Pandavas and all their elephants and infantry by hundreds all accompanied Yudhishthira.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ततः प्राप्तो महाराज धर्मराजः प्रतापवान्॥ द्वैपायनं ह्रदं घोरं यत्र दुर्योधनोऽभवत्। शीतामलजलं हृद्यं द्वितीयमिव सागरम्॥
en: Brave and righteous king Yudhishthira, O king, reached the lake Dvaipayana within which Duryodhana then was. Wide as the ocean itself, its view was delightful and its waters were cool and transparent.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: मायया सलिलं स्तभ्य यत्राभूत् ते स्थितः सुतः। अत्यद्भुतेन विधिना दैवयोगेन भारत॥
en: Making the waters solid by means of his wonderful power of illusion, your son Duryodhana, O Bharata, lived within that lake.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: सलिलान्तर्गतः शेते दुर्दर्शः कस्यचित् प्रभो। मानुष्यस्य मनुष्येन्द्र गदाहस्तो जनाधिपः॥
en: Indeed, within those waters lay, O lord, that king, armed with his mace, who, could not be defeated by any man.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा सलिलान्तर्गतो वसन्। शुश्रुवे तुमुलं शब्दं जलदोपमनिःस्वनम्॥
en: Living within the waters of that lake, king Duryodhana heard the tumult of the Pandava army which reseinbled the muttering of the clouds.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: युधिष्ठिरश्च राजेन्द्रं तं ह्रदं सह सोदरैः। आजगाम महाराज तव पुत्रवधाय वै॥
en: Yudhishthira then, O king, with his brothers, went to that lake for killing Duryodhana.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: महता शङ्खनादेन रथनेमिस्वनेन च। ऊर्ध्वं धुन्वन् महारेणुं कम्पयंश्चापि मेदिनीम्॥
en: Raising a thick dust, that son of Pandu made the earth tremble with the sounds of his car-wheels and the loud blare of his conch.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: यौधिष्ठिरस्य सैन्यस्य श्रुत्वा शब्दं महारथाः। कृतवर्मा कृपो द्रौणी राजानमिदमब्रुवन्॥ इमे ह्यायान्ति संहृष्टाः पाण्डवा जितकाशिनः। अपयास्यामहे तावदनुजानातु नो भवान्॥
en: Hearing the noise made by the army of Yudhishthira, those great car-warriors, viz., Kritavarman, Kripa and the son of Drona, said to the Kuru king:-"Elated with joy and desiring for victory the Pandavas are coining here, you know. We will, therefore, leave this place."

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: दुर्योधनस्तु तच्छुत्वा तेषां तत्र तरस्विनाम्। तथेत्युक्त्वा ह्रदं तं वै माययास्तम्भयत् प्रभो॥
en: Hearing those words of those active heroes, he answered them, saying-"Let it be so," and remained as before within the waters, having, O lord, turned them solid by his power of illusion.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: त्वनुज्ञाप्य राजानं भृशं शोकपरायणाः। जग्मुर्दूरे महाराज कृपप्रभृतयो रथाः॥
en: Those car-warriors, headed by Kripa, filled with grief, took leave of the king and went away to a remote place.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं न्यग्रोधं प्रेक्ष्य मारिष। न्यविशन्त भृशं श्रान्ताश्चिन्तयन्तो नृपं प्रति॥
en: Having proceeded far, they beheld a banian tree under whose shade they stopped, greatly exhausted and exceedingly anxious about the king and thinking thus.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: ते विष्टभ्य सलिलं सुतो धार्तराष्ट्रो महाबलः। पाण्डवाश्चापि सम्प्राप्तास्तं देशं युद्धमीप्सवः॥
en: "Having solidified the waters of the lake, the powerful son of Dhritarashtra lives at tine bed. The Pandavas have reached there from desire of battle.

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: कथं नु युद्धं भविता कथं राजा भविष्यति। कथं नु पाण्डवा राजन् प्रतिपत्स्यन्ति कौरवम्॥
en: How will the battle take place? What will become of the king? How will the Pandavas discover the King?"

description: Duryodhana lives in a lake. Drona, Kripa and Ashvatthaman meet him there. The Pandavas learn the whereabouts of Duryodhana from the hunters. They go to the lake and vilify him
sn: इत्येवं चिन्तयानास्तु रथेभ्योऽश्वान् विमुच्यते। तत्रासांचक्रिरे राजन् कृपप्रभृतयो रथाः॥
en: Thinking of these things, O king, those heroes, viz., Kripa and others, unyoked their horses from their cars and prepared to rest there for some time.

sn: संजय उवाच ततस्तेष्वपयातेषु रथेषु त्रिषु पाण्डवाः। ते ह्रदं प्रत्यपद्यन्त यत्र दुर्योधनोऽभवत्॥
en: Sanjaya said After those three car-warriors had left that place the Pandavas arrived at that lake within which Duryodhana was taking rest.

sn: आसाद्य च कुरुश्रेष्ठ तदा द्वैपायनं ह्रदम्। स्तम्भितं धार्तराष्ट्रेण दृष्ट्वा तं सलिलाशयम्॥ वासुदेवमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् कुरुनन्दनः।
en: Having arrived at the banks of the Dvaipayana lake, O best of Kuru's race, they saw that reservoir of waters enchanted by your son. Then Yudhishthira said to Vasudeva.

sn: पश्येमा धार्तराष्ट्रेण मायामप्सु प्रयोजिताम्॥ विष्टभ्य सलिलं शेते नास्य मानुषतो भयम्।
en: "Behold, the son of Dhritarashtra has enchanted these waters by his power of illusion. Having enchanted the waters, he lives within them. He entertains no fear of injury from man.

sn: दैवी मायामिमां कृत्वा सलिलान्तर्गतो ह्ययम्॥ निकृत्या निकृतिप्रज्ञो न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यते।
en: Having exercised his power of illusion he is now within the waters. By an act of deception, that deceiptful man has betaken to this refuge. He shall not however escape me alive.

sn: यद्यस्य समरे साह्यं कुरुते वज्रभृत् स्वयम्॥ तथाप्येनं हयं युद्धे लोका द्रक्ष्यन्ति माधव।
en: Even if the holder of the thunderbolt himself helps him in battle, people, O Mahadeva, shall yet seen him killed today.”

sn: वासुदेव उवाच मायाविन इमां मायां मायया जहि भारत॥ मायावी मायया वध्यः सत्यमेतद् युधिष्ठिर।
en: Vasudeva said With your own power of illusion, O Bharata, destroy this illusion of Duryodhana who is an expert in it. One conversant with illusion should be killed with illusion. This indeed is the truth, O Yudhishthira.

sn: क्रियाभ्युपायैर्बहुभिर्मायामप्सु प्रयोज्य च॥ जहि त्वं भरतश्रेष्ठ मायात्मानं सुयोधनम्।
en: By applying your power of illusion to these waters kill, O chief of the Bharatas, this Suyodhana who is the master of illusion.

sn: क्रियाभ्युपायैरिन्द्रेण निहता दैत्यदानवाः॥ क्रियाभ्युपायैर्बहुभिर्बलिर्बद्धो महात्मना।
en: By his illusory power Indra himself killed the Daityas and the Danavas. Vali himself was bound by that great one. viz., Upendra, with the aid of his illusory power.

sn: क्रियाभ्युपायैर्बहुभिर्हिरण्याक्षो महासुरः॥ हिरण्यकशिपुश्चैव क्रिययैव निषूदितौ। वृत्रश्च निहतो राजन् क्रिययैव न संशयः॥
en: The great Asura Hiranyaksha, as also that one, viz., Hiranyakashipu, was killed by the same power. Forsooth, O king, Vritra also was slain by the power of illusion.

sn: तथा पौलस्त्यतनयो रावणो नाम राक्षसः। रामेण निहतो राजन् सानुबन्धः सहानुगः॥ क्रियया योगमास्थाय तथा त्वमपि विक्रम।
en: Similarly was the Rakshasa Ravana of Pulastya's race, with his relatives and followers, killed by Rama. Relying upon your illusory power do you also display your prowess.

sn: क्रियाभ्युपायैर्निहतौ मया राजन् पुरातनौ॥ तारकाश्च महादैत्यो विप्रचित्तिश्च वीर्यवान्।
en: Those two highly energetic and ancient Daityas, viz., Taraka and Viprachitti were, in ancient time, O king, slain by the help of illusion.

sn: वातापिरिल्वलश्चैव त्रिशिराश्च तथा विभो॥ सुन्दोपसुन्दावसुरौ क्रिययैव निषूदितौ।
en: Likewise Vatapi and Ilwala and Trishiras, O lord and the Asuras Sunda and Upasunda were all killed by the aid of illusion.

sn: क्रियाभ्युपायैरिन्द्रेण त्रिदिव भुज्यते विभो॥ क्रिया बलवती राजन् नान्यत् किंचिद् युधिष्ठिर।
en: Indra himself enjoys heaven by the power of illusion. Action is very efficacious O king and nothing else is so, O Yudhishthira.

sn: दैत्याश्च दानवाश्चैव राक्षसाः पार्थिवास्तथा॥ क्रियाभ्युपायैर्निहताः क्रियां तस्मात् समाचर।
en: Daityas and Danavas and Rakshasas and king have been slain by the same. Do you, therefore, act.'

sn: संजय उवाच इत्युक्तो वासुदेवेन पाण्डवः संशितव्रतः॥ जलस्थं तं महाराज तव पुत्रं महाबलम्। अभ्यभाषत कौन्तेयः प्रहसन्निव भारत॥
en: Sanjaya continued Thus addressed by Vasudeva, Pandu's son of rigid vows, smilingly addressed, O Monarch, your powerful son who, O Bharata, was then within the waters of that lake, saying.

sn: सुयोधन किमर्थोऽयमारम्भोऽप्सु कृतस्त्वया। सर्वं क्षत्रं घातयित्वा स्वकुलं च विशाम्पते॥
en: "Why, O Suyodhana, have you charined these waters, after having caused all the Kshatriyas to die and after having, O king, brought about the extinction of your family?

sn: जलाशयं प्रविष्टोऽद्य वाञ्छञ्जीवितमात्मनः। उत्तिष्ठ राजन् युध्यस्व सहास्माभिः सुयोधन॥
en: Why have you entered into this lake today, with a view to save your own life? Arise, O king and fight us, O Suyodhana.

sn: स ते दो नरश्रेष्ठ स च मानः क्व ते गतः। यस्त्वं संस्तभ्य सलिलं भीतो राजन् व्यवस्थितः।।२०
en: Where, O best of men, has your sense of honour now gone, since, ( king, you have exchanged these waters and are now lying within them?

sn: सर्वे त्वां शूरं इत्येवं जना जल्पन्ति संसदि। व्यर्थं तद् भवतो मन्ये शौर्य सलिलशायिनः॥
en: All men describe you in assemblies as a hero. All that, however, is entirely false, I think, since you are now living concealed within these waters.

sn: उत्तिष्ठ राजन् युध्यस्व क्षत्रियोऽसि कुलोद्भवः। कौरवेयो विशेषेण कुलं जन्मं च संस्मर॥
en: Arise, O king and fight, for you are a Kshatriya born in a noble family. You are a Kaurava. Remember your birth.

sn: स कथं कौरवे वंशे प्रशंसञ्जन्म चात्मनः। युद्धाद् भीतस्ततस्तोयं प्रविश्य प्रतितिष्ठसि॥
en: How do you boast of your birth in Kuru's family, when you have concealed yourself within the depths of this lake, having fled away from battle in fear?

sn: अयुद्धमव्यस्थानं नैष धर्मः सनातनः। अनार्यजुष्टमस्वयँ रणे राजन् पलायनम्॥
en: This is no the duty of a Kshatriya. Flight from battle, O king, is not the practice of honourable men, nor it leads to heaven.

sn: कथं पारमगत्वा हि युद्धे त्वं वै जिजीवीषुः। इमान् निपतितान् दृष्ट्वा पुत्रान् भ्रातॄन् पितूंस्तथा।॥ सम्बन्धिनो वयस्यांश्च मातुलान् बान्धवांस्तथा। घातयित्वा कथं तात इदे तिष्ठसि साम्प्रतम्॥
en: How is it that without having terminated this war, though you were filled with the desire of victory, you live now within this lake, after having brought about the destruction of your sons and brothers and sires and relatives and friends and maternal uncles and kinsmen.

sn: शूरमानी न शूरस्त्वं मृषां वदसि भारत। शूरोऽहमिति दुर्बुद्धे सर्वलोकस्य शृण्वतः॥
en: Though always vaunting of your courage, you are however, not a hero. Falsely you describe yourself, O Bharata, before all men as a hero, O wicked wight.

sn: न हि शूराः पलायन्ते शत्रून् दृष्ट्वा कथञ्चन। ब्रूहि वा त्वं यया वृत्त्या शूर त्यजसि संगरम्॥
en: They, that are heroes, never fly away from their foes. Or tell us, O hero, about the nature of that courage by which you have fled from battle.

sn: स त्वमुत्तिष्ठ युध्यस्व विनीय भयमात्मनः। घातयित्वा सर्वसैन्यं भ्रातूंश्चैव सुयोधन॥ नेदानी जीविते बुद्धिः कार्या धर्मचिकीर्षया। क्षत्रधर्ममुपाश्रित्य त्वद्विधेन सुयोधन॥
en: Arise, O prince and fight fearlessly. Having caused all your troops and brothers to be killed O Suyodhana, you should not, if you are an honest man, think now of saving your life. A Kshatriya, O Suyodhana, like yourself, should not act in this way.

sn: यत् तु कर्णमुपाश्रित्य शकुनिं चापि सौबलम्। अमर्त्य इव सम्मोहात् त्वमात्मानं न बुद्धवान्॥
en: Relying upon Karna as also upon Shakuni the son of Şubala, you considered yourself immortal and could not understand your own self.

sn: तत् पापं सुमहत् कृत्वा प्रतियुद्ध्यस्व भारत। कथं हि त्वद्विधो मोहाद् रोचयेत पलायनम्॥
en: Having committed such a grievous iniquity fight now, O Bharata. How is it that you prefer flight from the field. Surely, you forget yourself.

sn: क्व ते तत् पौरुषं यातं क्व च मानः सुयोधन। क्व च विक्रान्तता याता क्व च विस्फूर्जितं महत्।।३३
en: Where is that manliness of yours, O sire and where, O Suyodhana, is that your pride? Where is your prowess and energy gone?

sn: क्व ते कृतास्त्रता याता किञ्च शेषे जलाशये। स त्वमुत्तिष्ठ युध्यस्व क्षत्रधर्मेण भारत॥
en: Where is that your mastery in weapons? Why do you live within this lake now? Arise, O Bharata and fight, following the duties of a Kshatriya.

sn: अस्मांस्तु वा पराजित्य प्रशाधि पृथिवीमिमाम्। अथवा निहतोऽस्माभिर्भूमौ स्वप्स्यसि भारत॥
en: Either govern the wide carth after defeating us or sleep, O Bharata, on the naked earth slain by us.

sn: एष ते परमो धर्मः सृष्टो धात्रा महात्मना। तं कुरुष्व यथातथ्यं राजा भव महारथ॥
en: Even this is your highest duty, as laid down by the illustrious Creator himself. Act according to the injunctions of the scriptures and be a king, O great car-warrior.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्तो महाराज धर्मपुत्रेण धीमता। सलिलस्थस्तव सुत इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya continued Thus addressed, O king, by the intelligent son of Dharma, your son answered him from within the waters in these words.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच नैतचित्रं महाराज यद्भीः प्राणिनमाविशेत्। न च प्राणभयाद् भीतो व्यपयातोऽस्मि भारत॥
en: Duryodhana said It is not at all surprising O king, that fear should possess the hearts of living creatures. As regards myself, however, O Bharata, I have not fled from the field of battle for the fear of life.

sn: अरथश्चानिषङ्गी च निहत:पार्णिसारथिः। एकश्चाप्यगणः संख्ये प्रत्याश्वासमरोचयम्॥
en: My car and quivers were destroyed and my Parshni drivers were slain. I was alone, without a single follower to help me in battle. It was for this that I wanted a little rest.

sn: न प्राणहेतोर्न भयान्न विषादाद् विशाम्पते। इदमम्भः प्रविष्टोऽस्मि श्रमात् त्विदमनुष्ठितम्॥
en: It was not for the sake of saving my life, it was not for fear, it was not from grief, O king, that I entered this lake. It was only out of fatigue that I did so.

sn: त्वं चाश्वसिहि कौन्तेय ये चाप्यनुगतास्तव। अहमुत्थाय वः सर्वान् प्रतियोत्स्यामि संयुगे॥
en: Do you, O son of Kunti, take a little rest with your followers. Rising from this lake I will surely fight all of you in battle.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आश्वस्ता एव सर्वे स्म चिरं त्वां मृगयामहे। तदिदानी समुत्तिष्ठ युध्यस्वेह सुयोधन॥
en: Yudhishthira said All of us have taken enough of rest. We searched you for a long while. Rise then now, O Suyodhana and give us battle.

sn: हत्वा वा समरे पार्थान् स्फीतं राज्यमवाप्नुहि। निहतो वा रणेऽस्माभिर्वीरलोकमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: Either killing the Parthas in battle make this prosperous kingdom your own or killed be us in battle go to the region reserved for heroes.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच यदर्थं राज्यमिच्छामि कुरूणां कुरुनन्दन। त इमे निहताः सर्वे भ्रातरो मे जनेश्वर॥
en: Duryodhana said The Kurus, O son of Kuru's race, for whose sake I desired sovereignty, those brothers of mine, O king, all lie dead on the field.

sn: क्षीणरत्नां च पृथिवी हतक्षत्रियपुङ्गवाम्। न ह्युत्सहाम्यहं भोक्तुं विधवामिव योषितम्॥
en: I do not like to enjoy and longer the Earth that does not contain wealth and best of Kshatriyas and that has accordingly become like a widow.

sn: अद्यापि त्वहमाशंसे त्वां विजेतुं युधिष्ठिर। भक्त्वा पाञ्चालपाण्डूनामुत्साहं भरतर्षभ॥
en: I, however, still hope to defeat you, O Yudhishthira, after checking the pride, O foremost of Bharata's race, of the Panchalas and the Pandus.

sn: न त्विदानीमाहं मन्ये कार्यं युद्धेन कर्हिचित्। द्रोणे कर्णे च संशान्ते निहते च पितामहे॥
en: There is, however, no longer any need for battle when Drona and Karna have been killed and when our grandfather Bhishma has been slain.

sn: अस्त्विदानीमियं राजन् केवला पृथिवी तव। असहायो हि को राजा राज्यमिच्छेत प्रशासितुम्।।४८
en: This empty Earth, O king, is now intended for you. What king would like to rule a kingdom divested of friends and allies?

sn: सुहृदस्तादृशान् हित्वा पुत्रान् भ्रातॄन् पितॄनपि। भवद्भिश्च हृते राज्ये को नु जीवेत मादृशः॥
en: Having caused friends such as I had and even sons and brothers and sires, to be slain and seeing my kingdom possessed by you, who is there like myself that would like to live?

sn: अहं वनं गमिष्यामि ह्यजिनैः प्रतिवासितः। रतिर्हि नास्ति मे राज्ये हतपक्षस्य भारत॥
en: Clad in deer-skins I would enter into woods. I have no desire for kingdom, shorn as I am of friends and allies, O Bharata.

sn: हतबान्धवभूयिष्ठा हताश्वा हतकुञ्जरा। एषा ते पृथिवी राजन् भुवनां विगतज्वरः॥
en: Deprived entirely of friends and allies, of horses and elephants, this Earth exists for you, O king. Do you enjoy her now cheerfully.

sn: वनमेव गमिष्यामि वसानो मृगचर्मणी। न हि मे निर्जनस्यास्ति जीवितेऽद्य स्पृहा विभो॥
en: As for myself, clad in deer-skins, I shall go to the forest. Friendless, as I am, I have no desire, O king, for even life.

sn: गच्छ त्वं भुक्ष्व राजेन्द्र पृथिवीं निहतेश्वराम्। हतयोधां नष्टरत्ना क्षीणवृत्तिर्यथासुखम्॥
en: Go, O king and rule the Earth destitute of kings, warriors, wcalth and without citadels, as you like.

sn: संजय उवाच दुर्योधनं तव सुतं सलिलस्थं महायशाः। श्रुत्वा तु करुणं वाक्यमभाषत युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Sanjaya continued Hearing those words of piercing anguish, the illustrious Yudhishthira said to your son Duryodhana who was still within the lake, saying-

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आर्तप्रलापान्मा तात सलिलस्थः प्रभाषिथा:। नैतन्मनसि मे राजन् वाशितं शकुनेरिव॥
en: Do not utter such ravings of sorrow, O sire, from within the lake. I do not, like Shakuni, feel any pity for you, O king, for such words as these.

sn: यदि वापि समर्थः स्यास्त्वं दानाय सुयोधन। नाहमिच्छेयमवनिं त्वया दत्तां प्रशासितुम्॥
en: You may now, O Suyodhana, be willing to make a gift of Earth to me. I, however, do not wish to rule the Earth as a gift from you.

sn: अधर्मेण न गृह्णीयां त्वया दत्तां महीमिमाम्। न हि धर्मः स्मृतो राजन् क्षत्रियस्य प्रतिग्रहः॥
en: I cannot sinfully accept this Earth as a gift from you. Acceptance of a gift, O king, is not the duty of a Kshatriya.

sn: त्वया दत्तां न चेच्छेयं पृथिवीमखिलामहम्। त्वां तु युद्धे विनिर्जित्य भोक्तास्मि वसुधामिमाम्।। ५८
en: I do not, therefore, wish to have the Earth as a gift from you. I shall, on the other hand, enjoy the Earth after defeating you in battle.

sn: अनीश्वरश्च पृथिवी कथं त्वं दातुमिच्छसि। त्वयेयं पृथिवी राजन् किन्न दत्ता तदैव हि॥ धर्मतो याचमानानां प्रशमार्थं कुलस्य नः।
en: You are not now the lord of the Earth. Why then do you wish to make a gift of that over which you have no right? Why, O king, did you not then give us the Earth when we, observing the rules of honesty and desirous of the welfare of our family, begged you for our portion?

sn: वार्ष्णेयं प्रथमं राजन् प्रत्याख्याय महाबलम्॥ किमिदानीं ददासि त्वं को हि के चित्तविभ्रमः।
en: Having first refused the request of the great Krishna, who do you now desire to give away the Earth? What is this folly of yours?

sn: अभियुक्तस्तु को राजा दातुमिच्छेद्धि मेदिनीम्॥ न त्वमद्य महीं दातुमीशः कौरवनन्दन। आच्छेत्तुं वा बलाद् राजन् स कथं दातुमिच्छसि॥
en: What king is there who, attacked by foes, would like to give away his kingdom, O son of Kuru's race. You have not the power today to give away the Earth. Why then do you wish to make a gift of that over which you have no right?

sn: मां तु निर्जित्य संग्रामे पालयेमां वसुन्धराम्। सूच्यमात्रेणापि यद् भूमेरपि भिद्येत भारत॥ तन्मात्रमपि तन्मह्यं न ददाति पुरा भवान्। स कथं पृथिवीमेतां प्रददासि विशाम्पते॥
en: Defeating me in battle, rule you this Earth. You did not formerly agree to give me even a portion of the Earth covered by the point of a needle. How then, O king, do you make me a gift of the whole Earth?

sn: सूच्यग्रं नात्यजः पूर्वं स कथं त्यजसि क्षितिम्। एवमैश्वर्यमासाद्य प्रशास्य पृथिवीमिमाम्॥ को हि मूढो व्यवस्येत शत्रोर्दातुं वसुन्धराम्।
en: How is it that you, who could not formerly give up even that much of land which the point of a needle would cover, now wish to make over the entire Earth. What fool would, after having got such prosperity and governed the entire Earth, think of giving over that Earth to his focs.

sn: त्वं तु केवलमौर्येण विमूढो नावबुद्ध्यसे॥ पृथिवीं दातुकामोऽपि जीवितेन विमोक्ष्यसे।
en: Fool as you are, you do not see the impropriety of this! Although you wish to give away the Earth, you shall not yet escape me with life.

sn: अस्मान् वा त्वं पराजित्य प्रशाधि पृथिवीमिमाम्॥६७ अथवा निहतोऽस्माभिर्ब्रज लोकाननुत्तमान्।
en: Either rule the Earth after having defeated us or go to the celestial regions after being slain by us.

sn: आवयोर्जीवतो राजन् मयि च त्वयि च ध्रुवम्॥ संशय:सर्वभूतानां विजये नौ भविष्यति।
en: If both of us, that is, yourself and myself, be alive, then all creatures will remain in doubt as to whom the victory belongs.

sn: जीवितं तव दुष्प्रज्ञं मयि सम्प्रति वर्तते॥ जीवयेयमहं कामं न तु त्वं जीवितुं क्षमः।
en: Your life, O indiscrect man, now depends upon me, If, I like, I can allow you to live, but you are not capable of saving your own life.

sn: दहने हि कृतो यत्नस्त्वयास्मासु विशेषतः॥ आशीविषैर्विषैश्चापि जले चापि प्रवेशनैः। त्वया विनिकृता राजन् राज्यस्य हरणेन च॥ अप्रियाणां च वचनैद्रौपद्याः कर्षणेन च। एतस्मात् कारणात् पाप जीवितं ते न विद्यते॥ उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ युध्यस्व युद्धे श्रेयो भविष्यति।
en: At one time you tried to burn us to death and to take our lives by means of snakes and other kinds of poison and by sinking us in water. We were also, O king, deprived by you of our kingdom. You spoke harsh words to us and maltreated Draupadi. For these reasons, O wretch, your life must be taken. Rise, rise and fight us. That will benefit you.

sn: एवं तु विविधा वाचो जययुक्ताः पुनः पुनः। कीर्तयन्ति स्म ते वीरास्तत्र तत्र जनाधिप॥
en: In this way, O king, those heroes, viz., the Pandavas, elated with victory, repeatedly spoke there.'

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच एवं संतज़मानस्तु मम पुत्रो महीपतिः। प्रकृत्या मन्युमान् वीरः कथमासीत् परंतपः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said "Thus remonstrated with by his enemy, how, indeed, did that scorcher of enemies, my heroic and royal son, who was angry by nature, then act.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: न हि संतर्जना तेन श्रुतपूर्वा कथञ्चन। राजभावेन मान्यश्च सर्वलोकस्य सोऽभवत्॥
en: He had never before brooked such a chastisement. He had before been treated by all respectfully like a king.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: यस्यातपत्रच्छायापि स्वका भानोस्तथा प्रभा। खेदायैवाभिमानित्वात् सहेत् सैवं कथं गिरः॥
en: He who could not formerly stand in the shade of an umbrella, thinking he had taken another's shelter-he who could not endure the very effulgence of the Sun, on account of his pride, how could he brooke these words of his enemies?

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: इयं च पृथिवी सर्वा सम्लेच्छाटविका भृशम्। प्रसादाद् भियते यस्य प्रत्यक्षं तव संजय॥
en: You have with your own eyes, O Sanjaya, seen the whole earth, with even her Mlecchas and nomad tribes, depend upon his grace.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: स तथा तय॑मानस्तु पाण्डुपुत्रैर्विशेषतः। विहीनश्च स्वकै त्यैर्निर्जने चावृतो भृशम्॥
en: Chastised there by the sons of Pandu, while lying concealed in such a solitary place after having been deprived of his followers and attendants, alas, how did he answer the Pandavas upon hearing such bitter and departed rebukes from his victorious enemies. Tell me everything, O Sanjaya, about it.'

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच तय॑मानस्तदा राजन्नुदकस्थस्तवात्मजः। युधिष्ठिरेण राजेन्द्र भ्रातृभिः सहितेन ह॥ श्रुत्वा स कटुका वाचो विषमस्थो नराधिपः। दीर्घमुष्णं च निःश्वस्य सलिलस्थः पुनः पुनः॥ सलिलान्तर्गतो राजा धुन्वन् हस्तौ पुनः पुनः। मनश्चकार युद्धाय राजानं चाभ्यभाषत॥
en: Sanjaya continued Thus chastised, O king, by Yudhishthira and his brothers, your royal son lying within the lake, O king of kings, heard those bitter words and became very wretched. Sighing heavily the king moved his arms again and again and making up his mind to fight, thus answered from within the lake, the royal son of Pandu.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: यूयं ससुहृदः पार्थाः सर्वे सरथवाहनाः। अहमेकः परियूनो विस्थो हतवाहनः॥
en: Duryodhana said O Parthas, all of you have friends cars and animals. I, however, am alone, today without a car and without an animal.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: आत्तशस्त्रै रथोपेतैर्बहुभिः परिवारितः। कथमेकः पदातिः सन्नशस्त्रो योद्धमुत्सहे॥
en: Alone as I am and shorn of weapons, how can I dare fight on foot, against numberless foes all well-armed and possessed of cars.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: एकैकेन तु मां यूयं योधयध्वं युधिष्ठिर। न ह्येको बहुभिवीरैाय्यो योधयितुं युधि॥ विशेषतो विकवचः श्रान्तश्चापत्समाश्रितः। भृशं विक्षतगात्रश्च श्रान्तवाहनसैनिकः॥
en: Do you, however, O Yudhishthira, fight me one at a time. It is not proper that one should in battle fight with many especially when that one is without armour, is fatigued, stricken with calamity, greatly wounded and shorn of both animals and troops.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: न मे त्वत्तो भयं राजन् न च पार्थाद् वृकोदरात्। फाल्गुनाद् वासुदेवाद् वा पञ्चालेभ्योऽथवा पुनः।।१४ यमाभ्यां युयुधानाद् वा ये चान्ये तव सैनिकाः। एकः सर्वानहं क्रुद्धो वारयिष्ये युधि स्थितः॥ धर्ममूला सतां कीर्तिर्मनुष्याणां जनाधिप। धर्मं चैवेह कीर्ति च पालयन् प्रब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: I do not cherish the least fear, O king, of either you or Vrikodara, the son of Pritha or Phalguna or Vasudeva or all the Panchalas or the twins or Yuyudhana or all the warriors you have. Standing in battle alone I shall resist all of you.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: अहमुत्थाय सर्वान् वै प्रतियोत्स्यामि संयुगे। अनुगम्यागतान् सर्वानृतून् संवत्सरो यथा॥
en: The fame, O king, of all righteous men depends on righteousness. I say all this to you who are both righteous and illustrious.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: अद्यः वः सरथान् साश्वानशस्त्रो विरथोऽपि सन्। नक्षत्राणीव सर्वाणि सविता रात्रिसंक्षये॥
en: Rising I shall fight all of you in battle Like the year that one by one meets with all the seasons, I shall meet with all of you in fight.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: तेजसा नाशयिष्यामि स्थिरीभवत पाण्डवाः। अद्यानृण्यं गमिष्यामि क्षत्रियाणां यशस्विनाम्॥
en: Wait, you Pandavas. Like the sun destroying by his effulgence the light of all the stars at dawn, I shall to day, though weaponless and carless, kill all of you possessed of cars and horses.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: बाह्रीकद्रोणभीष्माणां कर्णस्य च महात्मनः। जयद्रथस्य शूरस्य भगदत्तस्य चोभयोः॥ मद्रराजस्य शल्यस्य भूरिश्रवस एव च। पुत्राणां भरतश्रेष्ठ शकुनेः सौबलस्य च॥ मित्राणां सुहृदां चैव बान्धवानां तथैव च।
en: Today I shall release myself from the debt I woe to the many illustrious Kshatriyas, to Valhika and Drona and Bhishma and the great Karna, to the heroic Jayadratha and Bhagadatta, to Shalya the ruler of the Madras and Bhurishravas, to my sons, O best of Bharata's race and Shakuni the son of Subala, to all my friends and well-wishers and relatives.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: आनृण्यमद्य गच्छामि हत्वा त्वां भ्रातृभिः सह॥ एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं विरराम जनाधिपः।
en: Today I shall release myself from that debt by killing you with your brothers. Having said these words, he stopped.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दिष्ट्या त्वमपि जानीषे क्षत्रधर्मं सुयोधन॥ दिष्ट्या ते वर्तते बुद्धिर्युद्धायैव महाभुज।
en: Yudhishthira said By good luck, O Suyodhana, you are conversant with the duties of a Kshatriya. By good luck, O mighty-armed heroe, your heart is bent on a battle.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: दिष्ट्या शूरोऽसि कौरव्य दिष्ट्या जानासि संगरम्।। २४ यस्त्वमेको हि नः सर्वान् संगरे योद्भुमिच्छसि।
en: By good luck, you are a hero, O you of Kuru's race and by good luck, you are conversant with battle, since, alone, you wish to give all of us a battle.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: एक एकेन संगम्य यत् ते सम्मतमायुधम्॥
en: Fight any one of us taking whatever weapon you like. All of us will fight.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: तत् त्वमादाय युध्वस्व प्रेक्षकास्ते वयं स्थिताः। स्वयमिष्टं च ते कामं वीर भूयो ददाम्यहम्॥ हत्वैकं भवतो राज्यं हतो वा स्वर्गमाप्नुहि।
en: I grant you also, O hero, this other wish of yours viz., that if you kill any one of us, you shall then become king. Otherwise, killed by us, go to heaven.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच एकश्चैद् योद्धमाक्रन्दे शूरोऽद्य मम दीयताम्॥ आयुधानामियं चापि वृता त्वत्सम्मते गदा।
en: Duryodhana said Brave as you are, if you allow me the option of fighting only one of you, this mace, that I have in my hand, is the weapon that I select.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: हन्तैकं भवतामेकः शक्यं मां योऽभिमन्यते॥ पदातिर्गदया संख्ये स युध्यतु मया सह।
en: Let any of you, who thinks that he is a match for me, come forward and fight with me on foot, arined with mace.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: वृत्तानि रथयुद्धानि विचित्राणि पदे पदे॥ इदमेकं गदायुद्धं भवत्वद्याद्भुतं महत्।
en: Many wonderful single combats have taken place on cars. Let this one great and wonderful encounter with the mace take place today.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: अस्त्राणामपि पर्यायं कर्तुमिच्छन्ति मानवाः॥ युद्धानामपि पर्यायो भवत्वनुमते तव।
en: Men wish to change weapons in battle. Let the mode of fight be changed today, with your permission.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: गदया त्वां महाबाहो विजेष्यामि सहानुजम्॥ पञ्चालान् संजयांश्चैव ये चान्ये तव सैनिकाः। न हि मे सम्भ्रमो जातु शक्रादपि युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O you of great arms, I shall, with my mace, defeat you today with all your younger brothers, as also all the Panchalas and the Srinjayas and all the other troops you still possess. I do not entertain the least fear, O Yudhishthira, of even Shakra himself.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ गान्धारे मां योधय सुयोधन। एक एकेन संगम्य संयुगे गदया बली।॥
en: Yudhishthira said Rise, rise, O son of Gandhari and fight me, O Suyodhana. Alone as you are fight us, meeting one at a time, O you of great might, armed with your mace.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: पुरुषो भव गान्धारे युध्यस्व सुसमाहितः। अद्य ते जीवितं नास्ति यदीन्द्रोऽपि तवाश्रयः॥
en: Be a man, O son of Gandhari and fight carefully. Today you shall have to lose your life even if Indra becomes your ally. O you

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच एतत् स नरशार्दूलो नामृष्यत तवात्मजः। सलिलान्तर्गतः श्वभ्रे महानाग इव श्वसन्॥
en: Sanjaya continued That foremost of men, your son, could not brook those words of Yudhishthira. He sighed heavily from within the water like a huge snake from with its hole.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: तथासौ वाक्प्रतोदेन तुद्यमानः पुनः पुनः। वचो न ममृषे राजन्नुत्तमाश्वः कशामिव॥
en: Struck repeatedly with such wordy goads, he could not bear at all like a horse of high breed that cannot bear the strokes of a whip.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: संक्षोभ्य सलिलं वेगाद् गदामादाय वीर्यवान्। अद्रिसारमयीं गुर्वी काञ्चनाङ्गदभूषणाम्॥
en: Agitating the waters with great force that brave warrior rose like a prince of elephants from within the lake, sighing heavily in rage and armed with his heavy and strong mace of adamant decked with gold.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: अन्तर्जलात् समुत्तस्थौ नागेन्द्र इव नि:श्वसन्। स भित्त्वा स्तम्भितं तोयं स्कन्धे कृत्वाऽऽयसीं गदाम्॥
en: Cutting through the solidified waters your son rose carrying his mace made of iron at his shoulders, like the sun himself consuming everything with his rays.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: उदतिष्ठत पुत्रस्ते प्रतपन् रश्मिवानिव। ततः शैक्यायसीं गुर्वी जातरूपपरिष्कृताम्॥
en: Highly powerful your intelligent son began to handle his heavy mace made of iron and equipt with a sling.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: गदां परामृशद् धीमान् धार्तराष्ट्रो महाबलः। गदाहस्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा सशृङ्गमिव पर्वतम्॥ प्रजानामिव संक्रुद्धं शूलपाणिमिव स्थितम्। सगदो भारतो भाति प्रतपन् भास्करो यथा॥ तमुत्तीर्णं महाबाहुं गदाहस्तमरिंदमम्। मेनिरे सर्वभूतानि दण्डपाणिमिवान्तकम्॥
en: Seeing him with the mace and resembling a mountain crest or the trident wielding Rudra himself casting angry looks on living beings they marked that Bharata chief to shed a lustre around like the scorching sun himself in the sky. Indeed, all creatures then regarded that mighty-armed chastiser of foes, as he stood with his mace on his shoulders after rising from the waters, to look like the Death himself armed with his rod.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: वज्रहस्तं यथा शक्रः शूलहस्तं यथा हरम्। ददृशुः सर्वपञ्चालाः पुत्रं तव जनाधिप॥
en: Indeed, all the Panchalas then saw your royal son, resemble thunder-wielding Indra or the trident-wielding Hara.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: तमुत्तीर्णं तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य समहष्यन्त सर्वशः। पञ्चाला: पाण्डवेयाश्च तेऽन्योन्यस्य तलान् ददुः॥
en: Seeing him, however, rise from within the lake, all the Panchalas and the Pandavas began to rejoice and seize each others hands.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: अवहासं तु तं मत्वा पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। उद्धृत्य नयने क्रुद्धो दिधक्षुरिव पाण्डवान्॥ त्रिशिखां भृकुटीं कृत्वा संदष्टदशनच्छदः। प्रत्युवाच ततस्तान् वै पाण्डवान् सहकेशवान्॥
en: Your son Duryodhana considered that action of the onlookers to be an insult to nim. Rolling his eyes in anger and as if consuming the Pandavas with his looks and contracting his brow into three furrows and repeatedly biting his nether lip, he addressed the Pandavas with Keshava in their midst, saying-

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अस्यावहासस्य फलं प्रतिभोक्ष्यथ पाण्डवाः। गमिष्यथ हताः सद्यः सपञ्चाला यमक्षयम्॥
en: Duryodhana said "O you Pandavas, you shall have to bear the consequences of these insults! Killed by me today, you shall, with the Panchalas, have to go to the abode of Yama."

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच उत्थितश्च जलात् तस्मात् पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। अतिष्ठत गदापाणी रुधिरेण समुक्षितः॥
en: Sanjaya continued Rising from the water, your son Duryodhana stood there, with his mace and with limbs covered with blood.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: तस्य शोणितदिग्धस्य सलिलेन समुक्षितम्। शरीरं स्म तदा भाति स्रवत्रिव महीधरः॥
en: Covered with blood and wet with water, his body resembled a mountain discharging water from within it.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: तमुद्यतगदं वीरं मेनिरे तत्र पाण्डवाः। वैवस्वतमिव क्रुद्धं शूलपाणिमिव स्थितम्॥
en: As he stood with his mace, the Pandavas took him for the angry son of Surya himself armed with his bludgeon called Kinkara.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: स मेघनिनदो हर्षनर्दन्निव न गोवृषः। आजुहाव ततः पार्थान् गदया युधि वीर्यवान्॥
en: With voice deep as the mutterings of the clouds or of a bull roaring in joy, the highly powerful Duryodhana then, armed with his mace, asked the Parthas for battle.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच एकैकेन च मां यूयमासीद् युधिष्ठिर। न ह्येको बहुभिाय्यो वीरो योधयितुं युधि॥ न्यस्तवर्मा विशेषेण श्रान्तश्चाप्सु परिप्लुतः। भृशं विक्षतगात्रश्च हतवाहनसैनिकः॥
en: Duryodhana said You will have, O Yudhishthira, to meet me one at a time. It is not meet that one hero should fight with many at the same time, especially when he is divested of armour, worn out with fatigue, covered with water, greatly wounded and without cars, animals and troops.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: अवश्यमेव योद्धव्यं सर्वेरेव मया सह। युक्तं त्वयुक्तमित्येतद् वेत्सि त्वं चैव सर्वदा॥
en: I shall forsooth fight all of you. You will act as a judge, as you have the necessary qualifications for judging the propriety and impropriety of everything.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मा भूदियं तव प्रज्ञा कथमेवं सुयोधन। यदाभिमन्युं बहवो जघ्नुर्युधि महारथाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said How is it, O Duryodhana, that you had not this knowledge when many great car-warriors, in a body, killed Abhimanyu in battle.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: क्षत्रधर्मं भृशं क्रूरं निरपेक्षं सुनिघृणम्। अन्यथा तु कथं हन्युरभिमन्यु तथागतम्॥
en: This duties of a Kshatriya are high, cruel, shorn of all considerations and feelings of pity. Otherwise, how could you kill Abhimanyu under those circumstances.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: सर्वे भवन्तो धर्मज्ञाः सर्वे शूरास्तनुत्यजः। न्यायेन युध्यतां प्रोक्ता शक्रलोकगतिः परा॥
en: All of you were acquainted with the rules of fair fight. All of you were heroes. All of you were ready to sacrifice your lives in battle. The great aim for those that fight righteously is the attainment of the regions of Shakra.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: यद्येकस्तु न हन्तव्यो बहुभिर्धर्म एव तु। तदाभिमन्युं बहवो निजघ्नुस्त्वन्मते कथम्॥
en: If this be your duty, that one should not be killed by many, why is it then that Abhimanyu was killed by many, acting under your advice?

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: सर्वो विमृशते जन्तुः कृच्छुस्थो धर्मदर्शनम्। पदस्थः पिहितं द्वारं परलोकस्य पश्यति॥
en: In difficulty, every one forgets considerations of virtue. They then see the portals of the other world as being closed.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: आमुञ्च कवचं वीर मूर्धजान् यमयस्व च। यचान्यदपि ते नास्ति तदष्यादत्स्व भारत॥
en: Put on armour, O hero and blind your locks. Take everything else, O Bharata, which your require.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: इममेकं च ते कामं वीर भूयो ददाम्यहम्। पञ्चानां पाण्डवेयानां येनं त्वं योद्धुमिच्छसि॥ तं हत्वा वै भवान् राजा हतो वा स्वर्गमाप्नुहि। ऋते च जीविताद् वीर युद्धे किं कर्म ते प्रियम्॥
en: O hero, I however grant you an additional, favour, namely, if you can slay him amongst the five Pandavas with whom you wish to fight, you shall then be the king Otherwise, killed by him, you will proceed to heaven. Save your life, O hero, tell us what boon we may give you.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच ततस्तव सुतो राजन् वर्म जग्राह काञ्चनम्। विचित्रं च शिरस्त्राणं जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृतम्॥
en: Sanjaya continued Then your son, O king, put on armour made of gold and a beautiful head-gear adorned with pure gold.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: सोऽवबद्धशिरस्त्राणः शुभकाञ्चनवर्मभृत्। रराज राजन् पुत्रस्ते काञ्चनः शैलराडिव॥
en: Clad in bright armour of gold, he put on that head-gear. Indeed, O king, your son then looked resplendent like a golden summit.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: संनद्धः सगदो राजन् सज्जः संग्राममूर्धनि। अब्रवीत् पाण्डवान् सर्वान् पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव॥ भ्रातृणां भवतामेको युध्यतां गदया मया। सहदेवेन वा योत्स्ये भीमेन नकुलेन वा॥ अथवा फाल्गुनेनाद्य त्वया वा भरतर्षभ। योत्स्येऽहं संगरं प्राप्य विजेष्ये च रणाजिरे॥
en: Clad in amour, armed with mace and accoutered with other equipments your son Duryodhana then, O king, standing on the field of battle, addressed all the Pandavas, saying-"Amongst you five brothers let any one fight me, armed with mace. As regards myself, I ain willing to fight either Sahadeva or Bhima or Nakula or Phalguna or you today, O best of Bharata's race. If you give me battle, I will fight any one amongst you and will surely gain the victory on the field.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: अहमद्य गमिष्यामि वैरस्यान्तं सुदुर्गमम्। गदया पुरुषव्याघ्र हेमपट्टनिबद्धया॥
en: Today I will terminate these hostilities, with the help, O foremost of men, of my mace wrapped in a cloth of gold.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: गदायुद्धे न मे कश्चित् सदृशोऽस्तीति चिन्तये। गदया वो हनिष्यामि सर्वानेव समागतान्॥
en: I think there is none who can equal me in an encounter with the mace. With my mace I shall kill all of you one after another.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: न मे समर्थाः सर्वे वै योद्धं न्यायेन केचना न युक्तमात्मना वक्तुमेवं गर्वोद्धतं वचः। अथवा सफलं ह्येतत् करिष्ये भवतां पुरः॥
en: Amongst all of you there is no one who is able to fight fairly with me. It is not proper for me to vaunt thus about my own self. I shall, however, make these words of mine true before you.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सत्यं वा मिथ्या वैतद् भविष्यति। गृह्णातु च गदां यो वै योत्स्यतेऽद्य मया सह॥
en: Within this very hour, these words will either be proved or falsified. Let him amongst you take up the mace that will fight with me.

description: The battle of words between Yudi ishthira and Duryodhana
sn: अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सत्यं वा मिथ्या वैतद् भविष्यति। गृह्णातु च गदां यो वै योत्स्यतेऽद्य मया सह॥
en: Within this very hour, these words will either be proved or falsified. Let him amongst you take up the mace that will fight with me.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच एवं दुर्योधने राजन् गर्जमाने मुहुर्मुहुः। युधिष्ठिरस्य संक्रुद्धो वासुदेवोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Sanjaya said While Duryodhana, O king, was repeatedly crying aloud in this way, Vasudeva, worked up with wrath, said to Yudhishthira.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: यदि नाम ह्ययं युद्धे वरयेत् त्वां युधिष्ठिर। अर्जुनं नकुलं चैव सहदेवमथापि वा॥ किमिदं साहसं राजंस्त्वया व्याहृतमीदृशम्। एकमेव निहत्याजौ भव राजा कुरुष्विति॥
en: What indiscreet words have you given vent to, O king, saying that killing one amongst us be you the king of Kurus. If, indeed, O Yudhishthira, Duryodhana selects you for battle or Arjuna or Nakula or Sahadeva, (what will be the consequence?

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: न समर्थानहं मन्ये गदाहस्तस्य संयुगे। एतेन हि कृता योग्या वर्षाणीह त्रयोदश॥ आयसे पुरुषे राजन् भीमसेनजिघांसया।
en: With a view to kill Bhimasena, O king, Duryodhana has practiced with the mace upon a statue of iron.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: कथं नाम भवेत् कार्यमस्याभिर्भरतर्षभ॥ साहसं कृतवास्त्वं तु ह्यनुक्रोशानृपोत्तम।
en: How then, O best of Bharata's race will our object be accomplished? From pity, O best of kings, you have acted very indiscreetly.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: नान्यमस्यानुपश्यामि प्रतियोद्धारमाहवे॥ ऋते वृकोदरात् पार्थात् स च नातिकृतश्रमः।
en: I do not at this moment see any match for Duryodhana except Pritha's son Vrikodara. His practice again, with the mace, is not so great.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तदिदं द्यूतमारब्धं पुनरेव यथा पुरा॥ विषमं शकुंनेश्चैव तव चैव विशाम्पते।
en: You have, therefore, once more given preference to a game of chance as that one formerly between yourself and Shakuni, O monarch.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: बली भीमः समर्थश्च कृती राजा सुयोधनः॥ बलवान् वा कृती वेति कृती राजन् विशिष्यते।
en: Bhima is endued with might and prowess, King Duryodhana, however, is skillful. In a fight between might and skill, he, that is skillful, O king, always becomes successful.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: सोऽयं राजंस्त्वया शत्रुः समे पथि निवेशितः॥ न्यस्तश्चात्मा सुविषमे कृच्छ्रमापादिता वयम्।
en: Such an enemy, O king, you have, by your words placed in a comfortable and secure position. You have placed your oneself, however, in a difficult position. We have, for this, been placed in great peril.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: को नु सर्वान विनिर्जित्य शत्रूनेकेन वैरिणा॥ कृच्छप्राप्तेन च तथा हारयेद् राज्यमागतम्।
en: Who is there that would relinquish sovereignty within grasp, after having defeated all his enemy and when he has only one foe to kill who even is sunk in difficulties?

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: पणित्वा चैकपाणेन रोचयेदेवमाहवम्॥ न हि पश्यामि तं लोके योऽद्य दुर्योधनं रणे।
en: I do not see such a man in the world today, be he a god, who is able to defeat the macearmed Duryodhana in battle.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: गदाहस्तं विजेतुं वै शक्तः स्यादमरोऽपि हि॥ न त्वं भीमो न नकुलः सहदेवोऽथ फाल्गुनः। जेतुं न्यायेन शक्तोः वै कृती राजा सुयोधनः॥
en: Neither you, nor Bhima, nor Nakula nor Sahadeva, nor Phalguna is capable of defeating Duryodhana in fair fight. King Duryodhana is endued with great skill.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स कथं वदसे शत्रु युध्यस्व गदयेति हि। एकं च नो निहत्याजौ भव राजेति भारत॥
en: How then, O Bharata, can you address to such a foe words such as these viz.,., "Fight, selecting the mace as the weapon and if you can kill one amongst us, you shall then be the king."

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: वृकोदरं समासाद्य संशयो वै जये हि नः। न्यायतो युध्यमानानां कृती ह्येष महाबलः॥
en: If Duryodhana meets Vrikodara amongst us wishing to fight fairly with him, even then our victory will hang in the balance. Duryodhana is highly powerful and skillful.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: एकं वास्मान् निहत्य त्वं भव राजेति वै पुनः। नूनं न राज्यभागेषा पाण्डोः कुन्त्याश्च संततिः॥ अत्यन्तवनवासाय सृष्टा भैक्ष्याय वा पुनः।
en: How could you say to him-"Killing only one amongst us be you the king." Forsooth the children of Pandu and Kunti are not destined to enjoy kingdom. They have been born for passing their lives in continued exile in the forest or in mendicancy.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: भीमसेन उवाच मधुसूदन मा कार्षीर्विषादं यदुनन्दन॥ अद्य पारं गमिष्यामि वैरस्य भृशदुर्गमम्।
en: Bhimasena said O killer of Madhu, do not, O delighted of the Yadus, grieve. However difficult it may be, I shall terminate these hostilities.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अहं सुयोधनं संख्ये हनिष्यामि न संशयः॥ विजयो वै ध्रुवः कृष्ण धर्मराजस्य दृश्यते।
en: Forsooth, I shall kill Suyodhana in battle. It appears, O Krishna, that the victory of righteous Yudhishthira is certain.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अध्यर्धेन गुणेनेयं गदा गुरुतरी मम॥ न तथा धार्तराष्ट्रस्य मा कार्षीर्माधव व्यथाम्।
en: This mace of mine is heavier by one and a half times than Duryodhana's. Do no, O Madhava, grieve.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अहमेनं हि गदया संयुगे योद्धमुत्सहे॥ भवन्तः प्रेक्षकाः सर्वे मम सन्तु जनार्दन।
en: I dare fight him, selecting the mace as the weapon. Let all of you, O Janarddana, witness this encounter.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: सामरानपि लोकांस्त्रीन् नानाशस्त्रधरान् युधि॥ योधयेयं रणे कृष्ण किमुताद्य सुयोधनम्।
en: What do you say of Suyodhana, I would fight with the three worlds including the very celestials even if they be armed with every kind of weapon.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच तथा सम्भाषमाणं तु वासुदेवों वृकोदरम्॥ हृष्टः सम्पूजयामास वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्। त्वामाश्रित्य महाबाहो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥ निहतारिः स्वकां दीप्ता श्रियं प्राप्तो न संशयः।
en: Sanjaya continued After Vrikodara had said these words, Vasudeva, filled with glee, applauded him highly and said to him-"Depending on you, O you of great arms, the righteous king Yudhishthira will, forsooth, get back his prosperity after the destruction of all his foes.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: त्वया विनिहताः सर्वे धृतराष्ट्रसुता रणे॥ राजानो राजपुत्राश्च नागाश्च विनिपातिताः।
en: You have slain all the sons of Dhritarashtra in battle. At your hands many kings and princes and elephants have met with their death.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: कलिङ्गा मागधाः प्राच्या गान्धाराः कुरवस्तथा॥ त्वामासाद्य महायुद्धे निहतः पाण्डुनन्दन।
en: The Kalingas, the Magadhas, the Kauravas, the Westerners and the Gandharvas have all been killed in dreadful battles, O son of Pandu.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: हत्वा दुर्योधन चापि प्रयच्छोर्वी ससागराम्॥ धर्मराजाय कौन्तेय यथा विष्णुः शचीपतेः।
en: Killing Duryodhana then, O son of Kunti, bestow the earth with her oceans upon the righteous Yudhishthira like Vishnu conferring the sovereignty of the three worlds upon the lord of Shachi.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: त्वां च प्राप्य रणे पापो धार्तराष्ट्रो विनडक्ष्यति॥ त्वमस्य सक्थिनी भक्त्वा प्रतिज्ञा पालयिष्यसि।
en: Getting you for a foe in battle, the wretched son of Dhritarashtra, will forsooth meet with his death. You will certainly fulfill your promise by breaking his bones.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततस्तु सात्यकी यत्नेन तु सदा पार्थ योद्धव्यो धृतराष्ट्रजः॥ कृती च बलवांश्चैव युद्धशौण्डश्च नित्यदा।
en: You should however, O son of Pritha, always fight with care with the son of Dhritarashtra. He is endued with both skill and strength and always finds delight in battle.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: राजन् पूजयामास पाण्डवम्॥
en: Then Satyaki, O king, applauded the son of Pandu.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: पञ्चालाः पाण्डवेयाश्च धर्मराजपुरोगमाः। तद् वचो भीमसेनस्य सर्व एवाभ्यपूजयन्॥
en: The Panchalas and the Pandavas, also, headed by the righteous king Yudhishthira, all praised Bhimasena.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततो भीमबलो भीमो युधिष्ठिरमथाब्रवीत्। संजयैः सह तिष्ठन्तं तपन्तमिव भास्करम्॥ अहमेतेन संगम्य संयुगे योद्धमुत्सहे। न हि शक्तो रणे जेतुं मामेष पुरुषाधमः॥
en: Then Bhima, of terrible might, addressed Yudhishthira who was standing amid the Srinjayas like the burning Sun himself, saying-"I venture to fight with this man in battle. This wretch among men is not able to defeat me in fight.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अद्य क्रोधं विमोक्ष्यामि निहितं हृदये भृशम्। सुयोधने धार्तराष्ट्रे खाण्डवेऽग्निमिवार्जुनः॥
en: Today I shall vomit that ire which has been ranking in my bosom against Suyodhana the son of Dhritarashtra like Arjuna throwing fire on the forest of Khandava.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: शल्यमद्योद्धरिष्यामि तव पाण्डव हृच्छयम्। निहत्य गदया पापमद्य राजन् सुखी भव॥
en: I shall today pluck out the dart, O son of Pandu, that lay so long sticking to your heart. Be happy, O king, after I shall have struck down this wretch with my mace.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अद्य कीर्तिमयीं माला प्रतिमोक्ष्ये तवानघ। प्राणाश्रियं च राज्यं च मोक्ष्यतेऽद्य सुयोधनः॥
en: Today I shall recover, O sinless one, your garland of glory. Today Suyodhana shall renounce his life, his prosperity and his kingdom.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: राजा च धृतराष्ट्रोऽद्य श्रुत्वा पुत्रं मया हतम्। स्मरिष्यत्यशुभं कर्म यत् तच्छकुनिबुद्धिजम्॥
en: Today hearing of his son's death, king Dhritarashtra will remember all those wrongs that he did to us under Shakuni's advice."

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: इत्युक्त्वा भरतश्रेष्ठो गदामुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्। उदतिष्ठत युद्धाय शक्रो वृत्रमिवाह्वयन्॥
en: Having said these words, that energetic prince, of Bharata's race, stood up for battle, like Shakra summoning Vritra to an encounter.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तदाह्वानममृष्यन् वै तव पुत्रोऽतिवीर्यवान्। प्रत्युपस्थित एवाशु मत्तो मत्तमिव द्विपम्॥
en: Unable to endure that call your highly energetic son, proceeded to the encounter, like one infuriate elephant proceeding to assail another.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: गदाहस्त तव सुतं युद्धाय समुपस्थितम्। ददृशुः पाण्डवाः सर्वे कैलासमिव शृङ्गिणम्॥
en: The Pandavas saw your son, as he came armed with mace, as the summit of the mount Kailasa.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तमेकाकिनमासाद्य धार्तराष्ट्र महाबलम्। वियूथमिव मातङ्गं समहष्यन्त पाण्डवाः॥
en: Verily beholding that powerful son of yours standing alone like a prince of elephants separated from the herd, the Pandavas were filled with joy.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: न सम्भ्रमो न च भयं न च ग्लानिन च व्यथा। आसीद् दुर्योधनस्यापि स्थितः सिंह इवाहवे॥
en: Standing in battle like a very lion, Duryodhana had no fear, no pain, no anxiety.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: समुद्यतगदं दृष्ट्वा कैलासमिव शृङ्गिणम्। भीमसेनस्तदा राजन् दुर्योधनमथाब्रवीत्॥ राज्ञापि धृतराष्ट्रेण त्वया चास्मासु यत् कृतम्। स्मर तद् दृष्कृतं कर्म यद् भूतं वारणावते॥
en: Seeing him stand there with uplifted mace like the created mountain of Kailasa, Bhimasena, O monarch, addressed him, saying "Remember all those wrongs that king Dhritarashtra and yourself have inflicted on us. Remember what took place at Varanavata.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: द्रौपदी च परिकिष्टा सभामध्ये रजस्वला। द्यूते यद् विजितो राजा शकुनेबुद्धिनिश्चयात्॥
en: Remember how Draupadi, while in her season, was maltreated in the midst of the assembly and how king Yudhishthira was defeated at dice through Shakuni's advice.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: यानि चान्यानि दुष्टात्मन् पापानि कृतवानसि। अनाग:सु च पार्थेषु तस्य पश्य महत् फलम्॥
en: See now, O wicked man, the dreadful consequence of those acts as also of the other wrongs that you inflicted on the innocent Parthas.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: त्वकृते निहतः शेते शरतल्पे महायशाः। गाङ्गेयो भरतश्रेष्ठः सर्वेषां नः पितामहः॥
en: It is for you that, that illustrious chief of the Bharatas, the son of Ganga, the grandfather of us all, lies now on a bed of arrows.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: हतो द्रोणश्च कर्णश्च हतः शल्यः प्रतापवान्। वैरस्त चादिकर्ताऽसौ शकुनिनिहतो रणे॥
en: Drona also has been killed. Karna has been killed. Shalya of great valour has been killed. Yonder Shakuni also, the root of these enunities, has been killed in battle.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: भ्रातरस्ते हताः शूराः पुत्राश्च सहसैनिकाः। राजानश्च हताः शूराः समरेष्वनिवर्तिनः॥
en: Your heroic brothers and sons, with all your troops, have been killed. Other heroic kings also, who never retreated from battle, have been killed.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: एते चान्ये च निहता बहवः क्षत्रियर्षभाः। प्रातिकामी तथा पापो द्रौपद्याः केशकृद्धतः॥
en: These and many other leading Kshatriyas, as also Pratikamin, that wretch who had seized the locks of Draupadi, have been killed.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अवशिष्टस्त्वमेवैकः कुलमोऽधमपूरुषः। त्वामप्यद्य हनिष्यामि गदया नात्र संशयः॥
en: You alone are still alive, O destroyer of your family, O wretch among men. I shall forsooth kill you today with my mace.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अद्य तेऽहं रणे दर्पं सर्वं नाशयिता नृप। राज्याशां विपुला राजन् पाण्डवेषु च दुष्कृतम्॥
en: Today, O king, I shall, in battle, repress all your pride. I shall destroy also your hope of sovereignty, O king and pay off all your misdeeds to the sons of Pandu.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच किं कत्थितेन बहुना युद्ध्यस्वाद्य मया सह। अद्य तेऽहं विनेष्यामि युद्धश्रद्धां वृकोदर॥
en: Duryodhana said What is the use of speaking too much? Fight now with me. Today O Vrikodara, I shall subdue you desire for battle.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: किं न पश्यमि मां पाप गदायुद्धे व्यवस्थितम्। हिमवच्छिखराकारां प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्॥
en: Why do you not see me, O wretch, standing here for an encounter with the mace? Am I not armed with a formidable mace that looks like a summit of Himavat?

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: गदिनं कोऽध मां पाप हन्तुमुत्सहते रिपुः। न्यायतो युद्ध्यमानश्च देवेष्वपि पुरन्दरः॥
en: What enemy is there, O wretch, that would dare defeat me armed with this weapon? If it be a fair fight, Purandara himself, amongst the celestials, is not capable of doing it.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: मा वृथा गर्ज कौन्तेय शारदाभ्रमिवाजलम्। दर्शयस्व बलं युद्धे यावत् तत् तेऽद्य विद्यते॥
en: Do not, O son of Kunti, roar uselessly in this way like autumnal clouds shorn of water. Display all the strength you posses in battle now.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तस्य तद् वचन् श्रुत्वा पाण्डवाः सहसंजयाः। सर्वे सम्पूजयामासुस्तद्वचो विजिगीषवः॥
en: Hearing those words of his, the Pandavas with the Srinjayas, all filled with desire of victory, praised them highly.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: उन्मत्तमिव मातङ्गं तलशब्देन मानवाः। भूयः सहर्षयामासू राजन् दुर्योधनं नृपम्॥
en: Like men exciting an infuriate elephant with the clapping of hands, all of them then pleased king Duryodhana.

description: The exchange of angry words between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: बृंहन्ति कुञ्जरास्तत्र हया द्वेषन्ति चासकृत्। शस्त्राणि सम्प्रदीप्यन्ते पाण्डवानां जयैषिणाम्॥
en: The elephants began to grunt and the horses to neigh repeatedly. The weapons of the Pandavas who were filled with the desire of victory shone there. The elephants began to grunt and the horses to neigh repeatedly. The weapons of the Pandavas who were filled with the desire of victory shone there.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच तस्मिन् युद्धे महाराज सुसंवृत्ते सुदारुणे। उपविष्टेषु सर्वेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु॥ ततस्तालध्वजो रामस्तयोर्युद्ध उपस्थिते। श्रुत्वा तच्छिष्ययो राजन्नाजगाम हलायुधः॥
en: Sanjaya said When that fierce encounter O king, was about to take place and when all the great Pandavas had taken their seats indeed, having heard that a battle, between those two heroes, both of whom were his disciples, was about to begin, Rama, whose banner bore the emblem of the palmyra palm and who had the plough for his weapon, came there.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीताः पाण्डवाः सहकेशवाः। उपगम्योपसंगृह्य विधिवत् प्रत्यपूजयन्॥
en: Seeing him, the Pandavas, with Keshava, filled with joy, advanced towards himn and receiving him adored him properly.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: पूजयित्वा ततः पश्चादिदं वचनमब्रुवन्। शिष्ययोः कौशलं युद्धे पश्य रामेति पार्थिव॥
en: After adoring him, they then, O king said to him these words-"Witness, O Rama, the skill in battle of your two disciples.”

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अब्रवीच तदा रामो दृष्ट्वा कृष्णं सपाण्डवम्। दुर्योधनं च कौरव्यं गदापाणिमवस्थितम्॥ चत्वारिंशदहान्यद्य द्वे च मे निःसृतस्य वै। पुष्येण सम्प्रयातोऽस्मि श्रवणे पुनरागतः॥ शिष्ययोर्वै गदायुद्ध द्रष्टकामोऽस्मि माधव।
en: Looking at Krishna and the Pandavas and also at Duryodhana of Kuru's race who was standing there armed with mace, Rama then said-"Two and forty days have passed since I left home. I had set out under the constellation Pushya and have come back under Shravana. I am desirous, O Madhava, of witnessing this encounter with the mace between these two disciples of mine."

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततस्तदा गदाहस्तौ दुर्योधनवृकोदरौ॥ युद्धभूमिं गतौ वीरावुभावेव रराजतुः।
en: At that time the two heroes, viz., Duryodhana and Vrikodara, shone effulgent on the field, both armed with maces.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा परिष्वज्य हलायुधम्॥ स्वागतं कुशलं चास्मै पर्यपृच्छद यथातथम्।
en: Embracing him who had the plough for his weapon, king Yudhishthira, duly enquired about his welfare and welcomed him.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: कृष्णौ चापि महेष्वासावभिवाद्य हलायुधम्॥ सस्वजाते परिप्रीतौ प्रीयमाणौ यशस्विनौ।
en: Those great bowmen, viz., viz., the illustrious Krishnas, filled with joy, cheerfully saluted the hero who had the plough for his weapon and embraced him.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: माद्रीपुत्रो तथा शूरौ द्रौपद्याः पञ्च चात्मजाः॥ अभिवाद्य स्थिता राजन् रौहिणेयं महाबलम्।
en: Similarly the two sons of Madri and the five sons of Draupadi saluted Rohini's powerful son and stood at a respectful distance.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: भीमसेनोऽथ बलवान् पुत्रस्तव जनाधिप।॥ तथैव चोद्यतगदौ पूजयामासर्तुबलम्।
en: Bhimasena of great strength and your son, O monarch, both with uplifted maces in their arms, adored Baladeva.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स्वागतेन च ते तत्र प्रतिपूज्य समन्ततः॥ पश्य युद्धं महाबाहो इति ते राममब्रुवन्। एवमूचुर्महात्मानं रौहिणेयं नराधिपाः॥
en: The other kings honored him by welcoming him and then all of them said to Rama "Witness this encounter, O you of mighty arms.”—Even thus those mighty car-warriors said to the high-souled son of Rohini.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: परिष्वज्य तदा रामः पाण्डवान् सहसृञ्जयान्। अपृच्छत् कुशलं पार्थिवांश्चामितौजसः॥ तथैव ते समासाद्य पप्रच्छुस्तमनामयम्।
en: The highly energetic Rama, having embraced the Pandavas and the Srinjayas, enquired after the welfare of all the other kings. Likewise all of them, approaching him, enquired after his welfare.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: प्रत्यभ्यर्च्य हली सर्वान् क्षत्रियांश्च महात्मनः॥ कृत्वा कुशलसंयुक्तां संविदं च यथावयः। जनार्दनं सात्यकिं च प्रेम्णा स परिषस्वजे॥ मूर्ध्नि चैतावुपानाया कुशलं पर्यपृच्छत।
en: Having in return saluted all the great Kshatriyas and having made courteous inquiries about 'each according to their age, that heroe affectionately embraced Janarddana and Satyaki. Smelling their heads, he enquired after their welfare.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तौ च तं विधिवद् राजन् पूज्यामासतुर्गुरुम्॥ ब्रह्मामिव देवेशमिन्द्रोपेन्द्रौ मुदान्वितौ।
en: Those two in return, O king, duly adored him, their superior, with great pleasure, like Indra and Upendra adoring Brahma the king of the celestials.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततोऽब्रवीद् धर्मसुतो रौहिणेयमरिंदमम्॥ इदं भ्रात्रोर्महायुद्धं पश्य रामेति भारत।
en: Then Dharma's son, O Bharata, said to that chastiser of foes, viz., the son of Rohini "Witness, O Rama, this dreadful encounter between the two brothers."

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तेषां मध्ये महाबाहुः श्रीमान् केशवपूर्वजः॥ व्यविशत् परमप्रीतः पूज्यमानो महारथैः।
en: Thus adored by those great car-warriors, the mighty-armed elder brother of Keshava, of great beauty, took his seat amongst them.
