description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स बभौ राजमध्यस्थो नीलवासाः सितप्रभः॥ दिवीव नक्षत्रगणैः परिकीर्णो निशाकरः।
en: Clad in blue robes and possessed of a fair complexion, Rama, as he sat midst those kings shone like the Moon in the sky encircled by a number of stars.

description: The arrival of Balarama to witness the mace encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततस्तयोः संनिपातस्तुमुलो लोमहर्षणः॥ आसीदन्तकारो राजन् वैरस्य तव पुत्रयोः॥
en: Then that dreadful and hair-standing encounter took place between those two sons of yours O king, for terminating the long standing feud.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: जनमेजय उवाच पूर्वमेव यदा रामस्तस्मिन् युद्ध उपस्थिते। आमन्त्र्य केशवं यातो वृष्णिभिः सहितः प्रभुः॥
en: Janamejaya said On the eye the great battle (between the Kurus and the Pandus) Rama, with Keshava's permission, had left Dwaraka accompanied by many of the Vrishnis.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: साहाय्यं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य न च कर्तास्मि केशव। न चैव पाण्डुपुत्राणां गमिष्यामि यथागतम्॥
en: He had said to Keshava-"I will help neither the son of Dhritarashtra nor the sons of Pandu, but will go wherever I like."

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: एवमुक्त्वा तदा रामो यातः क्षत्रनिबर्हणः। तस्य चागमनं भूयो ब्रह्मशंसितुमर्हसि॥
en: Having said so, Rama that subduer of enemies, had gone away. O Brahmana, tell me everything about his return.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: आख्याहि मे विस्तरशः कथं राम उपस्थितः। कथं च दृष्ट्वान् युद्धं कुशलो ह्यसि सत्तम॥
en: Tell me in full how Rama came there and how he witnessed the battle. Indeed you are a skillful narrator.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उपप्लव्ये निविष्टेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। प्रेषितो धृतराष्ट्रस्य समीपं मधुसूदनः॥ शमं प्रति महाबाहो हितार्थं सर्वदेहिनाम्।
en: Vaishampayana said After the great Pandavas had taken up their post at Upaplavya, they sent Krishna to Dhritarashtra for the object of peace, O mighty-armed one and for the behoof of all creatures.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: स गत्वा हास्तिनपुरं धृतराष्ट्र समेत्य च॥ उक्त्वान् वचनं तथ्यं हितं चैव विशेषतः।
en: Having gone to Hastinapura and met Dhritarashtra, Keshava spoke whole-some and sincere words.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: न च तत् कृतवान् राजा यथा ख्यातं हि तत् पुरा॥ अनवाप्य शमं तज्ञ कृष्णः पुरुषसत्तमः। आगच्छत महाबाहुरुपप्लव्यं जनाधिप॥
en: The king, however, as I have told you before did not pay heed to his advice. Unable to secure peace, the mighty-armed Krishna, The foremost of men, returned, O king, to Upaplavya.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ततः प्रत्यागतः कृष्णो धार्तराष्ट्रविसर्जितः। अक्रियायां नरव्याघ्र पाण्डवानिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Dismissed by Dhritarashtra's son Krishna came back and upon the failure of his mission, O foremost of kings, said to the Pandavas.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: न कुर्वन्ति वचो मह्यं कुरवः कालनोदिताः। निर्गच्छध्वं पाण्डवेयाः पुष्येण सहिता मया॥
en: Urged by fate, the Kauravas have disregarded my words. Come, O sons of Pandu, with me, under the constellation Pushya.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ततो विभज्यमानेषु बलेषु बलिनां वरः। प्रोवाच भ्रातरं कृष्णं रौहिणेयो महामनाः॥
en: After this, while the troops of both parties were being collected and arrayed, the great son of Rohini, that foremost of all powerful persons, said to his brother Krishna.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: तेषामपि महाबाहो साहाय्यं मधुसूदन। क्रियतामिति तत् कृष्णो नास्य चक्रे वचस्तदा॥
en: "O mighty-armed one, O slayer of Madhu, let us help the Kurus.” Krishna, however, did not pay heed to those words of his.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ततो मन्युपरीतात्मा जगाम यदुनन्दनः। तीर्थयात्रां हलधरः सरस्वत्यां महायशाः॥
en: Enraged at this, that illustrious son of Yadu's race, viz., the wielder of the plough, then started on a pilgrimage of the Sarasvati.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: मैत्रनक्षत्रयोगे स्म सहित: सर्वयादवैः। आश्रयामास भोजस्तु दुर्योधनमरिंदमः॥ युयुधानेन सहितो वासुदेवस्तु पाण्डवान्।
en: Accompanied by all the Yadavas, he set out under the conjunction of the asterism called Maitra. The Bhoja chief (Kritavarman), however, took the side O Duryodhana. Accompanied by Yuyudhana, Vasudeva took that of the Pandavas.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: रौहिणेये गते शूरे पुष्येण मधुसूदनः॥ पाण्डवेयान् पुरस्कृत्य ययावभिमुखः कुरून्।
en: After the heroic son of Rohini had started under the constellation Pushya, the slayer of Madhu, placing the Pandavas in his van, went against the Kurus.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: गच्छन्नेव पथिस्थस्तु रामः प्रेष्यानुवाच ह॥ सम्भारांस्तीर्थयात्रायां सर्वोपकरणानि च। आनयध्वं द्वारकायामग्नीन् वै याजकांस्तथा॥
en: While proceeding, Rama ordered his servants on the way, saying-"Bring all the necessary articles of use for a pilgrimage. Bring the sacred fire that is at Dwaraka and our priests.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: सुवर्णं रजतं चैव धेनूर्वासांसि वाजिनः। कुञ्जरांश्च रथांश्चैव खरोष्ट्रं वाहनानि च॥
en: Bring gold, silver, kine, robes, horses, elephants, cars, mules, camels and other beasts of burden.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: क्षिप्रमानीयतां सर्वं तीर्थहेतोः परिच्छदम्। प्रतिस्रोतः सरस्वत्या गच्छध्वं शीघ्रगामिनः॥
en: Being all these necessaries for a sojourn to the sacred waters and proceed quickly towards the Sarasvati.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ऋत्विजश्चानयध्वं वै शतशश्च द्विजर्षभान्। एवं संदिश्य तु प्रेष्यान् बलदेवो महाबलः॥ तीर्थयात्रां ययौ राजन् कुरूणां वैशसे तदा। सरस्वती प्रतिस्रोतः समन्तादभिजग्मिवान्॥ ऋत्विग्भिश्च सुहृद्धिश्च तथान्यैर्द्विजसत्तमैः। स्थैर्गजैस्तताश्चैश्च प्रेष्यैश्च भरतर्षभ॥
en: Bring also some priests for the performance of a special rite and hundreds and hundreds of best Brahmanas.” Having given these orders to the servants, powerful Baladeva started on a pilgrimage at that time of great danger to the Kurus. Setting out towards the Sarasvati, he visited all the sacred shrines along her course, accompanied by priests, friends and many leading Brahmanas, as also with cars and elephants and horses and servants, O best of Bharata's race and with many vehicles drawn by kine and mules and camels.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: गोखरोष्ट्रप्रयुक्तैश्च यानैश्च बहुभिर्वृतः। श्रान्तानां कान्तवपुषां शिशूनां विपुलायुषाम्॥
en: Various sorts of necessaries of life were distributed profusely in various countries amongst the weary and worn, children and the old, in response, O king, to their prayers.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: देशे देशे तु देयानि दानानि विविधानि च। अर्चायै चार्थिना राजन् क्लृप्तानि बहुशस्तथा।२४॥ तानि यानीह देशेषु प्रतीक्षन्ति स्म भारत। बुभुक्षितानामर्थाय क्लृप्तमन्नं समन्ततः॥
en: Everywhere, O king, Brahmanas were sumptuously fed with whatever they wanted. At the command of Rohini's son, men, at different stages of the journey, stocked sufficient food and drink.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: यो यो यत्र द्विजो भोज्यं भोक्तुं कामयते तदा। तस्य तस्य तु तत्रैवमुपजह्वस्तदा नृप॥ तत्र तत्र स्थिता राजन् रौहिणेयस्य शासनात्। भक्ष्यपेयस्य कुर्वन्ति राशींस्तत्र समन्ततः॥
en: Costly garments and bedsteads and coverlets were distributed amongst the Brahmanas desirous of ease and comfort. Whatever a Brahmana or Kshatriya wanted, it was given to him.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: वासांसि च महार्हाणि पर्यङ्कास्तरणानि च। पूजार्थं तत्र क्लृप्तानि विप्राणं सुखमिच्छताम्॥ यत्र यः स्वपते विप्रो यो वा जागर्ति भारत। तत्र तत्र तु तस्यैव सर्वं क्लृप्तमदृश्यत॥ यथासुखं जन: सर्वो याति तिष्ठति वै तदा। यातुकामस्य यानानि पानानि तृषितस्य च॥ बुभुक्षितस्य चान्नानि स्वादूनि भरतर्षभ। उपज रास्तत्र वस्त्राण्याभरणानि च।॥
en: The party thus proceeded with great happiness and lived happily. Balarama's suite gave away vehicles to persons desirous of making journeys, drinks to them that were thirsty and rich food to them that were hungry, as also raiments and ornaments, O best of Bharata's race, to many.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: स पन्थाः प्रवभौ राजन् सर्वस्यैव सुखावहः। स्वर्गोपमस्तदा वीर नराणां तत्र गच्छताम्।
en: The road, O king, along which the party proceeded, looked resplendent, was comfortable for all and resembled heaven itself.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: नित्यप्रमुदितोपतेः स्वादुभक्ष्यः शुभान्वितः॥ विपण्यापणपण्यानां नानाजनशतैर्वृतः। नानाद्रुमलतोपेतो नानारत्नविभूषितः॥
en: There were rejoicings everywhere and rich food was procurable everywhere. There were shops and stalls and various objects were kept there for sale. The entire way was thronged with human beings. And it was decorated with various kinds of trees and creatures and various kinds of gems.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ददौ द्विजेभ्यः क्रतुदक्षिणाश्च यदुप्रवीरो हलभृत् प्रतीतः॥ ततो महात्मा नियमे स्थितात्मा पुण्येषु तीर्थेषु वसूनि राजन्।
en: The great Baladeva, observing rigid vows, distributed amongst the Brahmanas profuse wealth and plentiful sacrificial presents, O king, at various sacred spots.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: दोग्ध्रीश्च धेनूश्च सहस्रशो वै सुवाससः काञ्चनबद्धशृङ्गीः। हयांश्च नानाविधदेशजातान् यानानि दासांश्च शुभान् द्विजेभ्यः॥
en: That chief of Yadu's race also distributed thousands of milch kine covered with excellent cloths and having their horns coated with gold, many horses born in different countries, many vehicles and many beautiful slaves.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: प्यग्र्यं सुवर्ण रजतं सुसुद्धम्। अयस्मयं ताम्रमयं च भाण्डं ददौ द्विजातिप्रवरेषु रामः॥
en: Balarama also distributed to the foremost of the Brahmanas, the gems, garlands, diamonds, pure gold and silver and utensil made of iron copper.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: एवं स वित्तं प्रददौ महात्मा सरस्वतीतीर्थवरेषु भूरि। स्तत: कुरुक्षेत्रमुदारवृत्तिः॥
en: Thus did the great Rama distribute wealth in various sacred shrines on the Sarasvati. In course of his travels, that noble hero of matchless power at last came to Kurukshetra.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: जनमेजय उवाच सारस्वतानां तीर्थानां गुणोत्पात्त वदस्व मे। फलं च द्विपदां श्रेष्ठ कर्मनिर्वृत्तिमेव च॥
en: Janamejaya said Describe to me, O foremost of men, the characteristics, the origin and the merits of the several Tirthas on the Sarasvati and the rites to be performed while going there.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: यथाक्रमेण भगवंस्तीर्थानामनुपूर्वशः। ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मविदां श्रेष्ठ परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: Tell me these, in their order, O illustrious man. My curiosity is not to be satisfied, O foremost of all persons conversant with the knowledge of Brahman.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तीर्थानां च फलं राजन् गुणोत्पत्तिं च सर्वशः। मयोच्यमानं वै पुण्यं शृणु राजेन्द्र कृत्स्नशः॥
en: Vaishampayana said The account of the characteristics and origin of all these Tirthas, O king, is very lengthy. I shall, however, describe them to you. Listen to that sacred account, O king.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: पूर्वं महाराज यदुप्रवीर ऋत्विकसुहृद् विप्रगणैश्च सार्धम्। पुण्यं प्रभासं समुपाजगाम यत्रोडुराड् यक्ष्मणा विश्यमानः॥ विमुक्तशापः पुनराप्य तेजः सर्वं जगद् भासयते नरेन्द्र। एवं तु तीर्थप्रवरं पृथिव्यां प्रभासनात् तस्य ततः प्रभासः॥
en: Accompanied by his priests and friends, Baladeva first went to the Tirthas called Prabhasa. There, the Lord of the asterism (viz., Soma), who had been suffering from phthisis, was freed from his disease. Regaining energy there, O king, be now lights up the universe. And because that foremost of Tirthas on Earth had formerly invested Soma again with effulgence, it is, therefore, called Prabhasa.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं तु भगवान् सोमो यक्ष्मणा समगृह्यत। कथं च तीर्थप्रवरे तस्मिंश्चन्द्रो न्यमन्जत॥ कथमाप्लुत्य तस्मिंस्तु पुनराप्यायितः शशी। एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व विस्तरेण महामुने॥
en: Janamejaya said "For what was the worshipful Soma afflicted with phthisis? How also did he bathe in that tirtha? How did he, having bathed in that sacred water, regain his lost power? Describe it to me fully, O great Muni.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच दक्षस्य तनयास्तात प्रादुरासन् विशाम्पते। स सप्तविंशति कन्या दक्षः सोमाय वै ददौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said Daksha had twenty seven daughters, O king. There he gave away (in marriage) unto Soma.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: नक्षत्रयोगनिरताः संख्यानार्थं च ताभवन्। पल्यो वै तस्य राजेन्द्र सोमस्य शुभकर्मणः॥
en: Connected with the several constellations, those wives, O king, of Soma of glorious deeds, served to help men in calculating time.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: तास्तु सर्वा विशालाक्ष्यो रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि। अत्यात्यत तासां तु रोहिणी रूपसम्पदा॥
en: Endued with large eyes, all of them were peerless in beauty in the world. In beauty however, Rohini excelled them all.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ततस्तस्यां स भगवान् प्रीतें चक्रे निशाकरः। साऽस्य हृद्या बभूवाथ तस्मात् तां बुभुजे सदा॥
en: The worshipful Soma took great fancy for her. She was very much liked by him and therefore, he enjoyed the pleasures of her company alone.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: पुरा हि सोमो राजेन्द्र रोहिण्यामवसत् परम्। ततस्ताः कुपिताः सर्वा नक्षत्राख्या महात्मनः॥
en: Formerly, O king, Soma lived long with Rohini exclusively. For this, those other wives of his, the constellations, became displeased with that high-souled one.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ता गत्वा पितरं प्राहुः प्रजापतिमतन्द्रिताः। सोमो वसति नास्मासु रोहिणी भजते सदा॥
en: Going to their father Daksha, that Lord of creation, they said to him-"Soma does not live with us. He always lives with Rohini only.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ता वयं सहिताः सर्वास्त्वत्सकाशे प्रजेश्वर। वत्स्यामो नियताहारस्तपश्चरणतत्पराः॥
en: All of us, therefore, O Lord of creatures, shall live in your house practising austere penances."

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: श्रुत्वा तासां तु वचनं दक्षः सोममथाब्रवीत्। समं वर्तस्व भार्यासु मा त्वाऽधर्मो महान् स्पृशेत्।। ५२
en: Hearing those words of theirs, Daksha saw Soma and said to him, ""Treat all your wives equally. Do not commit a great sin."

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: तास्तु सर्वाऽब्रवीद् दक्षो गच्छध्वं शशिनोऽन्तिकम्। समं वत्स्यति सर्वासु चन्द्रमा मम शासनात्॥
en: And Daksha then said to those daughters of his-"Go, all of you, to Shashin. At my command, he, surnamed Chandramas, will treat you all equally,"

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: विसृष्टास्तास्तथा जग्मुः शीतांशुभवनं तदा। तथापि सोमो भगवान् पुनरेव महीपते॥ रोहिणी निवसत्येव प्रीयमाणो मुहुर्मुहुः।
en: Dismissed by him, they then proceeded to the house of him having cool rays. Still the worshipful Soma, O king, behaved as before, for pleased with Rohini alone, he always lived in her company.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ततस्ताः सहिताः सर्वा भूयः पितरमब्रुवन्॥ तव शुश्रूषणे युक्ता वत्स्यामो हि तवान्तिके। सोमो वसति नास्मासु नाकरोद् वचनं तव॥
en: His other wives then once more came to the abode of their father and said to him-"Serving you, we will live under your protection. Soma does not live with us and does not obey your commands."

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: तासां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा दक्षः सोममथाब्रवीत्। समं वर्तस्व भार्यासु मा त्वां शप्स्ये विरोचन॥
en: Hearing those words of theirs, Daksha once more said to Soma-"Treat all your wives equally. Let me not, O Virochana, curse you."

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: अनादृत्य तु तद् वाक्यं दक्षस्य भगवाशशी। रोहिण्या सार्धमवसत् ततस्ताः कुपिताः पुनः॥
en: Disregarding, however, the behest of Daksha, the worshipful Soma continued to live with Rohini alone. At this, his other wives became once more angry.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: गत्वा च पितरं प्राहुः प्रणम्य शिरसा तदा। सोमो वसति नास्मासु तस्मान्नः शरणं भव॥
en: Going to their father, they bowed to him by lowering their heads and said-"Soma does not live with us. Give us shelter.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: रोहिण्यामेव भगवान् सदा वसति चन्द्रमाः। न त्वद्वचो गणयति नास्मासु स्नेहमिच्छति॥ तस्मान्नस्त्राहि सर्वा वै यथानः सोम आविशेत्।
en: The worshipful Chandramas always lives with Rohini exclusively. He does not value your words and does not wish to love us. Therefore, save us so that Soma may accept us all.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान् क्रुद्धो यक्ष्माणां पृथिवीपते॥ ससर्ज रोषात् सोमाय त चोडुपतिमाविशत्।
en: Hearing those words, the worshipful Daksha, O king, became angry and imprecated the curse of phthisis upon Some. Thus did that disease affect the king of stars.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: स यक्ष्मणाभिभूतासमाक्षीयताहरहः शशी॥ यत्नं चाप्यकरोद् राजन् मोक्षार्थं तस्य यक्ष्मणः। इष्टवेभिर्महाराज विविधाभिर्निशाकरः॥ न चामुच्यत शापाद् वै क्षयं चैवाभ्यगच्छत्।
en: Afflicted with phthisis, the moon began to waste away day by day. He tried much to get rid of that disease by celebrating various sacrifices, O king. The Moon, however, could not free hiinself from that curse. On the other hand, hi daily grew lean and emaciated.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ततः सोमे ओषध्यो न प्रजज्ञिरे॥ निरास्वादरसाः सर्वा हतवीर्याश्च सर्वशः।
en: On account, of the wasting of Soma the deciduous herbs failed to grow, Their juices dried up they became tasteless and all of them lost their virtues.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ओषधीनां क्षये जाते प्राणिनामपि संक्षयः॥ कृशाश्चासन् प्रजाः सर्वाः क्षीयमाणे निशाकरे।
en: And on account of the absence of the deciduous herbs, living creatures also began to die. Indeed, owing to the wasting of Soma, all creatures grew emaciated.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ततो देवाः समागम्य सोममूचुर्महीपते॥ किमिदं भवतो रूपमीदृशं न प्रकाशते। कारणं ब्रूहि नः सर्वं येनेदं ते महद् भयम्॥
en: Then all the celestials, approaching Soma, O king, asked him, saying-"Why is it that your form is not so beautiful and resplendent as before? Tell us whence has originated this great calamity.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं त्वत्तो विधास्यामस्ततो वयम्। एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच सर्वांस्ताशशलक्षणः॥ शापस्य लक्षणं चैव यक्ष्माणं च तथाऽऽत्मनः। देवास्तथा वचः श्रुत्वा गत्वा दक्षमथाब्रुवन्॥
en: Hearing your answer, we shall do what is needed for removing your fear.” Thus addressed the god, having the hare for his mark, replied to them and informed them of the cause of the curse and of the phthisis with which he was attacked.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: प्रसीद भगवन् सोमे शापोऽयं विनिवर्त्यताम्। असौ हि चन्द्रमाः क्षीणः किञ्चिच्छेषो हि लक्ष्यते॥७०
en: Having heard those words the celestials repaired to Daksha and said-"Be pleased O worship one, with Soma. Withdrew your this curse.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: क्षयाचैवास्य देवेश प्रजाश्चैव गताः क्षयम्। वीरुदोषधयश्चैव बीजानि विविधानि च॥
en: The Moon is very emaciated. Only a small portion of his body is seen. On account of his wasting, O Lord of the celestials, all creatures also are wasting. Creepers and herbs of various sorts are also wasting.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: तेषां क्षये क्षयोऽस्माकं विनाऽस्मभिर्जगच किम्। इति ज्ञात्वा लोकगुरो प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: By their waste we ourselves also are suffering emaciation. Without us, what will this some universe be. Knowing this, O lord of the universe, it behoves you to be pleased with Soma."

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: एवमुक्तस्ततो देवान् प्राह वाक्यं प्रजापतिः। नैतच्छक्यं मम वचो व्यावर्तयितुमन्यथा॥
en: Thus addressed, Daksha, that Lord of creatures, said:-"It is impossible to make my words prove otherwise.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: हेतुना तु महाभाग निवर्तिष्यति केनचित्। समं वर्ततु सर्वासु शशी भार्यासु नित्यशः॥
en: By contrivance, however, O celestials, by words may be withdrawn. Let the moon treat his wives equally.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: सरस्वत्या वरे तीर्थे उन्मजशशलक्षणः। पुनर्वर्धिष्यते देवास्तद् वै सत्यं वचो मम॥
en: Having bathed also in that foremost of tirthas on the Sarasvati, the hare-embalmed god shall regain his strength. These words of mine are true.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: मासार्धं च क्षयं सोमो नित्यमेव गमिष्यति। मासार्धं तु सदा वृद्धिं सत्यमेतद् वचो मम॥
en: For half the month Soma shall decrease every day and for half the month following he will increase daily. These words of mine are true.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: समुद्रं पश्चिमं गत्वा सरस्वत्यब्धिसङ्गमम्। आराधयतु देवेशं ततः कान्तिमवाप्स्यति॥
en: Proceeding to the western ocean at the spot where the Sarasvati joins the ocean that vast repository of waters, let him worship that God of gods Mahadeva there. He will then regain his from and beauty."

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: सरस्वती ततः सोमः स जगामर्षिशासनात्। प्रभासं प्रथमं तीर्थं सरस्वत्या जगाम ह॥
en: Thus commanded by the Rishi Daksha, Soma then proceeded to the Sarasvati. He reached the greatest of tirthas called Prabhasa belonging to the Sarasvati.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: अमावास्यां महातेजास्तत्रोन्मजन् महाद्युतिः। लोकान् प्रभासयामास शीतंशुत्वमवाप च॥
en: Bathing there on the day of the new moon, that god of great energy and great effulgence women regained his cool rays and began again to lleum the universe.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: देवास्तु सर्वे राजेन्द्र प्रभासं प्राप्य पुष्कलम्। सोमेन सहिता भूत्वा दक्षस्य प्रमुखेऽभवन्॥
en: All the creatures also, O king, having gone to Prabhasa, returned with Soma amongst them to where Daksha was.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ततः प्रजापतिः सर्वा विससर्जाथ देवताः। सोमं च भगवान् प्रीतो भूयो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ मावमंस्थाः स्त्रियः पुत्र मा च विप्रान् कदाचन। गच्छ युक्तः सदा भूत्वा कुरु वै शासनं मम॥
en: Receiving them properly that Lord of creatures then sent them away. Plcased with Soma, the worshipful Daksha once more addressed him, saying-"Do not, O son, disregard and never disregard Brahmanas. Go and obey my commands."

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: स विसृष्टो महाराज जगामाथ स्वमालयम्। प्रजाश्च मुदिता भूत्वा पुनस्तस्थुर्यथा पुरा॥
en: Dismissed by him, Soma returned to his own abode. All creatures began to live joyously as before.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: एवं ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथा शप्तो निशाकरः। प्रभासं च यथा तीर्थं तीर्थानां प्रवरं महत्॥
en: I have thus told you everything about how the Moon had been cursed and how also Prabhasa became the best of all tirthas.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: अमावास्यां महाराज नित्यशः शशलक्षणः। स्नात्वा ह्याप्यायते श्रीमान् प्रभासे तीर्थ उत्तमे॥
en: On everyday of the new moon, O king, the god, having the hare for his mark, bathes in the excellent tirtha of Prabhasa and regains his form and beauty.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: अतक्षेतत् प्रजानन्ति प्रभासमिति भूमिप। प्रभां हि परमां लेभे तस्मिन्नुन्मज्ज्य चन्द्रमाः॥
en: O lord of Earth, that tirtha is known by the name of Prabhasa, because bathing there the moon regained his great (Prabha) effulgence.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: ततस्तु चमसोद्भेदमच्युतस्त्वगमद् बली। चमसोद्भेद इत्येवं यं जनाः कथयन्त्युत॥
en: After this, the mighty and illustrious Baladeva proceeded to Chamasodbheda, that is to that tirtha which is called by that name.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: तत्र दत्त्वा च दानानि विशिष्टानि हलायुधः। उषित्वा रजनीमेकां स्नात्वा च विधिवत्तदा॥
en: Distributing many precious presents at that place, the hero, having the plough for his weapon, passed one night there and performed his absolutions duly.

description: The origin of Prabhasa described by Vaishampayana
sn: उदपानमथागच्छत्त्वरावान् केशवाग्रजः। आद्यं स्वस्त्ययनं चैव यत्रावाप्य महत् फलम्॥ स्निग्धत्वादोषधीनां च भूमेश्च जनमेजय। जानान्ति सिद्धा राजेन्द्र नष्टामपि सरस्वतीम्॥
en: The elder brother of Keshava then speedily repaired to Udapana. Although the Sarasvati is not visible there, yet persons endued with ascetic success, no account of their obtaining great merits and sanctity of that spot and also of the coolness of the herbs and of the land there, know that the river has an invisible current, O king, underneath the earth there.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मान्नदीगतां चापि ह्युदपानं यशस्विनः। त्रितस्य च महाराज जगामाथ हलायुधः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Baladeva proceeded next to the tirtha Udapana in the Sarasvati, that had formerly been the habitation, O king, of the illustrious ascetic Trita.

sn: तत्र दत्त्वा बहु द्रव्यं पूजयित्वा तथा द्विजान्। उपस्पृश्य च तत्रैव प्रहृष्टो मुसलायुधः॥
en: Having distributed profuse wealth and worshipped the Brahmanas, the hero, having the plough for his weapon, bathed there and was filled with joy.

sn: तत्र धर्मपरो भूत्वा त्रितः स सुमहातपाः । कूपे च वसता तेन सोमः पीतो महात्मना॥
en: The great and pious ascetic Trita had lived there. While in a hole that great man had drunk the Soma juice.

sn: तत्र चैनं समुत्सृज्य भ्रातरौ जग्मतुर्ग्रहान्। ततस्तौ वै शशापाथ त्रितो ब्राह्मणसत्तमः॥
en: His two brothers, dashing him down into a pit, had returned home. That foremost of Brahmanas, viz., Trita, had thereupon cursed them both."

sn: जनमेजय उवाच उदपानं कथं ब्रह्मन् कथं च सुमहातपाः। पतितः किं च संत्यक्तो भ्रातृभ्यां द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Janamejaya said "What is the origin of Udapana? How did the great ascetic Trita fall into a pit there? Why was that foremost of Brahmanas thrown into that pit by his brothers?

sn: कूपे कथं च हित्वैनं भ्रातुरौ जग्मुतुहान्। कथं च याजयामास पपौ सोमं त वै कथम्॥ एतदाचक्ष्व मे ब्रह्मश्रोतव्यं यदि मन्यसे।
en: How did his brothers, after throwing him into that hole, come back to their home? How did Trita celebrate his sacrifice and how did he drink Soma? Describe all his O Brahmana, if you think that I am worthy of listening to it.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच आसन् पूर्वयुगे राजन् मुनयो भ्रातरस्त्रयः॥ एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितश्चादित्य संनिभाः।
en: Vaishampayana said In a former cycle, O king, there were three ascetic brothers. They were called Ekata, Dvita and Trita and all three were effulgent like the sun.

sn: सर्वे प्रजापतिसमाः प्रजावन्तस्तथैव च॥ ब्रह्मलोकजिताः सर्वे तपसा ब्रह्मवादिनः। तेषां त तपसा प्रीतो नियमेन दमेन च॥
en: They were like Lords of the creation and had children. Brahmavadins as they were they had, by their ascetic penances, acquired the privilege of attaining to the regions of Brahman after death.

sn: अभवद् गौतमो नित्यं पिता धर्मरतः सदा। स तु दीर्घेण कालेन तेषां प्रीतिमवाप्य च॥
en: For their penances, vows and self-restraint, their father, the virtuous Gautama, became highly pleased with them.

sn: जगाम् भगवान् स्थानमनुरूपमिवात्मनः। राजानस्तस्य ये ह्यासान् याज्या राजन् महात्मनः॥
en: Greatly pleased with his sons, the worshipful Gautama, after living a long life here, went at last to the region in the other world that was fit for him.

sn: ते सर्वे स्वर्गते तस्मिंस्तस्य पुत्रानपूजयन्। तेषां तु कर्मणा राजंस्तथा चाध्ययनेन च॥
en: Those kings, however, O king, that were the disciples of Gautama, continued to worship Gautama's sons after his ascension to heaven.

sn: त्रितः स श्रेष्ठतां प्राप यथैवास्य पिता तथा।
en: Amongst them however, Trita, by his acts and Vedic studies, O king, became the foremost, even like his father Gautama.

sn: तथा सर्वे महाभाग मुनयः पुण्यलक्षणा॥ अपूजयन् महाभागं यथास्य पितरं तथा।
en: Then all the great and pious ascetics began to worship Trita as they had worshipped his father Gautama before him.

sn: कदाचिद्धि ततो राजन् भ्रातरवेकतद्वितौ॥ यज्ञार्थं चक्रतुश्चिन्तां तथा वित्तार्थमेव च।
en: Once upon a time, the two brothers Etaka and Dvita thought of celebrating a sacrifice and became anxious for wealth.

sn: तयोर्बुद्धिः समभवत् त्रितं गृह्य परंतप॥ याज्यान् सर्वानुपादाय प्रतिगृह्य पशूस्ततः। सोमं पास्यामहे हृष्टाः प्राप्य यज्ञं महाफलम्॥ चक्रुश्चैवं तथा राजन् भ्रातरस्त्रय एव च।
en: They thought that they would take Trita with them and calling upon all their disciples and collecting the needful number of animals, they would joyfully drink the Soma juice and acquire the great merits of sacrifice. The three brothers, then O king, did as settled.

sn: तथा ते तु परिक्रम्य याज्यान् सर्वान् पशून् प्रति॥ याजयित्वा ततो याज्याँल्लब्ध्वा तु सुबहून पशून्। याज्येन कर्मणा तेन प्रतिगृह्य विधानतः॥ प्राची दिशं महात्मान आज्गमुस्ते महर्षयः।
en: Calling upon all their disciples for animals and helping them in their sacrifices and receiving a large number of animals from them as gifts for the priestly services rendered by them those high-souled and great Rishis came towards the east.

sn: समुपलप्स्यते। त्रितस्तेषां महाराज पुरस्ताद् याति हृष्टवत्॥ एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव पृष्टतः कालयन् पशून्।
en: Trita, O king, was cheerfully walking before them. Ekata and Dvita were in his rear, conducting the animals.

sn: तयोश्चिन्ता समभवद् दृष्ट्वा पशुगणं महत्॥ कथं च स्युरिमा गाव आवाभ्यां हि विना त्रितम्।
en: Sceing that large herd of animals they began to think as to how they two could appropriate that property without giving a share to Trita.

sn: तावन्योन्यं समाभाष्य एकतश्च द्वितश्च ह॥ यदूचतुर्मिथः पापौ तन्निबोध जनेश्वर।
en: Hear, O king, what those two sinful wretches, viz., Ekata and Dvita, said to each other.

sn: त्रितो यज्ञेषु कुशलस्त्रितो वेदेषु निष्ठितः॥ अन्यास्तु बहुला गावस्त्रितः
en: They said-"Trita is a clever priest. Trita is well read in the Vedas. Trita is capable of earning many other kine.

sn: तदावां सहितौ भूत्वा गाः प्रकाल्य व्रजावहे॥ त्रितोऽपि गच्छतां काममावभ्यां वै विना कृतः।
en: Let us two, therefore go away, taking the kine with us. Let Trita go wherever he likes, without being in our company."

sn: तेषामागच्छतां रात्रौ पथिस्थानां वृकोऽभवत्।॥ तत्र कूपोऽविदूरेऽभूत् सरस्वत्यास्तटे महान्।
en: As they proceeded, they were benighted on the way. They then saw a wolf before them. Not far from that spot was a deep hole on the bank of the Sarasvati.

sn: अद्य त्रितो वृकं दृष्ट्वा पथि तिष्ठन्तमग्रतः॥ तद्भयादपसर्पन वै तस्मिन् कूपे पपात ह।
en: Trita, who was going before, seeing the wolf, rain in fear and fell into that hole.

sn: अगाधे सुमहाघोरे सर्वभूतभयंकरे॥ त्रितस्ततो महाराज कूपस्थो मुनिसत्तमः।
en: That hole was deep and terrible and capable of striking terror to all creatures. Then Trita, O king, that best of ascetics, from within that hole, began to bewail. His two brothers heard his cries.

sn: आर्तनाद ततश्चक्रे तौ तु शुश्रुवतुर्मुनी॥ तं ज्ञात्वा पतितं कूपे भ्रातरावेकतद्वितौ। वृकत्रासाच लोभाच्च समुत्सृज्य प्रजग्मतुः॥
en: Knowing that he had fallen into a pit, his brothers Ekata and Dvita, actuated by fear of the wolf as also by temptation, went on, leaving behind their brother.

sn: भ्रातृभ्यां पशुलुब्धाभ्यामुत्सृष्टः स महातपाः। उदपाने तदा राजन् निर्जले पांसुसंवृते॥ त्रित आत्मानमालक्ष्य कूपे वीरुत्तृणावृते।
en: Thus left behind by his two brothers who were tempted to appropriate those animals, the great ascetic. Trita, O king, while within that lonely pit covered with dust.

sn: निमग्नं भरतश्रेष्ट नरके दुष्कृती यथा॥ स बुद्ध्यागणयत् प्राज्ञो मृत्योर्भीतो ह्यसोमपः।
en: Herbs and creepers, thought himself sunk, O best of the Bharatas, into hell like a sinful person.

sn: सोमः कथं तु पातव्य इहस्थेन मया भवेत्॥ स एवमभिनिश्चित्य तस्मिन् कूपे महातपाः।
en: He was afraid of dying became he had not earned the merit of drinking Soma juice. Greatly wise as he was he began to think with the help of his intelligence as to how he could succeed in drinking Soma cven there.

sn: ददर्श वीरुधं तत्र लम्बमानां यदृच्छया।॥
en: While thinking thus the great ascetic, standing in that pit, beheld a creeper hanging down into it.

sn: पांसुग्रस्ते ततः कूपे विचन्त्य सलिलं मुनिः। अग्नीन् संकल्पयामास होतॄनात्मानमेव च॥
en: Although the pit was dry still the sage perceived the existence of water and of sacrificial fires there. Imagining himself the sacrificial priest.

sn: ततस्तां वीरुधं सोमं संकल्प्य सुमहातपाः। ऋचो यजूषिं सामानि मनसा चिन्तयन् मुनिः॥
en: The great ascetic took the creeper for the Soma plant. He then mentally uttered the Rich's, the Yayushes and the Samans.

sn: ग्रावाण: शर्कराः कृत्वा प्रचक्रेऽभिषवं नृप। आज्यं च सलिलं चक्रे भागाश्च त्रिदिवौकसाम्॥
en: The pebbles lying there were converted into grains of sugar (in imagination) by Trita. He, then, O king, (mentally) performed his ablutions. He took the water for the clarified butter.

sn: ससोमस्याभिषवं कृत्वा चकार विपुल ध्वनिम्। चाविशद् दिवं राजन् पुनः शब्दस्त्रितस्य वैः॥ समवाप्य च तं यज्ञ यथोक्तं ब्रह्मावादिभिः।
en: He distributed amongst the celestials their respective shares (of those sacrificial offerings). Having next mentally drunk Soma, he began to inake a great noise. Those sounds, O king, first uttered by the sacrificing Rishi, entered into heaven and Trita performed that sacrifice after the manner laid down by Brahmavadins.

sn: वर्तमाने महायज्ञे त्रितस्य सुमहात्मनः॥ आविग्नं त्रिदिवं सर्वं कारणं च न बुद्ध्यते। ततः सुतुमुलं शब्दं शुश्रावाथ बृहस्पतिः॥
en: During the celebration of that sacrifice of the great Trita, the entire region of the celestials was agitated. None knew, however, the cause. Brihaspati heard that loud noise.

sn: श्रुया चैवाब्रवीत सर्वान् देवान् देवपुरोहितः। त्रितस्य वर्तते यज्ञस्तत्र गच्छामहे सुराः॥
en: The priest of the celestials said to them:"Trita is performing a sacrifice. We must go there, you celestials.

sn: स हि क्रुद्धः सृजेदन्यान् देवानपि महातपाः। तच्छुत्वा वचनं तस्य सहिताः सर्वदेवताः॥
en: He is gifted with great ascetic merit if willing, he is capable of creating other celestials."

sn: प्रययुस्तत्र यत्रासौ त्रितयज्ञः प्रवर्तते। ते तत्र गत्वा विबुधास्तं कूपं यत्र स त्रितः॥
en: Hearing those words of Brihaspati, all the gods, in a body, repaired where the sacrifice of Trita was going on.

sn: ददृशुस्तं महात्मानं दीक्षितं यज्ञकर्मसु। दृष्टा चैनं महात्मानं श्रिया परमया युतम्॥
en: Having proceeded to that spot, the gods beheld the great ascetic engaged in the performance of his sacrifice.

sn: ऊचुश्चैनं महाभागं प्राप्ता भागार्थिनो वयम्। अथाब्रवीदृषिर्देवान् पश्यध्वं मां दिवौकसः॥
en: Beholding that great beautiful ascetic the gods addressed him, saying-"We have come for our shares (in your offerings).

sn: अस्मिन् प्रतिभये कूपे निमग्नं नष्टचेतसम्। ततस्त्रितो महाराज भागांस्तेषां यथाविधि॥
en: The Rishi said to them-"Behold me, you denizens of heaven, fallen into this terrible pit almost deprived of my senses.

sn: मन्त्रयुक्तान् समददत् ते च प्रीतास्तदाभवन्।
en: Then Trita, O monarch, duly allotted to them their shares with proper mantras. The gods took them and were greatly delighted. Having duly received their respective shares, the denizens of heaven, pleased with him, granted him the boons he wanted.

sn: ततो यथाविधि प्राप्तान् भागान् प्राप्य दिवौकसः॥ प्रीतात्मानो ददुस्तस्मै वरान् यान् मनसेच्छति।
en: The boon, however, that he prayed for was that the gods should relieve him from his painful condition.

sn: स तु वने वरं देवांस्त्रातुमर्हथ मामितः॥ यश्चेहोपस्पृशेत् कूपे स सोमपगतिं लभेत्।
en: He also said-"Let him that bathes in this well, achieve the end that is attained by persons that have drunk Soma.'

sn: तत्र चोर्मिमती राजन्नुत्पपात सरस्वती॥ तयोत्क्षिप्तः समुत्तस्थौ पूजयंस्त्रिदिवौकसः।
en: Thereat, O king, the Sarasvati. with her waves, appeared within that well. Raised above by her, Trita came up and worshipped the celestials.

sn: तथेति चोक्त्वा विबुधा जग्मू राजन् यथागताः॥ त्रितश्चाभ्यागमत् प्रीतः स्वमेव निलयं तदा।
en: The gods then said to him-"By it as you wish." All of them then, O king, returned to their respective habitations and Trita, filled with joy, proceeded to his owe abode.

sn: क्रुद्धस्तु स समासाद्य तावृषी भ्रातरौ तदा॥ उवाच परुषं वाक्यं शशाप च महातपाः।
en: Meeting with those two Rishi, viz., his brothers, he became enraged with them. Endued with ascetic merit, he spoke harshly to them and cursed them, saying.

sn: पशुलुब्धौ युवां यस्मान्मामुत्सृज्य प्रधावितौ॥ तस्माद् वृकाकृती रौद्रौ दंष्ट्रिणावभितश्चरौ। भवितारौ मया शप्तौ पापेनानेन कर्मणा॥
en: Since, actuated by covetousness, you ran away, leaving me, therefore, you shall become dreadful wolves with sharp teeth and range the forest cursed by me on account of that sinful act of yours.

sn: प्रसवश्चैव युवयोर्गोलाङ्गलक्षवानराः। इत्युक्तेन तदा तेन क्षणादेव विशाम्पते॥ तथाभूतावदृश्येतां वचनात् सत्यवादिनः।
en: Your offspring will also consist of leopards and bears and apes!' After Trita had said these words, O monarch, his two brothers were soon transformed into tigers on account of the curse of that truthful sage.

sn: तत्राप्यमितविक्रान्तः स्पृष्ट्वा तोयं हलायुधः॥ दत्त्वा च विविधान् दायान् पूजयित्वा च वै द्विजान्। उदपानं च तं वीक्ष्य प्रशस्य च पुनः पुनः॥
en: The highly powerful Baladeva touched the waters of Udapana. And he gave away various kinds of wealth there and worshipped many Brahmanas.

sn: नदीगतमदीनात्मा प्राप्तो विनशनं तदा॥
en: Beholding Upadana and and praising it repeatedly, Baladeva next proceeded to Vinashana which also was on the Sarasvati.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो विनशनं राजन् जगामाथ हलायुधः। शूद्राभीरान् प्रति द्वेषाद् यत्र नष्टा सरस्वती॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Then Baladeva, O king, went to Vinashana where the Sarasvati has disappeared out of view in consequence of her hatred for Shudras and Abhiras.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तस्मात् तु ऋषयो नित्यं प्राहुर्विनशनेति च।
en: And because the Sarasvati, on account of this contempt, is lost there Rishis, O chief of the Bharatas, always name the place as Vinashana.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्राप्युपस्पृश्य बल: सरस्वत्यां महाबलः॥ सूभूमिकं ततोऽगच्छत् सरस्वत्यास्तटे वरे।
en: Having bathed in that tirtha of the Sarasvati, the powerful Baladeva then went to Subhumika situate on the excellent bank of the same river.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्र चाप्सरस: शुभ्रा नित्यकालमतन्द्रिताः॥ क्रीडाभिर्विमलाभिश्च क्रीडन्ति विमलाननाः।
en: There many fair-complexioned and beautiful-faced. Apsaras are always engaged in innocent pastimes.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्र देवा: सगन्धर्वा मासि मासि जनेश्वर॥ अभिगच्छन्ति तत् तीर्थं पुण्यं ब्राह्मणसेवितम्।
en: The celestials and the Gandharvas, every month, O king, go to that sacred shrine which is the resort of Brahman himself.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्रादृश्यन्त गन्धर्वास्तथैवाप्सरसां गणाः॥ समेत्य सहिता राजन् यथाप्राप्तं यथासुखम्।
en: The Gandharvas and various clans of Apsaras are to be seen there, O king, passing their days happily.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्र मोदन्ति देवाश्च पितरश्च सवीस्थः॥ पुण्यैः पुष्पैः सदा दिव्यैः कीर्यमाणाः पुनः पुनः।
en: There the celestials and departed manes in the midst of the showers of sacred and auspicious flowers sport in joy.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: आक्रीडभूमिः सा राजस्तासामप्सरसां शुभा॥ सुभूमिकेति विख्याता सरस्वत्यास्तटे वरे।
en: There all the creepers are covered with flowers. And because, O king, that spot is the beautiful sporting ground of those Apsaras, therefore is that shrine on the charming bank of the Sarasvati is called Subhumika.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्र स्नात्वा च दत्त्वा च वसु विप्राय माधवः॥ श्रुत्वा गीतं च तद् दिव्यं वादित्राणां च निःस्वनम्।
en: Baladeva of Madhu's race, having bathed in that tirtha and distributed immense riches amongst the Brahmanas, heard the sound of those celestial songs and musical instruments.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: छायाश्च विपुला दृष्ट्वा देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्॥ गन्धर्वाणां ततस्तीर्थमागच्छद् रोहिणीसुतः।
en: He also saw there many shadows of gods, Gandharvas and Rakshasas. The son of Rohini then proceeded to the tirtha of the Gandharvas.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: विश्वावसुमुखास्तत्र गन्धर्वास्तपसान्विताः॥ नृत्यवादित्रगीतं च कुर्वन्ति सुमनोरमम्।
en: There many Gandharvas, headed by Vishvavasu and possessed of ascetic merit, pass their time in dance and singing many sweet songs.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्र दत्त्वा हलधरो विप्रेभ्यो विविधं वसु॥ अजाविकं गोखरोष्ट्रं सुवर्णं रजतं तथा।
en: Giving away various kinds of riches to the Brahmanas, as also goat and sheep and kine and mules and camels and gold and silver.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: भोजयित्वा द्विजान् कामैः संतर्घ्य च महाधनैः॥ प्रययौ सहितो विप्रैः स्तूयमानश्च माधवः।
en: And feeding many Brahmanas and satisfying them with many rich gifts as desired by them, Baladeva, of Madhu's race, left that place accompanied by many Brahmanas and praised by them.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तस्माद् गन्धर्वतीर्थाच महाबाहुररिंदमः॥ गर्गस्रोतो महातीर्थमाजगामैककुण्डली।
en: Leaving that tirtha the favourite haunt of the Gandharvas, that mighty-armed chastiser of foes, having but one ear-ring, then went to the famous tirtha called Gargashrota.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्र गर्गेण वृद्धेन तपसा भावितात्मना॥ कालज्ञानगतिश्चैव ज्योतिषां च व्यतिक्रमः। उत्पाता दारुणाश्चैव शुभाश्च जनमेजय॥ सरस्वत्या शुभे तीर्थे विदिता वै महात्मना।
en: There, in that sacred tirtha of the Sarasvati, the illustrious and old Garga, having a soul cleansed by ascetic penances, O Janamejaya, had mastered the knowledge of time and its course, of the deviations of luminous bodies (in the sky) and of all auspicious and inauspicious portents.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तस्य नाम्ना च तत् तीर्थं गर्गस्रोत इति स्मृतम्॥ तत्र गर्गं महाभागमृषयः सुव्रता नृप। उपासांचक्रिरे नित्यं कालज्ञानं प्रति प्रभो॥
en: That tirtha was called after his name Gargashrota. There, ( king, highly blessed Rishis of firm vows always waited upon Garga, O lord, for acquiring a knowledge of time.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्र गत्वा महाराज बलः श्वेतानुलेपनः। विधिवद्धि धनं दत्त्वा मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्॥
en: Besmeared with white sandal-paste O king, Baladeva, going to that tirtha, duly distributed wealth amongst many ascetics of pure souls.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: उच्चावचांस्तथा भक्ष्यान् विप्रेभ्यो विप्रदाय सः। नीलवासास्तदागच्छच्छङ्घतीर्थं महायशाः॥
en: Having distributed also many sorts of rich food amongst the Brahmanas, that illustrious one, clad in blue robes, then went to the tirtha called Shankha.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्रापश्यन्महाशङ्ख महामेरुमिवोच्छ्रितम्। श्वेतपर्वतसंकाशमृषिसंधैर्निषेवितम्॥ सरस्वत्यास्तटे जातं नगं तालध्वजो बली।
en: There, on the bank of the Sarasvati that powerful palmyra-emblemed hero beheld a gigantic tree called Mahashankha, tall as Meru, looking like the white-mountain and resorted to by many Rishis.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: यक्षा विद्याधराश्चैव राक्षसाश्चामितौजसः॥ पिशाचाश्वामितबला यत्र सिद्धाः सहस्रशः।
en: There dwell Yakshas and Vidyadharas and Rakshasas of great energy and Pishachas of incomparable might and Siddhas, in thousands.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: ते सर्वे ह्यशनं त्यक्त्वा फलं तस्य वनस्पतेः॥ व्रतैश्च नियमैश्चैव काले काले स्म भुञ्जते। प्राप्तैश्च नियमैस्तैस्तैर्विचरन्तः पृथक् पृथक्॥ अदृश्यमाना मनुजैर्व्यचरन् पुरुषर्षभ। एवं ख्यातो नरव्याघ्र लोकेऽस्मिन् स वनस्पतिः॥२४
en: Desisting from other kinds of food, all of them observe vows and regulations and take at the proper time the fruits of that king of the forest for their sustenance and rove separately unseen by men, O foremost of men. That monarch of the forest, O king, is celebrated throughout the world.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: ततस्तथ सरस्वत्याः पावनं लोकविश्रुतम्। तस्मिंश्च यदुशार्दूलो दत्त्वा तीर्थे पयस्विनीः॥ ताम्रायसानि भाण्डानि वस्त्राणि विविधानि च। पूजयित्वा द्विजांश्चैव पूजितश्च तपोधनैः॥
en: That tree is the cause of this tirtha. Having given away many milch cows, vessels of copper and iron and diverse sorts of other vessels, that foremost Yadu's race, viz., Baladeva, having the plough for his weapon, worshipped the Brahmanas and was adored by them in return. He then, O king, went to the Dvaita lake.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: पुण्यं द्वैतवनं राजन्नाजगाम हलायुधः। तत्र गत्वा मुनीन् दृष्ट्वा नानावेषधरान् बलः॥
en: Arrived there, Vala saw various ascetics dressed diversely. Bathing in its waters, he adored the Brahmanas.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: आप्लुत्य सलिले चापि पूजयामास वै द्विजान्। तथैव दत्त्वा विप्रेभ्यः परिभोगान् सुपुष्कलान्।॥ ततः प्रायाद् बलो राजन् दक्षिणेन सरस्वतीम्।
en: Having distributed profusely amongst the Brahmanas various articles of enjoyment Baladeva then, O king, went on along the southern bank of the Sarasvati.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: गत्वा चैवं महाबाहुर्नातिदूरे महायशाः॥ धर्मात्मा नागधन्वानं तीर्थमागमदच्युतः।
en: The mighty-armed and illustrious Rama, of pure soul and unmitigated glory, then proceeded to the tirtha called Nagadhanvana.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: यत्र पन्नगराजस्य वासुकेः संनिवेशनम्॥ महाद्युतेर्महाराज बहुभिः पन्नगैर्वृतम्। ऋषीणां हि सहस्राणि यत्र नित्यं चतुर्दश॥
en: Abounding with snakes, O king, it was the abode of the highly effulgent Vasuki, the king of serpents. There four and then ten thousand Rishis also lived permanently.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: यत्र देवाः समागम्य वासुकिं पन्नगोत्तमम्। सर्वपन्नगराजानमभ्यषिञ्चन् यथाविधि॥ पन्नगेभ्यो भयं तत्र विद्यते न स्म पौरव।
en: Having come there in days of yore the celestials had, according to due rites, installed the great snake Vasuki as king of all the snakes. There is no fear of snakes in that place Oyou of Kuru's race.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: तत्रापि विधिवद् दत्त्वा विप्रेभ्यो रत्नसंचयान्॥ प्रायात् प्राची दिशं तत्र तत्र तीर्थान्यनेकशः। सहस्रशतसंख्यानि प्रथितानि पदे पदे॥
en: Duly distributing many valuable articles there amongst the Brahmanas Baladeva then set out with face towards the east and reached, one after another, hundreds and thousands of celebrated tirthas situated all around.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: आप्लुत्य तत्र तीर्थेषु यथोक्तं तत्र चर्षिभिः। कृत्वोपवासनियमं दत्त्वा दानानि सर्वशः॥ अभिवाद्य मुनीस्तान् वै तत्र तीर्थनिवासिनः। उद्दिष्टमार्गः प्रययौ यत्र भूयः सरस्वती॥ प्राङमुखं वै निववतै वृष्टिर्वातहता यथा। ऋषीणां नैमिषयाणामवेक्षार्थं महात्मनाम्॥
en: Bathing in all those tirthas and observing fasts and other vows as sanctioned by the Rishis and given away immense riches and saluting all the ascetics who lived there, Baladeva once more set out, along the way pointed out to him by those ascetics for reaching that spot where the Sarasvati turns in an eastward direction like torrents of rain bent by the velocity of the storm. The river took that course for seeing the great Rishis dwelling in the forest of Naimisha.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: निवृत्तां तां सरिच्छेष्टां तत्र दृष्ट्वा तु लागली। बभूव विस्मितो राजन् बल: श्वेतानुलेपनः॥
en: Always smeared with white sandal-paste, Vala, having the plough for his weapon, seeing that great river change her course, was O king, filled with wonder.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कस्मात् सरस्वती ब्रह्मन् निवृत्ता प्राडमुखीभवत्। व्याख्यातमेतदिच्छामि सर्वमध्वर्युसत्तम॥
en: Janamejaya said "Why O Brahmana, did the Sarasvati bend her course there towards the east. O best of Adhvaryus, you should tell me everything regarding this.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: कस्मिंश्चित् कारणे तत्र विस्मितो यदुनन्दनः। निवृत्ता हेतुना केन कथमेव सरिद्वरा॥
en: Why was that delighter of the Yadus filled with wonder? Why, indeed did that best of rivers thus change her course."

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पूर्वं कृतयुगे राजन् नैमिषेयास्तपस्विनः। वर्तमाने सुविपुले सत्रे द्वादशवार्षिके॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Formerly, in the Satya Yuga, O king, the ascetics living in Naimisha were engaged in a great sacrifice extending for twelve years.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: ऋषयो बहवो राजंस्तत् सत्रमभिपेदिरे। उषित्वा च महाभागास्तस्मिन् सत्रे यथाविधि॥ निवृत्ते नैमिषेये वै सत्रे द्वादशवार्षिके। आजग्मुर्ऋषयस्तत्र बहवस्तीर्थकारणात्॥
en: Many Rishis, O king, came to that sacrifice. Passing their time according to proper rites, in the celebration of that sacrifice, those great Rishis, after the termination of that twelve year's sacrifice at Naimisha, set out in large numbers for seeing the various sacred shrines.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: ऋषीणां बहुलत्वात्तु सरस्वत्या विशाम्पते। तीर्थानि नगरायन्ते कूले वै दक्षिणे तदा॥
en: On account of the number of the Rishis, O king, the tirthas on the southern banks of the Sarasvati all looked like towns and cities.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: समन्तपञ्चकं यावत्तावत्ते द्विजसत्तमाः। तीर्थलोभान्नरव्याघ्र नद्यास्तीरं समाश्रिताः॥
en: Those foremost of Brahmanas, O foremost of men, being anxious to enjoy the merits of tirthas, took up thcir abodes on the bank of the river up to Samantapanchaka.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: जुह्वतां तत्र तेषां तु मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्। स्वाध्यायेनातिमहता बभूवुः पूरिता दिशः॥
en: The whole region was as if filled with loud Vedic recitations of those Rishis of pure souls, all engaged in pouring libations of sacrificial fires.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: अग्निहोत्रैस्तस्ततेषां क्रियमाणैर्महात्मनाम्। अशोभत सरिच्छेष्टा दीप्यमानैः समन्ततः॥
en: That best of rivers shone highly beautiful with those burning homa fires all around, over which those great ascetics poured libations of clarified butter.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: वालखिल्या महाराज अश्मकुट्टाश्च तापसाः। दन्तोलूखलिनश्चान्ये प्रसंख्यानास्तथा परे॥ वायुभक्षा जलाहाराः पर्णभक्षाश्च तापसाः। नानानियमयुक्ताश्च तथा स्थण्डिलशायिनः॥ आसन् वै मुनयस्तत्र सरस्वत्याः समीपतः। शोभयन्तः सरिच्छेष्ठां गङ्गामिव दिवौकसः॥
en: Valakhilyas and Ashmarkuttas, Dantolukhalinas, Samprakshyanas and other ascetics, as also those living on air and those living on water and those living on dry leaves of trees and various others who practised diverse kinds of vows and those that lived on bare and hard earth, all came to that spot in the vicinity of the Sarasvati. And they rendered that foremost of rivers highly beautiful like the celestials beautifying with their presence the heavenly rivers called Mandakini.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: शतशश्च समापेतुर्ऋषयः सत्रयाजिनः। तेऽवकाशं न ददृशुः सरस्वत्या महाव्रताः॥
en: Hundreds of Rishis, all given to the observance of sacrifices, came there. Those observers of great vows could not find sufficient accommodation on the banks of the Sarasvati.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: ततो यज्ञोपवीतैस्ते तत्तीर्थं निर्मिमाय वै। जुहुवुश्चाग्निहोत्रांश्च चक्रुश्च विविधाः क्रियाः॥
en: Measuring small plots of land with their sacred threads, they celebrated Agnihotras and other rites.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: ततस्तमऋषिसंघातं निराशं चिन्तयान्वितम्। दर्शयामास राजेन्द्र तेषामर्थे सरस्वती॥
en: The river Sarasvati saw, O king, those Rishis filled with despair and anxiety for want of a commodious tirtha wherein to perform their rites.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: ततः कुञ्जान् बहून कृत्वा संनिवृत्ता सरस्वती। ऋषीणां पुण्यतपसां कारुण्याजनमेजय॥
en: Accordingly that best of streams came there, having made sufficient accommodation on her bank for those Rishis, out of compassion for them, O Janamejaya.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: ततो निवृत्य राजेन्द्र तेषामर्थे सरस्वती। भूयः प्रतीच्यभिमुखी प्रसुस्राव सरिद्वरा॥ अमोघा गमनं कृत्वा तेषां भूयो व्रजाम्यहम्। इत्युद्भुतं महचक्रे तदा राजन् महानदी॥
en: Having thus, O king, changed her course for their sake, the Sarasvati, that best of rivers, once more flowed in a westerly direction, to make the arrival of the Rishis there successful. O king, the great river accomplished there this wonderful feat.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: एवं स कुञ्जो राजन् वै नैमिषीय इति स्मृतः। कुरुश्रेष्ठ कुरुक्षेत्रे कुरुष्व महतीं क्रियाम्॥ तत्र कुञ्जान् बहून दृष्ट्वा निवृत्तां च सरस्वतीम्। बभूव विस्मयस्तत्र रामस्याथ महात्मनः॥
en: Thus those reservoirs of water, O king, where formed in Naimisha. There, Kurukshetra, O Kuru chief, do you celebrate grand sacrifices and rites. Beholding those innumerable reservoirs of water and seeing that best of rivers change her course, the highsouled Rama was filled with wonder.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: उपस्पृश्य तु तत्रापि विधिवद् यदुनन्दनः। दत्त्वा दायान् द्विजातिभ्यो भाण्डानि विविधानि च॥५९ भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च विविधं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रदाय च। ततः प्रायाद् बलो राजन् पूज्यमानो द्विजातिभिः॥ सरस्वतीतीर्थवरं नानाद्विजगणायुतम्। बलरेङगुदकाश्मर्यप्लक्षाश्वत्थबिभीतकैः॥ कङ्कोलैश्च पलाशैश्च करीरैः पीलुभिस्तथा। सरस्वतीतीर्थरुहैस्तरुभिर्विविधैस्तथा॥
en: Bathing in those tirthas duly and distributing wealth and various other articles of enjoyment ainongst the Brahmanas, that delighter of Yadu's race also gave away various kinds of food and desirable articles to them. Adored by those Rishis, Vala, O king, left that foremost of all tirthas on the Sarasvati, at (viz., Sapta-Sarasvat). Numerous birds also lived there. And it abounded with Vadari, Inguda, Kacmaryya, Plahsha, Ashvattha, Vibhitaka, Kakkola, Palasha, Karira, Pilu and various other kinds of trees that grow on the banks of the Sarasvati.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: करूषकवरैश्चैव बिल्वैराम्रातकैस्तथा। अतिमुक्तकषण्डैश्च पारिजातैश्च शोभितम्॥
en: And it was adorned with forests of Karushakas, Vilvas Vilvas and Amratakas and Atimuktas and Kashandas and Parijatas.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: कदलीवनभूयिष्ठं दृष्टिकान्तं मनोहरम्। वाय्वम्बुफलपर्णादैर्दन्तोलूखलिकैरपि॥ तथाश्मकुट्टैर्वानेयैर्मुनिभिर्बहुभिर्वृतम्। स्वाध्यायघोषसंघुष्टं मृगयूथशताकुलम्॥
en: It abounded with forests of Plantains pleasant to view and most charming. And it was haunted by various ascetics, some living on air, some water, some on fruits, some on leaves, some on raw raise again which they husked with the aid only of stones and some that were called Vaneyas. And it was filled with the chauntings of the Vedas and abounded with diverse kinds of animals.

description: The history of the Tirthas Vinashana, Gargashrota, Shakuha, Subhumika
sn: अहिंस्रैर्धर्मपरमैनूभिपत्यर्थसेवितम्। सप्तसारस्वतं तीर्थमाजगाम हलायुधः॥ यत्र मकुणक: सिद्धस्तपस्तेपे महामुनिः॥
en: And it was the favourite abode of men shorn of malice and devoted to righteousness. Baladeva, having the plough for his weapon, arrived at that tirtha, called the Sapta-Sarasvat, where the great ascetic Mankanaka had his penances successfully practised.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: जनमेजय उवाच सप्तसारस्वतं कस्मात् कश्च मङ्कणको मुनिः। कथं सिद्धः स भगवान् कश्चास्य नियमोऽभवत्॥
en: Janamejaya said "Why was that tirtha called Sapta-Sarasvat? Who was the ascetic Mankanaka? How was that worshipful one successful? What were his vows and observances?

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: कस्य वंशे समुत्पन्नः किं चाधीतं द्विजोत्तम। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विधिवद् द्विजसत्तम।॥
en: In whose family was he born? What books did that great Rishi study? I desire to hear all this, O foremost of Rishis.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच राजन् सप्त सरस्वत्यो याभिर्व्याप्तमिदं जगत्। आहूता बलवदभिर्हि तत्र तत्र सरस्वती॥
en: Vaishampayana said "O king, the seven Sarasvati cover this Universe. Wherever the Sarasvati was called the energetic Rishis, there she did go.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: सुप्रभा काञ्चनाक्षी त विशाला च मनोरमा। सरस्वती चौघवती सुरेणुर्विमलोदका॥
en: These are the seven forms of the Sarasvati, viz., Suprabha, Kanchanakshi, Vishala, Manorama, Oghavati, Surenu and Vimalodaka.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: पितामहस्य महतो वर्तमाने महामखे। वितते यज्ञवाटे च संसिद्धेषु द्विजातिषु॥
en: Brahma had at one time celebrated a great sacrifice. While that sacrifice was being celebrated on the site selected, many Rishis, crowned with ascetic success, came there.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: पुण्याहघोषैर्विमलैवैदानां निनदैस्तथा। देवेषु चैव व्यग्रेषु तस्मिन् यज्ञविधौ तदा॥
en: The spot was filled with the sound of the recitation and the chaunting of the Vedas. Seeing those sacrificial rites, even the very gods lost their temper.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: तत्र चैव महाराज दीक्षिते प्रपितामहे। यजतस्तस्य सत्रेण सर्वकामसमृद्धिना॥ मनसा चिन्तिता ह्या धर्मार्थकुशलैस्तदा। उपतिष्ठन्ति राजेन्द्र द्विजातींस्तत्र तत्र ह॥
en: There, O king, while the grandfather was initiated in the sacrifice and was performing the grand ceremony capable of granting prosperity and wished-for objects many great Rishis, conversant with virtue and profit, were present. As soon as they thought of necessary articles, they, O king, immediately came before the Rishis.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: जगुश्च तत्र गन्धर्वा ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः। वादित्राणि च दिव्यानि वादयामासुरञ्जसा॥
en: The Gandharvas sang and the Apsaras danced. And they played upon many celestial instruments.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: तस्य यज्ञस्य सम्पत्या तुतुषुर्देवता अपि। विस्मयं परमं जग्मुः किमु मानुषयोनयः॥
en: The provisions collected in that sacrifice satisfied the very celestials. What shall I say then of men? The very celestials were filled with wonder.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: वर्तमाने तथा यज्ञे पुष्करस्थे पितामहे। अब्रुवन्नृषयो राजन्नायं यज्ञो महागुणः॥ न दृश्यते सरिच्छेष्टा यस्मादिह सरस्वती। तच्छुत्वा भगवान् प्रीतः सस्माराथ सरस्वतीम्॥
en: During the progress of that sacrifice at Pushkara and in the presence of Brahma, the Rishis, O king, said-"This sacrifice is not successful, sine that foremost of rivers, viz., Sarasvati, is not to be seen here.” Hearing these words. the divine Brahman meditated on Sarasvati.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: पितामहेन यजता आहूता पुष्करेषु वै। सुप्रभा नाम राजेन्द्र नाम्ना तत्र सरस्वती॥
en: Summoned at Pushkara by the grandfather engaged in the celebration of a sacrifice, Sarasvati, O king came there under the name of Suprava.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: तां दृष्ट्वा मुनयस्तुष्टास्तवरायुक्तां सरस्वतीम्। पितामहं मानयन्तीं क्रतुं ते बहु मेनिरे॥
en: Seeing Sarasvati pay that regard to the grandfather, the ascetics regarded that sacrifice with great esteem.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: एवमेषा सरिच्छेष्टा पुष्करेषु सरस्वती। पितामहार्थ सम्भूता तुष्ट्यर्थं च मनीषिणाम्॥
en: Thus that foremost of rivers, viz., Sarasvati, made her appearance at Pushkara for pleasing the grandfather and the ascetics.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: नैमिषे मुनयो राजन् समागम्य समासते। तत्र चित्राः कथा ह्यासन् वेदं प्रति जनेश्वर॥
en: On another occasion, O king many Munis assembled at Naimisha. They had many discussions amongst them, O king, on the Vedas.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: यत्र ते मुनयो ह्यासन् नानास्वाध्यायवेदिनः। ते समागम्य मुनयः सस्मरुवै सरस्वतीम्॥
en: There those ascetics, conversant with various scriptures, thought of the Sarasvati.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: सा तु ध्याता महाराज ऋषिभिः सत्रयाजिभिः। समागतानां राजेन्द्र साहाय्यार्थं महात्मनाम्॥ आजगाम महाभाग तत्र पुण्या सरस्वती। नैमिषे काञ्चनाक्षी तु मुनीनां सत्रयाजिनाम्॥
en: Thus thought of, O king, by those Rishis performing a sacrifice, the highly blessed and sacred Sarasvati, for helping those great Munis, made her appearance at Naimisha and was accordingly called Kanchanakshi.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: आगता सरितां श्रेष्ठा तत्र भारत पूजिता। गयस्य यजमानस्य गयेष्वेव महाक्रतुम्॥ आहूता सरितां श्रेष्ठा गययज्ञे सरस्वती। विशालां तु गयस्यहुर्ऋषयः संशितव्रताः॥
en: Worshipped of all, that best of rivers, thus came there, O Bharata. While king Gaya was engaged in the celebration of a great sacrifice at Gaya the foremost of rivers, Sarasvati, summoned at Gaya's sacrifice, came there. The Rishis of rigid vows, that were present there, named her Vishala at Gaya.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: सरित् सा हिमावत्पाझंडत् प्रस्रुता शीघ्रगामिनी। औद्दालकेस्तथा यज्ञे यजतस्तस्य भारत।॥
en: That quick-coursing river originates from the side of Himavat. Ouddalaka had also, O Bharata, performed a sacrifice.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: समेते सर्वतः स्फीते मुनीनां मण्डले तदा। उत्तरे कोसलाभागे पुण्ये राजन् महात्मनः॥
en: A number of ascetics were also assembled there. It was in the sacred north Koshala, O kir that sacrifice of the great Ouddalaka was celebrated.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: उद्दालकेन यजता पूर्वं ध्यात्वा सरस्वती। आजगाम सरिच्छेष्ठा तं देशं मुनिकारणात्॥
en: Before Ouddalaka began his sacrifice, he had thought of the Sarasvati. That foremost of rivers came there for the sake of those Rishis.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: पूज्यमाना मुनिगणैर्वल्कलाजिसंवृत्तैः। मनोरमेति विख्याता सा हि तैर्मनसा कृता॥ सुरेणर्ऋषभे द्वीपे पुण्ये राजर्षिसेविते।
en: Worshipped of all those Munis clad in barks and deer-skins, she passed by the name of Manorama as those Rishis mentally called her.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: कुरोश्च यजमानस्य कुरुक्षेत्रे महात्मनः॥ आजगाम महाभाग सरिच्छेष्ठा सरस्वती।
en: While, again the great Kuru was engaged in a sacrifice at Kurukshetra, that foremost of rivers, the highly sacred Sarasvati, came there.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: ओघवत्यपि राजेन्द्र वसिष्ठेन महात्मना॥ समाहूता कुरुक्षेत्रे दिव्यातोया सरस्वती।
en: Summoned, O king, by the great Vashishtha who assisted Kuru in his sacrifice, the Sarasvati, of celestial water, came to Kurukshetra and passed by the name of Oghavati.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: दक्षेण यजता चापि गङ्गाद्वारे सरस्वती॥ सुरेणुरिति विख्याता प्रस्रुता शीघ्रगामिनी।
en: Daksha at one time celebrated a sacrifice at the source of Ganga. The Sarasvati appeared there under the name of the quick-coursing Surenu.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: विमलोदा भगवती ब्रह्मणा यजता पुनः॥ समाहूता ययौ तत्र पुण्ये हैमवते गिरौ।
en: Once again, while Brahınan was engaged in a sacrifice on the sacred forest of the Himavat mountains, the worshipful Sarasvati, summoned by him, came there.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: एकीभूतास्ततस्तास्तु तस्मिंस्तीर्थे समागताः॥ सप्तसारस्वतं तीर्थ ततस्तु
en: All these seven streams then came and joined together in that tirtha where Baladeva came. And because the seven joined together at that spot, therefore is that tirtha known on earth by the name of Sapta-Sarasvati.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: इति सप्तसरस्वत्यो नामतः परिकीर्तिताः॥ सप्ता सारस्वतं चैव तीर्थ पुण्य तथा स्मृतम्। प्रथितं भुवि।
en: Thus have I described to you the seven Sarasvatis, according to their names. I have also given you an account of the sacred tirtha called Satpa-Sarasvat.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: शृणु मङ्कणकस्यापि कौमारब्रह्मचारिणः॥ आपगामवगाढस्य राजन् प्रक्रीडितं महत्। दृष्ट्वा यदृच्छया यत्र स्त्रियमम्भसि भारत॥ जायन्तीं रुचिरापाङ्गी दिग्वाससमनिन्दिताम्। सरस्वत्यां महाराज चस्कन्दे वीर्यमम्भसि॥
en: Listen now to a great deed of Mankanaka, who had from his youth led the life of a Brahmacharin. While perforining his abolutions in the river, he saw one day, O Bharata, a damsel of beautiful features and fair brows, bathing in the river with her body uncovered. At this sight, O monarch, the seminal fluid of the Rishi dropped to the Sarasvati.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: तद् रेत: स तु जग्राह कलशे वै महातपाः। सप्तधा प्रविभागं तु कलशस्थं जगाम ह॥
en: The great ascetic took it up and kept it within his earthen pot. Deposited within that pot, the fluid was divided into seven parts.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: तत्रर्षयः सप्त जाता जज्ञिरे मरुतां गणाः। वायुवेगो वायुबलो वायुहा वायुमण्डलः॥ वायुज्वालो वायुरेता वायुचक्राश्च वीर्यवान्। एवमेते समुत्पन्ना मरुतां जनयिष्णवः॥
en: From those seven portions were born seven Rishis, from whom originated the forty nine Maruts. The Rishis named Vayuvega, Vayuhan, Vayumandala, Vayujata, Vayuretas, Vayuchakra. Thus were born those progenitors of the various Maruts.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: इदमत्यद्भुतं राजन्शृण्वाश्चर्यतरं भुवि। महर्षेश्चरितं यादृकं त्रिपुं लोकेषु विश्रुतम्॥
en: Hear now of a more wonderful account O king, of a highly marvellous conduct of that great Rishi which is well known in the three worlds.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: पुरा मङ्कणकः सिद्धः कुशाग्रेणेति नः श्रुतम्। क्षतः किल करे राजस्तस्य शाकरसोऽस्रवत॥
en: Formerly, after Mankanaka had become Successful, O king, his hand became pierced seven were with a Kusha blade. Thereupon a vegetable juice came out of the wound and not blood.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: स वै शाकरसं दृष्ट्वा हर्षाविष्टः प्रनृत्तवान्। ततस्तस्मिन् प्रनृत्ते वै स्थावरं जङ्गमं च यत्॥
en: Seeing that vegetable juice, the Rishi was filled with joy and danced about there. Beholding him dance, all mobile and immobile creatures, O hero, overpowered by his energy, began to dance.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: प्रनृत्तमुभयं वीर तेजसा तस्य मोहितम्। ब्रह्मादिभिः सुरै राजऋषिभिश्च तपोधनैः॥ विज्ञप्तो वै महादेव ऋषेरर्थे नराधिप। नायं नृत्येद् यथा देव तथा त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Then the celestials with Brahma at their head and the Rishis, having asceticism for their wealth, O king, all approached Mahadeva and informed him of the doings of the Rishi (Mankanaka). And they said to him-Thou shouldst, O god, do that which may prevent the Rishi from dancing."

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: ततो देवो मुनिं दृष्ट्वा हर्षाविष्टमतीव ह। सुराणां हितकामार्थं महादेवोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Then Mahadeva, seeing the Rishi filled with great joy and desirous of doing good to the celestials addressed him, saying.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: भो भो ब्राह्मण धर्मज्ञ किमर्थं नृत्यते भवान्। हर्षस्थानं किमर्थं च तवेदमधिकं मुने॥ तपस्विनो धर्मपथे स्थितस्य द्विजसत्तम।
en: Why, O Brahmana, do you dance in this way, you who know your duties well? What must be the cause of your joy, O sage, that being an ascetic, ( best of Brahmanas and walking in the path of virtue you should behave in this way?

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: ऋषिरुवाच किं न पश्यसि मे ब्रह्मन् कराच्छाकरसं स्रुतम्॥ यं दृष्ट्वा सम्प्रनृत्तो वै हर्षेण महता विभो।
en: The Rishi said Do you not see that a vegetable juice is flowing from this my wound? Seeing this, O lord, I am dancing in great glee.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: तं प्रहस्याब्रवीद् देवो मुनि रागेण मोहितम्॥ अहं न विस्मयं विप्र गच्छामीति प्रपश्य माम्।
en: Laughing at the Rishi who was overpowered by passion, the god said-"I do not, O Brahmana, at all wonder at this. Behold me!"

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: एवमुक्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठं महादेवेन धीमता॥ अमुल्यग्रेण राजेन्द्र स्वङ्गुष्ठस्ताडितोऽभवत्।
en: Having said this to that best of Rishis, the highly intelligent Mahadeva struck his thumb with the end of one of his fingers.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: ततो भस्म क्षताद् राजन् निर्गतं हिमसन्निभम्॥ तद् दृष्ट्वा वीडितो राजन् स मुनिः पादयोर्गतः। मेने देवं महादेवमिदं चोवाच विस्मितः॥
en: Thereupon, O king, ashes, white as snow, came out of that wound. Beholding this, the Rishi became ashamed, O monarch and fell at the feet of the God.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: नान्यं देवादहं मन्ये रुद्रात परतरं महत्। सुरासुरस्य जगतो गति स्त्वमसि शूलधृत्॥
en: He understood the deity to be none else than Mahadeva. Filled with wonder he said-"I do not think that thou art any one save Rudra, the great and Supreme being.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: त्वया सृष्टमिदं विश्वं वदन्तीह मनीषिणः। त्वामेव सर्वं व्रजति पुनरेव युगक्षये॥
en: O wielder of the trident, thou art the refuge of this universe consisting of gods and demons. The wise say that this universe has been created by you.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: देवैरपि न शक्यस्त्वं परिज्ञातुं कुतो मया। त्वयि सर्वेस्म दृश्यन्ते भावा ये जगति स्थिताः॥
en: At the universal dissolution, everything once more enters thee. Thou art incapable of being known by the celestials, how then canst thou be known by me?

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: त्वामुपासन्त वरदं देवा ब्रह्मादयोऽनघ। सर्वस्त्वमसि देवानां कर्ता कारयिता च ह॥ त्वत्प्रसादात् सुराः सर्वे मोदन्तीहाकुतोभयाः।
en: All creatures of the universe are seen in thee. The gods with Brahma at their head worship thee who dust give boons, O sinless one.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: एवं स्तुत्वा महादेवं स ऋषिः प्रणतोऽभवत्॥ यदिदं चापलं देव कृतमेतत् स्मयदिकम्।
en: Thou art everything. Thou art the creator of the gods. Through thy grace, the god pass their time joyously and fearlessly." Having lauded Mahadeva in this way, the Rishi bowed to him.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: ततः प्रसादयामि त्वां तपो मे न क्षरेदिति॥ ततो देवः प्रीतमनास्तमृषि पुनरब्रवीत्। तपस्ते वर्धतां विप्र मत्प्रसादात् सहस्रधा॥ आश्रमे चेह वत्स्यामि त्वया सार्धमहं सदा।
en: Let not my ridiculous childishness, that I displayed, O god, destroy my ascetic merit. I pray to thee for this. The god cheerfully replied-"Let your asceticism increase a thousand fold, O Brahmana, through my grace, I shall also always live with you in this hermitage."

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: सप्तासारस्वते चास्मिन यो मामर्चिष्यते नरः॥ न तस्य दुर्लभं किञ्चिद् भवितेह परत्र वा। सारस्वतं च ते लोकं गमिष्यन्ति न संशयः॥
en: The man that will adore me in this Pritha, viz., Sapta-sarasvat, will attain everything here or hereafter. Forsooth, such a one shall go to the region called Sarasvat in heaven, after death.

description: The history of Sapta Sarasvati and Mankanaka
sn: एतन्मङ्कणकस्यापि चरितं भूरितेजसः। स हि पुत्र सुकन्यायामुत्पन्नो मातरिश्वना॥
en: This is the history of Mankanaka. He was begotten by the god of wind upon Sukanya.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उषित्वा तत्र रामस्तु सम्पूज्याश्रमवासिनः। तथा मङ्कणके प्रीतिं शुभां चक्रे हलायुधः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having passed one night there, Rama, having the plough for his weapon, adored the dwellers of that tirtha and showed great respect for Mankanaka.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: दत्त्वा दानं द्विजातिभ्यो रजनी तामुपोष्य च। पूजितो मुनिसद्धैश्च प्रातरुत्थाय लागली॥ अनुज्ञाप्य मुनीन् सर्वान् स्पृष्ट्वा तोयं च भारत। प्रययौ त्वरितो रामस्तीर्थहेतोर्महावलः॥
en: Having distributed wealth amongst the Brahmanas and passed the night there the hero, having the plough for his weapon, was adored by the ascetics. Rising up in the morning, he took leave of all the ascetics and having touched the sacred water, O Bharata, started quickly for other tirthas.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: ततस्त्वौशनसं तीर्थमाजगाम हलायुधः कपालमोचनं नाम यत्र मुक्तो महामुनिः॥ महता शिरसा राजन् ग्रस्तजङ्घो महोदरः। राक्षसस्य महाराज रामक्षिप्तस्य वै पुरा॥
en: Baladeva then went to the tirtha known by the name of Ushanas. It is also called Kapalamochana. Formerly, Rama (the son of Dasharatha) slew a Rakshasa and threw his head to a great distance. That head, O king, fell upon the thigh of a great sage named Mahodara and struck to it. Bathing in this tirtha, the great Rishi was freed from that burthen. The great (Shukra) had practised his ascetic penances there.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: तत्र पूर्वं तपस्तप्तं काव्येन सुमहात्मना। यत्रास्य नीतिरखिला प्रादुर्भूता महात्मनः॥ यत्रस्थाश्चिन्तयामास दैत्यदानवविग्रहम्।
en: It was there that the science of politics and morals, .that passes by Shukra's name, was revealed to him. While living there. Shukra meditated upon the war of the Daityas and the Danavas.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: तत् प्राप्य च बलो राजंस्तीर्थप्रवरमुत्तमम्॥ विधिवद् वै ददौ वित्तं ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम्।
en: Arrived at that foremost of tirthas Baladeva, O king, duly made presents of the great Brahmanas.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कपालमोचनं ब्रह्मन्कथं यत्र महामुनिः॥ मुक्तः कथं चास्य शिरो लग्नं केन च हेतुना।
en: Janamejaya said Why is it called Kapalamochana, where the great Muni became freed (from the Rakshasa's head)? Why and how did that head stick to his thigh?"

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पुरा वै दण्डकारण्ये राघवेण महात्मना॥ वसता राजशार्दूल राक्षसान् शमयिष्यता।
en: Vaishampayana said "Formerly, O foremost of king, the great Rama (the son of Dasharatha) lived for sometime in the forest of Dandaka, for killing the Rakshasas.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: जनस्थाने शिरश्छिन्नं राक्षसस्य दुरात्मनः॥ क्षुरेण शितधारेण उत्पपात महावने।
en: At Janasthana he sundered the head of a wicked Rakshasa with highly sharp razorheaded arrow. That head dropped in the deep forest.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: महोदरस्य तल्लग्नं जंघाया वै यदृच्छया॥ वने विचरतो राजन्नस्थि भित्वाऽस्फुरत् तदा। स तेन लग्नेन तदा द्विजातिर्न शशाक ह॥
en: That head, coursing at will through the sky, fell upon the thigh of Mahodara while the latter was walking in the woods. Piercing his thigh, O king, it stuck to it and remained there.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: अभिगन्तुं महाप्राज्ञस्तीर्थान्यायतनानि च। स पूतिना विस्रवता वेदना” महामुनिः॥
en: That head thus sticking to his thigh, the greatly wise Brahmana could not (with ease), proceed to tirthas and other sacred places.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: जगाम सर्वतीर्थानि पृथिव्यां चेति नः श्रुतम्। स गत्वा सरितः सर्वाः समुद्रांश्च महातपाः॥
en: Feeling great pain and with putrid matter flowing from his thigh, he travelled to all the tirthas of the earth, one after another, as heard by us.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: कथयामास तत् सर्वमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्। आप्लुत्य सर्वतीर्थेषु न च मोक्षमवाप्तवान्॥ स तु शुश्राव विप्रेन्द्र मुनीनां वचनं महत्। सरस्वत्यास्तीर्थवरं ख्यातमौशनसं तदा॥ सर्वपापप्रशमनं सिद्धिक्षेत्रमनुत्तमम्। स तु गत्वा ततस्तत्र तीर्थमौशनसं द्विजः॥
en: He went to all the rivers and to the ocean as well. The great ascetic spoke of his pain to many Rishis of pure souls, about his having bathed in all the sacred spots without finding any relief. That best of Brahmanas then heard from those sages, about this foremost of tirthas situate on the Sarasvati, known by the name of Ushanasha, which could cleanse every sin and was an excellent place for acquiring ascetic merits.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: तत औशनसे तीर्थे तस्योपस्पृशतस्तदा। तच्छिरश्चरणं मुक्त्वा पपातान्तर्जले तदा॥
en: Then repairing to that Ushanasa tirtha, that Brahmana bathed in its waters. Thereat the Rakshasa's head, leaving the thigh, dropped into the water.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: विमुक्तस्तेन शिरसा परं सुखमवाप हा स चाप्यन्तर्जले मूर्धा जगामादर्शनं विभो॥
en: Freed from that head, the Rishi felt great ease. The head however was lost in the waters.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: ततः स विशिरा राजन् पूतात्मा वीतकल्मषः। आजगामाश्रमं प्रीतः कृतकृत्यो महोदरः॥
en: Then, O king, freed from the Rakshasa's head Mahodara gladly returned, with purified soul and all his sins cleansed, to his hermitage after attaining success.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: सोऽथ गत्वाऽऽश्रमं पुण्यं विप्रमुक्तो महातपाः। कथयामास तत् सर्वमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्॥
en: Thus freed, after returning to his sacred hermitage the great ascetic, spoke of what had taken place to those Rishis of pure souls.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: ते श्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य ततस्तीर्थस्य मानद। कपालमोचनमिति नाम चक्रुः समागताः॥
en: Having heard his story, those Rishis conferred the name of Kapalamochana on the tirtha.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
