sn: स चापि तीर्थप्रवरं पुनर्गत्वा महानृषिः। पीत्वा पयः सुविपुलं सिद्धिमायात् तदा मुनिः॥
en: Repairing once more to that foremost of tirthas, the great Rishi Mahodara, drank its water and acquired great ascetic success.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: तत्र दत्त्वा बहून दायान् विप्रान् सम्पूज्य माधवः। जगाम वृष्णिप्रवरो रुषङ्गोराश्रमं तदा॥
en: Having distributed much wealth amongst the Brahmanas and worshipped them, Baladeva then went to the hermitage of Rushangu.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: यत्र तप्तं तपो घोरमार्टिषेणेन भारत। ब्राह्मण्यं लब्धवांस्तत्र विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः॥
en: There, O Bharata, Arshtishena had in days of yore practised austerest of penances. There the great (Kshatriya) Muni Muni Vishvamitra became a Brahmana.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: सर्वकामसमृद्धं च तदाश्रमपदं महत्। मुनिभिर्ब्राह्मणैश्चैव सेवितं सर्वदा विभो॥
en: That great hermitage is capable of fructifying every wish. It always, O lord, the asylum of ascetics and Brahmanas.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: ततो हलधरः श्रीमान् ब्राह्मणैः परिवारितः। जगाम् तत्र राजेन्द्र रुषमुस्तनुमत्यजत्॥
en: Surrounded by Brahmanas, then the beautiful Baladeva went to that spot, O king, where Rushangu had, formerly, renounced his body.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: रुषगाह्मणो वृद्धस्तपोनित्यश्च भारत। देहन्यासे कृतमना विचिन्त्य बहुधा तदा॥
en: Rushangu, O Bharata, was an old Brahmana always devoted to penances. Determined to renounce his body, he thought for a long while.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: ततः सर्वानुपादाय तनयान् वै महातपाः। रुषङ्गुरब्रवीत् तत्र नयध्वं मां पृथूदकम्॥
en: A great ascetic as he was, he then summoned all his sons and asked them to take him to a spot where there was profuse water.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: विज्ञायातीतवयसं रुषहुं ते तपोधनाः तं च तीर्थमुपानिन्युः सरस्वत्यास्तपोधनम्॥
en: Knowing their father had become very old, those ascetics took him to a tirtha on the Sarasvati.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: स तैः पुत्रैस्तदा धीमानानीतो वै सरस्वतीम्। पुण्यां तीर्थशतोपेतां विप्रसङ्घनिषेविताम्॥ स तत्र विधिना राजन्नाप्लुत्य सुमहातपाः। सुप्रीतः पुरुषव्याघ्र सर्वान् पुत्रानुपासतः। सरस्वत्युत्तरे तीरे यस्त्यजेदात्मनस्तनुम्॥ पृथूदके जप्यपरो नैनं श्वोमरणं तपेत्। तत्राप्लुत्य स धर्मात्मा उपस्पृश्य हलायुधः॥
en: Brought by his sons to the sacred Sarasvati containing hundreds of tirthas and on whose banks lived Rishis disassociated from the world, that intelligent ascetic, of hard penances, bathed in that tirtha duly and conversant as that best of Rishis was with the virtues of tirthas, then cheerfully said to all his sons who were dutifully waiting upon him these words.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: दत्त्वा चैव बहून् दायान् विप्राणां विप्रवत्सलः। ससर्ज यत्र भगवाँल्लोकाँल्लोकपितामहः॥
en: He, that would renounce his body on the northern bank of the Sarasvati containing profuse water, reciting mentally sacred mantras, would never again he visited by death.'

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: यत्रार्टिषेणः कौरव्या ब्राह्मण्यं संशितव्रतः। तपसा महता राजन् प्राप्तवानृषिसत्तमः॥
en: Touching the water of that tirtha and bathing in it, the righteous Baladeva distributed wealth amongst the Brahmanas.

description: The origin of the name of Kapalamochana
sn: सिन्धुद्वीपश्च राजर्षिर्देवापिश्च महातपाः। ब्राह्मण्यं लब्धवान् यत्र विश्वामित्रस्तथा मुनिः॥ महातपस्वी भगवानुग्रतेजा महायशाः। तत्राजगाम बलवान् बलभद्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Possessed of great might and great prowess, Baladeva then proceeded to that tirtha where the worshipful Brahma had created the mountains called Lokaloka and where that best of Rishis, Arshtishena, of rigid vows, had by hard penances acquired the dignity of Brahmana-hood and where the royal saint Sindhudvipa and the great ascetic Devapi and the worshipful and illustrious Vishvamitra of hard penances and fierce energy, had all acquired a similar dignity.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथमार्टिषेणो भगवान् विपुलं तप्तवांस्तपः। सिन्धुद्वीपः कथं चापि ब्राह्मण्यं लब्धवांस्तदा॥
en: Janamejaya said "Why did the worshipful Arshtishena practise the severest of penances? How also did Sindhudvipa acquire the dignity of a Brahmana?

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: देवापिश्च कथं ब्रह्मन् विश्वामित्रश्च सत्तम। तन्ममाचक्ष्व भगवन् परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: How also did Devapi, O Brahmana and how did Vishvamitra, O best of men, become Brahmanas. Tell me all this, O worshipful One! Great is my curiosity to hear of all this."

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पुरा कृतयुगे राजन्नार्टिषेणो द्विजोत्तमः। वसन् गुरुकले नित्यं नित्यमध्ययने रतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Formerly, in the Krita age, O king, there was a great Rishi called Arshtishena. Living in his preceptor's house, he attended to his lessons every day.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: तस्य राजन् गुरुकुले वसतो नित्यमेव च। समाप्ति नागमद् विद्या नापि वेदा विशाम्पते।॥
en: Although, O king, he lived long in the residence of his preceptor, he could not master any branch of learning or the Vedas, O monarch.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: स निर्विणस्ततो राजंस्तपस्तेपे महातपाः। ततो वै तपसा तेन प्राप्य वेदाननुत्तमान्॥
en: Greatly disappointed, O king, the great ascetic practised very rigid penances. By his penances he afterwards acquired the mastery of the Vedas which is best of all forms of learning.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: वरान् प्रादात् त्रीनेव स विद्वान् वेदयुक्तश्च सिद्धश्चाप्यषिसत्तमः। तत्र तीर्थे सुमहातपाः॥
en: Acquiring great learning and a mastery of the Vedas, that best of Rishis became highly successful in that tirtha. He then conferred three boons on that place.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: अस्मिंस्तीर्थे महानद्या अद्यप्रभृति मानवः। आप्लुतो वाजिमेधस्य फलं प्राप्स्यति पुष्कलम्॥
en: He said-"From this day, a person, by bathing in this tirtha of the great river Sarasvati, shall reap the great fruit of a horse sacrifice.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: अद्यप्रभृति नैवात्र भयं व्यालाद् भविष्यति। अपि चाल्पेन कालेन फलं प्राप्स्यति पुष्कलम्॥
en: From this day there will be no fear in this tirtha from serpents and wild beasts. By the slightest of endeavours, again, one shall reap great results here."

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा जगाम त्रिदिवं मुनिः। एवं सिद्धः स भगवानार्टिषेणः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Having said these words, that energetic Rishi proceeded to heaven. Thus the worshipful Arshtishena became successful.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: तस्मिन्नेव तदा तीर्थे सिन्धुद्वीपः प्रतापवान्। देवापिश्च महाराज ब्राह्मण्यं प्रापतुर्मह ॥
en: In that very tirtha, in the Krita age th greatly energetic Sindhudvipa and Devapi also, had acquired the dignity of Brahman-hood.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: तथा च कौशिकस्तान् तपोनित्यो जितेन्द्रियः। तपसा वै सुतप्तेन ब्राह्मणत्वमवाप्तवान्॥
en: Similarly Kushika's ascetic son, having controlled his senses and practised austerities became a Brahmana.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: गाधिर्नाम महानासीत् क्षत्रियः प्रथितो भुवि। तस्य पुत्रोऽभवद् राजन् विश्वामित्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: There was a great Kshatriya, celebrated over the world, by the name of Gadhi. He had a son by the name of Vishvamitra of great prowess.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: स राजा कौशिकस्तात महायोग्यभवत् किला स पुत्रमभिषिच्याथ विश्वामित्रं महातपाः॥ देहन्यासे मनश्चक्रे तमूचुः प्रणताः प्रजाः। न गन्तव्यं महाप्राज्ञ त्राहि चास्मान् महाभयात्॥
en: King Kaushika became a great ascetic. Possessed of great ascetic merit, he wished to place his son Vishvamitra on his throne, himself having made up his mind to renounce his body. His subjects, bowing unto him, said-You should not go away, O you of great wisdom and protect us from a great fear.'

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच ततो गाधिः प्रजास्ततः। विश्वस्य जगतो गोप्ता भविष्यति सुतो मम॥
en: Thus addressed, Gadhi replied to his subjects, saying-"My son will be the protector of the vest universe.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: इत्युक्त्वा तु ततो गाधिर्विश्वामित्रं निवेश्य च। जगाम त्रिदिवं राजनं विश्वामित्रोऽभवन्नृपः॥ न स शक्नोति पृथिवीं यत्नवानपि रक्षितुम्।
en: Having said these words and placed Vishvamitra on the throne, Gadhi, O king ascended heaven and Vishvainitra became king. He could not, however, protect the earth even trying his level best.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: ततः शुश्राव राजा स राक्षसेभ्यो महाभयम्॥ निर्ययौ नगराचापि चतुरङ्गबलान्वितः।
en: The king then heard of the fear of Rakshasa in his kingdom. With his fourfold forces, he went out of his capital.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: स गत्वा दूरमध्वानं वसिष्ठाश्रममभ्ययात्॥ तस्य ते सैनिका राजंश्चक्रुस्तत्रानयान् बहून्।
en: Having proceeded far on his way, he reached the hermitage of Vashishtha. His troops, O king, caused immense mischief there.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: ततस्तु भगवान् विप्रो वसिष्ठोऽऽश्रममभ्ययात्॥ ददृशोऽथ ततः सर्वं भज्यमानं महावनम्।
en: The worshipful Brahman Vashishtha, when he came to his hermitage, saw the vast forest devastated.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: तस्य क्रुद्धो महाराज वसिष्ठो मुनिसत्तमः॥ सृजस्व शवरान् घोरानिति स्वां गामुवाच ह।
en: That best of Rishis, viz., Vashishtha O king, became angry with Vishvamitra. He commanded his own sacrificial cow, saying "Create a number of terrible Shavaras.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: तथोक्ता साऽसृजद् धेनुः पुरुषान् घोरदर्शनान्॥ ते तु तद्बलमासाद्य बभञ्जुः सर्वतोदिशम्।
en: Thus addressed the cow created a number of men of terrific visages. These fought with the army of Vishvamitra and made a great onslaught.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: तच्छुत्वा विद्रुतं सैन्यं विश्वामित्रस्तु गाधिजः॥ तपः परं मन्यमानस्तपस्येव मनो दधे।
en: Seeing this, the troops fled away. Regarding ascetic austerities highly efficacious, Vishvamitra, the son of Gadhi made up his mind to practise the same.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: सोऽस्मिंस्तीर्थवरे राजन् सरस्वत्याः समाहितः॥ नियमैश्चोपवासैश्च कर्षयन् देहमात्मनः।
en: In this best of tirthas of the Sarasvati, O king, he began to emaciate his own body by Vows and fasts.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: जलाहारो वायुभक्षः पर्णाहारश्च सोऽभवत्॥ तथा स्थाण्डिलशायी च ये चान्ये नियमाः पृथक्।
en: He lived on water, air and the fallen leaves of trees. He slept on the naked earth and practised other vows of the ascetics.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: असकृत्तस्य देवास्तु व्रतविघ्नं प्रचक्रिरे॥ न चास्य नियमाद् बुद्धिरपयाति महात्मनः।
en: The celestials repeatedly attempted for obstructing the observance of his vows. He, however, did not desist from practising his promised vow.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: ततः परेण यत्नेन तप्त्वा बहुविधं तपः॥ तेजसा भास्कराकारो गाधिजः समपद्यत।
en: Then having practised various austerities with great devotion, the son of Gadhi became effulgent like the Sun himself.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: तपसा तु तथा युक्तं विश्वामित्रं पितामहः॥ अमन्यत महातेजा वरदो वरमस्य तत्।
en: The boon-giving Brahmana, of great energy, resolved to grant Vishvamitra, when he had succeeded in his ascetic observances, the boon the latter wanted.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: स तु ववे वरं राजन् स्यामहं ब्राह्मणास्त्विति॥ तथेति चाब्रवीद् ब्रह्मा सर्वलोकपितामहः।
en: The boon that Vishvamitra prayed for was that he should be permitted to become a Brahmana. Brahmana, the grandfather of all the worlds, said to him-"So be it.'

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: स लम्वा तपसोग्रेण ब्राह्मणत्वं महायशाः॥ विचचार महीं कृत्स्नां कृतकामः सुरोपमः।
en: Having by his severe penances gained the status of Brahman-hood, the illustrious Vishvamitra, after the fulfillment of his desire, traveled over the whole earth like a god.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: अथ वस्त्राण्यलङ्कारं भक्ष्यं पेयं च शोभनम्॥ अददन्मुदितो राजन् पूजयित्वा द्विजोत्तमान्। तस्मिंस्तीर्थवरे रामः प्रदाय विविधं वसु॥
en: Distributing various sorts of wealth in that best of tirthas, Rama also gladly gave away milch cows, vehicles, beds, ornaments, food and drink of the best kinds, O king, to many foremost of Brahmanas, after having adored them dully.

description: The attainment of Brahmanahood by Arshtisena, Sindhudvipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra
sn: पयस्विनीस्तथा धेनूर्यानानि शयनानि च। ययौ राजंस्ततो रामो बकस्याश्रममन्तिकात्। यत्र तेपे तपस्तीव्र दाल्भ्यो बक इति श्रुतिः॥
en: Then, O king, Rama proceeded to the hermitage of Vaka which was not very far from where he was, the hermitage in which, as heard by us, Dalvya-vaka had practised the hardest of penances.”

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ब्रह्मयोनेरवाकीर्णं जगाम यदुनन्दनः। यत्र दाल्भ्यो बको राजन्नाश्रमस्थो महातपाः॥ जुहाव धृतराष्ट्रस्य राष्टं वैचित्रवीर्यणः। तपसा घोररूपेण कर्षयन् देहमात्मनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said "That delighter of the Yadus then proceeded to the hermitage (of Vaka) resonant with the chaunting of the Vedas. There the great ascetic, O king, named Dalvya-vaka, poured the kingdom of Dhritarashtra, the son of Vichitravirya, as a libation (on the sacrificial fire). By practising hard penances he emaciated his own body. The greatly energetic and virtuous Rishi did it being worked up with great wrath.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: क्रोधेन महताऽऽविष्टो धर्मात्मा वै प्रतापवान्। पुरा हि नैमिषीयाणां सत्रे द्वादशवार्षिके॥ वृत्ते विश्वाजितोऽन्ते वै पञ्चालानृषयोऽगमन्।
en: Formerly the Rishis, living in the Naimisha forest, had celebrated a sacrifice extending over twelve years. In the course of that sacrifice, after a particular one called Vishvajit had been completed, the Rishis started for the country of the Panchalas.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: तत्रेश्वरमयाचन्त दक्षिणार्थं मनस्वनः॥ तानब्रवीद बको दाल्भयो विभजघ्व पशूनिति॥
en: Going there, they requested the king to give them twenty one strong and healthy calves to be given away as Dakshina in the sacrifice they had finished.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: पशूनेतानहं त्यक्त्वा भिक्षिष्ये राजसत्तमम्। एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजऋषीन् सवान् प्रतापवान्॥
en: Dalvya-vaka, then said to those Rishis-"Do you divide those animals among ye! Giving away these (to ye), I shall beg a great king (for some more).'

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: जगाम धृतराष्ट्रस्य भवनं ब्राह्मणोत्तमः।
en: Saying it the greatly energetic Vaka, that best of Brahmanas, then went to the palace of Dhritarashtra.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: स समीपगतो भूत्वा धृतराष्ट्र जनेश्वरम्॥ अयाचत पशून् दाल्भ्यः स चैनं रुषितोऽब्रवीत्। यदृच्छया मृता दृष्ट्वा गास्तदा नृपसत्तमः॥ एतान् पशून् नय क्षिप्रं ब्रह्मबन्धो यदीच्छसि।
en: Going before Dhritarashtra, Dalvya begged some animals of him. Finding that some of his kine had died without any cause, the king angrily said to him-"Wretch of a Brahmana, take, if you wish, these (dead) kine.'

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: ऋषिस्तथा वचः श्रुत्वा चिन्तयामास धर्मवित्॥ अहो बत नृशसं वै वाक्यमुक्तोऽस्मि संसदि। नरपतेः पुराः।
en: Hearing these words, the dutiful Rishi thught-Alas, he has spoken cruel words to me in the assembly.'

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तेन रोषाविष्टो द्विजोत्तमः॥ मतिं चक्रे विनाशय धृतराष्ट्रस्य भूपतेः।
en: Having thought thus, thus, that best of Brahmanas, filled with rage, made up his mind for destroying king Dhritarashtra.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: स तूत्कृत्य मृतानां वै मांसानि मुनिसत्तमः॥ जुहाव धृतराष्ट्रस्य राष्ट्र अवाकीर्णे सरस्वत्यास्तीर्थे प्रज्वाल्य पावकम्॥ बको दाल्भ्यो महाराज नियम परमं स्थितः। स तैरेव जुहावास्य राष्ट्रं मांसैर्महातपाः॥
en: Cutting the flesh from the dead animals, that best of Rishis, having lighted a sacrificial fire on the tirtha of the Sarasvati, poured those pieces as libations for the destruction of king Dhritarashtra's kingdom. The great ascetic Dalvya-vaka, O king poured Dhritarashtra's kingdom as a libation on the fire.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: तस्मिंस्तु विधिवत् सत्रे सम्प्रवृत्ते सुदारुणे। अक्षीयत ततो राष्ट्रं धृतराष्ट्रस्य पार्थिव॥
en: Upon the commencement of that dreadful sacrifice with proper rites, the kingdom of Dhritarashtra, O king, began to dwindle.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: ततः प्रक्षीयमाणं तद् राज्यं तस्य महीपतेः। छिद्यमानं यथानन्तं वनं परशुना विभो॥ बभूवापद्गतं तच व्यवकीर्णमचेतनम्। दृष्ट्वा तथावकीर्णं तु राष्ट्रं स मनुजाधिपः॥
en: Indeed, O lord, the kingdom of that monarch began to dwindle as a large forest gradually disappears when men cut it down with the axe. Overtaken by dangers, the kingdom began to lose its prosperity and vitality.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: बभूव दुर्मना राजंश्चिन्तयामास च प्रभुः।
en: Seeing his kingdom thus afflicted the power king became very depressed and anxious.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: मोक्षार्थमकरोद् यत्नं ब्राह्मणैः सहितः पुरा॥ न च श्रेयोऽध्यगच्छत्तु क्षीयते राष्ट्रमेव च।
en: Consulting with the Brahmanas, he began to make mighty endeavours for releasing his kingdom (from affliction). No good, however, came of his endeavours, for the kingdom continued to dwindle.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: यदा स पार्थिवः खिन्नस्ते च विप्रास्तदानघ॥ यदा चापि न शक्नोति राष्ट्रं मोक्षयितुं नृप। अथ वै प्राश्निकांस्तत्र पप्रच्छ जनमेजय॥ ततो वै प्राश्निकाः प्राहुः पशोर्विप्रकृतस्त्वया।
en: The king became very much depressed. The Brahmanas also, O sinless one, became filled with grief. When at last the king failed to save his kingdom, he consulted the ministers, O Janamejaya, (about the remedy). The minister reminded him of the evil he had done regarding the dead kine.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: मासैरभिजुहोतीदं तव राष्ट्र मुनिर्बकः॥ तेन ते हूयमानस्य राष्ट्रस्यास्य क्षयो महान्।
en: And they said-"The ascetic Vaka is pouring your kingdom as a libation on the fire with the help of the flesh (of those animals). Therefore is this dwindling away of your kingdom.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: तस्यैतत् तपसः कर्म येन तेऽद्य लयो महान्॥ अपां कुर्छ सरस्वत्यास्तं प्रसादय पार्थिव।
en: This is the fruit of ascetic rites. Thence is this great calamity! Go, O king and propitiate that Rishi who is living on the bank of the Sarasvati.'

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: सरस्वतीं ततो गत्वा स राजा बकमब्रवीत्॥ निपत्य शिरसा भूमौ प्राञ्जलिर्भरतर्षभ।
en: Going to the bank of Sarasvati, the king fell at his feet, touched them with his head, joined his hands and said-"I propitiate you, O worshipful one, forgive me for my crime.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: प्रसादये त्वां भगवन्नपराधं क्षमस्व मे॥ मम दीनस्य लुब्धस्य मौर्येण हतचेतसः।
en: I am an insensate fool, a wretch filled with avarice. You are my refuge and protector, you should extend to me your favour.'

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: त्वं गतिस्त्वं च मे नाथः प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ तं तथा विलपन्तं तु शोकोपहतचेतसम्।
en: Seeing him thus laden with grief and indulging in lamentations like these, Vaka felt compassion for him and freed his kingdom.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: दृष्ट्वा तस्य कृपा जज्ञे राष्ट्रं तस्य व्यमोचयत्॥ ऋषिः प्रसन्नस्तस्याभूत् संरम्भं च विहाय सः। मोक्षार्थं तस्य राज्यस्य जुहाव पुनराहुतिम्॥
en: The Rishi became pleased with him and cast off his anger. For freeing his kingdom, the sage again poured libations on the fire.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: मोक्षयित्वा ततो राष्ट्र प्रतिगृह्य पशून् बहून्। हृष्टात्मा नैमिषारण्यं जगाम पुनरेव सः॥
en: Having freed the kingdom from calamities and taken many kine as a gift he became pleased at heart and once more proceeded to the Naimisha forest.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: धृतराष्ट्रोऽपि धर्मात्मा स्वस्थचेता महामनाः। स्वमेव नगरं राजन् प्रतिपेदे महर्द्धिमत्॥
en: The liberal and righteous king Dhrutarashtra, with a cheerful heart, returned to his own prosperous capital.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: तत्र तीर्थे महाराज बृहस्पतिरुदारधीः। असुराणामभावाय भवाय त दिवौकसाम्॥ मांसैरभिजुहावेष्टिमक्षीयन्त ततोऽसुराः। दैवतैरपि सम्भग्ना जितकाशिभिराहवे॥
en: In that tirtha, for the destruction of the Asuras and the prosperity of the celestials Brihaspati also poured libations on the sacrificial fire, with the aid of flesh. Upon this, the Asuras began to waste away and were killed by the celestials, filled with desire of victory, in battle.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: तत्रापि विधिवद् दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणेभ्यो महायशाः। वाजिनः कुञ्जरांश्चैव रथांश्चाश्वतरीयुतान्॥ रत्नानि च महार्हाणि धनं धान्यं च पुष्कलम्। ययौ तीर्थं महाबाहुर्यायातं पृथिवीपते॥
en: Having with due rites given to the Brahmanas horses and elephants and vehicles with mules yoked to them and precious jewels and immense wealth and profuse corn, the illustrious and mighty-armed Rama then proceeded, O king, to the tirtha called Yayata.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: तत्र यज्ञे ययातेश्च महाराज सरस्वती। सर्पिः पयश्च सुस्राव नाहुषस्य महात्मनः॥
en: There, O king, at the sacrifice of the highsouled Yayati, the son of Nahusha, the Sarasvati produced milk and clarified butter.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: तत्रेष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रो ययातिः पृथिवीपतिः। अक्रामदूर्ध्वं मुदितो लेभे लोकांश्च पुष्कलान्॥
en: That foremost of men, king Yayati, having performed a sacrifice there, went to heaven and secured many blissful regions.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: पुनस्तत्र च राज्ञस्तु ययातेर्यजतः प्रभोः। औदार्यं परमं कृत्वा भक्तिं चात्मनि शाश्वतीम्॥ ददौ कामान् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यान् यान् यो मनसेच्छति।
en: Once again, O lord, king Yayati, performed a sacrifice there. Beholding his great magnanimity of soul and his fixed devotion to herself, the river Sarasvati gave to the Brahmanas present there everything they desired to have.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: यो यत्र स्थित एवेह आहूतो यज्ञसंस्तरे॥ तस्य तस्य सरिच्छेष्टा गृहादिशयनादिकम्। षड्रसं भोजनं चैव दानं नानाविधं तथा॥
en: That foremost of rivers gave each of them that were invited to the sacrifice, here he was, houses and beds and food of the six different tastes and various other things.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: ते मन्यमाना राज्ञस्तु सम्प्रदानमनुत्तमम्। राजानं तुष्टुवुः प्रीता दत्त्वा चैवाशिषः शुभाः॥
en: The Brahmanas regarded those valuable gifts as presented by the king. Gladly they lauded the king and conferred their sacred blessing upon him.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: तत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वाः प्रीता यज्ञस्य सम्पदा। विस्मिता मानुषाश्चासन् दृष्ट्वा तां यज्ञसम्पदम्॥
en: The gods and the Gandharvas were all pleased with the numberless articles in that sacrifice. As regards men they were filled with wonder on seeing those articles.

description: The story of Dalvya-Valla. The history of the Tirtha Yayata
sn: ततस्तालकेतुर्महाधर्मकेतुर्महात्मा कृतात्मा महादाननित्यः। वसिष्ठापवाहं महाभीमवेगं धृतात्मा जितात्मा समभ्याजगाम॥
en: The illustrious and righteous Baladeva, of cleansed soul, having the palmyra on his banner and ever giving away the most valuable things, then proceeded to that tirtha of fierce current called Vashishthapavaha.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: जनमेजय उवाच वसिष्ठस्यापवाहोऽसौ भीमवेगः कथं नु सः। किमर्थं च सरिच्छेष्टा तमृषि प्रत्यवाहयत्॥
en: Janamejaya said "Why is the current of the tirtha known as Vashishthapavaha so rapid? For why did the foremost of rivers carry away Vashishtha?

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: कथमस्याभवद् वैरं कारणं किं च तत् प्रभो। शंस पृष्टो महाप्राज्ञ न हि तृष्यामि कथ्यति॥
en: What, O lord, was the cause of the quarrel between Vashishtha and Vishvamitra? Asked by me, O you of great wisdom, tell me all this. I am never satiated with hearing your account.”

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विश्वामित्रस्य विप्रर्वसिष्ठस्य च भारत। भृशं वैरमभूद् राजंस्तपः स्पर्धाकृतं महत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said A great enemity arose between Vishvamitra and Vashishtha, O Bharata, on account of their rivalry regarding ascetic penances.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: आश्रमो वै वसिष्ठस्य स्थाणुतीर्थेऽभवन्महान्। पूर्वतः पार्श्वतश्चासीद् विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः॥
en: The hermitage of Vashishtha was in the tirtha called Sthanu on the eastern bank of the Sarasvati. On the opposite bank was the hermitage of the intelligent Vishvamitra.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: यत्र स्थाणुर्महाराज तप्तवान् परमं तपः। तत्रास्य कर्म तद् घोरं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: There, in that tirtha, O king, Mahadeva had practised the hardest penances. Sages still speak of those penances.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: यत्रेष्ट्वा भगवान् स्थाणुः पूजयित्वा सरस्वतीम्। स्थापयामास तत् तीर्थं स्थाणुतीर्थमिति प्रभो॥
en: Having performed a sacrifice there and adored the river Sarasvati, Sthanu established that tirtha there. Therefore it is known by the name Sthanu-tirtha, O lord.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तत्र तीर्थे सुराः स्कन्दमभ्यषिञ्चन्नराधिप। सैनापत्येन महता सुरारिविनिबर्हणम्॥
en: In that tirtha, the celestials had, formerly, ) king, appointed Skanda, that destroyer of the enemies of the celestials, as the generalissimo of their army.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तस्मिन् सारस्वते तीर्थे विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः। वसिष्ठं चालयामास तपसोगेण तच्छृणु॥
en: The great Rishi Vishvamitra, by the help of his austere penances, brought Vashishtha, to that tirtha of the Sarasvati, listen to that account.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: विश्वामित्रवसिष्ठौ तावहन्यहनि भारत। स्पर्धा तपःकृतां तीव्रां चक्रतुस्तौ तपोधनौ॥
en: The two ascetics Vishvamitra and Vashishtha, O Bharata, competed keenly with each other in respect of superiority of their penances.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तत्राप्यादिकसंतापो विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः। दृष्ट्वा तेजो वसिष्ठस्य चिन्तामभिजगाम ह॥
en: Being jealous of the power of Vashishtha, the great Muni Vishvamitra began to think seriously.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तस्य बुद्धिरियं ह्यासीद् धर्मनित्यस्य भारत। इयं सरस्वती तूर्णं मत्समीपं तपोधनम्॥ आनयिष्यति वेगेन वसिष्ठं तपतां वरम्। इहागतं द्विजश्रेष्ठं हनिष्यामि न संशयः॥
en: Thought devoted to the performance of his duties, O Bharata, he formed the resolution, viz., This Sarasvati shall speedily bring, by force of her current, that foremost of ascetics, viz., Vashishtha, to my presence. After he shall have been brought hither, I shall forsooth kill that greatest of ascetics.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: एवं निश्चित्य भगवान् विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः। सस्मार सरितां श्रेष्ठां क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः॥
en: Having formed this resolution, the illustrious and great Rishi Vishvamitra, with eyes red in ire, thought of that foremost of rivers.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: सा ध्याता मुनिना तेन व्याकुलत्वं जगाम ह। जज्ञे चैनं महावीर्यं महाकोपं च भाविनी॥
en: Thus remembered by the ascetic, she became exceedingly agitated. The fair lady, repaired to that energetic and wrathful Rishi.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तत एनं वेपमानां विवर्णा प्राञ्जलिस्तदा। उपतस्थे मुनिवरं विश्वामित्रं सरस्वती॥
en: Pale and trembling, Sarasvati, with clasped hands, appeared before that best of sages.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: हतवीरा यथा नारी साऽभवद् दुःखिता भृशम्। ब्रूहि किं करवाणीति प्रोवाच मुनिसत्तमम्॥
en: Indeed, the lady was greatly afflicted with sorrow, even like a woman who has lost her powerful husband. And she said to that best of sages-"Tell me what I can do for you.'

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तामुवाच मुनिः क्रुद्धो वसिष्ठं शीघ्रमानय। यावदेनं निहन्म्यद्य तच्छ्रुत्वा व्यथिता नदी॥
en: Filled with ire, the ascetic said her-Bring here Vashishtha without delay, so that I my kill him.' Hearing these words, the river became agitated.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: प्राञ्जलिं तु ततः कृत्वा पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणा। प्राकम्पत भृशं भीता वायुनेवाहता लता॥
en: With clasped hands the lotus-eyed lady began to tremble in fear, like a creeper shaken by the wind.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तथारूपां तां दृष्ट्वा मुनिराह महानदीम्। अविचारं वसिष्ठं त्वमानयस्वान्तिकं मम॥
en: Beholding the great river in that condition, the ascetic said to her-"Bring Vashishtha before me without any scruple.'

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: सा तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा ज्ञात्वा पापं चिकीर्पितम्। वसिष्ठस्य प्रभावं च जानन्त्यप्रतिमं भुवि॥ साऽभिगम्य वसिष्ठं च इदमर्थमचोदयत्। यदुक्ता सरितां श्रेष्ठा विश्वामित्रेण धीमता॥
en: Hearing these words of his and knowing the evil he meant and acquainted also with the matchless power of Vashishtha she went to Vashishtha and informed him of what the intelligent Vishvamitra had said to her.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: उभयोः शापयोर्भीता वेपमाना पुनः पुनः। चिन्तयित्वा महाशापमृषिवित्रासिता भृशम्॥ तु
en: Fearing the course of both, she trembled again and again. Indeed, she stood in fear of both.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तां कृशां च विवर्णां च दृष्ट्वा चिन्तासमन्विताम्। उवाच राजन् धर्मात्मा वसिष्ठो द्विपदां वरः॥
en: Seeing her pale and anxious, the righteous Vashishtha, that foremost of men, O king, said to her.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच पाह्यात्मानं सरिच्छ्रेष्ठे वह मां शीघ्रगामिनी। विश्वामित्र: शद्धि त्वां मा कृथास्त्वं विचारणाम्।। २४
en: Vashishtha said O foremost of rivers, save yourself, O you of rapid current, bear me away, otherwise Vishvamitra will curse you! Do not feel the least scruple.'

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा कृपाशीलस्य सा सरित्। चिन्तयामास कौरव्य किं कृत्वा सुकृतं भवेत्॥
en: Hearing these words of that compassionate Rishi, the river began to think, O Kuru-chief, as to what she should do.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तस्याश्चिन्ता समुत्पन्ना वसिष्ठो मय्यतीव हि। कृतवान् हि दयां नित्यं तस्य कार्यं हितं मया॥
en: The thought Vashishtha shows great mercy for me. It is proper for me that I should serve him.'

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: अथ कूले स्वके राजन् जपन्तमृषिसत्तमम्। जुह्वानं कौशिकं प्रेक्ष्य सरस्वत्यभ्यचिन्तयत्॥ इदमन्तरमित्येवं ततः सा सरितां वरा। कूलापहारमकरोत् स्वेन वेगेन सा सरित्॥
en: Seeing then that best of Rishis, viz., Vashishtha engaged in silent recitation of Mantras on her bank and seeing Kushika's son Vishvamitra also engaged in homa, Sarasvati thought, this is my opportunity.' Then that foremost of rivers, by her current, washed away one of her banks.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तेन कूलापहारेण मैत्रावरुणिरौह्यत। उह्यमानः स तुष्टाव तदा राजन् सरस्वतीम्॥ पितामहस्य सरसः प्रवृत्ताऽसि सरस्वति। व्याप्तं चेदं जगत् सर्वं तवैवाम्भोभिरुत्तमैः॥
en: In washing away that bank, she carried away Vashishtha. While being borne away. ) king, Vashishtha lauded the river saying: "From Brahma's Manasa-lake you have originated, O Sarasvati! The entire carth is filled with thy pure waters!

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: त्वमेवाकाशगा देवि मेघेषु सृजसे पयः। सर्वाश्चापस्त्वमेवेति त्वत्तो वयमधीमहि॥
en: Passing through the sky, O Goddess, thou impartest thy waters to the clouds! All the waters are thee! Through thee we exercise our thinking faculties!

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: पुष्टिषुतिस्तथा कीर्तिः सिद्धिबुद्धिरुमा तथा। त्वमेव वाणी स्वाहा त्वं तवायत्तमिदं जगत्॥ त्वमेव सर्वभूतेषु वससीह चतुर्विधा।
en: Thou art Pushti and Dyuti, Kiriti and Siddhi and Uma! Thou art Speech and thou art Svaha! This entire universe depends on thee. Thou dwellest in all creatures, in four forms."

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: एवं सरस्वती राजन् स्तूयमाना महर्षिणा॥ वेगेनोवाह तं विप्रं विश्वामित्राश्रमं प्रति। न्यवेदयत चाभीक्ष्णं विश्वामित्राय तं मुनिम्॥
en: Thus lauded by that great Rishi, Sarasvati, O king, speedily bore that Brahmana towards the hermitage of Vishvamitra and repeatedly announced to the latter the arrival of the former.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तमानीतं सरस्वत्या दृष्ट्वा कोपसमन्वितः। अथान्वेषत् प्रहरणं वसिष्ठान्तकरं तदा॥
en: Seeing Vashishtha thus brought before him by Sarasvati, Vishvamitra, worked up with ire, began to look for a weapon where with to kill that Brahmana.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: तं तु क्रुद्धमभिप्रेक्ष्य ब्रह्मवध्याभयानदी। अपोवाह वसिष्ठं तु प्राची दिशमतन्द्रिता॥ उभयोः कुर्वती वाक्यं वञ्चयित्वा च गाधिजम्।
en: Seeing him wrathful, the river, fearing to behold a Brahmana's slaughter, quickly bore Vashishtha away to her eastern bank once more. She thus had obeyed the words of both, although she deceived Vishvamitra by her act.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: ततोऽपवाहितं दृष्ट्वा वसिष्ठमृषिसत्तमम्॥ अब्रवीद् दुःखसंक्रुद्धो विश्वामित्रो ह्यमर्षणः।
en: Seeing that best of Rishis, viz., Vashishtha, borne away, the vindictive Vishvamitra becoming enraged addressed Sarasvati, saying

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: यस्मान्मां त्वं सरिच्छ्रेष्ठे वञ्चयित्वा पुनर्गता॥ शोणितं वह कल्याणि रक्षोग्रामणिसम्मतम्।
en: Since, O best of rivers, thou hast gone away and deceived me, let thy current be changed into blood liked of Rakshasas!'

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: ततः सरस्वती शप्ता विश्वामित्रेण धीमता॥ अवहच्छोणितोन्मिभं तोयं संवत्सरं तदा।
en: Thus cursed by the intelligent Vishvamitra, Sarasvati flowed for a whole year, bearing blood mixed with water.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: अथर्षयश्च देवाश्च गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्तदा॥ सरस्वती तथा दृष्ट्वा बभूवुर्भृशदुःखिताः।
en: Beholding the Sarasvati in that plights the gods, the Gandharvas and the Apsaras became filled with great sorrow.

description: The history of the Tirtha Vasishthapavaha
sn: एवं वसिष्ठापवाहो लोके ख्यातो जनाधिप॥ आगच्छच्च पुनर्मार्ग स्वमेव सरितां वरा॥
en: For this reason, O king, the tirtha passed by the name of Vashishthapavaha on Earth. The best of rivers, however, once more regained her own proper condition.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा शप्ता तेन क्रुद्धेन विश्वामित्रेण धीमता। तस्मिंस्तीर्थवरे शुभ्रे शोणितं समुपावहत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Cursed by the intelligent Vishvamitra in anger, Sarasvati, in that sacred and best of tirthas, flowed in bloody current.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: अथाजग्मुस्ततो राजन् राक्षसास्तत्र भारत। तत्र ते शोणितं सर्वे पिबन्तः सुखमासते॥
en: Then, O king, many Rakshasas come and lived happily there, drinking the blood that flowed.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: तृप्ताश्च सुभृशं तेन सुखिता विगतज्वराः। नृत्यन्तश्च हसन्तश्च यथा स्वर्गजितस्तथा॥
en: Highly pleased with that blood, cheerfully and without anxiety of any kind, they danced and laughed there like persons that have (by virtue) attained to heaven.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य ऋषयः सुतपोधनाः। तीर्थयात्रां समाजग्मुः सरस्वत्यां महीपते॥
en: After some time had passed away, some Rishis, having asceticism for their wealth, came to the Sarasvati, O king, on pilgrimage.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: तेषु सर्वेषु तीर्थेषु स्वाप्लुत्य मुनिपुङ्गवाः। प्राप्य प्रीतिं परां चापि तपोलुब्धा विशारदाः॥ प्रययुर्हि ततो राजन् तेन तीर्थमसृग्वहम्। अथागम्य महाभागास्ततं तीर्थं दारुणं तदा।॥
en: Those foremost of ascetics, having bathed in all the tirthas and obtained great delight, became desirous of acquiring more merit. Those learned sages at last came. O king, to that tirtha where the Sarasvati flowed in a bloody current. Those highly blessed Rishis, arriving at that frightful tirtha.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: दृष्ट्वा तोयं सरस्वत्याः शोणितेन परिप्लुतम्। पीतमानं च रक्षोभिर्बहुभिर्नृपसत्तम॥
en: Beheld the water of the Sarasvati mixed with blood and numberless Rakshasas, O king, drinking it.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा राक्षसान् राजन् मुनयः संशितव्रताः। परित्राणे सरस्वत्याः परं यत्नं प्रचक्रिरे॥
en: Seeing those Rakshasas, O king, those ascetics of rigid vows tried much for rescuing the Sarasvati from that condition.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: ते तु सर्वे महाभागाः समागम्य महाव्रताः। आहूय सरितां श्रेष्ठामिदं वचनमब्रुवन्॥ कारणं ब्रूहि कल्याणि किमर्थं ते हृदो ह्ययम्। एवमाकुलतां यातः श्रुत्वा ध्यास्यामहे वयम्॥
en: Arriving there, those Rishis invoked that foremost of rivers and said to her-"Tell us the reason, O auspicious lady, why this lake in you has been distressed with such a plight. Hearing it, we shall use our efforts to restore its pristine condition.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: ततः सा सर्वमाचष्ट यथावृत्तं प्रवेपती। दुःखितामथ तां दृष्ट्वा ऊचुस्ते वै तपोधनाः॥
en: Thus accosted, Sarasvati, trembling as she spoke, informed them of everything that had taken place. Seeing her thus woe-begone, those ascetics told her-

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: कारणं श्रुतमस्माभिः शापश्चैव श्रुतोऽनघे। करिष्यन्ति तु यत् प्राप्तं सर्वं एव तपोधनाः॥
en: "We have heard of your curse, O sinless lady! All of us shall try."

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: एवंमुक्त्वा सरिच्छ्रेष्टामूचुस्तेऽथ परस्परम्। विमोचयामहे सर्वे शापादेतां सरस्वतीम्॥
en: Having said so to that foremost of rivers, they then consulted with one another-"All of us shall release Sarasvati from her curse."

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: ते सर्वे ब्राह्मणा राजस्तपोभिर्नियमैस्तथा। उपवासैश्च विविधैर्यमैः कष्टव्रतैस्तथा॥ आराध्य पशुभर्तारं महादेवं जगत्पतिम्। तां देवीं मोक्षयामासुः सरिच्छ्रेष्ठां सरस्वतीम्॥ तेषां तु सा प्रभावेण प्रकृतिस्था सरस्वती। प्रसन्नसलिला जज्ञे यथापूर्वं तथैव हि॥ निर्मुक्ता च सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा विबभौ सा यथा पुरा।
en: O king, adoring Mahadeva, that Lord of the universe and protector of all creatures, with penances, vows, fasts, abstinences and painful observances, all those Brahmanas emancipated that foremost of rivers, viz., the divine Sarasvati.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: दृष्ट्वा तोयं सरस्वत्या मुनिभिस्तैस्तथा कृतम्॥ तानेव शरणं जम्मू राक्षसाः क्षुधितास्तथा।
en: Beholding the water of Sarasvati purified by those ascetics, the Rakshasas (that lived there), stricken with hunger, sought the protection of those ascetics themselves.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: कृत्वाञ्जलिं ततो राजन् राक्षसाः क्षुधयाऽर्दिताः॥ ऊचुस्तान् वै मुनीन् सर्वान् कृपायुक्तान् पुनः पुनः। वयं च क्षुधिताश्चैव धर्माद्धीनाश्च शाश्वतात्॥ न च नः कामकारोऽयं यद् वयं पापकारिणः।
en: Stricken with hunger, the Rakshasas, with clasped hands, repeatedly said to those ascetics filled with compassion viz.-"All of us are hungry? We have deviated from the path of virtue! That we are sinful is not of our own free will!'

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: युष्माकं चाप्रसादेन दुष्कृतेन च कर्मणा॥ यत् पापं वर्धतेऽस्माकं ततः स्मो ब्रह्मराक्षसाः। योषितां चैव पापेन योनिदोषकृतेन च॥ एवं हि वैश्यशूद्राणां क्षत्रियाणां तथैव च। ये ब्राह्मणान् प्रद्विषन्ति ते भवन्तीह राक्षसाः॥ आचार्यमृत्विजं चैव गुरुं वृद्धजनं तथा। प्राणिनो येऽवमन्यन्ते ते भवन्तीह राक्षसाः॥
en: Through the want of your grace and our own evil deeds, as also for the sexual sins of our women, our sins multiply and we have become Brahma-Rakshasas! So amongst Vaishyas and Shudras and Kshatriyas, those that hate and injure Brahmanas became Rakshasas.'

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: तत् कुरुध्वमिहास्माकं तारणं द्विजसत्तमाः। शक्ता भवन्तः सर्वेषां लोकानामपि तारणे॥
en: O best of Brahmanas, arrange then for our relief. You are capable of saving all the worlds!'

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: तेषां वचनं श्रुत्वा तुष्टुवुस्तां महानदीम्। मोक्षार्थं रक्षसां तेषामूचुः प्रयतमानसाः॥ क्षुतं कीटावपन्नं च यचोच्छिष्टाचितं भवेत्। सुकेशमवधूतं च रुदितोपहतं च यत्॥
en: Hearing these words of theirs, those ascetics lauded the great river. For the rescue of those Rakshasas, with contracted minds those ascetics said-"The food over which one will sneeze, that in which there are worms and insects, that which may be mixed with refuges of food, that which is mixed with hair, that which is trampled. That which is mixed with tears shall make up the food of these Rakshasas!'

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: एभिः संसृष्टमन्नं च भागोऽसौ रक्षसामिह। तस्माज्ज्ञात्वा सदा विद्वानेतान् यत्नाद् विवर्जयेत्॥ राक्षसान्नमसौ भुङ्क्ते यो भुङ्क्ते ह्यन्नमीदृशम्।
en: Knowing all this, the learned man shall carefully avoid these kinds of food. He that shall take such food shall be considered as partaking of the food of Rakshasas.'

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: तु शोधयित्वा ततस्तीर्थमृषयस्ते तपोधनाः॥ मोक्षार्थं राक्षसानां च नदीं तां प्रत्यचोदयन्।
en: Having thus purified the tirtha, those ascetics thus prayed to that river for the relief of those Rakshasas.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: महर्षीणां मतं ज्ञात्वा ततः सा सरितां वरा॥ अरुणामानयामास स्वां तनूं पुरुषर्षभ।
en: Understanding the wishes of those great Rishis, that best of rivers caused her body, O foremost of men, to assume a new forn called Arjuna.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: तस्यां ते राक्षसाः स्नात्वा तनूस्त्यक्त्वा दिवं गताः।। अरुणायां महाराज ब्रह्मवध्यापहा हि सा।
en: Bathing in that new river the Rakshasas renounced their bodies and went to heaven.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: एतमर्थमभिज्ञाय देवराजः शतक्रतुः,॥ तस्मिंस्तीर्थे वीरे स्नात्वा विमुक्तः पाप्मना किल।
en: Ascertaining all this, the king of the celestials, viz., Indra, of a hundred sacrifices, bathed in that best of tirthas and was freed of a grievous sin."

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: जनमेजय उवाच किमर्थं भगवान् शक्रो ब्रह्मवध्यामवाप्तवान्॥ कथमस्मिंश्च तीर्थे वै आप्लुत्याकल्मषोऽभवत्।
en: Janamejaya said "Why was Indra affected with the sin of Brahmanicide! How also did he become freed by bathing in that tirtha?''

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: वैश्मपायन उवाच शृणुष्वैतदुपाख्यानं यथावृत्तं जनेश्वर॥ यथा बिभेद समयं नमुचेर्वासवः पुरा।
en: Vaishampayana said "Listen to that history, O king, listen to those events as they took place. Hear how Indra formerly broke his treaty with Namuchi.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: नमुचिर्वासवाद् भीत: सूर्यरश्मि समाविशत्॥ तेनेन्द्रः सख्यमकरोत् समयं चेदमब्रवीत्। न चाद्रेण न शुष्केण न रात्रौ नापि चाहनि॥ वधिष्याप्यसुरश्रेष्ठ सखे सत्येन ते शपे।
en: The Asura Namuchi, from fear of Vasava, had entered into a ray of the Sun. Indra then made friends with Namuchi and made a contract with him, saying-"O king, of Asuras, I shall not kill you, O friend, with anything that is wet or dry. I shall not kill you in the night or in the day! Forsooth I swear this to you.'

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: एवं स कृत्वा समयं दृष्ट्वा नीहारमीश्वरः॥ चिच्छेदास्य शिरो राजन्नपां फेनेन वासवः।
en: Having made this understanding, the lord Indra one day behold a fog. He then, O king, sundered Namuchi's head, using the foam of water as his weapon.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: तच्छिरो नमुचेश्छिन्नं पृष्ठतः शक्रमन्वियात्॥ भो भो मित्रघ्न पापेति ब्रुवाणां शक्रमन्तिकात्।
en: The severed head of Namuchi thereupon pursued Indra from behind, saying repeatedly from a near place-"O killer of a friend, O wretch!'

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: एवं स शिरसा तेन चोद्यमानः पुनः पुनः॥ पितामहाय संतप्त एतमर्थं न्यवेदयत्।
en: Thus addressed repeatedly by that head; Indra went to grandfather and informed him, sorrowfully of what had taken place.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: तमब्रवील्लोकगुरुररुणायां यथाविधि॥ इष्ट्वोपस्पृश देवेन्द्र तीर्थे पापभयापहे।
en: The supreme lord of the universe said to him-"Performing a sacrifice, bathe duly, O king of gods, in Aruna, the tirtha which saves all from the fear of sin!

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: एषा पुण्यजला शक्र कृता मुनिभिरेव तु॥ निगूढमस्यागमनमिहासीत् पूर्वमेव तु।
en: The water of that river, O Shakra, has been sanctified by the ascetics! Formerly the river lay there concealed.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: ततोऽभ्येत्यारुणां देवीं प्लावयामास वारिणा॥ सरस्वत्यारुणायाश्च पुण्योऽयं संगमो महान्।
en: The divine Sarasvati, repaired to the Aruna and overflowed it with her waters. This confluence of Sarasvati and Aruna is highly sacred!

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: इह त्वं यज देवेन्द्र दद दानान्यनेकशः॥ अत्राप्लुत्य सुघोरात् त्वं पातकाद् विप्रमोक्ष्यसे।
en: There, O king of gods, perform a sacrifice. Distribute enough of presents. Performing thy ablutions there, you shall be freed off of your sin.'

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: इत्युक्तः स सरस्वत्याः कुञ्जे वै जनमेजय॥ इष्ट्वा यथावद् बलभिदरुणायामुपस्पृशत्। स मुक्तः पाप्मना तेन ब्रह्मवध्याकृतेन च॥ जगाम संहृष्टमनास्त्रिदिवं त्रिदशेश्वरः।
en: Thus Addressed, Indra, at these words of Brahman, O Janamejaya, performed in that abode of Sarasvati various sacrifices. Distributing many presents and bathing in that tirtha, he of a hundred sacrifices, the destroyer of Vala, duly performed certain sacrifices and then bathed in the Aruna. He became freed from the sin caused by Brahmanicide. The king of the celestial region, then returned to heaven with a joyful heart.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: शिरस्तचापि नमुचेस्तत्रैवाप्लुत्य भारत। लोकान् कामदुघान् प्राप्तमक्षयान् राजसत्तम॥
en: The head of Namuchi also dropped into that stream O Bharata and Asura gained many blessed regions, O best of kings, that granted ever wish.”

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत्राप्युपस्पृश्य बलो महात्मा दत्त्वा च दानानि पृथग्विधानि। अवाप्य धर्मं परमार्थकर्मा जगाम सोमस्य महत् सुतीर्थम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said "The great Baladeva, having bathed in that tirtha and given away many kinds of gifts, acquired great virtue. Of righteous deeds, he then proceeded to the great tirtha of Soma.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: यत्रायजद् राजसूयेन सोमः साक्षात् पुरा विधिवत् पार्थिवेन्द्रः। अत्रिीमान् विप्रमुख्यो बभूव होता यस्मिन् ऋतुमुख्ये महात्मा॥ यस्यान्तेऽभूत् सुमहद् दानवानां दैतेयानां राक्षसानां च देवैः। यस्मिन् युद्धं तारकाख्यं सुतीव्र यत्र स्कन्दस्तारकाख्यं जघान॥
en: There, formerly Soma himself, O emperor, had celebrated the Rajasuya sacrifice. The great Atri, that foremost of Brahmanas, endued with great intelligence, became the sacrificial priest in that grand sacrifice. Upon the termination of that sacrifice, a great battle took place between the gods and the Danavas, the Daityas and the Rakshasas. That fierce battle known after the name of the Asura Taraka. In that battle Skanda killed Taraka.

description: The history of Indra's curse and expiation
sn: सैनापत्यं लब्धवान् देवतानां महासेनो यत्र दैत्यान्तकर्ता। साक्षाचैव न्यवसत् कार्तिकेयः सदा कुमारो यत्र स प्लक्षराजः॥
en: There, on the occasion, Mahasena, that destroyer of Daityas, became the generalissimo of the celestial forces. In that tirtha is a huge Ashvattha tree. Under its shade, Kartikeya, otherwise called Kumara, always lives in person."

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: जनमेजय उवाच सरस्वत्याः प्रभावोऽयमुक्तस्ते द्विजसत्तम। कुमारस्याभिषेकं तु ब्रह्मन् व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Janamejaya said "You have described the inerits of the Sarasvati, O best of Brahmanas. You should, O Rishi, describe to me the investiture of Kumara by the gods.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: यस्मिन् देशे च काले च यथा च वदतां वर। यैश्चाभिषिक्तो भगवान् विधिना येन च प्रभुः॥ स्कन्दो यथा च दैत्यानामकरोत् कदनं महत्। तथा मे सर्वामाचक्ष्व परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: Great is my curiosity. Tell me everything, therefore, about the time, place and manner in which the worshipful and powerful Skanda was appointed the commander-in-chief of the celestial hosts! Tell me also, O best of speakers, who invested him and who performed the actual rites and how the celestial generalissimo killed the Daityas."

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कुरुवंशस्य सदृशं कौतूहलमिदं तव। हर्षमुत्पादयत्येव वचो मे जनमेजय॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Your curiosity indeed becomes a Kuru. The words that I shall speak, will, O Janamejaya, please you.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि शृण्वानस्य नराधिप। अभिषेकं कुमारस्य प्रभावं च महात्मनः॥
en: I shall describe to you the appointment of Kumara and the prowess of that high-souled one, since, O king, you wish to hear it.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: तेजो माहेश्वरं स्कनमग्नौ प्रपतितं पुरा। तत् सर्वभक्षो भगवान् नाशकद् दग्धुमक्षयम्॥
en: In days of yore the vital seed of Maheshvara, dropped into a blazing fire. The consumer of everything, the worshipful Agni, could not burn that indestructible seed.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: तेनासीदतितेजस्वी दीप्तिमान् हव्यवाहनः। न चैव धारयामास गर्भ तेजोमयं तदा॥
en: On the other hand, the carrier of sacrificial libations, for that seed, became possessed of great energy and splendour. He could not bear within himself that powerful seed.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: स गङ्गामभिसंगम्य नियोगाद् ब्रह्मणः प्रभुः। गर्भमाहितवान् दिव्यं भास्करोपमतेजसम्॥
en: At the behest of Brahma, the lord Agni, approaching the river Ganga, threw into her that divine seed effulgent like the Sun.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: अथ गङ्गापि तं गर्भमसहन्ती विधारणे। उत्ससर्ज गिरौ रम्ये हिमवत्मरार्चिते॥
en: Ganga also, unable to hold it, threw it on the beautiful breast of Himavat adored of the celestials.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: स तत्र ववृधे लोकानावृत्य ज्वलनात्मजः। ददृशुर्चलनाकारं तं गर्भमथ कृत्तिकाः॥
en: Thereupon Agni's son began to grow there, overpowering all the worlds by his energy. Meanwhile the six Krittikas saw that child of fiery splendour.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: शरस्तम्बे महात्मानमनलात्मजमीश्वरम्। ममायमिति ताः सर्वाः पुत्रार्थिन्योऽभिचुक्रुशुः॥
en: Seeing that powerful lord, that great son of Agni, lying on a clump of reeds, all the six Krittikas, who wanted to have a son, cried aloud, saying-"This child is mine, this child is mine.'

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: तासां विदित्वा भावं तं मातृणां भगवान् प्रभुः। प्रस्तुतानां पय: षड्भिर्वदनैरपिबत् तदा॥
en: Understanding the feelings of those six mothers, the wonderful lord Skanda sucked the breasts of all, having assumed six months.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: तं प्रभावं समालक्ष्य तस्य बालस्य कृत्तिकाः। परं विस्मयमापन्ना देव्यो दिव्यवपुर्धराः॥
en: Beholding that power of the child, the Krittikas, those beautiful goddesses, were stricken with wonder.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: यत्रोत्सृष्टः स भगवान् गङ्गया गिरिमूर्धनि। स शैलः काञ्चनः सर्वः सम्बभौ कुरुसत्तम॥
en: And because the adorable child had been thrown by the river Ganga upon the summit of Himavat, that mountain looked beautiful, having, O delighter of the Kurus, been transformed into gold.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: वर्धता चैव गर्भेण पृथिवी तेन रञ्जिता। अतश्च सर्वे संवृत्ता गिरयः काञ्चनाकराः॥
en: With that growing child the whole Earth became beautiful and it was therefore that mountains produced gold.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: कुमारः सुमहावीर्यः कीर्तिकेय इति स्मृतः। गाङ्गेयः पूर्वमभवन्महायोगबलान्वितः॥
en: Possessed of great energy, the child passed by the name of Kartikeya. At first he had been called by the name of Gangeya. He was endued with high ascetic powers.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: शमेन तपसा चैव वीर्येण च समन्वितः। ववृधेऽतीव राजेन्द्र चन्द्रवत् प्रियदर्शनः॥
en: Possessed of self-restraint, asceticism and great energy, the child grew up. O king, into a person of highly charming features like Soma himself.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: स तस्मिन् काञ्चने दिव्ये शरस्तम्भे श्रिया वृतः। स्तूयमानः सदा शेते गन्धर्वैर्मुनिभिस्तथा॥
en: Highly beautiful the child lay on that excellent and golden clump of reeds, worshipped and lauded by Gandharvas and ascetics.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: तथैतमन्वनृत्यन्तः देवकन्या सहस्रशः। दिव्यवादित्रनृत्यज्ञाः स्तुवन्त्यश्चारुदर्शनाः॥
en: Thousands of celestial girls, of very handsome features, accomplished in celestial music and dance, lauded him and danced before him.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: अन्वास्ते च नदी देवं गङ्गा वै सरितां वरा। दधार पृथिवी चैनं बिभ्रती रूपमुत्तमम्॥
en: The best of all rivers, viz., Ganga, waited upon that god. The earth also, assuming great beauty, held the child on her lap.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: जातकर्मादिकास्तत्र क्रियाश्चक्रे बृहस्पतिः। वेदश्चैनं चतुर्मूर्तिरुपतस्थे कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: The celestial priest Brihaspati performed the usual rites consequent upon the birth, of that child. The Vedas, assuming a fourfold form, approached the child with clasped hands.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: धनुर्वेदश्चतुष्पादः शस्त्रग्रामः ससंग्रहः। तत्रैनं समुपातिष्ठत् साक्षाद् वाणी च केवला॥
en: The science of arms, with its four divisions and all the weapons, as also all kinds of arrows, came to him.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: स ददर्श महावीर्यं देवदेवमुमापतिम्। शैलपुत्र्या समासीनं भूतसंघशतैर्वृतम्॥
en: One day, the highly energetic child, saw that god of gods, viz., the lord of Uma, seated with the daughter of Himavat, amid a number of goblins.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: निकाया भूतसंघानां परमाद्भुतदर्शनाः। विकृता विकृताकारा बिकृताभरणध्वजाः॥
en: Those goblins, of lean bodies, had wonderful features. They were ugly both in person and in features and bore on this person awkward ornaments and marks.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: व्याघ्रसिंहर्क्षवदना विडालमकराननाः। वृषदंशमुखाश्चान्ये गजोष्ट्रवदनास्तथा॥ उलूकवदनाः केचिद् गृध्रगोमायुदर्शनाः।
en: Their faces were like those of tigers and lions and bears and cats and Makaras. Others had faces like those of scorpions; others had faces like those of elephant and camels and owls. And some had faces like those of vultures and jackals.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: क्रौञ्चपारावतनिभैर्वदनै राङ्कवैरपि।॥ श्वाविच्छल्यकगोधानामजैडकगवां तथा। सदृशानि वपूंष्यन्ये तत्र यत्र व्यधारयन्॥ केचिच्छैलाम्बुदप्रख्याश्चक्रोद्यतगदायुधाः। केचिदञ्जनपुञ्जाभाः केचिच्छ्वेताचलप्रभाः॥ सप्त मातृगणाश्चैव समाजग्मुर्विशाम्पते।
en: And some had faces like those of cranes and pigeons and Kurus. And some had bodies like those of dogs and porcupines and iguanas and goats and sheep and cows. And some resembled mountains and some, oceans and some stood with uplifted discs and maces for their weapons. And some looked like masses of antimony and some, like with mountains. The seven matris also were present there, O king.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: साध्या विश्वेऽथ मरुतो वसवः पितरस्तथा॥ रुद्रादित्यास्तथा सिद्धा भुजगाः दानवाः खगाः। ब्रह्मा स्वयम्भूभगवान् सपुत्रः सह विष्णुना॥ शक्रस्तथाभ्ययाद् द्रष्टुं कुमारवरमच्युतम्।
en: The Saddhyas, the Vishvedevas, the Maruts, the Vasus, the Pitris, the Rudras, the Adityas, the Siddhas, the Danavas, the birds, the self-create and worshipful Brahman with his sons and Vishnu and Shakra, all went there for beholding that child of ever-increasing glory.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: नारदप्रमुखाश्चापि देवगन्धर्वसत्तमाः॥ देवर्षयश्च सिद्धाश्च बृहस्पतिपुरोगमाः। पितरो जगतः श्रेष्ठा देवानामपि देवताः॥ तेऽपि तत्र समाजग्मुर्यामा धामाश्च सर्वशः।
en: And many leading celestials and Gandharvas, headed by Narada and many celestial Rishis and Siddhas headed by Brihaspati and the guardian deities of the universe, those foremost ones, they that are regarded as gods of the gods and the Yamas and the Dhamas, all went there.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: स तु बालोऽपि बलवान महायोगबलान्वितः॥ अभ्याजगाम देवेशं शूलहस्तं पिनाकिनम्।
en: Gifted with great strength and great ascetic power, the child proceeded before that lord of the gods, viz., Mahadeva, armed with trident and Pinaka.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: तमाव्रजन्तमालक्ष्य शिवस्यासीन्मनोगतम्॥ युगपच्छैलपुत्र्याश्च गङ्गायाः पावकस्य च। कं नु पूर्वमयं बालो गौरवादभ्युपैष्यति॥ अपि मामिति सर्वेषां तेषामासीन्मनोगतम्।
en: Seeing the child coming, the thought entered the mind of Shiva, that of Himavat's daughter and that of Ganga and of Agni, as to whom amongst the four, the child would first approach for honoring him or her. Each of them thought-He will come to me.'

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: तेषामेतमभिप्रायं चतुर्णामुपलक्ष्य सः॥ युगपद् योगमास्थाय ससर्ज विविधास्तनूः।
en: Understanding the desire of each of those four, he had recourse to his Yoga powers and assumed simultaneously four different forms.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: ततोऽभवचतुर्मूतिः क्षणेन भगवान् प्रभुः॥ तस्य शाखो विशाखश्च नैगमेयश्च पृष्ठतः।
en: The worshipful and powerful lord assumed those four forms in a instant. The three forms that stood behind were Shakra and Vishakha and Naigameya.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: एवं स कृत्वा ह्यात्मानं चतुर्धा भगवान् प्रभुः॥ यतो रुद्रस्ततः स्कन्दो गजामाद्भुतदर्शनः।
en: Having divided his self into four forms, he went towards the four that sat expecting him. The wonderful form called Skanda proceed where Rudra was sitting.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: विशाखस्तु ययौ येन देवी गिरीवरात्मजा॥ शाखो ययौ स भगवान् वायुमूर्तिर्विभावसुं। नैगमेयोऽगमद् गङ्गां कुमारः पावकप्रभः॥
en: Vishakha went where the divine daughter of Himavat was. The adorable Shakha, which is Kartikeya's airy form, went towards Agni. Naigameya, that child of fiery splendour, went before Ganga.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: सर्वे भासुरदेहास्ते चत्वारः समरूपिणः। तान् समभ्ययुरव्यग्रास्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: All those four forms, of similar appearance, were highly effulgent. The four forms went calmly to the four gods and goddesses. It was indeed wonderful.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: हाहाकारो महानासीद् देवदानवरक्षसाम्। तद् दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यमद्भूतं लोमहर्षणम्॥
en: The gods, the Danavas and the Rakshasas, made a loud noise seeing that exceedingly wonderful and hair stirring incident.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: ततो रुद्रश्च देवीं च पावकश्च पितामहम्। गड्या सहिताः सर्वे प्रणिपेतुर्जगत्पतिम्॥
en: Then Rudra and the goddess Uma and Agni and Ganga, all bowed unto Brahma, that lord of the universe.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: प्रणिपत्य ततस्ते तु विधिवद् राजपुङ्गवा उदमूचुर्वचो राजन् कार्तिकेयप्रियेप्सया॥ अस्य बालस्य भगवन्नाधिपत्यं यथेप्सितम्। अस्मात्प्रियार्थं देवेश सदृशं दातुमर्हसि॥
en: Having duly bowed into him, they said these words, O king, from desire of doing god unto Kartikeya:-"O Lord of the gods, for the sake of our happiness you should give this youth some kind of sovereignty that may suit him and that he may desire.'

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: ततः स भगवान् धीमान् सर्वलोकपितामहः। मनसा चिन्तयामास किमयं लभतामिति॥
en: Thereat, the worshipful grandfather of all the worlds, endued with great intelligence, began to think within his mind as to what he should confer of that youth.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: ऐश्वर्याणि च सर्वाणि देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्। भूतयक्षविहङ्गानां पन्नगानां च सर्वशः॥ पूर्वमेवादिदेशासौ निकायेषु महात्मनाम्। समर्थं च तमैश्वर्ये महामतिरमन्यत॥
en: He had formerly given away to the gods all kinds of wealth over which the great celestials, the Gandharvas, the Rakshasas, ghosts, Yakshas, birds and snakes now region. Brahman, therefore, considered that youth as fully qualified to have the dominion which had been bestowed upon the gods.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: ततो मुहूर्तं स ध्यात्वा देवानां श्रेयसि स्थितः। सैनापत्यं ददौ तस्मै सर्वभूतेषु भारत॥
en: Having thought for a moment, the grandfather, always seeking the well-being of the celestials, conferred upon him the dignity of a generalissimo among all creatures, O Bharata.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: सर्वदेवनिकायानां ये राजानः परिश्रुताः। तान् सर्वान् व्यादिदेशास्मै सर्वभूतपितामहः॥
en: He further ordered all those leading gods and other formless beings to wait upon him.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: ततः कुमारमादाय देवा ब्रह्मपुरोगमाः। अभिषेकार्थमाजग्मुः शैलेन्द्र सहितास्ततः॥
en: Then the gods headed by Brahman, taking that youth with them, came in a body to Himavat.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: पुण्यां हैमवती देवी सरिच्छेष्ठां सरस्वतीम्। समन्तपञ्चके या वै त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता॥
en: The site selected by them was the bank of the sacred and divine Sarasvati, that foremost of rivers, taking her rise from Himavat, which is celebrated over the three worlds by the name of Samantapanchaka.

description: The investiture of Kartikeya. His companions
sn: तत्र तीरे सरस्वत्याः पुण्ये सर्वगुणान्विते। निषेदुर्देवगन्धर्वाः सर्वे सम्पूर्णमानसाः॥
en: There, on the sacred bank of the Sarasvati, the gods and the Gandharvas took their seats with gladness on account of the gratification of all their desire."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽभिषेकसम्भारान् सर्वान् सम्भृत्य शास्त्रतः। बृहस्पतिः समिद्धेऽग्नौ जुहावाग्निं यथाविधि॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Collecting all articles sanctioned by Shastras for the ceremony of investiture. Brihaspati duly poured libations of the burning fire.

sn: ततो हिमवता दत्ते मणिप्रवरशोभिते। दिव्यारत्नाचिते पुण्ये निषण्णं परमासने॥
en: Himavat gave a seat which was set with many costly gems. Kartikeya was made a site on that sacred and best of seats set with excellent gems.

sn: सर्वमङ्गलसम्भारैर्विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम्। आभिषेचनिक द्रव्यं गृहीत्वा देवातगणाः॥
en: The gods collected there all sorts of sacred articles, with due rites and mantras, that were necessary for the ceremony.

sn: इन्द्राविष्णू महावी? सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ तथा। धाता चैव विधाता च तथा चैवानिलानलौ॥ पूष्णा भगेनार्यम्णा च अंशेन च विवस्वता। रुद्रश्च सहितो धीमान् मित्रेण वरुणेन च॥ रुद्रैर्वसुभिरादित्यैरश्विभ्यां च वृतः प्रभुः। विश्वेदेवैर्मरुद्भिश्च साध्यैश्च पितृभिः सह॥ गन्धवैरप्सरोभिश्च यक्षराक्षसपन्नगैः। देवर्षिभिरसंख्यातैस्तथा ब्रह्मर्षिभिस्तथा।॥ वैखानसैर्वालखिल्यैर्वाय्वारैर्मरीचिपैः। भृगुभिश्चाङ्गिरोभिश्च यतिभिश्च महात्मभिः॥ सपैर्विद्याधरैः पुण्यैर्योगसिद्धस्तथा वृतः। पितामहः पुलस्त्यश्च पुलहश्च महातपाः॥ अङ्गिराः कश्यपोऽपिश्च मरीचि गुरेव च। ऋतुर्हरः प्रचेताश्च मनुर्दक्षस्तथैव च॥ ऋतवश्च ग्रहाश्चैव ज्योतिषिं च विशाम्पते। मूर्तिमत्यश्च सरितो वेदाश्चैव सनातनाः॥ समुद्राश्च ह्रदाश्चैव तीर्थानि विविधानि च। पृथिवी द्यौर्दिशश्चैव पादपाश्च जनाधिप॥ अदितिर्देवमाता च ह्रीः श्रीः स्वाहा सरस्वती। उमा शची सिनीवाली तथा चानुमतिः कुहूः॥ राका च धिषणा चैव पन्यश्चान्या दिवौकसाम्। हिमवांश्चैव विन्ध्यश्च मेस्श्चानेकशृङ्गवान्॥ ऐरावतः सानुचरः कलाः काष्ठास्तथैव च। मासार्धमासा ऋतवस्तथा रात्र्यहनी नृप।॥ उच्चैःश्रवा हयश्रेष्ठो नागराजश्च वासुकिः। अरुणो गरुडश्चैव वृक्षाश्चौषधिभिः सह॥ धर्मश्च भगवान् देवः समाजग्मुर्हि सङ्गताः। कालो यमश्च मृत्युश्च यमस्यानुचराश्च ये॥
en: The various gods, viz., Indra, Vishnu, Surya, Chandramas, Dhatri, Vidhatri, Vayu, Agni, Pushan, Bhaga, Aryaman, Ansha, Vivasvat, Rudra, of great intelligence, Mitra, the eleven Rudras, the eight Vasus, the twelve Adityas, the twin Ashvins, the Vishvedevas, the Maruts, the Saddhyas, the Pitris, the Gandharvas, the Apsaras, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Pannagas, innumerable celestial Rishis, the Vaikhanasas, the Valakhilyas, those others among Rishis that live only on air and those that live on the rays of the Sun, the descendants of Bhrigu and Angiras, many great Yatis, all the Vidyadharas, all those that were crowned with ascetic success, the Grandfather, Pulastya, the great ascetic Pulaha, Angiras, Kashyapa, Atri, Marichi, Bhrigu, Kratu, Hara, Prachetas, Manu, Daksha, the Seasons, the Planets and all the luminaries, O monarch, all the rivers in their embodied forms, the eternal Vedas, the Seas, the Lakes, the various Tirthas, the Earth, the Sky, the Cardinal and Subsidiary points of the compass, all the Trees, Aditi the mother of the gods, Hri, Shri, Svaha, Sarasvati, Uma, Shachi, Sinivali, Anumati, Kuhu, the Day of the new Moon, the Day of the full Moon, the wives of the celestials, Himavat, Vindhya, Meru of many summits, Airavata with all his followers, the divisions of time called Kala, Kashtha, Fortnight, the Seasons, Night and Day O king, Uchchaishravas the king of horses, Vasuki the king of the Serpents, Aruna, Garuda, the Trees, the deciduous herbs and the worshipful god Dharma, all came there in a body. And there came also Kala, Yama, Mrityu and the followers of Yama.

sn: बहुलत्वाश्च नोक्ता ये विविधा देवतागणाः। ते कुमाराभिषेकार्थं समाजग्मुस्ततस्ततः॥
en: I do not mention the various other gods that came there lest the list be a heavy one. All of them came to that ceremony for investing Kartikeya with the dignity of generalissimo.

sn: जगृहुस्ते तदा राजन् सर्व एव दिवौकसः। आभिषेचनिकं भाण्डं मङ्गलानि च सर्वशः॥
en: All the celestials, O king brought there every thing necessary for the ceremony and every sacred article.

sn: दिव्यसम्भारसंयुक्तैः कलशैः काञ्चनैर्नृप। सरस्वतीभिः पुण्याभिर्दिव्यतोयाभिरेव तु॥ अभ्यषिञ्चन् कुमारं वै सम्प्रहृष्टा दिवौकसः। सेनापति महात्मानमसुराणां भयंकरम्॥
en: Gladly the celestials made that great youth, that terror of the Asuras, the generalissimo of the celestial hosts, after pouring upon his head the sacred and excellent water of the Sarasvati from golden jars that contained other sacred articles necessary for the purpose.

sn: पुरा यथा महाराज वरुणं वै जलेश्वरम्। तथाभ्यषिञ्चद् भगवान् सर्वलोकपितामहः॥
en: The Grandfather of the words, viz., Brahman and Kashyapa of great energy and all others, all poured water upon Skanda even as, O king, the gods had poured water on the head of Varuna, the lord of waters, when placing him in this dominion.

sn: कश्यपश्च महातेजा ये चान्ये लोककीर्तिताः। तस्मै ब्रह्मा ददौ प्रीतो बलिनो वातरंहसः॥ कामवीर्यधरान् सिद्धान् महापरिषदान् प्रभुः।
en: The lord Brahman then, with a pleased heart, gave to Skanda four powerful companions, gifted with speed of the wind, crowned with ascetic success and gifted with energy which they could increase at will.

sn: नन्दिसेनं लोहिताक्षं घण्टाकर्णं च सम्मतम्॥ चतुर्थमस्यानुचरं ख्यातं कुमुदमालिनम्।
en: They named Nandisena and Lohitaksha and Ghantakarna and Kumudamalin.

sn: तत्र स्थाणुर्महातेजा महापारिषदं प्रभुः॥ मायाशतधरं कामं कामवीर्यं बलान्वितम्।
en: The lord Sthanu, O king, gave to Skanda a companion possessed of great impetuosity, capable of producing a hundred illusions and gifted with might and energy that he could increase at will. And he was the great destroyer if Asuras.

sn: ददौ स्कन्दाय राजेन्द्र सुरारिविनिबर्हणम्॥ स हि देवासुरे युद्धे दैत्यानां भीमकर्मणाम्। जघान दोभ्या॑ संक्रुद्धः प्रयुतानि चतुर्दश॥
en: In the great battle between the gods and the Asuras, this companion that Sthanu gave, worked up with ire killed with his hands alone, fourteen millions of Daityas of terrible deeds. were

sn: तथा देवा ददुस्तस्मै सेनां नैर्ऋतसंकुलाम्। देवशत्रुक्षयकरीमजय्यां विष्णुरूपिणीम्॥
en: The god then made over to Skanda he celestial host, invincible containing many celestial troops, capable of destroying the enemies of the gods and of forms like that of Vishnu.

sn: जयशब्दं तथा चक्रुर्देवा: सर्वे सवासवाः। गन्धर्वा यक्षरक्षांसि मनुयः पितरस्तथा॥
en: The gods then, with Vasava at their head and the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Munis and the Pitris, all exclaimed-"Victory of Skanda.'

sn: ततः प्रादादनुचरौ यमः कालोपमावुभौ। उन्माथश्च प्रमाथश्च महावी? महाद्युती॥
en: Then Yama gave him two companions, both of whom resembled Death, viz., Unmatha and Pramatha, endued with great energy and splendour.

sn: सुभ्राजो भास्वरश्चैव यौ तौ सूर्यानुयायिनौ। तौ सूर्यः कार्तिकेयाय ददौ प्रीतः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Endued with great prowess, Surya, gladly gave Kartikeya two of his followers named Subhraja and Bhasvara.

sn: कैलासशृङ्गसंकाशो श्वेतमाल्यानुलेपनौ। सोमोऽप्यनुचरौ प्रादान्मणि सुमणिमेव च॥
en: Soma also gave him two companions, viz., Mani and Sumani, both of whom looked like summits of tea Kailasa mountain and always used white garlands and white unguents.

sn: ज्वालाजिर्जा तथा ज्योतिरात्मजाय हुताशनः। ददावनुचरौ शूरौ परसैन्यप्रमाथिनौ॥
en: Agni gave him two heroic companions, grinders of hostile armies, who were named Jvalajihva and Jyoti.

sn: परिघं च वटं चैव भीमं च सुमहाबलम्। दहति दहनं चैव प्रचण्डौ वीर्यसम्मतौ॥
en: Ansha gave the intelligent Skanda five companions, Parigha and Vata and Bhima of great strength and Dahati and Dahana both of whom were highly dreadful and energetic.

sn: अंशोऽप्यनुचरान् पञ्च ददौ स्कन्दाय धीमते। उत्क्रोशं पञ्चकं चैव वज्रदण्जधरावुभौ॥ तौ हि शत्रून् महेन्द्रस्य
en: Vasava, that destroyer of hostile heroes, gave Agni's son two companions, viz., Utkrosha and Panchaka who were armed respectively with thunderbolt and club. These had in battle killed many enemies of Indra.

sn: ददावनलपुत्राय वासवः परवीरहा। जनतुः समरे बहून्॥ चक्रं विक्रमकं चैव संक्रमं च महाबलम्।
en: The illustrious Vishnu gave Skanda three companions, viz., Chakra and Vikrama and Shankarma of great power.

sn: स्कन्दाय त्रीननुचरान् ददौ विष्णुर्महायशाः॥ वर्धनं नन्दनं चैव सर्वविद्याविशारदौ।
en: The Ashvins, O foremost of Bharatas gladly, gave Skanda two companions, viz., Vardhana and Nandana, masters of all sciences.

sn: स्कन्दाय ददतुः प्रीतावश्विनौ भिषजां वरौ॥ कुन्दं च कुसुमं चैव कुमुदं च महायशाः। डम्बराडम्बरौ चैव ददौ धाता महात्मने॥
en: The illustrious Dhatri gave that high-souled one five companions, viz., Kunda, Kushuma, Kumuda, Dambara and Adambara.

sn: चक्रानुचक्रौ बलिनौ मेघचक्रौ बलोत्कटौ। ददौ त्वष्टा महामायौ स्कन्दायानुतरावुभौ॥
en: Tashtri give Skanda two companions named Chakra and Anuchakra both of whom were very powerful.

sn: सुव्रतं सत्यसंघं च ददौ मित्रौ महात्मने। कुमाराय महात्मानौ तपोविद्याधरौ प्रभुः॥ सुदर्शनीयौ वरदौ त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतौ।
en: The lord Mitra gave the high-souled Kumara two illustrious companions named Suvrata and Satyasandha both of whom were highly learned and endued with ascetic merit, possessed of handsome features, capable of granting boons and well known over the three worlds.

sn: सुव्रतं च महात्मानं शुभकर्माणमेव च।॥ कार्तिकेयाय सम्प्रादाद् विधाता लोकविश्रुतौ।
en: Vidhatri gave Kartikeya two companions, viz., the great Suprabha and Shubhakarman.

sn: पाणीतकं कालिकं च महामायाविनावुभौ॥ पूषा च पार्षदौ प्रादात् कार्तिकेयाय भारत।
en: Pushan gave him iwo companions, viz., Panitraka and Kalika, both gifted with grcat powers of illusions,

sn: बलं चातिबलं चैव महावक्त्रौ महाबलौ॥ प्रददौ कार्तिकेयाय वायुर्भरतसत्तम।
en: Vayu gave him, O best of the Bharatas, two companions, viz., Vala and Atibala, possessed of great inight and very an large mouths.

sn: यमं चातियमं चैव तिमिवक्त्रौ महाबलौ॥ प्रददौ कार्तिकेयाय वरुणः सत्यसङ्गरः।
en: The truthful Varuna gave him Ghasa and Atighasa of great might and having a mouth like that of the Timi fish.

sn: सुवर्चसं महात्मानं तथैवाप्यतिवर्चसम्॥ हिमवान् प्रददौ राजन् हुताशनसुताय वै।
en: Himavat gave Agni's son two companions, O king, viz., Suvarchas and Ativarchas.

sn: काञ्चनं च महात्मानं मेघमालिनमेव च॥ ददावनुचरो मेरुरग्निपुत्राय भारत।
en: Meru, O Bharata, gave him two companions named Kanchana and Meghamalin.

sn: स्थिरं चातिस्थिरं चैव मेरुरेवापरौ ददौ॥ महात्मा त्वग्निपुत्राय महाबलपराक्रमौ।
en: Manu also gave Agni's son two others gifted with great strength and power viz., Sthira and Asthira.

sn: उच्छृतं चाग्निशृङ्गं च महापाषाणयोधिनौ॥ प्रददावग्निपुत्राय विध्यः पारिषदावुभौ।
en: Vindhya gave Angi's son two companions named Uchchhrita and Agnishringa both of whom fought with stones.

sn: संग्रहं विग्रहं चैव समुद्रोऽपि गदाधरौ॥ प्रददावग्निपुत्राय महापारिषदावुभौ।
en: Ocean gave himn two powerful companions named Sangraha and Vigraha both armed with mace.

sn: उन्मादं शङ्कुकर्णं च पुष्पदन्तं तथैव च॥ प्रददाबग्निपुत्राय पार्वती शुभदर्शना।
en: The beautiful Parvati gavc Agni's son Unmada and Pushpadanta and Shankukarna.

sn: जयं महाजयं चैव नागौ ज्वलनसूनवे॥ प्रददौ पुरुषव्याघ्र वासुकिः पन्नगेश्वरः।
en: Vasuki the king of the serpents, O king, gave the son of Agni two snakes named Jaya and Mahajaya.

sn: एवं साध्याश्च रुद्राश्च वसवः पितरस्तथा।॥ सागरा: सरितश्चैव गिरयश्च महाबलाः। ददुः सेनागणाध्यक्षान् शूलपट्टिशधारिणः॥ दिव्यप्रहरणोपेतान् नानावेपविभूषितान्।
en: Similarly the Saddhyas, the Rudra, the Vasus, the Pitris, the Seas, the Rivers and the Mountains, gave commanders of forces, armed with lances and battle axes and adorned with various kinds or ornaments.

sn: शृणु नामानि चाप्येषां येऽन्ये स्कन्दस्य सैनिकाः।।५५ विविधायुधसम्पन्नाश्चित्राभरणभूषिताः।
en: Listen now to the names of those other warriors armed with various weapons and clad in diverse kind of robes and ornaments, that Skanda got.

sn: शङ्कुकर्णो निकुम्भश्च पद्मः कुमुद एव च॥ अनन्तो द्वादशभुजस्तथा कृष्णोपकृष्णको। घ्राणश्रवाः कपिस्कन्धः काञ्चनाक्षो जलन्धमः॥ अक्षः संतर्जनो राजन् कुनदीकस्तमोऽन्तकृत्। एकाक्षो द्वादशाक्षश्च तथैवैकजटः प्रभुः॥ सहस्रबाहुर्विकटो व्याघ्राक्षः क्षितिकम्पनः। पुण्यमाना सुनामा च सुचक्रः प्रियदर्शनः॥ परिश्रुतः कोकनदः प्रियामाल्यानुलेपनः। अजोदरो गजशिराः स्कन्धाक्षः शतलोचनः॥ ज्वालाजिह्वः करालाक्षः शितिकेशो जटी हरिः। परिश्रुतः कोकनदः कृष्णकेशो जटाधरः॥ चतुर्दष्ट्रोऽष्टजिह्वश्च मेघनादः पृथुश्रवाः। विद्युताक्षो धनुर्वक्त्रो जाठरो मारुताशनः॥ उदारक्षो रथाक्षश्च वज्रनाभो वसुप्रभः। समुद्रवेगो राजेन्द्र शैलकम्पी तथैव च॥ वृषो मेष: प्रवाहश्च तथा नन्दोपनन्दकौ। धूम्रः श्वेतः कलिङ्गश्च सिद्धार्थो वरदस्था॥ प्रियकश्चैव नन्दश्च गोनन्दश्च प्रतापवान्। आनन्दश्च प्रमोदश्च स्वस्तिको ध्रुवकस्तथा॥ क्षेमवाहः सुवाहश्च सिद्धपात्रश्च भारत। गोव्रजः कनकापीडो महापारिषदेश्वरः॥ गायनो हसनश्चैव वाणः खड्गश्च वीर्यवान्। वैताली गतिताली च तथा कथकवातिकौ॥ हंसजः पङ्कदिग्धाङ्गः समुद्रोन्मादनश्च ह। रणोत्कटः प्रहासश्च श्वेतसिद्धश्च नन्दनः॥ कालकण्ठः प्रभासश्च तथा कुम्भाण्डकोदरः। कालकक्ष: सितश्चैव भूतानां मथनस्तथा॥ यज्ञवाहः सुवाहश्च देवयाजी च सोमपः। मजनश्च महातेजाः ऋथनाथौ च भारत॥ तुहरश्च तुहारश्च चित्रदेवश्च वीर्यवान्। मधुरः सुप्रसादश्च किरीटी च महाबलः॥ वत्सलो मधुवर्णश्च कलशोदर एव च। धर्मदो मन्मथकरः सूचीवक्त्रश्च वीर्यवान्॥ श्वेतवक्त्रः सुवक्त्रश्च चारुवक्त्रश्च पाण्डुरः। दण्डबाहुः सुबाहुश्च रजः कोकिलकस्तथा॥ अचल: कनकाक्षश्च बालानामपि यः प्रभुः। संचारकः कोकनदो गृघ्रपत्रश्च जम्बुकः॥ लोहाजवक्त्रो जवनः कुम्भवक्त्रश्च कुम्भकः। स्वर्णग्रीवश्च कृष्णौजाः हंसवक्त्रश्च चन्द्रभः॥ पाणिकूर्चाश्च शम्बूकः पञ्चवक्त्रश्च शिक्षकः। चाषवक्त्रश्च जम्बूकः शाकवक्त्रश्च कुञ्जलः॥
en: They Shankukarna, Nikumbha, Padma, Kumuda, Ananta, Dvadashakshuja, Krishna, Upakrishna, Ghranashravas, Kapiskandha, Kanchanaksha, Jalandhama, Akshasantarjana, Kunadia, Tambobhrakrit, Ekaksha, Dvadashaksha, Ekajata, Shashrabahu, Vikata, Vyaghraksha, Kshitikampana, Punyanaman, Sunaman, Suvaktra, Priyadarshana, Parishruta, Kokonada, Priyamalyanưlepana, Ajodara, Gajashiras, Skandahaksha, Shatalochana, Jvalajihbha, Karala, Shitakesha, Jati, Hari, Krishnakesha, Jatadhara, Chaturdanshtra, Ashtajibha, Meghanada, Prithushravas, Vidyutaksha, Dhanurvaktra, Jathara, Marutashana, Udaraksha, Rathaksha, Vajranabha, were Vasuprabha, Samudravega, Shaliakampin, Vrisha, Meshapravaha, Nanda, Upanandaka, Dhumra, Shveta, Kalinga, Siddhartha, Varada, Priyaka, Nanda, Gonanda, Ananda, Pramoda, Svastika, Dhruvaka, Kshemavaha, Suvaha, Siddhaptra, Goveraja, Kanakapida, Gapana, Hasana, Vana, Khadga, Vaitali, Vaitali, Alitali, Kathaka, Vatika, Hansaja, Pakshadigdhanga, Samudroniadana, Ranotkata, Prahasa, Shvetasiddha, Nandaka, Kalakantha, Prabhasa. Kumbhandaka, Kalakaksha, Shita, Bhutalonmathana, Yajnavaha, Pravaha, Devajaji, Somapa, Majjala, Kratha, Kratha. Tuhara, Gtuhara, Shitradeva, Madhura, Suprasada, Kiritin, Vatsala, Madhuvarna, Kalasodara, Dharmada, Manmathakara, Shuchivaktra, Shvetavaktra, Suvaktra, Charuvaktra, Padura, Dandavahu, Suvahu, Rajas, Kokilaka, Achala, Kanakaksha, Valakarakshaka, Sancharaka, Kokananda, Gridharapatra, Jambhuka, Lohajvaktra, Javana, Kumbhavaktra, Kumbhaka, Mundagriva, Krishnaujas, Hansavaktra, Chandrabha, Panikurchas, Shamyuka, Panchavaktra, Shikshaka, Chasavaktra, Jainbuka, Kharavaktra and Kunchaka.
