sn: योगयुक्ता महात्मानः सततं ब्राह्मणप्रियाः। पैतामहा महात्मानो महापारिषदाश्च ये॥
en: Besides these many other great and powerful companions, practising ascetic austerities and respecting Brahmanas, were given to him by the grandfather,

sn: यौवनस्थाश्च वालाश्च वृद्धाश्च जनमेजय। सहस्रशः पारिषदाः कुमारमवतस्थिरे॥
en: Some of them were young, some were old and some, O Janamejaya, were green youths. Thousands and thousands of such came to Kartikeya.

sn: वक्त्रैर्नानाविधैर्ये कूर्मकुक्कुटवक्त्राश्च शशोलूकमुखास्तथा॥ खरोष्ट्रवदनाश्चान्ये वराहवदनास्तथा। मार्जारशशवक्त्राश्च दीर्घवक्त्राश्च भारत॥ मत्स्यमेषाननाश्चान्ये अजाविमहिषाननाः। ऋक्षशार्दूलवक्त्राश्च द्वीपिसिंहाननास्तथा॥ भीमा गजाननाश्चैव तथा नक्रमुखाश्च ये। तु शृणु ताञ्जनमेजय।
en: They were possessed of various kinds of faces. Listen to me, O Janamejaya, as I describe them. Some had faces like those of tortoises and some like those of cocks. The faces of some were very long, O Bharata. Some again, had faces resembling those of dogs and wolves and hares and owls and asses and camels and hogs. Some had human faces and some had faces like those of sheep and jackals. Some were terrible and had faces like those of Makaras and porpoises. Some had faces like those of cats and some like those of flies; and the faces of some were very long. Some had faces like those of the mongoose, the owl and the crow. Some had faces like those of mice and peacocks and fishes and goats and sheep and buffaloes. Some had faces like those of bears and tigers and leopards and lions. Some had faces like those of elephants and crocodiles.

sn: गरुडाननाः कङ्कमुखा वृककाकमुखास्तथा॥ गोखरोष्ट्रमुखाश्चान्ये वृषदंशमुखास्तथा। महाजठरपादाङ्गास्तारकाक्षाश्च भारत॥ पारावतमुखाश्चान्ये तथा वृषमुखाः परे। कोकिलाभाननाश्चान्ये श्येनतित्तिरिकाननाः॥८५ कृकलासमुखाश्चैव विरजोऽम्बरधारिणः। व्यालवक्त्राः शूलमुखाश्चण्डवक्त्राः शुभाननाः॥ आशीविषाचीरधरा गोनासावदनास्तथा।
en: Some had faces like those of Garuda and the rhinoceros and the wolf. Some had faces like those of cows and mules and camels and cats. Having, large stomachs large legs and limbs, the eyes of some were like stars. The faces of some were like those of pigeons and bulls. Others had faces like those of kolilas and hawks and Tittiris and lizards. Some were clad in white dresses. Some had faces like those of snakes. The faces of some were like those of porcupines. Some had frightful and some very handsome faces; some were clad in snakes. The faces as also the nose of some were like those of cows,

sn: स्थूलोदरा: कृशाङ्गाश्च स्थूलाङ्गाश्च कृशोदराः॥ ह्रस्वग्रीवा महाकर्णा नानाव्यालविभूषणाः। नकुलोलूकवकनाश्च काकवक्त्रास्तथा परे। आखुबभ्रुकवकनाश्च मयूरवदनास्तथा॥ गजेन्द्रचर्मवसनास्तथा कृष्णाजिनाम्बराः॥ स्कन्धेमुखा महाराज तथाप्युदरतोमुखाः। पृष्ठेमुखा हनुमुखास्तथा जङ्घामुखा अपि॥ पार्थाननाश्च बहवो नानादेशमुखास्तथा। तथा कीटपतङ्गानां सदृशास्या गणेश्वराः॥ नानाव्यालमुखाश्चान्ये बहुबाहुशिरोधराः।
en: Some had large and protruding stomachs but other limbs very lean; some had large limbs but lean stomachs. The necks of some were very short and the ears of some were very Jarge. Some had various kinds of snakes for their ornaments. Some were clad in skins of large elephants. And some in black deer-skins. The mouths of some were on their shoulders. Some had mouths on their stomachs, some on their backs, some on their cheeks, some on their calves and some on their flanks and the mouths of many were placed on other parts of their bodies. The faces of some amongst those combatants were like those of insects and worms. The mouths of some amongst them were like those of various beasts of prey. Some had many arms and some many heads.

sn: नानावृक्षभुजाः केचित् कटिशीर्षास्तथा परे॥ भुजङ्गभोगवदना नानागुल्मनिवासिनः। चीरसंवृतगात्राश्च नानाकनकवाससः॥ नानावेषधराश्चैव नानामाल्यानुलेपनाः। नानावस्त्रधराश्चैव चर्मवासस एव च॥ उष्णीषिणो मुकुटिनं सुग्रीवाश्च सुवर्चसः। किरीटिनः पञ्चशिखास्तथा काञ्चनमूर्धजाः॥ त्रिशिखा द्विशिखाश्चैव तथा सप्तशिखाः परे।
en: The arms of some resembled trees and the heads of some were on their lions. The faces of some were tapering like the bodies of snakes. Many amongst them lived in various kinds of plants and herbs. Some were clad in rags, some in various kinds of bones, some were diversely clad and some wore various sorts of garlands and diverse kinds of unguents. Dressed variously, some had skins or their robes. Some had head-gears; the brow of some were furrowed into lines the necks of some bore marks like those on conch-shells; some were highly effulgent. Some had diadems, some had five tufts of hair on their heads and the hair of some were very hard. Some had two tufts, some three and some seven.

sn: शिखण्डीनो मुकुटिनो मुण्डाश्च जटिलास्तथा॥ चित्रमालाधराः केचित् केचिद् रोमाननास्तथा। विग्रहैकरसा नित्यमजेयाः सुरसत्तमैः॥ कृष्णा निर्मांसवक्त्राश्च दीर्घपृष्ठास्तनूदराः। स्थूलपृष्ठा ह्रस्वपृष्ठाः प्रलम्बोदरमेहनाः॥ महाभुजा ह्रस्वभुजा ह्रस्वगात्राश्च वामनाः। कुब्जाश्च ह्रस्वजङ्घाश्च हस्तिकर्णशिरोधराः॥
en: Some had feathers on their heads, some had crowns, some had heads that were perfectly bald and some had matted locks, Some were bedecked with beautiful garlands and the faces of some were covered with hairs. They took great delight only in battle and all of them were invincible by even the foremost ones amongst the gods. Many amongst them were dressed in various kinds of celestial robes. All were fond of battle. Some were of dark colour and the faces of some had no flesh on them. Some had very long backs and some had no stomachs. The backs of some were very large while those of some were very short. Some had long stomachs and some had long limbs. Some had long arms and others had short ones. Some were dwarfs. Some were haunch-backed. Some had short hips. The ears and heads of some were like those of elephants.

sn: हस्तिनासाः कूर्मनासा वृकनासास्तथा परे। दीर्घोच्छ्वासा दीर्घजङ्घा विकराला ह्यधोमुखाः॥ महादंष्ट्रा ह्रस्वदंष्ट्राश्चतुर्दष्ट्रास्तथा परे। वारणेन्द्रनिभाश्चान्ये भीमा राजन् सहस्रशः॥ सुविभक्तशरीराश्च दीप्तिमन्तः स्वलंकृताः। पिङ्गाक्षाः शकुकर्णाश्च रक्तनासाश्च भारत॥
en: Some had noses like those of eleepeHeesnts esnd tortoise, some, like those of wolves. Some had long lips, some had long hips and some were terrific, having their faces downwards. Some had very large teeth, some had very short teeth and some had only four teeth. Thousands among them, O king, were highly terrific in appearance, looking like huge infuriate elephants. Some were of symmetrical limbs, possessed of great lustre and adorned with ornaments. Some had yellow eyes, some had ears like arrows, some had noses like gavials, OBharata.

sn: पृथुदंष्ट्रा महादष्ट्राः स्थूलौष्ठा हरिमूर्धजाः। नानापादौष्ठदंष्ट्राश्च नानाहस्तशिरोधराः॥ नानाचर्मभिराच्छन्ना नानाभाषाश्च भारत। कुशला देशभाषसु जल्पन्तोऽन्योन्यमीश्वराः॥ हृष्टाः परिपतन्ति स्म महापारिषदास्तथा। दीर्घग्रीवा दीर्घनखा दीर्घपादशिरोभुजाः॥ पिङ्गाक्षा नीलकण्ठाश्च लम्बकर्णाश्च भारत। वृकोदरनिभाश्चैव केचिदञ्जनसंनिभाः॥ श्वेताक्षा लोहितग्रीवाः पिङ्गाक्षाश्च तथा परे। कल्माषा बहवो राजश्चित्रवर्णाश्च भारत॥ चामरापीडकनिभाः श्वेतलोहितराजयः। नानावर्णाः सवर्णाश्च मयूरसदृशप्रभाः॥
en: Some had broad teeth, some had broad lips and some had green hair. Possessed of various sorts of feet and lips and teeth, they had various kinds of arms and heads. Clad in various kinds of skins, they spoke different languages, O Bharata. Skilled in all provincial dialecis, those powerful ones talked with one another. Those powerful companions, filled with joy, moved about (around Kartikeya). Some were long-necked, some long-nailed, some long-legged. Some amongst them were large-headed and some large-armed. The eyes of some were yellow, the throats of some were blue and the ears of some were long, O Bharata. The stomachs of some were like masses of antimony. The eyes of soine were while, the necks of some were red and some had eyes of a twany hue. Many were dark in color and many, O king, were of various colors, O Bharata. Many were bedecked with ornainents that looked like yak-tails. Some bore white marks on their bodies and some bore red marks. Some were of various colors and some were gold-hued and some looked splendid like peacocks.

sn: पुनः प्रहरणान्येषां कीर्त्यमानानि मे शृणु। शेषैः कृतः पारिषदैपरायुधानां परिग्रहः॥ पाशोद्यतकराः केचिद् व्यादितास्याः खराननाः। पृष्ठाक्षा नीलकण्ठाश्च तथा परिघबाहवः॥ शतघ्नीचक्रहस्ताश्च तथा मुसलपाणयः।
en: I shall describe to you the weapons that were taken by those that came last to Kartikcya. Listen to me. Some had noses of their uplifted arms. Their faces were like those of tigers and asses. Their eyes were on their backs, their throats were blue and their arms resembled spiked clubs. Some were armed with Shataghnis and discs and some had heavy and short clubs. Some had swords and mallets and some were armed with bludgeons, O Bharata.

sn: असिमुद्गरहस्ताश्च दण्डहस्ताश्च भारत॥ गदाभुशुण्डिहस्ताश्च तथा तोमरपाणयः। आयुधैविविधैोरैर्महात्मानो महाजवाः॥ महाबलाः महावेगा महापारिषदास्तथा।
en: Some, huge-bodied and powerful combatants, were armed with lances and scimitars. Some were armed with maces and Bhushundis and some had spears on their hands. The powerful, noble and energetic and quick-coursing companions had various kinds of terrible weapons in their arins.

sn: अभिषेकं कुमारस्य दृष्ट्वा हृष्टा रणप्रियाः॥ घण्टाजालपिनद्धाङ्गा ननृतुस्ते महौजसः।
en: Beholding the investiture of Kartikeya, those mighty and energetic followers, taking delight in battle and wearing on their persons rows of tinkling bells, danced round him joyfully.

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो महापारिषदा नृप॥ उपतस्थुमहात्मानं कार्तिकेयं यशस्विनम्।
en: These and many other powerful companions, O king, came to the great and illustrious Kartikeya.

sn: दिव्याशाप्यान्तरिक्षाश्च पार्थिवाश्चानिलोपमाः॥ व्यादिष्टा दैवतैः शूराः स्कन्दस्यानुचरा भवन्।
en: Some belonged to the celestial regions, some to the acrial and some to the Earth, All of them were gifted with speed of the wind. Commanded by the gods, those brave and powerful ones became the companions of Kartikeya.

sn: तादृशानां सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च। अभिषिक्तं महात्मानं परिवार्योपतस्थिरे॥
en: Thousands and thousands, millions and millions, of such beings came there at the investiture of the great Kartikeya and stood encircling him."

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शृणु मातृगणान् राजन् कुमारानुचरानिमान्। कीर्त्यमानान् मया वीरं सपत्नगणसूदनान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Listen now to the numbers of the mothers, those destroyers of foes, O hero that became the companions of Kumara, as I name them.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: यशस्विनीनां मातृणां शृणु नामानि भारत। याभिाप्तास्त्रयो लोकाः कल्याणीभिश्च भागशः॥
en: Listen, O, Bharata, to the names of those illustrious mothers. The mobile and immobile universe is permeated by those auspicious ones.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: प्रभावती विशालाक्षी पालिता गोस्तनी तथा। श्रीमती बहुला चैव तथैव बहुपुत्रिका॥ अप्सु जाता च गोपाली बृहदम्बालिका तथा। जयावती मालतिका ध्रुवरत्ना भयंकरी॥ वसुदामा च दामा च विशोका नन्दिनी तथा। एकचूडा महाचूडा चक्रनेमिश्च भारत॥ उत्तेजनी जयत्सेना कमलाक्ष्यश्च शोभना। शत्रुञ्जया तथा चैव क्रोधना शलभी खरी॥ माधवी शुभवक्त्रा च तीर्थनेमिश्च भारत। गीतप्रिया च कल्याणी रुद्ररोमामिताशना॥ मेघस्वना भोगवती सुभ्रुश्च कनकावती। अलाताक्षी वीर्यवती विद्युजिह्वा च भारत॥ पद्मावती सुनक्षत्रा कन्दरा बहुयोजना। संतानिका च कौरव्य कमला च महाबला॥ सुदामा बहुदामा च सुप्रभा च यशस्विनी। नृत्यप्रिया च राजेन्द्र शतोलूखलमेखला॥ शतघण्टा शतानन्दा भगनन्दा च भाविनी। वपुष्मती चन्द्रशीता भद्रकाली च भारत॥ ऋक्षाम्बिका निष्कुटिका वामा चत्वरवासिनी। सुमङ्गला स्वस्तिमती बुद्धिकामा जयाप्रिया॥ धनदा सुप्रसादा च भवदा च जलेश्वरी। एडी भेडी समेडी च वेतालजननी तथा॥ कण्डूतिः कालिका चैव देवमित्रा च भारत। वसुश्री: कोटरा चैव चित्रसेनां तथाचला॥ कुक्कुटिका शङ्खलिका तथा शकुनिका नृप। कुण्डारिका कौकुलिका कुम्भिकाथ शतोदरी॥ उत्क्राथिनी जलेला च महावेगा च कङ्कणा। मनोजवा कण्टकिनी प्रघसा पूतना तथा॥ केशयन्त्री त्रुटिर्वामा क्रोशनाथ तडित्प्रभा। मन्दोदरी च मुण्डी च कोटरा मेघवाहिनी॥ सुभगा लम्बनी लम्बा ताम्रचूडा विकाशिनी। ऊर्ध्ववेणीधरा चैव पिङ्गाक्षी लोहमेखला॥ पृथुवस्त्रा मधुलिका मधुकुम्भा तथैव च। पक्षालिका मत्कुलिका जरायुर्जर्जरानना॥ ख्याता दहदहा चैव तथा धमधमा नृप। खण्डखण्डा च राजेन्द्रः पूषणा मणिकुट्टिका॥ अमोघा चैव कौरव्य तथा लम्बपयोधरा। वेणुवीणाधरा चैव पिङ्गाक्षी लोहमेखला॥ शशोलूकमुखी कृष्णा खरजङ्घा महाजवा। शिशुमारमुखी श्वेता लोहिताक्षी विभीषणा॥ जटालिका कामचरी दीर्घजिह्वा बलोत्कटा। कालेहिका वामनिका मुकुटा चैव भारत॥ लोहिताक्षी महाकाया हरिपिण्डा च भूमिप। एकत्वचा सुकुसुमा कृष्णकर्णी च भारत॥ क्षुरकी चतुष्कर्णी कर्णप्रावरणा तथा। चतुष्पथनिकेता च गोकर्णी महिषानना॥ खरकर्णी महाकर्णी भेरीस्वनमहास्वना। शङ्खकुम्भश्रवाश्चैव भगदा च महाबला॥ गणा च सुगणा चैव तथाऽभीत्यथ कामदा। चतुष्पथरता चैव भूतितीर्थान्यगोचरी॥ पशुदा वित्तदा चैव  सुखदा च महायशाः। पयोदा गोमहिषदा सुविशाला च भारत॥ प्रतिष्ठा सुप्रतिष्ठा च रोचमाना सुरोचना। नौकर्णी मुखकर्णी च विशिरा मन्थिनी तथा॥ एकचन्द्रा मेघकर्णा मेघमाला विरोचना।
en: They are Prabhabavati, Vishalakshi Palit Gonasi, Shrinati, Vahula, Vahuputrika, Apsujata, Gopali, Vrihadarnbalika, Jayavati, Malatika, Dhruvaratna, Bhayankari, Vasudama, Sudama, Vishoka, Nandini, Ekachuda, Mahachuda, Chakranemi, Uttejana, Jayatsena, Kamalakshi, Shobhana, Shatrunjaya, Krodhana, Shalabhi, Khari, Magadhi, Shubhavaktra, Tirthaseni, Gitipriya, Kalyani, Kodruroma, Amitashana, Meghasvana, Bhogavati, Shaubhru, Kanakavati, Alatakshi, Viryavati, Viddyutjihbha, Padmabati, Sunakshatra, Kandara, Bahuyojana, Santanika, Kamala, Mahavala, Sudama, Bahudama, Suprabha, Jashasvini, Nrityapriya, Shatolukhalainckhala, Shataghantata, Shatananda, Bhagananda, Bhavini, Vapsumati, Chandrashita, Bhadrakali, Jhankarika, Nishkuntika, Vaira, Chatwaravasini, Sumangala, Svastimati, Vriddhikama, Jayapriya, Ghanada, Suprsada, Bhavada, Janesvari, Edi, Bhedi, Samedi, Vetalojanani, Kanduti, Kalika, Devamitra, Tambusi, Ketaki, Chitrasena, Achala, Kukkutika, Shankshalika, Shakunika, Kundarika, Kokilika, Kumbhika, Shatodari, Utkrathini, Jalela, Mahavega, Kankana, Manojava, Kantakini, Pradhasa, Putana, Kheshaya, Antarghati, Vama, Kroshana, Tadiprabha, Mandodari, Tuhundi, Kotara, Meghavahini. Lambapayodhara, Venuvinadhara, Pingakshi, Lohamekshala, Shasholukaumkhi, Krishna, Kharajangha, Mahajava, Shishumaramukhi, Shveta, Lohitakshi, Vibhishana, Jatalika, Kamachari, Dirghajivha, Valotkata, Kalehika, Vamanika, Mukuta, Lohitakshi, Mahakaya, Harinpinda, Ekatwacha, Sukusuma, Krishnakarni, Kshurakarni, Shatushkarni, Karnapraverana, Shatushpathaniketa, Gokarni, Mahishanana, Kharakarni, Mahakarni, Bheriswanamahaswana, Shankshakumbhashrava, Bhagada, Gana, Sugana, Bhini, Kamada, Chatupatharata, Bhutirtha, Anyagochara, Pashuda, Vittada, Sukhada, Mahayasha, Payoda, Gomahishada, Suvishala, Pratishtha, Supratishtha, Rochamana, Surochana, Naukarni, Mukhakarni, Vashira, Manthini, Ekavaktra, Megharava, Meghamala and Virochana.

sn: एताश्चान्याश्च बहवो मातरो भतरर्षभ॥ कार्तिकेयानुयायिन्यो नानारूपा सहस्रशः।
en: These and many other mothers, O foremost of Bharata's race, numbering by thousands, of diverse forms, became the followers of Kartikeya.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: दीर्घनख्यो दीर्घदन्त्यो दीर्घतुण्ड्यश्च भारत॥ सबला मधुराश्चैव यौवनस्थाः स्वलंकृता।
en: There nails were long, their teeth were large and their lips also, O Bharata, were projecting. Of straight forms and handsome features, all of them, endowed with youth, were adorned with ornaments.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: माहात्म्येन च संयुक्ताः कामरूपधरास्तथा॥ निर्मांसगात्र्यः श्वेताश्च तथा काञ्चनसंनिभाः।
en: Of ascetic merit, they were capable of assuming forms at will. Not having fleshy limbs, they were of fair complexions and endued with the lustre of gold.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: कृष्णमेघनिभाश्चान्या धूम्राश्च भरतर्षभ॥ अरुणाभा महाभोगा दीर्घकेश्यः सिताम्बराः।
en: Some amongst them were dark and looked like clouds in hue and some were of the color of smoke, O best of Bharata's race. And some were endued with the effulgence of the morning sun and were highly blessed. Possessed of long were tresses, they were clad in what dresses.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ऊर्ध्ववेणीधराश्चैव पिङ्गाक्ष्यो लम्बमेखलाः॥ लम्बोदो लम्बकर्णास्तथा लम्बपयोधराः।
en: The braids of some were tied upwards and the eyes of some were twany and some had long girdles. Some had long stomachs, some had long cars and some had long breasts.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ताम्राक्ष्यस्ताम्रवर्णाश्च हर्यक्ष्यश्च तथा पराः॥ वरदाः कामचारिण्यो नित्यं प्रमुदितास्तथा।
en: Some had coppery eyes and coppery appearance and the eyes of some were green. Capable of granting boons and of walking at will, they were always cheerful.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: याम्या रौद्रास्तथा सौम्याः कौवेर्योऽथ महाबलाः॥३६ वारुण्योऽथ च माहेन्द्रयऽस्तथाऽऽग्नेय्यः परंतप।
en: Possessed of great strength, some amongst them partook of the nature of Yama, soine of Rudra, some of Soma, some of Kuvera, some of Varuna, some of Indra and some of Agni, O destroyer of foes.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: वायव्यश्चाथ कौमार्यो ब्राह्मयश्च भरतर्षभ॥ वैष्णव्यश्च तथा सौर्यो वाराह्यश्च महाबलाः।
en: And some were of the nature of Vayu, some of Kumara, some of Brahman, O foremost of Bharatas, race and some of Vishnu and some of Surya and some of Varaha.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: रूपेणाप्सरसां तुल्या मनोहार्यो मनोरमाः॥ परपुष्टोपमा वाक्ये तथा धनदोपमाः।
en: Of handsome and delightful features, they were beautiful like the Assuras. In voice they resembled the kokila and it walth, Kuvera.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: शक्रवीर्योपमा युद्धे दीप्तया वह्निस नास्तथा॥ शत्रूणां विग्रहे नित्यं भयदास्ता भवन्त्युत।
en: In battle, their energy esembled that of Shakra. In lustre they reseat-led fire. In battle they always struck terror to 'eir enemies.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: कामरूपधराश्चैव जवे वायुसम. या॥ अचिन्तबलवीर्याश्च तथाचिन्त्यपराक्रमाः।
en: Capable of assuming any form at will, in fleetness they resembled the very wind. Of inconceivable power and great energy, their prowess also was inconceivable.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: वृक्षचत्वरवासिन्यश्चतुष्पथनिकेतनाः॥ गुहाश्मशानवासिन्यः शैलप्रस्त्रवणालयाः।
en: They live in trees and open spots and crossings of four roads. They live also in caves and crematoriums, mountains and springs.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: नानाभरणधारिण्यो नानामाल्याम्बरास्तथा॥ नानाविचित्रवेषाच नानाभाषास्तथैव च।
en: Bedecked with various kinds of ornaments, they wear various kinds of dresses and speak different languages.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो गणाः शत्रुभयंकराः॥ अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं त्रिदशेन्द्रस्य सम्मते।
en: These and many other fairs (of the mothers), all capable of terrorizing the enemies, followed, the great Kartikeya, at the command of the king of gods.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ततः शक्त्यस्त्रमददद् भगवान् पाकशासनः॥ गुहाय राजशार्दूल विनाशाय सुरद्विषाम्।
en: The worship chastiser of Paka, ( foremost of kings, conferred on Kartikeya, a dart for the destruction of the enemies of the celestials.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: महास्वनां महाघण्टां द्योतमानां सितप्रभाम्॥ अरुणादित्यवर्णां च पताकां भतरर्षभ।
en: That dart produces a loud sound and is adorned with many large bells. Possessed of great lustre, it seemed to blaze with light. And Indra also gave him a banner effulgent as the morning sun.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ददौ पशुपतिस्तस्मै सर्वभूतमहाचमूम्॥ उग्रां नानाप्रहरणां तपोवीर्यबलान्विताम्।
en: Shiva gave him a large army, highly dreadful and armed with various kinds of weapons and endued with great energy of ascetic penances.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: अजेयां स्वगणैर्युक्तां नाम्ना सेनां धनंजयाम्॥ रुद्रतुल्यबलैर्युक्तां योधानामयुतैस्त्रिभिः।
en: Invincible and possessing all the qualities of a good army that force was known by the name of Dhananjaya. It was protected by thirty thousand warriors each of whom was powerful like Rudra himself. That force knew not how to fly from battle.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: न सा विजानाति रणात् कदाचिद् विनिवर्तितुम्॥ विष्णुर्ददौ वैजयन्ती मालां बलविवर्धिनीम्।
en: Vishnu Gave him a triumphal garland that increases the power of the wearer. Uma gave him two pieces of cloth, effulgent like the sun.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: उमा ददौ विरजसी वाससी रविसप्रभे॥ गङ्गा कमण्डलुं दिव्यममृतोद्भवमुत्तमम्।
en: With great pleasure Ganga gave Kumara a celestial water-pot, begotten of ambrosia and Brihaspati gave him a sacred stick.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ददौ प्रीत्या कुमाराय दण्डं चैव बृहस्पतिः॥ गरुडो दयितं पुत्रं मयूरं चित्रबर्हिणम्।
en: Garuda gave him his favorite son, a peacock of beautiful feathers.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: अरुणस्ताम्रचूडं च प्रददौ चरणायुधम्॥ नागं तु वरुणो राजा बलवीर्यसमन्वितम्।
en: Aruna gave him a cock of sharp talons, The royal Varuna gave him a powerful shake.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: कृष्णाजिनं ततो ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मण्याय ददौ प्रभुः॥ समरेषु जयं चैव प्रददौ लोकभावनः।
en: The lord Brahma gave him, his devout devotee, a black deer-skin. And the Creator of all the worlds also gave him Victory in all battles.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: सैनापत्यमनुप्राप्य स्कन्दो देवगणस्य ह॥ शुशुभे ज्वलितोऽर्चिष्मान् द्वितीय इव पावकः।
en: Having obtained the command of the celestial forces, Skanda shone like a blazing fire of bright flames.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: तत: पारिषदैश्चैव मातृभिश्च समन्वितः॥ ययौ दैत्यविनाशाय ह्लादयन् सुरपुङ्गवान्।
en: Accompanied by those companions and the mothers, he set out for the destruction of the demons, cheering up all the foremost of the celestials.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: सा सेना नैर्ऋती भीमा सघण्टोच्छ्रितकेतना॥ सभेरीशङ्खमुरजा सायुधा सपताकिनी। शारदी द्यौरिवाभाति ज्योतिर्भिरिव शोभिता॥
en: That terrible army of celestials, furnished with standards adorned with bells and equipt with drums and conchs and cymbals and armed with weapons and decked with many banners, shone like the autumnal sky, bespangled with planets and stars.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ततो देवनिकायास्ते नानाभूतगणास्तथा। वादयामासुरव्यग्रा भेरीः शङ्खांश्च पुष्कलान्॥
en: Then that vast host of celestials and various other creatures began cheerfully to beat their drums and blow their conchs numbering in thousands.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: पटहाञ्झर्झरांश्चैव क्रकचान् गोविषाणकान्। आडम्बरान् गोमुखांश्च डिण्डिमांश्च महास्वनान्॥
en: And they also played on their Patahas and Jharjharas and Krikachas and cow-horns and Adambaras and Gomukhas and Dindimas of loud sound.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: तुष्टुवुस्ते कुमारं तु सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः। जगुश्च देवगन्धर्वा ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः॥
en: All the gods, with Vasava at their head, lauded Kumara. The celestials and the Gandharvas sang and the Apsaras danced.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ततः प्रीतो महासेनस्त्रिदशेभ्यो वरं ददौ। रिपून् हन्तास्मि समरे ये वो वधचिकीर्घवः॥
en: Well pleased (with these attentions) Skanda granted a boon to all the celestials, saying-1 shall kill all your enemies, that wish to kill you.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: प्रतिगृह्य वरं देवास्तस्माद् विबुधसत्तमात्। प्रीतात्मानो महात्मानो मेनिरे निहतान् रिपुन॥
en: Having got this boon from that best of celestials, the illustrious gods considered their enemies as already killed.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: सर्वेषां भूतसंघानां हर्षान्नादः समुत्थितः। अपूरयत लोकांस्त्रीन् वरे दत्ते महात्मना॥
en: After Skanda had granted that boon a tremendous sound uprose from all those creatures full of joy, filling the three worlds.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: स निर्ययौ महासेनो महत्या सेनया वृतः। वधाय युधि दैत्यानां रक्षार्थं च दिवौकसाम्॥
en: Accompanied by that vast army, Skanda then started for the destruction of the Daityas and the protection of the celestial beings.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: व्यवसायो जयो धर्मः सिद्धिलक्ष्मीधृतिः स्मृतिः। महासेनस्य सैन्यानामग्रे जग्मुर्नराधिप॥
en: Exertion and Victory and Righteousness and Success and Prosperity and Courage and the Scriptures, (in their embodied forms) followed Kartikeya's army, O king.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: स तया भीमया देवः शूलमुद्गरहस्तया। ज्वलितालातधारिण्या चित्राभरणवर्मया॥ गदामुसलनाराचशक्तितोमरहस्तया। दृप्तसिंहनिनादिन्या विनद्य प्रययौ गुहः॥
en: With that awe-inspiring force, armed with lances and mallets and blazing hands and maces and heavy clubs and arrows and darts and spears and bedecked with beautiful ornaments and armour, the divine Guha set out with leonine roars.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: तं सर्वदैतेया राक्षसाः दानवास्तथा। व्यद्रवन्त दिशः सर्वा भयोद्विग्नाः समन्ततः॥
en: Beholding him, all the Daityas and Rakshasas and Danavas, overcome with fear, dispersed in all directions.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: अभ्यद्रवन्त देवास्तान् विविधायुधपाणयः। दृष्ट्वा च स ततः क्रुद्धः स्कन्दस्तेजोबलान्वितः॥
en: Arined with various weapons, the gods pursued them. Seeing the enemy flying away, the energetic and powerful Skanda, became swollen with anger.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: शक्त्यस्त्रं भगवान् भीमं पुनः पुनरवाकिरत्। आदधचात्मनस्तेजो हविषेद्ध इवानलः॥
en: He repeatedly hurled his terrible weapon, viz., the dart, he had received from Agni. The energy displayed by him then resembled a fire fed with libations of clarified butter.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: अभ्यस्यमाने शक्त्यस्त्रे स्कन्देनामिततेजसा। उल्काज्वाला महाराज पपात वसुधातले॥
en: While the dart was repeatedly hurled by Skanda of unfathomable energy, meteors, O king, dropped upon the Earth.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: संहादयन्तश्च तथा निर्घाताश्चापतन् क्षितौ। यथान्तकालसमये सुघोराः स्युस्तथा नृप॥
en: Thunder-bolts, also, with tremendous noise, dropped upon the Earth. Everything looked terrible, O king, as on the day of the universal dissolution.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: क्षिप्ता ह्येका यदा शक्तिः सुघोराऽनलसूनुना। तत: कट्यो विनिष्पेतुः शक्तीनां भरतर्षभ॥
en: When that terrible dart was once hurled by the son of Agni, millions of darts came out of it, O best of Bharatas.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ततः प्रीतो महासेनो जधान भगवान् प्रभुः। दैत्येन्द्रं तारकं नाम महाबलपराक्रमम्॥
en: The powerful and worshipful Skanda filled with joy, at last killed Taraka, the chief of the Daityas, cndued with great energy and prowess and surrounded in that battle, by a hundred thousand heroic and powerful Daityas.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: वृतं दैत्यायुतैवीरैर्बलिभिर्दशभिर्नृप। महिषं चाप्टभिः पौर्वृतं संख्ये निजनिवान्॥
en: In that battle, he then fell downı Mahisha, who was surrounded by eight Padmas of Daityas. He next killed Tripada who was surrounded by a thousand Ajutas of Dailyas.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: त्रिपादं चायुतशतैर्जघान दशभिर्वृतम्। ह्रदोदरं निखर्वैश्च वृतं दशभिरीश्वरः॥
en: The powerful Skanda then over-powered Hradodara, who encircled by Nikharvas of Daityas, with all his followers armed with various weapons.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: जघानानुचरैः सार्धं विविधायुधपाणिभिः। तथाकुर्वन्त विपुलं नादं वध्यत्सु शत्रुषु॥ कुमारानुचरा राजन् पूरयन्तो दिशो दश।
en: Filling the ten points of the horizon, the followers of Kumara, O king, made a loud noise, while those Daityas were being killed and danced and jumped and laughed in joy.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ननृतुश्च ववल्गुश्च जहसुश्च मुदान्विताः॥ शक्त्यस्त्रस्य तु राजेन्द्र ततोऽर्चिभिः समन्ततः।
en: Thousands of Daityas, O king, were reduced to ashes by the flames that came out Skanda's arrow, while other died at the very roars of Skanda.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: त्रैलोक्यं त्रासितं सर्वं जृम्भमाणाभिरेव च॥ दग्धाः सहस्रशो दैत्या नादैः स्कन्दस्य चापरे।
en: The three worlds were terrified at the yawns of Skanda's soldiers. The enemies were consumed with flames produced by Skanda. Many were killed by his roars only. was ten

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: पताकयाऽवधूताश्च हताः केचित् सुरद्विषः॥ केचिद् घण्टारवत्रस्ता निषेदुर्वसुधातले। केचित् प्रहरणैश्छिन्ना विनिष्येतुर्गतायुषः॥
en: Some amongst the enemies of the celestials, struck with banners, were killed. Some, frightened by the sounds of bells, dropped on the face of the earth. Some wounded with weapons, fell down dead.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: एवं सुरद्विषोऽनेकान् बलवानाततायिनः। जघान समरे वीरः कार्तिकेयो महाबलः॥
en: In this way the heroic and powerful Kartikeya killed numberless enemies of the gods, highly powerful that came to fight with him.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: बाणो नामाथ दैतेयो बलेः पुत्रो महाबलः। क्रौञ्चं पर्वतमाश्रित्य देवसंघानबाधत॥
en: Then Vali's powerful son Vana, getting upon the Kranucha mountain, fought with the celestial army.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: तमभ्ययान्महासेनः सुरशत्रुमुदारधीः। स कार्तिकेयस्य भयात् क्रौञ्चं शरणमीयिवान्॥
en: Highly intelligent, the great generalissimo Skanda rushed against that enemy of the gods. Fearing Kartikeya, he took shelter within the Krauncha mountain.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ततः क्रौझं महामन्युः क्रौञ्चनादनिनादितम्। शक्त्या विभेद भगवान् कार्तिकेयोऽग्निदत्तया॥
en: Worked up with ire, the worshipful Kartikeya then pierced that mountain with that dart given him by Agni. The mountain was called Krauncha (crane). for the sound it always produced resembled the cry of a crane.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: स शालस्कसन्धशबलं त्रस्तवानरवारणम्। प्रोड्डीनोद्धान्तविहगं विनिष्पतितपन्नगम्॥
en: That mountain was variegated with Shala trees. The monkey and elephants that lived on it were frightened. The birds that had lived there rose up and wheeled around in the sky. The serpents began to dart down its sides.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: गोलाङ्गुलर्क्षसंघेश्च द्रवद्भिरनुनादितम्। कुरङ्गमविनिर्घोषनिनादितवनान्तरम्॥
en: It resounded also with the cries of a large number of leopards and bears that ran hither and thither in fright. Other forests on it rang with the cries of hundreds of animals.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: विनिष्पतद्भिः शरभैः सिंहैश्च सहसा द्रुतैः। शोच्यामी दशां प्राप्तो रराजेव स पर्वतः॥
en: Sharabhas and lions suddenly run out. On account of all this, that mountain though it was reduced to a very pitiable condition still shone very beautiful.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: विद्याधराः समुत्पेतुस्तस्य शृङ्गनिवासिनः। किन्नराश्च समुद्विग्नाः शक्तिपातरवोद्धताः॥
en: Vidyadharas living on its summits soared into the air. The Kinnaras also became very anxious, bewildered by the fear caused by the fall of Skanda's arrow.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ततो दैत्या विनिष्पेतुः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। प्रदीप्तात् पर्वतश्रेष्ठाद् विचित्राभरणस्रजः॥ तान् निजघ्नुरतिक्रम्य कुमारानुचरा मृघे। स चैव भगवान् क्रुद्धो दैत्येन्द्रस्य सुतं तदा॥
en: The Daityas then, by hundreds and thousands, came out of that burning mountain, all bedecked with beautiful ornaments and garlands. The followers of Kumara, overpowering them in battle, killed them all, the worshipful Skanda worked up with ire, killed the son of the Daitya chief (Vali) along with his younger brother as Indra has killed Vritra formerly.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: सहानुजं जघानाशु वृत्रं देवपतिर्यथा। बिभेद क्रौञ्चं शक्त्या च पावकिः परवीरहा॥
en: The destroyer of hostile heroes, viz., Agni's son, pierced with his dart the Krauncha mountain, dividing his own-self sometimes into many and sometimes aggregating them all into one.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: बहुधा चैकधा चैव कृत्वाऽऽत्मानं महाबलः। शक्तिः क्षिप्ता रणे तस्य पाणिमेति पुनः पुनः॥
en: Repeatedly discharged by him, the arrow repeatedly came back to him. Indeed such was the power and glory of the worshipful son of Agni.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: एवंप्रभावो भगवांस्ततो भूयश्च पावकिः। शौर्यादिगुणयोगेन तेजसा यशसा श्रिया॥ क्रौञ्चस्तेन विनिर्भियो दैत्याश्च शतशो हताः।
en: With redoubled heroism, energy, fame and success, the god pierced the mountain and killed hundreds of Dailyas.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ततः स भगवान् देवो निहत्य विबुधद्विषः॥ सभाज्यमानो विबुधैः परं हर्षमवाप ह।
en: Having thus slain the enemies of the celestials, the worshipful god was worshipped and honored by the latter and was greatly delighted.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ततो दुन्दुभयो राजन् नेदुः शङ्खाश्च भारत॥
en: After the Krauncha mountain had been pierced and after the son of Chanda had been killed drums were beat, О king and conchs were blown.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: मुमुचुर्देवयोषाश्च पुष्पवर्षमनुत्तमम्। योगिनामीश्वरं देवं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: The celestial ladies showered flowers continually upon that divine lord of Yogins.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: दिव्यगन्धमुपादाय ववौ पुण्यश्च मारुतः। गन्धर्वास्तुष्टुवुश्चैनं यज्वानश्च महर्षयः॥
en: Auspicious winds began to blow, carrying divine perfumes. The Gandharvas and great Rishis always engaged in the performance of sacrifices, sang his praises.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: केचिदेनं व्यवस्यन्ति पितामहसुतं प्रभुम्। सनत्कुमारं सर्वेषां ब्रह्मयोनि तमग्रजम्॥
en: Some spoke of him as the powerful son of the Grandsire, viz., Sanatkumara, the eldest of all the sons of Brahman.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: केचिन्महेश्वरसुतं केचित् पुत्रं विभावसोः। उमायाः कृत्तिकानां च गङ्गायाश्च वदन्त्युत॥
en: Some described him as as the of Maheshvara and some a that of Agni. Some spoke of him as the son of Uma or of Krittakas or of Ganga.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: एकधा च द्विधा चैव चतुर्धा च महाबलम्। योगिनामीश्वरं देवं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Hundreds and thousands of people described that Lord of Yogins of shining form and great might, as the son of one of those or of either of two of those or of any one of four of those. son

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: एतत् ते कथितं राजन् कार्तिकेयाभिषेचनम्। शृणु चैव सरस्वत्यास्तीर्थवर्यस्य पुण्यताम्॥
en: "I have thus told you, O king, everything about the installation of Kartikeya. Listen now to the history of the sanctity of that best of Tirthas, on the Sarasvati.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: बभूव तीर्थप्रवरं हतेषु सुरशत्रुषु। कुमारेण महाराज त्रिविष्टपमिवापरम्॥
en: That best of Tirthas, O king after the enemies of the celestials had been killed, became a second heaven.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: ऐश्वर्याणि च तत्रस्थो ददावीशः पृथक् पृथक्। ददौ नैर्ऋतमुख्येभ्यस्त्रैलोक्यं पावकात्मजः॥
en: The powerful son of Agni gave to each of those leading celestials various kinds of dominion and wealth and at last the sovereignty of the three worlds.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: एवं स भगवांस्तस्मिंतीर्थे दैत्यकुलान्तकः अभिषिक्तो महाराज देवसेनापतिः सुरैः॥
en: Thus, O king was that adorable destroyer of the Daityas installed by the gods as their generalissimo.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: तीर्थं यत्र पूर्वमपां पतिः। अभिषिक्तः सुरगणैर्वरुणो भरतर्षभ॥
en: That other Tirtha, O best of Bharatas, where in days of Yore, Varuna, the Lord of water had been installed by the celestials, is known by the name of Taijasa.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: अस्मिंस्तीर्थवरे स्नात्वा स्कन्दं चाभ्यर्च्य लागली। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ रुक्मं वासांस्याभरणानि च॥
en: Having bathed in that Tirtha and adored Skanda, Rama gave to the Brahmans gold and clothes and ornaments and many other things.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: उषित्वा रजनीं तत्र माधवः परवीरहा। पूज्य तोयं च लागली॥
en: Passing one night there, that killer of hostile heroes, viz., Madhava, lauding that foremost of Tirthas and touching its water, became cheerful and happy.

description: The history of the Tirtha Taijasa and that of the installation of the King of Waters; The history of Agnitirtha
sn: हृष्टः प्रीतमनाश्चैव ह्यभवन्माधवोत्तमः। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। यथाभिषिक्तो भगवान् स्कन्दो देवैः समागतैः॥ तैजसं नाम तत् तीर्थवरं तच्च स्पृष्ट्वा
en: I have now told you everything about which you had enquired, viz., how the divine Skanda was installed by the celestials.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: जनमेजय उवाच अत्यद्भुतमिदं ब्रह्मन् श्रुतवानस्मि तत्त्वतः। अभिषेकं कुमारस्य विस्तरेण यथाविधि॥
en: Janamejaya said "This history, O Rishi, that I have heard from you is highly wonderful, namely this detailed description of the installation according to due rites of Skanda.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: यच्छ्रुत्वा पूतमात्मानं विजानामि तपोधन। प्रहृष्टानि च रोमाणि प्रसन्नं च मनो मम॥
en: O you having asceticism for your wealth, I consider myself cleansed by having listened to this account. My hair stands on end and my mind has become cheerful.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: अभिषेकं कुमारस्य दैत्यानां च वधं तथा। श्रुत्वा मे परमा प्रीतिर्भूयः कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: Having heard the history of the installation of Kumara and the destruction of the Daityas, I have been greatly pleased, I feel a curiosity, however, regarding another subject.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: अपां पतिः कथं ह्यस्मिन्नभिषिक्तः पुरा सुरैः। तन्मे ब्रूहि महाप्राज्ञ कुशलो ह्यसि सत्तम।॥
en: How was the king of the waters installed by the celestials in that Tirtha formerly. O best of men, tell me all that, for you are highly wise and are skilled narrator.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शृणु राजन्निदं चित्रं पूर्वकल्पे यथातथम्। आदौ कृतयुगे राजन् वर्तमाने यथाविधि॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Listen, O king, to this wonderful history as it took place in a previous Kalpa. In days of Yore, in the Satya Yoga, O king, all the celestials, duly approaching Varuna, said to him these words.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: वरुणं देवताः सर्वा यमेत्येदपथाब्रुवन्। यथास्मान् सुरराट्छक्रो भयेभ्यः पाति सर्वदा॥
en: As Indra the king of gods always protects us from every fear, similarly be you the Lord of all the rivers.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: तथा त्वमपि सर्वासां सरितां वै पतिर्भव। वासश्च ते सदा देव सागरे मकरालये॥
en: You always live, ogod, in the Ocean, that home of Makaras. This Ocean the lord of rivers, will then be under you.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: समुद्रोऽयं तव वशे भविष्यति नदीपतिः। सोमेन सार्धं च तव हानिवृद्धी भविष्यतः॥
en: You will then increase the decreases with Soma!-Varuna answered them saying-"Let it be so.'

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: एवमस्त्विति तान् देवान् वरुणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। समागम्य ततः सर्वे वरुणं सागरालयम्॥
en: All the celestials then assembled together, made Varuna living in the Ocean the Lord of all the waters, according to the rites sanctioned by the Scriptures.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: अपां पतिं प्रचक्रुर्हि विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा। अभिषिच्य ततो देवा वरुणं यादसां पतिम्॥
en: Having installed Varuna as the Lord of all aquatic animals and worshipping him duly, the celestials, returned their respective habitations.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: जग्मुः स्वान्येव स्थानानि पूजयित्वा जलेश्वरम्। अभिषिक्तस्ततो देवैर्वरुणोऽपि महायशाः॥
en: Installed by the celestials, the illustrious Varuna began to duly protect seas and lakes and rivers and others reservoirs of water as Indra protects the gods.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: सरितः सागरांश्चैव नदांश्चापि सरांसि च। पालयामास विधिना यथा देवाशतक्रतुः॥ ततस्तत्राप्युपस्पृश्य दत्त्वा च विविधं वसु। अग्नितीर्थं महाप्राज्ञो जगामाथ प्रलम्बहा॥ नष्टो न दृश्यते यत्र शमीगर्भे हुताशनः।
en: Bathing in that Tirtha also and giving away various kinds of presents, Baladeva, the destroyer of Pralamba, endued with great wisdom, then proceeded to Agni Tirtha, where to the cater of the clarified butter, disappearing from the view, became concealed within the entrails of the Shami word.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: लोकालोकविनाशे च प्रादुर्भूते तदानघ॥ उपतस्थुः सुरा यत्र सर्वलोकपितामहम्।
en: When the light of the words thus disappeared, O sinless one, the gods then went to the Grandsire of the universe.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: अग्निः प्रनष्टो भगवान् कारणं च न विद्महे॥ सर्वभूतक्षयो राजन् सम्पादय विभोऽनलम्।
en: And they said-"The worshipful Agni has disappeared. We do not know the reason. Let not creation go to destruction. Create fire, O powerful Lord?"

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: जनमेजय उवाच किमर्थं भगवानग्निः प्रनष्टो लोकभावनः॥ विज्ञातश्च कथं देवैस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व तत्त्वतः।
en: Janamejaya said "For what reason did Agni, the Creator of all the worlds, disappear? How also was he found out by the celestials? Tell me all this fully."

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भृगोः शापाद् भृशं भीतो जातवेदाः प्रतापवान्॥ शमीगर्भमथासाद्य ननाश भगवांस्ततः।
en: Vaishampayana said The highly powerful Agni became very much frightened at the curse of Bhrigu, Concealing himself within the entrails of the Shami wood, that worshipful god disappeared from the view.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: प्रनष्टे तु सदा वह्नौ देवाः सर्वे सवासवाः॥ अन्वैषन्त तदा नष्टं ज्वलनं भृशदुःखिताः।
en: Upon the disappearance of Agni, all the gods led by Vasava, in great affliction, searched for the missing god.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: ततोऽग्नितीर्थमासाद्य शमीगर्भस्थमेव हि॥ ददृशुर्व्वलनं तत्र वसमानं यथाविधि।
en: Finding Agni then, they saw that god lying within the entrails of the Shami wood,

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: देवाः सर्वे नरव्याघ्र बृहस्पतिपुरोगमाः॥ ज्वलनं तं समासाद्य प्रीताऽभूवन् सवासवाः।
en: The celestials, O foremost of kings, with Brihaspati at their head, having found out the god, became very glad with Vasava amongst them.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: पुनर्यथागतं जग्मुः सर्वभक्षश्च सोऽभवत्॥ भृगोः शापान्महाभाग यदुक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना।
en: They then returned to their respective abodes. Agni also, from Bhrigu's curse, became an cater of everything as said by the Brahmavadin.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: तत्राप्याप्लुत्य मतिमान् ब्रह्मयोनिं जगाम ह॥ ससर्ज भगवान् यत्र सर्वलोकपितामहः।
en: The intelligent Balarama, having bathed there, then went to Bramhayoni where the worshipful Grandsire of all the worlds had created the world.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: तत्राप्लुत्य ततो ब्रह्मा सह देवैः प्रभुः पुरा॥ ससर्ज तीर्थानि तथा देवतानां यथाविधि।
en: Formerly the Lord Bramhan having with all the gods bathed in that Tirtha, created all the Tirthas according to due rites, for the celestials.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: तत्र स्नात्वा च दत्वा च वसूनि विविधानि च।॥ कौबेरं प्रययौ तीर्थं तत्र तप्त्वा महत्तपः। धनाधिपत्यं सम्प्राप्तो राजन्नैलबिल प्रभुः॥
en: Bathing there and distributing various kinds of gifts, Baladeva then proceeded to the Tirtha called Kaurava where the powerful Ailavila, having practised severe austerities, became the king of riches.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: तत्रस्थमेव तं राजन् धनानि निधयस्तथा। उपतस्थुर्नरश्रेष्ठ तत् तीर्थं लागली बलः॥ गत्वा दत्वा च विधिवद् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनं ददौ।
en: While he dwelt there (practising austerities), all kinds of wealth and all the precious gems, came to him of their own accord. Baladeva, having gone to that Tirtha and bathed in its waters, distributed immense wealth amongst the Brahmanas with due rites.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: ददृशे तत्र तत् स्थानं कौबेरे काननोत्तमे॥ पुरा यत्र तपस्तप्तं विपुलं सुमहात्मना। यक्षराज्ञा कुबेरेण वरा लब्धाश्च पुष्कलाः॥
en: Rama saw at that spot the excellent woods of Kuvera. In days of yore, the great Kuvera the king of the Yakshas, having practised the severest austerities there, obtained many boons.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: धनादिपत्यं सख्यं च रुद्रेणामिततेजसा। सुरत्वं लोकपालत्वं पुत्रं च नलकूबरम्॥
en: There were the lordship of all riches, the friendship of powerful Rudra, the status of a god, the rcgency over a particular quarter (the north) and a son named Nalakuvara. These the king of the Yakshas speedily obtained there.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: यत्र लेभे महाबाहो धनाधिपतिरञ्जसा! अभिषिक्तश्च तत्रैव समागम्य मरुद्गणैः॥
en: The Maruts, coming there, installed him duly (in his sovereignty). He also obtained for a vehicle a well-equipt cclestial car, fleet as thought, as also as all the prosperity of a god.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: वाहनं चास्य तद् दत्तं हंसयुक्तं मनोजवम्। विमानं पुष्पकं दिव्यं नैऋतैश्चर्यमेव च।॥ तत्राप्लुत्य बलो राजन् दत्त्वा दायांश्च पुष्कलान्।
en: Bathing in that Tirtha and giving away immense wealth, Vala using white unguents thence went speedily to another Tirtha.

description: The story of the Tirtha Vadara-pachana and of Bharadvaja's daughter Sravati
sn: जगाम त्वरितो रामस्तीर्थं श्वेतानुलेपनः॥ निषेवितं सर्वसत्त्वैर्नाम्ना बदरपाचनम्। नानर्तुकवनोपेतं सदापुष्पफलं शुभम्॥
en: Abounding in various creatures, that Tirtha is known by the name of Badarapachana. There the fruits of every reason are always available and flowers and fruits of every kind always abundant."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तीर्थवरं रामो ययौ बदरपाचनम्। तपस्विसिद्धचरितं यत्र कन्या धृतव्रता॥ भरद्वाजस्य दुहिता रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि। श्रुतावती नाम विभो कुमारी ब्रह्मचारिणी॥
en: Vaishampayana said Rama then proceeded to the Tirtha called Vadarapachana where dwell many ascetics and Siddhas, there the daughter of Bharadvaja on was of a peerless Earth for beauty, named Shruvavati, practised severe austerities. She maiden who led the life Brahmacharini.

sn: तपश्चचार साऽत्युग्रं नियमैर्बहुभिर्वृता। भर्ता मे देवराजः स्यादिति निश्चित्य भामिनी॥
en: That beautiful damsel, observing various kinds of vows, practised the austerest of penances, moved by the desire of obtaining the Lord of the celestials for her husband.

sn: समास्तस्या व्यतिक्रान्ता बह्वयः कुरुकुलोद्वह। चरन्त्या नियमांस्तांस्तां स्त्रीभिस्तीवान् सुदुश्चरान्॥४
en: Many years passed away, O chief of Kuru's race, during which that damsel continually practised those various kinds of vows exceedingly difficult for women to practise.

sn: तस्यास्तु तेन वृत्तेन तपसा च विशाम्पते। भक्त्या च भगवान् प्रीतः परया पाकशासनः॥
en: The worshipful chastiser of Paka at last became pleased with her, for her penances and reverence shown to him.

sn: आजगामाश्रमं तस्यास्त्रिदशाधिपतिः प्रभुः। आस्थाय रूपं विप्रर्वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः॥
en: The powerful Lord of the celestials then came to that hermitage, having assumed the form of the great Rishi Vashishtha.

sn: सा तं दृष्ट्वोग्रतपसं वसिष्ठं तपतां वरम्। आचारैर्मुनिभिर्दृष्टैः पूजयामास भारत।॥
en: Seeing that best of ascetics, viz., Vashishtha, of the austerest penances, she adored him, O Bharata, according to the rites observed by ascetics.

sn: उवाच नियमज्ञा च कल्याणी सा प्रियंवदा। भगवन् मुनिशार्दूल किमाज्ञापयसि प्रभो॥
en: Conversant with vows, the auspicious and sweet-speeched damsel addressed him, saying-"O worshipful one, O foremost of ascetics, tell me your commands, O lord.

sn: सर्वमद्य यथाशक्ति तव दास्यामि सुव्रता शक्रभक्त्या च ते पाणिं न दास्यामि कथंचन॥
en: O you of excellent vows, I shall serve you, as much as I can. I will, however, not be able to marry you, for I seek Shakra.

sn: व्रतैश्च नियमैश्चैव तपसा च तपोधन। शक्रस्तोषयितव्यो वै मया त्रिभुवनेश्वरः॥
en: I am propitiating Shakra, the lord of the three worlds, with vows and rigid observances and ascetic penances.'

sn: इत्युक्तो भगवान् देवः स्मयन्निव निरीक्ष्य ताम्। उवाच नियमं ज्ञात्वा सांत्वयन्निव भारत॥ उग्रं तपश्चरसि वै विदिता मेऽसि सुव्रते। यदर्थमयमारम्भस्तव कल्याणि हृद्गतः॥
en: Thus addressed by her, the illustrious god, smiling as he looked at her and knowing her observances, addressed her sweetly, saying "Your practices of penances is known to me, O you of excellent vows, the object cherished in your heart, for which you have been trying your best, O auspicious one, shall, be accomplished. Everything attained by penances. Everything depends on penances.

sn: तच सर्वं यथाभूतं भविष्यति वरानने। तपसा लभ्यते सर्वं यथाभूतं भविष्यति॥ यथा स्थानानि दिव्यानि विबुधानां शुभानने। तपसा तानि प्राप्याणि तपोमूलं महत् सुखम्॥
en: All those sacred regions, O you beautiful damsel, that belong to the gods can be obtained by penances. Penances are the root of great happiness.

sn: इति कृत्वा तपो घोरं देहं संन्यस्य मानवाः। देवत्वं यान्ति कल्याणि शृणुष्वैकं वचो मम॥
en: Those men that renounce their bodies after having practised austere penances, obtain the status of gods, O auspicious one. Remember these words of mine.

sn: पञ्च चैतानि सुभगे बदराणि शुभव्रते। पचेत्युक्त्वा तु भगवाञ्जगाम बलसूदनः॥ आमन्त्रय तां तु कल्याणी ततो जप्यं जजाप सः। अविदूरे ततस्तस्मादाश्रमात् तीर्थमुत्तमम्॥ इन्द्रतीर्थेति विख्यातं त्रिषु लोकेषु मानद।
en: Do you now, O blessed damsel, boil these five jujubes, O you of excellent vows.' Having said these words, the worshipful slayer of Vala went away, taking leave, to recite mentally certain mantras at an excellent Tirtha not far from that herinitage. That Tirtha passed in the three worlds after the name of Indra, O giver of honours.

sn: तस्या जिज्ञासनार्थं स भगवान् पाकशासनः॥ बरदाणामपचनं चकार विबुधाधिपः।
en: Indeed, It was for testing the damsel's devotion that the king of the celestials acted in that way for obstructing the boiling of the jujubes.

sn: ततः प्रतप्ता सा राजन् वाग्यता विगतकमा॥ तत्परा शुचिसंवीता पावके समधिश्रयत्।
en: The damsel, O king, having purified himself, began her task; restraining speech and with fixed attention, she sat to her task, without experiencing the least fatigue.

sn: अपचद् राजशार्दूल बदराणि महाव्रता॥ तस्याः पतन्त्याः सुमहान् कालोऽगात् पुरुषर्षभ।
en: Thus that damsel of high vows, O best of kings, began to boil those jujubes. As she sat cmployed in her work, O foremost of men, day was almost gone, yet those jujubes showed no signs of softening.

sn: न च स्म तान्यपच्यन्त दिनं च क्षयमभ्यगात्॥ हुताशनेन दग्धश्च यस्तस्याः काष्ठसंचयः।
en: The fuel she had there was all consumed. Seeing the fire about to extinguish owing to want of fuel, she began to burn her own limbs.

sn: अकाष्ठमग्निं सा दृष्ट्वा स्वशरीरमथादहत्॥ पादौ प्रक्षिष्य सा पूर्वं पावके चारुदर्शना। दग्धौ दग्धौ पुनः पादावुपावर्तयतानघ॥
en: The beautiful maiden first dropped her feet into the fire. The innocent damsel sat still while her feet began to be consumed.

sn: चरणौ दह्यमानौ च नाचिन्तयदनिन्दिता। कुर्वाणा दुष्करं कर्म महर्षिप्रियकाम्यया॥
en: The beautiful girl did not at all mind her burning feet. Though it was a hard work, she did it from desire of doing good to the Rishi that had been her guest.

sn: न वैमनस्यं तस्यास्तु मुखभेदोऽथवाभवत्। शरीरमग्निनादीप्य जलमध्येऽव वहर्पिता॥
en: Her face did not at all change its colour under its agony, nor did she fell sorrow for it. Having thrust her limbs into the fire, she felt as much joy as if she had put them into cool water.

sn: तथास्या वचनं नित्यमवर्तद्धृदि भारता सर्वथा बदराण्येव पक्तव्यानीति कन्यका॥
en: The words of the Rishi, viz.-Cook these jujubes well-were remembered by her, O Bharata.

sn: सा तन्मनसि कृत्वैव महर्षेर्वचनं शुभा। अपचद् बदराण्येव न चापच्यन्त भारत॥
en: The auspicious damsel, recollecting those words of the great Rishi, began to cook those jujubes although the latter, O king, showed no signs of softening.

sn: तस्यास्तु चरणौ वह्निर्ददाह भगवान् स्वयम्। न च तस्या मनो दुःखं स्वल्पमप्यभवत् तदा॥
en: The worshipful Agni himself consumed her feet. For this, however, the maiden did not feel the slightest pain.

sn: अथ तत् कर्म दृष्ट्वास्याः प्रीतिस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरः। ततः संदर्शयामास कन्यायै रूपमात्मनः॥
en: Beholding this act of her, the lord of the three worlds, became highly pleased. He then appeared in his own proper form before the damsel.

sn: उवाच च सुरश्रेष्ठस्तां कन्यां सुदृढव्रताम्। प्रीतोऽस्मि ते शुभे भक्त्या तपसा नियमेन च॥
en: The king of the celestials then addressed that maiden of very austere vows, saying-"I am pleased with your devotion, penances and VOWS.

sn: तस्माद् योऽभिमतः कामः स ते सम्पत्स्यते शुभे। देहं त्यक्त्वा महाभागे त्रिदिवे मयि वत्स्यसि॥
en: Your wish, therefore, O auspicious one, shall be accomplished. Renouncing body, O blessed one, you shall in heaven live with me,

sn: इदं च ते तीर्थवरं स्थिरं लोके भविष्यति। सर्वपापापहं सुभ्र नाम्ना बदरपाचनम्॥ विख्यातं त्रिषु लोकेषु ब्रह्मर्षिभिरभिप्लुतम्।
en: This hermitage, again, shall become the foremost of Tirthas in the world, capable of cleansing from every sin. O you of fair eyebrows and shall pass by the name of Vadarapachana. It shall be celebrated in the three worlds and shall be lauded by great Rishis.

sn: अस्मिन् खलु महाभागे शुभे तीर्थवरेऽनघे॥ त्यक्त्वा सप्तर्षयो जग्मुहिमवन्तमरुन्धतीम्।
en: In this very Tirtha, O auspicious, sinless and highly blessed one, the seven Rishis had once left Arundhati (the wife of one of them) while they went to Himavat.

sn: ततस्ते वै महाभागा गत्वा तत्र सुसंशिताः॥ वृत्त्यर्थं फलमूलानि समाहर्तुं ययुः किल
en: Those regenerate ones, of very rigid vows, had gone there for collecting fruits and roots for their sustenance.

sn: तेषां वृत्यर्थिना तत्र वसतां हिमवद्वने॥ अनावृष्टिरनुप्राप्ता तदा द्वादशवार्षिकी।
en: While they thus lived in a forest of Himavat for procuring their food, a drought took place extending for twelve years.

sn: ते कृत्वा चाश्रमं तत्र न्यवसन्त तपस्विनः॥ अरुन्धत्यपि कल्याणी तपोनित्याभवत् तदा।
en: Those ascetics, having made a hermitage for themselves, continued to live there. Meanwhile Arundhati devoted herself to ascetic penances.

sn: अरुन्धतीं ततो दृष्ट्वा तीव्र नियममास्थिताम्॥ अथागमत् त्रिनयन: सुप्रीतो वरदस्तदा।
en: Beholding Arundhati practising the austerest of vows, the boon-giving and threecyed deity Mahadeva, highly gratified, came there.

sn: ब्रामं रूपं ततः कृत्वा महादेवो महायशाः॥ तामभ्येत्याब्रवीद् देवो भिक्षामिच्छाम्यहं शुभे।
en: Assuming the form of a Brahmana, the illustrious Mahadeva, came to her and said-I desire almas, O auspicious one!

sn: रत्युवाच ततः सा तं ब्राह्मणं चारुदर्शना॥ क्षीणाऽन्नसंचयो विप्र बदराणीह भक्षय।
en: The beautiful Arundhati said to him-Our food has been exhausted, O Brahmana. Do thou eat jujubes.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महादेवः पचस्वैतानि सुव्रते॥ इत्युक्ता साऽपचत् तानि ब्राह्मणप्रियकाम्यया। ा
en: Mahadeva replied-Cook these jujubes, O you of excellent vows. After these words, she began to cook those jujubes for pleasing that Brahmana,

sn: अधिश्रित्य समिद्धेऽग्नौ बदराणि यशस्विनी॥ दिव्या मनोरमाः पुण्याः कथाः शुश्राव सा तदा। अतीता सा त्वनावृष्टि?रा द्वादशवार्षिकी।॥
en: Placing those jujubes on the fire, the celebrated Arundhati listened to to various excellent and sound and sacred discourses (from the lips of Mahadeva). That twelve years, drought then passed away.

sn: अनश्नन्त्याः पचन्त्याश्च शृण्वन्त्याश्च कथाः शुभाः। दिनोपमः स तस्याथ कालोऽतीतः सुदारुणः॥
en: Without food and employed in cooking and listening to those sacred topics, that terrible period passed away as if like a single day.

sn: ततस्तु मुनयः प्राप्ताः फलान्यादाय पर्वतात्। ततः स भगवान् प्रीतः प्रोवाचारुन्धतीं ततः॥ उपसर्गस्व धर्मज्ञे यथापूर्वमिमानृषीन्। प्रीतोऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञे तपसा नियमेन त॥
en: Having collected fruits from the mountain, the seven Rishis returned there. The wonderful Mahadeva, highly pleased with Arundhati, said to her-Approach, as formerly, these Rishis, O righteous one! I have been satisfied with your penances and vows.

sn: ततः संदर्शयामास स्वरूपं भगवान् हरः। ततोऽब्रवीत् तदा तेभ्यस्तस्याश्च चरितं महत्॥
en: The adorable Hara appeared there in his own form. Pleased, he spoke to them about the noble conduct of Arundhati (in these words).

sn: भवद्भिर्हिमवत्पृष्ठे यत् तपः समुपार्जितम्। अस्याश्च यत् तपो विप्रा न समं तन्मतं मम॥
en: The ascetic merit, you Rishis, that this lady has acquired, is, I think, much greater than what you have earned on the breast of Himavat!

sn: अनया हि तपस्विन्या तपस्तप्तं सुदुश्चरम्। अनश्नन्या पचन्त्या च समा द्वादश पारिताः॥
en: The penances practised by this lady have been highly austere, for she passed twelve years in cooking, herself fasting all the time.

sn: ततः प्रोवाच भगवांस्तामेवारुन्धती पुनः। वरं वृणीष्व कल्याणि यत् तेऽभिलषितं हृदि॥
en: Then, addressing Arundhati, Mahadeva said, Pray for any boon, O auspicious dame, you like.

sn: साऽब्रवीत् पृथुताम्राक्षी देवं सप्तर्षिसंसदि। भगवान् यदि मे प्रीतस्तीर्थं स्यादिदमद्भुतम्॥ सिद्धदेवर्षिदयितं नाम्ना बरदपाचनम्। तथास्मिन् देवदेवेश त्रिरात्रमुषितः शुचिः॥
en: Then that lady of large and red eyes addressed that god in the midst of the seven Rishis, saying-If, O divine one, you are pleased with me, then let this place be an excellent Tirtha. Let it be known by the name of Vadarapachana and let it be the favorite resort of Siddhas and celestial Rishis!

sn: प्राप्नुयादुपवासेन फलं द्वादशवार्षिकम्। एवमस्त्विति तां देवः प्रत्युवाच तपस्विनीम्॥
en: May he, O god of gods, who observes a fast livre and lives for three nights after having purified himself, obtain the fruit of a twelve years fast.

sn: सप्तर्षिभिः स्तुतो देवस्ततो लोकं ययौ तदा। ऋषयो विस्मयं जग्मुस्तां दृष्ट्वा चाप्यरुन्धतीम्॥
en: The gods answered her, saying-Let it be so. Lauded by the seven Rishis, the god then went to heaven.

sn: अश्रान्तां चाविवर्णां च क्षुत्पिपासासमायुताम्। एवं सिद्धिः परा प्राप्ता अरुन्धत्या विशुद्धया॥
en: Indeed, the Rishis has been stricken with wonder on seeing the god and the chaste Arundhati herself as hale and hearty and capable of bearing hunger and thirst.

sn: यथा त्वया महाभागे मदर्थं संशितव्रते। विशेषो हि त्वया भद्रे व्रते ह्यस्मिन् समर्पितः॥
en: Thus the pure-souled Arundhati, formerly, obtained the highest success, like you, O highly blessed lady, for my sake, O damsel of rigid Vows!

sn: तथा चेदं ददाम्यद्य नियमेन सुतोषितः। विशेषं तव कल्याणि प्रयच्छामि वरं वरे॥ अरुन्धत्या वरस्तस्या यो दत्तो वै महात्मना। तस्य चाहं प्रभावेण तव कल्याणि तेजसा॥ प्रवक्ष्यामि परं भूयो वरमत्र यथाविधि। यस्त्वेका रजनी तीर्थे वत्स्यते सुसमाहितः॥ स स्नात्वा प्राप्स्यते लोकान् देहन्यासात् सुदुर्लभान्।
en: O amiable maiden, you have practised severer penances. Gratified with your vows, I shall also grant you this especial boon, O auspicious one, a boon that is superior to what was granted to Arundhati. Through the power of the great god who had granted that boon to Arundhati and through your own energy, O amiable one, I shall duly grant you another boon now, viz., that the person who will live in this Tirtha for only one night and bathe here with his mind concentrated, will, after renouncing his body, obtain many blissful regions that are difficult of acquisition.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा भगवान् देवः सहस्राक्षः प्रतापवान्॥ श्रुतावतीं तत: पुण्यां जगाम त्रिदिवं पुनः।
en: Having said these words of the pure Shrutavati, the thousand-eyed Shakra then went back to heaven.

sn: गते वज्रधरे राजंस्तत्र वर्षं पपात ह।६०॥ पुष्पाणां भरतश्रेष्ठ दिव्यानां पुण्यगन्धिनाम्।
en: After the wielder of the thunderbolt, O king, had gone, a shower of celestial flowers of sweet fragrance fell there, O Bharata's chief.

sn: देवदुन्दुभयश्चापि नेदुस्तत्र महास्वनाः॥ मारुतश्च ववौ पुण्यः पुण्यगन्धो विशाम्पते।
en: Celestial kettle-drums also, of loud sound, were beat there. Auspicious and perfumed breezes also blew there, O king.

sn: उत्सृज्य तु शुभा देहं जगामास्य च भार्यताम्॥ तपसोग्रेण तं लब्ध्वा तेन रेमे सहाच्युत।
en: The auspicious Shrutavati then renouncing her body, became the wife of Indra. Obtaining that dignity through austere penances, she began to pass her time, sporting with him."

sn: जनमेजय उवाच का तस्या भगवन् माता क्व संवृद्धा च शोभना। श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं विप्र परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: Janamejaya said "Who was the mother of Shrutavati and how was that fair damsel brought up. I desire to hear this, O Brahmana, for great is my curiosity."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भरद्वाजस्य विप्रर्षेः स्कन्नं रेतो महात्मनः॥ दृष्ट्वाऽप्सरसभायान्तीं घृताचीं पृथुलोचनाम्।
en: Vaishampayana said "The vital seed of the great Rishi Bharadvaja fell upon beholding the large eyed Apsara Ghritachi as the latter was passing by at one time.

sn: स तु जग्राह तद्रेत: करेण जपतां वरः॥ तदाऽपतत् पर्णपुटे तत्र सा समभवत् सुता।
en: That foremost of ascetics thereupon held it in his hand. It was then kept in a cup made of the Icaves of a tree. In that cup was born the girl Shruvavati.

sn: तस्यास्तु जातकर्मादि कृत्वा सर्वं तपोधनः॥ नाम चास्याः स कृतवान् भरद्वाजो महामुनिः।
en: Having performed the usual birth rites, the great ascetic Bharadvaja, gave her a name.

sn: श्रुतावतीति धर्मात्मा देवर्षिगणसंसदि। स्वे च तामाश्रमे न्यस्य जगाम हिमवद्वनम्॥
en: The name the pious Rishi gave her on the presence of the gods and Rishis was Shruvavati. Leaving the girl in his hermitage, Bharadvaja went to the forest of Himavat.

sn: तत्राप्युपस्पृश्य महानुभावो वसूनि दत्त्वा च महाद्विजेभ्यः। जगाम तीर्थं सुसमाहितात्मा शक्रस्य वृष्णिप्रवरस्तदानीम्॥
en: That best of the Yadus, the heroic Baladeva, of great dignity, having bathed in that Tirtha and distributed much wealth amongst the Brahmanas, then went with a concentrated mind to the Tirtha of Shakra.'

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इन्द्रतीर्थं ततो गत्वा यदूनां प्रवरो बलः। विप्रेभ्यो धनरत्नानि ददौ स्नात्वा यथाविधि॥
en: Vaishampayana said "The powerful chief of the Yadus, having gone to Indra's Tirtha, bathed there according to due rites and distributed wealth and gems amongst the Brahmanas.

sn: तत्र ह्यमरराजोऽसावीजे ऋतुशतेन च। बृहस्पतेश्च देवेशः प्रददौ विपुलं धनम्॥
en: There the chief of the celestials had performed a hundreds horse-sacrifices and given immense wealth to Brihaspati.

sn: निरन्लान् सजारूथ्यान् सर्वान् विविधदक्षिणान्। आजहार क्रतूंस्तत्र यथोक्तान् वेदपारगैः॥
en: Indeed, through the assistance of Brahmanas conversant with the Vedas, Shakra performed all those sacrifice there, according to rites sectioned by the scriptures. Those sacrifices were performed on a liberal scale. Horses of all breeds were brought there. The gifts to Brahmanas were immense.

sn: तान् क्रतून् भरतश्रेष्ठ शतकृत्वो महाद्युतिः। पूरयामास विधिवत् ततः ख्यातः शतक्रतुः॥
en: Having duly completed those hundred sacrifices, O chief of the Bharatas, Shakra passed by the name of Shatakratu.

sn: तस्य नाम्ना च तत् तीर्थं शिवं पुण्यं सनातनम्। इन्द्रतीर्थमिति ख्यातं सर्वपापप्रमोचनम्॥
en: That auspicious and sacred Tirtha, capable of dissipating every sin. came to be called after his name as Indra-Tirtha.

sn: उपस्पृश्य च तत्रापि विधिवन्मुसलायुधः। ब्राह्मणान् पूजयित्वा च सदाच्छादनभोजनैः॥ शुभं तीर्थवरं तस्माद् रामतीर्थं जगाम ह
en: Having duly bathed there, Baladeva worshipped the Brahmanas with excellent food and raiments. He then went to that auspicious and foremost of Tirthas called after the name of Rama.

sn: यत्र रामो महाभागो भार्गवः सुमहातपाः॥ असकृत् पृथिवीं जित्वा हतक्षत्रियपुङ्गवाम्।
en: The highly blessed and ascetic Rama of Bhrigu's race, repeatedly conquered the Earth and killed all the foremost of Kshatriyas.

sn: उपाध्यायं पुरस्कृत्य कश्यपं मुनिसत्तमम्॥ अयज वाजपेयेन सोऽश्वमेधशतेन च। प्रददौ दक्षिणां चैव पृथिवीं वै ससागराम्॥
en: Then Rama performed in that Tirtha a Vajapeya sacrifice and a hundred horse sacrifices through the assistance of his preceptor Kashyapa. There, as sacrificial fee, Rama gave to his preceptor the whole Earth with her oceans.

sn: दत्त्वा च दानं विविधं नानारत्नसमन्वितम्। सगोहस्तिकदासीकं साजावि गतवान् वनम्॥
en: The great Rama, having duly bathed there, made presents to the Brahmanas, O Janamejaya and adored them. Having made diverse presents consisting of various kinds of gems, kine, elephants, female slaves, sheep and goats, he then retired into the woods.

sn: पुण्ये तीर्थवरे तत्र देवब्रह्मर्षिसेविते। मुनींश्चैवाभिवाद्याथ यमुनातीर्थमागमत्॥
en: Having bathed in that sacred and foremost of Tirthas that was the resort of gods and Rishis. Baladeva duly adored the ascetics there, and then went to the Tirtha called Yamuna.

sn: यत्रानयामास तदा राजसूयं महीपते। पुत्रोऽदितेर्महाभागो वरुणो वै सितप्रभः॥
en: The highly effulgent and blessed son of Aditi, Varuna, had in days of yore performed in that Tirtha the Rajasuya sacrifice, O king.

sn: तत्र निर्जित्य संग्रामे मानुषान् देवतास्तथा। वरं क्रतुं समाजहे वरुणः परवीरहा॥ तस्मिन् क्रतुवरे वृत्ते संग्राम: समजायत। देवानां दानवानां च त्रैलोक्यस्य भयावहः॥
en: Having in battle subjugated both men and celestials and Gandharvas and Rakshasas, Varuna, O king, that slayer of hostile heroes, celebrated his grand sacrifice in that Tirtha. Upon the commencement of that foremost of sacrifices a baitle took place between the gods and the Danavas, terrorising the three worlds.

sn: राजसूये ऋतुश्रेष्ठे निवृत्ते जनमेजय। जायते सुमहाघोर: संग्रामः क्षत्रियान् प्रति॥
en: After the termination of that foremost of sacrifices, viz., the Rajasuya (of Varuna), a terrible battle, O Janamejaya, ensued amongst the Kshatriyas.

sn: तत्रापि लागली देव ऋषीनभ्यर्च्य पूजया। इतरेभ्योऽप्यदाद् दानमर्थिभ्यः कामदो विभुः॥
en: Having worshipped the Rishis there, the ever liberal and powerful Baladeva, inade many presents to those that desired them.

sn: वनमाली ततो हृष्टः स्तूयमानो महर्षिभिः। तस्मादादित्यतीर्थं च जगाम कमलेक्षणः॥
en: Filled with joy and lauded by the great Rishis, Baladeva, that hero ever decked with garlands of wild flower and possessed of eyes like lotus leaves, then went to the Tirtha called Aditya.

sn: यत्रेष्टवा भगवाज्योतिर्भास्करो राजसत्तम। ज्योतिषामाधिपत्यं च प्रभावं चाभ्यपद्यत॥
en: There, O best of kings, having performed a sacrifice, the worshipful and effulgent Sun, obtained the sovereignty of all luminous bodies (in the universe) and acquired also his great energy.

sn: तस्या नद्यास्तु तीरे वै सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः। विश्वेदेवाः समरुतो गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्च ह। द्वैपायनः शुकश्चैव कृष्णाश्च मधुसूदनः। यक्षाश्च राक्षसाश्चैव पिशाचाश्च विशाम्पते॥ एते चान्ये च बहवो योगसिद्धाः सहस्रशः। तस्मिंस्तीर्थे सरस्वत्याः शिवे पुण्ये परंतप॥ तत्र हत्वा पुरा विष्णुरसुरौ मधुकैटभौ। आप्लुत्य भरतश्रेष्ठ तीर्थप्रवर उत्तमे॥
en: There, in that Tirtha situate on the bank of that river, all the gods with Vasava at their head, the Vishvedevas, the Maruts, the Gandharvas, the Apsaras, the Island-born Vyasa, Shuka, Krishna the slayer of Madhu, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas and the Pisachas, O king and various others. thousands in numbers, all crowned with ascetic success, always live. Indeed, in that auspicious and sacred Tirtha of the Sarasvati, Vishnu himself having in days of yore slain the Asuras, Madhu and Kaitabha, had, O chief of the Bharatas, performed his ablutions.

sn: द्वैपायनश्च धर्मात्मा तत्रैवाप्लुत्य भारत। सम्प्राप्य परमं योगं सिद्धिं च परमां गतः॥
en: The Island-born Vyasa also, O Bharata, having bathed in that Tirtha, acquired great Yoga powers and Siddhi.

sn: असितो देवलश्चैव तस्मिन्नेव महातपाः। परमं योगमास्थाय ऋषिर्योगमवाप्तवान्॥
en: Having bathed in that very Tirtha with a concentrated mind, the Rishi Asita-Deval also obtained great Yoga powers.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिन्नेव त धर्मात्मा वसति स्म तपोधनः। गार्हस्थ्यं धर्ममास्थाय ह्यसितो देवलः पुरा॥
en: Vaishampayana said "In this Tirtha lived formerly a virtuous Rishi, named Asita-Devala, leading the life of a house-holder.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: धर्मनित्यः शुचिर्दान्तो न्यस्तदण्डो महातपाः। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा समः सर्वेषु जन्तुषु॥
en: He led life of purity and self-restraint. Possessed of great ascetic merit, he was compassionate to all creatures and never injured any one. In word, deed and thought, he behaved equally towards all creatures.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: अक्रोधनो महाराज तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः । प्रियाप्रिये तुल्यवृत्तिर्यमवत् समदर्शन:॥
en: O monarch, censure and praise were equal to him who was without wrath, he was, like Yama himself, thoroughly impartial, treating all alike,

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: काञ्चने लोष्ठभावे च समदर्शी महातपाः। देवानपूजयन्नित्यमतिथींश्च द्विजैः सह॥ ब्रह्मचर्यरतो नित्यं सदा धर्मपरायणः।
en: The great ascetic looked with an equal eye upon gold and pebbles. He daily worshipped the gods and guests and the Brahmanas. Righteous himself he always practised the vow of Brahmacharya

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: ततोऽभ्येत्य महाभाग योगमास्थाय भिक्षुकः॥ जैगीषव्यो मुनिर्धीमास्तस्मिंस्तीर्थं समाहितः। देवलस्याश्रमे राजन्न्यवसत् स महाद्युतिः॥
en: Once upon a time, an intelligent ascetic, O king, of the name of Jaigishavya, devoted to Yoga and rapt in meditation and leading the life of a mendicant, came to Devala's hermitage.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: योगनित्यो महाराज सिद्धि प्राप्तो महातपाः। तं तत्र वसमानं तु जैगीषव्यं महामुनिम्॥
en: That great ascetic ever practising Yoga, O monarch, while residing in Devala's hermitage became crowned with ascctic success.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: देवलो दर्शयन्नेव नैवायुञ्जत धर्मतः। एवं तयोर्महाराज दीर्घकालो व्यतिक्रमत्॥
en: Indeed, while the great Muni Jaigishavya lived there, Devala always paid him attention, never neglecting him at any time.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: जैगीषव्यं मुनिवरं व ददर्शाथ देवलः। आहारकाले मतिमान् परिवाड् जनमेजय॥
en: Thus, O king, they both lived long together. On one occasion, Devala lost sight of Jaigishavya, that foremost of ascetics.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: उपातिष्ठत धर्मज्ञो भैक्षकाले स देवलम्। स दृष्ट्वा भिक्षुरूपेण प्राप्तं तत्र महामुनिम्॥
en: At the hour, however, of dinner, O Janamejaya, the intelligent and righteous ascetic, leading a life of mendicancy, approached Devala for soliciting aims.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: गौरवं परमं चक्रे प्रीति च विपुला तथा। देवलस्तु यथाशक्ति पूजयामास भारत॥
en: Seeing that great ascetic re-appear in the guise of a mendicant, Devala paid him grcat honours and expressed much gratification.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: ऋषिदृष्टेन विधिना समा बह्वीः समाहितः।
en: And Devala adored his guest, О Bharata, according to his might, after the rites laid down by the Rishis and with great attention for many years.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: कदाचित् तस्य नृपते देवलस्य महात्मनः॥ चिन्ता सुमहती जाता मुनिं दृष्ट्वा महाद्युतिम्।
en: One day, however, O king, in the sight of that great Muni, a deep anxiety distributed the mind of the high-souled Devala.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: समास्तु समतिक्रान्ता बह्वयः पूजयतो मम॥ न चायमलसो भिक्षुरभ्यभाषत किंचन।
en: The latter thought within himself-"Many years have I passed in adoring this ascetic. This idle mendicant, however, has not yet spoken to me a single word!"

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: एवं विगणयन्नेव स जगाम महोदधिम्॥ अन्तरिक्षचरः श्रीमान् कलशं गृह्य देवलः।
en: Having thought thus the blessed Devala proceeded to the banks of the ocean through the sky, carrying his earthen pitcher.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: गच्छन्नेव स धर्मात्मा समुद्रं सरितां पतिम्॥ जैगीषव्यं ततोऽपश्यद् गतं प्रागेव भारत।
en: Arrived at the cost of the Ocean, that lord of rivers, O Bharata, the righteous Devala saw Jaigishavya arrived there before him.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तत: सविस्मयश्चिन्तां जगामाथामितप्रभः॥ कथं भिक्षुरयं प्राप्तः समुद्रेः स्नात एव च।
en: Thereat the lord Asita, became filled with wonder and thought within himself-"How could the mendicant come to the ocean and perform his ablutions even before my arrival?'

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: इत्येव चिन्तयामास महर्षिरसितस्तदा॥ स्नात्वा समुद्रे विधिवच्छुचिर्जप्यं जजाप सः।
en: Thus thought the great Rishi Asita. Duly performing his ablutions there and purifying himself thereby, he then began to silently recite the sacred mantras.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: कृतजप्याह्निकः श्रीमानाश्रमं च जगाम ह॥ कलशं जलपूर्णं वै गृहीत्वा जनमेजया
en: Having finished his ablutions and silent prayers, the blessed Devala returned to his hermitage, O Janamejaya, taking with him his carthen pitcher filled with water.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: ततः स प्रविशन्नेव स्वमाश्रमपदं मुनिः॥ आसीनमाश्रमे तत्र जैगीषव्यमपश्यत।
en: As the ascetic, however, entered his own hermitage, he saw Jaigishavya seated there.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: न व्याहरति चैवेनं जैगीषव्यः कथंचन॥ काष्ठभूतोऽऽश्रमपदे वसति स्म महातपाः।
en: The great ascetic Jaigishavya never spoke a word to Devala but lived in the latter's hermitage like a log of wood.
