description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा चाप्लुतं तोये सागरे सागरोपमम्॥ प्रविष्टमाश्रमं चापि पूर्वमेव ददर्श सः।
en: Having seen that ascetic, who was an ocean of austerities, plunged in the waters of the ocean (before his own arrival there), Asita now saw him returned to his hermitage before his Own return.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: असितो देवलो राजंश्चिन्तयामास बुद्धिमान्॥ दृष्ट्वा प्रभावं तपसो जैगीषव्यस्य योगजम्।
en: Witnessing this Yoga power, of Jaigishavya, the intelligent Asita-Devala, O king, began to think over the matter.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: चिन्तयामास राजेन्द्र तदा स मुनिसत्तमः॥ मया दृष्टः समुद्रे च आश्रमे च कथं त्वयम्।
en: Indeed, that best of ascetics, O king, wondered much, saying-"How could this one be seen in the ocean and again in my herinitage?'

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: एवं विगणयन्नेव स मुनिमन्त्रपारगः॥ उत्पपाताश्रमात् तस्मादन्तरिक्षं विशाम्पते। जिज्ञासार्थं तदा भिक्षोर्जेगीषव्यस्य देवलः॥ सोऽन्तरिक्षचरान् सिद्धान् समपश्यत् समाहितान्। जैगीषव्यं च तैः सिद्धैः पूज्यमानमपश्यत॥
en: While immersed in these thoughts, the ascetic Devala, conversant with mantras then soared aloft, O king, from his hermitage into) the sky, for ascertaining who the mendicant Jaigishavya really was. Devala numbers of sky-ranging Siddhas rapt in meditation and Jaigishavya reverentially adored by thcm.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: ततोऽसितः सुसंरब्धो व्यवसायी दृढव्रतः। अपश्यद् वै दिवं यान्तं जैगीषव्यं स देवलः॥
en: Devala become filled with wrath at the sight. He then saw Jaigishavya start for heaven. saw

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तस्मात् तु पितृलोकं तं व्रजन्तं सोऽन्वपश्यत। पितृलोकाच तं यान्तं याम्यं लोकमपश्यत॥
en: He next saw him proceed to the region of the Pitris. Devala saw him then proceed to the region of Yama.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तस्मादपि समुत्पत्य सोमलोकमभिप्लुतम्। व्रजन्तमन्वपश्यत् स जैगीषव्यं महामुनिम्॥ लोकान् समुत्पतन्तं तु शुभानेकान्तयाजिनाम्।
en: From Yama's region the great ascetic Jaigishavya was then seen to soar aloft and proceed to the region of Soma. He was then seen to proceed to the blessed regions of the perforiners of various rigid sacrifices.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: ततोऽग्निहोत्रिणां लोकांस्ततश्चाप्युत्पपात ह॥ दर्श च पौर्णमासं च ये यजन्ति तपोधनाः।
en: Thence he proceeded to the regions of the Agnihotris and thence to the regions of those ascetics that perform the Darsha and the Paurnamasa sacrifices.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तेभ्यः स दृदशे धीमाँल्लोकेभ्यः पशुयाजिनाम्॥ व्रजन्तं लोकममलमपश्यद् देवपूजितम्।
en: The intelligent Devala then behold him go from those regions of persons performing sacrifices by killing animals to that pure region which is adored by the very gods.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: चातुर्मास्यैर्बहुविधैर्यजन्ते ये तपोधनाः॥ तेषां स्थानं ततो यातं तथाग्निष्टोमयाजिनाम्। अग्निष्टुतेन च तथा ये यजन्ति तपोधनाः॥
en: Devala next saw the mendicant proceed to the place of those ascetics that perform the sacrifice called Chaturmasya and various others of the same kind. Thence he went to the region belonging to the performers of the Agnishtoma sacrifice. Devala then saw his guest go to the place of those ascetics that perforin the sacrifice called Agnishutta.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तत् स्थानमनुसम्प्राप्तमन्वपश्यत देवलः। वाजपेयं ऋतुवरं तथा बहुसुवर्णकम्॥
en: Devala next saw him in the regions of those highly wise inen that perform that foremost of sacrifices, viz., Vajapeya and the other sacrifice in which enough of gold is necessary.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: आहरन्ति महाप्राज्ञास्तेषां लोकेष्वपश्यत। यजन्ते राजसूयेन पुण्डरीकेण चैव ये॥
en: Then he saw Jaigishavya in the region of those that perform the Rajasuya and Pundarika.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तेषां लोकेष्वपश्यच जैगीषव्यं स देवलः। अश्वमेधं क्रतुवरं नरमेधं तथैव च॥
en: He then saw him in the regions of those foremost of men that perform the horsesacrifice and the sacrifice in which human beings are killed

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: आहरन्ति नरश्रेष्ठास्तेषां लोकेष्वपश्यत। सर्वमेधं त दुष्प्रापं तथा सौत्रामणिं च ये॥
en: Indeed, Devala saw Jaigishavya in the regions also of those that celebrate the sacrifice called Sautramani and that other in which the flesh of all living animals is required.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तेषां लोकेष्वपश्यच्च जैगीषव्यं स देवलः। द्वादशाहैश्च सत्रैश्च यजन्ते विविधैर्नृप॥
en: Jaigishavya was then seen in the regions of those that perform the sacrifice called Dadashaha and various others of a similar nature.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तेषां लोकेष्वपश्यच जैगीषव्यं स देवलः। मैत्रावरुणयोर्लोकानादित्य । तथैव च॥
en: Asita next saw his guest sojourning in the region of Mitravaruna and then in that of Adityas.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: सलोकतामनुप्राप्तमपश्यत ततोऽसितः। रुद्राणां च वसूनां च स्थानं यच्च बृहस्पतेः॥
en: Asita then saw his guest go through the regions of the Rudras, the Vasus and Brihaspati.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तानि सर्वाण्यतीतानि समपश्यत् ततोऽसितः। आरुह्य च गवां लोके प्रयातो ब्रह्मसत्रिणाम्॥ लोकानपश्यद् गच्छन्तं जैगीषव्यं ततोऽसितः।
en: Thereafter, Asita crossing all that saw him. Having soared next into the blessed region called Golaka, Jaigishavya was next scen to pass into those of the Brahmasatris.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: त्रील्लोकानपरान् विप्रमुत्पतन्तं स्वतेजसा॥ पतिव्रतानां लोकांश्च व्रजन्तं सोऽन्वपश्यत।
en: Having by his energy passed through three other regions, he was seen to go to those regions that are reserved for women that are chaste and devoted to their husbands,

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: ततो मुनिवरं भूयो जैगीषव्यमथासितः॥ नान्वपश्यत लोकस्थमन्तर्हितमरिंदम।
en: At this point, O chastiser of foes, Asita lost sight of Jaigishavya that foremost of ascetics, who, rapt in Yoga, disappeared from his view.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: सोऽचिन्तयन्महाभागो जैगीषव्यस्य देवलः॥ प्रभावं सुव्रतत्वं च सिद्धि योगस्य चातुलाम्।
en: The highly blessed Devala then reflected upon the power of Jaigishavya his vows and success in Yoga.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: असितोऽपृच्छत सदा सिद्धाँल्लोकेषु सत्तमान्॥ प्रयतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा धीरस्तान् ब्रह्मसत्रिणः। जैगीषव्यं न पश्यामि तं शंसध्वं महौजसम्॥ एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे।
en: Then the self-restrained Asita, with joined hands and in a reverential spirit, enquired of those foremost of Siddhas in the regions of the Brahmasatris, saying "I do not see Jaigishavya! Tell me when that energetic ascetic is! I desire to hear this, for great is my curiosity!'

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: सिद्धा उचुः शृणु देवल भूतार्थं शंसता नो दृढव्रत॥ जैगीषव्यं स वै लोकं शाश्वतं ब्रह्मणो गतः।
en: Siddhas said Listen, O Devala of rigid vows, we speak to you the truth! Jaigishavya has gone to the eternal region of Brahman!'

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स श्रुत्वा वचनं तेषां सिद्धानां ब्रह्मसत्रिणाम्॥ असितो देवलस्तूर्णमुत्पपात पपात च। ततः सिद्धास्त ऊचुर्हि देवलं पुनरेव ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Hearing these words of those Siddhas, living in the regions of the Brahmasatris, Asita tried to soar aloft but he soon fell down.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: न देवलगतिस्तत्र तव गन्तुं तपोधन। ब्रह्मणः सदने विप्र जैगीषव्यो यदाप्तवान्।॥ तद् वचनं
en: The Siddhas then, once more addressing Devala said to him-"You O Devala, are not competent to proceed to the region of Brahman, where Jaigishavya has gone!

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तेषां श्रुत्वा सिद्धानां देवलः : पुन:। अनुपूर्वेण लोकांस्तान् सर्वानवततार ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Hcaring those words of the Siddhas, Devala came down, descending from one region to another in due succession,

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: स्वमाश्रमपद् पुण्यमाजगाम पतत्रिवत्। प्रविशन्नेव चापश्यजैगीषव्यं स देवलः॥
en: He repaired to his own sacred hermitage very quickly, like a winged insect. As soon as he entered his abode he beheld Jaigishavya seated there.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: ततो बुद्ध्या व्यगणयद् देवलो धर्मयुक्त्या। दृष्ट्वा प्रभावं तपसो जैगीषव्यस्य योगजम्॥ ततोऽब्रवीन्महात्मानं जैगीषव्यं स देवलः। विनयावनतो राजन्नुपसर्प्य महामुनिम्॥ मोक्षधर्मं समास्थातुमिच्छेयं भगवन्नहम्।
en: Then beholding his Yoga power Devala, reflected upon it with his rightcous understanding and approaching that great ascetic, O king, with humility, addressed the great Jaigishavya, saying-I desire, O adorable one, to acquire Moksha (Emancipation)!'

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वां उपदेशं चकार सः॥ विधिं च योगस्य परं कार्याकार्यस्य शास्त्रतः।
en: Hearing these words of his, Jaigishavya gave him lessons. And he also initiated him in the mysteries of Yoga and taught him the all important and obligatory duties of individuals as also their reverses.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: संन्यासकृतबुद्धि तं ततो दृष्ट्वा महातपाः॥ सर्वाश्चास्य क्रियाश्चक्रे विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा।
en: The holy personage of hard austerities, seeing him thus determined, performed all the sacred rites according to the injunctions laid down for that purpose.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: संन्यासकृतबुद्धिः तं भूतानि पितृभिः सह॥ ततो दृष्ट्वा प्ररुरुदुः कोऽस्मान् संविभजिष्यति।
en: Then all creatures with the Pitris, seeing Devala determined to adopt the religion of emancipation began to weep, saying-"Alas, who will hereafter offer us food!'

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: देवलस्तु वचः श्रुत्वा भूतानां करुणं तथा॥ दिशो दश व्याहरतां मोक्षं त्यक्तुं मनो दधे।
en: Hearing these lamentations of all creatures that resounded through all the points of horizon, Devala thought of renouncing the religion of emancipation.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: ततस्तु फलमूलानि पवित्राणि च भारत॥ पुष्पाण्योषधयश्श्चैव रोरूयन्ति सहस्रशः। पुनर्नो देवलः क्षुद्रो नूनं छेत्स्यति दुर्मतिः॥ अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो यो दत्त्वा नावबुध्यते।
en: Then all sorts of sacred fruits and roots, O Bharata and thousands of flowers and deciduous herbs, began to weep, saying, the wicked and mean Devala will, forsooth, once more pluck and cut us! Alas, having once promised all creatures no injury, he sees not the wrong that he thinks of doing.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: ततो भूयो व्यगणयत् स्वबुद्ध्या मुनिसत्तमः॥ मोक्षे गार्हस्थ्यधर्मे वा किं नु श्रेयस्करं भवेत्।
en: Thereat that foremost of ascetics began to think with the help of his understanding, saying "Which of the two, viz., the religion of Moksha or that of a housc-holder, will be the better for me?

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: इति निश्चित्य मनसा देवलो राजसत्तम॥ त्यक्त्वा गार्हस्थ्यधर्मं स मोक्षधर्ममरोचयत्।
en: Meditating on this, Devala, O king, relinquished the life of a house-holder and adopted that of Moksha.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: एवमादीनि संचिन्त्य देवलो निश्चयात् ततः॥ प्राप्तवान् परमां सिद्धिं परं योगं च भारत।
en: Having thought thus, Devala, on account of this determination, acquired the highest success, O Bharata and the highest Yoga.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: ततो देवा: समागम्य बृहस्पतिपुरोगमा:॥ जैगीषव्ये तपश्चास्य प्रशंसन्ति तपस्विनः।
en: The celestials then, led by Brihaspati, praised Jaigishavya and the penances of that ascetic.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: अथाब्रवीदृषिवरो देवान् वै नारदस्तथा॥ जैगीषव्ये तपो नास्ति विस्मापयति योऽसितम्।
en: Then that best of ascetics, viz., Narada, said to the gods-"There is no penance in Jaigishavya since he filled Asita with wonder!'

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तमेवंवादिनं धीरं प्रत्यूचुस्ते दिवौकसः॥ नैवमित्येव शंसन्तो जैगीषव्यं महामुनिम्।
en: The inhabitants of heaven then said to Narada who has communicated such dangerous words. Do not say about the great ascetic Jaigishavya !

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: नातः परतरं किंचित् तुल्यमस्ति प्रभावतः॥ तेजसस्तपसञ्चास्य योगस्य च महात्मनः.
en: There is no one superior or even equal to this great one in energy, penance and Yoga.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: एवं प्रभावो धर्मात्मा जैगीषव्यस्तथासितः। तयोरिदं स्थानवरं तीर्थं चैव महात्मनोः॥
en: Such was the power of Jaigishavya as also of Asita. Here lived those two and this is the Tirtha of those two great persons.

description: The story of the Rishi Asita Devala
sn: तत्राप्युपस्पृश्य ततो महात्मा दत्त्वा च वित्तं हलभृद् द्विजेभ्यः। अवाप्य धर्मं परमार्थकर्मा जगाम सोमस्य महत् सुतीर्थम्॥
en: Bathing there and distributing wealth to the Brahmanas, the great wielder of the plough, of great deeds, acquired great merit and then went to the Tirtha of Soma."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच यत्रेजिवानुडुपती राजसूयेन भारत। तस्मिरतीर्थे महानासीत् संग्रामस्तारकामयः॥
en: Vaishampayana said "There, in that Tirtha, O Bharata, where the Moon had formerly celebrated the Rajasuya sacrifice, a great battle was fought in which Taraka was the root.

sn: तत्राप्युपस्पृश्य बले दत्त्वा दानानि चात्मवान्। सारस्वतस्य धर्मात्मा मुनेस्तीर्थं जगाम ह॥ तत्र द्वादशवार्षिक्यामनावृशष्टया द्विजोत्तमान्। वेदानध्यापयामास पुरा सारस्वतो मुनिः॥
en: Bathing in that Tirtha and distributing many presents, the virtuous Vala of pure soul went to the Tirtha of the Muni named Sarasvat. There, during a drought extending over twelve years, the sage Sarasvat, formerly taught the Vedas unto many best of Brahmanas.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं द्वादशवार्पिक्यामनावृष्ट्यां द्विजोत्तमान्। ऋषीनध्यापयामास पुरा सारस्वतो मुनिः॥
en: Janamejaya said "Why did the sage Sarasvat, O you of ascetic merit, teach the Vedas to the Rishis during a twelve years' drought?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच आसीत् पूर्वं महाराज मुनिर्धीमान् महातपाः। दधीच इति विख्यातो ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Formerly. O king, there was an intelligent sage of great ascetic viriuc. He was celebrated by the name of Dadhicha. Having governed his senses, he led the life of a Brahmacharin.

sn: तस्यातितपसः शक्रो विभेति सततं विभो। न स लोभयितुं शक्यः फलैर्बहुविधैरपि।॥
en: On account of his excessive ascetic austerities, Shakra was possessed by fear. The sage could not be dissuaded (from the practices of his penances) by the offer of even various kinds of rewards.

sn: प्रलोभनार्थं तस्याथ प्राहिणोत् पाकशासनः। दिव्यामप्सरसं पुण्यां दर्शनीयामलम्बुषाम्॥
en: At last, for tempting the sage, the chastiser of Paka, sent to him the highly beautiful and celestial Apsara by name Alambusha.

sn: तस्य तर्पयतो देवान् सरस्वत्यां महात्मनः। समीपतो महाराज सोऽपातिष्ठत भाविनी॥
en: On the banks of the Sarasvat the great sage was engaged in the worship of the gods and ! there the celestial nymphs, O king, arrived.

sn: तां दिव्यवपुषं दृष्ट्वा तस्य वितात्मनः। रेतः स्कन्नं सरस्वत्यां तत् सा जग्राह निम्नगा॥
en: Seeing that beautiful damsel the seminal fluid of thar ascetic came out. Having fallen into the Sarasvati, the latter preserved it with care.

sn: कुक्षौ चाप्यदधद्धृष्टा तद् रेत: पुरुषर्षभ। सा दधार च तं गर्भ पुत्रहेतोर्महानदी॥
en: Indeed, O foremost of men, the River, sceing that sced, held it in her womb. In time the secd developed into a fetus and the great river kept it so that it might have life and grow into a child.

sn: सुषुवे चापि समये पुत्रं सा सरितां वरा। जगाम पुत्रमादाय तमृर्षि प्रति च प्रभो॥
en: When the time came, the best of rivers delivered that child and then went, O lord, taking it with her, to that Rishi.

sn: ऋषिसंसदि तं दृष्ट्वा सा नदी मुनिसत्तमम्। ततः प्रोवाच राजेन्द्र ददती पुत्रमस्य तम्॥ ब्रह्मर्षे तव पुत्रोऽयं त्वद्भक्त्या धारितो मया। दृष्ट्वा तेऽप्सरसं रेतो यत् स्कन्नं प्रागलम्बुपाम्॥ तत् कुक्षिणा वै ब्रह्मर्षे त्वद्भक्त्या धृतवत्यहम्। न विनाशमिदं गच्छेत् त्वत्तेज इति निश्चयात्॥
en: Seeing that best of Rishis in a conclave, Sarasvati, O king, while handing over the child, said these words:-"O Rishi, this is your son whom I held out of respect for you! That seed of yours, which fell at seeing the nymph Alambusha, had been held by me in my womb, O Rishi, through devotion for you and knowing well that your sced would never be destroyed.

sn: प्रतिगृह्णीष्व पुत्रं स्वं मया दत्तमनिन्दितम्। इत्युक्तः प्रतिजग्राह प्रीति चावाप पुष्कलाम्॥
en: Given by me, accept this faultless child of your own!' Thus addressed by her, the Rishi accepted the child and was highly pleased.

sn: स्वसुतं चाप्यजिघ्रत् तं मूर्ध्नि प्रेम्णा द्विजोत्तमः। परिष्वज्यं चिरं कालं तदा भरतसत्तम॥
en: That best of Brahmanas then out of affection smelt the head of his son and embraced him closely, O best of Bharata, for some time.

sn: सरस्वत्यै वरं प्रादात् प्रीयमाणो महामुनिः। विश्वेदेवा सपितरो गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः॥ तृप्तिं यास्यन्ति सुभगे तयॆमाणास्तवाम्भसा।
en: Pleased with the River, the great ascetic Dadhicha then gave a boon to her, saying "The Vishvedevas, the Rishis and all the clans of the Gandharvas and the Apsaras, will henceforth, blessed one, derive great happiness when oblations of your water are presented to them!'

sn: इत्युक्त्वा स तु तुष्टाव वचोभिर्वै महानदीम्॥ प्रीतः परमहृष्टात्मा यथावच्छृणु पार्थिव।
en: Having said to that great river, the sage, pleased and filled with joy, then praised her in these words. Hear them duly, O king!

sn: प्रन्नुतासि महाभागे सरसो ब्रह्मणः पुरा॥ जानान्ति त्वां सरिच्छेष्ठे मनुयः संशितव्रताः।
en: Thou hast sprung, O highly blessed one, from the lake of Brahman in days of old. All ascetics know thee, O best of rivers.

sn: मम प्रियकरी चापि सततं प्रियदर्शने॥ तस्मात् सारस्वतः पुत्रो महांस्ते वरवर्णिनि।
en: Highly beautiful, you have done me great good! This your great child, O fair river, will be known by the name of Sarasvat.

sn: तवैव नाम्ना प्रथितः पुत्रस्ते लोकभावनः॥ सारस्वत इति ख्यातो भविष्यति महातपाः।
en: This your son, capable of creating new worlds, will pass after thy name! That great ascetic will be known by the name of Sarasvat!

sn: एष द्वादशवार्षिक्यामनावृष्ट्यां द्विजर्षभान्॥ सारस्वतो महाभागे वेदानध्यापयिष्यति।
en: During a drought extending over iwelve years, this Sarasvat, will teach the Vedas to many best of Brahmanas.

sn: पुण्याभ्यश्च सरिद्रयस्त्वं सदा पुण्यतमा शुभे॥ भविष्यसि महाभागे मत्प्रसादात् सरस्वति।
en: O blessed Sarasvati, through my grace, thou shalt always become the best of all sacred rivers!'

sn: एवं सा संस्तुताऽनेन वरं लब्ध्वा महानदी॥ पुत्रमादाय मुदिता जगाम भरतर्षभ।
en: Thus was the great River lauded by the sage after the latter had granted her boons. The River then, overjoyed went away, O best of Bharata's race! taking with her that child.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु विरोधे देवदानवैः॥ शक्रः प्रहरणान्वेषी लोकांस्त्रीन् विचचार ह।
en: Meanwhile, during a war between the gods and demons Shakra travelled through the three worlds in search of weapons.

sn: न चोपलेभे भगवाञ्छकः प्रहरणं तदा॥ यद्वैतेषां भवेद् योग्यं वधाय विबुधद्विषाम्।
en: The king of the celestials, however, failed to find such weapons as were fit to kill the enemies of the celestials.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् सुराज्शको न मे शक्या महासुराः॥ ऋतेऽस्थिभिर्दधीचस्य निहन्तुं त्रिदशद्विषः।
en: Shakra then said to the gods-"The great Asuras are incapable of being defeated by me. Save with the bones of Dadhicha, our foes cannot be killed.

sn: तस्माद् गत्वा ऋषिश्रेष्ठो याच्यतां सुरसत्तमाः॥ दधीचास्थीनि देहीति तैर्वधिष्यामहे रिपून्।
en: O best of celestials, go, therefore, to that best of Rishis and beg of him, saying-"Grant us, O Dadhicha, your bones! With them we will kill our enemies.'

sn: स च तैर्याचितोऽस्थीनि यत्नादृषिवरस्तदा॥ प्राणत्यागं कुरुश्रेष्ठ चकारैवाविचारयन्। स लोकानक्षयान् प्राप्तो देवप्रियकरस्तदा॥
en: Begged by them for his bones, that best of Rishis, O best of Kuru's race, unhesitatingly gave up his life. Having done what was agreeable to the celestials, the sage attained to the eternally blissful region.

sn: तस्यास्थिभिरथो शक्रः समप्रहृष्टमनास्तदा। कारयामास दिव्यानि नानाप्रहरणानि च॥ गदावज्राणि चक्राणि गुरून् दण्डांश्च पुष्कलान्।
en: With his bones, Shakra gladly made many kinds of weapons, such as thunder-bolts, disci, heavy maces and many kinds of clubs and bludgeons.

sn: स हि तीव्रण तपसा सम्भृतः परमर्षिणा॥ प्रजापतिसुतेनाथ भृगुणा लोकभावनः। अतिकायः स तेजस्वी लोकसारो विनिर्मितः.॥ जज्ञे शैलगुरुः प्रांशुर्महिम्ना प्रथितः प्रभुः। नित्यमुद्विजते चास्य तेजसः पाकशासनः॥
en: Equal to the Creator himself Dadhicha, had been begotten by the penances of great Rishi Bhrigu. Strongly built and highly energetic Dadhicha had been made the strongest of men in the world. The powerful and glorious Dadhicha, became tall like the king of mountains. The chastiser of Paka had always been in dread of his power.

sn: तेन वज्रेण भगवान् मन्त्रयुक्तेन भारत। भृशं क्रोधविसृष्टेन ब्रह्मतेजोद्भवेन च॥ दैत्यदानववीराणां जघान नवतीनव।
en: With the thunder-bolt created by Brahma and inspired with mantras, O Bharata, Indra made a loud noise when he hurled it and killed ninety-nine Daityas.

sn: अथ काले व्यतिक्रान्ते महत्यतिभयंकारे॥ अनावृष्टिरनुप्राप्ता राजन् द्वादशवार्षिकी।
en: After a dreadful long time a drought. O king, took place that extended over twelve years.

sn: तस्यां द्वादशवार्षिक्यामनावृष्ट्यां महर्षयः॥ वृत्यर्थं प्राद्रवन् राजन् क्षुधार्ताः सर्वतोदिशम्।
en: During that drought extending over twelve years, the great Rishis fled away, O king, on all sides to maintain themselves.

sn: दिग्भ्यस्तान् प्रद्रुतान् दृष्ट्वा मुनिः सारस्वतस्तदा॥ गमनाय मतिं चक्रे तं प्रोवाच सरस्वती। न गन्तव्यमितः पुत्र तवाहारमहं सदा॥ दास्यामि मत्स्यप्रवरानुष्यतागिह भारत।
en: Seeing them scattered on all sides, the sage Sarasvat also set his heart on flight. The river Sarasvati then said to him. You need not, O son, go away, for I will always supply you with food even here by giving you large fishes! Remain therefore, here!'

sn: इत्युक्तस्तर्पयामास स पितॄन् देवतास्तथा॥ आहारमकरोन्नित्यं प्राणान् वेदांश्च धारयन्।
en: Thus addressed (by the river), the sage continued to live there and offer oblations of food to the Rishis and the celestials, He got also his daily food and thus continued to support both himself and the gods.

sn: अथ तस्यामनावृष्ट्यामतीतायां महर्षयः॥ अन्योन्यं परिपप्रच्छुः पुनः स्वाध्यायकारणात्।
en: After the termination of that twelve years' drought the great Rishis requested one another to deliver discourses on the Vedas.

sn: तेषां क्षुधापरीतानां नष्टा वेदाऽभिधावताम्॥ सर्वेषामेव राजेन्द्र न कश्चित् प्रतिभानवान्।
en: While wandering hungrily the Rishis had forgotten the Vedas. There was indeed, not even one amongst thein that could interpret the Vedas.

sn: अथ कश्चिदृषिस्तेषां सारस्वतमुपेयिवान्॥ कुर्वाणं संशितात्मानं स्वाध्यायमृषिसत्तमम्।
en: It so happened that some one amongst them met Sarasvat, that foremost of Rishis, while the latter was reading the Vedas with concentrated attention.

sn: स गत्वाऽऽचष्ट तेभ्यश्च सारस्वतमतिप्रभम्॥ स्वाध्यायममरप्रख्यं कुर्वाणं विजने वने।
en: Returning to the assemblage of Rishis, he spoke to them of Sarasvat, of his matchless effulgence and celestial appearance and of deep concentration in the Vedas in a secluded forest.

sn: ततः सर्वे समाजग्मुस्तत्र राजन् महर्षयः॥ सारस्वतं मुनिश्रेष्ठमिदमूचुः समागताः। अस्मानध्यापयस्वेति तानुवाच ततो मुनिः॥ शिष्यत्वमुपगच्छध्वं विधिवद्धि ममेत्युत।
en: Then all the great Rishis came there unitedly and spoke to Sarasvat, that best of ascetics, these words.:-"Teach us, O sage!' The ascetic replied, saying-"Become my disciples duly!'

sn: तत्राब्रुवन् मुनिगणा बालस्त्वमसि पुत्रक॥ स तानाह न मे धर्मो नश्येदिति पुनर्मुनीन्।
en: The host of ascetics answered-"O son, you are too young.' Thereupon he answered the ascetics-"I must act in such a way that my religious merit may not suffer decrease'.

sn: यो ह्यधर्मेण वै ब्रूयाद् गृह्णीयाद् योऽप्यधर्मतः॥ हीयेतां तावुभौ क्षिप्तं स्यातां वा वैरिणावुभौ।
en: He that teaches improperly and he that learns improperly, are both doomed to destruction and mutual hatred.

sn: न हायनैर्न पलितैर्न वित्तेन न बन्धुभिः॥ ऋषयश्चक्रिरे धर्म योऽनूचानः स नो महान्।
en: It is not age or decrepitude, of wealth or the number of kinsmen, by which the Rishis claim their mcrit. He only is great who is capable of reading and understanding the Vedas.'

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य मुनयस्ते विधानतः॥ तस्माद् वेदाननुप्राप्य पुनधर्मं प्रचक्रिरे।
en: Hearing these words of his, those ascetics duly became his disciples and learning again from him the Vedas began to practise their rites.

sn: षष्टिर्मुनिसहस्राणि शिष्यत्वं प्रतिपेदिरे॥ सारस्वतस्य विप्रर्वेदस्वाध्यायकारणात्।
en: Sixty thousand ascetics became disciples of the great Rishi Sarasvat for the sake of learning again the Vedas from him.

sn: मुष्टिं मुष्टिं ततः सर्वे दर्भाणां ते छुपाहरन्। तस्यासनार्थं विप्र लस्यापि वशे स्थिताः॥
en: Obeying that beautiful Rishi though a boy, the ascetics each brought a handful of grass and offered it to him for his seat.

sn: तत्रापि दत्त्वा वसु रौहिणेयो महाबल: केशवपूर्वजोऽथ। जगाम तीर्थं मुदितः क्रमेण ख्यातं महद् वृद्धकन्या स्म यत्र॥
en: The powerful son of Rohini and elder brother of Keshava, having distributed wealth in that Tirtha, then joyfully went to another where lived formerly an old virgin lady.”

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं कुमारी भगवंस्तपोयुक्ता ह्यभूत् पुरा। किमर्थं च तपस्तेपे को वास्या नियमोऽभवत्॥ सुदुष्करमिदं ब्रह्मंस्त्वत्त: श्रुतमनुत्तमम्। आख्याहि तत्त्वमखिलं यथा तपसि सा स्थिता॥
en: Janamejaya said "Why, O Rishi did that maiden practise ascetic penances in day of yore. Why did she practise penances and what was her vow?” Matchless and mysterious is the topic that I have already heard from you. Describe particularly how that maid practised penances."

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ऋषिरासीन्महावीर्यः कुणिर्गो महायशाः। स तप्त्वा विपुलं राजस्तपो वै तपतां वरः॥ मनसाऽथ सुतां सुभुं समुत्पादितवान् विभुः। तां च दृष्ट्वा मुनिः प्रीतः कुणिर्गों महायशाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said "There a highly illustrious and energetic Rishi, named Kuni-Garga. Having practised the austerest of penances, O king, that best of ascetics, created a fair browed daughter by his desire. Secing her, the celebrated ascetic Kuni-Garga was filled with joy. He renounced his body, O king and then went to heaven.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: जगाम त्रिदिवं राजन् संत्यज्येह कलेवरम्। सुभूः सा ह्यथ कल्याणी पुण्डीरीकनिभेक्षणा॥
en: Meanwhile, that faultless and amiable and fair-browed maider, having eyes like lotus petals, continued to prectise severe and very rigid penances. She adored the Pitris and the gods with fasts.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: महता तपसोग्रेण कृत्वाऽऽश्रममनिन्दिता। उपवासैः पूजयन्ती पितॄन् देवांश्च सा पुरा॥ तस्यास्तु तपसोग्रेण महान् कालोऽत्यगानृप। सा पित्रा दीयमानापि तत्र नैच्छदनिन्दिता॥ आत्मनः सदृशं सा तु भर्तारं नान्वपश्यत।
en: She passed a long time in the practice of such severe penances. Though her father had been for giving her away in marriage, yet she did not wish for it, for she was no husband worthy of her.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: ततः सा तपसोगेण पीडयित्वाऽऽत्मनस्तनुम्॥ पितृदेवार्चनरता बभूव विजने वने।
en: Emaciating her body with austere penances, she began to worship the Pitris and the gods in that solitary forest.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: साऽऽत्मानं मन्यमानापि कृतकृत्यं श्रमान्विता॥
en: Although engaged in such a hard task, O king and although she cmaciated herself by age and austeritics, yet she thought herself happy.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: वार्धकेन च राजेन्द्र तपसा चैव कर्शिता। सा नाशकद् यदा गन्तुं पदात् पदमपि स्वयम्॥
en: At last when she became very old and physically incapable to move even a single step without being helped by any one, she made up her mind to depart to the other world.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: मोक्तुकामां तु तां दृष्ट्वा शरीरं नारदोऽब्रवीत्॥ असंस्कृतायाः कन्यायाः कुतो लोकास्तवानघे।
en: Seeing her about to relinquish her body, Narada said to her,"O sinless one, you cannot attain any blissful region since you have not cleansed yourself by the rite of marriage.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: एवं तु श्रुतमस्माभिर्देवलोके महाव्रते॥ तपः परमकं प्राप्तं न तु लोकास्त्वया जिताः।
en: O you of great vows, we have heard this in heaven. Great has been your ascetic merit, but you have no claim to blissful regions.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: तन्नारदवचः श्रुत्वा साब्रवीदृषिसंसदि॥ तपसोऽर्धं प्रयच्छामि पाणिग्राहस्य सत्तम।
en: Hearing these words of Narada, the old lady went to an assemblage of Rishis and said, 'I shall give him half my penances who will marry ine.'

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: इत्युक्ते चास्या जग्राह पाणिं गालवसम्भवः॥ ऋषिः प्राक् शृङ्गवान्नाम समयं चेममब्रवीत्। समयेन तवाद्याहं पाणिं स्प्रक्ष्यामि शोभने॥ योकगनं वस्त्वयं त्वया सह मयेति ह। तथेति सा प्रतिश्रुत्य तस्मै पाणिं ददौ तदा॥
en: After she had said these words. the Galava's son, a Rishi known by the name of Shringavai married her on on the following condition. 'On this term, O fair one, I shall marry you, viz., that you, shall live with me for only one night!' Having agreed to that term, she gave him her hand,

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: यथादृष्टेन विधिना हुत्वा चाग्निं विधानतः। चक्रे च पाणिग्रहणं तस्योद्वाहं च गालविः॥
en: According to the rites, and having duly poured libations on the fire, Galava's son accepted her hand and married her.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: सा रात्रावभवद् राजंस्तरुणी वरवर्णिनी। दिव्याभरणवस्त्रा च दिव्यगन्धानुलेपना॥
en: On the night, she became a handsome young lady robed in celestial dress, decked in celestial ornaments, and smeared with celestial ungucnts and perfumes.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: तां दृष्ट्वा गालविः प्रीतो दीपयन्तीमिव श्रिया। उवास च क्षपामेकां प्रभाते साऽब्रवीच तम्॥ यस्त्वया समया विप्र कृतो मे तपतां वर। तेनोषितास्मि भद्रं ते स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु व्रजाम्यहम्॥
en: Sceing her beauty, Galava's son became very happy and passed one night in her company. In the morning she said to him—the agreement, O Brahmana, I had made with you, has been satisfied, O best of ascetic! Blessed be you, I shall now leave you.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: सा निर्गताऽब्रवीद् भूयो योऽस्मिंस्तीर्थे समाहितः। वसन्ते रजनीमेकां तर्पयित्वा दिवौकसः॥ चत्वारिंशतमष्टौ च द्वौ चाष्टौ सम्यगाचरेत्। यो ब्रह्मचर्य वर्षाणि फलं तस्य. लभेत सः॥
en: After getting his permission, she once more said 'He who will with attention, pass one night in this Tirtha after having satisfied the celestials it oblations of water, shall obtain that inerit which one, observing the Vow of Brahmacharya for eight and fifty years, reaps.'

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: एवमुक्त्वा तत: साध्वी देहं त्यक्त्वा दिवं गता। ऋषिरप्यभवद् दीनस्तस्या रूपं विचिन्तयन्॥
en: Having said these words, that chaste lady left for heaven. Her husband the Rishi, became very disspiiited by thinking of her beauty.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: समयेन तपोऽर्धं त कृच्छ्रात् प्रतिगृहीतवान्। साधयित्वा तदाऽऽत्मानं तस्याः स गतिमन्वियात्।। २४ दुःखितो भरतश्रेष्ठ तस्या रूपबलात्कृतः।
en: On account of the agreement he had made, he accepted with difficulty half her penances. Casting off his body he soon followed her, O Bharata's chief, drawn by sorrow and her beauty.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: एतत्ते वृद्धकन्याया व्याख्यातं चरितं महत्॥ तथैव ब्रह्मचर्यं च स्वर्गस्य च गतिः शुभा।
en: This is the illustrious history of the old maid that I have narrated. This is the account of her Brahmacharya and her sacred departure for the celestial regions.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: तत्रस्थश्चापि शुश्राव हतं शल्यं हलायुधः॥ तत्रापि दत्त्वा दानानि द्विजातिभ्यः परंतपः। शुश्राव शल्यं संग्रामे निहतं पाण्डवैस्तदा॥
en: While there, Baladeva heard of the destruction of Shalya. Having made presents to the Brahmanas there, he bewailed, O destroyer of foes, for Shalya, who had been killed by the Pandavas in battle.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: समन्तपञ्चकद्वारात् ततो निष्क्रम्य माधवः। पप्रच्छर्षिगणान् रामः कुरुक्षेत्रस्य यत् फलम्॥
en: Then having come out of Samantapanchaka, Baladeva enquired at of the Rishis about the results of the battle at Kurukshetra.

description: The story of the old maiden
sn: ते पृष्टा यदुसिंहेन कुरुक्षेत्रफलं विभो। समाचख्युर्महात्मानस्तस्मै सर्वं यथातथम्॥
en: Asked by that Yadu's chief about the results of the battle at Kurukshetra, those great ones told him everything as it had taken place.

sn: ऋषय ऊचुः पजापतेरुत्तरवेदिरुच्यते सनातनं राम समन्तपञ्चकम्। समीजिरे यत्र पुरा दिवौकसो वरेण सत्रेण महावरप्रदाः॥
en: The Rishis said "O Rama, this Samantapanchaka the eternal northern alter of Brahman the Lord of all crcatures. There the celestials, the givers of great boons, performed in days of yore a great sacrifice.

sn: पुरा च राजर्षिवरेण धीमता बहूनि वर्षाण्यमितेन तेजसा। प्रकृष्टमेतत् कुरुणा महात्मना ततः कुरुक्षेत्रमितीह पप्रथे॥
en: That foremost of royal sages, viz., the great, intelligent and energetic Kuru, had cultivated this field for many years. Hence it came to be called Kurukshetra (the field of Kuru)!"

sn: राम उवाच किमर्थं कुरूणां कृष्टं क्षेत्रमेतन्महात्मना। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं कथ्यमानं तपोधनाः॥
en: Rama said “Why did the great Kuru cultivated this field? I desire to have this described by you, you Rishis of great penances."

sn: ऋषय ऊचुः पुरा किल कुरुं राम कर्षन्त सततोत्थितम्। अभ्येत्य शक्रस्त्रिदिवात् पर्यपृच्छत कारणम्॥ इन्द्र उवाच किमिदं वर्तते राजन् प्रयत्नेन परेण च। राजर्षे किमभिप्रेत्य येनेयं कृष्यते क्षितिः॥ कुरुरुवाच इह ये पुरुषाः क्षेत्रे मरिष्यन्ति शतक्रतो। ते गमिष्यन्ति सुकृताँल्लोकान् पापविवर्जितान्॥ अवहस्य ततः शक्रो जगाम त्रिदिवं पुनः। राजर्षिरप्यनिर्विण्णः कर्षत्येव वसुधराम्॥
en: The Rishis said “Formerly, O Rama, Kuru was engaged in perseveringly cultivating this field. Coming down from heaven Shakra asked him the reason, saying-Why, O king, art art thou assiduously employed (in this task). What is your object, O royal sage, for the accomplishment of which you are tilling the soil? Thereupon Kuru replied, saying-'O performer of a hundred sacrifices, they that will die upon this plain shall proceed to regions of blessedness after being freed of their sins!'Ridiculing this, the lord Shakra, returned to heaven. Without being at all depressed, the royal sage Kuru, however, continued to till the soil.

sn: आगम्यागम्य चैवेनं भूयोभूयोऽवहस्य च। शतक्रतुरनिर्विण्णं पृष्ट्वा पृष्ट्वा जगाम ह॥
en: Shakra repeatedly come to him and repeatedly receiving the same reply went away and ridiculed him. Kuru, however, was not at all depressed.

sn: यदा तु तपसोगेण चकर्ष वसुधां नृपः। ततः शक्रोऽब्रवीद् देवान् राजर्षेर्यचिकीर्षितम्॥
en: Seeing the king till the soil with great perseverance, Shakra summoned the celestials and informed them of the king's work.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वाब्रुवन् देवाः सहस्राक्षमिदं वचः। अस्माननिष्ट्वा क्रतुभिर्भागो नो न भविष्यति॥
en: Hearing Indra's words, the celestials said to their chief having thousand eyes-'Stop the royal sage, O Shakra, by granting him a boon, if you can.

sn: आगम्य च ततः शक्रस्तदा राजर्षिमब्रवीत्। अलं खेदेन भवतः क्रियतां वचनं मम॥ मानवा ये निराहारा देहं त्यक्ष्यन्तन्द्रिताः। युधि वा निहता: सम्यगपि तिर्यग्गता नृप॥
en: If only by dying there men were to come to heaven, without having performed sacrifices to us, our very existence will be imperilled'Thus spoken to, Shakra returned to that royal saint and. said-Do not work any more! Act according to my words!

sn: ते स्वर्गभाजो राजेन्द्र भविष्यन्ति महामते। तथास्त्विति ततो राजा कुरुः शक्रमुवाच ह।।॥
en: Those men that will die here, having fasted with all their senses awake, and those that will die here in battle, shall, O king, come to heaven.

sn: ततस्तमभ्यनुज्ञाप्य प्रहष्टेनान्तरात्मना। जगाम त्रिदिवं भूयः क्षिप्रं बलनिषूदनः॥
en: They shall enjoy the blessings of heaven, O king!'-Thus addressed, king Kuru answered Shakra, saying-'So be it!'-Taking Kuru's leave, the slayer of Vala, viz., Shakra, then, with a glad heart speedily returned to heaven.

sn: एवमेदतद् यदुश्रेष्ठं कृष्टं राजर्षिणा पुरा। शक्रेण चाभ्यनुज्ञातं ब्रह्माद्यैश्च सुरैस्तथा॥
en: Thus, O foremost of Yadu's race, that royal sage had, formerly cultivated this plain and Shakra had promised great merit to those that would give up their lives here.

sn: नातः परतरं पुण्यं भूमेः स्थानं भविष्यति। इह तप्स्यन्ति ये केचित्तपः परमकं नरा॥
en: It was so sanctioned by all the foremost celestials headed by Brahman, and by the sacred Rishis, that on Earth there should be no more sacred place than this.

sn: देहत्यागेन ते सर्वे यास्यन्ति ब्रह्मणः क्षयम्। ये पुनः पुण्यभाजो वै दानं दास्यन्ति मानवाः॥
en: Those men, that practise austere penances here, would all, after renouncing their bodies, repair to Brahman's region.

sn: तेषां सहस्रगुणितं भविष्यत्यचिरेण वै। ये चेह नित्यं मनुजा निवत्स्यन्ति शुभैषिणः॥
en: Those meritorious men, who would give away their wealth here, would soon have their wealth doubled.

sn: यमस्य विषयं ते तु न द्रक्ष्यन्ति कदाचन। यक्ष्यन्ति ये च क्रतुभिर्महद्भिर्मनुजेश्वराः॥
en: Those who will, in expectation of good, live constantly here, will never have to behold the region of Yama.

sn: तेषां त्रिविष्टपे वासो यावद्भूमिर्धरिष्यति। अपि चात्र स्वयं शक्रो जगौ गाथां सुराधिपः॥
en: Those kings that will perforin great sacrifices here will live as long in heaven as Earth herself will exist.

sn: कुरुक्षेत्रनिबद्धां वै तां शृणुष्व हलायुध। पांसवोऽपि कुरुक्षेत्राद् वायुना समुदीरिताः। अपि दुष्कृतकर्माणं नयन्ति परमां गतिम्॥ सुरर्षभा ब्राह्मणसत्तमाश्च तथा नृगाद्या नरदेवमुख्याः। इष्ट्वा महाहैः क्रतुभिर्नृसिंहा संत्यज्य देहान् सुगति प्रपन्नाः॥
en: The chief of the celestials, viz., Shakra, had himself composed a poem here and sang it. Listen to it, О Baladeva!-The very dust of Kurukshetra, carried by the wind, shall free persons of wicked acts and take them to heaven!. The leading celestials and Brahmanas and kings of the Earth such as Nriga and others, having performed rich sacrifices here, have, after renouncing their bodies, proceeded to heaven.

sn: तरन्तुकारन्तुकयोर्यदन्तरं रामह्रदानां च मचक्रुकस्य च। एतत् कुरुक्षेत्रसमन्तपञ्चक प्रजापतेरुत्तरवेदिरुच्यते॥
en: The space between the Tarantuka and the Arantuka and the lakes of Rama and Chamachakra is known Kurukshetra. Samantapanchaka is called the northern (sacrificial) alter of Brahman, the Lord of all creatures.

sn: शिवं महापुण्यमिदं दिवौकसां सुसम्मतं सर्वगुणैः समन्वितम्। अतश्च सर्वे निहता नृपा रणे यास्यन्ति पुण्यां गतिमक्षयां सदा॥
en: This place endued with all virtues is auspicious and highly sacred, and is much respected by the celestials. It is for this that Kshatriyas slain in battle here obtain sacred and blissful regions.

sn: इत्युवाच स्वयं शक्रः सह ब्रह्मादिभिस्तदा। तचानुमोदितं सर्वं ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वरैः॥
en: This was said by Shakra himself about the glory of Kurukshetra. All that Shakra said was again approved and sanctioned by Brahman, Vishnu, and Maheshivara. as

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कुरुक्षेत्रं ततो दृष्ट्वा दत्त्वा दायांश्च सात्वतः। आश्रमं सुमहद् दिव्यमगमजनमेजय॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Having visited Kurukshetra and distributed wealth there the Satwata hero then proceeded, O Janamejaya, to a large and exceedingly beautiful hermitage.

sn: मधूराम्रवणोपेतं प्लक्षन्यग्रोधसंकुलम्। चिरबिल्वयुतं पुण्यं पनसार्जुनसंकुलम्॥
en: That hermitage was overgrown with Madhuka and mango trees, and abounded with Plakshas and Nyagrodhas. And it contained many Vilvas and many excellent jack and Arjuna trees.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा यादवश्रेष्ठः प्रवरं पुण्यलक्षणम्। पप्रच्छ तानृषीन् सर्वान् कस्याश्रमवरस्त्वयम्॥
en: Seeing that beautiful hermitage Baladeva asked the Rishis as to whom it belonged.

sn: ते तु सर्वे महात्मानमूचु राजन् हालयुधम्। शृणु विस्तरशो राम यस्यायं पूर्वमाश्रमः॥
en: Those great ones, O king, said Baladeva 'Listen in full, O Rama, as to whose asylum this was formerly.

sn: अत्र विष्णुः पुरा देवस्तप्तवांस्तप उत्तमम्। अत्रास्य विधिवद् यज्ञाः सर्वे वृत्ताः सनातनाः॥
en: Here the god Vishnu formerly practised austere penances. Here he celebrated duly all the eternal sacrifices.

sn: अत्रैव ब्राह्मणी सिद्धा कौमारब्रह्मचारिणी। योगयुक्ता दिवं याता तप:सिद्धा तपस्विनी॥
en: Here leading from youth the vow of Brahmacharya, a Brahmani inaiden, was crowned with ascetic success. Ultimately possessed of Yoga powers that ascetic lady went to heaven.

sn: बभूव श्रीमती राजशाण्डिल्यस्य महात्मनः। सुता धृतव्रता साध्वी नियता ब्रह्मचारिणी॥
en: The great Shandilya, O king, had a beautiful daughter who was chaste, observant of severe vows self-restrained, and led a life of cclibacy.

sn: सा तु तत्त्वा तपो घोरं दुश्चरं स्त्रीजनेन ह। गता स्वर्ग महाभागा देवब्राह्मणपूजिता॥ श्रुत्वा ऋषीणां वचनमाश्रमं तं जगाम ह।
en: Having practised the hardest of penances such as the incapable of being performed by women, the blessed lady at last went to heaven, adored by the gods and Brahmanas. Having heard these words of the Rishis, Baladeva entered that hermitage.

sn: ऋषींस्तानभिवाद्याथ पार्श्वे हिमवतोऽच्युतः॥ संध्याकार्याणि सर्वाणि निर्वारुरुहेऽचलम्।
en: Bidding a farewell to the Rishis, Baladeva performed all the rites and ceremonies of the evening on the side of Himavat and then began to ascend mountain.

sn: नातिदूरं ततो गत्वा नगं तालध्वजो बली॥ पुण्यं तीर्थवरं दृष्ट्वा विस्मयं परमं गतः।
en: The powerful Valarama having the emblem of the palmyra of his banner had not ascended far when he saw a sacred and goodly Tirtha and was stricken with wonder at the sight.

sn: प्रभावं च सरस्वत्याः प्लक्षप्रस्रवणं बलः॥ सम्प्राप्तः कारपवनं प्रवरं तीर्थमुत्तमम्। हलायुधस्तत्र चापि दत्त्वा दानं महाबलः॥
en: Sceing the glory of the Sarasvati as also the Tirtha called Plakshaprasaravana, Vala next reached another excellent and foremost of Tirthas called Karavapana.

sn: आप्लुतः सलिले पुण्ये सुशीते विमले शुचौ। संतर्पयामास पितॄन् देवांश्च रणदुर्मदः॥
en: Having made many presents there, the powerful Baladeva bathed in the cool, clear, sacred, and sin-cleansing water (of that Tirtha).

sn: तत्रोष्यैकां त रजनी यतिभिर्ब्राह्मणैः सह। मित्रावरुणयोः पुण्यं जगामाश्रममच्युतः॥
en: Passing one night there with the ascetics and the Brahmanas, Rama then went to the sacred hermitage of the Mitravarunas.

sn: इन्द्रोऽग्निरर्यमा चैव यत्र प्राक् प्रीतिमाप्नुवन्। तं देशं कारपवनाद् यमुनायां जगाम ह॥
en: From Karavapana he proceeded to that spot on the Yamuna where formerly Indra and Agni and Aryaman had obtained great felicity.

sn: स्नात्वा तत्र च धर्मात्मा परां प्रीतिमवाप्य च। ऋषिभिश्चैव सिद्धैश्च सहितो वै महाबलः॥ उपविष्टः कथाः शुभ्राः शुश्राव यदुपुङ्गवः।
en: Bathing there, that Yadu's chief of pious soul, obtained great happiness. The hero then sat himself down with the Rishis and the Siddhas there for listening to their excellent discourses.

sn: तथा तु तिष्ठतां तेषां नारदो भगवानृषिः॥ आजगामाथ तं देशं यत्र रामो व्यवस्थितः।
en: There where Rama sat in the midst of that assemblage the adorable Rishi Narada came while trembling.

sn: जटामण्डलसंवीत: स्वर्णचीरो महातपाः॥ हेमदण्डधरो राजन् कमण्डलुधरस्तथा।
en: Wearing matted locks and shining like gold, he carried in his hands, O king, a golden stalf and a waterpot.

sn: कच्छपी सुखशब्दां तां गृह्य वीणां मनोरमाम्॥ नृत्ये गीते च कुशलो देवब्राह्मणपूजितः।
en: Accomplishment in song and dance and worshipped of gods and Brahmanas, he had with him a beautiful Vina of sweet notes, made of the tortoise-shell.

sn: प्रकर्ता कलहानां च नित्यं च कलहप्रियः॥ तं देशमदमद् यत्र श्रीमान् रामो व्यवस्थितः।
en: A creator of quarrels and ever fond of quarrel, the celestial Rishi came where the handsome Rama was resting.

sn: प्रत्युत्थाय च तं सम्यक् पूजयित्वा यतव्रतम्॥ देवर्षि पर्यपृच्छत् स यथा वृत्तं कुरून् प्रति।
en: Standing up and greatly honoring the celestial Rishis if restricted vows, Rama asked him about all that had befallen the Kurus.

sn: ततोऽस्याकथयद् राजन् नारदः सर्वधर्मवित्॥ सर्वमेतद् यथावृत्तमतीव कुरुसंक्षयम्।
en: Conversant with duty and practices, Narada, then, O king, told him everything, as it had occurred, about the dreadful destruction of the Kurus.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीद् रौहिणेयो नारदं दीनया गिरा॥ किमवस्थं तु तत् क्षत्रं ये तु तत्राभवन् नृपाः।
en: The Rohini's son then, in sorrowful words, enquired of the Rishi, saying-'What is the state of the field? How are those kings now that had assembled there?

sn: श्रुतमेतन्मया पूर्वं सर्वमेव तपोधन॥ विस्तरश्रवणे जातं कौतूहलमतीव मे।
en: I have heard everything before, O Rishi, but iny curiosity is great for hearing it in detail!'

sn: नारद उवाच पूर्वमेव हतो भीष्मो द्रोणः सिन्धुपतिस्तथा॥ हतो वैकर्तनः कर्णः पुत्राश्चास्य महारथाः।
en: Narada said Already Bhishma and Drona and the lord of the Sindhus have died! Vikartana's son Karna also has been killed, with his sons.

sn: भूरिश्रवा रौहिणेय मद्रराजश्च वीर्यवान्॥ एते चान्ये च बहवस्तत्र तत्र महाबलाः। प्रियान् प्राणान् परित्यज्य जयार्थं कौरवस्य वै॥ राजानो राजपुत्राश्च समरेष्वनिवर्तिनः।
en: Bhurishravas too, O son of Rohini, and the brave chief of the Madras have died! These and many other great heroes that had assembled there, rcady to sacrifice this dear life itself for the victory of Duryodhana—have all fallen!

sn: अहतांस्तु महाबाहो शृणु मे तत्र माधव॥ धार्तराष्ट्रबले शेषास्त्रयः समितिमर्दनाः।
en: Listen now to me, O Madhava, about those that yet alive! In the army of Dhritarashtra's son, only three yet survive.

sn: कृपश्च कृतवर्मा च द्रोणपुत्रश्च वीर्यवान्॥ तेऽपि वै विद्रुता राम दिशो दश भयात् तदा।
en: They are Kripa and Kritavarman and the powerful son of Drona! These also, O Rama, have from fear fled away on all sides!

sn: दुर्योधने हते शल्ये विदुतेषु कृपादिषु॥ ह्रदं द्वैपायनं नाम विवेश भृशदुःखितः।
en: After Shalya's fall and the fight of Kripa and the others, Duryodhana, in great sorrow had entered the Dvaipayana lake.

sn: शयानं धार्तराष्ट्रं तु सलिले स्तम्भिते तदा॥ पाण्डवाः सह कृष्णेन वाग्भिरुयाभिरादयन्।
en: While resting at the bottom of the lake after solidifying its waters, Duryodhana approached by the Pandavas with Krishna and cut to the quick by their cruel words. are was

sn: उत्थितः स ह्रदाद् स तुद्यमानो बलवान् वाग्मी रामसमन्ततः॥ वीरः प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्।
en: Cut with wordy darts, O Rama, from every side, the powerful and heroic Duryodhana has risen from the lake, armed with his heavy inace.

sn: स चाप्युपगतो योद्धं भीमेन सह साम्प्रतम्॥ भविष्यति तयोरा युद्धं राम सुदारुणम्।
en: He has come forward for fighting Bhima for the present. The terrible encounter, O Rama, will take place today!

sn: यदि कौतूहलं तेऽस्ति व्रज माधव मा चिरम्। पश्य युद्धं महाघोरं शिष्ययोर्यदि मन्यसे॥
en: If you feel any curiosity, then hasten O Madhava, without delay! Go, if you like and witness that terrible battle between your two disciples!'

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा तानभ्यर्च्य द्विजर्षभान्। सर्वान् विसर्जयामास ये तेनाभ्यागताः सह॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Hearing Narada, Rama bade a respectful farewell to those great Brahmanas and sent away all those that had accompanied him (in। his pilgrimage).

sn: गम्यतां द्वारकां चेति सोऽन्वशादनुयायिनः। सोऽवतीर्याचलश्रेष्ठात् प्लक्षप्रस्रवणाच्छुभात्॥
en: He ordered his attendant saying-Return you to Dwaraka!' He then got down from that prince of mountains and that fair hermitage called Plakshaprashravana.

sn: ततः प्रीतमना रामः श्रुत्वा तीर्थफलं महत्। विप्राणां संनिधौ श्लोकमगायदिममच्युतः॥
en: Having listened to the discourse of the sages about the great merits of Tirthas, Rama sang this verse in the midst of the Brahmanas.

sn: सरस्वतीवाससमा कुतो रतिः सरस्वतीवाससमाः कुतो गुणाः। सरस्वतीं प्राप्य दिवं गता जनाः सदा स्मरिष्यन्ति नदीं सरस्वतीम्॥
en: Where is such happiness as is obtainable by living by the Sarasvati? Where else such merits as those obtainable by living by the Sarasvati? Men have departed for heaven, having approached the Sarasvati! All should ever remember the Sarasvati! Sarasvati is the most sacred of all rivers.

sn: सरस्वती सर्वनदीषु पुण्या सरस्वती लोकशुभावहा सदा। सरस्वतीं प्राप्य जनाः सुदुष्कृतं सदा न शोचन्ति परत्र चेह च॥
en: Sarasvati always confers the greatest happiness on men! After approaching the Sarasvati, men will not have to give for their sins either here or hereafter!'

sn: ततो मुहुर्मुहुः प्रीत्या प्रेक्षमाण: सरस्वतीम्। हयैर्युक्तं रथं शुभ्रमातिष्ठत परंतपः॥
en: Repeatedly looking with joy at the Sarasvati, that destroyer of foes then ascended an excellent car to which were yoked beautiful horses.

sn: स शीघ्रगामिना तेन रथेन यदुपुङ्गवः। दिदृक्षुरभिसम्प्राप्तः शिष्ययुद्धमुपस्थितम्॥
en: Journeying then on that highly fleet car Baladeva, that best of Yadu's race, desirous of seeing the approaching encounter of his two disciples, arrived on the field.”

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं तदभवद् युद्धं तुमुलं जनमेजय। यत्र दुःखान्वितो राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Thus, O Janamejaya, did that terrible battle take place. King Dhritarashtra, in great sorrow, said thus about it.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच रामं संनिहितं दृष्ट्वा गदायुद्ध उपस्थिते। मम पुत्रः कथं भीम प्रत्ययुध्यत संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Beholding Rama approach that spot, when the mace-fight was about to take place, how, O Sanjaya, did my son fight with Bhima?'

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: संजय उवाच रामसांनिध्यमासाद्य पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। युद्धकामो महाबाहुः समहष्यत वीर्यवान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding the presence of Rama, your valiant son Duryodhana of mighty arms, desirous of battle, was gladdened.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: दृष्टवा लागलिनं राजा प्रत्युत्थाय च भारत। प्रीत्या परमया युक्तः समभ्यर्च्य यथाविधि॥ आसनं च ददौ तस्मै पर्यपृच्छदनामयम्।
en: Seeing Vala, king Yudhishthira, O Bharata, stood up and duly and gladly honored him. He gave him a seat and enquired after his welfare.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: ततो युधिष्ठरं रामो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ मधुरं धर्मसंयुक्तं शूराणां हितमेव च। मया श्रुतं कथयतामृषीणां राजसत्तम॥ कुरुक्षेत्रं परं पुण्यं पावनं स्वर्गमेव च। दैवतैऋषिभिर्जुष्टं ब्राह्मणैश्च महात्मभिः॥
en: Rama then answered Yudhisthira, in these sweet and righteous words, viz.-I have heard it said by the Rishis, O best of kings, that Kurukshetra is a highly sacred and sindestroying spot, equal to heaven itself, worshipped of gods and Rishis and great Brahmanas.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तत्र वै योत्स्यमाना य देहं त्यक्ष्यन्ति मानवाः। तेषां स्वर्गे ध्रुवो वासः शक्रेण सह मारिष॥
en: Those men that renounce their bodies, while engaged in battle on this field, are sure to live in heaven with Shakra himself.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तस्मात् समन्तपञ्चकमितो याम द्रुतं नृप। प्रथितोत्तरवेदी सा देवलोके प्रजापतेः॥
en: I shall for this, O king, speedily proceed to Samantapancka. In the celestial region that spot is known as the northern (sacrificial) altar of Brahman, the Lord of all creatures.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तस्मिन् महापुण्यतमे त्रैलोक्यस्य सनातने। संग्रामे निधनं प्राप्य ध्रुवं स्वर्गे भविष्यति॥
en: He that breathes his last in battle on that eternal and most sacred of spots in the three worlds, will surely obtain heaven,

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा महाराज कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। समन्तपञ्चकं वीरः प्रायादभिमुखः प्रभुः॥
en: Saying-So be it-O king, Kunti's brave son, lord Yudhishthira, proceeded towards Samantapanchaka.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्। पद्भ्यामपर्षी द्युतिमानगच्छत् पाण्डवैः सह।१२।।
en: King Duryodhana also, taking up his gigantic mace, angrily went on foot with the Pandavas.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तथाऽऽयान्तं गदाहस्तं वर्मणा चापि दंशितम्। अन्तरिक्षचरा देवाः साधु साध्वित्यपूजयन्॥ वातिकाचारणा ये तु दृष्ट्वा ते हर्षमागताः। स पाण्डवैः परिवृतः कुरुराजस्तवात्मजः॥ मत्तस्येव गजेन्द्रस्य गतिमास्थाय सोऽव्रजत्। ततः शङ्खनिनादेन भेरीणां च महास्वनैः॥ सिंहनादैश्च शूराणां दिशः सर्वाः प्रपूरिताः।
en: While going thus, armed with mace and clad in armour, the celestial in the sky applauded him, saying-Excellent, excellent! Sceing the Kuru king, the Charanas became filled with delight. Surrounding by the Pandavas, your son, the Kuru king proceeded, like an infuriate elephant. All the points of the compass were filled with the blare of conchs and the sounds of drums and the leonine roars of heroes.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: ततस्ते तु कुरुक्षेत्रं प्राप्ता नरवरोत्तमाः॥ प्रतीच्यभिमुखं देशं यथोद्दिष्टं सुतेन ते।
en: Proceeding with face westwards to the appointed spot, with your son (in their midst), they spread themselves on all sides when they reached it.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: दक्षिणेन सरस्वत्याः स्वयनं तीर्थमुत्तमम्॥ तस्मिन् देशे त्वनिरिणे ते तु युद्धमरोचयन्।
en: That was an excellent Tirtha on the southern side of the Sarasvati. The ground there was not sandy, and was therefore, selected for the battle.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: ततो भीमो महाकोटिं गदां गृह्याथ वर्मभृत्॥ बिभ्रद्रूपं महाराज सदृशं हि गरुत्मतः।
en: Clad in armour, and armed with his gigantic thick mace Bhima, O king, assumed the form of mighty Garuda.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: अवबद्धशिरस्त्राणः संख्ये काञ्चनवर्मभृत्॥ रराज राजन् पुत्रस्ते काञ्चनः शैलराडिव।
en: With head-gear on his head, and wearing a golden armour licking the corners of his mouth, O king, with eyes redened in wrath, and breathing hard, your son on that field, O king, shone like the golden Sumeru.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: वर्मभ्यां संयतौ वीरौ भीमदुर्योधनावुभौ॥ संयुगे च प्रकाशेते संरब्धाविव कुञ्जरौ।
en: Those two heroes Bhima and Duryodhana, wearing armour appeaered like two elephants with anger, in battle field.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: रणमण्डलमध्यस्थौ भ्रातरौ तौ नरर्षभौ॥ अशोभेतां महाराज चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ।
en: O king! In the midst of war-field both the brothers, foremost among the men were looked like a rising moon and the sun.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तावन्योन्यं निरीक्षेतां क्रुद्धाविव महाद्विपौ॥ दहन्तौ लोचनौ राजन् परस्परवधैषिणौ।
en: O king! Both angrily with burning eyes wishing kill cach other, they looked like two infuriate elephants.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: सम्प्रहृष्टमना राजन् गदामादाय कौरवः॥ सृक्किणी संलिहन् राजन् क्रोधरक्तेक्षणः श्वसन्। ततो दुर्योधनो राजन् गदामादाय वीर्यवान्॥ भीमसेनमभिप्रेक्ष्य गजो गजमिवाह्वयत्।
en: Taking up his mace, with cheerful mind, the highly energetic king Duryodhana, the son of Kuru, breathing repeatedly and looking at Bhimasena, challenged him to encounter like an elephant challenging a rival elephant.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: अद्रिसारमयीं भीमस्तथैवादाय वीर्यवान्॥ आह्वयामास नृपति सिंह सिंहो यथा वने।
en: Likewise the brave Bhima, taking up his adamantine mace, challenged the king like a lion challenging a lion. or or

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तावुद्यतगदापाणी दुर्योधनवृकोदरौ॥ संयुगे च प्रकाशेतां गिरी सशिखराविव।
en: Duryodhana and Bhima, with uplifted maces, shone in that battle like two mountains with tall sumınits.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तावुभौ समतिक्रुद्धावुभौ भीमपराक्रमौ॥ उभौ शिष्यौ गदायुद्धे रौहिणेयस्य धीमतः। उभौ सदृशकर्माणौ यमवासवयोरिव॥ तथा सदृशकर्माणौ वरुणस्य महाबलौ। वासुदेवस्य रामस्य तथा वैश्रवणस्य च॥ सदृशौ तौ महाराज मधुकैटभयोर्युधि।
en: Both of them were highly worked up with anger; both were possessed of awful prowess; in mace encounter both were disciples of Rohini's intelligent son; both resembled each other in their feat and looked like Maya and Vasava. Endued with great strength, both resembled Varuna in achievements. Each resembling Vasudeva, Rama Vishravana's son (Ravana), they appeared O king, like Madhu and Kaitabha.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: उभौ सदृशकर्माणौ तथा सुन्दोपसुन्दयोः॥ रामरावणयोश्चैव वालिसुग्रीवयोस्तथा।
en: They looked like Sunda and Upasunda or Rama and Ravana or Bali and Sugriva.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तथैव कालस्य समौ मृत्योश्चैव परंतपौ॥ अन्योन्यमभिधावन्तौ मत्ताविव महाद्विपौ। वासितासंगमे दृप्तौ शरदीव मदोत्कटौ॥ उभौ क्रोधविषं दीप्तं वमन्तावुरगाविव।
en: Those two of foes appeared like Kala and Mrityu. They then ran towards each other like two infuriate elephants; elated with pride and maddened with passion in the season of autumn and longing for the companionship of a she-elephant in her season. Each appeared to vomit upon the other the poison of his wrath like two fiery serpents.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: अन्योन्यमभिसंरब्धौ प्रेक्षमाणावरिंदमौ॥ उभौ भरतशार्दूलौ विक्रमेण समन्वितौ।
en: Those two chastisers of foes looked angrily upon each other. Both were foremost of Bharata's race, endued with great prowess.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: सिंहाविव दुराधर्षों गदायुद्धविशारदौ॥ नखदंष्ट्रायुधौ वीरौ व्याघ्राविव दुरुत्सहौ। प्रजासंहरणे क्षुब्धौ समुद्राविव दुस्तरौ॥ लोहिताङ्गाविव क्रुद्धो प्रतपन्तौ महारथौ। पूर्वपश्चिमजौ मेघौ प्रेक्षमाणावरिंदमौ॥ गर्जमानौ सुविषमं क्षरन्तौ प्रादृषीव हि। रश्मियुक्तौ महात्मानौ दीप्तिमन्तौ महाबलौ॥ ददृशाते कुरुश्रेष्ठौ कालसूर्याविवोदितौ।
en: In mace encounters those two scorchers of foes were invincible like lion. Those heroes were unbearable like two tigers having teeth and claws. They were like two uncrossable and furious oceans, or like two angry Suns risen for consuming everything. Those two powerful car-warriors looked like an Eastern and a Western cloud agitated by the wind, roaring awfully and pouring torrents of rain in the rainy season. Those two great and powerful heroes, both possessed of great effulgence, looked like two Suns risen at the hour of the Universal dissolution.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: व्याघ्राविव सुसंरब्धौ गर्जन्ताविव तोयदौ॥ जहषाते महाबाहू सिंहकेसरिणाविवा जगाविव सुसंरब्धौ ज्वलिताविव पावकौ॥ ददृशाते महात्मानौ सशृङ्गाविव पर्वतौ। रोषात् प्रस्फुरमाणोष्ठौ निरीक्षन्तौ परस्परम्॥ तौ समेतौ महात्मानौ गदाहस्तौ नरोत्तमौ।
en: Looking like two enraged tigers or like two roaring masses of clouds, they became glad like two manned lions. Like two angry or two blazing fires, those two great ones appeared like two mountains with tall summits. With lips swelling with rage and looking upon each other those two heroes, armed with maces, met each other. Both were elated with joy and each regarded the other as a worthy opponent.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: उभौ परमसंहृष्टावुभौ परमसम्मतौ॥ सदश्वाविव हेषन्तौ बृहन्ताविव कुञ्जरौ।
en: Duryodhana and Vrikodara then resembled two good horses neighing at each other, or two elephants grunting at each other.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: वृषभाविव गर्जन्तौ दुर्योधनवृकोदरौ॥ दैत्याविव बलोन्मत्तौ रेजतुस्तौ नरोत्तमौ। ततो दुर्योधनो राजन्निदमाह युधिष्ठिरम्॥ भ्रातृभिः संहितं चैव कृष्णेन च महात्मना। रामेणामितवीर्येण वाक्यं शौटीर्यसम्मतम्॥
en: Those two foremost of men then shone like a couple of Daityas swelling with pride. The Duryodhana, O king, said these haughty words unto Yudhishthira in the midst of his brothers and of the great Krishna and Rama.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: केकयैः सृञ्जयैर्दृप्तं पञ्चालैश्च महात्मभिः । इदं व्यवसितं युद्धं मम भीमस्य चोभयोः॥ उपोपविष्टाः पश्यध्वं सहितैनूपपुङ्गवैः। श्रुत्वा दुर्योधनवचः प्रत्यपद्यन्त तत्तथा॥ ततः समुपविष्टं तत् सुमहद्रजमण्डलम्। विराजमानं ददृशे दिवीवादित्यमण्डलम्॥
en: Protected by the Kaikeyas and the Srinjayas and the great Panchalas, behold you with all these leading kings, seated together, this encounter that is about to take place between me and Bhima!-Hearing these words of Duryodhana, they did as requested. Then those kings sat down and shone like celestials in heaven.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तेषां मध्ये महाबाहुः श्रीमान् केशवपूर्वजः। उपविष्टो महाराज पूज्यमानः समन्ततः॥
en: In the midst of that assemblage the mightyarmed and beautiful elder brother of Keshava, O king, as he sat down, was all adored by all around him.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: शुशुभे राजमध्यस्थो नीलवासाः सितप्रभः। नक्षत्रैरिव सम्पूर्णो वृतो निशि निशाकरः॥
en: In the midst of those kings, Baladeva clad in blue raiment and possessed of a fair complexion shone like the full moon surrounded in the night by thousands of stars.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: तौ तथा तु महाराज गदाहस्तौ सुदुःसहौ। अन्योन्यं वाग्भिरुग्राभिस्तक्षमाणौ व्यवस्थितौ॥
en: Meanwhile those two heroes, O king, both armed with maces, and both unbearable by foes, stood there, exasperating each other with fierce speeches.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana and Baladeva's presence there
sn: अप्रियाणि ततोऽन्योन्यमुक्त्वा तौ कुरुसत्तमौ। उदीक्षन्तौ स्थितौ तत्र वृत्रशक्रौ यथाऽऽहवे॥
en: Having addressed each other with unpleasant words, those two heroes of Kuru's race stood, looking angrily upon each other, like Shakra and Vritra in fight."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो वाग्युद्धमभवत् तुमुलं जनमेजय। यत्र दुःखान्वितो राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said “At the outset, O Janamejaya, a dreadful encounter of words took place between the two heroes. With respect to that, king Dhritarashtra, filled with grief, said thisधिगस्तु खलु मानुष्यं यस्य निष्ठेयमीदृशी।

sn: एकादशचमूभर्ता यज्ञ पुत्रो ममानघ॥
en: Oh, fie, on man, who has such an end! My son, O sinless one, had been the master of eleven hosts of troops!

sn: आज्ञाप्य सर्वान् नृपतीन् भुक्त्वा चेमां वसुंधराम्। गदामादाय वेगेन पदातिः प्रस्थितो रणे॥
en: He had all the kings under his command and had enjoyed the sovereignty of the whole Earth! Alas, he that had been so, was now reduced to a warrior proceeding to battle, on foot, shouldering his mace.

sn: भूत्वा हि जगतो नाथो ह्यनाथ इव मे सुतः। गदामुद्यम्य यो याति किमन्यद् भागधेयतः॥ अहो दुःखं महत् प्राप्तं पुत्रेण मम संजय। एवमुक्त्वा स दुःखार्तो विरराम जनाधिपः॥
en: My poor son, who had before been the lord of the universe, was now himself without help! Alas, he had, then, to proceed on foot, shouldering his mace! What can it be but Destiny? Alas, O Sanjaya, great was the grief that was felt by my son now! 'Having uttered these words, the king afflicted with great sorrow became silent.

sn: संजय उवाच स मेधनिनदो हर्षानिनदनिव गोवृषः। आजुहाव तदा पार्थं युद्धाय युधि वीर्यवान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Having a voice deep like a cloud, Duryodhana then roared from joy like a bull. Possessed of great energy, he challenged the son of Pritha to battle.

sn: भीममाह्वायाने तु कुरुराजे महात्मानि। प्रादुरासन् सुघोराणि रूपाणि विविधान्युत॥
en: When the great king of the Kurus thus summoned Bhima to the encounter, various awful portents appeared there.

sn: ववुर्वाताः सनिर्घाताः पांशुवर्षं पपात च। बभूवुश्च दिशः सर्वास्तिमिरेण समावृताः॥
en: Fierce winds began to blow with loud noises at intervals, and a shower of dust fell. All the points of the compass were covered with a thick darkness.

sn: महास्वनाः सुनिर्वातास्तुमुला लोमहर्षणा। पेतुस्तथोल्काः शतशः स्फोटयन्त्यो नभस्तलात्॥
en: Thunder-bolts of loud noise dropped on all sides, causing a great confusion and making the very hair to stand on end. Hundreds of meteors fell, with a loud noise from the sky.

sn: राहुश्चाग्रसदादित्यमपर्वणि विशाम्पते। चकम्पे च महाकम्पं पृथिवी सवनदुमा॥
en: Rahu devoured the Sun most untimely, O king! The Earth with her forest and trees shook violently.

sn: दीप्ताश्च वातः प्रवर्नीचैः शर्करकर्षिणः। गिरीणां शिखराण्येव न्यपतन्त महीतले॥
en: Hot winds blew, carrying showers of hard pebbles along the ground. The summits of mountains dropped down on the Earth's surfacc.

sn: मृगा बहुविधाकाराः सम्पतन्ति दिशो दश। दीप्ताः शिवाश्चाप्यनदन् घोररूपाः सुदारुणाः॥
en: Various Animals were seen to run in various directions. Terrible and fierce jackals, with firing mouths, yelled piteously.

sn: निर्घाताश्च महाघोरा बभूवुर्लोमहर्षणाः। दीप्तायां दिशि राजेन्द्र मृगाश्चाशुभवेदिनः॥
en: Loud and terrific hair-stirring sounds were heard on every side, the four quarters seemed to be on fire, and many animals of ill omen became visible.

sn: उदपानगताश्चापो व्यवर्धन्त समन्ततः। अशरीरा महानादाः श्रूयन्ते स्म तदा नृप॥
en: The water in the wells on all sides swelled up. Loud sounds came from every side without, O king, none to utter them being visible.

sn: एवमादीनि दृष्ट्वाऽऽथ निमित्तानि वृकोदरः। उवाच भ्रातरः ज्येष्ठं धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Beholding these and other evil omens Vrikodara said to his eldest brother, king

sn: नैष शक्तो रणे जेतुं मन्दात्मा मां सुयोधनः। अद्य क्रोधं विमोक्ष्यामि निगूढं हृदये चिरम्॥ सुयोधने कौरवेन्द्रे खाण्डवेऽग्निमिवार्जुनः। शल्यमद्योद्धरिष्यामि तव पाण्डव हृच्छयम्॥
en: This wicked Suyodhana is not able to defeat me in battle. I shall to-day vomit that vie, which I have been cherishing for a long time in the recesses of my heart, upon this lord of the Kurus like Arjuna throwing fire upon the forest of Khandava! To-day, O son of Pandu, I shall take out the dart that lies sticking to thy heart!

sn: निहत्य गदया पापमिमं कुरुकुलाधमम्। अद्य कीर्तिमयीं मालां प्रतिमोक्ष्याम्यहं त्वयि॥
en: Killing with my mace this sinful wretch of Kuru's race, I shall to-day, place around your neck the garland of Fame!

sn: हत्वेमं पापकर्माणं गदया रणमूर्धनि। अद्यास्य शतधा देहं भिनद्मि गदयाऽनया॥ नायं प्रवेष्टा नगरं पुनर्वारणसाह्वयम्।
en: Killing this sinful person with my mace on the field of battle, I shall to-day, with this very mace of mine, break his body into a hundred pieces! He shall not have again to enter the city of Hastinapur!

sn: सर्पोत्सर्गस्य शयने विषदानस्य भोजने।॥ प्रमाणकोट्यां पातस्य दाहस्य जतुवेश्मनि। सभायामवहासस्य सर्वस्वहरणस्य च॥ वर्षमज्ञातवासस्य वनवासस्य चानघ। अद्यान्तमेषां दुःखानां गन्ताहं भरतर्षभ।॥ एकाह्रा विनिहत्येमं भविष्याम्यात्मनोऽनृणः।
en: The setting of serpents at us while we were sleeping, the giving of venom to us while we were eating, the casting of our body into the water at Pramanakoti, the attempt to burn us at the house of lac, the insult given to us at the assembly, the robbing us of all our wealth, the whole year of our living in concealment, our exile into the forest, O sinless one, of all these misfortunes, O best of Bharata's race, I shall terminate to-day, O Bharata's chief! Killing this wretch, I shall, in one single day, pay off all the debts I owe him.

sn: अद्यायुर्धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्मतेरकृतात्मनः॥ समाप्तं भरतश्रेष्ठ मातापित्रोश्च दर्शनम्।
en: To-day the lease of life, of this wicked son of Dhritarashtra, of impure soul, has reached its end, O Bharata's chief. After this day he shall not again look at his father and mother!

sn: अद्य सौख्यं तु राजेन्द्र कुरुराजस्य दुर्मतेः॥ समाप्तं च महाराज नारीणां दर्शनं पुनः ।
en: To-day, O king, the happiness of this wicked king of the Kurus has terminated. After this day, O king, he shall not again see a beautiful damsel!

sn: अद्यायं कुरुराजस्य शान्तनोः कुलपांसनः॥ प्राणान् श्रियं च राज्यं च त्यक्त्वा शेष्यति भूतले।
en: To-day this disgrace of Shantanu's race shall sleep on the naked Earth, his life, his prosperity, and his kingdom gone!

sn: राजा च धृतराष्ट्रोऽद्य श्रुत्वा पुत्रं निपातितम्॥ स्मरिष्यत्यशुभं कर्म यत्तच्छकुनिबुद्धिजम्।
en: Hearing of the fall of his son to-day, king Dhritarashtra also shall recollect all those evil acts that were the creations of Shakuni!'

sn: इत्युक्त्वा राजशार्दूल गदामादाय वीर्यवान्।॥ अभ्यतिष्ठत युद्धाय शक्रो वृत्रमिवाह्वयन्। कुरुराजस्य शान्तनोः
en: Having said these words, ( foremost of kings, the highly energetic, Vrikodara armed with mace, stood for fight, like Shakra challenging the Asura Vritra.

sn: तमुद्यतगदं दृष्ट्वा कैलासमिव शृङ्गिणम्॥ भीमसेनः पुनः क्रुद्धो दुर्योधनमुवाच ह। राज्ञश्च धृतराष्ट्रस्य तथा त्वमपि चात्मनः॥ स्पर तद् दुष्कृतं कर्म यद् वृत्तं वारणावते।
en: Seeing Duryodhana also standing with uplifted mace like mount Kailasa, Bhimasena, worked up with ire, once more addressed him, saying— 'Remember that misdeed of yourself and king Dhritarashtra that occurred at Varnavata!

sn: द्रौपदी च परिविष्टा सभामध्ये रजस्वला॥ द्यूते न वञ्चितो राजा यत् त्वया सौबलेन च।
en: Remember the ill-treatment of Draupadi, while in her season, in the midst of the assembly! Remember how yourself and Subala's son deprived the king at dice.

sn: वने दुःखं च यत् प्राप्तमस्माभिस्त्वत्कृतं महत्॥ विराटनगरे चैव योन्यन्तरगतैरिव। तत् सर्वं पातयाम्यद्य दिष्ट्या दृष्टोऽसि दुर्मति॥
en: Remember the great misfortune suffered by L'S, for you, in the forest, as also in Virata's city, as if we had once more entered the womb! I shall avenge them all to-day. By good luck, I see you to-day!

sn: त्वकृतेऽसौ हतः शेते शरतल्पे प्रतापवान्। गाङ्गेयो रथिनां श्रेष्ठो निहतो याज्ञसेनिना॥
en: It is for you that foremost of car-warriors, viz., the highly powerful son of Ganga, struck down by Yajnasena's son, sleep on a bed of arrows.

sn: हतो द्रोणश्च कर्णश्च तथा शल्यः प्रतापवान्। वैराग्नेरादिकर्तासौ शकुनिः सौबलो हतः॥
en: Drona also has been killed, and Karna, and Shalya of great prowess! Subala's son Shakuni too, that root of all this evil has been killed!

sn: प्रातिकामी तथा पापो द्रौपद्याः कुशकृद्धतः। भ्रातरस्ते हताः सर्वे शूरा विक्रान्तयोधिनः॥
en: The wretched Pratikamin, who had seized Draupadi by her hair, has been killed! All your brave brothers also, who fought with great velour, have been killed!

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो निहतास्त्वत्कृते नृपाः। त्वामद्य निहनिष्यामि गदया नात्र संशयः॥
en: These and many other kings have been killed through your fault! I shall kill you to-day with my mace! There is not the least doubt about it!'

sn: इत्येवमुचै राजेन्द्र भाषमाणं वृकोदरम्। उवाच गतभी राजन् पुत्रस्ते सत्यविक्रमः॥ किं कत्थनेन बहुना युध्यस्व त्वं वृकोदर। अद्य तेऽहं विनेष्यामि युद्धश्रद्धां कुलाधम॥
en: While Vrikodara, O king, was uttering these words in a loud voice, your fearless son answered him, saying-'What is the use of bragging? Fight me, O Vrikodara! O wretch, to-day I shall satiate your desire of fight!

sn: न हि दुर्योधनः क्षुद्र केनचित् त्वद्विधेन वै। शक्यस्त्रासयितुं वाचां यथाऽन्यः प्राकृतो नरः॥
en: Mean as you are, know that Duryodhana is not capable, like an ordinary person, of being terrified by a person like you!

sn: चिरकालेप्सितं दिष्ट्या हृदयस्थमिदं मम। त्वया सह गदायुद्धं त्रिदशैरुपपादितम्॥
en: For a long time have I cherished this desire! For a long time I have been cherishing this desire! By good fortune the goods have at last brought it about!

sn: किं वाचा बहुनोक्तेन कत्थितेन च दुर्मते। वाणी सम्पद्यतामेषा कर्मणा मा चिरं कृथाः॥ तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्व एवाभ्यपूजयन्। राजानः सोमकाश्चैव ये तत्रासन् समागताः॥
en: What is the use of long talks and idle brag, O wicked man! Carry out these words of yours into acts! Do not delay at all!—Hearing these words of his, the Somakas and the other kings that were present there, all praised them highly.

sn: ततः सम्पूजितः सर्वैः सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः. भूयो धीरां मतिं चक्रे युद्धाय कुरुनन्दनः॥
en: Lauded by all, Duryodha's hair stood erect with joy, and he made of his mind for fight.

sn: उन्मत्तमिव मातङ्गं तलशब्दैर्नराधिपाः। भूयः संहर्षयाचक्रुर्दुर्योधनममर्षणम्॥
en: The kings present once again cheered your wrathful son with claps like persons exciting a mad elephant to a fight.

sn: तं महात्मा महात्मानं गदामुद्यम्य पाण्डवः। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन धार्तराष्ट्र वृकोदरः॥
en: Then uplifting his mace, the great Vrikodara, the son of Pandu, rushed furiously at your high-souled son.

sn: बृहन्ति कुञ्जरास्तत्र हया द्वेषन्ति चासकृत्। शस्त्राणि चाप्यदीप्यन्त पाण्डवानां जयैषिणाम्॥
en: The elephants present there grunted aloud and the horses neighed repeatedly. The weapons of the Pandavas, who were eager for victory, shone resplendent with their own luster.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच ततो दुर्योधनो दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनं तथागतम्। प्रत्युद्ययावदीनात्मा वेगेन महता नदन् ॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing Bhimasena in that state, Duryodhana rushed furiously against him uttering a loud roar.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: समापेततुरन्योन्यं शृङ्गिणौ वृषभाविव। महानिर्घातघोषचं प्रहाराणामजायत॥
en: They met each other like two bulls encountering each other with their horns. The strokes of their maces produced loud sounds like those of thunder-bolts.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अभवच तयोर्युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। जिगीषतोर्यथान्योन्यमिन्द्रप्रह्लादयोरिव॥
en: Each seeking victory, the battle that took place between them was terrible, making the hair stand erect, like that between Indra and Pralada.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्गौ गदाहस्तौ मनस्विनौ। ददृशाते महात्मानौ पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥
en: All their limbs covered with blood, the two great and energetic warriors both armed with maces, looked like two Kinshukas decked with flowers.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तथा तस्मिन् महायुद्धे वर्तमाने सुदारुणे। खद्योतसंधैरिव खं दर्शनीयं व्यरोचत॥
en: During the onset of that great and awful encounter, the sky looked beautiful as if it swarmed with fire-flies.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तथा तस्मिन् वर्तमाने संकुले तुमुले भृशम्। उभावपि परिश्रान्तौ युध्यमानावरिंदमौ॥
en: After that fierce and terrible battle had lasted for some time, both of them were exhausted.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तौ मुहूर्तं समाश्वस्य पुनरेव परंतपौ। अभ्यहारयतान्योन्यं सम्प्रगृह्य गदे शुभे॥
en: Having rested for sometime those two destroyers of foes, taking up their handsome maces, once again began to prevent each other's attacks.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तौ तु दृष्ट्वा महावी? समाश्वस्तौ नरर्षभौ। बलिनौ वारणौ यद्वद्वासितार्थे मदोत्कटौ॥
en: Indeed, when those two highly energetic warriors, those two foremost of men, both possessed of great strength, once more met each other after having rested a little, they looked like two infuriate elephants attacking each other for obtaining an elephants in season.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: समानवी? सम्प्रेक्ष्य प्रगृहीतगदावुभौ। विस्मयं परमं जग्मुर्देवगन्धर्वमानवाः॥
en: Seeing those two heroes, both arined with maces and equaling each other in energy, the gods and Gandharvas and men were filled with wonder.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: प्रगृहीतगदौ दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनवृकोदरौ। संशयः सर्वभूतानां विजये समपद्यत॥
en: Beholding Duryodhana and Vrikodara both armed with mace, all creatures became doubtful as to who amongst them would come off victorious.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: समागम्य ततो भूयो भ्रातरो बलिनां वरौ। अन्योन्यस्यन्तरप्रेप्सू प्रचक्रातेऽन्तरं प्रति॥
en: Rushing each other and desiring to take advantage of each other's weakness, those two great cousins waited each watching the other.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: यमदण्डोपमां गुर्वीमिन्द्राशनिमिवोद्यताम्। ददृशुः प्रेक्षका राजन् रौद्री विशसनीं गदाम्॥
en: People, O king, saw each armed with his uplifted mace, that was heavy dreadful and killing, and that resembled the bludgeon of Yama, or the thunder-bolt of Indra.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: आविद्ध्यतो गदां तस्य भीमसेनस्य संयुगे। शब्दः सुतुमुलो घोरो मुहूर्तं समपद्यत॥
en: While Bhimasena whirled his weapon, it produced a loud and dreadful sound.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: आविद्ध्यन्तमरिं प्रेक्ष्य धार्तराष्ट्रोऽथ पाण्डवम्। गदामतुलवेगां तां विस्मितः सम्बभूवह॥
en: Seeing his foe, the son of Pandu, thus whirling his mace, the impetuous Duryodhana was amazed.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: चरंश्च विविधानं मार्गान् मण्डलानि च भारत। अशोभत तदा वीरो भूय एव वृकोदरः॥
en: Indeed, the heroic Vrikodara, O Bharata, as he moved about in various courses, shone highly beautiful.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तौ परस्परमासाद्य यत्तावन्योन्यरक्षणे। मार्जाराविव भक्षार्ये ततक्षाते मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: Both bent upon carefully protecting themselves, they approached, they repeatedly wounded each other like two cats, fighting for a piece of meat.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अचरद् भीमसेनस्तु मार्गान् बहुविधांस्तथा। मण्डलानि विचित्राणि गतप्रत्यागतानि च।॥
en: Bhimasena performed various kinds of evolutions. He moved about in beautiful circles, advanced, and receded.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अस्त्रयन्त्राणि चित्राणि स्थानानि विविधानि च। परिमोक्षं प्रहाराणां वर्जनं परिधावनम्॥
en: He dealt blows and warded off those of his opponent, with wonderful dexterity. He took up various kinds of offensive and defensive position. He made attacks and warded off those as of his opponent. He ran at his enemy now turning to the right and now to the left.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अभिद्रवणमाक्षेपमवस्थानं सविग्रहम्। परिवर्तनसंवर्तमवप्लुतमुपप्लुतम्॥
en: He advanced straight against the foe. He made various tricks for drawing his foe. He stood immovable, bent upon attacking his cnemy as soon as the latter would expose himself to attack. He went round his foe, and prevented his foe from circumnambulating him. He avoided the attacks of his enemy by moving away in bent postures or jumping up.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: उपन्यस्तमपन्यस्तं गदायुद्धविशारदौ। एवं तौ विचरन्तौ तु परस्परमविध्यताम्॥
en: Facing his enemy he struck, or dealt backthrusts while moving away from him. Both experts in mace-fighting, Bhima and Duryodhana thus moved about and fought, and struck each other.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: वञ्जयानौ पुनश्चैव चेरतुः कुरुसत्तमौ। विक्रीडन्तौ सुबलिनौ मण्डलानि विचेरतुः॥
en: Those two leading Kuru's heroes fared thus, each avoiding the other's attacks. Indeed, those two great warriors thus moved about in circles and seemed to play with each other.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तौ दर्शयन्तौ समरे युद्धक्रीडां समन्ततः। गदाभ्यां सहसान्योन्यमाजघ्नतुररिंदमौ॥ परस्परं समासाद्य दंष्ट्राभ्यां द्विरदौ यथा। अशोभेतां महाराज शोणितेन परिप्लुतौ॥
en: Displaying in that encounter their skill in battle, those two destroyers of foes sometimes suddenly attacked each other with their weapons, like two elephants attacked each other with their tusks. Bathed in blood, they looked very beautiful, O king, on ine field.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: एवं तदभवद् युद्धं घोररूपं परंतप। परिवृत्तेऽहनि क्रूर वृत्रवासवयोरिव॥ गदाहस्तौ ततस्तौ तु मण्डलावस्थितौ बली।
en: Thus took place that dreadful battle before the very eyes of a large multitude, towards the close of the day, like the battle between Vritra and Vasava. Armed with maces, both began to move about in circles.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
