sn: दक्षिणं मण्डलं राजन् भीमसेनोऽभ्यवर्तत॥ सव्यं तु मण्डलं तत्र भीमसेनोऽभ्यवर्तत।
en: Duryodhana, O king, adopted the right Mandala, while Bhimasena adopted the left Mandala.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तथा तु चरतस्तस्य भीमस्य रणमूर्धनि॥ दुर्योधनो महाराज पार्श्वदेशेऽभ्यताडयत्।
en: While Bhima was thus moving about in circles on the field of battle, Duryodhana, O king, suddenly struck him a fierce blow on one of his flanks.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: आहतस्तु ततो भीमः पुत्रेण तव भारत।॥ आविद्धयत गदां गुर्वी प्रहारं तमचिन्तयन्।
en: Struck by your son, Bhima began to whir) his heavy mace for returning the same.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: इन्द्राशनिसमां घोरां यमदण्डमिवोद्यताम्॥ ददृशुस्ते महाराज भीमसेनस्य तां गदाम्।
en: People, O king, saw the mace of Bhimasena look as terrible as Indra's thunder-bolt or Yama's rod.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: आविध्यन्तं गदां दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनं तवात्मजः॥ समुद्यम्य गदां घोरां प्रत्यविध्यत् परंतपः।
en: Seeing Bhima whirl his mace, your son, took up his own terrible weapon, and struck him again.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: गदामारुतवेगेन तव पुत्रस्य भारत॥ शब्द आसीत् सुतुमुलस्तेजश्च समजायत।
en: A loud sound, O Bharata, was caused by the fall of your son's mace. So quick was that fall that it caused a flame of fire in sky.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स चरन् विविधान् मार्गान् मण्डलानि च भागशः।। समशोभत तेजस्वी भूयो भीमात् सुयोधनः।
en: Coursing in circles, adopting each motion at the proper time, the energetic Suyodhana, once more seemed to prevail over Bhima.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: आविद्धा सर्ववेगेन भीमेन महती गदा॥ सधूमं सार्चिषं चाग्निं मुमोचोग्रमहास्वना।
en: Meanwhile the massive of Bhimasena, whirled with his entire force, produced a tremendous sound with valleys of smoke, and sparks and flames of fire. mace

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: आधूतां भीमसेनेन गदां दृष्ट्वा सुयोधनः॥ अद्रिसारमयीं गुर्वीमाविध्यन् बहशोभता
en: Seeing Bhimasena whirling his mace, Suyodhana also whirled his heavy and adamantine mace, and appeared highly beautiful.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: गदामारुतवेगं हि दृष्ट्वा तस्य महात्मनः॥ भयं विवेश पाण्डूंस्तु सर्वानेव ससोमकान्।
en: Marking the vehemence of the wind, caused by the whirl of Duryodhana's mace, the Pandus and the Somakas were stricken with great fear.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तौ दर्शयन्तौ समरे युद्धक्रीडां समन्ततः॥ गदाभ्यां सहसान्योन्यमाजघ्नतुररिंदमौ। तौ परस्परमासाद्य दंष्ट्राभ्यां द्विरदौ यथा॥ अशोभेतां महाराज शोणितेन परिप्लुतौ।
en: Meanwhile showing on every side their skill in battle those two chastisers of foes continued to strike each other with their maces, like two elephants striking each other with their tusks. Both of them, O king, covered with blood, shone highly beautiful.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: एवं तदभवद् युद्धं घोररूपमसंवृतम्॥ परिवृत्तेऽहनि क्रूरं वृत्रवासवयोरिव।
en: Thus that dreadful battle went on before the very eyes of thousands of spectators at the close of day, like the fierce battle that took place between Vritra and Vasava.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: दृष्ट्वा व्यवस्थितं भीमं तव पुत्रो महाबलः॥ चरंश्चित्रतरान् मार्गान् कौन्तेयमभिदुद्रुवे।
en: Seeing Bhima firmly stationed on the field, your powerful son, moving about, rushed towards that son of Kunti.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तस्य भीमो महावेगां जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृताम्॥ अतिक्रुद्धस्य क्रुद्धस्तु ताडयामास तां गदाम्।
en: Worked up with wrath Bhima struck the mace, endued with great impetuosity and adorned with gold, of the angry Duryodhana.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: सविस्फुलिङ्गो नि दस्तयोस्तत्राभिघातजः॥ प्रादुरासीन्महाराज सृष्टयोर्वज्रयोरिव।
en: That clash of the two maces produced a loud sound with sparks of fire, which resembled the clash of two thunder-bolts from opposite directions.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: वेगवत्या तया तत्र भीमसेनप्रमुक्तया॥ निपतन्त्या महाराज पृथिवी समकम्पत।
en: Discharged by Bhimasena, his impetuous mace, as it dropped down, shook the very Earth.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तां नामृष्यत कौरव्यो गदां प्रतिहतां रणे॥ मत्तो द्विप इव क्रुद्धः प्रतिकुञ्जरदर्शनात्।
en: The Kuru prince could not see his own mace thus baffled in that attack. He was enraged like an infuriate elephant at the sight of a rival elephant.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स सव्यं मण्डलं राजा उद्भ्राम्य कृतनिश्चयः॥ आजम्ने मूर्ध्नि कौन्तेयं गदया भीमवेगया।
en: Adopting the left Mandala, O king, and whirling his mace, Suyodhana, then struck the son of Kunti on the head with his terrible weapon.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तया त्वभिहतो भीमः पुत्रेण तव पाण्डवः॥ नाकम्पत महाराज तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्।
en: Thus struck by your son, Bhima, the son of Pandu, did not even quake, O king, and the sight filled all present with wonder.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: आश्चर्यं चापि तद् राजन् सर्वसैन्यान्यपूजयन्॥ यद् गदाभिहतो भीमो नाकम्पत पदात् पदम्। ततो गुरुतरां दीप्तां गदां हेमपरिष्कृताम्॥ दुर्योधनाय व्यसृजद् भीमो भीमपराक्रमः।
en: That wonderful patience, O king, of Bhimasena, who did not move an inch, though struck so violently, was praised by all the combatants present there. Then Bhima hurled at Duryodhana his own heavy and shining mace adorned with gold.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तं प्रहारमसम्भ्रान्तो लाघवेन महाबलः॥ मोघं दुर्योधनश्चक्रे तत्राभूद् विस्मयो महान्।
en: The powerful and fearless Duryodhana prevented that blow by his activity. Seeing this the spectators were filled with great wonder.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: सा तु मोघा गदा राजन् पतन्ती भीमचोदिता॥ चालयामास पृथिवी महानिर्घातनि:स्वना।
en: That mace, hurled by Bhima, O king, Produced a loud sound like that of the thunderbolt, and shook the very Earth.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: आस्थाय कौशिकान् मार्गानुत्पतन् स पुनः पुनः॥ गदानिपातं प्रज्ञाय भीमसेनं च वञ्चितम्।
en: Adopting the manoeuvre called Kaushika, and jumping up again and again, Duryodhana, properly making the fall of Bhima's mace, made the latter useless.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: वञ्चयित्वा तदा भीमं गदया कुरुसत्तमः॥ ताडयामास संक्रुद्धो वक्षोदेशे महाबलः।
en: Baffling Bhimasena thus, the highly powerful Kuru king, at last in anger struck the former in the chest.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: गदया निहतो भीमो मुह्यमानो महारणे॥ नाभ्यमन्यत कर्तव्यं पुत्रेणाभ्याहतस्तव।
en: Struck very forcibly by your son in that dreadful battle, Bhimasena was stupefied, and for a time knew not what to do.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तमाने राजन् सोमकपाण्डवाः॥ भृशोपहतसंकल्या न हृष्टमनसोऽभवन्।
en: At that time, O king, the Somakas and the Pandavas were greatly disappointed and dispirited.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स तु तेन प्रहारेण मातङ्ग इव रोहितः॥ हस्तिवद्धस्तिसंकाशमभिदुद्राव ते सुतम्।
en: Worked up with anger at that blow, Bhima then rushed at your son like an elephant rushing against an elephant.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततस्तु तरसा भीमो गदया तनयं तव॥ अभिदुद्राव वेगेन सिंहो वनगजं यथा।
en: With uplifted mace, Bhima rushed furiously at Duryodhana like a lion rushing against a wild elephant.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: उपसृत्य तु राजानं गदामोक्षविशारदः॥ आविध्यत गदां राजन् समुद्दिश्य सुतं तव।
en: Approaching the Kuru king, the son of Pandu, O king, an expert in the use of the mace, began to whirl his weapon, aiming at your son.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: अताडयद् भीमसेनः पार्श्वे दुर्योधनं तदा॥ स विह्वलः प्रहारेण जानुभ्यामगमन्महीम्।
en: Bhimasena then struck Duryodhana on one of his sides. Stupefied at that blow, the latter dropped down on the Earth, supporting himself on his knees.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तस्मिन् कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठे जानुभ्यामवनीं गते॥ उदतिष्ठत् ततो नादः संजयानां जगत्पते।
en: When that Kuru's hero fell upon his knees, a loud cry arose from among the Srinjayas, O king!

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: तेषां तु निनदं श्रुत्वा संजयानां नरर्षभः॥ अमर्षाद् भरतश्रेष्ठ पुत्रस्ते समकुप्यता
en: Hearing that cry of the Srinjayas, O foremost of men, your son was worked up with rage.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: उत्थाय तु महाबाहुर्महानाग इव श्वसन्॥ दिधक्षन्निव नेत्राभ्यां भीमसेनमवैक्षत।
en: Rising up, the mighty-armed hero began to breathe like a powerful snake, and seemed to burn Bhimasena by looking upon him.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततः स भरतश्रेष्ठो गजापाणिरभिद्रवन्॥ प्रमथिष्यन्निव शिरो भीमसेनस्य संयुगे।
en: That best of the line of Bharata then rushed at Bhimasena, as if he would crush the head of his opponent in that battle,

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स महात्मा महात्मानं भीमं भीमपराक्रमः॥ अताडयच्छवदेशे न चचालाचलोपमः।
en: The great and highly powerful Duryodhana, then struck the high-souled Bhimasena on the forehead. The latter, however, stirred not an inch but stood fixed like a mountain.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स भूयः शुशुभे पार्थस्ताडितो गदया रणे। उद्भिन्नरुधिरो राजन्प्रभिन्न इव कुञ्जरः॥
en: Thus struck in that battle, the son of Pritha, O king, looked beautiful, as he bled profusely, like an elephant with temporal juice trickling down its temples.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततो गदां वीरहणीमयोमयां प्रगृह्य वज्राशनितुल्यानि:स्वनाम्। अताडयच्छत्रुममित्रकर्षणो बलेन विक्रम्य धनंजयाग्रजः॥
en: Then, taking up his hero-killing mace made of iron and producing a sound loud as that of the thunder-bolt, the elder brother of Dhananjaya struck his opponent with great force.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स भीमसेनाभिहतस्तवात्मजः पपात संकम्पितदेहबन्धनः। सुपुष्पितो मारुतवेगताडितो वने यथा शाल इवावघूर्णितः॥
en: Struck by Bhimnasena, your son dropped down, his bodying trembling all over, like a gigantic Shala in the forest, decked with flowers, uprooted by a tempest.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततः प्रणेदुर्जहषुश्च पाण्डवाः समीक्ष्य पुत्रं पतितं क्षितौ तव। ततः सुतस्ते प्रतिलभ्य चेतनां समुत्पपात द्विरदो यथा ह्रदात्॥
en: See your son laid on the Earth, the Pandavas became highly glad and uttered loud cries. Regaining his consciousness your son then rose, like an elephant from a lake.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स पार्थिवो नित्यममर्षितस्तदा महारथः शिक्षितवत् परिभ्रमन्। अताडयत् पाण्डवमग्रतः स्थितं स विह्वलाङ्गो जगतीमुपास्पृशत्॥
en: That angry king and great car-warrior then, moving about with great skill, great skill, struck Bhimasena who was before him. Thereat, the son of Pandu, with weakened limbs, dropped down on the Earth.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: स सिंहनादं विननाद कौरवो निपात्य भूमौ युधि भीममोजसा। बिभेद चैवाशनितुल्यमोजसा गदानिपातेन शरीररक्षणम्॥
en: Having by his power struck down Bhimasena on the ground, the Kuru prince sent up a leonine roar. By the fall of his mace, whose vehemence was like that of the thunder, he had, broken Bhima's coat-of-mail.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षे निनदो महानभूद् दिवौकसामप्सरसां च नेदुषाम्। पपात चौचैरमरप्रवेरितं विचित्रपुष्पोत्करवर्षमुत्तमम्॥
en: A loud uproar was then heard in they sky made by the celestials and the Apsaras. A shower of flowers of sweet fragrance, rained by the celestials, poured in.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततः परानाविशदुत्तमं भयं समीक्ष्य भूमौ पतितं नरोत्तमम्। अहीयमानं च बलेन कौरवं निशाम्य भेदं सुदृढस्य वर्मणः॥
en: Seeing Bhima prostrated on the Earth, and seeing his coat-of-mail out open, a great fear possessed the hearts of our foes.

description: The encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana
sn: ततो मुहूर्तादुपलभ्य चेतनां प्रमृज्य वक्त्रं रुधिराक्तमात्मनः। धृति समालम्व्य विवृत्य लोचने बलेन संस्तभ्य वृकोदरः स्थितः॥
en: Regaining his senses in a moment, and wiping his face which had been covered with blood, and gathering patience, Vrikodara stood up, with rolling eyes."

sn: संजय उवाच समुदीर्णं ततो दृष्ट्वा संग्रामें कुरुमुख्ययोः। अथाब्रवीदर्जुनस्तु वासुदेवं यशस्विनम्॥ अनयोरियोयुद्धे को ज्यायान् भवतो मतः। कस्य वा को गुणो भूयानेतद् वद जनार्दन॥
en: Sanjaya said “Seeing that fight thus ranging between those two greatest heroes of Kuru's race, Arjuna said to Vasudeva-'Who, in your superior between these two? What is their respective merit. Tell this, O

sn: वासुदेव उवाच उपदेशोऽनयोस्तुल्यो भीमस्तु बलवत्तरः। कृती यत्नपरस्त्वेष धार्तराष्ट्रो वृकोदरात्॥
en: Vasudeva said The instruction received by them has been equal. Bhima, however, is possessed of greater me strength while Duryodhana is possessed of greater skill and has worked harder.

sn: भीमसेनस्तु धर्मेण युद्ध्यमानो न जेष्यति। अन्यायेन तु युध्यन् वै हन्यादेव सुयोधनम्॥
en: If he were to fight fairly, Bhimasena will never succeed in gaining victory. If, however, he fights unfairly, he will surely be able to kill Duryodhana.

sn: मायया निर्जिता देवैरसुरा इति नः श्रुतम्। विरोचनस्तु शक्रेण मायया निर्जितः स वै॥
en: The Asuras were defeated by the gods deceptively. We have heard this. Virochana was defeated by Shakra with the aid of deception.

sn: मायया चाक्षिपत् तेजो वृत्रस्य बलसूदनः। तस्मान्मायामयं भीम आतिष्ठतु पराक्रमम्॥
en: The destroyer of Vala deprived Vritra his energy by an act of deception. Therefore, let Bhimasena put forth his prowess, by means of deception!

sn: प्रतिज्ञातं च भीमेन द्यूतकाले धनंजय। ऊरू भेत्स्यामि ते संख्ये गदयेति सुयोधनम्॥
en: At the time of the gambling, O Dhananjaya, Bhima promised to break the thighs of Suyodhana with his mace in battle.

sn: सोऽयं प्रतिज्ञां तां चापि पालयत्वरिकर्षणः। मायाविनं तु राजानं माययैव निकृन्ततु॥
en: Let this destroyer of foes, therefore, fulfill his vow. Let him, deceptively kill the Kuru king who is made of deception!

sn: यद्येष बलमास्थाय न्यायेन प्रहरिष्यति। विषमस्थस्ततो राजा भविष्यति युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: If depending upon his might alone, Bhima were to fight fairly, king Yudhishthira will meet with great peril.

sn: पुनरेव तु वक्ष्यामि पाण्डवेय निबोध मे। धर्मराजापराधेन भयं नः पुनरागतम्॥
en: I tell you again, O son of Pandu, listen to ine! It is through the fault of king Yudhishthira alone that danger has once more befallen us.

sn: कृत्वा हि सुमहत् कर्म हत्वा भीष्ममुखान् कुरून्। जयः प्राप्तो यशः प्राग्र्यं वैरं च प्रतियातितम्॥
en: Having performed great feats by the destruction of Bhishma and the other Kurus, the king had gained victory and glory, and had almost terminated the hostilities.

sn: तदेवं विजयः प्राप्तः पुनः संशयितः कृतः। अबुद्धिरेषा महती धर्मराजस्य पाण्डव॥ यदेकविजये युद्धं पाणितं घोरमीद्दशम्। सुयोधनः कृती वीर एकायनगतस्तथा॥
en: Having thus gained the victory, he pleased himself once more in a doubtful and perilous situation. This has been great mistake on the part of Yudhishthira, O Pandava, since he has made the result of the battle depend upon the victory or the defeat of only one warrior! Suyodhana is an expert, he is a hero; he is of firm determination.

sn: अपि चोशनसा गीतः श्रूयतेऽयं पुरातनः। श्लोकस्तत्त्वार्थसहितस्तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: We have all heard the old verse uttered by Ushanas, Hear I recite it to you with its true sense and meaning!

sn: पुनरावर्तमानानां भग्नानां जीवितैषिणाम्। भेतव्यमरिशेषाणामेकायनगता हि ते॥
en: The remnant of hostile force routed and flying away for life that really and come back to the fight, should always be feared, for they are of fixed determination and singleness of purpose!

sn: साहसोत्पतितानां च निराशानां च जीविते। न शक्यमग्रतः स्थातुं शक्रेणापि धनंजय॥
en: Shakra himself O Dhananjaya, cannot stand before them who rush in fury, giving up all hopes of life.

sn: सुयोधनमिमं भग्नं हतसैन्यं ह्रदं गतम्। पराजितं वनप्रेप्सुं निराशं राज्यलम्भने॥ को न्वेष संयुगे प्राज्ञः पुनर्द्वन्द्वे समाह्वयेत्। अपि नो निर्जितं राज्यं न हरेत सुयोधनः॥
en: This Suyodhana had been routed and fled. All his troops had been slain. He had entered the lake. He had been defeated, and, therefore, he had wished to retire into forest, having given up all hope of retaining his kingdom. What wise man is there, that would challenge such a person to a single-combat?

sn: यस्त्रयोदशवर्षाणि गदया कृतनिश्रमः। चरत्यूर्ध्वं च तिर्यक् च भीमसेनजिघांसया॥
en: I do not know whether Duryodhana will regain the kingdom that had already become ours! For full thirteen years he practised with the mace with great firmness. Even now, for filling Bhimasena, he jumps up and down.

sn: एनं चेन्न महाबाहुरन्यायेन हनिष्यति। एष वः कौरवो राजा धार्तराष्ट्रो भविष्यति॥ धनंजयस्तु श्रुत्वैतत् केशवस्य महात्मनः। प्रेक्षतो भीमसेनस्य सव्यमूरुमताडयत्॥
en: If the mighty-armed Bhima do not kill him unfairly, the son of Dhritarashtra will surely retain kingdom!?—Having heard those words of the great Keshava, Dhananjaya struck his own left thigh before the gaze of Bhimasena.

sn: गृह्य संज्ञां ततो भीमो गदया व्यचरद् रणे। मण्डलानि विचित्राणि यमकानीतराणि च॥
en: Understanding that sign, Bhima began to move about with his uplifted mace making many kinds of manoeuvres.

sn: दक्षिणं मण्डलं सव्यं गोमूत्रकमथापि च। व्यचरत् पाण्डवो राजन्नरिं सम्मोहयन्निव॥
en: Sometimes adopting the right Mandala, sometimes the left Mandala, and sometines Gomutraka, the son of Pandu began to move about, O king, stupefying his foe.

sn: तथैव तव पुत्रोऽपि गदामार्गविशारदः। व्यचरल्लघु चित्रं च भीमसेनजिघांसया॥
en: Likewise your son O king, who was an adept in the mace fight, moved about beautifully and with great activity, for killing Bhimasena.

sn: आधुन्वन्तो गदे घोरे चन्दनागरुरूषिते। वैरस्यान्तं परीप्सन्तौ रणे क्रुद्धाविवान्तकौ॥
en: Whirling their terrible maces which were smeared with sandal-paste and other unguents, the two heroes, desirous of terminating their hostilities, moved about in that battle like two angry Yamas.

sn: अन्योन्यं तौ जिघांसन्तौ प्रवीरौ पुरुषर्षभौ। युयुधाते गरुत्मन्तौ तथा नागामिषैषिणौ॥
en: Desirous of killing each other, those two best of men, possessed of great heroism, fought like two Garudas desirous of catching the same snake.

sn: मण्डलानि विचित्राणि चरतोपभीमयोः। गदासम्पातजास्तत्र प्रजजुः पावकार्चिषः॥
en: While the king and Bhima moved about in beautiful circles, their maces clashed, which created sparks of fire.

sn: समं प्रहरतोस्तत्र शूरयोर्बलिनोर्मधे। क्षुब्धयोर्वायुना राजन् द्वयोरिव समुद्रयोः॥
en: Those two heroic and powerful warriors struck each other equally in that battle. They then resembled, O king, two oceans agitated by the tempest.

sn: तयोः प्रहरतोस्तुल्यं मत्तकुञ्जरयोरिव। गदानिर्घातसंहादः प्रहाराणामजायत॥
en: Striking each other equally like two infuriate elephants, their clashing maces produced sounds like peals of thunder.

sn: तस्मिंस्तदा सम्प्रहारे दारुणे संकुले भृशम्। उभावपि परिश्रान्तौ युध्यमानावरिंदमौ॥
en: During the onset of that dreadful battle, both those chastisers of foes, while fight became exhausted.

sn: तौ मुहूर्तं समाश्वस्य पुनरेव परंतप। अभ्यहारयतां क्रुद्धो प्रगृह्य महती गदे॥
en: Having rested for a while, those two destroyers of foes, filled with rage and uplifting their maces, once more began to fight with each other.

sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं घोररूपमसंवृतम्। गदानिपातै राजेन्द्र तक्षतोः परस्परम्॥
en: When, O king, by the repeated falls of their maces, they wounded each other, the battle became exceedingly dreadful and perfectly unrestrained.

sn: समरे प्रद्रुतौ तौ तु वृषभाक्षौ तरस्विनौ। अन्योन्यं जनतुर्वीरौ पङ्कस्थौ महिषाविव॥
en: Rushing at each other in that fight, those two heroes, having eyes like those of bulls and gifted with great activity, struck each other fiercely like two buffaloes in the mire.

sn: जर्जरीकृतसर्वाङ्गौ रुधिरेणाभिसप्लुतौ। दद्दशाते हिमवति पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥
en: All their limbs wounded and bruised, and bathed in blood from head to foot, they looked like a couple of Kinshukas on the breast of Himavat.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तु पार्थेन विवरे सम्प्रदर्शिते। ईषदुन्मिषमाणस्तु सहसा प्रससार ह॥
en: During the onset of the fight, when : Vrikodara, seemed to give Duryodhana an opportunity, the latter, smiling a little, advanced forward.

sn: तमभ्याशगतं प्राज्ञो रणे प्रेक्ष्य वृकोदरः। अवाक्षिपद् गदां तस्मिन् वेगेन महता बली॥
en: Well-skilled in in battle, the powerful Vrikodara, seeing his adversary come up, suddenly hurled his mace at him.

sn: आक्षिपन्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते। अवासर्पत्ततः स्थानात् सा मोघा न्यपतद् भुवि॥
en: Seeing the mace thrown at him, your son, O king, moved away from that place at which the weapon fell down baffled.

sn: मोक्षयित्वा प्रहारं तं सुतस्तव सुसम्भ्रमात्। भीमसेनं त गदया प्राहरत् कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Having warded off that blow, your son, that foremost one of Kuru's race, quickly struck Bhimasena with his weapon.

sn: तस्य विस्यन्दमानेन रुधिरेणामितौजसः। प्रहारगुरुपाताच मूर्छव समजायत॥
en: A large quantity of blood being, drawn by that blow, as also owing to its violence, Bhimasena became stupefied.

sn: दुर्योधनो न तं वेद पीडितं पाण्डवं रणे। धारयामास भीमोऽपि शरीरमतिपीडितम्॥
en: Duryodhana, however, could not perceive that Pandu's son was so afflicted at that moment. Though deeply afflicted, Bhima kept himself, summoning all his patience.

sn: अमन्यत स्थितं ह्येनं प्रहरिष्यन्तमाहवे। अतो न प्राहरत् तस्मै पुनरेव तवात्मजः॥
en: Duryodhana, therefore, thought that he was all right and ready to return the blow. It was, therefore, that your son did not then strike him again.

sn: ततो मुहूर्तमाश्वस्य दुर्योधनमुपस्थितम्। वेगेनाभ्यपद् राजन् भीमसेनः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Having taken rest for a little while, the brave Bhimasena rushed furiously, O king, at Duryodhana who was standing near.

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य संरब्धममितौजसम्। मोघमस्य प्रहारं तं चिकीर्षुर्भरतर्षभ॥ अवस्थाने मतिं कृत्वा पुत्रस्तव महामनाः। इयेषोत्पतितुं राजञ्छलयिष्यन् वृकोदरम्॥
en: Seeing the energetic Bhimasena, filled with rage and rushing towards him your high-souled so, O Bharata's chief, desiring to thwart his blow, thought of showing the manoeuvre called Avasthana. He, therefore, desired to jump upwards, O king, king, for beguiling Vrikodara.

sn: अबुद्ध्यद् भीमसेनस्तु राज्ञस्तस्य चिकीर्षितम्। अथास्य समभिद्रुत्य समुत्क्रुश्य च सिंहवत्॥ सृत्या वञ्चयतो राजन् पुनरेवोत्पतिष्यतः। ऊरुभ्यां प्राहिणोद् राजन् गदां वेगेन पाण्डवः॥
en: Bhimasena fully understood the object of his opponent. Rushing at him, with a loud leonine roar, he fiercely dropped his mace at the thighs of the Kuru king, as the latter had jumped up for making the first aim useless.

sn: सा वज्रनिष्पेषसमा प्रहिता भीमकर्मणा। ऊरू दुर्योधनस्याथ बभञ्ज प्रियदर्शनौ॥
en: That mace, strong, like thunder and hurled by Bhima broke the two handsome thighs of Duryodhana.

sn: स पपात नरव्याघ्रो वसुधामनुनादयन्। भग्नोरुर्भीमसेनेन पुत्रस्तव महीपते॥
en: That foremost of men, viz., your son after his thighs had been broken by Bhimasena, fell down resounding the Earth.

sn: ववुर्वाताः सनिर्धाताः पांशुवर्षं पपात च। चचाल पृथिवी चापि सवृक्षापपर्वता॥
en: Fierce winds began to blow, with loud sounds, Showers of dust dropped. The Earth, with her trees and mountains, began to tremble.

sn: तस्मिन् निपतिते वीरे पत्यौ सर्वमहीक्षिताम्। महास्वना पुनर्दीप्ता सनिर्घाता भयंकरी॥ पपात चोल्का महती पतिते पृथिवीपतौ।
en: Upon the fall of that hero who was the head of all kings, fierce and fiery winds blew with a loud noise and with thunder falling frequently. When that lord of Earth fell, large meteors dropped down from the welkin.

sn: तथा शोणितवर्षं च पांशुवर्षं च भारत॥ ववर्ष मघवांस्तत्र तव पुत्रे निपातिते।
en: Bloody and dusty showers, fell, O Bharata! These were poured by Indra, upon the fall of your son.

sn: यक्षाणां राक्षसानां च पिशाचानां तथैव च॥ अन्तरिक्षे महानादः श्रूयते भतरर्षभ।
en: A loud noise was heard, O Bharata's chief, in the sky, caused by the Yakshas, Rakshasas and the Pishachas.

sn: तेन शब्देन घोरेण मृगाणामथ पक्षिणाम्॥ जज्ञे घोरतरः शब्दो बहूनां सर्वतोदिशम्।
en: At the terrible sound thousands of beasts and birds began to yell hideously on every side.

sn: ये तत्र वाजिनः शेषा गजाश्च मनुजैः सह॥ मुमुचुस्ते महानादं तव पुत्रे निपातिते। भेरीशङ्खमृदङ्गानामभवच स्वनो महान्॥
en: Those horses, elephants and men, forming the remnant of the Pandava's army, urtered loud cried when your son fell. Loud blare of conchs and the peal of drums and cymbals were heard.

sn: अन्तर्भूमिगतश्चैव तव पुत्रे निपातिते। बहुपादैर्बहुभुजैः कबन्धै?रदर्शनैः॥ नृत्यद्भिर्भयदैाप्ता दिशस्तत्राभवन् नृप।
en: A terrific noise seemed to come from the very bowels of the earth. Upon the fall of your son, O king, headless beings or dreadful appearance, possessed of many legs and many arms, and striking terror to all creatures, began to dance and cover the earth on all sides.

sn: ध्वजवन्तोऽस्त्रवन्तश्च शस्त्रवन्तस्तथैव च॥ प्राकम्पन्त ततो राजंस्तव पुत्रे निपातिते।
en: Warriors, O king, who stood with standards or weapons in their arms, began to tremble, O king, when your son fell.

sn: ह्रदाः कूपाश्च रुधिरमुढेमुपसत्तम॥ नद्यश्च सुमहावेगाः प्रतिस्रोतोवहाऽभवन्।
en: Lakes and wells, O best of kings, vomited forth blood. Swift coursing rivers flowed in opposite directions.

sn: पुंल्लिङ्गा इव नार्यस्तु स्त्रीलिङ्गाः पुरुषाभवन्॥ दुर्योधने तदा राजन् पतिते तनये तव।
en: Women seemed to look like men, and men like women, when your son Duryodhana fell.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तानद्भुतोत्पातान् पञ्चालाः पाण्डवैः सह॥ आविग्नमनसः सर्वे बभूवुर्भरतर्षभ।
en: Seeing those wonderful portents, Panchalas and the Pandavas, O Bharata's chief, were filled with anxiety.

sn: ययुर्देवा यथाकामं गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्तथा॥ कथयन्तोऽद्भुतं युद्धं सुतयोस्तव भारत।
en: The gods and Gandharvas went away to their wished-for regions, taking and discoursing on that wonderful battle between your sons.

sn: तथैव सिद्धा राजेन्द्र तथा वातिकचारणाः। नरसिंहौ प्रशंसन्तौ विप्रजग्मुर्यथागतम्॥
en: Similarly the Siddhas and the quickcoursing Charanas went to those places from which they had come, praising these two best of men. Inc

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: संजय उवाच तं पातितं ततो दृष्ट्वा महाशालमिवोद्गतम्। प्रहृष्टमनसः सर्वे दद्दशुस्तत्र पाण्डवाः॥ उन्मत्तमिव मातङ्ग सिंहेन विनिपातितम्। दद्दशुर्हष्टरोमाण: सर्वे ते चापि सोमकाः॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing Duryodhana struck down on Earth like a gigantic Shala uprooted by the storm, the Pandavas were filled with delight. The Somakas also saw, with their hair standing erect, the Kuru king felled upon the Earth, like an infuriate clephant felled by a lion.

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: ततो दुर्योधनं हत्वा भीमसेनः प्रतापवान्। पातितं कौरवेन्द्र तमुपगम्येदमब्रवीत्॥ गौगौरिति पुरा मन्द द्रौपदीमेकवाससम्। यत् सभायां हसन्नस्मांस्तदा वदसि दुर्मते॥ तस्यावहासस्य फलमद्य त्वं समवाप्नुहि। एवमुक्त्वा स वामेन पदा मौलिमुपास्पृशत्॥ शिरश्च राजसिंहस्य पादेन समलोडयत्।
en: Having struck Duryodhana down the brave Bhimasena, approaching the Kuru chief, addressed him, saying-O wretch, formerly laughing at Draupadi who had no cloth in the midst of the assembly, you, O fool, called us Cows. Bear now the consequences of that insult. Saying so, he struck the head of his fallen foe, with his left foot. Indeed, he struck the head of that best of kings with his foot.

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: तथैवः क्रोधसंरक्तो भीमः परबलार्दनः॥ पुनरेवाब्रवीद् वाक्यं यत् तच्छृणु नराधिप येऽस्मान् पुरोपनृत्यन्त मूढा गौरिति गौरिति॥ तान् वयं प्रतिनृत्यामः पुनर्गौरिति गौरिति। नास्माकं निकृतिर्वह्नि क्षयूतं न वञ्चना। स्वबाहुबलमाश्रित्य प्रबाधामो वयं रिपून्॥ सोऽवाप्य वैरस्य परस्य पारं वृकोदरः प्राह शनैः प्रहस्या युधिष्ठिरं केशवसंजयांश्च धनंजयं माद्रवतीसुतौ च॥
en: With eyes reddened in wrath, Bhimascna, that grinder of hostile armies, once more said these words. Listen to thein, O king, we will now dance and call them Cows!-who formerly insulted us by calling us so. We have no deceipt, no fire, no match at dice, no deception! Depending upon the strength of our own arins we our resist and check foes!-Having brought those fierce hostilities to a close, Vrikodara once more slowly and laughingly said these words unto Yudhisthira and Keshava and the Shrinjayas and Dhananjaya and the two sons of Madri.

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: रजस्वला द्रौपदीमानयन् ये ये चाप्यकुर्वन्त सदस्यवस्त्राम्। तान् पश्यध्वं पाण्डवैर्धार्तराष्ट्रान् रणे हतांस्तपसा याज्ञसेन्याः॥
en: Let them who had dragged Draupadi, while she was in her period, into the assembly, and had made her necked there, behold those Dhartarashtras slain in battle by the Pandavas through the ascetic penances of Yajnasena's daughter.

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: ये नः पुरा षण्ढतिलानवोचन् क्रूरा राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः। ते नो हताः सगणाः सानुबन्धाः कामं स्वर्ग नरकं वा पतामः॥ पुनश्च राज्ञः पतितस्य भूमौ स तां गदां स्कन्धगतां प्रगृह्या वामेन पादेन शिरः प्रमृद्य दुर्योधनं नैकृतिकं न्यवोचत्॥
en: Those wicked sons of king Dhritarashtra who had called us Sessame seeds without kernel, have all been killed by us with their relatives and followers! It is a matter of no consequence wivether we go to heaven or hell!-Once more, uplifting the mace that was on his shoulders he struck with his left, foot the head of the king who was lying on Earth, and addressing the deceitful Duryodhana said,

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: हृष्टेन राजन् कुरुसत्तमस्य क्षुद्रात्मना भीमसेनेन पादम्। दृष्ट्वा कृतं मूर्धनि नाभ्यनन्दन् धर्मात्मानः सोमकानां प्रबर्हाः॥
en: Seeing the foot of the rejoicing but mean Bhimasena placed upon the head of that foremost one Kuru's race, many of the leading warriors among the Somakas did not a all approve of it.

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: तव पुत्रं तथा हत्वा कत्थमानं वृकोदरम्। नृत्यमानं च बहुशो धर्मराजोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ गतोऽसि वैरस्यानृण्यं प्रतिज्ञा पूरिता त्वया। शुभेनाथाशुभेनैव कर्मणा विरमाधुना॥
en: After having stuck down your son, while Vrikodara was thus vaunting and dancing madly, king Yudhisthira said to him-You have wreaked your vengeance (on Duryodhana) and gained your ends by means fair or foul! Cease now, O Bhiima.

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: मा शिरोऽस्य पदा मार्दीर्मा धर्मस्तेऽतिगो भवेत्। राजा ज्ञातिर्हतश्चायं नैतन्त्र्याय्यं तवानघ॥
en: Do not crush his head with your foot! Do not act sinfully! Duryodhana is a king! He is, again, your kinsman! He is fallen! Your conduct, O sinless one, is not becoming.

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: एकादशचमूनाथं कुरूणामधिपं तथा। मा स्पाक्षी म पादेन राजानं ज्ञातिमेव च॥
en: Duryodhana was the lord of eleven Akshauhinis of troops. He was the king of the Kurus! Do not, O Bhima, strike a king and a kinsman with your foot!

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: हतबन्धुर्हतामात्यो भ्रष्टसैन्यो हतो मृधे। सर्वाकारेण शोच्योऽयं नावहास्योऽयमीश्वरः॥
en: His relatives are killed! His friends and counsellors are all slain! His troops have been destroyed! He has been struck down in battle! He is to be pitied in every respect! He deserves not to be insulted, of remember that he is a king!

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: विध्वस्तोऽयं हतामात्यो हतभ्राता हतप्रजः। उत्सन्नपिण्डो भ्राता च नैतन्याय्यं कृतं त्वया।॥
en: He is ruined! His friends and kinsmen have been killed! His brothers have been slain! His sons too have bcen killed! His funeral cake has been taken away! He is our brother! Your conduct towards him is not proper!

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: धार्मिको भीमसेनोऽसावित्याहुस्त्वां पुरा जनाः। स कस्माद् भीमसेन त्वं राजानमधितिष्ठसि॥ इत्युक्त्वा भीमसेनं तु साश्रुकण्ठो युधिष्ठिरः। उपसृत्याब्रवीद् दीनो दुर्योधनमरिंदमम्॥ तात मन्युन ते कार्यो नात्मा शोच्यस्त्वया तथा। नूनं पूर्वकृतं कर्म सुघोरमनुभूयते॥
en: Bhimasena is a righteous man! People used to say this before of thee! Why then, O Bhimasena, do you insult the king in this way?' Saying this to Bhimasena, Yudhishthira, with voice suppressed with tears, and afflicted with sorrows approached Duryodhana, and said to him. 'O brother, you should not give way to anger nor grieve for yourself! Forsooth, you suffer the dreadful consequences of your own former acts!

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: धात्रोपदिष्टं विषमं नूनं फलमसंस्कृतम्। यद् वयं त्वां जिघांसामस्त्वं चास्मान् कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Forsooth, this sad and woeful result had been ordained by the Creator himself, viz., that we should harm you and you should injure us, Oforemost one of Kuru's race!

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: आत्मनो ह्यपराधेन महद् व्यसनमीदृशम्। प्राप्तवानसि यल्लोभान्मदाद् बाल्याच भारत॥
en: Through thy own fault, avarice and pride and folly this great calamity has befallen you, OBharata!

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: घातयित्वा वयस्यांश्च भ्रातूनथ पितूंस्तथा। पुत्रान् पौत्रांस्तथा चान्यांस्ततोऽसि निधनं गतः॥
en: Having brought about the death of your companions and brothers and sires and sons and grandsons and others you now meet with your own death!

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: तवापराधदस्माभिर्धातरस्ते निपातिताः। निहता ज्ञातयश्चापि दिष्टं मन्ये दुरत्ययम्॥
en: For your folly your brothers, mighty carwarriors all, and your kinsmen, have been killed by us! I think all this is the work of irresistible Destiny!

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: आत्मा न शोचनीयस्ते श्लाघ्यो मृत्युस्तवानघ। वयमेवाधुना शोच्याः सर्वावस्थासु कौरव॥ । कृपणं वर्तयिष्यामस्तैींना बन्धुभिः प्रियैः।
en: You are not to be pitied! On the other hand, your death, O sinless one, is enviable! It is we that are objects of pity, O Kaurava! We shall have to carry on a miserable existence, shorn of all our dcar friends and kinsmen!

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: भ्रातृणां चैव पुत्राणां तथा वै शोकविह्वला:॥ कथं द्रक्ष्यामि विधवा वधूः शोकपरिप्लुताः।
en: Alas, how shall I see the widows, of my brothers and sons and grandsons, all overwhelmed with grief and stricken down with sorrow.

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: त्वमेकः सुस्थितो राजन् स्वर्गे ते निलयो ध्रुवः॥ वयं नरकसंज्ञं वै दुःखं प्राप्स्याम दारुणम्।
en: You are, O king, departing from this world! You will surely go to heaven! We are, on the other hand, creatures of hell, and shall continue to suffer the bitterest grief?

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: स्नुषाश्च प्रस्नुषाश्चैव धृतराष्ट्रस्य विह्वलाः। गर्हयिष्यन्ति नो नूनं विधवाः शोककर्शिताः॥
en: The wives of Dhritarashtra's sons and grandsons stricken with grief will, forsooth, curse us all!'

description: Bhima tries to crush Duryodhana's head with his foot and Yudhishthira prevents him
sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा सुदुःखार्तो निशश्वास स पार्थिवः। विललाप चिरं चापि धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Saying these words, Dharma's Yudhishthira, deeply afflicted with grief, began to sigh heavily and bewail." son

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अधर्मेण हतं दृष्ट्वा राजानं माधवोत्तमः। किमब्रवीत् तदा सूत बलदेवो महाबलः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said “Seeing the (Kuru) king struck dawn unfairly, what, O charioteer did the powerful Baladeva, that Madhu's chief, say.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: गदायुद्धविशेषज्ञो गदायुद्धविशारदः। कृतवान् रौहिणेयो यत् तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: “Tell me, O Sanjaya, what Rohini's son, well-skilled in mace encounters and well acquainted with all its rules did on that occasion!"

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: संजय उवाच शिरस्यभिहतं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनेन ते सुतम्। रामः प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठश्चक्रोध बलवद्वली॥
en: Sanjaya said "Secing your son struck at the thighs, the powerful Rama, that best of smiters, became highly angry.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: ततो मध्ये नरेन्द्राणामूर्ध्वबाहुर्हलायुधः। कुर्वन्नार्तस्वरं घोरं धिग् भीमेत्युवाच ह॥
en: Raising his arms up, the hero having the plough for his weapon, sorrowfully said in the midst of those kings-'Oh, fie on Bhima, fie on Bhima.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: अहो धिग् यदधो नाभेः प्रहृतं धर्मविग्रहे। नैतद् दृष्टं गदायुद्धे कृतवान् यद् वृकोदरः॥
en: Oh, fie, that in such a fair fight a blow has been inflicted below the navel! Never before has such an act, as has been done by Vrikodara, been seen in an encounter with the mace!

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: अधो नाभ्यां न हन्तव्यमिति शास्त्रस्य निश्चयः। अयं त्वशास्त्रविन्मूढः स्वच्छन्दात् सम्प्रवर्तते॥
en: No limb below the navel should be struck. This is the rule laid down in treatises! Bhima, however, is an ignorant wretch, unacquainted with the code of war! He, therefore, acted as he likes.'

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: तस्य तत्तद् ब्रुवाणस्य रोषः समभवन्महान्। ततो राजानमालोक्य रोषसंरक्तलोचनः॥ बलदेवो महाराज ततो वचनमब्रवीत्।
en: Uttering these words, Rama became very angry. Seeing on Duryodhana he became with reddened eyed and said these words:

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: न चैष पतितः कृष्ण केवलं मत्समोऽसमः॥ आश्रित्य तु दौर्बल्यादाश्रयः परिभर्यते। ततो लागलमुद्यम्य भीममभ्यद्रवद् बली॥
en: (Baladeva then replied-) O Sri Krishna! King Duryodhana was mighty not any way less than me. Nobody here was able to face him in war with mace. Fall of Duryodhana unjust way or by tactics has humiliated me also, the shelterer is being condemned/insulted owing to defects in the person sheltered.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: तमुत्पतन्तं जग्राह केशवो विनयान्वितः। बाहुभ्यां पीनवृत्ताभ्यां प्रयत्नाद् बलवद्वली॥
en: The powerful Keshava, however, ever bending with humility, caught the rushing Rama, with his massive and well-formed arms.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: सितासितौ यदुवरौ शुशुभातेऽधिकं तदा। नभोगतौ यथा राजश्चन्द्रसूर्यो दिनक्षये॥ तस्योर्ध्वबाहोः सदृशं रूपमासीन्महात्मनः। बहुधातुविचित्रस्य श्वेतस्येव महागिरेः॥
en: Those two Yadu heroes, the one dark in complexion and the other fair, shone exceedingly beautiful at that moment, like the Sun and the Moon, The great warrior with uplifted arms appeared like the huge mountain of Kailasa variegated with various kinds of metals.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: उवाच चैनं संरब्धं शमयन्निव केशवः। आत्मवृद्धिर्मित्रवृद्धिर्मित्रमित्रोदयस्तथा॥ विपरीतं द्विषत्स्वेतत् षड्विधा वृद्धिरात्मनः। आत्मन्यपि च मित्रे च विपरीतं यदा भवेत्॥
en: For pacifying the angry Rama, Keshava addressed him, saying, "There are six sorts of advancement that a person may scek, viz., one's own advancement, the advancement of one's friends' the destruction of one enemy, the destruction of one's enemy's friends, and the destruction of one's enemy's friends' friends.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: तदा विद्यान्मनोग्लानिमाशु शान्तिकरो भवेत्। अस्माकं सहजं मित्रं पाण्डवाः शुद्धपौरुषाः॥
en: When misfortunes befall one's own self or one's friends, it is a sign that one's fall is near, and, therefore, one should at such times seek for the remedy.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: स्वकाः पितृष्वसुः पुत्रास्ते परैनिकृता भृशम्। प्रतिज्ञापालनं धर्मः क्षत्रियस्येह वेम्यहम्॥
en: The Pandavas are our natural friends. They are the children of our own father's sister! They had been greatly assailed by their enemies.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: सुयोधनस्य गदया भक्ताम्यूरू महाहवे। इति पूर्वं प्रतिज्ञातं भीमेन हि सभातले॥
en: The fulfillment of one's promise is one's duty. Formerly Bhima had promised in the midst of the assembly that he would in great battle break with his mace the thighs of Duryodhana.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: मैत्रैयेणाभिशप्तश्च पूर्वमेव महर्षिणा। ऊरू ते भेत्स्यते भीमो गदयेति परंतप॥
en: The great Rishi Maitreya also had formerly imprecated Duryodhana, saying, Bhima will, with his mace, break your thighs.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: अतो दोषं न पश्यामि मा क्रुद्ध्यस्व प्रलम्बहन्। यौनः स्वैः सुखहादैच सम्बन्धः सह पाण्डवैः॥
en: For all this, I do not see any fault in Bhima! Do not yield to anger, O slayer of Pralamba! Our relationship with the Pandavas is based on birth, blood and love.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: तेषां वृद्ध्यां हि वृद्धिों मा क्रुधः पुरुषर्षभ। वासुदेववचः श्रुत्वा सीरभृत् प्राह धर्मवित्॥ धर्मः सुचरितः सद्भिः स च द्वाभ्यां नियच्छति। अर्थश्चात्यर्थलुब्धस्य कामश्चातिप्रसङ्गिणः॥
en: On their advancement depends our own. Do not, therefore, give away to anger, O foremost of men!'-Hearing these words of Vasudeva the wielder of the plough, who was well read in the Ethical lore, said, 'Morality is always followed by the good. Morality is always followed by two motives, viz., the desire for Profit cherished by those that follow it, or the desire for Pleasure.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: धर्मार्थो धर्मकामौ च कामार्थो चाप्यपीडयन्। धर्मार्थकामान् योऽभ्येति सोऽत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते॥
en: Whoever, without making distinction between Morality and Profit, or Morality and Pleasure, or Pleasure and Profit, follows all three, viz., Morality, Profit and Pleasure, always succeeds in obtaining great happiness.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: तदिदं व्याकुलं सर्वं कृतं धर्मस्य पीडनात्। भीमसेने न गोविन्द कामं तु यथाऽऽत्य माम्॥
en: It is because Bhimasena, has deviated from morality this harmony, of which I have spoken, has been disturbed, Inspite, O Govinda, of all your arguments to me!'

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच अरोषणो हि धर्मात्मा सततं धर्मवत्सलः। भवान् प्रख्यायते लोके तस्मात् संशाम्य मा क्रुधः॥२४
en: Krishna replied, saying-You are always described as shorn of wrath, and devoted to righteousness! Pacify yourself, therefore, and do not yield to wrath!

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: प्राप्तं कलियुगं विद्धि प्रतिज्ञां पाण्डवस्य च। आनृण्यं यातु वैरस्य प्रतिज्ञायाश्च पाण्डवः॥
en: Know that the Kali age is at hand. Remember also the promise made by the son of Pandu! Let, therefore, the son of Pandu be regarded to have requited the debt he owed to his enemy and to have carried out his promise."

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: संजय उवाच धर्मच्छलमपि श्रुत्वा केशवात् स विशाम्पते। नैव प्रीतमना रामो वचनं प्राह संसदि॥ हत्वाऽधर्मेण राजानं धर्मात्मानं सुयोधनम्। जिह्मयोधीते लोकेऽस्मिन् ख्याति यास्यति पाण्डवः॥
en: Sanjaya continued "Hearing this fallacious argument from Keshava, O king, Rama failed to remove his anger and become cheerful. He then said in that assembly, having unfairly killed the righteous king Suyodhana, the son of Pandu shall be known in the world as a wily warrior.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: दुर्योधनोऽपि धर्मात्मा गतिं यास्यति शाश्वतीम्। ऋजुयोधी हतो राजा धार्तराष्ट्रो नराधिपः॥
en: The righteous Duryodhana, on the other hand, shall acquire cternal blessedness! Dhritarashtra's royal son, who has been struck down, is a fair warrior!

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: युद्धदीक्षां प्रविश्याजौ रणयज्ञं वितत्य च। हुत्वाऽऽत्मानममित्राग्नौ प्राप चावभृथं यशः॥
en: Having made all possible arrangements for the Sacrifice of battle, and having performed the initiatory rites on the field, and lastly, having poured his life as a libation upon the fire of foes, Duryodhana had duly completed his Sacrifice by the final ablutions of glory!"

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: इत्युक्त्वा रथमास्थाय रौहिणेयः प्रतापवान्। श्वेताभ्रशिखराकारः प्रययौ द्वारकां प्रति॥
en: Having said these words, the brave son of Rohini, looking like a white cloud, got upon his chariot and went towards Dwaraka.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: पञ्चालाश्च सवार्ष्णेयाः पाण्डवाश्च विशाम्पते। रामे द्वारावतीं याते नातिप्रमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: The Panchalas, the Vrishnis and the Pandavas. O king, became rather dispirited after Rama had started for Dvaravati.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरं दीनं चिन्तापरमधोमुखम्। शोकोपहतसंकल्पं वासुदेवोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Then approaching Yudhishthira, who was exceedingly melancholy and anxious, and who hung down his head and knew not what to do in the great affliction of his heart, Vasudeva, said to him these words.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: वासुदेव उवाच धर्मराज किमर्थं त्वमधर्ममनुमन्यसे। हतबन्धोर्यदेतस्य पतितस्य विचेतसः॥ दुर्योधनस्य भीमेन मृद्यमानं शिरः पदा। उपप्रेक्षसि कस्मात् त्वं धर्मज्ञः सन्नराधिप।॥
en: Vasudeva said O Yudhishthira why do you allow such a wrong act, since you suffer the head of the insensible and fallen Duryodhana whose relatives and friends have all been killed to be thus struck by Bhima with his foot? conversant as thou art with the rules of Ethics, why do you, O king, look at this act with indifference?'

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच न ममैतत् प्रियं कृष्ण यद् राजानं वृकोदरः। पदा मूर्ध्यस्पृशत् क्रोधान्न हृष्ये कुलक्षये॥
en: Yudhishthira answered This act, O Krishna, of Vrikodara's angrily touching the head of the king with his foot, is not pleasant to me, nor am I glad at this extermination of my race!

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: निकृत्या निकृता नित्यं धृतराष्ट्रसुतैर्वयम्। बहूनि परुषाण्युक्त्वा वनं प्रस्थापिताः स्म ह॥
en: By gujle were we always imposed on by the sons of Dhritarastra! They spoke many harsh words to us. We were again exiled into the forest by them.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: भीमसेनस्य तद् दुःखमतीव हदि वर्तते। इति संचिन्त्य वार्ष्णेय मयैतत् समुपेक्षितम्॥
en: On account of all those acts great grief exists in Bhimasena's heart! Thinking of all this, O hero of the Vrishnis's race, I looked on with indifference!

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: तस्माद्धत्वाऽकृतप्रज्ञं लुब्धं कामवशानुगम्। लभतां पाण्डवः कामं धर्मेऽधर्मे च वा कृते॥
en: Having killed the covetous, foolish and passionate Duryodhana, let the son of Pandu satisfy his desire, be it by means fair or foul.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: संजय उवाच इत्युक्ते धर्मराजेन वासुदेवोऽब्रवीदिदम्। काममस्त्वेतदिति वै कृच्छ्राद् यदुकुलोद्वहः॥ इत्युक्तो वासुदेवेन भीमप्रियहितैषिणा। अन्वमोदत तत् सर्वं यद् भीमेन कृतं युधि॥ भीमसेनोऽपि हत्वाऽऽजौ तव पुत्रममर्षणः। अभिवाद्याग्रतः स्थित्वा सम्प्रहृष्टः कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: Sanjaya continued After Yudhishthira had said this, Vasudeva, said with difficulty-Let it be so! After Vasudeva had been addressed in those words by Yudhishthira, the former, who, always wished what was pleasant to, and beneficial for, Bhima, insooth, approved all those acts that Bhima had done in battle. Having struck down your son in battle, the wrathful Bhimasena, his heart overflowing with joy, stood with joined hands before Yudhishthira and saluted him duly.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: प्रोवाच सुमहातेजा धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। हर्षादुत्फुल्लनयनो जितकाशी विशाम्पते॥ तवाद्य पृथिवी सर्वा क्षेमा निहतकण्टका। तां प्रशाधि महाराज स्वधर्ममनुपालय॥
en: With eyes expanded in joy and proud of the victory he had acquired, the energetic Vrikodara, O king, said to his eldest brother, saying-'The Earth belongs to-day to you, O king, without quarrels to disturb her and with all her thorns gone! Govern her, O king, and observe the duties of your order.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: यस्तु कर्ताऽस्य वैरस्य निकृत्या निकृतिप्रियः। सोऽयं विनिहतः शेते पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपते॥
en: He, who was the root of these hostilities, and who fomented them by means of his wiliness, that wretched being, lies struck down, on the bare ground, O lord of Earth.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: दुःशासनप्रभृतयः सर्वे ते चोग्रवादिनः। राधेयः शकुनिश्चैव हताश्च तव शत्रवः॥
en: All those wretched led by Dusshasana, who used to utter cruel words, as also those other enemies of yours, viz., the son of Radha, and Shakuni, have been killed.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: सेयं रत्नसमाकीर्णा मही सवनपर्वता। उपावृत्ता महाराज त्वामद्य निहतद्विषम्॥
en: Filled with all sorts of gems, the Earth, with her forests and mountains, O king, once more approaches you who have no foes alive.'

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच गतो वैरस्य निधनं हतो राजा सुयोधनः। कृष्णस्य मतमास्थाय विजितेयं वसुन्धरा॥
en: Yudhishthira said Hostilities have been closed! King Suyodhana has been struck down! The Earth has been conquered (by us), under the advice of Krishna.

description: The anger of Rama at seeing the unfair fight. Krishna pacifies him
sn: दिष्ट्या गतस्त्वमानृण्यं मातु: कोपस्य चोभयोः। दिष्ट्या जयति दुर्धर्ष दिष्ट्या शत्रुर्निपातितः॥
en: By good luck, you had paid off your debt to your mother and to your wrath! By good luck, you have been victorious, O invincible hero, and by good luck, your enemy has been killed.'

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच हतं दुर्योधनं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनेन संयुगे। पाण्डवाः सृञ्जयाश्चैव किमकुर्वत संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said “Secing Duryodhana struck down in battle by Bhimasena, what, O Sanjaya did the Pandavas and the Srinjayas do?"

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच हतं दुर्योधनं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनेन संयुगे। सिंहेनेव महाराज मत्तं वनगजं यथा॥ प्रहृष्टमनसस्तत्र कृष्णेन सह पाण्डवाः। पञ्चाला सृञ्जयाश्चैव निहते कुरुनन्दने॥ आविद्ध्यन्नुत्तरीयाणि सिंहनादांश्च नेदिरे। नैतान् हर्षसमाविष्टानियं सेहे वसुंधरा॥
en: Sanjaya said “Seeing Duryodhana killed by Bhimasena in battle, O king, like a wild elephant slain by a lion the Pandavas with Krishna were filled with joy upon the fall of the Kuru king. The Panchalas and the Shrinjayas also waved their upper garments in the air) and sent up leonine roars. Even the Earth could not bear those rejoicing warriors.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: धनूंष्यन्ते व्याक्षिपन्त ज्याश्चाप्यन्ये तथाऽक्षिपन्। दध्मुरन्ये महाशङ्खानन्ये जघ्नुश्च दुन्दुभीन्॥
en: Some stretched their bows; others drew their bowstrings. Some blew their huge conchs; other beat their drums.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: चिक्रीडुश्च तथैवान्ये जहसुश्च तवाहिताः। अब्रुवंश्चासकृद् वीरा भीमसेनमिदं वचः॥ दुष्करं भवता कर्म रणेऽद्य सुमहत् कृतम्। कौरवेन्द्रं रणे हत्वा गदयाऽतिकृतश्रमम्॥ इन्द्रेणेव हि वृत्रस्य वधं परमसंयुगे। त्वया कृतममन्यन्त शत्रोर्वधमिमं जनाः॥
en: Some sported and juinped about others laughed aloud. Many heroes repeatedly said these words to Bhimasena— 'Highly difficult and great has been the feat that you have performed to-day in batile, by having struck down thc Kuru king, himself a great warrior, with your macc! This slaughter of your enemy is considered like that of Vritra by Indra himself!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: चरन्तं विविधान् मार्गान् मण्डलानि च सर्वशः। दुर्योधनमिमं शूरं कोऽन्यो हन्याद् वृकोदरात्॥
en: Who else, but you, O Vrikodara, could kill the heroic Duryodhana while moving about in various ways and performing various manoeuvres.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: वैरस्य च गतः पारं त्वमिहान्यैः सुदुर्गमम्। अशक्यमेतदन्येन सम्पादयितुमीदृशम्॥
en: You have brought these hostilities, to a close which none could do! This feat of yours is incapable of being done by any other warrior!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: कुञ्जरेणेव मत्तेन वीर संग्राममूर्धनि। दुर्योधनशिरो दिष्ट्या पादेन मृदितं त्वया॥
en: By good luck, you have, O hero, like an infuriate elephant, crushed with your foot the head of Duryodhana on the field of battle!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: सिंहेन महिषस्येव कृत्वा सङ्गरमुत्तमम्। दुःशासनस्य रुधिरं दिष्ट्या पीतं त्वयानघ॥
en: By good luck, O sinless one, you have quaffed the blood of Dussasana on the field of battle!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: ये विप्रकुर्वन् राजान् धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। मूर्ध्नि तेषां कृतः पादो दिष्ट्या ते स्वेन कर्मणा॥
en: By good luck, you have by your own energy, placed your foot on the head of all those that had injured the just king Yudhishthira!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: अमित्राणामधिष्ठानाद् वधाद् दुर्योधनस्य च। भीम दिष्ट्या पृथिव्यां ते प्रथितं सुमहद् यशः॥
en: For your having defeated the foes and having slain Duryodhana, by good luck, O Bhima, your fame has extended over the whole world.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: एवं नूनं हते वृत्रे शक्रं नन्दन्ति बन्दिनः। तथा त्वां निहतामित्रं वयं नन्दाम भारत॥
en: Bards and eulogists praised Shakra after the fall of Vritra as we are now applauding you, O Bharata, after the fall of your foes.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधनवधे यानि रोमाणि हृषितानि नः। अद्यापि न विकृष्यन्ते तानि तद् विद्धि भारत॥ इत्यब्रुवन् भीमसेनं वातिकास्तत्र सङ्गताः।
en: Know O Bharata, that the joy we felt upon the fall of Duryodhana has not yet decreased the least.' The assembled eulogists on that occasion addressed to Bhimasena these words,

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: तान् हृष्टान् पुरुषव्याघ्रान् पञ्चालान् पाण्डवैः सह।। १७ ब्रुवतोऽसदृशं तत्र प्रोवाच मधुसूदनः। न न्याय्यं निहतं शत्रु भूयो हन्तुं नराधिपाः॥ असकृद् वाग्भिरुयाभिनिहतो होष मन्दधीः।
en: Whilst, viz., Panchalas and the Pandavas, all filled with joy were thus expressing themselves, the slayer of Madhu addressed them, saying-Ye kings, it is not becoming to kill a slain fe with such cruel words repeatedly. This wicked man has already been slain.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: तदैवैष हतः पापो यदैव निरपत्रपः॥ लुब्धः पापसहायश्च सुहृदां शासनातिगः। बहुशो विदुरद्रोणकृपगाङ्गेयसंजयैः॥ पाण्डुभ्यः प्रार्थ्यमानोऽपि पित्र्यमंशं न दत्तवान्।
en: This sinful, shameless, and covetous wretch, surrounded by sinful counsellors and ever malignant of the advice of wise friends, encountered his death even then when he refused, though repeatedly urged to the contrary by Vidura, Drona, Kripa and Sanjaya, to give to the sons of Pandu their paternal share in the kingdom which thcy had begged of him.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: नैष योग्योऽद्य मित्रं वा शत्रुर्वा पुरुषाधमः॥ किमनेनातिभुग्नेन वाग्भिः काष्ठसधर्मणा।
en: This wretch is not to be regarded either as a friend or an enemy! What use in using harsh words to him who has now become a piece of wood.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: रथेष्वारोहत क्षिप्रं गच्छामो वसुधाधिपाः॥ दिष्ट्या हतोऽयं पापात्मा सामात्यज्ञातिबान्धवः। इति श्रुत्वा त्वधिक्षेपं कृष्णाद् दुर्योधनो नृपः॥ अमर्षवशमापन्न उदतिष्ठद् विशाम्पते। स्फिग्देशेनोपविष्टः स दो• विष्टभ्य मेदिनीम्॥
en: Get your cars quickly, you kings, for we should leave this place! By good luck, this sinful wretch has been killed with his counsellors and kinsmen and friends. Thus chastised by Krishna, king Duryodhana, O king, gave way to wrath and endeavoured to rise.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: दृष्टिं भूसङ्कटां कृत्वा वासुदेवो न्यपातयत्। अोन्नतशरीरस्य रूपमासीनृपस्य तु॥
en: Sitting on his haunches and supporting himself on his two arms, he contracted his eyebrows and looked angrily at Vasudeva.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: क्रुद्धस्याशीविषस्येव च्छिन्नपुच्छस्य भारत। प्राणान्तकरिणी घोरां वेदनामप्यचिन्तयन्॥
en: Duryodhana whose body was half raised, looked like a poisonous snake, O Bharata, shorn of its tail.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधनो वासुदेवं वाग्भिरुग्राभिरार्दयत्। कंसदासस्य दायाद न ते लज्जाऽस्त्यनेन वै॥ अधर्मेण गदायुद्धे यदहं विनिपातितः। ऊरू भिन्धीति भीमस्य स्मृति मिथ्या प्रयच्छता॥ किं न विज्ञातमेतन्मे यदर्जुनमवोचथाः।
en: Forgetting his poignant and unbearable pains, Duryodhana began to assail Vasudeva with keen and bitter words. 'O son of Kansa's slave, it seems you have no shame, for you have forgotten that I have been struck down most unfairly, according to the rules of inacefighting? It was you who unfairly caused this act by reminding Bhima about the breaking of my thighs. Do you think I did not mark it when Arjuna (under your advice) hinted to it to Bhima?

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: घातयित्वा महीपालानृजुयुद्धान् सहस्रशः॥ जिलैरुपायैर्बहुभिर्न ते लज्जा न ते घृणा।
en: Having caused the destruction of thousands of kings, who always fought fairly through various kinds of unfair means, do you not feel any shame or abhorrence for those acts?

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: अहन्यहनि शूराणां कुर्वाणः कदनं महत्॥ शिखण्डिनं पुरस्कृत्य घातितस्ते पितामहः।
en: Having daily bought about a great carnage of heroic warriors, you at last caused the grandshire to be slain by placing Shikhandin to the front.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: अश्वत्थाम्नः सनामानं हत्वा नागं सुदुते॥ आचार्यो न्यासितः शस्त्रं किं तन्न विदितं मया।
en: Having again caused an elephant of the same name of Ashvatthama to be killed, O you of vicious principle, you made the preceptor lay aside his weapons. Do you think that this is not known to me?

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: स चानेन नृशंसेन धृष्टद्युम्नेन वीर्यवान्॥ पात्यमानस्वया दृष्टो न चैनं त्वमवारयः।
en: While again that brave hero was about to be killed by this cruel Dhristadyumna, you did not dissuade the latter!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: वधार्थं पाण्डपुत्रस्य याचितां शक्तिमेव च॥ घटोत्कचे व्यंसयतः कस्त्वत्तः पापकृत्तमः।
en: The dart that had been begged (of Shakra as a boon) by Karna for the destruction of Arjuna, was baffled by you through Ghatotkacha! Who is there that is more sinful than you?

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: छिन्नहस्तः प्रायगतस्तथा भूरिश्रवा बली॥ त्वयाऽभिसृष्टेन हतः शैनेयेन महात्मना।
en: Likewise powerful Bhurishravas, with one of his arms cut off and while observing the Praya vow, was caused to be slain by you through the great Satyaki.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: कुर्वाणश्चोत्तमं कर्म कर्णः पार्थजिगीषया॥ व्यंसनेनाश्वसेनस्य पन्नगेन्द्रस्य वै पुनः।
en: Karna had done a great feat for defeating Partha. You frustrated the object of Ashvasena, the son of that prince of snakes (viz., Takshaka).

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: पुनश्च पतिते चक्रे व्यसनार्तः पराजितः॥ पातितः समरे कर्णश्चक्रव्यग्रोऽग्रणीनृणाम्।
en: When again the wheel of Karna's car sank in mire and Karna was assisted with calamity and almost defeated on that account, and-when, he became anxious to free his wheel—you caused that Karna to be then slain!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: यदि मां चापि कर्णं च भीष्मद्रोणौ च संयुतौ॥ ऋजुना प्रतियुध्येथा न ते स्याद् विजयो ध्रुवम्।
en: If he had fought me and Karna and Bhisma and Drona by fair means, victory then, forsooth, would never had been yours.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: त्वया पुनरनार्येण जिह्ममार्गेण पार्थिवाः॥ स्वधर्ममनुतिष्ठन्तो वयं चान्ये च घातिताः।
en: By adopting the most wily and unfair means you have caused the death of many kings observant of the duties of their order and of ourselves as well.'

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: वासुदेव उवाच हतस्त्वमसि गान्धारे सभ्रातृसुतबान्धवः॥ सगणः ससुहचैव पापं मार्गमनुष्ठितः।
en: Vasudeva said You, O son of Gandhari, have been killed with your brothers, sons, kinsmen, friends, and followers, for the sinful path you followed.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: तवैव दुष्कृतैर्वीरौ भीष्मद्रोणौ निपातितौ॥ कर्णश्च निहतः संख्ये तव शीलानुवर्तकः।
en: Through your deeds those two heroes, viz., Bhishma and Drona, have been killed. Karna has been slain for having followed your conduct !

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: याच्यमानं मया मूढ पित्र्यमंशं न दित्ससि॥ पाण्डवेभ्यः स्वराज्यं च लोभाच्छकुनिनिश्चयात्।
en: Requested by me, O fool, you did not, from avarice, give the Pandavas their paternal share, under the advice of Shakuni.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: विषं ते भीमसेनाय दत्तं सर्वे च पाण्डवाः॥ प्रदीपिता जतुगृहे मात्रा सह सुदुर्मते।
en: You gave poison to Bhimasena! You, O wicked man, tried to burn all the Pandavas with their mother at the palace of lace!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: सभायां याज्ञसेनी च कृष्टा द्यूते रजस्वला॥ तदैव तावद् दुष्टात्मन् वध्यस्त्वं निरपत्रप।
en: While gambling, you insulted the daughter of Yajnasena, while in her season, in the midst of assembly! Shameless as you are, you should have been killed there and then!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: अनक्षज्ञं च धर्मज्ञं सौबलेनाक्षवेदिना॥ निकृत्या यत् पराजैषीस्तस्मादसि हतो रणे।
en: Through Subala's son an expert in dice, you unfairly defeated the virtuous Yudhishthira who was unskilled in gambling! For that are killed.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: जयद्रथेन पापेन यत् कृष्णा केशिता वने॥ यातेषु मृगयां चैव तृणबिन्दोरथाश्रमम्।
en: Through the sinful Jayadratha again, Krishna was on another occasion insulted when the Pandavas, her lords, had gone out a thunting towards the hermitage of Trinavindu! you

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: अभिमन्युश्च यद् बाल एको बहुभिराहवे॥ त्वद्दोषैनिहतः पाप तस्मादसि हतो रणे।
en: Causing Abhimanyu, who was a child and alone, to be surrounded by many, you did kill that hero. For this sin, O sinful wretch, you are slain!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: यान्यकार्याणि चास्माकं कृतानीति प्रभाषसे॥ वैगुण्येन तवात्यर्थं सर्वं हि तदनुष्ठितम्।
en: All those sinful deeds which you attribute to us have in reality been perpetrated by you in consequence of your sinful nature!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: बृहस्पतेरुशनसो नोपदेशः श्रुतस्त्वया॥ वृद्धा नोपासिताश्चैव हितं वाक्यं न ते श्रुतम्।
en: You had never listened to the advice of Brihaspati and Ushanas! You had never respected the old! You had never heard the beneficial words!

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: लोभेनातिबलेन त्वं तृष्णया च वशीकृतः॥ कृतवानस्यकार्याणि विपाकस्तस्य भुज्यताम्।
en: Possessed by ungovernable covetousness and thirst of gain, you committed many unrighteous acts. Suffer now the consequences thereof.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अधीतं विधिवद् दत्तं भूः प्रशास्ता ससागरा॥ मूर्ध्नि स्थितममित्राणां को नु स्वन्ततरो पया।
en: Duryodhana said I have made various studies, made presents according to the ordinance, governed the wide Earth with her seas, and trumpeted over the heads of my fees. Who is there so fortunate as myself?

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: यदिष्टं क्षत्रबन्धूनां स्वधर्ममनुपश्यताम्॥ तदिदं निधनं प्राप्तं को नु स्वन्ततरो मया।
en: That end again which is sought by Kshatriya observant of the duties of their own order, viz., death in battle, I have also met with mine. Who, therefore, is so fortunate as myself?

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: देवार्हा मानुषा भोगाः प्राप्ता असुलभा नृपैः॥ ऐश्वर्यं चोत्तमं प्राप्त: को नु स्वन्ततरो मया।
en: I have enjoyed pleasures, such as were worthy of the very gods and such as could with difficulty, be obtained by other kings. I have attained the highest prosperity. Who then is so fortunate as myself?

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: ससुहृत् सानुगश्चैव स्वर्गं गन्ताहमच्युत॥ यूयं निहतसंकल्पाः शोचन्तो वर्तयिष्यथ॥
en: With all my well-wishers, and my younger brothers, I am going to heaven! As regards yourselves, with your baffled purposes and racked with grief, live you in this unhappy world.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: संजय उवाच अस्य वाक्यस्य निधने कुरुराजस्य धीमतः॥ अपतत् सुमहद् वर्षं पुष्पाणां पुण्यगन्धिनाम्। अवादयन्त गन्धर्वा वादिनं सुमनोहरम्॥ जगुश्चाप्सरसो राज्ञो यशःसम्बद्धमेव च। सिद्धाश्च मुमुचुर्वाचः साधु साध्विति पार्थिव॥ ववौ च सुरभिर्वायुः पुण्यगन्धो मृदुः सुखः। व्यराजंश्च दिशः सर्वा नभो वैदूर्यसंनिभम्॥
en: Sanjaya continued After the intelligent king of the Kurus, have said these words, a thick shower of fragrant flowers dropped from the sky. The Gandharvas beat many charming musical instruments. The Apsaras in a chorus sang the glory of king Duryodhana. The Siddhas cried-Praise to king Duryodhana! Sweet and delicious breezes mildly blew on all sides. All the quarters became clear and the firmament looked blue as the lapis lazuli.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: अयद्भुतानि ते दृष्ट्वा वासुदेवपुरोगमाः। दुर्योधनस्य पूजां तु दृष्ट्वा व्रीडामुपागमन्॥
en: Beholding these good signs, and this worship offered to Duryodhana, the Pandavas, with Vasudeva at their head, were put to shame.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: हतांश्चाधर्मतः श्रुत्वा शोकार्ताः शुशुचुर्हि ते। भीष्मं द्रोणं तथा कर्णं भूरिश्रवसमेव च॥
en: Hearing the invisible voice the Bhishma and Drona and Karna and Bhurishravas were killed unfairly, they were afflicted with remorse and wept in grief.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: तांस्तु चिन्तापरान् दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवान् दीनचेतसः। प्रोवाचेदं वचः कृष्णो मेघदुन्दुभिनिःस्वनः॥ नैष शक्योऽतिशीघ्रास्त्रस्ते च सर्वे महारथाः। ऋजुयुद्धेन विक्रान्ता हन्तुं युष्माभिराहवे॥
en: Seeing the Pandavas stricken with anxiety and grief. Krishna addressed them in a voice deep as that of the clouds or the drum, saying-''All of them were great car-warriors and quick hands in weapons! If you had displayed all your prowess, even then you could never have killed them in battle by a fair fight.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: नैष शक्यः कदाचित् तु हन्तु धर्मेण पार्थिवः। ते वा भीष्ममुखाः सर्वे महेष्वासा महारथाः॥
en: King Duryodhana also could never be killed in a fair fight! The same is the case with all those powerful car-warriors led led by Bhishma.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: मयानेकैरूपायैस्तु मायायोगेन चासकृत्। हतास्ते सर्व एवाजौ भवतां हितमिच्छता॥
en: For doing you good, I repeatedly applied my illusory powers and caused them to be killed by various means in battle.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: यदि नैवंविधं जातु कुर्यां जिह्ममहं रणे। कुतो वो विजयो भूयः कुतो राज्यं कुतो धनम्॥
en: If I had note adopted such deceitful ways in battle, you would never have been victorious, nor could have gained kingdom or wealth.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: ते हि सर्वे महात्मानश्चत्वारोऽतिरथा भुवि। न शक्या धर्मतो हन्तुं लोकपालैरपि स्वयम्॥
en: Those four were very great warriors and regarded as Atirathas in the world. The very Regents of the Earth could not kill them in fair fight.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: तथैवायं गदापाणिर्धार्तराष्ट्रो गतकमः। न शक्यो धर्मतो हन्तुं कालेनापीह दण्डिना॥
en: Likewise, the son of Diritarashtra, when armed with the mace, could not be killed in fair fight by Yama himself, armed with his bludgeon.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: न च वो हृदि कर्तव्यं यदयं घातितो रिपुः। मिथ्यावध्यास्तथोपायैर्बहवः शत्रवोऽधिकाः॥
en: Ye should not mind that this enemy of yours has been killed deceitfully. When the number of one's enemics becomes great, then destruction should be brought about by wily ways.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: पूर्वैरनुगतो मार्गो देवैरसुरघातिभिः। सद्धिश्चानुगतः पन्थाः स सर्वैरनुगम्यते॥
en: The gods themselves, in killing the Asuras, have followed by the celestials, may be followed by all.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: कृतकृत्याश्च सायाह्ने निवासं रोचयामहे। साश्चनागरथाः सर्वे विश्रमामो नराधिपाः॥
en: We have been crowned with success. It is evening. We had better retire to our tents. Let us all, you kings, take rest, with our horses and elephants and cars!'

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: वासुदेववचः श्रुत्वा तदानीं पाण्डवैः सह। पञ्चाला भृशसंहृष्टा विनेदुः सिंहसंघवत्॥
en: Hearing these words of Vasudeva, the Pandavas and the Panchalas filled with joy, roared like a number of lions.

description: The praise of Bhimasena. The lamentation of Duryodhana
sn: ततः प्राध्यापयशङ्खान् पाञ्चजन्यं च माधवः। हृष्टा दुर्योधनं दृष्ट्वा निहतं पुरुषर्षभ।७१॥
en: All of them blew their conchs and Madhava himself blew his Panchajanya, seeing Duryodhana struck down in battle.'

sn: संजय उवाच ततस्ते प्रययुः सर्वे निवासाय महीक्षितः। शङ्खान् प्रध्मापयन्तो वै हृष्टाः परिघबाहवः॥
en: Sanjaya said "All those kings, having arms resembling spiked bludgeons, then went towards their tents, overflowing with joy and blowing their conchs on their way.

sn: पाण्डवान् गच्छतश्चापि शिबिरं नो विशाम्पते। महेष्वासोऽन्वगात् पश्चाद् युयुत्सुः सात्यकिस्तथा॥ धृष्टद्युम्न: शिखण्डी च द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः। सर्वे चान्ये महेष्वासाः प्रययुः शिबिराण्युत॥
en: The Pandavas also, O king, proceeded towards our tents. The great bowmen Yuyutsu followed them, as also Satyaki, and Dhrishtadyumna, and Shikhandin, and the five sons of Draupadi. The other great bowmen also went towards our tents.

sn: ततस्ते प्राविशन् पार्था हतत्विट्कं हतेश्वरम्। दुर्योधनस्य शिबिरं रङ्गवद्विसृते जने॥
en: The Parthas then entered the tent of Duryodhana, shorn of its splendours and bereft of its master, and looking like a pleasureground deserted by spectators.

sn: गतोत्सवं पुरमिव हृतनागमिव ह्रदम्। स्त्रीवर्षवरभूयिष्ठं वृद्धामात्यैरधिष्ठितम्॥
en: That pavilion looked like a city void of festivities, or a lake without its elephant. It was filled with women and eunuchs and aged counsellors.

sn: तत्रैतान् पर्युपातिष्ठन् दुर्योधनपुरःसराः। कृताञ्जलिपुटा राजन् काषायमलिनाम्बराः।॥
en: Duryodhana and other heroes, dressed in yellow raiment's, formerly used, O king, to wait reverentially, with joined hands, on those old counsellors.

sn: शिबिरं समनुप्राप्य कुरुराजस्य पाण्डवाः। अवरुर्महाराज रथेभ्यो रथसत्तमाः॥
en: Arriving at the pavilion of the Kuru king, the Pandavas, those foremost of car-warriors, O king, got down from their cars.

sn: ततो गाण्डीवधन्वानमभ्यभाषत केशवः। स्थितः प्रियहिते नित्यमतीव भरतर्षभ।॥ अवरोपय गाण्डीवमक्षयौ च महेषुधी। अथाहमवरोक्ष्यामि पश्चाद् भरतसत्तम।॥
en: Ever engaged, in the good of his friend, Keshava, addressed the holder of Gandiva, saying, "Take down your Gandiva as also the two inexhaustible quivers. I shall get down after you, O best of the Bharatas.

sn: स्वयं चैवावरोह त्वमेतच्छ्रेयस्तवानघ। तचाकरोत् तथा वीरः पाण्डुपुत्रो धनंजयः॥
en: Get down, for this is for your own good, O sinless one!'-Pandu's brave son, Dhananjaya, did as he was directed.

sn: अथ पश्चात् ततः कृष्णो रश्मीनुत्सृज्य वाजिनाम्। अवारोहत मेधावी रथाद् गाण्डीवधन्वनः॥
en: Leaving the reins of the horses the intelligent Krishna then got down from the car of Dhananjaya.

sn: अथातवतीर्णे भूतानामीश्वरे सुमहात्मनि। कपिरन्तर्दधे दिव्यो ध्वजो गाण्डीवधन्वनः॥
en: After the great Lord of all creatures had got down from that car, the celestials Ape that was on the standard of Arjuna's car disappeared there and then.

sn: स दग्धो द्रोणकर्णाभ्यां दिव्यैरस्त्रैर्महारथः। अथादीप्तोऽग्निना ह्याशु प्रजज्वाल महीपते॥
en: That great car then, which had before been burnt by Drona and Karna with their celestial weapons, quickly caught fire, O king, without any thing being seen there.

sn: सोपासङ्गः सरश्मिश्च साश्वः सयुगबन्धुरः। भस्मीभूतोऽपतद् भूमौ रथो गाण्डीवधन्वनः॥
en: Indeed, the car of Dhananjaya, with its quivers, reins, horses, yoke, and shaft, fell down, all reduced to ashes.

sn: तं तथा भस्मभूतं तु दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुसुताः प्रभो। अभवन् विस्मिता राजन्नर्जुनश्चेदमब्रवीत्॥ कृताञ्जलिः सप्रणयं प्रणिपत्याभिवाद्य ह। गोविन्द कस्माद् भगवन् रथोदग्धोऽयमग्निना॥
en: Seeing the vehicle thus reduced to ashes, O Iord, the sons of Pandu filled with wonder, and Arjuna, O king, having saluted Krishna and bowed un.o him, said these words, with joined hands, 'O Govinda, O divine one, why has this car been consumed by fire?

sn: किमेतन्महदाश्चर्यमभवद् यदुनन्दन। तन्मे ब्रूहि महाबाहो श्रोतव्यं यदि मन्यसे॥
en: Whiat is this highly wonderful incident that has taken place before our eyes? O you of mighty arms, if you think that I can hear it without injury then tell me everything.'

sn: वासुदेव उवाच अस्त्रैर्बहुविधैर्दग्धः पूर्वमेवायमर्जुन। मदधिष्ठित्तत्वात् समरे न विशीर्णः परंतप॥
en: Vasudeva said That car, O Arjuna, had already been consumed by various sorts of weapons. It was because I had sat upon it during battle that it did not break into pieces, O destroyer of foes.

sn: इदानीं तु विशीर्णोऽयं दग्धो ब्रह्मास्त्रतेजा। भया विमुक्तः कौन्तेय त्वय्यद्य कृतकर्मणि।॥
en: Previously consumed by the power of Brahma weapons, it has been reduced to ashes upon my leaving it after you had achieved your object.

sn: ईपदुत्स्मयमास्तु भगवान् केशवोऽरिहा। परिष्वज्य च राजानं युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥ दिष्ट्या जयसि कौन्तेय दिष्ट्याते शत्रवो जिताः। दिष्टया गाण्डीवधन्वा च भीमसेनश्च पाण्डवः॥ त्वं चापि कुशली राजन् माद्रीपुत्रो च पाण्डवौ। मुक्ता वीरक्षयादस्मात् संग्रामानिहतद्विषः॥ क्षिप्रमुक्तरकालानि कुरु कार्याणि भारत। उपायतमुपप्लव्यं सह गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: Then, with a little pride, Lord Keshava embracing king Yudhishthira, said to him, 'By good luck, you have gained the victory, O son of Kunti! By good luck, your enemies have been defcated! By good luck, the holder of Gandiva and Bhimasena the son of Pandu, and yourself, O king, and the two sons of Madri have escaped alive from this battle so destructive of heroes, after having killed all your foes! Speedily do, O Bharata, what should now be done!

sn: आनीय मधुपर्कं मां यत् पुरा त्वमवोचथाः। एष भ्राता सखा चैव तव कृष्ण धनंजयः॥ रक्षितव्यो महाबाहो सर्वास्वापत्स्विति प्रभो। तव चैव ब्रुवाणस्य तथेत्येवाहमब्रुवम्॥ स सव्यसाची गुप्तस्ते विजयी च जनेश्वर।
en: After I had arrived at Upaplavya, you the holder of Gandiva, gave me honey and the customary ingredients, and said, O Lord, This Dhananjaya, O Krishna, is your brother and SO friend! He should, therefore, be protected by you in all dangers!-To your these words I answered saying-So be it!-That Savyasachin has always been protected by me. You have also gained victory, O king.

sn: भ्रातृभिः सह राजेन्द्र शूरः सत्यपराक्रमः॥ मुक्तो वीरक्षयादस्मात् संग्रामाल्लोमहर्षणात्। एवमुक्तस्तु कृष्णेन धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥ हृष्टरोमा महाराज प्रत्युवाच जनार्दनम्।
en: With his brothers, O king of kings, that truly powerful hero, has come out alive of this dreadful battle, destructive of heroes.'-Thus addressed by Krishna, king Yudhishthira with his hairs standing erect, O king, said to Janarddana.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच प्रमुक्तं द्रोणकर्णाभ्यां ब्रह्मास्त्रमरिमर्दन॥ कस्त्वदन्यः सहेत् साक्षादपि वज्री पुरंदरः।
en: Yudhishthira said Who else, except you. O destroyer of foes, not even thunder-holding Purandara himself, could have withstood the Brahma weapons discharged by Drona and Karna!

sn: भवतस्तु प्रसादेन संशप्तकगणा जिताः॥ महारणगतः पार्थो यच नासीत् पराङ्मुखः।
en: It was through your favour that the Samsaptakas were vanquished! It was through your favour that Partha had never to turn back from even the fiercest of battles!

sn: तथैव च महाबाहो पर्यायैर्बहुभिर्मया॥ कर्मणामनुसंतानं तेजसश्च गती: शुभाः। उपप्लव्ये महषिर्मे कृष्णद्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत्॥ यतो धर्मस्ततः कृष्णो यतः कृष्णस्ततो जयः।
en: It was through your favour O mighty-armed one, that I myself, with my descendants, have, by performing various feats, obtained the auspicious end of prowess and energy! At Upaplavya, the Rishi Krishna-Dvaipayana told me that where there is Krishna righteousness and victory will be there."

sn: इत्येवमुक्ते ते वीराः शिबिरं तव भारत॥ प्रविश्य प्रत्यपद्यन्त कोशरत्नर्धिसंचयान्। रजतं जातरूपं च मणीनथ च मौक्तिकान्॥ भूषणान्यथ मुख्यानि कम्बलान्यजिनानि च। दासीदासमसंख्येयं राज्योपकरणानि च॥ प्राप्य धनमक्षय्यं त्वदीयं भरतर्षभ। उदक्रोशन्महाभागा नरेन्द्र विजितारयः॥
en: Sanjaya continued After this conversation, those heroes entered your son's encampment, and secured the weapons of chest, many jewels, and much wealth, and silver and gold and gems and pearls and many rich ornaments and blankets and skins, and innumerable slaves male and female, and many other things required by kings. Having secured that inexhaustible wealth belonging to you, O foremost of Bharata's race, those highly-blessed ones, whose enemies had been killed, uttered loud cries of joy.

sn: ते तु वीराः समाश्वस्य वाहनान्यवमुच्य च। अतिष्ठन्त मुहुः सर्वे पाण्डवाः सात्यकिस्तथा।॥
en: Having unyoked their animals, the Pandavas and Satyaki took rest there awhile.

sn: अथाब्रवीन्महाराज वासुदेवो महायशाः। अस्माभिर्मङ्गलार्थाय वस्तव्यं शिबिराद् बहिः॥ तथेत्युक्त्वा हि ते सर्वे पाण्डवाः सात्यकिस्तथा। वासुदेवेन सहिता मङ्गलार्थं बहिर्ययुः॥
en: Then the illustrious Vasudeva said. We should, as the first sacred act, remain out of the camp for this night. Saying 'So be it!'—the Pandavas and Satyaki, accompanied by Vasudeva, went put of the camp for doing this auspicious act.

sn: ते समासाद्य सरितं पुण्यामोघवतीं नृप। न्यवसन्नथ तां रात्रि पाण्डवा हतशत्रवः॥
