en: Arrived on the banks of the sacred stream Oghavati, O king, the Pandavas, who had no enemies took up their quarters there for that night.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्ततो राजा प्राप्तकालमचिन्तयत्। तत्र ते गमनं प्राप्तं रोचते तव माधव॥ गान्धार्याः क्रोधदीप्तायाः प्रशमार्थमरिंदम। हेतुकारणयुक्तैश्च वाक्यैः कालसमीरितैः॥ क्षिप्रमेव महाभाग गान्धारी प्रशमिष्यसि। पितामहश्च भगवान् व्यासस्तत्र भविष्यति॥
en: King Yudhishthira then brought to his mind, the outright action with the time and said O enemy suppressor Madhava! It appears all good to visit at Hastinapura in order to pacify Gandhari who is burning with anger. O noble lord! You will only able to pacify Gandhari by referring to reasonable and time matching things to her. Our grand-father Vyasa will also present there.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सम्प्रेषयामासुर्यादवं नागसाह्वयम्। स च प्रायाजवेनाशुः वासुदेवः प्रतापवान्॥ दारुकं रथमारोप्य येन राजाम्बिकासुतः।
en: They then sent Keshava to Hastinapura. The highly powerful Vasudeva causing Daruka to get upon his car, proceeded very quickly to that place where the royal son of Ambika was.

sn: तमूचुः सम्प्रयास्यन्तं शैव्यसुग्रीववाहनम्॥ प्रत्याश्वासय गान्धारी हतपुत्रां यशस्विनीम्। स प्रायात् पाण्डवैरुक्तस्तत् पुरं सात्वतां वरः॥ आससाद ततः क्षिप्रं गान्धारीं निहतात्मजाम्॥
en: While about to start on his car, having Shaivya and Sugriva yoked to it, (the Pandavas) said to him—Comfort the helpless Gandhari who has lost all her sons.'-Thus addressed by the Pandavas, the chief of the Satvatas then set out for Hastinapura and arrived before Gandhari who had all her sons slain.”

sn: जनमेजय उवाच किमर्थं द्विजशार्दूलं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। गान्धार्याः प्रेषयामास वासुदेवं परंतपम्॥ यदा पूर्वं गतः कृष्णः शमार्थं कौरवान् प्रति। न च तं लब्धवान् कामं ततो युद्धमभूदिदम्॥
en: Janamejaya said “Why did that best of kings, viz., the righteous Yudhishthira, send that scorcher of foes, viz., Vasudeva, to Gandhari? Krishna had at first gone to the Kauravas for the sake of bringing about peace. He was not successful. For this the battle took place.

sn: निहतेषु तु योधेषु हते दुर्योधने तदा। पृथिव्यां पाण्डवेयस्य नि:सपत्ने कृते युधि॥ विद्रुते शिबिरे शून्ये प्राप्ते यशसि चोत्तमे। किं न तत् कारणं ब्रह्मन् येन कृष्णो गतः पुनः॥
en: When all the warriors were killed and Duryodhana was struck down, when for the battle the empire of Pandu's son became perfectly safe, when all the (Kuru) camp became empty, when the son of Pandu won great glory, what was the cause for which Krishna had once again to go (to Hastinapura)?

sn: न चैतत् कारपां ब्रह्मनल्पं विप्रतिभाति मे। यत्रागमदमेयात्मा स्वयमेव जनार्दनः॥
en: It seems to me, O Brahimana, that the cause could not be an insignificant one, since it was Janarddana had himself to make the journey.

sn: तत्त्वतो वै समाचक्ष्व सर्वमध्वर्युसत्तम। यचात्र कारणं ब्रह्मन् कार्यस्यास्य विनिश्चये॥
en: O foremost of all Adhyaryus, tell me in full what was the reason for undertaking such a mission."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच त्वयुक्तोऽयमनुप्रश्नो यन्मां पृच्छसि पार्थिव। तत्तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावद् भरतर्षभ।॥ हतं दुर्योधनं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनेन संयुगे। व्युत्क्रम्य समयं राजन् धार्तराष्ट्र महाबलम्॥ अन्यायेन हतं दृष्ट्वा गदायुद्धेन भारत। युधिष्ठिरं महाराज महद् भयमथाविशत्॥ चिन्तयानो महाभागं गान्धारी तपसान्विताम्। घोरेण तपसा युक्तां त्रैलोक्यमपि सा दहेत्॥ तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य बुद्धिः समभवत् तदा। गान्धार्याः क्रोधदीसाया पूर्वं प्रशमनं भवेत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said “The question you have put, O king, is, indeed, worthy of you! I will tell you everything truly truly as it happened. See Duryodhana, the powerful son of Dhritarashtra, struck down by Bhimasena against the rule of fair fight, and beholding the Kuru king slain unfairly. O Bharata, Yudhishthira, O monarch, was filled with great fear, thinking of the highly-blessed and ascetic Gandhari-'See has practised severe ascetic austerities and can, therefore, consume the three worlds,' this was the thought of the son of Pandu. By sending Krishna, the angry Gandhari, Gandhari, would be comforted before Yudhishthira's own arrival.

sn: सा हि पुत्रवधं श्रुत्वा कृतमस्माभिरीदृशम्। मानसेनाग्निना क्रुद्धा भस्मसान्न: करिष्यति॥
en: Hearing of the death of her son in such a way, she will, in anger, with the fire of her mind, reduce us to ashes.

sn: कथं दुःखमिदं तीव्र गान्धारी सा सहिष्यति। श्रुत्वा विनिहतं पुत्रं छलेनाजिह्मयोधिनम्॥ एवं विचिन्त्य बहुधा भयशोकसमन्वितः। वासुदेवमिदं वाक्यं धर्मराजोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: How will Gandhari bear such poignant grief, after hearing of her son, who always fought fairly, being slain unfairly by us?' Having thought thus for a long while, king Yudhishthira filled with fear and fried said these words to Vasudeva.

sn: तव प्रसादाद् गोविन्द राज्यं निहतकण्टकम्। अप्राप्यं मनसापीदं प्राप्तमस्माभिरच्युत॥ प्रत्यक्षं मे महाबाहो संग्रामे लोमहर्षणे। विमर्दः सुमहान् प्राप्तस्त्वया यादवनन्दन॥
en: Through your kindness, O Govinda, my kingdom has been freed from pests. We have gained now what we could not even imagine. Omighty-armed one, in battle, making the very hair to stand on end, thou hadst to bear voilent blows before my very eyes, O delighter of the Yadavas.

sn: त्वया देवासुरे युद्धे वधार्थममरद्विषाम्। यथा साह्यं पुरा दत्तं हताश्च विबुधद्विषः॥
en: Formerly in the battle between the gods and। the Asuras, thou hadst, lent your help for the destruction of the foes of the celestials, and those enemies were killed.

sn: साह्यं तथा महाबाहो दत्तमस्माकमच्युत। सारथ्येन च वार्ष्णेय भवता हि धृता वयम्॥
en: Similarly, O mighty-armed one, you have helped us, O you of unfading glory. By agreeing to act as our charioteer, O Vrishnihero, you have all along protected us.

sn: यदि न त्वं भवेर्नाथ: फाल्गुनस्य महारणे। कथं शक्यो रणे जेतुं भवेदेष बलार्णवः॥
en: If you had not protected Phalguna in dreadful battle, this sea of troops would not have been vanquished?

sn: गदाप्रहारा विपुलाः परिधैश्चापि ताडनम्। शक्तिभिर्भिन्दिपालैश्च तोमरैः सपरश्वधैः॥
en: You have suffered many blows of the mace, and many strokes of spiked bludgeons and dart and short arrows and lances and battle-axes.

sn: अस्मत्कृते त्वया कृष्ण वाचः सुपरुषाः श्रुताः। शस्त्राणां च निपाता वै वस्पर्शोपमा रणे॥
en: For our sake, O Krishna, you also put up with many harsh words and endure the violent fall of weapons in battle.

sn: ते च ते सफला जाता हते दुर्योधनेऽच्युत। तत्सर्वं न यथा नश्येत् क्रोधं बुद्ध्यस्व माधव॥
en: On account of Duryodhana's death, all this has not been fruitless, O you of unfading glory. O Krishna, our heart, however, is yet trembling in doubt. Know, O Madhava, that Gandhari's wrath, has been excited.

sn: सा हि नित्यं महाभाग तपसोग्रेण कर्शिता। पुत्रपौत्रवधं श्रुत्वा ध्रुवं नः सम्प्रधक्ष्यति॥ तस्याः प्रसादनं वीर प्राप्तकालं मतं मम।
en: That highly-blessed lady is always weakening herself with the austerest of penances. Hearing of the death of her sons and grandsons, she will forsooth, reduce us to ashes. It is time, O hero, I think, for pacifying her.

sn: कश्च तां क्रोधताम्राक्षी पुत्रव्यसनकर्शिताम्॥ वीक्षितुं पुरुषः शक्तस्त्वामृते पुरुषोत्तम।
en: Save you, O foremost of men, what other person is there that can even face that lady of red and ranging eyes and greatly overwhelmed with the misfortunes of her children.

sn: तत्र मे गमनं प्राप्तं रोचते तव माधव॥ गान्धार्याः क्रोधदीप्तायाः प्रशमार्थमरिंदम। त्वं हि कर्ता विकर्ता च लोकानां प्रभवाव्ययः॥
en: O Madhava, I think it is better for you to go, for pacifying Gandhari, O chastiser of foes, who is blazing with wrath. You are the Creator and the Destroyer. You are the first cause of all the worlds, yourself being eternal.

sn: हेतुकारणसंयुक्तैर्वाक्यैः कालसमीरितैः। क्षिप्रमेव महाबाहो गान्धारी शमयिष्यसि॥
en: With reasonable words, you will quickly, O you of great wisdomn, be able to pacify Gandhari.

sn: पितामहश्च भगवान् कृष्णस्तत्र भविष्यति। सर्वथा ते महाबाहो गान्धार्याः क्रोधनाशनम्॥ कर्तव्यं सात्वतां श्रेष्ठ पाण्डवानां हितार्थिना।
en: Our grandsire, the holy KrishnaDvaipayana, will be there. O mighty-armed one, it is your duty to remove by all means in thy power, the anger of Gandhari.

sn: धर्मराजस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा यदुकुलोद्वहः॥ आमन्त्र्य दारुकं प्राह रथः सजो विधीयताम्।
en: Hearing these words of king Yudhishthira, the Yadu-hero summoning Daruka, said 'Get may car ready.'

sn: केशवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा त्वरमाणोऽथ दारुकः॥ न्यवेदयद् रथं सज्जे केशवाय महात्मने।
en: Having received Keshava's command, Daruka speedily returned and represented to his great master that the car was ready.

sn: तं रथं यादवश्रेष्ठः समारुह्य परंतपः॥ जगाम हास्तिनपुरं त्वरितः केशवो विभुः।
en: That destroyer of foes and chief of Yadu's race, viz., the Lord Keshava, having got upon the car, proceeded speedily to the city of the Kurus.

sn: ततः प्रायान्महाराज माधवो भगवान् रथी॥ नागसाह्वयमासाद्य प्रविवेश न वीर्यवान्।
en: The worshipful Madhava then, mounting his vehicle, proceeded, and arrived Hastinapur. at

sn: प्रविश्य नगरं वीरो रथघोषेण नादयन्॥ विदितो धृतराष्ट्रस्य सोऽवतीर्य रथोत्तमात्। अभ्यगच्छददीनात्मा धृतराष्ट्रनिवेशनम्॥
en: Making the city resound with the rattle of his car-wheels as he entered it, he sent word to Dhritarashtra and then got down from his car and entered the palace of the old king.

sn: पूर्वं चाभिगतं तत्र सोऽपश्यदृषिसत्तमम्। पादौ प्रपीड्य कृष्णस्य राज्ञश्चापि जनार्दनः॥ अभ्यवादयदव्यग्रो गान्धारीं चापि केशवः। ततस्तु यादवश्रेष्ठो धृतराष्ट्रमधोक्षजः॥ पाणिमालम्ब्य राजेन्द्र सुस्वरं प्ररुरोद ह।
en: He there saw that best of Rishis, (viz., Dvaipayana), arrived before him. Embracing the feet of both Vyasa and Dhritarashtra, Janarddana quietly saluted Gandhari also. Then the best of the Yadavas, viz., Vishnu, holding Dhritarashtra by the hand, O king, began to weep.

sn: स मुहूर्तादिवोत्सृज्य बाष्पं शोकसमुद्भवम्॥ प्रक्षाल्य वारिणा नेत्रे ह्याचम्य च यथाविधि। उवाच प्रस्तुतं वाक्यं धृतराष्ट्रमरिंदमः॥ न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचिद् वृद्धस्य तव भारत। कालस्य च यथावृत्तं तत् ते सुविदितं प्रभो॥
en: Having wept for a while, he washed his eyes and his face with water according to rules, He then said sweetly to Dhritarashtra'Nothing is unknown to you, O Bharata, about the past and the future. You are wellacquainted, O lord, with the course of time.

sn: यदिदं पाण्डवैः सर्वैस्तव चित्तानुरोधिभिः। कथं कुलक्षयो न स्यात्तथा क्षत्रस्य भारत॥
en: Out of respect for you the Pandavas had tried to prevent the destruction of their family and the extermination of the Kshatriyas, O Bharata.

sn: भ्रातृभिः समयं कृत्वा क्षान्तवान् धर्मवत्सलः। द्यूतच्छलजितैः शुद्धर्वनवासो ह्युपागतः॥
en: Having made a compact with his brothers, the virtuous Yudhishthira had lived peacefully. He even went to exile after the unfair defeat at dice.

sn: अज्ञातवासचर्या च नानावेषसमावृतैः। अन्ये च बहवः केशात् त्वशक्तैरिव सर्वदा॥
en: With his brothers he lived in concealment and disguise. They also suffered various miseries as if they were quite helpless.

sn: मया च स्वयमागम्य युद्धकाल उपस्थिते। सर्वलोकस्य सांनिध्ये ग्रामांस्त्वं पञ्च याचितः॥
en: On the eve of batile I myself came, and before all begged of you only five villages.

sn: त्वया कालोपसृष्टेन लोभतो नापवर्जिताः। तवापराधान्नृपते सर्वं क्षत्रं क्षयं गतम्॥
en: Out of covetousness, and as destiny would nave it, you did not grant my request. Through you folly, O king, all the Kshatriyas have been exterminated.

sn: भीष्मेण सोमदत्तेन बाह्लीकेन कृपेण च। द्रोणेन च सपुत्रेण विदुरेण च धीमता॥ याचितस्त्वं शमं नित्यं न च तत्कृतवानसि।
en: Bhisma, and Somadatta, and Valhika, and Kripa, and Drona, and his son and the Wise Vidura, always begged you for peace. You did not, however, follow their advice.

sn: कालोपहतचित्ता हि सर्वे मुह्यन्ति भारत॥ यथा मूढो भवान् पूर्वमस्मिन्नर्थे समुद्यते।
en: Every one, it seems, loses sense under the influence of Destiny, O Bharata, since even you, O king, as regards this matter, did act so foolishly.

sn: किमन्यत् कालयोगाद्धि दिष्टमेव परायणम्॥ मा च दोषान् महाप्राज्ञ पाण्डवेषु निवेशय।
en: What else can it be but the effect of Time? Indeed, Destiny always reigns supreme! Do not, O you of great wisdom, attribute any fault to the Pandavas.

sn: अल्पोऽप्यतिक्रमो नास्ति पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्॥ धर्मतो न्यायतश्चैव स्नेहतश्च परंतप।
en: Judged by the standard of Ethics or reason or affection, the Pandavas have not committed the slightest offense, O scorcher of foes.

sn: एतत् सर्वं तु विज्ञाय ह्यात्मदोषकृतं फलम्॥ असूयां पाण्डुपुत्रेषु न भवान् कर्तुमर्हति।
en: Knowing all this to be the fruit of you own folly, it is proper for you not to entertain any ill felling towards the Pandavas.

sn: कुलं वंशश्च पिण्डाश्च यच्च पुत्रकृतं फलम्॥ गान्धार्यास्तव वै नाथ पाण्डवेषु प्रतिष्ठितम्।
en: The perpetuity of race, the offering of funeral cake, and every thing else that depends upon offspring, now depend on the Pandavas as regards both yourself and Gandhari.

sn: त्वं चैव कुरुशार्दूल गान्धारी च यशस्विनी॥ मा शुचो नरशार्दूल पाण्डवान् प्रति किल्बिषम्।
en: Both you and the renowned Gandhar also, should not entertain malice towards the Pandavas.

sn: एतत्सर्वमनुध्याय आत्मनश्च व्यतिक्रमम्॥ शिवेन पाण्डवान् पाहि नमस्ते भरतर्षभ।
en: Thinking of all this, and thinking also of your own sins, cherish good feelings towards the Pandavas. I bow to you, O Bharata chief.

sn: जानासि च महाबाहो धर्मराजस्य या त्वयि॥ भक्तिर्भरतशार्दूल स्नेहश्चापि स्वभावतः।
en: You know, O mighty armed one, the devotion of king Yudhisthira and his affection towards you.

sn: एतच कदनं कृत्वा शत्रूणामपकारिणाम्॥ दह्यते स दिवा रात्रौ न च शर्माधिगच्छति।
en: Having caused this destruction of foes that wronged him so, he is burning day and night in grief and does and enjoy peace of mind.

sn: त्वां चैव नरशार्दूल गान्धारीं च यशस्विनीम्॥ स शोचन् नरशार्दूल: शान्तिं नैवाधिगच्छति।
en: Grieving for you and for Gandhari, he does not enjoy any happiness.

sn: हिया च परयाऽऽविष्टो भवन्तं नाधिगच्छति॥ पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तं बुद्धिव्याकुलतेन्द्रियम्। एवमुक्त्वा महाराज धृतराष्ट्र यदूत्तमः॥ उवाच परमं वाक्यं गान्धारी शोककर्शिताम्। सौबलेयि निबोध त्वं यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु॥ त्वत्समा नास्ति लोकेऽस्मिन्नद्य सीमन्तिनी शुभे।
en: Out of shame he does not appear before you who are burning with grief on account of your children and whose understanding and senses have been bewildered.'—having said these words to Dhritarashtra, that foremost one Yadu's race, O king, addressed the griefstricken Gandhari in these words of great significance-O daughter of Subala, O you of excellent vows, hear what I say. O auspicious dame, there is no lady like you in world.

sn: जानासि च यथा राज्ञि सभायां मम संनिधौ॥ धर्मार्थसहितं वाक्यमुभयोः एक्षयोर्हितम्। उक्तवत्यसि कल्याणि न च ते तनयः कृतम्॥
en: You remember, O queen, those just and fair words which you gave utterance to the assembly before me, words that were beneficial to both the parties—but which your sons, ( auspicious lady, did not pay any heed to.

sn: दुर्योधनस्त्वया चोक्तो जयार्थी परुषं वचः। शृणु मूढ वचो मह्यं यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः॥ तदिदं समनुप्राप्तं तव वाक्यं नृपात्मजे। एवं विदित्वा कल्याणि मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः॥
en: Duryodhana, who coveted victory was reprimanded by you. You told him then-Listen, O fool, to these eternal words, viz., victory follows righteousness-your words, O princes, have now been fulfilled. Knowing all this, O auspicious lady, do not grieve.

sn: पाण्डवानां विनाशाय मा ते बुद्धिः कदाचन। शक्ता चासि महाभागे पृथिवीं सचराचराम्॥ चक्षुषा क्रोधदीप्तेन निर्दग्धुं तपसो बलात्।
en: Let not your heart be bent towards the destruction of the Pandavas. On account of the power of your penances, you are able, O highly blessed one, to consume with your cyes, burning in anger, the whole Earth with her mobile and immobile creatures.'

sn: वासुदेववचः श्रुत्वा गान्धारी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि केशव।
en: Hearing these words of Vasudeva, Gandhari said-'O Keshava, what you say is truel

sn: आधिभिर्दह्यमानाया मति: संचलिता मम॥ सा मे व्यवस्थिता श्रुत्वा तव वाक्यं जनार्दन।
en: My heart, burning in grief, had been unfixed. After hearing what you said, however, that heart, O Janarddana, has been settled.

sn: राज्ञस्त्वन्धस्य वृद्धस्य हतपुत्रस्य केशव॥ त्वं गतिः सहितैर्वीरैः पाण्डवैर्द्विपदां वर।
en: Regarding the blind old king, who had now become childless, O foremost of men, you and the sons of Pandu, are his refuge.'

sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं मुखं प्रच्छाद्य वाससा॥ पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्ता गान्धारी प्ररुरोद ह।
en: having said so Gandhari, burning in grief for the death of her sons, covered her face with her cloth and began to weep aloud.

sn: तत एनां महाबाहुः केशवः शोककर्शिताम्॥ हेतुकारणसंयुक्तैर्वाक्यैराश्वासयत् प्रभुः।
en: The mighty-armed lord Keshava then solaced the grief-stricken princess with reasonable words and examples.

sn: समाश्वास्य च गान्धारी धृतराष्ट्रं च माधवः॥ द्रौणिसंकल्पितं भावमवबुद्ध्यत् केशवः।
en: Having comforted Gandhari and Dhritarashtra, Keshava of Madhu's race, came to know the evil that was thought of by Drona's son.

sn: ततस्त्वरित उत्थाय पादौ मूर्धा प्रणम्य च॥ द्वैपायनस्य राजेन्द्र ततः कौरवमब्रवीत्। आपृच्छे त्वां कुरुश्रेष्ठ मा च शोके मनः कृथाः॥ द्रौणेः पापोऽस्त्यभिप्रायस्तेनास्मि सहसोत्थितः
en: Rising up quickly after worshipping the feet of Vyasa with his head, Keshava, O king, addressed Dhritarashtra, saying, 'I take your leave. O foremost of Kuru's race! Do not grieve. The son of Drona has an evil desire. It is for this that I rise so suddenly.

sn: पाण्डवानां वधे रात्रौ बुद्धिस्तेन प्रदर्शिता॥ एतच्छुत्वा तु वचनं गान्धार्या सहितोऽब्रवीत्। धृतराष्ट्रो महाबाहुः केशवं केशिसूदनम्॥ शीघ्रं गच्छ महाबाहो पाण्डवान् परिपालय।
en: It seems that he had formed a plan for destroying the Pandavas during the night.'.-Hearing these words, both Gandhari and Dhritarashtra said Keshava, the destroyer of Keshin, these words— 'Go quickly, O mighty-armed one, and protect the Pandavas.

sn: भूयस्त्वया समेष्यामि क्षिप्रमेव जनार्दन॥ प्रायात् ततस्तु त्वरितो दारुकेण सहाच्युतः।
en: See us again soon, O Janarddana!-Then Keshava of unfading glory proceeded with Daruka.

sn: वासुदेवे गते राजन् धृतराष्ट्र जनेश्वरम्॥ आश्वासयदमेयात्मा व्यासो लोकनमस्कृतः।
en: After Vasudeva had gone, O king, Vyasa, worshipped of the whole world, began to comfort king Dhritarashtra.

sn: वासुदेवोऽपि धर्मात्मा कृतकृत्यो जगाम ह॥ शिबिर हास्तिनपुराद् दिदृक्षुः पाण्डवान् नृप।
en: The righteous Vasudeva departed, having gained his object successfully, from Hastinapura, for seeing the camp and the Pandavas.

sn: आगम्य शिबिरं सोऽभ्यगच्छत पाण्डवान्। तच तेभ्यः समाख्याय सहितस्तैः समाहितः॥
en: Arrived at the camp, he went to the Pandavas, Informing them of everything he took his seat with them."

en: Dhritarashtra said "Struck on the head, his thighs broken, laid low on the ground, exceedingly proud, what, O Sanjaya, did my son then say? King Duryodhana was highly wrathful and his enmity to the sons of Pandu was deep-scated. When therefore, this great calamity befell him, what did he next say on the field?"

en: Sanjaya said "Hear me, O king, as I describe what took place. Listen, O king, to what Duryodhana said when possessed by misfortune.

en: With his thighs broken, the king, O king, covered with dust, collected his flowing locks, looking all sides.

en: Having with difficulty gathered his locks, he began to sigh like a serpent. Filled with ire and with tears flowing quickly from his eyes, he looked at me. He struck his arms against the Earth for some time like an infuriate elephant.

en: Shaking his loose locks, and gnashing his teeth, he began to blame the eldest son of Alas, I who had Shantanu's son Bhishma for my protector, and Karna, that foremost of all warriors, Gotama's son, Shakuni. Drona, Ashvatthaman, the heroic Shalya, and Kritavarman, have been reduced to this plight. It seems that Destiny is all powerful.

en: I was the master of eleven Chamus of troops and yet I have come by this plight. O mighty-armed one, no one can control Destiny.

en: Those of my side that have escaped alive from this battle should be informed how I have been struck down by Bhimasena against the rules of fair fight.

en: Many unfair and sinful acts have been perpetrated towards Bhurishravas, Bhishma, and Drona.

en: This is another very unfair act that the cruel Pandavas have perpetrated, for which, I am certain, they will incur the censure of all righteous men.

en: What pleasure can a pious man enjoy after having gained a victory by unfair acts? What wise man would approve of a person's disregarding the rules of equity?

en: What learned man would rejoice after having gained victory by such unfair means as that vile wretch, Vrikodara, the son of Pandu, is rejoicing himself in glee.

en: What can be more surprising then this viz., that Bhimasena in anger should with his foot touch the head of one like me while lying with my thighs broken.

en: Is that person, O Sanjaya, an honorable man who behaves thus towards a great man, endued with prosperity, living in the midst of friends?

en: My parents are not ignorant of the rules of warfare. As directed by me, O Sanjaya, tell them that are afflicted with grief these words: I have celebrated sacrifices, maintained a large number of servants properly governed the whole Earth with her seas, I stood on the heads of my living enemies.

en: I gave wealth of my kinsmen to the best of my power and I did what my friends liked. I withstood all my enemies. Who is there that is more fortunate than myself? I have marched through enemy's kingdoms and commanded kings as slaves I have acted lovingly towards all I loved and liked. Who is there more fortunate then myself!

en: I honored all my relations and looked to the well-being of all my dependants. I have observed the three objects of human existence. viz., Religion, Profit, and Pleasure. Who is there more fortunate then myself?

en: I commanded great kings, and acquired honor, unattainable by others, I always drove on the back of the very best of horses. Who is there more fortunate than myself?

en: I studied the Vedas and made gifts according to the ordinance. I have passed my life in happiness. By observing the duties of my own order, I have secured for myself many abodes of blessedness in the regions of eternity. Who is there more fortunate than myself?

en: By good luck, I have not been defeated in battle and subjected to the necessity of serving my foes as slaves. By good luck, O lord, it is only after my death that my rising Prosperity leaves me for waiting upon another!

en: I have met with that death which is desired by good Kshatriyas observant of the duties of their order. Who is there so fortunate as myself.

sn: दिष्ट्या नाहं परावृत्तो वैरात् प्राकृतवन्जितः॥ दिष्ट्या न विमति कांचिद् भजित्वा तु पराजितः। सुप्तं वाथं प्रमत्तं वा यथा हन्याद् विषेण वा॥ एवं व्युत्क्रान्तधर्मेण व्युत्क्रम्य समयं हतः।
en: By good luck, I was not defeated like an ordinary person. By good luck, I have not been defeated after I had done some mean act. Like killing a person who is aslecp or who is heedless, like killing one with poison, my destruction has taken place, for I have been killed unfairly against the rules of fair fight.

sn: अश्वत्थामा महाभागः कृतवर्मा च सात्वतः॥ कृपः शारद्वतश्चैव वक्तव्या वचनान्मम। अधर्मेण प्रवृत्तानां पाण्डवानामनेकशः॥ विश्वासं समयघ्नानां न यूयं गन्तुमर्हथ। वार्तिकांश्चाब्रवीद् राजा पुत्रस्ते सत्यविक्रमः॥ अधर्माद् भीमसेनेन निहतोऽहं यथा रणे।
en: The highly blessed Ashvatthaman, and Kritavarman, of the Satwata race, and Sharadvat's son Kripa, should be told these words of mine, viz.-. You should never place any confidence upon the Pandavas, those violators of rules who have committed many unrighteous acts. After this, your royal and bearers in these words:-I have, in battle, been killed by Bhimasena most unfairly.

sn: सोऽहं द्रोणं स्वर्गगतं कर्णशल्यावुभौ तथा॥ वृषसेनं महावीर्यं शकुनि चापि सौबलम्। जलसंधं महावीर्यं भगदत्तं च पार्थिवम्॥ सोमदत्तं महेष्वासं सैन्धवं च जयद्रथम्। दुःशासनपुरोगांश्च भ्रातृनात्मसमांस्तथा॥ दौःशासनिं च विक्रान्तं लक्ष्मणं चात्मजावुभौ। एतांश्चान्यांश्च सुबहून् मदीयांश्च सहस्रशः॥ पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यामि सार्थहीनो यथाऽध्वगः।
en: I am now like a moneyless wayfarer and shall follow suit with Drona who has already gone to heaven, with Karna and Shalya, with Vrishasena of great energy, with Shakuni the son of Subala, with Jalasandha of great valour, with king Bhagadatta, with Somadatta's son that mighty bowman, with Jayadratha the king of the Sindhuas, with all my brothers headed by Dusshasana and equal unto myself, with Dussasana's son of great prowess, and with Lakshmana my son, and thousands of others that fought for me.

sn: कथं भ्रातॄन् हताश्रुत्वा भर्तारं च स्वसा मम॥ रोरूयमाणा दुःखार्ता दुःशला सा भविष्यति।
en: Alas, how shall my sister laden with grief, live sorrowfully, after hearing of the death of her brothers and her husband.

description: Dhritarashtra's enquiring how Duryodhana met his death with his thighs broken and the last words that fell from him, Sanjaya narrates to the old king the lamentations of Duryodhanas his message to the three surviving Kauravas and his commands to inform his friend Charvaka of the circumstances of his death. The messengers' arrival to the camp of Drona's son. They communicate him his last words
sn: स्नुषाभिः प्रस्नुषाभिश्च वृद्धो राजा पिता मम॥ गान्धारीसहितश्चैव कां गतिं प्रतिपत्स्यति।
en: Alas, what shall be the condition of the old king, my father, with Gandhari, and his daughter-in-law and grand-daughter-in-law!

description: Dhritarashtra's enquiring how Duryodhana met his death with his thighs broken and the last words that fell from him, Sanjaya narrates to the old king the lamentations of Duryodhanas his message to the three surviving Kauravas and his commands to inform his friend Charvaka of the circumstances of his death. The messengers' arrival to the camp of Drona's son. They communicate him his last words
sn: नूनं लक्ष्मणमातापि हतपुत्रा हतेश्वरा॥ विनाशं यास्यति क्षिप्रं कल्याणी पृथलोचना।
en: Forsooth, the beautiful and large-eyed mother of Lakshmana, rendered sonless and husbandless will soon die.

description: Dhritarashtra's enquiring how Duryodhana met his death with his thighs broken and the last words that fell from him, Sanjaya narrates to the old king the lamentations of Duryodhanas his message to the three surviving Kauravas and his commands to inform his friend Charvaka of the circumstances of his death. The messengers' arrival to the camp of Drona's son. They communicate him his last words
sn: यदि जानाति चार्वाका परिवाड् वाग्विशारदः॥ करिष्यति महाभागो ध्रुवं चापचितिं मम।
en: If Charvaka, the mendicant devotee, who is a master of speech, learns everything he will forsooth avenge my death.

description: Dhritarashtra's enquiring how Duryodhana met his death with his thighs broken and the last words that fell from him, Sanjaya narrates to the old king the lamentations of Duryodhanas his message to the three surviving Kauravas and his commands to inform his friend Charvaka of the circumstances of his death. The messengers' arrival to the camp of Drona's son. They communicate him his last words
sn: समन्तपञ्चके पुण्ये त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुते॥ अहं निधनमासाद्य लोकान् प्राप्स्यामि शाश्वतान्। ततो जनसहस्राणि बाष्पपूर्णानि मारिष॥ प्रलापं नृपतेः श्रुत्वा व्यद्रवन्त दिशो दश।
en: By dying upon the sacred field of Samantapanchaka, celebrated over the three worlds, I shall, forsooth, go to the blessed abode of eternity.'-Then, having heard these lamentations of the king, O sire, thousands of men, with eyes full of tears, fled away in all directions.

description: Dhritarashtra's enquiring how Duryodhana met his death with his thighs broken and the last words that fell from him, Sanjaya narrates to the old king the lamentations of Duryodhanas his message to the three surviving Kauravas and his commands to inform his friend Charvaka of the circumstances of his death. The messengers' arrival to the camp of Drona's son. They communicate him his last words
sn: ससागरवना घोरा पृथिवी सचराचरा॥ चचालाथ सनिर्हादा दिशश्चैवाविलाभवन्।
en: The whole earth, with her forests and seas, with all her mobile and immobile creatures, began to shake and produce a loud noise. All the points of the horizon were covered with darkness.

description: Dhritarashtra's enquiring how Duryodhana met his death with his thighs broken and the last words that fell from him, Sanjaya narrates to the old king the lamentations of Duryodhanas his message to the three surviving Kauravas and his commands to inform his friend Charvaka of the circumstances of his death. The messengers' arrival to the camp of Drona's son. They communicate him his last words
sn: ते द्रोणपुत्रमासाद्य यथावृत्तं न्यवेदयन्॥ व्यवहारं गदायुद्धे पार्थिवस्य च पातनम्।
en: Repairing to Drona's son, the messengers communicated to him all that had taken place regarding the conduct of the mace-fight and the fall of the king.

description: Dhritarashtra's enquiring how Duryodhana met his death with his thighs broken and the last words that fell from him, Sanjaya narrates to the old king the lamentations of Duryodhanas his message to the three surviving Kauravas and his commands to inform his friend Charvaka of the circumstances of his death. The messengers' arrival to the camp of Drona's son. They communicate him his last words
sn: तदाख्याय ततः सर्वे द्रोणपुत्रस्य भारत। ध्यात्वा च सुचिरं कालं जग्मुरार्ता यथागतम्॥
en: Having represented everything to Drona's son, O Bharata, all of them remained in a pensive mood for a long time and then went away, laden with grief, to the places whence they came.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: संजय उवाच वार्तिकाणां सकाशात् तु श्रुत्वा दुर्योधनं हतम्। हतशिष्टास्ततो राजन् कौरवाणां महारथाः॥ विनिर्भिन्नाः शितैर्बाणैर्गदातोमरशक्तिभिः। अश्वत्थामा कृपश्चैव कृतवर्मा च सात्वतः॥ त्वरिता जवनैरश्वैरायोधनमुपागमन्। तत्रापश्यन् महात्मानं धार्तराष्ट्र निपातितम्॥ प्रभग्नं वायुवेगेन महाशालं यथा वने। भूमौ विचेष्टमानं तं रुधिरेण समुक्षितम्॥ महागजमिवारण्ये व्याधेन विनिपातितम्। विवर्तमानं वहुशो रुधिरौधपरिप्लुतम्॥
en: Sanjaya said “Having heard of Duryodhana's fall from the messengers, those powerful car-warriors, the remnant of the Kaurava arıny greatly wounded with keen arrows and maces and lances and darts-those three, viz.. Ashvathaman and Kripa and Kritavarman of the Satwata race, riding at breakneck pace on their swift chargers came to the field of battle. They saw there the high-souled son of Dhritarashtra lying low on the ground, like a gigantic Shala tree laid low in the forest by a storm. They saw him suffering on the mother Earth and covered with blood like a powerful elephant in the forest laid low by a hunter. They saw him suffering and bleeding profusely.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: यदृच्छया निपतितं चक्रमादित्यगोचरम्। महावातसमुत्थेन संशुष्कमिव सागरम्॥ पूर्णचन्द्रमिव व्योम्नि तुषारावृतमण्डलम्। रेणु ध्वस्तं दीर्घभुजं मातङ्गमिव विक्रमे॥
en: Indeed, they saw him lying on the ground like the Sun dropped on the Earth or like the Occan dried by a mighty wind, or like the Full Moon in the sky with his disc covered with fog. Like an elephant in prowess and possessing long arms, the king lay on the Earth, covered with dust.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: वृतं भूतगणैोरैः क्रव्यादैश्च समन्ततः। यथा धनं लिप्समानैर्भूत्यैर्नृपतिसत्तमम्॥
en: Around hiin were many terrible creatures and carnivorous animals, like satellites sceking wealth around a king in state.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: भृकुटीकृतवक्त्रान्तं क्रोधादुवृत्तचक्षुषम्। सामर्षं तं नरव्याघ्रं व्याघ्रं निपतितं यथा।॥
en: His forehead was contracted into furrows of rage and his eyes were rolling in anger. They saw the king, that foremost of men, full of rage, like a tiger struck down (by hunters).

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: ते तं दृष्ट्वा महेष्वासं भूतले पतितं नृपम्। मोहमभ्यागमन् सर्वे कृपप्रभृतयो रथाः।। १० ।
en: Seeing the king laid low on the Earth, those great bow-inen, viz., Kripa and others became stupefied.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: अवतीर्य रथेभ्यश्च प्राद्रवन् राजसंनिधौ। दुर्योधनं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य सर्वे भीमावुपाविशन्॥
en: Getting down from their cars, they ran towards the king. Seeing Duryodhana, all of them sat on the Earth around him.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: ततो द्रौणिर्महाराज बाष्पपूर्णेक्षणः श्वसन्। उवाच भरतश्रेष्ठं सर्वलोकेश्वरेश्वरम्॥
en: Then Drona's son, O king, with eyes full of tears and sighting like a snake, said these words to that chief of Bharata's race, that foremost of all the kings on Earth.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: न नूनं विद्यते सत्यं मानुषे किंचिदेव हि। यत्र त्वं पुरुषव्याघ्र शेषे पांसुषु रूषितः॥
en: Forsooth, there is nothing permanent in the world of men, since you, O foremost of men, lic on the mother Earth covered with dust.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: भूत्वा हि नृपतिः पूर्वं समाज्ञाप्य च मेदिनीम्। कथमेकोऽद्य राजेन्द्र तिष्ठसे निर्जने वने।॥
en: You were a king who had issued your commands to all the world! Why then, O foremost of kings, do you lie alone on the bare ground?

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: दुःशासनं न पश्यामि नापि कर्णं महारथम्। नापि तान् सुहृदः सर्वान् किमिदं भरतर्षभ॥
en: I do not see Dussasana by you, nor the great car-warrior Karna, nor those hundreds of your friends. What is this, O foremost of men?

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: दुःखं नूनं कृतान्तस्य गतिं ज्ञातुं कथंचन। लोकानां च भवान् यत्र शेषे पांसुषु रूषितः॥
en: Forsooth, it is difficult to learn the ways of Yama, since you, O lord of all the world, thus lie on the bare ground covered with dust.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: एष मूर्धाभिषिक्तानामग्रे गत्वा परंतपः। सतृणं ग्रसते पांसुं पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: Alas, this destroyer of foes used to trample at the head of all Kshatriyas that had their locks sprinkled with holy water at the time of coronation. Alas, he now eats the dust. Witness the reverses of fortune that time brings.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: क्व ते तदमलं छत्रं व्यजनं क्व च पार्थिव। सा च ते महतीं सेनां क्व गता पार्थिवोत्तमा॥
en: Where is that pure white umbrella of yours? Where is that fanning yak-tail also, O king? Where is that vast army of yours now gone, O best of kings?

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: दुर्विज्ञेया गतिर्नूनं कार्याणां कारणान्तरे। यद् वै लोकगुरुर्भूत्वा भवानेतां दशां गतः॥
en: The course of events is, forsooth, a mystery, since you, who were the master of the world, have been reduced to this state.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: अध्रुवा सर्वमत्र्येषु श्रीरूपालक्ष्यते भृशम्। भवतो व्यसनं दृष्ट्वा शक्रविस्पर्धिनो भृशम्॥
en: Forsooth, the prosperity of all mortals is very unstable, since you, who were equal unto Shakra himself, have now been reduced to such a miserable condition.'

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा दुःखितस्य विशेषतः। उवाच राजन् पुत्रस्ते प्राप्तकालमिदं वचः॥
en: Hearing these words of Ashvatthaman your son answered himn in words that were suited to the occasion.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: विमृज्य नेत्रे पाणिभ्यां शोकजं वाष्पमुत्सृजन्। कृपादीन् स तदा वीरान् सर्वानेव नराधिपः॥ ईदृशो लोकधर्मोऽयं धात्रा निर्दिष्ट उच्यते। विनाशः सर्वभूतानां कालपर्यायमागतः॥
en: He wiped his eyes with his hands and shed tears of grief again. The king then addressed all those heroes headed by Kripa and said *Subjection to death has been ordained by the Creator himself. Death comes to all in course of Time.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: सोऽयं मां समनुप्राप्तः प्रत्यक्षं भवतां हि यः। पृथिवीं पालयित्वाऽहमेतां निष्ठामुपागतः॥
en: That death has now come to me, before you all. I, who governed the whole Earth, I have now been reduced to this miserable state.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: दिष्ट्या नाहं परावृत्तो युद्धे कस्यांचिदापदि। दिष्ट्याहं निहतः पापैश्छलनैव विशेषतः॥
en: By good luck, I never turned back from battle, whatever misfortunes over-took me. By good luck, I have been killed by those sinful men, by the help of deceptive means.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: उत्साहश्च कृतो नित्यं मया दिष्ट्या युयुत्सता। दिष्ट्या चास्मिन् हतो युद्धे निहतज्ञातिबान्धवः॥
en: By good luck, while engaged in hostilities, I always showed courage and perseverance. By good luck, I am killed in battle, along with all my relatives and friends.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: दिष्ट्या च वोऽहं पश्यामि मुक्तानस्माजनक्षयात्। स्वस्तियुक्तांश्च कल्यांश्च तन्मे प्रियमनुत्तमम्॥
en: By good luck, I see you escaped alive from this great destruction, and are safe and sound! This is highly pleasing to me!

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: मा भवन्तो तप्यन्तां सौहृदानिधनेन मे। यदि वेदाः प्रमाणं वो जिता लोका मयाक्षयाः॥
en: Do not, from love grieve for me death! If the Vedas are in any way authoritative, I have certainly acquired many eternal regions!

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: मन्यमानः प्रभावं च कृष्णस्यामिततेजसः। तेन न च्यावितश्चाहं क्षत्रधर्मात् स्वनुष्ठितात्॥
en: I am not ignorant of the glory of Krishna. He had not made me disregard the Kshatriya duties!

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: स मया समनुप्राप्तो नास्मि शोच्यः कथंचन। कृतं भवद्भिः सदृशमनुरूपमिवात्मनः॥ यतितं विजये नित्यं दैवं तु दुरतिक्रमम्। एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं वाष्पव्याकुललोचनः॥
en: I have obtained him! No one should grieve for me. You have done what persons like you should do. You have always tried for my success. Destiny, however, is incapable of being defeated.'-Having said all this the king, with eyes bathed in tears, became silent, O king, agitated as he was with pain.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: तूष्णीं बभूव राजेन्द्र रुजासौ विह्वलो भृशम्। तथा दृष्ट्वा तु राजानं बाष्पशोकसमन्वितम्॥ द्रौणिः क्रोधेन जज्वाल यथा वह्निर्जगत्क्षये।
en: Seeing the king in tear and grief, Drona's son burned in anger like the fire at the universal dissolution.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: सच क्रोधसमाविष्टः पाणौ पाणिं निपीड्य च॥ बाष्पविह्वलया वाचा राजानमिदमब्रवीत्। पिता मे निहतः क्षुद्रैः सुनृशंसेन कर्मणा॥ न तथा तेन तप्यामि यथा राजंस्त्वयाऽद्य वै। शृणु चेदं वचो मह्यं सत्येन वदतः प्रभो॥ इष्टापूर्तेन दानेन धर्मेण सुकृतेन च।
en: Beside himself with anger he squeezed his hands, and addressing the king in a voice choked with tears, he said-'My father was killed by those wretches with a cruel contrivance. That act, however, do not pain me so keenly as this condition to which you have been reduced, O king, Listen to these words of mine which I swear by truth itself, O lord, and by all my acts of piety all my gifts, my religion and the religious merits I have won.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: अद्याहं सर्वपञ्चालान् वासुदेवस्य. पश्यतः॥ सर्वोपायैर्हि नेष्यामि प्रेतराजनिवेशनम्। अनुज्ञां तु महाराज भवान् मे दातुमर्हति॥ इति श्रुत्वा तु वचनं द्रोणपुत्रस्य कौरवः। मनसः प्रीतिजननं कृपं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ आचार्य शीघ्रं कलशं जलपूर्ण समानय। स तद् वचनमाज्ञाय राज्ञो ब्राह्मणसत्तमः॥ कलशं पूर्णमादाय राज्ञोऽन्तिकमुपागमत्।
en: I shall to-day, in the very presence of Vasudeva, dispatch all the Panchalas, by all means in my power, to the abode of Yama. You should O king, grant me permission.'-Hearing these words of Drona's son, that were highly pleasant, the Kuru king addressed Kripa, saying-'O preceptor, bring me soon a pot full of water.' — At these words of the king, that foremost of Brahmanas, soon brought a vessel full of water.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: तमब्रवीन्महाराज पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते॥ ममाज्ञया द्विजश्रेष्ठ द्रोणपुत्रोऽभिषिच्यताम्। सैनापत्येन भद्रं ते मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम्॥
en: Your son then, O king, said to Kripa-'Let the son of Drona, O foremost of Brahmanas, blessed by you, if you wish to do me good, be, at my command, appointed as generalissimo.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: राज्ञो नियोगाद् योद्धव्यं ब्राह्मणेन विशेषतः। वर्तता क्षत्रधर्मेण ह्येवं धर्मविदो विदुः॥
en: At the command of the king, even the Brahmana may fight, especially one who leads the life of Kshatriya. Those learned in the scriptures say this.'

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: राज्ञस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा कृपः शारद्वतस्तथा। द्रौणि राज्ञो नियोगेन सैनापत्येऽभ्यषेचयत्॥
en: Hearing these words of the king Kripa, the son of Sharadvat, installed Drona's son as generalissimo, at the mandate of the king.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: सोऽभिषिक्तो महाराज परिष्वज्य नृपोत्तमम्। प्रययौ सिंहनादेन दिशः सर्वा विनादयन्॥
en: After the ceremony, O King, Ashvathaman embraced that best of kings and left the place, having resounded the ten cardinal points with his war-cry.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: दुर्योधनोऽपि राजेन्द्र शोणितेन परिप्लुतः। तां निशां प्रतिपेदेऽथ सर्वभूतभयावहाम्॥
en: That best of kings, viz., Duryodhana, bathed in blood, began to pass there that night so dreadful to all creatures.

description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors' arrival at the battlefield. Ashvatthaman's lamentation at the sight of the fallen monarch and his reply. Ashvatthaman's vow and Duryodhana's command to Kripa for his being made their chief, the parting of the three warriors and Duryodhana's death
sn: अपक्रम्य तु ते तूर्णं तस्मादायोधनानृप। शोकसंविग्नमनसश्चिन्ताध्यानपराऽभवन्॥
en: Leaving quickly the field of battle, O king, those horses, with hearts shaken by grief, began to think anxiously and earnestly.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वती व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्॥
en: Having saluted Narayana, and Nara the foremost of all male beings, as also the goddess of learning Sarasvati, let us cry success.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: संजय उवाच ततस्ते सहिता वीराः प्रयाता दक्षिणामुखाः। उपास्तमनवेलायां शिविराभ्याशमागताः॥
en: Sanjaya said “Those heroes then in a body went towards the south. At sunset they reached a spot near the (Kuru) encampment.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: विमुच्य वाहांस्त्वरिता भीता समभवंस्तदा। गहनं देशमासाद्य प्रच्छन्ना न्यविशन्त ते॥
en: Letting loose their animals, they became very much frightened. Reaching then a forest, they secretly entered it.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: सेनानिवेशमभितो नातिदूरमवस्थिताः। निकृत्ता निशितैः शस्त्रैः समन्तात् क्षतविक्षताः॥ दीर्घमुष्णं च निःश्वस्य पाण्डवानेव चिन्तयतन्।
en: They took up their quarters there near the encampment. Wounded with many keen weapons, they breathed and sighted heavily, thinking of the Pandavas.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: श्रुत्वा च निनदं घोरं पाण्डवानां जयैषिणाम्॥ अनुसारभयाद् भीताः प्राङ्मुखाः प्राद्रवन् पुनः।
en: Hearing the loud noise set up by the victorious Pandavas, they feared a pursuit and therefore fled towards the east. were

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: ते मुहूर्तात् ततो गत्वा श्रान्तवाहाः पिपासिताः॥ नामृष्यन्त महेष्वासाः क्रोधामर्षवशं गताः। राज्ञो वधेन संतप्ता मुहूर्तं समवस्थिताः॥
en: Having gone for sometime, their animals became tired and they themselves stricken with thirst. Beside themselves with anger and vindictiveness, those great bowmen could not bear what had taken place, burning as they did with grief at the slaughter of the king. They, however, rested for a while.”

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अश्रद्धेयमिदं कर्म कृतं भीमेन संजय। यत् स नागायुतप्राणः पुत्रो मम निपातितः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said "The feat, O Sanjaya, that Bhima performed seems to be incredible, since my son who was struck down as endued with the strength of ten thousand elephants.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां वज्रसंहननो युवा। पाण्डवैः समरे पुत्रो निहतो मम संजय॥ न दिष्टमभ्यतिक्रान्तुं शक्यं गावल्गणे नरैः। यत् समेत्य रणे पाथैः पुत्रो मम निपातितः॥ अद्रिसारमयं नूनं हृदयं मम संजय। हतं पुत्रशतं श्रुत्वा यन्न दीर्णं सहस्रधा॥ कथं हि वृद्धमिथुनं हतपुत्रं भविष्यति। न ह्यहं पाण्डवेयस्य विषये वस्तुमुत्सहे॥
en: In the prime of life and having an adamantine body, he was not capable of being slain by any creatures. Alas, even such a son of mine was struck down by the Pandavas in battle. Forsooth, O Sanjaya, my heart is made of adamant, because it does not break into a thousand pieces even after hearing of the death of my hundred sons. Alas, what will be the condition of myself and my wife, an old couple, deprive of all children. I dare, not dwell in the kingdom of Pandu's son.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: कथं राज्ञः पिता भूत्वा स्वयं राजा च संजय। प्रेष्यभूतः प्रवर्तेयं पाण्डवेयस्य शासनात्॥
en: Having been the father of a king and a king myself, O Sanjaya, how shall I pass my days as a slave obeying he commands of Pandu's son.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: आज्ञाप्य पृथिवीं सर्वां स्थित्वा मूर्ध्नि च संजय। कथमद्य भविष्यामि प्रेष्यभूतो दुरन्तकृत्॥
en: Having commanded once the entire Earth and having trampled over the heads of all, O Sanjaya, how shall I live now as a wretched slave.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: कथं भीमस्य वाक्यानि श्रोतुं शक्ष्यामि संजय। येन पुत्रशतं पूर्णमेकेन निहतं मम॥
en: How shall I be able, O Sanjaya, to endure the words of Bhima who has alone killed a full hundred sons of mine?

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: कृतं सत्यं वचस्तस्य विदुरस्य महात्मनः। अकुर्वता वचस्तेन मम पुत्रेण संजय॥
en: The words of the great Vidura are now realised. Alas, my son, O Sanjaya, did not listen to those words.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: अधर्मेण हते तात पुत्रे दुर्योधने मम। कृतवर्मा कृपो द्रौणिः किमकुर्वत संजय॥
en: What, however, did Kritavarman and Kripa and Drona's son do after my son Duryodhana had been unfairly killed.”

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: संजय उवाच गत्वा तु तावका राजन् नातिदूरमवस्थिताः। अपश्यन्त वनं घोरं नानाद्रुमलतावृतम्॥
en: Sanjaya said "They had not proceeded far, O king, when they stopped, On seeing a dense forest covered with trees and creepers.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: ते मुहूर्तं तु विश्रम्य लब्धतोयैहयोत्तमैः। सूर्यास्तमनवेलायां समासेदुर्महद् वनम्॥
en: Having rested for a little while, they entered that great forest, proceeding on their cars drawn by their excellent horses whose thirst had been satisfied.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: नानामृगगणैर्जुष्टं नानापक्षिगणावृतम्। नानाद्रुमलताच्छन्नं नानाव्यालनिषेवितम्॥
en: That forest abounded with various kings of species of birds. And it was covered with many trees and creepers and was filled with numerous carnivorous creatures.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: नानातोयैः समाकीर्णं नानापुष्पोपशोभितम्। पद्मिनीशतसंछन्नं नीलोत्पलसमायुतम्॥
en: It was covered with many pools of water, adorned with various kinds of flowers, and lakes overgrown with blue lotuses.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: प्रविश्य तद् वनं घोरं वीक्षमाणाः समन्ततः। शाखासहस्रसंछन्नं न्यग्रोधं ददृशुस्ततः॥
en: Having entered that dense forest they looked about saw a gigantic banian tree with thousands of branches.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: उपेत्य तु तदा राजन् न्यग्रोधं ते महारथाः। ददृशुर्द्विपदां श्रेष्ठाः श्रेष्ठं तं वै वनस्पतिम्॥
en: Repairing to the shade of that banian, those great car-warriors, O king, those foremost of men, founded that to be the biggest tree in those forest.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: तेऽवतीर्य रथेभ्यश्च विप्रमुच्य च वाजिनः। उपस्पृश्य यथान्यायं संध्यामन्वासत प्रभो॥
en: Getting down from their cars, and letting loose their animals, they washed themselves and said their evening prayers.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: ततोऽस्तं पर्वतश्रेष्ठमनुप्राप्ते दिवाकरे। सर्वस्य जगतो धात्री शर्वरी समपद्यत॥ ग्रहनक्षत्रताराभिः सम्पूर्णाभिरलंकृतम्। नभोंऽशुकमिवाभाति प्रेक्षणीयं समन्ततः॥
en: The Sun then reached the setting hill, and Night, the mother of the universe, came. The sky, be spangled with planets and stars, shone alike an ornamented piece of brocade and presented a beautiful sight.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: इच्छया ते प्रवल्गन्ति ये सत्त्वा रात्रिचारिणः दिवाचराश्च ये सत्त्वास्ते निद्रावशमागताः॥
en: Creators, ranging in the night, began to howl and utter their cries at will, while they that range in the day began to sleep.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: रात्रिंचराणां सत्त्वानां निर्घोषोऽभूत् सुदारुणः। क्रव्यादाश्च प्रमुदिता घोरा प्राप्ता च शर्वरी॥
en: The night-ranging animals set up a dreadful noise. The carnivorous creatures were full of joy, and the night, as it advanced, became awful.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: तस्मिन् रात्रिमुखे घोरे दुःखशोकसमन्विताः। कृतवर्मा कृपो द्रौणिरुपोपविविशुः समम्॥
en: At that time filled with grief and sorrow, Kritavarman and Kripa and Drona's son all sat down together.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: तत्रोपविष्टाः शोचन्तो न्यग्रोधस्य समीपतः। तमेवार्थमतिक्रान्तं कुरुपाण्डवयोः क्षयम्॥
en: Seated under that banian, they began to express their sorrow regarding the destruction that had taken place of both the Kurus and the Pandavas.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: निद्रया च परीताङ्गा निषेदुर्धरणीतले। श्रमेण सुदृढं युक्ता विक्षता विविधैः शरैः॥
en: Feeling asleep they laid themselves down on the bare Earth. They had been greatly wounded with arrows.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: ततो निद्रावशं प्राप्तौ कृपभोजौ महारथौ। सुखोचितावदुःखार्ही निषण्णौ धरणीतले॥
en: The two great car-warriors, Kripa and Kritavarman, began to sleep. They ever deserving of happiness and undeserving of misery, slept on the bare ground.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: तौ तु सुप्तौ महाराज श्रमशोकसमन्वितौ। महार्हशयनोपेतौ भूमावेव ह्यनाथवत्॥
en: Indeed, O king, they, who had always slept on costly beds, not slept, like helpless persons, on the bare ground, worn out with fatigue and gricf.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: क्रोधामर्षवशं प्राप्तो द्रोणपुत्रस्तु भारत। न वै स्म स जगामाथ निद्रां सर्प इव श्वसन्॥
en: Subject to wrath and revenge, Drona's son, however, O Bharata, could not sleep, but continued to breathe like a snake.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: न लेभे स तु निद्रां वै दह्यमानो हि मन्युना। वीक्षाञ्चक्रे महाबाहुस्तद् वनं घोरदर्शनम्॥
en: Burning with rage he could not sleep. That mighty hero looked on all sides of that terrible forest.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: वीक्षमाणो वनोद्देशं नानसत्त्वैर्निषेवितम्। अपश्यत महाबाहुर्यग्रोधं वायसैर्युतम्॥
en: As he surveyed that forest filled with various kinds of creatures, the great warrior beheld large banian tree covered with crows.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: तत्र काकसहस्राणि तां निशां पर्यणामयन्। सुखं स्वपन्ति कौरव्य पृथक् पृथगुपाश्रयाः॥
en: On that banian thousands of crows roosted in the night. Each perching separately from its neighbour, those crows slept easily, O Kuru Chief.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: सुप्तेषु तेषु काकेषु विश्रव्येषु समन्ततः। सोऽपश्यत् सहसा यान्तमुलूकं घोरदर्शनम्॥
en: As, however, those birds were sleeping in security on every side, Ashvatthaman beheld a terrible owl suddenly appeared there.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: महास्वनं महाकायं हर्यक्षं बभ्रुपिङ्गलम्। सुदीर्घघोणानखरं सुपर्णमिव वेगितम्॥
en: Of frightful cries an huge body, with green eyes and tawny plumage, its nose and its talons were very large. And its speed was like that of Garuda.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: सोऽथ शब्दं मृदुं कृत्वा लीयमान इवाण्डजः। न्यग्रोधस्य ततः शाखां प्रार्थयामास भारत॥
en: Crying softly that winged creature O Bharata, secretly approached the branches of that banian tree.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: संनिपत्य तु शाखायां न्यग्रोधस्य विहङ्गमः। सुप्ताञ्जधान सुबहून् वायसान् वायसान्तकः॥
en: That sky-ranger, that slayer of crows, alighting on one of the branches of the banian, killed a large number of his sleeping enemies.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: केषांचिदच्छिनत् पक्षाशिरांसि च चकर्त ह। चरणांश्चैव केषांचिद् बभञ्ज चरणायुधः॥ क्षणेनाहन् स बलवान् येऽस्य दृष्टिपथे स्थिताः।
en: He tore the wings of some and cut off the heads of others with his sharp talons and broke the legs of many. Highly strong as he was, he killed many that fell down before his eyes. was

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: तेषां शरीरावयवैः शरीरैश्च विशाम्पते॥ न्यग्रोधमण्डलं सर्वं संछन्नं सर्वतोऽभवत्।
en: With the limbs and bodies, O king, of the slain crows, the ground covered by the spreading branches of the banian, overspread on all sides.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: तांस्तु हत्वा ततः काकान् कौशिको मुदितोऽभवत्।।४३ प्रतिकृत्य यथाकामं शत्रूणां शत्रुसूदनः।
en: Having killed those crows, the owl became overjoyed like a slayer of foes after having dealt with his foes according to his pleasure.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा सोपधं कर्म कौशिकेन कृतं निशि॥ तद्भावकृतसंकल्पो द्रोणिरेकोऽन्वचिन्तयत्।
en: Witnessing that deed perpetrated in the night by the owl, Drona's son began to reflect on it, desirous of guiding his own conduct after that example.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: उपदेशः कृतोऽनेन पक्षिणा मम संयुगे॥ शत्रूणां क्षपणे युक्तः प्राप्तः कालश्च मे मतः।
en: He said to him, "This owl teaches me a lesson in battle. Bent as I am upon the destruction of the enemy, the time for action is come.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: नाद्य शक्या मया हन्तुं पाण्डवा जितकाशिनः॥ बलवन्तः कृतोत्साहाः प्राप्तलक्ष्याः प्रहारिणः।
en: The victorious Pandavas are incapable of being killed by me! They are possessed of power and perseverance, sure of aim, and skilled in smiting.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: राज्ञः सकाशात् तेषां तु प्रतिज्ञातो वधो मया॥ पतङ्गाग्निसमां वृत्तिमास्थायात्मविनाशिनीम्।
en: In the presence, however, of the king I have promised to destroy them. I have thus promised to perform a deed that would bring on my own destruction like an insect trying to rush into a burning fire.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: न्यायतो युध्यमानस्य प्राणत्यागो न संशयः॥ छद्मना च भवेत् सिद्धिः शत्रूणां च क्षयो महान्। तत्र संशयितादाद् योऽर्थो निःसंशयो भवेत्॥
en: If I were to fight fairly with them. I shall, forsooth, have to lay down my life! By deceitful act, however, I may yet get success and a great destruction may overtake my enemies.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: तं जना बहुः मन्यन्ते ये च शास्त्रविशारदाः। यचाप्यत्र भवेद् वाच्यं गर्हितं लोकनिन्दितम्॥ कर्तव्यं तन्मनुष्येण क्षत्रधर्मेण वर्तता। निन्दितानि च सर्वाणि कुत्सितानि पदे पदे॥ सोपधानि कृतान्येव पाण्डवैरकृतात्मभिः।
en: People generally, as also those well-read in the scriptures, always prefer means which are certain to those which are uncertain. Censure and bad name, which soever this act may engender, ought to be incurred by a person who leads the life of a Kshatriya. The sinful Pandavas have, at every step, perpetrated very ugly, censurable and deceitful acts.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: अस्मिन्नर्थे पुरा गीता श्रूयन्ते धर्मचिन्तकैः॥ श्लोका न्यायमवेक्षद्भिस्तत्त्वार्थास्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः।
en: Regarding this matter, certain ancient verses, full of truth, are heard, sung by truthseeing and righteous persons.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: परिश्रान्ते विदीर्णे वा भुञ्जाने वापि शत्रुभिः॥ प्रस्थाने वा प्रवेशे वा प्रहर्तव्यं रिपोर्बलम्।
en: They are:-The enemy's force, even which fatigued, or wounded, or while eating, or when retiring, or when resting within their camp, should be beaten.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: निद्रार्तमर्धरात्रे च तथा नष्टप्रणायकम्॥ भिन्नयोधं बलं यच्च द्विधा युक्तं च यद् भवेत्। इत्येवं निश्चयं चक्रे सुप्तानां निशि मारणे॥ पाण्डूनां सह पञ्चालैोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान्।
en: They shouid be equally treated when sleeping at dead of night, or when reft of commanders, or when routed, or when labouring under an error.'-Having thought thus, the valiant son of Drona formed the resolution of killing during the night the sleeping Pandavas and the Panchalas,

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: स क्रूरां मतिमास्थाय विनिश्चित्य मुहुर्मुहुः॥ सुप्तौ प्राबोधयत् तौ तु मातुलं भोजमेव च।
en: Having formed this wicked resolution and promised to execute it, he awoke both his maternal uncle and the chief of the Bhojas. a

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: तौ प्रबुद्धौ महात्मानौ कृपभोजौ महाबलौ॥ नोत्तरं प्रतिपद्येतां तत्र युक्तं ह्रिया वृतौ।
en: Awakened from sleep, those two illustrious and powerful persons, viz., Kripa and the Bhoja chief, heard Ashvatthaman's scheme, Filled with shame, both of them could not give a suitable reply.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: स मुहूर्तमिव ध्यात्वा बाष्यविह्वलमब्रवीत्॥ हतो दुर्योधनो राजा एकवीरो महाबलः। यस्यार्थे वैरमस्माभिरासक्तं पाण्डवैः सह॥ एकाकी बहुभिः क्षुदैराहवे शुद्धविक्रमः। पातितो भीमसेनेन एकादशचमूपतिः॥
en: Having reflected for short time Ashvatthaman said with tearful eyes,-King Duryodhana, they only hero of great might, for whose sake we were fighting with the Pandavas, has been killed. Deserted and alone through he was, the master of eleven Akshauhinis of soldiers that hero of unsullied prowess has been struck down by Bhimasena in battle.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: वृकोदरेण क्षुद्रेण सुनृशंसमिदं कृतम्। मूर्धाभिषिक्तस्य शिरः पादेन परिमृद्नता॥
en: Another wicked act has been perpetrated by the mean Vrikodara for the latter has touched with his foot the head of a crowned person.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: विनर्दन्ति च पञ्चाला: श्वेलन्ति च हसन्ति च। धमन्ति शङ्खाशतशो हृष्टा जन्ति च दुन्दुभीन्॥
en: The Panchalas are sending up loud roars and cries and loud bursts of laughter. Overjoyed, they are blowing their conchs and beating their drums.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: वादित्रघोषस्तुमुलो विमिश्रः शङ्खनिःस्वनैः। अनिलेनेरितो घोरो दिशः पूरयतीव ह॥
en: The loud sound of their instruments, mingled with the blare of conchs, is fearful to the ear, and carried by the winds, is filling all the points of the horizon.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: अश्वानां हेषमाणानां गजानां चैव बुंहताम्। सिंहनादश्च शूराणां श्रूयते सुमहानयम्॥
en: Loud also is the neighing of their steeds and the grunting of their elephants and the roaring of their warriors.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: दिशं प्राची समाश्रित्य हृष्टानां गच्छतां भृशम्। रथनेमिस्वनाश्चैव श्रूयन्ते लोमहर्षणाः॥
en: That defending noise made by the rejoicing warriors as they are going to their quarters, as also the clatter of their car-wheels, comes to us from the east.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: पाण्डवैर्धार्तराष्ट्राणां यदिदं कदनं कृतम्। वयमेव त्रयः शिष्टा अस्मिन् महति वैशसे॥
en: So great has been the havoc made by the Pandavas on the Dhartarashtras that we three are the only survivors.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: केचिन्नागशतप्राणाः केचित् सर्वास्त्रकोविदाः। निहताः पाण्डवेयैस्ते मन्ये कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: Some were gifted with the strength of a hundred elephants and some were masters of all weapons. Yet they have been killed by the son of Pandu. I consider this to be an instance of the reverses caused by Destiny.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: एवमेतेन भाव्यं हि नूनं कार्वेण तत्त्वतः। यथा ह्यस्येदृशी निष्ठा कृतकार्येऽपि दुष्करे॥
en: Truly, this is the end of which such acts leads. Although the Pandavas have achieved such difficult feats, yet this should be the result of those feats.

description: Three survivors of the Kuru army proceed to south. They see a huge banian tree and sleep under it, Kripa and Kritavarman falls asleep, Ashvatthaman awakes them. The latter unfolds to the former his scheme of killing the Pandavas.
sn: भवेतास्तु यदि प्रज्ञा न मोहादपनीयते। व्यापन्नेऽस्मिन् महत्यर्थे यन्नः श्रेयस्तदुच्यताम्॥
en: If you have not lost your wisdom out of stupefaction, then say what is proper for us to do under these circumstances.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: कृप उवाच श्रुतं ते वचनं सर्वं यद् यदुक्तं त्वया विभो। ममापि तु वचः किंचिच्छृणुष्वाद्य महाभुजा. १॥
en: Kripa Said “We have heard all that you have said, O powerful one! Listen, now, to a few words of mine, O mighty-armed one!

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: आबद्धा मानुषाः सर्वे निबद्धाः कर्मणोर्द्वयोः। दैवे पुरुषकारे च परं ताभ्यां न विद्यते॥
