en: All men are subjected to, and governed by, these two forces, viz., Destiny and Manliness. There is nothing superior to these two.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: न हि दैवेन सिध्यन्ति कार्याण्येकेन सत्तम। न चापि कर्मणैकेन द्वाभ्यां सिद्धस्तु योगतः॥
en: Success is not the out come of destiny alone nor of manliness alone, O best of men! Success results from the union of the two.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: ताभ्यामुभाभ्यां सर्वार्था निबद्धा अधमोत्तमाः। प्रवृत्ताश्चैव दृश्यन्ते निवृत्ताश्चैव सर्वशः॥
en: All objects great and low, result from a union of those two. In the whole world, it is through these two that men either actor abstain.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: पर्जन्यः पर्वते वर्षन् किन्नु साधयते फलम्। कृष्ट क्षेत्रे तथा वर्षन् किन्न साधयते फलम्॥
en: No result is produced by the clouds pouring upon a mountain. But mighty results are produced by their pouring upon a cultivated field.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: उत्थानं चाप्यदैवस्य ह्यनुत्थानं च दैवतम्। ब्र्यं भवति सर्वत्र पूर्वस्तत्र विनिश्चयः॥
en: Manliness, where destiny is not auspicious, and want of manliness, where destiny is auspicious, both these are fruitless. What I have said before (about the union of the two) is all true.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: सुवृष्टे च यथा देवे सम्यक् क्षेत्रे च कर्षिते। बीजं महागुणं भूयात् तथा सिद्धिर्हि मानुषी॥
en: If the rains properly moisten a wellcultivated field the seed produces great results. Such is hymen success.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: तयोर्दैवं विनिश्चित्य स्वयं चैव प्रवर्तते। प्राज्ञाः पुरुषकारेषु वर्तन्ते दाक्ष्यमाश्रिताः॥
en: Sometimes, having settled a course of events, destiny acts of itself. For all that, the wise, always take recourse to manliness.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: ताभ्यां सर्वे हि कार्यार्था मनुष्याणां नरर्षभ। विचेष्टन्तः स्म दृश्यन्ते निवृत्तास्तु तथैव च।॥
en: All human acts, O foremost of men, are accomplished by the aid of these two together. Influenced by these two, men either actor abstain.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: कृतः पुरुषकारश्च सोऽपि दैवेन सिध्यति। तथास्य कर्मणः कर्तुरभिनिवर्तते फलम्॥
en: Recourse may be had to manliness. But manliness succeeds through destiny. By the influence of destiny one who sets himself to work, attain to success.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: उत्थानं च मनुष्याणां दक्षाणां दैववर्जितम्। अफलं दृश्यते लोके सम्यगप्युपपादितम्॥
en: The exertion, however, of even a capable man, even when well-directed, is, without the help of destiny, seen to be fruitless in the world.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: तत्रालसा मनुष्याणां ये भवन्त्यमनस्विनः। उत्थानं ते विगर्हन्ति प्राज्ञानां तन्न रोचते॥
en: Idle and dull men in this world disapprove of manliness. This, however, is not the view of the wise.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: प्रायशो हि कृतं कर्म नाफलं दृश्यते भुवि। अकृत्वा च पुनर्दुःखं कर्म पश्येन्महाफलम्॥
en: Generally no act ever becomes fruitless in the world. The want manliness again produces grave misery.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: चेष्टामकुर्वल्लभते यदि किंचिद् यदृच्छया। यो वा न लभते कृत्वा दुर्दर्शी तावुभावपि॥
en: There is hardly seen a person who obtains something of itself without haying made any exertion, as also one who does not obtain anything even after exertion.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: शक्नोति जीवितुं दक्षो नालसः सुखमेधते। दृश्यन्ते जीवलोकेऽस्मिन् दक्षाः प्रायो हितैषिणः॥ १५
en: One who is active is capable of supporting life. He, who is idle, is always unhappy. It is generally seen in this world that active men are always inspired by the desire of earning good.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: यदि दक्षः समारम्भात् कर्मणो नाश्नुते फलम्। नास्य वाच्यं भवेत् किंचिल्लब्धव्यं वाधिगच्छति॥
en: If an active man succeeds in gaining his object or fails to obtain the fruit of his acts, he does not become the but of censure in any way. one

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: अकृत्वा कर्म यो लोके फलं विन्दति धिष्ठितः। स तु वक्तव्यतां याति द्वेष्यो भवति भूयशः॥
en: If, however, any in the world luxuriously enjoys the fruits of action without exerting for the same, he generally incurs ridicule and becomes an object of hatred.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: एवमेतदनादृत्य वर्तते यस्त्वतोऽन्यथा। स करोत्यात्मनोऽनर्थानेष बुद्धिमतां नयः॥
en: He, who, neglecting this rule about action, liveth otherwise, is said to injure himself. This is the opinion held by the intelligent.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: हीनं पुरुषकारेण यदि दैवेन वा पुनः। कारणाभ्यामथैताभ्यामुत्थानमफलं भवेत्॥
en: Exertion generally becomes fruitless, because of these reasons, viz., destiny without manliness, and manliness without destiny.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: हीनं पुरुषकारेण कर्म त्विह न सिद्ध्यति। दैवतेभ्यो नमस्कृत्य यस्त्वर्थान् सम्यगीहते॥ दक्षो दाक्षिण्यसम्पन्नो न स मोधैर्विहन्यते।
en: Without manliness, no act in this world becomes successful. An active and clever man however, who, having bowed down to the celestials, seeks to achieve his object, is never lost.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: सम्यगीहा पुनरियं यो वृद्धानुपसेवते॥ आपृच्छति च यच्छ्रेयः करोति च हितं वचः।
en: Similarly a person is crowned with success, who duly waits upon the aged, asks of them what is for his food, and obeys their good advice.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: उत्थायोत्थाय हि सदा प्रष्टव्या वृद्धसम्मताः॥ ते स्म योगे परं मूलं तन्मूला सिद्धिरुच्यते।
en: One engaged in a work should seek the advice of those approved by the aged. These men are the means, and success depends on means.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: वृद्धानां वचनं श्रुत्वा योऽभ्युत्थानं प्रयोजयेत्॥ उत्थानस्य फलं सम्यक् तदा स लभतेऽचिरात्।
en: He who exert after listening to the words of the old, soon reaps abundant fruits.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: रागात् क्रोधाद् भयाल्लोभाद् योऽर्थानीहति मानवः॥ अनीशचावमानी च स शीघ्रं भ्रश्यते श्रियः।
en: He, who, without reverence and respect for persons competent to give him good advice, seeks to accomplish his object under the influence of anger, fear, and avarice, soon loses his prosperity.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: सोऽयं दुर्योधनेनार्थो लुब्धेनादीर्घदर्शिना॥ असमर्थ्य समारब्धो मूढत्वादविचिन्ततः।
en: Moved his covetousness and deprived of foresight, this Duryodhana had, without taking advice, foolishly sought the accomplishment of an ill-formed object.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: हितबुद्धीननादृत्य सम्मन्त्रसाधुभिः सह॥ वार्यमाणोऽकरोद् वैरं पाण्डवैर्गुणवत्तरैः।
en: Disregarding all his well-wishers and under the advice of only the evil-minded, he had, though dissuaded, created enmities with the Pandavas, who are his superiors in all good qualities.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: पूर्वमप्यतिदुःशीलो न धैर्यं कर्तुमर्हति॥ तपत्यर्थे विपन्ने हि मित्राणां न कृतं वचः।
en: He had, from the very commencement been very wicked. He could not check himself. He did not satisfy the wishes of friends. For all that, he is now sunk in grief and calamity.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: अनुवर्तामहे यत्तु तं वयं पापपूरुषम्॥ अस्मानप्यनयस्तस्मात् प्राप्तोऽयं दारुणो महान्।
en: Regarding ourselves, since we have followed that sinful wretch, this great calamity has, therefore befallen us.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: अनेन तु ममाद्यापि व्यसनेनोपतापिता॥ बुद्धिश्चिन्तयते किंचित् स्वं श्रेयो नावबुद्ध्यते।
en: This great calamity has burnt my good sense. Plunged in thought I fail to see what is for our good.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: मुह्यता तु मनुष्येण प्रष्टव्याः सुहृदो जनाः॥ तत्रास्य बुद्धिर्विनयस्तत्र श्रेयश्च पश्यति।
en: A man that is beside himself should seek the advice of his friends. In friends consists his understanding, his humility and his prosperity.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: ततोऽस्य मूलं कार्याणां बुद्ध्या निश्चित्य वै बुधाः॥३१ तेऽत्र पृष्टा यथा ब्रूयुस्तत् कर्तव्यं तथा भवेत्।
en: His actions should be guided by them. He should do which his intelligent friends, having settled by their understanding, should advise.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: ते वयं धृतराष्ट्रं च गान्धारी च समेत्य ह॥ उपपृच्छामहे गत्वा विदुरं च महामतिम्।
en: Let us, therefore, repair to Dhritarashtra and gandhari and the great Vidura, and ask them as what we should do.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: ते पृष्टास्तु वदेयुर्यच्छ्रेयो नः समनन्तरम्॥ तदस्माभिः पुनः कार्यमिति मे नैष्ठिकी मतिः।
en: Asked by us, they will advice us regarding our good. We should do what they say, this is my resolution.

description: .-CONTD. Kripa's reply promising to help Ashvatthaman if the latter would fight the next morning
sn: अनारम्भात् तु कार्याणां नार्थः सम्पद्यते क्वचित्॥ कृते पुरुषकारे तु येषां कार्यं न सिद्ध्यति। दैवेनोपहतास्ते तु नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥
en: Those men whose acts do not succeed even after the exertion, should, forsooth, be regarded as afflicted by destiny."

sn: संजय उवाच कृपस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा धर्मार्थसहितं शुभम्। अश्वत्थामा महाराज दुःखशोकसमन्वितः॥
en: Sanjaya Said "Hearing these auspicious, moral and profitable words of Kripa, Ashvatthaman, O king, became beside himself with sorrow and grief.

sn: दह्यमानस्तु शोकेन प्रदीप्तेनाग्निना यथा। क्रूरं मनस्ततः कृत्वा तावुभौ प्रत्यभाषत॥ पुरुषे पुरुषे बुद्धिर्या या भवति शोभना। तुष्यन्ति च पृथक् सर्वे प्रज्ञया स्वया स्वया।॥
en: Burning with grief, as if with fire, he formed a wicked resolution and then addressed them both, saying, understanding is different in different men. Each man, however, is pleased with his own understanding,

sn: सर्वो हि मन्यते लोक आत्मानं बुद्धिमत्तरम्। सर्वस्यात्मा बहुमतः सर्वात्मानं प्रशंसति॥ ते
en: Every man considers himself more intelligent than others. Every one respects and praises his own understanding.

sn: सर्वस्य हि स्वका प्रज्ञा साधुवादे प्रतिष्ठिता। परबुद्धिं च निन्दन्ति स्वां प्रशंसन्ति चासकृत्॥
en: Every one praises his own wisdom. Every one speaks ill of the wisdom of others, and well of his own, in all cases.

sn: कारणान्तरयोगेन योगे येषां समागतिः। अन्योन्येन च तुष्यन्ति बहु मन्यन्ति चासकृत्॥
en: Men whose opinions agree with regard to any that is not achieved, become gratified with and praise one another.

sn: तस्यैव तु मनुष्यस्य सा सा बुद्धिस्तदा तदा। कालयोगे विपर्यासं प्राप्यान्योन्यं विपद्यते॥
en: Again the opinions of the same persons, overwhelmed with reverses bought on by the influence of time, become opposed to another.

sn: विचित्रत्वात् तु चित्तानां मनुष्याणां विशेषतः। चित्तवैक्लव्यमासाद्य सा सा बुद्धिः प्रजायते॥
en: On account of the diversity of human intellects, judgments necessarily differ.

sn: यथा हि वैद्यः कुशलो ज्ञात्वा व्याधि यथाविधि। भैषज्यं कुरुते योगात् प्रशमार्थमिति प्रभो॥ एवं कार्यस्य योगार्थं बुद्धिं कुर्वन्ति मानवाः। प्रज्ञया हि स्वया युक्तास्तां च निन्दन्ति मानवाः॥
en: As a skillful physician, having duly diagnosed a disease, prescribes a medicine by his intelligence for effecting a cure, so men, for the accomplishment of their works, use their intelligence, helped by their own wisdom. What they do is not approved by others.

sn: अन्यया यौवने मयों बुद्ध्या भवति मोहितः। मध्येऽन्यया जरायां तु सोऽन्यां रोचयते मतिम्॥
en: A man, in youth, had one kind of understanding. In middle age, he has not the same, and in the period of decay, a different kind of understanding prevails in him.

sn: व्यसनं वा महाघोरं समृद्धिं चापि तादृशीम्। अवाप्य पुरुषो भोज कुरुते बुद्धिवैकृतम्॥ एकस्मिन्नेव पुरुषे सा सा बुद्धिस्तदा तदा। भवत्यकृतधर्मत्वात् सा तस्यैव न रोचते॥
en: When fallen into terrible misfortune or when enjoying great prosperity, the understanding of a person, chief of the Bhojas, undergoes changes. In one and the same person, want of wisdom, the understanding becomes different at different times. Understanding which at one time is good becomes quite the opposite at another time.

sn: निश्चित्य तु यथाप्रज्ञं या मतिं साधु पश्यति। तया प्रकुरुते भवं सा तस्योद्योगकारिका॥
en: Having resolved, however, according to one's wisdom, he should try to carry out his resolution. Such resolution, therefore, should make him display his manliness.

sn: सर्वो हि पुरुषो भोज साध्वेतदिति निश्चितः। कर्तुमारभते प्रीतो मारणादिषु कर्मसु॥
en: All persons, O chief of the Bhojas, gladly undertake enterprises that lead to death, in the belief that those enterprises will be accomplished by them.

sn: सर्वे हि बुद्धिमाज्ञाय प्रज्ञां वापि स्वकां नराः। चेष्टन्ते विविधां चेष्टां हितमित्येव जानते॥
en: All men, relying on their own judgment and wisdom, try to accomplish various objects, knowing them to be beneficial.

sn: उपजाता व्यसनजा येयमद्य मतिर्ममा युवयोस्तां प्रवक्ष्यामि मम शोकविनाशिनीम्॥
en: The resolution that I have formed in my mind to-day for of great calamity and which will despell my grief, I will now disclose to both of you.

sn: प्रजापतिः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा कर्म तासु विधाय च। वर्णे वर्णे समाधत्ते ह्येकैकं गुणभाग गुणम्॥
en: Having created his creatures, the Creator assigned to each his occupation. As regards the different castes he gave to each a portion of excellence.

sn: ब्राह्मणे वेदमग्रयं तु क्षत्रिये तेज उत्तमम्। दाक्ष्य वैश्ये च शूद्रे च सर्ववर्णानुकूलताम्॥
en: To Brahmanas he assigned that foremost of all things, viz., the Veda. To the Kshatriya he gave superior energy. To the Vaishya he gave skill, and to the Shudra he gave the duty of serving the three other castes.

sn: अदान्तो ब्राह्मणोऽसाधुनिस्तेजाः क्षत्रियोऽधमः। अदक्षो निन्द्यते वैश्यः शूद्रश्च प्रतिकूलवान्॥
en: Hence a Brahmana without self-restraint is an object of censure. A Kshatriya who has no energy is mean. A Vaishya without skill is an object of blame, as also a Shudra who is void of humility.

sn: सोऽस्मि जात: कुले श्रेष्ठे ब्राह्मणानां सुपूजिते। मन्दभाग्यतयास्म्येतं क्षत्रधर्ममनुष्ठितः॥
en: I am born in a worshipful and high family of Brahmanas. Through ill-luck, however, I am loading the life of a Kshatriya.

sn: क्षत्रधर्मं विदित्वाहं यदि ब्राह्मण्यमाश्रितः। प्रकुर्यां सुमहत् कर्म न मे तत् साधुसम्मतम्॥
en: If, conversant as I am with Kshatriya duties, I revert now to the order of a Brahmana and achieve a great object (by assuming selfrestraint under such injuries), that course would not be compatible.

sn: धारयंश्च धनुर्दिव्यं दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि चाहवे। पितरं निहतं दृष्ट्वा किं नु वक्ष्यामि संसदि॥
en: I hold an excellent bow and excellent weapons in battle. If I do not avenge the death of my father, how shall I be able to speak in the assembly of men?

sn: सोऽहमद्य यथाकामं क्षत्रधर्ममुपास्य तम्। गन्तास्मि पदवीं राज्ञः पितुश्चापि महात्मनः॥
en: Following Kshatriya duties, therefore, without hesitation, I shall to-day walk in the steps of my great father and the king.

sn: अद्य स्वप्स्यन्ति पञ्चाला विश्वस्ता जितकाशिनः। विमुक्तयुग्यकवचा हर्षेण च समन्विताः॥
en: The Panchalas, elated with victory, will sleep in confidence to-night, having put off their armour and in great joy at the thought of the victory they have gained, and exhausted with toil and exertion.

sn: जयं मत्वाऽऽत्मनश्चैत श्रान्ता व्यायामकर्शिताः। तेषां निशि प्रसुप्तानां सुस्थानां शिविरे स्वके॥
en: While sleeping easily during the night within their own camp, I shall make a great and terrible assault upon their camp.

sn: अवस्कन्दं करिष्यामि शिविरस्याद्य दुष्करम्। तानवस्कन्द्य शिविरे प्रेतभूतविचेतसः॥
en: Like Indra killing the Danavas, I shall, attacking them while dead in sleep in their camp, kill them all, by my power.

sn: सूदयिष्यामि विक्रम्य मघवानिव दानवान्। अद्य तान् सहितान् सर्वान् धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमान्॥ सूदयिष्यामि विक्रम्य कक्षं दीप्त इवानलः। निहत्य चैव पञ्चालान् शन्तिं लब्धास्मि सत्तम॥
en: Like a burning fire consuming a heap of dry grass, I shall kill all of them collected in one place with their leader Dhrishtadyumna. Having killed the Panchalas, I shall obtain peace of mind, O best of men.

sn: पञ्चालेषु भविष्यामि सूदयन्नद्य संयुगे। पिनाकपाणिः संक्रुद्धः स्वयं रुद्रः पशुष्विव॥
en: While engaged in the act of destruction I shall move about in their midst like the holder of Pinaka, viz., the angry Rudra himself, among living creatures!

sn: अद्याहं सर्वपञ्चालान् निहत्य च निकृत्य च। अर्दयिष्यामि संहृष्टो रणे पाण्डुसुतांस्तथा॥
en: Having cut off and killed all the Panahalas to-day, I shall then, in joy, assail the sons of Pandu in battle!

sn: अद्याहं सर्वपञ्चालैः कृत्वा भूमिं शरीरिणीम्। प्रहत्यैकैकशस्तेषु भविष्याम्यनृणः पितुः॥
en: Taking their lives one after another and causing the Earth to be covered with the bodies of all the Panchalas, I shall satisfy the debt I owe to my father!

sn: दुर्योधनस्य कर्णस्य भीष्मसैन्धवयोरपि। गमयिष्यामि पञ्चालान् पदवीमद्य दुर्गमाम्॥
en: I shall to-day made the Panchalas follow Duryodhana and Karna and Bhishma and the King of the Sindhus!

sn: अद्य पाञ्चालराजस्य धृष्टद्युम्नस्य वै निशि। नचिरात् प्रमथिष्यामि पशोरिव शिरो बलात्॥
en: Displaying my power, I shall tonight grind the head, like that any animal, of Dhrishtadyumna the king of the Panchalas.

sn: अद्य पाञ्चालपाण्डूनां शयितानात्मजान् निशि। खड्डेन निशितेनाजौ प्रमथिष्यामि गौतम
en: I shall to-night, O son of Gotama, strike with my sharp sword, in battle, the sleeping sons of the Panchalas and the Pandavas.

sn: अद्य पाञ्चालसेनां तां निहत्य निशि सौप्तिके। कृतकृत्यः सुखी चैव भविष्यामि महामते॥
en: Having rooted out the Panchala army tonight while asleep, I shall, enjoy great happiness and consider myself to have done my duty!

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: कृप उवाच दिष्ट्या ते प्रतिकर्तव्य मतिर्जातेयमच्युत। न त्वं वारयितुं शक्तो वज्रपाणिरपि स्वयम्॥
en: Kripa Said “By good luck, O you of great glory, your heart is bent to-day on vengeance! The holder of the thunder himself will not succeed in dissuading you to-day.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: अनुयास्यावहे त्वां तु प्रभाते सहितावुभौ। अद्य रात्रौ विश्रमस्व विमुक्तकवचध्वजः॥ अहं त्वामनुयास्यामि कृतवर्मा च सात्वतः। परानभिमुखं यान्तं रथावास्थाय दंशितौ॥
en: Both of us, however, shall accompany you in the morning putting off armours and taking down your standard rest for this night. I shall, clad in mail and riding on our cars, accompany you as also Kritavarman of the Satwata race, while you will proceed against the foe.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: आवाभ्यां सहितः शत्रूश्वो निहन्ता समागमे। विक्रम्य रथिनां श्रेष्ठ पञ्चालान् सपदानुगान्॥
en: United with ourselves, you will kill the enemy, viz., the Panchalas will all their followers, tomorrow in battle, displaying your prowess, O best of car-warriors.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: शक्तस्त्वमसि विक्रम्य विश्रमस्व निशामिमाम्। चिरं ते जाग्रत स्तात स्वप तावन्निशामिमाम्॥
en: If you display your energy your quite competent to achieve that feat! Take rest, therefore, for this night. You have kept us many a night.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: विश्रान्तश्च विनिद्रश्च स्वस्थचित्तश्च मानद। समेत्य समरे शत्रून् वधिष्यसि न संशयः॥
en: Having rested and slept, and having become quite refreshed, O giver of honours, meet the cnemy in battle! Forsooth, you will kill then the enemy.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: न हि त्वं रथिनां श्रेष्ठं प्रगृहीतवरायुधम्। जेतुमुत्सहते शश्वदपि देवेषु वासवः॥
en: No one, not even Vasava amongst the celestials, would venture to defeat you armed with best of weapons, O foremost of carwarriors.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: कृपेण सहितं यान्तं गुप्तं च कृतवर्मणा। को द्रौणिं युधि संरब्धं योधयेदपि देवराट्॥
en: Who is there that would, even if he be the king of the gods himself, fight Drona's son when the latter goes, accompanied by Kripa and protected by Kritavarman.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: ते वयं निशि विश्रान्ता विनिद्रा विगतज्वराः। प्रभातायां रजन्यां वै निहनिष्याम शात्रवान्॥
en: Therefore, having rested and slept this night, and removed fatigue, we shall kill the foe tomorrow morning.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: तव शस्त्राणि दिव्यानि मम चैव न संशयः। सात्वतोऽपि महेष्वासो नित्यं युद्धेषु कोविदः॥
en: You are a master of celestial weapons. I also am so. This hero of Satvata's race is a great bowman, always skilled in battle.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: ते वयं सहितास्तात सर्वाशत्रून् समागतान्। प्रसह्य समरे हत्वा प्रीतिं प्राप्स्याम पुष्कलाम्॥ विश्रमस्व त्वमव्यग्रः स्वप चेमां निशां सुखम्।
en: All of us, in a body, O son, shall succeed in killing our assembled foes in battle by displaying our powers. Great shall be our happiness then. Removing your anxiety, rest for this night and sleep happily.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: अहं च कृतवर्मा च त्वां प्रयान्तं नरोत्तमम्॥ अनुयास्याव सहितौ धन्विनौ परतापनौ। रथिनं त्वरया यान्तं रथमास्थाय दंशितौ॥
en: Myself and Kritavarman, both armed with bows and capable of consuming our enemies, will, clad in mail, follow you, O best of men, while you will move on your car against the enemy.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: स गत्वा शिविरं तेषां नाम विश्राव्य चाहवे। ततः कर्तासि शत्रूणां युध्यतां कदनं महत्॥
en: Proceeding to their camp, and announcing your name in battle, you will then made a great destruction of the foe.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: कृत्वा च कदनं तेषां प्रभाते विमलेऽहनि। विहरस्व यथा शक्रः सूदयित्वा महासुरान्॥
en: Having caused tomorrow morning, a great slaughter among them you will sport like Indra after the destruction of great Asuras.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: त्वं हि शक्तो रणे जेतुं पञ्चालान् वरूथिनीम्। दैत्यसेनामिव क्रुद्धः सर्वदानवसूदनः॥
en: You are quite competent to defeat the army of the Panchalas in battle, like the destroyer of the Danavas in defeating in anger the Danavas army.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: मया त्वां सहितं संख्ये गुप्तं च कृतवर्मणा। न सहेत विभुः साक्षाद् वज्रपाणिरपि स्वयम्॥
en: United with myself in battle and protected by Kritavarman, you are incapable of being defcated by the holder of the thunder-bolt himself.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: न चाहं समरे तात कृतवर्मा न चैव हि। अनिर्जित्य रणे पाण्डून् न च यास्यामि कर्हिचित्।। १८
en: Neither I, O son, nor Kritavarman will ever retreat from battle without having defeated the Pandus.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: हत्वा च समरे क्रुद्धान् पञ्चालान् पाण्डुभिः सह। निवर्तिध्यामहे सर्वे हता वा स्वर्गगा वयम्॥
en: Having killed the angry Panchalas along with the Pandavas, we shall come away, or killed by them we shall go to heaven.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: सर्वोपायैः सहायास्ते प्रभाते वयमाहवे। सत्यमेतन्महाबाहो प्रब्रवीमि तनावघ॥ एवमुक्तस्ततो द्रौणिर्मातुलेन हितं वचः। अब्रवीन्मातुलं राजन् क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः॥ आतुरस्य कुतो निद्रा नरस्यामर्षितस्य च। अर्थाश्चिन्तयतश्चापि कामयानस्य वा पुनः।
en: By every means in our power, we two shall help you in battle tomorrow morning. O you of mighty-arms, I tell you the truth, O innocent one."-Addressed in these wholesome words by his maternal uncle, the son of Drona, with eyes reddened in anger answered his uncle, O king, saying,-"Can a person who is afflicted, or one who is under the influence of anger, or one whose heart is always engaged in making plans for the acquisition of wealth, or one who is under the power of lust, get sleep.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: तदिदं समनुप्राप्तं पश्य मेऽद्य चतुष्टयम्॥ यस्य भागश्चतुर्थो मे स्वप्नमह्नाय नाशयेत्।
en: See, all these four causes are present in my case. Any one of these, can singly spoil sleep.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: किं नाम दुःखं लोकेऽस्मिन् पितुर्वधमनुस्मरन्॥ हृदयं निर्दहन्मेऽद्य रात्र्यहानि न शाम्यति।
en: How great is the sorrow of that person who is always thinking of the death of his father. My heart is now burning day and night! I cannot enjoy peace.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: यथा च निहतः पापैः पिता मम विशेषतः॥ प्रत्यक्षमपि ते सर्वं तन्मे मर्माणि कृन्तति।
en: The way in which my father particularly killed by those sinful wretches has been seen by you all. The thought of that destruction is cutting me to the quick.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: कथं हि मादृशो लोके मुहूर्तमपि जीवति॥ द्रोणो हतेति यद्वाचः पञ्चालानां शृणोम्यहम्।
en: How could a person like me live for even a moment after hearing the Panchalas say that they have killed by father?

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नमहत्वा तु नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥ स मे पितुर्वधाद् वध्यः पञ्चाला ये च संगताः। विलापो भग्नसक्थस्य यस्तु राज्ञो मया श्रुतः॥
en: was I cannot bear the thought of maintaining life without having killed Dhristadyumna in battle! For the slaughter of my father, he and those who are with him should be killed me.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: स पुनर्हदयं कस्य क्रूरस्यापि न निर्दहेत्। कस्य ह्यकरुणस्यापि नेत्राभ्यामश्रु नाव्रजेत्॥
en: Who is there so hard-hearted that would not fire up after having heard the cries of the king lying with broken thighs?

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: नृपतेर्भग्नसक्थस्य श्रुत्वा तादृग् वचः पुनः। यश्चायं मित्रपक्षो मे मयि जीवति निर्जितः॥
en: Who is there somerciless whose eyes would not be filled with tears after hearing such words uttered by the king with broken thighs.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: शोकं मे वर्धयत्येष वारिवेग इवार्णवम्। एकाग्रमनसो मेऽद्य कुतो निद्रा कुतः सुखम्॥
en: They, whom, I sided have been defeated. The thought of this increases my sorrow as a rush of waters increases the ocean.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: वासुदेवार्जुनाभ्यां च तानहं परिरक्षितान्। अविषह्यतमान् मन्ये महेन्द्रेणापि सत्तम॥
en: Protected, as they are by Vasudeva, and Arjuna, I consider, them O uncle, as irresistible by the great Indra himself.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: न चापि शक्तः संयन्तुं कोपमेतं समुत्थितम्। तं न पश्यामि लोकेऽस्मिन् यो मां कोपान्निवर्तयेत्।।
en: I am unable to check this rising anger in my heart. I do not see the man in this world than can suppress this wrath of mine.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: तथैव निश्चिता बुद्धिरेषा साधु मता मम। वार्तिकैः कथ्यमानस्तु मित्राणां मे पराभवः॥ पाण्डवानां च विजयो हृदयं दहतीव मे।
en: I am infouned by the messengers of the defeat of my friends and the victory of the Pandavas. That is consuming my heart.

description: .—Contd. Kripa promises to help Ashvatthaman and speaks of the latter's resolution
sn: अहं तु कदनं कृत्वा शत्रूणामद्य सौप्तिके। ततो विश्रमिता चैव स्वप्ता च विगतज्वरः॥
en: Having, however, caused a destruction of my enemies during their sleep, I shall then take rest and shall then sleep without anxiety.”

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: कृप उवाच शुश्रूषुरपि दुर्मेधाः पुरुषोऽनियतेन्द्रियः। नालं वेदयितुं कृत्स्नौ धर्मार्थाविति मे मतिः॥
en: Kripa Said "A person who is not intelligent and who has not controlled, his passions, cannot, even if he waits dutifully upon his superiors, understand morality. This is my opinion.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: तथैव तावन्मेधावी विनयं यो न शिक्षते। न च किंचन जानाति सोऽपि धर्मार्थनिश्चयम्॥
en: In the same way in intelligent person, who does not practise humility, cannot understand morality.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: चिरं ह्यपि जडः शूरः पण्डितं पर्युपास्य हि। न स धर्मान् विजानाति दर्वी सूपरसानिव॥
en: By waiting all his life upon a learned person, a brave man, void of understanding, cannot know his duties like a wooden ladle unable to taste the soup.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: मुहूर्तमपि तं प्राज्ञः पण्डितं पर्युपास्य हि। क्षिप्रं धर्मान् विजानाति जिह्वा सूपरसानिव॥
en: By waiting upon a learned person for even a moment, the wiseman, however, succeeds in understanding his duties like the tongue tasting the soup.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: शुश्रूषुस्त्वेव मेधावी पुरुषो नियतेन्द्रियः। जानीयादागमान् सर्वान् ग्राह्यं च न विरोधयेत्॥
en: An intelligent person who waits upon his superiors and who has controlled his passions succeeds in understanding all the rules of morality and never disputes what is accepted by all.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: अनेयस्त्ववमानी यो दुरात्मा पापपूरुषः। दिष्टमुत्सृज्य कल्याणं करोति बहुपापकम्॥
en: A sinful person of ungovernable, irreverent, wicked soul, commits sin in seeking his welfare by neglecting destiny.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: नाथवन्तं तु सुहृदः प्रतिषेधन्ति पातकात्। निवर्तते तु लक्ष्मीवान् नालक्ष्मीवान् निवर्तते॥
en: Well-wishers try to restrain a friend from committing sin. He who allows himself to be dissuaded succeeds in gaining prosperity. He, that does otherwise suffers misery,

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: यथा ह्युचावचैर्वाक्यैः क्षिप्तचित्तो नियम्यते। तथैव सुहृदा शक्यो न शक्यस्त्ववसीदति॥
en: As a person who has lost his brains is restrained by soothing words, so should a friend be restrained by well-wishers. He that allows himself to be so restrained, never suffers misery.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: तथैव सुहृदं प्राज्ञं कुर्वाणं कर्म पापकम्। प्राज्ञाः सम्प्रतिषेधन्ति यथाशक्ति पुनः पुनः॥ स कल्याणे मनः कृत्वा नियम्यात्मानमात्मना। कुरु मे वचनं तात येन पश्चान्न तप्यसे॥
en: When a wise friend is about to commit a wicked act, wise well-wishers repeatedly, and according to the best of their power, try to restrain him. Making up your mind to do what is really beneficial, and restraining yourself by your own self, do by command, O son, so that you may not have to repent afterwards.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: न वधः पूज्यते लोके सुप्तानामिह धर्मतः। तथैवापास्तशस्त्राणां विमुक्तरथवाजिनाम्॥
en: In this world the destruction of sleeping persons is not praised and sanctioned by religion. The same is the case with persons that have thrown off their arms and come down from cars and horses.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: ये च ब्रूयुस्तवास्मीति ये च स्युः शरणागताः। विमुक्तमूर्धजा ये च ये चापि हतवाहनाः॥
en: They should not also be killed who say-we are yours-and also they who surrender themselves, and they whose locks are dishevelled, and they whose animals have been killed under them or whose cars have been broken.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: अद्य स्वप्स्यन्ति पञ्चाला विमुक्तकवचा विभो। विश्वस्ता रजनी सर्वे प्रेता इव विचेतसः॥
en: All the Panchalas taking of their armours will sleep to-night, O lord. When asleep, they will be taken dead man.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: यस्तेषां तदवस्थानां दुह्येत पुरुषोऽनृजुः। व्यक्तं स नरके मज्जेदगाधे विपुलेऽप्लवे॥
en: That wicked man who would injure them then, would sink in deep and limitless hell without a raft to save himself.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: सर्वास्त्रविदुषां लोके श्रेष्ठस्त्वमसि विश्रुतः। न च ते जातु लोकेऽस्मिन् सुसूक्ष्ममपि किल्बिषम्।। १५
en: In this world you are celebrated as the foremost of all persons knowing the use of weapons, you have not as yet committed even a minute sin.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: त्वं पुन: सूर्यसंकाशः श्वोभूत उदिते रवौ। प्रकाशे सर्वभूतानां विजेता युधि शात्रवान्॥
en: When the sun rises next morning and light shall clear up all things, you, like a second effulgent sun will vanquish the foe in battle.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: असम्भावितरूपं हि त्वयि कर्म विगर्हितम्। शुक्ले रक्तमिव न्यस्तं भवेदिति मतिर्मम॥
en: This culpable deed, so impossible in one like you, will appear like a red spot on a white sheet. This my opinion.”

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: एवमेव यथाऽऽत्थ त्वं मातुलेह न संशयः। तैस्तु पूर्वमयं सेतुः शतधा विदलीकृतः॥
en: Ashvatthaman said “Forsooth what you say, O maternal uncle, is true. The Pandavas, however, have, before this, deviated from the path of righteousness.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: प्रत्यक्षं भूमिपाला भवतां चापि संनिधौ। न्यस्तशस्त्रो मम पिता धृष्टद्युम्नेन पातितः॥
en: Before all the kings, before your eyes also, my father after he had laid down his weapons, was killed by Dhrishtadyumna.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: कर्णश्च पतिते चक्रे रथस्य रथिनां वरः। उत्तम व्यसने मग्नो हतो गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: Karna also, that best of car-warriors after the wheel of his car had sunk and he had been assailed by great distress, was killed by the holder of Gandiva.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: तथा शान्तनवो भीष्मो न्यस्तशस्त्रो निरायुधः। शिखण्डिनं पुरस्कृत्य हतो गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: Similarly Shantanu's son Bhishma, after he had laid aside his weapons was killed by Arjuna with Shikhandin placed in his rear.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: भूरिश्रवा महेष्वासस्तथा प्रायगतो रणे। क्रोशतां भूमिपालानां युयुधानेन पातितः॥
en: So also, the great bowman Bhurishravas, while observing the Praya vow on the field of battle, was killed by Yuyudhana, disregarding the voice of all the kings.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: दुर्योधनश्च भीमेन समेत्य गदया रणे। पश्यतां भूमिपालानामधर्मेण निपातितः॥
en: Having met Bhima is battle with the mace, Duryodhana too has been killed unfairly by the former in the very presence of all the king.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: एकाकी बहुभिस्तत्र परिवार्य महारथैः। अधर्मेण नरव्याघ्रो भीमसेनेन पातितः॥
en: The king was all alone in the midst of a great number of powerful car-warriors cumstances was that king killed by Bhimasena.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: विलापो भग्नसक्थस्य यो मे राज्ञः परिश्रुतः। वार्तिकाणां कथयतां स मे मर्माणि कृन्तति॥
en: The lamentations of the king, lying prostrate on the Earth with his thighs broken, that I have heard from the messengers circulating the news, are cutting me to the quick.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: एवं चाधार्मिकाः पापाः पञ्चाला भिन्नसेतवः। तानेवं भिन्नमर्यादान् किं भवान् न निगर्हति॥
en: The unrighteous and sinful Panchalas, who have trumpeted virtue, are even such. Why do you not blame them who have transgressed the law of virtue.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: पितृहन्तनहं हत्वा पञ्चालान् निशि सौप्तिके। कामं कीटः पतङ्गो वा जन्म प्राप्य भवामि वै॥
en: Having killed the Panchalas, those destroyers of my father in the night when they are buried in sleep, I care not if I am born as a warın or an insect in my next birth.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: त्वरे चाहमनेनाद्य यदिदं मे चिकीर्षितम्। तस्य मे त्वरमाणस्य कुतो निद्रा कुतः सुखम्॥
en: My resolution is pressing me for its accomplishment. Urged on by it, how can I enjoy sleep and happiness.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: न स जातः पुमाँल्लोके कश्चिन्न स भविष्यति। यो मे व्यावर्तयेदेतां वधे तेषां कृतां मतिम्॥
en: That man is not yet born in the world, nor will be, who will be able to frustrate this resolution of mine."

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज द्रोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। एकान्ते योजयित्वाश्वान् प्रायादभिमुखः परान्॥
en: Sanjaya continued “Having said so, O king, the brave son of Drona yoked his horses to his car at a corner and started towards the direction of his enemies.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: तमबूतां महात्मनौ भोजशारद्वतावुभौ। किमर्थंस्यन्दनो युक्तः किञ्च कार्यं चिकीर्षितम्॥
en: Then Bhoja and Sharadvat's son, those great persons, addressed him saying,-'Why do you yoke the horses to your car? What do you want to do?

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: एकसार्थप्रयातौ स्वस्त्वया सह नरर्षभ। समदुःखसुखौ चापि नावां शङ्कितुमर्हसि॥
en: We are determined to accompany you tomorrow, O foremost of men! We sympathies with you in weal and woe. You should not mistrust us.'

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: अश्वत्थामा तु संक्रुद्धः पितर्वधमनुस्मरन्। ताभ्यां तथ्यंऽऽचख्यौ यदस्यात्मचिकीर्षितम्॥
en: Remembering the slaughter of his father, Ashvatthaman in anger told them truly about the work that he had resolved to accomplish.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: हत्वा शतसहस्राणि निशितैः शरैः। न्यस्तशस्त्रो मम पिता धृष्टद्युम्नेन पातितः॥
en: When my father having killed hundreds and thousands of warriors with sharp arrows, had thrown out his weapons, he was then killed by Dhrishtadyumna.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: तं तथैव हरिष्यामि न्यस्तधर्माणमद्य वै। पुत्रं पाञ्चालराजस्य पापं पापेन कर्मणा॥
en: I shall kill that slayer to-day under similar circumstances. I shall to-day slay the sinful son of the king of the Panchalas by a sinful act.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: कथं च निहतः पापः पाञ्चाल्यः पशुवन्मया। शस्त्रेण विजिताँल्लोकान् नाप्नुयादिति मे मति॥
en: It is my determination to slay like an animal that sinful prince of the Panchalas in such a way that he may not attain to regions gained by persons killed with weapons.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: क्षिप्रं संनद्धकवचौ सखड्गावात्तकार्मुकौ। मामास्थाय प्रतीक्षेतां रथवौ परंतपौ॥ इत्युक्त्वा रथमास्थाय प्रायदभिमुखः परान्। तपन्वगात् कृपो राजन् कृतवर्मा च सात्वतः॥
en: Put on your coats of mail soon and take your bows and swords, and wait for me here, O foremost of car-warriors.'—Having said so, Ashvatthaman got upon his car started towards the enemy. The Kripa, O king, and Kritavarman of the Satwata race, both followed him.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: ते प्रयाता व्यरोचन्त परानभिमुखास्त्रयः। हूयमाना यथा यज्ञे समिद्धा हव्यवाहनाः॥
en: While the three went on against the enemny, they shone like three blazing fires in sacrifice, fed with libations of clarified butter.

description: .-Contd. Kripa tries to prevent Ashvatthama. The latter's reply and exhortation
sn: ययुश्च शिविरं तेषां सम्प्रसुप्तजनं विभो। द्वारदेशं तु सम्प्राप्य द्रौणिस्तस्थौ महारथः॥
en: They proceeded, O lord, towards the encampment of the Panchalas within which everybody was asleep. Having approached the gate, Drona's son, that great car-warriors, stopped."

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच द्वारदेशे ततो द्रौणिमवस्थितमवेक्ष्य तौ। अकुर्वातां भोजकृपौ किं संजय वदस्व मे॥
en: Dhritarashtra Said “Seeing Drona's son stop at the gate of the camp, what, O Sanjaya, did those two great car-warriors, viz., Kripa and Kritavarman, do? Tell me this."

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: संजय उवाच कृतवर्माणमामन्त्र्य कृपं च स महारथः। द्रौणिर्मन्युपरीतात्मा शिविरद्वारमागमत्॥
en: Sanjaya said "Inviting Kritavarman as also the great carwarrior Kripa, Drona's son, worked up with rage, approached the gate of the camp.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: तत्र भूतं महाकायं चन्द्रार्कसदृशद्युतिम्। सोऽपश्यद् द्वारमाश्रित्य तिष्ठन्तं लोमहर्षणम्॥
en: He there saw a being of huge frame capable of making the very hair erect and endued with the effulgence of the Sun or the Moon, guarding the entrance.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: वसानं चर्म वैयाघ्रं महारुधिरविस्रवम्। कृष्णाजिनोत्तरासङ्गं नागयज्ञोपवीतिनम्॥
en: round his loins was a tiger-skin covered with blood, and he had a black deer for his upper garment. He had for his sacred thread a large snake.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: बाहुभिः स्वायतैः पीनैर्नानाप्रहरणोद्यतैः। बद्धाङ्गदमाहासर्प ज्वालामालाकुलाननम्॥
en: His arms were long and massive, and held many sorts of uplifted weapons. He had for his armlet a huge snake wound round his upper arin. His mouth was ablaze with flames of fire.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: दंष्ट्राकरलवदनं व्यादितास्यं भयानकम्। नयनानां सहस्त्रैश्च विचित्रैरभिभूषितम्॥
en: His teeth made his face terrible to look at. His mouth was open and dreadful. His face had a thousand of beautiful eyes.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: नैव तस्य वपुः शक्यं प्रवक्तुं वेष एव च। सर्वथा तु तदालक्ष्य स्फुटेयुरपि पर्वताः॥
en: His body and his dress were beyond description. Upon seeing him the very mountains would split into a thousand pieces.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: तस्यास्यान्नासिकाभ्यां च श्रवणाभ्यां च. सर्वशः। तेभ्यश्चाक्षिसहस्रेभ्यः प्रादुरासन महार्चिषः॥
en: From those blazing flames of fire came out of his mouth and nose and ears and all those thousand of eyes.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: तथा तेजोमरीचिभ्यः शङ्खचक्रगदाधराः। प्रादुरासन हषीकेशा: शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: From those blazing flames hundreds and thousands of Hrishikeshas came out armed with conchs and discs and maces.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: तदत्यद्भुतमालोक्य भूतं लोकभयंकरम्। द्रौणिरव्यथितो दिव्यैरस्त्रवर्षेरवाकिरत्॥
en: Seeing that extraordinary being capable of striking terror to the entire world, Drona's son, without any fear covered him with showers of celestial weapons. That being, however, devoured all those arrows discharged by Drona's son.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: द्रौणिमुक्ताञ्छरांस्तांस्तु तद् भूतं महदग्रसत्। उदधेरिव वार्यघान् पावको वडवामुखः॥
en: Like the Vadava fire devouring the waters of the ocean, that being devoured the arrows discharged by the son of Drona.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: अग्रसत् तांस्तथाभूतं द्रौणिना प्रहिताशरान्। अश्वत्थामा तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य शरौघांस्तान् निरर्थकान्॥
en: Seeing his arrowy showers prove fruitless, Ashvathaman discharged at him a long dart burning like fire.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: रथशक्तिं मुमोचासौ दीप्तामग्निशिखामिव। सा तमाहत्य दीप्ताग्रा रथशक्तिदीर्यत॥
en: That blazing dart striking against that being, broke into pieces like a huge meteor at the end of a cycle breaking and falling down from the sky after striking against.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: युगान्ते सूर्याहत्य महोल्केव दिवश्च्युता। अथ हेमत्सरं दिव्यं खड्गमाकाशवर्चसम्॥
en: Without losing a moment Ashvatthaman drew from its sheath an excellent sky-coloured scimitar having a golden hilt. The scimitar came out like a snake from its whole.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: कोशात् समुद्बबर्दाशु बिलाद् दीप्तमिबोरगम्। ततः खड्गवरं धीमान् भूताय प्राहिणोत् तदा॥
en: The intelligent son of Drona then threw that excellent scimitar at that being. approaching that being the weapon disappeared within his body like a mungoose disappearing in its hole.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: स तदासाद्य भूतं वै बिलं नुकलवद् ययौ। ततः स कुपितो द्रौणिरिन्द्रकेतुनिभां गदाम्॥
en: Worked up with anger the son of Drona then hurled a blazing mace huge as a pole set up in honor of Indra. That being devoured that mace also.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: ज्वलन्तीं प्राहिणोत् तस्मै भूतं तामपि चाग्रसत्। ततः सर्वायुधाभावे वीक्षमाणस्ततस्ततः॥
en: At last, when all his weapons were exhausted, Ashvatthaman, looking around, saw the entire sky densely crowded with images of Janarddana.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: अपश्यत् कृतमाकाशमनाकाशं जनार्दनैः। तदद्भुततमं दृष्ट्वा द्रोणपुत्रो निरायुधः॥ अब्रवीदतिसंतप्तः कृपवाक्यमनुस्मरन्। ब्रुवतामप्रियं पथ्यं सुहृदां न शृणोति यः॥
en: Seeing that wonderful spectacle Drona's son, divested of weapons, recollected the words of Kripa, and burning with grief, said,-"He who hears not the beneficial words of friends, repents being overwhelmed with calamity, as does my foolish self for having disregarded by two well-wishers.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: स शोचत्पादं प्राप्य यथाहमतिवर्त्य तौ। शास्त्रदृष्टानविद्वान् यः समतीत्य जिघांसति॥
en: That fool who, disregarding the way laid down by the scriptures, tries to kill his enemies, falls off from the path of righteousness and is lost in sin.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: स पथः प्रच्युतो धर्मात् कुपथे प्रतिहन्यते। गोब्राह्मणनृपस्त्रीषु सख्युर्मातुर्गुरोस्तथा॥ हीनप्राणजडान्धेषु सुप्तभीतोस्थितेषु च। मत्तोन्मत्तप्रमत्तेषु न शस्त्राणि च पातयेत्॥
en: One should not use weapons against kine, Brahmanas, kings, women, friends, one's own mother, one's own preceptor, a weak man, an idiot, a blind man, a sleeping man, a terrified man, one just got up from sleep, an intoxicated person, a lunatic, and one that is careless. The ancient preceptors always preached this truth to men.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: इत्येवं गुरुभिः पूर्वमुपदिष्टं नृणां सदा। सोऽहमुत्क्रम्य पन्थानं शास्त्रदिष्टं सनातनम्॥
en: By neglecting the eternal way pointed out by the scriptures and by trying to follow a wrong path I have, however, fallen into a dreadful distress.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: अमार्गेणैवमारभ्य घोरामापदमागतः। तां चापदं घोरतरां प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: It is described by the wise as a terrible calamily when one through fear, cannot achieve a great feat after having tried to do the same.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: यदुद्यम्य महत् कृत्यं भयादपि निवर्तते। अशक्तश्चैव तत् कर्तु कर्म शक्तिबलादिह॥
en: By using my skill and power, I am unable to achieve that which I have promised? Human exertion is never more powerful than destiny.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: न हि दैवाद् गरीयो वै मानुषं कर्म कथ्यते। मानुष्यं कुर्वतः कर्म यदि दैवान्न सिध्यति॥ स पथः प्रच्युतो धर्माद् विपदं प्रतिपद्यते।
en: If any action of a man that is undertaken becomes unsuccessful through destiny, the actor becomes like one who deviating from the path of virtue is lost in the wilderness of sin.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: प्रतिज्ञानं ह्यविज्ञानं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः॥ यदारभ्य क्रियां काञ्चिद् भयादिह निवर्तते।
en: The wise describe defeat as foolishness when one having undertaken a task abandons it from fear.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: तदिदं दुष्प्रणीतेन भयं मां समुपस्थितम्॥ न हि द्रोणसुतः संख्ये निवर्तेत कथंचन।
en: For the wickedness of my attempt, this great calamity has befallen me, otherwise Drona's son would never had been compelled to hold back from battle.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: इदं स समुहद् भूतं दैवदण्डमिवोद्यतम्॥ न चैतदभिजानामि चिन्तयन्नपि सर्वथा।
en: Again this being, who is before me, is most wonderful. He stands there like the uplifted rod of divine punishment. Thinking much even, I Cannot recognise this being.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: ध्रुवं येयमधर्मे में प्रवृत्ता कलुषा मतिः॥ तस्याः फलमिदं घोरं प्रतिघाताय कल्पते।
en: Forsooth, that being is the dreadful outcome of this my sinful determination which I had attempted to achieve by unfair means, He stands there for baffling my resolution.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: तदिदं दैवविहितं मम संख्ये निवर्तनम्॥ नान्यत्र दैवादुद्यन्तुमिह शक्यं कथंचना
en: It seems, therefore, that my casing from fight had been ordained by destiny. It is useless for me to try to accomplish my resolution unless density becomes favorable.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: सोऽहमद्य महादेवं प्रपद्ये शरणं विभुम्॥ दैवदण्डमिमं घोरं स हि मे नाशयिष्यति।
en: I shall, therefore, at this hour, seek the protection of the powerful Mahadeva. He will remove this dreadful rod of divine punishment uplifted before me.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: कपर्दिनं देवदेवमुमापतिमनामयम्॥ कपालमालिनं रुद्रं भगनेत्रहरं हरम्।
en: I will seek refuge with that god, that source of all good, viz., the lord of Uma, otherwise called Kaparddin, adorned with a garland of human skulls, that plucker of Bhaga's eyes, called also Rudra and Hara.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman goes to the Pandava camp and sees a huge being who devours all his Weapons
sn: स हि देवोऽत्यगाद् देवांस्तपसा विक्रमेण चा तस्माच्छरणमभ्येमि गिरिशं शूलपाणिनम्॥
en: In ascetic practices and power, he far! excells all the gods. I shall, therefore, seek refuge with Girisha armed with trident.'

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: संजय उवाच एवं संचिन्तयित्वा तु द्रोणपुत्रो विशाम्पते। अवतीर्य रथोपस्थाद् देवेशं प्रणतः स्थितः॥ उग्रं स्थाणुं शिवं रुद्रं शर्वमीशानमीश्वरम्। गिरिशं वरदं देवं भवभावनमीश्वरम्॥ शितिकण्ठमजं शुक्रं दक्षक्रतुहरं हरम्। विश्वरूपं विरूपाक्षं बहुरूपमुमापतिम्॥ श्मशानवासिनं दृप्तं महागणपतिं विभुम्। खट्वाङ्गधारिणं रुद्रं जटिलं ब्रह्मचारिणम्॥
en: Sanjaya Said “Having reflected thus, the son of Drona, O king, got down from his car and stood, bending his head to that supreme god, and said,-. I seek the protection of fierce, Sthanu, Shiva, Rudra, Sarva, Ishana, Ishvara, Girisha, of that boon-giving god who is the Creator and lord of the universe; of the blue-throated deity, who is without birth, who is called Shakra, who destroyed the sacrifice of Daksha, and who is called Hara; of Him whose form is the universe, who has three eyes, who has many forms, and who is the lord of Uma; of Him who lives in crematoriums, who is energetic, who is the master of ghosts and who is endued with undecaying prosperity and power; of Him who holds a club having a skull on the top, who is called Rudra, who bears matted locks on his head, and who is a Brahmacharin.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: मनसा सुविशुद्धेन दुष्करेणाल्पचेतसा। सोऽहमात्मोपहारेण यक्ष्ये त्रिपुरघातिनम्॥
en: Purifying my soul, and possessing small energy, I adore the Destroyer of the three cities, and offer myself as the victim.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: स्तुतं स्तुत्यं स्तूयमानममोघं कृत्तिवाससम्। विलोहितं नीलकण्ठमसह्यं दुर्निवारणम्॥
en: I sing your glory. Thy purposes are never baffled. Thou art clad in skin; thou hast red hair on your head; You are blue-throated; You are unbearable; You are irresistible.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: शुक्रं ब्रह्मसृजं ब्रह्म ब्रह्मचारिणमेव च। व्रतवन्तं तपोनिष्ठमनन्तं तपतां गतिम्॥ बहुरूपं गणाध्यक्षं त्र्यक्षं पारिषदप्रियम्। धनाध्यक्षेक्षितमुखं गौरीहृदयवल्लभम्॥ कुमारपितरं पिङ्गं गोवृषोत्तमवाहनम्। तनुवाससमत्युग्रहमुमाभूषणतत्परम्॥ परं परेभ्यः परमं परं यस्मान्न विद्यते। इष्वस्त्रोत्तमभर्तारं दिगन्तं देशरक्षिणम्॥ हिरण्यकवचं देवं चन्द्रमौलिविभूषणम्। प्रपद्ये शरणं देवं परमेण समाधिना॥
en: You are pure; You are that Creator of Brahman; You are Brahma; You are Brahmacharin; You are an observer of vows; You are given to ascetic austerities; You are infinite; You are the refuge of all hermits; thou hast many forms; You are the master of ghosts; You are three-eyed; You are found of your a companions; You are always seen by Kuvera; You are dear to Gauri's heart; You are the father of Kumara; You are twany; thou hast a bull for your carrier; You are clad in a subtile dress%3; thou are most dreadful; You are eager to adorn Uma; You are higher than all that is high; You are higher than everything; there is nothing higher than thou; You are the holder of weapons; You are immeasurable, and You are the protector of all quarters; You are clad in golden armour; You are divine; thou hast the moon as ornament on your brow. With fixed attention, I seek refuge with you, O god.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: इमां चेदापादं घोरं तराम्यद्य सुदुष्कराम्। सर्वभूतोपहारेण यक्ष्येऽहं शुचिना शुचिम्॥
en: In order that I may successfully tide over this calamity, I sacrifice to you, the purest of the pure, offering for your acceptance the five elements of which my body is made.'

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: इति तस्य व्यवसितं ज्ञात्वा योगात् सुकर्मणः। पुरस्तात् काञ्चनी वेदी प्रादुरासीन्महात्मनः॥
en: Knowing this to be his resolution for accomplishing his object, a golden altar appeared before the great son of Drona.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: तस्यां वेद्यां तदा राजंश्चित्रभानुरजायत। स दिशो विदिशः खं च ज्वालाभिरिव पूरयन्॥
en: Upon the altar, O king, appeared a blazing fire, filling all the points of the horizon, cardinal and subsidiary, with its effulgence.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: दीप्तास्यनयनाश्चात्र नैकपादशिरोभुजाः रत्नचित्राङ्गदधराः समुद्यतकरास्तथा॥ द्वीपशैलप्रतीकाशाः प्रादुरासन् महागणाः। श्ववराहोष्ट्ररूपाश्च हयगोमायुगोमुखाः॥ ऋक्षमार्जारवदना व्याघ्रद्वीपिमुखास्तथा। काकवक्त्राः प्लवमुखाः शुकवक्त्रास्तथैव च॥
en: Many powerful beings also, of burning mouths and eyes, of many feet, heads, and arms, adorned with arm-lets, set with gems, and with uplifted arms, and looking like elephants and mountains, appeared there. Their faces resembled those of hares, boars, camels, horses, jackals, cows, bears, cats, tigers, pards, crows, apes and parrots.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: महाजगरवक्त्राश्च हंसवक्त्राः सितप्रभाः। दार्वाघाटमुखाश्चापि चाषवत्राश्च भारत॥ कूर्मनक्रमुखाश्चैव शिशुमारमुखास्तथा। महामकरवक्त्राश्च तिमिवक्त्रास्तथैव च॥ हरिवक्त्रा: क्रौञ्चमुखाः कपोतेमुखास्तथा। पारावतमुखाश्चैव मद्गुवक्त्रास्तथैव च।॥
en: And the faces of some were like those of snakes, and others had faces like those ducks. And all of them were highly effulgent. And the faces of some were like those of wood-packers, and joys; of tortoises, alligators, porpoises, huge sharks, and whales; of lions, cranes, pigeons, elephants, and shags,.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: पाणिकर्णाः सहस्राक्षास्तथैव च महोदरा:। निर्मांसा काकवत्राश्च श्येनवक्त्राश्च भारत॥
en: Some had faces like those of ravens and hawks, some had ears on their hands; some had thousand eyes; some had huge stomach; and some had no flesh.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: तथैवाशिरसो राजन्नृक्षवक्त्राश्च भारत। प्रदीप्तनेत्रजिह्वाश्च ज्वालावर्णास्तथैव च।॥
en: And some, O king, had no heads, and some had faces like those of bears. The eyes of some were like fire, and some had fiery features.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: ज्वालाकेशाश्च राजेन्द्र ज्वलद्रोमचतुर्भुजाः। मेषवक्त्रास्तथैवान्ये तथा छागमुखा नृप॥
en: The hair on the heads and bodies of some were burning, and some had four arms, and some, O king, had faces like those of sheep and goats.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: शङ्खाभाः शङ्खवक्त्राश्च शङ्खवर्णास्तथैव च। शङ्खमालापरिकराः शङ्खध्वनिसमस्वनाः॥
en: The color of some was like that of conchs, and some had faces like conchs, and the ears of were like conchs, and some wore garlands inade of conchs, and the voices of some resembled the blare of conchs.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: जटाधराः पञ्चशिखास्था मुण्डाः कृशोदराः। चतुर्दंष्ट्राश्चतुर्जिह्वाः शङ्ककर्णाः किरीटिन:॥
en: Some had matted locks on their heads, and some had five tufts of hair or the head, and some had bald heads. Some had lean stomachs; some had four teeth, some had four tongues, some some had cars straight like arrows, and some had diadems on their brows.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: मौञ्जीधराश्च राजेन्द्र तथा कुञ्चितमूर्धजाः। उष्णीषिणो मुकुटिनश्चारुवक्त्राः स्वरङ्कता॥
en: Some had strings of grass on their bodies, O king, and some had curly locks. Some had head-gears made of cloth, some had coronets, some had beautiful faces, and some were bedecked with ornaments.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: पद्मोत्पलापीडधरास्तथा मुकुटधारिणः। माहात्म्येन च संयुक्ताः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Some had ornaments made of lotuses, and some wee adorned with flowers. They were hundreds and thousands in number.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: शतघ्नीवज्रहस्ताश्च तथा मुसलपाणयः। भुशुण्डीपाशहस्ताश्च दण्डस्ताश्च भारत॥
en: Some were armed with Sataghnis, some with thunder, and some had Mushalas in their hands. Some had Bhusundis, some had nooses, and some had maces in their hands.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: पृष्ठेषु वद्धेषुधयश्चित्रबाणोत्कटास्तथा। सध्वजाः सपताकाश्च सघण्टाः सपरश्वधाः॥
en: Some had quivers containing best arrows on their backs, and all were dreadful in battle. Some had standard containing banners and bells, and some were armed with battle-axes.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: महापाशोद्यतकरातस्तथा लगुडपाणयः। स्थूणाहस्ताः खड्गहस्ता सोच्छ्रितकिरीटिनः ॥
en: Some had large nooses in their hands, and some had clubs and bludgeons. Some had strong posts in their hands, some has scimitars, and some had snakes with raised hood for their crowns.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: महासर्पाङ्गदधराश्चित्राभरणधारिणः। रजोध्वस्ताः पङ्कदिग्धाः सर्वे शुक्लाम्बरस्रजः॥
en: Some had huge snakes for armlets, and some had beautiful ornaments on their body, Some were covered with dust, some with mire, and all were clad in white robes and garment, Some had blue limbs while others had twany limbs. And some were beardless.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: नीलाङ्गा पिङ्गलाङ्गाश्च मुण्डवक्त्रास्तथैव च। भेरीशङ्खमृदङ्गांश्च झर्झरानकगोमुखान्॥
en: Those beings, called companions, having golden complexions, and filled with joy, played upon drums. horns, cymbals, Jharjharas, Anakas and Gomukhas.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: अवादयन् पारिषदाः प्रहृष्टाः कनकप्रभाः। गायमानास्तथैवान्ये नृत्यमानास्तथा परे॥
en: And some sang and some danced about crying hideously, and some leapt forward and cut capers and jumped sideways.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: लवयन्तः प्लवन्तश्च वल्लान्तश्च महारथाः। धावन्तो जवना मुण्डाः पवनोद्धृतमूर्धजाः॥
en: Quick in their motions, they ran about most dreadfully, the hair on their heads waving in the air, like infuriate elephants and frequently sending up loud roars.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: मत्ता इव महानागा विनदन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः। सुभीमा घोररूपाश्च शूलपटिशपाणयः॥
en: Terrible, and armed with lances and battleaxes, they were clad in robes of various colours and decked with beautiful garlands and unguents.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: नानाविरागवसनाचित्रमाल्यानुलेपनाः। रत्नचित्राङ्गदधराः समुद्यतकरास्तथा॥
en: Adorned with Angadas set with gems, and with uplifted arms, they were possessed of great courage. Capable of killing all foes by force, they were irresistible in prowess.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: हन्तारो द्विषतां शूराः प्रसह्यासह्यविक्रमाः। पातारोऽसूग्वसौघानां मांसान्त्रकृतभोजनाः॥ चूडालाः कर्णिकाराश्च प्रहृष्टाः पिठरोदराः।
en: Drinkers of blood and fat and other animal matter, they lived on the flesh and entrails of animals. Some had their locks tied up above their heads. Some had single tufts on their heads; some had rings on their ears, and some had stomachs resembling earthen cooking vessels.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: अतिह्रस्वातिदीर्घाश्च प्रलम्बाश्चातिभैरवाः॥ विकटाः काललम्बोष्ठा बृहच्छेफाण्डपिण्डिकाः।
en: Some were of very short statures, and some were very high. Some were tall and very dreadful. Some had grim features, some had long lips, and some had long genital organs.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: महार्हनानामुकटा मुण्डाश्च जटिलाः परे॥ सार्केन्दुग्रहनक्षत्रां द्यां कुर्यस्ते महीतले। उत्सहेरंच ये हन्तुं भूतग्रामं चतुर्विधम्॥
en: Some had rich and various kinds of crowns upon their heads; and some had bald heads, and the heads of others were covered with matted locks. They could bring down the sky with the sun, moon, and stars, on Earth, and exterminating the four orders of created things.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: ये च वीतभया नित्यं हरस्य भृकुटीसहाः।
en: They know not fear, and are capable of enduring the frowns of Hara.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: कामकारकरा नित्यं त्रैलोक्यस्येश्वरेश्वराः॥ नित्यानन्दप्रमुदिता वागीशा वीतमत्सराः।
en: They always act as they like and are the masters of the lord of the three worlds. Always playing merrily they are perfect masters of speech and are entirely shorn of pride.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: प्राप्याष्टगुणमैश्वर्यं ये न यास्यन्ति वै स्मयम्॥ येषां विस्मयते नित्यं भगवान् कर्मभिर्हरः।
en: Having got the eight sorts of divine attributes, they are never elated with pride. The divine Hara always wonders at their feats.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: मनोवाक्कर्मभिर्युक्तैर्नित्यमाराधितश्च यैः॥ मनोवाक्कभिर्भक्तान् पाति पुत्रानिवौरसान्।
en: They are devout worshipper of Mahadeva. Worshipped by them in thought, speech, and deed, the great god protects those worshippers of his, regarding them, in thought, speech, and deed, as his own children.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: पिबन्तोऽसृग्वसाश्चान्ये क्रुद्धा ब्रह्मद्विषां सदा॥ चतुर्विधात्मकं सोमं ये पिबन्ति च सर्वदा।
en: Worked up with rage, they always drink the blood and fat of all haters of Brahman. They always drink also the Soma juice having four kind of taste.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: श्रुतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण तपसा च दमेन च॥ ये समार.ध्य शूलाङ्कं भवसायुज्यमागताः।
en: Having worshipped the trident-handed deity with Vedic recitations, with Brahmacharya, with ascetic austerities, and with self-restraint, they have secured the companionship of Bhava.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: यैरात्मभूतैर्भगवान् पार्वत्य च महेश्वरः॥ महाभूतगणैभुते भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुः।
en: The divine Maheshvara, that lord of the past, the present, and the future, as also Parvati, eat with those various clans of powerful beings that partake of their own nature.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: नानावादित्रहसितक्ष्वेडितोत्क्रुष्टगर्जितै॥ संत्रासयन्तस्ते विश्वमश्वत्थामानमभ्ययुः।
en: Causing the universe resound with the sound of various kinds of instruments, with noise of laughter, with loud sounds and cries and leonine roars, they approached Ashvatthaman.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: संस्तुवन्तो महादेवं भाः कुर्वाणा: सुवर्चसः॥ विवर्धयिषवो द्रौणेमहिमानं महात्मनः। जिज्ञासमानास्तत्तेजः सौप्तिकं च दिदृक्षवः॥ भीमोग्नपरिघालातशूलपटिशपाणयः। घोररूपा: समाजग्मुर्भूतसङ्घाः समन्ततः॥
en: Landing Mahadeva and spreading an effulgence all around, desirous of increasing the honor of Ashvatthaman and the glory of the great Hara, and wishing to ascertain the extent of Ashvatthaman's power, and desirous also of witnessing the destruction during the hour of sleep, armed with terrible and fierce bludgeons and fiery wheels and battle-axes, that host of strange beings, having terrible forins, came from all sides.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: जनयेयुर्भयं ये स्म त्रैलोक्यस्यापि दर्शनात्। तान् प्रेक्षमाणोऽपि व्यथां न चकार महाबलः॥
en: They were capable of striking terror to the three worlds by their sight. Beholding them, the, powerful Ashvatthaman however, felt no fear.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: अथ द्रौणिर्धनुष्पाणिर्बद्धगोधाङ्कुलित्रवान्। स्वयमेवात्मनात्मानमुपहारमुपाहरत्॥
en: Armed with bow, and fingers cased in fences made of iguana skins, Drona's son himself offered up his own self as a victim to Mahadeva.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: धनूंषि समिधस्तत्र पवित्राणि शिताः शराः। हविरात्मवतश्चात्मा तस्मिन् भारत कर्मणि॥
en: Bows were the fuel, and sliarp arrows were the ladles, and his own great soul was the libation, in that act of sacrifice.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: ततः सौम्येन मन्त्रेण द्रोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। उपहारं महामन्युरथात्मानमुपाहरत्॥
en: The brave and angry son of Drona then, with mantras offered up his own soul as the victim.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: तं रुद्रं रौद्रकर्माणं रौद्रैः कर्मभिरच्युतम्। अभिष्टुत्य महात्मानमित्युवाच कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: Having with dreadful rites worshipped Rudra, of dreadful deeds, Ashvatthaman, with joined hands said to that high-souled deity,-

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: द्रौणिरुवाच इममात्मानमद्याहं जातमाङ्गिरसे कुले। स्वग्नौ जुहोमि भगवन् प्रतिगृह्णीष्व मां बलिम्॥
en: Ashvatthaman said Born in Angira's family I am about to pour my soul, O god, as a lit ion on this fire. Accept, O lord, this victim.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: भवद्भक्त्या महादेव परमेण समाधिना। अस्यामापदि विश्वात्मन्नुपाकुर्मि तवाग्रतः॥
en: In this hour of distress, O Soul of the universe, I offer up my own self as the victim, from devotion to you and with heart fixed in meditation.

description: .-Contd. Ashvatthaman's hymn to Mahadeva. A golden alter appears before him. Many extraordinary beings appear. Ashvatthaman offers himself as libation. Mahadeva appears. he gives Ashvatthaman a sword and fills him with energy
sn: त्वयि सर्वाणि भूतानि सर्वभूतेषु चासि वै। गुणनां हि प्रधानानामेकत्वं त्वयि तिष्ठति॥
en: All creatures exist in you and thou dust exist in all creatures. Thou art a combination of ali high attributes.
