en: As regards yourself, all wise men know you as a coward and a sinful wretch. Always engaged in sinful deeds, you are the slayer of children. Therefore, you must have to bear the fruit of your sinful deeds.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: त्रीणि वर्षसहस्त्राणि चरिष्यसि महीमिमाम्॥ अप्राप्नुवन् क्वचित् काञ्चित् संविदं जातु केनचित्। निर्जनानसहायस्त्वं देशान् प्रविचरिष्यसि॥
en: For three thousand years you shall have to wander over this earth, without a companion and without being able to talk with any one.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: भवित्री न हि ते क्षुद्र जनमध्येषु संस्थितिः। पूयशोणितगन्धी च दुर्गकान्तारसंश्रयः॥ विचरिष्ससि पापात्मन् सर्वव्याधिसमन्वितः।
en: Alone, and without any one with you, you shall wander through various countries, O wretch, you shall have to live out side the pale of human society. The stench of puss and blood shall come out from your body, and you shall live in dense forest and dreary moors. Thou shall wander over the earth, O sinful wight, suffering from all diseases.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: वयः प्राप्य परिक्षित् तु वेदव्रतमवाप्य च॥ कृपाच्छारद्वताच्छूरः सर्वास्त्राण्युपपत्स्यते।
en: Coming of age and acquiring a knowledge of the Vedas, the heroic Parikshit, shall obtain all weapons from the son of Sharadvat.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: विदित्वा परमास्त्राणि क्षत्रधर्मव्रते स्थितः॥ षष्टिं वर्षाणि धर्मात्मा वसुधां पालयिष्यति।
en: Having acquired all knowledge of all high weapons and observing all Kshatriya duties, that righteous king shall rule the earth for sixty years.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: इतश्चोर्ध्वं महाबाहुः कुरुराजो भविष्यति॥ परिक्षिन्नाम नृपतिर्मिषतस्ते सुदुर्मते।
en: Moreover, that boy shall become the powerful king of the Kurus, known by the name of Parikshit, before your very eyes, O wicked man.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: अहं तं जीवयिष्यामि दग्धं शस्त्राग्नितेजसा। पश्य मे तपसो वीर्यं सत्यस्य च नराधम॥
en: Thought burnt by the energy of your weapon's fire, I shall revive him. O lowest of men, witness the power of my austerities and my truth.'

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: व्यास उवाच यस्मादनादृत्य कृतं त्वयास्मान् कर्म दारुणम् ब्राह्मणस्य सतश्चैव यस्मात् ते वृत्तमीदृशम्॥ तस्माद् यद् देवकीपुत्र उक्तवानुत्तमं वचः असंशयं ते तद् भावि क्षत्रधर्मस्त्वयाऽऽश्रितः॥
en: Vyasa said Since, obeying us, you have committed this highly cruel act, and since your conduct is such, although you are a good Brahmana by birth, therefore, those excellent words that Devaki's son had said, will, forsooth, be fulfilled regarding you, because you are living the life of a Kshatriya.'

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: अश्वत्थामोवाच सहैव भवता ब्रह्मन् स्थास्यामि पुरुषेष्विह। सत्यवागस्तु भगवानयं च पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: Ashvatthaman said was With yourself among all men, O Rishi, I shall reside. Let the words of this illustrious and foremost of men prove true.'

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रदायाथ मणिं द्रौणिः पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। जगाम विमनास्तेषां सर्वेषां पश्यतां वनम्॥
en: Having made over his gem to the great Pandavas, Drona's son cheerlessly proceeded, in their presence, to the forest.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: पाण्डवाश्चापि गोविन्दं पुरस्कृत्य हतद्विषः। कृष्णद्वैपायनं चैव नारदं च महामुनिम्॥ द्रोणपुत्रस्य सहजं मणिमादाय सत्वराः। द्रौपदीमभ्यधावन्त प्रायोपेतां मनस्विनीम्॥
en: The Pandavas, who had killed all their foes, put Govinda and the Krishna-Dvaipayana and the great ascetic Narada at their head, and taking the gem that born with Ashvatthaman, quickly returned to the intelligent Draupadi who was observing the Praya vow."

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते पुरुषव्याघ्राः सदश्वरनिलोपमैः। अभ्ययुः सहदाशार्हाः शिविरं पुनरेव हि॥
en: Vaishampayana said “Those foremost of men, borne by their excellent horses, quick-coursing like the wind, came back with Dasharha hero, to their encampment.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: अवतीर्य रथेभ्यस्तु त्वरमाणा महारथाः। ददृशुद्रौपदी कृष्णामार्तामार्ततराः स्वयम्॥
en: Quickly getting down from their cars, those great car-warriors, themselves much more afflicted, saw Draupada's daughter Krishna stricken with misery.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: तामुपेत्य निरानन्दा दुःखशोकसमन्विताम्। परिवार्य व्यतिष्ठन्त पाण्डवाः सहकेशवाः॥
en: Approaching the cheerless princess laden with sorrow and grief, the Pandavas with Keshava, sat round her.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: ततो राज्ञाभ्यनुज्ञातो भीमसेनो महाबलः। प्रददौ तं मणि दिव्यं वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ अयं भद्रे तव मणिः पुत्रहन्तुर्जितः स ते। उत्तिष्ठ शोकमुत्सृज्य क्षात्रधर्ममनुस्मर॥
en: Then the powerful Bhimasena, desired by the king, gave that celestial gem to her and said these words: 'This gem, O amiable lady, is yours. The slayer of your sons had been defeated. Rise, shake off your sorrow, and recollect the duties of a Kshatriya lady.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: प्रयाणे वासुदेवस्य शमार्थमसितेक्षणे। यान्युक्तानि त्वया भीरु वाक्यानि मधुघातिनि॥
en: O you of black eyes, when Vasudeva was about to start (from Upaplavya.) on his mission of pace, you had said these words to the slayer of Madhu.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: नैव मे पतयः सन्ति न पुत्रा भ्रातरो न च। न वै त्वमिति गोविन्द शममिच्छन्ति राजनि॥
en: I have no husbands. I have no sons, nor brothers. Nor are you alive, O Govinda, since the king seeks peace.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: उक्तवत्यसि तीव्राणि वाक्यानि पुरुषोत्तमम्। क्षत्रधर्मानुरूपाणि तानि संस्मर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Those bitter words were addressed by you to Krishna, that foremost of persons. You should recollect these words that were so consistent with Kshatriya usages.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: हतो दुर्योधन: पापो राज्यस्य परिपन्थिकः। दुःशासनस्य रुधिरं पीतं विस्फुरतो मया॥
en: The wretched Duryodhana, that thorn in the way of our sovereignty, has been killed. I have quaffed the blood of the living Dusshasana.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: वैरस्य गतमानृण्यं न स्म वाच्या विवक्षताम्। जित्वा मुक्तो द्रोणपुत्रो ब्राह्मण्याद् गौरवेण च॥
en: We have satisfied the debt we owed to our enemy! People, will not able to blame us any longer! Having defeated Drona's son, we have released him for his being a Brahmana and for the respect that should be shown to our deceased preceptor.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: यशोऽस्य पतितं देवि शरीरं त्ववशेषितम्। वियोजितश्च मणिना भ्रंशितश्चायुधं भुवि॥
en: His faine has been spoiled, O goddess, only his body remains! He has been divested of his gem and on earth he has been deprived of his gem and on Earth he has been deprived of his weapons.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: द्रौपद्युवाच केवलानृण्यमाप्तास्मि गुरुपुत्रो गुरुर्मम। शिरस्येतं मणिं राजा प्रतिबध्नातु भारत॥
en: Draupadi said I desired only to satisfy our debt for the injury we have suffered. The preceptor's son deserves my respect as the preceptor himself.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: तं गृहीत्वा ततो राजा शिरस्येवाकरोत् तदा। गुरोरुच्छिष्टमित्येव द्रौपद्या वचनादपि॥
en: Let the king put this gem on his head, O Bharata!'-The king then, taking that gem, placed it on his head, as desired by Draupadi and taking it as a gift from the preceptor.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: ततो दिव्यं मणिवरं शिरसा धारयन् प्रभुः। शुशुभे स तदा राजा सचन्द्र इव पर्वतः॥
en: Holding on his head that excellent and celestial gem, the powerful king shone like a mountain with the moon above it.

description: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman, he accepts the curse and give up the gem of his head. Pandavas return to Draupadi.
sn: उत्तस्थौ पुत्रशोकार्ता ततः कृष्णा मनस्विनी। कृष्णं चापि महाबाहुः परिपप्रच्छ धर्मराट्॥
en: Though laden with grief for the death of her sons, the princess Draupadi, possessed of great mental strength, gave up her vow. Then king Yudhishthira enquired of the powerful Krishna, saying the following words.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच हतेषु सर्वसैन्येषु सौप्तिके तै स्थैस्त्रिभिः। शोचन् युधिष्ठिरो राजा दाशार्हमिदब्रवीत्॥ कथं नु कृष्ण पापेन क्षुद्रेणाकृतकर्मणा। द्रौणिना निहताः सर्वे मम पुत्रा महारथाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said "After all the soldiers had been killed during the hour of sleep by those three carwarriors, king Yudhishthira sorrowfully said to Krishna:-'How, O Krishna, could my sons, all of whom were great car-warriors, be killed by the sinful and wretched Ashvatthaman who is not an expert in battle?

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: तथा कृतास्त्रविक्रान्तः सहस्त्रशतयोधिनः। द्रुपदस्यात्मजाश्चैव द्रोणपुत्रेण पातिताः॥
en: How also could Drona's son kill the children of Drupada, all of whom were masters of weapons, powerful and capable of fighting with hundreds of thousands of enemies?

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: यस्य द्रोणो महेष्वासो न प्रादादाहवे मुखम्। निजघ्ने रथिनां श्रेष्ठं धृष्टद्युम्नं कथं नु सः॥
en: How could he kill that best of car-warriors, viz., Dhrishtadyumna, before whom the great bowman Drona himself could not appear?

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: किं नु तेन कृतं कर्म तथायुक्तं नरर्षभ। यदेकः समरे सर्वानवधीनो गुरोः सुतः॥
en: What act was done by the preceptor' son, O foremost of men, for which he succeeded in killing, single-headed, all our men in battle?'

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच नूनं स देवदेवानामीश्वरेश्वरमव्ययम्। जगाम शरणं द्रौणिरेकस्तेनावधीद् बहून्॥
en: Krishna said Drona's son had sought the help of that highest of all the gods, the eternal Mahadeva! For this he could kill single-handed, so large a number of warriors,

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: प्रसन्नो हि महादेवो दद्यादमरतामपि। वीर्यं च गिरिशो दद्याद् येनेन्द्रमपि शातयेत्॥
en: If Mahadeva is pleased he can grant even immortality! Girisha can give such courage as will succeed in checking Indra himself.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: वेदाहं हि महादेवं तत्त्वेन भरतर्षभ। यानि चास्य पुराणानि कर्माणि विविधानि च॥
en: I know Mahadeva truly, foremost of Bharata's race! I know also his various former deeds.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: आदिरेष हि भूतानां मध्यमन्तश्च भारत। विचेष्टते जगच्चेदं सर्वमस्यैव कर्मणा॥
en: He, is the beginning, the middle, and the end of all creatures! This universe acts and moves through his power.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: एवं सिसृक्षुर्भूतानि ददर्श प्रथमं विभुः। पितामहोऽब्रवीच्चैनं भूतानि सृज मा चिरम्॥ हरिकेशस्तथेत्युक्त्वा भूतानां दोषदर्शिवान्। दीर्घकालं तपस्तेपे मग्नोऽम्भसि महातपाः॥
en: The powerful Grandfather, desirous of creating living animals saw Rudra; and the Grandfather asked him, saying,-Create living creatures immediately.—Thus addressed the twany haired Rudra said,-So be it!-and plunged himself into the water and practised austerities for a long time, because he was sensible of the defects of living creatures.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: सुमहान्तं ततः कालं प्रतीक्ष्यैनं पितामहः। स्रष्टारं सर्वभूतानां ससर्ज मनसा परम्॥
en: Having waited for Rudra for a very long time, the Grandfather by his willpower called into being another living being for the purpose of propagating his species.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: सोऽब्रवीत् पितरं दृष्ट्वा गिरिशं सुप्तमम्भसि। यदि मे नाग्रजोऽस्त्यन्यस्तत: स्रक्ष्याम्यहं प्रजाः॥
en: Seeing Girisha plunged into the water, this (second) being, said to his father,-If there be no other being born before me, then I shall multiply my self.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: तमब्रवीत् पिता नास्ति त्वदन्यः पुरुषोऽग्रजः। स्थाणुरेष जले मग्नो विस्रब्धः कुरु वैकृतम्॥
en: His father replied, saying,—There is no other born before you! Shiva has pledged himself into the water! Go and create living creatures, without any fear.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: भूतान्यन्वसृजत् सप्त दक्षादींस्तु प्रजापतीन्। यैरिमं व्यकरोत् सर्वं भूतग्रामं चतुर्विधम्॥
en: He then created many living creatures, having Daksha for their first, who created all those four-fold creatures.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: ताः सृष्टमात्राः क्षुधिताः प्रजाः सर्वाः प्रजापतिम्। बिभक्षयिषवो राजन् सहसा प्राद्रवंस्तदा॥
en: As soon, as they were born, they ran, O king, towards their father,. stricken with hunger and desirous of eating him up.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: स भक्ष्यमाणस्त्राणार्थी पितामहमुपाद्रवत्। आभ्यो मां भगवांस्त्रातु वृत्तिरासां विधीयताम्॥
en: The second being whom Brahman had created, thereupon ran towards him, seeking protection from his own offspring. And he said to the Grandfather,-Oillustrious one, save me from these, and let these creatures have their food.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: ततस्ताभ्यो ददावन्नमोषधी: स्थावराणि च। जङ्गमानि च भूतानि दुर्बलानि बलीयसाम्॥
en: Then the Grandfather gave herbs and plants and other vegetables as their food, and assigned for the strong the weaker creatures as their food.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: विहितान्नाः प्रजास्तास्तु जग्मुः सृष्टा यथागतम्। ततो ववृधिरे राजन् प्रीतिमत्यः स्वयोनिषु॥
en: Their means of sustenance having been thus settled the newly created creatures all went away where they liked, and cheerfully multiplied their respective species.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: भूतग्रामे विवृद्धे तु तुष्टे लोकगुरावपि। उदतिष्ठज्जलाज्ज्येष्ठः प्रजाश्चेमा ददर्श सः॥
en: After the creatures had multiplied and Brahma had become well gratified, the firstborn rose from water and saw the living creation.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: बहुरूपाः प्रजाः सृष्टा विवृद्धाश्च स्वतेजसा। चुक्रोध भगवान् रुद्रो लिङ्गं स्वं चाप्यविध्यत॥ तत् प्रविद्धं तथा भूमौ तथैव प्रत्यतिष्ठत। तमुवाचाव्ययो ब्रह्मा वचोभिः शमयन्निव॥ किं कृतं सलिले शर्व चिरकालस्थितेन ते। किमर्थं चेदमुत्पाद्य लिङ्गं भूमौ प्रवेशितम्॥
en: He saw that various kinds of creatures had been created and that they had multiplied themselves. Seeing it, Rudra became angry and made his generative organ disappear in the bowels of the Earth. Then soothing him by soft words, Brahman said to him-O Sarva, what were you doing so long within the water? Why have you made your generative organ disappear in the bowels of the Earth?

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: सोऽब्रवीजाजसंरम्भस्तथा लोकगुरुर्गुरुम्। प्रजाः सृष्टाः परेणेमाः किं करिष्याम्यनेन वै॥
en: Thus accosted, that lord of the universe angrily answered the lord Brahman,Somebody else has created all these creatures. What purpose then would be fulfilled by this organ of mine.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: तपसाधिगतं चान्नं प्रजार्थं मे पितामह। ओषध्यः परिवर्तेरन् यथैवं सततं प्रजाः॥
en: I have, by my active penances, O Grandfather, created all these creatures. These herbs and plants also will multiply like those that will live upon them.

description: Yudhishthria asks Krishna about the cause of Ashvatthaman's success. Krishna's reply about the glory of Mahadeva
sn: एवमुक्त्वा स सक्रोधो जगाम विमना भवः। गिरेर्मुञ्जवतः पादं तपस्तप्तुं महातपाः॥
en: Saying so, Bhava went away, dispirited and angry, to the foot of the Munjavat mountains for practising austere penances.”

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच ततो देवयुगेऽतीते देवा वै समकल्पयन्। यज्ञं वेदप्रमाणेन विधिवद् यष्टुमीप्सवः॥
en: The holy one said "After the Satya Yuga had passed away, the gods, desirous of celebrating a sacrifice, made preparations according to the Vedic prescription.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: कल्पयामासुरथ ते साधनानि हवींषि च। भागार्हा देवताश्चैव यज्ञियं द्रव्यमेव च॥
en: They collected clarified butter and the other necessary articles. And they not only collected the requisites of their sacrifice, but also determined those amongst themselves that should partake of the sacrificial offerings.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: ता वै रुद्रमजानन्त्यो याथातथ्येन देवताः। नाकल्पयन्त देवस्य स्थाणोर्भागं नराधिप॥
en: Not knowing Rudra truly, the gods, O king, reserved no share for the divine Sthanu.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: सोऽकल्प्यमाने भागे तु कृत्तिवासा मखेऽमरैः। ततः साधनमन्विच्छन् धनुरादौ ससर्ज ह॥
en: Seeing that the celestials reserved no share for him in the sacrificial offerings, Sthanu, clad in deer skins, desired to destroy that Sacrifice and with that object made a bow.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: लोकयज्ञः क्रियायज्ञे गृहयज्ञः सनातनः। पञ्चभूमनृयज्ञश्च जज्ञे सर्वमिदं जगत्॥
en: There are four sorts of Sacrifices, viz. the Loka-Sacrifice, the Sacrifice of especial rites, the eternal domestic Sacrifice, and the Sacrifice consisting in the gratification of man from his enjoyment of the five elemental substances and their compounds. From these four sorts of Sacrifice that the universe had emanated.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: लोकयज्ञैर्नृयज्ञैश्च कपर्दी विदधे धनुः। धनुः सृष्टमभूत् तस्य पञ्चकिष्कुप्रमाणतः॥
en: Kaparddin made that bow out of the materials of the first and the fourth kinds of Sacrifices. The length of that bow was five cubits.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: वषट्कारोऽभवज्या तु धनुषस्तस्य भारत। यज्ञाङ्गानि च चत्वारि तस्य संनहनेऽभवन्॥
en: the sacred (mantra) Vashat, O Bharata, was made its string. The four parts, of which a Sacrifice consists, became the ornaments of that bow.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महादेवस्तदुपादाय कार्मुकम्। आजगामाथा तत्रैव यत्र देवाः समीजिरे॥
en: Then Mahadeva, worked up with rage, and taking up that bow proceeded to that spot where the celestials were celebrating the Sacrifice.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: तमात्तकार्मुकं दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मचारिणमव्ययम्। विव्यथे पृथिवी देवी पर्वताश्च चकम्पिरे॥
en: Seeing the illustrious Rudra arrive there dressed as a Brahmacharin and armed with that bow, the goddess Earth shrank with fear and the mountains began to shake.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: न ववौ पवनश्चैव नाग्निर्जज्वाल वैधितः। व्यभ्रमचापि संविग्नं दिवि नक्षत्रमण्डलम्॥
en: The wind ceased to move, and fire itself, though fed, did not burn. The stars in the sky, in fear, moved irregularly.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: न बभौ भास्करचापि सोमः श्रीमुक्तमण्डलः। तिमिरेणाकुलं सर्वमाकाशं चाभवद् वृतम्॥
en: The Sun's effulgence decreased. The disc of the Moon lost its beauty. The entire sky was covered with a thick darkness.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: अभिभूतास्ततो देवा विषयान्न प्रजज्ञिरे। न प्रत्यभाच्च यज्ञः स देवतास्त्रेसिरे तथा॥
en: The celestials did not know what to do. Their Sacrifice ceased to blaze forth. The gods were all terrified.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: ततः स यज्ञं विव्याध रौद्रेण हृदि पत्रिणा। अपक्रान्तस्ततो यज्ञो मृगा भूत्वा सपावकः॥
en: Rudra then cut the embodiment of Sacrifice with a dreadful arrow in the heart. Assuming the shape of a deer, the embodied from of Sacrifice, fled away with the god of fire.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: स तु तेनैव रूपेण दिवं प्राप्य व्यराजत। अन्वीयमानो रुद्रेण युधिष्ठिर नभस्तले॥
en: Approaching heaven in that form, he shone in beauty. Rudra, however, O Yudhishthira, pursued him through the sky.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: अपक्रान्ते ततो यज्ञे सज्ञां न प्रत्यभात् सुरान्। नष्टसंज्ञेषु देवेषु न प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: After Sacrifice had fled away, the gods lost their beauty. Having lost their senses, the gods were bewildered.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: त्र्यम्बक सवितुर्बाहू भगस्य नयने तथा। पूष्णश्च दशनान् क्रुद्धो धनुष्कोट्या व्यशातयत्॥
en: Then the three-eyed Mahadeva, with his bow, broke in anger the arms of Savitri, and plucked out the eyes of Bhaga and the teeth of Pushna.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: प्राद्रवन्त ततो देवा यज्ञाङ्गानि च सर्वशः। केचित् तत्रैव पूर्णन्तो गतासव इवाभवन्॥
en: The gods and the several parts of Sacrifice fled away. Some amongst the them rolling dropped down senseless.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: स तु विद्राव्य तत् सर्वं शितिकण्ठोऽवहस्य च। अवष्टभ्य धनुष्कोटि रुरोध विबुधांस्ततः॥
en: Having agitated them thus the blue throated Rudra, laughed aloud and whirling his bow, paralysed them.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: ततो वागमरैरुक्ता ज्यां तस्य धनुषोऽच्छिनत्। आ तत् सहसा राजंश्छिन्नज्यं व्यस्फुरद् धनुः॥
en: The celestials then cried aloud. At their command, the string of the bow broke. The string having broken, the bow became straight as a line.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: ततो विधनुषं देवा देवश्रेष्ठमुपागमन्। शरणं सह यज्ञेन प्रसादं चाकरोत् प्रभुः॥
en: The gods then came to the god of gods, and, with the embodied form of Sacrifice, sought the protection of the powerful Mahadeva and tried to please him.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान् स्थाष्य कोपं जलाशये। स जलं पावको भूत्वा शोषयत्यनिशं प्रभो॥
en: Pleased, the great god threw his anger into the water. O king, assuming the from of fire, that wrath is always busy with consuming water.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: भगस्य नयने चैव बाहू च सवितुस्तथा। प्रादात् पूष्णश्च दशनान् पुनर्यज्ञांश्च पाण्डव॥
en: He then gave to Savitri his arms, Bhaga his eyes, and Pushna his teeth. And he also restored the Sacrifices themselves, O Pandava.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: ततः सुस्थमिदं सर्वं बभूव पुनरेव हि। सर्वाणि च हवींष्यस्य देवा भागमकल्पयन्॥
en: The world was once more saved. The gods assigned to Mahadeva all the libations of clarified butter as his share of sacrificial offerings.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: तस्मिन् क्रुद्धेऽभवत् सर्वमसुस्थं भुवनं प्रभो। प्रसन्ने च पुनः सुस्थं प्रसन्नोऽस्य च वीर्यवान्॥
en: O monarch, when Mahadeva had become angry, the whole world was thus agitated, and, when he became gratified, Everything was safe. Highly powerful, the god Mahadeva was pleased with Ashvatthaman.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: ततस्ते निहताः सर्वे तव पुत्रा महारथाः। अन्ये च बहवः शूराः पाञ्चालस्य पदानुगाः॥
en: Therefore your sons, those great carwarriors, could be killed by that warrior. And therefore also many other heroes, viz., the Panchala's, with all their followers, could be killed by him.

description: The great sacrifice of the gods in the Krita age. The destruction of the sacrifice by Rudra. Ashvatthaman's success is due to Rudra's help
sn: न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं न च तद् द्रौणिना कृतम्। महादेवप्रसादेन कुरु कार्यमनन्तरम्॥
en: You should not think of it. It was not Drona's son that performed that act. It was done through the power of Mahadeva. Do now what should be done next."

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्।
en: Having saluted the Supreme Deity (Narayana) and the highest of all male beings (Nara) and the goddess of learning (Sarasvati) let us cry success.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: जनमेजय उवाच हते दुर्योधने चैव हते सैन्ये च सर्वशः। धृतराष्ट्रो महाराज श्रुत्वा किमकरोन्मुने॥
en: Janamejaya said “After Duryodhana, and all the warriors had fallen, what, O sage, did king Dhritarashtra do after hearing of it.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: तथैव कौरवो राजा धर्मपुत्रो महामनाः। कृपप्रभृतयश्चैव किमकुर्वत ते त्रयः॥
en: What also did the great Kuru king Yudhishthira the son of Dharma do? What did the three survivors (of the Kuru army, viz.,) Kripa and the others do?

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: अश्वत्थाम्नः श्रुतं कर्म शापादन्योन्यकारितात्। वृत्तान्तमुत्तरं ब्रूहि यदभाषत संजयः॥
en: I have heard everything about the deeds of Ashvatthaman. Tell me what took place after that mutual denunciation of curses. Tell me all that Sanjaya said to the blind old king!”

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच हते पुत्रशते दीनं छिन्नशाखमिव दुमम्। पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तं धृतराष्ट्रं महीपतिम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said “After he had lost his hundred sons, king Dhritarashtra. stricken with grief on that account, dejected, and looking like a tree shorn of its branches became stupefied with anxiety and lost his power of speech.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: ध्यानमूकत्वमापन्नं चिन्तया सपभिप्लुतम्। अभिगम्य महाराज संजयो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ किं शोचसि महाराज नास्ति शोके सहायता।
en: Possessed of great wisdom, approaching the king the greatly wise Sanjaya, addressed him, saying-Why do you grieve, O monarch? Grief is absolutely useless.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: अक्षौहिण्यो हताश्चाष्टौ दश चैव विशाम्पते॥ निर्जनेयं वसुमती शून्या सम्प्रति केवला।
en: Eight and ten Akshauhinis of warriors, O king, have been killed. The Earth had become desolate, and is almost empty now.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: नानादिग्भ्यः समागम्य नानादेश्या नराधिपाः॥ सहैव तव पुत्रेण सर्वे वै निधनं गताः।
en: Kings of various countries, united with your son, and have all been killed.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: पितृणां पुत्रपौत्राणां ज्ञातीनां सुहृदां तथा। गुरूणां चानुपूर्येण प्रेतकार्याणि कारय॥
en: Let now the obsequial rites of your fathers, sons, grandsons, kinsmen and friends and preceptors be performed duly.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा करुणं वाक्यं पुत्रपौत्रवधार्दितः। पपात भुवि दुर्धर्षो वाताहत इव दुमः॥
en: Vaishampayana continued Deprived of sons, counselors and all his friends, the energetic king Dhritarashtra suddenly dropped down on the Earth like a tree uprooted by the wind.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच हतपुत्रो हतामात्यो हतसर्वसुहज्जनः। दुःखं नूनं भविष्यामि विचरन् पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Deprived as I am of sons, counselors and all my friends, I shall, forsooth, have to rove about sorrowfully over the Earth.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: किं नु बन्धुविहीनस्य जीवितेन ममाद्य वै। लूनपक्षस्य इव मे जराजीर्णस्य पक्षिणः॥
en: What necessity have I now of life itself, deprived as I am of relatives and friends, I am like a bird shorn of its wings and afflicted with decrepitude?

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: हृतराज्यो हतबन्धुर्हतचक्षुश्च वै तथा। न भ्राजिष्ये महाप्राज्ञ क्षीणरश्मिरिवांशुमान्॥
en: Deprived of kingdom, deprived of relatives, and shorn of eyes, I cannot, O you of great wisdom, shine any longer on Earth like a luminary divested of its splendour.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: न कृतं सुहृदां वाक्यं जामदग्न्यस्य जल्पतः। नारदस्य च देवर्षेः कृष्णद्वैपायनस्य च॥
en: I did not follow the advice of friends, of Jamadagni's son, of the celestial Rishi Narada, and of Krishna-Dvaipayana.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: सभामध्ये तु कृष्णेन यच्छ्रेयोऽभिहितं मम। अलं वैरेण ते राजन् पुत्रः संगृह्यतामिति॥ तच वाक्यमकृत्वाहं भृशं तप्यामि दुर्मतिः।
en: In the midst of the assembly, Krishna told me what was for my good, saying,-Do away with hostilities, O king! Let your son take the entire kingdom. I did not foolishly follow that advice, and I am now obliged to repent.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: न हि श्रोतास्मि भीष्मस्य धर्मयुक्तं प्रभाषितम्॥ दुर्योधनस्य च तथा वृषभस्येव नर्दतः। श्रुत्वा कर्णस्य च विपर्ययम्॥ द्रोणसूर्योपरागं च हृदयं मे विदीर्यते।
en: I did not listen to the good counsels of Bhishma. Alas, having heard of the destruction of Duryodhana whose roars were as deep as those of a bull, of the death of Dusshasana and the extinction of Karna and the setting of the Drona-sun, my-heart is not sundered into pieces.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: न स्मराभ्यात्मनः किंचित् पुरा संजय दुष्कृतम्॥ यस्येदं फलमोह मया मूढेन भुज्यते। दुःशासनवधं
en: I do not, O Sanjaya, remember any evil act committed by me in my pristine birth, consequences of which fool as I am, I am now suffering.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: नूनं व्यपकृतं किंचिन्मया पूर्वेषु जन्मसु॥ येन मां दुःखभागेषु धाता कर्मसु युक्तवान्।
en: Forsooth, I committed great sins in my previous lives, for which the great God has made me suffer such a grief.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: परिणामश्च वयसः सर्वबन्धुक्षयश्च मे॥ सुहृन्मित्रविनाशश्च दैवयोगादुपागतः। कोऽन्योऽस्ति दुःखिततरो मत्तोऽन्यो हि पुमान् भुवि॥
en: This destruction of all my relatives, wellwishers and friends, at this old age has been brought about by Destiny. Who is there on Earth more afflicted than my wretched self.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: तन्मामद्यैव पश्यन्तु पाण्डवाः संशितव्रताः। विवृतं ब्रह्मलोकस्य दीर्घमध्वानमास्थितम्॥
en: Therefore, let the Pandavas come and see me this very day determined upon following the long way that leads to the regions of Brahman."

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य लालप्यमानस्य बहुशोकं वितन्वतः। शोकापहं नरेन्द्रस्य संजयो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana continued-"While king Dhritarashtra was thus bewailing, Sanjaya addressed him in the following words for driving away his grief.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: शोकं राजन् व्यपनुद श्रुतास्ते वेदनिश्चयाः। शास्त्रागमाश्च विविधा वृद्धेभ्यो नृपसत्तम।॥ संजये पुत्रशोकार्ते यदूचुर्मुनयः पुरा।
en: Cast off your grief, O king! You have heard the teachings of the Vedas and various scriptures, from the lips of the old, O king! You have heard those words which the sages said to Srinjaya while the latter was stricken with grief on account of the death of his son.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: यथा यौवनजं दर्पमास्थिते तं सुते नृप॥ न त्वया सुहृदां वाक्यं ब्रुवतामवधारितम्। स्वार्थश्च न कृतः कश्चिल्लुब्धेन फलगृद्धिना॥
en: When your son, O king, grew elated with pride, you did not accept the advice offered to you by your well-wisher. You did not, through covetousness, do what was really for your good.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: असिनैवैकधारेण स्वबुद्ध्या तु विचेष्टितम्। प्रायशोऽवृत्तसम्पन्नाः सततं पर्युपासिताः॥
en: Your own intelligence, like a sharp sword, has cut you. You only sought the company of wicked men,

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: यस्य दुःशासनो मन्त्री राधेयश्च दुरात्मवान्। शकुनिश्चैव दुष्टात्मा चित्रसेनश्च दुर्मतिः॥ शल्यश्च येन वै सर्वं शल्यभूतं कृतं जगत्।
en: Your son had Dusshasana, the wicked son of Radha, the equally wicked Shakuni, Chritrasena and Shalya for his counsellor. Your son made the entire world his enemy.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: कुरुवृद्धस्य भीष्मस्य गान्धार्या विदुरस्य च॥ द्रोणस्य च महाराज कृपस्य च शरद्वतः। कृष्णस्य च महाबाहो नारदस्य च धीमतः॥ ऋषीणां च तथान्येषां व्यासस्यामिततेजसः। न कृतं तेन वचनं तव पुत्रेण भारत॥
en: You son, O Bharata, did not follow the words of Bhishma the reverend chief of the Kurus, of Gandhari and Vidura, of Drona, O king, of Kripa the son of Sharadvat of the mighty-armed Krishna, of the intelligent Narada, of many other Rishis, and of Vyasa himself.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: धर्म: सत्कृतः कश्चिन्नित्यं युद्धमभीप्सता। अल्पबुद्धिरहंकारी नित्यं युद्धमिति ब्रुवन्। क्रूरो दुर्मर्षणो नित्यमसंतुष्टश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: Though powerful your son was of little intelligence, proud, always anxious to fight, wicked, ungovernable, and discontented.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: श्रुतवानसि मेधावी सत्यवांश्चैव नित्यदा। न मुह्यन्तीदृशाः सन्तो बुद्धिमन्तो भवादृशाः॥
en: You are learned, intelligent, and always truthful. Righteous and intelligent persons like yourself, are never stupefied by grief.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: न धर्मः सत्कृतः कश्चित् तव पुत्रेण मारिष। क्षपिताः क्षत्रियाः सर्वे शत्रूणां वर्धितं यशः॥ न
en: For this the Kshatriya order has been exterminated, because they did not care for virtue, and always talked of battle, and the fame of your foes enhanced.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: मध्यस्थो हि त्वमप्यासीन क्षमकिञ्चिदुक्तवान्। दुधरेण त्वया भारस्तुलया न समं धृतः॥
en: You had occupied the position of an umpire, but you did not utter a word of wholesome advice. Unfitted as you were for the work, you did not hold the scales evenly.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: आदावेव मनुष्येण वर्तितव्यं यथाक्षमम्। यथा नातीतमर्थं वै पश्चात्तापेन युज्यते॥
en: Every one should, at the beginning follow such a line of action that he mey not have, in the end, to repent for something already done by him.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: पुत्रगृद्ध्या त्वया राजन् प्रियं तस्य चिकीर्षितम्। पश्चात्तापमिमं प्राप्तो न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि॥
en: Out of affection for your son, O king, you did what was agreeable to Duryodhana. You are obliged to repent for that now. You should not, however, grieve.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: केवलं दृष्ट्वा प्रपातं नानुपश्यति। स भ्रष्टो मधुलोभेन शोचत्येवं यथा भवान्॥
en: The man who always looks at the honey without seeing the fall, meets with destruction through his covetousness for honey. Such a man is obliged to repent like yourself.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: अर्थान्न शोचन् प्राप्नोति न शोचन् विन्दते फलम्। न शोचश्रियमाप्नोति न शोचन् विन्दते परम्॥
en: The man who indulges in grief never acquires wealth. By grieving one loses the fruits he seeks for. Grief again stands in the way of the acquisition of objects dear to us. The man who grieves loses even his salvation.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: स्वयमुत्पादयित्वागिनं वस्त्रेण परिवेष्टयन्। दह्यमानो मनस्तापं भजते न स पण्डितः॥
en: The man who keeps a burning coal within the folds of his cloth and is burnt by the fire thereof is surely called a fool if he grieves for his injuries.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: त्वयैव ससुतेनायं वाक्यवायुसमीरितः। लोभाज्येन स संसिक्तो ज्वलितः पार्थपावकः॥ मधु यः
en: with your You and your son, had with your words fanned the Partha-fire, and covetousness as clarified butter made that fire blaze forth into burning flames.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: तस्मिन् समिद्धे पतिताः शलभा इव ते सुताः। तान् वै शराग्निनिर्दग्धान्न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि॥
en: Yours fell into that burning fire like insects. You should not, however, grieve for them now that they have all been burnt in the fire of the enemy's arrows.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: यच्चाश्रुपातात् कलिलं वदनं वहसे नृप। अशास्त्रदृष्टमेतद्धि न प्रशंसन्ति पण्डिताः॥
en: The shedding of tears, O king, is not approved by the scriptures or praised by the wise.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: विस्फुलिङ्गा इव ह्येतान् दहन्ति किल मानवान्। जहीहि मन्यु बुद्ध्या वै धारयात्मानमात्मान॥
en: These tears, like sparks of fire, consume the head for whom they are shed. Drive away your grief with your intelligence, and cheer yourself up with your mental strength.

description: Lamentation of Dhritarastra after the loss of his hundred sons and the lose of his hundred sons and consolation
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमाश्वासितस्तेन संजयेन महात्मना। विदुरो भूय एवाह बुद्धिपूर्वं परंतप॥
en: Thus was the king consoled by the great Sanjaya. Vidura then, O scorcher of foes, once again addressed the king, showing great intelligence."

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽमृतसमैर्वाक्यै दयन् पुरुषर्षभम्। वैचित्रवीर्यं विदुरो यदुवाच निबोध तत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Listen, O Janamejaya, to the nectar like words that Vidura said to the son of Vichitravirya and by which be pleased that foremost of men.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: विदुर उवाच उत्तिष्ठ राजन् किं शेषे धारयात्मानमात्मना। एषा वै सर्वसत्त्वानां लोकेश्वर परा गतिः॥
en: Vidura said Rise, O king! Why are you lying on the Earth. Cheer yourself up. O king, this is the final end of all living creatures.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः। संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्॥
en: Everything is liable to destruction; everything that is high is sure to fall down. Union is sure to end in separation; life is sure to end in death.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: यदा शूरं च भीरुं च यमः कर्षति भारत। तत् किं न योत्स्यन्ति हि ते क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रियर्षभ॥
en: The Destroyer, O Bharata, takes both the hero and the coward. Why then, O foremost of Kshatriyas, should not Kshatriyas engage themselves in battle.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: अयुध्यमानो म्रियते युध्यमानश्च जीवति। कालं प्राप्य महाराज न कश्चिदतिवर्तते॥
en: He, who never fights has been seen to die, while he who engaged himself in battle has been seen to escape alive.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: अभावादीनि भूतानि भावमध्यानि भारत। अभावनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: As regards living creatures, they did not exist at first. They exist in the intervening period. In the end they once more become nonexistent. Why should then one grieve for the same?

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: न शोचन् मृतमन्वेति न शोचन् म्रियते नरः। एवं सांसिद्धिके लोके किमर्थमनुशोचसि।।७
en: The man who grieves does not succeed in meeting with the dead. By grieving one does not himself die. While such is the course of the world, why do you indulge in grief.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: कालः कर्षति भूतानि सर्वाणि विविधान्युत। न कालस्य प्रियः कश्चिन्न द्वेष्यः कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Death drags all creatures, even the gods. There is none dear or hateful to death, O Kuru chief.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: यथा वायुस्तृणाग्राणि संवर्तयति सर्वशः। तथा कालवशं यान्ति भूतानि भरतर्षभ॥
en: As the wind tears off all the blades of grass, even so, O foremost of Bharata's race, Death rules over all creatures.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: एकसार्थप्रयातानां सर्वेषां तत्र गामिनाम्। यस्य कालः प्रयात्यग्रे तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: All creatures are like members of a caravan bound for the same country. When death will overtake all, it is immaterial whom he meets first.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: न चाप्येतान् हतान् युद्धे राजशोचितुमर्हसि। प्रमाणं यदि शास्त्राणि गतास्ते परमां गतिम्॥
en: O king, you should not grieve for those who have been killed in battle. If the scriptures are authoritative all of them must have obtained the highest end.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: सर्वे स्वाध्यायवन्तो हि सर्वे च चरितव्रताः। सर्वे चाभिमुखाः क्षीणास्तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: All of them were well read in the Vedas; all of them had practised vows. All of them have met with death after fighting with the enemy. What is there to be sorry in this.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: अदर्शनादापतिताः पुनश्चादर्शनं गताः। नैते तव न तेषां त्वं तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: They had been invisible before birth. Having come from that unknown region, they have again become invisible. They are not yours, nor are you theirs. Why should you grieve then for such disappearance?

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: हतोऽपि लभते स्वर्ग हत्वा च लभते यशः। उभयं नो बहुगुणं नास्ति निष्फलता रणे॥
en: If killed, one acquires heaven. By killing, fame is acquired. Both of these, produce great merit. Battle, therefore, is not unproductive of good.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: तेषां कामदुधालँ लोकानिन्द्रः संकल्पयिष्यति। इन्द्रस्यातिथयो ोते भवन्ति भरतर्षभ।१५।।
en: forsooth, Indra will give them regions capable of granting every wish. These, O foremost of men, become the guests of Indra.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: न यज्ञैर्दक्षिणावद्भिर्न तपोभिर्न विद्यया। स्वर्ग यान्ति तथा मा यथा शूरा रणे हताः॥
en: By celebrating sacrifice with profuse gifts, by ascetic penances and by learning, men cannot, go so quickly to heaven as heroes killed in battle.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: शरीरग्निषु शूराणां जुहुवुस्ते शराहुतीः। हूयमानाशरांश्चैव सेहुस्तेजस्विनो मिथः॥
en: On the bodies of hostile heroes who were like the sacrificial fire, they poured libations of arrows. Highly energetic, they had in return to bear the arrowy libations poured upon them by their foes.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: एवं राजंस्तवाचक्षे स्वयं पन्थानमुत्तमम्। न युद्धादधिकं किंचित् क्षत्रियस्येह विद्यते॥
en: I tell you, O king, that for a Kshatriya in this world there is not a better way to heaven then battle.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: क्षत्रियास्ते महात्मानः शूराः समितिशोभनाः। आशिषः परमाः प्राप्त न शोर्ध्या सर्व एव हि॥
en: They were all great Kshatriyas; brave as they were, they were ornaments of assemblies. They have attained highest of blessed regions. They are not persons for whom we should be sorry.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: आत्मानमात्मनाऽऽश्वास्य मा शुचः पुरुषर्षभ। नाद्य शोकाभिभूतस्त्वं कायमुत्स्रष्टुमर्हसि॥
en: Solacing yourself, by you own self, cease to grieve, O best of men. You should not allow yourself to be overwhelmed with sorrow and to all action.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: मातापितृसहस्राणि पुत्रदारशतानि च। संसारेष्वनुभूतानि कस्य ते कस्य वा वयम्॥
en: There are thousands of mothers and fathers and sons and wives in this world. Whose are they and whose are we?

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: शोकस्थानसहस्राणि भयस्थानशतानि च। दिवसे दिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति च पण्डितम्॥
en: Thousands of causes spring up daily for sorrow and thousands for fear. These, however, affect the ignorant and not the wise.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: न कालस्य प्रियः कश्चिन्न द्वेष्यः कुरुसत्तम। न मध्यस्थः क्वचित्कालः सर्वं कालः प्रकर्षति॥
en: There is none dear of hateful to Time, O Kuru chief. Time is indifferent to none. All are equally dragged by time. give up

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: काल: पचति भूतानि कालः संहरते प्रजाः। कालः सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः॥
en: Time makes all creatures grow, and it is Time that destroys all. When all else is asleep, Time is awake. Time is irresistible.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: अनित्यं यौवनं रूपं जीवितं द्रव्यसंचयः। आरोग्यं प्रियसंवासो गृद्ध्येदेषु न पण्डितः॥
en: Youth, beauty, life, wealth, health, and friends, are all unstable. The wise will never seek any of these.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: न जानपदिकं दुःखमेकः शोचितुमर्हसि। अप्यभावेन युज्यते तचास्य न निवर्तते॥
en: You should not grieve for what is universal. By indulging in grief a person may himself die, but grief itself by being indulged in, never becomes light.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: अशोचन् प्रतिकुर्वीत यदि पश्येत् पराक्रमम्। भैषज्यमेतद् दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत्॥
en: If you feel any grief heavily, it should be overcome by not indulging in it. This is the only remedy for grief, viz., that one should not indulge in it.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते। अनिष्टसम्प्रयोगाच विप्रयोगात् प्रियस्य च॥ मानुषा मानसैर्दुःखैर्दह्यन्ते चाल्पबुद्धयः।
en: By indulging in it, one cannot lesson it. On the other hand, it increases when being indulged in. When any evil or when bereavement of some dear one, comes on, only they that are of little intelligence allow their minds to be laden with grief.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: नार्थो न धर्मो न सुखं यदेतदनुशोचसि॥ न च नापैति कार्यार्थात्रिवर्गाचैव हीयते।
en: This is neither Profit, nor Religion, nor Happiness, of which you are thinking.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: अन्यामन्यां धनावस्थां प्राप्य वैशेषिकी नराः॥ असंतुष्टाः प्रमुह्यनित संतोष यान्ति पण्डिताः। प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छरीरमौषधैः। एतद् विज्ञानसामर्थ्यं न बालैः समतामियात्॥
en: The indulgence of grief in the sure means of one's losing one's objects. Through it, one deviates from the three great ends of life. They, who are not contented are stupefied by the vicissitudes of fortune. The wise, are, on the other hand, unaffected by such changes. One should destroy mental grief by wisdom, as physical grief should be destroyed by medicine. Wisdom has this power. They, however, that are foolish, can never acquire equanimity of mind.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: शयानं चानुशेते हि तिष्ठन्तं चानुतिष्ठति। अनुधावति धावन्तं कर्म पूर्वकृतं नरम्॥
en: Pristine actions closely follow a man, so much so that they lie by him when he lies down, stand by him when he stands, and run with him when he runs.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: यस्यां यस्यामवस्थायां यत् करोति शुभाशुभम्। तस्यां तस्यामवस्थायां तत्फलं समुपाश्नुते॥
en: As a man acts well or ill, so he enjoys or suffers the fruit thereof.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: येन येन शरीरेण यद्यत् कर्म करोति यः। तेन तेन शरीरेण तत्फलं समुपाश्नुते॥
en: In physical actions also one enjoys or suffers the fruits according to his acts.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः। आत्मैव ह्यात्मनः साक्षी कृतस्यापकृतस्य च॥
en: One's own self is one's own friend, again one's own self is one's own enemy. One's own self is the witness of one's good and evil acts.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: शुभेन कर्मणा सौख्यं दुःखं पापेन कर्मणा। कृतं भवति सर्वत्र नाकृतं विद्यते क्वचित्॥
en: Good acts beget a state of happiness, and sinful deeds bring on woe. One always reaps the fruit of one's acts. One never enjoys of suffers happiness or misery that is not the outcome of one's own acts.

description: . Consolation to Dhritarashtra by Vidura. The power of Death
sn: न हि ज्ञानविरुद्धेषु बह्वपायेषु कर्मसु। मूलघातिषु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः॥
en: Intelligent persons like you, O king, never commit sinful deeds, that are disapproved by knowledge and that strike at the very root of virtue and happiness.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच सुभाषितैर्महाप्राज्ञ शोकोऽयं विगतो मम। भूय एव तु वाक्यानि श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said "O you of great wisdom, by grief has been removed by your excellent words. I wish you, however, to speak again.

sn: अनिष्टानां च संसर्गादिष्टानां च विसर्जनात्। कथं हि मानसैर्दुःखै प्रमुच्यन्ते तु पण्डिताः॥
en: How, indeed, do the wise free themselves from mental grief begotten by evil deeds and the bereavement of dear objects."

sn: विदुर उवाच यतो यतो मनो दुःखात् सुखाद् वा विप्रमुच्यते। ततस्ततो नियम्यैतच्छान्तिं विन्देत वै बुधः॥ अशाश्वतमिदं सर्वं चिन्त्यमानं नरर्षभ। कदलीसंनिभो लोकः सारो ह्यस्य न विद्यते॥
en: Vidura said He that is wise enjoys peace by subduing both grief and joy by means by which one may escape from grief and joy.

sn: यदा प्राज्ञाश्चे मूढाश्च धनवन्तोऽथ निर्धनाः। सर्वे पितृवनं प्राप्य स्वपन्ति विगतज्वराः॥
en: Every thing we are anxious for, O foremost of men, is ephemeral. The world is like a weak plantain tree.

sn: निर्मासैरस्थिभूयिष्ठैर्गात्रैःस्नायुनिबन्धनैः। किं विशेष प्रपश्यन्ति तत्र तेषां परे जनाः॥ येन प्रत्यवगच्छेयुः कुलरूपविशेषणम्। कस्मादन्योन्यमिच्छन्ति विप्रलब्धधियो नराः॥
en: Since the wise and the ignorant the rich and the poor, all, shorn of their anxieties, sleep on the crematorium, with bodies devoid of flesh and full of naked bones, and sinews, whom amongst them will the survivors regard as possessed of distinguishing marks by which the attributes of birth and beauty may be determined? Since every thing is equal in death why should men, whose understandings are always deceived covet one another's rank and position.

sn: गृहाणीव हि मानामाहुर्देहानि पण्डिताः। कालेन विनियुज्यन्ते सत्त्वमेकं तु शाश्वतम्॥
en: The learned say that the bodies of men are like house, which are destroyed in time. There is one being, however, that is eternal.

sn: यथा जीर्णमजीर्णं वा वस्त्रं त्यक्त्वा तु पूरुषः। अन्यद् रोचयते वस्त्रमेवं देहाः शरीरिणाम्॥
en: As a person casting off an old cloth puts on a fresh one, so is the case with the bodies of all embodied beings.

sn: वैचित्रवीर्य प्राप्यं हि दुःखं वा यदि वा सुखम्। प्राप्नुवन्तीह भूतानि स्वकृतेनैव कर्मणा॥
en: O son of Vichitravirja creatures reap happiness or misery, as the fruit of their own acts.

sn: कर्मणा प्राप्यते स्वर्गः सुखं दुःखं च भारत। ततो वहति तं भारमवशः स्ववशोऽपि वा॥
en: By their acts they secure heaven, O Bharata, or happiness, or misery. Whether competent or otherwise, they have to bear their burdens which are the result of their own acts.

sn: यथा च मृन्मयं भाण्डं चक्रारूढं विपद्यते। किंचित् प्रक्रियमाणं वा कृतमात्रमथापि वा॥ छिन्नं वाप्यवरोप्यन्तमवतीर्णमथापि वा। आर्द्र वाप्यथवा शुष्कं पच्यमानमथापि वा॥ उत्तार्यमाणमापाकादुद्धृतं चापि भारत। अथवा परिभुज्यन्तमेवं देहाः शरीरिणाम्॥
en: As amongst earthen pots some break while still on the potter's wheel, some while partially shaped, some as soon as shaped, some after removal from the wheel, some while in course of being removed, some after removal, some while wet, some while dry, some while being burnt, some while being removed from the kiln, some after removal therefrom, and some while being used, so is the case with the bodics of embodied creatures.

sn: गर्भस्थो वा प्रसूतो वाप्यथ वा दिवसान्तरः। अर्धमासगतो वापि मासमात्रगतोऽपि वा॥ संवत्सरगतो वापि द्विसंवत्सर एव वा। यौवनस्थोऽथ मध्यस्थो वृद्धो वापि विपद्यते॥
en: Some are destroyed while in embryo, some after coming out of the womb, some on the day after, some after a fortnight or a month, some on after a year or two, some in youth, some in middle age, and some when old.

sn: प्राक्कर्मभिस्तु भूतानि भवन्ति न भवन्ति च। एवं सांसिद्धिके लोके किमर्थमनुतप्यसे॥
en: Creatures are born or destroyed according to their pristine acts. When such is the course of the world, why do you grieve?

sn: यथा तु सलिलं राजन् क्रीडार्थमनुसंतरत्। उन्मजेच निमज्जेच किंचित् सत्त्वं नराधिप॥ एवं संसारगहने उन्मजननिमजने। कर्मभोगेन बध्यन्ते किश्यन्ते चाल्पबुद्धयः॥
en: As men, while swimming, sometimes dive and sometimes emerge, so, O king, creatures sink and emerge in life's stream. They that are of limited under standing suffer or meet with death as the result of their own acts.

sn: ये तु प्राज्ञाः स्थिताः सत्त्वे संसारेऽस्मिन् हितैषिणः। समागमज्ञा भूतानां ते यान्ति परमां गतिम्॥
en: They, however, that are wise, virtuous and desirous of doing good to all living creatures, who are acquainted with the real nature of beings in this world, attain at last to the highest end."

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कथं संसारगहनं विज्ञेयं वदतां वर एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तत्त्वमाख्याहि पृच्छतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said "O best of speakers, how may the wilderness of this world be known? I wish to hear this. Accosted by me, tell me this.”

sn: विदुर उवाच जन्मप्रभृति भूतानां क्रिया सर्वोपलक्ष्यते। पूर्वमेवेह कलिले वसते किंचिदन्तरम्॥
en: Vidura said "I will describe to you all the acts of creatures from the very beginning. In the beginning it lives in the mixture of blood and semen. Then it grows little by little. Then on the expiration of the fifth mouth it puts on a shape.

sn: ततः स पञ्चमेऽतीते मासे वासमकल्पयत्। ततः सर्वाङ्गसम्पूर्णो गर्भो वै स तु जायते॥
en: It next becomes a foetus with all its limbs made up, and live in a dirty place, covered with flesh and blood.

sn: अमेध्यमध्ये वसति मांसशोणितलेपने। ततस्तु वायुवेगेन अर्ध्वपादो ह्यधःशिराः॥
en: Then, by the action of the wind, its lower limbs are turned upwards and the head comes downwards. Getting by this posture at the mouth of the uterus, it suffers manifold miseries.

sn: योनिद्वारमुपागम्य बहून् क्लेशान् समृच्छति। योनिसम्पीडनाच्चैव पूर्वकर्मभिरन्वितः॥ तस्मान्मुक्तः स संसारादन्यान् पश्यत्युपद्रवान्।
en: On account of the contraction of the uterus, the creatures then comes out of it, bearing the results of all his pristine acts. He then meets in this world with other evils that best him. Misfortunes go to him like dogs drawn by the scent of ineat.

sn: ग्रहास्तमनुगच्छन्ति सारमेया इवामिषम्॥ ततः प्राप्तोत्तरे काले व्याधयश्चापि तं तथा।
en: Next various diseases assail him while he is enchained by his pristine acts.

sn: उपसर्पन्ति जीवन्तं बध्यमानं स्वकर्मभिः॥ तं बद्धमिन्द्रियैः पाशैः संगस्वादुभिरावृतम्।
en: Bound by the fetters of lust and women and wealth and other sweets of life, various evil practises also approach, him then, O king!

sn: व्यसनान्यपि वर्तन्ते विविधानि नराधिप।॥ बध्यमानश्च तैर्भूयो नैव तृप्तिमुपैति सः।
en: Caught by these, he never enjoys happiness. At that time he does not obtain the fruit of his acts, right or wrong. They, however, fix their minds on reflection, succeed in protection their souls.

sn: तदा नावैति चैवायं प्रकुर्वन् साध्वसाधु वा॥ तथैव परिरक्षिन्त ये ध्यानपरिनिष्ठितः। अयं न बुध्यते तावद् यमलोकमथागतम्॥
en: The person overcome by his senses does not know that death has come at his door. At last, dragged by the messengers of the Destroyer, he meets with death at the appointed time.

sn: यमदूतैर्विकृष्यंश्च मृत्यु कालेन गच्छति। वाग्धीनस्य च यन्मात्रमिष्टानिष्टं कृतं मुखे। भूय एवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं बध्यमानमुपेक्षते॥
en: Overcome by his senses, he does good and evil at the every commencement. Having enjoyed or suffered this fruits of these, he again becomes indifferent to his acts of selfdestruction.

sn: अहो विनिकृतो लोको लोभेन च वशीकृतः। लोभक्रोधभयोन्मत्तो नात्मानमवबुध्यते॥
en: Alas, the world is deceived, and covetousness subdues it. Deprived of sense by covetousness, anger, and fear, one knows not one's own self!

sn: कुलीनत्वे च रमे दुष्कुलीनान् विकुत्सयन्। धनदर्पण दृप्तश्च दरिद्रान् परिकुत्सयन्॥
en: Proud of his high birth, one is seen to speak ill of those that are but high born. Elated with pride of wealth, one is seen to hate the poor.

sn: मूर्खानिति परानाहं नात्मानं समवेक्षते। दोषान् क्षिपति चान्येषां नात्मानं शास्तुमिच्छति॥
en: One considers others as ignorant fools, but seldom gauges his own self. One attributes faults to others, but never wishes to punish his own self.

sn: यदा प्राज्ञाश्च मूर्खाश्च धनवन्तश्च निर्धनाः। कुलीनाश्चाकुलीनाश्च मानिनोऽथाप्यमानिनः॥ सर्वे पितृवनं प्राप्ताः स्वपन्ति विगतत्वचः। निर्मासैरस्थिभूयिष्ठैर्गात्रैः स्नायुनिबन्धनैः॥ विशेष न प्रपश्यन्ति तत्र तेषां परे जनाः। येन प्रत्यवगच्छेयुः कुलरूपविशेषणम्॥
en: Since the wise and the ignorant, the rich and the poor, the high-born and the low-born, the honored and the dishonored, all go to the place of the dead and sleep there shorn of anxiety, with bodies divested of flesh and full only of bones and dried up tendons, whom amongst then would the survivors regard as standing superior to others and by what marks would they determine the attributes of birth and beauty.

sn: यदा सर्वे समं न्यस्ता: स्वपन्ति धरणीतले। कस्मादन्योन्यमिच्छन्ति प्रलब्धुमिह दुर्बुधाः॥
en: When all shall sleep likewise on the bare ground, why then should men, foolishly, desire to deceive one another.

sn: प्रत्यक्षं च परोक्षं च यो निशम्य श्रुतिं त्विमाम्। अधुवे जीवलोकेऽस्मिन् यो धर्ममनुपालयन्। जन्मप्रभृति वर्तेत प्राप्नुयात् परमां गतिम्॥
en: He who, looking at this scriptural injunction with his own eyes or hearing it from others, practises virtue in this unstable world of life and sticks to it from early age, attains to the highest end.

sn: एवं सर्वं विदित्वा वै यस्तत्त्वमनुवर्तते। स प्रमोक्षाय लभते पन्थानं मनुजेश्वर॥
en: Learning all this, he that sticks to Truth, O king, gets over all paths.”

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यदिदं धर्मगहनं बुद्ध्या समनुगम्यते। तद्धि विस्तरतः सर्वं बुद्धिमार्ग प्रशंस मे॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Describ: fully to me the ways of that intelligence by which this wilderness of duties may be safely crossed.

sn: विदुर उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि नमस्कृत्वा स्वयंभुवे। यथा संसारगहनं वदन्ति परमर्षयः॥
en: Vidura said “Having saluted the Self-create, I will obey your command by telling, you how the great sages speak of the wilderness of life.

sn: कश्चिन्महति कान्तारे वर्तमानो द्विजः किल। महद् दुर्गमनुप्राप्तो वनं क्रव्यादसंकुलम्॥
en: A cretin Brahmana, living in the great world, found himself on one occasion in a large inaccessible forest abounding with beasts of prey.

sn: सिंहव्याघ्रगजौघैरतिघोरं महास्यनैः। पिशितादैरतिभयैर्महोग्राकृतिभिस्तथा॥ समन्तात् संपरिक्षिप्तं यत् स्म दृष्ट्वा त्रसेद् यमः।
en: It was full of lions and tigers and other animals looking like elephants, all of which were roaring aloud. Such was the view of that forest that Yama himself would be frightened.

sn: तदस्य दृष्ट्वा हृदयमुद्वेगमगमत् परम्॥ अभ्युच्छयश्च रोम्णां वै विक्रियाच परंतप।
en: Seeing the forest, the heart of the Brahmana was greatly agitated. His hairs stood erect, and other signs of fear manifested themselves, O destroyer of enemies.

sn: स तद् वनं व्यनुसरन् सम्प्रधावन्नितस्ततः॥ वीक्षमाणो दिशः सर्वाः शरणं व भवेदिति।
en: Entering it, he began to run hither and thither, looking every side for finding out somebody whose shelter he might seek.

sn: स तेषां छिद्रमन्विच्छन् प्रद्रुतो भयपीडितः॥ न च निर्याति वै दूरं न वा तैर्विप्रमोच्यते।
en: Wishing to avoid those terrible creatures, he ran about in fear. He could not go far away from them or free himself from their presence.

sn: अथापश्यद् वनं घोरं समन्ताद् वागरावृतम्॥ बाहुभ्यां सम्परिक्षिप्त स्त्रिया परमघोरया।
en: He then saw that terrible forest was surrounded with a net, and that a dreadful woman stood there, stretching her arms.

sn: पञ्चशीर्षधरै गैः शैलैरिव समुन्नतैः॥ नभःस्पृशैर्महावृक्षः परिक्षिप्तं महावनम्।
en: That large forest was also beset with many five-headed snakes of dreadful forms, tall as mountain summits touching the very sky.

sn: वनमध्ये च तत्राभूदुदपानः समावृतः॥ वल्लीभिस्तृणछन्नाभिर्दूढाभिरभिसंवृतः।
en: Within it was a pit whose mouth was covered with many hard and strong creepers and herbs.

sn: पपात स द्विजस्तत्र निगूढे सलिलाशये।॥ विलग्नश्चाभवत् तस्मिन् लतासंतानसंकुले। पनसस्य यथा जातं वृन्तवद्धं महाफलम्॥ स तथा लम्बते तत्र रार्ध्वपादो ह्यधःशिराः।
en: While wandering the Brahmana dropped into that invisible pit. He was entangled in those creepers that were interwoven with one another, like the large fruit of a jack tree hanging by its stalk. He remained there hanging with feet upwards and head downwards.

sn: अथ तत्रापि चान्योऽस्य भूयो जात उपद्रवः॥ कूपमध्ये महानागमपश्यत महाबलम्।
en: While in that state, he was visited by various other calamities. He saw a large and mighty snake within the pit. He also saw a gigantic elephant near its mouth.

sn: कूपवीनाहवेलायामपश्यत महागजम् ॥ षड्वक्त्रं कृष्णशुक्लं च द्विषट्कपदचारिणम्।
en: The elephant, was dark coloured and had six faces and twelve feet. And the animal gradually approached that pit overgrown with creepers and trees.

sn: क्रमेण परिसर्पन्तं वल्लीवृक्षसमावृतम्॥ तस्य चापि प्रशाखासु वृक्षशाखावलम्बिनः। नानारूपा मधुकरा घोररूपा भयावहाः॥ आसते मधु संवृत्य पूर्वमेव निकेतजाः।
en: About the twigs of the tree which was at the mouth of the pit. moved about many bees of dreadful forms, engaged from before in drinking the honey gathered in their comb.

sn: भूयो भूयः समीहन्ते मधूनि भरतर्षभ॥ स्वादनीयानि भूतानां यैर्बालो विप्रकृष्यते।
en: They repeatedly desired, O foremost of Bharata's race, to taste that honey which though sweet to all creatures could, however, attract children only. was not

sn: तत्रैव च मनुष्यस्य तेषां मधूनां बहुधा धारा प्रस्रवते तदा॥ आलम्बमानः स पुमान् धारां पिबति सर्वदा।
en: The honey (in the comb) fell in many gets below. The person who was hanging in the pit continually drank those jets.

sn: न चास्य तृष्णा विरता पिबमानस्य संकटे॥ अभीप्सति तदा नित्यमतृप्तः स पुनः पुनः।
en: Drinking that honey in such a pitiable condition, his thirst, however, appeased. Unsatiated with repeatedly drinking the same the person desired for more.

sn: न चास्य जीविते राजन् निर्वेदः समजायत॥ जीविताशा प्रतिष्ठिता। कृष्णाः श्वेताश्च तं वृक्षं कुट्टयन्ति च मूषिकाः॥
en: Even then, O king, he could not give up hopes of life. Still, the man expected to live. A number of black and white rates were eating away the roots of that tree.

sn: व्यालैश्च वनदुर्गान्ते स्त्रिया च परमोग्रया। कूपाधस्ताच नागेन वीनाहे कुञ्जरेण च॥ वृक्षप्रपाताच भयं मूषिकेभ्यश्च पञ्चमम्। मधुलोभान्मधुकरैः षष्ठमाहुर्महद् भयम्॥
en: There was fear from the beasts of prey, from that dreadful woman on the outskirts of that forest, from that snake at the bottom of the well, from that elephant near its top, from the fall of the tree brought about by the rats, and lastly from those bees flying about for drinking the honey.

sn: एवं स वसते तत्र क्षिप्तः संसारसागरे। न चैव जीविताशायां निर्वेदमुपगच्छति॥
en: He lived in that condition, deprived of his senses, in that forest, never losing at any time the hope of continuing his life.”

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अहो खलु महद् दुःखं कृच्छ्रवासश्च तस्य ह। कथं तस्य रतिस्तत्र तुष्टिर्वा वदतां वर॥
en: Dhritarashtra said “Alas great was the misery of that person and very painful his life. Tell me, O best of speakers, whence his attachment to life and whence his happiness was.

sn: स देशः क्व नु यत्रासौ वसते धर्मसंकटे। कथं वा स विमुच्येत नरस्तस्मान्महाभयात्॥
en: Where is that region, so inimical to the practice of virtue, where that person lives, Oh, tell me how that man will be freed from all those great dangers?

sn: एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व साधु चेष्टामहे तदा। कृपा मे महती जाता तस्याभ्युद्धरणेन हि॥
en: Tell me all this. We shall then try our best for him. I am stricken with pity on account of the difficulties that lie in the way of his release."

sn: विदुर उवाच उपमानामिदं राजन् मोक्षविद्भिरुदाहृतम्। सुकृतं विन्दते येन परलोकेषु मानवः॥
en: Vidura said O king, they that are conversant with the religion of Moksha cite this as a simile. Understanding this properly, a person may attain to blissful regions hereafter.

sn: उच्यते यत् तु कान्तारं महासंसार एव सः। वनं दुर्गं हि यच्चैतत् संसारगहनं हि तत्॥
en: That which is described as the forest is the great world. The inaccessible forest within it is the limited sphere of a man's life.

sn: ये च ते कथिता व्याला व्याधयस्ते प्रकीर्तिताः। या सा नारी बृहत्काया अध्यतिष्ठत तत्र वै॥ तामाहुस्तु जरां प्राज्ञा रूपवर्णविनाशिनीम्। यस्तत्र कूपो नृपते स तु देहः शरीरिणाम्॥
en: Those described as beasts of prey are the diseases. The huge woman living in the forest, is identified by the wise with Decrepitude which destroys complexion and beauty. The pit is the body of embodied creatures.

sn: यस्तत्र वसतेऽधस्तान्महाहिः काल एव सः। अन्तकः सर्वभूतानां देहिनां सर्वहार्यसौ॥
en: The huge snake living in the bottom of that pit is Time, the destroyer of all embodied beings. It is, indeed, the universal destroyer.

sn: कूपमध्ये च या जाता वल्ली यत्र स मानवः। प्रताने लम्बते लग्नो जीविताशा शरीरिणाम्॥
en: The cluster of creepers growing in that pit and by whose spreading stems the man hangs down is the man hangs down is the desire for life which every creature entertains.

sn: स यस्तु कूपवीनाहे तं वृक्षं परिसर्पति। षड्वक्त्रः कुञ्जरो राजन् स तु संवत्वरः स्मृतः॥
en: The six-faxed elephant, O king, which runs towards the tree standing at the mouth of the pit is the year. Its six faces are the seasons and its twelve feet are the twelve months.

sn: मुखानि ऋतवो मासाः पादा द्वादश कीर्तिताः। ये तु वृक्षं निकृन्तन्ति मूषिकाः सततोत्थिताः॥ रात्र्यहानि तु तान्याहुर्भूतानां परिचिन्तकाः।
en: The rats and the snakes that are eating up the tree are the days and nights that are continually lessening the periods of life of all creatures. The bees are our desires.

sn: ये ते मधुकरास्तत्र कामास्ते परिकीर्तिताः॥ यास्तु ता बहुशो धाराः स्रवन्ति मधुनिस्रवम्। तांस्तु कामरसान् विद्याद् यत्र मन्जन्ति मानवाः॥
en: The numerous jets that are pouring honey are the pleasures derived from the gratification of our desires and to which men and strongly addicted.

sn: एवं संसारचक्रस्य परिवृत्तिं विदुर्बुधाः। येन संसारचक्रस्य पाशांश्छिन्दन्ति वै बुधाः॥
en: The wise know life's course to be such. Through that knowledge they succeed in snapping its fetters.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अहोऽभिहितमाख्यानं भवता तत्त्वदर्शिना। भूय एव तु मे हर्षः श्रुत्वा वागमृतं तव॥
en: Dhritarashtra said “Excellent is this parable which you have described. Indeed, you are acquainted with Truth. Having listened to your nectar-like speech, I desire to hear more.'

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: विदुर उवाच शृणु भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि मार्गस्यैतस्य विस्तरम्। यच्छ्रुत्वा विप्रमुच्यन्ते संसारेभ्यो विचक्षणाः॥
en: Vidura said “Listen to me, O king, I shall once more fully describe the means an acquaintances with which enables the wise to free themselves from the fetters of the world.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: यथा तु पुरुषो राजन् दीर्घमध्वानमास्थितः। क्वचित् क्वचिच्छ्रमाच्छ्रान्तः कुरुते वासमेव वा॥ एवं संसारपर्याये गर्भवासेषु भारत। कुर्वन्ति दुर्बुधा वासं मुच्यन्ते तत्र पण्डिताः॥
en: As a person, O king, who has to travel a long distance, is sometimes obliged to halt for being fatigued so, O Bharata, they that are of little understanding traveling along the long way of life, have to make frequent halts in the shape of repeated births. The wise are, however, freed from that obligation.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: तस्मादध्वानमेवैतमाहुः शास्त्रविदो जनाः। यत्तु संसारगहनं वनमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: Men well read in scriptures, describe for this life's course as a long way. The wise also describe life's way with all its difficulties as a forest.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: सोऽयं लोकसमावर्तो मानां भरतर्षभ। चराणां स्थावराणां च न गृध्येत् तत्र पण्डितः॥
en: Creatures, O Bharata-chief, whether mobile or immobile, have to repeatedly return to the world. The wise alone escape. or

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: शारीरा मानसाश्चैव मानां ये तु व्याधयः। प्रत्यक्षाश्च परोक्षाश्च ते व्यालाः कथिता बुधैः॥
en: The diseases, mental and physical, to which mortals are subject, whether visible invisible, are described as beasts of prey by the wise.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: क्लिश्यमानाश्च तैर्नित्यं वार्यमाणाश्च भारत। स्वकर्मभिर्महाव्यालै!द्विजन्त्यल्पबुद्धयः॥
en: Men are always assailed by them, O Bharata. Again, those dreadful beasts of prey, which are their own acts in life, never cause any, anxiety to the foolish.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: अथापि तैर्विमुच्येत व्याधिभिः पुरुषो नृप। आवृणोत्येव तं पश्चाजरा रूपविनाशिनी॥
en: If any person, O king, somehow escapes from diseases, Decrepitude, that destroyer of beauty, assails him after-wards.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: शब्दरूपरसस्पर्शेर्गन्धैश्च विविधैरपि। मज्जमांसमहापङ्के निरालम्बे समन्ततः॥
en: Plunged in a slough by the objects of senses, viz., sound, form, taste, touch and scent, man remains there without anything to save him from there.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: संवत्सराश्च मासाश्च पक्षाहोरात्रसंधयः। क्रमेणास्योपयुञ्जन्ति रूपमायुस्तथैव च॥
en: Meanwhile, the years, the seasons, the mouths, the fortnights, the days and the nights, coming one after another, gradually deprive him of beauty and lessen the period of life.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: एते कालस्य निधयो नैताञ्जानन्ति दुर्बुधाः। धात्राभिलिखितान्याहुः सर्वभूतानि कर्मणा॥
en: These all are harbingers of death. The foolish do not regard them as such. The wise say that all creatures are ruled by the Ordainer through their acts.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: रथः शरीरं भूतानां सत्त्वमाहुस्तु सारथिम्। इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुः कर्मबुद्धिस्तु रश्मयः॥
en: The body of a creature is called the car. The vital principle is the driver of that car. The senses are the horses. Our acts and the understanding are the traces.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: तेषां हयानां यो वेगं धावतामनुधावति। स तु संसारचक्रेऽस्मिश्चक्रवत् परिवर्तते॥
en: He who follows after those running horses, has to come repeatedly by rebirths.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: यस्तान् संयमते बुद्ध्या संयतो न निवर्तते। ये तु संसारचक्रेऽस्मिंश्चक्रवत् परिवर्तिते॥
en: He, however, who, being self-restrained, restrains them by his understanding, has not to return.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: भ्रममाणा न मुह्यन्ति संसारे न भ्रमन्ति ते। संसारे भ्रमतां राजन् दुःखमेतद्धि जायते॥
en: They, however, who are not stupefied while following this wheel of life that is revolving like a real wheel, do not come by re-births.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: तस्मादस्य निवृत्त्यर्थं यत्नमेवाचरेद् बुधः। उपेक्षा नात्र कर्तव्या शतशाखः प्रवर्धते॥
en: He that is wise should certainly prevent the coming of re-birth. One should not neglect it, for indifference may subject us to it repeatedly.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: यतेन्द्रियो नरो राजन् क्रोधलोभनिराकृतः। संतुष्टः सत्यवादी यः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति॥
en: The Man, O king, who has controlled his senses and subdued anger and covetousness, who is contented, and truthful in speech, obtains peace.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: याम्यमाहू रथं ह्येनं मुह्यन्ते येन दुर्बुधाः। स चैतत् प्राप्नुयाद् राजन् यत् त्वां प्राप्तो नराधिप।।१९
en: This body is called the car of Yama. The foolish are stupefied by it. Such a person, O king, should obtain that which you have obtained.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: अनुतर्षुलमेवैतद् दुःखं भवति मारिष। राज्यनाशं सुहन्नाशं सुतनाशं च भारत॥
en: The loss of kingdom of friends, and of children, O Bharata, and such other things, visit him who is still under the influence of desire.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
