sn: साधुः परमदुःखानां दुःखभैषज्यमाचरेत्। ज्ञानौषधमवाप्येह दूरपारं महौषधम्। छिन्द्याद् दुःखमहाव्याधि नरः संयतमानसः॥
en: The wise should apply the medicine of intelligence to all great sorrows. Securing the medicine of wisdom, which is truly very efficacious and is almost unattainable the selfcontrolled man would kill that serious disease called sorrow.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: न विक्रमो न चाप्यर्थो न मित्रं न सुहृज्जनः। तथोन्मोचयते दुःखाद् यथाऽऽत्मा स्थिरसंयमः॥ तस्मान्मैत्रं समास्थाय शीलमापद्य भारत।
en: Neither power, nor riches, nor friends, nor well-wishers, can cure a man of his grief so successfully as the control of self. Therefore not injuring others and cherishing friendship for all creatures, be of pious behaviour, O Bharata!

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: दमस्त्यागोऽप्रमादश्च ते त्रयो ब्रह्मणो हयाः॥ शीलरश्मिसमायुक्तः स्थितो यो मानसे रथे। त्यक्त्वा मृत्युभयं राजन् ब्रह्मलोकं स गच्छति॥
en: Self-restraint, renunciation, and carefulness, are the three horses of Brahman. He who rides on the car of his soul, to which are yoked these horses with the help of traces furnished by good conduct, and drives it, shaking off all fear of death, goes, O king, to the regions of Brahman.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो यो ददाति महीपते। स गच्छति परं स्थानं विष्णोः पदमनामयम्॥
en: That person, O king, who gives to all creatures promise of his harmlessness goes to the best of regions, vilz., the blessed one of Vishnu.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: न तत् ऋतुसहस्रेण नोपवासैश्च नित्यशः। अभयस्य च दानेन यत् फलं प्राप्नुयान्नरः॥
en: The fruit that one reaps by giving as assurance to all creatures of his harmlessness cannot be obtained by celebrating a thousand sacrifices or by daily fasts.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: न ह्यात्मनः प्रियतरं किंचिद् भूतेषु निश्चितम्। अनिष्टं सर्वभूतानां मरणं नाम भारत॥ तस्मात् सर्वेषु भूतेषु दया कार्या विपश्चिता।
en: Of all things there is certainly nothing dearer than self. Death is, forsooth, disliked by all creatures, O Bharata. Therefore, pity should certainly be shown to all.

description: How men can free themselves from the fetters of the world
sn: नानामोहसमायुक्ता बुद्धिजालेन संवृताः॥ असूक्ष्मदृष्ट्यो मन्दा भ्राम्यन्ते तत्र तत्र ह। सुसूक्ष्मदृष्ट्यो राजन् व्रजन्ति ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्॥
en: Possessed by various kinds of mistakes, entangled by the net of their own intelligence, they that are wicked and are of good vision, visit repeatedly this Earth. The wise secure a union with Brahma."

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विदुरस्य तु तद् वाक्यं निशम्य कुरुसत्तमः। पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तः पपात भुवि मूर्छितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said “After hearting the words of Vidura, the chief of the Kurus, stricken with grief on account of the death of his sons, dropped down senseless on the Earth.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: तं तथा पतितं भूमौ नि:संज्ञं प्रेक्ष्य बान्धवाः। कृष्णद्वैपायनश्चैव क्षत्ता व विदुरस्तथा॥ संजयः सुहृदश्चान्ये द्वा:स्था ये चास्य सम्मताः। जलेन सुखशीतेन तालवृन्तैश्च भारत॥ पस्पृशुश्च करैर्गानं वीजमानाश्च यत्नतः। अन्वासन् सुचिरं कालं धृतराष्ट्र तथागतम्॥
en: Seeing him fall down in that state, his friends as also the island-born Vyasa, Vidura, Sanjaya, and other well-wishers, and the trust worthy attendants who used to wait at the gates, sprinkled cool water over his body, and fanned him with palm leaves, and gently rubbed him with their hands. for a long while they solaced the king while in that state.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य लब्धसंज्ञो महीपतिः। विललाप चिरं कालं पुत्राधिभिरभिप्लुतः॥
en: Regaining his senses, after a long time the monarch, wept for a long time, overwhelmed with grief on account of the death of his sons.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: धिगस्तु खलु मानुष्यं मानुषेषु परिग्रहे। यतो मूलानि दुःखानि सम्भवन्ति मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: He said:-'Fie on the humanity. Fie out the human body. The miseries that we suffer in this life frequently originate from the very state of humanity.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: पुत्रनाशेऽर्थनाशे च ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिनामथ। प्राप्यते सुमहद् दुःखं विषाग्निप्रतिमं विभो॥
en: Alas, O lord great is the grief, like poison or fire, that one suffers at the loss of sons, of riches, of kinsmen, and relatives.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: येन दह्यन्ति गात्राणि येन प्रज्ञा विनश्यति। येनाभिभूतः पुरुषो मरणं बहु मन्यते॥
en: That grief cosumes our limbs, and wisdom. Stricken with that grief, a person welcomes death.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: तदिदं व्यसनं प्राप्तं मया भाग्यविपर्ययात्। तस्यान्तं नाधिगच्छामि ऋते प्राणविमोक्षणात्॥
en: This calamity that has be fallen me terminate with life itself. O best of sages, I shall, therefore, put an end to my life this very day.'

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: तथैवाहं करिष्यामि अद्यैव द्विजसत्तम। इत्युक्त्वा तु महात्मानं पितरं ब्रह्मवित्तमम्॥ धृतराष्ट्रोऽभवन्मूढः स शोकं परमं गतः। अभूच तूष्णीं राजासौ ध्यायमानो महीपते॥
en: Saying so to his great sire, that foremost of all persons conversant with Brahma, Dhritarashtra, laden with grief, became stupefied. The king, O monarch, thinking of his miseries, became silent.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा कृष्णद्वैपायनः प्रभुः। पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तं पुत्रं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing these words of his the powerful Vyasa thus spoke to his son stricken with grief on account of the death of his children.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: व्यास उवाच धृतराष्ट्रो महाबाहो यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु। श्रुतवानसि मेधावी धर्मार्थकुशलः प्रभो॥
en: Vyasa said O mighty-armed Dhritarashtra, hear what I say. You are learned, intelligent, and you O powerful, one, are skilled in understanding duties.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचिद् वेदितव्यं परंतप। अनित्यतां हि मानां विजानासि न संशयः॥
en: Everything is know to you. O scorcher of foes. Forsooth you know the instability of all things doomed to death.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: अध्रुवे जीवलोके च स्थाने वा शाश्वते सति। जीविते मरणान्ते च कस्माच्छोचसि भारत॥
en: When this life is fickle, when this word itself is not eternal, when life is sure to end in death, why then, O Bharata, do you grieve?

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: प्रत्यक्षं तव राजेन्द्र वैरस्यास्य समुद्भवः। पुत्रं ते कारणं कृत्वा कालयोगेन कारितः॥
en: Before your very eyes, O king, Time, making your son the cause, created this enmity.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: अवश्यं भवितव्ये च कुरूणां वैशसे नृप। कस्माच्छोचसि ताशूरान् गतान् परमिकां गतिम्।।
en: This destruction of the Kurus, O king, was inevitable. Why then do you grieve for those heroes that have achieved the highest end?

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: जानता च महाबाहो विदुरेण महात्मना। यतितं सर्वयत्नेन शमं प्रति जनेश्वर॥
en: The high-souled Vidura knew every thing. he had tried his best, О king, to bring about peace.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: न च दैवकृतो मार्गः शक्यो भूतेन केनचित्। घटतापि चिरं कालं नियन्तुमिति मे मतिः॥
en: I Think the course marked by destiny cannot be controlled by any one, even if one struggles for ever.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: देवतानां हि यत् कार्यं मया प्रत्यक्षतः श्रुतम्। तत् देऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा स्थैर्यं भवेत् तव॥
en: The course that was settled by the celestial was known to me direct. I will recite it to you, so that you may enjoy peace of mind.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: पुराहं त्वरितो यातः सभामैन्द्री जितकमः। अपश्यं तत्र च तदा समवेतान् दिवौकसः॥
en: Once before, I went very quickly to the court of Indra. There I all the inhabitation's of heaven assembled together.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: नारदप्रमुखाश्चापि सर्वे देवर्षयोऽनघ तत्र चापि मया हृष्टा पृथिवी पृथिवीपते॥
en: There were, O sinless one, all the celestial Rishis also, headed by Narada. There, O king, I saw also the Earth in her embodied form. saw

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: कार्यार्थमुपसम्प्राप्ता देवतानां समीपतः। उपगम्य तदा धात्री देवानाह समागतान्॥ यत् कार्यं मम युष्माभिर्ब्रह्मणः सदने तदा। प्रतिज्ञातं महाभागास्तच्छीघ्रं संविधीयताम्॥
en: The latter had gone to the gods for the accomplishment of a particular mission. Approaching the gods, she said,—While you were in Brahman's abode you promised to do all for me. Let that be accomplished soon.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा विष्णुर्लोकनमस्कृतः। उवाच वाक्यं प्रहसन् पृथिवी देवसंसदि॥ धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राणां यस्तु ज्येष्ठः शतस्य वै। दुर्योधन इति ख्यातः स ते कार्यं करिष्यति॥ तं च प्राप्य महीपालं कृतकृत्या भविष्यसि।
en: Hearing these words of hers, Vishnu, adored of all the worlds, smilingly addressed her in the midst of the celestials, saving,-The eldest of the hundred sons of Dhritarashtra, viz., Duryodhana, will accomplish your work. Through that king you object will be achieved.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: तस्यार्थे पृथिवीपाला: कुरुक्षेत्रं समागताः॥ अन्योन्यं घातयिष्यन्ति दृढैः शस्त्रैः प्रहारिणः।
en: For his sake, many kings assemble together on the field of Kuru, They will cause one another to be killed through hard weapons.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: ततस्ते भविता देवि भारस्य युधि नाशनम्॥ गच्छ शीघ्रं स्वकं स्थानं लोकान् धारय शोभने।
en: It is evident, O goddess, that your bruden will then he lightened in battle, Go quickly to your won station and continue to bear the the weight of creatures, O beautiful damsel.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: य एष ते सुतो राजन् लोकसंहारकारणात्॥ कलेरंशः समुत्पन्नो गान्धार्या जठरे नृप।
en: From this you should know, O king that your son Duryodhana, born in Gandhari's womb, was a portion of Kali born for bringing about a universal slaughter.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: अमर्षी चपलश्चापि क्रोधनो दुष्प्रसाधनः॥ दैवयोगात् समुत्पन्ना भ्रातरश्चास्य तादृशाः।
en: He was vindictive, restless, wrathful and difficult of being pleased. Through the influence of Destiny his brothers also took after him.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: शकुनिर्मातुलश्चैव कर्णश्च परमः सखा॥ समुत्पन्ना विनाशार्थं पृथिव्यां सहिता नृपाः।
en: Shakuni became his maternal uncle and Karna his great friend. Many other kings were born on Earth for helping him in the work of destruction.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: यादृशो जायते राजा तादृशोऽस्य जनो भवेत्॥ अधर्मो धर्मतां याति स्वामी चेद् धार्मिको भवेत्।
en: As the king is, so are his subjects. If the king becomes pious, even unrighteousness becomes incarnate in his kingdom.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: स्वामिनो गुणदोषाभ्यां भृत्याः स्युर्नात्र संशयः॥ दुष्टं राजानमासाद्य गतास्ते तनया नृप।
en: Servants, forsooth, are affected by the merits and demerits of their masters. O king, having obtained a bad king, your other sons have all been destroyed.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: एतमर्थं महाबाहो नारदो वेद तत्त्ववित्॥ आत्मापराधात् पुत्रास्ते विनष्टाः पृथिवीपते। मा ताशोचस्व राजेन्द्र न हि शोकेऽस्ति कारणम्।।३५
en: Conversant with truth, Narada knew all this. Through their own faults, your sons have been destroyed, O king! Do not grieve for them, O king. There in no cause for grief.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: न हि ते पाण्डवाः स्वल्पमपराध्यन्ति भारत। पुत्रास्तव दुरात्मानो यैरियं घातिता मही॥
en: The Pandavas are not to be blamed, O Bharata, in the least, for what has taken place. Your sons were all wicked. It is they that caused this destruction on Earth.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: नारदेन च भद्रं ते पूर्वमेव न संशयः। युधिष्ठिरस्य समितौ राजसूये निवेदितम्॥ पाण्डवाः कौरवाः सर्वे समासाद्य परस्परम्। न भविष्यन्ति कौन्तेय यत् ते कृत्यं तदाचर॥
en: Narada had truly spoken out to Yudhishthira, all this in his court at the time of the Rajasuya sacrifice, saying, "The Pandavas and the Kauravas, meeting which each other, will be destroyed. Do that, O son of Kunti, which you should.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा तदाशोचन्त पाण्डवाः। एवं ते सर्वमाख्यातं देवगुह्यं सनातनम्॥
en: Hearing these words of Narada, the Pandavas were filled with grief. I have thus communicated to you, an eternal secret of the celestials.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: कथं ते शोकनाश: स्यात् प्राणेषु च दया प्रभो। स्नेहश्च पाण्डुपुत्रेषु ज्ञात्वा दैवकृतं विधिम्॥
en: This will dispell your sorrow and restore to you a love of life, and make you love the Pandavas, for all that had taken place has been due to what had been preordained by the gods.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: एष चार्थो महाबाहो पूर्वमेव मया श्रुतः। कथितो धर्मराजस्य राजसूये ऋतूत्तमे॥
en: O you, of mighty-arms, I had learnt all this sometime before. I also spoke of it to king Yudhishthira the just at the time of the Rajasuya sacrifice.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: यतितं धर्मपुत्रेण मया गुह्ये निवेदिते। अविग्रहे कौरवाणां दैवं तु बलवत्तरम्॥
en: When I secretly informed him of all this, Dharma's son, tried his best for preserving peace with the Kauravas. That, however, which is ordained by the gods proved too strong for him too strong for his to defeat.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: अनतिक्रमणीयो हि विधि राजन् कथंचन। कृतान्तस्य तु भूतेन स्थावरेण चरेण च॥
en: The determination, O king, of the Destroyer, cannot be baffled any how by mobile and immobile creatures.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: भवान् धर्मपरो यत्र बुद्धिश्रेष्ठश्च भारत। मुह्यते प्राणिनां ज्ञात्वा गतिं चागतिमेव च॥
en: You are virtuous and highly intelligent, O Bharata! You know also that which all creatures should do and that which they should not do.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: त्वां तु शोकेन संतप्तं मुह्यमानं मुहुर्मुहुः। ज्ञात्वा युधिष्ठिरो राजा प्राणानपि परित्यजेत्॥
en: If king Yudhishthira leans that you are overwhelmed with grief and losing your senses frequently, he will put an end to his life.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: कृपालुनित्यशो वीरस्तिर्यग्योनिगतेष्वपि। स कथं त्वयि राजेन्द्र कृपां नैव करिष्यति॥
en: He is always compassionate and wise. His kindness is displayed even towards all the inferior creatures. How is it possible, O king, that he will not show compassion to you, O king.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: मम चैव नियोगेन विधेश्चाप्यनिवर्तनात्। पाण्डवानां च कारुण्यात् प्राणान् धारय भारत।॥
en: At my behest, and knowing that which is ordained is inevitable, as also out of love for the Pandavas, live, O Bharata!

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: एवं ते वर्तमानस्य लोके कीर्तिर्भविष्यति। धर्मार्थः सुमहांस्तात तप्तं स्याच तपश्चिरात्॥
en: If you live thus, you fame will travel all over the world. You will then acquire a knowledge of all duties and find many years for acquiring ascetic merit.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: पुत्रशोकं समुत्पन्नं हुताशं ज्वलितं यथा। प्रज्ञाम्भसा महाभाग निर्वापय सदा सदा॥
en: Thus grief consequent on the death of your sons that has arisen in your heart, like a blazing fire, should always be extinguished, O king, by the water of wisdom.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा तस्य वचनं व्यासस्यामिततेजसः। मुहूर्तं समनुध्यायन् धृतराष्ट्रोऽभ्यभाषत।॥ महता शोकजालेन प्रणुन्नोऽस्मि द्विजोत्तम। नात्मानमवबुध्यामि मुह्यमानो मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Hearing these words of the energetic Vyasa and reflecting upon them for a little while, Dhritarashtra said,-'O best of Rishis, I am greatly stricken with grief. I am repeatedly losing consciousness and I am unable to bear up my own self.

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: इदं तु वचनं श्रुत्वा तव देवनियोगजम्। धारयिष्याम्यहं प्राणान् घटिष्ये न तु शोचितुम्॥
en: Hearing, however, these your words about what had been ordained by the gods, I shall not think of putting an end to my life and shall live and act without indulging in grief.'

description: Dhritarashtra becomes senseless and bewails. The mission of Yudhishthira
sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं व्यासः सत्यवतीसुतः। धृतराष्ट्रस्य राजेन्द्र तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Hearing these words of Dhritarashtra, O king, Satyavati's son Vyasa, disappeared then and there. Hearing these words of Dhritarashtra, O king, Satyavati's son Vyasa, disappeared then and there.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: जनमेजय उवाच गते भगवति व्यासे धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः। किमचेष्टत विप्रर्षे तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Janamejaya said After the holy Vyasa had gone away, what, O Rishi, did king Dhritarashtra do? You should tell me this.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: तथैव कौरवो राजा धर्मपुत्रो महामनाः। कृपप्रभृतयश्चैव किमकुर्वत ते त्रयः॥
en: What also did the Kuru king, the great son of Dharma, do? And what did those three, viz., Kripa and others do?

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: अश्वत्थाम्नः श्रुतं कर्म शापश्चान्योन्यकारितः। वृत्तान्तमुत्तरं ब्रूहि यदभाषत संजयः॥
en: I have heard of the wonderful deeds of Ashvatthaman and the exchange of curses. Tell me what took place next, and what Sanjaya next said to the old king."

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच हते दुर्योधने चैव हते सैन्ये च सर्वशः। संजयो विगतप्रज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रमुपस्थितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said "After Duryodhana and all his soldiers had been killed, Sanjaya, deprived of spiritual sight, returned to Dhritarashtra.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: संजय उवाच आगम्य नानादेशेभ्यो नानाजनपदेश्वराः। पितृलोकं गता राजन् सर्वे तव सुतैः सह॥
en: Sanjaya said The kings of various races, that came from various kingdoms, have all, O king, gone to the abode of Death along with your sons.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: याच्यमानेन सततं तव पुत्रेण भारत। घातिता पृथिवी सर्वा वैरस्यान्तं विधित्सता॥
en: Your son, O king, who had constantly been requested (for peace) but who always desired to terminate his hostility after killing the Pandavas has caused the Earth exterminated.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: पुत्राणामथ पौत्राणां पितॄणां च महीपते। आनुपूर्येण सर्वेषां प्रेतकार्याणि कारय॥
en: Do you, O king, cause the obsequia rites of your sons and grandsons and fathers to be duly performed.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं घोरं संजयस्य महीपतिः। गतासुरिव निश्चेष्टो न्यपतत् पृथिवीतले॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these dreadful words of Sanjaya, the king dropped down on the Earth and lay unconscious like one deprived of life.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: तं शयानमुपागम्य पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपतिम्। विदुरः सर्वधर्मज्ञ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ उत्तिष्ठ राजन् किं शेषे मा शुचो भरतर्षभ। एषा वै सर्वसत्त्वानां लोकेश्वर परा गतिः॥
en: Approaching the king, who was lying prostrate on the Earth, Vidura, conversant with all forms of duty, said: 'Rise, O king, why do you lie down thus? Do not grieve, O foremost of Bharata's! This O king, is the final end of all creatures.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: अभावादीनि भूतानि भावमध्यानि भारत। अभावनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: In the beginning creatures are non-existent. In the middle, O Bharata, they become existent. At the end, they once more become non-existent. What is there to be sorry for in all this.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: न शोचन् मृतमन्वेति न शोचन म्रियते नरः। एवं सांसिद्धिके लोके किमर्थमनुशोचसि॥
en: By grieving one cannot get back the dead. By indulging in grief, one cannot die himself. When such is the course of the world, why do you grieve?

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: अयुध्यमानो म्रियते युद्धयमानस्तु जीवति। कालं प्राप्य महाराज न कश्चिदतिवर्तते॥
en: One may die without fighting in battle. One also escapes alive after having engaged in battle. When one's appointed Time comes, O king, he cannot escape.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: कालः कर्षति भूतानि सर्वाणि विविधानि च। न कालस्य प्रियः कश्चिन्न द्वेष्यः कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Time drags all creatures. There is none dear or loathsome to Time, O Kuru's chief.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: यथा वायुस्तृणाग्राणि संवर्तयति सर्वतः। तथा कालवशं यान्ति भूतानि भरतर्षभ॥
en: As the wind tears off the ends of all blades of grass, so all creatures, O Bharata chief, are subjected by Time under its influence.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: एकसार्थप्रयातानां सर्वेषां तत्र गामिनाम्। यस्य कालः प्रयात्यग्रे तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: All creatures are like members of the same caravan bound for one destination. What is there to be sorry for if Time meets with one a little earlier than with another.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: यांश्चापि निहतान् युद्धे राजंस्त्वमनुशोचसि। न शोच्या हि महात्मानः सर्वे ते त्रिदिवं गताः॥
en: Those again, O king, that have fallen in battle and for whom you bewail, are not really objects of your grief, since all those illustrious persons to heaven.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: न यज्ञैर्दक्षिणावद्भिर्न तपोभिर्न विद्यया। तथा स्वर्गमुपायान्ति यथा शूरास्तनुत्यजः॥
en: By celebrating sacrifices with enough presents, by practising ascetic austerities, and by knowledge, people cannot so easily go to heaven as heroes by displaying courage in battle.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: सर्वे वेदविदः शूराः सर्वे सुचरितव्रताः। सर्वे चाभिमुखाः क्षीणास्तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: All those heroes were conversant with the Vedas; all of them were observant of vows: all of them have died, fighting the foe in battle. What is there to be sorry for then.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: शरीराग्निषु शूराणां जुहुवुस्ते शराहुतीः। हूयमानाशरांश्चैव सेहुरुत्तमपूरुषाः॥
en: have gone They poured their libations of arrows upon the bodies of their brave enemies as upon a fire. Great as they were, they bore in return the libations of arrows poured upon themselves.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: एवं राजंस्तवाचक्षे स्वयं पन्थानमुत्तमम्। न युद्धादधिकं किंचित् क्षत्रियस्येह विद्यते॥
en: I tell you. O king, that these is no superior way to heaven for a Kshatriya to one thought battle.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: क्षत्रियास्ते महात्मानः शूराः समितिशोभनाः। आशिषं परमां प्राप्ता न शोच्याः सर्व एव हि॥
en: All of them were great Kshatriya, all of them were heroes and ornaments of assemblies. They have attained to a highly blessed state. One should not grieve for them.

description: Sanjalya's return and consolation to the blind king
sn: आत्मनाऽऽत्मानमाश्वास्य मा शुचः पुरुषर्षभ। नाद्य शोकाभिभूतस्त्वं कार्यमुत्स्रष्टुमर्हसि।॥
en: Do you comfort your oneself. Do not grieve, O foremost of men. You should not allow yourself to be overwhelmed with so row and give up all work.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विदुरस्य तु तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा तु पुरुषर्षभः। युज्यतां यानमित्युक्त्वा पुनर्वचनमब्रवीत्॥ शीघ्रमानय गान्धारीं सर्वाश्च भरतस्त्रियः। वधूं कुन्तीमुपादाय याश्चान्यास्तत्र योषितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Hearing these words of Vidura, that foremost of Bharata's race, viz., Dhritarashtra, ordered for his car. The king once more said,—'Bring Gandhari here forthwith, and all the Bharata ladies. Bring here Kunti also, as well as all the other ladies with her.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: एवमुक्त्वा स धर्मात्मा विदुरं धर्मवित्तमम्। शोकविप्रहतज्ञानो यानमेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: Having said these words to Vidura conversant with every duty, the pious on Dhritarashtra, deprived of his senses by sorrow got on his car.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: गान्धारी पुत्रशोकार्ता भर्तुर्वचननोदिता। सह कुन्त्या यतो राजा सह स्त्रीभिरुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Then Gandhari, stricken stricken with grief consequent the death of his sons, accompanied by Kunti and the other ladies of the royal household, came, as ordered by her lord, where the latter was waiting for her.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: ताः समासाद्य राजानं भृशं शोकसमन्विताः। आमन्त्र्यान्योन्यमीयुः स्म भृशमुच्चुक्रुशुस्ततः॥
en: Stricken with great grief, they came together to the king. As they met, they addressed each other and cried aloud.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: ताः समाश्वासयत् क्षत्ता ताभ्यश्चार्ततरः स्वयम्। अश्रुकण्ठी: समारोप्य ततोऽसौ निर्ययौ पुरात्॥
en: Then Vidura, who had become more afflicted than those ladies, began to solace them. Placing those weeping ladies on the cars that stood ready for them, he left the city.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: ततः प्रणादः संजज्ञे सर्वेषु कुरुवेश्मसु। आकुमारं पुरं सर्वमभवच्छोककर्षितम्॥
en: At that time a loud cry of sorrow arose from every Kuru house. The whole city, including the very children, were stricken with grief.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: अदृष्टपूर्वा या नार्यः पुरा देवगणैरपि। पृथग्जनेन दृश्यन्ते तास्तदा निहतेश्वराः॥
en: Those ladies who had not before this been seen by the very celestials were now helpless as they were in the absence of their lords, seen by the common people.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: प्रकीर्य केशान् सुशुभान् भूषणान्यवमुच्य च। एकवस्त्रधरा नार्यः परिपेतुरनाथवत्॥
en: With their beautiful dishevelled hairs, and their ornaments thrown off, those ladies, each clad in a single piece of cloth, proceeded most sorrowfully.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: श्वेतपर्वतरूपेभ्यो गृहेभ्यस्तास्त्वपाक्रमन्। गुहाभ्य इव शैलानां पृषत्यो हतयूथपाः॥
en: Indeed, they came out of their houses looking like white mountains, like a herd of deer from their mountain caves after the fall of their leader.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: तान्युदीर्णानि नारीणां तदा वृन्दान्यनेकशः। शोकार्तान्यद्रवन् राजन् किशोरीणामिवाङ्गने॥
en: Those bevies of fair damsels, O king, came out filled with sorrow, and ran here and here like a herd of fillies on a circus yard.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: प्रगृह्य बाहून् क्रोशन्त्यः पुत्रान् भ्रातॄन् पितॄनपि। दर्शयन्तीव ता ह स्म युगान्ते लोकसंक्षयम्॥
en: Seizing each other's hands, they began to bewail aloud after their sons, brothers, and fathers. The presented a spectacle that takes place on the occasion of the universal destruction at the end of a cycle.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: विलपन्त्यो रुदत्यश्च धावमानास्ततस्ततः। शोकेनोपहतज्ञानाः कर्तव्यं न प्रजज्ञिरे॥
en: Weeping and crying and running here and there, deprived of their senses by sorrow, they knew not what to do.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: व्रीडां जग्मुः पुरा याः स्म सखीनामपि योषितः। ता एकवस्त्रा निर्लज्जाः श्वश्रूणां पुरतोऽभवन्॥
en: Those ladies who formerly felt abashed even in the presence of companions of their own sex, now felt no shame, though scantily clad, in coming out before their mothers-in-law.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: परस्परं सुसूक्ष्मेषु शोकेष्वाश्वासयंस्तदा। ताः शोकविह्वला राजन्नवैक्षन्त परस्परम्॥
en: Formerly they used to console each other while stricken with even slightest grief, Stupefied by grief, they, O king, could not look upon each other.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: ताभिः परिवृतो राजा रुदतीभिः सहस्रशः। निर्ययौ नगराद् दीनस्तूर्णमायोधनं प्रति॥
en: Surrounded by those thousands of wailing ladies, the king issued out of the city in great depression and proceeded quickly towards the battle-field.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: शिल्पिनो वणिजो वैश्याः सर्वकर्मोपजीविनः। ते पार्थिवं पुरस्कृत्य निर्ययुर्नगराद् बहिः॥
en: Issuing out of the city, artisans and traders and Vaishyas and all kinds of mechanics, followed the king.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: तासां विक्रोशमानानामार्तानां कुरुसंक्षये। प्रादुरासीन्महाशब्दो व्यथयन् भुवनान्युत॥
en: As those ladies, afflicted by the entire destruction of Kurus, cried in sorrow, a loud wail arose from among them that pierced all the words.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: युगान्तकाले सम्प्राप्ते भूतानां दह्यतामिव। अभावः स्यादयं प्राप्त इति भूतानि मेनिरे॥
en: All creatures that heard that cry thought that the hour of universal destruction was near at hand when all things would be devoured by the fire that arises at the end of the cycle.

description: The lamentation of Kuru ladies and of the inhabitants of Hastinapura
sn: भृशमुद्विग्नमनसस्ते पौराः कुरुसंक्षये। प्राक्रोशन्त महाराज स्वनुरक्तास्तदा भृशम्॥
en: The citizens also of Hastinapura devoted to the Kurus, whit hearts filled with anxiety at the destruction of their rulers, O king, cried aloud like those ladies.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच क्रोशमात्रं ततो गत्वा ददृशुस्तान् महारथान्। शारद्वतं कृपं द्रौणिं कृतवर्माणमेव च॥
en: Vaishampayana said “Within two miles after his departure Dhritarashtra, met with those three great carwarriors, viz., Sharadvat's son Kripa, Drona's son (Ashvatthaman), and Kritavarman.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: ते तु दृष्ट्वैव राजानं प्रज्ञाचक्षुषमीश्वरम्। अश्रुकण्ठा विनिःश्वस्य रुदन्तमिदमब्रुवन्॥ पुत्रस्तव महाराज कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। गतः सानुचरो राजशक्रलोकं महीपते॥
en: As soon as the latter saw the blind king, possessed of great power, the three heroes sighed in grief and with voices choked in tears weepingly said,-'Your royal son, O king, having performed the most difficult feats, has, with all his followers, gone to the region of Indra.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: दुर्योधनबलान्मुक्ता वयमेव त्रयो रथाः। सर्वमन्यत् परिक्षीणं सैन्यं ते भरतर्षभ॥
en: We are the only three car-warriors of Duryodhana's army that are yet alive. All the others, O foremost of Bharata's race, have died.'

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: इत्येवमुक्तवा राजानं कृपः शारद्वतस्ततः। गान्धारी पुत्रशोकार्तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ अभीता युद्ध्यमानास्ते जन्तः शत्रुगणान् बहून्। वीरकर्माणि कुर्वाणाः पुत्रास्ते निधनं गताः॥
en: Having said these words to the king, Sharadvat's son Kripa, addressing the griefstricken Gandhari, said to her,-'Your sons have fallen, performing heroic and wonderful deeds, in the battle-field.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: ध्रुवं सम्प्राप्य लोकांस्ते निर्मलाशस्त्रनिर्जितान्। भास्वरं देहमास्थाय विहरन्त्यमरा इव॥
en: Forsooth having, obtained those bright worlds that are attainable only by the use of weapons, they are playing there like celestials, having assumed shinning forms.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: न हि कश्चिद्वि शूराणां युद्ध्यमानः पराङ्मुखः। शस्त्रेण निधनं प्राप्तो न च कश्चित् कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: Amongst those heroes there was no one that fled from battle-field. Every one of them has fallen at the end of weapons. None of them joined his hands, and prayed for mercy.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: एवं तां क्षत्रियस्याहुः पुराणाः परमां गतिम्। शस्त्रेण निधनं संख्ये तत्र शोचितुमर्हसि॥
en: Death in battle by weapons has been described by the ancients as the best that a Kshatriya can obtain. You should not, therefore, grieve for any of them.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: न चापि शत्रवस्तेषामृद्ध्यन्ते राज्ञि पाण्डवाः। शृणु यत् कृतमस्माभिरश्वत्थामपुरोगमैः॥
en: Their enemies, O queen viz., the Pandavas, too, have not been more fortunate. Hear, what we, headed by Ashvatthaman, have done to them.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: अधर्मेण हतं श्रुत्वा भीमसेनेन ते सुतम्। सुप्तं शिविरमासाद्य पाण्डूनां कदनं कृतम्॥ ते
en: Learning that your son had been killed unrighteously by Bhima, we massacred the Pandavas when asleep after entering these camp.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: पञ्चाला निहताः सर्वे धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः। द्रुपदस्यात्मजाश्चैव द्रौपदेयाश्च पातिताः॥
en: All the Panchalas have been killed. Indeed, all the sons of Drupada, as also all the son of Draupadi, have been massacred.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: तथा विशसनं कृत्वा पुत्रशत्रुगणस्य ते। प्राद्रवाम रणे स्थातुं न हि शक्यामहे त्रयः॥
en: Having caused this massacre of the sons of our foes, we are flying away because we three cannot fight with them.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: ते हि शूरा महेष्वासाः क्षिप्रमेष्यन्ति पाण्डवाः। अमर्षवशमापन्ना वैरं प्रतिजिहीर्षवः॥
en: Our enemies, the Pandavas, are all heroes and great bowmen. They will soon attack us, filled with rage, for taking vengeance on us.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: हतानात्मजाञ्श्रुत्वाप्रमत्ताः पुरुषर्षभाः। निरीक्षन्तः पदं शूराः क्षिप्रमेव यशस्विनि॥
en: Informed of the massacre of their sons, those foremost infuriate with rage, those heroes,-Oillustrious lady, will soon pursue us.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: तेषां तु कदनं कदनं कृत्वा संस्थातुं नोत्सहामहे। अनुजानीहि नो राज्ञि मा च शोके मनः कृथाः॥
en: Having caused this massacre we dare not stay. Grant us permission, O queen. You should not grievc.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: राजंस्त्वमनुजानीहि धैर्यमातिष्ठ चोत्तमम्। दिष्टान्तं पश्य चापि त्वं क्षात्रं धर्मं च केवलम्॥
en: Grant us your permission also, O king! Summon fortitude, and observe the duties of a Kshatriya in their highest form.'

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा राजानं कृत्वा चाभिप्रदक्षिणम्। कृपश्च कृतवर्मा च द्रोणपुत्रश्च भारत॥ अवेक्षमाणा राजानं धृतराष्ट्रं मनीषिणम्। गङ्गामनु महाराज तूर्णमश्वानचोदयन्॥
en: Having said so to the king, and going round him, Kripa and Kritavarat man and Drona's son, O Bharata, without being able to take of men, son away their eyes from the wise king Dhritarashtra, urged their horses towards the banks of the Ganges.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: अपक्रम्य तु ते राजन् सर्व एव महारथाः। आमन्त्र्यान्योन्यमुद्विग्नास्त्रिधा ते प्रययुस्तदा॥
en: Leaving thàt place, O king those great carwarriors, with hearts stricken with anxiety, took one another's leave and separated from one another.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: जगाम हास्तिनपुरं कृपः शारद्वतस्तदा। स्वमेव राष्ट्रं हार्दिक्यो द्रौणिर्व्यासाश्रमं ययौ॥
en: Sharadvat's Kripa went to Hastinapura; Hridika's son went to his own kingdom; while the son of Drona started for the hermitage of Vyasa.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: एवं ते प्रययुर्वीरा वीक्षमाणाः परस्परम्। भयार्ताः पाण्डुपुत्राणामागस्कृत्वा महात्मनाम्॥
en: Thus those heroes, who had offended the great sons of Pandu, respectively proceeded to the places they selected, on one another.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: समेत्य वीरा राजानं तदा त्वनुदिते रवौ। विप्रजग्मुर्महात्माो यथेच्छकमरिदमाः॥
en: Having met the king thus, those heroes, went away before the sunrise, O king, to the places they selected.

description: Meeting between Dhritarashtra and Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. How the latter have killed the Pandava army
sn: समासाद्याथ वै द्रौणिं पाण्डुपुत्रा महारथाः। व्यजयंस्ते रणे राजन् विक्रम्य तदनन्तरम्॥
en: It was after this, O king, that the sons of Pandu, those great car-warriors, met the son of Drona, and displaying their prowess, defeated him, O king."

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच हतेषु सर्वसैन्येषु धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। शुश्रुवे पितरं वृद्धं निर्यान्तं गजसाह्वयात्॥
en: Vaishampayana said "After all the warriors had been massacred, king Yudhishthira heard that his uncle Dhritarashtra had left the city of Hastinapura.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: सोऽभ्ययात् पुत्रशोकार्तः पुत्रशोकपरिप्लुतम्। शोचमानं महाराज भ्रातृभिः सहितस्तदा॥
en: Afflicted with grief consequent on the death of his sons, Yudhishthira, O king, accompanied by his brothers, set out for meeting his uncle who was filled with sorrow for the death of his (hundred) sons.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: अन्वीयमानो वीरेण दाशार्हेण महात्मना। युयुधानेन च तथा तथैव च युयुत्सुना॥
en: The son of Kunti was followed by the great and heroic Krishna of Dasharha's race, by Yuyudhana, as also by Yuyutsu.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: तमन्वगात् सुदुःखार्ता द्रौपदी शोककर्शिता। सह पाञ्चालयोषिद्भिर्यास्तत्रासन् समागताः॥
en: The princess Draupadi also, laden with grief, and accompanied by those Panchala ladies that were with her, sorrowfully followed her husband.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: स गङ्गामनु वृन्दानि स्त्रीणां भरतसत्तम। कुररीणामिवार्तानां क्रोशन्तीनां ददर्श ह॥
en: Yudhishthira saw near the banks of the Ganges, O king, the crowd of Bharata ladies afflicted with sorrow and crying like a light of she-ospreys.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: ताभिः परिवृतो राजा क्रोशन्तीभिः सहस्रशः। ऊर्ध्वबाहुभिरार्ताभी रुदतीभिः प्रियाप्रियैः॥
en: The king was soon surrounded by those thousands of ladies who with arms raised up in grief, were bewailing aloud and uttering all sorts of words, agreeable and disagreeable.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: व नु धर्मज्ञता राज्ञः क्व नु साद्यानृशंसता। यचावधीत् पितॄन् भ्रातॄन् गुरुपुत्रान् सखीनपि।॥
en: Where, indeed, in that righteousness of the king, where his truth and pity, since he has killed sires and brothers and preceptors and sons and friends.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: घातयित्वा कथं द्रोणं भीष्मं चापि पितामहम्। मनस्तेऽभून्महाबाहो हत्वा चापि जयद्रथम्॥
en: How, O mighty-armed one, had your heart become tranquil after killing Drona, and your grandsire Bhishma, and Jayadratha.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: किं नु राज्येन ते कार्यं पितॄन् भ्रातृनपश्यतः। अभिमन्युं च दुर्धर्षं द्रौपदेयांश्च भारत॥
en: What is the use of sovereignty to you, after have your seen your sires and brothers, O Bharata, and the irresistible Abhimanyu and the sons of Draupadi, thus killed.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: अतीत्य ता महाबाहुः क्रोशन्तीः कुररीरिव। ववन्दे पितरं ज्येष्ठं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Leaving those ladies crying like a fight of she-ospreys, the mighty-armed king Yudhishthira the just bowed to the feet of his eldest uncle.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: ततोऽभिवाद्य पितरं धर्मेणामित्रकर्षणाः। न्यवेदयन्त नामानि पाण्डवास्तेऽपि सर्वशः॥
en: Having saluted their sire duly, those slayer of foes, viz., the Pandavas, announced themselves to him, each uttering his own name.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: तमात्मजान्तकरणं पिता पुत्रवधार्दितः। अप्रीयमाणाः शोकातः पाण्डवं परिषस्वजे॥
en: Greatly stricken with grief for the slaughter of his sons, Dhritarashtra unwillingly embraced the eldest son of Pandu, who was the cause of that slaughter.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: धर्मराजं परिष्वज्य सान्त्वयित्वा च भारत। दुष्टात्मा भीममन्वैच्छद् दिधक्षुरिव पावकः॥
en: Having embraced Yudhishthira and spoken a few solacing words to him, O Bharata, the wicked Dhritarashtra sought for Bhima, like a burning fire ready to burn everything that would approach it.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: स कोपपावकस्तस्य शोकवायुसमीरितः। भीमसेनमयं दावं दिधक्षुरिव दृश्यते॥
en: Indeed, the fire of his anger, fanned by the wind of his grief, seemed then to be ready to consume the Bhima-forest.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: तस्य संकल्पमाज्ञाय भीमं प्रत्यशुभं हरिः। भीममाक्षिप्य पाणिभ्यां प्रददौ भीममायसम्॥
en: Understanding the wicked intentions towards Bhima, Krishna, dragging away the real Bhima, prusented an iron statue of the second son of Pandu to the old king.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: प्रागेव तु महाबुद्धिर्बुद्ध्वा तस्येङ्गितं हरिः। संविधानं महाप्राज्ञस्तत्र चक्रे जनार्दनः॥
en: The highly intelligent, Krishna had, in the very beginning understood the object of Dhritarashtra, and had, therefore, kept such a contrivance ready for baffling them.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: तं गृहीत्वैव पाणिभ्यां भीमसेनमयस्मयम्। बभञ्ज बलवान् राजा मन्यमानो वृकोदरम्॥
en: Holding with his two arms that iron Bhima, the power king Dhritarashtra, endued with great strength, broke it into pieces, taking it for the real Bhima.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: नागायुतबलप्राणः स राजा भीममायसम्। भक्त्वा विमथितोरस्कः सुनाव रुधिरं मुखात्॥
en: Possessed of the strength of ten thousands elephants, the king broke that statue into pieces. His own breast, however, was considerably bruised and he began to vomit blood.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: ततः पपात मेदिन्यां तथैव रुधिरोक्षितः। प्रपुष्पिताग्रशिखरः पारिजात इव दुमः॥
en: Covered with blood the king dropped down on the ground like a blossoming Parijata tree.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: प्रत्यगृह्णाच तं विद्वान् सूतो गावल्गणिस्तदा। मैवमित्यब्रवीच्चैनं शमयन् सान्त्वयन्निव॥
en: His learned charioteer, Sanjaya the son of Gavalgana raised the king and soothing and comforting him, said'Do not act so.'

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: स तु कोपं समुत्सृज्य गतमन्युर्महामनाः। हा हा भीमेति चुक्रोश नृपः शोकसमन्वितः॥
en: Having cast off his wrath and regained his true nature the king then became filled with grief and began to weep aloud, saying, 'Alas, Oh Bhima, Alas, Oh Bhima!'

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: तं विदित्वा गतक्रोधं भीमसेनवधार्दितम्। वासुदेवो वरः पुंसामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ मा शुचो धृतराष्ट्रं त्वं नैष भीमस्त्वया हतः। आयसी प्रतिमा ह्येषा त्वया निष्पातिता विभो॥
en: Knowing that he was no longer under the influence of anger, and that he was truly sorry for having (as he believed) slain Bhima, Vasudeva, that foremost of men, said,-'Do not grieve, O Dhritarashtra, for you have not killed Bhimasena. That is an iron statue, O king, whica has been broken by you.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: त्वां क्रोधवशमापन्नं विदित्वा भरतर्षभ। मयापकृष्टः कौन्तेयो मृत्योर्दष्ट्रान्तरं गतः॥
en: Knowing that you were filled with anger, O foremost of Bharata's race, I dragged Bhima away from within the jaws of Death.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: न हि ते राजशार्दूल बले तुल्योऽस्ति कश्चन। कः सहेत महाबाहो बाह्वेर्विग्रहणं नरः॥
en: O best of kings, there is none equal to you in physical strength. Who is there, O mightyarmed one, that would bear pressure of your arms.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: यथान्तकमनुप्राप्य जीवन् कश्चिन्न मुच्यते। एवं बाह्वन्तरं प्राप्य तव जीवेन कश्चन॥
en: As no one can escape alive from a struggle with Death himself, so no body can come out safe from within your embrace.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: तस्मात्पुत्रेण या तेऽसौ प्रतिमा कारिताऽऽयसी। भीमस्य सेयं कौरव्य तवैवोपहता मया।॥
en: Therefore that iron statue of Bhima, which had been made by your son, had been kept ready for you.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तं धर्मादपकृतं मनः। तव राजेन्द्र तेव त्वं भीमसेनं जिघांससि॥
en: On account of the sorrow for the death of your sons, your mind has been filled with spite. Therefore, O great king, you seek kill Bhimasena.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: न त्वेतत् ते क्षमं राजन् हन्यास्त्वं यद् वृकोदरम्। न हि पुत्रा महाराज जीवेयुस्ते कथंचन॥
en: The destruction of Bhima, however, O king, would do you no good. Your sons, O king, would not be revived by it.

description: The Pandavas appear before Dhritarashtra who embraces an iron image of Bhima for killing him
sn: तस्माद् यत् कृतमस्माभिर्मन्यमानैः शमं प्रति। अनुमन्यस्व तत् सर्वं मा च शोके मनः कृथाः॥
en: Therefore, approve of what we have done to secure peace, and do not grieve any longer."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत एनमुपातिष्ठशाचार्थं परिचारकाः। कृतशौचं पुनश्चैनं प्रोवाच मधुसूदनः॥ राजन्नधीता वेदास्ते शास्त्राणि विविधानि च। श्रुतानि च पुराणानि राजधर्माश्च केवला:॥
en: Vaishampayana said "Thereupon a few maid-servants came to the king for washing him. After he had been properly washed, Krishna again addressed him, saying. You are, O king, well read in the Vedas and various scriptures. You have heard all old histories, and everything relating to the duties of kings.

sn: एवं विद्वान् महाप्राज्ञः समर्थः सन् बलाबले। आत्मापराधात् कस्मात् त्वं कुरुषे कोपमीदृशम्॥
en: You are learned wise and can understand strength and weakness. Why are you then angry when all that has befallen you is the outcome of your own folly.

sn: उक्तवांस्त्वां तदैवाहं भीष्मद्रोणौ च भारत। विदुरः संजयश्चैव वाक्यं राजन् न तत् कृथाः॥
en: I spoke this to you before the battle. Both Bhishma and Drona, O Bharata, did the same, as also Vidura and Sanjaya. You did not, however, then care to follow our advice.

sn: स वार्यमाणो नास्माकमकार्षीर्वचनं तदा। पाण्डवानधिकाञ्जानन् बले शौर्ये च कौरव॥
en: Although requested by us, you did not act according to the advice we offered, knowing that the Pandavas were superior to you and yours, O Kuru chief in strength and bravery!

sn: राजा हि यः स्थिरप्रज्ञः स्वयं दोषानवेक्षते। देशकालविभागं च परं श्रेयः स विन्दति॥
en: The king who sees his own shortcomings and knows the distinctions of place and time, enjoys great prosperity.

sn: उच्यमानस्तु यः श्रेयो गृहीते नो हिताहिते। आपदः समनुप्राप्य स शोचत्यनये स्थितः॥
en: That man, however, who, though advised by his well-wishers, does not follow their words, suffers miseries and is obliged to grieve for his evil policy.

sn: ततोऽन्यवृत्तमात्मानं समवेक्षस्व भारत। राजंस्त्वं ह्यविधेपात्मा दुर्योधनवशे स्थितः॥
en: Follow a different course of life now, O Bharata! You did not control yourself but suffered yourself to be ruled by Duryodhana.

sn: आत्मापराधादापन्नस्तत् किं भीमं जिघांससि। तस्मात् संयच्छ कोपं त्वं स्वमनुस्मर दुष्कृतम्॥
en: That which has befallen you is due to your own fault. Why then do you seek to kill Bhima? Remembering your own folly govern your anger now.

sn: यस्तु तां स्पर्धया क्षुद्रः पाञ्चालीमानयत् सभाम्। स हतो भीमसेनेन वैरं प्रतिजिहीर्षता॥
en: That mean wretch who had, from haughtiness caused the princess of Panchala to be brought into the court, has been justly killed by Bhimasena.

sn: आत्मनोऽतिक्रमं पश्य पुत्रस्य च दुरात्मनः। यदनागसि पाण्डूनां परित्यागस्त्वया कृतः॥
en: Look at your own evil deeds as also at those of your wicked-souled son. The sons of Pandu are perfectly innocent. Yet they have been treated most ruthlessly by you and him.“

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः स कृष्णेन सर्वं नित्यं जनाधिप। उवाच देवकीपुत्रं धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः॥ एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि माधव। पुत्रस्नेहस्तु बलवान् धैर्यान्मां समचालयत्॥
en: After he had thus been told the truth by Krishna, O king, Dhritarashtra replied to Devaki's son, saying. 'It is just so, O you of mighty arms! What you say, O Madhava, is perfectly truth! It is father's affection that made me deviate from the path of righteousness.

sn: दिष्ट्या तु पुरुषव्याघ्रो बलवान् सत्यविक्रमः। त्वद्गुप्तो नागमत् कृष्ण भीमो बाह्वन्तरं मम॥
en: By good luck, that foremost of men, the mighty Bhima of true prowess, protected by you, came not within my embrace.

sn: इदानीं त्वहमव्यग्रो गतमन्युर्गतज्वरः। मध्यमं पाण्डवं वीरं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि माधव॥
en: Now, I am free from wrath and fever. I wish eagerly, O Madhava to embrace that hero.

sn: हतेषु पार्थिवेन्द्रेषु पुत्रेषु निहतेषु च। पाण्डुपुत्रेषु वै शर्म प्रीतिश्चाप्यवतिष्ठते॥
en: When all the kings have been killed when by children are no more, my well-being and happiness depend upon the sons of Pandu.

sn: ततः स भीमं च धनंजयं च मायाश्च पुत्रौ पुरुषप्रवीरौ। पस्पर्श गात्रैः प्ररुदन् सुगात्रानाश्वास्य कल्याणमुवाच चैतान्॥
en: Having said so, the old king them embraced those beautiful princes, viz., Bhima and Dhananjaya and those tow foremost of men, viz., the two sons of Madri and wept, and comforted and blessed them.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धृतराष्ट्राभ्यनुज्ञातास्ततस्ते कुरुपाण्डवाः। अभ्ययुर्धातरः सर्वे गान्धारी सह केशवाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Ordered by Dhritarashtra, those foremost of Kuru's race, viz., the Pandava brothers, accompanied by Keshava, then went to see Gandhari.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: ततो ज्ञात्वा हतामित्रं युधिष्ठिरमुपागतम्। गान्धारी पुत्रशोकार्ता शप्तुमैच्छदनिन्दिता॥
en: The innocent Gandhari, stricken with grief on üccount of the death of her hundred sons, thought that king Yudhishthira the just had killed all his enemies, and wished to curse him.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: तस्याः पापमभिप्रायं विदित्वा पाण्डवान् प्रति। ऋषिः सत्यवतीपुत्रः प्रागेव समबुध्यत॥
en: Knowing her evil intentions towards the Pandavas, the Vyasa made himself ready for counteracting them at the very beginning.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: स गङ्गायामुपस्पृश्य पुण्यगन्धि पयः शुचि। तं देशमुपसम्पेदे परमर्षिर्मनोजवः॥
en: Having cleansed himself by the sacred and fresh water of the Ganges, the Great Rishi, capable going everywhere at will as quickly as the mind, came there.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: दिव्येन चक्षुषा पश्यन् मनसा तद्गतेन च। सर्वप्राणभृतां भावं स तत्र समबुध्यत॥
en: Capable of seeing the heart of everyone with his spiritual vision and desirous of doing the same, the sage came there.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: स स्नुषामब्रवीत् काले कल्यवादी महातपाः। शापकालमवाक्षिप्य शमकालमुदीरयन्॥
en: Endued with great ascetic merit and ever intent on saying what was for the good of creatures, the Rishi said to his daughter-in-law at the proper moment. Do not at this time imprecate a curse! Rather make a good use of this hour for showing your forgiveness.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: न कोपः पाण्डवे कार्यो गान्धारि शमभाप्नुहि! वचो निगृह्यतामेतच्छृणु चेदं वचो मम॥
en: Thou should not be angry with the Pandavas, O Gandhari! Set your heart on peace! Restrain the words that are about to drop from your lips! Listen to my advice.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: उक्तास्यष्टादशाहानि पुत्रेण जयमिच्छता। शिवमाशास्व मे मातयुध्यमानस्य शत्रुभिः॥ सा तथा याच्यमाना त्वं काले काले जयैषिणा। उक्तवत्यसि गान्धारि यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः॥ न चाप्यतीतां गान्धारि वाचं ते वितथामहम्। स्मरामि भाषमाणायास्तथा प्राणिहिता ह्यसि॥
en: Your son, seeking victory had requested you every day for the eighteen days of the battle, saying,-'O mother bless me who am fighting with my foes!' Solicited thus every day by your son desirous of victory, you always answered him saying,-'victory' is there where righteousness is.' I do not, O Gandhari, remember that your words, have ever been falsified! Those words, therefore, which you, requested by Duryodhana, said to him could not be false. You are always engaged in the well being of all creatures.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: विग्रहे तुमुले राज्ञां गत्वा पारमसंशयम्। जितं पाण्डुसुतैर्युद्धे नूनं धर्मस्ततोऽधिकः॥
en: Having undoubtedly reached the other shore in that dreadful battle of Kshatriyas, the sons of Pandu have certainly gained the victory and greater a righteousness.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: क्षमाशीला पुरा भूत्वा साद्य न क्षमसे कथम्। अधर्मं जहि धर्मज्ञे यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः॥
en: You formerly observed the virtue of forgiveness. Why would you not observe it now? Restrain unrighteousness, O you who are ever righteousness. There is victory where righteousness is.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: स्वं च धर्म परिस्मृत्य वाचं चोक्ता मनस्विनि। कोपं संयच्छ गान्धारि मैवं भूः सत्यवादिनि॥ भगवन्नाभ्यसूयामि नैतानिच्छामि नश्यतः। पुत्रशोकेन तु बलान्मनो विह्वलतीव मे॥
en: Remembering your own righteousness and the words spoken by your self, check your wrath, O Gandhari! Do not act otherwise, O beautiful speeches lady!' hearing these words, Gandhari said,-'O holy one, I don not entertain any ill feelings towards the Pandavas, nor do I wish that they should die. Out of grief for the death of my sons, my heart is greatly shaken.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: यथैव कुन्त्या कौन्तेया रक्षितव्यास्तथा मया। तथैव धृतराष्ट्रेण रक्षितव्या यथा त्वया॥
en: I know that I should protect the Pandavas with as much care as Kunti does, and that Dhritarashtra also should protect them as I should.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: दुर्योधनापराधेन शकुनेः सौबलस्य च। कणंदुःशासनाभ्यां च कृतोऽयं कुरुसंक्षयः॥
en: For the holly of Duryodhana and of Shakuni the son of Subala, and through the action of Karna and Dushasana, this extinction of the Kurus has taken place.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: नापराध्यति बीभत्सुर्न च पार्थो वृकोदरः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च नैव जातु युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: In this matter Vibhatsu of Pritha's son Vrikodara, or Nakula Or Sahadeva, Or Yudhishthira himself is not to blame in the least.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: युध्यमाना हि कौरव्याः कृन्तमानाः परस्परम्। निहताः सहिताश्चान्यैस्तच नास्त्यप्रियं मम॥
en: While engaged in battle. the Kauravas, puffed up with arrogance and pride have perished with many others who helped them. I am not grieved at this.

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: किं तु कर्माकरोद् भीमो वासुदेवस्य पश्यतः। दुर्योधनं समाहूय गदायुद्धे महामनाः॥ शिक्षयाभ्यधिकं ज्ञात्वा चरन्तं बहुधा रणे। अधो नाभ्याः प्रहतवांस्तन्मे कोपमवर्धयत्॥
en: But there has been one act done by Bhima in the very presence of Vasudeva that excites my anger. Having challenged Duryodhana to a dreadful mace encounter, and having come to know that my son, while making diverse kinds of motion in the battle, was superior to him in skill, the great Vrikodara struck the latter below the navel,

description: Krishna with the Pandavas approaches Gandhari and consoles her
sn: कथं नु धर्म धर्मज्ञैः समुद्दिष्टं महात्मभिः। त्यजेयुराहवे शूराः प्राणहेतोः कथंचन॥
en: It is this that excites my anger. Why should heroes, for the sake of their lives, forget their duties that have been determined by great persons conversant with every duty?'

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्या भीमसेनोऽथ भीतवत्। गान्धारी प्रत्युवाचेदं वचः सानुनयं तदा॥ अधर्मो यदि वा धर्मस्त्रासात् तत्र मया कृतः। आत्मानं त्रातुकामेन तन्मे त्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Vaishampayana said “Hearing these words of Gandhari, Bhimasena, in fear said these words for solacing her. "The deed may be fair or unfair, I did it through fear and for the object of protecting my own self! you should, therefore, forgive me now!

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: न हि युद्धेन पुत्रस्ते धर्येण स महाबलः। शक्यः केनचिदुद्यन्तुमतो विषममाचरम्॥
en: Your powerful son was incapable of being killed by anybody in a fair and righteous battle. And therefore I did what was unfair.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: अधर्मेण जितः पूर्वं तेन चापि युधिष्ठिरः। निकृताश्च सदैव स्म ततो विषममाचरम्॥
en: Duryodhana himself had formerly defeated Yudhishthira unfairly. He always acted treacherously towards us. It was therefore that I had recourse to an unfair act.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: सैन्यस्यैकोऽवशिष्टोऽयं गदायुद्धेन वीर्यवान्। मां हत्वा न हरेद् राज्यमिति वै तत् कृतं मया॥
en: Your son was then the only unslain warrior of his party. In order that brave prince might not kill me in the mace-encounter and once more deprive us of our kingdom, I acted in that way.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: राजपुत्री च पाञ्चालीमेकवस्त्रां रजस्वलाम्। भवत्या विदितं सर्वमुक्तवान् यत् सुतस्तव॥
en: You know what your son had said to the princes of Panchala while the latter, in her seasons, was clad in a single piece of cloth.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: सुयोधनमसंगृह्य न शक्या भूः ससागरा। केवला भोक्तुमस्माभिरतश्चैतत् कृतं मया॥
en: Without having killed Suyodhana it was impossible for us to rule peacefully whole Earth with seas. And therefore I acted in that way.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: तथाप्यप्रियमस्माकं पुत्रस्ते समुपाचरत्। द्रौपद्या यत् सभामध्ये सव्यमूरुमदर्शयत्॥
en: Your son wronged us in many ways. In the court he had shown his left thigh to Draupadi.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: तदैव वध्यः सोऽस्माकं दुराचारश्च ते सुतः। धर्मराजाज्ञया चैव स्थिताः स्म समये तदा।॥
en: For that wicked conduct of his your son deserved to be killed by us even then. However, commanded by king Yudhishthira the just, we allowed ourselves to be restrained by the agreement that had been made.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: वैरमुद्दीपितं राज्ञि पुत्रेण तव तन्महत्। क्लेशिताश्च वने नित्यं तत एतत् कृतं मया।।१०।
en: By this means, O queen, your son excited deadly hostilities with us. We suffered great miseries in the forest. Remembering all this, I acted in that way!

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: वैरस्यास्य गताः पारं हत्वा दुर्योधनं रणे। राज्यं युधिष्ठिरः प्राप्तो वयं च गतमन्यवः॥
en: Having killed Duryodhana in battle, we have terminated our hostilities. Yudhishthira has regained his kingdom, and we also have been freed from anger!'

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: गान्धार्युवाच न तस्यैष वधस्तात यत् प्रशंससि मे सुतम्। कृतवांश्चापि तत् सर्वं यदिदं भाषसे मयि॥
en: Hearing these words of Bhima, Gandhari said,– 'As you praise my son thus he did not deserve such a death! He, however, did all that you describe!

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: हताश्वे नकुले यत्तु वृषसेनेन भारत। अपिबः शोणितं संख्ये दुःशासनशरीरजम्॥
en: When Vrishasena, however, had deprived Nakula of his horses, O Bharata, you drank in battle the blood from Dussasana's body.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: सद्भिर्विगर्हितं घोरमनार्यजनसेवितम्। क्रूरं कर्माकृथास्तस्मात्तदयुक्तं वृकोदर॥
en: Such an act is cruel and is spoken ill of by the good. It becomes a most disrespectable person. It was a wicked act, O Vrikodara, which you then perpetrated. You should not have done it.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: भीमसेन उवाच अन्यस्यापि न पातव्यं रुधिरं किं पुनः स्वकम्। यथैवात्मा तथा भ्राता विशेषो नास्ति कश्चन॥
en: Bhima replied,-'It is improper to drink the blood of even a stranger, what then need be said about quaffing the blood of one's own self. One's brother, again, is like his own self. There is no difference between them.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: रुधिरं न व्यतिक्रामद् दन्तोष्ठं मेऽम्ब मा शुचः। वैवस्वतस्तु तद् वेद हस्तौ मे रुधिरोक्षितौ॥
en: The blood, however, did not, O mother, pass down my lips and teeth. Karna knew this well. My hands only were covered with Dussasana's blood.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: हताश्वं नकुलं दृष्ट्वा वृषसेनेन संयुगे। भ्रातृणां सम्प्रहृष्टानां त्रासः संजानितो मया॥
en: Seeing Nakula deprived of his horses by Vrishasena in battle, I caused the rejoicing Kaurava brothers to be filled with fear.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: केशपक्षपरामर्श द्रौपद्या द्यूतकारिते। क्रोधाद् यदब्रवं चाहं तच्च मे हृदि वर्तते॥
en: When after the gambling match the hairs of Draupadi were seized, I gave vent to certain words in anger. I do still remember those words.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: क्षत्रधर्माच्च्युतो राज्ञि भवेयं शाश्वतीः समाः। प्रतिज्ञां तामनिस्तीर्य ततस्तत् कृतवानहम्॥
en: I would for all years to come, have been regarded to have neglected the duties of a Kshatriya if I had left that promise unfulfilled. It was for this, O queen, that I did that act.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: न मामर्हसि गान्धारि दोषेण परिशङ्कितुम्। अनिगृह्य पुरा पुत्रानस्मास्वनपकारिषु। अधुना किं नु दोषेण परिशङ्कितुमर्हसि॥
en: You should not, O Gandhari, attribute any fault to me. Without having checked your sons formerly, should you attribute any fault to our innocent selves.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: वृद्धस्यास्य पुत्रान् निघ्नंस्त्वमपराजितः। कस्मानाशेषयः कंचिद् येनाल्पमपराधितम्॥
en: Gandhari said "Unvanquished by any one, you have killed a hundred sons of this old man! Oh, why did you not spare, O child, even one son of this old couple deprived of kingdom. Who had not committed a greater offense?

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: संतानमावयोस्तात वृद्धयोर्हतराज्ययोः। कथमन्धद्वयस्यास्य यष्टिरेका न वर्जिता॥
en: Why did you not leave even one crutch for this blind couple?

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: शेषे ह्यवस्थिते तात पुत्राणामन्तके त्वयि। न मे दुःखं भवेदेतद् यदि त्वं धर्ममाचरेः॥
en: O child, although you live unscathed, having killed all my sons, yet I would not have been sorry, if you had followed the path of righteousness in killing them.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु गान्धारी युधिष्ठिरमपृच्छत। व स राजेति सक्रोधा पुत्रपौत्रवधार्दिता॥
en: Vaishampayana continued Having said so, Gandhari, filled with anger at the slaughter of all her sons and grandsons enquired after Yudhishthira, saying.-'Where is the king?'

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: तमभ्यगच्छद् राजेन्द्रो वेपमानः कृताञ्जलिः। युधिष्ठिरस्त्विदं तत्र मधुरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ पुत्रहन्ता नृशंसोऽहं तव देवि युधिष्ठिरः। शापार्हः पृथिवीनाशे हेतुभूतः शपस्व माम्॥
en: After she had said these words, king Yudhishthira, trembling and with joined hands, approached her and said, 'Here is Yudhishthira, O goddess, that cruel destroyer of your sons! I deserve your curses, for I am the root of this universal destruction! Oh curse me!

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: न हि मे जीवितेनार्थो न राज्येन धनेन वा। तादृशान् सुहृदो हत्वा मूढस्यास्य सुहृद्रुहः॥
en: I do not care for life, for kingdom, for wealth! Having brought about the destruction of such friends, I have proved myself to be a great fool and a hater of friend.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: तमेवंवादिनं भीतं संनिकर्षगतं तदा। नोवाच किंचिद् गान्धारी निःश्वासपरमा भृशम्॥
en: Gandhari, singing heavily, said nothing to Yudhishthira-who spoke such words, who was overcome with fear, and who stood in ner presence.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: तस्यावनतदेहस्य पादयोर्निपतिष्यतः। युधिष्ठिरस्य नृपतेधर्मज्ञा दीर्घदर्शिनी॥ अंगुल्यग्राणि ददृशे देवी पट्टान्तरेण सा! ततः स कुनखीभूतो दर्शनीयनखो नृपः॥
en: Conversant with the rules of righteousness, the Kuru queen, possessed of great foresight, turned her eyes from within the folds of the cloth that covered them, to the tip of Yudhishthira's toe, as the prince with body bent forwards, was about to fall down at her feet. At this, the king, whose nails had before this been all very beautiful, got a sore nail on his toe.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा चार्जुनोऽगच्छद् वासुदेवस्य पृष्ठतः। एवं संचेष्टमानांस्तानितश्चेतश्च भारत॥
en: Seeing this, Arjuna went behind Vasudeva, and the other sons of Pandu became restless and moved about from one place to another.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: गान्धारी विगतक्रोधा सान्त्वयामास मातृवत्। तया ते समनुज्ञाता मातरं वीरमातरम्॥
en: Gandhari then, having shaken off her anger, comforted the Pandavas as a inother should,. With her permission those broadchested heroes then proceeded together to present themselves to their mother.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: अभ्यगच्छन्त सहिताः पृथां पृथुलवक्षसः। चिरस्य दृष्ट्वा पुत्रान् सा पुत्राधिभिरभिप्लुता॥
en: Having seen her sons after a long time, Kunti who had been filled with anxiety for them covered her face with her cloth and began to weep.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: बाप्पमाहारयद् देवी वस्त्रेणावृत्य वै मुखम्। ततो बाष्पं समुत्सृज्य सह पुत्रैस्तदा पृथा॥ अपश्यदेताशस्त्रौधैर्बहुधा क्षतविक्षतान्।
en: Having wept for sometime with her children, I'ritha saw the wounds and scars of many weapons of their bodies.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: सा तानेकैकशः पुत्रान् संस्पृशन्तीं पुनः पुनः॥ अन्वशोचत दुःखार्ता द्रौपदी च हृतात्मजाम्। रुदतीमथ पाञ्चालीं ददर्श पतितां भुवि॥
en: She then repeatedly embraced and patted each of her sons, and stricken with grief wept with Draupadi who had lost all her children and whom she saw lying on the naked Earth, piteously bewailing.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: द्रौपद्युवाच आर्येः पौत्राः क ते सर्वे सौभद्रसहिता गताः। न त्वां तेऽद्याभिगच्छन्ति चिरं दृष्ट्वा तपस्विनीम्॥ किं नु राज्येन वै कार्यं विहीनायाः सुतैर्ममा
en: Draupadi said O Venerable lady, were have all your grandsons, with Abhimanyu among them, gone? Seeing you in such distress why are they delaying in coming before you. Deprived as I am of my children, what need have I of kingdom.'

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: तां समाश्वासयामास पृथा पृथुललोचना॥ उत्थाप्य याज्ञसेनी तु रुदतीं शोककर्शिताम्।
en: Raising the grief-stricken princess of Panchala who was weeping thus, Pritha began to solace that lady having of large eyes.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: तयैव सहिता चापि पुत्रैरनुगता नृप॥ अभ्यगच्छत गान्धारीमार्तामार्ततरा स्वयम्।
en: Then Kunti, accompanied by the princess of Panchala, and followed by her sons proceeded towards the grief-afflicted Gandhari, though she herself was also in great sorrow.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तामुवाचाथ गान्धारी सह बध्वा यशस्विनीम्॥ मैवं पुत्रीति शोकार्ता पश्य मामपि दुःखिताम्।
en: Seeing that illustrious lady with her daughter-in-law, Gandhari said, 'Do not, O daughter, grieve so. See, I too am much afflicted with sorrow as you.

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: पन्ये लोकविनाशोऽयं कालपर्यायनोदितः॥ अवश्यभावी सम्प्राप्तः स्वभावाल्लोमहर्षणः।
en: I think, this universal destruction has been caused by the irresistible course of Time. This dreadful slaughter was inevitable, since it has not been brought about by human agency!

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: इदं तत् समनुप्राप्तं विदुरस्य वचो महत्॥ असिद्धानुनये कृष्णे यदुवाच महामतिः।
en: What Vidura of great wisdom foretold, after Krishna's suing in vain for peace, has now come to pass!

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: तस्मिन्नपरिहार्येऽर्थे व्यतीते च विशेषतः॥ माशुचो न हि शोच्यास्ते संग्रामे निधनं गताः।
en: Do not, therefore, grieve in a matter that was inevitable, especially when it has taken place! Having been dead in battle they should not be grieved for!

description: Bhima admits that he killed Duryodhana unfairly. Yudhishthira's lamentation. Gandhari comforts the Pandavas
sn: यथैवाहं तथैव त्वं को नावाश्वासयिष्यति। ममैव ह्यपराधेन कुलमयं विनाशितम्॥
en: I am in the same situation as you are! (If you act thus) who then will comfort us? Through my fault, this foremost of races has becn ruined.' I am in the same situation as you are! (If you act thus) who then will comfort us? Through my fault, this foremost of races has becn ruined.'

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु गान्धारी कुरूणामवकर्तनम्। अपश्यत्तत्र तिष्ठन्ती सर्वं दिव्येन चक्षुषा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said so, Gandhari, though standing on that spot which was distant from the field of battle, saw with her spiritual eye, the slaughter of the Kurus.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: पतिव्रता भागा समानव्रतचारिणी। उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता सततं सत्यवादिनी॥
en: Devoted to her lord, that highly blessed lady always practised high vows. Practising the severest penances, she was always truthful in her speech.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: वरदानेन कृष्णस्य महर्षेः पुण्यकर्मणः। दिव्यज्ञानबलोपेता विविधं पर्यदेवयत्॥
en: By virtue of the gift of the boon by the great Rishi Vyasa of pure deeds, she came by spiritual knowledge and power. The lady then piteously bewailed.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: ददर्श सा बुद्धिमती दूरादपि यथान्तिके। रणाजिरं नृवीराणामद्भुतं लोमहर्षणम्॥
en: The highly intelligent Kuru dame saw, from a distance, but as if from a near point, that field of battle, terrible to look at and full of wonderful sights, of those foremost of warriors.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: अस्थिकेशवसाकीर्णं शोणितौघपरिप्लुतम्। शरीरैर्बहुसाहौर्विनिकीर्णं समन्ततः॥
en: Strewn with bones and hair, and covered with streams of blood, that field was filled with thousands upon thousands of dead bodies on every side.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: गजाश्वरथयोधानामावृतं रुधिराबिलैः। शरीरैरशिरस्कैश्च विदेहैश्च शिरोगणैः॥
en: covered with the blood of elephants and horses and car-warriors and various warriors, it was filled with headless trunks and trunkless heads.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: गजाश्वनरनारीणां नि:स्वरैरभिसंवृतम्। शृगालबककाकोलकङ्ककाकनिवेधितम्॥
en: And it resounded with the cries of elephants and horses and men and women, and abounded with jackals and cranes and ravens and Kankas and crows.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: रक्षसां पुरुषादानं मोदनं कुरराकुलम्। अशिवाभिः शिवाभिश्च नादितं गृध्रसेवितम्॥
en: And it was the sporting ground of Rakshasas living on human flesh. And it was filled with ospreys and vultures and resounded with the inauspicious yells of jackals.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: ततो व्यासाभ्यनुज्ञातो धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः। पाण्डुपुत्राश्च ते सर्वे युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमाः॥ वासुदेवं पुरस्कृत्य हतबन्धुं च पार्थिवम्। कुरुस्त्रियः समासाद्य जग्मुरायोधनं प्रति॥
en: Then at the command of Vyasa king Dhritarashtra and all the sons of Pandu led by Yudhishthira, with Vasudeva and all the Kuru ladies, went to the battle-field.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: समासाद्य कुरुक्षेत्रं ताः स्त्रियो निहतेश्वराः। अपश्यन्त हतांस्तत्र पुत्रान् भ्रातृन् पितॄन् पतीन्॥ क्रव्यादैर्भक्ष्यमाणान् वै गोमायुबलवायसैः। भूतैः पिशाचै रक्षोभिर्विविधैश्च निशाचरैः॥
en: Having reached Kurukshetra, those widowed ladies beheld their killed their killed brothers and sons and sires and husbands lying on carth, as their bodies were being devoured by beasts of prey and wolves and ravens and crows and ghosts and Pishchas and Rakshasas and various other night-rangers.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: रुद्राक्रीडनिभं दृष्ट्वा तदा विशसनं स्त्रियः। महाहेभ्योऽथ यानेभ्यो विक्रोशन्त्यो निपेतिरे॥
en: Seeing that onslaught which resembled the spectacles seen on the sporting ground of Rudra, the ladies cried and quickly got down from their costly cars. were

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: अदृष्टपूर्वं पश्यन्त्यो दुःखार्ता भरतस्त्रियः। शरीरेष्वस्खलनन्याः पतन्त्यश्चापरा भुवि॥
