en: Witnessing sights the like of which they had never before seen, the Bharata ladies felt their limbs to be deprived of strength and dropped down on the ground.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: श्रान्तानां चाप्यनाथानां नासीत् काचन चेतना। पाञ्चालकुरुयोषाणां कृपणं तदभून्महत्॥
en: Others became so stupefied that they lost their consciousness. Indeed, the Panchala and the Kuru ladies plunged into indescribable distress.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: दुःखोपहतचित्ताभिः समन्तादनुनादितम्। दृष्ट्वाऽऽयोधनमत्युग्रं धर्मज्ञा सुबलात्मजा॥ ततः सा पुण्डरीकाक्षमामन्व्य पुरुषोत्तमम्। कुरूणां वैशसं दृष्ट्वा इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ पश्यैताः पुण्डरीकाक्ष स्नुषा मे निहतेश्वराः। प्रकीर्णकेशा: क्रोशन्ती: कुररीरिव माधव॥
en: Seeing that dreadful field of battle filled on all sides with the cries of those grief-stricken ladies, the daughter of Subala, acquainted with all forms of duty, addressed the louts-eyed, Keshava that foremost of all men. Beholding that universal destruction of the Kurus and filled with grief at the sight, she said,-'Look, O lotus-eyed Mahadeva, at these daughters-inlaw of mine! Deprived of their husbands they are with dishevelled hair, crying piteously like a flight of she-ospreys.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: अमूस्त्वभिसमागम्य स्मरन्त्यो भर्तृजान् गुणान्। पृथगेवाभ्यधावन्त्यः पुत्रान् भ्रातॄन् पितॄन् पतीन्॥
en: Seeing those dead bodies, they are remembering the great Bharata chiefs! They are running here and those in a body towards their sons and brothers and sires and husbands.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: वीरसूभिर्महाराज हतपुत्राभिरावृतम्। वचिच्च वीरपत्नीमिर्हतवीराभिरावृतम्॥
en: See, O mighty-armed one, the field is covered with mothers of heroes, all of whom, however, have been deprived of children! There, that part is covered with wives of heroes, who have however, been bereaved of their husbands.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: शोभितं पुरुषव्याप्रैः कर्णभीष्माभिमन्युभिः। द्रोणद्रुपदशल्यैश्च ज्वलद्भिरिव पावकैः॥
en: See the field of battle is adorned with those foremost of men, viz., Bhishma and Karna and Abhimanyu and Drona and Drupada and Shalya.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: काञ्चनैः कवचैर्निष्कर्मणिभिश्च महात्मनाम्। अङ्गदैर्हस्तकेयूरैःस्रग्भिश्च समलङ्कृतम्॥
en: See it is adorned also with the golden coasts of mail, and with the precious gems, of high-souled warriors, and with their Angadas and Keyuras and garlands.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: वीरबाहुविसृष्टाभिः शक्तिभिः परिधैरपि। खङ्गैश्च विविधैस्तीक्ष्णैः सशरैश्च शरासनैः॥
en: Behold, it is covered with darts and spikes discharged by heroic hands, and swords and various kinds of keen arrows and bows.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: क्रव्यादसंधैर्मुदितैस्तिष्ठद्भिः सहितैः क्वचित्। वचिदाक्रीडमानैश्च शयानैश्चापरैः क्वचित्॥
en: Beasts of prey, in a body, are standing or sporting or lying down according to their pleasure.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: एतदेवंविधं वीर सम्पश्यायोधनं विभो। पश्यमाना हि दह्यामि शोकेनाहं जनार्दन॥
en: Behold, O powerful hero, the field of battle in this state! At this sight, O Janarddana, I am burning with grief.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: पञ्चालानां कुरूणां च विनाशे मधुसूदन। पञ्चानामपि भूतानामहं वधमचिन्तयम्॥
en: With the destruction of the Panchalas and the Kurus, O slayer of Madhu, I think, the five elements have been destroyed.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: तान् सुपर्णाश्च गृध्राश्च कर्षयन्त्यसृगुक्षिताः। विगृह्य चरणैर्गध्रा भक्षयन्ति सहस्रशः॥
en: Dreadful vultures and thousands of others birds, are dragging those bodies stained with blood and seizing them by their armour, are devouring them.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: जयद्रथस्य कर्णस्य तथैव द्रोणभीष्मयोः। अभिमन्योर्विनाशं च कश्चिन्तयितुमर्हति॥
en: Who is there that could even imagine the death of such heroes as Jayadratha, Karna, Drona, Bhishma and Abhimanyu.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: अवध्यकल्पान् निहतान् गतसत्त्वानचेतसः। गृध्रकङ्कवटश्येनश्वशृगालादनीकृतान्॥
en: Alas, though incapable of being killed they have yet been killed, O slayer of Madhu! Behold, vultures, Kankas, ravens hawks, dogs and jackals are feasting upon them.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: अमर्षवशमापन्नान् दुर्योधनवशे स्थितान्। पश्येमान् पुरुषव्याघ्रान् संशान्तान् पावकानिव॥
en: There, those foremost of men, who fought on Duryodhana's side, and went to the field in anger and now lying like extinguished fires.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: शयाना ये परा सर्वे मृदूनि शयनानि च। विपन्नास्तेऽद्यं वसुधां विवृतामधिशेरते॥
en: All of them deserve sleeping on soft and clean beds, But alas, in a distressful condition they are sleeping to-day on the naked ground.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: बन्दिभिः सततं काले स्तुवद्भिरभिनन्दिताः। शिवानामशिवा घोराः शृण्वन्ति विविधा गिरः॥
en: Recounting their praises poets used to place them before at proper times. They are now listening to the fierce and inauspicious yells of jackals.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: ये पुरा शेरते वीराः शयनेषु यशस्विनः। चन्दनागुरुदिग्धाङ्गास्तेऽद्य पांसुषु शेरते॥
en: Those great heroes who used formerly to sleep on rich beds with their limbs smeared with sandal-paste and powered alone, are now sleeping on the dust.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: तेषामाभरणान्येते गृध्रगोमायुवायसाः। आक्षिपन्ति शिवा घोरा विनदन्त्यः पुनः पुनः॥
en: These vultures, wolves and ravens are now their ornaments. Uttering again and again inauspicious and fierce cries, those creatures are now dragging their bodies.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: बाणान् विनिशितान् पीतान् निस्त्रिंशान् विमला गदाः। युद्धाभिमानिनः सर्वे जीवन्त इव बिभ्रति॥
en: Those heroes, look even cheerful, now, and have still beside them their keen arrows, welltempered swords, and bright maces, as if life has not yet left them!

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: सुरूपवर्णा बहवः क्रव्यादैरवघट्टिताः। ऋषभप्रतिरूपाश्च शेरते हरितस्रजः॥
en: Many leading heroes, possessed of beauty and fair complexions and bedecked with garlands of gold, are sleeping on the ground! Look beasts of prey are dragging and tearing them.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: अपरे पुनरालिङ्गय गदाः परिघबाहवः। शेरतेऽभिमुखाः शूरा दयिता इव योषितः॥
en: Some with massive arms, are sleeping with maces under them as if those were beloved wives.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: बिभ्रतः कवचान्यन्ये विमलान्यायुधानि च। न धर्षयन्ति क्रव्यादा जीवन्तीति जनार्दन॥
en: Others with armour on, are holding in their hands their effulgent weapons. Beasts of prey are not tearing him, O Janarddana, thinking them to be still alive.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: क्रव्यादैः कृष्यमाणानामपरेषां महात्मनाम्। शातकौम्भ्यः सजश्चित्रा विप्रकीर्णाः समन्ततः॥
en: The beautiful golden garlands on the necks of other illustrious heroes, as the latter and being dragged by carnivorous creatures, are scattered about on all sides.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: एते गोमायवो भीमा निहतानां यशस्विनाम्। कण्ठान्तरगतान् हारानाक्षिपन्ति सहस्रशः॥
en: There, thousands of fierce wolves, are dragging the golden chains sound the necks of many illustrious but dead heroes.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: सर्वेष्वपररात्रेषु याननदन्त बन्दिनः। स्तुतिभिश्च पराया॑भिरुपचारैश्च शिक्षिताः॥ तानिमाः परिदेवन्ति दुःखार्ताः परमाङ्गनाः। कृपणं वृष्णिशार्दूल दुःखशोकार्दिता भृशम्॥
en: Many, whom clever bards formerly used with their hymns and panegyris, to delight every morning, are now surrounded by fair ladies stricken with grief and weeping and crying around them in distress, O foremost of Vrishni's race.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: रक्तोत्पलवनानीव विभान्ति रुचिराणि च। मुखानि परमस्त्रीणां परिशुष्काणि केशव॥
en: The faces of those beautiful ladies, O Keshava, though pale, still shine like red lotuses.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: रुदिताद् विरता ह्येता ध्यायन्त्यः सपरिच्छदाः। कुरुस्त्रियोऽभिगच्छन्ति तेन तेनैव दुःखिताः॥
en: Those Kuru ladies have ceased weeping with their followers and companions. They are all filled with anxiety. Bewilders with sorrows, they are running here and there.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: एतान्यादित्यवर्णानि तपनीयनिभानि च। रोषरोदनताम्राणि वक्त्राणि कुरुयोषिताम्॥
en: The faces of those fair ladies have, with weeping and ire, become effulgent as the morning sun, or gold, or burnished copper.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: श्यामानां वरवर्णानां गौरीणामेकवाससाम्। दुर्योधनवरस्त्रीणां पश्य वृन्दानि केशव॥
en: Hearing each other's unmeaning lamentations those ladies, on account of the loud cries of woe coming from every side, are unable to understand each other's meaning.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: आसामपरिपूर्णार्थं निशम्य परिदेवितम्। इतरेतरसंक्रन्दान्न विजानन्ति योषितः॥
en: Some amongst them, heavily sighing and repeatedly bewailing, are stupefied by grief and are giving up their lives.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: एता दीर्घमिवोच्छ्वस्य विक्रुश्य च विलष्य च। विस्पन्दमाना दुःखेन वीरा जहति जीवितम्॥
en: Many of them, seeing the bodies (of their sons, husbands, or sires,) are weeping and lamcnting. Others and striking their heads with their own soft hands.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: बढ्यो दृष्ट्वा शरीराणि क्रोशन्ति विलपन्ति च। पाणिभिश्चापरा घ्नन्ति शिरांसि मृदुपाणयः॥
en: The Earth, filled with heaps of heads and hands and other limbs, the sights of destruction, looks resplendent.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: शिरोभिः पतितैर्हस्तैः सर्वाङ्गै!थशः कृतैः। इतरेतरसम्पृक्तैराकीर्णा भाति मेदिनी॥
en: Secing many headless trunks of great beauty, and many heads without trunks, those fair ladies and lying unconscious on the ground for a long while.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: विशिरस्कानथो कायान् दृष्ट्वा ह्येताननिन्दितान्। मुह्यन्त्यनुगता नार्यो विदेहानि शिरांसि च॥ शिरः कायेन संधाय प्रेक्षमाणा विचेतसः। अपश्यन्त्योऽपरं तत्र नेदमस्येति दुःखिताः॥
en: Joining particular heads with particular trunks, those ladies, beside themselves with grief, are again discovering their mistakes, and saying,-This is not this one's—and are weeping more bitterly.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: बाहूरुचरणानन्यान् विशिखोन्मथितान् पृथक्। संदधत्योऽसुखाविष्टा मूर्च्छन्त्येताः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Other, uniting arms and thighs and feet, cut off with arrows, are grieving and losing their consciousness repeatedly.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: उत्कृत्तशिरसश्चान्यान् विजग्धान् मृगपक्षिभिः। दृष्ट्वा काश्चिन्न जानन्ति भर्तृन् भरतयोषितः॥
en: Some amongst the Bharata ladies, beholding the bodies of their husbands, mangled by animals and birds and shorn of heads,-are not recognising them.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: पाणिभिश्चापरा जन्ति शिरांसि मधुसूदन। प्रेक्ष्य भ्रातॄन् पितॄन् पुत्रान् पतींश्च निहतान् परैः॥
en: Others, seeing their brothers, sires, sons, and husbands killed by enemies, are, O slayer of Madhu, striking their heads with their own hands.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: बाहुभिश्च सखङ्गैश्च शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः। अगम्यकल्पा पृथिवी मांसशोणितकर्दमा॥
en: Covered with flesh and blood, the Earth has become impassable with arms still holding swords and with heads adorned with ear-rings.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: न दुःखेषूचिताः पूर्वं दुखं गाहन्त्यनिन्दिताः। भ्रातृभिः पतिभिः पुत्रैरुपाकीर्णा वसुंधरा॥
en: Seeing the field covered with the dead bodies of their brothers and sires, and sons, those faultless ladies, who had never before experienced the least distress, are now plunged into indescribable misery.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: यूथानीव किशोरीणां सुकेशीनां जनार्दन। स्नुषाणां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पश्य वृन्दान्यनेकशः॥
en: Look, O Janarddana, at those Dhritarashtra's daughters-in-law, resembling a number of beautiful fillies adorned with excellent manes.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: इतो दुःखतरं किं नु केशव प्रतिभाति मे। यदिमाः कुर्वते सर्वा रवमुच्चावचं स्त्रियः॥ नूनमाचरितं पापं मया पूर्वेषु जन्मसु। या पश्यामि हतान् पुत्रान् पौत्रान् भ्रातृ॑श्च माधव॥ एवमार्ता विलपती समाभाष्य जनार्दनम्। गान्धारी पुत्रशोकार्ता ददर्श निहतं सुतम्॥
en: O Keshava, is there a more sorrowful sight for me to see then that presented by those ladies of fair forms who are put into such a miserable plight? I must, forsooth, have perpetrated great sins in my previous existence, since I am beholding, O Keshava, my sons and grandsons and brothers all killed by foes.' While thus bewailing Gandhari saw the dead body of her son Duryodhana.

description: Gandhari saw the battle-field with her spiritual eye
sn: नूनमाचरितं पापं मया पूर्वेषु जन्मसु। या पश्यामि हतान् पुत्रान् पौत्रान् भ्रातृ॑श्च माधव॥ एवमार्ता विलपती समाभाष्य जनार्दनम्। गान्धारी पुत्रशोकार्ता ददर्श निहतं सुतम्॥
en: O Keshava, is there a more sorrowful sight for me to see then that presented by those ladies of fair forms who are put into such a miserable plight? I must, forsooth, have perpetrated great sins in my previous existence, since I am beholding, O Keshava, my sons and grandsons and brothers all killed by foes.' While thus bewailing Gandhari saw the dead body of her son Duryodhana.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच दुर्योधनं हतं दृष्ट्वा गान्धारी शोककर्शिता। सहसा न्यपतद् भूमौ छिन्नेव कदली वने॥
en: Vaishampayana said Secing Duryodhana, Gandhari, deprived of her senses by grief, suddenly dropped down on the Earth like an uprooted plantain tree.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: सा तु लब्ध्वा पुनः संज्ञां विक्रुश्य च विलप्य च। दुर्योधनमभिप्रेक्ष्य शयानं रुधिरोक्षितम्॥
en: Having regained her consciousness soon, she began to weep and lament seeing her son lying on the bare ground, bathed in blood.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: परिष्वज्य च गान्धारी कृपणं पर्यदेवयत्। हा हा पुत्रेति शोकार्ता विललापाकुलेन्द्रिया॥
en: Embracing her son, Gandhari bewailed piteously. Stricken with grief, and growing unconscious, the Kuru queen exclaimed, 'Alas, O son!' 'Alas, O son.'

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: सुगूढजत्रुविपुलं हारनिष्कविभूषितम्। वारिणा नेत्रजेनोरः सिंचन्ती शोकतापिता॥ समीपस्थं हृषीकेशमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। उपस्थितेऽस्मिन् संग्रामे ज्ञातीनां संक्षये विभो॥ मामयं प्राह वार्ष्णेय प्राञ्जलिर्नृपसत्तमः। अस्मिन् ज्ञातिसमुद्धर्ष जयमम्बा ब्रवीतु मे॥ इत्युक्ते जानती सर्वमहं स्वव्यसनागमम्। अब्रवं पुरुषव्याघ्र यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः॥
en: Burning with grief, the queen wetted with her tears the body of her son, possessed of massive and broad shoulders, and adorned with garlands and collar. Addressing Hrishikesha, who stood by her, she said,-'On the eve on this battie, O powerful one, that had exterminated this race, this foremost of kings, O Vrishny hero, said to me,-In this civil battle, O mother, wish me success!-When he said these words, myself, knowing that a great calamity had befallen us, told him, O foremost of men, Victory is there where righteousness is.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: यथा च युध्यमानस्त्वं न वै मुह्यासि पुत्रक। ध्रुवं शस्त्रजिताल्लोकान् प्राप्स्यस्यमरवत् प्रभो॥
en: And since, O son, you are bent upon fighting a battle. you will, forsooth, obtain those regions that can be gained by weapons and sport there like a celestial.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: इत्येवमब्रवं पूर्वं नैनं शोचामि वै प्रभो। धृतराष्ट्रं तु शोचामि कृपणं हतबान्धवम्॥
en: These were the words that I then said to him. I did not then grieve for my son. I am, however, sorry for the helpless Dhritarashtra deprived of friends and kinsmen.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: अमर्षणं युधां श्रेष्ठं कृतास्त्रं युद्धदुर्मदम्। शयानं वीरशयने पश्य माधव मे सुतम्॥
en: Look, O Madhava, at my son, that best of warriors, wrathful, expert in weapons, and irresistible in battle, sleeping on the bed of heroes.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: योऽयं मूर्धाभिषिक्तानामग्रे याति परंतपः। सोऽयं पांसुषु शेतेऽद्य पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: See the reverses brought about by Time, this subduer of enemies that used forinerly to walk at the head of all kings now sleeps on thc dust.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: ध्रुवं दुर्योधनो वीरो गतिं न सुलभां गतः। तथा ह्यभिमुखः शेते शयने वीरसेविते॥
en: Forsooth, the heroic Duryodhana, when he sleeps on that bed of the heroes, has attain to the best end.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: यं पुरा पर्युपासीना रमयन्ति वरस्त्रियः। तं वीरशयने सुप्तं रमयन्त्यशिवाः शिवाः॥
en: Inauspicious jackals are now pleasing that prince sleeping on the hero's bed, who was formerly counted by the fairest of ladies sitting round him.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: यं पुरा पर्युपासीना रमयन्ति महीक्षितः। महीतलस्थं निहतं गृध्रास्तं पर्युपासते॥
en: He who was formerly encircled by kings who competed with one another to give him pleasure, alas, is now slain and lying on the ground, encircled by vultures.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: यं पुरा व्यजनै रम्यैरुपवीजन्ति योषितः। तमद्य पक्षव्यजनैरुपवीजन्ति पक्षिणः॥
en: He who was formerly fanned with beautiful fans by fair damsels, is now fanned by (carnivorous) birds with flaps of their wings.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: एष शेते महाबाहुर्बलवान् सत्यविक्रमः। तमद्य द्विपः संख्ये भीमसेनेन पातितः॥
en: Endued with great strength and true prowess, this mighty-armed prince, killed by Bhimasena in battle, sleeps like in elephant killed by a lion.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: पश्य दुर्योधनं कृष्ण शयानं रुधिरोक्षितम्। निहतं भीमसेनेन गदा सम्मृज्य भारतम्॥
en: Look at Duryodhana, O Krishna, lying on the naked Earth, bathed in blood, killed by Bhimasena with his mace.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: अक्षौहिणीर्महाबाहुर्दश चैकां च केशव। आनयद् यः पुरा संख्ये सोऽनयान्निधनं गतः॥
en: That mighty-armed one who had in battle collected together eleven Akshauhinis of soldiers, O Keshava, has on account of his own evil policy, been now killed.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: एष दुर्योधनः शेते महेष्वासो महाबलः। शार्दूल इव सिंहेन भीमसेनेन पातितः॥
en: Alas, there that great bowman and powerful car-warrior sleeps, killed by Bhimasena, like a tiger killed by a lion,

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: विदुरं ह्यवमत्यैषं पितरं चैन मन्दभाक्। बालो वृद्धावमानेन मन्दो मृत्युवंश गतः॥
en: Having disobeyed Vidura, and his own father, this reckless, foolish, and wicked prince has met with death, on account of his disregard of the old.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: निःसपत्ना मही यस्य त्रयोदश समाः स्थिता। स शेते निहतो भूमौ पुत्रो मे पृथिवीपतिः॥
en: He who had unrivaled away over the Earth, for thirteen years, alas, that prince, that son of mine, sleeps to-day on the naked Earth, killed by his foes.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: अपश्यं कृष्ण पृथिवीं धार्तराष्ट्रानुशासिताम्। पूर्णां हस्तिगवाश्वैश्च वार्ष्णेय न तु तचिरम्॥
en: Not long before, O Krishna, I saw the Earth, full of elephants and kine and horses, ruled by Duryodhana.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: तामेवाद्य महाबाहो पश्याम्यन्यानुशासिताम्। हीनां हस्तिगवाशेन किं नु जीवामि माधव॥
en: To-day, O you of mighty-arms, I see her governed by another, and destitute of elephants and kine and horses. What need have I, O Madhava, of lie?

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: इदं कष्टतरं पश्य पुत्रस्यापि वधान्मम। यदिमाः पर्युपासन्ते हताशूरान् रणे स्त्रियः॥
en: Again, look at this sight, of these fair ladies weeping by the side of the killed heroes, that is more painful than the death of my son.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: प्रकीर्णकेशां सुश्रोणी दुर्योधनशुभाङ्कगाम्। रुक्मवेदीनिभां पश्य कृष्ण लक्ष्मणमातरम्॥
en: Behold, O Krishna, the mother of Lakshmana, that lady having large hips, with her hairs disheveled, that dear wife of Duryodhana, resembling a golden sacrificial altar.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: नूनमेषा पुरा बाला जीवमाने महीभुजे। भुजावाश्रित्य रमते सुभुजस्य मनस्विनी॥
en: While her mighty-armed husband was formerly alive, this highly intelligent damsel used to sport within the embrace of her lords' beautiful arms.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: कथं तु शतधा नेदं हृदयं मम दीर्यते। पश्यन्त्या निहतं पुत्रं पुत्रेण सहितं रणे॥
en: Why, indeed, does not my heart break into a hundred pieces seeing my son and grandson killed in battle.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: पुत्रं रुधिरसंसिक्तमुपजिघ्रत्यनिन्दिता। दुर्योधनं तु वामोरू: पाणिना परिमार्जती॥
en: Alas, that innocent lady now smells her son covered with blood. Again, that lady having beautiful thighs is gently rubbing Duryodhana's body with her fair hand.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: किं नु शोचति भर्तारं पुत्रं चैषा मनस्विनी। तथा ह्यवस्थिता भाति पुत्रं चाप्यभिवीक्ष्य सा॥
en: At one time she is grieving for her husband, and again for her son. At one time she looks on her lord, and again on her son.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: स्वशिरः पञ्चशाखाभ्यामभिहत्यायतेक्षणा। पतत्युरसि वीरस्य कुरुराजस्य माधव॥
en: See, O Madhava, striking her head with her hands, she falls upon the breast of her heroic husband, the king of the Kurus.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: पुण्डरीकनिभा भाति पुण्डरीकान्तरप्रभा। मुखं विमृज्य पुत्रस्य भर्तुश्चैव तपस्विनी।॥
en: Having a complexion like that of the filaments of the lotus, she looks beautiful like a lotus. The hapless princess, now rubs the face of her son, and again that of her husband.

description: Gandhari bewails at seeing Duryodhana addressing Krishna
sn: यदि सत्यगमाः सन्ति यदि वै श्रुतयस्तथा। ध्रुवं लोकानवाप्तोऽयं नृपो बाहुबलार्जितान्॥
en: If the scriptures and the Shrutis be true, forsooth, this king has obtained the blessed region that one may acquire by the use of weapons.'

sn: गान्धार्युवाच पश्य माधव पुत्रान्मे शतसंख्याञ्जितक्कमान्। गदया भीमसेनेन भूयिष्ठं निहतान् रणे॥
en: Gandhari said See, O Madhava, my hundred sons. who never knew fatigue in battle, have all been killed by Bhimasena with his mace in battle.

sn: इदं दुःखतरं मेऽद्य यदिमा मुक्तमूर्धजाः। हतपुत्रा रणे बालाः परिधावन्ति मे स्नुषाः॥
en: That which pains me more to-day is that these my young daughter-in-law, deprived of sons and with disheveled hairs, are wandering on the field today.

sn: प्रासादतलचारिण्यश्चरणैर्भूषणान्वितैः। आपना यत् स्पृशन्तीमां रुधिरार्दी वसुन्धराम्॥
en: Alas, they who formerly walked only on the terraces of magnificent edifices with feet decorated with many ornaments, are now, in great misery, obliged to touch with those feet of theirs this hard Earth, covered with blood.

sn: कृच्छ्रादुत्सारयन्ति स्म गृध्रगोमायुवायसान्। दुःखेनार्ता विघूर्णन्त्यो मत्ता इव चरन्त्युत॥
en: Reeling in sorrow, they are moving about like drunk persons, driving away with difficulty vulture and jackals and crows.

sn: एषान्या त्वनद्यागी करसम्मितमध्यमा। घोरमायोधनं दृष्ट्वा निपतत्यतिदुःखिता॥
en: Behold, seeing this terrible destruction, that lady of beautiful limbs, and slender waist, falls down, laden with grief.

sn: मे पार्थिवसुतामेतां लक्ष्मणमातरम्। राजपुत्रीं महाबाहो मनो न ह्युपशाम्यति॥
en: Beholding this princess, this mother of Lakshmana, O you of mighty-arms, my heart is torn with sorrow.

sn: भ्रातूंश्चान्याः पितॄश्चान्याः पुत्रांश्च निहतान् भुवि। दृष्ट्वा परिपतन्त्येताः प्रगृह्य सुमहाभुजान्॥
en: Some seeing their brothers, some their husbands, and some their sons, lying down dead on the naked earth, these beautiful ladies of fair arms, and themselves falling down, catching the arms of the killed.

sn: मध्यमानां तु नारीणां वृद्धानां चापराजित। आक्रन्दं हतबन्धूनां दारुणे वैशसे शृणु॥
en: Hear, O unvanquished one, the loud lamentations of those elderly ladies and those others of middle age on witnessing this terrible destruction.

sn: रथनीडानि देहांश्च हतानां गजवाजिनाम्। आश्रित्य श्रममोहार्ताः स्थिताः पश्य महाभुज॥
en: See, O you of great might, those dames, exhausted with fatigue, are taking rest, supporting themselves against broken boxes of cars and the bodies of slain elephants and steeds.

sn: अन्यां चापहृतं कायाचारुकुण्डलमुन्नसम्। स्वस्य बन्धोः शिरः कृष्ण गृहीत्वा पश्य तिष्ठतीम्॥१०
en: See, O Krishna, taking up some relative's severed head adorned with beautiful nose and ear-rings, some one amongst them, is standing sorrowfully.

sn: पूर्वजातिकृतं पापं मन्ये नाल्पमिवानघ। एताभिर्निरवद्याभिर्मया चैवाल्पमेधया॥ यदिदं धर्मराजेन पातितं नो जनार्दन। न हि नाशोऽस्ति वार्ष्णेय कर्मणोः शुभपापयोः॥
en: I think, O sinless one, they and myself of little understanding must have perpetrated great iniquities in our previous lives, since, O Janarddana, all our relatives and kinsmen have thus been killed by king Yudhishthira. Our acts, fair or unfair, must bear fruits, O you of Vrishni's race.

sn: प्रत्यग्रवयसः पश्य दर्शनीयकुचाननाः। कुलेषु जाता ह्रीमत्यः कृष्णपक्ष्माक्षिमूर्धजाः॥ हंसगद्गदभाषिण्यो दुःखशोकप्रमोहिताः। सारस्य इव वाशन्त्यः पतिताः पश्य माधव॥
en: See, O Madhava, those young ladies having beautiful breasts and abdomen, born in respectable families, of great modesty, having black eye-lashes and tresses of the same color on their heads, having voice sweet and dear like that of swans, are falling down, unconscious from great grief and crying piteously like fights of cranes.

sn: फुल्लपद्यप्रकाशानि पुण्डरीकाक्ष योषिताम्। अनवद्यानि वक्त्राणि तापयत्येष रश्मिवान्॥
en: See, O lotus-eyed, hero, there beautiful faces resembling full-blown lotuses, scorched by the sun.

sn: ईर्पूणां मम पुत्राणां वासुदेवावरोधनम्। मत्तमातङ्गदर्याणां पश्यन्त्यद्य पृथग्जनाः॥
en: Alas, O Vasudeva, the wives of my proud children who were powerful like infuriate are elephants, are now being looked at by common people.

sn: शतचन्द्राणि चर्माणि ध्वजांचादित्यवर्चसः। रौक्माणि चैव वर्माणि निष्कानापि च काञ्चनान्॥ शीर्षत्राणानि चैतानि पुत्राणां मे महीतले। पश्य दीप्तानि गोविन्द पावकान् सुहुतानिव॥
en: See, O Govinda, the shields decked with hundred moons, the sunny standards, the golden coats of mail, and the golden collars and cuirasses, and the head-gears, of my sons, scattered on the Earth, are shining like sacrificial fires over which have been poured libation of clarified butter.

sn: एष दुःशासनः शेते शूरेणामित्रघातिना। पीतशोणितसर्वाङ्गो युधि भीमेन पातितः॥
en: There, Dusshasana sleep, killed by Bhima, having the blood of all his limbs drunk by that heroic slayer of foes.

sn: गदया भीमसेनेन पश्य माधव मे सुतम्। द्यूतक्केशाननुस्मृत्य द्रौपदीनोदितेन च॥
en: Look at that other son of mine, O Madhava, killed by Bhima with his mace, actuated by Draupadi and the memory of his woes at the time of the match at dice.

sn: उक्ता ह्यनेन पाञ्चाली सभायां द्यूतनिर्जिता। प्रियं चिकीर्षता भ्रातुः कर्णस्य च जनार्दन॥ सहैव सहदेवेन नकुलेनार्जुनेन च। दासीभूतासि पाञ्चालि क्षिप्रं प्रविश नो गृहान्॥
en: Addressing the princess of Panchala, in the midst of the assembly, who had been won by dice, this Dusshasana, desirous of pleasing his (elder) brother and Karna, O Janarddana, had said,-You are now the wife of a slave! With Sahadeva and Nakula and Arjuna, O lady, enter our household now.

sn: ततोऽहमब्रवं कृष्ण तदा दुर्योधनं नृपम्। मृत्युपाशपरिक्षिप्तं शकुनि पुत्र वर्जय॥
en: At that time, O Krishna, I sad to king Duryodhana,-O son, discard the wrathful Shakuni.

sn: निबोधैनं सुदुर्बुद्धिं मातुलं कलहप्रियम्। क्षिप्रमेनं परित्यज्य पुत्र शाम्यस्व पाण्डवैः॥
en: Know your maternal uncle to be very wicked and greatly fond of quarrel. Discard him forthwith and make peace with the Pandavas, O son.

sn: न बुद्ध्यसे त्वं दुर्बुद्धे भीमसेनममर्षणम्। वाड्नाराचैस्तुदंस्तीक्ष्णैरुल्काभिरिव कुञ्जरम्॥
en: O fool, do you not think of Bhimasena filled with anger. You are cutting him with your words arrows like a person striking an elephant with burning brands.

sn: तानेवं रहसि क्रुद्धो वाक्शल्यानवधारयन्। उत्ससर्ज विषं तेषु सर्पो गोवृषभेष्विव॥
en: Alas, neglecting my wordy, he vomited his poison of words at them, who had already been cut with wordy arrows, like a snake vomiting his poison at a bull.

sn: एष दुःशासनः शेते विक्षिप्य विपुलौ भुजौ। निहतो भीमसेनेन सिंहेनेव महागजः॥
en: there that Dusshasana sleeps stretching his tow massive arms, killed by Bhimasena like a powerful elephant by a lion.

sn: अत्यर्थमकरोद् रौद्रं भीमसेनोऽत्यमर्षणः। दुःशासनस्य यत् क्रुद्धोऽपिबच्छोणितमाहवे॥
en: The very angry Bhimasena perpetrated a most dreadful deed by drinking in battle the blood of his foes.

sn: गांधार्युवाच एष माधव पुत्रो मे विकर्णः प्राज्ञसम्मतः। भूमौ विनिहतः शेते भीमेन शतधा कृतः॥
en: Gandhari said There, O Madhava, my. son Vikarma, praised by the wise, lies on the naked earth, killed by Bhima and wounded horribly.

sn: गजमध्ये हतः शेते विकर्णो मधुसूदन। नीलमेघपरिक्षिप्तः शरदीव निशाकरः॥
en: O destroyer of Madhu, Vikarna lies there dead in the midst of (slain) elephants like the moon in the autumnal sky surrounded by blue clouds.

sn: अस्य चापग्रहेणैव पाणिः कृतकिणो महान्। कथञ्चिच्छिद्यते गृधेरत्तुकामैस्तलत्रवान्॥
en: His broad palm, covered with leathern fence, and scarred by constant holding of the bow, is pierced with difficulty by vultures desirous of eating it up.

sn: अस्य भार्याऽऽमिषप्रेप्सून् गृध्रकाकांस्तपस्विनी। वारयत्यनिशं बाला न च शक्नोति माधव॥
en: His helpless young wife, O Madhava, is continually but unsuccessfully trying to drive away those vultures desirous of feeding on carrion.

sn: युवा वृन्दारकः शूरो विकर्णः पुरुषर्षभ। सुखोषितः सुखार्हश्च शेते पांसुषु माधव॥
en: The youthful, brave and beautiful Vikarna, O foremost of men, reared in luxury and worthy of every king of happiness, now sleeps on dust, O Madhava.

sn: कर्णिनालीकनाराचैर्भिन्नमर्माणमाहवे। अद्यापि न जहात्येनं लक्ष्मीर्भरतसत्तमम्॥
en: Thought all his vital parts have been cut with cloth-yard and bearded arrows and Nalikas, yet the natural beauty of his body has not left this best of the Bharatas.

sn: एष संग्रामशूरेण प्रतिज्ञा पालयिष्यता। दुर्मुखोऽभिमुखः शेते हतोऽरिगणहा रणे॥
en: There, my son Durmuksha, that destroyer of a great number of enemies, sleeps facing the enemy, slain by the heroic Bhiinasena in satisfaction of his promisc.

sn: तस्यैतद् वदनं कृष्ण श्वापदैरर्धभक्षितम्। विभात्यभ्यधिकं तात सप्तम्यामिव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: His face, O Krishna, half eaten away by beasts of prey, looks more beautiful like the moon on the seventh day of the light fortnight.

sn: शूरस्य हि रणे कृष्ण पश्याननमथेदृशम्। स कथं निहतोऽमित्रैः पांसून् असति मे सुतः॥
en: Look, O Krishna at the face of that heroic son of mine. How could that son of mine be killed by enemies and thus made to eat the dust.

sn: यस्याहमुखे सौम्य स्थिता नैवोपपद्यते। स कथं दुर्मुखोऽमित्रैर्हतो विबुधलोकजित्॥
en: O amiable one, how could that Durmukha, before whom no enemy could stand be killed by foes.

sn: चित्रसेनं हतं भूमौ शयानं मधुसूदन। धार्तराष्ट्रमिमं पश्य प्रतिमानं धनुष्मताम्॥
en: Look, O slayer of Madhu, at that other son of Dhritarashtra, viz., Chitrasena, the best of all bowmen, slain and lying on the ground.

sn: तं चित्रमाल्याभरणं युवत्यः शोककर्शिताः। क्रव्यादसंघैः सहिता रुदत्यः पर्युपासते॥
en: Those young ladies, stricken with grief and crying piteously and now sitting, with beasts of prey, around his beautiful body bedecked with wreaths and garlands.

sn: स्त्रीणां रुदितनिर्घोषः श्वापदानां च गर्जितम्। चित्ररूपमिदं कृष्णं विचित्रं प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: The piteous lamentations of women, and these cries and roars of beasts of prey, appear highly wonderful to me, OKrishna.

sn: युवा वृन्दारको नित्यं प्रवरस्त्रीनिषेवितः। विर्विशतिरसौ शेते ध्वस्तः पांसुषु माधव॥
en: Young and beautiful, and always waited upon and served by the most handsome ladies, my son Vivinshati, O Madhava, sleeps there, covered with dust.

sn: शरसंकृत्तवर्माणं वीरं विशसने हतम्। परिवार्यासते गृध्राः पश्य कृष्ण विविंशतिम्॥
en: His armour has been cut with arrows. Killed in the general destruction, the heroic Vivingshati is now encircled and waited upon by vultures.

sn: प्रविश्य समरे शूरः पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्। स वीरशयने शेते परः सत्पुरुषोचिते॥
en: Having in battle penetrated the ranks of the Pandavas army, that hero now sleeps on the bed of a most exalted and heroic Kshatriya.

sn: स्मितोपपन्नं सुनसं सुभ्रु ताराधिपोपमम्। अतीव शुभ्रं वदनं कृष्ण पश्य विविंशतः॥
en: Look, O Krishna, at his very beautiful and smiling face, having excellent nose and beautiful eyebrows, and resembling the shining Moon himself.

sn: एनं हि पर्युपासन्ते बहुधा वरयोषितः। क्रीडन्तमिव गन्धर्वं देवकन्याः सहस्रशः॥
en: Formerly a body of the most beautiful ladies used to wait upon him, like thousands of celestial girls upon a sporting Gandharva.

sn: हन्तारं परसैन्यानां शूरं समितिशोभनम्। निबर्हणममित्राणां दुःसहं विषहेत कः॥
en: Who again could stand before my son Dussaha, that destroyer of heroic enemies, that hero, that ornament of assemblies, that irresistible warrior, that resister of foes.

sn: दुःसहस्यैतदाभाति शरीरं संवृतं शरैः। गिरिरात्मगतैः कुल्लैः कर्णिकारिवाचितः॥
en: The body of Dussaha, covered with shafts, shines like a mountain overgrown with blossoming Karnikaras.

sn: शातकौम्या स्रजा भाति कवचेन च भास्वता। अग्निवेव गिरिः श्वेतो गतासुरपि दुःसहः॥
en: With his golden garland and his bright armour, Dussaha, though dead, shines yet, like a white mountain of fire.

sn: गान्धार्युवाच अध्यर्धगुणमाहुर्यं बले शौर्ये च केशव। पित्रा त्वया च दाशार्ह दृप्तं सिंहमिवोत्कटम्। यो बिभेद चमूमेको मम पुत्रस्य दुर्भिदाम्। स भूत्वा मृत्युरन्येषां मम पुत्रस्य मृत्युवशं गतः॥
en: Gandhari said He whose power and bravery were regarded, O Keshava, as a one and half times superior to those of his father and you, he who took after a dreadful and proud, lion, he who alone pierced the impenetrable army of my son, he who killed many, alas, he now sleeps there, himself dead.

sn: तस्योपलक्षये कृष्ण काऎरमिततेजसः। अभिमन्योर्हतस्यापि प्रभा नैवोपशाम्यति॥
en: I see, O Krishna, the splendour of that son of Arjuna, of that great hero, viz., Abhimanyu, has not diminished even in death.

sn: एषा विराट दुहिता स्नुषा गाण्डीवधन्वनः। आर्ता बालं पति वीरं दृष्ट्या शोचत्यनिन्दिता॥
en: There, the daughter of Virata, the daughterin-law of Arjuna, that girl of faultless beauty, stricken with grief on seeing her heroic husband, is bewailing.

sn: तमेषा हि समागम्य भार्या भर्तारमन्तिके। विराटदुहिता कृष्ण पाणिना परिमार्जति॥
en: Approaching her husband, that young wife, viz., the daughter of Virata, is gently rubbing him, O Krishna, with her hand.

sn: तस्य वक्त्रमुपाघ्राय सौभद्रस्य मनस्विनी। विबुद्धकमलाकारं कम्बुवृत्तशिरोधरम्॥ काम्यरूपवती चैषा परिष्वजति भामिनी। लजमाना पुरा चैनं माध्वीकमदमूच्छिता॥
en: Formerly, that highly intelligent and beautiful girl, inebriate with honied wines, used bashfully to embrace her lord, and kiss and face of Subhadra's son, resembling a fullblown lotus and supported on a neck bearing three lines like those of a conch-shell.

sn: तस्य क्षतजसंदिग्धं जातरूपपरिष्कृतम्। विमुच्य कवचं कृष्ण शरीरमभिवीक्षते॥
en: Taking of her husband's golden armour, O hero, that damsel is now looking on the body of her husband covered with blood.

sn: अवेक्षमाणा तं बाला कृष्ण त्वामभिभाषते। अयं ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष सदृशाक्षो निपातितः॥
en: Beholding her lord, O Krishna, that girl addresses you saying:-'O lotus-eyed one, this hero whose eyes resembled yours, has been killed.

sn: बले वीर्यं च सदृशस्तेजसा चैव तेऽनघ। रूपेण च तथाप्यर्थं शेते भुवि निपातितः॥
en: In power, energy, and prowess, he has your equal, O sinless one! He resembled you very much in beauty. Yet he sleeps on the ground, killed by the enemy.

sn: अत्यन्तं सुकुमारस्य राङ्कवाजिनशायिनः। कचिदद्य शरीरं ते भूमौ न परितप्यते॥
en: Addressing her own husband, she says again,-'You were reared up in every luxury. You used to sleep on soft skins of the Ranku deer. Alas, does not your body feet pain to-day by lying thus on this naked Earth.

sn: मातङ्गभुजवर्माणौ ज्याक्षेपकठिनत्वचौ। काञ्चनाङ्गदिनौ शेते निक्षिप्य विपुलौ भुजौ॥ व्यायम्य बहुधा नूनं सुखसुप्तः श्रमादिव। एवं विलपतीमा न हि मामभिभाषसे॥
en: Stretching your massive arms decorated with golden Angadas, resembling a couple of elephants trunks, and trunks, and coated with skin hardened by constant use of the bow, sleep, you, O lord, peacefully as if worn out with the fatigue of too much exercise. Alas, why do you not speak to me that am weeping so?

sn: न स्मराम्यपराधं ते किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे। ननु मां त्वं पुरा दूरादभिवीक्ष्याभिभाषसे॥
en: I do not remember to have ever offered you. Why do you not speak to me then? Formerly, you used to addressed me even when you would see me at a distance.

sn: आर्यामार्य सुभद्रां त्वमिमांश्च त्रिदशोपमान्। पितॄन् मां चैव दुःखार्ता विहाय क्व गमिष्यसि॥
en: Where will you go, leaving behind you the much-respected Subhadra, these your sires who take after the very celestials, and my own wretched self distracted with grief.

sn: तस्य शोणितदिग्धान् वै केशानुद्यम्य पाणिना। उत्सङ्गे वक्त्रमाधाय जीवन्तमिव पृच्छति॥ स्वतीयं वासुदेवस्य पुत्रं गाण्डीवधन्वनः। कथं त्वां रणमध्यस्थं जनुरेते महारथाः॥
en: See, O Krishna, collecting with her hands the blood-dyed hair of her husband and placing his head on her lap, beautiful lady is addressing him as if he were alive,-How could those great car-warriors kill you in the midst of battle,-you who are the sister's son of Vasudeva and the son of the bolder of Gandiva?

sn: धिगस्तु क्रूरकृत्स्वान् कृपकर्णजयद्रथान्। द्रोणद्रौणायनी चोभौ यैरहं विधवा कृता॥
en: Alas, fie on those wicked warriors, Kripa, Karna, Jayadratha, Drona and Drona's son, by whom you were killed!

sn: रथर्षभाणां सर्वेषां कथमासीत् तदा मनः। बालं त्वां परिवार्येकं मम दुःखाय जनुषाम्॥
en: What did those great car-warriors think at that time when they surrounded you, a warrior of tender years, and killed you to my grief?

sn: कथं नु पाण्डवानां च पञ्चालानां तु पश्यताम्। त्वं वीर निधनं प्राप्तो नाथवान् सन्ननाथवत्॥
en: How could you, O hero, who had so many protectors, be killed so helplessly before the very eyes of the Pandavas and the Panchalas?

sn: दृष्ट्वा बहुभिराक्रन्दे निहतं त्वां पिता तवा वीरः पुरुषशार्दूलः कथं जीवति पाण्डवः॥
en: Seeing you, O hero, killed in battle by many warriors in a body, how is that foremost of men, that son of Pandu, viz., your father, able to bear the burden of life?

sn: न राज्यलाभो विपुलः शत्रूणां च पराभवः। प्रीतिं धास्यति पार्थानां त्वामृते पुष्करेक्षण॥
en: Neither the acquisition of a vast territory, nor the discomfitures of their foes, gives joy to the Parthas bereft of you, O lotus-eyed one.

sn: तव शस्त्रजिताँल्लोकान् धर्मेण च दमेन च। क्षिप्रमन्वागमिष्यामि तत्र मां प्रतिपालय॥
en: By the practice of virtue and self-restraint, I shall very soon go to those blissful regions which you have acquired by the use of weapons. Protect me, O hero, when I go there.

sn: दुर्मरं पुनरप्राप्ते काले भवति केनचित्। यदहं त्वां रणे दृष्ट्वा हतं जीवामि दुर्भगा॥
en: Until the appointed time comes, one cannot die, since, wretched that I am, I am still alive after seeing you killed in battle.

sn: कामिदानीं नरव्याघ्र श्लक्ष्णया स्मितया गिरा। पितृलोके समेत्यान्यां मामिवामन्त्रयिष्यसि॥
en: Having gone to the region of the departed manes, whom else, like me, do you address now, O foremost of men, in sweet and smiling words.

sn: नूनमप्सरसां स्वर्गे मनांसि प्रमथिष्यसि। परमेण च रूपेण गिरा च स्मितपूर्वया।॥
en: Forsooth, you will agitated the hearts of the Apsaras in heaven, with your great beauty and soft and smiling words.

sn: प्राप्य पुण्यकृताँल्लोकानप्सरोभिः समेयिवान्। सौभद्र विहरन् काले स्मेरथाः सुकृतानि मे॥
en: Having attained the regions reserved for pious persons, you are now united, O son of Subhadra, with the Apsaras. While playing with them, recollect now and then my good acts towards you.

sn: एतावानिह संवासो विहितस्ते मया सह। षण्मासान् सप्तमे मासि त्वं वीर निधनं गतः॥
en: Your union with me in this world had, it seems, been ordained for only six months, for on the seventh, O hero, you lost your life.

sn: इत्युक्तवचनामेतामपकर्षन्ति दुःखिताम्। उत्तरां मोघसंकल्पां मत्स्यराजकुलस्त्रियः॥
en: O Krishna, the ladies of the royal house of Matsya are dragging away the sorrowful Uttara, disappointed, and even lamenting in this way.

sn: उत्तरामपकृष्यैनामार्तामार्ततराः स्वयम्। विराटं निहतं दृष्ट्वा क्रोशन्ति विलपन्ति च॥
en: Dragging away the sorrow-stricken Uttara, those ladies, themselves still more aggrieved then that girl, are weeping and bewailing aloud at sight of the slain Virata.

sn: द्रोणास्त्रशरसंकृत्तं शयानं रुधिरोक्षितम्। विराटं वितुदन्त्येते गृध्रगोमायुवायसाः॥
en: Wounded with the weapons and arrows of Drona, lying down oi. earth, and bathed in blood, Virata is encompassed by the screaming vultures and yelling jackals and crows ravens.

sn: वितुद्यमानं विहगैर्विराटमसितेक्षणाः। न शक्नुवन्ति विहगान् निवारयितुमातुराः॥
en: Those black-eyed ladies, approaching the dead body of Matsya king over which carnivorous birds are uttering cries of joy, are trying to turn the body. Weakened by grief, they are unable to do what they wish.

sn: आसामातपतप्तानामायासेन च योषिताम्। श्रमेण च विवर्णानां वक्त्राणां विप्लुतं वपुः॥
en: Scorched by the Sun, and exhausted with fatigue and toil, their faces have become colourless and pale.

sn: उत्तरं चाभिमन्युं च काम्बोजं च सुदक्षिणम्। शिशूनेतान् हतान् पश्य लक्ष्मणं च सुदर्शनम्॥ आयोधनशिरोमध्ये शयानं पश्य माधव॥
en: See also, O Madhava, those other children besides Abhimanyu, viz., Uttara, Sudakshina the prince of the Kamvojas, and the beautiful Lakshmana, all lying on the field of battle.' Scorched by the Sun, and exhausted with fatigue and toil, their faces have become colourless and pale.

sn: उत्तरं चाभिमन्युं च काम्बोजं च सुदक्षिणम्। शिशूनेतान् हतान् पश्य लक्ष्मणं च सुदर्शनम्॥ आयोधनशिरोमध्ये शयानं पश्य माधव॥
en: See also, O Madhava, those other children besides Abhimanyu, viz., Uttara, Sudakshina the prince of the Kamvojas, and the beautiful Lakshmana, all lying on the field of battle.'

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: गान्धार्युवाच एष वैकर्तनः शेते महेष्वासो महारथः। ज्वलितानलवत् संख्ये संशान्तः पार्थतेजसा॥
en: Gandhari said There the powerful Karna, that great bowman, lies prostrate on the earth. In battle he was like a burning fire. That fire, however, has now been put out by the power of Partha.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: पश्य वैकर्तनं कर्णं निहत्यातिरथान् बहून्। शोणितौघपरीताङ्गं शयानं पतितं भुवि॥
en: See, Vikartana's son Karna, after having killed many Atirathas, has been prostrated on the naked Earth and is covered with blood.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: अमर्षी दीर्घरोषश्च महेष्वासो महाबलः। रणे विनिहतः शेते शूरो गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: Wrathful and energetic, he was a great bowman and a powerful car-warrior. Killed in battle by holder of Gandiva, that hero now sleeps on the ground.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: यं स्म पाण्डवसंत्रासान्मम पुत्रा महारथाः। प्रायुध्यन्त पुरस्कृत्य मातङ्गा इव यूथपम्॥
en: My sons, those powerful car-warriors, from fear of the Pandavas, fought, fled by Karna, like a heart of elephants with its leader standing first.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: शार्दूलमिव सिंहेन समरे सव्यसाचिना। मातङ्गमिव मत्तेन मातङ्गेन निपातितम्॥
en: Alas, like a tiger killed by a lion, or an elephant by an infuriate elephant, that warrior has been killed in battle by Savyasachin.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: समेताः पुरुषव्याघ्र निहतं शूरमाहवे। प्रकीर्णमूर्धजाः पत्न्यो रुदत्यः पर्युपासते॥
en: collected together, O foremost of men, the wives of that warrior, with disheveled hairs and loud cried of grief, and sitting around that fallen hero.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: उद्विग्नः सततं यस्माद् धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। त्रयोदश समा निद्रां चिन्तयन् नाध्यगच्छत॥
en: Anxious about that warrior, king Yudhishthira the just could not sleep for thirteen years.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: अनाधृष्यः परैयुद्धे शत्रुभिर्मघवानिव। युगान्ताग्निरिवार्चिष्मान् हिमवानिव निश्चलः॥
en: Incapable of being restrained by foes in battle like Indra himself who is invincible by enemies, Karna was like the all-destroying fire of dreadful flames at the end of a cycle, and immovable like Himavat himself.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: स भूत्वा शरणं वीरो धार्तराष्ट्रस्य माधव! भूमौ विनिहतः शेते वातभग्न इव द्रुमः॥
en: That hero became the protector of Dhritarashtra's son, O Madhava! Alas killed, he now lies on the bare ground, like a tree struck down by the wind.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: पश्य कर्णस्य पत्नीं त्वं वृषसेनस्य मातरम्। लालप्यमानां करुणं रुदतीं पतितां भुवि।॥
en: Behold, the wife of Karna and mother of Vrishasena, is bewailing piteously and crying and weeping and falling upon the ground.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: आचार्यशापोऽनुगतो ध्रुवं त्वां यदग्रसच्चक्रमिदं धरित्री। ततः शरेणापहृतं शिरस्ते धनंजयेनाहवशोभिना युधि॥
en: Even now she exclaims-Forsooth your preceptors' curse has followed you. When the wheel of your car was sunk in the Earth, the cruel Dhananjaya cut off your head with a shaft.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: हाहा धिगेषा पतिता विसंज्ञा समीक्ष्य जाम्बूनदबद्धकक्षम्। कर्णं महाबाहुमदीनसत्त्वं सुषेणमाता रुदती भृशार्ता॥
en: That lady, the mother of Sushena, greatly stricken with woe and uttering cries of woe, is falling down, unconscious at the sight of the mighty-armed and brave Karna prostrated on the Earth, with his waist still encircled with a golden belt.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: अल्पावशेषोऽपि कृतो महात्मा शरीरभक्षैः परिभक्षयद्भिः। द्रष्टुं न नः प्रीतिकरः शशीव कृष्णस्य पक्षस्य चतुर्दशाहे॥
en: Feasting on the body of that illustrious hero, carnivorous animals, have reduced it greatly. This spectacle is indeed pitiable, like that of the moon on the fourteenth night of the darkfortnight.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of Karna
sn: मुत्थाय दीना पुनरेव चैषा। कर्णस्य वक्त्रं परिजिघ्रमाणा रोरूयते पुत्रवधाभितप्ता॥
en: Falling down on the ground the cheerless lady is rising up again. Filled with grief for the death of her son also, she comes and smelleth the face of her husband.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: गान्धार्युवाच आवन्त्यं भीमसेनेन भक्षयन्ति निपातितम्। गृघ्रगोमायवः शूरं बहुबन्धुमबन्धुवत्॥
en: Gandhari said "See, killed by Bhimasena, the king of Avanti lies there. Vultures and jackals and crows are feasting upon that hero. Through possessed of many friends, he lies now perfectly helpless.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: तं पश्य कदनं कृत्वा शूराणां मधुसूदन। शयानं वीरशयने रुधिरेण समुक्षितम्॥ तं
en: See, O slayer of Madhu, having made a great onslaught of enemies, that warrior is now lying on the bed of a hero, bathed in blood.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: शृगालाश्च कङ्काश्च क्रव्यादाश्च पृथग्विधाः। तेन तेन विकर्षन्ति पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: Jackals, and Kankas, and other carnivorous animals of various kinds, are dragging him now. Mark the reverses caused by Time.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: शयानं वीरशयने शूरमाक्रन्दकारिणम्। आवन्त्यमभितो नार्यो रुदत्यः पर्युपासते॥
en: His wives, all are crying in grief, and sitting around that hero who while alive was a terrible slayer of enemies but who now lies on the bed of a hero.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: प्रातिपेयं महेष्वासं हतं भल्लेन बाह्निकम्। प्रसुप्तमिव शार्दूलं पश्य कृष्ण मनस्विनम्॥
en: See, Pratipa's son Valhika, that powerful and highly energetic bowman, slain with a broad-headed shaft, is now lying on the ground like a sleeping tiger.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: अतीव मुखवर्णोऽस्य निहतस्यापि शोभते। सोमस्येवाभिपूर्णस्य पौर्णमास्यां समुद्यतः॥
en: Though dead, the color of his face is still highly bright, like that of the full moon, risen on the fifteenth day of the light fortnight.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: पुत्रशोकाभितप्तेन प्रतिज्ञां चाभिरक्षता। पाकशासनिना संख्ये वार्धक्षत्रिनिपातितः॥
en: Burning with grief on account of the death of his son, and desirous of fulfilling his vow, Indra's son Arjuna has killed there that son of Vriddhakshatra.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: एकादश चमूर्भित्त्वा रक्ष्यमाणं महात्मना। सत्यं चिकीर्षता पश्य हतमेनं जयद्रथम्॥
en: Behold that Jayadratha, who was protected by the illustrious Drona, killed by Partha bent on making good his promise, after penetrating through eleven Akshauhinis of soldiers.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: सिन्धुसौवीरभर्तारं दर्पपूर्णं मनस्विनम्। भक्षयन्ति शिवा गृध्रा जनार्दन जयद्रथम्॥
en: Inauspicious vultures, O Janarddana, are feasting upon Jayadratha, the proud and energetic lord of the Sindhu-Sauviras.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: संरक्ष्यमाणं भार्याभिरनुरक्ताभिरच्युत। भीषयन्त्यो विकर्षन्ति गहनं निम्नमन्तिकात्॥
en: See, O Achyuta, carnivorous creatures are dragging his body away to a neighbouring jungle, though his devoted wives are trying to protect it.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: तमेताः पर्युपासन्ते रक्ष्यमाणं महाभुजम्। सिन्धुसौवीरभर्तारं काम्बो जयवनस्त्रियः॥
en: The Kamvoja and Yavana wives of that powerful king of the Sindhus and the Sauviras are waiting upon him for protecting his body.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: यदा कृष्णामुपादाय प्राद्रवत् केकयैः सह। तदैव वध्यः पाण्डूनां जनार्दन जयद्रथः॥
en: At that time, O Janarddana, when Jayadratha, assisted by the Kekayas, tried to ravish Draupadi, he should have been killed by the Pandavas.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: दुःशलां मानयद्भिस्तु तदा मुक्तो जयद्रथः। कथमद्य न तां कृष्ण मानयन्ति स्म ते पुनः॥
en: Out of respect, for Dusshala, they liberated him on that occasion. Why, O Krishna, did they not show some respect for that Dusshala once more.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: सैषा मम सुता बाला विलपन्ती च दुःखिता। आत्मना हन्ति चात्मानमाक्रोशन्ती च पाण्डवान्॥
en: That young daughter of mine, is now crying sorrowfully. She is striking her body with her own hands and blaming the Pandavas.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: किं नु दुःखतरं कृष्णं परं मम भविष्यति। यत् सुता विधवा बाला स्नुषाश्च निहतेश्वराः॥
en: What, O Krishna, can be a greater grief to me than that my young daughter should be a widow and all my daughters-in-law should equally be so.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: हा हा धिग् दुःशलां पश्य वीतशोकभयामिव। शिरो भर्तुरनासाद्य धावमानामितस्ततः॥
en: Alas, alas, see, my daughter Dusshala having cast off her grief and fears, is running about in search of the head of her husband.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: वारयामास यः सर्वान् पाण्डवान् पुत्रगृद्धिनः। स हत्वा विपुला: सेनाः स्वयं मृत्युवंश गतः॥
en: After killing a vast army, he who had restrained all the Pandavas desirous of rescuing their son, at last himself yielded to death.

description: Gandhari laments for the death of the king of Avanti
sn: तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं वीरं परमदुर्जयम्। परिवार्य रुदन्त्येताः स्त्रियश्चन्द्रोपमाननाः॥
en: Alas, those wives of his, with faces as beautiful as the moon, are crying, sitting around that irresistible hero who took after an infuriate elephant.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: गान्धार्युवाच एष शल्यो हतः शेते साक्षान्नकुलमातुल: धर्मज्ञेन हतस्तात धर्मराजेन संयुगे॥
en: Gandhari said There lies Shalya, the maternal uncle himself of Nakula, killed in battle, by the pious and virtuous Yudhishthira.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: यस्त्वया स्पर्धते नित्यं सर्वत्र पुरुषर्षभ। स एष निहतः शेते मद्रराजो महाबलः॥
en: He used everywhere, O foremost of men, to boast of his equality with you. That powerful car-warrior, viz., the king of the Madras, now lies dead.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: येन संगृह्णता तात रथमाधिरथेर्युधि। जयार्थं पाण्डुपुत्राणां तथा तेजोवधः कृतः॥
en: When he accepted the drivership of Karna's car in battle, he tried to depress Karna for securing victory for the sons of Pandu.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: अहो धिक्पश्य शल्यस्य पूर्णचन्द्रसुदर्शनम्। मुखं पद्मपलाशाक्षं काकैरादष्टमव्रणम्॥
en: Alas, alas, look at the smooth face of Shalya, beautiful as the moon, and having eyes resembling lotus petals, eaten away by crows.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: अस्य चामीकराभस्य तप्तकाञ्चनसप्रभा। आस्याद् विनिः सृता जिह्वा भक्ष्यते कृष्ण पक्षिभिः॥५
en: There, the tongue of that king, beautiful like molten gold, looting out of his mouth, is, O। Krishna, being devoured by carnivorous birds.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: युधिष्ठिरेण निहतं शल्यं समितिशोभनम्। रुदत्यः पर्युपासन्ते मद्रराजं कुलाङ्गनाः॥
en: the ladies of the royal house of Madra, crying aloud, are sitting around the body of that king, that ornament of assemblies, killed by Yudhishthira.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: एताः सुसूक्ष्मवसना मद्रराजं नरर्षभम्। क्रोशन्त्योऽथ समासाद्य क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रियर्षभम्॥ शल्यं निपतितं नार्यः परिवार्याभितः स्थिताः। वासिता गृष्टयः पङ्के परिमग्नमिव द्विपम्॥
en: Those ladies are sitting around that fallen hero like a herd of she-elephants in their season around their leader sunk in mud.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: शल्यं शरणदं शूरं पश्येमं वृष्णिनन्दन। शयानं वीरशयने शरैर्विशकलीकृतम्॥
en: Look at the brave Shalya, the great protector and the foremost of car-warriors, stretched on the bed of heroes, his body wounded with arrows.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: एष शैलालयो राजा भगदत्तः प्रतापवान्। गजाङ्कुशधरः श्रीमाशेते भुवि निपातितः॥
en: There the highly powerful king Bhagadatta, the king of a mountainous kingdom, the foremost of all holders of good, lies dead on the Earth.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: यस्य रुक्ममयी माला शिरस्येषा विराजते। श्वापदैर्भक्ष्यमाणस्य शोभयन्तीव मूर्धजान्॥
en: Look at the golden and shining garland that he still wears on his head. Though the body is being devoroured by beasts of prey, that garland still adorns the beautiful hairs on his head.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: एतेन किल पार्थस्य युद्धमासीत् सुदारुणम्। रोमहर्षणमत्युग्रं शक्रस्य त्वहिना यथा॥
en: Dreadful was the battle that took place between this king and Partha, making the hairs stand erect, like that between Shakra and the Asura Vritra.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: योधयित्वा महाबाहुरेष पार्थं धनंजयम्। संशयं गमयित्वा च कुन्तीपुत्रेण पातितः॥
en: Having fought Dhananjaya ine son of Pritha, and brought him to a perilous condition,। this mighty-armed one, was at last killed by his antagonist.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: यस्य नास्ति समो लोके शौर्ये वीर्ये च कश्चन। स एष निहतः शेते भीष्मो भीष्मकृताहवे॥
en: He who had no equal on Earth in heroism and energy, that achiever of dreadful feasts in battle, viz., Bhishma, lies there dead.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: पश्य शान्तनवं कृष्ण शयानं सूर्यवर्चसम्। युगान्त इव कालेन पतितं सूर्यमम्बरात्॥
en: Behold the son of Shantanu, O Krishna, that hero effulgent like the sun, stretched on the Earth, like the Sun himself dropped off the sky at the end of the Yuga.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: एष तप्त्वा रणे शत्रूशस्त्रतापेन वीर्यवान्। नरसूर्योऽस्तमभ्येति सूर्योऽस्तमिव केशव॥
en: Having scorched his enemies with the fire of his weapons in battle, that brave warrior, that Sun among men, O Keshava, has set like the real Sun at evening.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: शरतल्पगतं भीष्ममूर्ध्वरेतसमच्युतम्। शयानं वीरशयने पश्य शूरनिषेविते॥
en: Look at that hero, O Krishna, who in knowledge of duty was equal to Devapi himself, now lying on a bed of arrows, worthy of heroes.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: कर्णिनालीकनाराचैरास्तीर्य शयनोत्तमम्। आविश्य शेते भगवान् स्कन्दः शरवणं यथा॥
en: Having spread his bed of barbed and unbarbed arrows, that hero lieth on it like Skanda on a clump of reeds.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: अतूलपूर्ण गाङ्गेयस्त्रिभिर्बाणैः समन्वितम्। उपधायोपधानाग्रयं दत्तं गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: Indeed, the son of Ganga lies there, resting his head on that excellent pillow, consisting of three arrows,-given him by Arjuna.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: पालयानः पितुः शास्त्रमूर्ध्वरेता महायशाः। एष शान्तनवः शेते माधवप्रतिमो युधि॥
en: For obeying the mandate of his father, this illustrious one drew up his vital seed. Peerless in battle, that son of Shantanu lies there, O Madhava.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: धर्मात्मा तात सर्वज्ञः पारावर्येण निर्णये। अमर्त्य इव मर्त्यः सन्नेष प्राणानधारयत्॥
en: Pious and acquainted with all forms of duty, by the help of his knowledge of both the worlds, that hero, though mortal, is still alive like an immortal.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: नास्ति युद्धे कृती कश्चिन्न विद्वान् न पराक्रमी। यत्र शान्तनवो भीष्मः शेतेऽद्य निहतः शरैः॥
en: When Shantanu's son lies to-day, struck down with arrows, it seems that no other person alive on Earth who is learned and powerful and who is competent to perform great feats in battle.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: स्वयमेते शूरेण पृच्छ्यमानेन पाण्डवैः। धर्मज्ञेनाहवे मृत्युरादिष्टःसत्यवादिना॥
en: Solicited by the Pandavas, this truthful, righteous, and virtuous hero, communicate to them the means of his own death.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: प्रणष्टः कुरुवंशश्च पुनर्येन समुद्धृतः। स गतः कुरुभिः सार्धं महाबुद्धिः पराभवम्॥
en: Alas, he who had revived the extinct line of Kuru, that illustrious and highly intelligent person, has left the world with all the Kurus in his company.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: कं नु परिप्रक्ष्यन्ति माधव। गते देवव्रते स्वर्ग देवकल्पे नरर्षभे॥
en: From whom, O Madhava, will the Kurus, receive instructions of religion and duty after that foremost of men, viz., Devavrata, who resembles a god, shall have gone to heaven?

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: अर्जुनस्य विनेतारमाचार्यं सात्यकेस्तथा। तं पश्य पतितं द्रोणं कुरूणां गुरुमुत्तमम्॥
en: See Drona, that best of Brahmanas, that preceptor of Arjuna, of Satyaki, and of the Kurus, is lying on the ground.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: अस्त्रं चतुर्विधं वेद यथैव त्रिदशेश्वरः। भार्गवो वा महावीर्यस्तथा द्रोणोऽपि माधव॥
en: The highly energetic Drona, O Madhava, was as a master of the four kinds of arms like Shukra of Vrigu's race.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: यस्य प्रसादाद् बीभत्सुः पाण्डव: कर्म दुष्करम्। चकार स हतः शेते नैनमस्त्राण्यपालयन्॥ धर्मेषु कुरवः
en: Through his favour, Vibhatsu the son of Pandu has achieved the most of difficult feats. He now lies dead on the ground. Weapons refused to come at last at his command.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: यं पुरोधाय कुरव आह्वयन्ति स्म पाण्डवान्। सोऽयं शस्त्रभृतां श्रेष्ठो द्रोणः शस्त्रैः परिक्षतः॥
en: Placing him at their head, the Kauravas had challenged the Pandavas. That foremost of all warriors was in the end wounded with weapons.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: यस्य निर्दहतः सेनां गतिरग्नेरिवाभवत्। स भूमौ निहतः शेते शान्तार्चिरिव पावकः॥
en: As he moved about in battle, scorching his enemies in every direction, his movement resembled that of a blazing fire. Alas, he now lies dead on the ground, like an extinguished fire.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: धनुर्मुष्टिरशीर्णश्च हस्तावापश्च माधव। द्रोणस्य निहतस्याजौ दृश्यते जीवतो यथा॥
en: The handle of the bow is yet in his grasp, The leathern fences, O Madhava, pre still on his fingers. Though killed, he still looks as if alive.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: वेदा यस्माच चत्वारः सर्वाण्यस्त्राणि केशव। अनपेतानि वै शूराद् यथैवादौ प्रजापतैः॥
en: The four Vedas, and all kinds, of weapons, O Keshava, did not leave that hero even as they do not the Lord Prajapati.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: वन्दनार्हविमौ तस्य बन्दिभिर्वन्दितौ शुभौ। गोमायवो विकर्षन्ति पादौ शिष्यशतार्चितौ॥
en: His auspicious feet, worthy of adoration and adored before by bards and eulogists, and worshipped by disciples, are now being dragged by jackals.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: द्रोणं दुपदपुत्रेण निहतं मधुसूदन। कृपी कृपणमन्वास्ते दुःखोपहतचेतना॥
en: Senseless with sorrow, Kripi sorrowfully attends, O destroyer of Madhu, on that Drona who has been killed by Draupada's son.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: तां पश्य रुदतीमार्ता मुक्तकेशीमधोमुखीम्। हतं पतिमुपासन्ती द्रोणं शस्त्रभृतां वरम्॥
en: Look at that sorrow-stricken lady, fallen upon the Earth, with disheveled hair and face Juser hanging down. Alas, she serves sorrowfully her lifeless husband, that best of all holders of weapons, lying on the ground.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: बाणैर्भिन्नतनुत्राणं धृष्टद्युम्नेन केशव। उपास्ते वै मृधे द्रोणं जटिला ब्रह्मचारिणी॥
en: Many Brahmana saints, with matted locks on their head, are serving the body of Drona that is cased in armour cut asunder, O Keshava, with the arrows of Dhrishtadyumna.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: प्रेतकृत्यं च यतते कृपी कृपणमातुरा। हतस्य समरे भर्तुः सुकुमारी यशस्विनी॥
en: The illustrious and delicate Kripi, depressed and Sorrow-stricken, is trying to perform the last rites on the body of her husband killed in battle.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: अग्नीनाधाय विधिवञ्चितां प्रज्वाल्य सर्वतः। द्रोणमाधाय गायन्ति त्रीणि सामानि सामगाः॥
en: There, having placed the body of Drona on the funeral pyre and having put fire with due rites, those reciters of Samans are singing the three verses.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: कुर्वन्ति च चितामेते जटिला ब्रह्मचारिणः। धनुभिः शक्तिभिश्चैव रथनीडैश्च माधव॥
en: Those Brahmana saints, with matted locks on their head, have made the funeral pyre of that Brahmana with bows and arrows and carboxes, O Madhava.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: शरैश्च विविधैरन्यैर्धक्ष्यते भूरितेजसम्। इति द्रोणं समाधाय शंसन्ति च रुदन्ति च॥
en: Having collected various other sorts of arrows, that highly energetic hero is being consumed by them. Having placed his body on the pyre, they are singing and weeping.

description: Gandhari laments the death of Shalya
sn: सामभिस्त्रिभिरन्तस्थैरनुशंसन्ति चापरे। अग्नावग्निं समाधाय द्रोणं हुत्वा हुताशने॥ गच्छन्त्यभिमुखा गङ्गां द्रोणशिष्या द्विजातयः। अपसव्यां चितिं कृत्वा पुरस्कृत्य कृपी च ते॥
en: Others are reciting the three well-known Saman verses that are used on such occasions. Burning the dead body of Drona on that fire, like fire in fire, those saintly disciples of his, are proceeding towards the banks of Ganga, along the left side of the pyre and having placed Kripi at their head."

sn: गान्धार्युवाच सोमदत्तसुतं पश्य युयुधानेन पातितम्। विद्युतमानं विहगैर्बहुभिर्माधवान्तिके॥
en: Gandhari said See the son of Somadatta, who was killed by Yuyudhana, is being cut by a large number of birds.

sn: पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तः सोमदत्तो जनार्दन। युयुधानं महेष्वासं गर्हयन्निव दृश्यते॥
en: Burning with sorrow at the death of his son, Somadatta, O Janarddana, seems to blame the great bowman Yuyudhana.

sn: असौ हि भूरिश्रवसो माता शोकपरिप्लुता। आश्वासयति भर्तारं सोमदत्तमनिन्दिता॥ दिष्ट्या नैनं महाराज दारुणं भरतक्षयम्। कुरुसंक्रन्दनं घोरं युगान्तमनुपश्यसि॥
en: There the mother of Bhurishravas that faultless lady, beside herself with grief, is addressing her lord Somadatta, saying,-By good luck, O king, you do not witness this terrible destruction of the Bharatas, this extermination of the Kurus, this sight resembling the spectacles occurring at the end of a cycle.

sn: दिष्ट्या यूपध्वजं पुत्रं वीरं भूरिसहस्रदम्। अनेकक्रतुयज्वानं निहतं नानुपश्यसि॥
en: By good luck, you do not see your heroic, son, who bore the device of the sacrificial stake on his banner and who celebrated numberless sacrifices with profuse presents to all, killed on the field of battle.

sn: दिष्ट्या स्नुषाणामाक्रन्दे घोरं विलपितं बहु। न शृणोषि महाराज सारसीनामिवार्णवे॥
en: By good luck, you do not hear those dreadful wails of woe uttered amidst this destruction by your daughter-in-law like the screams of a fight of cranes of the sea.

sn: एकवस्त्रार्धसंवीताः प्रकीर्णासितमूर्धजाः। स्नुषास्ते परिधावन्ति हतापत्या हतेश्वराः।। :॥
en: Your daughters-in-law, deprived of both husbands and sons, are running about, each clad in a single piece of cloth and each with her clad in a single piece of cloth and each with her black hairs all disheveled.

sn: श्वापदैर्भक्ष्यमाणं त्वमहो दिष्ट्या न पश्यसि। छिन्नबाहुं नरव्याघ्रमर्जुनेन निपातितम्॥
en: By good luck, you do not see to-day your son, that foremost of men, deprived of one of his arms, killed by Arjuna, and now being devoured by beasts of prey.

sn: शलं विनिहतं संख्ये भूरिश्रवसमेव च। स्नुषाश्च विविधाः सर्वा दिष्ट्या नाद्येह पश्यसि॥
en: By good luck, you do not see to-day your son Shala killed in battle, and Bhurishravas deprived of life, and your widowed daughterin-law plunged into grief.

sn: दिष्ट्या तत् काञ्चनं छत्रं यूपकेतोर्महात्मनः। विनिकीर्णं रथोपस्थे सौमदत्तेर्न पश्यसि॥
en: By good luck, you do not see the golden umbrella of that illustrious hero who had the sacrificial stake as his emblem on his banner, torn and broken on the terrace of his car.

sn: अमूस्तु भूरिश्रवसो भार्याः सात्यकिना हतम्। परिवार्यानुशोचन्ति भर्तारमसितेक्षणाः॥
en: There the black-eyed wives of Bhurishravas are bewailing piteously surrounding their lord killed by Satyaki.

sn: एता विलय करुणं भर्तृशोकेन कर्शिताः। पतन्त्यभिमुखा भूमौ कृपणं वत केशव॥
en: Stricken with sorrow on account of the slaughter of their husband, those ladies bewailing piteously, are falling down on the Earth with their faces toward the ground, and slowly approaching you, O Keshava!

sn: बीभत्सुरतिबीभत्सं कर्मेदमकरोत् कथम्। प्रमत्तस्य यदच्छत्सीद् बाहुं शूरस्य यज्वनः॥
en: Alas, why did Arjuna of pure deeds commit such a heinous crime, since he cut off the arm of a heedless warrior who was brave and used to perform sacrifices.

sn: ततः पापतरं कर्म कृतवानपि सात्यकिः। यस्मात् प्रायोविष्टस्य प्राहार्षीत् संशितात्मनः॥
en: Alas, Satyaki perpetrated a still more sinful act, for he killed a person of restrained soul while sitting in the observance of the praya VOW.

sn: एको द्वाभ्यां हतः शेषे त्वमधर्मेण धार्मिक। किं नु वक्ष्यति वै सत्सु गोष्ठीषु च सभासु च॥
en: Alas, O righteous one, you are lying on the ground, killed unfairly by two foes. Thus, O Madhava, those wives of Bhurishravas are crying aloud in sorrow.

sn: अपुण्यमयशस्यं च कर्मेदं सात्यकिः स्वयम्। इति यूपध्वजस्यैताः स्त्रियः क्रोशन्ति माधव॥ भार्या यूपध्वजस्यैषा करसम्मितमध्यमा। कृत्वोत्सङ्गे भुजं भर्तुः कृपणं परिदेवति॥
en: There, those wives of that warrior, all having slender waists, are placing upon their laps the cut off arm of their husband and weeping bitterly. Here is that arm which used to attack the girdles, grind the deep bosoms and touch the navel, the thighs, and the hips, of fair ladies, and loosen the ties of the drawers worn by them.

sn: अयं स हन्ता शूराणां मित्राणाप्रभयप्रदः। प्रदाता गोसहस्राणां क्षत्रियान्तकरः करः॥
en: Here is that arm which killed enemies and dispelled the fears of friends, which gave thousands of kine and rotted out the Kshatriyas in battle.

sn: वासुदेवस्य सांनिध्ये पार्थेनालिष्टकर्मणा। युध्यतः समरेऽन्येन प्रमत्तस्य निपातितः॥
en: In the presence of Vasudeva himself, Arjuna of pure deeds cut it off while you were heedless and engaged with another in battle.

sn: किं नु वक्ष्यासि संसत्सु कथासु च जनार्दन। अर्जुनस्य महत् कर्म स्वयं वा स किरीटभृत्॥ इत्येवं गर्हयित्वैषा तूष्णीमास्ते वराङ्गना तामेतामनुशोचन्ति सपत्न्यः स्वामिव स्नुषाम्॥
en: How will you, O Janarddana, describe this great fear of Arjuna while speaking of it in the midst of assemblies. What also will the diadem-decked Arjuna himself say of it?-Censuring you in this way, that best of ladies nas stopped at last. The co-wives of that lady are lamenting piteously with her as if she wee their daughter-in-law.

sn: गान्धारराजः शकुनिर्बलवान् सत्यविक्रमः। निहतः सहदेवेन भागिनेयेन मातुलः॥
en: There the powerful Shakuni, the king of the Gandharas, having irresistible prowess, has been killed by Sahadeva, the maternal uncle by the sister's son.

sn: यः पुरा हेमदण्डाभ्यां व्यजनाभ्यां स्म वीज्यते। स एष पक्षिभिः पक्षैः शयान उपवीज्यते॥
en: Formerly, he used to be fanned with a two gold-handed fans. Alas, now, his boy lunging on the ground is being fanned by birds with their wings.

sn: यः स्वरूपाणि कुरुते शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। तस्य मायाविनो माया दग्धाः पाण्डवतेजसा॥
en: He used to assume hundreds and thousands of forms. All the illusions, however, of that man possessed of great illusory powers, have been burnt by the energy of the son of Pandu.

sn: मायया निकृतिप्रज्ञो जितवान् यो युधिष्ठिरम्। सभायां विपुलं राज्य स पुनजीवितं जितः॥
en: Highly wily, he had defeated Yudhishthira in the assembly by his power of deception and won from him his vast kingdom. The son of Pandu, however, has now conquered Shakuni's life-breaths.

sn: शकुन्ताः शकुनि कृष्ण समन्तात् पर्युपासते। कैतवं मम पुत्राणां विनाशायोपशिक्षितम्॥
en: Look, O Krishna, a number of birds is not sitting around Shakuni. An expert in dice, alas, he had also mastered the means for the destruction of my sons.

sn: एतेनैतन्महद् वैरं प्रसक्तं पाण्डवैः सह। वधाय मम पुत्राणामात्मनः सगणस्य च॥
en: This fire of hostility with the Pandavas had been lighted by Shakuni, for the destruction of my children as also of himself and his followers ar relatives.

sn: यथैव ममत्राणां लोका: शस्त्रजिताः प्रभो। एवमस्यापि दुर्बुद्धेर्लोकाः शस्त्रेण वै जिताः॥
en: Like those gained by my sons, O powerful one, by the use of arms, this man too, however wicked-souled, has obtained many blissful regions by the use of weapons.

sn: कथं च नायं तत्रापि पुत्रान्मे भ्रातृभिः सह। विरोधयेदृजुप्रज्ञाननृजुर्मधुसूदन॥
en: My fear, O destroyer of Madhu, is that wily man may not create dissensions even there between my children all of whom are simple and confiding.

sn: गान्धार्युवाच काम्बोजं पश्य दुर्धर्षं काम्बोजास्तरणोचितम्। शयानमृषभस्कन्धं हतं पांसुषु माधव॥
en: Gandhari said Behold that irresistible king of Kambojas, that bull-necked hero lying in the dust, O Madhava, though worthy of sleeping comfortable on Kamboja blankets.

sn: यस्य क्षतजसंदिग्घौ बाहू चन्दनभूषितौ। अवेक्ष्य करुणं भार्या विलपत्यतिदुःखिता॥
en: Stricken with great sorrow, his wife is weeping bitterly at sight of his arms covered with blood, which, however, formerly used to be smeared with sandal-paste.

sn: इमौ तौ परिघप्रख्यौ बाहू शुभतलाङ्गुली। ययोर्विवरमापन्नां न रतिर्मा पुराजहात्॥
en: Indeed, the beautiful lady exclaims,-Even now adorned with beautiful palms and fingers, these two arins of yours resemble a couple of spiked maces, entering into whose clasp joy never felt me for a moment.

sn: कां गतिं तु गमिष्यामि त्वया हीना जनेश्वर। हतबन्धुरनाथा च वेपन्ती मधुरस्वरा॥
en: How shall I fare, O king, when I am deprived of you.-Possessing a sweet voice, the Kamvoja queen is weeping helplessly and trembling with emotion.

sn: आतपे लाम्यमानानां विविधानामिव स्रजाम्। कान्तानामपि नारीणां श्रीर्जहाति न वै तनूः॥
en: Look at that bevy of fair ladies there. Although tired with toil and worn out with heat, yet beauty does not leave them like the beauty of the garlands worn by the celestials although exposed to the Sun.

sn: शयानमभितः शूरं कालिङ्गं मधुसूदन। पश्य दीप्ताङ्गदयुगप्रतिनद्धमहाभुजम्॥
en: Behold, O destroyer of Madhu, the heroic king of the Kalingas lying there on the ground, with his mighty arms bedecked with a couple of Angadas.

sn: मागधानामधिपति जयत्सेनं जनार्दन। आवार्यं सर्वतः पत्न्यः प्ररुदत्यः सुविह्वलाः॥
en: Behold, O Janarddana, those Magadha ladies crying and standing around Jayastsena the king of the Magadhas.

sn: आसामायतनेत्राणां सुस्वराणां जनार्दन। मनःश्रुतिहरो नादो मनो मोहयतीव मे॥
en: The charming and sweet cries of those large-eyed and sweet-voiced damsels, O Krishna, are stupefying my heart greatly.

sn: प्रकीर्णवस्त्राभरणा रुदत्यः शोककर्शिताः। स्वास्तीर्णशयनेपिता मागध्यः शेरते भुवि॥
en: Having all their ornaments displaced, crying, and stricken with sorrow, alas, those ladies of Magadha, worthy of sleeping on costly beds, are now lying down on the naked earth.

sn: कोसलानामधिपतिं राजपुत्रं बृहद्बलम्। भर्तारं परिवार्यताः पृथक् प्ररुदिताः स्त्रियः॥
en: Surrounding their lord, the king of the Kosalas, viz., prince Vrihadvala, those other ladies are crying aloud.

sn: अस्य गात्रगतान् बाणान् कार्णिबाहुबलार्पितान्। उद्धरन्त्यसुखाविष्टा मूर्छमानाः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Engaged in taking out from his person the with which it was pierced by Abhimanyu with the full force of his arms, those ladies are again and again losing their consciousness.

sn: आसां सर्वानवद्यानामातपेन परिश्रमात्। प्रम्लाननलिनाभानि भान्ति वक्त्राणि माधव॥
en: The faces of those beautiful damsels, O Madhava, exhausted with toil and scorched by thc rays of the Sun, are appearing like faded lotuses.

sn: द्रोणेन निहताः शूराः शेरते रुचिराङ्गदाः। धृष्टद्युम्नसुताः सर्वे शिशवो हेममालिनः॥
en: arrows There, the brave sons of Dhrishtadyurnna, young in age, and bedecked with garlands of gold and beautiful Angadas, are lying, killed by Drona.

sn: रथाग्न्यगारं चापार्चिःशरशक्तिगदेन्धनम्। द्रोणमासाद्य निर्दग्धाः शलभा इव पावकम्॥
en: Like insects on a burning fire, they have all been consumed by falling upon Drona whose car was the chamber of fire, having the bow for its flames and arrows and darts and maces for its fuel.

sn: तथैव निहताः शूराः शेरते रुचिराङ्गदाः। द्रोणेनाभिमुखाः सर्वे भ्रातरः पञ्च केकयाः॥
en: Likewise, the five brave Kekaya brothers, adorned with beautiful Angadas, are lying on effort killed by Drona and with their faces turned towards that hero.

sn: तप्तकाञ्चनवर्माणस्तालध्वजरथव्रजाः। भासयन्ति महीं भासा ज्वलिता इव पावकाः॥
en: Their coats of mail, stinging like molten gold, and their tall standards and cars and garlands all made of gold, are shedding a bright lustre on the Earth like so many burning fires.

sn: द्रोणेन दुपदं संख्ये पश्य माधव पातितम्। महाद्विपमिवारण्ये सिंहेन महता हतम्॥
en: Look, O Madhava, at king Drupada overthrown in battle by Drona, like mighty elephant in the forest killed by a huge lion.

sn: पाञ्चालराज्ञो विमलं पुण्डरीकाक्ष पाण्डुरम्। आतपत्रं समाभाति शरदीव निशाकरः॥
en: The bright and white umbrella, of the king of the Panchalas, shines, O lotus-eyed one, like the moon in the autumnal sky.

sn: एतास्तु द्रुपदं वृद्धं स्नुषा भार्याश्च दुःखिताः। दग्ध्वा गच्छन्ति पाञ्चाल्यं राजानमपसव्यतः॥
en: Having burnt his body on the funeral pyre, the daughter-in-law and the wives of the old king, stricken with sorrow, are proceeding, keeping the pyre to their right.

sn: धृष्टकेतुं महात्मानं चेदिपुङ्गवमङ्गनाः। द्रोणेन निहतं शूरं हरन्ति हतचेतसः॥
en: There, those ladies, beside themselves with sorrow, are removing the brave and great bowman, viz., Dhrishtaketu, that foremost of the Chedis, killed by Drona.

sn: द्रोणास्त्रमभिहत्यैष विमर्दे मधुसूदन। महेष्वासो हतः शेते नद्या हत इव दुमः॥
en: Having counteracted many weapons of Drona, this destroyer of foes, O slayer of Madhu, this great bowman lies there, dead, like a tree uprooted by the wind.

sn: एष चेदिपतिः शूरो धृष्टकेतुर्महारथः। शेते विनिहतः संख्ये हत्वा शत्रून् सहस्रशः॥
en: After having slain thousands of enemies, that brave king of the Chedis, that mighty carwarrior, viz., Dhrishtaketu lies, himself deprived of life.

sn: वितुद्यमानं विहगैस्तं भार्याः पर्युपासिताः। चेदिराजं हृषीकेश हतं सबलबान्धवम्॥
en: There, O Hrishikesha, the wives of the king of the Chedis are sitting around his body still decked with beautiful hairs and ear-rings, though torn by carnivorous birds.

sn: दाशा_पुत्रजं वीरं शयानं सत्यविक्रमम्। आरोप्याङ्के रुदन्त्येताश्चेदिराजवराङ्गनाः॥
en: Placing upon their laps and prostrate form of the heroic Dhrishtaketu of Dasharha race, those foremost of ladies, are crying in sorrow.

sn: अस्य पुत्रं हृषीकेश सुवक्त्रं चारुकुण्डलम्। द्रोणेन समरे पश्य निकृतं बहुधा शरैः॥
en: Behold, O Hrishikesha, the son of that Dhrishtaketu, having fair locks and excellent car-rings, cut in battle by Drona with his arrows.

sn: पितरं नूनमाजिस्थं युद्ध्यमानं परैः सह। नाजहात् पितरं वीरमद्यापि मधुसूदन॥
en: He never deserted his father while the latter fought with his enemies. Mark, O destroyer of Madhu, he does not, even in death, leave the side of that heroic father.

sn: एवं ममापि पुत्रस्य पुत्रः पितरमन्वगात्। दुर्योधनं महाबाहो लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा॥
en: Thus. also, my grandson, that slayer of hostile heroes, viz., the mighty-armed Lakshmana, has followed his father Duryodhana.

sn: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ पतितौ पश्य माधव। हिमान्ते पुष्पितौ शालौ मरुता गलिताविव॥ ये
en: Look, O Keshava, at the two brothers of Avanti, viz., Vinda and Anuvinda, lying their on the fled, like two blossoming Shala trees in the spring uprooted by the wind.

sn: काञ्चनाङ्गदवर्माणौ बाणखड्गधनुर्धरौ। ऋषभप्रतिरूपाक्षौ शयानौ विमलस्रजौ॥
en: Clad in golden armour and bedecked with golden Angadas, they are still armed with swords and bows. Having eyes like those of a bull, and decked with shining garlands, both of them are lying on the field.

sn: अवध्याः पाण्डवाः कृष्ण सर्व एव त्वया सह। मुक्ता द्रोणभीष्माभ्यां कर्णाद् वैकर्तनात् कृपात्॥३० दुर्योधनाद् द्रोणसुतात् सैन्धवाच्च जयद्रथात्। सोमदत्ताद् विकर्णाच शूराच कृतवर्मणः॥
en: The Pandavas, O Krishna, as well as yourself, are surely unslayable, since they are you have escaped from Drona, Bhishma, Karna the son of Vikartana, Kripa, Duryodhana, the of son Drona, the mighty car-warrior Jayadratha, Somadatta, Vikarna, and from the brave Kritavarman.

sn: ये हन्युः शस्त्रवेगेन देवानपि नरर्षभाः। त इमे निहताः संख्ये पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: Mark the reverses created by Time. Those leading warriors who could slay the very celestials by force of their arms have themselves been killed.

sn: नातिभारोऽस्ति दैवस्य ध्रुवं माधव कश्चन। यदिमे निहताः शूराः क्षत्रियैः क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥
