en: forsooth, O Madhava, there is nothing difficult for destiny to bring about, since these leading men, these heroes, have been killed by Kshatriya warriors!

sn: तदैव निहताः कृष्ण मम पुत्रास्तरस्विनः। यदैवाकृतकामस्त्वमुपप्लव्यं गतः पुनः॥
en: I considered by energetic sons as slain even then, O Krishna, when you came back unsuccessful to Upaplavya!

sn: शान्तनोश्चैव पुत्रेण प्राज्ञेन विदुरेण च। तदैवोक्तास्मि मा स्नेहं कुरुष्वात्मसुतेष्विति॥
en: Shantanu's son and wise Vidura told me then, — withdraw your love for your children.

sn: तयोहि दर्शनं नैतन्मिथ्या भवितुमर्हति। अचिरेणैव मे पुत्रा भस्मीभूता जनार्दन॥
en: The interviews of those persons could never be useless. Soon, O Janarddana, have my sons been reduced to ashes!'

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा न्यपतद् भूमौ गान्धारी शोकमूर्छिता। दुःखोपहतविज्ञाना धैर्यमुत्सृज्य भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said “Having said so, Gandhari, beside herself with grief, dropped down on the Earth. Losing her fortitude, she became overwhelmed with grief.

sn: ततः कोपपरीताङ्गी पुत्रशोकपरिप्लुता। जगाम शौरि दोषेण गान्धारी व्यथितेन्द्रिया॥
en: Filled with anger and sorrow at the death of her sons, Gandhari, with agitated heart, attributed every fault to Keshava.

sn: गान्धार्युवाच पाण्डवा धार्तराष्ट्राश्च दग्धाः कृष्ण परस्परम्। उपेक्षिता विनश्यन्तस्त्वया कस्माज्जनार्दन॥
en: Gandhari said The Pandavas and the Dhartarashtra, O Krishna, have both been consumed. Whilst they were thus being rotted out, O Janarddana, why were you indifferent to them.

sn: शक्तेन बहुभृत्येन विपुले तिष्ठता बले। उभयत्र समर्थेन श्रुतवाक्येन चैव ह॥
en: You could prevent the slaughter, for you have a large following and a vast army. You had eloquence, and you had the power of making peace.

sn: इच्छतोपेक्षितो नाशः कुरूणां मधुसूदन। यस्मात् त्वया महाबाहो फलं तस्मादवाप्नुहि॥
en: Since deliberately, O slayer of Madhu, you were indifferent to this universal destruction therefore, O mighty-armed one, you should feel the consequences of this act.

sn: पतिशुश्रूषया यन्मे तपः किंचिदुपार्जितम्। तेन त्वां दुरवापेन शप्स्ये चक्रगदाधर॥
en: By the little merit I have acquired by serving dutifully by husband, by that merit so, difficult to attain, I shall curse you, O holder of the discus and the race.

sn: यस्मात् परस्परं अन्तो ज्ञातयः कुरुपाण्डवाः। उपेक्षितास्ते गोविन्द तस्माज्ज्ञातीन् वधिष्यसि॥
en: Since you were indifferent to the Kurus and the Pandavas whilst they killed each other, therefore, O Govinda, you will be the destroyer of your own kinsmen.

sn: त्वमप्युपस्थिते वर्षे षट्त्रिंशे मधुसूदन। हतज्ञातिर्हतामात्यो हतपुत्रो वनेचरः॥ अनाथवदविज्ञातो लोकेष्वनभिलक्षितः। कुत्सितेनाभ्युपायेन निधनं समवाप्स्यसि॥
en: On the thirty-sixty year froin this, O destroyer of Madhu, you will, after bringing about the death of your kinsmen and friends and sons, perish by disgustful means within the forest.

sn: तवाप्येवं हतसुता निहतज्ञातिबान्धवाः। स्त्रियः परिपतिष्यन्ति यथैता भरतस्त्रियः॥
en: The ladies of your family, deprived of sons, kinsmen, and friends, shall weep and cry even as these ladies of the Bharata family.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं घोरं वासुदेवो महामनाः। उवाच देवीं गान्धारीमीषदभ्युत्स्मयन्निव॥ जानेऽहमेतदप्येवं चीर्णं चरसि क्षत्रिये। दैवादेव विनश्यन्ति वृष्णयो नात्र संशयः॥
en: Vaishampayana continued Hearing these words, the great Krishna, addressing the worshipful Gandhari, said to her these words, smilingly,-'There is none in the world, save myself, who can exterminate the Vrishnis. I know this well. I am trying to bring it about. In imprecating this curse, O you of excellent vows, you have helped me in the accomplishment of that work.

sn: संहर्ता वृष्णिचक्रस्य नान्यो मद् विद्यते शुभे। अवध्यास्ते नरैरन्यैरपि वा देवदानवैः॥ परस्परकृतं नाशमतः प्राप्स्यन्ति यादवाः।
en: The Vrishnis and incapable of being killed by others, whether human beings or gods or Danavas. The Yadavas, therefore, shall be killed by one another.

sn: इत्युक्तवति दाशार्हे पाण्डवास्रस्तचेतसः। बभूवु शसंविग्ना निराशाश्चापि जीविते॥
en: After the Dasharha hero had said so, the Pandavas became stupefied. Stricken, with anxiety, all of them became hopeless of life.” After the Dasharha hero had said so, the Pandavas became stupefied. Stricken, with anxiety, all of them became hopeless of life.”

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ गान्धारि मा च शोके मनः कृथाः। तवैव ह्यपराधेन कुरवो निधनं गताः॥
en: Krishna said "Arise, arise, O Gandhari, do not grieve. Through your fault, this huge destruction has taken place.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: यत् त्वं पुत्रं दुरात्मानमीघुमत्यन्तमानिनम्। दुर्योधनं पुरस्कृत्य दुष्कृतं साधु मन्यसे॥
en: Your son Duryodhana, was wicked, envious,. and exceedingly arrogant. Praising his wicked acts, you thought them to be good.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: निष्ठुरं वैरपुरुषं वृद्धानां शासनातिगम्। कथमात्मकृतं दोषं मय्याधातुमिहेच्छसि॥
en: Highly ruthless, he was the embodiment of hostilities, and disobedient to the commands of the old. Why do you then attribute your own faults to me?

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: मृतं वा यदि वा नष्टं योऽतीतमनुशोचति। दुःखेन लभते दुःखं द्वावनौँ प्रपद्यते॥
en: Dead or lost, the person who grieves for what has already taken place, and suffers great grief. By grieving one increases it twofold.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: तपोर्थीयं ब्राह्मणी धत्त गर्भ गौर्वोढारं धावितारं तुरङ्गी। शूद्रा दासं पशुपालं च वैश्या वधार्थीयं त्वद्विधा राजपुत्री॥
en: A saintly woman bears children for the practice of austerities; the cow brings forth offspring for bearing burden; the mare brings forth her young for acquiring speed of motion; the Shudra woman bears a child for increasing the number of keepers of cattle. A princes, however, like you, brings forth soon for being killed.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा वासुदेवस्य पुनरुक्तं वचोऽप्रियम्। तूष्णीं बभूव गान्धारी शोकव्याकुललोचना॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words of Vasudeva that were unpleasant to her, Gandhari, with heart stricken greatly with grief, remained silent.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्तु राजर्षिर्निगृह्याबुद्धिजं तमः। पर्यपृच्छत धर्मज्ञो धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥ जीवतां परिमाणज्ञः सैन्यानामसि पाण्डव। हतानां यदि जानीषे परिमाणं वदस्व मे॥
en: Restraining the grief that originates from folly, the royal sage Dhritarashtra, enquired of Yudhishthira the just, saying,-'If, O son of Pandu, you know it, tell me the number of those that have been killed in this battle, as also of those that have escaped alive.'

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दशायुतानामयुतं सहस्राणि च विंशतिः। कोट्यः षष्टिश्च षट् चैव ह्यस्मिन् राजन् मृधे हताः॥९
en: Yudhishthira answered One billion six hundred and sixty millions and twenty thousand men have been killed in this battle:

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: अलक्षितानां वीराणां सहस्राणि चतुर्दशा दश चान्यानि राजेन्द्र शतं षष्टिश्च पञ्च च॥
en: The number is twenty-four thousand one hundred and sixty five heroes that have escaped.'

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच युधिष्ठिर गतिं कां ते गताः पुरुषसत्तम। आचक्ष्व मे महाबाहो सर्वज्ञो ह्यसि मे मतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Tell me, O mighty-armed one, for you know everything, what ends those foremost of men have attained to.'

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यैर्हतानि शरीराणि हृष्टैः परमसंयुगे। देवराजसमाल्लोकान् गतास्ते सत्यविक्रमः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Those truly powerful warriors that have cheerfully met with death in fierce battle, have all attained to regions like those of Indra.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: ये त्वहृष्टेन मनसा मर्तव्यमिति भारत। युध्यमाना हता: संख्ये गन्धर्वैः सह संगताः॥
en: Knowing death to be certain, they that have met it cheerlessly, have attained to the region of the Gandharvas.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: ये च संग्रामभूमिष्ठा याचमानाः पराङ्मुखाः। शस्त्रेण निधनं प्राप्ता गतास्ते गुह्यकान् प्रति॥
en: Those warriors that have been killed by weapons, while turning away from the field of begging for quarter, have reached the region of the Guhyakas.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: पात्यमानाः परैर्ये तु हीयमाना निरायुधाः। ह्रीनिषेवा महात्मानः परानभिमुखा रणे॥ छिद्यमानाः शितैः शस्त्रैः क्षत्रधर्मपरायणाः। गतास्ते ब्रह्मसदनं न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा॥
en: Those great warriors who, observing the duties of Kshatriyas and regarding flight from battle to be disgraceful, have fallen, wounded with keen weapons, while advancing unarmed against fighting foes, have all assumed bring forms and reached the regions of Brahman!

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: ये त्वत्र निहता राजन्नन्तरायोधनं प्रति। यथाकथंचित् पुरुषास्ते गतास्तूत्तरान् कुरून्॥
en: The remaining warriors, that have anyhow been killed on the field of battle, have attained to the region of the Uttara Kuru.'

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच केन ज्ञानबलेनैवं पुत्र पश्यसि सिद्धवत्। तन्मे वद महाबाहो श्रोतव्यं यदि वै मया॥
en: Dhritarashtra said By what knowledge, O son, you see these things like one crowned with ascetic success? Tell me this, O mighty-armed one, if you think that I can listen to it properly!'

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच निदेशाद् भवतः पूर्वं वने विचरता मया। तीर्थयात्राप्रसङ्गेन सम्प्राप्तोऽयमनुग्रहः॥
en: Yudhishthira said While at your behest I wandered in the foremost, I obtained this boon at the time of sojourning to the sacred places!

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: देवर्षिर्लोमशो दृष्टस्ततः प्राप्तोऽस्म्यनुस्मृतिम्। दिव्यं चक्षुरपि प्राप्तं ज्ञानयोगेन वै पुरा॥
en: I met with the celestial Rishi Lomasha and acquired from him the boon of spiritual vision. Again on another occasion I obtained second sight through the power of knowledge!

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अनाथानां जनानां च सनाथानां च भारत। कचित् तेषां शरीराणि धक्ष्यसे विधिपूर्वकम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said It is necessary that our people should burn duly the dead bodies of both who have friends and who have not?

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: न येषामस्ति संस्कर्ता न च येऽत्राहिताग्नयः। वयं च कस्य कुर्याम बहुत्वात् तात कर्मणाम्॥
en: What shall we do with those that have none to look after them and that have no sacred fires? We have many duties to perform. Who are those whose (funeral) rites we should perform?

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: यान् सुपर्णाश्च गृध्राश्च विकर्षन्ति यतस्ततः। तेषां तु कर्मणा लोका भविष्यन्ति युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O Yudhishthira, will they obtain blissful regions by the merit of their deeds, they whose bodies are now being torn and dragged by vultures and other birds?'

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तो महाराज कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। आदिदेश सुधर्माणं धौम्यं सूतं च संजयम्॥ विदुरं च महाबुद्धिं युयुत्सुं चैव कौरवम्। इन्द्रसेनमुखांश्चैव भृत्यान् सूतांश्च सर्वशः॥ भवन्तः कारयन्त्वेषां प्रेतकार्याण्यशेषतः। यथा चानाथवत् किंचिच्छरीरं न विनश्यति॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed, Kunti's son the highly wise Yudhisthira commanded Sudharman (the priest of the Kauravas), Dhaumya, Sanjaya of the Suta order, Vidura of great wisdom, and Yuyutsu of Kuru's race, and all his servants headed by Indrasena, and all the other Sutas that were with him, saying,—'Cause the funeral rites of the killed, numbering by thousands, to be duly performed, so that so body may die for want of men to take care of them!

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: शासनाद् धर्मराजस्य क्षत्ता सूतश्च संजयः। सुधर्मा धौम्यसहित इन्द्रसेनादयस्तथा॥ चन्दनागुरुकाष्ठानि तथा कालीयकान्युत। घृतं तैलं च गन्धांश्च क्षौमाणि वसनानि च॥ समाहृत्य महार्हाणि दारूणां चैव संजयान्। रथांश्च मृदितांस्तत्र नानाप्रहरणानि च॥ चिताः कृत्वा प्रयत्नेन यथामुख्यान् नराधिपान्। दाहयामासुरव्यग्राः शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus commanded by king Yudhishthira the just, Vidura, Sanjaya, Sudharman, Dhaumya and Indrasena and others, procuring sandal and other kinds of wood used on such occasions, as also clarified butter and oil and perfumes and rich silken robes and other kinds of cloth, and large heaps of dry wood, and broken car and various kinds of weapons, caused funeral pyres to be duly made and lighted and then without delay burnt duly, the dead bodies of the kings.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: दुर्योधनं च राजानं भ्रातृ॑श्चास्य महारथान्। शल्यं शलं च राजानं भूरिश्रवसमेव च॥ जयद्रथं च राजानमभिमन्युं च भारत। दौःशासनि लक्ष्मणं च धृष्टकेतुं च पार्थिवम्॥ बृहन्तं सोमदत्तं च संजयांश्च शताधिकान्। राजानं क्षेमधन्वानं विराटद्रुपदौ तथा॥ शिखण्डिनं च पाञ्चाल्यं धृष्टद्युम्नं च पार्षतम्। युधामन्युं च विक्रान्तमुत्तमौजसमेव च॥ कौसल्यं द्रौपदेयांश्च शकुनि चापि सौबलम्। अचलं वृषकं चैव भगदत्तं च पार्थिवम्॥ कर्णं वैकर्तनं चैव सहपुत्रममर्षणम्। केकयांश्च महेष्वासांस्त्रिगर्ताश्च महारथान्॥ घटोत्कचं राक्षसेन्द्रं बकभ्रातरमेव च। अलम्बुषं राक्षसेन्द्रं जलसन्धं च पार्थिवम्॥ एतांश्चान्यांश्च सुबहून् पार्थिवांश्च सहस्रशः। धृतधाराहुतैर्दीप्तैः पावकैः समदाहयन्॥
en: They properly burnt upon those fires burning with libations of clarified butter poured in torrents over them, the bodies of Duryodhana and his hundred brothers, of Shalya, and Shala, and king Bhruishravas; of king Jayadratha and Abhimanyu, O Bharata; of Dussasana's son and Lakshmana and king Dhrishtaketu; of Vrihanta and Somadatta and the hundreds of Srinjayas; of king Khemadhanvan and Virata and Drupada; of Shikhandin the prince of Panchalas, and Dhirishtadyumna of Prisata's race; of the valiant Yudhamanyu and Uttamaujas; of the ruler of the Kosalas, the sons of Draupadi, and Shakuni the son of Subala; of Achala and Vrisaka, and king Bhagadatta; of Karna and his son of great wrath; of those great bowmen, viz., the Kekaya princes, and those mighty carwarriors, viz., the Trigartas; of Ghatotkacha the prince of Rakshasas, and the brother of Vaka; of Alamvusha, that best of Rakshasas, and king Jalasandha; and of hundreds and thousands of others kings.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: पितृमेधाश्च केषांचित् प्रावर्तन्त महात्मनाम्। सामभिश्चाप्यगायन्त तेऽन्वशोचन्त चापरैः॥
en: The Pitri-medha rites in honor of some of the great persons who were dead were performed there, while some sang Samans, and some cried for the dead.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: साम्नामृचां च नादेन स्त्रीणां च रुदितस्वनैः। कश्मलं सर्वभूतानां निशायां समपद्यत॥
en: With the loud sound of Samans and Richs, and the cries of the women, all creatures became stupefied that night.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: ते विधूमाः प्रदीप्ताश्च दीप्यमानाश्च पावकाः। नभसीवान्वदृश्यन्त ग्रहास्तन्वभ्रसंवृताः॥
en: The funeral fires, smokeless and burning brightly looked like shining planets in the sky enveloped by clouds.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: ये चाप्यनाथास्तत्रासन् नानादेशसमागताः। तांश्च सर्वान् समानाय्य राशीन् कृत्वा सहस्रशः॥४२ चित्वा दारुभिरव्यप्रैः प्रभूतैः स्नेहपाचितैः। दाहयामास तान् सर्वान् विदुरो राजशासनात्॥
en: Those among the dead that had hailed from various kingdoms and had no friends, were collected together in thousands of heaps and, at the command of Yudhishthira, were caused to be burnt by Vidura with the help a large number of persons acting coolly out of goodwill and affection, on pyres made of dry wood.

description: .— Contd. Krishna consoles Gandhari. Dhritarastra asks Yudhishthira about the ends of the warriors killed and the latter's reply
sn: कारयित्वा ऋियास्तेषां कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। धृतराष्ट्र पुरस्कृत्य गङ्गामभिमुखोऽगमत्॥
en: Having performed their last rites, the Kuru king Yudhishthira, placing Dhritarashtra at his head, proceeded towards the river Ganga.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ते समासाद्य गङ्गां तु शिवां पुण्यजलोचिताम्। ह्रदिनीं च प्रसन्नां च महारूपां महावनाम्॥ भूषणान्युत्तरीयाणि वेष्टनान्यवमुच्य च। ततः पितॄणां भ्रातॄणां पौत्राणां स्वजनस्य च॥ पुत्राणामार्यकाणां च पतीनां च कुरुस्त्रियः। उदकं चक्रिरे सर्वा रुदत्यो भृशदुःखिताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Arrived at the holy Ganga full of sacred water, containing many lakes, adorned with high banks and broad shores, and having a vest bed, they threw off their ornaments, upper garments, and belts and girdles. The Kuru ladies, crying and stricken with great sorrow offered oblations of water of their fathers and grandsons and brothers and kinsmen and sons and seniors and husbands. Conversant with duties, they also performed the water-rite for their friends.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: सुहृदां चापि धर्मज्ञाः प्रचक्रुः सलिलक्रियाः। उदके क्रियमाणे तु वीराणां वीरपत्निभिः॥ सूपतीर्था भवद्गङ्गा भूयो विप्रससार च।
en: While those wives of heroes were performing this rite in honour of their heroic husband, the access to the stream became easy, although the paths (carved out by feet) disappeared afterwards.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: तन्महोदधिसंकाशं निरानन्दमनुत्सवम्॥ वीरपत्नीभिराकीर्णं गङ्गातीरमशोभत।
en: The shores of their river though crowded with those wives of heroes, looked as broad as the ocean and presented a sorrow of sorrow and cheerlessness.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: ततः कुन्ती महाराज सहसा शोककर्शिता॥ रुदती मन्दया वाचा पुत्रान् वंचनमब्रवीत्।
en: Then Kunti, O king, laden with grief, weepingly addressed her sons in these soft words.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: यः स वीरो महेष्वासो रथयूथपयूथपः॥ अर्जुनेनं जित: संख्ये वीरलक्षणलक्षितः। यं सूतपुत्रं मन्यध्वं राधेयमिति पाण्डवाः॥ यो व्यराजच भूमध्ये दिवाकर इव प्रभुः। प्रत्ययुध्यत वः सर्वान् पुरा यः सपदानुगान्॥ दुर्योधनबलं सर्वं यः प्रकर्षन् व्यरोचत। यस्य नास्ति समो वीर्ये पृथिव्यामपि पार्थिवः॥ योऽवृणीत यशः शूरः प्राणैरपि सदा भुवि। कर्णस्य सत्यसंधस्य संग्रामेष्वपलायिनः॥ कुरुध्वमुदकं तस्य भ्रातुरकिष्टकर्मणः। स हि वः पूर्वजो भ्राता भास्करान्मय्यजायत॥ कुण्डली कवची शूरो दिवाकरसमप्रभः।
en: That hero and great bowman, that chief of many car-divisions, that heroic warrior who has been killed by Arjuna in battle, that warrior whom, ye sons of Pandu, you knew as the son of the charioteer Radha, that hero who shone in the midst of his army like the Sun himself, who fought with all of you and your followers, who shone as he commanded the vast army of Duryodhana, who had no equal on Earth in energy, that hero who preferred glory to life, that brave warrior firm in truth and never fatigued with exertion, was your eldest brother! Offer oblations of water to that eldest brother of yours who was born of me by the Sun! That hero was born with a pair of earrings and clad in armour, and took after the Sun-God himself in effulgence.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: श्रुत्वा तु पाण्डवाः सर्वे मातुर्वचनमप्रियम्॥ कर्णमेवानुशोचन्तो भूयः क्लान्ततराभवन्।
en: Hearing these painful words of their mother, the Pandavas began to grieve for Karna. Indeed, they became more afflicted then ever.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रः कुलीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ उवाच मातरं वीरो निःश्वसन्निव पन्नगः। यः शरोमिर्ध्वजावर्तो महाभुजमहाग्रहः॥ तलशब्दानुनदितो महारथमहाह्रदः। यस्येषुपातमासाद्य नान्यस्तिष्ठेद् धनंजयात्॥ कथं पुत्रो भवत्याः स देवगर्भः पुराभवत्।
en: Then that foremost of men, viz., the heroic Yudhishthira, sighing like a snake asked his mother,-'Were you the mother of that Karna who was like a sea having arrows for his billows, his tall standard for his vortex, his own mighty arms for a couple of huge alligators, his large car for his deep lake, and the sound of his palms or his tempestuous roar, and whose force none could withstand except Dlananjaya? How was that son resembling a very god born of you in former days?

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: यस्य बाहुप्रतापेन तापिताः सर्वतो वयम्॥ तमग्निमिव वस्त्रेण कथं छादितवत्यसि।
en: The power of his arms scorched all of us! How, O mother, could you conceal him like a person concealing a fire within the folds of his cloth?

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: यस्य बाहुबलं नित्यं धार्तराष्ट्ररुपासितम्॥ उपासितं यथास्माभिर्बलं गाण्डीवधन्वनः।
en: His might of arms was always adored by the Dhritarashtras even as we always worship the might of the wilder of Gandiva.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: भूमिपानां च सर्वेषां बलं बलवतां वरः॥ नान्यः कुन्तीसुतात् कर्णादगृह्णाद् रथिनां रथी।
en: How was that foremost of powerful men, that first of car-warriors, who fought the united force of all the kings in battle, how was he a son of yours?

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: स नः प्रथमजो भ्राता सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः॥ असूत तं भवत्यग्रे कथमद्भुतविक्रमम्।
en: Was that foremost of all holders of weapons our eldest brother? How did you give birth to that child of wonderful prowess?

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: अहो भवत्या मन्त्रस्य गृहनेन वयं हताः॥ निधनेन हि कर्णस्य पीडितास्तु सबान्धवाः।
en: Alas, for your concealing this fact we have been undone! By the death of Karna, ourselves with all our friends have been greatly sorry.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: अभिमन्योर्विनाशेन द्रौपदेयवधेन च॥ पञ्चालानां विनाशेन कुरूणां पतनेन च। ततः शतगुणं दुःखमिदं मामस्पृशद् मशम्॥
en: The grief I fell at Karna's death is a hundred times great than that felt for the death of Abhimanyu and the sons of Draupadi, and the destruction of the Panchalas and the Kurus! Thinking of Karna, I am burning with grief, like a person thrown into a burning fire.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: कर्णमेवानुशोचामि दह्याम्यग्नाविवाहितः। नेह स्म किंचिदप्राप्यं भवेदपि दिवि स्थितम्॥ न चेदं वैशसं घोरं कौरवान्तकरं भवेत्।
en: Nothing could have been unattainable by us, not excepting things belonging to the celestial region. Alas, this terrible carnage, so destructive of the Kurus, would not have taken place.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: एवं विलप्य बहुलं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥ व्यरुदच्छनकै राजंश्चकारास्योदकं प्रभुः।
en: Thus bewailing, king Yudhishthira the just uttered loud wails of woe. The powerful king then offered oblations of water to his deceased elder brother.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: ततो विनेदुः सहसा स्त्रियस्ताः खलु सर्वशः॥ अभितो याः स्थितास्तत्र तस्मिन्नुदककर्मणि।
en: Then all the ladies that crowded the shores of the river suddenly cried aloud.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: तत आनाययामास कर्णस्य सपरिच्छदाः॥ स्त्रियः कुरुपति/मान् भ्रातुः प्रेम्णा युधिष्ठिरः।
en: The intelligent king of the Kurus, viz., Yudhishthira, had the wives and members of Karna's family brought before him.

description: .— Contd. Karna's birth disclosed to the Pandavas. The water-rite is performed
sn: स ताभिः सह धर्मात्मा प्रेतकृत्यमनन्तरम्॥ चकार विधिवद् धीमान् धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। पापेनासौ मया श्रेष्ठो भ्राता ज्ञातिनिपातितः। अतो मनसि यद् गुह्यं स्त्रीणां तन्न भविष्यति॥ इत्युक्त्वा स तु गङ्गाया उत्तताराकुलेन्द्रियः। भ्रातृभिः सहितः सर्वैर्गङ्गातीरमुपेयिवान्॥
en: The righteous-souled king performed, with them the water-rite in honor of his eldest brother. Having finished the ceremony, the king, with his mind greatly agitated, rose from the waters of Ganga."

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वतीं चैव ततो जयमदीरयेत्।।
en: Having saluted the Supreme Deity (Narayana), and the highest of all male beings (Nara), and also the Goddess of Learning (Sarasvati) let us cry success.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कृतोदकास्ते सुहृदां सर्वेषां पाण्डुनन्दनाः। विदुरो धृतराष्ट्रश्च सर्वाश्च भरतस्त्रियः॥ तत्र ते सुमहात्मानो न्यवसन् पाण्डुनन्दनाः। शौचं निवर्तयिष्यन्तो मासमानं बहिः पुरात्॥
en: “Having offered oblations of water to all their friends and kinsmen, the sons of Pandu, Vidura, Dhritarashtra, and all the Bharata ladies, continued to live on the banks of the sacred river. The noble sons of Pandu wished to pass the period of mourning, which lasted for a month, outside the Kuru city.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: कृतोदकं तु राजानं धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। अभिजग्मुर्महात्मानः सिद्धा ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमाः॥
en: After king Yudhishthira had performed the water-rites, many great sages endued with ascetic success and many sainted Rishis came there to see the king.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: द्वैपायनो नारदश्च देवलश्च महानृषिः। देवस्थानश्च कण्वश्च तेषां शिष्याश्च सत्तमाः॥
en: Among them were the Dvaipayana Vyasa, Narada, the great Rishi Devala, Devasthana, and Kanva. They had in their company the best of their pupils.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: अन्ये च वेदविद्वांसः कृतप्रज्ञा द्विजातयः। गृहस्थाः स्नातकाः सन्तो ददृशुः कुरुसत्तमम्॥
en: Many other Rishis, of great wisdom and well versed in the Vedic in the Vedic Lore. living as householders or belonging to the Snataka class, came to see the Kuru king.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: तेऽभिगम्य महात्मानः पूजिताश्च यथाविधि। आसनेषु महार्हेषु विविशुस्ते महर्षयः॥ प्रतिगृह्य ततः पूजां तत्कालसदृशीं तदा। पर्युपासन् यथान्यायं परिवार्य युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Those high-souled ones, as they came, were duly adored by Yudhishthira. The great Rishis then took their seats on rich carpets. Accepting the adoration suited to the period of mourning, they sat in due order around the king.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: पुण्ये भागीरथीतीरे शोकव्याकुलचेतसम्। आश्वासयन्तो राजानं विप्राः शतसहस्रशः॥
en: Thousands of Brahmanas consoled and comforted that king of kings living on the sacred banks of the Bhagirathi with heart exceedingly shaken by sorrow.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: नारदस्त्वब्रवीत् काले धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। सम्भाष्य मुनिभिः सार्धं कृष्णद्वैपायनादिभिः॥ भवता बाहुवीर्येण प्रसादान्माधवस्य च। जितेयमवनिः कृत्स्ना धर्मेण च युधिष्ठि॥
en: Having accosted first the Rishis headed by Vyasa, Narada addressed Yudhishthira the son of Dharma, saying, “Through the strength of your arms and the kindness of Krishna, the whole Earth, O Yudhishthira, has been righteously acquired by you.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: दिष्ट्या मुक्तस्तु संग्रामादस्माल्लोकभयंकरात्। क्षत्रधर्मरतश्चापि कच्चिन्मोदसि पाण्डव॥
en: By dint of good fortune, you have escaped alive from this dreadful battle. Ever abiding by the duties of a Kshatriya, why do you not rejoice, O son of Pandu?

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: कच्चिच्च निहतामित्रः प्रीणासि सुहृदो नृप। कच्चिच्छ्रियमिमां प्राप्य न त्वां शोकः प्रबाधते॥
en: Having killed all you foes, will you not please your friends, O King? Having secured this prosperity, I hope, you have nothing to be sorry of now.'."

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच विजितेयं मही कृत्स्ना कृष्णबाहुबलाश्रयात्। ब्राह्मणानां प्रसादेन भीमार्जुनबलेन च॥
en: Yudhishthira said Indeed, I have conquered the whole Earth through my reliance on the might of Krishna's arms, through the favour of the Brahmanas, and through the strength of Bhima and Arjuna.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: इदं मम महद् दुःखं वर्तते हृदि नित्यदा। कृत्वा ज्ञातिक्षयमिमं महान्तं लोभकारितम्॥ सौभद्रं द्रौपदेयांश्च घातयित्वा सुतान् प्रियान्। जयोऽयमजयाकारो भगवन् प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: But his heavy grief, is always preying on my mind, that through covetousness I have brought about this dreadful destruction of kinsmen. Having caused the death of the darling son of Subhadra, and of the sons of Draupadi, this victory, O Holy one, appears to me as being tantamount to defeat.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: किं नु वक्ष्यति वार्ष्णेयी वधूर्मे मधुसूदनम्। द्वारकावासिनी कृष्णमितः प्रतिगतं हरिम्॥
en: What will Subhadra of Vrishni's race, that sister-in-law of mine, say to me? what also will the inhabitants of Dwaraka say to the destroyer of Madhu when he goes there from this place?

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: द्रौपदी हतपुत्रेयं कृपणा हतबान्धवा। अस्मत्प्रियहिते युक्ता भूयः पीडयतीव माम्॥
en: This Draupadi, again, who is eve busy with pleasing us, bereaved of son and kinsmen, is causing me great pain.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: इदमन्यत् तु भगवन् यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि नारद। मन्त्रसंवरणेनास्मि कुन्त्या दुःखेन योजितः॥
en: There is another subject, O holy Narada, about which I will speak to you. For Kunti having hidden a very important matter, great has been my grief.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: यः स नागायुतबलो लोकेऽप्रतिरथो रणे। सिंहखेलगतिर्धीमान् घृणी दाता यतव्रतः॥ आश्रयो धार्तराष्ट्राणां मानी तीक्ष्णपराक्रमः। अमर्षी नित्यसंरम्भी क्षेप्तास्माकं रणे रणे।॥ शीघ्रास्त्रश्चित्रयोधी च कृती चाद्भुतविक्रमः। गूढोत्पन्नः सुतः कुन्त्या भ्रातास्माकमसौ किल॥
en: That hero who had the strength of ten thousand elephants, who in this world was peerless car-warrior, who was endued with the pride and gait of a lion, who was gifted with great intelligence and compassion, whose liberality was unbounded, who practised many high vows, who was the refuge of the Dhartarashtras, who was sensitive about his honour, whose prowess was irresistible, who was ready to repay all injuries and was always wrathful [in battle], who defeated us in various encounters, who was quick in the use of arms, conversant with every mode of battle, skilful and endued with wonderful courage, that Karna was a son of Kunti, given birth to by her .secretly, and, therefore, a uterine brother of ours.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: तोयकर्मणि तं कुन्ती कथयामास सूर्यजम्। पुत्रं सर्वगुणोपेतमवकीर्णं जले पुरा॥
en: Whilst we were offering oblations of water to the dead, Kunti described him as the son of Surya (Sun-God). Possessed of every accomplishment, that child had been thrown into the water.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: मञ्जूषायां समाधाय गङ्गास्रोतस्यमज्जयत्। यं सूतपुत्रं लोकोऽयं राधेयं चाभ्यमन्यत॥ स ज्येष्ठपुत्रः कुन्त्या वै भ्रातास्माकं च मातृजः। अजानता मया भ्रात्रा राज्यलुब्धेन घातितः॥ तन्मे दहति गात्राणि तूलराशिमिवानलः।
en: Having placed him in a basket made of grass, Kunti Floated it in the water of Ganga. He who was known to the world as the son of the charioteer Radha, was really the eldest son of Kunti, and, therefore, our uterine brother! Hankering after kingdom, alas, I have unknowingly brought about the death of that brother of mine. It is this that is burning my body, like a fire consuming a heap of cotton.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: न हि तं वेद पार्थोऽपि भ्रातरं श्वेतवाहनः॥ नाहं न भीमो न यमौ स त्वस्मान् वेद सुव्रतः।
en: Arjuna having white horses knew him not for a brother! Neither I, Nor Bhima, Nor the twins, knew him as such! He, however, a great bowman knew us (for his brothers).

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: गता किल पृथा तस्य सकाशमिति नः श्रुतम्॥ अस्माकं शमकामा वै त्वं च पुत्रो ममेत्यथ।
en: We have heard that once Pritha went to him for seeking our well-being and addressed him, saying, You are my son.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: पृथाया न कृतः कामस्तेन चापि महात्मना॥ अपि पश्चादिदं मातर्यवोचदिति नः श्रुतम्।
en: That illustrious hero, however, refused to satisfy Pritha's desire. Subsequently, we are informed, he said to his mother these words:न हि शक्ष्याम्यहं त्यत्वें नृपं दुर्योधनं रणे॥

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: अनार्यत्वं नृशंसत्वं कृतघ्नत्वं च मे भवेत्।
en: I am unable to leave Duryodhana's side in battle! If I do so, it would be a dishonourable, crucl, and ungrateful act.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: युधिष्ठिरेण संधिं हि यदि कुर्या मते तव॥ भीतो रणे श्वेतवाहादिति मां मंस्यते जनः।
en: If, in pursuance of your wishes, I make peace with Yudhishthira, people will say that I ani afraid of Arjuna having white horses.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: सोऽहं निर्जित्य समरे विजयं सहकेशवम्॥ संधास्ये धर्मपुत्रेण पश्चादिति च सोऽब्रवीत्।
en: Having defeated Arjuna with Keshava, therefore, in battle, I will afterwards make peace with Dharma's son! These were his words as we have heard.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: तमुवाच किल पृथा पुनः पृथुलवक्षसम्॥ चतुर्णामभयं देहि कामं युध्यस्व फाल्गुनम्।
en: Thus answered, Pritha once more addressed her son having broad chest and said,-'Fight with Phalguna then, but spare my four other sons.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: सोऽब्रवीन्मातरं धीमान् वेपमानां कृताञ्जलिः॥ प्राप्तान् विषह्यांश्चतुरो न हनिष्यामि ते सुतान्।
en: The intelligent Karna, with joined palms then replied to his trembling mother, saying,-'If I get your four other sons even under my power, I will not kill them.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: पञ्चैव हि सुता देवि भविष्यन्ति तव ध्रुवाः॥ सार्जुना वा हते कर्णे सकर्णा वा हतेऽर्जुने।
en: Forsooth, O goddess, you will always have five sons! If Karna be killed with Arjuna, You will have five! If, on the other hand, Arjuna be killed, You will have five, with me.'

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: तं पुत्रगृद्धिनी भूयो माता पुत्रमथाब्रवीत्॥ भ्रातृणां स्वस्ति कुर्वीथा येषां स्वस्ति चिकीर्षसि।
en: Seeking the well-being of her children, his mother once more said to him,-'Go, O Karna, do good to those brothers of yours whose good you always seek.'

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: एवमुक्त्वा किल पृथा विसृज्योपययौ गृहान्॥ सोऽर्जुनेन हतो वीरो भ्रात्रा भ्राता सहोदरः।
en: Having said these words, Pritha took his leave and returned to her residence. That hero has been killed by Arjuna,-the uterine brother by the brother.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: न चैव विवृतो मन्त्रः पृथायास्तस्य वा विभो॥ अथ शूरो महेष्वासः पार्थेनाजौ निपातितः।
en: Neither Pritha, nor he, had ever divulged the secret, O Sir! That hero and great bowman, was therefore killed by Arjuna in battle.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: अहं त्वज्ञासिषं पश्चात् स्वसोदर्यं द्विजोत्तम॥ पूर्वजं भ्रातरं कर्णं पृथाया वचनात् प्रभो।
en: Afterwards I have come to know, O best of Rishis, that he was my uterine brother! Indeed, according to Pritha's words, I am informed that Karna was our eldest-born.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: तेन मे दूयते तीव्र हृदयं भ्रातृघातिनः॥ कर्णार्जुनसहायोऽहं जयेयमपि वासवम्।
en: Having caused my brother to be killed, my heart is burning greatly. If I had both Karna and Arjuna for helping me, I could have defeated Vasudeva himself.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: सभायां क्लिश्यमानस्य धार्तराष्ट्रैर्दुरात्मभिः॥ सहसोत्पतितः क्रोधः कर्णं दृष्ट्वा प्रशाम्यति।
en: Whilst I was tormented in the court by the wicked sons of Dhritarashtra, my anger suddenly excited, became cooled on seeing Karma.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: यदा ह्यस्य गिरो रूक्षाः शृणोमि कटुकोदयाः॥ सभायां गदतो द्यूते दुर्योधनहितैषिणः। तदा नश्यति मे रोषः पादौ तस्य निरीक्ष्य ह॥ कुन्त्या हि सदृशौ पादौ कर्णस्येति मतिर्ममा
en: Even while hearing the harsh and bitter words of Karna himself on the occasion of our match at dice, which he uttered for pleasing Duryodhana, my wrath became cooled on seeing Karna's feet. It appeared to me that Karna's feet resembled the feet of our mother Kunti.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: सादृश्यहेतुमन्विच्छन् पृथायास्तस्य चैव ह॥ कारणं नाधिगच्छामि कथंचिदपि चिन्तयन्।
en: To make out the reason of that resemblance between him and our mother, I thought for a long time. Even trying my level best I could not find the cause.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: कथं नु तस्य संग्रामे पृथिवी चक्रमग्रसत्॥ कथं नु शप्तो भ्राता मे तत्त्वं वक्तुमिहार्हसि।
en: Why, indeed, did the Earth swallow up the wheels of his car at the time of battle? Why was my brother cursed? You should relate all this to me.

description: The period of mourning, Yudhishthira wants to know everything about Karna's birth
sn: श्रोतुमिच्छामि भगवंस्त्वत्तः सर्वं यथातथम्। भवान् हि सर्वविद् विद्वान् लोके वेद कृताकृतम्।।४४।
en: I wish to hear everything from you, O Rishi. You know everything of this world, as also of both the past and the future.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स एवमुक्तस्तु मुनि रदो वदतां वरः। कथयामास तत् सर्वं यथा शप्तः स सूतजः॥
en: Thus accosted that best of orators, viz., the sage Narada, described everything about the manner in which he who was known as a charioteers' son had been cursed.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: नारद उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि भारत। न कर्णार्जुनयोः किंचिदविषह्यं भवेद् रणे॥
en: Narada said "What you say, O mighty-armed one, is true O Bharata! Nothing could resist Karna and Arjuna in battle.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: गुह्यमेतत् तु देवानां कथयिष्यामि तेऽनघ। तन्निबोध महाबाहो यथा वृत्तमिदं पुरा॥
en: This, O sinless one, that I am about to tell you is unknown to the very celestials. Listen to me, O mighty-armed one, as it happened formerly.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: क्षत्रं स्वर्ग कथं गच्छेच्छस्त्रपूतमिति प्रभो। संघर्षजननस्तस्मात् कन्यागर्भो विनिर्मितः॥
en: The question was mooted, how all the Kshatriyas, purified by weapons, should attain to blissful regions. For this, a child was conceived by Kunti while she was a maid, capable of creating a general war.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: स बालस्तेजसा युक्तः सूतपुत्रत्वमागतः। चकाराङ्गिरसां श्रेष्ठाद् धनुर्वेदं गुरोस्तदा॥
en: Highly energetic that child became known as a Suta. He subsequently learnt the science of arms from the preceptor (Drona), that foremost of Angirasa's race.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: स बलं भीमसेनस्य फाल्गुनस्य च लाघवम्। बुद्धिं च तव राजेन्द्र यमयोर्विनयं तदा॥ सख्यं च वासुदेवेन बाल्ये गाण्डीवधन्वनः। प्रजानामनुरागं च चिन्तयानो व्यदह्यत॥
en: Thinking of the prowess of Bhimasena, the quickness of Arjuna in the use of arms, your intelligence, O King, the humility of the twins, the friendship, from earliest years, between Vasudeva and the holder of Gandiva, and the love of the people for you all, that young man was burnt with envy.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: स सख्यमकरोद् बाल्ये राज्ञा दुर्योधनेन च। युष्माभिनित्यसंद्विष्टो दैवाच्चापि स्वभावतः॥
en: In early age he contracted friendship with king Duryodhana, led by accident and his own nature and the hate he cherished against you all.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: वीर्याधिकमथालक्ष्य धनुर्वेदे धनंजयम्। द्रोणं रहस्युपागम्य कर्णो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ब्रह्मास्त्रं वेत्तुमिच्छामि सरहस्यनिवर्तनम्। अर्जुनेन समं चाहं युध्येयमिति मे मतिः॥
en: Making that Dhananjaya was superior to every one in the science of arms, Karna one day approached Drona privately and said these words to him,-I desire to master the Brahma weapon, with all its Mantras and the power of withdrawing it, for I wish to fight Arjuna.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: समः शिष्येषु वः स्नेहः पुत्रे चैव तथा ध्रुवम्। त्वत्प्रसादान्न मां ब्रूयुरकृतास्त्रं विचक्षणाः॥
en: Forsooth, the love you bear for every one of your pupils is equal to what you cherish for your own son! I pray that all masters of the science of arms may, by your favour consider me as one accomplished in weapons.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: द्रोणस्तथोक्तः कर्णेन सापेक्षः फाल्गुनं प्रति। दौरात्म्यं चैव कर्णस्य विदित्वा तमुवाच ह॥ ब्रह्मास्त्रं ब्राह्मणो विद्याद् यथावच्चरितव्रतः। क्षत्रियो वा तपस्वी यो नान्यो विद्यात् कथंचन।॥
en: Thus accosted by him, Drona, on account of partial love for Phalguna, as also from his knowledge of the wickedness of Karna, told him,-None save a Brahmana, who has duly practised all vows, should master the Brahma weapon, or a Kshatriya who has practised austere penances, and no other.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: इत्युक्तोऽङ्गिरसां श्रेष्ठमामन्त्र्य प्रतिपूज्य च। जगाम सहसा रामं महेन्द्रं पर्वतं प्रति॥
en: When Drona had answered thus, Karna, having adored him, took his permission and proceeded forthwith to Rama then living on the Mahendra mountains.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: स तु राममुपागम्य शिरसाऽभिप्रणम्य च। ब्राह्मणो भार्गवोऽस्मीति गौरवेणाभ्यगच्छत॥
en: Approaching Rama, hc bowed to him and said,-I am a Brahmana of Bhrigu's race!-This secured honour for him.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: समस्तं प्रतिजग्राह पृष्ट्वा गोत्रादि सर्वशः। उष्यतां स्वागतं चेति प्रीतिमांश्चाभवद् भृशम्॥
en: With this knowledge about his birth and family, Rama received him kindly and said, You are welcome!-at which Karna became highly pleased.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: तत्र कर्णस्य वसतो महेन्द्रे स्वर्गसंनिभे। गन्धर्व राक्षसैर्यक्षैर्देवैश्चासीत् समागमः॥
en: While living on the Mahendra mountains resembling heaven itself, Karna met and mixed with many Gandharvas, and Yakshas, and gods.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: स तत्रेष्वस्त्रमकरोद् भृगुश्रेष्ठाद् यथाविधि। प्रियश्चाभवदत्यर्थं देवदानवरक्षसाम्॥
en: While living there, he learnt the use of all the weapons duly, and became a great favourite of the gods, the Gandharvas, and the Rakshasas.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: स कदाचित् समुद्रान्ते विचरन्नाश्रमान्तिके। एकः खड्गधनुष्पाणिः परिचक्राम सूर्यजः॥
en: One day he walked on the sea shore by the side of that hermitage. Armed with bow and sword, Surya's son wandered alone.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: सोऽग्निहोत्रप्रसक्तस्य कस्यचिद् ब्रह्मवादिनः। जघानाज्ञानतः पार्थ होमधेनुं यदृच्छया।॥
en: While thus walking, O Partha, he inadvertently and unwittingly killed the Homa Cow of a certain Brahmavadin who daily performed his Agnihotra rite.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: तदज्ञानकृतं मत्वा ब्राह्मणाय न्यवेदयत्। कर्णः प्रसादयंश्चैनमिदमित्यब्रवीद् वचः॥ अबुद्धिपूर्वं भगवन् धेनुरेषा हता तव। मया तत्र प्रसादं च कुरुष्वेति पुनः पुनः॥ तं स विप्रोऽब्रवीत्क्रुद्धो वाचा निर्भर्त्सयन्निव। दुराचार वधार्हस्त्वं फलं प्रात्नुहि दुर्मते॥
en: Knowing that he had perpetrated that crime from carelessness, he informed the Brahmana of it. For pleasing the owner, Karna repeatedly said,-O Rishi, I have killed this your cow against my will. Forgive the act! Filled with anger the Brahmana, rebuking him, said, O wicked wight, you should be killed! May you suffer the fruit of this act, O you of wicked soul!

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: येन विस्पर्धसे नित्यं यदर्थं घटसेऽनिशम्। युध्यतस्तेन ते पाप भूमिश्चक्रं गृसिष्यति॥
en: While fighting him, O wretch, whom you always challenge, and for whom you are trying so much every day, the Earth shall swallow the wheel of your car.

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: ततश्चक्रे महीग्रस्ते मूर्धानं ते विचेतसः। पातयिष्यति विक्रम्य शत्रुर्गच्छ नराधम॥
en: And while the wheel of your car shall thus be swallowed up by the Earth, your enemy displaying his prowess, will cut off your head, you being stupefied then. Leave me, O vile man!

description: The account of Karna's life. Drona's curse-Karna becomes Rama's pupil
sn: यथेयं गौर्हता मूढ प्रमत्तेन त्वया मम। प्रमत्तस्य तथारातिः शिरस्ते पातयिष्यति॥ शप्तः प्रसादयामास कर्णस्तं द्विजसत्तमम्। गोभिर्घनैश्च रत्नैश्च स चैनं पुनरब्रवीत्॥ न हि मेऽव्याहृतं कुर्यात् सर्वलोकोऽपि केवलम्। गच्छ वा तिष्ठ वा यद् वा कार्यं ते तत् समाच।।२८। इत्युक्तो ब्राह्मणेनाथ कर्णो दैन्यादधोमुखः। राममभ्यगमद् भीतस्तदेव मनसा स्मरन्।॥
en: As you have carelessly killed this my cow, so will your enemy cut off your head while you will be careless!-Though cursed, Karna still tried to gratify that foremost of Brahmanas by offering him kine and wealth and gems. The latter, however, once more answered him,-All the worlds will not falsify the words of mine. Go hence or remain, do what you like.-Thus addressed by the Brahmana, Karna, Handing down his head in depression, returned timidly to Rama."

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: नारद उवाच कर्णस्य बाहुवीर्येण प्रणयेन दमेन च। तुतोष भृगुशार्दूलो गुरुशुश्रूषया तथा॥
en: Narada said That foremost of Bhrigu's race Rama was well pleased with the power of Karna's arms, his love (for him), his self-restraint, and the services he rendered to his preceptor.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: तस्मै स विधिवत् कृत्स्नं ब्रह्मास्त्रं सनिवर्तनम्। प्रोवाचाखिलमव्यग्रं तपस्वी तत् तपस्विने॥
en: Ever practising ascetic penances, Rama cheerfully communicated, with due forms, to his disciple who practised penances everything about the Brahma weapon with the Mantras for withdrawing it.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: विदितास्त्रस्ततः कर्णो रममाणोऽऽश्रमे भृगोः। चकार वै धनुर्वेदे यत्नमद्भुतविक्रमः॥
en: Having acquired a knowledge of that weapon, Karna began to live happily in Bhrigu's retreat, and highly powerful as he was, he devoted himself with great energy to the science of arms.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: ततः कदाचिद् रामस्तु चरन्नाश्रममन्तिकात्। कर्णेन सहितो धीमानुपवासेन कर्शितः॥
en: One day the highly intelligent Rama, while walking with Karna in the vicinity of his retreat, felt himsclf very weak for the fasts he had undergone.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: सुष्वाय जामदग्न्यस्तु विश्रम्भोत्पन्नसौहृदः। कर्णस्योत्सङ्ग आधाय शिरः क्लान्तमना गुरुः॥
en: From affection created by confidence, the tired son of Jamadagni, placing his head on Karna's lap, slept soundly.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: अथ कृमिः श्लेष्ममेदोमांसशोणितभोजनः। दारुणो दारुणस्पर्शः कर्णस्याभ्याशमागतः॥
en: While his preceptor was thus sleeping (with head] on his lap, a dreadful worm, whose bite was very painful and which lived on phlegm and fat and flesh and blood, appeared before Karna.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: स तस्योरुमथासाद्य बिभेद रुधिराशनः। न चैनमशकत् क्षेप्तुं हन्तुं वापि गुरोर्भयात्॥
en: Getting at Karna's thigh, that blooddrinking worm began to pierce it. Lest his preceptor might get up, Karna could neither throw away nor kill that animal.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: संदश्यमानस्तु तथा कृमिणा तेन भारत। गुरोः प्रबोधनाशङ्की तमुपैक्षत सूर्यजः॥
en: Though his limb was cut through by that worm, O Bharata, the son of Surya, lest his preceptor should awake, allowed it to do its pleasure.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: कणस्तु वेदनां धैर्यादसह्यां विनिगृह्य ताम्। अकम्पयन्नव्यथयन् धारयामास भार्गवम्॥
en: Though the pain was unbearable, Karna endured it with heroic patience, and continued to hold Bhrigu's son on his lap, without trembling in the least and without displaying any sign of pain.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: यदास्य रुधिरेणाङ्ग परिस्पृष्टं भृगूद्वहः। तदाबुद्ध्यत तेजस्वी संत्रस्तश्चेदमब्रवीत्॥ अहोऽस्म्यशुचितां प्राप्तः किमिदं क्रियते त्वया। कथयस्व भयं त्यक्त्वा याथातथ्यमिदं मम॥
en: When at last Karna's blood touched the body of the highly energetic Rama, the latter awoke and said these words in fear,-Alas, I have been polluted. What are you doing. Tell me, without any fear, what is the truth of this matter.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: तस्य कर्णस्तदाऽऽचष्ट कृमिणा परिभक्षणम्। ददर्श रामस्तं चापि कृमि सूकरसंनिभम्॥
en: Then Karna informed him of that worm's bite. Rama saw that worm which was like a hog in shape.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: अष्टपादं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्र सूचीभिरिव संवृतम्। रोमभिः संनिरुद्धाङ्गमलर्कं नाम नामतः॥
en: It had eight feet and very sharp teeth, and was covered with bristles pointed like needles. Its name was 'Alarka, its limbs were then shrunk [with fear].

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: स दृष्टमात्रो रामेण कृमि: प्राणानवासृजत्। तस्मिन्नेवासृजि क्लिन्नस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: As soon as Rama looked at it, the worm died melting in that blood which it had drawn. All this appeared wonderful.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षे ददृशे विश्वरूपः करालवान्। राक्षसो लोहितग्रीवः कृष्णाङ्गो मेघवाहनः॥
en: A Rakshasa of terrible form, dark in hue, of a red neck, capable of assuming forms at will, and staying on the clouds was seen in the sky.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: स रामं प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा बभाषे पूर्णमानसः। स्वस्ति ते भृगुशार्दूल गमिष्येऽहं यथागतम्॥ मोक्षितो नरकादस्माद् भवता मुनिसत्तम। भद्रं तवास्तु वन्दे त्वां प्रियं मे भवता कृतम्॥
en: His object fulfilled, the Rakshasa, with joined palms addressed Rama, saying, O best of ascetics, you have saved me from this hell! Blessed by you, I worship you have donc me good.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: तमुवाच महाबाहुर्जामदग्न्यः प्रतापवान्। कस्त्वं कस्माच्च नरकं प्रतिपन्नो ब्रवीहि तत्॥
en: The highly energetic and the mighty armed son of Jamadagni said to him,-Who are you? And why did you fall into hell? Tell me all this.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: सोऽब्रवीदहमासं प्राग्दंशो नाम महासुरः। पुरा देवयुगे तात भृगोस्तुल्यवया इव॥
en: He answered,-Formerly I was a great Asura by the name of Dansha. In the Krita cycle, O sire, I was of the same age with Bhrigu.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: सोऽहं भृगोः सुदयितां भार्यामपहरं बलात्। महर्षेरभिशापेन कृमिभूतोऽपतं भुवि।॥
en: I ravished the dearly-loved wife that sage. Cursed by him I fell down on the Earth in the form of a worm.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: अब्रवीद्धि स मां क्रुद्धस्तव पूर्वपितामहः। मूत्रश्लेष्माशनः पाप निरयं प्रतिपत्स्यसे॥
en: In anger your ancestor said to me, living on urine and phlegm, O wretch, you will live in hell.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: शापस्यान्तो भवेद् ब्रह्मन्नित्येवं तमथाब्रवम्। भविता भार्गवाद् रामादिति मामब्रवीद् भृगुः॥
en: I then begged him, saying-When, O Brahmana, will this curse end?-Bhrigu replied, saying-This curse shall end through Rama of my family.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: सोऽहमेनां गतिं प्राप्तो यथा न कुशलं तथा त्वया साधो समागम्य विमुक्तः पापयोनितः॥
en: It was for this I had led a life like one of uncleaned soul! O righteous one, by you, however, I have been rescued from that sinful life.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: एवमुक्त्वा नमस्कृत्य ययौ रामं महासुरः। रामः कर्णं च सक्रोधमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having said so, the great Asura, bowing to Rama, went away. Then Rama wrathfully addressed Karna, saying.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: अतिदुःखमिदं मूढ न जातु ब्राह्मणः सहेत्। क्षत्रियस्येव ते धैर्यं कामया सत्यमुच्यताम्॥
en: O fool, no Brahmana could bear such a pain! Your patience is like that of a Kshatriya! Tell me the truth, without fear.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: कर्णः शापाद् ब्रह्मक्षत्रान्तरे जातं सूतं मां विद्धि भार्गव॥ तमुवाच ततः भीतः प्रसादयन्।
en: Thus asked, Karna, fearing to be cursed, and trying to please him, said, O you of Bhrigu's race know me for a Suta, a race originating from the intermixture of Brahmanas with Kshatriyas.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: राधेयः कर्ण इति मां प्रवदन्ति जना भुवि। प्रसादं कुरु मे ब्रह्मन्नस्त्रलुब्धस्य भार्गव॥
en: People call me Karna the son of Radha! O you of Bhrigu's race, be propitiated with my poor self who have thus behaved for mastering the weapons.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: पिता गुरुर्न संदेहो वेदविद्याप्रदः प्रभुः। अतो भार्गव इत्युक्तं मया गोत्रं तवान्तिक॥
en: Forsooth, a reverend preceptor in the Vedas and other branches of learning is one's father! It was for this that I introduced myself to you as a person of your family.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: तमुवाच भृगुश्रेष्ठः सरोषः प्रदहन्निवा भूमौ निपतितं दीनं वेपमानं कृताञ्जलिम्॥ यस्मान्मिथ्योपचरितो ह्यस्त्रलोभादिह त्वया। तस्मादेतन ते मूढ ब्रह्मास्त्रं प्रतिभास्यति॥
en: Unto the cheerless and trembling Karna, that foremost one of Bhrigu's race, smiling though angry, said to the cheerless and trembling Karna who was lying on Earth with joined hands, since you have from avarice of weapons, behaved here falsely, therefore, O wretch, this Brahma weapon shall not remain in your remembrance.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: अन्यत्र वधकालात् ते सदृशेन समीयुषः। अब्राह्मणे न हि ब्रह्म ध्रुवं तिष्ठेत् कदाचन॥
en: Since you are not a Brahmana, this Brahma weapon shall not, up to the time of your death, live in you when you will be engaged with a warrior equal to yourself.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: गच्छेदानीं न ते स्थानमनृतस्येह विद्यते। न त्वया सदृशो युद्धे भविता क्षत्रियो भुवि॥
en: Go hence, this is not the place for a person who behaves falsely. On Earth, no Kshatriya will be your equal in battle.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: एवमुक्तः स रामेण न्यायेनोपजगाम हा दुर्योधनमुपागम्य कृतोस्त्रोऽस्मीति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus addressed by Rama, Karna came away, having duly taken his permission. Arriving then before Duryodhana, he informed him, saying-I have learnt all weapons.

description: Karna's trial. Jamadagni sleeps on his lap-His thigh is bored. Jamadagni's curse
sn: एवमुक्तः स रामेण न्यायेनोपजगाम हा दुर्योधनमुपागम्य कृतोस्त्रोऽस्मीति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus addressed by Rama, Karna came away, having duly taken his permission. Arriving then before Duryodhana, he informed him, saying-I have learnt all weapons.

sn: नारद उवाच कर्णस्तु समवाप्यैवमस्त्रं भार्गवनन्दनात्। दुर्योधनेन सहितो मुमुदे भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Narada Said Having thus learnt the use of weapons from Rama of Bhrigu's race, Karna began to live happily in the company of Duryodhana, O foremost of Bharata's race.

sn: ततः कदाचिद् राजानः समाजग्मुः स्वयंवरे। कलिङ्गविषये राजन् राज्ञश्चित्राङ्गदस्य च॥
en: Once on a time, O monarch, many kings went to a Svayamvara at the capital of Chitrangada, the king of the Kalingas.

sn: श्रीमद्राजपुरं नाम नगरं तत्र भारत। राजानः शतशस्तत्र कन्यार्थे समुपागमन्॥
en: That prosperous city, O Bharata, was known by the name of Rajapura. Hundreds of kings went there for securing the hand of the maiden.

sn: श्रुत्वा दुर्योधनस्तत्र समेतान् सर्वपार्थिवान्। रथेन काञ्चनाङ्गेन कर्णेन सहितो ययौ॥
en: Hearing that various kings had come there, : Duryodhana also, on his golden car, proceeded there, accompanied by Karna.

sn: ततः स्वयंवरे तस्मिन् सम्प्रवृत्ते महोत्सवे। समाजग्मुर्नृपतयः कन्यार्थे नृपसत्तम॥
en: When the festivities commenced in that Svayamvara various kings, O best of kings, came there for the hand of the maiden.

sn: शिशुपालो जरासंधो भीष्मको वक्र एव च। कपोतरोमा नीलश्च रुक्मी च दृढविक्रमः॥ शृगालश्च महाराजः स्त्रीराज्याधिपतिश्च यः। अशोकः शतधन्वा च भोजो वीरश्च नामतः॥
en: There were amongst them Shisupala, Jarasandha, Bhishmaka, Vakra, Kaportroman, Nila, Rukmi of steady prowess, Shrigala who was ruler of the kingdom of females, Ashoka, Satadhanvan and the heroic king of the Bhojas.

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो दक्षिणां दिशमाश्रिताः। म्लेच्छाचार्याश्च राजानः प्राच्योदीच्यास्तथैव च॥
en: Besides these, many others who lived in the Deccan and many preceptors of the Mlechchha tribes, and many kings from the East and the North, O Bharata, came there.

sn: काञ्चनाङ्गदिनः सर्वे शुद्धजाम्बूनदप्रभाः। सर्वे भास्वरदेहाश्च व्याघ्रा इव वलोत्कटाः॥
en: All of them were bedecked with golden Angadas and shone resplendent like pure gold. Of shining persons they were like tigers of fierce might.

sn: ततः समुपविष्टेषु तेषु राजसु भारत। विवेश रङ्गं सा कन्या धात्रीवर्षवरान्विता॥
en: After all those kings had taken their seats, O Bharata, the maiden entered the arena, accompanied by her nurse and a guard of eunuchs.

sn: ततः संश्राव्यमाणेषु राज्ञां नामसु भारत। अत्यकामद् धार्तराष्ट्र सा कन्या वरवर्णिनी॥
en: The names of the kings being mentioned to her that fair maiden passed by the son of Dhritarashtra as she had passed others before him.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तु कौरव्यो नामर्षयत लङ्घनम्। प्रत्यषेधच्च तां कन्यामसत्कृत्य नराधिपान्॥
en: Duryodhana, however, of Kuru's race could not bear that insult of self. Disregarding all the kings, he ordered the maiden to stop.

sn: स वीर्यमदमत्तत्वाद् भीष्मद्रोणावुपाश्रितः। रथमारोप्य तां कन्यामाजहार नराधिपः॥
en: Elated with the pride of power and relying upon Bhishma and Drona, king Duryodhana taking up that maiden on his car, carried her away forcibly.

sn: तमन्वगाद् रथी खड्गी बद्धगोधाङ्गद्धलित्रवान्। कर्णः शस्त्रभृतां श्रेष्ठः पृष्ठतः पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Armed with sword, clad in mail, and his fingers cased in leathern fences, Karna, that foremost of all holders of weapons, riding on his car, followed Duryodhana.

sn: ततो विमर्दः सुमहान् राज्ञामासीद् युयुत्सताम्। संनह्यतां तनुत्राणि रथान् योजयतामपि॥
en: A great tumult then took place among the kings, all the whom were bent upon fighting.-Put on your coats of mail. Get the cars ready!-(These were the words that were heard).

sn: तेऽभ्यधावन्त संक्रुद्धाः कर्णदुर्योधनावुभौ। शरवर्षाणि मुञ्चन्तो मेघाः पर्वतयोरिव॥
en: Filled with ire, they pursued Karna and Duryodhana, pouring their shafts upon them like masses of clouds pouring rain upon a couple of hills.

sn: कर्णस्तेषामापततामेकैकेन शरेण ह धषि च शरवातान् पातयामास भूतले॥
en: As they thus pursued them, Karna struck down their bows and arrows on the ground, each with a single arrow.

sn: ततो विधनुष: कांश्चित् कांश्चिदुद्यतकार्मुकान्। कांश्चिच्चोद्वहतो बाणान् रथशक्तिगदास्तथा॥
en: Amongst them some were deprived of bow, some rushed bow in hand, some were on the point of discharging their arrows, and some pursued them, armed with darts and maces.

sn: लाघवाद् व्याकुलीकृत्य कर्णः प्रहरतां वरः। हतसूतांश्च भूयिष्ठानवजिग्ये नराधिपान्॥
en: Endued with great lightness of hands, Karna, that foremost of all strikers, assailed them all. He deprived many kings of their drivers, and thus defeated them.

sn: ते स्वयं वाहयन्तोऽश्वान् पाहि पाहीति वादिनः। व्यपेयुस्ते रणं हित्वा राजानो भग्नमानसाः॥
en: They then themselves took up the reins of their horses, and saying.-Go away, go away-turned away from the battle with depressed hearts.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तु कर्णेन पाल्यमानोऽभ्ययात् तदा। हृष्टः कन्यामुपादाय नगरं नागसाह्वयम्॥
en: Protected by Karna, Duryodhana also came away, with a gladdened heart, bringing with him the maiden to Hastinapura.

sn: नारद उवाच आविष्कृतबलं कर्णं श्रुत्वा राजा स मागधः। आह्वयद् द्वैरथेनाजी जरासंधो महीपतिः॥ तयोः समभवद् युद्धं दिव्यास्त्रविदुषोईयोः। युधि नानाप्रहरणैरन्योन्यमभिवर्षतोः॥
en: Narada said Hearing of Karna's power the king of the Magadhas, Jarasandha, challenged him to a single combat. Both of them were masters of celestial weapons. A dreadful battle took place between them in which they struck each other with various kinds of weapons.

sn: क्षीणबाणौ विधनुषौ भग्नखड्गौ महीं गतौ। बाहुभिः समसज्जेतामुभावपि बलान्वितौ॥
en: At last when their arrows were run out, and bows and swords were broken, and they both lost their cars, they began, powerful as they were, to fight with bare arms.

sn: बाहुकण्टकयुद्धेन तस्य कर्णोऽथ युध्यतः। बिभेद सन्धिं देहस्य जरया श्लेषितस्य हि॥
en: While engaged with him a dreadful encounter with bare arms, Karna was about to cut the two portions of his antagonist's body that had been joined by Jara.

sn: स विकारं शरीरस्य दृष्ट्वा नृपतिरात्मनः। प्रीतोऽस्मीत्यब्रवीत् कर्णं वैरमुत्सृज्य दूरतः॥
en: Feeling himself very much pained, and giving up desire of hostility, the king of Magadha addressed Karma, saying,-I am pleased.

sn: प्रीत्या ददौ स कर्णाय मालिनी नगरीमथ। अड्रेषु नरशार्दूल स राजाऽऽसीत् सपत्नजित्॥ पालयामास चम्पां च कर्णः परबलार्दनः। दुर्योधनस्यानुमते तवापि विदितं तथा॥
en: Out of friendship he then gave to Karna the town Malini. Before this, that foremost of men and subjugator of all enemies (Karna), had been king of the Angas only, but from that time that grinder of hostile forces, began to rule over Champa also, as desired by Duryodhana, as you know.

sn: एवं शस्त्रप्रतापेन प्रथितः सोऽभवत् क्षितौ। त्वद्धितार्थं सुरेन्द्रेण भिक्षितो वर्मकुण्डले॥ स दिव्ये सहजे प्रादात् कुण्डले परमार्जिते। सहजं कवचं चापि मोहितो देवमायया।॥
en: Thus Karna became known on Earth for the strength of his arms. When, for your well-being the king of gods begged of him his (natural) coat-of-mail and ear-rings, stupefied by celestial illusion, he gave away those precious things.

sn: विमुक्तः कुण्डलाभ्यां च सहजेन च वर्मणा। निहतो विजयेनाजौ वासुदेवस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Deprived of his ear-rings and his natural armour, he was killed by Arjuna before Vasudeva.

sn: ब्राह्मणस्याभिशापेन रामस्य च महात्मनः। कुन्त्याच वरदानेन मायया च शतक्रतोः॥ भीष्मावमानात् संख्यायां रथस्यार्धानुकीर्तनात्। शल्यात् तेजोवधाच्चापि वासुदेवनयेन च॥॥ रुद्रस्य देवराजस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च। कुबेरद्रोणयोश्चैव कृपस्य च पहात्मनः॥ अस्त्राणि दिव्यान्यादाय युधि गाण्डीवधन्वना। हतो वैकर्तनः कर्णो दिवाकरसमद्युतिः॥
en: On account of a Brahmana's curse, as also of the curse of the great Rama, of the boon granted to Kunti and the illusion practised on him by Indra, of his being belittled by Bhishma as only half-a car-warrior, behind Rathas and Atirathas, of the destruction of his energy caused by Shalya, of Vasudeva's policy, and, lastly, of the celestial weapons acquired by Arjuna from Rudra and Indra and Yama and Varuna and Kuvera and Drona and the illustrious Kripa, Arjuna succeeded in killing. Vikartana's son Karna of solar effulgence.

sn: एवं शप्तस्तव भ्राता बहुभिश्चापि वञ्चितः। न शोच्यः पुरुषव्याघ्र युद्धेन निधनं गतः॥
en: Thus had your brother been cursed and beguiled by many! As, however, he has fallen in battle, you should not grieve for that foremost of man.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतावदुक्त्वा देवर्षिविरराम स नारदः। युधिष्ठिरस्तु राजर्षिर्दथ्यौ शोकपरिप्लुतः॥
en: Saying so the celestial Rishi Narada became silent. the royal sage Yudhishthira, filled with sorrow began to meditate.

sn: तं दीनमनसं वीरं शोकोपहतमातुरम्। निःश्वसन्तं यथा नागं पर्यश्रुनयनं तथा॥ कुन्ती शोकपरीताङ्गी दुःखोपहतचेतना। अब्रवीन्मधुराभाषा काले वचनमर्थवत्॥
en: Seeing that hero cheerless and unnerved by grief, sighing like a snake and shedding profuse tears, Kunti, herself filled with grief and almost beside herself with sorrow, addressed him in these sweet but weighty

sn: युधिष्ठिर महाबाहो नैनं शोचितुमर्हसि। जहि शोकं महाप्राज्ञ शृणु चेदं वचो मम॥
en: O mighty-armed Yudhishthira, you should not give way to sorrow thus! O you of at wisdom, destroy this grief and listen to what I say.

sn: यातितः स मया पूर्वं भ्राज्यं ज्ञापयितुं तव। भास्करेण च देवेन पित्रा धर्मभृतां वर॥
en: I tried formerly to inform Karna of his being your brother. The god Surya also, O best of all righteous men, did the same.

sn: यद्वाच्यं हितकामेन सुहृदा हितमिच्छता। तथा दिवाकरेणोक्तः स्वप्नान्ते मम चाग्रतः॥
en: That god said to Karna in a dream and once more in my presence, all that a well-wishing friend, from desire of good, should say.

sn: न चैनमशकद् भानुरहं वा स्नेहकारणैः। पुरा प्रत्यनुनेतुं वा नेतुं वाप्येकतां त्वया॥
en: Neither by affliction nor by reasons could Surya or myself succeed in pacifying him or inducing him to join you.

sn: ततः कालपरीतः स वैरस्योद्धरणे रतः। प्रतीपकारी युष्माकमिति चोपेक्षितो मया॥
en: Yielding to the influence of Time, he was determined on creating enmity with you. As he was determined upon doing injuries to you all, I myself gave up the attempt.'

sn: इत्युक्तो धर्मराजस्तु मात्रा बाष्पाकुलेक्षणः। उवाच वाक्यं धर्मात्मा शोकव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Thus addressed by his mother, king Yudhishthira, with tearful eyes and heart shaken by grief, said:-

sn: भवत्या गूढमन्त्रत्वात् पीडितोऽस्मीत्युवाच ताम्॥ शशाप च महातेजाः सर्वलोकेषु योषितः। न गुह्यं धारयिष्यन्तीत्येवं दुःखसमन्वितः॥
en: 'For you having concealed your counsels, this great calamity has befallen me.' The highly energetic and the righteous king then, in sorrow, cursed all the women of the world, saying,-'Henceforth no woman shall succeed in keeping a secret."

sn: स राजा पुत्रपौत्राणां सम्बन्धिसुहृदां तदा। स्मरन्नुद्विग्नहृदयो बभूवोद्विग्नचेतनः॥
en: Recollecting his sons and grandsons and kinsmen and friends, the king then became filled with anxiety and grief.

sn: ततः शोकपरीतात्मा सधूम इव पावकः। निर्वेदमगमद् धीमान् राजा संतापपीडितः॥
en: Stricken with sorrow, the intelligent king, resembling a fire covered with smoke, was filled with despair. Then the wise king endued with grief like the fire covered in the grip of dense smoke and thus he sank in agony.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरस्तु धर्मात्मा शोकव्याकुलचेतनः। शुशोच दुःखसंतप्तः स्मृत्वा कर्णं महारथम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said The righteous Yudhishthira, with an agitated heart and burning with grief, began to grieve for that powerful car warrior Karna.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: आविष्टो दुःखशोकाभ्यां निःश्वसंश्च पुनः पुनः। दृष्ट्वाऽर्जुनमुवाचेदं वचनं शोककर्शितः॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच यफ्रेक्ष्यमाचरिष्याम वृष्णयन्धकपुरे वयम्। ज्ञातीन् निष्पुरुषान् कृत्वा नेमां प्राप्स्याम दुर्गतिम्॥
en: Sighing repeatedly, he addressed Arjuna, saying,-'If, O Arjuna, we had lived like mendicants in the cities of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas, then we would not have been visited by this miserable end, for our having exterminated our kinsmen.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: अमित्रा नः समृद्धार्था वृत्तार्थाः कुरवः किलः। आत्मानमात्मना हत्वा किं धर्मफलमाप्नुमः॥
en: Our enemies, the Kurus, have gained in prosperity, while we have been deprived of all the objects of life, for what fruits of righteousness can be ours when we have been guilty of self-destruction?

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: धिगस्तु क्षात्रमाचारं धिगस्तु बलपौरुषम्। धिगस्त्वमर्षं येनेमामापदं गमिता वयम्॥
en: Fie on the practices of Kshatriyas, fie on might and valour, and fie on anger, since through these such a calamity has overtaken us.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: साधु क्षमा दमः शौचं वैराग्यं चाप्यमत्सरः। अहिंसा सत्यवचनं नित्यानि वनचारिणाम्॥
en: Blessed are forgiveness, and self-control, and purity, with renunciation and humility and abstention from injury, and truthfulness which are all practised by hermits dwelling in forests.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: वयं तु लोभान्मोहाच्च दम्भं मानं च संश्रिताः। इमामवस्थां सम्प्राप्ता राज्यलाभबुभुत्सया॥
en: Full of pride and haughtiness, we however, through covetousness and folly and from desire of enjoying the kingdom, have fallen into this plight.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: त्रैलोक्यस्यापि राज्येन नास्मान् कश्चित् प्रहर्षयेत्। बान्धवान् निहतान् दृष्ट्वा पृथिव्यां विजयैषिणः॥
en: Seeing those kinsmen of ours that were determined on acquiring the sovereignty of the world killed on the field of battle, we have been so much laden with grief that one cannot gladden us by giving us even the sovereignty of the three worlds.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: ते वयं पृथिवीहेतोरवध्यान् पृथिवीश्वरान्। सम्परित्यज्य जीवामो हीनार्था हतबान्धवाः॥
en: Alas, having killed for the sake of the Earth, such kings as deserved not to be slain by us, we are carrying on the burden of existence, deprived of friends and of the very objects of life.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: आमिषे गृध्यमानानामशुभं वै शुनामिव। आमिषं चैव नो हीष्टमामिषस्य विवर्जनम्॥
en: Like a pack of dogs fighting one another for a piece of meat, a great calamity has befallen us. That piece of meat is no longer dear to us. On the other hand, it shall be thrown aside.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: न पृथिव्या सकलया न सुवर्णस्य राशिभिः। न गवाश्वेन सर्वेण ते त्याज्या य इमे हताः॥
en: They who have been killed should not have been killed for the sake of even the whole Earth of mountains of gold, or all the horses and kine in this world.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: काममन्युपरीतास्ते क्रोधहर्षसमन्विताः। मृत्युयानं समारुह्य गता वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: All of them filled with envy and seeking all earthly objects, and influenced by anger and pleasure, following the road of Death, have repaired to the regions of Yama.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: बहुकल्याणसंयुक्तानिच्छन्ति पितरः सुतान्। तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण सत्येन च तितिक्षया॥
en: Practising asceticism, Brahmacharya, truth and renunciation, fathers wish for sons endued with every kind of prosperity.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: उपवासैस्तथेज्याभिव्रतकौतुकमङ्गलैः। लभन्ते मातरो गर्भान्मासान् दश च बिभ्रति॥
en: Likewise by facts and sacrifices and vows and sacred rites and sacred ceremonies, mothers conceive. They then hold the foetus for ten months.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: यदि स्वस्ति प्रजायन्ते जाता जीवन्ति वा यदि। सम्भाविता जातबलास्ते दधुर्यदि नः सुखम्॥ इह चामुत्र चैवेति कृपणाः फलहेतवः।
en: Passing their days in misery and in expectation of fruit, they always ask themselves-Shall these come out of the womb safely? Shall these live after birth? Shall they grow in power and be honoured on Earth? Will they give us happiness in this and the next world?

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: तासामयं समुद्योगो निर्वृत्तः केवलोऽफलः।१६।। यदासां निहताः पुत्रा युवानो मृष्टकुण्डलाः। अभुक्त्वा पार्थिवान् भोगानृणान्यनपहाय च॥ पितृभ्यो देवताभ्यश्च गता वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: But, all these acts became fruitless. Alas, since their young sons, wearing shining carrings, have been killed, therefore, their hopes have not been realised. Without having enjoyed the sweets of this world, and without having paid off the debts they owed to their fathers and the gods, they have gone to Yama's abode.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: यदैषामम्ब पितरौ जातकामावुभावपि। संजातधनरत्नेषु तदैव निहता नृपाः॥
en: Alas, O mother, those kings have been killed just at that time, when their parents expected to reap the fruits of their power and riches.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: संयुक्ताः काममन्युभ्यां क्रोधहर्षासमञ्जसाः। न ते जयफलं किंचिद् भोक्तारो जातु कर्हिचित्॥
en: They were always envious and hankered after earthly objects, and always yielded to anger and joy. Therefore they could never expect to enjoy at any time or any place the fruits of victory.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: पञ्चालानां कुरूणां च हता एव हि ये हताः। न चेत् सर्वानयं लोकः पश्येत् स्वेनैव कर्मणा॥
en: I think the Panchalas and the Kurus that have been killed (in this battle) have been lost, otherwise he who has killed would, by that act of his, obtain all blissful regions.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: वयमेवास्य लोकस्य विनाशे कारणं स्मृताः। धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रेषु तत् सर्वं प्रतिपत्स्यति॥
en: We are the root of the destruction that has overtaken the world. The fault, however, should be attributed the of Dhritarashtra.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: सदैव निकृतिप्रज्ञो द्वेष्टा मायोपजीवनः। मिथ्याविनीतः सततमस्मास्वनपकारिषु॥
en: Duryodhana's heart was always wily. Always malicious, he addicted to to sons deception. Although we never offended him, yet he always behaved treacherously towards us.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: न सकामा वयं ते च न चास्माभिर्न तैर्जितम्। न तैर्भुक्तेयमवनिर्न नार्यो गीतवादितम्॥
en: We have not gained our object, nor have they gained theirs. We have not defeated them, nor have they defeated us. The Dhartarashtras could not enjoy this Earth, nor could they enjoy women and music.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: नामात्यसुहृदां वाक्यं न च श्रुतवतां श्रुतम्। न रत्नानि पराानि न भून द्रविणागमः॥
en: They did not listen to the counsels of ministers and friends and men well read in the scriptures. They could not, indeed, enjoy their rich gems and well-equipped treasury and vast territories.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: अस्मद्वेषेण संतप्तः सुखं न स्मेह विन्दति। ऋद्धिमस्मासु तां दृष्ट्वा विवर्णो हरिणः कृशः॥ धृतराष्ट्रश्च नृपतिः सौबलेन निवेदितः। तं पिता पुत्रगृद्धित्वादनुमेनेऽनये स्थितः॥
en: Burning with the hate they cherished against us, they could not enjoy happiness and peace. Witnessing advancement, Duryodhana became colourless, pale and emaciated. Suvala's son informed king Dhritarashtra of this. Like an indulgent father, Dhritarashtra tolerated the evil policy of his Our son.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: अनपेक्ष्यैव पितरं गाङ्गेयं विदुरं तथा। असंशयं क्षयं राजा यथैवाहं तथा गतः॥ अनियम्याशुचिं लुब्धं पुत्रं कामवशानुगम्।
