en: Forsooth, by disregarding Vidura and the great son of Ganga, and neglecting to restrain his wicked and covetous son entirely under the influence of his passion, the king has met with destruction like my poor self.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: यशसः पतितो दीप्ताद् घातयित्वा सहोदरान्॥ इमौ हि वृद्धौ शोकाग्नौ प्रक्षिप्य स सुयोधनः। अस्मत्प्रद्वेषसंयुक्तः पापबुद्धिः सदैव ह॥ को हि बन्धुः कुलीनः संस्तथा ब्रूयात् सुहृज्जने। यथासाववदद् वाक्यं युयुत्सुः कृष्णसंनिधौ॥
en: Forsooth, Suyodhana, having caused his uterine brothers to be king and having cast this old pair into burning grief, has fallen off from shining glory. Burning with the hate he bore to us, Duryodhana was always sinful at heart. What other highly-born kinsman could use such language towards kinsman as he, with a view of fight, actually used in the presence of Krishna?

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: आत्मनो हि वयं दोषाद् विनष्टाः शाश्वतीः समाः। प्रदहन्तो दिशः सर्वा भास्वरा इव तेजसा॥
en: We also have through Duryodhana's folly, been lost for ever, like suns burning everything around them with their own heat.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: सोऽस्माकं वैरपुरुषो दुर्मतिः प्रग्रहं गतः। दुर्योधनकृते ह्येतत् कुलं नो विनिपातितम्॥ अवध्यानां वधं कृत्वा लोके प्राप्ताः स्म वाच्यताम्।
en: The wicked man, that embodiment of enmity, was our evil star. Alas, Alas, for Duryodhana's deeds alone, this race of ours has been rooted out. Having killed those whom we should never have killed, we have incurred the blame of the world.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: कुलस्यास्यान्तकरणं दुर्मतिं पापपूरुषम्॥ राजा राष्ट्रेश्वरं कृत्वा धृतराष्ट्रोऽद्य शोचति।
en: Having installed that wicked prince of sinful acts, that exterminator of his race, as the monarch, King Dhritarashtra is obliged to grieve today.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: हताः शूराः कृतं पापं विषयः स्वो विनाशितः॥ हत्वा नो विगतो मन्युः शोको मां रुन्धयत्ययम्।
en: Our heroic enemies have been killed. We have committed sin. His wealth and kingdom are gone. Having killed them, our anger has been pacified. But grief is overcoming me.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: धनंजय कृतं पापं कल्याणेनोपहन्यते॥ ख्यापनेनानुतापेन दानेन तपसापि वा। निवृत्त्या तीर्थगमनाच्छुतिस्मृतिजपेन वा॥ त्यागवांश्च पुनः पापं नालंकर्तुमिति श्रुतिः।
en: O Dhananjaya, sin is always expiated by pious acts, by giving wide publicity to it, by repentance, by alms giving, by penances, by sojourn to Tirthas after renunciation of everything, by constant meditation on the scriptures. Of all these, he who has practised renunciation is believed to be incapable of committing fresh sins.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: त्यागवाजन्ममरणे नाप्नोतीति श्रुतिर्यदा॥ प्राप्तवा कृतमतिर्ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा।
en: The Shrutis say that he who practices renunciation escapes from birth and death, and obtaining the right way, that person of controlled mind, attains Brahman.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: स धनंजय निर्द्वन्द्वो मुनिर्ज्ञानसमन्वितः॥ वनमामन्त्र्य वः सर्वान् गमिष्यामि परंतप।
en: I shall, therefore, O Dhananjaya, go to the forest, with your permission, O scorcher of enemies, disregarding all the pairs of opposites, adopting the vow of silence, and walking in the way pointed out by knowledge.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: न हि कृत्स्नतमो धर्मः शक्यः प्राप्तुमिति श्रुतिः॥ परिग्रहवता तन्मे प्रत्यक्षमरिसूदन।
en: O destroyer of foes, the Shrutis say it, and I myself have seen it with my eyes, that one who is addicted to worldly objects can never obtain any kind of religious merit.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: मया निसृष्टं पापं हि परिग्रहमभीप्सता॥ जन्मक्षयनिमित्तं च प्राप्तुं शक्यमिति श्रुतिः।
en: Desirous of obtaining worldly objects, I have committed sin, which as the Shrutis declare, begets birth and death.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: स परिग्रहमुत्सृज्य कृत्स्नं राज्यं सुखानि च॥ गमिष्यामि विनिर्मुक्तो विशोको निर्ममः क्वचित्।
en: Abandoning the whole of my kingdom, therefore, and all the worldly objects, I shall go to the forest, escaping from the worldly fetters, freed from grief, and without affection for anything.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: प्रशाधि त्वमिमामुर्वी क्षेमां निहतकण्टकाम्॥ न ममार्थोऽस्ति राज्येन भोगैर्वा कुरुनन्दन।
en: Do you govern this Earth, on which peace has been restored, and which has been freed of all its thorns. O best of Kuru's race, I do not require kingdom or pleasure.'

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। उपारमत् ततः पार्थः कनीयानभ्यभाषत॥
en: Having said so, King Yudhishthira just stopped. His younger brother Arjuna then addressed him as follows.

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: प्रशाधि त्वमिमामुर्वी क्षेमां निहतकण्टकाम्॥ न ममार्थोऽस्ति राज्येन भोगैर्वा कुरुनन्दन।
en: Do you govern this Earth, on which peace has been restored, and which has been freed of all its thorns. O best of Kuru's race, I do not require kingdom or pleasure.'

description: Yudhishthira bewails to Arjuna for the destruction of kinsmen
sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। उपारमत् ततः पार्थः कनीयानभ्यभाषत॥
en: Having said so, King Yudhishthira just stopped. His younger brother Arjuna then addressed him as follows.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथार्जुन उवाचेदमधिक्षिप्त इवाक्षमी। अभिनीततरं वाक्यं दृढवादपराक्रमः॥ दर्शयन्नैन्द्रिरात्मानमुग्रमुग्रपराक्रमः। स्पयमानो महातेजाः सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Like a person reluctant to forgive an insult, the highly energetic Arjuna of keen speech and prowess, betraying great fierceness and licking the corners of his mouth, said smilingly these

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अर्जुन उवाच अहो दुःखमहो कृच्छ्रमहो वैक्लव्यमुत्तमम्। यत् कृत्वामानुषं कर्म त्यजेथाः श्रियमुत्तमाम्॥
en: 'O how painful, how distressing, I am sorry to see this great agitation of your heart, since having performed such a superhuman feat, you are deterinined to forsake the world,

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: शत्रून् हत्वा महीं लब्ध्वा स्वधर्मेणोपपादिताम्। एवंविधं कथं सर्वं त्यजेथा बुद्धिलाघवात्॥
en: Having killed your enemies, and having the sovereignty of the Earth, which has been won ever by observing of the duties of your own order, why should you give up everything through fickleness of heart?

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: क्लीबस्य हि कुतो राज्यं दीर्घसूत्रस्य वा पुनः। किमर्थं च महीपालानवधीः क्रोधमूर्छितः॥
en: Where on Earth has a eunuch or a procrastinating person acquired sovereignty? Why then did you beside yourself with anger, slay all the kings of the Earth.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: यो ह्याजिजीविषेद् भैक्ष्यं कर्मणा नैव कस्यचित्। समारम्भान् बुभूषेत हतस्वस्तिरकिंचनः। सर्वलोकेषु विख्यातो न पुत्रपशुसंहितः॥
en: He that would lead the life of a mendicant, cannot, by any act of his, enjoy the good things of Earth. Shorn of prosperity and other resources, he can never acquire fame on Earth or sons and animals.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: कापाली नृप पापिष्ठां वृत्तिमासाद्य जीवतः। संत्यज्य राज्यमृद्धं ते लोकोऽयं किं वदिष्यति॥
en: If, O king, abandoning this prosperous kingdom, you lead the wretched life of a mendicant, what will the world say of you?

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: सर्वारम्भान् समुत्सृज्य हतस्वस्तिरकिंचनः। कस्मादाशंससे भक्ष्यं कर्तुं प्राकृतवत् प्रभो॥
en: Why do you say that leaving aside all the good things of the Earth, shorn of prosperity, and of resources, you will live like a mendicant and a vulgar person.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अस्मिन् राजकुले जातो जित्वा कृत्स्नां वसुंधराम्। धर्मार्थावखिलौ हित्वा वनं मौढ्यात् प्रतिष्ठसे॥
en: You are born in a royal family. Having conquered the whole Earth, do you foolishly wish to live in the forest after for-saking everything of virtue of profit?

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: यदीमानि हवींषीह विमथिष्यन्त्यसाधवः। भवता विप्रहीणानि प्राप्तं त्वामेव किल्बिषम्॥
en: In your absence, dishonest men will despoil sacrifices. That sin will certainly contaminate you.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: आकिंचन्यं मुनीनां च इति वै नहुघोऽब्रवीत्। कृत्वा नृशंसं ह्यधने धिगस्त्वधनतामिह॥
en: Having perpetrated many wicked acts in a state of poverty, king Nahusha spoke ill of that state and said that poverty is for recluses.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अश्वस्तनमृषीणां हि विद्यते वेद तद् भवान्। यं त्विमं धर्ममित्याहुर्धनादेष प्रवर्तते॥
en: To make no provision for the morrow is a practice that suits Rishis. You know this well! The religion of kings, however, depends entirely on wealth.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: धर्मं संहरते तस्य धनं हरति यस्य सः। ह्रियमाणे धने राजन् वयं कस्य क्षमेमहि॥
en: One who robs another of riches, robs him of his religion as well. Who amongst us, therefore, O king, would forgive an act of depriving us of our wealth.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अभिशस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति दरिद्रं पावतः स्थितम्। दरिद्रं पातकं लोके न तच्छंसितुमर्हति॥
en: It is seen that a poor man, even when he stands hard by, is accused falsely. Poverty is a sin. You should not, therefore, speak high of poverty.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: पतितः शोच्यते राजन् निर्धनश्चापि शोच्यते। विशेष नाधिगच्छामि पतितस्याधनस्य च॥
en: A degraded man as also a poor man, O king, have both to rue their fate, I see no difference between these two.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अर्थेभ्यो हि विवृद्धेभ्यः सम्भृतेभ्यस्ततस्ततः। क्रियाः सर्वाः प्रवर्तन्ते पर्वतेभ्य इवापगा:॥
en: The increased and deposited wealth like rivers from mountain begets all kinds of meritorious acts.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अर्थाद् धर्मश्च कामश्च स्वर्गश्चैव नराधिप। प्राणयात्रापि लोकस्य विना ह्यर्थं न सिद्ध्यति॥
en: From wealth originate all religious acts, all pleasures, and heaven itself, O king, Without wealth, a man cannot find the very means of maintaining his life.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अर्थेन हि विहीनस्य पुरुषस्याल्पमेधसः। विच्छिद्यन्ते क्रियाः सर्वा ग्रीष्मे कुसरितो यथा।॥
en: The acts of a person who, endued with little intelligence allows himself to be divested of wealth, are all dried up like shallow rivers in the summer.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: यस्यार्थास्तस्य मित्राणि यस्यार्थास्तस्य बान्धवाः। यस्यार्थाः स पुमॉल्लोके यस्यार्थाः स च पण्डितः।।
en: He who has wealth has friends. He who has wealth has kinsmen. He who has wealth is considered as a sincere man in the world. He who has wealth is regarded as a learned man.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अधनेनार्थकामेन नार्थः शक्यो विधित्सितुम्। अर्थरर्था निबध्यन्ते गजैरिव महागजाः॥
en: If a person who has no wealth desires to accomplish a particular object, he meets with failure. Wealth Wealth accumulates wealth, like elephants capturing (wild) elephants.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: धर्मः कामश्च स्वर्गश्च हर्षः क्रोधः श्रुतं दमः। अर्थादेतानि सर्वाणि प्रवर्तन्ते नराधिप।॥
en: Religious acts, pleasures, joy, courage, anger, learning, and sense of dignity, all originate from wealth, O king.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: धनात् कुलं प्रभवति धनाद् धर्म प्रवर्धते। नाधनस्यास्त्ययं लोको न परः पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: Wealth begets family prestige. wealth multiples one's religious merit. He who is without wealth has neither this world, nor the next,O foremost of men.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: नाधनो धर्मकृत्यानि यथावदनुतिष्ठति। धनाद्धि धर्मः स्त्रवति शैलादभि नदी यथा॥
en: The man who has no wealth cannot celebrate religious acts, for these originate from wealth, like rivers from a mountain.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: यः कृशार्थः कृशगवः कृशभृत्यः कृशातिथिः। सवै राजन् कृशो नाम न शरीरकृशः कृशः॥
en: He whose limbs are lean is not truly a lean man, but he who is lean in respect of horses and kine and servants and guests is truly so.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अवेक्षस्व यथान्यायं पश्य देवासुरं यथा। राजन् किमन्यज्जातीनां वधाद् गृद्ध्यन्ति देवताः॥
en: Judge truly, O kihg, and mark the conduct of the gods and the Danavas. O king, do the gods ever seek anything else than the destruction of their kinsmen (the Asuras)?

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: न चेद्धर्तव्यमन्यस्य कथं तद्धर्ममारभेत्। एतावानेव वेदेषु निश्चयः कविभिः कृतः॥
en: If the appropriation of another's wealth be not regarded as right, how, O monarch, will kings practise virtue on this Earth? Learned men have, in the Vedas, laid down this injunction.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अध्येतव्या त्रयी नित्यं भवितव्यं विपश्चिता। सर्वथा धनमाहार्यं यष्टव्यं चापि यत्नतः॥
en: The learned man have decreed that kings should live, reciting every day the three Vedas, seeking to acquire wealth, and carefully celebrating sacrifices with the wealth thus acquired.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: द्रोहाद् देवैरवाप्तानि दिवि स्थानानि सर्वशः। द्रोहात् किमन्यज्ज्ञातीनां गृद्ध्यन्ते येन देवताः॥
en: The gods, through civil war, have secured footing in the celestial region. When the very gods have won their prosperity through civil war, what fault can there be in such quarrels?

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: इति देवा व्यवसिता वेदवादाश्च शाश्वताः। अधीयतेऽध्यापयन्ते यजन्ते याजयन्ति च॥ कृत्स्नं तदेव तच्छेरूयो यदप्याददतेऽन्यतः। न पश्यामोऽनपकृतं धनं किंचित् क्वचिद् वयम्॥
en: Verily the gods, even behave thus. The eternal precepts of the Vedas also approve of it. To learn, teach, sacrifice, and assist at others sacrifices,-these are our primary duties. The wealth that kings appropriate from others, becomes the instrument of their prosperity. Wealth is never acquired without doing some injury to others.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: एवमेव हि राजानो जयन्ति पृथिवीमिमाम्। जित्वा ममेयं ब्रुवते पुत्रा इव पितुर्धनम्॥
en: It is even thus that kings conquer this world. Having conquered, they are justified to regard that wealth as theirs, just as sons speak of the wealth of their fathers as their own, The royal sages that have gone to heaven have described this to be the duty of kings.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: राजर्षयोऽपि ते स्वर्यो धर्मो ह्येषां निरुच्यते। यथैव पूर्णादुदधेः स्यन्दन्त्यापो दिशो दश॥
en: Like water flowing on every direction from a rising ocean, wealth goes on all sides from the treasuries of kings.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: एवं राजकुलाद् वित्तं पृथिवीं प्रति तिष्ठति। आसीदियं दिलीपस्य नृगस्य नहुषस्य च।॥
en: This Earth formerly belonged to king Dvilipa, Nahusha, Ambarisha, and Mandhatri. She is now yours.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: अम्बरीषस्य मान्धातुः पृथिवी सा त्वयि स्थिता। स त्वां द्रव्यमयो यज्ञः सम्प्राप्तः सर्वदक्षिणः॥
en: You should, therefore, celebrate a great sacrifice with enough presents of all sorts and a sufficient quantity of the Earth's produce. If you do not perform that sacrifice, O king, then the sins of this kingdom will visit you.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: तं चेन्न यजसे राजन् प्राप्तस्त्वं राज्यकिल्बिषम्। येषां राजाऽश्वमेधेन यजते दक्षिणावता॥
en: Those subjects whose king performs a horse-sacrifice with enough presents, are all freed from sins and sanctified by witnessing the ablutions at the end of the sacrifice.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: उपेत्य तस्यावभृथे पूताः सर्वे भवन्ति ते। विश्वरूपो महादेवः सर्वमेधे महामखे। जुहाव सर्वभूतानि तथैवात्मानमात्मना॥
en: In a great sacrifice requiring libations of all kinds of flesh, Mahadeva himself, poured all creatures as sacrificial libations and then his own self.

description: Arjuna cheers up Yudhishthira by saying that it is by prowess that one acquired kingdom
sn: शाश्वतोऽयं भूतिपथो नास्यान्तमनुशुश्रुम। महान् दाशरथः पन्था मा राजन् कुपथं गमः॥
en: This is the eternal and holy road. Its fruits are never destroyed. This is the great road called Dasharatha. Abandoning it, 'O king, what other path would you follow"? called Dasharatha. Abandoning it, 'O king, what other path would you follow"?

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मुहूर्तं तावदेकाग्रो मनःश्रोत्रेऽन्तरात्मनि। धारयन्नपि तच्छुत्वा रोचेत वचनं मम॥
en: Yudhishthira said For a little while, O Arjuna, concentrate your attention, thought and hearing on the inner self. If you hear my words in such a state of mind, you will like them!

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: साधुगम्यमहं मार्गं न जातु त्वत्कृते पुनः। गच्छेयं तद् गमिष्यामि हित्वा ग्राम्यसुखान्युत॥
en: Abandoning all earthly pleasure, I shall follow that path which is trod by the righteous! [ shall not, for your sake, follow the path pointed out by you.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: क्षेम्यश्चैकाकिना गम्यः पन्थाः कोऽस्तीति पृच्छ माम्। अथवा नेच्छसि प्रष्टुमपृच्छन्नपि मे शृणु॥
en: If you ask me what path is auspicious which only one should follow, I shall tell you! If you are not inclined to ask me, I shall yet, unasked by you, tell you of it.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: हित्वा ग्राम्यसुखाचारं तप्यमानो महत् तपः। अरण्ये फलमूलाशी चरिष्यामि मृगैः सह॥
en: Abandoning the pleasures and what men do in this world, and practising the austerity of penances, I shall wander in the forest, with the animals dwelling there, living on fruits and roots!

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: जुह्वानोऽग्निं यथाकालमुभौ कालावुपस्पृशन्। कृशः परिमिताहारश्चर्मचीरजटाधरः॥
en: Pouring libations on the fire at the appointed time and performing ablutions at morning, and evening I shall reduce myself by restricted diet. and clad in skins, bear matted locks on my head.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: शीतवातातपसहः क्षुत्पिपासाश्रमक्षमः। तपसा विधिदृष्टेन शरीरमुपशोषयन्॥ मनःकर्णसुखा नित्यं शृण्वन्नुच्चावचा गिरः। मुदितानामरण्येषु वसतां मृगपक्षिणाम्॥
en: Enduring cold, wind, and heat, as also hunger and thirst and toil, I shall emaciate my body by penances as sanctioned by the scriptures. I shall daily listen to the clear notes of happy birds and animals living in the forest, which please the heart and the ear.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: आजिघ्रन पेशलान् गन्धान फुल्लानां वृक्षवीरुधाम्। नानारूपान् वने पश्यन् रमणीयान् वनौकसः॥
en: I shall enjoy the fragrance of trees and creepers, covered with flowers and see various kinds of charining products that grow in the forest.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: वानप्रस्थजनस्यापि दर्शनं कुलवासिनाम्। नाप्रियाण्याचरिष्यामि किंपुनर्ग्रामवासिनाम्॥
en: I shall also see many recluses there. I shall not do the slightest harm to any creature, what to speak of those who live in villages and towns?

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: एकान्तशीली विमृशन् पक्वापक्वेन वर्तयन्। पितृन् देवांश्च वन्येन वाग्भिरद्भिश्च तर्पयन्॥
en: Leading a retired life and engaged in contemplation, I shall live upon ripe and unripe fruits and propitiate the departed manes and the gods with offerings of forest fruits and spring water and beautiful hymns.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: एवमारण्यशास्त्राणामुग्रमुग्रतरं विधिम्। सेवमानः प्रतीक्षिष्ये देहस्यास्य समापनम्॥
en: Thus leading an austere forest-life, I shall live on, calmly awaiting the dissolution of my body.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: अथवैकोऽहमेकाहमेकैकस्मिन् वनस्पतौ। चरन् भैक्ष्यं मुनिर्मुण्डः क्षपयिष्ये कलेवरम्॥
en: Or, living alone and observing the vow of silence, with iny head shaved clean, I shall live by begging each day of only one trees.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: पांसुभिः समभिच्छन्नः शून्यागारप्रतिश्रयः। वृक्षमूलनिकेतो वा त्यक्तसर्वप्रियाप्रियः॥
en: Smearing my body with ashes, and living in forsaken houses, or lying at the foot of trees, I shall live, forsaking all things dear or hateful.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: न शोचन्न पहष्यंश्च तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः। निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः॥
en: Without being over-grieved, or over-joyed, and considering censure and applause, hope and affection, in the same light and conquering the pairs of opposites, I shall live, casting off all the things of the world.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: आत्मारामः प्रसन्नात्मा जडान्धवधिराकृतिः। अकुर्वाणः परैः काञ्चित् संविदं जातु कैरपि॥
en: Without talking with anybody, I shall outwardly appear as a blind and deaf idiot, while living in contentment and deriving liappiness from my innerself.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: जङ्गमाजङ्गमान् सर्वानविहिसंश्चतुर्विधान्। प्रजाः सर्वाः स्वधर्मस्थाः समः प्राणभृतः प्रति॥
en: Without doing the least harm to the four kinds of movable and immovable creatures, I shall deal with all creatures equally whether fulfilling their duties, or guided entirely by the Senses.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: न चाप्यवहसन् कञ्चिन्न कुर्वन् भृकुटी: क्वचित्। प्रसन्नवदनो नित्यं सर्वेन्द्रियसुसंयतः॥
en: I shall not inock at any one, nor shall I frown at any body. governing all my senses, I shall always put on a cheerful face.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: अपृच्छन् कस्यचिन्मार्ग प्रव्रजन्नेव केनचित्। न देशं न दिशं काञ्चिद् गन्तुमिच्छन् विशेषतः॥
en: Without asking anybody about the way, proceeding along any way that I may happen to see, I shall go on, without caring for the country or the point of the compass to which or towards which I may go.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: गमने निरपेक्षश्च पश्चादनवलोकयन्। ऋजुः प्रणिहितो गच्छंस्त्रसस्थावरवर्जकः॥
en: Not caring where I may go, I shall not look behind. Divesting myself of desire and anger, and concentrating my look inwards, I shall go on forsaking pride of soul and body.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: स्वभावस्तु प्रयात्यग्रे प्रभवन्त्यशनान्यपि। द्वन्द्वानि च विरुद्धानि तानि सर्वाण्यचिन्तयन्॥
en: Nature always walks before : hence, food and drink will somehow come. I shall not think of those pairs of opposites that are inimical to such a life.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: अल्पं वास्वादु वा भोज्यं पूर्वालाभेन जातुचित्। अन्येष्वपि चरँल्लाभमलाभे सप्त पूरयन्॥
en: If even a small quantity of pure food be not available in the first house (where I may go) I shall secure it by going to other houses. If I cannot procure it by even such around, I shall go to seven houses successively and fill my cravings.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: विधूमे न्यस्तमुसले व्यङ्गारे भुक्तवज्जने। अतीतपात्रसंचारे काले विगतभिक्षुके॥ एककालं चरन् भक्ष्यं त्रीनथ द्वे च पञ्च वा। स्नेहपाशं विमुच्याहं चरिष्यामि महीमिमाम्॥
en: When the smoke of houses will cease to come out, their hearth-fires having been put out, when husking rods will cease working, and all the inmates will have taken their food, and when mendicants and guests will cease to walk, I shall select a moment for going out a begging and solicit alms at two, three, or five houses at the inost. I shall wander over the Earth, shorn of all desires.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: अलाभे सति वा लाभे समदर्शी महातपाः। न जिजीविषुवत् किंचिन्न मुमूर्षुवदाचरन्।॥
en: Unmoved in success and failure, I shall earn great ascetic merit, I shall behave neither like one who is fond of life nor like one who is about to die.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: जीवितं मरणं चैव नाभिनन्दन्न च द्विषन्। वास्यैकं तक्षतो बाहुं चन्दनेनैकमुक्षतः॥
en: I shall not show any liking for life or dislike for death. If one cuts off one arm of mine and another smears the other with sandal-paste, I shall not wish evil to the one or good to other.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: नाकल्याणं न कल्याणं चिन्तयन्नुभयोस्तयोः। याः काश्चिज्जीवता शक्याः कर्तुमभ्युदयक्रियाः। सर्वास्ताः समभित्यज्य निमेषादिव्यवस्थितः॥
en: Abandoning all those acts which lead to prosperity and which one can do in life, the only acts I shall perform will be to open and shut my eyes and take as much food and drink as will barely keep up of my existence.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: तेषु नित्यमसक्तश्च त्यक्तसर्वेन्द्रियक्रियः। सुपरित्यक्तसंकल्प: सुनिर्णिक्तात्मकल्मषः॥
en: Without ever being attached to action, and always restraining the senses, I shall abandon all desire and free the soul of all impurities.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: विमुक्तः सर्वसंगेभ्यो व्यतीतः सर्ववागुराः। न वशे कस्यचित्तिष्ठन् सधर्मा मातरिश्वनः॥
en: Freed from all attachments and snapping all fetters, I shall live free as the wind.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: वीतरागश्चरन्नेवं तुष्टिी प्राप्स्यामि शाश्वतीम्। तृष्णया हि महत् पापमज्ञानादस्मि कारितः॥
en: Being frced from affections, I shall enjoy everlasting contentment. Through desire, and ignorance, I have committed great sins.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: कुशलाकुशलान्येके कृत्वा कर्माणि मानवाः। कार्यकारणसंश्लिष्टं स्वजनं नाम बिभ्रति॥
en: Doing both auspicious and inauspicious acts here, a class of men maintain their wives, children, and kinsmen, all bound to them in relations of cause and effect.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: आयुषोऽन्ते प्रहायेदं क्षीणप्राणं कलेवरम्। प्रतिगृह्णाति तत् पापं कर्तुः कर्मफलं हि तत्॥
en: When the lease of their life expires, abandoning their weakened bodies, they take upon themselves all the effects of their sinful acts, for none but the actor is laden with the consequences of his own acts.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: एवं संसारचक्रेऽस्मिन् व्याविद्धे रथचक्रवत्। समेति भूतग्रामोऽयं भूतग्रामेण कार्यवान्॥
en: Thus, endued with actions, creatures come into this wheel of life that is continually turning like the wheel of a car, and coming there, they meet with their fellow-creatures.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिवेदनाभिरभिद्रुतम्। अपारमिव चास्वस्थं संसारं त्यजतः सुखम्॥
en: He, however, who gives up his worldly concern, which is really a passing illusion although it looks permanent, and which is afflicted by birth, death, decrepitude, disease, and pain, is sure to enjoy happiness.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: दिवः पतत्सु देवेषु स्थानेभ्यश्च महर्षिषु। को हि नाम भवेनार्थी भवेत् कारणतत्त्ववित्॥
en: Again, when the very gods drop down from heaven and great Rishis from their high positions, who that knows truths of causes (and effects) would wish to have even heavenly prosperity?

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: कृत्वा हि विविधं कर्म तत्तद् विविधलक्षणम्। पार्थिवैर्नृपतिः स्वल्पैः कारणैरेव बध्यते॥
en: Having performed various acts according to the diverse means of royal policy, insignificant kings, often destroy a great king through some contrivance.

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: तस्मात् प्रज्ञामृतमिदं चिरान्मां प्रत्युपस्थितम्। तत् प्राप्य प्रार्थये स्थानमव्ययं शाश्वतं ध्रुवम्॥
en: Meditating on these circumstances, this nectar of wisdom has come to me. Having attained it, I desire to get a permanent, eternal, and ever-abiding place (for myself).

description: Yudhishthira is bent upon following Renunciation.
sn: एतया संततं धृत्या चरन्नेवंप्रकारया। जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिवेदनाभिरभिद्रुतम्। देहं संस्थापयिष्यामि निर्भयं मार्गमास्थितः॥
en: Always (behaving) with such wisdom and acting in this wise, I shall, by following that fearless path of life, and this body that is subject to birth, death, decrepitude, disease, and pain.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: भीम उवाच श्रोत्रियस्येव ते राजन् मन्दकस्याविपश्चितः। अनुवाकहता बुद्धि:षा तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनी॥
en: Bhimasena said-Your understanding, O king, cannot perceive the truth, like that of a foolish and unintelligent reciter of the Veda for his recitation of those scriptures.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: आलस्ये कृतचित्तस्य राजधर्मानसूयतः। विनाशे धार्तराष्ट्राणां किं फलं भरतर्षभ॥
en: If censuring the duties of kings you would lead an idle life, then, O foremost of Bharata's race, this destruction of the Dhartarashtras was perfectly useless.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: क्षमानुकम्पा कारुण्यमानृशंस्यं न विद्यते। क्षात्रमाचरतो मार्गमपि बन्धोस्त्वदन्तरे॥
en: Does not a Kshatriya possess forgiveness and compassion and pity and abstention from injury?

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: यदीमां भवतो बुद्धिं विद्याम वयमीदृशीम्। शस्त्रं नैव ग्रहीष्यामो न वधिष्याम कंचन॥
en: If we knew that this was your intention, we would then have never taken up arms and killed a single creature.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: भैक्ष्यमेवाचरिष्याम शरीरस्याविमोक्षणात्। न चेदं दारुणं युद्धमभविष्यन्महीक्षिताम्॥
en: We would then have lived by begging till the destruction of this body! This dreadful battle between the kings would also have never taken place!

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: प्राणस्यान्नमिदं सर्वमिति वै कवयो विदुः। स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव सर्वं प्राणस्य भोजनम्॥
en: The learned have declared that what we see is food for the strong. This mobile and immobile world is worthy of being enjoyed by the strong.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: आददानस्य चेद् राज्यं ये केचित् परिपन्थिनः। हन्तव्यास्त इति प्राज्ञाः क्षत्रधर्मविदो विदुः॥
en: Wise men conversant with Kshatriya duties have said that they who stand in the way of the person taking the sovereignty of the Earth, should be killed.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: ते सदोषा हतास्माभी राज्यस्य परिपन्थिनः। तान् हत्वा भुड्क्ष्वधर्मेण युधिष्ठिर महीमिमाम्॥
en: Committing the same fault, those that stood as enemies of our kingdom have all been killed by us. Having killed then, O Yudhishthira, righteously govern this Earth!

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: यथा हि पुरुषः खात्वा कूपमप्राप्य चोदकम्। पङ्कदिग्धो निवर्तेत कर्मेदं नस्तथोपमम्॥
en: This act of our refusing the kingdom is like that of a person who having dug a well stops in his work before obtaining water and comes up covered with mire.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: यथाऽऽरुह्य महावृक्षमपहृत्य ततो मधु। अप्राश्य निधनं गच्छेत् कर्मेदं नस्तथोपमम्॥
en: Or, this our act is like that of a person who having climbed up a tall tree and collected honey therefrom dies before tasting it.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: यथा महान्तमध्वानमाशया पुरुषः पतन्। स निराशो निवर्तेत कर्मतन्नस्तथोपमम्॥
en: Or, it is like that of a person who having set out on a long journey comes back in despair without having reached his goal.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: यथा शत्रून् घातयित्वा पुरुषः कुरुनन्दन। आत्मानं घातयेत् पश्चात् कर्मेदं नस्तथोपमम्॥
en: Or, it is like that of a person who having killed all his enemies, O you of Kuru's race, at last dies at his own hand.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: यथान्नं क्षुधितो लब्ध्वा न भुञ्जीयाद् यदृच्छया। कामीव कामिनी लब्ध्वा कर्मेदं नस्तथोपमम्॥
en: Or, it is like that of a person with hunger, who having obtained food, refuses to take it, or of a person under the influence of passion, who having obtained a woman reciprocating his desire refuses to know her.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: वयमेवात्र गर्वा हि यद् वयं मन्दचेतसम्। त्वां राजन्ननुगच्छामो ज्येष्ठोऽयमिति भारत॥
en: We have become butts of censure, O Bharata, because, O king, we follow you who are of weak understanding, in consequence of yourself being our eldest brother!

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: वयं हि बाहुबलिनः कृतविद्या मनस्विनः। क्लीबस्य वाक्ये तिष्ठामो यथैवाशक्तयस्तथा॥
en: We are endued with the might of arms; we are accomplished in knowledge and gifted with great energy. Yet we follow the words of a eunuch as if we were entirely helpless!

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: अगतीकगतीनस्मान् नष्टार्थानर्थसिद्धये। कथं वै नानुपश्येयुर्जना: पश्यत यादृशम्॥
en: We are the refuge of all helpless persons. Yet, when people see us so, why would they not say that we are entirely powerless to acquire our objects? Think of what I say!

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: आपत्काले हि संन्यासः कर्तव्य इति शिष्यते। जरयाभिपरीतेन शत्रुभियंसितेन वा॥
en: It has been laid down that (a life of) Renunciation should be adopted, only in times of difficulty, by kings attacked with decrepitude or defeated by, enemies!

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: तस्मादिह कृतप्रज्ञास्त्यागं न परिचक्षते। धर्मव्यतिक्रमं चैव मन्यन्ते सूक्ष्मदर्शिनः॥
en: Wise men, therefore, do not praise Renunciation as the duty of a Kshatriya. On the other hand, the clear-sighted think that the adoption of such a life (by a Kshatriya) involves even the loss of virtue.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: कथं तस्मात् समुत्पन्नास्तनिष्ठास्तदुपाश्रयाः। तदेव निन्दा भाषेयुर्धाता तत्र न गर्यते॥
en: How can those who are born in that order, who follow the practices of that order, and that have their refuse in them, censure those duties? If indeed those duties be censurable, then why should not the Supreme Ordainer be blamed?

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: श्रिया विहीनैरधनैर्नास्तिकैः सम्प्रवर्तितम्। वेदवादस्य विज्ञानं सत्याभासमिवानृतम्॥
en: The persons who are shorn of prosperity and wealth and who are unbelievers, have laid down this precept of the Vedas as the truth. In reality, however, it is never, proper for a Kshatriya to do so.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: शक्यं तु मौनमास्थाय बिभ्रताऽऽत्मानमात्मना। धर्मच्छद्म समास्थाय च्यवितुं न तु जीवितुम्॥
en: He who can support life by prowess, he who can support himself by his own exertions, does note live, but really deviates from his duty, by following the life of Renunciation.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: शक्यं पुनररण्येषु सुखमेकेन जीवितुम्। अबिभ्रता पुत्रपौत्रान् देवर्षीनतिथीन् पितॄन्।॥
en: That man only is capable of leading a solitary life of happiness in the forest who cannot support sons and grandsons and the deities and Rishis and guests and Pitris.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: नेमे मृगाः स्वर्गजितो न वराहा न पक्षिणः। अथान्येन प्रकारेण पुण्यमाहुर्न तं जनाः॥
en: As the deer and boars and birds cannot attain to heaven, even so those Kshatriyas who are not shorn of prowess cannot attain to heaven by leading only a forest life. They should acquire religious merit by other means.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: यदि संन्यासत: सिद्धिं राजा कश्चिदवाप्नुयात्। पर्वताश्च दुमाश्चैव क्षिप्रं सिद्धिमवाप्नुयुः॥
en: If, O king, anybody could secure success from Renunciation, then mountains and trees would surely obtain it.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: एते हि नित्यसंन्यासा दृश्यन्ते निरुपद्रवाः। अपरिग्रहवन्तश्च सततं ब्रह्मचारिणः॥
en: These latter always lead lives of Renunciation. They do not harın any one. They do not lead a life of worldliness and are all Brahmacharins.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: अथ चेदात्मभाग्येषु नान्येषां सिद्धिमश्नुते। तस्मात् कर्मैव कर्तव्यं नास्ति सिद्धिरकर्मणः॥
en: If it be the truth that a person's success depends upon his own torture in life and not upon that of others, then you should take to action. He that is shorn of action can never attain success.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: औदकाः सृष्टयश्चैव जन्तवः सिद्धिमाप्नुयुः। तेषामात्मैव भर्तव्यो नान्यः कश्चन विद्यते॥
en: If they who fill only their own stomachs could achieve success, then all aquatic creatures would get it, for these have none else to support save their own selves.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: अवेक्षस्व यथा स्वैः स्वैः कर्मभिर्व्यापृतं जगत्। तस्मात् कर्मव कर्तव्यं नास्ति सिद्धिरकर्मणः॥
en: Behold, the world moves on, with every creature on it acting according to its nature, therefore, one should act. The man shorn of action can never attain success.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: औदकाः सृष्टयश्चैव जन्तवः सिद्धिमाप्नुयुः। तेषामात्मैव भर्तव्यो नान्यः कश्चन विद्यते॥
en: If they who fill only their own stomachs could achieve success, then all aquatic creatures would get it, for these have none else to support save their own selves.

description: Arjuna urges upon him the necessity of performing the duties of kings
sn: अवेक्षस्व यथा स्वैः स्वैः कर्मभिर्व्यापृतं जगत्। तस्मात् कर्मव कर्तव्यं नास्ति सिद्धिरकर्मणः॥
en: Behold, the world moves on, with every creature on it acting according to its nature, therefore, one should act. The man shorn of action can never attain success.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: अर्जुन उवाच अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। तापसैः सह संवादं शक्रस्य भरतर्षभ॥
en: Arjuna said The old history of the discourse between certain ascetics and Shakra, is cited in this connection, O foremost of Bharata's race!

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: केचिद् गृहान् परित्यज्य वनमभ्यागमन् द्विजाः। अजातश्मश्रवो मन्दाः कुले जाताः प्रवव्रजुः॥
en: Certain little-witted well-born Brahmana youths, without attaining manhood, forsaking their homes, came to the woods for leading a forest life.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: धर्मोऽयमिति मन्वानाः समृद्धा ब्रह्मचारिणः। त्यक्त्वा भ्रातृन् पिढेश्चैव तानिन्द्रोऽन्वकृपायत॥
en: Considering that to be virtue, those youths possessing sufficient resources desired to live as Brahmacharins, having abandoned their brothers and fathers. It so happened that Indra felt pity for them.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: तानाबभाषे भगवान् पक्षी भूत्वा हिरण्मयः। सुदुष्करं मनुष्यैश्च यत् कृतं विघसाशिभिः॥
en: Assuming the form of a golden bird, Indra addressed them, saying,-What is done by persons who eat the residue of a Sacrifice is the most difficult of acts that men can perform.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: पुण्यं भवति कर्मेदं प्रशस्तं चैव जीवितम्। सिद्धार्थास्ते गतिं मुख्यां प्राप्ता धर्मपरायणाः॥
en: Such an act is productive of great merit. The lives of such men are worthy of every praise. Having attained the object of life, those virtuous men, obtained the highest end!

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: ऋषय ऊचुः अहो बतायं शकुनिर्विघसाशान् प्रशंसति। अस्मान् नूनमयं शास्ति वयं च विघसाशिनः॥
en: Hearing these words, the Rishis said,-Lo, this bird praises those who live upon the remnants of Sacrifices! He mentions this to us, for we live upon such remnants!

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: शकुनिरुवाच नाहं युष्मान् प्रशंसामि पङ्कदिग्धान् रजस्वलान्। उच्छिष्टभोजिनो मन्दानन्ये वै विघसाशिनः॥
en: The bird then said The bird then said.-I do not praise you! You are covered with mire and very impure! Living upon offals, you are wicked! Ye you not persons living upon the remnants of Sacrifice!-

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: ऋषय ऊचुः इदं श्रेयः परमिति वयमेवाभ्युपास्महे। शकुने ब्रूहि यच्छेरूयो भृशं ते श्रद्धामहे॥
en: The Rishis said We consider this course of life to be highly : blessed! Tell us, O bird, what is for our wellbeing! Your words fill us with great faith!

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: शकुनिरुवाच यदि मां नाभिशङ्कध्वं विभज्यात्मानमात्मना। ततोऽहं वः प्रवक्ष्यामि याथातथ्यं हितं वचः॥
en: The bird said If by acting against your better selves, you do not refuse me your faith, then I shall tell you true and beneficial words.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: ऋषय ऊचुः शृणुमस्ते वचस्तात पन्थानो विदितास्तव। नियोगे चैव धर्मात्मन् स्थातुमिच्छाम शाधि नः॥
en: The Rishis said We shall hear words, O sire, for you know the different paths! O you of righteous soul, we desire also to obey your behests. Instruct us now!

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: शकुनिरुवाच चतुष्पदां गौः प्रवरा लोहानां काञ्चनं वरम्। शब्दानां प्रवरो मन्त्रो ब्राह्मणो द्विपदां वरः॥
en: among quadrupeds the cow is the foremost. Of metals, goid is the foremost. Of words, Mantras, and of human beings, Brahmanas, are the foremost.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: मन्त्रोऽयं जातकर्मादिाह्मणस्य विधीयते। जीवतोऽपि यथाकालं श्मशाननिधनादिभिः॥
en: These Mantras regulate all the rites of a Brahmana's life, beginning with those consequent upon birth and the period after it, and ending with those consequent on death and the obsequial rites.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: कर्माणि वैदिकान्यस्य स्वर्यः पन्थास्त्वनुत्तमः। अथ सर्वाणि कर्माणि मन्त्रसिद्धानि चक्षते॥
en: These Vedic rites constitute his heaven, path, and best of sacrifices, If it were Otherwise, how could the acts of persons seeking of heaven become successful through Mantras?

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: आत्मानं दृढवादीति तथा सिद्धिरिहेष्यते। मासार्धमासा ऋतव आदित्यशशितारकम्॥
en: He who, in this world, worships his self, knowing it to be a deity of a particular kind, attains to success consistent with a nature of that particular deity. Persons dying in two fortnights go to the Sun, the Moon, or the Stars.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: ईहन्ते सर्वभूतानि तदिदं कर्मसंज्ञितम्। सिद्धिक्षेत्रमिदं पुण्यमयमेवाश्रमो महान्॥
en: These three kinds of success, dependent upon action, are sought by every creature. The life of a householder is very superior and sacred and is called the field of success.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: अथ ये कर्म निन्दन्तो मनुष्याः कापथं गताः। मूढानामर्थहीनानां तेषामेनस्तु विद्यते॥
en: What path do those men follow that censure action? Foolish and poor as they are they incur sin.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: देववंशान् पितृवंशान् ब्रह्मवंशांश्च शाश्वतान्। संत्यज्य मूढा वर्तन्ते ततो यान्त्यश्रुतीपथम्॥
en: And since those little-witted men live by abandoning the eternal paths of the gods, of the Rishis, and of Brahma, therefore, they attain to paths disapproved of by the Shrutis.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: एतद्वोऽस्तु तपोयुक्तं ददामीत्वृषिचोदितम्। तस्मात् तत्तद् व्यवस्थानं तपस्वि तप उच्यते॥
en: There is a verse in the Maniras which says,-(Ye sacrificer, perform the sacrifice with gifts of costly things. I will give you the happiness represented by sons, animals, and heaven.) To live, therefore, in accordance with the ordinance is said to be the highest form of asceticism. Therefore, you should perform sacrifice and penances in the shape of gifts.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: देववंशान् ब्रह्मवंशान् पितृवंशांश्च शाश्वतान्। संविभज्य गुरोश्चर्यां तद् वै दुष्करमुच्यते॥
en: The proper performance of these eternal duties, viz., the worship of the gods, the study of the Vedas, and the gratification of the Pitris, as also respectful services to the preceptor,-is the austerest of penances.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: देवा वै दुष्करं कृत्वा विभूतिं परमां गताः। तस्माद् गार्हस्थ्यमुद्वोढुं दुष्करं प्रब्रवीमि वः॥
en: By practising such highly difficult penances, the gods have obtained the highest glory and power. I, therefore, ask you to satisfy the heavy duties of a householder.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: तपः श्रेष्ठं प्रजानां हि मूलमेतन्न संशयः। कुटुम्बविधिनानेन यस्मिन् सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्॥ एतद् विदुस्तपो विप्रा द्वन्द्वातीता विमत्सराः। तस्माद् व्रतं मध्यमं तु लोकेषु तप उच्यते॥
en: Forsooth, penances are the foremost of all things and are the root of all creatures, Asceticism, is attainable by leading the life a householder, upon which depends everything. The learned Brahmins having chack on malice, beyond the sphere of duality know that penance. The penance so observed by them is addressed as penance on the earth.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: दुराधर्षं पदं चैव गच्छन्ति विघसाशिनः। सायंप्रातर्विभज्यानं स्वकुटुम्बे यथाविधि॥
en: After duly distributing the food morning and evening among kinsmen, they who eat the residuc attain to the ends that are highly difficult of attainment.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: दत्त्वाऽतिथिभ्यो देवेभ्यः पितृभ्यः स्वजनाय च। अवशिष्टानि येऽश्नन्ति तानाहुर्विघसाशिनः॥
en: They are called eaters of the residue of feasts who cat after having fed guests and gods and Rishis and kinsmen.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: तस्मात् स्वधर्ममास्थाय सुव्रताः सत्यवादिनः। लोकस्य गुरवो भूत्वा ते भवन्त्यनुपस्कृताः॥
en: Therefore, those persons who observe their own duties, who practise excellent vows and are truthful in speech, are greatly respected in the world, with their own faith greatly strengthened.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: त्रिदिवं प्राप्य शक्रस्य स्वर्गलोके विमत्सराः। वसन्ति शाश्वतान् वर्षाञ्जना दुष्करकारिणः॥
en: Shorn pride, those achievers of the most difficult feats attain to heaven and live for ever in the regions of Shakra!

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: अर्जुन उवाच ततस्ते तद् वचः श्रुत्वा धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्। उत्सृज्य नास्तीति गता गार्हस्थ्यं समुपाश्रिताः॥
en: Arjuna continued Hearing these beneficial and righteous words, those ascetics abandoned the religion of Renunciation, saying, There is nothing in it,-and begin to live like householders.

description: An account of certain ascetics who taking instruction from a bird give up Renunciation and live like house-holders
sn: तस्मात् त्वमपि सर्वज्ञ धैर्यमालम्ब्य शाश्वतम्। प्रशाधि पृथिवीं कृत्स्ना हतामित्रां नरोत्तम॥
en: Therefore, O you, who are conversant with righteousness, availing of that eternal wisdom, rule the wide world, O monarch, that is now shorn of foes."

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अर्जुनस्य वचः श्रुत्वा नकुलो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। राजानमभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य सर्वधर्मभृतां वरम्॥ अनुरुथ्य महाप्राज्ञो भ्रातुश्चित्तमरिन्दम। व्यूढोरस्को महाबाहुस्ताम्रास्यो मितभाषिता॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Hearing these words of Arjuna, O chastiser of foes, the mighty-armed and broad chested, Nakula, temperate in speech and possessed of great wisdom, with copper coloured face, looked at the king, that foremost of all righteous persons, and spoke the these words, assailing his brother's heart (with reason).

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: नकुल उवाच विशाखयूपे देवानां सर्वेषामग्नयश्चिताः। तस्माद् विद्धि महाराज देवाः कर्मफले स्थिताः॥
en: Nakula said Even the gods had placed their fires in the reign called Vishakha-yupa, Know, therefore, O king, that the gods themselves depend upon the fruits of action!

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: अनास्तिकानां भूतानां प्राणदाः पितरश्च ये। तेऽपि कर्मैव कुर्वन्ति विधि सम्प्रेक्ष्य पार्थिव॥
en: Observing the Vedic ordinances (of the Creator as declared in the Vedas), the Pitris, who support (by rain) the lives of even all disbelievers, are, O king, engaged in action.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: वेदवादापविद्धांस्तु तान् विद्धि भृशनास्तिकान्। न हि वेदोक्तमुत्सृज्य विप्रः सर्वेषु कर्मसु॥ देवयानेन नाकस्य पृष्ठमाप्नोति भारत। अत्याश्रमानयं सर्वानित्याहुर्वेदनिश्चयाः॥
en: They are, indeed, consummate atheists who do not accept the injunction of the Vedas (which inculcate action). By following Vedic injunctions in all his acts, the person that is learned in the Vedas, attains, O Bharata, to the highest region of heaven by the way of the deities. All persons acquainted with Vedas have declared the life of a householder to be superior to all the (other) modes of life.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: ब्राह्मणाः श्रुतिसम्पन्नास्तान् निबोध नराधिप। वित्तानि धर्मलब्धानि ऋतुमुख्येष्ववासृजन्॥ कृतात्मा स महाराज स वै त्यागी स्मृतो नरः॥
en: O king, the person who in sacrifices give away his fairly acquired wealth to these Brahmanas who are well conversant with the Vedas, and contracts his soul, is, O monarch, regarded as the true Renouncer.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: अनवेक्ष्य सुखादानं तथैवोर्ध्वं प्रतिष्ठितः। आत्मत्यागी महाराज स त्यागी तामसो मतः॥
en: He, however, who, disregarding the life of a householder, the source of much happiness, adopts the next mode of life,-Renunciation, O monarch, is Renouncer possessed by the quality of darkness.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: अनिकेतः परिपतन् वृक्षमूलाश्रयो मुनिः। अपाचकः सदा योगी स त्यागी पार्थ भिक्षुकः॥
en: That man who is houseless, who roves over the world like a mendicant who has the foot of a tree for his refuge, who observes the vow of silence, never cooks for himself, and tries to control his senses, is, O Partha, a Renouncer observing the vow of mendicancy.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: क्रोधहर्षावनादृत्य पैशुन्यं च विशेषतः। विप्रो वेदानधीते यः स त्यागी पार्थ उच्यते॥
en: That Brahmana who, disregarding anger and joy, and especially deceitfulness, always devotes his time to the study of the Vedas, is a Renouncer observing the vow of mendicancy.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: आश्रमांस्तुलया सर्वान् धृतानाहुर्मनीषिणः। एकतश्च त्रयो राजन् गृहस्थाश्रम एकतः॥
en: The four different modes of life were at one time weighed in the balance. The wise have said, O king, that when the life of a householder was placed on one scale, it required the three others to balance it.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: समीक्ष्य तुलया पार्थ कामं स्वर्गं च भारत। अयं पन्था महर्षीणामियं लोकविदां गतिः॥
en: Marking the result of this examination by scales, O Partha, and seeing further, O Bharata, that the life of a householder alone contained both heaven and pleasure, the great Rishis and the persons conversant with the ways of the world followed it.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: इति यः कुरुते भावं स त्यागी भरतर्षभ। न य: परित्यज्य गृहान् वनमेति विमूढवत्॥
en: He, therefore,O foremost of Bharata's race, who follows this mode of life, thinking it to be his duty and abandoning all desire for fruit, is a true Renouncer, and not that man who having clouded understanding goes to the forest abandoning home.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: यदा कामान् समीक्षेत धर्मवैतंसिको नरः। अथैनं मृत्युपाशेन कण्ठे बध्नाति मृत्युराट्॥
en: A person, again, who, putting on the external marks of righteousness, fails to conquer his desires even while living in the forest, is bound by Death with his deadly fetters round the neck.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: अभिमानकृतं कर्म नैतत् फलवदुच्यते। त्यागयुक्तं महाराज सर्वमेव महाफलम्॥
en: Acts which are the outcome of vanity product no fruit. Those acts however, O monarch, which are the outcome of the spirit of Renunciation, always bear abundant fruits.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: शमो दमस्तथा धैर्यं सत्यं शौचमथार्जवम्। यज्ञो धृतिश्च धर्मश्च नित्यमा! विधिः स्मृतः॥
en: Tranquillity, self-restraint, fortitude, truth, purity, simplicity, sacrifices, perseverance, and righteousness,-these are always the virtues recommended by the Rishis.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: पितृदेवातिथिकृते समारम्भोऽत्र शस्यते। अत्रैव हि महाराज त्रिवर्गः केवलं फलम्॥
en: The householder performs acts intended for Pitris, gods, and guests, this mode of life alone, O monarch, contains the threefold objects.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: एतस्मिन् वर्तमानस्य विधावप्रतिषेधिते। त्यागिनः प्रसृतस्येह नोच्छित्तिर्विद्यते क्वचित्॥
en: The Renouncer that rigidly follows this mode of life, in which one is free to do all acts, has not to meet ruin either here or hereafter.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: असृजद्धि प्रजा राजन् प्रजापतिरकल्मषः। मां यक्ष्यन्तीति धर्मात्मा यज्ञैर्विविधदक्षिणैः॥
en: The holy Lord of all creatures, of righteous soul, created creatures with the purpose that they would worship him by sacrifices with profuse presents.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: वीस्थश्चैव वृक्षांश्च यज्ञार्थं वै तथौषधीः। पशृंश्चैव तथा मेध्यान् यज्ञार्थानि हवींषि च॥
en: Creepers, trees, deciduous herbs, and clean animals, and clarified butter, were created as materials of sacrifice.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: गृहस्थाश्रमिणस्तच्च यज्ञकर्म विरोधकम्। तस्माद् गार्हस्थ्यमेवेह दुष्करं दुर्लभं तथा॥
en: To a householder the performance of sacrifice is fraught with impediments. For this, that mode of life is described as exceedingly difficult and unattainable.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: तत् सम्प्राप्य गृहस्था ये पशुधान्यधनान्विताः। न यजन्ते महाराज शाश्वतं तेषु किल्बिषम्॥
en: The householders, who, possessed of wealth and corn and animals, do not perform sacrifices commit, o king, eternal sin.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: स्वाध्याययज्ञा ऋषयो ज्ञानयज्ञास्तथा परे। अथापरे महायज्ञान् मनस्येव वितन्वते॥
en: Amongst Rishis, there are some who consider the study of the Vedas to be a some sacrifice; and who consider contemplation to be a great sacrifice which they perform in their minds.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: एवं मनःसमाधानं मार्गमातिष्ठतो नृप। द्विजातेर्ब्रह्मभूतस्य स्पृहयन्ति दिवौकसः॥
en: The very gods, O king, seek the companionship of such a holy person, who on account of his following such a way which consists in the concentration of the mind, has become equal to Brahma.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: स रत्नानि विचित्राणि संहृतानि ततस्ततः। मखेष्वनभिसंत्यज्य नास्तिक्यमभिजल्पसि॥
en: By refusing to spend in Sacrifice the various kinds of wealth which you have collected from your enemies, you are only displaying your want of faith!

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: कुटुम्बमास्थिते त्यागं न पश्यामि नराधिप। राजसूयाश्वमेधेषु सर्वमेधेषु वा पुनः॥
en: I have never seen O monarch, a king living as a householder renouncing his wealth in any other way except 'in the Rajasuya, the Ashvamedha, and other kinds of Sacrifice!

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: ये चान्ये ऋतवस्तात ब्राह्मणैरभिपूजिताः। तैर्यजस्व महीपाल शक्रो देवपतिर्यथा॥
en: Like Shakra, the king of gods, O sire, perform those other sacrifices that are lauded by the Brahmanas!

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: राज्ञः प्रमाददोषेण दस्युभिः परिमुष्यताम्। अशरण्यः प्रजानां यः स राजा कलिरुच्यते॥
en: The king, through whose negligence the subjects are plundered by robbers, and who does not offer protection to those whom he is called upon to rule is said to be the personated Kali.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: अश्वान् गाश्चैव दासीश्च करेणूश्च स्वलंकृताः। ग्रामाजनपदांश्चैव क्षेत्राणि च गृहाणि च॥ अप्रदाय द्विजातिभ्यो मात्सर्याविष्टचेतसः। वयं ते राजकलयो भविष्याम विशाम्पते॥
en: If, without giving away horses and kine, and female slaves and elephants adorned with trappings, and villages, and populous countries, and fields, and houses, to Brahmanas, we retire into the forest with hearts not overflowing with friendly feelings towards kinsmen, even we shall be, O king, like so many Kali Kshatriyas.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: अदातारो शरण्याश्च राजकिल्विषभागिनः। दोषाणामेव भोक्तारो न सुखानां कदाचन॥
en: Kshatriyas who do not practise charity and give protection (to others), commit sin. Woe to thein hereafter and not bliss.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: अनिष्ट्वा च महायज्ञैरकृत्वा च पितृस्वधाम्। तीर्थेष्वनभिसम्लुत्य प्रव्रजिष्यसि चेत् प्रभो॥ छिन्नाभ्रमिव गन्तासि विलयं मारुतेरितम्। लोकयोरुभयोर्धष्टो ह्यन्तराले व्यवस्थितः॥
en: If, O lord, without celebrating great sacrifices and the rites in honour of your deceased manes, and if, without bathing in sacred waters, you lead the life of a mendicant, you will then meet with destruction like a sinall cloud, separated from a mass and driven by the winds. You will then fall off from both worlds and will be born in the Pishacha order.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: अन्तर्बहिश्च यत् किंचिन्मनोव्यासङ्गकारकम्। परित्यज्य भवेत् त्यागी न हित्वा प्रतितिष्ठति॥
en: A person becomes a true Renouncer by casting off internal and external attachments, and not simply by leaving home for dwelling in the forest,

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: एतस्मिन् वर्तमानस्य विधावप्रतिषेधिते। ब्राह्मणस्य महाराज नोच्छित्तिर्विद्यते क्वचित्॥
en: A Brahmana who follows all the ordinances in which there are no obstacles, does not fall off from this or the other world.

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: निहत्य शत्रूस्तरसा समृद्धान् शक्रो यथा दैत्यबलानि संख्ये। कः पार्थ शोचेन्निरतः स्वधर्मे पूर्वैः स्मृते पार्थिव शिष्टजुष्टे॥
en: Observing the duties of one's own order, respected by the ancients and practised by the best of men,-who is there, ( Partha, that would grieve, o king, for having killed in battle his enemies elated with prosperity, like Shakra killing the forces of the Daityas?

description: Nakula advocates the necessity of action
sn: क्षात्रेण धर्मेण पराक्रमेण जित्वा महीं मन्त्रविद्ध्यः प्रदाय। नाकस्य पृष्ठेऽसि नरेन्द्र गन्ता न शोचितव्यं भवताद्य पार्थ॥
en: Having, while observing Kshatriya duties, subjugated the world by the help of your prowess, and having made presents unto persons conversant with the Vedas, you can, O king, go to regions higher than heaven itself. You should not, O Partha, indulge in grief.'

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: सहदेव उवाच न बाह्यं द्रव्यमुत्सृज्य सिद्धिर्भवति भारत। शारीरं द्रव्यमुत्सृज्य सिद्धिर्भवति वा न वा॥
en: Sahadeva said By renouncing all external objects only, O Bharata, one does not obtain success. Even in the casting off of mental attachments, the attainment of, success is doubtful.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: बाह्यद्रव्यविमुक्तस्य शारीरेष्वनुगृध्यतः। यो धर्मो यत् सुखं वा स्याद् द्विषतां तत् तथास्तु नः॥२
en: May our enemies have that religious merit and that happiness which fall to the share of him, who has relinquished external objects, but whose mind still internally covets them.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: शारीरं द्रव्यमुत्सृज्य पृथिवीमनुशासतः। यो धर्मो यत् सुखं वा स्यात् सुहृदां तत् तथास्तु नः।।३
en: On the other hand, inay our friends enjoy that religious merit and happiness which fall 1O cause him, who governs the Earth, having shaken off all internal attachments.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: व्यक्षरस्तु भवेन्मृत्युस्त्र्यक्षरं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्। ममेति च भवेन्मृत्युर्न ममेति च शाश्वतम्॥
en: The word mama (mine), consisting of two letters, is veritable Death; while the opposite word na-mama (not mine) consisting of three letters, is eternal Brahma.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: ब्रह्ममृत्यू ततो राजन्नात्मन्येव समाश्रितौ। अदृश्यमानौ भूतानि योधयेतामसंशयम्॥
en: O king, entering invisibly into every soul, Brahma and Death, forsooth, all creatures to act.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: अविनाशोऽस्य सत्त्वस्य नियतो यदि भारत। हत्वा शरीरं भूतानां न हिंसा प्रतिपत्स्यते॥
en: If this being, O Bharata, which is called soul, is not subject to destruction, then by destroying the bodies of creatures one cannot be guilty of murder.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: अथापि च सहोत्पत्तिः सत्त्वस्य प्रलयस्तथा। नष्टे शरीरे नष्टः स्याद् वृथा च स्यात् क्रियापथः॥
en: If, on the other hand, the soul and the body are born or killed together, so that when the body is destroyed the soul also is destroyed, ten the religious rites and acts would be useless.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: तस्मादेकान्तमुत्सृज्य पूर्वैः पूर्वतरैश्च यः। पन्था निषेवित: सद्भिः स निषेव्यो विजानता॥
en: Therefore, driving away all misgivings regarding the immortality of the soul, the intelligent nian should adopt the path of the righteous of old and older times.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: लध्वापि पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां सहस्थावरजङ्गमाम्। न भुक्के यो नृपः सम्यङ् निष्फलं तस्य जीवितम्॥
en: The life of that king is certainly useless who having acquired the entire Earth with her mobile and immobile creatures, does not enjoy her.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: राजन् वने वन्येन जीवतः। द्रव्येषु यस्य ममता मृत्योरास्ये स वर्तते॥ अथवा वसतो
en: Regarding the man again who dwells in the forest upon wild fruits and roots, but whose attachment to earthly objects has not ceased, such a one, O king, lives within the jaws of Death.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: बाह्यान्तरं च भूतानां स्वभावं पश्य भारत। ये तु पश्यन्ति तद् भूतं मुच्यन्ते ते महाभयात्॥
en: Know, O Bharata, the hearts and the bodies of all creatures to be but manifestations of your own. They who regard all creatures as their own selves escape from the great fear of Death.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: भवान् पिता भवान् माता भवान् भ्राता भवान् गुरुः। दुःखप्रलापानार्तस्य तन्मे त्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: You are my father, you are my protector, you are my brother, and you my senior and preceptor. You should, therefore, forgive these incoherent utterances in sorrow of a woestricken person.

description: Sahadeva also urges upon the king the necessity of action
sn: तथ्यं वा यदि वातथ्यं यन्मयैतत् प्रभाषितम्। तद् विद्धि पृथिवीपाल भक्त्या भरतसत्तम॥
en: True or false, what I have said, O king, has been said from a due respect for you, O best of Bharatas!

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अव्याहरति कौन्तेये धर्मराजे युधिष्ठिरे। भ्रातॄणां ब्रुवतां तास्तान् विविधान् वेदनिश्चयान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said When after listening to his brothers who were telling these truths of the Vedas, Kunti's son king Yudhishthira just remained silent.

sn: महाभिजनसम्पन्ना श्रीमत्यायतलोचना। अभ्यभाषत राजेन्द्र द्रौपदी योषितां वरा॥ आसीनमृषभं राज्ञां भ्रातृभिः परिवारितम्। सिंहशार्दूलसदृशैर्वारणैरिव यूथपम्॥
en: That foremost of nobly born women, viz., Draupadi, of large eyes and great beauty, O king, said these words unto that foremost of kings seated in the midst of his brothers who were like many lions and tigers, and like the leader of an elephantine herd in the midst of a herd of elephants.

sn: अभिमानवती नित्यं विशेषेण युधिष्ठिरे। लालिता सततं राज्ञा धर्मज्ञा धर्मदर्शिनी॥ आमन्त्र्य विपुलश्रोणी साम्ना परमवल्गुना। भर्तारपभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Always expecting respectful love from all her husbands but especially from Yudhishthira, she was always treated with love and indulgence by the king. Conversant with duties and always satisfying them, that lady of large hips, eyeing her husband, drew his attention in soothing and sweet words, and said as follows:

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच इमे ते भ्रातरः पार्थ शुष्यन्ते स्तोकका इव। वावाश्यमानास्तिष्ठन्ति न चैनानभिनन्दसे॥
en: These your brothers, O Partha, are crying and drying their tongues like Chatakas, but you do not please them.

sn: नन्दयैतान् महाराज मत्तानिव महाद्विपान्। उपपन्नेन वाक्येन सततं दुःखभागिनः॥
en: O king, cheer up these your brothers, who are like infuriate elephants (in prowess) with proper words,-these heroes who have always suffered miseries!

sn: कथं द्वैतवने राजन् पूर्वमुक्त्वा तथा वचः। भ्रातृनेतान् स्म सहिताशीतवातातपार्दितान्॥ वयं दुर्योधनं हत्वा मृधे भोक्ष्याम मेदिनीम्। सम्पूर्णां सर्वकामानामाहवे विजयैषिणः॥
en: Why, O king, while living on the bank of the Dvaita lake, did you say to these your brothers then living with you, and suffering from cold and wind and sun, these words, viz.,-engaging in battle to win victory, we will kill Duryodhana and enjoy the Earth that is capable of granting every desire.

sn: विस्थांश्च रथान् कृत्वा निहत्य च महागजान्। संस्तीर्य च रथैर्भूमि ससादिभिररिन्दमाः॥ यजतां विविधैर्यज्ञैः समृद्धैराप्तदक्षिणैः। वनवासकृतं दुःखं भविष्यति सुखाय वः॥
en: Depriving great car-warriors of their cars and killing huge elephants, and covering the battle-field with the bodies of car-warriors and horsemen and horses, O chastiser of foes, you will celebrate great sacrifices of various kinds with profuse presents! All these sufferings of a life of exile in the forest will then end in happiness!

sn: इत्येतानेवमुक्त्वा त्वं स्वयं धर्मभृतां वर। कथमद्य पुनर्वीर विनिहंसि मनांसि नः॥
en: O foremost of the virtuous, having yourself said these words to your brothers then, why, O hero, do you depress our hearts now?

sn: न क्लीबो वसुधां भुक्के न क्लीबो धनमश्नुते। न क्लीबस्य गृहे पुत्रा मत्स्याः पङ्क इवासते॥
en: A eunuch can never enjoy wealth. A eunuch can never have children, as there can be no fish in a mud (destitute of water).

sn: नादण्डः क्षत्रियो भाति नादण्डो भूमिमश्नुते। नादण्डस्य प्रजा राज्ञः सुखं विन्दन्ति भारत॥
en: A Kshatriya without the rod of chastisement never prosper. Without the rod of chastisement a Kshatriya can never enjoy the Earth. The subjects of a king who has no rod of chastisement can never enjoy happiness!

sn: मित्रता सर्वभूतेषु दानमध्ययनं तपः। ब्राह्मणस्यैव धर्म: स्यान्न राज्ञो राजसत्तम॥
en: Love for all creatures, charity, study of the Vedas, penances, are are the duties of a Brahniana and not of a king, O best of kings!

sn: असतां प्रतिषेधश्च सतां च परिपालनम्। एष राज्ञां परो धर्मः समरे चापलायनम्॥
en: Suppressing the wicked, maintaining the honest, and never retreating from battle are the highest duties of kings! can

sn: यस्मिन् क्षमा च क्रोधश्च दानादाने भयाभये। निग्रहानुग्रहौ चोभौ स वै धर्मविदुच्यते॥
en: He is the master of duties in whom reside forgiveness and anger, giving and taking, terror and fearlessness, and chastisement and reward!

sn: न श्रुतेन न दानेन न सान्त्वेन न चेज्यया। त्वयेयं पृथिवी लब्धा न संकोचेन चाप्युत॥
en: It was not by study, or gift, or mendicancy, that you have acquired the Earth?

sn: यत् तद् बलममित्राणां तथा वीर्यसमुद्यतम्। हस्त्यश्वरथसम्पनं त्रिभिरङ्गैरनुत्तमम्॥ रक्षित द्रोणकर्णाभ्यामश्वत्थाम्ना कृपेण च। तत त्वया निहतं वीर तस्माद् भुक्ष्व वसुन्धराम्॥
en: That army of the enemy, O hero, ready to attack you with all its might, consisting of elephants and horses and cars, protected by Drona and Karna and Ashvatthaman and Kripa, has been defeated and killed by you, O hero. It is for this that I request you to enjoy the Earth.

sn: जम्बूद्वीपो महाराज नानाजनपदैर्युतः। त्वया पुरुषशार्दूल दण्डेन मृदितः प्रभो॥
en: (Formerly), O powerful one, you had, O king, governed with might, the region called Jaimbu, O foremost of men, abounding with populous districts!

sn: जम्बूद्वीपेन सदृशः क्रौञ्चद्वीपो नराधिप। अधरेण महामेरोर्दण्डेन मृदितस्त्वया॥
en: You had also, O king, governed with might, that other region called Kraunchadvipa situated on the west of the great Meru and equal to Jambudvipa itself!

sn: क्रौञ्चद्वीपेन सदृशः शाकद्वीपो नराधिप। पूर्वेण तु महामेरोर्दण्डेन मृदितस्त्वया॥
en: You had governed with might, O king, that other region called Shakadvipa on the east of the great Meru and equal to Kraunchadvipa itself!

sn: उत्तरेण महामेरोः शाकद्वीपेन सम्मितः। भद्राश्वः पुरुषव्याघ्र दण्डेन मृदितस्त्वया॥
en: The region called Bhadrashva, on the north of the great Meru and equal to Shakadvipa was also governed by you, O foremost of Men!

sn: द्वीपाश्च सान्तरद्वीया नानाजनपदाश्रयाः। विगाह्य सागरं वीर दण्डेन मृदितास्त्वया॥
en: You had even entered the ocean and governed with inight other regions, too, O hero, and the very islands encircled by the sea and containing many populous districts.

sn: एतान्यप्रतिमेयानि कृत्वा कर्माणि भारत। न प्रीयसे महाराज पूज्यमानो द्विजातिभिः॥
en: Having, O Bharata, made such wonderful conquests, and having obtained (through them) the worship of the Brahmanas, how is it that your mind is not satisfied.

sn: स त्वं भ्रातृनिमान् दृष्ट्वा प्रतिनन्दस्व भारत। ऋषभानिव सम्मत्तान् गजेन्द्रानूर्जितानिव॥
en: Seeing these brothers of your before you, O Bharata,these heroes endued with might and resembling bulls or infuriate clephants-why do you not speak to them sweet words.

sn: अमरप्रतिमाः सर्वे शत्रुसाहाः परंतपाः। एकोऽपि हि सुखायैषां मम स्यादिति मे मतिः।।२८।
en: All of you are like celestials. All of you are capable of withstanding enemies. All of you are capable of scorching your enemies. If only one of you had become my husband. my happiness would even then have been very considerable.

sn: किं पुनः पुरुषव्याघ्र पतयो मे नरर्षभाः। समस्तानीन्द्रियाणीव शरीरस्य विचेष्टने॥
en: What need I say then, O foremost of men, when all of you, five in number, are my husbands (and take care of me) like the five senses working up the body.

sn: अनृतं नाब्रवीच्छ्वश्रूः सर्वज्ञा सर्वदर्शिनी। युधिष्ठिरस्त्वां पाञ्चालि सुखे धास्यत्यनुत्तमे॥
en: The words of my mother-in-law who is endued with great knowledge and foresight, cannot be untrue. She said,-O princess of Panchala, Yudhishthira will always keep you in happiness, O excellent lady.

sn: हत्वा राजसहस्राणि बहून्याशुपराक्रमः। तद् व्यर्थं सम्प्रपश्यामि मोहात् तव जनाधिप॥
en: Having killed many thousands of powerful kings, I see, O monarch, that through your folly you are about to make such an attachment futile.

sn: येषामुन्मत्तको ज्येष्ठः सर्वे तेऽप्यनुसारिणः। तवोन्मादान्महाराज सोन्मादाः सर्वपाण्डवाः॥
en: They whose eldest brother runs mad, have all to follow him like mad men. For your madness, O king, all the Pandavas, are about to become mad.

sn: यदि हि स्युरनुन्मत्ता भ्रातरस्ते नराधिप। बद्ध्वा त्वां नास्तिकैः सार्धं प्रशासेयुर्वसुन्धराम्।।३३ कुरुते मूढ एवं हि यः श्रेयो नाधिगच्छति।
en: If, O King, these your brothers had been sane, they would then have locked you up with all unbelievers (in a prison) and taken charge of the government of the Earth. The man who for feeble intellect acts thus never succeeds in winning prosperity.

sn: धूपैरञ्जनयोगैश्च नस्यकर्मभिरेव च॥ भेषजैः स चिकित्स्यः स्याद् य उन्मार्गेण गच्छति।
en: The man who behaves like a mad, man should be subjected to medical treatment by the aid of incense and collyrium, of drugs applied through the nose, and of other medicaments.

sn: साहं सर्वाधमा लोके स्त्रीणां भरतसत्तम॥ तथा विनिकृता पुत्रैर्याहमिच्छामि जीवितुम्।
en: O best of the Bharatas, I am the worst of all females, since I wish to live on even though I am deprived of my children.

sn: एतेषां यतमानानां न मेऽद्य वचनं मृषा॥ त्वं तु सर्वां महीं त्यक्त्वा कुरुषे स्वयमापदम्।
en: You should not disregard the words spoken by me and by these brothers of yours who are trying thus to dissuade you. Indeed, abandoning the whole Earth, you are inviting adversity and danger to assail you.

sn: यथाऽऽस्तां सम्मतौ राज्ञां पृथिव्यां राजसत्तम॥ मान्धाता चाम्बरीषश्च तथा राजन् विराजसे।
en: You appear in splendour now, O monarch, even as those two foremost of kings, viz., Mandhatri and Ambarisha, respected by all the kings, did in former days.

sn: प्रशाधि पृथिवीं देवीं प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन्॥ सपर्वतवनद्वीपां मा राजन् विमना भव।
en: Protecting your subjects righteously, rule over the goddess Earth with her mountains and forests and islands. Do not, O king, become disspirited.

sn: यजस्व विविधैर्यज्ञैर्युध्यस्वारीन् प्रयच्छ च। धनानि भोगान् वासांसि द्विजातिभ्यो नृपोत्तम॥
en: Worship the gods with various sacrifices. Fight your foes! Present wealth, clothes and other objects of enjoyment to the Brahmanas, O foremost of kings!

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच याज्ञसेन्या वचः श्रुत्वा पुनरेवार्जुनोऽब्रवीत्। अनुमान्य महाबाहुं ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरमच्युतम्॥
en: Hearing these words of Yajnasena's daughter, Arjuna once more spoke, showing every respect for his mighty-armed and ever illustrious eldest brother.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: अर्जुन उवाच दण्डः शास्ति प्रजाः सर्वा दण्ड एवाभिरक्षति। दण्डः सुप्तेषु जागर्ति दण्डं धर्म विदुर्बुधाः॥
en: Arjuna said (A king with) the rod of chastisement sways all subjects and protects them. The rod of chastisement is awake when all else is under sleep. For this, the wise have designated the rod of chastisement as Righteousness itself.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: दण्डः संरक्षते धर्मं तथैवार्थ जनाधिप। कामं संरक्षते दण्डस्त्रिवर्गो दण्ड उच्यते॥
en: The rod of chastisement protects. Religion and Profit. It protects Pleasure also, O king! For this, the rod of chastisement is identified with the three-fold objects of life.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: दण्डेन रक्ष्यते धान्यं धनं दण्डेन रक्ष्यते। एवं विद्वानुपाधत्स्व भावं पश्यस्व लौकिकम्॥
en: Corn and riches are both protected by the rod of chastisement. Knowing this, O learned king, take up the rod of chastisement and follow the ways of the world!

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: राजदण्डभयादेके पापाः पापं न कुर्वते। यमदण्डभयादेके परलोकभयादपि॥
en: One class of wicked men refrain from committing sins through fear of the rod of chastisement in the king's hands. Another section desist from similar acts out of fear of Yama's rod, and another from fear of the next world.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: परस्परभयादेके पापाः पापं न कुर्वते। एवं सांसिद्धिके लोके सर्वं दण्डे प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Another class of persons refrain from committing sinful acts through fear of society. Thus, O king, in this world, everything depends on the rod of chastisement.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: दण्डस्यैव भयादेके न खादन्ति परस्परम्। अन्धे तमसि मज्जेयुर्यदि दण्डो न पालयेत्॥
en: There are persons who are checked by only the rod of chastisement from devouring one another. If the rod of chastisement did not protect people, they would have been immersed in the darkness of hell.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: यस्माददान्तान् दमयत्यशिष्टान् दण्डयत्यपि। दमनाद् दण्डनाच्चैव तस्माद् दण्डं विदुर्बुधाः॥
