en: The rod of chastisement (Danda) has been so designated by the wise, because it governs the ungovernable and punishes the wicked.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: वाचा दण्डो ब्राह्मणानां क्षत्रियाणां भुजार्पणम्। दानदण्डाः स्मृता वैश्या निर्दण्डः शूद्र उच्यते॥
en: The chastisement should be meted to the Brahmanas by words only; to the Kshatriyas, by giving them only that much of food as would suffice for the up-keep of life; to the Vaishyas, by the imposition of fines and forfeitures of property, while for the Sudras there is no punishment.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: असम्मोहाय मर्त्यानामर्थसंरक्षणाय च। मर्यादा स्थापिता लोके दण्डसंज्ञा विशाम्पते।॥
en: For compelling men to stick to their duties) and for the protection of property, punitive laws, O king, have been established in the world.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: यत्र श्यामो लोहिताक्षो दण्डश्चरति सूद्यतः। प्रजास्तत्र न मुह्यन्ते नेता चेत् साधु पश्यति॥
en: The subjects never forget their duties, where Chastisement, of dark complexion and red eyes, stand ready (to grapple with every offender) and the king is of righteous vision.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: ब्रह्मचारी गृहस्थश्च वानप्रस्थश्च भिक्षुकः। दण्डस्यैव भयादेते मनुष्या वर्त्मनि स्थिताः॥
en: The Brahmacharin and the householder, the hermit and the religious mendicant, all follow their respective duties through fear of chastisement only.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: नाभीतो यजते राजन् नाभीतो दातुमिच्छति। नाभीतः पुरुषः कश्चित् समये स्थातुमिच्छति॥
en: He that is without any fear, O king, never celebrates a sacrifice. He that is without fear never gives away. The man that is without any fear never desires to satisfy and engagement or contract.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: नाच्छित्त्वा परमर्माणि नाकृत्वा कर्म दुष्करम्। नाहत्वा मत्स्यघातीव प्राणोति महतीं श्रियम्॥
en: Without cutting the vital parts of others, without performing the most difficult deeds, and without killing creatures like a fisherman (slaying fish), no person can acquire great prosperity.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: नाघ्नतः कीर्तिरस्तीह न वित्तं न पुनः प्रजाः। इन्द्रो वृत्रवधेनैव महेन्द्रः समपद्यत॥
en: Without slaughter no man has been able to acquire fame in this world or wealth or subjects. Indra himself, by killing Vritra, became the great Indra.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: य एव देवा हन्तारस्ताँल्लोकोऽर्चयते भृशम्। हन्ता रुद्रस्तथा स्कन्दः शक्रोऽग्निवरुणो यमः॥
en: Those amongst the gods that are giving to killing others are worshipped much more by inen. Rudra, Skanda, Shakra, Agni, Varuna, are all destroyers.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: हन्ता कालस्तथा वायुर्मुत्युर्वैश्रवणो रविः। वसवो मरुतः साध्या विश्वेदेवाश्च भारत॥
en: Kala and Mrityu and Vayu and Kubera and Surya, the Vasus, the Maruts, the Saddhyas and the Vishvedevas, O Bharata, are all destroyers.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: एतान् देवान् नमस्यन्ति प्रतापप्रणता जनाः। न ब्रह्माणं न धातारं न पूषाणं कथंचना॥
en: Humiliated by their power, all people bow to these gods, but not to Brahmana or Dhatri or Pushan at any time.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: मध्यस्थान् सर्वभूतेषु दान्ताशमपरायणान्। यजन्ते मानवाः केचित् प्रशान्ताः सर्वकर्मसु॥
en: Only a few noble-ininded men worship in all their acts those among the gods who treat all creatures equally and who are self-restrained and peaceful.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: न हि पश्यामि जीवन्तं लोके कञ्चिदहिंसया। सत्त्वैः सत्त्वा हि जीवन्ति दुर्बलैर्बलवत्तराः॥
en: I do not see any such creature in this world that supports life without doing any act of injury to others. Animals live upon animals, the stronger upon the weaker.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: नकुलो मूषिकानत्ति बिडालो नकुलं तथा। विडालमत्तिश्वा राजश्वानं व्यालमृगस्तथा॥
en: The mungoose eats up mice; the cat eats up inungoose; the dog eats up the cat; the dog again is devoured by the spotted leopard.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: तानत्तिं पुरुषः सर्वान् पश्य कालो यथागतः। प्राणस्यान्नमिदं सर्वं जङ्गमं स्थावरं च यत्॥
en: Behold, all things again are eaten up by the Destroyer when he comes! This mobile and immobile universe is food for living creatures.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: विधानं दैवविहितं तत्र विद्वान् न मुह्यति। यथा सृष्टोऽसि राजेन्द्र तथा भवितुमर्हसि॥
en: This has been ordained by the celestials. The learned man, therefore, is never stupefied at it. You should, O great king, become what you are by birth!

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: विनीतक्रोधहर्षा हि मन्दा वनमुपाश्रिताः। विना वधं न कुर्वन्ति तापसा: प्राणयापनम्॥
en: Only the foolish (Kshatriyas) controlling anger and joy, dwell in the woods. The very ascetics cannot maintain their lives without killing creatures.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: उदके बहवः प्राणाः पृथिव्यां च फलेषु च। न च कश्चिन्न तान् हन्ति किमन्यत् प्राणयापनात्॥
en: Innumerable creature live in water, on earth and in fruits. It is not true that one does not kill them. What greater duty is there than supporting one's life?

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: सूक्ष्मयोनीनि भूतानि तर्कगम्यानि कानिचित्। पक्ष्मणोऽपि निपातेन येषां स्यात् स्कन्धपर्ययः॥
en: There are many creatures that are so ininute that their existence is not perceptible. The falling of the eyelids even kills them.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: ग्रामान् निष्क्रम्य मुनयो विगतक्रोधमत्सराः। वने कुटुम्बधर्माणो दृश्यन्ते परिमोहिताः॥
en: There are men who controlling anger and pride love like ascetics and abandoning villages and towns repair to the forests. Coming there, those men become so stupefied that they live like householder again.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: भूमि भित्त्वौषधीश्छित्त्वा वृक्षादीनण्डजान् पशून्। मनुष्यास्तन्वते यज्ञास्ते स्वर्ग प्राप्नुवन्ति च॥
en: Others living like householders and tilling the soil, uprooting herbs, cutting off trees and killing birds and animals celebrate sacrifices and at last attain to heaven.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: दण्डनीत्यां प्रणीतायां सर्वे सिद्ध्यन्त्युपक्रमाः। कौन्तेय सर्वभूतानां तत्र मे नास्ति संशयः॥
en: O son of Kunti, I am sure that the acts of all creatures become successful only when the policy of chastisement is properly applied.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: दण्डचेन्न भवेल्लोके विनश्येयुरिमाः प्रजाः। जले मत्स्यानिवाभक्ष्यन् दुर्बलान् बलवत्तराः॥
en: If chastisement were done away with in this word, creatures would soon be destroyed. Like fishes in the water, stronger animals devour the weaker.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: सत्यं चेदं ब्रह्मणा पूर्वमुक्तं दण्डः प्रजा रक्षति साधु नीतः। पश्याग्नयश्च प्रतिशाम्य भीताः संतर्जिता दण्डभयाज्ज्वलन्ति॥
en: Formerly Brahman himself, said that chastisement, properly applied, maintains creatures. Behold, the very fires, when put out, blaze up again, in fright, when blown! This is owing to the fear of force.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: अन्धं तम इवेदं स्यान्न प्राज्ञायत किंचना दण्डश्चेन्न भवेल्लोके विभजन साध्वसाधुनी॥
en: If there were no chastisement in the world differentiating the good from the evil, the whole world would have been covered with sheer darkness and all things would have been unsettled.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: येऽपि सम्भिन्नमर्यादा नास्तिका वेदनिन्दकाः। तेऽपि भोगाय कल्पन्ते दण्डेनाशु निपीडिताः॥
en: By chastisement the violators of laws, the atheists and scoffers of the Vedas, soon become disposed to observe rules and regulations.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: सर्वो दण्डजितो लोको दुर्लभो हि शुचिर्जनः। दण्डस्य हि भयाद् भीतो भोगायैव प्रवर्तते॥
en: Every one in this world is kept all right by chastisement. A person by nature pure and pious is rare. In fear of chastisement, man becomes disposed to observe rules and restrictions.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: चातुर्वर्ण्यप्रमोदाय सुनीतिनयनाय च। दण्डो विधात्रा विहितो धर्मार्थी भुवि रक्षितुम्॥
en: Chastisement was introduced by the Creator himself for protecting Religion and Profit, for the happiness of all the four orders, and for making thein pious and humble.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: यदि दण्डान्न बिभ्येयुर्वयांसि श्वापदानि च। अधुः पशून् मनुष्यांश्च यज्ञार्थानि हवींषि च॥
en: If there had been no fear of chastisement, then ravens and beasts of prey would have devoured all other animals and men and the clarified butter intended for sacrifices.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: न ब्रह्मचार्यधीयीत कल्याणी गौर्न दुह्यते। न कन्योद्वहनं गच्छेद् यदि दण्डो न पालयेत्॥
en: If chastisement did not keep up and protect (the world), then no body would have read the Vedas, nobody would have milked a milch cow, and no maiden would have married.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: विष्वग्लोपः प्रवर्तेत भिधेरन् सर्वसेतवः। ममत्वं न प्रजानीयुर्यदि दण्डो न पालयेत्॥
en: If chastisement did not uphold and protect, then destruction and confusion would have prevailed everywhere and all restrictions would have disappeared, and the idea of property would have gone away.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: न संवत्सरसत्राणि तिष्ठेयुरकुतोभयाः। विधिवद् दक्षिणावन्ति यदि दण्डो न पालयेत्॥
en: If chastisement did not uphold and protect, people could never duly celebrate annual sacrifices with profuse presents.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: चरेयुर्नाश्रमे धर्म यथोक्तं विधिमाश्रिताः। न विद्यां प्राप्नुयात् कश्चिद् यदि दण्डो न पालयेत्।।४०
en: If chastisement did not uphold and protect, no one would observe the duties of his own order as sanctioned (in the scriptures), and no one would have succeeded in gaining knowledge.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: न चोष्टा न बलीव नाश्वाश्वतरगर्दभाः। युक्ता वहेयुर्यानानि यदि दण्डो न पालयेत्॥
en: If chastisement did not reign supreme, neither, nor asses, would, even if yoked thereto, would carry cars and carriages.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: न प्रेष्या वचनं कुर्युर्न बाला जातु कर्हिचित्। न तिष्ठेद् युवती धर्मे यदि दण्डो न पालयेत्॥ दण्डे स्थिताः प्रजाः सर्वा भयं दण्डे विदुर्बुधाः। दण्डे स्वर्गो मनुष्याणां लोकोऽयं सुप्रतिष्ठितः॥
en: All creatures depend upon chastisement. The learned, therefore, declare that chastisement is the root of all things. Upon chastisement rests the heaven that people seek, and upon il rests this world also.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: न तत्र कूटं पापं वा वञ्चना वापि दृश्यते। यत्र दण्डः सुविहितश्चरत्यरिविनाशनः॥
en: No sin, no falsehood, and no wickedness, is to be seen there where foe-destroying chastisement is properly used.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: हविःश्वा प्रलिहेद् दृष्ट्वा दण्डश्चेन्नोद्यतो भवेत्। हरेत् काकः पुरोडाशं यदि दण्डो न पालयेत्॥
en: If the rod of chastisement be not taken up, the dog will lick the sacrificial butter. If that rod were not raised up, the crow also would take away the first (sacrificial) offering.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: यदीदं धर्मतो राज्यं विहितं यद्यधर्मतः। कार्यस्तत्र शोको वै भुक्ष्व भोगान् यजस्व च॥
en: Fairly or unfairly, this kingdom has not been gained by us. Our duty now is to give up grief. Do you, therefore, enjoy it and celebrate sacrifices!

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: सुखेन धर्मं श्रीमन्तश्चरन्ति शुचिवाससः। संवर्षन्तः फलैर्दानैर्भुजानाश्चान्नमुत्तमम्॥
en: Living with their dear wives the lucky men, cat good food, wear good clothes, and cheerfully acquire virtue by fruits and gifts.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: अर्थे सर्वे समारम्भाः समायत्ता न संशयः। स च दण्डे समायत्तः पश्य दण्डस्य गौरवम्॥
en: Forsooth, all our acts, depend on wealth : that wealth again depends on chastisement. Mark, therefore, the utility of chastisement!

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: लोकयात्रार्थमेवेह धर्मप्रवचनं कृतम्। अहिंसासाधुहिंसेति श्रेयान् धर्मपरिग्रहः॥
en: Duties have been laid down for maintaining the various relations of the world. There are two things here, viz., abstention from injury and injury done with righteous motives, Of these two, that which brings in righteousness is preferable.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: नात्यन्तं गुणवत् किंचिन्न चाप्यत्यन्तनिर्गुणम्। उभयं सर्वकार्येषु दृश्यते साध्वसाधु वा॥
en: There is no act that is entirely pure, nor any that is entirely simple. In all acts, right or wrong, something of both prevails.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: पशूनां वृषणं छित्त्वा ततो भिन्दन्ति मस्तकम्। वहन्ति बहवो भारान् बध्नन्ति दमयन्ति च॥
en: Animals are castrated, and their horns are cut off. They are then compelled to carry weights are tethered, and beaten.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: एवं पर्याकुले लोके वितथैर्जर्जरीकृते। तैस्तैायैर्महाराज पुराणं धर्ममाचर॥
en: In this world that is unsubstantial full of abuses and painful, O king, do you practise the old customs of men, following rules and examples quoted above.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: यज्ञ देहि प्रजां रक्ष धर्म समनुपालय। अमित्राञ्जहि कौन्तेय मित्राणि परिपालय॥
en: Celebrate sacrifices, distribute alms, protect your subjects, and practise righteousness. Kill your enemies, O son of Kunti, and protect your friends.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: मा च ते निघ्नतः शत्रून् मन्युर्भवतु पार्थिव। न तत्र किल्बिषं किंचित् कर्तुर्भवति भारत।॥
en: Be not dispirited. O king, while killing enemies! He that does it, О Bharata, does not commit the slightest sin!

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: आततायी हि यो हन्यादाततायिनमागतम्। न तेन भ्रूणहा स स्यान्मन्युस्तं मन्युमार्छति॥
en: He who takes up a weapon and kills an arined enemy advancing against him, does not incur the sin of killing a man, for it is the anger of the advancing enemy that excites the anger of the destroyer.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: अवध्यः सर्वभूतानामन्तरात्मा न संशयः। अवध्ये चात्मनि कथं वध्योभवति कस्यचित्॥
en: The soul of every creature cannot be killed. When the soul cannot be killed how then can one be killed by another?

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: यथा हि पुरुषः शालां पुनः सम्प्रविशेन्नवाम्। एवं जीवः शरीराणि तानि तानि प्रपद्यते॥
en: As a person enters a new house, so does a creature put on successive bodies.

description: Arjuna again asks Yudhishthira to exercise the Rod of Punishment
sn: देहान् पुराणानुत्सृज्य नवान् सम्प्रतिपद्यते। एवं मृत्युमुखं प्राहुर्जना ये तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥
en: Leaving behind decrepit bodies, a creature acquires new forms. People gifted with true insight consider this change as death.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अर्जुनस्य वचः श्रुत्वा भीमसेनोऽत्यमर्षणः। धैर्यमास्थाय तेजस्वी ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said After Arjuna had done the highly wrathful and energetic Bhimasena, collecting all his patience, said these words to his eldest brother:राजन् विदितधर्मोऽसि न तेऽस्त्यविदितं क्वचित्।

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: उपशिक्षाम ते वृत्तं सदैव न च शक्नुमः॥
en: 'You are, O king, conversant with all duties. There is nothing unknown to you. We always wish to imitate your conduct, but, alas, we cannot do it.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: न वक्ष्यामि न वक्ष्यामीत्येवं मे मनसि स्थितम्। अतिदुःखात्तु वक्ष्यामि तन्निबोध जनाधिप॥
en: I had wished not to say anything. Excited, however, by great grief I am compelled to say something. Listen to these words of mine, O king.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: भवतः सम्प्रमोहेन सर्वं संशयितं कृतम्। विक्लवत्वं च नः प्राप्तमवलत्वं तथैव च॥
en: Everything has been imperilled by the bewilderment of your faculties, and ourselves are being made disspirited and weak.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: कथं हि राजा लोकस्य सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः। मोहमापद्यसे दैन्याद् यथा कापुरुषस्तथा॥
en: How is it that you who are the king of the world, you who are the master of all branches of knowledge, allow your understanding to be clouded, with depression like a coward?

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: अगतिश्च गतिश्चैव लोकस्य विदिता तव। आयत्यां च तदात्वे च न तेऽस्त्यविदितंप्रभो॥
en: The fair and unfair paths of the world are known to you. Everything belonging either to the future or the present is known to you, O powerfiil one.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: एवं गते महाराज राज्यं प्रति जनाधिप। हेतुमत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि तमिहैकमनाः शृणु॥
en: When such in the case, O king, I will point out, O king, the reasons in favour of your assuming sovereignty. Listen to me with rapt attention.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: द्विविधो जायते व्याधिः शारीरो मानसस्तथा। परस्परं तयोर्जन्म निर्द्वन्द्वं नोपलभ्यते॥
en: There are two sorts of diseases, viz., physical and mental. Each originates from the other. None of them exists independently.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: शारीराज्जायते व्याधिर्मानसो नात्र संशयः। मानसाज्जायते वापि शारीर इति निश्चयः॥
en: Forsooth, mental diseases originate form physical ones. Likewise physical diseases originate from mental ones. This is the truth.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: शारीरं मानसं दुःखं योऽतीतमनुशोचति। दुःखेन लभते दुःखं द्वावनौँ च विन्दति॥
en: He who bewails for past physical or mental afflictions, reaps affliction from afflictions and suffers double afflictions.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: शीतोष्णे चैव वायुश्च त्रयः शारीरजा गुणाः। तेषां गुणानां साम्यं यत्तदाहुः स्वस्थलक्षणम्॥
en: Cold, heat, and winds,-are the three essentials of the body. Their harmonious existence indicates good heath.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: तेषामन्यतमोद्रेके विधानमुपदिश्यते। उष्णेन बाध्यते शीतं शीतेनोष्णं प्रबाध्यते॥
en: In case of one of the three prevailing over the rest, remedies have been prescribed. Cold is checked by heat, and heat is checked by cold.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति मानसाः स्युस्त्रयो गुणाः। तेषां गुणानां साम्यं यत्तदाहुः स्वस्थलक्षणम्॥
en: Goodness, darkness, and ignorance are the three qualities of the mind. The harmonious existence of these three is the sign of (mental) health.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: तेषामन्यतमोत्सेके विधानमुपदिश्यते। हर्षेण बाध्यते शोको हर्षः शोकेन बाध्यते॥
en: If one of these reigns supreme over the rest, remedies have been laid down. Grief is checked by joy, and joy is checked by grief.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: कश्चित् सुखे वर्तमानो दुःखस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छति। कश्चिद् दुःखे वर्तमानः सुखस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छति॥ स त्वं न दुःखी दुःखस्य न सुखी च सुखस्य वा। न दुःखी सुखजातस्य न सुखी दुःखजस्य वा॥ स्मर्तुमिच्छसि कौरव्य दिष्टं हि बलवत्तरम्। अथवा ते स्वभावोऽयं येन पार्थिव क्लिश्यसे॥ दृष्ट्वा सभागतां कृष्णामेकवस्त्रां रजस्वलाम्। मिषतां पाण्डुपुत्राणां न तस्य स्मर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: One, living in the present enjoyment of happiness, wishes to recollect his past miseries. Another, suffering in the present woe, wishes to recollect his past happiness. You, however, were never sorry in grief or glad in happiness. You should not, therefore, use your memory for becoming sad during times of happiness, or glad during times of miseries. It seems that Destiny is omnipotent. Or, if it be your nature, which afflicts you, why do you not then remember the sight you saw before, viz., the scantily-clad Krishna dragged, while in her season, before the assembly?

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: द्रौपद्या राजपुत्र्याश्च प्रव्राजनं च नगरादजिनैश्च विवासनम्। महारण्यनिवासश्च न तस्य स्मर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Why do you not remember our expulsion from the (Kuru) city and our exile (into the forest clad in deer-skins, as also our, living in the great forests?

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: जटासुरात् परिक्लेशं चित्रसेनेन चाहवम्। सैन्धवाच्च परिक्लेशं कथं विस्मृतवानसि॥
en: Why have you forgotten the woes inflicted by Jatasura, the battle with Chitrasena, and the miseries suffered at the hands of the Sindhu king?

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: पुनरज्ञातचर्यायां कीचकेन पदा वधम्। कथं विस्मृतवानसि॥
en: Why have you forgotten the princess Draupadi kicked by Kichaka while we were living in concealment?

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: यच्च ते द्रोणभीष्माभ्यां युद्धमासीदरिन्दम। मनसैकेन योद्धव्यं तत्ते युद्धमुपस्थितम्॥
en: A dreadful battle, O chastiser of foes, like that which you have fought with Bhishma and Drona is now before you, to be fought, (however) with your mind alone.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: यत्र नास्ति शरैः कार्यं न मित्रैर्न च बन्धुभिः । आत्मनैकेन योद्धव्यं तत्ते युद्धमुपस्थितम्॥
en: Indeed, a battle is now before you in which there is no necessity of arrows, friends, of relatives and kinsmen, but which will have to be fought with your mind only.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: तस्मिन्ननिर्जिते युद्धे प्राणान् यदि विमोक्ष्यसे। अन्यं देहं समास्थाय ततस्तैरपि योत्स्यसे॥
en: If you expire before conquering in this battle, then, assuming another body, you shall have to fight these very enemies again.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: तस्मादद्यैव गन्तव्यं युद्ध्यस्व भरतर्षभ। परमव्यक्तरूपस्य व्यक्तं त्यक्त्वा स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: Therefore, fight that battle this every day, O foremost of Bharata's race, not caring for your body, and helped by your own acts, conquer the enemy of your mind,

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: तस्मिन्ननिर्जिते युद्धे कामवस्थां गमिष्यसि। एतजित्वा महाराज कृतकृत्यो भविष्यसि॥
en: If you cannot win that battle what will be your condition? On the other hand, by acquiring victory in it, O monarch, you shall have attained the great end of life.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: एतां बुद्धिं विनिश्चित्य भूतानामागतिं गतिम्। पितृपैतामहे वृत्ते शाधि राज्यं यथोचितम्॥
en: Applying your intellect to this, and determining the right and the wrong paths of creatures, follow the course of your forefathers and govern properly your kingdom.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: दिष्ट्या दुर्योधनः पापो निहतः सानुगो युधि। द्रौपद्याः केशपाशस्य दिष्ट्या त्वं पदवीं गतः॥
en: By good luck, O king, the sinful Duryodhana has been killed with all his followers. By good luck, you too, like Draupadi's locks, have regained your normal position.

description: Bhima also asks Yudhishthira to follow their fore-fathers and govern the kingdom
sn: यजस्व वाजिमेधेन विधिवद् दक्षिणावता। वयं ते किंकराः पार्थ वासुदेवश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: Celebrate with due rites and enough presents the horse-sacrifice. We are your servants, O son of Pritha, as also the highly energetic Vasudeva.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच असंतोषः प्रमादश्च मदो रागोऽप्रशान्तता। बलं मोहोऽभिमानश्चाप्युद्वेगश्चैव सर्वशः॥ एभिः पाप्मभिराविष्टो राज्यं त्वमभिकाङ्क्षसे। निरामिषो विनिर्मुक्तः प्रशान्तः सुसुखी भव॥
en: Yudhishthira said Visited by the sins of discontent, heedlessness, attachment to earthly objects, the absence of tranquillity, power, folly, vanity, and anxiety, O Bhima, you covet sovereignty. Freed from desire, overcoming joy and grief and acquiring tranquillity, try to be happy.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: य इमामखिलां भूमि शिष्यादेको महीपतिः। तस्याप्युदरमेकं वै किमिदं त्वं प्रशंससि॥
en: That matchless king who will govern this unbounded Earth, will have but one stomach. Why do you then speak highly of this course of life?

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: नाह्ना पूरयितुं शक्यां न मासैर्भरतर्षभ। अपूर्यां पूरयन्निच्छामायुषापि न शक्नुयात्॥
en: One's desires, O foremost of Bharata's race, cannot be satisfied in a day, or in many months. Desire, which cannot be satisfied, is not satisfied in one's whole life.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: यथेद्धः प्रज्वलत्यग्निरसमिद्धः प्रशाम्यति।। अल्पाहारतया त्वग्निं शमयौदर्यमुत्थितम्॥
en: Fire, when fed with fuel, is lighted up; when not so fed, it is put out. Do you, therefore, put out with little food the fire in your stomach when it appears.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: आत्मोदरकृतेऽप्राज्ञः करोति विघसं बहु। जयोदरं पृथिव्या ते श्रेयो निर्जितया जितम्॥
en: He who is shorn of wisdom seeks much food for his stomach. Govern your stomach first (After conquering the Death, you will acquire what is for your permanent good.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: मानुषान् कामभोगांस्त्वमैश्वर्यं च प्रशंससि। अभोगिनोऽबलाश्चैव यान्ति स्थानमनुत्तमम्॥७॥
en: You speak highly of your worldly desires and enjoyinents and prosperity. But those who have renounced all enjoyments and reduced their bodies by penances obtain blissful regions.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: योगः क्षेमश्च राष्ट्रस्य धर्माधर्मों त्वयि स्थितौ। मुच्यस्व महतो भारात् त्यागमेवाभिसंश्रय॥
en: The acquisition and preservation of kingdom is attended with both fair and foul of your means. The desire for them is in you. Free yourself, however, from your great burdens, and practise Renunciation.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: एकोदरकृते व्याघ्रः करोति विघसं बहु। तमन्येऽप्युपजीवन्ति मन्दा लोभवशा मृगाः॥
en: The tiger, for filling one stomach of his, kills many animals. Other weak animals moved by covetousness live upon the tiger's prey.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: विषयान् प्रतिसंगृह्य संन्यासं कुरुते यतिः। न च तुष्यन्ति राजानः पश्य बुद्ध्यन्तरं यथा॥
en: If kings, accepting worldly possessions, practise Renunciation, they can never acquire contentinent. Mark the Joss understanding.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: पत्राहारैरश्मकुट्टैर्दन्तोलूखलिकैस्तथा। अब्भक्षैर्वायुभक्षैश्च तैरयं नरको जितः॥
en: They, however, who live no leaves of trees, or use two stones only at their teeth alone for husking their grain, or live upon water only or air alone, can conquer hell.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: यस्त्विमां वसुधां कृत्स्ना प्रशासेदखिलां नृपः। तुल्याश्मकाञ्चनो यश्च स कृतार्थो न पार्थिवः॥
en: Of the two, the king who rules this wide unbounded Earth, and the person who regards gold and pebbles in the same light, the latter is said to have attained the object of his life and not the former.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: संकल्पेषु निरारम्भो निराशो निर्ममो भव। अशोकं स्थानमातिष्ठ इह चामुत्र चाव्ययम्॥
en: Relying, therefore, upon that which is the eternal source of joy both here and hereafter, leave off all actions and attachment thereto.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: निरामिषा न शोचन्ति शोचसि त्वं किमामिषम्। परित्यज्यामिषं सर्वं मृषावादात् प्रमोक्ष्यसे॥
en: They who have given up desire and enjoyment have never to grieve. You, however, grieve for enjoyments. Abandoning desire and enjoyment, you may succeed in freeing yourself from false specch.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: पन्थानौ पितृयानश्च देवयानश्च विश्रुतौ। ईजानाः पितृयानेन देवयानेन मोक्षिणः॥
en: There are but two well-known roads (for : us), viz., the road of the Pitris and that of the celestials. They who celebrate sacrifices go by the Pitri-path, while they who want salvation, go by the celestial path.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण स्वाध्यायेन महर्षयः। विमुच्य देहांस्ते यान्ति मृत्योरविषयं गताः॥
en: By penances, by Brahmacharya, by study, the great Rishis, casting off their bodies, go to regions which are above the power of Death.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: आमिषं बन्धनं लोके कर्मेहोक्तं तथामिषम्। ताभ्यां विमुक्तः पापाभ्यां पदमाप्नोति तत् परम्॥
en: Worldly enjoyments are called fetters. They have also been called Action Freed from the sinful fetters of action, one attains to the highest end.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: अपि गाथां पुरा गीतां जनकेन वदन्त्युत। निर्द्वन्द्वेन विमुक्तेन मोक्षं समनुपश्यता॥
en: A verse was sung (of old) by Janaka who was liberated from the pairs of opposites, from desire and enjoyments, and observed the religion of Moksha.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: अनन्तं बत मे वित्तं यस्य मे नास्ति किञ्चन। मिथिलायां प्रदीप्तायां न मे दह्यति किञ्चन॥
en: The verse is,-My wealth is boundless, yet I have nothing. If the whole of Mithila were burnt to ashes, nothing of mine will be burnt.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: प्रज्ञाप्रासादमारुह्य अशोचशोचतो जनान्। जगतीस्थानिवाद्रिस्थो मन्दबुद्धीनवेक्षते॥
en: As a person from the summit of a hill looks down upon men on the plain below, so he that has got up on the top of the edifice of knowledge, sees people grieving for things which are not worth mourning for. He, however, who is of foolish understanding, does not mark this.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: दृश्यं पश्यति यः पश्यन् स चक्षुष्मान् स बुद्धिमान्। अज्ञातानां च विज्ञानात् सम्बोधाद् बुद्धिरुच्यते।।२शा
en: He who, really sees all visible things, is said to have eyes and understanding. The faculty of understanding is known as such, because of the knowledge and comprehension it gives of unknown and incomprehensible things.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: यस्तु वाचं विजानाति बहुमानमियात् स वै। ब्रह्मभावप्रपन्नानां वैद्यानां भावितात्मनाम्॥
en: He who understands the sayings of persons who are learned, who are of purified souls, and who have attained to a state of Brahma, secures great honours.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति। तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When a person regards creatures of innumerable varieties to be all of one and the same and to be but various emanations of the same essence, he is then said to have attained Brahma.

description: Yudhishthira denounces worldly enjoyments and activities. The real vision of men described.
sn: ते जनास्तां गतिं यान्ति नाविद्वांसोऽल्पचेतसः। नाबुद्धयो नातपसः सर्वं बुद्धौ प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Those who have acquired this high state of culture attain to that supreme and blissful end, and not they who have not acquired knowledge, or they who are of weak understanding, or they who are bereft of understanding, or they who do not practise penances. Indeed, everything rest on the understanding.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तूष्णीम्भूतं तु राजानं पुनरेवार्जुनोऽब्रवीत्। संतप्तः शोकदुःखाभ्यां राजवाक्छल्यपीडितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said When after saying these words, Yudhishthira became silent, Arjuna, pained by that speech of the king, and burning with sorrow and grief, once more said to his eldest brother,

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: अर्जुन उवाच कथयन्ति पुरावृत्तमितिहासमिमं जनाः। विदेहराज्ञः संवादं भार्यया सह भारत॥
en: Arjuna said People recite this old history, O Bharata, about the discourse between the king of the Videhas and his queen.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: उत्सृज्य राज्यं भिक्षार्थं कृतबुद्धिं नरेश्वरम्। विदेहराजमहिषी दुःखिता यदभाषत॥
en: It is the account of the words which the grief-stricken wife of the king of the Videhas had said to her lord when the latter, leaving his kingdom, had resolved to live like a mendicant.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: धनान्यपत्यं दाराश्च रत्नानि विविधानि च। पन्थानं पावकं हित्वा जनको मौढ्यमास्थितः॥
en: Leaving off wealth and children and wives and valuable possessions of all sorts and the established path for acquiring religious merit and fire itself, king Janaka shaved his head.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: तं ददर्श प्रिया भार्या भक्ष्यवृत्तिमकिंचनम्। धानामुष्टिमुपासीनं निरीहं गतमत्सरम्॥
en: His dear wife saw him deprived of wealth, practising the vow of mendicancy resolved to abstain from inflicting any kind of injury on others, shorn of vanity and prepared to subsist upon a handful of barley fallen off from the stalk.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: तमुवाच समागत्य भर्तारमकुतोभयम्। क्रुद्धा मनस्विनी भार्या विविक्ते हेतुमद् वचः॥
en: Approaching her husband when he was alone, the queen possessing great strength of mind, fearlessly and in anger, told him these reasonable words:-

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: कथमुत्सृज्य राज्यं स्वं धनधान्यसमन्वितम्। कापाली वृत्तिमास्थाय धानामुष्टिर्न ते वरः॥
en: 'Why have you adopted a life of mendicancy, leaving your prosperous kingdom : full of corn? A handful of fallen off barley is not your becoming diet.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: प्रतिज्ञा तेऽन्यथा राजन् विचेष्टा चान्यथा तव। यद् राज्यं महदुत्सृज्य स्वल्पे तुष्यसि पार्थिव॥
en: Your resolution does not agree with your acts, since leaving your large kingdom you, O king, seek a handful of grain.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: नैतेनातिथयो राजन् देवर्षिपितरस्तथा। अद्य शक्यास्त्वया भर्तुं मोघस्तेऽयं परिश्रमः॥
en: With this handful of barley, O king, you will not be able to gratify your guests, gods, Rishis, and Pitris? This your labour, therefore, is in vain.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: देवतातिथिभिश्चैव पितृभिश्चैव पार्थिव। सर्वरेतैः परित्यक्तः परिव्रजसि निष्क्रियः॥
en: Alas forsaken by gods, guests, and Pitris, you live like a wandering mendicant, o king, having cast off all action.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: यस्त्वं त्रैविद्यवृद्धानां ब्राह्मणानां सहस्रशः। भर्ता भूत्वा च लोकस्य सोऽद्य तै तिमिच्छसि॥
en: You, before this, supported thousands of Brahmanas versed in the three Vedas and many more others. How can you desire to beg of them your own food today.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: श्रियं हित्वा प्रदीप्तां त्वं श्ववत् सम्प्रति वीक्ष्यसे। अपुत्रा जननी तेऽद्य कौसल्या चापतिस्त्वया॥
en: Forsaking your blazing prosperity, you look about like a dog for his food. Your mother has to-day been made sonless by you, and your wife, the princess of Koshala, a widow.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: अमी च धर्मकामास्त्वां क्षत्रियाः पर्युपासते। त्वदाशामभिकाङ्क्षन्तः कृपणाः फलहेतुका॥
en: These helpless Kshatriyas, expecting fruits of religious merit, wait upon you, placing all their hopes on you.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: तांश्च त्वं विफलान् कुर्वन् कं नु लोकं गमिष्यसि। राजन् संशयिते मोक्षे परतन्त्रेषु देहिषु॥
en: By dissipating their hopes, to what regions will you go, O king, especially when salvation is doubtful and creatures are dependent on actions?

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: नैव तेऽस्ति परो लोको नापरः पापकर्मणः! धान् दारान् परित्यज्य यस्त्वमिच्छसि जीवितुम्॥
en: Sinful as you are, you will acquire neither this world nor the next, since you wish to live, having cast off your married wife?

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: स्त्रजो गन्धानलंकारान् वासांसि विविधानि च। किमर्थमभिसंत्यज्य परिव्रजसि निष्क्रियः॥
en: Why, indeed, do you lead a life of roving mendicancy, abstaining from all actions, after having forsaken garlands and perfumes and ornaments and robes of various sorts.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: निपानं सर्वभूतानां भूत्वा त्वं पावनं महत्। आढ्यो वनस्पतिर्भूत्वा सोऽन्यांस्त्वं पर्युपाससे॥
en: Having been, like a large and sacred lake to all creatures, having been a mighty tree worthy of adoration, alas, how can you wait upon and adore others?

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: खादन्ति हस्तिनं न्यासैः क्रव्यादा बहवोऽप्युत। बहवः कृमयश्चैव किं पुनस्त्वामनर्थकम्॥
en: If even an elephant gives up all work, carnivorous creatures and innumerable worms would eat it up. What need be said of yourself who are so powerless?

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: य इमां कुण्डिका भिन्द्यात् त्रिविष्टब्धं च यो हरेत्। वासश्चापि हरेत् तस्मिन् कथं ते मानसं भवेत्॥ यस्त्वयं सर्वमुत्सृज्य धानामुष्टेरनुग्रहः। यदानेन समं सर्वं किमिदं ह्यवसीयसे॥
en: How could your heart approve of that mode of life which recommends an earthen pot, and a triple-headed rod, and which compels one to give up his very clothes, and which sanctions the acceptance of only a handful of barley after leaving off everything? If, again, you hold that kingdom and a handful of barley are the same to you, then why do you abandon the foriner.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: धानामुष्टेरिहार्थश्चेत् प्रतिज्ञा ते विनश्यति। का वाहं तव को मे त्वं कश्च तेमय्यनुग्रहः॥
en: If, again, a handful of barley becomes an object of attachment with you, then your original resolution of leaving off everything becomes futile! If, again, you carry out your resolution of leaving off everything, then who am I to you, who are you to me, and what can be your favour to me?

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: प्रशाधि पृथिवीं राजन् यदि तेऽनुग्रहो भवेत्। प्रासादं शयनं यानं वासांस्याभरणानि च॥
en: If you wish to show your favour, rule then this Earth! They who seeks happiness but are very poor and abandoned by friends may adopt Renunciation.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: श्रिया विहीनैरधनैस्त्यक्तमित्रैरकिंचनैः। सौखिकैः सम्भृतानर्थान् यः संत्यजति किं नु तत्॥
en: But he who imitates those men by leaving off palatial edifices and beds and vehicles and dresses and ornaments, acts improperly, indeed.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: योऽत्यन्तं प्रतिगृह्णीयाद् यश्च दद्यात् सदैव हि। तयोस्त्वमन्तरं विद्धि श्रेयांस्ताभ्यां क उच्यते॥
en: One always accepts gifts from others, while another always makes gifts. You know the difference between the two, Who, indeed, of these two should be considered superior?

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: सदैव याचमानेषु तथा दम्भान्वितेषु च। एतेषु दक्षिणा दत्ता दावाग्नाविव दुर्हतम्॥
en: If a gift is made to one who always accepts gifts, or to one who is proud, that gift, becomes useless like the clarified butter that is poured upon a forest-fire.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: जातवेदा यथा राजन् नादग्ध्वैवोपशाम्यति। सदैव याचमानो हि तथा शाम्यति न द्विजः॥
en: As a fire, o king, never dies till it has consumed all that has been thrown into it, even so a beggar is silenced till he receives something.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: सतां वै ददतोऽन्नं च लोकेऽस्मिन् प्रकृतिर्बुवा। न चेद् राजा भवेद् दाता कुतः स्युर्मोक्षकाक्षिणः।।२७
en: In this world, the food given by a charitable person, is the support of the pious. If, therefore, the king does not give (food), where will the pious go to, who aspire for salvation.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: अन्नाद् गृहस्था लोकेऽस्मिन् भिक्षवस्तत एव च। अन्नात् प्राणः प्रभवति अन्नदः प्राणदो भवेत्॥
en: They that have food (in their houses) are householders. Mendicants are supported by them. Life is kept up by food. Therefore, the giver of food is the giver of life.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: गृहस्थेभ्योऽपि निर्मुक्ता गृहस्थानेव संश्रिताः। प्रभवं च प्रतिष्ठां च दान्ता विन्दन्त आसते॥
en: Coming out from among those who live as householders, mendicants depend upon those very persons from whom they come. By doing this, those self-controlled men acquire and enjoy fame and power.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: त्यागान भिक्षुकं विद्यान्न मौढ्यान्न च याचनात्। ऋजुस्तु योऽर्थं त्यजति नसुखं विद्धि भिक्षुकम्॥
en: One cannot be called a mendicant for his having only renounced his worldly possessions, or for his having only led a life of dependence on charity. He who forsakes sincerely the possessions and pleasures of the world to be regarded a true mendicant.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: असक्तः सक्तवद् गच्छन् निःसङ्गो मुक्तवन्धनः। समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च स वै मुक्तो महीपते॥
en: Unattachment at heart though showing attachment outwardly, standing aloof from the world, having broken all his fetters, regarding friend and foe in the same light, such a man, O king, is regarded to be liberated.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: परिव्रजन्ति दानार्थं मुण्डाः काषायवाससः। सिता बहुविधै पाशैः संचिन्वन्तो वृथामिषम्॥
en: Having shaved their heads clean and put on the brown robe, people rove like mendicants, though fettered by various ties and though always seeking useless wealth.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: त्रयीं च नाम वार्ता च त्यक्त्वा पुत्रान् व्रजन्ति ये। त्रिविष्टब्धं च वासश्च प्रतिगृह्णन्त्यबुद्धयः॥
en: They who, casting off the three Vedas, their usual avocations and children, live like mendicants by taking up the triple-headed rod and the brown robe, are really persons of weak understanding.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: अनिष्कषाये काषायमीहार्थमिति विद्धि तम्। धर्मध्वजानां मुण्डानां वृत्त्यर्थमिति मे मितिः॥
en: Without having cast off anger and other passions, wearing only the brown robe, O king, is due to the desire of earning the means of livelihood. Those persons of clean-shaved heads who hold up the banner of virtue, have the acquisition of sustenance for their only object in life.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: काषायैरजिनैश्चीरैर्नग्नान् मुण्डान् जटाधरान्। बिभ्रत् साधून महाराज जय लोकान् जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Therefore, O king, controlling your passions do you secure blissful regions for yourself hereafter by maintaining them that are truly pious amongst those having matted locks or clean-shaved heads, naked or clad in rags, or skins or brown clothes.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: अग्न्याधेयानि गुर्वर्थं क्रतूनपि सुदक्षिणान्। ददात्यहरहः पूर्वं को नु धर्मरतस्ततः॥
en: Who is there that is more virtuous then he who maintains his sacred fire, who celebrates sacrifices with presents of animals and money, and who administers charity day and night?

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: अर्जुन उवाच तत्त्वज्ञो जनको राजा लोकेऽस्मिन्निति गीयते। सोऽप्यासीन्मोहसम्पन्नो मा मोहवशमन्वगाः॥
en: Arjuna said King Janaka was known as a truth-knowing person in the world. Even he, was bewildered in the ascertainment of duty. Do not yield to stupefaction.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: एवं धर्ममनुक्रान्ताः सदा दानतपःपरा। आनृशंस्यगुणोपेताः कामक्रोधविवर्जिताः॥ प्रजानां पालने युक्ता दानमुत्तममास्थिताः। इष्टॉल्लोकानवाप्स्यामो गुरुवृद्धोपचायिनः॥
en: The duties of a householder are observed by person practising charity. By abstaining from all sorts of injuries, by casting off desire and anger, by being engaged in protecting all creatures, by making charities and lastly by making elders and aged persons, we shall succeed in attaining such blissful regions as are after our hearts.

description: The discourse between king Janaka and his Queen-the latter finding fault with the life of mendicancy.
sn: देवतातिथिभूतानां निर्वपन्तो यथाविधि। स्थानमिष्टमवाप्स्यामो ब्रह्मण्याः सत्यवादिनः॥
en: By duly satisfying gods, guests, and all creatures, by adoring Brahmanas, and by truthfulness of speech, we shall certainly attain to desirable regions of bliss.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच वेदाहं तात शास्त्राणि अपराणि पराणि च। उभयं वेदवचनं कुरु कर्म त्यजेति च॥
en: Yudhishthira said I know both the Vedas and the scriptures that lead to the attainment of Brahma. In the Vedas there are both kinds of precepts, viz., those that preach action and those that preach the renouncement of action,

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: आकुलानि च शास्त्राणि हेतुभिश्चिन्तितानि च। निश्चयश्चैव यो मन्त्रे वेदाहं तं यथाविधि॥
en: The scriptures are conflicting and their conclusions are based upon reasons. The truth of the mantras is duly known to me.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: त्वं तु केवलमस्त्रज्ञो वीरव्रतसमन्वितः। शास्त्रार्थं तत्त्वतो गन्तुं न समर्थः कथंचन॥
en: You are conversant only with weapons and the practices of heroes. You are unable to understand correctly the meaning of the scriptures.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: शास्त्रार्थसूक्ष्मदर्शी यो धर्मनिश्चयकोविदः। तेनाप्येवं न वाच्योऽहं यदि धर्मं प्रपश्यसि॥
en: If you were really acquainted with duty, then you could have understood that words like these ought not to have been addressed to me by one possessing the true knowledge of the scriptures and acquainted with the truths of religion.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: भ्रातृसौहृदमास्थाय यदुक्तं वचनं त्वया। न्याय्यं युक्तं च कौन्तेय प्रीतोऽहं तेन तेऽर्जुन॥
en: What, however, you have said to me out of fraternal affection, has been fit and proper, O son of Kunti. I am, therefore, gratified with thee, O Arjuna.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: युद्धधर्मेषु सर्वेषु क्रियाणां नैपुणेषु च। न त्वया सदृशः कश्चित् त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते॥
en: There is no one equal to you in the three worlds in all duties connected with battle and in skill in various kinds of acts,

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: धर्मं सूक्ष्मतरं वाच्यं तत्र दुष्प्रतरं त्वया। धनंजय न मे बुद्धिमभिशङ्कितुमर्हसि।॥
en: You are, therefore, competent to speak of the niceties of those subjects, that are not understood by others. You should not, however, O Dhananjaya, doubt my intelligence.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: युद्धशास्त्रविदेव त्वं न वृद्धाः सेवितास्त्वया। संक्षिप्तविस्तरविदां न तेषां वेत्सि निश्चयम्॥ तपस्त्यागोऽविधिरिति निश्चयस्त्वेष धीमताम्। परं परं ज्याय एषां येषां नैश्रेयसी मतिः॥
en: You are, a master of the science of battle, but you have never waited upon the aged. You know not the conclusions arrived at by those that have studied the subject briefly and fully. The conclusion of intelligent men who want salvation, is that of ascetic penances, renunciation, and knowledge of Brahma, the second is superior to the first, and the third is superior to the second.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: यस्त्वेतन्मन्यसे पार्थन ज्यायोऽस्ति धनादिति। तत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि यथा नैतत् प्रधानतः॥
en: Your conclusion, that there is nothing superior to wealth, is a mistake. I will convince you of it, so that you may not again regard wealth in that light.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: तप:स्वाध्यायशीला हि दृश्यन्ते धार्मिका जनाः। ऋषयस्तपसा युक्ता येषां लोकाः सनातनाः॥
en: All righteous men are seen to be devoted to ascetic penances and the study of the Vedas, The Rishis also, that have many eternal regions for them, enjoy the merit of penances.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: अजातशत्रवो धीरास्तथान्ये वनवासिनः। अरण्ये बहवश्चैव स्वाध्यायेन दिवं गताः॥
en: Others possessed equanimity of soul, having no enemies, and dwelling in the forest have, through penances and study of the Vedas, proceeded to heaven.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: उत्तरेण तु पन्थानमार्या विषयनिग्रहात्। अबुद्धिजं तमस्त्यक्त्वा लोकांस्त्यागवतां गताः॥
en: By controlling desire for worldly objects and casting off the darkness of sin, pious men proceed northward to the regions reserved for those who practise Renunciation.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: दक्षिणेन तु पन्थानं यं भास्वन्तं प्रचक्षते। एते क्रियावतां लोका ये श्मशानानि जिरे॥
en: The path that lies to the south and leads to regions of light is reserved for men devoted to action. These are acquired by persons subject to birth and death.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: अनिर्देश्चा गतिः सा तु यां प्रपश्यन्ति मोक्षिणः। तस्माद् योगः प्रधानेष्टः स तु दुःखं प्रवेदितुम्॥
en: That end, however, which persons who wishing to have salvation cannot be described. Yoga is the best means for attaining to it. It is not easy to explain it.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: अनुस्मृत्य तु शास्त्राणि कवयः समवस्थिताः। अपीह स्यादपीह स्यात् सारासारदिदृक्षया॥
en: Those that are learned live, meditating on the scriptures for finding out what is unreal. They, however, jump at this and that in the belief that the object of their search exists in this and that.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: वेदवादानतिक्रम्य शास्त्राण्यारण्यकानि च। विपाट्य कदलीस्तम्भं सारं ददृशिरे न ते॥
en: Having studied, however, the Vedas the Aranyakas, and the other scriptures, they miss the real like men failing to find solid timber in an uprooted Banana plant.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: अथैकान्तव्युदासेन शरीरे पाञ्चभौतिके। इच्छाद्वेषसमासक्तमात्मानं प्राहुरिङ्गित्तैः॥
en: There are some who, disbelieving in its oneness, consider the Soul, dwelling in the physical body consisting of the five elements, possessing the attributes of desire and hatred.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: अग्राह्यं चक्षुषा सूक्ष्ममनिर्देश्यं च तद्गिरा। कर्महेतुपुरस्कारं भूतेषु परिवर्तते।१९।।
en: Unseen by the eye, highly subtile, and indescribable by words, it goes on in a round (of rebirths) among the creatures of the Earth, keeping before it that which is the root of action.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: कल्याणगोचरं कृत्वा मनस्तृष्णां निगृह्य च। कर्मसंततिमुत्सृज्य स्थानिरालम्बनः सुखी।॥
en: Having made the Soul gradually come towards itself which is the root of all bliss, having controlled all mental desires, and having cast off all kinds of action, one may become perfectly independent and happy.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: अस्मिन्नेवं सूक्ष्मगम्ये मार्गे सद्भिर्निषेविते। कथमर्थमनाढ्यमर्जुन त्वं प्रशंससि॥
en: When there is such a path that is followed by the righteous and that is attainable by Knowledge, why, O Arjuna, do you speak highly of wealth which is full of all sorts of dangers?

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: पूर्वशास्त्रविदोऽप्येवं जनाः पश्यन्ति भारत। क्रियासु निरता नित्यं दाने यज्ञे च कर्मणि॥
en: Men of olden times who were conversant with the scriptures, O Bharata,-men who were always engaged in gifts and sacrifices and action, held this view, O Bharata.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: भवन्ति सुदुरावर्ता हेतुमन्तोऽपि पण्डिताः। दृढपूर्वे स्मृता मूढा नैतदस्तीतिवादिनः॥
en: There are some fools who, accomplished in the science of logic, deny the existence of the Soul, for the strength of their convictions of a pristine life. It is very difficult to make them accept this truth about final liberation.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: अनृतस्यावमन्तारो वक्तारो जनसंसदि। चरन्ति वसुधां कृत्स्नां वावदूका बहुश्रुताः॥
en: Those wicked men, though highly learned, travel all over the Earth, delivering lectures in assemblies, and deprecating the true doctrine about liberation.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: पार्थ यान्न विजानीमः कस्ताज्ञातुमिहार्हति। एवं प्राज्ञाः श्रुताश्चापि महान्तः शास्त्रवित्तमाः॥
en: O Partha, who else can understand what we do not understand? Similarly they do not succeed in knowing those wise and pious persons who are truly great and who are wellread in the scriptures.

description: Yudhishthira's decisions. He holds that it is a mistake to think that there is nothing superior to wealth.
sn: तपसा महदाप्नोति बुद्ध्या वै विन्दते महत्। त्यागेन सुखम् प्राप्नोति सदा कौन्तेय तत्त्ववित्॥
en: O son of Kunti, men acquainted with truth attain to Brahma by asceticism and intelligence, and great happiness by Renunciation.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अस्मिन् वाक्यान्तरे वक्ता देवस्थानो महातपाः। अभिनीततरं वाक्यमित्युवाच युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said After Yudhishthira had stopped, the great and eloquent ascetic Devasthana, said these words pregnant with reason to the king.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: देवस्थान उवाच यद् वचः फाल्गुनेनोक्तं न ज्यायोऽस्ति धनादिति। अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि तदेकान्तमनाः शृणु॥
en: Devasthana said *Phalguna has told you that there is nothing superior to wealth. I shall speak to you on that subject. Listen to me with rapt attention.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: अजातशत्रो धर्मेण कृत्स्ना ते वसुधा जिता। तां जित्वा च वृथा राजन् न परित्यक्तुनर्हसि॥
en: O you, having no enemy you have righteously conquered the Earth. Having won her, you should not, () king, abandon her without cause.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: चतुष्पदी हि नि:श्रेणी ब्रह्मण्येव प्रतिष्ठिता। तां क्रमेण महाबाहो यथावज्जय पार्थिव॥
en: Four modes of life and laid down in the Vedas. Do you, O king, duly pass through them one after another.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: तस्मात् पार्थ महायज्ञैर्यजस्व बहुदक्षिणैः। स्वाध्याययज्ञा ऋषयो ज्ञानयज्ञास्तथापरे॥
en: At present you should, therefore, celebrate great sacrifices with profuse presents. Amongst the very Rishis, some celebrate the sacrifice represented by Vedic study, and some that represented by knowledge.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: कर्मनिष्ठांश्च बुद्ध्येथास्तपोनिष्ठांश्च पार्थिव। वैखानसानां कौन्तेय वचनं श्रूयते यथा॥ ईहेत धनहेतोर्यस्तस्यानीहा गरीयसी। भूयान् दोषो हि वर्धेत् यस्तं धनमुपाश्रयेत्॥
en: Therefore, O Bharata, you must know that even the very ascetics also are devoted to action. The Vaikhanasas, however, are said to preach that he who does not seek for wealth is superior to him that seeks for it. I think that he who would follow that precept would be visited by many shortcomings.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: कृच्छ्राच्च द्रव्यसंहारं कुर्वन्ति धनकारणात्। धनेन तृषितोऽबुद्ध्या भ्रूणहत्यां न बुद्ध्यते॥
en: Men collect together various articles (for the celebration of sacrifices) according to the Vedic prescription. He who, impelled by his own foolish understanding, gives away wealth to an undeserving person without giving it to the deserving, does not know that he incurs the sin of killing a foetus.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: अनर्हते यद् ददाति न ददाति यदर्हते। अनिर्हापरिज्ञानाद् दानधर्मोऽपि दुष्करः॥
en: The distribution of charities after discriminating the deserving from the undeserving is not easy.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: यज्ञाय सृष्टानि धनानि धात्रा यज्ञोद्दिष्टः पुरुषो रक्षिता च। तस्मात् सर्वं यज्ञ एवोपयोज्यं धनं ततोऽनन्तर एव कामः॥
en: The Supreme Creator created wealth for Sacrifice, and He created man also for taking care of that wealth and for celebrating Sacrifice. For this reason, the entire wealth of a man should be devoted to the celebration of a sacrifice. This would beget pleasure as a matter of course.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: यज्ञैरिन्द्रो विविधै रत्नवर्द्धि र्देवान्सर्वानभ्ययाद् भूरितेजाः। तेनेन्द्रत्वं प्राप्य विभ्राजतेऽसौ तस्माद्यज्ञे सर्वमेवोपयोज्यम्॥
en: By the performance of various sacrifices with profuse gifts of valuables, the highly energetic Indra excelled all the gods. Having thus become their king, he shines in heaven. Therefore, everything should be given to Sacrifices.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: महादेवः सर्वयज्ञे महात्मा हुत्वाऽऽत्मानं देवदेवो बभूव। विश्वाल्लोकान् व्याप्य विष्टभ्य कीर्त्या विराजते द्युतिमान् कृत्तिवासाः॥
en: Clad in deer-skin the great Mahadeva, having poured his own self as a libation in the sacrifice called Sarva, become the first of gods, and excelling all creatures in the universe and reigning Supreme over them thereby, shines in resplendence.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: आविक्षितः पार्थिवोऽसौ मरुत्तो वृद्ध्या शक्रं योऽजयद् देवराजम्। यज्ञे यस्य श्रीः स्वयं संनिविश यस्मिन् भाण्डं काञ्चनं सर्वमासीत्॥
en: King Marutta, the son of a Avikshit by the profusion of his wealth, defeated Shakra ! himself, the king of the gods. In great sacrifice he performed, all the vessels were made of gold, and the Goddess of Prosperity herself came in person.

description: The ascetic Devasthana also advocates the acquisition of wealth.
sn: हरिश्चन्द्रः पार्थिवेन्द्रः श्रुतस्ते यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा पुण्यभाग् वीतशोकः। ऋद्ध्या शक्रं योऽजयन्मानुषः सं स्तस्माद् यज्ञे सर्वमेवोपयोज्यम्॥
en: You have heard that the great king Harishchandra, having celebrated sacrifices, earned great merit and great happiness. Though a man, he nevertheless defeated Shakra by wealth. For this reason everything should be given to Sacrifice.

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। इन्द्रेण समये पृष्टो यदुवाच बृहस्पतिः॥
en: Regarding this subject is cited an old history, viz., the discourse that Brihaspati, asked by Indra, delivered to him.

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: बृहस्पति उवाच संतोषो वै स्वर्गतमः संतोषः परमं सुखम्। तुष्टेन किंचित् परतः सा सम्यक् प्रतितिष्ठति॥
en: Brihaspati said 'Contentment is the highest heaven, and the greatest bliss. There is nothing superior to Contentment. Contentment heads all.

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: यदा संहरते कामान् कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः। तदऽऽत्मज्योतिरचिरात् स्वात्मन्येव प्रसीदति॥
en: When one contracts all his desires like a tortoise drawing in all his limbs, then the native cffulgence of his soul soon manifests itself.

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: न बिभेति यदा चायं यदा चास्मान्न बिभ्यति। कामद्वेषौ च जयति तदाऽऽत्मानं च पश्यति॥
en: When one does not fear any creature, nor any creature is frightened at one, when one contracts onc's desire and hatred, then is one said to see one's soul.

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: यदासौ सर्वभूतानां न दुह्यति न काङ्क्षति। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When one, seeks to injure nobody in deed, word, and thought, and cherishes no desire, he is said to attain to Brahma.

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: एवं कौन्तेय भूतानि तं तं धर्मं तथा तथा। तदाऽऽत्मना प्रपश्यन्ति तस्माद् बुद्ध्यस्व भारत॥
en: Thus, O son of Kunti, creatures reap fruits according to the religion they follow-Awaken yourself by this thought, O Bharata.

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: अन्ये साम प्रशंसन्ति व्यायामभपरे जनाः। नैकं न चापरं केचिदुभयं च तथापरे॥ यज्ञमेव प्रशंसन्ति संन्यासमपरे जनाः। दानमेके प्रशंसन्ति केचिच्चैव प्रतिग्रहम्॥
en: Some laud Peacefulness; some laud Activity; some laud Contemplation; some speak high of both Peacefulness and Activity. Some speak high of Sacrifice; others, Renunciation. some speak high of Gifts, others, Acceptance.

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: केचित् सर्वं परित्यज्य तूष्णीं ध्यायन्त आसते। राज्यमेके प्रशंसन्ति प्रजानां परिपालनम्॥ हत्वा छित्त्वा च भित्त्वा च केचिदेकान्तशीलिनः। एतत् सर्वं समालोक्य बुधानामेष निश्चयः॥ अद्रोहेणैव भूतानां यो धर्मः स सतां मतः। अद्रोहः सत्यवचनं संविभागो दया दमः॥ प्रजनं स्वेषु दारेषु मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्। एवं धर्मं प्रधानेष्टं मनः स्वाम्यभुवोऽब्रवीत्॥ तस्मादेतत् प्रयत्नेन कौन्तेय प्रतिपालय।
en: Some leaving off every thing, live in silent meditation. Some speak of sovereignty and the caring after subjects, after killing, cutting, and piercing (foes). Some prefer spending their days in retirement. Observing all this, the learned hold that religion which consists is not injuring any creature is the one approved of by the righteous. The practice of abstention from injury, truthfulness of speech, justice, compassion, self-control, procreation (of offspring) upon one's own wives, amiability, modesty, patience, is the best of all religious as said by the self-born Manu himself. Therefore, O son of Kunti, do you practise this religion!

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: यो हि राज्ये स्थितः शश्वद् वशी तुल्यप्रियाप्रियः॥ क्षत्रियो यज्ञशिष्टाशी राजा शास्त्रार्थतत्त्ववित्। असाधुनिग्रहरतः साधूनां प्रग्रहे रतः॥ धर्मवर्त्मनि संस्थाप्य प्रजा वर्तेत धर्मतः। पुत्रसंक्रामितश्रीश्च वने वन्येन वर्तयन्॥ विधिना श्रावणेनैव कुर्यात् कर्माण्यतन्द्रितः। य एवं वर्तते राजन् स राजा धर्मनिश्चितः॥ तस्यायं च परश्चैव लोकः स्यात् सफलोदयः। निर्वाणं हि सुदुष्प्राप्यं बहुविघ्नं च मे मतम्॥
en: That Kshatriya, who, knowing. well the royal duties, take sovereignty upon himself, controlling his soul at all times, regarding that which is dear and that which is not in the same light and living upon the residue of sacrificial feats, who is engaged in restraining the wicked and cherishing the righteous, who compels his subjects to follow the path of virtue and who himself follows that path, who at last hands over his crown to his son and retires into the forest, there to live on the products of the forest and act according to the ordinances of the Vedas after having thrown off all idleness, that Kshatriya who acts thus, following the well-known duties of kings,-is sure to reap excellent fruits in both this world and the next. The final emancipation, you speak of, is lightly difficult to obtain, and its pursuit is attended with many obstacles.

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: एवं धर्ममनुक्रान्ताः सत्यदानतपःपराः। आनृशंस्यगुणैर्युक्ताः कामक्रोधविवर्जिताः॥ प्रजानां पालने युक्ता धर्ममुत्तममास्थिताः। गोब्राह्मणार्थे युध्यन्त प्राप्ता गतिमनुत्तमाम्॥
en: They who follow such duties and practise charity and ascetic penances, penances, who are compassionate and are freed from desire and anger, who are engaged in ruling their subjects with righteousness and fighting for the sake of kine and Brahmanas, attain hereafter to a high end.

description: The discourse between Indra and Brihaspati-The ideal of true religion.
sn: एवं रुद्राः सवसवस्तथाऽऽदित्याः परंतप। साध्या राजर्षिसंघाश्च धर्ममेतं समाश्रिताः। अप्रमत्तास्ततः स्वर्गं प्राप्ताः पुण्यैः स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: For this the Rudras, with the Vasus and the Adityas, O destroyer of foes, and the Sadhyas and innumerable other kings adopt this religion. practising carefully the duties laid down by that religion, they attain to heaven through those acts of theirs.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अस्मिन्नेवान्तरे वाक्ये पुनरेवार्जुनोऽब्रवीत्। निविण्णमनसं ज्येष्ठमिदं भ्रातरमच्युतम्॥
en: After this, Arjuna again said to his eldest brother of unfading glory, king Yudhishthira of cheerless heart :

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: क्षत्रधर्मेण धर्मज्ञ प्राप्य राज्यं सुदुर्लभम्। जित्वा चारीन् नरश्रेष्ठ तप्यते किं भृशं भवान्॥
en: 'O you who are conversant with every kind of duty, having by the practise of Kshatriya duties acquired sovereignty that is so very difficult of acquisition, and having defeated all your foes, why do you grieve.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: क्षत्रियाणां महाराज संग्रामे निधनं मतम्। विशिष्टं बहुभिर्यज्ञैः क्षत्रधर्ममंनुस्मर॥
en: O king, as regards Kshatriyas, death in battle is regarded more meritorious for them than the celebration of various sacrifices. it is so laid down in the ordinance that describes the duties of Kshatriyas.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: ब्राह्मणानां तपस्त्यागः प्रेत्य धर्मविधिः स्मृतः। क्षत्रियाणां च निधनं संग्रामे विहितं प्रभो॥
en: Penances and Renunciation constitute the duties of Brahmanas. Such is also the ordinance about the next world, Indeed, O powerful one, death in battle is laid down for Kshatriyas.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: क्षात्रधर्मो महारौद्रःशस्त्रनित्य इति स्मृतः। वधश्च भरतश्रेष्ठ काले शस्त्रेण संयुगे॥
en: The duties of Kshatriyas are highly dreadful and are always connected with the use of weapons, and it has been ordained, O chief of the Bharatas, that they should, when the time comes, die by weapons on the field of battle.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: ब्राह्मणस्यापि चेद् राजन् क्षत्रधर्मेण वर्ततः। प्रशस्तं जीवितं लोके क्षत्रं हि ब्रह्मसम्भवम्॥
en: The life of even a Brahmana, O king, who follows the observances of a Kshatriya, is not blameable, for Kshatriyas also have originated from Brahman.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: न त्यागो न पुनर्यज्ञो न तपो मनुजेश्वर। क्षत्रियस्य विधीयन्ते न परस्वोपजीवनम्॥
en: Neither Renunciation, nor Sacrifice, nor Penances, nor dependence on the wealth of others, O king, has been laid down for Kshatriyas.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: स भवान् सर्वधर्मज्ञो धर्मात्मा भरतर्षभ। राजा मनीषी निपुणो लोके दृष्टपरावरः॥ त्यक्त्वा संतापजं शोकं दंशितो भव कर्मणि। क्षत्रियस्य विशेषेण हृदयं वज्रसंनिभम्॥
en: You know full well all duties, and you are of righteous soul, O foremost of Bharata's race. You are a wise king, of skilful deeds, You can discriminate what is right in this world from what is wrong. Shaking off this cheerlessness begotten by repentance engage in action vigorously. The heart of a Kshatriya is hard as adamant.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: जित्वारीन् क्षत्रधर्मेण प्राप्य राज्यमकण्टकम्। विजितात्मा मनुष्येन्द्र यज्ञदानपरो भव॥
en: Having by the performance of Kshatriya duties defeated your foes and acquired empire without a throne in its side, control your soul, O king, and be engaged in the performance of sacrifices and the practice of charity.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: इन्द्रो वै ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः क्षत्रियः कर्मणाभवत्। ज्ञातीनां पापवृत्तीनां जघान नवतीनव॥
en: Indra himself, though a Brahmana, become a Kshatriya in his deeds, and fought with his sinful kinsmen for eight hundred and ten times.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: तच्चास्य कर्म पूज्यं च प्रशस्यं च विशाम्पते। तेनेन्द्रत्वं समापेदे देवानामिति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: Those acts of his, o king, deserve every commendation. Through them, as we have heard, he became the king of the gods.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: स त्वं यज्ञैर्महाराज यजस्व बहुदक्षिणैः। यथैवेन्द्रो मनुष्येन्द्र चिराय विगतज्वरः॥
en: Do you, therefore, O monarch, celebrate sacrifices with profuse presents even as Indra did, Cking, and thereby free yourself from your fever.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: मम त्वमेवं गते किंचिच्छोचेथाः क्षत्रियर्षभ। गतास्ते क्षत्रधर्मेण शस्त्रपूताः परां गतिम्॥
en: Do not, O foremost of Kshatriyas grieve th... for what is gone. They that have been killed have attained to the highest end, purified by weapons and agreeably to the ordinances of the Kshatriyas religion.

description: The duties of a Kshatriya described by Arjuna.
sn: भवितव्यं तथा तच्च यद् वृत्तं भरतर्षभ। दिष्टं हि राजशार्दूल न शक्यमतिवर्तितुम्॥
en: That which has taken place was ordained to take place. Destiny, O foremost of kings, is incapable of being resisted.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु कौन्तेयो गुडाकेशेन पाण्डवः। नोवाच किंचित् कौरव्यस्ततो द्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by Arjuna of curly hair, the Kuru king, son of Kunti, remained silent. Then Dvaipayana (Vyasa) said.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: व्यास उवाच बीभत्सोर्वचनं सौम्य सत्यमेतद् युधिष्ठिर। शास्त्रदृष्टः परो धर्मः स्थितो गार्हस्थ्यमाश्रितः॥
en: Vyasa said The words of Arjuna, O amiable Yudhishthira, are true. The highest religion as sanctioned by the scriptures, consists in the duties of a householder.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: स्वधर्मं चर धर्मज्ञ यथाशास्त्रं यथाविधि। न हि गार्हस्थयमुत्सृज्य तवारण्यं विधीयते॥
en: You are acquainted with all duties. Do you then duly practise the duties prescribed for you (viz., the duties of a householder.) A life of retirement in the forest forgetting the duties of a householder, has not been laid down for you.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: गृहस्थं हि सदा देवाः पितरोऽतिथयस्तथा। भृत्याश्चैवोपजीवन्ति तान् भरस्व महीपते॥
en: The gods, Pitris, guests, and servants all depend (for their maintenance) upon householder. Do you then support all these, O king.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: वयांसि पशवश्चैव भूतानि च जनाधिप। गृहस्थैरेव धार्यन्ते तस्माच्छेरूष्ठो गृहाश्रमी॥
en: Birds and animals and various other creatures, O king, supported by a are householders. He, therefore, who belongs to that mode of life, is superior to all.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: सोऽयं चतुर्णामेतेषामाश्रमाणां दुराचरः। तं चराद्य विधि पार्थ दुश्चरं दुर्बलेन्द्रियैः
en: The life of a householder is the inost difficult of all the four modes of life. Do you practise that mode of life then, O Partha, which is difficult of being practised by persons of uncontrolled senses.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: वेदज्ञानं च ते कृत्स्नं तपश्चाचरितं महत्। पितृपैतामहं राज्यं धुर्यवद् वोढुमर्हसि॥
en: You have mastered all the Vedas. You have earned great ascetic merit. You should, therefore, bear like an ox the burden of your ancestral kingdom.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: तपो यज्ञस्तथा विद्या भक्ष्यमिन्द्रियसंयमः। ध्यानमेकान्तशीलत्वं तुर्ज्ञािनं च शक्तितः॥ ब्राह्मणानां महाराज चेष्टा संसिद्धिकारिका।
en: Penances, sacrifices, forgiveness, learning, mendicancy, restraint of senses, contemplation, living in solitude, contentment, and knowledge (of Brahma), should, O king, be practised by Brahmanas to the best of their ability for the attainment of success.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: क्षत्रियाणां तु वक्ष्यामि तवापि विदितं पुनः॥ यज्ञो विद्या समुत्थानमसंतोषः श्रियं प्रति। दण्डधारणमुग्रत्वं प्रजानां परिपालनम्॥ वेदज्ञानं तथा कृत्स्नं तपः सुचरितं तथा। द्रविणोपार्जनं भूरि पात्रे च प्रतिपादनम्॥ एतानि राज्ञां कर्माणि सुकृतानि विशाम्पते। इमं लोकममुं चैव साधयन्तीति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: I shall now tell you the duties of Kshatriyas. They are not unknown to you. Sacrifice, learning, activity, ambition, holding, the rod of chastisement, dreadfulness, protection of subjects, knowledge of the Vedas, practise of all kinds of penances, enances, good conduct, acquisition of wealth, and gifts to deserving person, these, o king, when performed properly by the Kshatriyas, secure for them both this world and the next, as heard by us.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: एषां ज्यायस्तु कौन्तेय दण्डधारणमुच्यते। बलं हि क्षत्रिये नित्यं बले दण्डः समाहितः॥
en: Of them, O son of Kunti, wielding the rod of chastisement has been declared to be the foremost. A Kshatriya must always have strength, and upon strength depends chastisement.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: एता विद्याः क्षत्रियाणां राजन् संसिद्धिकारिकाः। अपि गाथामिमां चापि बृहस्पतिरगायत॥
en: Those I have mentioned are, O king, the principle duties for Kshatriyas and lead greatly to their success. Brihaspati, in this matter, sang this verse :
