description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: भूमिरेतौ निगिरति सर्पो बिलशयानिव। राजानं चाविरोद्धारं ब्राह्मणं चाप्रवासिनम्।१५।।
en: Like a snake devouring a mouse, the Earth devours a king who is inclined to peace and a Brahmana who is greatly addicted to a life of domesticity!

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: सुद्युम्नश्चापि राजर्षिः श्रूयते दण्डधारणात्। प्राप्तवान् परमां सिद्धिं दक्षः प्राचेतसो यथा॥
en: It is heard again that the royal sage Sudyumna, only by wielding the rod of chastisement, gained the highest success, like Daksha himself, the son of Prachetas.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भगवन् कर्मणा केन सुद्युम्नो वसुधाधिपः। संसिद्धिं परमां प्राप्तः श्रोतुमिच्छामि तं नृपम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O holy sage, by what acts did king Sudyumna gain the highest success? (I wish to hear the king.)

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: व्यास उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। शङ्खच लिखितश्चास्तां भ्रातरौ संशितव्रतौ॥
en: Vyasa said 'In this matter is also cited this old history. There were two brothers, viz., Shankha and Likhita of rigid vows.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: तयोरावसथावास्तां रमणीयौ पृथक् पृथक्। नित्यपुष्पफलैर्वृक्षरुपेतौ बाहुदामनु॥
en: The two brothers had two separate beautiful houses. Situate by the bank of the river called Vahuda, both of those houses were decorated with trees always bearing flowers and fruits.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: ततः कदाचिल्लिखितः शङ्खस्याश्रममागतः। यदृच्छयाथशङ्खोऽपि निष्क्रान्तोऽभवदाश्रमात्॥
en: Once on a time Likhita come to the house of his brother Shankha. At that time, however, Shankha had left his asylum with no fixed purpose.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: सोऽभिगम्याश्रमं भ्रातुः शङ्खस्य लिखितस्तदा। फलानि पातयामास सम्यक्परिणतान्युत॥
en: Arrived at the asylum of his brother, Shankha, Likhita plucked many ripe fruits.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: तान्युपादाय विस्रब्यो भक्षयामास स द्विजः। तस्मिंश्च भक्षयत्येव शङ्खोऽप्याश्रममागतः॥
en: Getting them the Rishi Likhita began to eat them without feeling any pinch of conscience. While thus eating Shankha returned to his hermitage.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: भक्षयन्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा शङ्खो भ्रातरमब्रवीत्। कुतः फलान्यवाप्तानि हेतुना केन खादसि॥
en: Seeing him eating, Shankha addressed his brother, saying,-Whence have these fruits been got and for why are you eating them?

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: सोऽब्रवीद् भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठमुपसृत्याभिवाद्य च। इत एव गृहीतानि मयेति प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Approaching his elder brother and saluting him, Likhita smilingly replied, saying,—I have taken them even from this hermitage.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: तमब्रवीत् तथा शङ्खस्तीव्ररोषसमन्वितः। स्तेयं त्वया कृतमिदं फलान्याददता स्वयम्॥
en: Filled with great anger, Shankha said to him,—You have committed theft by taking yourself these fruits.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: गच्छ राजानमासाद्य स्वकर्म कथयस्व वै। अदत्तादानमेवं हि कृतं पार्थिवसत्तम॥
en: Go to the king confess what you have done. Tell him,-O best of kings, I have committed the offence of taking what was not given to me.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: स्तेनं मां त्वं विदित्वा च स्वधर्ममनुपालय। शीघ्रं धारय चौरस्य मम दण्डं नराधिप॥
en: Knowing me for a thief and following your duty of order, do you punish me O king, like a thief.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: इत्युक्तस्तस्य वचनात् सुद्युम्नं स नराधिपम्। अभ्यगच्छन्महाबाहो लिखितः संशितव्रतः॥
en: Thus commanded by his brother, the highly blessed Likhita of rigid vows proceeded to king Sudyumna.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: सुद्युम्नस्त्वन्तपालेभ्यः : श्रुत्वा लिखितमागतम्। अभ्यगच्छत् सहामात्यः पद्भ्यामेव जनेश्वरः॥
en: Hearing from his gate-keepers that Likhita had come, king Sudyumna, with his counsellors, went out (for receiving him.)

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: तमब्रवीत् समागम्य स राजा धर्मवित्तमम्। किमागमनमाचक्ष्व भगवन् कृतमेव तत्॥ एवमुक्तः स विप्रर्षिः सुद्युम्नमिदमब्रवीत्। प्रतिश्रुत्य करिष्येति श्रुत्वा तत् कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Meeting with him, the king addressed that best of all persons conversant with duties, saying,-Tell me, O reverend sir, why you have Know it is already accomplished.-Thus accosted, that Rishi said to Sudyumna,-Do you promise first that you will do it. You should then, after hearing me, fulfil that promise.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: सुद्युम्न उवाच अनिसृष्टानि गुरुणा फलानि मनुजर्षभ। भक्षितानि महाराज तत्र मां शाधि मा चिरम्॥ प्रमाणं चेन्मतो राजा भवतो दण्डधारणे। अनुज्ञायामपि तथा हेतुः स्याद् ब्राह्मणर्षभ।॥
en: O foremost of men, I ate some fruits that had not given me by my elder brother. Do you, o king, punish me for it forthwith, Sudyumna answered,-If the king be considered to wield the rod of chastisement, he come. should be regarded, O foremost of Brahmanas, as equally competent to pardon.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: स भवानभ्यनुज्ञातः शुचिकर्मा महाव्रतः। ब्रूहि कामानतोऽन्यांस्त्वं करिष्यामि हि ते वचः॥
en: Purged in sin, you of high vows, consider yourself as pardoned. Tell me now what else do you wish. I shall certainly accomplish those your commands.'

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: व्यास उवाच संछन्द्यमानो ब्रह्मषिः पार्थिवेन महात्मना। नान्यं स वरयामास तस्माद् दण्डादृते वरम्॥
en: “Thus honoured by the great king, the Rishi Likhita, however, did not ask for any other favour.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: ततः स पृथिवीपालो लिखितस्य महात्मनः। करौ प्रच्छेदयामास धृतदण्डो जगाम सः॥
en: Then that king caused the two hands of the high-souled Likhita to be cut off, whereupon the latter, bearing the punishment, went away.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: स गत्वा भ्रातरं शङ्खमार्तरूपोऽब्रवीदिदम्। धृतदण्डस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्भवांस्तत् क्षन्तुमर्हति॥
en: Returning to his brother Shankha, Likhita, in great agony said,-'You should now pardon this wretched man who has been duly punished (for what he did)'.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: शङ्ख उवाच न कुप्ये तव धर्मज्ञ न त्वं दूषयसे ममा सुनिर्मलं कुलं ब्रह्मन्नस्मिञ्जगति विश्रुतम्। धर्मस्तु ते व्यतक्रान्तस्ततस्ते निष्कृतिः कृताः॥
en: Shankha said "I am not angry with you nor have you injured me, O foremost of all persons conversant with duties. Your virtue, however, had deteriorated. I have saved you from that plight.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: त्वं गत्वा बाहुदां शीघ्रं तर्पयस्व यथाविधि। देवानृषीन् पिढेश्चैवं मा चाधर्मे मनः कृथाः॥
en: Proceed forthwith to the river Vahuda and please duly, with oblations of water, the gods, Rishis, and the Pitris, and never again think of sin.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा शङ्खस्य लिखितस्तदा। अवगाह्यापगां पुण्यामुदकार्थं प्रचक्रमे॥
en: Hearing these words of Shankha, Likhita performed his ablutions in the sacred river and began to perform the water-rite.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: प्रादुरास्तां ततस्तस्य करौ जलजसंनिभौ। ततः स विस्मितो भ्रातुर्दर्शयामास तौ करौ॥
en: Thereat, two hands, like two lotuses, appeared at the extremities of his stumps. Stricken with wonder he returned to his brother and showed him the two hands.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: शङ्ख उवाच ततस्तमब्रवीच्छङ्खस्तपसेदं कृतं मया। मा च तेऽत्र विशङ्काभूद् दैवमत्र विधीयते॥
en: Shankha said All this has been done by me through my penances! Do not be surprised at it. Providence is the instrument here.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: लिखित उवाच किं तु नाहं त्वया पूतः पूर्वमेव महाद्युते। यस्य ते तपसो वीर्यमीदृशं द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Likhita answered: O you of great splendour, why did you not purify me at first, when, O best of Rishis, such was the power of your penances?

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: शङ्ख उवाच एवमेतन्मया कार्यं नाहं दण्डधरस्तव। स च पूतो नरपतिस्त्वं चापि पितृभिः सह॥
en: Shankha said I should not have acted otherwise. I am not your punisher. The king has been himself purified as also yourself, along with the Pitris.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: व्यास उवाच स राजा पाण्डवश्रेष्ठ श्रेयान् वै तेन कर्मणा। प्राप्तवान् परमां सिद्धिं दक्षः प्राचेतसो यथा॥
en: Vyasa said That king, O eldest son of Pandu, became great by this act and obtained the greatest success like the lord Daksha himself.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: एष धर्मः क्षत्रियाणां प्रजानां परिपालनम्। उत्पथोऽन्यो महाराज मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः॥
en: Such is the duty of Kshatriyas, viz., the ruling of subjects. Any other, O king, would be considered as a wrong path for them. Do not grieve.

description: Vyasa also urges upon Yudhishthira to live like a house-holder. The histoy of the king Sudyumna.
sn: भ्रातुरस्य हितं वाक्यं शृणु धर्मज्ञ सत्तम। दण्ड एव हि राजेन्द्र क्षत्रधर्मो न मुण्डनम्॥
en: O best of all persons conversant with duty, listen to the wholesome words of this your brother. Holding the rod of chastisement, O king, is the duty of kings and not the shaving of the head. more

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पुनरेव महर्षिस्तं कृष्णद्वैपायनो मुनिः। अजातशत्रु कौन्तेयमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Once the great sage KrishnaDvaipayana said these words to the son of Kunti, who had no enemies.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: अरण्ये वसतां तात भ्रातृणां ते मनस्विनाम्। मनोरथा महाराज ये तत्रासन् युधिष्ठिर॥ तानिमे भरतश्रेष्ठ प्राप्नुवन्तु महारथाः। प्रशाधि पृथिवीं पार्थ ययातिरिव नाहुषः॥
en: Let these great car-warriors, possessing sufficient mental strength, O king, let these your brothers, O Yudhishthira the chief of the Bharatas, satisfying those wishes of theirs which they entertained while living in the woods. Rule you the Earth, O son of Pritha, like (another) Yayati the son of Nahusha.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: अरण्ये दुःखवसतिरनुभूता तपस्विभिः। दुःखस्यान्ते नरव्याघ्र सुखान्यनुभवन्तु वै॥
en: Before this you suffered misery while living in the woods in the observance of ascetic penances. That misery has ended, O foremost of men. Enjoy happiness, therefore, for some time.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: धर्ममर्थं च कामं च भ्रातृभिः सह भारत। अनुभूय ततः पश्चात् प्रस्थातासि विशाम्पते॥
en: Having, O Bharata, acquired and enjoyed religious merit and wealth and pleasure for some time with your brothers, you may then, O king, retire into the forest.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: अर्थनां च पितृणां च देवतानां च भारत। आनृण्यं गच्छ कौन्तेय तत् सर्वं च करिष्यसि॥
en: Be freed first, О Bharata, from the debt you owe to persons who may beg of you to the Pitris, and to the gods. You may then, O son of Kunti, follow all the other modes of life.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: सर्वमेधाश्वमेधाभ्यां यजस्व कुरुनन्दन। ततः पश्चान्महाराज गमिष्यसि परां गतिम्॥
en: Do you, O son of Kuru's race, celebrate the sacrifices of Sarvamedha and Ashvainedha. You will then attain, O king, to the highest end hereafter.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: भ्रातृ॑श्च सर्वान् ऋतुभिः संयोज्य बहुदक्षिणैः। सम्प्राप्तः कीतिमतुलां पाण्डवेय भविष्यसि॥
en: Making your brothers also perform great sacrifices with profuse presents, you will, O son of Pandu, acquire great fame.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: विद्यस्ते पुरुषव्याघ्र वचनं कुरुसत्तम। शृणुष्वैवं यथा कुर्वन् न धर्माच्च्यवसे नृप॥
en: There is a saying, O foremost of men and best of the Kurus! Listen to it, for by acting according to it, O king, you will not deviate from the path of virtue.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: आददानस्य विजयं विग्रहं च युधिष्ठिर। समानधर्मकुशलाः स्थापयन्ति नरेश्वर॥
en: Those men only O Yudhishthira, who behave like robbers, advise a king to undertake wars and acquire victory.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: देशकालप्रतीक्षी यो दस्यून् मर्षयते नृपः। शास्त्रजां बुद्धिमास्थाय युज्यत्ते नैनसा हि सः॥
en: That king who, knowing proper place and time and following the injunctions of the scriptures, pardons even a nuinber of robbers, incurs no sin.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: आदाय बलिषड्भागं यो राष्ट्र नाभिरक्षति। प्रतिगृह्णाति तत् पापं चतुथाङ्खशेन भूमिपः॥
en: That king, who, realising his tribute of a sixth, does not protect his kingdom, shares a fourth part of the sins of his kingdom.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: निबोध च यथाऽऽतिष्ठन् धर्मान्न च्यवते नृपः। निग्रहाद् धर्मशास्त्राणामनुरुद्ध्यन्नपेतभीः॥
en: Listen also to that by which a king may not deviate from the path of virtue. By disregarding the scriptures one incurs sin, while by obeying them one may live fearlessly.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: कामक्रोधावनादृत्य पितेव समदर्शनः। शास्त्रजां बुद्धिमास्थाय युज्यते नैनसा हि सः॥
en: That king who, following the scriptural injunctions and disregarding lust and anger, behaves impartially, like a father, towards all his subjects, never incurs sin.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: दैवेनाभ्याहतो राजा कर्मकाले महाद्युते। न साधयति यत् कर्म न तत्राहुरतिक्रमम्॥
en: O you of great splendour, if a king, possessed by destiny, fails to accomplish an act in proper time, such failure would not be called a trespass.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: तरसा बुद्धिपूर्वं वा निग्राह्या एव शत्रवः। पापैः सह न संदध्याद् राज्यं पण्यं न कारयेत्॥
en: By power and policy should the king subjugate his foes. He must not allow sin to be committed in his kingdom, but should cause virtue to be practised.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: शूराश्चार्याश्च सत्कार्या विद्वांसश्च युधिष्ठिर। गोमिनो धनिनश्चैव परिपाल्या विशेषतः॥
en: Brave men, the respectable, the virtuous, the learned, O Yudhishthira, Brahmanas conversant with Vedic texts and rites, and men of wcalth, should especially be protected.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: व्यवहारेषु धर्मेषु योक्तव्याश्च बहुश्रुताः। गुणयुक्तेऽपि नैकस्मिन् विश्वसेत विचक्षणः॥
en: In trying cases and performing religious acts, they who are possessed of great learning should alone be employed. A prudent king should never place his confidence in one individual however accomplished.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: अरक्षिता दुविनीतो मानी स्तब्धोऽभ्यसूयकः। एनसा युज्यते राजा दुर्दान्त इति चोच्यते॥
en: That king who does not protect his subjects, whose passions are not under-control, who is full of vanity, who is haughty and malicious, incurs sin and becomes notorious as a tyrant.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: येऽरक्ष्यमाणा हीयन्ते दैवेनाभ्याहता नृप। तस्करैश्चापि हीयन्ते सर्वं तद् राजकिल्बिषम्॥
en: If the subjects of a king, O monarch, die from want of protection and are afflicted by the gods and oppressed by robbers, the sin of all this affects the king himself.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: सुमन्त्रिते सुनीते च सर्वतश्चोपपादिते। पौरुषे कर्मणि कृते नास्त्यधर्मो युधिष्ठिर॥
en: There is no sin, O Yudhishthira, in doing an act with full heart, after mature consideration and consultation with men capable of giving good advice.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: विच्छिद्यन्ते समारब्धाः सिद्ध्यन्ते चापि दैवतः। कृते पुरुषकारे तु नैनः स्पृशति पार्थिवम्॥
en: Our works fail or succeed through destiny. If activity, however, be applied, sin would not affect the king.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: अत्र ते राजशार्दूल वर्तयिष्ये कथामिमाम्। यद् वृत्तं पूर्वराजर्षेर्हयग्रीवस्य पाण्डव॥ शत्रू न हत्वा हतस्याजौ शूरस्याक्लिश्कर्मणः। असहायस्य संग्रामे निर्जितस्य युधिष्ठिर॥
en: I shall recite to you, O foremost of kings, the story of what happened to an ancient king of the name of Hayagriva, O son of Pandu,the story of the heroic Hayagriva of unsullied deeds, who after having killed a host of enemies in battle, was himself defeated and killed while without a follower by his side.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: यत् कर्म वै निग्रहे शात्रवाणां योगश्चाम्यः पालने मानवानाम्। कृत्वा कर्म प्राप्य कीर्तिं स युद्धाद् वाजिग्रीवो मोदते स्वर्गलोके॥
en: Having done all for restraining his foes and adopted all those foremost of means by which men may be protected, Hayagriva won great fame from the battles he fought and is now enjoying great bliss in heaven.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: संयुक्तात्मा समरेष्वाततायी शस्त्रैश्छिन्नो दस्युभिर्वध्यमानः। अश्वग्रीवः कर्मशीलो महात्मा संसिद्धार्थो मोदते स्वर्गलोके॥
en: Wounded by robbers with weapons, bravely fighting with them, and giving up his life in battle, the great Hayagriva, ever devoted to his royal duties, achieved the object of his life and is now enjoying great bliss in heaven.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: धनुषूपो रशना ज्या शरः सुक् नुवः खङ्गो रुधिरं यत्र चाज्यम्। रथो वेदी कामगो श्चातुर्होत्रं चतुरो वाजिमुख्याः॥
en: The bow was his (sacrificial) stake and the bow-string was the cord for trying the animals. Arrows were the smaller ladle and the sword the larger one, and blood formed the clarified butter that he poured. The car constituted the altar and the anger he left in battle was the fire, and the four best of horses yoked to his vehicle were the four Hotris.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: हुत्वा तस्मिन् यज्ञवह्नावथारीन् पापान्मुक्तो राजसिंहस्तरस्वी। प्राणान् हुत्वा चावभृथे रणे स। वाजिग्रीवो मोदते देवलोके॥
en: Having poured upon that sacrificial fire his enemies as libations and then his own life at the termination of the sacrifice, that foremost of kings, Hayagriva, became freed from sin and is now playing in the regions of the celestials.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: राष्ट्र रक्षन् बुद्धिपूर्वं नयेन संत्यक्तात्मा यज्ञशीलो महात्मा। सर्वांल्लोकान् व्याप्य कीर्त्या मनस्वी वाजिग्रीवो मोदते देवलोके॥
en: Having protected his kingdom with policy and intelligence, the great and self-controlled Hayagriva of great strength of mind and given to the performance of sacrifices filled all the worlds with his glory and is now sporting in the region of the celestials.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: दैवीं सिद्धिं मानुषीं दण्डनीति योगन्यासैः पालयित्वा महीं च। तस्माद् राजा धर्मशीलो महात्मा वाजिग्रीवो मोदते देवलोके।॥
en: Having acquired the merit of celebrating sacrifices as also every kind of merit of human worlds, he held the rod of chastisement and ruled the Earth with vigour and without pride. For this the virtuous and great Hayagriva is sporting in the region of the celestials.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: विद्वांस्त्यागी श्रद्दधानः कृतर्ज स्त्यक्त्वा लोकं मानुषं कर्म कृत्वा। मेधाविनां विदुषां सम्मतानां तनुत्यजां लोकमाक्रम्य राजा॥
en: Learned men practising renunciation, cherishing faith, and grateful, that king, having performed various acts, left this world of men and attained the regions that are reserved for the intelligent and the wise and those who are of approved conduct and behaviour and prepared to kill themselves in battle.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: सम्यग् वेदान् प्राप्य शास्त्राण्यधीत्य सम्यग् राज्यं पालयित्वा महात्मा। चातुर्वर्ण्य स्थापयित्वा स्वधर्म वाजिग्रीवो मोदते देवलोके॥ जित्वा संग्रामान् पालयित्वा प्रजाश्च सोमं पीत्वा तर्पयित्वा द्विजाम्यान्। युक्त्या दण्डं धारयित्वा प्रजानां युद्धे क्षीणो मोदते देवलोके।॥
en: Having read the Vedas well and the other scriptures also, having governed his kingdom properly and made all the four orders follow their respective duties, the Hayagriva is sporting merrily in the regions of the celestials. Having gained many battles and cherished his subjects, having drunk the Soma juice in sacrifices and satisfied the foremost of Brahmanas with presents and judiciously held the rod of chastisement over those placed under his sway and at last sacrificed his life in battle, that king is living happily in heaven.

description: Vyasa points out the duties of a king. The history of the king Hayagriva.
sn: वृत्तं यस्य श्लाघनीयं मनुष्याः सन्तो विद्वांसोऽर्हयन्त्यर्हणीयम्। स्वर्गं जित्वा वीरलोकानवाप्य सिद्धिं प्राप्तः पुण्यकीर्तिर्महात्मा॥
en: His life was worthy of every complement. Learned and honest, men speak high of it, for it deserves every praise. Having acquired heaven and won the regions reserved for heroes, that great king of virtuous deeds became drowned with success.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच द्वैपायनवचः श्रुत्वा कुपिते च धनंजये। व्यासमामन्त्र्य कौन्तेयः प्रत्युवाच युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Hearing the words of Dvaipayana Vyasa and seeing Dhananjaya angry, Yudhishthira the son of Kunti saluted Vyasa and said.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच न पार्थिवमिदं राज्यं न भोगाश्च पृथग्विधाः। प्रीणयन्ति मनो मेऽद्य शोको मां रुन्धयत्ययम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said This earthly sovereignty and the various objects of enjoyments cannot give me any joy. On the other hand, this painful grief is cutting me to the quick.

sn: श्रुत्वा वीरविहीनानामपुत्राणां च योषिताम्। परिदेवपमानानां शान्तिं नोपलभे मुने।॥
en: Hearing the lamentations of these women who have lost their heroic husbands and children, I cannot enjoy peace, O sage.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचेदं व्यासो योगविदां वरः। युधिष्ठिरं महाप्राज्ञो धर्मज्ञो वेदपारगः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed, the virtuous Vyasa, the best of all persons conversant with Yoga, endued with great wisdom and a master of the Vedas, said to Yudhishthira.

sn: व्यास उवाच न कर्मणा लभ्यते चिन्तया वा नाप्यस्ति दाता पुरुषस्य कश्चित्। पर्याययोगाद् विहितं विधात्रा कालेन सर्वं लभते मनुष्यः॥
en: Vyasa said, No one can acquire anything by his own deeds or by sacrifices and adoration. No man can give anything to another. Man gets everything through Time. The Great Ordainer has made the course of Time the instrument of acquisition.

sn: न बुद्धिशास्त्राध्ययनेन शक्यं प्राप्तुं विशेषं मनुजैरकाले। मूर्योऽपि चाप्नोति कदाचिदर्थान् कालो हि कार्य प्रति निर्विशेषः॥
en: By mere intelligence of study of the scriptures, men, if Time be not propitious, cannot acquire any earthly object. Sometimes an ignorant fool may acquire wealth. Time is the the powerful instrument for the accomplishment of all acts.

sn: नाभूतिकालेषु फलं ददन्ति शिल्पानि मन्त्राश्च तथौषधानि। तान्येव कालेन समाहितानि सिद्ध्यन्ति वर्धन्ति च भूतिकाले॥
en: During the hour of adversity, neither science, nor incantations, nor drugs, produce any fruits. In prosperity, however, those very things, applied, yield abundant fruits.

sn: कालेन शीघ्राः प्रवहन्ति वाता: कालेन वृष्टिर्जलदानुपति। कालेन पद्मोत्पलवज्जलं च कालेन पुष्यन्ति वनेषु वृक्षाः॥
en: By time the winds blow violently; by Time the clouds become surcharged with rain; by Time tanks become adorned with lotuses of various sorts; by Time trees in the forest are covered with flowers.

sn: कालेन कृष्णाश्च सिताश्च रात्र्यः कालेन चन्द्रः परिपूर्णबिम्बः। नाकालतः पुष्पफलं दुमाणां नाकालवेगाः सरितो वहन्ति॥
en: By Time nights become dark or lighted. By Time the Moon becomes full. If the proper Time does not come, trees do not bear flowers and fruits. If the proper Time does not come, the currents of rivers do not become powerful.

sn: नाकालमत्ताः खगपन्नगाश्च मृगद्विपाः शैलमृगाच लोके। नाकालतः स्त्रीषु भवन्ति गर्भा नायान्त्यकाले शिशिरोष्णवर्षाः॥
en: Birds, snakes, deer, elephants and other animals never become excited when the proper Time does not come. If the proper Time does not come, women do not conceive. It is with Time that winter, summer, and the rainy seasons come.

sn: नाकालतो म्रियते जायते वा नाकालतो व्याहरते च बालः। नाकालतो यौवनमभ्युपैति नाकालतो रोहति बीजमुप्तम्॥
en: If the proper Time does not come, no one is born and no one dies. If the Time does not come, the infant does not gain power of speech. If the Time does not come one does not come by youth. It is with Time that the seed sown sprouts up.

sn: नाकालतो भानुरुपैति योगं नाकालतोऽङ्गिरिमभ्युपैति। नाकालतो वर्धते ही चन्द्रः समुद्रोऽपि महोर्मिमाली।॥
en: If the Time does not come, the Sun does not appear in the horizon, nor, when the Time for it does not come, does he set. If the Time for it does not come, the Moon does not increase nor wane, nor the ocean with its waves rise and ebb.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। गीतं राज्ञा सेनजिता दुःखार्तेन युधिष्ठिर॥
en: In this connection is related the old story, O Yudhishthira, by king Senajit in sorrow.

sn: सर्वानेवैष पर्यायो मान् स्पृशति दुःसहः। कालेन परिपक्वा हि म्रियन्ते सर्वपार्थिवाः॥
en: The powerful course of Time affects all mortals. All earthly objects, ripened by Time, meet with destruction.

sn: घ्नन्ति चान्यान् नरा राजस्तानप्यन्ये तथा नराः। संज्ञैषा लौकिकी राजन् न हिनस्ति न हन्यते॥
en: Some, O king, kill some men. The killers, again, are slain by others. This is what the world says. In reality, however, no one kills and no one is killed.

sn: हन्तीति मन्यते कश्चिन्न हन्तीत्यपि चापरः। स्वभावतस्तु नियतौ भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययौ॥
en: Some body thinks men kill (their fellow men). Another thinks men do not kill. The truth is that the birth and death of all creatures have been ordained to happen by their very nature.

sn: नष्टे धने वा दारे वा पुत्रे पितरि वा मृते। अहो दुःखमिति ध्यायन् दुःखस्यापचितिं चरेत्॥
en: At the loss of one's riches or the death of one's wife or son or father, one cries out saying-Alas what grief!-and the continued thought of that sorrow always increases it.

sn: स किं शोचसि मूढः सञ्शोच्यान् किमनुशोचसि। पश्य दुःखेषु दुःखानि भयेषु च भयान्यपि॥
en: Why do you, like a foolish man, grieve? Why do you grieve for them who are subject to grief? Mark, grief is enhanced by indulgence as fear is by fearing.

sn: आत्मापि चायं न मम सर्वापि पृथिवी मम। यथा मम तथान्येषामिति पश्यन् न मुह्यति॥
en: This body even is not mine. Nothing in this Earth is mine. The things of this Earth belong as much to others as to me. Seeing this, the wise do not allow themselves to be beguiled.

sn: शोकस्थानसहस्राणि हर्षस्थानशतानि च। दिवसे दिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम्॥
en: There are thousands of causes for sorrow and hundreds of causes for joy. These affect daily the ignorant only, but not the wise.

sn: एवमेतानि कालेन प्रियद्वेष्याणि भागशः। जीवेषु परिवर्तन्ते दुःखानि च सुखानि च॥
en: These in course of Time. become objects of love or hatred, and appearing as happiness or misery revolve for affecting living creatures.

sn: दुःखमेवास्ति न सुखं तस्मात् तदुपलभ्यते। तृष्णार्तिप्रभवं दुःखं दुःखार्तिप्रभवं सुखम्॥
en: There is only sorrow in this world and not happiness. Therefore sorrow only is felt. Desire begets sorrow and sorrow happiness.

sn: सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं दुःखस्यानन्तरं सुखम्। न नित्यं लभते दुःखं न नित्यं लभते सुखम्॥
en: Sorrow comes after happiness. and happiness after sorrow. One does not always suffer sorrow or always enjoy happiness.

sn: सुखमेवहि दुःखान्तं कदाचिद् दुःखतः सुखम्। तस्मादेतद् द्वयं जह्याद् य इच्छेच्छाश्वतं सुखम्॥
en: Happiness always ends in sorrow and sometimes originates from sorrow itself. He, therefore, who desires perpetual happiness must give up both.

sn: सुखान्तप्रभवं दुःखं दुःखान्तप्रभवं सुखम्। यन्निमित्तो भवेच्छोकस्तापो वा भृशदारुणः॥ आयासो वापि यन्मूलस्तदेकाङ्गमपि त्यजेत्।
en: When sorrow must arise upon termination of happiness, and happiness upon the termination of sorrow, and should, therefore, shake off, like a (snake-bit) limb, that which begets sorrow or that heart-burning which is reared by sorrow or that which is the root of his anxiety.

sn: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं प्रियं वा यदि वाप्रियम्। प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपासीत हृदयेनापराजितः॥
en: Happiness or sorrow, whatever comes should be borne with an unaffected heart.

sn: ईषदप्यङ्ग दाराणां पुत्राणां वा चराप्रियम्। ततो ज्ञास्यसि कः कस्य केन वा कथमेव च।॥
en: O amiable king, if you do not in the least, do what is agreeable to your wives and children, you shall then know who is whose, and why so, and for what.

sn: ये च मूढतमा लोके ये च बुद्धेः परं गताः। त एव सुखमेधन्ते मध्यमः क्लिश्यते जनः॥
en: Only those who stolid fools and those who are masters of their souls enjoy happiness here. They, however, who occupy an intermediate position suffering misery.

sn: इत्यब्रवीन्महाप्राज्ञो युधिष्ठिर स सेनजित्। परावरज्ञो लोकस्य धर्मवित् सुखदुःखवित्॥
en: This, O Yudhishthira, is what the highly wise the Senajit who was conversant with what is good or bad in this world, with duties, and with happiness and misery said.

sn: येन दुःखेन यो दुःखी न स जातु सुखी भवेत्। दुःखानां हि क्षयो नास्ति जायते ह्यपरात् परम्॥
en: He who is grieved at other people's griefs can never enjoy happiness. There is no end of grief, and grief originates from happiness itself.

sn: सुखं च दुःखं च भवाभवौ च लाभालाभौ मरणं जीवितं च। पर्यायतः सर्वमवाप्नुवन्ति तस्माद्धीरो नैव हृष्येन शोचेत्॥
en: Happiness and misery, prosperity and adversity, gain and loss, death and life, in their turn, visit all creatures. There the wise man, endued with equanimity soul would neither be puffed up with joy nor be depressed with sorrow.

sn: दीक्षां राज्ञः संयुगे युद्धमाई र्योगं राज्ये दण्डनीत्यां च सम्यक्। वित्तत्यागो दक्षिणानां च यज्ञे सम्यग् दानं पावनानीति विद्यात्॥
en: Battle has been described as the Sacrifice for a king; observance of chastisement is his Yoga; and the gift of riches in sacrifices in the form of presents his Renunciation. All these should be regarded as acts which purify him.

sn: रक्षन् राज्यं बुद्धिपूर्वं नयेन संत्यक्तात्मा यज्ञशीलो महात्मा। प्यूर्ध्वं देहान्मोदते देवलोके॥
en: By governing the kingdom with intelligence and policy, casting off wide, celebrating sacrifices, and looking at everything and all the persons with kindness and impartiality, a great king, after death, sports in the region of the celestials.

sn: जित्वा संग्रामान्पालयित्वा च राष्ट्र सोमं पीत्वा वर्धयित्वा प्रजाश्च। युक्त्या दण्डं धारयित्वा प्रजानांयुद्धे क्षीणो मोदते देवलोके॥
en: By gaining battles, protecting his kingdom, drinking the Soma juice, making his subjects prosper, holding judiciously the rod of chastisement, and renouncing his body at last in fight, a king enjoy happiness in heaven.

sn: सम्यग् वेदान् प्राप्य शास्त्राण्यधीत्य सम्यग् राज्यं पालयित्वा च राजा। चातुर्वर्ण्य स्थापयित्वा स्वधर्म पूतात्मा वै मोदते देवलोके॥
en: Having studied all the Vedas and the other scriptures duly, having protected the kingdom duly, and having made all the four orders follow their respective duties, a king become purified and finally sports in heaven.

sn: यस्य वृत्तं नमस्यन्ति स्वर्गस्थस्यापि मानवाः। पौरजानपदामात्याः स राजा राजसत्तमः॥
en: He is the best of kings whose conduct, even after his death, is praised by the denizens of the city and the country and by his counsellors and friends.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अस्मिन्नेव प्रकरणे धनंजयमुदारधीः। अभिनीततरं वाक्यमित्युवाच युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereat, the great Yudhishthira said to

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: यदेतन्मन्यसे पार्थ न ज्यायोऽस्ति धनादिति। न स्वर्गो न सुखं नार्थो निर्धनस्येति तन्मृषा॥
en: You think, O Partha, that there is nothing superior to wealth, and that the poor man can neither have heaven, nor happiness, nor the accomplishment of his wishes.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: स्वाध्याययज्ञसंसिद्धा दृश्यन्ते बहवो जनाः। तपोरताश्च मुनयो येषां लोकाः सनातनाः॥
en: This however, is not true. Many persons are scen who have become successful through Sacrifice in the shape of Vedic study. Many sages are seen who by practising penances have acquired eternal regions for themselves.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: ऋषीणां समयं शश्वद् ये रक्षन्ति धनंजय। आश्रिताः सर्वधर्मज्ञा देवास्तान् ब्राह्मणान् विदुः॥
en: They, O Dhananjaya who always follow the practice of the Rishis by leading the life of a Brahmacharin and who become acquainted with all duties, are regarded by the gods as Brahmanas.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: स्वाध्यायनिष्ठान् हि ऋषीन् ज्ञाननिष्ठांस्तथापरान्। बुद्ध्येथाः संततं चापि धर्मनिष्ठान् धनंजय॥
en: O Dhananjaya, you should always know those Rishis who are devoted to the study of the Vedas and those who are devoted to the pursuit of true knowledge as persons who are truly virtuous.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: ज्ञाननिष्ठेषु कार्याणि प्रतिष्ठाप्यानि पाण्डव। वैखानसानां वचनं यथा नो विदितं प्रभो॥
en: O son of Pandu, all our acts should be shaped by those who are devoted to the acquisition of true knowledge. Surely it is the opinion of the Vaikhanasas, O powerful one.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: अजाश्च पृश्नयश्चैव सिकताश्चैव भारत। अरुणाः केतवश्चैव स्वाध्यायेन दिवं गताः॥
en: The Ajas, the Prishnis, the Sikatas, O Bharata, Arunas, and the Ketavas, have all gone to heaven by the merit of Vedic study.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: अवाप्यैतानि कर्माणि वेदोक्तानि धनंजय। दानमध्ययनं यज्ञो निग्रहश्चैव दुर्ग्रहः॥ दक्षिणेन च पन्थानमर्यम्णो ये दिवं गताः। एतान् क्रियावतां लोकानुक्तवान् पूर्वमप्यहम्॥
en: By performing those acts, O Dhananjaya, that are laid down in the Vedas, viz., battle, study of the Vedas, Sacrifices, the control of passion that is so difficult, one goes to heaven by the southern path of the Sun. I have, before this, told you that those very regions are reserved for persons who perform (Vedic) acts.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: उत्तरेण तु पन्थानं नियमाद् यं प्रपश्यसि। एते यागवतां लोका भान्ति पार्थ सनातनाः॥
en: You will see, however, that the northern path is trodden by those who are devoted to Yoga. Those eternal and bright regions to which that path leads is reserved for Yogins.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: तत्रोत्तरां गतिं पार्थ प्रशंसन्ति पुराविदः। संतोषो वै स्वर्गतमः संतोषः परमं सुखम्॥
en: Of these two, the northern path is spoken highly by those conversant with the Puranas. You should know that one gains heaven through contentment begets happiness.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: तुष्टेर्न किञ्चित् परमं सा सम्यक् प्रतितिष्ठति। विनीतक्रोधहर्षस्य सततं सिद्धिरुत्तमा॥
en: There is nothing superior to contentment. To the Yogin who has controlled anger and joy, contentment is the greatest success.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीमा गाथा गीता ययातिना। याभिः प्रत्याहरेत् कामान् कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः॥
en: Regarding it is cited the discourse of Yayati. Listening to that discourse one can withdraw all his desires like a tortoise drawing in all his limbs.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: यदा चायं न बिभेति यदा चास्मात बिभ्यति। यदा नेच्छति न देशि ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When one entertains no fear of anything, when one is not feared by anything when one entertains no desire, when one bears no hate, then is one said to have attained to the dignity of Brahma.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: यदा न भावं कुरुते सर्वभूतेषु पापकम्। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When one does not commit sin by any creature, in deed, thought, or word, one is then said to have attained to Brahma.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: विनीतमानमोहश्च बहुसङ्गविवर्जितः। तदाऽऽत्मज्योतिषः साधोर्निर्वाणमुपपद्यते॥
en: When one has governed his pride and folly, and withdrawn himself from all attachments, it is then that pious man of controlled soul becomes fit for attaining to that emancipation which is brought about by the annihilation of personal existence.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: इदं तु शृणु मे पार्थ ब्रुवतः संयतेन्द्रियः। धर्ममन्ये वृत्तमन्ये धनमीहन्ति चापरे॥
en: Listen now to me with rapt attention, O son of Pritha, as I say it to you. Some seek virtue; some, good conduct, and some, wealth.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: धनहेतोर्य ईहेत तस्यानीहा गरीयसी। भूयान् दोषो हि वित्तस्य यश्च धर्मस्तदाश्रयः॥
en: One may desire wealth. The abandonment, however, of such desire is better for himn. There are many shortcomings attached to wealth and, therefore, to those religious acts that are performed with wealth.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: प्रत्यक्षमनुपश्यामि त्वमपि द्रष्टुमर्हसि। वर्जनं वर्जनीयानामीहमानेन दुष्करम्॥
en: We have seen it with our own eyes. You should also see this. He that desires wealth finds it very difficult to leave off that which should by all means be abandoned.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: ये वित्तमभिपद्यन्ते सम्यक्त्वं तेषु दुर्लभम्। दुह्यतः प्रैति तत् प्राहुः प्रतिकूलं यथातथम्॥
en: Good deeds are very rare in those who collect riches. It is said that wealth can never be acquired without injuring others, and that, when acquired, it is attended with various troubles.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: यस्तु सम्भिन्नवृत्तः स्याद् वीतशोकभयो नरः। अल्पेन तृषितो दुह्यन् भ्रूणहत्यां न बुध्यते॥
en: A weak minded person, disregarding the fear of repentance, oppresses others, tempted by even a little wealth, not knowing all while of the sin Brahmanicide that he incurs by his acts.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: दुष्यन्त्याददतो भृत्या नित्यं दस्युभयादिव। दुर्लभं च धनं प्राप्य भृशं दत्त्वानुतप्यते॥
en: Acquiring wealth which is so difficult of acquisition, one burns with grief if he has to give a part of it, even if it be, to his servants,-tantamount to what he would actually feel if he is robbed by others. If, on the other hand, one does not distribute his wealth, he becomes an object of censure.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: अधनः कस्य किं वाच्यो विमुक्तः सर्वशः सुखी। देवस्वमुपगृव धनेन न सुखी भवेत्॥
en: One, however, that has no wealth, is never blamed. Forsaking all attachments, such a person can become happy in all respects by living upon what little he may get as alms. No one, however, can be happy by acquiring riches.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: अत्र गाथां यज्ञगीतां कीर्तयन्ति पुराविदः। त्रयीमुपाश्रितां लोके यज्ञ संस्तरकारिकाम्॥
en: Regarding it certain verses relating to Sacrifices are recited by persons well read in ancient scriptures.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: यज्ञाय सृष्टानि धनानि धात्रा यज्ञाय सृष्टः पुरुषो रक्षिता च। तस्मात् सर्वं यज्ञ एवोपयोज्यं धनं न कामाय हितं प्रशस्तम्॥
en: Wealth was created by the Creator for celebrating Sacrifices, and man was created by hinn for protecting that wealth and performing Sacrifices. For this, all wealth should be devoted to Sacrifices. It is not proper that it should be spent for enjoyments.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: एतत् स्वार्थे च कौन्तेय धनं धनवतां वर। धाता ददाति मर्येभ्यो यज्ञार्थमिति विद्धि तत्॥
en: The Creator gives wealth to mortals for the sake of Sacrifices. Know this, O Son of Kunti, foremost of all wealthy persons.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: तस्माद् बुद्ध्यन्ति पुरुषा न हि तत् कस्यचिद्धवम्। श्रद्धानस्ततो लोको दद्याच्चैव यजेत च॥
en: Therefore the wise think that wealth, forsooth, is nobody's on Earth. One should celebrate Sacrifices with it and give it away with a confident heart.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: लब्धस्य त्यागमित्याहुन भोगं न च संचयम्। तस्य किं संचयेनार्थः कार्ये ज्यायसि तिष्ठति॥
en: One should make gift of what he has acquired, and not waste or spend it in gratifying his desire of enjoyment. What use is there in hoarding up wealth when proper objects exist in which to spend it.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: ये स्वधर्मादपेतेभ्यः प्रयच्छन्त्यल्पबुद्धयः। शतं वर्षाणि ते प्रेत्य पुरीषं भुञ्जते जनाः॥
en: Those foolish people who give away (wealth) to men who have neglected the duties of their order, have to live hereafter for a hundred years on ordure and dirt.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: अनर्हते यद् ददाति न ददाति यदर्हते। अनिर्हापरिज्ञानाद् दानधर्मोऽपि दुष्करः॥
en: Being unable to the discriminate between the deserving and the undeserving, men give to the undeserving and refrain from giving to the deserving. For this reason the administration of charity is difficult.

description: Yudhishthira describes the two paths to heaven. The necessity of Sacrifices and Vedic Study. The proper use of wealth.
sn: लब्धानामपि वित्तानां बोद्धव्यौ द्वावतिक्रमौ। अपात्रे प्रतिपत्तिश्च पात्रे चाप्रतिपादनम्॥
en: These are the two faults with wealth even when acquired, viz., gift to an undeserving person and abstaining to give to a deserving man.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अभिमन्यौ हते बाले द्रौपद्यास्तनयेषु च। धृष्टद्युम्ने विराटे च दुपदे च महीपतौ॥ वृषसेने च धर्मज्ञे धृष्टकेतौ तु पार्थिवे। तथान्येषु नरेन्द्रेषु नानादेश्येषु संयुगे॥ न च मुञ्चति मां शोको ज्ञातिघातिनमातुरम्। राज्यकामुकमत्युग्रं स्ववंशोच्छेदकारिणम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said On account of the death of young Abhimanyu of the sons of Draupadi, of Draupadi, of Dhrishtadyumna, of Virata, of king Drupada, of Vasusena conversant with every duty, of the royal Dhrishtaketu, and of Various other kings coming from various, countries in battle, grief does not forsake my wretched self that am a destroyer of kinsmen! Indeed, I covet very much for kingdom and am an exterminator of my own race.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: यस्माङ्के क्रीडमानेन मया वै परिवर्तितम्। स मया राज्यलुब्धेन गाङ्गेयो युधि पातितः॥
en: He upon whose breast and limbs I used to play, alas, that Ganga's son has been killed by me in battle out of desire for sovereignty.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: यदा ह्येनं विघूर्णन्तमपश्यं पार्थसायकैः। कम्पमानं यथा वड्रैः प्रेक्ष्यमाणं शिखण्डिना॥ जीर्णसिंहमिव प्रांशुं नरसिंह पितामहम्। कीर्यमाणं शरैर्दृष्ट्वा भृशं मे व्यथितं मनः॥
en: When I saw that foremost of men, viz., our grandfather, assailed by Shikhandin and trembling and reeling in consequence of Partha's arrows that resembled thunder-bolts in power, when I saw his tall form cut all over with blazing arrows and himself become weak like an aged lion, my heart was greatly pained.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: प्राङ्मुखं सीदमानं च रथे पररथारुजम्। घूर्णमानं यथा शैलं तदा मे कश्मलोऽभवत्॥
en: When I saw that destroyer of hostile cars reel like a mountain summit and drop down on the terrace of his own car with his face turned towards the east, my senses were bewildered.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: यः स बाणधनुष्पाणिर्योधयामास भार्गवम्। बहून्यहानि कौरव्यः कुरुक्षेत्रे महामृधे॥ समेतं पाथिवं क्षत्रं वाराणस्यां नदीसुतः। कन्यार्थमाह्वयद् वीरो रथेनैकेन संयुगे॥ येन चोग्रायुधो राजा चक्रवर्ती दुरासदः। दग्धश्चास्त्रप्रतापेन स मया युधि घातितः॥
en: That foremost of Kuru's race who with bow and arrow in hand had fought in dreadful battle for inany days with Rama himself of Bhrigu's race on the field purified by Kuru, that son of Ganga, that hero, who, at Varanasi, for the sake of maidens, had, on a single car, challenged to battle the assembled Kshatriyas of the world, he who had consumed by the power of his weapons that irresistible and best of kings Ugrayudha, alas, that hero has been killed in battle by me.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: स्वयं मृत्यु रक्षमाणः पाञ्चाल्यं यः शिखण्डिनम्। न बाणैः पातयामास सोऽर्जुनेन निपातितः॥
en: Knowing full well that Shikhandin the prince of Panchala was his slayer, that hero still refrained from killing the prince with his arrow. Alas, such a magnanimous warrior was killed by Arjuna.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: यदैनं पतितं भूमावपश्यं रुधिरोक्षितम्। तदैवाविशदत्युग्रो ज्वरो मां मुनिसत्तम॥
en: O best of sages, when I saw the grandfather stretched on the Earth and bathed in blood, a violent fever afflicted my heart.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: येन संवर्धिता बाला येन स्म परिरक्षिताः। स मया राज्यलुब्धेन पापेन गुरुघातिना॥
en: He who had protected and brought us up when we were children alas, he was caused to be killed by my sinful self that am covetous of kingdom, that am a slayer of reverend elders, and a perfect fool, for the sake of fickle sovereignty.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: अल्पकालस्य राज्यस्य कृते मूढेन घातितः। आचार्यश्च महेष्वासः सर्वपार्थिवपूजितः॥
en: I gave a false statement of his son to our preceptor, the great bowman Drona, worshipped of all the kings.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: अभिगम्य रणे मिथ्या पापेनोक्तः सुतं प्रति। तन्मे दहति गात्राणि यन्मां गुरुरभाषत॥ सत्यमाख्याहि राजंस्त्वं यदि जीवति मे सत्यमामर्षयन् विप्रो मयि तत् परिपृष्टवान्॥
en: The recollection of that act of mine is burning all my limbs. The preceptor said to me,-Tell me truly, O king, whether my son lives still,—Expecting truth from me, the Brahmana asked me only. By silently saying the word elephant, I behaved falsely towards him.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: सुतः। कुञ्जरं चान्तरं कृत्वा मिथ्योपचरितं मया। सुभृशं राज्यलुब्धेन पापेन गुरुघातिना॥ सत्यकञ्चकमुन्मुच्य मया स गुरुराहवे। अश्वत्थामा हत इति निरुक्तः कुञ्जरे हते॥
en: Sinful that I am, highly covetous of kingdom, and a destroyer of my reverend elders, I behaved even thus towards my preceptor in battle, casting off the garb of truth-for I said to him that Ashvatthama had been slain when, in sooth, an elephant of the name had been slain.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: काँल्लोकांस्तु गमिष्यामि कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। अघातयं च यत् कर्णं समरेष्वपलायिनम्॥
en: To what regions shall I go (hereafter) having committed such a crime? I caused also my eldest brother Karna to be killed, that terrible warrior who never retreated from battle. Who is there more sinful than I?

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: ज्येष्ठभ्रातरमत्युग्रं को मत्तः पापकृत्तमः। अभिमन्युं च यद् बालं जातं सिंहमिवाद्रिषु॥ प्रावेशयमहं लुब्धो वाहिनीं द्रोणपालिताम्।
en: Through covetousness I caused young Abhimanyu that hero who resembled a lion born in the hills, to enter into the array that was protected by Drona himself.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: तदाप्रभृति बीभत्सुं न शक्नोमि निरीक्षितुम्॥ कृष्णं च पुण्डरीकाक्षं किल्बिषी भ्रूणहा यथा।
en: I am guilty of infanticide. Sinful as I am, I have not, since then, been able to look at the face of Arjuna or the lotus-eyed Krishna.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: द्रौपदीं चापि दुःखार्ती पञ्चपुत्रैर्विनाकृताम्॥ शोचामि पृथिवीं हीनां पञ्चभिः पर्वतैरिव।
en: I grieve also for Draupadi who is deprived of her five sons like the Earth shorn of her five mountains.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: सोऽहमागस्करः पापः पृथिवीनाशकारकः॥ आसीन एवमेवेदं शोषयिष्ये कलेवरम्।
en: I am a great sinner and a destroyer of the Earth. Not rising from this seat which I now occupy, I will emaciate my body (by starvation) and meet with death.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: प्रायोपविष्टं जानीध्वमथ मां गुरुघातिनम्॥ जातिष्वन्यास्वपि यथा न भवेयं कुलान्तकृत्।
en: Know me who am the destroyer of my preceptor as one who has sat down here observing the Praya vow. A destroyer of my family, I must do so in order that I may not be born again in any of other orders of being.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: न भोक्ष्ये न च पानीयमुपभोक्ष्ये कथञ्चन॥ शोषयिष्ये प्रियान् प्राणनिहस्थोऽहं तपोधनाः।
en: I shall abstain from taking all food and drink, and without moving from here, O great ascetic, shall dry up my life-breaths which are sodear.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: यथेष्टं गम्यतां काममनुजाने प्रसाद्य वः॥ सर्वे मामनुजानीत तयक्ष्यामीदं कलेवरम्।
en: I humbly pray you to grant me permission in this and go wherever you please. Let every one grant me permission. I shall renounce this body of mine."

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तमेवंवादिनं पार्थं बन्धुशोकेन विह्वलम्॥ मैवमित्यब्रवीद् व्यासो निगृह्य मुनिसत्तमः।
en: Vaishampayana said Preventing Pritha's son, who beside himself with sorrow on account of his kinsmen, gave vent to such words, Vyasa, that best of ascetics, said, first telling him,-'This cannot be.'

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: व्यास उवाच अतिवेलं महाराज न शोकं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ पुनरुक्तं तु वक्ष्यामि दिष्टमेतदिति प्रभो।
en: Vyasa said 'You should not, O king, indulge in such painful grief. I shall again say what I have once said. All this is Destiny, O powerful one.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता जातानां प्राणिनां ध्रुवम्॥ बुबुदा इव तोयेषु भवन्ति न भवन्ति च। सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः॥ संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं हि जीवितम्।
en: Forsooth, all creatures that are born show at first a union (of various ingredients and forces). Dissolution, however, overtakes them at the end. Like bubbles in water they come and go away. All things collected together are sure to be dissipated, and all things that rise must fall down. Union terininates in dissolution and life terininates in death.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: सुखं दुःखान्तमालस्यं दाक्ष्यं दुःखं सुखोदयम्। भूतिः श्रीह्रीं धृतिः कीर्तिर्दक्षे वसति नालसे॥
en: Idleness, though pleasant for the time being, ends in misery, and skilful labour, though painful in beginning, ends in happiness. Affluence, Prosperity, Modesty, Contentment, and Fame reside in labour and skill but not in idleness.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: नालं सुखाय सुहृदो नालं दुःखाय शत्रवः। न च प्रजालमर्थेभ्यो न सुखेभ्योऽप्यलं धनम्॥
en: Friends cannot confer happiness nor foes inflict misery. Likewise wisdom does not give wealth nor does wealth bring happiness.

description: Yudhishthira's lamentations for the death of his people. Vyasa consoles him by saying that all this is the work ofDestiny.
sn: यथा सृष्टोऽसि कौन्तेय धात्रा कर्मसु तत् कुरु। अत एव हि सिद्धिस्ते नेशस्त्वं कर्मणां नृप॥
en: O son of Kunti, you have been created by your Maker to engage yourself in action. Success originates from work, You cannot, O king, avoid Work."

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ज्ञातिशोकाभितप्तस्य प्राणानभ्युत्सिसृक्षतः । ज्येष्ठस्य पाण्डुपुत्रस्य व्यासः शोकमपानुदत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Vyasa then removed the grief of the cldest of Pandu, who, filled with sorrow consequent on the destruction of his kinsmen, had resolved to throw off his life-brcaths.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: व्यास उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। अश्मगीतं नरव्याघ्र तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Vyasa said 'Regarding this subject is cited the old story, O foremost of men, that is known by the name of Ashma's discourse, Listen to it, O Yudhishthira.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: अश्मानं ब्राह्मणं प्राज्ञं वैदेहो जनको नृपः। संशयं परिपप्रच्छ दुःखशोकसमन्वितः॥
en: Janaka the king of the Videhas, O king, filled with sorrow and grief, asked a wise Brahmana of the name of Ashma for removing his doubts.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: जनक उवाच आगमे यदि वापाये ज्ञातीनां द्रविणस्य च। नरेण प्रतिपत्तव्यं कल्याणं कथमिच्छता॥
en: Janaka said How should a man seeking his own wellbeing act upon occasions of the accession and the destruction of both kinsmen and wealth?-

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: अश्मोवाच उत्पन्नमिममात्मानं नरस्यानन्तरं ततः। तानि तान्यनुवर्तन्ते दुःखानि च सुखानि च॥
en: Ashma said Immediately after the formation of a man's body, joys and sorrows are themselves attached to it.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: तेषामन्यतरापत्तौ यद् यदेवोपपद्यते। तदस्य चेतनामाशु हरत्यभ्रमिवानिलः॥
en: Although either of the two may overtake the person, yet whichever actually overtakes him quickly deprives him of his understanding like the wind dissipating gathering clouds.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: अभिजातोऽस्मि सिद्धोऽस्मि नास्मि केवलमानुषः। इत्येभिर्हेतुभिस्तस्य त्रिभिश्चित्तं प्रसिच्यते॥
en: In prosperity one thinks,-I am of highbirth.-I can do whatever I like.-I am not an ordinary person.-His mind because soaked with these three vain thoughts.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: सम्प्रसक्तमना भोगान् विसृज्य पितृसंचितान्। परिक्षीणः परस्वानामादानं साधु मन्यते॥
en: Addicted to all earthly pleasures, he begins to dissipate the wealth hoarded by his ancestors. Impoverished in course of time, he considers the misappropriation of others' property as even laudable.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: तमतिक्रान्तमर्यादमाददानमसाम्प्रतम्। प्रतिषेधन्ति राजानो लुब्धा मृगमिवेषुभिः॥
en: Like a hunter striking a deer with his arrows, the king then punishes the wicked man, that robber of other people's wealth, that transgressor, of law and regulations.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: ये च विंशतिवषर्ज वा त्रिंशद्वर्षाश्च मानवाः। परेण ते वर्षशतान्न भविष्यन्ति पार्थिव॥
en: Without attaining to a hundred years, such man scarcely live beyond twenty or thirty years.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: तेषां परमदुः :खानां बुद्ध्या भैषज्यमाचरेत्। सर्वप्राणभृतां वृत्तं प्रेक्षमाणस्ततस्ततः॥
en: Carefully observing the conduct of all creatures, a king should, by the exercise of his intelligence, concert measures for alleviating the great sorrows of his subjects.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः। अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते॥
en: The causes of all mental sorrow are twofold viz., delusion of the mind and distress. No third cause is there.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: एवमेतानि दुःखानि तानि तानीह मानवम्। विविधान्युपवर्तन्ते तथा संस्पर्शजान्यपि॥
en: All these various kinds of misery as also those arising from attachment to earthly pleasures that overtake man, are even such.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: जरामृत्यू हि भूतानां खादितारौ वृकाविव। बलिनां दुर्बलानां च ह्रस्वानां महतामपि॥
en: Like a pair of wolves Decrepitude and Death, devour all creatures, strong or weak, short or tall.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: न कश्चिज्जात्वतिक्रामेज्जरामृत्यू हि मानवः। अपि सागरपर्यन्तां विजित्येमां वसुन्धराम्॥
en: No man can escape decrepitude and death, not even the conqueror of the whole Earth encompassed by the sea.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं भूतानां पर्युपस्थितम्। प्राप्तव्यमवशैः सर्वं परिहारो न विद्यते॥
en: Happiness or sorrow whatever comes upon creatures, it should be enjoyed or borne without elation or depression. There is no means of escaping from them.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: पूर्वे वयसि मध्ये वाप्युत्तरे वा नराधिप। अवर्जनीयास्तेऽर्था वै कांक्षिता ये ततोऽन्यथा॥
en: The evils of life, O king, overtake one in infancy or youth or old age. They can never be avoided, while those which one seeks most never come.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: अप्रियैः सह संयोगो विप्रयोगश्च सुप्रियैः। अर्थानों सुखं दुःखं विधानमनुवर्तते॥
en: The absence of what is pleasant, the presence of what is disagreeable, good and evil, happiness and misery, follow Destiny.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: प्रादुर्भावश्च भूतानां देहत्यागस्तथैव च। प्राप्तिायामयोगश्च सर्वमेतत् प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Likewise, the birth of creatures and their death, and profit and loss, are all preordained.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: गन्धवर्णरसस्पर्शा निवर्तन्ते स्वभावतः। तथैव सुखदुःखानि विधानमनुवर्तते॥
en: As smell, colour, taste, and touch originate of themselves, so happiness and misery originate from what has been preordained.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: आसनं शयनं यानमुत्थानं पानभोजनम्। नियतं सर्वभूतानां कालेनैव भवत्युत॥
en: Seats, beds, cars, riches, drink and food, always come to living creatures in the due course of Time.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: वैद्याश्चाप्यातुराः सन्ति बलवन्तश्च दुर्बलाः। श्रीमन्तचापरे षण्ढा विचित्रः कालपर्ययः॥
en: Physicians even fall ill. The strong become weak. The rich man lose all and become poor. The course of Time is highly wonderful.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: कुले जन्म तथा वीर्यमारोग्यं रूपमेव च। सौभाग्यमुपभोगश्च भवितव्येन लभ्यते॥
en: Noble-birth, health, beauty, prosperity, and objects of pleasures, are all begotten by Destiny.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: सन्ति पुत्राः सुबहवो दरिद्राणामनिच्छताम्। नास्तिः पुत्रः समृद्धानां विचित्रं विधिचेश्तिम्॥
en: The poor, although they may not desire it, have many children. The rich again are seen to have none. Wonderful is the course of Destiny.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: व्याधिरग्निर्जलं शस्त्रं बुभुक्षाश्चापदो विषम्। ज्वरच मरणं जन्तोरुच्चाच्च पतनं तथा॥ निर्माणे यस्य यद् दिष्टं तेन गच्छति सेतुना। दृश्यते नाप्यतिक्रामन्न निष्क्रान्तोऽथवा पुनः॥ दृश्यते चाप्यतिक्रामन्ननिग्राह्योऽथवा पुनः।
en: The dangers of ailment, fire, water, weapons, hunger, poison, fever, and death, and falls from elevated places, visit a man according to the Destiny under which he is born. It is generally seen in this world, that somebody, without committing any sin, suffers many miseries while another, having committed sins, is not pressed down by the weight of calamity.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: दृश्यते हि युवैवेह विनश्यन्वसुमानरः। दरिद्रश्च परिक्लिष्टः शतवर्षो जरान्वितः॥
en: It is seen that a rich man dies in youth; while a poor man lives on suffering from decrepitude, for a hundred years.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: अकिञ्चनाश्च दृश्यन्ते पुरुषाश्चिरजीविनः। समृद्धे च कुले जाता विनश्यन्ति पतङ्गवत्॥
en: One born in a mean family may live very long while one descended from a noble family dies soon like an insect.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: प्रायेण श्रीमतां लोके भोक्तुं शक्तिर्न विद्यते। काष्ठान्यपि हि जीर्यन्ते दरिद्राणां च सर्वशः॥
en: It is very common in this world, that rich men have no appetite, while the poor can digest pieces of wood.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: अहमेतत् करोमीति मन्यते कालनोदितः। यद् यदिष्टमसंतोषाद् दुरात्मा पापमाचरेत्॥
en: Discontented with his position, whatever sins a wicked man commits, under the influence of destiny, saying,-I am the doer,-he considers to be all for his good.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: मृगयाऽक्षाः स्त्रियः पानं प्रसङ्गा निन्दिता बुधैः। दृश्यन्ते पुरुषाश्चात्र सम्प्रयुक्ता बहुश्रुताः॥
en: Hunting, dice, women, wine, quarrels, these are censured by the wise. many persons, well, and greatly, read in the scriptures, are seen to be addicted to them.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: इति कालेन सर्वार्थानीप्सितानीप्सितानिह। स्पृशन्ति सर्वभूतानि निमित्तं नोपलभ्यते॥
en: Objects, whether sought for or otherwise, come upon creature in course of Time. No other cause is seen.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: वायुमाकाशमग्निं च चन्द्रादित्यावहःक्षपे। ज्योतींषि सरितः शैलान् कः करोति बिभर्ति च॥
en: Who creates and maintains air, ether, fire, moon, sun, day, night, the planets, rivers, and mountains?

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: शीतमुष्णं तथा वर्ष कालेन परिवर्तते। एवमेव मनुष्याणां सुखदुः :खे नरर्षभ॥
en: Cold, and heat, and rain, come in turn in course of Time. Such is the case, O foremost of men, with the happiness and the misery of mankind.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: नौषधानि न मन्त्राश्च न होमा न पुनर्जपाः। त्रायन्ते मृत्युनोपेतं जरया चापि मानवम्॥
en: Neither medicines, nor incantations, can save the man attacked by decrepitude or overtaken by death.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महोदधौ। समेत्य च व्यपेयातां तद्वद् भूतसमागमः॥
en: As two pieces wood, floating on the great ocean, come together and are again separated, so creatures are united and are again separated in time.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: ये चैव पुरुषाः स्त्रीभिर्गीतवाद्यैरुपस्थिताः। य चानाथाः परान्नादा: कालस्तेषु समक्रियः॥
en: Time acts impartially towards rich men who enjoy the pleasure of song and dance in the company of women and those unfortunate men who live upon another's food.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: मातापितृसहस्राणि पुत्रदारशतानि च। संसारेष्वनुभूतानि कस्य ते कस्य वा वयम्॥
en: In this world a thousand sorts of relationship are made such as mother and father and son and wife. In truth, however, whose are they are whose are we?

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: नैवास्य कश्चिद् भविता नायं भवति कस्यचित्। पथि सङ्गतमेवेदं दारबन्धुसुहृज्जनैः॥
en: No one can become any one's own, nor can any one become anybody else's own. Our union here with wives and kinsmen and wellwishers is like that of travellers at an inn in the road.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: क्वासे क्व च गमिष्यामि को न्वहं किमिहास्थितः। कस्मात् किमनुशोचेयमित्येवं स्थापयेन्मनः॥
en: Where am I? Where shall I go?-Who am I?—How came I here?-Why and for whom should I grieve?-Thinking of all these questions one gets tranquillity.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: अनित्ये प्रियसंवासे संसारे चक्रवद्गतौ। पथि सङ्गतमेवैतद् भ्राता माता पिता सखा॥
en: Life and its surroundings are always revolving like a wheel, and the companionship of those who are dear in only for the time being. The union with brother, mother, father, and friend is like that of travellers in an inn.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: न दृष्टपूर्वं प्रत्यक्षं परलोकं विदुर्बुधाः। आगमांस्त्वनतिक्रम्य श्रद्धातव्यं बुभूषता॥
en: The wise men behold, as if with corporeal eyes, the next world which is unseen. Without setting at naught the scriptures, one desirous of knowledge should cherish faith.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: कुर्वीत पितृदैवत्यं धर्माणि च समाचरेत्। यजेच्च विद्वान् विधिवत् त्रिवर्गं चाप्युपाचरेत्॥
en: One possessed of knowledge should perform the rites laid down for the Pitris and the gods, perforin all religious duties, celebrate sacrifices, judiciously pursue religion, profit and pleasure.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: संनिमज्जेज्जगदिदं गम्भीरे कालसागरे। जरामृत्युमहाग्राहे न कश्चिदवबुध्यते॥
en: Alas, no one perceives that the world is sinking in the deep ocean of Time which is infested with those huge crocodiles called decrepitude and death.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: आयुर्वेदमधीयानाः केवलं सपरिग्रहाः। दृश्यन्ते बहवो वैद्या व्याधिभिः समभिप्लुताः॥
en: Many physicians are seen suffering from a disease along with all the members of their families, although they have carefully read the science of Life.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: ते पिबन्तः कषायांश्च सीषि विविधानि च। न मृत्युमतिवर्तन्ते वेलामिव महोदधिः॥
en: Taking bitters and various sorts of oily drugs, they cannot go beyond death as the ocean cannot transcend its continents.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: रसायनविदश्चैव सुप्रयुक्तरसायनाः। दृश्यन्ते जरया भग्ना नगा नागैरिवोत्तमैः॥
en: Despite the wise application of chemical compounds, men well-versed in chemistry, are seen to be broken down by decrepitude like trees broken down by elephants.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: तथैव तपसोपेताः स्वाध्यायाभ्यसने रताः। दातारो यज्ञशीलाश्च न तरन्ति जरान्तकौ॥
en: Likewise, persons endued with ascetic merit, devoted to study of the Vedas, practising charity and frequently celebrating sacrifices. cannot escape the hands of decrepitude and death.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: न शहानि निवर्तन्ते न मासा न पुनः समाः। जातानां सर्वभूतानां न पक्षा न पुनः क्षपाः॥ केनचित्।
en: as Neither years, nor months, nor fortnights, nor days, nor nights that have once gone away do ever return to creatures who are born.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: सोऽयं विपुलमध्वानं कालेन ध्रुवमध्रुवः। नरोऽवशः समभ्येति सर्वभूतनिषेवितम्॥
en: Man, whose existence is so transitory is compelled, in course of Time, whether he will or no, to come upon this inevitable and broad path of all creatures.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: देहो वा जीवतोऽभ्येति जीवो वाभ्येति देहतः। पथि सङ्गममभ्येति दारैरन्यैश्च बन्धुभिः॥
en: Whether the body originates from the creature, or the creature originates from the body, one's union, however, with wives and other friends is like that of travellers in an inn.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: नायमत्यन्तसंवासो लभ्यते जातु अपि स्वेन शरीरेण किमुतान्येन केनचित्॥
en: One cannot obtain another his companion for ever. One cannot obtain such union even with his own body. How then can it be secured with any one else?

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: क्व नु तेऽद्य पिता राजन् क्व नु तेऽद्य पितामहाः। न त्वं पश्यसि तानद्य न त्वां पश्यन्ति तेऽनघ॥
en: Where, O king, is your father, to-day and where your grandfathers? You do not see them to-day and they do not see you. O sinless one.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: न चैव पुरुषो द्रष्टा स्वर्गस्य नरकस्य च। आगमस्तु सतां चक्षुर्नृपते तमिहाचर॥
en: No person can see either heaven or hell. The sacred books, however, are the eyes of the virtuous. O king, regulate your conduct according to the scriptures.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: चरितब्रह्मचर्यो हि प्रजायेत यजेत च। पितृदेवमनुष्याणामानृण्यादनसूयकः॥
en: With a pure heart, one should lead the life of Brahmacharya and then procreate children and then celebrate sacrifices for satisfying the debt one owes of the Pitris, the gods and men.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: स यज्ञशीलः प्रजने निविष्टः प्रारब्रह्मचारी प्रविविक्तचक्षुः। आराधयेत् स्वर्गमिमं च लोकं परं च मुक्त्वा हृदयव्यलीकम्॥
en: Celebrating sacrifices and engaged in begetting (children),. after having first observed the vow of Brahmacharya, one who has eyes of wisdom shaking off all anxiety of heart, should seek heaven, this world, and his own soul.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: समं हि धर्मं चरतो नृपस्य द्रव्याणि चाभ्याहरतो यथावत्। प्रवृत्तधर्मस्य यशोऽभिवर्धते सर्वेषु लोकेषु चराचरेषु॥
en: That virtuous king who tries judiciously for acquiring Heaven and Earth and who takes his own share of earthly goods as sanctioned in the scriptures, acquires a reputation that spreads over all the worlds and among all creatures mobile and immobile.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: इत्येवमाज्ञाय विदेहराजो वाक्यं समग्रं परिपूर्णहेतुः। र्ययौ गृहं स्वं प्रति शान्तशोकः॥
en: Having heard these words pregnant with reason, the king of the Videhas of clear understanding became freed from grief, and taking Ashma's leave proceeded towards his house.

description: Conversation b-Janaka and Ashma as to how should a man act upon the accession and destruction of both kinsmen and wealth.
sn: तथा त्वमप्यच्युत मुञ्च शोर्क मुत्तिष्ठ शक्रोपम हर्षमेहि। क्षात्रेण धर्मेण मही जिता ते तां भुक्ष्व कुन्तीसुत मावमंस्था॥
en: O you of unfading glory, cast off your sorrow and rise up. You are equal to Shakra himself. Cheer up your heart. The Earth has been conquered by you by means of Kshatriya duties. Enjoy here, O son of Kunti, and do not disobey my words?"

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अव्याहरति राजेन्द्रे धर्मपुत्रे युधिष्ठिरे। गुडाकेशो हृषीकेशमभ्यभाषत पाण्डवः॥
en: "That highest of kings, viz., Yudhishthira the son of Dharma, still rentained silent and Pandu's son Arjuna addressed Krishna and spoke as follows.
