description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अर्जुन उवाच ज्ञातिशोकाभिसंतप्तो धर्मपुत्रः परंतपः। एष शोकार्णवे मग्नस्तमाश्वासय माधव॥
en: Arjuna said 'This scorcher of foes, viz., Dharma's son, is grieving for his slain kinsmen. Solace him, O Madhava.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सर्वे स्म ते संशयिताः पुनरेव जनार्दन। अस्य शोकं महाबाहो प्रणाशयितुमर्हसि॥
en: Again, O Janardana, all of us have fallen into great calamity, You should, O mightyarmed one, remove his sorrow.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु गोविन्दो विजयेन महात्मना। पर्यवर्तत राजानं पुण्डरीकेक्षणोऽच्युतः॥
en: Vaishampayana continued : Thus accosted by the great Arjuna, the lotus-eyed Govinda of unfading glory looked towards the king.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अनतिक्रमणीयो हि धर्मराजस्य केशवः। बाल्यात् प्रभृति गोविन्दः प्रीत्या चाभ्यधिकोऽर्जुनात्॥
en: Yudhishthira could never disobey Keshava. From his infancy Govinda was dearer to Yudhishthira than Arjuna himself.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सम्प्रगृह्य महाबाहुर्भुजं चन्दनभूषितम्। शैलस्तम्भोपमं शौरिरुवाचाभिविनोदयन्॥
en: Taking up the king's hand bedecked with sandal-paste and looking like a column of marble, the mighty-armed Krishna began to speak, cheering up all his hearers.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: शुशुभे वदनं तस्य सुदंष्ट्र चारुलोचनम्। व्याकोशमिव विस्पष्टं पद्मं सूर्य इवोदिते॥
en: His face, adorned with beautiful teeth and eyes, shone like a full-blown lotus at sunrise.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: वासुदेव उवाच मा कृथाः पुरुषव्याघ्र शोकं त्वं गात्रशोषप न हि ते सुलभा भूयो ये हतास्मिन् रणाजिरे॥
en: Vasudeva said Do not, O foremost of men, so grieve as will reduce your body. They who have been killed in this battle will by no mean be got back.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स्वपलब्धा यथा लाभा वितथाः प्रतिबोधने। एवं ते क्षत्रिया राजन् ये व्यतीता महारणे॥
en: Those Kshatriyas, O king, that have been killed in this great battle, are like objects that one gets in his dreams and which disappear when one awakes.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सर्वेऽप्यभिमुखाः शूरा विजिता रणशोभिन:। नैषां कश्चित् पृष्ठतो वा पलायन् वापि पातितः॥
en: All of them were heroes and ornaments of the field. They were defeated while attacking their enemies. No one amongst them was killed with wounds on the back or while flying away.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सर्वेत्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मनः प्राणान् युद्ध्वा वीरा महामृधे। शस्त्रपूता दिवं प्राप्ता न ताञ्छोचितुमर्हसि॥
en: All of them, having fought with heroes in great battle and having thrown off their lifebreaths then, have, purified by weapons, proceeded to heaven. You should not grieve for them.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: क्षत्रधर्मरताः शूरा वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः। प्राप्ता वीरगतिं पुण्यां तान् न शोचितुमर्हसि॥ मृतान् महानुभावांस्त्वं श्रुत्वैव पृथिवीपतीन्।
en: Always following the duties of Kshatriyas, endued with courage, well read in the Vedas and their branches, all of them have attained to that blissful region which is obtainable by heroes. You should not grieve for them after hearing those high-souled kings of Earth, of ancient days, that departed from this world.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्॥ संजयं पुत्रशोकार्तं यथायं नारदोऽब्रवीत्।
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse of Narada before Srinjaya when the latter was greatly stricken with grief on account of the death of his sons.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: नारद उवाच सुखदुःखैरहं त्वं च प्रजाः सर्वाश्च संजय॥ अविमुक्ता मरिष्यामस्तत्र का परिदेवना।
en: Narada said Subject to happiness and misery myself, yourself, and all creatures, Srinjaya, shall have to die. What cause then is there for grief.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: महाभाग्यं पुरा राज्ञां कीर्त्यमानं मया शृणु॥ गच्छावधानं नृपते ततो दुःखं प्रहास्यसि।
en: Listen to me as I describe the great bliss of (some) ancient kings. Hear me with rapt attention. You will then O king, cast off your sorrow.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: मृतान् महानुभावांस्त्वं श्रुत्वैव पृथिवीपतीन्॥ शममानय संतापं शृणु विस्तरशश्च मे।
en: Listening to the story of those high souled kings, lessen your sorrow. Hear me as I recite fully their stories to you.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: क्रूरग्रहाभिशमनमायुर्वर्धनमुत्तमम्॥ अग्रिमाणां क्षितिभुजामुपादानं मनोहरम्।
en: By listening to the charming and delightful history of those kings of ancient times, unfavourable stars may be propitiated and longevity may be increased.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: आविक्षितं मरुत्तं च मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम॥ यस्य सेन्द्राः सवरुणा बृहस्पतिपुरोगमाः। देवा विश्वसृजो राज्ञो यज्ञमीयुर्महात्मनः॥ यः स्पर्धयायजच्छकं देवराजं पुरंदरम्।
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that there was a king of the name of Marutta who was the son of Avikshit. He also met with death. The gods with Indra and Varuna and Brihaspati at their head came to the sacrifice, called Vishvasrij, celebrated by that great king. Challenging Shakra the king of the gods, that king defeated him in battle.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: शक्रप्रियैषी यं विद्वान् प्रत्याचष्ट बृहस्पतिः॥ संवर्तो याजयामास यवीयान् स बृहस्पतेः।
en: To do Indra a good turn the learned Brihaspati refused to officiate at Marutta's sacrifice. Thereupon Samvarta, the younger brother of Brihaspati, complied with the king's request.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यस्मिन् प्रशासति महीं नृपतौ राजसत्तम। अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी विबभौ चैत्यमालिनी॥
en: During the reign of that king, O best of kings, Earth produced crops without being tilled and was adorned with various kinds of ornaments.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: आविक्षितस्य वै सत्रे विश्वेदेवाः सभासदः। मरुतः परिवेशरः साध्याश्चासन् महात्मनः॥
en: In the sacrifice of that king, the Vishvedevas were the courtiers, the Maruts acted as distributors (of food and presents) and the great Saddhyas were also present.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: मरुद्गणा मरुत्तस्य यत् सोममपिबंस्ततः। देवान् मनुष्यान् गन्धर्वानत्यरिच्यन्त दक्षिणाः॥
en: In that sacrifice of Marutta, the Maruts drank Soma. The presents of the king excelled (in value) those ever made by the gods, the Gandharvas and men.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When even that king, O Srinjaya who was superior to you in religious merit, knowledge, renunciation, and wealth, and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सुहोत्रं चैवातिथिनं मृतं संजय शुश्रुम। यस्मिन् हिरण्यं ववृषे मघवा परिवत्सरम्॥
en: There was another king of the name of Suhotra the son of Atithi. We hear, O Srinjaya, that even he met with death. During his reign Indra showered gold for one whole year upon his kingdom.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सत्यनामा वसुमती यं प्राप्यासीज्जनाधिपम्। हिरण्यमवहन् नद्यस्तस्मिञ्जनपदेश्वरे॥ कूर्मान् कर्कटकान् नक्रान् मकराञ्छिशुकानपि। नदीष्वपातयद् राजन् मघवा लोकपूजितः॥
en: Obtaining that king for her master the Earth became, in sooth, Vasumati (endued with wealth). The rivers, during the administration of that king, bore golden tortoises, crabs, alligators, sharks, and porpoises, for the worshipful Indra, O king had showered these upon them.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: हिरण्यान् पातितान् दृष्ट्वा मत्स्यान् मकरकच्छपान्। सहस्रशोऽथ शतशस्ततोऽस्मयदथोऽतिथिः॥
en: Seeing those innumerable golden fishes and sharks and tortoises, Atithi's son was filled with wonder.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: तद्धिरण्यमपर्यन्तमावृतं कुरुजाङ्गले। ईजानो वितते यज्ञे ब्राह्मणेभ्य: समार्पयत्॥
en: Collecting that vast wealth of gold that covered the Earth, Suhotra celebrated a sacrifice at Kurujangala and distributed it amongst the Brahmanas.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When that king, O Srinjaya, who surpassed you in the four attributes of religious, merit, knowledge, renunciation, and wealth, and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अदक्षिणमयज्वानं श्वैत्य संशाम्य मा शुचः। अङ्गं बृहद्रथं चैव मृतं संजय शुश्रुम॥
en: Your son never celebrated a sacrifice and never made presents. Knowing this, console your mind and do not grieve. We hear also, O Srinjaya, that Brihadratha the king of the Angas, met with death.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यः सहस्रं सहस्राणां श्वेतानश्वानवासृजत्। सहस्रं च सहस्राणां कन्या हेमपरिष्कृतः॥ ईजानो वितते यज्ञे दक्षिणामत्यकालयत्।
en: He gave away a hundred thousand horses. He gave away as presents also a hundred thousand maidens, adorned with golden ornaments in a sacrifice he celebrated.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यः सहस्रं सहस्राणां गजानां पद्ममालिनाम्॥ ईजानो वितते यज्ञे दक्षिणामत्यकालयत्। शतं शतसहस्राणि वृषाणां हेममालिनाम्॥ गवां सहस्रानुचरं दक्षिणामत्यकालयत्। अङ्गस्य यजमानस्य तदा विष्णुपदे गिरौ॥ अमाद्यदिन्द्रः सोमेन दक्षिणाभिर्द्विजातयः। यस्य चक्षेषु राजेन्द्र शतसंख्येषु वै पुरा॥ देवान् मनुष्यान् गन्धर्वानत्यरिच्यन्त दक्षिणाः। न जातो जनिता नान्यः पुमान् यः सम्प्रदास्यति॥ यदङ्गः प्रददौ वित्तं सोमसंस्थासु सप्तसु।
en: He gave away as presents a hundred thousand elephants also of the best breed in another sacrifice celebrated by him. He gave away as presents a hundred millions also of bulls adorned with golden chains, with thousands of kine while the king of Anga performed his sacrifice by the hill called Vishnupada, Indra became intoxicated with the Soma he drank, and the Brahmanas with the presents they obtained. In the hundreds of sacrifices, o monarch, which this king performed of old, the sacrificial presents far surpassed those ever made by the gods, the Gandharvas, and men, No other man was born, or will ever be born, that gave or will give away so much wealth as was distributed by the king of the Angas in the seven sacrifices he celebrated in which Soma juice was given.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥ पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः।
en: When O Srinjaya, this Brihadratha even, who was your superior in the four attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: शिबिमौशीनरं चैव मृतं सुंजय शुश्रुम॥ य इमां पृथिवीं सर्वां चर्मवत्समवेश्यत्।
en: We hear also, O Srinjaya, that Shivi the son of Ushinara, met with death. That king governed the entire Earth as one holds, the leathern shield in his hand.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: महता रथघोषेण पृथिवीमनुनादयन्॥ एकच्छत्रां महीं चक्रे जैत्रेणैकरथेन यः।
en: Riding on a single car, which was crowned with success in every battle, king Shivi caused the whole Earth to resound with the rattle of his wheels and brought all kings under subjection.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यावदस्य गवाश्वं स्यादारण्यैः पशुभिः सह॥ तावतीः प्रददौ गाः स शिबिरौशीनरोऽध्वरे।
en: Ushinara's son Shibi distributed, in a sacrifice, all the kine and horses he had, both domestic and wild.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: न वोढारं धुरं तस्य कश्चिन्मेने प्रजापतिः॥ न भूतं न भविष्यं च सर्वराजसु संजय। अन्यत्रौशीनराच्छैब्याद् राजर्षेरिन्द्रविक्रमात्॥ अदक्षिणमयज्वानं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः।
en: Brahma himself thought that no one amongst the kings of the past or the future had or could have borne the burden, O Srinjaya, the Ushinara's son Shibi, that best of kings and that most powerful hero, equal to that of Indra himself bore. Do not, therefore, grieve for your son who never celebrated any sacrifice nor made any present.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय, चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: Indeed, O Srinjaya, when Shivi, who was far superior to your in four attributes and who was purer than your son met with death, do not grieve for your son, who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: भरतं चैव दौष्यन्तिं मृतं संजय शुश्रुमा शाकुन्तलं महात्मानं भूरिद्रविणसंचयम्॥
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that the great Bharata also the son of Dushyanta and Shakuntala, who had a vast and well-replenished treasury met with death.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यो बद्ध्वा त्रिशतं चाश्वान् देवेभ्यो यमुनामनु। सरस्वती विंशतिं च गङ्गामनु चतुर्दश॥ अश्वमेधसहस्रेण राजसूयशतेन च। इष्टवान् स महातेजा दौष्यन्तिर्भरतः पुरा॥
en: Dedicating three hundred horses to the gods on the banks of Yamuna, twenty on the banks of Sarasvati, and fourteen on the banks of Ganga, that highly energetic king, in days of old, (celebrated this order) a thousand Horsesacrifices and a hundred Rajasuyas. In days of yore, effulgent Bharata, the son of Dushyanta celebrated sacrifices.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: भरतस्य महत् कर्म सर्वराजसु पार्थिवाः। स्वं मर्त्या इव बाहुभ्यां नानुगन्तुमशक्नुवन्॥
en: No one amongst the kings of the Earth can imitate the great deeds of Bharata, as on man can, by the power of his arms rise up into the sky.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: परं सहस्राद् यो बद्धान् हयान् वेदीवितत्य च। सहस्रं यत्र पद्यानां कण्वाय भरतो ददौ॥
en: Erecting numerous sacrificial altars, he presented numberless horses and immense riches to the sage Kanva.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When even be, O Srinjaya, who was far superior to you in the four attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: रामं दाशरथिं चैव मृतं संजय शुश्रुम। योऽन्वकम्पत वै नित्यं प्रजाः पुत्रानिवौरसान्॥
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that Rama also, the son of Dasharatha, met with death. He always treated his subjects like his own begotten sons.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: विधवा यस्य विषये नानाथा: काश्चनाभवन्। सदैवासीत् पितृसमो रामो राज्यं यदन्वशात्॥
en: In his kingdom there were no widows and none that was helpless. Indeed, Rama while governing his kingdom always followed his father Dasharatha.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: कालवर्षी च पर्जन्यः सस्यानि समपादयत्। नित्यं सुभिक्षमेवासीद् रामे राज्यं प्रशासति॥
en: The clouds, pouring rain in season, caused the crops to grow profusely. During his regime, food was always abundant in his kingdom.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: प्राणिनो नाप्सु मज्जन्ति नान्यथा पावकोऽदहत्। रुजाभयं न तत्रासीद् रामे राज्यं प्रशासति॥
en: No death occurred by drowning or by fire. As long as Rama ruled it, there was no fear in his kingdom of any ailment.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: आसन् वर्षसहस्त्रिण्यस्तथा वर्षसहस्रकाः। अरोगा: सर्वसिद्धार्था रामे राज्यं प्रशासति॥
en: Every man lived for a thousand years, and every man was fortunate enough to have a thousand children. During Rama's reign, all men enjoyed health and obtained the fruition of their wishes.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: नान्योऽन्येन विवादोऽभूत् स्त्रीणामपि कुतो नृणाम्। धर्मनित्याः प्रजाश्चासन् रामे राज्यं प्रशासति॥
en: Even the women did not quarrel with one another, what to speak of men? During his reign his subjects were always devoted to virtue.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: संतुष्टाः सर्वसिद्धार्था निर्भयाः स्वैरचारिणः। नराः सत्यव्रताश्चासन् रामे राज्यं प्रशासति॥
en: During Rama's regime all men contented, obtained the fruition of their desire, and were fearless, free, and truthful.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: नित्यपुष्पफलाश्चैव पादपा निरुपद्रवाः। सर्वा द्रोणदुघा गावो रामे राज्यं प्रशासति॥
en: The trees always bore flowers and fruits and suffered form no accidents. Every cow gave milk filling a drona-full milk.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चतुर्दशवर्षाणि वने प्रोष्य महातपाः। दशाश्वमेधान् जारूथ्यानाजहार निरर्गलान्॥
en: Having lived for fourteen years in that forest practising severe penances, Rama were celebrated ten Horse-sacrifices to which the freest access was given to all.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: युवा श्यामो लोहिताक्षो मातङ्ग इव यूथपः। आजानुबाहुः सुमुखः सिंहस्कन्धो महाभुजः॥
en: Youthful and having a dark complexion, and red eyes, he looked like the leader of an elephantine herd. With arms extending down to his knees and of beautiful face, his shoulders were like those of a lion and the power of his arms was great.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च। अयोध्याधिपतिर्भूत्वा रामो राज्यमकारयत्॥
en: Seated on the throne of Ayodhya, he ruled for ten thousand and ten hundred years.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When he, O Srinjaya, who was superior to you in the four principal accomplishments and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: भगीरथं च राजानं मृतं संजय शुश्रुम। यस्येन्द्रो वितते यज्ञे सोमं पीत्वा मदोत्कटः॥ असुराणां सहस्राणि बहूनि सुरसत्तमः। अजयद् बाहुवीर्येण भगवान् पाकशासनः॥
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that king Bhagiratha also died. In one of the sacrifices of that king inebriate with drinking the Soma juice, Indra, the worshipful chastiser of Paka and the king of the gods, defeated by the strength of his arms, many thousands of Asuras.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यः सहस्रं सहस्राणां कन्या हेमविभूषिताः। ईजानो वितते यज्ञे दक्षिणामत्यकालयत्॥
en: King Bhagiratha, in one of the sacrifices he celebrated, gave away a million of maidens bedecked with ornaments of gold.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सर्वा रथगताः कन्या रथाः सर्वे चतुर्युजः। शतं शतं रथे नागाः पद्मिनो हेममालिनः॥
en: Each of those maidens sat upon a car to each of which were yoked four horses. With each car were a hundred elephants, all of the best breed and adorned with golden trappings. to

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सहस्रमश्वा एकैकं हस्तिनं पृष्ठतोऽन्वयुः। गवां सहस्रमश्वेऽश्वे सहस्रं गव्यजाविकम्॥
en: Behind each elephant were a thousand horses, and behind each horse a thousand kine, and behind each cow a thousand goats and sheep.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: उपह्वरे निवसतो यस्याङ्के निषसाद ह। गङ्गा भागीरथी तस्मादुर्वशी चाभवत् पुरा॥
en: Ganga, named (from before) Bhagirathi sat upon the lap of this king living near (her stream), and therefore, passed by the name of Urvashi.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: भूरिदक्षिणमिक्ष्वाकुं यजमानं भगीरथम्। त्रिलोकपथगा गङ्गा दुहितृत्वमुपेयुषी॥
en: The Ganga who had three courses had agreed to be the daughter of Bhagiratha of Ikshvaku's race, race, who always celebrated sacrifices with enough presents the Brahmanas.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When he, O Srinjaya, who was superior to you in respect of the four principle attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: दिलीपं च महात्मानं मृतं संजय शुश्रुम। यस्य कर्माणि भूरीणि कथयन्ति द्विजातयः॥
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that the great Dilipa also met with death. The Brahmanas take pleasure in recounting his innumerable deeds.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: य इमां वसुसम्पूर्णां वसुधां वसुधाधिपः। ददौ तस्मिन् महायज्ञे ब्राह्मणेभ्यः समाहितः॥
en: In one of his great sacrifices that king, gave away with full heart the entire Earth, abounding with wealth, to the Brahmanas.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यस्येह यजमानस्य यज्ञे यज्ञे पुरोहितः। सहस्रं वारणान् हैमान् दक्षिणामत्यकालयत्॥
en: In each sacrifice celebrated by him, the chief priest received as sacrificial fee a thousand elephants made of gold. seven was

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यस्य यज्ञे महानासीद् यूपः श्रीमान् हिरण्मयः। तं देवाः कर्म कुर्वाणाः शक्रज्येष्ठा उपाश्रयन्॥
en: In one of his sacrifices, the stake was made of gold and and looked highly beautiful. Performing the duties assigned to them, the gods having Shakra for their king, used to seek refuge with that king.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: चषाले यस्य सौवर्णे तस्मिन् यूपे हिरण्मये। ननृतुर्देवगन्धर्वाः षट् सहस्राणि सप्तधा॥ अवादयत् तत्र वीणां मध्ये विश्वावसुः स्वयम्। सर्वभूतान्यमन्यन्त मम वादयतीत्ययम्॥
en: Upon that highly effulgent golden stake decked with a ring, six thousand gods and Gandharvas danced in joy, and Vishvavasu himself, in their midst played on his Vina the notes according to the rules of concordance. Such the nature of Vishvavasu's music that every creature, wherever he might be, thought that the great Gandharva was playing to him alone.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: एतद् राज्ञो दिलीपस्य राजानो नानुचक्रिरे। यस्येभा हेमसंछन्नाः पथि मत्ताः स्म शेरते॥
en: No other king could imitate the deeds of king Dilipa. The elephants of that king, intoxicated and adorned with golden trappings used to lie down on the roads.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: राजानं शतधन्वानं दिलीपं सत्यवादिनम्। येऽपश्यन् सुमहात्मानं तेऽपि स्वर्गजितो नराः॥
en: Those men went to heaven who could obtain a glance even of the great king Dwilipa who was ever truthful in speech and whose bow could bear a hundred enemies powerful like a hundred Anantas.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: त्रयः शब्दा न जीर्यन्ते दिलीपस्य निवेशने। स्वाध्यायघोषो ज्याघोषो दीयतामिति वै त्रयः॥
en: Three sounds never ceased in Dwilipa's mansion, viz., the sound of Vedic recitations, the twang of bows, and cries of Let it be given.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When he, O Srinjaya, who was superior to you in the four principal attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: मान्धातारं यौवनाश्वं मृतं संजय शुश्रुम। यं देवा मरुतो गर्भ पितुः पार्थादपाहरन्॥
en: Yuvanashva's son Mandhatri also, O Srinjaya, we have heard, met with death. The celestials named Maruts took out that child from his father's stomach through one of its sides.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: समृद्धो युवनाश्वस्य जठरे यो महात्मनः। पृषदाज्योद्भवः श्रीमास्त्रिलोकविजयी नृपः॥
en: Born from a quantity of clarified butter that had been purified by Mantras Mandhatri was born in the stomach of the great Yuvanashva. Highly prosperous, king Mandhatri vanquished the three worlds.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यं दृष्ट्वा पितुरुत्सङ्गे शयानं देवरूपिणम्। अन्योन्यमब्रुवन् देवाः कमयं धास्यतीति वै॥
en: Seeing that child of celestial beauty lying on the lap of his father, the gods asked one another,-whose breasts shall this child suck?

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: मामेव धास्यतीत्येवमिन्द्रोऽथाभ्युपपद्यत। मान्धातेति ततस्तस्य नाम तस्य नाम चक्रे शतक्रतुः॥
en: Then Indra approached him,, saying,-He shall suck me.-From this incident the king of the deities named the child Mandhatri.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: ततस्तु पयसो धारां पुष्टिहेतोर्महात्मनः। तस्यास्ये यौवनाश्वस्य पाणिरिन्द्रस्य चास्रवत्॥
en: To give nourishment to that high-souled child of Yuvanashva, the finger of Indra, placed in his mouth, began to give a jet of milk.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: तं पिबन् पाणिमिन्द्रस्य शतमह्ना व्यवर्धत। स आसीद् द्वादशसमो द्वादशाहेन पार्थिवः॥
en: Sucking Indra's finger, he grew up in a hundred days. In twelve days he looked like a boy of twelve years,

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: तमिमं पृथिवी सर्वा एकाह्ना समपद्यता धर्मात्मानं महात्मानं शूरमिन्द्रसमं युधि॥
en: The whole Earth in one day was subjugated by that high-souled and virtuous and brave king who was like Indra himself in prowess.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यश्चाङ्गारं तु नृपतिं मरुत्तमसितं गयम्। अङ्ग बृहद्रथं चैव मान्धाता समरेऽजयत्॥
en: He defeated king Angara, Marutta, Asita, Gaya and Vrihadratha the king of the Angas.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यौवनाश्वो यदाङ्गारं समरे प्रत्ययुध्यत। विस्फारैर्धनुषो देवा द्यौरभेदीति मेनिरे॥
en: When Yuvanashva's son fought in battle with Angara, the gods thought that the sky was breaking with the twang of his bow.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यत्र सूर्य उदेति स्म यत्र च प्रतितिष्ठति। सर्वं तद् यौवनाश्वस्य मान्धातुः क्षेत्रमुच्यते॥
en: The whole Earth from the point from which the Sun rises to where he sets is said to be the field of Mandhatri.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अश्वमेधशतेनेष्ट्वा राजसूयशतेन च। अददाद् रोहितान् मत्स्यान् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो विशाम्पते॥
en: Having celebrated Horse-sacrifices and a hundred Rajasuyas, he gave to the Brahmanas many Rohita fishes.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: हैरण्यान् योजनोत्सेधानायतान् दशयोजनम्। अतिरिक्तान् द्विजातिभ्यो व्यभजस्त्वितरे जनाः॥
en: Those fishes were each ten Yojanas in length and one in breadth. The residue after gratifying the Brahmanas, were divided amongst themselves by the other classes.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When he, O Srinjaya, who was superior to you in respect of the four principal attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: ययातिं नाहुषं चैव मृतं संजय शुश्रुम। य इमां पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां विजित्य सहसागराम्॥ शम्यापातेनाभ्यतीयाद् वेदीभिश्चित्रयन् महीम्। ईजानः क्रतुभिर्मुख्यैः पर्यगच्छद् वसुन्धराम्॥
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that Yayati the son of Nahusha also met with death. Having brought under his sway the whole world with its seas, he journeyed through it, adorning it with various sacrificial altars the interstices between which were measured by throws of a heavy piece of wood. Indeed, he reached the very bank of the sea as he went on celebrating great sacrifices.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: दृष्ट्वा ऋतुसहस्रेण वाजपेयशतेन च। तर्पयामास विप्रेन्द्रांस्त्रिभिः काञ्चनपर्वतैः॥
en: Having celebrated a thousand sacrifices and a hundred Vajapeyas, he pleased the lcading Brahmanas with three mountains of gold.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: व्यूढेनासुरयुद्धेन हत्वा दैतेयदानवान्। व्यभजत् पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां ययातिनहुषात्मजः॥
en: Having killed many Daityas and Danavas duly in battle, Nahusha's son Yayati divided the whole Earth (among his children).

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अन्त्येषु पुत्रान् निक्षिप्य यदुद्रुह्युपुरोगमान्। पूरुं राज्येऽभिषिच्याथ सदारः प्राविशद् वनम्॥
en: At last discarding his other sons headed by Yadu and Druhyu, he installed (his youngest son) Puru on his throne and then returned to the forest accompanied by his wife.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When he, O Srinjaya, who was superior to you in the four principal attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अम्बरीषं च नाभागं मृतं संजय शुश्रुम। य प्रजा वव्रिरे पुण्यं गोप्तारं नृपसत्तमम्॥
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that Amvarisha also, the son of Nabhaga, met with death. That protector (of the world) and greatest of kings was considered by his subjects as the virtue incarnate.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यः सहस्रं सहस्राणां राज्ञामयुतयाजिनाम्। ईजानो वितते यज्ञे ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सुसंहितः॥
en: That king, in one of his sacrifices dedicated to the Brahmanas, for serving them, a million of kings who had themselves celebrated thousands of sacrifices each.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: नैतत् पूर्वे जनाचक्रुर्न करिष्यन्ति चापरे। इत्यम्बरीषं नाभागिमन्वमोदन्त दक्षिणाः॥
en: Pious men praised Ambarisha the son of Nabhaga, saying that such deeds had never been done before nor would be done in the future.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: शतं राजसहस्राणि शतं राजशतानि च। सर्वेऽश्वमेधैरोजानास्तेऽन्वयुदक्षिणायनम्॥
en: Those hundreds upon hundreds and thousands upon thousands of kings became (through Amvarisha's merits) crowned with the fruits of the Horse-sacrifice, and followed their chief by the Southern path to heaven).

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When he, O Srinjaya, who was superior to you in the four principal attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: शशबिन्दुं चैत्ररथं मृतं शुश्रुम सुंजय। यस्य भार्यासहस्राणां शतमासीन्महात्मनः॥ सहस्रं तु सहस्राणां यस्यासशाशबिन्दवाः। हिरण्यकवचाः सर्वे सर्वे चोत्तमधन्विनः॥
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that Shashabindu also, the son of Chitraratha, met with death. The great king had a hundred thousand wives, and a million of sons. All of them used to wear golden coats of mail and all of them were flowers of bowmen.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: शतं कन्या राजपुत्रमेकैकं पृथगन्वयुः। कन्यां कन्यां शतं नागा नागं नागं शतं रथाः॥
en: Each of those princes married a hundred princesses, and each princess brought a hundred elephants. With each each of those elephants were a hundred cars.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: रथे रथे शतं चाश्वा देशजा हेममालिनः। अश्वे अश्वे शतं गावो गवां तद्वदजाविकम्॥
en: With each car were a hundred horses, all of good breed and all adorned with golden trappings. With each horse were a hundred kine, and with each cow were a hundred sheep and goats.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: एतद् धनमपर्यन्तमश्वमेधे महामखे। शशबिन्दुर्महाराज ब्राह्मणेभ्यः समार्पयत्॥
en: The immense wealth, O King, Sashavindu distributed in a Horse-sacrifice amongst the Brahmanas.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्मार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When he, O Srinjaya, who was superior to you in the four principal attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: गयं चामूर्तरयसं मृतं शुश्रुम संजय। यः स वर्षशतं राजा हुतशिष्टाशनोऽभवत्॥
en: We hear, O Stinjaya, that Gaya also, the son of Amurtharayas, met with death. For a hundred years, that king lived upon the residue of sacrificial food.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यस्मै वह्निर्वरं प्रादात् ततो ववे वरान् गयः। ददतो योऽक्षयं वित्तं धर्मे श्रद्धा च वर्धताम्॥
en: (Pleased with his devotion) Agni offered him boons. The boons prayed for by Gaya were,-May not wealth suffer extinction even if I give ceaselessly. Let my respect virtue exist for ever.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: मनो मे रमतां सत्ये त्वत्प्रसादाद्भुताशन। लेभे च कामांस्तान् सर्वान् पावकादिति नः श्रुतम्॥११३
en: Let my heart ever love Truth, through your 'grace, O eater of sacrificial libations.-It has been heard by us that king Gaya secured all those wishes from Agni.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: दशैश्च पूर्णमासैश्च चातुर्मास्यैः पुनः पुनः। अयजद्धयमेधेन सहस्रं परिवत्सरान्॥
en: On days of the new moon, on those of the full moon, and on every fourth month, for a thousand years, Gaya repeatedly celebrated the Horse-sacrifice.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: शतं गवां सहस्राणि शतमश्वतराणि च। उत्थायोत्थाय वै प्रादात् सहस्रं परिवत्सरान्॥
en: Rising (at the termination of every sacrifice) he distributed a hundred thousand kine and hundreds of mules during this time.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: तर्पयामास सोमेन देवान् वित्तैर्द्विजानपि। पितृन् स्वधाभिः कामैश्च स्त्रियः स पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: That foremost of men pleased the gods with Soma, the Brahmanas, with wealth, the Pitris with Svadha, and the women with the satisfaction of all their desires.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सौवर्णी पृथिवीं कृत्वा दशव्यामां द्विरायताम्। 'दक्षिणामददद् राजा वाजिमेधे महाक्रतौ॥
en: In this great Horse-sacrifice, king Gaya had a golden ground made, measuring a hundred cubits in length and fifty in breadth, and gave it away as the sacrificial fee.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यावत्यः सिकता राजन् गङ्गायां पुरुषर्षभ। तावतीरेव गाः प्रादादामूर्तरयसो गयः॥
en: That foremost of men viz., Gaya the son Amurtarayas, distributed as many kine as there are sand grains, O king in the river Ganga.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When he, O Srinjaya, who was superior to you in the four principal attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: रन्तिदेवं च सांकृत्यं मृतं संजय शुश्रुम। सम्यगाराध्य यः शक्राद् वरं लेभे महातपाः॥ अन्नं च नो बहु भवेदतिथींच लभेमहि। श्रद्धा च नो मा व्यगमन्मा च याचिष्म कंचन॥
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that Sankriti's son Rantideva also met with death. Having practised the severest of penances and worshipped him with great reverence, he obtained these boons from Shakra, having solicited them, saying,-Let us have profuse good and innumerable guests! Let not my faith suffer any deterioration, and let us not have to beg anything of any person!

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: उपातिष्ठन्त पशवः स्वयं तं संशितव्रतम्। ग्राम्यारण्या महात्मानं रन्तिदेवं यशस्विनम्॥
en: The animals both domestic and wild, killed in his sacrifice, used to come to him, viz., the great Rantideva of rigid vows and great fame, of their own accord.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: महानदी चर्मराशेरुत्क्लेदात् ससृजे यतः। ततश्चर्मण्वतीत्येवं विख्याता सा महानदी॥
en: The secretions that came out of the skins of the animals produced a strong and celebrated river which till now passes by the name of Charmanvati.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ निष्कान् सदसि प्रतते नृपः। तुभ्यं निष्कं तुभ्यं निष्कमिति क्रोशन्ति वै द्विजाः।।१२४ सहस्रं तुभ्यमित्युक्त्वा ब्राह्मणान् सम्प्रपद्यते।
en: King Rantideva used to make presents to the. When the king said,-To you I give a hundred Nishkas! To you I give a hundred Nishkas! To you I give a hundred-the Brahinanas raised a hue and cry of refusal.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अन्वाहार्योपकरणं द्रव्योपकरणं च यत्॥ घटाः पात्र्यः कटाहानि स्थाल्यश्च पिठराणि च। नासीत् किंचिदसौवर्णं रन्तिदेवस्य धीमतः॥
en: When, however, the king said-I give a thousand Nishkas--the gifts were all accepted. All the vessels and plates in Rantideva's inansion for carrying food and other articles, all the jugs and pots, the pans and plates and cups were made of gold.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सांकृते रन्तिदेवस्य यां रात्रिमवसन् गृहे। आलभ्यन्त शतं गावः सहस्राणि च विंशतिः॥
en: There where the guests used to live in Rantideva's palace twenty thousand and one hundred kine had to be killed.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: तत्र स्म सूदाः क्रोशन्ति सुमृण्मणिकुण्डलाः। सूपं भूयिष्ठमश्नीध्वं नाद्य भोज्यं यथा पुरा॥ स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: Yet even on such occasions, the cooks, adorned with ear-rings, used to say,-There is abundant juice. Eat as much as you wish, but we have not as much to-day of meat as on former occasions.-When he O Srinjaya, who was far superior to you in the four principal attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: सगरं च महात्मानं मृतं शुश्रुम सुंजय। ऐक्ष्वाकं पुरुषव्याघ्रमतिमानुषविक्रमम्॥
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that the high-souled Sagara also met with death. He was born in the family of Ikshvaku, a foremost of men, and of superhuman power.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि यं यान्तमनुजग्मिरे। नक्षत्रराजं वर्षान्ते व्यभ्रे ज्योतिर्गणा इव॥
en: Sixty-thousand sons used to follow him, like countless stars waiting upon the Moon, in the cloudless autumnal sky.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: एकच्छत्रा मही यस्य प्रतापादभवत् पुरा। योऽश्वमेधसहस्रेण तर्पयामास देवताः॥
en: He ruled the whole of this Earth. He gratified the gods by celebrating a thousand Horse-sacrifices.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: यः प्रादात् कनकस्तम्भं प्रासादं सर्वकाञ्चनम्। पूर्णं पद्मदलाक्षीणां स्त्रीणां शयनसंकुलम्॥ द्विजातिभ्योऽनुरूपेभ्य: कामांश्च विविधान् बहून्। यस्यादेशेन तद् वित्तं व्यभजन्त द्विजातयः॥
en: He gave away to deserving Brahmanas palatial edifices with columns of gold and (other parts) made entirely of that precious metal, abounding in rich beds and bevies of beautiful ladies having eyes like lotus-petals, and various other sorts of valuable objects. At his behest the Brahmanas divided those gifts among themselves.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: खानयामास यः कोपात् पृथिवीं सागराङ्किताम्। यस्य नाम्ना समुद्रश्च सागरत्वमुपागतः॥
en: Out of wrath that king made the Earth to be excavated, whereupon she came to have the ocean on her bosom, and, therefore, the ocean is called Sagara after his name.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When he, O Srinjaya, who was superior to you in the four principal attributes and who was purer than your son, met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: राजानं च पृथु वैन्यं मृतं शुश्रुम संजय। यमभ्यषिञ्चन् सम्भूय महारण्ये महर्षयः॥
en: We hear, O Srinjaya, that king Prithu also, the son of Vena met with death, the great Rishis, assembled together in the great forest, installed him in the sovereignty of the Earth.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: प्रथयिष्यति वै लोकान् पृथुरित्येव शब्दितः। क्षताद्यो वै त्रायतीति स तस्मात्क्षत्रियः स्मृतः।।१३८
en: And because it was expected that he would advance all mankind, he was, accordingly, called Prithu (the advancer). And because also he protected people from injuries (Kshatta), he was, therefore, styled of Kshatriya (protector from injuries).

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: पृथु वैन्यं प्रजा दृष्ट्वा रक्ताः स्मेति यदब्रुवन्। ततो राजेति नामास्य अनुरागादजायत॥
en: Seeing Prithu the son of Vena, all the creatures of the Earth, exclaimed,-We love him affectionately!-And for the loving attachment (to him of all creatures), he was called a Raja (one who gratifies all).

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी पुटके पुटके मधु। सर्वा द्रोणदुधा गावो वैन्यस्यासन् प्रशासतः॥
en: The Earth, during his regime produced crops without being tilled, every leaf of the trees bore honey, and every cow gave a jugful of milk.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अरोगाः सर्वसिद्धार्था मनुष्या अकुतोभयाः। यथाभिकाममवसन् क्षेत्रेषु च गृहेषु च॥
en: All men enjoyed health and all their wishes were fructified. They had no fear of any kind. They used to live, as they pleased, in fields or houses.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: आपस्तस्तम्भिरे चास्य समुद्रमभियास्यतः। सरितश्चानुदीर्यन्त ध्वजभङ्गश्च नाभवत्॥
en: When Prithu desired to cross the sea, the waters become solidified. The rivers also never rose when he had to cross them but remained perfectly calm. The standard on his car moved freely everywhere.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: हैरण्यांस्त्रिनलोत्सेधान् पर्वतानेकविंशतिम्। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ राजा योऽश्वमेधे महामखे॥
en: King Prithu, in one of his great Horsesacrifices, distributed amongst the Brahmanas one and twenty mountains of gold, each measuring twelve hundred cubits.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: स चेन्ममार संजय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरश्चैव मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः॥
en: When he, O Srinjaya, who was far superior to you in the four principal attributes and who was purer than your son met with death, do not grieve for your son who is dead.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: किं वा तूष्णीं ध्यायसे संजयत्वं न मे राजन् वाचमिमां शृणोषि। न चेन्मोघं विप्रलप्तं ममेदं पथ्यं मुमूर्षोरिव सुप्रयुक्तम्॥
en: What are you, O Srinjaya, thinking of silently? It seems, O king, that you do not pay heed to these words of mine. If you have not heard them, then this discourse of mine has been fruitless like medicine or diet to a person on the point of death.'

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: संजय उवाच शृणोमि ते नारद वाचमेनां विचित्रार्थी स्त्रजमिव पुण्यगन्धाम्। राजर्षीणां पुण्यकृतां महात्मनां कीर्त्या युक्तानां शोकनिर्णाशनार्थाम्॥
en: I am all attention, ONarada, to this discourse of yours, of excellent sense and perfumed like a garland of flowers,-this discourse regarding the conduct of great royal sages of meritorious deeds and great fame, that can surely remove grief.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: न ते मोघं विप्रलप्तं महर्षे दृष्ट्वैवाहं नारद त्वां विशोकः। शुश्रूषे ते वचनं ब्रह्मवादिन् न ते तृप्याम्यमृतस्येव पानात्॥
en: Your discourse, O great sage, has not been fruitless. I have been freed from sorrow at your very sight! Like one never satiated with drinking nectar, I am not satiated with your words.

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: अमोघदर्शिन् मम चेत् प्रसाद संतापदग्धस्य विभो प्रकुर्याः। सुतस्य सञ्जीवनमद्य मे स्यात् तव प्रसादात् सुतसङ्गमश्च॥
en: O you of true vision, If you, O lord, be inclined to show your grace towards this man burning for the death of his son, then that son, through your favour, is sure to be revived and to mix once more with me (in this life).

description: Krishna consoles the king. The discourse between Narada and Shanjaya.
sn: नारद उवाच यस्ते पुत्रो गमितोऽयं विजातः स्वर्णष्ठीवी यमदात् पर्वतस्ते। पुनस्तु ते पुत्रमहं ददामि हिरण्यनाभं वर्षसहस्त्रिणं च॥
en: Narada said: I will give back to you that son of yours named Suvarnashthivin, whom Parvata gave you and who has been deprived of life! Effulgent like gold, that child shall live a thousand years.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच स कथं काञ्चनष्ठीवी संजयस्य सुतोऽभवत्। पर्वतेन किमर्थं वा दत्तस्तेन ममार च॥
en: How did the son as Srinjaya become Suvarnashthivin? Why also did Parvata give Srinjaya that child? And why did he die?

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: यदा वर्षसहस्रायुस्तदा भवति मानवः। कथमप्राप्तकौमार: संजयस्य सुतो मृतः॥
en: When all those men lived for a thousand years, why did Srinjaya's son die in infancy?

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: उताहो नाममात्रं वै सुवर्णष्ठीविनोऽभवत्। कथं वा काञ्चनष्ठीवीत्येतदिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: Or, was he in name only Suvarnashthivin? How also did he come to be so! I wish to know all this?

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच अत्र ते वर्णयिष्यामि यथावृत्तं जनेश्वर। नारदः पर्वतश्चैव द्वावृषी लोकसत्तमौ॥
en: Krishna said 'I will recount, О king, the incidents as they took place. There are two Rishis foremost in the world, named Narada and Parvata.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: मातुलो भागिनेयश्च देवलोकादिहागतौ। विहर्तुकामौ सम्प्रीत्या मानुषेषु पुरा विभो॥ हवि:पवित्रभोज्येन देवभोज्येन चैव हि। नारदो मातुलश्चैव भागिनेयश्च पर्वतः॥
en: Narada is the maternal uncle and Parvata is his sister's son. With cheerful hearts, the uncle Narada and the nephew Parvata had in days of yore, O king, left the celestial region for a journey on Earth for eating clarified butter and rice.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: तावुभौ तपसोपेताववनीतलचारिणौ। भुञ्जानौमानुषान् भोगान् यथावत् पर्यधावताम्॥
en: Both of them endued with great ascetic merit, they wandered over the Earth living on food taken by human beings.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: प्रीतिमन्तौ मुदा युक्तौ समयं चैव चक्रतुः। यो भवेद्धदि संकल्पः शुभो वा यदि वाशुभः॥ अन्योन्यस्य स आख्येयो मृषा शापोऽन्यथा भवेत्।
en: Filled with joy and cherishing great affection for each other, they entered into an agreement that whatever wish, good or bad, would be entertained by one, should be disclosed to the other, but if one happens to act otherwise, he should be visited by the other's curse.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: तौ तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय महर्षी लोकपूजितौ॥ संजयं श्वैत्यमभ्येत्य राजानमिदमूचतुः।
en: Coming at that understanding, those two great Rishis, worshipped of all the worlds, repaired to King Srinjaya the son of Shitya and said to him?

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: आवां भवति वत्स्यावः कञ्चित् कालं हिताय ते॥ यथावत् पृथिवीपाल आवयोः प्रगुणीभव।
en: We two, for your well-being shall live with you for a few days. O lord of Earth, do you satisfy all our wants duly! The king, saying,-So be it, began to treat them hospitably.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: तथेति कृत्वा राजा तौ सत्कृत्योपचचार ह॥ ततः कदाचित्तौ राजा महात्मानौ तपोधनौ।
en: After some time one day, the king, filled with joy, introduced to those illustrious ascetics his most beautiful daughter, saying,-This my daughter will serve you both.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: अब्रवीत् परमप्रीतः सुतेयं वरवर्णिनी॥ एकैव मम कन्यैषा युवां परिचरिष्यसि। दर्शनीयानवद्याङ्गी शीलवृत्तसमाहिता॥ सुकुमारी कुमारी च पद्मकिञ्जल्कसुप्रभा। परमं सौम्य मित्युक्तं ताभ्यां राजा शशास ताम्॥ कन्ये विप्रावुपचर देववत् पितृवच्च ह।
en: Resembling in effulgence the filaments of the lotus, she is beautiful and of faultless limbs, accomplished and of charming manners, and is called Sukumari by name.-The Rishis replied, saying, Very well. Thereupon the king directed his daughter, telling her,-O child, serve those two Brahmanas as you would the gods or your father.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: सा तु कन्या तथेत्युक्त्वा पितरं धर्मचारिणी॥ यथानिदेशं राज्ञस्तौ सत्कृत्योपचचार ह।
en: The pious princess, saying,-So be it-began to serve them in obedience to her father's command.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: तस्यास्तेनोपचारेण रूपेणाप्रतिमेन च।॥ नारदं हृच्छयस्तूर्णं सहसैवाभ्यपद्यत।
en: Her dutiful services and her peerless beauty very soon created love in Narada's heart.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: ववृधे हि ततस्तस्य हृदि कामो महात्मनः॥ यथा शुक्लस्य पक्षस्य प्रवृत्तौ चन्द्रमाः शनैः।
en: That tender feeling began to grow in the heart of the great saint, like the moon gradually increasing in the light fortnight.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: न च तं भागिनेयाय पर्वताय महात्मने॥ शशंस हृच्छयं तीव्र व्रीडमानः स धर्मवित्।
en: The virtuous Narada, however, out of shame, could not give out that burning love to his sister's son the high-souled Parvata.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: तपसा चेगित्तैश्चैव पर्वतोऽथ बुबोध तम्॥ कामार्तं नारदं क्रुद्धः शशापैनं ततो भृशम्।
en: By his ascetic power, as also by signs, Parvata understood all. Excited with rage, the latter thereupon made up his mind to curse the love-stricken Narada.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: कृत्वा समयमव्यग्रो भवान् वै सहितो मया॥ यो भवेद्धदि संकल्पः शुभो वा यदि वाशुभः। अन्योन्यस्य स आख्येय इति तद् वै मृषा कृतम्॥ भवता वचनं ब्रह्मस्तस्मादेष शपाम्यहम्।
en: And he said, ‘Having of your own accord made an agreement with me that, whatever wish, good or bad, would be entertained by either of us should be disclosed to the other you have violated it! These were your own words. O Brahman! It is for this that I shall curse you.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: न हि कामं प्रवर्तन्तं भवानाचष्ट मे पुरा॥ सुकुमार्यां कुमार्यां ते तस्मादेष शपाम्यहम्।
en: You did not tell me before that your heart has been stricken with the beauty of the maiden Sukumari, I shall, therefore, curse you.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: ब्रह्मचारी गुरुर्यस्मात् तपस्वी ब्राह्मणश्च सन्॥ अकार्षीः समयभ्रंशमावाभ्यां यः कृतो मिथः।
en: You are a Brahmacharin. You are my preceptor. You are an ascetic and a Brahmana. Yet you have broken the agreement you had made with me.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: शप्स्ये तस्मात् सुसंक्रुद्धो भवन्तं तं निबोध मे॥ सुकुमारी च ते भार्या भविष्यति न संशयः।
en: Filled with anger I shall, for this, curse even you. Listen to me. This Sukumari shall, forsooth, become your wife.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: वानरं चैव ते रूपं विवाहात् प्रभृति प्रभो॥ संद्रक्ष्यन्ति नराश्चान्ये स्वरूपेण विनाकृतम्।
en: From the time of your marriage, however, O powerful one, both she and all men shall see you a monkey, for your real features having disappeared, you will appear like a monkey to all.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: स तद् वाक्यं तु विज्ञाय नारदः पर्वतं तथा॥ अशपत्तमपि क्रोधाद् भागिनेयं स मातुलः। तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण सत्येन च दमेन च।॥ युक्तोऽपि नित्यधर्मश्च न वै स्वर्गमवाप्स्यसि।
en: Hearing these words of his uncle Narada, excited with ire cursed his nephew Parvata in return, saying,—although you possess ascetic merit and Brahmacharya and truth and selfcontrol, and although you are ever devoted to virtue, yet you will not succeed in proceeding to heaven.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: तौ तु शप्त्वा भृशं क्रुद्धौ परस्परममर्षणौ॥ पतिजग्मतुरन्योन्यं क्रुद्धाविव गजोत्तमौ।
en: Filled with anger and feelings of vengeance, they thus cursed each other like a pair of infuriate elephants.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: पर्वतः पृथिवीं कृत्स्ना विचचार महामतिः॥ पूज्यमानो यथान्यायं तेजसा स्वेन भारत।
en: From that time the great Parvata began to wander over the Earth, respected as he deserved, O Bharata, for his own power.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: अथ तामलभत् कन्यां नारदः सुंजयात्मजाम्॥ धर्मेण विप्रप्रवरः सुकुमारीमनिन्दिताम्। सा तु कन्या यथाशापं नारदं तं ददर्श ह॥
en: Narada then, that best of Brahmanas, duly married Srinjaya's daughter, the faultless Sukumari.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: पाणिग्रहणमन्त्राणां नियोगादेव नारदम्। सुकुमारी च देवर्षि वानरप्रतिमाननम्॥ नैवावामन्यत तदा प्रीतिमत्येव चाभवत्।
en: The princess, however, saw Narada exactly as he had been. Indeed, just after the last of the wedding Mantras had been recited, Sukumari saw the celestial Rishi to have a face like that of a monkey. She, however, did not for that disregard her husband. On the other hand, she bestowed her love on him.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: उपतस्थे च भर्तारं न चान्यं मनसाप्यगात्॥ देवं मुनि वा यक्षं वा पतित्वे पतिवत्सला।
en: Indeed, that chaste princess, devoted herself entirely to her husband and did not in her heart even desire any one else among the gods, Munis and Yakshas for a husband.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: ततः कदाचिद् भगवान् पर्वतोऽनुचचार ह॥ वनं विरहितं किंचित् तत्रापश्यत् स नारदम्।
en: One day, as the illustrious Parvata, while wandering about entered a solitary forest, he saw Narada there.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: ततोऽभिवाद्य प्रोवाच नारदं पर्वतस्तदा॥ भवान् प्रसादं कुरुतात् स्वर्गादेशाय मे प्रभो।
en: Bowing to him, Parvata said,-Favour me by permitting me, O powerful one, to go to heaven.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: तमुवाचा ततो दृष्ट्वा पर्वतं नारदस्तथा॥ कृताञ्जलिमुपासीनं दीनं दीनतरः स्वयम्। त्वयाहं प्रथमं शप्तो वानरस्त्वं भविष्यसि॥ इत्युक्तेन मया पश्चाच्छप्तस्त्वमपि मत्सरात्। अधप्रभृति वै वासं स्वर्गे नावाप्स्यसीति ह॥ तव नैतद्धि विसदृशं पुत्रस्थाने हि मे भवान्। न्यवर्तयेतां तौ शापावन्योन्येन तदा मुनी॥
en: Seeing the cheerless Parvata kneeling before him with joined palms, Narada, himself more disspirited, said to him.-You had cursed me first, saying,-Be you a monkey!-After you had said so to me, I cursed you from anger, saying,-From this day you will not live in heaven. You should not have done so, since you are like a son to me.-The two saints then released each other from their mutual curses.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: श्रीसमृद्धं तदा दृष्ट्वा नारदं देवरूपिणम्। सुकुमारी प्रदुद्राव परपत्यभिशङ्कया।॥
en: Seeing her husband possessed of celestial forin shining with beauty, Sukumari fled from him taking him, to be somebody other than her husband.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: तां पर्वतस्ततो दृष्ट्वा प्रद्रवन्तीमनिन्दिताम्। अब्रवीत् तव भर्तेष नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥
en: Seeing the beautiful princess flying away from her husband, Parvata addressed her, saying,-He is your husband. Do not entertain any scruple.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: ऋषिः परमधर्मात्मा नारदो भगवान् प्रभुः। तवैवाभेद्यहृदयो मा तेऽभूदत्र संशयः॥
en: He is the illustrious and powerful Rishi Narada, that foremost of virtuous persons. He is your husband entirely devoted to you. Do not cherish any doubt.

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: सानुनीता बहुविधं पर्वतेन महात्मना। शापदोषं च तं भर्तुः श्रुत्वा प्रकृतिमागता॥ पर्वतोऽथ ययौ स्वर्ग नारदोऽभ्यगमद् गृहान्।
en: Assured in various ways be the great Parvata and informed also of the curse on her husband the princess regained the calmness of men. Then Parvata proceeded to heaven and Narada to his home.'

description: Account of the Rishis Narada dna Parvata.
sn: वासुदेव उवाच प्रत्यक्षकर्ता सर्वस्य नारदो भगवानृषिः। एष वक्ष्यति ते पृष्टो यथावृत्तं नरोत्तम॥
en: The illustrious Rishi Narada, who himself did so, is here, O best of men, asked by you, he will tell you everything that took place."

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो राजा पाण्डुसुतो नारदं प्रत्यभाषत। भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि सुवर्णष्ठीविसम्भवम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: The royal son of Pandu then addressed Narada, saying,-'O holy one, I wish to hear of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु स मुनिर्धर्मराजेन नारदः। आचचक्षे यथावृत्तं सुवर्णष्ठीविनं प्रति॥
en: Thus accosted by king Yudhishthira the sage Narada began to describe to him all that had taken place about that child who passed golden excreta.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: नारद उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथायं केशवोऽब्रवीत्। कार्यस्यास्य तु यच्छेषं तत् ते वक्ष्यामि पृच्छतः॥
en: Narada said 'It is so, O you of mighty arms, as Keshava here has said, asked by you I shall now recite the remaining portion of this story.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: अहं च पर्वतश्चैव स्वस्त्रीयो मे महामुनिः। वस्तुकामावभिगतौ संजयं जयतां वरम्॥
en: Myself, and my sister's son, the great ascetic Parvata, once came to Srinjaya, that foremost of all victorious kings, for living with him.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: तत्रावां पूजितौ तेन विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा। सर्वकामैः सुविहितौ निवसावोऽस्य वेश्मनि॥
en: Honoured duly by him who gratified every wish of ours, we lived in his palace.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: व्यतिक्रान्तासु वर्षासु समये गमनस्य च। पर्वतो मामुवाचेदं काले वचनमर्थवत्॥
en: After the rains had gone, and when the time for our own departure arrived, Parvata said to me these weighty words suitable to the hour.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: आवामस्य नरेन्द्रस्य गृहे परमपूजितौ। उषितौ समये ब्रह्मस्तद् विचिन्तय साम्प्रतम्॥
en: We have, O Brahmana, lived in the house of this king for some time, highly respected by him. Think of what return we should make.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: ततोऽहमब्रवं राजन् पर्वतं शुभदर्शनम्। सर्वमेतत् त्वयि विभो भागिनेयोपपद्यते॥
en: I then, O king, said to Parvata,-O nephew, it is really like you, and, O ye of great power, all this depends upon yourself.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: वरेण च्छन्द्यतां राजा लभतां यद् यदिच्छति। आवयोस्तपसा सिद्धि प्राप्नोतु यदि मन्यसे॥
en: By your boons let the king be made happy and let him obtain his wishes. Or, if you wish, let hiin be crowned with success by the power of ascetic merits of both of us.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: तत आहूय राजानं संजयं जयतां वरम्। पर्वतोऽनुमतो वाक्यमुवाच कुरुपुङ्गव॥
en: After this, Parvata having summoned king Srinjaya, that foremost of victorious persons, said to him these words, O foremost of Kurus:प्रीतौ स्वो नृप सत्कारैर्भवदार्जवसम्भृतैः।

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: आवाभ्यामभ्यनुज्ञातो वरं नृवर चिन्तय॥
en: We have been highly gratified, O king, with your hospitality given with every sincerity. With our permission, O foremost of men, think of the boon you should pray.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: देवानामविहिंसायां न भवेन्मानुषक्षयम्। तद् गृहाण महाराज पूजार्हो नौ मतो भवान्॥
en: Let the boon, however, be such that it may not create enmity with the gods or bring on destruction to men. Accept then, O king, a boon, for you deserved one as we think.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: संजय उवाच प्रीतौ भवन्तौ यदि मे कृतमेतावता मम। एष एव परो लाभो निर्वृत्तो मे महाफलः॥
en: Hearing these words, Srinjaya replied,-If you have been pleased with me my object then has been gained, for this itself is the highest gain and the fruition of all my desires.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: तमेवंवादिनं भूयः पर्वतः प्रत्यभाषत। वृणीष्व राजन् संकल्पं यत् ते हृदि चिरं स्थितम्॥
en: To Srinjaya who said so, Parvata again said, —Pray, o king, for the fruition of that wish which you are cherishing in your heart for a long time.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: संजय उवाच अभीप्सामि सुतं वीरं वीरवन्तं दृढव्रतम्) आयुष्मन्तं महाभागं देवराजसमद्युतिम्॥
en: Srinjaya answered, I wish to have a son who will be heroic and endued with great energy, firm in his vows and of long life, highly blessed and effulgent like the king of gods.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: पर्वत उवाच भविष्यत्येष ते कामो न त्वायुष्मान् भविष्यति। देवराजाभिभूत्यर्थं संकल्पो ह्येष ते हृदि॥
en: At this, Parvata said,-This your desire will be satisfied. Your son, however shall not live long, since you wish to have such a son for prevailing over the king of the gods.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: ख्यातः सुवर्णष्ठीवीति पुत्रस्तव भविष्यति। रक्ष्यश्च देवराजात् स देवराजसमद्युतिः॥
en: Your son shall be known by the name of Suvarnashthivin. He shall be effulgent like the king of gods, but take care to protect him always from that deity.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: तच्छुत्वा सुंजयो वाक्यं पर्वतस्य महात्मनः। प्रसादयामास तदा नैतदेवं भवेदिति॥ आयुष्मान् मे भवेत् पुत्रो भवतस्तपसा मुने। न च तं पर्वत: किंचिदुवाचेन्द्रव्यपेक्षया॥
en: Hearing those words of the great Parvata, Srinjaya begged that saint for ordaining otherwise, saying,-May my son live long, O Muni, through your ascetic merit.-Parvata, however, said nothing, out of his partiality for Indra.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: तमहं नृपतिं दीनमब्रवं पुनरेव च। स्मर्तव्योऽस्मि महाराज दर्शयिष्यामि ते सुतम्॥
en: Seeing the king very cheerless, I said to him,-Think of me, O king, (in your distress), and I shall promise to come when thought of by you.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: अहं ते दयितं पुत्रं प्रेतराजवशं गतम्। पुनर्दास्यामि तद्रूपं मा शुचः पृथिवीपते॥
en: Do not grieve, O king. I will give you back your beloved child alive, even if he be dead.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु नृपतिं प्रयातौ स्वो यथेप्सितम्। संजयश्च यथाकामं प्रविवेश स्वमन्दिरम्॥
en: Having said so to that king both of us left him for coming to where we wished, and Srinjaya returned to his palace.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: संजयस्याथ राजर्षेः कस्मिंश्चित् कालपर्यये। जज्ञे पुत्रो महावीर्यस्तेजसा प्रज्वलन्निव॥
en: After some time had passed, the royal sage Srinjaya had born unto him a highly powerful and energetic son.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: ववृधे स यथाकालं सरसीव महोत्पलम्। बभूव काञ्चनष्ठीवी यथार्थं नाम तस्य तत्॥
en: The child grew up like a large lotus in a lake, and became Suvarnashthivin in reality as well as in name.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: तदद्भुततमं लोके पप्रथे कुरुसत्तम। बुबुधे तच्च देवेन्द्रो वरदानं महर्षितः॥
en: This wonderful fact, O best of the Kurus, soon became widely known over the world. The king of the gods also learnt of it as the outcome of Paravata's boon.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: ततः स्वाभिभवाद् भीतो बृहस्पतिमते स्थितः। कुमारस्यान्तरप्रेक्षी बभूव बलवृत्रहा॥
en: Fearing humiliation the slayer of Vala and Vritra began to watch for the loopholes in that prince.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: चोदयामास तद् वज्रं दिव्यास्त्रं मूर्तिमत् स्थितम्। व्याघ्रो भूत्वा जहीमं त्वं राजपुत्रमिति प्रभो॥
en: He commanded his celestial weapon Thunder, standing before him, in embodied from saying,-Go, O powerful one, and assuming the form of a tiger kill this prince.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: प्रवृद्धः किल वीर्येण मामेषोऽभिभविष्यति। संजयस्य सुतो वज्र यथैनं पर्वतोऽब्रवीत्॥ एवमुक्तस्तु शक्रेण वज्रः परपुरज्जयः। कुमारमन्तरप्रेक्षी नित्यमेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: When grown up, this child of Srinjaya may, by his deeds humiliate me, O Thunder, as Parvata had said, thus addressed by Shakra, the celestial weapon Thunder, the subjugator of enemy's towns, began from that day to continually watch for the weak points of the prince.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: संजयोऽपि सुतं प्राप्य देवराजसमद्युतिम्। हृष्टः सान्तःपुरो राजा वननित्यो बभूव ह॥
en: Srinjaya, meanwhile, having obtained that child who was effulgent like Indra himself, became filled with joy. The king, accompanied by his wives, and the other ladies of his household, took up his quarter in the midst of a forest.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: ततो भागीरथीतीरे कदाचिनिर्जने वने। धात्रीद्वितीयो बालः स क्रीडार्थं पर्यधावत॥
en: One day, on the bank of the Bhagirathi, the boy accompanied by his nurse, ran here and there in play.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: पञ्चवर्षकदेशीयो बालो नागेन्द्रविक्रमः। सहसोत्पतितं व्याघ्रमाससाद महाबलम्॥
en: Though only five years' old, his prowess, even then, resembled that of a powerful elephant. While thus playing the child met a powerful tiger that attacked him suddenly.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: स बालस्तेन निष्पिष्टो वेपमानो नृपात्मजः। व्यसुः पपात मेदिन्यां ततो धात्री विचुक्रुशे॥
en: The infant prince trembled greatly as he was being mangled by the tiger and soon fell down dead on the Earth. Seeing in the nurse cried aloud in grief.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: हत्वा तु राजपुत्रं स तत्रैवान्तरधीयत। शार्दूलो देवराजस्य माययान्तर्हितस्तदा॥
en: Having killed the prince, the tiger through Indra's powers of delusion, vanished there and then.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: धात्र्यास्तु निनदं श्रुत्वा रुदत्याः परमार्तवत्। अभ्यधावत तं देशं स्वयमेव महीपतिः॥
en: Hearing the cries of the nurse, the king in great anxiety ran there.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: स ददर्श शयानं तं गतासुं पीतशोणितम्। कुमारं विगतानन्दं निशाकरमिव च्युतम्॥
en: He saw his son there, his blood quaffed off and lying dead on the ground like the moon dropped from the sky.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: स तमुत्सङ्गमारोप्य परिपीडितमानसः। पुत्रं रुधिरसंसिक्तं पर्यदेवयदातुरः॥
en: Taking up on his lap the boy bathed in blood, and the king, with heart stricken with grief, began to lament piteously.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: ततस्ता मातरस्तस्य रुदत्यः शोककर्शिताः। अभ्यधावन्त तं देशं यत्र राजा स संजयः॥
en: The queen also smitten with sorrow, and crying, quickly ran where king Srinjaya was.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: ततः स राजा सस्मार मामेव गतमानसः। तदाहं चिन्तनं ज्ञात्वा गतवांस्तस्य दर्शनम्॥
en: In that plight the king thought of me with rapt attention. Knowing that the king was thinking of me I appeared before him.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: मयैतानि च वाक्यानि श्रावितः शोकलालसः। यानि ते यदुवीरेण कथितानि महीपते॥
en: Assailed with grief as the king was, I recounted to him all those stories, O king, that this hero of Yadu's race has already recited to you.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: संजीवितश्चापि पुनर्वासवानुमते तदा। भवितव्यं तथा तच्च न तच्छक्यमतोऽन्यथा॥
en: I restored Srinjaya's child to life with Indra's permission. That which is ordained must take place. It is impossible to make it otherwise.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: तत ऊर्ध्वं कुमारस्तु स्वर्णष्ठीवी महायशाः। चित्तं प्रसादयामास पितुर्मातुश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: After this prince Suvarnashthivin of great renown and power began to gladden the hearts of his parents.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: कारयामास राज्यं च पितरि स्वर्गते नृपा वर्षाणां शतमेकं च सहस्रं भीमविक्रमः॥
en: Of great prowess, he ascended the throne of his father after the latter had died, and reigned for one thousand and one hundred years.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: तत ईजे महायज्ञैर्बहुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः। तर्पयामास देवांश्च पितश्चैव महाद्युतिः॥
en: He worshipped the gods in many great sacrifices accompanied with profuse presents. Highly effulgent he gratified the gods and the Pitris.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: उत्पाद्य च बहून् पुत्रान् कुलसंतानकारिणः। कालेन महता राजन् कालधर्ममुपेयिवान्॥
en: Having begotten many sons all of whom by their children multiplied the race, he breathed his last, o king, after many years.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: स त्वं राजेन्द्र संजातं शोकमेनं निवर्तय। यथा त्वां केशवः प्राह व्यासश्च सुमहातपाः॥
en: Do you, O foremost of kings, remove this grief of your heart, as Keshava has advised you, as also Vyasa of austere penances.

description: The story of the birth of the child whose excreta were gold.
sn: पितृपैतामहं राज्यमास्थाय धुरमुद्वह। इष्ट्वा पुण्यैर्महायज्ञैरिष्टं लोकमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: Rise up, O king, and carry the burden of this your ancestral kingdom, and celebrate high and great sacrifices so, that you may obtain (hereafter) whatever regions you may wish to acquire. Rise up, O king, and carry the burden of this your ancestral kingdom, and celebrate high and great sacrifices so, that you may obtain (hereafter) whatever regions you may wish to acquire.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तूष्णीभूतं तु राजानं शोचमानं युधिष्ठिरम्। तपस्वी धर्मतत्त्वज्ञः कृष्णद्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana saidDvaipayana-Vyasa, that great ascetic conversant with the truths of religion, spoke again to king Yudhishthira, who still remained silent and plunged in grief.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: व्यास उवाच प्रजानां पालनं धर्मो राज्ञां राजीवलोचन। धर्मः प्रमाणं लोकस्य नित्यं धर्मानुवर्तिनः॥
en: Vyasa said 'O you having eyes like lotus petals, the protection of subjects is the duty of kings. Those men who are always observant of duty regard duty to be all powerful.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: अनुतिष्ठस्व तद् राजन् पितृपैतामहं पदम्। ब्राह्मणेषु तपो धर्मः स नित्यो वेदनिश्चितः॥
en: Do you, therefore, O king, follow your forefathers. The penances are the duty of the Brahmanas. This is the eternal prescription of the Vedas.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: तत् प्रमाणं ब्राह्मणानां शाश्वतं भरतर्षभ। तस्य धर्मस्य कृत्स्नस्य क्षत्रियः परिरक्षिता॥
en: Penances, therefore, O foremost of Bharata's race, are the eternal duty of the Brahmanas. A Kshatriya's duty is to protect all persons.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: यः स्वयं प्रतिहन्ति स्म शासनं विषये रतः। स बाहुभ्यां विनिग्राह्यों लोकयात्राविघातकः॥
en: That man, who addicted to earthly objects, disregards wholesome restrictions, that man who transgresses at social harmony, should be punished with a strong hand.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: प्रमाणमप्रमाणं यः कुर्यान्मोहवशं गतः। भृत्यो वा यदि वा पुत्रस्तपस्वी वाथ कश्चन॥ पापान् सर्वैरुपायैस्तान् नियच्छेच्छातयीत वा। अतोऽन्यथा वर्तमानो राजा प्राप्नोति किल्बिषम्॥
en: The fool who ties to transgress authority, be he an attendant, a son or even a saint-indeed all such sinful men,-should by every means be punished or even killed. That king who behaves otherwise incurs sin.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: धर्म विनश्यमानं हि यो न रक्षेत् स धर्महा। ते त्वया धर्महन्तारो निहताः सपदानुगाः॥
en: He who does not protect morality when it is being disregarded, is himself a trespasser of the same. The Kauravas transgressed morality. They have with their followers been killed by you.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: स्वधर्मे वर्तमानस्त्वं किं नु शोचसि पाण्डव। राजा हि हन्याद् दद्याच्च प्रजा रक्षेच्च धर्मतः॥
en: You have simply observed the duties of your own order. Why then, O son of Pandu, do you indulge in such grief? The king should kill those that deserve death, make gifts to persons deserving of charity, and protect his subjects according to the sacred laws.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच न तेऽभिशंके वचनं यद् ब्रवीषि तपोधन। अपरोक्षो हि ते धर्मः सर्वधर्मविदां वर॥
en: Yudhishthira said I do not doubt your words, O you of great ascetic merit? Everything regarding morality and duty is well known to you, O foremost of all persons, conversant with morality and duty.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: मया त्ववध्या बहवो घातिता राज्यकारणात्। तानि कर्माणि मे ब्रह्मन् दहन्ति च पचन्ति च॥
en: I have, however, for the sake of kingdom, caused many persons to be killed. Those deeds, O Brahmana, are burning and consuming me.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: व्यास उवाच कुरुते पुरुषः ईश्वरो वा भवेत् कर्ता पुरुषो वापि भारत। हठो वा वर्तते लोके कर्मजं वा फलं स्मृतम्॥
en: Vyasa said O Bharata, is the Supreme Being the actor, or is men the doer? Is everything the outcome of Chance in the worlds, or are the fruits of our pristine deeds?

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: ईश्वरेण नियुक्तो हि साध्वसाधु च भारत। कर्म फलमीश्वरगामि तत्॥
en: If man, O Bharata, does all acts, good or evil, being urged by the Supreme Being, then the fruits thereof should attach to the Supreme Being himself.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: यथा हि पुरुषश्छिद्याद् वृक्षं परशुना वने। छेत्तुरेव भवेत् पाएं परशोर्न कथञ्चन॥
en: If a person cuts down by an axe a tree in the forest, it is the person that commits the sin and not the axe.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: अथवा तदुपादानात् प्राप्नुयात् कर्मणः फलम्। दण्डशस्त्रकृतं पापं पुरुषे तन्न विद्यते॥
en: Or, if it be said that, the axe being only the material cause, the consequence of the act should attach to the animate agent, then the sin visits to the person who has made the axe. This, however, can scarcely be true.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: न चैतदिष्टं कौन्तेय यदन्येन कृतं फलम्। प्राप्नुयादिति यस्माच्च ईश्वरे तन्निवेशय॥
en: If this be not reasonable, O son of Kunti, that one man should be visited by the sin of an act done by another, then guided by this, you should throw all responsibility upon the Supreme Being.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: अथापि पुरुषः कर्ता कर्मणोः शुभपापयोः। न परो विद्यते तस्मादेवमेतच्छुभं कृतम्॥
en: If, on the other hand, man is himself the agent of all his acts, good and evil, then there is no Supreme Being and, therefore, whatever you have done cannot bring evil consequences on you.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: न हि कश्चित् क्वचिद् राजन् दिष्टं प्रतिनिवर्तते। दण्डशस्त्रकृतं पापं पुरुषे तन्न विद्यते॥
en: No one, O king, can ever escape from what is ordained. If, again, Destiny be the result of pristine acts, then no sin visits one in this life even as the sin of cutting down a tree cannot affect the maker of the axe.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: यदि वा मन्यसे राजन् हतमेकं प्रतिष्ठितम्। एवमप्यशुभं कर्म न भूतं न भविष्यति॥
en: If you say it is Chance only that acts in the world, then such an act of destruction could never take place nor will ever take place.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: अथाभिपत्तिर्लोकस्य कर्तव्या पुण्यपापयोः। अभिपन्नमिदं लोके राज्ञामुद्यतदण्डनम्॥
