en: If it is necessary to determine what is good and what bad in the world, attend to the scriptures. In those scriptures. In those scriptures it has been ordained that kings should stand with the rod of punishment uplifted in their hands.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: तथापि लोके कर्माणि समावर्तन्ति भारत। शुभाशुभफलं चैते प्राप्नुवन्तीति मे मतिः॥
en: I think, O Bharata, that acts, good and bad, are perpetually revolving here as on a wheel, and men reap the fruits of those acts, good or bad, that they do.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: एवमप्यशुभं कर्म कर्मणस्तत्फलात्मकम्। त्यज त्वं राजशार्दूल मैवं शोके मनः कृथाः॥
en: One sinful act begets another. Therefore,O foremost of kings, avoid all evil acts and do not indulge in grief.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: स्वधर्मे वर्तमानस्य सापवादेऽपि भारत। एवमात्मपरित्यागस्तव राजन् न शोभनः॥
en: You should follow, O Bharata, the duties, even if reproachable, of your own order. This self-destruction, o king, does not appear in you.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: विहितानि हि कौन्तेय प्रायश्चित्तानि कर्मणाम्। शरीरवांस्तानि कुर्यादशरीरः पराभवेत्॥
en: Expiations, O king, have been laid down for (evil) acts. He that is alive can perform them, but he that dies cannot perform them.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: तद् राजन् जीवनमानस्त्वं प्रायश्चित्तं करिष्यसि। प्रायश्चित्तमकृत्वा तु प्रेत्य तप्तासि भारत॥
en: Therefore, O king, without laying down your life, perform those expiatory acts. If you do not perform them you may have to repent in the next world.”

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: विहितानि हि कौन्तेय प्रायश्चित्तानि कर्मणाम्। शरीरवांस्तानि कुर्यादशरीरः पराभवेत्॥
en: Expiations, O king, have been laid down for (evil) acts. He that is alive can perform them, but he that dies cannot perform them.

description: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira saying that he has merely done his duties.
sn: तद् राजन् जीवनमानस्त्वं प्रायश्चित्तं करिष्यसि। प्रायश्चित्तमकृत्वा तु प्रेत्य तप्तासि भारत॥
en: Therefore, O king, without laying down your life, perform those expiatory acts. If you do not perform them you may have to repent in the next world.”

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच हताः पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च भ्रातरः पितरस्तथा। श्वशुरा गुरवश्चैव मातुलाश्च पितामहाः॥ क्षत्रियाश्च महात्मानः सम्बन्धिसुहृदस्तथा। वयस्या भागिनेयाश्च ज्ञातयश्च पितामह॥ बहवश्च मनुष्येन्द्रा नानादेशसमागताः। घातिता राज्यलुब्धेन मयैकेन पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Sons, grandsons, brothers, sires, fathers-inlaw, preceptors, maternal uncles, grandsires, many great Kshatriyas, many relatives, friends, companions, sisters' sons, and kinsmen, O grandfather, and many foremost of men hailing from various countries, have been killed. All these, O grandfather, have been caused to be killed by myself alone, from desire of kingdom.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: तांस्तादृशानहं हत्वा धर्मनित्यान् महीक्षितः। असकृत् सोमपान् वीरान् किं प्राप्स्यामि तपोधन॥
en: Having brought about the death of so many heroic kings who were always righteous and all of whom had drunk Soma in sacrifices, what end shall I obtain, O great ascetic.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: दह्याम्यनिशमद्यापि चिन्तयानः पुनः पुनः। हीनां पार्थिवसिंहैस्तैः श्रीमद्भिः पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: Thinking that this Earth has been deprived of many foremost of kings, all of whom enjoyed great prosperity, I burn continually to this day.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: दृष्ट्वा ज्ञातिवधं घोरं हतांश्च शतशः परान्। कोटिशश्च नरानन्यान् परितप्ये पितामह॥
en: Having seen this destruction of kinsmen and of millions of other men, I burn with grief, Ograndfather.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: का न तासां वरस्त्रीणामवस्थाद्य भविष्यति। विहीनानां तु तनयैः पतिभिर्धातृभिस्तथा॥
en: Oh, what will be the condition of those foremost of ladies who have been deprived of sons, of husbands, and of brothers.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: अस्मानन्तकरान् घोरान् पाण्डवान् वृष्णिसंहतान्। आक्रोशन्त्यः कृशा दीनाः प्रपतिष्यन्ति भूतले॥
en: Censuring the Pandavas and the Vrishnis as cruel murderers, those ladies, reduced greatly and sunk in grief, will throw themselves on the Earth.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: अपश्यन्त्यः पितॄन् भ्रातृन् पतीन् पुत्रांश्च योषितः। त्यक्त्वा प्राणान् स्त्रियः सर्वा गमिष्यन्ति यमक्षयम्॥ वत्सलत्वाद् द्विजश्रेष्ठ तत्र मे नास्ति संशयः। व्यक्तं सौक्ष्याच्च धर्मस्य प्राप्स्यामः स्त्रीवधंवयम्॥
en: Not seeing their father and brothers and husbands and sons, those ladies renouncing their lives in agony will go to the abode of Yama, O foremost of Brahmanas! I have no doubt of this! The course of morality is very subtile. It is clear that we shall be guilty of killing women for this.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: यद् वयं सुहृदो हत्वा कृत्वा पापमनन्तकम्। नरके निपतिष्यामो ह्यधःशिरस एव ह॥
en: Having killed our kinsmen and friends and thereby committed a sin which cannot be expiated, we shall have tù fall into hell with heads downwards.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: शरीराणि विमोक्ष्यामस्तपसोग्रेण सत्तम। आश्रमाणां विशेषं त्वमथाचक्ष्व पितामह॥
en: O best of men, we shall, therefore, reduce our bodies with the austerest of penances! Tell me, O grand-father, what mode of life I should follow.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरस्य तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा द्वैपायनस्तदा। निरीक्ष्य निपुणं बुद्ध्या ऋषिः प्रोवाच पाण्डवम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words of Yudhishthira, the Dvaipayana-Rishi, having reflected keenly for sometime, said again to the son of Pandu.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: व्यास उवाच मा विषादं कृथा राजन् क्षत्रधर्ममनुस्मरन्। स्वधर्मेण हता ह्येते क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रियर्षभ॥
en: Vyasa said, Remembering the duties of a Kshatriya, O king, do not indulge in grief! All those Kshatriyas, O foremost of Kshatriyas, have been killed while following their legitimate duties.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: काक्षमाणाः श्रियं कृत्स्नां पृथिव्यां च महद् यशः। कृतान्तविधिसंयुक्ताः कालेन निधनं गताः॥
en: Pursuing great prosperity and fame on Earth, those foremost of men, all of whom were liable to death, have died through the influence of Time.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: न त्वं हन्ता च भीमोऽयं नार्जुनो न यमावपि। कालः पर्यायधर्मेण प्राणानादत्त देहिनाम्॥
en: You have not been their slayer, nor this Bhima, nor Arjuna, nor the twins. It is Time that took away their lives according to the great law of change.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: न तस्य मातापितरौ नानुग्राह्यो हि कश्चन। कर्मसाक्षी प्रजानां यस्तेन कालेन संहृताः॥
en: Time has neither mother, nor father, nor anybody to whom he shows any mercy. He is the witness of the acts of all creatures, By him have they been snatched away.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: हेतुमात्रमिदं तस्य विहितं भरतर्षभ। यद्धन्ति भूतैर्भूतानि तदस्मै रूपमैश्वरम्॥
en: This battle, O foremost of Bharata's race, was only an occasion ordained by him. He brought out the destruction of creatures through the instrumentality of Time. In this manner it displays its irresistible power.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: कर्मसूत्रात्मकं विद्धि साक्षिणं शुभपापयोः। सुखदुःखगुणोदक कालं कालफलप्रदम्॥
en: Know that Time depends upon the fetters of action and is the witness of all actions good and evil. It is Time that brings about the fruits, pleasurable or miserable, of our actions.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: तेषामपि महाबाहो कर्माणि परिचिन्तय। विनाशहेतुकानि त्वं यैस्ते कालवशं गताः॥
en: Think, O mighty-armed one, of the acts of those Kshatriyas that have been killed. Those acts were the causes of their destruction and it is on account of them that they have died.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: आत्मनश्च विजानीहि नियतव्रतशासनम्। यदा त्वमीदृशं कर्म विधिनाऽऽक्रम्य कारितः॥
en: Think also of your own acts of observances of vows with controlled mind, And think also how you have been compelled by the Supreme Ordainer to do such an act.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: त्वष्ट्रेव विहितं यन्त्रं यथा चेष्टयितुर्वशे। कर्मणा कालयुक्तेन तथेदं चेष्टते जगत्॥
en: As a weapon made by a smith or carpenter is under the control of the person who uses it, and moves as moves it, likewise this universe, controlled by actions done in Time, moves as those actions move it.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: पुरुषस्य हि दृष्ट्वेमामुत्पत्तिमनिमित्ततः। यदृच्छया विनाशं च शोकहर्षावनर्थकौ॥
en: Beholding that the births and deaths of creatures take place without any perceptible cause and order, grief and joy are absolutely useless.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: व्यलीकमपि यत् त्वत्र चित्तवैतंसिकं तव। तदर्थमिष्यते राजन् प्रायश्चित्तं तदाचर॥
en: Although this confusion of your heart is a mere delusion, still, if you like, O king, perform expiatory rites.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: इदं तु श्रूयते पार्थ युद्धे देवासुरे पुरा। असुरा भ्रातरो ज्येष्ठा देवाश्चापि यवीयसः॥
en: It is heard, O Partha, that the gods and the Asuras fought against each other. The Asuras were the elder, and the gods the younger brothers.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: तेषामपि श्रीनिमित्तं महानासीत् समुच्छ्रयः। युद्धं वर्षसहस्राणि द्वात्रिंशदभवत् किल॥
en: Seeking prosperity, they fought a dreadful battle between them. The fight lasted for thirtytwo thousand years.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: एकार्णवां महीं कृत्वा रुधिरेण परिप्लुताम्। जघ्नुर्दैत्यांस्तथा देवास्त्रिदिवं चाभिलेभिरे॥
en: Converting the Earth to one vast sea of blood, the gods killed the Daityas and occupied the celestial region.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: तथैव पृथिवीं लब्ध्वा ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः। संश्रिता दानवानां वै साह्यार्थं दर्पमोहिताः॥
en: Having occupied the Earth, a host of Brahmanas, conversant with the Vedas, armed themselves, stupefied with pride, with the Danavas for helping in the fight.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: शालावृका इति ख्यातास्त्रिषु लोकेषु भारत। अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि ते चापि विबुधैर्हताः॥
en: They were known by the name of Shalavrika and were eighty-eight thousand in number. All of them, however, were killed by the gods.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: धर्मव्युच्छित्तिमिच्छन्तो येऽधर्मस्य प्रवर्तकाः। हन्तव्यास्ते दुरात्मानो देवैर्दैत्या इवोल्बणाः॥
en: Those wicked persons who desire to root out virtue and encourage sinfulness deserve io be killed even as the furious Daityas were killed by the gods.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: एकं हत्वा यदि कुले शिष्टानां स्यादनामयम्। कुलं हत्वा च राष्ट्रं च न तद् वृत्तोपघातकम्॥
en: If by killing a single individual a family may be saved, or, if by killing a single family the whole kingdom may be saved, such an act of slaughter is not sinful.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: अधर्मरूपो धर्मो हि कश्चिदस्ति नराधिप। धर्मश्चाधर्मरूपोऽस्ति तच्च ज्ञेयं विपश्चिता॥
en: Sin, O king, sometimes becomes virtue, and virtue sometimes becomes sin. The learned know which is which.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: तस्मात् संस्तम्भयात्मानं श्रुतवानसि पाण्डव। देवैः पूर्वगतं मार्गमनुयातोऽसि भारत॥
en: Therefore, console yourself, O son of Pandu, for you are well read in the scriptures. You have, O Bharata, only followed the path of the very gods.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: न हीदृशा गमिष्यन्ति नरकं पाण्डवर्षभ। भ्रातृनाश्वासयैतांस्त्वं सुहृदश्च परंतप॥
en: Men like yourselves never go to hell, o foremost of Pandu's race! Comfort these your brothers and all your friends, O scorcher of foes.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: यो हि पापसमारम्भे कार्ये तद्भावभावितः। कुर्वन्नपि तथैव स्यात् कृत्वा च निरपत्रपः॥ तस्मिंस्तत् कलुषं सर्वं समाप्तमिति शब्दितम्। प्रायश्चित्तं न तस्यास्ति ह्रासो वा पापकर्मणः॥
en: He who deliberately commits sinful acts, and committing them feels no compunction but continues the same as before, is known as a great sinner. There is no expiation for him, and his sins never disappear.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: त्वं तु शुक्लाभिजातीयः परदोषेण कारितः। अनिच्छमानः कर्मेदं कृत्वा च परितप्यसे॥
en: You are born in a noble family. Urged by the sons of others, you have most reluctantly done this, and having done this you repent for it.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: अश्वमेधो महायज्ञः प्रायश्चित्तमुदाहृतम्। तमाहर महाराज विपाष्मैवं भविष्यसि॥
en: The rite of Horse-sacrifice, has been indicated as an expiation for you. Make preparations for that sacrifice, O king, and you ! will be freed off of all your sins.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: मरुद्भिः सह जित्वारीन् भगवान् पाकशासनः। एकैकं क्रतुमाहृत्य शतकृत्व: शतक्रतुः॥
en: Having defeated his foes with the help of the Maruts, Indra gradually celebrated a hundred sacrifices and became Shatakratu.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: धूतपामाजितस्वर्गो लोकान् प्राप्य सुखोदयान्। मरुद्गणैर्वृतः शक्रः शुशुभे भासयन् दिशः॥
en: Freed from sin, occupying heaven, and having obtained many blissful regions and great happiness and prosperity, Shakra surrounded by the Maruts, is shining in beauty, and lighting up all the quarters with his effulgence.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: स्वर्गे लोके महीयन्तमप्सरोभिः शचीपतिम्। ऋषयः पर्युपासन्ते देवाश्च विबुधेश्वरम्॥
en: The lord of Shachi is worshipped in the heaven by the Apsaras. The Rishis and the other gods all adore himn with respect.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: सेयं त्वामनुसम्प्राप्ता विक्रमेण वसुन्धरा। निर्जिताच महीपाला विक्रमेण त्वयानध॥
en: You have obtained the Earth through your prowess. All the kings have been defeated by you, O sinless one, through your prowess.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: तेषां पुराणि राष्ट्राणि गत्वा राजन् सुहृवृतः। भ्रातॄन् पुत्रांश्चपौत्रांश्च स्वे स्वे राज्येऽभिषेचय॥
en: Proceeding with your friends to their kingdoms, O king, install their brothers, sons, or grandsons on their thrones.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: बालानपि च गर्भस्थान् सान्त्वेन समुदाचरन्। रञ्जयन् प्रकृती: सर्वाः परिपाहि वसुन्धराम्॥
en: Treating kindly even the children in the womb, make you subjects glad and happy, and govern the Earth,

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: कुमारो नास्ति येषां च कन्यास्तत्राभिषेचय। कामाशयो हि स्त्रीवर्गः शोकमेवं प्रहास्यसि॥
en: Install on their thrones the daughters of those that have no sons. Women are fond of pleasure and power. By this they will shake off their sorrows and become happy.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: एवमाश्वासनं कृत्वा सर्वराष्ट्रेषु भारत। यजस्व वाजिमेधेन यथेन्द्रो विजयी पुरा॥ अशोच्यास्ते महात्मानः क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रियर्षभा स्वकर्मभिर्गता नाशं कृतान्तबलमोहिताः॥
en: Having comforted the entire empire in this way, O Bharata, worship the gods in a Horsesacrifice as did the victorious Indra in days of yore. It is not proper for us to grieve for those great Kshatriyas, O foremost of Kshatriyas. Stupefied by the power of the Destroyer, they have died while satisfying the duties of their own order.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: अवाप्तः क्षत्रधर्मस्ते राज्यं प्राप्तमकण्टकम्। रक्षस्व धर्म कौन्तेय श्रेयान् यः प्रेत्य भारत॥
en: You have performed the duties of a Kshatriya and obtained the Earth thornless. Follow your own duties, O son of Kunti, for then, O Bharata, you will enjoy happiness in the next world.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कानि कृत्वेह कर्माणि प्रायश्चित्तीयते नरः। किं कृत्वा मुच्यते तत्र तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said 'What are the necessary rites of expiation? And what are those acts which one must do for being released from sin? Tell me this, O grandfather.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: व्यास उवाच अकुर्वन् विहितं कर्म प्रतिषिद्धानि चाचरन्। प्रायश्चित्तीयते ह्येवं नरो मिथ्यानुवर्तयन्॥
en: Vyasa said “Having omitted to perform those acts that have been ordained, and done those that have been forbidden, and have behaved deceitfully, a man becomes liable to perform expiation.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: सूर्येणाभ्युदितो यश्च ब्रह्मचारी भवत्युत। तथा सूर्याभिनिर्मुक्तः कुनखी श्यावदन्नपि॥ परिवित्तिः परिवेत्ता ब्रह्मघ्नो यश्च कुत्सकः। दिधिषूपपतिर्यः स्यादग्रेदिधिषुरेव च॥ अवकीर्णी भवेद् यश्च द्विजातिवधकस्तथा। अतीर्थे ब्राह्मणस्त्यागी तीर्थे चाप्रतिपादकः॥ ग्रामघाती च कौन्तेय मांसस्य परिविक्रयी। यश्चाग्नीनपविध्येत तथैव ब्रह्मविक्रयी॥ स्त्रीशूद्रवधको यश्च पूर्वः पूर्वस्तु गर्हितः। यथा पशुसमालम्भी गृहदाहस्य कारकः॥ अनृतेनोपवर्ती च प्रतिरोद्धा गुरोस्तथा। एतान्येनांसि सर्वाणि व्युत्क्रान्तसमयश्च यः॥
en: The Brahmacharin, who rises from bed after the sun rise, or goes to bed while the sun is setting, one who has a rotten nail or black tecth, one whose younger brother married first, one who marries before his elder brother is married, one who has been guilty of Brahmanicide, one who speaks ill of others, one who marries a younger sister before the elder sister has been married, one who marries an elder sister after having married a younger one, one who does not observe his vow, one kill who a saint, one who imparts a knowledge of the Vedas to a unworthy person, one who does not impart a knowledge thereof a worthy person, one who takes many lives, one who sells flesh, one who has abandoned his (sacred) fire, one who sells the knowledge of the Vedas, one who kills his preceptor or a woman, one born in a sinful family, one who kills an animal wilfully, one who gives fire to a dwelling house, one who lives by deceit, one who disobeys his preceptor, and one who has violated agreement,-these all are guilty of sins requiring expiation.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: अकार्याणि तु वक्ष्यामि यानि तानि निबोध मे। लोकवेदविरुद्धानि तान्येकाग्रमनाः शृणु॥
en: I shall now mention other acts which men should not do, viz., acts that are forbidden by men and the Vedas. Listen to me with rapt attention.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: स्वधर्मस्य परित्यागः परधर्मस्य च क्रिया। अयाज्ययाजनं चैव तथाभक्ष्यस्य भक्षणम्॥ शरणागतसंत्यागो भृत्यस्याभरणं तथा। रसानां विक्रयश्चापि तिर्यग्योनिवधस्तथा॥ आधानादीनि कर्माणि शक्तिमान करोति यः। अप्रयच्छंश्च सर्वाणि नित्यदेयानि भारत॥ दक्षिणानामदानं च ब्राह्मणस्वाभिमर्शनम्। सर्वाण्येतान्यकार्याणि प्राहुर्धर्मविदो जनाः॥
en: The rejection of one's own religion, the following of other people's religion, assisting at the sacrifice or the religious rites of one who does not deserve such assistance, eating of forbidden food, deserting one who seeks refuge, neglect in maintaining servants and dependents, selling salt and treacle, killing of birds and animals, refusal, though able to beget children, upon a soliciting woman, negligence of making the daily offering, negligence to present the Dakshina, humiliating a Brahmana, these all are considered as forbidden acts by persons conversant with duty.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: पित्रा विवदते पुत्रो यश्च स्याद् गुरुतल्पगः। अप्रजायन् नरव्याघ्र भवत्यधार्मिको नरः॥
en: The son that quarrels with the father, the person who violates the bed of his preceptor, one who neglects to beget children on his wife, are all sinful, O foremost of men.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: उक्तान्येतानि कर्माणि विस्तरेणेतरेण च। यानि कुर्वन्नकुर्वच प्रायश्चित्तीयते नरः॥
en: I have now described to you in brief as also in detail, those acts and omissions by which a man is compelled to perform expiation.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: एतान्येव तु कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि मानवाः। येषु येषु निमित्तेषु न लिप्यन्तेऽथ ताशृणु॥
en: Listen now to the circumstances under which men, by even committing these acts, are not sullied with sin.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: प्रगृह्य शस्त्रमायान्तमपि वेदान्तगं रणे। जिघांसन्तं जिघांसीयान्न तेन ब्रह्महा भवेत्॥
en: If a Brahmana well acquainted with the Vedas takes up arins and tries to kill you in battle, you may proceed against him for taking his life. By such an act the slayer does not become guilty of Brahmanicide.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: इति चाप्यत्र कौन्तेय मन्त्रो वेदेषु पठ्यते। वेदप्रमाणविहितं धर्मं च प्रब्रवीमि ते॥
en: There is a Mantra in the Vedas, O son of Kunti, that sanctions it, I describe to you only those practices which are sanctioned by the authority of the Vedas.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: अपेतं ब्राह्मणं वृत्ताद् यो हन्यादाततायिनम्। न तेन ब्रह्महा स स्यान्मन्युस्तन्मन्युमृच्छति॥
en: One who kills a Brahmana who deviates from his own duties and who goes armed for killing a man, does not truly become the killer of a Brahmania. In such a case it is the anger of the slayer that proceeds against the anger of the slain.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: प्राणात्यये तथाज्ञानादाचरन्मदिरामपि। आदेशितो धर्मपरैः पुनः संस्कारमर्हति॥
en: A person by drinking alcohol unknowingly or upon the advice of a virtuous physician when his life is in a danger should have the expiatory rites performed once more in his case.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं कौन्तेयाभक्ष्यभक्षणम्। प्रायश्चित्तविधानेन सर्वमेतेन शुद्ध्यति॥
en: All that I have told you, O son of Kunti, about the eating of forbidden food, inay be purified by such expiatory rites.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: गुरुतल्पं हि गुर्वर्थं न दूषयति मानवम्। उद्दालक: श्वेतकेतुं जनयामास शिष्यतः॥
en: Knowing the preceptor's wife at the preceptor's behest, does not stain the pupil. The sage Uddalaka caused his son Shvetaketu to be begotten by a disciple.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: स्तेयं कुर्वंच गुर्वर्थमापत्सु न निषिध्यते। बहुशः कामकारेण न चेद् यः सम्प्रवर्तते॥
en: A person by committing theft for his preceptor in a time of distress, is not sullied by that sin. One, however, who commits theft for procuring enjoyments for himself, becomes stained.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: अन्यत्र ब्राह्मणस्वेभ्य आददानो न दुष्यति। स्वयमप्राशिता यश्च न स पापेन लिप्यते॥
en: One is not sullied by stealing from other than Brahmanas in times of distress and for the sake of his preceptor. Only one who steals under such circumstances without reserving for himself any portion thereof, is not sullied by sin.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: प्राणत्राणेऽनृतं वाच्यमात्मनो वा परस्य च। गुर्वर्थे स्त्रीषु चैव स्याद् विवाहकरणेषु च॥
en: A falsehood may be uttered for saving one's own life or that of another, or for the sake of one's preceptor, or for gratifying a woman, or for bringing about a marriage.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: नावर्तते व्रतं स्वप्ने शुक्रमोक्षे कथंचन। आज्यहोमः समिद्धेऽग्नौ प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते॥
en: One's vow of celibacy is not broken by having nocturnal pollutions. In such cases the expiation consists in the pouring of libations of clarified butter on the burning fire.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: पारिवित्त्यं त पतिते नास्ति प्रव्रजिते तथा। भिक्षिते पारदार्यं च तद् धर्मस्य न दूषकम्॥
en: If the elder brother is killed or has left the world, the younger brother does not commit sin by marrying. He who solicited by a woman, knows her commits no sin.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: वृथा पशुसमालम्भं नैव कुर्यान्न कारयेत्। अनुग्रहः पशूनां हि संस्कारो विधिनोदितः॥
en: One should not kill or cause to be killed an animal except in a sacrifice. Animals have become sacred for the kindness shown towards them by the creator, himself in the ordinance laid down by him.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: अनर्हे ब्राह्मणे दत्तमज्ञानात् तन्न दूषकम्। सत्काराणां तथा तीर्थे नित्यं वाप्रतिपादनम्॥
en: By making a gift unknowingly to an undeserving Brahmana one does not commit sin. The ignorant omission of behaving with liberality towards a deserving person does not lead to sin.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: स्त्रियास्तथापचारिण्या निष्कृतिः स्याददूषिका। अपि सा पूयते तेन न तु भर्ता प्रदुष्यति॥
en: By forsaking an unchaste wife one does not incur sin. By such treatment the woman herself may be purified while the husband may avoid sin.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: तत्त्वं ज्ञात्वा नु सोमस्य विक्रयः स्याददोषवान्। असमर्थस्य भृत्यस्य विसर्गः स्याददोषवान्। वनदाहो गवामर्थे क्रियमाणो न दूषकः॥
en: One who knows the true uses of the Soma juice, does not commit sin by selling it. By dismissing a servant who is incapable of doing service, one is not visited with sin.

description: Vyasa exhorts him to cast off his grief and rule his kngdom.
sn: उक्तान्येतानि कर्माणि यानि कुर्वन्न दुष्यति। प्रायश्चित्तानि वक्ष्यामि विस्तरेमैव भारत॥
en: I have grow described those acts by doing which one does not commit sin. I shall now speak to you of expiation in detail.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: व्यास उवाच तपसा कर्मणा चैव प्रदानेन च भारत। पुनाति पापं पुरुषः पुनश्चेन्न प्रवर्तते॥
en: Vyasa said ‘By penances, religious rites, and gifts, O Bharata, a man purify his sins if he does not commit them again.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: एककालं तु भुञ्जीत चरन् भैक्ष्यं स्वकर्मकृत्। कपालपाणिः खट्वाङ्गी ब्रह्मचारी सदोत्थितः॥ अनसूयुरधःशायी कर्म लोके प्रकाशयन्। पूर्णीदशाभिर्वषैर्ब्रह्महा विप्रमुच्यते॥
en: By living upon only one meal a day, procured by begging, by doing all his acts himself, by going about begging with a human skull in one hand and a staff with a skull on it in another, by becoming a Brahmacharin and always ready for work, by renouncing all malice, by sleeping on the naked earth, by declaring his offence publicly, by doing all this for full twelve years, a person can cleanse himself from the sin of a Brahmanicide.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: लक्ष्यः शस्त्रभृतां वा स्याद् विदुषामिच्छयाऽऽत्मनः। प्रास्येदात्मानमग्नौ वा समिद्धे त्रिरवाक्छिराः॥ जपन् वान्यतमं वेदं योजनानां शतं व्रजेत्। सर्वस्वं वा वेदविदे ब्राह्मणायोपपादयेत्॥ धनं वा जीवनायालं गृहं वा सपरिच्छदम्। मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्याया गोप्ता गोब्राह्मणस्य च॥
en: By perishing by the weapons of a person living by the use of arms, of one's own accords and upon the advice of persons read in the scriptures, or by throwing one's self down, for three times, with head downwards, upon a burning fire, or by walking a hundred Yojanas reciting the Vedas, or by presenting one's all to a Brahmana well read in the Vedas, or at least so much by which he would live comfortably for life, or a house properly furnished, and by protecting kine and Brahmanas, one may be purged of the sin of Brahmanicide.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: षड्भिर्वर्षेः कृच्छ्रभोजी ब्रह्महा पूयते नरः। मासे मासे समश्नंस्तु त्रिभिर्वर्षेः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: By living upon poor diet every day for six years. a person may be purged off that sin. By observing a more difficult vow about food one may be cleansed in three years.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: संवत्सरेण मासाशी पूयते नात्र संशयः। तथैवोपवसन् राजन् स्वल्पेनापि प्रपूयते॥ क्रतुना चाश्वमेधेन पूयते नात्र संशयः। ये चाप्यवभृथस्नाताः केचिदेवंविधा नराः॥ ते सर्वे धूतपाप्मानो भवन्तीति परा श्रुतिः। ब्राह्मणार्थे हतो युद्धे मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया॥
en: By living upon one meal a month, one may be cleansed in a year. By an absolute fast, one may be cleansed within a very short time, one is again purified by a Horse-sacrifice. Men that have been guilty of Brahmanicide and who have succeeded in taking the final bath at the completion of the Horse-sacrifice, become washed off all their sins. This is highly authoritative injunction of the Shrutis. One again, by renouncing his life in a battle undertaking for a Brahmana, becomes cleansed of the sin of Brahmanicide.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: गवां शतसहस्रं तु पात्रेभ्यः प्रतिपादयेत्। ब्रह्महा विप्रमुच्येत सर्वपापेभ्य एव च।॥
en: By giving away a hundred thousand kine to deserving persons, one becomes cleansed of the sin of Brahmanicide as also of all other sins.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: कपिलानां सहस्राणि यो दद्यात् पञ्चविंशतिम्। दोग्ध्रीणां स च पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते॥
en: One that gives away twenty-five thousand kine of the Kapila breed all of them having calves becomes cleansed of all his sins.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: गोसहस्रं सवत्सानां दोग्ध्रीणां प्राणसंशये। साधुभ्यो वै दरिद्रेभ्यो दत्त्वा मुच्येत किल्बिषात्॥
en: One who, at the time of death, presents a thousand kine with calves to poor but deserving persons, becomes freed for sin.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: शतं वै यस्तु काम्बोजान् ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयच्छति। नियतेभ्यो महीपाल स च पापात् प्रमुच्यते॥
en: That man, o king, who gives away a hundred horse of the Kamvoja breed to Brahmanas of regulated conduct, becomes freed from sin.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: मनोरथं तु यो दद्यादेकस्मा अपि भारत। न कीर्तयेत दत्त्वा यः स च पापात् प्रमुच्यते॥
en: That man, O Bharata, who gives to even one man all that he asks for, and who, having given it, does not advertise his act, becomes freed from sin,

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: सुरापानं सकृत् कृत्वा योऽग्निवर्णां सुरां पिबेत्। स पावयत्यथात्मानमिह लोके परत्र च॥
en: If a person who has once taken wine, drinks hot water, he purifies himself both here and hereafter.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: मरुप्रपातं प्रपतन् ज्वलनं वा समाविशन्। महाप्रस्थानमातिष्ठन् मुच्यते सर्वकिल्विषैः॥
en: By falling from the summit of a mountain or entering a burning fire, or by going on journey for ever after renouncing the world, one is freed from all sins.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: बृहस्पतिसवेनेष्ट्वा सुरापो ब्राह्मणः पुनः। समितिं ब्राह्मणो गच्छेदिति वै ब्रह्मणः श्रुतिः॥
en: By celebrating the sacrifice laid down by Brihaspati, a Brahmana who drinks wine may obtain the region of Brahmana this has been said by Brahma himself.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: भूमिप्रदानं कुर्याद् यः सुरां पीत्वा विमत्सरः। पुनर्नच पिबेद् राजन् संस्कृतः स च शुद्ध्यति॥
en: If a person, after having drunk wine, becomes humble and makes a gift of land, and abstains himself from it ever afterwards he becomes purified and cleansed.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: गुरुतल्पी शिलां तप्तामायसीमभिसंविशेत्। अवकृत्यात्मनः शेर्फ प्रव्रजेदूर्ध्वदर्शनः॥
en: The person that has violated his preceptor's bed, should lie down on a sheet of heated iron, and having cut off the male organ, should leave the world and live in the woods, with eyes always turned upwards.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: शरीरस्य विमोक्षेण मुच्यते कर्मणोऽशुभात्। कर्मभ्यो विप्रमुच्यन्ते यत्ताः संवत्सरं स्त्रियः॥
en: By renouncing one's body, one become cleansed of all his sins. Women, by leading a regular life for one year, becomes freed off of all their sins.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: महाव्रतं चरेद् यस्तु दद्यात् सर्वस्वमेव तु। गुर्वर्थे वा हतो युद्धे स मुच्येत् कर्मणोऽशुभात्॥
en: The person who practises a very rigid vow, or gives away the whole of his wealth, or dies in a battle fought for the sake of his preceptor, becomes freed off of all his sins.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: अनृतेनोपवर्ती चेत् प्रतिरोद्धा गुरोस्तथा। उपाहृत्य प्रियं तस्मै तस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते॥
en: One who utters untruth before one's preceptor or acts against his wishes, becomes freed of that sin by doing something agreeable to one's preceptor.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: अवकीर्णिनिमित्तं तु ब्रह्महत्याव्रतं चरेत्। गोचर्मवासाः षण्मासांस्तथा मुच्येत किल्बिषात्॥
en: One who has deviated from the vow of celibacy may become freed of that sin by being clad in a hide of a cow for six months and observing the penances laid down for Brahmanicide.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: परदारापहारी तु परस्यापहरन् वसु। संवत्सरं व्रती भूत्वा तथा मुच्येत किल्बिषात्॥
en: One who has been guilty of adultery or of theft, is purified by practising rigid vows for a year.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: धनं तु यस्यापहरेत् तस्मै दद्यात् समं वसु। विविधेनाभ्युपायेन तदा मुच्येत किल्बिषात्॥
en: When one steals another's property, one should, by all means in his power, return to the said party another property of the value of what has been stolen. One may then be freed of the sin.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: कृच्छ्राद् द्वादशरात्रेण संयतात्मा व्रते स्थितः। परिवेत्ता भवेत् पूतः परिवित्तिस्तथैव च॥
en: The younger brother who has married before his elder brother is married, as also the elder brother whose younger brother has married before him, becomes freed by observing a rigid vow, with controlled mind for twelve nights.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: निवेश्यं तु पुनस्तेन सदा तारयता पितॄन्। न तु स्त्रिया भवेद् दोषो न तु सा तेन लिप्यते॥
en: The younger brother, however, should marry again for rescuing his departed manes. Upon such second marriage the first wife becomes purified and her husband himself would not commit sin by taking her.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: भोजनं ह्यन्तराशुद्धं चातुर्मास्ये विधीयते। स्त्रियस्तेन प्रशुध्यन्ति इति धर्मविदो विदुः॥
en: Men well read in the scriptures say that women may be freed of even the greatest sins by practising the vow of Chaturmasya living all the while upon restricted and pure diet.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: स्त्रियस्त्वाशङ्किताः पापा नोपगम्या विजानता। रजसा ता विशुध्यन्ते भस्मना भाजनं यथा॥
en: Persons well read in the scriptures take no notice of the sins that women may commit at heart. Whatever their sins may be they are cleaned by their menstrual course like a metallic plate that is cleansed with ashes.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: पादजोच्छिष्टकांस्यं यद् गवा ध्रातमथापि वा। गण्डूषोच्छिष्टमपि वा विशुध्येद् दशभिस्तु तत्॥
en: Plates desercated by a Shudra eating off it, or a vessel of the same metal that has been smelt by a cow, or stained by a Brahmana's Gandusha, may be cleansed by the ten purifying substances.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: चतुष्पात् सकलो धर्मो ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते। पादावकृष्टो राजन्ये तथा धर्मो विधीयते॥
en: It has been ordained that a Brahmana should acquire and practise all the virtues. For a Kshatriya it has been ordained that he should acquire and practise one fourth of all virtues.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: तथा वैश्ये च शूद्रे च पादः पादो विधीयते। विद्यादेवंविधेनैषां गुरुलाघवनिश्चयम्॥
en: So, a Vaishya should practise less (than a Kshatriya's) by a fourth, and a Shudra less (than a Vaishya's) for a fourth. The gravity or lightness of sins of each of the four orders, should thus be ascertained.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: तिर्यग्योनिवधं कृत्वा दुमाश्छित्त्वेतरान् बहून्। त्रिरात्रं वायुभक्षः स्यात् कर्म च प्रथयन्नरः॥
en: Having killed a bird or an animal, or cut down living trees, a person should declare his sin publicly and fast for three nights.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: अगम्यागमने राजन् प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते। । आर्द्रवस्त्रेण षण्मासान् विहार्य भस्मशायिना॥
en: By having intercourse with one whom intercourse is forbidden, the expiation consists in wandering in wet clothes and sleeping on a bed of ashes.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: एष एव तु सर्वेषामकार्याणां विधिर्भवेत्। ब्राह्मणोक्तेन विधिना दृष्टान्तागमहेतुभिः॥
en: These, O king, are the expiations for sins, as laid down in scriptures and by Brahmana himself.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: सावित्रीमप्यधीयीत शुचौ देशे मिताशनः। अहिंसो मन्दकोऽजल्यो मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः॥
en: A Brahmana may be freed off all sins by reciting the Gayatri in a sacred place, living all the while upon restricted fare, casting off malice, abandoning anger and hate, unaffected by praise and blame, and observing the vow of silence.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: अहःसु सततं तिष्ठेदभ्याकाशं निशां स्वपन्। त्रिरह्नि त्रिर्निशायां च सवासा जलमाविशेत्॥
en: He should during the day be under shelter of the sky and should sleep in the same way at night, thrice during the day, and thrice during the night, he should also plunge with the clothes into a river or lake for performing his ablutions.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: स्त्रीशूद्रं पतितं चापि नाभिभाषेद् व्रतान्वितः पापान्यज्ञानतः कृत्वा मुच्येदेवंव्रतो द्विजः॥
en: Practising rigid vows, he should abstain from speaking with women, Shudras, and degraded persons. A Brahmana by observing such rules may be freed off of all sins unconsciously committed by him.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: शुभाशुभफलं प्रेत्य लभते भूतसाक्षिकम्। अतिरिच्येत यो यत्र तत्कर्ता लभते फलम्॥
en: A person reaps in the next world the fruits, good or bad, of his acts here which are all seen by the elements. Proportionate to virtue or vice, one enjoys or suffers the consequences.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: तस्माद् दानेन तपसा कर्मणा च फलं शुभम्। वर्धयेदशुभं कृत्वा यथा स्यादतिरेकवान्॥
en: By knowledge, by penances, and by pious acts, therefore, one multiplies his happiness. One, therefore, may likewise increase his misery by committing sinful acts.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: कुर्याच्छुभानि कर्माणि निवर्तेत् पापकर्मणः। दद्यान्नित्यं च वित्तानि तथा मुच्येत किल्बिषात्॥
en: One should, therefore, perform righteous deeds and avoid altogether sinful ones.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: अनुरूपं हि पापस्य प्रायश्चित्तमुदाहृतम्। महापातकवर्जं तु प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते॥
en: I have now described what the expiations of the sins are. There is expiation for every sin except those that are (highly heinous.)

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: भक्ष्याभक्ष्येषु चान्येषु वाच्यावाच्ये तथैव च। अज्ञानज्ञानयो राजन् विहितान्यनुजानतः॥
en: As regards sins regarding unclean food and the like, and improper speeches, etc., they are of two classes, viz., those committed knowingly and those that committed unconsciously.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: जानता तु कृतं पापं गुरु सर्वं भवत्युत। अज्ञानात् स्वल्पको दोषः प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते॥
en: All sins that are committed knowingly are serious, while those that are committed unwittingly are light. there is expiation for both.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: शक्यते विधिनां पापं यथोक्तेन व्यपोहितुम्। आस्तिके श्रद्दधाने च विधिरेष विधीयते॥
en: Forsooth, sin is capable of being washed away by following the ordinances. Those ordinances, however, have been laid down only for them who have faith in God.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: नास्तिकाश्रद्दधानेषु पुरुषेषु कदाचन। दम्भद्वेषप्रधानेषु विधिरेष न दृश्यते॥
en: They are not for atheists or those that have no faith, or those who are full of pride and malice.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: शिष्टाचारश्च शिष्टश्च धर्मो धर्मभृतां वर। सेवितव्यो नरव्याघ्र प्रेत्येह च सुखेप्सुना॥
en: A person, O foremost of men, who seeks well-being both here and hereafter should, O foremost of virtuous men, always follow virtue, hear the righteous, and satisfy the duties that have been ordained for him.

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: स राजन् मोक्ष्यसे पापात् तेन पूर्णेन हेतुना। प्राणार्थं वा धनेनैषामथवा नृपकर्मणा॥
en: Therefore, for the reasons already pointed out by me, you, O king, shall be freed off of all your sins, for you have slain your enemies in the discharge of your duties as a king and for the protection of your life and inheritance,

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: अथवा ते घृणा काचित् प्रायश्चित्तं चरिष्यसि। मा त्वेवानार्यजुष्टेन मन्युना निधनं गमः॥
en: Or, if despite it, you still consider yourself sinful, perform expiation. Do not cast away your life for such grief that does not become a wise man.'

description: The necessary rites of expiation of sin are describe.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तो भगवता धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तेन प्रत्युवाच तपोधनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said This accosted by the holy Rishi, king Yudhishthira the just, having thought for a short time, said these words to the sage.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं भक्ष्यं चाप्यभक्ष्यं च किं च देयं प्रशस्यते। किं च पात्रमपात्रं वा तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, what food is clean and what, unclean, what gift is praiseworthy, and who is the deserving, and who, undeserving (recipients of gifts).

sn: व्यास उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। सिद्धानां चैव संवादं मनोश्चैव प्रजापतेः॥
en: Vyasa said “Regarding it is cited a old discourse between the ascetics and that lord of creation, viz., Manu.

sn: ऋषयस्तु व्रतपरा: समागम्य पुरा विभुम्। धर्मं पप्रच्छुरासीनमादिकाले प्रजापतिम्॥ कथमन्नं कथं पात्रं दानमध्ययनं तपः। कार्याकार्यं च यत् सर्वं शसं वै त्वं प्रजायते॥ तैरेवमुक्तो भगवान् मनुः स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत्। शुश्रूषध्वं यथावृत्तं धर्मं व्याससमासतः॥
en: In the Krita age, a concourse of Rishis, of rigid vows, having approached the great and powerful lord of creation, Manu, while seated at his case requested him to describe duties, saying,-What food should be taken, who is to be considered a deserving person (for gifts), what gifts should be made, how should a person study and what penances should one perform and how, and what acts should be done and what acts should not be done. O lord of creation, tell us everything in detail. Thus solicited by them, the divine and self-sprung Manu said to them,-Listen to me as I describe the duties in brief and in detail.

sn: अनादेशे जपो होम उपवासस्तथैव च। आत्मज्ञानं पुण्यनद्यो यत्र प्रायश्च तत्पराः॥ अनादिष्टं तथैतानि पुण्यानि धरणीभृतः। सुवर्णप्राशनमपि रत्नादिस्नानमेव च॥
en: In regions which have not been forbidden, silent recitation of sacred Mantras, homa round fasts, knowledge of soul, sacred rivers, regions inhabited by men devoted to pious acts,-these have been laid down as purifying acts and objects. Certain mountains also are purifying, as also the eating of gold and bathing in waters into which have been washed gems and precious stones.

sn: देवस्थानाभिगमनमाज्यप्राशनमेव च। एतानि मेध्यं पुरुषं कुर्वन्त्याशु न संशयः॥
en: Sojourn to sacred pilgrimages and eating of sanctified butter,-these also, forsooth, speedily cleanse a man.

sn: न गर्वेण भवेत् प्राज्ञः कदाचिदपि मानवः। दीर्घमायुरथेच्छन् हि त्रिरात्रं चोष्णपो भवेत्॥
en: No man would ever be called wise if he is proud. If he wishes to live long, he should for three nights drink hot water as an expiation for the same.

sn: अदत्तस्यानुपादानं दानमध्ययनं तपः। अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोध इज्या धर्मस्य लक्षणम्॥
en: Refusal to take what is not given, gift, study of sacred books, penance, abstention from injury, truth, freedom from anger, and adoration of the gods in sacrifices,-these are the marks of virtue.

sn: स एव धर्मः सोऽधर्मो देशकाले प्रतिष्ठितः। आदानमनृतं हिंसा धर्मो ह्यावस्थिकः स्मृतः॥
en: Virtue again, according to time and place, becomes sin. Thus misappropriation of another's property, untruth, and injury and killing, may under special circumstances, become virtue.

sn: द्विविधौ चाप्युभावेतौ धर्माधर्मी विजानताम्। अप्रवृत्तिः प्रवृत्तिश्च द्वैविध्यं लोकवेदयोः॥ अप्रवृत्तेरमर्त्यत्वं मर्त्यत्वं कर्मणः फलम्। अशुभस्याशुभं विद्याच्छुभस्य शुभमेव च। एतयोश्चोभयोः स्यातां शुभाशुभतया तथा॥
en: To persons capable of judging, acts are of two kinds, viz., virtuous and sinful. From the worldly and the Vedic points of view again, virtue and vice become good or bad. From the Vedic point of view, virtue and vice, would be classed under action and inaction. Inaction, i.e., abstention from Vedic rites leads to liberation (from re-birth while the fruits of action) i.e., performance of Vedic rites, leads to repeated death and re-birth. From the worldly point of view, acts that are evil, lead to sins and those that are good, or virtue. From the worldly point of view, therefore, virtue and vice are to be marked out by the good and the evil character of their fruits.

sn: दैवं च दैवसंयुक्तं प्राणश्च प्राणदश्च ह। अपेक्षापूर्वकरणादशुभानां शुभं फलम्॥
en: Even evil acts, when performed for divine purposes, the scriptures, life itself, and the means by which life is sustained, yield good consequences.

sn: ऊर्ध्वं भवति संदेहादिह दृष्टार्थमेव च। अपेक्षापूर्वकरणात् प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते॥
en: Expiation has been laid down, for an act undertaken for the purpose of doing mischief (to some one) in the future, as well as for an act done whose consequence is apparently mischievous.

sn: क्रोधमोहकृते चैव दृष्टान्तागमहेतुभिः। शरीराणामुपक्लेशो मनसश्च प्रियाप्रिये। तदौषधैश्च मन्त्रैश्च प्रायश्चित्तैश्च शाम्यति॥
en: When an act is performed from wrath or misjudgment, then expiation should be performed by paining the body, guided by example by scriptures, and by reason. when any action, is performed for pleasing or displeasing the mind, the sin originating thereform may be cleansed by pure food and recitation of Mantras.

sn: उपवासमेकरात्रं दण्डोत्सर्गे नराधिपः। विशुद्ध्यदात्मशुद्ध्यर्थं त्रिरात्रं तु पुरोहितः॥
en: The king who does not use (in a particular case) the rod of chastisement, should fast for one night. The priest who does not advise the king to inflict punishment (in a proper case) should fast for three nights.

sn: क्षयं शोकं प्रकुर्वाणो न म्रियेत यदा नरः। शस्त्रादिभिरुपाविस्त्रिरात्रं तत्र निर्दिशेत्॥
en: A man who, from grief, attempts to commit suicide by means of weapons, should fast for three nights.

sn: जातिश्रेण्यधिवासानां कुलधर्मांश्च सर्वतः। वर्जयन्ति च ये धर्मं तेषां धर्मो न विद्यते॥
en: There is no expiation for them who do not observe duties and practices of their order and caste, country, and family, and who forsake their own creed.

sn: दश वा वेदशास्त्रज्ञास्त्रयो वा धर्मपाठकाः। यद् ब्रू युः कार्य उत्पन्ने स धर्मो धर्मसंशये॥
en: When any doubt arises regarding what should be done, it should be settled by the injunction of the scriptures which ten persons versed in Vedic scriptures or three of those who frequently recite them may declare.

sn: अनड्वान् मृत्तिका चैव तथा क्षुद्रपिपीलिकाः। श्लेष्मातकस्तथा विप्रैरभक्ष्यं विषमेव च॥
en: The bull, earth, little ants, worms born in dirt, and poison, should not be eaten by Brahmanas.

sn: अभक्ष्या ब्राह्मणैर्मत्स्याः शल्कैर्ये वै विवर्जिताः। चतुष्यात् कच्छपादन्यो मण्डूका जलजाश्च ये॥
en: They should also abstain from eating fishes that have scales, and four-legged aquatic animals like frogs and others, except the tortoise.

sn: भासा हंसाः सुपर्णाश्च चक्रवाका: प्लवा बकाः। काको मद्गुश्च गृधश्च श्येनोलूकस्तथैव च॥ क्रव्यादा दंष्ट्रिणः सर्वे चतुष्पात् पक्षिणश्च ये। येषां चोभयतो दन्ताश्चतुर्दंष्ट्राश्च सर्वशः॥ एडकाश्वखरोष्ट्रीणां सूतिकानां गवामपि।
en: A Brahmana should not also take waterfowls called Bhasas, ducks, Suparnas, Chakravakas, diving ducks, cranes, crow, shags, vultures, hawks, owls, as also all fourlegged carnivorous animals and that have sharp and long teeth, and birds, and animals having two teeth and those having four teeth, as also the milk of the sheep, the she-ass, the shecamel, the newly-calved cow, women and dear.

sn: मानुषीणां मृगीणां च न पिबेद् ब्राह्मणः पयः॥ प्रेतान्नं सूतिकानं च यच्च किंचिदनिर्दशम्। अभोज्यं चाप्यपेयं च धेनोर्दुग्धमनिर्दशम्॥
en: Besides this the good that has been offered to the departed manes, that which has been usurer cooked by a woman who has recently given birth to a child, and food cooked by a unknown person, should not be taken. The milk also of a cow that has recently calved should not be drunk.

sn: राजान्नं तेज आदत्ते शूद्रानं ब्रह्मवर्चसम्। आयुः सुवर्णकारान्नमवीरायाश्च योषितः॥
en: If a Brahmana takes food which has been cooked by a Kshatriya, it diminishes his power; if lie takes the food supplied by effulgence; and if he takes the food supplied by a goldsmith or a woman who has neither husband nor children, it decreases his longevity.

sn: विष्ठा वाधुषिकस्यान्नं गणिकान्नमथेन्द्रियम्। मृष्यन्ति ये चोपपतिं स्त्रीजितान्नं च सर्वशः॥
en: The food supplied by an is equivalent to dirt, while that supplied by a prostitute is equivalent to semen. The food also supplied by persons who connive at the unchastity of their wives, and by persons who are henpecked, is forbidden.

sn: दीक्षितस्य कदर्यस्य ऋतुविक्रयिकस्य च। तक्ष्णश्चर्मावकर्तुश्च पुंश्चल्या रजकस्य च॥ चिकित्सकस्य यच्चान्नमभोज्यं रक्षिणस्तथा। गणग्रामाभिशस्तानां रङ्गस्त्रीजीविनां तथा॥ परिवित्तीनां पुंसां च बन्दिद्युतविदां यथा। वामहस्ताहृतं चान्नं भक्तं पर्युषितं च यत्॥ सुरानुगतमुच्छिष्टमभोज्यं शेषितं च यत्। पिष्टस्य चेक्षुशाकाना विकाराः पयसस्तथा॥
en: The food supplied by a person selected (for receiving present) at a sacrifice; by one who does not enjoy his riches or make any gifts, that supplied by one who sells Soma, or one who is a shoe-maker, by an unchaste woman, by a washerman, by a physician, by watchmen, by a number of persons, by one who is marked by a whole village, by one who lives on the income of dancing girls, by persons marrying before their elder brothers are married, by professional panegyrists and bards, and by gamblers, the food also which is brought with the left hand or which is stale, the food which is mixed with alcohol, the food which is already tasted, and the residue of a feast, should not be taken (by a Brahmana.) Cakes sugarcanes, potherbs, and rice boiled in sugared milk, when of relish should not be taken.

sn: सक्तधानाकरम्भाणां नोपभोग्याश्चिरस्थिताः। पायसं कृसरं मांसमपूपाश्च वृथाकृताः॥ अपेयाश्चाप्यभक्ष्याश्च ब्राह्मणैर्गृहमेधिभिः। देवानृषीन् मनुष्यांश्च पितॄन् गृह्याश्च देवताः॥ पूजयित्वा ततः पश्चाद् गृहस्थो भोक्तुमर्हति। यथा प्रव्रजितो भिक्षुस्तथैव स्वे गृहे वसेत्॥
en: The powder of fried barley and of other sorts of fried gain, mixed with curds, when stale with age, should not be taken, Rice boiled in Sugared milk, food mixed with the Tila seed, meat, and cakes, that have not been dedicated to the gods, should not be taken by Brahmanas, who live as householders. Having first pleased the gods, Rishis, guests, Pitris, and the tutelary deities, a Brahmana householder should then take his food. A householder by living thus in his own house becomes like a person of the mendicant order that has renounced the world.

sn: एवंवृत्तः प्रियैर्दारैः संवसन् धर्ममाप्नुयात्। न दद्याद् यशसे दानं न भयान्नोपकारिणे॥
en: A man of such conduct even living with his wives as a householder, earns great religious merit. No one should make a gift for gaining fame, or from fear of censure or to a benefactor.

sn: न नृत्यगीतशीलेषु हासकेषु च धार्मिकः। न मत्ते चैव नोन्मत्ते न स्तेने न च कुत्सके॥ न वाग्धीने विवणे वा नाङ्गहीने न वामने। न दुर्जने दौष्कुले वा व्रतैर्यो वा न संस्कृतः।
en: A pious man would never make gifts to persons living by singing and dancing or to those that are jesters by profession, or to a। drunkard, or to a mad man, or to a thief, or to slanderer or to an idiot, or to one that is pale coloured or to one that is defective of a limb, or to a dwarf, or to wicked person, or to one born in a degraded and wicked family, or to one that has not been sanctified by the observance of VOWS.

sn: न श्रोत्रियमृते दानं ब्राह्मणे ब्रह्मवर्जिते॥ असम्यक् चैव यद् दत्तमसम्यक् च प्रतिग्रहः। उभयं स्यादनाय दातुरादातुरेव च॥
en: No gift should be made to a Brahmana who has no knowledge of the Vedas Gifts should be made to him only who is well read in the Vedas. An improper gift and an improper acceptance beget bad consequences to both the giver and the acceptor.

sn: यथा खदिरमालम्ब्य शिलां वाप्यर्णवं तरन्। मज्जेत मज्जतस्तद्वद् दाता यश्च प्रतिग्रही।॥
en: As a person who tries to cross the sea with the help of a rock or a mass of catechu sinks with the supports, so the improper giver and the acceptor both sink together.

sn: काष्ठेरादैर्यथा वह्निरुपस्तीर्णो न दीप्यते। तपःस्वाध्यायचारित्रैरेवं हीनः प्रतिग्रही॥
en: As a fire that is covered with wet fuel does not burn, so the acceptor of a gift who has not practised penances, and piety to those who studied Vedas, but cannot confer any benefit (upon the giver).

sn: कपाले यद्वदापः स्युः श्वदृतौ च यथा पयः। आश्रयस्थानदोषेण वृत्तहीने तथा श्रुतम्॥
en: As water in a skull and milk in a bag made of dog-skin become impure for the uncleanness of the vessels in which they are kept, so the Vedas become fruitless in a person who is not of good conduct.

sn: निर्मन्त्रो निर्वृतो यः स्यादशास्त्रज्ञोऽनसूयकः। अनुक्रोशात् प्रदातव्यं हीनेष्वव्रतिकेषु च॥
en: One may give from pity to a low Brahmana who is without Mantras and vows, who is innocent of the scriptures and who is envious.

sn: न वै देयमनुक्रोशाद् दीनायाप्यपकारिणे। आप्ताचरित इत्येव धर्म इत्येव वा पुनः॥
en: One may, from pity, give to a person who is poor or afflicted or ill. But he should not make charities to such a person with the belief that he would drive any (spiritual) benefit from it or that he would acquire any religious merit by it.

sn: निष्कारणं स्मृतं दत्तं ब्राह्मणे ब्रह्मवर्जिते। भवेदपात्रदोषेण न चात्रास्ति विचारणा॥
en: Forsooth, gift made to a Brahmana ignorant of the Vedas, becomes perfectly fruitless for the shortcomings of the recipient.

sn: यथा दारुमयो हस्ती यथा चर्ममयो मृगः। ब्राह्मणश्चानधीयानस्त्रयस्ते नाम बिभ्रति॥
en: As an elephant made of wood, or an antelope made of leather, so is a Brahmana who has not read the Vedas. All the three have nothing but names.

sn: यथा षण्ढोऽफलः स्त्रीषु यथा गौर्गवि चाफला। शकुनिर्वाप्यपक्षः स्यान्निर्मन्त्रो ब्राह्मणस्तथा॥
en: As a eunuch cannot beget children on women, as a cow does not procreats on another cow, as a bird lives in vain that is featherless, even so is a Brahmana that without Mantras.

sn: ग्रामो धान्यैर्यथा शून्यो यथा कूपश्च निर्जलः। यथा हुतमनग्नौ च तथैव स्यान्निराकृतौ॥
en: As grain without kernel, as a well without water, as libations poured on ashes, even so is a gift to a Brahmana who is ignorant.

sn: देवतानां पितृणां च हव्यकव्यविनाशकः। शत्रुरर्थहरो मूर्यो न लोकान् प्राप्तुमर्हति॥
en: An unlearned Brahmana is an enemy (to all) and is the destroyer of the food that is offered to the gods and the departed manes. A gift made to such a person become useless. He is, therefore, like a robber. He can never attain to blissful regions hereafter.

sn: एतत् ते कथितं सर्वं यथावृत्तं युधिष्ठिर। समासेन महङ्ख्येतच्छ्रोतव्यं भरतर्षभ॥
en: now I have told you in brief, O Yudhishthira, all that was said by Manu on that occasion. This high discourse should be listened to by all, O foremost of Bharata's race.'

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रोतुमिच्छामि भगवन् विस्तरेण महामुने। राजधर्मान् द्विजश्रेष्ठ चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य चाखिलान्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O holy and great ascetic, I wish to hear at length what the duties of kings are and what the duties, in full, of all the four orders.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: आपत्सु च यथा नीतिः प्रणेतव्या द्विजोत्तम। धर्म्यमालक्ष्य पन्थानं विजयेयं कथं महीम्॥
en: I wish to hear, O foremost of Brahmanas, how persons should behave in times of distress, and how I may subjugate the world by following path of morality.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: प्रायश्चित्तकथा ह्येषा भक्ष्याभक्ष्यविवर्जिता। कौतूहलानुप्रवणा हर्ष जनयतीव मे॥
en: This discourse on expiation, describing facts and capable of exciting great curiosity, has pleased me.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: धर्मचर्या च राज्यं च नित्यमेव विरुध्यते। एवं मुह्याति मे चेतश्चिन्तयानस्य नित्यशः॥
en: The practice of virtue and the performance of royal duties are always inconsistent with each other. I am always perplexed to think how one may reconcile the two.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तमुवाच महाराज व्यासो वेदविदां वरः। नारदं समभिप्रेक्ष्य सर्वज्ञानां पुरातनम्॥ श्रोतुमिच्छसि चेद् धर्मं निखिलेन नराधिप। प्रैहि भीष्मं महाबाहो वृद्धं कुरुपितामहम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then Vyasa, O king, that foremost of all persons conversant with the Vedas, looking at that ancient and omniscient person, viz., Narada, said,-If O king, you wish to hear of duties and morality at length, then ask Bhishma, O mighty-armed one, that old grandfather of the Kurus.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: स ते धर्मरहस्येषु संशयान् मनसि स्थितान्। छेत्ता भागीरथीपुत्रः सर्वज्ञः सर्वधर्मवित्॥
en: Conversant with all duties and endued with universal knowledge that son of Bhagirathi will remove all your doubts regarding the difficult subjects of duties.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: जनयामास यं देवी दिव्या त्रिपथगा नदी। साक्षाद् ददर्श यो देवान् सर्वानिन्द्रपुरोगमान्॥
en: That goddess the celestial river of three courses, gave birth to him. He saw with his physical eyes all the celestials headed by Indra.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: बृहस्पतिपुरोगांस्तु देवर्षीनसकृत् प्रभुः। तोषयित्वोपचारेण राजनीतिमधीतवान्॥
en: Having pleased with his dutiful services the celestial Rishis, headed by Brihaspati, he acquired a knowledge of royal duties.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: उशना वेद यच्छास्त्रं यच्च देवगुरुर्द्विजः। तच्च सर्वं सवैयाख्यं प्राप्तवान् कुरुसत्तमः॥
en: That foremost one among the Kurus acquired a knowledge also of that science, with its interpretations, which Ushanas and the Rishi who is the preceptor of the celestials know.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: भार्गवाच्च्यवनाच्चापि वेदानगोपबंहितान्। प्रतिपेदे महाबाहुर्वसिष्ठाच्चरितव्रतः॥
en: Having practised rigid vows, that mightyarined one obtained a knowledge of all the Vedas and their branches, from Vashishtha and from Chyavana of Bhrigu's race.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: पितामहसुतं ज्येष्ठं कुमारं दीप्ततेजसम्। अध्यात्मगतितत्त्वज्ञमुपाशिक्षत यः पुरा॥
en: In the days of yore he studied under the eldest son of the Grandfather himself, viz., the effulgent Sanatkumara, well conversant with the truths of mental and spiritual science.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: मार्कण्डेयमुखात् कृत्स्नं यतिधर्ममवाप्तवान्। रामादस्त्राणि शक्राच्च प्राप्तवान् पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: He learnt the duties in full of the Yatis from Markandeya. That foremost of men learnt the science from Rama and Shakra.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: मृत्युरात्मेच्छया यस्य जातस्य मनुजेष्वपि! तथानपत्यस्य सतः पुण्यलोका दिवि श्रुताः॥
en: Although born as man, his death itself is in his own hands. Although childless, yet he has many blissful regions hereafter as heard by us.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: यस्य ब्रह्मर्षयः पुण्या नित्यमासन सभासदः। यस्य नाविदितं किंचिज्ज्ञानयज्ञेषु विद्यते॥
en: Rishis of great merit were his courtiers. There is nothing on earth which is unknown to him.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: स ते वक्ष्यति धर्मज्ञः सूक्ष्मधर्मार्थतत्त्ववित्। तमभ्येहि पुरा प्राणान् स विमुञ्चति धर्मवित्॥
en: Conversant with all duties and the subtile truths of morality, he wili describe to you the duty and morality. See him before he dies.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु कौन्तेयो दीर्घप्रज्ञो महामतिः उवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठं व्यासं सत्यवतीसुतम्॥
en: Thus accosted by him, the high-souled and wise son of Kunti, said the following to Satyavati's son Vyasa, that foremost of all orators.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच वैशसं सुमहत् कृत्वा ज्ञातीनां रोमहर्षणम्। आगस्कृत् सर्वलोकस्य पृथिवीनाशकारकः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Having caused a great and dreadful destruction of kinsmen, I have offended all and am a destroyer of the Earth.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: घातयित्वा तमेवाजौ छलेनाजिह्मयोधिनम्। उपसम्प्रष्टुमर्हामि तमहं केन हेतुना॥
en: Having caused that Bhishma himself, that honest warrior, to be killed deceitfully how shall I approach him for asking him (about duties and morality)?

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तं नृपतिश्रेष्ठं चातुर्वर्ण्यहितेप्सया। पुनराह महाबाहुर्यदुश्रेष्ठो महामतिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Actuated by the desire of benefiting all the four orders, the mighty-armed and great chief of Yadu's race once more addressed that

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: वासुदेव उवाच नेदानीमतिनिर्बन्धं शोके त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि। यदाह भगवान् व्यासस्तत् कुरुष्व नृपोत्तम॥
en: You should not thus continually indulge in grief. Do, O best of kings, what the holy Vyasa has said.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: ब्राह्मणास्त्वां महाबाहो भ्रातरच महौजसः। पर्जन्यमिव घर्मान्ते नाथमाना उपासते॥
en: The Brahmanas, O mighty-armed one, and these your highly energetic brothers stand before you beseechingly like persons soliciting Indra the gods of the clouds at the close of summer.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: हतशिष्टाश्च राजानः कृत्स्नं चैव समागतम्। चातुर्वण्र्यं महाराज राष्ट्रं ते कुरुजाङ्गलम्॥
en: The surviving kings, and the people belonging to all the four orders of your kingdom of Kurujangala, O king, are here.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: प्रियार्थमपि चैतेषां ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम्। नियोगादस्य च गुरोर्व्यासस्यामिततेजसः॥ सुहृदामस्मदादीनां द्रौपद्याश्च परंतप। कुरु प्रियममित्रन लोकस्य च हितं कुरु॥
en: For the sake of doing what is agreeable to these great Brahmanas, for satisfying the behest of your reverend senior Vyasa of immeasurable energy, and at the request of ourselves who are well-wishers, and of Draupadi, O destroyer of foes, do what is agreeable to us, O slayer of foes, and what is beneficial to the world.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः स कृष्णेन राजा राजीवलोचनः हितार्थं सर्वलोकस्य समुत्तस्थौ महात्मनाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by Krishna, the great king (Yudhishthira) having eyes like lotus petals, rose from his seat for the well-being of the entire world.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: सोऽनुनीतो नरव्याघ्र विष्टरश्रवसा स्वयम्। द्वैपायनेन च तथा देवस्थानेन जिष्णुना॥ एतैश्चान्यैश्च बहुभिरनुनीतो युधिष्ठिरः। व्यजहान्मानसं दुःखं संतापं च महायशाः॥
en: That foremost of men, the illustrious Yudhishthira, solicited by Krishna himself, by the Dvaipayana (Vyasa), by Devasthana, by Jishnu, by these and many others, shook off his grief, and anxiety.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: श्रुतवाक्यः श्रुतनिधिः श्रुतश्रव्यविशारदः। व्यवस्य मनसः शान्तिमगच्छत् पाण्डुनन्दनः॥
en: Full conversant with the teachings of the Srutis, with the science that explains them and with all that men usually hear and all that is worthy of being heard, the son of Pandu acquired peace of mind and resolved upon what he should next do.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: स तैः परिवृतो राजा नक्षत्रैरिव चन्द्रमाः। धृतराष्ट्र पुरस्कृत्य स्वपुरं प्रविवेश ह॥
en: Surrounded by them all like the moon by the stars, the king, placing Dhritarashtra at the head started for the city.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: प्रविविक्षुः स धर्मज्ञः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। अर्चयामास देवांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: Desirous of entering the city, Kunti's son Yudhishthira, conversant with everyday, worshipped the gods and thousands of Brahmanas.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: ततो नवं रथं शुभं कम्बलाजिनसंवृतम्। युक्तं षोडशभिर्गोभिः पाण्डुरैः शुभलक्षणैः॥ मन्त्रैरभ्यर्चितं पुण्यैः स्तूयमानश्च बन्दिभिः। आरुरोह यथा देवः सोमोऽमृतमयं रथम्॥
en: He then got upon a new and white car covered with blankets and deer-skins, and to which were yoked sixteen white bullocks endued with auspicious marks, and which had been purified with Vedic Mantras. Adored by panegyrists and bards, the king got upon that car like Soma riding upon his own nectarine vehicle.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: जग्राह रश्मीन् कौन्तेयो भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। अर्जुनः पाण्डुरं छत्रं धारयामास भानुमत्॥
en: His powerful brother Bhima took the reins. Arjuna held over his head a highly lustrous umbrella.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: ध्रियमाणं तच्छत्रं पाण्डुरं रथमूर्धनि। शुशुभे तारकाकीर्णं सितमभ्रमिवाम्बरे॥
en: That white a umbrella held upon the car shone like a white cloud adorned with stars in the sky.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: चामरव्यजने त्वस्य वीरौ जगृहतुस्तदा। चन्द्ररश्मिप्रभे शुभ्रे माद्रीपुत्रावलंकृते॥
en: The two heroic sons of Madri, viz., Nakula and Sahadeva, took up two yak-tails white as the rays of the moon and let with gems, for fanning the king.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: ते पञ्च रथमास्थाय भ्रातरः समलंकृताः। भूतानीव समस्तानि राजन् ददृशिरे तदा।॥
en: The five brothers, adorned with ornaments, having got upon the car, O king, shone like the five elements.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: आस्थाय तु रथं शुभ्रं युक्तमश्वैर्मनोजवैः। अन्वयात् पृष्ठतो राजन् युयुत्सुः पाण्डवाग्रजम्॥
en: Riding upon another white car to which were yoked horses fleet as thought, Yuyutsu, O king, followed the eldest son of Pandu.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: रथं हेममयं शुभं शैव्यसुग्रीवयोजितम्। सह सात्यकिना कृष्णः समास्थायान्वयात् कुरून्॥३९।
en: Upon his own shining car of gold to which were yoked Shivya and Sugriva. Krishna, with Satyaki, followed the Kurus.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: नरयानेन तु ज्येष्ठः पिता पार्थस्य भारत। अग्रतो धर्मराजस्य गान्धारीसहितो ययौ॥
en: The eldest uncle of Pritha's son, O Bharata, accompanied by Gandhari, headed the train, upon a vehicle carried by men.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: कुरुस्त्रियश्च ताः सर्वाः कुन्ती कृष्णा तथैव च। यानरुच्चावचैर्जग्मुर्विदुरेण पुरस्कृताः॥
en: The other Kuru ladies, as also Kunti and Krishna, all proceeded on excellent cars, headed by Vidura.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: ततो रथाश्च बहुला नागाश्वसमलंकृताः। पादाताश्च हयाश्चैव पृष्ठतः समनुव्रजन्॥
en: Then followed a large number of cars and elephants adorned with ornaments, and the infantry and horses.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: ततो वैतालिकैः सूतैर्मागधैश्च सुभाषितैः। स्तूयमानो ययौ राजा नगरं नागसाह्वयम्॥
en: His praises sung by sweet-voiced panegyrists and birds, the king went towards the city of Hastinapur.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: तत् प्रयाणं महाबाहोर्बभूवाप्रतिमं भुवि। आकुलाकुलमुत्क्रुष्टं हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलम्॥
en: The march, O might-armed one, of king Yudhishthira, was so beautiful that its like had never been witnessed on Earth. Containing healthy and cheerful men, the busy hum of numberless voices was heard there.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: अभियाने तु पार्थस्य नरैर्नगरवासिभिः। नगरं राजमार्गाश्च यथावत्समलकृताः॥
en: During the march of Pritha's son, the city and its streets were adorned with lively citizens.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: पाण्डुरेण च माल्येन पताकाभिश्च मेदिनी। संस्कृतो राजमार्गोऽभूद्धूपनैश्च प्रधूपितः॥
en: The part through which the king passed had been adorned with white festoons of flowers and numberless flags. The streets of the city were perfumed with incense.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: अथ चूर्णैश्च गन्धानां नानापुष्पप्रियङ्गद्धभिः। माल्यदामभिरासक्तै राजवेश्माभिसंवृतम्॥
en: The palace was covered with powdered perfumes and flowers and fragrant plants, and ornamented with garlands and wreaths.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: कुम्भाश्च नगरद्वारि वारिपूर्णा नवा दृढाः। सिताः सुमनसो गौरा: स्थापितास्तत्र तत्र ह॥
en: New inetallic jars, brimful with water, were kept at the door of every house, and bevies of beautiful maidens stood at different parts.

description: Vyasa describes what food is clean and what unclean.
sn: तथा स्वलंकृतद्वारं नगरं पाण्डुनन्दनः। स्तूयमानः शुभैर्वाक्यैः प्रविवेश सुहृवृतः॥
en: Accompanied by his friends, and welcomed with sweet words the son of Pandu, entered the city through its well-adorned gate.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रवेशने तु पार्थानां जनानां पुरवासिनाम्। दिदृक्षूणां सहस्राणि समाजग्मुः सहस्रशः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then the sons of Pritha entered the city, thousands of citizens came out to see the spectacle.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: स राजमार्गः शुशुभे समलंकृतचत्वरः। यथा चन्द्रोदये राजन् वर्धमानो महोदधिः॥
en: The well adorned squares and streets, with the crowd of men, shone like the ocean rising at the rise of the moon.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: गृहाणि राजमार्गेषु रत्नवन्ति महान्ति च। प्राकम्पन्तेव भारेण स्त्रीणां पूर्णानि भारत॥
en: The large palaces that stood on the streetsides, gaily decked and full of ladies seemed to shake, O Bharata, with their fair denizens.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: ताः शनैरिव सव्रीडं प्रशशंसुर्युधिष्ठिरम्। भीमसेनार्जुनौ चैव माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ॥
en: With soft and modest voices they described the praises of Yudhishthira, of Bhima and Arjuna, and of the two sons of Madri.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: धन्या त्वमसि पाञ्चालि या त्वं पुरुषसत्तमान्। उपतिष्ठसि कल्याणि महर्षीनिव गौतमी॥
en: And they said,-You deserve every praise, O blessed princess of Panchala, who wait by the side of these foremost of men like Gautaini by the side of the (seven) Rishis.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: तव कर्माण्यमोघानि व्रतचर्या च भाविनि। इति कृष्णां महाराज प्रशशंसुस्तदा स्त्रियः॥
en: 'Your acts and vows have fructified, O lady.' Thus, O king, the ladies praised the princess Krishna.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: प्रशंसावचनस्तासां मिथ:शब्दैश्च भारत। प्रीतिजैश्च तदा शब्दैः पुरमासीत् समाकुलम्॥
en: Praises being thus chanted, O Bharata, and they conversing with one another, and for the shouts of joy (uttered by the men), the city became filled with a loud noise.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: तमतीत्य यथायुक्तं राजमार्ग युधिष्ठिरः। अलंकृतं शोभमानमुपायाद् राजवेश्म ह॥
en: Having passed through the streets with becoming conduct, Yudhishthira then entered the beautiful palace (of the Kurus) adorned with all ornaments.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: ततः प्रकृतयः सर्वाः पौरा जानपदास्तदा। ऊचुः कर्णसुखा वाचः समुपेत्य ततस्ततः॥
en: Approaching the palace, citizens and villagers uttered speeches that were pleasing to his ears.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: दिष्ट्या जयसि राजेन्द्र शत्रूञ्छत्रुनिषूदन। दिष्ट्या राज्यं पुनः प्राप्तं धर्मेण च बलेन च।॥
en: 'By good luck, O foremost of kings, you have defeated your enemies, O slayer of foes. By good luck, you have regained your kingdom through virtue and prowess.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: भव नस्त्वं महाराज राजेह शरदां शतम्। प्रजाः पालय धर्मेण यथेन्द्रस्त्रिदिवं तथा॥
en: Be, O foremost of king, our monarch for a century and protect your subjects virtuously like Indra protecting the celestials'.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: एवं राजकुलद्वारि मङ्गलैरभिपूजितः। आशीर्वादान् द्विजैरुक्तान् प्रतिगृह्य समन्ततः॥ प्रविश्य भवनं राजा देवराजगृहोपमम्। श्रद्धाविजयसंयुक्तं रथात् पश्चादवातरत्॥
en: Thus welcomed at the palace-gate with words of blessings and accepting the benedictions uttered by the Brahmanas from all sides, the king, graced with victory and the blessings of his people, entered the palace resembling the mansion of Indra himself, and then got down from his car.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: प्रविश्याभ्यन्तरं श्रीमान् दैवतान्यभिगम्य च। पूजयामास रत्नैश्च गन्धमाल्यैश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Entering the palace, Yudhishthira approached the tutelary deities and adored them with gems and scents and garlands.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: निश्चक्राम ततः श्रीमान् पुनरेव महायशाः। ददर्श ब्राह्मणांश्चैव सोऽभिरूपानवस्थितान्॥
en: Endued with great fame and prosperity, the king came out once more and saw a number of Brahmanas waiting with sacred articles in their hands.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: स संवृतस्तदा विप्रैराशीर्वादविवक्षुभिः। शुशुभे विमलश्चन्द्रस्तारागणवृतो यथा॥
en: Surrounded by those Brahmanas desirous of uttering blessings on him, the king shone beautiful like the spotless moon in the midst of the stars.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: तांस्तु वै पूजयामास कौन्तेयो विधिवद् द्विजान्। धौम्यं गुरुं पुरस्कृत्य ज्येष्ठं पितरमेव च।॥ सुमनोमोदकै रत्नैर्हिरण्येन च भूरिणा। गोभिर्वस्त्रैश्च राजेन्द्र विविधैश्च किमिच्छकैः॥
en: Accompanied by his priest Dhaumya and his eldest uncle, the son of Kunti gladly adored, with due rites, those Brahmanas with sweets, gems, and profuse gold, and kine and dresses, O king, and with various other articles that each desired.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: ततः पुण्याहघोषोऽभूद् दिवं स्तब्ध्वेव भारत। सुहृदां प्रीतिजननः पुण्यः श्रुतिसुखावहः॥
en: Then loud acclamations of—This is a blessed day,-arose, filling the entire sky, O Bharata. That sacred sound which was sweet to the ear was highly gratifying to the friends and well-wishers of the Pandavas.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: हंसवद् विदुषां राजन् द्विजानां तत्र भारती। शुश्रुवे वेदविदुषां पुष्कलार्थपदाक्षरा॥
en: The king heard that sound uttered by those learned Brahmanas loud and clear like the sound of swans. He listened also to the melodious and significant speeches, of those persons well read in the Vedas.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: ततो दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषः शङ्खानां च मनोरमः। जयं प्रवदतां तत्र स्वनः प्रादुरभून्नृप॥
en: Then arose, O king, the peal of drums and the pleasant blare of conchs, indicative of triumph.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: निःशब्दे च स्थिते तत्र ततो विप्रजने पुनः। राजानं ब्राह्मणच्छद्या चार्वाको राक्षसोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Some time after, when the Brahmanas had become silent, a Rakshasa of the name of Charvaka, who had disguised himself as a Brahmana, addressed the king.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: तत्र दुर्योधनसखा भिक्षुरूपेण संवृतः। साक्षः शिखी त्रिदण्डी च धृष्टो विगतसाध्वसः॥ वृतः सर्वैस्तथा विप्रैराशीर्वादविवक्षुभिः। परःसहनै राजेन्द्र तपोनियमसंवृतः॥
en: He was a friend of Duryodhana and stood there under the disguise of a religious mendicant. With a rosary, with a tuft of hair on his head, and with a staff in his hand, he stood proudly and fearlessly in the midst of all those Brahmanas that had come there in thousands for uttering for blessings, (upon the king) O king, and all of whom had practised penances and vows.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
sn: स दुष्टः पापमाशंसुः पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। अनामन्त्र्यैव तान् विप्नांस्तमुवाच महीपतिम्॥
en: That wicked Rakshasa, desirous of doing evil to the high-souled Pandavas, and without having consulted those Brahmanas, said these words to the king.

description: Vyasa ask Yudhishthira, on being asked, to enquired of Bhishma the duties of the four orders.
