en: Does your knowledge, O sinless one, shine in you by inward light? I hope your heart does not feel pain and your mind is no longer agitated?'

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: भीष्म उवाच दाहो मोहः श्रमश्चैव क्लमो ग्लानिस्तथा रुजा। तव प्रसादाद् वार्ष्णेय सद्यः प्रतिगतानि मे॥
en: Bhishma said Burning, stupefaction, toil, exhaustion, and pain, through your Grace, O you of Vrishni's race, have all left me in a single day.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: यच्च भूतं भविष्यच्च भवच्च परमाते। तत् सर्वमनुपश्यामि पाणौ फलमिवार्पितम्॥
en: O you of matchless splendour, I behold as distinctly as a fruit placed in my hands, all that is past, all that is future, and all that is present.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: वेदोक्ताश्चैव ये धर्मा वेदान्ताधिगताच ये। तान् सर्वान् सम्प्रपश्यामि वरदानात् तवाच्युत॥
en: I behold clearly, O you of unfading glory, by virtue of the boon granted by you to me, all the duties laid down in the Vedas, and in the Vedantas.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: शिष्टैश्च धर्मो यः प्रोक्तः स च मे हृदि वर्तते। देशजातिकुलानां च धर्मज्ञोऽस्मि जनार्दन।॥
en: The duties that have been described by persons of learning and righteous conduct are still fresh in my memory. I am conversant also, O Janardana, with the duties and practices obtaining in particular countries and among particular tribes and families.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: चतुर्वाश्रमधर्मेषु योऽर्थः स च हृदि स्थितः। राजधर्मांश्च सकलानवगच्छामि केशव॥
en: I remember again everything regarding the four modes of life. I am acquainted, O Keshava, with the royal duties.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: यच्च यत्र च वक्तव्यं तद् वक्ष्यामि जनार्दन। तव प्रसादाद्धि शुभा मनो मे बुद्धिराविशत्॥
en: I would say, O Janardana, everything in its proper hour. Through your favour, I have acquired an auspicious understanding.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: युवेवास्मि समावृत्तस्त्वदनुधयनबंहितः। वक्तुं श्रेयः समर्थोऽस्मि त्वत्प्रसादाज्जनार्दन॥
en: Strengthened by contemplation of you, I feel as if I have become a young man again. Through your favour, O Janardana, I have become capable to talk on what is for the behoof of the world.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: स्वयं किमर्थं तु भवाश्रेयो न प्राह पाण्डवम्। किं ते विवक्षितं चात्र तदाशु वद माधव॥
en: Why, however, O holy one, do you not yourself describe to Pandu's son all that is good? What explanation can you give about it? Tell me quickly, O Madhava.'

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: वासुदेव उवाच यशसः श्रेयसंश्चैव मूलं मां विद्धि कौरव। मत्तः सर्वेऽभिनिर्वृत्ता भावाः सदसदात्मकाः॥
en: Vasudeva said Know, O you of Kuru's race, that I am the root of fame and of everything that produces good. All things, good or bad, emanate from me.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: शीतांशुश्चन्द्र इत्युक्ते लोके को विस्पयिष्यति। तथैव यशसा पूर्णे मयि को विस्मयिष्यति॥
en: Who on Earth will wonder if the Moon be said possessing cool rays? Similarly, who will wonder if I were described as one endued with the greatest fame.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: आधेयं तु मया भूयो यशस्तव महाद्युते। ततो मे विपुला बुद्धिस्त्वयि भीष्म समर्पिता॥
en: I have, however, resolved to enhance your fame, O you of great splendour. It is for this, O Bhishma, that I have just filled you with great intelligence.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: याबद्धि पृथिवीपाल पृथ्वीयं स्थास्यति ध्रुवा। तावत् तत्तवाक्षया कीर्तिर्लोकाननुचरिष्यति॥
en: As long, O king, as the Earth will last, so long will your fame travel with unmitigated lustre through all the worlds.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: यच्च त्वं वक्ष्यसे भीष्म पाण्डवायानुपृच्छते। वेदप्रवाद इव ते स्थास्यते वसुधातले॥
en: Whatever, O Bhishma, you will say to the inquiring son of Pandu, will pass on Earth like the authoritative declarations of the Vedas.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: यश्चैतेन प्रमाणेन योक्ष्यत्यात्मानमात्मना। स फलं सर्वपुण्यानां प्रेत्य चानुभविष्यति।॥
en: That person, who will follow the authority of your declarations, will obtain hereafter the meed of every meritorious act.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: एतस्मात् कारणाद् भीष्म मतिर्दिव्या मया हि ते। दत्ता यशो विप्रथयेत् कथं भूयस्तवेति ह॥
en: For this reason, O Bhishma, I have conferred on you celestial understanding so that your fame may be increased on Earth.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: यावद्धि प्रथते लोके पुरुषस्य यशो भुवि। तावत् तस्याक्षयं स्थानं भवतीति विनिश्चिता॥
en: As long as a man's fame lasts in the world, so long are his good deeds alive.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: राजानो हतशिष्टास्त्वां राजन्नभित आसते। धर्माननुयुयुक्षन्तस्तेभ्यः प्रब्रूहि भारत॥
en: The unslain residue of the kings are sitting around you, desirous of hearing your discourses on morality and duty. Do you speak to them, O Bharata.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: भवान् हि वयसा वृद्धः श्रुताचारसमन्वितः। कुशलो राजधर्माणां सर्वेषामपराश्च ये॥
en: You are aged and your conduct is consistent with the injunctions of the Shrutis. You are a master of the royal duties and of every other science of duty.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: जन्मप्रभृति ते कश्चिद् वृजिनं न ददर्श ह। ज्ञातारं सर्वधर्माणां त्वां विदुः सर्वपार्थिवाः॥
en: No one, has ever marked the slightest transgression in you since your very birth. All the kings know you to be master of the sciences of morality and duty.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: तेभ्यः पितेव पुत्रेभ्यो राजन् ब्रूहि परं नयम्। ऋषयश्चैव देवाश्च त्वया नित्यमुपासिताः॥
en: Like a father to his sons do you, therefore, O king, describe to them high morality. You have always adored the Rishis and the gods.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: तस्माद् वक्तव्यमेवेदं त्वयावश्यमशेषतः! धर्मं शुश्रूषमाणेभ्यः पृष्टेन च सता पुनः॥ वक्तव्यं विदुषा चेति धर्ममाहुर्मनीषिणाः।
en: You should discourse on these subjects fully to persons desirous of listening to discourses on morality and duty. A learned person, especially when requested by the righteous, should talk of the same. The sages have declared this to be a duty.

description: Yudhishthira with all the Pandavas go again to Bhishma.
sn: अप्रतिब्रुवत: कष्टो दोषो हि भविता प्रभो॥ तस्मात् पुत्रैश्च पौत्रेश्च धर्मान् पृष्टान् सनातनान्। विद्वाजिज्ञासमानस्त्वं प्रब्रूहि भरतर्षभ॥
en: O powerful one if you do not speak on such subjects, you will incur sin. Therefore, questioned by your sons and grandsons, o learned one, about the eternal duties (of men), do you, O foremost of the Bharatas, describe this subject them.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथाब्रवीन्महातेजा वाक्यं कौरवनन्दनः। हन्त धर्मान् प्रवक्ष्यामि दृढे वाङ्मनसी मम॥ तव प्रसादाद् गोविन्द भूतात्मा ह्यासि शाश्वतः।
en: Vaishampayana said The highly energetic delighter of Kurus, viz., Bhishma said,—'I shall describe the subject of duty. My speech and mind have become steady, through your favour, O Govinda, since you are the eternal soul of every being.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु धर्मात्मा मां धर्माननुपृच्छतु। एवं प्रीतो भविष्यामि धर्मान् वक्ष्यामि चाखिलान्॥
en: Let the righteous-souled Yudhishthira enquire of me about morality and duty. I shall then be much pleased to speak of all duties.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: यस्मिन् राजर्षभे जाते धर्मात्मनि महात्मनि। अहृष्यन्नृषयः सर्वे स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डव॥
en: Let the son of Pandu, that virtuous and noble royal sage, upon whose birth all the Vrishnis were filled with joy, question me.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: सर्वेषां दीप्तयशसां कुरूणां धर्मचारिणाम्। यस्य नास्ति समः कश्चित् स मां पृच्छतुं पाण्डवः॥४
en: Let the son of Pandu, who has no peer among all the Kurus, among all righteous persons and among celebrated men question me.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: धृतिर्दमो ब्रह्मचर्यं क्षमा धर्मश्च नित्यदा। यस्मिन्नोजश्च स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥
en: let the son of Pandu, who is endued with intelligence, self-restraint, Brahmacharya, forgiveness righteousness, mental vigour and energy, question me.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: सम्बन्धिनोऽतिथीन् भृत्यान् संश्रितांश्चैव यो भृशम्। सम्मानयति सत्कृत्य स मा पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥
en: Let the son of Pandu, who always by his favour honours his relative and guests and servants and dependants, question me.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: सत्यं दानं तपः शौर्य शान्तिर्दाक्ष्यमसम्भ्रमः। यस्मिन्नेतानि सर्वाणि स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥
en: Let the son of Pandu, who is settled in truth, charity, penances, heroism, peacefulness, cleverness, and fearlessness, question me.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: यो न कामान्न संरम्भान्न भयानार्थकारणात्। कुर्यादधर्मं धर्मात्मा स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥
en: Let the pious son of Pandu, who would never commit a sin actuated by desire of pleasure of profit or from fear, question me.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: सत्यनित्यः क्षमानित्यो ज्ञाननित्योऽतिथिप्रियः। यो ददाति सतां नित्यं स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥
en: Let the son of Pandu, who is ever truthful, forgiving, endued with knowledge, and attentive to guests and who always makes gifts to the pious, question me.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: इज्याध्ययननित्यस्य धर्मे च निरतः सदा। क्षान्तः श्रुतरहस्यश्च स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥
en: Let the son of Pandu, who always celebrates sacrifices and studies the Vedas and satisfies the morality and duty, who is ever peaceful and who has heard all mysteries, question me.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: वासुदेव उवाच लज्जया परयोपेतो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। अभिशापभयाद् भीतो भवन्तं नोपसर्पति॥
en: Vasudeva said 'King Yudhishthira, possessed by great shame and fearing your imprecations, does not venture to approach you.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: लोकस्य कदनं कृत्वा लोकनाथो विशाम्पते। अभिशापभयाद् भीतो भवन्तं नोपसर्पति॥
en: That king, O monarch, having caused a great carnage, ventures not to approach you from fear of your curse.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: पूज्यान् मान्यांश्च भक्तांश्च गुरून् सम्बन्धिबान्धवान्। अर्घार्हानिषुभिर्भित्त्वा भवन्तं नोपसर्पति॥
en: Having wounded with arrows those who were worthy of his worship, those who were devoted to him, those who were his preceptors, those who were his relatives and kinsmen, and those who deserved his highest regard, he ventures not to approach you.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: भीष्म उवाच ब्राह्मणानां यथा धर्मो दानमध्ययनं तपः। क्षत्रियाणां तथा कृष्ण समरे देहपातनम्॥
en: Bhishma said As the duty of the Brahmanas is to practise charity, to study, and perform penances, so the duty of Kshatriyas is to renounce their bodies, OKrishna, in battle.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: पितॄन् पितामहान् भ्रातृन् गुरून् सम्बन्धिबान्धवान्। मिथ्याप्रवृत्तान् यः संख्ये निहन्याद् धर्म एव सः॥
en: Kshatriyas should kill fathers and grandfathers and brothers and preceptors and relatives and kinsmen that may give them an unjust battle. This is their open duty.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: समयत्यागिनो लुब्धान् गुरूनपि च केशव। निहन्ति समरे पापान् क्षत्रियो यः स धर्मवित्॥
en: The Kshatriya, O Keshava, knows his own duty who kills in battle his very preceptors, if they happen to be sinful and covetous and negligent of restraints and vows.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: यो लोभान समीक्षेत धर्मसेतुं सनातनम्। निहन्ति यस्तं समरे क्षत्रियो वै स धर्मवित्॥
en: That Kshatriya knows his duty who kills in battle the person who out of covetousness neglects the eternal restrictions of virtue.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: लोहितोदां केशतृणां गजशैलां ध्वजगुमाम्। महीं करोति युद्धेषु क्षत्रियो यः स धर्मवित्॥
en: That Kshatriya knows his duty who in battle converts the Earth into a lake of blood, having the hairs of killed warriors for the grass and straw floating on it, and having elephants for its rocks, and standards for the trees on its banks.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: आहूतेन रणे नित्यं योद्धव्यं क्षत्रबन्धुना। धर्म्यं स्वर्यं च लोक्यं च युद्धं हि मनुरब्रवीत्॥
en: A Kshatriya, when challenged, must always fight in battle, for Manu has said that a righteous battle acquire both heaven and fame on Earth for him.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु भीष्मेण धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। विनीतवदुपागम्य तस्थौ संदर्शनेऽग्रतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said After Bhishma had spoken thus, Dharma's son Yudhishthira humbly approached the Kuru hero and stood before him.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: अथास्य पादौ जग्राह भीष्मश्चापि ननन्द तम्। मूर्ध्नि चैनमुपाघ्राय निषीदेत्यब्रवीत् तदा॥
en: He seized the feet of Bhishma who in return cheered him with affectionate words. Smelling his head, Bhishma asked Yudhishthira to take his seat.

description: Bhishma says that he remembers all the duties. Krishna says the authority of Bhishma's words
sn: तमुवाचाथ गाङ्गेयो वृषभः सर्वधन्विनाम्। मां पृच्छ तात विश्रब्धं मा भैस्त्वं कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Then Ganga's son, that best of bowmen, addressed Yudhishthira, saying,—'Do not fear, O best of the Kurus. Ask me, O child, without any hesitation.'

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रणिपत्य हृषीकेशमभिवाद्य पितामहम्। अनुमान्य गुरून् सर्वान् पर्यपृच्छद् युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Having saluted Hrishikesha, and Bhishma, and taken the permission of all the elders assembled there, Yudhishthira began to question Bhishma.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच राज्ञां वै परमो धर्म इति धर्मविदो विदुः। महान्तमेतं भारं च मन्ये तद् ब्रूहि पार्थिव॥
en: Yudhishthira said 'Persons conversant with duty and morality lecture that royal duties are the highest science of duty. I also regard the burden of those duties as being highly heavy. Do you, therefore, O king, describe those duties.

sn: राजधर्मान् विशेषेण कथयस्व पितामह। सर्वस्य जीवलोकस्य राजधर्मः परायणम्॥
en: O grandfather, do you speak fully on the duties of kings. The science of royal duties is the refuge of all creatures.

sn: त्रिवर्गो हि समासक्तो राजधर्मेषु कारैव। मोक्षधर्मश्च विस्पष्टः सकलोऽत्र समाहितः॥
en: O you of Kuru's race, Religion, Profit, and Pleasure depend on royal duties. It is also clear that the practices that lead to liberation equally depend on them.

sn: यथा हि रश्मयोऽश्वस्य द्विरदस्याङ्कद्धशो यथा। नरेन्द्रधर्मो लोकस्य तथा प्रग्रहणं स्मृतम्॥
en: As the reins govern the horse or the iron goad the elephant, so the science of royal duties forms the reins for restraining the world.

sn: तत्र चेत् सम्प्रमुोत धर्मे राजर्षिसेविते। लोकस्य संस्था न भवेत् सर्वं च व्याकुलीभवेत्॥
en: If one becomes bewildered regarding the duties observed by kings, disorder would prevail on Earth and everything will be in confusion.

sn: उदयन् हि यथा सूर्यो नाशयत्यशुभं तमः। राजधर्मास्तथालोक्यां निक्षिपन्त्यशुभां गतिम्॥
en: As the Sun rising removes darkness, so this science destroys all the evil consequences of the world.

sn: तदने राजधर्मान् हि मदर्थे त्वं पितामह। प्रब्रूहि भरतश्रेष्ठ त्वं हि धर्मभृतां वरः॥
en: Therefore, O grandfather, do you, for my sake, discourse on royal duties first of all, for you, O chief of the Bharatas, are the foremost of all persons conversant with duties.

sn: आगमश्च परस्त्वत्तः परंतप। भवन्तं हि परं बुद्धौ वासुदेवोऽभिमन्यते॥
en: O destroyer of foes, Vasudeva considers you as the foremost of all intelligent persons. Therefore, all of us expect the best knowledge from you.'

sn: भीष्म उवाच नमो धर्माय महते नमः कृष्णाय वेधसे। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो नमस्कृत्य धर्मान् वक्ष्यामि शाश्वतान्।।१० सर्वेषां नः
en: Bhishma said 'Saluting Dharma who is Supreme, Krishna who is Brahma in full, and the Brahmanas, I shall discourse on the eternal duties (of men).

sn: शृणु कात्स्येन मत्तस्त्वं राजधर्मान् युधिष्ठिर। निरुच्यमानान् नियतो यच्चान्यदपि वाञ्छसि॥
en: Hear from me, O Yudhishthira, with rapt attention, all the royal duties described accurately and fully and other duties that you may wish to know.

sn: आदावेव कुरुश्रेष्ठ राज्ञा रञ्जनकाम्यया। देवतानां द्विजानां च वर्तितव्यं यथाविधि॥
en: In the first place, O chief of Kuru's race, the king should, for pleasing (his subjects), wait humbly upon the gods and the Brahmanas, always following implicitly the ordinance.

sn: उत्थानेन सदा पुत्र दैवतान्यर्चयित्वा हि ब्राह्मणांश्च कुरूद्वह। आनृण्यं याति धर्मस्य लोकेन च समर्च्यते॥
en: By adoring the celestials and the Brahmanas, O increaser of Kuru's race, the king satisfies his debt to duty and morality, and acquires the respect of his subjects.

sn: प्रयतेथा युधिष्ठिर। न ह्युस्थानमृते दैवं राज्ञामर्थं प्रसादयेत्॥
en: O son, you should always exert promptly, O Yudhishthira, for without exertion and manliness mere destiny never accomplishes the objects the kings wish to achieve.

sn: साधारणं द्वयं ह्येतद् दैवमुत्थानमेव च। पौरुषं हि परं मन्ये दैवं निश्चितमुच्यते॥
en: These two, viz., exertion and destiny, are equal. Of them, I consider exertion to be superior for destiny is determined from the results of exertion.

sn: विपन्ने च समारम्भे संतापं मा स्म वै कृथाः। घटस्वैव सदाऽऽत्मानं राज्ञामेष परो नयः॥
en: Do not be sorry if what is undertaken ends disastrously, for you should then exert yourself in the same work with redoubled attention. This is the highest of royal duties.

sn: न हि सत्यादृते किंचिद् राज्ञां वै सिद्धिकारकम्। सत्ये हि राजा निरतः प्रेत्य चेह न नन्दति॥
en: There is nothing which leads so much to the success of kings as Truth. The king who is devoted to Truth enjoys happiness both here and hereafter.

sn: ऋषीणामपि राजेन्द्र सत्यमेव परं धनम्। तथा राज्ञां परं सत्यान्नान्यद् विश्वासकारणम्॥
en: Even to the Rishis, O king, Truth, is the greatest wealth. Likewise for the kings, there is nothing that so much creates confidence in them as Truth.

sn: गुणवाशीलवान् दान्तो मृदुर्धर्यो जितेन्द्रियः। सुदर्शः स्थूललक्ष्यश्च न भ्रश्येत सदा श्रियः॥
en: The king who is endued with all accomplishments and good conduct, who is self-controlled, Humble, and righteous, who has his passions under control, who is of a beautiful countenance and not too enquiring, never loses prosperity.

sn: आर्जवं सर्वकार्येषु श्रयेथाः कुरुनन्दन। पुनर्नयविचारेण त्रयीसंवरणेन च॥
en: By administering justice, by following these three expedients, viz., concealment of his own shortcomings, ascertainment of the loop-holes of foes, and keeping is own counsel close, as also by acting straight-forwardly, the king, O delighter of the Kurus, acquires prosperity.

sn: मृदुर्हि राजा सततं लङ्घयो भवति सर्वशः। तीक्ष्णाच्चोद्विजते लोकस्तस्मादुभयमाश्रय॥
en: If the king becomes mild, everybody disobey him. On the other hand, if he becomes fierce his subjects always fear him. Therefore, do you conduct yourself in both the ways.

sn: अदण्ड्याश्चैव ते पुत्र विप्राश्च ददतां वर। भूतमेतत् परं लोके ब्राह्मणो नाम पाण्डव॥
en: O foremost of liberal men, the Brahmanas should never be punished by you, for the Brahmana, O son of Pandu, is the foremost of human beings on the Earth.

sn: मनुना चैव राजेन्द्र गीतौ श्लोकौ महात्मना। धर्मेषु स्वेषु कौरव्य हृदि तौ कर्तुमर्हसि॥ अद्भ्योऽग्निर्ब्रह्मतः क्षत्रमश्मनो लोहमुत्थितम्। तेषां सर्वत्रगं तेजः स्वासु योनिषु शाम्यति॥
en: The great Manu, O king of kings, has written two Slokas. As regards your duties, O you of Kuru's race, you should always remember them. Fire has originated from water, the Kshatriya from the Brahmana, and iron from stone. The three, viz., fire, Kshatriya, and iron, can act on every other thing, but coming into contact with their respective origins, their force becomes neutralised.

sn: अयो हन्ति यदाश्मानमग्निना वारि हन्यते। ब्रह्म च क्षत्रियो देशि तदा सीदन्ति ते त्रयः॥ एवं कृत्वा महाराज नमस्या एव ते द्विजाः। भौमं ब्रह्म द्विजश्रेष्ठा धारयन्ति समर्चिताः॥ पुरा तात महर्षिणा।
en: When iron strikes stone, or fire fights with water, or Kshatriya treats a Brahmana inimically, these three soon become weak. When this is so, O king, (you will see that) the Brahmanas deserve to be worshipped. The foremost of the Brahmanas are gods on Earth. Duly adored they maintain the Vedas and the Sacrifices.

sn: एवं चैव नरव्याघ्र लोकत्रयविधातकाः। निग्राह्या एव सततं बाहुभ्यां ये स्युरीदृशाः॥
en: But they, O foremost of kings, who wish to have such honour, though they may be obstacles to the three worlds, should always be repressed by the strength of your arms.

sn: श्लोकौ चोशनसा गीतौ तौ निबोध महाराज त्वमेकाग्रमना नृप॥ उद्यम्य शस्त्रमायान्तमपि वेदान्तगं रणे। निगृह्णीयात् स्वधर्मेण धर्मापेक्षी नराधिपः॥
en: The great Rishi Ushanas, O son, recited two Slokas in days of yore. Listen to them, O king, with rapt attention. The true Kshatriya, ever observant of his duties, should punish a Brahmana, inspite of his being the master of the Vedas if he rushes to battle with an uplifted weapon.

sn: विनश्यमानं धर्मं हि योऽभिरक्षेत् स धर्मवित्। न तेन धर्महा स स्यान्मन्युस्तन्मन्युमृच्छति।॥ एवं चैव नरश्रेष्ठ रक्ष्या एव द्विजातयः। सापराधानपि हि तान् विषयान्ते समुत्सृजेत्॥
en: The Kshatriya, observant of his duties, who maintains righteousness when it is trespassed against, does not by that act, commit sin, for the anger of the assailant justifies the anger of the punisher. With these restrictions only, O foremost of kings, the Brahmanas should be protected. If they commit any offence they should be banished out of the country.

sn: अभिशस्तमपि ह्येषां कृपायीत विशाम्पते। ब्रह्मने गुरुतल्पे च भ्रूणहत्ये तथैव च।॥ राजद्विष्टे च विप्रस्य विषयान्ते विसर्जनम्। विधीयते न शारीरं दण्डमेषां कदाचन॥
en: Even when they deserve punishment you should, O king, show them mercy. If a Brahmana becomes guilty of Brahmanicide, or of violating the bed of his preceptor or other elders, or of causing miscarriage, or of treason against the king, he should be punished with banishment from your territories. No corporal punishment is laid down for them.

sn: दयिताश्च नरास्ते स्युभक्तिमन्तो द्विजेषु ये। न कोशः परमोऽन्योऽस्ति राज्ञां पुरुषसंचयात्॥
en: Those persons who revere the Brahmanas should be favoured by you. There is no wealth more valuable to kings than the proper selection of servants.

sn: दुर्गेषु च महाराज षट्स ये शास्त्रनिश्चिताः। सर्वदुर्गेषु मन्यन्ते नरदुर्गं सुदुस्तरम्॥
en: Among the six kinds of forts described in the scriptures, among every kind of other forts the service and the love of the subjects is of the most impregnable.

sn: तस्मान्नित्यं दया कार्या चातुर्वर्ये विपश्चिता। धर्मात्मा सत्यवाक् चैव राजा रञ्जयति प्रजाः॥
en: Therefore, a wise king should always show mercy towards the four orders of his subjects. The righteous and truthful king succeeds in pleasing his subjects.

sn: न च क्षान्तेन ते नित्यं भाव्यं पुत्र समन्ततः। अधर्मो हि मृदू राजा क्षमावानिव कुञ्जरः॥
en: You should not, however, O son, always forgive everybody, for a mild king is regarded as the worst like an elephant shorn of fierceness.

sn: बार्हस्पत्ये च शास्त्रे च श्लोको निगदितः पुरा। अस्मिन्नर्थे महाराज तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: In the Samhita of Brihaspati, a Sloka was recited in days of yore applicable to the present subject. Hear, O king, I shall recite it.

sn: क्षममाणं नृपं नित्यं नीचः परिभवेज्जनः। हस्तियन्ता गजस्यैव शिर एवारुरुक्षति॥
en: If the king becomes always forgiving, the lowest of persons influences him, as the driver who sits on the head of the elephant he guides.

sn: तस्मान्नैव मृदुर्नित्यं तीक्ष्णो नैव भवेन्नृपः। वासन्तार्क इव श्रीमान् न शीतो न च धर्मदः॥
en: The king, therefore, should not always be mild. Nor should be always be terrific. He should be like the vernal sun, neither too cold nor too hot.

sn: प्रत्यक्षेणानुमानेन तथौपम्यागमैरपि। परीक्ष्यास्ते महाराज स्वे परे चैव नित्यशः॥
en: By the direct evidence of the senses, by conjecture, by comparisons, and by the injunctions of the scriptures, O monarch, the king should study friends and enemies.

sn: व्यसनानि च सर्वाणि त्यजेथा भूरिदक्षिण। न चैव न प्रयुञ्जीत सङ्गं तु परिवर्जयेत्॥
en: O noble king, you should renounce all those evil practices which are called Vyasanas. It is not incumbent that you should never indulge in them. What, however, is necessary is that you should not be attached to them.

sn: लोकस्य व्यसनी नित्यं परिभूतो भवत्युत। उद्वेजयति लोकं च योऽतिद्वेषी महीपतिः॥
en: He that is attached to those practices is under the influence of every one. The king who does not love his subjects fills the latter with anxiety.

sn: भवितव्यं सदा राज्ञा गर्भिणीसहधर्मिणा। कारणं च महाराज शृणु येनेदमिष्यते॥
en: The king should always treat his subjects as a mother does the child of her womb. Hear, O king, why this is desirable.

sn: यथा हि गर्भिणी हित्वा स्वं प्रियं मनसोऽनुगम्। गर्भस्य हितमाधत्ते तथा राज्ञाप्यसंशयम्॥
en: As the mother, even not caring for those objects which she likes best, seeks the wellbeing of her child alone, so, forsooth, should kings treat their subjects.

sn: वर्तितव्यं कुरुश्रेष्ठ सदा धर्मानुवर्तिना। स्वं प्रियं तु परित्यज्य यद् यल्लोकहितं भवेत्॥
en: A righteous king, O foremost one of Kuru's race, should always act in such a manner, as to sacrifice what he loves most for the sake of securing the well-being of his people.

sn: न संत्याज्यं च ते धैर्य कदाचिदपि पाण्डव। धीरस्य स्पश्दण्डस्य न भयं विद्यते क्वचित्॥
en: You should never, O son of Pandu, abandon fortitude. The king who is crowned with fortitude and who punished wrong-doers, has no cause of fear.

sn: परिहासश्च भृत्यैस्ते नात्यर्थं वदतां वर। कर्तव्यो राजशार्दूल दोषमत्र हि मे शृणु॥
en: O foremost of speakers, you should never cut jokes with your servants. O foremost of kings, listen to the short-comings of such an act.

sn: अवमन्यन्ति भर्तारं संघर्षादुपजीविनः। स्वे स्थाने न च तिष्ठन्ति लङ्घयन्ति च तद्वचः॥
en: If the master mixes too freely with them, servants begin to disregard him. They forget their own position and do not care their master.

sn: प्रेष्यमाणा विकल्पन्ते गुह्यं चाप्यनुयुञ्जते। अयाच्यं चैव याचन्ते भोज्यान्याहारयन्ति च॥
en: Ordered to do a thing, they hesitate, and give out the master's secrets. They ask for unbecoming things and take the food that is intended for the master.

sn: क्रुश्यन्ति परिदीप्यन्ति भूमिपायाधितिष्ठते। उत्कोचैर्वञ्चनाभिश्च कार्याण्यनुविहन्ति च॥
en: They even display their anger and try to excel their master. They even try to reign supreme over the king, and taking bribes and practising deceit, hinder the business of the state.

sn: जर्जरं चास्य विषयं कुर्वन्ति प्रतिरूपकैः। स्त्रीरक्षिभिश्च सज्जन्ते तुल्यवेषा भवन्ति च॥
en: They ruin the state with abuses by falsifications and forgeries. They make love with the female warders of the palace and dress in the same way as their master.

sn: वान्तं निष्ठीवनं चैव कुर्वते चास्य संनिधौ। निर्लज्जा राजशार्दूल व्याहरन्ति च तद्वचः॥
en: They become so shameless as to pass wind and spit before the very eyes of their master, O foremost of kings, and they do not fear even to speak of him lightly before others.

sn: हयं वा दन्तिनं वापि रथं वा नृपसत्तम। अभिरोहन्त्यनादृत्य हर्षुले पार्थिवे मृदौ॥
en: If the king becomes mild and cuts jokes, his servants, disobeying him, ride on horses and elephants and cars as good as the king's.

sn: इदं ते दुष्करं राजन्निदं ते दुष्टचेष्टितम्। इत्येवं सुहृदो वाचं वदन्ते परिषद्गताः॥
en: His counsellors, in court, plainly say-This is beyond your power. This is a wicked attempt.

sn: क्रुद्धे चास्मिन् हसन्त्येव न च हृष्यन्ति पूजिताः। संघर्षशीलाश्च तदा भवन्त्यन्योन्यकारणात्॥
en: If the king becomes angry, they laugh; nor are they pleased if favours be conferred upon them, though they may express joy for other reasons.

sn: विस्त्रंसयन्ति मन्त्रं च विवृण्वन्ति च दुष्कृतम्। लीलया चैव कुर्वन्ति सावज्ञास्तस्य शासनम्॥
en: They give out the secret counsels of their master and speak of his evil deeds. Without the least anxiety they disregard the king's commands.

sn: अलंकारे च भोज्ये च तथा स्नानानुलेपने। हेलनानि नरव्याघ्र स्वस्थास्तस्योप शृण्वतः॥
en: If the king's jewels, or food, or the necessaries of his bath, or unguents, be not ready, the servants, in his very presence, do not display the least anxiety.

sn: निन्दन्ते स्वानधीकारान् संत्यजन्ते च भारत। न वृत्त्या परितुष्यन्ति राजदेयं हरन्ति च॥
en: They do not take what belongs to them legitimately. On the other hand, without being content with what has been given to them, they take to themselves what belongs to the king.

sn: क्रीडितुं तेन चेच्छन्ति ससूत्रेणेव पक्षिणा। अस्मत्प्रणेयो राजेति लोकांश्चैव वदन्त्युत॥
en: They wish to sport with the king as with a bird tied in a rope, and always make the people understand that the king is on very intimate terms with them and loves them dearly.

sn: एते चैवापरे चैव दोषाः प्रादुर्भवन्त्युत। नृपतौ मार्दवोपेत हर्षुले च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: If the king is mild and disposed to cut jokes. O Yudhishthira, these and many other evils originate from it. They wish to sport with the king as with a bird tied in a rope, and always make the people understand that the king is on very intimate terms with them and loves them dearly.

sn: एते चैवापरे चैव दोषाः प्रादुर्भवन्त्युत। नृपतौ मार्दवोपेत हर्षुले च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: If the king is mild and disposed to cut jokes. O Yudhishthira, these and many other evils originate from it.

sn: भीष्म उवाच नित्योद्युक्तेन वै राज्ञा भवितव्यं युधिष्ठिर। प्रशस्यते न राजा हि नारीवोद्यमवर्जितः॥
en: 'The king, O Yudhishthira, should always address himself for action. That king does not deserve praise who, like a woman, is destitute of exertion.

sn: भगवानुशना चाह श्लोकमत्र विशाम्पते। तदिहैकमना राजन् गदतस्तं निबोध मे॥
en: On this subject, the holy Ushanas has recited a Sloka, o king, Listen to it with attention, O king, as I recite it to you.

sn: द्वाविमौ ग्रसते भूमिः सर्पो बिलशयानिव। राजानं चाविरोद्धारं ब्राह्मणं चाप्रवासिनम्॥
en: Like a snake swallowing up mice, the Earth swallows up those two, viz., the king who does not like to fight and the Brahmana who is exceedingly found of his wives and children.

sn: तदेतत्ररशार्दूल हृदि त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि। संधेयानभिसंधत्स्व विरोध्यांश्च विरोधया।४।।
en: You should, O foremost of kings, always remember it. Make peace with those enemies with whom peace should be made, and fight with them with whom war should be waged.

sn: सप्ताङ्गस्य च राज्यस्य विपरीतं य आचरेत्। गुरुर्वा यदि वा मित्रं प्रतिहन्तव्य एव सः॥
en: He, who acts inimically towards your kingdom consisting of seven limbs, should be killed, may he be your preceptor or friend.

sn: मरुत्तेन हि राज्ञा वै गीत: श्लोकः पुरातनः। राजाधिकारे राजेन्द्र बृहस्पतिमते पुरा॥
en: There is an ancient Sloka recited by king Marutta, quite of a piece with Brihaspati's view, O king, about the duty of kings.

sn: गुरोरप्यवलिप्तस्य कार्याकार्यमजानतः। उत्पथप्रतिपन्नस्य दण्डो भवित शाश्वत:॥ बाहोः पुत्रेण राज्ञा च सगरेण च धीमता। असमञ्जाः सुतो ज्येष्ठस्त्यक्तः पौरहितैषिणा॥
en: According to the scriptural injunction, there is punishment for even the preceptor if he becomes haughty and disregardful of his duty, and if he transgresses all restrictions. Vahu's son, the highly intelligent king Sagara, from desire of doing good to the citizens, banished his own eldest son Asamanjas.

sn: असमंजाः सरय्वां स पौराणां बालकान् नृप। न्यमज्जयदत: पित्रा निर्भर्त्य स विवासितः॥
en: Asamanjas, O king, used to drown the children of the citizens in the Sarayu. His father, therefore, remonstrated with and exiled him.

sn: ऋषिणोद्दालकेनापि श्वेतकेतुर्महातपाः। मिथ्या विप्रानुपचरन् संत्यक्तो दयितः सुतः॥
en: The Rishi Uddalaka renounced his favourite son Svetaketu of rigid penances, because the latter used to invite Brahmanas with false promises of entertainment.

sn: लोकरञ्जनमेवात्र राज्ञां धर्मः सनातनः। सत्यस्य रक्षणं चैव व्यवहारस्य चार्जवम्॥
en: To make their subjects happy, to observe truth and to act sincerely are the eternal duties of kings.

sn: न हिंस्यात् परवित्तानि देयं काले च दापयेत्। विक्रान्तः सत्यवाक क्षान्तो नृपो न चलते पथः॥
en: The king should not hanker after the wealth of others. He should in time give what should be given. If the king be comes endued with prowess, truthful in speech, and forgiving in temper, he would never be shorn of prosperity.

sn: आत्मवांश्च जितक्रोधः शास्त्रार्थकृतनिश्चयः। धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च मोक्षे च सततं रतः॥
en: With soul purged off sins the king should be able to govern his anger and all his conclusions should be according to the scriptures. He should also always follow morality, worldly profit, pleasure and emancipation.

sn: त्रय्यां संवृतमन्त्रश्च राजा भवितुमर्हति। वृजिनं न नरेन्द्राणां नान्यच्चारक्षणात् परम्॥
en: The king should always keep his counsels close regarding these three. No greater misfortune can betake the king than the giving out of his counsels.

sn: चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य धर्माश्च रक्षितव्या महीक्षिता। धर्मसंकररक्षा च राज्ञां धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: Kings should protect the four castes in the discharge of their duties. it is the eternal duty of kings not to allow the confusion of duties of the different orders.

sn: न विश्वसेच्च नृपतिर्न चात्यर्थं च विश्वसेत्। पाड्गुण्यगुणदोषांश्च नित्यं बुद्ध्यावलोकयेत्॥
en: The king should not confide (in others than his own servants), nor should he place too much confidence (in even his servants). He should, by own intelligence, find out the merits and short-comings of the six principal works of sovereignty.

sn: द्विछिद्रदर्शी नृपतिर्नित्यमेव प्रशस्यते। त्रिवर्ग विदितार्थश्च युक्तचारोपधिसश्च यः॥
en: The king who marks the short-comings of his enemies and cleverly follows morality, profit, and pleasure, who engages intelligent spies for determining secrets and tries to win over the officers of his enemies by presents of wealth is indeed praise-worthy.

sn: कोशस्योपार्जनरतिर्यमवैश्रवणोपमः। वेत्ता च दशवर्गस्य स्थानवृद्धिक्षयात्मनः॥
en: The king should administer justice like the Regent of Death and amass riches like the god of wealth. He should also mark the merits and short-comings of his on acquisitions and losses and of his own territories.

sn: अभृतानां भवेद् भर्ता भृतानामन्ववेक्षकः। नृपतिः सुमुखश्च स्यात् स्मितपूर्वाभिभापिता॥
en: He should feed those who have not been fed, and enquire of those who have been fed. Always sweet-speeched he should spcak with a smiling face.

sn: उपासिता च वृद्धानां जिततन्द्रिरलोलुपः। सतां वृत्ते स्थितमति: संतोष्यश्चारुदर्शन: :॥
en: He should always wait upon his elders and put down procrastination. He should never covet others' properties.

sn: न चाददीत वित्तानि सतां हस्तात् कदाचन। असभ्यश्च समादद्यात् सद्भ्यस्तु प्रतिपादयेत्॥
en: He should strictly follow the conduct of the righteous. He should never take money from the righteous. Taking the wealth of those who are not righteous he should give it to them who are righteous.

sn: स्वयं प्रहर्ता दाता च वश्यात्मा रम्यसाधनः। काले दाता च भोक्ता च शुद्धाचारस्तथैव च॥
en: The king should himself be clever in smitting. He should be liberal. He should have his mind under control. He should dress himself gorgeously. He should make presents in proper time and be regular in his meals. He should also be of good conduct.

sn: शूरान् भक्तानसंहार्यान् कुले जातानरोगिणः। शिष्टाशिष्टाभिसम्बन्धान्मानिनोऽनवमानिनः॥ विद्याविदो लोकविदः परलोकान्ववेक्षकान्। धर्मे च निरतान् साधूनचलानचलानिव॥ सहायान् सततं कुर्याद् राजा भूतिपुरष्कृतः। तैश्च तुल्यो भवेद् भोगैश्छत्रमात्राज्ञयाधिकः॥
en: The king who seeks to acquire prosperity should always engage the services of men who are brave, devoted, and incapable of being imposed on by enemies well-born, healthy, well-behaved, and connected with wellbehaved and respectable families, families, never inclined to insult others, well read in all the sciences, possessing a knowledge of the worldly affairs, never unmindful of future life, always observant of their duties, honest, and firm like mountains. The objects of enjoyments should be the same with him and them. The only difference should be in his umbrella and his power of passing orders.

sn: प्रत्यक्षा च परोक्षा च वृत्तिश्चास्य भवेत् समा। एवं कुर्वन् नरेन्द्रोऽपि न खेदमिह विन्दति॥
en: He should always treat them equally before or behind. The king, who behaves in this way, is never overtaken by calamity.

sn: सर्वाभिशङ्की नृपतिर्यश्च सर्वहरो भवेत्। स क्षिप्रमनृजुर्लुब्धः स्वजनेनैव बध्यते॥
en: That crooked and covetous king, who suspect ever body and who imposes heavy taxes on his subjects, is soon killed by his own servants and relatives.

sn: शुचिस्तु पृथिवीपालो लोकचित्तग्रहे रतः। न पतत्यरिभिर्ग्रस्तः पतितश्चावतिष्ठते॥
en: That king, however, who is righteous and who is ever engaged in attracting the hearts of his people, is never ruined when attacked by foes. If defeated, he soon regains his position.

sn: अक्रोधनो ह्यव्यसनी मृदुदण्डो जितेन्द्रियः। राजा भवति भूतानां विश्वास्यो हिमवानिव॥
en: If the king is not angry by nature, if he is not addicted to evil habits and not severe in his punishment, if he succeeds in keeping his passions under restraint he becomes an object of confidence to all like the Himavat mountains.

sn: प्राज्ञस्त्यागगुणोपेतः पररन्ध्रेषु तत्परः। सुदर्शः सर्ववर्णानां नयापनयवित् तथा॥ क्षिप्रकारी जितक्रोधः सुप्रसादो महामनाः। अरोषप्रकृतिर्युक्तः क्रियावानविकत्थनः॥ आरब्धान्येव कार्याणि सुपर्यवसितानि च। यस्य राज्ञः प्रदृश्यन्ति स राजा राजसत्तमः॥
en: He is the best of kings who is wise, who is liberal, who is ready to take advantage of the short-comings of foes, who has an agreeable countenance, who is conversant with what is good and what is bad for each of the four orders of his subjects, who is prompt in action, who has anger under control, who is not vindictive, who is high-minded, who is angry by nature, who performs sacrifices and other religious acts, who does not brag and who vigorously brings to close all works by him.

sn: पुत्रा इव पितुर्गेहे विषये यस्य मानवाः। निर्भया विचरिष्यन्ति स राजा राजसत्तमः॥
en: He is best of kings in whose kingdom men live fearlessly like sons in the house of their father.

sn: अगूढविभवा यस्य पौरा राष्ट्रनिवासिनः। नयापनयवेत्तारः स राजा राजसत्तमः॥
en: He is the best of kings whose subjects have not to hide their wealth and know what is good and what is bad for them.

sn: स्वकर्मनिरता यस्य जना विषयवासिनः। असंघातरता दान्ताः पाल्यमाना यथाविधि॥ वष्टा नेया विधेयाश्च न च संघर्षशालिनः। विषये दानरुचयो नरा यस्य स पार्थिवः॥ न यस्य कूटं कपटं न माया न च मत्सरः। विषये भूमिपालस्य तस्य धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: He, indeed, is a king whose subjects follow their respective duties and do not fear to renounce their bodies for duty's call; whose subjects protected properly, are all of peaceful conduct, obedient, docile, governable, reluctant to dispute and liberal. That king carns eternal merit in whose kingdom kingdom there is wickedness, dissimulation, deception and envy.

sn: यः सत्करोति ज्ञानानि ज्ञेये परहिते रतः। सतां वानुगस्त्यागी स राजा राज्यमर्हति॥
en: That king truly deserves to govern who honours knowledge, who is devoted to the no scriptures and the good of his people, who wends the path of the righteous, and who is liberal.

sn: यस्य चाराश्च मन्त्राश्च नित्यं चैव कृताकृताः। न ज्ञायन्ते हि रिपुभिः स राजा राज्यमर्हति॥
en: That king deserves to rule whose counsels and acts done and undone remain close to his enemies.

sn: श्लोकश्चायं पुरा गीतो भार्गवेण महात्मना। आख्याते राजचरिते नृपति प्रति भारत॥
en: The following verse was recited in days of yore by Ushanas of Bhrigu's race, in the narrative called Ramacharita, on the subject, O Bharata, of royal duties.

sn: राजानं प्रथम विन्देत् ततो भार्यां ततो धनम्। राजन्यसति लोकस्य कुतो भार्या कुतो धनम्॥
en: One should first select a king. Then should he select a wife, and then acquire wealth. If there be no king, what would become of his wife and properties?

sn: तद्राज्ये राज्यकामानां नान्यो धर्मः सनातनः। ऋते रक्षां तु विस्पशं रक्षा लोकस्य धारिणी॥
en: About those who seek kingdom, there is no other eternal duty than the protection of subjects). The protection the king grants of his subjects maintains the world.

sn: प्राचेतसेन मनुना श्लोकौ चेमावुदाहृतौ। राजधर्मेषु राजेन्द्र ताविहैकमनाः शृणु।॥
en: Manu, the son of Prachetas, recited these two verses regarding the duties of kings. Listen to them with attention.

sn: षडेतान् पुरुषो जह्याद् भिन्नां नावमिवार्णवे। अप्रवक्तारमाचार्यमनधीयानमृत्विजम्॥ अरक्षितारं राजानं भार्यां चाप्रियवादिनीम्। ग्रामकामं च गोपालं वनकामं च नापितम्॥
en: These six persons should be shunned like a leaky boat on the sea, viz., a preceptor who does not speak, a priest who has not studied the scriptures, a king who does not give protection, herd who likes to rove within the village and a barber who wishes to go to the forest.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एतत् ते राजधर्माणां नवनीतं युधिष्ठिर। बृहस्पतिर्हि भगवान् न्याय्यं धर्मं प्रशंसति॥
en: 'Protection of the subjects, O Yudhishthira, is the quintessence of duties. the divine Brihaspati does not speak so highly of any other duty.

sn: विशालाक्षश्च भगवान् काव्यश्चैव महातपाः। सहस्राक्षो महेन्द्रश्च तथा प्राचेतसो मनुः॥ भरद्वाजश्च भगवांस्तथा गौरशिरा मुनिः। राजशास्त्रप्रणेतारो ब्रह्मण्या ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
en: The divine Kavi (Ushanas) of large eyes and austere penances, the thousand-eyed Indra, and Manu, the son of Prachetas, the divine Bharadwaja, and the sage Gaurasiras all devoted to Brahma and utterers of Brahma, have composed works on the duties of kings.

sn: रक्षामेव प्रशंसन्ति धर्मं धर्मभृतां वर। राज्ञां राजीवताम्राक्ष साधनं चात्र मे शृणु॥
en: All of them speak highly of the duty of protection, O foremost of virtuous persons regarding the kings. O you having eyes like lotus petals and copper-coloured, listen to the means by which protection may be obtained.

sn: चारश्च प्रणिधिश्चैव काले दानममत्सरात्। युक्त्यादानं न चादानमयोगेन युधिष्ठिर॥ सतां संग्रहणं शौर्यं दाक्ष्यं सत्यं प्रजाहितम्। अनार्जवैरार्जवैश्च शत्रुपक्षस्य भेदनम्॥ केतनानां च जीर्णानामवेक्षा चैव सीदताम्। द्विविधस्य च दण्डस्य प्रयोगः कालचोदितः॥ साधूनामपरित्यागः कुलीनानां च धारणम्। निचयश्च निचेयानां सेवा बुद्धिमतामपि॥ बलानां हर्षणं नित्यं प्रजानामन्ववेक्षणम्। कार्येष्वखेदः कोशस्य तथैव च विवर्धनम्॥ पुरगुप्तिरविश्वास: पौरसंघातभेदनम्। अरिमध्यस्थमित्राणां यथावच्चान्ववेक्षणम्॥ उपजापश्च भृत्यानामात्मनः पुरदर्शनम्। अविश्वासः स्वयं चैव परस्याश्वासनं तथा।॥ नीतिधर्मानुसरणं नित्यमुत्थानमेव च। रिपूणामनवज्ञानं नित्यं चानार्यवर्जनम्॥
en: They consist of the employment of spies and servants, paying them their just dues without pride, the realisation of taxes with mercy, never taking anything whimsically and unjustifiably. O Yudhishthira, the selection of honest men, heroism, skill and cleverness, truth, seeking the good of the people, creating discord and disunion among the enemy by fair or unfair means, the repair of old and dilapedated buildings, the infliction of corporal punishments and imposition of just fines, never abandoning the honest, giving employment and protection to respectable persons, the keeping in reserve of what should be kept, living in the company of intelligent persons, always gratifying the soldiers, supervision over the subjects, steadiness in the transaction of business, filling the treasury, absence of blind confidence on the guards of the city, creating disloyalty among the citizens of a hostile town, carefully looking after the friends and allies living in the midst of the enemy's country, keeping a strict eye on the servants and officers of the state, personal supervision of the city, distrust of servants, comforting the enemy with assurance, steadily following the settled policy, readiness for action, never disregarding an enemy, and driving away the wicked.

sn: उत्थानं हि नरेन्द्राणां बृहस्पतिरभाषत। राजधर्मस्य तन्मूलं श्लोकांश्चात्र निबोध मे॥
en: Readiness for action in kings is the root of royal duties. This has been said by Brihaspati. Listen to the verses recited by him.

sn: उत्थानेनामृतं लब्धमुत्थानेनासुरा हताः। उत्थानेन महन्द्रेण श्रेष्ठ्यं प्राप्तं दिवीह च॥
en: By exertion the ambrosia was obtained; by exertion the Asuras were killed; by exertion Indra himself acquired sovereignty in heaven and on earth.

sn: उत्थानवीरः पुरुषो वाग्वीरानधितिष्ठति। उत्थानवीरान् वाग्वीरा रमयन्त उपासते॥
en: The hero who works is superior to one who speaks. The heroes who speak, gratify and worship the heroes who work.

sn: उत्थानहीनो राजा हि बुद्धिमानपि नित्यशः। प्रधर्षणीयः शत्रूणां भुजङ्ग इव निर्विषः॥
en: The king, who is shorn of exertion, even if endued with intelligence, is always defeated by foes like a snake that is shorn of poison.

sn: न च शत्रुरवज्ञेयो दुर्बलोऽपि बलीयसा। अल्पोऽपि हि दहत्यग्निविषमल्पं हिनस्ति च॥
en: The king, even if very powerful, should not neglect a foe however weak. A scintillation of fire can produce a conflagration and a particle of Poison can kill.

sn: एकाङ्गेनापि सम्भूतः शत्रुर्दुर्गमुपाश्रितः। सर्वं तापयते देशमपि राज्ञः समृद्धिनः॥
en: With only one kind of force, an enemy, from within a fort, can assail the whole country of even a powerful and prosperous king.

sn: राज्ञो रहस्यं यद् वाक्यं जयार्थं लोकसंग्रहः। हृदि यच्चास्य जिह्यं स्यात्कारणेन च यद् भवेत्॥ यच्चास्य कार्यं वृजिनमार्जवेनैव धारयेत्। दम्भनार्थं च लोकस्य धर्मिष्ठामाचरेत् क्रियाम्॥
en: The secret speeches of a king, the collecting of troops for the purposes of victory, the wily purposes in his heart, desires for accomplishing particular objects, and the wrong acts he does or intends to do, should be concealed by assuming a bold appearance. He should act righteously for keeping his people under control.

sn: राज्यं हि सुमहत् तन्त्रं धार्यते नाकृतात्मभिः। न शक्यं मृदुना वोढुमायासस्थानमुत्तमम्॥
en: Wily persons can not govern an extensive empire, A king who is mild cannot acquire superior rank the acquisition of which depends upon exertion.

sn: राज्यं सर्वामिषं नित्यमार्जवेनेह धार्यते। तस्मान्मिश्रेण सततं वर्तितव्यं युधिष्ठिर॥
en: A kingdom, which is sought for by all like meat can never be protected by candour and simplicity. A king, O Yudhishthira, should, therefore, always resort to both candour and wiliness.

sn: यद्यप्यस्य विपत्तिः स्याद् रक्षमाणस्य वै प्रजाः। सोऽप्यस्य विपुलो धर्म एवंवृत्ता हि भूमिपाः॥
en: Even while protecting his subjects a king is beset with danger, he earns great merit. Such should be the conduct of kings.

sn: एष ते राजधर्माणां लेशः समनुवर्णितः। भूयस्ते यत्र संदेहस्तद् ब्रूहि कुरुसत्तम॥
en: I have now told you a part only of the duties of kings. Tell me, O best of Kurus, what more you wish to know.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो व्यासश्च भगवान् देवस्थानोऽश्म एव च। वासुदेवः कृपश्चैव सात्यकिः संजयस्तथा॥ साधु साध्विति संहृष्टाः पुष्ष्यमाणैरिवाननैः। अस्तुवंश्च नरव्याघ्रं भीष्मं धर्मभृतां वरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said The illustrious Vyasa, Devasthana, Ashva, Vasudeva, Kripa, Satyaki and Sanjaya, filled with joy, and with faces resembling full-blown flowers, said,-Excellent! Excellent!' and sang the praises of that best of men, viz., Bhishma, that foremost of virtuous persons.

sn: ततो दीनमना भीष्ममुवाच कुरुसत्तमः। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां पादौ तस्य शनैः स्पृशन्॥ श्व इदानीं स्वसन्देहं प्रक्ष्यामि त्वां पितामह। उपैति सविता शस्तं रसमापीय पार्थिवम्॥
en: Then Yudhishthira, that chief of Kuru's race, with a depressed heart and eyes bathed in tears, gently touched Bhishma's feet and said,—'O grandsire, I shall tomorrow enquire after those points about which I have my doubts, for today the sun, having sucked the moisture of the earth, is about to set.

sn: ततो द्विजातीनभिवाद्य केशवः कृपश्व ते चैव युधिष्ठिरादयः। प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य महानदीसुतं ततो रथानारुरुहुर्मुदान्विताः॥
en: Then Keshava, Kripa, Yudhishthira and others, saluting the Brahmanas and circumambulating Bhishma, gladly got on their cars.

sn: दृषद्वतीं चाप्यवगाह्य सुव्रताः कृतोदकार्थाः कृतजष्यमङ्गलाः। उपास्य संध्यां विधिवत् परंतर्पा स्तत: पुरं ते विविशुर्गजाह्वयम्॥
en: All of them, observant of excellent vows, then bathed in the river Drishadvati-Having offered oblations of water to their departed manes and silently recited the sacred mantras and performed other auspicious rites, and having adored the evening twilight with due rites, those scorchers of enemies entered the city of Hastinapur.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कल्यं समुत्थाय कृतपूर्वाह्निकक्रियाः। ययुस्ते नगराकारै रथैः पाण्डवयादवाः॥
en: Rising from their beds the next day and performing morning rites laid down in the scriptures, the Pandavas and the Yadavas started on their cars resembling fortified towns.

sn: प्रतिपद्य कुरुक्षेत्रं भीष्ममासाद्य चानघ। सुखां न रजनी पृष्ट्वा गाङ्गेयं रथिनां वरम्॥
en: Proceeding to the field of Kuru and approaching the sinless Bhishma, they enquired of that best of car-warriors if he had spent the night happily.

sn: व्यासदीनभिवाद्यर्षीन् सर्वैस्तैश्चाभिनन्दिताः। निषेदुरभितो भीष्मं परिवार्यं समन्ततः॥
en: Saluting all the Rishis, and having been blessed by them in return, the princes sat around Bhishma.

sn: ततो राजा महातेजा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिर्भीष्मं प्रतिपूज्य यथाविधि॥
en: Then having adored Bhishma, king Yudhishthira, said these words with joined hands.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच य एष राजन् राजेति शब्दश्चरति भारत। कथमेष समुत्पन्नस्तन्मे ब्रूहि परंतप॥
en: Yudhishthira said Whence came the word Rajan, O king, that is used, O Bharata, on Earth? Tell me this, O scorcher of foes.

sn: तुल्यपाणिभुजग्रीवस्तुल्यबुद्धीन्द्रियात्मकः। तुल्यदुःखसुखात्मा च तुल्यपृष्ठमुखोदरः॥ तुल्यशुक्रास्थिमज्जा च तुल्यमांसासृगेव च। निःश्वासोच्छ्वासतुल्यश्च तुल्यप्राणशरीरवान्॥ समानजन्ममरणः समः सर्वैर्गुणैर्नृणाम्। विशिष्टबुद्धीन् शूरांश्च कथमेकोऽधितिष्ठति॥
en: Having hands and arms and neck like others, having an understanding and senses like those of others, subject like others to the same kinds of weal and woe, having back, mouth and stomach similar to those of the rest of the world, having vital fluids and bones and marrow and flesh and blood similar to those of the rest of the world, drawing in and sending out breaths like others, possessed of vital airs and bodies like other inen, resembling others in birth and death, in fact, similar to others regarding all the attributes of men, why does one men, viz., the king govern the rest of world consisting of many brave and intelligent persons?

sn: कथमेको महीं कृत्स्ना शूरवीरार्यसंकुलाम्। रक्षत्यपि च लोकस्य प्रसादमभिवाञ्छति॥
en: Whence is it that one man governs the vast universe consisting of brave, energetic, wellborn and well-behaved men? Why do all men try to get his favour?

sn: एकस्य तु प्रसादेन कृत्स्नो लोकः प्रसीदति। व्याकुले चाकुलः सर्वो भवतीति विनिश्चयः॥
en: Why is it that one man becomes cheerful, the whole world is cheerful and if that one man is sorry the whole world is sorry?

sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तत्त्वेन भरतर्षभ। कृत्स्नं तन्मे यथातत्त्वं प्रब्रूहि वदतां वर॥
en: I wish to hear this in detail, O foremost of Bharata's race. O foremost of speakers, describe to me this fully.

sn: नैतत् कारणमल्पं हि भविष्यति विशाम्पते। यदेकस्मिन् जगत् सर्वं देववद् याति संनतिम्॥
en: O king, there must be some mighty reason for all this because it is seen that the whole world bows down to one man as to a god.'

sn: भीष्म उवाच नियतस्त्वं नरव्याघ्र शृणु सर्वमशेषतः। यथा राज्यं समुत्पन्नमादौ कृतयुगेऽभवत्॥
en: 'With rapt attentical, O foremost of kings, listen to it fully as to how in the golden cycle sovereignty was first instituted.

sn: न वै राज्यं न राजाऽऽसीन्न च दण्डो न दाण्डिकः। धर्मेणैव प्रजाः सर्वा रक्षन्ति स्म परस्परम्॥
en: At first there was no sovereignty, no king, no punishment, and no punisher. All men used to protect one another piously.

sn: पाल्यमानास्तथान्योन्यं नरा धर्मेण भारत। खेदं परमुपाजग्मुस्ततस्तान् मोह आविशत्॥
en: As they thus lived, O Bharata, righteously protecting one another, they found the task (in time), to be painful. Error then possessed their hearts.

sn: ते मोहवशमापन्ना मनुजा मनुजर्षभ। प्रतिपत्तिविमोहाच्च धर्मस्तेषामनीनशत्॥
en: Having become subject to error, the perceptions of men, O prince, became clouded, and thence their virtue began to wane.

sn: नष्टायां प्रतिपत्तौ च मोहवश्या नरास्तदा। लोभस्य वशमापन्नाः सर्वे भरतसत्तम॥
en: When their perceptions were clouded and when men became subject to error all of them became covetous, O chief of the Bharatas.

sn: अप्राप्तस्याभिमर्श तु कुर्वन्तो मनुजास्ततः। कामो नामापरस्तत्र प्रत्यपद्यत वै प्रभो॥
en: And because men tried to secure objects which were not their own, another passion called lust seized them.

sn: तांस्तु कामवशं प्राप्तान् रागो नाम समस्पृशत्। रक्ताश्च नाभ्यजानन्त कार्याकार्ये युधिष्ठिर॥
en: When they became subject to lust, another passion, named anger, soon attacked them. Once subject to anger, they lost all considerations of what should be done and what should not be.

sn: अगम्यागमनं चैव वाच्यावाच्यं तथैव च। भक्ष्याभक्ष्यं च राजेन्द्र दोषादोषं च नात्यजन्॥
en: Unrestrained sexual indulgence began. Men began to say what they liked. All distinctions between clean and unclean food and between virtue and vice disappeared.

sn: विप्लुते नरलोके वै ब्रह्म चैव ननाश ह। नाशाच्च ब्रह्मणो राजन् धर्मो नाशमथागमत्॥
en: When this confusion set in amongst men, the Vedas disappeared. Upon the disappearance of the Vedas, the righteousness also was gone.

sn: नष्टे ब्रह्मणि धर्मे च देवांस्त्रासः समाविशत्। ते त्रस्ता नरशार्दूल ब्रह्माणं शरणं ययुः॥
en: When both the Vedas and righteousness were lost, the gods, were overcome by fear. Overcome with fear. O foremost of men, they sought the help of Brahman.

sn: प्रसाद्य भगवन्तं ते देवं लोकपितामहम्। ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे दुःखवेगसमाहताः॥ भगवन् नरलोकस्थं ग्रस्तं ब्रह्म सनातनम्। लोभमोहादिभिर्भावस्ततो नो भयमाविशत्॥
en: Having propitiated the divine Grandfather of the universe, the gods, stricken with grief, said to him, with joined hands-"O god, the eternal Vedas have been afflicted in the world of men by covetousness and error. For this, we have been assailed with fear.

sn: ब्रह्मणश्च प्रणाशेन धर्मो व्यनशदीश्वर। ततः स्म समतां याता मत्यस्त्रिभुवनेश्व॥
en: With the loss of the Vedas, o Supreme Lord, righteousness also has been lost. For this, O Supreme Lord of the three worlds, we are about to be reduced to the status of human beings.

sn: अधो हि वर्षमस्माकं नरास्तूर्ध्वप्रवर्षिणः। क्रियाव्युपरमात् तेषां ततो गच्छाम संशयम्॥
en: Men used to pour upwards while we used to pour downwards. For the stoppage of all religious rites among men we will suffer great distress.

sn: अत्र निःश्रेयसं यन्नस्तद् ध्यायस्व पितामह। त्वत्प्रभावसमुत्थोऽसौ स्वभावो नो विनश्यति॥ तानुवाच सुरान् सर्वान् स्वयम्भूर्भगवांस्ततः। श्रेयोऽहं चिन्तयिष्यामि व्येतु वो भीः सुरर्षभाः॥ ततोऽध्यायसहस्राणां शतं चक्रे स्वबुद्धिजम्। यत्र धर्मस्तथैवार्थः कामश्चैवाभिवर्णितः॥
en: Do you then, O Grandfather, think of that which would be for our well-being so that the universe, created by your power, may not meet with destruction.” Thus addressed, the Selfcreate and divine Lord said to them-'I shall think of what will do you good, Ye foremost of gods, let your fears be removed.' The grandfather then composed by his own intelligence a work consisting of a hundred thousand lessons. In it were treated the subjects of religion, Profit and Pleasure.

sn: त्रिवर्ग इति विख्यातो गण एष स्वयम्भुवा। चतुर्थो मोक्ष इत्येव पृथगर्थः पृथग्गुणः॥
en: The self-create named the book as one of three subjects. He treated of a fourth subject called liberation whose meaning and attributes are different.

sn: मोक्षस्यास्ति त्रिवर्गोऽन्यः प्रोक्तः सत्त्वं रजस्तमः। स्थानं वृद्धिः क्षयश्चैव त्रिवर्गश्चैव दण्डजः॥
en: The three-fold characteristics of liberation according to the attributes of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance and another namely the performance of duty without the desire for fruits were also described in it. Another threefold characteristics of Punishment viz., Conservation, Growth, and Destruction, were treated in it.

sn: आत्मा देशश्च कालश्चाप्युपायाः कृत्यमेव च। सहायाः कारणं चैव षड्वर्गो नीतिजः स्मृतः॥
en: Another six consisting of the hearts of men, place, time, means, tacts, and alliances, and causes, were described in it.

sn: त्रयी चान्वीक्षिकी चैव वार्ता च भरतर्षभ। दण्डनीतिश्च विपुला विद्यास्तत्र निदर्शिताः॥
en: The religious rites laid down in the three Vedas, knowledge, and the acts necessary for the support of life, (viz., agriculture, trade, etc.), O foremost of Bharata's race, and the very extensive branch of learning called legislation, were described in it.

sn: अमात्यरक्षा प्रणिधी राजपुत्रस्य लक्षणम्। चारश्च विविधोपायः प्रणिधेयः पृथग्विधः॥ साम भेदः प्रदानं च ततो दण्डच पार्थिव। उपेक्षा पञ्चमी चात्र कात्स्न्येन समुदाहृता॥
en: The subjects also of behaviour towards ministers, of spies, the indications of princes, of secret agents, of envoys and agents of other kinds, conciliation, sowing seeds of discord, gifts, and punishment, O king, with toleration as the fifth, were fully described there.

sn: मन्त्रश्च वर्णितः कृत्स्नस्तथा भेदार्थ एव च। विभ्रमश्चैव मन्त्रस्य सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योश्च यत् फलम्॥ संधिश्च त्रिविधाभिख्यो हीनो मध्यस्तथोत्तमः। भयसत्कारवित्ताख्यं कात्स्येन परिवर्णितम्॥
en: Deliberation of all sorts, counsels for creating disunion, the mistakes of deliberation, the results of the success or failure of counsels of three kinds viz., bad, middling, and good, made through fear, good conduct and gifts of wealth, were described there.

sn: यात्राकालाश्च चत्वारस्त्रिवर्गस्य च विस्तरः। विजयो धर्मयुक्तश्च तथार्थविजयश्च ह॥ आसुरश्चैव विजयस्तथा कार्येन वर्णितः। लक्षणं पञ्चवर्गस्य त्रिविधं चात्र वर्णितम्॥
en: The four sorts of time for making journeys, the details of the aggregate of three, the three sorts of victory, viz, that secured piously, that acquired by riches and that obtained by deceit were described, fully. The three kinds of attributes, viz., bad, middling and good, of the five expedients (viz., counsellors, kingdom, fort, army, and treasury) were also described in it.

sn: प्रकाशश्चाप्रकाशश्च दण्डोऽथ परिशब्दितः। प्रकाशोऽविधस्तत्र गुह्यश्च बहुविस्तरः॥
en: Punishments of two kinds, viz, open and secret, were also described. The eight kinds of open punishments as also the eight kinds of secret punishment were described fully.

sn: रथा नागा हयाश्चैव पादाताश्चैव पाण्डव। विष्टिर्नावश्चराश्चैव देशिका इति चाष्टमम्॥ अङ्गान्येतानि कौरव्य प्रकाशानि बलस्य तु। जङ्गमाजङ्गमाश्चोक्ताश्चूर्णयोगा विषादयः॥ स्पर्श चाभ्यवहार्ये चाप्युपांशुर्विविधः स्मृतः। अरिर्मित्र उदासीन इत्येतेऽप्यनुवर्णिताः॥
en: Cars, elephants, horse, and infantry, O son of Pandu, forced labourers, crew, and paid attendants (of armies), and guides taken from the country which is the seat of war, these are the eight means, O Kauravya, of open punishment. The administration of movable and immovable poison was also mentioned regarding the three kinds, of things, viz., dress, food, and incantation. Enemies, allies, and neutrals,—these also were described.

sn: कृत्स्ना मार्गगुणाश्चैव तथा भूमिगुणाश्च हा आत्मरक्षणमाश्वासः सर्गाणां चान्ववेक्षणम्॥ कल्पना विविधाश्चापि नृनागरथवाजिनाम्। व्यूहाश्च विविधाभिख्या विचित्रं युद्धकौशलम्॥ उत्पाताश्च निपाताश्च सुयुद्धं सुपलायितम्। शस्त्राणां पालनं ज्ञानं तथैव भरतर्षभ॥ बलव्यसनमुक्तं च तथैव बलहर्षणम्। पीडा चापदकालश्च पत्तिज्ञानं च पाण्डव॥ तथा खातविधानं च योगः संचार एव च। चोरैराटविकैश्चोग्रैः परराष्ट्रस्य पीडनम्॥ अग्निर्दैगरदैश्चैव प्रतिरूपककारकैः। श्रेणिमुख्योपजापेन वीरधश्छेदनेन च॥ दूषणेन च नागानामातङ्कजननेन च। आराधनेन भक्तस्य प्रत्ययोपार्जनेन च॥ सप्ताङ्गस्य च राज्यस्य ह्रासवृद्धिसमञ्जसम्। दूतसामर्थ्यसंयोगात् सराष्ट्रस्य विवर्धनम्॥ अरिमध्यस्थमित्राणां सम्यक् चोक्तं प्रपञ्चनम्। अवमर्दः प्रतीघातस्तथैव च बलीयसाम्॥ व्यवहारः सुसूक्ष्मश्च तथा कण्टकशोधनम्। श्रमो व्यायामयोगश्च त्यागो द्रव्यस्य संग्रहः॥ अभृतानां च भरणं भृतानां चान्ववेक्षणम्। अर्थस्य काले दानं च व्यसने चाप्रसङ्गिता॥ तथा राजगुणाश्चैव सेनापतिगुणाश्च ह। कारणं च त्रिवर्गस्य गुणदोषास्तथैव च॥ दुश्चेष्टितं च विविधं वृत्तिश्चैवानुवर्तिनाम्। शङ्कितत्वं च सर्वस्य प्रमादस्य च वर्जनम्॥ अलब्धलाभो लब्धस्य तथैव च विवर्धनम्। प्रदानं च विवृद्धस्य पात्रेभ्यो विधिवत्ततः॥ विसर्गोऽर्थस्य धर्मार्थं कामहैतुकमुच्यते। चतुर्थं व्यसनाघाते तथैवात्रानुवर्णितम्॥
en: The various characteristics of roads (to follow), the nature of the soil on which to encamp, protection of self, superintendence of the construction of cars and other utensils of war and use, the various means for protecting and improving men, elephants, cars, and horses, the various kinds of arranging soldiers, strategies, and manoeuvres in war, planetary conjunctions indicating evil, evil auguries (such as earthquakes), skilful methods of warfare and retreat, knowledge of weapons and their proper care, the disorders of troops and how to get rid of them, the means of filling the army with joy and confidence, diseases, times of distress and danger, knowledge of guiding the infantry in battle, the methods of creating alarms and notifying orders, striking the enemy with fear by display of flags, the various means of assailing enemy's kingdom by means of robbers and dreadful wild-tribes, and fire-giver and poisoners and forgerers, by creating union among the principal officers of hostile armies, by cutting down crops and plants, by destroying the efficiency of the enemy's elephants, by producing alarms, by honouring those among the enemy's subject who are well disposed towards the invader, and by filling the enemy with confidence, the waste, growth, and harmony of the seven principal requisites of sovereignty, capacity for works, the means for accomplishing them, the methods of extending the kingdom, the means of winning over persons living in the enemy's country, the punishment and destruction, strong and the impartial administration of justice, the extermination of the the wicked, wrestling, shooting and throwing and hurling of weapons, the methods of making presents and of keeping in store necessary things, feeding the unfed and supervision over those that have been fed, gifts of wealth in season, freedom from the vices, the attributes of king, the qualification of military officers, the sources of the three requisites and its merits and short-comings, the various kinds of evil intents, the behaviour of dependents, suspicion against every one, the avoidance of carelessness, the acquisition of objects unattained, the improving of objects already obtained, gifts, to deserving persons, spending of wealth for religious purposes, for acquiring objects of desire, and for removing danger and distress, were all described in that work.

sn: क्रोधजानि तथोग्राणि कामजानि तथैव च। दशोक्तानि कुरुश्रेष्ठ व्यसनान्यत्र चैव ह॥
en: The ten dreadful vices, O chief of the Kurus, begotten by anger and lust, were described in that work.

sn: मृगयाक्षास्तथा पानं स्त्रियश्च भरतर्षभ। कामजान्याहुराचार्याः प्रोक्तानीह स्वयम्भुवा॥
en: The four kinds of vices begotten of lust, viz., hunting, gambling, drinking and sexual intercourse were described by the Self-sprung in that work.

sn: वाक्पारुष्यं तथोग्रत्वं दण्डपारुष्यमेव च। आत्मनो निग्रहस्त्यागो ह्यर्थदूषणमेव च॥
en: Roughness of speech, fierceness, severity of chastisement, infliction of pain on the body, suicide, and frustrating one's own objects, these six kinds of faults begotten of anger have also been described.

sn: यन्त्राणि विविधान्येव क्रियास्तेषां च वर्णिताः। अवमर्दः प्रतीघात: केतनानां च भञ्जनम्॥ चैत्यगुमावमर्दश्च रोधः कर्मानुशासनम्। अपस्करोऽथ वसनं तथोपायाश्च वर्णिताः॥
en: Various kinds of machines and their actions have been described there. Devastation of the enemy's territories, attacks upon enemies, the destruction and removal of boundary lines and other indications, the cutting down of large trees, siege of forts, supervision of agriculture and other useful operations, and the hoarding of necessaries, dresses and the best means of manufacturing them, were all described.

sn: पणवानकशङ्खानां भेरीणां च युधिष्ठिर। उपार्जनं च द्रव्याणां परिमर्दश्च तानि षट्॥ लब्धस्य च प्रशमनं सतां चैवाभिपूजनम्। विद्वद्भिरेकीभावश्च दानहोमविधिज्ञता।॥ मङ्गलालम्भनं चैव शरीरस्य प्रतिक्रिया। आहारयोजनं चैव नित्यमास्तिक्यमेव च॥ एकेन च यथोत्थेयं सत्यत्वं मधुरा गिरः। उत्सवानां समाजानां क्रियाः केतनजास्तथा॥ प्रत्यक्षाश्च परोक्षाश्च सर्वाधिकरणेष्वथा वृत्तेर्भरतशार्दूल नित्यं चैवान्ववेक्षणम्॥ अदण्ड्यत्वं च विप्राणां युक्त्या दण्डनिपातनम्। अनुजीविस्वजातिभ्यो गुणेभ्यश्च समुद्भवः॥ रक्षणं चैव पौराणां राष्ट्रस्य च विवर्धनम्। मण्डलस्था च या चिन्ता राजन् द्वादशराजिका॥ द्वासप्ततिविधा चैव शरीरस्य प्रतिक्रिया। देशजातिकुलानां च धर्माः समनुवर्णिताः॥
en: The characteristics and uses of Panavas, Anakas, conchs and drums. O Yudhishthira, the six sorts of articles viz., gems, animals, lands, dresses, female slaves, and gold and means of acquiring them and of destroying them, pacification of newly acquired kingdom, honouring the good, making friendship with the learned, knowledge of the rules of gifts and religious rites such as Homa, the touch of auspicious articles, attention to and adoring of the body, the manner of preparing and using food, piety of conduct, the attaininent of prosperity by following one path, truthfulness of speech, sweetness of speech, observance of acts on occasions of festivity and social gatherings and those done within the household, the open and secret acts of persons in all places of meeting, the constant supervision of the conduct of men, the freedom of Brahmanas from punishment, the infliction of reasonable punishment, honours paid to dependents for kinship and merit, the protection of subjects and the means of extending the territories, the advice that a king, who lives in the midst of a dozen kings, should follow regarding the four kinds of enemies, the four kinds of allies, and the four kinds of neutrals, the seventy two acts laid down in medical works about the protection, exercise, and improvement of the body, and the practices of particular countries, tribes and families, were all duly described in that work.

sn: धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च मोक्षश्चात्रानुवर्णिताः। उपायाश्चार्थलिप्सा च विविधा भूरिदक्षिण॥ मूलकर्मक्रिया चात्र मायायोगश्च वर्णितः। दूषणं स्त्रोतसां चैव वर्णितं चास्थिराम्भसाम्॥
en: Religion, Profit, Pleasure, and liberation were also treated in it. The various means of acquisition, the desire for various sorts of wealth, O giver of profuse presents, the methods of agriculture and other works constituting the chief source of the revenue, and the various means for producing and applying illusions, the methods by which stagnant water is rendered foul, were described in it.

sn: यैर्यैरुपायैर्लोकस्तु न चलेदार्यवर्त्मनः। तत् सर्वं राजशार्दूल नीतिशाकेऽभिवर्णितम्॥
en: All those means, O foremost of kings, by which men might be prevented from falling off from the path of righteousness and honesty were all treated in it.

sn: एतत् कृत्वा शुभं शास्त्रं ततः स भगवान् प्रभुः। देवानुवाच संहृष्टः सर्वाञ्छक्रपुरोगमान्॥
en: Having composed that highly beneficial work, the divine Lord cheerfully said to the deities led by Indra, these words.

sn: उपकाराय लोकस्य त्रिवर्गस्थापनाय च। नवनीतं सरस्वत्या बुद्धिरेषा प्रभाविता॥
en: For the behoof of the world and for establishing the three-fold objects (viz., Religion, Profit, and Pleasure), I have composed this science representing the very essence of speech.

sn: दण्डेन सहिता ह्येषा लोकरक्षणकारिका। निग्रहानुग्रहरता लोकाननुचरिष्यति॥
en: Helped by punishment this science will protect the world. Meting out rewards and punishments, this science will work among men.

sn: दण्डेन नीयते चेदं दण्डं नयति वा पुनः। दण्डनीतिरिति ख्याता त्रील्लोकानभिवर्तते॥
en: And because men will be governed by punishment, therefore will this science be known in the three worlds as Dandaniti (science of punishment).

sn: पाड्गुण्यगुणसारैषा स्थास्यत्यग्रे महात्मसु। धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाश्च सकला ह्यत्र शब्दिताः॥
en: Containing the cream of all the attributes of the six, this science will always be much respected by great persons. Religion, Profit, Pleasure, and Liberation have all been described in it.

sn: ततस्तां भगवान् नीति पूर्वं जग्राह शङ्करः। बहुरूपो विशालाक्षः शिवः स्थाणुरुमापतिः॥
en: After this, the husband of Uma,—the divine and many-formed Shiva of large eyes, the source of all blessings, first read and mastered it.

sn: प्रजानामायुषो ह्रासं विज्ञाय भगवाच्छिवः। संचिक्षेप ततः शास्त्रं महास्त्रं ब्रह्मणा कृतम्॥
en: In view, however, of the gradual decrease of the span of human existence, the divine Shiva abridged that highly important science compiled by Brahman.

sn: वैशालाक्षमिति प्रोक्तं तदिन्द्रः प्रत्यपद्यप्त। दशाध्यायसहस्राणि सुब्रह्मण्यो महातपाः॥
en: The abridgement, called Vaishalaksha, consisting of ten thousand chapters was then received by Indra, devoted to Brahman and possessed of great ascetic merit.

sn: भगवानपि तच्छास्त्रं संचिक्षेप पुरंदरः। सहस्रैः पञ्चभिस्तात यदुक्तं बाहुदन्तकम्॥
en: The divine Indra again abridged it into a work containing five thousand chapters and named it Vahudantaka.

sn: अध्यायानां सहस्रस्तु त्रिभिरेव बृहस्पतिः। संचिक्षेपेश्वरो बुद्ध्या बार्हस्पत्यं तदुच्यते॥
en: Afterwards the powerful Brihaspati, by his intelligence, further abridged the work, into one containing three thousand chapters and named it Barhaspatya.

sn: अध्यायानां सहस्रेण काव्यः संक्षेपमब्रवीत्। तच्छास्त्रममितप्रज्ञो योगाचार्यो महायशाः॥
en: Next, the famous teacher of Yoga, Kavi of unlimited wisdom, abridged it further into a work of a thousand chapters.

sn: एवं लोकानुरोधेन शास्त्रमेतन्महर्षिभिः। संक्षिप्तमायुर्विज्ञाय मानां ह्रासमेव च॥
en: Considering the period of human existence and the general decrease (of every thing), great Rishis did thus, for the well-being of the world, abridge that science.

sn: अथ देवाः समागम्य विष्णुमूचुः प्रजापतिम्। एको योऽर्हति मत्र्येभ्यः श्रेष्ठ्यं वै तं समादिश॥
en: Then, approaching that lord of creatures, viz., Vishnu, the god said to him,-Point out, O god, that one among men who deserves to reign supreme over the rest.

sn: ततः संचिन्त्य भगवान् देवो नारायणः प्रभुः। तैजसं वै विरजसं सोऽसृजन्मानसं सुतम्॥
en: The divine and powerful Narayana, thinking a little, created by his will a son born of his energy, named Virajas.

sn: विरजास्तु महाभागः प्रभुत्वं भुवि नैच्छत। न्यासायैवाभवद् बुद्धिः प्रणीता तस्य पाण्डव॥
en: The highly blessed Virajas, however, did not desire to rule on Earth. His mind, O son of Pandu, was bent for a life of renunciation.

sn: कीर्तिमांस्तस्य पुत्रोऽभत् सोऽपि पञ्चातिगोऽभवत्। कर्दमस्तस्य तु सुतः सोऽप्यतप्यन्महत् तपः॥
en: Virajas had a son named Krittimat. He too cast off pleasure and enjoyment. Krittimat had a son named Kardama. Kardama also practised severe austerities.

sn: प्रजापतेः कर्दमस्य त्वनङ्गो नाम वै सुतः। प्रजा रक्षयिता साधुर्दण्डनीतिविशारदः॥
en: The lord of creatures, Kardama, begot a son named Ananga, who became a protector of creatures, pious and well-read in the science of punishment.

sn: अनङ्गपुत्रोऽतिबलो नीतिमानभिगम्य वै। प्रतिपेदे महाराज्यमथेन्द्रियवशोऽभवत्॥
en: Ananga beget a son named Atibala, wellread in politics. Obtaining extensive empire after the death of his father, he became a slave of his passions.

sn: मृत्योस्तु दुहिता राजन् सुनीथा नाम मानसी। प्रख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु यासौ वेनमजीजनत्॥
en: Mrityu, O king, had a mind-begotten daughter named Sunitha well-known over the three worlds. She was married to Atibala and gave birth to a son named Vena.

sn: तं प्रजासु विधर्माणं रागद्वेषवशानुगम्। मन्त्रपूतैः कुशैर्जघ्नुर्ऋषयो ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
en: Vena, a slave of anger and malice, become impious and tyrannical towards all creatures. The Brahmavadin Rishis killed him with Kusha blades inspired with Mantras.

sn: ममन्थुर्दक्षिणं चोरुमृषयस्तस्य मन्त्रतः। ततोऽस्य विकृतो जज्ञे ह्रस्वाङ्गः पुरुषो भुवि॥ दग्धस्थूणाप्रतीकाशो रक्ताक्षः कृष्णमूर्धजः। निषीदेत्येवमूचुस्तमृषयो ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
en: Uttering Mantras all the while, those Rishis pierced the right thigh of Vena. Thereupon, from that thigh, sprang a short-limbed person on earth, resembling a charred brand, having blood-red eyes and black hair. Those Brahmavadins said to him,-Nishida (sit) here.

sn: तस्मान्निषादाः सम्भूताः क्रूराः शैलवनाश्रयाः। ये चान्ये विन्ध्यनिलया म्लेच्छाः शतसहस्रशः॥
en: From him have originated the Nishadas, viz., those wicked tribes who live in the hills and the forests, as also those hundreds and thousands of Mlechchhas, living on the Vindhya ranges.

sn: भूयोऽस्य दक्षिणं पाणिं ममन्थुस्ते महर्षयः। ततः पुरुष उत्पन्नो रूपेणेन्द्र इवापरः॥
en: The great Rishis then pierced right arm of Vena. Thence originated a person who was a second Indra in form.

sn: कवची बद्धनिस्त्रिंशः सशरः सशरासनः। वेदवेदाङ्गविच्चैव धनुर्वेदे च पारगः॥
en: Clad in mail, armed with swords, bows and arrows, and well-versed in the science of war, he was also a master of the Vedas and their auxiliaries.

sn: तं दण्डनीतिः सकला श्रिता राजन् नरोत्तमम्। ततस्तु प्राञ्जलिर्वैन्यो महर्षीस्तानुवाच ह॥
en: All the ordinances of the science of punishment, O king, came in their bodily forms to that best of men. The son of Vena then with joined-hands, said to those great Rishis.

sn: सुसूक्ष्मा मे समुत्पन्ना बुद्धिर्धर्मार्थदर्शिनी। अनया किं मया कार्यं तन्मे तत्त्वेन शंसत॥
en: I have got a very keen and fair understanding. Tell me fully what I shall do with it.

sn: यन्मां भवन्तो वक्ष्यन्ति कार्यमर्थसमन्वितम्। तदहं वै करिष्यामि नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥
en: I shall unhesitatingly accomplish any useful task which you will be pleased to indicate.

sn: तमूचुस्तत्र देवास्ते ते चैव परमर्षयः। नियतो यत्र धर्मो वै तमशङ्कः समाचर॥
en: Thus addressed, the gods that were present there, also the Rishis said to him,-"Do you fearlessly perform all sorts of righteous works.”

sn: प्रियाप्रिये परित्यज्य समः सर्वेषु जन्तुषु। कामं क्रोधं च लोभं च मानं चोत्सृज्य दूरतः॥ यश्च धर्मात् प्रविचलेल्लोके कश्चन मानवः। निग्राह्यस्ते स्वबाहुभ्यां शश्वद् धर्ममवेक्षता॥
en: Without caring for what is dear and what not so, regard all creatures with impartiality. Renounce lust, anger, covetousness and honour, and always following the dictates of righteousness, do you punish with your own hands the man, whoever he may be, who does not satisfy his duty.

sn: प्रतिज्ञा चाधिरोहस्व मनसा कर्मणा गिरा। पालयिष्याम्यहं भौमं ब्रह्म इत्येव चासकृत॥
en: Do you also swear that you would in thought, word, and deed, always maintain the religion laid on earth by the Vedas.

sn: यश्चात्र धर्मो नित्योक्तो दण्डनीतिव्यपाश्रयः तमशङ्कः करिष्यामि स्ववशो न कदाचन॥
en: Do you also swear that you would fearlessly follow the duties laid down in the Vedas with the help of the science of punishment, and that you would never act capriciously.

sn: अदण्ड्या मे द्विजाश्चेति प्रतिजानीहि हे विभो। लोकं च संकरात्कृत्स्नं त्रासास्मीति परंतप॥
en: O powerful one, know that Brahmanas are exempt from punishment, and promise further that you would protect the world from an intermixture of castes.

sn: वैन्यस्ततस्तानुवाच देवानृषिपुरोगमान्। ब्राह्मणा महाभागा नमस्याः पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Thus addressed, Vena's son replied to the deities headed by the Rishis, saying,-Those foremost of men, viz., the highly blessed Brahmanas shall ever be adored by me,

sn: एवमस्त्विति वैन्यस्तु तैरुक्तो ब्रह्मवादिभिः। पुरोधाश्चाभवत् तस्य शुक्रो ब्रह्ममयो निधिः॥
en: Those Brahmavadins then said to him, Let it be so,-Then Shukra, that great repository of Brahma became his priest.

sn: मन्त्रिणो वालखिल्याश्च सारस्वत्यो गणस्तथा। महर्षिर्भगवान् गर्गस्तस्य सांवत्सरोऽभवत्॥
en: The Valakhilyas became his ministers, and the Saraswats his companions. The great and illustrious Rishis Garga became his astrologer.'

sn: मे आत्मनाश्म इत्येव श्रुतिरेषा परा नृषु। उत्पन्नौ बन्दिनौ चास्य तत्पूर्वी सूतमागधौ॥
en: This great declaration of Shrutis is known among men that Prithu is the eighth from Vishnu, A little before two persons named Suta and Magadha were born. They became his bards and panegyrists.

sn: तयोः प्रीतो ददौ राजा पृथुर्वैन्यः प्रतापवान्। अनूपदेशं सूताय मगधं मागधाय च॥
en: Pleased, Prithu, the royal son of Vena, endued with great prowess, gave to Suta the land lying on the sea-cost, and to Magadha the country since known as Magadha.

sn: समतां वसुधायाश्च स सम्यगुदपादयत्। वैषम्यं हि परं भूमेरासीदिति च नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that the surface of the earth had before been very uneven. It was Prithu who levelled its surface.

sn: मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु विषमा जायते मही। उज्जहार ततो वैन्यः शिलाजालान् समन्ततः॥ धनुष्कोट्या महाराज तेन शैला विवर्धिताः। स विष्णुना च देवेन शक्रेण विबुधैः सह॥ ऋषिभिश्च प्रजापालैब्राह्मणैश्चाभिषेचितः। तं साक्षात् पृथिवी भेजे रत्नान्यादाय पाण्डव॥
en: In every period of Manu the earth becomes uneven. Vena's son removed the rocks lying all around. O king, with the horn of his bow. By this means the hills and mountains were increased in size. The: Vishnu, and the gods with Indra, and the Rishis, and the Regents of the world, and the Brahmanas, assembled for crowning Prithu. The earth herself, O son of Pandu, came incarnate to him, with a tribute of gems and jewels.

sn: सागरः सरितां भर्ता हिमवांश्चाचलोत्तमः। शक्रश्च धनमक्षय्यं प्रादात् तस्मै युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Ocean, that lord of rivers, and Himavat, the king of mountains, and Shakra, Yudhishthira, gave him inexhaustible wealth.

sn: रुक्मं चापि महामेरुः स्वयं कनकपर्वतः। यक्षराक्षसभर्ता च भगवान् नरवाहनः॥ धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च समर्थं प्रददौ धनम्। हया रथाश्च नागाश्च कोटिशः पुरुषास्तथा॥
en: The great Meru, that mountain of gold, gave him heaps of that precious metal. The divine Kubera carried on shoulders by men, that lord of Yakshas and Rakshasas, gave him wealth enough for perforining the necessary works of religion, profit, and pleasure. Horses, cars, elephants, and men, by millions.

sn: प्रादुर्बभूवर्वैन्यस्य चिन्तनादेव पाण्डव। न जरा न च दुर्भिक्षं नाधयो व्याधयस्तथा॥
en: O son of Pandu, were born as soon as Vena's son thought of them. At that time there prevailed neither decrepitude, nor famine, nor calamity, nor disease (on Earth).

sn: सरीसृपेभ्य: स्तेनेभ्यो न चान्योन्यात् कदाचन। भयमुत्पद्यते तत्र तस्य राज्ञोऽभिरक्षणात्॥
en: On account of the protection afforded by that king, nobody entertained any fear from reptiles and thieves of from any other source.

sn: आपस्तस्तम्भिरे चास्य समुद्रमभियास्यतः। पर्वताश्च ददुर्मार्ग ध्वजभङ्गश्च नाभवत्॥
en: When he went to the sea, the waters used to be turned solid. The mountains gave him way and his standard was never obstructed any where.

sn: तेनेयं पृथिवी दुग्धा सस्यानि दश सप्त च। यक्षराक्षसनागैश्चापीप्सितं यस्य यस्य यत्॥
en: He drew from the Earth, as a milcher from a COW, seventeen sorts of crops for the food of Yakshas, and Rakshasas, and Nagas, and other creatures.

sn: तेन धर्मोत्तस्थायं कृतो लोको महात्मना। रंजिताश्च प्रजाः सर्वास्तेन राजेति शब्द्यते॥
en: That great king caused all creatures to consider righteousness as the foremost of all things; and because he pleased all the people, therefore, he was called Rajan (king.)

sn: ब्राह्मणानां क्षतत्राणात् ततः क्षत्रिय उच्यते। प्रथिता धर्मतश्चेयं पृथिवी बहुभिः स्मृता॥
en: And because he also healed the wounds of Brahmanas, therefore, he passed by the name of Kshatriya. And because the Earth (during his regime) became celebrated for the practice of virtue, therefore, she passed by the name of Prithivi.

sn: स्थापनं चाकरोद् विष्णुः स्वयमेव सनातनः। नातिवर्तिष्यते कश्चिद् राजंस्त्वामिति भारत॥
