en: If you try to satisfy the duties of your order and wish to acquire the highest place in heaven, then give to the Brahmana all the land you may conquer, to him who is learned and of virtuous conduct, who is conversant with duties and observant of penances, who is contented with the duties of his order and not covetous of wealth.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: यो राजानं नयेद् बुद्ध्या सर्वतः परिपूर्णया। ब्राह्मणो हि कुले जातः कृतप्रज्ञो विनीतवान्॥
en: The well-born Brahmana, wise and humble, guides the king in every matter by his own great intelligence.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: श्रेयो नयति राजानं ब्रुवंश्चित्रां सरस्वतीम्। राजा चरति यद् धर्मं ब्राह्मणेन निदर्शितम्॥
en: By sound advice he makes the king acquire prosperity. The Brahmana points out to the king his duties.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: शुश्रूषुरनहंवादी क्षत्रधर्मव्रते स्थितः। तावता सत्कृतः प्राज्ञश्चिरं यशसि तिष्ठति॥ तस्य धर्मस्य सर्वस्य भागी राजपुरोहितः।
en: As long as a wish king, observant of the duties of his order, and shorn of pride, is desirous of listening to the advice of the Brahmana, so long is he respected and so long does he enjoy fame. The priest of the king, therefore, partakes, of the merit that the king acquires.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: एवमेव प्रजाः सर्वा राजानमभिसंश्रिताः॥ सम्यग्वृत्ताः स्वधर्मस्था न कुतश्चिद् भयान्विताः।
en: When the king behaves himself thus, all his subjects, depending upon him, become virtuous in their behaviour, follow their duties, and are freed from every fear.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: राष्ट्रे चरन्ति यं धर्म राज्ञा साध्वभिरक्षिताः॥ चतुर्थं तस्य धर्मस्य राजा भागं तु विन्दति।
en: The king shares a fourth part of those righteous acts which his subjects, wellprotected by him, perform in his kingdom.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: देवा मनुष्याः पितरो गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसाः॥ यज्ञमेवोपजीवन्ति नास्ति चेष्टमराजके।
en: The gods, men, Pitris, Gandharvas, Uragas, and Rakshasas, all derive their support from sacrifices. In a country having no king, their can be no sacrifice.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: इतो दत्तेन जीवन्ति देवताः पितरस्तथा॥ राजन्येवास्य धर्मस्य योगक्षेमः प्रतिष्ठितः।
en: The gods and the Pitris live upon the offerings made in sacrifices. Sacrifice, however, dependants upon the king.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: छायायामप्सु वायौ च सुखमुष्णेऽधिगच्छति॥ अग्नौ वाससि सूर्ये च सुखं शीतेऽधिगच्छति।
en: In summer, men seek comfort from the shade of trees, cool water, and cool breezes. In winter, they derive comfort from fire, warm clothing and the sun.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: शब्दे स्पर्शे रसे रूपे गन्धे च रमते मनः॥ तेषु भोगेषु सर्वेषु न भीतो लभते सुखम्।
en: The heart of man finds pleasure in sound, touch, taste, vision, and smell. The man, however, who is filled with fear, finds no pleasure in all these things.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: अभयस्य हि यो दाता तस्यैव सुमहत् फलम्। न हि प्राणसमं दानं त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते॥
en: That person, who removes the fears of men, acquires great merit. There is no present so valuable in three worlds as that of life.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: इन्द्रो राजा यमो राजा धर्मो राजा तथैव च। राजा बिभर्ति रूपाणि राज्ञा सर्वमिदं धृतम्॥
en: The king is Indra. The king is Yama. The king is Dharma. The king puts on different forms. The king preserves and supports every things.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: अभयस्य हि यो दाता तस्यैव सुमहत् फलम्। न हि प्राणसमं दानं त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते॥
en: That person, who removes the fears of men, acquires great merit. There is no present so valuable in three worlds as that of life.

description: The divine right of the king. How should he appoint a priest
sn: इन्द्रो राजा यमो राजा धर्मो राजा तथैव च। राजा बिभर्ति रूपाणि राज्ञा सर्वमिदं धृतम्॥
en: The king is Indra. The king is Yama. The king is Dharma. The king puts on different forms. The king preserves and supports every things.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: भीष्म उवाच राज्ञा पुरोहितः कार्यो भवेद् विद्वान् बहुश्रुतः। उभौ समीक्ष्य धर्मार्थावप्रमेयावनन्तरम्॥
en: Bhishma said The king, observing both religious merit and profit which are very intricate, should, forthwith, appoint a priest learned and acquainted intimately with the Vedas and the (other) scriptures.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: धर्मात्मा मन्त्रविद् येषां राज्ञां राजन् पुरोहितः। राजा चैवंगुणो येषां कुशलं तेषु सर्वशः॥
en: Those kings, who have priests, who are pious and conversant with policy, and are possessed of good attributes, enjoy prosperity everywhere.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: उभौ प्रजा वर्धयतो देवान् सर्वान् सुतान् पितृन्। भवेयातां स्थितौ धर्मे श्रद्धेयौ सुतपस्विनौ॥
en: Both the priest and the king should have such qualities as arrest honour, and should observe the vows and penances. They would then succeed in supporting the subjects, the deities. the Pitris, and the children.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: परस्परस्य सुहृदौ विहितौ समचेतसौ। ब्रह्मक्षत्रस्य सम्मानात् प्रजा सुखमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: It is laid down that they should have similar hearts and should be each other's friends. For such friendship between Brahmana and Kshatriya, the subjects become happy.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: विमाननात् तयोरेव प्रजा नश्येयुरेव हि। ब्रह्मक्षत्रं हि सर्वेषां वर्णानां मूलमुच्यते॥
en: If they do not respect each other, destruction would befall the people. The Brahmana and the Kshatriya are said to be the creators of all men.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। ऐलकश्यपसंवादं तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old story about the discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa. Listen to it, О Yudhishthira.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: ऐल उवाच यदा हि ब्रह्म प्रजहाति क्षत्रं क्षत्रं यदा वा प्रजहाति ब्रह्मा अन्वरबलं कतमेऽस्मिन्भजन्ते तथा वर्णाः कतमेऽस्मिन् ध्रियन्ते॥
en: Aila's son said When the Brahmana forsakes the Kshatriya or the Kshatriya forsakes the Brahmana, who amongst them should be considered superior, and upon whom would the other orders depend and maintain themselves?

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: कश्यप उवाच विद्धं राष्ट्र क्षत्रियस्य भवति। ब्रह्मक्षत्रं यत्र विरुद्ध्यतीह। अन्वग्बलं दस्यवस्तद्भजन्ते तथा वर्णं तत्र विदन्ति सन्तः॥
en: Kashyapa said Ruin befalls the kingdom of the Kshatriya when the Brahmana and Kshatriya fight with each other. Robbers attack that kingdom in which anarchy reigns and all good men regard the king as a Mlechchha.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: नैषां ब्रह्म च वर्धते नोत पुत्रा न गर्गरो मथ्यते नो यजन्ते। नैषां पुत्रा वेदमधीयते च यदा ब्रह्म क्षत्रियाः संत्यजन्ति॥
en: Their oxen do not thrive, nor do their children. Their pots (of milk) are not churned, and no sacrifices are celebrated there. The children do not study the Vedas in kingdoms where Brahmanas forsake Kshatriyas.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: नैषामर्थो वर्धते जातु गेहे नाधीयते सुप्रजा नो यजन्ते। अपध्वस्ता दस्यु ताः भवन्ति ये ब्राह्मणान् क्षत्रियाः संत्यजन्ति॥
en: In their houses wealth does not multiply. There children do not become good and do not read the scriptures and celebrate sacrifices. Those Kshatriyas that forsake the Brahmanas become impure in blood.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: एतौ हि नित्यं संयुक्तावितरेतरधारणे। क्षत्रं वै ब्रह्मणो योनिोनिः क्षत्रस्य वै द्विजाः॥
en: The Brahmana and the Kshatriya are connected with each other by nature, and each protects the other. The Kshatriya is the root of the Brahmana's advancement and the Brahmana is the root of the Kshatriya's advancement.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: उभावेतौ नित्यमभिप्रपन्नौ सम्प्रापतुर्महतीं सम्प्रतिष्ठाम्! तयोः संधिर्भिद्यते चेत् पुराण स्ततः सर्वं भवति हि सम्प्रमूढम्॥
en: When each helps the other, both enjoy great prosperity. If their friendship, existing from days of yore, is snapped anarchy prevails everywhere.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: नात्र पारं लभते पारगामी महागाधे गौरिव सम्प्रपन्ना। चातुर्वण्र्यं भवति हि सम्प्रमूढं प्रजास्ततः क्षयसंस्था भवन्ति॥
en: No person, desirous of crossing the ocean of life, succeeds in his attempts like a small boat floating on the bosom of the sea. The four orders of men become confounded and meet with destruction,

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: ब्रह्मवृक्षो रक्ष्यमाणो मधु हेम च वर्षति। अरक्ष्यमाण: सततमश्रु पापं च वर्षति॥
en: If the tree of a Brahmana is protected, it showers gold and honey. If on the other hand, it is not protected, it then showers tears and sin.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: न ब्रह्मचारी चरणादयेतो यदा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मणि त्राणमिच्छेत्। आश्चर्यतो वर्षति तत्र देव स्तत्राभीक्ष्णं दुःसहाश्चाविशन्ति॥
en: When Brahmanas neglect the study of the Vedas and seek protection from the scriptures, then Indra does not pour rain in time and various sorts of calamities constantly assail the kingdom.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: स्त्रियं हत्वा ब्राह्मणं वापि पाप: सभायां यत्र लभतेऽनुवादम्। राज्ञः सकाशे न बिभेति चापि ततो भयं विद्यते क्षत्रियस्या॥
en: When a sinful wretch, having killed a woman or a Brahmana, does not incur censure in assemblies of fellowmen and does not fear the king, then danger threatens the Kshatriya king.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: पापैः पापे क्रियमाणे हि चैल ततो रुद्रो जायते देव एषः। पापैः पापा: संजनयन्ति रुद्र ततः सर्वान् साध्वसाधून् हिनस्ति॥
en: For the sins perpetrated by sinful men, the god Rudra appears in the kingdom. Indeed, the sinful by their sins invite that god of vengeance. He then kills all, the honest and the wicked alike.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: ऐल एवाच कुतो रुद्रः कीदृशो वापि रुद्रः सत्त्वैः सत्त्वं दृश्यते वध्यमानम्। एतत् सर्वं कश्यप मे प्रचक्ष्व कुतो रुद्रो जायते देव एषः॥
en: Aila said Whence does Rudra originate? What also is his form? Creatures are seen to be destroyed by creatures. Tell me all this, O Kashyapa, Whence does the god Rudra originate.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: कश्यप उवाच आत्मा रुद्रो हृदयो मानवानां स्वं स्वं देहं परदेहं न हन्ति। वातोत्पातैः सदृशं रुद्रमार्ह र्देवैर्जीमूतैः सदृशं रूपमस्य॥
en: Kashyapa said Rudra exists in the hearts of men. He destroys the bodies themselves in which he lives as also the bodies of others. Rudra is like visitations of the sky and his form is like that of the wind-god.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: ऐल उवाच वातः परिवृणोति कर्थि न जीमूतो वर्षति नापि देवः। तथायुक्तो दृश्यते मानुषेषु कामद्वेषाद् बध्यते मुह्यते च॥ न वै
en: The Wind does not, by blowing, visible destroy men at all times, nor does Indra do so by purring rain. On the other hand, it is seen among men that they lose their senses and are killed through lust and malice.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: कश्यप उवाच यथैकगेहे जातवेदाः प्रदीप्तः कृत्स्नं ग्रामं दहते चत्वरं वा। विमोहनं कुरुते देव एष ततः सर्वं स्पृश्यते पुण्यपापैः॥
en: Kashyapa said, Fire burning in one house, burns a whole quarter or an entire village. Likewise this deity stupefies the senses of some one and then that stupefaction affects all, the honest and the wicked alike, without any distinction.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: ऐल उवाच यदि दण्डः स्पृशतेऽपुण्यपापं पापैः पापे क्रियमाणे विशेषात्। सुकृतं नाम कुर्याद् दुष्कृतं वा कस्य हेतोर्न कुर्यात्॥ कस्य हेतोः
en: Aila Said: If punishment affects all, viz., the honest and the wicked alike, on account of the sins committed by the sinful, why should men, in that case, perform acts that are meritorious? Indeed, why should they abstain from wicked acts.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: कश्यप उवाच असंत्यागात् पापकृतामपा स्तुल्यो दण्डः स्पृशते मिश्रभावात्। शुष्णा दह्यते मिश्रभार्वा न मिश्रः स्यात् पापकृद्भिः कथंचित्॥
en: By standing aloof from the sinful, one becomes pure and stainless. However, by being mixed with the sinful, the sinless are punished. Wet wood, if mixed with dry wood, is consumed by the fire for such mixture. The sinless, therefore, should never associate with the sinful.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: ऐल उवाच साध्वसाधून् धारयतीह भूमिः साध्वसाधूंस्तापयतीह सूर्यः। साध्वसाधूंश्चापि वातीह वायु रापस्तथा साध्वसाधून् पुनन्ति॥
en: Aila said The Earth contains the honest and the wicked. The sun warms the honest and the wicked. The wind blows equally for them. Water cleanses them equally.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: कश्यप उवाच एवमस्मिन्वर्तते लोक एव नामुत्रं वर्तते राजपुत्र। प्रेत्यैतयोरन्तरावान्विशेषो यो वै पुण्यं चरते यश्च पापम्॥
en: Kashyapa said Such, indeed, is the course of this world, O prince. It is not so, however, in another world. In the other world, there is a great difference between the person that acts virtuously and him that acts sinfully.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: पुण्यस्य लोको मधुमान् घृतार्चि हिरण्यज्योतिरमृतस्य नाभिः। तत्र प्रेत्य मोदते ब्रह्मचारी न तत्र मृत्युर्न जरा नोत दुःखम्॥
en: The regions which virtuous men acquire are full of honey and the splendour of gold or of fire upon which clarified butter has been poured. They are compared to the navel of ambrosia. The meritorious person enjoys great happiness there. Death, decrepitude, and sorrow are not there.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: पापस्य लोको निरयोऽप्रकाशो नित्यं दुःखं शोकभूयिष्ठमेवा तत्रात्मानं शोचति पापकर्मा बह्वीः समाः प्रतपन्नपतिष्ठः॥
en: The region for the sinful is hell. Darkness and constant pain are there, and it is full of sorrow. Sinking in infamy, the sinful man grieves for many years.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: मिथो भेदाब्राह्मणक्षत्रियाणां प्रजा दुःखं दुःसहं चाविशन्ति। एवं ज्ञात्वा कार्य एवेह नित्यं पुरोहितो नैकविद्यो नृपेणा॥
en: For a division between Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, numberless griefs assail the people. Knowing this, a king should appoint a (Brahmana) priest having experience and wide knowledge. owner

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: तं चैवान्वभिषिच्येत तथा धर्मो विधीयते। अग्रयो हि ब्राह्मणः प्रोक्तः सर्वस्यैवेह धर्मतः॥
en: A king should first engage the priest in his office, and then perform his own coronation. This has bean laid down in the scriptures. The ordinance declare that the Brahmana is the foremost of all creatures. Men who know the Vedas say that the Brahinana was created first.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: पूर्वं हि ब्राह्मणः सृष्टिरिति ब्रह्मविदो विदुः। ज्येष्ठेनाभिजनेनास्य प्राप्तं पूर्वं यदुत्तरम्॥
en: For the precedence of his birth, all things that are good in this world are in him, the Brahmana, who is the of best productions of the creation, is also for such precedence, worthy of the respect and the worship of all creatures.

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: तस्मान्यान्यश्च पूज्यश्च ब्राह्मणः प्रसृतागभुक्। सर्वं श्रेष्ठं विशिष्टं च निवेद्यं तस्य धर्मतः॥
en: A king, however powerful, powerful, should according to the injunctions of the scriptures confer upon the Brahmana whatever is best and superior to all others,

description: The appointment of a priest. The discourse between Aila's son and Kashyapa
sn: अवश्यमेव कर्तव्यं राज्ञा बलवतापि हि। ब्रह्म वर्धयति क्षत्रं क्षत्रतो ब्रह्म वर्धते। एवं राज्ञा विशेषेण पूज्या ब्राह्मणाः सदा॥
en: The Brahmana contributes to the advancement of the Kshatriya, Kshatriya, and the Kshatriya to that of the Brahmana. Brahmana should, therefore, be especially and always adored by kings.'

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: भीष्म उवाच योगक्षेमो हि राष्ट्रस्य राजन्यायत्त उच्यते। योगक्षेमो हि राज्ञो हि समायत्त पुरोहिते॥
en: Bhishma said It is said that the preservation and advancement of the kingdom depends upon the king. The preservation and advancement of the kings depends upon the king's priest.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: यत्रादृष्टं भयं ब्रह्म प्रजानां शमयत्युत। दृष्टं च राजा बाहुभ्यां तद् राज्यं सुखमेधते॥
en: That kingdom truly enjoys felicity where the invisible fears of the subjects, are removed by the Brahmana and all visible ones are suppressed by the king with the strength of his arin.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। मुचुकुन्दस्य संवादं राज्ञो वैश्रवणस्य च॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between king Muchukunda and Vaishravana.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: मुचुकुन्दो विजित्येमां पृथिवीं पृथिवीपतिः। जिज्ञासमानः स्वबलमभ्ययादलकाधिपम्॥
en: King Muchukunda, having conquered the entire Earth, went to the lord of Alaka for testing his strength.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: ततो वैश्रवणो राजा राक्षसानसृजत् तदा। ते बलान्यवमृद्गन्त मुचुकुन्दस्य नैर्ऋताः॥
en: King Vaishravana created a large army of Rakshasas. These grinded the army led by Muchukunda.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: स हन्यमाने सैन्ये स्वे मुचुकुन्दो नराधिपः। गर्हयामास विद्वांसं पुरोहितमरिंदमः॥
en: Witnessing the destruction of his army, king Muchukunda, O chastiser of foes, began to remonstrate with his own feared priest Vasishtha.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: तत उग्रं तपस्तप्त्वा वसिष्ठो धर्मवित्तमः। रक्षांस्युपावधीत् तस्य पन्थानं चाप्यविन्दत॥
en: Thereupon that foremost of righteous persons, viz, Vasishtha, practised very austere penances, and, causing those Rakshasas to be killed, ascertained the true course which Muchukunda was following.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: ततो वैश्रवणो राजा मुचुकुन्दमदर्शयत्। वध्यमानेषु सैन्येषु वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: When king Vaishravana's troops were being killed, he showed himself Muchukunda and said these words. to

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: धनद उवाच बलवन्तस्त्वया पूर्वे राजानः सपुरोहिताः। न चैवं समवर्तन्त यथा त्वमिह वर्तसे॥
en: The Lord of Death said Many kings of yore, more powerful than you, aided by their priests, had never approached me thus.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: ते खल्वपि कृतास्त्राश्च बलवन्तश्च भूमिपाः। आगम्य पर्युपासन्ते मामीशं सुखदुःखयोः॥
en: All of them were clever in weapons and all of them were powerful. Knowing me as the giver of happiness and misery, they approached me for offering adorations.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: यद्यस्ति बाहुवीर्यं ते तद् दर्शयितुमर्हसि। किं ब्राह्मणबलेन त्वमतिमात्र प्रवर्तसे॥
en: In truth, if you have might of arms you should display it. Why do you act so proudly helped by Brahmana power.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: मुचुकुन्दस्ततः क्रुद्धः प्रत्युवाच धनेश्वरम्। न्यायपूर्वमसंरब्धमसम्भ्रान्तमिदं वचः॥
en: Enraged at these words, Muchukunda, shorn of pride and fear, said to the Lord of Death these words pregnant with reason and justice.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: ब्रह्मक्षत्रमिदं सृष्टमेकयोनि स्वयम्भुवा। पृथग्बलविधानं तन्न लोकं परिपालयेत्॥
en: The Self-create Brahman created the Brahmana and the Kshatriya. They have a common origin. If they apply their energies separately, they would never be able to keep up the world.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: तपो मन्त्रबलं नित्यं ब्राह्मणेषु प्रतिष्ठितम्। अस्त्रबाहुबलं नित्यं क्षत्रियेषु प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: The power of penances and Mantras was given to the Brahmanas; the strength of arms and of weapons was conferred upon Kshatriyas.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: ताभ्यां सम्भूय कर्तव्यं प्रजानां परिपालनम्। तथा च मां प्रवर्तन्तं किं गर्हस्यलकाधिप।॥
en: Helped by both kinds of strength, kings should protect their subjects. I am acting in that way. Why do you, O lord of Alaka, remonstrate with me then?

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: ततोऽब्रवीद् वैश्रवणो राजानं सपुरोहितम्। नाहं राज्यमनिर्दिा कस्मैचिद् विदधाम्युत॥ नाच्छिन्दे चाप्यनिादमिति जानीहि पार्थिव।
en: Thus accosted, Vaishravana said to Muchukunda and his priest,-I never, without being ordered (by the Self-born) confr sovereignty upon any one. Nor do I ever, without his behest, snatch it away from any one. Know this, O king.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: प्रशाधि पृथिवीं कृत्स्ना मद्दत्तामखिलामिमाम्। एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच मुचुकुन्दो महीपतिः॥
en: Do you rule then the boundless Earth.—Thus addressed, king Muchukunda replied, saying.-

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: मुचुकुन्द उवाच नाहं राज्यं भवद्दत्तं भोक्तुमिच्छामि पार्थिव। बाहुवीर्यार्जितं राज्यम श्नीयामिति कामये॥
en: I do not, O king, desire to enjoy sovereignty given by you as a gift. I desire to enjoy sovereignty secured by the power of my own arms.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो वैश्रवणो राजा विस्मयं परमं ययौ। क्षत्रधर्मे स्थितं दृष्ट्वा मुचुकुन्दमसम्भ्रमम्॥
en: Bhishma said At these words of Muchukunda, Vaishravana, seeing the king undaunted in the observance of Kshatriya duties, was stricken with surprise.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: ततो राजा मुचुकुन्दः सोऽन्वशासद् वसुन्धराम्। बाहुवीर्यार्जितां सम्यक्षत्रधर्ममनुव्रतः॥
en: King Muchukunda, devoted to Kshatriya duties, continued to rule the entire Earth acquired by the power of his own arms.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: एवं यो धर्मविद् राजा ब्रह्मपूर्वं प्रवर्तते। जयत्यविजितामुर्वी यशश्च महदश्नुते॥
en: That virtuous king, who governs his kingdom, aided by and revering the Brahmana, succeeds in subjugating the whole Earth and acquiring great fame.

description: The necessity of a priest to a king, the discourse between Muchakunda and Vaisravana.
sn: नित्योदकी ब्राह्मणः स्यान्नित्यशस्त्रश्च क्षत्रियः। तयोहि सर्वमायत्तं यत् किञ्चिज्जगतीगतम्॥
en: The Brahmana should daily perform his religious rites and the Kshatriya should always be ready with weapons. They both are the rightful owners of everything in the world.'

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यथा वृत्त्या महीपालो विवर्धयति मानवान्। पुण्यांश्च लोकान् जयति तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Describe to me, O grandfather, the conduct by which a king succeeds in advancing his subjects and earning regions of happiness in the other world.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: भीष्म उवाच दानशीलो भवेद् राजा यज्ञशीलश्च भारत। उपवासतप:शीलः प्रजानां पालने रतः॥
en: Bhishma said "The king should be liberal and should celebrate sacrifices, O Bharata. He should observe vows and penances, and should be devoted to the duty of protecting his subjects.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: सर्वाश्चैव प्रजा नित्यं राजा धर्पण पालयन्। उत्थानेन प्रदानेन पूजयेच्चापि धार्मिकान्॥
en: Virtuously protecting all his subjects he should honour all pious persons by standing up when they come and by making presents to them.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: राज्ञा हि पूजितो धर्मस्ततः सर्वत्र पूज्यते। यद् यदाचरते राजा तत् प्रजानां स्म रोचते॥
en: If the king honours it, righteousness is honoured everywhere. Whatever acts and things a king likes they are liked by his subjects.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: नित्यमुद्यतदण्डश्च भवेन्मृत्युरिवारिषु। निहन्यात् सर्वतो दस्यून न कामात् कस्यचित् क्षमेत्॥५
en: The king should always be like Death to his enemies with the rod of punishment uplifted in his hands, He should root out robbers in his kingdom and never pardon any one capriciously.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: यं हि धर्मं चरन्तीह प्रजा राज्ञा सुरक्षिताः। चतुर्थं तस्य धर्मस्य राजा भारत विन्दति॥
en: The king, O Bharata, acquires a fourth part of merit that his subjects acquire under his shelter.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: यदधीते यद् ददाति यज्जुहोति यदर्चति। राजा चतुर्थभाक् तस्य प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन्॥ यद् राष्ट्रेऽकुशलं किञ्चिद् राज्ञोऽरक्षयतः प्रजाः। चतुर्थं तस्य पापस्य राजा भारत विन्दति॥
en: By only protecting his subjects the king acquires a fourth part of merit that his subjects acquire by study, by gift, by pouring libations, and by adoring the gods. The king acquires a fourth part of also the sin that his subjects commit on account, any distress in the kingdom arising from the king's neglect in satisfying the duty of protection.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: अप्याहुः सर्वमेवेति भूयोऽर्धमिति निश्चयः। कर्मणः पृथिवीपाल नृशंसोऽनृतवागपि॥
en: Some say that the king earns a half, and some say the full measure, of whatever sin is caused by his becoming cruel and a liar.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: तादृशात् किल्बिषाद् राजा शृणु येन प्रमुच्यते। प्रत्याहर्तुमशक्यं स्याद् धनं चोरैर्हतं यदि। तत् स्वकोशात् प्रदेयं स्यादशक्तेनोपजीवतः॥
en: Listen now to the means by which the king may purge off such sins. If the king fails to restore to a subject the wealth that has been stolen away by thieves he should then make good the loss from his own treasury, or, in case of inability, with wealth taken from his dependants.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: सर्ववर्णः सदा रक्ष्यं ब्रह्मस्वं ब्राह्मणा यथा। न स्थेयं विषये तेन योऽपकुर्याद् द्विजातिषु॥
en: All the cases should protect the wealth of a Brahmana as well as his body and life. The person that offends against Brahmanas should be banished from the kingdom.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: ब्रह्मस्वे रक्ष्यमाणे तु सर्वं भवति रक्षितम्। तस्मात् तेषां प्रसादेन कृतकृत्यो भवेन्नृपः॥
en: Everything is protected by protecting Brahmana's wealth. Through the favour of the Brahmanas, which may thus be secured, the king becomes crowned with success.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: पर्जन्यमिव भूतानि महाद्रुममिव द्विजाः। नरास्तमुपजीवन्ति नृपं सर्वार्थसाधकम्॥
en: Men seek the shelter of a capable king like creatures seeking relief from the clouds or birds seeking refuge in a large tree.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: न हि कामात्मना राज्ञा सततं कामबुद्धिना। नृशंसेनातिलुब्धेन शक्यं पालयितुं प्रजाः॥
en: A cruel and covetous king, always lustful and seeking the gratification of his desires can never protect his subject.'

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच नाहं राज्यसुखान्वेषी राज्यमिच्छाम्यपि क्षणम्। धर्मार्थं रोचये राज्यं धर्मश्चात्र न विद्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said I do not, for a moment, seek the happiness of sovereignty itself for its own sake. I desire it, however, for the sake of the merit one may gain from it. It seems to me that it has no merit.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: तदलं मम राज्येन यत्र धर्मो न विद्यते। वनमेव गमिष्यामि तस्माद् धर्मचिकीर्षया॥ तत्र मेध्येष्वरण्येषु न्यस्तदण्डो जितेन्द्रियः। धर्ममाराधयिष्यामि मुनिर्मूलफलाशनः॥
en: There is no such necessity by which no merit can be acquired. I shall, therefore, retire. into the forest acquiring religious merit. Laying aside the rod of punishment and controlling my senses, I shall go to the forest which is sacred and seek to acquire the merit of righteousness by becoming an ascetic living upon fruits and roots."

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: भीष्म उवाच वेदाहं तव या बुद्धिरानृशंस्यगुणैव सा। न च शुद्धनृशंस्येन शक्यं राज्यमुपासितम्॥
en: Bhishma said 'I know, O Yudhishthira, what the nature of your heart is, and how inoffensive you are. You will not, however, by inoffensiveness alone, succeed in governing your kingdom.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: अपि तु त्वां मृदुप्रज्ञमत्यार्यमतिधार्मिकम्। क्लीबं धर्मघृणायुक्तं न लोको बहु मन्यते॥
en: Your heart is mild by nature, you are merciful, and highly righteous. You are without energy, are virtuous and full of compassion. People, however, do not respect you.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: वृत्तं तु स्वमपेक्षस्व पितृपैतामहोचितम्। नैव राज्ञां तथा वृत्तं यथा त्वं स्थातुमिच्छसि॥
en: Follow the conduct of your father and grandfather. Kings should never follow the conduct which you seek to adopt.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: न हि वैक्लव्यसंसृष्टमानृशंस्यमिहास्थितः। प्रजापालनसम्भूतमाप्ता धर्मफलं ह्यसि॥
en: Never be affected by anxiety, and never adopt such inoffensive conduct. By becoming so, you would not earn that merit of righteousness which arises from protecting subjects.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: न ह्येतामाशिषं पाण्डुर्न च कुन्ती त्वयाचता तथैतत् प्रज्ञया तात यथाऽऽचरसि मेधया॥
en: The conduct you wish to follow urged on by your intelligence and wisdom, is not quiet of a piece with those blessings which your father Pandu or your mother Kunti used to solicit for you.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: शौर्य बलं च सत्यं च पिता तव सदाब्रवीत्। माहात्म्यं च महौदार्यं भवतः कुन्त्ययाचत॥
en: Your father always prayed for your courage, might, and truth. Kunti always prayed for your high-mindedness and liberality.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: नित्यं स्वाहा स्वधा नित्यं चोभे मानुषदैवते। पुढेष्वाशासते नित्यं पितरो दैवतानि च।॥
en: The offerings with Svaha and Svadha in Shraddhas and sacrifices are always solicited from children by the Pitris and the deities.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: दानमध्ययनं यज्ञं प्रजानां परिपालनम्। धर्ममेतदधर्मं वा जन्मनैवाभ्यजायथाः॥
en: Whether gifts, study, sacrifices and the protection of subjects, virtuous of sinful you are born to practise and perform them.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: काले धुरि च युक्तानां वहतां भारमाहितम्। सीदतामपि कौन्तेय न कीर्तिरवसीदति॥
en: The fame of men never suffers, even it they fail in bearing the burden which is placed on them and to which they are wedded for life.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: समन्ततो विनियतो वहत्यस्खलितो हि यः। निर्दोषः कर्मवचनात् सिद्धिः कर्मण एव सा॥
en: Even a horse, if properly trained, succeeds in carrying without dropping down a burden. One incurs no blame if only his acts and words be proper, for success depends upon them,

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: नैकान्तविनिपातेन विचचारेह कश्चन। धर्मी गृही वा राजा वा ब्रह्मचारी यथा पुनः॥
en: No person, be he a virtuous house-holder, or be he a king, or be he a Brahmacharin, has ever succeeded in conducting himself without failure.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: अल्पं हि सारभूयिष्ठं यत् कर्मोदारमेव तत्। कृतमेवाकृताच्छ्रेयो न पापीयोऽस्त्यकर्मणः॥
en: It is better to do an act which is good and which carries but limited merit than to totally abstain from all acts, for perfect inaction is very culpable.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: यदा कुलीनो धर्मज्ञः प्राणोत्यैश्वर्यमुत्तमम्। योगक्षेमस्तदा राज्ञः कुशलायैव कल्प्यते॥
en: When a high-born and righteous person acquires profuse wealth the king then succeeds in obtaining prosperity in all his works.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: दानेनान्यं बलेनान्यमन्यं सूनृतया गिरा। सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयाद् राज्यं प्राप्येह धार्मिकः॥
en: A virtuous king, having obtained a kingdom, should try to subdue some by presents, some by force, and some by sweet words.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: यं हि वैद्याः कुले जाता ह्यवृत्तिभयपीडिताः। प्राप्य तृप्ताः प्रतिष्ठन्ति धर्मः कोऽभ्यधिकस्ततः॥
en: There is no one more virtuous than he, upon whom high-born and learned persons depend from fear of losing their means of sustenance and depending upon upon whom they live contentedly.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं तात परमं स्वयँ का ततः प्रीतिरुत्तमा। किं ततः परमैश्वर्यं ब्रूहि मे यदि पश्यसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said What acts, O sir, lead to heaven? What is the nature of the great happiness that is derived from them? What also is the high prosperity that may be obtained from them? Tell me all this, if you know.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: भीष्म उवाच यस्मिन् भयादितः सम्यक् क्षेमं विन्दत्यपि क्षणम्। स स्वर्गजित्तमोऽस्माकं सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Bhishma said That man, from whom a person assailed by fear obtains even a momentary relief, deserves heaven from amongst the best of us. What I tell you is very true.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: त्वमेव प्रीतिमांस्तस्मात् कुरूणां कुरुसत्तम। भव राजा जय स्वर्ग सतो रक्षासतो जहि॥
en: Be you gladly the king of the Kurus, O foremost one of Kuru's race, acquire heaven, protect the good, and kill the wicked.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: अनु त्वां तात जीवन्तु सुहृदः साधुभिः सह। पर्यन्यमिव भूतानि स्वादुद्रुममिव द्विजाः॥
en: Let your friends, together with all honest man, derive their support from you, like all creatures from the god of the clouds and like birds from a large tree with sweet fruits.

description: The virtues by which a king acquires happiness in the next world.
sn: धृष्टं शूरं प्रहर्तारमनृशसं जितेन्द्रियम्। वत्सलं संविभक्तारमुपजीवन्ति तं नराः॥
en: Men seek refuge with that person who is dignified, courageous, capable of striking, merciful, has under control, is affectionate towards all, the impartial and just. senses

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच स्वकर्मण्यपरे युक्तास्तथैवान्ये विकर्मणि। तेषां विशेषमाचक्ष्व ब्राह्मणानां पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, amongst Brahmanas some follow the duties proper to their order while others follow other duties. Tell me the difference between tow lasses.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: भीष्म उवाच विद्यालक्षणसम्पन्नाः सर्वत्र समदर्शिनः। एते ब्रह्मसमा राजन् ब्राह्मणाः परिकीर्तिताः॥
en: Those Brahmanas, o king, who are learned and beneficent, and who look upon all creatures impartially, are said to be equal to। Brahma.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: ऋग्जयुःसामसम्पन्ना सर्वेषु कर्मस्ववस्थिताः। एते देवसमा राजन् ब्राह्मणानां भवन्त्युत॥
en: Those who are conversant with the Rishis, the Yajus, and the Samans and who follow the practices of their order, are, O king, equal to the very gods.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: जन्मकर्मविहीना ये कदर्या ब्रह्मबन्धवः। एते शूद्रसमा राजन् ब्राह्मणानां भवन्त्युत॥
en: Those, however, who are not well-born and do not follow the duties of their order, and are, addicted to evil practices, are like Shudras.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: अश्रोत्रियाः सर्व एव सर्वे चानाहिताग्नयः। तान् सर्वान् धार्मिको राजा बलिं विष्टिं च कारयेत्॥
en: A virtuous king should realise tribute from and compel to enter the public service without any remuneration those Brahmanas who are not well read in the Vedas and who have not their own fires to worship.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: आह्वायका देवलका नाक्षत्रा ग्रामयाजकाः। एते ब्राह्मणचाण्डाला महापथिकपञ्चमाः॥
en: Those, who are employed in law courts for summoning people, those who perform worship for other for money, those who perform the sacrifices of Vaishyas and Shudras, those who officiate in sacrifices on behalf of a whole village, and those who make voyages on the ocean,—these five are regarded as Chandalas among Brahmanas.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: ऋत्विक् पुरोहितो मन्त्री दूतो वार्तानुकर्षकः। एते क्षत्रसमा राजन् ब्राह्मणानां भवन्त्युत॥
en: Those who become Ritwijas, Purohitas, counsellors, envoys and messengers become, O king, equal to Kshatriyas.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: अश्वारोहा गजारोहा रथिनोऽथ पदातयः। एते वैश्यसमा राजन् ब्राह्मणानां भवन्त्युत॥
en: Those, who ride horses or elephants or cars or become foot-soldiers, become, O king, equal to Vaishyas.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: एतेभ्यो बलिमादद्याद्धीनकोशो महीपतिः। ऋते ब्रह्मसमेभ्यश्च देवकल्पेभ्य एव च॥
en: If the king's treasury is not well replenished, he may take tribute from these. In realising tribute, the king, however, should except those Brahmanas who are equal to the gods or Brahma.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: अब्राह्मणानां वित्तस्य स्वामी राजेति वैदिकम्। ब्राह्मणानां च ये केचिद् विकर्मस्था भवन्त्युत॥
en: The Vedas say that the king is the master of the wealth of all the orders except Brahmanas. He can take the wealth of those Brahmanas who have neglected to perform their legitimate duties.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: विकर्मस्थाश्च नोपेक्ष्या विप्रा राज्ञा कथंचन। नियम्याः संविभज्याश्च धर्मानुग्रहकारणात्॥
en: The king should never treat in-differently those Brahmanas who do not observe their duties. For the sake of making his people virtuous, he should punish and take them away from their betters.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: यस्य स्म विषये राजन् स्तेनो भवति वै द्विजः। राज्ञ एवापराधं तं मन्यन्ते तद्विदो जनाः॥
en: That king, O monarch, in whose territories a Brahmana becomes a thief, is charged by the learned as the doer of that misdeed.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: अवृत्त्या यो भवेत् स्तेनो वेदवित् स्नातकस्तथा। राजन् स राज्ञा भर्तव्य इति वेदविदो विदुः॥
en: Persons conversant with the Vedas declare that if a Brahmana versed in the Vedas and observant of vows becomes, through want of means, a thief, it is the duty of the king to support him.

description: The difference between the Brahmanas following the duties of their own orders-and those following other duties
sn: स चेन्नो परिवर्तेत कृतवृत्तिः परंतप। ततो निर्वासनीयः स्यात् तस्माद् देशात् सबान्धवः।
en: If, after provision has been made for his maintenance, he does not abstain from thefts, he should then, O scorcher of foes, be exiled from the kingdom with all his relatives.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच केषां प्रभवते राजा वित्तस्य भरतर्षभ। कया च वृत्त्या वर्तेत तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Of whose wealth, O foremost of Bharata's race, is the king considered to be the master? And what conduct also should the king follow? Describe to me this, O grandfather!

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: भीष्म उवाच अब्राह्मणानां वित्तस्य स्वामी राजेति वैदिकम्। ब्राह्मणानां च ये केचिद् विकर्मस्था भवन्त्युत॥
en: Bhishma said 'The Vedas declare that the king is the master of the wealth that belongs to all persons except Brahmanas, as also of those Brahmanas who do not follow their proper duties.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: विकर्मस्थाश्च नोपेक्ष्या विप्रा राज्ञा कथञ्चन। इति राज्ञां पुरावृत्तमाभिजल्पन्ति साधवः॥
en: The king should not spare those Brahmanas who do not follow their duties. The righteous say that this is the ancient practice of kings.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: यस्य स्म विषये राज्ञः स्तेनो भवति वै द्विजः। राज्ञ एवापराधं तं मन्यन्ते किल्बिषं नृप॥
en: That king, O monarch, in whose dominion a Brahmana becomes a thief, is considered to be the doer of that misdeed. The king is visited by sins on that account.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: अभिशस्तमिवात्मानं मन्यन्ते येन कर्मणा। तस्माद् राजर्षयः सर्वे ब्राह्मणानन्वपालयन्॥
en: For such an offence, kings consider themselves to be worthy of reproach. All righteous kings, therefore, provide Brahmanas with the means of sustenance,

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। गीतं कैकेयराजेन ह्रियमाणेन रक्षसा॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old narrative of the speech made by the king of the Kaikeyas to a Rakshasa while the latter was about to abduct him away.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: केकयानामधिपतिं रक्षो जग्राह दारुणम्। स्वाध्यायेनान्वितं राजन्नरण्ये संशितव्रतम्॥
en: Of rigid vows and well-read in the Vedas, the king of the Kaikeyas, O monarch, while living in the forest, was by force seized on a certain occasion by a Rakshasa.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: राजोवाच न मे स्तेनो जनपदे न कदर्यो न मद्यपः। नानाहिताग्नि यज्वा मामकान्तरमायिशः॥
en: The king said, There is no thief in my kingdom, nor any wicked person nor any one who drinks alcohol. There is no one in my kingdomn who does not preserve his sacred fire or who does not celebrate sacrifices. How then have you been able to possess by heart?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: न च मे ब्राह्मणोऽविद्वान्नाव्रती नाप्यसोमपः। नानाहिताग्नित यज्वा मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: There is not Brahmana in my territories who is not learned or who does not observe Vows or who has not drunk Soma. There is no one who does not preserve his sacred fire or who does not celebrate sacrifices. How then have you been able to possess my soul?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: नानाप्रदक्षिणैर्यज्ञैर्यजन्ते विषये मम। नाधीते नाव्रती कश्चिन्मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: In my kingdom no sacrifice has been celebrated without completing it by Dakshina. No one in my kingdom studies the Vedas who does not observe vows. How then have you been able to possess my soul?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: अधीयतेऽध्यापयन्ति यजन्ते याजयन्ति च। ददति प्रतिगृह्णन्ति षट्सु कर्मस्ववस्थिताः॥
en: The Brahmanas in my kingdom teach, study, sacrifice, officiate at others' sacrifices, give, and receive presents. All of them perform those six acts.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: पूजिताः संविभक्ताश्च मृदवः सत्यवादिनः। ब्राह्मणा मे स्वकर्मस्था मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: The Brahmanas in my kingdom devotedly follow the duties of their order. Adored and provided for, they are mild, and truthful in speech. How then have you been to possess my soul?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: न याचन्ते प्रयच्छन्ति सत्यधर्मविशारदाः। नाध्यापयन्त्यधीयते यजन्ते याजयन्ति न॥ ब्राह्मणान् परिरक्षन्ति संग्रामेष्वपलायिनः। क्षत्रिया मे स्वकर्मस्था मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: The Kshatriyas in my kingdom devotedly follow the duties of their order. They never beg but give, and are conversant with truth and virtue. They never teach but study, and celebrate sacrifices but never officiate at the sacrifices of others. They protect the Brahmanas and never fly from battlefield. How then have you been able to possess my soul,?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: कृषिगोरक्षवाणिज्यमुपजीवन्त्यमायया। अप्रमत्ताः क्रियावन्तः सुव्रताः सत्यवादिनः॥
en: The Vaishyas in my kingdom all follow the duties of their order. With simplicity and without deceit they gain their livelihood from agriculture, cattle-keeping, and trade. They are all careful, observant of religious rites and excellent vows, and truthful in speech.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: संविभागं दमं शौचं सौहदं च व्यपाश्रिताः। मम वैश्याः स्वकर्मस्था मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: They give to their guests what is their due, are self-controlled and pure, and devoted to their relatives and kinsmen. How then have you been to possess my heart?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: त्रीन् वर्णानुपजीवन्ति यथावदनसूयकाः। मम शूद्राः स्वकर्मस्था मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: The Shudras in my kingdom, always follow the duties of their order, humbly and duly serve and wait upon the other three orders without cherishing any inalice towards them. How then have you been able to possess my heart?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: कृपणानाथवृद्धानां दुर्बलातुरयोषिताम्। संविभक्तास्मि सर्वेषां मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: I support the helpless and the old, the weak, the ill, and helpless women by giving them all their necessaries. How then have you been able to possess my heart?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: कुलदेशादिधर्माणां प्रथितानां यथाविधि। अव्युच्छेत्तास्मि सर्वेषां मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: I have never done away with the special customs of families and of countries obtaining from days of yore. How then have you been able to possess my heart?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: तपस्विनो मे विषये पूजिता: परिपालिताः। संविभक्ताश्च सत्कृत्य मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: The ascetics in my kingdom are protected and adored. They are always honoured and fed with food. How then have you been able to posses my heart?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: नासं विभज्य भोक्तास्मि नाविशामि परस्त्रियम्। स्वतन्त्र जातु न क्रीडे मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: I never eat without feeding others from my food. I never know other people's wives. I never sport or recreate alone. How then have you been able to possess my heart?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: नाब्रह्मचारी भिक्षावाम्भिक्षुर्वाऽब्रह्मचर्यवान् अनृत्विजा हुतं नास्ति मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: No one in my kingdom save a Brahmacharin begs his food, and no one who lives a mendicant's life desires to be a Brahmacharin. No one but a Ritwij pours libations (of clarified butter) upon the sacrificial fire. How then have you been able to possess my soul?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: नावजानाम्यहं वैद्यान्न वृद्धान्न तपस्विनः। राष्ट्रे स्वपति जागर्मि मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: I never disrespect the learned or the old or those who practise penances. When all people are asleep, I keep up (for watching and protecting). How then have you been able to possess my heart?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: आत्मविज्ञानसम्पन्नस्तपस्वी सर्वधर्मवित्। स्वामी सर्वस्य राष्ट्रस्य धीमान् मम पुरोहितः॥
en: My priest is endued with the knowledge of self. He practises penances, and is a master of duties. Highly intelligent he has the fullest power over my kingdom.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: दानेन विद्यामभिवाञ्छयामि सत्येनार्थं ब्राह्मणानां च गुप्त्या। शुश्रूषया चापि गुरूनुपैमि न मे भयं विद्यते राक्षसेभ्यः॥
en: By presents I desire to acquire knowledge, and by truth and the protection of Brahmanas. I wish to attain blissful regions of heaven. I always strive to serve my preceptors with my services. I do not fear the Rakshasas.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: न मे राष्ट्रे विधवा ब्रह्मबर्दू ब्राह्मणः कितवो नोत चोरः। अयाज्ययाजी न च पापकर्मा न में भयं विद्यते राक्षसेभ्यः॥
en: In my kingdom there are no widows, no wicked Brahmanas, no Brahmana who had not satisfied his duties, no deceitful person, no thief, no Brahmana who officiates in the sacrifices of those for whom he should never officiate, and no perpetrator of sinful deeds. I do not fear the Rakshasas.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: न मे शस्त्रैरनिर्भिन्नं गात्रे व्यङ्गद्धलमन्तरम्। धर्मार्थं युध्यमानस्य मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: There is no space in my body, of even two fingers breadth, which does not contain the mark of a weapon-wound. I always fight for the sake of fairness. How then have you been able to possess my heart?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: गोब्राह्मणेभ्यो यज्ञेभ्यो नित्यं स्वस्त्ययनं मम। आशासते जना राष्ट्रे मामकान्तरमाविशः॥
en: The people of my kingdom always bless me so that I may always be able to protect kine and Brahmanas and celebrate sacrifices. How then have you been able to possess me?

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: राक्षस उवाच यस्मात् सर्वास्ववस्थासु धर्ममेवान्ववेक्षसे। तस्मात् प्राप्नुहि कैकेय गृहं स्वस्ति व्रजाम्यहम्॥
en: Since you satisfy your duties under all circumstances, therefore, O king of the Kaikeyas, go back to your palace. Blessed be you, I leave you.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: येषां गोब्राह्मणं रक्ष्यं प्रजा रक्ष्याश्च केकय। न रक्षोभ्यो भयं तेषां कुत एव तु पावकात्॥
en: They, O king of the Kaikeyas, who protect kine and Brahmanas and all their subjects, have no fear of Rakshasas, what speak of sinful persons.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: येषां पुरोगमा विप्रा येषां ब्रह्म परं बलम्। अतिथिप्रियास्तथा पौरास्ते वै स्वर्गजितो नृपाः॥
en: Those kings, who yield to Brahmanas and whose might depends upon that of the Brahmanas, and whose subjects are always hospitable, always succeed in gaining heaven.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: भीष्म उवाच तस्माद् द्विजातीन् रक्षेत ते हि रक्षन्ति रक्षिताः। आशीरेषां भवेद् राजन् राज्ञां सम्यक्प्रवर्तताम्॥
en: Bhishma continued:-You should; therefore, protect the Brahmanas. Protected by you, they will protect you in return. Their blessings, O king, would, forsooth, come upon righteous kings.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: तस्माद् राज्ञा विशेषेण विकर्मस्था द्विजातयः। नियम्याः संविभज्याश्च तदनुग्रहकारणात्॥
en: For the sake of righteousness, those Brahmanas who do not follow the duties of their order should be chastised and separated from their betters.

description: The wealth of which the king is master
sn: एवं यो वर्तते राजा पौरजानपदेष्विह। अनुभूयेह भद्राणि प्राप्नोतीन्द्रसलोकताम्॥
en: A king, who behaves thus towards the people of his city and the provinces, enjoys prosperity here and lives in heaven with Indra.'

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच व्याख्याता राजधर्मेण वृत्तिरापत्सु भारत। कथं स्विद् वैश्यधर्मेण संजीवेद् ब्राह्मणो न वा॥
en: Yudhishthira said "It is said that in seasons of distress a Brahmana may support himself by following Kshatriya duties. But can be, however, at any time, maintain himself by following the duties of the Vaishyas?”

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: भीष्म उवाच अशक्तः क्षत्रधर्मेण वैश्यधर्मेण वर्तयेत्। कृषिगोरक्ष्यमास्थाय व्यसने वृत्तिसंक्षये॥
en: "When a Brahmana loses his means of livelihood and is visited by distress, he may certainly act like a Vaishya and derive his support by agriculture and tending cattle, if, of course, he is not capable to perform Kshatriya duties.'

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कानि पण्यानि विक्रीय स्वर्गलोकान्न हीयते। ब्राह्मणो वैश्यधर्मेण वर्तयन् भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Yudhishthira said "If a Brahmana, O foremost of Bharata's race, follows the duties of a Vaishya, what articles may he sell without losing his chance of attaining heaven?"

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: भीष्म उवाच सुरा लवणमित्येव तिलान् केसरिणः पशून्। वृषभान् मधुमांसं च कृतान्नं च युधिष्ठिर॥ सर्वास्ववस्थास्वेतानि ब्राह्मणः परिवर्जयेत्। एतेषां विक्रयात् तात ब्राह्मणो नरकं व्रजेत्॥
en: Bhishma said 'A Brahmana must not sell wines, salt, sesamum seeds, animals having manes, bulls, honey, meat and cooked food, O Yudhishthira, under any circumstances. A Brahmana, by selling these, would go to hell.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: अजोऽग्निर्वरुणो मेषः सूर्योऽश्वः पृथिवी विराट्। धेनुर्यज्ञश्च सोमश्च न विक्रेयाः कथंचन॥
en: A Brahmana, by selling a goat, commits the sin of selling the god of fire; by selling a sheep, the sin of selling the god of water; by selling a horse, the sin of selling the sun-god; by selling cooked food, the sin of selling land; and by selling a cow, the sin of selling Sacrifices and the Soma juice. A Brahmana, therefore, must not sell these.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: पक्वेनामस्य निमयं न प्रशंसन्ति साधवः। निमयेत् पक्वमामेन भोजनार्थाय भारत॥
en: The good do not speak highly of the purchase of uncooked food by giving cooked food in return. Uncooked food, however, may be given for procuring cooked food, O Bharata!

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: वयं सिद्धमशिष्यामो भवान् साधयतामिदम्। एवं संवीक्ष्य नियमेन्नाधर्मोऽस्ति कथंचन॥
en: We will eat this cooked food of you. You may cook these raw things (that we give in return). In such an agreement there is no sin.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि यथा धर्मः सनातनः। व्यवहारप्रवृत्तानां तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Listen, O Yudhishthira, I shall describe to you the eternal practice, obtaining from days of yore, of persons conducting themselves according to approved usages.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: भवतेऽहं ददानीदं भवानेतत् प्रयच्छतु। रुचितो वर्तते धर्मो न बलात् सम्प्रवर्तते॥
en: I give you this. Give me this other thing in exchange. Such an exchange is righteous. To take things by force, is sinful.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: इत्येवं सम्प्रवर्तन्ते व्यवहाराः पुरातनाः। ऋषीणामितरेषां च साधु चैतदसंशयम्॥
en: Such is the old practice followed by the Rishis and others. Forsooth, this is righteous.' Yudhishthira said

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अथ तात यदा सर्वाः शस्त्रमाददते प्रजाः। व्युत्नामन्ति स्वधर्मेभ्यः क्षत्रस्य क्षीयते बलम्॥ राजा त्राता तु लोकस्य कथं च स्यात् परायणम्। एतन्मे संशयं ब्रूहि विस्तरेण नराधिप॥
en: “When, O sire, giving up their respective duties, all the castes take up arms against the king, then, of course, the power of the king suffers decrease. How would the king then become the protector and refuge of the people? Remove this doubt of mine, O king, by speaking to me fully." Bhishma said

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: भीष्म उवाच दानेन तपसा यज्ञैरद्रोहेण दमेन च। ब्राह्मणप्रमुखा वर्णाः क्षेममिच्छेयुरात्मनः॥
en: “By gifts, by penances, by sacrifices, by peacefulness, and by self-control, all the castes led by the Brahmanas should, on such occasions, seek their own behoof.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: तेषां ये वेदबलिनस्तेऽभ्युत्थाय समन्ततः। राज्ञो बलं वर्धयेयुर्महेन्द्रस्येव देवताः॥
en: Those amongst them who are gifted with Vedic strength, should rise up on all sides and like the celestial empowering Indra contribute (by Vedic rites) to increase the strength of the king.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: राज्ञोऽपि क्षीयमाणस्य ब्रह्मैवाहुः परायणम्। तस्माद् ब्रह्मबलेनैव समुत्थेयं विजानता॥
en: Brahmanas are said to be the refuge of the king while his power is gone. A wise king seeks the increase of his power by means of the power of the Brahmanas.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: यदा भुवि जयो राजा क्षेमं राष्ट्रेऽभिसंदधेत्। तदा वर्णा यथाधर्मं निविशेयुः कथंचन॥
en: When the king, after acquiring victory, tries to re-establish peace, all the castes then follow their respective duties.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: उन्मर्यादे प्रवृत्ते तु दस्युभिः संकरे कृते। सर्वे वर्णा न दुष्येयुः शस्त्रवन्तो युधिष्ठिर।॥
en: When robbers overcoming all restraints, lay waste the country, all the orders may take up arms. By doing so, they commit no sin, O Yudhishthira!'

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अथ चेत् सर्वतः क्षत्रं प्रदुष्येद् ब्राह्मणं प्रति। कस्तस्य ब्राह्मणस्त्राता को धर्मः किं परायणम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said “If all the Kshatriyas stand against the Brahmanas, who then will protect the Brahmanas and their Vedas? What then should be the duty of the Brahmanas and who will be their shelter?"

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: भीष्म उवाच तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण शस्त्रेण च बलेन च। अमायया मायया च नियन्तव्यं तदा भवेत्॥
en: Bhishma said By penances, by Brahmacharya, by weapons, and by (physical) power, applied with or without the help of deceit, the Kshatriyas should be vanquished.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: क्षत्रियस्यातिवृत्तस्य ब्राह्मणेषु विशेषतः। ब्रह्मैव संनियन्तृ स्यात् क्षत्रं हि ब्रह्मसम्भवम्॥
en: If the Kshatriya misbehaves himself, especially towards Brahmanas, the Vedas themselves will put them down. The Kshatriyas have originated from the Brahmanas.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: अद्भ्योऽग्निर्ब्रह्मतः क्षत्रमश्मनो लोहमुत्थितम्। तेषां सर्वत्रगं तेः स्वासु योनिषु शाम्यति॥
en: Fire has originated water; the Kshatriya, from the Brahmana; and iron, from stone. The power of fire, the Kshatriya, and iron, are irresistible. But when these conflict with their sources, their force becomes neutralised.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: यदा छिनत्त्ययोऽश्मानग्निश्चापोऽभिगच्छति। क्षत्रं च ब्राह्मणं द्वेशि तदा नश्यन्ति ते त्रयः॥
en: When iron strikes against stone, or fire fights with water, or the Kshatriya stands against the Brahmana, then the strength of each of those three is destroyed.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: तस्माद् ब्रह्मणि शाम्यन्ति क्षत्रियाणां युधिष्ठिर। समुदीर्णान्यजेयानि तेजांसि च बलानि च॥ ब्रह्मवीर्ये मृदुभूते क्षत्रवीर्ये च दुर्बले। दुष्टेषु सर्ववर्णेषु ब्राह्मणान् प्रति सर्वशः॥ ये तत्र युद्ध कुर्वन्ति त्यक्त्वा जीवितमात्मनः। ब्राह्मणान् परिरक्षन्तो धर्मामात्मानमेव च॥ मनस्विनो मन्युमन्तः पुण्य श्लोका भवन्ति ते। ब्राह्मणार्थं हि सर्वेषां शस्त्रग्रहणमिष्यते॥
en: Thus, O Yudhishthira, the energy and might of Kshatriya, however great and irresistible be, are destroyed as soon as they are directed against the Brahmanas. When the power of the Brahmanas becomes mild, when that of the Kshatriyas is weakened, when all men ill-treat the Brahmanas, those strong-minded persons, who moved by righteous indignation, then fight, casting off all fear of death, for protecting the Brahmanas. morality, and their own selves,-succeed in winning high regions of bliss hereafter. All persons should fight for the sake of Brahmanas.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: अतिस्विष्टमधीतानां लोकानतितपस्विनाम्। अनाशनाग्न्योर्विशतां शूरा यान्ति परां गतिम्॥
en: Those brave, persons who fight for Brahmanas, acquire those happy regions in heaven which are reserved for persons who have always studied the Vedas with attention, who have practised the austerest of penances, and that have, after fasting, cast off their bodies into burning fires.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: ब्राह्मणस्त्रिषु वर्णेषु शस्त्रं गृह्णन दुष्यति। एवमेवात्मनस्त्यागन्नान्यं धर्मं विदुर्जनाः॥
en: The Brahmana, by fighting for the three other castes, does not commit sin. People say that there is no higher duty then renouncing life under such circumstances.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: तेभ्यो नमश्च भद्रं च ये शरीराणि जुह्वते। ब्रह्मद्विषो नियच्छन्तस्तेषां नोऽस्तु सलोकता। ब्रह्मलोकजितः स्वर्यान् वीरांस्तान् मनुरब्रवीत्।॥
en: I bow to them and blessed be they who thus renounce their lives while trying to punish the enemies of Brahmanas. Let us attain to that region which is reserved for them. Manu himself has said that those heroes go to the region of Brahman.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: यथाश्वमेधावभृथे स्नाताः पूता भवन्त्युत। दुष्कृतस्य प्रणाशेन ततः शस्त्रहता रणे॥
en: As persons become freed off of all their sins by taking the final bath in a horse-sacrifice, so those who die by weapons while fighting wicked people are freed off of all their sins.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: भवत्यधर्मो धर्मो हि धर्माधर्मावुभावपि। कारणाद् देशकालस्य देशकालः स तादृशः॥
en: Righteousness becomes unrighteousness, and unrighteousness becomes righteousness, according to place and time, Such is the power of place and time.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: मैत्राः क्रूराणि कुर्वन्तो जयन्ति स्वर्गमुत्तमम्। धाः पापानि कुर्वाणा गच्छन्ति परमां गतिम्॥
en: The friends of humanity, by performing even acts of cruelty, have attained to exalted heaven. Pious Kshatriyas, by doing even sinful acts, to blessed ends.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: ब्राह्मणस्त्रिषु कालेषु शस्त्रं गृह्णन्न दुष्यति। आत्मत्राणे वर्णदोषे दुर्दम्यनियमेषु च॥
en: The Brahmana, by fighting on these three occasions, does not commit sin, viz., for protecting himself, for compelling the other castes to follow their duties, and for punishing robbers,

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अभ्युस्थिते दस्युबले क्षत्रार्थे वर्णसंकरे। सम्प्रमूढेषु वर्णेषु यद्यन्योऽभिभवेद् बली॥ ब्राह्मणो यदि वा वैश्यः शूद्रो वा राजसत्तम। दस्युभ्योऽथ प्रजा रक्षेद् दण्डं धर्मेण धारयन्॥ कार्यं कुर्यान्न वा कुर्यात् संवार्यो वा भवेन्न वा। तस्माच्छस्त्रं ग्रहीतव्यमन्यत्र क्षत्रबन्धुतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said If when robbers become powerful and an intermixture of the orders beings to take place on account of anarchy, and Kshatriyas become incapable, some powerful person except a Kshatriya seeks to put down those robbers for protecting the people, indeed, O best of kings, if that powerful person happens to be a Brahmana or a Vaishya or a Shudra, and if he succeeds in protecting the people by fairly holding the rod of punishment, is he justified in doing what he does, or is he restrained by the ordinances from accomplishing that duty? It seems that others, when the Kshatriyas are so incompetent, should take up arms.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: भीष्म उवाच अपारे यो भवेत् पारमप्लवे यः प्लवो भवेत्। शूद्रो वा यदि वाप्यन्यः सर्वथा मानमर्हति॥
en: Bhishma said Be he a Shudra or be he the member of any other caste, he that becomes a raft on a raftless current, or a means of crossing where no means exist, forsooth, deserves every respect.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: यमाश्रित्य नरा राजन् वर्तयेयुर्थथासुखम्। अनाथास्तप्यमानाश्च दस्युभिः परिपीडिताः॥ तमेव पूजयेयुस्ते प्रीत्या स्वमिव बान्धवम्। अभीरभीक्ष्णं कौरव्य कर्ता सन्मानमर्हति॥
en: That person, O king, depending upon whom helpless men, oppressed and made miserable by robbers, live happily, deserves to be adored by all as if he were a near relative. The person, O you of Kuru's race, that removes the fears of others, is worthy of every respect.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: किं तैर्येऽनडुहो नोह्याः किं धेन्वा वाप्यदुग्धया। वन्ध्यया भार्यया कोऽर्थः कोऽर्थो राज्ञाप्यरक्षता॥
en: What use is there of bulls, that would not carry burdens, or of kine that would not give milk, or of a wife who is barren? Likewise, what need is there for a king who is not capable to grant protection?

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: यथा दारुमयो हस्ती यथा चर्ममयो मृगः। यथा ह्यनथः षण्ढो वा पार्थ क्षेत्रं यथोषरम्॥ एवं विप्रोऽनधीयानो राजा यश्च न रक्षिता। मेघो न वर्षते यश्च सर्वथा ते निरर्थकाः॥
en: As an elephant made of wood, or a deer made of leather, as a person without riches, or one that is a eunuch, or a field which is barren, even so is a Brahmana who is void of Vedic learning and a king incapable of giving protection. Both of them are like a cloud that does not pour rain.

description: Can a Brahmana follow the duties of Vaishya?
sn: नित्यं यस्तु सतो रक्षेदसतश्च निवर्तयेत्। स एव राजा कर्तव्यस्तेन सर्वमिदं धृतम्॥
en: That person who always protects the good and checks the wicked, deserves to become a king and to govern the world.'

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच क्व समुत्थाः कथंशीला ऋत्विजः स्युः पितामह। कथंविधाश्च राजेन्द्र तद् ब्रूहि वदतां वर॥
en: Yudhishthira said How O grandfather, should persons, employed as priests in our sacrifices, act? What sort of persons should they be, O king? Tell me all this, O foremost of orators.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: भीष्म उवाच प्रतिकर्म पराचार ऋत्विजां स्म विधीयते। छन्दः सामादि विज्ञाय द्विजानां श्रुतमेव च॥
en: Bhishma said It is laid down for those Brahmanas who are competent to officiate as priests that they should know the Chhandas including the Samans, and all the rites laid down in the Shrutis, and that they should be able to perform all such religious acts as secure the prosperity of the king.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: ये त्वेकरतयो नित्यं धीराश्च प्रियवादिनः। परस्परस्य सुहृदः समन्तात् समदर्शिनः॥
en: They should be devotedly loyal and utter sweet words in addressing kings. They should also be friendly towards one another, and regard all impartially.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: अनृशंसाः सत्यवाक्या अकुसीदा अथर्जवः। अद्रोहोऽनभिमानश्च हीस्तितिक्षा दमः शमः॥ यस्मिन्नेतानि दृश्यन्ते स पुरोहित उच्यते। धीमान् सत्यधृतिर्दान्तो भूतानामविहिंसकः। अकामद्वेषसंयुक्तस्त्रिभिः शुक्लैः समन्वितः॥ अहिंसको ज्ञानतृप्तः स ब्रह्मासनमर्हति। एते महत्विजस्तात सर्वे मान्या यथार्हतः॥
en: They should be shom of cruelty, and truthful. They should never lay out money on interest and should always be simple and sincere. One that is peaceful in temper, shorn of vanity, modest charitable, self-controlled, and contented, intelligent, truthful, observant of vows, and harmless to all creatures, without lust and malice, and endued with the three other excellent qualities, devoid of envy and blessed with knowledge, is worthy of the seat of Brahman himself. Persons possessing such qualities, O sire, are the best of priests and deserve every respect.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यदिदं वेदवचनं दक्षिणासु विधीयते। इदं देयमिदं देयं न क्व चिद् व्यवतिष्ठते॥
en: Yudhishthira said There are Vedic texts relating to the gift of Dakshina in sacrifices. There is no ordinance, however, which says that so much should be given.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: नेदं प्रतिधनं शास्त्रमापद्धर्मानुशास्त्रतः। आज्ञा शास्त्रस्य घोरेयं न शक्तिं समवेक्षते॥
en: This ordinance (about the gift of Dakshina) is not the outcome of motives connected with the distribution of wealth. The command of the ordinance, when one cannot give according to the prescription, is terrible. That commandment has altogether neglected the capacity of the sacrificer.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: श्रद्धावता च यष्टव्यमित्येषा वैदिकी श्रुतिः। मिथ्योपेतस्य यज्ञस्य किमु श्रद्धा करिष्यति॥
en: It occurs in the Vedas that a person should with devotion, celebrate a sacrifice. But what can devotion do when the sacrifice is sullied by false substitutes?

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: भीष्म उवाच न वेदानां परिभवान्न शान्येन न मायया। कश्चिन्महदवाप्नोति मा तेऽभूद् बुद्धिरीदृशी॥
en: Bhishma said No man gains blessedness or merit by disregarding the Vedas or by deceitor falsehood. Never think that it is otherwise.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: यज्ञाझं दक्षिणा तात वेदानां परिबृंहणम्। न यज्ञा दक्षिणाहीनास्तारयन्ति कथंचन॥
en: Dakshina is one of the limbs of sacrifice and conduces to the nourishment of the Vedas. A sacrifice without Dakshina can never bring on salvation.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: शक्तिस्तु पूर्णपात्रेण सम्मिता न समाभवत्। अवश्यं तात यष्टव्यं त्रिभिर्वर्णर्यथाविधि॥
en: The efficacy, however, of a single Purnapatra is tantamount to that of any Dakshina however rich. Therefore, O sire, every one belonging to the three castes should celebrate sacrifices.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: सोमो राजा ब्राह्मणानामित्येषा वैदिकी स्थितिः। तं च विक्रेतुमिच्छन्ति न वृथा वृत्तिरिष्यते॥
en: The Vedas have settled that Soma is the king of the Brahmanas. Yet they wish to sell it for the sake of celebrating sacrifices, though they never wish to sell it for acquiring a livelihood.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: तेन क्रीतेन यज्ञेन ततो यज्ञः प्रतायते। इत्येवं धर्मतो ध्यातमृषिभिर्धर्मचारिभिः॥
en: Pious Rishis have declared, according to the dictates of morality, that a sacrifice performed with the income of the sale of Soma serves to extend sacrifices.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: पुमान् यज्ञश्च सोमश्च न्यायवृत्तो यदा भवेत्। अन्यायवृत्तः पुरुषो न परस्य न चात्मनः॥
en: These three, viz., a person, a sacrifice, and Soma, must have good character. A person of a bad character neither enjoy this nor the other world.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: शरीरवृत्तमास्थाय इत्येषा श्रूयते श्रुतिः। नातिसम्यक् प्रणीतानि ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम्॥
en: We have heard this Shruti that the sacrifice which high-souled Brahmanas perform by wealth acquired by excessive physical labour, does not yield great merit.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: तपो यज्ञादपि श्रेष्ठमित्येषा परमा श्रुतिः। तत् ते वपः प्रवक्ष्यामि विद्वंस्तदपि मे शृणु॥
en: There is an injunction in the Vedas that penances are higher than sacrifices. I shall now describe penances to you. O learned prince listen to me.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: अहिंसा सत्यवचनमानृशंस्यं दमो घृणा एतत् तपो विदुर्धारा न शरीरस्य शोषणम्॥
en: Abstention from injury, truthfulness of speech, benevolence, are considered as penances by the wise and not the emaciation of the body.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: अप्रामाण्यं च वेदानां शास्त्राणां चाभिलङ्घनम्। अव्यवस्था च सर्वत्र तद् वै नाशनमात्मनः।१९।।
en: Disregard of the Vedas, disobedience to the scriptural injunctions and violation of all healthy restraints, bring on self-destruction.

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: निबोध देवहोतृणां विधानं पार्थ यादृशम्। चित्तिः स्त्रुक् चित्तमाज्यं च पवित्रं ज्ञानमुत्तमम्॥
en: Listen, O son of Pritha, to what has been laid down by those who pour ten libations upon mercy,-these the fire at ten times of the day.-For them who perform the sacrifice of penance, the Yoga they strive to bring about with Brahma is their ladle the heart is their clarified butter and high knowledge is their Pavitra (a couple of Kusha blades for pouring clarified butter).

description: The appointment of sacrificial priests and their duties.
sn: सर्वं जिह्यं मृत्युपदमार्जवं ब्रह्मणः पदम्। एतावाज्ञानविषयः किं प्रलापः करिष्यति॥
en: All sorts of crookedness mean death and all sorts of sincerity are called Brahma. This is the subject of knowledge. The verses of philosophers cannot affect this.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यदप्यल्पतरं कर्म तदप्येकेन दुष्करम्। पुरुषेणासहायेन किमु राज्ञा पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Even the most insignificant act, O grandfather, cannot be accomplished by any man without co-operation. What then need be said of the king (who has to govern a kingdom)?

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: किंशील: किंसमाचारो राज्ञोऽथ सचिवो भवेत्। कीदृशे विश्वसेद् राजा कीदृशे न च विश्वसेत्॥
en: How should the king's minister act and behave? Upon whom should the king place confidence, and upon whom he should not?

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: भीष्म उवाच चतुर्विधानि मित्राणि राज्ञां राजन् भवन्त्युत। सहार्थो भजमानश्च सहजः कृत्रिमस्तथा॥
en: Bhishma said Kings, O monarch, have four sorts of friends. They are-one who has the same object, one who is devoted, one who is related by birth, and one who has been won over (by gifts and kindness).

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: धर्मात्मा पञ्चमश्चापि मित्रं नैकस्य न द्वयोः यतो धर्मस्ततो वा स्याद् धर्मस्थो वा ततो भवेत्॥
en: A righteous person, who would serve one and not both sides, is the fifth of the king's friends. Such a person follow that side on which righteousness is, and accordingly acts righteously.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: यस्तस्यार्थो न रोचेत न तं तस्य प्रकाशयेत्। धर्माधर्मेण राजानश्चरन्ति विजिगीषवः॥
en: Regarding such a person, the king should never disclose such purpose of his as would not find his sympathy, Kings who wish to attain success are compelled to adopt both kinds of roads, fair and unfair.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: चतुर्णां मध्यमौ श्रेष्ठौ नित्यं शङ्कयौ तथापरौ। सर्वे नित्यं शङ्कितव्याः प्रत्यक्षं कार्यमात्मनः॥
en: Of the four kinds of friends, the second and the third are superior, while the first and the fourth should always be looked upon with suspicion. Regarding those acts, however, which the king should do personally, he should always look with suspicion on all the four.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: न हि राज्ञा प्रमादो वै कर्तव्यो मित्ररक्षणे। प्रमादिनं हि राजानं लोकाः परिभवन्त्युत॥
en: The king should never act carelessly in watching his friends. A king who is careless is always overpowered by others.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: असाधुः साधुतामेति साधुर्भवति दारुणः। अरिश्च मित्रं भवति मित्रं चापि प्रदुष्यति॥
en: A wicked man puts on the appearance of honesty, and he who is honest becomes otherwise. An enemy may become a friend, and a friend may become an enemy.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: अनित्यचित्तः पुरुषस्तस्मिन् को जातु विश्वसेत्। तस्मात्प्रधानं यत् कार्यं प्रत्यक्षं तत् समाचरेत्॥
en: A man cannot always be of the same mind. Who is there that would trust him implicitly? All the principal works, therefore, a king should perform in his own presence.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: एकान्तेन हि विश्वासः कृत्स्नो धर्मार्थनाशकः। अविश्वासश्च सर्वत्र मृत्युना च विशिष्यते॥
en: An absolute confidence (in his ministers) destroys both morality and profit. A want of confidence again in all worse is than death.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: अकालमृत्युर्विश्वासो विश्वसन् हि विपद्यते। यस्मिन् करोति विश्वासमिच्छतस्तस्य जीवति॥
en: Over-confidence is premature death. One incurs danger by over-confidence, If one trusts another completely, he is said to live by the favour of the trusted person.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: तस्माद् विश्वसितव्यं च शङ्कितव्यं च केषुचित्। एषा नीतिगतिस्तात लक्ष्या चैव सनातनी॥
en: Therefore every one should be trusted as also mistrusted. This rule of policy, O sire, should always be kept in view.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: यं मन्येत ममाभावादिममर्थागमं स्पृशेत्। नित्यं तस्माच्छङ्कितव्यममित्रं तद् विदुर्बुधाः॥
en: One should always mistrust that person who would upon one's death, obtain one's wealth. The wise men describe such a person to be one's enemy.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: यस्य क्षेत्रादप्युदकं क्षेत्रमन्यस्य गच्छति। न तत्रानिच्छतस्तस्य भिघेरन् सर्वसेतवः॥
en: From the field of any person the water enters into the other's field, the ridge should not be brocken without owner's wish.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: तथैवात्युदकाद् भीतस्तस्य भेदनमिच्छति। यमेवंलक्षणं विद्यात् तममित्रं विनिर्दिशेत्॥
en: Terrified with the fear of huge quantity of water that might fill up in the field, one who wants to break the ridge, he is said as enemy.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: यस्तु वृद्ध्या न तृप्येत क्षये दीनतरो भवेत्। एतदुत्तममित्रस्य निमित्तमिति चक्षते॥
en: A person whose joy knows no limit upon seeing the advancement of the king and who feels pain upon seeing the king's decay, is one of the best friends of the king.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: यन्मन्येत ममाभावादस्याभावो भवेदिति। तस्मिन् कुर्वीत विश्वासं यथा पितरि वै तथा॥ तं शक्त्या वर्धमानश्च सर्वतः परिबृंहयेत्। नित्यं क्षताद् वारयति यो धर्मेष्वपि कर्मसु॥ क्षताद् भीतं विजानीयादुत्तमं मित्रलक्षणम्। ये तस्य क्षतमिच्छन्ति ते तस्य रिपवः स्मृताः॥
en: He who would meet with ruin by your fall, should be trusted by you completely even as you should trust your father. You should, to the best of your power, advance him as you secure advancement for yourself.
