One who, in even your religious rites, tries to save you from harm, would try to save you from harm in every other transaction. Such a one should be known as your best friend. They, on the other hand, who wish one harm are one's enemies.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: व्यसनान्नित्यभीतो यः समृद्ध्या यो न दुष्यति। यत् स्यादेवंविधं मित्रं तदात्मसममुच्यते॥
en: That friend is like your own self who is filled with fear when calamity befalls you and with joy when prosperity smiles on you.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: रूपवर्णस्वरोपेतस्तितिक्षुरनसूयकः। कुलीन: शीलसम्पन्नः स ते स्यात् प्रत्यनन्तरः॥
en: A person endued with beauty, fair complexion, sweet voice, liberality, highmindedness, and good birth, cannot be such a friend.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: मेधावी स्मृतिमान् दक्षः प्रकृत्या चानृशंस्यवान्। यो मानितोऽमानितो वा न च दुष्येत् कदाचन॥ ऋत्विग्वा यदि वाऽऽचार्यः सखा वात्यन्तसंस्तुतः। गृहे वसेदमात्यस्ते स स्यात् परमपूजितः॥
en: That person who is endued with intelligence and memory, who is smart in transacting business, who is by nature shorn of cruelty, who is never wrathful, and who whether honoured or neglected is never dissatisfied, be he your priest or preceptor or trusted friend, should always receive your adoration if he accepts the office of your counsellor and lives in your palace.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: स ते विद्यात् परं मन्त्रं प्रकृतिं चार्थधर्मयोः। विश्वासस्ते भवेत् तत्र यथा पितरि वै तथा॥
en: You may communicate to such a person your most secret counsels and the true state of never all your affairs, spiritual or temporal. You may trust him as you may your own father.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: नैव द्वौ न त्रयः कार्या न मृष्येरन् परस्परम्। एकार्थे ह्येव भूतानां भेदो भवति सर्वदा॥
en: One person should be appointed to one work, and not two or three. These may not tolerate each other. It is always seen that several persons, if engaged in one and the same work, disagree with one another.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: कीर्तिप्रधानो यस्तु स्याद् यश्च स्यात् समये स्थितः। समर्थान् यश्च न वश् िनानर्थान् कुरुते च यः॥ यो न कामाद् भयाल्लोभात् क्रोधाद् वा धर्ममुत्सृजेत्। दक्षः पर्याप्तवचनः स ते स्यात् प्रत्यनन्तरः॥
en: That person who acquires fame, who observes all restraints, who is never jealous of able and competent persons, who never does any evil act, who renounces righteousness from lust or fear or covetousness or wrath, who is smart in transaction business, and who always speaks wise and weighty words, should be your foremost of ministers.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: कुलीनः शीलसम्पन्नस्तितिक्षुरविकत्थनः। शूरश्चार्यश्च विद्वांश्च प्रतिपत्तिविशारदः॥ एते ह्यमात्याः कर्तव्याः सर्वकर्मस्ववस्थिताः। पूजिताः संविभक्ताश्च सुसहायाः स्वनुष्ठिताः॥
en: Well-behaved persons and born in good families, who are liberal and never given to brag, who are brave and respectable, and learned and full of resources, should be appointed as ministers for supervising all your affairs. Respected by you and gratified with riches, they would act for your well-being and be of great help to you.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: कृत्स्नमेते विनिक्षिप्ताः प्रतिरूपेषु कर्मसु। युक्ता महत्सु कार्येषु श्रेयांस्युत्थापयन्त्युत॥
en: Appointed of offices of emolument and of other important matters, they will always secure great prosperity.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: एते कर्माणि कुर्वन्ति रूपर्धमाना मिथः सदा। अनुतिष्ठन्ति चैवार्थमाचक्षाणाः परस्परम्॥
en: Actuated by a feeling of healthy rivalry, they satisfy all duties regarding profit, consulting with one another when necessary.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: ज्ञातिभ्यश्चैव बुद्ध्येथा मृत्योरिव भयं सदा। उपराजेव राजर्धि ज्ञातिर्न सहते सदा॥
en: You should fear your kinsmen as you should death itself. A kinsman can never bear a kinsmen's prosperity even as a feudatory chief cannot bear to see the prosperity of his lord.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: ऋजोर्मदोर्वदान्यस्य ह्रीमतः सत्यवादिनः। नान्यो ज्ञातेर्महाबाहो विनाशमभिनन्दति॥
en: None but a kinsman feels joy at the destruction of a kinsman endued with sincerity, mildness, liberality, modesty and truthfulness.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: अज्ञातिनोऽपि न सुखा नावज्ञेयास्ततः परम्। अज्ञातिमन्तं पुरुषं परे चाभिभवन्त्युत॥
en: They, again, who have no kinsmen, can not be happy. No man is more contemptible than he who has no kinsman. A person who has no kinsman is easily overthrown by enemies.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: निकृतस्य नरैरन्यैर्शातिरेव परायणम्। नान्यैनिकारं सहते ज्ञातिव्रते: कथञ्चन॥
en: Kinsmen are the refuge of one who is attacked by others, for kinsmen can never bear to see a kinsman assailed by other people.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: आत्मानमेव जानाति निकृतं बान्धवैरपि। तेषु सन्ति गुणाश्चैव नैर्गुण्यं चैव लक्ष्यते॥ नाज्ञातिरनुगृह्णाति न चाज्ञातिर्नमस्यति। उभयं ज्ञातिवर्गेषु दृश्यते साध्वसाधु च॥
en: When a kinsman is persecuted by even his friends, every kinsman of his considers the injury to be inflicted upon himself. In kinsmen, therefore, there both merits and shortcomings. A person having no kinsmen never shows favours to any one nor humbles himself to any one. In kinsmen, therefore, both mcrit and demerit are seen.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: सम्मानयेत् पूजयेच्च वाचा नित्यं च कर्मणा। कुर्याच्च प्रियमेतेभ्यो नाप्रियं किञ्चिदाचरेत्॥
en: One should, for this reason, always honour and adore his kinsmen in words and deeds, and are do what pleases them without injuring them at any time.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: विश्वस्तवदविश्वस्तस्तेषु वर्तेत सर्वदा। न हि दोषा गुणो वेति निरूप्यस्तेषु दृश्यते॥
en: Though one may mistrust them at heart, he should behave towards them as if he trusted them completely. Thinking of their nature, it seems that they have neither demerits nor merits.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: अस्यैवं वर्तमानस्य पुरुषस्याप्रमादिनः। अमित्राः संप्रसीदन्ति तथा मित्रीभवन्त्यपि॥
en: A person who carefully conducts himself in this way finds his every enemies shorn of hostility and converted into friends.

description: The necessity of co-operation for king
sn: य एवं वर्तते नित्यं ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिमण्डले। मित्रेष्वमित्रे मध्यस्थे चिरं यशसि तिष्ठति॥
en: One who always conducts himself in this way with his kinsmen and relatives and treats thus his friends and enemies, succeeds in acquiring everlasting fame.'

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवमग्राह्यके तस्मिज्ञातिसम्बन्धिमण्डले। मित्रेष्वमित्रेष्वपि च कथं भावो विभाव्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said If one cannot thus win over one's kinsmen and relatives, the intending friends become foes. How should one, then, behave so that the hearts of both friends and enemies may be won?

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। संवादं वासुदेवस्य सुरर्षेर्नारदस्य च॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old history of a discourse between Vasudeva and the divine saint Narada.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: वासुदेव उवाच नासुहृत् परमं मन्त्रं नारदार्हति वेदितुम्। अपण्डितो वापि सुहृत् पण्डितो वाप्यनात्मवान्॥
en: Once on a time Vasudeva said-Neither an illiterate and foolish friend, nor a learned friend of fickle mind, deserves, O Narada, to know one's secret counsels.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: स ते सौहृदमास्थाय किञ्चिद् वक्ष्यामि नारद। कृत्स्नं बुद्धिबलं प्रेक्ष्य सम्पृच्छेस्त्रिदिवंगम॥
en: Relying on your friendship for me, I shall say something to you, O sage! O you who can go to heaven at your pleasure, one should speak to another if he is convinced of the intelligence of that other.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: दास्यमैश्वर्यवादेन ज्ञातीनां न करोम्यहम्। अर्धं भोक्तास्मि वाग्दुरुक्तानि च क्षमे॥
en: I never behave with slavish tendency towards my kinsmen by flattering speeches about their prosperity, I give them half of what I have, and forgive their evil words.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: अरणीमग्निकामो वा मनाति हृदयं मम। वाचा दुरुक्तं देवर्षे तन्मे दहति नित्यदा॥
en: As a fire-stick is grinded by a person who seeks to get fire, so my heart is grinded by my kinsmen with their cruel words. Indeed, O celestial Rishi, those cruel words consume my heart every day.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: बलं संकर्षणे नित्यं सौकुमार्य पुनर्गदे। रूपेण मत्तः प्रद्युम्नः सोऽसहायोऽस्मि नारद॥
en: Power lives in Sankarshana; mildness in Gada; and as regards Pradyumna, he excels even myself in beauty. Still I am helpless, O Narada!

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: अन्ये हि सुमहाभागा बलवन्तो दुरुत्सहाः। नित्योत्थानेन सम्पन्ना नारदान्धकवृष्णयः॥
en: Many others among the Andhakas and the Vrishnis are endued with great prosperity, might, daring courage and constant perseverance.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: यस्य न स्युर्न वै स स्याद् यस्य स्युः कृत्स्नमेव तत्। द्वाभ्यां निवारितो नित्यं वृणोम्येकतरं न च॥
en: He, with whom they do not side, meets with destruction. He, on the other hand, with whom they side, acquires everything. Dissuaded by both Ahuka and Akrura, I do not side either of them.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: स्यातां यस्याहुकाक्रूरौ किं नु दुःखतरं ततः। यस्य चापि न तौ स्यातां किं नु दुःखतरं ततः॥
en: What can be more distressing for a person than to have both Ahuka and Akrura on his side? What, again, is more painful for one than not to have both of them on his side?

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: सोऽहं कितवमातेव द्वयोरपि महामते। एकस्य जयमाशंसे द्वितीयस्यापराजयम्॥
en: I am like the mother of two brothers gambling against each other, praying for victory to both.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: ममैवं क्लिश्यमानस्य नारदोभयतः सदा। वक्तुमर्हसि यच्छ्रेयो ज्ञातीनामात्मनस्तथा॥
en: I am thus, O Narada, afflicted by both. You should tell me that which is for the behoof of both myself and my kinsmen.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: नारद उवाच आपदो द्विविधाः कृष्ण बाह्याश्चाभ्यन्तराश्च ह। प्रादुर्भवन्ति वार्ष्णेय स्वकृता यदि वान्यतः॥
en: Narada said Calamities, O Krishna, are of two sorts, viz., external and internal. They are begotten, O you of Vrishni's race, by one's own acts or by the acts of others.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: सेयमाभ्यन्तरा तुभ्यमापत् कृच्छा स्वकर्मजा। अक्रूरभोजप्रभवा सर्वे ह्येते त्वदन्वयाः॥
en: The calamity that has now overtaken you is an internal one and is begotten of your own acts. Valadeva and others, of the Bhoja race, are partisans of Akrura, and have sided him either for wealth, or for mere caprice, or actuated by words or by hatred. As for you, you have given away wealth obtained by you to another.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: अर्थहेतोहि कामाद् वा वाचा बीभत्सयापि वा। आत्मना प्राप्तमैश्वर्यमन्यत्र प्रतिपादितम्॥ कृतमूलमिदानीं तज्ज्ञातिवृन्दं सहायवन्। न शक्यं पुनरादातुं वान्तमनमिव त्वया॥
en: Though having many friends, you have, however, by your own act, invited calamity over your head. You cannot take back that wealth, even as one cannot swallow again the food that he has vomited himself.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: बभूग्रसेनयो राज्यं नाप्तुं शक्यं कथंचन। ज्ञातिभेदभयात् कृष्ण त्वया चापि विशेषतः॥
en: The kingdom cannot be taken back from Babhru and Ugrasena. You, O Krishna, cannot, in particular, take it back from fear of creating intestine feuds.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: तच्च सिध्येत् प्रयत्लेन कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। महाक्षयं व्ययो वा स्याद् विनाशो वा पुनर्भवेत्॥
en: Supposing the attempt succeeds, it will do so after move trouble and after the achievement of the most difficult works. A great slaughter and a great loss of wealth will take place, perhaps, even total destruction.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: अनायसेन शस्त्रेण मृदुना हृदयच्छिदा। जिह्वामुद्धर सर्वेषां परिमृज्यानुमृज्य च॥
en: Use then a weapon which is not made of steel, which is very mild and yet capable of piercing all hearts. Sharpening that weapon again and again rectify the tongues of your kinsmen!

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: वासुदेव उवाच अनायसं मुने शस्त्रं मृदु विद्यामहं कथम्। येनैषामुद्धरे जिह्वां परिमृज्यानुमृज्य च।॥
en: Vasudeva said What is that weapon, O sage, which is not made of steel, which is mild, which still cuts all hearts, and which I must use for correcting the tongues of my kinsmen?

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: नारद उवाच शक्त्यान्नदानं सततं तितिक्षार्जवमार्दवम्। यथार्हप्रतिपूजा च शस्त्रमेतदनायसम्॥
en: Narada said The giving of food to the best of your ability, forgiveness, sincerity, mildness, and honour to whom honour is due,-these make a weapon which is not made of steel.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: ज्ञातीनां वक्तुकामानां कटुकानि लघूनि च। गिरा त्वं हृदयं वाचं शमयस्व मनांसि च॥
en: With soft words alone turn away the anger of kinsmen about to utter cruel words, and please their hearts and minds and slanderous words.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: नामहापुरुषः कश्चिन्नानात्मा नासहायवान्। महतीं धुरमाधत्ते तामुद्यम्योरसा वह॥
en: None who is not a great man with purified soul and endued with accomplishments and having friends can bear a heavy burden. Take up this great weight and bear it on your shoulders.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: सर्व एव गुरुं भारमनड्वान वहते समे। दुर्गे प्रतीतः सुगवो भारं वहति दुर्वहम्॥
en: All oxen can carry heavy loads on a level road. The stronger ones only among them can carry such loads on a difficult road.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: भेदाद् विनाशः संघानां संघमुख्योऽसि केशव। यथा त्वां प्राप्य नोत्सीदेदयं संघस्तथा कुरु॥
en: Disunion will create destruction which will befall all the Bhojas and the Vrishnis! You, O Keshava, are the foremost of them. Do you act in such a way that the Bhojas and the Vrishnis may not meet with destruction.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: नान्यत्र बुद्धिक्षान्तिभ्यां नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात्। नान्यत्र धनसंत्यागाद् गणः प्राज्ञेऽवतिष्ठते॥
en: Nothing but intelligence and forgiveness, control of the senses, and liberality, reside in a person of wisdom.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं स्वपक्षोद्भावनं सदा। ज्ञातीनामविनाशः स्याद् यथा कृष्ण तथा कुरु॥
en: The advancement of one's own race is always praiseworthy and glorious and conducive to long life. Do you, O Krishna, act in such a way that destruction may not overtake your kinsmen.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: आयत्यां च तदात्वे च न तेऽस्त्यविदितं प्रभो। पाड्गुण्यस्य विधानेन यात्रायानविधौ तथा॥
en: Use of the six qualities and riding on car (at the time of war), there is nothing about policy and art of war, O lord, which you do not know?

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: यादवाः कुकुरा भोजाः सर्वे चान्धकवृष्णयः। त्वय्यासक्ता महाबाहो लोका लोकेश्वराश्च ये॥ उपासते हि त्वबुद्धिमृषयश्चापि माधव।
en: The Yadavas, the Kukuras, the Bhojas, the Andhakas, and the Vrishni, all depend on you even as all the worlds and all the regents of their quarters, O mighty-armed one! The Rishis, O Madhava always pray for your advancement.

description: The means for acquiring the hearts of both friends and foes. The discourse between Vasudeva and Narada on this subject
sn: त्वं गुरुः सर्वभूतानां जानीषे त्वं गतागतम्। त्वामासाद्य यदुश्रेष्ठमेधन्ते यादवाः सुखम्॥
en: You are the lord of all creatures. You know the past, the present, and the future. You are the foremost of all the Yadavas. Depending on you, they expect to live happily.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एषा प्रथमतो वृत्तिद्वितीयां शृणु भारत। यः कश्चिज्जनयेदर्थं राज्ञा रक्ष्यः सदा नरः॥
en: Bhishma said This that I have told you is the first means. Listen now, O Bharata, to the second one. That man who seeks the advancement of the king should always be protected by him.

sn: ह्रियमाणममात्येन भृत्यो वा यदि वा भृतः। यो राजकोशं नश्यन्तमाचक्षीत युधिष्ठिर॥ श्रोतव्यमस्य च रहो रक्ष्यश्चामात्यतो भवेत्। अमात्या ह्यपहर्तारो भूयिष्ठं मन्ति भारत॥
en: If a person O Yudhishthira, who is paid or not, comes to you for informing you of the damage done to your treasury when its contents are being embezzled by a minister, you should grant him an audience in private and protect him also from the minister. The minister guilty of embezzlement seek, O Bharata, to kill such informants.

sn: राजकोशस्य गोप्तारं राजकोशविलोपकाः। समेत्य सर्वे बाधन्ते स विनश्यत्यरक्षितः॥
en: They who plunder the royal treasury combine together for opposing the person who tries to protect it, and if the latter be left unprotected, he is sure to be destroyed.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। मुनिः कालकवृक्षीयः कौसल्यं यदुवाच ह॥
en: Regarding it an old story also is cited of what the sage Kalakavrikshiya har said to the king of Koshala.

sn: कोसलानामाधिपत्यं सम्प्राप्तं क्षेमदशि मुनिः कालकवृक्षीय आजगामेति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that once on a time the sage Kalakavrikshiya came to Kshemadarshin, who had ascended the throne of Koshala.

sn: स काकं पञ्जरे बद्ध्वा विषयं क्षेमदर्शिनः। सर्वं पर्यचरद् युक्तः प्रवृत्त्यर्थी पुनः पुनः॥
en: Desirous of examining the conduct of all the officers of Kshemadarshin, the sage, with a crow kept with in cage in his hand, travelled again and again through every part of that king's dominions.

sn: अधीध्वं वायसी विद्यां शंसन्ति मम वायसाः। अनागतमतीतं च यच्च सम्प्रति वर्तते॥
en: men And he spoke to all the and said,-Study ye the practice of crows! The crows tell me the present, the past, and the future!

sn: इति राष्ट्रे परिपतन् बहुभिः पुरुषैः सह। सर्वेषां राजयुक्तानां दुष्करं परिदृष्टवान्॥
en: Proclaiming this in the kingdom, the sage, accompanied by a large number of men, began to mark the misdeeds of all the state officers.

sn: स बुद्ध्वा तस्य राष्ट्रस्य व्यवसायं हि सर्वशः। राजयुक्तापहारांश्च सर्वान् बुद्ध्वा ततस्ततः॥ ततः स काकमादाय राजानं द्रष्टुमागमत्। सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीति वचनं ब्रुवाणः संशितव्रतः॥ स स्म कौसल्यमागम्य राजामात्यमलंकृतम्। प्राह काकस्य वचनादमुत्रेदं त्वया कृतम्॥ असौ चासौ च जानीते राजकोशस्त्वया हतः। एवमाख्याति काकोऽयं तच्छीघ्रमनुगम्यताम्॥
en: Having ascertained all the affairs of the state, and having learnt that all the officers, appointed by the king were guilty of misdeeds, the sage, with his crow, came to see the king. Of rigid vows, he said to the king,-I know everything. Coming to the king, he said to his minister holding the insignia of his office that he had been informed by his crow that the minister had done such a crime in such a place, and that such and such persons know that he had robbed the royal treasury! My crow tells me this. Admit or prove the falsehood of the charge speedily.

sn: तथान्यानपि स प्राह राजकोशहरांस्तदा। न चास्य वचनं किंचिदनृतं श्रूयते क्वचित्॥
en: The sage then mentioned the names of other officers who had likewise been guilty of embezzlement, adding,-My crow never says anything false!

sn: तेन विप्रकृताः सर्वे राजयुक्ताः कुरूद्वह। तमस्यभिप्रसुप्तस्य निशि काकमवेधयन्॥
en: Thus accused and injured by the sage, all the officers of the king, O you of Kuru's race, in a body pierced his crow, while the sage slept at night.

sn: वायसं तु विनिर्भिन्नं दृष्ट्वा बाणेन पञ्जरे। पूर्वाह्ने ब्राह्मणो वाक्यं क्षेमदर्शिनमब्रवीत्॥ राजंस्त्वामभयं याचे प्रभुं प्राणधनेश्वरम्। अनुज्ञातस्त्वया ब्रूयां वचनं भवतो हितम्॥
en: Seeing his crow pierced with a shaft within the cage, the twice-born Rishi going to Kshemadarshin in the morning said to hiin,-O king, I seek your help. You are all powerful and you are the lord of the lives and riches of all! If you permit me I can then say what is for your well-bring. Sorry for you whom I regard as a friend, I have come to you, impelled by my devotion and ready to serve you with my whole heart.

sn: मित्रार्थमभिसंतप्तो भक्त्या सर्वात्मनाऽऽगतः। अयं तवार्थो ह्रियते यो ब्रूयादक्षमान्वितः॥
en: You are being robbed of your wealth, I have come to you for disclosing it without showing any mercy for the robbers. Like a driver that urges a good horse, I have come here for awakening you whom I consider a friend.

sn: सम्बुबोधयिषुर्मित्रं सदश्वमिव सारथिः। अतिमन्युप्रसक्तो हि प्रसह्य हितकारणात्॥
en: A friend who knows his own interests and seeks his own prosperity and advancement, should forgive a friend that intruded himself forcibly, actuated by devotion at anger, for doing what is beneficial.

sn: तथाविधस्य सुहृदा क्षन्तव्यं स्वं विजानता। ऐश्वर्यमिच्छता नित्यं पुरुषेण बुभूषता॥
en: The king replied to him, saying,—Why should I not hear anything which you will say, since I am not blind to what is for my good?

sn: तं राजा प्रत्युवाचेदं यत् किंचिन्मां भवान् वदेत्। कस्मादहं न क्षमेयमाकाङ्क्षन्नात्मनो हितम्॥
en: I grant you permission, O twice-born one! Tell me what you like. I shall certainly obey your instructions, O Brahmana!

sn: ब्राह्मण प्रतिजाने ते प्रब्रूहि यदिहेच्छसि। करिष्यामि हि ते वाक्यं यदस्मान्विप्र वक्ष्यसि॥
en: The Sage said, Ascertaining the merits and demerits of your servants, as also the dangers which you may meet with at their hands, I have come to you, actuated by my devotion, for informing you of everything.

sn: प्रागेवोक्तस्तु दोषोऽयमाचार्यैर्नृपसेविनाम्। अगतीकगतिझैषा पापा राजोपसेविनाम्॥
en: The ancient preceptors have declared what the curses are, O king, of those that serve others. The lot of those that serve the king is very miserable and wretched.

sn: आशीविषैश्च तस्याहुः संगतं यस्य राजभिः। बहुमित्राश्च राजानो बह्वमित्रास्तथैव च॥
en: He who has any connection with kings is said to have connection with snakes of deadly venom. Kings have many friends as also many enemies.

sn: तेभ्यः सर्वेभ्य एवाहुर्भयं राजोपजीविनाम्। तथैषां राजतो राजन् मुहूर्तादेव भीर्भवेत्॥
en: Those who serve kings have to fear all of them. Every moment, again, they entertain fear from the king himself, O monarch.

sn: नैकान्तेन प्रमादो हि शक्यः कर्तुं महीपतौ। न तु प्रमादः कर्तव्यः कथंचिद् भूतिमिच्छता॥
en: A person serving the king cannot escape the charge of carelessness in doing the king's work. Indeed, a servant who desires to acquire prosperity should never show carelessness in the discharge of his duties.

sn: मुनिरुवाच ज्ञात्वा पापानपापांश्च भृत्यतस्ते भयानि च। भक्त्या वृत्तिं समाख्यातुं भवतोऽन्तिकमागमम्॥
en: His carelessness may create the king's anger, and such anger may bring about his destruction. Carefully learning how to behave himself, one should sit before the king as he should in the presence of a burning fire.

sn: आशीविषमिव क्रुद्धं प्रभुं प्राणधनेश्वरम्। यत्नेनोपचरेन्नित्यं नाहमस्मीति मानवः॥
en: Prepared to give up his life itself at every moment, one should serve the king attentively, for the king is all powerful and lord of the lives and the riches of all, and, therefore, like to a snake of deadly venom.

sn: प्रमादाद्धि स्खलेद् राजा स्वलिते नास्ति जीवितम्। अग्नि दीप्तमिवासीदेद् राजानमुपशिक्षितः॥
en: He should always fear to utter evil words before the king, or to sit cheerlessly or in disrespectful postures, or to walk disdainfully, or to show insolent gestures and disrespectful motions of the limbs.

sn: दुर्व्याहताच्छङ्कमानो दुष्कृताद् दुरधिष्ठितात्। दुरासिताद् दुव्रजितादिङ्गित्तादङ्गचेश्तिात्॥
en: If the king becomes pleased he can shower prosperity like a god. If he becomes angry he can consume to the very roots like a burning fire.

sn: देवतेव हि सर्वार्थान् कुर्याद् राजा प्रसादितः। वैश्वानर इव क्रुद्धः समूलमपि निर्दहेत्॥
en: This, O king, was said by Yama. Its truth is seen in the wordly affairs. I shall now do what would increase your prosperity.

sn: इति राजन् यमः प्राह वर्तते च तथैव तत्। अथ भूयांसमेवार्थं करिष्यामि पुनः पुनः॥
en: Friends like ourselves can give to friends like you the help of their intelligence in times of danger. This crow of mine, O king, has been killed for doing your business.

sn: ददात्यस्मद्विधोऽमात्यो बुद्धिसाहाय्यमापदि। वायसस्त्वेष मे राजन् ननु कार्याभिसंहितः॥ न च मेऽत्र भवान् गर्यो न च येषां भवान्
en: I cannot, however, blame you for this. You are not loved by those who have killed this bird. Ascertain who are your friends and who, your foes. Do everything yourself without handing over your intelligence to others.

sn: हिताहितांस्तु बुद्ध्येथा मा परोक्षमतिर्भवे: :॥ ये त्वादानपरा एव वसन्ति भवतो गृहे।
en: Your establishment consists of all miscreants. They do not seek the well-being of your subjects. I have incurred their hostility.

sn: अभूतिकामा भूतानां तादृशैर्मेऽभिसंहितम्॥ यो वा भवद्विनाशेन राज्यमिच्छत्यनन्तरम्।
en: Making a conspiration with those servants who can always approach you, they covet the kingdom after destroying you. Their plans, however, have not succeeded owing to unforeseen circumstances.

sn: आन्तरैरभिसंधाय राजन् सिद्ध्यति नान्यथा॥ तेषामहं भयाद् राजन् गमिष्याम्यन्यमाश्रमम्। तैर्हि मे संधितो बाणः काके निपतितः प्रभो॥
en: Through fear of those men, O king, I shall leave this kingdom for some other hermitage. I have no worldly desire, yet those deceitful persons have shot this arrow at my crow, and have, O lord, sent the bird to Yama's abode. I have seen this, O king, with eyes whose vision has been improved by ascetic penances.

sn: छाकामैरकामस्य गमितो यमसादनम्। दृष्टं ह्येतन्मया राजंस्तपोदीर्धेन चक्षुषा॥
en: With the help of this single crow I have crossed this kingdom of yours that is like a river consisting of alligators, shark, crocodiles and whales.

sn: बहुनक्रझषग्राहां तिमिङ्गिलगणैर्युताम्। काकेन बालिशेनेमां यामतार्षमहं नदीम्॥
en: Indeed, with the help of that bird, I have passed through your dominions like Himalayan valley, impenetrable and inaccessible for these trunks of (fallen) trees and scattered rocks and thorny shrubs and lions and tigers and other beasts of prey.

sn: स्थाण्वश्मकण्टकवर्ती सिंहव्याघ्रसमाकुलाम्। दुरासदां दुष्प्रसहां गुहां हैमवतीमिव॥
en: The learned hold that a region inaccessible for darkness can be passed through with the a help of a light, and an unfordable river can be crossed by means of a boat. No means, however, exist for penetrating through the labyrinth of royal affairs.

sn: अग्निना तामसं दुर्गं नौभिराप्यं च गम्यते। राजदुर्गावतरणे नोपायं पण्डिता तिदुः॥
en: Your kingdom is like an inaccessible forest covered with darkness. You cannot trust it. How then can I.

sn: गहनं भवतो राज्यमन्धकारं तमोऽन्वितम्। नेह विश्वसितुं शक्यं भवतापि कुतो मया॥
en: Good and evil are seen here in the same light. To live here is not, therefore, safe. Here a righteous person meets with death, while an unrighteous man incurs no danger.

sn: अतो नायं शुभो वासस्तुल्ये सदसती इह। बधो ह्येवात्र सुकृते दुष्कृते न च संशयः॥
en: For the sake of justice, a person of unrighteous deeds should be killed but never one who is righteous in his deeds. It is not proper, therefore, for one to live in this kingdom long. A sensible man should leave this country soon.

sn: न्यायतो दुष्कृते घात: सुकृते न कथंचन। नेह युक्तं स्थिरं स्थातुं जवेनैवाव्रजेद् बुधः॥ सीता नाम नदी राजन् प्लवो यस्यां निमज्जति। तथोपमामिमां मन्ये वागुरां सर्वघातिनीम्॥
en: There is a river, O king, of the name of Sita. Boats sink in it. This your kingdom is like that river. An all-destructive net appears to have been cast around it.

sn: मधुप्रपातो हि भवान् भोजनं विषसंयुतम्। असतामिव ते भावो वर्तते न सतामिव॥ आशीविषैः परिवृत: कूपस्त्वमसि पार्थिव। दुर्गतीर्था बृहत्कूला कारीरा वेत्रसंयुता॥
en: You are like the fall which awaits the collectors of honey, or like attractive food containing poison. Your nature now resembles that of dishonest men and not that of the good. You are like a pit, o king, abounding with snakes of deadly venom.

sn: नदी मधुरपानीया यथा राजंस्तथा भवान्। श्वगृध्रगोमायुयुतो राजहंससमो ह्यसि॥
en: You resemble, O king, a river full of sweet water but difficult of access, with steep banks overgrown with Kariras and thorny canes. You are like a swan in the midst of dogs, vultures, and jackals.

sn: यथाऽऽश्रित्य महावृक्षं कक्षः संवर्धते महान्। ततस्तं संवृणोत्येव तमतीत्य च वर्धते॥ तेनैयोगेन्धनेनैनं दावो दहति दारुणः। तथोपमा ह्यमात्यास्ते राजस्तान् परिशोधय॥
en: Parasites, supported by a huge tree, grow luxuriously, and at last covering the tree itself overshadow it entirely. A forest fire sets in, and catching those grasses first, consumes the tree with them. Thy ministers, O king, resemble those parasites of which I speak, Do you check and correct them.

sn: त्वया चैव कृता राजन् भवता परिपालिताः। भवन्तमभिसंधाय जिघांसन्ति भवत्प्रियम्॥ उषितं शङ्कमानेन प्रमादं परिरक्षता।
en: They have been nourished by you, But making conspiracy against you, they are destroying your prosperity.

sn: अन्तःसर्प इवागारे वीरपत्न्या इवालये॥ शीलं जिज्ञासमानेन राज्ञश्च सहजीविनः। कच्चिज्जितेन्द्रियो राजा कच्चिदस्यान्तरा जिताः॥
en: Concealing the faults of your servants, I am living in your palace in constant dread of danger, even like a person living in a room with a snake within it or like the lover of a hero's wife. My object is to ascertain the behaviour of the king who lives with me.

sn: कच्चिदेषां प्रियो राजा कच्चिद् राज्ञः प्रियाः प्रजाः। विजिज्ञासुरिह प्राप्तस्तवाहं राजसत्तम॥
en: I wish to ascertain whether the king has his passions under restraint, whether his servants obey him, whether he is loved by them, and whether he loves his subjects. For the object of ascertaining all these points, O best of kings, I have come to you.

sn: तस्य मे रोचते राजन् क्षुधितस्येव भोजनम्। अमात्या मे न रोचन्ते वितृष्णस्य यथोदकम्॥
en: Like food to a hungry person, you have become dear to me. dislike your ministers, however, as a person, whose thirst has been satisfied, dislikes drink.

sn: भवतोऽर्थकृदित्येवं मयि दोषो हि तैः कृतः। विद्यते कारणं नान्यदिति मे नात्र संशयः॥
en: They have found fault with me, because I seek your well-being. I have no doubt that there is no other cause for their hostility to me.

sn: न हि तेषामहं दुग्धस्तत्तेषां दोषदर्शनम्। अरेर्हि दुहृदाद् भेयं भग्नपुच्छादिवोरगात्॥
en: I do not cherish any hostility towards them. I am engaged in only ascertaining their faults. As one should fear a wounded snake, cvery one should fear a wicked foe.

sn: राजोवाच भूयसा परिहारेण सत्कारेण च भूयसा। पूजितो ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठ भूयो वस गृहे मम॥
en: The king said Reside in my abode, O Brahmana. I shall always treat you with respect and honour, and always adore you.

sn: ये त्वां ब्राह्मण नेच्छन्ति ते न वत्स्यन्ति मे गृहे। भवतैव हि तज्ज्ञेयं यत्तदेषामनन्तरम्॥
en: They that will dislike you shall not live with me. Do you then yourself award what should be their proper sentence.

sn: यथा स्यात् सुधृतो दण्डो यथा च सुकृतं कृतम्। तथा समीक्ष्य भगवश्रेयसे विनियुझव माम्॥
en: Do you see, O holy one, then that the rod of punishment is wielded properly and that everything is done well in my kingdom. Reflecting upon everything, do you guide me in such a way that I may acquire prosperity!

sn: अदर्शयनिमं दोषमेकैकं दुर्बलीकुरु। ततः कारणमाज्ञाय पुरुषं पुरुषं जहि॥
en: The sage said Closing your eyes first of all to this offence of theirs, do you weaken them one by one. Prove their faults then and punish them one after another.

sn: एकदोषा हि बहवो मृद्नीयुरपि कण्टकान्। मन्त्रभेदभयाद् राजस्तस्मादेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: When many person become guilty of the same offence, they can, by acting in concert, soften the very points of the thorns. Lest your ministers (being suspected, act against you and) disclose your secret counsels, I advise you to proceed cautiously.

sn: मुनिरुवाच वयं तु ब्राह्मणा नाम मृदुदण्डाः कृपालवः। स्वस्ति चेच्छाम भवतः परेषां च यथाऽऽत्मनः॥
en: As regards ourselves, we are Brahmanas, by nature merciful and reluctant to give pain to any one. We desire your, as well as of others, well-being, even as we wish the good of ourselves.

sn: राजन्नात्मानमाचक्षे सम्बन्धी भवतो ह्यहम्। मुनिः कालकवृक्षीय इत्येवमभिसंज्ञितः॥
en: I speak of myself, O king! I am your friend. I am known as the sage Kalakavrikshiya.

sn: पितुः सखा च भवतः सम्मतः सत्यसङ्गरः। सर्वकामान् परित्यज्य तपस्तप्तं तदा मया। स्नेहात् त्वां तु ब्रवीम्येतन्मा भूयो विभ्रमेदिति॥ व्यापन्ने भवतो राज्ये राजन् पितरि संस्थिते॥
en: Always follow truth. Your father knew me as his friend. When distress overtook this kingdom during the reign of your father, O king, I performed many penances (for driving it off). Leaving off every other business. Out of my affection for you I say this to you so that you may not again commit the fault.

sn: उभे दृष्ट्वा दुःखसुखे राज्यं प्राप्य यदृच्छया। राज्येनामात्यसंस्थेन कथं राजन् प्रमाद्यसि॥
en: You have obtained a kingdom without any hitch. Think of everything connected with its happiness and misery. You have ministers in your kingdom. But why, O king, should you be guilty of carelessness?

sn: ततो राजकुले नान्दी संजज्ञे भूयसा पुनः। पुरोहितकुले चैव सम्प्राप्ते ब्राह्मणर्षभे॥
en: After this, the king of Koshala took a minister from the Kshatriya order, and appointed that foremost of Brahmana (viz., the sage Kalakavrikshiya), as his priest.

sn: एकच्छत्रां महीं कृत्वा कौसल्याय यशस्विने। मुनिः कालकवृक्षीय ईजे क्रतुभिरुत्तमैः॥
en: After these changes had been made, the king of Koshala brought the whole Earth under subjection and acquired great fame. The sage Kalakavrikshiya adored the gods in many grand sacrifices performed for the king.

sn: हितं तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कौसल्योऽप्यजयन्महीम्। तथा च कृतवान् राजा यथोक्तं तेन भारत॥
en: Having listened to his wholesome advice, the king of Koshala conquered the whole Earth and acted in every way as the sage directed.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सभासदः सहायाश्च सुहृदश्च विशाम्पते। परिच्छदास्तथामात्याः कीदृशाः स्युः पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said What should be the gratification, O grandfather, of the law-makers, the ministers of war, the countries, the commanders, and the counsellors of a king!

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: भीष्म उवाच ह्रीनिषेवास्तथा दान्ताः सत्यार्जवसमन्विताः। शक्ताः कथयितुं सम्यक् ते तव स्युः सभासदः॥
en: Bhishma said Such persons as are endued with modesty, self-control, truth, sincerity, and courage to say the proper thing, should be your law-makers.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: अमात्यांश्चातिशूरांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्च परिश्रुतान्। सुसंतुष्टांश्च कौन्तेय महोत्साहांश्च कर्मसु॥ एतान् सहायाँल्लिप्सेथाः सर्वास्वापत्सु भारत।
en: They who are always devoted to you who are gifted with great courage, who are of the twice-bom caste, highly learned, well pleased with you, and persevering in acts, should, O son of Kunti, be sought by you for becoming your ministers of war at all seasons of distress, O Bharata!

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: कुलीनः पूजितो नित्यं न हि शक्तिं निगृहति॥ प्रसन्नमप्रसन्नं वा पीडितं हतमेव वा।
en: One who is born in a high family, who treated honourably by you, always tries his best of your behalf, and who will never forsake you in happiness or misery, illness or death, should be kept by you as a courtier.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: आवर्तयति भूयिष्ठं तदेव ह्यनुपालितम्॥ कुलीना देशजाः प्राज्ञा रूपवन्तो बहुश्रुताः।
en: Those who are of high descent, who. are born in your kingdom, who have wisdom, beauty, great learning, and dignity of conduct, and who are, besides, devoted to you, should be employed as officers of your army.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: प्रगल्भाश्चानुरक्ताश्च ते तव स्युः परिच्छदाः॥ दौष्कुलेयाश्च लुब्धाश्च नृशंसा निरपत्रपाः।
en: Persons of low birth, who are covetous, cruel and shameless, would seek you, O sire, as long as they are paid.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: ते त्वां तात निषेवेयुर्याबदाईकपाणयः॥ कुलीनाशीलसम्पन्नानिङ्गितज्ञाननिष्ठुरान्। देशकालविधानज्ञान् भर्तृकार्यहितैषिणः॥ नित्यमर्थेषु सर्वेषु राजा कुर्वीत मन्त्रिणः।
en: Those who are of good-birth and good behaviour, who can interpret all sings and gestures, who are shorn of cruelty, who know the requirements of place and time, who always seek the well-being of their master in all works, should be appointed as ministers by the king in all his affairs.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: अर्थमानार्घ्यसत्कारैर्भोगैरुच्चावचैः प्रियान्॥ यानर्थभाजो मनयेथास्ते ते स्युः सुखभागिनः।
en: Those who have been swon over with gifts of wealth, honour, respectful receptions, and means of giving happiness, and who on that account may be known by you as persons inclined to do you good in all your affairs, should always be made sharers of your happiness.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: अभिन्नवृत्ता विद्वांसः सद्वृत्ताश्चरितव्रताः। न त्वां नित्यार्थिनो जझुरक्षुद्राः सत्यवादिनः॥
en: They who are unchangeable in conduct, endued with learning and good behaviour, observant of excellent vows, large-hearted, and truthful in speech, will always attend to your affairs and will never forsake you.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: अनार्या ये न जानन्ति समयं मन्दचेतसः। तेभ्यः परिजुगुप्सेथा ये चापि समयच्युताः॥
en: They, on the other hand, who disrespectable, who do not follow healthy control, who are wicked, and who have fallen away from good practices, should always be compelled by you to observe all healthy restraints.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: नैकमिच्छेद् गणं हित्वा स्याच्चेदन्यतरग्रहः। यस्त्वेको बहुभिः श्रेयान् कामं तेन गणं त्यजेत्॥
en: When the question arises as to which of two sides should be adopted, you should not abandon the many for adopting the side of one. When, however, that one person excels the many by virtue of his possessing many accomplishments, then you should for that one, forsake the many.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: श्रेयसो लक्षणं चैतद् विक्रमो यस्य दृश्यते। कीर्तिप्रधानो यश्च स्यात् समये यश्च तिष्ठति॥
en: The marks of superiority, are prowess, devotion to works that bring fame, and observance of healthy restraints. are

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: ते समर्थान् पूजयेद् यश्च नास्पर्धेः स्पर्धते च यः। न च कामाद् भयात् क्रोधाल्लोभाद् वा धर्ममुत्सृजेत्।। अमानी सत्यवान् क्षान्तो जितात्मा मानसंयुतः। स मन्त्रसहायः स्यात् सर्वावस्थापरीक्षितः॥
en: He, again, who honours all able persons that never cherishes feelings of rivalry with meritorious persons, who never forsakes righteousness from lust or fear or anger or covetousness, who is humble, who is truthful and forgiving, who has his mind under control, who has a sense of dignity, and who has been tried in every situation, should be appointed by you as your counsellor.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: कुलीनः कुलसम्पन्नस्तितिक्षुर्दक्ष आत्मवान्। शूरः कृतज्ञः सत्यश्च श्रेयसः पार्थ लक्षणम्॥
en: High birth, purity of blood, forgiveness, cleverness, and purify of mind, bravery gratefulness, and truthfulness are, O son of Pritha, characteristic of superiority and goodness.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: तस्यैवं वर्तमानस्य पुरुषस्य विजानतः। अमित्राः सम्प्रसीदन्ति तथा मित्रीभवन्त्यपि॥
en: A wiseman who conduct himself thus, succeeds in freeing his very enemies of their hostility and converting them into friends.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: अत ऊर्ध्वममात्यानां परीक्षेत गुणागुणम्। संयतात्मा कृतप्रज्ञो भूतिकामश्च भूमिपः॥
en: A king who has his mind under control, who is endued with wisdom, and who seeks prosperity, should carefully examine the merits and demerits of his ministers.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: सम्बन्धिपुरुषैराप्तैरभिजातैः स्वदेशजैः। अहायैरव्यभीचारैः सर्वशः सुपरीक्षितैः॥ यौनाः श्रौतास्तथा मौलास्तथैवाप्यनहंकृताः। कर्तव्या भूतिकामेन पुरुषेण बुभृषता॥
en: A king who seeks prosperity and wishes to outdo his contemporaries, should have for ministers trustworthy persons, of high descent, born in his own kingdom, incapable of being corrupted, unstained by adultery and similar vices, well proved, belonging to good families, possessed of learning, sprung from ancestors who held similar offices, and adorned with humility.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: येषां वैनयिकी बुद्धिः प्रकृतिश्चैव शोभना। तेजो धैर्य क्षमा शौचमनुरागः स्थिति तिः॥ परीक्ष्य च गुणान् नित्यं प्रौढभावान् धुरंधरान्। पञ्चोपधाव्यतीतांश्च कुर्याद् राजार्थकारिणः॥
en: The king should appoint five such persons to superintend his affairs, who are intelligent, shorn of pride, possessed of a good disposition, energy, patience, forgiveness, purity, loyalty, firmness, and courage, whose merits and faults have been well proved, who are aged, who are capable of bearing burden and who are free from deceit.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: पर्याप्तवचनान् वीरान् प्रतिपत्तिविशारदान्। कुलीनान् सत्त्वसम्पन्नानिङ्गित्तज्ञाननिष्ठुरान्॥ देशकालविधानज्ञान् भर्तृकार्यहितैषिणः। नित्यमर्थेषु सर्वेषु राजन् कुर्वीत मन्त्रिणः॥
en: Men who are wise in speech, who are endued which heroism, who are full of resources under difficulties, who are of high descent, who are truthful, who can read signs, who are shorn of cruelty, who know the requirements of place and time, and who seek the well-being of their masters, should be appointed by the king as his ministers in all affairs of the kingdom.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: हीनतेजोऽभिसंसृष्टो नैव जातु व्यवस्यति। अवश्यं जनयत्येव सर्वकर्मसु संशयम्॥
en: One who is shorn of energy and who has been forsaken by friends can never work with perseverance. Such a man if, appointed, fails in almost every work.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: एवमल्पश्रुतो मन्त्री कल्याणाभिजनोऽप्युत। धर्मार्थकामसंयुक्तो नालं मन्त्रं परीक्षितुम्॥
en: A minister possessing little learning, even if he be highly born and attentive to virtue, profit, and pleasure, cannot choose proper courses of action.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: तथैवानभिजातोऽपि काममस्तु बहुश्रुतः। अनायक इवाचक्षुर्मुह्यत्यणुषु कर्मसु॥
en: Likewise, a person of low birth, even if endued with great learning, always makes mistakes, like a blind man without a guide, in all acts requiring cleverness and foresight.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: यो वाप्यस्थिरसंकल्पो बुद्धिमानागतागमः। उपायज्ञोऽपि नालं स कर्म प्रापयितुं चिरम्॥
en: A person, again, who is of unsettled purposes, even if endued with intelligence and learning, and even if conversant with means, cannot long act with success.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: केवलात् पुनरादानात् कर्मणो नोपपद्यते। परामर्शो विशेषाणामश्रुतस्येह दुर्मतेः॥
en: A wicked man possessed of no learning may begin a work but he fails to determine what the results will be of his work.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: मन्त्रिण्यननुरक्ते तु विश्वासो नोपपद्यते। तस्मादननुरक्ताय नैव मन्त्रं प्रकाशयेत्॥
en: A king should never trust a minister who is not devoted to him. He should, therefore, never give out his counsels to a minister who is not devoted to him.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: व्यथयेद्धि स राजानं मन्त्रिभिः सहितोऽनृजुः। मारुतोपहितच्छिद्रैः प्रविश्याग्निरिव दुमम्॥
en: Such a wicked minister, in conjunction with the other minister of the king, may ruin his lord, like fire consuming a tree by entering into it through the holes in its body with the help of the wind.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: संक्रुद्धश्चैकदा स्वामी स्थानाच्चैवापकर्षति। वाचाक्षिपति संरब्धः पुनः पश्चात् प्रसीदति॥
en: Being angry, a master may, deprive a servant of his office or reprove him, from rage, in harsh words, and restore him to power again.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: तानि तान्यनुरक्तेन शक्यानि हि तितिक्षितुम्। मन्त्रिणां च भवेत् क्रोधो विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः॥
en: None save a servant devoted to the master stand and overlook such treatment. Ministers also become sometimes highly offended with their masters. can

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: यस्तु संसहते तानि भर्तुः प्रियचिकीर्षया। समानसुखदुःखं तं पृच्छेदर्थेषु मानवम्॥
en: That one, amongst them, who subdues his anger from desire of doing good to his master,-that person who partakes in the king's happiness and misfortune, should be consulted by the king in all his affairs.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: अनृजुस्त्वनुरक्तोऽपि सम्पन्नश्चेतरैर्गुणैः। राज्ञः प्रज्ञानयुक्तोऽपि न मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: An wily person, even if he be devoted to his master and possessed of wisdom and adorned with numerous accomplishments, should never be consulted by the king.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: योऽमित्रैः सह सम्बद्धो न पौरान् बहु मन्यते। असुहृत् तादृशो ज्ञेयो न मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: One who is allied with enemies and who does not care for the interests of the king's subjects, should be regarded as an enemy. The king should never consult him.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: अविद्वानशुचिः स्तब्धः शत्रुसेवी विकत्थनः। असुहृत् क्रोधनो लुब्धो न मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: One who is not learned, who is not pure, who is proud, who seeks the king's enemies, who is given to brag, who is unfriendly, wrathful, and covetous, should should not be consulted by the king.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: आगन्तुश्चानुरक्तोऽपि काममस्तु बहुश्रुतः। सत्कृतः संविभक्तो वा न मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: One who is a stranger, even if he be devoted to the king and possessed of great learning, may be honoured by the king and pleased with maintenance, but the king should never consult him in his affairs.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: विधर्मतो विप्रकृतः पिता यस्याभवत् पुरा। सत्कृतः स्थापितः सोऽपि न मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: A person whose father was unjustly exiled by royal order should not be consulted by the king, even if the king may have afterwards conferred honours upon him and given him the means of sustenance.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: यः स्वल्पेनापि कार्येण सुहृदाक्षारितो भवेत्। पुनरन्यैर्गुणैर्युक्तो न मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: A well-wisher whose property was once confiscated for a slight offences, even if he be endued with all accomplishments, should not still be consulted by the king.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: कृतप्रज्ञश्च मेधावी बुधो जानपदः शुचिः। सर्वकर्मसु यः शुद्धः स मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: A person endued with wisdom, intelligence, and learning, who is born within the kingdom, who is pure and righteous in all his works, should be consulted by the king.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: ज्ञानविज्ञानसम्पन्नः प्रकृतिज्ञः परात्मनोः। सुहृदात्मसमो राज्ञः स मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: One who is possessed of knowledge and wisdom, who knows the nature of friends and foes, who is a friend of the king like his second self, should be consulted.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: सत्यवाक् शीलसम्पन्नो गम्भीरः सत्रपो मृदुः। पितृपैतामहो यः स्यात् स मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: One who is truthful in speech and modest and mild, and who is a hereditary servant of the king, should be consulted.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: संतुष्टः सम्मतः सत्यः शौटीरो द्वेष्यपापकः। मन्त्रवित् कालविच्छूरः स मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: One who is contented and honoured, who is truthful and dignified, who hates wickedness and wicked men, who is conversant with policy and the requirements of time, and who is courageous, should be consulted by the king.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: सर्वलोकमिमं शक्तः सान्त्वेन कुरुते वशे। तस्मै मन्त्रः प्रयोक्तव्यो दण्डमाधित्सता नृप।॥
en: One who is capable to win over all men by conciliation should be consulted, O monarch, by the king, who wishes to rule according to the dictates of the science of punishment.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: पौरजानपदा यस्मिन् विश्वासं धर्मतो गताः। योद्धा नयविपश्चिच्च स मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हति॥
en: One whom the inhabitants of both the capital and the provinces truth for his righteous ! conduct, who is competent to right and conversant with the rules of policy, should be consulted by the king.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: तस्मात् सर्वैर्गुणैरेतैरुपपन्नाः सुपूजिताः। मन्त्रिणः प्रकृतिज्ञाः स्युस्त्र्यवरा महदीप्सवः॥
en: Therefore, men endued with such accomplishments, men conversant with the nature of all and desirous of achieving high acts, should be honoured by the king and made his ministers. Their number also should not be less than three.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: स्वासु प्रकृतिषुच्छिद्रं लक्षयेरन् परस्य च। मन्त्रिणां मन्त्रमूलं हि राज्ञो राष्ट्रं विवर्धते॥
en: Ministers should be employed in noticing the shortcomings of their masters, of themselves, of the subject, and of the foes of their masters. The kingdom depends upon the counsels of policy which the ministers give, and its growth originates from the same source.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: नास्य च्छिद्रं परः पश्येच्छिद्रेषु परमन्वियात्। गृहेत् कूर्म इवाङ्गानि रक्षेद् विवरमात्मनः॥ मन्त्रगूढा हि राज्यस्य मन्त्रिणो ये मनीषिणः। मन्त्रसंहननो राजा मन्त्राङ्गानीतरे जनाः॥
en: Ministers should act in such a way that the enemies of their master may not be able to detect his loopholes. On the other hand, when their shortcomings are seen, they should then be assailed. Like the tortoise protecting its limbs by withdrawing them within its shell, ministers should keep close their own counsels. They should, even thus, conceal their own short-comings. Those ministers of a kingdom, who succeed in keeping their counsels close, are said to be wise. Counsels are the armour of a king, and the limbs are his subjects and officers.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: राज्यं प्रणिधिमूलं हि मन्त्रसारं प्रचक्षते। स्वामिनं त्वनुवर्तन्ते वृत्त्यर्थमिह मन्त्रिणः॥
en: A kingdom depends upon spies and secret agents, and its strength lies in counsels of policy. If masters and ministers follow each other for getting support from each other, controlling pride and anger, and vanity and envy, they may then both become happy.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: संविनीय मदक्रोधौ मानमर्त्यां च निवृताः। नित्यं पञ्चोपधातीतैर्मन्त्रयेत् सह मन्त्रिभिः॥
en: A king should also consult such minister as are free from the five kinds of deceit.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: तेषां त्रयाणां विविधं विमर्श विबुद्ध्य चित्तं विनिवेश्य तत्र। स्वनिश्चयं तं परनिश्चयं च निवेदयेदुत्तरमन्त्रकाले।॥ धर्मार्थकामज्ञमुपेत्य पृच्छेद् युक्तो गुरुं ब्राह्मणमुत्तरार्थम्। निष्ठा कृता तेन यदा सहः स्यात् तं मन्त्रमार्ग प्रणयेदसक्तः॥
en: Ascertaining well, first of all, the different opinions of the three whom he has consulted, the king should, for subsequent settlement, go to his preceptor for informing him of those opinions and his own. His preceptor should be a Brahmana well read in all matters of virtue, profit and pleasure. Going, for such subsequent deliberation, to him, the king should, with a calm mind, ask his opinion. When a decision is got at after due deliberation with him, the king should then, without attachment, carry it out into practice.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: एवं सदा मन्त्रयितव्यमाई ये मन्त्रतत्त्वार्थविनिश्चयज्ञाः। तस्मात् तमेवं प्रणयेत् सदैव मन्त्रं प्रजासंग्रहणे समर्थम्॥
en: Those who know the science of consultation hold that kings should always hold consultation in this way. Having settled plans in this way, they should then carry them into execution, for then they will be able to win over all the subjects.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: न वामनाः कुब्जकृशा न खजा नान्धो जडः स्त्री च नपुंसकं च। न चात्र तिर्यक् च पुरों न पर्था नोर्ध्वं न चाधः प्रचरेत् कथंचित्।॥
en: There should be no dwarfs, no humpbacked persons, no lean man, no lame or blind man, no idiot, no woman, and no eunuch, at the spot where the king holds his consultations. Nothing should move there, before or behind, above or below, or in opposite directions.

description: The appointment of law-makers, ministers of wars, commanders, counsellors etc.
sn: आरुह्य वा वेश्म तथैव शून्य स्थलं प्रकाशं कुशकाशहीनम्। वागणदोषान्परिहत्य सर्वान् सम्मन्त्रयेत्कार्यमहीनकालम्॥
en: Getting up on a boat, or going to an open space shorn of grass and grassy bushes and whence the surrounding land may be distinctly seen, the king should hold consultations at the proper time, avoiding shortcomings of speech and gestures.'

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। बृहस्पतेश्च संवादं शक्रस्य च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said 'Regarding it, O Yudhishthira, the old account of a conversation between Brihaspati and Shakra is cited.

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: शक्र उवाच किं स्विदेकपदं ब्रह्मन् पुरुषः सम्यगाचरन्। प्रमाणं सर्वभूतानां यशश्चैवाप्नुयान्महत्॥
en: What is that one act, O twice-born one, by finishing which with care, a person may be respected by all creatures and become famous.

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच । सान्त्वमेकपदं शक्र पुरुषः सम्यगाचरन्। प्रमाणं सर्वभूतानां यशश्चैवाप्नुयान्महत्॥
en: Brihaspati said Sweetness of speech. O Shakra, is the one thing by practising which a person is esteemed by all and becomes famous.

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: एतदेकपदं शक्र सर्वलोकसुखावहम्। आचरन् सर्वभूतेषु प्रियो भवति सर्वदा॥
en: This is the one thing, O Shakra, which yields happiness to all. By practising it, one may always secure the love of all creatures.

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: यो हि नाभाषते किंचित् सर्वदा भृकुटीमुखः। द्वेष्यो भवति भूतानां स सान्त्वमिह नाचरन्॥
en: The person who does not speak a word and whose face is always marked with frowns is hated of all. Want of sweet speeches makes him so.

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: यस्तु सर्वमभिप्रेक्ष्य पूर्वमेवाभिभाषते। स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषी च तस्य लोकः प्रसीदति॥
en: That person who, on seeing others, speaks to them first with smiles, succeeds in winning over every one.

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: दानमेव हि सर्वत्र सान्त्वेनानभिजल्पितम्। न प्रीणयति भूतानि निर्व्यञ्जनमिवाशनम्॥
en: Even gifts, if not made with sweet speeches, do not please the recipients, like rice without curry.

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: आदानादपि भूतानां मधुरामीरयन् गिरम्। सर्वलोकमिमं शक्र सान्त्वेन कुरुते वशे॥
en: If even the wealth of men, O Shakra, be snatched away with sweet speeches, such sweetness of conduct can even propitiate the robbed.

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: तस्मात् सान्त्वं प्रयोक्तव्यं दण्डमाधिसतोऽपि हि। फलं च जनयत्येवं न चास्योद्विजते जनः॥
en: A king, therefore, who is desirous of even inflicting punishment, should use sweet words. Sweetness of speech never fails, while at the same time it never pains any heart.

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: सुकृतस्य हि सान्त्वस्य श्लक्ष्णस्य मधुरस्य च। सम्यगासेव्यमानस्य तुल्यं जातु न विद्यते॥
en: A person of good deeds and good, pleasant and sweet speeches, has no peer.

description: The one thing for which a man becomes famous.
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तः कृतवान् सर्व यथा शक्रः पुरोधसा। तथा त्वमपि कौन्तेय सम्यगेतत् समाचर॥
en: Bhishma continued Thus addressed by his priest, Shakra began to follow those instructions. Do you also, O son of Kunti, practise this virtue.'

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं स्विदिह राजेन्द्र पालयन् पार्थिवः प्रजाः। प्रीतिं धर्मविशेषेण कीर्तिमानोति शाश्वतीम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O foremost of kings, what is that method by which a king governing his subjects may, thereby, acquire great blessedness and eternal fame?

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: भीष्म उवाच व्यवहारेण शुद्धेन प्रजापालनतत्परः। प्राप्य धर्मं च कीर्तिं च लोकानाप्नोत्युभौ शुचिः॥
en: Bhishma said A king of pure soul and devoted to the duty of protecting his subjects acquires merit and fame, both here and hereafter, by acting righteously.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कीदृशैर्व्यवहारैस्तु कैश्च व्यवहरेन्नृपः। एतत्पृष्टो महाप्राज्ञ यथावद् वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said What should attitude of the king with regard to the treatment of others. Asked by me, O you of great wisdom, you should tell me everything duly!

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: ये चैव पूर्वं कथिता गुणास्ते पुरुषं प्रति। नैकस्मिन् पुरुषे ह्येते विद्यन्त इति मे मतिः॥
en: The virtues of men, which you have described, cannot be found to exist in any single individual. Bhishma said-

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमेतन्महाप्राज्ञ यथा वदसि बुद्धिमन्। दुर्लभः पुरुषः कश्चिदेभिर्युक्तो गुणैः शुभैः॥
en: You are highly intelligent, O Yudhishthira! It is what you say. The person is very rare who is endued with all those good qualities.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: किंतु संक्षेपत: शीलं प्रयत्नेनेह दुर्लभम्। वक्ष्यामि तु यथामात्यान् यादृशांश्च करिष्यसि॥
en: In short, such a one, [who is possessed of all those virtues) is very difficult to be seen even upon careful search. I shall, however, tell you what kinds of ministers should be appointed by you.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: चतुरो ब्राह्मणान् वैद्यान् प्रगल्भान् स्नातकाशुचीन्। क्षत्रियांश्च तथा चाष्टौ बलिनः शस्त्रपाणिनः॥ वैश्यान् वित्तेन सम्पन्नानेकविंशतिसंख्यया। त्रींश्च शूद्रान् विनीतांश्च शुचीन् कर्मणि पूर्वके॥ अष्टाभिश्च गुणैर्युक्तं सूतं पौराणिकं तथा। पञ्चाशद्वर्षवयसं प्रगल्भमनसूयकम्॥ श्रुतिस्मृतिसमायुक्तं विनीतं समदर्शिनम्। कार्ये विवदमानानां शक्तमर्थेष्वलोलुपम्॥ वर्जितं चैव व्यसनैः सुघोरैः सप्तभि शम्। अशनां मन्त्रिणां मध्ये मन्त्रं राजोपधारयेत्॥
en: Four Brahmanas, learned in the Vedas, endued with a sense of dignity, belonging to the Sanataka order, and of pure conduct, and eight Kshatriyas, all of whom should have physical strength and be capable of wielding weapons, and one and twenty Vaishyas, all of whom should be rich, and three Shudras, every one of whom should be humble and of pure conduct and devoted to his daily duties, and one man of the Suta caste, possessing of the knowledge of the Puranas and the eight principal virtues, should be your ministers. Every one of them should be fifty years old endued with sense of dignity, free from envy, masters of the Shrutis and the Smritis humble, impartial, capable of deciding then and there in the midst of disputants pointing out various courses of action, free from covetousness, and from the seven terrible vices called Vyasanas. The king should consult with those eight ministers and lead them.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: ततः सम्प्रेषयेद्राष्टे राष्ट्रीयाय च दर्शयेत्। अनेन व्यवहारेण द्रष्टव्यास्ते प्रजा: सदा॥
en: He should then announce in his kingdom, for the information of his subjects, the results of such consultations. You should always, following such a conduct, watch over your people.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: न चापि गूढं द्रव्यं ते ग्राह्यं कार्योपघातकम्। कार्ये खलु विपन्ने त्वां सोधर्मस्तांश्च पॆदयेत्॥ विद्रवेच्चैव राष्ट्रं ते श्येनात् पक्षिगणा इव। परिस्नवेच्च सततं नौर्विशीर्णेव सागरे॥
en: You should never confiscate what is deposited with you or appropriate the thing whose ownership is disputed by two persons. Such a conduct would spoil the administration of justice. If the administration of justice be thus spoiled will assail you, and afflict your kingdom as well and strike your people with fear as little birds on seeing the hawk. Your kingdom will then vanish like a boat wrecked on the sea.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: प्रजाः पालयतोऽसभ्यगधर्मेणेह भूपतेः। हार्द भयं सम्भवति स्वर्गश्चास्य विरुद्ध्यते॥
en: If a king governs his subjects unfairly, fear takes possession of his heart and the door of heaven is shut against him.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: अथयोऽधर्मतः पाति राजामात्योऽथ वाऽऽत्मजः। धर्मासने संनियुक्तो धर्ममूले नरर्षभ॥ कार्येष्वधिकृताः सम्यगकुर्वन्तो नृपानुगाः। आत्मानं पुरतः कृत्वा यान्त्यधः सहपार्थिवाः॥
en: A kingdom, O foremost of men, depends upon righteousness. That minister, or king's son, who acts unfairly, holding the seat of justice, and those officers who, having accepted responsible offices, act unjustly, actuated by self-interest, all sink in hell along with the king himself.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: बलात्कृतानां बलिभिः कृपणं बहु जल्पताम्। नाथो वै भूमिपो नित्यमनाथानां नृणां भवेत्॥
en: Helpless inen, who are oppressed by the strong and who consequently bewail piteously, have the king for their protector.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: ततः साक्षिबलं साधु द्वैधवादकृतं भवेत्। असाक्षिकमनाथं वा परीक्ष्यं तद् विशेषतः॥
en: In cases of dispute between two parties, the decision should depend upon the evidence of witness. If one of the parties has no witness and is helpless, the king should give the case his best consideration.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: अपराधानुरूपं च दण्डं पापेषु धारयेत्। वियोजयेद् धनैर्ऋदानधनानथ बन्धनैः॥
en: The king should punish the offenders according to their offences. The wealthy should be punished with fines and confiscations; the poor, with loss of liberty.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: विनयेच्चापि दुर्वृत्तान् प्रहारैरपि पार्थिवः। सान्त्वेनोपप्रदानेन शिष्टांश्च परिपालयेत्॥
en: The wicked should be punished by the king with corporal punishments. The king should maintain all good men with sweet speeches and presents of riches.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: राज्ञो वधं चिकीर्षेद् यस्तस्य चित्रो वधो भवेत्। आदीपकस्य स्तेनस्य वर्णसंकरिकस्य च॥
en: He who tries to bring about the death of the king should be punished with death to be effected by various means. One who becomes guilty of arson or theft or such co-habitation with women as may lead to an intermixture of castes, should be punished with death.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: सम्यक् प्रणयतो दण्डं भूमिपस्य विशाम्पते। युक्तस्य वा नास्त्यधर्मो धर्म एव हि शाश्वतः॥
en: A king, O monarch, who inflicts punishments duly and according to the dictates of the science of punishment, commits no sin by the act. On the other hand, he acquires eternal merit.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: कामकारेण दण्डं तु यः कुर्यादविचक्षणः। स इहाकीर्तिसंयुक्तो मृतो नरकमृच्छति॥
en: That foolish king who inflicts punishments whimsically, earns infamy here and sinks into hell hereafter.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: न परस्य प्रवादेन परेषां दण्डमर्पयेत्। आगमानुगमं कृत्वा बघ्नीयान्मोक्षयीत वा॥
en: One should not be punished for the fault of another. Bestowing sufficient thought upon the code, a person should be convicted or acquitted.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: न तु हन्यान्नृपो जातु दूतं कस्याञ्चिदापदि। दूतस्य हन्ता निरयमाविशेत् सचिवैः सह।॥
en: A king should never kill a messenger under any circumstances. That king who kills a messenger sinks into hell with all his ministers.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: यथोक्तवादिनं दूतं क्षत्रधर्मरतो नृपः। यो हन्यात् पितरस्तस्य भ्रूणहत्यामवाप्नुयुः॥
en: That king, mindful of Kshatriya practices, who kills a messenger faithfully speaking out his message, causes his departed manes to be stained with the sin of killing a foetus.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: कुलीन: शीलसम्पन्नो वाग्मी दक्षः प्रियंवदः। यथोक्तवादी स्मृतिमान् दूतः स्यात् सप्तभिर्गुणैः॥
en: A messenger should have these seven accomplishments, viz., he should be of high descent, of a good family, eloquent, clever, sweet-speeched, faithful in delivering the message with which he is sent, and possessed of good memory.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: एतैरेव गुणैर्युक्तः प्रतिहारोऽस्य रक्षिता। शिरोरक्षश्च भवति गुणैरेतैः समन्वितः॥
en: The aid-de-camp of the king, who guards his persons, should also possess similar qualities. The officer also that guards his capital or citadel should possess the same qualities.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: धर्मशास्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञः सांधिविग्रहिको भवेत्। मतिमान् धृतिमान् ह्रीमान् रहस्यविनिगूहिता॥
en: The king's minister should be well-read in the scriptures and capable in directing wars and making treaties. He should also be intelligent, courageous, modest, and capable of keeping secrets.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: कुलीनः सत्त्वसम्पन्नः शुक्लोऽमात्यः प्रशस्यते। एतैरेव गुणैर्युक्तस्तथा सेनापतिर्भवेत्॥
en: He should also be of high birth, have strength of mind, and be pure in conduct. If endued with these qualities, he should be regarded worthy. The commander of the king's forces should have also the same qualities.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: व्यूहयन्त्रायुधानां च तत्त्वज्ञो विक्रमान्वितः वर्षशीतोष्णवातानां सहिष्णुः पररन्ध्रवित्॥
en: He should also be master of the various sorts of battle array and with the uses of engines and weapons. He should be able to bear exposure to rain, cold, heat, and wind, and watchful of the shortcomings of foes.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: विश्वासयेत् परांश्चैव विश्वसेच्च न कस्यचित्। पुत्रेष्वपि हि राजेन्द्र विश्वासो न प्रशस्यते॥
en: The king, O monarch, should, be able to make his enemies sleep under a sense of security. He should not, however, himself trust any one. The reposing of confidence on even his own son is not good.

description: The deeds for which a king acquires eternal fame.
sn: एतच्छास्त्रार्थतत्त्वं तु मयाऽऽख्यातं तवानघ। अविश्वासो नरेन्द्राणां गुह्यं परममुच्यते॥
en: I have now, O sinless one, described to you what are the injunctions of the scriptures. Not to trust any one has been regarded one of the greatest mysteries of king-craft?

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथंविधं पुरं राजा स्वयमावस्तुमर्हति। कृतं वा कारयित्वा वा तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said What should be the kind of city within which the king should himself live? Should he select one already made, or should he cause one to be especially made? Tell me this, O grand-father!

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: भीष्म उवाच वस्तव्यं यत्र कौन्तेय सपुत्रज्ञातिबन्धुना। न्याय्यं तत्र परिप्रष्टुं वृत्तिं गुप्तिं च भारत॥
en: Bhishma said “It is proper, O Bharata, to enquire about how should a king live on a city, and how should he defend it, O son of Kunti.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: तस्मात् ते वर्तयिष्यामि दुर्गकर्म विशेषतः। श्रुत्वा तथा विधातव्यमनुष्ठेयं च यत्नतः॥
en: I shall, therefore, describe to you this subject, referring especially to the defences of forts. Having heard me, you should make the arrangements required and conduct yourself attentively as directed.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: षड्विधं दुर्गमास्थाय पुराण्यथ निवेशयेत्। सर्वसम्पत्प्रधानं यद् बाहुल्यं चापि सम्भवेत्॥
en: Keeping his eye on the six different sorts of forts the king should build his cities containing every kind of riches and every article of use in profusion.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: धन्वदुर्गं महीदुर्गं गिरिदुर्गं तथैव च। मनुष्यदुर्ग अब्दुर्गं वनदुर्गं च तानि षट्॥
en: Those six kinds are water-citadels, earthcitadels, hill-citadels, human-citadels, mud citadels, and forest-citadels.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: यत्पुरं दुर्गसम्पन्नं धान्यायुधसमन्वितम्। दृढप्राकारपरिखं हस्त्यश्वरथसंकुलम्॥ विद्वांसः शिल्पिनो यत्र निचयाश्च सुसंचिताः। धार्मिकश्च जनो यत्र दाक्ष्यमुत्तममास्थितः॥ ऊर्जस्विनरनागाश्वं चत्वरापणशोभितम्। प्रसिद्धव्यवहारं च प्रशान्तमकुतोभयम्॥ सुप्रभं सानुनादं च सुप्रशस्तनिवेशनम्। शूराढ्यजनसम्पन्नं ब्रह्मघोषानुनादितम्॥ समाजोत्सवसम्पन्नं सदा पूजितदैवतम्। वश्यामात्यबलो राजा तत्पुरं स्वयमाविशेत्॥
en: The king, with his ministers and the army perfectly loyal to him, should live in that city which is defended by a fort, which contains profuse rice and weapons, which is protected with impenetrable walls and a trench, which has a sufficient number of elephants, horses and cars, which is inhabited by learned men and well-versed in the mechanical arts, where storage of provisions of every sort has been made, whose inhabitants are virtuous and clear in business, strong-bodied and energetic and as also its animals, which has many open squares and rows of shops, where all persons are righteous, where peace reigns where no danger exists, which shines with beauty and resounds with music and songs, where the houses are all spacious, where the residents have among them many brave and rich persons, which echoes with the chanting of Vedic hymns, where festivities and rejoicings frequently take place, and where the deities are always adored.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: तत्र कोशं बलं मित्रं व्यवहारं च वर्धयेत्। पुरे जनपदे चैव सर्वदोषान् निवर्तयेत्॥
en: Living there, the king should always try to fill his treasury, to increase his army, multiply the number of his friends, and establish courts of justice. He should suppress all abuses and evils in both his cities and provinces.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: भाण्डागारायुधागारं प्रयत्नेनाभिवर्धयेत्। निचयान् वर्धयेत् सर्वांस्तथा यन्त्रायुधालयान्॥
en: He should collect provisions of all sorts and replenish his arsenals carefully. He should also increase his storage of rice and other grain, and strengthen his counsels.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: काष्ठलोहतुषाङ्गारदारू शृङ्गास्थिवैणवान्। मज्जा स्नेहवसा क्षौद्रमौषधग्राममेव च॥ शणं सर्जरसं धान्यमायुधानि शरांस्तथा। चर्म स्नायुं तथा वेत्रं मुञ्जबल्वजबन्धनान्॥
en: He should, increase his stores of fuel, iron, chaff, charcoal, timber, horns, bones, bamboos, marrow, oils, clarified butter, fat, honey, medicines, flax, resin, rice, weapons, arrows, leather, catgut, canes, and strings and cords made of Munja grass and other plants and creepers.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: आशयाचोदपानाश्च प्रभूतसलिलाकराः। निरोद्धव्याः सदा राज्ञा क्षीरिणश्च महीरुहाः॥
en: He should multiply the number of tanks and wells containing large quantities of water, and should protect all shady trees.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: सत्कृताश्च प्रयत्नेन आचार्यद्विकपुरोहिताः। महेष्वासाः स्थपतयः सांवत्सरचिकित्सकाः॥ प्राज्ञा मेधाविनो दान्ता दक्षाः शूरा बहुश्रुताः। कुलीनाः सत्त्वसम्पन्ना युक्ताः सर्वेषु कर्मसु॥
en: He should entertain with honour the teachers of various sciences, Ritwijas, priests, powerful bowmen, persons skilled in architecture, astronomers, astrologers, physicians, as well as all men endued with wisdom, intelligence, self-control, cleverness, courage, learning, high-descent and energy, and competent to do all work.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: पूजयेद् धार्मिकान् राजा निगृह्णीयादधार्मिकान्। नियुज्याच्च प्रयत्नेन सर्ववर्णान् स्वकर्मसु॥
en: The king should honour the righteous and punish the unrighteous. He should, acting with resolution, compell the several castes follow their respective duties,

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: बाह्ममाभ्यन्तरं चैव पौरजानपदं तथा। चारैः सुविदितं कृत्वा ततः कर्म प्रयोजयेत्॥
en: Knowing properly, through spies, the external conduct and the state of mind of the inhabitants of his city and provinces, he should take the necessary steps.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: चरान्मन्त्रं च कोशं च दण्डं चैव विशेषतः। अनुतिष्ठेत् स्वयं राजा सर्वं ह्यत्र प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: The king should himself look after his spies and counsels, his treasury, and the instrument for inflicting punishments. Everything depends upon these.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: उदासीनारिमित्राणां सर्वमेव चिकीर्षितम्। पुरे जनपदे चैव ज्ञातव्यं चारचक्षुषा॥
en: Having spies for his eyes, the king should learn all the acts and intentions of his foes, friends, and neutrals.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: ततस्तेषां विधातव्यं सर्वमेवाप्रमादतः। भक्तान् पूजयता नित्यं द्विषतश्च निगृह्णता॥
en: He should then, carefully, concert his own measures, honouring those that are loyal to him and chastising those that are hostile.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: यष्टव्यं क्रतुभिर्नित्यं दातव्यं चाप्यपीडया। प्रजानां रक्षणं कार्यं न कार्यं धर्मबाधकम्॥
en: The king should always worship the gods in sacrifices and make gifts without giving pain to anybody. He should protect his subjects, never doing anything that may stand in the way of righteousness.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: कृपणानाथवृद्धानां विधवानां च योषिताम्। योगक्षेमं च वृत्तिं च नित्यमेव प्रकल्पयेत्॥
en: He should always support and protect the helpless, the lordless, the aged, and widows.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: आश्रमेषु यथाकालं चैलभाजनभोजनम्। सदैवोपहरेद् राजा सत्कृत्याभ्यर्च्य मान्य च॥
en: The king should always honour the ascetics and present them, at proper times, with clothes, vessels and food.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: आत्मानं सर्वकार्याणि तापसे राष्ट्रमेव च। निवेदयेत् प्रयत्नेन तिष्ठेत् प्रहश्च सर्वदा॥
en: The king should, with sufficient care, inform the ascetics of the state of his own self, of all his measures, and of the kingdom, and should always behave humbly in their presence.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: सर्वार्थत्यागिनं राजा कुले जातं बहुश्रुतम्। पूजयेत् तादृशं दृष्ट्वा शयनासनभोजनैः॥
en: When he beholds anchorites of high descent and great learning that have forsaken all earthly objects, he should honour them with presents of beds and seats and food.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: तस्मिन् कुर्वीत विश्वासं राजा कस्याञ्चिदापदि। तापसेषु हि विश्वासमपि कुर्वन्ति दस्यवः॥
en: Whatever the distress which he befalls him, he should confide in an anchorite. The very ribbers place confidence upon persons of that character.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: तस्मिन् निधीनादधीत प्रज्ञां पर्याददीत च। न चाप्यभीक्ष्णं सेवेत भृशं वा प्रतिपूजयेत्॥
en: The king should keep his wealth in charge of an ascetic and should take wise counsels from him. He should not, however, always wait upon them or adore them at all times.

description: The description of the city in which a king should live.
sn: अन्यः कार्यः स्वराष्ट्रेषु परराष्ट्रेषु चापरः। अटवीषु परः कार्यः सामन्तनगरेष्वपि॥
en: From among those living in his own kingdom, he should select one for friendship. Likewise, he should select another from among those that live in the kingdom of his enemy.
