sn: तक्षेदात्मानमेवं स वनं परशुना यथा। यः सम्यग् वर्तमानेषु स्वेषु मिथ्या प्रवर्तते॥
en: That king, who treats deceitfully his own people that have not been guilty of any fault, cuts his own self like a person cutting down a forest with an axe.

sn: नैव द्विषन्तो हीयन्ते राज्ञो नित्यमनिघ्नतः। क्रोधं निहन्तुं यो वेद तस्य द्वेष्टा न विद्यते॥
en: If the king does not always attend to the task of killing his enemies, the latter do not diminish. That king, again, who knows to destroy his own anger, finds no enemies.

sn: यदार्यजनविद्विष्टं कर्म तन्नाचरेद् बुधः। यत् कल्याणमभिध्यायेत् तत्रात्मानं नियोजयेत्॥
en: If the king be wise, he would never do any act that is disapproved by good men. He would, however, always perform such acts as would do him and others good.

sn: नैनमन्येऽवजानन्ति नात्मना परितप्यते। कृत्यशेषेण यो राजा सुखान्यनुबुभूषति॥
en: That king, who, having performed all his duties, becomes satisfied with the verdict of his own conscience, has never to incur the displeasure of others nor has he any occasion to indulge in regrets.

sn: इदं वृत्तं मनुष्येषु वर्तते यो महीपतिः। उभौ लोकौ विनिर्जित्य विजये सम्प्रतिष्ठते॥
en: That king, who deals with men in such a way, succeeds in subjugating both the worlds and enjoy the fruits of victory.

sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तो वामदेवेन सर्वं तत् कृतवान् नृपः। तथा कुर्वंस्त्वमप्येतौ लोको जेता न संशयः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus accosted by Vamadeva, king Vasumanas did as he was directed. Forsooth, following these counsels, you will succeed in conquering both the worlds.

sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तो वामदेवेन सर्वं तत् कृतवान् नृपः। तथा कुर्वंस्त्वमप्येतौ लोको जेता न संशयः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus accosted by Vamadeva, king Vasumanas did as he was directed. Forsooth, following these counsels, you will succeed in conquering both the worlds.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अथ यो विजिगीषेत क्षत्रियः क्षत्रियं युधि। कस्तस्य विजये धर्मो ह्येतं पृष्टो वदस्व मे॥
en: Yudhishthira said If a Kshatriya wishes to subjugate another Kshatriya in battle, how should the former act there? Questioned by me, do you answer it.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: भीष्म उवाच ससहायोऽसहायो वा राष्ट्रमागम्य भूमिपः। ब्रूयादहं वो राजेति रक्षिष्यामि च वः सदा॥
en: Bhishma said-That king, with or without an army to follow him, entering the territories of the king he would bring under subjection, should say to all people,-I am your king! I shall always protect you!

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: मम धर्मबलिं दत्त किं वा मां प्रतिपत्स्यथ। ते चेत् तमागतं तत्र वृणुयुः कुशलं भवेत्॥
en: Give me the just tribute or fight with me!-If the people accept him as their king, there need not be any fighting.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: ते चेदक्षत्रियाः सन्तो विरुध्येरन् कथंचन। सर्वोपायैर्नियन्तव्या विकर्मस्था नराधिप॥
en: If, without being born Kshatriyas they show sings of hostility, they should then, because they follow practices not sanctioned for them be tried to be restrained by every means.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: अशस्त्रं क्षत्रियं मत्वा शस्त्रं गृह्णाद् यथापरः। त्राणायाप्यसमर्थं तं मन्यमानमतीव च॥
en: People of the other castes do take up arms if they see the Kshatriya not ready for fight, incompetent to protect himself, and too much afraid of the enemy.'

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अथ यः क्षत्रियो राजा क्षत्रियं प्रत्युपाव्रजेत्। कथं सम्प्रति योद्धव्यस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, how should that Kshatriya king fight who marches against another Kshatriya king!

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: भीष्म उवाच नैवासन्नद्धकवचो योद्धव्यः क्षत्रियो रणे। एक एकेन वाच्यश्च विसृजेति क्षिपामि च॥
en: Bhishma said A Kshatriya must not put on armour for fighting a Kshatriya who is not clad in coat of mail. One should fight one, and leave the opponent when the latter becomes disabled.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: स चेत् सन्नद्ध आगच्छेत् सन्नद्धव्यं ततो भवेत्। स चेत् ससैन्य आगच्छेत् ससैन्यस्तमथाह्वयेत्॥
en: If the enemy comes clad in mail, his opponent also should put on armour. If the enemy advances with an army at his back, one should, calling into requisition, his own strength, give him the battle.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: स चेन्निकृत्या युद्ध्येत निकृत्या प्रतियोधयेत्। अथ चेद् धर्मतो युद्ध्येद् धर्मेणैव निवारयेत्॥
en: If the enemy fights deceitfully, he should be paid in his own coin. If, however, he fights fairly, he should be resisted with fair means.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: नाश्वेन रथिनं यायादुदियाद् रथिनं रथी। व्यसने न प्रहर्तव्यं न भीताय जिताय च॥ इषुर्लिप्तो न कर्णी स्यादसतामेतदायुधम्।
en: One should not on horse-back run against a car-warrior. A car-warrior should fight with a car-warrior. When an antagonist is in a bad plight, he should not be struck; nor should one who has been frightened, nor one who has been defeated.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: यथार्थमेव योद्धव्यं न क्रुद्ध्येत जिघांसतः॥ साधूनां तु मिथो भेदात् साधुश्चेद व्यसनी भवेत्।
en: Poisoned or barbed arrows should not be used. These are the weapons used by the wicked. One should fight fairly, without giving way to anger or desiring to kill.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: निष्प्राणो नाभिहन्तव्यो नानपत्यः कथंचन॥ भग्नशस्त्रो विपन्नश्च कृत्तज्यो हतवाहनः। चिकित्स्यः स्यात् स्वविषये प्राप्यो वा स्वगृहे भवेत्।। निव्रणश्च स मोक्तव्य एष धर्मः सनातनः।
en: A weak or wounded man should not be killed, nor one who is sonless; nor one whose Weapon has been broken; nor one who has fallen into distress; nor one whose bowstring has been cut; nor one who has lost his car. A wounded opponent should either be sent to his own home, or, if brought to the victor's house, should have his wounds dressed by skilful surgeons. When for a fair fight between two kings, a righteous warrior is reduced to straits, he should, when cured, be liberated, This is the eternal duty.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: तस्माद् धर्मेण योद्धव्यमिति स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत्॥ सत्सु नित्यः सतां धर्मस्तमास्थाय न नाशयेत्।
en: Manu himself, the son of the Self-create (Brahman), has said that battles should be fought fairly. The righteous should always treat the righteous fairly. They should follow righteousness without destroying it.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: यो वै जयत्यधर्मेण क्षत्रियो धर्मसंगरः॥ आत्मानमात्मना हन्ति पापो निकृतिजीवनः।
en: If a Kshatriya, whose duty is to fight fairly, wins a victory by unfair means, he incurs sin thereby. Of deceitful conduct, such a person is said to destroy his ownself.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: कर्म चैतदसाधूनापसाधून् साधुना जयेत्॥ धर्मेण निधनं श्रेयो न जयः पापकर्मणा।
en: The wicked follow this practice. Even the wlicked should be subdued by fair means. It is better to sacrifice life itself in the observance of righteousness than to acquire victory by unfair means.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: नाधर्मश्चरितो राजन् सद्यः फलति गौरिव॥ मूलानि च प्रशाखाश्च दहन् समधिगच्छति।
en: Like a cow, O king, sin, when perpetrated, does not yield immediate fruits. That sin destroys the perpetrator after consuming his roots and branches.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: पापेन कर्मणा वित्तं लब्वा पापः प्रहृष्यति॥ स वर्धमानः स्तेयेन पापः पापे प्रसज्जति।
en: Acquiring wealth by foul means, a sinful person becomes overjoyed. But gaining advancement by sinful ways, the miscreant becomes a confirmed sinner.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: न धर्मोऽस्तीति मन्वानः शुचीनवहसन्निव॥ अश्रद्दधानश्च भवेद् विनाशमुपगच्छति। सम्बद्धो वारुणैः पाशैरमर्त्य इव मन्यते॥ महादृतिरिवाध्मातः सुकृते नैव वर्तते। ततः समूलो ह्रियते नदी कूलादिव द्रुमः॥
en: Thinking virtue as impotent, he scoffs at righteous men. Disbelieving in virtues, he at last is lost. Though bound in the noose of Varuna, he still considers himself immortal, Like a large leathern bag puffed up with wind, the sinner severs himself entirely from virtue. However, he soon disappears like a tree on the river side washed away with its very roots.

description: How should a king fight with another king
sn: अथैनमभिनिन्दन्ति भिन्नं कुम्भमिवाश्मनि। तस्माद् धर्मेण विजयं कोशं लिप्सेत भूमिपः॥
en: Then seeing him look like an earthen pot broken on a stone surface, people describe him as he deserves. The king should, therefore, seek both victory and the increment of his resources, by fair means.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: भीष्म उवाच नाधर्मेण महीं जेतुं लिप्सत जगतीपतिः। अधर्मविजयं लब्ध्वा को नु मन्येत भूमिप:॥
en: Bhishma said “A king should never desire to conquer the Earth by unfair means even if such subjugation would secure him the sovereignty of the whole Earth. What king is there who becomes happy after acquiring victory by unfair means?

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: अधर्मयुक्तो विजयो ह्यध्रुवोऽस्व→ एव च। सादयत्येष राजानं महीं च भरतर्षभ॥
en: A victory sullied by unrighteousness is uncertain and never leads to heaven. Such a victory, O foremost of Bharata's race, weakens both the king and the Earth.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: विशीर्णकवचं चैव तवास्मीति च वादिनम्। कृताञ्जलिं न्यस्तशस्त्रं गृहीत्वा न हि हिंसयेत्॥
en: A warrior whose armour has slipped off of his body, or who prays for rescue, saying-I am yours,-or joining his hands, or who has thrown off his weapon, may simply be captured but never killed.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: बलेन विजितो यश्च न तं युध्येत भूमिपः। संवत्सरं विप्रणयेत् तस्माज्जातः पुनर्भवेत्॥
en: If a hostile king be defeated by the army of the invader, the latter should not himself fight his defeated enemy. O the other hand, he should bring him to his place and induce him for whole year to say-I to say-I am your slave!-Whether he says or does not say this, the defeated enemy, by living for a year in the house of his victor, indeed gains a new life.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: नार्वाक्संवत्सरात् कन्या प्रष्टव्या विक्रमाता। एवमेव धनं सर्वं यच्चान्यत्सहसाऽऽहृतम्॥
en: If a king carries forcibly a maiden from the house of his defeated foe, he should keep her for a year and ask her whether she would a : marry him or any one else. If she does not agree, she should then be returned. He should likewise deal with all other kinds of wealth that are acquired by force.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: न तु वध्यधनं तिष्ठेत् पिबेयुर्ब्राह्मणाः पयः। युजीरन्नप्यनडुहः क्षन्तव्यं वा तदा भवेत्॥ राज्ञा राजैव योद्धव्यस्तथा धर्मो विधीयते। नान्यो राजानमभ्यस्येदराजन्यः कथञ्चन॥
en: The king should never appropriate the riches confiscated from thieves and others awaiting execution. The kine captured from the enemy by force should be given away to the Brahmanas so that they may drink their milk. The bulls taken from the enemy should be engaged in agricultural work or returned to the enemy. It is laid down that a king should fight with a king. One who is not a king should never strike a king.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: अनीकयोः संहतयोर्यदीयाद् ब्राह्मणोऽन्तरा। शान्तिमिच्छन्नुभयतो न योद्धव्यं तदा भवेत्॥
en: If a Brahmana, with a view to secure peace, fearlessly intervenes between the two contending armies, both should immediately stop fighting.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: मर्यादां शाश्वती भिन्द्याद् ब्राह्मणं योऽभिलङ्घयेत्। अथ चेल्लङ्घयेदेव मर्यादां क्षत्रियब्रुवः॥
en: He would break an eternal rule who would kill or wound such a Brahmana. If any Kshatriya breaks that rule, he would become the most cursed of his order.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: असंख्येयस्तदूर्ध्वं स्यादनादेयश्च संसदि। यस्तु धर्मविलोपेन मर्यादाभेदनेन च॥
en: Furthermore, the Kshatriya, who destroys righteousness and transgresses all wholesome restrictions, is not regarded as a Kshatriya and should be driven from society.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: तां वृत्तिं नानुवर्तेत विजीगीषुर्महीपतिः। धर्मलब्धाद्धि विजयाल्लाभः कोऽभ्यधिको भवेत्॥
en: A king, desirous of winning victory, should never behave thus. What gain can be greater than victory won fairly.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: सहसानार्यभूतानि क्षिप्रमेव प्रसादयेत्। सान्त्वेन भोगदानेन स राज्ञां परमो नयः॥
en: The sections of men who are liable to excite people (in a newly conquered kingdom) should forthwith, be conciliated with soothing words and presents. This is a good policy which the king should adopt.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: भुज्यमाना ह्ययोगेन स्वराष्ट्रादभितापिताः। अमित्रास्तमुपासीरन् व्यसनौघप्रतीक्षिणः॥
en: It instead of doing this, a king tries to govern them with impolicy, they would then leave the kingdom and side with his foes and wait for calamities to overwhelm him.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: अमित्रोपग्रहं चास्य ते कुर्यः क्षिप्रमापदि। संतुष्टाः सर्वतो राजन् राजव्यसनकाक्षिणः॥
en: Watching for the calamities of the king, discontented men promptly side with the latter's enemies, O monarch, in time of danger.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: नामित्रो विनिकर्तव्यो नातिच्छेद्यः कथञ्चन। जीवितं ह्यष्यतिच्छिन्नः संत्यजेच्च कदाचन॥
en: An enemy should not be imposed on by unfair means. Nor should he be wounded morally. For if struck morally, his very life may disappear.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: अल्पेनापि च संयुक्तस्युष्यत्येव नराधिपः। शुद्धं जीवितमेवापि तादृशो बहु मन्यते॥
en: If a king is satisfied with little resources he considers life alone as valuable.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: यस्य स्फीतो जनपदः सम्पन्नः प्रियराजकः। संतुष्टभृत्यसचिवो दृढमूलः स पार्थिवः॥
en: That king, whose dominions are extensive and rich, whose subjects are loyal, whose servants and officers are all contented, is said to be firmly settled.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्या ये चान्ये श्रुतसत्तमाः। पूजार्हाः पूजिता यस्य स वै लोकविदुच्यते॥
en: That king whose Ritvijas, priests, preceptors and others about him that are wellversed in the scriptures and worthy of honours are all duly honoured, is considered as the master of the worldly ways.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: एतेनैव च वृत्तेन महीं प्राप सुरोत्तमः। अनेन चेन्द्रविषयं विजिगीषन्ति पार्थिवाः॥
en: It was by such conduct that Indra became the king of the world. It is by this conduct that earthly kings attain to the dignity of Indra.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: भूमिवर्जं धनं राजा जित्वा राजन् महाहवे। अपि चान्नौषधीः शश्वदाजहार प्रतर्दनः॥
en: Defeating his enemies in great battle, King Pratardana took all their wealth, including their very grain and medicinal herbs, but left their land untouched.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: अग्निहोत्राग्निशेषं च हविर्भोजनमेव च। आजहार दिवोदासस्ततो विप्रकृतोऽभवत्॥
en: After subjugating his foes, King Divodasa brought away the very residue of their sacrificial fires, their clarified butter, and their food. Therefore he was deprived of the merit of his conquests.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: सराजकानि राष्ट्राणि नाभागो दक्षिणां ददौ। अन्यत्र श्रोत्रियस्वाच्च तापसार्थाच्च भारत॥
en: King Nabhaga gave away whole kingdoms with their rulers as sacrificial presents to the Brahmanas, save the wealth of learned Brahmanas and ascetics.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: उच्चावचानि वित्तानि धर्मज्ञानां युधिष्ठिर। आसन् राज्ञां पुराणानां सर्वं तन्मम रोचते॥
en: The conduct, O Yudhishthira, of all the righteous kings of yore, was excellent, and I approve of it wholly.

description: The duties of a king to wars his enemy.
sn: सर्वविद्यातिरेकेण जयमिच्छेन्महीपतिः। न मायया न दम्भेन य इच्छेद् भूतिमात्मनः॥
en: That king who wishes for his own prosperity should try to make conquests by fair means, but never with deceit but ones on or with pride.'

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच क्षत्रधर्माद्धि पापीयान्न धर्मोऽस्ति नराधिप। अपयानेन युद्धेन राजा हन्ति महाजनम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said No action O king, is more sinful than that of the Kshatriyas! While marching or in battle, the king destroys the Vaishyas.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: अथ स्म कर्मणा केन लोकान् जयति पार्थिवः। विद्वन् जिज्ञासमानाय प्रबूहि भरतर्षभ॥
en: By what acts then does the king acquire blessed regions? O foremost of Bharata's race, enlighten me on this, O learned one, I am as anxious to know.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: भीष्म उवाच निग्रहेण च पापानां साधूनां संग्रहेण च। यज्ञैर्दानैश्च राजानो भवन्ति शुचयोऽमलाः॥
en: Bhishma said By punishing the wicked, by winning over and maintaining the good, by sacrifices and gifts, kings become pure and cleansed.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: उपरुन्धन्ति राजानो भूतानि विजयार्थिनः। त एव विजयं प्राप्य वर्धयन्ति पुनः प्रजाः॥
en: It is true, kings, desirous of victory, torture many creatures, but after victory they secure the advancement of all,

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: अपविध्यन्ति पापानि दानयज्ञतपोबलैः। अनुग्रहाय भूतानां पुण्यमेषां विवर्धते॥
en: By the power of gifts, sacrifices, and penances, they dissipate their sins, and their merit increases so that they may be able to do good to all creatures.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: यथैव क्षेत्रनिर्याता निर्यातं क्षेत्रमेव च। हिनस्ति धान्यं कक्षं च न च धान्यं विनश्यति॥
en: For reclaiming a field, the reclaimer takes up both paddy blades and weeds. His course, however, instead, of destroying the blades of paddy, he makes them grow more vigorously.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: एवं शस्त्राणि मुञ्चन्तो प्रन्ति वध्याननेकथा। तस्यैषां निष्कृतिः कृत्स्ना भूतानां भावनं पुनः॥
en: Those, who use weapons, destroy many who deserve to be killed. Such wholesale destruction, however, helps the growth and advancement of the remnant.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: यो भूतानि धनाक्रान्त्या वधात् क्लेशाच्च रक्षति। दस्युभ्यः प्राणदानात् स धनदः सुखदो विराट्॥
en: He who protects people from plunder, destruction, and affliction, he, for thus saving their lives from robbers, is regarded as the giver of wealth, of life, and of food.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: स सर्वयज्ञैरीजानो राजाथाभयदक्षिणैः। अनुभूयेह भद्राणि प्राप्नोतीन्द्रसलोकताम्॥
en: Therefore, by thus worshipping the gods by means of a union of all sacrifices whose Dakshina is the removing of every body's fear, the king enjoys every king of happiness here and lives with Indra in heaven hereafter.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: ब्राह्मणार्थे समुत्पन्ने योऽरिभिः सृत्य युध्यति। आत्मानं यूपमुत्सृज्य स यज्ञोऽनन्तदक्षिणः॥
en: That king, who, going out, fights his enemies in battles that have arisen for the sake of Brahmanas, and sacrifices his life, is regarded as the embodiment of a sacrifice with endless presents.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: अभीतो विकिरशत्रून् प्रतिगृह्य शरांस्तथा। न तस्मात्रिदशा:श्रेयो भुवि पश्यन्ति किञ्चन॥
en: If a king, with his quivers full of arrows, shoots them fearlessly at his enemies, the very gods do not see any one superior to his on Earth.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: तस्य शस्त्राणि यावन्ति त्वचं भिन्दन्ति संयुगे। तावतः सोऽश्नुते लोकान् सर्वकामदुहोऽक्षयान्॥
en: In such a case, regions eternal and capable of granting every desire proportionate to the number of arrows he discharges for wounding the enemies, await him.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: यदस्य रुधिरं गात्रादाहये सम्प्रवर्तते। सह तेनैव रक्तेन सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: The blood that flows from his body purges him off of all his sins along with the very pain that he feels then.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: यानि दुःखानि सहते क्षत्रियो युधि तापितः। तेन तेन तपो भूय इति धर्मविदो विदुः॥
en: Persons well read in the scriptures say that the pains a Kshatriya suffers in battle act as penances for increasing his merit.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: पृष्ठतो भीरवः संख्ये वर्तन्तेऽधर्मपूरुषाः। शूराच्छरणमिच्छन्तः पर्जन्यादिव जीवनम्॥
en: Righteous persons, stricken with fear, stay in the rear, begging for life from heroes that have rushed to battle, even as men pray for rain from the clouds.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: यदि शूरस्तथा क्षेमं प्रतिरक्षेद् यथाभये। प्रतिरूपं जनं कुर्यान्न चेत् तद्वर्तते तथा॥
en: Without allowing the solicitors to incur the dangers of battle, if those heroes place them in the rear by themselves facing those dangers and defend them at that time of fear, they acquire great merit.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: यदि ते कृतमाज्ञाय नमस्कुर्युः सदैवतम्। युक्तं न्याय्यं च कुर्युस्ते न च तद् वर्तते तथा॥
en: And, if appreciating that act of bravery, those timid persons always respect those defenders, they do simply what is proper and just. By acting otherwise they cannot overcome fear.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: पुरुषाणां समानानां दृश्यते महदन्तरम्। संग्रामेऽनीकवेलायामुत्क्रुष्टेऽभिपतन्त्युत॥
en: There is really a great difference between men who seem outwardly equal. Some rush to battle, arnid its dreadful din, against armed enemies.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: पतत्यभिमुखः शूरः परान् भीरुः पलायते। आस्थाय स्वय॑मध्वानं सहायान् विषमे त्यजेत्॥
en: Indeed, it is the hero who only rushes against crowds of enemies, that leads him to the road to heaven. The coward, on the contrary, stricken with fear, seeks safety in flight, leaving behind his comrades in danger.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: मा स्म तांस्तादृशांस्तात जनिष्ठाः पुरुषाधमान्। ये सहायान् रणे हित्वा स्वस्तिमन्तो गृहान् ययुः॥ अस्वस्ति तेभ्यः कुर्वन्ति देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः। त्यागेन यः सहायानां स्वान् प्राणांस्त्रातुमिच्छति।॥ तं हन्युः काष्ठलोष्ठैर्वा दहेयुर्वा कटाग्निना। पशुवन्मारयेयुर्वा क्षत्रिया ये स्युरीदृशाः॥
en: Let not such wretches of men be born in your family! The very gods headed by Indra send calamities to them who leave behind their comrades in battle and come home unscathed and uninjured. He who desires to save his own life by leaving behind his comrades, should be killed with sticks or stones or rolled in a mat of dry grass for being burnt to death. The Kshatriyas who would be guilty of slich conduct should be slain like animals.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: अधर्मः क्षत्रियस्यैष यच्छय्यामरणं भवेत्। विसृजश्लेष्ममूत्राणि कृपणं परिदेवयन्॥
en: Quiet death on a bed, after throwing out phlegm and urine and uttering piteous cries, is sinful for a Kshatriya.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: अविक्षतेन देहेन प्रलयं योऽधिगच्छति। क्षत्रियो नास्य तत् कर्म प्रशंसन्ति पुराविदः॥
en: Persons well-read in the scriptures do not praise the death of a Kshatriya with unwounded body.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: न गृहे मरणं तात क्षत्रियाणां प्रशस्यते। शौटीराणामशौटीर्यमधर्म कृपणं च तत्॥
en: The death of a Kshatriya at home is not praiseworthy. They are heroes. Any unheroic act on their part is sinful and censurable.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: इदं दुःखं महत् कष्टं पापीय इति नष्टनन्। प्रतिध्वस्तमुखः पूतिरमात्याननुशोचयन्॥
en: In disease, people hear one crying,-What। sorrow! How painful! I must be a great sinner! : With face emaciated and bad smell coming out of his body and clothes, the sick man drowns his relatives into grief.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: अरोगाणां स्पृहयते मुहुर्मृत्युमपीच्छति। वीरो दृप्तोऽभिमानी च नेदृशं मृत्युमर्हति॥
en: Hankering after the condition of healthy men, such a man again and again desires for death itself. A hero, having dignity and pride, does not deserve such an inglorious death.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: रणेषु कदनं कृत्वा ज्ञातिभिः परिवारितः। तीक्ष्णैः शस्त्रैरभिक्लिष्टः क्षत्रियो मृत्युमर्हति॥
en: Surrounded by kinsmen and killing his enemies in battle, a Kshatriya should die at the edge of keen weapons.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: शूरो हि काममन्युभ्यामाविष्टो युद्ध्यते भृशम्। हन्यमानानि गात्राणि परैर्नैवावबुध्यते॥
en: Actuated by lustful desire and filled with rage, a hero fights furiously and does not feel the wounds inflicted on his person by enemies.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: स संख्ये निधनं प्राप्य प्रशस्तं लोकपूजितम्। स्वधर्मं विपुलं प्राप्य शक्रस्येति सलोकताम्॥
en: Meeting with death in battle, he acquires great merit, fame and the respect of the world which belongs to his order and in the end lives with Indra in heaven.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: सर्वोपायै रणमुखमातिष्ठंस्त्यक्तजीवितः। प्राप्नोतीन्द्रस्य सालोक्यं शूरः पृष्ठमदर्शयन्॥
en: The hero, by not retreating from battle and fighting by every means in his power, careless of life itself, at the van of battle, lives with Indra.

description: The acts by which a king acquires blessed regions
sn: यत्र यत्र हतः शूरः शत्रुभिः परिवारितः। अक्षयाँल्लभते लोकान् यदि दैन्यं न सेवते॥
en: Wherever the hero has met with death in the inidst of enemies without showing ignoble fear or cheerlessness, he has succeeded in acquiring blessed regions hereafter.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच के लोका युध्यमानानां शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम्। भवन्ति निधनं प्राप्य तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, what regions are earned by unretreating heroes by meeting with death in battle! Bhishma said

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। अम्बरीषस्य संवादमिन्द्रस्य च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: 'Regarding it, O Yudhishthira, is cited the old story of the discourse between Ambarisha and Indra.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: अम्बरीषो हि नाभागिः स्वर्गं गत्वा सुदुर्लभम्। ददर्श सुरलोकस्थं शक्रेण सचिवं सह॥
en: Having gone to heaven that is so difficult of acquisition, Ambarisha, the son of Nabhaga, saw his own commander in chief in those celestial regions in the company of Indra.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: सर्वतेजोमयं दिव्यं विमानवरमास्थितम्। उपर्युपरि गच्छन्तं स्वं वै सेनापतिं प्रभुम्॥
en: The king saw his powerful general shining with every kind of energy, gifted with celestial forin, seated on a very beautiful car, and going up and up towards still higher regions.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: स दृष्ट्वोपरि गच्छन्तं सेनापतिमुदारधीः। ऋद्धिं दृष्ट्वा सुदेवस्य विस्मितः प्राह वासवम्॥
en: Witnessing the prosperity of his general Sudeva, and observing how he passed through regions that were still higher, the great Ambarisha, stricken with wonder addressed Vasava, in the following manner.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: अम्बरीष उवाच सागरान्तां महीं कृत्स्नामनुशास्य यथाविधि। चातुर्वण्र्ये यथाशास्त्रं प्रवृत्तौ धर्मकाम्यया॥ ब्रह्मचर्येण घोरेण गुर्वाचारेण सेवया। वेदानधीत्य धर्मेण राजशास्त्रं च केवलम्॥ अतिथीनन्नपानेन पितृ॑श्च स्वधया तथा। ऋषीन् स्वाध्यायदीक्षाभिर्देवान् यज्ञैरनुत्तमैः॥ क्षत्रधर्मे स्थितो भूत्वा यथाशास्त्रं यथाविधि। उदीक्षमाणः पृतनां जयामि युधि वासव॥
en: Ambarisha said Having properly governed the entire Earth bounded by the oceans, having from desire of acquiring religious merit practised all those duties which are common to the four orders as sanctioned by the scriptures, having practised with rigid austerity all the duties of the Brahmacharya mode, having waited with obedience upon the preceptors and other reverend elders, having studied properly the Vedas and the scriptures treating on royal duties, having pleased the guests with food and drink, the Pitris with offerings in Shraddhas, the Rishis with attentive study of the scriptures and with initiation and the gods with many good and high sacrifices, having duly followed Kshatriya duties according to the injunctions of the scriptures, having looked fearlessly at hostile troops, I acquired many victories in battle, O Vasava.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: देवराज सुदेवोऽयं मम सेनापतिः पुरा। आसीद् योधः प्रशान्तात्मा सोऽयं कस्मादतीव माम्।।१०
en: This Sudeva, O king of the deities, was formerly the commander-in-chief of my army. It is true, he was a warrior of a controlled soul. For what reason, however, has he succeeded in superseding me?

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: अनेन क्रतुभिर्मुख्यैर्नेष्टं नापि द्विजातयः। तर्पिता विधिवच्छक सोऽयं कस्मादतीव माम्॥
en: He never adored the gods in high and great sacrifices. He never pleased the Brahmanas according to the ordinance. Why then, has he succeeded in superseding me?

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: इन्द्र उवाच एतस्य विततस्तात सुदेवस्य बभूव ह। संग्रामयज्ञः सुमहान् यश्चान्यो युद्ध्यते नरः॥
en: Indra said About this Sudeva, Osire, the great sacrifice of battle had often been performed by him. And such becomes the case with every other man who engages himself in battle.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: संनद्धो दीक्षितः सर्वो योधः प्राप्त चमूमुखम्। युद्धयज्ञाधिकारस्थो भवतीति विनिश्चयः॥
en: Every warrior clad a in coat of mail by advancing against enemies in battle, becomes installed in that sacrifice. Indeed, it is settled that such a person, by acting in this wise is regarded as the performer of the sacrifice of battle.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: अम्बरीष उवाच कानि यज्ञे हवींष्यस्मिन् किमाज्यं का च दक्षिणा। ऋत्विजश्चात्र के प्रोक्तास्तन्मे ब्रूहि शतक्रतो॥
en: Ambarisha said What are the libations in that sacrifice? What are its liquid offerings? What is its Dakshina? Who, again, are its Ritwijas? Tell me all this, Operformer of a hundred sacrifices.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: इन्द्र उवाच इत्विजः कुञ्जरास्तत्र वाजिनोऽध्वर्यवस्तथा! हवींषि परमांसानि रुधिरं त्वाज्यमुच्यते॥
en: Elephants are the Ritwijas of that sacrifice, and horses are its Adhyaryus. The flesh of foes are its libations, and blood is its liquid offering.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: शृगालगृध्रकाकोला: सदस्यास्तत्र पत्रिणः। आज्यशेषं पिबन्त्येते हविः प्रा श्नन्ति चाध्वरे॥
en: Jackals, vultures, and ravens, winged arrows are its Sadasyas. These drink the residue of the liquid offering in this sacrifice and eat the remnants of its libations. as also

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: प्रासतोमरसंघाताः खड्गशक्तिपरश्वधाः। ज्वलन्तो निशिताः पीताः स्त्रुचस्तस्याथ सत्रिणः॥
en: Masses of blazing, sharp, and welltempered, lances and spears, of swords and darts and axes from the ladles of the sacrificer.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: चापवेगायतस्तीक्ष्णः परकायावभेदनः। ऋजुः सुनिशितः पीतः सायकश्च स्रुवो महान्॥
en: Straight, sharp, and well-tempered shafts, with keen points and capable of piercing the bodies of enemies, shot off well-stretched bows, from its large double mouthed ladles.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: द्वीपीचर्मावनद्धश्च नागदन्तकृतत्सरुः। हस्तिहस्तहरः खड्गः सूयो भवेत् तस्य संयुगे॥
en: Sheathed in scabbard made of tiger-skin and equip with in ivory handle, and capable of cutting off the elephant's trunk, the sword forms the wooden-stick of this sacrifice.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: ज्वलितैर्निशितैः प्रासशक्त्यृष्टिसपरश्वधैः। शैक्यायसमयैस्तीक्ष्णैरभिघातो भवेद् वसु॥ संख्यासमयविस्तीर्णमभिजातोद्भवं बहु।
en: The strokes inflicted with shining and keen lances and darts and swords and axes, all made of hard iron, from its profuse wealth collected from the respectable people by agreement regarding the amount and period.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: आवेगाद् यच्च रुधिरं संग्रामे स्रवते भुवि॥ सास्य पूर्णाहुति)मे समृद्धा सर्वकामधुक्।
en: The blood that runs over the field for the fury of that attack, forms the final libation, which yields great merit and is capable of granting every wish in the Homa of this sacrifice.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: छिन्धि भिन्धीति यः शब्दः श्रुयते वाहिनीमुखे॥ सामानि सामगास्तस्य गायन्ति यमसादने।
en: 'Cut, Pierce,' and such other sounds, that are heard in the front ranks of the army, are the Samans sung by its Vedic chanters in the abode of Yama.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: परेषां वाहिनीमुखम्॥ कुञ्जराणां हयानां च वर्मिणां च समुच्चयः। हविर्धानं तु तस्याहुः अग्निः श्येनचितो नाम स च यज्ञे विधीयते॥
en: The front ranks of the enemy's army form the vessel for keeping libations. The number of elephant and horses and men equipt with shields form the Shyenachit fire of that sacrifice.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: उत्तिष्ठते कबन्धोऽत्र सहस्र निहते तु यः। स यूपस्तस्य शूरस्य खादिरोऽशस्त्रिरुच्यते॥
en: The headless trunks that rise up after thousands have been killed from the octagonal stake, made of Khadira wood, for the hero who celebrates that sacrifice.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: इडोपहूताः क्रोशन्ति कुञ्जरास्त्वंकुशेरिताः। व्याघुश्तलनादेव वषट्कारेण पार्थिव॥ उद्गाता तत्र सग्रामे त्रिसामा दुन्दुभिर्नृप।
en: The cries of the elephant when urged on with hooks, form its Ida Mantras. The kettledrums, with the striking of palms forming the Vashats, O king, are its Trisaman Udgatri.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: ब्रह्मस्व ह्रियमाणे तु त्यक्त्वा युद्धे प्रियां तनुम्॥ आत्मानं यूपमुत्सृज्य स यज्ञोऽनन्तदक्षिणः।
en: When the property of a Brahmana is being taken away, he who renounces his dear body for protecting that property, does, by that act of self-devotion, acquire the merit of a sacrifice accompanied with numberless presents.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: भर्तुरर्थे च यः शूरो विक्रमेद् वाहिनीमुखे॥ न भयाद् विनिवर्तेत तस्य लोका यथा मम।
en: That hero, who, for sake of his master, shows prowess at the van of the array and does not retreat through fear, acquires those re of happiness that are mine.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: नीलचर्मावृतैः खड्नैर्बाहुभिः परिघोपमैः॥ यस्य वेदिरुपस्तीर्णा तस्य लोका यथा मम।
en: He, who covers the altar of the sacrifice formed by battle, with swords cased in bluescabbards and severed arms resembling heavy bludgeons, acquires the happy regions like mine.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: यस्तु नापेक्षते कंचित् सहायं विजये स्थितः॥ विगाह्य वाहिनीमध्यं तस्य लोका यथा मम।
en: That warrior, who determined upon gaining victory, enters into the midst of the enemy's ranks without waiting for any help, acquires happy regions like mine.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: यस्य शोणितसंघाता भेरीमण्डूककच्छपा।॥ वीरास्थिशर्करा दुर्गा मांसशोणितकर्दमा। असिचर्मप्लवा घोरा केशशैवलशाद्वला॥ अश्वनागरथैश्चैव संच्छिन्नैः कृतसंक्रमा। पताकाध्वजवानीरा हतवारणवाहिनी॥ शोणितोदा सुसम्पूर्णा दुस्तरा पारगैर्नरैः। हतनागमहानका परलोकवहाशिवा॥ ऋश्खिड्गमहानौका गृध्रकङ्कबलप्लवा। पुरुषादानुचरिता भीरूणां कश्मलावहा॥ नदी योधस्य संग्रामे तदस्यावभृथं स्मृतम्।
en: That warrior, who in battle makes a river of blood to flow, dreadful and difficult to cross, having kettle,-drums for its frogs and tortoises, the bones of heroes for its sands, blood and flesh for its mire, swords and shields for its rafts, the hair of killed warriors for its floating weeds and moss, the number of horses and elephants and cars for its bridges, standards and banners for its bushes of cane, the bodies of killed elephants for its boats and huge alligators, swords and scimitars for its larger vessels, vultures and Kankas and ravens for the rafts that float upon it,—that warrior, who causes such a river, which can with difficulty be crossed by even those who are courageous and powerful and which terrorises all timid men, is said to complete the sacrifice by performing the final ablutions.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: वेदिर्यस्य त्वमित्राणां शिरोभ्यश्च प्रकीर्यते॥ अश्वस्कन्धैर्गजस्कन्धेस्तस्य लोका यथा मम।
en: That hero, whose altar is covered with the heads of foes, of horses, and of elephants, acquires regions of felicity like mine.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: पत्नीशाला कृता यस्य परेषां वाहिनीमुखम्॥ हविर्धानं स्ववाहिन्यास्तदस्याहुर्मनीषिणः। सदस्या दक्षिणा योधा आग्नीध्रश्चोत्तरां दिशम्॥ शत्रुसेनाकलत्रस्य सर्वलोका न दूरतः।
en: The sages have said that warrior, who considers the van of the hostile army as the quarters of his wives, who regards the van of his own army as the vessel for the preservation of sacrificial offerings, who takes the warriors standing to his south for his courtiers and those to this north as his holders of fire, and who regards the hostile army as his married wife, succeeds in acquiring all regions of felicity.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: यदा तूभयतो व्यूहे भवत्याकाशमग्रतः॥ सास्य वेदिस्तदा यज्ञैर्नित्यं वेदास्त्रयोऽग्नयः।
en: The open space, lying between two armies drawn up for fight, forms the altar of such as sacrificer, and the three Vedas are his three sacrificial fires. Upon that altar, helped by the recitation of the Vedas, he celebrates his sacrifice.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: यस्तु योधः परावृत्तः संत्रस्तो हन्यते परैः॥ अप्रतिष्ठः स नरकं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः।
en: That infamous warrior, who retreating from the fight in fear, is killed by foes, sinks into hell. There is no doubt in this.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: यस्य शोणितवेगेन वेदिः स्यात् सम्परिप्लुता॥ केशमांसास्थिसम्पूर्णा स गच्छेत् परमां गतिम्।
en: That warrior, on the other hand, whose blood drenches the sacrificial altar already covered with hair and flesh and bones, forsooth, succeeds in acquiring a glorious end.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: यस्तु सेनापतिं हत्वा तद्यानमधिरोहति॥ स विष्णुविक्रमकामी बृहस्पतिसमः प्रभुः।
en: That powerful warrior, who, having killed the commander of the hostile army, gets upon the car of his fallen antagonist, is considered as powerful as Vishnu himself and as intelligent as Brihaspati, the preceptor of the gods.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: नायकं तत्कुमारं वा यो वा स्याद् यत्र पूजितः॥ जीवग्राहं प्रगृह्णाति तस्य लोका यथा मम।
en: That warrior, who can capture alive the commander of the hostile army or his son or some other respected leader, acquires regions of felicity like mine.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: आहवे तु हतं शूरं न शोचेत कथंचन॥ अशोच्यो हि हतः शूरः स्वर्गलोके महीयते।
en: One should never lament for a hero killed in battle. A killed hero, if nobody grieves for him, goes to heaven and acquires the respect of its residents.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: न ह्यनं नोदकं तस्य न स्नानं नाप्यशौचकम्॥ हतस्य कर्तुमिच्छन्ति तस्य लोकाशृणुष्व मे।
en: Men do not wish to give food and drink. Nor do they bathe nor enter into mourning for him. Listen to me as I describe the happiness that is in store for such a person.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: वराप्सरः सहस्राणि शूरमायोधने हतम्॥ त्वरमाणाभिधावन्ति मम भर्ता भवेदिति। एतत् तपश्च पुण्यं च धर्मश्चैव सनातनः॥ चत्वारश्चाश्रमास्तस्य यो युद्धमनुपालयेत्।
en: Thousands of leading nymphs, go out speedily coveting him for their lord. That Kshatriya, who duly observes his duty in battle, wins by that act the merits of penances and of righteousness. Indeed, such conduct on his part is quite of a piece with the eternal path of duty. Such a man acquires the merits of all the four modes of life.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: वृद्धबालौ न हन्तव्यौ न च स्त्री नैव पृष्ठतः॥ तृणपूर्णमुखश्चैव तवास्मीति च यो वदेत्।
en: The aged and the children should not be killed; nor a woman nor one who is flying away; nor one that holds a straw in his lips (sign of unconditional surrender); nor one who says—I am yours.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: जम्भं वृत्रं बलं पाकं शतमायं विरोचनम्॥ दुर्वार्यं चैव नमुचिं नैकमायं च शम्बरम्। विप्रचित्तिं च दैतेयं दनोः पुत्रांश्च सर्वशः। प्रह्लादं च निहत्याजौ ततो देवाधिपोऽभवम्॥
en: Having killed in battle Jambha, Vritra, Vala, Paka, Shatamaya, Virochana, the irresistible Namuchi, Shamvara of numberless illusions, Viprachitti.—all these sons of Diti and Danu,-as also Prahlada, I myself have become the king of the gods.

description: The regions which a hero acquires by meeting with death in battle
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्येतच्छक्रवचनं निशम्य प्रतिगृह्य च। योधानामात्मनः सिद्धिमम्बरीषोऽभिपन्नवान्॥
en: Bhishma continued Hearing these words of Shakra and approving of them, king Ambarisha understood how warriors succeed in achieving success for themselves.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। प्रतर्दनो मैथिलश्च संग्रामं यत्र चक्रतुः॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old story of the battle between Pratardana and the king of Mithila.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: यज्ञोपवीती संग्रामे जनको मैथिलो यथा। योधानुद्धर्षयामास तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: The king of Mithila, viz., Janaka, after installation in the sacrifice of battle, pleased all his soldiers. Listen to me, O Yudhishthira, as I relate the story.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: जनको मैथिलो राजा महात्मा सर्वतत्त्ववित्। योधान् स्वान् दर्शयामास स्वर्ग नरकमेव च॥
en: Janaka, the great great king of Mithila, conversant with the truth of everything, showed both heaven and hell to his own warriors.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: अभीरूणामिमे लोका भास्वन्तो हन्त पश्यत। पूर्णा गन्धर्वकन्याभिः सर्वकामदुहोऽक्षयाः॥
en: He addressed them, saying-Look, these are the effulgent regions, reserved for those who fight fearlessly! Abounding with Gandharva girls, those regions are eternal and capable of granting every desire.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: इमे पलायमानानां नरकाः प्रत्युपस्थिताः। अकीर्तिः शाश्वती चैव यतितव्यमनन्तरम्॥
en: There, on the other side, are the regions of hell, reserved for those who retreat from battle! they would have to rot there for ever in everlasting shame.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: तान् दृष्ट्वारीन् विजयत भूत्वा संत्यागबुद्धयः। नरकस्याप्रतिष्ठस्य मा भूत वशवर्तिनः॥ त्यागमूलं हि शूराणां स्वर्गद्वारमनुत्तमम्।
en: Determined upon sacrificing your very lives, do you conquer your enemies! Do not fall into infamous hell! The sacrifice of life in battle forms the happy door of heaven for heroes!

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: अजयन्त रणे शत्रून् हर्षयन्तो नरेश्वरम्। तस्मादात्मवता नित्यं स्थातव्यं रणमूर्धनि॥ इत्युक्तास्ते नृपतिना योधाः परपुरंजय॥
en: Thus addressed by their king, O subduer of hostile towns, the warriors of Mithila, pleasing their king, defeated their enemies in battle. The strong-minded people should take their stand in the van of battle.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: गजानां रथिनो मध्ये रथानामनु सादिनः। सादिनामन्तरे स्थाप्यं पादातमपि दंशितम्॥
en: The car-warriors should be placed in the midst of elephants. Behind the car-warriors should stand the cavalry. Behind the last should be placed the infantry all clad in mail.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: य एवं व्यूहते राजा स नित्यं जयति द्विषः। तस्मादेवं विधातव्यं नित्यमेव युधिष्ठिर॥
en: That king, who makes his battle array in this way, always succeeds in defeating his enemies. Therefore, O Yudhishthira, the array of battle should always be formed thus.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: सर्वे स्वर्गतिमिच्छन्ति सुयुद्धेनातिमन्यवः। क्षोभयेयुरनीकानि सागरं मकरा यथा।॥
en: Filled with wrath, heroes wish to acquire blessedness in heaven by fighting fairly. Like Makaras agitating the sea, they agitate the ranks of the enemy.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: हर्षयेयुर्विषण्णांश्च व्यवस्थाप्य परस्परम्। जितां च भूमि रक्षेत भग्नान् नात्यनुसारयेत्॥
en: Assuring one another, they should cheer up the cheerless. The victor should protect the newly conquered country. He should not cause his troops to pursue the dispersed enemies.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: पुनरावर्तमानानां निराशानां च जीविते। वेगः सुदुःसहो राजस्तस्मान्नात्यनुसारयेत्॥
en: The attack of routed persons, who rally after being dispersed, is dreadful, since losing all hope of life and despairing of safety, they attack their pursuers. Therefore, O king, you should not cause your troops to pursue the dispersed foes too rashly.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: न हि प्रहर्तुमिच्छन्ति शूराः प्रद्रवतो भृशम्। तस्मात् पलायमानानां कुर्यान्नात्यनुसारणम्॥
en: Brave warriors do not wish to strike them that run away quickly. That is another reason why the scattered foe should not be pursued hotiy.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: चराणामचरा ह्यन्नमदंष्ट्रा दंष्ट्रिणामपि। आपः पिपासतामन्नमन्नं शूरस्य कातराः॥
en: Things immobile are devoured by those that are mobile; toothless creatures are devoured by those that have teeth, water is drunk by the thirsty; cowards are devoured by heroes.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: समानपृष्ठोदरपाणिपादाः पराभवं भीरवो वै व्रजन्ति। अतो भयार्ताः प्रणिपत्य भूयः कृत्वाञ्जलीनुपतिष्ठन्ति शूरान्॥
en: Cowards only sustain defeat, though they, like their victors, possess similar backs, stomachs, arms and legs. They, who are stricken with fear bend their heads and joining their hands stand before the courageous.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: शूरवाहुषु लोकोऽयं लम्बते पुत्रवत् सदा। तस्मात् सर्वास्ववस्थासु शूरः सम्मानमर्हति॥
en: This world depends on the arms of heroes like a son on those of his father. A hero, therefore, should be honoured under every circumstance.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: न हि शौर्यात् परं किंचित् त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते। शूरः सर्वं पालयति सर्वं शूरे प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: There is nothing superior of the three worlds to heroism. The hero protects and maintains all, and all things depend upon the hero.

description: The duties of heroes as described by king Janaka
sn: न हि शौर्यात् परं किंचित् त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते। शूरः सर्वं पालयति सर्वं शूरे प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: There is nothing superior of the three worlds to heroism. The hero protects and maintains all, and all things depend upon the hero.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यथा जयार्थिनः सेनां नयन्ति भरतर्षभ। ईषद्धर्मं प्रपीड्यापि तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, how kings seeking victory should, O foremost of Bharata's race, lead their troops to battle even by acting slightly against the rules of righteousness.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: भीष्म उवाच सतयेन हि स्थितो धर्म उपपत्त्या तथा परे। साध्वाचारतया केचित् तथैवौपयिकादपि॥
en: Bhishma said Some say that Righteousness is made permanent by Truth; some, by Reasoning; some, by good conduct; and some, by the application of means and contrivances.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: उपायधर्मान् वक्ष्यामि सिद्धार्थानर्थधर्मयोः। निर्मर्यादा दस्यवस्तु भवन्ति परिपन्थिनः॥
en: I shall presently describe to you the means and contrivances, which yield immediate fruit. Robbers, transgressing all wholesome limits, very often become destroyers of property and religious merit.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: तेषां प्रतिविघातार्थं प्रवक्ष्याम्यथ नैगमम्। कार्याणां सर्वसिद्ध्यर्थं तानुपायान् निबोध मे॥
en: For opposing and restraining them, I shall tell you the means indicated in the scriptures. Hear as I describe those means for the success of all deeds.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: उभे प्रज्ञे वेदितव्ये ऋज्वी वक्रा च भारत। जानन् वक्रां न सेवेत प्रतिबाधेत चागताम्॥
en: Both kinds of wisdom, plain and wily, should be within the king's reach. Though acquainted with it, he should not, however, apply the wily wisdom. He may use it for withstanding the dangers that may befall him.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: अमित्रा एव राजानं भेदेनोपचरन्त्युत। तां राजा निकृति जानन् यथामित्रान् प्रबाधते॥
en: Enemies frequently injure a king by creating disunion. The king, conversant with deceit, may, by the help of deceit, counteract those enemies.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: गजानां पार्थ वर्माणि गोवृषाजगराणि च। शल्यकण्टकलोहानि तनुत्रचमराणि च॥ सितपीतानि शस्त्राणि संनाहाः पीतलोहिताः। नानारञ्जनरक्ताः स्युः पताका: केतवश्च ह॥ ऋश्यस्तोमराः खड्गा निशिताश्च परश्वधाः। फलकान्यथ चर्माणि प्रतिकल्प्यान्यनेकशः॥
en: Leathern armour for protecting the bodies of elephants, as also those for bulls, bones, thorns, and keen-pointed iron weapons, coats of mail, yak-tails, sharp and well-tempered weapons, all kinds of armour yellow and red, banners and standards of various colours, swords, lances, sharp scimitars, battle axes, spears and shields should be manufactured and kept profusely in store.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: अभिनीतानि शस्त्राणि योधाश्च कृतनिश्चयाः। चैत्र्यां वा मार्गशीर्थ्यां वा सेनायोगः प्रशस्यते॥
en: The weapons should all be properly whetted. The soldiers should be filled with courage and resolution. It is proper to march the troops in the month of Chaitra Agrahayana.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: पक्वसस्या हि पृथिवी भवत्यम्बुमती तदा। नैवातिशीतो नात्युष्ण: कालो भवति भारत॥
en: The crops ripen about that time and water also is not scarce. That time of the year, O Bharata, is neither very cold nor very hot.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: तस्मात् तदा योजयेत परेषां व्यसनेऽथवा। एते हि योगाः सेनायाः प्रशस्ताः परवाधने॥
en: Troops should, therefore, be marched at that time. If the enemy, however, be reduced to a miserable plight, troops should immediately be despatched. These (two) are the best occasions for the movement of troops for defeating the enemies.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: जलवांस्तृणवान् मार्गः समो गम्यः प्रशस्यते। चारैः सुविदिताभ्यासः कुशलैर्वनगोचरैः॥
en: That road which has profuse water and grass along it, which is level and easy of march, should be taken. The regions lying near the road should previously be reconnoitred through skilful spies having an intimate knowledge of the woods.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: न हरण्येन शक्येत गन्तुं मृगगणैरिव। तस्मात् सेनासु तानेव योजयन्ति जयार्थिनः॥
en: The troops must not, like animals, be marched through forests. Kings desirous of victory should, therefore, follow good roads for marching their army.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: अग्रतः पुरुषानीकं शक्तं चापि कुलोद्भवम्। आवासस्तोयवान् दुर्ग: पर्याकाशः प्रशस्यते॥
en: In the van should be placed a detachment of brave, strong and high born men. As regards forts, one which has walls and a trench full of water on every side and only one entrance, is the best.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: परेषामुपसर्पाणां प्रतिषेधस्तथा भवेत्। आकाशात् तु वनाभ्याशं मन्यन्ते गुणवत्तरम्॥ बहुभिर्गुणजातैश्च ये युद्धकुशला जनाः। उपन्यासो भवेत् तत्र बलानां नातिदूरतः॥
en: While attacking enemies resistance may be offered from within it. In pitching the camp, a region lying near the forest is regarded as much better than one under the open sky by men who are masters of military science and warfare. The camp should be pitched for the troops not far from such a forest.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: उपन्यासावतरणं पदातीनां च गृहनम्। अथ शत्रुप्रतीघातमापदर्थं परायणम्॥
en: Pitching the camp at such a place, placing the infantry in a safe place, and meeting the foe as soon as he comes, are the means for preventing danger and distress.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: सप्तर्षीन् पृष्ठतः कृत्वा युध्येयुरचला इव। अनेन विधिना शत्रून् जिगीषेतापि दुर्जयान्॥
en: Keeping the constellation called Ursa Major behind them, the troops should fight, standing firmly like hills. By this means, one may defeat even irresistible foes.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: यतो वायुर्यतः सूर्यो यतः शुक्रस्ततो जयः। पूर्वं पूर्वं ज्याय एषां संनिपाते युधिष्ठिर॥
en: The soldiers should be placed in such a position that the wind, the sun, and the planet Shukra should blow and shine from behind them. For acquiring victory, the wind is superior to the Sun, and the sun is superior to Shukra, O Yudhishthira.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: अकर्दमामनुदकाममर्यादामलोष्टकाम्। अश्वभूमि प्रशंसन्ति ये युद्धकुशला जनाः॥
en: Men who know the art of warfare approve of a region which is freed from mire, and which is to watery, not uneven, and not abounding with bricks and stone, as well fitted for the operations of cavalry.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: अपङ्का गर्तरहिता रथभूमिः प्रशस्यते। नीचगुमा महाकक्षा सोदका हस्तियोधिनाम्॥
en: A field which is free from mire and holes is best suited for car-warriors. A region which abounds with bushes and large trees and which is under water is suited for elephant warriors.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: बहुदुर्गा महाकक्षा वेणुवेत्रसमाकुला। पदातीनां क्षमा भूमिः पर्वतोपवनानि च॥
en: A region which has many inaccessible spots, which abounds with huge trees and cane bushes, as also a hilly or woody region, is well suiles for the work of infantry.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: पदातिबहुला सेना दृढा भवति भारत। रथाश्वबहुला सेना सुदिनेषु प्रशस्यते॥
en: An army, O Bharata, which has a large infantry, is considered very strong. An army which has a greater number of cars and horsemen is considered to be very powerful in a clear day.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: पदातिनागबहुला प्रावृट्काले प्रशस्यते। गुणानेतान् प्रसंख्याय देशकालौ प्रयोजयेत्॥
en: An army, again, which consists of a greater number of infantry and elephants becomes effective in the rains. Having carefully observed these points, the king should devote his attention to the characteristics of place and time.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: एवं संचिन्त्य यो याति तिथिनक्षत्रपूजितः। विजयं लभते नित्यं सेना सम्यक् प्रयोजयन्।
en: That king, who, having attended to all these points, marches, under a proper constellation and an auspicious luminary, always succeeds in acquiring victory by properly leading his troops.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: प्रसुप्तांस्तृषिताश्रान्तान् प्रकीर्णान् नाभिघातयेत्॥ मोक्षे प्रयाणे चलने पानभोजनकालयोः। अतिक्षिप्तान् व्यतिक्षिप्तान् निहतान् प्रतनूकृतान्॥ सुविश्रब्धान् कृतारम्भानुपन्यासान् प्रतापितान्। बहिश्चरानुपन्यासान् कृतवेश्मानुसारिणः॥ पारम्पर्यागते द्वारे ये केचिदनुवर्तिनः। परिचर्यावतो द्वारे ये च केचन वर्गिणः॥
en: No one should kill the sleepy, or the thirsty, or the fatigued, or one whose armours have fallen away, or one who has set his heart on final liberation, or one who is flying away, or one who is walking along a road, or one engaged in drinking or eating, or one who is mad, or one who is insane, or one who has been wounded morally, or one who has been greatly weakened by his wounds, or one who is residing confidentally, or one who has begun any task without having been able to finish it, or one who is a master of some particular art, or one who is in grief, or one who goes out of the camp for procuring forage or fodder, or men who pitch camps or are camp-followers, or those who wait at the gates of the king or of his ministers, or his menials, or the head of such servants.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: अनीकं ये विभिन्दन्ति भिन्न संस्थापयन्ति च। समानाशनपानास्ते कार्याः द्विगुणवेतनाः॥
en: Those of your warriors who break the ranks of enemies, or rally your retreating soldiers, should have their pay doubled and should be honoured by you with food, drink, and seats equal to your own.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: दशाधिपतयः कार्याः शताधिपतयस्तथा। ततः सहस्राधिपतिं कुर्याच्छूरमतन्द्रितम्॥
en: The heads of ten soldiers amongst them should be made heads of a hundred. And the careful hero who is the head of a hundred soldiers, should be made the head of a thousand.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: यथामुख्यान् संनिपात्य वक्तव्याः संशपामहे। विजयार्थं हि संग्रामे न त्यक्ष्यामः परस्परम्॥
en: Gathering together the leading warriors, they should be addressed, saying,-Let us swear to conquer, and never to leave one another!

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: इहैव ते निवर्तन्तां ये च केचन भीरवः। ये घातयेयुः प्रवरं कुर्वाणास्तुमुलं प्रति॥
en: Let those, who are afraid of their life, remain where they are. Let those also stay behind who would cause their chiefs to be killed by themselves neglecting to act heroically in the thick of the fray!

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: न संनिपाते प्रदरं वधं वा कुर्युरीदृशाः। आत्मानं च स्वपक्षं च पालयन् हन्ति संयुगे॥
en: Let such men only come as would never retreat from battle or cause their own comrades to be killed! Protecting their own selves as also their comrades, they are sure to kill the enemy in fight.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: अर्थनाशो वधोऽकीर्तिरयशच पलायने। अमनोज्ञासुखा वाचः पुरुषस्य पलायने॥ प्रतिध्वस्तोष्ठदन्तस्य न्यस्तसर्वायुधस्य च। अमित्रैरवरुद्धस्य द्विषतामस्तु नः सदा॥
en: The result of retreating from battle is loss of wealth, death, infamy, and reproach. Unpleasant, sharp and cutting remarks await the fate of him who retreats from battle, who lose his lips and teeth, who casts off all his weapons, or who allows himself to be taken as a captive by the enemy. Let such evil results always befall the warriors of our enemies.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: मनुष्यापसदा ह्येते ये भवन्ति पराङ्मुखा। राशिवर्धनमात्रास्ते नैव ते प्रेत्य नो इह॥
en: Those who retreat from battle are wretches among men. They simply increase the number of men. They will neither pass in this world nor in the next for true manhood.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: अमित्रा हृष्टमनसः प्रत्युद्यान्ति पलायिनम्। जयिनस्तु नरास्तात चन्दनैर्मण्डनेन च॥
en: Victorious enemies, O Sire, proceed gladly in pursuit of the flying combatants, their praises all the while recited by bards.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: यस्य स्म संग्रामगता यशो वै मन्ति शत्रवः। तदसह्यतरं दुःखमहं मन्ये वधादपि॥
en: When enemies, coming to battle spoil the fame of a person, the misery the latter feels is more piercing, I think, than that of death itself.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: जयं जानीत धर्मस्य मूलं सर्वसुखस्य च। या भीरूणां परा ग्लानिः शूरस्तामधिगच्छति॥
en: Know that victory is the source of religious merit and of every sort of happiness. The heroes bear cheerfully what is regarded as the highest misery by cowards.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: ते वयं स्वर्गमिच्छन्तः संग्रामे त्यक्तजीविताः। जयन्तो वध्यमाना वा प्राप्नुयाम च सद्गतिम्॥
en: Determined upon acquiring heaven we should fight not caring for life itself, and prepared to conquer or die, and we would attain then a blessed end in heaven!

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: एवं संशप्तशपथाः समभित्यक्तजीविताः। अमित्रवाहिनीं वीराः प्रतिगाहन्त्यभीरवः॥
en: Having taken such an oath, and prepared to cast away his itself, heroes should bravely rush against the enemy's ranks.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: अग्रतः पुरुषानीकमसिचर्मवतां भवेत्। पृष्ठतः शकटानीकं कलत्रं मध्यतस्तथा॥
en: In the van should be posted a detachment of men armed with swords and shields. In the rear should be planted the car-division. In the interstice should be placed other classes of warriors.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: परेषां प्रतिघातार्थं पदातीनां च बृंहणम्। अपि तस्मिन् पुरे वृद्धा भवेयुर्ये पुरोगमाः॥
en: This should be the arrangement for attacking the enemy. The veterans of the army should fight in the van. They would protect their comrades in the rear.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: ये पुरस्तादभिमताः सत्त्ववन्तो मनस्विनः। ते पूर्वमभिवर्तेरंश्चैतानेवेतरे जनाः॥
en: Those who are the foremost of strength and courage, should be placed in the van. The others should stand behind them.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: अपि चोद्धर्षणं कार्य भीरूणामपि यलतः। स्कन्धदर्शनमात्रात्तु तिष्ठेयुर्वा समीपतः॥
en: The fear-stricken should, with care, be comforted and encouraged. These weaker combatants should be placed on the field only to show the number of the army to the foe.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: संहतान् योधयेदल्पान् कामं विस्तारयेद् बहून्। सूचीमुखमनीकं स्यादल्पानां बहुभिः सह॥
en: If the troops are few, they should be arranged closely for the fight. When necessary, if their leader wishes, the close arrangement may be extended wide. When a small number of soldiers is to fight with a great many, they should be arranged like a needle-point.

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: सम्प्रयुक्ते निकृष्टे वा सत्यं वा यदि वानृतम्। प्रगृह्य बाहून् क्रोशते भग्ना भग्नाः परे इति॥
en: When a small army is engaged with a larger one, the leader of the former may shake hands with his men and cry aloud, saying,-The enemy is routed! The enemy is routed!

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: आगतं मे मित्रबलं प्रहरध्वमभीतवत्। सत्त्ववन्तोऽभिधावेयुः कुर्वन्तो भैरवान् रवान्॥
en: The strong amongst them should resist the enemy, loudly saying to their comrades, Fresh friends have arrived! Fearlessly strike at your enemies!

description: How should kings lead their armies in the battle-field
sn: क्ष्वेडा: किलकिलाशब्दाः क्रकचा गोविषाणिकाः। भेरीमृदङ्गपणवान नादयेयुः पुरश्चरान्॥
en: Those who have gone in advance should utter loud shouts and make various kinds of noises and should blow and beas Krakachas, cow-horns, drums, cymbals, and kettle-drums.'

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किंशीला: किंसमाचाराः कथंरूपाश्च भारत। किंसन्नाहाः कथंशस्त्रा जनाः स्युः संगरे क्षमाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Of what nature, of what conduct, of what form, how clad, and how armed should the warriors be in order that they may be competent for battle?

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: भीष्म उवाच यथाऽऽचरितमेवात्र शस्त्रं पत्रं विधीयते। आचाराद् वीरपुरुषस्तथा कर्मसु वर्तते॥
en: Bhishma said The soldier should use those weapons and cars with which they have become familiar by use. Taking those weapons and vehicles, brave soldiers, engage in battle.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: गान्धाराः सिन्धुसौवीरा नखर प्रासयोधिनः। अभीरवः सुबलिनस्तद्वलं सर्वपारगम्॥
en: The Gandharas, the Sindhus, and the Sauviras fight best with their nails and lances. They are brave and very strong. Their armies are capable of defeating all forces.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: सर्वशस्त्रेषु कुशलाः सत्त्ववन्तो ह्यशीनराः। प्राच्या मातङ्गयुद्धेषु कुशलाः कूटयोधिनः॥
en: The Ushinaras are endued with great strength and skilled in all sorts of weapons. The Easterners are skilled in fighting from the backs of elephants and are masters of all the ways of unfair fight.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: तथा यवनकाम्बोजा मथुरामभितश्च ये। एते नियुद्धकुशला दाक्षिणात्यासिपाणयः॥
en: The Yavanas, the Kamvojas, and those that live around Mathura are well skilled in fighting with bare arms. The Southerners are expert in fighting with bare arms. Southerners are expert in fighting swords in hand.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: सर्वत्र शूरा जायन्ते महासत्त्वा महाबलाः। प्राय एव समुद्दिष्टा लक्षणानि तु मे शृणु॥
en: It is well known that persons endued with great strength and great courage are born in almost every country. Listen to me as I describe their characteristics.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: सिंहशार्दूलवाड्नेत्राः सिंहशार्दूलगामिनः। पारावतकुलिङ्क्षाक्षाः सर्वे शूराः प्रमाथिनः॥
en: Those, who have voices and eyes like those of the lion or the tiger, those who have a gait like that of the lion and the tiger, and those who have eyes like those of the pigeon or of the snake, are all heroes capable of grinding the enemies.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: मृगस्वरा द्वीपिनेत्रा ऋषभाक्षास्तरस्विनः। प्रमादिनश्च मन्दाश्च क्रोधनाः किङ्किणीस्वनाः॥
en: Those, who have a voice like a deer, and eyes like those of the leopard or the bull, are highly active. Those, whose voice is like that of bells, are excitable, wicked, and wrathful.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: मेघस्वनाः क्रोधमुखाः केचित् करभसंनिभाः। जिह्मनासाग्रजिह्वाश्च दूरगा दूरपातिनः॥
en: Those, who have a voice deep like the muttering of the clouds, who have angry faces or faces like those of camels, those who have hooked noses and tongues, are gifted with great speed and can shoot or hurl their weapons to a great distance.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: शीघ्राश्चपलवृत्ताश्च ते भवन्ति दुरासदाः॥
en: Those, who have bodies curved like that of the cat, and thin hair and thin skin are gifted with great speed and restlessness, and are almost invincible in battle.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: गोधानिमीलिताः केचिन्मृदुप्रकृतयस्तथा। तरङ्गगतिनि?षास्ते नरा: पारयिष्णवः॥
en: Some who have eyes closed like those of iguana, a mild disposition and speed and voice like the horse's are capable to fight all enemies,

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: सुसंहताः सुतनवो व्यूढोरस्काः सुसंस्थिताः। प्रवादितेषु कुप्यन्ति हृष्यन्ति कलहेषु च॥ गम्भीराक्षा निःसृताक्षाः पिङ्गाक्षा भृकुटीमुखाः। नकुलाक्षास्तथा चैव सर्वे शूरास्तनुत्यजः॥
en: Those, who have well-formed, and symmetrical and beautiful bodies, and broad chests, who are irate upon hearing the enemy's drum or trumpet, who take delight in fights of every kind, who have eyes indicative of gravity, or eyes which seem to shoot out, or eyes which are green, those who have frowning faces, or eyes like those of the mongoose, are all brave and capable of sacrificing their lives in battle.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: जिह्माक्षाः प्रललाटाश्च निर्मांसहनवोऽपि च। वज्रबाहङ्गुलीचक्राः कृशा धमनिसंतताः॥ प्रविशन्ति च वेगेन साम्पराये छुपस्थिते। वारणा इव सम्मत्तास्ते भवन्ति दुरासदाः॥
en: Those, who have crooked eyes, and broad foreheads, and check-bones not fleshy, and arms strong as thunderbolts, and fingers bearing circular marks, and who are sparely built, and whose arteries and nerves are visible, rush with great impetuosity when the collision of battle takes place. Resembling angry elephants, they become irresistible.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: दीप्तस्फुटितकेशान्ता: स्थूलपार्श्वहनूमुखाः। उन्नतांसाः पृथुग्रीवा विकटाः स्थूलपिण्डिकाः॥ उद्धता इव सुग्रीवा विनताविहगा इव।। पिण्डशीर्षातिवक्त्राश्च वृषदंशमुखास्तथा॥ उग्रस्वरा मन्युमन्तो युद्धेष्वारावसरिणः। अधर्मज्ञावलिप्ताश्च घोरा रौद्रप्रदर्शनाः॥ त्यक्तात्मानः सर्व एते अन्त्यजा ह्यनिवर्तिनः। पुरस्कार्याः सदा सैन्ये हन्यन्ते मन्ति चापि ये॥
en: They who have greenish and curling hairs, who have flanks, cheeks, and faces fat and fleshy, who have elevated shoulders and broad necks, who have fearful faces and fat calves, who are fiery like the horse Sugriva or like the son of Garuda the son of Vinata, who have round heads, large mouths, faces like those of cats, shrill voice and angry temper, who rush to battle, impelled by its din, who are wicked and full of arrogance, who are of dreadful countenances, and who live in the outlying districts never care for their lives and do rever fly away from battle. Such troops should always be planted in the van. They always kill their foes in fight and suffer themselves to be killed without flying.

description: The conduct and dress of the warriors
sn: अधार्मिका भिन्नवृत्ताः सान्त्वेनैषां पराभवः। एवमेव प्रकुप्यन्ति राज्ञोऽप्येते ह्यभीक्ष्णशः॥
en: Of wicked conduct and foreign manners, they consider soft speeches as marks of defeat. If treated leniently, they always show anger against their sovereign.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच जयित्र्याः कानि रूपाणि भवन्ति भरतर्षभ। पृतनायाः प्रशस्तानि तानि चेच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said What are the well-known signs, O foremost of Bharata's race, of the future success of an army? I wish to know them.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: भीष्म उवाच जयित्र्या यानि रूपाणि भवन्ति भरतर्षभ। पृतनाया:प्रशस्तानि तानि वक्ष्यामि सर्वशः॥
en: Bhishma said I shall tell you, O foremost of Bharata's race, all the well-known marks of the (future) success of an army?

description: The signs of a future success
sn: दैवे पूर्वं प्रकुपिते मानुषे कालचोदिते। तद्विद्वांसोऽनुपश्यन्ति ज्ञानदिव्येन चक्षुषा॥ प्रायश्चित्तविधिं चात्र जपहोमांश्च तद्विदः। मङ्गलानि च कुर्वन्ति शमयन्त्यहितानि च॥
en: When the gods become angry and men are impelled by Destiny, learned persons, seeing cverything with the eye of divine knowledge, perform various auspicious acts and expiatory rites including Homa and the silent recitation of Mantras, and thus counteract all evils.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: उदीर्णमनसो योधा वाहनानि च भारत। यस्यां भवन्ति सेनायां ध्रुवं तस्यां परो जयः॥
en: That army in which the troops and the animals are all hearty and cheerful, O Bharata is sure to gain a decided success.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: अन्वेतान् वायवो यान्ति तथैवेन्द्रधनूंषि च। अनुप्लवन्तो मेघाश्च तथाऽऽदित्यस्य रश्मयः॥
en: The wind blows favourably from behind such troops. Rainbows appear in the sky. The clouds cast their shadows upon them and occasionally the sun shines upon them.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: गोमायवश्चानुकूला बलगृध्राश्च सर्वशः। अर्हयेयुर्यदा सेनां तदा सिद्धिरनुत्तमा।।७।
en: The jackals, ravens and vultures become auspicious to them. When these show such regard to the army, great success is sure to be achieved by it.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: प्रसन्नभाः पावकचोर्ध्वरश्मिः प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखो विधूमः। पुण्या गन्धाश्चाहुतीनां भवन्ति जयस्यैतद् भाविनो रूपमाहुः॥
en: Their sacrificial fires burn up with a pure splendour, the light going upwards and the smokeless flames slightly bending towards the south. The libations poured thereon send out a sweet smell. These are the marks of future success.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: गम्भीरशब्दाश्च महास्वनाश्च शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च नदन्ति यत्र। युयुत्सवश्चाप्रतीपा भवन्ति जयस्यैतद् भाविनो रूपमाहुः॥
en: The conchs and drums blown and beat, send forth loud and deep peals. The warriors become filled with confidence. These are the marks of future success.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: इष्टा मृगाः पृष्ठतो वामतश्च सम्प्रस्थितानां च गमिष्यतां चा जिघांसतां दक्षिणाः सिद्धिमार्छ ये त्वग्रतस्ते प्रतिषेधन्ति॥
en: If deer and other quadrupeds be seen behind or to the left of those that have already started for battle or of those that are about to start, they are regarded auspicious. If they appear to the right of the warriors about to engage in slaughter, it is considered as a mark of success. If, however, they appear in the van of such persons, they presage disaster and defeat.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: माङ्गल्यशब्दाशकुना वदन्ति हंसाः क्रौञ्चा: शतपत्राश्च चाषा:। हृष्टा योधाः सत्त्ववन्तो भवन्ति जयस्यैतद् भाविनो रूपमाहुः॥
en: If the birds, swans, cranes, Shatapatras and Chashas utter auspicious cries, and all the ablebodied warriors become cheerful, these are considered as marks of future success.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: शस्त्रैर्यन्त्रैः कवचैः केतुभिश्च सुभानुभिर्मुखवणैश्च यूनाम्। भ्राजिष्मती दुष्प्रतिवीक्षणीया येषां चमूस्तेऽभिभवन्ति शत्रून्॥
en: They, whose arrangement shines forth and becomes terrible to look at for the lustre of their weapons, machines, armour, and standards, as also for the shining hue of the faces of the strong men which compose it, always succeed in defeating their enemies.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: शुश्रूषवश्चानभिमानिनश्च परस्परं सौहृदमास्थिताश्च। येषां योधाः शौचमनुष्ठिताश्च जयस्यैतद् भाविनो रूपमाहुः॥
en: If the warriors of an army be of pure conduct and modest manner and treat one another with loving kindness, it is regarded as a mark of future success.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: शब्दाः स्पर्शास्तथा गन्धा विचरन्ति मनः प्रियाः। धैर्यं चाविशते योधान् विजयस्य मुखं च तत्॥
en: If sweet sounds and odours and sensations of touch prevail, and if the warriors are filled with gratitude and patience, it is regarded as the root of success.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: इष्टो वामः प्रविष्टस्य दक्षिणः प्रविविक्षतः। पश्चात्संसाधयत्यर्थं पुरस्ताच्च निषेधति॥
en: The crow on the left of person engaged in battle and on the right of him who is about to engage in it, is considered auspicious. Appearing at the back, it presages the nonfulfilment of the objects in view, while its appearance in the front indicates danger.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: सम्भृत्य महतीं सेनां चतुरङ्गां युधिष्ठिर। साम्नैव वर्तयेः पूर्वं प्रयतेथास्ततो युधि॥
en: Even after enlisting a large army consisting of the fourfold forces, you should, O Yudhishthira, first behave peacefully. If your attempts to secure peace fail, then you may engaged in battle.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: जघन्य एष विजयो यद् युद्धं नाम भारत। यादृच्छिकोयुधि जयो दैवो वेति विचारणम्॥
en: The victory, O Bharata, that one gains by battle is very inferior. Victory in battle, depends on caprice or destiny.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: अपामिव महावेगस्त्रस्ता इव महामृगाः। दुनिवार्यतमा चैव प्रभग्ना महती चमूः॥
en: When a large army is routed and the troops begin to fly away, it is highly difficult to restrain their flight. The force of the fight resembles that of a mighty current of water of a frightened herd of deer.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: भग्ना इत्येव भज्यन्ते विद्वांसोऽपि न कारणम्। उदारसारा महती रुरुसंघोपमा चमूः॥
en: Seeing some routed, others, even through they are brave and skilled in fight, break without sufficient cause. A larger army, consisting of brave soldiers, is like a large herd or Ruru deer.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: परस्परज्ञाः संहृष्टास्त्यक्तप्राणाः सुनिश्चिताः। अपि पञ्चाशतं शूरा निघ्नन्ति परवाहिनीम्॥
en: Sometimes it is seen that even fifty men, firm and relying upon one another, cheerful and prepared to sacrifice their lives, succeed in grinding enemies much superior to them in number.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: अपि वा पञ्च षट् सप्त संहताः कृतनिश्चयाः। कुलीनाः पूजिताः सम्यग् विजयन्तीह शात्रवान्॥
en: Sometimes even five, or six, or seven men, firm and standing close together, of high birth and esteemed of those that know them, defeat enemies much superior to them in number.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: संनियातो न मन्तव्यः शक्ये सति कथंचन। सान्त्वभेदप्रदानानां युद्धमुत्तरमुच्यते॥
en: The collision of battle is not at all desirable as long as it can be avoided. The policy of conciliation, of creating disunion, and making gifts should first be tried; battle, it is said, should take place after these.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: संदर्शेनैव सेनाया भयं भीरून् प्रबाधते। वज्रादिव प्रज्वलितादियं क्व नु पतिष्यति॥
en: On seeing a hostile army, fear paralyses the timid, as on seeing a thunderbolt they ask,-Oh upon what would it fall?

description: The signs of a future success
sn: अभिप्रयातां समितिं ज्ञात्वा ये प्रतियान्त्यथ। तेषां स्यन्दन्ति गात्राणि योधानां विजयस्य च।॥
en: Having determined that a battle is raging, the limbs of those that go to join it, as also of him that is conquering, are covered with perspiration.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: विषयो व्यथते राजन् सर्वः सस्थाणुजङ्गमः। अस्य प्रतापतप्तानां मज्जा सीदति देहिनाम्॥
en: The entire seat of war, O king, becomes agitated and afflicted, with all its mobile and immobile residents. The very marrow of creatures, scorched with the heat of weapons, languishes with pain.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: तेषां सान्त्वं क्रूरमिश्रं प्रणेतव्यं पुनः पुनः। सम्पीड्यमाना हि पर्योगमायान्ति सर्वतः॥
en: A king should, therefore, at all times, use the means of conciliation, accompanied with hard measures. When people are assailed by enemies they always display a tendency to come to terms.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: आन्तराणां च भेदार्थं चरानभ्यवचारयेत्। यश्च तस्मात् परो राजा तेन सन्धिः प्रशस्यते॥
en: Secret agents should be sent for creating disunion amongst the allies of the enemy. Having created disunion, it is very desirable that peace should then be made with that king who is more powerful than the enemy.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: न हि तस्यान्यथा पीडा शक्या कर्तुं तथाविधा। यथा सार्धममित्रेण सर्वतः प्रतिबाधनम्॥
en: If the invader does not act thus, he can never succeed in crushing his enemy completely. In dealing with the foe, care should be taken for attacking him from all sides.

description: The signs of a future success
