sn: क्षमा वै साधुमायाति न ह्यसाधूक्षमा सदा। क्षमायाश्चाक्षमायाश्च पार्थ विद्धि प्रयोजनम्॥
en: Forgiveness always comes to the good. It never comes to the bad. Listen now, O Partha, to the uses of forgiveness and of hardness.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: विजित्य क्षममाणस्य यशो राज्ञो विवर्धते। महापराधे हाप्यस्मिन् विश्वसन्त्यपि शत्रवः॥
en: The fame of a king who shows forgiveness after conquest spreads more widely. The very enemies of a forgiving person trust him even when he becomes guilty of a heinous crime.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: मन्यते कर्षयित्वा तु क्षमा साध्वीति शम्बरः। असंतप्तं तु यद् दारु प्रत्येति प्रकृति पुनः॥
en: Shamvara has said that having assailed an enemy, forgiveness should be shown afterwards, for a wooden pole, if made straight without heat, very soon assumes its former state.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: नैतत् प्रशंसन्त्याचार्या न च साधुनिदर्शनम्। अक्रोधेनाविनाशेन नियन्तव्याः स्वपुत्रवत्॥
en: Persons conversant with the scriptures do not, however, praise this. Nor do they consider this a characteristic of a good king. On the other hand, they say that an enemy should be subdued and restrained like a father subduing and checking a son, without anger and without killing him.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: द्वेष्यो भवति भूतानामुग्रो राजा युधिष्ठिर। मृदुमप्यवमन्यन्ते तस्मादुभयमाचरेत्॥
en: If, O Yudhishthira, a king becomes severe, he is hated of all creatures. If, on the other hand, he becomes mild, he is disregarded by all. Do you, therefore, practise both severity and mildness.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: प्रहरिष्यन् ब्रूयात् प्रहरन्नापि भारत। प्रहत्य च कृपायीत शोचन्निव रुदनिवा॥
en: Before striking, O Bharata, and while sticking, utter sweet words; and while striking, utter sweet words; and after having beaten them, show them mercy and let them understand that you are grieving and weeping for them.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: न मे प्रियं यनिहताः संग्रामे मामकैनरैः। न च कुर्वन्ति मे वाक्यमुच्यमानाः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Having defeated an army, the king should address the survivors saying-I am not at all glad that so many have been killed by my men. Alas, the latter, through repeatedly dissuaded by me, have not obeyed my orders.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: अहो जीवितमाकाक्षेन्नेदृशो वधमर्हति! सुदुर्लभाः सुपुरुषाः संग्रामेष्वपलायिनः॥
en: I wish they were all alive. They do not deserve such death. They were all good and sincere men, and unretreating from battle. Such inan, indeed, are rare.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: कृतं ममाप्रियं तेन येनायं निहतो मधे। इति वाचा वदन् हन्तुन् पूजयेत रहोगतः॥
en: He that has killed such a hero in battle, has surely done that which I do not like.-Having said so before the survivors of the defeated enemy, the king should in secret honour those amongst his own troops that have bravely killed the foe.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: हन्तृणामाहतानां च यत् कुर्युरपराधिनः। क्रोशेद् बाहुं प्रगृह्यापि चिकीर्षन् जनसंग्रहम्॥
en: For comforting the wounded slayers for their sufferings at the hand of enemy, the king, desirous of securing their devotion to himself, should even weep, catching their hands affectionately.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: एवं सर्वास्ववस्थासु सान्त्वपूर्वं समाचरेत्। प्रियो भवति भूतानां धर्मज्ञो वीतभीनृपः॥
en: The king should thus, under all circumstances, behave with conciliation. A fearless and virtuous king, is loved by all creatures.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: विश्वासं चात्र गच्छन्ति सर्वभूतानि भारत। विश्वस्तः शक्यते भोक्तुं यथाकाममुपस्थितः॥
en: All creatures also, O Bharata, trust such a king. Winning their confidence, he succeeds in enjoying the Earth as he pleases.

description: The signs of a future success
sn: तस्माद् विश्वासयेद् राजा सर्वभूतान्यमायया। सर्वतः परिरक्षेच्च यो महीं भोक्तुमिच्छति॥
en: The king should, therefore, by casting off deceitfulness, seek to secure the confidence of all creatures. He should also try to protect his subjects from all fears if he seeks to enjoy the Earth.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं मृदौ कथं तीक्ष्णे महापक्षे च पार्थिव। आदौ वर्तेत नृपतिस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, how should a king treat a mild foe, one who is fierce, and one who has many allies and a large army.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। बृहस्पतेश्च संवादमिन्द्रस्य च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: 'Regarding it is cited, O Yudhishthira the old discourse between Brihaspati and Indra.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: बृहस्पति देवपतिरभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः। उपसंगम्य पप्रच्छ वासवः परवीरहा।॥
en: Once on a time, that destroyer of hostile heroes, viz., Vasava, the king of the gods, joining his hands, approached Brihaspati, and saluting him, said these words.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: इन्द्र उवाच अहितेषु कथं ब्रह्मन् प्रवर्तेयमतन्द्रितः। असमुच्छिद्य चैवैतान् नियच्छेयमुपायतः॥
en: Indra said How, O twice-born one, should I treat my enemies? How should I subdue them by various contrivances, without rooting them out?

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: सेनयोर्व्यतिषङ्गेण जयः साधारणो भवेत्। किंकुर्वाणं न मां जह्याज्ज्वलिता श्रीः प्रतापिनी॥
en: In a collision between two arinies, victory may be achieved by either side. In what way should I behave so that this shining prosperity that I have acquired and that scorches all my enemies, may not leave me?

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: ततो धर्मार्थकामानां कुशलः प्रतिभानवान्। राजधर्मविधानज्ञः प्रत्युवाच पुरंदरम्॥
en: Thus addressed, Brihaspati, skilled in Virtue, Profit, and Pleasure, endued with a knowledge of royal duties, and great intelligence, answered Indra as follows.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच न जातु कलहेनेच्छेन्नियन्तुमपकारिणः। बालैरासेवितं ह्येतद् यदम! यदक्षमा॥
en: One should never wish to vanquish his enemies by quarrel. Worked up with anger and shom of forgiveness, boys only seek quarrel.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: न शत्रुर्विवृतः कार्यो वधमस्याभिकाङ्गता। क्रोधं भयं च हर्षं च नियम्य स्वयमात्मनि॥
en: One who wishes for the destruction of a foe, should not make that foe careful. On the other hand, one should never display one's anger or fear or joy. He should conceal these within his own heart.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: अमित्रमुपसेवेत विश्वस्तवदविश्वसन्। प्रियमेव वदेन्नित्यं नाप्रियं किंचिदाचरेत्॥
en: Without trusting one's foe in reality, one should treat him in such a way as if he trusted him completely. One should always speak sweet words to one's enemies and never do anything that is disagreeable.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: विरमेच्छुष्कवैरेभ्यः कण्ठायासांश्च वर्जयेत्। यथा वैतंसिको युक्तो द्विजानां सदृशस्वनः॥ तान् द्विजान् कुरुते वश्यांस्तथा युक्तो महीपतिः। वशं चोपनयेच्छन् निहन्याच्च पुरंदर॥
en: One should avoid useless acts of hostility as also insolent speech. As a fowler, carefully uttering cries like those of the birds he wishes to catch, or destroy, captures and brings them under his control, even so should a king, O Purandara, bring his enemies under subjection and then kill them if he likes.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: न नित्यं परिभूयारीन् सुखं स्वपिति वासव। जागर्येव हि दुष्टात्मा संकरेऽग्निरिवोत्थितः॥
en: Having defeated one's enemies, one should not sleep at ease. A wicked enemy rises up against like a fire carelessly extinguished reappearing itself.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: न संनिपातः कर्तव्यः सामान्ये विजये सति। विश्वास्यैवोपसन्नार्थो वशे कृत्वा रिपुः प्रभो॥
en: When victory may be achieved by either side, a hostile collision of arms should be avoided. Having made an enemy feel security, one should subdue him and active one's end.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: सम्प्रधार्य सहामात्यैर्मन्त्रविद्भिर्महात्मभिः। उपेक्ष्यमाणोऽवज्ञातो हृदयेनापराजितः॥ अथास्य प्रहरेत् काले किंचिद्विचलिते पदे। दण्डं च दूषयेदस्य पुरुषैराप्तकारिभिः॥
en: Having consulted his ministers and intelligent persons conversant with policy, an enemy that is disregarded and neglected, never owning submission at heart, strikes the disregarder at the proper season, especially when the latter takes a false step. By engaging trustworthy agents of his own, such an enemy would also make the other's forces inefficient by creating disunion.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: आदिमध्यावसानज्ञः प्रच्छन्नं च विधारयेत्। बलानि दूषयेदस्य जानन्नेव प्रमाणतः॥ भेदेनोपप्रदानेन संसृजेदौषधैस्तथा। न त्वेवं खलु संसर्गं रोचयेदरिभिः सह॥
en: Knowing the beginning, the middle, and the end of his enemy, a king should secretly entertain feelings of hostility towards them. He should corrupt the forces of his enemy, determine everything by positive evidence, creating disunion, making gifts, and administering poison. A king should never live with his foes.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: दीर्घकालमपीक्षेत निहन्यादेव शात्रवान्। कालाकाङ्क्षीहि क्षपयेद् यथा विश्रम्भमाप्नुयुः॥ न सद्योऽरीन् विहन्याच्च द्रष्टव्यो विजयो ध्रुवः।
en: A king should wait long and then kill his enemies. Indeed, he should wait, for the opportunity, so that he might attack his enemy at a time when the latter would not expect him in the least. A king should never kill a large number of the enemy's army, although he should certainly do that which would secure him decisive victory.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: न शल्यं वा घटयति न वाचा कुरुते व्रणम्॥ प्राप्ते न प्रहरेत् काले न च संवर्तते पुनः। हन्तुकामस्य देवेन्द्र पुरुषस्य रिपून् प्रति॥
en: The king should never do such an injury to his enemy as would remain in the latter's heart. Nor should he afflict him with wordy darts and arrows. If the opportunity comes, he should strike him, without letting it slip. In this way, O king of the gods, should a king, desirous of killing his foes, treat them.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: यो हि कालो व्यतिक्रामेत् पुरुषं कालकाक्षिणम्। दुर्लभः स पुनस्तेन कालः कर्मचिकीर्षुणा॥
en: If an opportunity, with respect to the man who waits for it, once goes away it can never be secured again by the person desirous of acting.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: ओजश्च जनयेदेव संगृह्णन् साधुसम्मतम्। अकाले साधयेन्मित्रं न च प्राप्ते प्रपीडयेत्॥
en: Acting according to the advice of the wise, a king should only break the strength of his enemy. He should never, when the opportunity is not favourable, try to achieve his end. Nor should he, when the opportunity arises, persecute his enemy.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: विहाय कामं क्रोधं च तथाहंकारमेव च। युक्तो विवरमन्विच्छेदहितानां पुनः पुनः॥
en: Giving up lust, anger and pride, the king should carefully and continually watch for the shortcomings of his foes,

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: मार्दवं दण्ड आलस्यं प्रमादश्च सुरोत्तम। मायाः सुविहिताः शक्र सादयन्त्यविचक्षणम्॥
en: His own mildness, the hardship of his punishments, his inactivity and carelessness. O king of the gods, and the deceitful means well applied (by his foes), ruin a foolish king.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: निहत्यैतानि चत्वारि मायां प्रति विधाय च। ततः शक्नोति शत्रूणां प्रहर्तुमविचारयन्॥
en: That king who can overcome these four shortcomings and counteract the deceitful expedients of his enemies, succeeds, forsooth, in smiting them all.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: यदैवैकेन शक्येत गुह्यं कर्तुं तदाचरेत्। यच्छन्ति सचिवा गुह्यं मिथो विश्रावयन्त्यपि॥
en: When only one minister is capable to perform a secret object, the king should consult with that one minister only regarding such secret object. Many ministers, if consulted, try to throw the burden of the task upon the another's shoulders and even give out that object which should be kept close.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: अशक्यमिति कृत्वा वा ततोऽन्यैः संविदं चरेत्। ब्रह्मदण्डमदृष्टेषु दृष्टेषु चतुरङ्गिणीम्॥
en: If consultation with one is not proper, then only should the king consult with many. When enemies are not seen, he should invoke divine punishment upon them; when seen, the army, consisting of fourfold forces, should be set in motion.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: भेदं च प्रथमं युज्यात् तूष्णीं दण्डं तथैव च। काले प्रयोजयेद् राजा तस्मिंस्तस्मिंस्तदा तदा॥
en: The king should first use the means of creating disunion, as also those of conciliation. When the time for each particular means arrives, that particular expedient should be made use of.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: प्रणिपातं च गच्छेत काले शत्रोर्बलीयसः। युक्तोऽस्य वधमन्विच्छेदप्रमत्तः प्रमाद्यतः॥
en: Occasionally the king should even prostrate himself before a powerful enemy. It is again desirable that acting with every care, he should try to bring about the victor's destruction when the latter becomes careless.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: प्रणिपातेन दानेन वाचा मधुरया ब्रूवन्। अमित्रमपि सेवेत न च जातु विशङ्कयेत्।।३
en: By prostrating one's self, by giving tribute, by uttering sweet words, one should humble one's self before a more powerful king. One should never do anything that may create the suspicions of one's powerful enemy.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: स्थानानि शङ्कितानां च नित्यमेव विवर्जयेत्। न च तेष्वाश्वसेद् राजा जाग्रतीह निराकृताः॥
en: The weaker king should, under such circumstances, carefully avoid every act that may create suspicion. A victorious king, again, should not trust his defeated enemies, for the vanquished always remain alert.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: न ह्यतो दुष्करं कर्म किंचिदस्ति सुरोत्तमा यथा विविधवृत्तानामैश्वर्यममराधिप।॥
en: There is nothing, O best of gods, that is more difficult to be done than the acquisition of prosperity, O king of gods, by restless persons.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: तथा विविधवृत्तानामपि सम्भव उच्यते। यतते योगमास्थाय मित्रामित्रं विचारयेत्॥
en: The very existence of restless persons is dangerous. Kings should, therefore, with minute attention, determine their friends, and enemies.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: मृदुमप्यवमन्यन्ते तीक्ष्णादुद्विजते जनः मा तीक्ष्णो मा मृदुर्भूस्त्वं तीक्ष्णो भव मृदुर्भव॥
en: A mild king is always disregarded. If he becomes fierce, i.e., strikes people with fear. Therefore do not be fierce. Do not, again, be mild. But be both fierce and mild.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: यथा वप्रे वेगवति सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके। नित्यं विवरणाद् बाधस्तथा राज्यं प्रमाद्यतः॥
en: As a rapid current ceaselessly washes away the high bank and causes large landslips, so carelessness and mistake bring about the ruination of a kingdom.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: न बहूनभियुञ्जीत यौगपद्येन शात्रवान्। साम्ना दानेन भेदेन दण्डेन च पुरंदर॥ एकैकमेषां निष्पिष्य शिष्टेषु निपुणं चरेत्। न तु शक्तोऽपि मेधावी सर्वानेवारभेन्नृपः॥
en: Never attack many enemies simultaneously. By using the means of conciliation, or of gift, or of creation of disunion. O Purandara, they should be assailed one by one. The victor may treat peacefully the remnant. An intelligent king, even if competent for it, should not begin to crush all simultaneously.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: यदास्यान्महती सेना हयनागरथाकुला। पदातियन्त्रबहुला अनुरक्ता षडगिनी॥ यदा बहुविधां वृद्धिं मन्येत प्रतिलोमतः। तदा विवृत्य प्रहरेद् दस्यूनामविचारयन्॥
en: When a king happens to have a large army consisting of sixfold forces and enough of horse, elephant, cars, foot, and engines, all devoted to him, when he thinks himself superior to his enemies in many respects upon a fair comparison, then should he openly strike the enemy without hesitation.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: न सामदण्डोपनिषत् प्रशस्यते न मार्दवं शत्रुषु यात्रिकं सदा। न सस्यघातो न च संकरक्रिया न चापि भूयः प्रकृतेर्विचारणा॥
en: If the enemy be strong, the adoption of a policy of conciliation is not good. On the other hand, punishment by secret means should be inflicted. Such enemies shouid not be treated mildly, repeated attacks, destruction of crops, poisoning of wells and tanks, and suspicion regarding the seven branches of administration, should be made.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: मायाविभेदानुपसर्जनानि तथैव पापं न यशःप्रयोगात्। आप्तैर्मनुष्यरूपचारयेत पुरेषु राष्ट्रेषु च सम्प्रयुक्तान्॥
en: The king should, on such occasions, adopt various kinds of deception, various expedients for setting his foes against one another, and various kinds of hypocrisy. He should also, through trusted agents, learn the doings of his enemies in their cities and provinces.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: पुरापि चैषामनुसृत्य भूमिपाः पुरेषु भोगानखिलान् जयन्ति। पुरेषु नीति विहितां यथाविधि प्रयोजयन्तो बलवृत्रसूदन॥
en: Kings, O killer of Vala and Vritra, pursuing their enemies and entering their towers, seize and appropriate the best things that are to be had there, and adopt proper measures of policy in their own cities and dominions.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: प्रदाय गूढानि वसूनी राजन् प्रच्छिद्य भोगानवधाय च स्वान्। दुष्टान् स्वदोषैरिति कीर्तयित्वा पुरेषु राष्ट्रेषु च योजयन्ति॥
en: Presenting them wealth privately, and confiscating their properties publicly, without, however, injuring them materially, and proclaiming that they are all wicked men who have suffered for their own misdeeds, kings should despatch their agents to the cities and provinces of their enemies.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: तथैव चान्यैरपि शास्त्रवेदिभिः स्वलंकृतैः शास्त्रविधानदृष्टिभिः। सुशिक्षितैर्भाष्यकथाविशारदैः परेषु कृत्यामुपधारयेच्च॥
en: At the same time, in their own cities, they should, through other persons well-read in scriptures, endued with every accomplishment, acquainted with the injunctions of the sacred books; and possessed of learning, cause incantations, and foe-destroying rites to be performed.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: इन्द्र उवाच कानि लिङ्गानि दुष्टस्य भवन्ति द्विजसत्तम। कथं दुष्टं विजानीयामेतत् पृष्टो वदस्व मे॥
en: What are the marks, O best of the twiceborn, of a wicked person! Accosted by me, tell me how am I to know who is wicked!

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच परोक्षमगुणानाह सद्गुणानभ्यसूयते। परैर्वा कीर्त्यमानेषु तूष्णीमास्ते पराङ्मुखः॥
en: Brihaspati said A wicked person is he who speaks of the faults of others at their back, who is filled with envy on seeing the accomplishments of others, and who remains silent when the merits of other people are described before him, being most unwilling to join them.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: तूष्णीम्भावेऽपि विज्ञेयं न चेद्भवति कारणम्। निःश्वासं चोष्ठसंदंशं शिरसश्च प्रकम्पनम्॥
en: Mere silence is no mark of wickedness on such occasions. A wicked person breathes heavily, bites his lips, and snakes his head.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: करोत्यभीक्ष्णं संसृष्टमसंसृष्टश्च भाषते। अदृष्टितो न कुरुते दृशे नैवाभिभाषते॥
en: Such a person always mixes in society and talks irrelevantly. Such a man never does what he promises, when the person to whom he has given the assurance does not observe him. When this man observes him, the wicked man does not even refer to the subject.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: पृथगेत्य समश्नाति नेदमद्य यथाविधि। आसने शयने याने भावा लक्ष्या विशेषतः॥
en: The wicked man eats alone, and finds fault with the food placed before him, saying.-All is not right to-day, as before. His true nature comes out when sitting, lying down, and riding.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: आर्तिराते प्रिये प्रीतिरेतावन्मित्रलक्षणम्। विपरीतं तु बोद्धव्यमरिलक्षणमेव तत्॥
en: Lamenting in times of sorrow and rejoicing in times of joy are the marks of a friend, Contrary actions from the indications of an enemy.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: एतान्येव यथोक्तानि बुध्येथास्त्रिदशाधिप। पुरुषाणां प्रदुष्टानां स्वभावो बलवत्तरः॥
en: Keep in your heart these sayings, O king of the gods! The nature of wicked men can never be concealed.

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: इति दुष्टस्य विज्ञानमुक्तं ते सुरसत्तम। निशम्य शास्त्रतत्त्वार्थं यथावदमरेश्वर॥
en: I have now told you, O foremost of gods, what are the marks of a wicked person. Having listened to the truths given but in the scriptures, follow them duly, O king of the gods!

description: How should a king treat his enemies
sn: भीष्म उवाच स तद्वचः शत्रुनिबर्हणे रत स्तथा चकारावितथं बृहस्पतेः। चचार काले विजयाय चारिहा वशं च शत्रूननयत् पुरंदरः॥
en: Bhishma said Having heard these words of Brihaspati, Purandara, engaged in defeating his foes, followed them strictly. Bent upon victory, that destroyer of foes, when the opportunity came, followed these instructions and subdued all his enemies!'

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धार्मिकोऽर्थानसम्प्राप्य राजामात्यैः प्रबाधितः। च्युतः कोशाच्च दण्डाच्च सुखमिच्छन् कथं चरेत्॥
en: How should a righteous king, who is proposed by his own officers whose treasury and army are not under his control, and who has no wealth, act for acquiring happiness?"

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्रायं क्षेमदर्शीय इतिहासोऽनुगीयते। तत् तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर।॥
en: Bhishma said “Regarding it the story of Kshemadarshin is often related. I shall describe that story to you. Listen to it, O Yudhishthira.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: क्षेमदर्शी नृपसुतो यत्र क्षीणबलः पुरा। मुनि कालकवृक्षीयमाजगामेति नः श्रुतम्। तं पप्रच्छानुसंगृह्य कृच्छ्रामापदमास्थितः॥
en: We have heard that in days of yore, when prince Kshemadarshin had become weak in strength and fallen into great distress, he went to the sage Kalakavrikshiva and saluting him humbly, said him these words,

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: राजोवाच अर्थेषु भागी पुरुष ईहमानः पुनः पुनः। अलब्ध्वा मद्विधो राज्यं ब्रह्मन् किं कर्तुमर्हति॥ अन्यत्र मरणाद् दैन्यादन्यत्र परसंश्रयात्। क्षुद्रादन्यत्र चाचारात् तन्ममाचक्ष्व सत्तम॥
en: What should a person like me who is worthy to have wealth, but who has, after repeated attempts, failed to regain his kingdom, do, O Brahmana, excepting suicide, thieving and robbery, secking refuge with others, and other acts of meanness of a similar nature? O best of men, tell me this.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: व्याधिना चाभिपन्नस्य मानसेनेतरेण वा। धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च त्वद्विधः शरणं भवेत्॥
en: One like you who are conversant with morality and full of gratefulness is the refuge of a person suffering from disease mental or physical.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: निर्विद्यति नरः कामानिर्विद्य सुखमेधते। त्यक्त्वा प्रीतिं च शोकं च लब्ध्वा बुद्धिमयं वसु॥
en: Man should renounce his desires. By acting in that way, by casting off joy and sorrow, and acquiring the wealth of knowledge, he succeeds in acquiring happiness.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: सुखपाश्रयं येषामनुशोचामि तानहम्। मम ह्यर्थाः सुबहवो नष्टाः स्वप्न इवागताः॥
en: I am sorry for them who follow worldly happiness accruing from wealth. All that, however, disappears like a dream.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: दुष्करं बत कुर्वन्ति महतोऽस्त्यिजन्ति ये। वयं त्वेतान् परित्यक्तुमसतोऽपि न शक्नुमः॥
en: They who can renounce vast wealth achieve a most difficult task. As for ourselves we are unable to renounce that wealth which exists no longer.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: इमामवस्थां सम्प्राप्तं दीनमार्तं श्रिया च्युतम्। यदन्यत् सुखमस्तीह तद् ब्रह्मन्ननुशाधि माम्॥
en: I am shorn of prosperity and have been reduced to a miserable and unhappy plight! Instruct me, O Brahmana, what happiness I may yet try to secure.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: कौसल्येनैवमुक्तस्तु राजपुत्रेण धीमता। मुनिः कालकवृक्षीयः प्रत्युवाच महाद्युतिः॥
en: Thus accosted by the intelligent prince of Koshala, the sage Kalakavrikshiya gave the following answer,

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: मुनिरुवाच पुरस्तादेव ते बुद्धिरियं कार्या विजानता। अनित्यं सर्वमेवैतदहं च मम चास्ति यत्॥
en: The sage said-You have, it appears, already understood it. Endued with knowledge as you are, you should act as you think. Your belief is correct, namely,-All this that I see is brittle, myself as also everything that I have!

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: यत् किंचिन्मन्यसेऽस्तीति सर्वं नास्तीति विद्धि तत्। एवं न व्यथते प्राज्ञः कृच्छ्रामप्यापदं गतः॥
en: Know, O prince, that those things which you consider as existing do not in reality exist. The wise know this very well, and are, therefore, never pained with the distress whatever that may be.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: यद्धि भूतं भविष्यं च सर्वं तन्न भविष्यति। एवं विदितवेद्यस्त्वमधर्मेभ्यः प्रमोक्ष्यसे॥
en: What has taken place and what will bring to pass are all unreal, When you will know this which should be known by all, you will be shorn of unrighteousness.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: यच्च पूर्वं समाहारे यच्च पूर्वं परे परे। सर्वं तन्नास्ति ते चैव तज्ज्ञात्वा कोऽनुसंज्वरेत्॥
en: Whatever things had been acquired by those that came before, and whatever acquired by their successors, have all perished. Thinking of all this, who is there that will give way to grief?

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: भूत्वा च न भवत्येतदभूत्वा च भविष्यति। शोके न ह्यस्ति सामर्थ्यं शोकं कुर्यात् कथंचन॥
en: Things that were, are no more. Things that are, will again be no more. Grief cannot restore them. One should not, therefore, succumb to grief.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: क्व नु तेऽद्य पिता राजन् क्व नु तेऽद्य पितामहः। न त्वं पश्यसि तानद्य न त्वां पश्यन्ति तेऽपि च॥
en: Where, O king, is your father to-day and where your grandfather? To-day you see them not, nor do they now see you!

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: आत्मनोऽध्रुवतां पश्यंस्तांस्त्वं किमनुशोचसि। बुद्ध्या चैवानुबुद्ध्यस्व ध्रुवं हि न भविष्यसि॥
en: Meditating on your own instability, why do you grieve for them? Think with the help of your intelligence, and you will understand that you will cease to be!

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अहं च त्वं च नृपते सुहृदः शत्रवश्च ते। अवश्यं न भविष्यामः सर्वं च न भविष्यति॥
en: Myself, yourself, O king, your friends, and your foes, shall forsooth, cease to be. Indeed, everything will cease to be.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: ये तु विंशतिवर्षा वै त्रिंशद्वर्षाश्च मानवाः। अर्वागेव हि ते सर्वे मरिष्यन्ति शरच्छतात्॥
en: Those men who are now twenty or thirty years old, will, forsooth, all die within the next hundred years.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अपि चेन्महतो वित्तान्न प्रमुच्येत पूरुषः। नैतन्ममेति तन्मत्वा कुर्वीत प्रियमात्मनः॥
en: If a man cannot willingly relinquish his immense wealth, he should then try to think that his belongings, are not his own and by that means seek to do good to himself.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अनागतं यन्न ममेति विद्यादतिक्रान्तं यन्न ममेति विद्यात्। दिष्टं बलीय इति मन्यमार्ना स्ते पण्डितास्तत्सतां स्थानमाहुः॥
en: Future acquisitions should be considered by one as not one's own. Lost properties, should also be regarded by one as not his own. Destiny should be deemed as all powerful. They who think in this wise are considered wise. This mood of regarding all things is an attribute of the good.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अनाढ्याश्चापि जीवन्ति राज्यं चाप्यनुशासति। बुद्धिपौरुषसम्पन्नास्त्वया तुल्याधिका जनाः॥
en: Many persons who are equal of superior to you in intelligence and inanliness, though bereft of wealth, are not kings but are still alive.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: न च त्वमिव शोचन्ति तस्मात् त्वमपि मा शुचः। किं न त्वं तैनरैः श्रेयांस्तुल्यो वा बुद्धिपौरुषैः॥
en: They are not, like you. They do not indulge in grief like you. Therefore, ceases to grieve in this wise! Are you not superior to those men, or at least equal to them in intelligence and inanliness?

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: राजोवाच यादृच्छिकं सर्वमासीत् तद् राज्यमिति चिन्तये। ह्रियते सर्वमेवेदं कालेन महता द्विज॥
en: The king said I consider the kingdom which I had with all its parapharnalia to have been acquired by me without any exertion. Omnipotent Time, however, twice-born one, has swept it away.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: तस्यैव ह्रियमाणस्य स्त्रोतसेव तपोधन। फलमेतत् प्रपश्यामि यथालब्धेन वर्तयन्॥
en: The result, however, that I see, of my kingdom having been carried away by Time as by a stream, is that I am obliged to subsist upon whatever I get as alms.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: मुनिरुवाच अनागतमतीतं च याथातथ्यविनिश्चयात्। नानुशोचेत कौसल्य सर्वार्थेषु तथा भव॥
en: The sage said Actuated by the knowledge of what is true, one should never grieve for either the past or the future. Be you of such a mood of mind, o prince of Koshala, regarding every affair that may arrest your attention!

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अवाप्यान् कामयन्नर्थान् नानवाप्यान् कदाचन प्रत्युत्पन्नाननुभवनं मा शुचस्त्वमनागतान्॥
en: Wishing to possess only that which is obtainable and not what is unobtainable, do you enjoy your present belongings and never grieve for what is absent.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: यथालब्धोपपन्नाथस्तथा कौसल्य रंस्यसे। कच्चिच्छुद्धस्वभावेन श्रिया हीनो न शोचसि॥
en: Be you satisfied, O prince of Koshala, with whatever you can easily get. Even if divested of prosperity, do not grieve for it but try to maintain a pure character.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: पुरस्ताद् भूतपूर्वत्वाद्धीनभाग्यो हि दुर्मतिः। धातारं गर्हते नित्यं लब्धार्थश्च न मृष्यते॥
en: Only an unfortunate and foolish wight when divested of former prosperity, blames the supreme Ordainer, without being contented with his present position.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अनर्हानपि चैवान्यान्मन्यते श्रीमतो जनान्। एतस्मात् कारणादेतद् दुःखं भूयोऽनुवर्तते॥ ईर्ष्याभिमानसम्पत्रा राजन् पुरुषमानिनः। कच्चित् त्वं न तथा राजन् मत्सरी कोसलाधिप।॥
en: Such a person consider others however undeserving, as men blessed with prosperity. Therefore, those who are possessed of malice and vanity and puffed up with a sense of egoism, suffer more misery still. You however, O king, are not sullied by such vices.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: सहस्व श्रियमन्येषां यद्यपि त्वयि नास्ति सा। अन्यत्रापि सती लक्ष्मी कुशला भुञ्जते सदा॥
en: Bear the prosperity of others, inspite of your being divested of the same. Clever and expert men succeed in enjoying the prosperity of their enemies.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: श्रियं च पुत्रपौत्रं च मनुष्या धर्मचारिणः। योगधर्मविदो धीराः स्वयमेव त्यजन्त्युत॥
en: Prosperity relinquishes the person that hates others. Pious and wise men conversant with the duties of Yoga renounce prosperity and sons and grandsons of their own accord.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: बहुसंकुसुकं दृष्ट्वा विधित्सासाधनेन च। तथान्ये संत्यजन्त्येव मत्वा परमदुर्लभम्॥
en: Others, considering earthly possessions to be exceedingly unstable and unobtainable, and dependent upon continued exertion, are also scen to renounce it.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: त्त्वं पुनः प्राज्ञरूप: सन् कृपणं परितप्यसे। अकाम्यान् कामयानोऽर्थान् पराधीनानुपद्रवान्॥
en: You seem to be endued with wisdom. Why, then, do you grieve so piteously, seeking for things which should not be sought for, since they are unstable and dependent on others?

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: तां बुद्धिमुपजिज्ञासुस्त्क्मेवैतान् परित्यज। अनर्थाश्चार्थरूपेण ह्यश्चानर्थरूपिणः॥
en: You wish to know the temperament of mind which would give you happiness. The advice I give you is to renounce all objects of desire! Objects which should be discarded appear to one as those which he should seek to secure, while those which should be secured appear to him as objects which should be avoided.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अर्थायैव हि केषांचिद् धननाशो भवत्युत। आनन्त्यं तत्सुखं मत्वा श्रियमन्यः परीप्सति॥
en: Some loss their wealth while seeking the same. Others consider wealth, as the source of endless happiness, and, therefore pursue it eagerly.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: रममाणः श्रिया कश्चिन्नान्यच्छ्रेयोऽभिमन्यते। तथा तस्येहमानस्य समारम्भो विनश्यति॥
en: Some again, overjoyed with wealth, think that there is nothing superior to it. While cagerly seeking for the acquisition of wealth, such a person loses all other objects of life. renounce

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: कृच्छाल्लब्धमभिप्रेतं यदि कौसल्य नश्यति। तदा निर्विद्यते सोऽर्थात् परिभग्नक्रमो नरः॥
en: If, O prince of Koshala, a person loses that wealth which had been acquired with difficulty and after which he had hankered, he then, overcome by despair, gives up all desire of wealth.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: धर्ममेकेऽभिपद्यन्ते कल्याणाभिजना नराः। परत्र सुखमिच्छन्तो निर्विद्येयुश्च लौकिकात्॥
en: Some righteous and highly-born persons devote themselves to the acquisitions of virtue. These every king of worldly happiness from securing the same in the other world.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: जीवितं संत्यजन्त्येके धनलोभपरा जनाः। न जीवितार्थं मन्यन्ते पुरुषा हि धनादृते॥
en: Some persons sacrifice life itself, actuated by the desire of acquiring wealth. These do not think that life without wealth has any use.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: पश्य तेषां कृपणतां पश्य तेषामबुद्धिताम्। अध्रुवे जीविते मोहादर्थदृष्टिमुपाश्रिताः॥
en: Mark at their pitiable condition! Witness their foolishness! When life is so short and uncertain, these men, actuated by ignorance, seek wealth.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: संचये च विनाशान्ते मरणान्ते च जीवित। संयोगे च वियोगान्ते को नु विप्रणयेन्मनः॥
en: Who is there that would busy himself with boarding when destruction is its end, hanker after life when death is its end, and after union when separation is its end?

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: धनं वा पुरुषो राजन् पुरुषं वा पुनर्धनम्। अवश्यं प्रजहात्येव तद् विद्वान् कोऽनुसंज्वरेत्॥ अन्येषामपि नश्यन्ति सुहृदश्च धनानि च।
en: Sometimes man renounces wealth, and sometimes wealth renounces man. What man endued with knowledge is there who would grieve at the loss of wealth? There are many other persons in the world who lose wealth and friends.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: पश्य वुद्ध्या मनुष्याणां राजन्नापदमात्मनः॥ नियच्छ यच्छ संयच्छ इन्द्रियाणि मनो गिरम्।
en: See, O king, with your intelligence, and you will come to learn that the calamities which befall men are all owing to their own conduct! Do you, therefore, control your senses, mind and speech.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: प्रतिषेद्धा न चाप्येषु दुर्बलेष्वहितेष्वपि॥ प्राप्तिसृष्टेषु भावेषु व्यपकृष्टेष्वसम्भवे। प्रज्ञानतृप्तो विक्रान्तस्त्वद्विधो नानुशोचति॥
en: For, if these become weak and productive of evil there is no man who can stand aloof from temptation of external objects by which he is always surrounded. As no one can from a good idea of the past nor of the future, there being many intervals of time and place, a person like you who are endued with such wisdom and such prowess, never grieve for union and separation, for good or evil.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अल्पमिच्छन्नचपलो मृदुर्दान्तः सुनिश्चितः। ब्रह्मचर्योपपन्नश्च त्वद्विधो नैव शोचति॥
en: A person so mild by nature, of controlled self, and settled conclusions, and observant of Brahmacharya vows, never grieve and never becomes restless from the desire of acquiring from the fear of losing anything insignificant.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: न त्वेव जाल्मी कापाली वृत्तिमेषितुमर्हसि। नृशंसवृत्तिं पापिष्ठां दुष्टां कापुरुषोचिताम्॥
en: It is not proper that such a man should follow a deceitful life of mendicancy, a life that is sinful and wicked and cruel and which benefits only a human wretch.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अपि मूलफलाजीवो रमस्वैको महावने। वाग्यतः संगृहीतात्मा सर्वभूतदयान्वितः॥
en: Do you go to the great forest and lead a life of happiness there, all alone and subsisting upon fruits and roots, restraining words and soul, and filled with mercy for all creatures.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: सदृशं पण्डितस्यैतदीषादन्तेन दन्तिना। यदेको रमतेऽरण्येष्वारण्ये नैव तुष्यति॥
en: Or He, who cheerfully leads such a life in the forest, having elephants of large tusks for companions, with no human being by his side, and contented with the produce of the forest, is said to follow the footsteps of the wise.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: महाह्रदः संक्षुभित आत्मनैव प्रसीदति। एतदेवंगतस्याहं सुखं पश्यामि जीवितुम्॥
en: A large lake, when it becomes disturbed, becomes silent itself. Likewise, a wise men, when disturbed in such matters, becomes tranquil of himself. I see that a person, who has been reduced to such a plight as yours, may live happily even thus.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: असम्भवे श्रियो राजन् हीनस्य सचिवादिभिः। दैवे प्रतिनिविष्टे च किं श्रेयो मन्यते भवान्॥
en: When it is impossible for you to recover your prosperity and when you are without ministers and counsellors, such a course is open to you. Do you expect to reap any benefit by depending upon destiny?

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: मुनिरुवाच अथ चेत् पौरुषं किंचित् क्षत्रियात्मनि पश्यसि। ब्रवीमि तां तु ते नीति राज्यस्य प्रतिपत्तये।।।।
en: If, on the other hand, O Kshatriya, you think that you still possess any prowess, I shall describe to you about that line of policy which you may follow for recovering your kingdom.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: तां चेच्छक्नोषि निर्मातुं कर्म चैव करिष्यसि। शृणु सर्वमशेषेण यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: If you can adopt that policy and try to exert yourself, you can still regain your prosperity. Listen attentively to all that I say to you fully.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: आचरिष्यसि चेत् कर्म महतोऽर्थानवाप्स्यसि। राज्यं राज्यस्य मन्त्रं वा महतीं वा पुनः श्रियम्॥ अथैतद् रोचते राजन् पुनर्वृहि ब्रवीमि ते।
en: If you act according to those counsels, you may acquire immense wealth, your kingdom and kingly power and great prosperity. If you like it, O king, tell me, for then I shall describe to you that policy.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: राजोवाच ब्रवीतु भगवान्नीतिमुपपन्नोऽस्म्यहं प्रभो॥ अमोघोऽयं भवत्वद्य त्वया सह समागमः।
en: The king said Tell me, O holy one, what you wish to say. I am willing to hear and act according to your advice. Let this my meeting with you to-day produce mighty results.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: मुनिरुवाच हित्वा दम्भं च कामं च क्रोधं हर्ष भयं तथा॥ अप्यमित्राणि सेवस्व प्रणिपत्य कृताञ्जलिः।
en: Casting off pride, desire, anger and joy and fear, wait upon your very foes, humbling yourself and joining your hands.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: तमुत्तमेन शौचेन कर्मणा चाभिधारय॥ दातुमर्हति ते वित्तं वैदेहः सत्यसंगरः।
en: Do you wait upon Janaka the king of Mithila, always performing good and pure acts. The highly truthful king of Videha will, forsooth, give you great wealth.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: प्रमाणं सर्वभूतेषु प्रग्रहं च भविष्यसि॥ ततः सहायान् सोत्साहान् ल्लप्स्यसेऽव्यसनाशुचीन्।
en: You will then become the right arm of that king and secure the confidence of all persons. As an outcome of this, you will win over many courageous and persevering allies, pure in behaviour, and free from the seven cardinal faults.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: वर्तमानः स्वशास्त्रेण संयतात्मा जितेन्द्रियः॥ अभ्युद्धरति चात्मानं प्रसादयति च प्रजाः।
en: By following his duties, à person of subdued self and having his senses under control, succeeds in raising himself and cheering others.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: तेनैवत्व धृतिमता श्रीमता चाभिसत्कृतः॥ प्रमाणं सर्वभूतेषु गत्वा च ग्रहणं महत्।
en: Honoured by Janaka enducd with intelligence and prosperity, you will certainly become the right hand of that king and enjoy the confidence of all.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: ततः सुहृद्बलं लब्ध्वा मन्त्रयित्वा सुमन्त्रिभिः॥ आन्तरैर्भेदयित्वारीन् बिल्वं बिल्वेन भेदय। परैर्वा संविदं कृत्वा बलमप्यस्य घातय॥
en: Having then mustered a large force and held consultations with good ministers, do you create dissensions among your enemies, and setting them against one another, break them all like a person breaking a Vilva with a Vilva. Or, making peace with the enemies of your foe, destroy the latter's power.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अलभ्या ये शुभा भावाः स्त्रियश्चाच्छादनानि च। शय्यासनानि यानानि महार्हाणि गृहाणि च॥ पक्षिणो मृगजातानि रसगन्धः फलानि च। तेष्वेव सज्जयेथास्त्वं यथा नश्यत्वयं परः॥
en: You will then cause your enemies to be attached to such good things as are not easily · got at, to beautiful women and clothes, beds and seats and cars, all very costly, and houses, and birds and animals of various species, and juices and perfumes and fruits, so that your foe may be ruined of himself.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: यद्येवं प्रतिषेद्धव्यो यापेक्षणमर्हति। न जातु विवृतः कार्यः शत्रुः सुनयमिच्छता॥
en: If one's enemy be thus managed, or if he is treated in differently, one, who wishes to act according to good policy, should never allow that foe to know it at all.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: रमस्व परमामित्रे विषये प्राज्ञसम्मतः। भजस्व श्वेतकाकीयैर्मित्रधर्ममनर्थकैः॥
en: Following the conduct approved of the wise, do you enjoy every king of pleasure in the territories of your enemy, and imitating the conduct of the dog, the deer and the crow, be outwardly a friend to your enemies.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: आरम्भांश्चास्य महतो दुश्चरांश्च प्रयोजय। नदीवच्च विरोधांश्च बलवद्भिर्विरुध्यताम्॥
en: Make them undertake works which are difficult of accomplishment. See also that they enter into hostilities with powerful enemies.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: उद्यानानि महार्हाणि शयनान्यासनानि च। प्रतिभोगसुखेनैव कोशमस्य विरेचय॥
en: Making them attached to pleasure gardens and rich beds and seats, do you, by offering such objects of enjoyment, exhaust your eneiny's treasury.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: यज्ञदाने प्रशाध्यस्मै ब्राह्मणाननुवर्ण्य तान्। ते त्वां प्रतिकरिष्यन्ति तं भोक्ष्यन्ति वृका इव॥
en: Advising your enemy to celebrate sacrifices and making gifts, do you please the Brahmanas. The latter will do good to you in return, and devour your enemy like wolves.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: असंशयं पुण्यशीलः प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम्। त्रिविष्टपे पुण्यतमं स्थानं प्राप्नोति मानवः॥
en: Forsooth, a person of righteous deeds acquires a high end. By such deeds men earn highly happy regions in heaven.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: कोशक्षये त्वमित्राणां वशं कौसल्य गच्छति। उभयत्र प्रयुक्तस्य धर्मेणाधर्म एव च।॥ फलार्थमूलं व्युच्छिद्येत् तेन नन्दन्ति शत्रवः। न चास्मै मानुषं कर्म दैवमस्योपवर्णय॥
en: If the treasury of your foes be exhausted, every one of them, O prince of Koshala, may be subdued. The treasury is the source of happiness in heaven and victory on Earth. It is in consequence of their wealth that enemies enjoy such happiness. The treasury, therefore, should by every means be drained. Do not speak highly of manliness in the presence of your foe, but speak highly of destiny.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: असंशयं दैवपरः क्षिप्रमेव विनश्यति। याजयैनं विश्वजिता सर्वस्वेन वियुज्य तम्॥
en: Forsooth, the man who depends too much on acts of worship of the gods soon meets with ruin. Making your enemy perform the great sacrifice called Vishvajit and divest him by that means of all his wealth.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: ततो गच्छसि सिद्धार्थः पीड्यमानं महाजनम्। योगधर्ममिदं पुण्यं कंचिदस्योपवर्णयेत्॥
en: Through this your object object will be accomplished. You may then inform your enemy of the fact that the best men in his kingdom are being oppressed, and point out some great asceit a master of Yoga.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: अपि त्यागं बुभूषेत कच्चिद् गच्छेदनामयम्। सिद्धेनौषधियोगेन सर्वशत्रुविनाशिना। नागानश्वान् मनुष्यांश्च कृतकैरुपघातयेत्॥
en: Your enemy will then desire to adopt renunciation and retire into the woods seeking liberation. You will then, with the help of drugs prepared by boiling highly efficacious herbs and plants, and of artificial salts, kill the elephants and horses and men.

description: The duties of a king who is opposed by his own officers
sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो दम्भयोगाः सुचिन्तिताः। शक्या विषहता कर्तुं पुरुषेण कृतात्मना॥
en: These and the many other well-laid plans exist, but they are all connected with fraud. An intelligent person can thus destroy the denizens of a hostile kingdom with poison,

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: राजोवाच न निकृत्या न दम्भेन ब्रह्मन्निच्छामि जीवितुम्। नाधर्मयुक्तानिच्छेयमर्थान् सुमहतोऽप्यहम्॥
en: I do not wish, O Brahmana, to support life by deceit or fraud. I do not seek wealth, however profuse, which is to be acquired by unfair means.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: पुरस्तादेव भगवन् मयैतदपवर्जितम्। येन मां नाभिशङ्केत येन कृत्स्नं हितं भवेत्॥ आनृशंस्येन धर्मेण लोके ह्यस्मिन् जिजीविषुः। नाहमेतदलं कर्तुं नैतत् त्वय्युपपद्यते॥
en: In the very beginning of our present discourse I excepted these means. By adopting only such means as would not incur censure, such means as would benefit me in every respect, by doing only such acts as are not harmful, I wish to live in this world! I cannot follow these ways which you point out to me! Indeed, these instructions do not become you!

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: मुनिरुवाच उपपन्नस्त्वमेतेन यथा क्षत्रिय भाषसे। प्रकृत्या ह्युपपन्नोऽसि बुद्ध्या वा बहुदर्शनः॥
en: The sage said-These words, O Kshatriya. which you give vent to, point you out as a pious men. Indeed, you are pious by nature and understanding, O you of great experience.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: उभयोरेव वामर्थे यतिष्ये तव तस्य च। संश्लेषं वा करिष्यामि शाश्वतं पनपायिनम्॥
en: I shall try for the good of you both. I shall create a union, between you and that king, which should be eternal and cannot be broken.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: त्वादृशं कि कुले जातमनृशंसं बहुश्रुतम्। अमात्यं को न कुर्वीत राज्यप्रणयकोविदम्॥
en: Who is there that would not like to have a minister like you who are born of a noble family, who abstain from all unfair acts and cruelties, who are highly learned, and who are well versed in the art of government and of conciliation.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: यस्त्वं प्रच्यावितो राज्याद् व्यसनं चोत्तमं गतः। आनृशंस्येन वृत्तेन क्षत्रियेच्छसि जीवितुम्॥
en: I say this, O Kshatriya, because, though bereft of kingdom and plunged into great distress, still you wish to follow a pious course.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: आगन्ता मद्गहं तात वैदेहः सत्यसंगरः। अथाहं तं नियोक्ष्यामि तत् करिष्यत्यसंशयम्॥
en: The king of the Videhas, ever devoted to truth, will come to my residence soon. For sooth, he will do what I will request him to do.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: तत आहूय वैदेहं मुनिर्वचनमब्रवीत्। अयं राजकुले जातो विदिताभ्यन्तरो मम॥
en: Bhishma said Thereafter, inviting the king of the Videhas, the sage said these words to him,-This person is of royal birth. I know his very heart.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: आदर्श इव शुद्धात्मा शारदश्चन्द्रमा यथा। नास्मिन् पश्यामि वृजिनं सर्वतो मे परीक्षितः॥
en: His soul is as pure as the surface of a mirror or the disc of the autumnal moon. He has been perfectly examined by me. I do not see any shortcoming in him.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: तेन ते संधिरेवास्तु विश्वसास्मिन् यथा मयि। न राज्यमनमात्येन शक्यं शास्तुमपि त्र्यहम्॥
en: Let there be friendship between him and you. Do you place confidence in him as in myself. A king who has no capable minister cannot govern his kingdom even for three days.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: अमात्यः शूर एव स्याद् बुद्धिसम्पन्न एव वा। ताभ्यां चैवोभयं राजन् पश्य राज्यप्रयोजनम्॥
en: The minister should be brave and highly intelligent. By these two qualities one may conquer both the worlds. Mark, O king, these two qualities well, since they are necessary for governing a kingdom.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: धर्मात्मनां क्व चिल्लोके नान्यास्ति गतिरीदृशी। महात्मा राजपुत्रोऽयं सतां मार्गमनुष्ठितः॥
en: Pious kings have no such refuge as a minister endued with such attributes. This great person is of royal birth. He always treads the path of the righteous.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: सुसंगृहीतस्त्वेवैष त्वया धर्मपुरोगमः। संसेव्यमानः शत्रूस्ते गृह्णीयान्महतो गणान्॥
en: This one, who always follows righteousness, has been a valuable acquisition. If treated by you with respect, he will subdue your enemies.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: यद्ययं प्रतियुद्ध्येत् त्वां स्वकर्म क्षत्रियस्य तत्। जिगीषमाणस्त्वां युद्धे पितृपैतामहे पदे॥ त्वं चापि प्रतियुद्ध्येथा विजिगीषुव्रते स्थितः। अयुध्वैव नियोगान्मे वशे कुरु हिते स्थितः॥
en: If he engages in battle with you, he will do what as a Kshatriya he should do. Indeed, if, following the conduct of his ancestors, he fights for conquering you, it will be your duty to fight him, for as a Kshatriya it is your duty to conquer antagonists. Without engaging in battle, however, do you, at my behest, employ him under you from desire of benefiting yourself.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: स त्वं धर्ममवेक्षस्व हित्वा लोभमसाम्प्रतम्। न च कामान्न च द्रोहात् स्वधर्मं हातुमर्हसि॥
en: Have your eyes on righteousness, casting off covetousness. You should not abandon the duties of your order from lust or from desire of battle.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: नैव नित्यं जयस्तात नैव नित्वं पराजयः। तस्माद् भोजयतिव्यश्च भोक्तव्यश्च परो जनः॥
en: Victory, O sire, is not certain. Defeat also is not certain. Knowing this, peace should be made with an cnemy by giving him food and other things of enjoyment.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: आत्मन्यपि च संदृश्यावुभौ जयपराजयौ। निःशेषकारिणां तात निःशेषकरणाद् भयम्॥
en: One may witness victory and defeat his own case. They, who seek to root out an cnemy, are sometimes exterminated themselves in their endeavours!

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचेदं वचनं ब्राह्मणर्षभम्। प्रतिपूज्याभिसत्कृत्य पूजार्हमनुमान्य च॥ यथा ब्रूयान्महाप्राज्ञो यथा ब्रूयान्महाश्रुतः। श्रेयस्कामो यथा ब्रूयादुभयोरेव तत् क्षमम्॥ यद् यद् वचनमुक्तोऽस्मि करिष्यामि च तत् तथा। एतद्धि परमं श्रेयो न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा॥
en: Thus accosted, king Janaka, properly saluting and honouring that foremost of Brahınanas worthy of every honour, replied to him, saying,-You are highly learned and wise. What you have said from desire of benefiting us, is certainly advantageous for both of us. Such a course of conduct is highly beneficial to us. I do not hesitate to say this!

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: ततः कौसल्यमाहूय मैथिलो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। धर्मतो नीतितश्चैव लोकश्च विजितो मया॥
en: Then, addressing the prince of Koshala, the king of Videha said these words,-Following Kshatriya duties as also with the help of policy, I have conquered the world.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: अहं त्वया चात्मगुणैर्जितः पार्थिवसत्तम। आत्मानमनवज्ञाय जितवद् वर्ततां भवान्॥
en: I have, however, O best of kings, been conquered by you with your good qualities. Without feeling any sense of humiliation, live you with me as a victor.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: नावमन्यामि ते बुद्धिं नावमन्ये च पौरुषम्। नावमन्ये जयामिति जितवद् वर्ततां भवान्।॥
en: I honour you intelligence, and I honour your power. I do not disregard you, saying that I have conquered you. On the other hand, live you with me as a victor.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: यथावत् पूजितो राजन् गृहं गन्तासि मे भृशम्। ततः सम्पूज्य तौ विप्रं विश्वस्तौ जग्मतुर्ग्रहान्॥
en: Honoured duly by me, o king, you will go to my house-Both the kings then adored that Brahmana, and trusting each other, proceeded to the capital of Mithila.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: वैदेहस्त्वथ कौसल्यं प्रवेश्य गृहमञ्जसा। पाद्यार्घ्यमधुपर्केस्तं पूजाहँ प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: Making the prince of Koshala enter his house, the king of the Videhas honoured hiin, who was worthy of every honour, with offerings of water to wash his feet, honey and curds and the usual articles.

description: The advice of Janaka to king of Kosala
sn: ददौ दुहितरं चास्मै रत्नानि विविधानि च। एष राज्ञां परो धर्मोऽनित्यौ जयपराजयौ॥
en: King Janaka also conferred upon his guest his own daughter and various kinds of gems and jewels. This is the greatest duty of king; victory and defeat are both uncertain."

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परंतप। धर्मवृत्तं च वित्तं च वृत्त्युपायाः फलानि च॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have, O scorcher of foes, described the duties, the general conduct, the means of sustenance, with their results, of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: राज्ञां वित्तं च कोशं च कोशसंचयनं जयः। अमात्यगुणवृत्तिश्च प्रकृतीनां च वर्धनम्॥ पाड्गुण्यगुणकल्पश्च सेनावृत्तिस्तथैव च। परिज्ञानं च दुष्टस्य लक्षणं च सतामपि॥ समहीनाधिकानां च यथावल्लक्षणं च यत्। मध्यमस्य च तुष्ट्यर्थं यथा स्थेयं विवर्धता॥ क्षीणग्रहणवृत्तिश्च यथाधर्मं प्रकीर्तितम्। लघुना देशरूपेण ग्रन्थयोगेन भारत॥
en: You have described also the duties of kings, and discoursed on their treasures, the means of filling them, and on the subject of conquest and victory. You have also described the characteristics of ministers, the measures that secure the prosperity of the subjects, the characteristics of the six limbs of a kingdom, the qualities of armies, the means of marking out the wicked, and the marks of the good, the attributes of those that are equal, those that are inferior, and those that are superior, the conduct which a king seeking selfaggrandisement should follow towards the masses, and the manner in which the weak should be protected and cherished. You have described all these subjects, O Bharata, delivering instructions sanctioned by the scriptures.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: विजिगीषोस्तथा वृत्तमुक्तं चैव तथैव ते। गणानां वृत्तिमिच्छामि श्रोतुं मतिमतां वर॥
en: You have also described the conduct that should be followed by kings desirous of conquering their enemies. I desire now, O foremost of intelligent men, to hear how should a person treat the number of brave men (vassals) that gather round a king.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: यथा गणाः प्रवर्धन्ते न भिद्यन्ते च भारत। अरींश्च विजिगीषन्ते सुहृदः प्राप्नुवन्ति च।॥
en: I wish to hear how they may advance, how they may be attached to the person of the king, and how, O Bharata, they may subduing foes gain friends.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: भेदमूलो विनाशो हि गणानामुपलक्षये। मन्त्रसंवरणं दुःखं बहूनामिति मे मतिः॥
en: It appears to me that disunion alone can encompass their destruction. I think it is always difficult to keep counsels close when there are many in the assemblage.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं निखिलेन परंतप। यथा च ते न भिद्येरंस्तच्च मे वद पार्थिव॥
en: I desire to hear ail this fully, O scorcher of foes. Tell me also, O king, the means by which they may not happen to quarrel with the king."

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: भीष्म उवाच गणानां च कुलानां च राज्ञां भरतसत्तम। वैरसंदीपनावेतौ लोभामर्षी नराधिप।॥
en: Bhishma said "O king, avarice and anger between nobles and the kings create enmity.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: लोभमेको हि वृणुते ततोऽमर्षमनन्तरम्। तौ क्षयव्ययसंयुक्तावन्योन्यं च विनाशिनौ॥
en: The king yields to avarice. And, therefore, anger takes possession of the other. Each bent upon weakening and wasting the other, they both meet with destruction.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: चारमन्त्रबलादानैः सामदानविभेदनैः। क्षयव्ययभयोपायैः प्रकर्षन्तीतरेतरम्॥
en: By engaging spies, instruments of policy, and physical force, and adopting the means of conciliation, gifts, and dissension, and applying other methods for producing weakness, waste, and fear, the parties attack each other.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: तत्रादानेन भिद्यन्ते गणाः संघातवृत्तयः। भिन्ना विमनसः सर्वे गच्छन्त्यरिवशं भयात्॥
en: The aristocracy of a kingdom in a body becoine alienated from the king, if the latter seeks to exact too much from them. Alienated from the king, all of them become dissatisfied, and from fear join the enemies of the king.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: भेदे गणा विनेशुर्हि भिन्नास्तु सुजयाः परैः। तस्मात् संघातयोगेन प्रयतेरन् गणा: सदा॥
en: If again the aristocracy of a kingdom are divided, they meet with destruction. Disunited, they are easily ruined by their foes. The nobles, therefore, should always act unitedly.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: अर्थाश्चैवाधिगम्यन्ते संघातबलपौरुषैः। बाह्याश्च मैत्री कुर्वन्ति तेषु संघातवृत्तिषु॥
en: If they be united together, they may acquire valuable properties by means of their strength and prowess. When they are thus united, many people from outside seek their alliance.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: ज्ञानवृद्धाः प्रशंसन्ति शुश्रूषन्तः परस्परम्। विनिवृत्ताभि संधानाः संखमेधन्ति सर्वशः॥
en: Wise people speak highly of those nobles who are united with one another in ties of love. If of one purpose, all of them can be happy.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: धर्मिष्ठान् व्यवहारांश्च स्थापयन्तश्च शास्त्रतः। यथावत् प्रतिपश्यन्तो विवर्धन्ते गणोत्तमाः॥
en: They can establish fairness of conduct. By behaving properly, they grow prosperous.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: पुत्रान् भ्रातृन् निगृह्णन्तो विनयन्तश्च तान् सदा। विनीतांश्च प्रगृह्णन्तो विवर्धन्ते गणोत्तमाः॥
en: By restraining their sons and brothers and instructing them in their duties, and treating all persons kindly whose pridc has been subdued by knowledge, the aristocracy grow prosperous.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: चारमन्त्रविधानेषु कोशसंनिचयेषु च। नित्ययुक्ता महाबाहो वर्धन्ते सर्वतो गणाः॥
en: By always engaging spies and concerting measures of policy, and filling up their treasuries, the aristocracy, O you of mighty arms, grow prosperous.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: प्राज्ञाशूरान् महोत्साहान् कर्मसु स्थिरपौरुषान्। मानयन्तः सदा युक्ता विवर्धन्ते गणा नृप॥
en: By receiving properly those who are endued with wisdom, courage and perseverance and who show steady prowess in all kinds of work, the aristocracy grow prosperous.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: द्रव्यवन्तश्च शूराश्च शस्त्रज्ञाः शास्त्रपारगाः। कृच्छ्रास्वापत्सु सम्मूढान् गणाः संतारयन्ति ते॥
en: Having wealth and resources, and mastcred the scriptures and all the arts and sciences, the aristocracy rescue the ignorant masses from all sorts of distress and danger,

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: क्रोधो भेदो भयं दण्डः कर्षणं निग्रहो वधः। नयत्यरिवशं सद्यो गणान् भरतसत्तम॥
en: King's anger, disunion with him, terror, punishment, persecution, oppression, and executions, O chief of the Bharatas, quickly alienate the aristocracy from the king and make them side with kings' enemies.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: तस्मान्मानयितव्यास्ते गणमुख्याः प्रधानतः । लोकयात्रा समायत्ता भूयसी तेषु पार्थिव॥
en: Therefore, the leaders of the aristocracy should be honoured by the king. The affairs of the kingdom, o king, depend greatly upon them.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: मन्त्रगुप्तिः प्रधानेषु चारश्चामित्रकर्षण। न गणाः कृत्स्नशो मन्त्रं श्रोतुमर्हन्ति भारत॥
en: Consultations should be held with the leaders of the aristocracy, and secret agents should be engaged, O crusher of foes, to watch them. The king should not, O Bharata, consult with every member of the aristocracy.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: गणमुख्यैस्तु सम्भूय कार्यं गणहितं मिथः! पृथग्गणस्य भिन्नस्य विततस्य ततोऽन्यथा॥
en: Acting jointly with the leaders, the king, should do what is for the behoof of the whole order. When, however, the aristocracy are divided and disunited and have no leaders, other courses of action should be followed,

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: अर्थाः प्रत्यवसीदन्ति तथाना भवन्ति च। तेषामन्योन्यभिन्नानां स्वशक्तिमनुतिष्ठताम्॥
en: If the members of the aristocracy fall out with one another and act, each according to his means, without unity, their prosperity disappears and diverse sorts of evil occur.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: निग्रहः पण्डितैः कार्यः क्षिप्रमेव प्रधानतः। कुलेषु कलहा जाताः कुलवृद्धैरुपेक्षिताः॥ गोत्रस्य नाशं कुर्वन्ति गणभेदस्य कारकम्।
en: The leaned and wise amongst them should put down a dispute as soon as it takes place. Indeed, if the elders of a family grow indifferent, quarrels break out amongst the members. Such quarrels bring about the ruin of a family and create disunion among the nobles.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: आभ्यन्तरं भयं रक्ष्यमसारं बाह्यतो भयम्॥ आभ्यन्तरं भयं राजन् सद्यो मूलानि कृन्तति।
en: Protect yourself, O king, from all internal fears. External fears, however, are not very important. The first kind of fear, O king, may cut your roots in a single day.

description: How should a king treat his allies
sn: अकस्मात् क्रोधमोहाभ्यां लोभाद् वापि स्वभावजात्।। अन्योन्यं नाभिभाषन्ते तत्पराभवलक्षणम्। जात्या च सदृशाः सर्वे कुलेन सदृशास्तथा॥ न चोद्योगेन बुद्ध्या वा रूपद्रव्येण वा पुनः। तस्मात् संघातमेबाहुर्गणानां शरणं महत्॥
en: Persons who are equal in family and blood, under the influence of anger, folly and covetousness cease to speak with one another. This is an indication of defeat. It is not by courage, nor intelligence, nor by beauty, nor by riding, that enemies can destroy the aristocracy. It is only by disunion and gifts that it can be brought to subjugation. Therefore, union is the greatest refuge of the aristocracy.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच महानयं धर्मपथो बहुशाखश्च भारत। किंस्विदेवेह धर्माणामनुष्ठेयतमं मतम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said The path of duty in long. It has also, O Bharata, many branches. What are those duties which you hold to be the best to practise.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: किं कार्यं सर्वधर्माणां गरीयो भवतो मतम्। यथाहं परमं धर्ममिह च प्रेत्य चाप्नुयाम्॥
en: What are the most important duties in your view by the practice of which I may acquire the highest merit both in this world and in the next.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: भीष्म उवाच मातापित्रोर्गुरूणां च पूजा बहुमता मम। इह युक्तो नरो लोकान् यशश्च महदश्नुते॥
en: Bhishma said The adoration of mother, father, and preceptor is, I consider, the most important. The man, who satisfies that duty here, succeeds in winning great fame and many blessed regions.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: यच्च तेऽभ्यनुजानीयुः कर्म तात सुपूजिताः। धर्माधर्मविरुद्धं वा तत् कर्तव्यं युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Adored by you, whatever they will command you, be it consistent with righteousness, or be it inconsistent with it, you should carry it out unhesitatingly, O Yudhishthira.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: न च तैरभ्यनुज्ञातो धर्ममन्यं समाचरेत्। यं च तेऽभ्यनुजानीयुः स धर्म इति निश्चयः॥
en: One should never do what they forbid. Forsooth, there command should always be done.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: एत एव त्रयो लोका एत एवाश्रमास्त्रयः। एत एव त्रयो वेदा एत एव त्रयोऽग्नयः॥
en: They are the three worlds. They are the three modes of life. They are the three Vedas. They are the three sacred fires.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: पिता वै गार्हपत्योऽग्निर्दक्षिणः स्मृतः। गुरुराहवनीयस्तु साग्नित्रेता गरीयसी॥ त्रिष्वप्रमाद्यन्नेतेषु त्रील्लोकांश्च विजेष्यसि।
en: The father is said to be the Garhapatya fire; the mother, the Dakshina fire; and the preceptor is the fire upon which libations are poured. These three fires are, of course, the greatest. If you adore carefully these three fires, you will conquer the three worlds.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: पितृवृत्त्या त्विमं लोकं मातृवृत्त्या तथा परम्॥ ब्रह्मलोकं गुरोर्वृत्त्या नियमेन तरिष्यसि।
en: By serving the father regularly one may cross this world. By serving the mother in the same way, one may enjoy blessed regions in the next. By serving the preceptor regularly, one may acquire the region of Brahma.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: सम्यगेतेषु वर्तस्व त्रिषु लोकेषु भारत॥ यशः प्राप्स्यसि भद्रं ते धर्मं च सुमहत्फलम्।
en: Properly treat these three, O Bharata, you will then acquire great fame in the three worlds, and be you blessed, great will be your merit and reward.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: नैतानतिशयेज्जातु नात्यश्नीयान्न दूषयेत्॥ नित्यं परिचरेच्चैव तद् वै सुकृतमुत्तमम्।
en: Never transgress them in your deeds. Never eat before they eat, nor eat any thing that is better than what they eat. Never attribute any fault to them. One should always serve them humbly. That is an act of great merit.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: कीर्तिं पुण्यं यशो लोकान् प्राप्स्यसे राजसत्तम॥ सर्वे तस्यादृता लोका यस्यैते त्रय आदृताः।
en: By acting thus, O best of kings, you may acquire fame, merit, honour, and blessed regions hereafter. He, who honours these three is honoured of all the worlds.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: अनादृतास्तु यस्यैते सर्वास्तस्याफलाः क्रियाः॥ न चायं न परो लोकस्तस्य चैव परंतप।
en: He, however, who disregards these three, cannot acquire any merit from any of his acts. Such a man, O scorcher of foes, neither obtains this would nor the next.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: अमानिता नित्यमेव यस्यैते गुरवस्त्रयः॥ न चास्मिन्नपरे लोके यशस्तस्य प्रकाशते। न चान्यदपि कल्याणं परत्र समुदाहृतम्॥
en: He, who always disregards these three elders never enjoys fame either in this world or in the next. Such a man never reaps any good in the next world.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: तेभ्य एव हि यत् सर्वं कृत्वा च विसृजाम्यहम्। तदासीन्मे शतगुणं सहस्रगुणमेव च॥ तस्मान्मे सम्प्रकाशन्ते त्रयो लोका युधिष्ठिर।
en: All that I have dedicated to the honour of those three has multiplied a hundred-fold or a thousand-fold. On account of that merit that even now, Yudhishthira, the three worlds are clearly visible to me.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: दशैव तु सदाऽऽचार्यः श्रोत्रियानतिरिच्यते॥ दशाचार्यानुपाध्याय उपाध्यायान् पिता दश।
en: One Acharya is superior to ten Brahmanas learned in the Vedas. One Upadhyaya is again superior to ten Acharyas. The father, again, is superior to ten Upadhyayas.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: पितॄन् दश तु मातैका सर्वा वा पृथिवीमपि॥ गुरुत्वेनाभिभवति नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः।
en: The mother, again, is superior to ten fathers, or, perhaps, the whole world, there is no one so much worthy of reverence as the mother.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: गुरुर्गरीयान् पितृतो मातृतश्चेति मे मतिः॥ उभौ हि मातापितरौ जन्मन्येवोपयुज्यतः।
en: In my view, however, the preceptor deserves greater respect then the father or even the mother. The father and the mother are the creators of one's being.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: शरीरमेव सृजतः पिता माता च भारत॥ आचार्यशिष्टा या जातिः सा दिव्या साजरामरा।
en: The father and the mother, O Bharata, only create the body. The life, on the other hand, which one acquires from his preceptor, is divine. That life suffers no decays and is imimortal.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: अवध्या हि सदा माता पिता चाप्यपकारिणौ॥ न संदुष्यति तत् कृत्वा न च ते दूषयन्ति तम्। धर्माय यतमानानां विदुर्देवा महर्षिभिः॥
en: The father and the inother, even if they offend you, should never be killed. By not punishing a father and a mother one does not commit sin. Indeed, such reverend persons, by escaping punishment do not stain the king. The gods and the Rishis do not withhold their favours from such persons who try to maintain even their sinful fathers reverently.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: यश्चावृणोत्यवितथेन कर्मणा ऋतं ब्रुवन्ननृतं सम्प्रयच्छन्। तं वै मन्येत पितरं मातरं च तस्मै न दुह्येत् कृतमस्य जानन्।॥
en: He, who favours a person by giving him true instruction, by communicating the Vedas, and by giving immortal knowledge, should be honoured as parents. The disciple, out of gratitude for what the instructor has done, should never do what would injure the latter.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: विद्यां श्रुत्वा ये गुरुं नाद्रियन्ते प्रत्यासन्ना मनसा कर्मणा वा। तेषां पापं भ्रूणहत्याविशिष्टं नान्यस्तेभ्यः पापकृदस्ति लोके। यथैव ते गुरुभिर्भावनीर्या स्तथा तेषां गुरवोऽभ्यर्चनीयाः॥
en: They, who do not honour their preceptors after receiving instruction from them by obeying them dutifully in thought and deed commit the sin of killing a foetus. There is no greater sinner in this world than this. Preceptors always treat their disciples with great affection. The latter should, therefore, reverse their preceptors duly.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: तस्मात् पूजयतिव्याश्च संविभज्याश्च यत्नतः। गुरवोऽर्चयितव्याश्च पुराणं धर्मभिच्छता॥
en: He, therefore, who wishes to acquire that high merit which has existed from days of yore, should adore his preceptors and carefully share with them every object of enjoyment.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: येन प्रीणाति पितरं तेन प्रीतः प्रजापतिः। प्रीणाति मातरं येन पृथिवी तेन पूजिता॥
en: Prajapati himself is pleased with him who pleases his father, He, who pleases his mother, pleases the Earth herself.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: येन प्रीणात्युपाध्यायं तेन स्याद् ब्रह्म पूजितम्॥ मातृतः पितृतश्चैव तस्मात् पूज्यतमो गुरुः॥
en: He, who pleases his preceptor pleases Brahma. Therefore the preceptor deserves greater respect then enter the father or the mother.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: ऋषयश्च हि देवाश्च प्रीयन्ते पितृभिः सह। पूज्यमानेषु गुरुषु तस्मात् पूज्यतमो गुरुः॥
en: If preceptors are adored the very Rishis, and the gods, together the Pitris, are all pleased. Therefore, the preceptor deserves the highest respect.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: केनचिन्न च वृत्तेन ह्यववज्ञेयो गुरुर्भवेत्। न च माता न च पिता मन्यते यादृशो गुरुः॥
en: The preceptor should never in any way be dishonoured by the disciple. Neither the mother nor the father deserves the honour which the preceptor does.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: न तेऽवमानमर्हन्ति न तेषां दूषयेत् कृतम्। गुरूणामेव सत्कारं विदुर्देवा महर्षिभिः॥
en: No insult should be offered to the father, the mother, and the preceptor. No act of theirs should be censured. The good and the great Rishis are pleased with him who treats his preceptors reverentially.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: उपाध्यायं पितरं मातरं च येऽभिद्रुह्यन्ते मनसा कर्मणा वा। तेषां पापं भ्रूणहत्याविशिष्टं तस्मान्नान्यः पापकृदस्ति लोके॥
en: They, who injure in thought and deed their preceptors, or fathers, or mothers, commit the sin of killing a foetus. There is no sinner in the world equal to them.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: भृतो वृद्धो यो न बिभर्ति पुत्रः स्वयोनिजः पितरं मातरं च। तद् वै पापं भ्रूणहत्याविशिष्टं तस्मान्नान्य पापकृदस्ति लोके।॥
en: That son, who, being born of parents and brought up by them and when he comes to age, does not maintain them on his turn, commits the sin of killing a foetus. There is no sinner like him in the world.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: मित्रद्रुहः कृतघ्नस्य स्त्रीघ्नस्य गुरुघातिनः। चतुर्णां वयमेतेषां निष्कृतिं नानुशुश्रुम॥
en: We have never heard that these four, viz., he, who injures a friend, he, who is ungrateful, he, who kills a woman, and he, who kills preceptor, succeed in purifying themselves.

description: The most important duties described by Bhishma
sn: एतत्सर्वमनिर्देशेनैवमुक्तं यत्कर्तव्यं पुरुषेणेह लोके। एतच्छ्रेयो नान्यदस्माद्विशिष्टं सर्वान् धर्माननुसृत्यैतदुक्तम्॥
en: I have described to you in general all that a person should do in this world. Besides those duties that I have described, there is nothing which yields greater happiness. Thinking of all duties, I have described to you their essence. ever

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं धर्मे स्थातुमिच्छन् नरो वर्तेत भारत। विद्वन् जिज्ञासमानाय प्रब्रूहि भरतर्षभ॥
en: Yudhishthira said How, O Bharata, should a person act who wishes to follow virtue? O foremost of Bharata's race, learned as you are, enlighten me on the question put by me.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: सत्यं चेवानृतं चोभे लोकानावृत्य तिष्ठतः। दयोः किमाचरेद् राजन् पुरुषो धर्मनिश्चितः॥
en: Truth and falsehood exist, all over the world. Which of these two, O king, should a virtuous person follow.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: किंस्वित् सत्यं किमनृतं किंस्विद् धर्म्य सनातनम्। कस्मिन्काले वदेत्सत्यं कस्मिन्कालेऽनृतं वदेत्॥
en: What again is truth? What is falsehood? What, again, is eternal virtue? When should a person tell the truth, and when should he tell an untruth?

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: भीष्म उवाच सत्यस्य वचनं साधु न सत्याद् विद्यते परम्। तु लोकेषु दुर्ज्ञानं तत् प्रवक्ष्यामि भारत॥
en: Bhishma said s To tell the truth is righteous. There is nothing higher than truth. I shall now, O Bharata, tell you what men do not know generally.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: भवेत् सत्यं न वक्तव्यं वक्तव्यमनृतं भवेत्। यत्रानृतं भवेत् सत्यं सत्यं वाप्यनृतं भवेत्॥
en: There, where falsehood prevails as truth, truth should not be said. There, again, where truth passes for falsehood, even falsehood should be said.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: तादृशो बध्यते बालो यत्र सत्यमनिष्ठितम्। सत्यानृते विनिश्चित्य ततो भवति धर्मवित्॥
en: That ignorant person commits sin, who says truth which is not righteous. That person is a master of duties who can distinguish truth from untruth.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: अप्यनार्योऽकृतप्रज्ञः पुरुषोऽप्यतिदारुणः। सुमहत् प्राप्नुयात् पुण्यं बलाकोऽन्धवधादिव॥
en: Even a person, who is disreputable, who is of impure soul, and who is very truthless, may succeed in acquiring great merit as the hunter Balaka by killing the blind beast.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: किमाश्चर्यं च यन्मूढो धर्मकामोऽप्यधर्मवित्। सुमहत् प्राप्नुयात् पुण्यं गङ्गायामिव कौशिकः॥
en: How extraordinary it is that a foolish person though desirous of winning merit still perpetrated a sinful deed! An owl, again, living on the banks of the Ganges, acquired great merit.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: तादृशोऽयमनुप्रश्नो यत्र धर्मः सुदुर्लभः। दुष्करः प्रतिसंख्यातुं तत् केनात्र व्यवस्यति॥
en: The question you have put to me a difficult one, because it is difficult to say what is righteousness. It is not easy to describe it. No one describing righteousness, can describe it accurately.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: प्रभवार्थाय भूतानां धर्मप्रवचनं कृतम्। यः स्यात् प्रभवसंयुक्तः स धर्म इति निश्चयः॥
en: Righteousness was declared for the aggrandisement and growth of all creatures. Therefore, what brings on advancement and growth is righteousness.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: धारणाद् धर्ममित्याहुर्धर्मेण विधृताः प्रजाः। यः स्याद् धारणसंयुक्तः स धर्म इति निश्चयः॥
en: Righteousness was declared for preventing creatures from injuring one another. Therefore, Righteousness is that which prevents injury to creatures.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: अहिंसाय भूतानां धर्मप्रवचनं कृतम्। यः स्यादहिंसासम्पृक्तः स धर्म इति निश्चयः॥
en: Righteousness is also so called because it maintains all creatures. In fact, all creatures are kept up Righteousness, Therefore, Righteousness is what is capable of upholding all creatures.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: श्रुतिधर्म इति ह्येके नेत्याहुरपरे जनाः। न च तत्प्रत्यसूयामो न हि सर्वं विधीयते॥
en: Some say that Righteousness is the injunction of the Shrutis. Others do not agree to this. I would into blame them that say so. Everything, again, has not been described in the Shrutis.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: येऽन्यायेन जिहीर्षन्तो धनमिच्छन्ति कस्यचित्। तेभ्यस्तु न तदाख्येयं स धर्म इति निश्चयः॥
en: Sometimes men, desirous of getting hold of the wealth of some one, make enquiries. One should never answer such enquiries. That is settled duty.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
