sn: अकूजनेन चेन्मोक्षो नावकूजेत् कथंचन। अवश्यं कूजितव्ये वा शङ्करन् वाप्यकूजनात्॥ श्रेयस्तत्रानृतं वक्तुं सत्यादिति विचारितम्। यः पापैः सह सम्बन्धान्मुच्यते शपथादपि॥
en: If by becoming silent, one succeeds in escaping, one should remain silent, If, however, one's silence at a time when one must speak creates suspicion, it would be better then to say what is untrue than what is true. This is right conclusion. If one can escape from sinful men by an oath, one may take it without committing sin.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: न तेभ्योऽपि धनं देयं शक्ये सति कथंचन। पापेभ्यो हि धनं दत्तं दातारमपि पीडयेत्॥
en: One should not, even if he is able, give away his wealth to sinful men. Wealth given to sinful men assails even the giver.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: स्वशरीरोपरोधेन धनमादातुमिच्छतः। सत्यसम्प्रतिपत्त्यर्थं यद् ब्रूयुः साक्षिणः क्वचित्॥ अनुक्त्वा तत्र तद्वाच्यं सर्वे तेऽनृतवादिनः। प्राणात्यये विवाहे च वक्तव्यमनृतं भवेत्॥
en: If a creditor wishes to take from his debtor a payment of the load by bodily service, the witnesses would all perjure, it, summoned by the creditor for establishing the truth of the agreement, they did not say what should be said. When life is in danger, or on occasions of marriage, one may say an untruth.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: अर्थस्य रक्षणार्थाय परेषां धर्मकारणात्। परेषां सिद्धिमाकाङ्क्षन् नीचः स्याद् धर्मभिक्षुकः॥
en: One, who seeks for virtue, does not commit a sin by saying a falsehood, if it be said to save the wealth and prosperity of others, or for religious purposes.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: प्रतिश्रुत्य प्रदातव्यः स्वकार्यस्तु बलात्कृतः। यः कश्चिद् धर्मसमयात् प्रच्युतो धर्मसाधनः॥ दण्डनैव स हन्तव्यस्तं पन्थानं समाश्रितः। च्युतः सदैव धर्मेभ्योऽमानवं धर्ममास्थितः॥ शठः स्वधर्ममुत्सृज्य तमिच्छेदुपजीवितुम्।
en: Having promised to pay, one is bound to satisfy his promise, If failing, the selfappropriator must be forcibly enslaved. If a person without satisfying a fair engagement acts improperly, he should, forsooth, be punished with the rod of punishment for behaving thus. Deviating from all duties and abandoning those of his own order, a deceitful person always wishes to follow the conduct of Asuras for maintaining life.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: सर्वोपायैर्निहन्तव्यः पापो निकृतिजीवनः॥ धनमित्येव पापानां सर्वेषामिह निश्चयः।
en: Such a sinful wight living by deceit should be killed by all means. Such sinful creatures do not see anything in this world superior to wealth.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: अविषह्या ह्यसम्भोज्या निकृत्या पतनं गताः॥ च्युता देवमनुष्येभ्यो यथा प्रेतास्तथैव ते।
en: Such men should never be tolerated. No one should eat with them. They should be considered as degraded for their sins. Indeed, degraded from the status of humanity and shut out from the grace of the gods, they are even like evil genie.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: निर्यज्ञास्तपसा हीना मा स्म तैः सह सङ्गमः॥ धननाशाद् दुःखतरं जीविताद् विप्रयोजनम्।
en: Abandon their companionship who do not perform sacrifices and penances. If their wealth be lost, they commit even suicide which is highly pitiable.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: अयं ते रोचतां धर्म इति वाच्यः प्रयत्नतः॥ न कश्चिदस्ति पापानां धर्म इत्येष निश्चयः।
en: Of those sinful men there is none to whom you can say, This is your duty. Let your heart be to it!-Their firm belief is that there is nothing in this world which is equal to wealth.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: तथागतं च यो हन्यान्नासौ पापेन लिप्यते॥ स्वकर्मणा हतं हन्ति हत एव स हन्यते।
en: The person that would kill such a creature would commit no sin. He, who slays him, slays one that has been already killed by his own acts. If killed, it is the dead that is killed.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: तेषु यः समयं कश्चित् कुर्वीत हतबुद्धिषु॥ यथा काकाश्च गृध्राश्च तथैवोपधिजीविनः। अर्ध्वं देहविमोक्षात् ते भवन्त्येतासु योनिषु॥
en: He, who promises to kill those persons of lost senses, should keep his promise. Such sinners are like the crow and the vulture who live by deceit. When their bodies are dissolved, they are born again as crows and vultures.

description: The superiority of truth to false-hood
sn: यस्मिन् यथा वर्तते यो मनुर्घ्य स्तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तितव्यं स धर्मः। मायाचारो मायया बाधितव्यः साध्वाचारः साधुना प्रत्युपेयः॥
en: One should treat another as the latter does him. A deceitful person should be thwarted with deceit, while an honest man should be treated with honesty.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच क्लिश्यमानेषु भूतेषु तैस्तै वैस्ततस्ततः। दुर्गाण्यतितरेद् येन तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Creatures are seen to be assailed various means and almost continually. Tell me, O grandfather, in what way can one get over all those difficulties!

sn: आश्रमेषु यथोक्तेषु यथोक्तं ये द्विजातयः। वर्तन्ते संयतात्मानो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Bhishma said-Those members of the twice-born class, who duly follow, with restrained souls, the duty sanctioned by the scriptures for the several modes of life, succeed in getting over all these difficulties.

sn: ये दम्भात्राचरन्ति स्म येषां वृत्तिश्च संयता। विषयांश्च निगृह्णन्ति दुर्गाव्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who never practise deceit, those, whose conduct is regulated by wholesome restrictions, and those, who control all worldly desires, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: प्रत्याहु!च्यमाना ये न हिंसन्ति च हिंसिताः। प्रयच्छन्ति न याचन्ते दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who do not speak when addressed in evil words, those who do not injure others when injured themselves, those, who give but do not take, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: वासयन्त्यतिथीन् नित्यं नित्यं ये चानसूयकाः। नित्यं स्वाध्यायशीलाश्च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who always treat guests hospitably, those, who do not cherish malice, those, who constantly read the Vedas, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: मात्रापित्रोश्च ये वृत्तिं वर्तन्ते धर्मकोविदाः। वर्जयन्ति दिवा स्वजं दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those persons, who, conversant with duties, treat their parents properly, those, who do not sleep during the day, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: ये वा पापं न कुर्वन्ति कर्मणा मनसा गिरा। निक्षिप्तदण्डा भूतेषु दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who do not commit any kind of sin in thought, word, and deed, those, who never injure any creature, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: ये नलोभानयन्त्यर्थान् राजानो रजसान्विताः। विषयान् परिरक्षन्ति दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those kings, who do not, under the influence of passion and covetousness, impose oppressive taxes, and those who protect their own dominions succeed in getting over all difficulties

sn: स्वेषु दारेषु वर्तन्ते न्यायवृत्तिमृतावृतौ। अग्निहोत्रपराः सन्तो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who know their wedded wives in season without seeking the company of other women, those, who are honest and attentive to their Agnihotras, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: आहवेषु च ये शूरास्त्यक्त्वा मरणजं भयम्। धर्मेण जयमिच्छन्ति दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who are endued with courage and who, shaking off all fear of death, engage in battle, desirous of gaining victory by fair means, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: ये वदन्तीह सत्यानि प्राणत्यागेऽप्युपस्थिते। प्रमाणभूता भूतानां दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who always speak truth in this world even when life is in danger, and who are models for all creatures to follow, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: कर्माण्यकुहकार्थानि येषां वाचश्च सूनृताः। येषामाश्च सम्बद्धा दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति॥
en: Those who never act deceitfully, whose words are always sweet and whose wealth is always well spent, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: अनध्यायेषु ये विप्राः स्वाध्यायं नेह कुर्वते। तपोनिष्ठाः सुतपसो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those Brahmanas, who never study the Vedas at improper hours, and who practise penances with devotion, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: ये तपश्च तपस्यन्ति कौमारब्रह्मचारिणः। विद्यावेदव्रतस्नाता दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those Brahmanas, who follow the life of celibacy and Brahmacharya, who practise penances, and who are purified by learning, Vedic knowledge, and proper vows, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: ये च संशान्तरजसः संशान्ततमसच ये। सत्त्वे स्थिता महात्मानो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who have restrained the qualities belonging to Darkness and Ignorance, who are possessed of great souls, and who practise the quality of Goodness, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: येषां न कश्चित् त्रसति न त्रसन्ति हि कस्यचित्। येषामात्मसमो लोको दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, of whom no creatures are afraid, and those, who are not afraid, of any creatures themselves, those, who regard all creatures as their own self, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: परश्रिया न तप्यन्ति ये सन्तः पुरुषर्षभाः। ग्राम्यादर्थानिवृत्ताश्च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those foremost of men, who are good, who are never stricken with grief on seeing other people's prosperity, and who abstain from all kinds of ignoble conduct, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: सर्वान् देवान् नमस्यन्ति सर्वधर्मांश्च शृण्वते। ये श्रद्दधानाः शान्ताश्च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who bow to all the gods, who listen to the doctrines of all creeds, who have faith, and who are possessed of tranquil souls, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: ये न मानित्वमिच्छन्ति मानयन्ति च ये परान्। मान्यमानान् नमस्यन्ति दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who do not seek honour for themselves, who give honour to others, who bow down to those who deserve their adoration, succeed succeed in getting all difficulties.

sn: ये च श्राद्धानि कुर्वन्ति तिथ्यां तिथ्यां प्रजार्थिनः। सुविशुद्धेन मनसा दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who perform Shraddhas on the proper lunar days, with pure minds, for having offspring, succeed in getting all difficulties. Over over

sn: ये क्रोधं संनियच्छन्ति क्रुद्धान् संशमयन्ति च। न च कुप्यन्ति भूतानां दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who conquer their own anger and pacify the anger of others, and who are never irate with any one, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: मधु मांसं च ये नित्यं वर्जयन्तीह मानवाः। जन्मप्रभृति मद्यं च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who do not take, from their birth, honey and meat and intoxicating drinks, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: यात्रार्थं भोजनं येषां संतानार्थं च मैथुनम्। वाक् सत्यवचनार्थाय दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who take food for only supporting life, who live with women for the sake of offspring only, and who open their lips for speaking what is true, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: ईश्वर सर्वभूतानां जगतः प्रभवाप्ययम्। भक्ता नारायणं देवं दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who adore with devotion the god Narayana, that Supreme Lord of all creatures, that origin and destruction of the universe, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: य एष पद्मरक्ताक्षः पीतवासा महाभुजः। सुहृद् भ्राता च मित्रं च सम्बन्धी च तथाच्युतः॥
en: This Krishna here, having eyes red as the lotus, clad in yellow attire, possessed of mighty arms,—this Krishna, who is our well-wisher, brother, friend, and relative, is Narayana of undecaying glory.

sn: य इमान् सकलॉल्लोकांश्चर्मवत् परिवेश्येत्। इच्छन् प्रभुर चिन्त्यात्मा गोविन्दः पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: He of his own will cover all the worlds like a leathern case. He is the powerful Lord of inconceivable soul! He is Govinda, the best of all beings.

sn: स्थितः प्रियहिते जिष्णोः स एष पुरुषोत्तमः। राजंस्तव च दुर्धर्षो वैकुण्ठः पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: This Krishna, who always does what is agreeable and beneficial to Jishnu, as also to you, O king, is that foremost of all beings, that irresistible one, that abode of eternal happiness.

sn: य एनं संश्रयन्तीह भक्ता नारायणं हरिम्। ते तरन्तीह दुर्गाणि न चात्रास्ति विचारणा॥
en: Those, who devotedly seek the refuge of this Narayana, called also Hari, succeed in getting all difficulties.

sn: दुर्गातितरणं ये च पठन्ति श्रावयन्ति च। कथयन्ति च विप्रेभ्यो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: Those, who read these verses regarding the getting over of difficulties, who recite them to others, and who speak of them to Brahmanas, succeed in getting over all difficulties.

sn: इति कृत्यसमुद्देशः कीर्तितस्ते मयानघ। तरन्ते येन दुर्गाणि परत्रेह च मानवाः॥
en: I have now, O sinless one, described to you all those acts by which men may get over all difficulties both in this world and in the next.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच असौम्याः सौम्यरूपेण सौम्याश्चासौम्यदर्शनाः। ईदृशान् पुरुषांस्तात कथं विद्यामहे वयम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said Many persons here, who do not in reality, possess of tranquil souls, appear external as men of tranquil souls. There are again others, who are really of tranquil souls but that appear otherwise. How, O sire, shall we succeed in knowing these people.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरांतनम्। व्याघ्रगोमायुसंवादं तं निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Regarding it is recited the old story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal. Listen to it, О Yudhishthira.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: पुरिकायां पुरि पुरा श्रीमत्यां पौरिको नृपः। परहिंसारति: क्रूरो बभूव पुरुषाधमः॥
en: In days of yore, in a wealthy city called Paurika, there was a king named Paurika. That worst of beings was highly truthless and took pleasure in injuring others.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: स त्वायुषि परिक्षीणे जगामानीप्सितां गतिम्। गोमायुत्वं च सम्प्राप्तो दूषितः पूर्वकर्मणा॥
en: When the lease of his life ran out he obtained an undesirable end. In fact, sullied by the evil deeds of his human life, he was born again as a jackal.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: संस्मृत्य पूर्वभूतिं च निर्वेदं परमं गतः। न भक्षयति मांसानि परैरुपहृतान्यपि॥
en: Remembering his pristine prosperity, he was filled with grief and abstained from meat even when brought before him by others,

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अहिंस्रः सर्वभूतेषु सत्यवाक् सुदृढव्रतः। स चकार यथाकालमाहारं पतितैः फलैः॥
en: And he felt mercy for all creatures, and was truthful in speech, and firm in the observance of austere vows. At the appointed hour he took food which consisted of fruit which had dropped from the trees.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: श्मशाने तस्य चावासो गोमायोः सम्मतोऽभवत्। जन्मभूम्यनुरोधाच्च नान्यवासमरोचयत्॥
en: That jackal lived in a vast crematorium and liked to live there. And as it was his birth place, he never desired to change it for a better one.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: तस्य शौचममृष्यन्तस्ते सर्वे सहजातयः। चालयन्ति स्म तां बुद्धिं वचनैः प्रश्रयोत्तरैः॥
en: Unable to bear the purity of his conduct, the other jackals tries to make him change his resolution by addressing him in the following humble words

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: वसन् पितृवने रौद्रे शौचे वर्तितुमिच्छसि। इयं विप्रतिपत्तिस्ते यदा त्वं पिशिताशनः॥
en: Through living in this dreadful crematorium, you desire yet to live such a pure life. Is not this owing to your perverse understanding, since you are by nature an eater of carrion?

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: तत्समानो भवास्माभिर्भोज्यं दास्यामहे वयम्। भुक्षव शौचं परित्यज्य यद्धि भुक्तं सदास्तु ते॥
en: Be you like us! All of us will give you food, Eat that which ought always to be your food, leaving of such purity of conduct!

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: इति तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा प्रत्युवाच समाहितः। मधुरैः प्रसृतैर्वार्यहेतुमद्भिरनिष्ठुरैः॥
en: Hearing these words of theirs the jackal replied to them, with rapt attention, in these sweet and reasonable words, inculcating harmlessness to all-

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अप्रमाणा प्रसूतिर्मे शीलतः क्रियते कुलम्। प्रार्थयामि च तत्कर्म येन विस्तीर्यते यशः॥
en: My birth has been low. It is conduct, however, which determines the birth. I wish to act in such a way that my fame may spread.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: श्मशाने यदि मे वासः समाधिर्मे निशम्यताम्। आत्मा फलति कर्माणि नाश्रमो धर्मकारणम्॥
en: Although I live in this crematorium, yet listen to my vows regarding my conduct. One's own self is the root of one's acts. The mode of life which one may adopt is not the root of one's religious acts.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: आश्रमे यो द्विजं हन्याद् गां वा दद्यादनाश्रमे। किं तु तत्पातकं न स्यात् तद्वा दत्तं वृथा भवेत्॥
en: If one, while following a particular mode of life, kills a Brahmana, will not the sin of Brahmanicide assail him? If, on the other hand, one gives away a cow, while not even following any particular mode of life, will that pious gift yields on merit?

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: भवन्तः स्वार्थलोभेन केवलं भक्षणे रताः। अनुबन्धे त्रयो दोषास्तान् न पश्यन्ति मोहिताः॥
en: Actuated by the desire of getting what is agreeable, you are only busy with filling your stomachs. Overcome by folly, you are blind to the three faults which are in the end.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अप्रत्ययकृतां गामर्थापनयदूषिताम्। इह चामुत्र चानष्टां तस्माद् वृत्तिं न रोचये॥
en: I do not like to follow the life which you lead, which yields evil both in this world and in the next, and which is characterised by loss of virtue brought about by discontentment and temptation!

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: तं शुचिं पण्डितं मत्वा शार्दूलः ख्यातविक्रमः। कृत्वाऽऽत्मसदृशीं पूजां साचिव्येऽवरयत् स्वयम्।।
en: A tiger, well known for prowess, happened to overhear this conversation, and accordingly, taking the jackal for a learned person of pure conduct, offered him such respectful worship as became his own self and then expressed a desire for appointing him his minister.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: शार्दूल उवाच सौम्य विज्ञातरूपस्त्वं गच्छ यात्रां मया सह। ब्रियन्तामीप्सिताभोगाः परिहार्याश्च पुष्कलाः॥
en: The tiger said O righteous person, I know what you are! Do your look after the duties of government with myself! Do you look after the duties of government with myself! Enjoy whatever articles you may wish to have, leaving off whatever you may not have a liking for.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: तीक्ष्णा इति वयं ख्याता भवन्तं ज्ञापयामहे। मृदुपूर्वं हितं चैव श्रेयश्चाधिगमिष्यसि॥
en: As regards ourselves, we are known to be of a fierce nature. We inforın you beforehand of this. If you act with mildness, you will be benefited and reap advantages for yourself.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अथ सम्पूज्य तद् वाक्यं मृगेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः। गोमायुः संश्रितं वाक्यं बभाषे किंचिदानतः॥
en: Honouring these words of that great lord of all animals, jackal, bending low his head a little, said these humble words.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: गोमायुरुवाच सदृशं मृगराजैतत् तव वाक्यं मदन्तरे। यत् सहायान् मृगयसे धर्मार्थकुशलाशुचीन्॥
en: The jackal said O king of beasts, these words of yours about myself are such as become you. It is also becoming of you that you should cock for ministers of pure conduct and who conversant with duties and worldly affairs,

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: न शक्यं ह्यनमात्येन महत्त्वमनुशासितुम्। दुष्टामात्येन वा वीर शरीरपरिपन्थिना॥ सहायाननुरक्तांश्च नयज्ञानुपसंहितान्। परस्परमसंसृष्टान् विजिगीषूनलोलुपान्॥ अनतीतोपधान् प्राज्ञान् हिते युक्तान् मनस्विनः। पूजयेथा महाभाग यथाऽऽचार्यान् यथा पितृन्।॥
en: You cannot maintain your great power without a pious minister, O hero, or with a wicked minister who always tries to put an end to your very life. You should, O highly blessed one, honour those of your ministers who are devoted to you, who are conversant with policy, and who are independent of one another, desirous of securing victory for you, unstained by covetousness, free from deceit, wise, ever engaged in your well-being, and gifted with great mental vigour, even as you should honour your preceptor or parents.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: न त्वेव मम संतोषाद् रोचतेऽन्यन्मृगाधिप। न कामये सुखान् भोगानैश्वर्यं च तदाश्रयम्॥
en: But, o king of beasts, as I am perfectly contented with my present situation, I do not like to change it for anything else. I do not hanker after luxuries or the happiness that originates from them.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: न योक्ष्यति हि मे शीलं तव भृत्यैः पुरातनैः। ते त्वां विभेदयिष्यन्ति दुःशीलाश्च मदन्तरे॥
en: My conduct, again, my not be like that your old servants. If they be of wicked conduct, they will create disunion between you and me.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: सश्रयः श्लाघनीयस्त्वमन्येषामपि भास्वताम्। कृतात्मा सुमहाभागः पापकेष्वष्यदारुणः॥ दीर्घदर्शी महोत्साहः स्थूललक्ष्यो महाबलः। कृती चामोधकर्तासि भाग्यैश्च समलंकृतः॥
en: Dependence upon another, even if he be a bright person, is not desirable nor praiseworthy. I am of pure soul I am highly blessed. I cannot treat even sinners severely. I am gifted with great foresight. I have capacity for great exertion. I do not mind small things. I am endued with great strength. I am successful in acts, never uselessly. I have every object of enjoyment.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: किं तु स्वेनास्मि संतुष्टो दुःखवृत्तिरनुष्ठिता। सेवायां चापि नाभिज्ञः स्वच्छन्देन वनचरः॥
en: I am never satisfied with a little. I have never served another. I am, future more, unskilled in serving. I live according to my pleasure in the forest.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: राजोपक्रोशदोषाश्च सर्वे संश्रयवासिनाम्। व्रतचर्या तु नि:संगा निर्भया वनवासिनाम्॥
en: All who live in court have to suffer great pain for evil speeches against themselves. Those, however, who live in the forest, spend their days, fearlessly and without anxiety, observing vows.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: नृपेणाहूयमानस्य यत् तिष्ठति भयं हृदि। न तत् तिष्ठति तुष्टानां वने मूलफलाशिनाम्॥
en: The fear, which possesses the heart of a person, who is summoned by the king is unknown to persons passing their days happily in the forest, living upon fruits and roots.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: पानीयं वा निरायासं स्वाइन्नं वा भयोत्तरम्। विचार्य खलु पश्यामि तत्सुखं यत्र निर्वृतिः॥
en: Simple food and drink got without effort, and rich food procured with fear, widely differ from each other. Thinking of these two, I hold that there is happiness where there is not anxiety.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अपराधैर्न तावन्तो भृत्याः शिष्टा नराधिपः। उपघातैर्यथा भृत्या दूषिता निधनं गताः॥
en: A few only of the servants of kings are justly punished for their offences. A great number of them, however, meet with death under false charges.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: यदि त्वेतन्मया कार्यं मृगेन्द्र यदि मन्यसे। समयं कृतमिच्छामि वर्तितव्यं यथा मयि॥
en: If, notwithstanding all this, you appoint me, O king of beasts, as your minister, I wish to make an agreement with you regarding your treatment towards men.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: मदीया माननीयास्ते श्रोतव्यं च हितं वचः। कल्पित्ता या च मे वृत्तिः सा भवेत् त्वयि सुस्थिरा।।३५
en: Those words that I shall speak for your well being should be listened to, and honoured by you. The provision which you will make for me you will never interface with.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: न मन्त्रयेयमन्यैस्ते सचिवैः सह कर्हिचित्। नीतिमन्तः परीप्सन्तो वृथा ब्रूयुः परे मयि॥
en: I shall never consult with your other ministers. If I do, for they always seek superiority, they will then impute various kinds of faults to me.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: एक एकेन संगम्य रहो ब्रूयां हितं वचः। न च ते ज्ञातिकार्येषु प्रष्टव्योऽहं हिताहिते।॥
en: Meeting with you alone and in secret I shall say what is for your well-being. About you kinsmen, you will not ask me what is for your behoof or what is otherwise,

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: मया सम्मन्त्र्य पश्चाच्च न हिंस्याः सचिवास्त्वया। मदीयानां च कुपितो मा त्वं दण्डं निपातयेः॥
en: Having consulted with me you shall not punish your other ministers afterwards. Getting enraged you will not punish my followers and dependents.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: एवमस्त्विति तेनासौ मृगेन्द्रेणाभिपूजितः। प्राप्तवान् मतिसाचिव्यं गोमायुर्व्याघ्रयोनितः॥
en: Thus addressed by the jackal, the king of beasts answered him,-Let it be so!-and showed him every honour. The jackal then accepted the ministership of the tiger.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: तं तथा सुकृतं दृष्ट्वा पूज्यमान स्वकर्मसु। प्राद्विषन् कृतसंघाताः पूर्वभृत्या मुहुर्मुहुः॥ धनेन महता
en: Seeing the jackal treated with respect and supported in all his deeds, the old servants of the king, uniting together, began continually to show their hatred towards him.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: मित्रबुद्ध्या च गोमायुं सान्त्वयित्वा प्रसाद्य च। दोषैस्तु समतां नेतुमैच्छन्नशुभबुद्धयः॥
en: Those wicked persons at first tried to please and win him over with friendly conduct and make him put up with the various abuses which existed in the state.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अन्यथा झुषिताः पूर्वं परद्रव्याभिहारिणः। अशक्ताः किञ्चिदादातुं द्रव्यं गोमायुयन्त्रिताः॥
en: Robbing other people's property, they had long enjoyed their sports. Now, however, being governed by the jackal, they were unable to take anything belonging to others.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: व्युत्थानं च विकाङ्क्षद्भिः कथाभिः प्रतिलोभ्यते। चैव बुद्धिरस्य विलोभ्यते॥ न चापि स महाप्राज्ञस्तस्माद् धैर्याच्चचाल ह।
en: Seeking aggrandisement and prosperity, they began to tempt him with sweet words. Indeed, large bribes even were offered to tempt his heart. Highly wise, the jackal showed no signs of yielding to those temptations.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अथास्य समयं कृत्वा विनाशाय तथा परे॥ ईप्सितं तु मृगेन्द्रस्य मांसं यत् यत्र संस्कृतम्। अपनीय स्वयं तद्धि तैय॑स्तं तस्य वेश्मनि॥
en: Then some amongst them making an agreement amongst themselves for bringing about his destruction, snatched away the welldressed meat that was intended for, and much desired by the king of beasts, and kept it secretly in the house of the jackal.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: यदर्थं चाप्यपहृतं येन तच्चैव मन्त्रितम्। तस्य तद् विदितं सर्वं कारणार्थं च मर्षितम्॥
en: The jackal knew who had taken away the meat and the party who were connected with the act. But though he knew everything, he bore it for a particular object.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: समयोऽयं कृतस्तेन साचिव्यमुपगच्छता। नोपघातस्त्वया कार्यों राजन् मैत्रीमिहेच्छता॥
en: He had made an agreement with the king at the time of his becoming the minister, saying,-You seek my friendship, but you will not, O king, mistrust me without cause.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: भीष्म उवाच क्षुधितस्य मृगेन्द्रस्य भोक्तुमभ्युत्थितस्य च। भोजनायोपहर्तव्यं तन्मांसं नोपदृश्यते॥ मृगराजेन चाज्ञप्तं दृश्यतां चोर इत्युत।
en: Bhishma said Feeling hungry, when the king of beasts came to eat, he did not found the meat which should have been kept ready for his dinner. The king then ordered,-Let the thief be detected!

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: कृतकैश्चापि तन्मांसं मृगेन्द्रायोपवर्णितम्॥ सचिवेनापनीतं ते विदुषा प्राज्ञमानिना।
en: His deceitful ministers represented to him that the meat kept for him had been taken away by his learned minister, the jackal, that was so proud of his own wisdom.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: सरोषस्त्वथ शार्दूलः श्रुत्वा गोमायुचापलम्॥ बभूवामर्षितो राजा वधं चास्य व्यरोचयत्।
en: Hearing of this unwise act of the jackal, the tiger was insensate with rage. Indeed, the king, yielding to wrath, ordered his minister to be killed.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: छिद्रं तु तस्य तद् दृष्ट्वा प्रोचुस्ते पूर्वमन्त्रिणः॥ सर्वेषामेव सोऽस्माकं वृत्तिभङ्गे प्रवर्तते।
en: Finding the opportunity, the former ministers said to the king,-The jackal is always ready to take away from all of us the means of sustenance.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: निश्चित्यैव पुनस्तस्य ते कर्माण्यपि वर्णयन्।॥ इदं तस्येदृशं कर्म किं तेन न कृतं भवेत्।
en: Having said so, they once more spoke of the jackal's act of robbing the king of his food. And they said,-Such then is his conduct! What is there which he would not venture to do?

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: श्रुतश्च स्वामिना पूर्वं यादृशो नैव तादृशः॥ वाङ्मात्रेणैव धर्मिष्ठः स्वभावेन तु दारुणः।
en: He is not as you had heard. He is righteous in words, but he is really sinful by nature.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: धर्मच्छद्या ह्ययं पापो वृथाचारपरिग्रहः॥ कार्यार्थ भोजनार्थेषु व्रतेषु कृतवाश्रमम्।
en: At heart a wretch, he has disguised himself by assuming the grab of virtue. His conduct is really vicious. For serving his own purpose he had practised austerities in matters of diet and vows.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: यदि विप्रत्ययो ह्येष तदिदं दर्शयाम ते॥ तन्मांसं चैव गोमायोस्तैः क्षणादाशु ढौकितम्।
en: If you disbelieve this, we will give you proof!-Having said so, they immediately caused that meat to be found out by entering the jackal's house.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: मांसापनयनं ज्ञात्वा व्याघ्रः श्रुत्वा च तद्वचः॥ आज्ञापयामास तदा गोमायुर्वध्यतामिति।
en: Determining that the meat was brought back from the jackal's house and hearing all those representations of his old servants, the king ordered, saying,-Let the jackal be killed.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: शार्दूलस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शार्दूलजननी ततः॥ मृगराजं हितैर्वाक्यैः सम्बोधयितुमागमत्।
en: Hearing these words of the tiger, his mother came there for awakening her son's good sense with wholesome advice.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: पुत्र नैतत् त्वया ग्राह्यं कपटारम्भसंयुतम्॥ कर्मसंघर्षजैर्दोषैर्दुष्येताशुचिभिः शुचिः।
en: The venerabie dame said,-O son, you should not believe this deceitful charge. Actuated by envy and rivalry, wicked men impute faults to even an honest person.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: नोच्छ्रितं सहते कश्चित् प्रक्रिया वैरकारिका॥ शुचेरपि हि युक्तस्य दोष एव निपात्यते।
en: Enemies desirous of a quarrel cannot bear the elevation of an enemy engendered by his great deeds. Faults are attributed to even a person soul performing penances. of pure

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: मुनेरपि वनस्थस्य स्वानि कर्माणि कुर्वतः॥ उत्पाद्यन्ते त्रयः पक्षा मित्रोदासीनशत्रवः।
en: Even for an ascetic living in the forest and engaged in his own acts, there are three parties, viz., friends, neutrals, and foes.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: लुब्धानां शुचयो द्वेष्याः कातराणां तरस्विनः॥ मूर्खाणां पण्डिता द्वेष्या दरिद्राणां महाधनाः।
en: The rapacious hate the pure. The idle hate the active. The ignorant hate the learned. The poor hate the rich. The unrighteous hate the righteous. The ugly hate the beautiful.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अधार्मिकाणां धर्मिष्ठा विरूपाणां सुरूपिणः॥ बहवः पण्डिता मूर्खा लुब्धा मायो जीविनः। कुर्युर्दोषमदोषस्य बृहस्पतिमतेरपि॥
en: Many of the learned, the ignorant, the rapacious, and the deceitful, would falsely accuse an innocent person even if the latter is endued with the virtues and intelligence of Brihaspati himself.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: शून्यात् तच्च गृहान्मांसं यद्यप्यपहृतं तव। नेच्छते दीयमानं च साधु तावद् विमृश्यताम्॥
en: If meat had really been stolen from your house in your absence, remember the jackal refuses to take any meat that is even given to him. Let sufficient attention be paid to his fact.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: असभ्या: सभ्यसंकाशा: सभ्याश्चासभ्यदर्शनाः। दृश्यन्ते विविधा भावास्तेषु युक्तं परीक्षणम्॥
en: Wicked persons sometimes pass for the virtues, and the virtues are sometimes taken for the wicked. There are various aspects in creatures. It is, therefore, necessary to examine which is which.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: तलवद् दृश्यते व्योम खद्योतो हव्यवाडिव। न चैवास्ति तलं व्योम्नि खद्योते न हुताशनः॥
en: The sky seems to be like the solid base of a vessel. The fire-fly appears like the actual spark of fire. In sooth, however, the sky has no base and there is no fire in the fire-fly.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: तस्मात् प्रत्यक्षदृष्टोऽपि युक्तो ह्यर्थः परीक्षितुम्। परीक्ष्य ज्ञापयत्रर्थान पश्चात् परितप्यते॥
en: You should there scrutinise even things which you see with your own eyes. If a person determines everything after scrutiny, he never regrets afterwards.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: न दुष्करमिदं पुत्र यत् प्रभुर्घातयेत् परम्। श्लाघनीया यशस्या च लोके प्रभवतां क्षमा॥
en: It is not at all difficult, O son, for a master to put his servant to death. Forgiveness, however, in persons endued with power, is always praiseworthy and yields fame.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: स्थापितोऽयं त्वया पुत्र सामन्तेष्वपि विश्रुतः। दुःखेनासाद्यते पात्रं धार्यतामेष ते सुहृत्॥
en: You had made the jackal your first minister. For that act, you had acquired great fame among all the neighbouring chiefs. A good minister cannot be secured easily. The jackal is your well wisher. Let him, therefore, be supported.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: दूषितं परदोषैर्हि गृहीते योऽन्यथा शुचिम्। स्वयं संदूषितामात्यः क्षिप्रमेव विनश्यति॥
en: That king, who considers a really innocent person falsely accused by his enemies to be guilty, is soon ruined by the wicked ministers who create that conviction in him!

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: तस्मादप्यरिसंघाताद् गोमायोः कश्चिदागतः। धर्मात्मा तेन चाख्यातं यथैतत् कपटं कृतम्॥
en: After the tiger's mother had her say, a righteous agent of the jackal, coming out of that array of his enemies, disclosed everything about the way in which that false accusation had been made.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: ततो विज्ञातचरित: सत्कृत्य स विमोक्षितः। परिष्वक्तश्च सस्नेहं मृगेन्द्रेण पुनः पुनः॥
en: The jackal's innocence being proved, he was acquitted and respected by his master. The king of beasts embraced him affectionately again and again.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अनुज्ञाप्य मृगेन्द्रं तु गोमायुर्नीतिशास्त्रवित्। तेनामर्षेण संतप्तः प्रायमासितुमैच्छत॥
en: Burning with grief, the jackal, however, who was master of the science of policy, salutated the king of beasts and solicited his permission for sacrificing his life by observing the Praya vow.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: शार्दूलस्तं तु गोमायुं स्नेहात् प्रोत्फुल्ललोचनः। अवारयत् स धर्मिष्ठ पूजया प्रतिपूजयन्॥
en: Looking upon the virtuous jackal with affection and honouring him with reverential worship, the tiger, tried to dissuade him from fulfilling his wishes.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: तं स गोमायुरालोक्य स्नेहादागतसम्भ्रमम्। उवाच प्रणतो वाक्यं बाष्पगद्गदया गिरा॥
en: Seeing his master moved with affection, the jackal bowed down to him, and, in a voice suppressed with tears, said

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: पूजितोऽहं त्वया पूर्वं पश्चाच्चैव विमानितः। परेषामास्पदं नीतो वस्तुं नार्हाम्यहं त्वयि॥
en: Honoured by you first, I have afterwards been insulted by you. Your conduct towards me is calculated to make me an enemy of yours. It is not meet, therefore, that I should any longer live with you.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: असंतुष्टाश्च युताः स्थानान्मानात् प्रत्यवरोपिताः। स्वयं चोपहृता भृत्या ये चाप्युपहिताः परैः॥ परिक्षीणाश्च लुब्धाश्च क्रुद्धा भीताः प्रतारिताः। हतस्वा मानिनो ये च त्यक्तादाना महेप्सवः॥ संतापिताश्च ये केचिद् व्यसनौघप्रतीक्षिणः। अन्तर्हिता: सोपहितास्ते सर्वे परसाधनाः॥
en: Servants who are discontented, who have been dismissed from their offices, or who have been degraded from honourable situations, who have brought destitution upon themselves, or who have been ruined by their enemies, who have been weakened, who are rapacious, or enraged, or alarmed, or deceived, who have suffered confiscation, who are proud and willing to perform great feats but who are deprived of the means of acquiring wealth, and who burn with grief or anger for any injury done to them,-always wait for misfortunes to befall their masters. Being deceived, they forsake their masters and become powerful instruments in the hands of his enemies.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अवमानेन युक्तस्य स्थानभ्रष्टस्य वा पुनः कथं यास्यसि विश्वासमहं तिष्ठामि वा कथम्॥
en: I have been insulted by you and degraded from my place. How will you trust me again? How shall I continue to live with you?

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: समर्थ इति संगृह्य स्थापयित्वा परीक्षितः। कृतं च समय भित्त्वा त्वयाहमवमानितः॥
en: Knowing me to be competent you appointed me, and having examined me you had placed me in office. Violating the agreement then made (between us) you have insulted me.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: प्रथमं यः समाख्यातः शीलवानिति संसदि। न वाच्यं तस्य वैगुण्यं प्रतिज्ञां परिरक्षता॥
en: If one speaks of a particular person before others of righteous conduct, one should not, if desirous of keeping one's consistency, afterwards describe the same person as wicked.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: एवं चावमतस्येह विश्वास मे न यास्यसि। त्वयि चापेतविश्वासे ममोद्वेगो भविष्यति॥
en: I, who have thus been dishonoured by you, cannot any longer enjoy your confidence. On my part, when I shall find you withdraw your confidence from me, I shall be stricken with alarm and anxiety.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: शंकितस्त्वमहं भीतः परच्छिद्रानुदर्शिनः। अस्निग्धाश्चैव दुस्तोषा: कर्म चैतद् बहुच्छलम्॥
en: You entertaining suspicion and myself entertaining fear, our enemies will always try to find out opportunities for injuring us. Your subjects will, as a matter of fact, become anxious and discontented. Such a state of things has many shortcomings.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: दुःखेन श्लिष्यते भिन्नं श्लिष्टं दुःखेन भिद्यते। भिन्ना श्लिष्टा तु या प्रीतिर्न सा स्नेहेन वर्तते॥
en: It is difficult to unite again two who have been separated, as it is difficult to separate two that are united. If persons, reunited after separation, meet one another again, their conduct cannot be affectionate.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: कश्चिदेव हिते भर्तुर्दृश्यते न परात्मनोः। कार्यापेक्षा हि वर्तन्ते भावस्निग्धाः सुदुर्लभाः॥
en: No servant is to be seen who always wishes to do good to his master. People work with the desire of doing good to his master as also to one's own self. All works are undertaken from selfish desires. Unselfish works or motives are very rare.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: सुदु:खं पुरुषज्ञानं चित्तं ह्येषां चलाचलम्। समर्थो वाप्यशङ्को वा शतेष्वेकोऽधिगम्यते॥
en: Those kings, whose hearts are restless and unquiet; cannot gain a true knowledge of men. Only one in a hundred can be found who is either capable or undaunted.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अकस्मात् प्रक्रिया नृणामकस्माच्चापकर्षणम्। शुभाशुभे महत्त्वं च प्रकर्तुं बुद्धिलाघवम्॥
en: The prosperity of men, as also their downfall, originates of itself. Prosperity and adversity, and greatness, all originate from weakness of understanding.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवंविधं सान्त्वमुक्त्वा धर्मकामार्थहेतुमत्। प्रसादयित्वा राजानं गोमायुर्वनमभ्यगात्॥
en: Bhishma said Having said these conciliatory words pregnant with virtue, pleasure and profit, and having pleased the king, the jackal retired to the forest.

description: How to distinguish between men of tranquil souls and otherwise. The story of the discourse between a tiger and a jackal
sn: अगृह्यानुनयं तस्य मृगेन्द्रस्य च बुद्धिमान्। गोमायुः प्रायमास्थाय त्यक्त्वा देहं दिवं ययौ॥
en: Without heeding the entreaties of the king of beasts, the intelligent jackal renounced his body by sitting in Praya and went to heaven.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं पार्थिवेन कर्तव्यं किं च कृत्वा सुखी भवेत्। एतदाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन सर्वधर्मभृतां वर॥
en: Yudhishthira said What works should be done by a king, and what are those works by doing which a king may become happy? Tell me this fully, O you who are the foremost of all persons acquainted with duties.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: भीष्म उवाच हन्त तेऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु कार्यकनिश्चयम्। यथा राज्ञेह कर्तव्यं यच्च कृत्वा सुखी भवेत्॥
en: Bhishma said 'I shall tell you what you wish to know! Hear what should be done in this world by a king and what those works are by doing which a king may become happy.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: न चैवं वर्तितव्यं स्म यथेदमनुशुश्रुमा उष्ट्रस्य तु महद् वृत्तं तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: A king should not act like a camel of which we have heard. Listen to that history then, O Yudhishthira.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: जातिस्मरो महानुष्ट्रः प्राजापत्ये युगेऽभवत्। तपः सुमहदातिष्ठदरण्ये संशितव्रतः॥
en: There was, in the golden cycle, a huge camel who had recollection of his pristine deeds. Practising the most rigid vows, that camel practised very severe austerities in the woods.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: तपसस्तस्य चान्तेऽथ प्रीतिमानभवद् विभुः। वरेण च्छन्दयामास ततश्चैनं पितामहः॥
en: When his penances were terminated the powerful Brahman became pleased with him. The Grandfather, therefore, desired to grant him boons.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: उष्ट्र उवाच भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादान्मे दीर्घा ग्रीवा भवेदियम्। योजनानां शतं साग्रं गच्छामि चरितुं विभो॥
en: The camel said Let my neck, O holy one, become long through your favour, so that, O powerful lord, I may be able to get any food that may be even at the end of even a hundred Yojanas.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: एवमस्त्विति चोक्तः स वरदेन महात्मना। प्रतिलभ्य वरं श्रेष्ठं ययावुष्टः स्वकं वनम्॥
en: The great giver of boons said-Let it be so-Having got that boon, the camel then returned to his own forest.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: स चकार तदाऽऽलस्यं वरदानात् सुदुर्मतिः। न चैच्छच्चरितुं गन्तुं दुरात्मा कालमोहितः॥
en: Since the day of securing the boon, the foolish animal became idle. Indeed, stupefied by fate, the wretch did not from that day go out for grazing.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: स कदाचित् प्रसायैव तां ग्रीवां शतयोजनाम्। चचाराश्रान्तहृदयो वातश्चागात् ततो महान्॥
en: One day, while extending his long neck of a hundred Yojanas, the animal was engaged in picking his food without any trouble, there uprose a great storm.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: स गुहायां शिरो ग्रीवां निधाय पशुरात्मनः। आस्ते तु वर्षमभ्यागात् सुमहत् प्लावयज्जगत्॥
en: Keeping his head and a portion of the neck within the cave of a mountain, the camel resolved to wait till the storm would be over. Meanwhile rain came down in torrents, deluging the whole Earth.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: अथ शीतपरीताङ्गो जम्बुकः क्षुच्छ्रमान्वितः। सदारस्तां गुहामाशु प्रविवेश जलार्दितः॥
en: Wetted by the rain and shivering with cold, a jackal, with his wife, dragged himself with difficulty towards that very cave and entered it quickly for protection,

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: स दृष्ट्वा मांसजीवी तु सुभृशं क्षुच्छ्रमान्वितः। तु अभक्षयत् ततो ग्रीवामुष्ट्रस्य भरतर्षभ॥ यदा त्वबुध्यतात्मानं भक्ष्यमाणं स वै पशुः। तदा संकोचने यत्नमकरोद् भृशदुःखितः॥
en: Living as he did upon meat, and greatly hungry and tried as he was, O foremnost of Bharata's race, the jackal, seeing the camel's neck, began to eat as much of it as he could. When he perceived that his neck was being eaten, the camel tried sorrowfully to shorten it.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: यावदूर्ध्वमधश्चैव ग्रीवां संक्षिपते पशुः। तावत् तेन सदारेण जम्बुकेन स भक्षितः॥
en: But as he moved it up and down, the jackal and his wife, catching it, continued to eat it away.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: स हत्वा भक्षयित्वा च तमुष्ट्र जम्बुकस्तदा। विगते वातवर्षे निश्चक्राम गुहामुखात्॥
en: Within a short time the camel was dead. Having thus killed and eaten the camel, the jackal then came out of the cave after the storm and shower had ceased.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: एवं दुर्बुद्धिना प्राप्तमुष्ट्रेण निधनं तदा। आलस्यस्य क्रमात् पश्य महान्तं दोषमागतम्॥
en: Thus did that foolish camel die. See what a great evil followed idleness.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: त्वमप्येवंविधं हित्वा योगेन नियतेन्द्रियः। वर्तस्व बुद्धिमूलं तु विजयं मनुरब्रवीत्॥
en: As for yourself, avoiding idleness and controlling your senses, do everything in the world with proper means. Manu himself has declared that victory rests upon intelligence.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: बुद्धिश्रेष्ठानि कर्माणि बाहुमध्यानि भारत। तानि जवाजघन्यानि भारप्रत्यवराणि च॥
en: All acts that are performed with the help of intelligence are regarded as the highest, those performed, with the help of feet are inferior, while those done by carrying loads are the worst.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: राज्यं तिष्ठति दक्षस्य संगृहीतेन्द्रियस्य च। आर्तस्य बुद्धिमूलं हि विजयं मनुरब्रवीत्॥
en: If the king cleverly does his business and controls his senses, his kingdom lasts. Manu himself has declared that an ambitious person succeeds in gaining victories.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: गुह्यं मन्त्रं श्रुतवतः सुसहायस्य चानघ। परीक्ष्यकारिणो ह्यास्तिष्ठन्तीह युधिष्ठिर। सहाययुक्तेन मही कृत्स्ना शक्या प्रशासितुम्॥
en: In this world, O Yudhishthira, those, who listen to wise advice, those, O sinless one, who have allies, and act after proper scrutiny, succeeds in achieving all their objects. A person with such means succeeds in ruling the entire Earth.

description: The works of a king. The story of a camel
sn: इदं हि सद्भिः कथितं विधिज्ञैः पुरा महेन्द्रप्रतिमप्रभाव। मयापि चोक्तं तव शास्त्रदृष्ट्या यथैव बुद्ध्वा प्रचरस्व राजन्॥
en: O you powerful like Indra himself, this has been declared by ancient sages conversant with the scriptural injunctions! I, also, having my eyes on the scriptures, have said the same to you. Using your intelligence, do you act in this world, O king.'

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच राजा राज्यमनुप्राप्य दुर्लभं भरतर्षभ। अमित्रस्यातिवृद्धस्य कथं तिष्ठेदसाधनः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O foremost of Bharata's race, how a king, without the usual helps, having obtained a kingdom which is so valuable a possession, should treat a powerful enemy.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। सरितां चैव संवादं सागरस्य च भारत॥
en: Bhishma said-Regarding it is cited the old story of the discourse between the Ocean and the Rivers.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: सुरारिनिलयः शश्वत्सागरः सरिताम्पतिः। पप्रच्छ सरितः सर्वाः संशयं जातमात्मनः॥
en: In days of yore, eternal Ocean that lord of Rivers, that refuge of the enemies of the gods, asked all the Rivers for solving this doubt that had arisen in his mind.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: सागर उवाच समूलशाखान् पश्यामि निहतान् कायिनो दुमान्। युष्माभिरिह पूर्णाभिर्नास्तत्र न वेतसम्॥
en: The Ocean said Ye Rivers, I see that all of you, with our strong currents, wash away trees of huge trunks, with their roots and branches. You do not, however, ever bring to me a cane.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: अकायश्चाल्पसारश्च वेतसः कूलजश्च वः। अवज्ञया वा नानीतः किं च वा तेन वः कृतम्॥
en: The canes that grow on your banks have small stems and are not strong. Do you refuse to wash them down through contempt, or are they of any utility to you?

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि सर्वासामेव वो मतम्। यथा चेमानि कूलानि हित्वा नायाति वेतसः॥ तत्र प्राह नदी गङ्गा वाक्यमुत्तममर्थवत्। हेतुमद् ग्राहकं चैव सागरं सरिताम्पतिम्॥
en: I desire, therefore, to hear what is your motive about it. Indeed, why is it that canes, are not washed down by any of you from the banks were they grow?-Thus addressed, the River Ganga replied, to Ocean, that Lord of all Rivers, in these words of great significance, fraught with reason, and, therefore, liked of all.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: गङ्गोवाच तिष्ठन्त्येते यथास्थान नगा टेकनिकेतनाः। ते त्यजन्ति ततः स्थान प्रातिलोम्यान्न वेतसः॥
en: Ganga said Trees stand in one and the same place and are never displaced from where they stand. For this by their nature resisting our currents, they are obliged to leave the place of their growth. Canes, however, act otherwise.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: वेतसो वेगमायातं दृष्ट्वा नमति नापरे। सरिद्वेगेऽव्यतिक्रान्ते स्थानमासाद्य तिष्ठति॥
en: The cane, seeing the advancing current, bends to it. The others do not act in this way. After the current has passed away, the cane resumes its pristine posture.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: कालज्ञः समयज्ञश्च सदा वश्यश्च नोद्धतः। अनुलोमस्तथास्तब्धस्तेन नाभ्येति वेतसः॥
en: The cane is acquainted with the virtues of Time and opportunity. It is docile and obedient. It is yielding, but not stiff. Therefore, it stands where it grows, without being compelled to follow our current.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: मारुतोदकवेगेन ये नमन्त्युन्नमन्ति च। ओषध्यः पापदा गुल्मा न ते यान्ति पराभवम्॥
en: Those plants, trees, and creepers that bend and rise before the force of wind and water, are never rooted out.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: भीष्म उवाच यो हि शत्रोविवृद्धस्य प्रभोर्बन्धविनाशने। पूर्वं न सहते वेगं क्षिप्रमेव विनश्यति॥
en: Bhishma said-That person, who does not yield to the power of a powerful foe who has grown and who is competent to imprison or kill, soon meets with ruin.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: सारासारं बलं वीर्यमात्मनो द्विषतश्च यः। जानन् विचरति प्राज्ञो न स याति पराभवम्॥
en: That wise man, who acts after determining fully the strength and weakness, the power and energy, of himself and his enemies is never discomfitted.

description: The conduct of a king towards a powerful enemy
sn: एवमेव यदा विद्वान् मन्यतेऽतिबलं रिपुम्। संश्रयेद् वैतसी वृत्तिमेतत् प्रज्ञानलक्षणम्॥
en: An intelligent man, therefore, when he sees liis enemy to be more powerful than himself imitate the conduct of the cane. That is a sign of wisdom.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच विद्वान् मूर्खप्रगल्भेन मृदुतीक्ष्णेन भारत। आक्रुश्यमानः सदसि कथं कुर्यादरिंदम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said How, O Bharata, should a learned and modest man behave, O chastiser of foes, when attacked with harsh speeches in the court by an ignorant person puffed up with conceit?

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: भीष्म उवाच श्रूयतां पृथिवीपाल यथैषोऽर्थोऽनुगीयते। सदा सुचेताः सहते नरस्येहाल्पमेधसः।। :॥
en: Bhishma said Listen, O king, how this subject has been treated of (in the scriptures), i.e. how a person of good soul should endure in this world the abusive words of foolish persons.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: अरुष्यन् क्रुश्यमानस्य सुकृतं नाम विन्दति। दुष्कृतं चात्मनो मर्षी रुष्यत्येवापमाश् िवै॥
en: If a person, when abused my another, does not become irate, he is then sure to win the merit of all the good deeds that have been done by the abuser. The endurer, in such a case, transfers the demerit of all his own bad deeds to the person who being angry abuses him.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: टिट्टिभं तमुपेक्षेत वाशमानमिवातुरम्। लोकविद्वेषमापन्नो निष्फलं प्रतिपद्यते॥ इति संश्लाघते नित्यं तेन पापेन कर्मणा। इदमुक्तो मया कश्चित् सम्मतो जनसंसदि॥
en: An intelligent man should pay no attention to an utterer of abusive words who resembles, after all, only a Tittibha uttering dissonant notes. One, who is possessed by hate is said to live in vain. A fool is often heard to say,-I addressed such words to such a respectable man amid such an assembly of men!-and to cven boast of that wicked act.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: स तत्र वीडितः शुष्को मृतकल्पोऽवतिष्ठते। श्लाघन श्लाघनीयेन कर्मणा निरपत्रपः॥
en: He would add,-Abused by me, the man stood silent as if dead with shame!-Even thus does a shameless man boast of an act of which he should never boast.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: उपेक्षितव्यो यत्नेन तादृशः पुरुषाधमः। यद् यद् ब्रूयादल्पमतिस्तत्तदस्य सहेद्बुधः॥
en: Such a wretched wight should carefully be disregarded. The wise man should endure every thing that such a foolish person may say.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: प्राकृतो हि प्रशंसन् वा निन्दन वा किं करिष्यति। वने काक इवाबुद्धिर्वाशमानो निरर्थकम्॥
en: What can a vulgar person do by either his praise or blame? He is like a crow that caws uselessly in the forest.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: यदि वाग्भिः प्रयोगः स्यात् प्रयोगे पापकर्मणः। वागेवार्थो भवेत् तस्य न ह्येवार्थो जिघांसत्तः॥
en: If those, who blame others by only their words, could establish those accusations by such means, then, perhaps, their words would have been considered to be of some value. However, their words are as effective as those uttered by fools invoking death upon them with whom they fall out.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: निषेकं विपरीतं स आचष्टे वृत्तचेष्टया। मयूर इव कौपीनं नृत्यं संदर्शयन्निव॥
en: That man simply says that he is a bastard who indulges in such conduct and words. Indeed, he is like a peacock that dances while showing such a part of his body which should never be shown.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: यस्यावाच्यं न लोकेऽस्ति नाकार्यं चापि किंचन। वाचं तेन न संदध्याच्छुचिः संश्लिश्कर्मणा॥
en: A person of pure conduct should never even speak with that sinful person, who does not scruple to utter anything or do anything.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: प्रत्यक्षं गुणवादी यः परोक्षे चापि निन्दकः। स मानवः श्ववल्लोके नष्टलोकपरावरः॥
en: That man, who speaks of one's qualities when the latter marks him and who speaks ill of him when he does not see him, is really like a dog. Such a person does not acquire heaven and the fruits of any knowledge and virtue that he may have.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: तादृग्जनशतस्यापि यद्ददाति जुहोति च। परोक्षेणापवादी यस्तं नाशयति तत्क्षणात्॥
en: The man, who speaks ill of one in his absence, loses the fruits of all his libations on fire and of the gifts he may make to even a hundred persons.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: तस्मात् प्राज्ञो नरः सद्यस्तादृशं पापचेतसम्। वर्जयेत् साधुभिर्वयं सारमेयामिषं यथा।॥
en: A wise man, therefore, should unhesitatingly avoid such a sinful person who should always be shunned by all honest men, as he would avoid the flesh of the dog.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: परिवादं ब्रुवाणो हि दुरात्मा वै महाजने। प्रकाशयति दोषांस्तु सर्पः फणमिवोच्छ्रितम्॥
en: That wicked wretch, who mentions the faults of a high-souled person, really displays his own evil nature even as a snake shows his hood.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: तं स्वकर्माणि कुर्वाणं प्रतिकर्तुं य इच्छति। भस्मकूट इवाबुद्धिः खरो रजसि सज्जति॥
en: The sensible man, who tries to oppose such a back-biter always engaged in doing a work congenial to himself, finds himself in the painful situation of a stupid ass sunk in a heap of ashes.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: मनुष्यशालावृकमप्रशान्तं जनापवादे सततं निविष्टम्। मातङ्गमुन्मत्तमिवोन्नदन्तं त्यजेत तं श्वानमिवातिरौद्रम्॥
en: A man who always speaks ill of others, should be shunned like a furious wolf, or an infuriate elephant roaring madly, or a fierce dog.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: अधीरजुष्टे पथि वर्तमान दमादपेतं विनयाच्च पापम्। अरिव्रतं नित्यमभूतिकामं धिगस्तु तं पापमति मनुष्यम्॥
en: Fie on that sinful wretch, who has followed the footsteps of the foolish who has transgressed all healthy restraints and modesty, who always injures others, and who does not care for his own prosperity.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: प्रत्युच्यमानस्त्वभिभूय एर्भि र्निशाम्य मा भूस्त्वमथार्तरूपः। उच्चस्य नीचेन हि सम्प्रयोगं विगर्हयन्ति स्थिरबुद्धयो ये॥
en: If an honest man wishes to speak to such wretches when they try to humiliate him, he should thus be advised,-Do not allow yourself to be afflicted. A wordy torrents between a high and a low person is always disapproved by persons of sober intelligence.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: क्रुद्धो दशार्धेन हि ताडयेद् वा स पांसुभिर्वा विकिरेत् तुषैर्वा। विवृत्य दन्तांश्च विभीषयेद् वा सद्ध हि मूढे कुपिते नृशंसे॥
en: A slanderous wretch, when influenced by an anger, may strike another with his palms, or throw dust or chaff at another, or frighten another by showing or grinding his teeth. But all this is well-known.

description: The conduct of a learned man when insulted with harsh words in a court.
sn: विगर्हणां परमदुरात्मना कृतां सहेत यः संसदि दुर्जनान्नरः। पठेदिदं चापि निदर्शनं सदा न वाड्मयं स लभति किंचिदप्रियम्॥
en: That man, who bears the reproaches and slanders of wicked men uttered in assemblies, or who reads frequently these instructions, never suffers any pain from words.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामह महाप्राज्ञ संशयो मे महानयम्। संछेत्तव्यस्त्वया राजन् भवान् कुलकरो हि नः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O you of great wisdom, I have one great doubt which perplexes me! You should, O king, remove it! You are a promoter of our family.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: पुरुषाणामयं तात दुर्वृत्तानां दुरात्मनाम्। कथितो वाक्यसंचारस्ततो विज्ञापयामि ते॥
en: You have described to us the slanderous speeches uttered by wicked men of bad conduct. I desire, however, to question you further.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: यद्धितं राज्यतन्त्रस्य कुलस्य च सुखोदयम्। आयत्यां च तदात्वे च क्षेमवृद्धिकरं च यत्॥ पुत्रपौत्राभिरामं च राष्ट्रवृद्धिकरं च यत्। अन्नपाने शरीरे च हितं यत्तद् ब्रवीहि मे॥
en: That which is beneficial to a kingdom, that which yields happiness to the family of kings, that which yields good and advancement in the future and the present, that which is good regarding food, drink and the body, are topics upon which I wish you to dwell.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: अभिषिक्तो हि यो राजा राष्ट्रस्थो मित्रसंवृतः। ससुहृत्समुपेतो वा स कथं रजयेत् प्रजाः॥
en: How should a king, who has been put on the throne occupy it, surrounded by friends, ministers and servants, please his subjects?

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: यो ह्यसत्प्रग्रहरतिः स्नेहरागबलात्कृतः। इन्द्रियाणामनीशत्वादसज्जनबुभूषकः॥ तस्य भृत्या विगुणतां यान्ति सर्वे कुलोद्गताः। न च भृत्यफलैरथैः स राजा सम्प्रयुज्यते॥
en: That king, who, taken away by his natural propensities and proclivities, become devoted to evil companions, and flatters wicked men for his being under the influence of his senses, find all servants of good birth and blood displeased with him. Such a king never gets those objects the accomplishment of which depends upon one's having a number of good servants about him.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: एतन्मे संशयस्यास्य राजधर्मान् सुदुर्विदान्। बृहस्पतिसमो बुद्ध्या भवान् शंसितुमर्हति॥
en: You, who are equal to Brihaspati himself in intelligence, should describe to me these duties of kings which are difficult to be ascertained and thereby resolve my doubt.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: शंसिता पुरुषव्याघ्र त्वन्नः कुलहिते रतः। क्षत्ता चैको महाप्राज्ञो यो नः शंसति सर्वदा॥
en: You, O foremost of men, are ever engaged in encompassing the good of our family. For this reason you always describe to us on the duties of the kings. Endued with great wisdom, Vidura also gives always valuable instruction.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: त्वत्तः कुलहितं वाक्यं श्रुत्वा राज्यहितोदयम्। अमृतस्याव्ययस्येव तृप्तः स्वप्स्याम्यहं सुखम्॥
en: Hearing instructions from you which are productive of good to our family and kingdom, I shall be able to live happily like a person pleased with having drunk the immortal nectar.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: कीदृशाः संनिकर्षस्था भृत्याः सर्वगुणान्विताः। कीदृशैः किं कुलीनैर्वा सह यात्रा विधीयते॥
en: What classes of servants are to be considered as inferior and what as possessing all accomplishments? Helped by what class of servants or by servants of what kind of birth, should a king rule?

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: न ह्येको भृत्यरहितो राजा भवति रक्षिता। राज्यं चेदं जनः सर्वस्तत्कुलीनोऽभिकाङ्क्षति॥
en: If the king choose to act alone and without servants, he can never protect his people. All persons, however, of high birth wish for the acquisition of sovereignty? us

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: भीष्म उवाच न च प्रशास्तुं राज्यं हि शक्यमेकेन भारत। असहायवता तात नैवार्थाः केचिदप्युत॥ लब्धुं लब्धा ह्यपि सदा रक्षितुं भरतर्षभ।
en: Bhishma said The king, O Bharata, cannot along govern his kingdom. Without servants to help him, he cannot accomplish any object. Even if he gains any object, he cannot retain it.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: यस्य भृत्यजन: सर्वो ज्ञानविज्ञानकोविदः॥ हितैषी कुलजः स्निग्धः स राज्यफलमश्नुते॥
en: That king, whose servants are all gifted with knowledge and wisdom, who always seek the well being of their master, and who are of high birth and quiet disposition, enjoys the happiness of sovereignty.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: मन्त्रिणो यस्य कुलजा असंहार्याः सहोषिताः। नृपतेर्मतिदाः सन्तः सम्बन्धज्ञानकोविदाः॥ अनागतविधातार: कालज्ञानविशारदाः। अतिक्रान्तमशोचन्तः स राज्यफलम श्नुते॥
en: That king, whose ministers are all born in respectable families, incapable of being alienated from him, who always live with him, who always give advice to their master, who are endued with wisdom and goodness, who have a knowledge of all things, who can provide for future events and contingencies, who have a good knowledge of the virtues of time, and who never regret for the past, succeeds in enjoying the happiness of sovereignty.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: समदुःखसुखा यस्य सहायाः प्रियकारिणः। अर्थचिन्तापराः सत्याः स राज्यफलमश्नुते॥
en: That king, whose servants partake of his sorrows and joys, who always do what he likes, who always try to accomplish their maser's objects, and all of whom are faithful, enjoys the happiness of sovereignty.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: जनपदः संनिकर्षगतः सदा। अक्षुद्रः सत्पथालम्बी स राजा राज्यभाग्भवेत्॥ यस्य नार्तो
en: That king, whose subjects are always happy and magnanimous, and who always went to path of the righteous, enjoys the happiness of sovereignty.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: कोशाख्यपटलं यस्य कोशवृद्धिकरैर्नरैः। आप्तैस्तुष्टैश्च सततं चीयते स नृपोत्तमः॥
en: He is the best of kings, the various sources of whose revenue are managed and supervised by contented and trustworthy men who know fully the means of multiplying the finances.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: कोष्ठागारमसंहावैराप्तैः संचयतत्परैः। पात्रभूतैरलुब्धैश्च पाल्यमानं गुणी भवेत्॥
en: That king acquires great riches and merit whose repositories and barns are looked after by trustworthy, devoted, and uncovetous and scrupulous servants always always bent upon gathering.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: व्यवहारश्च नगरे यस्य कर्मफलोदयः। दृश्यते शंखलिखितः स धर्मफलभाङ् नृपः॥
en: That king in whose city justice is administered properly which leads to the fining the plaintiff or the defendant, if his case is untrue, and in which criminal laws are administered after the manner of Shankha and Likhita, acquires the merit of sovereignty.

description: The selection of servants and ministers by a king
sn: संगृहीतमनुष्यश्च यो राजा राजधर्मवित्। षड्वर्गं प्रतिगृह्णाति स धर्मफलमश्नुते॥
en: That king, who wins over subjects by kindness, who is master of the duties of kings, and who is mindful of six cardinal objects, acquires the merit of sovereignty.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। निदर्शनं परं लोके सज्जनाचरिते सदा॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the following ancient history. That history is considered as one of the greatest precedent amongst good and wisemen.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: अस्यैवार्थस्य सदृशं यच्छ्रुतं मे तपोवने। जामदग्न्यस्य रामस्य यदुक्तमृषिसत्तमैः॥
en: That history is connected with the present subject. I heard it in the asylum of Rama the son of Jamadagni, recited by many foremost of Rishis.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: वने महति कस्मिंश्चिदमनुष्यनिषेविते। ऋषिर्मूलफलाहारो नियतो नियतेन्द्रियः॥
en: In a certain large forest uninhabited by human beings, there lived an ascetic upon fruits and roots, practising rigid vows and with his senses under restraint.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: दीक्षादमपरः शान्तः स्वाध्यायपरमः शुचिः। उपवासविशुद्धात्मा सततं सत्त्वमास्थितः॥
en: Observing strict regulations and selfrestraint, of great and pure soul, always making Vedic recitations, and of heart purified by facts, he treated all creatures with goodness.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: तस्य संदृश्य सद्भावमुपविश्स्य धीमतः। सर्वे सत्त्वाः समीपस्था भवन्ति वनचारिणः॥
en: Highly intelligent, as he was, as he sat on his seat, the goodness of his conduct having been known to all the creatures that dwelt in that forest, they used to approach him with affection.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: सिंहव्याघ्रगणाः क्रूरा मत्ताश्चैव महागजाः। द्वीपिनः खङ्गभल्लूका ये चान्ये भीमदर्शनाः॥ ते सुखप्रश्नदाः सर्वे भवन्ति क्षतजाशनाः। तस्यर्षे: शिष्यवच्चैव न्यग्भूताः प्रियकारिणः॥
en: Dreadful lions and tigers, infuriate elephants of huge body, leopards, rhinoceroses, bears, and other dreadful animals, living upon blood, used to come to the Rishi and question him politely. Indeed, all of them behaved towards him like disciples and slaves and always did what was agreeable to him.,

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: दत्त्वा च ते सुखप्रश्नं सर्वे यान्ति यथागतम्। ग्राम्यस्त्वेकः पशुस्तत्रनाजहात् स महामुनिम्॥
en: Coming to him they made enquiries, and then went away to their respective habitations. One domestic animal, however, resided there permanently, never, leaving the ascetic at any time.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: भक्तोऽनुरक्तः सततमुपवासकृशोऽबलः। फलमूलोदकाहारः शान्तः शिष्टाकृतिर्यथा॥
en: He was greatly attached to the saint. Weak and emaciated with fasts, he lived upon fruits and roots and water, and was tranquil and of inoffensive character.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: तस्यर्षेरुपविश्स्य पादमूले महामते। मनुष्यवद्गतो भावो स्नेहबद्धोऽभवद् भृशम्॥
en: Lying at the feet of that great Rishi as the latter sat, the dog, with a humane heart, become greatly attached to him for the affection with which he was treated.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: ततोऽभ्ययान्महावीर्यो द्वीपी क्षतजभोजनः। स्वार्थमत्यन्तसंतुष्टः क्रूरकाल इवान्तकः॥
en: One day a very strong leopard came there, leaving upon blood. Of a cruel nature and always delighted at the prospect of prey, the dreadful animal looked like a second Yama.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: लेलिह्यमानस्तृषितः पुच्छास्फोटनतत्परः। व्यादितास्यः क्षुधाभुग्नः प्रार्थयानस्तदामिषम्॥
en: Licking the corners of his mouth with the tongue, and lashing his tail furiously, the leopard came there, stricken with hunger and thirst, with wide open jaws, desirous of catching the dog as his prey.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: दृष्ट्वा तं क्रूरमायान्तं जीवितार्थी नराधिप। प्रोवाच श्वा मुनिं तत्र तच्छृणुष्व विशाम्पते॥
en: Seeing that dreadful animal coming, O king, the dog, in fear of his life, spoke to the ascetic as follows. Listen to them, O king!-

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: श्वशत्रुर्भगवन्नेष द्वीपी मां हन्तुमिच्छति। त्वत्प्रसादाद् भयं न स्यादस्मान्मम महामुने॥ तथा कुरु महाबाहो सर्वज्ञस्त्वं न संशयः।
en: O Rishi, this leopard is an enemy of the dogs, It wishes to kill me. O great sage, do you so act that all my fears from this animal may be removed through your favour. O you of mighty arms, forsooth, you are omniscient.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: स मुनिस्तस्य विज्ञाय भावज्ञो भयकारणम्। रुतज्ञः सर्वसत्त्वानां तमैश्वर्यसमन्वितः॥
en: Reading the thoughts of all creatures, the sage felt that the dog had sufficient cause for fear. Endued with the six attributes and capable of reading the voices of all animals, the sage said as follows.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: मुनिरुवाच न भयं द्वीपीनः कार्यं मृत्युतस्ते कथंचन। एष श्वरूपरहितो द्वीपी भवसि पुत्रक॥
en: The sage said You shall have no fear of death from leopards any longer! Let your natural from disappear and be you a leopard, O son!

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: ततः श्वा द्वीपितां नीतो जाम्बूनदनिभाकृतिः। चित्राङ्गो विस्फुरदंष्ट्रो वने वसति निर्भयः॥
en: Thereat, the dog was metamorphosed into a leopard with skin bright as gold. With stripes on his body and with huge teeth, thenceforth he began to live in that forest fearlessly.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा सम्मुखे द्वीपी आत्मनः सदृशं पशुम्। अविरुद्धस्ततस्तस्य क्षणेन समपद्यत॥
en: Meanwhile, seeing before him an animal of his own species, the leopard, forthwith renounced all feelings of enmity towards it.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: ततोऽभ्ययान्महारौद्रो व्यादितास्यः क्षुधान्वितः। द्वीपीनं लेलिहद्वको व्याघ्रो रुधिरलालसः॥
en: Sometime after, there came into that asylum a dreadful and hungry tiger with mouth wide open. Licking the corners of his mouth with the tongue, and eagerly desirous of drinking blood, that tiger began to approach the animal that had been metamorphosed into a leopard.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: व्याघ्रं दृष्ट्वा क्षुधाभुग्नं दंष्ट्रिणं वनगोचरम्। द्वीपी जीवितरक्षार्थमृषिं शरणमेयिवान्॥
en: Seeing the hungry tiger of dreadful teeth approach that forest, the leopard sought the Rishi's protection for saving his life.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: संवासजं परं स्नेहमृषिणा कुर्वता तदा। स द्वीपी व्याघ्रतां नीतो रिपूणां बलवत्तरः॥
en: The sage, who had great affection for the leopard for its living in the same place with him, immediately transformed his leopard into a tiger powerful for all enemies.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: ततो दृष्ट्वा स शार्दूलो नाहनत् तं विशाम्पते। स तु श्वा व्याघ्रतां प्राप्य बलवान् पिशिताशनः॥ न मूलफलभोगेषु स्पृहामप्यकरोत् तदा।
en: The tiger seeing a beast of his own species did not injure him, O king. Having in course of time been metamorphosed into a powerful tiger living upon flesh and blood, the dog, abstained from his former food of fruits and roots.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: यथा मृगपतिर्नित्यं प्रकाइक्षति वनौकसः। तथैव स महाराज व्याघ्रः समभवत् तदा॥
