en: Indeed, from that time, O king, the transformed tiger lived, living upon the other animals of the forest, like a true king of beasts.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: भीष्म उवाच व्याघ्रश्चोटजमूलस्थस्तृप्तः सुप्तो हतैर्मृगैः। नागश्चागात् तमुद् देशं मत्तो मेघ इवोद्धतः॥
en: Bhishma said Gratified with the flesh of killed beasts, the dog metamorphosed into a tiger, slept at his ease. One day as he lay on the yard of the asylum, an infuriate elephant came there, resembling a cloud.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: प्रभिन्नकरटः प्रांशुः पद्मी विततकुम्भकः। सुविषाणो महाकायो मेघगम्भीरनिःस्वनः॥
en: Possessed of a huge stature, and rent cheeks, and having signs of the louts of his body, and with broad frontal globes, the animal had huge tusks and a voice deep as the muttering of the clouds.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा कुञ्जरं मत्तमायान्तं बलगर्वितम्। व्याघ्रो हस्तिभयात् त्रस्तस्तमृषि शरणं ययौ।॥
en: Seeing that infuriate elephant, proud of his strength, approach him, the tiger, moved with fear, sought refuge with the Rishi.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: ततोऽनयत् कुञ्जरत्वं व्यानं तमृषिसत्तमः। महामेघनिभं दृष्ट्वा स भीतो ह्यभवद् गजः॥
en: Thereupon that foremost of sages transformed the tiger into an elephant. Seeing an animal of his own species, the real elephant, huge as a mass of clouds, became afraid.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: ततः कमलपण्डानि शल्लकीगहनानि च। व्यचरत् स मुदायुक्तः पद्मरेणुविभूषितः॥
en: The Rishi's elephant then, covered with the filaments of lotus, dived gladly into lakes abounding with lotuses and walked by their banks filled with rabbit holes.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: कदाचिद् भ्रममाणस्य हस्तिनः सम्मुखं तदा। ऋषे स्तस्योटजस्थस्य कालोऽगच्छन्निशानिशम्॥ अथाजगाम तं देशं केसरी केसरारुणः। गिरिकन्दरजो भीमः सिंहो नागकुलान्तकः॥
en: Sufficient time passed away in this way. One day as the elephant was gladly passing along the vicinity of the asylum, there came before him a maned lion born in a mountain cave and accustomed to kill elephants.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा सिंहमायान्तं नागः सिंहभयार्दितः। ऋषि शरणमापेदे वेपमानो भयातुरः॥
en: Seeing the lion coming, the Rishi's elephant, from fear of life, began to tremble and sought refuge with the sage,

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: स ततः सिंहतां नीतो नागेन्द्रो मुनिना तदा। वन्यं नागणयत् सिंहं तुल्यजातिसमन्वयात्॥ दृष्ट्वा च सोऽभवत् सिंहो वन्यो भयसमन्वितः। स चाश्रमेऽवसत् सिंहस्तस्मिन्नेव महावने।॥
en: Thereupon the sage metamorphosed that prince of elephants into a lion. As the wild lion was an animal of the same species with him, the Rishi's lion no longer feared him. On the other hand, seeing a stronger beast of his own species before him, the wild lion became afraid.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: तद्भयात् पशवो नान्ये तपोवनसमीपतः। व्यदृश्यन्त तदा त्रस्ता जीविताकाक्षिणस्तथा॥
en: The Rishi's lion began to live in that asylumn within the forest. From fear of that animal, the other animals no longer ventured to approach the asylum. Indeed, they all seemed to be stricken with fear about the safety of their lives.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: कदाचित् कालयोगेन सर्वप्राणिविहिंसकः। बलवान् क्षतजाहारो नानासत्त्वभयंकरः॥ अष्टपादूर्ध्वनयनः शरभो वनगोचरः। तं सिहं हन्तुमागच्छन्मुनेस्तस्य निवेशनम्॥
en: Sometime after, one day a destroyer of all animals, endued with great strength, terrorising all creatures, having eight legs and eyes on the forehead, viz., a Sharabha, came there. He came to that very asylum for slaying the Rishi's lion.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: तं मुनिः शरभं चक्र बलोत्कटमरिंदम। ततः स शरभो वन्यो मुनेः शरभमग्रतः॥ दृष्ट्वा बलिनमत्युग्रं दुतं सम्प्राद्रवद् वनात्।
en: Seeing this, the sage transformed his lion into a very strong Sharabha. Seeing the Rishi's Sharabha before him more powerful than himself, the wild Sharabha forthwith fled away from that forest.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: स एवं शरभस्थाने संन्यस्तो मुनिना तदा॥ मुनेः पार्श्वगतो नित्यं शरभः सुखमाप्तवान्।
en: Having been thus metamorphosed into a Sharabha by the saint, the animal lived happily by the side of his transformer.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: ततः शरभसंत्रस्ताः सर्वे मृगगणास्तदा।॥ दिशः सम्प्राद्रवन् राजन् भयाज्जीवितकाक्षिणः।
en: All the animals then that lived in the neighbourhood were stricken with fear of that Sharabha. Their fear and the desire of saving their lives made them all fly away from that forest.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: शरभोऽन्प्यतिसंहष्टो नित्यं प्राणिवधे रतः॥ फलमूलाशनं कर्तुं नैच्छत् स पिशिताशनः।
en: Filled with delight, the Sharabha continued daily to kill animals for his food. Metamorphosed into a carnivorous beast, he no longer liked fruits and roots upon which he had lived before.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: ततो रुधिरतर्षेण बलिना शरभोऽन्वितः॥ इयेष तं मुनि हन्तुमकृतज्ञःश्वयोनिजः।
en: One day that ungrateful beast who had first been a dog but who was now metamorphosed into a Sharabha, eagerly thirsting for blood, wished to kill the sage.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: ततस्तेन तपःशक्त्या विदितो ज्ञानचक्षुषा॥ विज्ञाय स महाप्राज्ञो मुनिः श्वानं तमुक्तवान्।
en: The latter saw it all by his spiritual vision and ascetic power. Highly wise the sage, having learnt the object of the beast spoke to him these words.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: श्वा त्वं द्वीपित्वमापन्नो द्वीपी व्याघ्रत्वमागतः॥ व्याघ्रान्नागो मदपटुर्नागः सिंहत्वमागतः।
en: The sage said O dog, you were first metamorphosed into a leopard. From a leopard you were then made a tiger. From a tiger you became an elephant with the temporal juice trickling adown your cheeks. You were then transformed into a lion.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: सिंहस्त्वं बलमापन्नो भूयः शरभतां गतः॥ मया स्नेहपरीतेन विसृष्टो न कुलान्वयः।
en: From a powerful lion, you were then transformed into a Sharabha. Filled with love for you, it was I who transformed you into these various forms You did not, and do not belong by birth, to any of those species.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: यस्मादेवमपापं मां पाप हिंसितुमिच्छसि। तस्मात् स्वयोनिमापन्नः श्वैव त्वं हि भविष्यसि॥
en: Since, however, O sinful wretch, you wish to kill me who have done no injury to you, you will assume the form of your own species and be a dog again.

description: The story of the dog and leopard
sn: ततो मुनिजनद्वेष्टा दुष्टात्मा प्राकृतोऽबुधः। ऋषिणा शरभः शप्तस्तद्रूपं पुनराप्तवान्॥
en: After this, that mean, foolish, and wicked animal, transformed into a Sharabha, again for the Rishi's curse, put on his own proper form of a dog.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: भीष्म उवाच स श्वाप्रकृतिमापन्नः परं दैन्यमुपागतः। ऋषिणा हुकृतः पापस्तपोवनबहिष्कृतः॥
en: Having once more assumed his proper form, the dog became very dispirited. Chiding him the Rishi drove the sinful creature from his asylum.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: एवं राज्ञा मतिमता विदित्वा सत्यशौचताम्। आर्जवं प्रकृतिं सत्यं श्रुतं वृत्तं कुलं दमम्॥ अनुक्रोशं बलं वीर्यं प्रभावं प्रश्रयं क्षमाम्। भृत्याये यत्र योग्याः स्युस्तत्र स्थाप्या: सुरक्षिताः॥
en: Following this example an intelligent king should appoint servants, each fit for the office assigned to him, and exercise proper control over them, having first ascertained their qualifications of truthfulness, purity, sincerity, general disposition, knowledge of the scriptures, conduct, birth, self-control, mercy, ' strength, energy, dignity, and forgiveness.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: नापरीक्ष्य महीपाल: सचिवं कर्तुमर्हति। अकुलीननराकीर्णो न राजा सुखमेधते॥
en: A king should never appoint a minister without first having examined him. If a king has about him low-born persons he can never be happy.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: कुलजः प्राकृतो राज्ञा स्वकुलीनतया सदा। न पापे कुरुते बुद्धि भिद्यमानोऽप्यनागसि॥
en: Even if persecuted without any fault by his master, a person of high birth never thinks of, in consequence of the respectability of his blood, injuring his master.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: अकुलीनस्तु पुरुषः प्राकृतः साधुसंश्रयात्। दुर्लभैश्वर्यतां प्राप्तो निन्दितः शत्रुतां व्रजेत्॥
en: A mean and low-born individual, however, having obtained ever great riches from his connection with some honest men, becomes an enemy of the latter if he is merely reproached.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: कुलीनं शिक्षितं प्राज्ञं ज्ञानविज्ञानपारगम्। सर्वशास्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञं सहिष्णुं देशजं तथा॥ कृतज्ञं बलवन्तं च क्षान्तं दान्तं जितेन्द्रियम्। अलुब्धं लब्धसंतुष्टं स्वामिमित्रवुभूषकम्॥ सचिवं देशकालज्ञं सत्त्वसंग्रहणे रतम्। सततं युक्तमनसं हितैषिणमदन्द्रितम्॥ युक्तचारं स्वविषये संधिविग्रहकोविदम्। राज्ञस्त्रिवर्गवेत्तारं पौरजानपदप्रियम्॥ खातकव्यूहतत्त्वज्ञं बलहर्षणकोविदम्। इङ्गित्ताकारतत्त्वज्ञं यात्राज्ञानविशारदम्॥ हस्तिशिक्षासु तत्त्वज्ञमहंकारविवर्जितम्। प्रगल्भं दक्षिणं दान्तं बलिनं युक्तकारिणम्॥ चौक्षं चौक्षजनाकीर्णं सुमुखं सुखदर्शनम्। नायकं नीतिकुशलं गुणचेशसमन्वितम्॥ अस्तब्धं प्रश्रितं श्लक्ष्णं मृदुवादिनमेव च। धीरं शूरं महर्द्धिं च देशकालोपपादकम्॥
en: A minister should be possessed of high birth and strength; he should be forgiving for self-controlled, and have all his senses under restraint; he should be free from the vice of rapacity, contented with his just gain, pleased with the prosperity of his master and friends, well informed of the requirements place and time, ever engaged in attaching men to himself or his master by doing them good, always mindful of his duties seeking the good of his master, always careful faithful in the discharge of his own duties, a thorugh master of the art of war and peace, knowing full well king's requirements about three objects, beloved by both the citizens and the denizens of the provinces, acquainted with all kinds of battlearray for breaking the enemy's ranks, capable of gladdening the hearts of his master, and of reading signs and gestures, acquainted with all requirements about march, skilled in the art of training elephants, shorn of pride, confident of his own powers, clever in the transaction of business, always doing what is right, of fair conduct, surrounded by honest friends, of sweet speech, possessed of pleasing features, capable of leading men, well-versed in policy, endued with accomplishments, energetic in action, active, ingenuous, of a sweet temper, modest in conversation patient, brave, rich, and capable of taking measures according to the requirements of place and time.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: सचिवं यः प्रकुरुते न चैनमवमन्यते। तस्य विस्तीर्यते राज्यं ज्योत्स्ना ग्रहपतेरिव॥
en: That king, who gets such a minister can never be humiliated or defeated by any one. Indeed, his kingdom by and by spreads over the Earth like the light of the moon.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: एतैरेव गुणैर्युक्तो राजा शास्त्रविशारदः। एष्टव्यो धर्मपरमः प्रजापालनतत्परः॥
en: A king, again, who is well-read in the scriptures, who considers righteousness as being superior to everything, who always protects his subjects, and who is endued with the following virtues, secures the love of all. eftit wat ufarkingur: Gordt gelateral

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: शुश्रूषुः श्रुतवाश्रोता ऊहापोहविशारदः॥ मेधावी धारणायुक्तो यथान्यायोपपादकः। दान्तः सदा प्रियाभाषी क्षमावांश्च विपर्यये॥ दानाच्छेदे स्वयंकारी श्रद्धालुः सुखदर्शनः। आर्तहस्तप्रदो नित्यमाप्तामात्यो नये रतः॥ नाहंवादी न निर्द्वन्द्वो न यत्किचनकारकः। कृते कर्मण्यमात्यानां कर्ता भृत्यजनप्रियः॥
en: He should be patient, forgiving, of pure conduct, severe when necessity requires it, know the virtues of manliness, respectful towards his elder, possessed of a knowledge of the scriptures, ready to listen to the instructions and advice of competent men, capable of judging correctly from amongst the various course of action suggested to him, intelligent, of a retentive memory, ready to do what is just, self-controlled, always sweet-speeched, forgiving even to enemies, practising charity personally, possessed of faith, of lovely features, ready to help distressed persons, having ministers who always seek his wellbeing, free from egoism, never without a wife, and undisposed to do anything hastily. He should always reward his ministers when they perform anything great. He should love those who are devoted to him.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: संगृहीतजनोऽस्तब्धः प्रसन्नवदनः सदा। सदा भृत्यजनापेक्षी न क्रोधी सुमहामनाः॥
en: Avoiding idleness, he should always win over men by doing them good. He should always be cheerful in appearance. He should always look to the wants of his servants and never yield to anger. He should should be magnanimous.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: युक्तदण्डो न निर्दण्डो धर्मकार्यानुशासनः। चारनेत्रः प्रजावेक्षी धर्मार्थकुशलः सदा॥ राजा गुणशताकीर्ण एष्टव्यस्तादृशो भवेत्। योधाश्चैव मनुष्येन्द्र सर्वे गुणगणैर्वृताः॥
en: Without laying aside the rod of Punishment he should hold it with propriety. He should make all men about him act fairly. Having spies for his eyes, he should always look after the affairs of his subjects, and should be a master of all matters relating to virtue and wealth. A king, who endued with these hundred qualifications, acquires the love of all. Every king should attempt to be such. of

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: अन्वेष्टव्याः सुपुरुषाः सहाया राज्यधारणे। न विमानयितव्यास्ते राज्ञा वृद्धिमभीप्सता॥ योधाः समरशौटीराः कृतज्ञाः शस्त्रकोविदाः। धर्मशास्त्रसमायुक्ताः पदातिजनसंवृताः॥ अभया गजपृष्ठस्था रथचर्याविशारदाः। इष्वस्त्रकुशला यस्य तस्येयं नृपतेमही॥
en: The king should also, O king, seek out good warriors possessed the necessary qualifications, for helping him in protecting his kingdom. A king, who seeks his own advancement, should never disregard his army. That king, whose soldiers are brave in battle, grateful in conduct, and well-read in the scriptures, whose army consists of infantry thoroughly versed in the works on religion and duty, whose elephant-warriors are brave, whose car-warriors are skilled in their own mode of fighting and well-versed in discharging arrows and in holding other weapons, succeeds in subjugating the whole Earth.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: सर्वसंग्रहणे युक्तो नृपो भवति यः सदा। उत्थानशीलो मित्राढ्यः स राजा राजसत्तमः॥
en: That king, who always tries to win over men to himself, who is ready for work, who is rich in friends and allies, becomes the foremost of king.

description: The qualifications of a minister and a king
sn: शक्या चाश्वसहस्रेण वीरारोहेण भारत। संगृहीतमनुष्येण कृत्स्ना जेतुं वसुन्धरा॥
en: A king, who has won over all men to himself, may, O Bharata, with the help of even a thousand brave horsemen, succeed in conquering the entire Earth.'

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवं गुणयुतान् भृत्यान् स्वे स्वे स्थाने नराधिपः। नियोजयति कृत्येषु स राज्यफलमश्नुते॥ न श्वा स्वं स्थानमुत्क्रम्य प्रमाणमभिसत्कृतः। आरोष्यः श्वा स्वकात्स्थानादुत्क्रम्यान्यत् प्रमाद्यति॥
en: Bhishma said Following the lesson drawn from the story of the dog, that king, who appoints his servants to offices for which each is, competent, enjoys the happiness of sovereignty. A dog should not, with becoming honours, be posted in a position far above that for which he is fit. If a dog be posted above that situation which is fit for him, he becomes inebriate with haughtiness.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: स्वजातिगुणसम्पन्नाः स्वेषु कर्मसु संस्थिताः। प्रकर्तव्या ह्यमात्यास्तु नास्थाने प्रक्रिया क्षमा।॥
en: Ministers should be appointed to offices for which they are competent and should possess accomplishments necessary for the same. Appointment of unworthy persons is not at all approved.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: अनुरूपाणि कर्माणि भृत्येभ्यो यः प्रयच्छति। स भृत्यगुणसम्पन्नो राजा फलमुपाश्नुते॥
en: That king, who appoints servants to offices for which each is competent, succeeds, for such merit, to enjoy the happiness of sovereignty.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: शरभः शरभस्थाने सिंहः सिंह इवोर्जितः। व्याघ्रो व्याघ्र इव स्थाप्यो द्वीपी द्वीपी यथा तथा॥
en: A Sharabha should occupy the position of Sharabha; a lion should be elated with the power of lion; a tiger; should be placed in the position of a tiger, and a leopard should be placed in that of a leopard.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: कर्मस्विहानुरूपेषु न्यस्या भृत्या यथाविधि। प्रतिलोमं न भृत्यास्ते स्थाप्याः कर्मफलैषिणा॥
en: Servants should according to the scriptural injunction, be appointed to offices for which each is competent. If you wish to achieve success, you should never appoint servants in offices higher than what they deserve.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: यः प्रमाणमतिक्रम्य प्रतिलोमं नराधिपः। भृत्यान् स्थापयतेऽबुद्धिर्न स रञ्जयते प्रजाः॥
en: That foolish king, who, disregarding precedent, appoints servants to offices for which they are not fit, fails to please his people.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: न बालिशा न च क्षुद्रा नाप्राज्ञा नाजितेन्द्रियाः। नाकुलीना नराः सर्वे स्थाप्या गुणगणैषिणा॥
en: A king, who wishes to have accomplished servants should never appoint persons who are shorn of intelligence, who are low-minded, who are without wisdom, who are not masters of their senses, and who are not highly born.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: साधवः कुलजाः शूरा ज्ञानवन्तोऽनसूयकाः। अक्षुद्राः शुचयो दक्षाः स्युनरा: पारिपार्श्वकाः॥
en: Men, who are honest, born in high family, brave, learned, shorn of malice and envy, noble, pure in conduct, and clever in business, deserve to be appointed as minister.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: न्यग्भूतास्तत्पराः शान्ताश्चौक्षाः प्रकृतिजैः शुभाः। स्वस्थानानपक्रुष्टा ये ते स्यू राज्ञा बहिश्चराः॥
en: Persons, who are humble, always ready to perform their duties, of a peaceful nature, pure in mind, adorned with various other gifts of nature, and are never spoken ill of for the offices they hold should be the intimate companions of the king.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: सिंहस्य सततं पार्वे सिंह एवानुगो भवेत्। असिंहः सिंहसहितः सिंहवल्लभते फलम्॥
en: A lion should always associate with a lion, If one that is not a lion associates with a lion, it acquires all the advantages that belong to a lion.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: यस्य सिंहः श्रुभिः कीर्णः सिंहकर्मफले रतः। न स सिंहफलं भोक्तुं शक्तः श्वभिरुपासितः॥
en: That lion, however who while performing the duties of a lion, has a pack of dogs only for his companions, never succeeds for such companionship, in performing those duties.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: एवमेतन्मनुष्येन्द्र शूरैः प्राज्ञैर्बहुश्रुतैः। कुलीनैः सह शक्येत कृत्स्ना जेतुं वसुन्धरा॥
en: Thus, O monarch, a king may succeed in subjugating the entire Earth if he has for his ministers men endued with courage, wisdom, great learning, and high-birth.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: नाविद्यो नानृजुः पार्श्वे नाप्राज्ञो नामहाधनः। संग्राह्यो वसुधापालै त्यो भृत्यवतां वर॥
en: O foremost of kings, kings should never keep a servant who is shorn of learning, sincerity, wisdom and great wealth.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: बाणवद्विसृता यान्ति स्वामिकार्यपरा नराः। ये भृत्याः पार्थिवहितास्तेषां सान्त्वं प्रयोजयेत्॥
en: Those men who are devoted to the master proceed unimpeded like arrows. Kings should always speak sweet words to those servants who are always busy with doing good to their masters.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: कोशश्च सततं रक्ष्यो यत्नमास्थाय राजभिः। कोशमूला हि राजानः कोशो वृद्धिकरो भवेत्॥
en: Kings, should, always, diligently look after their treasuries. Indeed, kings depend on their treasuries A king should, always, try to swell his treasures.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: कोष्ठागारं च ते नित्यं ज्ञफीतैर्धान्यैःसुसंवृतम्। सदास्तु सत्सु संन्यस्तं धनधान्यपरो भव॥
en: Let your barns, O king, be filled with corn. And let them be entrusted to honest servants. Do your try to increase your wealth and corn.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: नित्ययुक्ताश्च ते भृत्या भवन्तु रणकोविदाः। वाजिनां च प्रयोगेषु वैशारद्यमिहेष्यते॥
en: Let your servants, skilled in battle, always attend to their duties. It is desirable that they should be skilful in the management of horses.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: ज्ञातिबन्धुजनावेक्षी मित्रसम्बन्धिसंवृतः। पौरकार्यहितान्वेषी भव कौरवनन्दन॥
en: O delighter of the Kurus, Look to the wants of your kinsmen and friends. Be encircled by friends and relatives. Seek the good of your city.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: एषा ते नैष्ठिकी बुद्धिः प्रजास्वभिहिता मया। शुनो निदर्शनं तात किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि।॥
en: By mentioning the example of the dog I have instructed you about the duties you should adopt towards your subjects. What further do you wish to hear?' O delighter of the Kurus, Look to the wants of your kinsmen and friends. Be encircled by friends and relatives. Seek the good of your city.

description: The fruits of appointing right men in right places
sn: एषा ते नैष्ठिकी बुद्धिः प्रजास्वभिहिता मया। शुनो निदर्शनं तात किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि।॥
en: By mentioning the example of the dog I have instructed you about the duties you should adopt towards your subjects. What further do you wish to hear?'

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच राजवृत्तान्यनेकानि त्वया प्रोक्तानि भारत। पूर्वैः पूर्वनियुक्तानि राजधर्मार्थवेदिभिः॥१॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have, O Bharata, described the many duties of king-craft, which were observed and laid down in days of yore by persons of ancient times conversant with royal duties.

sn: तदेव विस्तरेणोक्तः पूर्वदृष्टं सतां मतम्। प्रणेयं राजधर्माणां प्रब्रूहि भरतर्षभ॥
en: You have, indeed, described fully those duties as approved by the wise. Do you, however, O foremost of Bharata's race give us an abridgement of the same, so that we may keep it in memory.

sn: भीष्म उवाच रक्षणं सर्वभूतानामिति क्षात्रं परं मतम्। तद् यथा रक्षणं कुर्यात् तथा शृणु महीपते॥
en: Bhishma said The protection of all creatures is considered the highest duty of the Kshatriya. Listen now to me, o king, as to how the duty of protection to be performed.

sn: यथा बर्हाणि चित्राणि बिभर्ति भुजगाशनः। तथा बहुविधं राजा रूपं कुर्वीत धर्मवित्॥
en: A king conversant with his duties should put on many forms and the peacock displays plumes of various hues.

sn: तैक्ष्ण्यं जिह्मत्वमादाल्भ्यं सत्यमार्जवमेव च। मध्यस्थः सत्त्वमातिष्ठंस्तथा वै सुखमृच्छति॥
en: Keenness, crookedness, truth, and sincerity, are the qualities which should be present in him. He should practise impartially the qualities of goodness if he is to acquire happiness.

sn: यस्मिन्नर्थे हितं यत् स्यात् तद्वर्ण रूपमादिशेत्। बहुरूपस्य राज्ञो हि सूक्ष्मोऽप्यर्थो न सीदति॥
en: He must assume that particular colour or form which is beneficial for the particular object which he tries to achieve. A king who can put on various forms succeeds in achieving even the most subtile objects.

sn: नित्यं रक्षितमन्त्रः स्याद् यथा मूकः शरच्छिखी। श्लक्ष्णाक्षरतनुः श्रीमान् भवेच्छास्त्रविशारदः॥
en: Dumb like the peacock in autumn, he should keep his counsels close. He should speak little and that little should be sweet. He should be of good features and well-read in the scriptures.

sn: आपद्वारेषु युक्तः स्याज्जलप्रस्त्रवणेष्विव। शैलवर्षोदकानीव द्विजान् सिद्धान् समाश्रयेत्। अर्थकामः शिखां राजा कुर्याद्धर्मध्वजोपमाम्॥
en: He should always be very careful about those gates through which dangers may come and befall him, like men guarding breaks in embankments through which the waters of large tanks may rush and flood their fields and houses. He should seek the protection of Brahmanas crowned with ascetic success as men seek the refuge of powerful rivers caused by the rain-water deposited within mountain lakes. That king, who wishes to amass riches should act like religious hypocrites who keep Sikha or tuft of hair.

sn: नित्यमुद्यतदण्डः स्यादाचरेदप्रमादतः। लोके चायव्ययौ दृष्ट्वा बृहवृक्षमिवास्त्रवत्॥
en: The king should always have the rod of Punishment uplifted in his hands. He should always levy taxes carefully after examining the incomes and expenses of his subjects, like men going to a full-grown palmyra for drawing juice.

sn: जावान् स्यात् स्वयूथ्येषु भौमानि चरणैः क्षिपेत्। जातपक्षः परिस्पन्देत् प्रेक्षेद् वैकल्यमात्मनः॥
en: He should treat equitably his own subjects; cause the crops of his enemies to be crushed by the foot of his cavalry, march against enemies when his own wings have become strong; and mark all the sources of his own weakness.

sn: दोषान् विवृणुयाच्छत्रोः परपक्षान् विधूनयेत्। काननेष्विव पुष्पाणि बहिरर्थान् समाचरन्॥
en: He should announce the faults of his enemies; crush those who are their partisans; and collect riches from outside like a person plucking flowers from the forest.

sn: उच्छ्रितान् नाशयेत् स्फीतान् नरेन्द्रानचलोपमान्। श्रयेच्छायामविज्ञातां गुप्तं रणमुपाश्रयेत्॥
en: He should kill those foremost of kings who are puffed up with might and stand with upraised heads like mountains; by bribing the governors of the forests and by ambuscades and sudden attacks.

sn: प्रावृषीवासितग्रीवो मज्जेत निशि निर्जने। मायूरेण गुणेनैव स्त्रीभिश्चालक्षितश्चरेत्॥
en: Like the peacock in the rains, he should enter his nightly habitations alone and unseen. Indeed, he should enjoy, like the peacock, within his inner apartments, the company of his wives.

sn: न जह्याच्च तनुत्राणं रक्षेदात्मानमात्मना। चारभूमिष्वभिगतान् पाशांश्च परिवर्जयेत्॥
en: He should not put off his coat of mail. He should himself guard his own self and avoid the nets spread out for him by the spies and secret agents of his enemies.

sn: प्रणयेद् वापि तां भूमि प्रणश्येद् गहने पुनः। हन्यात्क्रुद्धानतिविषांस्तान् जिह्मगतयोऽहितान्॥ नाशयेद् बलबर्हाणि संनिवासान् निवासयेत्। सदा बर्हिनिभः कामं प्रशस्तं कृतमाचरेत्। सर्वतश्चाददेत् प्रज्ञा पतङ्गं गहनेष्विव॥
en: He should also gain over the spies of his enemies, but destroy them fully when opportunity presents itself. Like the peacocks the king should destroy his powerful and angry foes of crooked policy, and kill their force and drive them away from home. The king should also like the peacocks do what is good to him, and gather wisdom from all sides as they collect insects even from the forest.

sn: एवं मयूरवद् राजा स्वराज्यं परिपालयेत्। आत्मवृद्धिकरी नीतिं विदधीत विचक्षणः॥
en: An wise and peacock-like king should thus govern his kingdom and pursue a policy which is good for him.

sn: आत्मसंयमनं बुद्ध्या परबुद्ध्यावधारणम्। बुद्ध्या चात्मगुणप्राप्तिरेतच्छास्त्रनिदर्शनम्॥
en: By dint of his own intelligence, he should determine what he is to do. By consulting with others he should either leave off or conform such resolution. Helped by that intelligence which is sharpened by the scriptures, one can fix his courses of action. Herein consists the utility of the scriptures.

sn: परं विश्वासयेत् साम्ना स्वशक्तिं चोपलक्षयेत्। आत्मनः परिमर्शेन बुद्धि बुद्ध्या विचारयेत्॥
en: By following the means of conciliation, he should create confidence in the hearts of his enemies. He should show his own strength. By judging of various courses of action in his own mind he should by dint of his own intelligence, make his decision.

sn: सान्त्वयोगमतिः प्राज्ञः कार्याकार्यप्रयोजकः। निगूढबुद्धेर्धारस्य वक्तव्ये वा कृतं तथा॥
en: The king should be a master of the arts of conciliating policy; he should be endued with wisdom and should be able to do what should be done and avoid the otherwise. A highly wise and intelligent person does not require counsels or instruction.

sn: स निकृष्टां कथां प्राज्ञो यदि बुद्ध्या बृहस्पतिः। स्वभावमेष्यते तप्तं कृष्णायसमिवोदके॥ अनुयुञ्जीत कृत्यानि सर्वाण्येव महीपतिः। आगमैरुपदिशनि स्वस्य चैव परस्य च॥
en: A wise man, who is endued with the intelligence of Brihaspati, if he incurs obloquy, soon regains his true nature like heated iron dipped in water. A king should perform objects, of his own or of others, according to the injunctions of the scriptures.

sn: मृदुशीलं तथा प्राज्ञं शूरं चार्थविधानवित्। स्वकर्मणि नियुञ्जीत ये चान्ये च बलाधिकाः॥
en: A king, who knows well the means of acquiring riches, should always engage in his acts such men as are mild by nature and endued with wisdom, courage and great strength.

sn: अथ दृष्ट्वा नियुक्तानि स्वानुरूपेषु कर्मसु। सर्वांस्ताननुवर्तेत स्वरांस्तन्त्रीरिवायता॥
en: Seeing his servants employed in acts for which each is fit, the king should act in unision with them like the strings of a musical instrument, set to proper tension, according with their notes.

sn: धर्माणामविरोधेन सर्वेषां प्रियमाचरेत्। ममायमिति राजा यः स पर्वत इवाचलः॥
en: The king should do good to all persons without violating the injunctions of Righteousness. That king stands firm as a rock whom everybody regards-He is mine.

sn: व्यवसायं समाधाय सूर्यो रश्मीनिवायतान्। धर्ममेवाभिरक्षेत कृत्वा तुल्ये प्रियाप्रिये॥
en: While settling the claims of litigants, the king, without making any difference between persons who are liked and those who are disliked by him, should preserve justice.

sn: कुलप्रकृतिदेशानां धर्मज्ञान् मृदुभाषिणः। मध्ये वयसि निर्दोषान् हिते युक्तानविक्लवान्॥ अलुब्धाशिक्षितान् दान्तान् धर्मेषु परिनिष्ठितान्। स्थापयेत् सर्वकार्येषु राजा धर्मार्थरक्षिणः॥
en: The king should appoint in all his offices such men as know very well the characteristics of particular families of the people in general and of various countries; as are mild in words; as are of middle age; as have no shortcomings, as are devoted to good acts; as are never careless; as are free from rapacity; as are possessed of learning and self-control; and as are firm in virtue and always ready to preserve the interests of both virtue and profit.

sn: एतेन च प्रकारेण कृत्यानामागतिं गतिम्। युक्तः समनुतिष्ठेत तुष्टश्चारैरुपस्कृतः॥
en: In this way, having determined the course of actions and their final ends, the king should accomplish them carefully; and instructed in all matters by his spies, he may live happily.

sn: अमोघक्रोधहर्षस्य स्वयं कृत्यान्ववेक्षितुः । आत्मप्रत्ययकोशस्य वसुधैव वसुन्धरा॥
en: That king, who never yields to anger and joy without sufficient cause, who looks after all his acts himself, and who superintends his income and expenditure with his own eyes, succeeds in acquiring great wealth from the Earth.

sn: व्यक्तश्चानुग्रहो यस्य यथार्थश्चापि निग्रहः। गुप्तात्मा गुप्तराष्ट्रश्च स राजा राजधर्मवित्॥
en: That king is a master of his royal duties who rewards his officers and subjects publicly, who punishes those who deserve punishment, who protects his own self, and who protects his kingdom from very evil.

sn: नित्यं राष्ट्रमवेक्षेत गोभिः सूर्य इवोदितः। चरान् स्वनुचरान् विद्यात् तथा बुद्ध्या स्वयं चरेत्।।
en: Like the Sun shedding his rays upon everything underneath, the king should always look after his kingdom himself, and helped by his intelligence, be should supervise all his spies and officers.

sn: कालं प्राप्तमुपादद्यान्नार्थं राजा प्रसूचयेत्। अहन्यहनि संदुह्यान्महीं गामिव बुद्धिमान्॥
en: The king should collect wealth from his subjects at the proper time. He should never announce what he does. Like an intelligent person milking his cow every day, the king should milk his kingdom everyday.

sn: यथा क्रमेण पुष्पेभ्यश्चिनोति मधु षट्पदः। तथा द्रव्यमुपादाय राजा कुर्वीत संचयम्॥
en: As the bee gathers honey from flowers gradually, the king should collect wealth gradually from his kingdom for keeping it in store.

sn: यद्धि गुप्तावशिष्टं स्यात् तद्वित्तं धर्मकामयोः। संचयान्न विसर्गी स्याद् राजा शास्त्रविदात्मवान्॥
en: Having kept apart a sufficient portion, he should with the remaining portion, acquire religious merit and gratify his desires for pleasure. That king, who is acquainted with duties and who is gifted with intelligence, would never squander what has been stored.

sn: नार्थमल्पं परिभवेन्नावमन्येत शात्रवान्। बुद्ध्या तु बुद्ध्येदात्मानं न चाबुद्धिषु विश्वसेत्॥
en: The king should never disregard any wealth, however little it may be; he should never belittle his foes for their powerlessness; he should by his own intelligence, examine his ownself; he should never place confidence in ignorant persons.

sn: धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं संयमो बुद्धिरात्मा धैर्य शौर्य देशकालाप्रमादः। अल्पस्य वा बहुनो वा विवृद्धौ धनस्यैतान्यष्ट समिन्धनानि॥ अग्निः स्तोको वर्धतेऽप्याज्यसिक्तो बीजं चैकं रोहसहस्रमेति। आयव्ययौ विपुलौ संनिशाम्य तस्मादल्पं नावमन्येत वित्तम॥
en: Steadiness, cleverness, self-control, intelligence, health, patience, bravery, and attention to the requirements of time and place,-these eight qualities always multiply wealth, be it small or be it much. A little fire, fed with clarified butter, may end into a conflagration. A single seed may produce a thousand trees. A king, therefore, even when he knows that his income and expenditure are great, should not neglect the smaller items.

sn: बालोऽप्यबालः स्थविरो रिपुर्यः सदा प्रमत्तं पुरुषं निहन्यात्। कालेनान्यस्तस्य मूलं हरेत कालज्ञाता पार्थिवानां वरिष्ठः॥
en: An enemy, whether he be a child, a young man, or an aged one, succeeds in killing a careless person. An insignificant enemy, when he becomes powerful, may root out a king. A king, therefore, who is conversant with the requirements of time is the greatest of all kings.

sn: हरेत् कीर्ति धर्ममस्योपरुर्ध्या दर्थे दीर्घ वीर्यमस्योपहन्यात्। रिपुढेष्टा दुर्बलो वा बली वा तस्माच्छनोनॆव हीयेद् यतात्मा॥
en: An enemy, strong or weak, impelled by malice, may very soon destroy the fame of a king, impede the acquisition of religious merit by him; and deprive him of even his energy. Therefore, a king, who is of a controlled mind, should never be careless when he has an enemy.

sn: क्षयं वृद्धिं पालनं संचयं वा बुद्ध्वाप्युभौ संहतौ सर्वकामौ। ततश्चान्यन्मतिमान्संदधीत तस्माद् राजा बुद्धिमत्तां श्रयेत॥
en: If an intelligent king desires for riches and victory, he should after knowing his expenditure, income, savings, and administration, make either peace or war. For this reason the king should seek the help of an intelligent minister.

sn: बुद्धिर्दीप्ता बलवन्तं हिनस्ति बलं बुद्ध्या पाल्यते वर्धमानम्। शत्रुर्बुद्ध्या सीदते वर्धमानो बुद्धेः पश्चात् कर्म यत्तत् प्रशस्तम्॥
en: even a ever Brilliant intelligence weakens powerful person; by intelligence the growing power may be protected; a growing enemy is weakened by the help of intelligence; therefore, work which is undertaken with intelligence is deserving of praise.

sn: सर्वान् कामान् कामयानो हि धीरः सत्त्वेनाल्पेनाप्नुते हीनदोषः। यश्चात्मानं प्रार्थयतेऽर्थ्यमानैः श्रेयःपात्रं पूरयते च नाल्यम्॥
en: A king, who is patient and without any fault, may, if he likes, obtain the fruition of all his wishes, with the help of even a small force. That king, however, who wishes to be encircled by a number of self-seeking flatterers, can never derive the smallest benefit.

sn: तस्माद् राजा प्रगृहीतः प्रजासु मूलं लक्ष्म्याः सर्वशो ह्याददीत। दीर्घ कालं ह्यपि सम्पीड्यमानो विद्युत्सम्पातमपि वा नोजितः स्यात्॥
en: For these reasons, the king, should mildly colleci wealth from his subjects. If a king continually oppresses his people, he is destroyed like a flash of lighting that shines only for a second.

sn: विद्या तपो वा विपुलं धनं वा सर्वं ह्येतद् व्यवसायेन शक्यम्। बुद्ध्यायत्तं तन्निवसेद् देहवत्सु तस्माद् विद्याद् व्यवसायं प्रभूतम्॥
en: Learning, penances, immense wealth, indeed, everything, can be acquired by exertion. Exertion of embodied creatures is governed by intelligence. Exertion, therefore, is the greatest of all things.

sn: यत्रासते मतिमन्तो मनस्विनः शको विष्णुर्यत्र सरस्वती च। वसन्ति भूतानि च यत्र नित्यं तस्माद् विद्वान् नावमन्येत देहम्॥
en: The human body is the habitation of many intelligent, and energetic creatures, of Shakra, of Vishnu, of Sarasvati and of other brings. A learned men, therefore, should never disregard the body.

sn: लुब्धं हन्यात् सम्प्रदानेन नित्यं लुब्धस्तृप्तिं परवित्तस्य नैति। सर्वो लुब्धः कर्मगुणोपभोगे योऽर्थींनो धर्मकामौ जहाति।॥
en: A covetous man should be brought under control by continued presents. He that covetous is never satiated with taking other people's riches, Every one, however, becomes covetous of happiness. If a person, therefore, becomes destitute of wealth, he becomes shorn of virtue and pleasure.

sn: धनं भोगं पुत्रदारं समृद्धिं सर्वं लुब्धः प्रार्थयते परेषाम्। लुब्धे दोषाः सम्भवन्तीह सर्वे तस्माद् राजा न प्रगृह्णीत लुब्धम्॥
en: A covetous man seeks to take to himself the riches, the enjoyments, the sons and daughters, and the affluence of others. Every kind of fault is seen in covetous men. The king, therefore, should never appoint a covetous man as his minister or officer.

sn: संदर्शनेन पुरुषं जघन्यमपि चोदयेत्। आरम्भान् द्विषतां प्राज्ञः सर्वार्थाश्च प्रसूदयेत्॥
en: A king should even sent a low person to ascertain the disposition and doings of his enemies. A wise king should frustrate all the attempts and objects of his enemies.

sn: धर्मान्वितेषु विज्ञाता मन्त्री गुप्तश्च पाण्डव। आप्तो राजा कुलीनश्च पर्याप्तो राजसंग्रह॥
en: That confident and high-born king who seeks instruction from learned and pious Brahmanas and who is protected by his ministers, can keep all his tributary chiefs under proper control.

sn: विधिप्रयुक्तान् नरदेवधर्मा नुक्तान् समासेन निबोध बुद्ध्या। इमान् विदध्याद् व्यतिसृत्य यो वै राजा महीं पालयितुं स शक्तः॥
en: O king, I have briefly described to you of all the duties laid down in the scriptures. Attend to them, helped by your intelligence. That king, who, in obeying his protector, attends to these, succeeds in ruling the whole Earth.

sn: अनीतिजं यस्य विधानजं सुखं हठप्रणीतं विधिवत्प्रदृश्यते। न विद्यते तस्य गतिर्महीपर्ते न विद्यते राज्यसुखं ह्यनुत्तमम्॥
en: That king, who neglects the happiness which policy yields and seeks for that which chance may bring, never succeeds in enjoying the happiness of sovereignty or in acquiring blissful regions hereafter.

sn: धनैर्विशिष्टान् मतिशीलपूजितान् गुणोपपन्नान् युधि दृष्टविक्रमान्। गुणेषु दृष्ट्वा न चिरादिवात्मवान् यतोऽभिसंधाय निहन्ति शात्रवान्॥
en: By properly looking to the requirements of war and peace, a careful king, succeeds in killing even such foes as are highly rich, adored for intelligence and good conduct, endued with accomplishments, brave in battle, and ready for work.

sn: पश्येदुपायान् विविधैः क्रियापर्थे र्न चानुपायेन मतिं निवेशयेत्। श्रियं विशिष्टां विपुलं यशो धनं न दोषदर्शी पुरुषः समश्नुते॥
en: The king should find out those means which are supplied by different kinds of acts and measures. He should never depend upon destiny. One who sees faults in innocent persons, never succeeds in acquiring prosperity and fame.

sn: प्रीतिप्रवृत्तौ विनिवर्तितौ यथा सुहृत्सु विज्ञाय निवृत्य चोभयोः। यदेव मित्रं गुरुभारमावहेत् तदेव सुस्निग्धमुदाहरेद् बुधः॥
en: When two friends engage in doing one and the same act, a wise man always praises him among the two who undertakes the heavier share of work.

sn: एतान् मयोक्तांश्चर राजधर्मान् नृणां च गुप्तौ मतिमादधत्स्व। अवाप्स्यसे पुण्यफलं सुखेन सर्वो हि लोको नृप धर्ममूलः॥
en: Do you practise these duties of kings that I have described to you. Be ready to perform the duty of protecting men. You may then easily acquire the need of virtue. All the regions of happiness hereafter depend upon merit.'

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अयं पितामहेनोक्तो राजधर्मः सनातनः। ईश्वरश्च महादण्डो दण्डे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, you have now finished your discourse upon the duties of kings. From what you have said it appears that punishment occupies a high position and is the master of everything, for everything depends upon punishment.

sn: देवतानामृषीणां च पितृणां च महात्मनाम्। यक्षरक्ष:पिशाचानां साध्यानां च विशेषतः॥ सर्वेषां प्राणिनां लोके तिर्यग्योनिनिवासिनाम्। सर्वव्यापी महातेजा दण्डः श्रेयानिति प्रभो॥
en: It seems, O powerful one, that punishment, which is highly powerful and which is present everywhere, is the foremost of all beings among either gods and Rishis and great Pitris and Yakshas and Rakshasa and Pishachas and Sadhyas, or living beings in this world. consisting of beasts and birds.

sn: इत्येवमुक्तं भवता दण्डे वै सचराचरम्। पश्यता लोकमासक्तं ससुरासुरमानुषम्।
en: You have said that the entire universe, mobile and immobile, including gods, Asuras, and men, depends upon punishment.

sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं ज्ञातुं तत्त्वेन भरतर्षभ॥ को दण्डः कीदृशो द डः किंरूपः किंपरायणः। किमात्मकः कथंभूतः कथंमूर्तिः कथं प्रभो॥
en: I now wish, O foremost of Bharata's race, to know truly who punishment is. Of what kind is he? What is his form? What is his nature?

sn: जागर्ति च कथं दण्डः प्रजास्ववहितात्मकः। कश्च पूर्वापरमिदं जागर्ति प्रतिपालयन्॥
en: Of what is he made? Whence is his origin? What are his features? What is his splendour? How does he remain awake among living creatures so vigilantly?

sn: कश्च विज्ञायते पूर्व को वरो दण्डसंज्ञितः। किंसंस्थश्च भवेद् दण्डः का वास्य गतिरुच्यते॥
en: Who is he that remains perpetually awake, protecting this universe? Who is he that is known to be the greatest of all things? Who, indeed, is that high person called punishment? What is that upon which Punishment depends? And what is his movement?

sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु कौरव्य यो दण्डो व्यवहारो यथा च सः। यस्मिन् हि सर्वमायत्तं स दण्ड इह केवलः॥
en: Bhishma said Listen, O scion of the Kurus, who is punishment and why is he also called Vyavahara. That upon whom all things depend is called punishment.

sn: धर्मस्याख्या महाराज व्यवहार इतीष्यते। तस्य लोपः कथं न स्याल्लोकेष्ववहितात्मनः॥
en: Punishment is that by which righteousness is maintained. He is sometimes called Vyavahara. Punishment is called as such so that the righteousness of a king who is wide awake may not suffer extinction.

sn: इत्येवं व्यवहारस्य व्यवहारत्वमिष्यते। अपि चैतत् पुरा राजन् मनुना प्रोक्तमादितः॥ सुप्रणीतेन दण्डेन प्रियाप्रियसमात्मना। प्रजा रक्षति यः सम्यग्धर्म एव स केवलः॥
en: It is, therefore, that the name Vyavahara is applied to it. In days of yore, Manu, O king, declared first of all this truth, viz.,-He who protects all creatures, the loved and the hated equally, by impartially holding the rod of punishment, is said to be the righteousness incarnate.

sn: यथोक्तमेतद् सचनं प्रागेव मनुना पुरा। यन्मयोक्तं मनुष्येन्द्र ब्रह्मणो वचनं महत्॥
en: These words, that I have said, were, o king, first uttered in days of yore by Manu. They represent the great words of Brahmana.

sn: प्रागिदं वचनं प्रोक्तमतः प्राग्वचनं विदुः। व्यवहारस्य चाख्यानद् व्यवहार इहोच्यते॥
en: And because these words were spoken first, therefore, they are known as the first. And since Punishment which stops the misappropriation of other people's wealth, therefore, Punishment has come to be called by the name of Vyavahara.

sn: दण्डे त्रिवर्गः सततं सुप्रणीते प्रवर्तते। दैवं हि परमो दण्डो रूपतोऽग्निरिवोत्थितः॥
en: The aggregate of three objects always depends well-applied Punishment. Punishment is a great god. In form he looks like a burning fire.

sn: नीलोत्पलदलश्यामश्चतुर्दष्ट्रश्चतुर्भुजः। अष्टपान्नैकनयनः शंकुकर्णोर्ध्वरोमवान्॥
en: His complexion is dark like that of the petals of the blue lotus. He has four teeth, four arms and eight legs and many eyes. His ears are pointed like arrows and his hair stands upright. on

sn: जटी द्विजिह्वस्ताम्रास्यो मृगराजतनुच्छदः। एतद् रूपं बिभर्युग्रं दण्डो नित्यं दुराधरः॥
en: He has matted locks and two tongues. His face has the colour of copper, and he is clad in a lion's skin. That irresistible god assumes such a dreadful form.

sn: असिर्धनुर्गदा शक्तिस्त्रिशूलं मुद्गरः शरः। मुसलं परशुश्चक्रं पाशो दण्डष्टितोमराः॥ सर्वप्रहरणीयानि सन्ति यानीह कानिचित्। दण्ड एव स सर्वात्मा लोके चरति मूर्तिमान्॥
en: Assuming again the form of the sword, the bow, the mace, the dart, the trident, the mallet, the arrow, the thick and short club, the battleaxe, the discus, the noose, the heavy bludgeon, the rapier, the lance, and, in fact, of every sort of weapon that exist on Earth, Punishment moves in the world.

sn: भिन्दंश्छिन्दन् रुजन् कृन्तन् दारयन् पाटयंस्तथा। घातयन्नभिधावंश्च दण्ड एव चरत्युत॥
en: Indeed, Punishment moves on Earth, piercing and cutting and assenting and looping off and dividing and striking and killing and rushing against its victims.

sn: असिर्विशसनो धर्मस्तीक्ष्णवर्मा दुराधरः। श्रीगर्भो विजयः शास्ता व्यवहारः सनातनः॥ शास्त्रं ब्राह्मणमन्त्राश्च शास्ता प्राग्वदतां वरः। धर्मपालोऽक्षरो देवः सत्यगो नित्यगोऽग्रजः॥ असंगो रुद्रतनयो मनुर्येष्ठः शिवंकरः। नामान्येतानि दण्डस्य कीर्तितानि युधिष्ठिर॥
en: These, O Yudhishthira, are some of the names of Punishment viz., sword, Sabre, Righteousness, Fury, the Irresistible, the father of prosperity, Victory, Punisher, Checker, the Eternal, the Scriptures, Brahmana, Mantra, Avenger, the Foremost of first Legislators, Judge, the Undecaying, god, the individual of irresistible course, the Ever-going, the Firstborn, the individual without love the Soul of Rudra, the eldest Manu, and the great Benefiter.

sn: दण्डो हि भगवान् विष्णुर्दण्डो नारायणः प्रभुः। शश्वद् रूपं महद् बिभ्रन्महान् पुरुष उच्यते॥
en: Punishment is the holy Vishnu. He is the powerful Narayana. And because he always puts on dreadful from, therefore he is called Mahapurusha.

sn: तथोक्ता ब्रह्मकन्येति लक्ष्मीर्वृत्तिः सरस्वती। दण्डनीतिर्जगद्धात्री दण्डो हि बहुविग्रहः॥
en: His wife Morality passes by the names of Brahman's daughter, Lakshmi, Vritti, Sarasvati, and Mother of the universe. Punishment has thus many forms.

sn: अर्थानौँ सुखं दुःखं धर्माधर्मों बलाबले। दौर्भाग्यं भागधेयं च पुण्यापुण्ये गुणागुणौ॥ कामाकामावृतुर्मासः शर्वरी दिवसः क्षणः। अप्रमादः प्रमादश्च हर्षक्रोधौ शमो दमः॥ दैवं पुरुषकारच मोक्षामोक्षौ भयाभये। हिंसाहिसे तपो यज्ञः संयमोऽथ विषाविषम्॥ अन्तश्चादिश्च मध्यं च कृत्यानां च प्रपञ्चनम्। मदः प्रमादो दर्पश्च दम्भो धैर्यं नयानयौ॥ अशक्तिः शक्तिरित्येवं मानस्तम्भौ व्ययाव्ययौ। विनयश्च विसर्गश्च कालाकालौ च भारत॥ अनृतं ज्ञानिता सत्यं श्रद्धाश्रद्धे तथैव च। क्लीबता व्यवसायश्च लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ॥ तीक्ष्णता मृदुता मृत्युरागमानागमौ तथा। विरोधशाविरोधश्च कार्याकार्य बलाबले॥ असूया चानसूया च धर्माधर्मों तथैव च। अपत्रपानपत्रपे ह्रीश्च सम्पद्विपत्पदम्॥ तेजः कर्माणि पाण्डित्यं वाक्शक्तिस्तत्त्वबुद्धिता। एवं दण्डस्य कौरव्य लोकेऽस्मिन् बहुरूपता॥
en: Blessing and curse, pleasure and pain, righteousness and unrighteousness strength and weakness, fortune and misfortune, merit and demerit, virtue and fault, liking and disliking, season and month, night and day and hour, carefulness and carelessness, joy and anger, peace and self-control, destiny and manliness, salvation and damnation, fear and intrepidity, injury and abstention from injury, penances and sacrifice and rigid abstinence, poison and wholesome food, the beginning, the middle, and the end, the result of all murderous acts, insolence, insanity, arrogance, pride, patience, policy, impolicy, powerlessness and power, respect, disrespect decay and firmness, humility, tharity, fitness of time and unfitness of time, falsehood, wisdom, truth, belief, disbelief, importance, trade, profit, loss, success, defeat, fierceness, mildness, death, acquisition and non-acquisition, agreement, and disagreement, what would be done and what should not be done, strength and weakness, malice and good will, righteousness and unrighteousness, shame and shamelessness, modesty, prosperity, and adversity, energy, acts, learning, eloquence, keenness of understanding,—all these, O Yudhishthira, are forms of Punishment in this world. Therefore, punishment has many forms.

sn: न स्याद् यदीह दण्डो वै प्रमथेयुः परस्परम्। भयाद् दण्डस्य नान्योन्यं मन्ति चैव युधिष्ठिर॥
en: If punishment had not existed, all creatures would have struck one another. Through fear of punishment, O Yudhishthira, living creatures do not kill one another.

sn: दण्डेन रक्ष्यमाणा हि राजनहरहः प्रजाः। राजानं वर्धयन्तीह तस्माद् दण्डः परायणम्॥
en: O king, always protected by punishment, the subjects, increase the might of their ruler. It is for this that punishment is regarded as the highest refuge of all.

sn: व्यवस्थापयति क्षिप्रमिमं लोकं नरेश्वर। सत्ये व्यवस्थितो धर्मो ब्राह्मणेष्ववतिष्ठते॥
en: Punishment, o king, quickly sets the world on the path of righteousness. Depend upon truth, righteousness exits in Brahmanas.

sn: धर्मयुक्ता द्विजश्रेष्ठा वेदयुक्ता भवन्ति च। बभूव यज्ञो वेदेभ्यो यज्ञः प्रीणाति देवताः॥
en: Filled with righteousness, leading Brahmanas take to the study of the Vedas. From the Vedas the sacrifices originate. Sacrifices please the gods.

sn: प्रीताश्च देवता नित्यमिन्द्रे परिवदन्त्यपि। अन्नं ददाति शऋचाप्यनुगृह्णन्निमाः प्रजाः॥
en: The gods being gratified, commend the dwellers of the Earth to Indra. For benefiting the inhabitants of the Earth, Indra gives them food.

sn: प्राणाश्च सर्वभूतानां नित्यमन्ने प्रतिष्ठिताः। तस्मात् प्रजाः प्रतिष्ठन्ते दण्डो जागर्ति तासु च॥
en: The life of all creatures depends upon food. From food creatures derive their support and growth. Punishment in the shape of king remains wakeful amongst them.

sn: एवं प्रयोजनश्चैव दण्डः क्षत्रियतां गतः। रक्षन् प्रजाः स जागर्ति नित्यं स्ववहितोऽक्षरः॥
en: For serving this object, punishment assumes the form of a Kshatriya among men. Protecting men he remains awake, always careful and never decaying.

sn: ईश्वरः पुरुषः प्राणः सत्त्वं चित्तं प्रजापतिः। भूतात्मा जीव इत्येवं नामभिः प्रोच्यतेऽष्टभिः॥
en: Punishment has again these other eight names, viz., God, Men, Life, Power, Heart, the Lord of all creatures, the Soul of all things, and the Living creature.

sn: धृतमैश्वर्यमेव च। बलेन यश्च संयुक्तः सदा पञ्चविधात्मकः॥
en: God gave both prosperity and the rod of punishment to the king who is possessed of strength and who is a combination of five expedients.

sn: कुलं बहुधनामात्याः प्रज्ञा प्रोक्ता बलानि तु। आहार्यमष्टकैर्द्रव्यैर्बलमन्यद् युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Nobility of blood, rich ministers, knowledge, the various kinds of forces with the eight objects mentioned below, and the other forces, should be sought for by the king, o Yudhishthira.

sn: हस्तिनोऽश्वा रथाः पत्ति वो विष्टिस्तथैव च। दैशिकाश्चाविकाश्चैव तदष्टाङ्गं बलं स्मृतम्॥ अददद् दण्डमेवास्मै
en: a Those eight objects are elephants, horses, cars, infantry, boats, impressed labourers, increase of population, and cattle such as sheep, etc.

sn: अथवाङ्गस्य युक्तस्य रथिनो हस्तियायिनः। अश्वारोहा: पदाताश्च मन्त्रिणो रसदाश्च ये॥
en: Well-armed soldiers car-warriors, elephantwarriors, cavalry, infantry officers and surgeons form the limbs.

sn: भिक्षुकाः प्राड्विवाकाश्च मौहूर्ता दैवचिन्तकाः। कोशो मित्राणि धान्यं च सर्वोपकरणानि च॥ सप्तप्रकृति चाष्टाङ्गं शरीरमिह यद् विदुः। राज्यस्य दण्डमेवाङ्गं दण्डः प्रभव एव च।॥
en: Beggars, principal judges, judges, astrologers, performers of propitiatory and Atharvan rites, treasury, allies, grain, and all other requisites, form the body, composed of seven attributes and eight limbs, of a kingdom. Punishment is another powerful limb of kingdom. Punishment is the creator of a kingdom.

sn: ईश्वरेण प्रयत्नेन कारणात् क्षत्रियस्य च। दण्डो दत्तः समानात्मा दण्डो हीदं सनातनम्॥
en: God himself has, with great care, sent Punishment for the use of the Kshatriya. This eternal universe is impartial Punishment's self.

sn: राज्ञां पूज्यतमो नान्यो यथा धर्मः प्रदर्शितः। ब्रह्मणा लोकरक्षार्थं स्वधर्मस्थापनाय च॥
en: There is nothing which deserves greater respect from kings than Punishment by which the ways of Righteousness are marked out. Brahman himself, for the protection of the world and for establishing the duties of different orders, sent down Punishment.

sn: भर्तृप्रत्यय उत्पन्नो व्यवहारस्तथापरः। तस्माद् यः स हितो दृष्टो भर्तुप्रत्ययलक्षणः॥
en: There is another kind of Vyavahara (Law) originating from the disputes of litigants which also has sprung from Brahman. Principally marked by a belief in either of the two parties, that Vyavahara, (Law) yields great good.

sn: व्यवहारस्तु वेदात्मा वेदप्रत्यय उच्यते। मौलश्च नरशार्दूल शास्त्रोक्तश्च तथा परः॥
en: There is another kind of Vyavahara which has the Veda for its soul. It also originates from the Veda. There is, O foremost of kings, a third kind of Vyavahara (Law) which is connected with family customs but which is quite of a piece with the scriptures.

sn: उक्तो यश्चापि दण्डोऽसौ भर्तृप्रत्ययलक्षणः। ज्ञेयो नः स नरेन्द्रस्थौ दण्डः प्रत्यय एव च॥
en: That Vyavahara (Law) which has, as above, been said to be marked by a belief in either of two litigant parties, should be known by us as being inherent in the king. It should be also known by the name of Punishment, as also by the name of Evidence.

sn: दण्डः प्रत्ययदृष्टोऽपि व्यवहारात्मकः स्मृतः। व्यवहारः स्मृतो यश्च स वेदविषयात्मकः॥
en: Although Punishment is regulated by Evidence, yet it depends upon Law. Vyavahara (law) is really based upon Vedic precepts.

sn: यश्च वेदप्रसूतात्मा स धर्मो गुणदर्शनः। धर्मप्रत्यय उद्दिष्टो यथाधर्मं कृतात्मभिः॥
en: That Vyavahara (Law), which originates from the Vedas, is Morality or duty. It yields good to persons believing in duty and morality; men of purified souls have spoken of that Vyavahara (Law) as they have done of ordinary law.

sn: व्यवहारः प्रजागोप्ता ब्रह्मदिष्टो युधिष्ठिर। त्रीन् धारयति लोकान् वै सत्यात्मा भूतिवर्धनः॥
en: The third kind of Vyavahara is also a protector of men, and it also originates from the Veda, O Yudhishthira! It keeps up the three worlds. It has Truth for its soul and yields prosperity.

sn: यश्च दण्डः स दृष्टो नो व्यवहारः सनातनः। व्यवहारश्च दृष्टो यः स वेद इति निश्चितम्॥
en: That which is punishment is eternal Vyavahara. That which has been said to be Vyavahara is really the Veda.

sn: यश्च वेदः स वै धर्मो यश्च धर्मः स सत्पथः। ब्रह्मा पितामहः पूर्वं बभूवाथ प्रजापतिः॥
en: That which is the Veda is morality and duty. What is morality and duty is the path of Righteousness. This last in the beginning had been the Grandfather Brahman, that Lord of all creatures.

sn: लोकानां स हि सर्वेषां ससुरासुररक्षसाम्। समनुष्योरगवतां कर्ता चैव स भूतकृत्॥
en: Brahman is the Creator of the entire universe with the gods and Asuras and Rakshasas and human beings and snakes, and of every other things.

sn: ततोऽन्यो व्यवहारोऽयं भर्तृप्रत्ययलक्षणः। तस्मादिदमथोवाच व्यवहारनिदर्शनम्॥
en: Hence that law which is characterised by a belief in either of two litigant parties has also originated from him. Therefore, he has laid down the following regarding Vyavahara.

sn: माता पिता च भ्राता च भार्या चैव पुरोहिताः। नादण्ड्यो विद्यते राज्ञो यः स्वधर्मे न तिष्ठति॥
en: Neither mother, nor father, nor brother, nor wife, nor priest, is unpunishable with that king who governs agreeable to his duty.'

sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीपमितिहासं पुरातनम्। अङ्गेषु राजा द्युतिमान् वसुहोम इति श्रुतः॥
en: Bhishma said “Regarding it is cited the following old story. There was among the Angas a highly effulgent king called Vasuhoma.

sn: स राजा धर्मविन्नित्यं सह पत्न्या महातपाः। मुञ्जपृष्ठं जगामाथ पितृदेवर्षिपूजितम्॥
en: That king was always engaged in acts of piety, and accompanied by his wife he always practised the austerest penances. He went to the spot called Munjaprishtha highly respected by the Pitris and the celestial Rishis.

sn: तत्र शृङ्गे हिमवतो मेरौ कनकपर्वते। यत्र मुजावटे रामो जटाहरणमादिशत्॥
en: There, on that peak of Himavat, near the golden mountain of Meru. Rama, sitting under the shade of a well-known banian, had tied his matted locks together.

sn: तदाप्रभृति राजेन्द्र ऋषिभिः संशितव्रतैः। मुजपृष्ठ इति प्रोक्तः स देशो रुद्रसेवितः॥
en: From that time, O king, the spot, which is a favourite resort of Rudra, passed by the naine of Munjaprishtha among Rishis of rigid vows.

sn: स तत्र बहुभुिर्यक्तस्तदा श्रुतिमयैर्गुणैः। ब्राह्मणानामनुमतो देवर्षिसदृशोऽभवत्॥
en: Living there, king Vasuhoma acquired many pious attributes and, having gained the regard of the Brahmanas, came to be regarded as a celestial Rishi in holiness.

sn: तं कदाचिददीनात्मा सखा शक्रस्य मानितः। अभ्यगच्छन्महीपालो मान्धाता शत्रुकर्शनः॥
en: One day, that grinder of enemies, that friend of Shakra, viz., king Mandhata of great soul, came to Vasuhoma on his mountain retreat.

sn: सोपसृत्य तु मान्धाता वसुहोमं नराधिपम्। दृष्ट्वा प्रकृष्टतयसं विनेतोऽग्रेऽभ्यतिष्ठत॥
en: Arrived there, and seeing king Vasuhoma of austere penances, stood humbly before the latter.

sn: वसुहोमोऽपि राज्ञो वै पाद्यमयँ न्यवेदयत्। सप्ताङ्गस्य तु राज्यस्य पप्रच्छ कुशलाव्यये॥
en: Vasuhoma offered his guest water to wash his feet, and the Arghya consisting of the usual articles, and enquired of him about the wellbeing or otherwise of his kingdom consisting of seven limbs.

sn: सद्भिराचरितं पूर्वं यथावदनुयायिनम्। अपृच्छद् वसुहोमस्तं राजन् किं करवाणि ते॥
en: After this, Vasuhoma addressed his royal guest who strictly followed the conduct of the righteous men of old, saying,-What, О king, shall I do for you.

sn: सोऽब्रवीत्परमप्रीतो मान्धाता राजसत्तमम्। वसुहोमं महाप्राज्ञमासीनं कुरुनन्दन॥
en: Thus addressed, O delighter of the Kurus, Mandhatri, that best of kings, highly pleased, answered the greatly wise Vasuhoma seated at his ease, in the following words.

sn: मान्धातोवाच बृहस्पतेर्मतं राजन्नधीतं सकलं त्वया। तथैवोशनसं शास्त्रं विज्ञातं ते नरोत्तम॥
en: Mandhatri said You have, O king, studied all the doctrines of Brihaspati! O best of men, you know also the doctrines laid down by Ushanas.

sn: तदहं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि दण्ड उत्पद्यते कथम्। किं चास्य पूर्वं जागर्ति किं वा परममुच्यते॥
en: I wish to know what is the origin of Punishment? What also is said to be its end?

sn: कथं क्षत्रियसंस्थश्च दण्डः सम्प्रत्यवस्थितः। ब्रूहि मे समुहाप्राज्ञ ददाम्याचार्यवेतनम्॥
en: How Came Punishment to depend upon the Kshatriya? Tell me all this, O you of great wisdom. I approach you as a disciple ready to give you the tuition fee.

sn: वसुहोम उवाच शृणु राजन् यथा दण्डः सम्भूतो लोकसंग्रहः। प्रजाविनयरक्षार्थं धर्मस्यात्मा सनातनः॥
en: Vasuhoma said Listen, O king, as to how Punishment, that upholder of the world, sprang up. It is the soul of righteousness, and eternal, and was created for preserving the proper government of all creatures.

sn: ब्रह्मा यियक्षुर्भगवान् सर्वलोकपितामहः। ऋत्विजं नात्मनस्तुल्यं ददर्शेति हि नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that once upon a time, the Grandfather of all the worlds, viz., the divine Brahmana, desiring to celebrate a sacrifice, could not find a priest equally qualified like himself.

sn: स गर्भ शिरसा देवो बहुवर्षाण्यधारयत्। पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु स गर्भः क्षुवतोऽपतत्॥
en: Therefore, he once conceived in his brain and held the foetus there for many long years. After a thousand years, the great god sneezed. In that act, the foetus dropped from his head.

sn: स क्षुपो नाम सम्भूतः प्रजापतिररिंदम्। ऋत्विगासीन्महाराज यज्ञे तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: The divine being, O chastiser of foes, who was thus born from Brahman passed by the name of Kshupa. Highly powerful be became a lord of creatures. That Kshupa officiated as priest, O king, in the sacrifice of the highsouled Grandfather.

sn: तस्मिन् प्रवृत्ते सत्रे तु ब्रह्मणः पार्थिवर्षभ। दृष्ट्रपप्रधानत्वाद् दण्डः सोऽन्तर्हितोऽभवत्॥
en: Upon the commencement of that sacrifice, of Brahman, O best of kings, punishment disappeared on account of the visible form that the Grandfather was then obliged to assume.

sn: तस्मिन्नन्तर्हिते चापि प्रजानां संकरोऽभवत्। नैव कार्यं न वाकार्यं भोज्याभोज्यं न विद्यते॥
en: Punishment having disappeared, a great confusion arose among all creatures. There was no longer any distinction between what should be done and what should not. All difference, again, between clean and unclean food disappeared.

sn: पेयापेये कुतः सिद्धिर्हिसन्ति च परस्परम्। गम्यागम्यं तदा नासीत् स्वं परस्वं च वै समम्॥
en: Men could not distinguish between what drink was allowable and what drink was not. All creatures began to injure one another. There were no restraints about the union of the sexes. All idea of property disappeared.

sn: परस्परं विलुम्पन्ति सारमेया यथामिषम्। अबलान् बलिनो मन्ति निर्मर्यादमवर्तत॥
en: All creatures began to rob, snatching meat from one another. The strong began to kill the weak. Nobody cared the least for his neighbour.

sn: ततः पितामहो विष्णुं भगवन्तं सनातनम्। सम्पूज्य वरदं देवं महादेवमथाब्रवीत्॥ अत्र त्वमनुकम्पां वै कर्तुमर्हसि शंकर। संकरो न भवेदत्र यथा तद् वै विधीयताम्॥
en: Then, having adored the divine and eternal Vishnu, the grandfather addressed that great boon-giving god, saying,-You should, O Keshava, show mercy on the present occasion. Let it be so ordained by you that the confusion that has already set in may disappear.

sn: ततः स भगवान् ध्यात्वा चिरं शूलवरायुधः। आत्मानमात्मना दण्डं ससृजे देवसत्तमः॥
en: Thus addressed, that foremost of gods, armed with an enormous Shula, thinking for some time, converted his ownself into the form of Punishment.

sn: तस्माच्च धर्मचरणानीतिर्देवी सरस्वती। ससृजे दण्डनीतिं सा त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता॥
en: From that form, having Righteousness for its legs, the goddess Sarasvati created Dandaniti (Science of Punishment) which very soon became celebrated all over the world.

sn: भूयः स भगवान् ध्यात्वा चिरं शूलवरायुधः। तस्य तस्य निकायस्य चकारैकैकमीश्वरम्॥
en: Thereafter the great god armed with a huge Shula, having again reflected for sometime, appointed a few among the gods as the rulers of their respective classes.

sn: देवानामीश्वरं चक्रे देवं दशशतेक्षणम्। यमं वैवस्वतं चापि पितृणामकरोत् प्रभुम्॥
en: It was then that he made the divine Indra of a thousand eyes the king of gods. Yama the son of Vivasvat was made the lord of the departed manes.

sn: धनानां राक्षसानां च कुबेरमपि चेश्वरम्। पर्वतानां पति मेरुं सरितां च महोदधिम्॥
en: Kubera was made the lord of riches and of all the Rakshasas. Meru was made the king of the mountains, and Oceans was made the lord of the rivers.

sn: अर्पा राज्येऽसुराणां च विदधे वरुणं प्रभुम्। मृत्युं प्राणेश्वरमथो तेजसां च हुताशनम्॥
en: The powerful Varuna was made the lord of the waters and of the Asuras. Death was made the lord of life and of all living creatures, and Fire was made the chief of all things possessed of energy.

sn: रुद्राणामपि चेशानं गोप्तारं विदधे प्रभुम्। महात्मानं महादेवं विशलाक्षं सनातनम्॥
en: The powerful Ishana the great and eternal Mahadeva, of three eyes, was made the king of the Rudras.

sn: वसिष्ठमीशं विप्राणां वसूनां जातवेदसम्। तेजसा भास्करं चक्रे नक्षत्राणां निशाकरम्॥
en: Vashishtha was made the king of the Brahmanas, and Jatavedas was made the chief of the Vasus. Surya was made the lord of all luminous bodies and Chandramas was made the lord of Stars and constellations,

sn: वीरुधामंशुमन्तं च भूतानां च प्रभुं वरम्। कुमारं द्वादशभुजं स्कन्दं राजानमादिशत्॥
en: Anshumat was made the chief of all herbs, and the powerful and foremost of deities, viz., Kumara or Skanda, having twelve arms, was made the lord of all the spirits and ghosts.

sn: कालं सर्वेशमकरोत् संहारविनयात्मकम्। मृत्योश्चतुर्विभागस्य दुःखस्य च सुखस्य च॥
en: Time, containing the seeds of both origin and destruction was made the lord of all creatures, as also of the four parts of Death viz., weapons, diseases, Yama, and acts, and, lastly of grief and joy.

sn: ईश्वरः सर्वदेवस्तु राजराजो नराधिपः। सर्वेषामेव रुद्राणां शूलपाणिरिति श्रुतिः॥
en: The Shrutis say that the great god Mahadeva, the lord of lords, O king, armed with Shula, is the lord of the Rudras.

sn: तमेनं ब्रह्मणः पुत्रमनुजातं क्षुपं ददौ। प्रजानामधिपं श्रेष्ठं सर्वधर्मभृतामपि॥
en: The rod of punishment was given to Brahmana's latest-born son, viz., Kshupa, the lord of all creatures and the foremost of the virtuous.

sn: महादेवस्ततस्तस्मिन् वृत्ते यज्ञे यथाविधि। दण्डं धर्मस्य गोप्तारं विष्णवे सत्कृतं ददौ॥
en: Upon the completion of that sacrifice according to due rites, Mahadeva after making proper reverence handed over Punishment, that protector of Righteousness, to Vishnu.

sn: विष्णुरङ्गिरसे प्रादादङ्गिरा मुनिसत्तमः। प्रादादिन्द्रमरीचिभ्यां मरीचि गवे ददौ॥
en: Vishnu gave it to Angiras, and Angiras, that foremost of ascetics, handed it over to Indra and Marichi. Marichi gave it to Bhrigu.

sn: भृगुर्ददावृषिभ्यस्तु दण्डं धर्मसमाहितम्। ऋषयो लोकपालेभ्यो लोकपालाः क्षुपाय च॥
en: Bhrigu gave that rod intended for the protection of righteousness to all the Rishis. The Rishis gave it to the Regents of the quarters, and the Regents made it over again to Kshupa.

sn: क्षुपस्तु मनवे प्रादादादित्यतनयायं च। पुत्रेभ्यः श्राद्धदेवस्तु सूक्ष्मधर्मार्थकारणात्॥
en: Kshupa then handed it over to Manu the son of Surya. The god of Shraddhas (viz., Manu), gave it to his sons for the sake of true righteousness and riches.

sn: विभज्य दण्डः कर्तव्यो धर्मेण न यदृच्छया। दुष्टानां निग्रहो दण्डो हिरण्यं बाह्यतः क्रिया॥
en: Punishment should be meted out with discrimination, guided by righteousness and not by caprice. It is intended for checking the wicked. Fines and confiscation are intended for creating terror, and not for replenishing the king's treasury.

sn: व्यङ्गत्वं च शरीरस्य वधो नाल्पस्य कारणात्। शरीरपीडास्तास्ताश्च देहत्यागो विवासनम्॥
en: The wounding of one's body or the infliction of death should not be made for trivial causes. The infliction of physical pain by various means, hurling from tops of mountains, and punishment also, should not be guided by similar causes.

sn: तं ददौ सूर्यपुत्रस्तु मनुर्वे रक्षणार्थकम्। आनुपूर्व्याच्च दण्डोऽयं प्रजा जागर्ति पालयन्॥
en: Surya's son Manu gave the rod of punishment, (to his sons) for the protection of the world. Punishment in the hands of successive holders, remains awake, protecting all creatures.

sn: इन्द्रो जागर्ति भगवानिन्द्रादग्निर्विभावसुः। अग्नेर्जागर्ति वरुणो वरुणाच्च प्रजापतिः॥ प्रजापतेस्ततो धर्मो जागर्ति विनयात्मकः। धर्माच्च ब्रह्मणः पुत्रो व्यवसायः सनातनः॥ व्यवसायात् ततस्तेजो जागर्ति परिपालयत्। ओषध्यस्तेजसस्तस्मादोषधीभ्यश्च पर्वताः॥ पर्वतेभ्यश्च जागर्ति रसो रसगुणात् तथा। जाति निर्ऋतिर्देवी ज्योतींषि निर्ऋतेरपि॥ वेदाः प्रतिष्ठाः ज्योतिर्यस्ततो हयशिराः प्रभुः। ब्रह्मा पितामहस्तस्माज्जागर्ति प्रभुरव्ययः॥ पितामहान्महादेवो जागर्ति भगवाशिवः। विश्वेदेवाः शिवाच्चापि विश्वेभ्यश्च तथर्षयः॥ ऋषिभ्यो भगवान् सोमः सोमाद् देवाः सनातनाः। देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणा लोके जाग्रतीत्युपधारय॥
en: At the top of the ladder, the divine Indra is awake; after him, Agni of burning flames; after him, Varuna; after Varuna; Prajapati; after Prajapati, Righteousness whose essence is restraint; after Righteousness, the son of Brahman, viz., the eternal Law; after Law; Energy is awake, employed in the act of protection; after Energy, the herbs; after the herbs, the mountains; after the mountains, all kinds of juices and their attributes; after these the goddess Nirriti; after Nirriti, the planets and the luminous bodies in heaven; after these, the Vedas; after the Vedas, the powerful form of the Vishnu with the horse head; after him the almighty and eternal grandfather, viz., Brahma; after the grandfather, the divine and blessed Mahadeva; after Mahadeva, the Vishvedevas; after them, the great Rishis; after the Rishis, the divine Soma; after soma; the eternal duties; after the gods, the Brahmanas are awake.

sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च राजन्या लोकान् रक्षन्ति धर्मतः। स्थावरं जगमं चैव क्षत्रियेभ्यः सनातनम्॥
en: After the Brahmanas, the Kshatriyas are piously protecting all creatures. The universe, consisting of mobile and immobile creatures, is kept awake by the Kshatriyas.

sn: प्रजा जागर्ति लोकेऽस्मिन् दण्डो जागर्ति तासु च। सर्वं संक्षिपते दण्डः पितामहसमप्रभः॥
en: Creatures are kept awake in this world, and Punishment is awake is among them. Effulgent like the Grandfather himself, Punishment keeps together and maintains everything.

sn: जागर्ति कालः पूर्वं च मध्ये चान्ते च भारत। ईश्वरः सर्वलोकस्य महादेवः प्रजापतिः॥ देवदेवः शिवः सर्वो जागर्ति सततं प्रभुः। कपर्दी शङ्गो रुद्रः शिवः स्थाणुरुमापतिः॥
en: Time, O Bharata, is always awake, in the beginning, the middle, and the end. The lord of all the worlds, the lord of all creatures, the powerful and blessed Mahadeva, the god of gods, is always awake, He passes also by the names Kapardin, Shankara, Rudra, Bhava, Sthanu, and the lord of Uma.

sn: इत्येष दण्डो विख्यात आदौ मध्ये तथावरे। भूमिपालो यथान्यायं वर्तेतानेन धर्मवित्॥
en: Thus Punishment also keeps awake in the beginning, the middle and the end. A virtuous king should duly rule, guided by Punishment.

sn: भीष्म उवाच इतीदं वसुहोमस्य शृणुयाद् यो मतं नरः। श्रुत्वा सम्यक् प्रवर्तेत सर्वान् कामानवाप्नुयात्॥
en: The person who listens to this teaching of Vasuhoma, and having listened to it behaves according to its trend, is sure to acquire the fruition of all his desires.

sn: इति ते सर्वमाख्यातं यो दण्डो मनुजर्षभ। नियन्ता सर्वलोकस्य धर्माकान्तस्य भारत॥
en: I have now, O foremost of men, told you everything as to who punishment is, that restrainer of the universe which is governed by righteousness.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच तात धर्मार्थकामानां श्रोतुमिच्छामि निश्चयम्। लोकयात्रा हि कार्येन तिष्ठेत् केषु प्रतिष्ठिता॥
en: Yudhishthira said I wish, O sire, to hear the final conclusions about Virtue, Profit and Pleasure. Depending upon which of these does life proceed?

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: धर्मार्थकामाः किंमूलास्त्रयाणां प्रभवश्च कः। अन्योन्यं चानुषज्जन्ते वर्तन्ते च पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: What are origins of Virtue, Profit, and Pleasure? What is again the out come to those three? They are sometimes seen intermixed with one another, and sometimes to exist separately and independently of one another,

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: भीष्म उवाच यदा ते स्युः सुमनसो लोके धर्मार्थनिश्चये। कालप्रभवसंस्थासु सज्जन्ते च त्रयस्तदा॥
en: When men in this world try with pure hearts to gain Profit with the help of Virtue, then those three, viz., Virtue, Profit, and Pleasure, may be seen to exist in a state of union regarding time, cause, and action.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: धर्ममूलः सदैवार्थः कामोऽर्थफलमुच्यते। संकल्पमूलास्ते सर्वे संकल्पो विषयात्मकः॥
en: Profit originates f um virtue, and Pleasure is the fruit of Profit. All the three again originate from Will. Will is connected with the objects.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: विषयाचैव कात्स्न्येन सर्व आहारसिद्धये। मूलमेतत् त्रिवर्गस्य निवृत्तिर्मोक्ष उच्यते॥
en: All objects exist in a body for gratifying the desire of enjoyment. Upon these dependent the threefold objects of life. Renunciation of all objects is liberation.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: धर्माच्छरीरसंगुप्तिधर्मार्थं चार्थ उच्यते। कामो रतिफलश्चात्र सर्वे ते च रजस्वला:॥
en: It is said that Virtue is sought for the protection of the body, and Profit is for the acquisition of Virtue. Pleasure is merely the gratification of the sense. All the three are, therefore, pervaded the quality of Rajas (darkness).

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: संनिकृष्टांश्चरेदेतान् न चैतान् मनसा त्यजेत्। विमुक्तस्तपसा सर्वान् धर्मादीन् कामनैष्ठिकान्॥
en: Virtue, Profit, and Pleasure, when sought for the sake of heaven and such other rewards, are considered remote, because the rewards themselves are remote. They are near when sought, however, for the sake of Knowledge of Self. One should seek them for the purity of soul. One should not renounce them even in mind. If Virtue, Profit, and Pleasure are to be abandoned, one should abandon them when one has liberated one's self by ascetic penances.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: श्रेष्ठे बुद्धिस्त्रिवर्गस्य यदयं प्राप्नुयान्नरः। कर्मणा बुद्धिपूर्वेण भवत्यर्थो न वा पुनः॥
en: The aim of the threefold objects is emancipation. I wish men could attain it. One's acts, undertaking and completed with even the " help of intelligence may or may not yield the expected fruits.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: अर्थार्थमन्यद् भवति विपरीतमथापरम्। अनर्थार्थमवाप्यार्थमन्यत्राद्योपकारकम्। बुद्ध्याबुद्धिरिहार्थे न तदज्ञाननिकृष्टया।॥
en: Virtue is not always the root of Profit, for other things then Virtue lead to Wealth. There is again the opposite view. In some cases, Wealth acquired has produced evil. Other things again than Wealth have brought on the acquisition of Virtue. Therefore, an ignorant man, whose understanding has been debased by ignorance, never succeeds in acquiring the highest object of Virtue and Profit, viz., Emancipation.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: अपध्यानमलो धर्मो मलोऽर्थस्य निगूहनम्। सम्प्रमोदमल: कामो भूयः स्वगुणवर्जितः॥
en: The defeat of Virtue consists in the desire of reward; that of Profit consists in amassing it; when freed from these impurities, they yield mighty fruits.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। कामन्दकस्य संवादमाङ्गरिष्ठस्य चोभयोः॥
en: Regarding it is cited the discourse that took place in days of yore between Kamandaka and Angarishtha.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: कामन्दमृषिमासीनमभिवाद्य नराधिपः। आङ्गरिष्ठोऽथ पप्रच्छ कृत्वा समयपर्ययम्॥
en: One day having waited for the opportunity, king Angarishtha saluted the Rishi Kamanda as he was seated at his ease, and put to him the

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: यः पापं कुरुते राजा काममोहबलात्कृतः। प्रत्यासन्नस्य तस्यर्षे किं स्यात् पापप्रणाशनम्॥
en: If a king, under the influence of lust and folly, commits sin for which he afterwards repents, how, O Rishi, can those sins be destroyed.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: अधर्मं धर्म इति च योऽज्ञानादाचरेन्नरः। तं चापि प्रथितं लोके कथं राजा निवर्तयेत्॥
en: If again a man, guided by ignorance, does what is sinful in the belief that he is acting piously, how shall the king suppress that sin prevalent among men?

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: कामन्दक उवाच यो धर्मार्थी परित्यज्य काममेवानुवर्तते। स धर्मार्थपरित्यागात् प्रज्ञानाशमिहार्छति॥
en: Kamanda said That man, who renouncing Virtue and Profit, pursues only Pleasure, reaps as the result of such conduct the destruction of his intelligence.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: प्रज्ञानाशात्मको मोहस्तथा धर्मार्थनाशकः। तस्मान्नस्तिकता चैव दुराचारश्च जायते॥
en: The destruction of intelligence is followed by carelessness which at once destroys both Virtue and Profit. Such carelessness, beget dreadful atheism and systematic wickedness.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: दुराचारान् यदा राजा प्रदुष्टान् न नियच्छति। तस्मादुद्विजते लोकः सर्पाद् वेश्मगतादिव॥
en: If the king does not subdue those wicked men of sinful conduct, all good subjects then live in dread of him like a person living in a room within which a snake has concealed itself.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: तं प्रजा नानुवर्तन्ते ब्राह्मणा न च साधवः। ततः संशयमाप्नोति तथा वध्यत्वमेति च॥
en: The subjects do not follow such a king. Brahmanas and all pious persons also do the same. As a consequence the king incurs grave danger, and ultimately the risk of his life.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: अपध्वस्तस्त्ववमतो दुःखं जीवितमृच्छति। जीवेच्च यदपध्वस्तस्तच्छुद्धं मरणं भवेत्॥
en: Laden with infamy and insult, he has to carry on a miserable existence. A life of infamy, however, is tantamount to death.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: अत्रैतदाहुराचार्याः पापस्य परिगहणम्। सेवितव्या त्रयी विद्या सत्कारो ब्राह्मणेषु च॥
en: Men well read in the scriptures have laid down the following expedients for suppressing sin. The king should always study the three Vedas. He should respect the Brahmanas and do them good.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: महामना भवेद् धर्मे विवहेच्च महाकुले। ब्राह्मणांश्चापि सेवेत क्षमायुक्तान् मनस्विनः॥
en: He should be given to righteousness. He should make alliance with high families. He should serve the great Brahmanas endued with the virtue of forgiveness.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: जपेदुदकशीलः स्यात् सततं सुखमास्थितः। धर्मान्वितान् सम्प्रविशेद् बहिः कृत्वेह दुष्कृती॥
en: He should perform ablutions and recite sacred Mantras and thus spend his days happily. Banishing all wicked subjects from himself and his kingdom, he should live with virtuous men.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: प्रसादयेन्मधुरया वाचा वाप्यथ कर्मणा। तवास्मीति वदेन्नित्यं परेषां कीर्तयन् गुणान्॥
en: He should please all persons by. sweet words or good acts. He should say to all,-I am yours,-and declare the virtues of even his enemies.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: अपापो ह्येवमाचारः क्षिप्रं बहुमतो भवेत्। पापान्यपि हि कृच्छ्राणि शमयेन्नात्र संशयः॥
en: By behaving thus he may soon cleanse himself of his sins, and gain the high esteem of all. Forsooth, by such a conduct all his sins will be destroyed.

description: An account of virtue, Profit and pleasure
sn: गुरवो हि परं धर्मं यं ब्रूयुस्तं तथा कुरु। गुरूणां हि प्रसादाद् वै श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: You should satisfy all those great duties which your seniors and preceptors would indicate. You are sure to acquire, great blessings through the grace of your seniors and preceptors.'

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच इमे जना नरश्रेष्ठ प्रशंसन्ति सदा भुवि। धर्मस्य शीलमेवादी ततो मे संशयो महान्॥शा
en: Yudhishthira said All persons on Earth, O foremost of men, speak highly of virtuous conduct, I have, however, great misgivings regarding this subject of their praise.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: यदि तच्छक्यमस्माभिर्जातुं धर्मभृतां वर। श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत् सर्वं यथैतदुपलभ्यते॥
en: If the subject be not far from our comprehension, O foremost of virtuous men, I wish to hear everything about the way in which virtuous conduct can be acquired.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: कथं तत् प्राप्यते शीलं श्रोतुमिच्छामि भारत। किंलक्षणं च तत् प्रोक्तं ब्रूहि मे वदतां वरः॥
en: How is, that conduct acquired, O Bharata! I wish to hear it. Tell me also, O foremost of orators, what are the characteristics of that conduct.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: भीष्म उवाच पुरा दुर्योधनेनेह धृतराष्ट्राय मानद। आख्यातं तप्यमानेन श्रियं दृष्ट्वा तथागताम्॥ इन्द्रप्रस्थे महाराज तव सभ्रातृकस्य ह। सभायां चाह वचनं तत् सर्वं शृणु भारत॥
en: Bhishma said 'Formerly, O givers of honours, Duryodhana while burning within at your and your brothers' prosperity at Indraprastha, and for the jeers he received for his mistakes at the grand palace, had asked his father Dhritarashtra the same question. Hear what transpired at that time, O Bharata.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: भवतस्तां सभां दृष्ट्वा समृद्धिं चाप्यनुत्तमाम्। दुर्योधनस्तदाऽऽसीनः सर्वं पित्रे न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Having seen that grand palace and that great prosperity of yours, Duryodhana, while sitting before his father described to him of all he had seen.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: श्रुत्वा हि धृतराष्ट्रश्च दुर्योधनवचस्तदा। अब्रवीत् कर्णसहितं दुर्योधनमिदं वचः॥
en: Having heard the words of Duryodhana, Dhritarashtra, addressing his son and Karna, replied to him as follows.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच किमर्थं तप्यसे पुत्र श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः। श्रुत्वा त्वामनुनेष्यामि यदि सम्यग् भविष्यति॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Why do you grieve, O son! I wish to hear the cause fully. If after hearing the reasons they appear to be sufficient, I shall then try to instruct you.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
