sn: त्वया च महदैश्वर्यं प्राप्तं परपुञ्जय। किंकरा भ्रातरः सर्वे मित्रसम्बन्धिनः सदा॥
en: O subjugator of hostile towns, you too have acquired great affluence. All your brothers are ever obedient to your, as also all your friends and relatives.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: आच्छादयसि प्रावारान नासि पिशितौदनम्। आजानेया वहन्त्यश्वाः केनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: You are clad in the best robes. You take the richest food. Horses of the best species bear you. Why then have you become pale and emaciated?

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच दश तानि सहस्राणि स्नातकानां महात्मनाम्। भुञ्जते रुक्मपात्रीभिर्युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने॥
en: Duryodhana said Ten thousands of great Snataka Brahmanas daily take their food at Yudhishthira's palace from plates of gold.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: दृष्ट्वा च तां सभां दिव्यां दिव्यपुष्पफलान्विताम्। अश्वांस्तित्तिरकल्माषान् वस्त्राणि विविधानि च॥ दृष्ट्वा तां पाण्डवेयानामृद्धिं वैश्रवणीं शुभाम्। अमित्राणां सुमहतीमनुशोचामि भारत॥
en: Seeing his beautiful palaces adorned with excellent flowers and fruits, his horses of the Tittiri and the Kalmasha breeds, his dresses of various sorts, indeed, seeing that high prosperity of my enemies, viz., the sons of Pandu,-a prosperity resembling that of Vaishravana himself,-I am burning with grief, O Bharata!-

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यदीच्छसि श्रियं तात तादृशी सा युधिष्ठिरे। विशिष्टां वा नरव्याघ्र शीलवान् भव पुत्रक॥
en: Dhritarashtra said If you wish, O sire, to acquire prosperity like that of Yudhishthira or that which is even superior to it, do you then, O son, try to be of virtuous conduct.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: शीलेन हि त्रयो लोकाः शक्या जेतुं न संशयः। न हि किंचिदसाध्यं वै लोके शीलवतां भवेत्॥
en: Forsooth, one may, by his conduct alone, conquer the three words. There is nothing which virtuous persons cannot obtain.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: एकरात्रेण मान्धाता त्र्यहेण जनमेजयः। सप्तरात्रेण नाभागः पृथिवीं प्रतिपेदिरे॥
en: Mandhata conquered the whole word in only one night, Janamejaya, in course of three; and Nabhaga, in course of seven.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: एते हि पार्थिवाः सर्वे शीलवन्तो दयान्विताः। अतस्तेषां गुणक्रीता वसुधा स्वयमागता॥
en: All these kings were endued with mercy and virtuous conduct. Therefore, the Earth came to them at their will, won over by their virtues!

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच कथं तत् प्राप्यते शीलं श्रोतुमिच्छामि भारत। येन शीलेन तैः प्राप्ता क्षिप्रमेव वसुन्धरा॥
en: Duryodhana said I wish to hear, O Bharata, how that conduct may be acquired, by which the Earth was won by them so quickly!-

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। नारदेन पुरा प्रोक्तं शीलमाश्रित्य भारत॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Regarding it the following old narrative is cited. It was formerly recited by Narada, with regard to virtuous conduct.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: प्रहादेन हृतं राज्यं महेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः। शीलमाश्रित्या दैत्येन त्रैलोक्यं च वशे कृतम्॥
en: In days of yore, the Daitya Prahlada, by the merit of his conduct, snatched from the great Indra his sovereignty and brought the three worlds under subjection.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: ततो बृहस्पति शक्रः प्राञ्जलिः समुपस्थितः। तमुवाच महाप्राज्ञः श्रेय इच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: Shakra then, with joined hands, approached Brihaspati. Endued with great wisdom, the god of the celestials addressed to the great preceptor, saying,-I desire you to tell me the source of happiness.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: ततो बृहस्पतिस्तस्मै ज्ञानं नैःश्रेयसं परम्। कथयामास भगवान् देवेन्द्राय कुरूद्वह॥
en: Thus accosted, Brihaspati said to him that Knowledge is the source of the greatest happiness.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: एतावच्छ्रेय इत्येव बृहस्पतिरभाषत। इन्द्रस्तु भूयः पप्रच्छ को विशेषो भवेदिति॥
en: Indeed, Brihaspati pointed out knowledge to be the source of supreme happiness. Indra, however, once more asked him as to whether there was any thing superior to that.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच विशेषोऽस्ति महांस्तात भार्गवस्य महात्मनः। अत्रागमय भद्रं ते भूय एवं सुरर्षभ॥
en: Brihaspati said There is some thing, O son, which is still higher. The great Bhargava (Ushanas) will instruct your better. Go to him, blessed be you, and enquire of him, O king of the celestials!

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: आत्मनस्तु ततः श्रेयो भार्गवात् सुमहातपाः। ज्ञानमागमयत् प्रीत्या पुनः स परमद्युतिः।।२५]
en: Endued with great ascetic merit and effulgence, the king of the celestials then went to Bhargava and acquired from him, with a gratified heart, a knowledge of that which was to his greatest good.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: तेनापि समनुज्ञातो भार्गवेण महात्मना। श्रेयोऽस्तीति पुनर्भूयः शुक्रमाह शतक्रतुः॥
en: Acquiring the permission of the great Bhargava, the celebrator of a hundred sacrifices once more asked the sage as to whether there was anything superior to what the sage had already told him.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: भार्गवस्त्वाह सर्वज्ञः प्रहादस्य महात्मनः। ज्ञानमस्मि विशेषेणेत्युक्तो हृष्टश्च सोऽभवत्॥
en: The omniscient Bhargava said,-The great Prahlada has better knowledge!-Learning this, Indra became highly pleased.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: स ततो ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा प्रहादं पाकशासनः। गत्वा प्रोवाच मेधावी श्रेय इच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: The chastiser of Paka, endued with supreme intelligence, assumed the form of a Brahman and going to Prahlada, asked him saying-I desire to hear what conduces to felicity.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: प्रहादस्त्वब्रवीद् विप्रं क्षणो नास्ति द्विजर्षभ। त्रैलोक्यराज्यसक्तस्य ततो नोपदिशामि ते॥
en: Prahlada answered the Brahmana, saying,-O chief of the twice-born, I have no time, being wholly engaged with the task of ruling the three worlds!-I cannot therefore, instruct you.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: ब्राह्मणस्त्वब्रवीद् राजन् यस्मिन् काले क्षणो भवेत्। तदोपादेष्टुमिच्छामि यदाचयमनुत्तमम्॥
en: The Brahmana said,-O king when you may have leisure, I wish to listen to your instructions about that conduct which yields good!

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: ततः प्रीतोऽभवद् राजा प्रह्लादो ब्रह्मवादिनः। तथेत्युक्त्वा शुभे काले ज्ञानतत्त्वं ददौ तदा॥
en: At this answer, king Prahlada became pleased with that Brahmavadin. Saying,-So be it!-he availed of a favourable opportunity for delivering to the Brahma the truths of knowledge.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: ब्राह्मणोऽपि यथान्यायं गुरुवृत्तिमनुत्तमाम्। चकार सर्वभावेन यदस्य मनसेप्सितम्॥
en: The Brahmana duly treated Prahlada as a disciple should his preceptor, and began with his whole heart to do what Prahlada wished.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: पृष्टश्च तेन बहुशः प्राप्तं कथमनुत्तमम्। त्रैलोक्यराज्यं धर्मज्ञ कारणं तद् ब्रवीहि मे। प्रह्लादोऽपि महाराज ब्राह्मणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Many a time the Brahmana enquired, saying,O chastiser of enemies by what means have you been able to acquire the sovereignty of the three worlds? Tell me, O pious king, what those means are!-Prahlada, O king, answered the question of the Brahmana.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: प्रह्लाद उवाच नासूयामि द्विजान् विप्र राजास्मीति कदाचन। काव्यानि वदतां तेषां संयच्छामि वहामि च॥
en: Prahlada said I do not, O twice-born one, feel any pride for my being a king, nor do I entertain any hostile feeling towards the Brahmanas! On the other hand, I accept and follow the policy they describe to me based upon the teachings of Shukra.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: ते विश्रब्धाः प्रभाषन्ते संयच्छन्ति च मां सदा। ते मां काव्यपथे युक्तं शुश्रूषुमनसूयकम्॥
en: Full confident they say to me what they wish to say, and restrain me from unrighteous or improper courses. I am ever obedient to the teachings of Shukra. I wait upon and serve the Brahmanas and my elders. I bear no malice.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: धर्मात्मानं जितक्रोधं नियतं संयतेन्द्रियम्। समासिञ्चन्ति शास्तारः क्षौद्रं मध्विव मक्षिकाः॥
en: I am of righteous soul. I have conquered anger. I am self-controlled, and all my senses are under restraint. Those twice-born ones that are my instructors give me wholesome advice like bees dropping honey into the cells of their comb.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: सोऽहं वागाविद्यानां रसानामवलेहिता। स्वजात्यानधितिष्ठामि नक्षत्राणीव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: I taste the ambrosia dropped by those learned men, and like the Moon among the stars I live among the members of my family.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: एतत् पृथिव्याममृतमेतच्चक्षुरनुत्तमम्। यद् ब्राह्मणमुखे काव्यमेतच्छुत्वा प्रवर्तते॥
en: Even listening to the teachings of Shukra from the lips of Brahmanas and following them in practise, is this nectar on Earth, even this is the clearest eye.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: एतावच्छ्रेय इत्याह प्रह्लादो ब्रह्मवादिनम्। शुश्रूषितस्तेन तदा दैत्येन्द्रो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ यथावद् गुरुवृत्त्या ते प्रीतोऽस्मि द्विजसत्तमा वरं वृणीष्व भद्रं ते प्रदातास्मि न संशयः॥
en: The good of a man consists in these, Thus said Prahlada to that utterer of Brahma. Served dutifully by him, the chief of the Asuras once more said,-O foremost of twice-born ones, I am highly pleased with you for your dutiful conduct towards me. Ask of me the boon you wish, blessed be you, for I shall grant you what you will ask.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: कृतमित्येव दैत्येन्द्रमुवाच स च वै द्विजः। प्रह्लादस्त्वब्रवीत् प्रीतो गृह्यतां वर इत्युत॥
en: The Brahmana answered the king of the Asuras saying,-Very well. I will obey you.-Prahlada, pleased with him, said,-Take what you wish.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच यदि राजन् प्रसन्नस्त्वं मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम्। भवतः शीलमिच्छामि प्राप्तुमेष वरो मम॥
en: The Brahmana said for. If, O king, you have been pleased with me and if you wish to do what is agreeable to me, I wish then to acquire your behaviour? This is the boon that I pray

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: ततः प्रीतस्तु दैत्येन्द्रो भयमस्याभवन्महत्। वरे प्रदिष्टे विप्रेण नाल्पतेजायमित्युत॥
en: At this, though pleased, Prahlada became stricken with a great fear. Indeed when this boon was indicated by the Brahmana, the Asura king thought that the solicitor could not be an ordinary person.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: एवमस्त्विति स प्राह प्रह्लादो विस्मितस्तदा। उपाकृत्य तु विप्राय वरं दुःखान्वितोऽभवत्॥
en: Wondering much, Prahlada at last said,-Let it be so!-Having, however, granted the boon, the Asura king became filled with grief.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: दत्ते वरे गते विप्रे चिन्ताऽऽसीन्महती तदा। प्रह्लादस्य महाराज निश्चयं न च जग्मिवान्॥
en: Having received the boon, the Brahmana went away, but Prahlada, O king, was stricken with a deep anxiety and knew not what to do.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: तस्य चिन्तयतस्तावच्छायाभूतं महाद्युति। तेजो विग्रहवत् तात शरीरमजहात् तदा॥ तमपृच्छन्महाकायं प्रह्लादः को भवानिति। प्रत्याहतं तु शीलोऽस्मि त्यक्तो गच्छाम्यहं त्वया।॥
en: While the Asura king sat brooding over the matter, a flame of light came out of his person. It had a shadowy form of great effulgence and huge proportions. Prahlada asked the form, saying,-Who are You?-The form answered, saying-—I am the embodiment of your conduct. Renounced by you I am going away.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: तस्मिन् द्विजोत्तमे राजन् वत्स्याम्यहमनिन्दिते। योऽसौ शिष्यत्वमागम्य त्वयि नित्यं समाहितः॥
en: I shall henceforth, O king, dwell in that blameless and foremost of Brahmanas who had become your devoted disciple!-Having said these words, the form vanished and soon after entered the body of Shakra.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: तस्मिंस्तेजसि याते तु तादृगरूपस्ततोऽपरः॥ शरीरानिःसृतस्तस्य को भवानिति चाब्रवीत्।
en: After the disappearance of that form, another of similar form issued out of Prahlada's body. The Daitya king addressing it, said,-Who are you?

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: इत्युक्त्वान्तर्हितं तद् वै शक्रं चान्वाविशत् प्रभो। धर्म प्रह्लाद मां विद्धि यत्रासौ द्विजसत्तमः॥ तत्र यास्यामि दैत्येन्द्र यतः शीलं ततो ह्यहम्।
en: The form answered, saying,-Know me, O Prahlada, for the embodiment of Righteousness, I shall go there where that foremost of Brahmanas is, for, o king of the Daityas, I reside there where Conduct lives!

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: ततोऽपरो महाराज प्रज्वलन्निव तेजसा॥ शरीरानिःसृतस्तस्य प्रह्लादस्य महात्मनः।
en: Upon the disappearance of Righteousness, a third highly effulgent form, O monarch, issued out of the body of the great Prahlada.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: को भवानिति पृष्टश्च तमाह स महाद्युतिः॥ सत्यं विद्ध्यसुरेन्द्राद्य प्रयास्ये धर्ममन्वहम्।
en: Asked by Prahlada as to who he was, that highly effulgent form answered, sayingKnow, O king of the Daityas, that I am Truth. I shall leave you, following the way of Righteousness!

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: तस्मिन्ननुगते सत्ये महान् वै पुरुषोऽपरः॥ निश्चक्राम ततस्तस्मात् पृष्टश्चाह महाबलः। वृत्तं प्रह्लाद मां विद्धि यतः सत्यं ततो ह्यहम्॥
en: After Truth had left Prahlada, following Righteousness, another great person issued out of Prahlada's body. Asked by the Daitya king, the mighty being answered, being answered, I am the embodiment of good works. Know, O Prahlada, that I live there were the Truth lives!

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: तस्मिन् गते महाशब्दः शरीरात् तस्य निर्ययौ। पृष्टश्चाह बलं विद्धि यतो वृत्तमहं ततः॥
en: After this one had left Prahlada, another being come out, giving vent to loud and deep cries. Addressed by Prahlada, he answered,-Know that I am Power. I live there where good works are.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ तत्र यतो वृत्तं नराधिप। ततः प्रभामयी देवी शरीरात् तस्य निर्ययौ॥
en: Having said these words, Power went away where good works had gone. After this, a goddess of great effulgence came out of Prahlada's person.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: तामपृच्छत् दैत्येन्द्रः सा श्रीरित्येनमब्रवीत्। उषितास्मि स्वयं वीर त्वयि सत्यपराक्रम॥ त्वया त्यक्ता गमिष्यामि बलं ह्यनुगता ह्यहम्।
en: The Daitya king asked her and she answered him saying that she was the embodiment of Prosperity, adding,-I lived in you, O hero, O you of prowess incapable of being baffled. Renounced by you, I shall follow Power.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: ततो भयं प्रादुरासीत् प्रह्लादस्य महात्मनः॥ अपृच्छत् स ततो भूयः क्व यासि कमलालये।
en: The great Prahlada, stricken with fear, once more asked the goddess, saying,-Where do you go, O goddess, O you that live amid lotuses?

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: त्वं हि सत्यव्रता देवी लोकस्य परमेश्वरी। कश्चासौ ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठस्तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: You are ever devoted to truth, O goddess, and you are the foremost of deities. Who is that foremost of Brahmanas? I wish to know the truth!

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: श्रीरुवाच स शक्रो ब्रह्मचारी यस्त्वत्तश्चैवोपशिक्षितः। त्रैलोक्ये ते यदैश्वर्यं तत् तेनापहृतं प्रभो॥
en: The goddess of Prosperity said Practising the vow of Brahmacharya, that Brahmana who was instructed by you was Shakra. O foremost one, he robbed you of that sovereignty which you had over the three worlds.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: शीलेन हि त्रयो लोकास्त्वया धर्मज्ञ निर्जिताः। तद्विज्ञाय सुरेन्द्रेण तव शीलं हृतं प्रभो॥
en: O Righteous one, it was by your conduct that you had reduced the three worlds to subjection. Knowing this the king of the gods robbed you of your conduct!

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: धर्मः सत्यं तथा वृत्तं बलं चैव तथाप्यहम्। शीलमूला महाप्राज्ञ सदा नास्त्यत्र संशयः॥
en: Righteousness and Truth and good works and Power and myself, O you of great wisdom, all originate from conduct.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्त्वा गता श्रीस्तु ते च सर्वे युधिष्ठिर। दुर्योधनस्तु पितरं भूय एवाब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: Bhishma said Having said these words, the goddess of Prosperity went away, as also all the rest, O Yudhishthira. Once more addressing his father.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: शीलस्य तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेत्तुं कौरवनन्दन। प्राप्यते च यथा शीलं तं चोपायं वदस्व मे॥
en: Duryodhana said O delighter of the Kurus, I wish to know the truth about conduct. Tell me the means by which it may be acquired.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच सोपायं पूर्वमुद्दिष्टं प्रह्लादेन महात्मना। संक्षेपेण तु शीलस्य शृणु प्राप्तिं नरेश्वर॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Those means were described by the great Prahlada while discoursing to Indra. Listen, however, O king, as to how in brief conduct may be acquired.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु कर्मणा मनसा गिरा। अनुग्रहश्च दानं च शीलमेतत् प्रशस्यते॥
en: Abstention from injury, by act, thought, and word to all creatures, mercy, and gift, constitute the praise-worthy behaviour.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: यदन्येषां हितं न स्यादात्मनः कर्म पौरुषम्। अपत्रपेत वा येन न तत् कुर्यात् कथंचन॥
en: That act or exertion which does not do good to other, or that act for which one has to feel shame, should never be done.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: तत्तु कर्म तथा कुर्याद् येन श्लाध्येत संसदि। शीलं समासेनैतत् ते कथितं कुरुसत्तम॥
en: That act, on the other hand, should be done for which one may be lauded in society. O best of the Kurus, I have now told you briefly as to what conduct is.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: यद्यप्यशीला नृपते प्राप्नुवन्ति श्रियं क्वचित्। न भुञ्जते चिरं तात समूलाश्च न सन्ति ते॥
en: If, O king, wicked persons do ever acquire prosperity, they do not enjoy it long, O son, and are soon rooted out.

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: एतद् विदित्वा तत्त्वेन शीलवान् भव पुत्रका यदीच्छसि श्रियं तात सुविशिष्टां युधिष्ठिरात्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Knowing all this truly, do you, O son, be of good conduct, if you wish to obtain greater prosperity than Yudhishthira.'

description: The characteristics of virtuous conduct and how it can be acquired
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतत् कथितवान् पुत्रे धृतराष्ट्रो नराधिपः। एतत् कुरुष्व कौन्तेय ततः प्राप्स्यसि तत्फलम्॥
en: Bhishma said This was what king Dhritarashtra said to his son. Do you follow these instructions, O son of Kunti, and you will then surely acquire their fruit.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच शीलं प्रधानं पुरुषे कथितं ते पितामह। कथं त्वाशा समुत्पन्ना या चाशा तद् वदस्व मे॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have said, O grandfather, that conduct is the first thing (for a man). Whence, however, does Hope arise? Tell me what it is.

sn: संशयो मे महानेष समुत्पन्नः पितामह। छेत्ता च तस्य नान्योऽस्ति त्वत्तः परपुरजय॥
en: This great doubt has occupied my mind. There is no other person than you, Osubjugator of hostile towns, who can remove it!

sn: पितामहाशा महती ममासीद्धि सुयोधने। प्राप्ते युद्धे तु तद् युक्तं तत् कर्तायमिति प्रभो॥
en: O grandfather, I had great hope about Suyodhana that when a battle was about to take place, he would, O lord, do what was proper.

sn: सर्वस्याशा सुमहती पुरुषस्योपजायते। तस्यां विहन्यमानायां दुःखो मृत्युर्न संशयः॥
en: Hope is tne sheet-anchor of every man. When that hope is destroyed, great grief follows which, forsooth, is almost equal to death itself.

sn: सोऽहं हताशो दुर्बुद्धिः कृतस्तेन दुरात्मना। धार्तराष्ट्रेण राजेन्द्र पश्य मन्दात्मतां मम॥
en: Fool that I am, Dhritarashtra's wicked son, Duryodhana, destroyed the hope I had entertained. Mark, O king, the foolishness of my mind.

sn: आशां महत्तरां मन्ये पर्वतादपि सदुमात्। आकाशादपि वा राजनप्रमेयैव वा पुनः॥
en: I think that hope is bigger than a mountain with all its trees. Or, perhaps, it is bigger than the sky itself. Or, perhaps, O king, it is really immeasurable.

sn: एषा चैव कुरुश्रेष्ठ दुर्विचिन्त्या सुदुर्लभा। दुर्लभत्वाच्च पश्यामि किमन्यद् दुर्लभं ततः॥
en: Hope, O chief of the Kurus, is highly difficult of being understood and equally difficult of being conquered. Seeing this last attribute of Hope, I ask, what else is so unconquerable as this?

sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि युधिष्ठिर निबोध तत्। इतिहासं सुमित्रस्य निर्वृत्तमृषभस्य च॥
en: Bhishma said I shall describe to you, O Yudhishthira, regarding it, the discourse between Sumitra and Rishabha that took place in days of yore, Listen to it!

sn: सुमित्रो नाम राजर्षिर्हहयो मृगयां गतः। ससार स मृगं विद्ध्वा बाणेनानतपर्वणा॥
en: A royal sage of the Haihaya family, Sumitra by namre, went a hunting. Having pierced a deer with a straight arrow, he pursued it.

sn: स मृगो बाणमादाय यथामितविक्रमः। स च राजा बलात् तूर्णं ससार मृगयूथपम्॥
en: Endued with great strength, the deer ran ahead, with the arrow sticking to him. The king was equally powerful, and accordingly pursued his precious game with great speed.

sn: ततो निम्न स्थलं चैव स मृगोऽद्रवदाशुगः। मुहूर्तमिव राजेन्द्र समेन स पथागमत्॥
en: The animal, highly fleet, quickly ran a low ground and then a level plain.

sn: ततः स राजा तारुण्यादौरसेन बलेन च। ससार बाणासनभृत् सखगोऽसौ तनुत्रवान्॥
en: The king, young, active, and strong, and armed with bow and sword and protected with a coat of mail, still pursued it.

sn: ततो नदान नदीश्चैव पल्वलानि बनानि च। अतिक्रम्याभ्यतिक्रम्य ससारैको वनेचरः॥
en: Having none with him to chase the animal through the forest, the king crossed many rivers and lakes.

sn: स तु कामान्मृगो राजन्नासाद्यासाद्य तं नृपम्। पुनरभ्येति जवनो जवेन महता ततः॥
en: Possessed of great fleetness the animal, at its will, appearing now and then before the king, ran on with great quickness.

sn: स तस्य बाणैर्बहुभिः समभ्यस्तो वनेचरः। प्रक्रीडन्निव राजेन्द्र पुनरभ्येति चान्तिकम्॥
en: Pierced with many arrows by the king, that wild animal, O monarch, as if in sport, again and again lessened the distance between itself and the pursuer.

sn: पुनश्च जवमास्थाय जवनो मृगयूथपः। अतीत्यातीत्य राजेन्द्र पुनरभ्येति चान्तिकम्॥
en: Repeatedly showing its quickness and crossing one forest after another, it now and then appeared before the king at a near point.

sn: तस्य मर्मच्छिदं घोरं तीक्ष्णं चामित्रकदर्शनः। समादाय शरं श्रेष्ठं कार्मुके तु तथासृजत्॥
en: At last, taking up a very excellent arrow, sharp, terrible, and capable of cutting the very vitals, the crusher of foes, set it on his bowstring.

sn: ततो गव्यूतिमात्रेण मृगयूथपयूथपः। तस्य बाणपथं मुक्त्वा तस्थिवान् प्रहसन्निव॥
en: That huge animal then, as if laughing at the pursuer's efforts, suddenly went to a great distance by reaching a point full four miles ahead of the range of the arrow.

sn: तस्मिन् निपतिते बाणे भूमौ ज्वलिततेजसि। प्रविवेश महारण्यं मृगो राजाप्यथाद्रवत्॥
en: That effulgent arrow accordingly fell on the ground. The deer entered a large forest, but the king still pursued it.

sn: भीष्म उवाच प्रविश्य स महारण्यं तापसानामथाश्रमम्। आससाद ततो राजा श्रान्तचोपाविशत् तदा।॥
en: Bhishma said Having entered that large forest, the king arrived at an asylum of ascetics. Worn out with toil, he sat himself down for rest.

sn: तं कार्मुकधरं दृष्ट्वा श्रमार्तं क्षुधितं तदा। समेत्य ऋषयस्तस्मिन् पूजां चक्रुर्यथाविधि॥
en: Seeing him armed with bow, exhausted with toil, and hungry, the ascetics approached him and honoured him duly.

sn: स पूजामृषिभिर्दत्तां सम्प्रगृह्य नराधिपः। अपृच्छत् तापसान् सर्वांस्तपसो वृद्धिमुत्तमाम्॥
en: Accepting the honours offered by the Rishis, the king asked them about the progress and advancement to their penances.

sn: ते तस्य राज्ञो वचनं सम्प्रगृह्य तपोधनाः। ऋषयो राजशार्दूलं तमपृच्छन् प्रयोजनम्॥
en: Duly answering the questions of the king, those Rishis having asceticism for wealth, asked that foremost of kings as to the cause of his coming to that retreat.

sn: केन भद्र सुखार्थेन सम्प्राप्तोऽसि तपोवनम्। पदातिर्बद्धनिस्त्रिंशो धन्वी बाणी नरेश्वर॥
en: And they said,-Blessed be you, in pursuit of what delightful object have you, O king, come to this hermitage, walking on foot and armed with sword, bow and arrows?

sn: एतदिच्छामहे श्रोतुं कुतः प्राप्तोऽसि मानद। कस्मिन् कुले तु जातस्त्वं किंनामा चासि ब्रूहि नः॥
en: We wish to hear whence you are coming, O giver of honours! Tell us also in what family you are born and what your name is!-

sn: ततः स राजा सर्वेभ्यो द्विजेभ्यः पुरुषर्षभ। आचचक्षे यथान्यायं परिचर्यां च भारत॥ हैहयानां, कुले जातः सुमित्रो मित्रनन्दनः। चरामि मृगयूथानि निनन् बाणैः सहस्रशः॥ बलेन महता गुप्तः सामात्यः सावरोधनः। मृगस्तु विद्धो बाणेन मया सरति शल्यवान्॥
en: Thus addressed, O foremost of men, the king described himself, O Bharata, saying.-I am born in the family of the Haihayas. My name is Sumitra, and I am the son of Mitra. I chase herds of deer, killing them in thousands with my shafts. Accompanied by a large army and my ministers and the ladies of my household, I have come out ahunting. I struck a deer with a shaft, but the animal with the arrow shaft, but the animal with arrow sticking to his body ran speedily.

sn: तं द्रवन्तमनुप्राप्तो वनमेतद् यदृच्छया। भवत्सकाशं नष्टश्रीर्हताशः श्रमकर्शितः॥
en: In chasing it I have, purposelessly arrived at this forest and find myself before you, shorn of splendour, toil worn, and with hope disappointed.

sn: किं नु दुःखमतोऽन्यद् वै यदहं श्रमकर्शितः। भवतामाश्रमं प्राप्तो हताशो भ्रष्टलक्षणः॥
en: What can be more pitiable than this, viz., that I have arrived at this hermitage, exhausted with toil, shorn of the signs of royalty, and disappointed of my hopes.

sn: न राजलक्षणत्यागो न पुरस्य तपोधनाः। दुःखं करोति तत् तीनं यथाऽऽशा विहता मम॥
en: I am not at all sorry, Oh ye ascetics, at my being now divested of the sins of royalty or at my being now at a distance from my capital. I feel, however, a great grief for my hopes being frustrated.

sn: हिमवान् वा महाशैलः समुद्रो वा महोदधिः। महत्त्वान्नान्वपद्येतां नभसो वान्तरं तथा॥
en: The king of mountains, viz., Himavat, and that vast receptacle of waters, viz., the ocean, cannot, for its vastness, equal the extent of the sky.

sn: आशायास्तपसि श्रेष्ठास्तथा नान्तमहं गतः। भवतां विदितं सर्वं सर्वज्ञा हि तपोधनाः॥
en: Oh ye ascetics, likewise, I also cannot make out the limit of hope. With penances you have made yourselves omniscient. There is nothing which is hidden from you.

sn: भवन्तः सुमहाभागास्तस्मात् पृच्छामि संशयम्। आशावान् पुरुषो यः स्यादन्तरिक्षमथापि वा॥ किं नु ज्यायस्तरं लोके महत्त्वात् प्रतिभाति वः। एतदिच्छामि तत्त्वेन श्रोतुं किमिह दुर्लभम्॥
en: You are also highly blessed. I beg you, therefore, to remove my doubt. Which of these two appears vaster to you, hope of man, or the wide sky? I desire to hear fully, what is so unconquerable as hope.

sn: यदि गुह्यं न वो नित्यं तदा प्रब्रूत मा चिरम्। न गुह्यं श्रोतुमिच्छामि युष्मद्भयो द्विजसत्तमाः॥
en: If the subject be one which you can properly describe, then tell me all about it forthwith. I do not wish, ye foremost of the twice-born, to hear anything from you be a mystery and improper to describe. that may

sn: भवत् तपोविघातो वा यदि स्याद् विरमे ततः। यदि वास्ति कथायोगो योऽयं प्रश्नो मयेरितः॥ एतत् कारणसामर्थ्यं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः। भवन्तोऽपि तपोनित्या ब्रूयुरेतत् समन्विताः॥
en: If again the subject be injurious to your penances, I would not wish you to describe. If the question asked by me be a befitting subject of discourse, I would then wish to hear the cause fully. Devoted to penances as ye are, do ye all instruct me on the subject.'

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततस्तेषां समस्तानामृषीणामृषिसत्तमः। ऋषभो नाम विप्रर्षिविस्मयन्निदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhishma said Then the best of Rishis, viz., the twice-born Rishabha, sitting in the midst of all those Rishis, smiled a little and said

sn: पुराहं राजशार्दूल तीर्थान्यनुचरन् प्रभो। समासादितवान् दिव्यं नरनारायणाश्रमम्॥
en: Formerly, O foremost of Kings, while sojourning among sacred places, I arrived O lord, at the beautiful hermitage of Nara and Narayana.

sn: यत्र सा बदरी रम्या ह्रदो वैहायसस्तथा। यत्र चाश्वशिरा राजन् वेदान् पठति शाश्वतान्॥
en: There lies the charming spot called Badari, and there also is that lake in the sky. There the sage Ashvashiras, O king, reads the eternal Vedas.

sn: तस्मिन् सरसि कृत्वाहं विधिवत् तर्पणं पुरा। पितृणां देवतानां च ततोऽऽश्रममियां तदा॥
en: Having performed my ablutions in that lake duly offered libations of water to the departed manes and the gods, I entered the hermitage.

sn: रेमाते यत्र तौ नित्यं नरनारायणावृषी। अदूरादाश्रमं कञ्चिद् वासार्थमगमं तदा॥
en: Within that retreat the Rishis Nara and Narayana always spend their time happily. Not far from that place I went to another hermitage for taking up my quarter.

sn: तत्र चीराजिनधरं कृशमुच्चमतीव च। अद्राक्षमृषिमायान्तं तनुं नाम तपोधनम्॥
en: While seated there I saw a very tall and emaciated Rishi, clad in rags and skins, coming towards me. Rich in penances, he was named Tanu,

sn: अन्यैर्नरैर्महाबाहो वपुषाष्टगुणान्वितम्। कृशता चापि राजर्षे न दृष्टा तादृशी क्वचित्॥
en: Compared, O mighty-armed one, with other men, his height was eight times greater. Regarding his leanness, O royal sage, I can say that I have never seen its like.

sn: शरीरमपि राजेन्द्र तस्य कानिष्ठिकासमम्। ग्रीवा बाहू तथा पादौ केशाश्चाद्भुतदर्शनाः॥
en: His body, O king, was as thin as one's little finger. His neck and arms and legs and hair were all of extraordinary character.

sn: शिरः कायानुरूपं न कर्णी नेत्रे तथैव च। तस्य वाक्चैव चेष्टा च सामान्ये राजसत्तम॥
en: His head was proportionate to his body, and his ears and eyes, also, were the same. His speech, O best of kings, and his movements were highly feeble.

sn: दृष्ट्वाहं तं कृशं विप्रं भीतः परमदुर्मनाः। पादौ तस्याभिवाद्याथ स्थितः प्राञ्जलिरग्रतः॥
en: Seeing that highly emaciated Brahmana I became very dispirited and frightened. Saluting his feet, I stood before him with clasped hands.

sn: निवेद्य नामगोत्रे च पितरं च नरर्षभ। प्रदिष्टे चासने तेन शनैरहमुपाविशम्॥
en: Having given out to him my name and family, and having told him also the name of my father, O foremost of men, I slowly sat myself down on a seat that was pointed out by him.

sn: ततः स कथयामास कथां धर्मार्थसंहिताम्। ऋषिमध्ये महाराज तनुर्धर्मभृतां वरः॥
en: Then, o king, that foremost of virtuous men, viz., Tanu, began to describe in the midst of the Rishis living in that hermitage the topics regarding Righteousness and Profit.

sn: तस्मिंस्तु कथयत्येव राजा राजीवलोचनः। उपायाज्जवनैरश्वैः सबल: सावरोधनः॥
en: While engaged in discourse, a king, having eyes like lotus-petals and accompanied by his forces and the ladies of his seraglio, came on a car drawn by quick-coursing horses.

sn: स्मरन् पुत्रमरण्ये वै नष्टं परमदुर्मनाः। भूरिद्युम्नपिता श्रीमान् वीरद्युम्नो महायशाः॥
en: The name of that king was Viradyumna. Of beautiful features, he was highly illustrious. His son's name was Bhuridyumna. The child has been missing, and the father, highly dispirited, came there in there in course of his wanderings amid the forest in pursuit of the missing one.

sn: इह द्रक्ष्यामि तं पुत्रं द्रक्ष्यामीहेति पार्थिवः। एवमाशाहतो राजा चरन् वनमिदं पुरा॥
en: I shall find my son here!-I shall find my son here!-Carried on by hope in this way, the king wandered through that forest in those days.

sn: दुर्लभः स मया द्रष्टुं नूनं परमधार्मिकः। एकः पुत्रो महारण्ये नष्ट इत्यसकृत् तदा॥
en: Addressing the emaciated Rishi he said,-Forsooth, that highly virtuous son of mine cannot be traced by me. Alas, he was my only son. He is lost and can nowhere be found.

sn: दुर्लभः स मया द्रष्टुमाशा च महती मम। तया परीतगात्रोऽहं मुमूर्षुर्नात्र संशयः॥
en: Though he cannot be discovered my hope, however, of finding him is very great! With that hope (which is frequently disappointed) I am almost on the point of death.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु भगवांस्तनुर्मुनिवरोत्तमः। अवाक्शिरा ध्यानपरो मुहूर्तमिव तस्थिवान्।१८।।
en: Hearing these words of the king, that foremost of ascetics, viz., the holy Tanu, remained for a short while with head lowering down and himself immersed in contemplation.

sn: तमनुध्यान्तमालक्ष्य राजा परमदुर्मनाः। उवाच वाक्यं दीनात्मा मन्दं मन्दमिवासकृत्॥ दुर्लभं किं नु देवर्षे आशायाश्चैव कि महत्। ब्रवीतु भगवानेतद् यदि गुह्यं न ते मयि॥
en: Seeing him immersed in contemplation, the king became highly disspirited. With great sorrow he began to say slowly and softly,-What, Ocelestial, Rishi, is that which cannot be conquered and what is it that is greater than hope? O holy one, tell me this if I may hear it without any objection.

sn: मुनिरुवाच महर्षिभगवांस्तेन पूर्वमासीद् विमानितः। बालिशां बुद्धिमास्थाय मन्दभाग्यतयाऽऽत्मनः॥
en: The ascetic said A holy and great ascetic had been insulted by your son. He had done it through ill luck, actuated by his foolish understanding.

sn: अर्थयन् कलशं राजन् काञ्चनं वल्कलानि च। अवज्ञापूर्वकेनापि न सम्पादितवांस्ततः। निविण्णः स तु विप्रर्षिनिराशः समपद्यत॥
en: The ascetic has asked your son for a golden jar and vegetable barks. Your son refused, out of contempt, to please the ascetic.

sn: एवमुक्तोऽभिवाद्याथ तमृषि लोकपूजितम्। श्रान्तोऽवसीदद् धर्मात्मा यथा त्वं नरसत्तम॥
en: Thus treated by your son, the great sage became disappointed!-Thus addressed, the king adored that ascetic worshipped of all the world. Of virtuous soul, Viradyumna sat there, worn out with toil even as you, O best of men, noware.

sn: अर्घ्यं ततः समानीय पाद्यं चैव महानृषिः। आरण्येनैव विधिना राज्ञे सर्वं न्यवेदयत्।॥
en: The great ascetic, in return, offered the dwellers, water to wash his feet and the Arghya.

sn: ततस्ते मुनयः सर्वे परिवार्य नरर्षभम्। उपाविशन् नरव्याघ्र सप्तर्षय इव ध्रुवम्॥
en: Then all the ascetics, O. foremost of kings, sat there, encircling that foremost of men like the stars of the constellation of Ursa Major surrounding the Pole star.

sn: अपृच्छंश्चैव तं तत्र राजानमपराजितम्। प्रयोजनमिदं सर्वमाश्रमस्य निवेशने॥
en: And they asked the unvanquished king about the cause of his arrival at that hermitage.

sn: राजोवाच वीरद्युम्न इति ख्यातो राजाहं दिक्षु विश्रुतः। भूरिद्युम्नं सुतं नष्टमन्वेष्टुं वनमागतः॥
en: The king said I am a king named Viradyumna. My fame has travelled everywhere. My Bhuridyumna has been lost. To find him out I have come to this forest.

sn: एकः पुत्रः स विप्राय बाल एव च मेऽनघ। न दृश्यते वने चास्मिंस्तमन्वेष्टुं चराम्यहम्॥
en: O ye foremost of Brahmanas, that child was my only son and, O ye of sinless ones, he is very young. He cannot, however, be found here. I am travelling everywhere for finding him out. son

sn: ऋषभ उवाच इत्येवमुक्ते वचने राज्ञा मुनिरधोमुखः। तूष्णीमेवाभवत् तत्र न च प्रत्युक्तवान् नृपम्॥
en: Rishabha said After the king had said so, the ascetic Tanu lowered his head. He remained absolutely silent, without giving any response.

sn: स हि तेन पुरा विप्रो राज्ञा नात्यर्थमानितः। आशाकृतश्च राजेन्द्र तपो दीर्घं समाश्रितः॥ प्रतिग्रहमहं राज्ञां न करिष्ये कथञ्चन। अन्येषां चैव वर्णानामिति कृत्वा धियं तदा॥ आशा हि पुरुषं बालमुत्थापयति तस्थुषी।
en: Formerly that Brahmana had not been much respected by the king. Out of disappointment, O king, he had practised austere penances for a long time, being determined that he should never accept anything as present from either kings or members of any other caste.

sn: तामहं व्यपनेष्यामि इति कृत्वा व्यवस्थितः। वीरद्युम्नस्तु तं भूयः पप्रच्छ मुनिसत्तमम्॥
en: And he said to himself,-Hope moves every foolish man. I shall banish hope from my mind!-Such was his resolution. Viradyumna once more asked that foremnost of ascetics, saying,

sn: राजोवाच आशायाः किं कृशत्वं च किं चेह भुवि दुर्लभम्। ब्रवीतु भगवानेतत् त्वं हि धर्मार्थदर्शिवान्॥
en: What is the extent of the faintness of Hope? What on Earth is highly difficult to acquire? Tell me this, O holy one, for you are master of virtue and profit.

sn: तत: संस्मृत्य तत् सर्वं स्मारयिष्यन्निवाब्रवीत्। राजानं भगवान् विप्रस्ततः कृशतनुस्तदा॥
en: Rishabha said Remembering all the past incidents and calling them back to the recollection of the king also, that holy Brahmana of emaciated body said to the king.

sn: ऋषिरुवाच कृशत्वेन समं राजन्नाशामा विद्यते नृप। तस्या वै दुर्लभत्वाच्च प्रार्थिताः पार्थिवा मया॥
en: The sage said-There is nothing, o king, which is so slender as Hope, I had requested many kings and found that there is nothing which is so The sage difficult of acquiring as an image presented by Hope before the mind!-

sn: राजोवाच कृशाकृशे मया ब्रह्मन् गृहीते वचनात् तव। दुर्लभत्वं च तस्यैव वेदवाक्यमिव द्विज॥
en: The king said At your words, O Brahmana, I understand what is feeble and what is not so. I understand also now difficult it is to acquire the images placed by hope before the mind. I consider these words of yours as Shruti.

sn: संशयस्तु महाप्राज्ञ संजातो हृदये मम तन्मुने मम तत्त्वेन वक्तुमर्हसि पृच्छतः॥
en: O you of great wisdom, one doubt, however, is in my mind. You should, O sage, explain it fully to me.

sn: त्वत्तः कृशतरं किं नु ब्रवीतु भगवानिदम्। यदि गुह्यं न ते किञ्चिद् विद्यते मुनिसत्तम॥
en: What is slenderer than your body? Tell me this, O holy one, if, however, O best of sages, the subject is one, which may fairly be dealt with.

sn: कृश उवाच दुर्लभोऽप्यथवा नास्ति योऽर्थी धृतिमवाप्नुयात्। स दुर्लभतरस्तात योऽर्थिनं नावमन्यते॥
en: It highly difficult to find a contented applicant. Perhaps, there is none such in the world. Still rare, O sire, is the man who never disregards an applicant.

sn: सत्कृत्य नोपकुरुते परं शक्त्या यथार्हतः। या सक्ता सर्वभूतेषु साऽऽशा कृशतरी मया॥
en: The hope in persons who do not, after making promises, do good to others, to the best of their abilities and according to the fitness of the applicant, is slenderer than even my body.

sn: कृतघ्नेषु च या सक्ता नृशंसेष्वलसेषु च। अपकारिषु चासत्ता साऽऽशा कृशतरीमया॥
en: The hope in an ungrateful man, or in one who is cruel, or in one who is idle, or in one who injures others, is slenderer than even my body.

sn: एकपुत्रः पिता पुत्रे नष्टे वा प्रोषितेऽपि वा। प्रवृत्तिं यो न जानाति साऽऽशा कृशतरी मया॥
en: The hope entertained by a father who has only one son, of once more seeing him after he has been lost or missed, is slenderer than even my body.

sn: प्रसवे चैव नारीणां वृद्धानां पुत्रकारिता। तथा नरेन्द्र धनिनां साऽऽशा कृशतरी मया।॥
en: The hope that old women hold of giving birth to sons, O king, and which is cherished by rich men, is slenderer than even my body.

sn: प्रदानकाक्षिणीनां च कन्यानां वयसि स्थिते। श्रुत्वा कथास्तथायुक्ताः साऽऽशा कृशतरी मया॥
en: The hope of marriage in grown up maidens when they hear any body only talk of it in their presence, is slenderer than even my body.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा ततो राजन् स राजा सावरोधनः। संस्पृश्य पादौ शिरसा निपपात द्विजर्षभम्॥
en: Hearing these words, O monarch, king Viradyumna, and the ladies of his household, laid themselves low before that foremost of Brahmanas and touched his feet with their bent heads.

sn: राजोवाच प्रसादये त्वां भगवन् पुत्रेणेच्छामि संगमम्। यदेतदुक्तं भवता सम्प्रति द्विजसत्तम॥
en: The king said I beg your favour, O holy one. I wish to meet with my child. What you have said, O best of Brahmanas, is very true. There is not doubt of the truth of your words.

sn: ऋषभ उवाच सत्यमेतन्न संदेहो यदेतद् व्याहृतं त्वया। ततः प्रहस्य भगवांस्तनुर्धर्मभृतां वरः॥
en: Rishabha continued The holy Tanu, that best of virtuous persons, smiling, caused, by virtue of his learning and his penances, the king's son to be brought there.

sn: पुत्रमस्यानयत् क्षिप्रं तपसा च श्रुतेन च। स समानीय तत्पुत्रं तमुपालभ्य पार्थिवम्॥
en: Having caused the prince to be brought there, the sage remonstrated with the king (his father). That foremost of virtuous persons then showed himself to be the god of righteousness.

sn: आत्मानं दर्शयामास धर्म धर्मभृतां वरः। स दर्शयित्वा चात्मानं दिव्यमद्भुतदर्शनम्। विपाष्मा विगतक्रोधश्चचार वनमन्तिकात्॥
en: Indeed, having shown his own wonderful and celestials form, he entered an adjacent forest, with heart shorn of anger and the desire of revenge.

sn: एतद् दृष्टं मया राजंस्तथा च वचनं श्रुतम्। आशामपनयस्वाशु ततः कृशतरीमिमाम्॥
en: I saw all this, O king, and heard the words I have said. Dispell your hope that is even slenderer than any of those which the sage pointed out.

sn: भीष्म उवाच स तथोक्तस्तदा राजन् ऋषभेण महात्मना। सुमित्रोऽपनयत् क्षिप्रमाशां कृशतरी ततः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed, O king, by the great Rishabha, king Sumitra quickly renounced the hope that was in his heart and which was slenderer than any of the various sorts of hope pointed out by the emaciated Rishi.

sn: एवं त्वमपि कौन्तेय श्रुत्वा वाणीमिमां मम। स्थिरो भव महाराज हिमवानिव पर्वतः॥
en: Do you also, O son of Kunti, hearing these words of mine, be calm and composed like Himavat.

sn: त्वं हि प्रष्टा च श्रोता च कृच्छ्रेष्वनुगतेष्विह। श्रुत्वा मम महाराज न संतप्तुमिहार्हसि॥
en: Stricken with distress you have questioned me and heard my answer. Fiaving heard it, O monarch, you should remove these regrets of yours.

description: The discourse on Morality between Gotama and Yama
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच नामृतस्येव पर्याप्तिर्ममास्ति ब्रुवति त्वयि। यथा हि स्वात्मवृत्तिस्थस्तथा तृप्तोऽस्मि भारत॥
en: Yudhishthira said Like one who drinks ambrosia my thirst is never satiated with the nectar of your words of wisdom as they fall from your mouth. As a person endued with a knowledge of self is never satiated with meditation, even so I am never satiated with hearing you.

description: The discourse on Morality between Gotama and Yama
sn: तस्मात् कथय भूयस्त्वं धर्ममेव पितामह। न हि तृप्तिमहं यामि पिबन् धर्मामृतं हि ते॥
en: Do you, therefore, O grandfather, describe again morality. I am never satiated with drinking the ambrosia of your discourses upon morality.

description: The discourse on Morality between Gotama and Yama
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। गौतमस्य च संवादं यमस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: Bhishma said “Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Gotama ard the illustrious Yama.

description: The discourse on Morality between Gotama and Yama
sn: पारियानं गिरिं प्राप्य गौतमस्याश्रमो महान्। उवास गौतमो यं च कालं तमपि मे शृणु॥ षष्टिं वर्षसहस्राणि सोऽतप्यद् गौतमस्तपः।
en: Gotama had a wide retrert on the Paripatra hills. Listen to me as to how many years he lived in that asylum. For sixty thousand years that sage practises ascetic austerities in that asylum.

description: The discourse on Morality between Gotama and Yama
sn: तमुग्रतपसा युक्तं भावितं सुमहामुनिम्॥ उपयातो नरव्याघ्र लोकपालो यमस्तदा। तमपश्यत् सुतपस पृषि वै गौतमं तदा॥
en: One day, the Regent of the dead. Yama, O foremost of men, went to that great sage of purified soul while he was practising the severest austerities. Yama saw the great ascetic Gotama of rigid penances.

description: The discourse on Morality between Gotama and Yama
sn: स तं विदित्वा ब्रह्मर्षिर्यममागतमोजसा। प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतो भूत्वा उपविष्टस्तपोधनः॥
en: Understanding that it was Yama who had come, the twice-born quickly saluted him and sat with closed hands in an attentive attitude,

description: The discourse on Morality between Gotama and Yama
sn: तं धर्मराजो दृष्दैव सत्कृत्यैव द्विजर्षभम्। न्यमन्त्रयत धर्मेण क्रियतां किमिति ब्रुवन्॥
en: Beholding that foremost of Brahmanas, the royal Dharma duly saluted him and addressing him asked what he should do for him.

description: The discourse on Morality between Gotama and Yama
sn: गौतम उवाच मातापितृभ्यामानृण्यं किं कृत्वा समवाप्नुयात्। कथं च लोकानाप्नोति पुरुषो दुर्लभाशुचीन्॥
en: Gotama said How does a man liberate his self from the debt he owes to his parents? How, also, does he succeed in acquiring blissful regions which it is so difficult to acquire.

description: The discourse on Morality between Gotama and Yama
sn: यम उवाच तप:शौचवता नित्यं सत्यधर्मरतेन च। मातापित्रोरहरहः पूजनं कार्यमञ्जसा॥
en: Yama said Practising truth, purity and penances, one should continuously adore his parents.

description: The discourse on Morality between Gotama and Yama
sn: अश्वमेधैश्च यष्टव्यं बहुभिः स्वाप्तदक्षिणैः। तेन लोकानवाप्नोति पुरुषोऽद्भुतदर्शनान्॥
en: One should, also, celebrate Horse-sacrifices with profuse presents to the Brahmanas. By such acts one acquires many happy and wonderful regions.'

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मित्रैः प्रहीयमाणस्य बह्वमित्रस्य का गतिः। राज्ञः संक्षीणकोशस्य बलहीनस्य भारत॥
en: Yudhishthira said How should a king behave who is shorn of friends, has many enemies, and an exhausted treasury, and is destitute of troops, O Bharata.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: दुष्टामात्यसहायस्य च्युतमन्त्रस्य सर्वतः। राज्यात् प्रच्यवमानस्य गतिमभ्यामपश्यतः॥ परचक्राभियातस्य परराष्ट्राणि मृद्गतः। विग्रहे वर्तमानस्य दुर्बलस्य वलीयसा॥ असंविहितराष्ट्रस्य देशकालावजानतः। अप्राप्यं च भवेत् सान्त्वंभेदो वाप्यतिपीडनात्। जीवितं त्वर्थहेतुर्वा तत्र किं सुकृतं भवेत्॥
en: Again how should he behave hiinself when he is surrounded by wicked ministers, when his counsels are all divulged, when he does not find his way clearly before him, when he attacks another kingdom, when he is engaged in grinding a hostile kingdom, and when though weak he is at war with a powerful king? How should a king act whose affairs are iilmanaged and who disregards the requirements of place and time, who is unable, for his oppressions, to bring about peace and create disunion among his enemies? Should he try to acquire wealth by foul means or should he sacrifice his life without seeking wealth?

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: भीष्म उवाच गुह्यं धर्मज मा प्राक्षीरतीव भरतर्षभ। अपृष्ठो नोत्सहे वक्तुं धर्ममेतं युधिष्ठिर॥ धर्मो ह्यणीयान् वचनाद् बुद्धिश्च भरतर्षभ। श्रुत्वोपास्य सदाचारैः साधुर्भवति स क्वचित्॥
en: Bhishma said Conversant as you are with duties, you have, O foremost of Bharata's race, asked me a question dealing with the mystery of duties. Without being asked, O Yudhishthira, I could not venture to dwell upon this duty. Morality is very subtile. One understands it, О foremost of Bharata's race by the help of scriptural texts. By remembering what one has heard and by doing good acts, some one in some place may become a righteous person.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: कर्मणा बुद्धिपूर्वेण भवत्याढ्यो न वा पुनः। तादृशोऽयमनुप्रश्नः संव्यवस्यः स्वया धिया॥
en: By acting intelligently the king may or may not acquire wealth. Guided by your own intelligence do you think what reply should be given to your query on this subject.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: उपायं धर्मबहुलं यात्रार्थं शृणु भारत। नाहमेतादृशं धर्मं बुभूषे धर्मकारणात्॥
en: Listen, O Bharata, to the highly meritorious expedient which kings should follow (during times of distress). For the sake of true morality, however, I would not call those means fair.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: दुःखादान इह ह्येष स्यात् तु पश्चात् क्षयोपमः। अभिगम्यमतीनां हि सर्वासामेव निश्चयः॥
en: If the treasury filled by oppression, such a conduct brings the king to the brink of destruction. Such is the conclusion of all intelligente men who have deliberated upon the subject.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: यथा यथा हि पुरुषो नित्यं शास्त्रमवेक्षते। तथा तथा विजानाति विज्ञानमथ रोचते।॥
en: The scriptures or science which one always studies imparts him the knowledge becomes agreeable to him.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: अविज्ञानादयोगो हि पुरुषस्योपजायते। विज्ञानादपि योगश्च योगो भूतिकरः परः॥ अशङ्कमानो वचनमनसूयुरिदं शृणु।
en: Ignorance yields barrenness of invention about means. Finding out of expedicnts, again, through the help of knowledge, becomes the source of great happiness. Without cherishing any misgivings and any malice, here these instructions.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: राज्ञः कोशक्षयादेव जायते बलसंक्षयः॥ कोशं च जनयेद् राजा निर्जलेभ्यो यथा जलम्।
en: Through the decrease of the treasury, the king's army suffers deterioration. The king should, therefore, replenish his treasury like one creating water in a forest which is without water.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: कालं प्राप्यानुगृह्णीयादेष धर्मः सनातनः। उपायधर्म प्राप्येमं पूर्वैराचरितं जनैः॥
en: In pursuance of this code of morality practised by the ancients, the king should, when the opportunity presents itself, show mercy to his subjects. This is eternal duty.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: अन्यो धर्मः समर्थानामापत्स्वन्यश्च भारत। प्राक्कोशात् प्राप्यतें धर्मो वृत्तिधर्माद् गरीयसी॥
en: For able and competent men the duties are of one kind. In times of distress, however, one's duties assume a different aspect. Without riches a king may, by penances acquire religious merit. Life, however, is much more important than religious merit.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: धर्मं प्राप्य न्यायवृत्तिं न बलीयान् न विन्दति। यस्माद् बलस्योपपत्तिरेकान्तेन न विद्यते॥ तस्मादापत्स्वधर्मोऽपि श्रूयते धर्मलक्षणः। अधर्मो जायते तस्मिन्निति वै कवयो विदुः॥
en: By acquiring only religious merit, a king, who is weak never succeeds in acquiring just and proper means for maintenance; and because he cannot, by even his best endeavours, acquire power by the help of only religious merit, therefore the practices in time of distress are sometimes regarded as quite of a piece with morality. The learned, however, opine that those practices beget sinfulness.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: अनन्तरं क्षत्रियस्य तत्र किं विचिकित्स्यते। यथास्य धर्मो न ग्लायेन्नेयाच्छत्रुवशं यथा। तत् कर्तव्यमिहेत्याहुर्नात्मानमवसादयेत्॥
en: After the time of distress is over, what should the Kshatriya do? He should act in such a way that his merit may not be dissipated. He should also act in such a way that he may not have to yield to his foes. These are his duties. He should not be despondent.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: सर्वात्मनैव धर्मस्य न परस्य न चात्मनः। सर्वोपायैरुज्जिहीर्षेदात्मानमिति निश्चयः॥ तत्र धर्मविदां तात निश्चयो धर्मनैपुणम्। उद्यमो नैपुणं क्षात्रे बाहुवीर्यादिति श्रुतिः॥
en: He should not try to save the merit of others or of himself. On the other hand, he should save his own self. This is the settled conclusion. There runs this Shruti, viz., that Brahmanas, who are conversant with duties, should be proficient in them. Likewise, as regards the Kshatriya, his proficiency should be in exertion, since might of arms is his great wealth.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: क्षत्रियो वृत्तिसंरोधे कस्य नादातुमर्हति। अन्यत्र तापसस्वाच्च ब्राह्मणस्वाच्च भारत॥
en: When a Kshatriya's means of sustenance are gone, what should he not take excepting what belongs to ascetics and Brahmanas?

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: यथा वै ब्राह्मणः सीदन्नयाज्यमपि याजयेत्। अभोज्यानानि चाश्नीयात् तथेदं नात्र संशयः॥
en: Even as a Brahmana in a time of distress may officiate at the sacrifice of a person for whom he should never officiate and eat forbidden food, so there is no doubt that a Kshatriya may take riches from every one say ascetics and Brahmanas.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: पीडितस्य किमद्वारमुत्पथो विधृतस्य च। अद्वारतः प्रद्रवति यदा भवति पीडितः॥
en: Even one attacked (by an enemy and seeking the means of escape) what can be an unfair means? For a person confined in a ungeon and seeking escape what can be an improper path? When a person becomes afflicted, he escapes by even an improper way.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: यस्य कोशबलग्लान्या सर्वलोकपराभवः। भैक्ष्यचर्या न विहिता न च विट् शूद्रजीविका॥
en: For a Kshatriya who has, for his insufficient treasury and army, become exceedingly humiliated, neither a life of mendicancy nor the profession of a Vaishya or that of a Shudra has been sanctioned.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: स्वधर्मानन्तरा वृत्तिर्जात्याननुपजीवतः। जहतः प्रथमं कल्पमनुकल्पेन जीवनम्॥
en: The profession prescribed for a Kshatriya is the acquisition of wealth by battle and victory. He should never beg of a member of his own caste. The person who maintains himself ordinarily by following the practices primarily sanctioned, for him, may, in times of distress, support himself by following the practices laid down in the alternative.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: आपद्गतेन धर्माणामन्यायेनोपजीवनम्। अपि ह्येतद् ब्राह्मणेषु दृष्टं वृत्तिपरिक्षये॥
en: In a time of distress, when ordinary practices cannot be followed, a Kshatriya may support himself by even unjust and improper means. The very Brahmanas, it is seen, do the same when their means of living run out.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: क्षत्रिये संशयः कस्मादित्येवं निश्चितं सदा। आददीत विशिष्टेभ्यो नावसीदेत् कथंचन॥ हन्तारं रक्षितारं च प्रजानां क्षत्रियं विदुः। तस्मात् संरक्षता कार्यमादानं क्षत्रबन्धुना॥
en: When the Brahmanas act thus, what doubt is there regarding the conduct of the Kshatriya)? This is, indeed, settled. Without despairing and yielding to destruction, a Kshatriya nay, by force, take, what he can, from rich persons. Know that the Kshatriya may, by force, take, what he can, from rich persons. Know that the Kshatriya is the protector and the destroyer of the people. Therefore, a Kshatriya in difficulty should take by force, what he can, with a view to protect the people.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: अन्यत्र राजन् हिंसाया वृत्तिर्नेहास्ति कस्यचित्। अप्यरण्यसमुत्थस्य एकस्य चरतो मुनेः॥
en: No person in this world, O king, can maintain himself without injuring other creatures. The very ascetic leading a solitary life in the forest is no exception.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: न शङ्खलिखितां वृत्तिं शक्यमास्थाय जीवितुम्। विशेषतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ प्रजापालनमीप्सया॥
en: A Kshatriya should not live, depending upon destiny, especially he, O chief of the Kurus, who wishes to rule.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: परस्परं हि संरक्षा राज्ञा राष्ट्रेण चापदि। नित्यमेव हि कर्तव्या एष धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: The king and the kingdom should always mutually protect each other. This is an eternal duty.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: राजा राष्ट्रं यथाऽऽपत्सु द्रव्यौघैरपि रक्षति। राष्ट्रेण राजा व्यसने रक्षितव्यस्तथा भवेत्॥
en: As the king protects, by spending all his money, the kingdom, when it is in distress, so should the kingdom protect the kingdom protect the king when he is in distress.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: कोशं दण्डं बलं मित्रं यदन्यदपि संचितम्। न कुर्वीतान्तरं राष्ट्र राजा परिगतः क्षुधा।॥
en: The king, even when reduced to straits, should never abandon his treasury, his machinery for punishing the wicked, his army, his friends and allies, and uther necessary institutions and the chiefs living in his kingdom.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: बीजं भक्तेन सम्पाद्यमिति धर्मविदो विदुः। अत्रैतच्छम्बरस्याहुमहामायस्य दर्शनम्॥
en: Masters of duty say that one must keep his seeds, even from his very food. This a truth cited from the work of Shamvara, well-known for his great powers of illusion.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: धिक् तस्य जीवितं राज्ञो राष्ट्रं यस्यावसीदति। अवृत्त्यान्यमनुष्योऽपि यो वैदेशिक इत्यपि॥
en: Fie on the life of that king whose kingdom is weakened. Fie on the life of that men who from want of means goes to a foreign country in quest of a living.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: राज्ञः कोशबलं मूलं कोशमूलं पुनर्बलम्। तन्मूलं सर्वधर्माणां धर्ममूलाः पुनः प्रजा:॥
en: The king depends upon his treasury and army. His army, again, depends on his treasury. His army is the source of all his religious merits. His religious merits, again, are the root of his people.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: नान्यानपीडयित्वेह कोशः शक्यः कुतो बलम्। तदर्थं पीडयित्वा च दोषं प्राप्तुं न सोऽर्हति॥
en: The treasury can never be replenished without oppressing others. How then can the army be maintained without oppression? The king, therefore, in times of difficulty, commits no sin by oppressing his subjects for filling the treasury.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: अकार्यमपि यज्ञार्थं क्रियते यज्ञकर्मसु। एतस्मात् कारणाद् राजा न दोषं प्राप्तुमर्हति॥
en: For celebrating sacrifices many improper deeds are done. Therefore a king commits no sin by doing improper acts (when he seeks to fill his treasury in a time of distress).

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: अर्थार्थमन्यद् भवति विपरीतमथापरम्। अनर्थार्थमथाप्यन्यत् तत् सर्वं ह्यर्थकारणम्। एवं बुद्ध्या सम्प्रपश्येनमेधावी कार्यनिश्चयम्॥
en: For the sake of wealth improper practices are followed in seasons of distress. If (at such times) such improper practices be not followed, evil is the sure consequence. All those institutions that are maintained for working destruction and miso y exist for the sake of collecting wealth. Guided by such considerations, an intelligent king should settle his conduct.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: यज्ञार्थमन्यद् भवति यज्ञोऽन्यार्थस्तथा परः। यज्ञस्यार्थार्थमेवान्यत् तत् सर्वं यज्ञसाधनम्॥
en: As animals and other articles are a necessary or sacrifices, as sacrifices are for purifying the heart, and as animals, sacrifices, and purity of the heart, are all for final liberation, even so policy and punishment exist for the treasury, the treasury, exists for the army, and policy and treasury and army all the three exists for defeating enemies and protecting or enlarging the kingdom.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: उपमामत्र वक्ष्यामि धर्मतत्त्वप्रकाशिनीम्। यूपं छिन्दन्ति यज्ञार्थं तत्र ये परिपन्थिनः॥ दुमाः केचन सामन्ता ध्रुवं छिन्दन्ति तानपि। ते चापि निपतन्तोऽन्यान् निघ्नन्त्येव वनस्पतीन्॥
en: I shall here quote an example illustrating the true way of morality. A large tree is cut down for making out of it a sacrificial stake. In cutting it, other trees which stand in its way have also to be cut down. These, also, while falling down, kill others standing there about.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: एवं कोशस्य महतो ये नराः परिपन्थिनः। तानहत्वा न पश्यामि सिद्धिमत्र परंतप॥
en: So they who stand in the way of replenishing a treasury must be killed. I do not see how else success can be acquired.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: धनेन जयते लोकावुभौ परमिमं तथा। सत्यं च धर्मवचनं यथा नास्त्यधनस्तथा॥
en: By wealth, both the worlds, viz., this and the other, can be acquired, as also Truth and religious merit. A person who has no wealth is more dead than alive.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: सर्वोपायैराददीत धनं यज्ञप्रयोजनम्। न तुल्यदोषः स्यादेवं कार्याकार्येषु भारत॥
en: Wealth for the celebration of sacrifices should be won by every means. The demerit of an act, done in an hour of difficulty, does not equal to that which permeates the same, if done at other tinies, O Bharata.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: नैतौ सम्भवतो राजन् कथंचिदपि पार्थिवा न हरण्येषु पश्यामि धनवृद्धानहं क्वचित्॥
en: The acquisition of wealth and its abandonment cannot both be possibly suen in the same individual, O king. I do not see a rich man in the forest.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: यदिदं दृश्यते वित्तं पृथिव्यामिह किंचन। ममेदं स्यान्ममेदं स्यादित्येवं काक्षते जनः॥
en: With respect to wealth which is seen in this world, every one fights with every one else, saying,-This shall be mine.-This shall be imine.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: न च राज्यसमो धर्मः कश्चिदस्ति परंतप। धर्मः संशब्दितो राज्ञामापदर्थमतोऽन्यथा।॥
en: There is nothing, O scorcher of foes, which yields greater merit to a king than the possession of a kingdom. It is sinful for a king to oppress his subjects with heavy taxes at ordinary times. In a season of distress, it is quite different.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: दानेन कर्मणा चान्ये तपसान्ये तपस्विनः। बुद्ध्या दाक्ष्येण चैवान्ये विन्दन्ति धनसंचयान्॥
en: Some acquire wealth by gifts and sacrifices; some who like penances acquire the same by penances; some acquire it by the help of their intelligence and cleverness.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: अधनं दुर्बलं प्राहुर्धनेन बलवान् भवेत्। सर्वं धनवता प्राप्यं सर्वं तरति कोशवान्॥
en: A person who has no wealth is said to be weak, while he who has wealth becomes powerful. A man of riches may acquire everything. A king who has a well-replenished treasury can accomplish everything.

description: The conduct of a king when he has no friends or when he is surrounded by wicked ministers
sn: कोशेन धर्मः कामश्च परलोकस्तथा ह्ययम्। तं च धर्मेण लिप्सेत नाधर्मेण कदाचन॥
en: By his treasury a king may acquire religious merit, gratify his desire for pleasure, acquire the next world, and this also. The treasury, however, should be filled by the help of righteousness and never by unrighteous deeds, which pass for righteousness in times of difficulty.

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच क्षीणस्य दीर्घसूत्रस्य सानुक्रोशस्य बन्धुषु। परिशङ्कितवृत्तस्य श्रुतमन्त्रस्य भारत॥
en: Yudhishthira said What, besides this, should be done by a king, who is weak and procrastinating, who does not engage in battle from anxiety for the lives of his friends, who is always stricken with fear, and who cannot keep his counsels close?

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: विभक्तपुरराष्ट्रस्य निर्द्रव्यनिचयस्य च। असम्भावितमित्रस्य भिन्नामात्यस्य सर्वशः॥ परचक्राभियातस्य दुर्बलस्य बलीयसा। आपन्नचेतसो ब्रूहि किं कार्यमवशिष्यते॥
en: What, indeed, should that king do whose cities and kingdoms have been divided and appropriated by enemies, who is divested of wealth, who cannot honour his friends and win them over to himself, whose ministers are disunited or brought over by his enemies, who is obliged to stand in the face of enemies, whose army has been diminished, and whose heart has been agitated by some strong enemy?

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: भीष्म उवाच बाह्यश्चेद् विजिगीषुः स्याद् धर्मार्थकुशलः शुचिः। जवेन संधिं कुर्वीत पुर्वभुक्तान् विमोचयेत्॥
en: If the attacking enemy be of pure heart and if he be a master of both virtue and profit, a king of the sort you have pointed out, should forthwith, make peace with the invader and secure the restoration of those parts of the kingdom which have already been conquered.

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: योऽधर्मविजिगीषुः स्याद् बलवान् पापनिश्चयः। आत्मनः संनिरोधेन संधिं तेनापि रोचयेत्॥
en: If, again, the invader be powerful and iniquitious and seek to acquire victory by unfair means, the king should inake peace with him, too, by leaving off a portion of his kingdom.

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: अपास्य राजधानी वा तरेद् द्रव्येण चापदम्। तद्भावयुक्तो द्रव्याणि जीवन् पुनरुपार्जयेत्॥
en: If the invader be reluctant to make peace, the king should then leave his very capital and all his properties for escaping from danger. If he can save his life he may expect to make similar acquisitions in future.

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: यास्तु कोशबलत्यागाच्छक्यास्तरितुमापदः। कस्तत्राधिकमात्मानं संत्यजेदर्थधर्मवित्॥
en: What man who knows virtue is there, who would sacrifice his own self, which is a more valuable property, for meeting that danger from which he can escape by abandoning his treasury and army?

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: अवरोधान् जुगुप्सेत का सपत्नधने दया। न त्वेवात्मा प्रदातव्यः शक्ये सति कथंचन॥
en: A king should protect the ladies of his seraglio. If these fall into the hands to the enemy, he should not show any mercy. As long as he can, he should never surrender his own self to the enemy.

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आभ्यन्तरे प्रकुपिते बाह्ये चोपनिपीडिते। क्षीणे कोशे श्रुते मन्त्रे किं कार्यमवशिष्यते॥
en: What should a king do when his own people are dissatisfied with him, when he is oppressed by invaders, when his treasury is exhausted and when his counsels are given out?

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: भीष्म उवाच क्षिप्रं वा संधिकाम: स्यात् क्षिप्रं वा ताणविक्रमः। तदापनयनं क्षिप्रमेतावत् साम्परायिकम्॥
en: Bhishma said: A king, under such circumstances, should (if his enemy be righteous) try to make peace with him. If the enemy be vicious, he should then display his courage. He should by such means, try to cause the enemy to retire from his kingdom; or, fighting bravely, he should sacrifice his life and ascend to heaven.

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: अनुरक्तेन चेष्टेन हृष्टेन जगतीपतिः। अल्पेनापि हि सैन्येन महीं जयति भूमिपः॥
en: A king can conquer the whole Earth with the help of even a small army if that army be loyal, contented, and devoted to his well-being.

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: हतो वा दिवमारोहेद्धत्वा वा क्षितिमावसेत्। युद्धे हि संत्यजन् प्राणान् शक्रस्यैति सलोकताम्॥
en: If killed in battle, he is sure to ascend to heaven. If he succeed in killing (his enemies), he is sure to enjoy the Earth. By sacrificing one's life in battle, one lives with Indra himself.'

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: सर्वलोकागमं कृत्वा मृदुत्वं गन्तुमेव च। विश्वासाद् विनयं कुर्याद् विश्वसेच्चाप्युपायतः॥
en: Pleasing all people of opposition taking them in trust with humble, king should search other means to regain previous ones.

description: The conduct of king who is weak, and whose kingdom is divided
sn: अपचिक्रमिषुः क्षिप्रं साम्ना वा परिसान्त्वयन्। विलवयित्वा मन्त्रेण ततः स्वयमुपक्रमेत्॥
en: Or by the sweetest words he should please them by means of conciliation and again by the consultation with wise men he should act to regain it.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच हीने परमके धर्म सर्वलोकाभिसंहिते। सर्वस्मिन् दस्युसाद्भूते पृथिव्यामुपजीवने॥ केन स्विद् ब्राह्मणो जीवेज्जघन्ये काल आगते। असंत्यजन् पुत्रपौत्राननुक्रोशात् पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said When virtuous practices calculated to be beneficial the worlds, disappear, when all the means and resources for subsistence fall into the hands of robbers, when such a calamitous time appears, by what means should a Brahmana, O grandfather, who from affection cannot leave his sons and grandsons maintain himself?

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: भीष्म उवाच विज्ञानबलमास्थाय जीवितव्यं तथागते। सर्वं साध्वर्थमेवेदमसाध्वर्थं न किंचन॥
en: Bhishma said When such a time appears the Brahmana should live by the help of knowledge. Everything in this world is for the good. Nothing here is for the wicked.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: असाधुभ्योऽर्थमादाय साधुभ्यो यः प्रयच्छति। आत्मानं संक्रमं कृत्वा कृच्छ्रधर्मविदेव सः॥
en: He, who, himself being an instrument of acquisition, takes wealth from the wicked and gives it to the good, is said to be conversant with the virtue of adversity.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: आकाङ्क्षन्नात्मनो राज्यं राज्ये स्थितिमकोपयन्। अदत्तमेवाददीत दातुर्वित्तं ममेति च॥
en: Desirous of preserving his rule, the king, O monarch, without making his subjects indignant and rebellious may take what is not given to him by the owner, of his own accord, saying,-This is mine.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: विज्ञानबलपूतो यो वर्तते निन्दितेष्वपि। वृत्तिविज्ञानवान् धीरः कस्तं वा वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: That wise man, who, purified by the possession of knowledge, power and righteous conduct at other times, acts censurably in such times, does not really deserve to be blamed.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: येषां बलकृता वृत्तिस्तेषामन्या न रोचते। तेजभासिप्रवर्तन्ते बलवन्तो युधिष्ठिर।॥
en: They, who always support themselves by displaying their power, never prefer any other mode of living. The powerful, O Yudhishthira, always live by the help of prowess.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: यदैव प्राकृतं शास्त्रमविशेषेण वर्तते। तदैवमभ्यसेदेवं मेधावी वाप्यथोत्तरम्॥
en: The ordinary injunctions of the scriptures, without exceptions of any kind, should be followed by a king at such times, while following those scriptures, an intelligent king would do something more.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: ऋत्विकपुरोहिताचार्यान् सत्कृतानभिसत्कृतान्। न ब्राह्मणान् घातयीत दोषान् प्राप्नोति घातयन्॥
en: At such times, however, the king should not oppress Ritwijas, Purohitas preceptors and Brahmanas, all of whom are respected and held in high esteem. By oppressing them, even at such times, he incurs blame and sin.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: एतत् प्रमाणं लोकस्य चक्षुरेतत् सनातनम्। तत् प्रमाणोऽवगाहेत तेन तत् साध्वसाधु वा॥
en: This is considered as an authority in the world. Indeed, this is the eternal eye. One should be guided by this authority. This determines whether a king is to be called good or wicked.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: बहवो ग्रामवास्तव्या रोषाद् ब्रूयुः परस्परम्। न तेषां वचनाद् राजा सत्कुर्याद् घातयीत वा॥
en: It is seen that moved by jealousy and anger many persons, living in villages and towns, vilify one another. The king should never, as said by them, honour or punish any body.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: न वाच्यः परिवादोऽयं न श्रोतव्यः कथञ्चन। कर्णावथ पिधातव्यौ प्रस्थेयं चान्यतो भवेत्॥
en: Slander should never be circulated. If spoken, it should never be heard. When any slanderous conversation goes on, one should close one's ears or leave the place immediately.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: असतां शीलमेतद् वै परिवादोऽथ पैशुनम्। गुणानामेव वक्तारः सन्तः सत्सु नराधिप॥
en: Slanderous conversation becomes only wicked men. It is assign of depravity. They, on the cther hand, O king, who mention the virtues of others in assemblies of the god, are good men.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: यथा सुमधुरौ दम्यौ सुदान्तौ साधुवाहिनौ। धुरमुद्यम्य वहतस्तथा वर्ते: वै नृपः॥
en: As a pair of good-tempered bulls, governable and well-trained to bear loads, put their necks to the yoke and drag the cart willingly, so should the king bear his burden in times of difficulty.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: यथा यथास्य बहवः सहायाः स्युस्तथा परे। आचारमेव मन्यन्ते गरीयो धर्मलक्षणम्॥
en: Others say that a king should behave in such a way that he may succeed in acquiring a large number of allies. Some consider ancient practices as the highest mark of righteousness.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: अपरे नैवमिच्छन्ति ये शङ्खलिखितप्रियाः। मात्सर्यादथवा लोभान ब्रूयुर्वाक्यमीदृशम्॥
en: They, however, who laud the conduct followed by Shankha towards Likhita, do not hold this opinion. They do not pass such an opinion through either malice or covetousness.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: आर्षमप्यत्र पश्यन्ति विकर्मस्थस्य पातनम्। न तादृक्सदृशं किञ्चित् प्रमाणं दृश्यते क्वचित्॥
en: There are even great Rishis who have laid down that even preceptors, if addicted to evil practices, should be punished. But there is no recognised authority for such a holding.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: देवताश्च विकर्मस्थं पातयन्ति नराधमम्। व्याजेन विन्दन् वित्तं हि धर्मात् स परिहीयते॥
en: The gods will punish such men when they happen to be vile and guilty of wicked practices. The king, who replenishes his treasury by fraudulent means, certainly deviates from the path of righteousness.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: सर्वतः सत्कृतः सद्भिर्भूतिप्रवरकारणैः। हृदयेनाभ्यनुज्ञातो यो धर्मस्तं व्यवस्यति॥
en: That code of morality which is honoured by good persons in affluent circumstances, and which is approved by every honest man, should be followed.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: यश्चतुर्गुणसम्पन्नं धर्मं ब्रूयात् स धर्मवित्। अहेरिव हि धर्मस्व पदं दुःखं गवेषितुम्॥
en: He is the master of duty who knows it as depending on all the four foundations. It is as difficult to find out the reasons of duties as it is difficult to find out the legs of the snake.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: यथा मृगस्य विद्धस्य पदमेकं पदं नयेत्। स्रक्षेद् रुधिरलेपेन तथा धर्मपदं नयेत्॥
en: As a hunter discovers the track of a deer wounded with arrow by marking spots of blood on the ground, so should one try to find out the reasons of duties.

description: When robbers attack a kingdom how should a Brahman maintain his own people
sn: एवं सद्धिविनीतेन पथा गन्तव्यमित्युत। राजर्षीणां वृत्तमेतदवगच्छ युधिष्ठिर।॥
en: Thus should a man follow humbly the path of the good. Such was the conduct of the great royal sages of yore, O Yudhishthira.

description: How should a king replenish his Treasury in emergency
sn: भीष्म उवाच स्वराष्ट्रात् परराष्ट्राच्च कोशं संजनयेन्नृपः। कोशाद्धि धर्मः कौन्तेय राज्यमूलं च वर्धते॥
en: Bhishma said By taking riches from his own kingdom as also from the kingdoms of his enemies, the king should, replenish his treasury. Religious merit springs from the treasury, O son of Kunti, and it is through the treasury that the roots of his kingdom extend.

description: How should a king replenish his Treasury in emergency
sn: तस्मात् संजनयेत् कोशं सत्कृत्य परिपालयेत्। परिपाल्यानुतनुयादेष धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: For these reasons the treasury must be replenished; and when filled, it should be carefully kept, and even sought to be increased. This is the eternal practice.

description: How should a king replenish his Treasury in emergency
sn: न कोशः शुद्धशौचेन न नृशंसेन जातुचित्। मध्यमं पदमास्थाय कोशसंग्रहणं चरेत्॥
en: The treasury cannot be replenished by (acting with) purity and fairness, nor by (acting with) ruthless cruelty. It should be filled by following a middle course.

description: How should a king replenish his Treasury in emergency
sn: अबलस्य कुत: कोशो ह्यकोशस्य कुतो बलम्। अबलस्य कुतो राज्यमराज्ञः श्रीर्भवेत् कुतः॥
en: How can a weak king have a treasury? How can a king who has no treasury have strength? How can a weak man maintain a kingdom? How, again, can one, who has no kingdom of his own, acquire prosperity?

description: How should a king replenish his Treasury in emergency
sn: उच्चैर्वृत्तेः श्रियो हानिर्यथैव मरणं तथा। तस्मात् कोशं बलं मित्रमथ राजा विवर्धयेत्॥
en: Adversity is like death to a person of high rank. Therefore, the king should always multiply his treasury, and army, and allies and friends.

description: How should a king replenish his Treasury in emergency
sn: हीनकोशं हि राजानमवजानन्ति मानवाः। न चास्याल्पेन तुष्यन्ति कार्यमप्युत्सहन्ति च॥
en: All men disregard a king, who has an empty treasury. Without being pleased with the little that such a king can give, his servants never show any zeal in his business.

description: How should a king replenish his Treasury in emergency
