en: Yudhishthira said “When virtue is deteriorated and is transgressed by all, when sin is considered as virtue, and virtue become vice, when all healthy restraints are washed a way, and all truths regarding righteousness are disturbed and confounded, when people are oppressed by kings and robbers, when men of all the four modes of life become stupefied about their duties, and all works are shorn of merit, when men see cause of fear on all sides for lust and covetousness and folly, when all creatures cease to trust one another, when they kill one another by deceitful means and impose upon one another, when houses are consumed throughout the country, when the Brahmanas are greatly assailed, when the clouds do not discharge a drop of rain, when every one's hand is turned against his neighbour, when all the necessaries of life are misappropriated by robbers, when, indeed, such a season of dreadful distress sets in by what means should a Brahmana live who is reluctant to renounce mercy and his children? How, indeed, should a Brahmana maintain himself at such a time? Tell me this, O grandfather! How also should the king live at such a time when iniquity possess the world? How, O scorcher of enemies, should the king live so that he might not deviate from both virtue and profit.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: भीष्म उवाच राजमूला महाबाहो योगक्षेमसुवृष्टयः। प्रजासु व्याधयश्चैव मरणं च भयानि च॥
en: 'O mighty-armed one, the peace and prosperity of subjects, profuse and seasonable rain, disease, death, and other calamities, all depend on the king.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: कृतं त्रेतां द्वापरं च कलिश्च भरतर्षभ। राजमूला इति मतिर्मम नास्त्यत्र संशयः॥
en: I have no doubt also in this, O foremost of Bharata's race, that the setting of Krita, Treta, Dvapara and Kali, all depend on the king's conduct.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: तस्मिंस्त्वभ्यागते काले प्रजानां दोषकारके। विज्ञानबलमास्थाय जीवितव्यं भवेत् तदा॥
en: When such a time of calamity as has been described by you sets in, virtuous men should support themselves by the help of judgement.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। विश्वामित्रस्य संवादं चाण्डालस्य च पक्कणे॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old story of the conversation between Vishvamitra and the Chandala in a village of Chandalas.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: त्रेताद्वापरयोः संधौ तदा दैवविधिक्रमात्। अनावृष्टिरभूद् घोरा लोके द्वादशवार्षिकी।॥
en: Towards the end of Treta and the commencement of Dvapara, a dreadful drought took place, extending for twelve years, in consequence of what the gods had ordained.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: प्रजानामतिवृद्धानां युगान्ते समुपस्थिते। त्रेताविमोक्षसमये द्वापरप्रतिपादने॥ ववर्ष सहस्त्राक्षः प्रतिलोमोऽभवद् गुरुः। जगाम दक्षिणं मार्गं सोमो व्यावृत्तलक्षणः॥ न
en: At that time which was the end of Treta and the commencement of Dvapara, when the time came for many sufficiently old creatures to give up their lives, the thousand-eyed god poured no rain. The planet Brihaspati began to move in the opposite course, and Soma, giving up his own orbit, receded towards the south.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: नावश्यायोऽपि तत्राभूत् कुत एवाभ्रजातयः। नद्यः संक्षिप्ततोयौघाः किंचिदन्तर्गतास्ततः॥
en: Not even could a dew-drop be seen, what to speak of the gathering clouds? The rivers were all reduced into narrow streamlets.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: सरांसि सरितश्चैव कूपाः प्रस्रवणानि च। हतत्विषो न लक्ष्यन्ते निसर्गाद् दैवकारितात्॥
en: Everywhere, lakes, well and springs disappeared and lost their beauty for that change brought about by the gods.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: उपशुष्कजलस्थाया विनिवृत्तसभाप्रपा। निवृत्तयज्ञस्वाध्याया निर्वषट्कारमङ्गला॥
en: Water becoming scarce, the places for the distribution of charities became desolate. The Brahmanas abstained from the celebration of sacrifices and recitation of the Vedas. They did no longer utter Vashats and performed other propitiatory rites.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: उच्छिन्नकृषिगोरक्षा निवृत्तविपणापणा! निवृत्तयूपसम्भारा विप्रणष्टमहोत्सवा॥
en: Agriculture and tending of cattle were given up. Markets and shops were abandoned. Stakes for binding sacrificial animals disappeared. People no longer collected various sorts of articles for sacrifices. All festivals and amusements died.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: अस्थिसंचयसंकीर्णा महाभूतरवाकुला। शून्यभूयिष्ठनगरा दग्धग्रामनिवेशना॥
en: Everywhere heaps of bones were seen and every place was filled with the shrill cries and yells of terrific creatures. The cities and towns of the Earth were shorn of inhabitants. Villages and hamlets were burnt down.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: क्व चिच्चोरैः क्व चिच्छस्त्रैः क्व चिद् राजभिरातुरैः। परस्परभयाच्चैव शून्यभूयिष्ठनिर्जना॥
en: Some assailed by robbers, some, by weapons and some, by bad kings, and in fear of one another, began to fly away.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: गतदैवतसंस्थाना वृद्धबालविनाकृता। गोजाविमहिषीहीना परस्परपराहता।॥
en: Temples and places of worship became desolate. The aged were forcibly turned out of their houses. Kine, goats, sheep and buffaloes fought (for food) and died in large numbers. The Brahmanas began to die on all sides.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: हतविप्रा हतारक्षा प्रणशैषधिसंचया। सर्वभूतरुतप्राया बभूव वसुधा तदा॥
en: Protection was at an end. Herbs and plants were dried up. The Earth was divested of all her beauty and looked highly awful like the trees in a crematorium.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: तस्मिन् प्रतिभये काले क्षते धर्मे युधिष्ठिर। बभूवुः क्षुधिता माः खादमानाः परस्परम्॥
en: In that dreadful period, when righteousness was lost, O Yudhishthira, men in hunger, lost their senses and began to eat one another.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: ऋषयो नियमांस्त्यक्त्वा परित्यज्याग्निदेवताः। आश्रमान् सम्परित्यज्य पर्यधावन्नितस्ततः॥
en: The very Rishis, giving up their vows and their fires and deities, and deserting their forest-retreats, began to walk about in quest of food.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्रोऽथ भगवान् महर्षिरनिकेतनः। क्षुधापरिगतो धीमान् समन्तात् पर्यधावत॥
en: The holy and great Rishi Vishvamitra, endued with great intelligence, wandered homeless and stricken with hunger.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: त्यक्त्वा दारांश्च पुत्रांश्च कस्मिंश्च जनसंसदि। भक्ष्याभक्ष्यसमो भूत्वा निरग्निरनिकेतनः॥
en: Leaving his wife and son in some place of shelter, the Rishi walked about, fireless and homeless, without caring for pure or impure food.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: स कदाचित् परिपतश्वपचानां निवेशनम्। हिंस्त्राणां प्राणिघातानामाससाद वने क्वचित्॥
en: One day he arrived at a hamlet, in the midst of a forest, inhabited by cruel hunters given to the destruction of living creatures.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विभिन्नकलशाकीर्णं श्वचर्मच्छेदनायुतम्। वराहखरभग्नास्थिकपालघटसंकुलम्॥
en: The little hamlet was filled with broken jars, and pots made of earth. Dog-skins were seen here and there. Heaps of bones and skulls, of boars and asses, lay in various places.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: मृतचैलपरिस्तीर्णं निर्माल्यकृतभूषणम्। सर्पनिर्मोकमालाभिः कृतचिह्नकुटीमठम्॥
en: Clothes of the dead lay here and there, and the huts were adorned with garlands of used up flowers. Many of the denizens again were dressed with sloughs cast off by snakes.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: कुक्कुटारावबहुलं गर्दभध्वनिनादितम्। उद्घोषद्भिः खरैर्वाक्यैः कलहद्भिः परस्परम्॥
en: The place was resonant with the loud crowing of cocks and hens and the discordant bray of asses. The inhabitants quarrelled with one another, uttering harsh words in shrill voices.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: उलूकपक्षिध्वनिभिर्देवतायतनैर्वृतम्। लोहघण्टापरिष्कारं श्वयूथपरिवारितम्॥
en: There were temples of gods on all sides bearing emblems of owls and other birds. Resounding with the sound of iron bells, the hamlet was filled with dogs standing or lying on every side.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: तत् प्रविश्य क्षुधाविष्टो विश्वामित्रो महानृषिः। आहारान्वेषणे युक्तः परं यत्नं समास्थितः॥
en: Stricken with hunger and engaged in search after food, the great Rishi Vishvamitra entered that hamlet and tried his level best to find something to eat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: न च क्व चिदविन्दत् स भिक्षमाणोऽपि कौशिकः। मांसमन्नं फलं मूलमन्यद् वा तत्र किञ्चन॥
en: Though the son of Kushila begged again and again, yet he could not get any meat or rice or fruit or root or any other kind of food.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: अहो कृच्छं मया प्राप्तमिति निश्चित्य कौशिकः। पपात भूमौ दौर्बल्यात् तस्मिंश्चाण्डालपक्कणे॥
en: The then, exclaiming-Alas, great is my suffering!-dropped down from weakness in that hamlet of the Chandalas.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: स चिन्तयामास मुनिः किं नु मे सुकृतं भवेत्। कथं वृथा न मृत्युः स्यादिति पार्थिवसत्तम॥
en: The sage began to reflect, aside,-What is best for me to do now?-Indeed, O best of kings, he then thought oniy of the means by which he could avoid immediate death.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: स ददर्श श्वमांसस्य कुतन्त्री विवतां मुनिः। चाण्डालस्य गृहे राजन् सद्यः शस्त्रहतस्य वै॥
en: He saw, O king, a huge piece of flesh, of a dog that had recently been killed with a weapon, spread on the floor of a Chandala's hut.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: स चिन्तयामास तदा स्तैन्यं कार्यमितो मया। न हीदानीमुपायो मे विद्यते प्राणधारणे॥
en: The sage thought and decided that he should steal that meat. And he said to himself, I have no means now of keeping up my life.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: आपत्सु विहितं स्तैन्यं विशिष्टसमहीनताः। विप्रेण प्राणरक्षार्थ कर्तव्यमिति निश्चयः॥
en: Theft is sanctioned in an hour of distress for even a great man. It will not divest him of his eminence. Even a Brahmana for saving his life may do it. This is certain.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: हीनादादेयमादौ स्यात् समानात् तदनन्तरम्। असम्भवे वाऽऽदीत विशिष्टादपि धार्मिकात्॥
en: First of all one should steal from a degraded person. Failing such a person one may steal from one's equal. Failing an equal, one may steal from even a great and virtuous man.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: सोऽहमन्त्यावसायानां हराम्येनां प्रतिग्रहात्। न स्तैन्यदोषं पश्यामि हरिष्यामि श्वजाघनीम्॥
en: I shall then, at this time when my life itself is almost gone, steal this meat. I do not see sin in such theft. I shall, therefore, steal this haunch of dog's meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: एतां बुद्धिं समास्थाय विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः। तस्मिन् देशे स सुष्वाप श्वपचो यत्र भारत॥
en: Having thus resolved this resolution, the great sage Vishvamitra lay down for sleep where the Chandala was.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: स विगाढां निशां दृष्ट्वा सुप्ते चाण्डालपक्कणे। शनैरुत्थाय भगवान् प्रविवेश कुटीमठम्॥
en: Seeing sometime after that the night had advanced and that the whole Chandala hamlet were in sleep, the holy Vishvamitra, quietly rising up, entered that hut.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: स सुप्त इव चाण्डालः श्लेष्मापिहितलोचनः। परिभिन्नस्वरो रूक्षः प्रोवाचाप्रियदर्शनः॥
en: The Chandala who was the owner of it, with eyes covered with pleghm, was lying like one asleep. Of disagreeable look, he said these harsh words in a broken and discordant voice.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच कः कुतन्त्री घटयति सुप्ते चाण्डालपक्कणे। जागर्मि नात्र सुप्तोऽस्मि हतोऽसीति च दारुणः॥
en: The Chandala said Who is there, busy with opening up the latch? The whole Chandala hamlet is asleep. I, however, am awake and not asleep. Whoever you are, you are about to be killed!-These were the harsh words that met the sage's ears.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्रस्ततो भीतः सहसा तमुवाच ह। तत्र व्रीडाकुलमुखः सोद्वेगस्तेन कर्मणा॥ विश्वामित्रोऽहमायुष्मन्नागतोऽहं बुभुक्षितः। मा वधीर्मम सबुद्धे यदि सम्यक् प्रपश्यसि॥
en: Stricken with fear, his face reddened with the blushes of shame, and his heart filled with anxiety caused by that act of theft which he had tried, he answered, saying,-Oh you long-lived one, I am Vishvamitra! I have come here suffering from hunger. O you of righteous soul, do not kill me, if your vision be clear!

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: चाण्डालस्तद् वचः श्रुत्वा महर्षे वितात्मनः। शयनादुपसम्भ्रान्त उद्ययौ प्रति तं ततः॥
en: Hearing these words of that great Rishi of pure soul the Chandala rose up in fear from his bed and approached the sage.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: स विसृज्याश्रु नेत्राभ्यां बहुमानात् कृताञ्जलिः। उवाच कौशिकं रात्रौ ब्रह्मन् किं ते चिकीर्षितम्॥
en: Clasping his hands from respect and with eyes bathed in tears, he addressed Kushika's son, saying,-What do you seek here in the night, O Brahmana?

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्रस्तु मातङ्गमुवाच परिसान्त्वयन्। क्षुधितोऽहं गतप्राणो हरिष्यामि श्वजाघनीम्॥
en: Conciliating the Chandala, Vishvamitra said, I am greatly hungry and about to die of starvation. I wise to take away that haunch of dog's meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: क्षुधित: कलुषं यातो नास्ति हीरशनार्थिनः। क्षुच्च मां दूषयत्यत्र हरिष्यामि श्वजाघनीम्॥
en: Being hungry I have become sinful. One who seeks food has no shame. It is hunger which is actuating me to commit this sin. It is for this that I wish to take away that haunch of dog's meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: अवसीदन्ति मे प्राणाः श्रुतिर्मे नश्यति क्षुधा। दुर्बलो नष्टसंज्ञश्च भक्ष्याभक्ष्यविवर्जितः॥ सोऽधर्मं बुद्ध्यमानोऽपि हरिष्यामि श्वजाघनीम्।
en: My life is on the point of departure. Hunger has sullied my Vedic learning. I am weak and have lost my senses. I have no scruple about pure and impure food. Although I know it is sinful still I wish to take away that haunch of dog's meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: अटन् भैक्ष्यं न विन्दामि यदा युष्माकमालये॥ तदा बुद्धिः कृता पापे हरिष्यामि श्वजाघनीम्।
en: After I had failed to secure any alms, having wandered from house to house in this your hamlet, I determined to perpetrate this sinful act of taking away this haunch of dog's meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: अग्निर्मुखं पुरोधाश्च देवानां शुचिषाड् विभुः॥ यथावत् सर्वभुम् ब्रह्मा तथा मां विद्धि धर्मतः। तमुवाच स चाण्डालो महर्षे शृणु मे वचः॥
en: Fire is the mouth of the gods. He is also their priest. He should, therefore, take nothing save pure and clean things. At times, however, that great god becomes a consuiner of everythings. Know that I have now become like him.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्रुत्वा तत् त्वं तथाऽऽतिष्ठ यथा धर्मो न हीयते। धर्म वापि विप्रर्षे शृणु यत् ते ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: Hearing these words of the great Rishi, the Chandala answered him, saying,-Listen to me. Having heard these truthful words of mine, act in such a way that your religious merit may not suffer.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: शृगालादधमं श्वानं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः। तस्याप्यधम उद्देशः शरीरस्य श्वजाघनी॥
en: Hear, O regenerate Rishi, What I say to you about your duty. The wise say that a dog is impurer than a jackal. The haunch, again, of a dog is impurer then any other part of his body.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: नेदं सम्यग् व्यवसितं महर्षे धर्मगर्हितम्। चाण्डालस्वस्य हरणमभक्ष्यस्य विशेषतः॥
en: This is not wise resolution of yours, therefore, O great Rishi, this act, this theft of what belongs to a Chandala this theft, moreover of impure food, is not right.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: साध्वन्यमनुपश्य त्वमुपायं प्राणधारणे। न मांसलोभात् तपसो नाशस्ते स्यान्महामुने॥
en: Blessed to you, do you look out for some other means for keeping your life. O great sage, let not your penances suffer destruction for this your strong desire for dog's meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: जानता विहितं धर्मं न कार्यो धर्मसंकरः। मा स्म धर्म परित्याक्षीस्त्वं हि धर्मभृतां वरः॥
en: Knowing as you do the duties sanctioned in the scriptures, you should not do a act which leads to a confusion of duties. Do not renounce righteousness, for you are the foremost of all pious persons.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्रस्ततो राजनित्युक्तो भरतर्षभ। क्षुधातः प्रत्युवाचेदं पुनरेव महामुनिः॥ निराहारस्य सुमहान् मम कालोऽभिधावतः। न विद्यतेऽप्युपायश्च कश्चिन्मे प्राणधारणे॥
en: Thus addressed, O king, the great Rishi Vishvamitra, stricken with hunger, O foremost of Bharata's race, once more said,-A long time has passed away without my having taken any food, I do not see any means again for keeping up my life.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: येन येन विशेषेण कर्मणा येन केनचित्। अभ्युज्जीवेत् साद्यमानः समर्थो धर्ममाचरेत्॥
en: One should, when he is about to die, keep up his life by any means in his power without judging of their charter. Afterwards, when able, he should seek the acquisition of merit.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: ऐन्द्रो धर्मः क्षत्रियाणां ब्राह्मणानामथाग्निकः। ब्रह्मवह्निर्मम बलं भक्ष्यामि शमयन् क्षुधाम्॥
en: The Kshatriyas should follow the conduct of Indra. It is the duty of the Brahmanas to behave like Agni. The Vedas are fire. They form my strength. I shall, therefore, eat even this impure food for satisfying my appetite.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: यथा यथैव जीवेद्धि तत् कर्तव्यमहेलया। जीवितं मरणाच्छ्यो जीवन् धर्ममवाप्नुयात्॥
en: That by which life may be preserved should, forsooth, be done unhesitatingly. Life is better than death. By living, one may acquire virtue.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: सोऽहं जीवितमाकाङ्क्षन्नभक्ष्यस्यापि भक्षणम्। व्यवस्ये बुद्धिपूर्वं वै तद् भवाननुमन्यताम्॥
en: Seeking to preserve my life, I wish, with my perfect sense, to eat this impure food. You just order me.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: बलवन्तं करिष्यामि प्रणोत्स्याम्यशुभानि तु। तपोभिर्विद्यया चैव ज्योतीषीव महत्तमः॥
en: Continuing to live I shall try to acquire virtue and shall dissipate by penances and by knowledge the calamities which have befallen me, like the luminaries of the sky destroying even the thickest darkness.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच नैतत्खादन्प्राप्नुते दीर्घमायु नैव प्राणान्नामृतस्येव तृप्तिः। भिक्षामन्यां भिक्ष मा ते मनोऽस्तु श्वभक्षणेश्वा ह्यभक्ष्यो द्विजानाम्॥
en: The Chandala said By eating this food one like yourself cannot live long. Nor can one (like you) get strength (from such food), nor that gratification which ambrosia yields. Do you beg for some other kind of alms. Be not bent upon eating dog's imeat. The meat of dog is, forsooth, an impure food for the twice-born ones.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच न दुर्भिक्षे सुलभं मांसम च्छ्वपाक मन्ये न च मेऽस्ति वित्तम्। क्षुधार्तश्चाहमगतिर्निराशः श्वमांसे चास्मिन् षडरूसान् साधु मन्ये॥
en: Vishvamitra said Any other sort of meat cannot be easily had during a famine like this.Besides, OChandala, I have no money. I am very much hungry. I cannot move any longer. I am utterly hopeless. I think that all the six sorts of taste exist in that piece of dog's meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच पञ्च पञ्चनखा भक्ष्या ब्रह्मक्षत्रस्य वै विशः। यथा शास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते माभक्ष्ये मानसं कृथाः॥
en: The Chandala said Only five sorts of meat are clean food for Brahmanas and Kshatriyas and Vaishyas, as sanctioned in the scriptures. Do not wish to have forbidden food.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच अगस्त्येनासुरो जग्धो वातापिः क्षुधितेन वै। अहमापद्गतः क्षुत्तो भक्षयिष्ये श्वजाघनीम्॥
en: Vishvamitra said While hungry, the great Rishi Agastya ate up the Asura named Vatapi. I am in distress. I am hungry. I shall, therefore, eat that haunch of dog's meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच भिक्षामन्यामाहरेति न च कर्तुमिहार्हसि। न नूनं कार्यमेतद् वै हर कामं श्वजाघनीम्॥
en: The Chandala said Do you beg for something else. You should not do such a thing. Verily you should not do such an act. If, however, you like, you may take away this piece of dog's meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच शिष्टा वै कारणं धर्मे तवृत्तमनुवर्तये। परां मेध्याशनामेनां भक्ष्यां मन्ये श्वजाघनीम्॥
en: Vishvamitra said The good are the authorities in matters of duty. I am following their example. I now consider this dog's haunch to be better food than any other pure food.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच असता यत् समाचीर्णं न च धर्मः सनातनः। नाकार्यमिह कार्यं वै मा छलेनाशुभं कृथाः॥
en: The act of an impious man can never be regarded as an eternal practice. An improper act can never be a proper one. Do not commit a sin by deception.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच न पातकं नावमतमृषिः सन् कर्तुमर्हति। समौ च श्वमृगौ मन्ये तस्माद् भोक्ष्ये श्वजाघनीम्।।७५।
en: Vishvamitra said A man who is a Rishi cannot commit a sin. In the present case, deer and dog, I think, are the same. I shall, therefore, eat this dog's haunch.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच यद्ब्राह्मणार्थे कृतमर्थितेन तेनर्षिणा तदवस्थाधिकारे। स वै धर्मो यत्र न पापमस्ति सर्वैरुपायैर्गुरवो हि न रक्ष्याः॥
en: The Chandala said Begged by the Brahmans, the Rishi (Agastya) did that act. Under the circumstances it could not be a sin. Righteousness is that in which there is no sin. Besides, the Brahmanas, who are the preceptors of the three other orders, should be protected and maintained by all means.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच मित्रं च मे ब्राह्मणस्यायमात्मा प्रियश्च मे पूज्यतमश्च तं धर्तुकामोऽहमिमां जिहीषे। नृशंसानामीदृशानां न बिभ्ये॥ लोके।
en: I am a Brahman. This my body is my friend. It is very dear to me and deserves the highest respect from me. In order to keep up the body I wish to take away that dog's haunch. I have become so eager that I do not fear you and your dreadful brother any longer.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच कामं नरा जीवितं संत्यजन्ति न चाभक्ष्ये क्वचित् कुर्वन्ति बुद्धिम्। सर्वान् कामान् प्राप्नुवन्तीह विद्वन् प्रियस्व कामं सहितः क्षुधैव॥
en: Men give up their lives but still they do not seek impure food. All their wishes are fulfilled who can conquer appetite in this world. Do you also conquer your hunger and obtain those rewards.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच स्थाने भवेत् संशयः प्रेत्यभावे निःसंशयः कर्मणां वै विनाशः। अहं पुनव्रतनित्यः शमात्मा मूलं रक्ष्यं भक्षयिष्याम्यभक्ष्यम्॥
en: Vishvamitra said About myself, I always observe rigid vows and my heart is set on peace. For preserving the root of all religious merit, I shall eat impure food.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: बुद्ध्यात्मके व्यक्तमस्तीति पुण्यं मोहात्मके यत्र यथा श्वभक्ष्ये। यद्यप्येतत् संशयात्मा चरामि नाहं भविष्यामि यथा त्वमेव॥
en: It is clear that such an act would be considered moral for a person of pure soul. To a person, however, of impure soul the eating of dog's flesh would appear sinful. Even if my conclusion be wrong (and if I eat this dog's ineat) I shall not, for that act, become one like you.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच गोपनीयमिदं दुःखमिति मे निश्चिता मतिः। दुष्कृतोऽब्राह्मणः सत्रं यस्त्वामहमुपालभे॥
en: The Chandala said It is my settled conclusion that I should try my best to prevent you from this sin. By doing a wicked act a Brahmana goes down from his elevated station. It is for this that I am remonstrating with you.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच पिबन्त्येवोदकं गावो मण्डूकेषु रुवत्स्वपि। न तेऽधिकारो धर्मेऽस्ति मा भूरात्मप्रशंसकः॥
en: Vishvamitra said Kine go on drinking without caring for the croaking of the frogs. You have no right to decide what is right (and what, not). Do not speak highly of yourself.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच सुहृद् भूत्वानुशासे त्वां कृपा हि त्वयि मे द्विजा यदिदं श्रेय आधत्स्व मा लोभात् पातकं कृथाः॥
en: The Chandala said I have become your friend, therefore, I am speaking thus to you. Do what is good. Do not, from temptation, do what is sinful.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच सुहृन्मे त्वं सुखेप्सुश्चेदापदो मां समुद्धर। जानेऽहं धर्मतोऽऽत्मानं शौनीमुत्सृज जाघनीम्॥
en: Vishvamitra said If you be a friend who wishes me happiness, do you then extricate me from this distress. In that case, casting off this dog's haunch, I may think myself saved by the help of righteousness (and not by that of sinfulness).

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच नैवात्सहे भवतो दातुमेतां नोपेक्षितुं ह्रियमाणं स्वमन्नम्। उभौ स्यावः पापलोकावलिप्तौ दाता चाहं ब्राह्मणस्त्वं प्रतीच्छन्॥
en: The Chandala said I dare not present this piece of meat to you, nor can I quietly allow you to rob me of my own food. If I give you this meat and if you take it, yourself being a Brahmana, both of us will go down to regions of misery in the next world.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच अद्याहमेतद् वृजिनं कर्म कृत्वा जीवंश्चरिष्यामि महापवित्रम्। स पूतात्मा धर्ममेवाभिपत्स्य। यदेतयोर्गुरु तद् वै ब्रवीहि॥
en: Vishvamitra said By committing this sin to-day I shall certainly save my life which is very sacred. Having saved my life I shall afterwards practice virtue and purify my soul. Tell me which of these two is preferable.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच आत्मैव साक्षी कुलधर्मकृत्ये त्वमेव जानासि यदत्र दुष्कृतम्। यो ह्याद्रियाद्भक्ष्यमितिश्चमांसं मन्ये न तस्यास्ति विवर्जनीयम्॥
en: The Chandala said One's own self is the best judge, while discharging the duties of his own caste or family. You yourself know which of those two acts is sinful. He who would consider dog's meat as pure food, I think, would not shrink from taking anything and everything.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच उपादने खादने चास्ति दोषः कार्यात्यये नित्यमत्रापवादः। यस्मिन् हिंसा नानृतं वाच्यलेझे ऽभक्ष्यक्रिया यत्र न तद्गरीयः॥
en: Vishvamitra said There is sin in accepting (an unclean present) or in eating (unclean food). When one's life is in peril, there is no sin in accepting such a present or eating such food. Besides, the eating of unclean food, when it does not involve destruction and deception and when the act will excite only mild rebuke, is not a very important matter.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच यद्येष हेतुस्तव खादने स्यान्न ते वेदः कारणं नार्यधर्मः। तस्माद्भक्ष्येऽभक्षणे वा द्विजेन्द्र दोषं न पश्यामि यथेदमत्र॥
en: The Chandala said If this be your argument for taking impure food, it is then evident you do not respect the Veda and Aryan morality. Taught by what you are about to do, I see, O foremost of Brahmanas, there is no sin in neglecting the difference between pure and impure food.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच नैवातिपापं भक्ष्यमाणस्य दृष्टं सुरां तु पीत्वा पततीति शब्दः। अन्योन्यकार्याणि यथा तथैव न पापमात्रेण कृतं हिनस्ति॥
en: Vishvamitra said It is not seen that a person commits a grave sin by taking interdicted food. It is only an oral precept which says that one becomes fallen by drinking wine. The other forbidden acts,-in fact, every sin,-cannot destroy one's merit.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: श्वपच उवाच अस्थानतो हीनतः कुत्सिताद् वा तद् विद्वांसं बाधते साधुवृत्तम्। श्वानं पुनर्यो लभतेऽभिषङ्गात् तेनापि दण्डः सहितव्य एव॥
en: The Chandala Said That learned man who takes away dog's meat from an unworthy place like this), from an impure wretch (like me), from a wicked man (like me), commits an act which is never done by the good. On the other hand, for his connection with such act, he is sure to undergo the pangs of repentance.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्त्वा निववृत्ते मातङ्गः कौशिकं तदा। विश्वामित्रो जाहरैव कृतबुद्धिः श्वजाघनीम्॥
en: Bhishma said Having said these words to Kushika's son, the Chandala became silent, Vishvamitra then, of refined understanding, took away that haunch of dog's meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: ततो जग्राह स श्वाङ्गं जीवितार्थी महामुनिः। सदारस्तामुपाहृत्य वने भोक्तुमियेष सः॥
en: Having secured the piece of dog's meat for saving his life, the great ascetic took it away into the forest and wished with his wife to eat it.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: अथास्य बुद्धिरभवद् विधिनाहं वजाघनीम्। भक्षयामि यथाकामं पूर्वं संतर्घ्य देवताः॥
en: He thought that having first duly pleased the gods, he should then eat that haunch of dog's meat at his pleasure.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: ततोऽग्निमुपसंहृत्य ब्राह्मण विधिना मुनिः। ऐन्द्राग्नेयेन विधिना चळं श्रपयत स्वयम्॥
en: Lighting up a fire according to the Brahma rites, the ascetic, in pursuance of the rites of Aindragneya, began himself to cook that meat into sacrificial Charu.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: ततः समारभत् कर्म दैवं पित्र्यं च भारत। आहूय देवानिन्द्रादीन् भागं भागं विधिक्रमात्॥
en: He then, O Bharata, began to perform the ceremonies in honour of the gods and the departed manes, by dividing that Charu into as many parts as were necessary, according to the injunctions of the scriptures, and by invoking the gods headed by Indra.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु प्रववर्ष स वासवः। संजीवयन् प्रजाः सर्वा जनयामास चौषधीः॥
en: Meanwhile, the king of the gods began to pour profusely. Reviving all creatures by those showers, he made plants and herbs grow once more.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: विश्वामित्रोऽपि भगवांस्तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषः। कालेन महता सिद्धिमवाप परमाद्भुताम्॥
en: However, having completed the rites in honour of the gods and the Pitris and having pleased them duly, Vishvamitra, himself took that meat.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: स संहत्य च तत् कर्म अनास्वाद्य च तद्धविः। तोषयामास देवांश्च पितुंश्च द्विजसत्तमः॥
en: Consuming all his sins afterwards by his penances, the sage after a long time, gained the most wonderful (ascetic) success.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: एवं विद्वानदीनात्मा व्यसनस्थो जिजीविषुः। सर्वोपायैरुपायज्ञो दीनमात्मानमुद्धरेत्॥
en: Thus, having the preservation of life itself in view, a high-souled person, endued with learning and acquainted with means, should rescue his own cheerless self when fallen into distress, by all means in his power.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: एतां बुद्धिं समास्थाय जीवितव्यं सदा भवेत्। जीवन् पुण्यमवाप्नोति पुरुषो भद्रमश्नुते॥
en: With such a view one should always preserve his life. person, if alive, can acquire religious merit and enjoy happiness and prosperity.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: तस्मात् कौन्तेय विदुषा धर्माधर्मविनिश्चये। बुद्धिमास्थाय लोकेऽस्मिन् वर्तितव्यं कृतात्मना॥
en: Therefore, O son of Kunti, a person of purified soul and endued with learning should live and act in this world, depending upon his own intelligence in ascertaining virtue and vice. With such a view one should always preserve his life. person, if alive, can acquire religious merit and enjoy happiness and prosperity.

description: The duties of a king when sin prevails in his kingdom
sn: तस्मात् कौन्तेय विदुषा धर्माधर्मविनिश्चये। बुद्धिमास्थाय लोकेऽस्मिन् वर्तितव्यं कृतात्मना॥
en: Therefore, O son of Kunti, a person of purified soul and endued with learning should live and act in this world, depending upon his own intelligence in ascertaining virtue and vice.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यदि घोरं समुद्दिष्टमश्रद्धयमिवानृतम्। अस्मि स्विद् दस्युमर्यादा यामहं परिवर्जये॥
en: Yudhishthira said If such a terrible act which should always be discarded like falsehood, be pointed (as duty), then what act is there from which I should forbear? Why also should not robbers then be honoured?

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: सम्मुह्यामि विषीदामि धर्मो मे शिथिलीकृतः। उद्यम नाधिगच्छामि कदाचित् परिसान्त्वयन्॥
en: I am stupefied! My heart is pained. All the bonds that tie me to morality are loosened. I cannot compose my mind and dare act in the way pointed out by you.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: भीष्म उवाच नैतच्छ्रुत्वाऽऽगमादेव तव धर्मानुशासनम्। प्रजासमवहारोऽयं कविभिः सम्भृतं मधु॥
en: Bhishma said I do not instruct you regarding duty, taught by what I have heard from the Vedas alone. What I have told you is the result of wisdom and experience. This is the honey that the learned have gleaned.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: बयः प्रतिविधातव्याः प्रज्ञा राज्ञा ततस्ततः! नैकशाखेन धर्मेण यत्रैषा सम्प्रवर्तते॥
en: Kings should collect wisdom from various sources. One cannot go successfully through the worldly course with the help of a one-sided morality.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: बुद्धिसंजननो धर्म आचारश्च सतां सदा। ज्ञेयो भवति कौरव्य सदा तद् विद्धि मे वचः॥
en: Duty must originate from the understanding and the practices of the good should always be determined, O son of Kuru. Obey these words of mine.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: वुद्धिश्रेष्ठा हि राजानश्चरन्ति विजयैषिणः। धर्मः प्रतिविधातव्यो बुद्ध्या राज्ञा ततस्ततः॥
en: Only kings of superior intelligence can rule, cxpccting victory. A king by the help of his understanding and guided by knowledge gathered from various sources, should so arrange that inoral laws may be observed.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: नैकशाखेन धर्मेण राज्ञो धर्मो विधीयते। दुर्बलस्य कुतः प्रज्ञा पुरस्तादनुपाहृता॥
en: The duties of a king can never be satisfied by rules drawn from a one-sided morality. A weak king can never show wisdom for his not having drawn it from the examples before him.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: अद्वैधज्ञः पथि द्वैधे संशयं प्राप्तुमर्हति। बुद्धिद्वैधं वेदितव्यं पुरस्तादेव भारत॥
en: Righteousness sometimes appears like unrighteousness. The latter also some-times appears like the former. He who does not know this, becomes confused when an actual instance presents itself before him. Before the time comes, one should, O Bharata, understand the circumstances, under which righteousness and its opposite become confused.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: पार्श्वतः करणं प्राज्ञो विम्भित्वा प्रकारयेत्। जनस्तच्चरितं धर्मं विजानात्यन्यथान्यथा॥
en: Having gained this knowledge, a wise king should, when the time comes, act accordingly, helped by his judgement. His acts at such a time are misunderstood by ordinary people.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: अमिथ्याज्ञानिनः केचिन्मिथ्याविज्ञानिनः परे। तद्वै यथायथं बुद्ध्वा ज्ञानमाददते सताम्॥
en: Some persons are endued with true knowledge. Some persons have false knowledge. Truly determining the nature of each kind of knowledge, a wise king derives knowledge from the good.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: परिमुष्णन्ति शास्त्राणि धर्मस्य परिपन्थिनः। वैषम्यमर्थविद्यानां निरर्थाः ख्यापयन्ति ते॥
en: The violators of moral laws find fault with the scriptures. They who have themselves no money, point out the inconsistencies of the works on the laws of wealth.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: आजिजीविषवो विद्यां यशःकामौ समन्ततः। ते सर्वे नृप पापिष्ठा धर्मस्य परिपन्थिनः॥
en: Those who wish to gain knowledge merely for carrying their sustenance, are, o king, sinful, besides being enemies of morality.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: अपक्वमतयो मन्दा न जानन्ति यथातथम्। यथा ह्यशास्त्रकुशलाः सर्वत्रायुक्तिनिष्ठिताः॥
en: Wicked men of unripe understandings, can never know things truly, as persons ignorant of scriptures are unable in all their acts to be guided by reason.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: परिमुष्णन्ति शास्त्राणि शास्त्रदोषानुदर्शिनः। विज्ञानमर्थविद्यानां न सम्यगिति वर्तते।॥
en: Always seeing the faults of the scriptures, they decry them. Even if they understand the true import of the scriptures, they are still in the habit of saying that scriptural injunctions are unsound.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: निन्दया परविद्यानां स्वविद्यां ख्यापयन्ति च। वागस्त्रा वाक्छरीभूता दुग्धविद्याफला इव॥
en: By decrying the knowledge of others, such men announce the superiority of their own knowledge. They have words for their weapons and arrows and speak, as if they are well grounded in those sciences.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: तान् विद्यावणिजो विद्धि राक्षसानिव भारत। व्याजेन सद्भिर्विहितो धर्मस्ते परिहास्यति॥
en: Consider them, O Bharata, as traders in learning and Rakshasas among men. By the help of mere pretext they renounce that morality, which has been established by good and wise men.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: न धर्मवचनं वाचा नैव बुद्ध्येति नः श्रुतम्। इति बार्हस्पतं ज्ञानं प्रोवाच मघवा स्वयम्॥
en: We have heard that the texts of morality cannot be understood by either discussion or one's own intelligence. Indra himself has said that such is the opinion of the sage Brihaspati.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: न त्वेव वचनं किंचिदनिमित्तादिहोच्यते। सुविनीतेन शास्त्रेण न व्यवस्यन्त्यथापरे॥
en: Some hold that no scriptural text has been written without a reason, Others again, even if they properly understand the scriptures, never follow them.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: लोकयात्रामिहैके तु धर्मं प्राहुर्मनीषिणः। समुद्दिष्टं सतां धर्मं स्वयमूहेत पण्डितः॥
en: One section of wise men say that morality is nothing else than the approved conduct of the world. The man of true knowledge should find out for himself the moral laws laid down for the good.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: अमर्षाच्छास्त्रसम्मोहादविज्ञानाच्च भारत। शास्त्रं प्राज्ञस्य वदतः समूहे यात्यदर्शनम्॥
en: If even a wise man speaks of morality when he is angry or bewildered or ignorant, his speech produces no effect.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: आगतागमया बुद्ध्या वचनेन प्रशस्यते। अज्ञानाज्ज्ञानहेतुत्वाद् वचनं साधु मन्यते॥
en: Discourses on morality made with the help of an intelligent understanding of the true letter and spirit of the scriptures, should be lauded and not those which are made with the help of anything else. Sensible words, even if heard from an ignorant person, are regarded as pious and wise.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: अनया हतमेवेदमिति शास्त्रमपार्थकम्। दैतेयानुशना प्राह संशयच्छेदनं पुरा॥
en: In days of yore, Ushanas said to the Daityas this truth, which dispels all doubts, that scriptures are no scriptures if they cannot stand the crucible test of reason.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: ज्ञानमप्यपदिश्यं हि यथा नास्ति तथैव तत्। तं तथा छिन्नमूलेन सन्नोदयितुमर्हसि॥
en: The possession or absence of doubtful, knowledge is the same thing. You should root out and drive off such knowledge.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: अनव्यवहितं यो वा नेदं वाक्यमुपाश्नुते। उग्रायैव हि सृष्टोऽसि कर्मणे न त्वमीक्षसे॥
en: He who does not listen to these words of minc, is to be known as one who has suffered himself to be misguided. Do you not observe that you were created for the performance of terrific deeds?

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: अङ्ग मामन्ववेक्षस्व राजन्याय बुभूषते। यथा प्रमुच्यते त्वन्यो यदर्थं न प्रमोदते।॥
en: See me, O dear child, how, by following the duties of my own order, I have sent innumerable Kshatriyas to heaven! There are some who are not pleased with me for this.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: अजोऽश्वः क्षत्रमित्येतत् सदृशं ब्रह्मणा कृतम्। तस्मादभीक्ष्णं भूतानां यात्रा काचित् प्रसिद्ध्यति॥
en: Goat, horse, and Kshatriya, were created by Brahman for the same purpose (of being useful to everybody). A Kshatriya, therefore, should always seek the happiness of all creatures.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: यस्त्ववध्यवधे दोषः स वध्यस्यावधे स्मृतः। या चैव खलु मर्यादा यामयं परिवर्जयेत्॥
en: The sin of killing a person unworthy of being killed is tantamount to that which is incurred by not killing one who deserves to be killed. Such is the established order of things which a weak-minded king never thinks of attending to.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: तस्मात् तीक्ष्णः प्रजा राजा स्वधर्मे स्थापयेत् ततः। अन्योन्यं भक्षयन्तो हि प्रचरेयुर्वृका इव॥
en: Therefore, a king should force all his subjects to observe their respective duties. If this is not done, they will prowl like wolves, devouring one another,

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: यस्य दस्युगणा राष्ट्र ध्वांक्षा मत्स्यान् जलादिव। विहरन्ति परस्वानि स वै क्षत्रियपासनः॥
en: He is a wretch among Kshatriyas in whose kingdom robbers go about pillaging the property of other people like crows taking little fishes from water.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: कुलीनान् सचिवान् कृत्वा वेदविद्यासमन्वितान्। प्रशाधि पृथिवीं राजन् प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन्॥
en: Appointing high-born men with Vedic knowledge as your ministers, do you govern the Earth, protecting your subjects piously.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: विहीनं कर्मणान्यायं यः प्रगृह्णाति भूमिपः। उपायस्याविशेषज्ञं तद् वै क्षत्रं नपुंसकम्॥
en: That Kshatriya who, innocent of the established customs and contrivances, improperly taxes his people, is considered as a eunuch of his order.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: नैवोग्रं नैव चानुग्रं धर्मेणेह प्रशस्यते। उभयं न व्यतिक्रामेदुग्रो भूत्वा मृदुर्भव॥
en: A king should neither be severe nor mild. If he rules fairly he deserves praise. A king should not renounce both that qualities; on the other hand, becoming severe when (it is necessary), he should be mild when it is necessary to be so.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: कष्टः क्षत्रियधर्मोऽयं सौहृदं त्वयि मे स्थितम्। उग्रकर्मणि सृष्टोऽसि तस्माद् राज्यं प्रशाधि वै॥
en: The observance of Kshatriya duties is highly difficult. I love you greatly. You are created for the performance of severe acts. Therefore, do you rule kingdom.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: अशिष्टनिग्रहो नित्यं शिष्टस्य परिपालनम्। एवं शुक्रोऽब्रवीद् धीमानापत्सु भरतर्षभ।॥
en: The highly intelligent Shakra has said that in times of distress the great duty of a king is to punish the wicked and protect the good.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अस्ति चेदिह मर्यादा यामन्यो नाभिलवयेत्। पृच्छामि त्वां सतां श्रेष्ठ तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Is there any such rule (regarding royal duties) which should, under no circumstances) be violated? I ask you this, O foremost of virtuous persons! Tell me, O grandfather.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: भीष्म उवाच ब्राह्मणानेव सेवेत विद्यावृद्धास्तपस्विनः। श्रुतचारित्रवृत्ताढ्यान् पवित्रं ह्येतदुत्तमम्॥
en: Bhishma said One should always adore Brahmanas respected for learning, devoted to penances, and observant of Vedic injunctions. This, indeed, is a high and sacred duty.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: या देवतासु वृत्तिस्ते सास्तु विप्रेषु नित्यदा। क्रुद्धैर्हि विप्रैः कर्माणि कृतानि बहुधा नृप॥
en: You should always treat the Brahmanas like the gods. The Brahmanas, if enraged, can inflict pains in a variety of ways, O King.

description: The means by which kings should collect wisdom
sn: प्रीत्या यशो भवेन्मुख्यमप्रीत्या परमं भयम्। प्रीत्या ह्यमृतवद् विप्राः क्रुद्धाश्चैव विषं यथा।॥
en: If they be pleased, you will win high fame. If otherwise, great will be your fear. If pleased, the Brahmanas become like ambrosia. If enraged, they become like poison.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामह महाप्राज्ञ सर्वषास्त्रविशारद। शरणं पालयानस्य यो धर्मस्तं वदस्व मे।।।
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O you of great wisdom, O you who are a master of scriptures, tell me what the merit is of one who supports a person seeking his protection.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: भीष्म उवाच महान् धर्मो महाराज शरणागतपालने। अर्हः प्रष्टुं भवांश्चैव प्रश्नं भरतसत्तम॥
en: Bhishma said Great is the merit, O king, in supporting a suppliant. It is worthy of you, O best of the Bharatas, to ask such a question.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: शिबिप्रभृतयो राजन् राजानः शरणागतान्। परिपाल्य महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः॥
en: Those great kings of yore, viz., Shivi and others, o king, acquired supreme heavenly bliss by having supported suppliants.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: श्रूयते च कपोतेन शत्रुः शरणमागतः। पूजितश्च यथान्यायं स्वैश्च मांसैर्निमन्त्रितः॥
en: We have heard that a pigeon received reverentially a suppliant enemy according to due rites and even fed him with his own flesh.'

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं कपोतेन पुरा शत्रुः शरणमागतः। स्वमांसं भोजितः कां च गति लेभे स भारत॥
en: Yudhishthira said How, indeed, did a pigeon in days of yore feed a suppliant enemy with his own flesh? What end, O Bharata, did he win by such conduct.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु राजन् कथां दिव्यां सर्वपापप्रणाशिनीम्। नृपतेर्मुचुकुन्दस्य कथितां भार्गवेण वै॥
en: Listen, O king, to this most Beautiful story which cleanses the hearer of every sin, and which Bhrigu's son (Rama) had recited to king Muchukunda.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: पार्थ मुचुकुन्दो नराधिपः। भार्गवं परिपप्रच्छ प्रणतः पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: This very question, O son of Pritha, had been put humbly to Bhrigu's son by Muchukunda.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: इममर्थं पुरा तस्मै शुश्रूषमाणाय भार्गवोऽकथयत् कथाम्। इमां यथा कपोतेन सिद्धिः प्राप्ता नराधिप॥
en: The son of Bhrigu described this story to him of how a pigeon, O king, won success.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: मुनिरुवाच धर्मनिश्चयसंयुक्तां कामार्थसहितां कथाम्। शृणुष्वावहितो राजन् गदतो मे महाभुज॥
en: The sage said O mighty-armed king, listen to me as I describe to you this story containing lessons of Virtue, profit, and Desire.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: कश्चित् क्षुद्रसमाचारः पृथिव्यां कालसम्मितः। विचचार महारण्ये घोरः शकुनिलुब्धकः॥
en: A wicked and dreadful fowler, resembling the Destroyer himself, used in days of yore to wander through the great wilderness.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: काकोल इव कृष्णाङ्गो रक्ताक्षः कालसम्मितः। दीर्घजको ह्रस्वपादो महावक्त्रो महाहनुः॥
en: He was black as a raven and his eyes were blood red. He looked like Yama himself. He had long legs, short feet, large mouth, and protruding cheeks.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: नैव तस्य सुहृत् कश्चिन्न सम्बन्धी न बान्धवाः। स हि तैः सम्परित्यक्तस्तेन रौद्रेण कर्मणा॥
en: He had no friend, no relative, no kinsman. He had been discarded by them all for the exceedingly cruel life he led.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: नरः पापसमाचारस्त्यक्तव्यो दूरतो बुधैः। आत्मानं योऽभिसंधत्ते सोऽन्यस्य स्यात् कथं हितः।।१३।
en: Indeed, a wicked man should be shunned from a distance by the wise, for he who injures his ownself cannot be expected to do others good.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: ये नृशंसा दुरात्मानः प्राणिप्राणहरा नराः। उद्वेजनीया भूतानां व्याला इव भवन्ति ते॥
en: Those cruel and wicked men who destroy the lives of other creatures are always like venomous snakes, a source of trouble to all creatures.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: वै क्षारकमादाय द्विजान् हत्वा वने सदा। चकार विक्रयं तेषां पतङ्गानां जनाधिप॥
en: Taking his nets with him, and killing birds in the forests, he used to sell the meat, О king.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: एवं तु वर्तमानस्य तस्य वृत्तिं दुरात्मनः। अगमत् सुमहान् कालो न चाधर्ममबुध्यत॥
en: Thus working, the wicked wretch lived for many long years without ever understanding the sinfulness of his life.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: तस्य भार्यासहायस्य रममाणस्य शाश्वतम्। दैवयोगविमूढस्य नान्या वृत्तिररोचत॥
en: He was in the habit of sporting with his wife in the forest for many long years in the pursuit of this profession, and stupefied by destiny, he liked no other profession.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: ततः कदाचित् तस्थाय वनस्थस्य समन्ततः। पातयन्निव वृक्षांस्तान् सुमहान् वातसम्भ्रमः॥
en: One day as he was wandering through the forest carrying on his business a great storm took place that shook the trees, almost uprooting them.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: मेघसंकुलमाकाशं विद्युन्मण्डलमण्डितम्। संछन्नस्तु मुहूर्तेन नौसाथैरिव सागरः॥
en: In a moment dense masses of clouds set in the sky, accompanied with lightning and presenting the view of a sea covered with merchant boats and vessels.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: वारिधारासमूहेन सम्प्रविष्टः शतक्रतुः। क्षणेन पूरयामास सलिलेन वसुन्धराम्॥
en: The god of a hundred sacrifices having entered the clouds with a profuse supply of rain, the Earth became flooded with water in a moment.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: ततो धाराकुले काले सम्भ्रमन् नष्टचेतनः। शीतार्तस्तद् वनं सर्वमाकुलेनान्तरात्मना॥
en: While the rain fell in torrents, the flower lost his sense from fear. Trembling with cold and stricken with fear, he roamed through the forest.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: नैव निम्न स्थलं वापि सोऽविन्दत विहङ्गहा। पूरितो हि जलौघेन तस्य मार्गो वनस्य च॥
en: He could not find any elevated spot (which was not under water). The paths of the forest were all under water.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: पक्षिणो वर्षवेगेन हता लीनास्तदाभवन्। मृगसिंहवराहाच स्थलमाश्रित्य शेरते॥
en: For the force of the rain, many birds dropped down dead on the ground. Securing some elevated spots they had found, lions and bears and to her animals lay down to rest.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: महता वातवर्षेण त्रासितास्ते वनौकसः। भयार्ताश्च क्षुधार्ताश्च बभ्रमुः सहिता वने॥
en: All the dwellers of the forest were stricken with fear for that dreadful storm and rain. Terrified and hungry, they roved through the forest in small and large packs.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: स तु शीतहतैर्गात्रैर्न जगाम न तस्थिवान्। ददर्श पतितां भूमौ कपोती शीतविह्वलाम्॥
en: With limbs benumbed by cold, the fowler, however, could neither stop where he was, nor could he move. While in this state he saw shepigeon lying on the ground, benumbed with cold.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: दृष्ट्वाऽऽर्तोऽपि हि पापात्मा स तां पञ्जरकेऽक्षिपत्। स्वयं दुःखाभिभूतोऽपि दुःखमेवाकरोत् परे॥ पापात्मा पापकारित्वात् पापमेव चकार सः।
en: Beholding the birds, the sinful person, though he himself himself was in better circumstances, picked her up and put her in a cage. Himself afflicted with distress, he did not hesitate to overwhelm a fellow-creature with painful affliction.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: सोऽपश्यत् तरुखण्डेषु मेघनीलवनस्पतिम्॥ सेव्यमानं विहङ्गौघैश्छायावासफलार्थिभिः।
en: Indeed, through force of habit alone, the wretch committed that sin even at such a time. He then saw in midst of that wood a huge tree blue as the clouds. no

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: धात्रा परोपकाराय स साधुरिव निर्मितः॥ अथाभवत् क्षणेनैव वियद् विमलतारकम्।
en: It was the refuge of numberless birds seeking shade and shelter, as if it were placed there by the Creator for the behoof of all creatures like a good man in the world.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: महत्सर इवोत्फुल्लं कुमुदच्छरितोदकम्॥ ताराढ्यं कुमुदाकारमाकाशं निर्मलं बहु।
en: Soon the sky cleared and became spangled with myriads of stars appearing like a splendid lake smiling with blooming lilies.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: घनैर्मुक्तं नभो दृष्ट्वा लुब्धकः शीतविह्वलः॥ दिशो विलोकयामास विगाढां प्रेक्ष्य शर्वरीम्।
en: Looking at the clear sky, rich with stars, the fowler began to advance, still trembling with cold. Seeing the sky cleared of clouds, he looked around and finding that he had already been benighted, he began to think.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: दूरतो मे निवेशश्च अस्माद् देशादिति प्रभो॥ कृतबुद्धिर्द्धमे तस्मिन् वस्तुं तां रजनी ततः।
en: My house is at a great distance from where I am!-He then thought of passing the night under the shade of that tree.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: साञ्जलिः प्रणतिं कृत्वा वाक्यमाह वनस्पतिम्॥ शरणं यामि यान्यस्मिन् दैवतानि वनस्पतौ।
en: Bowing down to it with clasped hands, he addressed that king of the forest, saying,-I seek refuge with all the gods who have this tree for their resting place.

description: The merit of a person who supports a beseeching men
sn: स शिलायां शिरः कृत्वा पर्णान्यास्तीर्य भूतले। दुःखेन महताऽऽविश्स्ततः सुष्वाप पक्षिहा॥
en: Having said so, he spread some leaves for a bed, and laid himself down on it, placing his head on a stone. In spite of his being overwhelmed with affliction, the man soon fell asleep.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच अथ वृक्षस्य शाखायां विहङ्गः ससुहज्जनः। दीर्घकालोषितो राजंस्तत्र चित्रतनूरुहः॥
en: In one of the branches of that tree, a pigeon having beautiful feather, o king, lived for many years with his family.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: तस्य कल्पगता भार्या चरितुं नाभ्यवर्तत। प्राप्तां च रजनीं दृष्ट्वा स पक्षी पर्यतप्यत॥
en: That morning his wife had gone out in quest of food but had not yet come back. Seeing the approach of night and his wife still not returning, the bird began be bewail, saying

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: वातवर्ष महच्चासीन्न चागच्छति मे प्रिया। किं नु तत् कारणं येन साद्यापि न निवर्तते॥
en: O, what a great storm and a terrible shower took place to-day! Alas, you have come not come back yet, O dear wife! Woe is on me, what must be the cause of her not returning yet.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: अपि स्वस्ति भवेत् तस्याः प्रियाया मम कानने। तया विरहितं हीदं शून्यमद्य गृहं मम॥
en: In cverything right with that dear wife of mine in the forest? Separated from her, this my home appears to me void.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: पुत्रपौत्रवधूभृत्यैराकीर्णमपि सर्वतः। भार्याहीनं गृहस्थस्य शून्यमेव गृहं भवेत्॥
en: A house-holder's home, even if filled with sons, grandsons daughters-in-law and servants, is regarded empty if there is no housewife.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: न गृहं गृहमित्याहुहिणी गृहमुच्यते। गृहं तु गृहिणीहीनमरण्यसदृशं मतम्॥
en: One's house is not his home; one's wife only is his home. a house without the wife is desolate like a forest.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: यदि सा रक्तनेत्रान्ता चित्राङ्गी मधुरस्वरा। अद्य नायाति मे कान्ता न कार्यं जीवितेन मे॥
en: If that dear wife of mine, having red eyes, variegated plumes, and sweet voice, does not return to-day, my life itself will have no value.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: न भुक्के मय्यभुक्ते या नास्नाते स्नाति सुव्रता। नातिष्ठत्युपतिष्ठेत शेते च शयिते मयि॥
en: Practising most excellent vows, she never eats before I eat, and never bathes before I bathe. She never sits before I sit down, and never lies before I lie down.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: हृष्टे भवति सा हृष्टा दुःखिते मयि दुःखिता। प्रोषिते दीनवदना क्रुद्धे च प्रियवादिनी॥
en: She rejoices when I rejoice, and becomes sorry when I am sorry. She is cheerless when I am away, and she is all sweetness when I am angry.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: पतिव्रता पतिगतिः पतिप्रियहिते रता। यस्य स्यात् तादृशी भार्या धन्यः स पुरुषो भुवि।।१०।
en: Always devoted to her husband and ever relying upon him, she always did what was agreeable to and beneficial for her lord. Indeed, such a person deserves praise on Earth who has such a wife.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: सा हि श्रान्तं क्षुधार्तं च जानीते मां तपस्विनी। अनुरक्ता स्थिरा चैव भक्ता स्निग्धा यशस्विनी॥
en: That amiable creature knows that I am worn out and hungry. Devoted to me and firm in her love, my genial wife is devout in her adoration to me.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: वृक्षमूलेऽपि दयिता यस्य तिष्ठति तद् गृहम्। प्रासादोऽपि तया हीनः कान्तार इति निश्चितम्॥
en: Even the food of a tree is one's home, if he lived there with his wife as a companion. Without one's wife, even a palace is a desolate forest.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: धर्मार्थकामकालेषु भार्या पुंसः सहायिनी। विदेशगमने चास्य सैव विश्वासकारिका॥
en: One's wife is his companion in all his acts of virtue, profit and desire. When one starts for a strange country his wife is his trusted companion.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: भार्या हि परमो ह्यर्थः पुरुषस्येह पठ्यते। असहायस्य लोकेऽस्मिल्लोकयात्रासहायिनी॥
en: It is said that the wife is the richest treasure of her husband. In this world the wife is the only companion of her husband in all the worldly affairs.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: तथा रोगाभिभूतस्य नित्यं कृच्छ्रगतस्य च। नास्ति भार्यासमं किंचिन्नरस्यार्तस्य भेषजम्॥
en: One, who is suffered from disease and surrounded with many troubles, his wife is the best of panaceas and good medicine in sickness of that person.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: नास्ति भार्यासमो बन्धुर्नास्ति भार्यासमा गतिः। नास्ति भार्यासमो लोके सहायो धर्मसंग्रह॥
en: There is no friend like wife. There is no refuge better than the wife. There is no better associate in the world than the wife in acts undertaken for the acquisition of religious merit.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: यस्य भार्या गृहे नास्ति साध्वी च प्रियवादिनी। अरण्यं तेन गन्तव्यं यथारण्यं तथा गृहम्॥
en: He who has not in his house a wife, chaste and of sweet speech, should go to the forest. For such a one there is no difference between a home and a forest.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवं विलपतस्तस्य श्रुत्वा तु करुणं वचः। गृहीता शकुनिभेन कपोती वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these piteous cries of the pigeon on the tree, the she-pigeon caught by the fowler began to say aside thus.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: अहोऽतीव सुभाग्याहं यस्या मे दयितः पतिः। असतो वा सतो वापि गुणानेवं प्रभाषते॥
en: Whether I have any inerit or not, indeed, there is no limit to my good fortune when my dear husband thus speaks of me.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: न सा स्त्री ह्यभिमन्तव्या यस्यां भर्ता न तुष्यति। तुष्टे भर्तरि नारीणां तुष्टाः स्युः सर्वदेवताः॥ अग्निसाक्षिकमित्येव भर्ता वै दैवतं परम्।
en: She is no wife with whom her husband is not pleased. If their husbands are pleased with women all the gods also become pleased with them. Since the marriage union takes place in the presence of fire, the husband is the wife's greatest god.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: दावाग्निनेव निर्दग्धा सपुष्पस्तवका लता॥ भस्मीभवति सा नारी यस्या भर्ता न तुष्यति।
en: That wife with whom her husband is not pleased is reduced to ashes, like a creeper adorned with flowers in a forest fire.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: इति संचिन्त्य दुःखार्ता भर्तारं दुःखितं तदा॥ कपोती लुब्धकेनापि गृहीता वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
en: Having thought thus, the she-pigeon, stricken with woe, and encaged by the fowler, thus spoke to her woe-stricken husband.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: हन्त वक्ष्यामि ते श्रेयः श्रुत्वा तु कुरु तत् तथा॥ शरणागतसंत्राता भव कान्त विशेषतः।
en: I shall say what is now good for you. Hearing me follow my advice, O dear husband, be you the rescuer of a suppliant.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: एष शाकुनिकः शेते तव वासं समाश्रितः॥ शीतार्तश्च क्षुधार्तश्च पूजामस्मै समाचर।
en: This fowler lies here by your house stricken with cold and hunger. Treat him hospitably.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: ये हि कश्चिद् द्विजं हन्याद् गां च लोकस्य मातरम्।।८ शरणागतं च यो हन्यात् तुल्यं तेषां च पातकम्।
en: The sin that a person commits by killing a Brahmana or that mother of the world, viz., a cow, is equal to what one commits by allowing suppliant to die.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: अस्माकं विहिता वृत्तिः कापोती जातिधर्मतः॥ सान्याय्याऽत्मवता नित्यं त्वद्विधेनानुवर्तितुम्।
en: You are endued with the knowledge of self. You should, therefore, follow that course which has been ordained for us as pigeons on account of our birth.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: यस्तु धर्मं यथाशक्ति गृहस्थो ह्यनुवर्तते॥ स प्रेत्य लभते लोकानक्षयानिति शुश्रुम।
en: We have heard that the house-holder who practises virtue according to his abilities, acquires hereafter endless regions of bliss.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: स त्वं संतानवानद्य पुत्रवानसि च द्विज॥ तत् स्वदेहे दयां त्यक्त्वा धर्मार्थी परिगृह्य च। पूजामस्मै प्रयुक्ष्व त्वं प्रीयेतास्य मनो यथा।॥
en: You have sons. You have progeny. O bird, casting off all love for your own body, therefore, and for acquiring virtue and profit, adore this fowler so that he may be pleased.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: मत्कृते मा च संतापं कुर्वीथास्त्वं विहङ्गम। शरीरयात्राकृत्यर्थमन्यान् दारानुपैष्यसि॥
en: Do not, O bird, grieve for me. You may live, marrying other wives.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: इति सा शकुनी वाक्यं पञ्जरस्था तपस्विनी। अतिदुःखान्विता प्रोक्त्वा भर्तारं समुदैक्षत॥
en: The amiable she-pigeon, laden with sorrow, and casting her eyes upon her husband from the fowler's cage within which she had been put, said these words to him.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच स पल्या वचनं श्रुत्वा धर्मयुक्तिसमन्वितम्। हर्षेण महता युक्तो वाक्यं व्याकुललोचनः॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words of morality and reason spoken by his wife, the pigeon was filled with great delight and his eyes were bathed in tears of joy.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: तं वै शाकुनिकं दृष्ट्वा विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा। स पक्षी पूजयामास यत्नात् तं पक्षिजीविनम्॥
en: Seeing that fowler whose profession was to kill birds, the pigeon honoured him scrupulously according to scriptural rites.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: उवाच स्वागतं तेऽद्य ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते। संतापश्च न कर्तव्यः स्वगृहे वर्तते भवान्॥
en: Addressing him, he said,-You are welcome to-day. Tell me what I shall do for you. You should not repent. This is your home.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: तद् ब्रवीतु भवान् क्षिप्रं किं करोमि किमिच्छसि। प्रणयेन ब्रवीमि त्वां त्वं हि नः शरणागतः॥
en: Tell me quickly what I am to do and what is your pleasure. I ask you this in good spirit, for you have sought protection of us.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: अरावप्युचितं कार्यमातिथ्यं गृहमागते। छेत्तुमप्यागते छायां नोपसंहरते दुमः॥
en: Hospitality should be shown to even one's enemy when the latter comes to his house. The tree does not withdraw its shade from even the person who comes for cutting it down.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: शरणागतस्य कर्तव्यमातिथ्यं हि प्रयत्नतः। पञ्चयज्ञप्रवृत्तेन गृहस्थेन विशेषतः॥
en: One should, with diligence do the duties of hospitality towards a person who seeks shelter. Indeed, one is particularly bound to do so if he leads the life of a house-holder that consists of the five sacrifices.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: पञ्चयज्ञांस्तु यो मोहान्न करोति गृहाश्रमे। तस्य नायं न च परो लोको भवति धर्मतः॥
en: If one, while living like a house-holder, does, not from want of judgement, celebrate the five sacrifices, one loses, as laid down in the scriptures, both this and the next world.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: तद् ब्रूहि मां सुविश्रब्धो यत् त्वं वाचा वदिष्यसि! तत् करिष्याम्यहं सर्वं मा त्वं शोके मनः कृथाः॥
en: Tell me then clearly and confidently what your wishes are. I will accomplish them all. Do not think of grieving.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा शकुनेर्लुब्धकोऽब्रवीत्। वाधते खलु मे शीतं संत्राणं हि विधीयताम्॥
en: Hearing these words of the bird, the fowler replied to him, saying,-I am benumbed with cold. Just make arrangements for warming me.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: एवमुक्तस्तत: पक्षी पर्णान्यास्तीर्य भूतले। यथाशक्त्या हि पर्णेन ज्वलनार्थं दुतं ययौ॥
en: Thus addressed, the bird collected a number of dry leaves on the ground, and taking a leaf in his beaks quickly went away for fetching fire.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: स गत्वाङ्गारकर्मान्तं गृहीत्वाग्निमथागतम्। स संदीप्तं महत् कृत्वा तमाह शरणागतम्। प्रतापय सुविश्रब्धः स्वगात्राण्यकुतोभयः॥ ततः शुष्केषु पर्णेषु पावकं सोऽप्यदीपयत्॥
en: Going where fire is kept, he got a little fire and returned. He then set fire to those dry leaves, and when they blazed up into a powerful fire, he said to his guest, Do you with confidence and fearlessness warm your limbs.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: स तथोक्त स्तथेत्युक्त्वा लुब्धो गात्राण्यतापयत्। अग्निं प्रत्यागतप्राणस्ततः प्राह विहङ्गमम्॥ हर्षेण महताऽऽविष्टो वाक्यं व्याकुललोचनः। तथेमं शकुनिं दृष्ट्वा विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥ दत्तमाहारमिच्छामि त्वया क्षुद् बाधते हि माम्। स तद्वचः प्रतिश्रुत्य वाक्यमाह विहङ्गमः॥ न मेऽस्ति विभवो येन नाशयेयं क्षुधां तव। उत्पन्नेन हि जीवामो वयं नित्यं वनौकसः॥
en: Thus addressed, the fowler said-So be it:-and began to warm his stiffened limbs. Regaining as if his life, the fowler said to his host,-Hunger is distressing me. I wish you to give me some food! — Hearing his words the bird said,-I have nothing in store by which you may satisfy your hunger. We, dwellers of the forest, always live upon what we get every day.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: संचयो नास्ति चास्माकं मुनीनामिव भोजने। इत्युक्त्वा तं तदा तत्र विवर्णवदनोऽभवत्॥
en: Like the ascetics of the forest we never amass for the morrow!-Having said so, the bird's face grew pale.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: कथं न खलु कर्तव्यमिति चिन्तापरस्तदा। बभूव भरतश्रेष्ठ गर्हयन् वृत्तिमात्मनः॥
en: He began to think aside as to what he should do and mentally blamed his own mode of living.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: मुहूर्ताल्लब्धसंज्ञस्तु स पक्षी पक्षिघातिनम्। उवाच तर्पयिष्ये त्वां मुहूर्त प्रतिपालय॥
en: Soon, however, his mind became clear. Addressing the destroyer of birds, he said,-I shall please you!-Wait for a moment!

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: इत्युक्त्वा शुष्कपर्णस्तु समुज्ज्वाल्य हुताशनम्। हर्षेण महताऽऽविष्टः स पक्षी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ऋषीणां देवतानां च पितृणां च महात्मनाम्। श्रुतः पूर्वं मया धर्मो महानतिथिपूजने॥
en: Saying these words he lighted up a fire with the help of some dry leaves, and filled with joy, said,-I heard formerly from great Rishis, gods and Pitris that there is great merit in honouring a guest.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: कुरुष्वानुग्रहं सौम्य सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते। निश्चिता खलु मे बुद्धिरतिथिप्रतिपूजने॥
en: O amiable one, be kind to me. To tell you the truth my heart is bent upon honouring you my guest.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: ततः कृतप्रतिज्ञो वै स पक्षी प्रहसनिव) तमग्निं त्रि:परिक्रम्य प्रविवेश महामतिः॥
en: Having thus made up his mind, the great bird, with a smiling face, thrice went round that fire and then entered its flames.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: अग्निमध्ये प्रविष्टं तु लुब्धो दृष्ट्वा तु पक्षिणम्। चिन्तयामास मनसा किमिदं वे मया कृतम्॥
en: Seeing the bird enter that fire, the fowler began to think! and asked himself,-What have I done.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: अहो मम नृशंसस्य गर्हितस्य स्वकर्मणा। अधर्मः सुमहान् घोरो भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: Alas, dreadful will be the sin, the outcome of my own acts. I am highly ruthless and blameable.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: एवं बहुविधं भूरि विललाप स लुब्धकः। गार्हयन् स्वानि कर्माणि द्विजं दृष्ट्वा तथागतम्॥
en: Indeed, seeing the bird lay down his life, the fowler, considering his own acts, began to bewail thus piteously.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: एवं बहुविधं भूरि विललाप स लुब्धकः। गार्हयन् स्वानि कर्माणि द्विजं दृष्ट्वा तथागतम्॥
en: Indeed, seeing the bird lay down his life, the fowler, considering his own acts, began to bewail thus piteously.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः स लुब्धकः पश्यन् क्षुधयापि परिप्लुतः। कपोतमग्निपतितं वाक्यं पुनरुवाच ह॥ किमीदृशं नृशंसेन मया कृतमबुद्धिना। भविष्यति हि मे नित्यं पातकं कृतजीविनः॥
en: Beholding the pigeon fall into the fire, the fowler filled with compassion once more said,-Alas, cruel and senseless that I am, what have I done! I am, forsooth, a mean wretch! Great will be my sin which will last for ever.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: स विनिन्दंस्तथाऽऽत्मानं पुनः पुनरुवाच ह। अविश्वास्यः सुदुर्बुद्धिः सदा निकृतिनिश्चयः॥
en: Thus censuring himself he began to say again and again,-I do not deserve any credit! My understanding is wicked! I am ever sinful!

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: शुभं कर्म परित्यज्य सोऽहं शकुनिलुब्धकः। नृशंसस्य ममाद्यायं प्रत्यादेशो न संशयः॥ दत्तः स्वमांसं दहता कपोतेन महात्मना।
en: Alas, renouncing all sorts of honourable occupation, I have become a fowler! A cruel wretch that I am, forsooth, this noble pigeon, by sacrificing his own life, has taught me a great lesson.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: सोऽहं त्यक्ष्ये प्रियान् प्राणान् पुत्रान् दारांस्तथैव च।।५। उपदिष्टे हि मे धर्मः कपोतेन महात्मना।
en: Renouncing wives and sons, I shall certainly cast off my very life which is so dear! The great pigeon has taught me that duty.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: अद्यप्रभृति देहं स्वं सर्वभोगैर्विवर्जितम्॥ यथा स्वल्पं सरो ग्रीष्मे शोषयिष्याम्यहं तथा।
en: From this day, denying every comfort to my body, I shall exhaust it like a shallow tank in summer.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: क्षुत्पिपासातपसहः कृशो धमनिसंततः॥ उपवासैर्बहुविधैश्चरिष्ये पारलौकिकम्।
en: Capable of bearing hunger, thirst, and penances, and being emaciated with veins visible all over, I shall by various sorts of fasts, practise such vows as will take me to the other world.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: अहो देहप्रदानेन दर्शितातिथिपूजना॥ तस्माद् धर्मं चरिष्यामि धर्मो हि परमा गतिः। दृष्टो धर्मो हि धर्मिष्ठे यादृशो विहगोत्तमे॥
en: Alas, by giving up his body the pigeon has shown how a guest should be adored! Taught by his example, I shall hereafter practise righteousness. Righteousness is the greatest refuge! Indeed, I shall practise the righteousness shown by the virtuous pigeon, that foremost of all winged creatures.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: एवमुक्त्वा विनिश्चित्य रौद्रकर्मा स लुब्धकः। महाप्रस्थानमाश्रित्य प्रययौ संशितव्रतः॥
en: Having thus made up his mind and said these words, that fowler, once of dreadful deeds, started on a journey never to end, observing all the while the most rigid vows.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: ततो यष्टिं शलाकां च क्षारकं पञ्जरं तथा। तां च बद्धा कपोती स प्रमुच्य विससर्ज ह॥
en: He threw away his strong staff, his sharp iron-stick, his nets and springes, and his iron cage, and liberated the she-pigeon that he had caught and imprisoned.'

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो गते शाकुनिके कपोती प्राह दुःखिता। संस्मृत्य सा च भर्तारं रुदतो शोककर्शिता।।।।
en: Bhishma said After the fowler had left there, the shepigeon, remembering her husband and stricken with grief for him, wept profusely and bewailed thus:नाहं ते विप्रियं कान्त कदाचिदपि संस्मरे।

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: सर्वापि विधवा नारी बहुपुत्रापि शोचते॥ शोच्या भवति बन्धूनां पतिहीना तपस्विनी।
en: I cannot, O dear husband, remember a single instance of your having done me an injury! Widows, even when they are mothers of many children, are still miserable! Bereft of husband, a woman becomes helpless and an object of pity to her friends.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: लालिताहं त्वया नित्यं बहुमानाच्च पूजिता॥ वचनैर्मधुरैः स्निग्धैरसंक्लिष्टमनोहरैः।
en: I was always supported by you and for the great respect you had for me I was always honoured by you with sweet, agreeable, charming, and delightful words.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: कन्दरेषु च शैलानां नदीनां निझरेषु च॥ दुमागेषु च रम्येषु रमिताहं त्वया सह।
en: I have sported with you in valleys of mountans, in springs of rivers and on charming trees.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: आकाशगमने चैव विहृताहं त्वया सुखम्॥ रमामि स्म पुरा कान्त तन्मे नास्त्यद्य किञ्चन।
en: I was also made happy by you while passing with you through the skies! I used to sport with you before, O dear husband, but where are those joys now.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: मितं ददाति हि पिता मितं भ्राता मितं सुतः॥ अमितस्य हि दातारं भर्तारं का न पूजयेत्।
en: The gifts of the father, of the brother, and of the son to a woman are but limited. But unlimited are the gifts that her husband alone makes to her! What woman is there that would not, therefore, worship her husband.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: नास्ति भर्तृसमो नाथो नास्ति भर्तृसमं सुखम्॥ विसृज्य धनसर्वस्वं भर्ता वै शरणं स्त्रियाः।
en: A word has no protector like her husband, and no happiness like her husband. Casting off all her riches and possessions, a woman should follow her husband as her only refuge.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: न कार्यमिह मे नाथ जीवितेन त्वया विना॥ पतिहीना तु का नारी सती जीवितुमुत्सहेत्।
en: Useless is life to me, O lord, now that I am separated from you! What chaste woman is there who would, when bereft of her husband, venture to bear the burden of life.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: एवं विलप्य बहुधा करुणं सा सुदुःखिता॥ पतिव्रता सम्प्रदीप्तं प्रविवेश हुताशनम्।
en: Filled with sorrow and bewailing thus, the she-pigeon, devoted to her husband cast herself on the burning fire.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: ततश्चित्राङ्गदधरं भर्तारं सान्वपश्यत॥ विमानस्थं सुकृतिभिः पूज्यमानं महात्मभिः।
en: She then saw her husband bedecked with bracelets, seated on a (celestial) car, and worshipped of many great and meritorious beings standing around him.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: चित्रमाल्याम्बरधरं सर्वाभरणभूषितम्॥ विमानशतकोटीभिरावृतं पुण्यकर्मभिः।
en: Indeed, there he was in the sky, decked with excellent garlands and clad in excellent robes, and adorned with every ornament. There were numberless celestial cars around him ridden by beings who had acted meritoriously while in this world.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject. 233
sn: ततः स्वर्गं गतः पक्षी विमानवरमास्थितः। कर्मणा पूजितस्तत्र रेमे स सह भार्यया॥
en: Seated on his own celestial car, the bird went to heaven, and getting proper honours for his deeds in this world, continued to sport in joy, accompanied by his spouse. Seated on his own celestial car, the bird went to heaven, and getting proper honours for his deeds in this world, continued to sport in joy, accompanied by his spouse.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच विमानस्थौ तु तौ राजंल्लुब्धकः खे ददर्श ह। दृष्ट्वा तौ दम्पती राजन् व्यचिन्तयत तां गतिम्॥
en: Bhishma said lt so chanced that the fowler, O king, saw that pair while seated on their celestial car. Seeing the couple he became filled with sorrow and began to think of the means of acquiring the same end.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: ईदृशेनैव तपसा गच्छेयं परमां गतिम्। इति बुद्ध्या विनिश्चित्य गमनायोपचक्रमे।॥
en: And he said to himself,-I must, by austerities like those of the pigeon, acquire such a high end!—Having made this resolution, the fowler, who had lived by the destruction of birds, started on an unreturning journey.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: महाप्रस्थानमाश्रित्य लुब्धकः पक्षिजीवकः। निश्चेष्टो मरुदाहारो निर्ममः स्वर्गकाझया॥
en: Without any attempt (for getting food) and living upon air alone, he renounced all other desires for acquiring heaven.
