description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: ततोऽपश्यत् सुविस्तीर्णं हृद्यं पद्माभिभूषितम्। नानापक्षिगणाकीर्णं सरः शीतजलं शिवम्॥
en: After he had gone for some distance, he saw an extensive and charming lake full of cool and pure water, adorned with lotuses and abounding with various sorts of water-fowi.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: पिपासार्तोऽपि तद् दृष्ट्वा तृप्त: स्यान्नात्र संशयः। उपवासकृशोऽत्यर्थं स तु पार्थिव लुब्धकः॥ अनवेक्ष्यैव संहृष्टः श्वापदाध्युषितं वनम्। महान्तं निश्चयं कृत्वा लुब्धकः प्रविवेश ह॥ प्रविशन्नेव स वनं निगृहीतः सकण्टकैः।
en: Forsooth, the very sight of such a lake is capable of satisfying the thirst of a person. Physically reduced with fasts, the fowler, however, O king, without casting his eyes upon it, gladly entered into a forest inhabited by beasts of prey, having previously learnt its wide extent. After he had entered the forest, he was painfully cut by sharp-pointed thorns.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: स कण्टकैर्विभिन्नाङ्गो लोहितार्दीकृतच्छविः॥ बभ्राम तस्मिन् विजने नानामृगसमाकुले।
en: Cut and torn by prickles, and bathed in blood, he began to wander in that forest, shorn of men but abounding with animals of various species.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: ततो दुमाणां महता पवनेन वने तदा॥ उदतिष्ठत संघर्षात् सुमहान् हव्यवाहनः।
en: Sometime after, on account of the friction of some huge trees caused by a strong wind, a wide spread forest-fire arose.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: तद् वनं वृक्षसम्पूर्ण लताविटपसंकुलम्॥ ददाह पावकः क्रुद्धो युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभः।
en: The raging element, appearing like the fire at the end of the Cycle, the powerful fire began to consume that large forest abounding with tall trees and thick bushes and creepers.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: स ज्वालैः पवनोदतैर्विस्फुलिङ्गैःसमन्ततः॥ ददाह तद् वनं घोरं मृगपक्षिसमाकुलम्।
en: Indeed, with flames fanned by the wind and numberless sparks flying about in all directions, the all-consuming god began to consume that dense forest teeming with birds and beasts.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: ततः स देहमोक्षार्थं सम्प्रहृष्टेन चेतसा॥ अभ्यधावत वर्धन्तं पावकं लुब्धकस्तदा।
en: The fowler, desirous of renouncing his body, ran with a delighted heart towards that spreading fire.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: ततस्तेनाग्निना दग्धो लुब्धको नष्टकल्मषः। जगाम परमां सिद्धिं ततो भरतसत्तम॥
en: Consumed by that fire the fowler became purged of all his sins and acquired, O best of the Bharatas, high success.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: ततः स्वर्गस्थमात्मानमपश्यद् विगतज्वरः। यक्षगन्धर्वसिद्धानां मध्ये भ्राजन्तमिन्द्रवत्॥
en: The anxiety of his mind gone, he at last saw himself in heaven, shining like Indra in midst of Yakshas and Gandharvas and persons endued with ascetic success.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: एवं खलु कपोतश्च कपोती च पतिव्रता। लुब्धकेन सह स्वर्गं गताः पुण्येन कर्मणा॥
en: Thus the pigeon and his devoted wife, with the fowler, went to heaven for their meritorious acts.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: यापि चैवंविधा नारी भर्तारमनुवर्तते। विराजते हि सा क्षिप्रं कपोतीव दिवि स्थिता॥
en: The woman who thus follows her husband speedily ascends to heaven and shines there like the she-pigeon of whom I have spoken.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: एवमेतत् पुरावृत्तं लुब्धकस्य महात्मनः। कपोतस्य च धर्मिष्ठा गतिः पुण्येन कर्मणा॥
en: This is the ancient history of the great fowler and the pigeon. Thus did they acquire highly meritorious end by their righteous acts.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: यश्चेदं शृणुयान्नित्यं यश्चेदं परिकीर्तयेत्। नाशुभं विद्यते तस्य मनसापि प्रमादतः॥
en: No evil overtakes the person who listens every day to this story or who recites it every day, even if error possesses his mind.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: युधिष्ठिर महानेष धर्मो धर्मभृतां वर। गोनेष्वपि भवेदस्मिनिष्कृतिः पापकर्मणः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, O foremost of all righteous persons, the protection of a suppliant is, indeed, a great act of merit. By following this duty, even the killer of a cow may be cleansed of sin.

description: The story of a pigeon on the subject
sn: न निष्कृतिर्भवेत् तस्य यो हन्याच्छरणागतम्। इतिहासमिमं श्रुत्वा पुण्यं पापप्रणाशनम्। न दुर्गतिमवाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति॥
en: That man, however, will never be cleansed who kills a suppliant. By listening to this sacred and sin-destroying story one becomes freed from distress and goes to heaven at last.'

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अबुद्धिपूर्वं यत् पापं कुर्याद् भरतसत्तम। मुच्यते स कथं तस्मादेतत् सर्वं वदस्व मे॥
en: Yudhishthira said O best of the Bharatas, when a person commits sin from want of discrimination, how may he be purified by it? Tell me all about it.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि पुराणमृषिसंस्तुतम्। इन्द्रोत: शौनको विप्रो यदाह जनमेजयम्॥
en: Bhishma said In this connection I shall recite to you the old narrative, spoken highly of by the Rishis, of what the twice-born Indrota, the son of Shunaka, said to Janamejaya.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: आसीद् राजा महावीर्यः परिक्षिज्जनमेजयः। अबुद्धिपूर्वामागच्छद् ब्रह्महत्यां महीपतिः॥
en: There was, in days of old, a highly energetic king, called Janamejaya, who was the son of Parikshit. On one occasion from want of discrimination, that king became guilty of Brahmanicide.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: ब्राह्मणाः सर्व एवैते तत्यजुः सपुरोहिताः। स जगाम वनं राजा दह्यमानो दिवानिशम्॥
en: Upon this, all the Brahmanas together with his priests cast him off. Burning day and night with grief, the king retired into the forest.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: प्रजाभिः स परित्यक्तश्चकार कुशलं महत्। अतिवेलं तपस्तेपे दह्यमानः स मन्युना॥
en: Deserted by his subjects too, he adopted this course for acquiring great merit. Reduced by repentance, the king practised the most rigid austerities.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: ब्रह्महत्यापनोदार्थमपृच्छद् ब्राह्मणान् बहून्। पर्यटन् पृथिवीं कृत्स्ना देशे देशे नराधिपः॥
en: For purifying himself of the sin of Brahmanicide he asked many Brahmanas, and travelled from one country to another over the whole Earth.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: तत्रेतिहासं वक्ष्यामि धर्मस्यास्योपबृंहणम्। दह्यमानः पापकृत्या जगाम जनमेजयः॥
en: I shall now tell you the story of his expiation. Burning with the recollection of his sin, Janamejaya wandered about.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: चरिष्यमाण इन्द्रोतं शौनकं संशितव्रतम्। समासाद्योपजग्राह पादयोः परिपीडयन्॥
en: One day, in course of his peregrinations, he met Indrota, the son of Shunaka, of rigid vows, and approaching him touched his feet.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: ऋषिर्दृष्ट्वा नृपं तत्र जगहें सुभृशं तदा। कर्ता पापस्य महतो भ्रूणहा किमिहागतः॥
en: Seeing the king before him, the sage reproved him, saying,-You have committed a great sin. You have been guilty of foeticide. Why have you come here.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: किं त्वयास्मासु कर्तामा मां स्प्राक्षीः कथंचन। गच्छ गच्छ न ते स्थानं प्रीणात्यस्मानिति ब्रुवन्॥
en: What have you to do with us? Do not touch me! Go, go away! Your presence does not give us pleasure!

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: रुधिरस्येव ते गन्धः शवस्येव च दर्शनम्। अशिवः शिवसंकाशो मृतो जीवन्निवाटसि॥
en: Your body smells like blood. You look like a corpse. Though impure, you appear as pure, and though dead you move like a living being!

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: ब्रह्ममृत्युरशुद्धात्मा पापमेवानुचिन्तयन्। प्रबुद्ध्यसे प्रस्वपिषि वर्तसे परमे सुखे॥
en: Dead within, you are of impure soul for you always wish to commit sin. Though you sleep, and wake, your life, however, is spent in great misery.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: मोघं ते जीवितं राजन् परिक्लिष्टं च जीवसि। पापायैव हि सृष्टोऽसि कर्मणे हि यवीयसे॥
en: Useless is your life, O king. You live most miserably. You have been created for ignoble and sinful acts.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: बहुकल्याणमिच्छन्ति ईहन्ते पितरः सुतान्। तपसा दैवतेज्याभिर्वन्दनेन तितिक्षया॥
en: Fathers wish for sons for obtaining various kinds of blessings, and hoping they would perform penances and sacrifices, adore the gods, and practise renunciation.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: पितृवंशमिमं पश्य त्वत्कृते नरकं गतम्। निरर्थाः सर्व एवैषामाशाबन्धास्त्वदाश्रयाः॥
en: See all your ancestors have fallen into hell for your acts. All the hopes your fathers had placed upon you have been frustrated,

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: यान् पूजयन्तो विन्दन्ति स्वर्गमायुर्यशः प्रजाः। तेषु त्वं सततं द्वेष्टा ब्राह्मणेषु निरर्थकः॥
en: You live in vain, for you, always entertain hatred and malice towards the Brahmanas,-by worshipping whom other men acquire long life, fame, and heaven.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: इमं लोकं विमुच्य त्वमवाङ्मूर्द्धा पतिष्यसि। अशाश्वतीः शाश्वतीश्च समाः पापेन कर्मणा॥
en: Leaving this world, you shall have to fall (into hell) with head downwards and remain in that posture for numberless years for your sinful deeds.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: अर्धमानो यत्र गृधैः शितिकण्ठैरयोमुखैः। ततश्च पुनरावृत्तः पापयोनि गमिष्यसि॥
en: There you will be tortured by vultures and peacocks having iron beaks. Returning thence into this world, you will be born again in a wretched order of creatures.

description: The purification of a person who commits sin from want of discrimination
sn: यदिदं मन्यसे राजन् नायमस्ति कुतः परः। प्रतिस्मारयितारस्त्वां यमदूता यमक्षये॥
en: If you think, o king, that this world is nothing and that the next world is nothing and that the next world is but a shadow, the attendants of Yama in the infernal regions will convince you, removing your scepticism.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच तं मुनि जनमेजयः। गीं भवान् गर्हयते निन्द्यं निन्दति मां पुनः॥
en: Thus accusted, Janamejaya replied to the sage, saying,-You chastise one who deserves to be chastised. You censure one who is worthy of being censured.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: धिक्कार्यं मां धिक्कुरुते तस्मात् त्वाहं प्रसादये। सर्वं हीदं दुष्कृतं मे ज्वलाम्यग्नाविवाहितः॥
en: You blame me and my acts. I beg you to be kind to me! All my acts have been sinful. I burn, however, with repentance as if I am in the midst of burning fire.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: स्वकर्माण्यभिसंधाय नाभिनन्दति मे मनः। प्राप्यं घोरं भयं नूनं मया वैवस्वतादपि॥
en: Remembering my deeds, I am cheerless. Indeed, I am much afraid of Yama.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: तत्तु शल्यमनिर्हत्य कथं शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्। सर्वं मन्यु विनीय त्वमभि मां वद शौनक॥
en: How can I live without taking out that dart from my heart! O Shaunaka, suppressing all your anger, instruct me now!

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: महानासं ब्राह्मणानां भूयो वक्ष्यामि साम्प्रतम्। अस्तु शेषं कुलस्यास्य मा पराभूदिदं कुलम्॥
en: Formerly I used to show a great reverence to Brahmanas. I solemnly say that I shall once more show.the same respect to them. Let not my family be extinct. Let not the family in which I am born be reduced to the dust.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: न हि नो ब्रह्मशप्तानां शेषं भवितुमर्हति। स्तुतीरलभमानानां संविदं वेदनिश्चितान्॥
en: It is not proper that they who have injured Brahmanas and have for that, on account of Védic injunctions, forfeited all claim to the I arn respect of the world and to social intercourse with their fellowmen, should have any one who will continue the name of their family.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: निर्विद्यमानः सुभृशं भूयो वक्ष्यामि शाश्वतम्। भूयश्चैवाभिरक्षन्तु निर्धनान् निर्जना इव॥
en: I am overwhelmed with despair. I, therefore, repeat my promises. I pray you to protect me like sages who always protect the poor.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: न ह्ययज्ञा अमुं लोकं प्राप्नुवन्ति कथञ्चन। आपातान् प्रतितिष्ठन्ति पुलिन्दशबरा इव॥
en: Abstaining from sacrifices, sinful persons never attain to heaven. Leaving (this world), they have to pass their time in hell like the degraded tribes of Pulindas and Khasas.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: अविज्ञायैव मे प्रज्ञा बालस्येव स पण्डितः। पुत्रस्य प्रीतिमान् भव शौनक॥
en: Ignorant as I am, give me wisdom like a learned preceptor to his pupil or like a father to his son. Be pleased with ine, O Shaunaka!

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: शौनक उवाच किमाश्चर्यं यदप्राज्ञो बहु कुर्यादसाम्प्रतम्। इति वै पण्डितो भूत्वा भूतानां नानुकुप्यते॥ ब्रह्मन् पितेव
en: Shaunaka said What wonder is there that an ignorant wight should do many improper acts? Knowing this, a really wise person is never angry with foolish creatures.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: प्रज्ञाप्रासादमारुह्य अशोच्यः शोचते जनान्। जगतीस्थानिवांद्रिस्थः प्रज्ञया प्रतिपत्स्यति॥
en: By getting upon the top of wisdom's palace, one grieves for others, his own self being then too pure to be grieved by others. For his wisdom one surveys all creatures in the world like a person on a mountain-top seeing people below.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: न चोपलभ्यते तेन न चाश्चर्याणि कुर्वते। निविण्णात्मा परोक्षो वा धिक्कृतः पूर्वसाधुषु॥
en: The person who is censured by good men, who hates good men and who hides himself from their view, never acquires any blessing and never understands the fitness of acts.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: विदितं भवतो वीर्यं माहात्म्यं वेद आगमे। कुरुष्वेह यथाशान्ति ब्रह्मा शरणमस्तु ते॥ तद् वै पारत्रिकं तात ब्राह्मणानामकुप्यताम्। अथवा तप्यसे पापे धर्ममेवानुपश्य वै॥
en: You know the energy and the nobility of the Brahmana as laid down in the Veda and other scriptures. Act now in such a way that you may have tranquillity of heart and let Brahmanas be your refuge. If the Brahmanas do not be angry with you, you will, forsooth, enjoy happiness in heaven. If, again, you repent for sins, your sight will be clear and you will succeed in seeing righteousness.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: जनमेजय उवाच अनुतप्ये च पापेन न च धर्मं विलोपये। बुभूधू भजमानं च प्रीतिमान् भव शौनक॥
en: Janamejaya said, I am repenting for my sins. I will never again try to suppress virtue. I wish to obtain blessedness. Be you pleased with me.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: शौनक उवाच छित्त्वा दम्भं च मानं च प्रीतिमिच्छामि ते नृप। सर्वभूतहितं तिष्ठ धर्मं चैव प्रतिस्मरन्॥
en: Shaunaka said Removing arrogance and pride, O king, I wish you to respect me. Do good to all creatures, always remembering the dictates of virtue.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: न भयान्न च कार्पण्यान्न लोभात् त्वामुपाहये। तां मे दैवीं गिरं सत्यां शृणु त्वं ब्राह्मणैः सह॥
en: I am not blaming you from fear or narrowness of mind or covetousness. Listen now, with these Brahmanas here, to the words of truth.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: सोऽहं न केनचिच्चार्थी त्वां च धर्मादुपाह्वये। क्रोशतां सर्वभूतानां हाहा धिगिति जल्पताम्॥
en: I do not ask for anything. I shall, however, instruct you in the ways of virtue. All persons will croak and bray and cry fie on me.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: वक्ष्यन्ति मामधर्मज्ञं त्यक्ष्यन्ति सुहृदो जनाः। ता वाचः सुहृदः श्रुत्वा संज्वरिष्यन्ति मे भृशम्॥
en: They will even call me sinful. My kinsmen and friends will renounce me. However, hearing the words I speak, my kinsmen and friends will surely succeed in vigorously crossing the difficulties of life.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: केचिदेव महाप्राज्ञाः प्रतिज्ञास्यन्ति तत्त्वतः। जानीहि मत्कृतं तात ब्राह्मणान् प्रति भारत।॥ यथा ते मत्कृते क्षेमं लभन्ते ते तथा कुरु। प्रतिजानीहि चाद्रोहं ब्राह्मणानां नराधिप॥
en: The wise will understand me aright. Know, O child, what are my views, O Bharata, regarding the Brahmanas. Do you act in such a way that they may, through my efforts, obtain every blessing! Do you also, O king, promise that you will not again injure the Brahmanas.

description: The fruit of satisfying the Brahmanas
sn: जनमेजय उवाच नैव वाचा न मनसा पुनर्जातु न कर्मणा। द्रोग्धास्मि ब्राह्मणान् विप्र चरणावपि ते स्पृशे॥
en: Janamejaya said I swear, touching even your feet, that I shall never again, in thought, word, or deed, harm the Brahmanas.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: शौनक उवाच तस्मात् तेऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि धर्ममावृतचेतसे। श्रीमान् महाबलस्तुष्टः स्वयं धर्ममवेक्षसे॥
en: Shaunaka said I shall for these reasons describe to you virtue, you whose heart has been exceedingly agitated. Endued with knowledge, great strength, and a contented heart, you seek virtue of your own accord.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: पुरस्ताद् दारुणो भूत्वा सुचित्रतरमेव तत्। अनुगृह्णाति भूतानि स्वेन वृत्तेन पार्थिवः॥
en: First becoming exceedingly stern, a king then shows mercy and does good to all creatures by his acts. This is certainly very wonderful.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: कृत्स्नं नूनं स दहति इति लोको व्यवस्यति। यत्र त्वं तादृशो भूत्वा धर्ममेवानुपश्यसि॥
en: People say that that king who begins with sternness consumes the entire world. You were stern before. But you now seck righteousness.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: हित्वा तु सुचिरं भक्ष्यं भोज्यांश्च तप आस्थितः। इत्येतदभिभूतानामद्भुतं जनमेजय॥
en: Forsaking luxurious food and all articles of enjoyment, you are now practising rigid penances for a long time. All this, O Janamejaya, is sure to appear wonderful to those kings who are sunk in sin.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: योऽदुर्लभो भवेद् दाता कृपणो वा तपोधनः। अनाश्चर्यं तदित्याहु तिदूरेण वर्तते॥
en: It is not at all wonderful that he who has wealth should become liberal, or that he who has wealth of asceticism should become unwilling to spend it. It has been said that the one does not live far off from the other.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: एतदेव हि कार्पण्यं समग्रमसमीक्षितम्। यचेत्सममीक्षयैव स्याद्भवेत्तस्मिस्ततो गुणः॥
en: An ill-judged thing produces enough of miserics. That, on the other hand, which is done with the help of sound judgement yields excellent results.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: यज्ञो दानं दया वेदाः सत्यं च पृथिवीपते। पञ्चैतानि पवित्राणि षष्ठं सुचरितं तपः॥ तदेव राज्ञां परमं पवित्रं जनमेजया
en: Sacrifice, gift, mercy, the Vedas, and truth, O king,-these five,-are purifying. The sixth is penance well-practised. This last, O Janamejaya, is highly purifying for kings.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: तेन सम्यग्गृहीतेन श्रेयांसं धर्ममाप्स्यसि॥ पुण्यदेशाभिगमन पवित्रं परमं स्मृतम्।
en: By following it duly, you are sure to acquire great merit and blessedness. Pilgrimage to sacred places has also been described to be highly purifying

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीमां गाथां गीतां ययातिना॥ यो मर्त्यः प्रतिपद्येत आयुर्जीवितमात्मनः। यज्ञमेकान्ततः कृत्वा तत् संन्यस्य तपश्चरेत्॥
en: Regarding it is cited the following verse sung by Yayati-That mortal who would acquire life and longevity should, after having celebrated sacrifices with devotion, renounce them and practise penances.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: पुण्यमाहुः कुरुक्षेत्रं कुरुक्षेत्रात् सरस्वतीम्। सरस्वत्याश्च तीर्थानि तीर्थेभ्यश्च पृथूदकम्॥ यत्रावगाह्य पीत्वा च नैनं श्वोमरणं तपेत्। महासरः पुष्कराणि प्रभासोत्तरमानसे॥
en: The field of Kuru has been described to be sacred. The river Sarasvati is considered more so. The Tirthas of the Sarasvati are inore sacred than the Sarasvati herself; and the Tirtha called Prithudaka is more sacred than all the Tirthas of the Sarasvati. One that has bathed in Prithudaka and drunk its waters will not have to be sorry for a premature death.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: कालोदकं च गन्तासि लब्धायुर्जीविते पुनः। सरस्वतीदृषद्वत्योः संगमो मानसः सरः॥ स्वाध्यायशीलः स्थानेषु सर्वेषु समुपस्पृशेत्। त्यागधर्मः पवित्राणां संन्यासं मनुरब्रवीत्॥
en: You should go to Mahasaras, to all the Tirthas known by the name of Pushkara, to Prabhasa, to the northern lake Manasa, and to Kalodaka. You will then regain life and acquire longevity. Lake Manasa is where the Sarasvati and the Drishadvati join each other. A person endued with Vedic lore should bathe in these places. Manu has said that liberality is the highest of all duties, and that renunciation is better than liberality.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीमा गाथाः सत्यवता कृताः। यथा कुमारः सत्यो वै नैव पुण्यो न पापकृत्॥
en: Regarding it is cited the following verse composed by Satyavat (One should act) as a child full of simplicity and shorn of either merit or sin.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: न ह्यस्ति सर्वभूतेषु दुःखमस्मिन् कुतः सुखम्। एवं प्रकृतिभूतानां सर्वसंसर्गयायिनाम्॥
en: For all creatures there is in this world neither misery nor happiness. Such is the true nature of all living creatures.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: त्यजतां जीवितं श्रेयो निवृत्ते पुण्यपापके। यत्त्वेव राज्ञो ज्यायिष्ठं कार्याणां तद् ब्रवीमि ते ॥
en: Of all creatures, they are superior who have betaken themselves to renunciation and abstained from acts both meritorious and sinful, I shall now tell you those acts which are best for a king.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: बलेन संविभागैश्च जय स्वर्ग जनेश्वर। यस्यैव बलमोजश्च स धर्मस्य प्रभुर्नरः॥
en: By showing your power and liberality do you conquer heaven, O king. that man who is endued with might and energy acquired righteousness.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: ब्राह्मणानां सुखार्थं हि त्वं पाहि वसुधां नृप। यथैवैतान् पुराऽऽक्षेप्सीस्तथैवैतान् प्रसादय॥
en: Do you govern the Earth, O king, for the sake of the Brahmanas and for the sake of happiness. You used formerly to blame the Brahmanas. Do you please them now.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: अपि धिक्रियमाणोऽपि त्यज्यमानोऽप्यनेकधा। आत्मनो दर्शनाद् विप्रान्न हन्तास्मीति मार्गया घटमानः स्वकार्येषु कुरु निःश्रेयसं परम्॥
en: Though they have censured you and though they have deserted you, do you still, guided by knowledge of self, solemnly promise never to injure them, Engaged in becoming acts, try to do what is for your highest good.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: हिमाग्निघोरसदृशो राजा भवति कश्चन। लांगलाशनिकल्पो वा भवेदन्यः परंतप॥
en: Amongst kings some one becomes as cool as snow; some one, as fierce as fire; some one becomes like a plough; and some one, again, becomes like a thunder-bolt.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: न विशेषेण गन्तव्यमविच्छिन्नेन वा पुनः। न जातु नाहमस्मीति सुप्रसक्तमसाधुषु।॥
en: He who wishes to prevent self-destruction, should never mix with wicked persons for general or particular purposes.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: विकर्मणा तप्यमानः पापाद् विपरिमुच्यते। नैतत् कार्यं पुनरिति द्वितीयात् परिमुच्यते॥
en: From a sinful act committed only once, one may clear himself by repenting for it. From an act committed twice, one may purify himself by vowing never to repeat the act.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: करिष्ये धर्ममेवेति तृतीयात् परिमुच्यते। शुचिस्तीर्थान्यनुचरन् बहुत्वात्परिमुच्यते॥
en: From such an act committed thrice, one may purify himself by determining to act virtuously all along afterwards. By committing such an act again and again, one may purify himself by visiting sacred places.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: कल्याणमनुकर्तव्यं पुरुषेण बुभूषता। ये सुगन्धीनि सेवन्ते तथागन्धा भवन्ति ते॥ ये दुर्गन्धीनि सेवन्ते तथागन्धा भवन्ति ते!
en: One who wishes to acquire prosperity should do all that yields blessedness. They who live amidst fragrance themselves become fragrant by virtue thereof. They, on the other hand, who live in the midst of foul smell themselves become foui.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: तपश्चर्यापरः सद्यः पापाद् विपरिमुच्यते॥ संवत्सरमुपास्याग्निमभिशस्तः प्रमुच्यते।
en: One who practises ascetic austerities is soon purged of all one's sins. By adoring the sacrificial fire for a year, one sullied by various sins becomes purified.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: त्रीणि वर्षाण्युपास्याग्निं भ्रूणहा विप्रमुच्यते।।२७ महासरः पुष्कराणि प्रभासोत्तरमानसे। अभ्येत्य योजनशतं भ्रूणहा विप्रमुच्यते॥ यावतः प्राणिनो हन्यात् तज्जातीयांस्तु तावतः प्रमीयमानानुन्मोच्य प्राणिहा विप्रमुच्यते॥
en: One guilty of foeticide is purified by adoring the fire for three years. One guilty for foeticide becomes purifies at even a hundred Yojanas from Mahasara, or the Tirthas called Pushkara, or Prabhasa, or Manasa on the north, if only he sets out for any of them. A slayer of creatures is purged of his sins by saving from impending danger as many creatures of that particular kind as have been killed by him.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: अपि चाप्सु निमज्जेत जपंस्त्रिरघमर्षणम्। यथाश्वमेधावभृथस्तथा तन्मनुरब्रवीत्॥
en: Manu has said that by diving in water after reciting thrice the sin-destroying Mantras, one rcaps the fruits of the final bath in a Horsesacrifice.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: तत्क्षिप्रं नुदते पापं सत्कारं लभते यथा। अपि चैनं प्रसीदन्ति भूतानि जडमूकवत्॥
en: Such an act very soon purifies one of all his sins, and he becomes, once again, the esteemed of the world. All creatures obey such a person, like helpless idiots.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: बृहस्पति देवगुरुं सुरासुराः सर्वे समेत्याभ्यनुयुज्य राजन्। धर्म्यं फलं वेत्थ फलं महर्षे तथैव तस्मिन्नरके पारलोक्ये॥
en: Approaching, in days of yore, the celestial preceptor Brihaspati, the gods and Asuras, O king, humbly enquired of him, saying,-You are cognisant, O great Rishi, of the fruits of virtue, as also the fruits of those other acts which lead to hell in the next world.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: उभे तु यस्य सदृशे भवेतां किंस्वित्तयोस्तत्र जयोथ न स्यात्। आचक्ष्व नः पुण्यपैलं महर्षे कथं पापं नुदते धर्मशीलः।।३३।
en: Can not that person free himself from both virtue and sin who regards the two (happiness and inisery) equally? Tell us, O great Rishi, what are the fruits of righteousness, and how does a virtuous person remove his sins!

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच कृत्वा पापं पूर्वमबुद्धिपूर्व पुण्यानि चेत्कुरुते बुद्धिपूर्वम्। स तत्पापं नुदते कर्मशीलो वासो यथा मलिनं क्षारयुक्तम्॥
en: Brihaspati answered If, having committed sin through foolishness, one performs meritorious acts understanding their nature, he succeeds, by such righteousness, in cleansing himself from sin even as a piece of dirty cloth is washed clean by some saline substance.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: पापं कृत्वाभिमन्येत नाहमस्मीति पूरुषः। तच्चिकीर्षति कल्याणं श्रद्दधानोऽनसूयकः॥
en: One should not brag after having committed sin. By having faith and by freeing one's self from malice, one acquires blessedness.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: छिद्राणि विवृतान्येव साधूनां चावृणोति यः। यः पापं पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते॥
en: That person who screens the faults of good men, even when exposed, acquires blessedness even after committing sins.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: यथाऽऽदित्यः प्रातरुद्यंस्तमः सर्वं व्यपोहति। कल्याणमाचरन्नेवं सर्वपापं व्यपोहति॥
en: As the sun rising on the morning removes all darkness, so does one dissipate all his sins by acting virtuously.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु राजानमिन्द्रोतो जनमेजयम्। याजयामास विधिवद् वाजिमेधेन शौनकः॥
en: Bhishma said Having said these words to king Janamejaya, Indrota, the son of Shaunaka, assisted him in the celebration of the Horsesacrifice.

description: The purificatory rites of a king
sn: ततः स राजा व्यपनीतकल्मष: श्रेयोवृतः प्रज्वलिताग्निरूपवान्। विवेश राज्यं स्वममित्रकर्षणो यथा दिवं पूर्णवपुर्निशाकरः॥
en: Purged of his sins, and regaining blessedness, the king shone like a burning fire, and that slayer of enemies then entered his kingdom like moon in his full form entering the celestial region. and that slayer of enemies then entered his kingdom like moon in his full form entering the celestial region.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कच्चित् पितामहेनासीच्छुतं वा दृष्टमेव च। कच्चिन्मो मृतो राजन् पुनरुज्जीवितोऽभवत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said Have you, O grandfather, ever seen or heard of any mortal restored to life after having met with death.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु पार्थ यथावृत्तमितिहासं पुरातनम्। गृध्रजम्बुकसंवादं यो वृत्तो नैमिषे पुरा॥
en: 'Listen, O king, to the discourse between a vulture and a jackal as it took place in days of yore. This incident happened in the forest of Naimisha.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: कस्यचिद् ब्राह्मणस्यासीद् दुःखलब्धः सुतो मृतः। बाल एव विशालाक्षो बालग्रहनिपीडितः॥
en: Once upon a time a Brahmana had, after great difficulties, got a son of large eyes. The child died of infantile convulsions.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: दुःखिताः केचिदादाय बालमप्राप्तयौवनम्। कुलसर्वस्वभूतं वै रुदन्तः शोकविह्वला:॥
en: Violently agitated by grief and bewailing aloud, some of his kinsmen took up the little boy who was the only wealth of his family.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: बालं मृतं गृहीत्वाथ श्मशानाभिमुखाः स्थिताः। अङ्केनैव च संक्रम्य रुरुदुर्भृशदुःखिताः॥
en: Taking the dead child they went in the direction of the crematorium. Going there they began to take the child from one another's breast and cry more bitterly in sorrow.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: शोचन्तस्तस्य पूर्वोक्तान् भाषितांश्चासकृत् पुनः। तं बालं भूतले क्षिप्य प्रतिगन्तुं न शक्नुयुः॥
en: Remembering with sorrowful hearts the former speeches of their minion again and again, they could not return home casting the body on the naked earth.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: तेषां रुदितशब्देन गृध्रोऽभ्येत्य वचोऽब्रवीत्। एकात्मजमिमं लोके त्यक्त्वा गच्छत मा चिरम्॥
en: Hearing their cries, a vulture came there and said-Go away, and do not delay, you who have to cast off but one child!

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: इह पुंसां सहस्राणि स्त्रीसहस्राणि चैव ह। समानीतानि कालेन हित्वा वै यान्ति बान्धवाः॥
en: Kinsmen always go away leaving here thousands of men and women brought here in course of time.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: सम्पश्यत जगत् सर्वं सुखदुःखैरधिष्ठितम्। संयोगो विप्रयोगश्च पर्यायेणोपलभ्यते॥
en: See, the entire universe is subject to happiness and misery. Union and disunion are seen in turns.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: गृहीत्वा ये च गच्छन्ति ये न यान्ति च तान् मृतान्। तेऽप्यायुषः प्रमाणेन स्वेन गच्छन्ति जन्तवः॥
en: They who have come to the crematorium with the dead bodies of their relatives, and they who sit by those bodies themselves go away from the world for their own acts when the allotted periods of their own lives expire.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अलं स्थित्वा श्मशानेऽस्मिन् गृध्रगोमायुसंकुले। कङ्कालबहुले रौद्रे सर्वप्राणिभयङ्करे॥
en: There is no necessity of your waiting in the crematorium, this dreadful place, which abounds with vultures, jackals and skeletons and fills every creature with fear.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: न पुनर्जीवितः कश्चित् कालधर्ममुपागतः। प्रियो वा यदि वा द्वेष्यः प्राणिनां गतिरीदृशी॥
en: Whether friend or enemy, no one becomes alive having once yielded to the power of Time. Such, indeed, is the destiny of all creatures.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: सर्वेण खलु मर्तव्यं मर्त्यलोके प्रसूयता। कृतान्तविहिते मार्ग मृतं को जीवयिष्यति॥
en: In this world of mortals, everyone who is born is sure to die. Who shall restore to life one that is dead and gone on the way ordained by the destroyer?

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: कर्मान्तविरते लोके अस्तं गच्छति भास्करे। गम्यतां स्वमधिष्ठानं सुतस्नेहं विसृज्य वै॥
en: At this hour when men are about to terminate their daily labours, the Sun is retiring to the setting hills. Go to your homes, renouncing this love for the child.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: ततो गृध्रवचः श्रुत्वा प्राक्रोशन्तस्तदा नृप। बान्धवास्तेऽभ्यगच्छन्त पुत्रमुत्सृज्य भूतले॥
en: Hearing these words of the vulture, the grief of the kinsmen seemed to decrease, and placing the child on the naked earth they were about to go away.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: विनिश्चित्याथ च तदा विक्रोशन्तस्ततस्ततः। मृतमित्येव गच्छन्तो निराशास्तस्य दर्शने॥
en: Knowing very well that the child had died and giving up every hope to see him again, they began to go back, bewailing loudly.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: निश्चितार्थाश्च ते सर्वे संत्यजन्तः स्वमात्मजम्। निराशा जीविते तस्य मार्गमावृत्य धिष्ठिताः॥
en: Firmly assured, and giving up all hopes of restoring the dead to life, they cast off that offspring of their family and prepared to turn back from that spot.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: ध्वांक्षपक्षसवर्णस्तु विलानिःसृत्य जम्बुकः। गच्छमानान् स्म तानाह निघृणाः खलु मानुषाः॥
en: At this time a jackal, black as a raven, came out of his hole and said to those departing kinsmen, forsooth, you who are kinsmen of that dead child have no affection.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: आदित्योऽयं स्थितो मूढाः स्नेहं कुरुत मा भयम्। बहुरूपो मुहूर्तश्च जीवेदपि कदाचन॥
en: There the Sun still shines in the sky, ye fools! Give vent to your feelings, fearlessly! Many are the virtues of the hour. This child may regain its life.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: यूयं भूमौ विनिक्षिप्य पुत्रस्नेहविनाकृताः। श्मशाने सुतमुत्सृज्य कस्माद् गच्छत निघृणाः॥
en: Spreading a few blades of Kusha grass on the ground and leaving that dear child on the crematorium, why do you go away with hearts of steel and renouncing every affection for the darling.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: न वोऽस्त्यस्मिन् सुते स्नेहो बाले मधुरभाषिणि। यस्य भाषितमात्रेण प्रसादमधिगच्छत॥
en: Surely, you have no love for that sweetspeeched little child, whose words, as soon as they left his lips, used to please you greatly!

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: ते पश्यत सुतस्नेहो यादृशः पशुपक्षिणाम्। न तेषां धारयित्वा तान् कश्चिदस्ति फलागमः॥
en: Mark the affection that even birds and beasts cherish for their young ones. They get no return for rearing up their young ones!

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: चतुष्पात्पक्षिकीटानां प्राणिनां स्नेहसङ्गिनाम्। परलोकगतिस्थानां मुनियज्ञक्रिया इव॥
en: Like the sacrifice of the Rishis, the love of quadrupeds, of birds, and insects, yields no reward in heaven.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: तेषां पुत्राभिरामाणामिहलोके परत्र च। न गुणो दृश्यते कश्चित् प्रजाः संधारयन्ति च॥
en: Though they love their children, they are never seen to derive any benefit from the latter either in this world or in the next. Yet they love their young ones.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अपश्यतां प्रियान् पुत्रांस्तेषां शोको न तिष्ठति। न च पुष्णन्ति संवृद्धास्ते मातापितरौ क्वचित्॥
en: Growing up, their children never maintain them in age. Still do they not feel pained when they do not see their title ones?

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: मानुषाणां कुतः स्नेहो येषां शोको भविष्यति। इमं कुलकरं पुत्रं त्यक्त्वा क्व न गमिष्यथ॥
en: How is affection to be seen in human beings since they only indulge in grief? Where would you go leaving here this child who is the perpetuator of his family.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: चिरं मञ्चत बाष्पं च चिरं स्नेहेन पश्यत। एवंविधानि हीष्टानि दुस्त्यजानि विशेषतः॥
en: Do you shed tears for him for some time, and look at him a little longer with affection. It is difficult to cast off objects which are so dear.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: क्षीणस्याभियुक्तस्य श्मशानाभिमुखस्य च। बान्धवा यत्र तिष्ठन्ति तत्रान्यो नाधितिष्ठति॥
en: It is friends and not others who wait by the side of the weak, of the prosecuted in a court of law, and of him who is borne towards the burning place.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: सर्वस्य दयिताः प्राणाः सर्वः स्नेहं च विन्दति। तिर्यग्योनिष्वपि सतां स्नेहं पश्यत यादृशम्॥
en: Life is dear to all, and all feel the influence of love. See the affection that is cherished by beasts and birds.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: त्यक्त्वा कथं गच्छथेमं पद्मलोलायताक्षिकम्। यथा नवोद्वाहकृतं स्नानमाल्यविभूषितम्॥
en: How can you go away, casting off this boy having eyes large as the lotus petal, and beautiful as a newly-wedded youth washed clean and bedecked with garlands.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: जम्बुकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा कृपणं परिदेवतः। न्यवर्तन्त तदा सर्वे शवार्थं ते स्म मानुषाः॥
en: Hearing these words of the jackal who had been thus giving vent to expressions of grief, the men turned back for the sake of the dead body.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: गृध्र उवाच अहो वत नृशंसेन जम्बुकेनाल्पमेधसा। क्षुद्रेणोक्ता हीनसत्त्वा मानुषाः किं निवर्तथ॥
en: The Vulture said Alas, you men shorn of strength of mind, why do you turn back at the call of a cruel, nmean and little-witted jackal.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: पञ्चेन्द्रियपरित्यक्तं शुष्कं काष्ठत्वमागतम्। कस्माच्छोवथ तिष्ठन्तमात्मानं किं न शोचथ॥
en: Why do you lament for that compound of five elements deserted by their presiding gods, no longer occupied (by the soul), motionless, and stiff as a piece of wood? Why do you not grieve for your own selves.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: तपः कुरुत वै तीव्र मुच्यध्वं येन किल्बिषात्। तपसा लभ्यते सर्वं विलापः किं करिष्यति॥
en: Do you practise austerities by which you will succeed in purifying yourselves from sin! Everything may be got by penances. What will lamentations do?

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अनिष्टानि च भाग्यानि जातानि सह मूर्तिना। येन गच्छति बालोऽयं दत्त्वा शोकमनन्तकम्॥
en: Death is born with the body. It is for ill-luck that this boy has departed, plunging you into infinite grief!

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: धनं गावः सुवर्णं च मणिरत्नमथापि च। अपत्यं च तपोमूलं तपोयोगाच्च लभ्यते॥
en: Wealth, kine, gold, precious gems, children, all originate from penances. Penances again are the outcome of Yoga.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: यथाकृता च भूतेषु प्राप्यते सुखदुःखिता। गृहीत्वा जायते जन्तुर्दुःखानि च सुखानि च॥
en: Amongst creatures, the measure of happiness or misery depends on pristine deeds. Every creature is born in the world, taking with him his own measure of happiness and misery.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: न कर्मणा पितुः पुत्रः पिता वा पुत्रकर्मणा। मार्गेणान्येन गच्छन्ति वद्धाः सुकृतदुष्कृतैः॥
en: The son is not fettered by the acts of the father, or the father by those of the son. Fettered by their own acts good and bad, all have to wend this common road.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: धर्मं चरत यत्नेन न चाधर्मे मनः कृथाः। वर्तध्वं च यथाकालं दैवतेषु द्विजेषु च॥
en: Duly follow all the duties, and abstain from acts of unrighteousness! Reverentially wait, according to scriptural injunctions, upon the gods and the Brahmanas!

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: शोकं त्यजत दैन्यं च सुतस्नेहान्निवर्तत। त्यज्यतामयमाकाशे ततः शीघ्रं निवर्तत॥
en: Shake off sorrow and cheerlessness, and abstain from parental affection! Lcave the child on this open ground, and go away forthwith.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: यत् करोति शुभं कर्म तथा कर्म सुदारुणम्। तत् कतैव समश्नाति बान्धवानां किमत्र ह॥
en: The doer alone reaps the fruits of his good or bad acts. What concern have kinsmen with them.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: इह त्यक्त्वा न तिष्ठन्ति बान्धवा बान्धवं प्रियम्। स्नेहमुत्सृज्य गच्छन्ति बाष्पपूर्णाविलेक्षणाः॥
en: Leaving dead kinsman however dear, kinsman leave this spot. With eyes full of tcars, they go away, ccasing to show affection for the dead.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: प्राज्ञो वा यदि वा मूर्खः सधनो निर्धनोऽपि वा। सर्वः कालवशं याति शुभाशुभसमन्वितः॥
en: Wise or ignorant, rich or poor, every one yields to Time, endued with good and bad acts.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: किं करिष्यथ शोचित्वा मृतं किमनुशोचथ। सर्वस्य हि प्रभुः कालो धर्मतः समदर्शनः॥
en: Of what use is mourning? Why do you grieve for the dead? Time is the master of all, and he by his very nature looks impartially on all things.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: यौवनस्थांश्च बालांश्च वृद्धान् गर्भगतानपि। सर्वानाविशते मृत्युरेवंभूतमिदं जगत्॥
en: In proud youth or in helpless infancy, in age or while lying in the mother's womb, every one is subject to be attacked by Death. Such is the course of the world.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: जम्बुक उवाच अहो मन्दीकृतः स्नेहो गृध्रेणेहाल्पबुद्धिना। पुत्रस्नेहाभिभूतानां युष्माकं शोचतां भृशम्॥
en: Alas, the love which you entertain for your dead child, and manifested in your sorrowing cyes and mournful looks, has been lessened by that foolish vulture.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: समैः सम्यक्प्रयुक्तैश्च वचनैः प्रत्ययोत्तरैः। यद्गच्छति जनश्चायं स्नेहमुत्सृज्य दुस्त्यजम्॥
en: It is, indeed, so, since influenced by his well-applied words teaching tranquility and capable of producing conviction, that man there returns to the town, casting off affection that is so hard to throw off.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अहो पुत्रवियोगेन मृतशून्योपसेवनात्। क्रोशतां सुभृशं दुःखं विवत्सानां गवामिव॥
en: Alas, I had thought that the grief felt by men bewailing aloud for the death of a child and for the corpse on a creinatorium, is great like that of kine bereft of calves.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अद्य शोकं विजानामि मानुषाणां महीतले। स्नेहं हि कारणं कृत्वा ममाप्यश्रूण्यथापतन्॥
en: To-day, however, I perceive the extent of grief of human beings on earth. Seeing their great affection I had shed tears myself.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: यत्लो हि सततं कार्यस्ततो दैवेन सिद्ध्यति। दैवं पुरुषकारश्च कृतान्तेनोपपद्यते॥
en: One should always exert. From it and through destiny one succeeds. Exertion and destiny, joining together, yield fruits.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अनिर्वेदः सदा कार्यो निर्वेदाद्धि कुतः सुखम्। प्रयत्नात् प्राप्यते ह्यर्थः कस्माद् गच्छथ निर्दयम्॥
en: One should always exert hopefully. How can happiness be secured from despondency? Objects of desire may be acquired by resolution. Why then do you return so heartlessly?

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: आत्ममांसोपवृत्तं च शरीरार्धमयीं तनुम्। पितृणां वंशकर्तारं वने त्यक्त्वा क्व यास्यथ॥
en: Where do you go, leaving in the forest this your own begotten son, this perpetuator of the race of his father.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अथवास्तंगते सूर्ये संध्याकाल उपस्थिते। ततो नेष्यथ वा पुत्रमिहस्था वा भविष्यथ॥
en: Stay here till the sun sets and the evening comes. You may then take away this boy with yourselves or remain here with him.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: गृध्र उवाच अद्य वर्षसहस्रं मे साग्रं जातस्य मानुषाः। न च पश्यमि जीवन्तं मृतं स्त्रीपुंनपुंसकम्॥
en: I am, Ye men, thousand years old this day, but I have never seen a dead creature, male or female or eunuch, revive after death.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: मृता गर्भेषु जायन्ते जातमात्रा म्रियन्ति च। चङ्क्रमन्तो म्रियन्ते च यौवनस्थास्तथा परे॥
en: Some die in the womb; some die soon after birth; some die while crawling; some die in youth; and some in old age.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अनित्यानीह भाग्यानि चतुष्पात्यक्षिणामपि। जङ्गमानां नगानां वाप्यायुरग्रेऽवतिष्ठते॥
en: The fortunes of all creatures, including beasts and birds, are fickle. The extent of life of all mobile and immobile creatures is fixed beforehand.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: इष्टदारवियुक्ताश्च पुत्रशोकान्वितास्तथा। दह्यमानाः स्म शोकेन गृहं गच्छन्ति नित्यशः॥
en: Shorn of wives and dear ones and filled with sorrow for children, men leave this spot every day with aggrieved hearts for returning home.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अनिष्टानां सहस्राणि तथेष्टानां शतानि च। उत्सृज्येह प्रयाता वै बान्धवा भृशदुःखिताः॥
en: Leaving here thousands of both friends and enemies, kinsmen stricken with grief go back to their homes.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: त्यज्यतामेष निस्तेजाः शून्यः काष्ठत्वमागतः। अन्यदेहविषक्तं हि शावं काष्ठत्वमागतम्॥ त्यक्तजीवस्य चैवास्य कस्माद्धित्वा न गच्छत।
en: Leave off this dead body which has no longer any animal heat in it and which is as stiff as a piece of wood. Why then do you not go away, leaving the body of this child which is like a piece of wood and whose life had entered a new body?

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: निरर्थको ह्ययं स्नेहो निष्फलश्च परिश्रमः॥ चक्षुर्त्यां न च कर्णाभ्यां सं शृणोति समीक्षते।
en: This your love has no meaning, and this caressing of the child is useless. He does not see with his eyes or hear with ears.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: कस्मादेनं समुत्सृज्य न गृहान् गच्छताशु वै॥ मोक्षधर्माश्रितैर्वाक्यैर्हेतुमद्भिः सुनिष्ठुरैः। मयोक्ता गच्छत क्षिप्रं स्वं स्वमेव निवेशनम्॥
en: Leaving him here go away forthwith. Thus addressed by me in words which are seemingly cruel but which in reality are reasonable and are directly connected with the great religion of emancipation, return he to your respective homes.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: प्रज्ञाविज्ञानयुक्तेन बुद्धिसंज्ञाप्रदायिना। वचनं श्राविता नूनं मानुषाः संनिवर्तत। शोको द्विगुणतां याति दृष्ट्वा स्मृत्वा च चेष्टितम्॥
en: Addressed thus by the vulture gifted with wisdom and knowledge and capable of giving intelligence and awakening the understanding, those men were about to go away from the crematorium. Grief becomes two-fold two-fold on seeing its object and on remembering the acts of that object (in life).

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: इत्येतद् वचनं श्रुत्वा संनिवृत्तास्तु मानुषाः। अपश्यत् तं तदा सुप्तं द्रुतमागत्य जम्बुकः॥
en: Having heard these words of the vulture, the men resolved to leave that place. Just at that time the jackal, coming there quickly, spied the child lying in the sleep of death.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: जम्बुक उवाच इमं कनकवर्णाभं भूषणैः समलंकृतम्। गृध्रवाक्यात् कथं पुत्रं त्यजध्वं पितृपिण्डदम्॥
en: Why, indeed, do you leave, at the vulture's suggestion, this child bearing golden hue, adorned with ornaments, and capable of giving the obsequial cake to his departed manes?

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: न स्नेहस्य च विच्छेदो विलापरुदितस्य च। मृतस्यास्य परित्यागात् तापो वै भविता ध्रुवम्॥
en: If you abandon him, your love will not terminate, nor these piteous cries. On the other hand, your grief will multiply itself.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: श्रूयते शम्बुके शूद्रे हते ब्राह्मणदारकः। जीवितो धर्ममासाद्य रामात् सत्यपराक्रमात्॥
en: We have heard that a Shudra named Shambuka having been killed and virtue having been upheld by the powerful Rama, a (dead, Brahmana child was restored to life.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: तथा श्वेतस्य राजर्षेर्बालो दृष्टान्तमागतः। श्वेतेन धर्मनिष्ठेन मृतः संजीवितः पुनः॥
en: Likewise the son of the royal sage Shveta had died (prematurely). But the virtuous monarch succeeded in reviving his dead child.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: तथा कश्चिल्लभेत् सिद्धो मुनिर्वा देवतापि वा। कृपणानामनुक्रोशं कुर्याद् वो रुदतामिह॥
en: Similarly, in your case also, some sage or god may be willing to grant your desire and show mercy to you that are crying piteously.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: इत्युक्तास्ते न्यवर्तन्त शोकार्ताः पुत्रवत्सलाः। अङ्के शिरः समाधाय रुरुदुर्बहुविस्तरम्। तेषां रुदितशब्देन गृध्रोऽभ्येत्य वचोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus accosted by the jackai, the men, stricken with grief and full of affection for the child, returned, and placing the child's head on their laps one after another, began the bewail piteously. Hearing their cries, the vulture, coming there, once more spoke to them as follows.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: गृध्र उवाच अश्रुपातपरिक्लिन्नः पाणिस्पर्शप्रपीडितः। धर्मराजप्रयोगाच्च दीर्घनिद्रां प्रवेशितः॥
en: The Vulture said Why are you bathing this child with your tears? Why are you pressing him with your palms in this way? At the behest of the grim king of justice the child has been sent to that sleep which will never be broken.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: तपसापि हि संयुक्ता धनवन्तो महाधियः। सर्वे मृत्युवशं यान्ति तदिदं प्रेतपत्तनम्॥
en: Those who have acquired the merit of penances, those who are gifted with wealth, those who are endued with great intelligence, in fact, all yield to death. This is the place intended for the dead.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: बालवृद्धसहस्राणि सदा संत्यज्य बान्धवाः। दिनानि चैव रात्रीश्च दुःखं तिष्ठन्ति भूतले॥
en: It is always seen that casting off thousands of kinsmen, young and old kinsmen pass their nights and days in grief, rolling on the naked earth.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अलं निर्बन्धमागत्य शोकस्य परिधारणे। अप्रत्ययं कुतो ह्यस्य पुनरोह जीवितम्॥
en: Stop this ardour in putting on the trappings of woe. It is impossible that this child would be restored to life again.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: मृतस्योत्सृष्टदेहस्य पुनर्देहो न विद्यते। नैव मूर्तिप्रदानेन जम्बुकस्य शतैरपि॥
en: He will not regain his life ai the call of the jackal. If a person once dies and deserts his body, this body never regains animation.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: शक्यं जीवयितुं ह्येष बालो वर्षशतैरपि।
en: By sacrificing their own lives, hundreds of jackals will not be able to revive this child in hundreds of years.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अथ रुद्रः कुमारो वा ब्रह्मा वा विष्णुरेव च॥ वरमस्मै प्रयच्छेयुस्ततो जीवेदयं शिशुः।
en: If, however, Rudra, Kumara, Brahma, or Vishnu, grant him a boon, then only may this child be restored to life.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: नैव बाष्पविमोक्षेण न वा श्वासकृते न च॥ न दीर्घरुदितेनायं पुनर्जीवं गमिष्यति।
en: Neither the shedding of tears, nor the heaving of long sighs, nor profuse lamentations, will restore this one to life.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अहं च क्रोष्टकश्चैव यूयं ये चास्य बान्धवाः॥ धर्माधर्मो गृहीत्वेह सर्वे वर्तामहेऽध्वनि। अप्रियं परुषं चापि परद्रोहं परस्त्रियम्॥ अधर्ममनृतं चैव दूरात् प्राज्ञो विवर्जयेत्। धर्मं सत्यं श्रुतं न्याय्यं महतीं प्राणिनां दयाम्॥ अजिह्मत्वमशाठ्यं च यत्नतः परिमार्गत। मातरं पितरं वापि बान्धवान् सुहृदस्तथा॥ जीवतो ये न पश्यन्ति तेषां धर्मविपर्ययः।
en: Myself, the jackal, you all, and all the relatives of this one, with all our virtues and sins, are vending the same way. Seek with care virtue, truth, the good of others justice, mercy for all creature, sincerity and honesty. They incur sin who, while living, do not take care of their parents, kinsmen and friends.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: यो न पश्यति चक्षुर्त्यां नेङ्गते च कथञ्चन॥ तस्य निष्ठावसानान्ते रुदन्तः किं करिष्यथ।
en: What will you profit by crying, for him after death, who does not see with his eyes and stir in the least.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: इत्युक्तास्ते सुतं त्यक्त्वा भूमौ शोकपरिप्लुताः। दह्यमानाः सुतस्नेहात् प्रययुर्बान्धवा गृहम्॥
en: Thus addressed, the men, laden with sorrow and burning with grief on account of their love for the child, departed for their homes, leaving the body.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: जम्बुक उवाच दारुणो मर्त्यलोकोऽयं सर्वप्राणिविनाशनः। इष्टबन्धुवियोगश्च तथेहाल्पं च जीवितम्॥
en: The jackal said Alas, dreadful is this world of mortals! Here no creature can escape. Every creature's life is short. Beloved friends are always going.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: बह्वलीकमसत्यं चाप्यतिवादाप्रियंवदम्। इमं प्रेक्ष्य पुनर्भावं दुःखशोकविवर्धनम्॥ न मे मानुषलोकोऽयं मुहूर्तमपि रोचते।
en: It is full of vanities and falsehoods, accusations and evil reports! Witnessing again this incident which increases pain and grief, I do not for a moment like this world of men.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: अहो धिग् गृध्रवाक्येन यथैवाबुद्धयस्तथा॥ कथं गच्छत निःस्नेहाः सुतस्नेहं विसृज्य च। प्रदीप्ताः पुत्रशोकेन संनिवर्तत मानुषाः॥ श्रुत्वा गृध्रस्य वचनं पापस्येहाकृतात्मनः।
en: Alas, shame on you, you men, who thus return like foolish persons, on hearing the vulture's words, though you are burning with grief on account of the death of this child. You cruel men, how can you go away, renouncing parental affection upon hearing the words of a sinful vulture of impure soul.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं दुःखस्यानन्तरं सुखम्॥ सुखदुःखावृते लोके नेहास्त्येकमनन्तरम्। इमं क्षितितले त्यक्त्वा बालं रूपसमन्वितम्॥ कुलशोभाकरं मूढाः पुत्रं त्यक्त्वा क्व यास्यथा रूपयौवनसम्पन्नं द्योतमानमिव श्रिया॥ जीवन्तमेव पश्यामि मनसा नात्र संशयः।
en: Happiness is followed by misery, and misery by happiness. In this world which has both happiness and misery, none of these two exists without break. You little-witted men, where will go, casting off on the naked earth this beautiful child, this son who is a13 ornament of your family. Verily, I cannot conceive that this child endued with grace, youth and beauty is dead.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: विनाशो नास्य न हि वै सुखं प्राप्स्यथ मानुषाः॥ पुत्रशोकाभितप्तानां मृतानामद्य वः क्षमम्।
en: It is not proper that he should die. It seems that you are sure to gain happiness. You who are stricken with grief for the death of this child will, forsooth, have good luck to-day.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: सुखसम्भावनं कृत्वा धारयित्वा सुखं स्वयम्। त्यक्त्वा गमिष्यथ क्वाद्य समुत्सृज्याल्पबुद्धिवत्॥
en: Anticipating inconvenience and pain and seeking your own comfort, where will you, like persons of little intelligence, go, leaving this darling.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: भीष्म उवाच तथा धर्मविरोधेन प्रियमिथ्याभिधायिना। श्मशानवासिना नित्यं रात्रिं मृगयता नृप॥ ततो मध्यस्थतां नीता वचनैरमृतोपमैः। जम्बुकेन स्वकार्यार्थं बान्धवास्तस्य धिष्ठिताः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus, O king, the kinsmen of the dead child, unable to settle what they should do, were, for fulfilling his own purpose, induced by that sinful jackal who uttered sweet falsehoods-that dweller of the crematorium who went there every night in search of food.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: गृध्र उवाच अयं प्रेतसमाकीर्णो यक्षराक्षससेवितः। दारुणः काननोद्देशः कौशिकैरभिनादितः॥
en: Dreadful is that spot, this wilderness, which resounds with the screams of owls and is filled with spirits and Yakshas and Rakshasas.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: भीमः सुघोरश्च तथा नीलमेघसमप्रभः। अस्मिञ्छवं परित्यज्य प्रेतकार्याण्युपासत॥
en: It appears dreadful like a mass of blue clouds. Casting off the body, perform the funeral rites.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: भानुवत् प्रयात्यस्तं यावच्च विमला दिशः। तावदेनं परित्यज्य प्रेतकार्याण्युपासत॥
en: Throwing away the body, perform those rites before the sun sets and before the points of compass are covered with darkness.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: नदन्ति परुषं श्येना: शिवाः क्रोशन्ति दारुणम्। मृगेन्द्राः प्रतिनन्दन्ति रविरस्तं च गच्छति॥
en: The hawks are uttering hideous cries. Jackals are howling hideously. Lions are roaring. The sun is setting.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: चिताधूमेन नीलेन संरज्यन्ते च पादपाः। श्मशाने च निराहारा: प्रतिनर्दन्ति देहिनः॥
en: The trees on the crematorium are appearing dark for the blue smoke of the funeral pyres. Stricken with hunger the carnivorous animals are yelling in rage.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: सर्वे विकृतदेहाश्चाप्यस्मिन् देशे सुदारुणे। युष्मान् प्रधर्षयिष्यन्ति विकृता मांसभोजिनः॥१००।
en: All those creatures of dreadful forms which live in this fearful place, all those grim-visaged animals that haunt this desert, will soon attack you.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: क्रूरश्चायं वनोद्देशो भयमद्य भविष्यति। त्यज्यतां काष्ठभूतोऽयं मृष्यतां जाम्बुकं वचः॥ यदि जम्बुकवाक्यानि निष्फलान्यनृतानि च। श्रोष्यथ भ्रष्टविज्ञानास्ततः सर्वे विनइक्ष्यथ॥
en: This forest is certainly dreadful. Danger will beset you. The child is like a dry wood. Indeed, if you listen to these false and useless words of the jackal against your own good sense, all of your will surely meet with death.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: जम्बुक उवाच स्थीयतां नेह भेतव्यं यावत् तपति भास्करः। तावदस्मिन् सुते स्नेहादनिर्वेदेन वर्तत॥
en: Remain where you are. There is no fear even in this desert as long as the sun shines. Do you remain herc hopefully, moved by parental affection till the sun sets.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: स्वैरं रुदन्तो विश्रब्धाश्चिरं स्नेहेन पश्यत। (दारुणेऽस्मिन् वनोद्देशे भयं वो न भरिष्यति। अयं सौम्यो वनोद्देशः पितॄणां निधनाकरः।) स्थीयतां यावदादित्यः किं च क्रव्यादभाषितैः॥
en: Without any fear, bewailing as you please, continue to look at this child with loving eyes. Though this forest is dreadful, no danger will overtake you. In sooth, this wilderness is quiet and peaceful. It is here that the Pitris by thousands departed from the world. Wait as long as the sun shines. Of what avail are this vulture's words to you?

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: यदि गृध्रस्य वाक्यानि तीव्राणि रभसानि च। गृह्णीत मोहितात्मानः सुतो वो न भविष्यति॥
en: If, being stupefied, you follow the cruel and harsh words of the vulture, then your child will never regain life.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: भीष्म उवाच गृध्रोऽस्तमित्याह गतो गतो नेति च जम्बुकः। मृतस्य तं परिजनमूचतुस्तौ क्षुधान्वितौ॥
en: Bhishma said The vulture then said to those men, that the sun had set. The jackal said that it was not so. Both the vulture and the jackal fell hungry and thus addressed thc kinsmen of the dead child.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: स्वकार्यबद्धकक्षौ तौ राजन् गृध्रोऽथ जम्बुकः। क्षुत्पिपासापरिश्रान्तौ शास्त्रमालम्ब्य जल्पतः॥
en: Both of them were deterinined upon accomplishing their respective purposes. Exhausted with hunger and thirst, they thus quarrelled, taking advantage of the scriptures.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: तयोविज्ञानविदुषोईयोर्मुगपतत्रिणोः। वाक्यैरमृतकल्पैस्तैः प्रतिष्ठन्ति व्रजन्ति च॥
en: Moved by these words, sweet as ambrosia, of those two creatures, viz., the bird and the beast, both of whom had wisdom and knowledge, the kinsmen at one time desired to go away and at another to remain there.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: शोकदैन्यसमाविष्टा रुदन्तस्तस्थिरे तदा। स्वकार्यकुशलाभ्यां ते सम्भ्राम्यन्ते ह नैपुणात्॥
en: At last, actuated by sorrow and depression, they waited there, bewailing piteously. They did not know that the beast and the bird, very clever in achieving their ends, had only stupefied them (by their words).

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: तथा तयोर्विवदतोर्विज्ञानविदुषोईयोः। बान्धवानां स्थितानां चाप्युपातिष्ठत शङ्करः॥
en: While both the bird and the beast were thus disputing and while the kinsmen of the dead child sat listening to them, the great god Shankara, urged by his divine consort (Uma), arrived there with eyes bathed in tears of mercy.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: देव्या प्रणोदितो देवः कारुण्यार्दीकृतेक्षणः। ततस्तानाह मनुजान वरदोऽस्मीति शङ्करः॥ ते प्रत्यूचुरिदं वाक्यं दुःखिताः प्रणताः स्थिताः। एकपुत्रविहीनानां सर्वेषां जीवितार्थिनाम्॥ पुत्रस्य नो जीवदानाज्जीवितं दातुमर्हसि।
en: Addressing the kinsmen of the dead child, the god said,-I am Shankara the granter of boons!-With hearts laden with grief, those men laid themselves low before the great god and said to him in reply,-Bereft of this our only child, all of us are on the brink of death. Be you pleased to grant us life by granting life to this our son.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: एवमुक्तः स भगवान् वारिपूर्णेन चक्षुषा॥ जीवितं स्म कुमाराय प्रादाद् वर्षशतानि वै।
en: Thus begged, the illustrious god, taking up some water in his hands, granted to that dead child life extending for a hundred years.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: तथा गोमायुगृध्राभ्यां प्राददत् क्षुद्विनाशनम्॥ वरं पिनाकी भगवान् सर्वभूतहिते रतः।
en: Ever engaged in the behoof of all creatures, the illustrious holder of Pinaka granted a boon to both the jackal and the vulture for which their hunger was appeased.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: कृतकृत्याः सुखं हृष्टाः प्रातिष्ठन्त तदा विभो। अनिर्वेदेन दीर्पण निश्चयेन ध्रुवेण च॥ देवदेवप्रसादाच्च क्षिप्रं फलमवाप्यते। ततः प्रणम्य ते देवं प्रायो हर्षसमन्विताः॥
en: Filled with joy and having gained great prosperity, the men bowed to the god. Gaining success, they then, O king, left that spot in great glee. Through continued hopefulness and firm determination and the grace of the great god, the fruits of one's acts are gained forthwith.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: पश्य दैवस्य संयोगं बान्धवानां च निश्चयम्॥ कृपणानां तु रुदतां कृतमश्रुप्रमार्जनम्।
en: Mark the combination of circumstances and the determination of those kinsmen. While crying with heavy hearts, their tears were wiped and dried up.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: पश्य चाल्पेन कालेन निश्चयान्वेषणेन च॥ प्रसादं शङ्करात् प्राप्य दुःखिताः सुखमाप्नुवन्।
en: See, how within only a short time, through their firmness of resolution, they gained the grace of Shankara, and their sorrows removed, they were made happy.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: ते विस्मिताः प्रहृष्टाश्च पुत्रसंजीवनात् पुनः॥ बभूवुर्भरतश्रेष्ठ प्रसादाच्छङ्करस्य वै।
en: Indeed, through Shankara's favour, O chief of the Bharatas, those sorrowing kinsmen were filled with wonder and joy at the restoration of their child to life.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: ततस्ते त्वरिता राजंस्त्यक्त्वा शोकं शिशूद्भवम्॥ विविशुः पुत्रमादाय नगरं हृष्टमानसाः। एषा बुद्धिः समस्तानां चातुर्वण्र्ये निदर्शिता॥
en: Then, O king, shaking off that grief caused by their child, those Brahmanas, filled with joy, quickly returned to their town; taking the restored child with them. Such a conduct has been laid down for all the four castes.

description: Whether a man revives after death. The conversation between a Vulture and a Jackal
sn: धर्मार्थमोक्षसंयुक्तमितिहासमिमं शुभम्। श्रुत्वा मनुष्यः सततमिहामुत्र च मोदते॥
en: By frequently listening to this auspicious story fraught with virtue, profit, and emancipation, a man acquires happiness both in this world and the next.'

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच बलिनः पत्यमित्रस्य नित्यमासन्नवर्तिनः। उपकारापकाराभ्यां समर्थस्योद्यतस्य च॥ मोहाद् विकत्थनामात्रैरसारोऽल्पबलो लघुः। वाग्भिरप्रतिरूपाभिरभिद्रुह्य पितामह॥ आत्मनो बलमास्थाय कथं वर्तेत मानवः। आगच्छतोऽतिक्रुद्धस्य तस्योद्धरणरकाम्यया॥
en: Yudhishthira said If a weak, worthless and light-hearted person, O grandfather, does from folly excite, by improper and boastful words, a powerful enemy always living near him, capable of doing good and chastising and always ready for action, how should the former, relying on his own strength, act when the later proceeds against him in anger for extirpating him?

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। संवादं भरतश्रेष्ठ शाल्मले: पवनस्य च॥
en: Bhishma said-'Regarding it is cited, O chief of the Bharatas, the old discourse between Shalmali and Pavana.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: हिमवन्तं समासाद्य महानासीद् वनस्पतिः। वर्षपूगाभिसंवृद्धः शाखी स्कन्धी पलाशवान्॥
en: There was a huge (Shalmali) tree on one of the peaks of Himavat. Having grown for many hundred years, he had spread out his branches wide around. His trunk also was huge and his twigs and leaves were numberless.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: तत्र स्म मत्तमातङ्गा धर्मार्ताः श्रमकर्शिताः। विश्राम्यन्ति महाबाहो तथान्या मृगजातयः॥
en: Under his shade elephants, exhausted and covered with temporal juice and sweat, used to rest, and as also many other animals.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: नल्वमात्रपरीणाहो घनच्छायो वनस्पतिः। सारिकाशुकसंजुष्टः पुष्पवान् फलवानपि॥
en: The circumference of his trunk was four hundred cubits, and the shade of his branches and leaves was dense. Laden with flowers and fruits, it was the abode of numberless parrots male and female.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: सार्थिका वणिजश्चापि तापसाश्च वनौकसः। वसन्ति तत्र मार्गस्थाः सुरम्ये नगसत्तमे॥
en: While travelling, caravans of merchants and traders, and ascetics living in the forest, used to rest under the shade of that charming king of the forest.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: तस्य ता विपुला: शाखा दृष्ट्वा स्कन्धं च सर्वशः। अभिगम्याब्रवीदेनं नारदो भरतर्षभ॥ अहो नु रमणीयस्त्वमहो चासि मनोहरः। प्रीयामहे त्वया नित्यं तरुप्रवर शाल्मले॥
en: One day, O foremost of Bharata's race, seeing the wide-extending and numberless branches of that tree and the circumference of his trunk, the sage Narada, approached and addressed him, saying,-O, you are delightful! O, you are charming! O foremost of trees, O Shalmali, I am always pleased to see you.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: सदैव शकुनास्तात मृगाश्चाथ तथा गजाः। वसन्ति तव संहृष्टा मनोहर मनोहराः॥
en: O charming tree, beautiful birds of various kinds, and elephants and other animals gladly live on your branches and under their shade.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: तव शाखा महाशाख स्कन्धांश्च विपुलांस्तथा। न वै प्रभग्नान् पश्यामि मारुतेन कथंचन॥
en: Your branches, O wide-branched king of the forest, are lofty and majestic as huge is your trunk! I never see any of them broken by the god of wind.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: किं नु ते पवनस्तात प्रीतिमानथवा सुहृत्। त्वां रक्षति सदा येन वनेऽत्र पवनो ध्रुवम्॥
en: Is it, O child, because that Wind-god is pleased with you and is your friend so that he protects you always in these woods?

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: भगवान् पवन: स्थानाद् वृक्षानुच्चावचानपि। पर्वतानां च शिखराण्याचालयति वेगवान्॥
en: The illustrious Pavana of great speed and force unfixes the tallest and strongest trees, and even mountain summits.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: शोषयत्येव पातालं वहन् गन्धवहः शुचिः। सरांसि सरितश्चैव सागरांश्च तथैव च।॥
en: That sacred carrier of perfumes, blowing at his pleasure dries up rivers, lakes and seas, including the very nether region.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: संरक्षति त्वां पवनः सखित्वेन न संशयः। तस्मात् त्वं बहुशाखोऽपि पर्णवान् पुष्पवानपि॥
en: Forsooth, Pavana protects you out of friendship. It is, therefore, that, though possessed of numberless branches, you have still leaves and flowers.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: इदं च रमणीयं ते प्रतिभाति वनस्पते। यदिमे विहगास्तात रमन्ते मुदितास्त्वयि॥
en: O king of the forest, this your hue is delightful since these birds, O child, filled with joy, sport on your twigs and branches.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: एषा पृथक् समस्तानां श्रूयते मधुरस्वरः। पुष्पसम्मोदने काले वाशतां सुमनोहरम्॥
en: When you put forth your blossoms, the sweet notes of all these dwellers of your branches are heard separately when they sing their melodious songs.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: तथेमे गर्जिता नागा: स्वयूथकुलशोभिताः। धर्मास्त्विां समासाद्य सुखं विन्दन्ति शाल्मले॥
en: Again, O Shalmali, these most beautiful elephants, bathed in sweat and indulging in cries (of joy), approach you and enjoy happiness here.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: तथैव मृगजातीभिरन्याभिरभिशोभसे। तथा सर्वाधिवासैश्च शोभसे मेरुवद्रुम्॥
en: Similarly various other animals living in the woods, also adorn you. Indeed, O tree, you appear beautiful even like the mountains of Meru, peopled by all creatures.

description: The duty of a king when a neighbouring, but a powerful enemy is offended by him.
sn: ब्राह्मणैश्च तपःसिद्धेस्तापसैः श्रमणैस्तथा। त्रिविष्टपसमं मन्ये तवायतनमेव हि॥
en: Resorted to also by Brahmanas endued with ascetic success, by others engaged in penances, and by Yatis devoted to meditation this your region, I think, is like the celestial region itself.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: नारद उवाच बन्धुत्वादथवा सख्याच्छाल्मले नात्र संशयः। पालयत्येव सततं भीमः सर्वत्रगोऽनिलः॥
en: Narada said Forsooth, O Shalmali, the dreadful and irresistible god of wind always protects you friendliness.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: न्यग्भावं परमं वायोः शाल्मले त्वमुपागतः। तवाहमस्मीति सदा येन रक्षति मारुतः॥
en: It seems, O Shalmali, that a close intimacy exists between you and the Wind. It seems, you have said him these words, viz.,-I. am yours-and it is, therefore, that the Wind-god protects you.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: न तं पश्याम्यहं वृक्षं पर्वतं वेश्म चेदृशम्। यं न वायुबलाद् भग्नं पृथिव्यामिति मे मतिः॥
en: I do not see the tree or mountain or palace in this world which may not, I think, be broken by the Wind.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: त्वं पुनः कारणैनं रक्ष्यसे शाल्मले यथा। वायुना सपरीवारस्तेन तिष्ठस्यसंशयम्॥
en: Forsooth, you stand here with all your branches and twigs and leaves, simply because, O Shalmali, you are protected by the Wind for some reason or reasons (unknown to us)!

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: शाल्मलिरुवाच न मे वायुः सखा ब्रह्मन्न बन्धुर्न च सुहृत्। परमेष्ठी तथा नैव येन रक्षति वानिलः॥ मे
en: The Wind, O twice-born one, is either my friend nor companion nor well-wisher. Nor is he iny great Creator that he should protect me.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: मम तेजो बलं भीमं वायोरपि हि नारद। कलामष्टादशी प्राणैर्न मे प्राप्नोति मारुतः॥
en: My terrific energy and power, O Narada, are the greater than the Wind's. In sooth, the strength of the Wind is only an eighteenth part of mine.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: आगच्छन् परुषो वायुर्मया विष्टम्भितो बलात्। भञ्जन् दुमान् पर्वतांश्च यच्चान्यदपि किंचन॥
en: When the Wind blows fearfully, tearing up trees and mountains and other things, I abate his strength by displaying mine.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: स मया बहुशो भग्नः प्रभञ्जन् वै प्रभञ्जनः। तस्मान्न बिभ्ये देवर्षे क्रुद्धादपि समीरणात्॥
en: Indeed, the Wind that breaks many things has himself been again and agair broken by me. Therefore, O celestial Rishi, I am not afraid of him even when he comes in fury.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: नारद उवाच शाल्मले विपरीतं ते दर्शनं नात्र संशयः। न हि वायोर्बलेनास्ति भूतं तुल्यबलं क्वचित्॥
en: Narada said-O Shalmali, what you think seems to be quite the reverse of truth. There is no doubt in this. There is no created thing which is so strong as the Wind.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: इन्द्रो यमो वैश्रवणो वरुणश्च जलेश्वरः। नैतेऽपि तुल्या मरुतः किं पुनस्त्वं वनस्पते॥
en: Even Indra, Yama, Vaishravana, of Varuna the king of the waters, is not equal to the god of wind in might. What to speak of you who are only a tree.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: यच्च किंचिदिह प्राणी चेष्टते शाल्मले भुवि। सर्वत्र भगवान् वायुश्चेष्टाप्राणकरः प्रभुः॥
en: The illustrious Wind-god is always the root of all the acts of creatures in this world, since it is he that is the giver of life.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: एष चेश्यते सम्यक् प्राणिनः सम्यगायतः। असम्यगायतो भूयश्चेष्टते विकृतं नृषु॥
en: When the god does his work properly, he makes all living creatures live at their ease. When, however, he does it improperly, calamities visit the Earth.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: स त्वमेवंविधं वायुं सर्वसत्त्वभृतां वरम्। न पूजयसि पूज्यं तं किमन्यद् बुद्धिलाघवात्॥
