en: What else can it be but weakness of understanding which induces you not to adore the god of wind, that foremost of beings in the universe, and worthy of adoration.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: असारश्चापि दुर्मेधाः केवलं बहु भाषसे। क्रोधादिभिरवच्छन्नो मिथ्या वदसि शाल्मले॥
en: You are worthless and of a wicked understanding, you are but making an idleboast. Your intelligence being confounded by anger and other passions, you indulge in untruths, O Shalmali.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: मम रोषः समुत्पन्नस्त्वय्येवं सम्प्रभाषति। ब्रवीम्येष स्वयं वायोस्तव दुर्भाषितं बहु॥
en: I am certainly angry with you, for your giving vent to such words. I shall myself communicate to the Windgod all these derogatory words of yours.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: चन्दनैः स्यन्दनैः शालैः सरलैर्देवदारुभिः। वेतसैर्धन्वनैश्चापि ये चान्ये बलवत्तराः॥
en: Chandanas, Syandanas, Shalas, Saralas, Devadarus, Vetasas and Dhanvanas and other noble trees that are far stronger than you, have never, you of wicked understanding, spoken such evil words against the Wind.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: तैश्चापि नैवं दुर्बुद्धे क्षिप्तो वायुः कृतात्मभिः। तेऽपि जानन्ति वायोश्च बलमात्मन एव च॥ तस्मात् तं वै नमस्यन्ति श्वसनं तरुसत्तमाः।
en: All of them are cognisant of the power of the Wind as also the power that each of them possesses. For these reasons those foremost of trees respectfully salute that god.

description: The conversation between Narada and Shalmali
sn: त्वं तु मोहान्न जानीषे वायोर्बलमनन्तकम्। एवं तस्माद् गमिष्यामि सकाशं मातरिश्वनः॥
en: However, through folly, you are only unaware of the infinite power of the Wind, I shall, therefore, go to that god.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु राजेन्द्र शाल्मलिं ब्रह्मवित्तमः। नारदः पवने सर्वं शाल्मलेर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhishma said-Having said these words to the Shalmali, that foremost of all persons conversant with Brahma, viz., Narada, communicated to the Wind-god all that the Shalmali had said about him.

sn: नारद उवाच हिमवत्पृष्ठजः कश्चिच्छाल्मलिः परिवारवान्। बृहन्मूलो बृहच्छायः स त्वां वायोऽवमन्यते॥
en: Narada said There is a a certain Shalmali on the Himalaya, adorned with branches and leaves. His roots have gone deep into the Earth and its branches have spread wide around. That tree, O Wind-god, disrespects you.

sn: बहुव्याक्षेपयुक्तानि त्वामाह वचनानि सः। न युक्तानि मया वायो तानि वक्तुं तवाग्रतः॥
en: He spoke many insulting words against yourself. It is not meet, O Wind, that I should repeat them in your hearing.

sn: जानामि त्वामहं वायो सर्वप्राणभृतां वरम्। वरिष्ठं च गरिष्ठं च क्रोधे वैवस्वतं यथा॥
en: I know, O Wind, that you are greatest of all created things. I know too that you are a very superior and very powerful being, and that in anger you resemble the Destroyer himself.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एतत् तु वचनं श्रुत्वा नारदस्य समीरणः। शाल्मलिं तमुपागम्य क्रुद्धो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing these words of Narada, the Windgod going to that Shalmali, said to him angrily as follows.

sn: वायुरुवाच शाल्मले नारदो गच्छंस्त्वयोक्तो मद्विगर्हणम्। अहं वायुः प्रभावं ते दर्शयाम्यात्मनो बलम्॥
en: The Wind-god said O Shalmali, you have uttered derogatory words against me before Narada, know that I am the God of wind. I shall certainly show you my power and might.

sn: अहं त्वामभिजानामि विदितश्चासि मे दुम। पितामहः प्रजासर्गे त्वयि विश्रान्तवान् प्रभुः॥
en: I know you well. You are no stranger to me. While creating the world, the powerful Grandfather had for a time rested under you.

sn: तस्य विश्रमणादेष प्रसादो मत्कृतस्तव। रक्ष्यसे तेन दुर्बुद्धे नात्मवीर्याद् दुमाधम॥ यन्मां त्वमवजानीषे यथान्यं प्राकृतं तथा। दर्शयाम्येष चात्मानं यथा मां नावमन्यसे॥
en: For this incident I have hitherto shown you favour. O worst of trees, it is for this that you stand uninjured and not for your own power. You consider me lightly as if I were a vulgar thing. I shall, however, appear to you in such a way that you may not disrespect me again.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्तस्ततः प्राह शाल्मलिः प्रहसन्निव। पवन त्वं च मे क्रुद्धो दर्शयात्मानमात्मना॥
en: Thus addressed, the Shalmali laughed in contempt and replied, saying,-O Wind-god, you are angry with me. Do not stop showing the extent of your power.

sn: मयि वै त्यज्यतां क्रोधः किं मे क्रुद्धः करिष्यसि। न ते बिभेमि पवन यद्यपि त्वं स्वयं प्रभुः॥
en: Do you vomit all your anger upon me. By becoming angry, what will you do to me? Even if your power had been all your own, I would not still have been afraid of you. I am superior to you in power. I am not afraid of you.

sn: बलाधिकोऽहं त्वत्तश्च न भी: कार्या मया तव। ये तु बुद्ध्या हि बलिनस्ते भवन्ति बलीयसः॥
en: Those who are strong in understanding are strong in reality. Those who endued with only physical strength are not to be regarded strong.

sn: प्राणमात्रबला ये वै नैव ते बलिनो मताः। इत्येवमुक्तः पवनः श्व इत्येवाब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: Thus addressed, the Wind-god said,Tomorrow I shall test your strength,Thereafter night came.

sn: दर्शयिष्यामि ते तेजस्ततो रात्रिरुपागमत्। अथ निश्चित्य मनसा शाल्मलिर्वातकारितम्॥
en: Determining in his mind the extent of the Wind's might and seeing his ownself to be inferior to the god, the Shalmali began to say aside,

sn: पश्यमानस्तदाऽऽत्मानमसमं मातरिश्वना। नारदे यन्मया प्रोक्तं वचनं प्रति तन्मृषा॥
en: All that I said to Narada is untrue. I am, forsooth, inferior in power to the Wind. Verily, he is superior in strength.

sn: असमर्थो ह्यहं वायोर्बलेन बलवान् हि सः। मारुतो बलवान् नित्यं यथा वै नारदोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: The Wind, as Narada said, is always powerful. Forsooth, I am weaker than other trees.

sn: अहं तु दुर्बलोऽन्येभ्यो वृक्षेभ्यो नात्र संशयः। किं तु बुद्ध्या समो नास्ति मया कश्चिद् वनस्पतिः।।१७।
en: But in intelligence no tree is equal to me. Therefore, depending upon my intelligence I shall view this fear which arises from the wind.

sn: तदहं बुद्धिमास्थाय भयं मोक्ष्ये समीरणात्। यदि तां बुद्धिमास्थाय तिष्ठेयुः पर्णिनो वने॥
en: If the other trees in the forest all depend upon the same kind of intelligence, then, no injury can come to them from the Wind-god when he is irate.

sn: अरिष्टाः स्युः सदा क्रुद्धात् पवनान्नात्र संशयः। ते तु बाला न जानन्ति यथा वै तान् समीरणः। समीरयति संक्रुद्धो यथा जानाम्यहं तथा॥
en: All of them, however, are shorn of understanding, and, therefore, they do not know, as I know, why or how the Wind succeeds in shaking and tearing them up.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो निश्चित्य मनसा शाल्मलिः क्षुभितस्तदा। शाखा: स्कन्धान प्रशाखाश्च स्वयमेव व्यशातयत्॥
en: Bhishma said Having thus deterinined, the Shalmali, himself sorrowfully caused all his branches, man and minor, to be cut off.

sn: स परित्यज्य शाखाश्च पत्राणि कुसुमानि च। प्रभाते वायुमायान्तं प्रत्यक्षत वनस्पतिः॥
en: Casting off his branches, leaves and flowers, in the morning the tree looked firmly at the Wind as he came towards him.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धः श्वसन् वायुः पातयन् व महादुमान्। आजगामाथ तं देशमास्ते यत्र स शाल्मलिः॥
en: Filled with anger and breathing hard, the Wind came, felling large trees, where the Shalmali stood.

sn: तं हीनपर्णं पतिताग्रशाखं निशीर्णपुष्पं प्रसमीक्ष्य वायुः। उवाच वाक्यं स्मयमान एवं मुदा युतः शाल्मलिमुग्रशाखम्॥
en: Seeing him divested of top, branches, leaves and flowers, the Wind, filled with joy, smilingly said to that lord of the forest which had before such a huge appearance.

sn: वायुरुवाच अहमप्येवमेव त्वां कुर्वाण: शाल्मले रुषा। आत्मना यत्कृतं कृच्छ्रे शाखानामपकर्षणम्॥
en: The Wind said-Filled with anger, O Shalmali, I would have done to you exactly what you have done to yourself by cutting off all your branches.

sn: हीनपुष्पाग्रशाखस्त्वं शीर्णाकुरपलाशकः। आत्मदुर्मन्त्रितेनेह मद्वीर्यवशगः कृतः॥
en: You are now shorn of your proud top and flowers, and you are now without your shoots and leaves. For your own bad counsels, you have been brought under my control.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचो वायोः शाल्मलिीडितस्तदा। अतप्यत वचः स्मृत्वा नारदो यत् तदाब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing these words of the Wind, the Shalmali feit great shame. Remembering also the words of Narada, he began to repent greatly for his mistake.

sn: एवं हि राजशार्दूल दुर्बलः सन् बलीयसा। वैरमारभते बालस्तप्यते शाल्मलिर्यथा॥ तस्माद् वैरं न कुर्वीत दुर्बलो बलवत्तरैः। शोचेद्धि वैरं कुर्वाणो यथा वै शाल्मलिस्तथा॥
en: Thus, O foremost of kings, a weak and foolish person, by exciting the enmity of a powerful enemy, is at last compelled to repent like the Shalmali in story. Therefore, a weak person should not behave hostility with a strong person.

sn: न हि वैरं महात्मानो विवृण्वन्त्यपकारिषु। शनैः शनैर्महाराज दर्शयन्ति स्म ते बलम्॥
en: Even when gifted with equal might, people do not suddenly create enmities with those who have injured them. On the other hand, they show their power gradually, O king.

sn: वैरं न कुर्वीत नरो दुर्बुद्धिर्बुद्धिजीविना। बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतो याति तृणेष्विव हुताशनः॥
en: A foolish person should never excite the hostility of an intelligent person. In such cases the intelligence of the intelligent man works like fire penetrating a heap of dry grass.

sn: न हि बुद्ध्या समं किंचिद् विद्यते पुरुषे नृप। तथा बलेन राजेन्द्र न समोऽस्तीह कश्चन॥
en: Intelligence is the most valuable thing that a person can have. Likewise, O king, a man can have nothing here more valuable than power.

sn: तस्मात् क्षमेत बालाय जडान्धबधिराय च। बलाधिकाय राजेन्द्र तद् दृष्टं त्वयि शत्रुहन्॥
en: One should, therefore, pass over the wrongs inflicted by a person possessed of superior strength, as one should overlook the acts of a child, an idiot, or one who is blind or deaf. The wisdom of this saying is seen in your case, O slayer of foes.

sn: अक्षौहिण्यो दशैका च सप्त चैव महाद्युते। बलेन न समा राजन्नर्जुनस्य महात्मनः॥
en: The eleven Akshauhinis (of Duryodhana), and the seven (collected by yourself), were not, in power, equal to the single-handed Arjuna of great soul.

sn: निहताश्चैव भग्नाश्च पाण्डवेन यशस्विना। चरत बलमास्थाय पाकशासनिना मृधे॥
en: All the troops (of Duryodhana), therefore, were dispersed and killed by that illustrious Pandava, that son of Paka's chastiser, as he moved about in the field of battle, depending on his own strength.

sn: उक्ताश्च ते राजधर्मा आपद्धर्माश्च भारत। विस्तरेण महाराज किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: I have, O Bharata, described to you the duties of kings and ethics of con-in detail. What else, O king, do you wish to hear.

sn: निहताश्चैव भग्नाश्च पाण्डवेन यशस्विना। चरत बलमास्थाय पाकशासनिना मृधे॥
en: All the troops (of Duryodhana), therefore, were dispersed and killed by that illustrious Pandava, that son of Paka's chastiser, as he moved about in the field of battle, depending on his own strength.

sn: उक्ताश्च ते राजधर्मा आपद्धर्माश्च भारत। विस्तरेण महाराज किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: I have, O Bharata, described to you the duties of kings and ethics of con-in detail. What else, O king, do you wish to hear.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पापस्य यदधिष्ठानं यतः पापं प्रवर्तते। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तत्त्वेन भरतर्षभ॥
en: Yudhishthira said-I wish, O foremost of Bharata's race, to hear fully the source from which sin proceeds and the basis upon which it depends.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: भीष्म उवाच पापस्य यदधिष्ठानं तच्छृणुष्व नराधिप। एको लोभो महाग्राहो लोभात् पापं प्रवर्तते॥
en: Bhishma said Hear, O king, what is the origin of sin! Covetousness alone is a great destroyer. From covetousness originates sin.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: अतः पापमधर्मश्च तथा दुःखमनुत्तमम्। निकृत्या मूलमेतद्धि येन पापकृतो जनाः॥
en: Sin and impiety proceed from this source, along with great misery. This covetousness is the root of also all the cunning and hypocrisy in the world. It is covetousness that makes men perpetrate sin.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: लोभात् क्रोधः प्रभवति लोभात् कामः प्रवर्तते। लोभान्मोहच माया च मानः स्तम्भः परासुता॥ अक्षमा ह्रीपरित्यागः श्रीनाशो धर्मसंक्षयः। अभिध्याप्रख्यता चैव सर्वं लोभात् प्रवर्तते॥
en: From covetousness originates anger, from covetousness grows lust; and it is covetousness which begets loss of judgement, decision, pride, haughtiness, malice, vindictiveness shamelessness, loss of prosperity, loss of virtue, anxiety, and infamy.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: अत्यागश्चातितर्षश्च विकर्मसु च याः क्रियाः। कुलविद्यामदश्चैव रूपैश्वर्यमदस्तथा॥ सर्वभूतेष्वभिद्रोहः सर्वभूतेष्वसत्कृतिः। सर्वभूतेष्वविश्वासः सर्वभूतेष्वनार्जवम्॥ हरणं परवित्तानां परदाराभिमर्शनम्। वाग्वेगो मनसो वेगो निन्दावेगस्तथैव च॥ उपस्थोदरयोर्वेगो मृत्युवेगश्च दारुणः। ईर्ष्यावेगश्च बलवान् मिथ्यावेगश्च दुर्जयः॥ रसवेगश्च दुर्वार्यः श्रोत्रवेगश्च दुःसहः। कुत्सा विकत्था मात्सर्यं पापं दुष्करकारिता॥
en: Covetousness also begets miserliness, cupidity, inclination for every sort of improper deed, pride of birth, pride of learning, pride of beauty, pride of riches, mercilessness for all creatures, malevolence towards all, trustlessness in respect of all, insincerity towards all, appropriation of other people's property, ravishment of other people's wives, harshness of speech, anxiety, desire to speak ill of others, strong lustful desire, gluttony, liability to premature death, strong inclination to malice, strong desire for falsehood, irrepressible desire for indulging the passions, insatiable desire for indulging the ear, evilspeaking, bostfulness, arrogance, neglect of duties, rashness, and perpetration of every kind of evil deed.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: साहसानां च सर्वेषामकार्याणां क्रियास्तथा। जातौ बाल्ये च कौमारे यौवने चापि मानवाः॥
en: Men are unable, whether infants or youths or men, to cast off covetousness in life. Such is the nature of covetousness that it never disappears even with the loss of life.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: न संत्यजन्त्यात्मकर्म यो न जीर्यति जीर्यतः। यो न पूरयितुं शक्यो लोभः प्राप्त्या कुरूद्वह॥
en: Like the ocean that can never be filled by the continued flow of even numberless rivers of immeasurable depths, covetousness is incapable of being conquered by any number of acquisitions.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: नित्यं गम्भीरतोयाभिरापगाभिरिवोदधिः। न प्रहृष्यति यो लाभैः कामैर्यश्च न तृष्यति॥ यों न देवैर्न गन्धर्नासुरैर्न महोरगैः। ज्ञायते नृप तत्त्वेन सर्वैर्भूतगणैस्तथा॥
en: That covetousness, however, which is never satisfied by acquisitions and satiated by the fulfilment of desires, that the real nature of which is not known to the gods, the Gandharvas, the Asuras, the great snakes, and, in fact, to all beings, that irresistible passion, together with that foolishness which draws the heart to the unrealities of the world, should always be conquered by a person of purified soul.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: स लोभः सह मोहेन विजेतव्यो जितात्मना। दम्भो द्रोहश्च निन्दा च पैशुन्यं मत्सरस्तथा॥
en: Pride, malice, slander, wiliness and incapacity to hear other people's good, are vices, O Kuru chief, that are to be seen in persons of impure soul under the influence of covetousness.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: भवन्त्येतानि कौरव्य लुब्धानामकृतात्मनाम्। सुमहान्त्यपि शास्त्राणि धारयन्ति बहुश्रुताः॥
en: Even highly learned men who recollect all the scriptures, and who are capable of removing the doubts of others, appear very weak in this matter and feel great misery for this passion.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: छेत्तारः संशयानां च क्लिश्यन्तीहाल्पबुद्धयः। द्वेषक्रोधप्रसक्ताश्च शिष्टाचारबहिष्कृताः॥ अन्तःक्रूरा वाङ्मधुराः कूपाश्छन्नास्तृणैरिवा
en: Covetous men are swayed by malice and spite. They are beyond the range of good conduct. Wily as they are in their hearts, their speeches are sweet. They are like dark pits whose mouths are covered with grass.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: धर्मवैतं सिकाः क्षुद्रा मुष्णन्ति ध्वजिनो जगत्॥ कुर्वते च बहून् मार्गांस्तान् हेतुबलमाश्रिताः। सतां मार्गान् विलुम्पन्ति लोभाज्ञानेषु निष्ठिताः॥
en: They dress themselves in the hypocritical garb of religion, Low minded as they are, they rob the world, showing the standard of religion and virtue. Depending upon the strength of palpable reasons, they create various divisions in religion. Being anxious to serve cupidity, they destroy the ways of righteousness.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: धर्मस्य ह्रियमाणस्य लोभग्रस्तैर्दुरात्मभिः। या या विक्रियते संस्था ततः सापि प्रपद्यते॥
en: When wicked men under the influence of covetousness practise for the inere show of righteousness, the result is that the desecrations committed by them, soon become current among men.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: दर्पः क्रोधो मदः स्वप्नो हर्षः शोकोऽतिमानिता। एव एव हि कौरव्य दृश्यन्ते लुब्धबुद्धिषु॥
en: Pride, anger, arrogance, insensibility, fits of joy and sorrow, and self-conceit, all these, O descendant of Kuru, are to be seen in persons under the influence of covetousness.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: एतानशिष्टान् बुध्यस्व नित्यं लोभसमन्वितान्। शिष्टांस्तु परिपृच्छेथा यान् वक्ष्यामि शुचिव्रतान्॥
en: They who are always under the influence of covetousness are wicked. I shall now tell you of those about whom you ask,—those who are called good and whose practices are pure.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: येष्वावृत्तिभयं नास्ति परलोकभयं न च। नामिषेषु प्रसंगोऽस्ति न प्रियेष्वप्रियेषु च॥ शिष्टाचारः प्रियो येषु दमो येषु प्रतिष्ठितः। सुखं दुःखं समं येषां सत्यं येषां परायणम्॥ दातारो न ग्रहीतारो दयावन्तस्तथैव च। पितृदेवातिथेयाश्च नित्योधुक्तास्तथैव च॥ सर्वोपकारिणो वीराः सर्वधर्मानुपालकाः। सर्वभूतहिताश्चैव सर्वदेयाश्च भारत॥
en: They who fear no obligation of returning to this world (after death), they who have no fear of the next world, they who do not take animal food and who have no liking for what is agreeable and no dislike for what is otherwise, they to whom good conduct is always dear, they who practise self-restraint, they who consider pleasure and pain as same, they who have truth for their refuge, they who give but not take, they who have mercy, they who adore, Pitris, gods, and guests, they who are always ready to work (for the behoof of others), they who are universal benefactors, they who are endued with great courage (of mind), they who follow all the duties sanctioned by the scriptures, they who are devoted to the well-being of all, they who can give their all and sacrifice their very lives for others, are considered as good and virtuous, O Bharata.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: न ते चालयितुं शक्या धर्मव्यापारकारिणः। न तेषां भिद्यते वृत्तं यत्पुरा साधुभिः कृतम्॥
en: Those promoters of virtue cannot be seduced from the path of virtue. Their conduct, in imitation of that of virtuous men of yore, can never be otherwise.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: न त्रासिनो न चपला न रौद्राः सत्पथे स्थिताः। ते सेव्याः साधुभिर्नित्यं येष्वहिंसा प्रतिष्ठिता॥
en: They are perfectly fearless; they are tranquil; they are mild; and they always follow the right path. Full of mercy, they are always adored by the good.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: कामक्रोधव्यपेता ये निर्ममा निरहंकृताः। सुव्रताः स्थिरमर्यादास्तानुपास्व च पृच्छ च॥
en: They are free from lust and anger. They are not attached to any worldly object. They have no pride. They observe excellent vows. They always command respect. Do you, therefore, always attend them and seek instruction from them.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: न धनार्थं यशोऽर्थं वा धर्मस्तेषां युधिष्ठिर। अवश्यं कार्य इत्येव शरीरस्य क्रियास्तथा।॥
en: They never acquire virtue, O Yudhishthira, for the sake of riches or of fame. They acquire error it only, because they know it as a duty like that of supporting the body.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: न भयं क्रोधचापल्ये न शोकस्तेषु विद्यते। न धर्मध्वजिनश्चैव न गुह्यं कञ्चिदास्थिताः॥
en: Fear, anger, restlessness, and sorrow do not live in them. They carry no external garb of religion for misleading their fellow-men. They observe no mystery.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: येष्वलोभस्तथामोहो ये च सत्यार्जवे स्थिताः। तेषु कौन्तेय रज्येथा येषां न भ्रश्यते पुनः॥
en: They are perfectly contended. They have of judgement originating from covetousness. They always follow truth and sincerity. Their hearts never deviate from righteousness. You should always respect them, O son of Kunti!

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: ये न हृष्यन्ति लाभेषु नालाभेषु व्यथन्ति च। निर्ममा निरहंकाराः सत्त्वस्थाः समदर्शिनः॥
en: They are never overjoyed at any acquisition or pained at any loss. Without being attached to anything, and shorn of pride, they are devoted to the quality of Goodness, and they regard all impartially.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: लाभालाभौ सुखदुःखे च तात प्रियाप्रिये मरणं जीवितं च। समानि येषां स्थिरविक्रमाणां बुभुत्सतां सत्त्वपथे स्थितानाम्॥
en: Gain and loss, happiness and misery, the agreeable and the disagreeable, life and death, are held in equal estimation by those men of firm mind, engaged in acquiring (divine) knowledge, and wending the path of tranquility and righteousness.

description: The source and basis of sin
sn: धर्मप्रियांस्तान्सुमहानुभावान् दान्तोऽप्रमत्तश्च समर्चयेथाः। दैवान्सर्वे गुणवन्तो भवन्ति शुभाशुभे वाक्प्रलापास्तथान्ये॥
en: Keeping your senses under control and without yielding to carelessness, you should always adore those great persons who bear such love for virtue. O blessed one, one's words always yield good only through the favour of the gods. Under other circumstances, words beget evil consequence. words always yield good only through the favour of the gods. Under other circumstances, words beget evil consequence.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अनर्थानामधिष्ठानमुक्तो लोभः पितामह। अज्ञानमपि वै तात श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have said, O grandfather, that the root of all evils is covetousness. I wish, O sire, to licar fully of ignorance.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: भीष्म उवाच करोति पापं योऽज्ञानानात्मनो वेत्ति च क्षयम्। प्रद्वेष्टि साधुवृत्तांश्च स लोकस्यैति वाच्यताम्॥
en: Bhishma said The person who commits sin out of ignorance, who does not know that his end is near, and who always hates persons of good conduct, soon incurs infamy in the world.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: अज्ञानान्निरयं याति तथाज्ञानेन दुर्गतिम्। अज्ञानात् क्लेशमाप्नोति तथापत्सु निमज्जति॥
en: In consequence of ignorance one goes to hell. Ignorance one suffers miseries and incurs great danger.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अज्ञानस्य प्रवृत्तिं च स्थानं वृद्धिक्षयोदयौ। मूलं योगं गतिं कालं कारणं हेतुमेव च॥ श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वेन यथावदिह पार्थिव। अज्ञानप्रसवं हीदं यद् दुःखमुपलभ्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said I wish, O king, to hear fully the origin, the place, the growth, the decay, the rise, the root, the attribute, the course, the time, the cause, and the result of ignorance. The misery that is felt here is the outcome of ignorance.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: रागो द्वेषस्तथा मोहो हर्षः शोकोऽभिमानिता। कामः क्रोधश्च दर्पश्च तन्द्री चालस्यमेव च॥ इच्छा द्वेषस्तथा तापः परवृद्ध्युपतापिता। अज्ञानमेतन्निर्दिष्टं पापानां चैव याः क्रियाः॥
en: Bhishma said Attachment, hate, loss of judgement, joy, sorrow, vanity, lust, anger, pride, procrastination, idleness, desire, aversion, jealousy, envy, and all other sinful habits pass by the common name of ignorance.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: एतस्य वा प्रवृत्तेश्च वृद्ध्यादीन्यांश्च पृच्छसि। विस्तरेण महाराज शृणु तच्च विशेषतः॥
en: Hear fully now, O king, about its nature, growth and other characteristics after which you enquire.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: उभावेतौ समफलौ समदोषौ च भारत। अज्ञानं चातिलोभश्चाप्येकं जानीहि पार्थिव॥
en: These two, viz., ignorance and covetousness, know, O king, are the same. Both produce the same fruits and same faults, O Bharata.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: लोभप्रभवमज्ञानं वृद्धं भूयः प्रवर्धते। स्थाने स्थानं क्षये क्षैण्यमुपैति विविधां गतिम्॥
en: Ignorance originates from covetousness. Ignorance grows along with coveteousness. Ignorance exists simultaneously with covetousness. Ignorance decreases with covetousness. It rises with the rise of covetousness. Manifold again is its course.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: मूलं लोभस्य मोहो वै कालात्मगतिरेव च। छिन्ने भिन्ने तथा लोभे कारणं काल एव च॥ तस्याज्ञानाद्धि लोभो हि लोभादज्ञानमेव च। सर्वदोषास्तथा लोभात् तस्माल्लोभंविवर्जयेत्॥
en: The root of covetousness is loss of judgement. Loss of judgement, again, is its inseparable quality. Eternity is ignorance's course. The time when ignorance occurs is when the objects of covetousness are not gained.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: जनको युवनाश्वच वृषादर्भिः प्रसेनजित्। लोभक्षयाद् दिवं प्राप्तास्तथैवान्ये नराधिपाः॥
en: From ignorance proceeds covetousness, and from the latter proceeds ignorance. Covetousness produces all faults. For these reasons every one should avoid covetousness. Janaka, Yuvanashva, Vrishadarbhi, Prasenajit, and other kings acquired heaven for their having conquered covetousness.

description: Covetousness is the root of all evils
sn: प्रत्यक्षं तु कुरुश्रेष्ठ त्यज लोभमिहात्मना। त्यक्त्वा लोभं सुखं लोके प्रेत्य चानुचरिष्यसि॥
en: Do you before all persons, avoid covetousness by a strong determination, O Kuru chief. Avoiding covetousness you will acquire happiness both here and in the next world.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच स्वाध्याये कृतयत्नस्य नरस्य च पितामह। धर्मकामस्य धर्मात्मन् किं नु श्रेय इहोच्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O you of virtuous soul, what, indeed, yields great merit for a person assiduously engaged in the study of the Vedas and desirous of gaining virtue.

sn: बहुधा दर्शने लोके श्रेयो यदिह मन्यसे। अस्मिल्लोके परे चैव तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: That which yields in this world high merit is of various kinds as described in the scriptures. Tell me, O grandfather, about what is regarded as such both in this world and in the next.

sn: महानयं धर्मपथो बहुशाखश्च भारत। किंस्विदेवेह धर्माणामनुष्ठेयतमं मतम्॥
en: The path of duty is long and has numberless branches, O Bharata. Amongst those duties what are those few which should, in your opinion, be observed in preference to all others?

sn: धर्मस्यो महतो राजन् बहुशाखस्य तत्त्वतः। यन्मूलं परमं तात तत् सर्वं ब्रूह्यशेषतः॥
en: Tell me, O king, fully about that which is so vast and which has so many branches.

sn: भीष्म उवाच हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि येन श्रेयो ह्यवाप्स्यसि। पीत्वामृतमिव प्राज्ञो ज्ञानतृप्तो भविष्यसि॥
en: Bhishma said I shall describe to you that by which you may acquire high merit. Wise as you are, you will be satisfied with the knowledge I will impart to you, like a person gratified with having drunk ambrosia.

sn: धर्मस्य विधयो नैके ये वै प्रोक्ता महर्षिभिः। स्वं स्वं विज्ञानमाश्रित्य दमस्तेषां परायणम्॥
en: The rules of duty described by the great Rishis, each depending upon his own wisdom, are many. The highest among them all is selfcontrol.

sn: दमं निःश्रेयसं प्राहुर्वृद्धा निश्चितदर्शिनः। ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेण दमो धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: Those amongst the ancient Rishis that were acquainted with truth said that self-control, leads to the highest merit. Self-control is the eternal duty of the Brahmanas especially.

sn: दमात् तस्य क्रियासिद्धिर्यथावदुपलभ्यते। दमो दानं तथा यज्ञानधीतं चातिवर्तते॥
en: It is from self-control that he acquires the due fruition of his acts. Self-control of surpasses (in merit) charity and sacrifice and study of the Vedas.

sn: दमस्तेजो वर्धयति पवित्रं च दम: परम्। विपाप्मा तेजसा युक्तः पुरुषो विन्दते महत्॥
en: Self-control increases (his) energy. Selfcontrol is highly sacred. Through self-control a man becomes purified of all his sins and gifted with energy, and therefore, acquires the highest blessedness.

sn: दमेन सदृशं धर्मं नान्यं लोकेषु शुश्रुम। दमो हि परमो लोके प्रशस्तः सर्वधर्मिणाम्॥
en: We have not heard that there is any other duty in all the worlds equal to self-control. Self-control, according to all virtuous persons, is the highest virtues in this world.

sn: प्रेत्य चात्र मनुष्येन्द्र परमं विन्दते सुखम्। दमेन हि समायुक्तो महान्तं धर्ममश्नुते॥
en: Through self-control, O foremost of men, a person enjoys the highest happiness both in this world and in the next. Gifted with self-control, one wins great virtue.

sn: सुखं दान्तः प्रस्वपिति सुखं च प्रतिबुध्यते। सुखं पर्येति लोकांश्च मनश्चास्य प्रसीदति॥
en: The self-controlled man sleeps in happiness and awakes in happiness, and moves through the world in happiness. His mind is always cheerful.

sn: अदान्तः पुरुषः क्लेशमभीक्ष्णं प्रतिपद्यते। अनर्थांश्च बहूनन्यान् प्रसृजत्यात्मदोषजान्॥
en: The man who is without self-control always suffers misery. Such a man brings upon himself many calamities all begotten by his own faults.

sn: आश्रमेषु चतुर्बाहुर्दममेवोत्तमं व्रतम्। तस्य लिङ्गानि वक्ष्यामि येषां समुदयो दमः॥
en: It has been said that in all the four modes of life self-control is the best of vows. I shall now describe to you the characteristic marks the sum-total of which is called self-control.

sn: क्षमा धृतिरहिंसा च समता सत्यमार्जवम्। इन्द्रियाभिजयो दाक्ष्यं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्॥ अकार्पण्यमसंरम्भः संतोषः प्रियवादिता। अविहिंसानसूया चाप्येषां समुदयो दमः॥
en: Forgiveness, patience, abstention from injury, impartiality, truth, sincerity, control of the senses, cleverness, mildness, modesty, firmness, liberality, freedom from anger, contentment, sweetness of words, benevolence, freedom from malice, all these combined make up self-control.

sn: गुरुपूजा च कौरव्य दया भूतेष्वपैशुनम्। जनवादं मृषावादं स्तुतिनिन्दाविसर्जनम्॥ कामं क्रोधं च लोभं च दर्प स्तम्भं विकत्थनम्। रोषमीया॑वमानं च नैव दान्तो निषेवते॥
en: It also consists, O son of Kuru, of respect for the preceptor and mercy for all. The selfcontrolled man avoids both adulation and slander. Depravity, infamy, falsehood, lust, covetousness, pride, arrogance, self-edification, fear, envy, and disrespect, are all shunned by the self-controlled man.

sn: अनिन्दितो ह्यकामात्मा नाल्पेष्वर्थ्यनसूयकः। समुद्रकल्पः स नरो न कथंचन पूर्यते॥
en: He never incurs obloquy. He is free from envy. He is never satisfied with trivial acquisitions. He is like the ocean which can never be filled.

sn: अहं त्वयि मयि त्वं च मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्। पूर्वसम्बन्धिसंयोग नैतद् दान्तो निषेवते॥
en: The self-controlled man is never fettered by the attachments originating from earthly connections and sentiments like these,-'I am yours, You are yours. They are in me, and I am in them.

sn: सर्वा ग्राम्यास्तथाऽऽरण्या याश्च लोके प्रवृत्तयः। निन्दां चैव प्रशंसां च यो नाश्रयति मुच्यते॥
en: Such a man who follows the practices of either cities or the woods, and who never vilifies others nor indulges in adulation, acquires liberation.

sn: मैत्रोऽथ शीलसम्पन्नः प्रसन्नात्माऽऽत्मविच्च यः। मुक्तस्य विविधैः सङ्गैस्तस्य प्रेत्य फलं महत्॥
en: Practising universal friendliness, and virtuous conduct, and possessed of cheerful spirit and psychic knowledge, and freed from the various attachments of the Earth, a person acquires great reward in the next world.

sn: सुवृत्तः शीलसम्पन्नः प्रसन्नात्माऽऽत्मविद् बुधः। प्राप्येह लोके सत्कारं सुगति प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Of excellent behaviour and observant of duties, cheerful and endued with learning and knowledge of self, such a man acquires esteem while in this world and attains to a high end hereafter.

sn: कर्म यच्छुभमेवेह सद्भिराचरितं च यत्। तदेव ज्ञानयुक्तस्य मुनेवर्त्म न हीयते॥
en: All acts that are considered as good on Earth,-all those acts that are practised by the righteous, form the path of the ascetic endued with knowledge. A person that is good never transgresses that path.

sn: निष्क्रम्य वनमास्थाय ज्ञानयुक्तो जितेन्द्रियः। कालाकाङ्क्षी चरत्येवं ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते॥
en: Retiring from the world, and living in the woods, that learned person, having a complete mastery over the senses who treads in that path, expecting his own demise, is sure to acquire the state of Brahma.

sn: अभयं यस्य भूतेभ्यो भूतानामभयं यतः। तस्य देहाद् विमुक्तस्य भयं नास्ति कुतश्चन॥
en: He who has no fear of any creature, and whom no creature fears, has, after, the dissolution of his body, no fear to meet.

sn: अवाचिनोति कर्माणि न च सम्प्रचिनोति ह। समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मैत्रायणगतिश्चरेत्॥
en: He who exhausts his merits without trying to hoard them up, who considers all creatures equally and cherishes friendship for the entire universe, attains to Brahma.

sn: शकुनीनामिवाकाशे जले वारिचरस्य च। यथा गतिर्न दृश्येत तथा तस्य न संशयः॥
en: As the route of birds along the sky or of fowl over the surface of water cannot be made out, so the path of such a person (on Earth) does not attract notice.

sn: गृहानुत्सृज्य यो राजन् मोक्षमेवाभिपद्यते। लोकास्तेजोमयास्तस्य कल्पन्ते शाश्वतीः समाः॥
en: O king, many bright worlds await him for eternal enjoyment, who renouncing his domestic life, adopts the religious course of emancipation. acts,

sn: संन्यस्य सर्वकर्माणि संन्यस्य विधिवत्तपः। संन्यस्य विविधा विद्याः सर्वं संन्यस्य चैव ह॥ कामे शुचिरनावृत्तः प्रसन्नात्माऽऽत्मविच्छुचिः। प्राप्येह लोके सत्कारं स्वर्ग समभिपद्यते॥
en: If abandoning all abandoning penances in due time, leaving off the various branches of study, in fact, leaving off all things, one becomes pure in his desires, freed from all restraints, of cheerful soul, conversant with self, and of pure heart, he then acquires esteem in this world and at last attains to heaven.

sn: यच्च पैतामहं स्थानं ब्रह्मराशिसमुद्भवम्। गुहायां पिहितं नित्यं तद् दमेनाभिगम्यते॥
en: That eternal region of the grandfather which originates from Vedic penances, and which is concealed in a cave, can only be acquired by self-control.

sn: ज्ञानारामस्य बुद्धस्य सर्वभूताविरोधिनः। नावृत्तिभयमस्तीह परलोकभयं कुतः॥
en: He who finds pleasure in true knowledge, who has become enlightened, and who never injures any creature, has no fear of returning to this world, not to speak of any fear from the other.

sn: एक दव दमे दोषो द्वितीयो नोपपद्यते। यदेनं क्षमया युक्तमशक्तं मन्यते जनः॥
en: There is only one fault in self-control. No second fault is seen in it. A person who has self-control is considered by men as weak and imbecile.

sn: एकोऽस्य सुमहाप्राज्ञः दोषः स्यात् सुमहान् गुणः। क्षमया विपुला लोकाः सुलभा हि सहिष्णुता।॥
en: you of great wisdom, this attribute has only one defect. Its merits are many. By forgiveness, the man of self-control may easily acquire numberless worlds.

sn: दान्तस्य किमरण्येन तथाऽदान्तस्य भारत। यत्रैव निवसेद् दान्तस्तदरण्यं स चाश्रमः॥
en: Of what use is forest to a man of selfcontrol. Likewise, O Bharata, of what use is the forest to him that has no self-control? That is a forest where the man of self-control lives, and that is even a sacred asylum.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतद् भीष्मस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा युधिष्ठिरः। अमृतेनेव संतृप्तः प्रहृष्टः समपद्यत॥
en: Hearing these words of Bhishina, Yudhishthira became highly pleased as if he had drunk nectar.

sn: पुनश्च परिपप्रच्छ भीष्मं धर्मभृतां वरम्। तपः प्रति स चोवाच तस्मै सर्वं कुरूद्वह॥
en: Again the king asked that foremost of virtuous men. That perpetuator of Kuru's race once more began to discourse cheerfully on the subject.

sn: भीष्म उवाच सर्वमेतत् तपोमूलं कवयः परिचक्षते। न ह्यतप्ततपा मूढः क्रियाफलमवाप्नुते॥
en: Bhishma said They who arc endued with knowledge say that everything springs from penance. That foolish person who has not practised penances does not get the rewards of even his own acts.

sn: प्रजापतिरिदं सर्वं तपसैवासृजत् प्रभुः। तथैव वेदानृषयस्तपसा प्रतिपेदिरे॥
en: The powerful Creator created all this universe with the help of penances. In ihe same way, the Rishis won ihe Vedas by the power of penanccs.

sn: तपसैव ससर्जानं फलमूलानि यानि च। त्रील्लोकांस्तपसा सिद्धाः पश्यन्ति सुसमाहिताः॥
en: It was by the help of penances that the Grandfather created food, fruits and roots. It is one by penances that ascetics behold the three worlds, with enraptured souls.

sn: औषधान्यगदादीनि क्रियाश्च विविधास्तथा। तपसैव हि सिद्ध्यन्ति तपोमूलं हि साधनम्॥
en: Medicines and all antidotes to poisonous articles, and the various acts (seen here), produce their intended results through the help of penance. The fulfilment of all purposes depends upon penance.

sn: यद् दुरापं भवेत् किंचित् तत्सर्वं तपसो भवेत्। ऐश्वर्यमृषयः प्राप्तास्तपसैव न संशयः॥
en: Whatever things there are which seem to be unattainable are sure to be acquired by penance. forsooth, the Rishis acquired their sixfold divine attributes through penance.

sn: सुरापोऽसम्मतादायी भ्रूणहा गुरुतल्पगः। तपसैव सुतप्तेन नरः पापात् प्रमुच्यते॥
en: A person who takes intoxicating liquors, who appropriates others' properties without their consent, one guilty of foeticide, one who violates his preceptor's bed, are all purified by penance duly performed.

sn: तपसो बहुरूपस्य तैस्तैारैः प्रवर्ततः। निवृत्या वर्तमानस्य तपो नानशनात् परम्॥
en: Penances manifold. They throw themselves through various channels. Of all sorts of penance, however, that one may practise after abstaining from pleasure and enjoyment, abstention from food is the greatest and best.

sn: अहिंसा सत्यवचनं दानमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः। एतेभ्यो हि महाराज तपो नानशनात् परम्॥
en: The penance of abstention from food is superior, O king, even to mercy, truthfulness, gifts, and restraint of senses.

sn: न दुष्करतरं दानान्नातिमातरमाश्रयः। विद्यभ्यः परं नास्ति संन्यासः परमं तपः॥
en: There is not act more hard to perform than gift. There is no mode of life which is superior to serving one's mother. There is no creature are superior to those who are conversant with the three Vedas. Likewise, Renunciation is the highest penance.

sn: इन्द्रियाणीह रक्षन्ति स्वर्गधर्माभिगुप्तये। तस्मादर्थे च धर्मे च तपो नानशनात् परम्॥
en: People restrain their senses for taking care of their virtue and heaven. There is no penance higher than abstention from food in control over the senses as also in the acquisition of virtue.

sn: ऋषयः पितरो देवा मनुष्या मृगपक्षिणः। यानि चान्यानि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च॥ तपः परायणाः सर्वे सिद्ध्यन्ति तपसा च ते। इत्येवं तपसा देवा महत्त्वं प्रतिपेदिरे॥
en: The Rishis, the gods, human beings, beasts, birds, and all other creatures, mobile or immobile, practise penances, and whatever success they acquire is won through penance. It was through penance that the gods acquired their superiority.

sn: इमानीष्टविभागानि फलानि तपसः सदा। तपसा शक्यते प्राप्तुं देवत्वमपि निश्चयात्॥
en: The luminous bodies in the sky have got their position through penance. Forsooth, through penance the very status of godhead may be gained.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सत्यं धर्मं प्रशंसन्ति विप्रर्षिपितृदेवताः। सत्यमिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Brahmanas, Rishis, Pitris and the gods all speak highly of the duty of truth. I wish to hear of truth. Describe it to me, O grandfather.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: सत्यं किंलक्षणं राजन् कथं वा तदवाप्यते। सत्यं प्राप्य भवेत् किं च कथं चैव तदुच्यताम्॥
en: What are the marks, O king of truth? How may it be acquired? What is acquired by practising truth, and how? Tell me all this.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: भीष्म उवाच चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य धर्माणां संकरो न प्रशस्यते। अविकारितमं सत्यं सर्ववर्णेषु भारत॥
en: Bhishma said A confusion of the duties of the four castes is never highly spoken of. What is called Truth always exists in a pure and unmixed state in every one of those four castes.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: सत्यं सत्सु सदा धर्मः सत्यं धर्मः सनातनः। सत्यमेव नमस्येत सत्यं हि परमा गतिः॥
en: Truth is always a duty with the good. Indeed, Truth is eternal duty. One should respectfully bow to Truth. Truth is the greatest refuge (of all).

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: सत्यं धर्मस्तपो योगः सत्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम्। सत्यं यज्ञः परः प्रोक्तः सर्वं सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Truth is duty; Truth is penance; Truth is Yoga; and Truth is the eternal Brahma. Truth has been said to be a great sacrifice. Everything depends upon Truth.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: आचारानिह सत्यस्य यथावदनुपूर्वशः। लक्षणं च प्रवक्ष्यामि सत्यस्येह यथाक्रमम्॥
en: I shall now tell you the forms of Truth one after another, and its characteristic marks also in due order.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: प्राप्यते च यथा सत्यं तच्च श्रोतुमिहार्हसि। सत्यं त्रयोदशविधं सर्वलोकेषु भारत॥
en: You should hear also as to how Truth may be won. Truth, O Bharata, as it exists in all the world, is of thirteen sorts.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: सत्यं च समता चैव दमश्चैव न संशयः। अमात्सर्यं क्षमा चैव ह्रीस्तितिक्षानसूयता॥ त्यागो ध्यानमथार्यत्वं धृतिश्च सततं स्थिरा। अहिंसा चैव राजेन्द्र सत्याकारास्त्रयोदश॥
en: The various forms of Truth are impartiality, self-control, forgiveness, modesty, endurance, goodness, renunciation, meditation, dignity, fortitute, compassion, and abstention from injury. These, O great king, are the thirteen forms of Truth'.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: सत्यं नामाव्ययं नित्यमविकारि तथैव च। सर्वधर्माविरुद्धेन योगेनैतदवाप्यते॥
en: Truth is immutable, eternal, and unchangeable. It may be won through practices which do not oppose any of the other virtues. It may also be won through Yoga.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: आत्मनीष्टे तथानिष्टे रिपौ च समता तथा। इच्छाद्वेषक्षयं प्राप्य कामक्रोधक्षयं तथा॥
en: When desire and hatred, as also lust and anger, are destroyed, that quality by virtue of which one is able to look impartially upon one's own self and one's enemy, upon one's good and one's evil, is called impartiality.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: दमो नान्यस्पृहा नित्यं गाम्भीर्यं धैर्यमेव च। अभयं रोगशमनं ज्ञानेनैतदवाप्यते॥
en: Self-control consists in never wishing for another man's property, in gravity and patience and power to remove the fears of others regarding one's own self, and freedom from disease. It may be won through knowledge.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: अमात्सर्यं बुधाः प्राहुर्दाने धर्मे च संयमः। अवस्थितेन नित्यं च सत्येनामत्सरी भवेत्॥
en: Devoted to liberality and the performance of all duties are considered by the wise as forming good-will. One gains universal good will by continued devotion to Truth.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: अक्षमायाः क्षमायाश्च प्रियाणीहाप्रियाणि च। क्षमते सम्मतः साधुः साध्वाप्नोति च सत्यवाक्॥
en: Regarding unforgiveness and forgiveness, it should be said that the quality by which an esteemed and good man puts up with both what is agreeable and disagreeable, is said to be forgiveness. This virtue may be acquired by the practice of truthfulness.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: कल्याणं कुरुते बाढं धीमान् न ग्लायते क्वचित्। प्रशान्तवाङ्मना नित्यं ह्रीस्तु धर्मादवाप्यते॥
en: That virtue by which an intelligent man contended in mind and words performs mnany good deeds and is never blamed by others, is called modesty. It is acquired by the help of righteousness.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: धर्मार्थहेतोः क्षमते तितिक्षा क्षान्तिरुच्यते। लोकसंग्रहणार्थं वै सा तु धैर्येण लभ्यते॥
en: That virtue which forgives for the sake of virtue and religious profit is called endurance. It is one of the form of forgiveness. It is gained through patience, and its object is to attach people to one's self.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: त्यागः स्नेहस्य यत् त्यागो विषयाणां तथैव च। रागद्वेषप्रहीणस्य त्यागो भवति नान्यथा॥
en: The casting off of worldly desires as also of all earthly possessions, is designated renunciation. Renunciation can never be gained except by one who is shorn of anger and malice.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: आर्यता नाम भूतानां यः करोति प्रयत्नतः। शुभं कर्म निराकारो वीतरागस्तथैव च॥
en: That virtue under the influence of which one does good, with diligence and care, to all creatures is designated goodness. It has no particular form and consists in the casting off of all selfish attachments.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: धृतिर्नाम सुखे दुःखे यथा नाप्नोति विक्रियाम्। तां भजेत सदा प्राज्ञो य इच्छेद् भूतिमात्मनः॥
en: That virtue by which remains unchanged in weal and woe is called fortitude. That wise man who seeks his own well-being always practises this virtue.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: सर्वथा क्षमिणा भाव्यं तथा सत्यपरेण च। वीतहर्षभयक्रोधो धृतिमाप्नोति पण्डितः॥
en: One should always practise forgiveness and be devoted to truth. The wise man who can renounce joy, fear and anger, can gain fortitude.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु कर्मणा मनसा गिरा। अनुग्रहश्च दानं च सतां धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: Abstention froin injury to all creatures in thought, word, and deed, and kindness, and gift, are the permanent duties of the good. one

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: एते त्रयोदशाकाराः पृथक् सत्यैकलक्षणाः। भजन्ते सत्यमेवेह बृंहयन्ते च भारत॥
en: These thirteen qualities, though seemingly different, have but one and the same shape, namely Truth. All these, O Bharata, hold up truth and strengthen it.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: नान्तः शक्यो गुणानां च वक्तुं सत्यस्य पार्थिव। अतः सत्यं प्रशंसन्ति विप्राः सपितृदेवताः॥
en: It is impossible, o king, to exhaust the merits of Truth. For these reasons the Brahman as, the Pitris and the gods speak highly of truth.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: नास्ति सत्यात् परो धर्मो नानृतात् पातकं परम्। स्थितिर्हि सत्यं धर्मस्य तस्मात्सत्यं न लोपयेत्॥
en: There is no duty which is higher than Truth, and no sin more dreadful than untruth. Indeed, Truth is the very root of righteousness. Therefore one should never destroy Truth.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: उपैति सत्याद् दानं हि तथा यज्ञाः सदक्षिणाः। त्रेताग्निहोत्रं वेदाश्च ये चान्ये धर्मनिश्चयाः॥
en: From Truth originate gifts, and sacrifice with presents as well the threefold Agnihotras the Vedas and everything else which leads to righteousness.

description: The purificatory rites of a king.
sn: अश्वमेधसहस्रं च सत्यं च तुलया धृतम्। अश्वमेधसहस्राद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते॥
en: On one occasion a thousand Horsesacrifices and Truth were weighed against each other and in the balance. Truth proved heavier than a thousand Horse-sacrifices. as

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यतः प्रभवति क्रोधः कामो वा भरतर्षभ। शोकमोहौ विधित्सा च परासुत्वं तथा मदः॥ लोभो मात्सयमीp च कुत्सासूया कृपा तथा। एतत् सर्वं महाप्राज्ञ याथातथ्येन मे वद॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O you of great wisdom, everything about that from which originate anger and lust. O foremost of Bharata's race, and sorrow, loss of judgement, inclination to injure others, jealousy, malice, pride envy, slander. incapacity to see the good of others, unkindness, and fear. Tell me everything truly and fully about all these.

sn: भीष्म उवाच त्रयोदशैतेऽतिबलाः शत्रवः प्राणिनां स्मृताः। उपासन्ते महाराज समन्तात् पुरुषानिह॥
en: Bhishma said These thirteen vices are known as very powerful enemies of all creatures. These, O king, approach men and tempt them from all sides.

sn: एते प्रमत्तं पुरुषमप्रमत्तास्तुदन्ति च। वृका इव विलुम्पन्ति दृष्ट्वैव पुरुषं बलात्॥
en: They goad and afflict a careless or a foolish man. Indeed, as soon as they see a person, they attack him powerfully like wolves jumping upon their pray.

sn: एभ्यः प्रवर्तते दुःखमेभ्यः पापं प्रवर्तते। इति मयो विजानीयात् सततं पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: From these originate all sorts of grief. From these originate all sorts of sin. Every man, O foremost of men, should always know this.

sn: एतेषामुदयं स्थानं क्षयं च पृथिवीपते। हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि क्रोधस्योत्पत्तिमादितः॥
en: I shall now describe to you their origin, the objects upon which they rest, and the means of their destruction, O king. Listen, first, О king, with rapt attention, to the origin of anger truly and fully.

sn: यथातत्त्वं क्षितिपते तदिहैकमनाः शृणु। लोभात् क्रोधः प्रभवति परदोषैरुदीर्यते॥
en: Anger originates from covetousness. It is strengthened by the shortcomings of others. Through forgiveness it lies dormant, and through forgiveness it disappears.

sn: क्षमया तिष्ठते राजन् क्षमया विनिवर्तते। संकल्पाज्जायते कामः सेव्यमानो विवर्धते॥
en: Regarding lust, it originates from resolution. Indulgence strengthens it. When a wise man resolutely turns away from it, it disappears and dies.

sn: यदा प्राज्ञो विरमते तदा सद्यः प्रणश्यति। परासुता क्रोधलोभादभ्यासाच्च प्रवर्तते॥ दयया सर्वभूतानां निर्वेदात् सा निवर्तते। अवद्यदर्शनादेति तत्त्वज्ञानाच्च धीमताम्॥
en: Envy of others originates from between anger and covetousness. It disappears by mercy and knowledge of self. For mercy for all creatures, and for disregard for all worldly objects, it disappears. It also springs from seeing the weakness of other people. But in intelligent men it quickly disappears by virtue of true knowledge.

sn: अज्ञानप्रभवो मोहः पापाभ्यासात् प्रवर्तते। यदा प्राज्ञेषु रमते तदा सद्यः प्रणश्यति॥
en: Loss of judgement originates from ignorance and sinfulness of habit. When the man whom this fault attacks begins to find pleasure in wise men, the vice at once and immediately disappears.

sn: विरुद्धानीह शास्त्राणि ये पश्यन्ति कुरूद्वह। विधित्सा जायते तेषां तत्त्वज्ञानान्निवर्तते॥
en: Men, O you of Kuru's race find divergent scriptures. Therefrom originates the desire for various kinds of action. When true knowledge has been acquired, that desire is satisfied.

sn: प्रीत्या शोकः प्रभवति वियोगात् तस्य देहिनः। यदा निरर्थकं वेत्ति तदा सद्यः प्रणश्यति॥
en: The sorrow of an embodied creature originates from affection which is created by separation. When, however, one learns that the dead do not come back, it disappears.

sn: परासुता क्रोधलोभादभ्यासाच्च प्रवर्तते। दयया सर्वभूतानां निर्वेदात् सा निवर्तते।॥
en: Incapacity to bear other people's good originates from anger and covetousness. Though mercy for every creature and by virtue of indifference to all worldly objects, it is put out.

sn: सत्यत्यागात् तु मात्सर्यमहितानां च सेवया। एतत् तु क्षीयते तात साधूनामुपसेवनात्॥
en: Malice springs from the casting off of truth and indulgence in wickedness. This vice, O child, disappears when one waits upon the wise and good.

sn: कुलाज्ज्ञानात् तथैश्वर्यान्मदो भवति देहिनाम्। एभिरेव तु विज्ञातैः स च सद्यः प्रणश्यति॥
en: Pride, in men, originates from birth, learning and prosperity. When those three, are truly known, that vice immediately disappears.

sn: ईर्ष्या कामात् प्रभवति संहर्षाच्चैव जायते। इतरेषां तु सत्त्वानां प्रज्ञया सा प्रणश्यति॥
en: Jealousy originates from lust and delight in low and mean people. It is destroyed by wisdom.

sn: विभ्रमाल्लोकबाह्यानां द्वेष्यैर्वाक्यैरसम्मतैः। कुत्सा संजायते राजंल्लोकान् प्रेक्ष्याभिशाम्यति॥
en: Slander originates from errors of men's daily conduct and through disagreeable speeches expressing aversion. It disappears, O King, when the whole world is seen.

sn: प्रतिकर्तुं न शक्ता ये बलस्थायापकारिणे। असूया जायते तीव्रा कारुण्याद् विनिवर्तते॥
en: When the person that injures is powerful and the one injured is unable to avenge the injury, hate appears. It disappears, however, through kindless.

sn: कृपणान् सततं दृष्ट्वा ततः संजायते कृपा। धर्मनिष्ठां यदा वेत्ति तदा शाम्यति सा कृपा॥
en: Mercy proceeds from seeing the helpless and miserable persons with whom the world abounds. It disappears when one understands the strength of virtue.

sn: अज्ञानप्रभवो लोभो भूतानां दृश्यते सदा। अस्थिरत्वं च भोगानां दृष्ट्वा ज्ञात्वा निवर्तते॥
en: Covetousness originates from ignorance. It disappears when one sees the instability of all objects of enjoyment.

sn: एतान्येव जितान्याहुः प्रशमाच्च त्रयोदश। एते हि धार्तराष्ट्राणां सर्वे दोषास्त्रयोदश॥ त्वया सत्यार्थिना नित्यं विजिता ज्येष्ठसेवनात्॥
en: It has been said that tranquility of soul, can alone conquer all these thirteen faults. All these thirteen faults visited the sons of Dhritarashtra. Yourself, always desirous of truth, have conquered all the those vices of virtue of your respect for your elders,

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आनृशंस्यं विजानामि दर्शनेन सतां सदा। नृशंसान्न विजानामि तेषां कर्म च भारत॥
en: Yudhishthira said I know what benevolence is, because I have always marked the conduct of good people. I de not, however, know them who are malevolent, nor the nature of their deeds, O Bharata.

sn: कण्टकान् कूपमग्निं च वर्जयन्ति यथा नराः। तथा नृशंसकर्माणं वर्जयन्ति नरा नरम्॥
en: Indeed, people always shun malevolent persons of ruthless deeds even as they avoid thorns and pitfalls and fire.

sn: नृशंसो दह्यते नित्यं प्रेत्य चेह च भारत। तस्मात् त्वं ब्रूहि कौरव्य तस्य धर्मविनिश्चयम्॥
en: It is evident, О Bharata, that he who is malevolent is sure to be consumed with misery both in this world and in the next. Therefore, O you of Kuru's race, tell me what, in sooth, the acts of such a person are.

sn: भीष्म उवाच स्पृहा स्याद् गर्हिता चैव विधित्सा चैव कर्मणाम्। आक्रोष्टा क्रुश्यते चैव वञ्चितो बुद्ध्यते स च॥
en: Bhishma said Malevolent persons always commit sinful acts and feel an irresistible inclination for doing them. They speak ill of others and are themselves censured. They always consider themselves as cheated of what is their due.

sn: दत्तानुकीर्तिर्विषमः क्षुद्रो नैकृतिकः शठः। असंविभागी मानी च तथा सङ्गी विकत्थनः॥
en: A malevolent person always speaks of his own charitable acts. He sees others with malicious eyes. He is very mean. He is deceitful, and wily. He never pays others their dues. He is haughty. He lives in evil company and is always boastful.

sn: सर्वातिशङ्की पुरुषो बलीशः कृपणोऽथवा। वर्गप्रशंसी सततमाश्रमद्वेषसंकरी॥
en: He fears and suspects all with whom he mixes. He is foolish in understanding. He is miserly. He praises his companions. He feels excessive aversion and hatred for all hermits who have retired into the forest.

sn: हिंसाविहारः सततमविशेषगुणागुणः। बबलीकोऽमनस्वी च लुब्धोऽत्यर्थं नृशंसकृत्॥
en: He finds pleasure in injuring others. He is perfectly careless in marking the merits and faults of others. He is a liar. He is discontented. He is highly covetous, and always acts cruelly.

sn: धर्मशीलं गुणोपेतं पापमित्यवगच्छति। आत्मशीलप्रमाणेन न विश्वसिति कस्यचित्॥
en: Such a man considers a virtuous and qualified person as a pest, and thinking every one else to be like himself never trusts any one.

sn: परेषां यत्र दोषः स्यात् तद् गुह्यं सम्प्रकाशयेत्। समानेष्वेव दोषेषु वृत्त्यर्थमुपघातयेत्॥
en: Such a person trumpets the faults of other people however unsuspected those faults might be. But about similar faults in his ownself, he does not refer to them even remotely, for the sake of the advantage he reaps from them.

sn: तथोपकारिणं चैव मन्यते वञ्चितं परम्। दत्त्वापि च धनं काले संतपत्युपकारिणे॥
en: He considers the person who does him good as a simpleton whom he has imposed upon. He repents for having at any time made any gift of wealth even to a benefactor.

sn: भक्ष्यं पेयमथालेह्यं यच्चान्यत् साधु भोजनम्। प्रेक्षमाणेषु योऽश्नीयान्नृशंसमिति तं वदेत्॥
en: Know him for a malevolent and a wicked person who quietly and alone takes choice foods and drinks even when persons stand by with eager eyes.

sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रदायाग्रं यः सुहृद्भिः सहाश्नुते। स प्रेत्य लभते स्वर्गमिह चानन्त्यमश्नुते॥
en: He, however, who dedicates the first portion of Brahmanas, and takes the residue, dividing it with friends and kinsmen acquires great felicity in the next world and infinite happiness here.

sn: एष ते भरतश्रेष्ठ नृशंसः परिकीर्तितः। सदा विवर्जनीयो हि पुरुषेण विजानता।॥
en: I have now, O foremost of Bharatas, said to you what the marks are of the wicked and malevolent man. Such a person should always be shunned by a wise man.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: भीष्म उवाच हृतार्थो यक्ष्यमाणश्व सर्ववेदान्तगश्च यः। आचार्यपितृकार्यार्थं स्वाध्यायार्थमथापि च॥ एते वै दृष्टा ब्राह्मणा धर्मभिक्षवः। निःस्वेभ्यो देयमेतेभ्यो दानं विद्या च भारत॥ साधवो
en: Bhishma said Wealth and knowledge, O Bharata, should be given to such pious and impoverished Brahmanas as have been robbed of their wealth (by thieves), as are engaged in the celebration of sacrifices, as are well-read in all the Vedas, and as are desirous of acquiring the merit of righteousness, so that they may satisfy their duties to preceptors and the Pitris, and spend their days in reciting and studying the scriptures.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: अन्यत्र दक्षिणादानं देयं भरतसत्तम। अन्येभ्योऽपि बहिर्वेदि चाकृतान्नं विधीयते॥ सर्वरत्नानि राजा हि यथार्ह प्रतिपादयेत्।
en: Only the Dakshina, O best of the Bharatas, should be given to those Brahmanas who are not poor. Uncooked food should be given beyond the limits of the sacrificial altar, to those Brahmanas that have fallen away in consequence of their sinful deeds) from their own dignity.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: ब्राह्मणा एव वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च बहुदक्षिणाः। अन्योन्यं विभवाचारा यजन्ते गुणतः सदा॥
en: The Brahmanas represent the Vedas themselves and all the sacrifices with profuse presents. Desirous of excelling one another, they always celebrate sacrifices, actuated by their various desires. The king should, therefore, make presents of various sorts of valuable wealth to them.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: यस्य त्रैवार्षिकं भक्तं पर्याप्तं भृत्यवृत्तये। अधिकं चापि विद्येत स सोमं पातुमर्हति॥
en: That Brahmana who has sufficient stores for feeding his family for three or more years, deserves to drink the Soma.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: यज्ञश्चेत् प्रतिरुद्धः स्यादंशेनैकेन यज्वनः। ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेण धार्मिके सति राजनि॥ यो वैश्यः स्याद् बहुपशु-नक्रतुरसोमपः। कुटुम्बात् तस्य तद् वित्तं यज्ञार्थं पार्थिवो हरेत्॥
en: If inspite of the presence of a pious king on the throne, the sacrifice undertaken by any one, but especially by a Brahmana, cannot be completed for want of only a fulptrt of the estimated cost, then the king should, for the completion of that sacrifice, take away from his relatives the wealth of a Vaishya who has a farge flock of cattle but who is averse from sacrifices and abstains from drinking Soma.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: आहरेदथ नो किञ्चत् कामं शूद्रस्य वेश्मनः। न हि यज्ञेषु शूद्रस्य किञ्चिदस्ति परिग्रहः॥
en: The Shudra is not competent to celebrate a sacrifice. The king should, therefore, take away (wealth for such a purpose) from a Shudra's house.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: योऽनाहिताग्निः शतगुरयज्वा च सहस्रगुः। तयोरपि कुटुम्बाभ्यामाहरेदविचारयन्॥
en: The king should, also, unscrupulously take away from their kinsmen the wealth of him who does not celebrate sacrifices although he has a hundred kine, and also of him who does not perform sacrifices although he has a thousand kine.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: अदातृभ्यो हरेद् वित्तं विख्याप्य नृपतिः सदा। तथैवाचरतो धर्मो नृपते: स्यादथाखिलः॥
en: The king should, always, publicly take away the wealth of a person who does not perform charities. By acting in this wise the King acquires great merit.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: तथैव शृणु मे भक्तं भक्तानि षडनश्नतः। अश्वस्तनविधानेन हर्तव्यं हीनकर्मणः॥ खलात् क्षेत्रात् तथा रामाद् यतो वाप्युपपद्यते। आख्यातव्यं नृपस्यैतत् पृच्छतेऽपृच्छतेऽपि वा॥
en: Listen again to me. That Brahmana who has been compelled by want to fast for three days, may take away without permission, according to the rule of a person who cares only for toclay and not for the morrow, only what is necessary for a single mcal, from the husking tub or the field or the garden or any other place of even a degraded man. He should, however, whether asked or unasked, inform the king of his deed.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: न तस्मै धारयेद् दण्डं राजा धर्मेण धर्मवित्। क्षत्रियस्य तु बालिश्या ब्राह्मणः क्लिश्यते क्षुधा॥
en: If the king knows his own duty he should not punish such a Brahmana. He should remember that a Brahmana becomes stricken with hunger only through the fault of the Kshatriya.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: श्रुतशीले समाज्ञाय वृत्तिमस्य प्रकल्पयेत्। अथैनं परिरक्षेत पिता पुत्रमिवौरसम्॥
en: Having learnt a Brahmana's learning and conduct, the king should provide for his living and protect him as a father protects his own begotten son.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: इष्टिं वैश्वानरों नित्यं निर्वयेदब्दपर्यये। अनुकल्पः परो परो धर्मो धर्मवादैस्तु केवलम्॥
en: On the expiry of every year, one should celebrate the Vaishyanara sacrifice. Those who are conversant with religious codes say that the practice of an alternative act, does not destroy virtue.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: विश्वैर्देवैश्च साध्यैश्च ब्राह्मणैश्च महर्षिभिः। आपत्सु मरणाद् भीतैर्विधिः प्रतिनिधीकृतः॥
en: Fearing death in seasons of distress, the Vishvedevas, the Saddhyas, the Brahmanas, and great Rishis, do not hesitate to follow the alternative provisions laid down in the scriptures.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: प्रभुः प्रथमकल्पस्य योऽनुकल्पे न वर्तते। न साम्परायिकं तस्य दुर्मतेर्विद्यते फलम्॥
en: That man, however, who while able to live according to the first provision, as laid down above, follows the alternative, comes to be known as a wicked person and never succeeds in acquiring any happiness in heaven.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: न ब्राह्मणो निवेदेत किंचिद् राजनि वेदवित्। स्ववीर्याद् राजवीर्याच्च स्ववीर्यं बलवत्तरम्॥
en: A Brahmana conversant with the Vedas should mention his power and knowledge to the king. Comparing again the power of a Brahmana with that of the king, the former will always be found to be superior to the latter. never

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: तस्माद् राज्ञः सदा तेजो दुःसहं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्। कर्ता शास्ता विधाता च ब्राह्मणो देव उच्यते॥
en: Therefore the power of the Brahmanas can hardly be borne or resisted by a king. The Brahmana is said to be creator, king, ordainer, and god.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: तस्मिन्नाकुशलं ब्रूयान्न शुष्कामीरयेद् गिरम्। क्षत्रियो बाहुवीर्येण तरेदापदमात्मनः॥
en: No abusive word or dry speeches, should be spoken to a Brahmana. The Kshatriya should get over all his difficulties by the help of the power of his arms.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: धनैवैश्यश्च शूद्रश्च मन्त्रैर्हो मैश्च वै द्विजः। नैव कन्या न युवति मन्त्रज्ञो न बालिशः॥ परिवेष्टाग्निहोत्रस्य भवेन्नासंस्कृतस्तथा। नरकं निपतन्त्येते जुह्वानाः स च यस्य तत्। तस्माद् वैतानकुशलो होता स्याद् वेदपारगः॥
en: The Vaishya and the Shudra should get over their difficulties by riches; the Brahmana should do so by Mantras and Homa. None of these, viz., a maiden, a young woman, a person unacquainted with Mantras, an ignorant person, or one who is impure, is competent to pour libations on the sacrificial fire. If any of these do so he or she is sure to go to hell, with him on whose behalf they act. Therefore none but a Brahmana well-read in the Vedas and skilled in all sacrifices should pour sacrificial libations.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: प्राजापत्यमदत्त्वाश्वमग्न्याधेयस्य दक्षिणाम्। अनाहिताग्निरिति स प्रोच्यते धर्मदर्शिभिः॥
en: They who are well-acquainted with the scriptures hold that man who, having lighted the sacrificial fire, does not give away the dedicated food as Dakshina, is not the kindler of a sacrificial fire,

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: पुण्यानि यानि कुर्वीत श्रद्दधानो जितेन्द्रियः। अनाप्तदक्षिणैर्यज्ञैर्न यजेत कथञ्चन॥
en: A person should, after having controlled his senses, and with proper devotion, do all the meritorious acts. One should never adore gods in sacrifices in which no Dakshina is given.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: प्रजाः पशृंश्च स्वर्गे च हन्ति यज्ञो ह्यदक्षिणः। इन्द्रियाणि यशः कीर्तिमायुश्चाप्यवकृन्तति॥
en: A sacrifice not completed with Dakshina, encompasses the destruction of one's children, animals, and heaven. Such a sacrifice destroys also the senses, the glory the achievements, and the very life, itself.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: उदक्यामासते ये च द्विजाः केचिदनग्नयः। होमं चाश्रोत्रियं येषां ते सर्वे पापकर्मिणः॥
en: Those Brahmanas who know women in their season, or who never celebrate sacrifices, or whose families have no members well-read in the Vedas, are considered as Shudras in act.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: उदपानोदके ग्रामे ब्राह्मणो वृषलीपतिः। उषित्वा द्वादश समाः शूद्रकर्मैव गच्छति॥
en: That Brahmana who, having married a Shudra girl, lives for twelve years continually in a village which has only a well to give water, becomes a Shudra in act.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: अभार्यां शयने बिभ्रच्छूद्रं वृद्ध च वै द्विजः। अब्राह्मणं मन्यमानस्तुणेष्वासीत पृष्ठतः। तथा संशुध्यते राजशृणु चात्र वचो मम॥
en: That Brahmana who brings to his bed a maiden, or allows a Shudra, knowing him as deserving of respect, to sit upon the same carpet with him, should sit on a bed of dry grass behind some Kshatriya or Vaishya and show him respect in that way. It is in this way that he can be purified. Hear, O king, my words on this subject.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: यदेकरात्रेण करोति पापं निकृष्टवर्णं ब्राह्मणः सेवमान:। स्थानासनाभ्यां विहरन् व्रती स त्रिभिर्वर्षेः शमयेदात्मपापम्॥
en: The sin that a Brahmana perpetrates in one night by respectfully serving a member of a lower caste or by playing with him in the same spot or on the same bed, is purified by observing the practice of sitting behind by observing the practice of sitting behind a Kshatriya or a Vaishya on a bed of dry grass for three years continually.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: न नर्मयुक्तमनृतं हिनस्ति न स्त्रीषु राजन्न विवाहकाले। न गुर्वर्थं नात्मनो जीवितार्थे पञ्चानृतान्याहुरपातकानि॥
en: An untruth spoken for jest is not sinful; nor one spoken at the time of wedding; nor one spoken for doing good to one's preceptor; nor one spoken for saving one's own life. These five sorts of falsehood in speech, it has been said, are not sinful.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: श्रद्दधानः शुभां विद्यां हीनादपि समाप्नुयात्। सुवर्णमपि चामेध्यादाददीताविचारयन्।॥
en: One may gain useful knowledge from even a person of degraded calling, with devotion and reverence. One may take up gold, unhesitatingly from even an unclean spot.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: स्त्रीरत्नं दुष्कुलाच्चापि विषादप्यमृतं पिबेत्। अदृष्या हि स्त्रियो रत्नमाप इत्येव धर्मतः॥
en: A woman who is the ornament of her sex may be married from even a vile race. Nectar, if extracted from poison, may be drunk; women, jewels and other valuables, as also water, can never, according to the scriptural injunction, be impure or unclean.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: गोब्राह्मणहितार्थं च वर्णानां संकरेषु च। वैश्यो गृह्णीत शस्त्राणि परित्राणार्थमात्मनः॥
en: For the good of Brahmanas and kine, and on occasions when mixture of castes takes place, even a Vaishya may take up weapons for his own safety.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: सुरापानं ब्रह्महत्या गुरुतल्पमथापि वा। अनिर्देश्यानि मन्यन्ते प्राणान्तमिति धारणा॥
en: Drinking wine, killing a Brahmana, and the violation of the preceptor's bed, are sins when committed consciously, can never be expiated. The only expiation laid down for them is death.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: सुवर्णहरणं स्तैन्यं विप्रस्वं चेति पातकम्। विहरन् मद्यपानाच्च अगम्यागमनादपि॥
en: The sarne may be said of stealing gold, and the theft of a Brahmana's property. By drinking winc, by knowing prohibited women, by mingling with a degraded person, by knowing a Brahmana's woman, one becomes for ever fallen.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: पतितैः सम्प्रयोगाच्च ब्राह्मणीयोनितस्तथा। अचिरेण महाराज पतितो वै भवत्युत॥
en: By associating with a fallen person for one whole year in sacrifices and teaching and sexual intercourse, one becomes fallen. One, however, does not become so by associating with a fallen person in riding on the same car, sitting on the same seat, and eating in the same line.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: संवत्सरेण पतति पतितेन सहाचरन्। याजनाध्यापनाद् यौनान्न तु यानासनाशनात्॥
en: Excluding the five heinous sins that have been mentioned above, all other sins have expiations. Expiating those sins according to the ordinances laid down for them, one should not commit them again.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: एतानि हित्वातोऽन्यानि निर्देश्यानीति भारत। निर्देश्यानेन विधिना कालेनाव्यसनी भवेत्॥ अन्नं वीर्यं ग्रहीतव्यं प्रेतकर्मण्यपातिते। त्रिषु त्वेतेषु पूर्वेषु न कुर्वीत विचारणाम्॥
en: Except all those, O Bharata! Many other sins have been described as removable by penance. Thus he gives up the sinful habit. Regarding those who have been guilty of the first three of these five sins, (namely, drinking wine, killing a Brahmana, and violation of the preceptor's bed), their (surviving) kinsmen have no restrictions about taking food and wearing ornaments, even if their funeral rites remain unperformed when they die. The surviving kinsmen need make no scruple about such things at such times.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: अमात्यान् वा गुरून् वापि जह्याद् धर्मेण धार्मिकः। प्रायश्चित्तमकुर्वाणै तैरर्हति संविदम्॥ अधर्मकारी धर्मेण तपसा हन्ति किल्विषम्। ब्रुवन् स्तेन इति स्तेनं तावत् प्राप्नोति किल्बिषम्॥
en: A virtuous man should, while observing his duties, discard his very friends and elders. In fact, so long as they do not perform expiation, the virtuous should not even talk with those sinners. A man who has committed sins dissipates them by acting virtuously afterwards and by penances. By calling a thief a thief, one conimits the sin of theft.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: अस्तेनं स्तेन इत्युक्त्वा द्विगुणं पापमाप्नुयात्। त्रिभागं ब्रह्महत्यायाः कन्या प्राप्नोति दुष्यती॥ यस्तु दूषयिता तस्याः शेषं प्राप्नोति पाप्मनः।
en: By calling a person thief who, however, is not a thief, one commits a sin just double the sin of theft. The maiden who spoils her virginity incurs three-fourths of the sin of Brahmanicide, while the man who knows her incurs a sin equal to a fourth part of that of Brahmanicide.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: ब्राह्मणानवगर्नेह स्पृष्ट्वा गुरुतरं भवेत्॥ वर्षाणां हि शतं तावत् प्रतिष्ठां नाधिगच्छति।
en: By speaking against Brahmanas or by striking them, one sinks in infamy for a hundred years.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: सहस्रं चैव वर्षाणां निपत्य नरकं वसेत्॥ तस्मान्नैवावगर्खेत नैव जातु निपातयेत्।
en: By slaying a Brahmana one undergoes the torments of hell for a thousand years. No one should, therefore, speak ill of a Brahmana or slay him.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: शोणितं यावत: पांसून् संगृह्णीयाद् द्विजक्षतात्॥ तावती: स समा राजन् नरके प्रतिपद्यते।
en: If a man wounds a Brahmana with a weapon, he will have to live in hell for as many years as the grains of dust that are soaked by the blood flowing from the body of the wounded.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: भ्रूणहाऽऽहवमध्ये तु शुद्ध्यते शस्त्रपाततः॥ आत्मानं जुहुयादग्नौ समिद्धे तेन शुद्ध्यते।
en: One guilty of foeticide becomes purified if he dies of wounds received in battle fought for the sake of kine and Brahmanas. He may also be purified by casting his person on a burning fire.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: सुरापो वारुणीमुष्णां पीत्वा पापाद् विमुच्यते॥ तया स काये निर्दग्धे मृत्युं वा प्राप्य शुद्ध्यति। लोकांश्च लभते विप्रो नान्यथा लभते हि सः॥
en: A drinker of spirituous liquors becomes purified by drinking hot spirit. He is purified by his death, brought on by that hot drink, in the other world. A Brahmana stained by such a sin attains regions of felicity by such a course, and such a course only, and not by any other.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: गुरुतल्पमधिष्ठाय दुरात्मा पापचेतनः। स्त्र्याकारां प्रतिमां लिंग्य मृत्युना सोऽभिशुद्ध्यति॥
en: The wicked and sinful wretch who violates the bed of a preceptor, becomes purified by the death that results from embracing a heated iron statue of a female.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: अथवा शिश्नवृषणावादायाञ्जलिना स्वयम्॥ नैर्ऋती दिशमास्थाय निपतेत् स त्वजिह्मगः।
en: Or, emasculating himself and cutting off his organ, and bearing them in his hands, he should go straight way towards the south-west and then give up his ghost.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: ब्राह्मणार्थेऽपि वा प्राणान् संत्यजेत् तेन शुद्ध्यति॥ अश्वमेधेन वापीष्ट्वा अथवा गोसवेन वा। अग्निष्टोमेन वा सम्यगिह प्रेत्य च पूज्यते॥
en: Or, he may cleanse himself of all his sins, by meeting with death for the sake of benefiting a Brahmana. Or, he may regain esteem both in this world and in the next by performing a Horse-sacrifice or a Cowsacrifice or an Agnishtoma.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: तथैव द्वादशसमाः कपाली ब्रह्महा भवेत्। ब्रह्मचारी भवेन्नित्यं स्वकर्म ख्यापयन् मुनिः॥
en: The killer of a Brahmana should practise the vow of Brahmacharya for twelve years, and devoting himself to penances, he should wander, holding in his hands the skull of the killed all the time and the time and proclaiming his sin to all. on

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: एवं वा तपसा युक्तो ब्रह्महा सवनी भवेत्। एवं तु समभिज्ञातामात्रेयीं वा निपातयेत्॥
en: He should even adopt such a course, devoted to penances and leading the life of an ascetic. Even such is the expiation provided for one who skills a woman quick with child, knowing her condition.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: द्विगुणा ब्रह्महत्या वै आत्रेयीनिधने भवेत्। सुरापो नियताहारो ब्रह्मचारी क्षितीशयः॥ ऊर्ध्वं त्रिभ्योऽपि वर्षेभ्यो यजेताग्निष्टुता परम्। ऋषभैकसहस्रं वा गा दत्त्वा शौचमाप्नुयात्॥
en: The man that knowingly kills such a woman incurs double the sin that follows from Brahmanicide. A drinker of spirituous liquor should live spare diet, practising Brahmacharya vows, and sleep on the naked earth, and perform, for more than three years the sacrifice next to the Agnishtoma. He should then present a thousand kine with one bull (to a good Brahmana). He would then regain his purily by doing all this.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: वैश्यं हत्वा तु वर्षे द्वे ऋषभैकशतं च गाः। शूद्रं हत्वाब्दमेवैकमृषभं च शतं च गाः॥ श्ववराहखरान् हत्वा शौद्रमेव व्रतं चरेत्।
en: Having killed a Vaishya one Vaishya one should perform such a sacrifice for two years and present a hundred kine with one bull. Having killed a Shudra, one should perform such a sacrifice for one year and present a hundred kine with one bull. Having killed a dog or a bear or a camel, one should perform the same penance that is laid down for killing a Shudra.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: मार्जारचाषमण्डूकान् काकं व्यालं च मूषिकम्॥ उक्तः पशुसमो दोषो राजन् प्राणिनिपातनात्।
en: For killing a cat, a chasa, a frog, a crow, a reptile or a rat, it has been said, one incurs the sin of animal slaughter O king.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: प्रायश्चित्तान्यथान्यानि प्रवक्ष्याम्यनुपूर्वशः॥ अल्पे वाप्यथ शोचेत पृथक् संवत्सरं चरेत्।
en: I shall now tell you of other kinds of expiations one after the other. For all minor sins one should repent or practise some vow for one year.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: त्रीणि श्रोत्रियभार्यायां परदारे च द्वे स्मृते॥ काले चतुर्थे भुञ्जानो ब्रह्मचारी व्रती भवेत्।
en: For ravishing the wife of a Brahmana well read in the Vedas, one should, for three years, practise the vow of Brahmacharya, living on spare diet at the fourth part of the day. For ravishing any other woman one should undergo similar penances for two years.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: स्थानासनाभ्यां विहरेत् त्रिरह्नाभ्युपयन्नपः। एवमेव निराकर्ता यश्चाग्नीनपविध्यति॥
en: For enjoying oneself in the company of a woman as by sitting with her on the same spot or on the same seat, one should live only on water for three days. By doing this he may purify himself of his sin. The same is laid down for one who befouls a burning fire (by throwing impure things on it.)

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: त्यजत्यकारणे यश्च पितरं मातरं गुरुम्। पतितः स्यात्स कौरव्य यथा धर्मेषु निश्चयः॥ ग्रासाच्छादनमात्रं तु दद्यादिति निदर्शनम्। (ब्रह्मचारी द्विजेभ्यश्च दत्त्वा पापात् प्रपुच्यते।) भार्यायां व्यभिचारिण्यां निरुद्धायां विशेषतः। यत् पुंसः परदारेषु तदेनां चारयेद् व्रतम्॥
en: He who, without sufficient reason leaves his father or mother or preceptor, forsooth, becomes degraded, O ye scion of Kuru's race, as is laid down in the scriptures. Only food and clothes shall be given to a wife guilty of fornication or one confined in a prison. Indeed, the vows that are laid down for a male person guilty of fornication should also be forced on a woman who is as well guilty of the same.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: श्रेयांसं शयनं हित्वा यान्यं पापं निगच्छति। श्वभिस्तामर्दयेद् राजा संस्थाने बहुविस्तरे॥
en: That woman who abandoning a husband of a superior caste, commits adultery with a vile person (of a lower order), should be made by the king to be devoured by dogs in a public place in the midst of a large number of spectators.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: पुमांसमुन्नयेत् प्राज्ञः शयने तप्त आयसे। अप्यादधीत दारूणि तत्र दह्येत पापकृत्॥
en: A wise king should make the male person, committing adultery under such circumstances to be placed upon a heated bed of iron and then, placing woods underneath, burn the sinner thereon.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: एष दण्डो महाराज स्त्रीणां भर्तृष्वतिक्रमात्। संवत्सरोऽभिशस्तस्य दुष्टस्य द्विगुणो भवेत्॥
en: The same punishment, O king, holds for the woman who is guilty of adultery. The wicked sinner who does not perform expiatory rite within a year of the perpetration of the sin incurs demerit that is double of what attaches to the original sin.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: द्वे तस्य त्रीणि वर्षाणि चत्वारि सहसेविनि। कुचरः पञ्चवर्षाणि चरेद् भैक्ष्यं मुनिव्रतः॥
en: One who mixes with such a person for two years must walk over the Earth, devoting himself to penances and living upon alms. One mixing with a sinner for four years should follow such a mode of life for five years.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: परिवित्तिः परिवेत्ता या चैव परिविद्यते। पाणिग्रहास्त्वधर्मेण सर्वे ते पतिताः स्मृताः॥
en: If a young brother marries before his elder brother, then the younger brother, the elder brother, and the woman that is married, all three, on account of such wedding, become degraded.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: चरेयुः सर्व एवैते वीरहा यद् व्रतं चरेत्। चान्द्रायणं चरेन्मासं कृच्छ्रे वा पापशुद्धये॥ परिवेत्ता प्रयच्छेत तां स्नुषां परिवित्तये।
en: All of them should observe the vows laid down for a person who has neglected his sacrificial fire, or practise the of Chandrayana for month, or some other painful vow, for purging themselves off their sin.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: ज्येष्ठेन त्वभ्यनुज्ञातो यवीयानप्यनन्तरम्। एवं च मोक्षमाप्नोति तौ च सा चैव धर्मतः॥
en: The younger brother, marrying should give his wife to his unmarried elder brother. Having acquired the permission of the elder brother, the younger brother may take back his wife. By such means all three may be cleansed of their sin.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: अमानुषीषु गोवामनावृष्टिर्न दुष्यति। अधिष्ठात्रवमन्तारं पशूनां पुरुषं विदुः॥
