en: By killing animals except a cow, the killer is not stained. The learned hold that man has supremacy over all the lower animals.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: परिधायोर्ध्ववालं तु पात्रमादाय मृन्मयम्। चरेत् सप्तगृहान्नित्यं स्वकर्म परिकीर्तयन्।॥ तत्रैव लब्धभोजी स्याद् द्वादशाहात्स शुद्ध्यति। चरेत् संवत्सरं चापि तद् व्रतं येन कृन्तति॥
en: Holding in his hand a yak-tail and an earthen pot, a sinner should go about, giving a publicity to his sin. He should every day beg of only seven families, and live upon what may thus be got. By doing this for twelve days he may be purified of his sin. He who cannot hold in his hand the yak-tail while practising this vow should become a mendicant (as stated above) for one whole year.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: भवेत्तु मानुषेष्वेवं प्रायश्चित्तमनुत्तमम्। दानं वा दानशक्तेषु सर्वमेतत् प्रकल्पयेत्॥
en: Amongst men such expiation ranks foremost. The practice of charity has been sanctioned in all such cases for those that are able to practise charity.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: अनास्तिकेषु गोमात्रं दानमेकं प्रचक्षते। ववराहमनुष्याणां कुक्कुटस्य खरस्य च॥
en: Those who have faith and virtue may purify themselves by giving away only one cow.

description: The distribution of wealth among Brahmanas
sn: मांसं मूत्रं पुरीषं च प्राश्य संस्कारमर्हति। ब्राह्मणास्तु सुरापस्य गन्धमादाय सोमपः॥ अपस्त्र्यहं पिबेदुष्णं त्र्यहमुष्णं पयः पिबेत्। त्र्यहमुष्णं पयः पीत्वा वायुभक्षो भवेत् त्र्यहम्॥ एवमेतत् समुद्दिष्टं प्रायश्चित्तं सनातनम्। ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेण यदज्ञानेन सम्भवेत्॥
en: One who eats or drinks the flesh, ordure, or urine of a dog, a boar, a man, a cock or a camel must have the ceremony of putting on the sacred thread performed again. If a Somadrinking Brahmana smells alcohol from the mouth of one who has drunk it, he should drink warm water for three days or warm milk for the same period. Or, drinking warm water for three days he should live for that period upon air alone. These are the eternal injunctions prescribed for the expiation of sin, especially for a Brahmana who has perpetrated these sins through ignorance and want of judgement.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कथान्तरमथासाद्य खड्गयुद्धविशारदः। नकुलः शरतल्पस्थमिदमाह पितामहम्॥
en: When this discourse was finished, Nakula who was an expert swordsman thus questioned the Kuru grandfather lying on his bed of arrows.

sn: नकुल उवाच धनुः प्रहरणं श्रेष्ठमतीवात्र पितामह। मतस्तु मम धर्मज्ञ खड्ग एव सुसंशितः॥ विशीर्णे कार्मुके राजन् प्रक्षीणेषु च वाजिषु। खड्ड्रेन शक्यते युद्धे साध्वात्मा परिरक्षितुम्॥
en: Nakula said-The bow, O grand-father, known as the foremost of weapons in this world. I, however, prefer the sword, since when the bow, O king, is cut off or broken, when horses are dead or weakened, a good warrior, well-trained in the sword, can protect himself by means of his sword.

sn: शरासनधरांश्चैव गदाशक्तिधरांस्तथा। एकः खड्गधरो वीरः समर्थः प्रतिबाधितुम्॥
en: A hero armed with the sword can, alone, withstand inany bowmen and many antagonists armed with maces and arrows.

sn: अत्र मे संशयश्चैव कौतूहलमतीव च। किंस्वित् प्रहरणं श्रेष्ठं सर्वयुद्धषु पार्थिव॥
en: I have this doubt, and I am anxious to know the truth. Which, O king, is really the foremost of weapons in all battles.

sn: कथं चोत्पादितः खड्गः कस्मै चाय केन च। पूर्वाचार्यं च खड्गस्य प्रब्रूहि प्रपितामह॥
en: How was the sword first created and why? Who also was the first teacher in that weapon? Tell me all this, O grandfather.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा माद्रीपुत्रस्य धीमतः। स तु कौशल संयुक्तं सूक्ष्मचित्रार्थसम्मतम्॥ ततस्तस्योत्तरं वाक्यं स्वरवर्णोपपादितम्। शिक्षया चोपपन्नाय द्रोणशिष्याय भारत॥ उवाच स तु धर्मज्ञो धनुर्वेदस्य पारगः। शरतल्पगतो भीष्मो नकुलाय महात्मने॥
en: Hearing these words of the intelligent son of Madri, the virtuous Bhishma, that perfect master of the science of the bow, lying upon his bed of arrows, answered in many refined words of great significance, of sweet cadence, and showing considerable skill, to the great Nakula, that discipline of Drona of skilful training.

sn: भीष्म उवाच तत्त्वं शृणुष्व माद्रेय यदेतत् परिपृच्छसि। प्रबोधितोऽस्मि भवता धातुमानिव पर्वतः॥
en: Bhishma said Hear the truth, O son of Madri, about what you have asked me! I am worked up by this question of yours, like a hill of red chalk.

sn: सलिलैकार्णवं तात पुरा सर्वमभूदिदम्। निष्पकम्पमनाकाशमनिर्देश्यमहीतलम्॥
en: In days of yore the universe was one vast sheet of water, fixed and skyless, and without this Earth existing in it.

sn: तमसाऽऽवृतमस्पर्शमतिगम्भीरदर्शनम्। निःशब्दं चाप्रमेयं च तत्र जज्ञे पितामहः॥
en: Covered with darkness, and unseen, it presented a dreadful aspect. Perfect silence prevailed everywhere and it was immeasurable in extent. In his own proper time the Grandfather (of the universe) was born.

sn: सोऽसृजद् वातमग्निं च भास्करं चापि वीर्यवान्। आकाशमसृजच्चोर्ध्वमधो भूमिं च नैर्ऋतीम्॥ नभः सचन्द्रतारं च नक्षत्राणि ग्रहांस्तथा। संवत्सरानृतून् मासान् पक्षानथ लवान् क्षणान्॥
en: He then created wind, and fire, and the highly powerful sun. He also created the sky, the heavens, the nether regions, Earth, the quarters, the firmament with the moon and the stars, the constellations, the planets, the year, the seasons, the months, the two fortnights and the smaller divisions of time.

sn: ततः शरीरं लोकस्थं स्थापयित्वा पितामहः। जनयामास भगवान् पुत्रानुत्तमतेजसः॥
en: Assuming a visible form the divine Grandfather then begot (by the power of his will) some highly energetic sons.

sn: मरीचिमृषिमत्रिं च पुलस्त्यं पुलहं ऋतुम्। वसिष्ठाङ्गिरसौ चोभौ रुद्रं च प्रभुमीश्वरम्॥ प्राचेतसस्तथा दक्षः कन्याषष्टिमजीजनत्। ता वै ब्रह्मर्षयः सर्वाः प्रजार्थं प्रतिपेदिरे॥
en: They are the sages Marichi, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vashishtha, Angiras, and the mighty and powerful lord Rudra, and Prachetas. The last beget Daksha, who in his turn beget sixty daughters. All those daughters were accepted by the twice-born sages for the purpose of begetting children upon them.

sn: ताभ्यो विश्वानि भूतानि देवाः पितृगणास्तथा। गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव रक्षांसि विविधानि च॥ पतत्रिमृगमीनाश्च प्लवङ्गाश्च महोरगाः। तथा पक्षिगणाः सर्वे जलस्थलविचारिणः॥ उद्भिदः स्वेदजाश्चैव साण्डजाश्च जरायुजाः। जज्ञे तात जगत्सर्वं तथा स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥
en: From them originated all the creatures of the universe, including the gods, Pitris, Gandharvas, Apsaras all sorts of Rakshasas, birds, animals, fishes, monkeys, great snakes, and various species of fowl ranging in the air or the water and vegetables, and all oviparous or viviparous being or those or born of filth. In this wise the whole universe consisting of mobile and immobile creatures came into being.

sn: भूतसर्गमिमं कृत्वा सर्वलोकपितामहः। शाश्वतं वेदपठितं धर्म प्रयुयुजे ततः॥
en: Having thus created all mobile and immobile creatures, then the universal Grandfather preached the eternal religion of the Vedas.

sn: तस्मिन् धर्मे स्थिता देवा: सहाचार्यपुरोहिताः। आदित्या वसवो रुद्राः ससाध्या मरुदतश्विनः॥ भृग्वत्र्यङ्गिरसः सिद्धाः काश्यपाश्च तपोधनाः। वसिष्ठगौतमागस्त्यास्तथा नारदपर्वतौ॥ ऋषयो वालखिल्याश्च प्रभासा: सिकतास्तथा। घृतपा: सोमवायव्या वैश्वानरमरीचिपाः॥ अकृष्टाश्चैव हंसाश्च ऋषयो वाग्नियोनयः। वानप्रस्थाः पृश्नयश्च स्थिता ब्रह्मानुशासने॥
en: That religion was accepted by the gods, with their preceptors and priests, the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Saddhyas, the Maruts, the Ashvins, Bhrigu, Atri, Angiras, the Siddhas, Kashyapa of Penances, Vashishtha, Gautama, Agastya, Narada, Parvata, the Valkhilya Rishis, those other Rishis known as Prabhasas, the Sikatas, the Ghritapas, the Somavayavyas, the Vaishvanaras, the Marichipas, the Akrishtas, the Hansas, those born of Fire, the Vanaprasthas, and the Prashins. All of them followed the commands of Brahman.

sn: दानवेन्द्रास्त्वतिक्रम्य तत् पितामहशासनम्। धर्मस्यापचयं चक्रुः क्रोधलोभसमन्विताः॥
en: Disregarding the cominands of the Grandfather, and giving way to anger and covetousness, the foremost of the Danavas, however, began to bring about the destruction of virtue.

sn: हिरण्यकशिपुश्चैव हिरण्याक्षो विरोचनः। शम्बरो विप्रचित्तिश्च विराधो नमुचिर्बलिः :॥
en: They were Hiranyakashipu, Hiranyaksha, Virochana, Shamvara, Viprachitti, Prahlada, Namuchi and Vali.

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवः सगणा दैत्यदानवाः। धर्मसेतुमतिक्रम्य रेमिरेऽधर्मनिश्चयाः॥
en: Disregarding all restraints of duty and religion, these and many other Daityas and Danavas sported and found pleasure in all sorts of wicked acts.

sn: सर्वे तुल्याभिजातीया यथा देवास्तथा वयम्। इत्येवं धर्ममास्थाय स्पर्धमानाः सुरर्षिभिः॥
en: Considering themselves equal in point of birth with the gods, they began to challenge them and the pure sages.

sn: न प्रियं नाप्यनुक्रोशं चक्रुर्भूतेषु भारत। त्रीनुपायानतिक्रम्य दण्डेन रुरुधुः प्रजाः॥
en: They never did any good to the other creatures of the universe or showed mercy for any of them. Neglecting the three well-known means, they began to persecute and assail all creatures by holding only the rod of chastisement.

sn: न जग्मुः संविदं तैश्च दर्पादसुरसत्तमाः॥ तदा हिमवतः शृङ्गे सुरम्ये पद्मतारके। शतयोजनविस्तारे मणिरत्नचयाचिते॥
en: Indeed, those foremost of Asuras, filled with pride did not treat other creatures as friends. Accompanied by the twice-born ones the divine Brahman, proceeded to a delightful summit of Himavat, extending for a hundred Yojanas in area, adorned with various sorts of jewels and gems, and upon whose surface the stars existed like so many lotuses on a lake.

sn: तस्मिन् गिरिवरे पुत्र पुष्पितद्रुमकानने। तस्थौ स विबुधश्रेष्ठो ब्रह्मा लोकार्थसिद्धये॥
en: On that king of mountains, O sire, filled with forests of blossoming trees, that foremost of the gods, viz., Brahmana, lived for sometime for accomplishing the business of the world.

sn: ततो वर्षसहस्रान्ते वितानमकरोत् प्रभुः। विधिना कल्पदृष्टेन यथावच्चोपपादितम्॥
en: After the expiration of a thousand years, the powerful lord made arrangements for a grand sacrifice according to the ordinances prescribed in the scriptures.

sn: ऋषिभिर्यज्ञपटुभिर्यथावत् कर्मकर्तृभिः। समिद्भिः परिसंकीर्णं दीप्यमानैश्च पावकैः॥
en: The sacrificial altar was adorned with Rishis skilled in sacrifice and capable of performing all acts, with sacrificial fuel, and with burning fires.

sn: काञ्चनैर्यज्ञभाण्डैश्च भ्राजिष्णुभिरलंकृतम्। वृतं देवगणैश्चैव प्रवरैर्यज्ञमण्डलम्॥
en: And it looked highly beautiful for the sacrificial plates and vessels having been all made of gold. All the leading gods sat there.

sn: तथा ब्रह्मर्षिभिश्चैव सदस्यैरुपशोभितम्। तत्र घोरतमं वृत्तमृषीणां मे परिश्रुतम्॥
en: The platform was further adorned with Sadasyas who were all high regenerate Rishis. I have heard from the Rishis that something very awful soon took place in that sacrifice.

sn: चन्द्रमा विमलं व्योम यथाभ्युदिततारकम्। विकीर्याग्निं तथा भूतमुत्थितं श्रूयते तदा॥
en: It is heard that a creature came out (from the sacrificial fire) scattering the flames around him, and whose effulgence equalled that of the Moon himself when he rises in the sky be spangled with stars.

sn: नीलोत्पलसवर्णाभं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्र कृशोदरम्। प्रांशुं सुदुर्धर्षतरं तथैव ह्यमितौजसम्॥
en: His complexion was dark like that of the petals of the blue lotus. His teeth were keen. His stomach was lean. His stature was tall. He appeared highly irresistible and energetic.

sn: तस्मिन्नुतपतमाने च प्रचचाल वसुन्धरा। महोर्मिकलितावर्तश्चुक्षुभे स महोदधिः॥
en: When that being appeared, the Earth shook. The Ocean became agitated with mountain billows and dreadful eddies.

sn: पेतुरुल्का महोत्पाताः शाखाश्च मुमुचुर्दुमाः। अप्रशान्ता दिशः सर्वाः पवनश्चाशिवो ववौ॥ मुहुर्मुहुश्च भूतानि प्राव्यथन्त भयात् तथा।
en: Meteors, foreboding great calamities, passed through the sky. The branches of trees began to fall down. All the points of the horizon became unquite. Inauspicious winds blew. All creatures began to tremble with fear every moment.

sn: तत: स तुमुलं दृष्ट्वा तं च भूतमुपस्थितम्॥ महर्षिसुरगन्धर्वानुवाचेदं पितामहः।
en: Seeing that dreadful agitation of the universe and that Being originated from the sacrificial fire, the Grandfather said to the great Rishis, the gods, and the Gandharvas.

sn: मयैवं चिन्तितं भूतमसि मैष वीर्यवान्।॥ रक्षणार्थाय लोकस्य वधाय च सुरद्विषाम्।
en: This Being was thought of by me. Highly energetic his name is Asi (sword or scimitar). I have created him for the protection of the world and the destruction of the enemies of the celestials.

sn: ततस्तद्रूपमुत्सृज्य बभौ निस्त्रिंश एव सः॥ विमलस्तीक्ष्णधारश्च कालान्तक इवोद्यतः।
en: Leaving off the form he had first assumed, that being then took the shape of a sword of great effulgence, highly polished, sharp-edged, and sprang like the all-destructive Being at the end of the cycle.

sn: ततः स शितिकण्ठाय रुद्रायाभिकेतवे॥ ब्रह्मा ददावसिं तीक्ष्णमधर्मप्रतिवारणम्।
en: Then Brahman handed over that sharp weapon to the blue-throated Rudra who has for his emblem the foremost of bulls, for empowering him to suppress irreligion and sin.

sn: ततः स भगवान् रुद्रो महर्षिजनसंस्तुतः॥ प्रगृह्यासिममेयात्मा रूपमन्यच्चकार ह।
en: At this, the divine and great Rudra, praised by the great Rishis, took up that sword and assumed a different forin.

sn: चतुर्बाहुः स्पृशन् मूर्खा भूस्थितोऽपि दिवाकरम्॥ उर्ध्वदृष्टिर्महालिङ्गो मुखाज्ज्वालाः समुत्सृजन्।
en: Displaying four arms, he became so tall that though he stood on the Earth he touched the very sun with his head. With eyes turned upwards, and with every limb extended wide, he began to eject flames of fire from his mouth.

sn: विकुर्वन् बहुधा वर्णान् नीलपाण्डुरलोहितान्॥ बिभ्रत्कृष्णाजिनं वासो हेमप्रवरतारकम्। नेत्रं चैकं ललाटेन भास्करप्रतिमं वहन्॥ शुशुभातेऽतिविमले द्वे नेत्रे कृष्णपिङ्गले।
en: Assuming various hues such as blue, white and red, and wearing a black deer-skin set with stars of gold, he bore on his forehead a third eye resembling the effulgent sun. His two other eyes, one of which was black and the other twany, shone very brilliantly.

sn: ततो देवो महादेवः शूलपाणिर्भगाक्षिहा॥ सम्प्रगृह्य तु निस्त्रिंशं कालाग्निसमवर्चसम्। त्रिकूटं चर्म चोद्यम्य सविद्युतमिवाम्बुदम्। चचार विविधान् मार्गान् महाबलपराक्रमः॥ विधुन्वन्नसिमाकाशे तथा युद्धचिकीर्षया।
en: Taking up the sword which was effulgent like the all-destructive Yuga fire, and wielding a large shield with three high bosses which shone like a mass of dark clouds stricken with flashes of lightning, the divine Mahadeva, the bearer of the Shula, the tearer of Bhaga's eye, began to perform various kinds of evolutions. Endued with great with great prowess, he began to whirl the sword in the sky, seeking an encounter. an

sn: तस्य नादं विनदतो महाहासं च मुञ्चतः॥ बभौ प्रतिभयं रूपं तदा रुद्रस्य भारत।
en: He uttered loud roars and awful was the sound of his laughter. Indeed, O Bharata, then Rudra assumed exceedingly terrible appearance.

sn: तद्रूपधारिणं रुद्रं रौद्रकर्मचिकीर्षया।॥ निशम्य दानवाः सर्वे हृष्टाः समभिदुद्रुवुः। अश्मभिश्चाभ्यवर्षन्त प्रदीप्तैश्च तथोल्मुकैः॥
en: Hearing that Rudra had assumed that form for performing dreadful deeds, the Danavas, filled with joy, began to come towards him quickly, showering huge rocks upon him as they came, and burning brands of wood, and various kinds of terrible weapons made of iron cach sharp as of a razor.

sn: घोरैः प्रहरणैश्चान्यैः क्षुरधारैरयोमयैः। ततस्तु दानवानीकं सम्प्रणेतारमुच्यतम्॥
en: However, seeing that foremost of all beings, the indestructible powerful Rudra, swelling with might, the Danavas army became stupefied and began to tremble.

sn: रुद्रं दृष्ट्वा बलोद्भूतं प्रमुमोह चचाल च। चित्रं शीघ्रपदत्वाच्च चरन्तमसिपाणिनम्॥ तमेकमसुराः सर्वे सहस्रमिति मेनिरे।
en: Although Rudra was alone and singlehanded, yet so quickly did he move about on the field of battle with the sword in his hand that the Asuras thought there were a thousand Rudras fighting with them.

sn: छिन्दन भिन्दन् रुजन् कृन्तन् दारयन् पोथयन्नपि॥ अचरद् वैरिसङ्केषु दावाग्निरिव कक्षगः।
en: Tearing and piercing and assailing and cutting and lopping off and grinding down, the great god moved about quickly among the large number of his enemies like a forest-fire amid heaps of dry grass spread around.

sn: असिवेगप्रभग्नास्ते छिन्नबाहूरुवक्षसः॥ सम्प्रकीर्णान्त्रगात्राश्च पेतुरुआं महाबलाः।
en: Assailed by the god with his sword, with arms and thighs and chests cut off and pierced, and with heads cut off, the powerful Asuras began to drop down on the Earth.

sn: अपरे दानवा भग्नाः खड्गपातावपीडिताः॥ अन्योन्यमभिनर्दन्तो दिशः सम्प्रतिपेदिरे।
en: Stricken with strokes of the sword, other Danavas broke and fled in all directions, cheering up one another as they fled.

sn: भूमि केचित् प्रविविशुः पर्वतानपरे तथा॥ अपरे जग्मुराकाशमपरेऽम्भः समाविशन्।
en: Some entered into the bowels of the Earth; others got into the caves of mountains. Some went upwards; others entered into the sea.

sn: तस्मिन् महति संवृत्ते समरे भृशदारुणे॥ बभूव भूः प्रतिभया मांसशोणितकर्दमा।
en: During that dreadful and fierce battle, the Earth was covered with flesh and blood, and dreadful spectacles appeared on all sides.

sn: दानवानां शरीरैश्च पतितैः शोणितोक्षितैः॥ समाकीर्णा महाबाहो शैलैरिव सकिंशुकैः।
en: Covered with the fallen bodies of Danavas bathed in blood, the Earth looked as if overspread with mountain summits filled with Kinshukas.

sn: स रुद्रो दानवान् हत्वा कृत्वा धर्मोत्तरं जगत्॥ रौद्र रूपमथोत्क्षिप्य चक्रे रूपं शिवं शिवः।
en: Having killed the Danavas and reestablished virtue on Earth, the auspicious Rudra cast off his dreadful form and put on his beneficient shape.

sn: ततो महर्षयः सर्वे सर्वे देवगणास्तथा॥ जयेनाद्भुतकल्पेन देवदेवं तथार्चयन्।
en: Then all the Rishis and all the gods adored that god of gods with loud cries of his victory.

sn: ततः स भगवान् रुद्रो दानवक्षतजोक्षितम्॥ असिं धर्मस्य गोप्तारं ददौ सत्कृत्य विष्णवे।
en: After this the divine Rudra gave the sword, that protector of religion, covered with the blood of Danavas, to Vishnu with proper adorations.

sn: विष्णुर्मरीचये प्रादान्मरीचिर्भगवानपि॥ महर्षिभ्यो ददौ खड्गमृषयो वासवाय च।
en: Vishnu gave it to Marichi. The divine Marichi gave it to all the great Rishis. the latter gave it to Vasava.

sn: महेन्द्रो लोकपालेभ्यो लोकपालास्तु पुत्रका।६७।। मनवे सूर्यपुत्राय ददुः खड्गं सुविस्तरम्।
en: Vasava gave it to the Regents of the quarters. The Regents, O son, gave that large sword to Manu the son of the Sun-god.

sn: उचुश्चैनं तथा वाक्यं मानुषाणां त्वमीश्वरः॥ असिना धर्मगर्भेण पालयस्व प्रजा इति।
en: At the time of giving it to Manu, they said-You are the lord of all men. Protect all creatures with this sword having religion within its womb.

sn: धर्मसेतुमतिक्रान्ताः स्थूलसूक्ष्मात्मकारणात्॥ विभज्य दण्डं रक्ष्यास्तु धर्मतो न यदृच्छया।
en: Properly punishing those who have disregarded the restraints of virtue for the sake of the body or the mind, they should be protected according to the ordinances but never according to caprice.

sn: दुर्वाचा निग्रहो दण्डो हिरण्यबहुलस्तथा॥ व्यङ्गता च शरीरस्य वधो वानल्पकारणात्।
en: Some should be punished with rebukes, fines and forfeitures. Loss of limb or death should never be inflicted for slight offences.

sn: असेरेतानि रूपाणि दुरादीनि निर्दिशेत्॥ असेरेवं प्रमाणानि परिपाल्य व्यतिक्रमात्।
en: These punishments, having rebukes as their first, are considered as so many forms of the sword. They are the forms that the sword assumes for the sins of persons under the protection (of the king).

sn: स विसृज्याथ पुत्रं स्वं प्रजानामधिपं ततः॥ मनुः प्रजानां रक्षार्थं क्षुपाय प्रददावसिम्।
en: In time Manu installed his own son Kshupa as the king of all creatures, and gave him the sword for their protection.

sn: क्षुपाज्जग्राह चेक्ष्वाकुरिक्ष्वाकोश्च पुरूरवाः॥ आयुश्च तस्माल्लेभे तं नहुषश्च ततो भुवि।
en: Kshupa gave it to Ikshaku, and Ikshaku to Pururavas. Pururavas gave it to Ayus, and Ayus to Nahusha.

sn: ययातिनहुषाच्चापि पूरुस्तस्माच्च लब्धवान्॥ अमूर्तरयसस्तस्मात्ततो भूमिशयो नृपः।
en: Nahusha gave it to Yayati, and Yayati to Puru. Puru gave it to Amurttaraya. From Amurttaraya it went to the royal Bhumishaya.

sn: भरतश्चापि दौष्यन्तिर्लेभे भूमिशयादसिम्॥ तस्माल्लेभे च धर्मज्ञो राजन्नैलविलस्तथा।
en: Bhumishaya gave it to Dhushmanta's son Bharata. Bharata, O king, gave it to the righteous Ailavila.

sn: ततस्त्वैलविलाल्लेभे धुन्धुमारो नरेश्वरः॥ धुन्धुमाराच्च काम्बोजो मुचुकुन्दस्ततोऽलभत्।
en: Ailavila gave it to king Dhundumara. Dhundumara gave it to Kamvoja, and Kamvoja to Muchukunda.

sn: मुचुकुन्दान्मरुत्तश्च मरुत्तादपि रैवतः॥ रैवताद् युवनाश्वश्च युवनाश्वात्ततो रघुः।
en: Muchukunda gave it to Marutta, and Marutta to Raivata. Raivata gave it to Yuvanashva, and Yuvanashva to Raghu.

sn: इक्ष्वाकुवंशजस्तस्माद्धरिणाश्वः प्रतापवान्॥ हरिणावादसि लेभे शुनकः शुनकादपि। उशीनरो वै धर्मात्मा तस्माद् भोजः स यादवः॥
en: Raghu gave it to the valiant Harinashva. Harinashva gave the sword to Sunaka, and Sunaka to the righteous-souled Ushinara. From the last it was taken by the Bhojas and the Yadavas.

sn: यदुभ्यश्च शिबिर्लेभे शिबेश्चापि प्रतर्दनः। प्रतर्दनादष्टकश्च पृषदश्वोऽष्टकादपि॥
en: The Yadus gave it to Shivi. Shivi gave it to Pratarddana. Pratarddana gave it to Ashtaka, and Ashtaka to Prishadashva.

sn: पृषदश्वाद् भरद्वाजो द्रोणस्तस्मात् कृपस्ततः। ततस्त्वं भ्रातृभिः सार्धं परमासिमवाप्तवान्॥
en: Prishadashva gave it to Bharadwaja, and Bharadwaja to Drona. Drona gave it to Kripa. Kripa gave that best of swords to you and your brothers.

sn: कृत्तिकास्तस्य नक्षत्रमसेरग्निश्च दैवतम्। रोहिणी गोत्रमस्याथ रुद्रश्च गुरुरुत्तमः॥
en: The constellation under which the sword was born in Kritika. Agni is its god, and Rohini is its Gotra. Rudra is its great preceptor.

sn: असेरष्टौ हि नामानि रहस्यानि निबोध मे। पाण्डवेय सदा यानि कीर्तयन् लभते जयम्॥
en: The sword has eight names which are not generally known. Hear as I name them to you. If one mentions these names, O son of Pandu, one may always acquire victory.

sn: असिर्विशसनः खड्गस्तीक्ष्णधारो दुरासदः। श्रीगर्भो विजयश्चैव धर्मपालस्तथैव च॥
en: Those names then are Asi, Vaishasana, Khadga, Sharp-edged, hard of acquisition, Shrigarbha, victory and protector of virtue.

sn: अग्रयः प्रहरणानां च खड्गो माद्रवतीसुत। महेश्वरप्रणीतश्च पुराणे निश्चयं गतः॥
en: Of all weapons, O son of Madravati, the sword is the greatest. The Puranas truly say that it was first held by Mahadeva.

sn: पृथुस्तूत्पादयामास धनुराधमरिंदमः। तेनेयं पृथिवी दुग्धा सस्यानि सुबहून्यपि। धर्मेण च यथापूर्वं वैन्येन परिरक्षिता॥
en: Regarding the bow, again, O chastiser of enemies, it was Prithu who first created it. It was with the help of this weapon that that son of Vena, while he ruled the Earth virtuously for many years, milked her profusely of crops and grain.

sn: तदेतदाएं माद्रेय प्रमाणं कर्तुमर्हसि। असेच पूजा कर्तव्या सदा युद्धविशारदैः॥
en: You should, O son of Madri, consider what the Rishis have said as sufficient proof. All persons skilled in battle should adore the sword.

sn: इत्येष प्रथमः कल्पो व्याख्यातस्ते सुविस्तरात्। असेरुत्पत्तिसंसर्गो यथावद् भरतर्षभ॥
en: I have now told you truly the first portion of your question fully, about the origin and creation of the sword, O foremost of Bharata's family.

sn: सर्वथैतदिदं श्रुत्वा खड्गसाधनमुत्तमम्। लभते पुरुषः कीर्ति प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते॥
en: By hearing of this excellent story of the origin of the sword, a man acquires fame in this world and eternal happiness in the next.'

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तवति भीष्मे तु तूष्णीभूत युधिष्ठिरः। पप्रच्छावसथं गत्वा भ्रातृन् विदुरपञ्चमान्॥ धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च लोकवृत्तिः समाहिता। तेषां गरीयान् कतमो मध्यमः को लघुश्च कः॥
en: Vaishampayana said When after having said this, Bhishma became silent, Yudhishthira (and the others) returned home. Addressing his brothers with Vidura forming the fifth, the king said,-'The course of the world depends upon Virtue, Profit and Desire. Amongst these three, which is the foremost, which the second, and which the last, in importance.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: कस्मिंश्चात्मा निधातव्यस्त्रिवर्गविजयाय वै। संहष्टा नैष्ठिकं वाक्यं यथावद् वक्तुमर्हथ॥
en: For suppressing the three vices, viz., lust, anger and covetousness), upon which of the first three (viz., Virtue, Profit and Desire) should the mind be fixed? You should all cheerfully answer this question in true words.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: ततोऽर्थगतितत्त्वज्ञः प्रथमं प्रतिमानवान्। जगाद विदुरो वाक्यं धर्मशास्त्रमनुस्मरन्॥
en: Thus addressed by the Kuru chief, Vidura, who was conversant with the science of Profit, with the course of the world and with the real nature of thing, and endued with great intellect, spoke first these words, remembering the contents of the scriptures.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: विदुर उवाच बाहुश्रुत्यं तपस्त्यागः श्रद्धा यज्ञक्रिया क्षमा। भावशुद्धिर्दया सत्यं संयमश्चात्मसम्पदः॥
en: Vidura said Study of the various scriptures, asceticism, gift, faith, celebration of sacrifices, forgiveness, sincerity of purpose, mercy, truth, self-control,-these form the possessions of Virtue.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: एतदेवाभिपद्यस्व मा तेऽभूच्चलितं मनः। एतन्मूलौ हि धर्मार्थावेतदेकपदं हि मे॥
en: Do you adopt Virtue. Let not your heart go away from it. Both virtue and worldly profit originate from these. I think that all these may be signified by one term.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: धर्मेणैवर्षयस्तीर्णा धर्मे लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः। धर्मेण देवा ववृधुर्धर्मे चार्थः समाहितः॥
en: It is by virtue that the Rishis have crossed the world. All the worlds depend upon virtue. It is by virtue that the gods acquired their superior position. Upon Virtue, Profit or Wealth depends.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: धर्मो राजन् गुणः श्रेष्ठो मध्यमो ह्यर्थ उच्यते। कामो यवीयानिति च प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: Virtue, O king, is foremost of all. Profit is said to be middling. Desire it is said by the wise, is the lowest of the three.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: तस्माद् धर्मप्रधानेन भवितव्य यतात्मना। तथा च सर्वभूतेषु वर्तितव्यं यथात्मनि॥
en: Therefore, one should live with controlled soul, paying his best attention to Virtue. One should also treat all creatures as he should do himself.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच समाप्तवचने तस्मिन्नर्थशास्त्रविशारदः। पार्थो धर्मार्थतत्त्वज्ञो जगौ वाक्यं प्रचोदितः॥
en: After Vidura had finished his say, Pritha's son Arjuna, well-skilled in the science of Profit, and conversant also with the truths of both Virtue and Profit, urged urged on (by Yudhishthira's question), said.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: अर्जुन उवाच कर्मभूमिरियं राजनिह वार्ता प्रशस्यते। कृषिर्वाणिज्यगोरक्षं शिल्पानि विविधानि च॥ अर्थ इत्येव सर्वेषां कर्मणामव्यतिक्रमः। न ह्यतेऽर्थेन वर्तेत धर्मकामाविति श्रुतिः॥
en: Arjuna said This world O king, is the field of work. Action, therefore, is spoken highly of here. Agriculture, trade, tending of cattle, and various kinds of arts, form what is called profit. Profit, again, is the end of all such acts. Without profit or wealth, both virtue and desire cannot be acquired. This is the injunction of the Shruti.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: विषयैरर्थवान् धर्ममाराधयितुमुत्तमम्। कामं च चरितुं शक्तो दुष्प्रापमकृतात्मभिः॥
en: Even persons of impure souls, if possessed of various sorts of wealth, can perform the highest acts of virtue and gratify desires that cannot be easily satisfied.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: अर्थस्यावयवावेतौ धर्मकामाविति श्रुतिः। अर्थसिद्ध्या विनिर्वृत्तावुभावेतौ भविष्यतः॥
en: Virtue and Desire are the limbs of Wealth as the Shruti says. With the acquisition of Wealth, both Virtue and the objects of desire may be acquired.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: तद्गतार्थं हि पुरुषं विशिष्टतरयोनयः। ब्रह्माणमिव भूतानि सततं पर्युपासते॥
en: Like all creatures adoring Brahman, even persons of superior birth adore man possessed of Wealth.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: जटाजिनधरा दान्ताः पङ्कदिग्धा जितेन्द्रियाः। मुण्डा निस्तन्तवश्चापि वसन्त्यार्थिनः पृथक्॥
en: Even they who are clad in deerskins and bear matted locks on their heads, who are selfcontrolled, who smear their bodies with mire, who have their senses under complete control, even they who have bald heads and that are devoted Brahmacharins, and ad who live separated from one another, cherish a desire for Wealth.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: काषायवसनाश्चान्ये श्मश्रुला हीनिषेविणः। विद्वांसश्चैव शान्ताश्च मुक्ताः सर्वपरिग्रहैः॥ अार्थिनः सन्ति केचिदपरे स्वर्गकाङ्क्षिणः। कुलप्रत्यागमाश्चैके स्वं स्वं धर्ममनुष्ठिताः॥
en: Other clad in yellow robes, bearing long beards endued with modesty, and learning, contented, and freed from all attachments seek Wealth. Others, following the conduct of their ancestors, and observing their respective duties, and others desirous of heaven, do the same.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: आस्तिका नास्तिकाश्चैव नियताः संयमे परे। अप्रज्ञानं तमोभूतं प्रज्ञानं तु प्रकाशिता॥
en: Believers and unbelievers, and those who practise the highest Yoga all speak of the excellence of Wealth.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: भृत्यान् भोगैर्द्विषो दण्डैर्यो योजयति सोऽर्थवान्। एतन्मतिमतां श्रेष्ठ मतं मम यथातथम्। अनयोस्तु निबोध त्वं वचनं वाक्यकण्ठयोः॥
en: He, indeed, is said to be truly possessed of Wealth who pleases his dependants with objects of enjoyment, and punishes his enemies. This, O foremost of intelligent men, is my opinion. Hear now Nakula and Sahadeva, who are about to speak.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो धर्मार्थकुशलौ माद्रीपुत्रावनन्तरम्। नकुलः सहदेवश्च वाक्यं जगदतुः परम्॥
en: After Arjuna had ceased, the two sons of Madri, viz., Nakula and Sahadeva, said these words of high import.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: नकुलसहदेवावूचतुः आसीनश्च शयानश्च विचरन्नपि वा स्थितः। अर्थयोगं दृढं कुर्याद् योगैरुच्चावचैरपि॥
en: Sitting or lying, walking or standing, one should try to acquire Wealth even by the most difficult means.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: अस्मिंस्तु वै विनिर्वृत्ते दुर्लभे परमप्रिये। इह कामानवाप्नोति प्रत्यक्षं नात्र संशयः॥
en: If Wealth, which is difficult of acquisition and highly agreeable, be acquired, the person who has acquired it, forsooth, is seen to earn all the objects of Desire.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: योऽर्थो धर्मेण संयुक्तो धर्मो यश्चार्थसंयुतः। तद्धि त्वामृतसंवादं तस्मादेतौ मताविह॥
en: That Wealth which is connected with Virtue, as also that Virtue which is connected with Wealth, is certainly like ambrosia. For this reason we hold these opinions.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: अनर्थस्य न कामोऽस्ति तथार्थोऽधर्मिणः कुतः। तस्मादुद्विजते लोको धर्मार्थाद् यो बहिष्कृतः॥
en: A person without wealth cannot satisfy any desire; likewise, there can be no Wealth in one who is destitute of virtue. He, therefore, who has no virtue, or wealth, is feared by the world.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: तस्माद् धर्मप्रधानेन साध्योऽर्थः संयतात्मना। विश्वस्तेषु हि भूतेषु कल्पते सर्वमेव हि॥
en: One should, therefore, try to acquire Wealth with a devoted mind, without neglecting the requirements of Virtue. They who have faith in this injunction succeed in gaining whatever they desire.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: धर्मं समाचरेत् पूर्वं ततोऽर्थं धर्मसंयुतम्। ततः कामं चरेत् पश्चात् सिद्धार्थः स हि तत्परम्॥
en: One should first practise Virtue; next amass Wealth without sacrificing virtue; and then seek the gratification of Desire; for this should be the last act of one who has successfully acquired Wealth.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विरेमतुस्तु तद् वाक्यमुक्त्वा तावश्विनोः सुतौ। भीमसेनस्तदा वाक्यमिदं वक्तुं प्रचक्रमे॥
en: Vaishampayana continued After having said these words, the twin son of the Ashvins remained silent. Then Bhimasena began to say.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: भीमसेन उवाच नाकामः कामयत्यर्थं नाकामो धर्ममिच्छति। नाकामः कामयानोऽस्ति तस्मात् कामो विशिष्यते॥
en: Bhimasena said One without Desire never seeks Wealth. One without Desire never seeks Virtue. One who is destitute of Desire has no wish. Desire, therefore, is the foremost of all the three.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: कामेन युक्ता ऋषयस्तपस्येव समाहिताः। पलाशफलमूलादा वायुभक्षाः सुसंयताः॥
en: It is under the influence of Desire that the very Rishis practise penances, living upon fruits, or living upon roots or air only.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: वेदोपवेदेष्वपरे युक्ताः स्वाध्यायपारगाः। श्राद्धयज्ञक्रियायां च तथा दानप्रतिग्रहे॥
en: Others endued with Vedic learning always read the Vedas and their auxiliaries or perform rites of faith and sacrificial acts, or make gifts or accept them.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: वणिजः कर्षका गोपाः कारवः शिल्पिनस्तथा। देवकर्मकृतश्चैव युक्ताः कामेन कर्मसु॥
en: Traders, agriculturists, cattle-keepers, artists and artisans, and those who are engaged in rites of propitiation, all act from Desire.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: समुद्रं वा विशन्त्यन्ये नराः कामेन संयुताः। कामो हि विविधाकारः सर्वं कामेन संततम्॥
en: There are some who go into the depths of the ocean, actuated by Desire. Desire, indeed, assumes various forms. Everything is permeated by the principle of Desire.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: नास्ति नासीन्नाभविष्यद् भूतं कामात्मकात् परम्। एतत् सारं महाराज धर्मार्थावत्र संस्थितौ॥
en: A man who has no Desire never is, was, or will be, seen in this world. This, O king, is the truth. Both Virtue and Wealth depend upon Desire.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: नवनीतं यथा दध्नस्तथा कामोऽर्थधर्मतः। श्रेयस्तैलं हि पिण्याकाद् घृतं श्रेय उदश्वितः।
en: As butter is the essence of curds, so is Desire the essence of Profit and Virtue. Oil is better than oil-seeds. Clarified butter is better than sour milk.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: श्रेयः पुष्पफलं काष्ठात् कामो धर्मार्थयोर्वरः॥ पुष्पतो मध्विव रसः काम आभ्यां तथा स्मृतः। कामो धर्मार्थयोर्योनिः कामश्चाथ तदात्मकः॥
en: Flowers and fruits are better than wood. Likewise, Desire is better than Virtue and Profit. As honey is extracted from flowers, so is desire from these two. Desire is the father of Virtue and profit. Desire is the soul of these two.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: नाकामतो नाकामतो ददति ब्राह्मणेभ्यः। नाकामतो विविधा लोकचेष्टा तस्मात्कामः प्राक् त्रिवर्गस्य दृष्टः॥
en: Without Desire the Brahmanas would never give either sweets or riches to Brahmanas. Without Desire the various kinds of action which are seen in the world would never have been seen. For these reasons, Desire is the foremost of the three objects.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: र्मदोत्कटाभिः प्रियदर्शनाभिः। रमस्व योषाभिरुपेत्य कामं कामो हि राजन्परमो भवेन्नः॥
en: Approaching beautiful women clad in excellent robes, decorated with ornaments and up with sweet wines, do you sport with them. Desire, O king, is the foremost of the three with us.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: बुद्धिर्ममैषा परिखास्थितस्य माभृद्विचारस्तव धर्मपुत्र। स्यात् संहितं सद्भिरफल्गुसारं ममेति वाक्यं परमानृशंसम्॥
en: Thinking upon the question to its very roots, I have arrived at this conclusion. Do not hesitate to accept this conclusion, O son of Dharma! These words of mine are not shallow. Fair as they are, they will be acceptable to all good men.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: धर्मार्थकामाः सममेव सेव्या यो होकभक्तः स नरो जघन्यः। तयोस्तु दाक्ष्यं प्रवदन्ति मध्यं स उत्तमो योऽभिरतस्त्रिवर्गे॥
en: Virtue, Profit, and Desire should all be equally pursued. That man who follows only one of them is certainly not a superior person. He is middling who follows only two of them. He, on the other hand, is the best who follows all the three.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: प्राज्ञः सुहृच्चन्दनसारलिप्तो विचित्रमाल्याभरणैरुपेतः। ततो वचः संग्रहविस्तरेण प्रोक्त्वाथ वीरान् विरराम भीमः॥
en: Having said these words both briefly and fully, to those heroes, Bhima endued with wisdom, surrounded by friends smeared with sandal-paste, and decorated with beautiful garlands and ornaments, remained silent.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: ततो मुहूर्तादथ धर्मराजो वाक्यानि तेषामनुचिन्त्य सम्यक्। उवाचवाचावितथं स्मयन् वै लब्धश्रुतां धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठः॥
en: Then the just king Yudhishthira, that foremost of virtuous men, endued with great of you learning, thinking only for some time upon the words spoken by all of them, and thinking all those speeches to be false philosophy himself spoken as follows:

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच निःसंशयं निश्चितधर्मशास्त्राः सर्वे भवन्तो विदितप्रमाणाः। विज्ञातुकामस्य ममेह वाक्यमुक्तं यद्वै नैष्ठिकं तच्छ्रुतं मे।
en: Yudhishthira said Forsooth, all have settled conclusions regarding the scriptures, and all of you know well the authorities. I have heard these words.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: इदं त्ववश्यं गदतो ममापि वाक्य निबोधध्वमनन्यभावाः॥ यो वै न पापे निरतो न पुण्ये नार्थे न धर्मे मनुजो न कामे। विमुक्तदोषः समलोष्टकाञ्चनो विमुच्यते दुःखसुखार्थसिद्धेः॥
en: Listen now, with rapt attention, to what I say to you. He who is not employed in virtue or in sin, he who does not attend to Profit, or Virtue, or Desire, who is above all shortcomings, who regards gold and a clod of Earth with equal eyes, becomes freed from pleasure and pain and the necessity of accomplishing his purposes.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: भूतानि जातिस्मरणात्मकानि जराविकारैश्च समन्वितानि। भूयश्च तैस्तैः प्रतिबोधितानि। मोक्ष प्रशंसन्ति न तं च विद्मः॥
en: All creatures are subject to birth and death. All are liable to decay and change. Risen to their senses by the various benefits and evils of life, all of them speak highly of liberation. We do not know, however, what liberation is.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: स्नेहेन युक्तस्य न चास्ति मुक्तिरिति स्वयम्भूर्भगवानुवाच। बुधाश्च निर्वाणपरा भवन्ति तस्मान्न कुर्यात् प्रियमप्रियं च॥
en: The Self-sprung and divine Brahman has said that there is no liberation for him who is fettered with ties of attachment and love. The learned, however, seek Extinction. Therefore, one should never regard anything as either pleasant or unpleasant.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: एतत् प्रधानं च न कामकारो यथा नियुक्तोऽस्मि तथा करोमि। भूतानि सर्वाणि विधिनियुङ्क्ते विधिर्वलीयानिति वित्त सर्वे॥
en: This view seems to be the best. Not one in this world can act as he likes. I act precisely as I am made to do. The great Creator makes all creatures move as He wills. The Creator is Supreme. Know this, all of you.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: न कर्मणाऽऽप्नोत्यनवाष्यमर्थे यद्भावि तद्वै भवतीति वित्त। त्रिवर्गहीनोऽपि हि विन्दतेऽर्थं तस्मादहो लोकहिताय गुह्यम्॥
en: No one can, by his deed, acquire what is unobtainable. That which is to be, occurs. Know this. And since one who has withdrawn himself from the three-fold objects may acquire liberation, it seems, therefore, that liberation yields the highest good,

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तदग्रयं वचनं मनोमुगं समस्तमाज्ञाय ततो हि हेतुमत्। तदा प्रणेदुश्च जहर्षिरे च ते कुरुप्रवीराय च चक्रिरेऽञ्जलिम्॥
en: Having heard all these most significant reasonable and pleasant words, Bhima and others were filled with joy and joining their hands, bowed to that prince of Kuru's race.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: सुचारुवर्णाक्षरचारुभूषितां मनोनुगां निधुतवाक्यकण्टकाम्। निशम्य तां पार्थिव पार्थभाषितां गिरं नरेन्द्राः प्रशशंसुरेव ते॥
en: O king, having heard those sweet words of the king, acceptable to the heart, and divested of dissonant sounds and words, indeed, those foremost of men began to speak highly of Yudhishthira.

description: The question of Nakula-the first creation of the sword and the author thereof
sn: स्तदा प्रतीतान् प्रशशंस वीर्यवान्। पुनश्च पप्रच्छ सरिद्वरासुतं ततः परं धर्ममहीनचेतसम्॥
en: The great and highly energetic son of Dharma, in return, praised his auditors; and more the king addressed Bhishma, possessed of a high soul, for enquiring about duties. once

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामह महाप्राज्ञ कुरूणां प्रीतिवर्धन। प्रश्नं कञ्चितप्रवक्ष्यामि तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: O grandfather, you of great wisdom, I shall ask you a question. You should, O enhancer of the joy of the Kurus, to describe it fully to me.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: कीदृशा मानवाः सौम्याः कैः प्रीतिः परमा भवेत्। आयत्यां च तदात्वे च के क्षमास्तान् वदस्व मे॥
en: What kind of man are gentle by nature? With whom may the best friendship exists? Tell us also who are able to do good now and in the future.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: न हि तत्र धनं स्फीतं न च सम्बन्धिबान्धवाः। तिष्ठन्ति यत्र सुहृदस्तिष्ठन्तीति मतिर्मम॥
en: I think that neither increasing wealth, nor relatives, nor kinsmen occupy that place which well-meaning friends do.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: दुर्लभो हि सुहच्छ्रोता दुर्लभश्च हितः सुहृत्। एतद् धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ सर्वं व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: A friend capable of hearing beneficial advice, and also of doing good, is highly rare! You should foremost of virtuous men, describe fully those subjects.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: भीष्म उवाच संधेयान् पुरुषान् राजन्नसंधेयांश्च तत्त्वतः। वदतो मे निबोध त्वं निखिलेन युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said Hear, O Yudhishthira, as I speak to you fully of those men with whom friendships may be contracted and those with whom friendships should not be made.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: लुब्धः क्रूरस्त्यक्तधर्मा निकृतिः शठ एव च। क्षुद्रः पापसमाचारः सर्वशङ्की तथालसः॥ दीर्घसूत्रोऽनृजुः क्रुष्टो गुरुदारप्रधर्षकः। व्यसने यः परित्यागी दुरात्मा निरपत्रपः॥ सर्वतः पापदर्शी च नास्तिको वेदनिन्दकः। सम्प्रकीर्णेन्द्रियो लोके यः कामं निरतश्चरेत्॥ असत्यो लोकविद्विष्टः समये चानवस्थितः। पिशुनोऽथाकृतप्रज्ञो मत्सरी पापनिश्चयः॥ दुःशीलोऽथाकृतात्मा च नृशंसः कितवस्तथा। मित्रैरपकृतिनित्यमिच्छतेऽर्थं परस्य यः॥ ददतश्च यथाशक्ति यो न तुष्यति मन्दधीः। अधैर्यमपि यो युङ्क्ते सदा मित्रं नरर्षभ॥ अस्थानक्रोधनोऽयुक्तो यश्चाकस्माद् विरुध्यते। सुहृदश्चैव कल्याणानाशु त्यजति किल्बिषी॥ अल्पेऽप्यपकृते मूढस्तथाज्ञानात् कृतेऽपि च। कार्यसेवी च मित्रेषु मित्रद्वेषी नराधिप॥ शत्रुमित्रमुखो यश्च जिह्यप्रेक्षी विलोचनः। न विरज्यति कल्याणे यस्त्यजेत् तादृशं नरम्॥
en: One who is covetous, one who has cast off the duties of his castes, one who is dishonest, one who is a knave, one who is mean, one who is of sinful deeds, one who suspects all, one who is idle, one who is procrastinating, one who is of a crooked nature, one who is a butt of universal censure one who dishonours the life of his preceptor, one who is addicted to the seven well-known vices, one who shuns distressed friends, one who is wicked, one who is shameless, one whose eyes are always on sin, one who is an atheist, one who vilifies the Vedas, one whose senses are not under control, one who is lustful, one who is untruthful, one who is forsaken by all, one who disregards all restraints, one who is deceitful, one who is destitute of wisdom, one who is envious, one who is sinful, one whose conduct is bad, one whose soul is not been purified, one who is cruel, one who is a gambler, one who always tries to injure friends, one who covets an other's wealth, that wicked man who is never content with what another may give him according to his means, one who is never pleased with his friends, O foremost of men, one who becomes angry on bad occasions, one who is of restless mind, one who quarrels without cause, that sinful man who feels no scruple in deserting well-meaning friends, that wretch who always seeks his own interests and who, O king, falls out with friends when these do him a very slight injury or do him a wrong unknowingly, one who acts like an enemy but speaks like a friend, one who is perverse in perception, one who does not see his own good, one who never finds pleasure in what is good for himself or others, should be shunned.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: पानपो द्वेषणः क्रोधी निघृणः परुषस्तथा। परोपतापी मित्रध्रुक् तथा प्राणिवधे रतः॥ कृतघ्नश्चाधमो लोके न संधेयः कदाचन। छिद्रान्वेषी ह्यसंधेयः संधेयानपि मे शृणु॥
en: One who drinks wine, one who hates others, one who is angry, one who is merciless, one who feels pain on seeing other's happiness, one who injures friends, one who always kills living creatures, one who is ungrateful, one who is vile, should be shunned. Friendship should never be contracted with any of them. Likewise, no friendship should be made with him who is always busy with seeing the faults of others. Listen now to me as I mention the persons, with whom friendship may be contracted.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: कुलीना वाक्यसम्पन्ना ज्ञानविज्ञानकोविदाः। रूपवन्तो गुणोपेतास्तथाऽलुब्धा जितश्रमाः॥ सन्मित्राश्च कृतज्ञाश्च सर्वज्ञा लोभवर्जिताः। माधुर्यगुणसम्पन्नाः सत्यसंधा जितेन्द्रियाः॥ व्यायामशीलाः सततं कुलपुत्राः कुलोद्वहाः। दोषैः प्रमुक्ताः प्रथितास्ते ग्राह्या: पार्थिवैर्नराः॥
en: The well-born, the eloquent, the polite, the learned and scientific men, they that are of beautiful and pleasant features, the accomplished and meritorious persons, those who are free from covetousness, those who are never worn out with labour those who are good to their friends, the grateful, those who keep varied information and knowledge, those who are shorn of avarice, those who are endued with agreeable qualities, those who are firm in truth, those who have subjugated their senses, those who are devoted to athletic and other exercises, those who are nobly born, those who multiply their families, those who are shorn of faults, those who are possessed of fame, should be accepted by kings for making friendship with them.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: यथाशक्ति समाचाराः सम्प्रतुष्यन्ति हि प्रभो। नास्थाने क्रोधवन्तश्च न चाकस्माद् विरागिणः। विरक्तश्च न दुष्यन्ति मनसाप्यर्थकोविदाः॥ आत्मानं पीडयित्वापि सुहृत्कार्यपरायणाः। विरज्यन्ति न मित्रेभ्यो वासो रक्तमिवाविकम्॥ क्रोधाच्च लोभमोहाभ्यां नानर्थे युवतीषु च। न दर्शयन्ति सुहृदो विश्वस्ता धर्मवत्सलाः॥ लोष्टकाञ्चनतुल्यार्थाः सुहृत्सु दृढबुद्धयः। ये.चरन्त्यभिमानानि सृष्टार्थमनुषङ्गिणः॥ संगृह्णन्तः परिजनं स्वाम्यर्थपरमाः सदा। ईदृशैः पुरुषश्रेष्ठैर्यः संधिं कुरुते नृपः॥ तस्य विस्तीर्यते राज्यं ज्योत्स्ना ग्रहपतेरिव।
en: Those, again, O king, who become pleased and contented if one treats them according to the best of his powers, those who never get angry on occasions when anger should be displayed, those who never become displeased without sufficient cause, those persons who are well-read in the science of Profit and who even when annoyed, can keep their minds quiet, those who give themselves up to the service of friends at personal sacrifice, those who never cast off their friends, but who remain unchanged in their attachment) like a red blanket made of wool, those who never disregard, from anger, those who are poor, those who never dishonour young women by giving way to lust and loss of judgement, those who never show wrong paths to friends, those who are trustworthy, those who always, practise righteousness, those who consider gold and clod of earth with an equal eye, those who are devoted to friends and well-wishers, those who collect their own people and try to be friend them, without caring for their own dignity and their own respectability, should be considered as persons with whom (friendship) should be formed. Indeed, the kingdoms of that king spread on all sides, like the light of the moon, who makes friendship with such superior men.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: शास्त्रनित्या जितक्रोधा बलवन्तो रणे सदा॥ जन्मशीलगुणोपेताः संधेयाः पुरुषोत्तमाः।
en: Friendship should be formed with men who are well-practised in weapons, who have completely subjugated their anger, who are always strong in battle and are highly born, and are of good behaviour, and varied accomplishments.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: ये च दोषसमायुक्ता नराः प्रोक्ता मयानघ।॥ तेशामप्यधमा राजन् कृतघ्ना मित्रघातकाः। त्यक्तव्यास्तु दुराचाराः सर्वेषामिति निश्चयः॥
en: Amongst the vicious men, O sinless one, that I have mentioned, the vilest, o king, are those who are ungrateful and who injure friends. Those wicked persons should be shunned by all. This, indeed, is a settled injunction.'

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच विस्तरेणाथ सम्बन्धं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः। मित्रद्रोही कृतघ्नश्च यः प्रोक्तस्तद् वदस्व मे।।२८।
en: Yudhishthira said I wish to hear fully this description. Tell me who they are who injure friends and ungrateful persons.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: भीष्म उवाच हन्त ते वर्तयिष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम्। उदीच्यां दिशि यद् वृत्तं म्लेच्छेषु मनुजाधिप॥
en: I shall recite to you an old story the incidents of which took place in the country, O king, of the Mlecchas that lies to the north.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: ब्राह्मणो मध्यदेशीयः कश्चिद् वै ब्रह्मवर्जितः। ग्रामं वृद्धियुतं वीक्ष्य प्राविशद भैक्ष्यकासया॥
en: There was a certain Brahmana of the middle country. He had no Vedic learning. (One day), seeing a prosperous village, the man entered it from desire of getting alms.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: तत्र दस्युर्धनयुतः सर्ववर्णविशेषवित्। ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यसंधश्च दाने च निरतोऽभवत्।॥
en: In that village lived a very rich robber conversant with the characteristics of all the castes, devoted to the Brahmanas, firm in truth, and always engaged in making gifts.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: तस्य क्षयमुपागम्य ततो भिक्षामयाचत। प्रतिश्रयं च वासार्थं भिक्षां चैवाथ वार्षिकीम्॥
en: Going to the house of that robber, the Brahmana begged for alms. Indeed, he prayed for a house to live in and the necessaries of life lasting for a year.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: प्रादात् तस्मै स विप्राय वस्त्रं च सदृशं नवम्। नारी चापि वयोपेतां भ; विरहितां तथा॥
en: Thus begged by the Brahmana, the robber gave him a piece of new cloth with its ends complete, and a young widow.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: एतत् सम्प्राप्य हृष्टात्मा दस्योः सर्वं द्विजस्तथा। तस्मिन् गृहवरे राजंस्तया रेमे स गौतमः॥
en: Getting all those things from the robber, the Brahmana become filled with joy. Gautama began to live happily in that big house given to him by the robber.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: कुटुम्बार्थं च दास्याश्च साहाय्यं चाप्यथाकरोत्। तत्रावसत् स वर्षांश्च समृद्धे शबरालये॥
en: He began to help the relatives and kinsmen of the female slave the robber-chief gave him. Thus he lived for many years in that prosperous village of hunters.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: बाणवेधे परं यत्नमकरोच्चैव गौतमः। चक्राङ्गान् स च नित्यं वै सर्वतो वनगोचरान्॥ जघान गौतमो राजन् यथा दस्युगणास्तथा। हिंसापटुघृणाहीन: सदा प्राणिवधे रतः॥ गौतमः संनिकर्षेण दस्युभिः समतामियात्।
en: He began to practise with great zeal the art of archery. Every day, like the other robbers living there, Gautama, o king, went into the forest and killed a large number of wild cranes. Always engaged in killing living creatures, he became well-skilled in that act and soon became shorn of mercy. For his intimacy with robbers he became one like one of them.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: तथा तु वसतस्तस्य दस्युग्रामे सुखं तदा॥ अगमन् बहवो मासा निघ्नतः पक्षिणो बहून्।
en: Living happily in that robber village for many months, he killed a number of wild cranes.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: ततः कदाचिदपरो द्विजस्तं देशमागतः॥ जटाचीराजिनधरः स्वाध्यायपरमः शुचिः।
en: One day another Brahmana came to that village. He was clad in rags and deer-skins and bore matted locks on his head. Of highly pure conduct, he was devoted to the study of the Vedas.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: विनीतो नियताहारो ब्रह्मण्यो वेदपारगः॥ स ब्रह्मचारी तद्देश्यः सखा तस्यैव सुप्रियः।
en: Of a humble disposition, of restricted diet, devoted to the Brahmanas, well-read in ihe Vedas, and observant of Brahmacharya vows, that Brahmana had been a dear friend of Gautama and belonged to that part of the country from which Gautama had come.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: तं दस्युग्राममगमद् यत्रासौ गौतमोऽवसत्॥ स तु विप्रगृहान्वेषी शूद्रानपरिवर्जकः।
en: In course of his peregrinations, as already said, the Brahmana came to that robber village where Gautama was living. He never accepted any food if given by a Shudra and, therefore, began to look for the house of a Brahmana there.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: ग्रामे दस्युसमाकीर्णे व्यचरत् सर्वतोदिशम्॥ ततः स गौतमगृहं प्रविवेश द्विजोत्तमः। गौतमश्चापि सम्प्राप्तस्तावन्योन्येन संगतौ॥ चक्राङ्गभारस्कन्धं तं धनुष्पाणिं धृतायुधम्। रुधिरेणावसिक्ताङ्गं गृहद्वारमुपागतम्॥
en: Accordingly he wandered in every direction in that village filled with robber-families. At last that foremost of Brahmanas came to the house of Gautama. It so happened that just then Gautama also, returning from the forest, was entering his house. The two friends met. Armed with bow and sword, he carried on his shoulders a load of killed cranes, and his body was covered with the blood that trickled down from the bag on his shoulders.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा पुरुषादाभमपध्वस्तं क्षयागतम्। अभिज्ञाय द्विजो व्रीडत्रिदं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing that man who looked like a cannibal and who had fallen away from the pure practices of his caste, and entering his house, the newly-arrived guest, recognising him, O king, said these words

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: किमिदं कुरुषे मोहाद् विप्रस्त्वं हि कुलोद्वहः। मध्यदेशपरिज्ञातो दस्युभावं गतः कथम्॥ पूर्वान् स्मर द्विज ज्ञातीन् प्रख्यातान् वेदपारगान्। तेषां वंशेऽभिजातस्त्वमीदृशः कुलपांसनः॥
en: What is this that you are doing here out of ignorance. You are a Brahmana, and the perpetuator of a Brahmana family. Born in a respectable family belonging to the Middle country, how is it that you have become like a robber in your conduct.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: अवबुध्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं सत्त्वं शील श्रुतं दमम्। अनुक्रोशं च संस्मृत्य त्यज वासमिमं द्विज॥
en: Recollect, O twice-born one, your famous kinsmen of former times, all of whom were well-read in the Vedas. Born in their family, alas, you have sullied it.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: स एवमुक्तः सुहृदा तेन तत्र हितैषिणा। प्रत्युवाच ततो राजन् विनिश्चित्य तदार्तवत्॥
en: Awake yourself by your own exertions. Remembering the power, the conduct, the learning, the self-control, the mercy (which belong to your caste), leave this your present house, O twice-born one.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: निर्धनोऽस्मि द्विजश्रेष्ठ नापि वेदविदप्यहम्। वित्तार्थमिह सम्प्राप्तं विद्धि मां द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Thus spoken to by that well-meaning friend of his, O king, Gautama answered him in great distress of heart, saying,-O foremost of twiceborn ones, I am poor. I have no knowledge of the Vedas. Know, O best of Brahmanas, that I have taken up my quarters here for the sake of money only.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: त्वदर्शनात् तु विप्रेन्द्र कृतार्थोऽस्म्यद्य वै द्विज। आवां हि सह यास्यावः श्वो वसस्वाद्य शर्वरीम्॥
en: Seeing you, however, I am blessed to-day. We shall together leave this place tomorrow. Do you spend the night here with me.

description: Vidura's discourse on virtue, Profit and Pleasure. An account of men gentle by nature and of true friends
sn: स तत्र न्यवसद् विप्रो घृणी किञ्चिदसंस्पृशन्। क्षुधितश्छन्द्यमानोऽपि भोजनं नाभ्यनन्दत॥
en: Thus accosted, the newly-arrived Brahmana, full of mercy as he was, passed the night there, without touching anything. Though hungry and requested again and again, the guest refused to touch any food in that house.

sn: भीष्म उवाच तस्यां निशायां व्युष्टायां गते तस्मिन् द्विजोत्तमे। निष्क्रम्य गौतमोऽगच्छत् समुद्रं प्रति भारत॥
en: Bhishma said After the expiration of that night, and that best of Brahmanas had left the house, Gautama issuing from his house, began to proceed towards the sea, O Bharata.

sn: सामुद्रिकान् स वणिजस्ततोऽपश्यत् स्थितान् पथि। स तेन सह सार्थेन प्रययौ सागरं प्रति॥
en: On the way he saw some sea-faring merchants. With that caravan of merchants he proceeded towards the sea.

sn: स तु सार्थो महान् राजन् कस्मिंश्चिद् गिरिगह्वरे। मत्तेन द्विरदेनाथ निहतः प्रायशोऽभवत्॥
en: It so took place, however, O king, that large caravan was attacked, while passing through a mountain valley, by an infuriate elephant. Almost all the persons were killed.

sn: स कथंचिद् भयात् तस्माद् विमुक्तो ब्राह्मणस्तथा। कांदिग्भूतो जीवितार्थी प्रदुद्रोवात्तरां दिशम्॥
en: Somehow escaping from the great danger, the Brahmana fled towards the north for saving his life, not knowing where he went.

sn: स तु सार्थपरिभ्रष्टस्तस्माद् देशात् तथा च्युतः। एकाकी व्यवरत् तत्र वने किंपुरुषो यथा।॥
en: Separated from the caravan and gone to a great distance, he began to travel alone in a forest, like a Kimpurusha.

sn: स पन्थानमथासाद्य समुद्राभिसरं तदा। आससाद वनं रम्यं दिव्यं पुष्पितपादपम्॥
en: At last coming upon a road leading towards the ocean, he travelled on till the reached a charming and heavenly forest filled with blossoming trees.

sn: सर्वर्तुकैराम्रवणैः पुष्पितैरुपशोभितम्। नन्दनोद्देशसदृशं यक्षकिन्नरसेवितम्।।७।
en: It was adorned with mango trees which carried flowers and fruits throughout the year. It appeared like the garden of Nandana (in heaven) and was inhabited by Yakshas and Kinnaras.

sn: शालैस्तालैस्तमालैश्च कालागुरुवनैस्तथा। चन्दनस्य च मुख्यस्य पादपैरुपशोभितम्।
en: It was also decked with Shalas Palmyras, Tamalas, and with clusters of black aloes, and many large sandal trees.

sn: गिरिप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु तेषु तेषु सुगन्धिषु॥ समन्ततो द्विजश्रेष्ठास्तत्राकूजन्त वै तदा।
en: Upon the charming tablelands that he beheld there, fragrant with perfumes of various kinds, birds of the best species were always heard to send out their sweet notes.

sn: मनुष्यवदनाश्चान्ये भारुण्डा इति विश्रुताः॥ भूलिङ्गशकुनाश्चान्ये सामुद्राः पर्वतोद्भवाः।
en: Other birds, called Bharundas and having faces like human beings, and those called Bhulingas, and others belonging mountainous regions and to the sea, poured forth their sweet notes.

sn: स तान्यतिमनोज्ञानि विहगानां रुतानि वै॥ शृण्वन् सुरमणीयानि विप्रोऽगच्छत् गौतमः।
en: Gautama went through that forest, listening, as he went, to those delightful and charming notes of nature's songsters.

sn: ततोऽपश्यत् सुरम्येषु सुवर्णसिकताचिते॥ देशे समे सुखे चित्रे स्वर्णोद्देशसमे नृप।
en: On his way he saw a very charming and level spot of land covered with golden sands and resembling heaven itself, O king, in its beauty.

sn: श्रिया जुष्टं महावृक्षं न्यग्रोधं च सुमण्डलम्॥ शाखाभिरनुरूपाभिर्भूयिष्ठं क्षत्रसंनिभम्।
en: On that plot was huge and beautiful banian with a spherical top. Having numberless branches which wore like the parent tree in beauty and size, that banian looked like an umbrella set over the plain, to

sn: सुखः शिवः। तस्य मूलं च संसिक्तं वरचन्दनवारिणा॥ दिव्यपुष्पान्वितं श्रीमत् पितामहसभोपमम।
en: The spot underneath that beautiful tree was drenched with water perfumed with the most fragrant sandal. Highly beautiful and abounding with sweet flowers all around, the spot appeared like the court of the Grandfather himself.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा गौतमः प्रीतो मन:कान्तमनुत्तमम॥ मेध्यं सुरगृहप्रख्यं पुष्पितैः पादपैर्वृतम्।
en: Seeing that charming and peerless spot, filled with blossoming trees, sacred, and looking like the house of a very god, Gautama was highly pleased.

sn: तमासाद्य मुदा युक्तस्तस्याधस्तादुपाविशत्॥ तत्रासीनस्य कौन्तेय गौतमस्य पुष्पाणि समुपम्पृश्य प्रववावनिल: शुभः। ह्लादयन् सर्वगात्राणि गौतमस्य तदा नृप॥
en: Arrived there, he sat himself down with a delighted mind. While sitting there, O son of Kunti, a swect, charming, and auspicious breeze, carrying the perfume of many kinds of flowers, began to blow softly, cooling the limbs of Gautama and filling him with divine pleasure, O king.

sn: स तु विप्रः प्रशान्तश्च स्पृष्टः पुण्येन वायुना। सुखमासाद्य सुष्वाप भास्करश्चास्तमभ्ययात्॥
en: Fanned by that sweet-scented breeze, the Brahmana became refreshed, and for the pleasure he felt ho soon fell asleep. Meanwhile the sun set behind the setting hills.

sn: ततोऽस्तं भास्करे याते संध्याकाल उपस्थिते। आजगाम स्वभवनं ब्रह्मलोकात् खगोत्तमः॥
en: When the shining luminary entered his chambers in the west and the evening twilight came, a bird that was the best of his species, returned there, which was his home, from the regions of Brahinan.

sn: नाडीजङ्घ इति ख्यातो दयितो ब्रह्मणः सखा। बकराजो महाप्राज्ञः कश्यपस्यात्मसम्भवः॥
en: His name was Nadijangha and he was a great friend of the Creator. He was a prince of Cranes; endued with great wisdom, and a son of (the sage) Kashyapa.

sn: राजधर्मेति विख्यातो बभूवाप्रतिमो भुवि। देवकन्यासुतः श्रीमान् विद्वान् देवसमप्रभः॥
en: He was also known widely on Earth by the name of Rajdharman. Indeed, he excelled every one on Earth in fame and wisdom. The child of a celestial maiden, endued with great beauty and learning, he shone like a celestial.

sn: पृष्टाभरणसम्पन्नो भूषणैरर्कसंनिभैः। षितः सर्वगात्रेषु देवगर्भः श्रिया ज्वलन्॥
en: Decorated with the many ornaments that he wore and that were as brilliant as the sun himself, that child of a celestial girl shone in great beauty.

sn: तमागतं खगं दृष्ट्वा गौतमो विस्मितोऽभवत्। क्षुत्पिपासापरिश्रान्तो हिंसार्थी चाभ्यवेक्षत॥
en: Seeing that bird arrived there, Gautama was stricken with wonder. Worn out with hunger and thirst, the Brahmana began to look at the bird from desire of killing him.

sn: राजधर्मोवाच स्वागतं भवतो विप्र दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि मे गृहम्। अस्तं च सविता यातः संध्येयं समुपस्थिता।॥
en: Rajdharman said Welcome, O Brahmana! By good luck have I got you to-day in my house! The sun is set. The evening twilight has came.

sn: मम त्वं निलय प्राप्तः प्रियातिथिरनिन्दितः। पूजितो यास्यसि प्रातर्विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: Having come to my house you are to-day my dear and excellent guest! Having received my adorations according to the rites laid down in the scriptures, you may go where you like tomorrow morning.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: भीष्म उवाच गिरं तां मधुरां श्रुत्वा गौतमो विस्मितस्तदा। कौतूहलान्वितो राजन् राजधर्माणमैक्षत॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these sweet words Gautama was filled with wonder. Feeling at the same time a great curiosity, he looked at Rajadharman without being able to with draw his eyes from him.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: राजधर्मोवाच भोः कश्यपस्य पुत्रोऽहं माता दाक्षायणी च मे। अतिथिस्त्वं गुणोपेतः स्वागतं ते द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Rajadharman said O Brahmana, I am the son of Kashyapa by one of the daughters of (the sage) Dhaksha. Highly meritorious as you are, you are my guest to-day! You are welcome, O foremost of Brahmana.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: भीष्म उवाच तस्मै दत्त्वा स सत्कारं विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा। शालपुष्मयीं दिव्यां बृसीं वै समकल्पयत्।॥
en: Bhishma said Having offered him hospitality according to the scriptural rites, the crane made an excellent bed of the Shala flowers that lay all around.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: भगीरथरथाक्रान्तदेशान् गङ्गानिषेवितान्। ये चरन्ति महामीनास्तांश्च तस्यान्वकल्पयत्॥
en: He also gave him several large fishes caught from the deep waters of the Bhagirathi.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: वह्निं चापि सुसंदीप्तं मीनांश्चापि सुपीवरान्। स गौतमायातिथये न्यवेदयत काश्यपिः॥
en: Indeed, the son of Kashyapa offered for the acceptance of his guest Gautama a burning fire and certain large fishes.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: भुक्तवन्तं च तं विप्रं प्रीतात्मानं महातपाः। क्लमापनयनार्थं स पक्षाभ्यामभ्यवीजयत्॥
en: After the Brahmana had eaten and became satisfied, the bird having asceticism for his wealth began to fan him with his wings for removing his fatigue.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: ततो विश्रान्तमासीनं गोत्रप्रश्नमपृच्छत। सोऽब्रवीद् गौतमोऽस्मीति ब्रह्म नान्यदुदाहरत्॥
en: Seeing his guest seated at his ease, he asked him about his birth. The man answered, saying, I am a Brahmana by the name of Gautama!-and then became silent.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: तस्मै पर्णमयं दिव्यं दिव्यपुष्पाधिवासितम्। गन्धाढ्यं शयनं प्रादात् स शिश्ये तत्र वै सुखम्॥
en: The bird offered his guest a soft bed made of leaves and perfumed with many sweetscented flowers. Gautama lay on it, and felt great happiness.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: अथोपविष्टं शयने गौतमं धर्मराट् तदा। पप्रच्छ काश्यपो वाग्मी किमागमनकारणम्॥
en: When Gautama had laid himself down, the eloquent son of Kashyapa, who was like Yama himself in his knowledge of duties, asked him about the cause of his arrival there.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: तोऽब्रवीद् गौतमस्तं दरिद्रोऽहं महामते। समुद्रगमनाकाङ्क्षी द्रव्यार्थमिति भारत॥
en: Gautama answered him, saying, I am, O great one, very poor. For acquiring riches I wish to go to the sea.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: तं काश्यपोऽबवीत् प्रीतो नोत्कण्ठां कर्तुमर्हसि। कृतकार्यो द्विजश्रेष्ठ सद्रव्यो यास्यसे गृहान्॥
en: The son of Kashyapa cheerfully told him,You should not feel any anxiety. You shall succeed, O foremost of Brahmanas, and shall return home with property.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: चतुर्विधा ह्यर्थसिद्धिवृहस्पतिमतं यथा। पारम्पर्य तथा दैवं काम्यं मैत्रमिति प्रभो॥
en: The sage Brihaspati has mentioned four kinds of expedients for the acquisition of wealth, viz., inheritance, sudden acquisition due to good luck or the favour of the gods, acquisition by labour, and acquisition through the help or kindness of friends.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: प्रादुर्भूतोऽस्मि ते मित्रं सुहत्त्वं च मम त्वयि। सोऽहं तथा यतिष्यामि भविष्यसि यथार्थवान्॥
en: I have become your friend. I entertain good feelings towards you! I shall, therefore, try in such a way that you may acquire wealth.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: ततः प्रभातसमये सुखं दृष्ट्वाब्रवीदिदम्। गच्छ सौम्य पथानेन कृतकृत्यो भविष्यसि॥
en: The night passed away and morning came. Seeing his guest rise cheerfully from bed, the bird said, Go, O amiable one, along this very path and you are sure to succeed.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: इतस्त्रियोजनं गत्वा राक्षसाधिपतिर्महान्। विरूपाक्ष इति ख्यातः सखा मम महाबलः॥
en: At the distance of about three Yojanas from this place, there is a powerful king of the Rakshasas. Highly strong as he is, his name is Virupaksha, and he is a friend of mine.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: तं गच्छ द्विजमुख्यं त्वं स मद्वाक्यप्रचोदितः। कामानभीप्सितांस्तुभ्यं दाता नास्त्यत्र संशयः॥
en: Go to him, O foremost of Brahmanas! That chief, at my request, will, forsooth, give you as much wealth as you wish to have.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: इत्युक्तः प्रययौ राजन् गौतमो विगतक्लमः। फलान्यमृतकल्पानि भक्षयन् स यथेतः॥
en: Thus addressed, O king, Gautama cheerfully started from that place, eating on the way, to his best satisfaction, fruits sweet as nectar.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: चन्दनागुरुमुख्यानि त्वक्पत्राणां वनानि च। तस्मिन् पथि महाराज सेवमानो द्रुतं ययौ॥
en: Seeing the sandal and aloe and birch trees that stood along the road, and enjoying their refreshing shade, the Brahmana went on quickly.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: ततो मेरुव्रजं नाम नगरं शैलतोरणम्। शैलप्राकारवप्रं च शैलयन्त्राकुलं तथा॥
en: He then reached the city of Meruvraja. It had lare porches made of stone, and high stone walls. It was also girted on all sides with a ditch, and large pieces of rock and engines of many kinds were kept in readiness on the ramparts.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: विदितश्चाभवत् तस्य राक्षसेन्द्रस्य धीमतः। प्रहितः सुहृदा राजन् प्रीयमाण: प्रियातिथिः॥
en: He soon became known to the highly intelligent Rakshasa chief O king, as a dear guest sent to him by the chief's friend (the crane). The chief received Gautama very gladly.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: ततः स राक्षसेन्द्रः स्वान् प्रेष्यानाह युधिष्ठिर। गौतमो नगरद्वाराच्छीघ्रमानीयतामिति॥
en: The king of the Rakshasas then, O Yudhishthira, ordered his attendants, saying,Bring Gautama soon here from the gate.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: ततः पुरवरात् तस्मात् पुकषा: श्येनचेष्टनाः। गौतमेत्यभिभाषन्तः पुरद्वारमुपागमन्॥
en: At the behest of the king, certain persons, quick as hawks, went out from the splendid palace of their ruler, and proceeding to the gate accosted Gautama.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: ते तमूचुर्महाराज राजप्रेष्यास्तदा द्विजम्। त्वरस्व तूर्णमागच्छ राजा त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छति॥
en: The royal messengers, O monarch, said to that Brahmana,-Come quickly, the king wishes to see you.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: राक्षसाधिपतिर्वीरो विरूपाक्ष इति श्रुतः। स त्वां त्वरति वै द्रष्टुं तत् क्षिप्रं संविधीयताम्॥
en: You may have heard of the king of the Rakshasas, Virupaksha by name, endued with great courage. He is impatient of seeing you! Come quickly and delay not.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: ततः स प्राद्रवद् विप्रो विस्मयाद् विगलक्लमः। गौतमः परमधिं तां पश्यन् परमविस्मितः॥
en: Thus accosted, the Brahmana, forgetting is exhaustion in his surprise, ran with the messengers. Seeing the great prosperity of the city, he was filled with wonder.

description: The meeting of Goutama with the Rakshasa chief
sn: तैरेव सहितो राज्ञो वेश्म तूर्णमुपाद्रवत्। दर्शनं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य काङ्खमाणो द्विजस्तदा।॥
en: He soon entered the king's palace in the company of the messengers, desirous of seeing the king of the Rakshasas. He soon entered the king's palace in the company of the messengers, desirous of seeing the king of the Rakshasas.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः स विदितो राज्ञः प्रविश्य गृहमुत्तमम्। पूजितो राक्षसेन्द्रेण निषसादासनोत्तमे॥
en: Bhishma said Conducted into a spacious apartment, Gautama was introduced to the king of the Rakshasas. Adored by the latter, he sat on an excellent seat.

sn: पृष्टश्च गोत्रचरणं स्वाध्यायं ब्रह्मचारिकम्। न तत्र व्याजहारान्यद् गोत्रमात्रादृते द्विजः॥
en: The king asked him about his caste and his practices, his study of the Vedas and his observance of the Brahmacharya vow. The Brahmana, however, without answering the other questions, only stated his name and caste.

sn: ब्रह्मवर्चसहीनस्य स्वाध्यायोपरतस्य च। गोत्रमात्रविदो राजा निवासं समपृच्छत॥
en: Having ascertained only the name and the caste of his guest, and finding that he was shorn of Brahmanic splendour and Vedic studies, the king next enquired about the country of his residence.

sn: राक्षस उवाच क्वते निवासः कल्याण किंगोत्रा ब्राह्मणी च ते। तत्त्वं ब्रूहि न भी: कार्या विश्वसस्व यथासुखम्॥
en: The Rakshasa said.mom Where is your residence, O blessed one, and to what race does your wife belong? Tell us truly. Do not fear Trust us without anxiety.

sn: गौतम उवाच मध्यदेशप्रसूतोऽहं वासो मे शबरालये। शूद्रा पुनर्भूर्भार्या मे सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Gautama said I belong by birth to the Middle country. I live in a village of hunters. I have married a Shudra woman who had been a widow. What I tell you is the truth.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो राजा विममृशे कथं कार्यमिदं भवेत्। कथं वा सुकृतं मे स्यादिति बुद्ध्यान्वचिन्तयत्॥
en: Bhishma said The king then began to think as to what he should do. Indeed, the king began to think how he might acquire merit.

sn: अयं वै जन्मना विप्रः सुहृत् तस्य महात्मनः। सम्प्रेषितश्च तेनायं काश्यपेन ममान्तिकम्॥
en: He said to himself,-This man is by birth a Brahmana. He is, again, a friend of the great Rajadharman. He has been sent to me by that son of Kashyapa.

sn: तस्य प्रियं करिष्यामि स हि मामाश्रितः सदा। भ्राता मे बान्धवश्चासौ सखा च हृदयङ्गमः॥
en: I must do as my friend desires me. He is very intimate with me. He is my brother, and a dear relative. He is, indeed a friend, of my heart.

sn: कातिक्यामद्य भोक्तारः सहस्रं मे द्विजोत्तमाः। तत्रायमपि भोक्ता च देयमस्मे च मे धनम्॥
en: On this day of the month of Kartika, a thousand Brahmanas of the highest order are to be entertained in my house. This Gautama also shall be entertained with them and I shall give wealth to him too.

sn: स चाद्य दिवस: पुण्यो ह्यतिथिश्चायमागतः। संकल्पितं चैव धनं किं विचार्यमतः परम्॥
en: This is a sacred day. Gautama has come here as a guest. The wealth that is to be given away is ready. What is there then to think of.

sn: ततः सहस्रं विप्राणां विदुषां समलंकृतम्। स्नातानामनुसम्प्राप्तं सुमहत् क्षौमवाससाम्॥
en: Just about this time a thousand Brahmanas, endued with great learning, with bodies purified by baths and adorned with sandalpaste and flowers, and clad in long robes of linen, came there.

sn: तानागतान् द्विजश्रेष्ठान् विरूपाक्षो विशाम्पते। यथार्ह प्रतिजग्राह विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: The Rakshasa king Virupaksha, O monarch, received the guests, as they came, duly and according to the rites sanctioned in the scriptures.

sn: बृस्यस्तेषां तु संन्यस्ता राक्षसेन्द्रस्य शासनात्। भूमौ वरकुशा: स्तीर्णाः प्रेष्यैर्भरतसत्तम्॥
en: By the order of the king, skins were spread out of them. The royal servants then, O best of the Bharatas, spread mats of Kusha grass on the ground.

sn: तासु ते पूजिता राज्ञा निषण्णा द्विजसत्तमाः। तिलदर्भोदकेनाथ अर्चिता विधिवद् द्विजाः॥
en: Having been duly adored by the king, those foremost of Brahmanas, sat down on those seats. The Rakshasa chief once more adored his guests, according to the ordinance, with sesame seeds, green blades of grass, and water.

sn: विश्वेदेवाः सपितरः साग्नयचोपकल्पिता:। विलिप्ताः पुष्पवन्तश्च सुप्रचाराः सुपूजिताः। व्यराजन्त महाराज नक्षत्रपतयो यथा।॥
en: Some of them were selected for representing the Vishvedevas, the Pitris, and the gods of fire. These were smeared with sandal-paste, and flowers were offered to them. They were also worshipped with the other sorts of costly offerings.

sn: ततो जाम्बूनदीः पात्रीर्वज्राङ्का विमलाः शुभाः। वरान्नपूर्णा विप्रेभ्यः प्रादान्मधुघृतप्लुताः॥ तस्य नित्यं सदाऽऽषाढ्यां माध्यां च बहवो द्विजाः। ईप्सितं भोजनवरं लभन्ते सत्कृतं सदा॥ विशेषतस्तु कार्तिक्यां द्विजेभ्यः सम्प्रयच्छति। शरट्यपाये रत्नानि पौर्णमास्यामिति श्रुतिः॥ सुवर्णं रजतं चैव मणीनथ च मौक्तिकान्॥ वज्रान महाधनांश्चैव वैदूर्याजिनराङ्कवान्। रत्नराशीन् विनिक्षिप्य दक्षिणार्थे स भारत॥ ततः प्राह द्विजश्रेष्ठान् विरूपाक्षो महाबलः। गृह्णीत रत्नान्येतानि यथोत्साहं यथेष्टतः॥
en: After such worship, every one of them looked as effulgent as the moon in the sky. Then bright and polished golden plates, adorned with engravings, and filled with rich viands prepared with clarified butter and honey, were given to those Brahmanas. Every year in the month of Ashada and Magha, a great number of Brahmanas used to receive from he Rakshasa chief, after proper honours, the most excellent food which they desired. Especially, on the day of full moon in the month of Kartika, after the termination of autumn, the king use to give to the Brahmanas much wealth of various kinds, including gold, silver, jewels, gems, pearls, costly diamonds, stones of the lapis lazuli variety, deer-skins, and skins of the Ranku deer.
