Indeed, O Bharata, throwing a mass of wealth of various sorts for giving it away as Dakshina, the powerful Virupaksha, addressing those foremost Brahmanas, said to them,-Take from these jewels and gems as much as you wish and can hope to carry away.

sn: येषु येषु च भाण्डेषु भुक्तं वो द्विजसत्तमाः। तान्येवादाय गच्छध्वं स्ववेश्मानीति भारत॥
en: He also said to them, O Bharata, these words—Taking those golden plates, and vessels which you have used for your dinner, go away, O foremost of Brahmanas.

sn: इत्युक्तवचने तस्मिन् राक्षसेन्द्रे महात्मनि। यथेष्टं तानि रत्नानि जगृहुर्ब्राह्मणर्षभाः॥
en: When these words were uttered by the great Rakshasa chief, those foremost of Brahmanas, took as much wealth as each desired.

sn: ततो महाहैस्ते सर्वे रत्नैरभ्यर्चिताः शुभैः। ब्राह्मणा मृष्टवसनाः सुप्रीता: स्म ततोऽभवन्॥
en: Adored with those rich jewels and gems, those best of Brahmanas, clad in excellent robes, were filled with delight.

sn: ततस्तान् राक्षसेन्द्रश्च द्विजानाह पुनर्वचः। नानादेशगतान् राजन् राक्षसान् प्रतिषिध्य वै॥ अद्यैकं दिवसं विप्रा न वोऽस्तीह भयं क्वचित्। राक्षसेभ्यः प्रमोदध्वमिष्टतो यात माचिरम्॥
en: Having restrained the Rakshasas that had come to his palace from various countries, the Rakshasa king, once more, addressed those Brahmanas and said,—This one day, ye twiceborn ones, you need have no fear from the Rakshasas here. Sport you as you wish, and then go away quickly.

sn: ततः प्रदुद्रुवुः सर्वे विप्रसंघाः समन्ततः। गौतमोऽपि सुवर्णस्य भारमादाय सत्वरः॥
en: Then, leaving that place, the Brahmanas, went away in all directions quickly. Gautama also, having taken up a heavy quantity of gold immediately, went away.

sn: कृच्छ्रात् समुद्धरन् भारं न्यग्रोधं समुपागमत्। न्यषीदच्च परिश्रान्तः क्लान्तश्च क्षुधितश्च सः॥
en: Carrying the load with difficulty, he reached the former banian tree. He sat down, fatigued, worn out, and hungry.

sn: ततस्तमभ्यगाद् राजन् राजधर्मा खगोत्तमः। स्वागतेनाभिनन्दंश्च गौतमं मित्रवत्सलः॥
en: While Gautama was taking rest there, that best of birds, viz., Rajadharman, O king, came there. Devoted to friends, he gladdened Gautama by welcoming him.

sn: तस्य पक्षाग्रविक्षेपैः क्लमं व्यपनयत् खगः। पूजां चाप्यकरोद् धीमान् भोजनं चाप्यकल्पयत्।॥
en: By flapping his wings he began to fan his guest and remove his fatigue. Highly intelligent as he was, he adored Gautama and made arrangements for his food.

sn: स भुक्तवान् सुविश्रान्तो गौतमोऽचिन्तयत् तदा। हाटकस्याभिरूपस्य भारोऽयं सुमहान् मया॥ गृहीतो लोभमोहाभ्यां दूरं च गमनं मम। न चास्ति पथि भोक्तव्यं प्राणसंधारणं मम॥
en: Having eaten and refreshed himself, Gautama began to think,—Heavy is the load which I have taken of bright gold, actuated by covetousness and folly. I have a long way to travel. I have no food by which I can live on Imy way.

sn: किं कृत्वा धारयेयं वै प्राणानित्यभ्यचिन्तयत्। ततः स पथि भोक्तव्यं प्रक्षमाणो न किंचन॥
en: What should I do for keeping my life?— Thus he thought. It so happened that even upon much thinking he found no food which he could eat on the way.

sn: कृतघ्नः पुरुषव्याघ्र मनसेदमचिन्तयत्। अयं बकपतिः पार्श्वे मांसराशिः स्थितो महान्॥ इमं हत्वा गृहीत्वा च यास्येऽहं समाभिद्रुतम्॥
en: Ungrateful as he was, O foremost of men, he thus thought.-This prince of cranes, so large and having a heap of flesh, is by my side. Killing and bagging him, I shall leave this place and go away quickly.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अथ तत्र महार्चिष्माननलो वातसारथिः। तस्याविदूरे रक्षार्थ खगेन्द्रेण कृतोऽभवत्॥
en: Bhishma said There, under that banian tree for the protection of his guest, the prince of birds had lighted and kept up a fire with high and burning flames.

sn: स चापि पार्श्वे सुष्वाप विश्वस्तो बकराट् तदा। कृतघ्नस्तु स दुष्टात्मा तं जिघांसुरथाग्रतः॥
en: On one side of the fire, the bird slept confidently. The ungrateful and wicked wretch prepared to kill his sleeping host.

sn: ततोऽलातेन दीप्तेन विश्वस्तं निजघान तम्। निहत्य च मुदा युक्तः सोऽनुबन्धनं दृष्टवान्॥
en: With the help of that blazing fire he killed the trustful bird, and having killed him, became filled with joy, never thinking there was sin in what he did.

sn: स तं विपक्षरोमाणं कृत्वाग्नावपचत् तदा। तं गृहीत्वा सुवर्णं व ययौ द्रुततरं द्विजः॥
en: Clearing off the feathers and the down, he roasted the flesh on that fire. Then taking it up with the gold he had brought, the Brahmana fled quickly from that place.

sn: (ततो दाक्षायणीपुत्रं नागतं तं तु भारत। विरूपाक्षश्चिन्तयन् वै हृदयेन विदूयता)। ततोऽन्यस्मिन् गते चाह्नि विरुपाक्षोऽब्रवीत् सुतम्। न प्रेक्षे राजधर्माणमद्य पुत्र खगोत्तमम्॥
en: The next day, the Rakshasa king, Virupaksha, said to his son, Alas, O son, I do not sce Rajdharman, that best of birds, to-day.

sn: स पूर्वसंध्यां ब्रह्माणं वन्दितुं याति सर्वदा। मां वा दृष्ट्वा कदाचित् स न गच्छति गृहं खगः॥
en: Every morning he goes to the regions of Brahman for worshipping the Grandfather. While returning, he never goes home without seeing me.

sn: उभे द्विरात्रिसंध्ये वै नाभ्यगात् स ममालयम्। तस्मान्न शुद्ध्यते भावो मम स ज्ञायतां सुहृत्॥
en: These two inornings and two nights have passed away, and he has not come to my house. My mind, therefore, is not in peace. You enquire after my friend.

sn: स्वाध्यायेन वियुक्तो हि ब्रह्मवर्चसवर्जितः। तव्रतस्तत्र मे शंका हन्यात तं स द्विजाधमः॥
en: Gautama, who came here, is shorn of Vedic learning and Brahmanic effulgence. He has scen the abode of my friend, I greatly fear that wretch of Brahmanas has killed Rajdharman.

sn: दुराचारस्तु दुर्बुद्धिरिङ्गित्तैर्लक्षितो मया। निष्कृतो दारुणाकारो दुष्टो दस्युरिवाधमः॥ गौतमः स गतस्तत्र तेनोद्विग्नं मनो मम।
en: Addicted to evil practices and of wicked understanding, I read him through by the signs he showed. Without mercy, of cruel and grim visage, and of wicked disposition, that vilest of men is like a robber. That Gautama has gone to the house of my friend. For this reason my heart is extremely anxious.

sn: पुत्र शीघ्रमितो गत्वा राजधर्मनिवेशनम्॥ ज्ञायतां स विशुद्धात्मा यदि जीवति मा चिरम्।
en: O son, going hence with great speed to the house of Rajdharman, learn whether that puresouled bird is still alive! Do not delay.

sn: स एवमुक्तस्त्वरितो रक्षोभिः सहितो ययौ॥ न्यग्रोधं तत्र चापश्यत् कङ्कालं राजधर्मणः।
en: Thus addressed by his father, the prince, accompanied by other Rakshasas, went away quickly. Going to the foot of that banian, he saw the remains of Rajdharman.

sn: स रुदन्नगमत् पुत्रो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य धीमतः॥ त्वरमाणः परं शक्त्या गौतमग्रहणाय वै।
en: Weeping with sorrow the son of the intelligent king of the Rakshasas, ran quickly to the best of his power, for seizing Gautama.

sn: ततोऽविदूरे जगृहुर्गौतमं राक्षसास्तदा।॥ राजधर्मशरीरं च पक्षास्थिचरणोज्झितम्।
en: The Rakshasas had not to go far when they caught the Brahmana and found the body of Rajdharman shorn of wings, bones, and feet.

sn: तमादायाथ रक्षांसि द्रुतं मेरुव्रजं ययुः॥ राज्ञश्च दर्शयामासुः शरीरं राजधर्मणः। कृतघ्नं परुषं तं च गौतमं पापकारिणम्॥
en: Taking the captive with them, the Rakshasas returned quickly to Meruvraja, and showed the king the mutilated body of Rajdharman, and that ungrateful and sinful wretch, Gautama.

sn: रुरोद राजा तं दृष्ट्वा सामात्यः सपुरोहितः। आर्तनादश्च सुमहानभूत् तस्य निवेशने॥
en: Seeing the remains of his friend, the king, with his counsellors and priest, began to weep aloud. Loud-lamentations were heard in his house.

sn: सस्त्रीकुमारं च पुरं बभूवास्वस्थमानसम्। अथाब्रवीन्नृपः पुत्रं पापोऽयं वध्यतामिति॥ अस्य मांसैरिमे सर्वे विहरन्तु यथेष्टतः।
en: The entire city of the Rakshasa king,-men, women, and children,-was plunged in grief. The king then ordered his son, saying,-Let this sinful wretch be killed! Let these Rakshasas here eai merrily his flesh.

sn: पापाचार: पापकर्मा पापात्मा पापसाधनः॥ हन्तव्योऽयं मम मतिर्भवद्भिरिति राक्षसाः। इत्युक्ता राक्षसेन्द्रेण राक्षसा घोरविक्रमा:।१९॥ नैच्छन्त तं भक्षयितुं पापकर्माणमित्युत।
en: Of sinful decds, of sinful habits, of sinful soul, and used to sin, this wretch, I think, should be killed by you!—Thus addressed by the Rakshasa king, many Rakshasas of dreadful prowess cxpressed their reluctance to eat the flesh of that sinner.

sn: दस्यूनां दीयतामेष साध्वद्य पुरुषाधमः॥ इत्यूचुस्ते महाराज राक्षसेन्द्रं निशाचराः।
en: Indeed, those night-rangers addressing their king, said,-Let this vilest of men be handed over to the robbers.

sn: शिरोभिः प्रणताः सर्वे व्याहरन् राक्षसाधिपम्॥ न दातुमर्हसि त्वं नो भक्षणायास्य किल्बिषम्।
en: Lowering their heads to their king, they told him so, adding, you should not give us this sinful wretch for our food.

sn: एवमस्त्विति तानाह राक्षसेन्द्रो निशाचरान्॥ दस्यूनां दीयतामेष कृतघ्नोऽद्यैव राक्षसाः।
en: The king said to them,-Let it be so! Let this ungrateful person be forthwith delivered to the robbers.

sn: इत्युक्ता राक्षसास्तेन शूलपट्टिशपाणयः॥ कृत्वा तं खण्डशः पापं दस्युभ्यः प्रददुस्तदा।
en: Thus ordered by him, the Rakshasas, armed with lances and battle-axes, hacked that sinful wretch into pieces and gave them away to the robbers.

sn: दस्यवश्चापि नैच्छन्त तमत्तुं पापकारिणम्। क्रव्यादा अपि राजेन्द्र कृतघ्नं नोपभुञ्जते॥
en: It so came about that even the very robbers refused to eat the flesh of that vile man. Though cannibals, O king, they would not eat an ungrateful person.

sn: ब्रह्मने च सुरापे च चौरे भग्नव्रते तथा। निष्कृतिर्विहिता राजन् कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः॥
en: There is expiation, o king, for one who slays a Brahmana, for one who drinks winc, for one who steals, for one that has not fulfilled a vow. But there is no expiation for an ungrateful person.

sn: मित्रद्रोही नृशंसश्च कृतघ्नश्च नराधमः। क्रव्यादैः कृमिभिश्चैव न भुज्यन्ते हि तादृशाः॥
en: That cruel and mean man who does injury to a friend and turns ungrateful, is not eaten even by the very cannibals nor by the worms that feed on carrion.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततश्चितां बकपते: कारयामास राक्षसः। रत्नैर्गन्धैश्च बहुभिर्वस्त्रैश्च समलंकृताम्॥
en: Bhishma Said The Rakshasa king then caused a funeral pyre to be made for that king of cranes and decked it with jewels, gems, perfumes, and, costly dresses.

sn: ततः प्रज्वाल्य नृपतिर्बकराज प्रतापवान्। प्रेतकार्याणि विधिवद् राक्षसेन्द्रश्चकार ह॥
en: Setting fire to it with the body of that prince of birds, the powerful king of the Rakshasas caused the obsequial rites of his friend to be performed according to the ordinance.

sn: तस्मिन् काले च सुरभिर्देवी दाक्षायणी शुभा। उपरिष्टात् ततस्तस्य सा बभूव पयस्विनी॥
en: At that time, the auspicious goddess Surabhi, the daughter of Daksha, appeared in the sky above the place where the pyre had been made. Her breasts were full of milk.

sn: तस्या वक्त्राच्च्युतः फेनः क्षीरमिश्रस्तदानघ। सोऽपतद् वै ततस्तस्यां चितायां राजधर्मणः॥
en: From her mouth, O sinless king, froth mixed with milk dropped upon the funeral pyre of Rajdharman.

sn: ततः संजीवितस्तेन बकराजस्तदानघ। उत्पत्य च समीयाय विरूपाक्षं बकाधिपः॥
en: There at the prince of cranes became revived. Rising up, came to his friend Virupaksha, the king of Rakshasas.

sn: ततोऽभ्यगाद् देवराजो विरूपाक्षपुरं तदा। प्राह चेदं विरूपाक्षं दिष्ट्या संजीवितस्त्वया॥
en: At this time, the king of the gods himself came to the city of Virupaksha. Addressing the Rakshasa king, Indra said, —By good luck, you have revived the prince of cranes.

sn: श्रावयामास चन्द्रस्तं विरूपाक्षं पुरातनम्। यथा शापः पुरा दत्तो ब्रह्मणा राजधर्मणः॥
en: The king of the gods further recited to Virupaksha the old story of the course imprecated by the Grandfather upon that best of birds named Rajdharman.

sn: यदा बकपती राजन् ब्रह्माणं नोपसर्पति। ततो रोषादिदं प्राह खगेन्द्राय पितामहः॥ यस्मान्मूढो मम सभां नागतोऽसौ बकाधमः। तस्माद् वधं स दुष्टात्मा नचिरात् समवाप्स्यति॥
en: Addressing the king he said, Once on a time, O monarch, this prince of cranes did not come to the region of Brahman when he was required. In anger the Grandfather said to this prince of birds,Since this vile crane has not come to-day in my assembly, therefore, that wicked one shall not soon die.

sn: तदयं तस्य वचनानिहतो गौतमेन वै। तेनैवामृतसिक्तश्च पुन: संजीवितो बकः॥
en: Over the In consequence of these words of the Grandfather, the prince of cranes, though killed by Gautama, has been restored to life, by the nectar with which his body was drenched.

sn: राजधर्मा बकः प्राह प्रणिपत्य पुरन्दरम्। यदि तेऽनुग्रहकृता मयि बुद्धि सुरेश्वर॥ सखायं मे सुदयितं गौतमं जीवयेत्युत।
en: After Indra had become silent, Rajadharman, having bowed unto the king of the gods, said, O king of gods, if you wish to show me favour, then let my dear friend Gautama be restored to life.

sn: तस्य वाक्यं समादाय वासवः पुरुषर्षभ॥ सिक्त्वामृतेन तं विप्रं गौतमं जीवयत् तदा।
en: Hearing these words of his, Vasava, O king, sprinkled ambrosia Brahmana Gautama and restored him to life.

sn: सभाण्डोपस्करं राजंस्तमासाद्य बकाधिपः॥ सम्परिष्वज्य सुहृदं प्रीत्या परमया युतः।
en: Coming to his friend Gautama who still bore on his shoulders the load of gold, the king of cranes embraced him and felt great joy.

sn: अथ तं पापकर्माणं राजधर्मा बकाधिपः॥ विसर्जयित्वा सधनं प्रविवेश स्वमालयम्।
en: Dismissing Gautama of sinful deeds, with his wealth, then Rajadharman, that prince of cranes, returned to his own abode.

sn: यथोचितं च स बको ययौ ब्रह्मसदस्तथा॥ ब्रह्मा चैनं महात्मानमातिथ्येनाभ्यपूजयत्।
en: At the due hour he went (the next day) to the Grandfather's region. The latter honoured the great bird with such attentions as are shown to a guest.

sn: गौतमश्चापि सम्प्राप्य पुनस्तं शबरालयम्। शूद्रायां जनयामास पुत्रान् दुष्कृतकारिणः॥
en: Gautama also, coming back to his home in the village of the hunters, begot many sinful children upon his Shudra wife.

sn: शापश्च सुमहांस्तस्य दत्तः सुरगणैस्तदा। कुक्षौ पुनर्वाः पापोऽयं जनयित्वाचिरात् सुतान्॥ निरयं प्राप्स्यति महत् कृतघ्नोऽयमिति प्रभो।
en: A great curse was imprecated upon him by the gods that having begouen, within a few years, upon the body of his remarried wife many children, that ungrateful sinner should sink into a dreadful hell for many years.

sn: एतत् प्राह पुरा सर्वं नारदो मम भारत॥ संस्मृत्य चापि सुमहदाख्यानं भरतर्षभ।
en: All this, O Bharata, was described to me formerly by Narada. Remembering the incidents of his important story, O best of Bharata's race, I have recited it to you fully.

sn: मयापि भवते सर्वं यथावदनुवर्णितम्॥ कुतः कृतघ्नस्य यशः कुतः स्थानं कुतः सुखम्। अश्रद्धेयः कृतघ्नो हि कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः॥
en: Whence can an ungrateful person acquire fame? Where is his place? Whence can he enjoy happiness? An ungrateful person should not be trusted. An ungrateful person can never escape.

sn: मित्रद्रोहो न कर्तव्यः पुरुषेण विशेषतः। मित्रधुड्नरकं घोरमनन्तं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: No person should injure a friend. He who injures a friend sinks into dreadful and everlasting hell.

sn: कृतज्ञेन सदा भाव्यं मित्रकामेन चैव ह। मित्राच्च लभते सर्वं मित्रात् पूजां लभेत च॥
en: Every one should be grateful, and every one should try to do good to his friends. Everything may be got from a friend. Honours may be got from friend.

sn: मित्राद् भोगांश्च भुञ्जीत मित्रेणापत्सु मुच्यते। सत्कारैरुत्तमैमित्रं पूजयेत विचक्षणः॥
en: For friends one may enjoy various objects of life. By the exertions of friends, one may escape from various sorts of danger and distress. He who is wise would honour his friends to the best of his power.

sn: परित्याज्यो बुधैः पापः कृतघ्नो निरपत्रपः। मित्रद्रोही कुलाङ्गारः पापकर्मा नराधमः॥
en: An ungrateful, shameless and sinful wretch should be shunned by the wise. One who injures his friends is a despicable character. Such a sinful person is the vilest of men.

sn: एष धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ प्रोक्तः पापो मया तव। मित्रद्रोही कृतघ्नो वै किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: I have thus told you, O foremost of all virtuous men the characteristics of a sinful wretch who is stained by ingratitude and who injures his friend. What else do you wish to hear.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा तदा वाक्यं भीष्मेणोक्तं महात्मना। युधिष्ठिरः प्रीतमना बभूव जनमेजय॥
en: Hearing these words spoken by the great Bhishma, Yudhishthira, O Janamejaya, was highly pleased.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धर्माः पितामहेनोक्ता राजधर्माश्रिताः शुभाः। धर्ममाश्रमिणां श्रेष्ठं वक्तुमर्हसि पार्थिव॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have, O grandfather, described the sacred duties of kings regarding the persons in distress. O king, you should tell me now those foremost of duties of those who lead the (four) modes of life.

sn: भीष्म उवाच सर्वत्र विहितो धर्मः स्वर्ग्यः सत्यफलं तपः। बहुद्वारस्य धर्मस्य नेहास्ति विफला क्रिया॥
en: Bhishma said Religion has many doors. The observance of the duties sanctioned by religion can never be useless. Duties have been laid down regarding every mode of life. The fruits of Penance with regard to the development of the Soul, are to be had in this worid.

sn: यस्मिन् यस्मिस्तु विषये यो यो याति विनिश्चयम्। स तमेवाभिजानाति नान्यं भरतसत्तम॥
en: The object to which one devotes oneself, whatever it may be, O Bharata, and nothing else, appears to as the highest of acquisitions fraught with the greatest of blessings.

sn: यथा यथा च पर्येति लोकतन्त्रमसारवत्। तथा तथा विरागोऽत्र जायते नात्र संशयः॥
en: When one meditates properly, one comes to know that the things of this world are useless one as straw. Forsooth, one is then freed from attachment of those things.

sn: एवं व्यवसिते लोके बहुदोषे युधिष्ठिर। आत्ममोक्षनिमित्तं वै यतेत मतिमान् नरः॥
en: When the world, O Yudhishthira, which is full of shortcomings, is so framed, every intelligent man, should try to acquire the liberation of his soul.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच नष्टे धने वा दारे वा पुत्रे पितरि वा मृते। यया बुद्ध्या नुदेच्छोकं तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, by what condition of mind should one kill his grief when he loses his riches, or his wife, or son, or father.

sn: भीष्म उवाच नष्ट धने वा दारे वा पुत्रे पितरि वा मृते। अहो दुःखमिति ध्यायशोकस्यापचितिं चरेत्॥
en: Bhishma said, When one's wealth is lost, or one's wife or son or father is dead, he certainly says to oneself,-Alas, it is a great sorrow,-But then one should, by the help of meditation, try to kill that grief.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। यथा सेनजितं विप्रः कश्चिदेत्याब्रवीत् सुहृत्॥
en: Regarding it is mentioned the old story of the speech that a twice-born friend of his, coming to Senajit's court, made to that king.

sn: पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तं राजानं शोकविह्वलम्। विषण्णमनसं दृष्ट्वा विप्रो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing the monarch stricken with grief and burning with sorrow on account of the death of his son, the Brahmana said to that king of very

sn: किं नु मुह्यसि मूढस्त्वं शोच्यः किमनुशोचसि। यदा त्वामपि शोचन्तः शोच्या यास्यन्ति तां गतिम्।।१०
en: Why are you stupefied? You are without any intelligence. You are yourself an object of grief, why do you grieve (for others)? A few days hence others will grieve for you, and in their turn they will be grieved for by others still.

sn: त्वं चैवाहं च ये चान्ये त्वामुपासन्ति पार्थिव। सर्वे तत्र गमिष्यामो यत एवागता वयम्॥
en: Yourself, myself, and others who wait upon you, O king, shall all repair whence all of us have come.

sn: सेनजिदुवाच का बुद्धिः किं तपो विप्र कः समाधिस्तपोधना किं ज्ञानं किं श्रुतं चैव यत् प्राप्य न विषीदसि॥
en: Senajit said What is that intelligence, what that penance, O learned Brahmana, what that concentration of mind, O you having asceticism for wealth, what that knowledge, and what that learning, by gaining which you do not give way to grief?

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच पश्य भूतानि दुःखेन व्यतिषिक्तानि सर्वशः। उत्तमाधममध्यानि तेषु तेष्विह कर्मसु॥
en: The Brahmana said See, all creatures-the superior, the middling, and the inferiorm-on account of their respective acts, and entangled in sorrow.

sn: आत्मापि चायं न मम सर्वा वा पृथिवी मम। यथा मम तथाऽन्येषामिति चिन्त्य न मे व्यथा।।
en: I do not consider even my own self to be mine. On the other hand, I consider the whole world to be mine. I again consider all this as much mine as it belongs to others. Grief cannot attack me for this thought.

sn: एतां बुद्धिमहं प्राप्य न प्रहृष्ये न च व्यथे॥ यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महोदधौ। समेत्य च व्यपेयातां तद्वद्भूतसमागमः॥
en: Having gained such an understanding, I do not give way to joy or to grief. As two pieces of wood floating on the sea meet together at one time and are again separated, so is the union of (living) creatures in this world.

sn: एवं पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च ज्ञातयो बान्धवास्तथा। तेषां स्नेहो न कर्तव्यो विप्रयोगो ध्रुवो हि तैः॥
en: Sons, grandsons, kinsmen relatives, are all of this nature. One should One should never feel attachment for them, for separation with them is inevitable.

sn: अदर्शनादापतितः पुनश्चादर्शनं गतः। न त्वासौ वेद न त्वं तं कः सन् किमनुशोचसि॥
en: Your son came from an invisible quarter. He has gone away and become invisible. He did not know you. You did not know him. Who are you and for whom do you grieve.

sn: तृष्णार्तिप्रभवं दुःखं दुःखार्तिप्रभवं सुखम्। सुखात् संजायते दुःखं दुःखमेवं पुनः पुनः॥
en: Grief is the child of the disease created by desire. Happiness again comes when the disease of desire is cured. From joy originates sorrow, and sorrow comes again and again.

sn: सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं दुःखस्यानन्तरं सुखम्। सुखदुःखे मनुष्याणां चक्रवत् परिवर्ततः॥
en: Sorrow comes after joy, and joy after sorrow. The joys and sorrows of human beings are revolving on a wheel.

sn: सुखात् त्वं दुःखमापन्न पुनरापत्स्यसे सुखम्। न नित्यं लभते दुःखं न नित्यं लभते सुखम्॥
en: After happiness sorrow has come to you. You will again enjoy happiness for good and no one enjoys happiness for good.

sn: शरीरमेवायतनं सुखस्य दुःखस्य चाप्यायतनं शरीरम्। यद्यच्छरीरेण करोति कर्म तेनैव देही समुपाश्नुते तत्।।
en: The body is the abode of both sorrow and happiness. An embodied creature suffers the consequences of whatever acts he performs with the help of his body.

sn: जीवितं च शरीरेण जात्यैव सह जायते। उभे सह विवर्तेते उभे सह विनश्यतः॥
en: Life comes with the creation of the body. The two exist together, and the two die together.

sn: स्नेहपाशैर्बहुविधैराविष्टविषया जनाः। अकृतार्थाश्च सीदन्ते जलैः सैकतसेतवः॥
en: Men of impure souls, attached to worldly objects by various fetters, disappear like embankments of sand in water.

sn: स्नेहेन तिलवत् सर्वं सर्गचक्रे निपीड्यते। तिलपीडैरिवाक्रम्य क्लेशैरज्ञानसम्भवैः॥
en: Miseries of various sorts begotten by ignorance, act like pressers of oil-seeds, for attacking all creatures for their attachments; these press them like oil-seeds in the oilmaking machine subjecting them to the round of re-births.

sn: संचिनोत्यशुभं कर्म कलत्रापेक्षया नरः। एकः क्लेशानवाप्नोति परत्रेह च मानवः॥
en: Man, for the sake of his wife, commits numberless evil deeds, but suffers alone various kinds of misery both in this and the next world.

sn: पुत्रदारकुटुम्बेषु प्रसक्ताः सर्वमानवाः। शोकपङ्कार्णवे मग्ना जीर्णा वनगजा इव॥
en: All men, attached to children, wives kinsmen and relatives sink in the miry sea of sorrow like wild elephants, when shom of strength, sinking in a miry slough.

sn: पुत्रनाशे वित्तनाशे ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिनामपि। प्राप्यते सुमहद् दुःखंदावाग्निप्रतिमं विभो।
en: Indeed, O king, upon loss of wealth or son or kinsmen or relatives, man suffers great misery burning him like a forest fire.

sn: दैवायत्तमिदं सर्वं सुखदुः :खे भवाभवौ॥ असृहत् ससुहृच्चापि सशत्रुर्मित्रवानपि। सप्रज्ञः प्रज्ञया हीनो दैवेन लभते सुखम्॥
en: All this, viz., joy and grief, existence and non-existence depend upon destiny. One having friends as well as one having none, one having enemies as well as one having none, one having wisdom as well as one shorn of it, each and every one amongst these, enjoys happiness through destiny.

sn: नालं सुखाय सुहृदो नालं दुःखाय शत्रवः। न च प्रज्ञालमर्थानां न सुखानामलं धनम्॥
en: Friends are not the root of one's happiness. Enemies are not the root of one's misery. Wisdom cannot bring on wealth; wealth cannot give happiness.

sn: न बुद्धिर्धनलाभाय न जाड्यमसमृद्धये। लोकपर्यायवृत्तान्तं प्राज्ञो जानाति नेतरः॥
en: Intelligence cannot give wealth, nor is stupidity the cause of poverty. Only a wise man, and none else, understands the order of the world.

sn: बुद्धिमन्तं च शूरं च मूढं भीरुं जडं कविम्। दुर्बलं बलवन्तं च भागिनं भजते सुखम्॥
en: Of the intelligent, the heroic, the foolish, the cowardly, the idiotic, the earned, the weak, or the strong, happiness comes to him only for whom it is ordained.

sn: धेनुर्वत्सस्य गोपस्य स्वामिनस्तस्करस्य च। पयः पिबति यस्तस्या धेनुस्तस्येति निश्चयः॥
en: The cow belongs to the calf, to the cowherd who is her master, and to the thief. Indeed, she is his who drinks her milk.

sn: ये च मूढतमा लोके ये च बुद्धेः परं गताः। ते नराः सुखमेधन्ते क्लिश्यत्यन्तरितो जनः॥
en: They whose understandings are dormant, and they who have that state of the mind which lies beyond the range of the intellect, succeed in enjoying happiness. Only they who are between these two classes, suffer misery.

sn: अन्त्येषु रेमिरे धीरा न ते मध्येषु रेमिरे। अन्त्यप्राप्तिं सुखामाहुर्दुःखमन्तरमन्त्ययोः॥
en: The wise find pleasure in the two extremes but not in the intermediate states. The sages have said that the attainment of any of these two extremes form happiness. Misery lies in the intermediate states between the two.

sn: ये च बुद्धिसुखं प्राप्ता द्वन्द्वातीता विमत्सराः। तान् नैवार्था न चाना व्यथयन्ति कदाचन॥
en: Those who have succeeded in acquiring real happiness, and who have become freed from the pleasures and pains of this world, and who are shorn of envy, are never moved by either the accession of wealth or its loss.

sn: अथ ये बुद्धिमप्राप्ता व्यतिक्रान्ताश्च मूढताम्। तेऽतिवेलं प्रहृष्यन्ति संतापमुपयान्ति च॥
en: Those who have not gained that intelligence which brings on real happiness, but who have got over folly and ignorance yield to excessive joy and excessive misery.

sn: नित्यं प्रमुदिता मूढा दिवि देवगणा इव। अवलेपेन महता परिभूत्या विचेतसः॥
en: Men who have no ideas of right or wrong, who are beside themselves with pride and with success over others, give way to transports of delight like the celestials.

sn: सुखं दुःखान्तमालस्यं दुःखं दाक्ष्यं सुखोदयम्। भूतिस्त्वेवं श्रिया सार्धं दक्षे वसति नालसे॥
en: Happiness must terminate in misery. Idleness is misery; while cleverness (in action) is the root of felicity. Affluence and prosperity live in a clever man, but not in an idle wight.

sn: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं प्रियं वा यदि वाप्रियम्। प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपासीत हृदयेनापराजितः॥
en: Be it happiness or be it misery, be it pleasant or be it otherwise, what comes to one should be enjoyed or put up with an unconquered heart.

sn: शोकस्थानसहस्त्राणि भयस्थानशतानि च। दिवसे दिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम्॥
en: Every day a thousand occasions for sorrow, and a hundred occasions for fear attack an ignorant and foolish man but a wise man is never so affected.

sn: बुद्धिमन्तं कृतप्रज्ञं शुश्रूषुमनसूयकम्। दान्तं जितेन्द्रियं चापि शोको न स्पृशते नरम्॥
en: Sorrow can never touch an intelligent man, one who has acquired wisdom, one who obeys the instructions of his elders, one who has no envy, and one who has controlled his self.

sn: एतां बुद्धिं समास्थाय गुप्तचित्तश्चरेद् बुधः। उदयास्तमयज्ञं हि न शोकः स्पष्टुमर्हति॥
en: Depending upon such an understanding, and guarding his heart (against the influences of desire and the passions), the wise man should work on in this world. Indeed, sorrow cannot affect him who knows that Supreme Self from which everything emanate and to which everything disappears.

sn: यन्निमित्तं भवेच्छोकस्तापो वा दुःखमेव च। आयासो वा यतो मूलमेकाङ्गमपि तत् त्यजेत्॥
en: The very root of grief, or heart-burning, or sorrow or of action, should, even if it be a part of one's body, the cast off.

sn: किंचिदेव ममत्वेन यदा भवति कल्पितम्। तदेव परितापार्थं सर्वं सम्पद्यते तथा॥
en: That object, whatever it may be, which one considers as his own, is a source of grief and heart-burning.

sn: यद् यत् यजति कामानां तत् सुखस्याभिपूर्यते। कामानुसारी पुरुषः कामाननुविनश्यति॥
en: If objects, of desire, are renounced they become sources of happiness. The man who follows objects of desire is ruined in that pursuit.

sn: यच्च कामसुखं लोके यच्च दिव्यं महत् सुखम्। तृष्णाक्षयसुखस्यैते नार्हतः षोडशी कलाम्॥
en: Neither the happiness which is derived from a gratification of the senses nor that great happiness which one may enjoy in heaven, even comes up to a sixteenth part of the happiness which originates from the destruction of all desire.

sn: पूर्वदेहकृतं कर्म शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्। प्राज्ञं मूढं तथा शूरं भजते यादृशं कृतम्॥
en: The consequences of pristine decds, right or wrong, affect the wise and the foolish, the brave and the mind.

sn: एवमेव किलैतानि प्रियाण्येवाप्रियाणि च। जीवेषु परिवर्तन्ते दुःखानि च सुखानि च॥
en: Thus joy and sorrow, the agreeable and the disagreeable, continually revolve among living creatures.

sn: एतां बुद्धिं समास्थाय सुखमास्ते गुणान्वितः। सर्वान् कामान् जुगुप्सेत कामान् कुर्वीत पृष्ठतः॥
en: Thus knowing an intelligent and wise man lives at ease. A person should renounce all his desires, and never give way to anger.

sn: वृत्त एष हृषि प्रौढो मृत्युरेष मनोभवः। क्रोधो नाम शरीरस्थो देहिनां प्रोच्यते बुधैः॥
en: This anger originates in the heart and becomes powerful there. This anger which lives in the bodies of men and is born in their minds, is described by the wise as Death.

sn: यदा संहरते कामान् कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः। तदाऽऽत्मज्योतिरात्मायमात्मन्येव प्रपश्यति॥
en: When a person withdraws all his desires like a tortoise withdrawing all its limbs, then its soul, which is self-luminous, can see itself.

sn: न बिभेति यदा चायं यदा चास्मान्न बिभ्यति। यदा नेच्छति न दृष्टि ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When a person himself feels no fear and is feared by no one, when he has no desire and no hatred, he is then said to attain to the state of Brahima.

sn: उभे सत्यानृते त्यक्त्वा शोकानन्दौ भयाभये। प्रियाप्रिये परित्यज्य प्रशान्तात्मा भविष्यति॥
en: Renouncing both truth and falsehood, grief and joy, fear and courage, the agreeable and the disagreeable, you may acquire equanimity of soul.

sn: यदा न कुरुते धीरः सर्वभूतेषु पापकम्। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When a person does no wrong to any creature, in thought, word, or deed, he is then said to attain to a state of Brahma.

sn: या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः। योऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम्।।५५
en: He alone enjoys true happiness who can renounce that thirst which cannot be cast off by the misguided, which does not decay with decrepitude, and which is considered as a fatal disease.

sn: अत्र पिङ्गलया गीता गाथाः श्रूयन्ति पार्थिव। यथा सा कृच्छ्रकालेऽपि लेभे धर्मं सनातनम्॥
en: About it, O king, are heard the verses sung by Pingala regarding the way in which she had acquired eternal inerit even at a very unfavourable time.

sn: संकेते पिङ्गला वेश्या कान्तेनासीद् विनाकृता। अथ कृच्छ्रगता शान्ता बुद्धिमास्थापयत् तदा॥
en: Having gone to the appointed place, a fallen woman of the name of Pingala could not enjoy the company of her lover through an accident. At that time of great misery, she acquired equanimity of soul.

sn: पिङ्गलोवाच उन्मत्ताहमनुन्मत्तं कान्तमन्ववसं चिरम्। अन्तिके रमणं सन्तं नैनमध्यगमं पुरा॥
en: Pingala said Alas, I have for many years lived ignorantly, by the side of tha dear Self in whom there is nothing but tranquility. Death has been at my door. Ere this, I did not, however, approach that Essence of Purity.

sn: एकस्थूणं नवद्वारमपिधास्याम्यगारकम्। का हि कान्तमिहायान्तमयं कान्तेति मंस्यते॥
en: I shall cover this house of one column and nine doors, i.e., body, (by means of true knowledge). What woman is there who considers that dear. Supreme Soul, even when He is so near, as really dear.

sn: अकामां कामरूपेण धूर्ता नरकरूपिणः। न पुनर्वञ्चयिष्यन्ति प्रतिबुद्धास्मि जागृमि॥
en: I am now awake. I have been roused from the sleep of ignorance. I am no longer under the influence of desire. Human lovers, who are, in fact, so many embodiments of hell, shall no longer impose upon me by approaching me lustfully.

sn: अनर्थो हि भवेदर्थो दैवात् पूर्वकृतेन वा। सम्बुद्धाहं निराकारा नाहमद्याजितेन्द्रिया॥
en: Evil yields good through destiny or through pristine deeds. Roused from the sleep of ignorance, I have renounced all desire for worldly objects. I have gained a complete mastery over my senses.

sn: सुखं निराशः स्वपिति नैराश्यं परमं सुखम्। आशामनाशां कृत्वा हि सुखं स्वपिति पिङ्गला॥
en: One freed from desire and hope sleeps happily. Freedom from hope and desire is happiness. Having renounced desire and hope, Pingala sleeps happily.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एतैश्चान्यैश्च विप्रस्य हेतुमद्भिः प्रभाषितैः। पर्यवस्थापितो राजा सेनजिन्मुमुदे सुखी॥
en: Bhishma said Consoled with these and other words of the learned Brahmana, king Senajit enjoyed delight and became very happy.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अतिक्रामति कालेऽस्मिन् सर्वभूतक्षयावहे। किं श्रेयः प्रतिपद्येत तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Time, which destroys every created thing, is rolling on. Tell me, O grandfather, what is that good thing which one should seek.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। पितुः पुत्रेण संवादं तं निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it, O king, an old discourse between father and son, O Yudhishthira, is mentioned.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: द्विजाते: कस्यचित् पार्थ स्वाध्यायनिरतस्य वै। बभूव पुत्रो मेधावी मेधावी नाम नामतः॥
en: A certain Brahmana, O Partha, who was given to the study of the Vedas, got a very intelligent son who was called Medhavin.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: सोऽब्रवीत् पितरं पुत्रः स्वाध्यायकरणे रतम्। मोक्षधर्मार्थकुशलो लोकतत्त्वविचक्षणः॥
en: One day, the son, who was cognisant of the truths of the religion of liberation, and acquainted also with worldly affairs, addressed his father given to the study of the Vedas.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: पुत्र उवाच धीरः किंस्वित्तात कुर्यात्प्रजानन् क्षिप्रं ह्यायुर्धश्यते मानवानाम्। पितस्तदाचक्ष्व यथार्थयोगं मामनुपूव्यां येन धर्मं चरेयम्॥
en: The son said — Seeing that the lease of human life is passing away so very speedily, what should a wise man do? O father, tell me the duties which one should perform, without failing to mention the fruits. Having heard you, I wish to practise those duties.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: पितोवाच वेदानधीत्य ब्रह्मचर्येण पुत्र पुत्रानिच्छेत् पावनार्थं पितृणाम्। अग्नीनाधाय विविवच्चेश्यज्ञो वनं प्रविश्याथ मुनिळूभूषेत्॥
en: The sire said O son, following the life of celibacy, one should first read the Vedas. He should then wish for children for saving his departed ancestors. Kindling his fire next, he should try to celebrate the (prescribed) sacrifices according to due rites. At last, he should enter into woods for practising contemplation.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: पुत्र उवाच एवमभ्याहते लोके समन्तात् परिवारिते। अमोघासु पतन्तीषु किं धीर इव भाषसे॥
en: The son said-When the world is thus encircled on all sides and is thus attacked, and when such irresistible things of dreadful consequences fall upon it, how can you say these words so calmly.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: पितोवाच कथमभ्याहतो लोकः केन वा परिवारितः। अमोघा: काः पतन्तीह किं नु भीषयसीव माम्॥
en: The sire said How is the world attacked? What is that by which it is encircled? What again, are those irresistible things of dreadful consequences that fall upon it? Why do you terrify me thus?

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: पुत्र उवाच मृत्युनाभ्याहतो लोको जरया परिवारितः। अहोरात्राः पतन्त्येते ननु कस्मान्न बुध्यसे॥
en: The son said Death is what assails the world. Decrepitude brings it about. Those irresistible objects which come and go away are the nights.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: अमोघा रात्रयश्चापि नित्यमायान्ति यान्ति च। यदाहमेतज्जानामि न मृत्युस्तिष्ठतीति ह।
en: When I know that Death waits for none, how can I pass my days without covering myself with the raiment of knowledge.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: सोऽहं कथं प्रतीक्षिष्ये जालेनापिहितश्चरन्॥ राज्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामायुरल्पतरं यदा।
en: When passing away, each succeed-night lessens the lease of human life, the wise man should consider the day to be fruitless.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: गाधोदके मत्स्य इव सुखं विन्देत कस्तदा॥ तदैव वन्ध्यं दिवसमिति विद्याद् विचक्षणः।
en: What man is there who would, like a fish in a shallow water, feel happy? Death approaches a man before all his desires have been fulfilled.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: अनवाप्तेषु कामेषु मृत्युरभ्येति मानवम्॥ शष्पाणीव विचिन्वन्तमन्यत्रगतमानसम्।
en: Death takes away a person when he is engaged in plucking flowers and when his heart is otherwise busy, like a tigress carrying away a ram.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: वृकीवोरणमासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति॥ अद्यैव कुरु यच्छ्रेयो मा त्वां कालोऽत्यगादयम्।
en: Do you, this very day, do what is for your well-being. Let not this death approach. Death drags its victims before their acts are done.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: अकृतेष्वेव कार्येषु मृत्युबै सम्प्रकर्षति॥ श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्ने चापराह्निकम्।
en: What should be done tomorrow should be done to-day, and the deeds of the afternoon in the forenoon. Death does not wait to see whether the acts of its victim have all been done or not.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: न हि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम्॥ को हि नाजाति कस्याद्य मृत्युकालो भविष्यति। युवैव धर्मशीलः स्यादनित्यं खलु जीवितम्। कृते धर्मे भवेत् कीर्तिरिह प्रेत्य च वै सुखम्॥
en: Who knows that Death will not approach him even to-day? In prime of life one should begin the practice of virtue. Life is fickle. If virtue be practised, one will meet fame in this, and happiness in the other, world.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: मोहेन हि समाविष्टः पुत्रदारार्थमुद्यतः। कृत्वा कार्यमकार्यं वा पुष्टिमेषां प्रयच्छति॥
en: Possessed by ignorance, one is ready to work hard for sons and wives. Doing good or evil deeds, one brings them up and advances their interest.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: तं पुत्रपशुसम्पन्नं व्यासक्तमनसं नरम्। सुप्तं व्याघ्रो मृगमिव मृत्युरादाय गच्छति॥
en: Like a tiger carrying away a sleeping deer, Death takes away the man addicted to the gratification of desire and the enjoyment of sons and animals.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: संचिन्वानकमेवैनं कामानामवितृप्तकम्। व्याघ्रः पशुमिवादाय मृत्युरादाय गच्छति॥
en: Before he has been able to pluck the flowers which he seeks, before he has been satiated with the acquisition of the objects of desire, Death carries him away like a tiger carrying away its prey.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: इदं कृतमिदं कार्यमिदमन्यत् कृताकृतम्। एवमीहासुखासक्तं कृतान्तः कुरुते वशे॥
en: Death attacks a man while he enjoys the happiness arising from the gratification of desire, and while he still thinks,-this has been done; this is be done; this has been half-done.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: कृतानां फलमप्राप्तं कर्मणां कर्मसंज्ञितम्। क्षेत्रापणगृहासक्तं मृत्युरादाय गच्छति॥
en: Death carries away the man, whatever he is called according to his calling, attached to his field, his shop, or his home, before he has acquired the fruit of his acts.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: दुर्बलं बलवन्तं च शूरं भीरूं जडं कविम्। अप्राप्तं सर्वकामार्थान् मृत्युरादाय गच्छति॥
en: Death carries away the weak, the strong, the brave, the timid, the idiotic, and the learned, before any of these acquires the fruits of his acts.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: मृत्युर्जरा च व्याधिश्च दुःखं चानेककारणम्। अनुषक्तं यदा देहे किं स्वस्थ इव तिष्ठसि॥
en: When death, decrepitude, disease, and grief originating from various causes, are all living in your body, how is it that you live as if you are perfectly hale.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: जातमेवान्तकोऽन्ताय जरा चान्वेति देहिनम्। अनुषक्ता द्वयेनैते भावाः स्थावरजङ्गमाः॥
en: As soon as an embodied creature is born, Decrepitude and Death follow him to bring about his destruction. All things, mobile and immobile, are affected by these two.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: मृत्योर्वा मुखमेतद् वै या ग्रामे वसतो रतिः। देवानामेष वै गोठो यदरण्यमिति श्रुतिः॥
en: The attachment which one feels for living in villages and towns is considered as the very mouth of Death. The forest, on the other hand, is considered as the fold within which the senses may be penned up. This is the injunction of the Shrutis.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: निबन्धनी रज्जुरेषा या ग्रामे वसतो रतिः। छित्त्वैतां सुकृतो यान्ति नैनां छिन्दन्ति दुष्कृतः॥
en: The attachment a person feels for living in a village or town is like a cord which fetters him strongly. Those that are good break that cord and acquire liberation, while they the wicked cannot break them.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: न हिंसयति यो जन्तून् मनोवाक्कायहेतुभिः। जीवितार्थापनयनैः प्राणिभिर्न स हिंस्यते॥
en: He who never injures living creatures by thought, word, or deed, is never injured by such agencies as wild beasts and lawless men always destroying life and property.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: न मृत्युसेनामायान्तीं जातु कश्चित् प्रबाधते। ऋते सत्यमसत् त्याज्यं सत्ये ह्यमृतमाश्रितम्॥
en: Nothing can resist the emissaries of Death when they advance except Truth which devours Untruth. Immortality, lives in Truth.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: तस्मात् सत्यव्रताचारः सत्ययोगपरायणः। सत्यागमः सदा दान्तः सत्येनैवान्तकं जयेत्॥
en: For these reasons, one should practise the vow of Truth; one should devote himself too Truth; one should accept Truth for one's Veda; and controlling is senses, one should defcat the Death by Truth.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च द्वयं देहे प्रतिष्ठितम्। मृत्युमापद्यते मोहात् सत्येनापद्यतेऽमृतम्॥
en: Both immortality and Death are in the body. One meets with Death through ignorance and loss of judgement; while Immortality is gained by Truth.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: सोऽहं ह्यहिस्रः सत्यार्थी कामक्रोधबहिष्कृतः। समदुःखसुखः क्षेमी मृत्यु हास्याम्यमर्त्यवत्॥
en: I shall, therefore, injure no one and try to acquire Truth, and transgressing the control of desire and anger, consider pleasure and pain impartially, and gaining tranquility, avoid Death like an immortal.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: शान्तियज्ञरतो दान्तो ब्रह्मयज्ञे स्थितो मुनिः। वामनः कर्मयज्ञश्च भविष्याम्युदगायने॥
en: When with the coming of the season the Sun will march towards the north, I shall, controlling my senses, engage in the practice of self-denial in the reflection of Vedantic truths, in the recitation of the mystic syllable OM, and in the contemplation of the Supreme Self.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: पशुयज्ञैः कथं हिंस्रैर्मादृशो यष्टुमर्हति। अन्तवद्भिरिव प्राज्ञः क्षेत्रयज्ञैः पिशाचवत्॥
en: How can one like me adore his Maker with animal-sacrifices involving cruelty, or sacrifices of the body such as Pishachas only can perform and such as yield transitory fruits.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: यस्य वाङ्मनसी स्यातां सम्यक् प्रणिहिते सदा। तपस्त्यागश्च सत्यं च स वै सर्वमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: That person person whose whose words, thoughts penances, renunciation, and Yoga meditation, all depend on Brahma, acquires the highest good.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति सत्यसमं तपः। नास्ति रागसमं दुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम्॥
en: There is no eye which is equal to that of knowledge. There is no penance like Truth. There is no sorrow like Attachment. There is no happiness like Renunciation.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: आत्मन्येवात्मना जात आत्मनिष्ठोऽप्रजोऽपि वा। आत्मन्येव भविष्यामि न मां तारयति प्रजा॥
en: I have sprung from Brahma through Brahma. I shall devote myself to Brahma, though I have no child. I shall return to Brahma. I do not require a son for rescuing me.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: नैतादृशं ब्राह्मणस्यास्ति वित्तं यथैकता समता सत्यता च। शीलं स्थितिर्दण्डनिधानमार्जवं ततस्ततश्चोपरमः क्रियाभ्यः॥
en: A Brahmana can have no wealth which is the state of being alone, the state by virtue of which he can look upon everything impartially, the practice of truthfulness, good conduct, patience, abstention from injury, simplicity and avoidance of all rites and sacrifices,

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: किं ते धनैर्बान्धवैर्वापि किं ते किं ते दारैर्ब्राह्मण यो मरिष्यसि। आत्मानमन्विच्छ गुहां प्रविष्टं पितामहास्ते क्व गताः पिता च॥
en: Why do you, O Brahmana, care for wealth or kinsmen and relatives and wives, when you shall have to die? Seek yourself which is concealed in a cave. Where are your grandfathers and where is your sire.

description: The duties of men in view of approaching death
sn: भीष्म उवाच पुत्रस्यैतद् वचः श्रुत्वा यथाकार्षीत् पिता नृप। तथा त्वमपि वर्तस्व सत्यधर्मपरायणः॥
en: Bhishma said Do you also, O king, act yourself like the father (in this story), behaved himself devoted to the religion of Truth, after having heard the words of his son.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धनिनश्चाधना ये च वर्तयन्ते स्वतन्त्रणः। सुखदुःखागमस्तेषां कः कथं वा पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, whence and how happiness and misery approach the rich, and the poor, but who follow different practices and rites.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। शम्पाकेनेह मुक्तेन गीतं शान्तिगतेन च॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old history of what was sung by Champaka who had acquired tranquility and liberation for himself.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: अब्रवीन्मां पुरा कश्चिद् ब्राह्मणस्त्यागमाश्रितः। क्लिश्यमानः कुदारेण कुचैलेन बुभुक्षया।॥
en: In days of yore a certain Brahmana made iniserable by a bad wife, bad dress, and hunger, and practising the vow of renunciation, sang me these verses.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: उत्पन्नमिह लोके वै जन्मप्रभृति मानवम्। विविधामन्युपवर्तन्ते दुःखानि च सुखानि च।॥
en: Various sorts of sorrow and happiness overtake, from the day of birth, the person who is born on the Earth.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: तयोरेकतरे मार्गे यदेनमभिसन्नयेत्। न सुखं प्राप्य संहष्येन्नासुखं प्राप्य संज्वरेत्॥
en: If he could ascribe either of them to the work of Destiny, he would then be indifferent w either happiness or misery as they fall to his share,

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: न वै चरसि यच्छ्रेय आत्मनो वा यदीशिषे। अकामात्मापि हि सदा धुरमुद्यम्य चैव ह॥
en: Though your mind is freed of desire, yet you bear a heavy burden. You do not strive to accomplish your own good. Are you not successful in subduing your mind?

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: अकिंचनः परिपतन् सुखमास्वादयिष्यसि। अकिंचनः सुखं शेते समुत्तिष्ठति चैव ह॥
en: Having renounced home and coveted wealth, if you go about, you shall then know what is real happiness. One who is shorn of everything, sleeps soundly and rises happily.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: आकिंचन्यं सुखं लोके पथ्यं शिवमनामयम्। अनमित्रपथो ह्येष दुर्लभः सुलभो मतः॥
en: Abject poverty, in this world, is the road to happiness. It is the safest way, it leads to the source of all blessings, and the path is not beset with any peril. Persons cherishing desire, cannot reach this goal (but those who have ridden over their desire, can easily do so.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: अकिंचनस्य शुद्धस्य उपपन्नस्य सर्वतः। अवेक्षमाणस्त्रील्लोकान् न तुल्यमिह लक्षये॥
en: Stretching my eyes on every part of the three worlds, I do not find the person who can be equal to a poor man of unblemished character and who is indifferent to worldly things.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: आकिंचन्यं च राज्यं च तुलया समतोलयम्। अत्यरिच्यत दारियं राज्यादपि गुणाधिकम्॥
en: I weighed poverty and sovereignty in the balance, and found sovereignty wanting, and poverty to all appearances possessed greater merits then sovereignty.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: आकिंचन्ये च राज्ये च विशेषः सुमहानयम्। नित्योद्विग्नो हि धनवान् मृत्योरास्यगतो यथा॥
en: Between poverty and sovereignty there is this great difference, viz., that the sovereign of vast possessions is always troubled with painful anxiety and seems to be an easy prey of death.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: नैवस्याग्निर्न चारिष्टो न मृत्युनं च दस्यवः। प्रभवन्ति धनत्यागाद् विमुक्तस्य निराशिषः॥
en: Regarding, however, the poor man who has no wealth to call his own, nor any hopes to entertain, and as such has emancipated himself, neither fire, nor foe, nor death, nor thieves, can override him.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: तं वै सदा कामचरमनुपस्तीर्णशायिनम्। बाहूपधानं शाम्यन्तं प्रशंसन्ति दिवौकसः॥
en: The very gods praise such a man who wnders about according to his will who lies down on the naked Earth with his arm for a pillow, and who possesses a tranquil soul.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: धनवान् क्रोधलोभाभ्यामाविष्टो नष्टचेतनः। तिर्यगीक्षः शुष्कमुखः पापको भृकुटीमुखः॥
en: The man of wealth, affected by anger and lust, stains himself with his sinful heart. He casts sidelong glances and makes dry specches. He becomes sinful and his countenance loses its luster with his wry face.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: निर्दशनधरोष्ठं च क्रुद्धो दारुणभाषिता। कस्तमिच्छेत् परिद्रष्टुं दातुमिच्छति चेन्महीम्॥
en: Biting his lips, and worked up with passion, he gives vent to harsh and cruel words. If such a man desires to make even a gift of the whole world, who is there that would like to look at him even.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: श्रिया ह्यभीक्ष्णं संवासो मोहयत्यविचक्षणम्। सा तस्य चित्तं हरति शारदाभ्रमिवानिलः॥ अथैनं रूपमानश्च धनमानश्च विन्दति।
en: Continuous Prosperity stupefies a person of weak intellect. Like the wind driving off the autumnal clouds, it drives off his judgement. Association with Prosperity induces him to think,-~-I am beautiful. I am wealthy.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: अभिजातोऽस्मि सिद्धोऽस्मि नास्मि केवलमानुषः॥ इत्येभिः कारणैस्तस्य त्रिभिश्चित्तं प्रमाद्यति।
en: I am high-born! I am successful in my undertakings! I am no ordinary individual!...For these three reasons, his heart becomes intoxicated.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: सम्प्रसक्तमना भोगान् विसृज्य पितृसंचितान्। परिक्षीणः परस्वानामादानं साधु मन्यते॥
en: He makes a waste of the possessions left by his ancestors by following the bent of his heart cager for worldly enjoyments. And then when reduced to want he does not regard the appropriation of other's wealth as sinful.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: तमतिक्रान्तमर्यादमाददानं ततस्ततः। प्रतिषेधन्ति राजानो लुब्धा मृगामिवेषुभिः॥
en: At this stage when he outstrips all barriers and becomes reckless of conduct as regards his appropriation of other's possessions from every side the rulers of men checks and afflict him like sportsmen afflicting a deer with their sharp arrows which they espied in the woods.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: एवमेतानि दुःखानि तानि तानीह मानवम्। विविधान्युपपद्यन्ते गात्रसंस्पर्शजान्यपि॥
en: Such a man is then overwhelmed with many other afflictions of a like nature that originate in fire and weapons.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: तेषां परमदुः :खानां बुद्ध्या भैषज्यमाचरेत्। लोकधर्ममवज्ञाय ध्रुणावामध्रुवैः सह॥
en: Therefore, becoming indifferent to all worldly attachments i.e., for children and wives) together with all fleeting phantons (as the physical body, etc.,) one should , helped by his intelligence, treat himself with proper medicine for the cure of those painful afflictions.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: नात्यक्त्वा सुखमाप्नोति नात्यक्त्वा विन्दते परम्। नात्यक्त्वा चाभयः शेते त्यक्त्वा सर्वं सुखी भव॥
en: Without Renunciation one can never be happiness. Without Renunciation one never be successful in gaining what is his highest good. Without Renunciation one can never be at his ease even in sleep. Therefore, renouncing every thing, makc happiness your can Own.

description: The root of happiness and misery
sn: इत्येद्धास्तिनपुरे ब्राह्मणेनोपवर्णितम्। शम्पाकेन पुरा मह्यं तस्मात् त्यागः परो मतः॥
en: A Brahmana, told me all this, at Hastinapur, in times gone by, about what Champaka had sung. I hold Renunciation, therefore, as the foremost of things.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ईहमानः समारम्भान् यदि नासादयेद् धनम्। धनतृष्णाभिभूतश्च किं कुर्वन् सुखमाप्नुयात्॥
en: Yudhishthira said If any person, desirous of accomplishing acts of charity and sacrifices, fails to find (the necessary) wealth, and thirst of wealth gets the better of him, what course should he pursue to obtain happiness?

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: भीष्म उवाच सर्वसाम्यमनायासं सत्यवाक्यं च भारत। निर्वेदश्चाविधित्सा च यस्य स्यात् स सुखी नरः॥
en: He who makes no difference between two opposite agents, viz., pleasure and pain, honour and insult, etc., who never troubles himself for the gratification of his desire for worldly possessions, who observes veracity of speech, who has freed himself from all kinds of attachment, and who has renounced his desire for action, is, O Bharata, a happy man.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: एतान्येव पदान्याहुः पञ्च वृद्धाः प्रशान्तये। एष स्वर्गश्च धर्मश्च सुखं चानुत्तमं मतम्॥
en: The ancients say these are the five means by which perfect tranquility or emancipation could be obtained. These are called Heaven. These are Religion. These form the highest happiness.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। निर्वेदान्मङ्किना गीतं तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old story of what Manki had sung, when freed from attachments. Hear it, O Yudhishthira.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: ईहमानो धनं मङ्किर्भग्नेहश्च पुनः पुनः। केनचिद्धनशेषेण क्रीतवान् दम्यगोयुगम्॥
en: Manki, desirous of wealth, found that he was doomed to an unending series of disappointinents. With a little remnant of his property hc purchased at last a couple of young bulls with a yoke for training them (to pastoral labour).

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: सुसम्बद्धौ तु तौ दम्यौ दमनायाभिनिःसृतौ। आसीनमुष्ट्रं मध्येन सहसैवाभ्यधावताम्॥ तयोः सम्प्राप्तयोरुष्ट्रः स्कन्धदेशममर्षणः। उत्थायोक्षिप्य तौ दम्यौ प्रससार महाजवः॥
en: One day the two bulls, properly yoked, were taken out for training (in the fields). Shying at the sight of a camel which was lying down on the road, the animals suddenly ran towards the camel, and fell upon its neck. Enraged at finding the bulls fall upon its neck, the camel, possessed of great speed, got up and ran with full speed, bearing away the two helpless creatures dangling on either side of its neck.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: ह्रियमाणौ तु तौ दम्यौ तेनोष्ट्रेण प्रमाथिना। नियमाणौ च सम्प्रेक्ष्य मङ्किस्तत्राब्रवीदिदम्॥ न चैवाविहितं शक्यं दक्षणापीहितुं धनम्। युक्तेन श्रद्धया सम्यगीहां समनुतिष्ठता॥
en: Beholding his two bulls thus carried away by the strong camel, and seeing that they were: on the point of death, Manki began to say,-If it is not ordained by destiny, wealth can never be obtained even by a clever man strenuously and confidently striving and skilfully doing all that is necessary towards the accomplishment of his object.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: कृतस्य पूर्वं चानथैर्युक्तस्याप्यनुतिष्ठतः। इमं पश्यत संगत्या मम दैवमहपप्लवम्॥
en: I had, all along, tried by all manner and means, and with great devotion, to acquire riches. But all this misfortune to my property is due to Destiny.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: उद्यम्योद्यम्य मे दम्यौ विषमेणैव गच्छतः। उत्क्षिप्य काकतालीयमुत्पथेनैव धावतः॥
en: My bulls are carried away, rising and falling, as the camel is running in the uneven course. This event seems to be an accident like the one brought about by the crow to a ripe fruit while perching on a palmyra free.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: मणी वोष्ट्रस्य लम्बेते प्रियौ वत्सतरौ मम। शुद्धं हि दैव्मेवेदं हठेनैवास्ति पौरुषम्॥
en: Alas, those dear bulls of mine are dangling on the camel's neck like a couple of gems! This is the result of Destiny alone. Exertion is of no avail in what is due to Chance.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: यदि वाप्युपपद्येत पौरुषं नाम कर्हिचित् अन्विष्यमाणं तदपि दैवमेवावतिष्ठते॥
en: Or, if the existence of anything like Exertion (as a resulting factor) be admitted, a little more scrutiny would find that Destiny is at the bottom.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: तस्मानिर्वेद एवेह गन्तव्यः सुखमिच्छता। सुखं स्वपिति निर्विण्णो निराशश्चार्थसाधने॥
en: Therefore, he who is desirous of happiness, should renounce all attachment. He who is indifferent to worldly surroundings, has renounced all desires for acquiring wealth, can sleep happily.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: अहो सम्यक् शुकेनोक्तं सर्वतः परिमुच्यता। प्रतिष्ठता महारण्यं जनकस्य निवेशनात्॥
en: He, it was well-said by Shuka while going to the great forest from his father's house, renouncing everything.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: यः कामानाप्नुयात् सर्वान् यश्चैतान् केवलांस्त्यजेत्। प्रापणात् सर्वकामानां परित्यागो विशिष्यते॥
en: Amongst these two, viz., one who obtains the fruition of all his desires, and one who renounces all desires, the latter, who casts off everything is superior to the first who obtains the fruition of all his desires.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: नान्तं सर्वविधित्सानां गतपूर्वोऽस्ति कश्चन। शरीरे जीविते चैव तृष्णा मन्दस्य वर्धते॥
en: No one could ever attain to the end of desire. Only he who is destitute of knowledge and judgement feels and avidity for protecting his body and life.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: निवर्तस्व विधित्साभ्यः शाम्य निर्विद्य कामुक असकृच्चासि निकृतो न च निर्विद्यसे ततः॥
en: Renounce all desire for action. O my Soul which has become a prey of cupidity, adopt tranquillity by freeling yourself from all worldly attachments. Repeatedly have you been cheated (by phantomis of hope). How is it that you do not still free yourself from attachments?

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: यदि नाहं विनाश्यस्ते यद्येवं रमसे मया। मा मां योजय लोभेन वृथा त्वं वित्तकामुक॥
en: If I am not one who deserves to be crushed by you, if I am one with whom you should play in delight, then, O my wealth-coveting Soul, do not induce me towards cupidity.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: संचितं संचितं द्रव्यं नष्टं तव पुनः पुनः। कदाचिन्मोक्ष्यसे मूढ धनेहां धनकामुक॥
en: You have now and again lost your hoarded wealth! O my wealth-covering and foolish Soul, when will you succeed in getting rid of your desire for wealth?

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: अहो न मम बालिश्यं योऽहं क्रीडनकस्तव। किं नैवं जातु पुरुषः परेषां प्रेष्यतामियात्॥
en: Shame on my foolishness. I have become a toy of yours. It is thus that one becomes a slave of others.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: न पूर्वे नापरे जातु कामानामन्तमाप्नुवन्। त्यक्त्वा सर्वसमारम्भान् प्रतिबुद्धोऽस्मि जागृमि॥
en: No one born on Earth did ever attain to the end of desire, and no one who will be born hereafter will succeed in attaining to it. Renouncing all acts, I have at last been roused from sleep. I am now awake.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: नूनं ते हृदयं काम वज्रसारमयं दृढम्। यदनर्थशताविष्टं शतधा न विदीर्यते॥
en: Without doubt, O Desire, your heart is hard like that of an adamant, since though affected by a hundred reverses, you do not break into as many fragments.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: जानामि काम त्वां चैव यच्च किंचित् प्रियं तव। तवाहं प्रियमन्विच्छन्नात्मन्युपलभे सुखम्॥
en: I know you, O Desire, and all those things that are dear to you. Seeking what is dear to you, I shall feel happiness in my own Self.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: काम जानामि ते मूलं संकल्पात् किल जायसे। न त्वां संकल्पयिष्यामि समूलो न भविष्यसि॥
en: O desire, I know your origin. You originate from Will. I shall, therefore, avoid Will. You will then be rooted out.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: ईहा धनस्य न सुखं लब्ध्वा चिन्ता च भूयसी। लब्धनाशे यथा मृत्युर्लब्धं भवति वा न वा॥
en: The desire for wealth can never yield happiness. If acquired, the acquirer feels great anxiety. If lost after acquisition it is felt like death. Again acquisition itself, is very uncertain.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: परित्यागे न लभते ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्। न च तुष्यति लब्धेन भूय एव च मार्गति॥
en: Wealth cannot be secured by even the surrender of one's person. What can be more painful than this? When acquired, one is never gratified with its quantity, but one continues to hanker after it.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: अनुतर्षुल एवार्थः स्वादु गाङ्गमिवोदकम्। मद्विलापनमेतत्तु प्रतिबुद्धोऽस्मि संत्यज॥
en: Like the sweet water of the Ganges, riches only enhances one's hankering. It is my destruction. I am now awakened. Do you, O desire, leave me.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: य इमं मामकं देहं भूतग्रामः समाश्रितः। स यात्वितो यथाकामं वसतां वा यथासुखम्॥
en: May that desire which resides in this my body,-this compound of (five), elements,-go wherever it likes and live happily wherever it likes.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: न युष्मास्विह मे प्रीतिः कामलोभानुसारिषु। तस्मादुत्सृज्य कामान् वै सत्त्वमेवाश्रयाम्यहम्॥
en: I do not like you all who are not of the Soul, for you bring on Desire and Cupidity! Forsaking all of you I shall seek refuge with the quality of Goodness.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: सर्वभूतान्यहं देहे पश्यन् मनसि चात्मनः। योगे बुद्धिं श्रुते सत्त्वं मनो ब्रह्मणि धारयन्॥ विहरिष्याम्यनासक्तः सुखी लोकान् निरामयः। यया मां त्वं पुन:वं दुःखेषु प्रणिधास्यसि॥
en: Seeing all creatures in my own body and my own mind, and devoting my reason to Yoga, my life to the instructions of the wise, and soul to Brahma, I shall happily rove through the world, without attachment and without calamities of any kind, so that you may not be able to plunge me again into such sorrows.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: त्वया हि मे प्रणुन्नस्य गतिरन्या न विद्यते। तृष्णाशोकश्रमाणां हि त्वं काम प्रभवः सदा॥
en: If I continue to be unruffled by you, O desire, I shall necessarily be without a path (by which to effect my salvation). You O desire, are always the parent of thirst, of sorrow, and of fatigue and toil.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: धननाशेऽधिकं दुःखं मन्ये सर्वमहत्तरम्। ज्ञातयो ह्यवमन्यन्ते मित्राणि च धनाच्च्युतम्॥
en: I consider the sorrow that one feels at the loss of wealth is proportionately greater than what one feels under any other adverse circumstance. Relatives and friends forsake him who has lost his wealth.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: अवज्ञानसहौस्तु दोषाः कष्टतराऽधने। धने सुखकला या तु सापि दुःखैर्विधीयते॥
en: With all sorts of humiliation numbering by thousands, there are many other faults in property which are even much more painful. On the other hand, the very small happiness that resides in wealth is mingled with pain and sorrow.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: धनमस्येति पुरुषं पुरो निमन्ति दस्यवः। क्लिश्यन्ति विविधैर्दण्डैनित्यमुद्वेजयन्ति च॥
en: Robbers kill, in the sight of all, the person who has riches, or torment him with all sorts of severity, or put him into fright now and again.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: अर्थलोलुपता दुःखमिति बुद्धं चिरान्मया। यद् यदालम्बसे काम तत्तदेवानुरुध्यसे।॥ अतत्त्वज्ञोऽसि बालश्च दुस्तोषोऽपूरणोऽनलः।
en: At last, after a long time, I have realised that the desire for wealth is attended with sorrow. Whatever the object, O desire, upon which you set your heart, you force me to follow it! You are without judgement. You are a fool. You are difficult of being satisfied. You can never be contented. You burn like fire.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: नैव त्वं वेत्थ सुलभं नैव त्वं वेत्थ दुर्लभम्॥ पाताल इव दुष्पूरो मां दुःखैर्योक्तुमिच्छसि। नाहमद्य समावेष्टुं शक्यः काम पुनस्त्वया॥
en: You do not enquire when following the object you pursue, whether it is easy or difficult of attainment. Like the nether region you cannot be filled to the brim. You wish to cast into grief. From this day, O desire, I am incapable of living with you.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: निर्वेदमहमासाद्य द्रव्यनाशाद् यदृच्छया। निर्वृत्तिं परमां प्राप्य नाद्य कामान् विचिन्तये॥
en: I who was disappointed, at first, at the loss of my property, have now attained to the high state of perfect freedom from attachments. At this moment I no longer think of you and your train. I

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: अतिक्लेशान् सहामीह नाहं बुद्ध्याम्बुद्धिमान्। निकृतो धननाशेन शय सर्वाङ्गविज्वरः॥
en: I had, before this, felt great misery on your account. I do not (now) regard myself as devoid of intelligence. Having taken to Renunciation on account of the loss of my property, I now can .rest, being freed from every kind of fever.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: परित्यजामि काम त्वा हित्वा सर्वमनोगती:। न त्वं मया पुनः काम वत्स्यसे न च रंस्यसे॥
en: I cast you off, O Desire, with all the passions of my heart. You shall not, again, find any place in me nor shall you sport with me.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: क्षमिष्ये क्षिपमाणानां न हिसिष्ये विहिंसितः। द्वेष्ययुक्तः प्रियं वक्ष्यासम्यनादृत्य तदप्रियम्॥
en: I shall forgive them who will slander or speak ill of me. I shall not harm even when I am injured. If anybody from aversion speaks disparagingly of me, without caring for those disagrccable words shall greet him courteously. With a contented heart and with an easy mind, I shall always live upon what I may obtain for myself.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: तृप्तः स्वस्थेन्द्रियो नित्यं यथालब्धेन वर्तयन्। न सकामं करिष्यामि त्वामहं शत्रुमात्मनः॥ निर्वेदं निर्वृतिं तृप्तिं शान्ति सत्यं दमं क्षमाम्। सर्वभूतदयां चैव विद्धि मां समुपागतम्॥
en: I shall not gratify those wishes of yours which are inimical to me. Indifference to worldly concerns, renunciation, contentment, tranquillity, veracity, self-control, forgiveness, and universal mercy, have now come to be my qualifications.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: तस्मात् कामश्च लोभश्च तृष्णा कार्पण्यमेव च। त्यजन्तु मां प्रतिष्ठन्तं सत्त्वस्थो ह्यस्मि साम्प्रतम्॥
en: Therefore, let Desire, Cupidity, Thirst, and Miserliness, bid me aided. I have now taken to the path of Goodness.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: प्रहाय कामं लोभं च सुखं प्राप्तोऽस्मि साम्प्रतम्। नाद्य लोभवशं प्राप्तो दुःखं प्राप्स्याम्यनात्मवान्॥
en: Having renounced Desire and Cupidity, my happiness has now been great. I shall no longer surrender myself to the influence of Cupidity, nor shall I undergo the pangs of misery like a person of impure soul.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: यद् यत् त्यजति कामानां तत् सुखस्याभिपूर्यते। कामस्य वशगो नित्यं दुःखमेव प्रपद्यते॥
en: Inasmuch as one renounces his desires so sure is he to reap his deserts. Truly he who surrenders himself to Desire always undergoes the pangs of misery.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: कामानुबन्धं नुदते यत् किंचित् पुरुषो रजः। कामक्राधोद्भवं दुःखमहाररतिरव च॥
en: Whatever passions arising from Desire are cast off by a person, all come under the category of Passion. Sorrow and shamelessness, as also discontent, all owe their origin to Desire and Wealth.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: एष ब्रह्मप्रतिष्ठोऽहं ग्रीष्मे शीतमिव ह्रदम्। शाम्यामि परिनिर्वामि सुखं मामेति केवलम्॥
en: As in the hot summery a person plunges himself into a cool lake, I have now merged myself into Brahma. I have renounced work. I have extricated myself from grief. Unalloyed happiness has now come to my share.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: यच्च कामसुखं लोके यच्च दिव्यं महत्सुखम्। तृष्णाक्षयसुखस्यैते नार्हतः षोडशी कलाम्॥
en: The happiness which results from the fruition of Desire, or the serene happiness which one enjoys in heaven, is not equal to a sixteenth part of that which springs from renunciation of all kinds of thirst.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: आत्मना सप्तमं कामं हत्वा शत्रुमिवोत्तमम्। : प्राप्यावध्यं ब्रह्मपुरं राजेव स्यामहं सुखी॥
en: Laying axe at the root of desire, which with the body makes an aggregate of seven, and which is a bitter foe, I have made my way to the immortal city of Brahma and there shall I pass my days in happiness like a king.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: एतां बुद्धिं समास्थाय मङ्किनिर्वेदमागतः। सर्वान् कामान् परित्यज्य प्राप्य ब्रह्म महत्सुखम्॥
en: Putting his faith upon such, intelligence, Manki succeeded in freeing himself from attachments, by his self-renunciation and obtained the blissful region of Brahma.

description: The root of happiness, The story of Manki
sn: दम्यनाशकृते मङ्किरमृतत्वं किलागमत्। अच्छिनत् काममूलं स तेन प्राप महत्सुखम्॥
en: Forsooth, on account of the loss of his two bulls, Manki attained to immortality. In fact, because he laid the axe at the very roots of desire, he succeeded, through that means to obtain for himself supreme happiness.

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। गीतं विदेहराजेन जनकेन प्रशाम्यता॥
en: "Regarding it is also cited the old story of the verses sung by Janaka, the king of the Videhas, who had so qualified himself as to obtain tranquillity of the soul.

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: अनन्तमिव मे वित्तं यस्य मे नास्ति किञ्चन। मिथिलायां प्रदीप्तायां न मे दह्यति किञ्चन॥
en: What the monarch said was,-My wealth is unlimited, At the same time I have nothing. If the whole of (my kingdom) Mithila be reduced to ashes in a conflagration, I shall lose nothing.

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीमं बोध्यस्य पदसंचयम्। निर्वेदं प्रति विन्यस्तं तं निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Once on a time the royal son of Nahusa (Yayati) asked the Rishi Vodhya who had, on account of Rcnunciation, attained to tranquillity of soul and who had a through knowledge of the scriptures. The king said

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: बोध्यं शान्तमृषि राजा नाहुषः पर्यपृच्छत। निर्वेदाच्छान्तिमापन्नं शास्त्रप्रज्ञानतर्पितम्॥ उपदेशं महाप्राज्ञ शमस्योपदिशस्व मे। का बुद्धिं समनुध्याय शान्तश्चरसि निर्वृतः॥
en: O you of great wisdom, vouchsafe me those instructions which lead to tranquillity. What is that understanding which had enabled you to wander over the world in tranquillity of soul and free yourself from all acts?

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: बोध्य उवाच उपदेशेन वर्तामि नानुशास्मीह कंचन। लक्षणं तस्य वक्ष्येऽहं तत् स्वयं परिमृश्यताम्॥
en: Vodhya said I follow the principles of others and never thrust inyself as an instructor. I shall, however, give you the outlines of those principles. Reflection will enable you to catch their spirit.

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: पिङ्गलाककुररः सर्पः सारङ्गान्वेषणं वने। इषुकारः कुमारी च षडेते गुरवो मम॥
en: Pingala, the osprey, the snake, the bee in the forest, the maker of shafts (in the story), and the maiden (in the story),-these six are my preceptors.

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: भीष्म उवाच आशा बलवती राजन् नैराश्यं परमं सुखम्। आशां निराशां कृत्वा तु सुखं स्वपिति पिङ्गला॥
en: Hope is the one powerful agent to agitate human breast, O king. Freedom from hope is supreme bliss. Reducing hope to a nullity, Pingala sleeps in peace.

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: सामिषं कुररं दृष्ट्वा वध्यमानं निरामिषैः। आमिषस्य परित्यागात् कुररः सुखमेधते॥
en: Seeing an osprey with a piece of meat in his breaks, those that have been unable to find any meat for themselves, pounce upon him and finally make him a osprey, while a certain other osprey, by abstaining from meat altogether, became happy.

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: गृहारम्भो हि दुःखाय न सुखाय कदाचन। सर्पः परकृतं वेश्म प्रविश्य सुखमेधते॥
en: To build a house for one's ownself conduces not to his happiness but becomes the source of his annoyance. The snake residing in another creature's place of abode, lives in happiness.

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: सुखं जीवन्ति मुनयो भैक्ष्यवृत्तिं समाश्रिताः। अद्रोहेणैव भूतानां सारङ्गा इव पक्षिणः॥
en: Adopting the life of mendicancy, the ascetics live in happiness, without having any object of fear from any creature, like the bees in the forest.

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: इषुकारो नरः कश्चिदिषावासक्तमानसः। समीपेनापि गच्छन्तं राजानं नावबुद्धवान्॥
en: A certain shaft-maker busy with his work, was so deeply engrossed with it that he did not notice the king who was passing by him.

description: Value of wealth. The various instructions
sn: बहूनां कलहो नित्यं द्वयोः संकथनं ध्रुवम्। एकाकी विचरिष्यामि कुमारीशंखको यथा॥
en: When many herd together, it foments dispute. Even when two reside together, they are sure to talk with each other. I, however, like the anklet made of sea-shells in the wrist of the maiden in the story wander alone.'

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच केन वृत्तेन वृत्तज्ञ वीतशोकश्चरेन्महीम्। किञ्च कुर्वन्नरो लोके प्राप्नोति गतिमुत्तमाम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O you who are an adept in the mystery a human conduct, tell me what course of person should pursue to succeed in this world, freed from grief. And how should he behave himself to gain his end?

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। प्रह्लादस्य च संवादं मुनेराजगरस्य च।॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old story of the discourse between Prahlada and the sage Ajagara.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: चरन्तं ब्राह्मणं कञ्चित् कल्पचित्तमनामयम्। पप्रच्छ राजा प्रह्लादो बुद्धिमान् बुद्धिसम्मतम्॥
en: Once on a time king Prahlada endued with great intelligence, enquired of a wandering Brahmana of great intelligence and of a purified and tranquil soul.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: प्रह्लाद उवाच स्वस्थः शक्तो मृदुर्दान्तो निर्विधित्सोऽनसूयकः। सुवाक् प्रगल्भो मेधावी प्राज्ञश्चरसि बालवत्॥
en: Prahlada said Shorn of desire, with a purified soul, of humans disposition, and given to the practices of self-restraint, without desire of action, free from malice, agreeable in speech, endued with dignity and intelligence and wisdom, you live (in simplicity) like a child.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: नैव प्रार्थयसे लाभं नालाभेष्वनुशोचसि। नित्यतृप्त इव ब्रह्मन् न किञ्चिदिव मन्यसे॥
en: You never covet for any kind of gain, nor are you overpowered with any kind of loss. You are always cheerful, O Brahmana, and do not seem to have any liking for anything in the world.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: स्रोतसा ह्रियमाणासु प्रजासु विमना इव। धर्मकामार्थकार्येषु कूटस्थ इव लक्ष्यसे॥
en: While all other creatures are being carried away in the stream of desire and passion, you are perfectly indifferent to all works of Religion, Profit and Pleasure. You seem to be in a state of quietude, having nothing to disturb the perfect equanimity of your soul.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: नानुतिष्ठसि धर्मार्थो न कामे चापि वर्तसे। इन्द्रियार्थाननादृत्य मुक्तश्चरसि साक्षिवत्॥
en: Regardless of all sensuous enjoyments, you move like an emancipated self, only witnessing everything, (but never taking part in anything).

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: का नु प्रज्ञा श्रुतं वा किं वृत्तिर्वा का नु ते मुने। क्षिप्रमाचक्ष्व मे ब्रह्मन् श्रेयो यदिह मन्यसे॥
en: O sage, what is your wisdom, what your learning, and what your behaviour (through which all this has become possible)? Tell me this without delay, if, O Brahmana, you think it will conduce to my well-being.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: भीष्म उवाच अनुयुक्तः स मेधावी लोकधर्मविधानवित्। उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा प्रह्लादमनपार्थया॥
en: Thus questioned by by Prahlada, that intelligent Brahmana who was well-conversant with the duties of the world, answered him in words of melodious sounds and of great significance.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: पश्य प्रह्लाद भूतानामुत्पत्तिमनिमित्ततः। ह्रासं वृद्धिं विनाशं च न प्रहृष्ये न च व्यथे।॥
en: Behold, O Prahlada, the origin of creatures, their growth, decay, and death, cannot be ascribed 10 any intelligible cause. It is for this reason that I do not give way to either joy or SOITOW.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: स्वभावादेव संदृश्या वर्तमानाः प्रवृत्तयः। स्वभावनिरताः सर्वाः परितुष्येन केनचित्॥
en: All the propensities (for action) in the universe may be seen to come from the innate nature of the creatures. All things (in the universe are dependent on their respective nature. Hence I am not delighted with anything.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: पश्य प्रह्लाद् संयोगान् विप्रोगपरायणान्। संचयांश्च विनाशान्तान् न क्वचिद् विदधे मनः॥
en: Behold, O Prahlada, all kinds of union are subject to severance. All acquisitions are certain to end in destruction. Hence I never set my heart upon the acquisition of any object.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: अन्तवन्ति च भूतानि गुणयुक्तानि पश्यतः। उत्पत्तिनिधनज्ञस्य किं कार्यमवशिष्यते॥
en: All things possessed of attributes are sure to come to an end. What remains there for å person then to do who (like me) is familiar with both the origin and the end of things.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: जलजानामपि ह्यन्तं पर्यायेणोपलक्षये। महतामपि कायानां सूक्ष्माणां च महोदधौ॥
en: The end is noticeable of all aquatic creatures of large or small bodied in this ocean.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: जङ्गमस्थावराणां च भूतानामसुराधिप। पार्थिवानामपि व्यक्तं मृत्यु पश्यामि सर्वशः॥
en: I see also the death, which is manifest, O chief of Asuras, of all things, mobile and immobile, belonging to the earth.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: अन्तरिक्षचराणां च दानवोत्तम पक्षिणाम्। उत्तिष्ठते यथाकालं मृत्युर्बलवतामपि॥
en: O best of Danavas, death comes in season even to the strongest of winged creatures which float in the air.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: दिवि संवरमाणानि ह्रस्वानि च महान्ति च। ज्योतीष्यपि यथाकालं पतमानानि लक्षये।१७॥
en: I see again that the luminous bodies, large and small, which range the firmament, fall down when their time comes.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
