sn: इति भूतानि सम्पश्यन्ननुषक्तानि मृत्युना। सर्वसामान्यगो विद्वान् कृतकृत्यः सुखं स्वपे॥
en: Seeing all created things to be ihus subject to death, endued with knowledge, and thinking all things to be possessed of the same nature, I sleep in comfort with no thought to disturb me.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: सुमहान्तमपि ग्रास ग्रसे लब्धं यदृच्छया। शये पुनरभुजानो दिवसानि बहून्यपि॥
en: If I get without trouble a heavy meal I waver not to enjoy it. On the other hand, I am used to pass many days together without tasting anything.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: आशयन्त्यपि मामन्नं पुनर्बहुगुणं बहु। पुनरल्पं पुन:स्तोकं पुनर्नवोपपद्यते॥
en: Sometimes people feed me with luxurious edibles in profusion, sometimes with a small quantity, sometimes even with less, and sometimes I get no food at all.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: कणं कदाचित् खादामि पिण्याकमपि च ग्रसे। भक्षसे शालिमांसानि भक्षांश्चोच्चावचान् पुनः॥
en: I sometimes eat only a portion of a grain; sometimes the dry sesame cakes from which the oil has been expressed. I sometimes eat rice and meat and other food of the richest kind.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: शये कदाचित् पर्यङ्के भूमावपि पुनः शये। प्रासादे चापि मे शय्या कदाचिदुपपद्यते॥
en: Sometimes I sleep on an elevated bedstead of the best kind; sometimes I sleep on the naked Earth; sometimes I lay myself down on a comfortable bed made within a fine palace or a beautiful mansion.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: धारयामि च चीराणि शाणक्षौमाजिनानि च। महार्हाणि च वासांसि धारयाम्यहमेकदा॥
en: Sometimes I am clad in rages, sometimes in sackcloth, sometimes in raiments of fine texture, sometimes in deer-skins, sometimes in richest robes.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: न संनिपतितं धर्म्यमुपभोगं यदृच्छया। प्रत्याचक्षे न चाप्येनमनुरुध्ये सुदुर्लभम्॥
en: I never reject such enjoyments as are not inconsistent with virtue and as can be secured without effort. I do not at the same time, stir myself for gaining objects difficult of acquisition.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: अचलमनिधनं शिवं विशोकं शुचिमतुलं विदुषां मते प्रविष्टम्। व्रतमिदमाजगरं शुचिश्चरामि॥
en: The rigid vow I have betaken to, is called Ajagara. That vow can secure immortality. It is auspicious and griefless. It is peerless and pure. It is in harmony with the advises of the sages. It is disregarded by persons of weak intellect who never practise it. With pure heart I conduct myself in accordance with to it.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: अचलितमतिरच्युतः स्वधर्मात् परिमितसंसरणः परावरज्ञः। विगतभयकषायलोभमोहो व्रतमिदमाजगरं शुचिश्चरामि॥
en: My mind never swerves from this vow. I have not swerved from the practices of my order. I am abstemious in everything. I know the past and the present. Shorn of fear and anger and cupidity and errors of judgement, I practise this vow with a pure heart.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: अनियतफलभक्ष्यभोज्यपेयं विधिपरिणामविभक्तदेशकालम्। व्रतामिदमाजगरं शुचिश्चरामि॥
en: There are no interdictions in respect of good and drink and other objects of enjoyment for one practising this vow. As everything is dependent on destiny, there is no observance of the consideration of time and place for one like us. The vow I practise contributes to true happiness of the heart. It is never followed by those that are wicked. I observe it with a pure heart.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: इदमिदमिति तृष्णयाभिभूतं जनमनवाप्तधनं विषीदमानम्। निपुणमनुनिशम्य तत्त्वबुद्ध्या व्रतमिदमाजगरं शुचिश्चरामि।२८।।
en: Led by cupidity, men pursue different kinds of wealth. If foiled in the attempt, brokenhearted and dispirited the become. Thinking properly upon all this by the help of my intelligence which has penetrated the truths of things, I practise this vow with pure heart.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: बहुविधमनुदृश्य चार्थहेतोः कृपणामिहार्यमनार्यमाश्रयन्तम्। उपशमरुचिरात्मवान् प्रशान्तो व्रतमिदमाजगरं शुचिश्चरामि॥
en: I have seen persons in distress seeking, for the acquisition of wealth, the shelter of both good and bad men. Devoted to tranquillity and with my passions under control, I observe this vow with a pure heart.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: सुखमसुखमलाभमर्थलाभं रतिमरतिं मरणं च जीवितं च। विधिनियतमवेक्ष्य तत्त्वतोऽहं व्रतमिदमाजगरं शुचिश्चरामि॥
en: Seeing by the help of truth, that happiness and misery, profit and loss, attachment, and renunciation, life and death are all ordained by destiny, I observe this vow with a pure heart.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: अपगतभयरागमोहदो धृतिमतिबुद्धिसमन्वितः प्रशान्तः। उपगतफलभोगिनो निशम्य व्रतमिदमाजगरं शुचिश्चरामि॥
en: Shorn of fear and attachment and errors of judgement and pride, and possessed of wisdom, intelligence, and understanding, and devoted to tranquillity, and hearing that large snakes, without stirring out enjoy the fruit that comes to them of itself, I follow their practice with a pure heart.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: अनियतशयनासनः प्रकृत्या दमनियमव्रतसत्वशौचयुक्तः अपगतफलसंचयः प्रहृष्टो व्रतमिदमाजगरं शुचिश्चरामि॥
en: Without restrictions of any kind in respect of bed and food, endued by my nature with Self-restraint, abstemiousness, pure vows, truth and purity of conduct, and without any desire to store (for future use) the rewards of action, I observe, this vow with a delighted and pure heart.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: रुपगतबुद्धिरवेक्ष्य चात्मसंस्थम्। तृषितमनियतं मनो नियन्तुं व्रतमिदमाजगरं शुचिश्चरामि॥
en: All causes of grief have fled from me on account of my having ridden over desire. Having received an accession of light, I observe this Vow with a pure heart, for controlling my soul which is thirsty and uncontrolled but which is capable of depending upon itself.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: हृदयमनुरुध्य वाङ्मनो वा प्रियसुखदुर्लभतामनित्यतां च। तदुभयमुपलक्षयन्निवाह व्रतमिदमाजगरं शुचिश्चरामि॥
en: Without paying any attention to the matters, towards which my heart, mind and words would like to lead me, and knowing that the happiness which these afford is both hard of being acquired and transitory, in duration, I follow this vow with a pure heart.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: बहुकथितमिदं हि बुद्धिमद्भिः कविभिरपि प्रथयद्भिरात्मकीर्तिम्। इदमिदमिति तत्र तत्र हन्त स्वपरमतैर्गहनं प्रतर्कषद्भिः॥
en: Learned and highly intelligent men, desirous of giving a publicity to their own feats, have while supporting their own theories and censuring those of others, indulged in vague expressions in delivering themselves on the topic which is beyond the scope of argumentation.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: तदिदमनुनिशम्य विप्रपातं पृथगभिपन्नमिहाबुधैर्मनुष्यैः। अनवसितमनन्तदोषपारं नृषु विहरामि विनीतदोषतृष्णः॥
en: Foolish men cannot properly understand this vow. I, however, see that it kills Ignorance. To safeguard against this immortality and various sorts of evil. I travel among men, having controlled all shortcomings and having freed myself from thirst thirst after material enjoyments.

description: The root of success. The story of Praharda
sn: भीष्म उवाच अजगरचरितं व्रतं महात्मा य इह नरोऽनुचरेद्विनीतरागः। अपगतभयलोभमोहमन्युः स खलु सुखी विचरेदिमं विहारम्॥
en: That great person who, having freed himself from attachments and got rid of fear, cupidity, foolishness, and anger, follows this Ajagara vow, or indulges in this sport, as it may be called, surely spends his time in great happiness.'

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच बान्धवाः कर्म वित्तं वा प्रज्ञा वेह पितामह। नरस्य का प्रतिष्ठा स्यादेतत् पृष्टो वदस्व मे॥
en: Yudhishthira said When of these, O grandfather, viz., relatives, or acts or riches, or wisdom, should be the refuge of a person? Accosted by men, answer me this!

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: भीष्म उवाच प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठा भूतानां प्रज्ञा लाभः परो मतः। प्रज्ञा निःश्रेयसी लोके प्रज्ञा स्वर्गो मतः सताम्॥
en: Bhishma said 'Wisdom is the refuge of creatures. Wisdom is considered as the greatest of acquisitions. Wisdom is the greatest happiness in the world. Wisdom is regarded by the good and virtuous as heaven.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: प्रज्ञया प्रापितार्थो हि बलिरैश्वर्यसंक्षये। प्रह्लादो नमुचिर्मङ्किस्तस्याः किं विद्यते परम्॥
en: It was through wisdom that Vali, Prahlada, Namuchi, and Manki, when they lost their prosperity, succeeded in gaining happiness, What is there that is superior to wisdom.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। इन्द्रकाश्यपसंवादं तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old story of the conversation between Indra and Kashyapa. Listen to it,O Yudhishthira!

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: वैश्यः कश्चिदृषिसुतं काश्यपं संशितव्रतम्। रथेन पातयामास श्रीमान् दृप्तस्तपस्विनम्॥
en: Once on a time a rich Vaishya, enjoying the highest state of prosperity and elated with his affluence, threw down, by rashly driving his car, a Rishi's son of rigid vows, named Kashyapa, given to penances.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: आर्तः स पतितः क्रुद्धस्त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मानमथाब्रवीत्। मरिष्याम्यधनस्येह जीवितार्थो न विद्यते॥ तथा मुमूर्षुमासीनमकूजन्तमचेतसम्। इन्द्रः शृगालरूपेण बभाषे लुब्धमानसम्॥ मनुष्ययोनिमिच्छन्ति सर्वभूतानि सर्वशः। मनुष्यत्वे च विप्रत्वं सर्व एवाभिनन्दति॥
en: Laid low on the ground, the young man, in great pain, yielded to his anger; and in despair resolved, saying, I shall renounce my life. A poor man has no necessity of life in this world!-While the Brahmana was lying in that condition, silent and agitated, shorn of energy and on the verge of death, Indra appeared there in the shape of a jackal and addressing him, said,-All (inferior) creatures seek to be born as men. Among men, again, the dignity of a Brahmana is much coveted.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: मनुष्यो ब्राह्मणश्चासि श्रोत्रियश्चासि काश्यप। सुदुर्लभमवाप्यैतन्न दोषान्मर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: You, O Kashyapa, are a human being! Amongst men you are again a Brahmana. Among Brahmanas, you are again well-read in the Vedas. Having acquired that which is difficult to get, you should not give up life from folly.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: सर्वे लाभाः साभिमाना इति सत्यवती श्रुतिः। संतोषणीयरूपोऽसि लोभाद् यदभिमन्यसे॥
en: All sorts of earthly) acquisitions are fraught with pride. What the Shrutis hold about it is perfectly true. You appear as the embodiment. In forming such a resolution about renouncing your life, you act from cupidity.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अहो सिद्धार्थता तेषां येषां सन्तीह पाणयः। अतीव स्पृहये तेषां येषां सन्तीह पाणयः॥
en: Those who have hands become successful. I eagerly wish to be like those creatures who have hands.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: पाणिमद्भ्यः स्पृहास्माकं यथा तव धनस्य वै। न पाणिलाभादधिको लाभः कश्चन विद्यते॥
en: We seek hands as eagerly as you seek riches. There is no acquisition more valuable than that of hands.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अपाणित्वाद् वयं ब्रह्मन् कण्टकं नोद्धरामहे। जन्तूनुच्चावचानङ्गे दशतो न कषाम वा॥
en: See, O Brahmana, I cannot get out this thorn that has entered my body, or crush these insects and worms that are biting and paining me greatly.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अथ येषां पुनः पाणी देवदत्तौ दशाङ्गुली। उद्धरन्ति कृमीनङ्गाद् दशतो निकषन्ति च॥
en: Those who have got two hands with ten fingers, can throw away or crush the worms that bite their limbs.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: वर्षाहिमातपानां च परित्राणानि कुर्वते। चैलमन्नं सुखं शय्यां निवातं चोपभुञ्जते॥
en: They can make shelters for themselves against rain, cold and heat. They can also enjoy excellent clothes for themselves, good food, comfortable beds, and excellent houses.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अधिष्ठाय च गां लोके भुञ्जते वाहयन्ति च। उपायैर्बहुभिश्चैव वश्यानात्मनि कुर्वते॥
en: Living on this Earth, those who have hands enjoy kine and other animals and cause them to carry loads or draw their cars, and by the help of various means make those animals obey them.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: ये खल्वजिह्वाः कृपणा अल्पप्राणा अपाणयः। सहन्ते तानि दुःखानि दिष्ट्या त्वं न तथा. मुने॥
en: Those living creatures that are without tongues, that are helpless, that have little strength, and that have no hands, suffer all kinds of misery. By good luck, O ascetic, you are not like them.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: दिष्ट्या त्वं न शृगालो वै न कृमिर्न च मूषकः। न सर्पो न च मण्डूको न चान्यः पापयोनिजः॥
en: By good luck, you are not a jackal, nor a worm, nor a mouse, nor a snake, nor a frog, or nor any other wretched animal.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: एतावतापि लाभेन तोष्टुमर्हसि काश्यप। किं पुनर्योऽसि सत्त्वानां सर्वेषां ब्राह्मणोत्तमः॥
en: With this gain, you should O Kashyapa, be contented. How happy, again, should you feel yourself, as you think that amongst living creatures you are a superior Brahmana.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: इमे मां कृमयोऽदन्ति येषामुद्धरणाय वै। नास्ति शक्तिरपाणित्वात् पश्यावस्थामिमां मम॥
en: These worms are biting me. For want of hands I cannot drive them off. Look at this my miserable condition.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अकार्यमिति चैवेमं नात्मानं संत्यजाम्यहम्। नातः पापीयसी योनि पतेयमपरामिति॥
en: I do not renounce life because it is a very sinful act, and lest, indeed, I may have a more miserable birth.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: मध्ये वै पापयोनीनां शार्गाली यामहं गतः। पापीयस्यो बहुतरा इतोऽन्याः पापयोनयः॥
en: This birth, to which I now belong, is rather tolerable. Miserable as it is, there are many more orders below it which miserable.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: जात्यैवैके सुखितराः सन्त्यन्ये भृशदुःखिताः। नैकान्तं सुखमेवेह क्वचित्पश्यामि कस्यचित्॥
en: By birth certain classes of creatures become happier than other who suffer great miseries. But I never see that there is any order of being which can enjoy consummate happiness.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: मनुष्या ह्याढ्यतां प्राप्य राज्यमिच्छन्त्यनन्तरम्। राज्याद् देवत्वमिच्छन्ति देवत्वादिन्द्रतामपि॥
en: more come Having acquired riches men next wish for sovereignty. Having acquired riches men next wish for sovereignty. Having acquired sovereignty they next wish to be gods. Having acquired that status they then wish to be the king of the gods.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: भवेस्त्वं यद्यपि त्वाट्यो न राजा न च दैवतम्। देवत्वं प्राप्य चेन्द्रत्वं नैव तुष्येस्तथा सति॥
en: If you become affluent, you will never become a king, nor a god. If by any means you become a god, you will then wish for the kingship of the gods. In no state you will be contented.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: न तृप्ति: प्रियलाभेऽस्ति तृष्णा नाद्भिः प्रशाम्यति। सम्प्रज्वलति सा भूयः समिद्भिग्वि पावकः॥
en: Contentment does not from acquisition of objects of desire. Thirst is never satiated although there is sufficient water. The thirst for acquisition is only increased by each fresh acquisition like a fire with new fuels thrown into it.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अस्त्येव त्वयि शोकोऽपि हर्षश्चापि तथा त्वयि। सुखदुःखे तथा चोभे तत्र का परिवेदना॥
en: You have grief for your associate. But joy, at the same time, lives in you. Both happiness and misery live in you. Why should you then yield to grief?

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: परिच्छिद्यैव कामानां सर्वेषां चैव कर्मणाम्। मूलं बुद्धीन्द्रियग्रामं शकुन्तानिव पञ्जरे॥
en: One should shut up, like birds in a cage, the very springs, viz., the understanding and the senses, of his desires and acts.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: न द्वितीयस्य शिरसश्छेदनं विद्यते क्वचित्। न च पाणेस्तृतीयस्य यन्नास्ति न ततो भयम्॥
en: A second head, or a third hand, can never by cut. That which does not exist produces no fear,

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: न खल्वप्यरसज्ञस्य कामः क्वचन जायते। संस्पर्शाद् दर्शनाद् वापि श्रवणाद् वापि जायते।॥
en: One who has not experienced the enjoyment of a certain object, never feels a desire for that object. Desires originate from the actual experience of the pleasures that touch, or sight, or hearing gives.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: न त्वं स्मरसि वारुण्या लट्वाकानां च पक्षिणाम्। ताभ्यां चाभ्यधिको भक्ष्यो न कश्चिद् विद्यते क्वचित्।।
en: You have no idea of the taste of the wine called Varuni or of the meat of the birds called Ladvaka. There is no drink and no so food sweeter than these.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: यानि चान्यानि भूतेषु भक्ष्यजातानि कस्यचित्। येषामभुक्तपूर्वाणि तेषामस्मृतिरेव ते॥
en: You have no idea also, O Kashyapa, of every other superior kind of drink and edible that exists among men, for you have never tasted it.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अप्राशनमसंस्पर्शमसंदर्शनमेव च। पुरुषस्यैष नियमो मन्ये श्रेयो न संशयः॥
en: Forsooth, therefore, a man to acquire happiness should vow not to taste, not to touch, and to see.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: पाणिमन्तो बलवन्तो धनवन्तो न संशयः। मनुष्या मानुषैरेव दासत्वमुपपादिताः॥ वधबन्धपरिक्लेशैः क्लिश्यन्ते च पुनः पुनः। ते खल्वपि रमन्ते च मोदन्ते च हसन्ति च॥
en: Creatures that have hands, forsooth, become strong and acquire riches. men are forced by men to become servants, and are repeatedly afflicted with death, imprisonment, and other punishments. Although such is their condition yet even they laugh and sport and become merry.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अपरे बाहुबलिनः कृतविद्या मनस्विनः। जुगुप्सितां च कृपणां पापवृत्तिमुपासते॥
en: Although gifted with strength of arms, knowledge and great energy of mind, others again, follow censurable, sinful, and miserable callings.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: उत्सहन्ते च ते वृत्तिमन्यामप्युपसेवितुम्। स्वकर्मणा तु नियतं भवितव्यं तु तत् तथा॥
en: They try to change such professions or better ones but then they are fettered by their pristine deeds and by the force of Destiny.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: न पुल्कसो न चाण्डाल आत्मानं त्यक्तुमिच्छति तया तुष्टः स्वया योन्या मायां पश्यस्व यादृशीम्॥
en: The vilest man of the Pukkasa or the Chandala orders never wishes to renounce his life. He is quiet satisfied with his birth. Mark the illusion in it.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: दृष्ट्वा कुणीन् पक्षहतान् मनुष्यानामयाविनः। सुसम्पूर्णः स्वया योन्या लब्धलाभोऽसि काश्यप॥
en: Seeing those amongst your order that have no arms, or are struck with palsy, or suffering from other diseases, you can consider yourself as very happy and possessed of valuable properties amongst the members of your own order.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: यदि ब्राह्मण देहस्ते निरातङ्कोनिरामयः। अङ्गानि च समग्राणि न च लोकेषु धिक्कृतः॥
en: If this your regenerated body remains all right, and free from disease, and all your limbs remain perfect, you will incur reproach amongst men.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: न केनचित् प्रवादेन सत्येनैवापहारिणा। धर्मायोत्तिष्ठ विप्रर्षे नात्मानं त्यक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: You should not, O Brahmana, renounce your life, even if any blame affects you which can be proved and which can you which can be proved and which lead your excommunication. Rise, and practise virtue. You should not throw away your life.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: यदि ब्रह्मशृणोष्येतच्छ्रद्दधासि च मे वचः। वेदोक्तस्यैव धर्मस्य फलं मुख्यमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: If, O twice-born one, you listen to me and confide in my words, you will acquire the highest reward of the religion laid down in the Vedas.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: स्वाध्यायमग्निसंस्कारमप्रमत्तोऽनुपा सत्यं दमं च दानं च स्पर्धिष्ठा मा च केनचित्॥
en: Engage, in Vedic studies, and properly maintain your consecrated hearth, and observe can to truth, and self-control, and charity. Never compare yourself boastfully with another.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: ये केचन स्वध्ययनाः प्राप्ता यजनयाज । कथं ते चानुशोचेयुायेयुर्वाप्यशोभनम्।
en: They who, by studying the Vedas, become competent for celebrating sacrifices for themselves and others, need no. regret or fear any sort of evil.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: इच्छन्तस्ते विहाराय सुखं महदवाप्नुयुः॥ उत जाताः सुनक्षत्रे सुतिथौ सुमुहूर्तजाः। यज्ञदानप्रजेहायां यतन्ते शक्तिपूर्वकम्॥
en: They who are born under an auspicious constellation on an auspicious lunation and at an auspicious hour, try their best for performing sacrifices, practising charity, and procreating children, and wishing to pass their time cheerfully in those acts, at last acquire very great happiness.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: नक्षत्रेष्वासुरेष्वन्ये दुस्तिथौ दुर्मुहूर्तजाः। सम्पतन्त्यासुरी योनि यज्ञप्रसववर्जिताः॥
en: They, on the other hand, who are born under evil slaves, inauspicious lunations and at evil hours, cannot perform sacrifices and get progeny and at last fall into the Asura order.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अहमासं पण्डितको हैतुको वेदनिन्दकः। आन्वीक्षिकी तर्कविद्यामनुरक्तो निरर्थिकाम्॥
en: In my previous birth 1 had much useless learning. I always tried to find out reasons and had very little faith. I used to censure the Vedas. I was unacquainted with the fourfold objects of life, and was devoted to the science of reaping which is based upon ocular or tangible proofs.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: हेतुवादान् प्रवदिता वक्ता संसत्सु हेतुमत्। आक्रोष्टा चाभिवक्ता च ब्रह्मवाक्येषु च द्विजान्॥
en: I used to speak of reasons only. Indeed, in assemblies, I always spoke of reasons. I used to speak irreverently of the injunctions of the Shrutis and address Brahmanas haughtily.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: नास्तिकः सर्वशङ्की च मूर्खः पण्डितमानिकः। तस्येयं फलनिर्वृत्तिः शृगालत्वं मम द्विज॥
en: I was an atheist a sceptic, and though really ignorant, proud of my learning. This birth of a jackal that I have got in this life is the outcome, twice-born one, of those sins of mine.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: अपि जातु तथा तस्मादहोरात्रशतैरपि। यदहं मानुषी योनि शृगालः प्राप्नुयां पुनः॥ संतुष्टश्चाप्रमत्तश्च यज्ञदानतपोरतिः। ज्ञेयज्ञाता भवेयं वै वर्ण्यवर्जयिता तथा॥
en: If even after hundreds of days and nights, a jackal that I am now, I can once again secure the birth of humanity, I shall then pass my life in contentment, caring for the true objects of existence, and engaged in sacrifices and gifts. I shall then know what should be known, and shun what should be shunned.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: ततः स मुनिरुत्थाय काश्यपस्तमुवाच ह। अहो बतासि कुशलो बुद्धिमांश्चेति विस्मित:॥
en: Thus addressed, the ascetic Kashyapa, rising up, said-0, you are surely endued with great knowledge, and intelligence. I really wonder at all this.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: समवैक्षत तं विप्रो ज्ञानदीभ्रुण चक्षुषा। ददर्श चैनं देवानां देवमिन्द्रं शचीपतिम्॥
en: With eye whose vision was extended by knowledge, the Brahmana then saw that being who had addressed him as Indra the king on the gods and the lord of Shachi.

description: Relatives, acts, riches and wisdom—which of them should be the refuge
sn: ततः सम्पूजयामास काश्यपो हरिवाहनम्। अनुज्ञातस्तु तेनाथ प्रविवेश स्वमालयम्॥
en: Kashyapa then adored that god having the best of horses to carry him. Receiving afterwards with the god's permission, the Bralunana returned to his house.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यद्यस्ति दत्तमिष्टं वा तपस्तप्तं तथैव च। गुरूणां वापि शुश्रूषा तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grand-father, if gifts, sacrifices, penances and dutiful services offered to preceptors, yield wisdom and supreme bliss.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: भीष्म उवाच आत्मनानर्थयुक्तेन पापे निविशते मनः। स्वकर्मकलुषं कृत्वा कृच्छ्रे लोके विधीयते॥
en: Bhishma said 'If the mind is stricken with desire, anger and other evil passions, it then inclines towards sin. If one's acts are sullied by sin, he is obliged to dwell in painful regions.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: दुर्भिक्षादेव दुर्भिक्षं क्लेशात् क्लेशं भयाद् भयम्। मृतेभ्यः प्रमृतं यान्ति दरिद्राः पापकारिणः॥
en: Sinful men are born as poor men and suffer again and again the pangs of fainine, woe, fear, and death.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: उत्सवादुत्सवं यान्ति स्वर्गात् स्वर्ग सुखात् सुखम्। श्रद्दधानाश्च दान्ताश्च धनाढ्याः शुभकारिणः॥
en: The virtuous, the faithful, and the selfrestrained, become born as affluent men and continually enjoy festivities and heaven and happiness.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: व्यालकुञ्जरदुर्गेषु सर्पचोरभयेषु च। हस्तावापेन गच्छन्ति नास्तिकाः किमतः परम्॥
en: Unbelievers, with their hands bound, are sent to regions rendered inaccessible by carnivorous beasts and elephants, and dreadful with snakes and robbers, What more should I say of them.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: प्रियदेवातिथेयाश्च वदान्याः प्रियसाधवः। क्षेम्यमात्मवतां मार्गमास्थिता हस्तदक्षिणम्॥
en: They, on the other hand, who respects god and guests, who are liberal who love good and honest men, enjoy for their acts of charity, that happy way which belongs to persons of purified souls.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: पुलाका इव धान्येषु पुत्तिका इव पक्षिषु। तद्विधास्ते मनुष्याणां येषां धर्मो न कारणम्॥
en: They who have no respect for virtue are as vile among men as seedless grains among corn or the gnat among birds.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: सुशीघ्रमपि धावन्तं विधानमनुधावति। शेते सह शयानेन येन येन यथा कृतम्॥
en: The pre-ordained act follows the doer even if the latter tries his best for leaving it behind. It sleeps when he sleeps and does whatever else he does.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: उपतिष्ठति तिष्ठन्तं गच्छन्तमनुगच्छति। करोति कुर्वतः कर्म च्छायेवानुविधीयते॥
en: Like his shadow it takes rest when he rests, goes on when he goes on, and acts when he acts.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: येन येन यथा यद् यत् पुरा कर्म समीहितम्। तत्तदेकतरो भुङ्क्ते नित्यं विहितमात्मना॥
en: Whatever acts a man does in his previous birth, he certainly enjoys the fruits thereof.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: स्वकर्मफलनिक्षेपं विधानपरिरक्षितम्। भूतग्राममिमं कालः समन्तात् परिकर्षति॥
en: Death is dragging all creatures who are destined to take birth according to their deserts and are liable to enjoy or suffer that which has been ordained as the fruit of their acts.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: अचोद्यमानानि यथा पुष्पाणि च फलानि च। स्वं कालं नातिवर्तन्ते तथा कर्म पुरा कृतम्॥
en: Pristine acts develop their consequences in their own proper time even as flowers and fruits, without any outward efforts, never fail to appear when the proper season sets in.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: सम्मानश्चावमानश्च लाभालाभौ क्षयोदयौ। प्रवृत्ता विनिवर्तन्ते विधानान्ते पुनः पुनः॥
en: After the ordained consequences of pristine acts have been dissipated (by enjoyment or sufferance), honour and disgrace, profit and loss, development and decay no longer come. This takes place again and again.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: आत्मना विहितं दुःखामात्मना विहितं सुखम्। गर्भशय्यामुपादाय भुज्यते पौर्वदेहिकम्॥
en: While still in the mother's womb, a creature enjoys or suffers the happiness of the misery that has been ordained for him by his own acts,

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: बालो युवा च वृद्धश्च यत् करोति शुभाशुभम्। तस्यां तस्यावस्थायां तत्फलं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: In childhood or youth or old age whenever a man does a good or bad act the consequences there of surely visit him in his next life at precisely the same period.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम्। तथा पूर्वकृतं कर्म कर्तारमनुगच्छति॥
en: As a calf recognises and comes to it mother in the midst of even a thousand kine, so the pristine acts recognise and visit the doer in his new life.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: समुन्नमग्रतो वस्त्रं पश्चाच्छुध्यति कर्मणा। उपवासैः प्रतप्तानां दीर्घं सुखमनन्तकम्॥
en: Washed in water a piece of cloth becomes clean. Likewise, men, repenting (for their past misdeeds), get eternal happiness by proper penances.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: दीर्घकालेन तपसा सेवितेन तपोवने। धर्मनिर्धूतपापानां सम्पद्यन्ते मनोरथाः॥
en: By living in the woods and by practising austerities for a long period, one can wash themselves of their sins, and get the objects of their hearts.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: शकुनानामिवाकाशे मत्स्यानामिव चोदके। पदं यथा न दृश्येत तथा ज्ञानविदां गतिः॥
en: As no one can mark the track of birds in the sky or of fishes in the water, so the track of persons whose souls have been purified by knowledge cannot be seen by any.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: अलमन्यैरुपालम्भैः कीर्तितैश्च व्यतिक्रमैः। पेशलं चानुरूपं च कर्तव्यं हितमात्मनः॥
en: There is no need of speaking more of sinful acts. Suffice it to say that one should, with proper judgement and as best as can, do what is for his well-being. This is the means by which wisdom and great happiness may be acquired." persons whose souls have been purified by knowledge cannot be seen by any.

description: Whether gifts, sacrifices, penance's and dutiful services to preceptors yield wisdom and bliss
sn: अलमन्यैरुपालम्भैः कीर्तितैश्च व्यतिक्रमैः। पेशलं चानुरूपं च कर्तव्यं हितमात्मनः॥
en: There is no need of speaking more of sinful acts. Suffice it to say that one should, with proper judgement and as best as can, do what is for his well-being. This is the means by which wisdom and great happiness may be acquired."

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कुत: सृष्टमिदं विश्वं जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्। प्रलये च कमभ्येति तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Whence has this universe, consisting of mobile and immobile creatures, originated? Whom does it go to when it is destroyed? Tell me this, O grandfather.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: ससागरः सगगन सशैलः सबलाहकः। सभूमिः साग्निपवनो लोकोऽयं केन निर्मित:॥
en: Indeed, by whom has this universe with its oceans, its sky, its mountains, its clouds, its lands, its fire, and its wind, been created.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: कथं सृष्टानि भूतानि कथं वर्णविभक्तयः। शौचशौचं कथं तेषां धर्माधर्मविधिः कथम्॥
en: How were all objects created? Whence has this division of creatures originated? Whence are their purity and impurity, and the laws about virtue and vice?

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: कीदृशो जीवतां जीवः क्व वा गच्छन्ति ये मृताः। अस्माल्लोकादमुं लोकं सर्वं शंसतु नो भवान्॥
en: Of what nature is the life of living creatures? Where also do they go who die? Tell us everything about this and the next world.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। भृगुणाभिहितं शास्त्रं भरद्वाजाय पृच्छते॥
en: Bhishina said Regarding it is cited the old discourse of the sacred words the Bhrigu said in reply to the questions of Bharadwaja addressed him thusकैलासशिखरे दृष्ट्वा दीप्यमानं महौजसम्।

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: भृगु महर्षिमासीनं भरद्वाजोऽन्वपृच्छत्॥
en: Seeing the sage Bhrigu, endued with high power and effulgent seated on the peak of Kailasa mountain, Bharadvaja said him

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: ससागर: सगगनः सशैल: सबलाहकः। सभूमिः साग्निपवनो लोकोऽयं केन निर्मितः॥
en: Bharadwaja said By whom was this world its ocean, its sky, its mountains, its clouds, its lands, its fire, and its wind, created?

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: कथं सृष्टानि भूतानि कथं वर्णविभक्तयः। शौचाशौचं कथं तेषां धर्माधर्मविधिः कथम्॥
en: How were all creatures first created? Whence originated this distinction of castes? Whence the purity and the impurity of conduct, and whence the laws about virtue and vice, for living creatures?

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: कीदृशो जीवतां जीवः क्व वा गच्छन्ति ये मृताः। परलोकमिमं चापि सर्वं शंसितुमर्हसि॥
en: What type of individual soul is of the living creatures? Where they go after the death. What is this and next world? You are able to explain all the things.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: एवं स भगवान् पृष्टो भरद्वाजेन संशयम्। ब्रह्मर्षिर्ब्रह्मसंकाशः सर्वं तस्मै ततोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus accosted about his doubts by Bharadwaja, the illustrious and twice-born Rishi Bhrigu who took after Brahma itself, replied to him thus.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: भृगुरुवाच मानसो नाम विख्यातः श्रुतपूर्वो महर्षिभिः। अनादिनिधनो देवस्तथाभेद्योऽजरामरः॥
en: Bhrigu said There is a Primeval Being, known to the great Rishis, by the name of Manasa. He is without beginning and without end. That Divine being cannot be cut by weapons. he is without decay and is immortal.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: अव्यक्त इति विख्यातः शाश्वतोऽथाक्षयोऽव्ययः। यतः सृष्टानि भूतानि जायन्ते च म्रियन्ति च॥
en: He is Unmanifest. he is Eternal, Undecaying, and Unchangeable. By Him are crcatures born and through Him they die.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: सोऽसृजत् प्रथमं देवो महान्तं नाम नामतः। महान् ससर्जाहंकारं स चापि भगवानथ॥ आकाशमिति विख्यातं सर्वभूतधरः प्रभुः।
en: He first created a Divine Being known by the name of Mahat (Great). Mahat created Consciousness, who created Space. That powerful Being holds all created objects.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: आकाशादभवद् वारि सलिलादग्निमारुतौ। अग्निमारुतसंयोगात् ततः समभवन्मही॥
en: From Space was born Water, and from Water were born Fire and Wind. Through the union of Fire and Wind was born the Earth.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: ततस्तेजोमयं दिव्यं पद्मं सृष्टं स्वयम्भुवा। तस्मात् पद्मात् समभवद् ब्रह्मा वेदमयो निधिः॥
en: Self-born Manasa then created a divine Lotus of Energy. From that Lotus originated Brahmana, that Ocean of Veda.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: अहंकार इति ख्यातः सर्वभूतात्मभूतकृत्। ब्रह्मा वै स महातेजा य एते पञ्च धातवः॥
en: The Shrutis say that as soon as born, that divine Being uttered the words—I am He. For this He passed by the name of Consciousness. All created things are his body and He is their Creator. These five elements that we see are the Brahman of great energy.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: शैलास्तस्यास्थिसंज्ञास्तु मेदो मांसं च मेदिनी। समुद्रास्तस्य रुधिरमाकाशमुदरं तथा॥
en: The Mountains from his bones. the Earth forins his fat and flesh. the Oceans constitute his blood. space is his stomach.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: पवनश्चैव निःश्वासस्तेजोऽग्निर्निम्नगाः शिराः। अग्नीषोमौ तु चन्द्रार्को नयने तस्य विश्रुते॥
en: The Wind forins his breath. Fire his energy. The rivers forms his arteries and veins. Agni and Soma, otherwise called the Sun and the Moon, are his eyes.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: नभश्चोर्ध्वं शिरस्तस्य क्षितिः पादौ भुजौ दिशः। दुर्विज्ञेयो ह्यचिन्त्यात्मा सिद्धैरपि न संशयः॥
en: The sky is above his head. The Earth is his two feet. The cardinal and minor points of compass are his arms, Forsooth, He is incapable of being known and His Soul cannot be conceived even by successful ascetics.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: स एष भगवान् विष्णुरनन्त इति विश्रुतः। सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्थो दुर्विज्ञेयोऽकृतात्मभिः॥
en: That Divine Being, who pervades the entire universe, passes also by the name of Ananta (Infinite). He lives in Consciousness, and persons of impure souls cannot know him.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: अहंकारस्य यः स्रष्टा सर्वभूतभवाय वै। यतः समभवद् विश्वं पृष्टोऽहं यदिह त्वया॥
en: Asked by you I have now told you of Him who created objects, and from whom this universe had originated.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: भरद्वाज उवाच गगनस्य दिशां चैव भूतलस्यानिलस्य वा। कान्यत्र परिमाणानि संशयं छिन्धि तत्त्वतः॥
en: Bharadwaja said What is the extent of the sky, of the points of the horizon, of the surface of this Earth, and of the Wind? By telling me the truth, remove my doubts.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: भृगुरुवाच अनन्तमेतदाकाशं सिद्धदैवतसेवितम्। रम्यं नानाश्रयाकीर्णं यस्यान्तो नाधिगम्यते॥
en: The sky you see above is infinite. It is the abode of successful ascetics and of celestial beings. It is lovely and consists of various regions. Its limits cannot be determined.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: उर्ध्वं गतेरधस्तात्तु चन्द्रादित्यौ न दृश्यतः। तत्र देवाः स्वयं दीप्ता भास्वराभाग्निवर्चसः॥
en: The Sun and Moon cannot sec, above or below, beyond the range of their own rays. There where are rays of the Sun and the Moon cannot go are luminaries which are selfeffulgent and shining like the Sun or the fire.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: ते चाप्यन्तं न पश्यन्ति नभसः प्रथितौजसः। दुर्गमत्वादनन्तत्वादिति मे विद्धि मानद॥
en: Know this, O giver of honours, that even these luminaries which have great effulgence, do not see the limits of the sky for the inaccessibility and infinity of those limits.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: उपरिष्टोपरिष्टात्तु प्रज्वलद्भिः स्वयंप्रभैः। निरुद्धमेतदाकाशमप्रमेयं सुरैरपि॥
en: This Space which even the very celestials cannot measure contains many shining and self-luminous worlds each above the other.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: पृथिव्यन्ते समुद्रास्तु समुद्रान्ते तमः स्मृतम्। तमसोऽन्ते जलं प्राहुर्जलस्यान्तेऽग्निरेव च॥
en: Beyond the limits of land are oceans, Beyond water is darkness. Beyond darkness is water again, and beyond water is fire.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: रसातलान्ते सलिलं जलान्ते पन्नगाधिपाः। तदन्ते पुनराकाशमाकाशान्ते पुनर्जलम्॥
en: Underneath, beyond the neither regions is water. Beyond water is the region of the great serpents. Beyond that is sky once more, and beyond the sky is water again.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: एवमन्तं भगवतः प्रमाणं सलिलस्य च। अग्निमारुततोयेभ्यो दुर्जेयं दैवतैरपि॥
en: Thus exist water and sky alternately without end. Such are the limits of the god of water. The very gods cannot determine the limits of fire and wind and water.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: अग्निमारुततोयानां वर्णाः क्षितितलस्य च। आकाशादवगृह्यन्ते भिद्यन्तेऽतत्त्वदर्शनात्॥
en: The nature of fire, wind, water, and land, is like that of space. It is the absence of true knowledge that draws distinction between them.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: पठन्ति चैव मुनयः शास्त्रेषु विविधेषु च। त्रैलोक्ये सागरे चैव प्रमाणं विहितं यथा॥
en: Sages read in various scriptures the limits of the three worlds and the ocean.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: अदृश्याय त्वगम्याय कः प्रमाणमुदाहरेत्। सिद्धानां देवतानां च यदा परिमिता गतिः॥
en: Who is there, however, who can set limits to what cannot be seen and what is inaccessible?

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: तदा गौणमनन्तस्य नामानन्तेति विश्रुतम्। नामधेयानुरूपस्य मानसस्य महात्मनः॥
en: If even it becomes possible to learn the limits of the sky which is the region of the gods and successful ascetics, it is not possible to set limits to that which is limitless and passes by the name of the Infinite, to that which answers its name, viz., the high-souled Manasa?

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: यदा तु दिव्यं तद् रूपं ह्रसते वर्धते पुनः। कोऽन्यस्तद्वेदितुं शक्तो योऽपि स्यात् तद्विधोऽपरः॥३४
en: When again His form is sometimes contracted and sometimes expanded, how can any one else save one who is equal to him, perceive his limits?

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: ततः पुष्करतः सृष्टः सर्वज्ञो मूर्तिमान् प्रभुः। ब्रह्मा धर्ममयः पूर्वः प्रजापतिरनुत्तमः॥
en: From the Lotus sprang first the Omniscient lord Brahman, endued with form, of the essence of Righteousness, and the Creator of all mobile and immobile things.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: भरद्वाज उवाच पुष्कराद् यदि सम्भूतो ज्येष्ठं भवति पुष्करम्। ब्रह्माणं पूर्वजं चाह भवान् संदेह एव मे॥
en: Bharadwaja said If Brahman originated from the Lotus, then it is the Lotus that should be considered as the first-born and not Brahman. Why, however, is Brahman said to be the first? Do you dispel this doubt of mine.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: भृगुरुवाच मानसस्येह या मूर्तिर्ब्रह्मत्वं समुपागता। तस्यासनविधानार्थं पृथिवी पद्ममुच्यते॥
en: Bhrigu said The Earth is called that Lotus. It was created for giving a seat to that form of Manasa which became Brahman.

description: The origin of the universe. The creator and the living creature
sn: कर्णिका तस्य पद्मस्य मेरुर्गगनमुच्छ्रितः। तस्य मध्ये स्थितो लोकान् सृजते जगतः प्रभुः॥
en: Extending up to heaven itself, the Sumeru became the pericarp of that Lotus. Remaining within it, the powerful Lord of the Universe created all the worlds.

sn: भरद्वाज उवाच प्रजाविसर्ग विविध कथं स सृजते प्रभुः। मेरुमध्ये स्थितो ब्रह्मा तद् ब्रूहि द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Bharadwaja said-Tell me, O best of Brahmans, how the powerful Brahman, living within Meru, created these various kinds of objects.

sn: भृगुरुवाच प्रजाविसर्ग विविधं मानसो मानसासृजत्। संरक्षणार्थं भूतानां सृष्टं प्रथमतो जलम्॥
en: Bhrigu said The great Manasa (in his form of Brahman) created the various objects by his Will. For the protection of all creatures, he first created water.

sn: यत् प्राणः सर्वभूतानां वर्धन्ते येन च प्रजाः। परित्यक्ताश्च नश्यन्ति तेनेदं सर्वमावृतम्॥
en: Water is the life of all creatures, and it helps their growth. If there be no water, all creatures would die. The cntire universe is pervaded by water.

sn: पृथिवी पर्वता मेघा मूर्तिमन्तश्च ये परे। सर्वं तद् वारुणं ज्ञेयमापस्तस्तम्भिरे यतः॥
en: Earth, mountains, clouds, and all things which have form, are all as transformations of water. They have all been produced by water being solidified.

sn: भरद्वाज उवाच कथं सलिलमुत्पन्नं कथं चैवाग्निमारुतौ। कथं वा मेदिनी सृष्टेत्यत्र मे संशयो महान्॥
en: Bharadwaja said, How did water originate? How fire and Wind? How also was the Earth created? I have great doubts about it.

sn: भृगुरुवाच ब्रह्मकल्पे पुरा ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मर्षीणां समागमे। लोकसम्भवसंदेहः समुत्पन्नो महात्मनाम्॥
en: O twice-born one, in very ancient times called the Brahma-Kalpa, great Rishis, when they assembled together, felt this very doubt about the creation of the universe.

sn: तेऽतिष्ठन् ध्यानमालम्ब्य मौनमास्थाय निश्चलाः। त्यक्तहाराः पवनपा दिव्यं वर्षशतं द्विजाः॥
en: Governing speech, they remained immovable, engaged in contemplation. Having abstained from food, they lived upon air alone, and remained thus for a thousand divine years.

sn: तेषां ब्रह्ममयी वाणी सर्वेषां श्रोत्रमागमत्। दिव्या सरस्वती तत्र सम्बभूव नभस्तलात्॥
en: At the end of that time, certain words as sacred as those of the Vedas simultaneously reached the ears of all. Indeed, this celestial voice was heard in the sky to say—

sn: पुरा स्तिमितमाकाशमनन्तमचलोपमम्। नष्टचन्द्रार्कपवनं प्रसुप्तमिव सम्बभौ॥
en: Formerly there was only infinite Space, motionless and immovable. Without sun, moon, stars, and wind, it seemed to be asleep.

sn: ततः सलिलमुत्पन्नं तमसीवापरं तमः। तस्माच्च सलिलोत्पीडादुदतिष्ठत मारुतः॥
en: Then water originated like something darker within darkness. Then from the pressure of water sprang wing.

sn: यथा भाजनमच्छिद्रं निःशब्दमिव लक्ष्यते। तच्चाम्भसा पूर्यमाणं सशब्दं कुरुतेऽनिलः॥ तथा सलिलसंरुद्धे नभसोऽन्ते निरन्तरे। भित्त्वार्णवतलं वायुः समुत्पतति घोषवान्॥
en: As an empty vessel having no hole appears at first to have no sound, but when filled with water, air appears and makes a great noise, so when infinite Space was filled with water, the wind arose with a great noise, passing through the water.

sn: स एष चरते वायुरर्णवोत्पीडसम्भवः। आकाशस्थानमासाद्य प्रशान्ति नाधिगच्छति॥
en: Generated by the pressure of the ocean of water, that wind still passes on. Occupying empty space, its motion is never stoppcd.

sn: तस्मिन् वाय्वम्बुसंघर्षे दीप्ततेजा महाबलः। प्रादुरभूदूर्ध्वशिखः कृत्वा निस्तिमिरं नमः॥
en: Then on account of the friction of wind and water, fire endued with great power and burning energy, came into being, with flames directed upwards. That fire dissipated the darkness that had covered Space.

sn: अग्निः पवनसंयुक्तः खं समाक्षिपते जलम्। सोऽग्निमारुतसंयोगाद्घनत्वमुपपद्यते॥
en: Helped by the wind, fore combined Space and Water. In fact, combining with the wind, fire became solidified.

sn: तस्याकाशे निपतितः स्नेहस्तिष्ठति योऽपरः। स संघातत्वमापन्नो भूमित्वमनुगच्छति॥
en: While dropping from the sky, the liquid portion of fire being solidified again became what is known as the Earth.

sn: रसानां सर्वगन्धानां स्नेहानां प्राणिनां तथा। भूमिर्यानिरिह ज्ञेया यस्यां सर्वं प्रसूयते॥
en: The Earth or land, in which everything is born, is the root of all sorts of taste, of all sorts of scent, of all sorts of liquids, and of all kinds of animals,

sn: भरद्वाज उवाच त एते धातवः पञ्च ब्रह्मा यानसृजत् पुरा। आवृता यैरिमे लोका महाभूताभिसंज्ञिताः॥ यदासृजत सहस्राणि भूतानां स महामतिः। पञ्चानामेव भूतत्वं कथं समुपपद्यते॥
en: When the great Brahman has created thousands of creatures why is it that only these five elements which he created first, which permeate the entire universe and which are great creatures.

sn: भृगुरुवाच अमितानां महाशब्दो यान्ति भूतानि सम्भवम्। ततस्तेषां महाभूतशब्दोऽयमुपपद्यते॥
en: Bhrigu said All things which belong to the Infinite or the Vast are known by the name of Great. Therefore these five clements are called Great creatures.

sn: चेष्टा वायुः खमाकाशमूष्माग्निः सलिलं द्रवः। पृथिवी चात्र संघातः शरीरं पाञ्चभौतिकम्॥
en: Activity is wind. The sound is space. The heat that lives within it is fire. The liquid juices cc:itained in it are water. The solidified matter, viz., flesh and bones from the Earth. The bodies are thus made of the five elements.

sn: इत्येतैः पञ्चमिर्भूतैर्युक्तं स्थावरजङ्गमम्। श्रोत्रं घ्राणं रसः स्पर्शो दृष्टिश्चेन्द्रियसंज्ञिताः॥
en: All mobile and immobile objects are formed of these five elements. The five senses also made of the give clements. The car is formed of the properties of space. The nose of earth; the tongue of water; touch of wind; and eyes of tire.

sn: भरद्वाज उवाच पञ्चभिर्यदि भूतैस्तु युक्ताः स्थावरजङ्गमाः। स्थावराणां न दृश्यन्ते शरीरे पञ्च धातवः॥
en: Bharadwaja said If all mobile and immobile objects be made of these five elements, why is it that in all immobile objects those elements are not seen.

sn: अनूष्मणामचेष्टानां घनानां चैव तत्त्वतः। वृक्षाणां नोपलभ्यन्ते शरीरे पञ्च धातवः॥
en: Trees do not appear to have possessed any heat. They appear to have no motion. They are again formed of thick particles. The five elements are not seen in them.

sn: न शृण्वन्ति न पश्यन्ति न गन्धरसवेदिनः। न च स्पर्श विजानन्ति ते कथं पाञ्चभौतिकाः॥
en: Trees do not hear; they do not sec; they cannot smell or taste. They cannot touch. How then can they be regarded as formed of the five elements.

sn: अद्रवत्वादनग्नित्वादभूमित्वादवायुतः। आकाशस्याप्रमेयत्वाद् वृक्षाणां नास्ति भौतिकम्॥
en: It appears to me that for the absence of any liquid matter in them, of any heat, of any earth, of any wind, and of any empty space, trees cannot be considered as compounds of the five primary elements.

sn: भृगुरुवाच घनानामपि वृक्षाणामाकाशोऽस्ति न संशयः। तेषां पुष्पफलव्यक्तिर्नित्यं समुपपद्यते॥
en: Bhrigu said Forsooth, though possessed of density, trees have space within them. They always bear flowers and fruits.

sn: उष्मतो म्लायते पण त्वक् फलं पुष्पमेव च। म्लायते शीर्यते चापि स्पर्शस्तेनात्र विद्यते॥
en: They have heat within them for which leaf, bark, fruit, and flower are seen to fall off. They sicken and dry up. This indicates that they have perception of touch.

sn: वाय्वग्न्यशनिनिर्घोषैः फलं पुष्पं विशीर्यते। श्रोत्रेण गृह्यते शब्दस्तस्माच्छृण्वन्ति पादपाः॥
en: By sound of wind and fire and thunder, their fruits and flowers fall down. Sound is perceived through the ear. Trees have, therefore, ears and do hear.

sn: वल्ली वेश्यते वृक्षं सर्वतश्चैव गच्छति। न ह्यदृष्टेश्च मार्गोऽस्ति तस्मात् पश्यन्ति पादपाः॥
en: A creeper entwines a tree all around. A blind thing cannot see its way. Therefore it is evident that trees have vision.

sn: पुण्यापुण्यैस्तथा गन्धैर्दू पैश्च विविधैरपि। अरोगाः पुष्पिता: सन्ति तस्माज्जिघ्रन्ति पादपाः॥
en: Again trees regain vigour and put forth flowers for good and bad smell, of the sacred incense of all sorts. It is evident that trees have scent.

sn: पादैः सलिलपानाच्च व्याधीनां चापि दर्शनात्। व्याधिप्रतिक्रियत्वाच्च विद्यते रसनं दुमे॥
en: They draw water by their roots. They catch all sorts of diseases. Those diseases again are cured by various operations. From this it is clear that trees have perception of taste.

sn: वक्त्रेणोत्पलनालेन यथोर्ध्वं जलमाददेत्। तथा पवनसंयुक्तः पादैः पिबति पादपः॥
en: As one can draw water through the hole of a lotus-stalk, trees also, with the help of wind, drink through their roots.

sn: सुखदुःखयोश्च ग्रहणाच्छिन्नस्य च विरोहणात्। जीवं पश्यामि वृक्षाणामचैतन्यं न विद्यते॥
en: They are subject to pleasure and pain, and grow when cut or lopped off. These facts clearly prove that trees have life. They are not manimate.

sn: तेन तज्जलमादत्तं जरयत्यग्निमारुतौ। आहारपरिणामाच्च स्नेहो वृद्धिश्च जायते॥
en: Fire and wind cause the water thus drawn up to be digested. The tree grows and becomes humid proportionate to the quantity of the water taken up.

sn: जङ्गमानां च सर्वेषां शरीरे पञ्च धातवः। प्रत्येकशः प्रभिद्यन्ते यैः शरीरं विचेष्टते॥
en: In the bodies of all mobile things the five elements reside. The proportions are different in each. Mobile objects can move for these five elements.

sn: त्वद् च मांसं तथास्थीनि मज्जा स्नायुश्च पञ्चमम्। इत्येतदिह संघातं शरीरे पृथिवीमयम्॥
en: Skin, fresh, bones, marrow, and arteries and veins, that exist together in the body are formed of earth.

sn: तेजो ह्यग्निस्तथा क्रोधश्चक्षुरूष्मा तथैव च। अग्निर्जस्यते यश्च पञ्चाग्नेयाः शरीरिणः॥
en: Energy, anger, eyes, internal heat, and the heat which digests the good taken, these five, form the fire that exists in all embodied creatures.

sn: श्रोत्रं घ्राणं तथाऽऽस्यं च हृदयं कोष्ठमेव च। आकाशात् प्राणिनामेते शरीरे पञ्च धातवः॥
en: The cars, nostrils, mouth, heart, and Stomach, these five, form the element of space that exists in the bodies of living creatures.

sn: श्लेष्मा पित्तमथ स्वेदो वसा शोणितमेव च। इत्यापः पञ्चधा देहे भवन्ति प्राणिनां सदा॥
en: Phlegm, bile, sweat, fat, blood are the five kinds of water that exist in inobile bodies.

sn: प्राणात् प्रणीयते प्राणी व्यानाद् व्यायच्छतेतथा। गच्छत्यपानोऽधश्चैव समानो हृद्यवस्थितः॥
en: Through the vital breath called Prana, a living creature is capable of moving about. Through that called Vyana they act. That called Apana goes downward. That called Samana lives within the heart.

sn: उदानादुच्छ्वसिति च प्रतिभेदाच्च भाषते। इत्येते वायवः पञ्च चेश्यन्तीह देहिनम्॥
en: Through that called Udana one passes exertion and is enabled to speak by virtue of its going through (the lungs, the throat, and the mouth). These are the five sorts of vital airs that cause an embodied creature to live and Imove.

sn: भूमेर्गन्धगुणान् वेत्ति रसं चाभ्यः शरीरवान्। ज्योतिषा चक्षुषा रूपं स्पर्श वेत्ति च वाहिना॥
en: Through the earth-element an embodied creature perceives the properties of scent. From the water-element he perceives taste. From the fire-element as represented by the eyes, he perceives forms, and from the wind-element he perceives touch.

sn: गन्धः स्पृशो रसो रूपं शब्दश्चात्र गुणाः स्मृताः। तस्य गन्धस्य वक्ष्यामि विस्तराभिहितान् गुणान्॥
en: Scent, touch, taste, vision and sound, are considered as the common properties of all mobile and immobile objects. I shall first describe the several sorts of scent.

sn: इष्टश्चानिष्टगन्धश्च मधुरः कटुरेव च। निर्हारी संहतः स्निग्धो रूक्षो विशद एव च॥
en: They are pleasant, unpleasant, sweet, pungent, far-reaching, varied, dry, indifferent.

sn: एवं नवविधो ज्ञेयः पार्थिवे गन्धविस्तरः। ज्योतिः पश्यति चक्षुर्त्या स्पर्श वेत्ति च वायुना॥
en: Scent which is formed of the earth element, consists of these nine sorts. Light is seen by the eyes, and touch through the wind-clement.

sn: शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसञ्चापि गुणा: स्मृताः। रसज्ञानं तु वक्ष्यामि तन्मे निगदतः शृण॥
en: Sound, touch, vision and taste are the properties of water. I shall describe fully that now the perception of taste. Listen to me.

sn: रसो बहुविधः प्रोक्त ऋषिभिः प्रथितात्मभिः। मधुरो लवणास्तिक्तः कषायोऽम्लः कटुस्तथा॥
en: Great Rishis have mentioned various sorts of taste. They are sweet, saltish, bitter, astringent, sour, and pungent.

sn: एष पड्विधविस्तारो रसो वारिमयः स्मृतः। शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च त्रिगुणं ज्योतिरुच्यते॥
en: These are the six sorts of taste belonging to the water-element. The light is the combind result of sound, touch and forin

sn: ज्योतिः पश्यति रूपाणि रूपं च बहुधा स्मृतम्। ह्रस्वो दीर्घस्तथा स्थूलश्चतुरस्रोऽनृवृत्तवान्॥ शुक्ल: कृष्णस्तथा रक्तः पीतो नीलारुणस्तथा। कठिनश्चिक्कणः श्लक्ष्ण: पिच्छिलो मृदुदारुणः॥
en: Through light one perceives forins. Form is of various kinds, Short, tall, thick square, round, white, black, red, blue, yellow, reddish, hard, bright, smooth, oily, soft and terrible.

sn: एवं पोडशविस्तारो ज्योतीरूपगुणः स्मृतः। शब्दस्पर्शी च विज्ञेयौ द्विगुणो वायुरित्युत॥ वायव्यस्तु गुणः स्पर्श: स्पर्शश्च बहुधा स्मृतः। उष्णः शीत: सुखो दुःखः स्निग्धो विशद एव च॥
en: These are the sixteen sorts of forin which forms the property of light or vision. The property of the wind element is touch. Touch is of various sorts; warm, cold, agreeable and disagrecable, indifferent, burning, mild, soft, light and heavy.

sn: तथा खरो मृदु रूक्षो लघुर्गुरुतरोऽपि च। एवं द्वादशधा स्पर्शो वायव्यो गुण उच्यते॥
en: Both sound and touch form the two properties of the wind-element. These are the eleven properties which belong to the wind.

sn: तत्रैकगुणमाकाशं शब्द इत्येव तत्स्मृतम्। तस्य शब्दस्य वक्ष्यामि विस्तरं विविधात्मकम्॥
en: Space has only one property, namely sound. I shall now describe to you the different sorts of sound.

sn: षड्ज ऋषभगान्धारौ मध्यमो धैवतस्तथा। पञ्चमश्चापि विज्ञेयस्तथा चापि निषादवान्॥
en: They are the seven original notes called Shadaja, Rishabha, Gandhara, Maddhyaina, Dhaivata, Panchama, and Nishada.

sn: एष सप्तविधः प्रोक्तो गुण आकाशसम्भवः। ऐश्वर्येण तु सर्वत्र स्थितोऽपि पटहादिषु॥
en: These are the seven sorts of the property which belongs to space. Sound pervades like the Supreme Being the entire space though attached especially to drums drums and other instruments.

sn: मृदङ्गभेरीशङ्खानां स्तनयित्नो रथस्य च। यः कश्चिच्छ्रयते शब्दः प्राणिनोऽप्राणिनोऽपि वा। एतेषामेव सर्वेषां विषये सम्प्रकीर्तितः॥
en: Whatever sound is heard from small and large drums and conch-shells, and cloucis, and cars, and animate and inanimates creatures, are all contained in these seven sorts of sound already mentioned.

sn: एवं बहुविधाकारः शब्द आकाशसम्भवः। आकाशजं शब्दमाहुरेभिर्वायुगुणैः सह॥ अव्याहतैश्चेतयते न वेत्ति विषमस्थितैः। आप्याय्यन्ते च ते नित्यं धातवस्तैस्तु धातुभिः॥
en: Thus sound, which is the property of space, is of various sorts. The learned have described sound to be born of space. When created by the various kinds of touch, which is the property of the wind, it may be heard. It cannot, however, be heard, when the different kinds of touch are not used. Mixed with their counter parts in the body, the elements increase and grow.

sn: आपोऽग्निर्मारुतश्चैव नित्यं जाग्रति देहिषु। मूलमेते शरीरस्य व्याप्य प्राणानिह स्थिताः॥
en: Water, fire, wind, always live in the bodies of living creatures. They form the roots of the body. Pervading the five vital airs they live in the body.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: भरद्वाज उवाच पार्थिवं धातुमासाद्य शारीरोऽग्निः कथं प्रभो। अवकाशविशेषेण कथं वर्तयतेऽनिलः॥
en: How docs bodily fire or heat, entering the body, live there? How also does the wind, getting space for itself, cause the body to move and work?

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: भृगुरुवाच वायोर्गतिमहं ब्रह्मन् कथयिष्यामि तेऽनघ। प्राणिनामनिलो देहान् यथा चेश्यते बली॥
en: I shall, O twice-born one describe to you the course in which the wind moves, and how, O sinless one, that powerful element makes the bodies of living creatures move and work.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: श्रितो मूर्धानमात्मा तु शरीरं परिपालयन्। प्राणो मूर्धनि चाग्नौ च वर्तमानो विचेष्टते॥
en: Heat lives within the head (brain) and protects the body. The vital air called Prana, living within the head and the heat that is there, create all sorts of exertion.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: स जन्तुः सर्वभूतात्मा पुरुषः स सनातनः। मनो बुद्धिरहङ्कारो भूतानि विषयश्च सः॥
en: That Prana is the living creature, the universal self, the eternal Being, and the Mind, Intellect and Consciousness of all living creatures, as also all the objects of the senses.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: एवं त्विह स सर्वत्र प्राणेन परिचाल्यते। पृष्ठतस्तु समानेन स्वां स्वां गतिमुपाश्रितः॥
en: Thus Prana makes the living creature move about and exert. Then by virtue of the other vital air called Samana, every one of the senses performs its own work.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: बस्तिमूलं गुदं चैव पावकं समुपाश्रितः। वहन्मूत्रं पुरीषं चाप्यपान: परिवर्तते॥
en: The vital air called Apana, by the help of the heat that is in the urethra, abdomen and intestines, moves, carrying out urine and excreta.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: प्रयत्ने कर्मणि बले य एकस्त्रिषु वर्तते। उदान इति तं प्राहुरध्यात्मविदुषो जनाः॥
en: That single vital air which works in these three, is called Udana by those who are wellread in this science.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: संधिष्वपि च सर्वेषु संनिविष्टस्तथानिलः। शरीरेषु मनुष्याणां व्यान इत्युपदिश्यते॥
en: That vital air which works, living in all the joints, is called Vyana.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: धातुष्वग्निस्तु विततः समानेन समीरितः। रसान् धातूंश्च दोषांश्च वर्तयन्नवतिष्ठते॥
en: Heat is circulated all over the bodies of living creatures by the vital air Samana. Living creatures by the vital air Samana. Living thus in the body, that vital air works upon the various sorts of watery and other elementary substances and all bad humours.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: अपानप्राणयोर्मध्ये प्राणापानसमाहितः। समन्वितस्त्वधिष्ठानं सम्यक्पचति पावकः॥
en: The heat, living between Apana and Prana, in the navel, works, with the help of those two vital airs, in digesting all food that is taken by a living creature.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: आस्यं हि पायुपर्यन्तमन्ते स्याद् गुदसंज्ञितम्। स्रोतस्तस्मात् प्रजायन्ते सर्वस्रोतांसि देहिनाम्॥
en: There is a canal beginning from the mouth down to the anus. Its extremity is called the anus. From this main canal various minor oncs branch out in the bodies of all living creatures.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: प्राणानां संनिपाताच्च संनिपातः प्रजायते। उष्मा चाग्निरिति ज्ञेयो योऽनं पचति देहिनाम्॥
en: The various vital air passing through these canals mix with each other. The heat which lives in Prana is called Ushman. This heat causes digestion in embodied creatures.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: अग्निवेगवहः प्राणो गुदान्ते प्रतिहन्यते। स उर्ध्वमागम्य पुनः समुत्क्षिपति पावकम्॥
en: The vital air called Prana, carrying a current of heat, goes (from the head) downwards to the extremity of the anal canal and thence goes up once more. Returning to the head again, it once more sends down the heat it carries.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: पक्वाशयस्त्वधो नाभ्यामूर्ध्वमामाशय: स्थितः। नाभिमध्ये शरीरस्य सर्वे प्राणाश्च संस्थिताः॥
en: Below the navel is the quarter of digested maller. Above it is that for the food which is taken. In the navel reside all the forces of life that keep up the body.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: प्रस्थिता हृदयात् सर्वे तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधस्तथा। वहन्त्यन्नरसान् नाड्यो दश प्राणप्रचोदिताः॥
en: Urged by the ton sorts of vital airs having Prana for their first, the canals, branching out from the heart, carry the liquid juices of food, upwards, downwards, and in contrary directions.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: एप मार्गोऽथ योगानां येन गच्छन्ति तत्पदम्। जितक्लमा: समा धीरा मूर्धन्यात्मानमादधन्॥
en: The main channel leading from the mouth to the anus is the path by which Yogins, knowing no fatigue, calm in happiness and misery, and highly patient, succeed in attaining to Brahma by drawing the soul within the brain.

description: The work of fire and wind.
sn: एवं सर्वेषु विहितः प्राणापानेषु देहिनाम्। तस्मिन् समिध्यते नित्यमग्निः स्थाल्यामिवाहितः॥
en: Thus is heat placed in the vital air called Prana and Apana and others, of all embodied creatures. That heat is always burning thcre like a fire placed in vessel which can be seen.

sn: भरद्वाज उवाच यदि प्राणयते वायुर्वायुरेव विचेष्टते। श्वसित्याभाषते चैव तस्माज्जीवो निरर्थकः॥
en: Bharadwaja said If it is the air that keeps us alive, if it is the air that makes us inove and act is if it, the air that makes us breathe and speak, then it appears that life is not worth much.

sn: यष्मभाव आग्नेयो वह्निना पच्यते यदि। अग्निर्जरयते चैतत् तस्माज्जीवो निरर्थकः॥
en: If the animal heat be of the nature of fire, and if it is that fire which helps digestion by dissolving the food we take, then life is not worth much.

sn: जन्तोः प्रमीयमाणस्य जीवो नैवोपलभ्यते। वायुरेव जहात्येनमूष्मभावश्च नश्यति॥
en: When an animal dies, that which is called its life is never seen to depart. Only the vital air relinquishes it, and the internal heat is put out.

sn: यदि वायुमयो जीव: संश्लेषो यदि वायुना। वायुमण्डलवद् दृश्यो गच्छेत् सह मरुद्गणैः॥
en: If life were nothing else than air, or if life depended only on the air, then it could have been seen like the outward sea of air, and when passing out it would have been mixed with that air.

sn: संश्लेषो यदि वातेन यदि तस्मात् प्रणश्यति। महार्णवविमुक्तत्वादन्यत् सलिलभाजनम्॥ कूपे वा सलिलं दद्यात् प्रदीपं वा हुताशने। क्षिप्रं प्रविश्य नश्येत यथा नश्यत्यसौ तथा॥
en: If life depended upon air, and if it ended with the passing of that air from the body, it would then mingle with the eternal air like a portion of water passing into the great sea and thereby only changing the place of its residence. If a quantity of water be thrown into a well, or if the flame of a lamp be thrown into a burning fire, either of them, entering the original element, loses its independent existence. If life were air, it also, when the animal died, would merge in the great sea of air outside.

sn: पञ्चधारणके ह्यस्मिन् शरीरे जीवितं कुतः। तेषामन्यतराभावाच्चतुर्णां नास्ति संशयः॥
en: How we can say that there is life in this animal body which is composed of the five elements? If one of those clements disappear, the dissolution of the other four is brought about.

sn: नश्यन्त्यापो ह्यनाहाराद् वायुरुच्छ्वासनिग्रहात्। नश्यते कोष्ठभेदात् खमग्निर्नश्यत्यभोजनात्॥
en: The element of water dries up if food is not taken. The element of air disappears if the breath is controlled. The element of space disappears if the excretions cease. So also the element of fire disappears if food does not go in.

sn: व्याघ्रिवणपरिक्लेशैर्मेदिनी चैव शीर्यते। पीडितेऽन्यतरे ह्येषां सघातो याति पञ्चधा॥
en: The element of earth is shattered to pieces by disease, wounds and other sufferings. If only one of the five is spoiled, the union is dissolved and the five go away into five different directions.

sn: तस्मिन् पञ्चत्वमापन्ने जीवः किमनुधावति। किं वेदयति वा जीवः किं शृणोति ब्रवीति च॥
en: When the five ingredients of the body which is a compound of the five elements, are separated, where does life go? What does it then know. What does it then hear? What does it then say?

sn: एषा गौः परलोकस्थं तारयिष्यति मामिति। यो दत्त्वा म्रियते जन्तुः सा गौः कं तारयिष्यति॥
en: The cow, it is said, will save me in the next world. The animal, however, which is given away, itself dies. Whom then will this cow save?

sn: गौश्च प्रतिग्रहीता च दाता चैव समं यदा। इहैव विलयं यान्ति कुतस्तेषां समागमः॥
en: The taker of the cow and the giver are both equally subject to death. Both of them meet with destruction in this world. How then will they meet again?

sn: विहगैरुपभुक्तस्य शैलाग्रात् पतितस्य च। अग्निना चोपयुक्तस्य कुतः संजीवनं पुनः॥
en: How will the man that has been eaten up by birds, or that has been shattered to pieces by a fall from a mountain summit, or that has been consumed by fire, regain life?

sn: छिन्नस्य यदि वृक्षस्य न मूलं प्रतिरोहति। बीजान्यस्य प्रवर्तन्ते मृतः क्व पुनरेष्यति॥
en: The root of a tree that has been cut down docs not revive. Only the seeds put forth sprouts. Where is the person who having died regains life?

sn: बीजमात्रं पुरा सृष्टं यदेतत् परिवर्तते। मृतामृताः प्रणश्यन्ति बीजाद् बीजं प्रवर्तते॥
en: Only seeds were originally created. All this universe is the creation of seeds in succession. They that die, die for ever. Seeds come from seeds.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: भृगुरुवाच न प्रणाशोऽस्ति जीवस्य दत्तस्य च कृतस्य च। याति देहान्तरं प्राणी शरीरं तु विशीर्यते॥
en: Bhrigu said The living creature, or what is given, or our other acts, are never destroyed. The death of a creature is only a change of form. The body alone is dissolved.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: न शरीराश्रितो जीवस्तस्मिन् नष्टे प्रणश्यति। समिधामिव दग्धानां यथाग्निर्दृश्यते तथा॥
en: The living creature, though it depends upon the body, is not destroyed when the body is destroyed. It is not seen after the destroyed. It is not seen after the destruction of the physical body just as fire is not visible after the consumption of the fuel with which it was lighted.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: भरद्वाज उवाच अग्नेर्यथा तथा तस्य यदि नाशो न विद्यते। इन्धनस्योपयोगान्ते स चाग्निर्नोपलभ्यते॥
en: Bharadwaja said If there is no destruction of the living creature like that of fire, I say, fire itself is not visible after consumption of the fuel (that ignited it).

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: नश्यतीत्येव जानामि शान्तमग्निमनिन्धनम्। गतिर्यस्य प्रमाणं वा संस्थानं वा न विद्यते॥
en: When the supply of a fuel is stopped, the fire is put out, and as far as I know, is destroyed. What has no longer any action should be considered as destroyed, for it proves its non-existence and which no longer occupics any space.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: भृगुरुवाच समिधामुपयोगान्ते यथाग्निर्नोपलभ्यते। आकाशानुगतत्वाद्धि दुर्ग्राह्यो हि निराश्रयः॥
en: Bhrigu said, It is true that after the consumption of fuel fire is no longer visible. It mixes with space because there is no longer any visible object wherein it can abide, and hence it cannot be perceived by us.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: तथा शरीरसंत्यागे जीवो ह्याकाशवत् स्थितः। न गृह्यते तु सूक्ष्मत्वाद् यथा ज्योतिर्न संशयः॥
en: Likewise, upon renouncing the body, the creature lives in space, and cannot be seen for its extreme subtility as is the case with fire.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: प्राणान् धारयते ह्यग्निः स जीव उपधार्यताम्। वायुसंधारणो ह्यग्निर्नश्यत्युच्छ्वासनिग्रहात्॥
en: It is fire or heat that kceps us the vital airs called Prana and the others. Know this heat is called life or the living agent. The heat which keeps up vital airs, is extinguished for the suppression of breath.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: तस्मिन् नष्टे शरीराग्नौ ततो देहमचेतनम्। पतितं याति भूमित्वमयनं तस्य हि क्षितिः॥
en: With the extinction of heat, the body itself loses aniination. Falling down, it it is metamorphosed into earth, its ultimate destination.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: जङ्गमानां हि सर्वेषां स्थावराणां तथैव च। आकाशं पवनोऽन्वेति ज्योतिस्तमनुगच्छति। तेषां त्रयाणामेकत्वाद् द्वयं भूमौ प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: The breath that exists in all mobile and immobile objects mingles with space, and the heat which is in them follows that breath. These three (viz., space, air, and fair), mingle together. The other two (viz., water and earth), exist together in the shape of earth.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: यत्र खं तत्र पवनस्तत्राग्निर्यत्र मारुतः। अमूर्तयस्ते विज्ञेया मूर्तिमन्तः शरीरिणाम्॥
en: There is wind where space is, and there is fire where is. They have in reality no forms, and become endued with form only in embodied creatures.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: भरद्वाज उवाच यद्याग्निमारुतौ भूमिः खमापश्च शरीरिषु। जीव: किंलक्षणस्तत्रेत्येतदाचक्ष्व मेऽनघ॥
en: Bharadwaja said If in the bodies of all living creatures there are heat, wind, earth, space, and water, what then are the sins of the living agent? Tell me these, O sinless one.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: पञ्चात्मके पञ्चरतौ पञ्चविज्ञानचेतने। शरीरे प्राणिनां जीवं वेत्तुमिच्छामि यादृशम्॥
en: I wish to know the nature of the life that exists in the bodies of living beings,composed of the five principal elements, engaged in the five principal elements, engaged in the five acts, endued with the five senses and animation.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: मांसशोणितसंघाते मेदःस्नाय्वस्थिसंचये। भिद्यमाने शरीरे त जीवो नैवोपलभ्यते॥
en: After the dissolution of the body which is a compound of flesh and blood, a mass of fat, sinews and bones, that which is the living agent is not seen.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: यद्यजीवं शरीरं तु पञ्चभूतसमन्वितम्। शरीरे मानसे दुःखे कस्तां वेदयते रुजम्॥
en: If this body, composed of the give elements, has no life, who or what then is that which feels misery on account of either physical or metal pain?

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: शृणोति कथितं जीवः कर्णाभ्यां न शृणोति तत्। महर्षे मनसि व्यग्रे तस्माज्जीवो निरर्थकः॥
en: The living agent hears what is said, through the ears. It is, again, the fact, O great Rishi, that the same agent hears not when the mind is elsewhere engaged. It appears, therefore, that what is called the living agent serves no purpose.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: सर्वं पश्यति यद् दृश्यं मनोयुक्तेन चक्षुषा। मनसि व्याकुले चक्षुः पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति॥
en: What the living agent sces with eyes acting in unison with the mind, the eye sees not, even when lying before it, if the mind elsewhere engaged.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: न पश्यति न चाघ्राति न शृणोति न भाषते। न च स्पर्शरसौ वेत्ति निद्रावशगतः पुनः॥
en: Then again, when it is asleep, that agent neither sees nor smells, nor hears, nor speaks, nor feels the perceptions of touch and taste.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: हष्यति क्रुद्ध्यते कोऽत्र शोचत्युद्विजते चकः। इच्छति ध्यायति द्वेष्टि वाचमीरयते च कः॥
en: Who or what then is that which feels joy, becomes angry, or sorry and suffers tribulation? What is that which wishes, thinks, feels hatred and utters words.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: भृगुरुवाच च्छरीरमेको बहतेऽन्तरात्मा। स वेत्ति गन्धांश्च रसाश्रुतीश्च स्पर्श च रूपं च गुणाश्च येऽन्ये॥
en: Bhrigu said The mind, like the body also, is made of the five elements. Therefore it is useless regarding the acts mentioned by you. Only the soul sustains the body. It is he that perceives smell, taste, sound, touch, forin and other properties.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: पञ्चात्मके पञ्चगुणप्रदर्शी स सर्वगात्रानुगतोऽन्तरात्मा। स वेत्ति दुःखानि सुखानि चात्र तद्विप्रयोगात् तु न वेत्ति देहः॥
en: Permeating all the limbs, that Soul witness the acts of the mind possessing five attributes and living within the body composed of the five elements. It is he who feels pleasure and pain, and when separated from him the body does not feel them.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: यदा न रूपं न स्पर्शो नोष्मभावश्च पञ्चके। तदा शान्ते शरीराग्नौ देहत्यागे न नश्यति॥
en: When one has no perception of form or of touch, when there is no heat in the fire of the body,—when the animal heat is gone,-the body, being renounced by the Soul, meets with destruction.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: आपोमयमिदं सर्वमापो मूर्तिः शरीरिणाम्। तत्रात्मा मानसो ब्रह्मा सर्वभूतेषु लोककृत्॥
en: The whole universe is made of water. Water is the form of all embodied creatures. In that water lives the Soul which is seen in the mind. That Soul is the Creator Brahman who exists in all things.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: आत्मा क्षेत्रज्ञ इत्युक्तः संयुक्तः प्राकृतैर्गुणैः। तैरेव तु विनिर्मुक्तः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः॥
en: When the Soul is endued with ordinary attributes, it is called Kshetrajna. When freed from those attributes, attributes, it is designated Paramatman or Supreme Self.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: आत्मानं तं विजानीहि सर्वलोकहितात्मकम्। तस्मिन् यः संश्रितो देहे ह्यब्विन्दुरिव पुष्करें।२४॥
en: Know that Soul. He is full of universal benevolence. He lives in the body like a drop of water in a lotus.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: क्षेत्रज्ञं तं विजानीहि नित्यं लोकहितात्मकम्। तमो रजश्च सत्त्वं च विद्धि जीवगुणानिमान्॥
en: Know well what is called Kshetrajna and which had universal benevolence. Goodness, darkness, and ignorance are the three attributes of the living agent.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: सचेतनं जीवगुणं वदन्ति स चेष्टते चेश्यते च सर्वम्। अतः परं क्षेत्रविदो वदन्ति। प्रावर्तयद् यो भुवनानि सप्त॥
en: The learned hold that the Soul had Consciousness and has the attributes of life. The Soul works and makes everything to work. Persons cognisant of the Soul say that the Soul is different from life. It is the Supreme Soul that has created the seven words and makes them works.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: न जीवनाशोऽस्ति हि देहभेदे मिथ्यैतदाहुर्मत इत्यबुद्धाः। जीवस्तु देहान्तरितः प्रयाति दशार्धतैवास्य शरीरभेदः॥
en: There is no destruction of the living agent even when the body is dissolved. Men shorn of intelligence say that it dies. That is in fact false. All that the living agent does is that it goes from one body to another. What is called death is merely the dissolution of the body.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: एवं सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढचरति संवृतः। दृश्यते त्वग्रयया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया तत्त्वदर्शिभिः॥
en: It is thus that the Soul, covered with various forms, goes form to form, unseen and unnoticed by others. Persons endued with true Knowledge witness the Soul by their keen and subtile intelligence.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: तं पूर्वापररात्रेषु युञ्जानः सततं बुधः। लब्धाहारो विशुद्धात्मा पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि॥
en: Living on restricted diet, and with heart purged of all sins, devoting himself to meditation, a wise man succeeds every night, before sleep and after sleep, in sceing Soul by the help of his Soul.

description: Death is only a change of form
sn: चित्तस्य हि प्रसादेन हित्वा कर्म शुभाशुभम्। प्रसन्नात्माऽऽत्मनि स्थित्वा सुखमानन्त्यमश्नुते॥ मानसोऽग्निः शरीरेषु जीव इत्यभिधीयते। सृष्टिः प्रजापतेरेषा भूताध्यात्मविनिश्चये॥
en: The king, effulgent, like fire living within the mind is called the living agent. It is from that Lord of everything that this creation has originated. This is the conclusion of the enquiry into the origin of creatures and the soul.

description: The creation of the Prajapatis—of Duty, truth, Penance etc., No distinction of castes.
