sn: अकृतप्रज्ञको बालो मोहं गच्छति जापकः। स मोहान्निरयं याति तत्र गत्वानुशोचति॥
en: The Reciter who is not gifted with wisdom and who is foolish, becomes stupefied or deluded; and for such delusion has to go to hell where he is obliged to grieve.

sn: दृढग्राही करोमीति जाप्यं जति जापकः। न सम्पूर्णो न संयुक्तो निरयं सोऽनुगच्छति॥
en: If a person even of fixed heart, determining in to complete the discipline, makes, recitation, but fails to come to the end, for his having freed himself from attachments by a violent stretch without genuine conviction of their worthlessness of harmful character, he also has to go to hell.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अनिवृत्तं परं यत्तदव्यक्तं ब्रह्मणि स्थितम्। तद्भूतो जापकः कस्मात् स शरीरमिहाविशेत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said When the Reciter attains to the essence of that which exists in its own nature, which is Supreme, which is beyond description and comprehension, and which dwells in the syllable. OM forming the subject of both recitation and meditation, why is it that they have a gain to take birth in embodied forms?

sn: भीष्म उवाच दुष्प्रज्ञानेन निरया बहवः समुदाहृताः। प्रशस्तं जापकत्वं च दोषाश्चैते तदात्मकाः॥
en: Reciters, for want of true knowledge and wisdom, go to various descriptions of hell. The discipline followed by Reciters is surely very superior. These, however, that I have spoken o! are their weak points.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कीदृशं निरयं याति जापको वर्णयस्व मे। कौतूहलं हि राजन् मे तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me what sort of hell is obtained by a Reciter? I am curious, O king, to know this. You should describe this subject to me.'

sn: भीष्म उवाच धर्मस्यांशप्रसूतोऽसि धर्मिष्ठोऽसि स्वभावतः। धर्ममूलाश्रयं वाक्यं शृणुष्वावहितोऽनध॥
en: Bhishma said “You have originated from a portion of the good of righteousness. You are by nature observant of righteousness. Listen, O sinless one, with undivided attention, to these words having righteousness for their root.

sn: अमूनि यानि स्थानानि देवानां परमात्मनाम्। नानासंस्थानवर्णानि नानारूपफलानि च।॥ दिव्यानि कामचारीणि विमानानि सभास्तथा। आक्रीडा विविधा राजन् पद्मिन्यश्चैव काञ्चनाः॥ चतुर्णा लोकपालानां शुक्रस्याथ बृहस्पतेः। मरुतां विश्वदेवानां साध्यानामश्विनोरपि॥ रुद्रादित्यवसूनां च तथान्येषां दिवौकसाम्। एते वै निरयास्तात स्थानस्य परमात्मनः॥
en: Those regions that are owned by the great gods, that are of various aspects and colours, of various descriptions and productive of various fruits, and that are of great excellence, those cars again that move at the desire of the riders, those beautiful palaces and hells, those various pleasure-gardens decorated with golden lotuses, those regions that belong to the four Regents and Shukra and Brihaspati and the Maruts and Vishvedevas and Saddhyas and the Ashvins, and the Rudras and the Adityas and the Vasus, and other dwellers of heaven, are, O sire, spoken of as hells, when compared with the region of the Supreme Self.

sn: अभयं चानिमित्तं च न तत् क्लेशसमावृतम्। द्वाभ्यां मुक्तं त्रिभिर्मुक्तमष्टाभिस्त्रिभिरेव च॥ चतुर्लक्षणवर्जं तु चतुष्कारणवर्जितम्। अप्रहर्षमनानन्दमशोकं विगतक्लमम्॥
en: The region last spoken of it shorn of fear, increate, without pain of any sort, without any agreeable or disagreeable element, beyond the reach of the three qualities, freed from the eight things (viz., the five primal elements, the senses, the mind, and the intellect), without the three (distinctions between the knower, the known, and act knowing); freed also from the four attributes (seeing, hearing, thinking, and knowing), without the fourfold causes (of knowledge) without joy and delight ard sorrow and disease.

sn: कालः सम्पद्यते तत्र कालस्तत्र न वै प्रभुः। स कालस्य प्रभू राजन् स्वर्गस्यापि तथेश्वरः॥
en: Time makes it appearance there for usc. Time is not the ruler there. That supreme region is the ruler of Time as also of Heaven.

sn: आत्मकेवलतां प्राप्तस्तत्र गत्वा न शोचति। ईदृशं परमं स्थानं निरयास्ते च तादृशाः॥
en: That Reciter who becomes identified with his Soul (by withdrawing everything into it) goes there. He has, after this, never to experience any sorrow. This region is called Supreme. The other regions are hell.

sn: एते ते निरयाः प्रोक्ताः सर्व एव यथातथम्। तस्य स्थानवरस्येह सर्वे निरयसंज्ञिता:॥
en: I have not told you of all those regions that are called hell. Indeed, as compared with that foremost of regions all the others are called hell.'

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कालमृत्युयमानां ते इक्ष्वाकोर्ब्राह्मणस्य च। विवादो व्याहतः पूर्वं तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Yudhishthira said You had mentioned the dispute between Time, Mrityu, Yama, Ikshvaku, and a Brahmana. You should describe the story in full.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। इक्ष्वाकोः सूर्यपुत्रस्य तद् वृत्तं ब्राह्मणस्य च॥ कालस्य मृत्योश्च तथा यद् वृत्तं तन्निबोध मे। यथा स तेषां संवादो यस्मिन् स्थानेऽपि चाभवत्॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding this subject that I am describing, is cited the old story of what too place between Surya's son Ikshvaku and a certain Brahmana, and Tiine and Mrityu. Listen to me as to what happened, and what was the conversation that took place between them and the place where it happened.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मणो जापकः कश्चिद् धर्मवृत्तो महायशाः। षडङ्गविन्महाप्राज्ञः पैप्पलादिः स कौशिकः॥
en: There was a certain the highly famous and pious Brahınana. He was a Reciter. Greatly wise, he was conversant with the six branches (of the Vedas). He was of the Kushika race and son of Pippalada.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: तस्यापरोक्षं विज्ञानं षडङ्गेषु बभूव ह। वेदेषु चैव निष्णातो हिमवत्पादसंश्रयः॥
en: He acquired (by his austerities) spiritual insight into the various branches of the Vedas. Residing at the foot of Himavat, he was devoted to the Vedas,

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: सोद्यं ब्राह्म तपस्तेपे संहितां संयतो जपन्। तस्य वर्षसहस्रं तु नियमेन तथा गतम्॥
en: He practised, silently reciting the Gayatri, severe austerities for attaining to Brahma. A thousand years passed away while he was engaged in the observance of vows and fasts.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: स देव्या दर्शितः साक्षात् प्रीतास्मीति तदा किल। जष्यमावर्तयंस्तूष्णीं न स तां किञ्चिदब्रवीत्॥
en: The goddess (of Gayatri or Savitri) appeared before him and said,-I am pleased with you.-Continuing to recite the sacred Mantra, the Brahmana remained silent and spoke not a word to the goddess.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: तस्यानुकम्पया देवी प्रीता समभवत् तदा। वेदमाता ततस्तस्य तज्जप्यं समपूजयत्॥
en: The goddess felt mercy for him and became highly pleased. Then the mother of the Vedas spoke highly of that recitation in which the Brahmana had been engaged.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: समाप्तजप्यस्तूत्थाय शिरसा पादयोस्तदा। पपात देव्या धर्मात्मा वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ दिष्ट्या देवि प्रसन्ना त्वं दर्शनं चागता मम। यदि चापि प्रसन्नासि जप्ये मे रमतां मनः॥
en: After finishing his recitation the Brahmana stood up and, lowering his head, laid himself down before the goddess's feet. The pious Reciter, addressing the goddess, said,-By good luck, O goddess, you have been pleased with me and shown yourself to me. If, indeed, you are pleased with me, the boon I ask is that my heart may find pleasure in the act of recitation.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: सावित्र्युवाच किं प्रार्थयसि विप्रर्षे किं चेष्टं करवाणि ते। प्रब्रूहि जपतां श्रेष्ठ सर्वं तत् ते भविष्यति॥
en: What do you ask, O twice-born Rishi? What wish of yours shall I make good? Tell me, O foremost of Reciters, everything will be as you wish.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: इत्युक्तः स तदा देव्या विप्रः प्रोवाच धर्मवित्। जप्यं प्रति ममेच्छेयं वर्धत्विति पुनः पुनः॥
en: Thus addressed by the goddess, the Brahmana, conversant with duties, replied, saying,-Let me wish about continuing my recitation s go on increasing every day.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: मनसश्च समाधिर्मे वर्धेताहरहः शुभे। तत् तथेति ततो देवी मधुरं प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Let also, O auspicious goddess, my Samadhi be more complete!-The goddess sweetly said,-Let it be as you wish.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: इदं चैवापरं प्राह देवी तत्प्रियकाम्यया। निरयं नैव याता त्वं यत्र याता द्विजर्षभाः॥
en: Desiring to do good to the Brahmana, the goddess once again said to him-You shall not have to go to hell, i.e., there where great Brahmanas go.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: यास्यसि ब्रह्मणः स्थानमनिमित्तमनिन्दितम्। साधये भविता चैतद् यत्त्वयाहमिहार्थिता॥
en: You shall go to the region of Brahma which is incrcate and free from every fault. I go hence, but that which you have asked me shall take place.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: नियतो जप चैकाग्रो धर्मस्त्वां समुपैष्यति। कालो मृत्युर्यमश्चैव समायास्यन्ति तेऽन्तिकम्॥
en: Go on reciting with controlled soul and rapt attention. The god Dharma will in person come lo you. Time, Mrityu, and Yama also will come to you. There will be a dispute of morality.'

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: भविता च विवादोऽत्र तव तेषां च धर्मतः। भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्त्वा भगवती जगाम भवन स्वकम्॥ ब्राह्मणोऽपि जपन्नास्ते दिव्यं वर्षशतं तथा। सदा दान्तो जितक्रोधः सत्यसंधोऽनसूयकः॥
en: The goddess, having said these words returned to her own house. The Brahimana continued in recitation for a thousand divine years. Restraining anger, and always controlling self, he passed his time firmly devoting himself to truth and shorn of malice.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: समाप्ते नियमे तस्मिन्नथ विप्रस्य धीमतः। साक्षात् प्रीतस्तदा धर्मो दर्शयामास तं द्विजम्॥
en: Upon the completion of the observance by the intelligent Brahmana, Dharma, pleased with him, appeared before that twice-born one.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: धर्म उवाच द्विजाते पश्य मां धर्ममहं त्वां द्रष्टुमागतः। जप्यस्यास्य फलं यत्तत् सम्प्राप्तं तच्च मे शृणु॥
en: Dharma said O twice-born one, see me who am Dharma. I have come here for seeing you. You have acquired the meed of this recitation in which you had been engaged. Listen to me as to what that rewards is.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: जिता लोकास्त्वया सर्वे ये दिव्या ये च मानुषाः। देवानां निलयान् साधो सर्वानुत्क्रम्य यास्यसि॥
en: You have acquired all the regions of felicity which belong to either gods or men. O good man, you shall ascend above all the abodes of the gods.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: प्राणत्यागं कुरु मुने गच्छ लोकान् यथेप्सितान्। त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मनः शरीरं च ततो लोकानवाप्स्यसि॥
en: O ascetic, cast off your vital breaths then, and to go whatever regions you please. By casting off your body you will acquire many regions of felicity.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच किं नु लोकैर्हि मे धर्म गच्छ त्वं च यथासुखम्। बहुदुःखसुखं देहं नोत्सृजेयमहं विभो॥
en: The Brahmana said What have I to do which those regions of felicity of which you speak. O Dharma, go wherever you like. I will not, O powerful lord, cast off this body which is subject to much happiness and misery.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: धर्म उवाच अवश्यं भोः शरीरं ते त्यक्तव्यं मुनिपुङ्गव। स्वर्गमारोह भो विप्र किं वा वै रोचतेऽनघ॥
en: Your body, O foremost of ascetics, should certainly be cast off. Do you ascend to heaven, O Brahmana. Or, tell us what else would please you, O sinless one.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच न रोचये स्वर्गवासं विना देहमहं विभो। गच्छ धर्म न मे श्रद्धा स्वर्गं गन्तुं विनाऽऽत्मना॥
en: The Brahmana said I do not, O powerful lord, wish to live in heaven itself without this body of mine. Leave, me, O Dharma. I have no desire to go. to heaven itself without my own body.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: धर्म उवाच अलं देहे मनः कृत्वा त्यक्त्वा देहं सुखी भव। गच्छ लोकानरजसो यत्र गत्वा न शोचसि॥
en: Dharma said Without setting your heart on your body, cast it off and be happy. Go into regions that are free from the quality of Ignorance. Indeed, going there, you shall never have to experience any misery.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच रमे जपन् महाभाग किं लोकैः सनातनैः। सशरीरेण गन्तव्यं मया स्वर्गं न वा विभो॥ नु
en: The Brahmana said O highly-blessed one, I take great pleasure in recitation. What necessity have I for those eternal regions of which you speak? Indeed, O powerful lord, I do not wish to go to heaven even with this body of mine.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: धर्म उवाच यदि त्वं नेच्छसे त्यक्तुं शरीरं पश्य वै द्विजा एष कालस्तथा मृत्युर्यमश्च त्वामुपागताः॥
en: Dharma said If you do not wish to cast off your body, behold O twice-born one, there is Time, and there is Mrityu, and there is Yama, who are all approaching you.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: भीष्म उवाच अथ वैवस्वत: कालो मृत्युश्च त्रितयं विभो। ब्राह्मणं तं महाभागमुपगम्येदमब्रुवन्॥
en: Bhishma said After Dharma has said this, the three Vivasvat's son (Yama), Time and Mrityu, approached that Brahmana, 0 blessed king, and addressed him thus.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: यम उवाच तपसोऽस्य सुतप्तस्य तथा सुचरितस्य च। फलप्राप्तिस्तव श्रेष्ठा यमोऽहं त्वामुपब्रुवे।॥
en: Yama said I am Yama. I say to you that a high reward awaits you for these well-performed penances of yours and for this your pious conduct.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: काल उवाच यथावदस्य जप्यस्य फलं प्राप्तमनुत्तमम्। कालस्ते स्वर्गमारोढुं कालोऽहं त्वामुपागतः॥
en: Time said You have acquired a high reward which is, indeed, commensurate with the recitation that you have finished. The time is come for you to ascent to heaven. I am Time and I have come to you.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: मृत्युरुवाच मृत्यु मां विद्धि धर्मज्ञ रूपिणं स्वयमागतम्। कालेन चोदितो विप्र त्वामितो नेतुमद्य वै॥
en: Mrityu said — You who are conversant with righteousness, know me for Mrityu herself in her own proper form! I have come to you in person, urged by Time, for taking you hence, O Brahmana.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच स्वागतं सूर्यपुत्राय कालाय च महात्मने। मृत्यवे चाथ धर्माय किं कार्यं करवाणि वः॥
en: 'Welcome to Surya's son, to great time, to Mrityu, and to Dharma. What shall I do for you all.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: भीष्म उवाच अयं पाद्यं च दत्त्वा स तेभ्यस्तत्र समागमे। अब्रवीत् परमप्रीतः स्वशक्त्या किं करोमि वः॥
en: Bhishma said In that meeting, the Brahmana gave them water to wash their feet, and the usual articles of the Arghya. Highly pleased, he then addressed them, saying,—What shall I do for you all to the best of my power.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: तस्मिन्नेवाथ काले तु तीर्थयात्रामुपागतः। इक्ष्वाकुरगमत् तत्र समेता यत्र ते विभो॥
en: Just at that time, O monarch, (king) Ikshvaku, who had started on a pilgrimage to holy waters and shrines, came there where those gods had been assembled together. are

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: सर्वानेव तु राजर्षिः सम्पूज्याथ प्रणम्य च। कुशलप्रशनमकरोत् सर्वेषां राजसत्तमः॥
en: The royal sage Ikshvaku bowed his head and adored them all. That best of king then enquired after the welfare of all of them.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: तस्मै सोऽथासनं दत्त्वा पाद्यमर्थ्य तथैव च। अब्रवीद् ब्राह्मणो वाक्यं कृत्वा कुशलसंविदम्॥
en: The Brahmana offered the king a seat, as also water to wash his feet, and the usual Arghya. Having next made the usual enquiries of courtesy, he said,-

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: स्वागतं ते महाराज ब्रूहि यद् यदिहेच्छसि। स्वशक्त्या किं करोमीह तद् भवान् प्रब्रवीतु माम्।।३८।
en: You welcome, 0 great king. communicate to me all your wishes. Let your noble self tell me what I shall have to do for you by putting forth my might,

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच राजाहं ब्राह्मणश्च त्वं यदा षट्कर्मसंस्थितः। ददानि वसु किंचित्ते प्रथितं तद् वदस्व मे॥
en: The king said I am a king. You are a Brahmana observing the six well-known duties. I will give you some wealth. That is well-known. Tell me how much I shall give you.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच द्विविधा ब्राह्मणा राजन् धर्मश्च द्विविधः स्मृतः। प्रवृत्ताश्च निवृत्ताश्च निवृत्तोऽहं प्रतिग्रहात्॥
en: The Brahmana said There are two kinds of Brahmanas, O king, Morality or righteousness also is of two sorts : devotion to work, and abstention from work. As regards myself, I do not accept gifts.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: तेभ्यः प्रयच्छ दानानि ये प्रवृत्ता नराधिप। अहं न प्रतिगृह्णामि किमिष्टं किं ददामि ते। ब्रूहि त्वं नृपतिश्रेष्ठ तपसा साधयामि किम्॥
en: Give presents to them, O king, who. are given to the duty of work and acceptance. I shall not, therefore, accept any gift. On the other hand, I ask you, what is for your wellbeing. What, indeed, shall I give you? Tell me, O foremost of kings, and I shall do it with the help of my penances.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच क्षत्रियोऽहं न जानामि देहीति वचनं क्वचित्। प्रयच्छ युद्धमित्येवंवादिनः स्मो द्विजोत्तम॥
en: The king Said I am a Kshatriya. I do not know how to say the word-Give. The only thing, O best of twice-born ones, that we can say is-Give (us)

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच तुष्यसि त्वं स्वधर्मेण तथा तुष्टा वयं नृप। अन्योन्यस्यान्तरं नास्ति यदिष्टं तत् समाचर॥
en: The Brahmana said You are content with the observance of the duties of your order. Likewise, I am content with the duties of mine, O king. there is, therefore, little difference between us. Do what you please.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच स्वशक्त्याहं ददानीति त्वया पूर्वमुदाहृतम्। याचे त्वां दीयतां मह्यं जप्यस्यास्य फलं द्विज॥
en: You gave vent to these words first, viz., I shall give you according to my might.-I, therefore, pray, O twice-born one,-Give me the fruits of this your recitation.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच युद्धं मम सदा वाणी याचतीति विकत्थसे। न च युद्धं मया साधु किमर्थं याचसे पुनः॥
en: The Brahmana said You boasted that your words always pray for battle. Why then do you not pray for a battle with me.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच वाग्वज्रा ब्राह्मणाः प्रोक्ताः क्षत्रिया बाहुजीविनः। वाग्युद्धं तदिदं तीवं मम विप्र त्वया सह॥
en: The king said It is said that Brahinanas are armed with the thunder of speech, and that Kshatriyas have might of arms. hence, O learned Brahmana, this wordy warfare has taken place between you and me.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच सैवाद्यापि प्रतिज्ञा मे स्वशक्त्या किं प्रदीयताम्। ब्रूहि दास्यामि राजेन्द्र विभवे सति मा चिरम्॥
en: The Brahmana said As regards myself, this is my resolution today. What shall I give you according to my might? Tell me, O king of kings, and I shall give you. Do not delay.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच यत्तद् वर्षशतं पूर्ण जप्यं वै जपता त्वया। फलं प्राप्तं तत् प्रयच्छ मम दित्सुर्भवान् यदि॥
en: If, indeed, you wish to give me anything, then give me the fruits you have acquired by practising recitation for these thousand years.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच परमं गृह्यतां तस्य फलं यज्जपितं मया। अर्धं त्वमविचारेण फलं तस्य ह्यवाप्नुहि॥
en: The Brahmana said Take the greatest fruit of the recitations I have practised. Indeed, take half, without any hesitation the entire fruits of that recitation.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: अथवा सर्वमेवेह मामकं जापकं फलम्। राजन् प्राप्नुहि कामं त्वं यदि सर्वमिहेच्छसि॥
en: Or, O king, if you desire, take without any hesitation the entire fruits of my recitations.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच कृतं सर्वेण भद्रं ते जप्यं यद् याचितं मया। स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि किञ्च तस्य फलं वद॥
en: The king said Blessed be you, I have no necessity for the fruits of your recitations which I have begged. Blessings on your head. I am about to leave you. Tell me, however, what those fruits are.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच फलप्राप्तिं न जानामि दत्तं यज्जपितं मया। अयं धर्मश्च कालश्च यमो मृत्युश्च साक्षिणः॥
en: The Brahmana said I have no knowledge of the fruits I have acquired. I have, however, given you those fruits that I have acquired by recitation. These, viz., Dharma and time and Yama, and Mrityu, are witnesses.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच अज्ञातमस्य धर्मस्य फलं किं मे करिष्यति। फलं ब्रवीषि धर्मस्य न चेज्जप्यकृतस्य माम्। प्राप्नोतु तत् फलं विप्रो नाहमिच्छे ससंशयम्॥
en: The king said I will not accept any other word (from you). I have given you the fruits of my recitations. Let, O royal sage, both your words and mine prove true.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच नाददेऽपरवक्तव्यं दत्तं चास्य फलं मया। वाक्यं प्रमाणं राजर्षे ममाद्य तव चैव हि॥
en: never I will not accept any words, as I have given the frut of recitations. O king of sages, these words only are considered as authoritative.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: नाभिसंधिर्मया जप्ये कृतपूर्वः कदाचन। जष्यस्य राजशार्दूल कथं वेत्स्याम्यहं फलम्॥
en: As regards my recitations, I entertained any particular desire to do. How then, O foremost of kings, should I have any knowledge of what are the fruits of those recitations?

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ददस्वेति त्वया चोक्तं ददानीति मया तथा। न वाचं दूषयिष्यामि सत्यं रक्ष स्थिरो भव॥
en: You said-Give! I said, I give!-I shall not falsify these words. Keep the truth. Be calm.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: अथैवं वदतो मेऽद्य वचनं न करिष्यसि। महानधर्मो भविता तव राजन् मृषा कृतः॥
en: If you refuge to keep my word, O king, great sin of untruth will visit you.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: न युक्तं तु मृषा वाणी त्वया वक्तुमरिंदम्। तथा मयाप्यभिहितं मिथ्या कर्तुं न शक्यते॥
en: O chastiser of foes, you should not utter what is untrue. Likewise, I dare not falsify what I have said.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: संश्रुतं च मया पूर्वं ददानीत्यविचारितम्। तद् गृह्णीप्वाविचारेण यदि सत्ये स्थितो भवान्॥
en: I have, before this, unhesitatingly said, I give! If, therefore, you are firm in truth, accept my gift.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: इहागम्य हि मां राजन् जाप्यं फलमयाचथाः। तन्मे निसृष्टं गृह्णीष्व भव सत्ये स्थिरोऽपि च॥
en: Coming here, O king, you begged of me the fruits of my recitations. Therefore, take what I have given away, if, indeed, you are truthful.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न च पूर्वान् स तारयेत्। कुत एव जनिष्यांस्तु मृषावादपरायणः॥
en: He who is given to falsehood has neither this world nor the next. Such a person cannot rescue his departed manes. How again shall he succeed in doing good to progeny?

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: न यज्ञाध्ययने दानं नियमास्तारयन्ति हि। यथा सत्यं परे लोके तथेह पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: The rewards of sacrifices and gifts, as also of fasts and religious observances, are not so powerful in rescuing as truth, O foremost of men, in both this and the next world.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: तपांसि यानि चीर्णानि चरिष्यन्ति च यत् तपः। शतैः शतसहस्रैश्च तैः सत्यान्न विशिष्यते॥
en: All the penances that have been practised by you and all those that you will practised in the future of hundreds and thousands of years are more cfficacious than truth.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: सत्यमेकाक्षरं ब्रह्म सत्यमेकाक्षरं तपः। सत्यमेकाक्षरो यज्ञः सत्यमेकाक्षरं श्रुतम्॥
en: Truth is the one undecaying Brahma. Truth is the one undecaying Penance. Truth is the one undecaying Sacrifice. Truth is the one undecaying Veda.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: सत्यं वेदेषु जागर्ति फलं सत्ये परं स्मृतम्। सत्याद् धर्मो दमश्चैव सर्वं सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Truth is awake in the Vedas. The fruits attached to truth have been described as the highest. From truth originate Righteousness and Self-control. Everything depends on truth.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: सत्यं वेदास्तथाङ्गानि सत्यं विद्यास्तथा विधिः। व्रतचर्या तथा सत्यमोङ्कारः सत्यमेव च॥
en: Truth is the Vedas and their branches. Truth is knowledge. Truth is the Ordinance. Truth is the observance of vows and fasts. Truth is the Prime Syllable OM.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: प्राणिनां जननं सत्यं सत्यं संततिरेव च। सत्येन वायुरभ्येति सत्येन तपते रविः॥
en: Truth is the origin of creatures. Truth is their progeny. It is by truth that the Wind moves. It is by truth that the Sun gives heat.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: सत्येन चाग्निर्दहति स्वर्गः सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितः। सत्यं यज्ञस्तपो वेदाः स्तोभा मन्त्राः सरस्वती॥
en: It is by truth that Fire burns. It is on truth that Heaven rests. Truth is Sacrifice. Penance, Vedas, the verses of Samans, Mantras, and Sarasvati.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: तुलामारोपिता धर्मः सत्यं चैवेति नः श्रुतम्। समकक्षा तुलयतो यतः सत्यं ततोऽधिकम्॥
en: We have heard that once on a time truth and all religious observances were weighted in a scale. When both were weighted, that scale on which truth was, proved heavier.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: यतो धर्मस्ततः सत्यं सर्वं सत्येन वर्धते। किमर्थमनृतं कर्म कर्तुं राजंस्त्वमिच्छसि॥
en: There is truth where Righteousness is. Everything multiplies through truth. Why, O king, do you wish to do false act.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: सत्ये कुरु स्थिरं भावं मा राजन्ननृतं कृथाः। कस्मात्त्वमनृतं वाक्यं देहीति कुरुषेऽशुभम्॥
en: Be firm in truth. Do not fact falsely, O king. Why do you falsify the falsify the words-Give (me)!-which you have said?

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: यदि जप्यफलं दत्तं मया नैषिष्यसे नृप। धर्मेभ्यः सम्परिभ्रष्टो लोकाननुचरिष्यसि॥
en: If you refuse, O king, to accept the fruits that I have given you of my recitations, you shall then have to wander over the world, fallen away from Righteousness.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: संश्रुत्य यो न दित्सेत याचित्वा यश्च नेच्छति। उभावानृतिकावेतौ न मृषा कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: That person who does not give after having promised, and he also that does not accept after having begged, are both stained with falsehood. You should not, therefore, falsify your own words.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच योद्धव्यं रक्षितव्यं च क्षत्रधर्मः किल द्विज। दातारः क्षत्रियाः प्रोक्ता गृह्णीयां भवतः कथम्॥
en: The king said To fight and to protect from the duties of Kshatriyas. It is said that Kshatriyas are givers. How then shall I take anything from you.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच न च्छन्दयामि ते राजन्नापि ते गृहमाव्रजम्। इहागम्य तु याचित्वा न गृह्णीषे पुनः कथम्॥
en: The Brahmana said I never pressed you, O king. I did not seek your house. Yourself, coming here, coming here, you yourself begged of me, Why then do you not take?

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: धर्म उवाच अविवादोऽस्तु युवयोर्वित्त मां धर्ममागतम्। द्विजो दानफलैर्युक्तो राजा सत्यफलेन च॥
en: Dharma said Know you both that I am Dharma himself, Let there be no dispute between you. Let the Brahmana possess the reward of gift, and let the king also obtain the merit of truth.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: स्वर्ग उवाच स्वर्ग मां विद्धि राजेन्द्र रूपिणं स्वयमागतम्। अविवादोऽस्तु युवयोरुभौ तुल्यफलौ युवाम्॥
en: Heaven said Know, O great king, that I am Heaven's self-incarnate, come here in person. Let this dispute between you cease. You are both equal in respect of the merit or rewards that you have acquired.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच कृतं स्वर्गेण मे कार्यं गच्छ स्वर्ग यथागतम्। विप्रो यदीच्छते गन्तुं चीर्णं गृह्णातु मे फलम्॥
en: The king said I have no use with heaven. Go, O Heaven, to the place you have come from. If this learned Brahmana wishes to go to you, let him take the rewards that I have acquired.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच बाल्ये यदि स्यादज्ञानान्मया हस्तः प्रसारितः। निवृत्तलक्षणं धर्ममुपासे संहितां जपन्॥
en: Thc Brahmana said In the boyhood I had, through Ignorance, stretched my hand for accepting gifts. Now, however, I recite the Gayatri, observing the duty of abstention.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: निवृत्तं मां चिराद्राजन् विप्रलोभयसे कथम्। स्वेन कार्यं करिष्यामि त्वत्तो नेच्छे फलं नृप। तप:स्वाध्यायशीलोऽहं निवृत्तश्च प्रतिग्रहात्॥
en: Why do you, O king, tempt me thus, me who have for a long time followed duty of abstention? I shall myself do what my duty is. I do not wish to participate in the rewards acquired by you, O king. I am given too penances and to the study of the Vedas, and I have abstained from acceptance.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच यदि विप्र विसृष्टं ते जप्यस्य फलमुत्तमम्। आवयोर्यत् फलं किञ्चित् सहितं नौ तदस्त्विह॥
en: The king said If, O Brahmana, you are really prepared to give me the excellent reward of your recitation, then let half that reward be mine, you also take at the same time half the reward that I myself have gained by my acts.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: द्विजाः प्रतिग्रहे युक्ता दातारो राजवंशजाः। यदि धर्मः श्रुतो विप्र सहैव फलमस्तु नौ॥
en: Brahmanas follows the duty of acceptance. Persons born in the royal order follow the duty of giving. If you are not unaware of the duties, let our fruits be equal.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: मा वा भूत् सहभोज्यं नौ मदीयं फलमाप्नुहि। प्रतीच्छ मत्कृतं धर्मं यदि ते मय्यनुग्रहः॥
en: Or, if you do not wish to be my equal regarding our rewards, that I may have gained. Do take the merit I have gained if you wish to show me favour.'

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो विकृतवेषौ द्वौ पुरुषौ समुपस्थितौ। गृहीत्वान्योन्यमावेष्ट्य कुचैलावूचतुर्वचः॥
en: Bhishma continued 'At this time two very ugly persons came there. Each had his arm upon the other's shoulder; both were ill-dressed. They said these

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: न मे धारयसीत्येको धारयामीति चापरः। इहास्ति नौ विवादोऽयमयं राजानुशासकः॥
en: You owe me nothing!-I really owe you!-If we dispute in this way, here is the king, who governs men.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: सत्यं ब्रवीम्यहमिदं न मे धारयते भवान्। अनृतं वदसीह त्वमृणं ते धारयाम्यहम्॥
en: I say truly, you owe me nothing!-You speak falsely. I owe you a debt!

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: तावुभौ सुभृशं तप्तौ राजानमिदमूचतुः। परीक्ष्य त्वं यथा स्याबो नावामिह विगर्हितौ॥
en: Both of them, greatly exercises in dispute, then addressed the king, saying,-See, O king, that none of us may be visited by sin!

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: विरूप उवाच धारयामि नरव्याघ्र विकृतस्येह गोः फलम्। ददतश्च न गृह्णाति विकृतो मे महीपते॥
en: Virupa said I owe my companion Vikrita, O king, the merits of the gift of a cow. I am willing to satisfy that debt. This Vikrita, however, refuses to accept repayment.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: विकृत उवाच न मे धारयते किञ्चिद् विरूपोऽयं नराधिप। मिथ्या ब्रवीत्ययं हि त्वां सत्याभासं नराधिप॥
en: Vikrita said This Virupa, O king, owes me nothing. He speaks an untruth under the appearance of truth, O King.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच विरूप किं धारयते भवानस्य ब्रवीतु मे। श्रुत्वा तथा करिष्येऽहमिति मे धीयते मनः॥
en: The king said Tell me, O Virupa, what is that which you owe your friend here. I wish to first hear you and then do what is proper.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: विरूप उवाच शृणुष्वावहितो राजन् यथैतद् धारयाम्यहम्। विकृतस्यास्य राजर्षे निखिलेन नराधिप॥
en: Virupa said Hear attentively, 0 king, all the circumstances fully about how I owe my companion, viz., this Vikrita, O king.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: अनेन धर्मप्राप्त्यर्थं शुभा दत्ता पुरानघ। धेनुर्विप्राय राजर्षे तप:स्वाध्यायशीलिने॥
en: This Vikrita had, in days gone by, for the sake of acquiring merit, O sinless onc, given away an auspicious cow, O royal sage, to a Brahmana given to penances and the study of the Vedas.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: तस्याश्चायं मया राजन् फलमभ्येत्य याचितः। विकृतेन च मे दत्तं विशुद्धनान्तरात्मना॥
en: Going to him, O king, I begged of him the reward of that act. With a pure heart, Vikrita made a gift to me of that reward.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ततो मे सुकृतं कर्म कृतमात्मविशुद्धये। गावौ च कपिले क्रीत्वा वत्सले बहुदोहने॥
en: I then, for my purification, did some good acts. I also bought two Kapila cows with calves, both of which used to give large quantities of milk.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ते चोच्छवृत्तये राजन् मया समपवर्जिते। यथाविधि यथाश्रद्धं तदस्याहं पुनः प्रभो॥ इहाद्यैव गृहीत्वा तु प्रयच्छे द्विगुणं फलम्। एवं स्यात् पुरुषव्याघ्र कः शुद्धः कोऽत्र दोषवान्।।९६।
en: I then presented according to due rites and with proper devotion, those two cows to a poor Brahmana living by picking solitary grains. Having formerly accepted the gift from my companion, I wish, O lord, even here, to give him in return twice the reward. The circumstances being such, O foremost of men, who amongst us two shall be innocent and who guilty?

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: एवं विवदमानौ स्वस्त्वामिहाभ्यागतौ नृप। कुरु धर्ममधर्म वा विनये नौ समादध॥
en: Disputing with each other about this, we have both come to you, O King, Whether you judge rightly or wrongly, settle our dispute and put us in peace.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: यदि नेच्छति मे दानं यथा दत्तमनेन वै। भवानत्र स्थिरो भूत्वा मार्गे स्थापयिताद्य नौ॥
en: If this my companion does not wish to take from me in return a gift equal to what he gave me, you shall have to judge patiently and put us both on the right road.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच दीयमानं न गृह्णासि ऋणं कस्मात् त्वमद्य वै। यथैव तेऽभ्यनुज्ञातं तथा गृह्णीष्व मा चिरम्॥
en: The king said, Why do you not accept payment that is sought lo be made for the debt that he owes to you? Do not delay, but accept payment of what you know, to be your due!

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: विकृत उवाच धारयामीत्यनेनोक्तं ददानीति तथा मया। नायं मे धारयत्यद्य गच्छतां यन वाञ्छति॥
en: Vikrita said-This one says that he owes me. tell him that what I gave I give away. He does not, therefore, owe me anything, Let him go wherever he likes.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच ददतोऽस्य न गृह्णासि विषमं प्रतिभाति मे। दण्ड्यो हि त्वं मम मतो नास्त्यत्र खलु संशयः॥
en: He is ready to give.you. You are, however, reluctant to take. It does not appear proper to me! I think you should be punished for this. There is little doubt in this.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: विकृत उवाच मयास्य दत्तं राजर्षे गृह्णीयां तत् कथं पुनः। काममत्रापराधो मे दण्डमाज्ञापय प्रभो॥
en: I made a gift to him, O royal sage! How can I take it back? If I am guilty in this, do you declare the punishment, O powerful one.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: विरूप उवाच दीयमानं यदि मया नेषिष्यसि कथञ्चन। नियंस्यति त्वां नृपतिरयं धर्मानुशासकः॥
en: Virupa said If you refuge to take when I am ready to give, this king will, forsooth, punish you, for he is an upholder of justice. Vikrita said,

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: विकृत उवाच स्वं मया याचितेनेह दत्तं कथमिहाद्य तत्। गृह्णीयां गच्छतु भवानभ्यनुज्ञां ददानि ते॥
en: Vikrita said Begged by him I gave him what was my own. How shall I now take it back. You may go away. I permit you.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच श्रुतमेतत्त्वया राजन्नन्योः कथितं द्वयोः। प्रतिज्ञातं मया यत्ते तद् गृहाणाविचारितम्॥
en: The Brahmana said You have heard, O king, the words of these two. Do you take unhesitatingly what I have promised to give you.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच प्रस्तुतं सुमहत् कार्यमनयोर्गह्वरं यथा। जापकस्य दृढीकारः कथमेतद् भविष्यति॥
en: This subject is, indeed, as deep as an unfathomable pit. How will the tenaciousness of this Reciter end.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: यदि तावन्न गृह्णामि ब्राह्मणेनापवर्जितम्। कथं न लिप्येयमहं पापेन महताद्य वै॥
en: If I do not take what has been given by this Brahmana, how shall I avoid being polluted with a great sin?

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: तौ चोवाच स राजर्षिः कृतकार्यो गमिष्यथः। नेदानी मामिहासाद्य राजधर्मो भवेन्मृषा॥
en: The royal sage then said to the two disputants,-having acquired your respective objects, go you both. I should see that kingly duties, which are in me, may not become useless.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: स्वधर्मः परिपाल्यस्तु राज्ञामिति विनिश्चयः। विप्रधर्मश्च गहनो मामनात्मानमाविशत्॥
en: It is settled that kings should follow the duties sanctioned for them. To my misfortune, however, the course of duties laid down for Brahmanas has affected my wretched self.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच गृहाण धारयेऽहं च याचितं संश्रुतं मया। न चेद् ग्रहीष्यसे राजशपिष्ये त्वां न संशयः॥
en: The Brahmana said Accept, O king! I owe you, You begged it of me, and I also have promised! If, however, you refuse to take, O king, I shall forsooth curse you.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच धिग्राजधर्मं यस्यायं कार्यस्येह विनिश्चयः। इत्यर्थं मे ग्रहीतव्यं कथं तुल्यं भवेदिति॥
en: Fie on royal duties, the fixed action of which is even such! I should, however, take what you give only for making the two sorts of duty exactly equal.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: एष पाणिरपूर्वं मे निक्षेपार्थं प्रसारितः। यन्मे धारयसे विप्र तदिदानी प्रदीयताम्॥
en: This my hand, that was never before expanded, is not stretched forth. Give me what you owe me.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच संहितां जपता यावान् गुणः कश्चित् कृतो मया। तत् सर्वं प्रतिगृह्णीष्व यदि किञ्चिदिहास्ति मे॥
en: If I have acquired any fruits by reciting the Gayatri, accept them all.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: राजोवाच जलमेतन्निपतितं मम पाणौ द्विजोत्तम। सममस्तु सहैवास्तु प्रतिगृह्णातु वै भवान्॥
en: The king said-These drops of water, see, O foremost of Brahmanas, have fallen upon my hand. I also wish to give you. Accept my gift. Let us both stand equal.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: विरूप उवाच कामक्रोधौबिद्धिनौ त्वमावाभ्यां कारितो भवान्। सहेति च यदुक्तं ते समा लोकास्तवास्य च॥
en: Virupa said Know, O king, that we two are Desire and Anger. We have induced you to act thus! You have made a gift in return to the Brahmana. Let there be equality between you and this twiceborn one regarding blessed regions in the next world.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: नायं धारयते किञ्चिज्जिज्ञासा त्वत्कृते कृता। कालो धर्मस्तथा मृत्युः कामक्रोधौ तथा युवाम्॥ सर्वमन्योन्यनिष्कर्ष निघृष्टं पश्यतस्तव। गच्छ लोकान् जितान् स्वेन कर्मणा यत्रवाञ्छसि॥११७।
en: This Vikrita really does not owe me anything. We appealed to you for your own sake. Time, Dharma, Mrityu, and we two, have cxamined everything about you, here in your very presence, by creating this quarrel between you and that Brahmana. go now, as you like, to those regions of happiness which you have acquired by means of your deeds.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: जापकानां फलावाप्तिर्मया ते सम्प्रदर्शिता। गतिः स्थानं च लोकाच जापकेन यथा जिताः॥
en: Bhishma said I have now told you how Reciters win the fruits (of their recitation) and what, indeed, is their object, what the place, and what the region of surya.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: प्रयाति संहिताध्यायी ब्रह्माणं परमेष्ठिनम्। अथबाग्नि समायाति सूर्यमाविशतेऽपि वा॥
en: A Reciter of Gayatri goes to the supreme god Brahiman, or to Agni or enters the regions, that a Reciter may acquire.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: स तैजसेन भावेन यदि तत्र रमत्युत। गुणास्तेषां समाधत्ते रागेण प्रतिमोहितः॥
en: If he plays there in his new form, then stupefied by such attachment, he is affected by the attributes of those particular regions.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: एवं सोमे तथा वायौ भूम्याकाशशरीरगः। सरागस्तत्र वसति गुणांस्तेषां समाचरन्॥
en: He is equally affected if he goes to Soma, or Vayu, or Earth, or Space. The fact is, he lives in all these, with attachment, and shows the attributes peculiar to those regions.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: अथ तत्र विरागी स गच्छति त्वथ संशयम्। परमव्ययमिच्छन् स तमेवाविशते पुनः॥
en: If, however, after having freed himself from attachments, he goes to those regions and does not trust the happiness he enjoys) and wishes for That Which is Supreme and Immutable, he then enters even That.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: अमृताच्चामृतं प्राप्तः शान्तीभूतो निरात्मवान्। ब्रह्मभूतः स निर्द्वन्द्वः सुखी शान्तो निरामयः॥
en: In that case he acquires the ambrosia of ambrosia, to a state free from desire and individual consciousness. He becomes Brahma's self, freed from the influence of the pairs of opposites, happy, tranquil, the without pain.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: ब्रह्मस्थानमनावर्तमेकमक्षरसंज्ञकम्। अदुःखमजरं शान्तं स्थानं तत् प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Indeed, he acquires that state which is free from pain, which is tranquil, which is called Brahma, whence there is no return, and which is called the One and Jummutable.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: चतुर्भिर्लक्षणीनं तथा षड्भिः सषोडशैः। पुरुषं तमतिक्रम्य आकाशं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: He becomes freed from the four means of perception, viz., Direct knowledge (through the senses), Revelation, Inference, and Intuition, the six conditions, (Hunger, Trust, Grief, Delusion, Disease, and Death), and also the other six and ten senses, attributes, viz., five breaths, the ten senses, and the mind. Transcending the Creator (Brahiman), he becomes at one with the One Supreme Soul.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: अथ नेच्छति रागात्मा सर्वं तदधितिष्ठति। यच्च प्रार्थयते तच्च मनसा प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Or, if moved by attachments, he does not wish for such absorption, but wishes to have a separate existence depending on that Supreme Cause of everything, then he gets the fruition of all his desires.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: अथवा चेक्षते लोकान् सर्वान् निरयसंज्ञितान्। निस्पृहः सर्वतो मुक्तस्तत्र वै रमते सुखम्॥
en: Or, if he hates all regions of happiness, which have been called hells, he then, driving off desire and freed from everything, enjoys supreme happiness even in those very regions.

description: The discourse of the subject by Savitri
sn: एवमेषा महाराज जापकस्य गतिर्यथा। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: Thus, O king, I have described to you about the end acquired by Reciters. I have told you everything. What else do you wish to hear from me?

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किमुत्तरं तदा तौ स्म चक्रतुस्तस्य भाषिते। ब्राह्मणो वाथवा राजा तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, what reply was given by either the Brahmana or the king to Virupa after he had finished his speech.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: अथवा तौ गतौ तत्र यदेतत् कीर्तितं त्वया। संवादो वा तयोः कोऽभूत् किं वा तौ तत्र चक्रतुः॥
en: What king of end was it, amongst those described by you, that they acquired? What, indeed, was the conversation that took place between them, and what did they do there?"

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: भीष्म उवाच तथेत्येवं प्रतिश्रुत्य धर्मं सम्पूज्य च प्रभो। यमं कालं च मृत्युं च स्वर्ग सम्पूज्य चार्हतः॥
en: Saying,-Let it be as you have said, the Brahmana, adored Dharma and Yama and Time and Mrityu and Heaven all of whom deserved adorations.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: पूर्वं ये चापरे तत्र समेता ब्राह्मणर्षभाः। सर्वान् सम्पूज्य शिरसा राजानं सोऽब्रवीद् द्विजः॥ फलेनानेन संयुक्तो राजर्षे गच्छ मुख्यताम्। भवता चाभ्यनुज्ञातो जपेयं भूय एव ह॥
en: He also adored all those foremost of Brahmanas that had come there by bending his head to them. Addressing the king then, he said,-Gifted with the reward of my recitation, O royal sage, acquire an eminent position. With your permission I shall set myself to my recitations again.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: वरच मम पूर्वं हि दत्तो देव्या महाबला श्रद्धा ते जपतो नित्यं भवत्विति विशाम्पते॥
en: O you of great power, the goddess Savitri gave me a boon, saying,-Let, your devotion to recitation be continuous.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: राजोवाच यद्येवमफला सिद्धिः श्रद्धा च जपितुं तव। गच्छ विप्र मया साधु जापकं फलमाप्नुहि॥
en: If your success has become futile, and if your heart is bent upon practising again, go, O learned Brahmana, half and half with me, and you alone enjoy the reward of the recitations.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच कृतः प्रयत्नः सुमहान् सर्वेषां संनिधाविह। सह तुल्यफलावावां गच्छावो यत्र नौ गतिः॥
en: The Brahmana said You have exerted your best before all these men. Let us then become equal regarding our rewards, and let us go to receive our end.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: भीष्म उवाच व्यवसायं तयोस्तत्र विदित्वा त्रिदशेश्वरः। सह देवैरुपययौ लोकपालैस्तथैव च॥
en: Apprised of these determination, the king of the celestials came there, accompanied by the gods and the Regents of the world.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: साध्याश्च विश्वे मरुतो वाद्यानि सुमहान्ति च। नद्यः शैला: समुद्राश्च तीर्थानि विविधानि च।॥ तपांसि संयोगविधिर्वेदाः स्तोभाः सरस्वती। नारदः पर्वतश्चैव विश्वावसुर्हहाहुहूः॥ गन्धर्वश्चित्रसेनश्च परिवारगणैर्युतः। नागाः सिद्धाश्च मुनयो देवदेवः प्रजापतिः॥ विष्णुः सहस्रशीर्षश्च देवोऽचिन्त्यः समागमत्। अवाद्यन्तान्तरिक्षे च भेर्यस्तूर्याणि वा विभो॥
en: The Sadhyas, the Vishvas, the Mantras, various sorts of loud and sweet music, the Rivers, the Mountains, the Seas, the Sacred Waters, the Penances, the Ordinances about Yoga, the Vedas, the Sounds accompanying the singing of the Samans, Sarasvati, Narada, Parvata, Vishvavasu, the Hahas, the Huhus, the are Gandharva Chitrasena with all the members of his family, the Nagas, the Siddhas, the Munis, the god of gods, viz., Prajapati, and the inconceivable and thousand-headed Vishnu himself, came there. Drums and trumpets were beat and blown in the sky.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: पुष्पवर्षाणि दिव्यानि तत्र तेषां महात्नाम्। ननृतुश्चाप्सरःसंघास्तत्र तत्र समन्ततः॥
en: Celestial flowers were poured upon those great beings. Bevies of Apsaras danced all around.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: अथ स्वर्गस्तथा रूपी ब्राह्मणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। संसिद्धस्त्वं महाभाग त्वं च सिद्धस्तथा नृप॥
en: Heaven, in his embodied form, came there. Addressing the Brahmana, he said,-You have acquired Success. You highly blessed.-Then addressing the king, said,-You have also, O king acquired success.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: अथ तौ सहितौ राजन्नन्योन्यविधिना ततः। विषयप्रतिसंहारमुभावेव प्रचक्रतुः।।१६
en: O king having done good to each other, the king and the Brahmana, withdrew their senses from the objects of the world.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: प्राणापानौ तथोदानं समानं व्यानमेव च। एवं तौ मनसि स्थाप्य दधतुः प्राणयोर्मनः॥
en: Fixing the vital airs Prana, Apana Samana, Udana, and Vyana in the heart, they fixed the mind in Prana and Apana united together.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: उपस्थितकृतौ तौ च नासिकाग्रमधो भ्रुवोः। भृकुट्या चैव मनसा शनैर्धारयतस्तदा॥
en: They then placed the two united airs in the abdomen, and fixed their eyes on the tip of the nose and then immediately below the nose and then immediately below the two eye-brows. They next saw the two airs, with the help of the mind, in the interstice between the two eyebrows, bringing them there by and by.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: निश्चेष्टाभ्यां शरीराभ्यां स्थिरदृष्टी समाहितौ। जितात्मानौ तथाऽऽधाय मूर्धन्यात्मानमेव च॥
en: With bodies perfectly motionless they were absorbed with fixed gaze. Having controlled their souls, they then placed the soul within the brain.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: तालुदेशमथोद्दाल्य ब्राह्मणस्य महात्मनः। ज्योतिर्चाला सुमहती जगाम त्रिदिवं तदा॥
en: Then passing the crown of the great Brahmana a fiery flame of great effulgence went up to heaven,

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: हाहाकारस्तथा दिक्षु सर्वेषां सुमहानभूत्। तज्ज्योतिः स्तूयमानं स्म ब्राह्मणं प्राविशत् तदा॥
en: Loud exclamations of sorrow, uttered by all creatures, were then heard on all sides. Lauded by all, that splendour then entered Brahmana's self.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: ततः स्वागतमित्याह तत् तेजः प्रपितामहः। प्रादेशमात्रं पुरुषं प्रत्युद्गम्य विशाम्पते॥
en: Coming forward, the great grandfather addressed that splendour which had become like a span in size saying,-Welcome.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: भूयश्चैवापरं प्राह वचनं मधुर तदा। जापकैस्तुल्यफलता योगानां नात्र संशयः॥
en: And again he uttered these sweet words: Verily, Reciters acquire the same end with the Yogins.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: योगस्य तावदेतेभ्यः प्रत्यक्षं फलदर्शनम्। जापकानां विशिष्टं तु प्रत्युत्थानं समाहितम्॥
en: When the Yogins attains his end he gets a direct vision unto all these (here assembled). Regarding Reciters, however, there is this distinction, that they are honoured by Brahmana's advancing forward to receive them.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: उष्यतां मयि चेत्युक्त्वाचेतयत् सततं पुनः। अथास्यं प्रविवेशास्य ब्राह्मणो विगतज्वरः॥
en: Live you in me,-Thus spoke Brahman and once more gave consciousness to that splendour. Indeed, then, freed from all anxieties, the Brahmana entered the mouth of the Creator.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: राजाप्येतेन विधिना भगवन्तं पितामहम्। यथैव द्विजशार्दूलस्तथैव प्राविशत् तदा॥
en: The king Ikshvaku, too, in the same way, entered the divine Grandfather like that best of Brahmanas.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: स्वयम्भुवमथो देवा अभिवाद्य ततोऽब्रुवन्। जापकानां विशिष्टं तु प्रत्युत्थानं समाहितम्॥
en: The deities saluted the self-create and said, A very superior end is, indeed, laid down for Reciters.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: जापकार्थमयं यत्नो यदर्थं वयमागताः। कृतपूजाविमौ तुल्यौ त्वया तुल्यफलाविमौ॥
en: This your exertion is for Reciters. We only came here for seeing it. You have made these two equal, honoured them equally, and granted them an equal end.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: योगजापकयोदृष्टं फलं सुमहदद्य वै। सर्वा ल्लोकानतिक्रम्य गच्छेतां यत्र वाञ्छितम्॥
en: We have seen to-day the high end that is reserved for both. Yogins and Reciters. Transcending all happy regions, these two are capable of going wherever they like.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच महास्मृतिं पठेद् यस्तु तथैवानुस्मृतिं शुभाम्। तावप्येतेन विधिना गच्छेतां मत्सलोकताम्॥
en: Brahmana said-He also who would read the great Smriti (viz., the Vedas) and he too who would read the other sacred Smritis that follow the former, (viz., Manu's and the rest), would, similarly allain to the same region with me.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: यश्च योगे भवेद् भक्तः सोऽपि नास्त्यत्र संशयः। विधिनानेन देहान्ते मम लोकानवाप्नुयात्। साधये गम्यतां चैव यथास्थानानि सिद्धये॥
en: He also, who is devoted to Yoga, will, forsooth, acquire likewise, after death, my own regions. I go hence. Go ye all to your respective abodes for the accomplishment of your ends.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्त्वा स तदा देवस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयता आमन्त्र्य च ततो देवा ययुः स्वं स्वं निवेशनम्॥
en: Having said so that foremost of gods disappeared there and then. Having obtained a leave from him beforehand the gods returned to their respective quarters.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: ते च सर्वे महात्मानो धर्म सत्कृत्य तत्र वै। पृष्ठतोऽनुययू राजन् सर्वे सुप्रीतचेतसः॥
en: Having honoured Dharma, all those great beings proceeded with well-pleased hearts, O king, walking behind that great god.

description: The reply of the Brahmana to Virupa
sn: एतत् फलं जापकानां गतिश्चैषा प्रकीर्तिता। यथाश्रुतं महाराज किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: These are the rewards of reciters and this their end. I have described them to you as ] myself had heard of them. What else, O king, do you wish to hear of?

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं फलं ज्ञानयोगस्य वेदानां नियमस्य च। भूतात्मा च कथं ज्ञेयस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said What are the fruits of the Jnana Yoga, of all the Vedas, and of the (various) observances and vows? How also may the individual soul be known? Tell me this, O grand father.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। मनोः पजापतेर्वादं महर्षेश्च बृहस्पतेः॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old narrative of the conversation between that lord of creatures, viz., Manu, and the great Rishi Brihaspati.

sn: प्रजापतिं श्रेष्ठतमं प्रजानां देवर्षिसंघप्रवरो महर्षिः। बृहस्पतिः प्रश्नमिमं पुराणं पप्रच्छ शिष्योऽथ गुरुं प्रणम्य॥ यत्कारणं यत्र विधिः प्रवृत्तो ज्ञाने फल यत्प्रवदन्ति विप्राः। यन्मन्त्रशब्दैरकृतप्रकाशं तदुच्यतां मे भगवन्यथावत्॥
en: In days of yore, the foremost of celestial Rishis, viz., Brihaspati, who was a disciple of Manu bowed to his preceptor and addressing that king and first of all creatures, said,-What is the origin of the universe? Whence have the ordinances originated? What are those fruits attributed by the learned to Knowledge? Tell me also truly, O illustrious one, what is that which the Vedas have not been able to show?

sn: र्यज्ञैरनेकैरथ गोप्रदानैः। फलं महद्भिर्यदुपास्यते च किं तत्कथं वा भविता क्व वा तत्॥
en: What are those fruits which are respected by eminent sages conversant with the science of Artha, with the Vedas, and with the mantras, through sacrifices and profuse gifts of kine? Whence do those fruits originate? Where are they do be found?

sn: मही महीजाः पवनोऽन्तरिक्षं जलौकसश्चैव जलं दिवं च। स्तदुच्यतां मे भगवन् पुराणम्॥
en: Tell me also this old history, viz., whence have the Earth, all earthly objects, wind, sky aquatic animals, water, heaven, and the dwellers of heaven, all originated.

sn: ज्ञानं यतः प्रार्थयते नरो वै ततस्तदर्था भवति प्रवृत्तिः। न चाप्यहं वेद परं पुराणं मिथ्याप्रवृत्तिं च कथं नु कुर्याम्।
en: Man is inclined towards that object which he seeks to know. I have no knowledge of that Ancient and Supreme Being. How shall I free myself from a false display of my leaning towards Him?

sn: ऋक्सामसंघांश्च यजूंषि चापि च्छन्दांसि नक्षत्रगति निरुक्तम्। अधीत्य च व्याकरणं सकल्पं शिक्षां च भूतप्रकृतिं न वेदि॥
en: I have read the Riks, all the Samans, all the Yajuses, the Chhandas, Astronomy, Nirukta, Grammar, Sankalpa, and Shiksha. But I have no knowledge of the nature of the five principal elements which forin everything.

sn: स मे भवान् शंसतु सर्वमेतत् सामान्यशब्दैश्च विशेषणैश्च। ज्ज्ञाने फलं कर्मणि वा यदस्ति॥
en: Describe to me all I have asked you, by making only simple statements and using qualifying adjectives or attributes. Tell me what the fruits are of Knowledge, sacrifices and other religious rites. Explain to me how also an embodied being leaves his body and acquires a new one.

sn: यथा च देहाच्च्यवते शरीरी पुनः शरीरं च यथाभ्युपैति। मनुरुवाच स्तदेव दुःखं प्रवदन्त्यनिष्टम्।
en: What is agreeable to one constitutes his happiness. Likewise what is disagreeable to one forms his misery, feeling-"By this I shall acquire happiness and prevent misery”_-men perform all religious acts.

sn: देतत्कृते कर्मविधिः प्रवृत्तः। त्येतत्कृते ज्ञानविधिः प्रवृत्तः॥
en: The efforts for the acquisition of Knowledge, however, originate from a desire for avoiding both happiness and misery.

sn: कामात्मकाश्छन्दसि कर्मयोगा एभिर्विमुक्तः परमश्नुवीत। नानाविधे कर्मपथे सुखार्थी नरः प्रवृत्तो न परं प्रयाति॥
en: The ordinances about sacrifices and other observances, which are in the Vedas, all originate from desire. He, however, who frees himself from desire of acquiring happiness, performs various acts is constrained to go to hell.

sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच इष्टं त्वनिष्टं च सुखासुखे च साशीस्त्वबच्छन्दति कर्मभिश्च।
en: Men aspire to acquire the agreeable which ends in happiness, to avoid the disagreeable which begets misery. Such acquisition and such avoidance again are brought about by acts.

sn: मनुरुवाच एभिर्विमुक्तः परमाविवेश एतत् कृते कर्मविधिः प्रवृत्तः। कामात्मकांश्छन्दति कर्मयोग एभिर्विमुक्तः परमाददीत॥
en: By freeing oneself from acts that a man succeeds in entering into Brahma. The injunctions of Karma or acts are laid down for that very end. The ordinances of Karma tempt only those whose hearts are not shorn of desire. By freeing oneself from acts one wins the highest state.

sn: आत्मादिभिः कर्मभिरिन्ध्यमानो धर्मे प्रवृत्तो द्युतिमान् सुखार्थी। परं हि तत् कर्मपथादपेतं निराशिषं ब्रह्मपरं ह्यवैति॥
en: By performing religious rites, one who wishes liberation becomes purified (from attachments, for these acts have for their object the purification of the soul, and at last acquires great splendour. By freeing oneself from acts, one acquires the highest end, viz., Brahma, which reigns Supreme over the reward which acts give.

sn: प्रजाः सृष्टा मनसा कर्मणा च द्वावेवैतौ सत्पथौ लोकजुष्टौ। दृष्टं कर्म शाश्वतं चान्तवच्च मनस्त्यागः कारणं नान्यदस्ति॥
en: Creatures have all been engendered by Mind and Act. These are the two best paths adored of all. External acts yields fruits that are both transitory as also eternal. For acquiring the latter there is no other means than relinquishing the desire for fruits by the mind,

sn: स्वेनात्मना चक्षुरिव प्रणेता निशात्यये तमसा संवृतात्मा। ज्ञानं तु विज्ञानगुणेन युक्तं कर्माशुभं पश्यति वर्जनीयम्॥
en: As the eye, when night passes away and the veil of darkness is gone, leads its possessor by its own power, so the Understanding, when it becomes endued with Knowledge, sees all evils which should be shunned.

sn: सर्पान्कुशाग्राणि तथोदपानं ज्ञात्वा मनुष्याः परिवर्जयन्ति। ज्ज्ञाने फलं पश्य यथा विशिष्टम्॥
en: Men avoid snakes, sharp blades, of Kusha and pits, when they find them on their way. If some tread upon or fall into them, they do so by ignorance. Mark the superiority of the fruits of knowledge.

sn: कृत्स्नस्तु मन्त्रो विधिवत् प्रयुक्तो यथा यथोक्तास्त्विह दक्षिणाश्च। अन्नप्रदानं मनसः समाधिः पञ्चात्मकं कर्मफलं वदन्ति॥
en: Duly administered Mantras, sacrifices, the presents called Dakshina, gift of food and concentration of the mind are the five acts which yield fruits, there being none else.

sn: स्तस्मान्मन्त्रो मन्त्रपूर्वं हि कर्म। विधिविधेयं मनसोपपत्तिः फलस्य भोक्ता तु तथा शरीरी॥
en: Acts have the three Gunas (of Satva Rajas, and Tamas) for their soul. The Vedas say this. The Mantras, therefore, have the same three qualities, since it is with Mantras that acts are performed. The ritual also is possessed by the same three qualities. The fruits of action depend upon the mind. It is the embodied creature who enjoys those fruits.

sn: शब्दाश्च रूपाणि रसाश्च पुण्या: स्पर्शाश्च गन्धाश्च शुभास्तथैव। देतत् पुलं सिद्ध्यति कर्मलोके।॥
en: All excellent sorts of sound, form, tastes, touch, and scent, are the fruits of acts, being acquired in the region of acts. As for, however, the fruits of knowledge, man acquires them even here before death.

sn: यद् यच्छरीरेण करोति कर्म शरीरयुक्तः समुपाश्नुते तत्। शरीरमेवायतनं सुखस्य दुःखस्य चाप्यायतनं शरीरम्॥
en: Whatever acts are perforined by means of the body, one enjoys the fruits thereof in this body. The body is, indeed, the structure to which adhere both happiness and misery.

sn: वाचा तु यत्कर्म करोति किंचिद् वाचैव सर्वं समुपाश्नुते तत्। न्मन:स्थ एवायमुपाश्नुते तत्॥
en: Whatever acts are performed by means of words, their fruits are enjoyed in a state in which words can be spoken. Likewise, whatever acts are performed by the mind, their fruits are enjoyed in a state in which one is not treed from the mind.

sn: यथा यथा कर्मगुणं फलार्थी करोत्ययं कर्मफले निविष्टः। तथा तथायं गुणसम्प्रयुक्तः शुभाशुभं कर्मफलं भुनक्ति॥
en: Seeking the fruits of acts, whatever acts (Satvika or Rajasika or Tamasika) a person performs, the fruits, good or bad, that he actually enjoys are permeated by their nature.

sn: मत्स्यो यथा स्रोत इवाभिपाती तथा कृतं पूर्वमुपैति कर्म। शुभे त्वसौ तुष्यति दुष्कृते तु न तुष्यते वै परमः शरीरी॥
en: Like fishes going against a current of water, pristine acts visit the actor. The embodied creature enjoys happiness for his good acts, and suffers misery for his evil ones.

sn: यतो जगत् सर्वमिदं प्रसूतं ज्ञात्वाऽऽत्मवन्तो व्यतियान्ति यत् तत्। यन्मन्त्रशब्दैरकृतप्रकाशं तदुच्यमानं शृणु मे परं यत्॥
en: I will now describe Him from whom this universe has originated, Him by knowing whom persons of purified souls cross this world, Him who has not been expressed by Vedic Mantras and Words. Listen to me as I speak of that greatest of the grcat.

sn: रसैविमुक्तं विविधैश्च गन्धै रशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपवच्चा अग्राह्यमव्यक्तमवर्णमेकं पञ्चप्रकारान् ससृजे प्रजानाम्॥
en: Himself freed from the several sorts of tasto and scent, and sound and touch and forin, He is incapable of being comprehended by the senses, unmanifest, without colour, the One, and He has created the five kinds of objects for His creatures.

sn: न स्त्री पुमान् नापि नपुंसकं च न सन्न चासत् सदसच्च तन्न। स्तदक्षरं न क्षरतीति विद्धि॥
en: He is neither female, nor male, nor of the neuter sex. He is neither existent, nor nonexistent, nor existent-non-existent. Only those that are acquainted with Bralıma see Him. He knows no deterioration.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: मनुरुवाच अक्षरात् खं ततो वायुस्ततो ज्योतिस्ततो जलम्। जलात् प्रसूता जगती जगत्यां जायते जगत्॥
en: From that eternal and undecaying. One first originated Space; from space came Wind; from wind came Light; from light came Water. From water originated the Universe; and from the universe, all things that exist in it.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: एतैः शरीरैर्जलमेव गत्वा जलाच्च तेजः पवनोऽन्तरिक्षम् खाद् वै निवर्तन्ति न भाविनस्ते मोक्षं च ते वै परमाप्नुवन्ति॥
en: The bodies of all (earthly) objects, thence to light or heat, thence to the wind, and thence to space. The who seek liberation have not to return from space. On the other hand, they attain to Brahma.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: नोष्णं न शीतं मृदु नापि तीक्ष्णं नाम्लं कषायं मधुरं न तिक्तम्। न्न रूपवत्तत् परमस्वभावम्॥
en: The refuge of liberation, viz., Brahma, is neither hot, nor cold, neither mild nor fierce, neither sour nor astringent, neither sweet nor bitter. He is not endued with sound, or scent, or form. He transcends all these and everything, and is without size.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: स्पर्श तनुर्वेद रसं च जिह्वा घ्राणं च गन्धान् श्रवणौ च शब्दान्। रूपाणि चक्षुर्न च तत्परं यद् गृह्णन्त्यनध्यात्मविदो मनुष्याः॥
en: The skin perceives touch; the tongue, taste; the nose, scent; the ears, sounds; and the eye, forms. Men not conversant with Adhyatma succeed not in seeing what is above these.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: निवर्तयित्वा रसनां रसेभ्योः घ्राणं च गन्धाच्छ्रवणौ च शब्दात्। स्ततः परं पश्यति स्वं स्वभावम्॥
en: Having withdrawn the tongue from tastes, the nose from scents, the ears from sounds, and the eye from forms, one sees his ownself.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: यतो गृहीत्वा हि करोति यच्च यस्मिश्च तामारभते प्रवृत्तिम्। यस्मिश्च यद् केन च यश्च कर्ता यत् कारणं ते समुदायमाहुः॥
en: It has been said that which is the Cause of the actor, the act, the material with which the act is done, the place and the time of the act, and the inclinations and propensities about happiness and misery, is called the Self (or Soul).

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: यद् व्याप्यभूद् व्यापकं साधकं च यन्मन्त्रवत् स्थास्यति चापि लोके। यः सर्वहेतुः परमात्मकारी तत् कारणं कार्यमतो यदन्यत्॥
en: That which permeates everything which does everything, that which exists in the universe even as the Mantras say, that which is the cause of all, that which is the highest of the high, and that which is One without a second and does all things, is the Cause. Every thing clse is effect.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: यथा हि कश्चित् सुकृतैर्मनुष्यः शुभाशुभं प्राप्नुतेऽथाविरोधात्। एवं शरीरेषु शुभाशुभेषु स्वकर्मजैनिमिदं निबद्धम्॥
en: It is seen that person, on account of the acts performed by him, reaps fruits both good and evil, which exist harmoniously. Indeed, as the good and evil fruits begotten by their own acts live together in the bodies of creatures which are their refuge, so Knowledge lives in the .body.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: यथा प्रदीप्तः पुरतः प्रदीपः प्रकाशमन्यस्य करोति दीप्यन्। तथेह पञ्चेन्द्रियदीपवृक्षा ज्ञानप्रदीप्ताः परवन्त एव॥
en: As a lighted lamp, while burning, sees other objects before it, so the five senses which are like lamps fixed on high trees, find out their respective objects when lighted by Knowledge.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: यथा च राज्ञा बहवो ह्यमात्याः पृथक् प्रमाणं प्रवदन्ति युक्ताः। तद्वच्छरीरेषु भवन्ति पञ्च ज्ञानैकदेशः परमः स तेभ्यः॥
en: As the various ministers of a king, in a body, give him advice so the five senses which exist in the body all obey Knowledge. The latter is superior to all of them.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: यथार्चिषोऽग्नेः पवनस्य वेगो मरीचयोऽर्कस्य नदीषु चापः। स्तद्वच्छरीराणि शरीरिणां तु॥
en: As the flames of fire, the current of the wind, the rays of the sun, and the waters of rivers, go and come, again and again, so the bodies of embodied creatures are going and coming repeatedly.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: यथा च कश्चित् परशुं गृहीत्वा धूमं च पश्येज्ज्वलनं च काष्ठे। तद्वच्छरीरोदरपाणिपादं छित्त्वा न पश्यन्ति ततो यदन्यत्॥
en: As a person by taking up an axe cannot, by cutting open a piece of wood, see either smoke or fire in it, so one cannot, by cutting open the arms, feet and stomach of a person, cannot see the principle of knowledge, which, does not partake of the nature of stomach, the arms, and feet.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: तान्येव काष्ठानि यथा विमथ्य धूमं च पश्येज्ज्वलनं च योगात्। तद्वत् सबुद्धिः सममिन्द्रियात्मा बुधः परं पश्यति तं स्वभावम्॥
en: As again one sees both smoke and fire in wood by rubbing it against another piece, só a person endued with true intelligence and wisdom, by uniting the senses and the soul, may see the Supreme Soul which, of course, exists in its own nature.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: यथात्मनोऽङ्गं पतितं पृथिव्यां स्वप्नान्तरे पश्यति चात्मनोऽन्यत्। र्लिङ्गात्तथा गच्छति लिङ्गमन्यत्॥
en: As in the midst of a dream one sees his own body lying on the ground s something distinct from one's own self, so a person, having the five senses, the mind, and the understanding, sees (after death) his own body and then goes from one into another form.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: न युज्यतेऽसौ परमः शरीरी। अनेन लिङ्गेन तु लिङ्गमन्यद् गच्छत्यदृष्टः फलसंनियोगात्॥
en: The Soul does not undergo birth, growth, decay, and destruction. Acts of life being followed by effects, the Soul, clothed in body into another, unseen by others.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: न चक्षुषा पश्यति रूपमात्मनो न चापि संस्पर्शमुपैति किंचित्। न चापि तैः साधयते तु कार्य ते तं न पश्यन्ति स पश्यते तान्॥
en: No one can see with the eye the form of the Soul. The Soul again, is not touched by another. With the senses, the Soul performs no act. The senses do not approach the Soul. The Soul, however, apprehends them all.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: यथा समीपे ज्वलतोऽनलस्य संतापजं रूपमुपैति कश्चित्। न चान्तरं रूपगुणं बिभर्ति तथैव तद् दृश्यति रूपमस्य॥
en: As anything, placed in a burning fire before a spectator, assumes a certain colour on account of the light and heat that acts upon it, without taking any other colour or attribute, even so the Soul's form is seen to take its colour from the body.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: मदृश्यमन्यद् विशते शरीरम्। विसृज्य भूतेषु महत्सु देहं तदाश्रयं चैव बिभर्ति रूपम्॥
en: Likewise, men, renouncing one body, enters another, unseen by all. Indeed, casting off his body to the five great principal elements, he assumes a form that is likewise made of the same elements.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: खं वायुमग्नि सलिलं तथोर्वी समन्ततोऽभ्याविशते शरीरी। नानाश्रयाः कर्मसु वर्तमानाः श्रोत्रादयः पञ्च गुणान् श्रयन्ते।॥
en: Upon the destruction of his body the embodied creature enters space, wind, fire, water, and earth in such a way that each particular element in his body mingles with the particular element (out of his body) partaking of its nature. The senses also, which are engaged in various occupations and depend on the five elements enter their five elements what call forth their functions.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: स्तेजोमयं रूपमथो विपाकः। जलाश्रयं स्वेदमुक्तं रसं च वाय्वात्मकः स्पर्शकृतो गुणश्च॥
en: The ear derives its power from space; and the smell from the earth. From, which is the property of the eye, is the outcome of light or fire. Fire or heat depends on water. The tongue which has for its property taste, is merged in water. The skin which has touch for its property, is lost in the wind whose nature it partakes.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: महत्सु भूतेषु वसन्ति पञ्च पञ्चेन्द्रियार्थाश्च तथेन्द्रियाणि। सर्वाणि चैतानि मनोऽनुगानि बुद्धिं मनोऽन्वेति मतिः स्वभावम्॥
en: The fivefold attributes, (viz., sound, etc.) dwell in the five principal elements. Those fivefold objects of the senses (viz., space, etc.,) live in the (five) senses, All these again follow the mind. The mind follows the Understanding, and the Understanding follows That which exists in its true and pure nature, viz., the Supreme Self.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: शुभाशुभं कर्म कृतं यदन्यत् तदेव प्रत्याददते स्वदेहे। मनोऽनुवर्तन्ति परावराणि जलौकसः स्रोत इवानुकूलम्॥
en: The actor in his new body receives all the good and bad acts done by him here, as also all acts done by him in his pristine existence. All these acts done in this life and the next ones follow the mind even as aquatic animals pass along a current.

description: The origin of the elements and the formation of the bodies
sn: चलं यथा दृष्टिपथं परति सूक्ष्मं महद रूपमिवाभिभाति। स्वरूपमालोचयते च रूपं परं तथा बुद्धिपथं परैति॥
en: As a quickly-moving restless object comes in view, as a minute object appears huge (when seen through spectacles), as a mirror shows a person his own face, so the soul becomes an object of the Understanding's apprehension. (when seen through spectacles), as a mirror shows a person his own face, so the soul becomes an object of the Understanding's apprehension.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: मनुरुवाच यदिन्द्रियैस्तूपहितं पुरस्तात् प्राप्तान् गुणान् सस्मरते चिराय। तेष्विन्द्रियेषूपहतेषु पश्चात् स बुद्धिरूप: परमः स्वभावः॥
en: Manu said The mind united with the senses, remembers after a long time the impressions of objects received in the past. When the action of the senses is suspended, the Supreme Soul in the form in the Understanding, exists in its own true nature.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: नोपेक्षते कृत्स्नमतुल्यकालम्। स्तस्मात् स एकः परमः शरीरी॥
en: When the Soul does not in the least regard all those objects for their simultaniety or otherwise in point of time but collecting them from all directions holds them before it together, it necessarily happens that he wanders among all incongruous things. He is, therefore, the Witness. Hence the Soul put in body is something having a distinct and independent existence.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: रजस्तमः सत्त्वमथो तृतीयं गच्छत्यसौ स्थानगुणान् विरूपान्। तथेन्द्रियाण्याविशते शरीरी हुताशनं वायुरिवेन्धनस्थम्॥
en: There is Rajas, there is Tamas, and there is Satva the third. There arc again three conditions of the understanding, viz., waking, dreaming, and sound sleep. The Soul perceives the pleasures and pains, which are all contradictory, of those states, and which partake of the nature of the three-fold qualities first mentioned. The Soul enters the senses like the wind entering the fire in piece of wood.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: न चक्षुषा पश्यति रूपमात्मनो न पश्यति स्पर्शनमिन्द्रियेन्द्रियम्। न श्रोत्रलिङ्गं श्रवणेन दर्शनं तथा कृतं पश्यति तद् विनश्यति॥
en: One cannot see the forın of the Soul by his eye, nor can the sense of touch, amongst the senses, apprehend it. The Soul, is not, again, perceived by the ear. It may, however, be seen by the help of the Shrutis and the instructions of the wise. As for senses, that particular senses which apprehends it, loses upon such apprehension its existence as a sense.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: श्रोत्रादीनि च पश्यन्ति स्वं स्वमात्मानमात्मना। सर्वज्ञः सर्वदर्शी च सर्वज्ञस्तानि पश्यति॥
en: The senses cannot themselves apprehend their respective forms. The Soul is omniscient. It sees all things. Being omniscient, it is the Soul that sees the senses.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: यथा हिमवतः पाक् पृष्ठं चन्द्रमसो यथा। न दृष्टपूर्वं मनुजैन च तन्नास्ति तावता॥
en: Nobody has seen the other side of the Himavat mountains, nor the reverse of the moon's disc. Yet it cannot be said that they do not exist.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: तद्वद् भूतेषु भूतात्मा सूक्ष्मो ज्ञानात्मवानसौ। अदृष्टपूर्वश्चक्षुर्त्यां न चासौ नास्ति तावता॥
en: Likewise though never apprehended by the senses, yet nobody can say that the Soul, which dwells in all creatures, which is subtile, and which has knowledge for its essence, does not exist.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: पश्यन्नपि यथा लक्ष्म जगत् सोमे न विन्दति। एवमस्ति न चोत्पन्नं न च तन्न परायणम्॥
en: People see the world reflected on the inoon's disc in the shape of spots. Though seeing, they do not know that it is the world that is so reflected there. Such is the knowledge of the Soul. That knowledge must come of itself. The Soul depends upon the Soul itself.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: रूपवन्तमरूपत्वादुदयास्तमने बुधाः। धिया समनुपश्यन्ति तद्गताः सवितुर्गतिम्॥
en: Reflecting on the formlessness of visible objects before birth and after destruction, wise men behold by the help of intelligence, the forinlessness of objects that have visible forins. Similarly although the Sun's motion cannot be seen, yet persons, by watching its rising and Setting, conclude that the sun has motion.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: तथा बुद्धिप्रदीपेन दूरस्थं सुविपश्चितः। प्रत्यासन्नं निनीषन्ति ज्ञेयं ज्ञानाभिसंहितम्॥
en: Likewise learned and wise men see the Soul by the help of the lamp of intelligence, though it is at a great distance from them, and seek to merge the fivefold elements, which are near, into Brahma.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: न हि खल्वनुपायेन कश्चिदर्थोऽभिसिद्ध्यति। सूत्रजालैर्यथा मत्स्यान् बनन्ति जलजीविनः॥
en: Verily, an object cannot be performed without the application of means. Fishermen catch fish by means of nets made of strings.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: मृगैर्मुगाणां ग्रहणं पक्षिणां पक्षिभिर्यथा। गजानां च गजैरेव ज्ञेयं ज्ञानेन गृह्यते॥
en: Animals are caught by employing animals as the agents. Birds are caught by employing birds as the agents. Elephants are taken by employing elephants. In this way the Soul may be apprehended by the principle of Knowledge.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: अहिरेव ाहेः पादान् पश्यतीति हि नः श्रुतम्। तद्वन्मूर्तिषु मूर्तिस्थं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानेन पश्यति॥
en: It is heard that only a snake can see a snake's legs. Likewise one sees, through Knowledge, the Soul encased in subtle form and living within the gross body.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: नोत्सहन्ते यथा वेत्तुमिन्द्रियैरिन्द्रियाण्यपि। तथैवेह परा बुद्धिः परं बोध्यं न पश्यति।१४॥
en: People cannot, through their senses, know : the senses. Likewisc mere Intelligence at its highest cannot see the Soul which is supreme.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: यथा चन्द्रो ह्यमावास्यामलिङ्गत्वान्न दृश्यते। न च नाशोऽस्य भवति तथा विद्धि शरीरिणम्॥
en: The moon, on the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight, cannot be seen on account of its form being hidden. It cannot be said, however, that destruction overtakes it. Such is the case with the Soul living in the body.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: क्षीणकोशो ह्यमावास्यां चन्द्रमा न प्रकाशते। तद्वन्मूर्तिविमुक्तोऽसौ शरीरी नोपलभ्यते॥
en: On the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight, the gross body of the moon is seen. Similarly the Soul, when freed from the body, cannot be apprehended.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: यथाऽऽकाशान्तरं प्राप्य चन्द्रमा भ्राजते पुनः। तद्वल्लिङ्गान्तरं प्राप्य शरीरी भ्राजते पुनः॥
en: As gaining another point in the sky, the moon begins to shine once more, similarly the soul, acquiring a new body, begins to manifest itself once more.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: जन्म वृद्धिः क्षयश्चास्य प्रत्यक्षेणोपलभ्यते। सा तु चान्द्रमसी वृत्तिर्न तु तस्य शरीरिणः॥
en: The birth, growth, and disappearance of the moon can all be directly perceived by the eye. These phenomena, however, belong to the gross form of that luminary. The like are not the attributes of the Soul,

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: उत्पत्तिवृद्धिवयसा यथा स इति गृह्यते। चन्द्र एव त्वमावास्यां तथा भवति मूर्तिमान्॥
en: The moon, when it appears after its disappearance on the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight, is considered as the same luminary that had become invisible. Similarly despite the changes represented by birth, growth, and age, a person is considered as the same individual without any doubt of his identity.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: नोपसर्पद् विमुञ्चद् वा शशिनं दृश्यते तमः। विसृजंश्योपसर्पश्च तद्वत् पश्य शरीरिणम्॥
en: It is not distinctly seen how Rabu approaches and leaves the moon. Likewise the Soul cannot be seen how it leaves one body and enters another.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: यथा चन्द्रार्कसंयुक्तं तमस्तदुपलभ्यते। तद्वच्छरीरसंयुक्तः शरीरीत्युपलभ्यते॥
