en: Rahu becomes visible only when it exists with the sun or the moon. Likewise the Soul is apprehended only when it exists with the body.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: यथा चन्द्रार्कनिर्मुक्तः स राहु!पलभ्यते। तद्वच्छरीरनिर्मुक्तः शरीरी नोपलभ्यते॥
en: When freed from the sun or the moon, Rahu is no longer seen. Likewise the Soul, freed from the body, can no longer be seen.

description: The Soul and the three Gunas
sn: यथा चन्द्रो ह्यमावास्यां नक्षत्रैर्युज्यते गतः। तद्वच्छरीरनिर्मुक्तः फलैर्युज्यति कर्मणः॥
en: Then again, as the moon, even when it disappears on the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight, is not left by the constellations and the stars, the Soul also, even though separated from the body, is not deserted by the fruits of the acts it has won in that body.

sn: मनुरुवाच यथा व्यक्तमिदं शेते स्वप्ने चरति चेतनम्। ज्ञानमिन्द्रियसंयुक्तं तद्वत् प्रेत्य भवाभवौ॥
en: As in a dream this body (inactive) and the enlivening spirit in its subtile form, separating itself from the former, walks forth, so, in the state called deep sleep (or death), the subtile forin with all the senses becomes inactive, and the Understanding, separated from it, remains awake. The same is the case with Existence and Non-Existence.

sn: यथाम्भसि प्रसन्ने तु रूपं पश्यति चक्षुषा। तद्वत्प्रसन्नेन्द्रियत्वाज्ज्ञेयं ज्ञानेन पश्यति॥
en: As when a sheet of water is clear, images reflected in it can be seen by the eye, similarly, if the senses be undisturbed, the Soul is capable of being seen by the understanding.

sn: स एव लुलिते तस्मिन् यथा रूपं न पश्यति। तथेन्द्रियाकुलीभावे ज्ञेयं ज्ञाने न पश्यति॥
en: If, however, the piece of water is agitated, the person standing by it can no longer sce those images. Likewise, if the senses become disturbed, the Soul can no longer be seen by the understanding.

sn: अबुद्धिरज्ञानकृता अबुद्ध्या कृष्यते मनः। दुष्टस्य मनसः पञ्च सम्प्रदुष्यन्ति मानसाः॥
en: Ignorance produces Delusion. Delusion possesses the mind. When the mind becomes impure, the five senses which have the mind for their refuge becomed corrupted also.

sn: अज्ञानतृप्तो विषयेष्ववगाढो न तृप्यते। अदृष्टवच्च भूतात्मा विषयेभ्यो निवर्तते॥
en: Overfilled with Ignorance, and sunk in their mire of worldly objects, one cannot enjoy the sweets of contentment or tranquillity. The Soul with its good and evil acts, returns again and again to the objects of the world.

sn: तर्षच्छेदो न भवति पुरुषस्येह कल्मषात्। निवर्तते तदा तर्षः पापमन्तगतं यदा॥
en: On account of sin one's thirst is never satisfied. One's thirst is then satisfied when one's sin is dissipated.

sn: विषयेषु तु संसर्गाच्छाश्वतस्य तु संश्रयात्। मनसा चान्यथा काङ्क्षन् परं 7 प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: On account of attachment to earthly objects, which has a tendency, to multiply itself, one wishes for things other than those for which one should wish, and accordingly fails to attain to the Supreme.

sn: ज्ञानमुत्पद्यते पुंसां क्षयात् पापस्य कर्मणः। यथाऽऽदर्शतले प्रख्ये पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि॥
en: From the destruction of all sinful acts, knowledge originates in When Knowledge arises a person sees his Soul in his understanding even as one sees his own image in a polished mirror. men.

sn: प्रसृतैरिन्द्रियैर्दुःखी तैरेव नियतैः सुखी। तस्मादिन्द्रियरूपेभ्यो यच्छेदात्मानमात्मना॥
en: One reaps misery for his senses being not controlled. One acquires happiness on account of his senses being restrained. Therefore, a person should control his mind by self-exertion from objects apprehended by the senses.

sn: इन्द्रियेभ्यो मनः पूर्वं बुद्धिः परतरा ततः। बुद्धेः परतरं ज्ञानं ज्ञानात् परतरं महत्॥
en: Above the senses is the mind; above the mind is the understanding; above the understanding is the Soul; above the Soul is the Supreme.

sn: अव्यक्तात् प्रसृतं ज्ञानं ततो बुद्धिस्ततो मनः। मनः श्रोत्रादिभिर्युक्तं शब्दादीन् साधु पश्यति॥
en: From the Unmanifest originates the Soul; from the Soul has originated the understanding; from the understanding has' originated the mind. When the mind is united with the senses, than it apprehends sound and the other objects of the senses.

sn: यस्तांस्त्यजति शब्दादीन् सर्वाश्च व्यक्तस्तथा। विमुञ्चत् प्राकृतान्ग्रामांस्तान् मुक्त्वामृतमश्नुते॥
en: He who renounces those objects as well as all those that are manifest, he who liberates himself from all things that arise from primordial matter, enjoys immortality.

sn: उद्यन् हि सविता यद्वत्सृजते रश्मिमण्डलम्। स एवास्तमपागच्छंस्तदेवात्मनि यच्छति॥
en: The Sun rising spreads his rays. When he sets, he withdraws to himself those very rays that were spread by him.

sn: अन्तरात्मा तथा देहमाविश्येन्द्रियरश्मिभिः। प्राप्येन्द्रियगुणान् पञ्च सोऽस्तमावृत्य गच्छति॥
en: Similarly, the Soul, entering the body, obtains the fivefold objects of the senses by spreading over them his rays represented by the senses. When, however, he turns back, he is said to set by withdrawing those rays to himself.

sn: प्रणीतं कर्मणा मार्ग नीयमानः पुनः पुनः। प्राप्नोत्ययं कर्मफलं प्रवृत्तं धर्ममाप्तवान्॥
en: Continually driven along the path that is created by acts, he reaps the fruit of his acts for his having followed the practice of acts.

sn: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः। रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते॥
en: Desire for the object of the senses does not affect a person who has no such desire. Desire, leaves him who has seen his soul, which, of course, is entirely free from desire.

sn: बुद्धिः कर्मगुणैींना यदा मनसि वर्तते। तदा सम्पद्यते ब्रह्म तत्रैव प्रलयं गतम्॥
en: When the Understanding, shorn of the attachment to the objects of the senses, is concentrated in the mind, then does one succeed in attaining to Brahma, for it is there that the mind with with the understanding withdrawn into it can possibly be destroyed.

sn: अस्पर्शनम शृण्वानमनास्वादमदर्शनम्। अघ्राणमवितर्कं च सत्त्वं प्रविशते परम्॥
en: Brahma is not an object of touch or of hearing, or of taste, or of sight, or of smell, or of any other inference. Only the Understanding can get it.

sn: मनस्याकृतयो मग्ना मनस्त्वभिगतं मतिम्। मतिस्त्वभिगता ज्ञानं ज्ञानं चाभिगतं परम्॥
en: All objects that the mind apprehends through the senses can be withdrawn into the mind; the mind can be withdrawn into the understanding; the Understanding can be withdrawn into the Soul, and the Soul into the Supreme.

sn: नेन्द्रियैर्मनसः सिद्धिर्न बुद्धिं बुद्ध्यते मनः। न बुद्धिर्बुद्ध्यतेऽव्यक्तं सूक्ष्मं त्वेतानि पश्यति॥
en: The senses cannot lead to the success of the mind. The mind cannot apprehend the Understanding. The Understanding cannot apprehend the manifested Soul. The Soul, however, which is subtile, sees these all.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: मनुरुवाच दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते। यस्मिन् न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तं नानुचिन्तयेत्॥
en: When physical and mental sorrow, appear one cannot practise Yoga. Therefore, one should not brood over such sorrow.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: भैषज्यमेतद् दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत्। चिन्त्यमानं हि चाभ्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्तते॥
en: The inedicine for sorrow is abstention from brooding over it. When sorrow is brooded over, it becomes multiplicd.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः। एतद् विज्ञानसामर्थ्यं न बालैः समतामियात्॥
en: One should remove mental sorrow by wisdom, and physical sorrow should be cured by medicines. Wisdom teaches this. One should not, while under sorrow, act like a child.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: अनित्यं यौवनं रूपं जीवितं द्रव्यसंचयः। आरोग्यं प्रियसंवासो गृध्येत् तत्र न पण्डितः॥
en: A wise man should never hanker after youth, beauty, longevity, accumulation of riches, health, and the companionship of those that are dear, all of which are transitory.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: न जानपदिकं दुःखमेकः शोचितुमर्हति। अशोचन् प्रतिकुर्वीत यदि पश्येदुपक्रमम्॥
en: One should not only grieve for a sorrow that affects a whole community. Without grieving, should, if he finds opportunity, seek to use a remedy.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: सुखाद् बहुतरं दुःखं जीविते नास्ति संशयः। स्निग्धस्य चेन्द्रियार्थेषु मोहान्मरणमप्रियम्।।६
en: Forsooth, sorrow is much greater than happiness in life. Death which is disagreeable comes for his stupefaction to one who is content with the object of the senses. one an

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: परित्यजति यो दुःखं सुखं वाप्युभयं नरः। अभ्येति ब्रह्म सोऽत्यन्तं न ते शोचन्ति पण्डिताः॥
en: That man who avoids both sorrow and happiness attain to Brahma. Such wise persons have never to grieve.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: दुःखमर्था हि युज्यन्ते पालनेन च ते सुखम्। दुःखेन चाधिगम्यन्ते नाशमेषां न चिन्तयेत्॥
en: Worldly belongings beget sorrow. In protecting them one can enjoy no happiness. They are again acquired with misery. One should not, therefore, mind their loss.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयाभिनिवृत्तं विद्धि ज्ञानगुणं मनः। प्रज्ञाकरणसंयुक्तं ततो बुद्धिः प्रवर्तते॥
en: Pure Knowledge, exists in the various objects of knowledge. Know that mind is only an attribute of Knowledge. When the mind is united with the faculties of knowledge, then the understanding sets in.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: यदा कर्मगुणैर्हीना बुद्धिर्मनसि वर्तते। तदा प्रज्ञायते ब्रह्म ध्यानयोगसमाधिना॥
en: When freed from the attributes of action, the understanding is directed towards the mind; then does it succeed in knowing Brahma by meditation or Yoga ending in complete absorption (Samadhi).

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: सेयं गुणवती बुद्धिर्गुणेष्वेवाभिवर्तते। अपरादभिनिःसृत्य गिरेः शृङ्गादिवोदकम्॥
en: The Understanding, originating from Ignorance, and endued with the senses and attributes, runs towards external objects, like a river originating from a mountain summit and flowing towards other quarters.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: यदा निर्गुणमानोति ध्यानं मनसि पूर्वजम्। तदा प्रज्ञायते ब्रह्म निकषं निकषे यथा॥
en: When the understanding, with-drawn into the mind, succeeds in absorbing itself into contemplation that is shorn of attributes, it acquires a knowledge of Brahma like the touch of gold on a touch-stone.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: मनस्त्वपहृतं पूर्वमिन्द्रियार्थनिदर्शकम्। न समक्षगुणापेक्षि निर्गुणस्य निदर्शकम्॥
en: The mind apprehends the objects of the senses. It must first be extinguished. Depend upon the attributes of objects that are before it, the mind can never show that which is without attributes.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: सर्वाण्येतानि संवार्य द्वाराणि मनसि स्थितः। मनस्येकाग्रतां कृत्वा तत्परं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Closing all the doors formed by the senses the Understanding should be with-drawn into the mind. In this condition when absorbed in contemplation, it acquires the knowledge of Brahma.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: यथा महान्ति भूतानि निवर्तन्ते गुणक्षये। तथेन्द्रियाण्युपादाय बुद्धिर्मनसि वर्तते॥
en: As upon the destruction of the attributes by which they are known, the fivefold great creatures are contracted into their subtile forms, so the Understanding may dwell in the mind alone, with the senses all withdrawn from their objects.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: यदा मनसि सा बुद्धिवर्ततेऽन्तरचारिणी। व्यवसायगुणोपेता तदा सम्पद्यते मनः॥
en: When the Understanding, though endued with the quality of certainty, lives in the mind, busied with the internal, even then it is nothing but the mind.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: गुणवद्भिर्गुणोपेतं यदा ध्यानगुणं मनः। सदा सर्वान् गुणान् हित्वा निर्गुणं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: When the mind of consciousness, which attains to perfection through contemplation, succeeds in identifying qualities with their possessors, then can it cast off all attributes and attain to Brahma which is without qualities.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: अव्यक्तस्येह विज्ञाने नास्ति तुल्यं निदर्शनम्। यत्र नास्ति पदन्यासः कस्तं विषयमाप्नुयात्॥
en: There is no indication that which can give a knowledge of the Unseen. That which cannot be described in language, cannot be acquired by anyone.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: तपसा चानुमानेन गुणैर्जात्या श्रुतेन च। निनीषेत् परमं ब्रह्म विशुद्धनान्तरात्मना॥
en: With purified soul, one should try to approach the Supreme Brahma, through the help afforded by penances, by inferences, by self-control, by the practices and observances sanctioned for one's own order, and by the Vedas.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: गुणहीनो हि तं माग बहिः समनुवर्तते। गुणाभावात् प्रकृत्या वा निस्तयं ज्ञेयसम्मितम्॥
en: Persons of clear vision seek him in even external forms by freeing themselves from qualities. The Supreme, which is called by the name of what should be known, on account of the absence of all qualities, or of its own nature, can never be apprehended by argument.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: नैर्गुण्याद् ब्रह्म चाप्नोति सगुणत्वानिवर्तते। गुणप्रचारिणी बुद्धि ताशन इवेन्धने॥
en: When the Understanding becomes freed from qualities, then only can it attain to Brahma. When it is endued with qualities, it falls back from the Supreme. Indeed, such is the nature of the understanding that it rushes towards qualities and moves among them like fire among fuel.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: यथा पञ्च विमुक्तानि इन्द्रियाणि स्वकर्मभिः। तथा हि परमं ब्रह्म विमुक्तं प्रकृतेः परम्॥
en: As in the state of deep and dreamless sleep the five senses exist freed from their respective works, similarly the Supreme Brahma exists high above Prakriti, freed from all its qualities.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: एवं प्रकृतितः सर्वे प्रवर्तन्ते शरीरिणः। निवर्तन्ते निवृत्तौ च स्वर्गं चैवोपयान्ति च॥
en: Embodied creatures perform various actions on account of attributes. When they abstain therefrom, they acquire liberation. Some again go to heaven.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: पुरुषः प्रकृतिर्बुद्धिविषयाश्चेन्द्रियाणि च। अहंकारोऽभिमानश्च समूहो भूतसंज्ञकः॥
en: The living creature, primordial nature, the understanding, the objects of the senses, the senses, consciousness, consciousness of Ego, are called creatures.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: एतस्याद्या प्रवृत्तिस्तु प्रधानात् सम्प्रवर्तते। द्वितीया मिथुनव्यक्तिमविशेषान्नियच्छति॥
en: The original creation of all these proceeded from the Supreme. Their second creation is due to the union of couples or pairs and is confined to all things except the principal five, and is governed by law for which the same species produce the same species.

description: Worthlessness of physical and mental sorrow. he value of wisdom
sn: धर्मादुत्कृष्यते श्रेयस्तथाश्रेयोऽप्यधर्मतः। रागवान् प्रकृति ह्येति विरक्तो ज्ञानवान् भवेत्॥
en: From righteousness creatures obtain a great end, and from sinfulness they earn a low end. He who is not freed from attachments, goes through rebirth; while he who is freed therefrom, attains to Knowledge (or Brahma).

sn: मनुरुवाच यदा तैः पञ्चभिः पञ्च युक्तानि मनसा सह। अथ तद् रक्ष्यते ब्रह्म मणौ सूत्रमिवापितम्॥
en: Manu said When the five attributes are united with the five senses and the mind, then is Brahma seen by the individual like a thread passing through a gem.

sn: तदेव च यथा सूत्रं सुवर्णे वर्तते पुनः। मुक्तास्वथ प्रवालेषु मृन्मये राजते तथा॥ तद्वद् गोऽश्वमनुष्येषु तद्वद्धस्तिमृगादिषु। तद्वत् कीटपतङ्गेषु प्रसक्तात्मा स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: As a thread may lie within gold or a pearl or a coral or any earthen object, so one's soul, for his own acts, may live within a cow, a horse, a man, an elephant or any other animal, or with a worm or an insect.

sn: येन येन शरीरेण यद्यत्कर्म करोत्ययम्। तेन तेन शरीरेण तत् तत् फलमुपाश्नुते॥
en: The good deeds with a person performs in a particular body yield rewards that the individual enjoys in that particular body.

sn: यथा ह्येकरसा भूमिरोषध्यर्थानुसारिणी। तथा कर्मानुगा बुद्धिरन्तरात्मानुदर्शिनी॥
en: A soil, seemingly drenched with one particular kind of liquid, supplies to each different sort of Herb or plant that grows on it the sort of juice it requires for itself. Similarly, the Understanding, whose course is witnessed by the Soul, is obliged to follow the path marked out by pristine deeds.

sn: ज्ञानपूर्वा भवेल्लिप्सा लिप्सापूर्वाभिसंधिता। अभिसधिपूर्वकं कर्म कर्ममूलं ततः फलम्॥
en: From knowledge originates desire. From desire originates resolution. From resolution proceeds action. From action proceed fruits.

sn: फलं कर्मात्मकं विद्यात् कर्म ज्ञेयात्मकं तथा। ज्ञेयं ज्ञानात्मकं विद्याजानं सदसदात्मकम्॥
en: Fruits, therefore, have actions as their cause. Actions have the understanding for their root. The understanding has knowledge for its ot, and knowledge has the Soul for its cause.

sn: ज्ञानानां च फलानां च ज्ञेयानां कर्मणां तथा। क्षयान्ते यत् फलं विद्याज्ज्ञानं ज्ञेयप्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: That excellent outcome which is gained by the destruction of knowledge, of fruits, of the understanding, and of acts is called knowledge of Brahma.

sn: महद्धि परमं भूतं यत् प्रपश्यन्ति योगिनः। अबुधास्तं न पश्यन्ति ह्यात्मस्थं गुणबुद्धयः॥
en: High indeed is that self-existent Essence which Yogins witness. They who are devoid of wisdom, and whose understandings are addicted to worldly objects never see that which exists in the soul itself.

sn: पृथिवीरूपतो रूपमपामिह महत्तरम्। अद्भयो महत्तरं तेजस्तेजसः पवनो महान्॥
en: Water is superior to the Earth; Light is superior to Water; Wind is superior to Light.

sn: पवनाच्च महद् व्योम तस्मात् परतरं मनः। मनसो महती बुद्धिर्बुद्धेः कालो महान् स्मृतः॥
en: Space is superior to Wind; Mind is superior 10 Space; Understanding is superior to Mind; Time is superior to Understanding.

sn: कालात् स भगवान् विष्णुर्यस्य सर्वमिदं जगत्। नादिर्न मध्यं नैवान्तस्तस्य देवस्य विद्यते॥
en: The Divine Vishnu, who is identical with this universe, is superior to Time. That god is without beginning, middle, and end.

sn: अनादित्वादमध्यत्वादनन्तत्वाच्च सोऽव्ययः। अत्येति सर्वदुःखानि दुःखं ह्यन्तवदुच्यते॥
en: For his being without beginning, iniddle, and cnd, he is Unchangeable. He is above all Sorrow, for Sorrow has limits.

sn: तद् ब्रह्म परमं प्रोक्तं तद्धाम परमं पदम्। तद् गत्वा कालविषयाद् विमुक्ता मोक्षमाश्रिताः॥
en: That Vishnu is called the Supreme Brahma. He is the refuge or object of what is called the Highest. Knowing Him, they who are wise, freed from everything which is under the influence of Time, acquire liberation.

sn: गुणेष्वेते प्रकाशन्ते निर्गुणत्वात् ततः परम्। निवृत्तिलक्षणो धर्मस्तथाऽऽनन्त्याय कल्पते॥
en: What we perceive is displayed in attributes. That which is called Brahma, being without attributes, is superior to these. Abstention from acts constitutes the greatest religion. That religion is sure to bring on deathlessness.

sn: ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि शरीराणि व्यपाश्रिताः। जिह्वाग्रेषु प्रवर्तन्ते यत्नसाध्या विनाशिनः॥
en: The Richs, the yajuses and the Samans depend on the body. They flow from the end of the tongue. They cannot be acquired without exertion and are subject to destruction.

sn: न चैवमिष्यते ब्रह्म शरीराश्रयसम्भवम्। न यत्नसाध्यं तद् ब्रह्म नादिमध्यं न चान्तवत्॥ ।
en: Brahma, however, cannot be acquired in this way, for it depends upon that (Soul) which has the body for its refuge. Without beginning, middle, or end, Brahma cannot be acquired by effort.

sn: ऋचामादिस्तथा साम्नां यजुषामादिरुच्यते। अन्तश्चादिमतां दृष्टो न त्वादिब्रह्मणः स्मृतः॥
en: The Richs, the Samans, the Yajuses, have each a beginning. Those that have a beginning have also an end. But Brahma is said to be without beginning.

sn: अनादिन्वादनन्तत्वात्तदन्तमथाव्ययम्। अव्ययत्वाच्च निर्दुःखं द्वन्द्वाभावस्ततः परम्॥
en: And because Brahma has neither beginning nor end, it is said to be infinite and unchangeable. On account of unchangeableness, Brahma transcends all sorrow as also pairs of opposites.

sn: अदृष्टतोऽनुपायाच्च प्रतिसंधेश्च कर्मणः। न तेन माः पश्यन्ति येन गच्छन्ति तत् पदम्॥
en: Through unfavourable destiny, through inability to find out the proper expedient, and through the obstacles put in by acts, men cannot see the path by which Brahına may be reached.

sn: विषयेषु च संसर्गाच्छाश्वतस्य च दर्शनात्। मनसा चान्यदाकाङ्क्षन् परं न प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: On account of attachment to worldly objects, in view of the joys of the highest heaven, and for seeking something other than Brahma, men do not attain to the Supremc.

sn: गुणान् यदिह पश्यन्ति तदिच्छन्त्यपरे जनाः। परं नैवाभिकाङ्क्षन्ति निर्गुणत्वाद् गुणार्थिनः॥
en: Others seeing worldly objects seek their possession. When they hanker after such objects, they do not see Brahma inasmuch as it is shorn of all attributes.

sn: गुणैर्यस्त्ववरैर्युक्तः कथं विद्यात् परान् गुणान्। अनुमानाद्धि गन्तव्यं गुणैरवयवैः परम्॥
en: How can one who is endued with inferior qualities, acquire a knowledge of him who is possessed of superior qualities? It is by inference that one can arrive at a knowledge of Him who transcends all things in attributes and form.

sn: सूक्ष्मेण मनसा विद्यो वाचा वक्तुं न शक्नुमः। मनो हि मनसा ग्राह्यं दर्शनेन च दर्शनम्॥
en: We can know him only. By subtile intelligence, we cannot describe Him in words. The mind is caught by the mind, the eye by the eye.

sn: ज्ञानेन निर्मलीकृत्य बुद्धिं बुद्ध्या मनस्तथा। मनसा चेन्द्रियग्राममक्षरं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: By knowledge the understanding can be purged off of its impurities The understanding may be engaged for purifying the mind. The senses should be restrained by the mind. Performing all this, one may attain to the Unchangeable.

sn: बुद्धिप्रवीणो मनसा समृद्धो निराशिषं निर्गुणमभ्युपैति। परं त्यजन्तीह विलोड्यमाना हुताशनं वायुरिवेन्धनस्थम्॥
en: One who has, by contemplation, become freed from attachments, and who has the wealth of a discerning mind, succeeds in attaining to Brahma which is without desire and above all attributes. As the wind does not touch the fire that lies within a piece of wood, so persons, who are moved (by desire for worldly objects stand aloof from that which is Supreme).

sn: गुणादाने विप्रयोगे च तेषां मनः सदा बुद्धिपरावराभ्याम्। अनेनैव विधिना सम्प्रवृत्तो गुणापाये ब्रह्म शरीर मेति॥
en: When all earthly objects are destroyed, the mind always attains to That which is higher than the Understanding; while upon their separation the mind always acquires that which is below the Understanding. Therefore, a person, who, according to the method already described, becomes engaged in destroying carthly objects, becomes immersed in Brahma.

sn: अव्यक्तात्मा पुरुषो व्यक्तकर्मा सोऽव्यक्तत्वं गच्छति दन्तकाले। ग्लायद्भिर्वाऽऽवर्ततेऽकामरूपः॥
en: Though the Soul is unmanifest, yet when endued with qualities, its acts become manifest. When dissolution sets in it once more becomes unmanifest. The Soul is really inactive. Its exists, endued with the senses which create either happiness or misery.

sn: सर्वैरयं चेन्द्रियैः सम्प्रयुक्तो देहं प्राप्तः पञ्चभूताश्रयः स्यात्। नासामर्थ्याद् गच्छति कर्मणेह हीनस्तेन परमेणाव्ययेन॥
en: United with all the senses and body, it takes refuge in the five primal elements. It cannot, however, act through want of power, however, when it is deprived of force by the Supreme and Unchangeable.

sn: पृथ्व्यां नरः पश्यति नान्तमस्या ह्यन्तश्चास्या भविता चेति विद्धि। परं नयन्तीह विलोड्यमानं यथा प्लवं वायुरिवार्णवस्थम्॥
en: No man sees the end of this earth, but know this, viz., that the Earth's end will surely come. Man moved here (by attachments) is surely led to his last resort like the wind leading a vessel, tossed on the sea to a safe harbour at last.

sn: दिवाकरो गुणमुपलभ्य निर्गुणो यथा भवेदपगतरश्मिमण्डलः। तथा ह्यसौ मुनिरिह निर्विशेषवान् स निर्गुणं प्रविशति ब्रह्म चाव्ययम्॥
en: Diffusing his rays the sun becomes the possessor of an attribute, withdrawing his rays he once more becomes an object shorn of attributes, Similarly a person casting off all distinctions and practising penances, at last enters the indestructible Brahma which is shorn of all attributes.

sn: अनागतं सुकृतवतां परां गति स्वयम्भुवं प्रभवनिधानमव्ययम्। सनातनं यदमृतमव्ययं ध्रुवं निचाय्य तत् परममृतत्वमश्नुते॥
en: By knowing Him who is without birth, who is the highest refuge of all pious men, who is self-create, from whom everything originates and whom everything returns, who is unchangeable, who is without beginning, middle, and end, and who is self and supreme, a person attains to immortality.'

sn: अनागतं सुकृतवतां परां गति स्वयम्भुवं प्रभवनिधानमव्ययम्। सनातनं यदमृतमव्ययं ध्रुवं निचाय्य तत् परममृतत्वमश्नुते॥
en: By knowing Him who is without birth, who is the highest refuge of all pious men, who is self-create, from whom everything originates and whom everything returns, who is unchangeable, who is without beginning, middle, and end, and who is self and supreme, a person attains to immortality.'

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामह महाप्राज्ञ पुण्डरीकाक्षमच्युतम्। कर्तारमकृतं विष्णुं भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययम्॥ नारायणं हृषीकेशं गोविन्दमपराजितम्। तत्त्वेन भरतश्रेष्ठ श्रोतुमिच्छामि केशवम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O you of great wisdom, I wish to hear fully, O chief of the Bharatas, of that lotus-eyed and indestructible one, who is the Crcator of all but who has been created by none, who is called Vishnu, who is the origin of all creatures and to whom all creatures return, who is known by the names of Narayana and Hrishikesha and Govinda and Keshava, and who is incapable of being defeated by any one.

sn: भीष्म उवाच श्रुतोऽयमर्थो रामस्य जामदग्न्यस्य जल्पतः। नारदस्य च देवर्षेः कृष्णद्वैपायनस्य च॥
en: Bhishma said I have heard of this subject from Jamadagni's son Rama while he described it from the celestial saint Narada and from Krishna-Dvaipayana. to

sn: असितो देवलस्तात वाल्मीकिश्च महातपाः। मार्कण्डेयश्च गोविन्दे कथयन्त्यद्भुतं महत्॥
en: Asita-Devala, O son, Valmiki of austere penances and Markandeya, describe Govinda as the most Wonderful and the Supreme.

sn: केशवो भरतश्रेष्ठ भगवानीश्वरः प्रभुः। पुरुषः सर्वमित्येव श्रूयते बहुधा विभुः॥
en: Keshava, O chief of Bharata's race, is the divine and powerful Lord of all. He is called Purusha, and is present in everything, having multiplied himself.

sn: किं तु यानि विदुर्लोके ब्राह्मणा: शार्ङ्गधन्वनि। माहात्म्यानि महाबाहो शृणु तानि युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Listen now, O Yudhisthira of powerful arms, those attributes which great Brahmanas say are to be seen in the great wielder of Sharnga.

sn: यानि चाहुर्मनुष्येन्द्र ये पुराणविदो जनाः। कर्माणि त्विह गोविन्दे कीर्तयिष्यामि तान्यहम्॥
en: I shall also, O king recite to you those acts which persons well-read in old histories attribute to Govinda.

sn: महाभूतानि भूतात्मा महात्मा पुरुषोत्तमः। वायुयॊतिस्तथा चापः खं च गां चान्वकल्पयत्॥
en: He is the soul of all creatures, the great one, and the foremost of all beings. He crealed (by his will) the five elements viz., Wind, Light, Water, Space and Earth.

sn: स सृष्ट्वा पृथिवीं चैव सर्वभूतेश्वरः प्रभुः। अप्स्वेव भवनं चक्रे महात्मा पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: Having created the Earth that powerful Lord of all things, that great one, that foremost of all beings, lay on the surface of the waters.

sn: सर्वतेजोमयस्तस्मिशयानः पुरुषोत्तमः। सोऽग्रजं सर्वभूतानां संकर्षणमकल्पयत्॥
en: While thus floating upon the waters, that foremost of all beings, that resort of every sort of energy and splendour, created consciousness, the first-born of all beings in the universe.

sn: आश्रयं सर्वभूतानां मनसेतीह शुश्रुम। स धारयति भूतानि उभे भूतभविष्यती॥
en: We have heard that He created consciousness with the mind,-Consciousness which is the resort of all created things. That Consciousness maintains all creatures and both the past and the future.

sn: ततस्तस्मिन् महाबाहौ प्रादुर्भूते महात्मनि। भास्करप्रतिमं दिव्यं नाभ्यां पद्ममजायत॥
en: After that great Being. O mighty-armed one, viz., Consciousness originated a highly beautiful lotus effulgent like the Sun out of the navel of the Supreme Being.

sn: स तत्र भगवान देवः पुष्करे भ्राजयन् दिशः। ब्रह्मा समभवत् तात् सर्वभूतपितामहः॥
en: Then, O son the illustrious and divine Brahman, the Grandfather of all creatures, came into being from that lotus, lighting all the points of the horizon with his effulgence.

sn: तस्मिन्नपि महाबाहौ प्रादुर्भूते महात्मनि। तमसा पूर्वजो जज्ञे मधुर्नाम महासुरः॥
en: After the high-souled Grandfather had, O mighty-armed one, thus originated from the primeval lotus, a great Asura of the name of Madhu, having no beginning, came into being from the quality of ignorance, (Tamas).

sn: तमुग्रमुग्रकर्माणमुग्रं कर्म समास्थितम्। ब्रह्मणोपचितिं कुर्वन् जघान पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: The foremost of all Beings for helping Brahman, killed that dreadful Asura of terrific deeds, engaged even then in the fearful act of killing the Grandfather.

sn: तस्य तात वधात् सर्वे देवदानवमानवाः। मधुसूदनमित्याहुर्ऋषभं सर्वसात्वताम्॥
en: For slaying this demon, O son, all the gods and the Danavas and men called that foremost of all righteous person by the name of Madhusudana (slayer of Madhu).

sn: ब्रह्मानुससृजे पुत्रान् मानसान् दक्षसप्तमान्। मरीचिमत्र्यङ्गिरसं पुलस्त्यं पुलहं क्रतुम्॥
en: After this, Brahman, created, by his will, seven sons with Daksha at their head. They were Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu.

sn: मरीचिः कश्यपं तात पुत्रमग्रजमग्रजः। मानसं जनयामास तैजसं ब्रह्मवित्तमम्॥
en: The eldest born, viz., Marichi, beget, by his will, a son named Kashyapa, highly energetic and the foremost of all person conversant with Brahma.

sn: अङ्गुष्ठात् ससृजे ब्रह्मा मरीचेरपि पूर्वजम्। सोऽभवद् भरतश्रेष्ठ दक्षो नाम प्रजापतिः॥
en: From his toe, Brahmana had, even before the birth of Marichi, created a son. That son, O Bharata's chief, was Daksha, the progenitor of creatures.

sn: तस्य पूर्वमजायन्त दश तिस्रश्च भारत। प्रजापतेर्दुहितरस्तासां ज्येष्ठाभवद् दितिः॥
en: Daksha begot thirteen daughters, 0 Bharata, the eldest of whom was called Diti.

sn: सर्वधर्मविशेषज्ञः पुण्यकीर्तिर्महायशाः। मारीचः कश्यपस्तात सर्वासामभवत् पतिः॥
en: Marichi's son Kashyapa, O son, who was a master of duties and their distinctions, who was of righteous deeds and great fame, espoused them.

sn: उत्पाद्य तु महाभागस्तासामवरजा दश। ददौ धर्माय धर्मज्ञो दक्ष एव प्रजापतिः॥
en: The highly blessed Daksha next beget ten other daughters. That progenitor of creatures, viz., the righteous Daksha, conferred these upon Dharma.

sn: धर्मस्य वसवः पुत्रा रुद्राश्चामिततेजसः। विश्वेदेवाश्च साध्याश्च मरुत्वन्तश्च भारत॥
en: Dharma became father of the Vasus, the highly energetic Rudras the Vishvedevas, the Saddhyas, and the Maruts, O Bharata.

sn: अपराश्च यवीयस्यस्ताभ्योऽन्याः सप्तविंशतिः। सोमस्तासां महाभागः सर्वासामभवत् पतिः॥
en: Daksha next beget twenty-seven other younger daughters. The highly blessed Soma espoused them all.

sn: इतरास्तु व्यजायन्त गन्धर्वांस्तुरगान् द्विजान्। गाश्च किंपुरुषान्मत्स्यानुद्भिज्जांश्च वनस्पतीन्॥
en: The other wives of Kashyapa gave births to Gandharvas, horses, birds, kine, Kimpurushas, fishes, and trees and plants.

sn: आदित्यानदितिर्जज्ञे देवश्रेष्ठान् महाबलान्। तेषा विष्णुर्वामनोऽभूद् गोविन्दश्चाभवत् प्रभुः॥
en: Aditi gave birth to the Adityas, the foremost ones among the gods, and highly powerful. Amongst them Vishnu was born in the form of a dwarf. Otherwise called Govinda, he became the foremost of them all.

sn: तस्य विक्रमणाच्चापि देवानां श्रीळवर्धत। दानवाश्च पराभूता दैतेयी चासुरी प्रजा॥
en: By his power the prosperity of the gods increased. The Danavas were defeated. The children of Diti were the Asuras.

sn: विप्रचित्तिप्रधानांश्च दानवानसृजद् दनुः। दितिस्तु सर्वानसुरान् महासत्त्वानजीजनत्॥
en: Danu gave birth to the Danavas having Viprachitti as their head. Diti gave birth to all the powerful Asuras.

sn: अहोरात्रं च कालं च यथर्तु मधुसूदनः। पूर्वाह्न चापराह्नं च सर्वमेवानुकल्पयत्॥
en: The destroyer of Madhu also created the Day and the Night, and the Seasons in their order, and the Morning and the Evening.

sn: प्रध्याय सोऽसृजन्मेघांस्तथा स्थावरजङ्गमान्। पृथिवीं सोऽसृजद् विश्वां सहितां भूरितेजसा॥
en: After meditation he also created the clouds, and all the immobile and mobile objects. Highly energetic he also created the Vishvas and the Earth with all things upon her.

sn: ततः कृष्णो महाभागः पुनरेव युधिष्ठिर। ब्राह्मणानां शतं श्रेष्ठं मुखादेवासृजत् प्रभुः॥
en: Then the highest used and powerful Krishna, O Yudhishthira, once again created from his mouth one hundred foremost Brahmans.

sn: बाहुभ्यां क्षत्रियशतं वैश्यामानामूरुतः शतम्। पद्भ्यां शूद्रशतं चैव केशवो भरतर्षभ॥
en: From his two arms, he created one hundred Kshatriyas, and from his thighs one hundred. Vaishyas. Then, O foremost of Bharata's racc, Keshava created from his two feet one hundred Shudras.

sn: स एवं चतुरो वर्णान् समुत्पाद्य महातपाः। अध्यक्षं सर्वभूतानां धातारमकरोत् स्वयम्॥
en: Endued with great ascetic merit, the destroyer of Madhu, having thus created the four orders of men, made (Dhatri Brahman) the master and ruler of all created beings.

sn: वेदविद्याविधातारं ब्रह्माणममितद्युतिम्। भूतमातृगणाध्यक्षं विरूपाक्षं च सोऽसृजत्॥
en: Of incomparable effulgence, Brahman became also the exponent of the Vedic lore. And Keshava made himn called Virupaksha, the ruler of the spirits and ghosts and of those females called the Matrikas (mothers).

sn: शासितारं च पापानां पितृणां समवर्तिनम्। असृजत् सर्वभूतात्मा निधिपं च धनेश्वरम्॥
en: And he made Yama the ruler of the departed manes of all sinful men. The Supreme Soul of ail creatures also made Kuvera the lord of all riches.

sn: यादसामसृजन्नाथं वरुणं च जलेश्वरम्। वासवं सर्वदेवानामध्यक्षमकरोत् प्रभुः॥
en: He then created Varuna the lord of waters and governor of all acquatic animals. The powerful Vishnu made Vasava the king of all celestials.

sn: यावद्यावदभूच्छ्रद्धा देहं धारयितुं नृणाम्। तावत् तावदजीवंस्ते नासीद् यमकृतं भयम्॥
en: In those times, men lived as long as they chose to live, and had no fear of Yama.

sn: न चैषां मैथुनो धर्मो बभूव भरतर्षभ। संकल्पादेव चैतेषामपत्यमुपपद्यते॥
en: Sexual intercourse, O chief of the Bharatas, was then not necessary for perpetuating the race. In those days, offspring were begotten by the will.

sn: ततस्त्रेतायुगे काले संस्पर्शाज्जायते प्रजा। न ह्यभून्मैथुनो धर्मस्तेषामपि जनाधिप॥
en: In the cycle that followed, viz., Treta, children were begotten by touch alone. The people of that cycle even, O king, had no necessity of sexual intercourse.

sn: द्वापरे मैथुनो धर्मः प्रजानामभवन्नृप। तथा कलियुगे राजन् द्वन्द्वमापेदिरे जनाः॥
en: It was in the next cycle, viz., Dvapara, that the practice of sexual intercourse originated, O king, amongmen. In the Kali age, O monarch, men have come to marry and live in pairs.

sn: एष भूतपतिस्तात स्वध्यक्षश्च तथोच्यते। निरपेक्षांश्च कौन्तेय कीर्तयिष्यामि तच्छृणु॥
en: I have now told you of the supreme Lord of all creatures. He is also called the Ruler of all and everything. I shall now, O son of Kunti, describe to you the sinful creatures of the Earth. Listen to me.

sn: दक्षिणापथजन्मानः सर्वे नरवरान्ध्रकाः। गुहाः पुलिन्दाः शबराश्चूचुका मद्रकैः सह॥
en: Those men, O king, are born in the southern region and are called Andhakas, Gushes, Palinodes, Shavers, Chuchukas, Madrakas.

sn: उत्तरापथजन्मानः कीर्तयिष्यामि तानपि। यौनकाम्बोजगान्धारा: किराता बर्बरैः सह॥
en: I shall also name those that are born in the northern region. They are Yaunas, Kambojas, Ghandharas, Kiratas, and Barbbaras.

sn: एते पापकृतस्तात चरन्ति पृथिवीमिमाम्। श्वापाकबलगृध्राणां सधर्माणो नराधिप॥
en: All of them, O son, are sinful, and live on this Earth, acting like Chandalas, ravens and vultures.

sn: नैते कृतयुगे तात चरन्ति पृथिवीमिमाम्। त्रेताप्रभृति वर्धन्ते ते जना भरतर्षभ॥
en: In the Krita cycle, O son, they did not live on Earth. It is from the Treta that they sprang and began to multiply, O chief of Bharata's race.

sn: ततस्तस्मिन् महाघोरे संध्याकाल उपस्थिते। राजानः समसज्जन्त समासाद्येतरेतरम्॥
en: When the terrible period of the junction of Treta and the Dvapara, set in the Kshatriyas, approaching one another, began to fight.

sn: एवमेष कुरुश्रेष्ठ प्रादुर्भूतो महात्मना। एकः कर्ता स कृष्णश्च ज्ञानिनां परमा गतिः। इदमाश्रित्य देवेन्द्रो देवा रुद्रास्तथाश्विनौ।। देवं देवर्षिराचष्ट नारदः सर्वलोकदृक्॥
en: Thus, O chief of Kuru's race, this universe was created by the great Krishna. He is the end of intelligent. That observer of all the worlds, viz., the celestial saint Narada, has said that Krishna is the Supreme God.

sn: नारदोऽप्यथ कृष्णस्य परं मेने नराधिप। शाश्वतत्वं महाबाहो यथावद् भरतर्षभ॥
en: Even Narada, O king, acknowledge the supremacy and eternity of Krishna, O mightyarmed chief of Bharata's race.

sn: एवमेष महाबाहुः केशवः सत्यविक्रमः। अचिन्त्यः पुण्डरीकाक्षो नैष केवलमानुषः॥
en: Thus, O mighty-armed one, is Keshava of unvanquishable prowess. That lotus-eyed one is not a man. He is inconceivable!'

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच के पूर्वमासन् पतयः प्रजानां भरतर्षभ। के चर्षयो महाभागा दिक्षु प्रत्येकशः स्मृताः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Who are the first Patriarch, O foremost of Bharata's race? What highly blessed Rishis are there, and on which quarters do each of them dwell?

sn: भीष्म उवाच श्रूयतां भरतश्रेष्ठ यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। प्रजानां पतयो येऽस्मिन् दिक्षु ये चर्षयः स्मृताः॥
en: 'Hear me, O chief of the Bharatas, about what you ask. I shall tell you who the Patriarchs were and what Rishis are mentioned as living on which points of the horizon.

sn: एकः स्वयम्भूर्भगवानाद्यो ब्रह्मा सनातनः। ब्रह्मणः सप्त व पुत्रा महात्मानः स्वयम्भुवः॥
en: There was at first one Eternal, Divine, and Self-create Brahman. The self-create Brahman begat seven illustrious sons.

sn: मरीचिरत्र्यङ्गिरसौ पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः। वसिष्ठश्च महाभागः सदृशो वै स्वयम्भुवा॥
en: They were Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and the highly blessed Vasistha who was equal to the Self-create himself.

sn: सप्तब्रह्माण इत्येते पुराणे निश्चयं गताः। अत उर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वानेव प्रजापतीन्॥
en: These seven sons have been described in the Puranas as seven Brahmanas. I shall now name the succeeding Patriarchs.

sn: अत्रिवंशसमुत्पन्नो ब्रह्मयोनिः सनातनः। प्राचीनबहिर्भगवांस्तस्मात् प्राचेतसो दश॥
en: In Atri's family was born the eternal and divine Varhi the ancient, born of penances. From Varhi the ancient were born the ten Prachetasas.

sn: दशानां तनयस्त्वेको दक्षो नाम प्रजापतिः। तस्य द्वे नामनी लोके दक्षः क इति चोच्यते॥
en: The ten Prachetasas had one son between them, viz., the Prajapati called by the name of Daksha. This last has two names in the world, viz., Daksha and Ka.

sn: मरीचेः कश्यपः पुत्रस्तस्य द्वे नामनी स्मृते। अरिष्टनेमिरित्येके कश्यपेत्यपरे विदुः॥
en: Marichi had one son called Kashyapa. This last also has two names. Some call him Arishtanemi, and some Kashyapa.

sn: अत्रेश्चैवौरसः श्रीमान् राजा सोमश्च वीर्यवान्। सहस्रं यश्च दिव्यानां युगानां पर्युपासिता॥
en: Atri had another son born of his lions, viz., the handsome and princely Soma of great power. He practised penances for a thousand divine cycles.

sn: अर्यमा चैव भगवान् ये चास्य तनया विभो। एते प्रदेशाः कथिता भुवनानां प्रभावनाः॥
en: The divine Aryaman and his sons, O king, have been described as those who issued injunctions, and as creators of all creatures.

sn: शशबिन्दोश्च भार्याणां सहस्राणि दशाच्युत। एकैकस्यां सहस्रं तु तनयानामभूत् तदा॥ एवं शतसहस्राणां शतं कस्य महात्मनः। पुत्राणां च न ते कंचिदिच्छन्त्यन्यं प्रजापतिम्॥
en: Shashavindu had ten thousand wives. Upon each of them he begat a thousand sons, and thus they were ten thousand in number. Those sons refused to call any body else save themselves as Patriarch.

sn: प्रजामाचक्षते विप्राः पुराणाः शाशबिन्दवीम्। स वृष्णिवंशप्रभवो महावंशः प्रजापतेः॥
en: The ancient Brahmanas bestowed a name on the creatures of the world, derived from Shashavindu. That extensive family of the Patriarch Shashavindu became in time the progenitor of the Vrishni race.

sn: एते प्रजानां पतयः समुद्दिष्टा यशस्विनः। अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि देवांस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरान्॥
en: These that I have named are noted as the illustrious Patriarchs. After this, I shall name the celestials who are the lords of the three worlds.

sn: भर्गोऽशश्चार्यमा चैव मित्रोऽथ वरुणस्तथा। सविता चैव धाता च विवस्वांश्च महाबलः॥
en: Bhaga, Ansha, Aryaman, Mitra, Varuna, Savitri, Dhatri, Vivasvat of great might.

sn: त्वष्टा पूषा तथैवेन्द्रो द्वादशो विष्णुरुच्यते। इत्येते द्वादशादित्याः कश्यपस्यात्मसम्भवाः॥
en: Tashtri, Pushan, Indra, and Vishnu know as the twelfth,-these are the twelve Adityas, all originated from Kashyapa.

sn: नासत्यश्चैव दस्रश्च स्मृतौ द्वावश्विनावपि। मार्तण्डस्यात्मजावेतावष्टमस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Nasatya and Dashra are mentioned as the two Ashvins. These two are the sons of the illustrious Martanda, the eighth in the above.

sn: ते च पूर्वं सुराश्चेति द्विविधाः पितरः स्मृताः। त्वष्टश्चैवात्मजः श्रीमान् विश्वरूपो महायशाः॥ अजैकपादहिर्बुध्न्यो विरूपाक्षोऽथ रैवतः। हरश्च बहुरूपश्च त्र्यम्बकश्च सुरेश्वरः॥ सावित्रश्च जयन्तश्च पिनाकी चापराजितः। पूर्वमेव महाभागा वसवोऽष्टौ प्रकीर्तिताः॥
en: These were called first gods and the two classes of departed manes. Tashtri had many sons. Amongst them were the beautiful and famous Visharupa. Ajaikapat, Ahi, Bradhna, Virupaksha, and Raivata. Then there were Hara and Vahurupa, Tryamyaka the chief of the Deities, and Savitrya, Jayanta and Pinaki the invincible. The highly blessed eight Vasus have formerly been enumerated by me.

sn: एत एवंविधा देवा मनोरेव प्रजापतेः। ते च पूर्वं सुराश्चेति द्विविधाः पितरः स्मृताः॥
en: These were considered as gods at the time of the Prajapati Manu. These were at first called the gods and the Pitris.

sn: शीलयौवनतस्त्वन्यस्तथान्यः सिद्धसाध्ययोः। ऋभवो मरुतश्चैव देवानां चोदितो गणः॥
en: The Siddhas and the Saddhyas were divided into two classes for their conduct and youth. The deities were formerly divided into two classes, viz., the Ribhus and the Maruts.

sn: एवमेते समाम्नाता विश्वेदेवास्तथाश्विनौ। आदित्याः क्षत्रियास्तेषां विशश्च मरुतस्तथा॥
en: Thus have the Vishvas, the gods, and the Ashvins, been enumerated. Amongst them, the Adityas are Kshatriyas, and the Maruts are Vaishyas.

sn: अश्विनौ तु स्मृतौ शूद्रौ तपस्युगे समास्थितौ। स्मृतास्त्वङ्गिरसो देवा ब्राह्मणा इति निश्चयः॥
en: The two Ashvins, practising severe penances, have been said to be Shudras. The deities sprung from Angirasa's family have been said to be Brahmanas. This is certain.

sn: इत्येतत् सर्वदेवानां चातुर्वर्ण्य प्रकीर्तितम्। एतान् वै प्रातरुत्थाय देवान् यस्तु प्रकीर्तयेत्॥ स्वजादन्यकृताच्चैव सर्वपापात् प्रमुच्यते। यवक्रीतोऽथ रैभ्यश्च अर्वावसुपरावसू॥ औशिजश्चैव कक्षीवान् बलश्चाङ्गिरसः सुताः। ऋषिर्मेधातिथेः पुत्रः कण्वो बर्हिषदस्तथा॥ त्रैलोक्यभावनास्तात प्राच्यां सप्तपर्यस्तथा। उन्मुचो विमुचश्चैव स्वस्त्यात्रेयश्च वीर्यवान्॥ प्रमुचश्चेध्यवाहश्च भगवांश्च दृढव्रतः। मित्रावरुणयोः पुत्रस्तथागस्त्यः प्रतापवान्॥ एते ब्रह्मर्षयो नित्यमास्थिता दक्षिणां दिशम्। कवषो धौम्यः परिव्याधश्च वीर्यवान्।॥ एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रिश्तचैव महर्षयः। अत्रेः पुत्रश्च भवांस्तथा सारस्वतः प्रभुः॥ एते चैव महात्मनः पश्चिमामाश्रिता दिशम्। आत्रेयश्च वसिष्ठच कश्यपश्च महानृषिः॥ गौतमोऽथ भरद्वाजो विश्वामित्रोऽथ कौशिकः। तथैव पुत्रो भगवानृचीकस्य महात्मनः॥ जमदग्निश्च सप्तैते उदीचीमाश्रिता दिशम्। एते प्रतिदिशं सर्वे कीर्तितास्तिग्मतेजसः॥
en: Thus have I told you about the fourfold order among the gods. The person who, after rising from his bed in the morning, recites the names of these deities, becomes purged off of all his sins-whether committed by himself intentionally or unintentionally, or whether born of his intercourse with others. Yavakrita, Raivya, Arvavasu, Paravasu, Ausija, Kakshivat, and Vala, are described as the sons of Angiras. These and Kanwa son of the Rishi Medhatithi, and Varhishada, and the wellknown seven Rishis who are the progenitors of the three worlds, all live in the East. Unmucha, Vimucha, the highly energetic Sastyatreya, Pramucha, Idhmavaha, and the divine Dridavrata, and Mitravaruna's highly energetic son Agastya, these twice-born Rishis all live in the South Ushanga, Karusha, Dhaumya, Parivyadha of great energy, and those great Rishis called Ekata, Dvita, and Trita, and Atri's son, viz., the illustrious and powerful Sarasvat, these high-souled ones live in the West. Atreya, and Vashishtha, and the great Rishi Kashyapa, and Gautama, Bharadvaja, and Vishvamitra the son of Kushika, and the illustrious son of the high-souled Richika, viz., Jamadagni,-these seven live the North. Thus have I described to you the great Rishis of fiery energy who live in the different points of the world.

sn: साक्षिभूता महात्मानो भुवनानां प्रभावनाः। एवमेते महात्मानः स्थिताः प्रत्येकशो दिशम्॥
en: Those great ones are the witnesses of the universe, and the creators of all the worlds. Thus do they live in their respective quarters. unui anilda Bacall duur wordt

sn: यस्यां यस्यां दिशि ोते तां दिशं शरणं गतः। मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यः स्वस्तिमांश्च गृहान् व्रजेत्॥
en: By reciting their names one is purged off of all his sins. A person by sojourning to those quarters becomes freed of all his sins and succeeds in returning home safely.'

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामह महाप्राज्ञ युधि सत्यपराक्रम। श्रोतुमिच्छामि कात्स्येन कृष्णमव्ययमीश्वरम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O you of great wisdom and invincible prowess in battle, I wish to hear fully of Krishna who is immutable omnipotent.

sn: यच्चास्य तेजः सुमहद् यच्च कर्म पुरा कृतम्। तन्मे सर्वं यथातत्त्वं ब्रूहि त्वं पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of men, tell me truly everything about his great energy and the great deeds performed by him in days of yore.

sn: तिर्यग्योनिगतं रूपं कथं धारितवान् प्रभुः। केन कार्यनिसर्गेण तमाख्याहि महाबल॥
en: Why did that powerful one assume the form of an animal, and that for performing what particular act? Tell me all this, O mighty warrior.

sn: भीष्म उवाच पुराहं मृगयां यातो मार्कण्डेयाश्रमे स्थितः। तत्रापश्यं मुनिगणान् समासीनान् सहस्रशः॥
en: 'Formerly, on one occasion, while out on hunting, I arrived at the asylum of Markandeya. There I saw various classes of ascetics seated by thousands.

sn: ततस्ते मधुपर्केण पूजां चक्रुरथो मयि। प्रतिगृह्य च पूजां प्रत्यनन्दमृषीनहम्॥
en: The Rishis honoured me by offering honey and curds. Accepting their adoration, I reverentially saluted them in return.

sn: कथैषा कथिता तत्र कश्यपेन महर्षिणा। मनःप्रह्लादिनी दिव्यां तामिहैकमनाः शृणु॥
en: What I shall recite was described there by the great Rishi Kashyapa. Listen with rapt attention to that excellent and charming throne.

sn: पुरा दानवमुख्या हि क्रोधलोभसमन्विताः। बलेन मत्ता शतशो नरकाद्या महासुराः॥ तथैव चान्ये बहवो दानवा युद्धदुर्मदाः। न सहन्ते स्म देवानां समृद्धिं तामनुत्तमाम्॥
en: Formerly the principal Danavas, possessed by anger and cupidity, and hundreds of powerful Asuras having Naraka for their first, elated with power, and numberless other Danavas invincible in battle, became highly jealous of the peerless prosperity of the gods.

sn: दानवैरर्चमानास्तु देवा देवर्षयस्तथा। न शर्म लेभिरे राजन् विशमानास्ततस्ततः॥
en: Oppressed by the Danavas and finding no peace, the gods and the celestial Rishis, fled away in all directions.

sn: पृथिवीमार्तरूपां ते समपश्यन् दिवौकसः। दानवैरभिसंस्तीर्णां घोररूपैर्महाबलैः॥
en: The dwellers of heaven saw the Earth loO king like one one sunk in sore distress. Overspread with mighty Danavas of terrible countenance, the Earth seemed to be oppressed with a heavy load, Cheerless and grief-stricken, she seemed as if going down into the neither region.

sn: भारार्तामप्रहृष्टां च दुःखितां संनिमज्जतीम्। अथादितेयाः संत्रस्ता ब्रह्माणमिदमब्रुवन्॥
en: The Adityas, stricken with fear, went to Brahman, and said,-How O Brahman, shall we continue to put up with these oppressions of the Danavas.

sn: कथं शक्ष्यामहे ब्रह्मन् दानवैरभिमर्दनम्। स्वयम्भूस्तानुवाचेदं निसृष्टोऽत्र विधिर्मया॥
en: The self-create answered them, saying,-I have already ordained what is to be done in this matter.

sn: ते वरेणाभिसम्पन्ना बलेन च मदेन च। नावबुध्यन्ति सम्मूढा विष्णुमव्यक्तदर्शनम्॥ वराहरूपिणं देवमधृष्यममरैरपि। एष वेगेन गत्वा हि यत्र ते दानवाधमाः॥ अन्तर्भूमिगता घोरा निवसन्ति सहस्रशः। शमयिष्यति तच्छ्रुत्वा जहषुः सुरसत्तमाः॥
en: Having obtained boons, and possessed of power, and elated with pride, those senseless wretches do not know that Vishnu of invisible form, that god incapable of being defeated by the very gods in a body, has assumed the form of a boar. That Supreme Deity, going to the spot where those wretched Danavas, of terrible mien, are living in thousands below the Earth, will kill them all! Hearing these words of the Grandfather, those foremost one among the deities were overjoyed.

sn: ततो विष्णुर्महातेजा वाराहं रूपमास्थितः। अन्तर्भूमि सम्प्रविश्य जगाम दितिजान् प्रति॥
en: Sometime after, Vishnu of mighty energy, assuming the form of a Boar, penetrating into the neither regions, rushed against those children of Diti.

sn: दृष्ट्वा च सहिताः सर्वे दैत्याः सत्त्वममानुषम्। प्रसह्य तरसा सर्वे संतस्थुः कालमोहिताः॥
en: Seeing that extraordinary creature, all the Daityas, in a body stupefied by Time, quickly proceeded against it for displaying their strength, and stood encircling it.

sn: ततस्ते समभिदुत्य वराहं जगृहुः समम्। संक्रुद्धाश्च वराहं तं व्यकर्षन्त समन्ततः॥
en: Soon after, they all rushed against that Boar and caught it simultaneously. Filled with anger they tried to drag the animal from every side.

sn: दानवेन्द्रा महाकाया महावीर्यबलोच्छ्रिताः। नाशक्नुवंश्च किंचित् ते तस्य कर्तुं तदा विभो॥
en: Those foremost of Danavas, of huge bodies, endued with mighty energy, swelling with strength, O monarch, could do nothing to that Boar.

sn: ततोऽगच्छत् विस्मयं ते दानवेन्द्रा भयं तथा। संशयं गतमात्मानं मेनिरे च सहस्रशः॥
en: At this they were stricken with wonder and fear. Numbering in thousands, they thought that their last hour had come.

sn: ततो देवाधिदेवः स योगात्मा योगसारिथः। योगमास्थाय भगवांस्तदा भरतसत्तम॥
en: Then that Supreme God of all the gods, having Yoga for his soul and companion, became immersed in Yoga, O chief of the Bharatas, and began to roar terribly agitating those Daityas and Danavas.

sn: विननाद महानादं क्षोभयन् दैत्यदानवान्। संनादिता येन लोकाः सर्वाश्चैव दिशो दश॥
en: All the worlds and the ten cardinal points resounded with those roars, which for this reason, agitated all creatures and struck them with fear.

sn: तेन संनादशब्देन लोकानां क्षोभ आगमत्। संत्रस्ताश्च भृशं लोके देवाः शक्रपुरोगमा:॥
en: The very gods headed by Indra became terror-stricken. The whole universe became calm in consequence of that sound. It was a dreadful time.

sn: निर्विचेष्टं जगच्चापि बभूवातिभृशं तदा। स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव तेन नादेन मोहितम्॥ ततस्ते दानवाः सर्वे तेन नादेन भीषिताः। पेतुर्गतासवश्चैव विष्णुतेज:प्रमोहिताः॥
en: All mobile and immobile beings became stupefied by that sound. The Danavas, terrified by that sound, began to fall down dead, paralysed by the energy of Vishnu. The Boar, with its hoops, began to pierce those enemies of the gods, those dwellers of the nether regions, and tear their flesh, fat, and bones.

sn: रसातलगतश्चापि वराहस्त्रिदशद्विषाम्। खुरैर्विदारयामास मांसमेदोऽस्थिसंचयान्॥
en: On account of those tremendous roars, Vishnu passed by the name of Sanalana.

sn: नादेन तेन महता सनातन इति स्मृतः। पद्मनाभो महायोगी भूताचार्यः स भूतराट्॥
en: He is also called Padmanabha. He is foremost of Yogins. He is the Preceptor of all creatures, and their supreme Lord. All the sects of the gods then went to the Grandfather.

sn: ततो देवगणाः सर्वे पितामहमुपाद्रवन्। तत्र गत्वा महात्मानमूचुश्चैव जगत्पतिम्॥ नादोऽयं कीदृशो देव नैतं विद्म वयं प्रभो। कोऽसौ हि कस्य वा नादो येन विह्वलितं जगत्॥ देवाश्च दानवाश्चैव मोहितास्तस्य तेजसा।
en: Going there, those illustrious addressed the Lord of the universe, saying-What sort of noise is this, O powerful one? We do not understand it. Who is this one, ones or whose is this sound by which the universe has been stupefied. With the power of this sound or of its maker, the gods and the Danavas have all been deprived of their senses.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे विष्णुराहं रूपमास्थितः। उदतिष्ठन्महाबाहो स्तूयमानो महर्षिभिः॥
en: Meanwhile, O mighty-armed one, Vishnu in his Boar form came before the assembled gods, his praises lauded by the great Rishis.

sn: पितामह उवाच निहत्य दानवपतीन् महावा महाबलः। एष देवो महायोगी भूतात्मा भूतभावनः॥
en: The Grandfather said That is the Supreme God, the Creator of all beings, the Soul of all creatures, the foremost of all Yogins. Of huge body and great strength, he comes here, having killed the leading Danavas.

sn: सर्वभूतेश्वरो योगी मुनिरात्मा तथाऽऽत्मनः। स्थिरीभवत कृष्णोऽयं सर्वविघ्नविनाशनः॥
en: He is the Lord of all beings, the master of Yoga, the great ascetic, the Soul of all living beings. Be silent, all of you? He is Krishna, the destroyer of all impediments.

sn: कृत्वा कर्मातिसाध्वेतदशक्यममितप्रभः। समायातः स्वमात्मानं महाभागो महाद्युति॥
en: That Supreme God of immeasurable sheen, that great refuge of all blessings, having performed a most difficult task that cannot be accomplished by others, has returned to his own pure nature.

sn: पद्मनाभो महायोगी महात्मा भूतभावनः। न संतापो न भी: कार्या शोको वा सुरसत्तमाः॥
en: It is He from whose navel the primeval lotus had sprung. He is the foremost of Yogins. Of supreme soul, He is the creator of all beings. There is no necessity for sorrow or fear or grief, ye foremost of celestials.

sn: विधिरेष प्रभावश्च काल: संक्षयकारकः। लोकान् धारयता तेन नादो मुक्तो महात्मना॥
en: He is the Ordainer. He is the Creating Principle. He is all-destroying Time. It is He who maintains all the worlds. These roars that have alarmed you are being uttered by that great one.

sn: स एष हि महाबाहुः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः। अच्युतः पुण्डरीकाक्षः सर्वभूतादिरीश्वरः॥
en: Of mighty arms, He is the object of universal adoration. Incapable of deterioration, that lotus-eyed one is the origin of all beings and their lord.' He is the Ordainer. He is the Creating Principle. He is all-destroying Time. It is He who maintains all the worlds. These roars that have alarmed you are being uttered by that great one.

sn: स एष हि महाबाहुः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः। अच्युतः पुण्डरीकाक्षः सर्वभूतादिरीश्वरः॥
en: Of mighty arms, He is the object of universal adoration. Incapable of deterioration, that lotus-eyed one is the origin of all beings and their lord.'

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच योगं मे परमं तात मोक्षस्य वद भारत। तमहं तत्त्वतो ज्ञातुमिच्छामि वदतां वर॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O sire, that high Yoga by which, O Bharata, I may obtain liberation. O foremost of speakers, I wish to know everything about that Yoga truly.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। संवादं मोक्षसंयुक्तं शिष्यस्य गुरुणा सह॥
en: Bhishma said 'Regarding it is cited the old narrative of the discourse between a preceptor and disciple on the subject of liberation.

sn: कश्चिद् ब्राह्मणमासीनमाचार्यमृषिसत्तमम्। तेजोराशिं महात्मानं सत्यसंधं जितेन्द्रियम्॥
en: There was a twice-born preceptor who was the foremost of Rishis. He looked like a mass of effulgence. Endued with a high soul, he was firm in truth and a complete master of his senses.

sn: शिष्यः परममेधावी श्रेयोऽर्थी सुसमाहितः। चरणावुपसंगृह्य स्थितः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्॥ उपासनात् प्रसन्नोऽसि यदि वै भगवन् मम। संशयो मे महान् कश्चित् तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि।
en: Once upon a time, a highly intelligent and attentive disciple, desirous of obtaining what was for his highest good touched the preceptor's feet, and standing with joined palms before him, said,-If O illustrious one, you have been pleased with the adoration I have offered you, you should solve a great doubt of mine.

sn: कुतश्चाहं कुतश्च त्वं तत् सम्यग्ब्रूहि यत्परम्॥ कथं च सर्वभूतेषु समेषु द्विजसत्तम। सम्यग्वृत्ता निवर्तन्ते विपराताः क्षयोदयाः॥ वेदेषु चापि यद् वाक्यं लौकिकं व्यापकं च यत्। एतद् विद्वन् यथातत्त्वं सर्वं व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Whence am I am and whence are you? Tell me this fully. Tell me also what is the final cause. Why also, O best of twice-born ones, when the material and destruction take place in such dissimilar ways? You should, O you of great learning, also explain the object of the saying in the Vedas, the meaning of the injunctions of the Smritis and of those injunctions which apply to all classes of men.

sn: गुरुरुवाच शृणु शिष्य महाप्राज्ञ ब्रह्मगुह्यमिदं परम्। अध्यात्म सर्वविद्यानामागमानां च यद्वसु॥
en: Listen, O disciple, O you of great wisdom. This what you have asked me is not described even in the very Vedas and is the highest subject for thought or discourse. It is called Adhyatma and is the most precious of all branches of learning and of all sacred institutes.

sn: वासुदेवः परमिदं विश्वस्य ब्रह्मणो मुखम्। सत्यं ज्ञानमथो यज्ञस्तितिक्षा दम आर्जवम्॥
en: Vasudeva is the Supreme (cause) of the universe. He is the origin of the Vedas (viz., Om). He is Truth, Knowledge, Sacrifice, Renunciation, self-control, and Righteousness.

sn: पुरुषं सनातनं विष्णुं यं तं वेदविदो विदुः। स्वर्गप्रलयकर्तारमव्यक्तं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्॥
en: Persons well-read in Vedas know Him as pervading, all Eternal, Omnipresent, the Creator and the Destroyer, the Unmanifest, Brahma, Immutable.

sn: तदिदं ब्रह्म वार्ष्णेयमितिहासं शृणुष्व मे। ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणैः श्राव्यो राजन्यः क्षत्रियैस्तथा॥ वैश्यो वैश्यैस्तथा श्राव्यः शूद्रः शूरैर्महामनाः। माहात्म्यं देवदेवस्य विष्णोरमिततेजसः॥
en: Hear now from me the story of Him who was born in the Vrishni family. A Brahmana should hear the greatness of that God of gods, called Vishnu of immeasurable energy, from the lips of Brahmanas. A Kshatriya should hear it from persons of that order. One who is a Vaishya, should hear it from Vaishyas, and a high-souled Shudra should hear it from Sudras.

sn: अर्हस्त्वमसि कल्याणं वार्ष्णेयं शृणु यत्परम्। कालचक्रमनाद्यन्तं भावाभावस्वलक्षणम्॥
en: You deserve to hear it. Listen now to the sacred accounts of Krishna, that theme which is foremost of all themes. Vasudeva is the Wheel of Time, without beginning and without end. Existence and Non-existence are the qualities by which His real nature is known.

sn: त्रैलोक्यं सर्वभूतेशे चक्रवत्परिवर्तते। यत्तदक्षरमव्यक्तममृतं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्। वदन्ति पुरुषव्याघ्र केशवं पुरुषर्षभम्॥
en: The universe rolls like a wheel, depending upon that Lord of all beings. O best of men, Keshava, that foremost of all beings is said to be Indestructible, unmanifest, Immortal Brahma, and Immutable.

sn: पितृन देवानृषीश्चैव तथा वै यक्षराक्षसान्। नागासुरमनुष्यांश्च सृजते परमोऽव्ययः॥
en: The highest of the high, and without change or destruction himself, he created the departed manes, the gods, the Rishis, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Nagas, the Asuras, and mankind.

sn: तथैव वेदशास्त्राणि लोकधर्माश्च शाश्वतान्। प्रलयं प्रकृति प्राप्य युगादौ सृजते पुनः॥
en: He also created the Vedas and the eternal duties and customs of men. Having reduced everything into nothing, he once more, in the beginning of a (new) cycle, creates Prakriti.

sn: यथाव॒तुलिङ्गानि नानारूपाणि पर्यये। दृश्यन्ते तानि तान्येव तथा भावा युगादिषु॥
en: As the various phenomena of the several seasons set in one after another according to the season that comes, so creatures come into being at the commencement of every cycle.

sn: अथ यद्यद् यदा भाति कालयोगाद् युगादिषु। तत् तदुत्पद्यते ज्ञानं लोकयात्राविधानजम्॥
en: Corresponding with those creatures who came into being, rules and duties are paid for regulating the world's course.

sn: युगान्तेऽन्तर्हितान् वेदान् सेतिहासान् महर्षयः। लेभिरे तपसा पूर्वमनुज्ञाताः स्वयम्भुवा॥
en: At the end of every cycle the Vedas and all other scriptures disappear. Through the favour of the Self-create, the great Rishis, by mcans of their penances, first re-acquire the lost Vedas and the scriptures.

sn: वेदविद् वेद भगवान् वेदाङ्गानि बृहस्पतिः। भार्गवो नीतिशास्त्रं तु जगाद जगतो हितम्॥
en: The Self-create (Brahman) first acquired the Vedas. Their branches called the Angas were first acquired by Brihaspati. Bhrigu's son (Shukra) first acquired the science of ethics which is so beneficial for the universe.

sn: गान्धर्वं नारदो वेद भरद्वाजो धनुर्ग्रहम्। देवर्षिचरितं गार्ग्य: कृष्णात्रेयश्चिकित्सितम्॥
en: Narada acquired the science of music; Bharadvaja that of arms; Gargya, the history of the celestial Rishis; the dark son of Atri that of medicine.

sn: न्यायतन्त्राण्यनेकानि तैस्तैरुक्तानि वादिभिः। हेत्वागमसदाचारैर्यदुक्तं तदुपास्यताम्॥
en: are Various other Rishis whose names connected therewith, promulgated various other sciences such as Philosophy, Logic, etc. Let that Brahma which those Rishis have described by arguments drawn from reason, by means of the Vedas, and by inferences drawn from the direct evidence of the senses, be worshipped.

sn: अनाद्यं तत्परं ब्रह्म न देवा नर्षयो विदुः। एकस्तद् वेद भगवान् धाता नारायणः प्रभुः॥
en: Neither the gods nor the Rishis were able to grasp Brahma who is without beginning and who is the highest of the high. Only the divine creator of all things, viz., the powerful Narayana, had known of Brahma.

sn: नारायणादृषिगणास्तथा मुख्याः सुरासुराः। राजर्षयः पुराणाश्च परमं दुःखभेषजम्॥
en: From Narayana, the Rishis the foremost of the deities, the Asuras, and the royal sages of old, acquired the knowledge of that highest panacea for the cure of sorrow.

sn: पुरुषाधिष्ठितान् भावान् प्रकृतिः सूयते यदा। हेतुयुक्तमतः पूर्वं जगत् सम्परिवर्तते॥
en: When Prakriti creates through the action of Purusha, the universe with all its potencies begins to spring from it.

sn: दीपादन्ये यथा दीपाः प्रवर्तन्ते सहस्रशः। प्रकृतिः सूयते तद्वदानन्त्यान् नापचीयते॥
en: From one lighted lamp thousands of other lamps are capable of being lighted. Similarly, Prakriti produces thousands of existent things. On account of its infinity, primordial matter is never exhausted,

sn: अव्यक्तकर्मजा बुद्धिरहंकारं प्रसूयते। आकाशं चाप्यहंकाराद् वायुराकाशसम्भवः॥
en: From the Unmanifest flows the Understanding determined by acts. The Understanding creates Consciousness. From Consciousness proceeds Space. From Space proceeds Wind.

sn: वायोस्तेजस्ततश्चाप अद्भ्योऽथ वसुधोद्गता। मूलप्रकृतयो ह्यष्टौ जगदेतास्ववस्थितम्॥
en: From the Wind proceeds Heat. From Heat proceeds Water, and from Water is produced the Earth. These Eight form primordial Prakriti. The universe rests on them.

sn: ज्ञानेन्द्रियाण्यतः पञ्च पञ्च कर्मेन्द्रियाण्यपि। विषयाः पञ्च चैकं च विकारे घोडशं मनः॥
en: From those Eight have originated the five organs of knowledge, the five organs of action, the five objects of the (first five) organs, and the one, viz., the Mind, forining the sixteenth, which is the outcome of their modification.

sn: श्रोत्रं त्वक्चक्षुषी जिह्वा घ्राणं ज्ञानेन्द्रियाण्यथ। पादौ पायुरूपस्थश्च हस्तौ वाकर्मणी अपि॥
en: The car, the skin, the two eyes, the tongue, and the nose are the five organs of knowledge. The two feet, the anus, the organ of generation, the two arms, and speech, are the five organs of action.

sn: शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसो गन्धस्तथैव च। विज्ञेयं व्यापकं चित्तं तेषु सर्वगतं मनः॥
en: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are the five objects of the senses, covering all things. The Mind lives upon all the senses and their objects.

sn: रसज्ञाने तु जिह्वयं व्याहते वाक् तथोच्यते। इन्द्रियैर्विविधैर्युक्तं सर्वं व्यक्तं मनस्तथा॥
en: In the perception of taste, the Mind becomes the tongue, and in speech Mind become words. Covered with the different senses, Mind becomes all the objects.

sn: विद्यात् तु षोडशैतानि दैवतानि विभागशः। देहेषु ज्ञानकर्तारमुपासीनमुपासते।॥
en: These sixteen, existing in their respective forms, should be known as god. These adore Him who creates all knowledge and lives within the body.

sn: तद्वत् सोमगुणा जिह्वा गन्धस्तु पृथिवीगुणः। श्रोतं नभोगुणं चैव चक्षुरग्नेर्गुणस्तथा। स्पर्श वायुगुणं विद्यात् सर्वभूतेषु सर्वदा॥
en: Taste in the attribute of water; scent is the attribute of space; vision is the attribute of fire or light; and touch is the attribute of the wind. This is the case with all creatures at all times.

sn: मनः सत्त्वगुणं प्राहुः सत्त्वमव्यक्तजं तथा। सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्थं तस्माद् बुद्ध्येत बुद्धिमान्॥
en: The Mind, is the attribute of existence. Existence springs from the Prakriti which exists in That which is the Soul of all existent beings.

sn: एते भावा जगत् सर्वं वहन्ति सचराचरम्। श्रिता विरजसं देवं यमाहुः प्रकृतेः परम्॥
en: These existence's, resting upon the supreme Divinity that is above Prakriti and that is inactive, uphold the entire universe of the mobile and immobile objects.

sn: नवद्वारं पुरं पुण्यमेतैर्भावैः समन्वितम्। व्याप्य शेते महानात्मा तस्मात् पुरुष उच्यते॥
en: This sacred building of nine doors (body) is endued with all these existences. That which is high above them, viz., the Soul, lives within it, pervading it all over. Therefore it is called Purusha.

sn: अजर: सोऽमरश्चैव व्यक्ताव्यक्तोपदेशवान्। व्यापक: सगुणः सूक्ष्मः सर्वभूतगुणाश्रयः॥
en: The Soul is not subject to decay and death. It has knowledge of what is manifest and what is unmanifest. It is again all-pervading, endued with qualities, subtile, and the refuge of all existence and qualities.

sn: यथा दीपः प्रकाशात्मा ह्रस्वो वा यदि वा महान्। ज्ञानात्मानं तथा विद्यात् पुरुषं सर्वजन्तुषु॥
en: As a lamp shows all objects great or small, similarly the Soul dwells in all creatures as the principle of knowledge.

sn: श्रोत्रं वेदयते वेद्यं स शृणोति स पश्यति। कारणं तस्य देहोऽयं स कर्ता सर्वकर्मणाम्॥
en: Making the car to hear what it hears, it is the Soul that hears. Likewise, making the works, it is the Soul that sees. This body supplies the means by which the Soul derives knowledge. The bodily organs are not the doers, but it is the Soul that is doer, of all acts.

sn: अग्निर्दारुगतो यद्वद् भिन्ने दारौ न दृश्यते। तथैवात्मा शरीरस्थो योगेनैवानुदृश्यते॥
en: There is fire in wood, but it is never seen by cutting upon a piece of wood. Similarly, the Soul lives within the body, but it can never be seen by cutting the body.

sn: अग्निर्यथा झुपायेन मथित्वा दारु दृश्यते। तथैवात्मा शरीरस्थो योगेनैवात्र दृश्यते॥
en: The fire which exists in wood may be seen by proper means, viz., rubbing the wood. Similarly, the Soul which lives within the body may be seen by employing proper means, viz., Yoga.

sn: नदीष्वापो यथा युक्ता यथा सूर्ये मरीचयः। संततत्वाद् यथा यान्ति तथा देहाः शरीरिणाम्॥
en: Water must exits in rivers. Rays of light are always attached to the sun. Similarly, thc Soul has a body. This connection is not stopped because of the constant succession of bodies that Soul has to pass through.

sn: स्वप्नयोगे यथैवात्मा पञ्चेन्द्रियसमायुतः। देहमुत्सृज्य वै याति तथैवात्मोपलभ्यते॥
en: In a dream, the Soul, endued with the five senses, leaves the body and moves over wide areas. Similarly, when death takes place, the Soul passes out of one body for entering another.

sn: कर्मणा बाध्यते रूपं कर्मणा चोपलभ्यते। कर्मणा नीयतेऽन्यत्र स्वकृतेन बलीयसा॥
en: The Soul is fettered by its pristine acts. Fettered by acts done by it in one state. Indeed, it is led from one into another body by its owni acts which are of very powerful consequences.

sn: स तु देहाद् यथा देहं त्यक्त्वान्यं प्रतिपद्यते। तथान्यं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि भूतग्रामं स्वकर्मजम्॥
en: I will not describe how the owner of a human body, casting off his body, enters another, and then again into another, and how, indeed, the whole range of beings is the result of their respective acts.

sn: गुरुरुवाच चतुर्विधानि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च। अव्यक्तप्रभवान्याहुरव्यक्तनिधनानि च। अव्यक्तलक्षणं विद्यादव्यक्तात्मात्मकं मनः॥
en: Bhishma said 'All immobile and mobile beings, divided into four classes, have been described to be of unmanifest birth and unmanifest death. Existing only in the unmanifest Soul, the Mind is said to possess the attributes of the unmanifest.

sn: यथाश्वत्थकणीकायामन्तर्भूतो महाद्रुमः। निष्पन्नो दृश्यते व्यक्तमव्यक्तात् सम्भवस्तथा॥
en: As a vast tree lies within a small unblown Ashvatha flower and is seen only when it comes out, so birth takes place from what is unmanifest.

sn: अभिद्रवत्ययस्कान्तमयो निश्चेतनं यथा। स्वभावहेतुजा भावा यद्वदन्यदपीदृशम्॥
en: A piece of iron, which is inanimate runs towards a piece of loadstone. Likewise, inclinations and propensities due to natural instincts, and all else, run towards the Soul in a 11cw lifc.

sn: तद्वदव्यक्तजा भावाः कर्तुः कारणलक्षणाः। अचेतनाश्चेतयितुः कारणादभिसंहता॥
en: Indeed, as those propensities bom of Darkness and Ignorance, and inactive in their nature, are united with the Soul when re-born, similarly, those other inclinations and aspirations of the Soul that have their look directed towards Brahma become united with it, coming to it directly from Brahima itself.

sn: न भून खं द्यौर्भूतानि नर्षयो न सुरासुराः। नान्यदासीदृते जीवमासेदुर्न तु संहतम्॥
en: Neither earth, nor sky, nor heaven, nor things, nor the vital airs, nor virtue and vice, nor anything else, existed before, except the Intelligence-Soul. Nor have they any necessary connection with even the Intelligence-Soul corrupted by Darkness.

sn: पूर्वं नित्यं सर्वगतं मनोहेतुमलक्षणम्। अज्ञानकर्म निर्दिष्टमेतत् कारणलक्षणम्॥
en: The Soul is eternal. It is indestructible. It is in every creature. It is the cause of the Mind. It is without qualities. This universe before us is due to Darkness or Ignorance. The Soul's apprehensions of form, etc., are due to past desires.

sn: तत्कारणैर्हि संयुक्त कार्यसंग्रहकारकम्। येनैतद् वर्तते चक्रमनादिनिधनं महत्॥
en: The Soul, when it becomes endued with desires, engages in acts. On account of that condition, this vast wheel of existence revolves with beginning and without end.

sn: अव्यक्तनाभं व्यक्तारं विकारपरिमण्डलम्। श्रेत्रज्ञाधिष्ठितं चक्रं स्निग्धाक्षं वर्तते ध्रुवम्॥
en: The Understanding, is the nave of that wheel. The body with the senses, forms its spokes. The perceptions and acts are its circumference. Urged by on the quality of Darkness, the Soul presides over it.

sn: स्निग्धत्वात् लिवत् सर्वं चक्रेऽस्मिन् पीड्यते जगत्। तिलपीडैरिवाक्रम्य भोगैरज्ञानसम्भवैः॥
en: Like oilmen pressing oilseeds pressing oilseeds in their machine, the consequences born of Darkness, assailing the universe which is moistened by Darkness, press or grind it in that wheel.

sn: कर्म तत् कुरुते तर्षादहंकारपरिग्रहात्। कार्यकारणसंयोगे स हेतुरुपपादितः॥
en: In that succession of births, the individual Soul, seized by the idea of Ego in consequence of desire, performs acts. In the union of cause and effect, those acts again become fresh causes.

sn: नाभ्येति कारणं कार्यं न कार्य कारणं तथा। कार्याणां तूपकरणे कालो भवति हेतुमान्॥
en: Effects do not enter into causes. Nor do causes enter into effects. Time is the instrumental in the production of effects.

sn: हेतुयुक्ताः प्रकृतयो विकाराश्च परस्परम्। अन्योन्यमभिवर्तन्ते पुरुषाधिष्ठिताः सदा॥
en: The primordial essences, and their changes endued with causes, exist unitedly, on account of their being always presided over by the Soul.

sn: राजसैस्तामसैर्भावैर्युतो हेतुबलान्वितः। क्षेत्रज्ञमेवानुयाति पांसुर्वातेरितो यथा॥
en: Like dust following the wind that moves it, the individual Soul, shorn of body, but endued still with inclinations born of Darkness and Ignorance with principles of causes formed by pristine deeds, moves on, following the direction of the Supreme Soul.

sn: न च तैः स्पृश्यते भावैर्न ते तेन महात्मना। सरजस्कोऽरजस्कश्च नैव वायुर्भवेद् यथा॥
en: The Soul, however, is never affected by those inclinations and propensities. Nor are these affected by the Soul that is superior to them. The wind, which is naturally pure, is never sullied by the dust it carries.

sn: तथैतदन्तरं विद्यात् सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्बुधः। अभ्यासात् स तथा युक्तो न गच्छेत् प्रकृति पुनः।।
en: As the wind is separate from the dust it carries away, so, the wise man should know, is the connection between life and the Soul. No one should think that the Soul, on account of its seeming union with the body and the senses and the other inclinations and beliefs and unbeliefs, is really endued therewith as its necessary and absolute qualities. On the other hand, the Soul should be considered as existing in its own nature.

sn: संदेहमेतमुत्पन्नमच्छिनद् भगवानृषिः। तथा वार्ता समीक्षेत कृतलक्षणसम्मिताम्॥
en: Thus did the divine Rishi remove the doubt that had taken possession of his disciple's mind. Inspite of all this, people depend upon means consisting of acts and scriptural rites for removing misery and acquiring happiness.

sn: बीजान्यग्न्युपदग्धानि न रोहन्ति यथा पुनः। ज्ञानदग्धैस्तथा क्लेशै त्मा सम्पद्यते पुनः॥
en: Seeds that are burnt by fire do not put forth sprouts. Likewise, if everything that produces misery be consumed by the fire of true knowledge, the Soul is freed from the obligation of re-birth in the world.

sn: भीष्म उवाच प्रवृत्तिलक्षणो धर्मो यथा समुपलभ्यते। तेषां विज्ञाननिष्ठानामन्यत्तत्वं न रोचते॥
en: Bhishma said more Persons who perform acts consider the performance of acts highly. Likewise, those who are devoted to Knowledge do not regard anything other than Knowledge.

sn: दुर्लभा वेदविद्वांसो वेदोक्तेषु व्यवस्थिताः। प्रयोजनं महत्त्वात्तु मार्गमिच्छन्ति संस्तुतम्॥
en: Rare are persons fully conversant with the Vedas and depending upon the injunctions contained therein. The intelligent however consider the abstention from acts as the better of the two, viz., heaven and liberation.

sn: सद्भिराचरितत्वात्तु वृत्तमेतदगर्हितम्। इयं सा बुद्धिरभ्येत्य यया याति परां गतिम्॥
en: Abstention of acts is observed by highly wise That conduct, therefore, is praiseworthy. The intelligence which advocates abstention from acts, is that by which one attains to liberation. men.

sn: शरीरवानुपादत्ते मोहात् सर्वान् परिग्रहान्। क्रोधलोभादिभिर्भावैर्युक्तो राजसतामसैः॥
en: Endued with body, a person, through folly, and endued with anger and cupidity and all the propensities born of Darkness and Ignorance, cherishes attachment for all earthly objects.

sn: नाशुद्धमाचरेत् तस्मादभीप्सन् देहयापनम्। कर्मणा विवरं कुर्वन्न लोकानाप्नुयाच्छुभान्॥
en: One, therefore, who wishes to destroy his connection with the body, should never perforin any impure act. On the other hand, one should create by his acts a path for attaining to Liberation, without wishing for regions of happiness.

sn: लोहयुक्तं यथा हेम विपक्वं न विराजते। तथापक्वकषायाख्यं विज्ञानं न प्रकाशते॥
en: As gold, when united with iron, losses its purity and cannot shine, so Knowledge, when existing with attachment to earthly objects and such other shortcomings, fails to display its splendour.

sn: यश्चाधर्मं चरेल्लोभात् कामक्रोधावनुप्लवन्। धर्म्य पन्थानमाक्रम्य सानुबन्धो विनश्यति॥
en: He who, influenced by cupidity, desire and anger, practises unrighteousness, transgressing the path of righteousness, is completely destroyed.

sn: शब्दादीन् विषयांस्तस्मान्न संरागादयं व्रजेत्। क्रोधो हर्षो विषादश्च जायन्तेह परस्परात्॥
en: One who is desirous of benefiting oneself should never seek, with too much attachment, earthly possessions representing by the objects of the senses. If one does it, anger and joy and sorrow arise from one another.

sn: पञ्चभूतात्मके देहे सत्त्वे राजसतामसे। कमभिष्टुवते चायं कं वाऽऽक्रोशति किं वदन्॥
en: When every one's body is made up of the five original elements as also of the three qualities of Goodness. Darkness, and Ignorance, whom shall one worship and whom shall one censure with what words?

sn: स्पर्शरूपरसाद्येषु सङ्गं गच्छन्ति बालिशाः। नावगच्छन्त्यविज्ञानादात्मानं पार्थिवं गुणम्॥
en: Only the fools become attached to the objects of the senses. On account of folly they do not know that their bodies are only modifications of earth.

sn: मृन्मयं शरणं यद्वन्मृदैव परिलिप्यते। पार्थिवोऽयं तथा देहो मृद्विकारान्न नश्यति॥
en: As a house made of earth is covered over with earth, so this body which is made of earth is saved from destruction by food which is only a change of earth.

sn: मधु तैलं पयः सर्पिर्मांसानि लवणं गुडः। धान्यानि फलमूलानि मृविकाराः सहाम्भसा॥
en: Honey, oil, milk, butter, meat, salt, treacle and grain of all kinds and fruit and roots are all modifications of earth and water.

sn: यद्वत् कान्तारमातिष्ठन्नौत्सुक्यं समनुव्रजेत्। ग्राम्यमाहारमादद्यादस्वाद्वपि हि यापनम्॥
en: Giving up all desire (for rich food) herinits living in the forest take simple and unsavoury food, for only keeping up the body.

sn: तद्वत् ससारकान्तारमातिष्ठश्रमतत्परः। यात्रार्थमद्यादाहारं व्याधितो भेषजं यथा॥
en: Likewise, a person who lives in the forest of the world, should be ready for labour and should take food for passing life, like a patient taking medicine.

sn: सत्यशौचार्जवत्यागैर्वर्चसा विक्रमेण च। क्षान्त्या धृत्या च बुद्ध्या च मनसा तपसैव च॥ भावान् सर्वानुपावृत्तान् समीक्ष्य विषयात्मकान्। शान्तिमिच्छन्नदीनात्मा संयच्छेदिन्द्रियाणि च॥
en: Examining all earthly things that meet him, by the help of truth, purity, candour, a spirit of। renunciation, enlightenment, courage, forgiveness, fortitude, intelligence, reflection, and austerities, and desirous of securing tranquillity, a person of great soul should restrain his senses.

sn: सत्त्वेन रजसा चैव तमसा चैव मोहिताः। चक्रवत् परिवर्तन्ते ह्यज्ञानाज्जन्तवो भृशम्॥
en: All creatures, stupefied by Ignorance by the qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance and continually revolving like a wheel.

sn: तस्मात् सम्यक् परीक्षेत दोषानज्ञानसम्भवान्। अज्ञानप्रभवं दुःखमहंकारं परित्यजेत्॥
en: All faults, begotten of Ignorance should be closely examined and the idea of Self, which originates from Ignorance, and creates misery, should be avoided.

sn: महाभूतानीन्द्रियाणि गुणाः सत्त्वं रजस्तमः। त्रेलोक्यं सेश्वरं सर्वमहंकारे प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: The five elements, the senses, the qualities of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance, the three worlds with the Supreme Being himself, and acts, all rest on Self-consciousness.

sn: यथेह नियतः कालो दर्शयत्यार्तवान् गुणान्। तद्वद्भूतेष्वहंकारं विद्यात् कर्मप्रवर्तकम्॥
en: As Time, under its own laws, always creates the seasons one after another, so one should know that Consciousness in all creatures is the mover of acts.

sn: सम्मोहकं तमो विद्यात् कृष्णमज्ञानसम्भवम्। प्रीतिदुःखनिबद्धांश्च समस्तांस्त्रीनथो गुणान्॥
en: Ignorance produces delusions. It is like Darkness and is born of Ignorance. All the joys and sorrows belong to the three qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance.

sn: सत्त्वस्य रजसश्चैव तमसश्च निबोध तान्। प्रसादो हर्षजा प्रीतिरसंदहो धृतिः स्मृतिः। एतान् सत्त्वगुणान् विद्यादिमान् राजसतामसान्॥
en: Listen now to those consequences that spring from the qualities of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance. Contentment, the satisfaction that arises from joy, certainty, intelligence, and memory,-these are the results of the quality of Goodness. I shall now describe the consequences of Darkness and Ignorance.

sn: कामक्रोधौ प्रमादश्च लोभमोहौ भयं क्लमः। विषादशोकावरतिर्मानदर्पावनार्यता।॥
en: Desire, anger, error, cupidity stupefaction, fear, and fatigue, belong to the quality of Darkness. Cheerlessness, grief discontent, vanity, pride, and wickedness, all belong to Ignorance.

sn: दोषाणामेवमादीनां परोक्ष्य गुरुलाघवम्। विमृशेदात्मसंस्थानमेकैकमनुसंततम्॥
en: Examining the weight or lightness of these and other evils that exist in the Soul, one should reflect upon each of them one after another.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच के दोषा मनसा त्यक्ताः के बुद्ध्या शिथिलीकृताः। के पुनः पुनरायान्ति के मोहादफला इव॥
en: Yudhishthira said, What eviis are shunned by persons sceking Liberation? What are those that are weakened by them? What are the evils that come again and again? What, again, are regarded as week, through stupefaction.

sn: केषां बलाबलं बुद्ध्या हेतुभिर्विमशेद् बुधः। एष मे संशयस्तात तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: What, indeed, are those evils upon whose gravity and weakness a wise man should reflect with the help of intelligence and of reason? I have doubts upon these subjects. Describe these to me, O grandfather.

sn: भीष्म उवाच दोषैर्मूलादवच्छिन्नविशुद्धात्मा विमुच्यते। विनाशयति सम्भूतमयस्मयमयो यथा। तथा कृतात्मा सहजैर्दोषैर्नश्यति तामसैः॥
en: Bhishma said-‘By rooting out all evils, a person of pure Soul succeeds in obtaining Liberation.
