As an axe made of steel cuts a steel chain, similarly, a person of cleansed Soul, destroying all the evils that originate from Darkness and that are born with the Soul, succeeds in cutting off his connection with the body.

sn: राजसं तामसं चैव शुद्धात्मकमकल्मषम्। तत् सर्वं देहिनां बीजं सत्त्वमात्मवतः समम्॥
en: The qualities having their origin in Darkness, those that originate from Ignorance, and those stainless ones characterised by purity, form as it were the seed from which all embodied creatures have sprung. Amongst these, the quality of Goodness alone is the cause through which persons of pure souls succeed in attaining to Liberation.

sn: तस्मादात्मवता वर्षं रजश्च तम एव च। रजस्तमोभ्यां निर्मुक्तं सत्त्वं निर्मलतामियात्॥
en: A person of pure soul, therefore, should cast off all the qualities begotten of Darkness and Ignorance. Then again when the quality of Goodness becomes frced from those of Darkness and Ignorance it shines the more.

sn: अथवा मन्त्रवढ्युरात्मादानाय दुष्कृतम्। स वै हेतुरनादाने शुद्धधर्मानुपालने॥
en: Some say that sacrifices and other acts performed with the help of Mantras, and which bring about the purification of the Soul, are evil or cruel acts. On the other hand, those acts are the chief instruments for dissociating the Soul from all worldly attachments, and for the observance of the religion of peace.

sn: रजसाधर्मयुक्तानि कार्याण्यपि समाप्नुते। अर्थयुक्तानि चात्यर्थं कामान् सर्वांश्च सेवते॥
en: Through the influence of the qualities born of Darkness, all impious acts are perpetrated and all earthly acts as well as such acts as originate from desire are performed.

sn: तमसा लोभयुक्तानि क्रोधजानि च सेवते। हिंसाविहाराभिरतस्तन्द्रीनिद्रासमन्वितः॥
en: Through qualities born of Ignorance, one does all acts fraught with cupidity and springing from anger. In consequence of the attribute of Ignorance, one feels sleep and procrastination and becomes addicted to all acts of crucily and carnality.

sn: सत्त्वस्थः सात्त्विकान् भावाशुद्धान् पश्यति संश्रितः। स देही विमलः श्रीमाश्रद्धाविद्यासमन्वितः॥
en: That person, however, who endued with faith and scriptural knowledge, follows the quality of Goodness, attends only to all good things and becomes endued with beauty and a soul free froin every corruption.

sn: भीष्म उवाच रजसा साध्यते मोहस्तमसा भरतर्षभ। क्रोधलोभौ भयं दर्प एतेषां सादनाच्छुचिः॥
en: Bhishma said Delusion or loss of judgement arises from the quality of Darkness. Anger, cupidity, fear and pride originate from the quality of Ignorance, O foremost of Bharata's race. When all these are destroyed, one becomes pure.

sn: परमं परमात्मानं देवमक्षयमव्ययम्। विष्णुमव्यक्तसंस्थानं विदुस्तं देवसत्तमम्॥
en: By obtaining purity, a person acquires the knowledge of the Supreme Soul which is effulgent, incapable of deterioration, without change, pervading all things, having the unmanifest for his refuge, and the foremost of all the gods.

sn: तस्य मायापिनद्धाङ्गा नष्टज्ञाना विचेतसः। मानवा ज्ञानसम्मोहात् ततः क्रोधं प्रयान्ति वै॥
en: By His illusory power men fall away from knowledge and become senseless, and their knowledge being darkened, yield to anger.

sn: क्रोधात् काममवाप्याथ लोभमोहौ च मानवाः। मानदर्पावहङ्कारमहङ्कारात् ततः क्रियाः॥
en: From anger, they become subject to desire. From desire originate cupidity, delusion, vanity, pride and selfishness. From such selfishness proceed various sorts of acts.

sn: क्रियाभिः स्नेहसम्बन्धात्स्नेहाच्छोकमनन्तरम्। सुखदुःखक्रियारम्भाज्जन्माजन्मकृतक्षणाः॥
en: From acts originate various ties of affection and from those ties of affection springs sorrow or misery and from acts imbued with joy and sorrow proceeds the liability to birth and death.

sn: जन्मतो गर्भवासं तु शुक्रशोणितसम्भवम्। पुरीषमूत्रविक्लेदं शोणितप्रभवाविलम्॥
en: On account of the obligation of birth, one is compelled to live within the womb,—for the union of vital seed and blood. Living there is defiled with excreta urine and phlegm, and always fouled with blood that is created there.

sn: तृष्णाभिभूतस्तैर्बद्धस्तानेवाभिपरिप्लवन्। संसारतन्त्रवाहिन्यस्तत्र बुद्ध्येत योषितः॥
en: Overwhelmed by thirst, the Intelligence Soul becomes fettered by anger and the rest that have been described above. It seeks, however, to escape those evils. In this respect, women must be considered as instruments which set the stream of Creation a going.

sn: प्रकृत्या क्षेत्रभूतास्ता नराः क्षेत्रज्ञलक्षणाः। तस्मादेवाविशेषेण नरोऽतीयाद् विशेषतः॥
en: By their nature, women are Kshetra, and men are Kshetrajna in respect of qualities. Therefore, wise persons should not pursue women especially.

sn: कृत्या ह्येता घोररूपा मोहयन्त्यविचक्षणान्। रजस्यन्तर्हिता मूर्तिरिन्द्रियाणां सनातनी॥
en: Indeed, women are like dreadful Mantra powers. They stupefy persons shorn of wisdom. They are sunk in the quality of Darkness. They are the eternal embodiment of the senses.

sn: तस्मात् तदात्मकाद् रागाद् बीजाज्जायन्ति जन्तवः। स्वदेहजानस्वसंज्ञान् यद्वदङ्गात् कृमीस्त्यजेत्। स्व संज्ञानस्वकांस्तद्वत् सुतसंज्ञान् कृमींस्त्यजेत्॥
en: On account of the strong desire that men cherish for women, offspring proceed from them, due to the action of the seminal fluid. As one throws off from his person such vermin as are born there but as are not on that account any part of oneself, so should one cast off those verinin of one's body that are called children, who, though regarded as one's own, are not his own in sooth.

sn: शुक्रतो रसतश्चैव देहाज्जायन्ति जन्तवः। स्वभावात् कर्मयोगाद् वा तानुपेक्षेत बुद्धिमान्॥
en: From the seminal fluid and sweat creatures spring from the body, influenced by pristino acts or in the course of nature. Therefore, a wise man should feel no regard for them.

sn: रजस्तमसि पर्यस्तं सत्त्वं च रजसि स्थितम्। ज्ञानाधिष्ठानमव्यक्तं बुद्ध्यहङ्कारलक्षणम्॥ तद् बीजं देहिनामाहुस्तद् बीजं जीवसंज्ञितम्। कर्मणा कालयुक्तेन संसारपरिवर्तनम्॥
en: The quality of Darkness rests on that of Ignorance. The quality of Goodness, again, rests on that of Darkness. Darkness which is unmanifest overspreads itself on Knowledge, and creates the phenomena of Intelligence and Consciousness has been described as the seed of individual Souls. That, again, which is the seed of such knowledge is called the Jiya (or Individual Soul). On account of acts and the virtue of time, the Soul goes through birth and repeated rounds of re-birth.

sn: रमत्ययं यथा स्वप्ने मनसा देहवानिव। कर्मग:गुणैर्देही गर्भे तदुपलभ्यते॥
en: As in a dream the Soul plays as if invested with a body which, of course, is due to the action of the mind, similarly, it gets in the mother's womb a body in consequence of qualities and propensities created by pristine deeds.

sn: कर्मणा बीजभूतेन चोद्यते यद् यदिन्द्रियम्। जायते तदहङ्काराद् रागयुक्तेन चेतसा॥
en: Whatever senses, while it is there, are awakened by pristine deeds as the operating cause, become created in Consciousness in consequence of the mind co-existing with attachments.

sn: शब्दरागाच्छ्रात्रमस्य जायते भावितात्मनः। रूपरागात् तथा चक्षुघ्रीणं गन्धचिकीर्षया॥
en: On account of the past thoughts of sound that are awakened in it, the Soul, subjected to such influences, gets the organ of hearing. Similarly, from attachment to forms, its eye is produced, and from its desire after smell its organ of smelling.

sn: स्पर्शने त्वक् तथा वायुः प्राणापानव्यपाश्रयः। व्यानोदानौ समानश्च पञ्चधा देहयापनम्॥
en: From thoughts of touch it acquires the skin. Likewise, the five vital airs are acquired by it, viz., Prana, Apana, Vyana, Udana, and Samana, which make the body agoing.

sn: संजातैर्जायते गात्रैः कर्मजैर्वम॑णा वृतः। दुःखाद्यन्तैर्दुःखमध्यैर्नरः शारीरमानसैः॥
en: Encased in body with all limbs fully developed on account of pristine deeds, the Soul takes birth, with both physical and mental sorrow, in the beginning, iniddle, and end.

sn: दुःखं विद्यादुपादानादभिमानाच्च वर्धते। त्यागात् तेभ्यो निरोधः स्यान्निरोधज्ञो विमुच्यते॥
en: It should be known that sorrow originates from the very formation of body in the womb). It increases with the idea of self. From renuciation of these, sorrow is destroyed. He who knows sorrow's end attains to Liberation.

sn: इन्द्रियाणां रजस्येव प्रलयप्रभवावुभौ। परीक्ष्य संचरेद् विद्वान् यथावच्छास्त्रचक्षुषा॥
en: Both the origin and the destruction of the senses depend on the quality of Darkness. A wise man should act with proper scrutiny with the help of the eye of the scriptures.

sn: ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थान्नोपसर्पन्त्यतर्षुलम्। हीनैश्च करणैर्देही न देहं पुनरर्हति॥
en: The senses of knowledge, if they succeed in acquiring all their objects, can never stupefy the man who is without thirst. The embodied Soul, by making its senses weak, is saved from the obligation of re-birth.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्रोपायं प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावच्छास्त्रचक्षुषा। तत्त्वज्ञानाच्चरन् राजन् प्राप्नुयात्परमां गतिम्॥
en: 'I shall now describe to you the means of conquering the senses as seen with the eye of the scriptures. A person, O king, will attain to the highest and by shaping his conduct accordingly.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पुरुषः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते। पुरुषेभ्यो द्विजानाहुर्द्विजेभ्यो मन्त्रदर्शिनः॥
en: Amongst all living creatures man is said to be the foremost. Among men, the twice-born, persons well read in the Vedas are the foremost.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: सर्वभूतात्मभूतास्ते सर्वज्ञाः सर्वदर्शिनः। ब्राह्मणा वेदशास्त्रज्ञास्तत्त्वार्थगतनिश्चयाः॥
en: These last are considered as the souls of all living creatures. Indeed, those Brahmanas who have mastered the Vedas are considered as allseeing and omniscient. They are persons who have become conversant with Brahma.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: नेत्रहीनो यथा ह्येकः कृच्छ्राणि लभतेऽध्वनि। ज्ञानहीनस्तथा लोके तस्माज्ज्ञानविदोऽधिकाः॥
en: As a blind man, without a guide, meets with many difficulties on a road, so has a person shorn of knowledge to meet with many impediments in the world. Therefore those who are endued with knowledge arc considered as superior to the rest.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: तांस्तानुपासते धर्मान् धर्मकामा यथागमम्। न त्वेषामर्थसामान्यमन्तरेण गुणानिमान्॥
en: Those who wish to acquire virtue practise various rites according to the scriptural injunctions. They do not, however, attain to Liberation. They only acquire those good qualities which I shall presently mention.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: वाग्देहमनसां शौचं क्षमा सत्यं धृतिः स्मृतिः। सर्वधर्मेषु धर्मज्ञा ज्ञापयन्ति गुणाञ्छुभान्॥
en: Purity of speech, of body, and of mind, forgiveness, truth, firmness and intelligence,-these good qualities are shown by pious persons who observe both kinds of religion.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: यदिदं ब्रह्मणो रूपं ब्रह्मचर्यमिति स्मृतम्। परं तत् सर्वधर्मेभ्यस्तेन यान्ति परां गतिम्॥
en: What is called Brahmacharya is considered as the means of attaining to Brahma. That is the foremost of all religions. It is by the practice of that religion that one acquires the highest end.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: लिङ्गसंयोगहीनं यच्छब्दस्पर्शविवर्जितम्। श्रोत्रेण श्रवणं चैव चक्षुषा चैव दर्शनम्॥
en: Brahmacharya has no connection with the five vital airs, mind, understanding, the five senses of perception, and the five senses of action. It is, therefore, free from all the perceptions that the senses give. It is heard only as a word, and its form, is not seen, but can only be conceived.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: वाक्सम्भाषाप्रवृत्तं यत् तन्मनःपरिवर्जितम्। बुद्ध्या चाध्यवसीयीत ब्रह्मचर्यमकल्मषम्॥
en: It is a state of existence only on the mind. It has no connection with the senses. That pure state should be attained to by the understanding alone.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: सम्यग्वृत्तिर्ब्रह्मलोकं प्राप्नुयान्मध्यमः सुरान्। द्विजाग्रयो जायते विद्वान् कन्यसी वृत्तिमास्थितः॥
en: He who practises it duly attains to Brahma; he who practises it half and half, attains to the status of the gods; while be who practises it indifferently, is born among Brahmanas and possessed of learning attains to eminence.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: सुदुष्करं ब्रह्मचर्यमुपायं तत्र मे शृणु। सम्प्रदीप्तमुदीर्णं च निगृह्णीयाद् द्विजो रजः॥
en: Brahmacharya is highly difficult to practise. Listen now to the means thereof. That twiceborn one who follows it should subdue the quality of Darkness as soon as it begins to show itself or as soon as it begins to be powerful.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: योषितां न कथा श्राव्या न निरीक्ष्या निरम्बराः। कथञ्चिद् दर्शनादासां दुर्बलानां विशेद्रजः॥
en: One who has taken that yow should not speak with women. He should never look at a naked woman. The sight of women, under even indifferent circumstances, excites the passion of all weak-minded men.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: रागोत्पन्नश्चरेत् कृच्छं महार्तिः प्रविशेदपः। मग्नः स्वप्ने च मनसा विर्जपेदघमर्षणम्॥
en: If a person feels a desire for women rising in his heart, he should observe the vow called Krichcchra and also pass three days in water. If desire is formed even in a dream, one should, diving in water, mentally repeat for three times the three Riks by Aghamarshana.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: पाप्मानं निर्दहेदेवमन्तर्भूतरजोमयम्। ज्ञानयुक्तेन मनसा संततेन विचक्षणः॥
en: That wise man who follows this VOW should, with a liberal and enlightened mind, consume the sins in his mind which are created by the quality of Darkness.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: कुणपामध्यसंयुक्तं यद्वदच्छिद्रबन्धनम्। तद्वद् देहगतं विद्यादात्मानं देहबन्धनम्॥
en: As the passage that carries away the refuge of the body is very closely connected with the body, so the embodied Soul is very closely connected with the body that confines it.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: वातपित्तकफाद् रक्तं त्वडमांसं स्नायुमस्थि च। मज्जां देहं शिराजालैस्तर्पयन्ति रसा नृणाम्॥
en: The different sorts of juices, passing through the network of arteries, nourish men's wind, bile, phlegm, blood, skin, flesh, intestines, bones, marrow, and the whole body.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: दश विद्याद् धमन्योऽत्र पञ्चेन्द्रियगुणावहाः। याभिः सूक्ष्माः प्रतायन्ते धमन्योऽन्याः सहस्रशः॥
en: Know that there are ten principle canals. These help the functions of the five senses. From those ten issue out thousands of other passages that are minuter in form.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: एवमेताः शिरा नद्यो रसोदा देहसागरम्। तर्पयन्ति यथाकालमापगा इव सागरम्॥
en: Like rivers filling the ocean at the proper time, all these channels, containing juices, nourish the body.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: मध्ये च हृदयस्यैका शिरा तत्र मनोवहा। शुक्र संकल्पजं नृणां सर्वगात्रैर्विमुञ्चति॥
en: There is a channel leading to the heart called Manovaha. It draws from every part of the human body the seminal fluid which is born of desire.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: सर्वगात्रप्रतायिन्यस्तस्या ह्यनुगताः शिराः। नेत्रयोः प्रतिपद्यन्ते वहन्त्यस्तैजसं गुणम्॥
en: Numberless other channels issuing from that principal one extend into every part of the body and bearing the element of heat cause the sense of vision (and the rest).

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: पयस्यन्तर्हितं सर्पिर्यद्वन्निर्मथ्यते खजैः। शुक्र निर्मथ्यते तद्वद् देहसंकल्पजैः खजैः॥
en: As the butter that lies within milk is churned up by churing rods, so the desires that are created in the mind draw together the vital sced that lies within the body.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: स्वप्नेऽप्येवं यथाभ्येति मन:संकल्पजं रजः। शुक्र संकल्पजं देहात् सृजत्यस्य मनोवहा॥
en: In the midst of even our dreams passion originating in imagination attacks the mind, with the result that the passage already named, viz., Manovaha, throws out the seminal fluid born of desire.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: महर्षिर्भगवानत्रिर्वेद तच्छुक्रसम्भवम्। त्रिबीजमिन्द्रदैवल्यं तस्मादिन्द्रियमुच्यते॥
en: The great and divine Rishi Atri is a inaster of the subject of the generation of the vital secd. The juices that are produced by food, the passage called Manovaha, and the desire that is born of imagination,-these three are the causes which create the seminal fluid which has Indra for its presiding god. The passion that helps the passing out of this fluid is, therefore, called Indriya.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: ये वै शुक्रगति विद्युभूतसंकरकारिकाम्। विरागा दग्धदोषास्ते नाप्नुयुर्देहसम्भवम्॥
en: Those persons, who know that the course of seminal fluid is the cause of intermixture of castes, are men of controlled passions. Their sins are considered to have been consumed, and they are never subjected to re-birth.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: गुणानां साम्यमागम्य मनसैव मनोवहम्। देहकर्मा नुदन् प्राणानन्तकाले विमुच्यते॥
en: He who performs action simply for the purpose of maintaining his body, reducing with the help of the mind the qualities into a state of equilibrium, and brings at his last moments the vital airs to the channel called Manovaha, is freed from re-birth.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: भविता मनसो ज्ञानं मन एव प्रजायते। ज्योतिष्मद्विरजो नित्यं मन्त्रसिद्धं महात्मनाम्॥
en: The Mind is sure to acquire Knowledge. It is the Mind which assumes the form of all things. Acquiring success through meditation, the minds of all great persons, become freed from desire, eternal, and shining.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: तस्मात् तदभिघाताय कर्म कुर्यादकल्मषम्। रजस्तमश्च हित्वेह यथेष्टां गतिमाप्नुयात्॥
en: Therefore, for destroying the mind, one should perform only pure deeds, and frecing himself from the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance, one is sure to acquire a very desirable end.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: तरुणाधिगतं ज्ञानं जरादुर्बलतां गतम्। विपक्वबुद्धिः कालेन आदत्ते मानसं बलम्॥
en: Knowledge (ordinarily) acquired in younger days becomes weakened with decrepitude. Through the good effects of past lives, a person, however, of ripe understanding succeeds in killing his desires.

description: The means of conquering the senses
sn: सुदुर्गमिव पन्थानमतीत्य गुणबन्धनम्। यथा पश्येत् तथा दोषानतीत्यामृतमश्नुते॥
en: Such a person, by getting over the fetters of the body and the senses like a traveller crossing a path full of impediments, and transgressing all faults he sees, succeeds in testing the ambrosia (of Liberation.)

sn: भीष्म उवाच दुरन्तेष्विन्द्रियार्थेषु सक्ताः सीदन्ति जन्तवः। ये त्वसक्ता महात्मानस्ते यान्ति परमां गतिम्॥
en: Bhishma said By being attached to objects of the senses which are always imbued with evil, living creatures become helpless. Those great persons, however, who are not attached to them, acquire the greatest end.

sn: जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्व्याधिभिर्मानसक्लमैः। दृष्ट्वैव संततं लोकं घटेन्मोक्षाय बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Seeing the world beset with the evils formed by birth, death, decrepitude, sorrow, disease, and anxieties, the man of intelligence should try for the attainment of Liberation.

sn: वाड्मनोभ्यां शरीरेण शुचिः स्यादनहंकृतः। प्रशान्तो ज्ञानवान् भिक्षुनिरपेक्षश्चरेत् सुखम्॥
en: He should be pure in words, thought and body; he should be shorn of pride. Of tranquil soul and endued with knowledge, he should live like a mendicant, and pursue happiness without being attached to any wordły object.

sn: अथवा मनसः सङ्गं पश्येद् भूतानुकम्पया। तत्राप्युपेक्षां कुर्वीत ज्ञात्वा कर्मफलं जगत्॥
en: Again, if his mind is filled with attachment for mercy to creatures, he should, seeing that the universe is the result of acts, one should show indifference even to mercy itself.

sn: यत् कृतं स्याच्छुभं कर्म पापं वा यदि वाश्नुते। तस्माच्छुभानि कर्माणि कुर्याद् वा बुद्धिकर्मभिः॥
en: Whatever good acts are done, or whatever sin is committed, the actor reaps the points thereof. Hence, one should, in words, thought, and deed, do only good acts.

sn: अहिंसा सत्यवचनं सर्वभूतेषु चार्जयम्। क्षमा चैवाप्रमादश्च यस्यैते स सुखी भवेत्॥
en: He enjoys happiness who practises abstention from injuring (others), truthfulness of speech, honesty towards all creatures, and forgiveness, and who is never careless.

sn: यश्चैनं परमं धर्मं सर्वभूतसुखावहम्। दुःखान्निःसरणं वेद सर्वज्ञः स सुखी भवेत्॥
en: Hence one, exercising his intelligence, should fix his mind, after training it, on peace towards all creatures.

sn: तस्मात् समाहितं बुद्ध्या मनो भूतेषु धारयेत्। नापध्यायेन स्पृहयेन्नाबद्धं चिन्तयेदसत्॥
en: That man who considers the practice of the virtues mentioned above as the greatest duty as securing the happiness of all creatures, and as destroying all sorts of sorrow, is possessed of the greatest knowledge, and succeeds in acquiring happiness. Hence, one should, exercising his intelligence, fix his mind, after training it, on peace towards all creatures.

sn: अथामोधप्रयत्नेन मनो ज्ञाने निवेशयत्। वाचामोघप्रयासेन मनोज्ञं तत् प्रवर्तते॥
en: One should never think of committing evil to others, One should not covet what is far above his power to acquire. One should not fix his thoughts on objects which are not real. One should, on the other hand, direct mind towards knowledge by continued exertions.

sn: विवक्षता च सद्वाक्यं धर्मं सूक्ष्ममवेक्षता। सत्यां वाचमहिंस्रां च वदेदनपवादिनीम्॥ कल्कापेतामपरुषामनृशंसामपैशुनाम्। ईदृगल्पं च वक्तव्यमविक्षिप्तेन चेतसा॥ वाक्प्रबद्धो हि संसारो विरागाद् व्याहरेद् यदि। बुद्ध्याप्यनुगृहीतेन मनसा कर्म तामसम्॥ रजोभूतैर्हि करणैः कर्मणि प्रतिपद्यते। स दुःखं प्राप्य लोकेऽस्मिन् नरकायोपपद्यते। तस्मान्मनोवाक्शरीरै राचरेद् धैर्यमात्मनः॥
en: With the help of the injunctions of the Shrutis and of continued efforts calculated to bring success, Knowledge is sure to originate. One who is desirous of saying good words or observing a religion which is purged off of all impurities, should speak only truth which is not fraught with any malice or censure. One who has got a sound heart should speak words which are not fraught with dishonesty, which are not harsh, which are not cruel, which are not evil, and which are not characterised by garrulity. The universe is bound in words. If a person disposed to renunciation he should proclaim, with a humble mind and a cleansed understanding, his own evil deeds. He who performs action, urged there to by propensities pervaded by the quality of Darkness, suffers much misery in this world and at last sinks into hell. One should, therefore, practise selfcontrol in body, words and mind.

sn: प्रकीर्णमेषभारं हि यद्वद् धार्येत दस्युभिः। प्रतिलोमां दिशं बुद्ध्वा संसारमबुधास्तथा॥
en: Ignorant persons bearing the weight of the world are like robbers laden with their booty of straggling sheep. The latter always avoid roads which are not favourable to them,

sn: तमेव च यथा दस्युः क्षिप्त्वा गच्छेच्छिवां दिशम्। तथा रजस्तमःकर्माण्युत्सृज्य प्राप्नुयाच्छुभम्॥
en: Indeed, as robbers have to throw away their booty if they wish safety, so should a person cast off all acts induced by Darkness and Ignorance, if he is to acquire happiness.

sn: नि:संदिग्धमनीहो वै मुक्तः सर्वपरिग्रहैः। विविक्तचारी लघ्वाशी तपस्वी नियतेन्द्रियः॥ ज्ञानदग्धपरिक्लेशः प्रयोगरतिरात्मवान्। निष्प्रचारेण मनसा परं तदधिगच्छति॥
en: Forsooth, a person who is shorn of desire, free from the fetters of the world, contented to live in solitude, abstemious in diet, devoted to penances, and with senses under restraint, who has consumed all his sorrows by knowledge, who finds pleasure in practising Yoga and who has a cleansed soul, succeeds, on account of his mind being withdrawn into itself, in attaining to Brahina or Liberation.

sn: धृतिमानात्मवान् बुद्धिं निगृह्णीयादसंशयम्। मनो बुद्ध्या निगृह्णीयाद् विषयान्मनसाऽऽत्मनः॥
en: One endued with patience and a pure soul should, forsooth, control his understanding. With the understanding, one should next restrain mind, and then with the mind overpower the objects of the senses.

sn: निगृहीतेन्द्रियस्यास्य कुर्वाणस्य मनो वशे। देवतास्तत् प्रकाशन्ते हृष्टा यान्ति तमीश्वरम्॥
en: Upon the mind being thus restrained and the senses being all subdued, the senses will shine and gladly enter into Brahma.

sn: ताभिः संयुक्तमनसो ब्रह्म तत् सम्प्रकाशते। शनैश्चोपगते सत्त्वे ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते॥
en: When one's senses are withdrawn into the mind, the result becomes that Brahma becomes manifested in it. Indeed, when the senses are destroyed, and the soul returns to the quality of pure existence, it is regarded as being transformed into Brahma.

sn: अथवा न प्रवर्तेत योगतन्त्रैरुपक्रमेत्। येन तन्त्रयतस्तन्त्रं वृत्तिः स्यात् तत् तदाचरेत्॥
en: Then again, one should never show his Yoga power. On the other hand, one should always try to restrain his senses by practising the rules of Yoga. Indeed, one engaged in the practice of Yoga should do all those acts by which his conduct and nature may become pure.

sn: कणकुल्माषपिण्याकशाकयावकसक्तवः। तथा मूलफलं भक्ष्यं पर्यायेणोपयोजयेत्॥
en: One should rather live upon broken grains of corn, ripe beans, dry cakes of seeds from which the oil has been pressed out, potherbs, half-ripe barley, flour of fried pulses, fruits, and roots, secured by begging.

sn: आहारनियमं चैव देशे काले च सात्त्विकम्। तत् परीक्ष्यानुवर्तेत तत्प्रवृत्त्यनुपूर्वकम्॥
en: Reflecting upon the characteristics of time and place, one should according to his inclinations observe, after proper search, vows and rules about fasts.

sn: प्रवृत्तं नोपरुन्धेत शनैरग्निमिवेन्धयेत्। ज्ञानान्वितं तथा ज्ञानमर्कवत् सम्प्रकाशते।॥
en: One should not suspend a rite that has been begun. Like one slowly creating a fire, one should by and by perform an act that is prompted by knowledge. By so doing, Brahma by and by shines in one like the Sun.

sn: ज्ञानाधिष्ठानमज्ञानं त्रौंल्लोकानधितिष्ठति। विज्ञानानुगतं ज्ञानमज्ञानेनापकृष्यते॥
en: The Ignorance which rests on Knowledge, extends its influence over all the three states. The knowledge, again, that follows the Understanding, is attacked by Ignorance.

sn: पृथक्त्वात् सम्प्रयोगाच्च नासूयुर्वेद शाश्वतम्। स तयोरपवर्गज्ञो वीतरागो विमुच्यते॥
en: The evil-hearted person cannot acquire a knowledge of the Self for his considering it as united with the three states although in reality it transcends them all. When, however, he perceives the limits under which the two, viz., union with the three states and separation from them are manifested, it is then that he becomes shorn of attachment and attains to Liberation.

sn: ततो वीतजरामृत्युर्ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्म सनातनम्। अमृतं तदवाप्नोति यत् तदक्षरमव्ययम्॥
en: When such an apprehension has been acquired, one transcends the effects of age, rises superior the consequences of decrepitude and death, and obtains Brahma which is eternal, deathless, immutable, and underetiorating. to

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: भीष्म उवाच निष्कल्मषं ब्रह्मचर्यमिच्छता चरितुं सदा। निद्रा सर्वात्मना त्याज्या स्वप्नदोषानवेक्षता॥
en: Bhishma said The Yogin who wishes to always practise pure Brahmacharya and who is cognizant of the faults attaching to dreams, should, with his whole heart, try to give up sleep.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: स्वप्ने हि रजसा देही तमसा चाभिभूयते। देहान्तरमिवापन्नश्चरत्युपगतस्पृहः॥
en: In dreams, the embodied soul, possessed by the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance, seems to become possessed of another body and move and act influenced by desire.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: ज्ञानाभ्यासाज्जागरणं जिज्ञासार्थमनन्तरम्। विज्ञानाभिनिवेशात्तु स जागर्त्यनिशं सदा॥
en: On account of application for acquiring knowledge and of continued reflection and recapitulation, the Yogin remains always awake. Indeed, the Yogin can keep himself continually awake by giving himself up to knowledge.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: अत्राह को न्वयं भावः स्वप्ने विषयवानिव। प्रलीनैरिन्द्रियैर्देही वर्तते देहवानिव॥
en: Regarding this subject it has been asked what its this state in which the embodied creature thinks himself encircled by and engaged in objects and acts? It is true that the embodied being, with its senses really suspended, still considers itself to be possessed of body with all the sense of knowledge and of action.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: अत्रोच्यते तथा ह्येतद् वेद योगेश्वरो हरिः। तथैतदुपपन्नार्थं वर्णयन्ति महर्षयः॥
en: It is said that that master of Yoga, named Hari, perceives truly how it happens. The great Rishis say that the explanation given by Hari is correct and reasonable.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: इन्द्रियाणां श्रमात् स्वप्नमाहुः सर्वगतं बुधाः। मनसस्त्वप्रलीनत्वात् तत् तदाहुर्निदर्शनम्॥
en: The learned says that it is on account of the senses being exhausted with fatigue, dreams are seen by all creatures. The mind, however, never becomes inactive and hence arise dreams. This considered as their principal cause.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: कार्ये व्यासक्तमनसः संकल्पो जाग्रतो ह्यपि। यद्वन्मनोरथैश्वर्यं स्वप्ने तद्वन्मनोगतम्॥
en: As the imagination of a person who is awake and engaged in acts, is due only to the creative power of the mind, similarly, the impressions in a dream belong only to the mind.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: संस्काराणामसंख्यानां कामात्मा तदवाप्नुयात्। मनस्यन्तर्हितं सर्वं स वेदोत्तमपूरुषः॥
en: A person with desire and attachment receives those imaginations based upon the impressions of numberless pristine lives. Nothing, that impresses the mind once is ever lost, and the Soul being cognisant of all those impressions makes them appear.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: गुणानामपि यद्येतत् कर्मणा चाप्युपस्थितम्। तत् तच्छंसन्ति भूतानि मनो यद्भावितं यथा।॥
en: Whichever among the three qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance is caused by the influence of pristine acts and by whichever amongst them the mind is affected for the time being in whatever way, the elements in their subtile forms) or indicate accordingly (in the way of images).

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: ततस्तमुपसर्पन्ति गुणा राजसतामसाः। सात्त्विका वा यथायोगमानन्तर्यफलोदयम्॥
en: After images have thus been created the particular quality of Goodness Darkness or Ignorance that inay have been brought by pristine acts rises in the mind and produces its last result, viz., happiness or misery.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: ततः पश्यन्त्यसम्बुद्ध्या वातपित्तकफोत्तरान्। रजस्तमोगतै वैस्तदण्याहु१रत्ययम्॥
en: Those images originating principally wind, bile, and phlegm, which men apprehend through ignorance and in consequence of tendency pervaded by Darkness and Ignorance, cannot, it has been said, be easily discarded.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: प्रसन्नैरिन्द्रियैर्यद् यत् संकल्पयति मानसम्। तत् तत् स्वप्नेऽप्युगते मनो हृष्यन्निरीक्षते॥
en: (When one is awake) whatever objects a person perceives in the mind through the senses in a clear state are apprehended by the mind in dreams while the senses are inactive.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: व्यापकं सर्वभूतेषु वर्ततेऽप्रतिघं मनः। आत्मप्रभावात् विद्यात् सर्वा ह्यात्मनि देवताः॥
en: The Mind exists without obstruction in all things. This is due to the nature of the Soul. The Soul should be comprehended. All the elements and the objects they form exist in the Soul.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: मनस्यन्तर्हितं द्वारं देहमास्थाय मानुषम्। यद् यत् सदसदव्यक्तं स्वपित्यस्मिन्निदर्शनम्। सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्थं तमध्यात्मगुणं विदुः॥
en: In the state called dreamless sleep the manifest human body which, of course, is the door of dreams, disappears in the mind. Possessing the body the mind enters the Soul which is unmanifest and upon which all existent and non-existent things depend, and becomes a wakeful witness with certainly of apprehension. Thus living in pure Consciousness which is the soul of all things, it is considered by the learned as transcending both Consciousness and all things in the universe.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: लिप्सेत मनसा यश्च संकल्पादैश्वरं गुणम्। आत्मप्रसादं तं विद्यात् सर्वा ह्यात्मनि देवताः॥
en: That Yogin who by desire covets any of the divine qualities (of Knowledge or renunciation, etc.,) should regard a pure mind to be at one with the object of his desire. All things exist in a pure mind or soul.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: एवं हि तरसा युक्तमर्कवत् तमसः परम्। त्रैलोक्यप्रकृतिदेही तमसोऽन्ते महेश्वरः॥
en: This is the result acquired by one who practises penances. That Yogin, however, who has got over Darkness or ignorance, is endued with transcending effulgence. When Darkness or Ignorance has been got over, the embodied Soul becomes Supreme Brahma, the cause of the universe.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: तपो ह्यधिष्ठितं देवैस्तयोघ्नमसुरैस्तमः। एतद् देवासुरैर्गुप्तं तदाहुनिलक्षणम्॥
en: The deities have penances and Vedic rites. Darkness (or pride and cruelty), which destroys the former, has been adopted by the Asuras. This viz., Brahma, which has been said to have knowledge only for its quality, is difficult of attainment by either the gods or the Asuras.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति देवासुरगुणान् विदुः। सत्त्वं देवगुणं विद्यादितरावासुरौ गुणौ॥
en: It should be known that the qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance belong to the gods and the Asuras. Goodness is the quality of the gods; while the two others belong to the Asuras.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: ब्रह्म तत् परम् ज्ञानममृतं ज्योतिरक्षरम्। विदुर्भावितात्मानस्ते यान्ति परमां गतिम्॥
en: Brahma transcends all those qualities. It is pure Knowledge. It is immortality. It is pure effulgence. it is undecaying. Those persons of pure souls who know Brahma attain to the highest end.

description: A Yogin should give up sleep.
sn: हेतुमच्छक्यमाख्यातुमेतावज्ज्ञानचक्षुषा। प्रत्याहारेण वा शक्यमक्षरं ब्रह्म वेदितुम्॥
en: One having knowledge for his eye can say this much with the help of reason and analogy. Brahma which is indestructible can be comprehended by only withdrawing the senses and the mind.

sn: भीष्म उवाच न स वेद परं ब्रह्म यो न वेद चतुष्टयम्। व्यक्ताव्यक्तं च यत् तत्त्वं सम्प्रोक्तं परमर्षिणा॥
en: Bhishma said 'He does not know Brahma who does not know the four topics, namely, dreams, dreamless sleep, immanent, and transcendent Brahma, as also what is Manifest (viz., the body), and what is Unmanifest (the intelligence-soul), which the great Rishi (Narayana) has described as Tattvam (pure principle).

sn: व्यक्तं मृत्युमुखं विद्यादव्यक्तमृतं पदम्। प्रवृत्तिलक्षणं धर्ममृषिर्नारायणोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: That which is manifest is subject to death. That which is unmanifest transcends, death. The Rishi Narayana has described the religion of inclination.

sn: तत्रैवावस्थितं सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्। निवृत्तिलक्षणं धर्ममव्यक्तं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्॥
en: Upon that depends the entire universe with its mobile and immobile creatures. The religion of disinclination again leads to the unmanifest and eternal Brahma.

sn: प्रवृत्तिलक्षणं धर्मं प्रजापतिरथाब्रवीत्। प्रवृत्तिः पुनरावृत्तिनिवृत्तिः परमा गतिः॥
en: The Creator (Brahman) has described the religion of inclination. Inclination indicates rebirth or return. Disinclination on the other hand, indicates the highest end.

sn: तां गतिं परमामेति निवृत्तिपरमो मुनिः। ज्ञानतत्त्वपरो नित्यं शुभाशुभनिदर्शकः॥
en: The ascetic who wish to discriminate exactly between good and evil, who is always bent on conceiving the nature of the Soul, and who devotes himself to the religion of disinclination, attains to that high end.

sn: तदेवमेतौ विज्ञेयावव्यक्तपुरुषावुभौ। अव्यक्तपुरुषाभ्यां तु यत् स्यादन्यन्महत्तरम्॥ तं विशेषमवेक्षेत विशेषेण विचक्षणः। अनाद्यन्तावुभावेतावलिङ्गौ चाप्युभावपि॥
en: One who wishes to accomplish this, should know both the Unmanifest and Purusha of which I shall speak now. That, again, which is different from both the Unmanifest and Purusha, and which transcends them both, and which is distinguished from all beings, should be particularly seen by an intelligent man. Both, Prakriti and Purusha are without beginning and without end. Both are incapable of being known by their likes.

sn: उभौ नित्यावविचलौ महद्भ्यश्च महत्तरौ। सामान्यमेतदुभयोरेवं ह्यन्यद्विशेषणम्॥
en: Both are eternal and indestructible. Both are greater than the greatest. They are similar in these. There are point of dissimilarity again between them.

sn: प्रकृत्या सर्गधर्मिण्या तथा त्रिगुणधर्मया। विपरीतमतो विद्यात् क्षेत्रज्ञस्य स्वलक्षणम्॥
en: Prakriti is endued with the three qualities. It is also engaged in creation. The true attributes of Kshetrajna (Purusha or the Soul) are different.

sn: प्रकृतेश्च विकाराणां द्रष्टारमगुणान्वितम्। अग्राह्यौ पुरुषावेतावलिङ्गत्वादसंहतौ॥
en: Purusha apprehends all the changes of Prakriti (but cannot be apprehended himself.) He transcends all qualities. As regards Purusha and the Supreme Soul again, both of them cannot be comprehended. Again for their both being without qualities by which they can be distinguished, both are greatly distinguished froin all else.

sn: संयोगलक्षणोत्पत्तिः कर्मणा गृह्यते यथा। करणैः कर्मनिवृत्तिः कर्ता यद् यद् विचेष्टते। कीर्त्यते शब्दसंज्ञाभिः कोऽहमेषोऽप्यसाविति॥
en: The creation is the result of relation between Prakriti and Purusha (the soul), but we understand it by action. All movements come through the senses by person. "Who, I, This" etc. are only wordily statements.

sn: उष्णीषवान् यथा वस्त्रैस्त्रिभिर्भवति संवृतः। संवृतोऽयं तथा देही सत्त्वराजसतामसैः॥
en: A person putting on a turban has his head circled with three folds of a piece of cloth. Similarly the embodied Soul is invested with the three qualities of Goodness, and Ignorance. But though thus invested, the Soul is not identical with those qualities.

sn: तस्माच्चतुष्टयं वेद्यमेतैर्हेतुभिरावृतम्। यथासंज्ञो ह्ययं सम्यगन्तकाले न मुह्यति॥
en: Hence these four topics, which are covered by these four considerations, should be understood. One who understands all this is never stupefied when he tries to form conclusions.

sn: श्रियं दिव्यामभिप्रेप्सुर्वम॑वान् मनसा शुचिः। शारीरैर्नियमैरुग्रैश्चरेन्निष्कल्मषं तपः॥
en: He who wishes to secure high prosperity should become pure in mind, and practising austere practices regarding the body and the senses, should devote himself to yoga without seeking for fruits.

sn: त्रैलोक्यं तपसा व्याप्तमन्तर्भूतेन भास्वता। सूर्यश्च चन्द्रमाश्चैव भासतस्तपसा दिवि॥
en: The universe is permeated by yoga power secretly passing through every part of it and lighting it up brightly. The sun and the moon shine in the sky of the heart on account of yoga power.

sn: प्रकाशस्तपसो ज्ञानं लोके संशब्दितं तपः। रजस्तमोघ्नं यत् कर्म तपसस्तत् स्वलक्षणम्॥
en: The result of yoga is Knowledge. Yoga is spoken of highly in the world. Whatever acts destroy Darkness and Ignorance form yoga of the in respect of its real character.

sn: ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते। वाङ्मनोनियमः सम्यमानसं तप उच्यते॥
en: Brahmacharya and abstention from injury form yoga of the body; while restraining of mind and words form yoga of the mind.

sn: विधिज्ञेभ्यो द्विजातिभ्यो ग्राह्यमन्नं विशिष्यते। आहारनियमेनास्य पाप्मा शाम्यति राजसः॥
en: The food which is acquired by begging from twice-born persons conversant with the ritual is distinguished from all other food. By taking that food abstemiously, one's sins begotten of Darkness are dissipated.

sn: वैमनस्यं च विषये यान्त्यस्य करणानि च। तस्मात् तन्मात्रमादद्याद् यावदत्र प्रयोजनम्॥
en: Living upon such food a Yogin finds his senses gradually withdrawn from their objects. Hence, he should take only that quality of food which is barely necessary for the support of his body.

sn: अन्तकाले बलोत्कर्षाच्छनैः कुर्यादनातुरः। एवं युक्तेन मनसा ज्ञानं यदुपपद्यते॥
en: Knowledge which one acquires gradually by mind devoted to yoga should be made one's own on the verge of death by a forcible stretch of power.

sn: रजोवर्धोऽप्ययं देही देहवाञ्छब्दवच्चरेत्। कार्यैरव्याहतमतिर्वैराग्यात् प्रकृतौ स्थितः॥
en: The embodied Soul, when divested of Darkness, assumes a subtile form with all the senses of perception and moves about in space. When his mind becomes untouched by acts, he, on account of such renunciation, becomes merged in Prakriti.

sn: आ देहादप्रमादाच्च देहान्ताद् विप्रमुच्यते। हेतुयुक्तः सदा सर्गो भूतानां प्रलयस्तथा॥
en: After the destruction of this gross body, one who through absence of carelessness escapes from all the three bodies, succeeds in attaining to Liberation. The birth and death of creatures is always brought about by by Avidya (Ignorance.)

sn: परप्रत्ययसर्गे तु नियति नुवर्तते। भावान्तप्रभवप्रज्ञा आसते ये विपर्ययम्॥
en: When knowledge of Brahman originates, the person on longer feels the pinch of necessity. Those, however, who believe what is the reverse of truth whose understandings are always busy with the birth and death of all existent things.

sn: धृत्या देहान् धारयन्तो बुद्धिसंक्षिप्तचेतसः। स्थानेभ्यो ध्वंसमानाश्च सूक्ष्मत्वात् तदुपासते॥
en: Keeping their bodies by the help of patience, withdrawing their hearts by the help of their understanding, and withdrawing are men themselves from the world of senses, some Yogins worship the senses for their subtility.

sn: यथागमं च गत्वा वै बुद्ध्या तत्रैव बुद्ध्यते। देहान्तं कश्चिदन्वास्ते भावितात्मा निराश्रयम्॥
en: Some of them, with mind purified by yoga, proceeding according to the scriptures and reaching the highest, succeed in knowing it by help of the understanding and live in that which is the highest and which without resting on any other thing rests on itself.

sn: युक्तं धारणया सम्यक् सतः केचिदुपासते। अभ्यस्यन्ति परं देवं विद्युत्संशब्दिताक्षरम्॥
en: Some adore Brahma in images. Some adore Him as devoid of qualities. Divinity which has been described to be like a flash of lightning and which is again indestructible.

sn: अन्तकाले [पासन्ते तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषाः। सर्व एते महात्मानो गच्छन्ति परमां गतिम्॥
en: Others who have consumed their sins by penances, attain to Brahman in the end. All these great persons attain to the highest end.

sn: सूक्ष्मं विशेषणं तेषामवेक्षेच्छास्त्रचक्षुषा। देहान्तं परमं विद्याद् विमुक्तमपरिग्रहम्। अन्तरिक्षादन्यतरं धारणासक्तमानसम्॥
en: With the eye of scriptures one should mark the subtile attributes of these several forms, as distinguished by attributes, of Brahma that are adored by men. The Yogin who has gone above the necessity, as the Supreme Divinity, or as that which is Unmanifest.

sn: मर्त्यलोकान् विमुच्यन्ते विद्यासंसक्तचेतसः। ब्रह्मभूता विरजसस्ततो यान्ति परां गतिम्॥
en: They whose hearts are given to the acquisition of knowledge succeed first in disassociating themselves for the world of mortals. Afterwards, by renouncing attachments they partake of the nature of Brahma and at last attain to the highest end.

sn: एवमेकायनं धर्ममाहुर्वेदविदो जनाः। यथाज्ञानमुपासन्तः सर्वे यान्ति परां गतिम्॥
en: Thus persons conversant with the Vedas have described the religion that brings on the attaininent of Brahma. They who follow that religion according to the extent of their respective knowledge all succeed in acquiring the highest end.

sn: कपायवर्जितं ज्ञानं येषामुत्पद्यते चलम् यान्ति तेऽपि पराँल्लोकान् विमुच्यन्ते यथाबलम्॥
en: Those persons who can acquire a knowledge which is incapable of being shaken and which makes its possessors shorn of all sorts of attachments acquire different high regions after death and become emancipate according to the extent of their knowledge.

sn: भगवन्तमजं दिव्यं विष्णुमव्यक्तसंज्ञितम्। भावेन यान्ति शुद्धा ये ज्ञानतृप्ता निराशिषः॥
en: Those pure-hearted persons who have acquired contentment from knowledge, and who have contentment from knowledge, and who have renounced all desires and attachments, gradually approach in respect of their nature nearer Brahma which is unmanifest by nature, which is divine, and without birth and death.

sn: ज्ञात्वाऽऽत्मस्थं हरि चैव न निवर्तन्ति तेऽव्ययाः। प्राप्य तत् परमं स्थानं मोदन्तेऽक्षरमव्ययम्॥
en: Realising that Brahma lives in their souls, they become themselves immutable and have never to come back to the Earth). Acquiring that supreme, indestructible and eternal state they live in happiness.

sn: एतावदेतद् विज्ञानमेतदस्ति च नास्ति च। तृष्णाबद्धं जगत् सर्वं चक्रवत् परिवर्तते।॥
en: The knowledge of this world is this: (Persons who have overcome ignorance think that) it does not exist. The whole universe, feltered by desire, is revolving like a wheel.

sn: बिसतन्तुर्यथैवायमन्तःस्थः सर्वतो बिसे। तृष्णातन्तुरनाद्यन्तस्तथा देहगतः सदा॥
en: As the fibres of a lotus-stalk overspread themselves into every part of the stalk, likewise the fibres of desire, which are without beginning or end, spread themselves over every part of the body.

sn: सूच्या सूत्रं यथा वस्त्रे संसारयति वायकः। तद्वत् संसारसूत्रं हि तृष्णासूच्या निबद्ध्यते॥
en: As a weaver drives his threads into a cloth by means of his shuttle, similarly the threads that constitute the fabric of the universe are woven by the shuttle of Desire.

sn: विकारं प्रकृतिं चैव पुरुषं च सनातनम्। यो यथावद् विजानाति स वितृष्णो विमुच्यते॥
en: He who understands the changes of Nature, Nature herself, and Purusha, becomes freed from Desire and acquires Liberation.

sn: प्रकाशं भगवानेतदृषिर्नारायणोऽमृतम्। भूतानामनुकम्पार्थं जगाद जगतो गतिः॥
en: The divine Rishi Narayana, that refuge of the universe, for the sake of mercy towards all creatures, distinctly laid down these means for the acquisition of immortality.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच केन वृत्तेन वृत्तज्ञ जनको मिथिलाधिपः। जगाम मोक्षं मोक्षज्ञो भोगानुत्सृज्य मानुषान्॥
en: By acting how, O you who are conversant with all courses of conduct, did Janaka the king of Mithila, versed in the religion of Liberation, succeed in acquiring Liberation, after casting off all worldly enjoyments?

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। येन वृत्तेन धर्मज्ञः स जगाम महत्सुखम्॥
en: “Regarding it is cited the following old narrative of the particular conduct by which that king, a master of all courses of conduct, succeeded in acquiring the highest happiness.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: जनको जनदेवस्तु मिथिलायां जनाधिपः। और्ध्वदेहिकधर्माणामासीद् युक्तो विचिन्तने॥
en: There was a king in Mithila of the name of Janadeva of Janaka's race. He was ever engaged in thinking of the courses of conduct that might lead to the attainment of Brahma.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: तस्य स्म शतमाचार्या वसन्ति सततं गृहे। दर्शयन्तः पृथग्धर्मान् नानाश्रमनिवासिनः॥
en: One hundred preceptors always used to live in his palace, describing to him the various courses of duty followed by people who had adopted the various modes of life.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: स तेषां प्रेत्यभावे च प्रेत्यजातौ विनिश्चये। आगमस्थः स भूयिष्ठमात्मतत्त्वे न तुष्यति॥
en: Well read in the Vedas, he was not very well satisfied with the speculations of his instructors on the nature of the Soul, and in their teachings of his extinction upon the dissolution of the body or of re-birth after death.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: तत्र पञ्चशिखो नाम कापिलेयो महामुनिः। परिधावन महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम मिथिलामथ॥
en: Once upon a time a great ascetic named Panchashikha the son of Kapila, having roamed over the whole world, arrived at Mithila.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: सर्वसंन्यासधर्माणां तत्त्वज्ञानविनिश्चये। सुपर्यवसितार्थश्च निर्द्वन्द्वो नष्टसंशयः॥
en: Having made conclusions about the diverse duties connected with renunciation, he was above all pairs of opposites, and had no doubts.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: ऋषीणामाहुरेकं तं यं कामानावृतं नृषु। शाश्वतं सुखमत्यन्तमन्विच्छन्तं सुदुर्लभम्॥
en: He was considered as the foremost of Rishis. Living wherever he pleased, he wished to place before the reach of all men eternal happiness that is so difficult of attainment.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: यमाहुः कपिलं सांख्याः परमर्षि प्रजापतिम्। स मन्ये तेन रूपेण विस्मापयति हि स्वयम्॥
en: It appeared that he roamed, amazing the world, having put on the form of none else then that great Rishi, that lord of creatures, whom the followers of the Sankhya doctrine knew by the name of Kapila.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: आसुरेः प्रथमं शिष्यं यमाहुश्चिरजीविनम्। पञ्चस्रोतसि यः सत्रमास्ते वर्षसहस्रिकम्॥
en: He was the greatest of all the disciples of Asuri and was called the undying. He had performed a mental Sacrifice lasting for a thousand years.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: तं समासीनमागम्य कापिलं मण्डलं महत्। पञ्चस्रोतसि निष्णातः पञ्चरात्रि विशारदः॥ पञ्चज्ञः पञ्चकृत्पञ्चगुणः पञ्चशिखः स्मृतः। पुरुषावस्थमव्यक्तं परमार्थं न्यवेदयत्॥
en: He was firm in mind, and had performed all the rites and sacrifices that are enjoyed in the scriptures and that lead to the attainment of Brahma. He knew full well the five sacs that cover the Soul. He was devoted to the five acts regarding the adoration of Brahma, and had the five qualities. Know by the name of Panchashikha, he had approached one day a large assembly of Rishis following the Sankhya doctrines and enquired of them about the highest object of human acquisition, namely, the Unmanifest or that upon which the five sacs rest.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: इष्टसत्रेण संसिद्धो भूयश्च तपसाऽऽसुरिः। क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्व्यक्तिं बुबुधे देवदर्शनः॥
en: For acquiring a knowledge of the Soul, Asuri had enquired of his preceptor. On account of the latter's instructions and of his own penances, Asuri understood the distinction between the body and the Soul and had gained celestial vision.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: यत् तदेकाक्षरं ब्रह्म नानारूपं प्रदृश्यते। आसुरिर्मण्डले तस्मिन् प्रतिपेदे तदव्ययम्॥
en: In that assembly of ascetics, Asuri described the Immutable, One, and Indestructible Brahma which is seen in various forms.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: तस्य पञ्चशिखः शिष्यो मानुष्या पयसा भृतः। ब्राह्मणी कपिला नाम काचिदासीत् कुटुम्बिनी॥
en: Panchashikha became a disciple of Asuri. He lived on human milk. There was a certain Brahman lady named Kapila. She was Asuri's wife.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: तस्याः पुत्रत्वमागम्य स्त्रियाः स पिबति स्तनौ। ततः स कापिलेयत्वं लेभे बुद्धिं च नैष्ठिकीम्॥
en: Panchashikha was accepted by her as a son and he used to suck her breasts. For this, he came to be known as the son of Kapila and his understanding became fixed on Brahma.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: एतन्मे भगवानाह कापिलेयस्य सम्भवम्। तस्य तत् कापिलेयत्वं सर्ववित्त्वमनुत्तमम्॥
en: The divine Rishi said to me, all this, regarding the circumstances of his birth and those about his becoming the son of Kapila. The latter also told me about the omniscience of Panchashikha.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: सामान्यं जनकं ज्ञात्वा धर्मज्ञो ज्ञानमुत्तमम्। उपेत्य शतमाचार्यान् मोहयामास हेतुभिः॥
en: Knowing fully all the forms of duty, Panchashikha, after having himself gained high knowledge, (came to Janaka) and knowing that that king had equal reverence for all his preceptors, began to startle those hundred preceptors (by a very sensible exposition of his doctrine).

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: जनकस्त्वभिसंरक्तः कापिलेयानुदर्शनात्। उत्सृज्य शतमाचार्यान् पृष्ठतोऽनुजगाम तम्॥
en: Marking the genius of the son of Kapila, Janaka became exceedingly attacked to him, and abandoning his hundred preceptors, began to follow him.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: तस्मै परमकल्याय प्रणताय च धर्मतः। अब्रवीत् परमं मोक्षं यत् तत् सांख्येऽभिधीयते॥
en: Then Kapila's son began to discourse to Janaka, who had according to the ordinance bent his head to him and who was fully competent to understand the sage's instructions, upon that great religion of Liberation which is explained in Sankhya treatises.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: जातिनिर्वेदमुक्त्वा स कर्मनिर्वेदमब्रवीत्। कर्मनिर्वेदमुक्त्वा च सर्वनिर्वेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Describing first of all the miseries of birth, he spoke next of the miseries of (religious) acts. Having finished that topic he explained the miseries of all states of existence ending even with that in the high region of the Creator.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: यदर्थं धर्मसंसर्गः कर्मणां च फलोदयः। तमनाश्वासिकं मोहं विनाशि चलमध्रुवम्॥
en: He also described that Delusion which beget the practice of religion, and acts, and their fruits, and which is highly untrustworthy, destructible, unsteady, and uncertain.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: दृश्यमाने विनाशे च प्रत्यक्षे लोकसाक्षिके। आगमात् परमस्तीति ब्रुवन्नपि पराजितः॥
en: Sceptics say that when death is seen directly by all, they who hold, on account of their faith in the scriptures, that something distinct from the body, called the Soul, exists, are necessarily defeated in argument.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: अनात्मा ह्यात्मनो मृत्युः क्लेशो मृत्युर्जरामयः। आत्मानं मन्यते मोहात् तदसम्यक् परं मतम्॥
en: They also hold that one's Soul, and that sorrow, decrepitude, and disease indicate (partial) death of the Soul. He who holds owing to error, that the Soul is distinct from the body and exists after the loss of body, entertains an unreasonable opinion.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: अथ चेदेवमप्यस्ति यल्लोके नोपपद्यते। अजरोऽयममृत्युश्च राजासौ मन्यते यथा।॥
en: If that is considered as existent which does not really exist in the world, then it may be mentioned that the king, being known so, is really never subject to decrepitude or death. But is he, therefore, to be really believed to be beyond decrepitude and death?

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: अस्ति नास्तीति चाप्येतत् तस्मिन्नसति लक्षणे। किमधिष्ठाय तद् ब्रूयाल्लोकयात्राविनिश्चयम्॥
en: When the question arises whether an object exists or not, and when that whose existence in asserted presents all the signs of non-existence, what is that upon which ordinary people depend in settling the affairs of life?

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: प्रत्यक्षं ह्येतयोर्मूलं कृतान्तैतिह्ययोरपि। प्रत्यक्षेणागमो भिन्नः कृतान्तो वा न किञ्चन॥
en: Direct evidence is the basis of both inference and the scriptures. The scriptures can be contradicted by direct evidence. As to inference its evidence is not much.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: यत्र यत्रानुमानेऽस्मिन् कृतं भावयतोऽपि च। नान्यो जीवः शरीरस्य नास्तिकानां मते स्थितः॥
en: Do not reason on inference only whatever may be the subject. There is nothing else called individual soul than this body.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: रेतो वटकणीकायां घृतपाकाधिवासनम्। जातिः स्मृतिरयस्कान्तः सूर्यकान्तोऽम्बुभक्षणम्॥
en: The capacity to produce leaves, flowers, fruits, roots and bark lies in a banian seed. The grass and water that is taken by a cow produce milk and butter, substances differing in nature from that of the causes. Various substances when allowed to decompose in water for sometime produce spirituous liquors whose nature is quite different from that of those substances producing them. Likewise, from the vital seed in produced the body and its attributes with the understanding, consciousness, wood, and other qualities. Two pieces of wood, rubbed together, beget fire. Coming in contact with the rays of the Sun, the stone called Suryakanta begets fire. Any solid metal, heated in fire, dries up water when coming in contact with it. Likewise, the material body produces the mind and its attributes of perception, memory, imagination, etc. As the loadstone moves iron, likewise the . senses are controlled by the mind.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: प्रेतीभूतेऽत्ययश्चैव देवताधुपयाचनम्। मृते कर्मनिवृत्तिश्च प्रमाणमिति निश्चयः॥
en: Thus do the sceptics reason, who are, however, mistaken. The disappearance (of animation) upon the body becoming lifeless means death. The supplication of the gods by the very men who deny the separate existence of the Soul is another good argument (for the proposition that the Soul is separate from the body). Another argument against the sceptic is that his proposition argues a destruction of acts.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: नन्वेते हेतवः सन्ति ये केचिन्मूर्तिसंस्थिताः। अमूर्तस्य हि मूर्तेन सामान्यं नोपपद्यते॥
en: These that have been mentioned and have material forms, cannot possible be the causes (of the immaterial Soul and its immaterial accompaniments). The identity of immaterial things with objects that are material cannot be comprehended.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: अविद्या कर्म तृष्णा च केचिदाहुः पुनर्भवे। कारणं लोभमोहौ तु दोषाणां तु निषेवणम्॥
en: Some hold that there is re-birth which is caused by Ignorance, the desire for acts, cupidity, carelessness, and bent towards other vices.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: अविद्यां क्षेत्रमाहुर्हि कर्म बीजं तथा कृतम्। तृष्णा संजननं स्नेह एष तेषां पुनर्भवः॥
en: They say that Ignorance is the soil. Acts form the seed that is placed in that soil. Desire is the water that causes that seed to grow. In this manner they explained re-birth.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: तस्मिन् गूढे च दग्धे च भिन्ने मरणधर्मिणि। अन्योऽस्माज्जायते देहस्तमाहुः सत्त्वसंक्षयम्॥
en: They hold that ignorance being ingrained in an imperceptible way, one mortal body being destroyed, another originates at once from it; and that when it is consumed by the help of knowledge, the destruction of existence itself follows, or the person attains to what is called annihilation.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: यदा स्वरूपतश्चान्यो जातितः शुभतोऽर्थतः। कथमस्मिन् स इत्येवं सर्वं वा स्यादसंहितम्॥
en: This opinion also is mistaken, It may be asked that when the being that is thus re-bom is a different one in its nature, birth, and objects of virtue and vice, why should it then be considered to be identical with the being that was? Indeed, the only inference that can be made is that the entire chain of existences of a particular being is not really one of connected links.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: एवं सति च का प्रीतिर्दानविद्यातपोबलैः। यदस्याचरितं कर्म सर्वमन्यत् प्रपद्यते॥
en: Then, again, if the being that is the outcome of a re-birth be really different from what it was in a pristine existence, it may be asked what satisfaction is to a person from the exercise of the spirit of charity, or from the acquisition of knowledge or of ascetic power, since the acts perforined by one are to bear fruits upon another person in another state of existence.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: अपि ायमिहैवान्यैः प्राक्कृतैर्दुःखितो भवेत्। सुखितो दुःखितो वापि दृश्यादृश्यविनिर्णयः॥
en: Another refutation of the doctrine would be that one in this life may rendered miserable by the acts of another in a pristine life, or having become miserable may again become happy. By witnessing however, what actually takes place in the world, a proper conclusion may be drawn regarding the unseen.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: तथा हि मुसलैर्हन्युः शरीरं तत् पुनर्भवेत्। पृथग्ज्ञानं यदन्यच्च येनैतन्त्रोपपद्यते॥
en: The separate Consciousness that is the outcome of re-birth is different from the Consciousness that had preceded it in a pristine existence. The way, however, in which the appearance of that separate Consciousness is explained by that theory is not at all consistent or reasonable. The Consciousness was the very opposite of eternal, being only transitory, extending as it did till dissolution of the body. That which had an end cannot be considered as the cause for the production of a second Consciousness appearing after the end. If again, the very very loss of of the previous Consciousness be considered as the cause of the production of the second Consciousness, then when the death of a human body is caused by a heavy bludgeon, a second body would originate from the body that is thus deprived of animation.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: ऋतुसंवत्सरौ तिष्यः शीतोष्णेऽथ प्रियाप्रिये। यथातीतानि पश्यन्ति तादृशः सत्त्वसंक्षयः॥
en: Again, their doctrine of annihilation is subject to the objection that extinction will become a revolving phenomenon like that of the seasons, or the year, or the Yuga, or heat, or cold, or agreeable or disagreeable objects.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: जरयाभिपरीतस्य मृत्युना च विनाशिना। दुर्बलं दुर्बलं पूर्व गृहस्येव विनश्यति॥
en: If for avoiding these objections, the followers of this doctrine hold the existence of a Soul that is permanent and with which cach new Consciousness is attached, they again subject themselves to the new objection that that permanent substance, by being overcome with decrepitude, and with death that causes destruction, may in time be itself weakened and destroyed. If the supports of a palace are weakened by time, the mansion itself is sure to fall down in the end.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: इन्द्रियाणि मनो वायुः शोणितं मांसमस्थि च। आनुपूर्व्या विनश्यन्ति स्वं धातुमुपयान्ति च॥
en: The senses, the mind, wind, blood, flesh, bones, one after another, meet with destruction and enter each into its own productive causes.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: लोकयात्राविघातश्च दानधर्मफलागमे। तदर्थं वेदशब्दाश्च व्यवहाराश्च लौकिकाः॥
en: If again the existence of an eternal Soul is held which is immutable, which is the refuge of the understanding, consciousness, and other similar attributes, and which is dissociated from all these, such an assertion is subject to a serious objection for then all that is usually done in the world would be meaningless, especially with reference to the attaininent of the fruits of charity and other religious acts. All the injunctions in the Shrutis regarding those acts, and all acts connected with the conduct of in the world, would be equally men meaningless, for the Soul being dissociated form, the understanding and the mind, there is no one to enjoy the fruits of good acts and Vedic rites.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: इति सम्यङ्मनस्यते बहवः सन्ति हेतवः। एतदस्तीदमस्तीति न किञ्चित्प्रतिदृश्यते॥
en: Thus various sorts of speculations arise in the mind. Nothing can settle whether this opinion is right or that is right.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: तेषां विमृशतामेव तत् तत्समभिधावताम्। क्वचिन्निविशते बुद्धिस्तत्र जीर्यति वृक्षवत्॥
en: Reflecting on these opinions, particular persons follow particular lines of speculation. The understanding of these, directed to particular theories become immersed and are at last entirely lost in them.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: एवमथैरनथैश्च दुःखिताः सर्वजन्तवः। आगमैरपकृष्यन्ते हस्तिपैर्हस्तिनो यथा॥
en: Thus all men are made miserable by pursuits good or bad. Bringing them back to the right path, the Vedas alone, guide them along it, like grooms conducting their elephants.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: अर्थांस्तथात्यन्तसुखावहांश्च लिप्सन्त एते बहवो विशुष्काः। महत्तरं दुःखमनुप्रपन्ना हित्वाऽऽमिषं मृत्युवशं प्रयान्ति॥
en: Many men, with weakened minds, seek objects of great happiness. These, however, have soon to meet with a larger quantity of SOITow, and then, alienated by force from their coveted mcat, they subject themselves to the sway of death.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: विनाशिनो ह्यध्रुवजीवितस्य किं बन्धभिभिन्नपरिग्रहैश्चा विहाय यो गच्छति सर्वमेव क्षणेन गत्वा न निवर्तते च॥
en: What has one, who is subject to destruction and whose life is fickle, to do with kinsmen and friends and wives and other like possessions? He who meets death after having relinquished all these, passes easily out of the world and has never to return.

description: The acquirement of Liberation by Janaka
sn: भूव्योमतोयानलवायवोऽपि सदा शरीरं प्रतिपालयन्ति। इतीदमालक्ष्य रतिः कुतो भवेद् विनाशिनोऽप्यस्य न शर्म विद्यते॥ इदमनुपधिवाक्यमच्छल परमनिरामयमात्मसाक्षिकम्। नरपतिरभिवीक्ष्य विस्मित: पुनरनुयोक्तुमिदं प्रचक्रमे॥
en: Earth, ether, water, heat, and wind, always keep up and nourish the body. Thinking of this, how can one feet any attachment for his body? Indeed, the body, which is subject to destruction, has no happiness in it.-Having heard these words Panchashikha that were shorn of deception, and delusion highly salutary, and treating of the Soul, king Janaka became filled with wonder, and prepared himself to address the Rishi once more.'

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: भीष्म उवाच जनको जनदेवस्तु ज्ञापितः परमर्षिणा। पुनरेवानुपप्रच्छ साम्पराये भवाभुवौ॥
en: Bhishma said "Thus instructed by the great Rishi Panchashikha, Janadeva of the family of Janaka, once more asked him about the subject of existence or non-existence after death.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: जनक उवाच भगवन् यदि न प्रेत्य संज्ञा भवति कस्यचित्। एवं सति किमज्ञानं ज्ञानं वा किं करिष्यति॥
en: O illustrious one, if no person, retains any knowledge after departing from this state of existence, if, indeed, this is true, what then is the difference between Ignorance and Knowledge? What do we gain then by knowledge and what do we lose by ignorance?

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: सर्वमुच्छेदनिष्ठं स्यात् पश्य चैतद् द्विजोत्तम! अप्रमत्तः प्रमत्तो वा किं विशेषं करिष्यति॥
en: See, O foremost of the twice-born, that if liberation be such, then all religious acts and vows terminate only in annihilation? Of what use would then the distinction be between heedfulness and heedlessness.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: असंसर्गो हि भूतेषु संसर्गो वा विनाशिषु। कस्मै क्रियेत कल्प्येत निश्चयः कोऽत्र तत्त्वतः॥
en: If Liberation means dissociation from all objects of pleasure or an association with objects that are not lasting, why should then men cherish a desire for action or having set themselves to action, continue to find out the necessary means for the accomplishment of desired ends? What then is the truth.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: भीष्म उवाच तमसा हि प्रतिच्छन्नं विभ्रान्तमिव चातुरम्। पुनः प्रशमयन् वाक्यैः कविः पञ्चशिखोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhishma said Seeing the king enveloped in thick darkness, stupefied by error, and become helpless, the learned Panchashikha put his mind at rest by once more addressing him thus.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: उच्छेदनिष्ठा नेहास्ति भावनिष्ठा न विद्यते। अयं ह्यपि समाहारः शरीरेन्द्रियचेतसाम्। वर्तते पृथगन्योन्यमप्यपाश्रित्य कर्मसु॥
en: In Liberation the consummation is not Extinction. Nur is that consummation any kind of Existence. What we see is a union of body senses, and mind. Existing independently as also depending on one another, these go on acting.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: धातवः पञ्च भूतेषु खं वायुर्योतिषो धरा। ते स्वभावेन तिष्ठन्ति वियुज्यन्ते स्वभावतः॥
en: The ingredients that form the body are water, ether, wind, heat, and earth. These exisi together according to their own nature. They become separated again according to their own nature.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: आकाशोवायुरूष्मा च स्नेहो यश्चापि पार्थिवः! एष पञ्चसमाहारः शरीरमपि नैकवाटा
en: Ether, wind, heat, water and earth,-these five objects in a state of union form the body. The body is not one element.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: ज्ञानमूष्मा च वायुश्च त्रिविधः कार्यसंग्रह। इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियाथाश्च स्वभावश्चेतना मनः। प्राणापानौ विकारश्च धातवश्चात्र नि:सृताः॥
en: Intelligence, stomachic heat, and the vital airs, called Prana, etc., that are all wind, three are the organs of action. The senses, the objects of the senses, the power by which they become capable of being perceived the faculties by which they succeed in perceiving them, the mind, the vital airs called Prana. Apana and the rest, and the various juices and humours that are the results of the digestive organs, flow from the three organs already named.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: श्रवणं स्पर्शनं जिह्वा दृष्टि सा तथैव च। इन्द्रियाणीति पञ्चैते चित्तपूर्वं गता गुणाः॥
en: Hearing, touch, taste, vision, and scent,-these are the five senses. They have derived their attributes from the mind which is their cause.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: तत्र विज्ञानसंयुक्ता त्रिविधा चेतना ध्रुवा। सुखदुःखेति यामाहुरदुःखामसुखेति च॥
en: The mind, which is as an attribute of Chit, has three states, viz., pleasure, pain and absence of both pleasure and pain.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: शब्द: स्पर्श च रूपं च रसो गन्धश्च मूर्तयः। एते ह्यामरणात् पञ्च षड्गुणा ज्ञानसिद्धये॥
en: Sound, touch, form, taste, scent, and the objects to which they are attached these till the time of one's death are causes for the production of one's knowledge.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: तेषु कर्मविसर्गश्च सर्वतत्त्वार्थनिश्चयः। तमाहुः परमं शुक्र बुद्धिरित्यव्ययं महत्॥
en: Upon the senses depend all acts (leading to lucavon), as also renunciation (leading to the attainment of Brahma), and also the ! ascertainment of truth regarding all topics of enquiry. The learned say thai ascertainment of truth) is the highest end of existences, and is the root of Liberation and regarding Intelligence, they say that it leads to Liberation and Brahma.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: इमं गुणसमाहारमात्मभावेन पश्यतः। असम्यग्दर्शनैर्दुःखमनन्तं नोपशाम्यति॥
en: That person who considers this union of perishable attributes as the Soui, feeis, on account of such imperfect knowledge, unending misery

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: अनात्मेति च यद् दृष्टं तेनाह न ममेत्यपि। वर्तते किमधिष्ठानात् प्रसक्तादुःखपमृतिः॥
en: Those persons, who, however, regard alll worldly objects as not-Soui, and who on that account cease to have any affection or attachment for them, have never to suffer any misery, for sorrow, in their case, stands in need of some foundation upon which to depend.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: अत्र सम्यग्वधो नाम त्यागशास्त्रमनुत्तमम्। शृणु यत् तव मोक्षाय भाष्यमाणं भविष्यति॥
en: About it there is the unrivalled branch of knowledge which treats of Renunciation. It is called Samyagvadha. I shall describe it to you. Listen to it for the sake of your Liberation.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: त्याग एव हि सर्वेषां युक्तानामपि कर्मणाम्। नित्यं मिथ्याविनीतानां क्लेशो दुःखवहो मतः॥
en: Renunciation of acts is (laid down) for all persons who seek Liberation earnestly. They, however, who have not been instructed correctly have to bear a heavy load of sorrow,

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: द्रव्यत्यागे तु कर्माणि भोगत्यागे व्रतान्यपि। सुखत्यागे तपो योगं सर्वत्यागे समापना॥
en: Vedic sacrifices and other rites exist for renunciation of wealth and other earthly (objects. For renunciation of all enjoyments, exist yows and fasts of various sorts. For renunciation of pleasure and happiness exist penances and yoga. Renunciation everything, is the highest kind of renunciation,

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: तस्य मार्गोऽयमद्वैधः सर्वत्यागस्य दर्शितः विप्रहाणाय दुःखस्य दुर्गतिस्त्वन्यथा भवेत्॥
en: This that I shall presently describe to you is the one path pointed out by the learned for that renunciation of everything. They who follow that path succeed in driving off all sorrow. They, however, that deviate from it suffer distress and misery

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: पञ्चज्ञानेन्द्रियाण्युक्त्वा मनःषष्ठानि चेतसि। बलषष्ठानि वक्ष्यामि पञ्चकर्मेन्द्रियाणि तु!॥
en: First speaking of the five organs of knowledge having the mind for the sixth, und all of which live in the understanding, i stall describe the five organs of action having strength for their sixth.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: हस्तौ कर्मेन्द्रियं ज्ञेयमथ पादौ गतीन्द्रियम्। प्रजनानन्दयोः शेफो निसर्गे पायुरिन्द्रियम्।।२११
en: The two hands forms the two organs of action. The two legs are two organs for moving from one place to another. The sexual organ is for both pleasure and the continuation of in species. The lower channel, leading from the stomach downwards, is the organ for purging off of all used-up matter. aran a prafastarffuta usati fag: 1

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: एवमेकादशैतानि बुद्ध्याऽऽशु विसृजेन्मनः॥
en: The organ of speaking exists for the expression of sounds. These five organs of action belong to the mind. These are the eleven organs of knowledge and of action. One should speedily cast off the inind with the understanding.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: कर्णी शब्दश चित्तं च त्रयः श्रवणसंग्रहे। तथा स्पर्श तथा रूपे तथैव रसगन्धयोः॥
en: In the act of hearing, three causes must exist simultaneously, viz., the two ears, sound, and the mind. The same is the case with the perception of touch; the same with that of form; the same with that of taste and smell.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: एवं पञ्चत्रिका ह्येते गुणास्तदुपलब्धये। येनायं त्रिविधो भावः पर्यायात् समुपस्थितः॥
en: These fifteen attributes are necessary for the several kinds of perception. In consequence of them, every man becomes conscious of three separate things regarding those perceptions.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: सात्त्विको राजसश्चापि तामसश्चापि ते त्रयः। त्रिविधा वेदना येषु प्रसूताः सर्वसाधनाः॥
en: There are again three classes (of mental perception, viz., those that appertain to Goodness, those that belong of Darkness, and those that belong to Ignorance. With them are connected three kinds of consciousness, including all feelings and emotions.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: प्रहर्षः प्रीतिरानन्दः सुखं संशान्तचित्तता। अकुतश्चित् कुतश्चिद्वा चिन्तितः सात्त्विको गुणः॥
en: Pleasure, satisfaction, joy, happiness, and tranquillity, originating in the mind from any perceptible cause or in the absence of any apparent cause, appertain to the quality of Goodness.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: अतुष्टिः परितापश्च शोको लोभस्तथाक्षमा। लिङ्गानि रजसस्तानि दृश्यन्ते हेत्वहेतुतः॥
en: Discontent, regret, grief, cupidity, and vindictiveness, having no cause or occasioned by any perceptible cause, are the marks of the quality of Darkness.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: अविवेकस्तथा मोहः प्रमोदः स्वप्नतन्द्रिता। कथंचिदपि वर्तन्ते विविधास्तामसा गुणाः॥
en: Wrong judgement, stupefaction, carelessness, dreams, and sleepiness, however, caused, appertain to the quality of Ignorance.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: अत्र यत् प्रीतिसंयुक्तं काये मनसि वा भवेत्। वर्तते सात्त्विको भाव इत्यपेक्षेत तत् तथा॥
en: Whatever state of consciousness exists, regarding either the body or the mind, united with joy or satisfaction, should be considered as due to the quality of Goodness.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: यत् त्वसंतोषसंयुक्तमप्रीतिकरमात्मनः। प्रवृत्तं रज इत्येवं ततस्तदपि चिन्तयेत्॥
en: Whatever state of consciousness exists united with any feeling of discontent or depression should be considered as the outcome of the quality of Darkness.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: अथ यन्मोहसंयुक्तं काये मनसि वा भवेत्। अप्रत_मविज्ञेयं तमस्तदुपधारयेत्॥
en: Whatever state, of the body or the body or the mind, exists with error or carelessness, is the outcome of Ignorance which is incomprehensible and inexplicable.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: श्रोतं व्योमाश्रितं भूतं शब्दः श्रोतं समाश्रितः। नोभयं शब्दविज्ञाने विानस्येतरस्य वा॥
en: The organ of hearing rests on either; it is either itself (under limitations); Sound has that organ for its refuge. In perceiving sound, one may not immediately acquire a knowledge of the organ of hearing and of ether. But when sound is perceived, the organ of hearing and ether do not long remain unknown.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: एवं त्वक्चक्षुषी जिह्वा नासिका चेति पञ्चमी। स्पर्श रूपे रसे गन्धे तानि चेतो मनश्च तत्॥
en: The same is the case with the skin, the eyes, the tongue, and the nose forming the fifth. They exist in touch, form, taste, and smell. They form the faculty of perception and they are the mind.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: स्वकर्मयुगपद्भावो दशस्वेतेषु तिष्ठति। चित्तमेकादशं विद्धि बुद्धिादशमी भवेत्॥
en: Each doing its own particular function, all the five organs of action and the five others of knowledge exist simultaneously, and upon the union of the ten dwells the mind as the eleventh and upon the mind the understanding as the twelfth.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: तेषामयुगपद्भाव उच्छेदो नास्ति तामसे। आस्थितो युगपद्भावो व्यवहारः स लौकिकः॥
en: It is be said that these twelve do not exist simultaneously, then the consequence would be that there would be death in dreamless sleep. But as there is no death in dreamless sleep, it must be admitted that these twelve exist simultaneously as regards themselves but of past separately from the Soul. The co-existence of those twelve with the Soul that is ordinarily spoken is only a common form of speech with the vulgar for ordinary purposes of the world.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: इन्द्रियाण्यपि सूक्ष्माणि दृष्ट्वा पूर्वश्रुतागमात्। चिन्तयन्नानुपर्येति निभिरेवान्वितो गुणैः॥
en: The dreamer, on account of the appearance sensual impressions, becomes conscious of his senses in their subtile forms, and endued as he already is with the three qualities, he considers his senses as existing with their respective objects and, therefore, acts and moves about with an imaginary body after the manner of his own self while awake.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: यत् तमोपहतं चित्तमाशु संहारमध्रुवम्। करोत्युपरमं काये तदाहुस्तामसं बुधाः॥
en: That dissociation of the Soul from the understanding and the mind with the senses, which speedily disappears, which has no stability, and which the mind causes to arise only when influenced by Ignorance is happiness that partakes as the learned say, of the nature of Ignorance and is experienced in this gross body only.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: यद् यदागमसंयुक्तं न कृच्छ्रमनुपश्यति। अथ तत्राप्युपादत्ते तमोऽव्यक्तमिवानृतम्॥
en: Over the felicity of Liberation also, the felicity, viz., which is created by the inspired teaching of Vedas and in which no one sees the slightest mark of sorrow,-the same indescribable and truth-concealing darkness seems to spread itself.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: एवमेष प्रसंख्यातः स्वकर्मप्रत्ययो गुणः। कथञ्चिद् वर्तते सम्यक् केषांचिद् वा निवर्तते।॥
en: Like to what occurs in dreamless sleep, in liberation also, subjective and objective existences, which have their origin in one's : acts, are all discarded.
