In some, that are possessd by Ignorance, these exits, firmly grafted with them. They never approach others who have transcended Avidya and have acquired knowledge.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: एतदाहुः समाहारं क्षेत्रमध्यात्मचिन्तकाः। स्थितो मनसि यो भावः स वै क्षेत्रज्ञ उच्यते॥
en: Those who know thoroughly well the character of Soul and non-Soul, say that this sum total of the senses, etc.,) is body. That existent thing which rests, upon the mind is called Soul.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: एवं सति क उच्छेदः शाश्वतो वा कथं भवेत्। स्वभावाद् वर्तमानेषु सर्वभूतेषु हेतुतः॥
en: When such is the case, and when all creatures, on account of the well-known cause, exist, due to a state of union between Soul and body, which of these two then is destructible and how can that which is said to be eternal, suffer destruction?

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: यथार्णवगता नद्यो व्यक्तीर्जहति नाम च। नदाश्च ता नियच्छन्ति तादृशः सत्त्वसंक्षयः॥
en: As small rivers falling into larger ones lose their forms and names, and the larger ones falling into the ocean lose their forms and names too, similarly called Liberation.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: एवं सति कुत: संज्ञा प्रेत्यभावे पुनर्भवेत्। प्रतिसम्मिश्रिते जीवेऽगृह्यमाणे च सर्वतः॥
en: Likewise, the individual Soul which is characterised by qualities, is received into the Universal Soul, and when all its attributes disappear, how can it be differently mentioned?

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: मात्मानमन्विच्छति चाप्रमत्तः। न लिप्यते कर्मफलैरनिष्टः पत्रं विसस्येव जलेन सिक्तम्॥
en: One who is conversant with that understanding which brings on Liberation and who carefully seeks to know the soul, is never sullied by the evil fruits of his acts water is never soaked by it.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: दृढ़र्हि पाशैर्बहुभिर्विमुक्तः प्रजानिमित्तैरपि दैवतैश्च। यदा ह्यसौ सुखदुःखे जहाति मुक्तस्तदग्यां गतिमेत्यलिङ्गः॥
en: When one becomes freed from the very many strong fetters, occasioned by affection for children and wives and love for sacrifices and other rites, when one renounces both joy and sorrow and transcends all attachments, one then attains to the highest end and entering into the Universal Soul becomes immersed in it.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: श्रुतिप्रमाणागममङ्गलैच शेते जरामृत्युभयादभीतः। क्षीणे च पुण्ये विगते च पापे ततो निमित्ते च फले विनष्टे। मास्थाय पश्यन्ति महत्यसक्ताः॥
en: When one has understood the injunction of the Shrutis that lead to correct conclusion (about Brahma) and has practised those auspicious virtues which the same and other Scriptures teach, one may lie down at ease, disregarding the fears of decrepitude and death. When both merits and demerits disappear, and the fruits, in the form of joy and sorrow, originating therefrom, and destroyed, men, unattached to everything, seek refuge at first with personal Brahma, and then behold impersonal Brahma in their understandings.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: स्तन्तुक्षय तिष्ठति पात्यमानः। तथा विमुक्तः प्रजहाति दुःखं विध्वंसते लोष्ट इवाद्रिमृच्छन्॥
en: In course of its downwards descent under the influence of ignorance individual soul lives (within its cell formed by acts) like a silkworm living within its cell made of threads woven by itself. Like the freed silk-worm again that quits its cell, individual soul also abandons its house forined by its acts. The final result, is that its sorrows are then dissipated like a clump of carth falling violently upon a rocky mass.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: यथा रुरुः शृङ्गमथो पुराणं हित्वा त्वचं वाप्युरगो यथा च। स्तथा विमुक्तो विजहाति दुःखम्॥
en: As the Ruru deer casting off its hold horns or the snake casting off slough passes on without arresting any notice, similarly a person who is unattached renounces all his sorrows.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: मुत्सृज्य पक्षी निपतत्यसक्तः। तथा ह्यसौ सुखदुःखे विहाय मुक्तः पराक्र्धा गतिमेत्यलिङ्गः॥
en: As a bird leaves a tree that is about to fall down upon a water and sits on a (new) resting place, similarly similarly the person freed from attachinents renounces both joy and sorrow and dissociated even from his subtile and subtler forms attains to that end which is full of the highest prosperty.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: भीष्म उवाच अपि च भवति मैथिलेन गीतं नगरमुपाहितमग्निनाभिवीक्ष्य। न खलु मम हि दह्यतेऽत्र किंचित् स्वयमिदमाह किल स्म भूमिपालः॥
en: Seeing his city burning in a fire, their own ancestor Janaka, the king of Mithila himself proclaimed-'In this fire nothing of mine is burning.'

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: इदममृतपदं निशम्य राजा स्वयमिह पञ्चशिखेन भाष्यमाणम्। निखिलमभिसमीक्ष्य निश्चितार्थः परमसुखी विजहार वीतशोकः॥
en: Having heard these words capable of giving imınortality and uttered by Panchashikha, and arriving at the truth after carefully reflecting upon everything that the latter had said King Janadeva cast off his sorrows and lived on in the enjoyment of great happiness.

description: The conversation between Panchashikha and king Janaka
sn: इमं हि यः पठति विमोक्षनिश्चयं महीपते सततमवेक्षते तथा। उपद्रवान् नानुभवत्यदुःखितः प्रमुच्यते कपिलमिवैत्य मैथिलः॥
en: He who reads this discourse, O king, that deals with emancipation and who always reflects upon it, is never pained by any misfortune, and freed from sorrow, attains to liberation like Janadeva the king of Mithila after his meeting with Panchashikha.' He who reads this discourse, O king, that deals with emancipation and who always reflects upon it, is never pained by any misfortune, and freed from sorrow, attains to liberation like Janadeva the king of Mithila after his meeting with Panchashikha.'

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं कुर्वन् सुखमाप्नोति किं कुर्वन् दुःखमाप्नुयात्। किं कुर्वनिर्भयो लोके सिद्धश्चरति भारत॥
en: By doing what does one gain happiness, and what is that by doing which one meets with misery? What also is that, O Bharata, by doing which one becomes freed from fear and sojourns here successfully,

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: भीष्म उवाच दममेव प्रशंसन्ति वृद्धाः श्रुतिसमाधयः। सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः॥
en: Bhishma said The ancients who had there minds, directed to the Shrutis, spoke highly of the duty of selfcontrol for all the castes in general, but for the Brahmanas in especial.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: नादान्तस्य क्रियासिद्धिर्यथावदुपपद्यते। क्रिया तपश्च सत्यं च दमे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: One who is not self-controlled never enjoys success in religious rites. Religious rites, penances, truth, all these depend upon selfcontrol.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: दमस्तेजो वर्धयति पवित्रं दम उच्यते। विपाप्मा निर्भयो दान्तः पुरुषो विन्दन्ते महत्॥
en: Self-control increases one's energy. Self-। control is said to be sacred. The man of selfcontrol becomes sinless and fearless and acquires great results.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: सुखं दान्तः प्रस्वपिति सुखं च प्रतिबुद्ध्यते। सुखं लोके विपर्येति मनश्चास्य प्रसीदति॥
en: One who is self-controlled sleeps happily and wakes happily. He lives happily in the world and his mind always remains cheerful

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: तेजो दमेन ध्रियते तन्न तीक्ष्णोऽधिगच्छति। अमित्रांश्च बहून् नित्यं पृथगात्मनि पश्यति॥
en: Every sort of excitement is quietly controlled by self-control. One who is not selfcontrolled fails in a similar endeavour. The self-controlled man sees his numberless focs (such as lust, desire, and anger, etc.') as if these dwell in a separate body.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: क्रव्याट्य इव भूतानमदान्तेभ्यः सदाभयम्। तेषां विप्रतिषेधार्थं राजा सृष्टः स्वयम्भुवा॥
en: Like tigers and other carnivorous animals, persons shorn of self-control always strike all creatures with fear. For controlling these men, the Self-create (Brahma) created kings.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: आश्रमेषु च सर्वेषु दम एव विशिष्यते। यच्च तेषु फलं धर्मे भूयो दान्ते तदुच्यते॥
en: In all the modes of life, the practice of selfcontrol is distinguished above all other virtues. The fruits of self-control are much greater than those obtainable in all the modes of life.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: तेषां लिङ्गानि वक्ष्यामि येषां समुदयो दमः। अकार्पण्यमसंरम्भः संतोष: श्रद्दधानता॥ अक्रोध आर्जवं नित्यं नातिवादोऽभिमानिता। गुरुपूजानसूया च दया भूतेष्वपैशुनम्॥ जनवादमृषावादस्तुतिनिन्दाविवर्जनम्। साधुकामश्च स्पृहयेन्नायति प्रत्ययेषु च॥
en: I shall now describe the characteristic marks of those persons who value self-control highly. They are nobility, calmness of nature, contentment, faith, forgiveness, invariable simplicity, the absence of talk-activeness, humility, reverence for elders, benevolence, mercy for all creatures, frankness, abstention from talk upon kings and men in authority, from all false and useless topics, and from applause and censure of others. The selfcontrolled man becomes desirous of liberation and, quietly bearing present joys and griefs, is never overjoyed or depressed by prospective (Ones.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: अवैरकृत् सूपचारः समो निन्दाप्रशंसयोः। सुवृत्तः शीलसम्पन्नः प्रसन्नात्मऽऽत्मवान् प्रभुः॥
en: Shom of vindictiveness and all sorts of guile, and unaffected by praise and censure, such a man is well-behaved, has good manners is pure of soul, had fortitude, and is a complete master of his passions.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: प्राप्य लोके च सत्कारं स्वर्ग वै प्रेत्य गच्छति। दुर्गमं सर्वभूतानां प्रापयन् मोदते सुखी॥
en: Gaining honours in this world, such a man in after life goes to heaven. Making all creatures gain what they cannot acquire without his help, such a man rejoices and becomes happy.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: सर्वभूतहिते युक्तो न स्म यो द्विषते जनम्। महाह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यः प्रज्ञातृप्तः प्रसीदति॥
en: Devoted to universal benevolence, such a man never feels animosity for any one. Tranquil like a calm ocean, wisdom feels his soul and he is ever cheerful.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: अभयं यस्य भूतेभ्यः सर्वेषामभयं यतः। नमस्यः सर्वभूतानां दान्तो भवति बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Endued with intelligence, and deserving of universal reverence, the self-controlled man never fears any creature and is feared by no creature in return.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: न हृष्यति महत्यर्थे व्यसने च न शोचति। स वै परिमितप्रज्ञः स दान्तो द्विज उच्यते॥
en: That man who never rejoices even at large accessions and never feels sorrow when overtaken by misfortune, is said to be endued with contented wisdom. Such a man is said to he self-controlled. Indeed, such a man is said to be a twice-born man.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: कर्मभिः श्रुतिसम्पन्नः सद्भिराचरितैः शुचिः। सदैव दमसंयुक्तस्तस्य भुङ्क्ते महाफलम्।।१७
en: Well-read in the scriptures and gifted with a pure soul, the man of self-controi, performing all those acts that are done by the good, enjoys their high fruits.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: अनसूया क्षमा शान्तिः संतोषः प्रियवादिता। सत्यं दानमनायासो नैष मार्गो दुरात्मनाम्॥
en: The wicked men, however, never follow the path of benevolence, forgiveness, tranquillity, contentment, sweetness of speech, trutli, liberality, and comfort.

description: The acquirement of happiness and misery
sn: कामक्रोधौ च लोभश्च परस्येाविकत्थना। कामक्रोधौ वशे कृत्वा ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः ॥ विक्रम्य घोरे तपसि ब्राह्मणः संशितव्रतः। कालाकाङ्क्षी चरेल्लोकान् निरपाय इवात्मवान्॥
en: They follow the path of lust, anger, cupidity, envy of others, and boastfulness. Overcoming lust and anger, practising the vow of Brahmacharya and becoming a complete master of his senses, the Brahman practising patiently the austerest penances, and observing the most rigid restraints, should live in this world, calmly waiting for his time like one seeming to have a body through fully knowing that he is not subject to destruction.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच द्विजातयो व्रतोपेता यदिदं भुञ्जते हविः। अन्नं ब्राह्मणकामाय कथमेतत् पितामह॥
en: Yudhisthira said The three twice-born classes, who perform sacrifices and other rites, some times eat the remnants, consisting of meat and wine, of sacrifices in honour of the gods, from motives of obtaining children and heaven. What, O grandfather, is the nature of this act?

sn: भीष्म उवाच अवेदोक्तव्रतोपेता भुञ्जाना: कार्यकारिणः। वेदोक्तेषु च भुञ्जाना व्रतलुब्धा युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said Those who eat forbidden food without performing the sacrifices and vows ordained in the Vedas are known as wilful men. Those, on the other hand, who eat such food in the observance of Vedic sacrifices and vows and actuated by the desire of fruits in the shape of heaven and children, ascend to heaven but drop down on the termination of their merits.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यदिदं तप इत्याहुरुपवासं पृथग्जनाः। एतत् तपो महाराज उताहो किं तपो भवेत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said Common people say that fasting is penance. Is fasting, however, really so, or is penance somethings different?

sn: भीष्म उवाच मासपक्षोपवासेन मन्यन्ते यत् तपो जनाः। आत्मतन्त्रोपघातस्तु न तपस्तत्सतां मतम्॥
en: Bhishma said People really consider fast, measured by months or fortnights or days, as penance. The good, however, hold that such is not penance. On the other hand, fast is an obstacle to the acquirement of the knowledge of the Soul.

sn: त्यागश्च संनतिश्चैव शिष्यते तप उत्तमम्। सदोपवासी च भवेद् ब्रह्मचारी सदा भवेत्॥
en: The renunciation of acts and humility form the highest penance. It is superior to all kinds of penance. He who performs such penance is considered as one who is always fasting and who is always leading a life of Brahmacharrya.

sn: मुनिश्च स्यात् सदा विप्रो दैवतं च सदा भवेत्। कुटुम्बिको धर्मकामः सदास्वप्नश्च भारत॥
en: Such a Brahman will become a Muni always, a deity, and sleepless forever, and one engaged in the pursuit of virtue only, even if he lives in a family.

sn: मांसादी सदा च स्यात् पवित्रश्च सदा भवेत्। अमृताशी सदा च स्याद् देवतातिथिपूजकः॥
en: He will become a vegetarian always, and pure for ever. He will become an eater always of ambrosia, and an worshipper always of gods and guests.

sn: विघसाशी सदा च स्यात् सदा चैवातिथिव्रतः। श्रद्दधानः सदा च स्याद् देवताद्विजपूजकः॥
en: Indeed, he will be considered as one always living on sacrificial residue, as one ever devoted to the duty of hospitality, as one always full of faith, and as one always adoring gods and guests.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कधं सदोपवासी स्याद् ब्रह्मचारी कथं भवेत्। विघसाशी कथं च स्यात् सदा चैवातिथिव्रतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said one ever How can one practising such penance come to be known as one who is always fasting or as who follows the VOW of Brahmacharya, or as one who always lives upon sacrificial residue, or as one who always worships guests.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अन्तरा प्रातराशं च सायमाशं तथैव च। सदोपवासी स भवेद् योन भुङ्क्तेऽन्तरा पुनः॥
en: Bhishma said He will be considered as one who is always fasting if he eats once during the day and once during the night at the fixed hours without eating anything in the interim.

sn: भार्यां गच्छन् ब्रह्मचारी ऋतौ भवति वै द्विजः। ऋतुवादी भवेन्नित्यं ज्ञाननित्यश्च यो नरः॥
en: Such a Brahman, by always speaking the truth and by following always wisdom, and by going to his wife only in her season and never at other times, becomes a Brahmacharin.

sn: अभक्षयेत् तथा मांसमपांसाशी भवत्यपि। दाननिता; पवित्रश्च अस्वप्नश्च दिवास्वपन्॥
en: By never cating meat of animals not killed for sacrifice, he will become a strict vegetarian. By always becoming charitable he will become ever pure, and by abstaining from sleep during De day he will become one who is always awake.

sn: भृत्यातिथिषु यो शुढे भुक्तवत्सु सदा सदा। अमृतं केवलं भुते इति विद्धि युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Know, O Yudhisthira, that the man who eats only after having fed his servants and guests becomes an eater always of ambrosia.

sn: (अदत्त्वा योऽतिथिभ्योऽन्नं न भुङ्क्ते सोऽतिथिप्रियः। अदत्त्वान्नं दैवतेभ्यो यो न भुङ्क्ते स दैवतम्।।) अभुक्तवत्सु नाश्नानः सततं यस्तु वै द्विजः। अभोजनेन तेनास्य जित: स्वर्गो भवत्युत॥
en: The Brahmana who never eats till gods and guests are fed, acquires by such abstention, heaven itself.

sn: देवताभ्यः पितृभ्यश्च भृत्येभ्योऽतिथिभिः सह। अवशिष्टं तु योऽश्नाति तमाहुर्विघसाशिनम्॥
en: He is said to live upon sacrificial residue who eats only what remains after feeding the gods, the Pitris, servants and guests.

sn: तेषां लोका ह्यपर्यन्ता: सदने ब्रह्मणा सह। उपस्थिताश्चाप्सरोभिः परियान्ति दिवौकसः॥
en: Such men acquires numberless blessed regions in next life. The gods and the Apsaras with Brahman himself, come to their homes.

sn: देवताभिश्च ये सार्धं पितृभिश्चोपभुञ्जते। रमन्ते पुत्रपौत्रैश्च तेषां गतिरनुत्तमा॥
en: They who share their food with the gods and the Pitris pass their days always happily with their sons and grandsons, and at last, leaving off this body, acquire a very high end.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यदिदं कर्म लोकेऽस्मिन् शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्। पुरुषं योजयत्येव फलयोगेन भारता॥१
en: Yudhisthira said In this world, O Bharata, good and bad acts attach themselves to man for the purpose of producing fruits for enjoyment or endurance.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: कर्तास्ति तस्य पुरुष उताहो नेति संशयः। एतदिच्छामि तत्त्वेन त्वत्तः श्रोतुं पितामह॥
en: Is man, however, to be regarded as their doer or is he not to be considered so? My mind is full of doubts regarding this question. I wish to hear this fully from you, O grandfather.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। प्रह्लादस्य च संवादमिन्द्रस्य च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it, О Yudhisthira, is cited the old discourse between Prahlada and Indra.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: असक्तं धूतपाप्मानं कुले जातं बहुश्रुतम्। अस्तब्धमनहङ्कारं सत्त्वस्थं समये रतम्॥ तुल्यनिन्दास्तुति दान्तं शून्यागारनिवासिनम्। चराचराणां भूतानां विदितप्रभवाप्ययम्॥ अक्रुध्यन्तमहष्यन्तमप्रियेषु प्रियेषु च। काञ्चने वाथ लोष्टे वा उभयोः समदर्शनम्॥
en: The king of the Daityas, viz., Prahlada, was unattached to all worldly objects. His sins had been dissipated. Of respectable parentage, he was endued with great learning. Free from stupefaction and pride, ever pervaded by the quality of goodness, and devoted to various vows, he considered praise and censure in the same light. Endued with self-control he was then passing his time in an empty room. Conversant with the origin and the destruction of all created objects mobile and immobile, he was never angry with things that displeased him and never rejoiced at the acquisition of agreeable objects. He considered equally gold and a clod of earth.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: आत्मनि श्रेयसि ज्ञाने धीरं निश्चितनिश्चितम्। परावरज्ञं भूतानां सर्वज्ञं समदर्शनम्॥
en: Earnestly studying the Soul and acquiring Emancipation, and firm in knowledge, he had acquired firm conclusions about truth.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: शक्रः प्रह्लादमासीनमेकान्ते संयतेन्द्रियम्। बुभुत्समानस्तत्प्रज्ञामभिगम्येदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Acquainted with what is supreme and what is not so among all things, omniscient and of universal sight, as he was seated on day in a solitary room with his senses under complete control, Shakra approached him, and desirous

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: यैः कश्चित् सम्मतो लोके गुणैः स्यात् पुरुषो नृषु। भवत्यनपगान् सर्वांस्तान् गुणाल्लँक्षयामहे॥
en: O king, I see all those qualities permanently living in you by which a person acquires the esteem of all.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: अथ ते लक्ष्यते बुद्धिः समा बालजनैरिह। आत्मानं मन्यमानः सन् श्रेयेः किमिह मन्यसे॥
en: Your understanding seems to be like that of a child, free from attachment and aversion. You know the soul. What, do you think, is the best means by which a knowledge of the Soul may be acquired.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: बद्धः पाशैश्च्युतः स्थानाद् द्विषतां वशमागतः। श्रिया विहीनः प्रह्लाद शोचितव्ये न शोचसि॥
en: You are now bound in fetters, fallen off from your former position, brought under the sway of your foes, and divested of prosperity. Your present circumstances are such as may well give room to grief. Yet how is it, O Prahlada, that you do not grieve.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: प्रज्ञालाभात् तु दैतेय उताहो धृतिमत्तया। प्रह्लाद सुस्थरूपोऽसि पश्यन् व्यसनमात्मनः॥
en: Is this owing, O son of Diti, to the acquisition of wisdom or is it on account of your fortitude? Behold your calamities, O Prahlada, and yet you appear like one that is happy and tranquil.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: इति संचोदितस्तेन धीरो निश्चितनिश्चयः। उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा स्वां प्रज्ञामनुवर्णयन्॥
en: Thus urged by Indra, the king of the Daityas, endued with firinness and with fixed conclusions about truth, replied in these sweet words showing great wisdom.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: प्रह्लाद उवाच प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च भूतानां यो न बुद्ध्यते। तस्य स्तम्भो भवेद् बाल्यानास्ति स्तम्भोऽनुपश्यतः।।१४।
en: Prahlada said “He who does not know the origin and the destruction of all created objects, is, on account of such ignorance, stupefied. He, however, who knows these two things, is never stupefied.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: स्वभावात् सम्प्रवर्तन्ते निवर्तन्ते तथैव च। सर्वे भावास्तथाभावाः पुरुषार्थो न विद्यते॥ पुरुषार्थस्य चाभावे नास्ति कश्चिच्च कारकः। स्वयं न कुर्वतस्तस्य जातु मानो भवेदिह॥
en: All kinds of entities and non-entities come into being or cease on account of their own nature. No kind of personal exertion is necessary (for their production). In the absence of personal exertion it is clear that no personal agent exists for the production of all this that we perceive. But though the person never does anything, yet through the influence of Ignorance a consciousness regarding agency over spreads itself on it.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: यस्तु कर्तारमात्मानं मन्यते साध्वसाधु वा। तस्य दोषवती प्रज्ञा अतत्त्वज्ञेति मे मतिः॥
en: He who regards himself as the doer of good or bad acts possesses a vile wisdom. Such a person is, in my opinion, does not know the truth.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: यदि स्यात् पुरुषः कर्ता शक्रात्मश्रेयसे ध्रुवम्। आरम्भास्तस्य सिद्ध्येयुर्न तु जातु परा भवेत्॥ अनिष्टस्य हि निर्वृत्तिरनिर्वृत्तिः प्रियस्य च। लक्ष्यते यतमानानां पुरुषार्थस्ततः कुतः॥
en: If, O Shakra, the being known as person were really the actor, then all acts undertaken for his own benefit would certainly be successful. None of those acts would be futile. Persons struggling their utmost to avoid what is not desired and to bring about what is desired are not to be seen. What becomes then of personal exertion?

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: अनिष्टस्याभिनिर्वृत्तिमिष्टसंवृत्तिमेव च। अप्रयत्नेन पश्यामः केषाञ्चित् तत्स्वभावतः॥
en: In the case of some, we see that without any exertion on their part, what is not desired is not brought about and what is desired, is done. This then must be the result of Nature.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: प्रतिरूपतराः केचिद् दृश्यन्ते बुद्धिमत्तराः। विरूपेभ्योऽल्पबुद्धिभ्यो लिप्समाना धनागमम्॥
en: Some extraordinary persons again are seen, for though possessed of superior intelligence they have to seek wealth from others that are vulgar in features and gifted with little intelligence.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: स्वभावप्रेरिताः सर्वे निविशन्ते गुणा यदा। शुभाशुभास्तदा तत्र कस्य किं मानकारणम्॥
en: Indeed, when all qualities, good or bad, enter a person impelled by Nature, what is there for one to boast (of his superior possessions)?

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: स्वभावादेव तत्सर्वमिति मे निश्चिता मतिः। आत्मप्रतिष्ठा प्रज्ञा वा मम नास्ति ततोऽन्यथा॥
en: All these come from Nature. This is my seitled belief. Even Liberation and knowledge of self, in my view, originate from the same Source.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: कर्मजं त्विह मन्यन्ते फलयोगं शुभाशुभम्। कर्मणां विषयं कृत्स्नमहं वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु॥
en: In this world all fruits, good or bad, that attach themselves to persons, are considered as the outcome of acts. I shall now describe fully the subject of acts. Hear me.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: यथा वेदयते कश्चिदोदनं वायसो ह्यदन्। एवं सर्वाणि कर्माणि स्वभावस्यैव लक्षणम्॥
en: As a crow, while eating some food, announces the presences of that food by its repeated cawing, similarly all our acts only proclaim the indications of Nature.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: विकारानेव यो वेद न वेद प्रकृतिं पराम्। तस्य स्तम्भौ भवेद् बाल्यान्नास्ति स्तम्भोऽनुपश्यतः॥२६
en: He who is acquainted with only the metamorphoses of Nature but not with Nature which is supreme and exist by herself, feels stupefication on account of his ignorance. He, however, who understands the difference between Nature and her metamorphoses is never stupefied.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: स्वभावभाविनो भावान् सर्वानेवेह निश्चयात्। बुद्ध्यमानस्य दर्पो वा मानो वा किं करिष्यति॥
en: All things originate from Nature. On account of one's certain conviction about it, he would never be affected by pride or arrogance.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: वेद धर्मविधि कृत्स्नं भूतानां चाप्यनित्यताम्। तस्माच्छक न शोचामि सर्वं ह्येवेदमन्तवत्॥
en: When I know the origin of all the ordinances of mortality and when I ain acquainted with the instability of all objects, I can not, O Shakra, indulge in grief. All this is endued with an end.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: निर्ममो निरहंकारो निराशीर्मुक्तबन्धनः। स्वस्थो व्यपेतः पश्यामि भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययौ॥
en: Without attachments, without pride, without desire and hope, freed from all fetters, and dissociated from everything, I am passing my time happily, seeing that appearance and disappearance of all created objects.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: कृतप्रज्ञस्य दान्तस्य वितृष्णस्य निराशिषः। नायासो विद्यते शक्र पश्यतो लोकमव्ययम्॥
en: For one who is wise, who is self-controlled, who is contented, who is without desire and hope, and who sees all things with the light of self-knowledge, on trouble or anxiety exists, O Shakra.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: प्रकृतौ च विकारे च न मे प्रीतिर्न च द्विषे। द्वेष्टारं च न पश्यामि यो मामद्य ममायते॥
en: I have no liking or aversion for either Nature or her changes. I do not see any one now who is my enemy nor any one who is mine own.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: नोर्ध्वं नावाङ् न तिर्यक् च न क्वचिच्छक कामये। न हि ज्ञेये न विज्ञाने न ज्ञाने कर्म विद्यते॥
en: I do not, O Shakra, at any time seek either heaven, or this world, or the nether regions. It is not the fact that there is no happiness in understanding the Soul. But the Soul, being dissociated from everything, cannot enjoy happiness. Hence I desire nothing.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: शक्र उवाच येनैषा लभ्यते प्रज्ञा येनु शान्तिरवाप्यते। प्रब्रूहि तमुपायं मे सम्यक् प्रह्लाद पृच्छतः॥
en: Shakra said Tell me the means, O Prahlada, by which this kind of wisdom may be acquired and by which this kind of tranquillity may be made one's own. I pray you.'

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: प्रह्लाद उवाच आर्जवेनाप्रमादेन प्रसादेनात्मवत्तया। वृद्धशुश्रषया शक्र पुरुषो लभते महत्॥
en: Prahlada said 'By simplicity, by carefulness, by purifying the soul, by controlling the passions, and by waiting upon elders, O Shakra, a person acquires liberation.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: स्वभावाल्लभते प्रज्ञां शान्तिमेति स्वभावतः। स्वभावादेव तत्सर्वं यत्किचिदनुपश्यसि॥
en: Know this, however, that one gains wisdom from Nature, and that the acquisition of tranquillity also is owing to the same cause. Indeed, everything else that you see is due to Nature.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: इत्युक्तो दैत्यपतिना शक्रो विस्मयमागमत्। प्रीतिमांश्च तदा राजस्तद्वाक्यं प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: Thus addressed by the king of the Daityas, Shakra became filled with wonder and lauded those words, O king, with a cheerful heart.

description: Is the man doer of good and bad acts
sn: स तदाभ्यर्च्य दैत्येन्द्रं त्रैलोक्यपतिरीश्वरः। असुरेन्द्रमुपामन्त्र्य जगाम स्वं निवेशनम्॥
en: The king of the three worlds then, having adored the lord of the Daityas, took his leave and proceeded to his own quarter.'

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यथा बुद्ध्या महीपालो भ्रष्टश्रीविचरेन्महीम्। कालदण्डविनिष्पिष्टस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhisthira said Tell me, O grandfather, by adopting what sort of intelligence may a king, who has been divested of prosperity and crushed by Time's heavy bludgeon, still live on this Earth.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। वासवस्य च संवादं बलेवैरोचनस्य च॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Vasava and Virochana's son Vali.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: पितामहमुपागम्य प्रणिपत्यकृताञ्जलिः। सर्वानेवासुरान् जित्वा बलिं पप्रच्छ वासवः॥
en: After having defeated all the Assuras, one day Vasava went to the Grandfather and joining his hands bowed to him and enquired after the whereabouts of Vali.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: यस्य स्म ददतो वित्तं न कदाचन हीयते। तं बलिं नाधिगच्छामि ब्रह्मन्नाचक्ष्व मे बलिम्॥
en: Tell me, O Brahman, where may I now find that Vali whose wealth continued undiminished even though he used to distribute it as largely as he wished.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: स वायुर्वरुणश्चैव स रविः स च चन्द्रमाः। सोऽग्निस्तपति भूतानि जलं च स भवत्युत॥
en: He was the god of wind. He was Varuna. He was Surya. He was Soma. He was Agni that used to warm all creatures. He became water. I do not find where he now is. Indeed, O Brahmana, tell me where I may find Vali now.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: तं बलिं नाधिगच्छामि ब्रह्मन्नाचक्ष्व मे बलिम्। स एव ह्यस्तमयते स स्म विद्योतते दिशः॥ स वर्षति स्म वर्षाणि यथाकालमतन्द्रितः। तं बलिं नाधिगच्छामि ब्रह्मन्नाचक्ष्व मे बलिम्॥
en: Formerly, it was he who used to light up all the cardinal points and to set. Shaking off idieness, it was he who used to pour rain upon all creatures at the proper season. I do not now see that Vali. Indeed, tell me, O Brahman, where I may find that king of the Asuras now.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच नैतत् ते साधु मघवन् यदेनमनुपृच्छसि। पृष्टस्तु नानृतं ब्रूयात् तस्माद् वक्ष्यामि ते बलिम्॥
en: Brahman said You should not, O Maghavat, thus enquire after Vali now! One should not, however, speak a falsehood when he is questioned by another. I shall tell you the whereabouts of Vali.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: उष्टेषु यदि वा गोषु खरेष्वश्वेषु वा पुनः। वरिष्ठो भविता जन्तुः शून्यागारे शचीपते॥
en: O husband of Sachi, Vali may now have taken his birth among camels or bulls or asses or horses, and having become the foremost of his species may now be living in an empty room.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: शक्र उवाच यदि स्म बलिना ब्रह्मशून्यागारे समेयिवान्। हन्यामेनं न वा हन्यां तद् ब्रह्मन्ननुशाधि माम्॥
en: Shakra said 'If, O Brahman, I happen to meet with Vali in an empty room, shall I kill him or spare him? Tell me how I shall act!'

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच मा स्म शक्र बलिं हिंसीन बलिर्वधमर्हति। न्यायस्तु शक्र प्रष्टव्यस्त्वया वासव काम्यया॥
en: Brahma said 'Do not, O Shakra, injure Vali! Vali does not deserve death. You should, on the other hand, O Vasava, seek instruction from him about morality, O Shakra, as you wish,'

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: एवमुक्तो भगवता महेन्द्रः पृथिवीं तदा। चचारैरावतस्कन्धमधिरुह्य श्रिया वृतः॥
en: ‘Thus addressed by the divine Creator, Indra travelled over the Earth, seated on Airavata in great splendour.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: ततो ददर्श स बलिं खरवेषेण संवृतम्। यथाऽऽख्यातं भगवता शून्यागारकृतालयम्॥
en: He succeeded in meeting with Vali, who, as the Creator had said, was living in an empty room, clothed in the form of an ass.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: शक्र उवाच खरयोनिमनुप्राप्तस्तुषभक्षोऽसि दानव। इयं ते योनिरधमा शोचस्याहो न शोचसि॥
en: 'You are now, O Danava, born as an ass living on chaff. This your birth is certainly a low one. Do you or do you not grieve for it?

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: अदृष्टं बत पश्यामि द्विषतां वशामागतम्। श्रिया विहीनं मित्रैश्च भ्रष्टवीर्यपराक्रमम्॥
en: I see what I had never seen before, viz., yourself brought under the control of your enemies, divested of prosperity and friends, and shorn of energy and prowess.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: यत् तद् यानसहौस्त्वं ज्ञातिभिः परिवारितः। लोकान् प्रतापयन् सर्वान् यास्यस्मानवितर्कयन्॥
en: Formerly you used to march through the words, with your train consisting of thousands of carriages and thousands of kinsmen, and to move along, burning, everybody with your splendour and disregarding us all.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: त्वन्मुखाश्चैव दैतेय व्यतिष्ठंस्त्व शासने। अकृष्टपच्या च मही तवैश्वर्ये बभूव ह॥
en: Considering you as their protector the Daityas lived under your sway! Through your power, the Earth used to yield crops without waiting for tillage. To-day, however, I behold you overtaken by this dire calamity! Do you or do you not grieve for this.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: इदं च तेऽद्य व्यसनं शोचस्याहो न शोचसि। यदाऽऽतिष्ठः समुद्रस्य पूर्वकूले विलेलिहन्॥
en: When formerly you used with pride beaming on your face, to divide on the eastern shores of the ocean your vast wealth among thy kinsmen, what then was the state of your mind?

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: ज्ञातीन् विभजतो वित्तं तदाऽऽसीत् ते मनः कथम्। यत् ते सहस्रसमिता ननृतुर्देवयोषितः॥
en: Formerly, for many years, when shining with splendour, you used to sport, thousands of celestial damsels used to dance before you.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: कथमद्य तदा चैव मनस्ते दानवेश्वर। छत्रं तवासीत् सुमहत् सौवर्णं रत्नभूषितम्॥
en: All of them were decorated with garlands of lotuses and all had companions bright as gold. What, O king of Danavas, was the state of your mind then and what is it now.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: बहूनि वर्षपूगानि विहारे दीप्यतः श्रिया। सर्वाः पुष्करमालिन्यः सर्वाः काञ्चनसप्रभाः॥
en: You had a very large golden umbrella set with jewels and gems. Fully forty-two thousand Gandharvas used in those days to dance before you.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: ननृतुस्तत्र गन्धर्वाः षट् सहस्राणि सप्तधा। यूपस्तवासीत् सुमहान् यजतः सर्वकाशनः॥
en: In your sacrifices you had a very large stake made entirely of gold. On such occasions you used to give away millions and millions of kine. What, O Ditya, was the state of your mind then?

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: यत्राददः सहस्राणि अयुतानां गवां दश। अनन्तरं सहस्रेण तदाऽऽसीद् दैन्य का मतिः॥
en: Formerly, engaged in sacrifice, you had gone round the whole Earth, following the rule of the hurling of the Shamya. What was the state of your mind then?

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: यदा च पृथिवीं सर्वां यजमानोऽनुपर्यगाः। शम्याक्षेपेण विधिना तदाऽऽसीत् किं तु ते हृदि॥ न ते पश्यामि भृङ्गारं न च्छत्रं व्यजने न च। ब्रह्मदत्तां च ते मालां न पश्याम्यसुराधिप॥
en: I do not now see that golden jar of yours, nor that umbrella of yours, nor those fans. I behold not also, O king of the Asuras, that garland which was given given to you by Grandfather.'

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: बलिरुवाच न त्वं पश्यसि भृङ्गारं न च्छत्रं व्यजने न च। ब्रह्मदत्तां च मे मालां न त्वं द्रक्ष्यसि वासव॥
en: Bali said. 'You do not behold now, O Vasava, my jar and umbrella and fans. You do not see also my garland, that was given by the Grandfather.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: गुहायां निहितानि त्वं मम रत्नानि पृच्छसि। यदा मे भविता कालस्तदा त्वं यानि द्रक्ष्यसि॥
en: Those valuable possessions of mine about which you ask are now buried in the darkness of a cave. When my time comes again, you will, forsooth, behold them again.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: न त्वेतदनुरूपं ते यशसो वा कुलस्य च। समृद्धार्थोऽसमृद्धार्थं यन्मां कस्थितुमिच्छसि॥
en: This conduct of yours, however, does not become your fame or birth. Yourself enjoying prosperity, you wish to mock me that am sunk in adversity.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: न हि दुःखेषु शोचन्ते न प्रहृष्यन्ति चर्धिषु। कृतप्रज्ञा ज्ञानतृप्ताः क्षान्ताः सन्तो मनीषिणः॥
en: They who acquired wisdom, and have won contentment therefrom, they who are of tranquil should, who are virtuous and good among creatures, never grieve in misery nor rejoice in happiness.

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: त्वं तु प्राकृतया बुद्ध्या पुरन्दर विकत्यसे। यदाहमिव भावी स्यास्तदा नैवं वदिष्यसि॥
en: Guided, however, by a vulgar intelligence, you are bragging, O Purandara. When you will become like me you will not then give vent to speeches like these.'

description: By following what intelligence can a king born of prosperity live on earth
sn: त्वं तु प्राकृतया बुद्ध्या पुरन्दर विकत्यसे। यदाहमिव भावी स्यास्तदा नैवं वदिष्यसि॥
en: Guided, however, by a vulgar intelligence, you are bragging, O Purandara. When you will become like me you will not then give vent to speeches like these.'

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच पुनरेव तु तं शक्रः प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्। निःश्वसन्तं यथा नागं प्रव्याहाराय भारत॥
en: Bhishma said Again, laughing at Vali who was sighing like a snake, Shakra addressed him for saying something more painful than what he had said before.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: शक्र उवाच यत् तद् यानसहस्रेण ज्ञातिभिः परिवारितः। लोकान् प्रतापयन् सर्वान् यास्यस्मानवितर्कयन्॥
en: Shakra said Formerly, attended by a train consisting of thousands of vehicles and kinsmen, you used to march, burning all the worlds with your splendour and disregarding us all.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: दृष्ट्वा सुकृपणां चेमामवस्थामात्मनो बले। ज्ञातिमित्रपरित्यक्तः शोचस्याहो न शोचसि॥
en: You are now, however, deserted by both kinsmen and friends. Beholding this miserable condition of yours, do you or do you not indulge in grief?

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: प्रीतिं प्राप्यातुलां पूर्वं लोकांश्चात्मवशे स्थितान्। विनिपातमिमं बाह्यं शोचस्याहो न शोचसि॥
en: Formerly all the worlds were under your sway and great was your joy. I ask, do you or you not grieve now, for this loss of your splendour?

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: बलिरुवाच अनित्यमुपलक्ष्येह कालपर्यायधर्मतः। तस्माच्छक न शोचामि सर्वं ह्येवेदमन्तवत्॥
en: Vali said Regarding all this as transitory,-due, indeed, to the course of time,-I do not, O Shakra, grieve. These things have an end.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: अन्वन्त इमे देहा भूतानां च सुराधिप। तेन शक न शोचामि नापराधादिदं मम॥
en: These bodies of creatures, O king of the celestials, are all transitory. Therefore, 0 Shakra, I do not grieve. Nor is this form due to any fault of mine.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: जीवितं च शरीरं च जात्यैव सह जायते। उमे सह विवर्धते उभे सह विनश्यतः॥
en: The animating principle and the body come into existence simultaneously for their own nature. They grow together and meet with destruction together.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: न हीदृशमहं भावमवशः प्राप्य केवलम्। यदेवमभिजानामि का व्यथा मे विजानतः॥
en: Having obtained this form of birth I have not been enslaved by it for good. Since I know this, I have no cause for sorrow.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: भूतानां निधनं निष्ठा स्रोतसामिव सागरः। नैतत् सम्यग्विजानन्तो नरा मुह्यन्ति वज्रधृक्॥ य त्वेवं नाभिजानन्ति रजोमोहपरायणाः। ते कृच्छं प्राप्य सीदन्ति बुद्धिर्येषां प्रणश्यति॥
en: As the final place of all rivers is the ocean, so the end of all embodied creatures is death. Those persons that know this well are never stupefied, O holder of the thunder-bolt. 10. They, however, who, overwhelmed with Darkness and loss of judgement, do not know this, they whose understanding is lost, sink under the load of misfortune.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: बुद्धिलाभात् तु पुरुषः सर्वं तुदति किल्बिषम्। विपाप्मा लभते सत्त्वं सत्त्वस्थः सम्प्रसीदति॥
en: A person wins a keen understanding, succeeds in dissipating all his sins. A sinless person acquires the quality of Goodness, and having acquired it becomes cheerful.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: ततस्तु ये निवर्तन्ते जायन्ते वा पुनः पुनः। कृपणाः परितप्यन्ते तैरथैरभिचोदिताः॥
en: They, however, that deviate from the quality of Goodness, and go through repeated re-births, are obliged to indulge in sorrow and grief, led on by desire and the objects of the senises,

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: अर्थसिद्धिमनर्थं च जीवितं मरणं तथा। सुखदुःखफले चैव न दृष्मि न च कामये॥
en: I neither dislike nor like success or defeat, regarding the attainment of all objects of desire, life, or death, the fruits of action that are represented by pleasure or pain.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: हतं हन्ति हतो ह्येव यो नरो हन्ति कञ्चन। उभौ तौ न विजानीतो यश्च हन्ति हतश्च यः॥
en: When one kills another, he kills only that other's body. That man who thinks that it is he who kills another, is himself killed. Indeed, both of then do not know the truth, viz., he who kills and he who is killed.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: हत्वा जित्वा च मघवन् यः कश्चित् पुरुषायते। अकर्ता होव भवति कर्ता ह्येव करोति तत्॥
en: O Maghavat, that person, who having killed or defeated any one brags of his manliness, should know that he is not the actor, but that the act has been performed by another who is the real agent.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: को हि लोकस्य कुरुते विनाशप्रभवावुभौ। कृतं हि तत् कृतेनैव कर्ता तस्यापि चापरः॥
en: When it is asked that who is it that brings about the creation and destruction of things in the world, it is generally thought that some person has caused it. Know, however, that the person who is so known has a creator.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: पृथिवी ज्योतिराकाशमापो वायुश्च पञ्चमः। एतद्योनीनि भूतानि तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: Earth, light or heat, ether, water, and wind form the fifth-from these do all creatures originate. (When I know this) what sorrow can I feel?

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: महाविद्योऽल्पविद्यश्च बलवान् दुर्बलश्च यः। दर्शनीयो विरूपश्च सुभगो दुर्भगश्च यः॥ सर्वं काल: समादत्ते गम्भीरः स्वेन तेजसा। तस्मिन् कालवशं प्राप्ते का व्यथा मे विजानतः॥
en: One who is endued with great learning, one who is not much learned, one who is strong, one who is destitute of strength, one who is beautiful, and one who is very ugly, one who is lucky, and one who is not blessed by fortune, are all carried away by Time, which is too deep to be measured by its own energy. When I know that I have been defeated by Time what sorrow can I feel.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: दग्धमेवानुदहति हतमेवानुहन्यते। नश्यते नष्टमेवाग्रे लब्धव्यं लभते नरः॥
en: One that burns anything burns a thing that has been already burnt. One who kills, only kills, a victim already killed. One who is destroyed, has been before destroyed. A thing that is acquired by a person is what is already arrived and intended for his acquirement.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: नास्य द्वीप: कुतः पारो नावारः सम्प्रदृश्यते। नान्तमस्य प्रपश्यामि विधेर्दिव्यस्य चिन्तयन्॥
en: This Time is like an ocean. There is no island in it. Its other shore is beyond reach. Its boundary cannot be seen. Thinking even deeply, I do not see the end of this continuous steam that is the great ordainer of all things and that is, forsooth celestial.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: यदि मे पश्यतः कालो भूतानि न विनाशयेत्। स्यान्मे हर्षश्च दर्पश्च क्रोधश्चैव शचीपते॥
en: If I did not know that it is Time which destroys all creatures, then, perhaps, I would have experienced the emotions of joy, pride and anger, O husband of Shachi.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: तुषभक्षं तु मां ज्ञात्वा प्रविविक्तजने गृहे। बिभ्रतं गार्दभं रूपमागत्य परिगर्हसे॥२३॥
en: Have you come here to condemn me, having come to know that I am now assuming the form of an ass that lives upon chaff and that is now passing his days in a lonely spot remote from the dwellings of men.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: इच्छन्नहं विकुर्यां हि रूपाणि बहुधाऽऽत्मनः। विभीषणानि यानीक्ष्य पलायेथास्त्वमेव मे॥
en: If I wish, even now I can assume various dreadful forms, seeing any one of which you would immediately fly away from my presence.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: कालः सर्वं समादत्ते कालः सर्वं प्रयच्छति। कालेन विहितं सर्वं मा कृथाः शक्र पौरुषम्॥
en: It is Time that gives every thing and again takes away everything. It is Time that ordains all things. Do not, O Shakra, brag of your manliness.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: पुरा सर्वं प्रव्यथितं मयि क्रुद्धे पुरंदर। अवैमि त्वस्य लोकस्य धर्मं शक्र सनातनम्॥
en: Formerly, O Purandara, whenever, I used to be angry everything used to become agitated. I know, however, O Shakra, that eternal attributes of all things in the world.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: त्वमप्येवमवेक्षस्व माऽऽत्मना विस्मयं गमः। प्रभवश्च प्रभावश्च नात्मसंस्थः कदाचन।॥
en: Do you also know the truth. Do not allow yourself to be filled with wonder. Prosperity and its origin are not under one's control.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: कौमारमेव ते चित्तं तथैवाद्य यथा पुरा। समवेक्षस्व मघवन् बुद्धिं विन्दस्व नैष्ठिकीम्॥
en: Your mind is like that of a child. It is the same as it was before. Open your eyes, O Maghavat and acquire an understanding which is sure and true.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: देवा मनुष्याः पितरो गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसाः। आसन् सर्वे मम वशे नत् सर्वं वेत्थ वासव॥
en: In days gone by, that gods, men, the Pitris, the Gandharvas, the Nagas, and the Rakshasas, were all under my control. You know this, O Vasava.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: नमस्तस्यै दिशेऽप्यस्तु यस्यां वैरोचनो बलिः इति मामभ्यपद्यन्त बुद्धिमात्सर्यमोहिताः॥ । नाहं तदनुशोचामि नात्मभ्रंशं शचीपते। एवं मे निश्चिता बुद्धिः शास्तुस्तिष्ठाम्यहं वशे॥
en: Having their understandings overcome by ignorance, all creatures used to flatter me, saying,-Salutations to that cardinal point where Virochana's son Vali may now be living, O husband of Sachi, I do not at all grieve when I think of that honour. I am not sorry for this fall of mine. My understanding is very strong here, viz., that I will abide by the sway of the Ordainer.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: दृश्यते हि कुले जातो दर्शनीयः प्रतापवान्। दुःखं जीवन् सहामात्यो भवितव्यं हि तत् तथा॥
en: It is seen that some one of nobly born highly beautiful and powerful, lives in misery, with all his counsellors and friends. This happens because it has been so ordained.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: दौष्कुलेयस्तथा मूढो दुर्जातः शक्र दृश्यते। सुखं जीवन् सहामात्यो भवितव्यं हि तत् तथा॥
en: Likewise, some one born in an ignoble race, devoid of knowledge, and with even a stain on his birth, is seen, O Shakra, to live happily with all his counsellors and friends. This also happens because it has been so oridained.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: कल्याणी रूपसम्पन्ना दुर्भगा शक्र दृश्यते। अलक्षणा विरूपा च सुभगा दृश्यते परा॥
en: An auspicious and beautiful woman, O Shakra, is seen to pass her life miserably. Likewise, ugly woman with every inauspicious mark is seen to live in great happiness.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: नैतदस्मत्कृतं शक्र नैतच्छक त्वया कृतम्। यत् त्वमेवंगतो जिन् यच्चाप्येवंगता वयम्॥
en: That we have now become so is not owing to any act of ours, O Shakra. That you are now so is not owing, O holder of the thunderbolt, to any act of yours?

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: न कर्म भविताप्येतत् कृतं मम शतक्रतो। ऋद्धिर्वाप्यथवा नद्धिः पर्यायकृतमेव तत्॥
en: You have not done anything, O you of a hundred sacrifices, for which you are now an enjoying this prosperity. Nor have I done anything for which I have now been shorn of prosperity. Prosperity and adversity come in succession.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: पश्यामि त्वां विराजत्वं देवराजमवस्थितम्। श्रीमन्तं द्युतिमन्तं च गर्जमानं ममोपरि॥
en: I now see you blazing with splendour, endued with prosperity, possessed of beauty, placed at the head of all the gods, and thus roaring at me.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: एवं नैव न चेत् कालो मामाक्रम्य स्थितो भवेत्। पातयेयमहं त्वाद्य सवज्रमपि मुष्टिना॥
en: This would never be but for the Time standing near after having attacked me. Indeed, if Time had not attacked me I would have today slain you with only a blow of my fists albeit you are armed with the thunder.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: न तु विक्रमकालोऽयं शान्तिकालोऽयमागतः। कालः स्थापयते सर्वं काल: पचति वै तथा॥
en: This, however, is not the time for displaying my prowess. On the other hand, the time that has come when I should conduct myself with peace and tranquillity. It is Time which establishes all things. Time acts upon all things and brings about their final consummation.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: मां चेदभ्यागतः कालो दानवेश्वरपूजितम्। गर्जन्तं प्रतपन्तं च कमन्यं नागमिष्यति॥
en: I was the adored king of the Danavas. Consuming all with my energy, I used to roar in strength and pride. When Time has attacked even myself, who is there whom he will not attack.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: द्वादशानां तु भवतामादित्यानां महात्मनाम्। तेजांस्येकेन सर्वेषां देवराज धृतानि मे॥
en: Formerly, O king of the gods, singly I bore the energy of all the twelve illustrious Adityas with yourself amongst them.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: अहमेवोद्वहाम्यापो विसृजामि च वासव। तपामि चैव त्रैलोक्यं विद्योताम्यहमेव च॥
en: It was I that used to bear up water and then to shower it as rain. O Vasava! It was I who used to give both light and heat to the three worlds.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: संरक्षामि विलुम्पामि ददाम्यहमथाददे। संयच्छामि नियच्छामि लोकेषु प्रभुरीश्वरः॥
en: It was I who used to protect and it was I that used to destroy. It was I who gave and it was I who took. It was I who used to bind and it was I who used to unbind. In all the worlds I was the one powerful master.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: तदद्य विनिवृत्तं मे प्रभुत्वममराधिप। कालसैन्यावगाढस्य सर्वं न प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: That sovereign control which I had, O king of the gods, is now gone. I am now attacked by the foreces of Time. Those things, therefore, are no longer seen to shine in me.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: नाहं कर्ता न चैव त्वं नान्यः कर्ता शचीपते। पर्यायेण हि भुज्यन्ते लोकाः शक्र यदृच्छया॥
en: I am not the actor. You are not the actor. None else, O husband of Sachi, is the doer. It is Time, O Shakra, that protects or destroys all things.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: मासमासार्धवेश्मानमहोरात्राभिसंवृतम्। ऋतुद्वारं वर्षमुखमायुर्वेदविदो जनाः॥
en: Persons well-read in the Vedas say that me is Brahma. The fortnights and months are his body. That body is clothed with days and nights as its dresses. The seasons are his senses. The year is his mouth.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: आहुः सर्वमिदं चिन्त्यं जनाः केचिन्मनीषया। अस्याः पञ्चैव चिन्तायाः पर्येष्यामि च पञ्चधा॥
en: Some people, on account of their superior intelligence, say that the entire universe should be conceived as Brahma. The Vedas, however, teach, that the five sacs that cover the Soul should be known as Brahma.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: गम्भीरं गहनं ब्रह्म महत्तोयार्णवं यथा। अनादिनिधनं चाहुरक्षरं क्षरमेव च॥
en: Brahma is deep and inaccessible like a deep ocean. It is said that it has neither beginning nor end, and that it is both indestructible and destructible.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: सत्त्वेषु लिङ्गमावेश्य निर्लिङ्गमपि तत् स्वयम्। मन्यन्ते ध्रुवमेवैनं ये जनास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥
en: Though it is by nature without attributes yet it enters all existent objects and as such is clothed with attributes. Those persons who know truth consider Brahma as eternal.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: भूतानां तु विपर्यासं कुरुते भगवानिति। न ह्येतावद् भवेद् गम्यं न यस्मात् प्रभवेत् पुनः॥
en: Through the force of Ignorance, Brahma makes the attribute of materiality to invest the Chit or Soul which is immaterial spirit. Materiality, however, is not the true attribute of the Soul.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: गतिं हि सर्वभूतानामगत्वा क्व गमिष्यति। यो धावता न हातव्यस्तिष्ठन्नपि न हीयते॥
en: Brahma in the form of Time is the refuge of all creatures. Where can you go transcending that Time? Time or Brahma, indeed, cannot be shunned by running nor by standing still.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: तमिन्द्रियाणि सर्वाणि नानुपश्यन्ति पञ्चधा। आहुश्चै केचिदग्नि केचिदाहुः प्रजापतिम्॥ ऋतून् मासार्धमासांश्च दिवसांश्च क्षणांस्तथा। पूर्वाह्लमपराहं च मध्याह्नमपि चापरे॥ मुहूर्तमपि चैवाहुरेकं सन्तमनेकधा। तं कालमिति जानीहि यस्य सर्वमिदं वशे॥
en: All the five senses cannot perceive Brahma. Some have said that Brahma is Fire ; some that he is Prajapati, some that he is the Seasons; some that he is the Month; some that he is the Fortnight; some that he is the Days; some that he is the Hours; some that he is the Morning; some that he is the Noon; some that he is the Evening, and some that he is the Moment. Thus various people speak variously of him, who is one. Know that he is Eternity, under whose control exist all things.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: बहूनीन्द्रसहस्राणि समतीतानि वासव। बलवीर्योपपन्नानि यथैव त्वं शचीपते।॥
en: Many thousands of Indras have gone away, O Vasava, cach of whom was endued with great strength and prowess. Similarly you also, O lord of Shachi, shall have to pass away.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: त्वामप्यतिबलं शक्र देवराज बलोत्कटम्। प्राप्ते काले महावीर्यः कालः संशमयिष्यति॥
en: The omnipotent Time will destroy you too, O Shakra, who are endued with swelling might and that are the chief of the deities, when your hour comes.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: य इदं सर्वमादत्ते तस्माच्छक स्थिरो भव। मया त्वया च पूर्वेश्च न स शक्योऽतिवर्तितुम्॥
en: Time carries away all things. Therefore, O Indra, do not brag! Time cannot be quieted by either you or me or by those gone before us.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: योमतां प्राप्य जानीषे राज्यश्रियमनुत्तमाम्। स्थिता मयीति तन्मिथ्या नैषा होकत्र तिष्ठति॥
en: This kingly prosperity which you have acquired and which you consider incomparable, had formerly been possessed by me. It is unsubstantial and unreal. She does not live long in one place.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: स्थिता हीन्द्र सहस्रेषु त्वद्विशिष्टतमेष्वियम्। मां च लोला परित्यज्य त्वामगाद् विबुधाधिप॥
en: Indeed, she had lived in thousands of Indras before you, all of whom, again, were, very much superior to you! Unstable as she is, leaving me she has now approached you, O king of the gods.

description: The dialogue between Shakra and Vali on the subject
sn: मैवं शक्र पुनः कार्षीः शान्तो भवितुमर्हसि। त्वामप्येवंविधं ज्ञात्वा क्षिप्रमन्यं गमिष्यति॥
en: Do not, O Shakra, brag again! You should become tranquil! Knowing you to be full of vanity, she will very soon leave you.'

sn: भीष्म उवाच शतक्रतुरथापश्यद् बलेर्दीप्तां महात्मनः। स्वरूपिणी शरीराद्धि निष्कामन्तीं तदा श्रियम्॥
en: Bhishma said “After this, the god of a hundred sacrifices saw the goddess of Prosperity, in her own embodied, but shining, form, issue out of the body of the great Vali.

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा प्रभया दीप्तां भगवान् पाकशासनः। विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयनो बलिं पप्रच्छ वासवः॥
en: Beholding the goddess blazing with radiance, the illustrious chastiser of Paka, addressed Vali thus with eyes expanded in wonder.

sn: शक्र उवाच बले केयमपक्रान्ता रोचमाना शिखण्डिनी। त्वत्त: स्थिता सकेयूरा दीप्यमाना स्वतेजसा।॥
en: Shakra said 'O Vali, who is this one, thus shining effulgently, thus adorned with a crown, thus adorned with golden bracelets on her upper arms, and thus emitting a halo on all sides on account of her energy that is issuing out of your body.'

sn: बलिरुवाच न हीमामासुरी वेदि न दैवीं च न मानुषीम्। त्वमेनां पृच्छ वा मा वा यथेष्टं कुरु वासव॥
en: Vali said I do not know whether she is an Asura woman or a celestial one, or a human one. You may or may not ask her yourself. Do what pleases you."

sn: शक्र उवाच का त्वं बलेरपक्रान्ता रोचमाना शिखण्डिनी। अजानतो ममाचक्ष्व नामधेयं शुचिस्मिते॥
en: Shakra said 'O You of sweet smiles, who are you who are so effulgent and adorned with plumes that thus issue from the body of Vali! I do not know you, kindly tell me your name.

sn: का त्वं तिष्ठसि मामेवं दीप्यमाना स्वतेजसा। हित्वा दैत्यवरं सुभ्र तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः॥
en: Who, indeed, are you that thus stand here as Maya herself, shining with your own splendour, after having left the lord of the Daityas? O, tell me this as I ask you.'

sn: श्रीरुवाच न मां विरोचनो वेद नायं वैरोचनो बलिः। आहुर्मी दुःसहेत्येवं विधिति च मां विदुः॥
en: Virochana did not know, me, His son this Vali knows me not. The learned called me by the name of Dusshaha (born with difficulty). Some knew me by the name of Vidhitsa (desire for action).

sn: भूतिर्लक्ष्मीति मामाहुः श्रीरित्येवं च वासव। त्वं मां शक न जानीषे सर्वे देवा न मां विदुः॥
en: I have other names also, O Vasava! They are Bhuti, Lakshmi, and Shree (prosperity). You know me not, O Shakra, nor does any one among the gods know me.'

sn: शक्र उवाच किमिदं त्वं मम कृते उताहो बलिनः कृते। दुःसहे विजहास्येनं चिरसंवासिनी सती॥
en: Shakra said-'O lady who is difficult of being borne, why do you leave Vali now after having lived in him for a long time? It is owing to any act of mine or is it owing to any act of Vali's.'

sn: श्रीरुवाच नो धाता न विधाता मां विदधाति कथंचन। कालस्तु शक्र पर्यागा-मैनं शक्रावमन्यथाः॥
en: Shree said 'Neither the Creator nor the Ordainer governs me. It is Time that takes me from one place to another. Do not, O Shakra, disrespect Vali.'

sn: शक्र उवाच कथं त्वया बलिस्त्यक्तः किमर्थं वा शिखण्डिनि। कथं च मां न जह्यास्त्वं तन्मे ब्रूहि शुचिस्मिते॥
en: Shakra said 'Why O goddess adorned with plumes, do you leave Vali? Why also do you approach me? Tell me this, O you of sweet smiles!

sn: श्रीरुवाच सत्ये स्थितास्मि दाने च व्रते तपसि चैव हि। पराक्रमे च धर्मे च पराचीनस्ततो बलिः॥
en: Shree said 'I reside in truth, in gifts, in good vows, in penances in prowess, and in virtue! Vali has fallen off from all these.

sn: ब्रह्मण्योऽयं पुरा भूत्वा सत्यवादी जितेन्द्रियः। अभ्यसूयद् ब्राह्मणानामुच्छिष्टश्चास्पृशद् घृतम्॥
en: Formerly he was devoted to the Brahmanas. He was truthful and had mastered his passions. Latterly, however, he began to entertain feelings of animosity towards the Brahmanas and touched clarified butter with impure hands.

sn: यज्ञशीलः सदा भूत्वा मामेव यजत स्वयम्। प्रोवाच लोकान् मूढात्मा कालेनोपनिपीडितः॥
en: Formerly he was always used to perform sacrifices. At last, blinded by ignorance and possessed by Time he began to brag before all persons, saying that his adorations towards me were ceaseless.

sn: अपाकृता ततः शक्र त्वयि वत्स्यामि वासवा अप्रमत्तेन धार्यास्मि तपसा विक्रमेण च॥
en: Leaving him I shall henceforth, O Shakra, live in you! You should bear me vigilantly, and with penances and prowess.

sn: शक्र उवाच नास्ति देवमनुष्येषु सर्वभूतेषु वा पुमान्। यस्त्वामेको विषहितुं शक्नुयात् कमलालये॥
en: Shakra said O you who live in lotuses, there is not a single person among gods, men, and all creatures, that can bear you for ever!

sn: श्रीरुवाच नैव देवो न गन्धर्वो नासुरो न च राक्षसः। यो मामेको विषहितुं शक्तः कश्चित् पुरंदर॥
en: 'Truly, O Purandara, there is none among gods, Gandharvas, Asuras, or Rakshasas, who can bear me for ever!'

sn: शक्र उवाच तिष्ठेथा मयि नित्यं त्वं यथा तद् ब्रूहि मे शुभे। तत् करिष्यामि ते वाक्यमृतं तद् वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Shakra said O auspicious lady, tell me how I should behave so that you may live in me perpetually. I shall, forsooth, obey your commands. You should answer me truly.'

sn: श्रीरुवाच स्थास्यामि नित्यं देवेन्द्र यथा त्वयि निबोध तत्। विधिना वेददृष्टेन चतुर्धा विभजस्व माम्॥
en: Shree said four parts 'O King of the deities, I shall tell you as to how I may be entitled to live in you perpetually. Divide me into four according to the Vedic injunction.'

sn: शक्र उवाच अहं वै त्वां निधास्यामि यथाशक्ति यथाबलम्। न त मेऽतिक्रमः स्याद् स्याद् वै सदा लक्ष्मि तवान्तिके॥
en: Shakra said I shall give you habitations according to their strength and power in bearing you. As regards myself, I shall always take care, O Lakshmi, that I may not offend you in any way.

sn: भूमिरेव मनुष्येषु धारिणी भूतभाविनी। सा ते पादं तितिक्षेत समर्था हीति मे मतिः॥
en: Amongst men, the Earth, that mother of all things, bears them all. She shall bear a fourth part of yourself. I think she has the strength to do so.

sn: श्रीरुवाच एष मे निहितः पादो योऽयं भूमौ प्रतिष्ठितः। द्वितीयं शक्र पादं मे तस्मात् सुनिहितं कुरु॥
en: Shree said-Here, I give up a quarter of myself. Let it be placed on the Earth. Do you, next, make a proper distribution, O Shakra, for my second quarter.

sn: शक्र उवाच आप एव मनुष्येषु द्रवन्त्यः परिचारिणीः। तास्ते पादं तितिक्षन्तामलमापस्तितिक्षितुम्॥
en: Shakra said 'The waters, among men, in their liquid form, do various services to men. Let the waters bear a fourth part of your person. They have the strength to bear a fourth part of you person. They have the strength to bear a portion of yours.'

sn: श्रीरुवाच एष मे निहितः पादो योऽयमप्सु प्रतिष्ठितः। तृतीयं शक्र पादं मे तस्मात् सुनिहितं कुरु॥
en: 'I give up another quarter of mind that is to be placed in the waters. Do you, next, O Shakra, assign a proper place for my third quarter.

sn: शक्र उवाच यस्मिन् वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च यस्मिन् देवा: प्रतिष्ठिताः। तृतीयं पादमग्निस्ते सुधृतं धारयिष्यति॥
en: Shakra said 'The Vedas, the sacrifices, and the gods are all established in Fire. Fire will bear your third quarter, when it is placed therein.'

sn: श्रीरुवाच एष मे निहितः पादो योऽयमग्नौ प्रतिष्ठितः। चतुर्थं शक्र पादं मे तस्मात् सुनिहितं कुरु॥
en: Shree said 'Here I give up my third quarter which is to be placed in Fire. Do you, O Shakra, after this, ! assign a proper place for my last quarter!'

sn: शक्र उवाच ये वै सन्तो मनुष्येषु ब्रह्मण्याः सत्यवादिनः। ते ते पादं तितिक्षन्तामलं सन्तस्तितिक्षितुम्॥
en: Shakra said They who are good among men devoted to Brahmanas, and truthful in speech, may bear your fourth quarter. The good have the power to it.

sn: श्रीरुवाच एष मे निहितः पादो योऽयं सत्सु प्रतिष्ठितः। एवं हि निहिता शक्र भूतेषु परिधत्स्व माम्॥
en: Shree said “Here, I give up my fourth quarter that is to be placed among the good. My portions thus given to different creatures, do you continue to protect me, O Shakra.'

sn: शक्र उवाच भूतानामिह यो वै त्वां मया विनिहितां सतीम्। उपहन्यात् स मे धृष्यस्तथा शृण्वन्तु मे वचः॥ ततस्त्यक्तः श्रिया राजा दैत्यानां बलिरब्रवीत्। यावत् पुरस्तात् प्रतपेत् तावद् वै दक्षिणां दिशम्। पश्चिमां तावदेवापि तथोदीची दिवाकरः॥
en: Shakra said ‘Listen to my words. I have thus distributed you among different creatures. Those among creatures that will offend you shall be punished by me.-The king of the Daityas, viz., Vali, thus left by Shree, then said, at present the Sun shines equally in the east, west, north and south.

sn: तथा मध्यंदिने सूर्यो नास्तमेति यदा तदा। पुनर्देवासुरं युद्धं भावि जेतास्मि वस्तदा॥
en: When, however, withdrawing himself from all quarters, the Sun will shine only upon the region of Brahman that is situate in the middle of Sumeru, then will again take place a great battle between the gods and the Asuras, and in that fight I shall certainly defeat all of you.

sn: सर्वलोकान् यदाऽऽदित्य एकस्थस्तापयिष्यति। तदा देवासुरे युद्धे जेताहं त्वां शतक्रतो॥
en: When withdrawing himself from all quarters, the Sun will shine fixedly upon only the region of Brahman, then will again take place a great battle between the gods and the Asuras, and in the fight I shall certainly defeat all of you..

sn: शक्र उवाच ब्रह्मणोऽस्मि समादिष्टो न हन्तव्यो भवानिति। तने तेऽहं बले वज्रं न विमुञ्चामि मूर्धनि॥
en: Shakra said Brahman has commanded me, saying that I should never kill you. It is, therefore, O Vali, that I do not hurl my thunderbolt upon your head.

sn: यथेष्टं गच्छ दैत्येन्द्र स्वस्ति तेऽसतु महासुर। आदित्यो नैव तपिता कदाचिन्मध्यत: स्थितः॥
en: Go wherever you like, O king of the Daityas! O great Asuras, peace to you! No time will come when the sun will shine from only the meridian.

sn: स्थापितो ह्यस्य समयः पूर्वमेव स्वयम्भुवा। अजस्रं परियात्येष सत्येनावतपन् प्रजाः॥
en: The self-create has before this ordinated the laws which regulate the Sun's motions. Giving light and heat to all creatures, he shines continually.

sn: अयनं तस्य षण्मासानुत्तरं दक्षिणं तथा। येन संयाति लोकेषु शीतोष्णे विसृजन् रविः॥
en: For six months he travels in a northward course and then for the other six in a southward course. The Sun travels by these courses, creating winter and summer for all creatures.'

sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु दैत्येन्द्रो बलिरिन्द्रेण भारत। जगाम दक्षिणामाशामुदीची तु पुरंदरः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by Indra, O Bharata, Vali the king of the Daityas proceeded towards the south. Purandara proceeded towards the north.

sn: इत्येतद् बलिना गीतमनहंकारसंज्ञितम्। वाक्यं श्रुत्वा सहस्राक्षः खमेवारुरुहे तदा॥
en: After having listened to the wrong of Vali which were marked by no pride, the thousandeyed Indra then ascended the skies.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। शतक्रतोश्च संवादं नमुचेश्च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is also cited the old discourse between him of a hundred sacrifices and the Asura Namuchi,OYudhisthira.

sn: श्रिया विहीनमासीनमक्षोभ्यमिव सागरम्। भवाभवज्ञं भूतानामित्युवाच पुरंदरः॥
en: When the Asura Namuchi, who knew well the birth and the death of all creatures was sitting, shorn of prosperity but undisturbed at heart like the huge ocean in perfect stillness, Purandara addressed him these words-..

sn: नमुचि रुवाच बद्धः पाशैश्चयुतः स्थानाद् द्विषतां वशमागतः। श्रिया विहीनो नमुचे शोचस्याहो न शोचसि॥
en: Namuchi said *Fallen off from your place, fettered with cords, brought under the influence of your enemies, and shorn of prosperity, do you, O Namuchi, grieve or live cheerfully.'

sn: अनिवार्येण शोकेन शरीरं चोपतप्यते। अमित्राश्च प्रहष्यन्ति शोके नास्ति सहायता॥
en: ‘By indulging in such sorrow as cannot be avoided one only wastes his body any cheering his enemies. Then, again, no one can lighten another's sorrow by putting any portion of it upon oneself. For these reasons, O Shakra, I do not grieve. All this that you see has one end.

sn: तस्माच्छक न शोचामि सर्वं ह्येवेदमन्तवत्। संतापाद् भ्रश्यते रूपं संतापाद् भ्रश्यते श्रियः॥
en: Indulgence in sorrow mars personal beauty, prosperity, life, and virtue itself, O king of the gods.

sn: संतापाद भ्रश्यते चायुर्धर्मश्चैव सुरेश्वर। विनीय खलु तद् दुःखमागतं वैमनस्यजम्॥ ध्यातव्यं मनसा हृद्यं कल्याणं संविजानता।
en: Forsooth, suppressing that sorrow which comes upon oneself and which is begotten by a weak mind, one endued with true knowledge should reflect in his mind of that which yields the highest good not which lives in the heart itself.

sn: यदा यदा हि पुरुषः कल्याणे कुरुते मनः। तदा तस्य प्रसिध्यन्ति सर्वार्था नात्र संशयः॥
en: When one sets his mind upon what is for one's highest good, forsooth, the result that all his objects are accomplished.

sn: एकः शास्ता न द्वितीयोऽस्ति शास्ता गर्भे शयानं पुरुषं शास्ति शास्ता। तेनायुयुक्तः प्रवणादिवोदकं यथा नियुक्तोऽस्मि तथा वहामि॥
en: There is One Ordainer, and no second. His sway extends the embryo. Controlled by the great Ordainer I go on as He moves me on, like water running along a downward path.

sn: भवाभवौ त्वभिजानन् गरीयो ज्ञानाच्छ्रेयो न तु करोमि। आशासु धासु परासु कुर्वन् यथा नियुक्तोऽस्मि तथा वहामि॥
en: Knowing what is existence and what liberation, and understanding also that the latter is superior to the former, I do not, however, try to attain to it. Doing virtuous and sinful acts I go on as He moves me on.

sn: यथा यथास्य प्राप्तव्यं प्राप्नोत्येव तथा तथा। भवितव्यं यथा यच्च भवत्येव तथा तथा॥
en: One gets those things that are ordained to be got. That which is to happen actually takes place.

sn: यत्र यत्रैव संयुक्तो धात्रा गर्भे पुनः पुनः। तत्र तत्रैव वसति न यत्र स्वयमिच्छति॥
en: Over even One has repeatedly to live in such wombs in which one is placed by the Ordainer. He has no choice in the matter.

sn: भावो योऽयमनुप्राप्तो भवितव्यमिदं मम। इति यस्य सदा भावो न स मुह्येत् कदाचन॥
en: That person never feels himself stupefied, who when placed in any particular condition, accepts it as that which he was ordained to be placed in.

sn: पर्यायैर्हन्यमानानामभियोक्तो न विद्यते। दुःखमेतत् तु यद् द्वेष्टा कर्ताहमिति मन्यते॥
en: Men are affected by pleasure and pain that come by turns in Time. There is no personal agency in this matter. In this lies sorrow.

sn: ऋषींश्च देवांश्च महासुरांश्च त्रैविद्यवृद्धांश्च वने मुनींश्च। कानापदो नोपनमन्ति लोके परावरज्ञास्तु न सम्भ्रमन्ति॥
en: Who is there amongst Rishis, gods, great Asuras, persons fully conversant with the three Vedas, and hermits living in the forest, whom calamities do not approach? Those, however, who know well, the Soul and not-Soul never fear calamities.

sn: न पण्डितः क्रुद्ध्यति नाभिपद्यते न चापि संसीदति न प्रहष्यति। न चार्थकृच्छ्रव्यसनेषु शोचते स्थितः प्रकृत्या हिमवानिवाचलः॥
en: The wise person, naturally standing immovable like Himavat, never yields to anger; never allows himself to be addicted to the objects of the senses; never suffers pain in sorrow or rejoices in happiness. When overwhelmed with even great afflictions, such a person never grieves.

sn: यमर्थसिद्धिः परमा न मोहयेत् तथैव काले व्यसनं न मोहयेत्। सुखं च दुःखं च तथैव मध्यम निषेवते यः स धुरंधरो नरः॥
en: That person is, indeed, a great man whom even great success cannot gladden and even great calamities cannot stupefy, and who bears pleasure and pain, and that which is between them both, with an unaffected mind.

sn: यां यामवस्थां पुरुषोऽधिगच्छेत् तस्यां रमेतापरितप्यमानः। एवं प्रवृद्धं प्रणुदन्मनोज संतापनीयं सकलं शरीरात्॥
en: A person should always be cheerful and not sorry into whatever condition he may fall, thus should a person remove his increasing sorrow which is born in his mind and that is (if not removed) sure to give pain.

sn: न तत्सदः सत्परिवत् सभा च सा प्राप्य यां न कुरुते सदा भयम्। धर्मतत्त्वमवगाह्य बुद्धिमान् योऽभ्युपैति स धुरंधरः पुमान्॥
en: That concourse of learned men engaged in the discussion of the ethics of both the Shrutis and the Smritis is not a good assembly,-indeed, that does not deserve to be called so,-entering which a wicked man is not stricken with fear. That men is the foremost of his sex, who having made a proper enquiry after righteousness acts according to the conclusions to which he arrives.

sn: प्राज्ञस्य कर्माणि दुरन्वयानि न वै प्राज्ञो मुह्यति मोहकाले। स्तावत् कृच्छ्रामापदं प्राप्य वृद्धः॥
en: The acts of a wise man are not easily understood. A wise man is never stupefied when afflictions overtake him. Even if he falls away from his position like Gautama in his old age, on account of the direst calamity, he does not allow himself to be stupefied.

sn: न मन्त्रबलवीर्येण प्रज्ञया पौरुषेण च। न शीलेन न वृत्तेन तथा नैवार्थसम्पदा। अलभ्यं लभते मर्त्यस्तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: Can a person by Mantras, strength, energy, wisdom, prowess, behaviour, conduct, or wealth, acquire that which has not been ordained to be acquired by him? What sorrow then is there if a person cannot acquire that which he seeks at heart.

sn: यदेवमनुजातस्य धातार विदधुः पुरा। तदेवानुचरिष्यामि किं ते मृत्युः करिष्यति॥
en: Before I was born, the ordainers had ordained that I am to do and suffer. I am fulfilling what was thus ordained for me. What then can death do to me.

sn: लब्धव्यान्येव लभते गन्तव्यान्येव गच्छति। प्राप्तव्यान्येव चाप्नोति दुःखानि च सुखानि च॥
en: One gets only what has been ordained. One goes whence he was ordained to go. Those sorrows and joys only are obtained that are ordained so.

sn: एतद् विदित्वा कात्र्येन यो न मुह्यति मानवः। कुशली सर्वदुःखेषु स वै सर्वधनो नरः॥
en: That man who, knowing this well, does not allow himself to be stupefied, and who is contented with both happiness and misery, is considered as the foremost of his sex.

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मग्नस्य व्यसने कृच्छ्रे किं श्रेयः पुरुषस्य हि। बन्धुनाशे महीपाल राज्यनाशेऽथवा पुनः॥
en: Yudhisthira said What, indeed, is good for a man who is sunk in dire distress, consequent on the loss of friends or kingdom, O king.

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: त्वं हि नः परमो वक्ता लोकेऽस्मिन् भरतर्षभ। एतद् भवन्तं पृच्छामि तन्मे तवं वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: In this world, O foremost of Bharata's race, you are the greatest of our instructors! I ask you this. You should tell me what I ask."

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: भीष्म उवाच पुत्रदारैः सुखैश्चैव वियुक्तस्य धनेन वा। मग्नस्य व्यसने कृच्छ्रे धृतिः श्रेयस्करी नृप॥ धैर्येण युक्तस्य सत: शरीरं न विशीर्यते।
en: 'Fortitude is of the greatest good, O king, for one who has been deprived of sons and wives and pleasures of every sort and wealth, and who has been plunged into dire distress. The body is never emaciated of one who is always endued with fortitude.

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: विशोकता सुखं धत्ते धत्ते चारोग्यमुत्तमम्॥ आरोग्याच्च शरीरस्य स पुनर्विन्दते श्रियम्।
en: Want of sorrow carries happiness with it, and also health which is a superior possession. Again, on account of this health, one may acquire prosperity.

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: यच्च प्राज्ञो नरस्तात सात्त्विकी वृत्तिमास्थितः॥ तस्यैश्वर्यं च धैर्यं च व्यवसायश्च कर्मसु।
en: That wise man, O sire, who always follows righteous conduct succeeds in acquiring prosperity, patience, and perseverance in the accomplishment of all his objects.

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्॥ बलिवासवसंवादं पुनरेव युधिष्ठिर।
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Vali and Vasava,OYudhisthira.

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: वृत्ते देवासुरे युद्धे दैत्यदानवसंक्षये॥ विष्णुक्रान्तेषु लोकेषु देवराजे शतक्रतो।
en: After the battle between the gods and the demons in which a large number of Daityas and Danavas fell, had come to a close, Vali became king. He was deceived by Vishnu who once more established his supremacy over all the worlds. The god of a hundred sacrifices was once more invested with the sovereignty of the celestials.

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: इज्यमानेषु देवेषु चातुर्वर्ण्य व्यवस्थिते॥ समृद्धमात्रे त्रैलोक्ये प्रीतियुक्ते स्वयम्भुवि।
en: After the celestial adininistration had thus been re-established, and the four orders of men had been re-established in performance of their respective duties, the three worlds once inore swelled with prosperty, and the Self-create . became glad of heart.

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: रुद्रैर्वसुभिरादित्यैरश्विभ्यामपि चर्षिभिः॥ गन्धर्वैर्भुजगेन्दैश्च सिद्धैश्चान्यैर्वृतः प्रभुः। चतुर्दन्तं सुदान्तं च वारणेन्द्रं श्रिया वृतम्। आरुरािवतं शक्रस्त्रैलोक्यमनुसंययौ॥
en: At that time, accompanied by the Rudras, the Vasus, the Adityas, the Ashvins, the celestial Rishis, the Gandharvas, the Siddhas, and other superior orders of beings, the powerful Shakra seated on his four-tusked prince of elephants, called Airavata, marched through all the worlds.

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: स कदाचित् समुद्रान्ते कस्मिश्चिद् गिरिगह्वरे। बलिं वैरोचनि वज्री ददर्शोपससर्य च॥
en: One day, while thus engaged, the holder of the thunderbolt was Virochana's son Vali within a certain mountain cave on the seashore. Seeing the king of Danavas, he came near him.

description: What is the good for a man who is the distress for loss of friends of kingdom
sn: तमैरावतमूर्धस्थं प्रेक्ष्य देवगणैर्वृतम्। सुरेन्द्रमिन्द्रं दैत्येन्द्रो न शुशोच न विव्यथे॥
