en: He always tries to conquer all earthly desires by listening to Vedic recitations and attending to the Puranas. He is a great renouncer and he never disrespects any one. For this he is adored everywhere with respect.

description: The conversation between Krishna land Ugrasena about the man who pleases all
sn: समत्वाच्च प्रियो नास्ति नाप्रियश्च कथंचन। मनोऽनुकूलवादी च तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥ बहुश्रुतश्चित्रकथः पण्डितोऽलालसोऽशठः। अदीनोऽक्रोधनोऽलुब्धस्तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥
en: He is endued with great learning in the scriptures. His conversation is varied and charming. His knowledge and wisdom are great. He is free from cupidity. He is free also from deception. He is large-hearted. He has conquered anger and cupidity. For this he is adored everywhere with respect.

description: The conversation between Krishna land Ugrasena about the man who pleases all
sn: नार्थे धने वा कामे वा भूतपूर्वोऽस्य विग्रहः। दोषाश्चास्य समुच्छिन्नास्तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥ दृढभक्तिरनिन्दात्मा श्रुतवाननृशंसवान्।
en: His devotion (to Brahma) is firm. His soul is blameless. He is well-versed in the Shrutis. He is free from cruelty. He is above the influence of delusion or faults. For this he is adored everywhere with respect.

description: The conversation between Krishna land Ugrasena about the man who pleases all
sn: वीतसम्मोहदोषश्च तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥ असक्तः सर्वभूतेषु सक्तात्मेव च लक्ष्यते। अदी संशयो वाग्मी तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥
en: He is unattached to all objects of attachment (for others). For all that he seems to be attached to all things. He does not suffer long from the influence of any doubt. For this he is everywhere adored with respect.

description: The conversation between Krishna land Ugrasena about the man who pleases all
sn: समाधिर्नास्य कामार्थे नात्मानं स्तौति कर्हिचित्। अनीर्घHदुसंवादस्तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥
en: He has no longing for objects of profit and pleasure. He never speaks highly of his own self. He is shorn of malice. He is mild in speech. Therefore he is everywhere adored with respect.

description: The conversation between Krishna land Ugrasena about the man who pleases all
sn: लोकस्य विविधं चित्तं प्रेक्षते चाप्यकुत्सयन्। संसर्गविद्याकुशलस्तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥
en: He sees the hearts, different from one another, of all men, without blaming any of them. He is well-versed in all matters relating to the origin of things.

description: The conversation between Krishna land Ugrasena about the man who pleases all
sn: नासूयत्यागमं कंचित् स्वनयेनोपजीवति। अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥
en: He never disregards or hates any kind of sense. He lives according to his own standard of morality. He never passes time idly. He has controlled his soul. Therefore he is everywhere adored with respect.

description: The conversation between Krishna land Ugrasena about the man who pleases all
sn: कृतश्रमः कृतप्रज्ञो न च तृप्तः समाधितः। नित्ययुक्तोऽप्रमत्तश्च तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥
en: He has worked hard in subjects worthy of hard application. He has acquired knowledge and wisdom. He is never satiate with yoga. He is always attentive and ready for work. He is ever careful. For this he is everywhere adored with respect.

description: The conversation between Krishna land Ugrasena about the man who pleases all
sn: नापत्रपश्च युक्तश्च नियुक्तः श्रेयसे परैः। अभेत्ता परगुह्यानां तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥
en: He does not feel shame for any deficiency of his. He is very attentive. He is always engaged by others for doing what is for their behoof. He never divulges the secrets of others. For this he is everywhere adored with respect.

description: The conversation between Krishna land Ugrasena about the man who pleases all
sn: न हृष्यत्यर्थलाभेषु नालाभे तु व्यथत्यपि। स्थिरबुद्धिरसक्तात्मा तस्मात् सर्वत्र पूजितः॥
en: He is never puffed up with joy at the time of making even valuable acquisitions. He is never pained at losses. His understanding is firm and fixed. His mind is unattached to all things. Therefore he is everywhere adored with respect.

description: The conversation between Krishna land Ugrasena about the man who pleases all
sn: तं सर्वगुणसम्पन्नं दक्षं शुचिमनामयम्। कालज्ञं च प्रियज्ञं च कः प्रियं न करिष्यति॥
en: Who, indeed, is there who will not love him who is thus endued with every merit and accomplishment, who is expert in all things, who is pure in body and mind, who is perfectly auspicious, who is well-versed with the course of time and the opportuneness it affords for particular acts, and who is well-acquainted with all agreeable things?

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आद्यन्तं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञातुमिच्छामि कौरव। ध्यानं कर्म च कालं च तथैवायुर्युगे युगे॥
en: I wish, O Kuru hero, to know what origin and what the end is of all creatures; what the nature of their meditation is and what their acts; what the divisions of time are, and what is the spare of human existence in the respective cycles.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: लोकतत्त्वं च कात्स्येंन भूतानामागतिं गतिम्। सर्गश्च निधनं चैव कुत एतत् प्रवर्तते॥
en: I wish also to know fully the truth about the genesis and the conduct of the world; the you. coming of creatures into the world and their exit. Indeed; whence their creation and destruction?

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: यदि तेऽनुग्रहे बुद्धिरस्मास्विह सतां वर। एतद्भवन्तं पृच्छामि तद् भवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे॥
en: O best of virtuous persons, if you wish to favour us, do tell this about which I ask

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: पूर्वं हि कथितं श्रुत्वा भृगुभाषितमुत्तमम्। भरद्वाजस्य विप्रर्षस्ततो मे बुद्धिरुत्तमा॥ जाता परमधर्मिष्ठा दिव्यसंस्थानसंस्थिता। ततो भूयस्तु पृच्छामि तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Having heard before this the excellent discourse of Bhrigu to the twice-born sage Bharadvaja, which you did recite, my understanding, shorn of ignorance, has become greatly attached to yoga, and withdrawn from worldly objects rests upon heavenly purity. I ask you about the subject, therefore, once more. You should describe it to me fully.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम्। जगौ यद् भगवान् व्यासः पुत्राय परिपृच्छते॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it I shall recite to you an old narrative of what the divine Vyasa said to his son Shuka when the latter had asked the former.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: अधीत्य वेदानखिलान् साङ्गोपनिषदस्तथा। अन्विच्छन्नैष्ठिकं कर्म धर्मनैपुणदर्शनात्॥ कृष्णद्वैपायनं व्यासं पुत्रो वैयासकिः शुकः। पप्रच्छ संदेहमिमं छिन्नधर्मार्थसंशयम्॥
en: Having studied the measureless Vedas with all their branches and the Upanishads, and desirous of leading a life of celibacy on account of his having acquired excellence of religious merit, Shuka put these very questions, about which his doubts had not been removed, to his father Dvipayana, who had removed (by study and contemplation) all doubt regarding true duties.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: श्रीशुक उवाच भूतग्रामस्य कर्तारं कालज्ञाने च निश्चयम्। ब्राह्मणस्य च यत् कृत्यं तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Shuka said You should tell me who the Creator is of all beings, as fixed by a knowledge of time, and what the duties are of a Brahmana!

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: भीष्म उवाच तस्मै प्रोवाच तत् सर्वं पिता पुत्राय पृच्छते। अतीतानागते विद्वान् सर्वज्ञः सर्वधर्मवित्॥
en: Bhishma said The father, having a knowledge of both the past and the future, conversant with all duties and gifted with omniscience, thus described the subject to his son, who had questioned him.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: व्यास उवाच अनाद्यन्तमजं दिव्यमजरं ध्रुवमव्ययम्। अप्रतर्व्यमविज्ञेयं ब्रह्माने सम्प्रवर्तते॥
en: Vyasa said Only Brahma, who is without beginning without end, unborn, effulgent, above decay, immutable, indestructible, inconceivable and transcending knowledge, exists before the Creation.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: काष्ठा निमेषा दश पञ्च चैव त्रिंशत्तु काष्ठा गणयेत् कलां ताम्। त्रिंशत्कलश्चापि भवेन्मुहूर्ता भागः कलाया दशमश्च यः स्यात्॥ त्रिंशन्मुहूर्तं तु भवेदहश्च रात्रिश्च संख्या मुनिभिः प्रणीता। मासः स्मृतो रात्र्यहनी च त्रिंशत् संवत्सरो द्वादशमास उक्तः॥ संवत्सरं द्वे त्वयने वदन्ति संख्याविदो दक्षिणमुत्तरं च॥
en: The Rishis, measuring time, have given particular names to particular portions. Five and ten winks of the eye make what is called a Kashtha: Thirty Kashthas make what is called a Kala. Thirty Kalas, with the tenth part of a Kala, make a Muhurta. Thirty Muhurtas make up one day and night. Thirty days and nights form a month, and twelve months form a year. Persons well-read in mathematical science say that a year is made up of two solar motions. viz., the northern and the southern.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: अहोरात्रे विभजते सूर्यो मानुषलौकिके। रात्रिः स्वमाय भूतानां चेष्टायै कर्मणामहः॥
en: The sun makes the day and the night for men. The night is for the sleep of all living creatures, and the day is for work.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: पित्र्ये रात्र्यहनी मास: प्रविभागस्तयोः पुनः। शुक्लोऽहं कर्मचेष्टायां कृष्णः स्वप्नाय शर्वरी॥
en: A month of human beings is equal to a day and night of the departed manes. That division consists in this: the light half of the month is their day which is for work; and the dark fortnight is their night for sleep.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: दैवे रात्र्यहनी वर्ष प्रविभागस्तयोः पुनः। अहस्तत्रोदगयनं रात्रिः स्याद् दक्षिणायनम्॥
en: A year (of men) is equal to a day and night to the gods. This division consists in this: the half year for which the sun travels from the vernal to the autumnal equinox is the day of the gods, and the half year for which the sun moves from the latter to the former is their night.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: ये ते रात्र्यहनी पूर्व कीर्तिते जीवलौकिके। तयोः संख्याय वर्षाग्रं ब्राह्मे वक्ष्याम्यहःक्षपे॥
en: Calculating by the days and nights of human beings about which I have told you, I shall speak of the day and night of Brahman and his years also.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: पृथक् संवत्सराग्राणि प्रवक्ष्याम्यनुपूर्वशः। कृते त्रेतायुगे चैव द्वापरे च कलौ तथा॥
en: I shall, in their order, tell you the number of years, that are for different purposes calculated differently, in the Krita, the Treta, the Dvapara, and the Kali Yugas.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: चत्वार्याहुः सहस्राणि वर्षाणां तत्कृतं युगम्। तस्य तावच्छती संध्या संध्यांशश्च तथाविधः॥
en: Four thousand celestial years is the duration of the first or Krita age. The morning of that cycle consists of four hundred years and its evening is of four hundred years.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: इतरेषु ससंध्येषु संध्यांशेषु ततस्त्रिषु। एकपादेन हीयन्ते सहस्राणि शतानि च॥
en: Regarding the other cycles, the duration of each gradually decreases by a quarter in respect of both the principal period with the minor portion and the conjoining portion itself.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: एतानि शाश्वताल्लोकान् धारयन्ति सनातनान्। एतद् ब्रह्मविदां तात विदितं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्॥
en: These periods always keep up the neverending and eternal worlds. They who know Brahma, O child, regard this as Immutable Brahma.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: चतुष्पात् सकलो धर्मः सत्यं चैव कृते युगे। नाधर्मेणागमः कश्चित् परस्तस्य प्रवर्तते॥
en: In the Krita age all the duties exist in full, along with Truth. Men of that age never acquired knowledge or object through unrighteous or forbidden means.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: इतरेष्वागपाद् धर्मः पादशस्त्ववरोप्यते। चौर्यकानृतमायाभिरधर्मश्चोपचीयते॥
en: In the other cycles duty, as laid down in the Vedas, is seen to gradually decline by a quarter in each. Sinfulness multiplies by theft, untruth, and deception.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: अरोगाः सर्वसिद्धार्थाश्चतुर्वर्षशतायुषः। कृते त्रेतायुगे त्वेषां पादशो ह्रसते वयः॥
en: In the Krita age, all persons are free from disease and achieve their objects, and all live for four hundred years. In the Treta, the period of life decreases by a quarter.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: वेदवादाश्चानुयुगं ह्रसन्तीतीह नः श्रुतम्। आयूंषि चाशिषश्चैव वेदस्यैव च यत्फलम्॥
en: We have heard that, in the succeeding Yugas, the words of the Vedas, the periods of life, the blessings and the fruits of Vedic rites, all decrease gradually.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: अन्ये कृतयुगे धर्मास्त्रेतायां द्वापरेऽपरे। अन्ये कलियुगे नृणां युगह्रासानुरूपतः॥
en: The duties set down for the Krita Yuga are of one kind. Those for the Treta are otherwise. Those for the Dwapara are different. And those for the Kali are otherwise. This is in accordance with the decline which marks every succeeding cycle.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: तपः परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां ज्ञानमुत्तमम्। द्वापरे यज्ञमेवाहुर्दानमेकं कलौ युगे।॥
en: In the Krita, Penance is the foremost. In the Treta, Knowledge is foremost. In Dvapara, Sacrifice has been said to be the foremost. In the Kali Yuga, only gift is sanctioned.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: एता द्वादशसाहस्री युगाख्यां कवयो विदुः। सहस्रपरिवर्तं तद् ब्राह्यं दिवसमुच्यते॥
en: The learned say that these twelve thousand celestial years from what is celled a cycle. A thousand such cycles form a single day of Brahman.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: रात्रिमेतावतीं चैव तदादौ विश्वमीश्वरः। प्रलये ध्यानमाविश्य सुप्त्वा सोऽन्ते विबुद्ध्यते॥
en: The same is the duration of Brahman's night. With the beginning of Brahman's day the universe begins to come into being. During the period of universal dissolution the Creator sleeps, in Yoga-meditation. When the period of sleep expires, He awakes.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यब्रह्मणो विदुः। रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः॥
en: What is Brahman's day covers a thousand such cycles. His night also covers a thousand similar cycles. They who know this are said to know the day and the night.

description: The origin and end of all creatures
sn: प्रतिबुद्धो विकुरुते ब्रह्माक्षय्यं क्षपाक्षये। सृजते च महद्भूतं तस्माद् व्यक्तात्मकं मनः॥
en: On the expiry of His night, Brahman, waking up modifies the indestructible intelligence by causing it to be overlaid with ignorance. He then causes Consciousness to spring up, whence originates Mind which is at one with the Manifest.

sn: व्यास उवाच ब्रह्म तेजोमयं शुक्रं यस्य सर्वमिदं जगत्। एकस्य ब्रह्मभूतस्य द्वयं स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥
en: Vyasa said Brahma is the effulgent seed from which existing as it does by itself, has originated the entire universe consisting of two kinds of being, viz., the mobile and the immobile,

sn: अहर्मुखे विवुद्धः सन् सृजतेऽविद्यया जगत्। अग्र एव महद्भूतमाशु व्यक्तात्मकं मनः॥
en: At the dawn of His day, waking up, He creates with the aid of Avidya this universe. Mahat or the principle of Greatness at first springs up. That Mahat is speedily changed into Mind which is the soul of the Manifest.

sn: अभिभूयेह चार्चिष्मद् व्यसृजत् सप्त मानसान्। दूरगं बहुधागामि प्रार्थनासंशयात्मकम्॥ मनः सृष्टिं विकुरुते चोद्यमानं सिसृक्षया। आकाशं जायते तस्मात् तस्य शब्दं गुणं विदुः॥
en: Overwhelming the Intelligence, which is effulgent, with Ignorance, Mind creates seven great entities. Urged by the desire of creating, Mind, which is far-reaching, which has many courses, and which had desire and doubt for its leading signs, beings to create various kinds of objects by modifications of itself. Ether first originates from it. Know that its property is Sound.

sn: आकाशात् तु विकुर्वाणात् सर्वगन्धवहः शुचिः। बलवाञ्जायते वायुस्तस्य स्पर्शो गुणो मतः॥
en: From Ether, by modification, originates the bearer of all scents, viz., the pure, and powerful Wind. It is said to possess the property of Touch.

sn: वायोरपि विकुर्वाणाज्ज्योतिर्भवति भास्वरम्। रोचिष्णु जायते शुक्रं तद्रूपगुणमुच्यते॥
en: From Wind also, by modification, originates Light endued with effulgence. Beautiful and called also Shukram, it is thus created, possessing the attribute of Form.

sn: ज्योतिषोऽपि विकुर्वाणाद् भवन्त्यापो रसात्मिकाः। अद्भ्यो गन्धवहा भूमिः सर्वेषां सृष्टिरुच्यते॥
en: From light, by modification, originates Water having taste for its attribute. From Water originates Earth having Scent for its attribute. These are said to represent primary creation.

sn: गुणाः सर्वस्य पूर्वस्य प्राप्नुवन्त्युत्तरोत्तरम्। तेषां यावद् यथा यच्च तत्तत् तावद्गुणं स्मृतम्॥
en: These, in succession, acquire the attributes of the immediately preceding ones from which they have originated. Each has not only its own special attribute but each succeeding one has the attributes of all the previous ones.

sn: उपलभ्याप्सु चेद्गन्धं केचिद् ब्रूयुरनैपुणात्। पृथिव्यामेव तं विद्यादपां वायोश्च संश्रितम्॥
en: If anybody, perceiving Scent in Water, were from ignorance to say that it belongs to Water, he would make a mistake, for Scent is the attribute of Earth though it may exist in Water and also Wind.

sn: एते सप्तविधात्मानो नानावीर्याः पृथक् पृथक्। नाशक्नुवन् प्रजाः स्रष्टुमसमागम्य कृत्स्नशः॥
en: These seven kinds of entities, possessing various kinds of energy, at first existed separately from one another. They could not create objects without all of them acting in a body.

sn: ते समेत्य महात्मानो ह्यन्योन्यमभिसंश्रिताः। शरीराश्रयणं प्राप्तास्ततः पुरुष उच्यते॥
en: All these great entities coming together, and mixing with one another, form the constituent parts of the body which are called limbs.

sn: शरीरं श्रयणाद् भवति मूर्तिमत् षोडशात्मकम्। तमाविशन्ति भूतानि महान्ति सह कर्मणा॥
en: On account of the combination of those limbs,-the sum-total, invested with form and having sixteen constituent parts, becomes what is called the body, (When the gross body is thus forined), the subtile principle of greatness, with the unexhausted remnant of acts, then enters that combination called the gross body.

sn: सर्वभूतान्युपादाय तपसश्चरणाय हि। आदिकर्ता स भूतानां तमेवाहुः प्रजापतिम्॥
en: The original Creator of all beings, then having by His Maya divided Himself, enters that subtile form for overloO king everything. And because he is the original Creator of all beings he is called the lord of all beings.

sn: स वै सृजति भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च। ततः स सृजति ब्रह्मा देवर्षिपितृमानवान्॥ लोकान् नदी: समुद्रांश्च दिशः शैलान् वनस्पतीन्। नरकिन्नररक्षांसि वय:पशुमृगोरगान्।
en: It is he who creates all beings mobile and immobile. After having thus assumed the form the Brahman, he creates the worlds of the gods, the Rishis, the Pitris, and men; the rivers, the Seas and the oceans, the cardinal points, countries and provinces, hills and mountains, and large trees, human beings, Kinnaras, Rakshasas, birds, animals domestic and wild, and snakes.

sn: अव्ययं च व्ययं चैव द्वयं स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥ तेषां ये यानि कर्माणि प्राक्सृष्ट्यां प्रतिपेदिरे। तान्येव प्रतिपाद्यन्ते सृज्यमानाः पुनः पुनः॥ हिंस्राहिंस्र मृदुरे धर्माधर्मावृतानृते। तद्भाविताः प्रपद्यन्ते तस्मात् तत् तस्य रोचते॥
en: He creates both kinds of mobile and immobile; and those that are destructible and those that are indestructible. Of theses created objects each gets those attributes which it had during the previous Creation; and each obtains repeatedly the attributes at every subsequent Creation. Having a formed character by either injuriousness peacefulness, mildness fierceness, righteousness or unrighteousness, truthfulness, or untruthfulness, each creature, at every new creation, gets that particular attribute which it had got before. For this the particular attribute attaches to it. same or or

sn: महाभूतेषु नानात्वमिन्द्रियार्थेषु पूर्तिषु। विनियोगं च भूतानां धातैव विदधात्युत॥
en: It is the Ordained himself who attaches variety to the great entities to the objects of the senses and to size or bulk of existent matter, and settles the relations of creatures with those various entities.

sn: केचित् पुरुषकारं तु प्राहुः कर्मसु मानवाः। दैवमित्यपरे विप्राः स्वभावं भूतचिन्तकाः॥
en: Of men who had devoted themselves to the science of things, there are some who say that, in the production of effects, Exertion is supreme. Some learned persons hold that Destiny is supreme, and some that it is Nature which is the agent.

sn: पौरुषं कर्म दैवं च फलवृत्तिः स्वभावतः। त्रय एतेऽपृथग्भूता न विवेकं तु केचन॥
en: Others hold that Acts flowing from Exertion and Destiny, produce effects, helped by Nature. Instead of considering any of these as alone powerful for the production of effects, they say that it is the union of all three that produces all effects.

sn: एतमेव च नैवं च न चोभे नानुभे न च। कर्मस्था विषयं ब्रूयुः सत्त्वस्थाः समदर्शिनः॥
en: About this subject, some say that such is the case; some, that such is not the case; some, that both of these are not the case; and some that it is not that the reverse of both are not. These, of course, are the contentions of those who depend on Acts, with reference to objects. They, however, whose see the truth consider Brahma as the causes.

sn: तपो निःश्रेयसं जन्तोस्तस्य मूलं शमो दमः। तेन सर्वानवाणोति यान् कामान् मनसेच्छति॥
en: Penance is the greatest good for living creatures. The roots of penance are tranquillity and self-control. By penance one acquires all things that he longs for in his mind.

sn: तपसा तदवाप्नोति यद्भूतं सृजते जगत्। स तद्भूतश्च सर्वेषां भूतानां भवति प्रभुः॥
en: By penance one attains to that Being who creates the universe. He who thus succeeds in attaining to that Being becomes the powerful lord of all beings.

sn: ऋषयस्तपसा वेदानध्यैषन्त दिवानिशम्। अनादिनिधना विद्या वागुत्सृष्टा स्वयम्भुवा।२४॥
en: it is by penance that the Rishis can read the Vedas without interruption. In the beginning the self-create caused those excellent Vedic sounds, that are embodiments of knowledge and that have neither beginning nor end. From those sounds have sprung all sorts of actions.

sn: ऋषीणा नामधेयानि याश्च वेदेषु सृश्यः। नानारूपं च भूतानां कर्मणां च प्रवर्तनम्॥
en: The names of the Rishis, all things that have been created, the varieties of form seen in things, and the course of all actions, have all originated from the Vedas.

sn: वेदशब्देश्य एवादी निर्मिमीते स ईश्वरः। नामधेयानि चर्षीणां याश्च वेदेषु सृश्यः॥
en: Indeed, in the beginning the Supreme Lord of all beings, ceated all things from the words of the Vedas. Truly, the names of the Rishis, and all else that has been created, are seen in the Vedas. Upon the expiration of his night, the Increate Brahman creates, from models that existed before, all things which are, of course, weil-made by Him.

sn: शर्वर्यन्ते सुजातानामान्येभ्यो विदधात्यजः। नामभेदतप:कर्मयज्ञाख्या लोकसिद्धयः॥ आत्मसिद्धिस्तु वेदेषु प्रोच्यते दशभिः क्रमैः।
en: in the Vedas has been described the subject of the Soul's Liberation, along with the ten means formed by study of the Vedas, adoption of the domestic mode of life. penances, observance of all duties, common to all the modes of life, sacrifices, performance of all acts leading to pure fame meditation which is of three kinds, and that kind of Liberation called success (Siddhi) attainable in this life.

sn: यदुक्तं वेदवादेषु गहनं वेददर्शिभिः। तदन्तेषु यथायुक्तं क्रमयोगेन लक्ष्यते॥
en: That incomprehensible Brahma which has been described in the words of the Vedas, and which has been described more clearly in the Upanishads by those who have an insight into the Vedas, can be realised by gradually following the practices referred to above.

sn: कर्मजोऽयं पृथग्भावो द्वन्द्वयुक्तोऽपि देहिनः। तमात्मसिद्धिर्विज्ञानाज्जहाति पुरुषो बलात्॥
en: This consciousness of duality, fraught again with that of pairs opposites, is born only of acts in which he is engaged to a person who thinks he has a body. That person, however, who has attained to Liberation aided by his knowledge, drives off by force that consciousness of duality.

sn: द्वे ब्रह्मणी वेदितव्ये शब्दब्रह्म परं च यत्। शब्दब्रह्मणि निष्णातः परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति॥
en: Two Brahmas should be known viz., the Brahma represented by the Vedas and that which is beyond the Vedas and is supreme. One who is conversant with Brahma represented by sound succeeds in attaining to Brahma that is Supreme.

sn: आलम्भयज्ञाः क्षत्राश्च हविर्यज्ञा विशः स्मृताः। परिचारयज्ञाः शूद्रास्तु तपोयज्ञा द्विजातयः॥
en: The destruction of animals is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Kshatriyas. The growing of corn is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Vaisshyas. Serving the three other orders is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Shudras. Penance is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Brahmanas.

sn: त्रेतायुगे विधिस्त्वेष यज्ञानां न कृते युगे। द्वापरे विप्लवं यान्ति यज्ञाः कलियुगे तथा॥
en: In the Krita age the perforinance of sacrifices was not required. Such performance became necessary in the Treta age. In the Dvapara, sacrifices have begun to fall off. In the Kali, the same is the case with them,

sn: अपृथग्धर्मिणो मा ऋक्सामानि यजूंषि च। काम्या इष्टीः पृथग् दृष्ट्वा तपोभिस्तप एव च।॥
en: In the Krita age, worshipping only one Brahma, men regarded the Richs, the Samans, the Yajushas, and the rites and sacrifices that are performed from motives of advantage, as all different from the object of their worship, and practised only Yoga by means of penances.

sn: त्रेतायां तु समस्ता समस्ता ये प्रादुरासन् महाबलाः। संयन्तारः स्थावराणां जगमानां च सर्वशः॥
en: In the Treta age, many powerful men flourished who governed all mobile and immobile objects.

sn: त्रेतायां संहता वेदा यज्ञा वर्णाश्रमास्तथा। संरोधादायुषस्त्वेते भ्रश्यन्ते द्वापरे युगे॥
en: Accordingly, in that age, the Vedas, and sacrifices, and the distinctions between the several orders, and the four modes of life, existed in a body. On account, however, of the decrease in the period of life in Dvapara, all these, it that age, fall off from that compact condition.

sn: दृश्यन्ते न च दृश्यन्ते वेदाः कलियुगेऽखिला:। उत्सीदन्ते सयज्ञाश्च केवलाधर्मपीडिताः॥
en: In the Kali age, all the Vedas become so scarce that they are not seen by men. Afflicted by iniquity, they become extinct along with the rites and sacrifices laid down in them.

sn: कृते युगे यस्तु धर्मो ब्राह्मणेषु प्रदृश्यते। आत्मवसु तपोवत्सु श्रुतवत्सु प्रतिष्ठितः॥
en: The righteousness which is seen in the Krita age is now seen in such Brahmanas as are of purified souls and as are devoted to penances and the study of the scriptures.

sn: सधर्मव्रतसंयोगं यथाधर्म युगे युगे। विक्रियन्ते स्वधर्मस्था वेदवादा यथागमम्॥
en: As regards the other cycles, it is seen that without at once giving up the duties and acts that are consistent with righteousness, men, observing the practices of their respective orders, and conversant with the ordinances of the Vedas, are led, by the authority of the scriptures, and from motives of advantage and interest to perform sacrifices and vows and sojourns to sacred waters and places.

sn: यथा विश्वानि भूतानि वृष्ट्या भूयांसि प्रावृषि। सृज्यन्ते जङ्गमस्थानि तथा धर्मा युगे युगे॥
en: As in the rainy reason a large variety of new objets of the immobile order are caused to come into being by the showers that fall from the clouds, so many new kinds of duty or religious observances are brought about in each new cycle.

sn: यथर्तुष्वृतुलिङ्गानि नानारूपाणि पर्यये। दृश्यन्ते तानि तान्येव तथा ब्रह्महरादिषु॥
en: As the same phenomena reappear with the reappearance of the seasons, so, at each new Creation of the same attributes appear in each new Brahman and Hara.

sn: विहितं कालनानात्वमनादिनिधनं तथा। कीर्तितं तत्पुरस्तात् ते तत्सूते चात्ति च प्रजाः॥
en: I have, before this, spoken to you of Time which is without beginning and without end, which ordains this variety in the universe. It is that Time which creates and destroys all creatures.

sn: दधाति प्रभवे स्थानं भूतानां संयमो यमः। स्वभावेनैव वर्तन्ते द्वन्द्वयुक्तानि भूरिशः॥
en: All the numberless creatures which exist subject to pairs of opposites and according to their respective natures, have Time for their refuge. It is Time that puts on those forms and it is Time which upholds them.]

sn: सर्गकालक्रिया वेदाः कर्ता कार्य क्रियाफलम्। प्रोक्तं ते पुत्र सर्वं वै यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: I have thus described to you, O son, the topics about which you had asked, viz., Creation, Time, Sacrifices and other rites, the Vedas, the real actor in the universe, action, and the results of action.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: व्यास उवाच प्रत्याहारं तु वक्ष्यामि शर्वर्यादौ गतेऽहनि। यथेदं कुरुतेऽध्यात्म सुसूक्ष्मं विश्वमीश्वरः॥
en: Vyasa said I shall now tell you how, when his day is gone and his night comes, he withdraws ali things to himself, or how the Supreme Master, making this gross universe exceedingly subtile, inerges every thing into his Soul.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: दिवि सूर्यस्तथा सप्त दहन्ति शिखिनोऽर्चिषः। सर्वमेतत् तदार्चिभिः पूर्ण जाज्वल्यते जगत्॥
en: When the time for universal dissolution comes twelve Suns, and Agni with his seven flames, begin to burn. Wrapt by those flames, the entire universe begins to blaze forth in a huge fire.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: पृथिव्यां यानि भूतानि जङ्गमानि ध्रुवाणि च। तान्येवाने प्रलीयन्ते भूमित्वमुपयान्ति च॥
en: All things mobile and immobile that are on the Earth first disappear and merge into the substance of which this planet is formed.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: ततः प्रलीने सर्वस्मिन् स्थावरे जङ्गमे तथा। निर्वृक्षा निस्तृणा भूमिदृश्यते कूर्मपृष्ठवत्॥
en: After all mobile and immobile objects have thus disappeared, the Earth, shorn of trees and herbs, looks nude like a tortoise shell.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: भूमेरपि गुणं गन्धमाप आददते यदा। आत्तगन्धा तदा भूमिः प्रलयत्वाय कल्पते॥
en: Then water takes up the attribute of earth, viz., scent. When earth becomes shorn of its principal attribute, that element is about to be destroyed.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: आपस्तत्र प्रतिष्ठन्ति उर्मिमत्यो महास्वनाः। सर्वमेवेदमापूर्य तिष्ठन्ति च चरन्ति च॥
en: Water then prevails. Surging into big billows and roaring dreadfully only water fills this space and moves about or stands still.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: अपामपि गुणं तात ज्योतिराददते यदा। आपस्तदा त्वात्तगुणा ज्योतिःषूपरमन्ति वै॥
en: Then the attribute of water is taken by Heat, and losing its own attribute, water emerges in that element.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: यदाऽऽदित्यं स्थितं मध्ये गृहन्ति शिखिनोऽर्चिषः। सर्वमेवेदमर्चिभिः पूर्ण जाज्वल्यते नभः॥
en: Dazzling flames of fire, ablaze all around, hide the Sun that is in the centre of ether. Indeed, then, ether itself, full of those flames, burns in a vast fire.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: ज्योतिषोऽपि गुणं रूपं वायुराददते यदा। प्रशाम्यति ततो ज्योतिर्वायुर्दोधूयते महान्॥
en: Then Wind comes and takes the attribute, viz., form, of Heat of Light, which, possessed of great power, begins to be awfully agitated.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: ततस्तु स्वनमासाद्य वायुः सम्भवमात्मनः। अधश्चोर्ध्वं च तिर्यक् च दोधवीति दिशो दश॥
en: Obtaining its own attribute, viz., sound the Wind begins to move upwards and downwards and transversely along all the ten points.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: वायोरपि गुणं स्पर्शमाकाशं ग्रसते यदा। प्रशाम्यति तदा वायुः खं तु तिष्ठति नादवत्॥
en: Then Space takes the attribute, viz., sound, of Wind, upon which the latter is extinguished and enters into a state of existence resembling that of unheard or unuttered sound.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: अरूपमरसस्पर्शमगन्धं न च मूर्तिमत्। सर्वलोकप्रणदितं खं तु तिष्ठति नादवत्॥
en: Then Space is all that remains, that element whose attribute, viz., sound, exists in all the other elements, shorn of the attributes of form, and taste, and touch, and scent, and without shape of any kind, like sound in its unmanifest form of existence.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: आकाशस्य गुणं शब्दमभिव्यक्तात्मकं मनः। मनसो व्यक्तमव्यक्तं ब्राह्मः सम्प्रतिसंचरः॥
en: Then sound, which is the attribute of space, is swallowed up by Mind which is the essence of all manifest things. Thus Mind which in itself is unmanifest withdraws all that is manifested by Mind. This withdrawal of manifest Mind into unmanifest Mind, is called the destruction of the external universe.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: तदात्मगुणमाविश्य मनो ग्रसति चन्द्रमाः। मनस्युपरते चापि चन्द्रमस्युपतिष्ठते॥
en: Then the Moon having made Mind withdraw its attribute into itself, swallows it up. When Mind, ceasing to exist, thus enters into the Moon, the other attributes of Creator are all that remain.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: तं तु कालेन महता संकल्पः कुरुते वशे। चित्तं ग्रसति संकल्पं तच्च ज्ञानमनुत्तमम्॥
en: This Moon which is called also determination, is then, after a very long time, brought under Creator's sway, the reason being that determination has to perform a very difficult work, viz., the destruction of the faculties that are employed in the process of judgement. When this has been done, the condition reached is said to be of high knowledge.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: कालो गिरति विज्ञानं कालं बलमिति श्रुतिः। बलं कालो ग्रसति तु तं विद्वान् कुरुते वशे॥
en: Then time swallows up this Knowledge, and as the Shruti says, Time itself in its turn is devoured by Might or Energy. Might or cnergy, however, is (again) devoured by time, which last is then brought under her sway by kilowledge.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: आकाशस्य यथा घोषं तं विद्वान् कुरुतेऽऽत्मनि। तदव्यक्तं परं ब्रह्म तच्छाश्वतमनुत्तमम्। एवं सर्वाणि भूतानि ब्रह्मैव प्रतिसंचरः॥
en: Possessed of Knowledge, the Creator then swallows up non-existence itself into his Soui. That is Unmanifest and Supreme Brahma. That is Eternal, and that is the Highest of the High. Thus all existent creatures are withdrawn into Brahma.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: यथावत् कीर्तितं सम्यगेवमेतदसंशयम्। बोध्यं विद्यामयं दृष्ट्वा योगिभिः परमात्मभिः॥
en: Truly has this, which should be conceived (with the aid of the scriptures) and which is a topic of Science, been thus said by Yogins endued with Supreme Souls, after actual experience.

description: The night and day of Brahma
sn: एवं विस्तारसंक्षेपौ ब्रह्माव्यक्ते पुनः पुनः। युगसाहस्रयोरादावहोरात्रस्तथैव च॥
en: Even thus does Unmanifest Brahma repeatedly practise the processes of Creation and Destruction, and even thus are Brahman's Day and Night each consisting of a thousand Yugas.

sn: व्यास उवाच भूतग्रामे नियुक्तं यत् तदेतत् कीर्तितं मया। ब्राह्मणस्य तु यत् कृत्यं तत् ते वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु॥
en: Vyasa said-I have described to you fully that which you had asked me about the Creation of all beings. Listen to me as I tell you now what the duties are of a Brahmana.

sn: जातकर्मप्रभृत्यस्य कर्मणां दक्षिणावताम्। क्रिया स्यादासमावृत्तेराचार्ये वेदपारगे॥
en: The rituals of all ceremonies for which sacrificial fees are sanctioned, beginning with birth-rite and ending with Sama-vartana (return from preceptor's house) depend for their performance upon a preceptor well-versed in the Vedas.

sn: अधीत्य वेदानखिलान् गुरुशुश्रूषणे रतः। गुरूणामनृणो भूत्वा समावर्तेत यज्ञवित्॥
en: Having read all the Vedas and having showed submission towards his preceptor while living with him, and having paid the preceptor's fee, the youth should return home with a perfect knowledge of all sacrifices.

sn: आचार्येणाभ्यनुज्ञातश्चतुर्णामेकमाश्रमम्। आविमोक्षाच्छरीरस्य सोऽवतिष्ठेद् यथाविधि॥
en: Obtaining the permission of his preceptor, he should follow one of the four modes of life and live in it duly satisfying its duties till he renounces his body.

sn: प्रजासर्गेण दारैश्च ब्रह्मचर्येण वा पुनः! वने गुरुसकाशे वा यतिधर्मेण वा पुनः॥
en: He should either live like a house-holder with wives and engaged in creating offspring, or live the life of celibacy or in the forest in the company of his preceptor, or follow the duties of a Yati.

sn: गृहस्थस्त्वेष धर्माणां सर्वेषां मूलमुच्यते। यत्र पक्वकषायो हि दान्तः सर्वत्र सिध्यति॥
en: A house-holder's life is said to be the root of all the other modes of life. A self-controlled house-holder who has mastered all his attachments of worldly objects always becomes successful.

sn: प्रजावाश्रोत्रियो यज्वा मुक्त एव ऋणैस्त्रिभिः। अथान्यानाश्रमान् पश्चात् पूतो गच्छेत कर्मभिः॥
en: By procreating children, by gaining a knowledge of the Vedas, and by celebrating sacrifices, a Brahmana satisfies the three debts he owes. He should then enter the other inodes of life, having purified himself by his acts.

sn: यत् पृथिव्यां पुण्यतमं विद्यात् स्थानं तदावसेत्। यतेत तस्मिन् प्रामाण्यं गन्तुं यशसि चोत्तमे॥
en: He should live for good in that place which he may ascertain to be the most sacred spot on earth, and he should try, in all matters leading to fame, for attaining to an eminent position.

sn: तपसा वा सुमहता विद्यानां पारणेन वा। इज्यया वा प्रदानैर्वा विप्राणां वर्धते यशः॥
en: The fame of Brahmanas increases through austere penances, through mastery of the various branches of knowledge, through sacrifices, and through gifts.

sn: यावदस्य भवत्यस्मिन् कीर्तिर्लोके यशस्करी! तावत् पुण्यकृता लोकाननन्तान् पुरुषोऽश्नुते॥
en: Truly, a person enjoys endless regions of the righteous as long as his deeds or the memory thereof exists in this world.

sn: अध्यापयेदधीयीत याजयेत यजेत वा। न वृथा प्रतिगृह्णीयान च दद्यात् कथंचना॥
en: A Brahmana should teach, study, officiate at other people's sacrifices, and offer sacrifices himself. He should not give away uselessly or accept other people's gifts uselessly.

sn: याज्यतः शिष्यतो वापि कन्याया वा धनं महत्। यदाऽऽगच्छेद् यजेद् दद्यान्नकोऽश्नीयात् कथंचन॥
en: Profuse wealth, that may come from one who is assisted in a sacrifice, from a pupil, or from marriage of a daughter, should be spent in the celebration of a sacrifice, or in making gifts. Wealth coming from any of these sources should never be enjoyed by a Brahmana alone.

sn: गृहमावसतो ह्यस्य नान्यत तीर्थं प्रतिग्रहात्। देवर्षिपितृगुर्वर्थं वृद्धातुरबुभुक्षताम्॥
en: For a Brahmana living like a house-holder, there is no means save the acceptance of gifts for the sake of the gods, or the Rishis, or the Pitris, or the preceptor, or the aged, or the diseased, or the hungry.

sn: अन्तर्हिताधितप्तानां यथाशक्ति बुभूषताम्। देवानामतिशक्त्यापि देयमेषा कृतादपि॥
en: One should make gifts from his own siock, including even cooked food, more than he can fairly afford, to those who are persecuted by unseen foes, or those who are trying to the best of their power to acquire Knowledge.

sn: अर्हतामनुरूपाणां नादेय ह्यस्ति किंचन। उचैःश्रवसमप्यश्चं प्रापणीयं सतां विदुः॥
en: There is nothing that cannot be given to a deserving person. The good and the wise deserve to have even the best of horses, called Uchchaishravas, belonging to Indra himself.

sn: अनुनीय यथाकामं सत्यसंधो महाव्रतः। स्वैः प्राणैाह्मणप्राणान् परित्राय दिवं गतः॥
en: Of high vows, Satyasanaha, having, with due humility, offered his own life for saving a Brahmana, ascended to heaven.

sn: रन्तिदेवश्च सांकृत्यो वसिष्ठाय महात्मने। अप: प्रदाय शीतोष्णा नाकपृष्ठे महीयते॥
en: Sankriti's son Rantideva, having given only lukewarm water to the great Vasistha, ascended to heaven and received great honours there.

sn: आत्रेयश्चेन्द्रदमनो ह्यहते विविधं धनम्। दत्त्वा लोकान् ययौ धीमाननन्तान् स महीपतिः॥
en: Aftri's royal and highly intelligent son Indradamana, having given various kinds of wealth to a deserving person, acquired various regions of felicity in the next world,

sn: शिबिरौशीनरोऽङ्गानि सुतं च प्रियमौरसम्। ब्राह्मणार्थमुपाहृत्य नाकपृष्ठमितो गतः॥
en: Ushinara's son Shivi, having given away his own limbs and his dear son for the sake of a Brahmana, ascended to heaven from this world.

sn: प्रतर्दनः काशिपतिः प्रदाय नयने स्वके। ब्राह्मणायातुलां कीर्तिमिह चामुत्र चाश्नुते॥
en: Having given away his very eyes to a Brahmana, Pratarddana, the king of Kasi, enjoyed great fame both here and hereafter.

sn: दिव्यमष्टशलाकं तु सौवर्णं परमर्द्धिमत्। छत्रं देवावृधो दत्त्वा सराष्ट्रोऽभ्यपतद् दिवम्॥
en: Having given away a very beautiful and costly umbrella, with eight golden ribs, King Devavriddha proceeded to heaven with all the denizens of his kingdom.

sn: सांकृतिश्च तथाऽऽत्रेय: शिष्येभ्यो ब्रह्म निर्गुणम्। उपदिश्य महातेजा गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: Having given instruction to his disciples on the subject of Impersonal Brahma, Sanskriti of Atri's race, endued with great energy, proceeded to the regions of great felicity.

sn: अम्बरीषो गवां दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रतापवान्। अर्बुदानि दशैकं च सराष्ट्रोऽभ्यपतद् दिवम्॥
en: Having given to the Brahmanas eleven Arvudas of kine, Amvarisha of great prowess, proceeded to heaven with all the denizens of his kingdom.

sn: सावित्री कुण्डले दिव्ये शरीरं जनमेजयः। ब्राह्मणार्थं परित्यज्य जग्मतुलॊज्ञकमुत्तमम्॥
en: By giving away her ear-rings, Savitri, and, by giving away his own body, king Janamejaya both proceeded to high regions of felicity.

sn: सर्वरत्नं वृषादर्भिर्युवनाश्वः प्रियाः स्त्रियः। रम्यमावसथं चैव दत्वा स्वर्लोकमास्थितः॥
en: By giving away various kinds of gems, a fine palace, and inany beautiful women, Yuvanashva the son of Vrishadabha ascended to heaven.

sn: निमी राष्ट्रं च वैदेहो जामदग्न्यो वसुन्धराम्। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ चापि गयश्चार्वी सपत्तनाम्॥
en: Nimi, the king the Videhas, gave away his kingdom, Jamadagni's son (Rama) gave away the whole Earth; and Gaya gave away the Earth with all her towns and cities, to the Brahmanas.

sn: अवर्षति च पर्जन्ये सर्वभूतानि भूतकृत्। वसिष्ठो जीवयामास प्रजापतिरिव प्रजाः॥
en: Once when the clouds ceased to pour, Vashishtha, resembling Brahman himself, kept alive all creatures like Prajapati (by his power and kindness).

sn: करन्धमस्य पुत्रस्तु कृतात्मा मरुतस्तथा। कन्यामङ्गिरसे दत्त्वा दिवमाशु जगाम ह॥
en: By giving away his daughter to Angiras, Karandha's son Marutta of purified soul, quickly ascended to heaven.

sn: ब्रह्मदत्तश्च पाञ्चाल्यो राजा बुद्धिमतां वरः। निधि शङ्ख द्विजाग्रेभ्यो दत्त्वा लोकानवाप्तवान्॥
en: Brahmadatta, the king of the Panchalas, possessed of great intelligence, by giving away two costly jewels called Nidhi and Shankha to some of the foremost of the Brahmanas, acquired many regions of felicity.

sn: राजा मित्रसहश्चापि वसिष्ठाय महात्मने। मदयन्तीं प्रियां दत्त्वा तया सह दिवं गतः॥
en: Having given his own dear wife Mayadanti to the great Vasistha, King Mitrasaha ascenued to heaven with that wife of his.

sn: सहस्रजिच्च राजर्षिः प्राणानिष्टान् महायशाः। ब्राह्मणार्थं परित्यज्य गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: The royal and highly illustrious sage Shasrajit, having cast off his own dear life for the sake of a Brahmana, ascended to regions of great happiness.

sn: सर्वकामैश्च सम्पूर्णं दत्त्वा वेश्म हिरण्मयम्। मुद्गलाय गतः स्वर्गं शतद्युम्नो महीपतिः॥
en: Having given to Mudgala a golden palace furnished with every object of comfort and use, king shatadyumna ascended to heaven.

sn: नाम्ना च द्युतिमान् नाम शाल्वराजः प्रतापवान्। दत्त्वा राज्यमृचीकाय गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: The king of the Shalvas, named Dyatimat, endued with great prowess gave to Richika his entire kingdom and ascended to heaven.

sn: लोमपादश्च राजर्षिः शान्तां दत्त्वा सुतां प्रभुः। ऋष्य शृङ्गाय विपुलैः सर्वकामैरयुज्यत॥ मदिराश्वश्च राजर्षिर्दत्त्वा कन्यां सुमध्यमाम्। हिरण्यहस्ताय गतो लोकान् देवैरभिष्टुतान्॥
en: By giving away daughter Shanta to Rishyarshringa, the highly powerful royal sage Lomapada obtained the fruition of all his wishes. By giving away his slender waisted daughter of Hiranyahasta, the royal sage Madirashva, ascended to regions esteemed of the very gods.

sn: दत्त्वा शतसहस्रं तु गवां राजा प्रसेनजित्। सवत्सानां महातेजा गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: By giving away a hundred thousand kine with calves, the highly energetic king Prasenajit ascended to excellent regions of happiness.

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो दानेन तपसैव च। महात्मानो गताः स्वर्ग शिष्टात्मानो जितेन्द्रियाः॥
en: These and many others, endued with great and well-ordered souls, and having their senses under control, ascended, by means of gifts and penances, to heaven.

sn: तेषां प्रतिष्ठिता कीर्तिर्यावत् स्थाम्यति मेदिनी। दानयज्ञप्रजासगैरेते हि दिवमाप्नुवन्॥
en: Their fame will last as long as the Earth lierself will exist. All of them have, by gifts and sacrifices and procreation of children proceeded to heaven.

sn: व्यास उवाच त्रयीं विद्यामवेक्षेत वेदेषूक्तामथाङ्गतः। ऋक्सामवर्णाक्षरतो यजुषोऽथर्वणस्तथा॥ तिष्ठत्येतेषु भगवान् षट्सु कर्मसु संस्थितः।
en: Vyasa said The three-fold knowledge which occurs in the Vedas and their branches should be required. That knowledge is to be got from the Richs, the Samans, and the sciences called Varna and Akshara. There are besides, the Yajushas and the Atharvans. The Divine Being lives in the six sorts of acts indicated in these.

sn: वेदवादेषु कुशला ह्यध्यात्मकुशलाश्च ये॥ सत्त्ववन्तो महाभागाः पश्यन्ति प्रभवाप्ययौ।
en: They who are well-read in the injunctions of the Vedas, who have knowledge of the Soul, who are attached to the quality of Goodness, and who are highly blessed, succeed in understanding the origin and the end of all things.

sn: एवं धर्मेण वर्तेत क्रियां शिष्टवदाचरेत्॥ असंरोधेन भूतानां वृत्तिं लिप्सेत वै द्विजः।
en: A Brahmana should follow the duties laid down in the Vedas. He should do all his works like a good man of controlled soul. He should acquire his livelihood without injuring any creature.

sn: सद्भय आगतविज्ञान: शिष्टः शास्त्रविचक्षणः॥ स्वधर्मेण क्रिया लोके कुर्वाणः सत्यसंगरः। तिष्ठते तेषु गृहवान् घट्सु कर्मसु स द्विजः॥
en: Having derived knowledge from the good and wise, he should govern his passions and desires. Well-versed in the scriptures, he should follow those duties which have been laid down for him, and do all works in this world guided by the qualities of goodness. Living even like a house-holder, the Brahmana should perform the six acts already spoken of.

sn: पञ्चभि सततं यज्ञैः श्रद्दधानो यजेत च। धृतिमानप्रमत्तश्च दान्तो धर्मविदात्मवान्॥ वीतहर्षमदक्रोधो ब्राह्मणो नावसीदति।
en: With his heart full of faith, he should adore the deities in the five well-known sacrifices. Possessed of patience, ever vigilant, having self-control, conversant with duties, with a purified soul, divested of joy, pride, and anger, the Brahmana should never sink in langour.

sn: दानमध्ययनं यज्ञस्तपो हीरार्जवं दमः॥ एतैर्वर्धयते तेजः पाप्मानं चापकर्षति।
en: Gifts, study of the Vedas, sacrifices, penances, modesty, guilelessness and selfcontrol,-these increase one's energy and dissipate one's sins.

sn: धूतपाप्मा च मेधावी लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः॥ कामक्रोधौ वशे कृत्वा निनीषेद् ब्रह्मण: पदम्।
en: One gifted with intelligence should be abstemious in diet and should conquer his senses. Indeed, having subdued both lust and anger and having dissipated all his sins, he should try to attain Brahina.

sn: अग्नींश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चार्चेद् देवताः प्रणमेत च॥ वर्जयेदुशती वाचं हिंसां चाधर्मसंहिताम्।
en: He should adore the Fire and Brahmanas, and bow to the gods. He should avoid all sorts of inauspicious talk, and all acts of unrighteous talk, and all acts of unrighteous injury.

sn: एषा पूर्वगता वृत्तिाह्मणस्य विधीयते॥ ज्ञानागमेन कर्माणि कुर्वन् कर्मसु सिध्यति।
en: This preliminary course of conduct is first sanctioned for a Brahmana. Subsequently, when knowledge comes, he should begin work, for success lies in works.

sn: पञ्चेन्द्रियजलां घोरां लोभकूला सुदुस्तराम्॥ मन्युपङ्कामनाधृष्यां नदी तरति बुद्धिमान्।
en: The Brahmana who is gifted with intelligence succeeds in crossing over the river of life that is so difficult to cross and so furious a and terrible, having the five senses for its waters, cupidity for its origin, and anger for its mire.

sn: कालमभ्युद्यतं पश्येन्नित्यमत्यन्तमोहनम्॥ महता विधिदृष्टेन बलेनाप्रतिघातिना।
en: He should never overlook the fact that Time stands behind him in threatening mien,-Time who is the great stupefier of all things, and who is armed with a very great and irresistible force issuing from the great Creator himself.

sn: स्वभावस्रोतसा वृत्तमुह्यते सततं जगत्॥
en: Formed by the current of Nature, the universe is being ceaselessly carried along.

sn: कालोदके महता वर्षावर्तेन संततम्। मासोमिंणर्तुवगेन पक्षोलपतृणेन च॥ निमेषोन्मेषफेनेन अहोरात्रजलेन च। कामग्राहेण घोरेण वेदयज्ञप्लवेन च॥ धर्मद्वीपेन भूतानां चार्थकामजलेन च। ऋतवाङ्मोक्षतीरेण विहिसातरुवाहिना॥ युगह्रदौघमध्येन ब्रह्मप्रायभवेन च। धात्रा सृष्टानि भूतानि कृष्यन्ते यमसादनम्॥
en: The powerful river of Time, overspread with eddies formed by the years, having the months for its waves and the seasons for its current, the fortnights for its floating straw and grass, and the rise and fall of the eyelids for its froth, the days and the nights for its water, and desire and lust for its dreadful crocodiles, the Vedas and sacrifices for its rafts, and the righteousness of creatures for its islands, and Profit and Pleasure for its springs, Truthfulness of Speech and Liberation for its shores, benevolence for the trees floating along it, and the Yugas for the lakes along its course.-the powerful river of Time-which has an origin as inconceivable as that of Brahma itself, is ceaselessly carrying away all beings created by the great Ordainer towards the adobe of Yaina.

sn: एतत् प्रज्ञामयैर्धीरा निस्तरन्ति मनीषिणः। प्लवैरप्लववन्तो हि किं करिष्यन्त्यचेतसः॥
en: Wise and patient persons always succeed in crossing over this dreadful river by engaging the rafts of knowledge and wisdom. What, however, can insensiate fools, destitute of similar rafts, do?

sn: उपपन्नं हि यत् प्राज्ञो निस्तरेन्नेतरो जनः। दूरतो गुणदोषौ हि प्राज्ञः सर्वत्र पश्यति॥
en: It is reasonable that only he that is wise should succeed in crossing this river and not the man of little understanding. The former sees from a distance the merits and faults of everything.

sn: संशयं स तु कामात्मा चलचित्तोऽल्पचेतनः। अप्राज्ञो न तरत्येनं यो ह्यास्ते न स गच्छति॥
en: The man, however, of weak and little understanding, and whose soul is full of desire and cupidity, is always stricken with doubt. Hence, the man shorn of wisdom never succeeds in crossing over that stream. He also who sits inactively, can never cross it over.

sn: अप्लवो हि महादोषं मुह्यमानो नियच्छति। कामग्राहगृहीतस्य ज्ञानमप्यस्य न प्लवः॥
en: The man shorn of the raft of wisdom in consequence of his having to bear the heavy burden of great faults, sinks down. One that is seized by the crocodile of desire, even if endued with knowledge, can never make knowledge his raft.

sn: तस्मादुन्मज्जनस्यार्थे प्रयतेत विचक्षणः। एतदुन्मज्जनं तस्य यदयं ब्राह्मणो भवेत्॥
en: For these reasons the wise and intelligent {}}en should try to float over the stream of Time. He indeed, succeeds in keeping himself afloat who knows Brahma.

sn: अवदातेषु संजातस्त्रिसंदेहस्त्रिकर्मकृत्। तस्मादुन्पज्जने तिष्ठेत् प्रज्ञया निस्तरेद् यथा।॥
en: One born in a noble family, abstaining from the three duties of teaching, officiating at other's sacrifices, and accepting gifts, and doing only the three other acts, viz., studying, Sacrificing, and giving, should, for those reasons, try to float over the river. Such a man is sure to cross it over helped by the raft of wisdom.

sn: संस्कृतस्य हि दान्तस्य नियतस्य यतात्मनः। प्राज्ञस्यानन्तरा सिद्धिरिहलोके परत्र च॥
en: One who is pure in conduct, who is selfcontrolled and observant of good vows, whose soul is under restraint, and who is endued with wisdom, certainly gains success in this and the other world.

sn: वर्तेत तेषु गृहवानक्रुद्ध्यननसूयकः। पजभिः सततं यज्ञैर्विघसाशी यजेत च॥
en: The Brahmana living like a house-holder should conquer anger and envy, practise the virtues already named, and adoring the gods in the five sacrifices, eat after having fed the gods, Pitris, and guests.

sn: सतां धर्मेण वर्तेत क्रियां शिष्टवदाचरेत्। असंरोधेन लोकस्य वृत्तिं लिप्सेदगर्हिताम्॥
en: He should perform those duties which are observed by the good; he should, do all his acts like a self-controlled person and he should without injuring any creature, earn his livelihood by following a course which is not censurable.

sn: श्रुतिविज्ञानतत्त्वज्ञः शिष्टाचारो विचक्षणः। स्वधर्मेण क्रियावांश्च कर्मणा सोऽप्यसंकरः॥ क्रियावाश्रद्दधानो हि दान्तः प्राज्ञोऽनसूयकः। धर्माधर्मविशेषज्ञः सर्वं तरन्ति दुस्तरम्॥
en: One who is well-read in the truths of the Vedas and the other branches of knowledge, whose conduct is like that of a person of wellgoverned soul, who is gifted with a clear vision, who follows the duties of his order, who does not by his acts make an intermixture of duties, who follows the observances laid down in the scriptures, who is endued with wisdom, who is shorn of envy and malice, and who is well conversant with the differences between righteous and iniquity, succeeds in overcoming all his difficulties.

sn: धृतिमानप्रमत्तश्च दान्तो धर्मविदात्मवान्। वीतहर्षमदक्रोधो ब्राह्मणो नावसीदति॥
en: That Brahmana who is gifted with fortitude, who is always careful, who is self-controlled who is conversant with righteousness, whose soul is under restraint, and who has gone over joy, pride, and anger, has never to languish in grief,

sn: एषा पुरातनी वृत्तिर्ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते। ज्ञानवत्त्वेन कर्माणि कुर्वन् सर्वत्र सिध्यति॥
en: This is the course of conduct laid down in days of yore for a Brahmana. He should try to acquire knowledge, and do all the scriptural acts. By living thus, he is sure to acquire Success.

sn: अधर्मं धर्मकामो हि करोति ह्यविचक्षणः। धर्मं वाधर्मसंकाशं शोचत्रिव करोति सः॥
en: One who is not gifted with clear vision, does wrong even when one wishes to do right. By even exercising his judgement, such a person, does such acts of virtue as are wrong.

sn: मधर्मकामश्च करोति धर्मम्। उभे बाल: कर्मणी न प्रजानन् स जायते म्रियते चापि देही॥
en: Desiring to do what is right one does what is wrong. Likewise desiring to do what is wrong, one does what is right. Such a person is a fool. Not knowing the two kinds of acts, one has to go through repeated re-births and deaths.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: व्यास उवाच अथ चेद् रोचयेदेतदुह्येत स्रोतसा यथा। उन्मज्जंश्च निमज्जंश्च ज्ञानवान् प्लववान् भवेत्॥
en: Vyasa said If Liberation is sought for, then knowledge should be acquired. For a person who is carried up and down along the stream of Time or life, Knowledge is the raft by which he can reach the shore.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: प्रज्ञया निश्चिता धीरास्तारयन्त्यबुधान् प्लवैः। नाबुधास्तारयन्त्यन्यानात्मानं वा कथंचन॥
en: Those wise men who have acquired fixed conclusions of the nature of the soul by the help of wisdom, are able of assist the ignorant in crossing the river of time or life with the raft of knowledge. The ignorant, are unable to save either themselves or others.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: छिन्नदोषो मुनिर्योगान् युक्तो युजीत द्वादश। देशकर्मानुरागार्थानुपायापायनिश्चयैः॥ चक्षुराहारसंहारैर्मनसा दर्शनेन च।
en: He who has freed himself from desire and all other faults, and who has freed himself from all attachments, should attend to these twelve requirements of Yoga, viz., place, acts, affection, objects, means, destruction, certainty, eyes, food, suppression, mind and survey.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: यच्छेद् वाङ्मानसी बुद्ध्या इच्छेज्ज्ञानमुत्तमम्॥ ज्ञानेन यच्छेदात्मानं य इच्छेच्छान्तितात्मनः।
en: He who wishes to acquire superior Knowledge, should, by the help of his understanding, restrain both speech and mind. He who wishes to have tranquillity, should, by the help of his knowledge, govern his soul.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: एतेषां चेदनुद्रष्टा पुरुषोऽपि सुदारुणः॥ यदि वा सर्ववेदज्ञो यदि वाप्यनृचो द्विजः। यदि वा धार्मिको यज्वा यदि वा पापकृत्तमः॥ यदि वा पुरुषव्याघ्रो यदि वा क्लेशधारितः। तरत्येवं महादुर्गं जरामरणसागरम्॥
en: Whether he becomes merciful or cruel, whether he becomes conversant with all the Vedas or ignorant of the Richs, whether he becomes pious and observant of sacrifices or the worst of sinners, whether be becomes eminent for power and wealth or sunk into misery, that person who directs his mind towards these, is sure to cross the ocean of life which is so difficult to cross over.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: एवं ह्येतेन योगेन युञ्जानो ह्येवमन्ततः। अपि जिज्ञासमानोऽपि शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते॥
en: Without speaking of the results of the attainment of Brahma by Yoga, it may be said that he who engages himself to only enquire after the Soul rises above the necessity of observing the acts laid down in the Vedas.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: धर्मोपस्थो हीवरूथ उपायापायकूबरः। अपानाक्षः प्राणयुगः प्रज्ञायुर्जीवबन्धनः॥ चेतनाबन्धुरचास्याचारग्रहनेमिनान्। दर्शनस्पर्शनवहो घ्राणश्रवणवाहनः॥ प्रज्ञानाभिः सर्वतन्त्रप्रदोतो ज्ञानसारथिः। क्षेत्रज्ञाधिष्ठितो धीरः श्रद्धादमपुरःसरः॥ त्यागसूक्ष्मानुगः क्षेम्यः शौचगो ध्यानगोचरः। जीवयुक्तो रथो दिव्यो ब्रह्मलोके विराजते॥
en: The body with individual soul within it is an excellent car. When sacrifices and religious rights are made its upastha, shame, its varutha, Upaya and Apaya, its Kuvara, the vital air called Apana, its Aksha, the vital air called Prana, its Yuga, knowledge and the span of existence its points for tieng the horses, carefulness, its Vandhura, the assumption of good conduct, its nemi, vision, touch, scent, and hearing, its four horses, wisdom, its nabhi, all the scriptures, its pratoda, certain knowledge of the scriptural sayings, its driver, the soul, its firinly-seated rider, faith, and self-control, its fore-runners, renunciation, its inseparable companion following behind and bent upon doing it good, purity the path along which it goes, meditaion, its goal, then may that car reach Brahma and shine there effulgently.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: अथ संत्वरमाणस्य रथमेवं युयुक्षतः अक्षरं गन्तुमनसो विधिं वक्ष्यामि शीघ्रगम्॥
en: I shall now tell you the speedy means that should be followed by the person who would get ready his car in such a way for passing through this forest of the world in order to reach the goal formed by Brahma that is above decrepitude and destruction.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: सप्त या धारणाः कृत्स्ना वाग्यतः प्रतिपद्यते। पृष्ठतः पार्वतश्चान्यास्तावत्यस्ताः प्रधारणाः॥
en: To fix the mind upon one thing at a time is called Dharana, following proper vows and restraints, the Yogin practises in all seven kinds of Dharana. There are, again, as many sorts of Dharanas originating out of these, upon subjects which are near or distant.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: क्रमशः पार्थिवं यच्च वायव्यं खं तथा पयः। ज्योतिषो यत् तदैश्वर्यमहङ्कारस्य बुद्धितः। अव्यक्तस्य तथैश्वर्यं क्रमशः प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Through these the Yogin by and by, lords Earth, Wind, Ether, Water, Fire, Consciousness, and Understanding. After this he gradually lords over the Unmanifest.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: विक्रमाश्चापि यस्यैते तथा युक्तेषु योगतः। तथा योगस्य युक्तस्य सिद्धिमात्मनि पश्यतः॥
en: I shall now describe to you the conceptions in their order that are realised by particular individuals amongst those who practise Yoga according to the rules and ordinances sanctioned for them. I shall tell you also of the nature of the success of Yoga undertaken by him who looks within his own self.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: निर्मुच्यमानः सूक्ष्मत्वाद् रूपाणीमानि पश्यतः। शैशिरस्तु यथा धूमः सूक्ष्मः संश्रयते नभः॥
en: The Yogin who casts off his gross body, following the instructions of his preceptor, sees his soul displaying the following forms on account of its subtility. To him, in the first stage, the sky appears to be filled with a subtile substance like fog.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: तथा देहाद् विमुक्तस्य पूर्वं रूपं भवत्युत। अथ धूमस्य विरमे द्वितीयं रूपदर्शनम्॥
en: Such becomes the form of the Soul which has been separated from the body. When this fog disappears, a second form is seen.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: जलरूपमिवाकाशे तथैवात्मनि पश्यति। अपां व्यतिक्रमे चास्य वह्निरूपं प्रकाशते ।१९।।
en: For then the Yogin sees within himself, in the sky of his heart, the form of Water. After the disappearance of water, the form of Fire appears.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: तस्मिन्नुपरतेऽजोऽस्य पीतशस्त्रः प्रकाशते। उर्णारूपसवर्णस्य तस्य रूपं प्रकाशते॥
en: When this disappears, the form that is seen that of Wind as effulgent as a well-tempered and highly polished weapon. Gradually the form shown by Wind becomes like that of the thinnest gossamer.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: अथ श्वेतां गतिं गत्वा वायव्यं सूक्ष्ममप्युत। अशुक्लं चेतसः सौक्ष्यमप्युक्तं ब्राह्मणस्य वै॥
en: Then having gained whiteness, and the subtility of air, the Brahman's soul attains the supreme whiteness and subtilety of Ether.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: एतेष्वपि हि जातेषु फलजातानि मे शृणु। जातस्य पार्थिवैश्वर्यैः सृष्टिरत्र विधीयते॥
en: Listen to me, as I tell you the results of these various conditions when they take place. That Yogin who has been able to conquer the element of Earth, acquires by such mastery the power of Creation.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: प्रजापतिरिवाक्षोभ्यः शरीरात् सृजते प्रजाः। अङ्गुल्यङ्गुष्ठमात्रेण हस्तपादेन वा तथा॥ पृथिवीं कम्पयत्येको गुणो वायोरिति श्रुतिः। आकाशभूतश्चाकाशे सवर्णत्वात् प्रकाशते॥
en: Like a second Prajapati possessed of a nature which knows no disturbances he can, from his own body, create all sorts of creatures. With only his foe, or with his hand or fcet, that person can, alone, make the entire Earth tremble who has conquered the Wind. Even this is the attribute of the Wind as said in the Shruti. The Yogin who has conquered count of his having attained to uniformity with that element, and can also disappear at will.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: वर्णतो गुह्यते चापि कामात् पिबति चाशयान्। न चास्य तेजसा रूपं दृश्यते शाम्यते तथा। अहङ्कारेऽस्य विजिते पञ्चैते स्युर्वशानुगाः॥
en: By mastering over Water, one can drink up rivers, lakes, and oceans. By mastering over Fire, the Yogin becomes so effulgent that his form cannot be spied. He becomes visible only when he puts out the fire within him. When the Yogin succeeds in destroying the consciousness of Ego, these five elements come within his control.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: षण्णामात्मनि बुद्धौ च जितायां प्रभवत्यथ। निर्दोषप्रतिभा ह्येनं कृत्स्ना समभिवर्तते॥
en: When the Understanding, which is the soul of the five elements and of the consciousness of Ego, is conquered, the Yogin acquires Omnipotence, and Omniscience.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: तथैव व्यक्तमात्मानमव्यक्तं प्रतिपद्यते। यतो नि:सरते लोको भवति व्यक्तसंज्ञकः॥
en: For this, the Manifest is fused into the Unmanifest or Supreme Soul from which the world comes into being and becomes what is called Manifest.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: तत्राव्यक्तमयी विद्यां शृणु त्वं विस्तरेण मे। तथा व्यक्तमयं चैव सांख्ये पूर्वं निबोध मे॥
en: Listen now to me fully as I explain the science of Unmanifest. But first of all listen to me about all that is Manifest as explained in the Sankhya system of philosophy.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: पञ्चविंशति तत्त्वानि तुल्यान्युभयतः समम्। योगे सांख्येऽपि च तथा विशेषं तत्र मे शृणु।॥
en: In both the Yoga and the Sankhya systems, twenty-five subjects of knowledge have been treated in nearly the same way. Here me as I describe their chief characteristics.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: प्रोक्तं तद् व्यक्तमित्येव जायते वर्धते च यत्। जीर्यते म्रियते चैव चतुर्भिर्लक्षणैर्युतम्॥३०
en: What is Manifest is possessed of those four attributes, viz., birth, growth, decay and death.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: विपरीतमतो यत् तु तदव्यक्तमुदाहृतम्। द्वावात्मानौ च वेदेषु सिद्धान्तेष्वप्युदाहृतौ॥
en: What does not possess these attributes is said to to be Unmanifest. Two Souls are mentioned in the Vedas and in their auxiliary sciences.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: चतुर्लक्षण त्वाद्यं चतुर्वर्गं प्रचक्षते। व्यक्तमव्यक्तजं चैव तथा बुद्धमथेतरत्।
en: The first is endued with the four attributes already mentioned, and has a longing for the four-fold objects of life. This soul is called Manifest, and it is born of the Unmanifest. It is both Intelligent and non-Intelligent.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: सत्त्वं क्षेत्रज्ञ इत्येतद् द्वयमप्यनुदर्शितम्॥ द्वावात्मानौ च वेदेषु विषयेष्वनुरज्यतः।
en: I have thus told you of Sattva (inert matter) and Kshetrajna (immaterial spirit). Both kinds of Soul, as said in the Vedas, become attached to objects of the senses.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: विषयात् प्रतिसंहारः सांख्यानां सिद्धिलक्षणम्॥ निर्ममश्चानहङ्कारो निर्द्वन्द्वश्छिन्नसंशयः। नैव क्रुद्ध्यति न द्वेष्टि नानृता भाषते गिरः॥ आक्रुष्टस्ताडितश्चैव मैत्रेण ध्याति नाशुभम्। वाग्दण्डकर्ममनसां त्रयाणां च निवर्तकः॥ समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु ब्रह्माणमभिवर्तते। नैवेच्छति न चानिच्छो यात्रामात्रव्यवस्थितः॥ अलोलुपोऽव्यथा दान्तो न कृती न निराकृतीः। नास्ये न्द्रियमनेकाग्रं न विक्षिप्तमनोरथः॥ सर्वभूतसदृड्मैत्रः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः। तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः॥ अस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो ब्रह्मचर्यदृढव्रतः। अहिंस्रः सर्वभूतानामीदृक् सांख्यो विमुच्यते।३९।।
en: The doctrine of the Sankhyas is that one should stand aloof or dissociated from objects of the senses, That Yogin who is freed from attachment and pride, who transcends all pairs of opposites such as pleasure and pain, heat and cold, etc., who never yields to anger or hate, who never speaks an untruth, who though, censured or struck still shows friendship for the slanderer or the striker, who never thinks of injuring others, who restrains these three, viz., speech, acts, and mind, and who treats all creatures equally, succeeds in approaching the presence of Brahman. That person who has no desire for earthly objects, who is not unwilling to take what comes, who is dependent on earthly objects so far as they are required for sustaining life, who is free from cupidity, who has driven off all sorrow, who has controlled his senses, who performs all necessary acts, who does not care for beauty and dress, whose senses are all collected, whose purposes are never left undone, who treats all creatures like friends, who considers equally a clod of earth and a lump of gold, who is equally disposed towards friend and enemy, who is endued with patience, who treats praise and blame equally, who is free from longing for all objects of desire, who practises Brahmacharya, and who is firin and steady in all his vows and observances, who cherishes no malice or envy for any creature in the universe, is a Yogin who according to the Sankhya system succeeds in acquiring Liberation. 27217 yrir fagreint frustrate na

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: योगैश्वर्यमतिक्रान्तो यो निष्कामति मुच्यते॥
en: Hear now of the way and the means by which a person may acquire Liberation through Yoga. That person who moves and acts after having transcended the power that follows the practise of Yoga succeeds in acquiring Liberation.

description: How knowledge is to be acquired
sn: इत्येषा भावजा बुद्धिः कथिता ते न संशयः। एवं भवति निर्द्वन्द्वो ब्रह्माणं चाधिगच्छति॥
en: I have thus described to you those topics, viz., Liberation according to the Yoga system which are dissimilar if the speaker be disposed to treat them as such. Thus can one get over all pairs of opposites. thus can one attain to Brahma.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: व्यास उवाच अथ ज्ञानप्लवं धीरो गृहीत्वा शान्तिमात्मनः! उन्मजंश्च निमश्च ज्ञानमेवाभिसंश्रयेत्॥
en: Vyasa said Carried up and down in life's ocean, he that is capable of meditation catches the raft of Knowledge, and for achieving his Liberation adheres to Knowledge itself.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: शुक उवाच किं तज्ज्ञानमयो विद्या यथा निस्तरते द्वयम्। प्रवृत्तिलक्षणो धर्मो निवृत्तिरिति वा वद॥
en: Shuka said What is that Knowledge? Is it that learning by which, when error is gone, the truth reveals itselt? Or, is it those duties consisting of acts to be done or achieved, by the help of which the object sought for, may be understood or attained? Or, is it those duties, called absention from acts by which an extinction of the Soul is to be sought? Do tell me what it is, so that by its help the two, viz., birth and death, may be avoided.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: व्यास उवाच यस्तु पश्यन् स्वभावेन विनाभावमचेतनः। पुष्यते च पुनः सर्वान् प्रज्ञया मुक्तहेतुकान्॥
en: Vyasa said That fool who, believing that all this exists by its own Nature without, in sooth, an eternal foundation, satisfies by such instruction the aspirations of disciples, defeating by his dialectical ingenuity the reasons the latter might urge to the contrary, succeeds not in acquiring any truth.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: येषां चैकान्तभावेन स्वभावात् कारणं मतम्। पूत्वा तृणमिषीकां वा ते लभन्ते न किंचन॥
en: They again, who firinly believe that all Cause is due to the Nature of things, cannot acquire any truth by even listening to learned 17en or the Rishis.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: ये चैनं पक्षमाश्रित्य निवर्तन्त्यल्पमेधसः। स्वभावं कारणं ज्ञात्वा न श्रेयः प्राप्नुवन्ति ते॥
en: Those little-witted men who stop (in their speculations), having adopted either of these doctrines, those men who regard Nature as the Cause never succeed in acquiring any benefit for themselves.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: स्वभावो हि विनाशाय मोहकर्म मनोभवः। निरुतमेतयोरेतत् स्वभावपरिभावयोः॥
en: This belief in Nature (as the producing and the sustaining Cause), originating as it does from a mind labouring under the influence of error, causes the destruction of the person who cherishes it. Hear of the truth regarding these two doctrines which hold (1) that things exist by their own Nature and (2) that they flow accordingly from others that are different form, and that precede, them.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: कृष्यादीनीह कर्माणि सस्यसंहरणानि च। प्रज्ञावद्भिः प्रक्लृप्तानि यानासनगृहाणि च॥
en: Wise men take to agriculture and tillage, and the acquisition of crops and of vehicles, seats, carpets and houses.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: आक्रीडानां गृहाणां च गदानामगदस्य च। प्रज्ञावन्तः प्रयोक्तारो ज्ञानवद्भिरनुष्ठिताः॥
en: They also look to the laying of pleasuregardens, the construction of spacious palaces and the preparation of medicines for all sorts of diseases.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: प्रज्ञा संयोजयत्यथैः : प्रजा श्रेयोऽधिगच्छति। राजानो भुञ्जते राज्यं प्रज्ञया तुल्यलक्षणाः॥
en: It is wisdom (which consists in the application of means) which brings about the fruition of objects. It is wisdom which gains beneficial results. It is wisdom which enables kings to exercise and enjoy sovereignty although they are endued with attributes equal to those of persons over whom they rule.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: परावरं तु भूतानां ज्ञानेनैवोपलभ्यते। विद्यया तात सृष्टानां विद्यैवेह परा गतिः॥
en: It is by wisdom that the difference is made between the high and the low among beings. It is by wisdom that the superior and the inferior ones among created objects are made out. It is wisdom or knowledge which is greatest refuge of all things.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: भूतानां जन्म सर्वेषां विविधानां चतुर्विधम्। जरायुजाण्डजोद्भिज्जस्वेदजं चोपलक्षयेत्॥
en: All the sorts of created things have four kinds of birth. They are viviparous, oviparous, vegetables, and those born of filth.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: स्थावरेभ्यो विशिष्टानि जङ्गमान्युपधारयेत्। उपपन्नं हि यच्चेष्टा विशिष्येत विशेष्यया॥
en: Mobile creatures should be regarded superior to the immobile. It is reasonable that intelligence which differentiates (all nonintelligent matter), should be considered superior to (non-intelligent) matter.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: आहुः बहुपादानि जङ्गमानि द्वयानि तु। बहुपाट्यो विशिष्टानि द्विपदानि बहून्यपि॥
en: Mobile creatures, whose number is legion, are of two sorts, viz., those that are many legs and those that have two. The latter, however, are superior to the former.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: द्विपदानि द्वयान्याहुः पार्थिवानीतराणि च। पार्थिवानि विशिष्टानि तानि ह्यन्नानि भुञ्जते॥
en: Bipeds, again, are of two sorts, viz., those that live on land and those that are otherwise. Of these, the former are superior to the latter. The superior ones eat various sorts of cooked food.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: पार्थिवानि द्वयान्याहुर्मध्यमान्यधमानि तु। मध्यमानि विशिष्टानि जातिधर्मोपधारणात्॥
en: Bipeds moving on land are of two sorts, viz., middling or intermediate, and those that are foremost. Of these, the middling or intermediate are considered as superior (to the foriner) for their observing the duties of caste.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: मध्यमानि द्वयान्याहुर्धर्मज्ञानीतराणि च। धर्मज्ञानि विशिष्टानि कार्याकार्योपधारणात्॥
en: The middling or intermediate ones are said to be of two sorts, viz., those who are conversant with duties, and those who are otherwise. Of those, the former are superior for they can discriminate between what should be done and what should not.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: धर्मज्ञानि द्वयान्याहुर्वेदज्ञानीतराणि च। वेदज्ञानि विशिष्टानि वेदो ह्येषु प्रतिष्ठितः॥
en: Those conversant with duties are said to be of two sorts, viz., those who are acquainted with the Vedas and those who are otherwise. Of those the former are superior, for the Vedas are said to live in them.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: वेदज्ञानि द्वयान्याहुः प्रवक्तृणीतराणि च। प्रवक्तणि विशिष्टानि सर्वधर्मोपधारणात्॥ विज्ञायन्ते हि यैर्वेदाः सधर्माः सक्रियाफला:। सधर्मा निखिला वेदाः प्रवक्तृभ्यो विनिःसृताः॥
en: Those who are acquainted with the Vedas are said to be of two sorts, viz., those who lecture on the Vedas and those who are otherwise. Of these the former, who are wellread in the Vedas, and are conversant with the duties and the rites laid down in them, and the fruits of those duties and rites, are superior for their declaring all those duties and rites. Indeed, all the Vedas, with the duties laid down in them, are said to emanate from them.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: प्रवक्तृणि द्वयान्याहुरात्मज्ञानीतराणि च। आत्मज्ञानि विशिष्टानि जन्माजन्मोपधारणात्॥
en: Preceptors of the Vedas are of two sorts, viz., those who are conversant with the Self and those that are otherwise. Of these the former are superior on account of their knowledge of Birth and Death.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: धर्मद्वयं हि यो वेद स सर्वज्ञः स सर्ववित्। स त्यागी सत्यसंकल्पः सत्यः शुचिरथेश्वरः॥
en: Duties, again, are of two kinds (viz., Pravritti and Nivritti). He who is conversant with duties is said to be omniscient or endued with universal knowledge. Such a man is a Renouncer. Such a man is firin in the fulfilment of his objects. Such a man is truthful, pure and endued with prowess.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: ब्रह्मज्ञानप्रतिष्ठं हि तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः। शब्दब्रह्मणि निष्णातं परे च कृतनिश्चयम्॥
en: The gods know him as a Brahmana who is devoted to knowledge of Brahma. Such a man is versed also in the Vedas are earnestly given to the study of the Self.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: अन्तःस्थं च बहिष्ठं च साधियज्ञाधिदैवतम्। ज्ञानान्विता हि पश्यन्ति ते देवास्तात ते द्विजाः॥
en: They who have true knowledge see their own self as existing both in and out. Such men, O child, are truly twice-born and such men are gods.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: तेषु विश्वमिदं भूतं सर्वं च जगदाहितम्। तेषां माहात्म्यभावस्य सदृशं नास्ति किंचन।॥
en: This world of beings depends upon these, and in them exist this whole universe. There is nothing equal to their greatness.

description: Knowledge by which birth and death may be avoided
sn: आद्यन्ते निधनं चैव कर्म चातीत्य सर्वशः। चतुर्विधस्य भूतस्य सर्वस्येशाः स्वयम्भुवः॥
en: Transcending birth, and death, and distinctions and all acts, they are the lords of the four kinds of creatures, and are the equals of Self-create himself.

sn: व्यास उवाच एषा पूर्वतरा वृत्तिाह्मणस्य विधीयते। ज्ञानवानेव कर्माणि कुर्वन् सर्वत्र सिध्यति॥
en: Vyasa said These then are the obligatory acts laid down for Brahmanas. One gifted with knowledge, always attains to success by going through (the prescribed acts).

sn: तत्र चेन्न भवेदेवं संशयः कर्मसिद्धये। कि तु कर्म स्वभावोऽयं ज्ञानं कर्मेति वा पुनः॥
en: If no doubt is entertained about acts, then acis done are sure to lead to success. The doubt we speak of is whether acts are obligatory or optional.

sn: तत्र वेदविधिः स स्याज्ञानं चेत् पुरुषं प्रति। उपपत्त्युपलब्धिभ्यां वर्णयिष्यामि तच्छृणु॥
en: About this if acts, are ordained for man for gaining knowledge, they should be considered as obligatory. I shall now describe them by the light of inferences and experience. Here me. some

sn: पौरुषं कारणं केचिदाहुः कर्मसु मानवाः। दैवमेके प्रशंसन्ति स्वभावमपरे जनाः॥
en: Regarding acts men hold that Exertion is their root. Others say that Necessity is their cause. Others, again, hold that Nature is the cause.

sn: पौरुषं कर्म दैवं च कालवृत्तिस्वभावतः। त्रयमेतत् पृथग्भूतमविवेकं तु केचन॥
en: Some hold that acts are the outcome of both Exertion and Necessity. Some hold that acts originate from Time, Exertion, and Nature. Some hold that of the three, one only is the cause. Some hold that all three combined are the cause.

sn: एतदेवं च नैवं च न चोभे नानुभे तथा। कर्मस्था विषयं ब्रूयुः सत्त्वस्थाः समदर्शिनः॥
en: Some persons who perform acts say, with respect to all objects that they exist, that they do not exist, that they cannot be said to exist, that they cannot be said not to exist, that it is not that they cannot be said to exist, and lastly, that it is not that they cannot be said not to exist. These then are the diverse views entertained by men. The Yogins, however, see Brahma as the universal cause.

sn: त्रेतायां द्वापरे चैव कलिजाश्च ससंशया:। तपस्विनः प्रशान्ताश्च सत्त्वस्थाश्च कृते युगे॥
en: The men of the Treta, the Dvapara, and the Kali Yugas, are filled with doubts. The men, however, the Krita Yuga, are given to penances, endued with tranquil souls, and observant of righteousness,

sn: अपृथग्दर्शनाः सर्वे ऋक्सामसु यजुःषु च। कामद्वेषौ पृथक् कृत्वा तपः कृत उपासते॥
en: In that age all men consider the Richs, the Samans, and the Yajushes as Identical, despite their seeming diversity. Analysing desire and hatred, they adore only penance.

sn: तपोधर्मेण संयुक्तस्तपोनित्यः सुसंशितः। तेन सर्वानवाप्नोति कामान् यान् मनसेच्छति॥
en: Given to the practice of penances, firm in them, and rigid in their observance, one acquires the fruition of all desires by penances alone.

sn: तपसा तदवाप्नोति यद् भूत्वा सृजते जगत्। तद् भूतश्च ततः सर्वभूतानां भवति प्रभुः॥
en: By penance one acquires to that portion, by becoming which one creates the universe. By penance one becomes that by which one becomes the powerful master of all things.

sn: तदुक्तं वेदवादेषु गहनं वेददर्शिभिः। वेदान्तेषु पुनर्व्यक्तं कर्मयोगेन लक्ष्यते॥
en: That Brahma has been expounded in the injunctions of the Vedas. For all that, Brahma cannot be conceived by even those who are conversant with those declarations. Once more has Brahma been described in the Vedanta. Brahına, however, cannot be seen by means of acts.

sn: आलम्भयज्ञाः क्षत्राश्च हविर्यज्ञा विशः स्मृताः। परिचारयज्ञाः शूद्राश्च जपयज्ञा द्विजातयः॥
