en: The sacrifices ordained for Brahmanas consist in recitation, that for Kshatriyas consists in the destruction of (clean) animals for the satisfaction of the gods; that for Vaishyas consists in the rearing of crops and the kecp of domestic animals and that for Shudras in menial service of the three other castes.

sn: परिनिष्ठितकार्यो हि स्वाध्यायेन द्विजो भवेत्। कुर्यादन्यन्न वा कुर्यान्मैत्रो ब्राह्मण उच्यते॥
en: By observing the duties sanctioned for him, and by studying the Vedas and other scriptures, one becomes a twice-born one whether one does any other deed or not, he becomes a Brahmana by becoming the friend of all creatures.

sn: त्रेतादौ केवला वेदा यज्ञा वर्णाश्रमास्तथा। संरोधादायुषस्त्वेते व्यस्यन्ते द्वापरे युगे॥
en: In the beginning of Treta, the Vedas and sacrifices and the distribution of caste and the several modes of life existed in full. On account of the duration of life being decreased in Dvapara, those suffer decline.

sn: द्वापरे विप्लवं यान्ति वेदाः कलियुगे तथा। दृश्यन्ते नापि दृश्यन्ते कलेरन्ते पुन: किल॥
en: In Dvapara age as also in the Kali, the Vedas become of doubtful interpretation. Towards the close of Kali again, it is doubtful if they ever can be seen by the eye.

sn: उत्सीदन्ति स्वधर्माश्च तत्राधर्मेण पीडिताः। गवां भूमेश्च ये चापामोषधीनां च ये रसाः॥
en: In that age, the duties of the respective castes disappear, and men become possessed by sin, the juicy attributes of kine, of the earth, of water, and of herbs, disappear.

sn: अधर्मान्तर्हिता वेदा वेदधर्मास्तथाऽऽश्रमाः। विक्रियन्ते स्वधर्मस्थाः स्थावराणि चराणि च॥
en: Through (universal) sin the Vedas disappear, and with them all the duties laid down in them, as also the duties of the four imodes of life. They who follow the duties, of their own order become afflicted, and all mobile and immobile objects suffer a change for the worse.

sn: यथा सर्वाणि भूतानि वृष्टि मानि वर्षति। सृजते सर्वतोऽङ्गानि तथा वेदा युगे युगे॥
en: As the rain from the sky causes all products of the Earth to grow, likewise the Veda develops all its auxilliaries.

sn: निश्चितं कालनानात्वमनादिनिधनं च यत्। कीर्तितं यत् पुरस्तान्मे सूते यच्चात्ति च प्रजाः॥
en: Forsooth, Time assumes various shapes. It has neither beginning nor end. It is Time which creates all creatures and again devours them. I have already spoken of it to you.

sn: यच्चेदं प्रभवः स्थानं भूतानां संयमो. यमः। ' स्वभावेनैव वर्तन्ते द्वन्द्वसृष्टानि भूरिश:॥ सर्गः कालो धृतिर्वेदाः कर्ता कार्य क्रियाफलम्। एतत् ते कथितं तात यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: Time is the origin of all creatures; it is Time which makes them grow; Time is their destroyer; and lastly it is Time which is their ruler. Subject to pairs of opposites, innumerable sorts of creatures rest on Time, according to their own natures.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तोऽभिप्रशस्यैतत् परमर्षस्तु शासनम्। मोक्षधर्मार्थसंयुक्तमिदं प्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by his father, Shuka, highly praising these instructions of the great Rishi, began to ask the following questions regarding the import of duties which brings on Liberation.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: शुक उवाच प्रज्ञावाश्रोत्रियो यज्वा कृतप्रज्ञोऽनसूयकः। अनागतामनैतिचं कथं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति॥
en: Shuka said By what means does a wise man well-read in the Vedas, observant of sacrifices, and shorn of malice attains to Brahma which is incapable of being apprehended by either direct evidence or inference, and incapable of being described by the Vedas.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: तवयस ब्रह्मचर्येण सर्वत्यागेन मेधया। सांख्ये वा यदि वा योग एतत् पृष्टो वदस्व मे॥
en: Asked by me, tell me by what means can Brahma be known. Is it by penance, by Brahmacharya, by renunciation of everything, by intelligence, by help of the Sankhya philosophy, or by the Yoga?

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: मनसश्चेन्द्रियाणां च यथैकाम्यमवाप्यते। येनोपायेन पुरुषैस्तत् त्वं व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: What are the means and what sort of singleness of purpose may inen acquire regarding both, viz., the mind and the senses? You should explain all this to me!

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: व्यास उवाच नान्यत्र विद्यातपसोर्नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात्। नान्यत्र सर्वसंत्यागात् सिद्धिं विन्दति कश्चन॥
en: Vyasa said No man achieves success by any other means save the acquisition of knowledge, the practice of penances, the control of the senses, and renunciation of everything.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: महाभूतानि सर्वाणि पूर्वसृष्टिः स्वयम्भुवः। भूयिष्ठं प्राणभृदग्नामे निविष्टानि शरीरिषु॥
en: The great elements (five in number) represent the first creation of the Self-create. They have been very largely put in embodied creatures living in the world of life.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: भूमेदेहो जलात् स्नेहो ज्योतिषश्चक्षुषी स्मृते। प्राणापानाश्रयो वायु: खेष्वाकाशं शरीरिणाम्॥
en: The bodies of all embodied creatures are originated from earth. Their humours originate from water. Their eyes originate from light. Prana, Apana (and other vital breaths), depend on the wind. And, lastly, all unoccupied apertures within them originate from Space.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: क्रान्ते विष्णुर्बले शक्रः कोष्ठेऽग्निर्भोक्तुमिच्छति। कर्णयोः प्रदिशः श्रोत्रं जिह्वायां वाक् सरस्वती॥
en: Vishnu is in the feet (of living creatures). Indra is in their arms. Within the stomach lies Agni, desirous of eating. The points of the horizon are in the ears, the organ of hearing. Speech, which is the goddess of learning, is in the tongue.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: कर्णी त्वक् चक्षुषी जिह्वार नासिका चैव पञ्चमी। दर्शनीयेन्द्रियोक्तानि द्वाराण्याहारसिद्धये॥
en: The ears, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose forming the fifth, are the senses of knowledge. These exist for apprehending their respective objects.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: शब्दः स्पर्शस्तथा रूपं रसो गन्धश्च पञ्चमः। इन्द्रियार्थान् पृथग्विद्यादिन्द्रियेभ्यस्तु नित्यदा॥
en: Sound, touch, from, taste, and scent for the fifth, are the objects of the (five) senses. These should always be considered as distinct from the senses.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: इन्द्रियाणि मनोयुङ्क्ते वश्यान् यन्तेव वाजिनः। पनश्चापि सदा युङ्क्ते भूतात्मा हृदयाश्रितः॥
en: Like the charioteer driving his well trained horses along the paths he likes, the mind, imoves the senses. The mind, in its turn, is inoved by the Understanding sitting in the heart.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: इन्द्रियाणां तथैवैषां सर्वेषामीश्वरं मनः। नियमे च विसर्गे च भूतात्मा मानसस्तथा॥
en: The mind is the lord of all these senses employing them in their functions and guiding controlling them. Likewise, the Understanding is the lord of the mind.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थाश्च स्वभावश्चेतना मनः। प्राणापानौ च जीवश्च नित्यं देहेषु देहिनाम्॥
en: The senses, the objects of the senses, the attributes of the objects of Nature, understanding, mind, the vital our and individual soul dwell in the bodies of all embodied creatures.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: आश्रयो नास्ति सत्त्वस्य गुणाः शब्दो न चेतना। सत्त्वं हि तेजः सृजति न गुणान् वै कथंचन॥
en: The body within which the Understanding lives, has no real existence. The body, therefore, is not the seat of the Understanding. Nature (Prakriti), endued with three qualities, is the refuge of the Understanding which exists only in the form of a sound. The Soul also is not the refuge of the Understanding. It is Desire which creates the Understanding. Desire, however, never creates the three qualities.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: एवं सप्तदशं देहे वृतं षोडशभिर्गुणैः। मनीषी मनसा विप्रः पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि॥
en: The wise man, capable of controlling his senses, sees the seventeenth, viz., the Soul as surrounded by six and ten qualities, in his own Understanding by the help of the mind.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: न ह्ययं चक्षुषा दृश्यो न च सर्वैरपीन्द्रियैः। मनसा तु प्रदीपेन महानात्मा प्रकाशते॥
en: The Soul cannot be seen with the help of the eye, or with that of all the senses. Getting over all, the Soul can be seen by only the light of the mind's lamp.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: अशब्दस्पर्शरूपं तदरसागन्धमव्ययम्। अशरीरं शरीरेषु निरीक्षेत निरिन्द्रियम्॥
en: Shorn of the properties of sound and touch and form, without taste and smell, indestructible and without a body and without senses, it is nevertheless seen within the body.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: अव्यक्तं सर्वदेहेषु मर्येषु परमाश्रितम्। योऽनुपश्यति स प्रेत्य कल्पते ब्रह्मभूयसे॥
en: Unmanifest and supreme, it lives in all mortal frames, Guided by the preceptor and the Vedas, he who sees it hereafter becomes Brahma's self.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: विद्याभिजनसम्पन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि। शुचि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः॥
en: The wise see impartially a Brahmana gifted with knowledge and disciples, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and a Chandala.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: स हि सर्वेषु भूतेषु जङ्गमेषु ध्रुवेषु च। वसत्येको महानात्मा येन सर्वमिदं ततम्॥
en: Transcending all things, the Soul lives in all creatures, mobile and immobile.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि। यदा पश्यति भूतात्मा ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When a living creature sees his own Soul in all things, and all things in his own Soul, he is said to attain to Brahma.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: यावानात्मनि वेदात्मा तावानात्मा परात्मनि। य एवं सततं वेद सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते॥
en: One occupies the Supreme Soul proportionate to what is occupied in one's own soul by Vedic sound. He who can always realise the identity of all things with his own self, forsooth, acquires immortality.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्य विभोर्भूतहितस्य च। देवाऽपि मार्गे मुह्यन्ति अपदस्य पदैषिणः॥
en: Even the gods are stupefied in the path of that trackless man who forms the soul of all creatures, who is engaged in the well being of all creatures and who wishes to attain to the final refuge (of all things).

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: शकुन्तानामिवाकाशे मत्स्यानामिव चोदके। यथा गतिर्न दृश्येत तथा ज्ञानविदां गतिः॥
en: Indeed, the road which is followed by men of knowledge is as invisible as that of birds in the sky or of fish in water.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: काल: पचति भूतानि सर्वाण्येवात्मनात्मनि। यस्मिस्तु पच्यते कालस्तं वेदेह न कश्चन॥
en: Time, by its own power, cooks all entities within itself. No one, however, knows That in which Time, again, is itself cooked.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: न तदूर्ध्वं न तिर्यक् च नाधो न च पुनः पुनः । न मध्ये प्रतिगृह्णीते नैव किंचित् कुतश्चन॥
en: That does not take place above, or in the middle or below, or in transverse or in any Other direction. That is no tangible thing and cannot be found in any placc.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: सर्वेऽन्तःस्था इमे लोका बाह्ममेषां न किंचन। यद्यजस्रं समागच्छेद् यथा बाणो गुणच्युतः॥ नैवान्तं कारणस्येयाद् यद्यपि स्यान्मनोजवः। तस्मात् सूक्ष्मात् सूक्ष्मतरं नास्ति स्थूलतरं ततः॥
en: All these worlds exists within That. There is nothing in these worlds which exists out of That. Even if one goes on ceaselessly with the motion of arrow shot off the bow-string, even if one goes on with the speed of the mind itself, one would not still get at the end of that which is the cause of all this. There is nothing grosser than that.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत् सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्। सर्वतःश्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति॥
en: His hands and feet are everywhere. His cyes, head, and face are everywhere. His ears are everywhere in the universe. He exists Occupying all things.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: तदेवाणोरणुतरं तन्महद्भ्यो महत्तरम्। तदन्तःसर्वभूतानां ध्रुवं तिष्ठन्न दृश्यते॥
en: That is minuter than the minutest, and is the heart of all things. Though existing, that is still imperceptible.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: अक्षरं च क्षरं चैव द्वैधीभावोऽयमात्मनः। क्षरः सर्वेषु भूतेष दिव्यं तमृतमक्षरम्॥
en: Indestructible and destructible,-these are the dual forms of the (Supreme) Self. The existence it shows in all mobile and immobile entities is destructible; while the existence in shows in Chaitanya is celestial, immortal, and indestructible.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: नवद्वारं पुरं गत्वा हंसो हि नियतो वशी। ईशः सर्वस्य भूतस्य स्थावरस्य चरस्य च॥
en: Though the master of all existent beings both mobile and immobile, though inactive and shorn of attributes, it enters nevertheless the well-known house of nine doors and becomes engaged in action.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: हानिभङ्गविकल्पानां नवानां संचयेन च। शरीराणामजस्याहुहँसत्वं पारदर्शिनः॥
en: Wise men who can see the other shore hold that the Supreme Soul becomes endued with the attribute of action on account of motion, pleasure and pain, variety of form, and the nine well-known possessions.

description: The means by which Brahma can be known
sn: हंसोक्तं चाक्षरं चैव कूटस्थं यत् तदक्षरम्। तद् विद्वानक्षरं प्राप्य जहाति प्राणजन्मनी॥
en: That indestructible Soul which is said to be endued with the attribute or action is nothing else than the indestructible Soul which is said to be inactive. A learned person, by attaining to that indestructible essence, gives up for ever both life and birth.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: व्यास उवाच पृच्छतस्तव सत्पुत्र यथावदिह तत्त्वतः। सांख्यज्ञानेन संयुक्तं यदेतत् कीर्तितं मया॥
en: Vyasa said O excellent son, accosted by you. I have told you truly what the answer to your question should be according to the doctrine of Knowledge as explained in the Sankhya system.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: योगकृत्ये तु ते कृत्स्नं वर्तयिष्यामि तच्छृणु। एकत्वं बुद्धिमनसारिन्द्रियाणां च सर्वशः॥ आत्मनो व्यापिनस्तात ज्ञानमेतदनुत्तमम्। तदेतदुपशान्तेन दान्तेनाध्यात्मशीलिना॥ आत्मारामेण बुद्धेन बोद्धव्यं शुचिकर्मणा। योगदोषान् समुच्छिद्य पञ्च यान् कवयो विदुः॥ कामं क्रोधं च लोभं च भयं स्वप्नं च पञ्चमम्। क्रोधं शमेन जयति कामं संकल्पवर्जनात्॥
en: Listen now to me as I explain to you all that should be done according to the Yoga doctrine. The unison of intellect and Mind, and all the Senses, and the all-prevading Soul is said to be the highest kind of knowledge. That Knowledge should be gained by one who is of a tranquil mind, who has governed his senses, who is capable of seeing the Soul, who takes pleasure in (such) meditation, who is gifted with intelligence and purity in acts. One should try to gain this knowledge by abandoning those five obstacles of Yoga which are known to the wise, namely, desire, anger, cupidity, fear, and sleep. Anger is conquered by tranquility of disposition. Desire is defeated by giving up all purposes.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: सत्त्वसंसेवनाद् धीरो निद्रामुच्छेत्तुमर्हति। धृत्या शिश्नोदरं रक्षेत् पाणिपादं च चक्षुषा॥
en: By meditating with the help of the understanding upon topics deserving meditation one, gifted with patience, succeeds in relinquishing sleep. By steady endurance one should govern his organs of generation and the stomach. One should protect his hands and feet by his eyes.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: चक्षुःश्रोत्रे च मनसा मनोवाचं च कर्मणा। अप्रमादाद् भयं जह्याद् दम्भं प्राज्ञोपसेवनात्॥
en: One should protect his eyes and ears by the help of his mind, and his mind and speech by his acts, One should avoid fear by carefulness, and pride by attending the wise.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: एवमेतान् योगदोषान् जयेन्नित्यमतन्द्रितः। अग्नीश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चार्चेद् देवताः प्रणमेत च॥
en: Controlling procrastination, one should by these means subdue these obstacles of Yoga. One should pay his adorations to fire and the Brahmanas and should bow his head to the gods.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: वर्जयेदुशती वाचं हिंसायुक्तां मनोनुदाम्। ब्रह्म तेजोमयं शुक्रं यस्य सर्वमिदं रसः॥
en: One should avoid all kinds of unholy conversation and malicious speech and words which pain other minds. Brahma is the effulgent seed. It is again, the essence of that seed from which proceeds all this.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: एतस्य भूतं भव्यस्य दृष्टं स्थावरजङ्गमम्। ध्यानमध्ययनं दानं सत्यं हीरार्जवं क्षमा॥ शौचमाचारसंशुद्धिरिन्द्रियाणां च निग्रहः। एतैर्विवर्धते तेजः पाप्मानं चापकर्षति॥
en: Brahma became the eye, in the form of this mobile and immobile universe, of all elements that were born. Meditation, study, gift, truth, modesty, simplicity, forgiveness, purity of body, purity of conduct, and subjugation of the senses, these increase one's energy which dissipates his sins.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: सिध्यन्ति चास्य सर्वार्था विज्ञानं च प्रवर्तते। समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु लब्धालब्धेन वर्तयन्॥
en: By treating impartially all creatures and by living contentedly upon what is gained easily and without exertion one acquires the fruition of all his objects and succeeds in gaining knowledge.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: धूतपाप्मा तु तेजस्वी लध्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः। कामक्रोधौ वशे कृत्वा निनीषेद् ब्रह्मणः पदम्॥
en: Purged of all sins, gifted with energy, sparing in diet, with senses under complete control, one should, after having subdued his desire and anger, try to attain to Brahima.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: मनसश्चेन्द्रियाणां च कृत्वैकाम्यं समाहितः। पूर्वरात्रापरार्धं च धारयेन्मन आत्मनि॥
en: Uniting firmly the senses and the mind with gaze fixed inwards, one should, in the silent hours of evening or those before dawn, fix his mind upon the understanding.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: जन्तोः पञ्चेन्द्रियस्यास्य यदेकं छिद्रमिन्द्रियम्। ततोऽस्य स्रवते प्रज्ञा दृतेः पादादिवोदकम्।१५।।
en: If even one of the five senses of a human being be kept ungoverned all his wisdom escapes through it like water through a hole not made up at the bottom of a leather bag.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: मनस्तु पूर्वमादद्यात् कुमीनमिव मत्स्यहा! ततः श्रोत्रं ततश्चक्षुर्जिह्वां घ्राणं च योगवित्॥
en: The mind in the first instance should be controlled by the Yogin like a fisherman trying at the commencement to make that one among the fish powerless from which he auticipates the greatest danger to his nets. Having first governed the mind, the Yogin should then proceed to subdue his ears, then his tongue, and then his nose.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: तत एतानि संयम्य मनसि स्थापयेद् यतिः। तथैवापोह्य संकल्पान्मनो ह्यात्मनि धारयेत्॥
en: Having controlled these, he should fix there on the mind. Then withdrawing the mind from all purposes. He should settle it on the understanding.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि संधाय मनसि स्थापयेद् यतिः। यदैतान्यवतिष्ठन्ति मनःषष्ठान्यथात्मनि॥ प्रसीदन्ति च संस्थाय तदा ब्रह्म प्रकाशते। विधूम इव दीप्तार्चिरादित्य इव दीप्तिमान्॥
en: Indeed having governed the five senses, the Yati should fix them on the mind. When these with the mind for the sixth become concentrated in the understanding, and thus centred remain steady and firm then Brahma becomes perceptible like a smokeless blazing fire or the effulgent Sun.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: वैद्युतोऽग्निरिवाकाशे दृश्यतेऽऽत्मा तथाऽऽत्मनि। सर्वस्तत्र स सर्वत्र व्यापकत्वाच्च दृश्यते॥
en: Indeed, one then beholds in himself his own soul like lightning in the firmament. Everything then appears in it and it appears in cverything on account of its infinitude.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: तं पश्यन्ति महात्मानो ब्राह्मणा ये मनीषिणः। धृतिमन्तो महाप्राज्ञाः सर्वभूतहिते रताः॥
en: Those great Brahmanas, who are possessed of wisdom, who are endued with fortitude, who are possessed of high knowledge and who are cngaged in the well being of all creatures, succeed in saying it.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: एवं परिमितं कालमाचरन् संशितव्रतः। आसीनो हि रहस्येको गच्छेदक्षरसात्मताम्॥
en: Practising austere vows, the Yogin, who acts thus for six months seated by himself on a lonely spot, becomes at one with the Indestructible.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: प्रमोहो भ्रम आवर्तो प्राणं श्रवणदर्शने। अद्भुतानि रसस्पर्शे शीतोष्णे मारुताकृतिः॥ प्रतिभामुपसर्गाश्चाप्युपसंगृह्य योगतः। तांस्तत्त्वविदनादृत्य आत्मन्येव निवर्तयेत्॥
en: Acquiring by Yoga annihilation, extension, power to present different shapes in the same person or body, celestial scents, and sounds, and sights, the most agreeable sensations of taste and touch, pleasurable sensations of coolness and warmth, equality with the wind, power to understanding the meaning of scriptures and every work of genius, living with celestial damsels, the Yogin should not care for them and merge them all in the Understanding.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: कुर्यात् परिचयं योगे त्रैकाल्ये नियतो मुनिः। गिरि शृङ्गे तथा चैत्ये वृक्षाग्रेषु च योजयेत्॥
en: Restraining words and the senses should practise Yoga after dusk and before dawn seated on a mountain summit, or at the foot of a huge tree or with a tree before him.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्राम कोष्ठे भाण्डमना इव! एकाग्रं चिन्तयेन्नित्यं योगानोद्वेजयेन्मनः॥
en: Controlling all the senses within the heart, one should, with faculties concentrated, think on the Eternal and Indestructible like a man of the world thinking of wealth and other valuable properties. One should never, while practising Yoga, with draw his mind from it. one

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: येनोपायेन शक्येत संनियन्तुं चलं मनः। तं च युक्तो निषेवेत न चैव विचलेत् ततः॥
en: One should with devotion pursue those mcans by which he may control the restive mind. One should never suffer himself to fall away from it.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: शून्या गिरिगुहाश्चैव देवतायतनानि च। शून्यागाराणि चैकाग्रो निवासार्थमुपक्रमेत्॥
en: With the senses and the mind withdrawn from everything else, the Yogin should repair 10 empty caves of mountains, to temples consecrated to the gods and to empty houses or apartiments, for living there.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: नाभिष्वजेत् परं वाचा कर्मणा मनसापि वा। उपेक्षको यताहारो लब्धालब्धे समो भवेत्॥
en: One should not mix with another in either speech, act or thought. Disregarding all things and eating very sparingly the Yogin should regard equally objects acquired or lost.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: यश्चैनमभिनन्देत यश्चैनमपवादयेत्। समस्तयोश्चाप्युभयो भिध्यायेच्छुभाशुभम्॥
en: He should treat equally one who praises and one who censures him. He should not seek the good or the evil of one or the other.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: न प्रहृष्येत लाभेषु नालाभेषु च चिन्तयेत्। समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु सधर्मा मातरिश्वनः॥
en: He should not rejoice at an acquisition or be sorry at a failure or loss. Treating all beings equally he should imitate the wind.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: एवं स्वस्थात्मनः साधोः सर्वत्र समदर्शिनः। षण्मासान्नित्ययुक्तस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते॥
en: Brahma, represented by sound, appcars very clearly unto one whose mind is thus turned to itself, who leads a pure life, and who sees all things equally, indeed unto one who is ever engaged in Yoga thus for even six months.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: वेदनार्ताः प्रज्ञा दृष्ट्वा समलोष्ठाश्मकाञ्चनः। एतस्मिन्विरतो मार्गे विरमेन च मोहितः॥
en: Seeing all men stricken with anxiety the Yogin should regard a clod of earth, a piece of stone, and a lump of gold with an equal eye. Indeed, he should withdraw himself from this path, cherishing a hatred for it, and never allow himself to be stupefied.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: अपि वर्णावकृष्टस्तु नारी वा धर्मकाङ्क्षिणी। तावण्येतेन मार्गेण गच्छेतां परमां गतिम्॥
en: By following the path indicated above, even a person of an inferior caste, or a woman, will surely acquire the highest end.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: अजं पुराणमजरं सनातनं यदिन्द्रियैरुपलभेत निश्चलैः। अणोरणीयो महतो महत्तरं तदात्मना पश्यति मुक्तमात्मवान्।॥
en: He who has subdued his mind sees in his own self, by the help of his own understanding the Increate, Ancient, Undeteriorating, and Eternal Brahma,-That which cannot be attained to except by controlled senses,-That which is subtler than the most subtile, and grosser than the most gross, and which is Emancipation's self.

description: The doctrine of knowledge according the Yoga system
sn: इदं महर्षेर्वचनं महात्मनो यथावदुक्तं मनसानुदृश्य च। अवेक्ष्य चेमां परमेष्ठिसाम्यतां प्रयान्ति चाभूतगतिं मनीषिणः॥
en: Bhishma said By ascertaining from the preceptors and by themselves reflecting with their minds upon these words of the great Rishi spoken so properly wise persons become at one with Brahima himself, till, indeed, the time when the universal dissolution sets in that swallows up all existent beings.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: शुक उवाच यदिदं वेदवचनं कुरु कर्म त्यजेति च। कां दिशं विद्यया यान्ति कां च गच्छन्ति कर्मणाशा ॥
en: Shuka said The injunctions of the Vedas are twofold. They once lay down the command,Do all acts. They again declare renounce acts.-I ask-where do persons go by the help of Knowledge and where by the help of acts.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: एतद् वै श्रोतुमिच्छामि तद् भवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे। एतच्चान्योन्यवरूप्ये वर्तेते प्रतिकूलतः॥
en: I wish to hear this. Do tell me this. Indeed, these injunctions about knowledge and acts are dissimilar and even contradictory.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचेदं पराशरसुतः सुतम्। कर्मविद्यामयावेतौ व्याख्यास्यामि क्षराक्षरौ॥ यां दिशं विद्यया यान्ति यां च गच्छन्ति कर्मणा। शृणुष्वैकमना वत्स गह्वरं ह्येतदन्तरम्॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed, the son of Parasara said to his son,-I shall explain to you the two paths, viz., the destructible and the indestructible, resting respectively upon acts and knowledge. Listen with rapt attention, O child, to me as I point out to you the place which is reached by one with the help of knowledge, and that other place which is reached with the help of acts. The difference between these two places is as great as the endless firmament.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: अस्ति धर्म इति प्रोक्तं नास्तीत्यत्रैव यो वदेत्। तस्य पक्षस्य सदृशमिदं मम भवेद् व्यथा।॥
en: The question which you have asked me has given me such pain as an athestic talk gives to a religious man.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: द्वाविमावथ पन्थानौ यत्र वेदाः प्रतिष्ठिताः। प्रवृत्तिलक्षणो धर्मो निवृत्तौ च सुभाषितः॥ कर्मणा बध्यते जन्तुर्विद्यया तु प्रमुच्यते। तस्मात् कर्म न कुर्वन्ति यतयः पारदर्शिनः॥
en: These are the two paths upon which the Vedas are settled: the duties (Acts) indicated by action and those based on renunciation described so beautifully.By acts a living creature is destroyed. By knowledge, whoever, he becomes free. Therefore, Yogins, who see the other sides of the ocean of life, never perform acts.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: कर्मणा जायते प्रेत्य मूर्तिमान् षोडशात्मकः। विद्यया जायते नित्यमव्यक्तं ह्यव्ययात्मकम्॥
en: Through acts one is compelled to take rebirth, after death which a body composed of the sixteen ingredients. Through knowledge, however, one becomes metamorphosed into that which is Eternal, is Eternal, Unmanifest, and Immutable.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: कर्म त्वेके प्रशंसन्ति स्वल्पबुद्धिरता नराः। तेन ते देहजालानि रमयन्त उपासते॥
en: Little-witted persons speak highly of acts. On account of this they have to assume bodies ceaselessly.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: ये स्म बुद्धिं परां प्राप्ता धर्मनैपुण्यदर्शिनः। न ते कर्म प्रशंसन्ति कूपं नद्यां पिबन्निव॥
en: Those men, who have keen perceptions about duties and who have attained to that high understanding, never speak highly of acts even as persons, who depend for their drinking water upon the supply of streams never speak highly of wells and tanks.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: कर्मणः फलमाप्नोति सुखदुःखे भवाभवौ। विद्यया तदवाप्नोति यत्र गत्वा न शोचति॥ यत्र गत्वा न म्रियते यत्र गत्वा न जायते। न पुनर्जायते यत्र यत्र गत्वा न वर्तते॥ यत्र तद् ब्रह्म परममव्यक्तमचलं ध्रुवम्। अव्याकृतमनायासमव्यक्तं चावियोगि च॥ द्वन्द्वैर्न यत्र बाध्यन्ते मानसेन च कर्मणा। समाः सर्वत्र मैत्राश्च सर्वभूतहिते रताः॥
en: The fruit of acts consist of pleasure and pain, of existence and non-existence. By knowledge one attains to that where there is no occasion for grief; where one becomes freed from both birth and death; where one not subject to decrepitude; where one gets over the state of conscious existence; where is Brahma which is Supreme, Unmanifest, immutable, ever-existent, imperceptible, above the reach of pain, immortal, and transcending destruction; where all become freed from the influence of all pairs of opposites as also of wish or purpose. Raching that stage, they regard everything equally, become universal friends and devoted to the well being of all creatures. There is a huge gulf, O son, between one given to knowledge and one given to acts.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: विद्यामयोऽन्यः पुरुषस्तात कर्ममयोऽपरः। विद्धि चन्द्रमसं दर्शे सूक्ष्मया कलया स्थितम्॥
en: Know that without suffering destruction, the man of knowledge exists for ever like the moon on the last day of the dark fortnight existing in a subtile form.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: तदेतदृषिणा प्रोक्तं विस्तरेणानुमीयते। नवजं शशिनं दृष्ट्वा वक्रतन्तुमिवाम्बरे॥
en: The great Rishi had described this more fully. Regarding the man given to acts his nature may be inferred from seeing the new moon which appears like a bent thread in the sky.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: एकादशविकारात्मा कलासम्भारसम्भृतः। मूर्तिमानिति तं विद्धि तात कर्मगुणात्मकम्॥
en: Know, O son, that the man of acts is born again with a body with eleven elements for its component parts which are the results of modification, and with a subtile form which represents a total of sixteen.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: देवो यः संश्रितस्तस्मिन्नब्बिन्दुरिव पुष्करे। क्षेत्रमं तं विजानीयान्नित्यं योगजितात्मकम्॥
en: The god who resides in that (material) form, like a drop of water on a lotus leaf, should be known as Kshetrajna (Soul) which is Eternal and which gets over by Yoga both the mind and the understanding.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: तमो रजश्च सत्त्वं च विद्धि जीवगुणात्मकम्। जीवमात्मगुणं विद्यादात्मानं परमात्मनः॥
en: Goodness, darkness, and ignorance are the qualities of the Understanding. The understanding is the attribute of the individual soul living within the body. The individual soul, in its turn, emanates froin the Supreme Soul.

description: The injunctions about knowledge and act
sn: सचेतनं जीवगुणं वदन्ति स चेष्टते जीवयते च सर्वम्। ततः परं क्षेत्रविदो वदन्ति प्राकल्पयद् यो भुवनानि सप्त॥
en: The body with the soul is said to be the attribute of individual soul. It is individual soul which acts and causes all bodies to live. He who has created the seven worlds is said by those who are acquainted with what is Kshatra to be above individual soul.

sn: शुक उवाच क्षरात्प्रभृति यः सर्गः सगुणानीन्द्रियाणि च। बुद्ध्यैश्वर्यातिसर्गोऽयं प्रधानश्चात्मनः श्रुतम्॥
en: Shuka said I have now understood that there are two kinds of creation, viz., one universal emanating from the (universal) Soul. The other consisting of the senses with their objects, originates from the power of the Understanding. This last transcends the other and is considered to be the foremost.

sn: भूय एव तु लोकेऽस्मिन् सवृत्तिं कालहैतुकीम्। यया सन्तः प्रवर्तन्ते तदिच्छाम्यनुवर्तितुम्॥
en: I wish however, to once more hear of that path of righteousness which runs in this world, regulated by the virtue of Time and according to which all good men form their conduct.

sn: वेदे वचनमुक्तं तु कुरु कर्म त्यजेति च। कथमेतद् विजानीयां तच्च व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: In the Vedas there are both kinds of saying, do acts and avoid acts. How shall I succeed in determining which of the two is right? You should explain this clearly.

sn: लोकवृत्तान्ततत्त्वज्ञः पूतोऽहं गुरुशासनात्। कृत्वा बुद्धिं विमुक्तात्मा द्रक्ष्याम्यात्मानमव्ययम्॥
en: Having acquired through your instructions, a thorough knowledge of the course of conduct of human beings, having purified myself by the practice of only righteousness, and having cleansed my understanding, I shall, after renouncing my body, see the indestructible Soul.

sn: व्यास उवाच यथा वै विहिता वृत्तिः पुर ताद् ब्रह्मणा स्वयम्। एषा पूर्वतरैः सद्भिराचीर्णा परमर्षिभिः॥
en: The course of conduct that was fist laid down by Brahman himself was duly followed by the wise and pious persons of yore viz., the great Rishis of ancient times.

sn: ब्रह्मचर्येण वै लोकान् जयन्ति परमर्षयः। आत्मनश्च ततः श्रेयांस्यन्विच्छन् मनसाऽऽत्मनि॥ वने मूलफलाशी च तप्यन् सुविपुलं तपः। पुण्यायतनचारी च भूतानामविहिंसकः॥ विधूमे सन्नमुसले वानप्रस्थप्रतिश्रये। काले प्राप्ते चरन् भैक्ष्यं कल्पते ब्रह्मभूयसे॥
en: The great Rishis conquer all the worlds by the practice of celebacy. Seeking all things which are good for himself, by fixing the mind the understanding, practising austerities, by living in forest and lying on fruits and roots, by treading on sacred spots, by practising universal benevolence, and by begging alms at the proper time from the huts of herinits when these become smokeless and the sound of the husking rod is hushed a person attains to Brahma.

sn: नि:स्तुतिनिर्ममस्कारः परित्यज्य शुभाशुभे। अरण्ये विचरैकाकी येन केनचिदाशितः॥
en: Abstaining from flattery and from bowing your head to others, and avoiding both good and evil, live in the forest alone appeasing hunger by any means that presents itself before you.

sn: शुक उवाच यदिदं वेदवचनं लोकवादे विरुध्यते। प्रमाणे वाप्रमाणे च विरुद्ध शास्त्रता कुतः॥
en: The saying of the Vedas are, in the opinion of the ordinary person, contradictory. Whether on severe ! this is authoritative or that is so, when there is this conflict, how can they be considered to be spiritual.

sn: इत्येतच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि प्रमाणं तूभयं कथम्। कर्मणामविरोधेन कथं मोक्षः प्रवर्तते॥
en: I wish to hear this; how can both be considered as authoritative. How indeed, can liberation be obtained without violating the ordinance regarding the obligatory character of acts.

sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचेदं गन्धवत्याः सुतः सुतम्। ऋषिस्तत्पूजयन् वाक्यं पुत्रस्यामिततेजसः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed the son of Gandhavati, viz., the Rishi, praising these words of his highly energetic son, replied to him as follows.

sn: व्यास उवाच ब्रह्मचारी गृहस्थश्च वानप्रस्थोऽथ भिक्षुकः। यथोक्तचारिणः सर्वे गच्छन्ति परमां गतिम्॥
en: Vyasa said One who is a Brahmacharin, one who lives like a house-holder, one who is a herinit and one who lives like a mendicant, all reach the same high end by duly satisfying the duties of their respective modes of life.

sn: एको वाप्याश्रमानेतान् योऽनुतिष्ठेद् यथाविधि। अकामद्वेषसंयुक्तः स परत्र विधीयते॥
en: Or if one, and the same person, shorn of desire and aversion, follows (one after another) all these four modes of life according to the ordinances that have been laid down, he is certainly gratified (by such conduct) to understand Brahma.

sn: चतुष्पदी हि निःश्रेणी ब्रह्मण्येषा प्रतिष्ठिता। एतामारुह्य निःश्रेणी ब्रह्मलोके महीयते॥
en: The four modes of life form a ladder or flight of steps. That fight attaches to Brahma. By ascending that flight one reaches the region of Brahma.

sn: आयुषस्तु चतुर्भागं ब्रह्मचार्यनसूयकः। गुरौ वा गुरुपुत्रे वा वसेद् धर्मार्थकोविदः॥
en: For following the fourth mode of life the Brahmacharya, conversant with the distinctions of duty and shorn of malice, should live with the preceptor or his preceptor's son.

sn: जघन्यशायी पूर्वं स्यादुत्थाय गुरुवेश्मनि। यच्च शिष्येण कर्तव्यं कार्यं दासेन वा पुनः॥ कृतमित्येव तत्सर्वं कृत्वा तिष्ठेत पार्श्वतः। किंकरः सर्वकारी स्यात् सर्वकर्मसु कोविदः॥
en: While living in the preceptor's house, he should seek bed after the preceptor has gone to his and rise therefrom before the preceptor rises from his. He should do all such acts again which a disciple as also a menial servant should do. Doing these he should humbly stand by his preceptor. Skilled in every kind of work, he should act like a menial servant, doing every act for his preceptor.

sn: कर्मातिशेषेण गुरावध्येतव्यं बुभूषता। दक्षिणोऽनपवादी स्यादाहूतो गुरुमाश्रयेत्॥
en: Having performed all acts, he should study, sitting at the feet of his preceptor, with anxious desire to learn. He should always behave with simplicity, avoid evil speech, and take lessons only when his preceptor asks him for it.

sn: शुचिर्दक्षो गुणोपेतो ब्रूयादिष्टमिवान्तरा। चक्षुषा गुरुमव्यग्रो निरीक्षेत जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Becoming pure in body and mind, and acquiring cleverness and other virtues he should now and then speak what is pleasant, Controlling his senses he should look at his preceptor without curiosity.

sn: नाभुक्तवति चाश्नीयादपीतवति नो पिबेत्। नातिष्ठति तथाऽऽसीत नासुप्ते प्रस्वपेत च॥
en: He should never eat before his preceptor has eaten; never drink before his preceptor has drunk; never sit down before is preceptor has sat down; and never go to bed before his preceptor has gone.

sn: उत्तानाभ्यां च पाणिभ्यां पादावस्य मृदु स्पृशेत्। दक्षिणं दक्षिणेनैव सव्यं सव्येन पीडयेत्॥
en: He should gently touch his preceptor's feet with palms, the right foot with the right hand and the left foot with the left.

sn: अभिवाद्य गुरुं ब्रूयादधीष्व भगवन्निति। करिष्ये भगवन्निदं चापि कृतं मया।॥ ब्रह्मस्तदपि कर्तास्मि यद् भवान् वक्ष्यतेपुनः।
en: Reverentially saluting the preceptor, he should say to him:-O illustrious one, teach me! I shall do this, O illustrious one! This ] have already done, O twice born one. I am ready to do whatever else your reverend self may be pleased to command.

sn: इति सर्वमनुज्ञाप्य निवेद्य च यथाविधि॥ कुर्यात कृत्वा च तत्सर्वमाख्येयं गुरवे पुनः।
en: Having said all this, and having duły offered himself (thus), he should perform whatever acts of his preceptor wait for doing and having completed them inform the preceptor once more that they have been done.

sn: यांस्तु गन्धान् रसान् वापि ब्रह्मचारी न सेवते॥ सेवेत तान् समावृत्य इति धर्मेषु निश्चयः।
en: What scents or tastes the Brahmacharin may abstain from while actually leading a life of celebacy may be used by him after his return from the preceptor's house. This is according to the ordinance.

sn: ये केचिद् विस्तरेणोक्ता नियमा ब्रह्मचारिणः॥ तान् सर्वानाचरेन्नित्यं भवेच्चानपगो गुरोः।
en: Whatever observances have been laid down in full for Brahmacharins should all be regularly practised by him. He should all be regularly practised by him. He should be always at the beck and call of his preceptor.

sn: स एवं गुरवे प्रीतिमुपहत्य यथाबलम्॥ आश्रमादाश्रमेष्वेव शिष्यो वर्तेत कर्मणा।
en: Having pleased his preceptor in this way to the best of his powers, the disciple should, from that mode of life, enter into the others and practise the duties of each.

sn: वेदव्रतोपवासेन चतुर्थे चायुषो गते॥ गुरवे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा समावर्तेद्यथाविधि॥
en: Having (thus) spent a fourth part of his life in the study of the Vedas, and observance of vows and fasts, and given the preceptor his fee, the disciple should, according to the ordinance, bidadicu and return home for becoming a house-holder.

sn: धर्मलब्धैर्युतो दारैरग्नीनुत्पाद्य यत्नतः। द्वितीयमायुषो भागं गहमेधी भवेद् व्रती॥
en: Then, having married according to the ordinances, and having carefully established the domestic fire, he should, observing all the Vows and fasts, become a house-holder and pass the second period of life. the disciple should, according to the ordinance, bidadicu and return home for becoming a house-holder.

sn: धर्मलब्धैर्युतो दारैरग्नीनुत्पाद्य यत्नतः। द्वितीयमायुषो भागं गहमेधी भवेद् व्रती॥
en: Then, having married according to the ordinances, and having carefully established the domestic fire, he should, observing all the Vows and fasts, become a house-holder and pass the second period of life.

sn: व्यास उवाच द्वितीयमायुषो भागं गृहमेधी गृहे वसेत्। धर्मलब्धैर्युतो दारैरग्नीनाहृत्य सुव्रतः॥
en: Vayasa said Performing meritorious vows, ihe house holder, for the second period of his life, should live in his house, having married according to the ordinance and having established a fire.

sn: गृहस्थवृत्तयश्चैव चतस्रः कविभि: स्मृताः। कुसूलधान्यः प्रथमः कुम्भधान्यस्त्वनन्तरम्॥
en: Four kinds of conduct have been enunciated by the learned for the domestic mode of life. The first consists of keeping grain in store sufficient to last for three years. The second is of keeping a store to last for one year.

sn: अश्वस्तनोऽथ कापोतीमाश्रितो वृत्तिमाहरेत्। तेषां पर: परो ज्यायान् धर्मतो धर्मजित्तमः॥
en: The thirds is of providing for the day without thinking of the borrow. The fourth consists of collecting grain like a pegion. Of these cach one is superior in merit to its predecessor as has been laid down by the scriptures.

sn: षट्कर्मा वर्तयत्येकस्त्रिभिरन्यः प्रवर्तते। द्वाभ्यामेकश्चतुर्थस्तु ब्रह्मसत्रे व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Observing the first kind of conduct a householder may practise all the six well as known duties. He who observes the second kind of conduct should perform three only of these duties, namely learning, giving and taking. He who follows the third kind of conduct should practise only two of the duties (viz., learning, and giving and taking. He who follows the third kind of conduct should practise only two of duties (viz., learning, and giving). The householder practising the fourth mode of life should observe only one duty (viz., reading the scriptures).

sn: गृहमेधिव्रतान्यत्र महान्तीह प्रचक्षते। नात्मार्थे पाचयेदनं न वृथा घातयेत् पशून्॥
en: The duties of the householder are all considered highly meritorious. The householder should never cook any food only for his own use; nor should lie kill animals (for food) except in sacrifices.

sn: प्राणी वा यदि वाप्राणी संस्कारं यजुषार्हति। न दिवा प्रस्वपेज्जातु न पूर्वापररात्रिषु॥
en: If a householder wishes to slay (for food), or to cut down a tree (for fuel), he should do both the acts according to the ritual laid down in the Yajur for that much is due to both animate and inanimate creation. The householder should never sleep during the day, or in the first or the last part of the night.

sn: न भुञ्जीतान्तरा काले नानृतावाह्वयेत् स्त्रियम्। नास्यानश्नन् गृह विप्रे वसेत् कश्चिदपूजितः॥
en: He should never take two meals between morning and evening, and should never call his wife to bed except in her season. In his house no Brahmana should be allowed to remain unfed or unadorned.

sn: तथास्यातिथयः पूज्या हव्यकव्यवहाः सदा। वेदविद्याव्रतस्नाताः श्रोत्रिया वेदपारगाः॥ स्वधर्मजीविनो दान्ताः क्रियावन्तस्तपस्विनः। तेषां हव्यं च कव्यं चाप्यहणार्थं विधीयते॥
en: He should always adore such guests who present sacrificial offerings, who are cleansed by Vedic learning, who observe excellent vows, who are high-born and conversant with the scriptures, who are self-controlled, mindful of all religious acts, and devoted to penances. The scriptures hold that what is offered to the gods and the departed manes in sacrifices and religious rites, is meant for the service of guests like these.

sn: नखरैः सम्प्रयातस्य स्वधर्मज्ञापकस्य च। अपविद्धाग्निहोत्रस्य गुरोर्वालीककारिणः॥ संविभागोऽत्र भूतानां सर्वेषामेव शिष्यते। तथैवापचमानेभ्यः प्रदेयं गृहमेधिना॥
en: In this mode of life. the scriptures hold that a portion of food, should be given to every creature, to one, who for the sake of show, keeps his nails and beard, to one who from pride shows what his own (religious) practises are, to one who has unduly abandoned his sacred fire, and even to one who has injured his preceptor. A house holder should give (food) to Brahmacharins and Sanyasins.

sn: विघसाशी भवेन्नित्यं नित्यं चामृतभोजनः। अमृतं यज्ञशेषं स्याद् भोजनं हविषा समम्॥ भृत्यशेषं तु योऽश्नाति तमाहुर्विघसाशिनम्।
en: The house-holder, should every day eat Vighasa and ambrosia. Mixed with clarified butter, the remains of the food, which is offered in sacrifices, make ambrosia. That householder who eats after having fed his servants, is said to eat Vighasa. The food, which remains after the servants have been fed, is called Vighasa, and that which is left after the presentation of sacrificial offerings, is called Amrita.

sn: विघसं भृत्यशेषं तु यज्ञशेषमथामृतम्॥ स्वदारनिरतो दान्तो ह्यनसूयुर्जितेन्द्रियः।
en: A householder should be content with his own married wife. He should be selfcontrolled. He should avoid malice and control his senses.

sn: ऋत्विक पुरोहिताचार्यैर्मातुलातिथिसंश्रितैः॥ वृद्धवालातुरैर्वेद्यैातिसम्बन्धिबान्धवैः मातापितृभ्यां जामीभिर्धात्रा पुत्रेण भार्यया॥ दुहित्रा दासवर्गेण विवादं न समाचरेत्।
en: He should never fall out with his sacrificial priest, ordinary, and preceptor, with his maternal uncle and guests and dependants, with the aged and the young, with those who suffer from diseases, with those who practise as physicians, with kinsmen, relatives, and friends, with his parents, with women who belong to his own paternal family, with his brother and son and wife, with his daughter, and with his servants.

sn: एतान् विमुच्य संवादान् सर्वपापैर्विमुच्यते॥ एतैर्जितस्तु जयति सर्वाल्लोकान् न संशयः।
en: By avoiding quarrels with these, the householder becomes purged of all sins. By conquering such disputes, he succeeds in conquering all the blessed regions. There is no doubt in this.

sn: आचार्यो ब्रह्मलोकेशः प्राजापत्ये पिता प्रभुः॥ अतिथिस्त्विन्द्रलोकस्य देवलोकस्य चर्विजः। जामयोऽप्सरसां लोके वैश्वदेवे तु ज्ञातयः॥
en: The preceptor is able to take one to the regions of Brahman. The father can take to the regions of Prajapati. The guest is powerful enough to lead to the region of Indra. The priest has the power to take to the regions of the celestials. Female relatives on the father's side have power over the regions of the Apsaras, and blood relatives over the regions of the Vishvedevas.

sn: सम्बन्धिबान्धवा दिक्षु पृथिव्यां मातृमातुलौ। वृद्धवालातुरकृशास्त्वाकाशे प्रभविष्णवः॥
en: Relation by marriage and collateral kinsmen have power over the several quarters of the horizon (viz., north, etc.) and the mother and the maternal uncle have power over the Earth. The old, the young, the afflicted, the worn out have power over the firmament.

sn: भ्राता ज्येष्ठः समः पित्रा भार्या पुत्रः स्वका तनुः। छाया स्वा दासवर्गश्च दुहिता कृपणं परम्॥
en: The eldest brother is like a father to all his younger brother). The wife and the son are one's own body. One's menial servants are his shadow. The daughter is an object of great love.

sn: तस्मादेतैरधिक्षिप्तः सहेन्नित्यमसंज्वरः। गृहधर्मपरो विद्वान् धर्मशीलो जितक्लमः॥
en: Therefore a householder, gifted with learning, observant of duties and endued with endurance, should hear without excitement or anxiety every sort of annoyance and even censure from the last-named relatives.

sn: न चार्थबद्धः कर्माणि धर्मवान् कश्चिदाचरेत्। गृहस्थवृत्तयस्तिस्रस्तासां निःश्रेयसं परम्॥
en: No pious householder should do any act, out of consideration for money. There are three courses of duly attached to the domestic mode of a life. Of these every succeeding one is more meritorious than the preceding one.

sn: परं परं तथैवाहुश्चातुराश्रम्यमेव तत्। यथोक्ता नियमास्तेषां सर्वं कार्यं बुभूषता॥
en: The same rule of merit holds good regarding the four modes of life also viz., every succeeding one is superior to the one preceding it.

sn: कुम्भधान्यैरुञ्छशिलैः कापोतीं चास्थितास्तथा। यस्मिश्चैते वसन्त्यहीस्तद् राष्ट्रमभिवर्धते॥
en: That kingdom becomes prosperous where these highly deserving persons dwell viz., those who live like householders according to the Kumbhadhanya method, they who live according to the Uncha method, and they who live according to the Kapoti method.

sn: पूर्वान् दश दश परान् पुनाति च पितामहान्। गृहस्थवृत्तीश्चाप्येता वर्तयेद् यो गतव्यथः॥
en: That man, who cheerfully lives like a householder, observing those duties, succeeds in sanctifying ten generations of his ancestors above and ten generations below.

sn: स चक्रधरलोकानां सदृशीमाप्नुयाद् गतिम्। जितेन्द्रियाणामथवा गतिरेषा विधीयते॥
en: A householder, duly observing the duties of domestic life, acquires what gives in the end happiness, equal to what takes place in the regions attained by great kings and emperors. Even such is the end of those who have controlled their senses.

sn: स्वर्गलोको गृहस्थानामुदारमनसां हितः। स्वर्गो विमानसंयुक्तो वेददृष्टः सुपुष्पितः॥
en: Heaven has been ordained for all great householders. That heaven is filled with charming cars for each. Even that is the charming heaven described in the Vedas.

sn: स्वर्गलोको गृहस्थानां प्रतिष्ठा नियतात्मनाम्। ब्रह्मणा विहिता योनिरेषा यस्माद् विधीयते। द्वितीयं क्रमशः प्राप्य स्वर्गलोके महीयते॥
en: The regions of heaven form the high mead for all householders of controlled minds. The Self-born Brahma ordained that the domestic life, should secure heaven, and since it has been so ordained, a person, by gradually following the second mode of life, obtains happiness in heaven.

sn: अतः परं परममुदारमाश्रम तृतीयमाहुस्त्यजतां कलेवरम्। वनौकसां गृहपतिनामनुत्तमं शृणुष्व संश्लिष्टशरीरकारिणाम्॥
en: After this comes that high and superior mode of life, called the third, for those that are desirous of renouncing their bodies. Superior to that of householders is the life of hermits,-who reduce their bodies into skeletons overlaid with dried skins. Listen as I describe to this subject to you further more.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: भीष्म उवाच प्रोक्ता गृहस्थवृत्तिस्ते विहिता या मनीषिभिः। तदनन्तरमुक्तं यत् तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said You have been told what the duties of a householders are as ordained by the wise. Listen now, O Yudhisthira, to the next class of duties.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: क्रमशस्त्ववधूयैनां तृतीयां वृत्तिमुत्तमाम्। संयोगव्रतखिन्नानां वानप्रस्थाश्रमौकसाम्॥
en: Gradually leading off the domestic mode, one should enter the third mode which is good. It is the mode which is followed by persons who living with their wives pain themselves by means of austerities. It is the mode followed by those who live in forest as hermits.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: श्रूयतां पुत्र भद्रं ते सर्वलोकाश्रमात्मनाम्। प्रेक्षापूर्वं प्रवृत्तानां पुण्यदेशनिवासिनाम्॥
en: Blessed be you, O son, listen to the duties observed by those who follow this mode of life in which are set forth the practices of all men and all modes of life. Listen, indeed, to the duties of those who live in sacred spots and who have adopted this mode after proper consideration.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: व्यास उवाच गृहस्थस्तु यदा पश्येद् वलीपलितमात्मनः। अपत्यस्यैव चापत्यं वनमेव तदा श्रयेत्॥
en: Vyasa said When the householder sees his body wrinkled and hair white on his head, and children of his children, he should then retire into the forest.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: तृतीयमायुषो भागं वानप्रस्थाश्रमे वसेत्। तानेवाग्नीन् परिचरेद् यजमानो दिवौकसः॥
en: He should pass the third portion of his life as Vanaprastha. He should worship those sacred fires to which he had attended while a householder. Desirous of performing sacrifices, he should also worship the gods.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: नियतो नियताहारः षष्ठभुक्तोऽप्रमत्तवान्। तदग्निहोत्रं ता गावो यज्ञाङ्गानि च सर्वशः॥
en: Observing vows and being sparing in diet, he should eat only once, during the sixth part of the day. He should be always careful. Adoring his fires, he should keep some kine, serving them dutifully. He should perform all the rituals of a sacrifice.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: अफालकृष्टं व्रीहियवं नीवारं विघसानि च। हींषि सम्प्रयच्छेत मखेष्वत्रापि पञ्चसु॥
en: He should live upon rice and wheat which grows indigenously, and upon other sorts of grains, growing wildly. He should eat the remnant after feeding guests. In the third mode of life, he should make offerings of clarified butter in the five celebrated Sacrifices.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: वानप्रस्थाश्रमेऽप्येताश्चतस्रो वृत्तयः स्मृताः। सद्य:प्रक्षालकाः केचित् केचिन्मासिकसंचयाः॥
en: Four courses of conduct have been laid down for the Vanaprastha mode of life. Some gather only what is necessary for the day. Some store up things for a month.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: वार्षिकं संचयं केचित् केचिद् द्वादशवार्षिकम्। कुर्वन्त्यतिथिपूजार्थं यज्ञतन्त्रार्थमेव वा॥
en: Some collect grain and other necessaries sufficient to last for twelve years. Hermits may act thus for adoring guests and performning sacrifices.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: अभ्रावकाशा वर्षासु हेमन्ते जलसंश्रयाः। ग्रीष्मे च पञ्च तपसः शश्वच्च मितभोजनाः॥
en: They should during the rains, expose themselves to rain and go to water during the autumn. In summer, they should sit in the midst of four fires with the sun burning overhead. Throughout the year, however, they should be sparing in deit.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: भूमौ विपरिवर्तन्ते तिष्ठन्ति प्रपदैरपि। स्थानासनैर्वर्तयन्ति सवनेष्वभिषिञ्चते॥
en: They should sit and sleep on the naked earth. They stand on only their toes. They should be satisfied with the bare earth and with small mats of grass. They perform their ablutions morning, noon, and evening.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: दन्तोलूखलिकाः केचिदश्मकुट्टास्तथा परे। शुक्लपक्षे पिबन्त्येके यवागू क्वथितां सकृत्॥
en: Some amongst them use only their teeth for cleaning grain. Others use only stones for the same, Some amongst them drink, only during the light fortnight, boiled very lightly, gruel of wheat (or other, grain).

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: कृष्णपक्षे पिबन्त्यन्ये भुजते वा यथागतम्। मूलैरेके फलैरेके युष्पैरेके दृढव्रताः॥ वर्तयन्ति यथान्यायं वैखानसगतिं श्रिताः।
en: Others drink similar gruel only during the dark fortnight. Some eat what only comes of itself. Some practising rigid vows, live upon only roots, some upon only fruits, some upon only flowers, duly following the method followed by the Vaikhanashas.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: एताश्चान्याश्च विविधा दीक्षास्तेषां मनीषिणाम्॥ चतुर्थश्चौपनिषदो धर्म: साधारणः स्मृतः। वानप्रस्थाद् गृहस्थाच्च ततोऽन्यः सम्प्रवर्तते॥
en: These and various other observances are practised by those wise and pious men. The fourth mode of life is based upon the Upanishads. The duties prescribed for it may be observed in all the modes of life equally. Differing from the others this mode comes afler domestic and forest life.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: अस्मिन्नेव युगे तात विप्रैः सर्वार्थदर्शिभिः। अगस्त्यः सप्त ऋषयो मधुच्छन्दोऽघमर्षणः॥ सांकृतिः सुदिवा तण्डियथावासोऽकृतश्रमः। अहोवीर्यस्तथा काव्यस्ताण्ड्यो मेधातिथिर्बुधः॥ बलवान् कर्णनिर्वाक: शून्यपालः कृतश्रमः। एनं धर्म कृतवन्तस्ततः स्वर्गमुपागमन॥
en: In this very cycle, O son, many learned Brahmanas knowing the truths of all things, have been known to observe this mode. Agastya, the seven Rishis Madhuchchhandas, Aghamarshana, Sankriti, Sudivatandi who lived with her soever he pleased and was content to take what came (without ever secking for anything), Ahovirya, Kavya, Tandya, the learned medhatithi, the highly energetic Karnanirvaka, and Shunyapala who had worked hard (for acquiring Yoga powel), were the authors of this course of duties, and themselves practising them, have all gone to heaven.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: तात प्रत्यक्षधर्माणस्तथा यायावरा गणाः। ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां धर्मनैपुणदर्शिनाम्॥ अन्ये चापरिमेयाश्च ब्राह्मणा वनमाश्रिताः। वैखानसा वालखिल्याः सैकताश्च तथा परे॥ कर्मभिस्ते निरानन्दा धर्मनित्या जितेन्द्रियाः। गताः प्रत्यक्षधर्माणस्ते सर्वे वनमाश्रिताः॥
en: Many great Rishis, O son, who had the power to see immediately the fruits of their ascetic merit, those numberless ascetics who pass by the appellation of Yayavaras, many Rishis of very austere penances and endued with accurate knowledge about distinctions of duty, and many other Brahınanas too numerous to mention, adopted the forest mode of life. The Vaikhanasas, the Valikhilyas, the Saikatas, all of whom were given to austere penances, who were firm in virtue, who had controlled their senses, and who used to see the fruits of their penances immediately, adopted this mode of life and finally went to heaven.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: अनक्षत्रास्त्वनाधृष्या दृश्यन्ते ज्योतिषां गणाः। जरया च परिधनो व्याधिना च प्रपीडितः॥ चतुर्थे चायुषः शेषे वानप्रस्थाश्रमं त्यजेत्। सद्यस्कारां निरूप्येष्टिं सर्व वेदसदक्षिणाम्॥ आत्मयाजी सोऽऽत्मरतिरात्मक्रीडात्मसंश्रयः। आत्मन्यग्नीन् समारोप्य त्यक्त्वा सर्वपरिग्रहान्॥
en: Freed from fear and not counted with the stars and planets, these have become visible in the sky as luminaries. When the fourth or last part of life is got at, and when one is weakened by decrepitude and possessed by disease, one should leave off the forest mode of life. Performing a sacrifice capable of being completed in a single day and in which the sacrificial fee should be everything he has, he should himself perforin his own funeral rite. Withdrawn from every other object, he should devote himself to his own self, taking pleasure in himself, and depending also on his own self. He should put up all his sacrificial fires (thenceforth) upon his ownself, and sever all sorts of bonds and attachments.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: साधरकांश्च यजेद् यज्ञानिष्टीश्चैवेह सर्वदा। यदैव याजिनां यज्ञादात्मनीज्या प्रवर्तते।॥ त्रींश्चैवाग्नीन् यजेत् सम्यगात्मन्येवात्ममोक्षणात्। प्राणेभ्यो यजुषः पञ्च षट् प्राश्नीयादकुत्सयन्॥
en: He should always celebrate such sacrifices and rites as are completed in a single day. When, however, from performance of the (ordinary) sacrifices of sacrificers, the Sacrifice in Self begins, then for liberation he should sacrifice his own self in the three fires. Without linding fault with his food he should take five or six mouthfuls, offering them duly to the five vital airs uttering Mantras of the Yajurveda.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: केशलोमनखान् वाप्य वानप्रस्थो मुनिस्ततः। आश्रमादाश्रमं पुण्यं पूतो गच्छति कर्मभिः॥
en: Practising austerities while living like a forest recluse, one should shave off and having purified himself by acts, pass into the fourth and the last holy mode of life.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो दत्त्वा यः प्रव्रजेद् द्विजः। लोकास्तेजोमयास्तस्य प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते॥
en: That twice-born one who enters the fourth mode of life, giving pledges of assurance to all creatures, succeeds in acquiring many effulgent regions hereafter and ultimately attains to the Infinite.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: सुशीलवृत्तो व्यपनीतकल्मषो न चेह नामुत्र च कर्तुमीहते। अरोषमोहो गतसंधिविग्रहो भवेदुदासीनवदात्मविन्नरः॥
en: Of excellent disposition and conduct, with sins all purged off the person who is conversant with his own self never wished to perform any act for either this or the other world. Shorn of anger, error, anxiety and without friendship, such a person live in this world like one having nothing to do with it.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: यमेषु चैवानुगतेषु न व्यथे स्वशास्त्रसूत्राहुतिमन्त्रविक्रमः। भवेद् यथेष्टागतिरात्मवेदिनि न संशयो धर्मपरे जितेन्द्रिये।॥
en: One in the (observance of Sannyasa) should not be unwilling in satisfying the duties included in Yama and those also that walk behind them. Such a person should live energetically according to the ordinances laid down his own mode, and leave off Vedic study and the sacred thread which marks his birth. Given to righteousness and having his senses under complete control, such a person endued with knowledge of self, attains forsooth, to the end for which he tries.

description: The duties of the Vanaprastha mode of Life
sn: रधिष्ठितं त्रीनधिवृत्तिमुत्तमम्। चतुर्थमुक्तं परमाश्रमं शृणु प्रकीर्त्यमानं परमं परायणम्॥
en: After the third is the fourth mode of life. It is very superior, and has numberless high virtues. In merit it reigns supreme over the three other modes of life. It is said to occupy the very highest place. Listen to me as I describe the duties belonging to that mode which is very supreme and which is the high refuge of all.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: शुक उवाच वर्तमानस्थैवात्र वानप्रस्थाश्रमे यथा। योक्तव्योऽऽत्मा कथं शक्त्या वेद्यं वै कासता परम्॥
en: Shuka said While living satisfying duly the duties of the forest life, how should one, who tries to attain to that which is the highest object of knowledge, set his soul on Yoga according to be best of his power?

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: व्यास उवाच प्राप्य संस्कारमेताभ्यामाश्रमाभ्यां ततः परम्। यत्कार्यं परमार्थ तदिहैकमनाः शृणु॥ तु
en: Vyasa said Having acquired purity by the practice of the first two modes of life, viz., Brahmacharya and domesticity, one should, thereafter, set his mind on Yoga in the third mode of life. Listen now with rapt attention to what should be done for attaining to the highest object of acquisition.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: कषायं पाचयित्वाऽऽशु श्रेणिस्थानेषु च त्रिषु। प्रव्रजेच्च परं स्थानं पारिवाज्यमनुत्तमम्॥
en: Having conquered all shortcomings of the mind of heart by easy means in the practice of the first three modes of life, one should pass into the best and the highest of all the modes, viz., Sannyasa or Renunciation.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: तद् भवानेवमभ्यस्य वर्ततां श्रूयतां तथा। एक एव चरेद् धर्मं सिद्ध्यर्थमसहायवान्॥
en: Do you then pass your days, having acquired the purity. Listen also to me. One should, alone and without anybody to help him or bear him company, practise Yoga for achieving success.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: एकश्चरति यः पश्यन् न जहाति न हीयते। अनग्निरनिकेतश्च ग्राममन्नार्थमाश्रयेत्॥
en: One who practises Yoga without any one in his company, who sees everything as repetition of his own self, and who never discard anything, never falls away from Liberation. Without keeping the sacrificial fires and without a fixed dwelling, such a person should enter a village for only begging his food.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: अश्वस्तनविधाता स्यान्मुनिर्भावसमाहितः। लध्वाशी नियताहारः सकृदन्ननिषेविता॥
en: He should provide himself for the day without keeping any thing in store for the morrow. He should practise penances, with heat fixed on the Supreme. Eating little and that even under proper restrictions, he should not take more than one meal in a day.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: कपालं वृक्षमूलानि कुचैलमसहायता। उपेक्षा सर्वभूतानामेतावद् भिक्षुलक्षणम्॥
en: The other marks of a mendicant are the human skull, protection under trees, rags for wearing, companionless solitude, and indifference to all creatures.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: यस्मिन् वाचः प्राविशन्ति कूपे त्रस्ता द्विपा इव। न वक्तारं पुनर्यान्ति कैवल्याश्रमे वसेत्॥
en: That person into whom words enter like terrified elephants into a well, and from whom they never return to the speaker, is fit to lead this mode of life which had Libcration for its end.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: नैव पश्येन्न शृणुयादवाच्यं जातु कस्यचित्। ब्राह्मणानां विशेषेण नैव ब्रूयात् कथंचन॥
en: The mendicant should never mind the evil deeds of any person. He should never hear vilifications of others. He should especially guard against reviling a Brahmana.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: यद् ब्राह्मणस्य कुशलं तदेव सततं वदेत्। तूष्णीमासीत निन्दायां कुर्वन् भैषज्यमात्मनः॥
en: He should always say only what is pleasant to the Brahmanas. When anything is said against him, he should remain perfectly silent. Such silence is the medical treatment prescribed for him.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: येन पूर्णमिवाकाशं भवत्येकेन सर्वदा। शून्यं येन जनाकीर्णं तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: That person for whose single self the spot he occupies becomes like the eastern sky, and who can regard as perfectly lonely a spot teeming with thousands of men and things, is considered by the gods to be a true Brahmana.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: येन केनचिदाच्छन्नो येन केनचिदाशितः। यत्र क्वचन शायी च तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: The gods know him for a Brahmana who puts on whatever comes by the way, who lives upon whatever he gets, and who sleeps on what ever spot he finds.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: अहेरिव गणाद् भीतः सौहित्यानरकादिव। कुणपादिव च स्त्रीभ्यस्तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: The gods regard him as a Brahmana who fears company like a snake; the full measure of gratification (from foods and drinks) as of hell; and women as a corpse.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: न क्रुद्ध्येन प्रहृष्येच्च मानितोऽमानितश्च यः। सर्वभूतेष्वभयदस्तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: The gods know him as a Brahmana who is never glad when honoured and never angry when insulted, and who has given assurances of mercy to all creatures.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: नाभिनन्देत मरणं नाभिनन्देत जीवितम्। कालमेघ प्रतीक्षते निदेशं भृतको यथा॥
en: One following the last mode of life should not regard death with joy. Nor should he regard life with joy. He should only wait for his hour like a servant waiting for his master's command.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: अनभ्याहतचित्त स्यादनभ्याहतवाग् भवेत्। निर्मुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यो निरमित्रस्य किं भयम्॥
en: He should purify his heart of all shortcomings. He should purify his speech of all faults. He should purge himself of all sins. Shorn as he is of enemies what fear can attack him.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो भूतानामभयं ततः। तस्य मोहाद् विमुक्तस्य भयं नास्ति कुतश्चन॥
en: He who fears no creature and whom no creature fears, can have no fear from any quarter, freed as he is from every form of mistake.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: यथा नागपदेऽन्यानि पदानि पदगामिनाम्। सर्वाण्येवापिधीयन्ते पदजातानि कौञ्जरे॥
en: As the foot-prints of all other creatures moving upon legs are engulfed within those of elephants, likewise all ranks and conditions are absorbed within Yoga.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: एवं सर्वमहिंसायां धर्मार्थमपिधीयते। अमृतः स नित्यं वसति यो हिंसां न प्रपद्यते॥
en: Similarly, every other duty and observance is encompassed within the one duty of abstention froin injury. He who avoids injuring other creatures, lives an eternal life of joy.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: अहिंसकः समः सत्यो धृतिमान् नियतेन्द्रियः। शरण्यः सर्वभूतानां गतिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम्॥
en: One who abstains from injury, who regards all creatures impartially, who is devoted to truth, who is gifted with fortitude, who has his senses under restraints, and who extends protection to all beings, attains to a peerless end.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: एवं प्रज्ञानतृप्तस्य निर्भयस्य निराशिषः। न मृत्युरतिगो भावः स मृत्युमधिगच्छति॥
en: The state of death cannot with selfknowledge, who is shorn of fear, desire and expectancy. On the other hand, such a person conquers death.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: विमुक्तं सर्वसङ्गेभ्यो मुनिमाकाशवत् स्थितम्। अस्वमेकचरं शान्तं तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: The gods know him for a Brahmana who is freed from attachments of every kind, who practises penances, who lives like space which while containing everything is yet unattached to all things, who has nothing which he can call his own, who reads a lonely life, and who possesses equanimity of soul.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: जीवितं यस्य धर्मार्थं धर्मो हर्यर्थमेव च। अहोरात्राश्च पुण्यार्थं तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: The gods regard him as a Brahmana whose life is for the practice of righteousness, whose righteousness is for the behoof of them who wait dutifully upon him, and whose days and nights exist only for acquiring religious merit.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: निराशिषमनारम्भं निर्नमस्कारमस्तुतिम्। निर्मुक्तं बन्धनैः सर्वैस्तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: The gods regard him as a Brahmana who is shorn of desire, who never struggles (for worldly emoluments), who never lowers his head to any one, who never flatters another, and who is shorn of all sorts of attachment.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: सर्वाणि भूतानि सुखे रमन्ते सर्वाणि दुःखस्य भृशं त्रसन्ते। तेषां भयोत्पादनजातखेदः कुर्यान्न कर्माणि हि श्रद्दधानः॥
en: All creatures are filled with pleasure at the prospect of happiness or miserable at the prospect of grief. The man of faith, therefore who should feel sorry at the prospect of afflicting other other creatures, must abstain absolutely from all acts.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: दानं हि भूताभयदक्षिणायाः सर्वाणि दानान्यधितिष्ठतीह। तीक्ष्णां तनुं यः प्रथमं जहाति सोऽऽनन्त्यमाप्नोत्यभयं प्रजाभ्यः॥
en: The gift of assurances of harmlessness to all creatures is superior in point of merit all other gifts. He who, at the beginning, promises abstention from injury, acquires Liberation whence is the assurance of harınlessness to all creatures.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: उत्तान आस्येन हविर्जुहोति लोकस्य नाभिर्जगतः प्रतिष्ठा। तस्याङ्गमङ्गानि कृताकृतं च वैश्वानरः सर्वमिदं प्रपेदे॥
en: That man who does not put into his open mouth even the five or six inouthfuls which are sanctioned for the forest recluse, is said to be the navel of the world, and the refuge of the universe. The fire occupies the head and other limbs, as also the acts good and bad.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: प्रादेशमाने हृदि निःसृतं यत् तस्मिन् प्राणानात्मयाजी जुहोति। तस्याग्निहोत्रं हुतमात्मसंस्थं सर्वेषु लोकेषु सदेवकेषु॥
en: Such a man, who performs a sacrifice in his own self, makes a libation of his senses and mind into the fire which lives within the limited space of his own heart. On account again of his pouring such a libation into such a fire within his own self, the universe with all creatures including the very celestials, becomes pleased.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: देवं त्रिधातुं त्रिवृतं सुपर्णं ये विद्युरग्रयां परमात्मतां च। ते सर्वलोकेषु महीयमाना देवाः समाः सुकृतं वदन्ति॥
en: They, who know the Sentiency which is endued with effulgence, which is covered with T: three sheaths, which has three qualities for its characteristics, to be Ishvara partaking of that which is highest, viz., the nature of the Supreme Soul, are respected of all the worlds. They very gods with all human beings applaud their merits.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: मथो निरुक्तं परमार्थतां च। सर्वं शरीरात्मनि यः प्रवेद तस्यैव देवाः स्पृहयन्ति नित्यम्॥
en: He who succeeds is seeing in the Soul which lives in his own body all the Vedas, ether and the other objects of perception, the rituals of the scriptures, all those entities which are perceptible in sound only, and the superior nature of the Supreme Soul, adored of the very gods as the foremost of all beings.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: भूमावसक्तं दिवि चाप्रमेयं हिरण्मयं योऽण्डजमण्डमध्ये। पतत्रिणं पक्षिणमन्तरिक्ष यो वेद भोग्यात्मनि रश्मिदीप्तः॥
en: He who sees in the Soul which lives within his body that foremost of beings which is not attached to the Earth, which is not attached to the Earth, which is immeasurable in even the limitless sky, which is made of gold, which is begotten of the egg and lives within the egg, which is equipped with many feathers, and which has two wings like a bird, and which is rendered effulgent by many rays of light is adored of the very gods as the foremost of all beings.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: आवर्तमानमजरं विवर्तनं षण्णाभिकं द्वादशारं सुपर्व। यस्येदमास्ये परियाति विश्वं तत्कालचक्रं निहितं गुहायाम्॥
en: The very gods adore him in whose understanding is set the wheel of Time, which is constantly revolving, which knows no deterioration, which devours the span of existence of every creature, which has the six seasons for its naves, which is equipped with twelve radii consisting of the twelve months, which has excellent joints, and towards whose gaping mouth goes on this universe.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: यः सम्प्रसादो जगतः शरीरं सर्वान्स लोकानधिगच्छतीह। स्ते वै तृप्तास्तर्पयन्त्यास्यमस्य॥
en: The Supreme Soul is the huge unconsciousness of dreamless sleep. That Unconsciousness form the body of the universe. It pervades all created things. Sentiency occupying a portion of that capacious unconsciousness, pleases the gods. These last, being pleased, gratify the open mouth of the unconsciousness.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: तेजोमयो नित्यमयः पुराणो लोकाननन्तानभयानुपैति। भूतानि यस्मान्न वसन्ते कदाचित्स भूतानां न त्रसते कदाचित्॥
en: Endued with effulgence as also with the principle of eternity, Sentiency is without a beginning. It wins infinite regions of eternal happiness. He whom no creature fears, has never to fear any creature.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: अगर्हणीयो न च गर्हतेऽनयान्स वै विप्रः परमात्मानमीक्षेत्। विनीतमोहो व्यपनीतकल्मषो न चेह नामुत्र च सोऽन्नमृच्छति॥
en: He who never does anything blameable and who never censures another, is said to be a truly twice-born one. Such a man succeeds in seeing the Supreme Soul. He whose ignorance has been removed and whose sins have been washed away, never enjoys either here or hereafter the happiness that is enjoyed by others.

description: The means for acquiring the highest subject of acquisition
sn: अरोषमोहः समलोष्टकाञ्चनः प्रहीणकोशो गतसंधिविग्रहः। श्वरन्नुदासीनवदेष भिक्षुकः॥
en: A person following the fourth mode of life wanders on the Earth like one not attached to anything. Such a person is shorn of anger and crror. Such a person regards equally a clod of earth and a lump of gold. such a man never keeps anything in store for his use. Such a person has no friends and enemies. Such a person does not care praise or blame, and the agreeable and the disagreeable.

sn: व्यास उवाच प्रकृत्यास्तु विकारा ये क्षेत्रज्ञस्तैरधिष्ठितः। न चैनं ते प्रजानन्ति स त जानाति तानपि॥
en: Vyasa said The Sentiency is endued with all thse entities which are modifications of Nature. These do not know the Soul but the Soul knows them all.

sn: तैश्चैवं कुरुते कार्यं मनःषष्ठैरिहेन्द्रियैः। सुदान्तैरिव संयन्ता दृढैः परमवाजिभिः॥
en: Like a good driver going on with the help of strong, well-trained, and very good horses along the paths he chooses, thc Soul acts with the help of these, called the senses, having the mind for their sixth.

sn: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परे ह्या अर्थेभ्यः परमं मनः। मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा महान् परः॥
en: The objects of the senses are superior to the senses themselves. The mind is superior to those objects. The understanding is superior to the mind. Mahat or the principle of greatness is superior to the understanding.

sn: महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात् परतोऽमृतम्। अमृतान्न परं किंचित् सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः॥
en: Superior to Mahat is the Prakriti. Superior to the Prakriti is Brahma. There is nothing superior to Brahma. That is the highest limit of goodness and the highest end.

sn: एवं सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोऽऽत्मा न प्रकाशते। दृश्यते त्वम्यया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया सूक्ष्मदर्शिभिः॥
en: The Supreme Soul is hidden in every creature. It is not so manifest that ordinary men can see. Only Yogins with subtile vision see the Supreme Soul with the help of their keen and subtile understandings.

sn: अन्तरात्मनि संलीय मनःषष्ठानि मेधया। इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थांश्च बहुचिन्त्यमचिन्तयन्॥ ध्यानेनोपरमं कृत्वा विद्यासम्पादितं मनः। अनीश्वरः प्रशान्तात्मा ततोऽर्छत्यमृतं पदम्॥
en: Merging the senses having the mind for their sixth and all the objects of the senses into the inner self by the help of the understanding, and meditating upon the three states of consciousness, viz., the object thought, the act of thinking, and the thinker, and abstaining by contemplation from every kind of enjoyment, replenishing his mind with the knowledge that he is Brahma's self, laying aside at the same time all consciousness of power, and there by making his Soul perfectly tranquil, the Yogin attains to immortality.

sn: इन्द्रियाणां तु सर्वेषां वश्यात्मा चलितस्मृतिः। आत्मनः सम्प्रदानेन मर्यो मृत्युमुपाश्नुते॥
en: That person, however, who becomes the slave of all his senses and whose ideas of right and wrong have been confounded, already subject as he is to death, actually meets with death by such surrender of self.

sn: आहत्य सर्वसंकल्पान् सत्त्वे चित्तं निवेशयेत्। सत्त्वे चित्तं समावेश्य ततः कालंजरो भवेत्॥
en: Destroying all desires, one should drown the gross understanding into one's subtile Understanding. Having thus drowned the gross into the subtile Understanding, one is sure to become a second Kalanjara mountain.

sn: चित्तप्रसादेन यति हातीह शुभाशुभम्। प्रसन्नात्माऽऽत्मनि स्थित्वा सुखमत्यन्तमश्नुते॥
en: By purifying his heart, the Yogin gets over both righteousness and its opposite. By purifying his hcart and by living in his own true nature, he acquires the highest happiness.

sn: लक्षणं तु प्रसादस्य यथा स्वप्ने सुखं स्वपेत्। युञ्जनात्मानमात्मनि। निवाते वा यथा दीपो दीप्यमानो न कम्पते॥
en: The sign of that purity of heart is that one who has acquired it experiences that state of unconsciousness which is similar to that of dreamless slumber. The Yogin who has acquired that state lives like the steady flame of a lamp which burns in a place where the atmosphere is perfectly still.

sn: एवं पूर्वापरे काले लध्वाहारो विशुद्धात्मा पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि॥
