en: Being sparing in diet, and having purified his heart, that Yogin who applies his Soul to the Soul, sees the Soul in the Soul.

sn: रहस्यं सर्ववेदानामनैतिह्यमनागमम्। आत्मप्रत्ययिकं शास्त्रमिदं पुत्रानुशासनम्॥
en: This topic, O son, intended for your instruction, is the essence of all the Vedas. The truths expounded in it cannot be understood by the help of inference alone or by that of mere study of the scriptures. One must understand in himself by the help of faith.

sn: धर्माख्यानेषु सर्वेषु सत्याख्याने च यद् वसु। दशेदमृक्सहस्राणि निर्मथ्यामृतमुद्धतम्॥
en: By churning the riches contained in all religious works and in all topics based on truth, as also the ten thousand Riches, this ambrosia has been acquired.

sn: नवनीतं यथा दनः काष्ठादग्निर्यथैव च। तथैव विदुषां ज्ञानं पुत्र हेतोः समुद्धृतम्॥
en: As butter from curds and fire from wood, so this has been raised for the sake of my son,-this which forms the knowledge of all truly wise men.

sn: स्नातकानामिदं शास्त्रं वाच्यं पुत्रानुशासनम्। तदिदं नाप्रशान्ताय नादान्तायातपस्वि ने॥
en: This topic, O son, fraught with solid instruction, is intended for Brahmana who having studied the Vedas, have become householders. It should never be delivered to one who is not of tranquil soul, or one is not selfcontrolled, or who one who has not practised penances.

sn: नोदविदुषे वाच्यं तथा नानुगताय च। नासूयकाजानृजवे न चानिर्दिष्टकारिणे॥
en: It should not be delivered to one who is not conversant with the Vedas, or one who do not humbly wait upon his preceptor, or one who is not shorn of malice, or one who is not possessed of sincerity and candour, or one who is of reckless conduct.

sn: न तर्कशास्त्रदग्धाय तथैव पिशुनाय च। श्लाघिने श्लाघनीयाय प्रशान्ताय तपस्विने॥ इदं प्रियाय पुत्राय शिष्यायानुगताय च। रहस्यधर्मं वक्तव्यं नान्यस्मै तु कथंचन॥
en: It should never be delivered to one whose intellect has been consumed by disputation, or one who is vile or low. This topic containing the quintessence of duties, should be communicated to that person, however, who is possessed of fame, or who deserves praise, or who is of tranquil soul, or possessed of ascetic merit, to a Brahimana who is such to one's son or dutiful disciple, but on no account should it be delivered to others.

sn: यद्यप्यस्य महीं दद्याद् रत्नपूर्णामिमां नरः। इदमेव ततः श्रेय इति मन्येत तत्त्ववित्॥
en: If any person gives away the entire Earth with all her treasures, to one conversant with truth, the latter should still consider the gifts of This knowledge as very much superior to that gift.

sn: अतो गुह्यतरार्थं तदध्यात्ममतिमानुषम्। यत् तन्महर्षिभिर्दृष्टं वेदान्तेषु च गीयते॥ तत् तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यामि यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि।।२
en: I shall now describe to you a subject which is a greater mystery than this, a subject connected with the Soul, which is above the ordinary understandings of human beings, which has been seen by the foremost of Rishis, what has been treated in the Upanishads, and which forms the topic of your inquiry.

sn: यच्च ते मनसि वर्तते परं यत्र चासित तव संशयः क्वचित्। श्रूयतामयमहं तवाग्रतः पुत्र किं हि कथयामि ते पुनः॥
en: Tell me what, after this, is in your mind? Tell me in what you have still any doubt? Listen, for here I am. So son, seated before you! Upon what, indeed, shall I once more discourse to you.

sn: शुक उवाच अध्यात्म विस्तरेणेह पुनरेव वदस्व मे। यदध्यात्म यथा वेद भगवनृषिसत्तम्॥
en: Shuka said O illustrious one, O foremost of Rishis, once again describe to me fully the subject bearing on soul. Tell me what, in deed, is spiritual topic and whence does it come?

sn: व्यास उवाच अध्यात्मं यदिदं तात पुरुषस्येह पठ्यते। तत् तेऽहं वर्तयिष्यामि तस्य व्याख्यामिमां शृणु॥
en: Vyasa said That, O son, which is considered as spiritual with reference to human beings, I shall now mention to you, and listen to the explanation I give.

sn: भूमिरापस्तथा ज्योतिर्वायुराकाश एव चा महाभूतानि भूतानां सागरस्योर्मयो यथा।॥
en: Earth, water, light, wind, and entities are the great principles which form the component parts of all creatures, and though really one are yet considered different like the waves of the Ocean.

sn: प्रसार्येह यथाङ्गानि कूर्मः संहरते पुनः। तद्वन्महान्ति भूतानि यवीयःसु विकुर्वते॥
en: Like a tortoise extending out its limbs and withdrawing then again, the great elements, by living in innumerable small forms, go through transformations.

sn: इति तन्मयमेवेदं सर्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम्। सर्गे च प्रलये चैव तस्मिन् निर्दिश्यते तथा॥
en: All this universe of mobile and immobile objects has for its component parts these five elements. Everything, regarding creation and destruction, is referable to this fivefold elements.

sn: महाभूतानि पञ्चैव सर्वभूतेषु भूतकृत्। अकरोत् तात वैषम्यं यस्मिन् यदनुपश्यति॥
en: These five elements are in all existent things. The Creator of all things, however, has made an unequal distribution of those elements for serving different ends.

sn: शुक उवाच अकरोद् यच्छरीरेषु कथं तदुपलक्षयेत्। इन्द्रियाणि गुणाः केचित् कथं तानुपलक्षयेत्॥
en: How can one understand that unequal distribution in the various objects of the universe? Which amongst them are the senses and which the attributes? How may this be understood?

sn: व्यास उवाच एत् ते वर्तयिष्यामि यथावदनुपूर्वशः। शृणु तत् त्वमिहैकाग्रो यथातत्त्वं यथा च तत्॥
en: Vyasa said I shall explain this to you properly, one after another. Listen with rapt attention to the subject as I explain how what I have said actually takes place.

sn: शब्दः श्रोतं तथा स्वानि त्रयमाकाशसम्भवम्। प्राणश्चेष्टा तथा स्पर्श एते वायुगुणास्त्रयः॥
en: Sound, the sense of hearing, and all the cavities within the body,-these three Originate-from ether. The vital airs, the action of the limbs, and touch are the attributes of the wind.

sn: रूपं चक्षुर्विपाकश्च त्रिधा ज्योतिर्विधीयते। रसोऽथ रसनं स्नेहो गुणास्त्वेते त्रयोऽम्भसः॥
en: From eyes and the digestive fire within the stomach, originate from light. Taste, tongue, and all the humours,—these three originate from water.

sn: प्रेयं घ्राणं शरीरं च भूमेरेते गुणास्त्रयः। एतावानिन्द्रियग्रामैर्व्याख्यातः पाञ्चभौतिकः॥
en: Scent, nose, and the body,-these three,-form the attributes of earth. These then, as I have explained to you, are the changes of the five (great) elements in connection with the senses.

sn: वायोः स्पर्शो रसोऽङ्ग्यश्च ज्योतिषो रूपमुच्यते। आकाशप्रभवः शब्दो गन्धो भूमिगुणः स्मृतः॥
en: Touch is said to be attribute of the wind; taste of water; form of light. Sound originate from ether, and scent is the property of earth.

sn: मनो बुद्धिः स्वभावश्च त्रय एते स्वयोनिजाः। न गुणानतिवर्तन्ते गुणेभ्यः परमागताः॥
en: Mind, Understanding, and Nature,—these three, originate from their own previous states, and acquiring a position higher than the attributes, do not get over those attributes.

sn: यथा कूर्म इहाङ्गानि प्रसार्य विनियच्छति। एवमेवेन्द्रियग्रामं बुद्धिः सृष्ट्वा नियच्छति॥ एतस्मिन्नेव कृत्ये तु वर्तते बुद्धिरुत्तमा॥
en: As the tortoise extends its limbs and withdraws them once again within itself, so the Understanding creates the senses and once again withdraws them into itself. The consciousness of ego which arises about what is above the soles of the feet and below the crown of the head, is mainly due to the action of the Understanding.

sn: गुणान् नेनीयते बुद्धिर्बुद्धिरेवेन्द्रियाण्यपि। मनःषष्ठानि सर्वाणि बुद्ध्यभावे कुतो गुणाः॥
en: It is the Understanding which is transformed into the (five) attributes. It is the Understanding also which is transformed into the (five) senses with the mind for the sixth. Where the attributes when the Understanding is nowhere? are Own

sn: इन्द्रियाणि नरे पञ्च षष्ठं तु मन उच्यते। सप्तमी बुद्धिमेवाहुः क्षेत्रज्ञं पुनरष्टमम्॥
en: There are five senses in man. The mind is called the sixth. The Understanding is called the seventh. The Soul is the eighth.

sn: चक्षुरालोचनायैव संशयं कुरुते मनः। बुद्धिरध्यवसानाय साक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञ उच्यते॥
en: The eyes and the other senses are for only receiving impressions of form, etc. The mind exists for doubting. The Understanding determines those doubts. The Soul is said to only see every work without mingling with them.

sn: रजस्तमश्च सत्त्वं च यत्र एते स्वयोनिजाः। समाः सर्वेषु भूतेषु तान् गुणानुपलक्षयेत्॥
en: The qualities of goodness, darkness and ignorance originate from their counterparts. These exist equally in all creatures. These are called qualities and should be known by the actions they produce.

sn: तत्र यत् प्रीतिसंयुक्तं किंचिदात्मनि लक्षयेत्। प्रशान्तमिव संशुद्धं सत्त्वं तदुपधारयेत्॥
en: Regarding those actions, all such states of cheerfulness or joy, of tranquillity and purity which one becomes conscious of in one self, should be known as due to the quality of goodness.

sn: यत् तु संतापसंयुक्तं काये मनसि वा भवेत्। प्रवृत्तं रज इत्येवं तत्र चाप्युपलक्षयेत्॥
en: All such states of sorrow in either the body or the mind, should be considered as due to the influence of the quality of darkness.

sn: यदूर्ध्वं पादतलयोरवाङ्मूर्ध्नश्च पश्यति। यत् तु सम्मोहसंयुक्तमव्यक्तविषयं भवेत्। अप्रतय॑मविज्ञेयं तमस्तदुपधार्यताम्॥
en: All such states of stupefaction whose cause cannot be deterinined (by either reason or inward light), should be known as due to the action of Ignorance.

sn: प्रहर्षः प्रीतिरानन्दः साम्यं स्वस्थात्मचित्तता। अकस्माद् यदि वा कस्माद् वर्तन्ते सात्त्विका गुणाः।।२
en: Delight, cheerfulness, joy, equanimity, contentment of heart, due to any known cause or originating otherwise, are all effects of the quality of goodness.

sn: अभिमानो मृघावादो लोभो मोहस्तथाक्षमा। लिङ्गानि रजसस्तानि वर्तन्ते हेत्वहेतुतः॥
en: Pride, false speech, cupidity, stupefaction, vindictiveness, whether originating from any known cause or otherwise, are characteristics of the quality of darkness.

sn: तथा मोहः प्रमादश्च निद्रा तन्द्राप्रबोधिता। कथंचिदभिवर्तन्ते विज्ञेयास्तामसा गुणाः॥
en: Stupefaction of judgement, carelessness, sleep, lethargy, and indolence, from whatever cause these may originate, are to be regarded as the characteristics of the quality of Ignorance.

sn: व्यास उवाच मनो विसृजते भावं बुद्धिरध्यवसायिनी। हृदयं प्रियाप्रिये वेद त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना॥
en: Vyasa said The mind creates innumerable ideas. The Understanding, differentiates things and ascertains their true nature. The heart discriminates which is pleasant and which unpleasant. There are the three forces which produce acts.

sn: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यः परमं मनः। मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा परो मतः॥
en: The objects of the senses are superior to the senses. The mind is superior to those objects. The Understanding is superior to mind. The Soul is considered superior to Understanding.

sn: बुद्धिरात्मा मनुष्यस्य बुद्धिरेवात्मनाऽऽत्मनि। यदा विकुरुते भावं तदा भवति सा मनः॥
en: as on Ordinarily the Understanding is a man's Soul. When the Understanding, by itself, forms ideas (of objects) within itself, it is then called Mind.

sn: इन्द्रियाणां पृथग्भावाद् बुद्धिविक्रियते ह्यतः। शृण्वती भवति श्रोत्रं स्पृशती स्पर्श उच्यते॥
en: The senses being different from one another, the Understanding presents different aspects account of its different modifications. When it hears, it becomes the organ of hearing, and when it touches, it becomes the organ of touch.

sn: पश्यती भवते दृष्टी रसती रसनं भवेत्। जिघ्रती भवति घ्राणं बुद्धिर्विक्रियते पृथक्॥
en: Likewise, when it sees, it becomes the organ of vision, and when it tastes, it becomes the organ of taste and when it smells, it becomes the organs of scent. It is the Understanding which appears under different guises by modification.

sn: इन्द्रियाणि तु तान्याहुस्तेष्वदृश्योऽधितिष्ठति। तिष्ठती पुरुषे बुद्धिस्त्रिषु भावेषु वर्तते॥
en: These modifications of the Understanding are called the senses. The invisible Soul is placed over them as their presiding chief. Living in the body, the Understanding exists in the three states (of qualities).

sn: कदाचिल्लभते प्रीतिं कदाचिदपि शोचति। न सुखेन न दुःखेन कदाचिदिह युज्यते॥
en: Sometimes it acquires cheerfulness, sometimes it yields to grief and sometimes its condition becomes such that it is united with neither joy nor sorrow.

sn: सेयं भावात्मिका भावांस्त्रीनेतानतिवर्तते। सरितां सागरो भर्ता महावेलामिवोर्मिमान्॥
en: The Understanding, however, whose chief function is to create elements, transcends those three states as the ocean, the king of rivers, stands against the powerful currents of the rivers that fall into it.

sn: यदा प्रार्थयते किंचित् तदा भवति सा मनः। अधिष्ठानानि वै बुद्ध्यां पृथगेतानि संस्मरेत्। इन्द्रियाण्येव मेध्यानि विजेतव्यानि कृत्स्नशः॥
en: When the Understanding desires anything, it is called by the name of Mind. The senses, again, should all be considered as contained within the Understanding. The senses, which are engaged in bearing impressions of form, scent, etc., should all be controlled.

sn: सर्वाण्येवानुपूर्वेण यद् यदानुविधीयते। अविभागगता बुद्धिर्भावे मनसि वर्तते॥
en: When one sense becomes subordinate to the Understanding, the latter, though really not different, enters the Mind in the form of existent things. Such is the case with the senses one after another with reference to the ideas that are said to be apprehended by them.

sn: ये चैव भावा वर्तन्ते सर्व एष्वेव ते त्रिषु। अन्वर्थाः सम्प्रवर्तन्ते रथनेमिमरा इव॥
en: All the three states which exist, viz., Sativa, Rajas, and Tamas, attach to those three (viz., Mind, Understanding, and Consciousness), and like the spokes of a car-wheel acting for their attachment, to the circumference of the wheel, they follow the various objects.

sn: प्रदीपार्थं मनः कुर्यादिन्द्रियैर्बुद्धिसत्तमैः। निश्चरद्भिर्यथायोगमुदासीनैर्यदृच्छया॥
en: The mind must covert the senses into a lamp for removing the darkness which obstructs the knowledge of the Supreme Self. This knowledge which is gained by Yogins with the help of the especial instruments of Yoga, is acquired without any particular exertion by men who abstain from worldly objects.

sn: एवं स्वभावमेवेदमिति विद्वान् न मुह्यति। अशोचन्नप्रहृष्यन् हि नित्यं विगतमत्सरः॥
en: The universe is of the nature. The man of knowledge, therefore, become never stupefied. Such a man never grieves, never rejoices, and is shorn of envy.

sn: न चात्मा शक्यते द्रष्टुमिन्द्रियैः कामगोचरैः। प्रवर्तमानैरनये दुष्करैरकृतात्मभिः॥
en: The soul cannot be seen with the help of the senses whose nature is to roam about among all objects of desire. Even pious men, whose senses are pure, cannot see the soul with their help what then should be said of the vicious whose senses are impure.

sn: तेषां तु मनसा रश्मीन् यदा सम्यनियच्छति। तदा प्रकाशतेऽस्यात्मा दीपदीप्ता यथाऽऽकृतिः॥
en: When, however, a person, with the help of his mind, firmly holds their reins, it is then that his Soul sees itself like an object coming in view on account of the light of a lamp.

sn: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां तमस्यपगते यथा। प्रकाशं भवते सर्वं तथेदमुपधार्यताम्॥
en: As all things are seen when the darkness that covers them is removed, so the soul becomes manifest when the darkness that covers it is dispelled.

sn: यथा वारिचर: पक्षी न लिप्यति जले चरन्। विमुक्तात्मा तथा योगी गुणदोषैर्न लिप्यते॥
en: As a water fowl, though floating on the water, is never drenched by it, similarly the Yogin of freed soul is never sullied by the imperfections of the three qualities,

sn: एवमेव कृतप्रज्ञो न दोषैविषयांश्चरन्। असज्जमान: सर्वेषु कथंचन न लिप्यते॥
en: Likewise, a wise man by even enjoying all earthly objects without being attached to any of them, is never affected by shortcomings of any kind.

sn: त्यक्त्वा पूर्वकृतं कर्म रतिर्यस्य सदाऽऽत्मनि। सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्य गुणवर्गेष्वसज्जतः॥ सत्त्वमात्मा प्रसरति गुणान् वापि कदाचन। न गुणा विदुरात्मानं गुणान् वेद स सर्वदा॥
en: He who avoids acts after having performed them properly, and takes delight in the one really existent, viz., the Soul who has formed hinself the soul of all created beings, and who keeps himself understanding and senses which are created by the soul. The qualities can not apprehend the Soul. The Soul, however, apprehends them always.

sn: परिद्रष्टा गुणानां च परिस्रष्टा यथातथम्। सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेतदन्तरं विद्धि सूक्ष्मयोः॥
en: The Soul is the witness which sees the qualities and duly works them up. Mark this difference between the Understanding and the Soul both which are highly subtile.

sn: सृजतेऽत्र गुणानेक एको न सृजते गुणान्। पृथग्भूतौ प्रकृत्या तौ सम्प्रयुक्तौ च सर्वदा॥
en: One of them creates the qualities. The other does not create them. Though they are different from each other by nature, they are, however, always united.

sn: यथा मत्स्योऽद्भिरन्यः स्यात् सम्प्रयुक्तोतथैव तौ। मशकोदुम्बरौ वापि सम्प्रयुक्तौ यथा सह॥
en: The fish residing in the water is different from the element in which it resides. But as the fish and the water forming its residence are always united, likewise the quality of goodness and the individual soul exist in a state of union. The gnat begotten of a rotten fig is really not the fig but different from it. As the gnat and the fig are seen to be united with each other, so are the qualities of goodness and the individual Soul.

sn: इषीका वा यथा मुजे पृथक् च सह चैव च। तथैव सहितोवेतावन्योन्यस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितौ॥
en: As the blade in a clump of grass though distinct from the clump, exists in a state of union with it, so these two, though different from each other and each exists in its own self, are to be seen in a state of perpetual union.

sn: व्यास उवाच सृजते तु गुणान् सत्त्वं क्षेत्रज्ञस्त्वधितिष्ठति। गुणान् विक्रियत: सर्वानुदासीनवदीश्वरः॥
en: The objects by which one is encircled are created by the Understanding. Without being connected with them, the Soul stands aloof, lording over them. The Understanding creates all objects. The three principal qualities are continually being transformed. The Soul, gifled with power, lords over them all, without, however, mingling with them.

sn: स्वभावयुक्तं सर्वं यदिमान् सृजते गुणान्। उर्णनाभिर्यथा सूत्रं सृजते तद्गुणांस्तथा॥
en: The objects created by the Understanding partake of its own nature. Like the threads created by the spider, the objects created by the Understanding partake of the nature of Understanding.

sn: प्रध्वस्ता न निवर्तन्ते प्रवृत्तिर्नोपलभ्यते। एवमेके व्यवस्यन्ति निवृत्तिरिति चापरे॥
en: Some hold that the qualities, when done away with by yoga or knowledge, do not cease to exist. They hold this because when once gone, the marks only of their return are not perceived. Others hold that when destroyed by knowledge, they are at once destroyed never to rcturn.

sn: उभयं सम्प्रधायैतदध्यवस्येद् यथामति। अनेनैव विधानेन भवेद् गर्भशयो महान्॥
en: Meditating duly upon these two opinions, one should try his best according to the way one thinks proper. It is by this way that one should acquire eminence and take refuge in his own Soul alone.

sn: अनादिनिधनो ह्यात्मा तं बुद्ध्वा विचरेन्नरः। अक्रुरध्यन्नप्रहृष्यंश्च नित्यं विगतमत्सरः॥
en: The Soul is without beginning and without end. Understanding his Soul properly man should move and act, without yielding to anger, without indulging in joy, and always shorn of envy.

sn: इत्येवं हृदयग्रन्थिं बुद्धिचिन्तामयं दृढम्। अनित्यं सुखमासीत अशोचंश्छिन्नसंशयः॥
en: Cutting by this means the knot that is in his heart, created by the faculties of the Understanding, which is hard (to cut), but which can be destroyed by knowledge, one should live happily, without yielding to grief, and with his doubts removed.

sn: ताम्येयुः प्रच्युताः पृथ्व्या यथा पूर्णा नदी नराः। अवगाढा ह्यविद्वांसो विद्धि लोकमिमं तथा॥
en: Know that they who mix in worldly affairs, are as distressed in body and mind as persons ignorant of the art of swimming when they fall from the land into a vast and deep river.

sn: न तु ताम्यति वै विद्वान् स्थले चरति तत्त्ववित्। एवं यो विन्दतेऽऽत्मानं केवलं ज्ञानमात्मनः॥
en: Being conversant with the truth, the learned man, however, is never distressed, for he feels like one walking over firm land. Indeed, he who perceives his Soul to be such, viz., as full of consciousness which has knowledge alone for its mark, is never distressed.

sn: एवं बुद्ध्वा नरः सर्वं भूतानामागतिं गतिम्। समवेक्ष्य च वैषम्यं लभते शममुत्तमम्॥
en: By thus knowing the origin and end of all creatures, and by thus apprehending their distinctions, a person succeeds in acquiring high felicity.

sn: एतद् वै जन्मसामर्थ्य ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः। आत्मज्ञानं शमश्चैव पर्याप्तं तत्परायणम्॥
en: This knowledge is the possession of a Brahmana in particular by virtue of his birth. Knowledge of the Soul, and happiness like above, are each fully sufficient to lead to Liberation.

sn: एतद् बुद्ध्वा भवेद् बुद्धः किमन्यद् बुद्धलक्षणम्। विज्ञायैतद् विमुच्यन्ते कृतकृत्या मनीषिणः॥ न भवति विदुषां महद्भयं यदविदुषा समुहद्भयं परत्र। न हि गतिरधिकास्ति कस्यचिद् भवति हि या विदुषः सनातनी॥
en: By gaining such knowledge one really becomes learned. What else is the mark of a person of knowledge? Having gained such knowledge, the wise men consider themselves successful and become liberated. Those things which produce fear to men shorn of knowledge do not do so to those who are gifted with knowledge. There is no end higher than the eternal end which is acquired by a learned person.

sn: स्तत्तदेव च निरीक्ष्य शोचते। तत्र पश्य कुशलानशोचतो ये विदुस्तदुभयं कृताकृतम्॥
en: One sees with aversion all earthly objects of enjoyment which are, of course, full of shortcomings. Again seeing others pursue such objects with pleasure, another is filled with sorrow. But they who are conversant with both objects, viz., that which is fictitious and that which is not so, are never grieved and are truly happy.

sn: यत्करोत्यनभिसंधिपूर्वकं तच्च निर्गुदति तत् पुराकृतम्। न प्रियं तदुभयं न चाप्रियं तस्य तज्जनयतीह कुर्वतः॥
en: What a man does without expectation of fruits dissipates his acts of a pristine life. The acts, however, of such a person both of this end and his pristine life cannot lead to Liberation. On the other hand, such destruction of former acts and such acts of this life cannot bring what is disagreeable (viz., hell), even if the wise man engages in acts.

sn: शुक उवाच यस्माद् धर्मात् परो धर्मो विद्यते नेह कश्चन। यो विशिष्टश्च धर्मेभ्यस्तं भवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे॥
en: Shuka said May your reverend self describe what is the foremost of all duties, indeed, of that duty then which no higher one exists in this world.

sn: व्यास उवाच धर्मं ते सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि पुराणमृषिभिः कृतम्। विशिष्टं सर्वधर्मभ्यस्तमिहैकमनाः शृणु॥
en: Vyasa said I shall now describe to you duties having a very ancient origin and laid down by the Rishis, duties which are superior to all others. Listen to me with rapt attention.

sn: इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि बुद्ध्या संयम्य यत्नतः। सर्वतो निष्पतिष्णूनि पिता बालानिवात्मजान्॥
en: The maddening senses should carefully be governed by the understanding like a father checking his own in experienced children liable to fall into various evil habits.

sn: मनसश्चेन्द्रियाणां चाप्यैकाम्यं परमं तपः। तज्ज्यायः सर्वधर्मेभ्यः स धर्मः पर उच्यते॥
en: To withdraw the mind and the senses from all unworthy objects and their duc concentration (upon higher objects) is the highest penance. That is the highest of all duties. Indeed, that is said to be the highest duty.

sn: तानि सर्वाणि संधाय मनःषष्ठानि मेधया। आत्मतृप्त इवासीत बहुचिन्त्यमचिन्तयन्॥
en: Directing, by the help of the understanding, the senses having the mind for their sixth, and without, thinking of worldly objects which create innumerablc kinds of thought, one should live contented with his own self.

sn: गोचरेभ्यो निवृत्तानि यदा स्थास्यन्ति वेश्मनि। तदा त्वमात्मनाऽऽत्मानं परं द्रक्ष्यसि शाश्वतम्॥
en: When withdrawn from the fields where they generally run loose, senses and the mind return for living in their proper abode, it is then that you will see in your own self the Eternal and Supreme Soul.

sn: सर्वात्मानं महात्मानं विधूममिव पावकम्। तं पश्यन्ति महात्मानो ब्राह्मणा ये मनीषिणः॥
en: Those great Brahmanas who are endud with wisdom succeed in seeing that Supreme and Universal Soul which resembles a blazing fire in effulgence.

sn: यथा पुष्पफलोपेतो बहुशाखो महाद्रुमः। आतमनो नाभिजानीते क्व मे पुष्पं क्व मे फलम्॥ एवमात्मा न जानीते क्व गमिष्ये कुतस्त्वहम्। अन्यो ह्यत्रान्तरात्मास्ति यः सर्वमनुपश्यति॥
en: As a large tree enveloped with numberless branches and filled with many flowers and fruits, does not know in which part it has flowers and in which it has fruits, similarly the Soul, as modified by birth and other qualities, does not know whence it has come and whither it is to go. There is, however, an inner Soul, which sees every thing.

sn: ज्ञानदीपेन दीप्तेन पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि। दृष्ट्वा त्वमात्पनाऽऽत्मानं निरात्मा भव सर्ववित्॥
en: One sees the Soul with the help of the lamp of knowledge. Seeing, therefore, yourself with you ownself, cease to regard your body as yourself and acquire omniscience.

sn: विमुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यो मुक्तत्वच इवोरगः। परां बुद्धिमवाप्येह विपाप्मा विगतज्वरः॥
en: Purged of all sins, like a snake that has cast off its slough, one acquires high intelligence here and becomes free from every anxiety and the obligation of acquiring a new body.

sn: सर्वतः स्रोतसं घोरां नदी लोकप्रवाहिनीम्। पञ्चेन्द्रियग्राहवती मन:संकल्परोधसम्॥
en: Having its current spread in various directions, dreadful is this river of life carrying the world onward in its course. The five senses are its crocodiles. The mind and its objects are the shores.

sn: लोभमोहतृणच्छन्नां कामक्रोधसरीसृपाम्। सत्यतीर्थानृतक्षोभां क्रोधपङ्का सरिद्वराम्॥
en: Cupidity and bewilderment of judgement are the grass and straw and anger are the dreadful reptiles which live in it. Truth forms the landing stage by its miry banks. Falsehood forms its surges, and anger its mire.

sn: अव्यक्तप्रभवां शीघ्रां दुस्तरामकृतात्मभिः। प्रतरस्व नदी बुद्ध्या कामग्राहसमाकुलाम्॥
en: Originating from the Unmanifest, rapid is its current, and incapable of being crossed by persons of impure souls. Do you, with the help of the understanding, cross that river having desires for its alligators.

sn: संसारसागरगमां योनिपातालदुस्तराम्। आत्मकर्मोद्भवां तात जिह्वावर्ती दुरासदाम्॥
en: The worldly concerns form the ocean towards which that river runs. Genus and species form its unfathomable depth that none can understand. One's birth, O child, is the source from which that stream originates. Speech forms its eddies.

sn: यां तरन्ति कृतप्रज्ञा धृतिमन्तो मनीषिणः। तां तीर्णः सर्वतो मुक्तो विधृतात्माऽऽत्मविच्छुभिः॥
en: Only men endued with learning wisdom, and understanding succeed in crossing it which is so difficult to cross. Crossing it, you will free yourself from every attachment, acquiring a tranquil heart, knowing the Soul, and becoming pure in every way.

sn: उत्तमां बुद्धिमास्थाय ब्रह्मभूयान् भविष्यसि। संतीर्णः सर्वसंसारात् प्रसन्नात्मा विकल्मषः॥ भूमिष्ठानीव भूतानि पर्वतस्थो निशामया अक्रुध्यन्नप्रहष्यंश्च न नृशंसमतिस्तथा॥
en: Depending then on a purged and elevated understanding, you will succeed in becoming Brahma's self. Having estranged yourself from every worldly attachment, having acquired a purified Soul and conquering every sort of sin, look you upon the world like a person loO king from the mountain summit upon creatures creeping below on the Earth's surface! Without being subject to anger or joy, and without making any cruel wish, you will see the origin and the destruction of all created objects,

sn: ततो द्रक्ष्यसि सर्वेषां भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययौ। एनं वै सर्वभूतेभ्यो विशिष्टं मेनिरे बुधाः। धर्मं धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठा मुनयस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥
en: Wise men consider such an act to be the foremost of all things. Indeed, this act of crossing the river of life is considered by the foremost of pious persons, by ascetics conversant with the truth, to be the greatest of all acts that one can perform.

sn: आत्मनो व्यापिनो ज्ञानमिदं पुत्रानुशासनम्। प्रयताय प्रवक्तव्यं हितायानुगताय च॥
en: This knowledge of the all-pervading Soul should be delivered to one's son. It should be inculcated upto one who is of controlled Senses, who is honest in conduct, and. that is docile or submissive.

sn: आत्मज्ञानमिदं गुह्यं सर्वगुह्यतमं महत्। अब्रुवं यदहं तात आत्मसाक्षिकमञ्जसा॥
en: This knowledge of Soul, which I have just explained to you, O child, and the evidence of whose truth is supplied by the Soul itself, is, indeed, the greatest of all mysteries, and the very highest knowledge which one can acquire.

sn: नैव स्त्री न पुमानेतन्नैव चेदं नपुंसकम्। अदुःखमसुखं ब्रह्म भूतभव्यभवात्मकम्॥
en: Brahma has no sex,-inale, a female, or neuter. It is neither sorrow nor happiness. Its essence the past, the future, and the present.

sn: नैतज्ज्ञात्वा पुमान् स्त्री वा पुनर्भवमवाप्नुते। अभवप्रतिपत्त्यर्थमेतद् धर्मं विधीयते॥
en: Whatever the sex may be, male or female, the person who acquires the knowledge of Brahma hath never to go through re-births. This duty (of Yoga) has been described for acquiring Liberation from re-birth.

sn: यथा मतानि सर्वाणि तथैतानि यथा तथा। कथितानि मया पुत्र भवन्ति न भवन्ति च॥
en: These words which I have used for answering your question lead to Liberation in the same way as the various other opinions held by various other sages who have described this subject. I have explained the subject to you in the manner in which it should be explained. Those opinions sometimes yield fruit and sometimes not.

sn: तत्प्रीतियुक्तेन गुणान्वितेन पुत्रेण सत्पुत्र दमान्वितेना पृष्टो हि सम्प्रीतमना यथार्थ ब्रूयात्सुतस्येह यदुक्तमेतत्॥
en: Therefore, good child, when asked by a contented, meritorious, and self-controlled son or disciple, a preceptor should, with a delighted hcart, explain, according to their true import, these instructions which I have delivered for your benefit my son.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: व्यास उवाच गन्धान् रसान् नानुरुन्ध्यात्सुखं वा नालंकारांश्चाप्नुयात्तस्य तस्य। मानं च कीर्ति च यशश्च नेच्छेत्स वै प्रचारः पश्यतो ब्राह्मणस्य॥
en: Vyasa said One should not show any liking for scents and tastes and other sorts of enjoyment. Nor should one accept ornaments and other articles giving the enjoyment of the senses of scent and taste. One should not seek honour and achievements and fame. Even this is the conduct of a Brahmana endued with vision.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: सर्वान् वेदानधीयीत शुश्रूषुर्ब्रह्मचर्यवान्। ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि न तेन न स वै द्विजः॥
en: He who has mastered all the Vedas, having served dutifully his preceptor and practised the vow of celibacy, he who knows all the Richs, Yajushes, and Samans, is not a twice-born one.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: ज्ञातिवत् सर्वभूतानां सर्ववित् सर्ववेदवित्। नाकामो म्रियते जातु न तेन न च वै द्विजः॥
en: One who treats all creatures like his kinsman, and one who is acquainted with Brahma, is said to be the master of all the Vedas. One who is shorn of desire, never dies. It is by such a conduct and such a bent of mind that one becomes a truly twice-born one.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: इष्टीश्च विविधाः प्राप्य ऋतूंश्चैवाप्तदक्षिणान्। प्राप्नोति नैव ब्राह्मण्यमविधानात् कथंचन॥ कल्पते॥
en: Having performed only various sorts or religious rights and various sacrifices completed with sacrificial presents, one does not gain the dignity of a Brahmana if he is devoid of mercy and has not renounced desire.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: यदा चायं न बिभेति यदा चास्मान्न बिभ्यति। यदा नेच्छति न द्वेष्टि ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When one ceases to fear all creatures and when all creatures cease to fear him, when one never desires for anything nor entertains hatred for anything, then he is said to acquire the dignity of Brahma.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: यदा न कुरुते भावं सर्वभूतेषु पापकम्। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When one one abstains from injuring all creatures in thought, words, and acts, then he is said to acquire the dignity of Brahma.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: कामबन्धनमेवैकं नान्यदस्तीह बन्धनम्। कामबन्धनमुक्तो हि ब्रह्मभूयाय
en: There is only one kind of fetter in this world, viz., the chain of desire, and no other. One who is freed from the chain of desire acquires the dignity of Brahma.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: कामतो मुच्यमानस्तु धूम्राभ्रादिव चन्द्रमाः। विरजाः कालमाकाङ्क्षन् धीरो धैर्येण वर्तते।॥
en: Shorn of desire like the Moon emerged from clouds, the wise man, purged of all stains, live patiently expecting his time.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्। तद्वत् कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामः॥
en: That person into whose mind all sorts of desire enter like various rivers falling into the ocean without being able to increase its limits by their discharge, acquires equaniinity, but not he who cherishes desire for all worldly objects.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: स कामकान्तो न तु कामकाम: स वै कामात्स्वर्गमुपैति देही॥
en: Such a person becomes happy for the fruition of all his wishes, and not he who entertains desire for worldly objects. The latter, even if he acquires heaven, has to fall away from it.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: वेदस्योपनिषत् सत्यं सत्यस्यापनिषद् दमः। दमस्योपनिषद् दानं दानस्योपनिषत् तपः॥
en: The Vedas have truth for their object. Truth has the mastering of the senses for its object. The subjugation of the senses has charity for its object. Charity has penance for its object.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: तपसोपनिषत् त्यागस्त्यागस्योपनिषत् सुखम्। सुखस्योपनिषत् स्वर्गः स्वर्गसयोपनिषच्छमः॥
en: Penance has renunciation for its recondite object. Renunciation has happiness for its object. Happiness has heaven for its object. Heaven has tranquillity for its object.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: क्लेदनं शोकमनसो संतापं तृष्णया सह। सत्त्वमिच्छसि संतोषाच्छान्तिलक्षणमुत्तमम्॥
en: For the sake of contentment you should desire to acquire a serene understanding which is a valuable possession, indicating Liberation, and which, scorching sorrow and all objects or doubts together with thirst, destroys them entirely in the long run.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: विशोको निर्ममः शान्तः प्रसन्नात्मा विमत्सरः। षड्भिर्लक्षणवानेतैः समग्रः पुनरेष्यति॥
en: One endued with those six qualities, viz., contentment, sorrowlessness, freedom from fetters, peacefulness, cheerfulness, and freedom from envy, is sure to become full or complete.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: षभिः सत्त्वगुणोपेतैः प्राज्ञैरधिगतं त्रिंभिः। ये विदुः प्रेत्य चात्मानमिहस्थं तं गुणं विदुः॥
en: They who, transcending all consciousness of body, know the Soul which lives within the body and which is understood by only wise persons with the help of the six entities when endowed with only the quality of goodness, and with the help also of the other three, succeed in attaining to Liberation.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: अकृत्रिममसंहार्यं प्राकृतं निरुपस्कृतम्। अध्यात्म सुकृतं प्राप्तः सुखमव्ययमश्नुते॥
en: The wise man enjoys endless beatitude by understanding the Soul which reigns within the body, which is shorn of the attributes of birth and death, which exists in its own true nature, which being uninvested with attributes requires no acts of purification, and which is identical with Brahma.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: निष्प्रचारं मनः कृत्वा प्रतिष्ठाप्य च सर्वशः। यामयं लभते तुष्टिं सा न शक्याऽऽत्मनोऽन्यथा॥
en: The pleasure which a man enjoys by governing his mind from roving in all directions and fixing it entirely on the Soul is such that its like cannot be acquired by one through any other means.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: येन तृप्यत्यभुञ्जानो येन तृप्यत्यवित्तवान्। येनोस्नेहो बलं धत्ते यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्॥
en: He is said to be a qualified master of the Vedas who is conversant with what gratifies one whose stomach is empty, which pleases one who is angry, and which invigorates one whose limbs are dry.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: संगुप्तान्यात्मनो द्वाराण्यपिधाय विचिन्तयन्। यो ह्यास्ते ब्राह्मणः शिष्टः स आत्मरतिरुच्यते॥
en: Suspending his senses that have been properly checked from unworthy indulgence, he who lives in Yoga meditation, is said to be a Brahma. Such a person is said to acquire his joys from the Soul.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: समाहितं परे तत्त्वे क्षीणकाममवस्थितम्। सर्वतः सुखमन्वेति वपुश्चान्द्रमसं यथा॥
en: Regarding one who lives after having destroyed desire and devoting himself to the highest subject of existence, it should be said that his happiness is continuously increased like the lunar disc.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: अविशेषाणि भूतानि गुणांश्च जहतो मुनेः। सुखेनापोह्यते दुःखं भास्करेण तमो यथा॥
en: Like the Sun removing darkness, happiness removes the sorrows of that Yogin who gets over both the gross and the subtile elements, as also the intellectual principle and the Unmanifest.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: मुक्तः समः तमतिक्रान्तकर्माणमतिक्रान्तगुणक्षयम्। ब्राह्मणं विषयाश्लिष्टं जरामृत्यू न विन्दतः॥
en: Decrepitude and death cannot attack that Brahma who has got beyond the sphere of acts, who has gone the destruction of the qualities themselves, and who is no longer attached to earthly objects.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: स यदा सर्वतो पर्यवतिष्ठते। इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थाश्च शरीरस्थोऽतिवर्तते॥
en: Indeed, when freed from everything, the Yogin, lives in a state transcending both attachment and hatred, he is said to be, even ill this life, above his senses and all their objects.

description: The account of a true Yogin
sn: कारणं परमं प्राप्य अतिक्रान्तस्य कार्यताम्। पुनरावर्तनं नास्ति सम्प्राप्तस्य परं पदम्॥
en: That Yogin, who having gone above Prakriti attains to the Highest Cause, becomes freed from the obligation of a re-birth on account of his having attained 10 that which is the highest.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: व्यास उवाच द्वन्द्वानि मोक्षजिज्ञासुरर्थधर्मावनुष्ठितः। वक्त्रा गुणवता शिष्यः श्राव्यः पूर्वमिदं महत्॥
en: Vyasa said A qualified preceptor should, first of all, describe the most capacious subject of spirituality, that has been explained in the previous chapter, to a disciple who wishes to enquire after Liberation after having transcended all pairs of opposites and performed the concerns of both profit and religion.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: आकाशं मारुतो ज्योतिरापः पृथ्वी च पञ्चमी। भावाभावौ च कालश्च सर्वभूतेषु पञ्चसु॥
en: Ether, wind, light, water, and earth as the fifth, and existence and non-existence and time, exist in all living creatures having the five for their component ingredients.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: अन्तरात्मकमाकाशं तन्मयं श्रोत्रमिन्द्रियम्। तस्य शब्दं गुणं विद्यान्मूर्तिशास्त्रविधानवित्॥
en: Space is unoccupied interstice. The organs of hearing consist of space. One knowing the science of elements endued with form should know that ether has sound for its attribute.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: चरणं मारुतोत्मेति प्राणापानौ च तन्मयौ। स्पर्शनं चेन्द्रियं विद्यात् तथा स्पर्श च तन्मयम्॥
en: Wind is essence of the feet. The vital airs are made of wind. Wind is the essence of the sense of touch, and touch is the attribute of wind.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: ताप: पाकः प्रकाशश्च ज्योतिश्चक्षुश्च पञ्चमम्। तस्य रूपं गुणं विद्यात् ताम्रगौरासितात्मकम्॥
en: Heat, the digestive fire in the stomach, light that manifests all things, the heat of the body, and eye as the fifth, are all of light which has forin of various colours for its attribute.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: प्रक्लेदः क्षुद्रता स्नेह इत्यपामुपदिश्यते। असृङ्मज्जा च यच्चान्यत् स्निग्धं विद्यात् तदात्मकम्॥६
en: Solubility, and all kinds of liquid matter partake of water. Blood, marrow, and all else that is cool, have water for their essence. The longue is the sense of taste, and taste is known as the attribute of water

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: रसनं चेन्द्रियं जिह्वा रसश्चापां गुणो मतः। संघातः पार्थिवो धातुरस्थिदन्तनखानि च।॥
en: All solid substances partake of earth, as also bones, teeth, nails, beard, the hairs on the body, hair, nerves, sinews, and skin.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: श्मश्रु रोम च केशाश्च शिरा स्नायु च चर्म च। इन्द्रियं घ्राणसंज्ञातं नासिकेत्यभिसंज्ञिता॥
en: The nose is known as the organ of smell. The object of that senses, viz., scent, is known as the attribuite of earth.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: गन्धश्चेवेन्द्रियार्थोऽयं विज्ञेयः पृथिवीमयः। उत्तरेषु गुणाः सन्ति सर्वसत्त्वेषु चोत्तराः॥ पञ्चानां भूतसंघानां संततिं मुनयो विदुः।
en: Each subsequent element partakes of the attribute or attributes of the preceding one in addition to its own. The (three) supplementary entities exist in all living creatures. The Rishis thus described the five elements and the effects and qualities emanating from or belonging to them.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: मनो नवममेषां तु बुद्धिस्तु दशमी स्मृता॥ एकादशस्त्वनन्तात्मा स सर्वः पर उच्यते।
en: The mind is the ninth, and the understanding is the tenth. The Soul, which is infinite, is the eleventh. It is considered as the highest of all.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिर्मनो व्याकरणात्मकम्। कर्मानुमानाद् विज्ञेयः स जीवः क्षेत्रसंज्ञकः॥
en: The mind has doubt or its essence. The understanding discriminates and produces certainty. The Soul becomes known as Jiva or individual soul when invested with body through the consequences of acts.

description: The subject of spirituality; the formation of elements
sn: एभिः कालात्मकैर्भावैर्यः सर्वैः सर्वमन्वितम्। पश्यत्यकलुषं कर्म स मोहं नानुवर्तते॥
en: That man who regards all living creatures as unsullied though endued with all these entities having time for their essence, has never to perform acts moved on by error.

sn: व्यास उवाच शरीराद् विप्रमुक्तं हि सूक्ष्मभूत शरीरिणम्। कर्मभिः परिपश्यन्ति शास्त्रोक्तैः शास्त्रवेदिनः॥
en: Vyasa said Those who are well-read in the scriptures see, with the help of acts laid down in the scriptures, the Soul which is encased in a subtile body and is highly subtile and which is dissociated from the gross body in which it lives.

sn: यथा मरीच्यः सहिताश्चरन्ति सर्वत्र तिष्ठन्ति च दृश्यमानाः। स्तथैव सत्त्वान्यतिमानुषाणि॥
en: As the rays of the Sun which move in dense masses through every part of the sky, cannot be seen by the naked eye though their existence can be perceived by reason, likewise, existent beings freed from gross bodies and moving in universe are above the reach of human vision,

sn: प्रतिरूपं यथैवाप्सु तापः सूर्यस्य लक्ष्यते। सत्त्ववत्सु तथा सत्त्वं प्रतिरूपं स पश्यति॥
en: As the shining solar disc is seen reflected in the reflected water so the Yogin sees reflected within gross bodies the existent self.

sn: तानि सूक्ष्माणि सत्त्वानि विमुक्तानि शरीरतः। स्वेन सत्त्वेन सत्त्वज्ञाः पश्यन्ति नियतेन्द्रियः॥
en: All those souls again that are encased in subtile forins after being alienated from the gross bodies in which they lived, are perceptible to Yogins, who have controlled their senses and who are gifted with knowledge of the soul. Indeed, helped by their own souls, Yogins see those invisible beings,

sn: स्वपतां जाग्रतां चैव सर्वेषामात्मचिन्तितम्। प्रधानाद्वैधमुक्तानां जहतां कर्मजं रजः॥ यथाहनि तथा रात्रौ यथा रात्रौ तथाहनि। वशे तिष्ठति सत्त्वात्मा सततं योगयोगिनाम्॥
en: Whether asleep or awake, during the day or in the night, and during the night or in the day, they who practise Yoga after renouncing all the creations of the understanding the passion engendered by acts, and the power which Yoga begets, succeed in keeping their subtile form under complete control.

sn: तेषां नित्यं सदा नित्यो भूतात्मा सततं गुणैः। सप्तभिस्त्वन्वितः सूक्ष्मैश्चरिष्णुरजरामरः॥
en: The individual soul which lives in such Yogins, always endued with the seven subtile principles, moves in all blissful regions, freed from decrepitude and death. I say “always,' and 'freed from death, as in common parlance, for, in sooth, that subtile form is also terininable.

sn: मनोबुद्धिपराभूतः स्वदेहपरदेहवित्। स्वप्नेष्वपि भवत्येष विज्ञाता सुखदुःखयोः॥
en: That man, however, who is under the influence of his mind and understanding, differentiates, even in his dreams, his own body from that of another and experiences both pleasure and pain.

sn: तत्रापि लभते दुःखं तत्रापि लभते सुखम्। क्रोधलोभौ तु तत्रापि कृत्वा व्यसनमृच्छति॥
en: Really, even in his dreams he enjoys happiness and suffers misery; and yielding to anger and cupidity, suffers all sorts of calamities.

sn: प्रीणितश्चापि भवति महतोऽर्थानवाप्य हि। करोति पुप्यं तत्रापि जीवन्निव च पश्यति॥
en: In his dreams he acquires great riches and feels highly satisfied: performs meritorious acts, and sees as he does when he is awake.

sn: महोष्मान्तर्गतश्चापि गर्भत्वं समुपेयिवान्। दश मासान् वसन् कुक्षौ नैषोऽन्नमिव जीर्यते॥
en: It is wonderful to mark that individual soul which has to lie within the uterus and amid much internal heat, and which has to pass there full ten months, is not digested and destroyed like food within the stomach.

sn: तमेतमतितेजोऽशं भूतात्मानं हृदि स्थितम्। तमोरजोभ्यामाविष्टा नानुपश्यन्ति मूर्तिषु॥
en: Men possessed by the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance never succeed in sceing within the gross body the sentiency which is a portion of the Supreme Soul to transcendent effulgence and which lies within the heart of every creature.

sn: योगशास्त्रपरा भूत्वा तमात्मानं परीप्सवः। अनुच्छ्वासान्यमूर्तानि यानि वज्रोपमान्यपि॥
en: They who learn Yoga for the purpose of obtaining a knowledge of Self succeed in getting over the inanimate and gross body, the imperceptible subtile body, and the casual body which is not destroyed on the occasion of even the universal destruction.

sn: पृथग्भूतेषु सृष्टेषु चतुर्थाश्रमकर्मसु। समाधौ योगमेवैतच्छाण्डिल्यः शममब्रवीत्॥
en: Of the duties laid down for the various modes of life including the fourth mode, these which I have described, which have Yoga for their foremost, and which indicate a complete stoppage of all operations of the Mind and the Understanding, have been laid down by Shandilya.

sn: विदित्वा सप्त सूक्ष्माणि षडङ्गं च महेश्वरम्। प्रधानविनियोगज्ञः परं ब्रह्मानुपश्यति॥
en: Having comprehended the seven subtile principles, having comprehended also the Supreme Cause of the universe with the six attributes, and lastly having understood that the universe so only a modification of nescience endued with the three qualities, one succeeds in seeing high Brahina,

sn: व्यास उवाच हृदि कामद्रुमश्चित्रो मोहसंचयसम्भवः। क्रोधमानमहास्कन्धो विधित्सापरिषेचनः॥
en: Vyasa said There is a wonderful tree in the heart of man, called Desire. It is born of the seed called Error. Anger and Pride from its large trunk. The desire for work is the hollow ground around its foot.

sn: तस्य चाज्ञानमाधारः प्रमादः परिषेचनम्। सोऽभ्यसूयापलाशो हि पुरा दुष्कृतसारवान्॥
en: Ignorance is the root of that tree, and carelessness is the water which nourishes it. Envy forms its leaves. The evil acts of pristine lives supply it with vigour.

sn: सम्मोहचिन्ताविटपः शोकशाखो भयाङ्कुर। मोहनीभिः पिपासाभिलताभिरनुवेष्टितः॥
en: Loss of judgement and anxiety are its twigs; grief forms its huge branches; and fear it is sprout. Thirst which seems agreeable, forms the creepers which twine round it on all sides.

sn: उपासते महावृक्षं सुलुब्धास्तत्फलेप्सवः। आयसैः संयुताः पाशैः फलदं परिवेष्ट्य तम्॥
en: Avaricious men, fettered in chains of iron, sitting around that fruit-producing tree, worship it, in expectation of its fruit.

sn: यस्तान् पाशान् वशे कृत्वा तं वक्षमपकर्षति। गतः स दुःखयोरन्तं जरामरणयोर्द्वयोः।
en: He who, subduing those chains, cuts down that tree and seeks to renounce both sorrow and joy, succeeds in attaining to the end of both.

sn: संरोहत्यकृतप्रज्ञः सदा येन हि पादपम्। स तमेव ततो हन्ति विषग्रन्थिरिवातुरम्॥
en: That foolish wight who nourishes this tree by enjoying the objects of the senses is destroyed by those very objects like a poisonous pill destroying the patient to whom it is given.

sn: तस्यानुगतमूलस्य मूलमुध्रियते बलात्। योगप्रसादात् कृतिना साम्येन परमासिना॥
en: However, by the help of Yoga, a clever man forcibly cuts off with the sword of concentration, the far-reaching root of this tree.

sn: एवं यो वेद कामस्य केवलस्य निवर्तनम्। बन्धं वै कामशास्त्रस्य स दुःखान्यतिवर्तते॥
en: One who understands that the end of all acts performed from the desire of fruit is rebirth or chains that bind, succeeds in getting over all sorrow.

sn: शरीरं पुरमित्याहुः स्वामिनी बुद्धिरिष्यते। तत्त्वबुद्धेः शरीरस्थं मनो नामाथचिन्तकम्॥
en: The body is compared to a city. The understanding is its mistress. The mind living within the body is the minister of that mistress whose chief duty is to decide.

sn: इन्द्रियाणि मन:पौरास्तदर्थं तु पराकृतिः। तत्र द्वौ दारुणौ दोषौ तमो नाम रजस्तथा।
en: The senses are the citizens who are employed by the mind. For maintaining those citizens the mind shows a strong inclination for various sorts of acts. Two great faults are seen in those acts, namely, Darkness and ignorance.

sn: तदर्थमुपजीवन्ति पौराः सह पुरेश्वरैः॥ अद्वारेण तमेवार्थं द्वौ दोषावुपजीवतः।
en: Upon the fruits of those acts depend those citizens along with the chiefs of the city. The two faults live upon the fruits of those acts which are done by forbidden means.

sn: तत्र बुद्धिर्हि दुर्धर्षा मनः सामान्यमश्नुते॥ पौराश्चापि मनस्त्रस्तास्तेषामपि चला स्थितिः।
en: Such being the case, the understanding, which of itself is unconquerable, goes down to a state of equality with the mind. Then again the senses, moved by the stained mind, lose their own firmness.

sn: तदर्थं बुद्धिरध्यास्ते सोऽनर्थः परिषीदति॥ यदर्थं पृथगध्यास्ते मनस्तत्परिषीदति।
en: Those objects again to acquire which the understanding tries, tries, produce grief and ultimately meet with destruction. Those objects, after destruction, are remembered by the mind, and accordingly they afflict the mind even after they are lost.

sn: पृथग्भूतं मनो बुद्धया मनो भवति केवलम्॥ तत्रैनं विधृतं शून्यं रजः पर्यवतिष्ठते।
en: The understanding is also afflicted, for the mind is said to be different from the understanding only when the mind is viewed regarding its chief function of getting impressions about whose certainty it is no judge. In sooth, however, the mind is identical with the understanding. The quality of Darkness which is in the understanding then overwhelms the Soul itself that lies over that understanding sullied by Darkness like an image upon a mirror.

sn: तन्मनः कुरुते सख्यं रजसा सह सङ्गतम्। चादाय जनं पौरं रजसे सम्प्रयच्छति॥
en: It is the mind that first becomes united with darkness. Having united itself, it attacks the soul, the understanding, and the senses, and surrenders them to Rajas."

sn: भीष्म उवाच भूतानां परिसंख्यानं भूयः पुत्र निशामय। द्वैपायनमुखाद् भ्रष्टं श्लाघया परयानघ॥ दीप्तानलनिभः प्राह भगवान् धूमवर्चसे। ततोऽहमपि वक्ष्यामि भूयः पुत्र निदर्शनम्॥
en: Bhishma said Do you, O son, O sinless one, listen once more, with feeling of great pride, to the words given vent to by the Island-born Rishi on the subject of the enumeration of the principles. Like a blazing fire, the great Rishi said these words to his son who took after a fire wrapped in smoke. Instructed by what he said, I also, O son, shall again explain to you that certain knowledge.

sn: भूमेः स्थैर्यं गुरुत्वं च काठिन्यं प्रसवार्थता। गन्धो गुरुत्वं शक्तिश्च संघातः स्थापना धृतिः॥
en: The properties of earth are immobility, weight, hardness, productiveness, scent, density, capacity to absorb all sorts of scents, cohesion, habitableness, and that attribute of the mind which is called patience.

sn: अपां शैत्यं रसः क्लेदो द्रवत्वं स्नेहसौम्यता। जिह्वा विस्यन्दनं चापि भौमानां श्रपणं तथा॥
en: The properties of water are coolness, taste, moisture, liquidity, softness, agreeableness, tongue, fluidity, capacity to the congealed, and power to melt all earthy products.

sn: अग्नेर्दुर्धर्षता ज्योतिस्ताप: पाकः प्रकाशनम्। शोको रागो लघुस्तैक्ष्ण्यं सततं चोर्ध्वभासिता॥
en: The properties of fire are irresistible energy, inflammability, heat, capacity to soften, light, sorrow, disease, speed, fury, and upward motion.

sn: वायोरनियमस्पर्शी वादस्थानं स्वतन्त्रता। बलं शैघ्यं च मोक्षं च कर्म चेष्टाऽऽत्मता भवः॥
en: The properties of the wind are touch that is neither hot nor cool, power to help the organs of speech, independence, strength, celerity, power to help all kinds of discharge, power to raise other objects, breaths inhaled and exhaled, life, and birth.

sn: आकाशस्य गुणः शब्दो व्यापित्वं च्छिद्रतापि च। अनाश्रयमनालम्बमव्यक्तमविकारिता॥ अप्रतीघातिता चैव भूतत्वं विकृतानि च। गुणा: पञ्चाशतं प्रोक्ताः पञ्चभूतात्मभाविताः॥
en: The properties of space are sound, extension, capacity of being enclosed, absence of refuge, power of being unmanifest, capacity for modification, incapacity for resistance, material cause for producing the sense of hearing, and the unoccupied parts of the human body. These are the fifty properties, as declared, which form the essences of the five elementary entities.

sn: धैर्योपपत्तिर्व्यक्तिश्च विसर्गः कल्पना क्षमा। सदसच्चाशुता चैव मनसो नव वै गुणाः॥
en: Patience, reasoning, remembrance, forgetfulness or error, imagination, endurance, inclination towards good, inclination towards evil, and restlessness,-are the properties of the mind.

sn: इष्टानिष्टविपत्तिश्च व्यवसाय: समाधिता। संशयः प्रतिपत्तिश्च बुद्धेः पञ्चगुणान् विदुः।१०।।
en: Destruction of both good and evil thoughts, perseverance, concentration, decision, and ascertainment of all things depending upon direct evidence, form the five properties of the understanding.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं पञ्चगुणा बुद्धिः कथं पञ्चेन्द्रिया गुणाः। एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व सूक्ष्मज्ञानं पितामह॥
en: Yudhisthira said How can the understanding be said to have five properties? How again, can the five senses be described as properties. Explain to me, O grandfather, all this abstruse topic.

sn: भीष्म उवाच आहुः षष्टिं बुद्धिगुणान्वै भूतविशिष्टा नित्यविषक्ताः। भूतविभूतीश्चाक्षरसृष्टाः पुत्र न नित्यं तदिह वदन्ति॥
en: Bhishma said The understanding is said to possess altogether sixty properties, for the understanding includes the five clements. All those properties exist in the Soul. The Vedas say, O son, that the elements, their properties, are all created by Him who is above all decay. These entities, therefore, are not eternal.

sn: तत्पुत्र चिन्ताकलिलं तदुक्तमनागतं वै तव सम्प्रतीह। भूतार्थतत्त्वं तदवाप्य सर्वं भूतप्रभावाद् भव शान्तबुद्धिः।।
en: The theories contradicting the Revelation which have in the previous Verses, O son, been placed before you, are all defective in the eye of reason. Minding, however, in this world all that I have said to you about the Supreme Brahma, do you after acquiring the power which the knowledge of Brahma offers, seek to acquire tranquillity of heart.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच य इमे पृथिवीपाला: शेरते पृथिवीतले। पृतनामध्य एते हि गतसंज्ञा महाबलाः॥
en: Yudhisthira said These kings who lie on the Earth's surface amid their respective armies, these princes of great power, are now all deprived of life.

sn: एकैकशो भीमबला नागायुतबलास्तथा। एते हि निहताः संख्ये तुल्यतेजोबलैनरैः॥
en: Every one of these powerful kings was endued with strength equal to that of ten thousand elephants. Alas! these have all have killed by men equally powerful and strong.

sn: नैषां पश्यामि हन्तारं प्राणिनां संयुगे परम्। विक्रमेणोपसम्पन्नास्तेजोबलसमन्विताः॥
en: I do not see any one else that could kill any of these men in battle. All of them were gifted with great prowess, great energy, and great strength.

sn: अथ चेमे महाप्राज्ञाः शेरते हि गतासवः। मृता इति च शब्दोऽयं वर्तत्येषु गतासुषु॥
en: Highly wise, they are now lying dead on the naked earth. about them, however, that are deprived of life, the word that is used is that they are dead.

sn: इमे मृता नृपतयः प्रायशो भीमविक्रमाः। तत्र मे संशयो जातः कुतः संज्ञा मृता इति॥
en: All these highly powerful kings are said to be dead. On this subject a doubt lies in my mind. Whence is life and whence is death.

sn: कस्य मृत्युः कुतो मृत्युः केन मृत्युरिह प्रजाः। हरत्यमरसंकाश तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Who is it that dies? whence is death? Whence is death? Why does death take away living creatures. O grandfather, tell me this, O you who are like a god.

sn: भीष्म उवाच पुरा कृतयुगे तात राजा ह्यासीदकम्पनः। स शत्रुवशमापन्नः संग्रामे क्षीणवाहनः॥
en: Bhishma said In days of yore, in the Krita age, O son, there was a king of the name of Anukampaka. His cars, elephants, horse and men having been reduced in number, he succumbed to the power of his enemies in battle.

sn: तस्य पुत्रो हरि म नारायणसमो बले। स शत्रुभिर्हतः संख्ये सबलः सपदानुगः॥
en: His son, named Hari, who was like Narayana himself in strength, was in that battle killed by his enemies along with all his followers and troops.

sn: स राजा शत्रुवशगः पुत्रशोकसमन्वितः। यदृच्छया शान्तिपरो ददर्श भुवि नारदम्॥
en: Stricken with grief consequent on the death of his son, and himself brought under the control of enemies, the king devoted himself thence to a life of peacefulness. One day, while wandering listlessly he met the sage Narada on the Earth.

sn: तस्मै स सर्वमाचष्ट यथावृत्तं जनेश्वरः। शत्रुाभिर्ग्रहणं संख्ये पुत्रस्य मरणं तथा॥
en: The king told Narada all that had taken place, viz., the death of his son in battle and his own capture by his enemies.

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा नारदोऽथ तपोधनः आख्यानमिदमाचष्ट पुत्रशोकापहं तदा॥
en: Having heard him Narada, endued with wealth of penances, then recited to him the following narrative for removing his grief consequent on the death of his son.

sn: नारद उवाच राजशृणु समाख्यानमद्येदं बहुविस्तरम्। यथावृत्तं श्रुतं चैव मयेदं वसुधाधिप॥
en: Narada said Listen now, O king, to the following long narrative which had taken place. I myself heard it formerly, O king!

sn: प्रजाः सृष्टाः महातेजाः प्रसार्गे पितामहः। अतीव वृद्धा बहुला नामृष्यत पुनः प्रजाः॥
en: Endued with great energy, the Grandfather, at the time of the creation of the universe, created a large number of living beings. These multiplied greatly, and none of them died.

sn: न ह्यन्तरमभूत् किञ्चित् क्वचिज्जन्तुभिरच्युत। निरुच्छ्वासमिवोन्नद्धं त्रैलोक्यमभवन्नृप॥
en: There was not a part of the universe which was not overcrowded with living creatures, O you of great glory! Indeed, O king, the three worlds appeared to swell with living beings, and became, as it were, breathless.

sn: तस्य चिन्ता समुत्पन्ना संहारं प्रति भूपते। चिन्तयन् नाध्यगच्छच्च संहारे हेतुकारणम्॥
en: Then, O king, the Grandfather thought as to how he should destroy the surplus population. Thinking of the matter, the Self-create, however, could not decide by what means the destruction of life was to be performed.

sn: तस्य रोषान्महाराज खेभ्योऽग्निरुदतिष्ठत। तेन सर्वा दिशो राजन् ददाह स पितामहः॥
en: Thereupon, O king, Brahman gave way to anger and in consequence of his anger a fire issued out of his body. With that fire born of his anger, the Grandfather burnt all the quarters of the universe, O king.

sn: ततो दिवं भुवं खं च जगच्च सचराचरम्। ददाह पावको राजन् भगवत्कोपसम्भवः॥
en: Indeed, that fire begotten of the Divine Lord's anger, O king, burnt Heaven and Earth and the Sky and the whole Universe with all its mobile and immobile beings.

sn: तत्रादह्यन्त भूतानि जङ्गमानि ध्रुवाणि च। महता क्रोधवेगेन कुपिते प्रपितामहे॥
en: Truly, when the Grandfather thus became angry, all mobile and immobile beings began to be consumed by the irresistible power of that anger.

sn: ततोऽध्वरजटः स्थाणुर्वेदाध्वरपतिः शिवः। जगाम शरणं देवो ब्रह्माणं परवीरहा।॥
en: Then the divine and sacred Sthanu, that destroyer of hostile heroes, that lord of the Vedas and the scriptures, filled with pity, tried to please Brahma.

sn: तस्मिन्नभिगते स्थाणौ प्रजानां हितकाम्यया। अब्रवीत् परमो देवो ज्वलन्निव तदा शिवम्॥ करवाण्यद्य कं काम वरा.ऽसि मतो मम। कर्ता ह्यस्मि प्रियं शम्भो तव यद्धदि वर्तते॥
en: When Sthanu came to Brahma out of feelings of benevolence, the great God addressed him, saying,-you deserved boons at my hands! What desire of yours shall I fulfil? I shall do you good by doing whatever you wish.

sn: स्थाणुरुवाच पजासर्गनिमित्तं मे कार्यवत्तामिमां प्रभो। विद्धि सृष्टास्त्वया हीमा मा कुप्यासां पितामह॥
en: Sthanu said Know, O lord, that my prayer to you is in behalf of the created beings of the universe! These beings have been created by you. Do not be angry with them, O Grandfather.

sn: तव तेजोऽग्निना देव प्रजा दह्यन्ति सर्वशः। ता दृष्ट्वा मम कारुण्यं मा कुष्यासां जगत्प्रभो॥
en: By the fire born of your anger, illustrious one, all the created beings are being burnt. Seeing them placed in such a condition, I am filled with compassion. Do not be angry with them, O maker of the universe.

sn: प्रजापतिरुवाच न कुप्ये न च मे कामो न भवेयुः प्रजा इति। लाघवार्थं धरण्यास्तु ततः संहार इष्यते॥
en: The lord of all created beings said, I am not angry, nor is it my desire that all the create beings should perish. It is only for lightening the lord of the Earth that destruction is desirable.

sn: इयं हि मां सदा देवी भारार्ता समचोदयत्। संहारार्थं महादेव भारेणाप्सु निमज्जति॥
en: The godess Earth, suffering from the load of creatures, requested me, O Mahadeva, for destroying them, especially as she appeared to sink under their load into the water.

sn: यदाहं नाधिगच्छामि बुद्ध्या बहु विचारयन्। संहारमासां वृद्धानां ततो मां क्रोध आविशत्॥
en: When after exercising my intelligence even for a long time I could not find out the means by which to bring about the destruction of this overgrown population, it was then that I was possessed by ire.

sn: स्थाणुरुवाच संहारार्थं प्रसीदस्व मा क्रुधो विबुधेश्वर। मा प्रजाः स्थावरं चैव जङ्गमं च व्यनीनशत्॥
en: Do not give way to anger, O lord of the celestials, about the destruction of living creatures! Be-pleased! Let not these mobile and immobile beings be destroyed.

sn: पल्वलानि च सर्वाणि सर्वं चैव तृणोपलम्। स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव भूतग्रामं चतुर्विधम्॥ तदेतद् भस्मसाद्भूतं जगत् सर्वमुपल्लुतम्। प्रसीद भगवन् साधो वर एष वृतो मया॥
en: All tanks, all sorts of grass and herbs, all immobile beings, and all the four divisions of mobile creatures, are being consumed. The whole universe is about to be shorn of beings. Be pleased, O divine Lord! O you of pious soul this is the boon that I seek at your hands.

sn: नष्टा न पुनरेष्यन्ति प्रजा ह्येताः कथंचन। तस्मानिवर्ततामेतत् तेन स्वेनैव तेजसा॥
en: If destroyed, these creatures would not return. Therefore, let this energy of yours be neutralised by your own energy.

sn: उपायमन्यं सम्पश्य भूतानां हितकाम्यया। यथामी जन्तवः सर्वे न दोरन् पितामह॥ अभावं हि न गच्छेयुरुच्छिन्नप्रजनाः प्रजाः। अधिदैवे नियुक्तोऽस्मि त्वया लोकेश्वरेश्वर॥
en: Moved by pity for all created beings, find some means so that, O Grandfather, these living creatures may not be consumed! Oh, let not these living creatures die with even their descendants thus destroyed! You have appointed me to preside over the consciousness of all living creatures, O Lord of all the lords of the universe.

sn: त्वद्भवं हि जगन्नाथ एतत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्। प्रसाद्य त्वां महादेव याचाम्यावृत्ति जाः प्रजाः॥
en: All this inobile and immobile creatures, O lord of the universe, originated from you. Pacifying you, O god of gods, I beg of you that living creatures may repeatedly come back into the world, undergoing repeated deaths!

sn: नारद उवाच श्रुत्वा तु वचनं देवः स्थाणोनियतवाङ्मनाः। तेजस्तत् संनिजग्राह पुनरेवान्तरात्मनि॥
en: Narada continued Hearing these words of Sthanu, the divine Brahma of controlled speech and mind himself suppressed that energy of his within his own heart.

sn: ततोऽग्निमुपसंगृह्य भगवाँल्लोकपूजितः। प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कल्पयामास वै प्रभुः॥
en: Suppressing that fire that had been destroying the universe, the illustrious Brahma, worshipped of all, and endued with illimitable power, then arranged for both birth and death of all living creatures.

sn: उपसंहरतस्तस्य तमग्नि रोषजं तदा। प्रादुर्बभूव विश्वेभ्यः खेभ्यो नारी महात्मनः॥ कृष्णरक्ताम्बरधरा कृष्णनेत्रतलान्तरा। दिव्यकुण्डलसम्पन्ना दिव्याभरणभूषिता॥
en: After the Self-create had withdrawn and suppressed that fire, there came out, from all the pores of his body, a lady dressed in robes of black and red, with black eyes, black palms, wearing a pair of charming ear-rings and bedecked with celestial ornaments.

sn: सा विनिःसृत्य वै खेभ्यो दक्षिणामाश्रिता दिशम्। ददृशाते च तां कन्यां देवौ विश्वेश्वरावुभौ॥
en: Having originated from Brahman's body, the lady sat on his right. The two foremost of gods thereupon espied her.

sn: तामाहूय तदा देवो लोकानामादिरीश्वरः। मृत्यो इति महीपाल जहि चेमाः प्रजा इति॥
en: Then, O king, the powerful Self-create, the prime Cause of all the worlds, saluted her and said, O Death, kill these creatures of the universe.

sn: त्वं हि संहारबुद्ध्या मे चिन्तिता रुषितेन च। तस्मात् संहर सर्वांस्त्वं प्रजाः सजडपण्डिताः॥
en: Filled with ire and resolved to encompass the destruction of created beings, I have called you. Do you, there, begin to destroy all creatures foolish or learned.

sn: अविशेषेण चैव त्वं प्रजाः संहर कामिनि। मम त्वं हि नियोगेन श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: O lady, kill all created beings without any exception. At my command you will acquire great prosperity.

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी मृत्युः कमलमालिनी। प्रदध्यौ दुःखिता बाला साश्रुपातमतीव॥
en: Thus addressed, the the goddess Death, adorned with a garland of lotuses, began to think sorrowfully and shed profuse tears.

sn: पाणिभ्यां चैव जग्राह तान्यश्रूणि जनेश्वरः। मानवानां हितार्थाय ययाचे पुनरेव ह॥
en: Without suffering her tears, however, to fall down, she held them, O king, in her joinedhands. She then solicited the Self-born, moved by the desire of doing good to mankind.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: नारद उवाच विनीय दुःखमबला साऽऽत्मनैवायतेक्षणा। उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा लतेवावर्जिता तदा॥
en: Narada said The lady having large eyes, controlling her grief by self-exertion, addressed the Grandfather, with joined hands and bending low like a creeper.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: त्वया सृष्टा कथं नारी मादृशी वदतां वर। रौद्रकर्माभिजायेत सर्वप्राणिभयङ्करी॥
en: And she said, How, O foremost of speakers, shall a lady like me who has sprung from you proceed to perform such a terrible feat-a feat, which is sure to terrorize all living creatures.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: विभेम्यहमधर्मस्य धर्नामादिश कर्म मे। त्वं मां भीतामवेक्षस्व शिवेनेक्षस्व चक्षुषा॥
en: I fear to do any thing that is iniquitious! Do you find out a holy work for me. You see that I am frightened. Oh, look upon me mercifully.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: बालान् वृद्धान् वयस्थांश्च न हरेयमनागसः। प्राणिनः प्राणिनामीश नमस्तेऽस्तु प्रसीद मे॥
en: I shall not be able to cut off living creatures,-infants, youths, and elderly ones,-who have done me no injury! O lord of all creatures, I bow to you, be pleased with me.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: प्रियान् पुत्रान् वयस्यांश्च भ्रातृन् मातृः पितृनपि। अपध्यास्यन्ति यद्येवं मृतास्तेषां बिभेम्यहम्॥
en: I shall not be able to cut off dear sons, loved friends and brothers and mothers and fathers! If these perish their surviving relatives will surely curse me. Thinking of this I am filled with fear.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: कृपणाश्रुपरिक्लेदो देहन्मां शाश्वतीः समाः। तेभ्योऽहं बलवद् भीता शरणं त्वामुपागता॥
en: The tears of the sorrow-stricken survivors will burn me for good. I am very much afraid of them. I seek your protection.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: यमस्य भवने देव पात्यन्ते पापकर्मिणः। प्रसादये त्वां वरद प्रसादं कुरु मे प्रभो॥
en: All sinful creatures will have to sink into hell. I seek to please you, O boon-giving god! Extend to me your favour, O powerful lord.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं कामं त्वत्तो लोकपितामह। इच्छेयं त्वत्प्रसादार्थं तपस्तप्तुं महेश्वर॥
en: I seek the satisfaction of this wish, O Grandfather, of all the worlds. O foremost of all the gods, I seek, through your grace, permission to practise austere penances.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: पितामह उवाच मृत्यो संकल्पिता मे त्वं प्रजासंहारहेतुना। गच्छ संहर सर्वास्त्वं प्रजा मा च विचारय॥
en: The Grandfather said O Death, I have selected you for the destruction of all creatures! Go, and begin the task of killing all. Do not think thus.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: एतदेवमवश्यं हि भविता नैतदन्यथा। क्रियतामनवद्याङ्गि यथोक्तं मद्वचोऽनघे॥
en: This must surely take place. It cannot be otherwise. O sinless one, O fair lady do you satisfy the order I have given.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: एवमुक्ता महाबाहो मृत्युः परपुरंजय। न व्याजहार तस्थौ च प्रह्वा भगवदुन्मुखी॥
en: Thus addressed, O you of mighty arms, the lady called Death, O conqueror of hostile cities, did not utter a word, but humbly stood there with her eyes turned towards the powerful Lord of all creatures.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: पुनः पुनरथोक्ता सा गतसत्त्वेव भामिनी। तूष्णीमासीत् ततो देवो देवानामीश्वरेश्वरः॥
en: Brahma addressed her again and again, but the lady appeared to be herself deprived of life. Seeing her thus, the god of gods, that lords of lords, became silent.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: प्रससाद किल ब्रह्मा स्वयमेवात्मनाऽऽत्मनि। स्मयमानश्च लोकेशो लोकान् सर्वानवैक्षत॥
en: Indeed, the Self-create by an effort of his will, became pleased. Smiling the lord of all the worlds then looked at the universe.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: निवृत्तरोषे तस्मिस्तु भगवत्यपराजिते। सा कन्याथ जगामास्य समीपादिति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that when that unconquered and illustrious lord controlled his anger, the lady (called Death) went away from his side.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: अपसृत्याप्रतिश्रुत्य प्रजासंहरणं तदा। त्वरमाणेव राजेन्द्र मृत्युर्धेनुकमभ्यगात्॥
en: Leaving Brahma's side without having promised to bring about the destruction of living creatures, Death speedily went, O king, 10 the sacred spot known by the name of Dhenuka.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: सा तत्र परमं देवी तपोऽचरद् दुश्चरम्। समा होकपदे तस्थौ दश पद्मानि पञ्च च॥
en: There the goddess performed austere penances for fifteen billions of years, standing upon one foot.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: तां तथा कुर्वतीं तत्र तपः परमदुश्चरम्। पुनरेव महातेजा ब्रह्मा वचनमब्रवीत्॥ कुरुष्व मे वचो मृत्यो तदनादृत्य सत्वरा। तथैवैकपदे तात पुनरन्यानि सप्त सा॥ तस्थौ पद्मानि षट् चैव पञ्च द्वे चैव मानद। भूयः पद्मायुतं तात मृगैः सह चचार सा॥
en: After she had practised such highly severe austerities in that place, the highly energetic Brahma once more said to her,-Do you satisfy iny command, O Death! Disregarding this order, the lady once more practised austerities standing upon one foot for twenty billions of years, O giver of honours! And once more, O son, she lived in the forest with the deer for another long period of ten thousand billions of years.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: द्वे चायुते नरश्रेष्ठ वायवाहारा महामते। पुनरेव ततो राजन् मौनमातिष्ठदुत्तमम्॥ अप्सु वर्षसहस्राणि सप्त चैकं च पार्थिवा ततो जगाम सा कन्या कौशिकी नृपसत्तम॥
en: And once more, O foremost of men, she passed twenty thousand years living upon air only. Once again, O king she observed the excellent vow of silence for eight thousand years passing the whole period in water. Then that maiden, O best of kings, went to river Kaushiki.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: तत्र वायुजलाहारा चचार नियम पुनः। ततो ययौ महाभागा गङ्गां मेरुं च केवलम्॥
en: There she began to pass her days observing another vow, living upon only water and air. After this, O king, the blessed maiden proceeded to the Ganges and thence to the mount Meru.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: तस्थौ दार्विव निश्चेष्टा प्रजानां हितकाम्यया। ततो हिमवतो मूनि यत्र देवाः समीजिरे॥ तत्राङ्गुष्ठेन राजेन्द्र निखर्वमपरं ततः। तस्थौ पितामहं चैव तोषयामास यत्नतः॥
en: Actuated by the desire of doing good to all living creatures, she stood perfectly motionless there like a piece of wood. Going thence to the summit of Himavat where the gods had celebrated their great sacrifice, she stood there for another hundred billions of years, standing upon only the toes of her feet, with the object of pleasing the Grandfather with such an act of austerity.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: ततस्तामब्रवीत् तत्र लोकानां प्रभवाप्ययः। किमिदं वर्तते पुत्रि क्रियतां मम तद् वचः॥
en: Going there the Creator and Destroyer of the universe again addressed her saying,-What are you doing, O daughter! Satisfy those words of mine!

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् पुनर्मृत्युर्भगवन्तं पितामहम्। न हरेयं प्रजा देव पुनश्चाहं प्रसादये॥
en: Addressing the divine Grandfather, the maiden once more said, I am unable to destroy living creatures, O god! I seek to please you.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: तामधर्मभयाद् भीतां पुनरेव प्रयाचतीम्। तदाब्रवीद् देवदेवो निगृह्येदं वचस्ततः॥
en: Frightened at doing the prospect of iniquity as she then was and employed in soliciting the Grandfather to excuse her for disobedience the Grandsire silenced her, and once more said to her',-

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: अधर्मो नास्ति ते मृत्यो संयच्छेमाः प्रजाः शुभे। मया हुक्तं मृषा भद्रे भविता नेह किंचन॥
en: No sin shall visit you, O Death,! Do you, O auspicious maiden, begin the task of destroying living creatures! What I have said, O amiable girl, cannot be falsified.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: धर्मः सनातनश्च त्वामिहैवानुप्रवेक्ष्यति। अहं च विबुधाश्चैव त्वद्धिते निरताः सदा॥
en: Eternal virtue shall now live in you. Myself and all the gods shall always be busy with secking your well-being.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: इममन्यं च ते कामं ददानि मनसेप्सितम्। न त्वां दोषेण यास्यन्ति व्याधिसम्पीडिताः प्रजाः॥
en: I grant you this other wish that is in your heart! Living creatures shall be possessed by disease, and shall not censure you.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: पुरुषेषु स्वरूपेण पुरुषस्त्वं भविष्यसि। स्त्रीषु स्त्रीरूपिणी चैव तृतीयेषु नपुंसकम्॥
en: You will become a male in all male beings, a female in all female beings, and a eunuch in all those who are so.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: सैवमुक्ता महाराज कृताञ्जलिरुवाच ह। पुनरवे महात्मानं नेति देवेशमव्ययम्॥ तामब्रवीत् तदा देवो मृत्यो संहर मानवान्।
en: Thus addressed by Brahma, O king, the maiden at last said, with joined hands to that great and undecaying lord of all the gods-I am unable to satisfy your order. The great God again said to her, O Death, do you kill men!

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: अधर्मस्ते न भविता तथा ध्यास्याम्यहं शुभे॥ यानश्रुबिन्दूम्पतितानपश्यं ये पाणिभ्यां धारितास्ते पुरस्तात्। ते व्याधयो मानवान् घोररूपाः। प्राप्ते काले कालयिष्यन्ति मृत्यो॥
en: I shall so ordain that you will not commit any sin by doing this, O auspicious lady. The tears that I see fall from your eyes, and which you still hold in joined hands, shall take the form of terrible diseases and even they shall destroy men when their time comes.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: सर्वेषा त्वं प्राणिनामन्तकाले कामक्रोधौ सहितौ योजयेथाः। एवं धर्मस्त्वामुपैष्यत्यमेयो न चाधर्मं लप्स्यसे तुल्यवृत्तिः॥
en: When the end of living creatures arrives you will send Desire and Anger together against them. You shall reap immeasurable merit. You will not commit sin, being yourself perfectly equal in your conduct.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: एवं धर्म पालयिष्यस्यथो त्वं न चात्मानं मज्जयिष्यस्यधर्मे। तस्मात् कामं रोचयाभ्यागतं त्वं संयोज्याथो संहरस्वेह जन्तून।३६॥
en: By doing this you will only observe righteousness instead of committing sin. Do you, therefore, mind the work in hand, and addressing Desire and Anger begin to kill all living creatures.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: सा वै तदा मृत्युसंज्ञापदेशा गीता शापाद्बाढमित्यब्रवीत् तम्। अथो प्राणान्प्राणिनामन्तकाले कामक्रोधौ प्राप्य निर्मोह्य हन्ति॥
en: Thus addressed, that lady, Death, became afraid of Brahma's curse and answered him, saying,-Yes! Thence-forward she began to send Desire and Anger at the last hours of living creatures, and through their agency to kill them.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: मृत्योर्ये ते व्याधयश्चाश्रुपाता मनुष्याणां रुज्यते यैः शरीरम्। सवेषां वै प्राणिनां प्राणनान्ते तस्माच्छोकं मा कृथा बुद्ध्य बुद्ध्या॥
en: Those tears that Death had shed are the diseases by which the bodies of men are possessed. At the destruction, therefore, of living creatures, one should not, understanding with the help of the intelligence, give way to grief.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: सर्वे जीवाः प्राणिनां प्राणनान्ते गत्वा वृत्ताः संनिवृत्तास्तथैव। एवं सर्वे मानवाः प्राणनान्ते गत्वा वृत्ताः देववद्राजसिंह॥
en: As the senses of all creatures disappear when they are in dreamless slumber and return once more when they awake, similarly, upon the dissolution of their bodies, all human beings have to go into the other world and return thence to this, O foremost of kings.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: वायुीमो भीमनादो महौजा: स सर्वेषां प्राणिनां प्राणभूतः। नानावृत्तिर्देहिनां देहभेदे तस्माद्वायुर्देवदेवो विशिष्टः॥
en: The element called wind, which has terrible energy and mighty prowess and dealening roars, acts as the life in all living creatures. When the bodies of living creatures are destroyed, that wind, passing from the old performs various functions in various new bodies. Therefore the wind is called the lord of senses and is superior to all other elements forming the gross body.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: सर्वे देवा मर्त्यसंज्ञाविशिष्टाः सर्वे मर्त्या देवसंज्ञाविशिष्टाः। तस्मात् पुत्रं मा शुचो राजसिंह पुत्रः स्वर्ग प्राप्य ते मोदते ह॥
en: The gods, without any exception, have to take birth as mortal creatures on Earth. Likewise, all mortal creatures also, succeed in acquiring the dignity to gods. Therefore, O foremost of kings, do not grieve for you son. Your son has gone to heaven, and is enjoying great happiness there.

description: The Colloquy between Death and Brahma
sn: एवं मृत्युर्देवसृष्टा प्रजानां प्राप्ते काले संहरन्ती यथावत्। तस्याश्चैव व्याधयस्तेऽश्रुपाताः प्राप्ते काले संहरन्तीह जन्तून्॥
en: It was thus, O king, that Death was created by the Self-Create and it is in this way that she kills duly all living creatures when their time comes. the tears she had shed became diseases, which when their last hours come, snatch away all beings gifted with life.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच इमे वै मानवाः सर्वे धर्म प्रति विशङ्किताः। कोऽयं धर्मः कुतो धर्मस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥ धर्मस्त्वयमिहार्थः किमुत्रार्थोऽपि वा भवेत्। उभयार्थो हि वा धर्मस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhisthira said All men who live on this Earth, are filled with doubts regarding the nature .or righteousness. Who is this that is called Righteousness? Whence also does Righteousness come? come? Tell me this, O Grandfather! Is Righteousness for this world or for the next world? Or, is it for both here and hereafter? Tell me this, O grandfather?"

sn: भीष्म उवाच सदाचारः स्मृतिर्वेदास्त्रिविधं धर्मलक्षणम्। चतुर्थमर्थमित्याहुः कवयो धर्मलक्षणम्॥
en: The practices of the good, the Smritis and the Vedas, are the three marks of righteousness. Besides these, the learned have said that the object (of doing works) is the fourth mark.

sn: अपि झुक्तानि धाणि व्यवस्यन्त्युत्तरावरे। लोकयात्रार्थमेवेह धर्मस्य नियमः कृतः॥
en: The Rishis of old have said what acts are righteous and also classificd them as superior or inferior in point of merit. The rules of righteousness have been sanctioned for the conduct of the affairs of the world.

sn: उभयत्र सुखोदर्क इह चैव परत्र च । अलध्वा निपुणं धर्मं पाप: पापेन युज्यते॥
