en: In both the worlds, here and hereafter, righteousness begets happiness as its fruit. A sinful person, unable to acquire merit by subtile ways, becomes sullied with sin only.

sn: न च पापकृतः पापान्मुच्यन्ते केचिदापदि। अपापवादी भवति यथा भवति धर्मकृत्। धर्मस्य निष्ठा त्वाचारस्तमेवाश्रित्य भोत्स्यसे॥
en: Some hold that sinful wights can never be purged of their sins. In times of difficulty a person by even speaking an untruth acquires the merit of speaking the truth. So a person who performs a sinful act acquires by that very means the merit of having done a pious act. Conduct is the refuge of righteousness. Helped by it you should know what righteousness is.

sn: यथा धर्मसमाविष्टो धानं गृह्णाति तस्करः। रमते निर्हरन् स्तेनः परवित्तमराजके॥
en: The very thief, stealing others things, spends them in acts of seeming virtue. During anarchy, the thief takes great pleasure in approaching what belongs to others.

sn: यदास्य तद्धरन्त्यन्ये तदा राजानमिच्छति। तदा तेषां स्पृहयते ये वै तुष्टाः स्वकैर्धनैः॥
en: When others, however, rob him of what he has gained by robbery, he then seeks a king. At even such a time, when he is highly indignant for his rights of property being violated, he secretly hankers after the riches of those who are contented with their own.

sn: अभीतः शुचिरभ्येति राजद्वारमशङ्कितः। न हि दुश्चरितं किंचिदन्तरात्मनि पश्यति॥
en: Fearlessly and without a doubt in his mind he goes to the king's palace, with a mind purged of every sin. Within even his own heart he does not see mark of any evil act.

sn: सत्यस्य वचनं साधु न सत्याद् विद्यते परम्। सत्येन विधृतं सर्वं सर्वं सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: To speak the truth is meritorious. There is nothing superior to truth. Everything is supported by truth, and everything depends upon truth.

sn: अपि पापकृतो रौद्राः कृत्वा पृथक् पृथक्। अद्रोहमविसंवादं प्रवर्तन्ते तदाश्रयाः॥ ते चेन्मिथोऽधृतिं कुर्युविनश्येयुरसंशयम्।
en: Even the sinful and dreadful persons swearing to keep the truth amongst themselves, do away with all grounds of quarrel and in a body perform their (sinful) deeds, depending upon truth. If they behaved falsely towards one another, they would, forsooth, he destroyed.

sn: न हर्तव्यं परधनमिति धर्मः सनातनः॥ मन्यन्ते बलवन्तस्तं दुर्बलैः सम्प्रवर्तितम्।
en: One should not take other's properties. That is an eternal duty. Powerful men consider it as one that has been introduced by the weak.

sn: यदा नियतिदौर्बल्यमथैषामेव रोचते॥ न ह्यत्यन्तं बलवन्तो भवन्ति सुखिनोऽपि वा।
en: When, however, ill luck overtakes, these men they the approve of this injunction. Again, they who surpass others in strength or power do not necessarily become happy.

sn: तस्मादनार्जवे बुद्धिर्न कार्या ते कदाचन॥ असाधुभ्योऽस्य न भयं न चौरेभ्यो न राजतः। अकिंचित् कस्यचित् कुर्वन् निर्भयः शुचिरावसेत्॥
en: Therefore, do not ever think of doing a wrong act. One behaving in this way has no fear of dishonest men or thieves, or the king. Not having injured any one, such a man lives fearlessly and with a pure heart.

sn: सर्वतः शङ्कते स्तेनो मृगो ग्राममिवेयिवान्। बहुधाऽऽचरितं पापमन्यत्रैवानुपश्यति॥
en: A thief fears every body, like a deer driven from the forest into the midst of an inhabited village. He considers other people as sinful as himself.

sn: मुदितः शुचिरभ्येति सर्वतो निर्भयः सदा। न हि दुश्चरितं किंचिदात्मनोऽन्येषु पश्यति॥
en: A pure-hearted person is always filled with cheerfulness and has no fear from any where. Such a person never sees his own misconduct in other persons.

sn: दातव्यमित्ययं धर्म उक्तो भूतहिते रतैः। तं मन्यन्ते धनयुताः कृपणैः सम्प्रवर्तितम्॥
en: Persons who do good to all creatures have said that charity is another high duty. The rich people think that this duty has been laid down by the poor.

sn: यदा नियतिकार्पण्यमथैषामेव रोचते। न हत्यन्तं धन्वन्तो भवन्ति सुखिनोऽपि वा॥
en: When, however, those wealthy men become poor on account of some bad turn of fortune, they then appreciate the practice of charity. Men who are highly rich do not necessarily experience happiness.

sn: यदन्यैर्विहितं नेच्छेदात्मनः कर्म न तत् परेषु कुर्वीत जानन्नप्रिययात्मनः॥
en: A person should never do that to others which he does not like to be done to him by others, knowing how painful it is to himself.

sn: पूरुषः। योऽन्यस्य स्यादुपपतिः स कं किं वक्तुमर्हति। यदन्यस्य ततः कुर्यान्न मृष्येदिति मे मतिः॥
en: What can a man seeking another man's wife say to another man? It is seen, however, that even such a man, when he sees his wife with another person, becomes unable to forgive the act.

sn: जीवितुं यः स्वयं चेच्छेत् कथं सोऽन्यं प्रघातयेत्। यद् यदात्मनि चेच्छेत तत् परस्यापि चिन्तयेत्॥
en: How can a person who wishes to himself take breath think of preventing another by a murderous act from doing the same? Whatever wishes one cherishes about his own self, one should certainly cherish regarding another.

sn: अतिरिक्तैः संविभजेद् भोगैरन्यानकिंचनान्। एतस्मात् कारणाद् धात्रा कुसीदं सम्प्रवर्तितम्॥
en: With his surplus riches he should remove the wants of the poor. Therefore the Creator ordained the practice of multiplying one's wealth.

sn: यस्मिस्तु देवाः समये संतिष्ठेरंस्तथा भवेत्। अथवा लाभसमये स्थितिधर्मेऽपि शोभना॥
en: One should walk along that road by proceeding along which he may hope to meet with the gods; or, at such times when wealth is acquired, the duties of sacrifice and gift are highly spoken of.

sn: सर्वं प्रियाभ्युपगतं धर्ममाहुर्मनीषिणः। पश्यैतं लक्षणोद्देशं धर्माधर्मे युधिष्ठिर॥
en: The sages have said that righteousness consists in the performance of objects by means of agreeable means. See, O Yudhisthira, that this is the standard that has been upheld in pointing out the marks of virtue and sin.

sn: लोकसंग्रहसंयुक्तं विधात्रा विहितं पुरा। सूक्ष्मधर्मार्थनियतं सतां चरितमुत्तमम्॥
en: In days of yore the Creator ordained virtue gifting it with the power of holding the world together. The excellent conduct of the good, is subjected to restraints for acquiring virtue which depends upon many delicate considerations.

sn: धर्मलक्षणमाख्यातमेतत् ते कुरुसत्तम। तस्मादनार्जवे बुद्धिर्न ते कार्या कथंचन॥
en: The marks of virtue have now been described to you, O best of Kuru's race? Do not, therefore, at any time think of doing a wrong act.

sn: धर्मलक्षणमाख्यातमेतत् ते कुरुसत्तम। तस्मादनार्जवे बुद्धिर्न ते कार्या कथंचन॥
en: The marks of virtue have now been described to you, O best of Kuru's race? Do not, therefore, at any time think of doing a wrong act.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सूक्ष्मं साधु समादिष्टं भवता धर्मलक्षणम्। प्रतिभा त्वस्ति मे काचित् तां ब्रूयामनुमानतः॥
en: Yudhisthira said You say that virtue or duty depends upon delicate consideration, that it is marked out by the conduct of the good, that it is fraught with restraints, and that its characteristics are also contained in the Vedas. It appears to me, however, that I have a certain inward light by virtue of which I can differentiate between right and wrong by inferences.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: भूयांसो हृदये ये मे प्रश्नास्ते व्याहृतास्त्वया। इदं त्वन्यत् प्रवक्ष्यामि न राजन् निग्रहादिव॥
en: Numberless questions which I had wished to ask you have all been answered by you. There is one question, however, that I shall just now put. It is not prompted, O king, by desire of mere discussion.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: इमानि हि प्राणयन्ति सृजन्त्युत्तारयन्ति च। न धर्मः परिपाठेन शक्यो भारत वेदितुम्॥
en: All these embodied creatures, it seems, take birth, exist, and renounce their bodies, of their own nature. Duty and its opposite, therefore, cannot be determined, O Bharata, by study of the scriptures alone.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: अन्यो धर्मः समस्थस्य विषमस्थस्य चापरः। आपदस्तु कथं शक्याः परिपाठेन वेदितुम्॥
en: The duties of a rich person are of one sort. Those of a person who has fallen into distress are of another sort. How can duty in the time of poverty be determined by reading the scriptures alone?

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: सदाचारो मतो धर्मः सन्तस्त्वाचारलक्षणाः। साध्यासाध्यं कथं शक्यं सदाचारो ह्यलक्षणः॥
en: The acts of the good, as you have said, form virtue. The good, however, are to be known by their acts. The definition, therefore, has at the bottom a begging of the question, and the result is that what is meant by conduct of the good remains unsettled.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: दृश्यते हि धर्मारूपेणाधर्मं प्राकृतश्चरन्। धर्मं चाधर्मरूपेण कश्चिदप्राकृतश्चरन्॥
en: It is seen that some ordinary man commits sin while apparently achieving virtue. Some extraordinary person again may be seen who achieves virtue by committing acts which are seemingly sinful.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: पुनरस्य प्रमाणं हि निर्दिष्टं शास्त्रकोविदैः। वेदवादाश्चानुयुगं ह्रसन्तीतीह नः श्रुतम्॥ अन्ये कृतयुगे धर्मास्त्रेतायां द्वापरे परे। अन्ये कलियुगे धर्मा यथाशक्ति कृता इव॥
en: Then, again, the proof has been given by even those who are well-conversant with the scriptures themselves, for we have heard that the ordinances of the Vedas disappear gradually in every successive cycle. The duties in the Krita age are of one sort. Those in the Treta are of another sort, and those in the Dvapara are of a different sort. The duties in the Kali age, again, are entirely of a different character. It seems, therefore, that duties have been sanctioned for the respective cycles according to the powers of human beings in the different ages.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: आम्नायवचनं सत्यमित्ययं लोकसंग्रहः। आम्नायेभ्यः पुनर्वेदाः प्रसृताः सर्वतोमुखाः॥
en: When, therefore, all the declarations in the Vedas do not suit equally all the ages, the saying that the Vedas are true is only a popular parlance given vent to for popular satisfaction. whose range From the Shrutis have originated the Smritis is very wide.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: ते चेत् सर्वप्रमाणं वै प्रमाणं ह्यत्र विद्यते। प्रमाणेऽप्यप्रमाणेन विरुद्ध शास्त्रता कुतः॥
en: If the Vedas be considered authoritative everywhere, then the Smritis also would be considered authoritative, for the latter are based on the former. But when the Shrutis and the Smritis contradict each other, how can either be authoritative.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: धर्मस्य क्रियमाणस्य बलवद्भिर्दुरात्मभिः। या या विक्रियते संस्था ततः सापि प्रणश्यति॥
en: Then, again, it is seen, that when some wicked wights of great power cause certain portions of religious acts to be stopped, these are destroyed for ever.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: विद्म चैवं न वा विद्म शक्यं वा वेदितुं न वा। अणीयान् क्षुरधाराया गरीयानपि पर्वतात्॥
en: Whether we know it or not, whether we are able to determine it or not, the course of duty is sharper than the edge of a razor and grosser than even a mountain.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: गन्धर्वनगराकारः प्रथमं सम्प्रदृश्यते। अन्वीक्ष्यमाणः कविभिः पुनर्गच्छत्यदर्शनम्॥
en: Virtue at first appears in the form of the romantic house of vapour seen in the distant sky. When, however, it is examined by the ! learned, it disappears.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: निपानानीव गोभ्योऽपि क्षेत्रे कुल्ये च भारत। स्मृतिर्हि शाश्वते धर्मो विप्रहीणो न दृश्यते॥
en: Like the small ponds at which cattle drink or the shallow canals along cultivated fields, that dry up very soon, the eternal practices laid down in the Smrities, falling into discontinuance, at last disappear for good.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: कामादन्येच्छया चान्ये कारणैरपरैस्तथा। असन्तोऽपि वृथाचारं भजन्ते बहवोऽपरे॥
en: Amongst good men, some are seen to become hypocrites by allowing themselves to be moved by desire. Some become so, desiring by others. Many others tread in the same path, moved by various other motives of a similar nature.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: धर्मो भवति स क्षिप्रं प्रलापस्त्वेव साधुषु। अथैतानाहुरुन्मत्तानपि चावहसन्त्युत॥
en: It cannot be gainsaid that such acts are righteous. Fools, again, hold that virtue is an empty sound among those called good. They ridicule such persons and consider them as men bereft of reason.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: महाजना छुपावृत्ता राजधर्म समाश्रिताः। न हि सर्वहितः कश्चिदाचारः सम्प्रवर्तते॥
en: Many great men, again, neglecting the duties of their own order, follow those of the Kshatriyas. No such conduct, therefore, is to be seen, which is for universal benevolence.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: तेवैवान्यः प्रभवति सोऽपरं बाधते पुनः। दृश्यते चैव स पुनस्तुल्यरूपो यदृच्छया॥
en: By a certain action, one becomes really meritorious. The same actions prevent another from the acquisition of merit. Another, by performing those actions at his pleasure, it is seen, remains unchanged.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: येनैवान्यः प्रभवति सोऽपरानपि बाधते। आचाराणामनैकाम्यं सर्वेषामुपलक्षयेत्॥
en: Thus that action by which one reaps merit, obstructs another in the acquisition of merit. One may thus seen that all actions are not peculiar in motive and character.

description: Question by Yudhishthira about virtues and duties
sn: चिराभिपन्नः कविभिः पूर्वं धर्म उदाहृतः। तेनाचारेण पूर्वेण संस्था भवति शाश्वती॥
en: It seems, therefore, that only that which the learned of old denominated righteousness is righteousness to this day; and through that course of conduct the distinctions and limitations have become eternal.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। तुलाधारस्य वाक्यानि धर्मे जाजलिना सह॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old conversation of Tuladhara with Jajali on the subject of virtue. There was once a Brahmana named Jajali who lived in a certain forest, like a forest-recluse.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: वने वनचरः कश्चिज्जाजलि म वै द्विजः। सागरोद्देशमागम्य तपस्तेपे महातपाः॥
en: Practising austere penances, he proceeded at a certain time towards the sea-shore, and arrived there began to practise the most austere penances.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: नियतो नियताहारथीराजिनजटाधरः। मलपङ्कधरो धीमान् बहून् वर्षगणान् मुनिः॥
en: Observing many vows and restraints his food restricted by fast, his body clad in rags and skins, bearing matted locks on his head, his entire body smeared with filth and clay, the intelligent Brahmana passed many years there, speechless.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: स कदाचिन्महातेजा जलवासो महीपते। चचार लोकान् विप्रर्षिः प्रेक्षमाणो मनोजवः॥
en: Highly energetic that regenerate ascetic, O king, while living within the waters, travelled through all the worlds with the speed of the mind, desirous of seeing all things.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: स चिन्तयामास मुनिर्जलवासे कदाचन। विप्रेक्ष्य सागरान्तां वै महीं सवनकाननाम्॥
en: Having seen the whole Earth bounded by the ocean and adorned with rivers and lakes and forests, the ascetic one day, while sitting under the water, began to think thus:न मया सदृशोऽस्तीह लोके स्थावरजङ्गमे।

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: अप्सु वैहायसं गच्छेन्मया योऽन्यः सहेति वै॥
en: In this world of mobile and immobile creatures there is none who can equal me! Who can travel with me among the stars and planets in the sky and live again within the waters!

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: अदृश्यमानो रक्षोभिर्जलमध्ये वदंस्तथा। अब्रुवंश्च पिशाचास्तं नैवं त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Unseen by the Rakshasas while he said this to himself, the Pishachas said to him,-You should not say so!

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: तुलाधारो वणिग्धर्मा वाराणस्यां महायशाः। सोऽप्येवं नार्हते वक्तुं यथा त्वं द्विजसत्तम॥
en: There is a man named Tuladhara highly illustrious and doing the business of buying and selling, Even he, O best of twice-born ones, is not worthy of saying such words as you say!

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: इत्युक्तो जाजलिर्भूतैः प्रत्युवाच महातपाः। पश्येयं तमहं प्राज्ञं तुलाधारं यशस्विनम्॥
en: Thus addressed by those beings, Jajali of austere penances replied to them, saying,-I shall see that famous Tuladhara who is endued with such wisdom!

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: इति ब्रुवाणं तमृषि रक्षास्युद्धृत्य सागरात्। अब्रुवन् गच्छ पन्थानमास्थायेमं द्विजोत्तम्॥
en: When the Rishi said this, those superhuman beings raised him from the sea, and said to him,-best of twice-born one, go along this road!

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: इत्युक्तो जाजलिर्भूतैर्जगाम विमनास्तदा। वाराणस्यां तुलाधारं समासाद्याब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Thus addressed by those beings, Jajali went onwards with a depressed heart. Arrived at Baranasi he met Tuladhara whom he addressed thus.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं कृतं दुष्कर तात कर्म जाजलिना पुरा। येन सिद्धिं परा प्राप्तस्तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhisthira said What, O sire, are those difficult feats which Jajali had performed before for which he had acquired such great success? You should describe them to me.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: भीष्म उवाच अतीव तपसा युक्तो घोरेण स बभूव ह। तथोपस्पर्शनरतः सायं प्रातर्महातपाः॥
en: Bhishma said Jajali had practised penances of the severest austerities. He used to perform ablutions morning and cvening.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: अग्नीन् परिचरन् सम्यक् स्वाध्यायपरमोद्विजः। वानप्रस्थविधानज्ञो जाजलिवलितः श्रिया॥
en: Carefully serving his fires, he was given to the study of the Vedas. Well conversant with the duties laid down for hermits, Jajali, seemed to shine with effulgence.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: वने तपस्यतिष्ठत् स न च धर्ममवैक्षत। वर्षास्वाकाशशायी च हेमन्तं जलसंश्रयः॥
en: He continued to live in the forest, performing penances, But he never took himself for one who had acquired any merit by his acts. During the rains he slept under the open sky. In auturnn he sat in water.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: वातातपसहो ग्रीष्मे न च धर्ममविन्दत। दुःखशय्याश्च विविधा भूमौ च परिवर्तते॥
en: In summer he exposed himself to the sun and the wind. Still he never took himself for one who had acquired any merit by such acts. He used to sleep on various sorts of painful beds and also on the naked earth.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: ततः कदाचित् स मुनिर्वर्षास्वाकाशमास्थितः। अन्तरिक्षाज्जलं मूर्धा प्रत्यगृह्णान्मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: On one occasion that ascetic, while standing under the sky during the rainy season, received on his head repeated showers froin the clouds.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: अथ तस्य जटाः क्लिना बभूवुर्ग्रथिताः प्रभो। अरण्यगमनान्नित्यं मलिनोऽमलसंयुतः॥
en: He had to pass through the forests again and again. Partly with exposure to the rains and partly with the filth they caught, the locks of that pure Rishi became entangled and intertwined with one another.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: स कदाचिनिराहारो वायुभक्षो महातपाः। तस्थौ काष्ठवदव्यग्रो न चचाल च कर्हिचित्॥
en: At one time abstaining entirely from food and living upon air alone, that great ascetic, stood in the forest like a wooden post Unmoved at heart, he stood there, without once moving an inch.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: तस्य स्म स्थाणुभूतस्य निर्विचेष्टस्य भारत। कुलिङ्गशकुनौ राजन् नीडं शिरसि चक्रतुः॥
en: While he stood there unmoved like a wooden post, О Bharata, a pair of Kulinga birds, O king, built their nest on his head.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: स तौ दयावान् ब्रह्मर्षिरुपप्रेक्षत दम्पती। कुर्वाणौ नीडकं तत्र जटासु तृणतन्तुभिः॥
en: Filled with pity, the great Rishis allowed those birds in building their nest among his matted locks with pieces of grass.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: यदा न स चलत्येव स्थाणुभूतो महातपाः। ततस्तौ सुखविश्वस्तौ सुखं तत्रोषतुस्तदा॥
en: And as the ascetic stood there like a wooden post, the two birds lived on his head happily and confidingly.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: अतीतास्वथ वर्षासु शरत्काल उपस्थिते। प्राजापत्येन विधिना विश्वासात् काममोहितौ॥ तत्रापातयतां राजन् शिरस्यण्डानि खेचरौ।
en: The rainy season passed away and autumn set in. Actuated by desire, the couple approached each other according to the law of the Creator, and with perfect confidence laid their eggs, O king, on the head of that Rishi.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: तान्यबुध्यत तेजस्वी स विप्रः संशितव्रतः॥ बुद्ध्वा च स महातेजा न चचाल च जाजलि। धर्मे कृतमना नित्यं नाधर्मं स त्वरोचयत्॥
en: Of rigid vows and endued with energy, the ascetic knew it. Knowing even what the birds had done, Jajali did not move. Bent strongly upon acquiring merit, no act involving the slightest injury to others could meet with his approval.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: अहन्यहनि चागत्य ततस्तौ तस्य मूर्धनि। आश्वासितौ निवसतः सम्प्रहृष्टौ तदा विभो॥
en: Going away and returning every day from, and to his head, the birds happily and trustfully lived there, O powerful king.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: अण्डेभ्यस्त्वथ पुष्टेभ्यः प्राजायन्त शकुन्तकाः। व्यवर्धन्त च तत्रैव न चाकम्पत जाजलिः॥
en: When in the course of time the eggs became mature and young ones came out, they began to grow up in that nest, for Jajali moved not in the least.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: स रक्षमाणस्त्वण्डानि कुलिङ्गानां धृतव्रतः। तथैव तस्थौ धर्मात्मा निर्विचेष्टः समाहितः॥
en: Firmly observing his vows, the righteous Rishi continued to hold and protect those eggs by standing on that very spot perfectly motionless and immersed in Yoga meditation.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: ततस्तु कालसमये बभूवुस्तेऽथ पक्षिणः। बुबुधे तांस्तु स मुनिर्जातपक्षान् कुलिङ्गकान्॥
en: In course of time the young ones grew and became endued with wings. The Muni knew that the young Kulingas had grown up so.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: ततः कदाचित् तांस्तत्र पश्यन् पक्षीन् यतव्रतः। बभूव परमप्रीतस्तदा मतिमतां वरः॥
en: That foremost of intelligent men, of austere VOWS, one day saw those young ones and became filled with pleasure.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: तथा तानपि संवृद्धान् दृष्ट्वा चाप्नुवतां मुदम्। शकुनौ निर्भयौ तत्र उपतुश्चात्मजैः सह॥
en: Seeing their young ones endued with wings, the parent birds became very happy and continued to live in the Rishi's head with them in perfect confidence.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: जातपक्षांश्च सोऽपश्यदुड्डीनान् पुनरागतान्। सायं सायं द्विजान् विप्रो न चाकम्पत जाजलिः॥
en: The learned Jajali saw that when the young birds had wings they flew to the air every evening and came back to his head without having gone far. He still stood motionless there.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: कदाचित् पुनरभ्येत्य पुनर्गच्छन्ति संततम्। त्यक्ता मातापितृभ्यां ते न चाकम्पत जाजलिः॥
en: Sometime after he saw that, left by their parents, they went out alone and came back again alone, Jajali did not still move.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: तथा वे दिवसं चापि गत्वा सायं पुनर्नृप। उपावर्तन्त तत्रैव निवासार्थं शकुन्तकाः॥
en: Sometime after, the young birds going away in the morning spent the whole day out of his sight but returned in the evening for living in the nest.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: कदाचिद् दिवसान् पञ्च समुत्पत्य विहङ्गमाः। षष्ठेऽहनि समाजग्मुर्न चाकम्पत जाजलिः॥
en: Sometime after, leaving their nest for five days at a time, they returned on the sixth day. Jajali still did not move.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: क्रमेण च पुनः सर्वे दिवसान् सुबहूनथ। नोपावर्तन्त शकुना जातप्राणाः स्म ते यदा॥
en: Subsequently, when they gained their full strength, they left him and did not return at all even after many days.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: कदाचिन्मासमात्रेण समुत्पत्य विहङ्गमाः। नैवागच्छंस्ततो राजन् प्रातिष्ठत स जाजलिः॥
en: At last, at another time, leaving him, they did not come even after a month. Then, O king, Jajali left that place.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: ततस्तेषु प्रलीनेषु जाजलिर्जातविस्मयः। सिद्धोऽस्मीति मतिं चक्रे ततस्तं मान आविशत्॥
en: When they had thus gone away for ever, Jajali wondered much and thought that he had gained ascetic success. Then pride entered his heart.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: स तथा निर्गतान् दृष्ट्वा शकुन्तान् नियतव्रतः। सम्भावितात्मा सम्भाव्य भृशं प्रीतमनाऽभवत्॥
en: Ever observing vows, the great ascetic, seeing the birds thus leave him. After having been brought up on his head, thought highly of himself, and became filled with joy.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: स नद्यां समुपस्पृश्य तर्पयित्वा हुताशनम्। उदयन्मथादित्यमुपातिष्ठन्महातपाः॥
en: He then bathed in a river and poured libations on the sacred fire, and worshipped the rising Sun.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: सम्भाव्य चटकान् मूनि जाजलिर्जपतां वरः। आस्फोटयत् तथाऽऽकाशे धर्मः प्राप्तो मयेति वै॥
en: Having thus made those chataka birds, grow on his head, Jajali that foremost of ascetics, began to strike his armpits and cry loudly through the sky, I have acquired great merit.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: अथान्तरिक्षे वागासीत् तां च शुश्राव जाजलिः। धर्मेण न समस्त्वं वै तुलाधारस्य जाजले॥
en: Then an unseen voice arose in the sky and Jajali heard these words:-You are not equal, O Jajali, to Tuladhara in righteousness.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: वाराणस्यां महाप्राज्ञस्तुलाधारः प्रतिष्ठितः। सोऽप्येवं नार्हते वक्तुं यथा त्वं भाषसे द्विज॥
en: Highly wise, that Tuladhara lives at Baranasi. Even he is not competent to say what you say, O twice-born one!

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: सोऽमर्षवशमापन्नस्तुलाधारदिदृक्षया। पृथिवीमचरद् राजन् यत्र सायंगृहो मुनिः॥
en: Hearing these words, Jajali became possessed by anger and desirous of meeting with Tuladhara, O king, began to roam over the whole Earth, observing the vow of silence and passing the night where he met with evening.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: सोऽपि दृष्ट्वैव तं विप्रमायान्तं भाण्डजीवनः। समुत्थाय सुसंहृष्टः स्वागतेनाभ्यपूजयत्॥
en: After a long time he reached the city of Baranasi, and saw Tuladhara engaged in selling miscellaneous articles.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: कालेन महतागच्छत् स तु वाराणसी पुरीम्। विक्रीणन्तं च पण्यानि तुलाधारं ददर्श सः॥
en: As soon as the shop-keeper Tuladhara saw the Brahmana arrived at his place, he cheerfully stood up and adored the guest with proper salutations.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: तुलाधार उवाच आयानेवासि विदितो मम ब्रह्मन् न संशयः। ब्रवीमि यत् तु वचनं तच्छृणुष्व द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Tuladhara said For tsooth, O Brahmana, I know that you have come to me. Listen, however, Oforemost of twice-born ones, to what I say!

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: सागरानूपमाश्रित्य तपस्तप्तं त्वया महत्। न च धर्मस्य संज्ञां त्वं पुरा वेत्थ कथंचन॥
en: Living on a low land near the sea-shore you had practised very hard penancces. But you had no consciousness of having acquired religious merit.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: ततः सिद्धस्य तपसा तव विप्र शकुन्तकाः। क्षिप्रं शिरस्यजायन्त ते च सम्भावितास्त्वया॥
en: When you had at last acquired ascetic success, certain birds were born on your head. You took great care of the little creatures:

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: जातपक्षा यदा ते च गताचारीमितस्ततः। मन्यमानस्ततो धर्मं चटकप्रभवं द्विज॥
en: When at last those birds came winged and when they began to leave your head for going here and there in search of food, it was then that, for your having thus assisted at the birth of those Chatakas, you began to feel pride, O Brahmana, thinking you had acquired great merit.

description: The story of Tuladhara and Jajali
sn: खे वाचं त्वमथाश्रौषीर्मा प्रति द्विजसत्तम। अमर्षवशमापन्नस्ततः प्राप्तो भवानिह। करवाणि प्रियं किं ते तद् ब्रूहि द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Then, O foremost of twice-born ones, you heard in the sky a voice that spoke of me. The words you had heard filled you with anger and for that you have come here! Tell me, what wish of yours shall I fulfil, O best of Brahmanas.

sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तः स तदा तेन तुलाधारेण धीमता। प्रोवाच वचनं धीमाजाजलिर्जपतां वरः॥
en: Thus accosted by the intelligent Tuladhara on that occasion, the highly intelligent Jajali, that foremost of ascetics, said these words to him:

sn: जाजलिरुवाच विक्रीणत: सर्वरसान् सर्वगन्धांश्च वाणिज। वनस्पतीनोषधीश्च तेषां मूलफलानि च॥
en: You sell all sorts of juices and scents, O son of a trader, as also (barks and leaves of) huge trees and herbs and their fruits and roots.

sn: अध्यगा नैष्ठिकी बुद्धिं कुतस्त्वामिदमागतम्। एतदाचक्ष्व मे सर्वं निखिलेन महामते॥
en: But how have you gained this stability of understanding? How have you gained this knowledge? O you of great intelligence, tell me all this fully.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्तस्तुलाधारो ब्राह्मणेन यशस्विना। उवाच धर्मसूक्ष्माणि वैश्यो धर्मार्थतत्त्ववित्॥
en: Thus accosted by that highly famous Brahmana, Tuladhara of the Vaishya caste, well acquatinted with the truths of morality and contented with knowledge, described to Jajali who had practised severe penances, the ways of morality.

sn: तुलाधार उवाच वेदाहं जाजले धर्मं सरहस्यं सनातनम्। सर्वभूतहितं मैत्रं पुराणं यं जना विदुः॥
en: Tuladhara said a O Jajali, I know, with all its mysteries, morality, which is eternal. It is nothing else but that ancient morality which every body knows, and which consists of universal friendliness, and beneficence to all creatures.

sn: अद्रोहेणैव भूतानामल्पद्रोहेण वा पुनः। या वृत्तिः स परो धर्मस्तेन जीवामि जाजले॥
en: The highest form of morality consists in a living which is founded upon total harmlessness towards all creatures or upon the smallness of such harin. I live according to that mode,OJajali.

sn: परच्छिन्नैः काष्ठतृणैर्मयेदं शरणं कृतम्। अलक्तं पद्मकं तुझं गन्धांश्चोच्चावचांस्तथा॥ रसांश्च तांस्तान् विप्रर्षे मद्यवान् बहूनहम्। क्रीत्वा वै प्रतिविक्रीणे परहस्तादमायया॥
en: This my house hath been made with wood and grass cut by other people's hands, Lacdye, the roots of Nymphoea lotus, filaments of the lotus, various sorts of good scents, and many kinds of liquids, O twice-born Rishi, with the exception of wines, I purchase from other people and sell without cheating.

sn: सर्वेषां यः सुहृन्नित्यं सर्वेषां च हिते रतः। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा स धर्म वेद जाजले।॥
en: He, O Jajali, only knows morality or righteousness is, who is always the friend of all creatures and who is always engaged in the behoof of all creatures, in thought, word, and deed.

sn: नानुरुद्ध्ये निरुध्ये वा न द्वेष्मि न च कामये। समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु पश्य मे जाजले व्रतम्।
en: I never beg of any one, I never fall out with any one; I never hate any one. I never desire for anything. I regard equally all things and all creatures. See, O Jajali, this is my vow.

sn: तुला मे सर्वभूतेषु समा तिष्ठति जाजले।॥ नाहं परेषां कृत्यानि प्रशंसामि न गर्हये। आकाशस्येवविप्रेन्द्र पश्यल्लोकस्य चित्रताम्॥
en: My scales are perfectly even, O Jajali, as regards all creatures. I neither praise nor blame the deeds of others, considering this variety in the world. O foremost of Brahmanas, as the variety seen in the sky.

sn: इति मां त्वं विजानीहि सर्वलोकस्य जाजले। समं मतिमतां श्रेष्ठ समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनम्॥
en: Know, O Jajali, that I regard equally all creatures. O highest of intelligent men, I perceive no difference between a clod of earth, a piece of stone, and a lump of gold.

sn: यथान्धबधिरोन्मत्ता उच्छ्वासपरमाः सदा। देवैरपिहितद्वारा: सोपमा पश्यतो मम॥
en: As the blind, the deaf, and they who are bereft of reason, find consolation for the loss of their senses, likewise, I find consolation by their example.

sn: यथा वृद्धातुरकृशा निःस्पृहा विषयान् प्रति। तथार्थकामभोगेषु ममापि विगता स्पृहा॥
en: As they who are possessed by decrepitude, they who are afflicted by disease, and they who are weakened and emaciated, do not like any sort of enjoyments, similarly, I feel no inclination for wealth pleasure enjoyments.

sn: यदा चायं न विभेति यदा चास्मान्न बिभ्यति। यदा नेच्छति न द्वेष्टि ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: Then only a person attains to Brahma when he fears nothing and is not feared himself, when he cherishes no desire and does not hate anything.

sn: यदा न कुरुते भावं सर्वभूतेषु पापकम्। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: Then only a person attains to Brahma when he does not behave sinfully towards any creature in thought, word, or deed.

sn: न भूतो न भविष्योऽस्ति न च धर्मोऽस्ति कश्चन। योऽभयः सर्वभूतानां स प्राप्नोत्यभयं पदम्॥
en: There is no past, no future, There is no morality or virtue. He who is not an object of fear with any creature acquires a state in which there is no fear. or or

sn: यस्मादुद्विजते लोकः सर्वो मृत्युमुखादिव। वाक्क्राद् दण्डपरुषात् स प्राप्नोति महद् भयम्॥
en: On the other hand, that person who for his harsh words and bad temper, is troublesome to all creatures like death itself, certainly attains to a state full of fear.

sn: यथावद् वर्तमानानां वृद्धानां पुत्रपौत्रिणाम्। अनुवर्तामहे वृत्तमहिंस्राणां महात्मनाम्॥
en: I follow the practices of great and benevolent men of advanced years who with their children and grand children live observing duly the ordinance laid down in the scritptures.

sn: प्रणष्टः शाश्वतो धर्मस्त्वनाचारेण मोहितः। तेन वैद्यस्तपस्वी वा बलवान् वा विमुह्यते॥
en: The eternal Vedic practices are entirely abandoned by one who allows himself to be stupefied by some mistakes that he may have marked in the conduct of those who are admittedly good and wise. One, however, who is gifted with learning, or one who has controlled his senses, or one who has strength of mind, acquires liberations by virtue of that very conduct.

sn: आचाराज्जाजले प्राज्ञः क्षिप्रं धर्मवाप्नुयात्। एवं यः साधुभिर्दान्तश्चरेदद्रोहचेतसा॥
en: That wise man who, having controlled his senses, follows with a heart purged off all desire of injuring others, the conduct of the good, is, sure, O Jajali, to acquire the merit of righteousness.

sn: नद्यां चेह यथा काष्ठमुह्यसानं यदृच्छया। यदृच्छयैव काष्ठेन सन्धिं गच्छेत केनचित्॥ तत्रापराणि दारूणि संसृज्यन्ते परस्परम्। तृणकाष्ठकरीषाणि कदाचिन्न समीक्षया।॥
en: In this world, as in a river, a piece of wood that is being carried away by the current, is seen to come into contact (for some time) with another piece which is being likewise carried away. There on the current, other pieces of wood that had been collected together, are scen to again separate from one another. Grass, sticks, and cow dung cakes are seen to be joined together. This union is merely accidental and not brought about by any set design.

sn: यस्मान्नोद्विजते भूतं जातु किंचित् कथंचन। अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यः स प्राप्नोति सदा मुने॥
en: He, whom no creature fears, is himself, O ascetic, never frightened by any creature.

sn: यस्मादुद्विजते विद्वन् सर्वलोको वृकादिव। क्रोशतस्तीरमासाद्य यथा सर्वे जलेचराः॥
en: He, on the other hand, O learmed man, whom every creature fears like a wolf, becomes himself filled with fear as aquatic animals when compelled to leap on the shore from fear of the roaring Vadava fire.

sn: स भयं सर्वभूतेभ्यः सम्प्राप्नोति महामते। एवमेवायमाचारः प्रादुर्भूतो यतस्ततः। सहायवान् द्रव्यवान् यः सुभगोऽथ परस्तथा॥
en: This practice of universal harmlessness has thus originated. One may follow it by every means in his power. He who has a following and he who has riches, may seek to adopt it. It is sure to bring on prosperity and heaven.

sn: ततस्तानेव कवयः शास्त्रेषु प्रवदन्त्युत। कीर्त्यर्थमल्पहल्लेखाः पटवः कृत्स्ननिर्णया:॥
en: On account of their power to remove the fears of others, men having riches and followers are considered as foremost by the learned. Those, who seek common-place happiness, practise this duty of universal harmlessness for the sake of fame; while they, who are truly skilled, practise the same for attaining to Brahma.

sn: तपोभिर्यज्ञदानैश्च वाक्यैः प्रज्ञाश्रितैस्तथा। प्राप्नोत्यभयदानस्य यद् यत् फलमिहाश्नुते॥
en: Whatever fruits one enjoys by penances, by sacrifices, by making charities, by speaking the truth, and by seeking wisdom, may all be acquired by practising the duty of harmlessness.

sn: लोके यः सर्वभूतेभ्यो ददात्यभयदक्षिणाम्। स सर्वयज्ञैरीजानः प्राप्नोत्यभयदक्षिणाम्॥
en: That person who declares to all creatures the assurance of harmlessness acquires the merit of all the sacrifices and at last acquires fearlessness for himself as his meed.

sn: न भूतानामहिंसाया ज्यायान् धर्मोऽस्ति कश्चन। यस्मानोद्विजते भूतं जातु किंचित् कथंचन। सोऽभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यः सम्प्राप्नोति महामुने॥
en: There is no duty superior to the duty of not injuring other creatures. He whom, 0 great ascetic, no creature fears in the least, does not himself fear any creatures.

sn: यस्मादुद्विजते लोकः सर्पाद् वेश्मगतादिव। न स धर्ममवाप्नोति इहलोके परत्र च॥
en: He whom every body fears like a snake lying in ones bed-room, never acquires any merit in this world or in the next.

sn: सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्य सर्वभूतानि पश्यतः। देवाऽपि मार्गे मह्यन्ति अपदस्य पदैषिणः॥
en: The very celestials, in their search after it, become bewildered in the track of that person who rises above all states, the person, viz., who himself is the soul of all creatures and who considers all creatures as identical with his own self.

sn: दानं भूताभयस्याहुः सर्वदानेभ्य उत्तमम्। ब्रवीमि ते सत्यमिदं श्रद्दधस्व च जाजले॥
en: Of all gifts, the promise of harmlessness to all creatures in the greatest. I tell you truly, believe me, O Jajali.

sn: स एव सुभगो भूत्वा पुनर्भवति दुर्भगः। व्यापत्तिं कर्मणां दृष्ट्वा जुगुप्सन्ति जनाः सदा॥
en: One who performs acts at first acquires prosperity, but then he once more meets with adversity. Seeing the destruction of the merits of) acts, the wise do not speak highly of them.

sn: अकारणो हि नैवास्ति धर्मः सूक्ष्मो हि जाजले। भूतभव्यार्थमेवेह धर्मप्रवचनं कृतम्॥
en: There is no duty, O Jajali, that is not done by some motive (of happiness). Duty, however, is very subtile. Duties have been ordained in the Vedas for both Brahma and heaven.

sn: सूक्ष्मत्वान्न स विज्ञातुं शक्यते बहुनिह्नवः। उपलभ्यान्तरा चान्यानाचारानवबुध्यते॥
en: The subject of duties is full of secrets and mysteries. It is so subtile that one cannot understand it fully. Amongst various conflicting ordinances, some succeed in understanding duty by observing the acts of the good.

sn: ये च च्छिन्दन्ति वृषणान् ये च भिन्दन्ति नस्तकान्। वहन्ति महतो भारान् बधन्ति दमयन्ति च॥ हत्वा सत्त्वानि खादन्ति तान् कथं न विगर्हसे। मानुषा मानुषानेव दासभावेन भुञ्जते॥ वधबन्धनिरोधेन कारयन्ति दिवानिशम्। आत्मनश्चापि जानाति यद् दुःखं वधबन्धने॥
en: Why do you not destroy them who emasculate bulls and bore their noses and make them bear heavy loads and bind them and put them under various sorts of restraint, and who eat the flesh of living creatures after killing them. Men are seen to acquire men as slaves, and by beating, by binding, and by otherwise subjugating them, make them work day and night. These people are not ignorant of the pain that is caused by beating and chains.

sn: पञ्चेन्द्रियेषु भूतेषु सर्वं वसति दैवतम्। आदित्यश्चन्द्रमा वायुर्ब्रह्मा प्राणः क्रतुर्यमः॥
en: All the gods live in every creature who have the five senses. The Sun, the Moon, the God of Wind, Brahman, Vital Airs, Kratu and Yama, (these live in living creatures).

sn: तानि जीवानि विक्रय का मृतेषु विचारणा। अजोऽग्निर्वरुणो मेषः सूर्योऽश्वः पृथिवी विराट्॥
en: There are men who maintain themselves by trading in living creatures. When they acquire a living by such a sinful trade, what scruples have they in selling dead carcasses? The goat is Agni. The sheep is Varuna. The horse is the Sun. Earth is the god Virat.

sn: धेनुर्वत्सश्च सोमो वै विक्रीचैतन्त्र सिध्यति। का तैले का घृते ब्रह्मन् मधुन्यप्यौषधेषु वा॥
en: The cow and the calf are Soma. The man who sells these can never acquire success. But what fault is there in selling oil, clarified butter, honey, or drugs, Otwice-born one?

sn: अदंशमशके देशे सुखसंवर्धितान् यशून्। तांश्च मातुः प्रियाजानन्नाक्रम्य बहुधा नराः॥ बहुदंशाकुलान् देशान् नयन्ति बहुकर्दमान्। वाहसम्पीडिता धुर्याः सीदन्त्यविधिना परे॥
en: There are many animals which grow up in ease and comfort in places free from gnats and biting insects. Knowing that their mothers love them dearly, men, persecute them in various ways, and lead them into mire full of biting insects. Many beasts of burden are oppressed with heavy loads. Others, again, are made to languish for the treatment not sanctioned by the scriptures.

sn: न मन्ये भ्रूणहत्यापि विशिष्टा तेन कर्मणा। कृषि साध्विति मन्यन्ते सा च वृत्तिः सुदारुणा॥
en: I think that such acts of injury done to animals are the same as foeticide. People consider the calling of agriculture as sinless. That profession, however, is again fraught with cruelty.

sn: भूमिं भूमिशयांश्चैव हन्ति काष्ठमयोमुखम्। तथैवानडुहो युक्तान् समवेक्षस्व जाजले॥
en: The iron plough wounds the soil and many creatures which live there. Look, O Jajali, at those bullocks yoked to the plough.

sn: अघ्या इति गवां नाम क एता हन्तुमर्हति। महच्चकाराकुशलं वृषं गां वाऽऽलभेत् तु यः॥
en: Kine called in the Shrutis the Undestructible. That man commits a great iniquity who kills a bull or a cow.

sn: ऋषयो यतयो ह्येतन्नहुषे प्रत्यवेदयन्। गां मातरं चाप्यवधीवृषभं च प्रजापतिम्॥
en: In ancient times, many Rishis with controlled addressed Nahusha, saying,-You have, O king, killed a cow which is regarded in the scriptures like one's mother! You have also killed a bull, which is declared to be like the Creator himself.

sn: अकार्यं नहुषाकार्षीर्लप्स्यामस्त्वत्कृते व्यथाम्। शतं चैकं च रोगाणां सर्वभूतेष्वपातयन्॥
en: are senses You have committed a sin, O Nahusha, and we have been greatly pained at it!-For purifying Nahusha, however, they divided that sin, into a hundred and one parts and metamorphosing the pieces into diseases cast them among all creatures.

sn: ऋषयस्ते महाभागाः प्रजास्वेव हि जाजले। भ्रूणहं नहुषं त्वाहुन ते होध्यामहे हविः॥ इत्युक्त्वा ते महात्मानः सर्वे तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः। ऋषयो यतयः शान्तास्तपसा प्रत्यवेदयन्॥
en: Thus, O Jajali, did those highly blessed Rishis cast that sin of all living creatures and addressing Nuhusha who had committed foeticide, said,-We shall not be able to pour libations in your sacrifice! Thus said those great Rishis and Yatis conversant with truth, having learnt by their ascetic power that king Nahusha had not committed the sin intentionally.

sn: ईदृशानशिवान् घोरानाचारानिह जाजले। केवलाचरितत्वात् तु निपुणो नावबुद्ध्यसे॥
en: These, O Jajali, are some of the wicked and dreadful practices of this world. You do them because they are practised by all men from days of your, and not because they are approved of your purified understanding.

sn: कारणाद् धर्ममन्विच्छन्न लोकचरितं चरेत्। यो हन्याद् यश्च मां स्तौति तत्रापि शृणु जाजले॥
en: One should perform his duty guided by reasons, instead of blindly following the conduct of the world. Listen now, O Jajali, how I treat him who injures and him who praises me.

sn: समौ तावपि मे स्यातां न हि मेऽस्ति प्रियाप्रियम्। एतदीदृशकं धर्मं प्रशंसन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: I regard both of them equally. I have none whom I like and none whom I dislike. The wise speak highly of such a course of conduct as consistent with duty or religion.

sn: उपपत्त्या हि सम्पन्नो यतिभिश्चैव सेव्यते। सततं धर्मशीलैश्च निपुणेनोपलक्षितः॥
en: The Yatis also follow this course of conduct, which is consistent with reasons. The righteous always observe it with eyes having purified vision.

sn: जाजलिरुवाच अयं प्रवर्तितो धर्मस्तुलां धारयता त्वया। स्वर्गद्वारं च वृत्ति च भूतानामवरोत्स्यते॥
en: Jajali said This duty which you, O holder of scales, describe, shuts the door of heaven against all creatures and puts a stop to the very means of their livelihood.

sn: कृष्या ह्यन्नं प्रभवति ततस्त्वमपि जीवसि। पशुभिश्चौषधीभिश्च मा जीवन्ति वाणिज॥
en: From agriculture comes food. That food gives maintenance even to you. With the help of animals, crops and herbs, human beings, O trader, can maintain themselves.

sn: ततो यज्ञः प्रभवति नास्तिक्यमपि जल्पसि। न हि वर्तेदयं लोको वार्तामुत्सृज्य केवलाम्॥
en: From animals and food sacrifices originate. Your doctrines are atheistical. This world will come to an end if the means by which life is upheld have to be given up.

sn: तुलाधार उवाच वक्ष्यामि जाजले वृत्तिं नास्मि ब्राह्मण नास्तिकः। न यज्ञं च विनिन्दामि यज्ञवित् तु सुदुर्लभः॥४॥
en: Tuladhara said I shall now describe the topic of the means of livelihood. I am not, O Brahmana, an atheist. I do not speak against Sacrifices. The man, however, is very rare who is truly an adept in sacrifice.

sn: नमो ब्राह्मणयज्ञाय ये च यज्ञविदो जनाः। स्वयज्ञं ब्राह्मणा हित्वा क्षत्रयज्ञमिहास्थिताः॥
en: I bow to that Sacrifice which is laid down for Brahmanas, I bow also to them who are adepts in that Sacrifice. Alas, having abandoned the Sacrifice that is ordained for them, the Brahmanas have begun to perform Sacrifices that are for Kashatriyas.

sn: लुब्धैर्वित्तपरैर्ब्रह्मन् नास्तिकैः सम्प्रवर्तितम्। वेदवादानविज्ञाय सत्याभासमिवानृतम्॥
en: Many persons of faith, O twice-born one, who hanker after wealth, without having understood the true meaning of the sayings of the Shrutis, and proclaiming things that are in sooth false but that have the show of truth, have introduced many sorts of Sacrifices,

sn: इदं देयमिदं देयमिति चायं प्रशस्यते। अतः स्तैन्यं प्रभवति विकर्माणि च जाजले॥
en: This should be given away in this Sacrifice. This other thing should be given away in this other Sacrifice. The first of this is very praiseworthy.-The result, however, of all this, ( Jajali, is that theft and many evil acts originate.

sn: यदेव सुकृतं हव्यं तेन तुष्यन्ति देवताः। नमस्कारेण हविषा स्वाध्यायैरौषधैस्तथा॥
en: It should be known that only that sacrificial offering which was gained by fair means can please the deities. There are abundant proofs in the scriptures that the adoration of the gods may be done with bows, with libations poured on the fire, with recitation or changing of the Vedas, and with plants and herbs.

sn: पूजा स्याद् देवतानां हि यथा शास्त्रनिदर्शनम्। इष्टापूर्तादसाधूनां विगुणा जायते प्रजा॥
en: Sinful men get wicked children, from their religious acts. Covetous men beget covetous children, and contented men beget contented children.

sn: लुब्धेभ्यो जायते लुब्धः समेभ्यो जायते समः। यजमाना यथाऽऽत्मानमृत्विजश्च तथा प्रजाः॥ यज्ञात् प्रजा प्रभवति नभसोऽम्भ इवामलम्।
en: If the sacrificer and the priest allow themselves to be guided by desire of fruit, their children take the stigma. If, however, they are not moved by the desire of fruit, their children become the same. From Sacrifices originate children like clear water from the sky.

sn: अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिर्ब्रह्मचादित्यमुपगच्छति॥ आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिर्वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः।
en: The libations poured on the sacrificial fire get up to the Sun. From the Sun originates rain. From rain comes food. From food are born living creatures.

sn: तस्मात् सुनिष्ठिताः पूर्वे सर्वान् कामांश्च लेभिरे॥ अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी आशीर्भिर्वीरुधोऽभवन्।
en: In days of yore inen religiously given to Sacrifices used to attain therefrom the fruition of all their wishes. The Earth gave crops without cultivation. The blessings of the Rishis produced herbs and plants.

sn: न ते यज्ञेष्वात्मसु वा फलं पश्यन्ति किंचन॥ शङ्कमानाः फलं यज्ञे ये यजेरन् कथंचन। जायन्तेऽसाधवो धूर्ता लुब्धा वित्तप्रयोजनाः॥ स स्म पापकृतां लोकान् गच्छेदशुभकर्मणा। प्रमाणमप्रमाणेन यः कुर्यादशुभं नरः॥ पापात्मा सोऽकृतप्रज्ञः सदैवेह द्विजोत्तम।
en: The men of ancient times never celebrated Sacrifices from desire of fruits and never considered themselves as bound to enjoy those fruits. Those who somehow or other celebrate Sacrifices, doubting their efficacy, are born in their next lives as dishonest, wily, and greedy men greatly covetous of wealth. That man who by the help of false reasoning show all the authoritative scriptures as fraught with evil, is certain to go, for such a sinful deed, into the regions of the sinful. Such a man is surely possessed of a sinful soul, O foremost of Brahmanas, and always remains here, shorn of wisdom.

sn: कर्तव्यमिति कर्तव्यं वेत्ति वै ब्राह्मणो भयम्॥ ब्रह्मैव वर्तते लोके नैव कर्तव्यतां पुनः।
en: That man who consider those acts as bounden which have been laid down in the Vedas and directed to be performed every day, who is filled with fear if he fails to perform them any day, who considers all the essentials of Sacrifices as identical with Brahma, and who never considers himself as the actor, is truly a Brahinana.

sn: विगुणं च पुनः कर्म ज्याय इत्यनुशुश्रुम॥ सर्वभूतोपघातश्च फलभावे च संयमः।
en: If the acts of such a person remain incomplete or if their completion is hindered by all unclean animals, even then those acts arc, as we have heard, of supreme efficacy. If, however, those acts are performed from desire of fruit then expiation would become necessary.

sn: सत्ययज्ञा दमयज्ञा अर्थलुब्धार्थतृप्तयः॥ उत्पन्नत्यागिनः सर्वे जना आसन्नमत्सराः।
en: They, who seek the acquisition of the highest object of life, who do not hanker after carthly riches, who do not care for future provision, and who are shorn of envy, follow the course of truth and practise self-control as their Sacrifice.

sn: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञतत्त्वज्ञाः स्वयज्ञपरिनिष्ठिताः॥ ब्राह्यं वेदमधीयन्तस्तोषयन्त्यपरानपि।
en: They who know the distinction between body and soul, who are given to Yoga, and who meditate on OM, always succeed in pleasing others.

sn: अखिलं दैवतं सर्वं ब्रह्म ब्रह्मणि संश्रितम्॥ तुष्यन्ति तृप्यतो देवास्तृप्तास्तृप्तस्य जाजले।
en: The universal Brahma, which is the soul of all the gods, lives in him who is conversant with Brahma. When, therefore, such a man eats and is pleased, all the gods, O Jajali, become pleased and are contented.

sn: यथा सर्वरसैस्तृप्तो नाभिनन्दति किंचन॥ तथा प्रज्ञानतृप्तस्य नित्यतृप्तिः सुखोदया।
en: As one who is satisfied with all sorts of taste fells no desire for any particular taste, similarly one who is pleased with knowledge has eternal gratification which to him is a source of perfect happiness.

sn: धर्माधारा धर्मसुखाः कृत्स्नव्यवसितास्तथा।॥ आस्ति नस्तत्त्वतो भूय इति प्राज्ञस्त्ववेक्षते। ते
en: Those wise men who are the refuge of righteousness and whose joy is in righteousness, are persons who have certain knowledge of what is duty and what is otherwise. One endued with such wisdom always considers all things in the universe as emanating from his own self.

sn: ज्ञानविज्ञानिनः केचित् परं पारं तितीर्षवः॥ अतीव पुण्यदं पुण्यं पुण्याभिजनसंहितम्। यत्र गत्वा नशोचन्ति च च्यवन्ति व्यथन्ति च॥ तु तद् ब्रह्मणः स्थान प्राप्नुवन्तीह सात्त्विकाः।
en: Some who are gifted with knowledge, who try to reach the other shore (of this ocean of life), and who have faith, succeed in going to the region of Brahman, which yields great blessings, is highly sacred, and inhabited by pious men,-a region which is freed from sorrow, whence no body returns, and where there is no agitation or pain.

sn: नैव ते स्वर्गमिच्छन्ति न यजन्ति यशोधनैः॥ सतां वानुवर्तन्ते यजन्ते चाविहिंसया।
en: Such men do not hanker after heaven. They do not worship Brahma in costly Sacrifices. They trade the path of the virtuous. The Sacrifices they celebrate are performed without injury to any creature.

sn: वनस्पतीनोषधीयश्च फलं मूलं च ते विदुः॥ न चैतानृत्विजो लुब्धा याजयन्ति फलार्थिनः।
en: These men consider trees, herbs, fruits and roots as the only sacrificial offerings. Greedy priests who seek riches, never officiate at the sacrifices of these (poor) inen.

sn: स्वमेव चार्थं कुर्वाणा यज्ञं चक्रुः पुनर्द्विजाः॥ परिनिष्ठतकर्माणः प्रजानुग्रहकाम्यया।
en: These regenerate men, although all their acts have been done, still perform sacrifices for doing good to all creatures making their own selves as sacrificial offerings.

sn: तस्मात् तानृत्विजो लुब्धा याजयन्त्यशुभान् नरान्॥ प्रापयेयुः प्रजाः स्वर्गे स्वधर्माचरणेन वै। इति मे वर्तते बुद्धिः समा सर्वत्र जाजले॥
en: Therefore, greedy priests officiate at the Sacrifices of only those misguided persons who, without trying to attain to Liberation, scck for heaven. Those, however, who are really good, always try, by performing their own duties, to cause others to go to heaven. LoO king at both these kinds of conduct, O Jajali, I have come to regard all creatures impartially.

sn: यानि यज्ञेष्विहेज्यन्ति सदा प्राज्ञा द्विजर्षभा। तेन ते देवयानेन पथा यान्ति महामुने।।३०
en: Gifted with wisdom, many leading Brahmanas celebrate Sacrifices. By performing those Sacrifices, they walk, O great ascetic, along the path wended by the gods.

sn: आवृत्तिस्तस्य चैकस्य नास्त्यावृत्तिर्मनीषिणः। उभौ तौ देवयानेन गच्छतो जाजले यथा॥
en: Of the class of Sacrificers there is return (from the region where they go). Of those, however, who are truly wise there is no return. Although both classes of sacrificers, O Jajali, wend the path trodden by the gods, yet such is the difference between their ultimate ends.

sn: सव्यं चैषामनडुहो युज्यन्ति च वहन्ति च। स्वयमुस्राश्च दुह्यन्ते मन:संकल्पसिद्धिभिः॥
en: On account of the success of the purposes such men form in their minds, bulls, without being forced thereto, willingly set their shoulders to the plough for helping the cultivation and to the yoke for dragging their Cars, and kine pour forth milk from udders without being touched by human hands.

sn: स्वयं यूपानुपादाय यजन्ते स्वाप्तदक्षिणैः। यस्तथा भावितात्मा स्यात् स गामालब्धुमर्हति॥
en: Creating sacrificial stakes by their willforce, they celebrate many kinds of Sacrifice with profuse presents. One who is of such a purified soul may kill a cow.

sn: ओषधीभिस्तथा ब्रह्मन् यजेरंस्ते न तादृशाः। इति त्यागं पुरस्कृत्य तादृशं प्रब्रवीमि ते॥
en: They, therefore, who are otherwise, should celebrate Sacrifices with herbs and plants, Because Renunciation has such merit, there I have kept it in view in speaking to you.

sn: निराशिषमनारम्भं निर्नपस्कारमस्तुतिम्। अक्षीणं क्षीणकर्माणं तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: The gods consider him a Brahmana who has cast of all desire of fruit, who does not exert for worldly acts, who never bows down his head to any one, who never praises others, and who is gifted with strength though his acts have all been weakened.

sn: न श्रावयन् न च यजन् न ददद् ब्राह्मणेषु च। काम्यां वृत्तिं लिप्समानः किंगतिं याति जाजले। इदं तु दैवतं कृत्वा यथा यज्ञमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: What, O Jajali, will be the end of him who does not recite the Vedas to others, who does not celebrate Sacrifices, who does not make gifts to Brahmans, and who follows a calling in which every sort of desire is indulged? By duly respecting, however, the duties which belong to Renunciation, one is sure to attain to Brahima.

sn: जाजलिरुवाच न वै मुनीनां शृणुमः स्म तत्त्वं पृच्छामि ते वाणिज कष्टमेतत्। पूर्वे पूर्वे चास्य नावेक्षमाणा नातः परं तमृषयः स्थापयन्ति॥
en: We had never before, O son of a trader, heard of these subtle doctrines of ascetics who perform only mental Sacrifices. These doctrines are very difficult to understand. It is, therefore, I ask you (about them). The sages of yore were not followers of these doctrines of Yoga. Hence the succeeding sages have not mentioned them.

sn: यस्मिन्नेवात्मतीर्थे न पशवः प्राप्नुयुर्मखम्। अथ स्म कर्मणा केन वाणि प्राप्नुयात् सुखम्॥ शंस ते तन्महाप्राज्ञ भृशं वै श्रद्दधामि ते।
en: If you hold that only men mentally bent like brutes fail to achieve sacrifices in the soil of the Soul, then, O son of a trader, by what acts would they succeed in securing their happiness? Tell me this, O you of great wisdom. I have great faith in your words.

sn: तुलाधार उवाच उत यज्ञा उतायज्ञा मखं नार्हन्ति ते क्वचित्॥ आज्येन पयसा दना पूर्णाहुत्या विशेषतः। बालैः शृङ्गेण पादेन सम्भरत्येव गौर्मखम्॥
en: Tuladhara said Sometimes sacrifices celebrated by some persons do not become sacrifices. These men, it should be said, do not deserve performing any sacrifice. Regarding the faithful, however, only one thing, viz., the cow, is fit for upholding all sacrifices by means of full libations of clarified butter, milk, and curds, the hair at end of her tail, her horns, and her hoofs.

sn: पत्नी चानेन विधिना प्रकरोति नियोजयन्। इष्टं तु दैवतं कृत्वा यथा यज्ञमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: In celebrating sacrifices, however, according to the mode I have mentioned, one may convert Faith into his married wife, for dedicating such offerings to the gods. By duly honouring such sacrifices, one is sure to attain to Brahma.

sn: पुरोडाशो हि सर्वेषां पशूनां मध्य उच्यते। सर्वा नद्यः सरस्वत्यः सर्वे पुण्या: शिलोच्चयाः॥
en: Excluding all animals, the rice-ball is a worthy offering in sacrifices. All rivers are as sacred as the Sarasvati, and all mountains are sacred.

sn: जाजले तीर्थमात्मैव मा स्म देशातिथिर्भव। एतानीदृशकान् धर्मानाचरनिह जाजले।॥ कारणैर्धर्मन्विच्छन् स लोकानाप्नुते शुभान्।
en: O Jajali, the Soul is itself a sacred shrine. Do not roam about on the Earth for visiting sacred places! A person, by following these duties and by seeking to acquire merit according to his own ability, undoubtedly succeeds in getting blessed regions hereafter.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एतानीदृशकान् धर्मांस्तुलाधारः प्रशंसति॥ उपपत्त्याभिसम्पन्नान् नित्यं सद्भिर्निषेवितान्॥
en: These are the duties, O Yudhishthira, which Tuladhara spoke highly of-duties which are consistent with reason, and which are always followed by the good and the wise.

sn: तुलाधार उवाच सद्भिर्वा यदि वासद्भिः पन्थानमिमतास्थितम्। प्रत्यक्षं क्रियतां साधु ततो ज्ञास्यसि तद् यथा॥
en: Tuladhara said See with your own eyes, O Jajali, who, amongst the good or otherwise, have followed this path of duty which I have spoken of! You will understand properly how the truth stands.

sn: एते शकुन्ता बहवः समन्ताद् विचरन्ति ह। तवोत्तमाङ्गे सम्भूताः श्येनाश्चान्याश्च जायतः॥
en: See, many birds are roving in the sky! Amongst them are those who were brought up on your head, as also many hawks and many others of different kinds.

sn: आहूयैनान् महाब्रह्मन् विशमानांस्ततस्ततः। पश्येमान् हस्तपादैश्च श्लिष्टान् देहेषु सर्वशः॥
en: See, O Brahmana, those birds have got their wings and legs for entering their respective nests. Call them, O twice-born one.

sn: सम्भावयन्ति पितरं त्वया सम्भाविताः खगाः। असंशयं पिता वै त्वं पुत्रानाहूय जाजले॥
en: There, those birds, treated affectionately by you, are showing their love for you who are their father! Forsooth, you are their father, O Jajali! Do you call your children!

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो जाजलिना तेन समाहूताः पतत्रिणः। वाचमुच्चारयन्ति स्म धर्मस्य वचनात् किल॥
en: Bhishma continued-Then those birds, summoned by Jajali, answered according to the dictates of that religion which preaches abstention from injury to any creature.

sn: अहिंसादिकृतं कर्म इह चैव परत्र च। श्रद्धां निहन्ति वै ब्रह्मन् सा हता हन्ति तं नरम्॥
en: All acts that done without injuring any creature come to use both here and hereafter. Those acts, however, that injure others, destroy faith, and faith being destroyed, brings ruin on the destroyer.

sn: समानां श्रद्दधानानां संयतानां सुचेतसाम्। कुर्वतां यज्ञ इत्येव न यज्ञो जातु नेष्यते॥
en: The sacrifice of those who regard equally both acquisition and non-acquisition, who are endued with faith, who are self controlled, who have tranquil minds, and who celebrate sacrifices from a sense of duty yield fruits.

sn: श्रद्धा वैवस्वती सेयं सूर्यस्य दुहिता द्विज। सावित्री प्रसवित्री च बहिर्वाङ्मनसी ततः॥
en: Faith in Brahma is the daughter of the SunGod, O twice-bom one. She is the protectress and the giver of good birth. Faith is superior to the merit begotten by recitations and meditation.

sn: वाग्वृद्धं त्रायते श्रद्धा मनोवृद्धं च भारत। श्रद्धावृद्धं वाङ्मनसी न कर्म त्रातुमर्हति॥
en: An act vitiated by faulty speech is saved by Faith. An act sullied by defect of mind is saved by Faith. But neither speech nor mind can save an act which is sullied by want of Faith.

sn: अत्र गाथा ब्रह्मगीताः कीर्तयन्ति पुराविदः। शुचेरश्रद्दधानस्य श्रद्दधानस्य चाशुचेः॥ देवा वित्तममन्यन्त सदृशं यज्ञकर्मणि। श्रोत्रियस्य कदर्यस्य वदान्यस्य च वाधुषेः॥
en: Men who know the past recite in this connection the following verse sung by Brahman. The gods regard as equal the offerings in sacrifices of a person who is pure but wanting in Faith, and of another who is impure but has Faith. After mature consideration the gods have considered equal the food, again, of a person conversant with the Vedas but miserly in conduct, and that of a usurer who is liberal in conduct.

sn: मीमांसित्वोभयं देवाः सममन्नमकल्पयन्। प्रजापतिस्तानुवाच विषमं कृतमित्युत॥ श्रद्धापूतं वदान्यस्य हतमश्रद्धयेतरत्। भोज्यमन्नं वदान्यस्य कदर्यस्य न वाधुषेः॥
en: The supreme Lord of all creatures, then told them that they had committed a mistake, The food of a liberal person is purified by Faith. The food, however, of the person who has Faith is lost for such want of Faith. The food of a liberal usurer can be accepted but not the food of a miser.

sn: अश्रद्दधान एवैको देवानां नाहते हविः। तस्यैवान्नं न भोक्तव्यमिति धर्मविदो विदुः॥
en: Only one person in the world viz., he who has no Faith, is unfit to make offerings to the gods. The food of only such a man is unfit to be eaten. This is the opinion of men who know duties.

sn: अश्रद्धा परमं पापं श्रद्धा पापप्रमोचिनी। जहाति पापं श्रद्धावान् सर्पो जीर्णामिव त्वचम्॥
en: Want of Faith is a great sin. Faith is a purifier of sins. Like a snake casting off its slough, the man of Faith succeeds in shaking off all his sins.

sn: ज्यायसी या पवित्राणां निवृत्तिः श्रद्धया सह। निवृत्तशीलदोषो य: श्रद्धावान् पूत एव सः॥
en: The religion of abstention with Faith is superior to all shortcomings of conduct, he who follows Faith, becomes purified.

sn: किं तस्य तपसा कार्यं किं वृत्तेन किमात्मना। श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः॥
en: What need has such a person of penances, or of conduct, or of endurance? Every man has Faith. Faith, however, is of three sorts, viz., as partaking of the nature of the qualities of goodness, darkness, and ignorance, and according to the nature of Faith which one has, one is named.

sn: इति धर्मः समाख्यातः सद्भिर्धर्मार्थदर्शिभिः। वयं जिज्ञासमानास्तु सम्प्राप्ता धर्मदर्शनात्॥
en: Person gifted with goodness and endued with insight into the true import of morality have thus described the subject of duties. We have, on enquiry, got all this from the sage Dharınadarshana.

sn: श्रद्धां कुरु महाप्राज्ञ ततः प्राप्स्यसि यत् परम्। श्रद्धावाश्रद्दधानश्च धर्मश्चैव हि जाजले। स्ववर्त्मनि स्थितश्चैव गरीयानेव जाजले॥
en: O you of great wisdom, adopt Faith, for you will then acquire what is superior. He who believes (in the sayings of the Shrutis), and who acts according to their sense, is, indeed, of righteous soul. O Jajali, he who follows his own path is surely a superior person.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततोऽचिरेण कालेन तुलाधारः स एव च। दिवं गत्वा महाप्राज्ञौ विहरेतां यथासुखम्॥ स्वं स्वं स्थानमुपागम्य स्वकर्मफलनिर्जितम्। एवं बहुविधार्थं च तुलाधारेण भाषितम्॥
en: Bhishma said After a short time Tuladhara and Jajali, both of whom had been gifted with great wisdom, ascended to heaven and played there in great happiness, having reached their respective places won by their respective deeds. Tuladhara had spoken many truths of this sort.

sn: सम्यक् चेदमुपालब्धो धर्मश्चोक्तः सनातनः। तस्य विख्यातवीर्यस्य श्रुत्वा वाक्यानि स द्विजः॥
en: That great person understood this religion perfectly. These eternal duties were accordingly declared by him.

sn: तुलाधारस्य कौन्तेय शान्तिमेवान्वपद्यत। एवं बहुमतार्थं च तुलाधारेण भाषितम्। यथौपम्योपदेशेन किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि।॥
en: O son of Kunti, having heard these words of Tuladhara of celebrated energy, the twiceborn Jajali betook himself to tranquillity. In this way many truths of deep sense were spoken by Tuladhara, illustrated by examples for instruction. What other truths do you wish to hear?

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: भीष्म उवाच भीष्म अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। प्रजारनामनुकम्पार्थं गीतं राज्ञा विचख्नुना॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited an old discourse of what was recited by king Vicharakhu through pity for all creatures.

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: छिन्नस्थूणं वृषं दृष्ट्वा विलापं च गवां भृशम्। गोग्रहे यज्ञवाटस्य प्रेक्षमाणः स पार्थिवः॥ स्वस्ति गोभ्योऽस्तु लोकेषु ततो निर्वचनं कृतम्। हिंसायां हि प्रवृत्तायामाशीरेषा तु कल्पिता॥
en: Seeing the mangled body of a bull, and hearing the highly painful groans of the kine in a cow-killing sacrifice, and observing the cruel Brahmanas collected there for assisting at the ceremonies, that king said these words:Prosperity to all the kine in the world!-When the slaughter had begun, these

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: अव्यवस्थितमर्यादैविमूढ स्तिकैनरैः। संशयात्मभिरव्यक्तैर्हिसा समनुवर्णिता॥
en: And the king further said,-Only those who transgress fixed limits, who are shorn of intelligence, who are atheists and sceptics, and who desire the acquisition of celebrity by sacrifices and religious rites, speak highly of the destruction of animals in sacrifices.

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: सर्वकर्मस्वहिंसा हि धर्मात्मा मनुरब्रवीत्। कामकाराद् विहिंसन्ति बहिर्वेद्यां पशून् नराः॥
en: The pious Manu has spoken highly of harmlessness in all acts. Indeed, men kill animals in sacrifices, actuated only by the desire of fruit. an a

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: तस्मात् प्रमाणत: कार्यो धर्मः सूक्ष्मो विजानता। अहिंसा सर्वभूतेभ्यो धर्मेभ्यो ज्यायसी मता॥
en: Hence, guided by authority one conversant (with the scriptures) should practise the true course of duty which is highly subtile. Harmlessness to all creatures is the highest of all duties.

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: उपोष्य संशितो भूत्वा हित्वा वेदकृताः श्रुतीः। आचार इत्यनाचारः कृपणा: फलहेतवः॥
en: Living near inhabited place and practising rigid vows, and disregarding the fruits of Vedic acts, one should give up the life of house-holder, adopting that of Renunciation. Only they who are mean are actuated by the desire of fruit.

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: यदि यज्ञांश्च वृक्षांश्च यूपांश्चोद्दिश्य मानवाः। वृथा मांसं न खादन्ति नैष धर्मः प्रशस्यते॥
en: Mentioning respectfully sacrifices and trees and sacrificial stakes, men do not eat tainted meat. This practice, however, is now worthy of praise.

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: सुरा मत्स्या मधु मासंमासवं कृसरौदनम्। धूर्तेः प्रवर्तितं ह्येतन्नैतद् वेदेषु कल्पितम्॥
en: Knavas have introduced wine, fish, honey, meat, alchohol, and preparations of rice and sesame seeds. The use of these is not sanctioned in the Vedas.

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: मानान्मोहाच्च लोभाच्च लौल्यमेतत्प्रकल्पितम्। विष्णुमेवाभिजानन्ति सर्वयज्ञेषु ब्राह्मणाः॥
en: The hankering after these originates from pride, error of judgement, and cupidity. The Brahmanas realise the presence of Vishnu in every sacrifice.

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: पायसैः सुमनोभिश्च तस्यापि यजनं स्मृतम्। यज्ञियाश्चैव ये वृक्षा वेदेषु परिकल्पिता:॥ यच्चापि किंचित् कर्तव्यमन्यच्चोक्षैः सुसंस्कृतम्। महासत्त्वैः शुद्धभावैः सर्वं देवार्हमेव तत्॥
en: His adoration, it has been laid down, should be made with sweet Payasa. (The leaves and flower of such trees as have been mentioned in the Vedas, whatever act is considered as worthy and whatever else is held as pure by persons of pure hearts and purified natures and those eminent for knowledge and holiness, are well worthy of being offered to the Supreme God and not unworthy of His acceptance.

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच शरीरमापदश्चापि विवदन्त्यविहिंसतः। कथं यात्रा शरीरस्य निरारम्भस्य सेत्स्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said The body and all sorts of dangers and calamities continually fight with each other, How, therefore, will a person who is absolutely free from the desire of injuring and who on this account will not be able to act succeed in maintaining his body.

description: The story of king Vicharakhu about sacrifices
sn: भीष्म उवाच यथा शरीरं न ग्लायेन्येयान्मृत्युवशं यथा। तथा कर्मसु वर्तेत समर्थो धर्ममाचरेत्॥
en: Bhishma said One should, when able, acquire merit and act in such a way that his body may not languish and suffer pain, and that death may not come.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं कार्यं परीक्षेत शीघ्रं वाथ चिरेण वा। सर्वथा कार्यदुर्गेऽस्मिन् भवान् नः परमो गुरुः॥
en: Yudhishthira said You, O grandfather, are our highest preceptor in the matter of all acts which it is difficult to perform. I ask, how should one judge of an act regarding one's obligation to do it or of abstaining from it? Is it to be judged quickly or with delay?

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। चिरकारेस्तु यत् पूर्वं वृत्तमाङ्गिरसे कुले॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse of what took place regarding Chirakarin born in the race of Angirasa.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरकारिक भद्रं ते भद्रं ते चिरकारिक। चिरकारी हि मेधावी नापराध्यति कर्मसु॥
en: Twice blessed be the man who thinks long before he acts! One man who thinks long before he acts is surely possessed of great intelligence. Such a man never offends in an act.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरकारी महाप्राज्ञो गौतमस्याभवत् सुतः। चिरेण सर्वकार्याणि विमृश्यार्थान् प्रपद्यते॥
en: There was once a highly wise man by name Chirakarin, who was the son of Gautama. Thinking for a long time upon every aspect of proposed acts, he used to do all he had to do.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरं स चिन्तयत्यर्थांश्चिरं जाग्रच्चिरं स्वपन्। चिरं कार्याभिपत्तिं च चिरकारी तथोच्यते॥
en: He passed by the name of Chirakarin because he used to think long upon all matters, to remain awake for a long time, to sleep for a long time, and to take a long time in performing such acts.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: अलसग्रहणं प्राप्तो दुर्मेधावी तथोच्यते। बुद्धिलाघवयुक्तेन जनेनादीर्घदर्शिना॥
en: But still he passed for an idle man. He was also considered as a foolish person, by every person of a light understanding and shorn of foresight.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: व्यभिचारे तु कस्मिश्चिद् व्यतिक्रम्यापरान् सुतान्। पित्रोक्तः कुपितेनाथ जहीमां जननीमिति॥
en: On a certain occasion, seeing an act of great fault in his wife, the father Gautama, passing over his other children commanded in anger this Chirakarin, saying,-kill this women!

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: इत्युक्त्वा स तदा विप्रो गौतमो जपतां वरः। अविमृश्य महाभागो वनमेव जगाम सः॥
en: Having said these words without much thought, the learned Gautama, that foremost of persons engaged in the practice of Yoga, that highly blessed ascetic, left for the forest.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: स तथेति चिरेणोक्त्वा स्वभावाच्चिरकारिकः। विमृश्य चिरकारित्वाच्चिन्तयामास वैचिरम्॥
en: Having after a long while assented to it, saying,-So be it,-Chirakarin, on account of his very nature, and owing to his habit of never performing any act without much thought, began to think for a long while.-पितुराज्ञां कथं कुर्यां न हन्यां मातरं कथम्।

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: कथं धर्मच्छलेनास्मिन् निमज्जेयमसाधुवत्।१०॥
en: How shall I obey the order of my father, and yet how avoid killing my mother? How shall I avoid sinking, like a wicked man, into sin in this plight in which contradictory duties are dragging me into opposite directions?

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: पितुराज्ञा परो धर्मः स्वधर्मो मातृरक्षणम्। अस्वतन्त्रं च पुत्रत्वं किं तु मां नानुपीडयेत॥
en: Obedience to the orders of the father forms the highest merit. The protection of the mother again is a clear duty. The condition of a son is fraught with dependence. How shall I avoid being affected by sin?

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: स्त्रियं हत्वा मातरं च को हि जातु सुखी भवेत्। पितरं चाप्यवज्ञाय कः प्रतिष्ठामवाप्नुयात्॥
en: Who is there that can be happy after having killed a woman, especially his mother? Who again can acquire prosperity and fame by disobeying his own father.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: अनवज्ञा पितुर्युक्ता धारणं मातृरक्षणम्। युक्तक्षमावुभावेतौ नातिवर्तेत मां कथम्॥
en: Regard for the father's order is obligatory. The protection of my mother is equally a duty. How shall I so act that both obligations may be satisfied?

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: पिता ह्यात्मानमाधत्ते जायायां जज्ञिवानिति। शीलचारित्रगोत्रस्य धारणार्थं कुलस्य च॥
en: The father puts his own self within the mother's womb and takes birth as the son, for continuing his practices, conduct, name and race.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: सोऽहं मात्रा स्वयं पित्रा पुत्रत्वे प्रकृतः पुनः विज्ञानं मे कथं न स्याद् द्वौ बुद्ध्ये चात्मसम्भवम्॥
en: I have been begotten as a son by both my mother and my father. Knowing as I do my own birth, why should I not have this knowledge?

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: जातकर्मणि यत् प्राह पिता यच्चोपकर्मणि। पर्याप्तः स दृढीकारः पितुर्गौरवनिश्चये।१६।।
en: The words spoken by the father while performing the initial rite consequent upon birth, and those that were spoken by him on the occasion of the subsidiary rite are sufficient (evidence) for settling the respect due to him and, indeed, confirm the respect actually paid to him.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: गुरुरम्यः परो धर्मः पोषणाध्यापनान्वितः। पिता यदाह धर्मः स वेदेष्वपि सुनिश्चितः॥
en: On account of his bringing up the son and instructing him, the father is the son's foremost of superiors and the highest religion. The very Vedas sanction it as certain that the son should consider what the father says as his highest duty.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: प्रीतिमात्रं पितुः पुत्रः सर्वं पुत्रस्य वै पिता। शरीरादीनि देयानि पिता त्वेकः प्रयच्छति॥
en: The son is only a source of joy to his father. The father is all in all to a son. The body and all else that the son has he has got from the father alone.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: तस्मात् पितुर्वचः कार्यं न विचार्यं कदाचन। पातकान्यपि पूयन्ते पितुः शासनकारिणः॥
en: Hence, the commands of the father should be obeyed without ever questioning them in the least. The very sins of one who obeys his father are cleansed.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: भोग्ये भोज्ये प्रवचने सर्वलोकनिदर्शने। भर्चा चैव समायोगे सीमन्तोन्नयने तथा॥
en: The father is the giver of all articles of enjoyment, of all articles of food, of instructions in the Vedas, and of all other knowledge of the world. The father is the performer of such rites as Garbhadhana (the ceremony for the attainment of puberty by the wife), and Simantonnayana the ceremony performed by the husband in the fourth, sixth, or eighth, month of gestation.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: पिता धर्म: पिता स्वर्गः पिता हि परमं तपः। पितरि प्रीतिमापन्ने सर्वाः प्रीयन्ति देवताः॥
en: The father is religion. The father is heaven. The father is the highest penance. The father being pleased all the gods are pleased.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: आशिषस्ता भजन्त्येनं परुषं प्राह यत् पिता। निष्कृतिः सर्वपापानां पिता यच्चाभिनन्दति॥
en: Whatever words are spoken by the father, become blessings that attach to the son. The words of joy that the father utters purify the son of all his sins.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: मुच्यते बन्धनात् पुष्पं फलं वृक्षात् प्रमुच्यते। क्लिश्यन्नपि सुतं स्नेहैः पिता पुत्रं न मुञ्चति॥
en: The flower is seen to drop down from the stalk. The fruit is seen to drop down from the tree. But the father, in whatever difficulty he may be, moved by parental affection, never leaves the son.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: एतद् विचिन्तितं तावत् पुत्रस्य पितृगौरवम्। पिता नाल्पतरं स्थानं चिन्तयिष्यामि मातरम्॥
en: These then are my thoughts upon the respect due from the son to the father. The father is not an ordinary object to the son, I shall now think upon the mother.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: यो ह्ययं मयि संघातो मयत्वे पाञ्चभौतिकः। यस्य मे जननी हेतुः पावकस्य यथारणिः॥
en: Of this the mother is the principal cause of those union of the five elements in me due to my birth as a human being, as the fire-sticks of fire.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: माता देहारणिः पुंसां सर्वस्यार्तस्य निर्वृतिः। मातृलोभे सनाथत्वमनाथत्वं विपर्यये॥
en: The mother is as the fire-stick about the bodies of all men. She is the medicine for all sorts of calamities. The existence of the mother grants protection to one; the reverse deprives one of all protection.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: न च शोचति नाप्येनं स्थाविर्यमपकर्षति। श्रिया हीनोऽपि यो गेहमम्बेति प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: The man who, thought shorn of prosperity, enters his house uttering the words-0 mother!-does not suffer from grief. Nor does decrepitude ever attack him.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: पुत्रपौत्रोपपन्नोऽपि जननीं यः समाश्रितः। अपि वर्षशतस्यान्ते स द्विहायनवच्चरेत्॥
en: A person whose mother exists, even if he has sons and grandsons and even if he is a hundred years old, looks like a child of two.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: समर्थं वासमर्थं वा कृशं वाप्यकृशं तथा। रक्षत्येव सुतं माता नान्यः पोष्टा विधानतः॥
en: Able or disabled, lean or robust, the son is always protected by the mother. None else, according to the Scripture, is the son's protector.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: तदा स वृद्धो भवति तदा भवति दुःखितः। तदा शून्यं जगत् तस्य यदा मात्रा वियुज्यते॥
en: When the mother leaves him then does the son become old, then does he become stricken with grief, then does the world look empty in his eyes.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: नास्ति मातृसमा छाया नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः। नास्ति मातृसमं त्राणं नास्ति मातृसमा प्रिया॥
en: There is no shelter like the mother. There is no refuge like the mother. There is no defence like the mother. There is no one dearer than the mother.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: कुक्षिसंधारणाद् धात्री जननाज्जननी स्मृता। अङ्गानां वर्धनादम्बा वीरसूत्वेन वीरसूः॥
en: For having borne him in her womb the mother is the son's Dhatri. For having been the principal cause of his birth, she is his Janani. For having reared his young limbs, she is called Amva. For giving birth to a child possessed of courage, she is called Virasu.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: शिशोः शुश्रूषणाच्छुश्रूर्माता देहमनन्तरम्। चेतनावान् नरो हन्याद् यस्य नासुषिरं शिरः॥
en: For nursing and loO king after the son, she is called Shushru. The mother is one's own body. What rational man is there who would kill his mother to whose care only his own head did not lie on the street like a dry gourd?

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: दम्पत्योः प्राणसंश्लेषे योऽभिसंधिः कृतः किल। तं माता च पिता चेति भूतार्थो मातरि स्थितः॥
en: When husband and wife unite themselves for procreation, the desire for a son is cherished by both, but about its fruition more depends upon the mother than on the father.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: माता जानाति यद्गोत्रं माता जानाति यस्य सः। मातुर्भरणमात्रेण प्रीतिः स्नेहः पितुः प्रजाः॥
en: The mother knows the family in which the son is born and the father who has begotten him. From the time of conception the mother beings to show affection to her child and find joy in him. On the other hand, the Scriptures hold that the issue belong to the father only.
