description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: पाणिबन्धं स्वयं कृत्वा सह धर्ममुपेत्य च। यदा यास्यन्ति पुरुषाः स्त्रियो नार्हन्ति वाच्यताम्॥
en: If men, after taking wives and pledging themselves to acquire religious merit without being dissociated from them, seek union with other people's wives, they then cease to deserve respect.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: भरणाद्धि स्त्रियो भर्ता पालनाद्धि पतिस्तथा। गुणस्यास्य निवृत्तौ तु न भर्ता न पुनः पतिः॥
en: The husband, because he maintains the wife, is called Bharta, and he is called Pati, because he protects her. When he fails to discharge these two functions, he ceases to both Bhartri and Pati.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: एवं स्त्री नापरानोति नर एवापराध्यति। व्युच्चरंश्च महादोषं नर एवापराध्यति॥
en: Then again woman can commit no fault. It is man only who commits commits faults. By committing an act of adultery, the man only becomes sullied with sin.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: स्त्रिया हि परमो भर्ता दैवतं परमं स्मृतम्। तस्यात्मना तु सदृशमात्मानं परमं ददौ॥
en: It has been said that the husband is the highest object with the wife and the highest god to her. My mother resigned her sacred person to one who came to her in the shape of hcr own husband.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: नापराधोऽस्ति नारीणां नर एवापराध्यति। सर्वकार्यापराध्यत्वान्नापराध्यन्ति चाङ्गनाः॥
en: Women can commit no sin. It is man who becomes sullied with sin. Indeed, on account of the natural weakness of the sex as shown in every act, and their liability to solicitation, women cannot be considered as offenders.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: यश्च नोक्तोऽथ निर्देशः स्त्रिया मैथुनतृप्तये। तस्य स्मारयतो व्यक्तमधर्मो नास्ति संशयः॥
en: Then again the sinfulness is evident of Indra himself who made the recollection of the request that had been made to him in days of yore by woman. There is no doubt that my mother is sinless.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: एवं नारी मातरं च गौरवे चाधिके स्थिताम्। अवध्यां तु विजानीयुः पशवोऽप्यविचक्षणाः॥
en: She whom I have been ordered to kill is a woman. That woman is again my own mother. She occupies, therefore, a place of greater respect. The very beasts which are irrational, know that the mother should not be killed.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: देवतानां समावायमेकस्थं पितरं विदुः। मानां देवातनां च स्नेहादभ्येति मातरम्॥
en: The father must be known to be a combination of all the gods together. The mother, however, is a combination of all mortal creatures and all the gods.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: एवं विमृशतस्तस्य चिरकारितया बहु। दीर्घ कालो व्यतिक्रान्तस्ततोऽस्याभ्यागमत् पिता॥
en: On account of his habit of reflecting long before acting, Gautama's son Chirakarin, by thinking thus, passed a long time. After many days, his father Gautama came back.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: मेधातिथिर्महाप्राज्ञो गौतमस्तपसि स्थितः। विमृश्य तेन कालेन पन्याः संस्थाव्यतिक्रमम्॥
en: Gifted with great wisdom, Medhatithi of Gautama's race. Practising penances, returned, convinced, after having meditated for that long time, of the impropriety of the punishment he had ordered to be inflicted upon his wife.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: सोऽब्रवीद् भृशंसंतप्तो दुःखेनाश्रूणि वर्तयन्। श्रुतधैर्यप्रसादेन पश्चात्तापमुपागतः॥
en: Burning with grief and shedding profuse tears, for repentance had come to hiin on account of the wholesome effects of that calmness of temper which is caused by a knowledge of the scriptures, he said:-

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: आश्रमं मम सम्प्राप्तस्त्रिलोकेशः पुरंदरः। अतिथिव्रतमास्थाय ब्राह्मणं रूपमास्थितः॥
en: The lord of the three worlds, viz., Purandara, came to my asylum, in the guise of a Brahmana asking for hospitality.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: स मया सान्त्वितो वाग्भिः स्वागतेनाभिपूजितः। अर्घ्यं पाद्यं यथान्यायं मया च प्रतिपादितः॥
en: He was received by me with becoming words, and welcomed and presented in due form with water to wash his feet and the usual offerings of the Arghya. I also gave him the rest he had asked for.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: परवानस्मि चेत्युक्तः प्रणयिष्यति तेन च। अत्र चाकुशले जाते स्त्रिया नास्ति व्यतिक्रमः॥
en: I further told him that I had acquired a protector in him, I thought that such conduct on my part would make him treat me as a friend. When, however, not-withstanding all this, he misbehaved himself, my wife Ahalya could not be considered to have committed any sin.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: एवं न स्त्री न चैवाहं नाध्वगस्त्रिदशेश्वरः। अपराध्यति धर्मस्य प्रमादस्त्वपराध्यति॥
en: It seems that neither my wife, nor myself, nor Indra himself who while passing through the firmament had seen my wife, could he held to have committed any sin. The blame really is the result of the carelessness of my Yoga power.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: ईर्ष्याजं व्यसनं प्राहुस्तेन चैवोर्ध्व रेतसः। ईर्ष्णया त्वहमाक्षिप्तो मग्नो दुष्कृतसागरे॥
en: The sages have said that all calamities originate from envy, which, in its turn, springs from mistaken judgement. By that envy, also, I have been dragged from where I was plunged into an ocean of sin.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: हत्वा साध्वी च नारी च व्यसनित्वाच्च वासिताम्। भर्तव्यत्वेन भार्यां च को न मां तारयिष्यति॥
en: Alas, I have killed a woman,-a woman who is again my wife-one, who, on account of her sharing her husband's misfortunes passed by the name of Vasita, one, who was called Bharya owing to my obligation for maintaining her, Who is there who can save me from this sin ?

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: अन्तरेण मयाऽऽज्ञप्तश्चिरकारीत्युदारधीः। यद्यद्य चिरकारी स्यात् स मां त्रायेत पातकात्॥
en: Acting carelessly I ordered the great Chirakarin! If on the present occasion he proves true to his name then may he save me from this sin.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरकारिक भद्रं ते भद्रं ते चिरकारिक। यद्यद्य चिरकारी त्वं ततोऽसि चिरकारिकः॥
en: Twice blessed be you, O Chirakarin! If on this occasion you have delayed accomplishing the work, then are you truly worthy of your name!

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: त्राहि मां मातरं चैव तपो यच्चार्जितं मया। आत्मानं पातकेभ्यश्च भवाद्य चिरकारिकः॥
en: Save me, and your mother, and the penances I have won, as also your own self, from grave sins:-Be you truly a Chirakarika to-day!

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: सहजं चिरकारित्वमतिप्रज्ञतया तव। सफलं तत् तथा तेऽस्तु भवाद्य चिरकारिकः॥
en: Ordinarily, on account of your great wisdom you take a long time for reflection before performing any act. Let not you conduct be otherwise to-day! Be you a true Chirakarika to-day.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरमाशंसितो मात्रा चिरं गर्भेण धारितः। सफलं चिरकारित्वं कुरु त्वं चिरकारिक॥
en: Your mother had expected you coming for a long time. For a long time did she carry you in her womb. O Chirakarika, let your habit of reflecting long before acting yield beneficial results to-day!

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरायते च संतापाच्चिरं स्वपिति वारितः। तु :खितः। आवयोश्चिरसंतापादवेक्ष्य चिरकारिकः॥
en: Perhaps, my son Chirakarika is delaying today, anticipating the sorrow it would cause me! Perhaps, he is sleeping over that order, bearing it in his heart. Perhaps, he is delaying, anticipating the grief it would cause both him and me, and thinking upon the circumstances of the case!-

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: एवं स दुःखितो राजन् महर्षिगौतमस्तदा। चिरकारि ददर्शाथ पुत्रं स्थितमथान्तिके॥
en: Repenting in this way, O king, the great Rishi Guatama then saw his son Chirakarin sitting near him.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरकारी पितरं दृष्ट्वा परमदुः शस्त्रं त्यक्त्वा ततो मूर्धा प्रसादायोपचक्रमे॥
en: Seeing his father return to their house, the son Chirakarin, laden with grief, cast away the weapon and bowing his head began to pacify Gautama.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: गौतमस्तं ततो दृष्ट्वा शिरसा पतितं भुवि। पत्नीं चैव निराकारां परामभ्यागमन्मुदम्॥
en: Seeing his son prostrated before him with bent head, and seeing also his wife almost petrified with shame, the Rishi became filled with great joy.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: न हि सा तेन सम्भेदं पत्नी नीता महात्मना। विजने चाश्रमस्थेन पुत्रश्चापि समाहितः॥
en: From the time the great Rishi, living in that solitary hermitage did not live separately from his wife or his careful son.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: हन्या इति समादेशः शस्त्रपाणै सुते स्थिते। विनीते प्रसवत्यर्थे विवासे चात्मकर्मसु॥
en: Having made the command that his wife should be killed he had gone away from his asylum for accomplishing some object of his own. Since then his son had stood in an humble manner, weapon in hand, for satisfying that command on his mother.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: बुद्धिशासीत् सुतं दृष्ट्वा पितुरचरणयोर्नतम्। शस्त्रग्रहणचापल्यं संवृणोति भयादिति॥
en: Seeing that son prostrated at his feet, the father thought that, filled with fear, he was asking for pardon for the offence he had perpetrated in taking up a weapon.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: ततः पित्रा चिरं स्तुत्वा चिरं चाघ्राय मूर्धनि। चिरं दो• परिष्वज्य चिरं जीवेत्युदाहृतः॥
en: The father praised his son for a long time, and smelt his head for a long time, and embraced him for a long time, and blessed him, uttering the words-Do you live long.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: एवं स गौतमः पुत्रं प्रीतिहर्षगुणैर्युतः। अभिनन्द्य महाप्राज्ञ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then, filled with joy and contented with what had taken place, Gautama, O you of great Wisdom, said to his son.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरकारिक भद्रं ते चिरकारी चिरं भव। चिराय यदि ते सौम्य चिरमस्मि न दुःखितः॥
en: Blessed be you, O Chirakarika! Do you always think long before acting! By your delay in carrying out my command you have to-day made me happy for ever!

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: गाथाश्चाप्यब्रवीद् विद्वान् गौतमो मुनिसत्तमः। चिरकारिषु धीरेषु गुणोद्देशसमाश्रयाः॥
en: That learned and best of Rishis then saying these verses upon the subject of the merits of such cool men as think for a long time before doing any work,-

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरेण मित्रं बघ्नीयाच्चिरेण च कृतं त्यजेत्। चिरेण हि कृतं मित्रं चिरं धारणमर्हति॥
en: If it be the death of a friend, one should perform it after a long time. If one has to give up a project already begun, he should do it after a long time. A friendship that is contracted after a long examination lasts for a long time.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: रागे दर्पे च माने च द्रोहे पापे च कर्मणि। अप्रिये चैव कर्तव्ये चिरकारी प्रशस्यते॥
en: In yielding to anger, to arrogance, to pride, to disputes, to sinful deeds, and in performing all disagreeable works, he who delays long, deserves praise!

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: बन्धूनां सुहृदां चैव भृत्यानां स्त्रीजनस्य च। अव्यक्तेष्वपराधेषु चिरकारी प्रशस्यते॥
en: When the offence is not distinctly proved against a relative, a friend, a servant, or a wife, he who thinks long before inflicting the punishment, is praised.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: एवं स गौतमस्तत्र प्रीतः पुत्रस्य भारत। कर्मणा तेन कौरव्य चिरकारितया तथा॥
en: Thus, O Bharata, was Gautama pleased with his son, O you of Kuru's race or that act of delay on the latter's part in satisfying the former's order.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: एवं सर्वेषु कार्येषु विमृश्य पुरुषस्ततः। चिरेण निश्चयं कृत्वा चिरं न परितप्यते॥
en: In all deeds a man should, in this wise, think for a long time and then settle what he should do. By acting thus one is sure to avoid grief for a long time.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरं धारयते रोष चिरं कर्म नियच्छति। पश्चात्तापकरं कर्म न किंचिदुपपद्यते॥ चिरं वृद्धानुपासीत चिरमन्वास्य पूजयेत्। चिरं धर्मं निषेवेत कुर्याच्चान्वेषणं चिरम्॥
en: That man who nurses his anger for a long time, who thinks long before doing any work, never does any act which produces repentance. One should wait for a long time upon the aged, and sitting near them show them respect. One should satisfy his duties for a long time and be engaged for a long time in determining them.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: चिरमन्वास्य विदुषश्चिरं शिष्टान् निषेव्य च। चिरं विनीय चात्मानं चिरं यात्यनवज्ञताम्॥
en: Serving for a long time the learned, and reverentially serving for a long time those who are good in conduct and keeping one's soul for a long while under proper control, one succeeds in enjoying the respect of the world for a long time.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: ब्रुवतश्च परस्यापि वाक्यं धर्मोपसंहितम्। चिरं पृष्टोऽपि च ब्रूयाच्चिरं न परितप्यते॥
en: One instructing others on the subject of religion and duty, should, when asked by another for information on those subjects, take a long time to think before giving an answer. He will not then repent.

description: The determination of an obligatory act
sn: उपास्य बहुलास्तस्मिन्नाश्रमे सुमहातपाः। समाः स्वर्गं गतो विप्रः पुत्रेण सहितस्तदा॥
en: Regarding Gautama of austere penances, that Rishi, having worshipped the gods for a long while in that asylum of his, at last went up to heaven with his son.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं राजा प्रजा रक्षेन्न च किंचित् प्रघातयेत्। पृच्छामि त्वां सतां श्रेष्ठ तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhisthira said How, indeed, should the king protect his subjects without harming anybody? I ask you this, O grandfather, tell me, O foremost of good men!

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। धुमत्सेनस्य संवादं राज्ञा सत्यवता सह॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old conversation between Dyumutsena and king Satyavat.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: अव्याहृतं व्याजहार सत्यवानिति नः श्रुतम्। वधायोनीयमानेषु पितुरेवानुशासनात्॥
en: We have heard that upon a certain number of individuals having been brought out for execution at the command of his father, prince Satyavat gave vent to certain words that had never before been said by any body else.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: अधर्मतां याति धर्मो यात्यधर्मश्च धर्मताम्। वधो नाम भवेद् धर्मो नैतद् भवितुमर्हति॥
en: Sometimes virtue assumes the form of sin, and sin assumes the form of virtue. It can never be possible that destruction of individuals can ever be a virtuous act.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: धुमत्सेन उवाच अथ चेदवधो धर्मोऽधर्मः को जातु चिद् भवेत्। दस्यवश्चेन्न हन्येरन् सत्यवन् संकरो भवेत्॥
en: Dyumutsena said If the sparing of those who should be killed, by virtue, if robbers be spared, O Satyavat, then all distinctions (between virtue and vice) would disappear.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: ममेदमिति नास्यैतत् प्रवर्तेत कलौ युगे। लोकयात्रा न चैव स्यादथ चेद् वेत्थ शंस नः॥
en: 'This is mine,'-'This is not his'-ideas like these will not prevail in the Kali age. (If the wicked be not punished) the affairs of the world will come to an end. If you know how the world may go on, then describe it to ine.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: सत्यवानुवाच सर्व एते त्रयो वर्णाः कार्या ब्राह्मणबन्धनाः। धर्मपाशनिबद्धानामन्योऽप्येवं चरिष्यति॥
en: Satyvat said The three other castes should be placed under the control of the Brahmanas. If those three castes be kept within the limits of virtue, then the subsidiary caste (that have sprung from intermixture) will imitate their practises.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: यो यस्तेषामपचरेत् तमाचक्षीत वै द्विजः। अयं मे न शृणोतीति तस्मिन् राजा प्रधारयेत्॥
en: Of them those who will violate (these commands) be reported to the king.-This one does not care commands!-upon such a complaint being lodged by a Brahmana, the king should punish the offender.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: तत्त्वाभेदेन यच्छास्त्रं तत् कार्यं नान्यथाविधम्। असमीक्ष्यैव कर्माणि नीतिशास्त्रं यथाविधि॥
en: Without destroying the body of the offender the king should punish him as ordained by the Scriptures. The king should not act otherwise, neglecting to think properly upon the character shall for my of the offence and upon the science of morality.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: दस्यून् निहन्ति वै राजा भूयसो वाप्यनागसः। भार्या माता पिता पुत्रो हन्यन्ते पुरुषेण ते। परेणापकृतो राजा तस्मात् सम्यक् प्रधारयेत्॥
en: By killing the wicked, the king kills a large number of innocent men. See, by killing a single robber, his wife, mother, father, and children are all killed. When injured by a wicked person, the king should, therefore, think seriously on the question of punishment.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: असाधुश्चैव पुरुषो लभते शीलमेकदा। साधोश्चापि ह्यसाधुभ्यः शोभना जायते प्रजा॥
en: Sometimes a wicked man is seen to imbibe good conduct from a pious person. It is seen that good children spring from wicked persons.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: न मूलघातः कर्तव्यो नैष धर्मः सनातनः। अपि स्वल्पवधेनैव प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते॥ उद्वेजनेन बन्धेन विरूपकरणेन च। वधदण्डेन ते क्लिश्या न पुरोहितसंसदि॥ यदा पुरोहितं वा ते पर्येयुः शरणैषिणः। करिष्यामः पुनर्ब्रह्मन् न पापमिति वादिनः॥ तदा विसर्गमर्हाः स्युरितीदं धातृशासनम्। बिभ्रद् दण्डाजिनं मुण्डो ब्राह्मणोऽर्हति शासनम्॥
en: The wicked, therefore, should not be uprooted. The extermination of the wicked is not quite of a piece with eternal practice. By punishing them gently, by depriving them of all their riches, by chains and imprisonment, by disfiguring them they may be made to expiate their offences. Their relatives should not be punished by the infliction of capital sentences on them. If in the presence of the priest and others, they give themselves up to him from desire of protection, and swear, saying,-0 Brahmana, we shall never again commit any sin,-they would then be discharged without any punishment. This is command of the Creator himself. Even the Brahmana who puts on a deer-skin and the wand and has his head shaved, should be punished.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: गरीयांसो गरीयांसमपराधे पुनः पुनः। तदा विसर्गमर्हन्ति न यथा प्रथमे तथा॥
en: If great men transgress, their punishment should be proportionate to their greatness. As regards them who offend again and again, they should not be let off without punishment as on their first offence.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: द्युमत्सेन उवाच यत्र यत्रैव शक्येरन् संयन्तुं समये प्रजाः। स तावान् प्रोच्यते धर्मो यावन्न प्रतिलझ्यते॥
en: Dyumatsena said As long as those limits within which men should be kept are not outstripped, so long are they known by the name of virtue.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: अहन्यमानेषु पुनः सर्वमेव पराभवेत्। पूर्वे पूर्वतरे चैव सुशास्या ह्यभवन् जनाः॥
en: If they who transgressed those limits were not punished with death, those barriers would soon be destroyed. Men of more ancient times were capable of being governed easily.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: मृदवः सत्यभूयिष्ठा अल्पद्रोहाल्पमन्यवः। पुरा धिगदण्ड एवासीद् वाग्दण्डस्तदनन्तरम्॥
en: They were very truthful. They were little bent upon quarrelling. They seldom gave way to anger, or, if they did, their anger never became ungovernable. In those days mere disapproval of offence sufficient punishment. After this came the punishment represented by harsh words or censures.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: आसीदादानदण्डोऽपि वधदण्डोऽद्य वर्तते। वधेनापि न शक्यन्ते नियन्तुमपरे जनाः॥
en: Then came the punishment of fines and forfeitures. In this age, however, the punishment of death is in vogue. Wickedness has increased to such an extent that by killing one others cannot be controlled.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: नैव दस्युर्मनुष्याणां न देवानामिति श्रुतिः। न गन्धर्वपितृणां च कः कस्येह न कश्चन॥
en: The robber has no connection with men, with the gods, with the Gandharvas, and with the Pitris. What is he to whom? He is not any was body to any one. This is the saying of the Shrutis.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: पद्मं श्मशानादादत्ते पिशाचाच्चापि दैवतम्। तेषु यः समयं कश्चित् कुर्वीत हतबुद्धिषु॥
en: The robber takes away the ornaments of dead bodies from cemeteries, and consumes from men afflicted by spirits. That man is a fool who would enter into any agreement with those miscreants or exact any oath from them.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: सत्यवानुवाच तान् न शक्नोषि चेत् साधून् परित्रातुमहिंसया। कस्यचिद् भूतभव्यस्य लाभेनान्तं तथा कुरु॥
en: Satyavat said If you cannot make honest men of those rogues and in saying them by means other than destruction, do you then root them out by celebrating some sacrifice.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: राजानो लोकयात्रार्थं तप्यन्ते परमं तपः। तेऽपत्रपन्ति तादृग्भ्यस्तथावृत्ता भवन्ति च।॥
en: Kings practise severe penances for the sake of enabling their subjects to grow prosperous in their callings. When thieves and robbers increase in their territories they become ashamed. They, therefore, perform penances for putting down thefts and robberies and making their subjects live happily.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: वित्रास्यमानाः सुकृतो न कामाद् जन्ति दुष्कृतीन्। सुकृतेनैव राजानो भूयिष्ठं शासते प्रजाः॥
en: Subjects can be made honest by, being only terrorized. Good kings never kill the wicked from motives of retribution. Good kings succeed in ruling their subjects properly with the help of good conduct.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: श्रेयसः श्रेयसोऽप्येवं वृत्तं लोकोऽनुवर्तते। सदैव हि गुरोर्वृत्तमनुवर्तन्ति मानवाः॥
en: If the king act properly, the high class subjects imitate him. The inferior people, again, imitate their immediate superiors. Men are so formed that they imitate those whom they consider as their betters.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: आत्मानमसमाधाय समाधित्सति यः परान्। विषयेष्विन्द्रियवशं मानवाः प्रहसन्ति तम्।॥
en: That king who, without controlling himself, seeks to govern others (from evil ways) becomes an object of ridicule with all men on account of his being engaged in the enjoyment of all worldly pleasures as a slave of his senses.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: यो राज्ञो दम्भमोहेन किंचित् कुर्यादसाम्प्रतम्। सर्वोपयैर्नियम्यः स तथा पापान्निवर्तते॥
en: That man who, through pride or mistaken judgement, offends against the king in any way, should be governed by every means. It is by this way that he is prevented from committing fresh offences.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: आत्मैवादौ नियन्तव्यो दुष्कृतं संनियच्छता। दण्डयेच्च महादण्डैरपि बन्धूननन्तरान्॥
en: The king should first control his own self if he mean to control other offenders. He should punish sufficiently even his friends and near relatives.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: यत्र वै पापकृन्नचो न महद् दुःखमर्च्छति। वर्धन्ते तत्र पापानि धर्मो हसति च ध्रुवम्॥
en: In that kingdom where a wicked offender is not sufficiently punished, offences increase and virtue decreases forsooth.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: इति कारुण्यशीलस्तु विद्वान् वै ब्राह्मणोऽन्वशात्। इति चैवानुशिष्टोऽस्मि पूर्व स्तात पितामहैः॥ आश्वासयद्भिः सुभृशमनुक्रोशात् तथैव च। एतत् प्रथमकल्पेन राजा कृतयुगे जयेत्॥
en: Formerly, a Brahmana, endued with mercy and knowledge, taught me this. And, son, I have thus been instructed by also our grandfathers of olden days, who gave such assurances of harınlessness to people, actuated by pity. Their words were,-In the Krita age, kings should govern their subjects by adopting harmless ways.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: पादोनेनापि धर्मेण गच्छेत् त्रेतायुगे तथा। द्वापरे तु द्विपादेन पादेन त्वधरे युगे॥
en: In that Treta age kings should act according to ways that follow virtue lessened by a fourth part. In the Dvapara age, they act according to ways conforming with virtue decreased by half, and in the age following, according to ways conforming with virtue decreased by threefourths.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: तथा कलियुगे प्राप्ते राज्ञो दुश्चरितेन ह। भवेत् कालविशेषण कला धर्मस्य षोडशी॥
en: When the Kali age begins, through the wickedness of kings and no account of the nature of the age itself, fifteen parts of even that fourth portion of virtue disappear, a sixteenth portion thereof being all that then remains.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: अथ प्रथमकल्पेन सत्यवन् संकरो भवेत्। आयुः शक्तिं च कालं च निर्दिश्य तप आदिशेत्॥
en: If, O Satyavat, by adopting the way mentioned first, confusion sets in, the king, considering the span of human life, the strength of human beings, and the nature of the time that has come, should give punishments.

description: How should a king protect his subjects without harming any body. The conversation between Dyumutsena and Satyavat
sn: सत्याय हि यथा नेह जह्याद् धर्मफलं महत्। भूतानामनुकम्पार्थं मनुः स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Indeed, Manu, the son of the Self create, has, through pity for human beings, indicated the way by means of which men may follow knowledge for the sake of Liberation."

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अविरोधेन भूतानां योगः षाड्गुण्यकारकः। यः स्यादुभयभाग्धर्मस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥ गार्हस्थ्यस्य च धर्मस्य योगधर्मस्य चोभयोः। अदूरसम्प्रस्थितयोः किंस्विच्छ्रेयः पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have already explained to me O grandfather, how the religion of Yoga, which produces six well-known attributes, may be adopted and practised without injuring any creature. Describe to me, O grandfather that religion which produces enjoyment and Liberation. O these two, both of which lead to the same end, which is superior?”

sn: भीष्म उवाच उभौ धर्मो महाभागावुभौ परमदुश्चरौ। उभौ महाफलौ तौ तु सद्भिराचरितावुभौ॥
en: Bhishma said “Both courses of duty are highly sacred. Both are extremely difficult of performance. Both yield high fruits. Both are practised by those who are admittedly good.

sn: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि प्रामाण्यमुभयोस्तयोः। शृणुष्वैकमनाः पार्थ च्छिन्नधर्मार्थसंशयम्॥
en: I shall now describe to you on the authoritativeness of both these duties, for removing your doubts about their true meaning. Listen to me with rapt attention.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। कपिलस्य गोश्च संवादं तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Kapila and the cow. Listen to it, O Yudhishthira.

sn: आम्नायमनुपश्यन् हि पुराणं शाश्वतं ध्रुवम्। नहुषः पूर्वमालेभे त्वष्टुर्गामिति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that in days of yore when the god Tashtri came to the palace of king Nahusha, the latter, for satisfying the duties of hospitality, was on the point of slaying a cow in accordance with the true, ancient, and eternal injunction of the Vedas.

sn: तां नियुक्तामदीनात्मा सत्त्वस्थः संयमे रतः। ज्ञानवान् नियताहारो ददर्श कपिलस्तथा॥ स बुद्धिमुत्तमां प्राप्तो नैष्ठिकीमकुतोभयाम्। सतीमशिथिला सत्यां वेदा इत्यब्रवीत् सकृत्॥ तां गाषिः स्यूमरश्मिः प्रविश्य यतिमब्रवीत्। हंहो वेदा यदि मता धर्माः केनापरे मताः॥
en: Seeing that cow tied for slaughter, Kapila of liberal soul, ever following Sattvika duties, always engaged in controlling his senses, endued with true knowledge, and sparing in diet, having gained an excellent understanding that was characterised by faith, perfectly fearless, beneficial, firm, and ever directed towards truth, uttered-Alas, ye Vedas!-At that time a Rishi by name Syumarashmi, entering the form of that cow, addressed the Yati Kapila, saying,-Silence, O Kapila! If the Vedas are censurable, whence have those other duties come to regarded as authoritative.

sn: तपस्विनो धृतिमन्तः श्रुतिविज्ञानचक्षुषः। सर्वमाष हि मन्यन्ते व्याहृतं विदितात्मनः॥
en: Men given to penances and endued with intelligence, and who have the Shrutis and knowledge for their eyes, consider the injunctions of the Vedas, which have been declared through and compiled by the Rishis, to be the words of God himself.

sn: तस्यैवं गततृष्णस्य विज्वरस्य निराशिषः। का विवक्षास्ति वेदेषु निरारम्भस्य सर्वतः॥
en: What can a person say regarding the contents of the Vedas when these are the words of the Supreme Being himself, who is shorn of the desire of fruit, who is without the fever, who is addicted to nothing, and who is shorn of all exertion.

sn: कपिल उवाच नाहं वेदान् विनिन्दामि न विवक्ष्यामि कर्हिचित्। पृथगाश्रमिणां कर्माण्येकार्थानीति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: Kapila said-I do not censure the Vedas, I do not wish to disparage them. We have heard that the different classes of duty laid down for the different modes of life, all lead to the same end.

sn: गच्छत्येव परित्यागी वानप्रस्थश्च गच्छति। गृहस्थो ब्रह्मचारी च उभौ तावपि गच्छतः॥
en: The Sanyasin attains to a high end. The herinit also attains to a hight end. Both the other two, also, viz., the house-holder and the Brahmacharin, attain to the same end.

sn: देवयाना हि पन्थानश्चत्वारः शाश्वता मता: एषां ज्याय: कनीयस्त्वं फलेषूक्तं बलाबलम्॥
en: All the four modes of life have always been considered as Deva-yana ways. The respective strength or weakness of these, are represented by their respective superiority or inferiority, has been declared in the character of their respective ends.

sn: एवं विदित्वा सर्वार्थानारभेतेति वैदिकम्। नारभेतेति चान्यत्र नैष्ठिकी श्रूयते श्रुतिः॥
en: Knowing these, perform acts which lead to heaven and other blessings,—this is a Vedic declaration.-Do not perform acts,—this also is another obligatory declaration of the Vedas.

sn: अनालम्भे ह्यदोषः स्यादालम्भे दोष उत्तमः। एवं स्थितस्य शास्त्रस्य दुर्विज्ञेयं बलाबलम्॥
en: If abstention from acts produces merit, then their performance must be highly reprehensible. When the scriptures say this, the strength or weakness of particular sayings must be difficult to determine.

sn: यद्यत्र किञ्चित् प्रत्यक्षमहिंसायाः परं मतम्। ऋते त्वागमशास्त्रेभ्यो ब्रूहि तद् यदि पश्यसि॥
en: If you know of any class of duty which is superior to the religion of harmlessness, and which depends upon direct evidence instead of that of the scriptures, do you then describe them to me,

sn: स्यूमरश्मिरुवाच स्वर्गकामो यजेतेति सततं श्रूयते श्रुतिः। फलं प्रकल्प्य पूर्वं हि ततो यज्ञः प्रतायते॥
en: One should celebrate sacrifices from desire of heaven'-we always hear this Shruti. Thinking first of the fruit, one makes preparations for sacrifice.

sn: अजश्चाश्वश्च मेषश्च गौश्च पक्षिगणाश्च ये। ग्राम्यारण्याचौषधयः प्राणस्यानमिति श्रुतिः॥
en: Goat, horse, sheep, cow, all sorts of birds, domestic or wild, and herbs and plants, constitute the food of living creatures. We have heard this.

sn: तथैवान्नं ह्यहरहः सायंप्रातर्निरूप्यते। पशवश्चाथ धान्य च यज्ञस्याङ्गमिति श्रुतिः॥
en: Food again ought to be taken day after day morning and evening. Again the Shruti says that aniinals and grain form the limbs of Sacrifice.

sn: एतानि सह यज्ञेन प्रजापतिकल्पयत्। तेन प्रजापतिर्देवान् यज्ञेनायजत प्रभुः॥
en: The Lord of the universe created them along with Sacrifice. The powerful Lord of all creatures made the god celebrate sacrifices with their help.

sn: तदन्योन्यवराः सर्वे प्राणिनः सप्त सप्तधा। यज्ञेषूपाकृतं विश्वं प्राहुरुत्तमसंज्ञितम्॥
en: Altogether seven (domestic) and seven (wild animals are declared fit for sacrifice. Instead of all being equally fit, each succeeding one is inferior to the preceding one. The Vedas again say that the whole universe is appointed for sacrifice. The Vedas have appointed Purusha for the same purpose.

sn: एतच्चैवाभ्यनुज्ञातं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरैस्तथा। को जातु न विचिन्वीत विद्वान् स्वां शक्तिमात्मनः।।२३।
en: This again has been sanctioned by men of ancient times. What learned man is there who does not sclect, according to his own power, individuals from among living creatures for sacrifice?

sn: पशवश्च मनुष्याश्च दुमाश्चौषधिभिः सह। स्वर्गमेवाभिकाङ्क्षन्ते न च स्वर्गस्ततो मखात्॥
en: The inferior animals, human beings, trees and herbs, all desire for the attainment of heaven. There is no means, however, except sacrifice, by which they can acquire the fruition of that desire.

sn: ओषध्यः पशवो वृक्षा वीरुदाज्यं पयो दधि। हविर्भूमिर्दिशः श्रद्धा कालश्चैतानि द्वादश॥ ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि यजमानश्च षोडश। अग्नि यो गृहपतिः स सप्तदश उच्यते॥ अङ्गान्येतानि यज्ञस्य यज्ञो मूलमिति श्रुतिः। आज्येन पयसा दधा शकृताऽऽमिक्षया त्वचा॥ वालैः शृङ्गेण पादेन सम्भवत्येव गौमखम्। एवं प्रत्येकशः सर्वं यद् यदस्य विधीयते॥ यज्ञं वहन्ति सम्भूय सहत्विग्भिः सदक्षिणैः। संहृत्यैतानि सर्वाणि यज्ञं निवर्तयन्त्युत॥
en: The deciduous herbs, animals, trees, creepers, clarified butter, milk, curds, meat and other selected things land, the points of the horizon, faith, and time which forms the twelfth, the Richs, the Yajushes, the Samans, and the sacrificer himself froming the sixteenth, and Fire which should be known as the householder, these seventeen are said to be the linbs of Sacrifice. Sacrifice, the Shruti says, is the root of the world and its movement. With clarified butter, milk, curds, dung, curds mixed with milk, skin, the hair in her tail, horns, and hoofs, the cow alone is able to supply all the necessaries of sacrifice. For particular sacrifices are sanctioned particular ones, Ritwijas and presents together sustain Sacrifices. By collecting these things together, people celebrate sacrifices.

sn: यज्ञार्थानि हि सृष्टानि यथार्था श्रूयते श्रुतिः। एवं पूर्वतरा: सर्वे प्रवृत्ताश्चैव मानवाः॥
en: This Shruti, quite of a piece with the truth, is heard that all things have been created for the celebration of Sacrifice. It was thus that all men of yore undertook the celebration of sacrifices.

sn: न हिनस्ति नारभते नाभिद्रुह्यति किंचन। यज्ञो यष्टव्य इत्येव यो यजत्यफलेप्सया॥
en: Regarding that person, however, who celebrates sacrifices, because of the belief that sacrifices should be celebrated not for the sake of fruit or reward, it is seen that he does not injure any creature or treat any one with hostility, or engage in the performance of any worldly work.

sn: यज्ञाङ्गान्यपि चैतानि यज्ञोक्तान्यनुपूर्वशः। विधिना विधियुक्तानि धारयन्ति परस्परम्॥
en: The things named above as the limbs of sacrifice, and those that have been mentioned as necessary in sacrifices and that are indicated in the ordinances, all maintain one another when used according to the approved ritual.

sn: आम्नायमाएं पश्यामि यस्मिन् वेदाः प्रतिष्ठिताः। तं विद्वांसोऽनुपश्यन्ति ब्राह्मणस्यानुदर्शनात्॥
en: I see also the Smritis compiled by the Rishis, into which the Vedas have been introduced. Learned men regard them as authoritative on account of their following the Brahmanas.

sn: ब्राह्मणप्रभवो यज्ञो ब्राह्मणार्पण एव च। अनुयज्ञं जगत् सर्वं यज्ञश्चानुजगत् सदा॥
en: Sacrifices have the Brahmanas for their progenitor, and truly they depend upon the Brahmanas. The whole universe depends upon sacrifices, and sacrifice depends upon the universe.

sn: ओमिति ब्रह्मणो योनिनमः स्वाहा स्वधा वषट्। यस्यैतानि प्रयुज्यन्ते यथाशक्ति कृतान्यपि॥ न तस्य त्रिषु लोकेषु परलोकभयं विदुः। इति वेदा वदन्तीह सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः॥
en: The syllable OM is the root from which the Vedas have originated. He has no fear about next life in all the three worlds, who has uttered for him the syllables 'OM, Namas, Svaha, Svadha, and Vashat, and who has according to his means, celebrated sacrifices and other rites. The Vedas and sages crowned with ascetic success, and the foremost of Rishis declare thus.

sn: ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि स्तोभाश्च विधिचोदिताः। यस्मिन्नेतानि सर्वाणि भवन्तीह स वै द्विजः॥
en: He, indeed, is a Brahmana in whom are the Riches, the Yajushes, the Samans, and the explctives necessary for completing the rhythm of the Samans according to the rules laid down in Vedic grammars.

sn: अग्न्याधेये यद् भवति यच्च सोमे सुते द्विज यच्चेतरैर्महायज्ञैर्वेद तद् भगवान् पुनः॥
en: You know, O worshipful Brahmana, what are the fruits of Agnihotra, of the Somasacrifice, and of the other great sacrifices.

sn: तस्माद् ब्रह्मन् यजेच्चैव याजयेच्चाविचारयन्। यजतः स्वर्गविधिना प्रेत्य स्वर्गफलं महत्॥
en: I, therefore, hold that one should sacrifice and assist at other people's sacrifices, without any hesitation whatsoever. One who celebrates sacrifices leading to heaven (such as Yotishtoma, etc.,) acquires great rewards in the next world in the form of heavenly bliss.

sn: नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञानां परचेति विनिश्चयः। वेदवादविदश्चैव प्रमाणमुभयं तदा॥
en: This is certain, viz., that they who do not celebrate sacrifices have neither this world nor the next. They who are really conversant with the sayings of the Vedas consider both kinds of declarations as equally authoritative.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: कपिल उवाच एतावदनुपश्यन्ति यतयो यान्ति मार्गगाः। नैषां सर्वेषु लोकेषु कश्चिदस्ति व्यतिक्रम॥
en: Kapila said Seeing that all the fruits that can be gained by acts are instable instead of being eternal, Yatis, by adopting self-control and tranquallity, attain to Brahma through the path of knowledge. There is nothing in any of the worlds that can stand in their way.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: निर्द्वन्द्वां निर्नमस्कारा निराशीर्बधना बुधाः। विमुक्ताः सर्वपापेभ्यश्चरन्ति शुचयोऽमला:॥
en: They are freed from the influence of all pairs of opposites. They never offer their salutation to anything or to any creature. They are above all the fetters of want. Wisdom is theirs. They are purged of every sin. Pure and stainless they live rove about.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: अपवर्गेऽथ संत्यागे बुद्धौ च कृतनिश्चयाः। ब्रह्मिष्ठा ब्रह्मभूताश्च ब्रह्मण्येव कृतालयाः॥
en: They have, in their own understandings, formed fixed conclusions regarding all destructible objects and a life of at are Renunciation. Devoted to Brahma, and already at one with Brahma, they have taken refuge in Brahma.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: विशोका नष्टरजसस्तेषां लोकाः सनातनाः। तेषां गतिं परां प्राप्य गार्हस्थ्ये किं प्रयोजनम्॥
en: Getting over grief, and freed from the quality of darkness, their acquisitions eternal. When the high end of these men is within reach of attainment, what need has one for performing the duties of the domestic mode of life.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: स्यूमरश्मिरुवाच योषा परमा काष्ठा योषा परमा गतिः। गृहस्थानव्यपाश्रित्य नाश्रमोऽन्यः प्रवर्तते॥
en: If, indeed, that be the highest object of acquisition, if that be truly the highest end then the importance of the domestic mode of life becomes clear, because without the domestic mode no other mode of life ever becomes possible.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: यथा मातरमाश्रित्य सर्वे जीवन्ति जन्तवः। एवं गाहस्थ्यमाश्रित्य वर्तन्त इतराश्रमाः॥
en: Indeed, as all living creatures live on account of their dependence on their respective mothers, similarly the three other modes of life exist on account of their dependence upon the domestic mode.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: गृहस्थ एव यजते गृहस्थस्तप्यते तपः। गार्हस्थ्यमस्य धर्मस्य मूलं यत्किचिदेजते॥
en: The householder who lives like a householder, celebrates sacrifices and practise penances. Whatever is done by anybody for acquiring happiness has for its root the domestic mode of life.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: प्रजनाद्यभिनिर्वृत्ताः सर्वे प्राणभृतो जनाः। प्रजनं चाप्युतान्यत्र न कथंचन विद्यते॥
en: All living creatures consider the procreation of offspring as a root of great happiness. The procreation of children, however, becomes impossible in any other mode of life.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: यास्तु स्युर्बर्हिरोषध्यो बहिरन्यास्तथाद्रिजाः। ओषधिभ्यो बहिर्यस्मात् प्राणात् कश्चिन्न दृश्यते॥
en: Every sort of grass and straw, all plants and herbs, and others of the same class growing on hills and mountains, have the domestic mode of life for their root. Upon these rests the life of living creatures. And since nothing else is seen than life, domesticity may be regarded as the refuge of the entire universe.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: कस्यैषा वाग् भवेत् सत्या मोक्षो नास्ति गृहादिति। अश्रद्दधानप्राज्ञैः सूक्ष्मदर्शनवर्जितैः॥ निरासैरलसैः श्रान्तैस्तप्यमानैः स्वकर्मभिः। शमस्योपरमो दृष्टः प्रव्रज्यायामपण्डितैः॥
en: Who then speaks the truth who says that domesticity cannot bring on the acquisition of Liberation? Only those who have no faith and wisdom and penetration, only those who have no reputation, who are idle and toil-worn who have misery in their lot on account of their pristine deeds, only those who are destitute of learning, see the profusion of tranquillity in a life of mendicancy.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: त्रैलोक्यस्यैव हेतुर्हि मर्यादा शाश्वती ध्रुवा। ब्राह्मणो नाम भगवान् जन्मप्रभृति पूज्यते॥
en: The central and unfailing (Vedic) distinctions are the causes that keep up the three worlds. That Illustrious person of the highest caste who is conversant with the Vedas, is adored from the very date of his birth.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: प्राग्गर्भाधानात्मन्त्रा हि प्रवर्तन्ते द्विजातिषु। अविश्रम्भेषु वर्तन्ते विश्रम्भेष्वष्यसंशयम्॥
en: Besides the celebration of Garbhadhana, Vedic Mantras become necessary for enabling persons of the twice-born classes to perforin all their acts regarding both this and the oiher world.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: दाहे पुनः संश्रयणे संश्रिते पात्रभोजने। दाने गवां पशूनां वा पिण्डानामप्सु मज्जने॥
en: In cremating his body in attainment of a second body, in that of his drink and food after such attainment, in that of giving away kine and other animals for helping him to cross the river that divides this world from that of Yama, in that of sinking the funeral cakes in water, Vedic Mantras are necessary.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: अर्चिष्मन्तो बर्हिषदः कव्यादाः पितरस्तथा। मृतस्याप्यनुमन्यन्ते मन्त्रान् मन्त्राश्च कारणम्॥
en: Then again the three classes of Pitris, viz., the Archishmats, the Varihshads, and the Kravyads, approve of the necessity of Mantras about the dead, and Mantras are regarded as powerful causes.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: एवं क्रोशत्सु वेदेषु कुतो मोक्षोऽस्ति कस्यचित्। ऋणवन्तो यदा मर्त्याः पितृदेवद्विजातिषु॥
en: When the Vedas proclaim this so loudly and when again human beings are said to owe debts to the Pitris, the Rishis, and the gods, how can any one attain to Liberation.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: श्रिया विहीनैरलसैः पण्डितैः सम्प्रवर्तितम्। वेदवादापरिज्ञानं सत्याभासमिवानृतम्॥
en: This false doctrine (of incorporeal existence called Emancipation), seemingly consistent with truth, but subversive of the real meaning of the injunctions of the Vedas, has been introduced by learned men shorn of prosperity and eaten up by idleness.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: न वै पापैर्हियते कृष्यते वा यो ब्राह्मणो यजते वेदशास्त्रैः। उर्ध्वं यज्ञैः पशुभिः सार्धमेति संतर्पितस्तर्पयते च कामैः॥
en: That Brahmana who celebrates sacrifices according to the injunctions of the Vedas, is never seduced by sin. Through sacrifices, such a person acquires high regions of happiness along with the animals he has killed in those sacrifices, and himself, pleased by the acquisition of all his wishes succeeds in pleasing those animals by fulfilling their wishes.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: न वेदानां परिभवान्न शाठ्येन न मायया। महत् प्राप्नोति पुरुषो ब्रह्माणि ब्रह्म विन्दति॥
en: By neglecting the Vedas, by guile, or by deception, one never succeeds in attaining to the Supreme. On the other hand, it is by practising Vedic rites that one succeeds in attaining to Brahina.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: कपिल उवाच दर्श च पौर्णमासं च अग्निहोत्रं च धीमतः। चातुर्मास्यानि चैवासंस्तेषु धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: Kapila said There are the Darsha, the Pauranmasha, the Agnihotra, the Chaturmashya, and other rites which an intelligent man should perform. Eternal merit consists in their performance.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: अनारम्भाः सुधृतयः शुचयो ब्रह्मसंज्ञिताः। ब्रह्मणैव स्म ते देवांस्तर्पयन्त्यमृतैषिणः॥
en: Those that have adopted the Sanyasa mode of life, who abstain from all acts, who are endued with patience, who are cleansed, and who are conversant with Brahma, succeed by such knowledge of Brahma in satisfying the debts to the gods, (also the Pitris and the Rishis), described to be so very fond of libations poured in sacrifices.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्य सर्वभूतानि पश्यतः। देवाऽपि मार्गे मुह्यन्ति अपदस्य पदैषिणः॥
en: The very gods become stupefied in finding out the path of that pathless person who forms himself the soul of all creatures and who regards all creatures impartially.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: चतुरं पुरुषं चतुर्मुखं चतुर्धा चैनमुपयाति वाचा। बाहुभ्यां वाच उदरादुपस्थात्तेषां द्वारं द्वारपालो बुभूषेत।।
en: Through instructions delivered by the preceptor one knows that which lives within this body to be of a four-fold nature, having besides four doors and four mouths. In consequence of two arms the organ of speech, the stomach, and the organ of pleasure, the very duties are said to have four doors. One should, therefore, do his best to keep those doors under control.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: नारैर्दीव्येन्नाददीतान्यवित्तं न वायोनीयस्य शृतं प्रगृह्णात्। सतथास्य तत्पाणिपादं सुगुप्तम्॥
en: One should not gamble with dice. One should not appropriate others properties. One should not officiate at the sacrifice of a person of a mean birth. One should not, yielding to anger, smite another with hands or feet. That intelligent man who acts thus is said to have his hands and feet well-governed.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: नाक्रोशमृच्छेन्न वृथा वदेच्च न पैशुनं जनवादं च कुर्यात्। स्तथास्य वाग्द्वारमथो सुगुप्तम्॥
en: One should not make loud abuse or censure. Onc should not speak useless words. One should forbear from knavery and from accusing others. One should observe the vow of truthfulness, be sparing of speech, and always careful. By acting thus one will have his organ of speech well-governed.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: दलोलुपः साधुभिरागतः स्यात्। यात्रार्थमाहारमिहाददीत तथास्य स्याज्जाठरी द्वारगुप्तिः॥
en: One should not abstain entirely from food. One should not eat too much. One should give up covetousness, and always seek company of the good. One should eat only so much as is necessary for keeping life. By acting thus one succeeds in properly governing the door represented by his stomach.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: न वीरपत्नी विहरेत नारी न चापि नारीमनृतावाह्वयीत। भार्याव्रतं ह्यात्मनि धारयीत तथास्योपस्थद्वारगुप्तिर्भवेत्॥
en: One should not, O hero, out of lust take another wife when he has a wedded wife. One should never call a woman to bed except in her season. One should confine himself to her own married spouse without seeking union with other women. By acting thus one is said in have his organ of pleasure properly governed.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: द्वाराणि यस्य सर्वाणि सुगुप्तानि मनीषिणः। उपस्थमुदं बाहू वाक् चतुर्थी स वै द्विजः॥
en: That wise man is truly a regenerate person who has all his four doors, viz., the organ of pleasure, the stomach, the two arms (and two feet), and the organ of speech, properly governed.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: मोधान्यगुप्तद्वारस्य सर्वाण्येव भवन्त्युत। किं तस्य तपसा कार्य किं यज्ञेन किमात्मना॥
en: Everything becomes useless of that person whose doors are not well governed. O what avail are the penances of such a man? Of what avail are his sacrifices? What can be gained by his body?

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: अनुत्तरीयवसनमनुपस्तीर्णशायिनम्। बाहूपधानं शाम्यन्तं तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: The gods consider him a Brahmana who has cast off his upper garment, who sleeps on the naked earth, who makes his arm a pillow, and whose heart is endued with tranquillity.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: द्वन्द्वारामेषु सर्वेषु य एको रमते मुनिः। परेषामननुध्यायंस्तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: That person who, given to contemplation, singly enjoys all the happiness that married couples enjoy, and who pays no attention to the joys and griefs of others, should be known as a Brahmana.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: येन सर्वमिदं बुद्धं प्रकृतिर्विकृतिश्च या। गतिज्ञः सर्वभूतानां तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: That man who properly understands all this as it really is and its various metamorphoses, and who knows what the end is of all created objects, is known by the gods as a Brahmana.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: सर्वभूतात्मभूतो यस्तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः॥
en: One who entertains no fear from any creature and from whom no creature has any fear, and who forms hiinself the soul of all creatures, should be known as a Brahmana.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यः सर्वेषामभयं यतः। नान्तरेणानुजानन्ति दानयज्ञक्रियाफलम्। अविज्ञाय च तत् सर्वमन्यद् रोचयते फलम्॥
en: Without having gained purity of heart which is the true end of all religions acts such as gifts and sacrifices, men of foolish a even understandings do not succeed in acquiring a knowledge of what is necessary in making one Brahmana when explained by preceptors. Shorn of a knowledge of all this, these men desire fruits of a different sort, viz., heaven and its joys.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: स्वकर्मभिः संश्रितानां तपो घोरत्वमागतम्। तं सदाचारमाश्रित्य पुराणं शाश्वतं ध्रुवम्॥ अशक्नुवन्तश्चरितुं किंचिद् धर्मेषु सूत्रितम्। निरापद्धर्म आचारो ह्यप्रमादोऽपराभवः॥ फलनवन्ति च कर्माणि व्युष्टिमन्ति ध्रुवाणि च। विगुणानि च पश्यन्ति तथानैकान्तिकानि च॥
en: Unable to practise even a small part of that good conduct which has descended from remote times, which is eternal, which is characterised by certainty, which enters as a thread in all our duties, and by following which men of knowledge belonging to all the modes of life convert their respective duties and penances into dreadful weapons for killing the ignorance and evils of worldliness, men of foolish understandings regard acts which yield visible fruits, which are fraught with the highest power, and that are deathless, as fruitless after all and as deviations not sanctioned by the scriptures. In sooth, however, that conduct, comprising practices the very opposite to those that are seen in times of distress, is the very essence of carefulness and is never affected by lust and anger and other passions of a similar nature.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: गुणाश्चात्र सुदुर्जेया ज्ञाताश्चात्र सुदुष्कराः। अनुष्ठिताश्चान्तवन्त इति त्वमनुपश्यसि॥
en: About sacrifices again, it is very difficult to determine all their particulars. If ascertained, it is very difficult to follow them in practice. If practised, the fruits which they beget are terminable. Mark this well.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: स्यूमरश्मिरुवाच यथा च वेदप्रामाण्यं त्यागश्च सफलो यथा। तौ पन्थानावुभौ व्यक्तौ भगवंस्तद् वदस्व मे॥
en: The Vedas sanction acts and disallow them. Whence then is their authority when their injunctions thus contradict each other? Renunciation of acts, again, yield great benefit. Both these ways have been laid down in the Vedas. Do you describe to me this subject, O Brahmana.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: कपिल उवाच प्रत्यक्षमिह पश्यन्ति भवन्तः सत्पथे स्थिताः। प्रत्यक्षं तु किमत्रास्ति यद् भवन्त उपासते॥
en: Kapila said Adopting the path of the good (viz., Yoga), do you in even this life realise its fruits by the direct evidence of your senses! What, however, are the palpable results of those other objects which pursue?

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: स्यूमरश्मिरुवाच स्यूमरश्मिरहं ब्रह्मन् जिज्ञासार्थमिहागतः। श्रेयस्कामः प्रत्यवोचमार्जवान्न विवक्षया॥
en: O Brahmana, I am Syumarashmi by name! I have come here for gaining knowledge. Desirous of done good to myself I have begun this conversation in all simplicity and not from desire of argumentation.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: इमं च संशयं घोरं भगवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे। प्रत्यक्षमिह पश्यन्तो भवन्तः सत्पथे स्थिताः। किमत्र प्रत्यक्षतमं भवन्तो यदुपासते॥
en: This doubt has filled my mind. O illustrious one, solve it to me! You have said that they who adopt the path of the good (viz., Yoga), by which Brahma is attained, realise its fruits by the direct evidence of their senses. What, indeed, is that which can be realised by the direct evidence of the senses and which is followed by yourselves?

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: अन्यत्र तर्कशास्त्रेभ्य आगमार्थं यथागमम्। आगमो वेदवादास्तु तर्कशास्त्राणि चागमः॥
en: Avoiding all sciences that have disputation only for their highest object, I have so studied the Agama as to have duly understood their true import. By Agama I understand the injunctions of the Vedas. I also include in that word those sciences based on logic which have for their object the explanation of the real meaning of the Vedas.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: यथाश्रममुपासीत आगमस्तत्र सिध्यति। सिद्धिः प्रत्यक्षरूपा च दृश्यत्यागमनिश्चयात्॥
en: Without avoiding the duties sanctioned for the particular inode of life which one may follow, one should follow the practices laid down in Agama. Such observance of the practices laid down in Agama gives one success. On account of the certainty of the conclusions of Agama, the success which the latter brings on may be said to be almost realisable by direct evidence.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: नौ वीव निबद्धा हि स्रोतसा सनिबन्धना। ह्रियमाणा कथं विप्र कुबुद्धीस्तारयिष्यति। एतद् ब्रवीतु भगवानुपपन्नोऽस्म्यधीहि भोः॥
en: As a boat, that is tied to another bound for a different port, cannot take its passengers to the port they wish to reach, so ourselves, dragged by our acts due to past desires, can never cross the eternal river of birth and death. Describe to me this subject, O illustrious one! Teach me as a preceptor teaches a disciple.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: नैव त्यागी न संतुष्टो नाशोको न निरामयः। न निर्विधित्सो नावृत्तोनापवृत्तोऽस्ति कश्चन॥
en: No one is seen among men who has perfectly renounced all earthly objects, nor one who is perfectly contented with oneself, nor one who has gone over grief, nor one who is perfectly free from disease, nor one who is absolutely free from the desire to act, nor one who has absolute distaste for companionship, nor one who has entirely abstained froin acts of every sort.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: भवन्तोऽपि च हृषयन्ति शोचन्ति च यथा वयम्। इन्द्रियार्थाश्च भवतां समानाः सर्वजन्तुषु॥
en: Even men like yourself are seen to yield to joy and indulge in grief as persons like ourselves. Like other creatures the senses of persons like yourselves have their functions or objects. an

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: एवं चतुर्णां वर्णानमाश्रमाणां प्रवृत्तिषु। एकमालम्बमानानां निर्णये किं निरामयम्॥
en: Tell me, in what then, if we are to determine the question of happiness, consists pure happiness for all the four castes and all the four modes of life who and which have the same basis.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: कपिल उवाच यद् यदाचरते शास्त्रमर्थ्यं सर्वप्रवृत्तिषु। यस्य यत्र ह्यनुष्ठानं तत्र तत्र निरामयम्॥
en: Kapila said Whatever may be the Shastras according to which one performs the acts, the ordinances laid down in it for regulating those acts never become fruitless. Whatever again the school of opinion according to which one may act, one is sure to attain to the highest end by only following the duties of self-control or Yoga.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: ज्ञानं प्लावयते सर्वं यो ज्ञानं ह्यनुवर्तते। ज्ञानादपेत्य या वृत्तिः सा विनाशयति प्रजाः॥
en: Knowledge helps that man in crossing (over the river of life and death), who follows knowledge. That conduct, however, which men follow after deviating from the path of knowledge, pains them.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: भवन्तो ज्ञानिनो व्यक्तं सर्वतश्च निरामयाः। ऐकात्म्यं नाम कश्चिद्धि कदाचिदुपपद्यते॥
en: It is clear that ye are endued with knowledge and dissociated from every earthly object that may produce pain. But have any of you at any time, succeeded in gaining that knowledge by which everything is capable of being seen as at one with one Universal Self.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: शास्त्रं ह्यबुद्ध्वा तत्त्वेन केचिद् वादबलाज्जनाः। कामद्वेषाभिभूतत्वादहङ्कारवशं गताः॥
en: Without a correct understanding of the scriptures, some there are, fond only of argumentation who, on account of being overwhelmed by desire and hatred, become the slaves of pride and arrogance.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: याथातथ्यमविज्ञाय शास्त्राणां शास्त्रदस्यवः। ब्रह्मस्तेना निरारम्भा दम्भमोहवशानुगाः॥
en: Without having correctly understood the meaning of scriptural sayings, these robbers of the scriptures, these depredators of Brahma, actuated by arrogance and mistake, refuse to pursue tranquillity and practise self-control;.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: नैर्गुण्यमेव पश्यन्ति न गुणाननुयुञ्जते। तेषां तमःशरीराणां तम एव परायणम्॥
en: These men see fruitlessness on every side, and if they succeed in acquiring the power of knowledge they never give it to others for rescuing them. Made up entirely of the quality of ignorance, they have ignorance only for their refuge.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: यो यथाप्रकृतिर्जन्तुः प्रकृतेः स्याद् वशानुगः। तस्य द्वेषश्च कामश्च क्रोधो दम्भोऽनृतं मदः। नित्यमेवाभिवर्तन्ते गुणाः प्रकृतिसम्भवाः॥
en: One becomes subject to all the characteristics of that nature which one imbibes. Accordingly, of him who has ignorance for his refuge, the passions of envy, lust, anger, pride, falsehood, and vanity, continually grow, for one's qualities have one's nature for their root.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: एवं ध्यात्वानुपश्यन्तः संत्यजेयुः शुभाशुभम्। परां गतिमभीप्सन्तो यतयः संयमे रताः॥
en: Thinking in this way and seeing these faults, Yatis, who seek the highest end, follow Yoga, leaving both good and ill.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: स्यूमरश्मिरुवाच सर्वमेतन्मया ब्रह्मन् शास्त्रतः परिकीर्तितम्। न ह्यविज्ञाय शास्त्रार्थं प्रवर्तन्ते प्रवृत्तयः॥
en: O Brahmana, all that I have said is strictly according to the scriptures. It is, however, very true that without a correct understanding of the meaning of the scriptures, one does not feel inclined to obey what the scriptures really say.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: यः कश्चिन्याय्य आचारः सर्वं शास्त्रमिति श्रुतिः। यदन्याय्यमशास्त्रं तदित्येषा श्रूयते श्रुतिः॥
en: Whatever conduct is consistent with equity, is conformable with the scriptures. Even that is what the Shruti says, Likewise, whatever conduct is inconsistent with equity in incompatible with the scriptures. This also is held by the Shruti.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: न प्रवृत्ति ॠते शास्त्रात् काचिदस्तीति निश्चयः। यदन्यद् वेदवादेभ्यस्तदशास्त्रमिति॥
en: It is certain that no one can do a scriptural act by violating the scriptures. That which is against the Vedas is unscriptural. The Shruti says this. are

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: शास्त्रादपेतं पश्यन्ति बहवो व्यक्तमानिनः। शास्त्रदोषान् न पश्यन्ति शोचन्ति च यथा वयम्। इन्द्रियार्थाश्च भवतां समानाः सर्वजन्तुषु॥
en: Many men, who believe only what directly appeals to their senses, see only this world. They do not see what the scriptures declare to be faults. They have, accordingly, like ourselves, to yield to grief. Those objects of the sense which concern men like you are the same with which other living creatures concerned.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: एवं चतुर्णां वर्णानामाश्रमाणां प्रवृत्तिषु। एकमालम्बमानानां निर्णये सर्वतोदिशम्॥ आनन्त्यं वदमानेन शक्तेनावर्जितात्मना। अविज्ञानहतप्रज्ञा हीनप्रज्ञास्तमोवृताः॥
en: All the four castes of men and all the four modes of life, however different their duties, seek the same single end. You are gifted with unquestioned talents and abilities. For determining that particular conduct which is well calculated to fulfil the desired end, you have by describing to me the Infinite (Brahma), filled my soul with tranquallity. As regards ourselves, on account of our inability to understand the Soul we are deprived of a correct understanding of life reality. Our wisdom is concerned with low things, and we are covered with thick darkness,

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: शक्यं त्वेकेन युक्तोन कृतकृत्येन सर्वशः। पिण्डमानं व्यपाश्रित्य चरितुं विजितात्मना॥ वेदवादं व्यपाश्रित्य मोक्षोऽस्तीति प्रभाषितुम्। अपेतन्यायशास्त्रेण सर्वलोकविगहिणा॥
en: Only he who is given to Yoga, who has satisfied all his duties, who is capable of roving everywhere depending only on his own body, who has brought his soul under perfect restraint, who has gone above the requirements of the science of morality and who disregards the whole world, can transgress the declarations of the Vedas regarding acts, and say that there is Liberation,

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: इदं तु दुष्करं कर्म कुटुम्बमभिसंश्रितम्। दानमध्ययनं यज्ञः प्रजासंतानमार्जवम्॥ यद्येतदेवं कृत्वापि न विमोक्षोऽस्ति कस्यचित्। धिक् कर्तारं च कार्य च श्रमश्चायं निरर्थकः॥६६॥
en: For one, however, who lives in the midst of relatives, this course of conduct is highly difficult to follow. Gift, study of the Vedas, sacrifices begetting children, simplicity of conduct, when by doing even these no one attains to Liberation, fie on him who seeks to altain to it. and on Liberation itself that is sought! It appears that the labour spent upon acquiring it is all fruitless.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: नास्तिक्यमन्यथा च स्याद् वेदानां पृष्ठतः क्रिया। एतस्यानन्त्यमिच्छामि भगवश्रोतुमञ्जसा॥
en: One is charged with atheism if he disregards the Vedas by not doing the acts they declare. O illustrious one, I wish to hear forthwith about that which comes in the Vedas after the injunctions about acts.

description: Various religious rites described by Kapila
sn: तत्त्वं वदस्व मे ब्रह्मन्नुपसन्नोऽस्म्यधीहि भोः। यथा वे विदितो मोक्षस्तथेच्छाम्युपशिक्षितुम्॥
en: Do tell me the truth, O Brahmana! I sit at your feet as a disciple. Teach me kindly! I wish to know as much about Liberation as is known to you, O learned one!

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: कपिल उवाच वेदाः प्रमाणं लोकानां न वेदाः पृष्ठतः कृताः। द्वे ब्रह्मणी वेदितव्ये शब्दब्रह्म परं च यत्॥
en: Kapila said The Vedas are considered as an authority by all. People never disobey them. Brahma is of two kinds, viz., Brahma is represented by sound, and Brahma as Supreme.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: शब्दब्रह्मणि निष्णातः परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति। शरीरमेतत् कुरुते यद् वेदे कुरुते तनुम्॥
en: One conversant with Brahma of sound succeeds in attaining to Supreme Brahma. Beginning with the rites of Garbhadhana, that body which the father creates with the help of Vedic Mantras is purified (after birth) by Vedic Mantras.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: कृतशुद्धशरीरो हि पात्रं भवति ब्राह्मणः। आनन्त्यमत्र बुद्ध्यदं कर्मणां तद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: When the body, has been purified with purificatary rites, the owner thereof is called a Prahmana and becomes a vessel fit for receiving knowledge of Brahma. Know that the meed of acts is purity of heart which only brings on Liberation. I shall now speak to you of that.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: अनागममनैतिचं प्रत्यक्षं लोकसाक्षिकम्। धर्म इत्येव ये यज्ञान् वितन्वन्ति निराशिषः॥ उत्पन्नत्यागिनोऽलुब्धाः कृपासूयाविवर्जिताः। धनानामेष वै पनास्तीर्थेषु प्रतिपादनम्॥
en: Whether purity of heart has been acquired or not, is what can be known to the person himself who has acquired it. It can never be known with the help of either the Vedas or inference. They who have no expectations, who discard every sort of riches by not keeping anything for future use, who are not covetous, and who are free from every sort of affection and aversion, celebrate sacrifices believing only that their performance is a duty. To make gifts to deserving persons is the end of all riches.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: अनाश्रिताः पापकर्म कदाचित् कर्मयोगिनः। मन:संकल्पसंसिद्धा विशुद्धज्ञाननिश्चयाः॥ अक्रुध्यन्तोऽनसूयन्तो निरहङ्कारमत्सराः। ज्ञाननिष्ठास्त्रिशुक्लाश्च सर्वभूतहिते रताः॥ आसन् गृहस्था भूयिष्ठा अव्युत्क्रान्ताः स्वकर्मसु। राजानश्च तथा युक्ता ब्राह्मणाश्च यथाविधि॥
en: Never addicted at any time to sinful deeds, observant of rites sanctioned by the Vedas, capable of fructifying all their wishes, gifted with certain conclusions through pure knowledge, never giving way to anger,-never indulging in envy, free from pride and malice, firm in Yoga, of unsullied conduct, and unsullied learning, given to the behoof of all creatures, there were in days of yore many men living like householders and thoroughly devoted to the their own duties, there were many kings also of the same accomplishment, devoted to Yoga, and many Brahmanas also of the same character.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: समा ह्यार्जवसम्पन्नाः संतुष्टा ज्ञाननिश्चयाः। प्रत्यक्षधर्माः शुचयः श्रद्दधानाः परावरे॥
en: They treated all creatures equally and were gifted with perfect sincerity. They had contentiment, certainty of knowledge. The rewards of their righteousness were apparent, and they were pure in conduct and heart. They were endued with faith in Brahma of both forms.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: पुरस्ताद् भावितात्मानो यथावच्चरितव्रताः। चरन्ति धर्म कृच्छेऽपि दुर्गे चैवापि संहताः॥
en: At first making their hearts pure, they duly observed all vows. They observed the duties of righteousness on even occasions of distress and great difficulty, without deviating in any particular.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: संहत्य धर्मं चरतां पुराऽऽसीत् सुखमेव तत्। तेषां नासीद् विधातव्यं प्रायश्चित्तं कथंचन॥
en: Uniting together they used to celebrate meritorious acts. In this they found great happiness. And inasmuch as they never transgressed, they had never to perform any expiatory rite.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: सत्यं हि धर्ममास्थाय दुराधर्षतमा मताः। न मात्रामनुरुध्यन्ते न धर्मच्छलमन्ततः॥
en: Depending upon the true course of virtue, they became gifted with irresistible energy. They never followed their own understandings while acquiring merit but followed the injunctions of the scriptures along for that end. Accordingly they were never guilty of guile in performing acts of righteousness.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: य एव प्रथमः कल्पस्तमेवाभ्याचरन् सह। तेषां नासीद् विधातव्यं प्रायश्चित्तं कदाचन॥
en: On account of their observing unitedly the perfect ordinances of the scriptures without following the rites laid down in the alternative, they were never compelled to perform any expiation.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: तस्मिन् विधौ स्थितानां हि प्रायश्चित्तं न विद्यते। दुर्बलात्मन उत्पन्न प्रायश्चित्तमिति श्रुतिः॥
en: There is no expiation for men who follow the ordinances laid down in the scriptures. The Shruti says that expiation exists for only men who are weak and unable to follow the absolute provisions of the sacred law.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: एवं बहुविधा विप्राः पुराणा यज्ञवाहनाः। विद्यवृद्धाः शुचयो वृत्तवन्तो यशस्विनः॥
en: Many Brahmanas of this kind in days of yore, devoted to the celebration of Vedas, endued with purity, good conduct and fame.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: यजन्तोऽहरहर्यज्ञैर्निराशीर्बन्धना बुधाः। तेषां यज्ञाश्च वेदाश्च कर्माणि च यथागमम्॥ आगमाच यथाकाले संकल्पाच यथाक्रमम्। अपेतकामक्रोधानां दुश्चराचारकर्मणाम्॥ स्वकर्मभिः संशितानां प्रकृत्या शंसितात्मनाम्। ऋजूनां शमनित्यानां स्वेषु कर्मसु वर्तताम्॥ सर्वमानन्त्यमेवासीदिति नः शाश्वती श्रुतिः। तेषामदीनसत्त्वानां दुश्चराचारकर्मणाम्॥ स्वकर्मभिः सम्भृतानां तपो घोरत्वमागतम्। तं सदाचारमाश्चर्यं पुराणं शाश्वतं ध्रुवम्॥ अशक्नुवद्भिश्चरितुं किंचिद् धर्मेषु सूक्ष्मताम्। निरापद्धर्म आचारो ह्यप्रमादोऽपराभवः॥ सर्ववर्णेषु जातेषु नासीत कश्चिद् व्यतिक्रमः। व्यस्तमेकं चतुर्धा हि ब्राह्मणा आश्रमं विदुः॥
en: They always adored Brahma in the sacrifices, and were free from desire. Endued with learning they got over all the bonds of life. The sacrifices of these men, their Vedic knowledge, their acts performed according to the ordinances, their study of the scriptures at the proper hours, and the wishes they formed, freed as they were from lust and anger, observant as they were of pious conduct and acts despite all difficulties, famous as they were for performing the duties of their own castes and mode of life, purified as their souls were on account of their very nature, characterised as they were by thorough sincerity, devoted as they were to tranquillity, and attentive as they were to their own practises, were at one with Infinite Brahma. This is the eternal Shruti we have heard. The penances of men who were so noble, of men whose conduct and acts were so difficult of observance and accomplishment, of men those wishes were crowned with success on account of the strict satisfaction of their duties, became potent instruments for the destruction of all worldly desires. The Brahmanas hold that that Good conduct, which is wonderful, whose origin may be traced to very old times, which is eternal, and whose marks are unchangeable, which differs from the practices which even the good follow in time of distress and represents their acts in other situations, which is at one with carefulness, over which lust, anger, and other evil passions have no control, and on account of which there was no transgression in all mankind, subsequently became divided into four sub-divisions, agreeing with the four modes of life, by person unable to follow its duties in ininute detail and entirety.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: तं सन्तो विधिवत् प्राप्य गच्छन्ति परमां गतिम्। गृहेभ्य एव निष्क्रम्य वनमन्ये समाश्रिताः॥
en: By properly following that course of Good Conduct after adoption of the Sanyasa mode of life, the good attain to the highest end. They also who become forest recluses, reach the same high end.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: गृहमेवाभिसंश्रित्य ततोऽन्ये ब्रह्मचारिणः। त एते दिवि दृश्यन्ते ज्योतिर्भूता द्विजातयः॥
en: They also who observe the domestic mode of life, attain to the highest end; and lastly, those who lead the Brahmacharya mode, attain to the same end. Those Brahmanas are seen to shine in the sky as luminaries shedding beneficent rays of light all around.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: नक्षत्राणीव धिष्ण्येषु बहवस्तारकागणाः। आनन्त्यमुपसम्प्राप्ताः संतोषादिति वैदिकम्॥
en: Those countless Brahmanas have become stars and constellations set in their fixed roads. By virtue of contentment they have all acquired Infinity as the Vedas say.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: यद्यागच्छन्ति संसारं पुनर्योनिषु तादृशाः। न लिप्यन्ते पापकृत्यैः कदाचित् कर्मयोनितः॥
en: If such men have to return to the world through the wombs of living creatures, they are never sullied by sins which have the unexhausted remnant of pristine deeds for their originating cause.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: एवमेव ब्रह्मचारी शुश्रूषुर्घोरनिश्चयः। एवं युक्तो ब्राह्मणः स्यादन्यो ब्राह्मणको भवेत्॥
en: Indeed, one who has lived like a Brahmacharin and served dutifully his preceptor, who has arrived at fixed conclusions, and who has devoted hiinself to Yoga thus, is truly a Brahmana. Who else is worthy of being called a Brahmana?

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: कमैवं पुरुषस्याह शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्। एवं पक्वकषायाणामानन्त्येन श्रुतेन च।॥ सर्वमानन्त्यमासीद् वै एवं नः शाश्वती श्रुतिः। तेषामपेततृष्णानां निर्णिक्तानां शुभात्मनाम्॥ चतुर्थोपनिषद् धर्म: साधारण इति स्मृतिः। संसिद्धैः साध्यते नित्यं ब्राह्मणैर्नियतात्मभिः॥
en: When acts alone settle who is a Brahmana and who is not; acts must be held to point out the happiness or misery of a person. About those who have by conquering all evil passions acquired purity of heart, we have heard the eternal Shruti that, on account of the Infinity which they acquire and of the knowledge of Brahma (they acquire through the declarations of Shrutis), they see everything as Brahma. The duties followed by those pure-hearted men, who are shorn of desire, and who have Liberation only for their object, for acquisition of the knowledge of Brahma, are equally sanctioned for all the four castes and all the four modes of life. That knowledge is always gained by Brahmanas of pure hearts and controlled soul.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: संतोषमूलस्त्यागात्मा ज्ञानाधिष्ठानमुच्यते। अपवर्गमतिनित्यो यतिधर्मः सनातनः॥
en: One whose soul is for Renunciation based upon contentment, is considered as the refuge of true knowledge. Renunciation, wherein exists the knowledge leading to Liberation, and which is highly necessary for a Brahmana, is eternal.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: साधारणः केवलो वा यथाबलमुपासते। गच्छतां गच्छतां क्षेमं दुर्बलोऽत्रावसीदति। ब्रह्मणः पदमन्विच्छन् संसारान्मुच्यते शुचिः॥
en: Renunciation is sometimes found mixed with the duties of other modes. But whether existing in that state or by itself, one practises it according to his power. Renunciation is the root of great benefit to every sort of person. Only he who is weak, fails to pursue it. That pure-hearted man who seeks to attain to Brahma becomes saved from the world.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: स्यूमरश्मिरुवाच ये भुञ्जते ये ददते यजन्तेऽधीयते च ये। मात्राभिरुपलब्धाभिर्ये वा त्यागं समाश्रिताः॥ एतेषां प्रेत्यभावे तु कतमः स्वर्गजित्तमः। एतदाचक्ष्व मे ब्रह्मन् यथातत्त्वेन पृच्छतः॥
en: Of them who are given up to enjoyment, they who make gifts, they who celebrate sacrifices, they who are given to the study of the Vedas, and they who follow the life of Renunciation after having acquired and enjoyed riches and all its pleasures, when they depart from this world, who is it who gets the foremost place in heaven? I ask you this, O

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: कपिल उवाच परिग्रहाः शुभाः सर्वे गुणतोऽभ्युदयाश्च ये। न तु त्यागसुखं प्राप्ता एतत् त्वमपि पश्यसि॥
en: Those who live like householders are surely auspicious and gain every sort of excellence. They are unable, however, to enjoy the happiness of Renunciation. Even you may see this.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: स्यूमरश्मिरुवाच भवन्तो ज्ञाननिष्ठा वै गृहस्थाः कर्मनिश्चयाः। आश्रमाणां च सर्वेषां निष्ठायामैक्यमुच्यते॥
en: You depend upon knowledge as the means. Those who live like householders, have placed their faith in acts. It has, however, been said that the end of all modes of life is Liberation.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन विशेषो नात्र दृश्यते। तद् यथावद् यथान्यायं भगवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे॥
en: No difference, therefore, is seen between them about either their superiority or inferiority of power. O illustrious one do you, then, clear out the mystery and enlighten me.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: कपिल उवाच शरीरपक्तिः कर्माणि ज्ञानं तु परमा गतिः। कषाये कर्मभिः पक्वे रसज्ञाने च तिष्ठति।॥ आनृशंस्यं क्षमा शान्तिरहिंसा सत्यमार्जवम्। अद्रोहोऽनभिमानश्च ह्रीस्तितिक्षा शमस्तथा॥
en: Kapila said-Acts only purify the body, Knowledge, however, is the highest end. When all defects of the heart are cured, and when the happiness of Brahma becomes established in knowledge. benevolence, forgiveness, tranquillity, mercy, truthfulness, and open-mindedness, abstention from injury, absence of pride, modestry, renunciation, and abstention from work are acquired.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: पन्थानो ब्रह्मणस्त्वेते एतैः प्राप्नोति यत्परम्। तद् विद्वाननुबुद्ध्येत मनसा कर्मनिश्चयम्॥
