en: These form the path of Brahma. By those one acquires the Highest. A wise man when he acquires these qualities, understands that the cure of all defects of the heart is the result of acts.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: यां विप्राः सर्वतः शान्ता विशुद्धा ज्ञाननिश्चयाः। गतिं गच्छन्ति संतुष्टास्तामाहुः परमां गतिम्॥
en: That, indeed, is considered as the highest end which is acquired by Brahmanas gifted with wisdom, withdrawn from all acts, possessed of purity and the surety of knowledge.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: वेदांश्च वेदितव्यं च विदित्वा च यथास्थितिम्। एवं वेदविदित्याहुरतोऽन्यो वातरेचकः॥
en: One who acquires a knowledge of the Vedas, of that which is taught by the Vedas, and the details of acts, is said to be conversant with the Vedas. Any other man is only a bag of wind.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: सर्वं विदुर्वेदविदो वेदे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। वेदे हि निष्ठा सर्वस्य यद् यदस्ति च नास्ति च॥
en: One who is master of the Vedas, knows everything, for everything is established on the Veda. The present, past, and future all exist in the Vedas.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: एषैव निष्ठा सर्वत्र यत् तदस्ति च नास्ति च। एतदन्त च मध्यं च सच्चासच्च विजानतः॥
en: This is the one conclusion of all the scriptures viz., that this universe exists and does not exist. To the man of knowledge this is both existent and non-existent. To him this all is both the end and the middle.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: समाप्तं त्याग इत्येव सर्ववेदेषु निष्ठितम्। संतोष इत्यनुगतमपवर्गे प्रतिष्ठितम्॥ ऋतं सत्यं विदितं वेदितव्यं सर्वस्यामा स्थावरं जङ्गमं च। सर्वं सुखं यच्छिवमुत्तरं च ब्रह्माव्यक्तं प्रभवश्चाव्ययं च॥
en: This truth depends upon all the Vedas, viz., that when complete Renunciation takes place one acquires what is sufficient. Then, again, the highest contentment follows and depends upon Liberation, which is absolute, which exists as the soul of all moral and immortal things, which is well-known as such universal soul, which is the highest object of knowledge as being at one with all mobile and immobile objects, which is full, which is perfect happiness, which is without duality, which is the foremost of all things, which is Brahma, which is Unmanifest and the cause also of the Unmanifest, and which is without any sort of decay.

description: The importance of the Vedas and the Vedic rites
sn: तेजः क्षमा शान्तिरनामयं शुभं तथाविधं व्योम सनातनं ध्रुवम्। स्तस्मै नमो ब्रह्मणे ब्राह्मणाय॥
en: Power to control the senses, forgiveness and abstention from work owing to the absence of desire,-these three are the cause of perfect happiness. With the help of these three qualities, men having understanding for their eyes, succeed in reaching that Brahma which is increate, which is the supreme cause of the universe, which is unchangeable, and which is beyond destruction. I bow to that Brahma, which is at one with him that knows it.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धर्ममर्थं च कामं च वेदाः शंसन्ति भारत। कस्य लाभो विशिष्टोऽत्र तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhisthira said The Vedas, O Bharata, describe Religion, Profit, and Pleasure. Tell me, however, O grand-father, the attainment of which is considered as superior.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि इतिहासं पुरातनम्। कुण्डधारेण यत् प्रीत्या भक्तायोपकृतं पुरा॥
en: Bhishma said About it I shall recite to you the ancient discourse of the benefit which Kundadhara in days of yore had conferred upon one who was devoted to him.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: अधनो ब्राह्मणः कश्चित् कामाद् धर्ममवैक्षत। यज्ञार्थं सततोऽर्थार्थी तपोऽतप्यत दारुणम्॥
en: Once on a time a Brahmana shorn of riches tried to win virtue, actuated by the desire of fruit. He continually thought of riches for employing it in the celebration of sacrifices. For gaining his end he engaged in the practice of the austerest penances.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: स निश्चयमथो कृत्वा पूजयामास देवताः। भक्त्या न चैवाध्यगच्छद् धनं सम्पूज्य देवताः॥
en: Determined to achieve his object, he began to adore the gods with great devotion. But he failed to acquire riches by such adoration of the gods.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततश्चिन्तामनुप्राप्त: कतमदैवतं तु तत्। यन्मे दुतं प्रसीदेत मानुषैरजडीकृतम्॥
en: He thereupon began to think aside, What is that god, hitherto not worshipped by men, who may be forthwith favourably disposed towards me?

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: सोऽथ सौम्येन मनसा देवानुचरमन्तिके। प्रत्यपश्यज्जलधरं कुण्डधारमवस्थितम्॥
en: While thinking thus with a cool mind, he saw stationed before him that retainer of the gods, viz., the Cloud called Kundadhara.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: दृष्ट्वैव तं महाबाहुं तस्य भक्तिरजायत। अयं मे धास्यति श्रेयो वपुरेतद्धि तादृशम्॥
en: As soon as he saw that mighty-armed being, the Brahmana's feelings of devotion were excited, and he said to himself,-This one will surely give me prosperity! Indeed, his form indicates it.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: संनिकृष्टश्च देवस्य न चान्यैर्मानुषैर्वृतः। एष मे दास्यति धनं प्रभूतं शीघ्रमेव च।॥
en: He lives near the gods. He has not as yet been worshipped by other man. He will surely give me profuse riches without any delay!

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततो धूपैश्च गन्धैश्च माल्यैरुच्चावचैरपि। बलिभिर्विविधाभिश्च पूजयामास तं द्विजः॥
en: The Brahmana then, having determined thus, adored that Cloud with incense, perfumes and garlands of flowers of the most superior kind, and with various sorts of offerings.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततस्त्वल्पेन कालेन तुष्टो जलधरस्तदा। तस्योपकारनियतामिमां वाचमुवाच ह॥
en: Thus adored, the Cloud became very soon pleased with his worshipper, and uttered these words of benefit to that Brahmana:

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ब्रह्मने च सुरापे च चौरे भग्नव्रते यथा। निष्कृतिर्विहिता सद्भिः कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः॥
en: The wise have laid down expiation for one guilty of Brahmanicide, or of drinking alcohol, or of stealing, or of neglecting all meritorious vows. There is no expiation, however, for one who is ungrateful.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: आशायास्तनयोऽधर्मः क्रोधोऽसूयासुतः स्मृतः। लोभः पुत्रो निकृत्यास्तु कृतम्रो नार्हति प्रजाम्॥
en: Expectation has a child named Sin. Anger, again, is considered to be a child of Envy. Cupidity is the child of Deceit. Ingratitude, however, is barnen.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततः स ब्राह्मणः स्वप्ने कुण्डधारस्य तेजसा। अपश्यत् सर्वभूतानि कुशेषु शयितस्तदा॥
en: After this, that Brahmana, stretched on a bed of Kusha grass, and penetrated with the energy of Kundadhara, saw all living beings in a dream.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: शमेन तपसा चैव भक्त्या च निरुपस्कृतः। शुद्धात्मा ब्राह्मणो रात्रौ निदर्शनमपश्यत॥
en: Indeed, on account of his absence of passion, penances, and devotion, that Brahmana of purified soul and standing aloof from all enjoyments saw in the night that effect of his devotion to Kundadhara.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: मणिभद्रं स तत्रस्थं देवतानां महाद्युतिम्। अपश्यत महात्मानं व्यादिशन्तं युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Indeed, O Yudhishthira, he saw the great and highly effulgent Manibhadra stationed in the midst of the gods, engaged in giving his orders.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: तत्र देवाः प्रयच्छन्ति राज्यानि च धनानि च। शुभैः कर्मभिरारब्धाः प्रच्छिन्दन्त्यशुभेषु च॥
en: There the gods seemed to be engaged in granting kingdoms and riches to men, induced by their good deeds, and in taking them away when men deviated from goodness.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: पश्यतामथ यक्षाणां कुण्डधारो महाद्युतिः। निपत्य पतितो भूमौ देवानां भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then, O foremost of Bharata's race, the highly effulgent Kundadhara, bending himself low, laid himself down on the ground before the gods in the presences of all the Yakshas.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततस्य देववचनान्मणिभद्रो महामनाः। पतितं भूमौ कुण्डधार किमिष्यते॥
en: At the command of the gods the Manibhadra said to the prostrate Kundadhara,-What does Kundadhara want?

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: कुण्डधार उवाच यदि प्रसन्ना देवा मे भक्तोऽयं ब्राह्मणो मम। अस्यानुग्रहमिच्छामि कृतं किंचित् सुखोदयम्॥
en: Thereupon Kundadhara replied,-If, indeed, the gods are gratified with me, there, that Brahmana respects me greatly. I pray for some favour being shown to him, something, that may bring him happiness.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततस्तं मणिभद्रस्तु पुनर्वचनमब्रवीत्। देवानामेव वचनात् कुण्डधारं महाद्युतिम्॥
en: Hearing this, Manibhadra, ordered by the gods, once more said to the highly intelligent Kundadhara.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: मणिभद्र उवाच उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते कृतकृत्यः सुखी भव। धनार्थी यदि विप्रोऽयं धनमस्मै प्रदीयताम्॥ यावद् धनं प्रार्थयते ब्राह्मणोऽयं सखा तव। देवानां शासनात् तावदसंख्येयं ददाम्यहम्॥
en: Rise, Rise up, O Kundadhara; Your prayer has borne success! Be you happy! If this Brahmana seeks riches, let as much wealth be given to him, as he wishes. at the command of the gods I shall give him immeasurable riches.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: विचार्य कुण्डधारस्तु मानुष्यं चलमध्रुवम्। तपसे मतिमाधत्त ब्राह्मणस्य युधिष्ठिर।॥
en: Then, thinking upon the fieeting and unreal character of the humanity, Kundadhara set his heart, O Yudhisthira, upon inclining the Brahmana to penances.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: कुण्डधार उवाच नाहं धनानि याचामि ब्राह्मणाय धनप्रदा अन्यमेवाहमिच्छामि भक्तायानुग्रहं कृतम्॥
en: Indeed, Kundadhara said,-I do not, O giver of riches, beg for wealth on behalf of this Brahmana. I desire the bestowed of another favour upon him.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: पृथिवीं रत्नपूर्णां वा महद् वा रत्नसंचयम। भक्ताय नाहमिच्छामि भवेदेष तु धार्मिकः॥
en: I do not pray for this devotee of mine mountains of pearls and gems, or even the whole Earth with all her riches. I wish, however, that he should be virtuous.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: धर्मेऽस्य रमतां बुद्धिर्धर्मं चैवोपजीवतु। धर्मप्रधानो भवतु ममैषोऽनुग्रहो मतः॥
en: Let his heart find pleasure in virtue! Let him have virtue for his support. Let virtue be the foremost of all his objects. This is the favour which I am inclined to give my support. Manibhadra said

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: मणिभद्र उवाच सदा धर्मफलं राज्यं सुखानि विविधानि च। फलान्येवायमनातु कायक्लेशविवर्जितः॥
en: The fruits of virtue are always kingdom and happiness of various sorts. Let this one enjoy those fruits, always freed from all sorts of physical sufferings.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततस्तदेव बहुशः कुण्डधारो महायशाः। अभ्यासमकरोद् धर्मे ततस्तुष्टास्तु देवताः॥
en: Thus addressed, the highly illustrious Kundadhara, repeatedly prayed for virtue alone for that Brahmana. The gods were highly pleased at it.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: मणिभद्र उवाच प्रीतास्ते देवताः सर्वा द्विजस्यास्य तथैव च। भविष्यत्येष धर्मात्मा धर्मे चाधास्यते मतिः॥
en: Then Manibhadra said The gods are all pleased with you as also with this Brahmana. This one shall become a virtuous man. He shall devote his mind to virtue.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततः प्रीतो जलधरः कृतकार्णे युधिष्ठिर। ईप्सितं मनसो लब्ध्वा वरमन्यैः सुदुर्लभम्॥
en: The Cloud, Kundadhara, became pleased,O Yudhishthira, at thus having been successful in gaining his wish. The boon that he had got was one that could not be acquired by anybody else.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततोऽपयत चीराणि सूक्ष्माणि द्विजसत्तमः। पार्श्वतोऽभ्याशतो न्यस्तान्यथ निर्वेदमागतः॥
en: The Brahinana then saw scattered around him many fine fabrics of cloth. Without caring for them at all, the Brahmana came to disrelish the world.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अयं न सुकृतं वेत्ति को न्वन्यो वेत्स्यते कृतम्। गच्छामि वनमेवाहं वरं धर्मेण जीवितुम्।३२॥
en: When this one does not attach any value to good deeds, who else will? I had better go to the forest for leading a life of righteousness.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: भीष्म उवाच निर्वेदाद् देवतानां च प्रसादात् स द्विजोत्तमः। वनं प्रविश्य सुमहत् तप आरब्धवांस्तदा।॥
en: Bhishma said as Cherishing a distaste for the world, and through the grace also of the gods, that foremost of Brahmanas entered the forest and began to practise the austerest of penances.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: देवतातिथिशेषेण फलमूलाशनो द्विजः। धर्मे चास्य महाराज दृढा बुद्धिरजायत॥
en: Living upon such fruits and roots remained after serving the gods and guests, the mind of that twice-born one, O king, was firmly set upon virtue.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: त्यरत्वा मूलफलं सर्वं पर्णाहारोऽभवद् द्विजः। पर्णं त्यक्त्वा जलाहारः पुनरासीद् द्विजस्तदा।॥
en: By and bye the Brahmana, leaving off fruits and roots, began to use leaves of trees as his food. Then leaving off leaves, he took to water only as his subsistence.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: वायुभक्षस्ततः पश्चाद् बहून वर्षगणानभूत्। न चास्य क्षीयते प्राणस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Thereafter he passed many years by living upon air only. All this time, however, his strength did not decrease. This seemed highly wonderful.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: धर्मे च श्रद्दधानस्य तपस्युग्रे च वर्ततः। कालेन महता तस्य दिव्या दृष्टिरजायत॥
en: Devoted to virtue and engaged in the practice of the severest austerities, after a long time he gained spiritual vision.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: तस्य बुद्धिः प्रादुरासीद् यदि दद्यामहं धनम्। तुष्टः कस्यचिदेवेह मिथ्यावाङ् न भवेन्मम॥
en: He then thought, saying to himself,-If, being pleased with anybody I give him riches, my speech would never be untrue.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततः प्रहृष्टवदनो भूय आरब्धवांस्तपः। भूयश्चचिन्तयत् सिद्धो यत्परं सोऽभिमन्यते॥
en: With a face lighted up by smiles, he once more began to practise severer austerities.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: यदि दद्यामहं राज्यं तुष्टो वै यस्य कस्यचित्। स भवेदचिराद् राजा न मिथ्या वाग् भवेन्मम॥
en: And once more, having gained (higher) success, he thought that he could by his-will force, then create the very highest objects. If, pleased with any person whatsoever I give him even sovereignty, he will immediately become a king, for my words will never be falsified.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: तस्य साक्षात् कुण्डधारो दर्शयामास भारत। ब्राह्मणस्य तपोयोगात् सौहृदेनाभिचोदितः॥
en: While he was thinking thus, kundadhara, actuated by his friendship for the Brahmana and no less by the ascetic success which the Brahmana had gained, appeared before him, O Bharata.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: समागम्य स तेनाथ पूजांचक्रे यथाविधि। ब्राह्मणः कुण्डधारस्य विस्मितश्चाभवन्नृप॥
en: Meeting with him the Brahmana offered him adorations according to the observances ordained. The Brahmana, however, felt some surprise, O king.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् कुण्डधारो दिव्यं ते चक्षुरुत्तमम्। पश्य राज्ञां गतिं विप्र लोकांश्चैव तु चक्षुषा॥
en: Then Kundadhara addressed the Brahmana, saying, you have now got an excellent and spiritual eye! See with this vision of yours the end which is attained by kings, and see all the worlds besides.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततो राजसहस्राणि मग्नानि निरये तदा। दूरादपश्यद् विप्रः स दिव्ययुक्तेन चक्षुषा॥
en: The Brahmana then, then, his spiritual vision, saw from a distance thousands of kings sunk in hell.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: कुण्डधार उवाच मां पूजयित्वा भावेन यदि त्वं दुःखमाप्नुयाः। कृतं मया भवेत् किं ते कश्च तेऽनुग्रहो भेवत्॥
en: Kundadhara said After having adored me with devotion you had got sorrow for your share, what then would have been the good done to you by me, and what the value of my favour.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: पश्य पश्य च भूयस्त्वं कामानिच्छेत् कथं नरः। स्वर्गद्वारं हि संरुद्धं मानुषेषु विशेषतः॥
en: Look, look, for what end do men seek the gratification of carnal enjoyments! The door of heaven is closed to men.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततोऽपश्यत् स कामं च क्रोधं लोभं भयं मदम्। निद्रां तन्द्री तथाऽऽलस्यमावृत्य पुरुषान् स्थितान्॥
en: Bhishma said The Brahmana then saw many men living in this world, embracing lust, anger, avarice, fear, pride, sheep, procrastination, and activity.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: कुण्डधार उवाच एतैर्लोकाः संसुरुद्धा देवानां मानुषाद् भयम्। तथैव देववचनाद् विघ् कुर्वन्ति सर्वशः॥
en: All human beings are enchained with these. The gods are afraid of men. These vices, at the order of the gods, mar and disconcert on all sides.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: न देवैरननुज्ञातः कश्चिद् भवति धार्मिकः। एष शक्तोऽसि तपसा दातुं राज्यं धनानि च॥
en: No man can become virtuous unless allowed by the gods. You have become competent to give away kingdoms and riches through your penances!

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः पपात शिरसा ब्राह्मणस्तोयधारिणे। उवाच चैनं धर्मात्मा महान् मेऽनुग्रहः कृतः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed, the pious Brahmana, bending his head to that Cloud, laid himself low on the ground, and said,-You have, indeed, done me a great favour!

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: कामलोभानुबन्धेन पुरा ते यदसूयितम्। मया स्नेहमविज्ञाय तत्र मे क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Unconscious of the great love shown by you towards me,I through the influency of desire and avarice, could not show good will towards you.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: क्षान्तमेव मयेत्युक्त्वा कुण्डधारो द्विजर्षभम्। सम्परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Then Kundadhara said That foremost of twice-born ones,-I have forgiven you!-and having embraced him with his arms disappeared there and then.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: ततः सर्वांस्तदा लोकान् ब्राह्मणोऽनुचचार हा कुण्डधारप्रसादेन तपसा सिद्धिमागतः॥
en: The Brahmana then travelled through all the worlds, having acquired ascetic through the favour of Kundadhara.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: विहायसा च गमनं तथा संकल्पितार्थता। धर्माच्छक्तया तथा योगाद् या चैव परमा गतिः॥
en: Through the power gained from virtue and penances, one acquires power to pass through the skies and to fructify all his wishes and purposes, and finally attain to the highest end.

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: देवताः ब्राह्मणा: सन्तो यक्षा मानुषचारणाः। धार्मिकान् पूजयन्तीह न धनाढ्यान् न कामिनः॥
en: Thë gods, Brahmanas, Yakshas, and all good men and Charanas always adore the virtuous but never the rich given up to the indulgence of their desires. success

description: Religion, Profit and Pleasure-which of them is superior. The discourse of Kundadhara
sn: सुप्रसन्ना हि ते देवा यत्ते धर्मे रता मतिः। धने सुखकला काचिद् धर्मे तु परमं सुखम्॥
en: The gods are truly placed with you since your mind is devoted to virtue. In riches there may be a very little happiness but in virtue the extent of happiness is very great.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच बहूनां यज्ञतपसामेकार्थानां पितामह। धर्मार्थं न सुखार्थार्थं कथं यज्ञः समाहितः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Of all sorts of sacrifices, all of which, of course, are said to have but one object, tell me, O grandfather, what that sacrifice is which has been ordained for only the sake of virtue and not for the acquisition of either heaven or riches.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि नारदेनानुकीर्तितम्। उच्छवृत्तेः पुरावृत्तं यज्ञा ब्राह्मणस्य च॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it I shall relate to you the history, formerly recited by Narada, of a Brahmana who for celebrating sacrifices, lived like a beggar.

sn: नारद उवाच राष्ट्रे धर्मोत्तरे श्रेष्ठे विदर्भेष्वभवद् द्विजः। उच्छवृत्तिर्ऋषिः कश्चिद् यज्ञं यष्टुं समादधे॥
en: Narada said In one of the foremost of kingdins that was known for virtue, there lived a Brahmana. Devoted to penances and living like a wretched beggar, that Brahmana was earnestly engaged in worshipping Vishnu in sacrifices.

sn: श्यामाकमशनं तत्र सूर्यपर्णी सुवर्चला। तिक्तं च विरसं शाकं तपसा स्वादुतां गतम्॥
en: He had Shyamaka for his food, as also Suryaparni and Suvarchala and other kinds of potherbs that were bitter and distasteful. for his penances, all these tasted sweet.

sn: उपगम्य वने सिद्धिं सर्वभूताविहिंसया। अपि मूलफलैरिष्टो यज्ञः स्वर्यः परंतप॥
en: Not injuring any creature, and leading the life of a forest recluse, he acquired ascetic success. With roots and fruits, O scorcher of foes, he used to worship Vishnu in sacrifices that were intended to bestow heaven upon him.

sn: तस्य भार्या व्रतकृशा शुचिः पुष्करधारिणी। यज्ञपत्नी समानीता सत्येनानुविधीयते॥ सा तु शापपरित्रस्ता तत्स्वभावानुवर्तिनी। मायूरजीर्णपर्णानां वस्त्रं तस्याश्च वर्णितम्॥
en: The Brahmana, whose name was Satya, had a wife namely Pushkaradharini. She was pureminded, and had emaciated herself by practising many austere vows. She did not, however, approve of the conduct of her husband. Summoned, however, to sit by him as his wife (in a sacrifice), she feared to incur his curse and, therefore, comported herself with his conduct. The garments that covered her body consisted of the plumes of peacocks.

sn: अकामया कृतस्तत्र यज्ञो होत्रनुशासनात्। शुक्रस्य पुनराजातिः पर्णादो नाम धर्मवित्॥ तस्मिन् वने समीपस्थो मृगोऽभूत् सहवासिकः। वचोभिरब्रवीत् सत्यं त्वयेदं दुष्कृतं कृतम्॥ यदि मन्त्रागहीनोऽयं यज्ञो भवति वै कृतः। मां भोः प्रक्षिप होत्रे त्वं गच्छ स्वर्गमनिन्दितः॥
en: Although reluctant she still celebrated that sacrifice at the command of her husband who had become its Hotri. In that forest, near to the Brahmana's hermitage, lived a neighbour of his, viz., the virtuous Parnada of Shukra's race, having assumed the form of a deer. He addressed that Brahmana, whose name was Satya. in open words and said to him:-You would be acting very improperly, if this sacrifice of yours were accomplished being defective in Mantras and other particulars of ritual! I, therefore, ask you to kill and cut me into pieces for making libations therewith on your sacrificial fire! Do this and becoming blameless go to heaven!

sn: ततस्तु यज्ञे सावित्री साक्षात् तं संन्यमन्त्रयत्। निमन्त्रयन्ती प्रत्युक्ता न हन्यां सहवासिनम्॥
en: Then the presiding goddess of the solar disc, viz., Savitri, came to that sacrifice in her incarnate form and insisted upon that Brahmana in doing what he was desired by that deer to do. The Brahmana said to that goddess, however, who thus insisted,-I shall not kill this deer who lives with me in this same neighbourhood!

sn: एवमुक्ता निवृत्ता सा प्रविष्टा यज्ञपावकम्। किं नु दुश्चरितं यज्ञे दिदृक्षुः सा रसातलम्॥
en: Thus addressed by the Brahmana, the goddess Savitri desisted and entered the sacrificial fire from desire of seeing the nether world, and wishing to avoid the sight of other short-comings in that sacrifice.

sn: स तु बद्धाञ्जलिं सत्यमयाचद्धरिणः पुनः। सत्येन स परिष्वज्य संदिष्टो गम्यतामिति॥
en: The deer then, with joined hands, again begged of Satya for that. Satya, however, embraced him in friendship and sent him away,-Go!

sn: ततः स हरिणो गत्वा पदान्यष्टौ न्यवर्तत। साधु हिंसय मां सत्य हतो यास्यामि सद्गतिम्॥
en: At this, the deer seemed to leave that place. But after he had gone eight steps he came back and said,-Verily, do you kill me! Truly do I say, killed by you I am sure to attain to a pious end!

sn: पश्य ह्यप्सरसो दिव्या मया दत्तेन चक्षुषा। विमानानि विचित्राणि गन्धर्वाणां महात्मनाम्॥
en: I give you (spiritual) vision. Behold the celestial Apsaras and the handsome cars of the great Gandharvas!

sn: ततः स सुचिरं दृष्ट्वा स्पृहालग्नेन चक्षुषा। मृगमालोक्य हिंसायां स्वर्गवासं समर्थयत्॥
en: Seeing (that spectacle) for a long time, with longing eyes, and seeing the deer and thinking that living in heaven can be acquired by only slaughter, he approved (of it).

sn: स तु धर्मो मृगो भूत्वा बहुवर्षोषितो वने। तस्य निष्कृतिमाधत्त न त्वसौ यज्ञसंविधिः॥
en: It was Dharına himself who had become a deer that lived in that forest for many years. Dharma provided for his salvation and advised him, saying,-This (destruction of living creatures) is not according to the ordinances about Sacrifice..

sn: तस्य तेनानुभावेन मृगहिंसात्मनस्तदा। तपो महत्समुच्छिन्नं तसमाद्धिंसा न यज्ञिया।॥
en: The penances, which had been of very great measure, of that Brahmana whose mind had cherished the desire of killing the deer, diminished greatly on account of that thought itself. The injuring of living creatures, therefore, is no part of sacrifice.

sn: ततस्तं भगवान् धर्मो यज्ञं याजयत स्वयम्। समाधानं च भार्याया लेभे स तपसा परम्॥
en: Then the illustrious Dharma, himself assisted that Brahmana, by acting as the priest, to perforin a sacrifice. The Brahmana, after this, on account of his penances, attained to the same state of mind with his wife.

sn: अहिंसा सकलो धर्मो हिंसाधर्मस्तथाहितः। सत्यं तेऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि यो धर्मः सत्यवादिनाम्॥
en: Abstention from injury is the religion which is perfect about its rewards. The religion of cruelty is only so far beneficial that it leads to heaven. I have described to you the religion of Truth which, indeed, is the religion of those who utter Brahma.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं भवति पापात्मा कथं धर्मं करोति वा। केन निर्वेदमादत्ते मोक्षं वा केन गच्छति॥
en: Yudhisthira said By what means does a man become sinful, by what does he acquire virtue, by what does he acquire renunciation, and by what does he acquire Liberation.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: भीष्म उवाच विदिताः सर्वधर्मास्ते स्थित्यर्थं त्वं तु पृच्छसि। शृणु मोक्षं सनिर्वेदं पापं धर्मं च मूलतः॥
en: Bhishma said now You know all duties. This question which you have put to me is only for confirmation of your conclusions. Listen fully to Liberation, and Renunciation, and Sin, and Virtue.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: विज्ञानार्थं हि पञ्चानामिच्छा पूर्वं प्रवर्तते। प्राप्यैकं जायते कामो द्वेषो वा भरतर्षभ॥
en: Perceiving any one of the five objects, desire runs after it at first. Indeed, obtaining them within the pale of the senses, O foremost of Bharata's family, desire or hatred originates.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: ततस्तदर्थं यतते कर्म चारभते महत्। इष्टानां रूपगन्धानामभ्यासं स चिकीर्षति॥
en: One then, for the sake of that object, trics and begins acts that require much labour. One tries his best for enjoying again and again those forms and scents that appear very sweet.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: ततो रागः प्रभवति द्वेषश्च तदनन्तरम्। ततो लोभः प्रभवति मोहश्च तदनन्तरम्॥
en: Gradually, attachment, hatred, greed and errors of judgement originate, answer

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: ततो रागः प्रभवति द्वेषश्च तदनन्तरम्। ततो लोभः प्रभवति मोहश्च तदनन्तरम्॥
en: The mind of one possessed by greed and mistake and affected by attachment and hatred is never bent to virtue. One then begins with hypocrisy to do deeds which are good.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: व्याजेन चरते धर्ममर्थ व्याजेन रोचते। व्याजेन सिद्ध्यमानेषु धनेषु कुरुनन्दन॥ तत्रैव कुरुते बुद्धिं ततः पापं चिकीर्षति। सुहृद्भिर्वार्यमाणोऽपि पण्डितैश्चापि भारत॥ उत्तरं न्याससम्बद्धं ब्रवीति विधिचोदितम्।
en: Indeed, with hypocrisy one then tries to acquire virture and with hypocrisy one likes to acquire riches. When one succeeds, O son of Kuru's family, in acquiring riches with hypocrisy, one gives his heart to such acquisition wholly. It is then that a person begins to do sinful acts, despite the admonitions of well-wishers and the wise, to all whom he makes reasonable conformable to the scriptural injunctions.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: अधर्मस्त्रिविधस्तस्य वर्धते रागमोहजः॥ पापं चिन्तयते चैव प्रब्रवीति करोति च।
en: Begotten of attachment and mistake, his sins of three sorts, rapidly multiply for he thinks sinfully, speaks sinfully, and acts sinfully.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: तस्याधर्मप्रवृत्तस्य दोषान पश्यन्ति साधवः॥ एकशीलाश्च मित्रत्वं भजन्ते पापकर्मिणः।
en: When he clearly begins to commit sin, the good notice his wickedness. Those, however, who are sinfully disposed contract friendship with him.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: स नेह सुखमाप्नोति कुत एव परत्र वै॥ एवं भवति पापात्मा धर्मात्मानं तु मे शृणु।
en: He cannot acquire happiness even here. Whence then would he succeed in acquiring happiness hereafter? It is thus that one becomes sinful. Listen now to me as I describe to you one who is righteous.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: यथा कुशलधर्मा स कुशलं प्रतिपद्यते॥ कुशलेनैव धर्मेण गतिमिष्टां प्रपद्यते।
en: Such a man, seeking, as he does, the wellbeing of others, succeeds in acquiring good for himself. By doing duties which are fraught with other people's well-being, he attains at last to a highly agreeable end.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: य एतान् प्रज्ञया दोषान् पूवमेवानुपश्यति॥ कुशलः सुखदुःखानां साधूंश्चाप्यथ सेवते। तस्य साधुसमाचारादभ्यासाच्चैव वर्धते॥
en: He who, helped by his wisdom, succeeds beforehand seeing the faults referred to above, who is skilled in determining what is happiness and what is sorrow and how each is engendered, and who waits respectfully upon the good, makes progress in acquiring virtue, both on account of his habit and such companionship of the good. The mind of such a person finds pleasure in virtue, and he live on, making virtue his stay.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: प्रज्ञा धर्मे च रमते धर्मं चैवोपजीवति। सोऽथ धर्मादवाप्तेषु धनेषु कुरुते मनः॥
en: If he wishes to acquire riches, he wishes only such wealth as inay be gained in righteous ways.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: तस्यैव सिञ्चते मूलं गुणान् पश्यति तत्र वै। धर्मात्मा भवति ह्येवं मित्रं च लभते शुभम्॥
en: In fact, he waters the roots of only thosc objects in which he sees merit. Thus does not become righteous and make friends with the good.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: स मित्रधनलाभात् तु प्रेत्य चेह च नन्दति। शब्दे स्पर्शे रसे रूपे तथा गन्धे च भारत॥ प्रभुत्व लभते जन्तुर्धर्मस्यैतत् फलं विदुः। स तु धर्मफलं लध्वा न हृष्यति युधिष्ठिर॥
en: On account of his acquisition of friends, of riches, and of children, he sports happily both here and hereafter. The mastery that a living being acquires over sound, touch, taste, forin, and scent, O Bharata, represents the fruit of virtue. Remember this. Having acquired the fruit of virtue, O Yudhishthira, such a man does not yield to joy.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: अतृप्यमाणो निर्वेदमादत्ते ज्ञानचक्षुषा। प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्यदा कामे रसे गन्धे न रज्यते॥ शब्दे स्पर्श तथा रूपे न च भावयते मनः। विमुच्यते तदा कामान्न च धर्मं विमुञ्चति॥
en: Without being satisfied with such fruits of virtue he follows Renunciation, led on by the eye of knowledge, When, having gained the eye of knowledge he ceases to find pleasure in the gratification of desire, in taste and in scent, when he does not allow his mind to run towards sound, touch and form, it is then that he succeeds in freeing himself from desire. He does not, however, even then renounce virtue or righteous acts.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: सर्वत्यागे च यतते दृष्ट्वा लोकं क्षयात्मकम्। ततो मोक्षाय यतते नानुपायादुपायतः॥
en: Seeing then all the worlds as being subject top destruction, he tries to renounce virtue and tries to attain to Liberation by the (well-known) means.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: शनैर्निर्वेदमादत्ते पापं कर्म जहाति च। धर्मात्मा चैव भवति मोक्षं च लभते परम्॥
en: Gradually renouncing all sinful deeds he follows Renunciation, and becoming righteoussouled succeeds at last in acquiring Liberation.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: एतत् ते कथितं तात यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। पापं धर्मस्तथा मोक्षो निर्वेदश्चैव भारत॥
en: I have now told you, O Son, of that about which you had asked me, viz., the topics of Sin, Righteousness, Renunciation, and Liberation, O Bharata.

description: Description of Liberation, Renunciation, sin and virtue
sn: तस्माद् धर्मे प्रवर्तेथाः सर्वावस्थं युधिष्ठिर। धर्मे स्थितानां कौन्तेय सिद्धिर्भवति शाश्वती॥
en: You should, therefore, O Yudhishthira, follow virtue under all circumstances. Eternal is the success, O son of Kunti, of you who follow righteousness.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मोक्षः पितामहेनोक्त उपायान्नानुपायतः। तमुपायं यथान्यायं श्रोतुमिच्छामि भारत॥
en: Yudhisthira said You have said, O grand-father, that Liberation is to be acquired by means and not otherwise. I wish to hear duly what those means are.

sn: भीष्म उवाच त्वय्येवैतन्महाप्राज्ञ युक्तं निपुणदर्शनम्। येनोपायेन सर्वार्थं नित्यं मृगयसेऽनघ॥
en: Bhishma said O you of great wisdom, this enquiry which you have made me and which is connected with a subtle topic, is really worthy of you, since you, O sinless one, always try to accomplish all your objects by the application of means.

sn: करणे घटस्य या बुद्धिर्घटोत्पत्तौ न सा मता। एवं धर्माभ्युपायेषु नान्यधर्मेषु कारणम्॥
en: That state of mind which one feels when he makes an earthen jar for his use, disappears after the jar has been completed. Likewise, that cause which makes persons who regard virtue as the root of advancement and prosperity ceases to act with them who seek to acquire Liberation.

sn: पूर्वे समुद्रे यः पन्थाः स न गच्छति पश्चिमम्। एकः पन्था हि मोक्षस्य तन्मे विस्तरतः शृणु॥
en: That path which leads to the Eastern Ocean is not the path by which one can go to the Western Ocean. There is only one path which leads to Liberation. Listen to me as I describe it to you in detail.

sn: क्षमया क्रोधमुच्छिन्द्यात् कामं संकल्पवर्जनात्। सत्त्वससंसेवनाद् धीरो निद्रां च च्छेत्तुमर्हति॥
en: One should, by practising forgiveness, root out anger and by renouncing all purposes, root out desire. By practising the quality of goodness one should conquer sleep.

sn: अप्रमादाद् भयं रक्षेच्छ्वासं क्षेत्रज्ञशीलनात्। इच्छां द्वेषं च कामं च धैर्येण विनिवर्तयेत्॥ भ्रमं सम्मोहमावर्तमभ्यासाद् विनिवर्तयेत्। निद्रां च प्रतिभां चैव ज्ञानाभ्यासेन तत्त्ववित्॥
en: By carefulness one should keep off fear, and by contemplation of the Soul one should conquer vital airs. One should remove by patience desire, hatred, and lust; and error, ignorance, and doubt, by study of truth. By pursuit of knowledge one should avoid inquiry after uninteresting things.

sn: उपद्रवांस्तथा रोगान् हितजीर्णमिताशनात्। लोभं मोहं च संतोषाद् विषयास्तत्त्वदर्शनात्॥
en: By frugal and easily digestible food one should dispell all disorders and diseases. By contentment one should remove greed and stupefaction of judgement, and all earthly concerns should be avoided by a knowledge of the truth.

sn: अनुक्रोशादधर्मं च जयेद् धर्ममवेक्षया। आयत्या च जयेदाशामर्थं संगविवर्जनात्॥
en: By practising benevolence one should conquer sin, and by regard for all creatures one should gain virtue. One should avoid expectation by thinking that it is connected with the future; and one should renounce riches by abandoning desire itself.

sn: अनित्यत्वेन च स्नेहं क्षुधां योगेन पण्डितः। कारुण्येनात्मनो मानं तृष्णां च परितोषतः॥
en: The intelligent man should cast off affection by thinking that everything is fickle. He should control hunger by practising Yoga. By practising benevolence one should keep off all ideas of ego, and remove all sorts of craving by adopting contentment.

sn: उत्थानेन जयेत् तन्द्री वितर्कं निश्चयाज्जयेत्। मौनेन बहुभाष्यं च शौर्येण च भयं त्यजेत्॥
en: By exertion should subdue procrastination, by certainty all kinds of doubt, one by taciturnity, loquaciousness, and by courage every sort of fear.

sn: यच्छेद् वाङ्मनसी बुद्ध्या तां यच्छेज्ज्ञानचक्षुषा। ज्ञानमात्मावबोधेन यच्छेदात्मानमात्मना॥
en: Speech and mind are to be controlled by the Understanding, and the Understanding, in its turn, by the eye of knowledge. Knowledge, again, is to be controlled by the knowledge of the Soul, and finally the Soul it to be controlled by the Soul.

sn: तदेतदुपशान्तेन बोद्धव्यं शुचिकर्मणा। योगदोषान् समुच्छिद्य पञ्च यान् कवयो विदुः॥
en: This last is acquired by those who are of pure acts and endued with tranquillity of soul, the means being the subjugation of those five obstacles of Yoga of which the learned speak.

sn: कामं क्रोधं च लोभं च भयं स्वप्नं च पञ्चमम्। परित्यज्य निषेवेत यतवाग् योगसाधनान्॥ ध्यानमध्ययनं दानं सत्यं ह्रीरार्जवं क्षमा। शौचमाहारतः शुद्धिरिन्द्रियाणां च संयमः॥
en: By renouncing desire, anger covetousness, fear and sleep, one should controlling speech, practise the observances favourable to Yoga, viz., contemplation, study, gift, truth, modesty, candour, forgiveness, purity of heart, purity of food, and the subjugation of the senses.

sn: एतैर्विवधते तेजः पाप्मानमुपहन्ति च। सिध्यन्ति चास्य संकल्या विज्ञानं च प्रवर्तते॥
en: By these one's energy is increased, sins are removed, wishes crowned with success, and knowledge gained.

sn: धूतपाप: स तेजस्वी लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः। कामक्रोधौ वशे कृत्वा निनीषेद् ब्रह्मणः पदम्॥
en: When one becomes purged of sins and possessed of energy and abstemious in diet and the master of his senses, one then, having conquered both desire and anger, seeks to attain to Brahma.

sn: अमूढत्वमसंगित्वं कामक्रोधविवर्जनम्। अदैन्यमनुदीर्णत्वमनुद्वेगो व्यवस्थितिः॥ एष मार्गो हि मोक्षस्य प्रसन्नो विमलः शुचिः। तथा वाक्कायमनसां नियमः कामतोऽन्यथा॥
en: The avoidance of ignorance, the absence of attachment, freedom from desire and anger, the power that is acquired by Yoga, the absence of pride and haughtiness, freedom from anxiety, absence of attachment to anything like home and family,—these forin the path of Liberation. That path is delightful, stainless, and pure. Likewise, the control of speech, of body, and of mind, when practised from the absence of desire, forms also the path of Liberation.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। नारदस्य च संवादं देवलस्यासितस्य च॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old discourse that took place between Narada, and Asita-Devala.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: आसीनं देवलं वृद्धं बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमतां वरम्। नारदः परिपप्रच्छ भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययम्॥
en: Once on a time Narada, seeing that foremost of intelligent men, viz., Devala of venerable years, seated at his ease, asked him about the origin and the destruction of all creatures.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: नारद उवाच कुत: सृष्टमिदं विश्वं ब्रह्मन् स्थावरजङ्गमम्। प्रलये च कमभ्येति तद् भवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे॥
en: Narada said Whence, O Brahmana, has this universe, consisting of mobile and iminobile objects, been created? When, again, the all-embracing destruction sets in, into whom does it merge! Let your learned self describe this to me.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: असित उवाच येभ्यः सृजति भूतानि काले भावप्रचोदितः। महाभूतानि पञ्चेति तान्याहुर्भूतचिन्तकाः॥
en: are Those from which the Supreme Self, when the time comes, actuated by the desire of existence in various forms, creates all creatures, and said by persons conversant with objects to be the five essential principles.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: तेभ्यः सृजति भूतानि काल आत्मप्रचोदितः। एतेभ्यो यः परं ब्रूयादसद् ब्रूयादसंशयम्॥
en: Time, moved by the Understanding, created other objects from them. He who says that there is anything else save these, says the untruth.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: विद्धि नारद पञ्चैताशाश्वतानचलान् ध्रुवान्। महतस्तेजसो राशीन् कालषष्ठान् स्वभावतः॥
en: Know, O Narada, that these five are eternal, indestructible, and without beginning and without end. With Kala as their sixth, these five essential ingredients naturally possessed of great power.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: आपश्चैवान्तरिक्षं च पृथिवी वायुपावको। नासीद्धि परमं तेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो मुक्तसंशयम्॥
en: Water, Ether, Earth, Air, and Fire,—these are those five principal elements. Forsooth, there is nothing higher or superior to these.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: नोपपत्त्या न वा युक्त्या त्वसद् ब्रूयादसंशयम्। वेत्यैतानभिनिर्वृत्तान् घडेते यस्य राशयः॥
en: The existence of nothing else can is inferred by any one agreeably to the conclusions of the Shrutis or arguments drawn from reason. If any one does hold the existence of anything else, then his assertion would, in sooth, be useless. Know that these six form all others. That of which are all these is called non-existent.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: पञ्चैव तानि कालश्च भावाभावौ च केवलौ। अष्टौ भूतानि भूतानां शाश्वतानि भवात्ययौ॥
en: These five, and Kala (or Jiva), the effects of past acts, and Ignorance,-these eight eternal essences are the causes of the birth and destruction of creatures.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: अभावं यान्ति तेष्वेव तेभ्यश्च प्रभवन्त्यपि। विनष्टोऽप्यनु तान्येव जन्तुर्भवति पञ्चधा॥
en: When creatures are destroyed it is into these that they merge; and when they are born, it is again from them that they do so. Indeed, after destruction, a creature resolves itself into those five elements.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: तस्य भूमिमयो देहः श्रोत्रमाकाशसम्भवम्। सूर्याच्चक्षुरसुयोरञ्ज्यस्तु खलु शोणितम्॥
en: His body is made of earth; his ear is made of ether; his eye has light for it cause, his life is of air, and his blood is of water.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: चक्षुषी नासिकाकर्णी त्वक् जिह्वेति च पञ्चमी। इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थानां ज्ञानानि कवयो विदुः॥
en: The two eyes, the nose, the two ears, the skin, and the tongue, are the senses. These, the learned hold, exist for perception of their various objects.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: दर्शनं श्रवणं घ्राणं स्पर्शनं रसनं तथा। उपपत्त्या गुणान् विद्धि पञ्च पञ्चसु पञ्चधा॥
en: Seeing, hearing, smelling, touching and tasting are the actions of the senses. The five senses, are connected with five objects in five ways. Know, by the inference of reason, their similitude of attributes.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: रूपं गन्धो रसः स्पर्शः शब्दश्चैवाथ तद्गुणाः। इन्द्रियैरुपलभ्यन्ते पञ्चधा पञ्च पञ्चभिः॥
en: Form, scent, taste, touch, and sound, are the five properties that are perceived by the five senses in five different ways.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: रूपं गन्धं रसं स्पर्श चैवाथ तद्गुणान्। इन्द्रियाणि न बुध्यन्ते क्षेत्रज्ञस्तैस्तु बुध्यते॥
en: These five properties, viz., form scent, taste, touch, and sound, are not really perceived by the senses, but it is the Soul that apprehends them through the senses.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: चित्तमिन्द्रियसंघातात् परं तस्मात् परं मनः। मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिः क्षेत्रज्ञो बुद्धितः परः॥
en: That which is called Faculty is superior to all the Superior to Mind is Understanding, and superior to Understanding is Soul. senses.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: पूर्वं चेतयते जन्तुरिन्द्रियैर्विषयान् पृथक्। विचार्य मनसा पश्चादथ बुद्ध्या व्यवस्यति। । इन्द्रियैरुपलब्धार्थान् बुद्धिमांस्तु व्यवस्यति॥
en: At first a living creature perceives various objects through the senses. With Mind he reflects over them, and then with the help of Understanding, he arrives at certainty of knowledge. Endued with Understanding, one arrives at certainty of conclusions regarding objects perceived through the senses.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: चित्तमिन्द्रियसंघातं मनो बुद्धिस्तथाष्टमी। अष्टौ ज्ञानेन्द्रियाण्याहुरेतान्यध्यात्मचिन्तकाः॥
en: The five senses, Faculty, Mind, and Understanding,-these are regarded as organs of knowledge by those conversant with the spiritual science.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: पाणिपादं च पायुश्च मेहनं पञ्चमं मुखम्। इति संशब्द्यमानानि शृणु कर्मेन्द्रियाण्यपि॥
en: The hands, the feet, the anus, the inembrum virile, the mouth, form the five organs of actions.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: जल्पनाभ्यवहारार्थं मुखमिन्द्रियमुच्यते। गमनेन्द्रियं तथा पादौ कर्मणः करणे करौ॥
en: The mouth is spoken of as an organ of action because it contains the instrument of speech, and that of eating. The feet are organs of locomotion and the hands for doing various sorts of work.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: पायूपस्थं विसर्गार्थमिन्द्रिये तुल्यकर्मणी। विसर्गे च पुरीषस्य विसर्गे चापि कामिके॥
en: The anus and the membrum virile are two organs which exist for evacuation. The first is for evacuation of stools, the second for that of urine as also of the semen when one feels the influence of desire.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: बलं षष्ठं षडेतानि वाचा सम्यग्यथा मम। ज्ञानचेष्टेन्द्रियगुणाः सर्वेषां शब्दिता मया॥
en: Besides these, there is a sixth organ of action. It is called muscle. These then are the names of the six organs of action according to the book written on the subject. I have now described to you the names of all the organs of knowledge and of action, and all the attributes of the five elements.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: इन्द्रियाणां स्वकर्मेभ्यः श्रमादुपरमो यदा। भवतीन्द्रियसंत्यागादथ स्वपिति वै नरः॥
en: When on account of the organs being fatigued, they cease to discharge their respective functions, the owner of those organs, their action being suspended is said to sleep.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: इन्द्रियाणां व्युपरमे मनोऽव्युपरतं यदि। सेवते विषयानेव तं विद्यात् स्वप्नदर्शनम्॥
en: If when the action of these organs is stopped, the action of the mind, does not cease, but on the other hand the mind continues to act, that state of Consciousness is called Dream.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: सात्त्विकाश्चैव ये भावास्तथा तामसराजसाः। कर्मयुक्तान् प्रशंसन्ति सात्त्विकानितरांस्तथा॥
en: During wakefulness there are three states of the mind viz., that connected with Goodness, that with Darkness, and that with Ignorance. In dream also the mind is connected with the same three states. Those very states, when they appear is dreams, connected with pleasurable actions, are spoken highly of.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: आनन्दः कर्मणां सिद्धिः प्रतिपत्तिः परा गतिः। सात्त्विकस्य निमित्तानि भावान् संश्रयते स्मृतिः॥ जन्तुष्वेकतमेष्वेवं भावा ये विधिमास्थिताः। भावयोरीप्सितं नित्यं प्रत्यक्षं गमनं तयोः॥
en: Happiness, success, knowledge, and absence of attachment are the marks of the quality of Goodness. Whatever states are experienced by living creatures, as shown in acts, during their hours of wakefulness, reappear in memory during their hours of sleep when they dream. The passage of our ideas as they exist during wakefulness into those of dreams, and that of ideas as they exist in dreams into those of wakefulness, become directly perceptible in that state of consciousness which is called dreamless sleep. That is eternal, and that is desirable.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: इन्द्रियाणि च भावाश्च गुणाः सप्तदश स्मृताः। तेषामष्टादशो देही यः शरीरे स शाश्वतः॥
en: There are five organs of knowledge, and five of action; with muscular power, mind, understanding, and faculty, and with also the three qualities of goodness, darkness and ignorance, the number, it has been said, comes up to seventeen. The eighteenth in the calculation is he who owns the body. Indeed, he who lives in this body is eternal.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: अथवा सशरीरास्ते गुणाः सर्वे शरीरिणाम्। संश्रितास्तद् वियोगे हि सशरीरा न सन्ति ते॥
en: All those seventeen (with Avidya or nesciene as eighteenth) living in the body, exist attached to him who owns the body. When the owner disappear from the body, those eighteen cease to live together in the body.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: अथवा संनिपातोऽयं शरीरं पाञ्चभौतिकम्। एकश्च दश चाष्टौ च गुणाः सह शरीरिणा॥
en: Or, this body made up the five principal elements only a combination. The eighteen attributes, with him that owns the body, and counting stomachic heat numbering twentieth, form that which is known as the Combination of the Five.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: उष्मणा सह विंशो वा संघातः पाञ्चभौतिकः। महान् संधारयत्येतच्छरीरं वायुना सह॥
en: There is a Being called Mahat (principal of greatness) which, with the help of the wind (called Prana), keeps up this combination containing the twenty ihings that have been named, and in the matter of the destruction of that body the wind is only the instrument in the hands of that same Mahat.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: तस्य प्रभावयुक्तस्य निमित्तं देहभेदने। यथैवोत्पद्यते किंचित् पञ्चत्वं गच्छते तथा॥ पुण्यपापविनाशान्ते पुण्यपापसमीरितः। देहं विशति कालेन ततोऽयं कर्मसम्भवम्॥
en: Whatever creature is born is resolved once more into the five principal elements upon the exhaustion of his merits and demerits; and moved again by the merits and demerits acquired in that life enters into another body resulting from his deeds.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: हित्वा हित्वा ह्ययं प्रैति देहाद् देहं कृताश्रयः। कालसंचोदितः क्षेत्री विशीर्णाद् वा गृहाद् गृहम्॥
en: His habitation always resulting from nescience, desire, and acts, he migrates from body to body, leaving off one after another repeatedly, urged on by Time, like a person leaving house after in succession.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: तत्र नैवानुतप्यन्ते प्राज्ञा निश्चितनिश्चयाः। कृपणास्त्वनुतप्यन्ते जनाः सम्बन्धदर्शिनः॥
en: The wise, wise, gifted with certainty of knowledge, do not yield to grief upon seeing this. Only the foolish, erroneously supposing relationships indulge in grief on seeing such changes of habitation.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: न ह्ययं कस्यचित् कश्चिन्नास्य कश्च न विद्यते। भवत्येको ह्ययं नित्यं शरीरे सुखदुःखभाक्॥
en: This individual soul is no one's relation; there is none again that may be said to belong to him. He is always alone, and he is himself the creator of his own body and his own happiness and misery.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: नैव संजायते जन्तुर्न च जातु विपद्यते। याति देहमयं मुक्त्वा कदाचित्परमां गतिम्॥
en: This individual is never born, nor does he ever die. Freed from the fetters of body, he succeeds sometimes in acquiring the highest end.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: पुण्यपापमयं देहं क्षपयन् कर्मसंक्षयात्। क्षीणदेहः पुनर्देही ब्रह्मत्वमुपगच्छति॥
en: Deprived of body, because freed through the dissipation of acts from bodies that are the outcome of merits and demerits, individual at last attains to Brahma.

description: The discourse between Narada and Asita Devala about creation
sn: पुण्यपापक्षयार्थं हि सांख्यज्ञानं विधीयते। तत्क्षये ह्यस्य पश्यन्ति ब्रह्मभावे परां गतिम्॥
en: For the dissipation of both merits and demerits, Knowledge has been described as the cause in the Sankhya school. Upon the dissipation of merit and demerit, when individual soul attains to the status of Brahma, the learned behold the attainment of individual soul to the highest end.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: येयमर्थोद्भवा तृष्णा युधिष्ठिर उवाच भ्रातरः पितरः पौत्रा ज्ञातयः सुहृदः सुताः। अर्थहेतोर्हताः क्रूरैरस्माभिः पापकर्मभिः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Cruel and sinful as we are, alas, we have killed brothers and fathers and grandsons and relatives and friends and sons.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: कथमेतां पितामह। निवर्तयेयं पापानि तृष्णया कारिता वयम्॥
en: How, O grandfather, shall we remove this thirst for riches. Alas, through that thirst we have committed many sinful deeds.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। गीतं विदेहराजेन माण्डव्यायानुपृच्छते॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old narrative of what was said by the king of the Videhas to the enquiring Mandavya.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: सुसुखं बत जीवामि यस्य मे नास्ति किंचन। मिथिलायां प्रदीप्तायां न मे दह्यति किंचन॥
en: The king of the Videhas said, I have nothing, yet I live in great happiness. If the whole of Mithila be reduced to ashes nothing of mine will be burnt down.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: अर्थाः खलु समृद्धा हि बाढं दुःखं विजानताम्। असमृद्धास्त्वपि सदा मोहयन्त्यविचक्षणान्॥
en: Tangible possessions of what value they may be, are a source of sorrow to men of knowledge; while properties of cven little value attract the foolish. one

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: यच्च कामसुखं लोके यच्च दिव्यं महत्सुखम्। तृष्णाक्षयसुखस्यैते नार्हतः षोडशी कलाम्॥
en: Whatever happiness is in this world, owing to the gratification of desire, and whatever celestial happiness exists of high value, do not form even a sixteenth part of the felicity that accrues from the disappearance of desire.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: यथैव शृङ्गं गोः काले वर्धमानस्य वर्धते। तथैव तृष्णा वित्तेन वर्धमानेन वर्धते॥
en: As the horns of a cow grow with the growth of the cow itself, similarly the thirst for riches multiplies with increasing acquisitions of wealth.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: किंचिदेव ममत्वेन यदा भवति कल्पितम्। तदेव परितापाय नाशे सम्पद्यते पुनः॥
en: The object for which feels an attachment, becomes a source of pain to him when it is lost.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: न कामाननुरुद्धयेत दुःखं कामेषु वै रतिः। प्राप्यार्थमुपयुञ्जीत धर्मं कामान् विसर्जयेत्॥
en: One should not entertain desire. Attachment to desire brings on sorrow. When riches have been acquired one should devote it to virtuous purposes. One should even then relinquish desire.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: विद्वान् सर्वेषु भूतेषु आत्मना सोपमो भवेत्। कृतकृत्यो विशुद्धात्मा सर्वं त्यजति चैव ह॥
en: The man of knowledge always considers other creatures like unto himself. Having purified his soul and gained success, he casts off everything here.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: उभे सत्यानृते त्यक्त्वा शोकानन्दौ प्रियाप्रिये। भयाभयं च संत्यज्य स प्रशान्तो निरामयः॥
en: By shaking off both truth and falsehood, grief and joy, the agreeable and disagreeable, fearlessness and fear, one acquires tranquillity, and becomes free from anxiety.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः। योऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम्॥१२।
en: That thirst which cannot be shaken off by men of foolish understanding, which does not decrease with the decline of the body, and which is considered as dreadful disease, one who succeeds in shaking off is sure to find happiress.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: चारित्रमात्मनः पश्यंश्चन्द्रशुद्धमनामयम्। धर्मात्मा लभते कीर्तिं प्रेत्य चेह यथासुखम्॥
en: The virtuous man by seeing his own conduct has become bright as the moon and free from every sort of evil, succeeds in happily acquiring great fame both here and hereafter.

description: How the thirst for riches can be removed. The discourse between Janaka and Mandavya
sn: राज्ञस्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रीतिमानभवद् द्विजः। पूजयित्वा च तद् वाक्यं माण्डव्यो मोक्षमाश्रितः॥
en: Hearing these words of the king, the Brahmana became filled with joy, and speaking highly of what he heard, Mandavya followed the path of Liberation.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अतिक्रामति कालेऽस्मिन् सर्वभूतभयावहे। किं श्रेयः प्रतिपद्येत तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह।१।।
en: Yudhishthira said Time, which is a terror to all creatures, is rolling on. What is that source of good for which one should try? Tell me this, O grandfather.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। पितुः पुत्रेण संवादं तं निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old discourse between father and son. Listen to it, 0 Yudhishthira.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: द्विजातेः कस्यचित् पार्थ स्वाध्यायनिरतस्य वै। पुत्रो बभूव मेधावी मेधावी नाम नामतः॥
en: Once on a time, O son of Pritha, a twiceborn person devoted to only the study of the Vedas had a very intelligent son who passed by the name of Medhavin.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: सोऽब्रवीत् पितरं पुत्रः स्वाध्यायकरणे रतम्। मोक्षधर्मेष्वकुशलं मोक्षधर्मविचक्षणः॥
en: Himself a master of the religion of Liberation, the son one day asked his father who was not conversant with that religion and who was engaged in following the Vedic precepts, this question.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: पुत्र उवाच धीर: किंस्वित् तात कुर्यात् प्रजानन् क्षिप्रं ह्यायुर्धश्यते मानवानाम्। पितस्तथाऽऽख्याहि यथार्थयोगं ममानुपूर्व्या येन धर्मं चरेयम्॥
en: The son said What should an intelligent men do, O father, knowing that the life of men runs speedily away? Tell me this truly and in due order, O father, so that, guided by your instruction I may undertake the acquisition of virtue.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: पितोवाच अधीत्य वेदान् ब्रह्मचर्येषु पुत्र पुत्रानिच्छेत्पावनाय पितृणाम्। अग्नीनाधाय विधिवच्चेश्यज्ञो वनं प्रविश्याथ मुनिळूभूषेत्॥
en: The father said Having read the Vedas all the while following the duties of Brahmacharya, O son, one should then desire for children for the sake of rescuting one's departed manes. Having established his fire then and performing the sacrifices that are ordained, one should then retire into the forest and then become a hermit.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: पुत्र उवाच एवमभ्याहते लोके सर्वतः परिवारिते। अमोघासु पतन्तीषु किं धीर इव भाषसे॥
en: The son said, When the world is thus attacked on all sides, and when such irresistible things are falling on all sides, how can you speak so calinly?

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: पितोवाच कथमभ्याहतो लोकः केन वा परिवारितः। अमोघाः काः पतन्तीह किं नु भीषयसीवमाम्॥
en: The sire said How is the world attacked?-By what is it besieged? What are those irresistible things that are falling on all sides? Do you frighten me with your words?-

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: पुत्र उवाच मृत्युनाभ्याहतो लोको जरया परिवारितः। अहोरात्राः पतन्तीमे तच्च कस्मान्न बुद्ध्यसे॥
en: The world is attacked by Death. It is attacked by Decrepitude. Days and Nights are continually falling. Why do you not take care of these.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: यदाहमेव जानामि न मृत्युस्तिष्ठतीति ह। सोऽहं कथं प्रतीक्षिष्ये ज्ञानेनापिहितश्चरन्॥
en: When I know that Death does not wait here for any one how can I possibly wait thus covered in a sheath of Ignorance and attending affairs?

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: रात्र्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामायुरल्पतरं यदा। गाधोदके मत्स्य इव सुखं विन्त कस्तदा॥
en: When with every night the period of a man's existence wears away, when, indeed, one's position is similar to that of a fish a pool of shallow water, who can be happy?

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: पुष्पाणीव विचिन्वन्तमन्यत्र गतमानसम्। अनवाप्तेषु कामेषु मृत्युरभ्येति मानवम्॥
en: Death meets one in the very midst of his affairs, before the attainment of his objects, finding one as careless as a person while plucking flowers. to my

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्ने चापराह्निकम्। न हि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतं वास्य न वा कृतम्॥
en: What is kept for being done tomorrow should be done to-day; and what one thinks of doing in the afternoon should be done in the forenoon. Death does not wait for a man whether he has, or has not done his acts.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: अद्यैव कुरु यच्छ्यो मा त्वां कालोऽत्यगान्महान्। को हि जानाति कस्याद्य मृत्युकालो भविष्यति॥
en: Do to-day what is for your behoof! See that Death, who is irresistible, may not overcome you. Who knows that Death will not come to one this very day.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: अकृतेष्वेव कार्येषु मृत्यु सम्प्रकर्षति। युवैव धर्मशीलः स्यादनिमित्तं हि जीवितम्॥
en: Before a person's acts are done, Death drags one away. One should, therefore, begin to practise virtue while he is still young, for life is uncertain.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: कृते धर्मे भवेत् प्रीतिरिह प्रेत्य च शाश्वती। मोहेन हि समाविष्टः पुत्रदारार्थमुद्यतः॥
en: By acquiring virtue one is sure to acquire eternal happiness both in this world and in the next. Overpowered by folly one is up and doing on behalf of his sons and wives.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: कृत्वा कार्यमकार्यं वा तुष्टिमेषां प्रयच्छति। तं पुत्रपशुसम्पन्नं व्यासक्तमनसं नरम्॥ सुप्तं व्याघ्रं महौघो वा मृत्युरादाय गच्छति। संचिन्वानकमेवैनं कामानामवितृप्तकम्॥ वृकीवोरणमासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति। इदं कृतमिदं कार्यमिदमन्यत् कृताकृतम्॥ एवमीहासमायुक्तं मृत्युरादाय गच्छति। कृतानां फलमप्राप्तं कार्याणां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्॥ क्षेत्रापणगृहासक्तं मृत्युरादाय गच्छति। दुर्बलं बलवन्तं च प्राशं शूरं जडं कविम्॥ अप्राप्तसर्वकामार्थं मृत्युदाराय गच्छति। मृत्युर्जरा च व्याधिश्च दुःखं चानेककारणम्॥ असंत्याज्यं यदा मत्यैः किं स्वस्थ इव तिष्ठसि। जातमेवान्तकोऽन्ताय जरा चाभ्येति देहिनम्॥
en: By performing deeds good or bad, one pleases his people. Death seizes him possessed of sons and animals, and with mind given to them, and runs away like a tiger carrying away a sleeping deer. While still engaged in acquiring various objects of desire, and while still unsatiated with their enjoyment, Death attacks him and runs away like a she-wolf seizing a sheep and running away with it.-_'This has been done,-this remain to be done this other is half done'-one may say thus, but Death, not caring for a person's desire to finish his unfinished acts, seizes and drags him away. Death seizes and carries away one who has not yet gained the fruit of what he has already done, amongst those attached to action, one busied with his field or shop or house. Death seizes and carries away the weak, the strong, the wise, the brave, the idiotic, the learned, or him who has not yet obtained the gratification of any of his desires. Death, decrepitude, disease, sorrow, and many things of a similar nature, cannot he shunned by mortals. How then O father, can you sit so at your ease? As soon as an embodied creature is born, Decrepitude and Death come and possess him for his destruction.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: अनुषत्तु द्वयेनैते भावाः स्थावरजङ्गमाः। न मृत्युसेनामायान्तीं जातु कश्चित् प्रबाधते॥ बलात् सत्यमृते त्वेकं सत्ये ह्यमृतमाश्रितम्। मृत्योर्वा गृहमेतद् वै या ग्रामे वसतो रतिः॥
en: All forms of existence, mobile and immobile, are possessed by these two. When the soldiers, which constitute Death's army, march, nothing can resist them except that one thing, viz., the power of Truth, for in Truth alone Immortality lives. The joy which one feels of living in the midst of men is residence of Death.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: देवानामेष वै गोष्ठो यदरण्यमिति श्रुतिः। निबन्धनी रज्जुरेषा या ग्रामे वसतो रतिः॥
en: The Shruti says that what is called the forest is the true fold for the deities, while the joy one feels in living in the midst of men is, as it were, the fetter for binding the dweller.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: छित्त्वैनां सुकृतो यान्ति नैनां छिन्दन्ति दुष्कृतः। यो न हिंसति सत्त्वानि मनोवाक्कर्महेतुभिः॥ जीवितार्थापनयनैः प्राणिभिर्न स बुद्ध्यते। तस्मात् सत्यव्रताचारः सत्यव्रतपरायणः॥ सत्यकाम: समो दान्तः सत्येनैवान्तकं जयेत्। अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च द्वयं देहे प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: The pious cut it and escape. The sinful can not cut it. He who does not injure other creatures in thought, word, and deed, and who never injures others by taking away their means of livelihood, is never injured by any crcature. Therefore, one should practise the vow of truth, be steadfastly devoted to the vow of truth, and should wish for nothing but the truth. Governing all his senses and regarding all creatures impartially, one should defeat Death with the help of Truth. Both Immortality and Death are in the body.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: मृत्युरापद्यते मोहात् सत्येनापद्यतेऽमृतम्। सोऽहं सत्यमहिंसाथी कामक्रोधबहिष्कृतः॥ समाश्रित्य सुखं क्षेमी मृत्युं हास्याम्यमृत्युवत्। शान्तियज्ञरतो दान्तो ब्रह्मयज्ञे स्थितो मुनिः॥ वाङ्मनःकर्मयज्ञश्च भविष्याम्युदगायने। पशुयज्ञैः कथं हिंस्रैर्मादृशो यष्टुमर्हति॥
en: Death comes from folly, and Immortality is acquired by Truth. Transcending desire and anger, abstaining from injury, I shall adopt Truth and happily acquiring what is for my behoof avoid Death like an Immortal. Engaged in the Sacrifice that is formed by Peace, and employed also in the Sacrifice of Brahma, and controlling my senses, the Sacrifices I shall perform and those of speech, mind, and deeds, when the sun enters his northerly course. How can one like me celebrate an Animal Sacrifice which is full of cruelty.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: अन्तवद्भिरुत प्राज्ञः क्षत्रयज्ञैः पिशाचवत्। आत्मन्येवात्मना जात आत्मनिष्ठोऽप्रजः पितः॥
en: How can one like me, endued with wisdom, perform like a cruel being, a Sacrifice of destruction after the manner of what is sanctioned for the Kshatriyas,-a Sacrifice which produces only fickle rewards, In myself have I been begotten by myown self. O father, without seeking to procreate progeny, I shall rest myself on my own self!

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: आत्मयज्ञो भविष्यामि न मां तारयति प्रजा। यस्य वाङ्मनसी स्यातां सम्यक् प्रणिहिते सदा॥ तपस्त्यागश्च योगश्च स तैः सर्वमवाप्नुयात्। नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति विद्यासमं फलम्॥ नास्ति रागसमं दुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम्॥
en: I shall celebrate the Sacrifice of Self, I require no children to rescue me. He whose words and thoughts are always well-governed, he who has penances and Renunciation, and Yoga, is sure to acquire everything through these. There is no eye like Knowledge. There is no reward like Knowledge. There is no sorrow like attachment. There is no happiness like Renunciation.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: नैतादृशं ब्राह्मणस्यास्ति वित्तं यथैकता समता सत्यता च। शीले स्थितिर्दण्डनिधानमार्जवं ततस्ततश्चोपरमः क्रियाभ्यः॥
en: For a Brahmana there can be no wealth like living in solitude, an impartial eye for all creatures, truthfulness of speech, steady observance of good conduct, the total abandonment of the rod (of chastisement), simplicity, and the gradual abstention from all acts.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: किं ते धनैर्बान्धवैर्वापि किं ते कि ते दारैर्ब्राह्मण यो मरिष्यसि। आत्मानमन्विच्छ गुहां प्रविष्टं पितामहास्ते क्व गताः पिता च॥
en: Why do you require riches, relatives, friends, and wives? You are a Brahmana and you have death to encounter! Search you own Self which is concealed in a cave. Where have your grandfathers gone and where your father too?

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: भीष्म उवाच पुत्रस्यैतद् वचः श्रुत्वा तथाकाषीत् पिता नृप। तथा त्वमपि वर्तस्व सत्यधर्मपरायणः॥
en: Bhishma said, Hearing these words of his son, the father acted in the way that was pointed out, O king! Do you also act similarly, devoted to the religion of Truth.

description: The duty of a man as knowing that the life of a man runs speedily. The discourse between a father and a son
sn: भीष्म उवाच पुत्रस्यैतद् वचः श्रुत्वा तथाकाषीत् पिता नृप। तथा त्वमपि वर्तस्व सत्यधर्मपरायणः॥
en: Bhishma said, Hearing these words of his son, the father acted in the way that was pointed out, O king! Do you also act similarly, devoted to the religion of Truth.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किंशीलः किंसमाचारः किंविद्यः किंपरायणः। प्राप्नोति ब्रह्मणं स्थानं यत् परं प्रकृतेर्बुवम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said "What should be a man's conduct, what his acts, what his knowledge, and to what must he be devoted, for attaining to Brahma's place which is above Nature and which is unchangeable?”

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: भीष्म उवाच मोक्षधर्मेषु निरतो लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः। प्राप्नोति परमं स्थानं यत् परं प्रकृतेऽवम्॥
en: One who is devoted to the religion of Liberation, abstemious in diet, and the master of his senses, attains to that high place which is above Prakriti and is unchangeable.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: (अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। हारीतेन पुरा गीतं तं निबोध युधिष्ठिर।।) स्वगृहादभिनिस्सृत्य लाभेऽलाभे समो मुनिः। समुपोढेषु कामेषु निरपेक्षः परिव्रजेत्॥
en: Retiring from his home, considering equally gain and loss, governing the senses and disregarding all objects of desire even when they are ready (for enjoyment), one should follow the life of Renunciation.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: । न चक्षुषा न मनसा न वाचा दूषयेदपि। न प्रत्यक्षं परोक्षं वां दूषणं व्याहरेत् क्वचित्॥
en: Neither with eye, nor with word, nor in thought, should one disparage another. Nor should one speak ill of any person either in or out of his hearing.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: न हिंस्यात् सर्वभूतानि मैत्रायणगतश्चरेत्। नेदं जीवितमासाद्य वैरं कुर्वीत केनचित्॥
en: One should refrain from injuring any creature, and fact observing the course of the Sun. Having come into this life, one should not treat with unfriendliness any creature.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: अतिवादांस्तितिक्षेत नाभिमन्येत कंचन। क्रोध्यमानः प्रियं ब्रूयादाक्रुष्टः कुशलं वदेत्॥
en: One should disregard disgraceful speeches, and never in pride consider himself as superior to another. When sought to be angered by another, one should still give vent to agreeable speeches. Even when spoken ill of one should not calumniate in return.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: प्रदक्षिणं च सव्यं च ग्राममध्ये च नाचरेत्। भैक्षचर्यामनापन्नो न गच्छेत् पूर्वकेतितः॥
en: One should not act in a friendly or an unfriendly manner in the midst of human beings. One should not go about many houses in this round of mendicancy. Nor should one go to any house having obtained a previous invitation.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: अवकीर्णः सुगुप्तश्च न वाचा ह्यप्रियं वदेत्। मृदुः स्यादप्रतिक्रूरो विस्रब्धः स्यादकत्थनः॥
en: Even when filled with filth, one should, firmly following his duties, refrain from addressing unpleasant words to such men. One should be merciful. One should not return an injury. One should be fearless; one should not speak highly of himself.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: विधूमे न्यस्तमुसले व्यङ्गारे भुक्तवज्जने। अतीतपात्रसंचारे भिक्षां लिप्सेत वै मुनिः॥
en: The man of controlled senses should beg alms in a householder's house when the smoke has ceased to rise from it, when the sound of the husking rod is heard no more, when the hearth-fire is gone, when all the inmates have taken their food, or when the hour for setting the dishes is over.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: प्राणयात्रिकमात्रः स्यान्मात्रालाभेष्वनादृतः। अलाभे न विहन्येत लाभश्चैनं न हर्षयेत्॥ लाभं साधारणं नेच्छेन्न भुञ्जीताभिपूजितः। अभिपूजितलाभं हि जुगुप्सेतैव तादृशः॥
en: He should be satisfied with only as much as is hardly necessary for keeping the body and soul together. Even that much of food which yields gratification should not be sought by him. When he fails to get what he wants, he should not cherish discontent. Success, again, in obtaining what he wants, should not elate him. He should never wish for such things as are sought by ordinary men. He should never take his meals at any body's house when respectfully invited thereto. One like him should hate any thing that is presented with honour.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: न चान्नदोषान् निन्देत न गुणानभिपूजयेत्। शय्यासने विविक्ते च नित्यमेवाभिपूजयेत्॥
en: He should never find fault with the food put before him, nor should he speak highly of its merits. He should seek a bed and a seat that are removed from human habitations.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: शून्यागारं वृक्षमूलमरण्यमथवा गुहाम्। अज्ञातचर्यां गत्वान्यां ततोऽन्यत्रैव संविशेत्॥
en: The places he should seek should be such as an abandoned house, the foot of a tree, a forest, or a cave. Without making his practices to be known by others, or concealing their real nature by appearing to adopt others, he should enter his own Self.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: अनुरोधविरोधाभ्यां समः स्यादचलो ध्रुवः। सुकृतं दुष्कृतं चोभे नानुरुध्येत कर्मणा॥
en: By association with Yoga and dissociation from company, he should be perfectly calm, steadily fixed, and uniform. He should not acquire either merit or demerit by means of acts.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: नित्यतृप्तः सुसंतुष्टः प्रसन्नवदनेन्द्रियः। विभीर्जप्यपरो मौनी वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः॥
en: He should be always be always pleased, well contented, of cheerful countenance and senses, fearless, always engaged in mental recitation of sacred Mantras, silent, and a follower of a life of Renunciation.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
