sn: अभ्यस्तं भौतिकं पश्यन् भूतानामागतिं गतिम्। नि:स्पृहः समदर्शी च पक्वापक्वेन वर्तयन्। आत्मना य: प्रशान्तात्मा लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Seeing the repeated formation and dissolution of his own body with the senses that originate from and resolve into the primary elements, and seeing also the coming and departure of (other) creatures, he should become shorn of desire and learn to see all things impartially, living upon both cooked and uncooked food. Abstemious in diet, and controlling his senses, he gains tranquillity of Self by Self.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: वाचो वेगं मनसः क्रोधवेगं हिंसावेगमुदरोपस्थवेगम्। एतान् वेगान् विषहेद् वै तपस्वी निन्दा चास्य हृदयं नोपहन्यात्॥
en: One should govern the impulses of words, of the mind, of anger of envy, of hunger, and of lust. Given to penances for purifying his heart, he should never allow the censures (of others) to pain his heart.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: मध्यस्थ एव तिष्ठेत प्रशंसानिन्दयोः समः। एतत् पवित्रं परमं परिव्राजक आश्रमे॥
en: Becoming neutral, should live, regarding praise and censure as equal. This, indeed, is the holiest and the highest path of Renunciation.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: महात्मा सर्वतो दान्तः सर्वत्रैवानपाश्रितः। अपूर्वचारकः सौम्यो अनिकेतः समाहितः॥
en: Endued with great soul, the Sannyasin should control his senses from all things and stand aloof from all attachments. He should never go to the places visited by him and the men known to him while he lived otherwise, Agreeable to all creatures, and without a fixed dwelling, he should be given to the contemplation of Self. one

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: वानप्रस्थगृहस्थाभ्यां न संसृज्येत कर्हिचित्। अज्ञातलिप्सं लिप्सेत न चैनं हर्ष आविशेत्॥
en: He should never mingle with house-holders and hermits. He should eat such food as he may get without effort. He should never allow joy to possess his heart.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: विजानतां मोक्ष एष श्रमः स्यादविजानताम्। मोक्षयानमिदं कृत्स्नं विदुषां हारितोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Such a life of Renunciation brings on Liberation to those that are wise. The practice of these duties is a great burden to those, however, that are fools, The sage Harita declared all this to be the path by which Liberation can be acquired.

description: How should a man attain to Brahma
sn: अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो दत्त्वा यः प्रव्रजेद् गृहात्। लोकास्तेजोमयास्तस्य तथाऽऽनन्त्याय कल्पते॥
en: He who leaves his home, having assured all creatures of his perfect harmlessness, acquires many bright and eternal regions of felicity.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धन्या धन्या इति जनाः सर्वेऽस्मान् प्रवदन्त्युत। न दुःखिततरः कश्चित् पुमानस्माभिरस्ति ह॥
en: All men describe ourselves as highly fortunate. In sooth, however, there is no person more wretched than ourselves.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: लोकसम्भावितैर्दुःखं यत् प्राप्तं कुरुसत्तम। प्राप्य जाति मनुष्येषु देवैरपि पितामह॥ कदा वयं करिष्यामः संन्यासं दुःखसंज्ञकम्। दुःखमेतच्छरीराणां धारणं कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Though respected of all the world, O best of the Kurus, and though we have been born among men, O grandfather, having been begotten by the very gods, yet when so much sorrow has come to us, it appears, O reverened chief, that birth in an embodied form is the root of all sorrow! Alas, when shall we adopt a life of Renunciation which dissipates sorrow?

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: विमुक्ताः सप्तदशभिर्हेतुभूतैश्च पञ्चभिः। इन्द्रियार्थैर्गुणैश्चैव अष्टाभिश्च पितामह॥ न गच्छन्ति पुनर्भावं मुनयः संशितव्रताः। कदा वयं गमिष्यामो राज्यं हित्वा परंतप॥
en: Sages of rigid vows freed from the seventeen (i.e., the five vital airs, mind, understanding, and the ten organs of knowledge and action), from the five shortcomings of Yoga (viz., desire, anger, covetousness, fear, and sleep), which form the chief causes (for subjugating man to repeated re-birth), and from the other eight, (viz., the five objects of the senses and the three qualities), have never to incur rebirth. When, O scorcher of enemies, shall we succeed in renouncing sovereignty for adopting a life of Renunciation.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: भीष्म उवाच नास्त्यनन्तं महाराज सर्वं संख्यानगोचरः। पुनर्भावोऽपि विख्यातो नास्ति किंचिदिहाचलम्॥
en: Bhishma said Everything, O great king, has an end. Everything has limits assigned to it! Even rebirth, it is well known, has an end. In this world there is nothing unchangeable.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: न चापि मन्यसे राजन्नेष दोषः प्रसङ्गतः। उद्योगादेव धर्मज्ञा कालेनैव गमिष्यथ।॥
en: You think, O king, that this portion is a fault. that it is not true, regarding our present subject of discussion. You, however, know virtue, and have readiness. It is certain, therefore, that you will go to the end of your sorrow in time.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: नरेशेऽयं सततं देही नृपते पुण्यपापयोः। तत एव समुत्थेन तमसा रुध्यतेऽपि च॥
en: Individual with body, O king, is not the author of his merits and demerits. On the other hand, he becomes covered with the Darkness that is begotten by his merits and demerits.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: यथाञ्जमनयो वायुः पुनर्मानःशिलं रजः। अनुप्रविश्य तद्वर्णो दृश्यते रञ्जयन् दिशः॥ तथा कर्मफलैर्देही रञ्जितस्तमसाऽऽवृतः। विवर्णो वर्णमाश्रित्य देहेषु परिवर्तते॥
en: As the wind (having no colour of its own) assumes the colour of the substances which it has seized and tinges the different points of the horizon, similarly Individual Soul, though himself colourless, assumes a colour on account of its being enveloped by Darkness and variegated by the fruits of action, and passes from body to body.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: ज्ञानेन हि यदा जन्तुरज्ञानप्रभवं तमः। व्यपोहति तदा ब्रह्म प्रकाशति सनातनम्॥
en: When Individual Soul succeeds in removing by means of Knowledge the Darkness which covers him in consequence of Ignorance, then immutable Brahma becomes manifest.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: अयत्नसाध्यं मुनयो वदन्ति ये चापि मुक्तास्त उपासितव्याः। त्वया च लोकेन च सामरेण तस्मान्नमस्यामि महर्षिसङ्घान्॥
en: The Sages say that return to Immutable Brahma cannot be attained by Acts. Yourself, others in the world, and the gods too, should respect them who have acquired Liberation. All the great Rishis never desist from culture of Brahma.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: अस्मिन्नर्थे पुरा गीतं शृणुष्वैकमना नृप। यथा दैत्येन वृत्रेण भ्रष्टैश्वर्येण चेष्टितम्॥
en: Regarding it is cited that discourse which was recited (by Shukra) in days of old. Listen, O king, with rapt attention to the course of conduct that was followed by the Daitya Vritra after he was shorn of all his prosperity.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: निर्जितेनासहायेन हृतराज्येन भारत। अशोचता शत्रुमध्ये बुद्धिमास्थाय केवलाम्॥
en: Depending only upon his intelligence, he did not grieve in the midst of his enemies, although he had been defeated, although he was friendless, and although he was deprived of sovereignty, O Bharata!

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: भ्रष्टैश्वर्यं पुरा वृत्रमुशना वाक्यमब्रवीत्। काचित् पराजितस्याद्य न व्यथा तेऽस्ति दानव।१५।।
en: When in days of old Vritra was reft of sovereignty, (his preceptor) Ushanas said to him, I hope, O Danava, that on account of your defeat your cherish no grief.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: वृत्र उवाच सत्येन तपसा चैव विदित्वासंशयं ह्यहम्। न शोचामि न हृष्यामि भूतानामागतिं गतिम्॥
en: Vritra said Forsooth, having understood, by the help of truth and penances, the coming and going of all living creatures, I have ceased to grieve or joy.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: कालसंचोदिता जीवा मज्जन्ति नरकेऽवशाः। परितुष्टानि सर्वाणि दिव्यान्याहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: Urged by Times creatures sink helplessly in hell. Some again, the sages hold, go to heaven. All these pass their time happily.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: क्षपयित्वा तु तं कालं गणितं कालचोदिताः। सावशेषेण कालेन सम्भवन्ति पुनः पुनः॥
en: Passing their fixed time in heaven and hell, and with some portion of their merits and demerits unexhausted, they again and again take birth, moved by Time.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: तिर्यग्योनिसहस्राणि गत्वा नरकमेव च। निर्गच्छन्त्यवशा जीवाः कामबन्धनबन्धनाः॥
en: Fettered by the bonds of Desire, creatures pass through numberless intermediate lives and fall helplessly into hell.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: एवं संसरमाणानि जीवान्यहमदृष्टवान्। यथा कर्म तथ लाभ इति शास्त्रनिदर्शनम्॥
en: I have seen that creatures come and go even thus. The lesson taught in the Scriptures is that one's acquisitions tally with his acts.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: तिर्यग् गच्छन्ति नरकं मानुष्यं दैवमेव च। सुखदुःखे प्रिये द्वेष्ये चरित्वा पूर्वमेव ह॥ कृतान्तविधिसंयुक्तः सर्वो लोकः प्रपद्यते। गतं गच्छन्ति चाध्वानं सर्वभूतानि सर्वदा॥ कालसंख्यानसंख्यातं सृष्टिस्थितिपरायणम्। तं भाषमाणं भगवानुशना प्रत्यभाषत। धीमान् दुष्टप्रलापांस्त्वं तात कस्मात् प्रभाषसे॥
en: Creatures are born as men or as intermediate animals or as gods and go to hell. Having acted in pristine lives in such a way as to deserve them, all creatures subject to the ordinances of the Destroyer, experience happiness and misery, the agreeable and the disagreeable. Having enjoyed the measure of happiness or misery commensurate with their acts, creatures always return by the old path, which is measured by the measure of acts. Then the illustrious Ushanas said to the Asura Vritra who was thus talking of the highest refuge of the creation, saying,-0 intelligent Daitya, why, O child, do you utter such foolish rhapsodies?

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: वृत्र उवाच प्रत्यक्षमेतद् भवतस्तथान्येषां मनीषिणाम्। मया यज्जयलुब्धेन पुरा तप्तं महत् तपः॥
en: Vritra said You and also other sages know full well the severe penances which I practised from greed of victory.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: गन्धानादाय भूतानां रसांश्च विविधानपि। अवर्धं त्रीन् समाक्रम्य लोकान् वै स्वेन तेजसा॥
en: Appropriating various scents and various sorts of tastes that other creatures had for enjoying, I swelled up with my own energy, assailing the three worlds.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: ज्वालामालापरिक्षिप्तो वैहायसचरस्तथा। अजेयः सर्वभूतानामासं नित्यमपेतभीः॥
en: Decked with numberless effulgent rays I used to pass through the skies incapable of being defeated by any creature and fearing none.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: ऐश्वर्यं तपसा प्राप्तं भ्रष्टं तच्च स्वकर्मभिः। धृतिमास्थाय भगवन् न शोचामि ततस्त्वहम्॥
en: I acquired great prosperity through my penenaces and lost it again through my own deeds. Depending on my fortitude, however, I do not grieve for this change.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: युयुत्सुना महेन्द्रेण पुंसा सार्धं महात्मना। ततो मे भगवान् दृष्टो हरिर्नारायणः प्रभुः॥ वैकुण्ठः पुरुषोऽनन्तः शुक्लो विष्णुः सनातनः। मुञ्जकेशो हरिश्मश्रुः सर्वभूतपितामहः॥
en: Desirous of fighting the great Indra, the great ruler of the celestial region, I beheld in that battle the illustrious Hari, the powerful Narayana, He who is called Vaikuntha, Purusha, Ananta, Shukla, Vishnu, Sanatana, Munjakesha, Harishmashru, and the Grandsire of all creatures.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: नूनं तु तस्य तपसः सावशेषमिहास्ति वै। यदहं प्रष्टुमिच्छामि भगवन् कर्मणः फलम्॥
en: Forsooth, there is still a residue of the rewards of that penance represented by a sight of the great Hari! On account of this unspent residue that I have become desirous of asking you, O illustrious one, about the fruits of action.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: ऐश्वर्यं वै महद् ब्रह्म वर्णे कस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितम्। निवर्तते चापि पुनः कथमैश्वर्यमुत्तमम्॥
en: Upon which order (of men) has been placed high Brahma prosperity? In what manner, again, does high prosperity fall off?

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: कस्माद् भूतानि जीवन्ति प्रवर्तन्ते तथा पुनः। किंवा फलं परं प्राप्य जीवस्तिष्ठति शाश्वतः॥
en: From whom do creatures originate and live? Through whom again do they act? What is that great Fruit by acquiring which a creature succeeds in living for good as Brahma?

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: केन वा कर्मणा शक्यमथ ज्ञानेन केन वा। तदवाप्तुं फलं विप्र तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: By what Act or by what Knowledge can that fruit be acquired? You should, O learned Brahmana, expound these to me!

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: इतीदमुक्तः स मुनिस्तदानीं प्रत्याह यत्तच्छृणु राजसिंह। मनन्यचित्तः सह सोदरीयैः॥
en: Described by me, O foremost of kings, listen, with rapt attention, O best of men, with all your brothers, to what the sage Ushanas then said after he had been thus addressed by that king of Danavas.

description: Yudhishthira asks when he should renounce sovereignty and adopt a life of Renunciation
sn: इतीदमुक्तः स मुनिस्तदानीं प्रत्याह यत्तच्छृणु राजसिंह। मनन्यचित्तः सह सोदरीयैः॥
en: Described by me, O foremost of kings, listen, with rapt attention, O best of men, with all your brothers, to what the sage Ushanas then said after he had been thus addressed by that king of Danavas.

sn: उशनोवाच नमस्तस्मै भगवते देवाय प्रभविष्णवे। यस्य पृथ्वीतलं तात साकाशं बाहुग्रोचरः॥
en: Ushana said I bow to that divine and illustrious and powerful Being who holds this Earth with the sky in his arms.

sn: मूर्धा यस्य त्वनन्तं च स्थानं दानवसत्तम। तस्याहं ते प्रवक्ष्यामि विष्णोर्माहात्म्यमुत्तमम्॥
en: I shall speak to you of the pre-eminent greatness of that Vishnu whose head, O best of the Danavas, is that Infinite place.

sn: तयोः संवदतोरेवमाजगाम महामुनिः। सनत्कुमारो धर्मात्मा संशयच्छेदनाय वै॥
en: While they were thus talking with each other there came to them the great sage Sanatkumara of pious soul for the purpose of removing their doubts.

sn: स पूजितोऽसुरेन्द्रेण मुनिनोशनसा तथा। निषसादासने राजन् महार्हे मुनिपुङ्गवः॥
en: Adored of the king of Asuras and the sage Ushanas, that foremost of sages sat down on a rich seat.

sn: तमासीनं महाप्रज्ञमुशना वाक्यमब्रवीत्। ब्रूह्यस्मै दानवेन्द्राय विष्णोर्माहात्म्यमुत्तमम्॥ एष चाक्षिपते काले
en: After the highly wise Kumara had been seated, Ushanas said to him,-Describe to this king of the Danavas the pre-eminent greatness of Vishnu.

sn: सनत्कुमारस्तु ततः श्रुत्वा प्राह वचोऽर्थवत्। विष्णोर्माहात्म्यसंयुक्तं दानवेन्द्राय धीमते॥
en: Hearing these words, Sanatkumara said to the following, fraught with grave sense, upon the pre-cminent greatness of Vishnu to the intelligent king of the Danavas.

sn: शृणु सर्वमिदं दैत्य विष्णोर्माहात्म्यमुत्तमम्। विष्णौ जगत् स्थितं सर्वमिति विद्धि परंतप॥
en: Listen, O Daitya, to everything regarding the greatness of Vishnu. Know, O destroyer of foes, that the entire universe depends on Vishnu.

sn: सृजत्येष महाबाहो भूतग्रामं चराचरम्। काले विसृजते पुनः॥
en: O you of mighty arms, it is He who creates all creatures mobile and immobile. In course of Time it is He, again, who withdraws all things and in Time it is He who once more sends them from Himself.

sn: अस्मिन् गच्छन्ति विलयमस्माच्च प्रभवन्त्युत। नैष ज्ञानवता शक्यस्तपसा नैव चेज्यया। सम्प्राप्तुमिन्द्रियाणां तु संयमेनैव शक्यते॥
en: Into Hari all things merge at the universal dissolution, and from Hiin all things again come forth. Men having scriptural learning cannot get him by such lore. Nor can He be acquired by Penances, nor by Sacrifices. The only means by which He can be acquired is by controlling the Senses.

sn: बाह्ये चाभ्यन्तरे चैव कर्मणोर्मनसि स्थितः। निर्मलीकुरुते बुद्ध्या सोऽमुत्रानन्त्यमश्नुते॥
en: Not that sacrifices are absolutely useless towards such an end. For a person, by relying upon both external and internal acts, and upon his own mind, can purify (them) by his own understanding. By such means, one can enjoy Infinity in the world.

sn: यथा हिरण्यकर्ता वै रूप्यमग्नौ विशोधयेत्। बहुशोऽतिप्रयत्नेन महताऽऽत्मकृतेन ह॥ तद्वज्जातिशतैर्जीवः शुद्ध्यतेऽनेन कर्मणा। यत्नेन महता चैवाप्येकजातौ विशुद्ध्यते॥
en: As a goldsmith purifies the dross of his metal by repeatedly putting it into the fire with very great efforts of his own, similarly Individual Soul succeeds in purifying himself by his course through hundreds of births. Some one may be seen to purify himself in only one life by great efforts.

sn: लीलयाल्पं यथा गात्रात् प्रमृज्यादात्मनो रजः। बहुयत्नेन महता दोषनिर्हरणं तथा॥
en: As one should with care remove stains from his body before they become thick, similarly one should with great efforts, wash off his sins.

sn: यथा चाल्पेन माल्येन वासितं तिलसर्षपम्। न मुञ्चति स्वकं गन्धं तद्वत् सूक्ष्मस्य दर्शनम्॥
en: By mixing only a few flowers with them, grains of sesame cannot be made to renounce their own smell. Similarly, one cannot, by purifying his heart only a little, succeed in seeing the Soul.

sn: तदेव बहुभिर्माल्यैर्वास्यमानं पुनः पुनः। विमुञ्चति स्वकं गन्धं माल्यगन्धे च तिष्ठति॥
en: When, however, those grains are perfumed repeatedly with the help of a large quantity of flowers, it is then that they cast off their own smell and assume that off the flowers with which they are mixed.

sn: एवं जातिशतैर्युक्तो गुणैरेव प्रसङ्गियु। बुद्ध्या निवर्तते दोषो यत्नेनाभ्यासजेन ह॥
en: Similarly, faults, in the form of attachments to all our environments, are removed by the understanding in course of many lives, with the help of a large quantity of the quality of goodness, and by means of efforts born of practice.

sn: कर्मणा स्वनुरक्तानि विरक्तानि च दानव। यथा कर्मविशेषांश्च प्राप्नुवन्ति तथा शृणु।॥
en: Listen, O Danava, by what means creatures attached to acts and those unattached to them get at the causes bringing on their respective states mind.

sn: यथावत् सम्प्रवर्तन्ते यस्मिस्तिष्ठन्ति वा विभो। तत् तेऽनुपूर्व्या व्याख्यास्ये तदिहैकमनाः शृणु॥
en: Listen to me with rapt attention. I shall in their due order, describe to you, O powerful Danava, as to how creatures follow action and how they give up action.

sn: अनादिनिधनः श्रीमान् हरिर्नारायणः प्रभुः। देवः सृजति भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च॥
en: The Supreme Lord creates all creatures mobile and immobile. He is beginingless and endless. Unendued with attributes and endless. Unendued with attributes of any sort, he assumes attributes. He is the universal Destroyer, the Refuge of all things, the supreme Ordainer, and pure Intelligence.

sn: स वै सर्वेषु भूतेषु क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च। एकादशविकारात्मा जगत् पिबति रश्मिभिः॥
en: In all creatures it is He who lives as the mutable and the immutable. It is He who, having eleven modifications for His essence, drinks this universe with His rays.

sn: पादौ तस्य महीं विद्धि मूर्धानं दिवमित्युत। बाहवस्तु दिशो दैत्य श्रोत्रमाकाशमेव च॥
en: Know that the Earth is His feet. His head is formed by Heaven. His arms, O Daitya, are the several points of the horizon. The intermediate space is His ears.

sn: तस्य तेजोमयः सूर्यो मनश्चन्द्रमसि स्थितम्। बुद्धिर्ज्ञानगता नित्यं रसस्त्वप्सु प्रतिष्ठितः॥
en: The light of His eye is the Sun, and His mind is in the Moon. His Understanding lives always in Knowledge, and His tongue is in Water.

sn: भ्रुवोरन्तरास्तस्य ग्रहा दानवसत्तम। नक्षत्रचक्रं नेत्राभ्यां पादयोर्भूश्च दानव॥
en: O best of Danavas, the Planets are in the midst of His brows. The stars and constellations originate, from the light of His eyes. The Earth is in His feet, O Danava.

sn: रजस्तमश्च सत्त्वं च विद्धि नारायणात्मकम्। सोऽऽश्रमाणां फलं तात कर्मणस्तत् फलं विदुः॥
en: Know also that the qualities of Rajas, Tamas, and Sattva are of Him. He is the fruit of all the modes of life, and He it is who should be known as the fruit of all religious acts.

sn: अकर्मणः फलं चैव स एव परमव्ययः। छन्दांसि यस्य रोमाणि ह्यक्षरं च सरस्वती॥
en: The Highest and Immutable, He is also the fruit of abstention from all work. The Chcchandas are the hair on His body, and Pranava is His word.

sn: बह्वाश्रयो बहुमुखो धर्मो हृदि समाश्रितः। स ब्रह्म परमो धर्मस्तपश्च सदसच्च सः॥
en: The various orders (of men) and the modes of life are His refuge. His mouths are many. duty is put in his heart. He is Brahma, He is the highest Righteousness; He is existent and He is non-existent.

sn: श्रुतिशास्त्रग्रहोपेतः षोडशविक् क्रतुश्च सः। पितामहश्च विष्णुश्च सोऽश्विनौ स पुरंदरः।
en: He is Shruti. He is the scriptures. He is Sacrificial vessels. He is the sixteen sacrificial priests. He is all the Sacrifices. He is the Grandfather (Brahman), He is Vishnu. He is the two Ashvins, and he is Purandara.

sn: मित्रोऽथ वरुणश्चैव यमोऽथ धनदस्तथा॥ ते पृथग्दर्शनस्तस्य संविदन्ति तथैकताम्। एकस्य विद्धि देवस्य सर्वं जगदिदं वशे॥
en: He is Mitra, He is Varuna, He is Yama, He is Kuvera—the lord of riches. Although the Ritwijas seem to see Him as separate, He is, however, known to them as one and the same. Know that this entire universe is under the control of One divine Being.

sn: नानाभूतस्य दैत्येन्द्र तस्यैकत्वं वदत्ययम्। जन्तुः पश्यति विज्ञानात् ततो ब्रह्म प्रकाशते॥
en: The Veda that is in the soul, O king of Daityas, regards the unity of various creates. When a living creature realizes this unity on account of true knowledge, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

sn: स्तिष्ठन्ति जीवाः प्रचरन्ति चान्ये। प्रजाविसर्गस्य पारिमाण्यं वापीसहस्राणि बहूनि दैत्य॥
en: The period of time during which one creation exists or owing which it ceases to exist is called a Kalpa. Living creatures exist for a thousand millions of such Kalpas, Immobile creatures also exists for an equal time. The period for which a particular creation exists is measured by many thousands of lakes, O Daitya!

sn: वाप्यः पुनर्योजनविस्तृतास्ताः क्रोशं च गम्भीरतयावगाढाः। आयामतः पञ्चशताश्च सर्वाः प्रत्येकशो योजनतः प्रवृद्धाः॥
en: Conceive a lake that is one Yojana in width, one Krosha is depth, and five hundred Yojanas in length. Imagine many thousands of such lakes.

sn: वाप्या जलं क्षिप्यति वालकोट्या त्वन्हा सकृच्चाप्यथ न द्वितीयम्। तासां क्षये विद्धि परं विसर्ग संहारमेकं च तथा प्रजानाम्॥
en: Try then to dry up those lakes by taking from them, only once a day, as much water as may be taken up with the end of a single hair. The number of days that would be necessary to drying them up perfectly by this process forins the period that is required by the life of one creation from its beginning to the time of its destruction.

sn: षड् जीववर्णाः परमं प्रमाणं कृष्णो धूम्रो नीलमथास्य मध्यम्। राक्तं पुन: सह्यतरं सुखं तु हारिद्रवर्णं सुसुखं च शुक्लम्॥
en: The highest Evidence says that creatures have six colours, viz., Dark, Tawny, Blue, Red, Yellow, and White. These colours produced by mixtures in various degrees of are three qualities of Rajas, Tamas, and Sattva. Where Tamas prevents Sattva falls below the mark, and Rajas remains the same, the result is the colour called Dark. When Tamas prevails as before, but the relations between Sattva sand Rajas, are changed the result is the color called Tawny. When Rajas prevents, Sattva goes down, and Tamas remains the same, the result is the colour called Blue. When Rajas prevents as before and the proportion change between Sativa and Tamas, the result is the intermediate colour called Red. That colour is more agreeable. When Sattva prevents Rajas falls down and Tamas keeps on the same, the result is the colour called Yellow. It yields happiness. When Sativa prevails and the proportion is changed between Rajas and Tamas, the result is the colour called White. It yields great happiness.

sn: परं तु शुक्लं विमलं विशोकं गतक्लमं सिद्ध्यति दानवेन्द्र। गत्वा तु योनिप्रभवाणि दैत्य सहस्रशः सिद्धिमुपैति जीवः॥
en: The White is the foremost colour, It is sinless on account of its being free from attachment and aversion. It is without grief, and free from the exertion necessary by desire for action. Hence, White, O king of Danavas, brings on Liberation. O Daitya, having undergone thousands of births derived through the womb, Individual Soul attains to success.

sn: गतिं च यां दर्शनमाह देवो गत्वा शुभं दर्शनमेव चापि। गतिः पुनर्वर्णकृता प्रजानां वर्णस्तथा कालकृतोऽसुरेन्द्र।।
en: That success is the same end which the divine Indra declared after having studied many sacred scriptural books and which has for its essence the apprehension of the Soul. The end again that creatures obtain depends on their colour, and colour, in its turn, depends upon the character of the Time that sets in, O Daitya.

sn: शतं सहस्राणि चतुर्दशेह परागतिर्जीवगणस्य दैत्य आरोहणं तत्कृतमेव विद्धि स्थानं तथा निःसरणं च तेषाम्॥
en: The stages of existence, O Daitya, through which individual soul must pass are not unlimited. They are fourteen hundreds of thousands in number. In consequence of them individual soul, ascends, stays, and falls down as the case may be.

sn: कृष्णस्य वर्णस्य गतिर्निकृष्टा स सज्जते नरके पच्यमानः। स्थानं तथा दुर्गतिभिस्तु तस्य प्रजाविसर्गान् सुबहून् वदन्ति॥
en: The end that is acquired by an individual soul of dark colour is very low, for he becomes addicted to acts leading to hell and then has to rot in hell. The learned say that on account of his wickedness, the continuance of an individual is measured by many thousands of Kalpas.

sn: शतं सहस्राणि ततश्चरित्वा प्राप्नोति वर्णं हरितं तु पश्चात्। स चैव तस्मिन् निवसत्यनीशो युगक्षये तपसा संवृतात्मा॥
en: Having passed many hundred thousands of years in that stage, Individual Soul then attains to the colour called Tawny. In that condition he lives in perfect helplessness. At last when his sins are spent his mind, shaking off all attachments, cherishes Renunciation.

sn: स्तमो व्यपोहन् घटते स्वबुद्ध्या। स लोहितं वर्णमुपैति नीलान् मनुष्यलोके परिवर्तते च॥
en: When Individual Soul becomes endued with the quality of goodness, he then dispels everything connected with Darkness by the help of his intelligence, and exerts (for acquiring what is for his good). As the outcome of this, Individual Soul attains to the colour called Red. If the quality of goodness, however, be not acquired, Individual Soul then travels in a round of re-births in the world of men having attained to the colour called Blue.

sn: स तत्र संहारविसर्गमेकं स्वधर्मजैर्बन्धनैः क्लिश्यमानः। ततः स हारिद्रमुपैति वर्ण संहारविक्षेपशते व्यतीते॥
en: Having attained to that end, and having been afflicted for the duration of one creation by the fetters of his own acts Individual Soul then attains to the colour called Yellow (or becomes a Deity). Existing in that condition for the period of a hundred creations, he then leaves it to return to it once more.

sn: हारिद्रवर्णस्तु प्रजाविसर्गात् सहस्रशस्तिष्ठति संचरन् वै। अविप्रमुक्तो निरये च दैत्य ततः सहस्राणि दशापराणि॥ गतीः सहस्राणि च पञ्च तस्य चत्वारि संवर्तकृतानि चैवा विमुक्तमेनं निरयाच्च विद्धि सर्वेषु चान्येषु च सम्भवेषु॥
en: Having acquired the Yellow colour, Individual Soul exists for thousands of Kalpas, sporting as a Deity. Without, however, being emancipated, he has to live in hell, enjoying or enduring the fruits of his acts of past Kalpas and passing through nine and then thousand courses. Know that Individual Soul then becomes freed from the hell as represented heaven. Similarly Individual Soul escapes other births.

sn: स देवलोके विहरत्यभीक्ष्णं ततश्च्युतो मानुषतामुपैति। संहारविक्षेपशतानि चाष्टौ मर्येषु तिष्ठत्यमृतत्वमेति।।४३। सोऽस्मादथ भ्रश्यति कालयोगात् कृष्णे तले तिष्ठति सर्वकृष्ट। स्तत्तेऽभिधास्याम्यसुरप्रवीर॥
en: Individual Soul sports for many long Kalpas in the world of Devas. Falling thence, he once more becomes a man. He then lives in that condition for the period of a hundred and cight Kalpas. He then attains once more to the a status of a Deity. If while born as a man he falls through Kala, he then sinks into the Dark colour and thus occupies the very lowest of all stages of existence. I shall tell you, now, O foremost of Asuras, how Individual Soul succeeds in bringing about his Liberation.

sn: दैवानि स व्यूहशतानि सप्त रक्तो हरिद्रोऽथ तथैव शुक्लः। मष्टावरानच॑तमान्स लोकान्॥
en: Desirous of Liberation, Individual Soul relying upon seven hundred kinds of acts every one of which is permeated-by predominance of the quality of goodness, gradually passes through Red and Yellow and at last attains to White. Arrived here, Individual Soul travels through several most adorable regions which have the Eight wellknown regions of felicity beneath them, and all the while follows that pure and effulgent form existence which is Liberation,

sn: अष्टौ च षष्टिं च शतानि चैव मनोनिरुद्धानि महाद्युतीनाम्। शुक्लस्य वर्णस्य परा गतिर्या त्रीण्येव रुद्धानि महानुभाव॥
en: Know that the Eight which are identical with the Sixty hundreds, are to those who are highly effulgent, only creations of the mind. The highest, object of acquisition with one who is of White colour, is that condition which is above the three other states of consciousness, viz., Wakefulness and Dream and Dreamless sleep.

sn: संहारविक्षेपमनिष्टमेकं चत्वारि चान्यानि वसत्यनीशः। षष्ठस्य वर्णस्य परा गतिर्या सिद्धावसिद्धस्य गतक्लमस्य॥
en: As regards that Yogin who cannot renounce the joy that Yoga-power begets, he has to live (in one and the same body) for one hundred Kalpas in auspiciousness and after that in four other regions. Even that is the highest end of one belonging to the sixth colour, and who is Unsuccessful though crowned with Success, and who has gone above all attachments and passions.

sn: सप्तोत्तरं तत्र वसत्यनीशः संहारविक्षेपशतं सशेषम्। तस्मादुपावृत्य मनुष्यलोके ततो महान् मानुषतामुपैति॥
en: That Yogin, again, who deviates from Yoga practices lives in the celestial region for a liundred Kalpas with the unspent residue of his pristine deeds and with the seven (viz., the five senses of knowledge and mind and understanding) purged of all stains on account of their predisposition towards the quality of goodness. After that period, such a person has 10 come to the world of men where he acquires great eminence.

sn: तस्मादुपावृत्य ततः क्रमेण सोऽग्रेण संतिष्ठति भूतसर्गम्। स सप्तकृत्वश्च परैति लोकान् संहारविक्षेपकृतप्रभावः॥
en: Returning from the world of men, he departs for attaining to new forms of life that run higher and higher in the upwards scale. While engaged in this, he passes through seven regions for seven times, his power being always multiplied on account of his mental concentration and the re-awakening from it.

sn: सप्तैव संहारमुपप्लवानि सम्भाव्य संतिष्ठति जीवलोके। ततोऽव्ययं स्थानमनन्तमेति देवस्य विष्णोरथ ब्रह्मणश्च। शेषस्य चैवाथ नरस्य चैव देवस्य विष्णोः परमस्य चैव॥
en: The Yogin who wishes for final Liberation suppresses by Yoga-knowledge the seven, and continues to live in the world of life, shorn of attachments, and taking those seven for certain means of grief, he renounces them and attains after wards to that state which is Indestructible and Infinite. Some, say that that is the region of Mahadeva; some of Vishnu; some, of Brahiman; some, of Cesha; some, of Nara; some, of the effulgent Intelligence; and some, of the All-pervading.

sn: संहारकाले परिदग्धकाया ब्रह्माणमायान्ति सदा प्रजा हि। चेष्टात्मनो देवगणाश्च सर्वे ये ब्रह्मलोकेअपराः स्म तेऽपि॥
en: When universal dissolution sets in, those persons who have succeeded in completely destroying by knowledge their gross and subtle and casual bodies, always enter into Brahma. All their Senses also which have action for their essence and which are not at one with Brahma, merge into the same.

sn: प्रजाविसर्गं तु सशेषकाले स्थानानि स्वान्येव सरन्ति जीवाः। निःशेषतस्तत्पदं यान्ति चान्ते सर्वे देवा ये सदृशा मनुष्याः॥
en: When the time of universal dissolution sets in, those Individual Souls who have acquired the position of Devas and who have an unspent residue of the fruits of acts to enjoy or endure, return to those stages of life in the subsequent Kalpa which had been theirs in the pristine one. This is owing to the likeness of every successive Kalpa to every previous one.

sn: ये तु च्युताः सिद्धलोकात् क्रमेण तेषां गतिं यान्ति तथाऽऽनुपूर्व्या। जीवाः परे तद्बलतुल्यरूपाः स्वं स्वं विधिं यान्ति विपर्ययेण॥
en: Those again whose acts, at the time of universal dissolution, have been exhausted by enjoyment or endurance of their fruits, descending from heaven, are born among men, in the subsequent Kalpa, for without Knowledge one cannot dissipate his acts in even a hundred Kalpas. All superior Being again, gifted with similar powers and similar forms, revert to their respective destinies at a new creation after a universal dissolution, ascending and descending precisely in the same way as during the creation that is dissolved.

sn: स यावदेवास्ति सशेषभुक् ते प्रजाश्च देव्यौ च तथैव शुक्ले। तावत् तदङ्गेषु विशुद्धभावः संमम्य पञ्चेन्द्रियरूपमेतत्॥
en: As regards, again, the person who knows Brahma, as long as he continues to enjoy and endure the unspent residue of his deeds of pristine Kalpas, it is said that all creatures and the two pure sciences live in his body. When his Intelligence becomes purified by Yoga, and when he prastises restraint, this perceptible universe appears to him as only his own fivefold senses.

sn: शुद्धां गतिं तां परमां परैति शुद्धेन नित्यं मनसा विचिन्वन्। ततोऽव्ययं स्थानमुपैति ब्रह्म दुष्प्रापमभ्येति स शाश्वतं वै॥
en: Enquiring with a purified mind, individual soul attains to a high and pure end. Thence he attains to a spot which knows no destruction, and thence attains to eternal Brahma which is so difficult of acquisition.

sn: इत्येतदाख्यातमहीनसत्त्व नारायणस्येह बलं मया ते॥
en: Thus, O you of great power, I have described to you the greatness of Narayana.

sn: वृत्र उवाच एवं गते मे न विषादोऽस्ति कश्चित् सम्यक् च पश्यामि वच स्तथैतत्। श्रुत्वा तु ते वाचमदीनसत्त्व विकल्मषोऽस्म्यद्य तथा विपाप्मा॥
en: Vritra said I see, these your words are perfectly consonant with the truth. When this is so, I have no grief. Having heard your words, O you of great mental powers, I have become freed from sorrow and sin of every sort.

sn: प्रवृत्तमेतद् भगवन् महर्षे महाद्युतेश्चक्रमनन्तवीर्यम्। विष्णोरनन्तस्य सनातनं तत् स्थानं सर्गा यत्र सर्वे प्रवृत्ताः। स वै महात्मा पुरुषोत्तमो वै तस्मिन् जगत् सर्वमिदं प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: O illustrious Rishi, O holy one, I see this wheel of Time, endued with great energy, of the most effulgent and Infinite Vishnu, has been set in motion. Eternal is that station from which all sorts of creation originate. That Vishnu is the Supreme Soul. He is the foremost of Beings. In Him this entire universe lives.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्त्वा स कौन्तेय वृत्रः प्राणान वासृजत्। योजयित्वा तथाऽऽत्मानं परं स्थानमवाप्तवान्॥
en: Bhishma continued Having said these words, O son of Kunti, Vritra renounced his life-breaths, uniting his soul (with the Supreme Soul), and attained to highest station.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अयं स भगवान् देवः पितामह जनार्दनः। सनत्कुमारो वृत्राय यत्तदाख्यातवान् पुरा॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, whether this Janardana (Krishna) is that illustrious and powerful Lord of whom Sanatkumara spoke to Vritra in days of yore.

sn: भीष्म उवाच मूलस्थायी महादेवो भगवान् स्वेन तेजसा। तत्स्थः सृजति तान् भावान् नानारूपान् महामनाः॥
en: Bhishma said The Highest Deity, gifted with six attributes is at the Root. Staying there, the Supreme Soul, with his own energy, creates all these various existent things.

sn: तुरीयांशेन तस्येमं विद्धि केशवमच्युतम्। तुरीयार्धेन लोकांस्त्रीन् भावयत्येव बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Know that this Keshava who knows no decay from His eighth part. Gifted with the greatest Intelligence, it is this Keshava who creates the three worlds with an eighth portion.

sn: अर्वाक् स्थितस्तु यः स्थायी कल्पान्ते परिवर्तते। स शेते भगवानप्सु योऽसावतिबलः प्रभुः। तान् विधाता प्रसन्नात्मा लोकांश्चरति शाश्वतान्॥
en: Coming immediately after Him who lies at the Bottom, this Keshava who is eternal, changes at the end of each Kalpa, He, however, who lies at the Root and who is gifted with great might and power lies in the waters when universal dissolution sets in Keshava is that Creator of pure Soul who passes through all the eternal words.

sn: सर्वाण्यशून्यानि करोत्यनन्तः सनातनः संचरते च लोकान्। स चानिरुद्धः सृजते महात्मा तत्स्थं जगत् सर्वमिदं विचित्रम्॥
en: Infinite and Eternal as He is, He fills all space and passes through the universe. Freed as He is from all limitations such as the possession of attributes would imply, he allows himself to be invested with ignorance and awakened to Consciousness, Keshava of Supremne Soul creates all things. In Him rests this wonderful universe fully.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच वृत्रेण परमार्थज्ञ दृष्टा मन्येऽऽत्मनो गतिः। शुभा तस्मात् स सुखितो न शोचति पितामह॥
en: Yudhisthira said-O who are conversant with the highest object of knowledge, I think that Vritra behold before hand the excellent end that awaited him. It is for this, O grandfather, that he was happy and did not sucumb to grief.

sn: शुक्ल: शुक्लाभिजातीय: साध्यो नावर्ततेऽनघ। तिर्यग्गतेश्च निर्मुक्तो निरयाच्च पितामह॥
en: He who is of White colour, who has taken birth in a pure or stainless family, and who has attained to the rank of a Saddhya, does not, O a sinless one, return. Such person, O grandfather, is freed from both hell and all intermediate stations,

sn: हारिद्रवर्णे रक्ते वा वर्तमानस्तु पार्थिव। तिर्यगेवानुपश्येत कर्मभिस्तामसैर्वृतः॥
en: He, however, O king, who has acquired either the Yellow or the Red colour, is seen sometimes to be overwhelmed by darkness and fall among the order of Intermediate creatures.

sn: वयं तु भृशमापन्ना रक्ता दुःखसुखेऽसुखे। कां गतिं प्रतिपत्स्यामो नीलां कृष्णाधमामथ॥
en: As regards ourselves, we are greatly afflicted and attached to objects which produce sorrow. Alas, what will be our end? Will it be the Blue or the Dark which is the lowest of all colours.

sn: भीष्म उवाच शुद्धाभिजनसम्पन्नाः पाण्डवाः संशितव्रताः। विहृत्य देवलोकेषु पुनर्मानुषमेष्यथ॥
en: Bhishma said You are Pandavas! you have been born in a stainless family. You are of rigid vows. Having sported happily in the celestial regions, you shall return to the world of men.

sn: प्रजाविसर्गं च सुखेन काले प्रत्येत्य देवेषु सुखानि भुक्त्वा। सुखेन संयास्यथ सिद्धसंख्यां मा वो भयं भूद् विमलाः स्थ सर्वे॥
en: Living happily as long as the creation lasts, all of you at the next new creation will be admitted among the gods, and enjoying all sorts of happiness you will at last be coloured among the Siddhyas! Let no fear be yours. Be you cheerful.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अहो धर्मिष्ठता तात वृत्रस्यामिततेजसः। यस्य विज्ञानमतुलं विष्णोर्भक्तिश्च तादृशी॥
en: How great was the love of virtue possessed by Vritra of incomparable energy, whose knowledge was incomparable and whose devotion to Vishnu was so great.

sn: दुर्विज्ञेयं पदं तात विष्णोरमिततेजसः। कथं वा राजशार्दूल पदं तु ज्ञातवानसौ।२।।
en: The position occupied by Vishnu of immeasurable energy is difficult, of being perceived. How, O foremost of kings, could Vritra comprehend it?

sn: भवता कथितं ह्येतच्छ्रद्दधे चाहमच्युत। भूयस्तु मे समुत्पन्ना बुद्धिरव्यक्तदर्शनात्॥
en: You have described Vritra's acts. I too have heard you in full faith. Because, on account of my seeing that one point is unintelligible that my curiosity has been roused for asking you again.

sn: कथं विनिहतो वृत्रः शक्रेण पुरुषर्षभ। धार्मिको विष्णुभक्तश्च तत्त्वज्ञश्च पदान्वये॥
en: How, indeed, was Vritra, who was virtuous, devoted to Vishnu, gifted with knowledge of truth derivable from a just comprehension of the Upanishads and Vedanta, defeated by Indra, O foremost of men.

sn: एतन्मे संशयं ब्रूहि पृच्छते भरतर्षभ। वृत्रस्तु राजशार्दूल यथा शक्रेण निर्जितः॥
en: O king of the Bharatas, remove this my doubt! Indeed, tell me, O foremost of kings, how Vritra was defeated by Shakra.

sn: यथा चैवाभवद् युद्धं तच्चाचक्ष्व पितामह। विस्तरेण महाबाहो परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: O grandfather, O you of mighty arms, tell me fully how the battle took place. Great is my curiosity to hear it.

sn: भीष्म उवाच रथेनेन्द्रः प्रयातो वै सार्धं देवगणैः पुरा। ददर्शाथाग्रतो वृत्रं धिष्ठितं पर्वतोपमम्॥
en: Bhishma said-In days of yore, Indra, accompanied by the celestial army, proceeded on his car, and saw the Asura Vritra stationed before him like a mountain.

sn: योजनानां शतान्यूज़ पञ्चोच्छ्रितमरिंदम्। शतानि विस्तरेणाथ त्रीण्येवाभ्यधिकानि वै॥
en: He was full five hundred Yojanas in height, 0 chastiser of enemies and three hundred Yojanas in circumference.

sn: तत् प्रेक्ष्य तादृशं रूपं त्रैलोक्येनापि दुर्जयम्। वृत्रस्य देवाः संत्रस्ता न शान्तिमुपलेभिरे॥
en: Seeing that form of Vritra, which was incapable of being defeated by the three worlds united together, the celestials became stricken with fear and full of anxiety.

sn: शक्रस्य तु तदा राजनूरुस्तम्भो व्यजायत। भयाद् वृत्रस्य सहसा दृष्ट्वा तद्रूपमुत्तमम्॥
en: Indeed, suddenly beholding that huge form of his enemy, O king, Indra was paralysed in the lower extremities.

sn: ततो नादः समभवद् वादित्राणां च निःस्वनः। देवासुराणां सर्वेषां तस्मिन् युद्धे ह्युपस्थिते॥
en: Then, on the eve of that great battle between the gods and the demons, there arose loud peals from both sides, and drums and other musical instruments were beaten and blown.

sn: अथ वृत्रस्य कौरव्य दृष्ट्वा शक्रमवस्थितम्। न सम्भ्रमो न भीः काचिदास्था वा समजायत॥
en: Seeing Indra stationed before him, you of Kuru's race, Vritra felt neither awe nor fear, nor was he disposed to collect all his energies for the battle.

sn: ततः समभवद् युद्धं त्रैलोक्यस्य भयंकरम्। शक्रस्य च सुरेन्द्रस्य वृत्रस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: Then the battle took place filling the three worlds with fear, between Indra the king of the gods and Vritra of great energy.

sn: असिभिः पट्टिशैः शूलैः शक्तितोमरमुद्गरैः। शिलाभिर्विविधाभिश्च कार्मुकैश्च महास्वनैः॥ शस्त्रैश्च विविधैर्दिव्यैः पावकोल्काभिरेव च। देवासुरैस्ततः सैन्यैः सर्वमासीत् समाकुलम्॥
en: The entire sky was covered by the warriors of both sides with swords, axes, lances, darts, spears and heavy clubs and rocks of various sizes and bows of loud sound and various sorts of celestial weapons and fires and burning brands.

sn: पितामहपुरोगाश्च सर्वे देवगणास्तथा। ऋषयश्च महाभागास्तद् युद्धं द्रष्टुमागमन्॥ विमानागौमहाराज सिद्धाश्च भरतर्षभ। गन्धर्वाश्च विमानागौरप्सरोभिः समागमन॥
en: All the deities led by the Grand-father, and all the highly-blessed Rishis, came to see the battle, on their best of cars; and the Siddhas, also, O foremost of Bharata's family, and the Gandharvas, with the Apsaras, on their own beautiful and foremost of cars, came there.

sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षमावृत्य वृत्रो धर्मभृतां वरः। अश्वमवर्षेण देवेन्द्रं समाकिरदतिद्रुतम्॥
en: Then Vritra, that foremost of virtuous persons, speedily overwhelmed the sky and the king of gods with a thick shower of rocks.

sn: ततो देवगणाः क्रुद्धाः सर्वतः शरवृष्टिभिः। अश्मवर्षमपोहन्त वृत्रप्रेरितमाहवे॥
en: Thereat, filled with ire the celestials dispelled with their showers of arrows that thick down-pour of rocks showered by Vritra in battle.

sn: वृत्रस्तु कुरुशार्दूल महामायो महाबलः। मोहयामास देवेन्द्र मायायुद्धेन सर्वशः॥
en: Then Vritra, O foremost of Kurus, endued with mighty strength and large powers of illusion, stupefied the king of illusion. was

sn: तस्य वृत्रार्दितस्याथ मोह आसीच्छतक्रतोः। रथन्तरेण तं तत्र वसिष्ठः समबोधयत्॥
en: When the god of hundred sacrifices, thus afflicted by Vritra, possessed by stupefaction, the sage Vashishtha restores him to his senses by chanting Samans.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच देवश्रेष्ठोऽसि देवेन्द्र दैत्यासरुनिबर्हण। त्रैलोक्यबलसंयुक्तः कस्माच्छक विषीदसि॥
en: Vashishtha said You are the foremost of the gods, O chief of the gods, O destroyer of Daityas and Asuras! The strength of the three worlds lies in you! Why, then, O Shakra, do you languish so!

sn: एष ब्रह्मा च विष्णुश्च शिवश्चैव जगत्पतिः। सोमश्च भगवान् देवः सर्वे च परमर्षयः॥
en: See, there are Brahma and Vishnu, and Shiva, that lord of the universe, the illustrious and divine Soma, and all the great Rishis.

sn: माकार्षीः कश्मलं शक्र कश्चिदेवेतरो यथा। आर्यां युद्धे मतिं कृत्वा जहि शत्रून् सुराधिप॥
en: Do not, O Indra, yield to weakness, like an ordinary mortal! Firmly determined on battle, kill your enemies, O king of the gods.

sn: एष लोकगुरुस्त्र्यक्षः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः। निरीक्षते त्वां भगवांस्त्यज मोहं सुराधिप॥
en: There, that lord of all the worlds, viz., the Three-eyed (Shiva), worshipped of all the worlds, is seeing you! Shake off this stupefaction, O king of the gods.

sn: एते ब्रह्मर्षयश्चैव बृहस्पतिपुरोगमाः। स्तवेन शक्र दिव्येन स्तुवन्ति त्वां जयाय वै॥
en: There, those twice-born Rishis, headed by Brihaspati, are lauding you for your victory, in celestial hymns.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एवं सम्बोध्यमानस्य वसिष्ठेन महात्मना। अतीव वासवस्यासीद् बलमुत्तमतेजसः॥
en: Bhishma said-While the highly energetic Vasava was thus being restored to senses by the great Vashishtha, his strength became greatly increased.

sn: ततो बुद्धिमुपागम्य भगवान् पाकशासनः। योगेन महता युक्तस्तां मायां व्यपकर्षत॥
en: The illustrious punisher of Paka then, depending upon his intelligence, had recourse to high Yoga and with its help removed these illusions of Vritra.

sn: ततोऽङ्गिरःसुतः श्रीमांस्ते चैव सुमहर्षयः। दृष्ट्वा वृत्रस्य विक्रान्तमुपागम्य महेश्वरम्॥ ऊचुर्वृत्रविनाशार्थं लोकानां हितकाम्यया।
en: Then Brihaspati, the son of Angiras, and those greatest of Rishis endued with great prosperity, seeing the prowess of Vritra, went to Mahadeva, and moved by the desire of benefiting the three worlds, urged him to kill the great Asura.

sn: ततो भगवतस्तेजो ज्वरो भूत्वा जगत्पतेः॥ समाविशत् तदा रौद्रो वृत्रं लोकपतिं तदा।
en: The energy of that illustrious lord of the universe thereupon assumed the nature of a fierce fever and entered the body of Vritra the lord of Asuras.

sn: विष्णुश्च भगवान् देवः सर्वलोकाभिपूजितः॥ ऐन्द्रं समाविशद् वज्रं लोकसंरक्षणे रतः।
en: The illustrious and divine Vishnu, worshipped of all the worlds, bent upon protecting the universe, entered the thunderbolt of Indra.

sn: ततो बृहस्पति/मानुपागम्य शतक्रतुम्। वसिष्ठश्च महातेजाः सर्वे च परमर्षयः॥ ते समासाद्य वरदं वासवं लोकपूजितम्। ऊचुरेकाग्रमनसो जहि वृत्रमिति प्रभो॥
en: Then the highly intelligent Brihaspati and Vashishtha of great energy and all the other foremost of Rishis, going to the God of hundred sacrifices, viz., the boon-giving Vasava, the worshipped of all the worlds, said to him kill forthwith Vritra, O powerful one.

sn: महेश्वर उवाच एष वृत्रो महाशक्र बलेन महता वृतः। विश्वात्मा सर्वगश्चैव बहुमायश्च विश्रुतः॥
en: Maheshvara said There, O Shakra, stands the great Vritra, accompanied by a great army. He is the soul of the universe, capable of going everywhere, gifted with great powers of illusion, and highly illustrious.

sn: तदेनमसुरश्रेष्ठं त्रैलोक्येनापि दुर्जयम्। जहि त्वं योगमास्थाय मावमंस्थाः सुरेश्वर॥
en: This foremost of Asuras is, therefore incapable of being defeated by even the threeworlds in a body. Helped by Yoga, do you kill him, O king of the celestials. Do not neglect him.

sn: अनेन हि तपस्तप्तं बलार्थममराधिप। षष्टिं वर्षसहस्राणि ब्रह्मा चास्मै वरं ददौ॥ महत्त्वं योगिनां चैव महामायत्वमेव च। महाबलत्वं च तथा तेजश्चाम्यं सुरेश्वर।॥
en: O king of the celestials, Vritra had practised, for full sixty thousand years, the severest penances for acquiring strength. Brahma gave him the boons he had prayed for, viz., the greatness that belongs to Yogins, large powers of illusion, enough of might, and superabundant energy.

sn: एतत् त्वां मामकं तेजः समाविशति वासव। व्यग्रमेनं त्वमप्येनं वज्रेण जहि दानवम्॥
en: I give you my energy, O Vasava! The Danava has now lost his coolness. Do you, therefore, kill him now with your thunderbolt.

sn: शक्र उवाच भगवंस्त्वप्रसादेन दितिजं सुदुरासदम्। वज्रेण निहनिष्यामि पश्यतस्ते सुरर्षभ॥
en: Shakra said Before your eyes, O foremost of gods, I shall, through your favour kill with my thunderbolt this invincible son Diti.

sn: भीष्म उवाच आविश्यमाने दैत्ये तु ज्वरेणाथ महासुरे। देवतानामृषीणां च हर्षान्नादो महानभूत्॥
en: Bhishma said. When the great Asura or Daitya was possessed by that fever, the gods and the Rishis, filled with joy, sent up loud cheers.

sn: ततो दुन्दुभयश्चैव शङ्खाश्च सुमहास्वनाः। मुरजा डिण्डिमाश्चैव प्रावाद्यन्त सहस्रशः॥
en: At the same time drums, and conchs of loud blare, and kettle-drums and tabors in thousands began to beat and blow.

sn: असुराणां तु सर्वेषां स्मृतिलोपो महानभूत्। मायानाशश्च बलवान् क्षणेन समपद्यत॥
en: Suddenly all the Asuras lost in a body their memory. At that moment their powers of illusion, also, disappeared.

sn: तथाविष्टमथो ज्ञात्वा ऋशयो देवतास्तथा। स्तुवन्तः शक्रमीशानं तथा प्राचोदयन्त्रपि॥
en: Knowing the enemy to be thus possessed, the Rishis and gods lauded both Shakra and Ishana, and began to urge the former.

sn: रथस्थस्य हि शक्रस्य युद्धकाले महात्मनः। ऋषिभिः स्तूयमानस्य रूपमासीत् सुदुर्दृशम्॥
en: The form that Indra assumed on the eve of the battle, while seated on his car and while his praises were being lauded by the Rishis, became such that none could look at it without dread.

sn: भीष्म उवाच शरीरे तानि मे शृणु।॥ वृत्रस्य तु महाराज ज्वराविष्टस्य सर्वशः। अभवन् यानि लिङ्गानि
en: Bhishma said-Hear me, O king, I describe the symptoms that appeared on the body of Vritra when he was possessed by that fever.

sn: ज्वलितास्योऽभवद् घोरो वैवयं चागमत् परम्। गात्रकम्पश्च सुमहाश्वासश्चाप्यभवन्महान्॥
en: The heroic Asura's mouth began to send out flames of fire. He became greatly pale. His body began to tremble all over. His breath became hard.

sn: रोमहर्षश्च तीव्रोऽभूनिःश्वासश्च महान् नृप। शिवा चाशिवसंकाशा तस्य वक्त्रात् सुदारुणा॥ निष्पपात महाघोरा स्मृतिः सा तस्य भारत। उल्काश्च ज्वलितास्तस्य दीप्ताः पार्श्वे प्रपेदिरे॥
en: His hairs stood erect. His breath was very hard. His memory, O Bharata, went out of his mouth in the shape of a dreadful, and inauspicious jackal. Burning and blazing meteors dropped on his right and left.

sn: गृध्राः कङ्का बलाकाश्च वाचोऽमुञ्चन् सुदारुणाः। वृत्रस्योपरि संसृष्टाश्चक्रवत् परिबभ्रमुः॥
en: Vultures, Kankas, and cranes yelled fierce cries, as they moved over Vritra's head.

sn: ततस्तं रथमास्थाय देवाप्यायित आहवे। वज्रोद्यतकरः शक्रस्तं दैत्यं समवैक्षत॥
en: Then, in that battle, Indra, worshipped of the gods, and armed with the thunderbolt, looked hard at the demon as the latter sat on his car.

sn: आमनुषमथो नादं स मुमोच महासुरः। व्यजृम्भच्चैव राजेन्द्र तीव्रज्वरसमन्वितः॥
en: Possessed by that dreadful fever, the powerful Asura, O king, yawned and uttered inhuman cries.

sn: अथास्य जम्भतः शक्रस्ततो वज्रमवासृजत्। स वज्रः सुमहातेजा: कालाग्निसदृशोपमः॥ क्षिप्रमेव महाकायं वृत्रं दैत्यमपातयत्।
en: While the Asura was yawning, Indra discharged his thunderbolt at him. Endued with great enrgy and resembling the fire that destroys the creation at the end of the cycle, that thunderbolt overthrew in a moment Vritra of gigantic form.

sn: ततो नादः समभवत् पुनरेव समन्ततः॥ वृत्रं विनिहतं दृष्ट्वा देवानां भरतर्षभः।
en: The gods on all sides cried aloud when they saw Vritra killed, O foremost of Bharata's race.

sn: वृत्रं तु हत्वा मघवा दानवारिर्महायशाः॥ वज्रेण विष्णुयुक्तेन दिवमेव समाविशत्।
en: Having killed Vritra, Mghavat, that enemy of the Danavas, of great entered heaven with that thunderbolt pervaded by Vishnu,

sn: अथ वृत्रस्य कौरव्य शरीरादभिनिःसृता॥ ब्रह्मवध्या महाघोरा रौद्रा लोकभयावहा।
en: Just then, O you of Kuru's family, the sin of Brahmanicide, fierce and dreadful and striking all the worlds with fear, came out of the person of the killed Vritra.

sn: करालदशना भीमा विकृता कृष्णपिङ्गला॥ प्रकीर्णमूर्धजा चैव घोरनेत्रा च भारता कपालमालिनी चैव कृत्येव भरतर्षभ॥ रुधिरार्द्रा च धर्मज्ञ चीरवल्कलवासिनी। साभिनिष्क्रम्य राजेन्द्र तादृगूपा भयावहा॥ वज्रिणं मृगमायास तदा भरतसत्तम।
en: Of terrible teeth and dreadful countenance, hideous for ugliness, and dark and tawny, with hair dishevelled, and dreadful eyes, O Bharata, with a garland of skulls round her neck, and loO king like Incantation incarnate, O foremost of Bharatas, bathed in blood, and clad in rags and barks of trees, O you of righteous soul, she came out of Vritra's body. Of such dreadful form and countenance, O king, she sought the holder of the thunderbolt.

sn: कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य वृत्रहा कुरुनन्दन॥ स्वर्गायाभिमुखः प्रायाल्लोकानां हितकाम्यया।
en: A little while after, O you of Kuru's race, the killer of Vritra, for the behoof of the three worlds, was proceeding towards heaven.

sn: सा विनिः :सरमाणं तु दृष्ट्वा शक्रं महौजसम्॥ जग्राह वध्या देवेन्द्रं सुलग्ना चाभवत् तदा।
en: Seeing Indra of great energy thus proceeding on his mission, she caught the king of the gods and from that moment stuck to him.

sn: स हि तस्मिन् समुत्पन्ने ब्रह्मवध्याकृते भय॥ नलिन्या बिसमध्यस्थ उवासाब्दगणान् बहून्।
en: When the sin of Brahmanicide thus stuck to his body and filled him with terror, Indra entered the fibres of a lotus-stalk and lived there for many years.

sn: अनुसृत्य तु यत्नात् स तथा वै ब्रह्महत्यया॥ तदा गृहीतः कौरव्य निस्तेजाः समपद्यत।
en: But the sin of Brahmanicide followed him closely. Indeed, O son of Kuru, seized by her, Indra became shorn of all his energies.

sn: तस्या व्यपोहने शक्रः परं यत्नं चकार ह॥ न चाशकत् तां देवेन्द्रो ब्रह्मवध्यां व्यपोहितुम्।
en: He tried much for driving her from him, but all those attempts proved useless,

sn: गृहीत एव तु तया देवेन्द्रो भरतर्षभ।॥ पितामहमुपागम्य शिरसा प्रत्यपूजयत्।
en: Seized by her, O foremost of Bharata's race, the king of the gods at last presented himself before the Grandfather and adored him by bending low his head.

sn: ज्ञात्वा गृहीतं शक्रं स द्विजप्रवरवध्यया।॥ ब्रह्मा स चिन्तयामास तदा भरतसत्तम।
en: Knowing that Indra was possessed by the sin of Brahmanicide, Brahman began to think, 0 best of the Bharatas, (of the measures for freeing him).

sn: तामुवाच महाबाहो ब्रह्मवध्यां पितामहः॥ स्वरेण मधुरेणाथ सान्त्वयन्निव भारत। मुच्यतां विदशेन्द्रोऽयं मत्प्रियं कुरु भाविनि॥ ब्रूहि किं ते करोम्यद्य कामं किं त्वमिहेच्छसि॥
en: The Grandfather at last, O you of great arms, addressed Brahmanicide in sweet words as if from the desire of pacifying her, and said.-0 amiable one, let the king of the gods, who is a favourite of mine, be freed from you. Tell me, what shall I do for you? What wish of yours shall I satisfy?

sn: ब्रह्मवध्योवाच त्रिलोकपूजिते देवे प्रीते त्रैलोक्यकर्तरि। कृतमेव हि मन्यामि निवासं तु विधत्स्व मे॥
en: Brahmanicide said When the Creator of the three worlds, when the illustrious god worshipped of the universe, has been pleased with me, I consider my wishes as already fulfilled. Let my residence be now fixed.

sn: त्वया कृतेयं मर्यादा लोकसंरक्षणार्थिना। स्थापना वै सुमहती त्वया देव प्रवर्तिता॥
en: Desirous of preserving the worlds, this rule has been laid down by you. It was you, O lord, who had introduced this important rule.

sn: प्रीते तु त्वयि धर्मज्ञ सर्वलेकेश्वर प्रभो। शक्रादपगमिष्यामि निवासं संविधत्स्व मे॥
en: As you have been pleased with me, O righteous Lord, O powerful Master of all the worlds, I shall surely leave Shakra! But grant me an abode to live in.

sn: भीष्म उवाच तथेति तां प्राह तदा ब्रह्मवध्यां पितामहः। उपायतः स शक्रस्य ब्रह्मवध्यां व्यपोहत॥
en: Bhishma said. The Grandfather replied to Brahmanicide, saying,-So be it! Indeed, the Grandfather found out means for removing Brahmanicide from the body of Indra.

sn: ततः स्वयम्भुवा ध्यातस्तत्र वह्निर्महात्मना। ब्रह्माणमुपसंगम्य ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ प्राप्तोऽस्मि भगवन् देव त्वत्सकाशमनिन्दित। ततः स्वयम्भुवा ध्यातस्तत्र वह्निर्महात्मना। यत् कर्तव्यं मया देव तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: The Self-sprung thought of the great Agni. The latter immediately appeared before Brahman and said:-O illustrious and divine Lord, O defeatless one, I have appeared before you. You should say what I shall have to do.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच बहुधा विभजिष्यामि ब्रह्मवध्यामिमामहम्। शक्रस्याघविमोक्षार्थं चतुर्भागं प्रतीच्छ वै॥
en: Bhishma said I shall divide this sin of Brahmanicide into several parts. For freeing Shakra from her, do you take a fourth portion of that sin.

sn: अग्निरुवाच मम मोक्षस्य कोऽन्तो वै ब्रह्मन् ध्यायस्व वै प्रभो। एतदिच्छामि विज्ञातुं तत्त्वतो लोकपूजित॥
en: How shall I be saved from her, O Brahman? O powerful Lord, do you appoint the way. I wish to know the means fully, O worshipped of all the worlds.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच यस्त्वांज्वलन्तमासाद्य स्वयं वै मानवः क्वचित्। बीजौषधिरसैर्वते न यक्ष्यति तमोवृतः॥ तमेषा यास्यति क्षिप्रं तत्रैव च निवत्स्यति। ब्रह्मवध्या हव्यवाह व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: That portion of Brahmanicide which you will take upon yourself shall immediately enter into, and leaving you shall live in, that man who, overwhelmed by the quality of darkness, will abstain from offering your blazing form, seeds, herbs, and juices. O carrier of oblations, let the fever of your heart be dispelled.

sn: इत्युक्तः प्रतिजग्राह तद् वचो हव्यकव्यभुक्। पितामहस्य भगवांस्तथा च तदभूत् प्रभो॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by the Grandfather, the eater of oblations and sacrificial offerings accepted his order. A fourth of that sin then entered his body, O king.

sn: ततो वृक्षौषधितृणं समाहूय पितामहः। इममर्थं महाराज वक्तुं समुपचक्रमे॥
en: The Grandfather then summoned the tree, the herbs, and all sorts of grass to him, and begged them to take upon themselves a fourth of that sin.

sn: ततो वृक्षौषधितृणं तथैवोक्तं यथातथम्। व्यथितं वह्निवद् राजन् ब्रह्माणमिदमब्रवीत्॥ अस्माकं ब्रह्मवध्यायाः कोऽन्तो लोकपितामह। दैवेनाभिहतानस्मान् न पुनर्हन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Addressed by him, the trees and herbs and grasses became as much moved as Agni had been at the command and they replied to the Grandfather, saying, How shall we, O grandfather of all the worlds, be ourselves saved from this sin? You should not afflict us that have already been assailed by the fates.

sn: वयमग्नि तथा शीतं वर्षं च पवनेरितम्। सहामः सततं देव तथा च्छेदनभेदने।॥
en: O god, we have always to bear heat and cold and the showers driven by the winds, besides the cutting and tearing.

sn: ब्रह्मवध्यामिमामद्य भवतः शासनाद् वयम्। ग्रहीष्यामस्त्रिलोकेश मोक्षं चिन्तयतां भवान्॥
en: We are willing, O lord of the three worlds, to take at your order this sin of Brahmancide. May you point out the means of our rescue.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच पर्वकाले तु सम्प्राप्ते यो वै च्छेदनभेदनम्। करिष्यति नरो मोहात् तमेषानुगमिष्यति॥
en: This sin that you shall take, shall assail the man who through stupefaction of judgement will cut or tear any of you on a full-moon day.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो वृक्षौषधितृणमेवमुक्तं महात्मना। ब्रह्माणमभिसम्पूज्य जगामाशु यथागतम्॥
en: Thus addressed by the great Brahman, the trees, herbs and grasses worshipped the Creator and then went away without waiting there.

sn: आहूयाप्सरसो देवस्ततो लोकपितामहः। वाचा मधुरया प्राह सान्त्वयन्निव भारत॥ इयमिन्द्रादनुप्राप्ता ब्रह्मवध्या वराङ्गनाः। चतुर्थमस्या भागांशं मयोक्ताः सम्प्रतीच्छत॥
en: The Grandfather of all the worlds then sent for the Apsaras and pleasing them with sweet words, O Bharata, said,-This foremost of ladies, viz., Brahmanicide, has come out of Indra's body. Begged by me, do you take a fourth part of her into your own body.

sn: अप्सरस ऊचुः ग्रहणे कृतबुद्धीनां देवेश तव शासनात्। मोक्षं समयतोऽस्माकं चिन्तयस्व पितामह॥
en: The Apsaras said O Lord of all the gods, at your command We are fully willing to take a portion of this sin. But, O Grandfather our compact is that you do think of the means by which we ourselves may be rescued from this.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच रजस्वलासु नारीषु यो वै मैथुनमाचरेत्। तमेषा यास्यति क्षिप्रं व्येतु वो मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: Brahman said Let the fever of your hearts be removed. The portion of this sin that you will take upon yourselves shall leave you and immediately possess that men who will seek cohabitation with women in their menses.

sn: भीष्म उवाच तथेति हृष्टमनस इत्युक्त्वाप्सरसां गणाः। स्वानि स्थानानि सम्प्राप्य रेमिरे भरतर्षभ॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by the Grandfather, O foremost of Bharata's race, the various clans of the Apsaras, with delighted hearts repaired to their respective places and began to sport in joy.

sn: ततस्त्रिलोककृद् देवः पुनरेव महातपाः। अप:संचिन्तयामास ध्यातास्ताश्चाप्यथागमन्॥
en: The illustrious Creator of the three worlds, gifted with great ascetic merit, then thought of the Waters which immediately came to him.

sn: तास्तु सर्वाः समागम्य ब्रह्माणममितौजसम्। इदमूचुर्वचो राजन् प्रणिपत्य पितामहम्॥ इमाः स्म देव सम्प्राप्तास्त्वत्सकाशमरिंदम्। शासनात् तव लोकेश समाज्ञापय नः प्रभो॥
en: Arrived before Brahman of great energy, thc Waters bowed to him and said:-We have come before you, O chastiser of enemies, at your behest! O powerful Master of all the worlds, tell us what we are to do.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच इयं वृत्रादनुप्राप्ता पुरुहूतं महाभया। ब्रह्मवध्या चतुर्थांशमस्या यूयं प्रतीच्छत॥
en: Brahman said-This dreadful sin has possessed Indra on account of his having killed Vritra. Take you a fourth part of Brahmanicide.

sn: आप ऊचुः एवं भवतु लोकेश यथा वदसि नः प्रभो। मोक्षं समयतोऽस्माकं संचिन्तयितुमर्हसि॥
en: The Waters said Let it be as you order, O master of all the worlds. You should, however, O powerful Lord of ours, concert the means by which we may be rescued from this.

sn: त्वं हि देवेश सर्वस्य जगतः परमा गतिः। कोऽन्यः प्रसादो हि भवेद् यन्नः कृच्छ्रात् समुद्धरेत्।।५३
en: You are the Lord of all the gods, and the supreme refuge of the universe. Who else is there whom we may worship so that he may save us from distress.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच अल्पा इति मतिं कृत्वा यो नरो बुद्धिमोहितः। श्लेष्ममूत्रपुरीषाणि युष्मासु प्रतिमोक्ष्यति।॥ तमियं यास्यति क्षिप्रं तत्रैव च निवत्स्यति। तथा वो भविता मोक्ष इति सत्यं ब्रवीमि वः॥
en: Brahman said This one shall forthwith go to, and thenceforth live in, that man who stupefied by his understanding and regarding you lightly will throw into you phlegm and urine and excreta. It is this, verily true do I say to you, that your rescue shall be brought about.

sn: ततो विमुच्य देवेन्द्रं ब्रह्मवध्या युधिष्ठिर। यथा विसृष्टं तं वासमगमद्देवशासनात्॥
en: Bhishma said Then, leaving the king of the deities, the sin of Brahmanicide, O Yudhishthira, proceeded to the abodes that were settled for her at the Grandfather's behest.

sn: एवं शक्रेण संप्राप्ता ब्रह्मवध्या जनाधिप। पितामहमनुज्ञाप्य सोऽश्वमेधमकल्पयत्॥
en: It was thus, O king, that Indra had become attacked by that dreadful sin. With the Grandfather's permission Indra then resolved to celebrate a Horse-sacrifice.

sn: श्रूयते च महाराज संप्राप्ता वासवेन वै। ब्रह्मवध्या ततः शुद्धिं हयमेधेन लब्धवान्॥
en: O king! It is listen to that Indra have got relieved from the sin of Brahmanicide by celebrating a Horse-sacrifice.

sn: समवाप्य श्रियं देवो हत्वारीश्च सहस्रशः। प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे वासवः पृथिवीपते॥
en: Regaining his prosperity and killing thousands of enemies, that Vasava acquired great joy, O lord of Earth.

sn: वृत्रस्य रुधिराच्चैव शिखण्डाः पार्थ जज्ञिरे। द्विजातिभिरभक्ष्यास्ते दीक्षितैश्च तपोधनैः॥
en: From the blood of Vritra, O son of Pritha, were born high-crested cocks. Therefore, those fowls are unclean (as food) for the twice-born ones, and those ascetics that have undergone the rite of initiation.

sn: सर्वावस्थं त्वमप्येषां द्विजातीनां प्रियं कुरु। इमे हि भूतले देवाः प्रथिताः कुरुनन्दन॥
en: Under all circumstances, O king, do you encompass what is agreeable to the twice-born, for these, O king, are known as gods on Earth.

sn: एवं शक्रेण कौरव्य बुद्धिसौक्ष्म्यान्महासुरः। उपायपूर्वं निहतो वृत्रो ह्यमिततेजसा॥
en: It was thus, O Kuru chief, that the powerful Asura Vritra was killed by Shakra of great energy by the help of subtle intelligence and through the application of means. son

sn: एवं त्वमपि कौन्तेय पृथिव्यामपराजितः। भविष्यसि यथा देवः शतक्रतुरमित्रहा॥
en: You will, also, O of Kunti, unvanquished on Earth, become another Indra and the killer of all your enemies.

sn: ये तु शक्रकथां दिव्यामिमां पर्वसु पर्वसु। विप्रमध्ये वदिष्यन्ति न ते प्राप्स्यन्ति किल्बिषम्॥
en: Those men who, on every Parva day, will recite this sacred narrative of Vritra in the midst of Brahmanas shall never be sullied by any sin.

sn: इत्येतद् वृत्रमाश्रित्य शक्रस्यात्यद्भुतं महत्। कथितं कर्म ते तात किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: I have now recited to you one of the greatest and most wonderful feats of Indra about Vritra, What else do you wish to hear."

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामह महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद। अस्मिन् वृत्रवधे देव विवक्षा मम जायते॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather you are endued with great wisdom and thoroughly grounded in every branch of learning. From this very narrative of the destruction of Vritra the wish has arisen in my mind of asking you a question.

sn: ज्वरेण मोहितो वृत्रः कथितस्ते जनाधिप। निहतो वासवेनेह वज्रेणेति तदानघ।।२।
en: You have said, O king, that Vritra was Stupefied by Fever, and that then, O sinless one, he was killed by Vasava with the thunderboli.

sn: कथमेष महाप्राज्ञ ज्वरः प्रादुर्बभौ कुतः। ज्वरोत्पत्तिं निपुणतः श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं प्रभो॥
en: How did this Fever, O you of great wisdom, originale, O lord, I wish to hear fully of the origin of Fever,

sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु राजन् ज्वरस्येमं सम्भवं लोकविश्रुतम्। विस्तरं चास्य वक्ष्यामि यादृशश्चैव भारत॥
en: Listen, O king, to the origin, known all over the world, of Fever! I shall describe fully this topic, fully explaining how Fever first came into existence, O Bharata.

sn: पुरा मेरोमहाराज शृङ्गं त्रैलोक्यपूजितम्। ज्योतिष्कं नाम सावित्रं सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्॥
en: In days of yore, O king, there was a summit, named Savitri, of the mountains of Meru. Adored of all the worlds, it was endued with great effulgence and adorned with every sort of jewels and gems.

sn: अप्रमेयमनाधृष्यं सर्वलोकेषु भारत। तत्र देवो गिरितटे हेमधातुविभूषिते॥
en: That summit was immeasurable in extent and no one could go there. On that mountain summit the divine Mahadeva used to sit shiningly as if on a bed-stead adorned with gold.

sn: पर्यङ्क इव विभ्राजन्नुपविष्टो बभूव ह। शैलराजसुता चास्य नित्यं पार्वे स्थिता बभौ॥ तथा देवा महात्मानो वसवश्वामितौजसः। तथैव च महात्मानावश्विनौ भिषजां वरौ। तथा वैश्रवणो राजा गुह्यकैरभिसंवृतः॥ यक्षाणामीश्वरः श्रीमान् कैलासनिलयः प्रभुः। उपासन्त महात्मानमुशना च महामुनिः॥ सनत्कुमारप्रमुखास्तथैव च महर्षयः। अङ्गिरःप्रमुखाश्चैव तथा देवर्षयोऽपरे॥ विश्वावसुश्च गन्धर्वस्तथा नारदपर्वतौ। अप्सरोगणसंघाश्च समाजग्मुरनेकशः॥
en: Sitting by his side, the daughter of the king of mountains shone in brilliance. The great gods, the Vasus of immeasurable energy, the great Ashvins, those foremost of physicians, and king Vaishravana attended by many a Guhyaka,-that king of the Yakshas, endued with prosperity and power, and having his abode on the suminit of Kailasa,-all waited upon the great Mahadeva. And the great sage Ushanas, and the foremost of Rishis headed by Sanatkumara, and the other celestial Rishis headed by Angiras, and the Gandharva Vishvavasu, and Narada and Parvata, and the various clans of Apsaras, all came there to wait upon the king of the universe.

sn: ववौ सुखः शिवो वायु नागन्धवहः शुचिः। सर्वर्तुकुसुमोपेताः पुष्पवन्तो द्रुमास्तथा॥
en: A pure and auspicious air carrying various sorts of perfumes, blew there. The trees that stood there were adorned with the flowers of all seasons.

sn: तथा विद्याधराश्चैव सिद्धाश्चैव तपोधनाः। महादेवं पशुपति पर्युपासन्त भारत॥
en: A large number of Vidyadharas, Siddhas and ascetics, too, O Bharata, went there for waiting upon Mahadeva, that Lord of all creatures.

sn: भूतानि च महाराज नानारूपधराण्यथ। राक्षसाश्च महारौद्राः पिशाचाश्च महाबलाः॥ बहुरूपधरा हृष्टा नानाप्रहरणोद्यताः। देवस्यानुचरास्तत्र तस्थिरे चानलोपमाः॥
en: Many ghosts also, of various forms and aspects, and many fearful Rakshasas and powerful Pishachas, of various forms, mad with joy, and armed with various sorts of uplifted weapons forming the train of Mahadeva, were there, every one of whom looked like a blazing fire energy.

sn: नन्दी च भगवांस्तत्र देवस्यानुमते स्थितः। प्रगृह्य ज्वलितं शूलं दीप्यमानः स्वतेजसा॥
en: The illustrious Nandi stood there obeying the great god, shining with his own energy and armed with a lance that resembled a flame of fire.

sn: गङ्गा च सरितां श्रेष्ठा सर्वतीर्थजलोद्भवा। पर्युपासत तं देवं रूपिणी कुरुनन्दन॥
en: Ganga, also, that foremost of all Rivers and originating from all sacred waters in the universe, waited there in her embodied form, O son of Kuru, upon that illustrious gods.

sn: स एवं भगवांस्तत्र पूज्यमानः सुरर्षिभिः। देवैश्च सुमहातेजा महादेवो व्यतिष्ठत॥
en: Thus worshipped by the celestial Rishis and the gods, the illustrious Mahadeva of great energy lived on that summit of Meru.

sn: कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य दक्षो नाम प्रजापतिः। पूर्वोक्तेन विधानेन यक्ष्यमाणोऽन्वपद्यत॥
en: After sometime had gone away, the Prajapati Daksha began to celebrate a sacrifice according to ancient rites.

sn: ततस्तस्य मखं देवाः सर्वे शक्रपुरोगमाः। गमनाय समागम्य बुद्धिमापेदिरे तदा॥
en: All the gods in a body headed by Sakra, resolved to repair to that sacrifice of Daksha.

sn: ते विमानैर्महात्मानो ज्वलनार्कसमप्रभैः। देवस्यानुमतेऽगच्छन् गङ्गाद्वारमिति श्रुतिः॥
en: We have heard that the great gods ordered by Mahadeva, mounted their celestial cars resembling the fire or the Sun in sheen, and proceeded to that spot whence the Ganges is said to issue.

sn: प्रस्थिता देवता दृष्ट्वा शैलराजसुता तदा। उवाच वचनं साध्वी देवं पशुपति पतिम्॥ भगवन् क्वनु यान्त्येते देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः। ब्रूहि तत्त्वेन तत्त्वज्ञ संशयो मे महानयम्॥
en: Seeing the deities depart, the excellent daughter of the king of mountains, addressed her divine husband, viz., the Lord of all creatures, and said, O illustrious one, who are those gods headed by Shakra going? O you who know the truth, tell me truly, for a great doubt has possessed my mind.

sn: महेश्वर उवाच दक्षो नाम महाभागे प्रजानां पतिरुत्तमः। हयमेधेन यजते तत्र यान्ति दिवौकसः॥
en: Maheshvara said 0 highly blessed lady, the excellent Prajapati Daksha is worshipping the gods in a House Sacrifice! These Dwellers of heaven are going there.

sn: उमोवाच यज्ञमेतं महादेव किमर्थं नाधिगच्छसि। केन वा प्रतिषेधेन गमनं ते न विद्यते॥
en: Uma said Why, O Mahadeva do you not go to that Sacrifice? What objection is there of your going to that place?

sn: महेश्वर उवाच सुरैरेव महाभागे पूर्वमेतदनुष्ठितम्। यज्ञेषु सर्वेषु मम न भाग उपकल्पितः॥
en: O highly blessed lady, the gods in days of yore made a compact by virtue of which no share was allotted to me of offerings in all Sacrifices.

sn: पूर्वोपायोपपन्नेन मार्गेण वरवर्णिनि। न मे सुराः प्रयच्छन्ति भागं यज्ञस्य धर्मतः॥
en: According to that arrangement, O fair one, the gods do not give me, following the old custom, any share of the sacrificial offerings!

sn: उमोवाच भगवन् सर्वभूतेषु प्रभावाभ्यधिको गुणैः। अजय्यश्चाप्यधृष्यश्च तेजसा यशसा श्रिया॥
en: Uma said-O illustrious one, among all gods, you are the foremost in prowess. In merit, in energy, in fame, and in prosperity you are second to none, and you are, indeed superior to all.

sn: अनेन ते महाभाग प्रतिषेधेन भागतः। अतीव दुःखमुत्पन्नं वेपथुश्च ममानघ॥
en: On account, however, of this disability regarding a share I am filled with great grief, O sinless one, and a treinour fills me from head to foot.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु सा देवी तदा पशुपति पतिम्। तूष्णीभूताभवद् राजन् दह्यमानेन चेतसा॥
en: Bhishma said Having said these words to her consort, the Lord of all creatures, O monarch, the goddess Parvati remained silent, her heart burning the while in grief.

sn: अथ देव्या मतं ज्ञात्वा हृद्गतं यच्चिकीर्षितम्। स समाज्ञापयामास तिष्ठ त्वमिति नन्दिनम्॥
en: Then, understanding what was in her heart and what her thoughts were (for wiping off that disgrace), Mahadeva addressed Nandi, saying,-Wait here.

sn: ततो योगबलं कृत्वा सर्वयोगेश्वरेश्वरः। तं यज्ञं स महातेजा भीमैरनुचरैस्तदा।॥ सहसा घातयामास देवदेवः पिनाकधूक्। केचिन्नादानमुञ्चन्त केचिद्धासांश्च चक्रिरे॥ रुधिरेणापरे राजंस्तत्राग्नि समवाकिरन्। केचिद् यूपान् समुत्पाट्य बभ्रमुर्विकृताननाः॥ आस्यैरन्ये चाग्रसन्त तथैव परिचारकान्।
en: Summoning all his Yoga powers, that Lord of all lords of Yoga, that god of gods, that holder of Pinaka, possessed of great energy, quickly proceeded to the place accompanied by all his dreadful followers and destroyed that Sacrifice. Of these followers of his, some yelled, and some laughed terribly, and some, O king, extinguished the fires with blood; and some, having dreadful faces, pulling up the sacrificial stakes, began to whirl them. Others began to devour those that were celebrating the Sacrifices.

sn: ततः स यज्ञो नृपते वध्यमानः समन्ततः॥ आस्थाय मृगरूपं वै खमेवाभ्यगमत् तदा।
en: Then thus afflicted on every side, that Sacrifice, assumed the form of a deer and tried to fly away through the firmanent.

sn: तं तु यज्ञं तथारूपं गच्छन्तमुपलभ्य सः॥ धनुरादाय बाणेन तदान्वसरत प्रभुः।
en: Learning that the Sacrifice was running away in that form, the powerful Mahadeva began to pursue him with bow and sorrow.

sn: ततस्तस्य सुरेशस्य क्रोधादमिततेजसः॥ ललाटात् प्रसृतो घोरः स्वेदबिन्दुर्बभूव ह।
en: On account of the ire which then filled the heart of that foremost of all gods, possessed of matchless energy, a dreadful drop of sweat appeared on his forehead.

sn: तस्मिन् पतितमात्रे च स्वेदबिन्दौ तदा भुवि॥ प्रादुर्बभूव सुमहानग्निः कालानलोपमः।
en: When the drop of sweat fell down on the Earth, there immediately appeared a blazing fire resembling the conflagration that appears at the end of the cycle.

sn: तत्र चाजायत तदा पुरुषः पुरुषर्षभ॥ ह्रस्वोऽतिमात्रं रक्ताक्षो हरिश्मश्रुर्विभीषणः।
en: From that fire came out a dreadful being, O king of very short stature, having blood-red cyes and a green beard.

sn: उर्ध्व केशोऽतिरोमाङ्ग श्येनोलूकस्तथैव च॥ करालकृष्णवर्णश्च रक्तवासास्तथैव च। तं यज्ञं सुमहासत्त्वोऽदहत् कक्षमिवानलः॥
en: His body was covered all over with hair like a hawk's or an owl's and his hair stood erect. Of dreadful form, his complexion was dark and his dress blood-red. Like a fire burning a heap of dry grass or straw, that Being of high energy speedily consumed the embodied form of Sacrifice.

sn: व्यचरत् सर्वतो देवान् प्राद्रवत् स ऋषींस्तथा। देवाश्चाप्याद्रवन् सर्वे ततो भीता दिशो दश॥ तेन तस्मिन् विचरता पुरुषेण विशाम्पते। पृथिवी ह्यचलद् राजन्नतीव भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Having performed that feat, he then rushed towards the gods and the Rishis that had gathered there. The gods filled with fear, fled on all sides. The earth shook with that Being's tread, O King, O foremost of Bharata's race.

sn: हाहाभूतं जगत् सर्वमुपलक्ष्य तदा प्रभुः। पितामहो महादेवं दर्शयन् प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Exclamation of 'Oh' and 'Alas' arose throughout the universe. Marking this, the before powerful Grandfather, appearing Mahadeva, addressed him thus.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच भवतोऽपि सुराः सर्वे भागं दास्यन्ति वै प्रभो। क्रियतां प्रतिसंहारः सर्वदेवेश्वर त्वया॥
en: O powerful one, the deities will henceforth give you a share of the sacrificial offerings! O Lord of all the gods, let this anger of yours be withdrawn by you.

sn: इमा हि देवताः सर्वा ऋषयश्च परंतप। तव क्रोधान्महादेव न शान्तिमुपलेभिरे॥
en: O scorcher of enemies, there, those gods, and the Rishis, on account of your anger, O Mahadeva, have become greatly agitated.

sn: यश्चैष पुरुषो जात: स्वेदात् ते विबुधोत्तम। ज्वरो नामैष धर्मज्ञ लोकेषु प्रचरिष्यति॥
en: This Being, also, that has originated from your sweat, O foremost of gods, shall walk among creatures, O righteous-souled one, under the name of Fever.

sn: एकीभूतस्य न त्वस्य धारणे तेजसः प्रभो। समर्था सकला पृथ्वी बहुधा सृज्यतामयम्॥
en: O powerful one, if the energy of this Being remains intact, then the entire Earth herself will not be able to bear him. Let him, therefore, be divided into many parts.

sn: इत्युक्तो ब्रह्मणा देवो भागे चापि प्रकल्पिते। भगवन्तं तथेत्याह ब्रह्माणममितौजसम्॥
en: When Brahman had said these words, and when his proper share was appointed of the sacrificial offerings, Mahadeva replied to the Grandfather of great energy, saying,-So be it.

sn: परां च प्रीतिमगमदुत्स्मयंश्च पिनाकधृक्। अवाप च तदा भागं यथोक्तं ब्रह्मणा भवः॥
en: Indeed, the holder of Pinaka, viz., Bhava, smiled and became filled with joy. And he accepted the share that the Grandfather settled the offerings in sacrifices.

sn: ज्वरं च सर्वधर्मज्ञो बहुधा व्यसृजत् तदा। शान्त्यर्थं सर्वभूतानां शृणु तच्चापि पुत्रक॥
en: Knowing the constituents of everything, Mahadeva then divided. Fever into many parts, for the peace of all creatures. Listen, O son, as how he did this.

sn: शीर्षाभितापो नागानां पर्वतानां शिलाजतु। अपां तु नीलिका विद्यान्निर्मोकं भुजगेषु च॥ खोरकः सौरभेयाणामूषरं पृथिवीतले। पशूनामपि धर्मज्ञ दृष्टिप्रत्यवरोधनम्॥ रन्ध्रागतमथाश्वानां शिखो दश्च बर्हिणाम्। नेत्ररोगः कोकिलस्य ज्वरः प्रोक्तो महात्मना॥
en: The heat in the heads of elephants, the bitumen of mountains, the moss that floats on water, the slough of snakes, the sores that appear in the hoofs of bulls, the barren tracts of Earth full of saline matter, the dullness of vision of all animals, the diseases in the throats of horses, the crests appearing on the heads of peacocks, the eye-disease of the koel, each of these was named Fever by the great Mahadeva.

sn: अवीनां पित्तभेदश्च सर्वेषामिति नः श्रुतम्। शुकानामपि सर्वेषां हिक्किका प्रोच्यते ज्वरः॥ शार्दूलेष्वथ धर्मज्ञ श्रमो ज्वर इहोच्यते।
en: This is what we have heard. The liverdisease also of sheep, and the hiccup of parrots are also known as forms of Fever. To this must be added the toil that tigers suffer, for that also, O righteous king, is known as a forms of Fever.

sn: मानुषेषु तु धर्मज्ञ ज्वरो नामैष भारत॥ मरणे जन्मनि तथा मध्ये चाविशते नरम्।
en: Besides these, O Bharata, amongst men, Fever, enters all bodies at the time of birth, of death, and on other occasions.

sn: एतन्माहेश्वरं तेजो ज्वरो नाम सुदारुणः॥ नमस्यश्चैव मान्यश्च सर्वप्राणिभिरीश्वरः।
en: This Fever is known to be the dreadful power of Maheshvara. He has authority over all creatures and should, therefore, be respected and adored by all.

sn: अनेन हि समाविष्टो वृत्रो धर्मभृतां वरः॥ व्यजृभत ततः शक्रस्तस्मै वज्रमवासृजत्।
en: It was by him that Vritra, that foremost of virtuous persons, was possessed when he yawned. It was then that Shakra discharged his thunderbolt at him.

sn: प्रविश्य वज्रं वृत्रं च दारयामास भारत॥ दारितश्च स वज्रेण महायोगी महासुरः। जगाम परमं स्थानं विष्णोरमिततेजसः॥
en: The thunderbolt, entering the body of Vritra, O Bharata, divided him in two parts. Divided in two by the thunderbolt, the great Asura endued with great Yoga powers, went to the region of Vishnu of great energy.

sn: विष्णुभक्त्या हि तेनेदं जगद् व्याप्तमभूत् तदा। तस्माच्च निहतो युद्धे विष्णोः स्थानमवाप्तवान्॥
en: It was on account of his devotion to Vishnu that he had succeeded in overwhelming the whole universe. And it was owing to his devotion to Vishnu that he ascended, when killed, to the region of Vishnu.

sn: इत्येष वृत्रमाश्रित्य ज्वरस्य महतो मया। विस्तरः कथितः पुत्र किमन्यत् प्रब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Thus, O son, while describing the story of Vritra have I recited to you fully the narrative of Fever! What else shall I describe to you?

sn: इमां ज्वरोत्पत्तिमदीनमानसः पठेत् सदा यः सुसमाहितो नरः। विमुक्तरोगः स सुखी मुदा युतो लभेत कामान् स यथामनीषितान्॥
en: That man who will read this account of the origin of Fever with rapt attention and cheerful heart shall become free from disease and shall always have happiness for his lot. Filled with joy he shall have all his wishes gratified.

description: The destruction of the sacrifice of Daksha by Mahadeva
