en: When the state of Rajas is awakened, the Understanding becomes changed into Rajas. Delight, joy, gladness, happiness, and contentment, these when somehow excited, are the properties of Sattva. Heart-burning, grief, sorrow, discontentment, and unforgiveness, arising from particular causes, are the outcome of Rajas. Ignorance, attachment and mistake, carelessness, stupefaction, and terror, meanness, cheerlessness. sleep and procrastination,-these, when engendered by particular causes, are the properties of Tamas.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: तत्र यत् प्रीतिसंयुक्तं काये मनसि वा भवेत्। वर्तते सात्त्विको भाव इत्युपेक्षेत तत् तथा॥
en: Whatever state of body of mind, either joy or happiness, arises, should be considered as due to the state of Sattva.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: अथ यद् दुःखसंयुक्तमप्रीतिकरमात्मनः। प्रवृत्तं रज इत्येव तदसंरभ्य चिन्तयेत्॥
en: Whatever, again, is full of sorrow and is disagreeable to oneself, should be considered as originating from Rajas. Without undertaking any such act, one should turn his attention to it.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: अथ यन्मोहसंयुक्तं काये मनसि वा भवेत्। अप्रतय॑मविज्ञेयं तमस्तदुपधारयेत्॥
en: Whatever is full of error or stupefaction in either body or mind, and is inconceivable and mysterious, should be known as being outcome to Tamas.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: इति बुद्धिगतीः सर्वा व्याख्याता यावतीरिह। एतद् बुद्ध्वा भवेद् बुद्धः किमन्यद् बुद्धलक्षणम्॥
en: Thus have I explained to you that all things in this world live in the Understanding. By knowing this one becomes wise. What else can be the characteristics of wisdom?

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेतदन्तरं विद्धि सूक्ष्मयोः। सृजतेऽत्र गुणानेक एको न सृजते गुणान्।॥
en: Know now the difference between these two subtile things, viz., Understanding, the Soul. One of these viz., the Understanding, creates qualities. The other, i.e., the Soul, does not create them.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: पृथग्भूतौ प्रकृत्या तु सम्प्रयुक्तौ च सर्वदा। यथा मत्स्योऽद्भिरन्यः स्यात् सम्प्रयुक्तो भवेत् तथा।।३४।
en: Although they are, by nature, distinct from each other, yet they always dwell in a state of union. A fish is different from the water in which it lives, but the fish and the water exist together.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: न गुणा विदुरात्मानं स गुणान् वेद सर्वतः। परिद्रष्टा गुणानां तं संस्रष्टा मन्यते यथा।॥
en: The qualities cannot know the Soul. The Soul, however, knows them. The ignorant regard the Soul as existing in a state of union with the qualities like qualities existing with their possessors. This, however, is not the case, for the Soul is only an idle spectator of everything.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: आश्रयो नास्ति सत्त्वस्य गुणसर्गेण चेतना। सत्त्वमस्य सृजन्त्यन्ये गुणान् वेद कदाचन॥
en: The Understanding has no refuge. That which is called life originates from the effects of the qualities coming together. Others, acting as causes, create the Understanding that lives in the body. No one can apprehend the qualities in the true nature or from of existence.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: सृजते हि गुणान् सत्त्वं क्षेत्रज्ञः परिपश्यति। सम्प्रयोगस्तयोरेष सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्भुवः॥
en: The Understanding, as already said, creates the qualities. The Soul simply sees them. This union between the Understanding and the Soul is eternal.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: इन्द्रियैस्तु प्रदीपार्थं क्रियते बुद्धिरन्तरा। निश्चक्षुर्भिरजानाद्भिरिन्द्रियाणि प्रदीपवत्॥
en: The Understanding living within, perceives all things through the Senses which are by nature inanimate and unapprehending. In sooth, the senses are only like lamps.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: एवंस्वभावमेवैतत् तद् बुद्ध्वा विहरेन्नरः। अशोचन्नप्रहष्यंश्च स वै विगतमत्सरः॥
en: This is there nature. Knowing this, one should live cheerfully, without giving way to either grief or joy. Such a man is above the influence of pride.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: स्वभावसिद्धमेवैतद् यदिमान् सृजते गुणान्। उर्णनाभिर्यथा सूत्रं विज्ञेयास्तन्तुवद् गुणाः॥
en: Owing to her nature, the Understanding creates all these attributes, as a spider weaves threads. These qualities should be known as the threads the spider weaves.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: प्रध्वस्ता न निवर्तन्ते प्रवृत्तिर्नोपलभ्यते। एवमेके व्यवस्यन्ति निवृत्तिरिति चापरे॥
en: When destroyed, the qualities do not cease to exist; only, their existence becomes invisible. When, however, a thing is beyond the range of the senses, its existence (or otherwise) is understood by inference. This is the opinion of some persons. Others hold that with destruction the qualities cease to be. are

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: इतीदं हृदयग्रन्थि बुद्धिचिन्तामयं दृढम्। विमुच्य सुखमासीत विशोकश्छिन्नसंशयः॥
en: Solving this hard problem of the understanding and reflection, and removing all doubt, one should renounce sorrow and live happily.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: ताम्येयुः प्रच्युताः पृथ्वीं मोहपूर्णा नदी नराः। यथा गाधमविद्वांसो बुद्धियोगमयं तथा॥
en: As men not knowing the bottom become distressed when they fall upon this Earth which is like a river filled with the waters of stupefaction, so is that man pained who falls away from that state in which there is a union with the Understanding.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: नैव ताम्यन्ति विद्वांसः प्लवन्तः पारमम्भसः। अध्यात्मविदुषो धीरा ज्ञानं तु परमं प्लवः॥
en: Learned men, however, conversant with spiritual science and armed with fortitu never afflicted, because they can go to the other end of those waters. Indeed, Knowledge is a good vessel.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: न भवति विदुषां महद्भयं यदविदुषां सुमहद्भयं भवेत्। न हि गतिरधिकास्ति कस्यचित् सकृदुपदर्शयतीह तुल्यताम्॥
en: Men of knowledge have not to meet those fears which terrify them that are shorn of knowledge. Regarding the righteous, none of them attains to an end which is superior to that of any other person amongst them. In fact, the righteous display an equality about it.

description: The origin and nature of all spiritual Science
sn: स्तच्च दूषयति यत्पुरा कृतम्। नाप्रियं तदुभयं करोत्यसौ यच्च दूषयति यत् करोति च।।४६।
en: Regarding the man of knowledge, whatever acts have been done by him in pristine times out of Ignorance and whatever sinful acts he does, he destroys both by Knowledge as his sole means. Then, again, upon the attainment of Knowledge he ceases to commit these two evils, viz., blaming the wicked acts of others and doing any wicked acts himself under the influence of attachment.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच शोकाद् दुःखाच्च मृत्योश्च त्रसन्ते प्राणिनः सदा। उभयं नो यथा न स्यात् तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Living creatures always dread sorrow and death. Tell me, O grandfather, how the occurrence of these two may be warded off.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। नारदस्य च संवादं समङ्गस्य च भारत॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it, O Bharata, is cited the old discourse between Narada and Samanga.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: नारद उवाच उरसेव प्रणमसे बाहुभ्यां तरसीव च। सम्प्रहृष्टमना नित्यं विशोक इव लक्ष्यसे॥
en: Narada said You salute your elders by prostrating yourself on the ground till your chest touches the ground. You appear to be engaged in crossing (the river of life) with your hands. You appear to be always free from sorrow and greatly cheerful.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: उद्वेगं न हि ते किंचित् सुसूक्ष्ममपि लक्षये। नित्यतृप्त इव स्वस्थो बालवच्च विचेष्टसे॥
en: I do not see that have the least anxiety. You are always content and happy, and you appear to play happily like a child.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: समङ्ग उवाच भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च सर्वमेतत् तु मानन्। तेषां तत्त्वानि जानामि ततो न विमना ह्यहम्॥
en: Samanga said O giver of honours, I know the truth about the Past, the Present, and the Future. Hence I never become dispirited.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: उपक्रमानहं वेद पुनरेव फलोदयान्। लोके फलानि चित्राणि ततो न विमना ह्यहम्॥
en: I know also what the commencement of acts is in this world, what, of their fruits and how different are those fruits. Hence I never give way to sorrow.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: अगाधाचाप्रतिष्ठाश्च गतिमन्तश्च नारद। अन्धा जडाश्च जीवन्ति पश्यास्मानपि जीवतः॥
en: You see, O Narada, the illiterate, the destitute, the prosperous, the blind, idiots and madmen, and ourselves also, all live.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: विहितेनैव जीवन्ति अरोगाङ्गा दिवौकसः। बलवन्तोऽबलाश्चैव तस्मादस्मान् सभाजय॥
en: These live by virtue of their pristine deeds. The very gods, who are freed from diseases, exist by virtue of their pristine deeds. The strong and the weak, all, live by virtue of their pristine deeds. It is proper, therefore, you should regard us with respect.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: सहस्रिणोऽपि जीवन्ति जीवन्ति शतिनस्तथा। शाकेन चान्ये जीवन्ति पश्यास्मानपि जीवतः॥
en: The masters of thousands live. The master of hundreds also live. They who overwhelmed with sorrow live. See, we too are living.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: यदा न शोचेमहि किं नु नः स्याद् धर्मेण वा नारद कर्मणा वा। कृतान्तवश्यानि यदा सुखानि दुःखानि वा यन्न विधर्षयन्ति॥
en: When we, O Narada. do not yield to grief, what can the practice of the duties or the observance of acts do to us? And since all joys and sorrows do not terminate, they are, therefore, unable to agitate us at all. are

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: यस्मै प्राज्ञाः कथयन्ते मनुष्याः प्रज्ञामूलं हीन्द्रियाणां प्रसादः। मुह्यन्ति शोचन्ति तथेन्द्रियाणि प्रज्ञालाभो नास्ति मूढेन्द्रियस्य॥
en: Indeed, the very root of wisdom, is the freedom of the senses from mistake. It is the senses which produce error and grief. One whose senses are subject to mistake can never be said to have acquired wisdom.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: मूढस्य दर्पः स पुनर्मोह एव मूढस्य नायं न परोऽस्ति लोकः। न ह्येव दुःखानि सदा भवन्ति सुखस्य वा नित्यशो लाभ एव॥
en: That pride which a man, subject to error, entertains, is only a form of the error to which he is subject. As regards the man of error, neither this world nor the next is for him. It should be remembered that griefs do not last for ever and that happiness cannot be acquired always.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: भवात्मकं सम्परिवर्तमान न मादृशः संज्वरं जातु कुर्यात्। इष्टान् भोगान् नानुरुध्येत् सुखं वा न चिन्तयेहुःखमभ्यागतं वा॥
en: One like me would never adopt worldly life with all its changes and painful incidents. Such a one would not care for objects of enjoyments, and would not think at all of the happiness which they yield, or, indeed, of the griefs that come on.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: समाहितो न स्पृहयेत् परेषां नानागतं चाभिनन्देच्च लाभम्। न चापि हृष्येद् विपुलेऽर्थलाभे तथार्थनाशे च न वै विषीदेत्॥
en: One capable of depending on his own self, would never hanker after the possessions of others; would not think of unfair gains, would not feel overjoyed at the acquisition of even immense riches; and would not give way to sorrow at the loss of riches.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: न बान्धवा न च वित्तं न कौल्यं न च श्रुतं न च मन्त्रा न वीर्यम्। दुःखात् त्रातुं सर्व एवोत्सहन्ते परत्र शीलेन तु यान्ति शान्तिम्॥
en: Neither friends, nor riches, nor high birth, nor sacred learning, nor Mantras, nor energy, can succeed in saying one from sorrow in the next world. It is only by conduct that one can acquire happiness there.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य नायोगाद् विन्दते सुखम्। धृतिश्च दुःखत्यागश्चेत्युभयं तु सुखं नृप॥ प्रियं हि हर्षजननं हर्ष उत्सेकवर्धनः।
en: The understanding of the man who is not acquainted with Yoga can never be directed towards Liberation. One unacquainted with Yoga can never gain happiness. Patience and the determination to shake off sorrow, these two mark the setting in of happiness.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: उत्सेको नरकायैव तस्मात् तान् संत्यजाम्यहम्॥
en: Anything agreeable brings on pleasure. Pleasure induced pride. Pride, again, produces sorrow. For these reasons, I avoid all these.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: एताशोकभयोत्सेकान् मोहनान् सुखदुःखयोः। पश्यामि साक्षिवल्लोके देहस्यास्य विचेष्टनात्॥
en: Grief, Fear, Pride,—these that stupefy the heart, and also Pleasure and Pain, I see as witness since my body is endued with life and moves about.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: अर्थकामौ परित्यज्य विशोको विगतज्वरः। तृष्णामोहौ तु संत्यज्य चरामि पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: Knowing both riches and pleasure, and thirst and mistake, I wander over the Earth, freed from grief and every sort of anxiety of heart.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: न च मृत्योर्न चाधर्मान्न लोभान्न कुतश्चन) पीतामृतस्येवात्यन्तमिह वामुत्र च भयम्॥
en: Like one that has drunk nectar I have no fear, either in this world or in the next, of death, or sin, or cupidity, or anything of that sort.

description: How death and sorrow may be avoided. The discourse between Narada and Samanga
sn: एतद् ब्रह्मन् विजानामि महत् कृत्वा तपोऽव्ययम्। तेन नारद सम्प्राप्तो न मां शोकः प्रबाधते॥
en: I have gained this knowledge, O Brahmana, as the outcome of my severe and indestructible penances. Therefore, O Narada, even when it comes to me, cannot affect me.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अतत्त्वज्ञस्य शास्त्राणां सततं संशयात्मनः। अकृतव्यवसायस्य श्रेयो ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O Grandfather, what is for the behoof of one who is not acquainted with the truths of the scriptures, who is always in doubt, and who abstains from self-control and the other practices the object where of the knowledge of the Soul.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: भीष्म उवाच गुरुपूजा च सततं वृद्धानां पर्युपासनम्। श्रवणं चैव शास्त्राणां कूटस्थं श्रेय उच्यते॥
en: Bhishma said Adoring the preceptor, always reverentially attending the aged, and listening to the scriptures,-these are said to be of supreme benefit.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। मालवस्य च संवादं देवर्षे रदस्य च॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Galava and the celestial Rishi Narada.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: स्वाश्रमं समनुप्राप्तं नारदं देववर्चसम्। वीतमोहक्लमं विप्रं ज्ञानतृप्तं जितेन्द्रियः। श्रेयस्कामो यतात्मानं नारदं गालवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Once on a time Galava, desirous of securing what was for his behoof, addressed an Narada freed from error and fatigue, well-read in scriptures, pleased with knowledge a thorough master of his senses, and with soul devoted to Yoga, and said

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: यैः कश्चित् सम्मतो लोके गुणैश्च पुरुषो मुने। भवत्यनपगान् सर्वांस्तान् गुणाल्लक्षयामहे॥
en: I see, O Ascetic, those virtues by the possession of which a person is respected in the world, live permanently in you.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: भवानेवंविधोऽस्माकं संशयं छेत्तुमर्हति। अमूढश्चिरमूढानां लोकतत्त्वमजानताम्॥
en: You are freed from error and, therefore, you should remove the doubts that fill the minds of men like ourselves who are subject to error and who are unacquainted with truths of the world.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: ज्ञाने ह्येवं प्रवृत्तिः स्यात् कार्याणामविशेषतः। यत् कार्यं न व्यवस्यामस्तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: We do not know our duties, for the injunctions of the scriptures create inclination for Knowledge simultaneously with the inclination for acts. You should describe these subject to us.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: भगवन्नाश्रमाः सर्वे पृथगाचारदर्शिनः। इदं श्रेय इदं श्रेय इति सर्वे प्रबोधिताः॥
en: O illustrious one, the different modes of life approve different courses of conduct,-'This is beneficial,'_'This is beneficial',-the scriptures exhort us often in this way.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: तांस्तु विप्रस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा शास्त्रैः शास्त्राभिनन्दिनः। स्वशास्त्रैः परितुष्टाश्च श्रेयो नोपलभामहे॥
en: Seeing the followers of the four modes of life, who are thus exhorted by the scriptures and who fully approve of what the scriptures have sanctioned for them, Thus travelling in various courses, and beholding that ourselves also are equall; content with our own scriptures, we cannot understand what is truly wholesome.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: शास्त्रं यदि भवेदेकं श्रेयो व्यक्तं भवेत् तदा। शास्त्रैश्च बहुभिर्भूयः श्रेयो गुह्यं प्रवेशितम्॥
en: If the scriptures were all of one opinion, then what is truly beneficial would have become clear. On account, however, of the scriptures being multifarious, that which is truly beneficial is filled with mystery.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: एतस्मात् कारणाच्छ्रेयः कलिलं प्रतिभाति मे। ब्रवीतु भगवांस्तन्मे उपसन्नोऽस्म्यधीहि भोः॥
en: For these reasons, that which is truly beneficial, appears to as full of confusion. Do you, then, O illustrious one, describe to me the subject. I have come to you (for this). Instruct me.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: नारद उवाच आश्रमास्तात चत्वारो यथासंकल्पिताः पृथक्। तान् सर्वाननुपश्य त्वं समाश्रित्येति गालव॥
en: The modes of life four in number, O child! All of them serve the object for which they have been designed; and the duties they declare differ from one another. Learning them first from competent preceptor's, reflect upon them, OGalava.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: तेषां तेषां तथा हि त्वमाश्रमाणां ततस्ततः। नानारूपगुणोद्देशं पश्य विप्र स्थितं पृथक्॥
en: See, the merits of those modes of life, as described, are varied in their form, divergent in their matter, and contradictory in their observances.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: न यान्ति चैव ते सम्यगभिप्रेतमसंशयम्। अन्येऽपश्यंस्तथा सम्यगाश्रमाणां परां गतिम्॥
en: When seen with gross vision, all the Ashramas do not exhibit their true intent! Others, however, having subtle sight, see their highest end.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: यत् तु निश्रेयसं सम्यक् तच्चैवासंशयात्मकम्॥ अनुग्रहं च मित्राणाममित्राणां च निग्रहम्। संग्रहं च त्रिवर्गस्य श्रेय आहुर्मनीषिणः॥ निवृत्तिः कर्मणः पापात् सततं पुण्यशीलता। सद्भिश्च समुदाचारः श्रेय एतदसंशयम्॥
en: That which is truly and, without any doubt, wholesome, viz., good offices to friends, and suppression of enemies, and the acquisition of be supreme the three-fold objects of life, has been described by the wise to excellence. Abstention, from sinful deeds, righteous disposition, good conduct towards the good and pious,-these, forsooth, constitute excellence.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: मार्दवं सर्वभूतेषु व्यवहारेषु चार्जवम्। वाक् चैव मधुरा प्रोक्ता श्रेय एतदसंशयम्॥
en: Mildness towards all creatures, sincerity of conduct, and sweet words,-these, forsooth, constitute excellence.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: दैवतेभ्यः पितृभ्यश्च संविभागोऽतिथिष्वपि। असंत्यागश्च भृत्यानां श्रेय एतदसंशयम्॥
en: A just distribution of one's riches among the gods, the Pitris, and guests, and adherence to servants,—these, forsooth, constitute excellence.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: सत्यस्य वचनं श्रेयः सत्यज्ञानं तु दुष्करम्। यद् भूतहितमत्यन्तमेतत् सत्यं ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: Truthfulness of speech is excellent. The knowledge of truth is, however, every difficult of acquisition. I hold that as truth which is highly beneficial to creatures.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: अहंकारस्य च त्यागः प्रमादस्य च निग्रहः। संतोषश्चैकचर्या च कूटस्थं श्रेय उच्यते॥
en: The absence of pride, the suppression of carelessness, contentment, living by one's own self,-these form the supreme excellence.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: धर्मेण वेदाध्ययनं वेदान्तानां तथैव च। ज्ञानार्थानां च जिज्ञासा श्रेय एतदसंशयम्॥
en: The study of the Vedas, and their branches, according to the well-known rules, and all enquiries and pursuits leading to the acquisition of knowledge,-are, forsooth excellent.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: शब्दरूपरसस्पर्शान् सह गन्धेन केवलान्। नात्यर्थमुपसेवेत श्रेयसोऽर्थी कथंचन॥
en: One wishing to acquire what is excellent should never enjoy to excess sound and form and taste and touch and scent, and should not enjoy them for their sake alone.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: नक्तंचर्या दिवास्वप्नमालस्यं पैशुनं मदम्। अतियोगमयोगं च श्रेयसोऽर्थी परित्यजेत्॥
en: Walking in the night, sleep during the day, indulgence in idleness, villainy, pride, excessive indulgence and total abstention from enjoyment in objects of the senses, should be shunned by one desirous of acquiring what is excellent.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: आत्मोत्कर्षं न मार्गेत परेषां परिनिन्दया। स्वगुणैरेव मार्गेत विप्रकर्षं पृथग्जनात्॥
en: One should not seek self-elevation by putting down others. Indeed, one should by his merits only seek superiority over persons who are distinguished but never over those who are inferior.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: निर्गुणास्त्वेव भूयिष्ठमात्मसम्भाविता नराः। दोषैरन्यान् गुणवतः क्षिपन्त्यात्मगुणक्षयात्॥
en: Men having no real merit and filled with a sense of self-admiration depreciate men of real merit, by mentioning their own virtues and riches.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: अनूच्यमानास्तु पुनस्ते मन्यन्तु महाजनात्। गुणवत्तरमात्मानं स्वेन मानेन दर्पिताः॥
en: Puffed up with a sense of their own importance, these men, when none stops them, consider themselves to be superior to men of real distinction.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: अब्रुवन् कस्यचिनिन्दामात्मपूजामवर्णयन्। विपश्चिद् गुणसम्पन्नः प्राप्नोत्येव महद् यशः॥
en: One having true wisdom and real merits, wins great fame by abstaining from speaking ill of others and from indulging in self-praise.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: अब्रुवन् वाति सुरभिर्गन्धः सुमनसां शुचिः। तथैवाव्याहरन् भाति विमलो भानुरम्बरे॥
en: Flowers shed their pure and sweet odour without speaking of their own excellence. Likewise, the effulgent Sun scatters his shining rays in the sky in perfect silence.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: एवमादीनि चान्यानि परित्यक्तानि मेधया। ज्वलन्ति यशसा लोके यानि न व्याहरन्ति च॥
en: Similarly those men shine in the world with celebrity who by the help of their intelligence, renounce these and similar other faults and who do not blaze forth their own virtues.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: न लोके दीप्यते मूर्खः केवलात्मप्रशंसया। अपि चापिहितः श्वभ्रे कृतविद्यः प्रकाशते॥
en: The fool can never shine in the world by speaking out his own praise. The man, however, of real merit and learning acquires celebrity even if he be hidden in a pit.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: असदुच्चैरपि प्रोक्तः शब्दः समुपशाम्यति। दीप्यते त्वेव लोकेषु शनैरपि सुभाषितम्॥
en: Evil words, uttered with what strength of voice, die out. Good words, uttered, however softly, shine forth in the world.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: मूढानामवलिप्तानामसारं भाषितं बहु। दर्शयत्यन्तरात्मानमग्निरूपमिवांशुमान्॥
en: As the Sun shows his fiery form so the multitude of words, of little sense, that fools filled with vanity give vent to show their hearts.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: एतस्मात् कारणात् प्रज्ञां मृगयन्ते पृथग्विधाम्। प्रज्ञालाभो हि भूतानामुत्तमः प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: For these reasons men try to acquire wisdom of various sorts. It appears to me that of all acquisitions that of wisdom is the most precious.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: नापृष्टः कस्यचिद् ब्रूयान्नाप्यन्यायेन पृच्छतः। ज्ञानवानपि मेधावी जडवत् समुपाविशेत्॥
en: One should not speak until one is asked; nor should one speak when one is asked improperly. Even if endued with intelligence and knowledge, one should still sit in silence like an idiot.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: ततो वासं परीक्षेत धर्मनित्येषु साधुषु। मनुष्येषु वदान्येषु स्वधर्मनिरतेषु च।॥
en: One should seek to live among honest men given to righteousness and liberality and the observance of the duties of their own order,

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: चतुर्णां यत्र वर्णानां धर्मव्यतिकरो भवेत्। न तत्र वासं कुर्वीत श्रेयोऽर्थी वै कथंचन॥
en: One desirous of acquiring what is excellent should never live in a place where people make a confusion of their respective duties.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: निरारम्भोऽप्ययमिह यथालब्धोपजीवनः। पुण्यं पुण्येषु विमलं पापं पापेषु चाप्नुयात्॥
en: A person may be seen to live who abstains from all works and who is well-content with whatever little is gained without exertion. By living amid the righteous, one succeeds in acquiring pure virtue, Similarly one by living amid the sinful, becomes sullied with sin.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: अपामग्नेस्तथेन्दोश्च स्पर्श वेदयते यथा। तथा पश्यामहे स्पर्शमुभयोः पुण्यपापयोः॥
en: As the touch of water or fire or the rays of the moon immediately carry the sensation of cold or heat, similarly the impressions of virtue and vice create happiness or misery.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: अपश्यन्तोऽनुविषयं भुञ्जते विघसाशिनः। भुजानाश्चात्मविषयान् विषयान् विद्धि कर्मणाम्॥
en: Those who eat Vighasa eat without marking the flavours of the foods placed before them. They, however, who eat carefully marking the flavours of the duties prepared for them, should be known as persons still fettered by the bonds of action.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: यत्रागमयमानानामसत्कारेण पृच्छताम्। प्रब्रूयाद् ब्रह्मणो धर्मं त्यजेत् तं देशमात्मवान्॥
en: The pious men should leave that place where a Brahmana describes duties to disciples desirous of acquiring knowledge, as based on reasons, of the Soul, but who do not reverentially enquire after such knowledge.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: शिष्योपाध्यायिकावृत्तिर्यत्र स्यात् सुसमाहिता। यथावच्छास्त्रसम्पन्ना कस्तं देशं परित्यजेत्॥
en: Who, however, will leave that place where exists fully that conduct between disciples and preceptors which is consistent with what has been sanctioned by the scriptures?

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: आकाशस्था ध्रुवं यत्र दोषं ब्रूयुर्विपश्चिताम्। आत्मपूजाभिकामो वै को वसेत् तत्र पण्डितः॥
en: What learned man who cares for his respect will live there where people talk about the faults of the learned even when such have no foundations to stand upon?

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: यत्र संलोडिता लुब्धैः प्रायशो धर्मसेतवः। प्रदीप्तमिव चैलान्तं कस्तं देशं न संत्यजेत्॥
en: Who is there that will not leave that place, like a garment whose end has caught fire, where covetous men tries to break down the limits of virtue?

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: यत्र धर्ममनाशङ्काश्चरेयुर्वीतमत्सराः। भवेत् तत्र वसेच्चैव पुण्यशीलेषु साधुषु॥
en: One should remain and live in that place, among good men of pious disposition, where persons possessed of humility are engaged in fearlessly practising the duties of religion.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: धर्ममर्थनिमित्तं च चरेयुर्यत्र मानवाः। न ताननुवसेज्जातु ते हि पापकृतो जनाः॥
en: One should not dwell there where men practise the duties of religion for the sake of wealth and other worldly purposes, for the people of that place are all to be considered as sinful.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: कर्मणा यत्र पापेन वर्तन्ते जीवितेप्सवः। व्यवधावेत् ततस्तूर्णं ससर्पाच्छरणादिव॥
en: One should fly away quickly from that place, as if from a room which there is a snake, where the inhabitants, desirous of acquiring the means of life, are engaged in the practice of sinful deeds.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: येन खट्वां समारूढः कर्मणानुशयी भवेत्। आदितस्तन्न कर्तव्यमिच्छता भवमात्मनः॥
en: One desirous of what is wholesome, should, from the beginning, avoid that act for which one becomes stretched, as it were, on a bed of thorns and for which one becomes invested with the desires born of the pristine deeds.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: यत्र राजा च राज्ञश्च पुरुषाः प्रत्यनन्तराः। कुटुम्बिनामग्रभुजस्त्यजेत् तद् राष्ट्रमात्मवान्।॥
en: The pious man should leave that kingdom where the king and the king's officers exercise equal authority and where people eat before feeding their relatives.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: श्रोत्रियास्त्वग्रभोक्तारो धर्मनित्याः सनातनाः। याजनाध्यापने युक्ता यत्र तद् राष्ट्रमावसेत्॥
en: One should live in that country where Brahmanas having a knowledge of the scriptures are fed first; where they always practise religious duties, and where they are engaged in teaching disciples and officiating at the sacrifices of others.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: स्वाहास्वधावषट्कारा यत्र सम्यगनुष्ठिताः। अजस्रं चैव वर्तन्ते वसेत् तत्राविचारयन्॥
en: One should unhesitatingly live in that country where the sounds Svaha, Svadha, and Vashat are duly and continuously uttered.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: अशुचीन् यत्र पश्येत ब्राह्मणान् वृत्तिकर्शितान्। त्यजेत् तद् राष्ट्रमासन्नमुपसृष्टमिवामिषम्॥
en: One should leave that kingdom, like poisoned meat, where one sees Brahmanas compelled to follow unholy practices, by want of the means of life.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: प्रीयमाणा नरा यत्र प्रयच्छेयुरयाचिताः। स्वस्थचित्तो वसेत् तत्र कृतकृत्य इवात्मवान्॥
en: With a contented heart and considering all his wishes as already gratified, a pious man should live in that country whose denizens gladly give away before even they are asked.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: दण्डो यत्राविनीतेषु सत्कारश्च कृतात्मसु। चरेत् तत्र वसेच्चेव पुण्यशीलेषु साधुषु॥
en: One should live and move about, among good men devoted to pious acts in that country where the wicked are punished, and where respect and good offices are done to those who are of controlled and purified souls.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: उपसृष्टेषु दान्तेषु दुराचारेषु साधुषु। अविनीतेषु लुब्धेषु सुमहद् दण्डधारणम्॥ यत्र राजा धर्मनित्यो राज्यं धर्मेण पालयेत्। अपास्य कामान् कामेशो वसेत् तत्राविचारयन्॥
en: One should unhesitatingly live in that country whose king is given to virtue and which the king rules virtuously, casting off desires and possessed of prosperity, and where severe punishment is inflicted on those who subject self-controlled to the consequences of their anger, on those who treat men treat wickedly the righteous, on those who commit acts of violence, and on the covetious.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: यथाशीला हि राजानः सर्वान् विषयवासिनः। श्रेयसा योजयत्याशु श्रेयसि प्रत्युपस्थिते॥
en: Kings endued with such a disposition, secure the prosperity of those who live in their kingdoms when prosperity is on the point of leaving them.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: पृच्छतस्ते मया तात श्रेय एतदुदाहृतम्। न हि शक्यं प्रधानेन श्रेयः संख्यातुमात्मनः॥
en: I have thus told you, O son, in answer to you enquiry, what is beneficial or excellent. No one can describe, on account of its exceedingly high character, what is beneficial or excellent for the Soul.

description: What tends to the good of one who is not acquainted with Scriptures
sn: एवं प्रवर्तमानस्य वृत्तिं प्राणिहितात्मनः। तपसैवेह बहुलं श्रेयो व्यक्तं भविष्यति॥
en: Many and high will the excellences be, through the performance of the duties laid down for his, of the man who for earning his livelihood during the time of his stay in this world, acts in the way indicated above and who devotes his soul to the well-being of creatures.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं नु युक्तः पृथिवीं चरेदस्मद्विधो नृपः। नित्यं कैश्च गुणैर्युक्तः संगपाशाद् विमुच्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said How, O grandfather, should a king like us act in this world, keeping in view the great object of acquisition? What attributes, again, should he always possess so that he may be liberated from attachments.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम्। अरिष्टनेमिना प्रोक्तं सगरायानुपृच्छते॥
en: Bhishma said-I shall in this connection recite to you the old narrative that was uttered by Arishtanemi to Sagara who had sought his advice.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: सगर उवाच किं श्रेयः परमं ब्रह्मन् कृत्वेह सुखमश्नुते। कथं न शोचेन्न क्षुभ्येदेतदिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: Sagara said What is that good, O Brahmana, by doing which one may enjoy happiness here? How, indeed, may one avoid grief and agitation? I wish to know all this.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्तस्तदा तार्क्ष्यः सर्वशास्त्रविदां वरः। विबुध्य सम्पदं चाग्र्यां सद्वाक्यमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by Sagara, Arishtanemi of Tarkshya's race, conversant with all the scriptures, considering the enquiries ad deserving fully of his instructions, said these words:सुखं मोक्षसुखं लोके न च मूढोऽवगच्छति।

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: प्रसक्तः पुत्रपशुषु धनधान्यसमाकुलः॥
en: The happiness of Liberation is true happiness in the world. The ignorant man knows is not, attached, as he is, to children and animals and possessed of riches and corn.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: सक्तबुद्धिरशान्तात्मा न शक्यं तच्चिकित्सितुम्। स्नेहपाशसितो मूढो न स मोक्षाय कल्पते॥
en: The understanding that is attached to worldly objects and the longing mind baffle all skilful treatment. The ignorant man who is bound is the fetters of affection cannot acquire Liberation.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: स्नेहजानिह ते पाशान् वक्ष्यामि शृणु तान् मम। सकर्णकेन शिरसा शक्याः श्रोतुं विजानता॥
en: I shall now describe to you all the fetters which originate from the affections. Hear them with attention. Indeed, they can be heard with profit by one who is endued with knowledge.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: सम्भाव्य पुत्रान् कालेन यौवनस्थान् विवेश्य च। समर्थान् जीवने ज्ञात्वा मुक्तश्चर यथासुखम्॥
en: Having procreated children in due time and married them when they become young men, and having found them to be competent for earning their livelihood, do you free youself from all attachments and rove about happily.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: भार्यां पुत्रवती वृद्धां लालितां पुत्रवत्सलाम्। ज्ञात्वा प्रजहि कालेन परार्थमनुदृश्य च॥
en: When you find you dear consort grown old in years and attached to the son she has given birth to, do you leave her in time, keeping in view the highest object of acquisition.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: सापत्यो निरपत्यो वा मुक्तश्चर यथासुखम्। इन्द्रियैरिन्द्रियार्थांस्त्वमनुभूय यथाविधि॥
en: Whether you get a son or not, having, during the first years of your life, duly enjoyed with your senses the objects thereof, liberate yourself from attachments and rove about in happiness.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: कृतकौतूहलस्तेषु मुक्तश्चर यथासुखम्। उपपत्त्योपलब्धेषु लोकेषु च समो भव॥
en: Having satisfied the senses with their objects, you should suppress the desire of further indulging them. Liberating yourself from attachments, you should rove in happiness, contenting yourself with what is got without exertion and previous calculation, and loO king impartially towards all creatures and objects.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: एष तावत् समासेन तव संकीर्तितो मया। मोक्षार्थो विस्तरेणाथ भूयो वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु॥
en: Thus, O son, have I told you briefly. Hear me now, for I shall tell you fully, the desirability of the acquisition of Liberation.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: मुक्ता वीतभया लोके चरन्ति सुखिनो नराः। सक्तभावा विनश्यन्ति नरास्तत्र न संशयः॥
en: Those persons who live in this world shorn of attachments and fear, succeed in acquiring happiness. Those persons, however, who are attached to worldly objects, forsooth, meet with destruction,

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: आहारसंचयाश्चैव तथा कीटपिपीलिकाः। असक्ताः सुखिनो लोके सक्ताश्चैव विनाशिनः॥
en: Worms and ants are engaged in the acquisition of food and are seen to die in the search. They who are shorn or attachments are happy, while they who are attached to worldly objects meet with destruction.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: स्वजने न च ते चिन्ता कर्तव्या मोक्षबुद्धिना। इमे मया विनाभूता भविष्यन्ति कथं त्विति॥
en: If you wish to acquire Liberation you should never place your thoughts on your relatives, thinking, How shall these live without me?

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: स्वयमुत्पद्यते जन्तुः स्वयमेव विवर्धते। सुखदुःखे तथा मृत्यु स्वयमेवाधिगच्छति॥
en: A living creature takes birth by himself, and, grow by himself, and acquires happiness and misery, and death by himself.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: भोजनाच्छादने चैव मात्रा पित्रा च संग्रहम्। स्वकृतेनाधिगच्छन्ति लोके नास्त्यकृतं पुरा॥
en: In this world people enjoy and obtain good and cloth and other acquisitions acquired by either their parents or themselves. This is the result of the acts of pristine lives, for nothing can be had in this life which is not the result of the past.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: धात्रा विहितभक्ष्याणि सर्वभूतानि मेदिनीम्। लोके विपरिधावन्ति रक्षितानि स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: All creatures live on the Earth, protected by their own acts, and acquiring their food as the result of what is ordained by Him who allots the fruits of acts.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: स्वयं मृत्पिण्डभूतस्य परतन्त्रस्य सर्वदा। को हेतुः स्वजनं षोष्टुं रक्षितुं वादृढात्मनः॥
en: A man is but a lump of clay, and always depends completely on their forces. A man, being thus so weak, what rational motive can one have for protecting and feeding his relatives?

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: स्वजनं हि यदा मृत्युर्हन्त्येव तव पश्यतः। कृतेऽपि यत्ने महति तत्र बोद्धव्यमात्मना॥
en: When your relatives are carried away by Death in your very presence and despite you utmost efforts to save them, that circumstance alone should awaken you.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: जीवन्तमपि चैवैनं भरणे रक्षणे तथा। असमाप्ते परित्यज्य पश्चादपि मरिष्यसि॥
en: In the very life-time of your relatives and before own duty is completed of feeding and protecting them, you may yourself die and leave them.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: यदा मृतं च स्वजनं न ज्ञास्यसि कदाचन। सुखितं दुःखितं वापि ननु बोद्धव्यमात्मना॥
en: After your relatives have been carried away from this world by death, you cannot know what becomes of them there,—that is, whether they are happy or miserable. This fact ought to awaken you.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: मृते वा त्वयि जीवे वा यदा भोक्ष्यति वै जनः। स्वकृतं ननु बुद्ध्वैवं कर्तव्यं हितमात्मनः॥
en: When on account of the fruits of their own acts your relatives can maintain themselves in this world whether you live or die, thinking of this you should do what is for your own wellbeing.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: एवं विजानल्लोकेऽस्मिन् कः कस्येत्यभिनिश्चितः। मोक्षे निवेशय मनो भूयश्चाप्युपधारय॥
en: When such is the case, who is the world is to be considered as whose? Do you, therefore, think of acquiring Liberation. Hear now what more I shall say to you.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: क्षुत्पिपासादयो भावा जिता यस्येह देहिनः। क्रोधोलोभस्तथा मोहः सत्त्वन् मुक्त एव सः॥
en: That man of firm Soul, forsooth, liberated who has conquered hunger and thirst and such other states of the body, as also anger and cupidity and error.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: द्यूते पाने तथा स्त्रीषु मृगयायां च यो नरः। न प्रमाद्यति सम्मोहात् सततं मुक्त एव सः॥
en: That man is always liberated who does not forget himself, through folly, by indulging in gambling and drinking and concubinage and the chase.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: दिवसे दिवसे नाम रात्रौ रात्रौ पुमान् सदा। भोक्तव्यमिति यः खिन्नो दोषबुद्धिः स उच्यते॥
en: That man who is really affected by sorrow for being compelled to eat every day and every night for maintaining life, is said to be congnisant of the faults of life.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: आत्मभावं तथा स्त्रीषु मुक्तमेव पुनः पुनः। यः पश्यति सदा युक्तो यथावन्मुक्त एव सः॥
en: Once who, as the outcome of careful reflection, considers his repeated births as due to sexual congress with women, is held to be freed from attachments.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: सम्भवं च विनाशं च भूताना चेष्टितं तथा। यस्तत्त्वतो विजानाति लोकेऽस्मिन् मुक्त एव सः॥
en: That man is certainly Liberated who knows truly the nature of the birth, the destruction, and the acts of living creatures.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: प्रस्थं वाहसहस्रेषु यात्रार्थं चैव कोटिषु। प्रासादे मञ्चकं स्थानं यः पश्यति स मुच्यते॥
en: That man becomes certainly freed who seeks only a handful of corn, for the support of life, from amidst millions upon millions of carts loaded with gain, and who finds no difference between a shad of bamboo and reeds and a palace.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: मृत्युनाभ्याहतं लोकं व्याधिभिश्चोपपीडितम्। अवृत्तिकर्शितं चैव यः पश्यति स मुच्यते॥
en: That man becomes certainly freed who seeks the world as afflicted by death, disease and famine.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: यः पश्यति स संतुष्टो न पश्यंश्च विहन्यते। यश्चाप्यल्पेन संतुष्टो लोकेऽस्मिन् मुक्त एव सः॥
en: Indeed, one who sees the world to consist of eaters and edibles, and who is never affected by pleasure and pain begotten by illusion, is considered as liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: अग्नीषोमाविदं सर्वमिति यश्चानुपश्यति। न च संस्पृश्यते भावैरद्भुतैर्मुक्त एव सः॥
en: One, who sees all the objects in the form of Fire and Soma, he is never affected by wonderful pleasures and is considered as liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: पर्यङ्कशय्या भूमिश्च समाने यस्य देहिनः। शालयश्च कदन्नं च यस्य स्यान्मुक्त एव सः॥
en: That man who considers a soft bed on a fine bed-stead and the hard ground as equal, and who considers good shali rice and hard thick rice as equal, is liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: क्षौमं च कुशचीरं च कौशेयं वल्कलानि च। आविकं चर्म च समं यस्य स्यान्मुक्त एव सः॥
en: That man who considers linen and cloth made of grass as equal, and who considers cloth of silk and barks of trees as the same, and who sees no difference between cleans sheepskin and unclean leather, is liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: पञ्चभूतसमुद्भूतं लोकं यश्चानुपश्यति। तथा च वर्तते दृष्ट्वा लोकेऽस्मिन् मुक्त एव सः॥
en: That man who considers this world as the result of the combination of the five principal elements, and who acts in this world, keeping this notion foremost, is liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: सुखदुःखे समे यस्य लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ। इच्छाद्वेषौ भयोद्वेगौ सर्वथा मुक्त एव सः॥
en: That man who considers pleasure and pain in the same light and gain and loss as equal, and victory and defeat as the same to whom like and dislike are the same, and who is unmoved under fear and anxiety, is perfectly liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: रक्तमूत्रपुरीषाणां दोषाणां संचयांस्तथा। शरीरं दोषबहुलं दृष्ट्वा चैव विमुच्यते॥
en: That man who considers his body which had so many inperfections, to be only a mass of blood, urine and excreta, as also of disorders and diseases, is liberated,

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: वलीपलितसंयोगे कायँ वैवर्ण्यमेव च। कुब्जभावं च जरया यः पश्यति स मुच्यते॥
en: That man becomes liberated who always recollects that this body, when possessed by decrepitude, becomes assailed by wrinkless and white hairs and leanness and paleness of complexion and a bending of the form.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: पुंस्त्वोपघातं कालेन दर्शनोपरमं तथा। बाधिर्यं प्राणमन्दत्वं यः पश्यति स मुच्यते॥
en: That man who considers his body as subject to loss of power, weakness of sight, deafness, and loss of strength, is liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: गतानृषींस्तथा देवानसुरांश्च तथा गतान्। लोकादस्मात् परं लोकं यः पश्यति स मुच्यते॥
en: That man who knows that the very Rishis, the gods, and the Asuras are beings that have to depart form their respective spheres to other regions, is liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: प्रभावैरन्वितास्तैस्तैः पार्थिवेन्द्राः सहस्रशः। ये गताः पृथिवींत्यत्वा इति ज्ञात्वा विमुच्यते॥
en: That man who knows that thousands of kings possessed of even great power have dies, succeeds in becoming liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: अर्थांश्च दुर्लभाँल्लोके क्लेशांश्च सुलभांस्तथा। दुःखं चैव कुटुम्बार्थे यः पश्यति स मुच्यते॥
en: That man who knows that in this world the acquisition of objects is always hard, that pain of profuse, and that the maintenance of relative is always painful becomes liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: अपत्यानां च वैगुण्यं जनं विगुणमेव च। पश्यन् भूयिष्ठशो लोके को मोक्षं नाभिपूजयेत्॥
en: Seeing the abundant faults of children and of other men, who is there that would worship Liberation?

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: शास्त्राल्लोकाच्च यो बुद्धः सर्वं पश्यति मानवः। असारमिव मानुष्यं सर्वथा मुक्त एव सः॥
en: That man who, enlightened by the scriptures and the experience of the world sees every human concern in this world to be unreal, becomes liberated.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा मम वचो भवांश्चरतु मुक्तवत्। गार्हस्थ्ये यदि वा मोक्षे कृता बुद्धिरविक्लवा॥
en: Remembering these words of mine, do you act like one who has become liberated, whether it is a life of domesticity that you would lead or pursue Liberation without allowing your understanding to be confounded.

description: How grief may be avoided and happiness enjoyed. The conversation between Sagara and Arishthanimi
sn: तत् तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सम्यक् स पृथिवीपतिः। मोक्षजैश्च गुणैर्युक्तः पालयामास च प्रजाः॥
en: Hearing these words of his with attention, king Sagara, acquired those virtues which yield liberation and continued, with their help to rule his subjects.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच तिष्ठते मे सदा तात कौतूहलमिदं हृदि। तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि त्वत्तः कुरुपितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said This curiosity, O sire, is always living in my mind. O grandfather to the Kurus, I wish to hear everything about it form you!

sn: कथं देवर्षिरुशना सदा काव्यो महामतिः। असुराणां प्रियकरः सुराणामप्रिये रतः॥
en: Why was the celestial Rishi, the great Ushanas, called also Kavi, engaged in doing what was agreeable to the Asuras and disagreeable to the gods.

sn: वर्धयामास तेजश्च किमर्थममितौजसाम्। नित्यं वैरनिबद्धाश्च दानवाः सुरसत्तमैः॥
en: Why was he engaged in diminishing the energy of the gods? Why the Danavas always fought with the foremost of the gods.

sn: कथं चाप्युशना प्राप शुक्रत्वममरद्युतिः। ऋद्धिं च स कथं प्राप्तः सर्वमेतद् वदस्व मे॥
en: Endued with the effulgence of an immortal, why did Ushanas obtain the name of Shukra? How also did he acquire such superior excellence? Tell me all about these things.

sn: न याति च स तेजस्वी मध्येन नभसः कथम्। एतदिच्छामि विज्ञातुं निखिलेन पितामह॥
en: Though highly energetic, why can he not go to the centre of the sky? I wish, O grandfather, to learn everything about all these matters.

sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु राजन्नवहितः सर्वमेतद् यथातथम्। यथामति यथा चैतच्छुतपूर्वं मयानघ॥
en: Bhishma said Listen, O king, attentively to all this as it actually took place, O sinless one, I shall describe these masters to you as I have heard and understood them.

sn: एष भार्गवदायादो मुनिर्मान्यो दृढव्रतः। सुराणां विप्रियकरो निमित्ते कारणात्मके॥
en: O firm vows and respected by all, Ushanas, that descendant of Bhrigu's race, became engaged in doing what was disagreeable to the gods for some good cause.

sn: इन्द्रोऽथ धनदो राजा यक्षरक्षोऽधियः सदा। प्रभविष्णुश्च कोशस्य जगतश्च तथा प्रभुः॥
en: The royal Kuvera, the chief of the Yakshas and the Rakshas, is the lord of the wealth of Indra, that master of the universe.

sn: तस्यात्मानमथाविश्य योगसिद्धो महामुनिः। रुद्ध्वा धनपतिं देवं योगेन हतवान् वसु॥
en: The great ascetic Ushanas, crowned with Yoga-success, entered the person of Kuvera, and depriving the lord of wealth of his liberty by means of Yoga, robbed him of all his riches.

sn: हृते धने ततः शर्म न लेभे धनदस्तथा। आपन्नमन्युः संविग्नः सोऽभ्यगात् सुरसत्तमम्॥
en: Seeing his riches taken away from him, the lord of wealth became highly displeased. Filled anxiety, and his anger also being worked up, he want to that foremost of god, viz., Mahadeva.

sn: निवेदयामास तदा शिवायामिततेजसे। देवश्रेष्ठाय रुद्राय सौम्याय बहुरूपिणे॥
en: Kuvera reported the matter to Shiva of great energy, that first of gods, fierce and amiable, and endued with various forms.

sn: योगात्मकेनोशनसा रुद्ध्वा मम हृतं वसु। योगेनात्मगतं कृत्वा निःसृतश्च महातपाः॥
en: He said Ushanas, having spiritualised himself by Yoga, entered my body and depriving myself of liberty, has taken away all my riches. Having by Yoga entered my body he has again left it.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा ततः क्रुद्धो महायोगी महेश्वरः। संरक्तनयनो राजशूलमादाय तस्थिवान्॥
en: Hearing these words, Maheshvara of Supreme Yoga-powers became filled with ire. His eyes, O king, became blood-red, and taking up his lance he waited.

sn: क्वासौ क्वासाविति प्राह गृहीत्वा परमायुधम्। उशना दूरतस्तस्य बभौ ज्ञात्वा चिकीर्षितम्॥
en: Having taken up that foremost of weapons, the great god began to say, Where is he? Where is he?—Meanwhile, Ushanas, having learnt the purpose of Mahadeva from a distance, waited silently.

sn: स महायोगिनो बुद्ध्वा तं रोषं वै महात्मनः। गतिमागमनं वेत्ति स्थानं चैव ततः प्रभुः॥
en: Having learnt the fact of the anger of the great Maheshvara of superior Yoga-power, the powerful Ushanas began to think as to whether he should go to Maheshvara or fly away or remain where he was.

sn: संचिन्त्योग्रेण तपसा महात्मानं महेश्वरम्। उशना योगसिद्धात्मा शूलाग्रे प्रत्यदृश्यत्॥
en: Thinking, with the help of his severe penances, of the great Mahadeva, Ushanas, of soul crowned with Yoga-success, put himself on the point of Mahadeva's lance.

sn: विज्ञातरूपः स तदा तप:सिद्धोऽथ धन्विना। ज्ञात्वा शूलं च देवेशः पाणिना समनामयत्॥
en: Understanding that Ushanas, whose penances had been crowned with success and who had converted himself into the from of pure Knowledge, was staying at the point of his lance, the bow-armed Rudra, bent that weapon with his hand.

sn: आनतेनाथ शूलेन पाणिनामिततेजसा। पिनाकमिति चोवाच शूलमुग्रायुधः प्रभुः॥
en: When the fierce-armed and powerful Mahadeva of great energy had thus bent his lance that weapon came to be called from that time by the name of Pinaka.

sn: पाणिमध्यगतं दृष्ट्वा भार्गवं तमुमापतिः। आस्यं विवृत्य ककुदी पाणिना प्राक्षिपच्छनैः॥
en: The lord of Uma, seeing Bhargava thus brought upon the palm of his hand, opened his mouth. The chief of the gods then threw Bhargava into his mouth and swallowed him up.

sn: स तु प्रविष्ट उशना कोष्ठं माहेश्वरं प्रभुः। व्यचरच्चापि तत्रासौ महात्मा भृगुनन्दनः॥
en: The powerful and great Ushanas of Bhrigu's race, entering the stomach of Maheshvara, began to wander there.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किमर्थं व्यचरद् राजनुशना तस्य धीमतः। जठरे देवदेवस्य किं चाकार्षीन्माहद्युतिः॥
en: Yudhishthira said How, O king, could Ushanas wander within the stomach of that foremost (god) of superior intelligence? What also did that great god do while the Brahmana was within his stomach.

sn: भीष्म उवाच पुरा सोऽन्तर्जलगताः स्थाणुभूतो महाव्रतः। वर्षाणामभवद् राजन् प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च॥
en: Bhishma said Then Mahadeva of severe vows, entered the water and remained there like an immovable wooden stake, O king, for millions of years.

sn: उदतिष्ठत् तपस्तप्त्वा दुश्चरं च महाह्रदात्। ततो देवातिदेवस्तं ब्रह्मा वै समसर्पत॥ तपोवृद्धिमपृच्छच्च कुशलं चैवमव्ययः। तपः सुचीर्णमिति च प्रोवाच वृषभध्वजः॥
en: His Yoga penances of the austerest type having been over, he rose from the great lake. Then that prime god of the gods, viz., the eternal Brahman, approached him, and enquired after the progress of his penances and well-being. The god having the bull for his emblem answered, saying,—My penances have been well practised.

sn: तत्संयोगेन वृद्धिं चाप्यपश्यत् स तु शंकरः। महामतिरचिन्त्यात्मा सत्यधर्मरतः सदा॥
en: Of inconceivable soul, endued with great intelligence, and ever devoted to the religion of truth, Shankara saw that Ushanas within his stomach had become greater on account of those penances of his.

sn: स तेनाढ्यो महायोगी तपसा च धनेन च। व्यराजत महाराज त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान्॥
en: That foremost of Yogins. (viz., Ushanas), rich with that wealth of penances and the wealth (of Kuvera), shone brightly in the three worlds, gifted with great energy.

sn: ततः पिनाकी योगात्मा ध्यानयोगं समाविशत्। उशना तु समद्विग्नो निलिल्ये जठरे ततः॥
en: After this, Mahadeva armed with Pinaka, that soul of Yoga, once more began to roam within the stomach of the great god.

sn: तुष्टाव च महायोगी देवं तत्रस्थ एव च। नि:सारं काङ्क्षमाणः स तेन स्म प्रतिहन्यते॥
en: The great ascetic began to sing the praises of the god from where he was desirous of finding on outlet for escape. But, having stopped all his outlets, Rudra, prevented him from coming out.

sn: उशना तु तथोवाच जठरस्थो महामुनिः। प्रसादं मे कुरुष्वेति पुनः पुनररिंदम॥
en: The great ascetic Ushanas, however, O chastiser of enemies, from within Mahadeva's stomach repeatedly addressed the god, saying,-Show me your kindness.

sn: तमुवाच महादेवो गच्छ शिश्नेन मोक्षणम्। इति सर्वाणि स्रोतांसि रुद्ध्वा त्रिदशपुङ्गवः॥
en: To him Mahadeva said,-Go out through my urethra!-He had closed up all other outlets of his body.

sn: अपश्यमानस्तद् द्वारं सर्वतः पिहितो मुनिः। पर्यक्रामद् उह्यमान इतश्चेतश्च तेजसा॥
en: Closed on all sides and unable to find out the outlet pointed out, the asetic began to roam hither and thither. burning all the while with Mahadeva's energy.

sn: स वै निष्क्रम्य शिश्नेन शुक्रत्वमभिपेदिवान्। कार्येण तेन नभसो नाध्यगच्छत मध्यतः॥
en: At last he found the outlet and came out through it. On account of this incident he passed by the name of Shukra, and it is for this he also became unable to attain the central point of the sky.

sn: विनिष्कान्तं तु तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा। भवो रोषसमाविष्टः शूलोद्यतकरः स्थितः॥
en: Seeing him come out of his stomach and shining bringhtly with energy, Bhava filled with anger, stood with lance uplifted in his hand.

sn: अवारयत तं देवी क्रुद्धं पशुपति पतिम्। पुत्रत्वमगमद् देव्या वारिते शंकरे च सः॥
en: The goddess Uma then interposed and forbade the angry lord of all creatures, viz., her consort, to kill the Brahmana. And on account of Uma's having thus prevented her lord from fulfilling his purpose, the ascetic Ushanas became the son of the goddess.

sn: देव्युवाच हिंसनीयस्त्वया नैव मम पुत्रत्वमागतः। न हि देवोदरात् कश्चिनिःसृतो नाशमृच्छति॥
en: The goddess said-This Brahmana no longer deserves to be killed by you. He has become my son. O god, one who comes out of your stomach does not deserve to be killed by you.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः प्रीतो भवो देव्याः प्रहसंश्चेदमब्रवीत्। गच्छत्वेष यथाकाममिति राजन् पुनः पुनः॥
en: Bhishma said Pacified by these words of his wife, Bhava smiled and said repeatedly these words, O king, viz.,-Let this one go wherever he likes.

sn: ततः प्रणम्य वरदं देवं देवीमुमां तथा। उशना प्राप तद्धीमान् गतिमिष्टां महामुनिः॥
en: Bowing to the boon-giving Mahadeva and also to his wife the goddess Uma, the great ascetic Ushanas, gifted with superior intelligence, proceeded to the place he chose.

sn: एतत् ते कथितं तात भार्गवस्य महात्मनः। चरितं भरतश्रेष्ठ यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: I have thus described to you, O chief of the Bharatas, the story of the great Bhargava about which you had asked me.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अतः परं महाबाहो यच्छ्रेयस्तद् वदस्व मे। न तृप्याम्यमृतस्येव वचसस्ते पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said O you of great arms, tell me, after this, what is beneficial for us, O grandfather, I am never satiated with your words which seem to me like ambrosia.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: किं कर्म पुरुषः कृत्वा शुभं पुरुषसत्तम। श्रेयः परमवाप्नोति प्रेत्य चेह च तद् वद॥
en: What are those good acts, O best of men, by doing which a man succeeds in obtaining what is for his greatest good, both in the world, and in the next, O giver of boons.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि यथापूर्वं महायशाः। पराशरं महात्मानं पप्रच्छ जनको नृपः॥
en: Bhishma said-Regarding it I shall describe to you what the celebrated king Janaka had enquired, in days of great Parashara.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: किं श्रेयः सर्वभूतानामस्मिल्लोके परत्र चा यद् भवेत् प्रतिपत्तव्यं तद् भवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे॥
en: What is beneficial for all creatures both in this world and the next? Do you tell me what should be known by all about it.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: ततः स तपसा युक्तः सर्वधर्मविधानवित्। नृपायानुग्रहमना मुनिर्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus accosted Parashara, endued with great ascetic merit and conversant with the ordinances of every religion, said these words, desirous of favouring the king.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: पराशर उवाच धर्म एव कृतः श्रेयानिह लोके परत्र च। तस्माद्धि परमं नास्ति यथा प्राहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: Parashara said Virtue acquired by acts is of supreme benefit both in this world and the next. The sages of old have said that there is nothing higher than virtue.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: प्रतिपद्य नरो धर्म स्वर्गलोके महीयते। धर्मात्मकः कर्मविधिर्देहिनां नृपसत्तम॥ तस्मिन्नाश्रमिणः सन्तः स्वकर्माणीह कुर्वते॥
en: By accomplishing the sacred duties a man becomes honoured in heaven. The virtue, again, of embodied creatures, O best of kings, consists in the ordinances on the subject of acts. All good men belonging to the several modes of life, fixing their faith on virtue, perform their respective duties.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: चतुर्विधा हि लोकेऽस्मिन् यात्रा तात विधीयते। मा यत्रावतिष्ठन्ते सा च कामात् प्रवर्तते॥
en: Four modes of life, O child, have been laid down in this world. Wherever men live the means of maintenance come to them of themselves.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: सुकृतासुकृतं कर्म निषेव्य विविधैः क्रमैः। दशार्धप्रविभक्तानां भूतानां बहुधा गतिः॥
en: Doing by different means virtuous or sinful acts, living creatures, when dissolved into their five constituent elements, attain to various ends.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: सौवर्ण राजतं चाप यथा भाण्डं निषिच्यते। तथा निषिच्यते जन्तुः पूर्वकर्मवशानुगः॥
en: As vessels of white brass, when steeped in liquified gold or silver, get the hue of these metals, so a living creature, who is entirely dependant upon the acts of his pristine lives, takes his colour from the nature of those acts.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: नाबीजाज्जायते किंचिन्नाकृत्वा सुखमेधते। सुकृतैर्विन्दते सौख्यं प्राप्य देहक्षयं नरः॥
en: Nothing can originate without a seed. No one can acquire happiness without having performed acts capable of bringing on happiness. When one's body is dissolved, he succeeds in acquiring happiness only on account of the good acts of pristine lives.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: दैवं तात न पश्यामि नास्ति दैवस्य साधनम्। स्वभावतो हि संसिद्धा देवगन्धर्वदानवाः॥
en: The sceptic argues, O child, saying,-I do not see that anything in this world is the result of destiny or the virtuous and sinful deeds of pristine lives. Inference cannot settle the existence or operation of destiny. The gods, the Gandharvas and the Danavas have become what they are on account of their own nature.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: प्रेत्य जातिकृतं कर्म न स्मरन्ति सदा जनाः। ते वै तस्य फलप्राप्तौ कर्म चापि चतुर्विधम्॥
en: People never recollect in their next lives the acts done by them in pristine ones. For explaining the acquisition of fruits in any particular life people seldom name the four sorts of acts alleged to have been performed in pristine lives.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: लोकयात्राश्रयश्चैव शब्दो वेदाश्रयः कृतः। शान्त्यर्थं मनसस्तात नैतद् वृद्धानुशासनम्॥
en: The declarations have the Vedas for their authority have been made for guiding the conduct of men in his world, and for tranquillizing the minds of men. These, O child, cannot represent the saying of truly wise men.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: चक्षुषा मनसा वाचा कर्मणा च चतुर्विधम्। कुरुते यादृशं कर्म तादृशं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: This opinion is wrong. In sooth, one acquires the fruits of whatever among the four sorts of acts one does with the eye, the mind, the tongue, and muscles.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: निरन्तरं च मिश्रं च लभते कर्म पार्थिव। कल्याणं यदि वा पापं न तु नाशोऽस्य विद्यते॥
en: As the fruit of his acts, O king, a person, sometimes acquires happiness wholly, sometimes misery in the same way, and sometimes happiness and misery united together. Whether virtuous or sinful, acts are never destroyed.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: कदाचित् सुकृतं तात कूटस्थमिव तिष्ठति। मज्जमानस्य संसारे यावद् दुःखाद् विमुच्यते॥
en: Sometimes, 0 child, the happiness consequent on good acts remains concealed and covered in such a way that it does not shew itself in the case of the person who is sinking in life's ocean till his sorrows disappear.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: ततो दुःखक्षयं कृत्वा सुकृतं कर्म सेवते। सुकृतक्षयाद् दुष्कृतं तद् विद्धि मनुजाधिप॥
en: After sorrow has been dissipated, one begins to enjoy (the fruits of) his good acts. And know, O king, that upon the exhaustion of the fruits of good deeds, those of sinful ones begain to throw themselves.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: दमः क्षमा धृतिस्तेजः संतोषः सत्यवादिता। ह्रीरहिंसाव्यसनिता दाक्ष्यं चेति सुखावहाः॥
en: Self-control, forgiveness, patience, energy, contentment, truthfulness, modesty, abstention from injury, freedom from the evil practices called Vyasana, and cleverness,—these yield happiness.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: दुष्कृते सुकृते चापि न जन्तुर्नियतो भवेत्। नित्यं मन:समाधाने प्रयतेत विचक्षणः॥
en: No creature is perpetually subject to the fruits of his good or bad acts. The wise man should always try to collect and concentrate his mind.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: नायं परस्य सुकृतं दुष्कृतं चापि सेवते। करोति यादृशं कर्म तादृशं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: One never has to enjoy or endure the good and bad deeds of another. Indeed, one enjoys and endures the fruits of only those acts that he does oneself.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: सुखदुःखे समाधाय पुमानन्येन गच्छति। अन्येनैव जनः सर्वः संगतो यश्च पार्थिवः॥
en: The person who renounces both happiness and misery walks along a particular path. Those men, however, O king, who allow themselves to be attached to all worldly objects, walk along an entirely different path.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: परेषां यदसूयेत न तत् कुर्यात् स्वयं नरः। यो ह्यसू युस्तथायुक्तः सोऽवहासं नियच्छति॥
en: A person should not himself do that act which, if done by another, will bring censure on him. Indeed, by doing an act that one censures in others, one meets with ridicule.

description: The means by which one acquires the greatest good both in this world and in the next
sn: भीरू राजन्यो ब्राह्मणः सर्वभक्ष्यो वैश्योऽनीहावान् हीनवर्णोऽलसञ्च। विद्वांश्चाशीलो वृत्तहीनः कुलीन: सत्याद् विभ्रष्टो धार्मिकः स्त्री च दुष्टा॥ मूर्यो वक्ता नृपहीनं च राष्ट्रम्। एते सर्वे शोच्यतां यान्ति राजन् यश्चायुक्तः स्नेहहीनः प्रजासु॥
en: A Kshatriya shorn of courage, a Brahmana who takes every sort of food, a Vaishya shorn of exertion, a Shudra who is idle, learned person without good conduct, one of high birth but shorn of righteous conduct, a Brahmana fallen away from truth, a woman who is unchastc and wicked, a Yogin endued with attachments, one that cooks food for his own self, an ignorant person employed in making a discourse, a kingdom without a king, and king who cherishes no love for his subjects and who is shorn of Yoga,-these all, O king, are deserving of pity.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: पराशर उवाच मनोरथरथं प्राप्य इन्द्रियाख्यहयं नरः। रश्मिभिर्ज्ञानसम्भूतैर्यो गच्छति स बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Parashara said That man, who, having got this car, viz., his body endued with mind, goes on, restraining with the reins of knowledge the horses of the objects of the senses, should certainly be considered as an intelligent one.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: सेवाऽऽश्रितेन मनसा वृत्तिहीनस्य शस्यते। द्विजातिहस्तान्निर्वृत्ता न तु तुल्यात् परस्परात्॥
en: The homage by a person whose mind depends on itself and who has renounced the means of livelihood, is worthy of high praise, that homage, namely, O twice born one, from one who has succeeded in getting over acts, but not acquired from the mutual discussion of men in the same state of progress.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: आयुर्न सुलभं लब्वा नावकर्षेद् विशाम्पते। उत्कर्षार्थं प्रयतेत नरः पुण्येन कर्मणा॥
en: Having got the allotted period of life, O king, with such difficulty, one should not diminish it. On other hand, man should always try, by righteous deeds, for his gradual advancement.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: वर्णेभ्यो हि परिभ्रष्टो न वै सम्मानमर्हति। न तु यः सक्रियां प्राप्य राजसं कर्म सेवते॥
en: Among the six different colours that individual Soul attains at different periods of his existence, he who falls away from a superior colour deserves blame and censure. Hence, one who has acquired the result of good decds should act in such a way as to avoid all acts sullied by the quality of Darkness.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: वर्णोत्कर्षमवाप्नोति नरः पुण्येन कर्मणा। दुर्लभं तमलब्ध्वा हि हन्यात् पापेन कर्मणा॥
en: Man attains to a superior colour by pious deeds. Unable to acquire a superior colour for such acquisition is highly difficult, a person, by doing sinful deeds only kills himself.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: अज्ञानाद्धि कृतं पापं तपसैवाभिनिर्णदेत्। पापं हि कर्म फलति पापमेव स्वयं कृतम्।
en: All sinful deeds that are perpetrated unconsciously or in ignorance are destroyed by penances. A sinful deed, however, that is committed knowingly, yields much sorrow.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: तस्मात् पापं न सेवेत कर्म दुःखफलोदयम्॥
en: Hence, one should never commit sinful deeds which have for their fruit only sorrow.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: पापानुबन्धं यत् कर्म यद्यपि स्यान्महाफलम्। तन्न सेवेत मेधावी शुचिः कुशलिनं यथा॥
en: The intelligent man would never do a sinful act even if it produce the greatest advantage, just as a person who is pure would never touch a Chandala.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: किं कष्टमनुपश्यामि फलं पापस्य कर्मणः। प्रत्यापन्नस्य हि ततो नात्मा तावद् विरोचते॥
en: How miserable is the fruit I behold of sinful deeds. Through sin the very vision of the sinner become perverse, and he mistakes his body and its unstable accompaniments for the soul.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: प्रत्यापत्तिश्च यस्येह बालिशस्य न जायते। तस्यापि सुमहांस्तापः प्रस्थितस्योपजायते॥
en: That foolish man who does not succeed in following Renunciation in this world becomes stricken with great grief when he goes to the next world.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: विरक्तं शोध्यते वस्त्रं न तु कृष्णोपसंहितम्। प्रयत्नेन मनुष्येन्द्र पापमेवं निबोध मे॥
en: An uncoloured cloth, when dirty, can be purified, but not a piece of cloth which is dyed with black; so, O king, listen to me with care, is it the case with sin.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: स्वयं कृत्वा तु यः पापं शुभमेवानुतिष्ठति। प्रायश्चित्तं नरः कर्तुमुभयं सोऽश्नुते पृथक्॥
en: That man who, having knowingly perpetrated a sin, acts righteously for expiating that sin, has to enjoy and endure the fruits of his good and bad deeds separately.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: अज्ञानात् तु कृतां हिंसामहिंसा व्यपकर्षति। ब्राह्मणाः शास्त्रनिर्देशादित्याहुर्ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
en: The Brahmavadins hold, under the authority of what has been sanctioned in the Vedas, that all acts of injury committed in ignorance are made good by virtuous acts.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: तथा कामकृतं नास्य विहिंसैवानुकर्षति। इत्याहुर्ब्रह्मशास्त्रज्ञा ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
en: A sin, however, however, that is committed knowingly is never repaired by righteousness. Thus the twice-born Brahmavadins who are conversant with the scriptures of Brahman.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: अहं तु तावत् पश्यामि कर्म यद् वर्तते कृतम्। गुणयुक्तं प्रकाशं वा पापेनानुपसंहितम्॥
en: But I hold that whatever acts are done, be they righteous or sinful, be they done knowingly or otherwise, they remain till their fruits are enjoyed or endured.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: यथा सूक्ष्माणि कर्माणि फलन्तीह यथातथम्। बुद्धियुक्तानि तानीह कृतानि मनसा सह॥
en: Whatever acts are done by the mind with full deliberation, yield, according to their grossness or subtility, fruits which are gross or subtile.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: भवत्यल्पफलं कर्म सेवितं नित्यमुल्बणम्। अबुद्धिपूर्वं धर्मज्ञ कृतमुग्रेण कर्मणा॥
en: Those acts, however, O you of righteous soul, which are fraught with great injury, if done in ignorance do, forsooth, produce consequences which lead to hell, with this difference that are disproportionate in point of gravity to the acts that produce them.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: कृतानि यानि कर्माणि दैवतैर्मुनिभिस्तथा। न चरेत् तानि धर्मात्मा श्रुत्वा चापि न कुत्सयेत्॥
en: As to those acts of the gods or repeated ascctics, a pious man should never do their like or, informed to them, should never censure them.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: संचिन्त्य मनसा राजन् विदित्वा शक्यमात्मनः। करोति यः शुभं कर्म स वै भद्राणि पश्यति॥
en: That man, who, reflecting with his mind, O king, and ascertaining his own ability, performs pious deeds, forsooth, acquires what is for his well-being.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: नवे कपाले सलिलं संन्यस्तं हीयते यथा। नवेतरे तथाभावं प्राप्नोति सुखभावितम्॥ सतोयेऽन्यत् तु यत् तोयं तस्मिन्नेव प्रसिच्यते। वृद्धे वृद्धिमवाप्नोति सलिले सलिलं यथा॥ एवं कर्माणि यानीह बुद्धियुक्तानि पार्थिव। समानि चैव यानीह तानि पुण्यतमान्यपि॥
en: Water poured into an unbaked pitchers gradually becomes less and less and finally disappears altogether. If kept, however, in a baked vessel, it remains without its quantity being decreased. Similarly, acts done without thought with the help of the understanding do not become wholesome; while acts done with judgement remain with unmitigated excellence and produce happiness as their result. If into a vessel containing water other water be poured, the original water increases in quantity; so all acts done with judgement, be they just or otherwise, only increase one's stock of virtue.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: राज्ञा जेतव्याः : शत्रवश्चोन्नताश्च सम्यक् कर्तव्यं पालनं च प्रजानाम्। रन्त्ये मध्ये वा वनमाश्रित्य स्थेयम्॥
en: A king should subjugate his enemies and all who seek to assert their superiority, and he should properly rule and protect his subjects. One should ignite his sacred fires and pour libations on them in various sacrifices, and retiring into the woods in either his middle or old age, should live there.

description: Parasara's discourse on acts and expiation of sin
sn: दमान्वितः पुरुषो धर्मशीलो भूतानि चात्मानमिवानुपश्येत्। गरीयसः पूजयेदात्मशक्त्या सत्येन शीलेन सुखं नरेन्द्र॥
