en: Gifted with self-control, and possessed of righteous conduct, one should regard all creatures as his ownself. One should again respect his superiors. By the practice of truth and of good conduct, O king one is sure to acquire happiness.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: पराशर उवाच कः कस्य चोपकुरुते कश्च कस्मै प्रयच्छति। प्राणी करोत्ययं कर्म सर्वमात्मार्थमात्मना॥
en: Nobody in this world does good to another. Nobody makes gifts to others. All persons are seen to act for their own selves.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: गौरवेण परित्यक्तं निःस्नेहं परिवर्जयेत्। सोदर्यं भ्रातरमपि किमुतान्यं पृथग्जनम्॥
en: People are seen to abandon their very parents and their uterine brothers when these cease to love them. What need be said then of relatives of other grades.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: विशिष्टस्य विशिष्टाच्च तुल्यौ दानप्रतिग्रहौ। तयोः पुण्यतरं दानं तद् द्विजस्य प्रयच्छतः॥
en: Gifts a distinguished person and acceptance of the gifts made by a distinguished person both produce equal merit. Of these two acts, however, the making of a gift is superior to the acceptance thereof.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: न्यायागतं धनं चैव न्यायेनैव विवर्धितम्। संरक्ष्यं यत्नमास्थाय धर्मार्थमिति निश्चयः॥
en: to That wealth is gained by fair means and is multiplied by fair means, should be protected with care for the sake of acquiring virtue. This is an accepted truth.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: न धर्मार्थी नृशंसेन कर्मणा धनमर्जयेत्। शक्तितः सर्वकार्याणि कुर्यान्नर्द्धिमनुस्मरेत्॥
en: One desirous of gaining virtue, should never gain riches by means involving injury to others. One should perform his acts according to his power, without zealously seeking riches.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: अपो हि प्रयतः शीतास्तापिता ज्वलनेन वा। शक्तितोऽतिथये दत्त्वा क्षुधार्तायाश्नुते फलम्॥
en: By giving water, whether cold or heated by fire, with a devoted mind, to a (thirsty) guest, according to the best of his might, one acquires the merit of the act of giving food to a hungry man.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: रन्तिदेवेन लोकेष्टा सिद्धिः प्राप्ता महात्मना। फलपत्रैरथो मूलैर्मुनीनर्चितवांश्च सः॥
en: The great Rantideva acquired success in all the worlds by adoring the ascetics with offerings of only roots and fruits and leaves.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: तैरेव फलपत्रैश्च स माठरमतोषयत्। तस्माल्लेभे परं स्थानं शैब्योऽपि पृथिवीपतिः॥
en: The royal son of Shaivi also acquired the highest regions of happiness by having pleased the Son-god along with his companion with offerings of the same sort.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: देवतातिथिभृत्येभ्यः पितृभ्यश्चात्मनस्तथा। ऋणवान् जायते मर्त्यस्तस्मादनृणतां व्रजेत्॥
en: All men, by being born, become indebted to gods, guests, servants, Pitris, and their own selves. Every one should, therefore do his best for satisfying those debts.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: स्वाध्यायेन महर्षिभ्यो देवेभ्यो यज्ञकर्मणा। पितृभ्यः श्राद्धदानेन नृणामभ्यर्चनेन च॥
en: One frees oneself from his debt to the great Rishis by studying the Vedas. One satisfies his debts to the gods by celebrating sacrifices. By performing the rites of the Shraddha one satisfies the debts to the Pitris. One satisfies the debt to his fellow men by doing good to them. son son

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: वाचा शेषावहार्येण पालनेनात्मनोऽपि च। यथावद् भृत्यवर्गस्य चिकीत् कर्म आदितः॥
en: One satisfies the debts he owns to one's own self by listening to Vedic recitations and reflecting on their meaning, by eating the remnants of sacrifices, and by supporting his body. One should duly perform all the acts, from the beginning, that he owes to his servants.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: प्रयत्नेन च संसिद्धा धनैरपि विवर्जिताः। सम्यग्घुत्वा हुतवहं मुनयः सिद्धिमागताः॥
en: Through shorn of wealth, men are seen to attain to success by great exertions. Ascetics by duly adoring the gods, and by duly pouring libations of clarified butter on the sacred fire, have been seen to acquire ascetic success.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: विश्वामित्रस्य पुत्रत्वमृचीकतनयोऽगमत्। ऋग्भिः स्तुत्वा महाबाहो देवान् वै यज्ञभागिनः॥
en: Richika's became the of Vishvamitra. By worshipping the gods who have shares in sacrificial offerings, with Riches, (he acquired success in after life).

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: गतः शुक्रत्वमुशना देवदेवप्रसादनात्। देवीं स्तुत्वा तु गगने मोदते यशसा वृतः॥
en: Ushanas became Shukra by having pleased the god of gods. Indeed, by singing the praises of the goddess (Uma), he sports in the sky, in the great effulgence.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: असितो देवलश्चैव तथा नारदपर्वतौ। कक्षीवान् जामदग्न्यश्च रामस्ताण्ड्यस्तथाऽऽत्मवान्।। वसिष्ठो जमदग्निश्च विश्वामित्रोऽत्रिरेव च। भरद्वाजो हरिश्मश्रुः कुण्डधारः श्रुतश्रवाः॥ एते महर्षयः स्तुत्वा विष्णुमृग्भिः समाहिताः। लेभिरे तपसा सिद्धिं प्रसादात् तस्य धीमतः॥
en: Then, again, Asita and Devala, and Narada and Paravata, and Kakshivat, and Jamadagni's son Rama, and Tandya possessed of purified soul, and Vashishtha, and Jamadagni, and Vishvamitra, and Atri, and Bharadvaja, and Harishmashru, and Kundadhara, and Shrutashravas,-these great Rishis, by worshipping Vishnu with concentrated minds with the help of Richs, and by penances, acquired success through the grace of that great god gifted with intelligence.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: अनश्चिाहतां प्राप्ताः सन्तः स्तुत्वा तमेव ह। न तु वृद्धिमिहान्विच्छेत् कर्म कृत्वा जुगुप्सितम्॥
en: Many undeserving men, by worshipping that good god, won great distinction. One should not seek for advancement by committing any wicked or censurable deed.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: येऽर्था धर्मेण ते सत्या येऽधर्मेण धिगस्तु तान्। धर्मं वै शाश्वतं लोके न जह्याद् धनकाझ्या॥
en: That wealth which acquired by fair means is true wealth. Fie on that wealth however, which is acquired by unfair means. Virtue is eternal. It should never, in this world, be renounced from desire of riches.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: आहिताग्निर्हि धर्मात्मा यः स पुण्यकृदुत्तमः। वेदा हि सर्वे राजेन्द्र स्थितास्त्रिष्वग्निषु प्रभो॥
en: That pious person who keeps his sacred fire and offers his daily adorations to the gods is considered as the foremost of righteous persons. All the Vedas, O foremost of kings, are established on the three sacred fires.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: स चाप्यग्न्याहितो विप्रः क्रिया यस्य न हीयते। श्रेयो ह्यनाहिताग्नित्वमग्निहोत्रं न निष्क्रियम्॥
en: That Brahmana is said to possess the sacred fire whose acts exist in full. It is better to at once leave off the sacred fire than to keep it, abstaining from acts.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: अग्निरात्मा च माता च पिता जनयिता तथा। गुरुश्च नरशार्दूल परिचर्या यथातथम्॥
en: The sacred fire, the mother, the father who has begotten, and the preceptor, O foremost men, should all be duly attended and served with humility.

description: Discourse on virtue and wealth : The duties of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas
sn: मानं त्यक्त्वा यो नरो वृद्धसेवी विद्वान् क्लीबः पश्यति प्रीतियोगात्। दाक्ष्येण हीनो धर्मयुक्तो नदान्तो लोकेऽस्मिन् वै पूज्यते सद्भिरार्यः॥
en: That man, who, renouncing all feelings of pride, humbly attends upon and serves them who are venerable for age, who is endued with learning and shorn of lust, who regains all creatures equally with an eye of love, who nas no riches, who is righteous in his acts, and who is shorn of the desire of inflicting any kind of injury, that truly respectable man is adored in this world by the good and pious.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: पराशर उवाच वृत्तिः सकाशाद् वर्णेभ्यस्त्रिभ्यो हीनस्य शोभना। प्रीत्योपनीता निर्दिष्टा धर्मिष्ठान् कुरुते सदा॥
en: Parashara said The lowest order, it is proper, should derive their maintenance from the three other orders. Such service, rendered with love and respect, makes them pious.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: वृत्तिश्चेन्नास्ति शूद्रस्य पितृपैतामही ध्रुवा। न वृत्तिं परतो मार्गेच्छुश्रूषां तु प्रयोजयेत्॥
en: If the ancestors of any Shudra were not engaged in service, he should not still engage himself in any other occupation. Truly, he should take up service as his occupation.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: सद्भिस्तु सह संसर्गः शोभते धर्मदर्शिभिः। नित्यं सर्वास्ववस्थासु नासद्भिरिति मे मतिः॥
en: In my opinion, it is proper for them to mix under all circumstances, with good men devoted to virtue, but never with the wicked.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: यथोदयगिरौ द्रव्यं संनिकर्षेण दीप्यते। तथा सत्संनिकर्षेण हीनवर्णोऽपि दीप्यते॥
en: As in the Eastern hills, jewels and metals blaze with greater effulgence on account of their nearness to the Sun, so the lowest order shines on account of their association with the good.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: यादृशेन हि वर्णेन भाव्यते शुक्लमम्बरम्। तादृशं कुरुते रुपमेतदेवमवेहि मे॥
en: A piece of white cloth assumes that colour with which it is dyed. Such is the case with Shudras.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: तस्माद् गुणेषु रज्येथा मा दोषेषु कदाचन। अनित्यमिह मानां जीवितं हि चलाचलम्॥
en: Therefore, one should also attach him to all good qualities but never to bad qualities. The life of human beings in this world is fickle and transitory.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: सुखे वा यदि वा दुःखे वर्तमानो विचक्षणः। यश्चिनोति शुभान्येव स तन्त्राणीह पश्यति॥
en: That wise man who, in happiness as also in misery, acquire only what is good, is considered as a true observer of the scriptures.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: धर्मादपेतं यत् कर्म यद्यपि स्यान्महाफलम्। न तत् सेवेत मेधावी न तद्धितमिहोच्यते॥
en: That man who is gifted with intelligence would never do an act which is alienated from virtue, however great may that advantages be of that act. Indeed, such an act is not considered as truly wholesome.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: यो हत्वा गोसहस्राणि नृपो दद्यादरक्षिता। स शब्दमात्रफलभाग् राजा भवति तस्करः॥
en: That lawless king who, taking thousands of kine from their lawful owners, gives them away acquires on fruit save an empty sound. On the other hand, he cominits the sin of theft.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: स्वयम्भूरसृजच्चाग्रे धातारं लोकसत्कृतम्। धातासृजत् पुत्रमेकं लोकानां धारणे रतम्॥
en: The Self-create at first created the Being called Dhatri held in universal esteem. Dhatri created a son who was engaged in maintaining all the worlds.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: तमर्चयित्वा वैश्यस्तु कुर्यादत्यर्थमृद्धिमत्। रक्षितव्यं तु राजन्यैरुपयोज्यं द्विजातिभिः॥
en: Adoring that God, the Vaishya engages for the means of his support, in agriculture and the tending of cattle. The Kshatriyas should undertake the task of protecting all the other classes. The Brahmanas should only enjoy.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: अजिौरशठक्रोधैर्हव्यकव्यप्रयोक्तृभिः। शूद्रनिर्मार्जनं कार्यमेवं धर्मो न नश्यति॥
en: As regards the Shudras, they should take up the task of humbly and honestly collecting together the articles that are to be offered in sacrifices, and in cleaning altars and other places where sacrifices are to be celebrated. If each order acts in this way, virtue would not suffer any decrease.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: अप्रणष्टे ततो धर्मे भवन्ति सुखिताः प्रजाः। सुखेन तासां राजेन्द्र मोदन्ते दिवि देवताः॥
en: If virtue is preserved in its full, all creatures inhabiting the Earth would be happy, Seeing the happiness of all creatures on Earth, the gods in heaven become filled with gladness.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: तस्माद् यो रक्षति नृपः स धर्मेणेति पूज्यते। अधीते चापि यो विप्रो वैश्यो यश्चार्जने रतः॥ यश्च शुश्रूषते शूद्रः सततं नियतेन्द्रियः। अतोऽन्यथा मनुष्येन्द्र स्वधर्मात् परिहीयते॥
en: Hence, that king, who, according to the duties laid down for his order, protects the other classes, becomes worthy of respect. similarly, the Brahmana who is employed in studying the scriptures, the Vaishya who is engaged in acquiring riches, and the Shudra who is always engaged in serving the three other classes with rapt attention, become objects of reverence. By acting in other ways, O king, each order is said to deviate from virtue.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: प्राणसंतापनिर्दिष्टाः काकिण्योऽपि महाफलाः। न्यायेनोपार्जिता दत्ता: किमुतान्याः सहस्रशः॥
en: Keeping aside gifts by thousands, even twenty cowries that one may give painfully, having acquired them righteously, will yield great benefit.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: सत्कृत्य हि द्विजातिभ्यो यो ददाति नराधिपः। यादृशं तादृशं नित्यमश्नाति फलमूर्जितम्॥
en: Those persons, O king, who make gifts to Brahmanas after respecting them duly, reap excellent fruits proportionate to those gifts.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: अभिगम्य च तत् तुष्ट्या दत्तमाहुरभिष्टुतम्। याचितेन तु तद् दत्तं तदाहुर्मध्यमं बुधाः॥
en: The gift is highly valued which the donor inakes after seeking out the done and respecting him properly. That gift is middling which the donor makes upon being prayed for it.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: अवज्ञया दीयते यत् तथैवाश्रद्धयापि वा। तमाहुरधमं दानं मुनयः सत्यवादिनः॥
en: That gift, however, which is made contemptuously and without any respect, is said to be very inferior. This is what the truthful sages say.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: अतिक्रामेन्मज्जमानो विविधेन नरः सदा। तथा प्रयत्नं कुर्वीत यथा मुच्येत संश्रयात्॥
en: While sinking in this ocean of life, man should always try to cross that ocean by various means. Indeed, he should so exert himself that he might be released from the fetters of this world.

description: The duties of the Sudras. The gift to Brahmanas
sn: दमेन शोभते विप्रः क्षत्रियो विजयेन तु। धनेन वैश्यः शूद्रस्तु नित्यं दाक्ष्येण शोभते॥
en: The Brahmana shines by self-control; the Kshatriya by victory; the Vaishya by riches; while the Shudra always shines in glory through clever serving.

sn: पराशर उवाच प्रतिग्रहागता विप्रे क्षत्रिये युधि निर्जिताः। वैश्य न्यायार्जिताश्चैव शूद्रे शुश्रूषयार्जिताः॥ स्वल्पाप्यर्थाः प्रशस्यन्ते धर्मस्यार्थे महाफलाः। नित्यं त्रयाणां वर्णानां शुश्रूषुः शूद्र उच्यते॥
en: Parashara said In the Brahmana, wealth gained by acceptance of gifts, in the Kshatriya that acquired by victory in battle, in the Vaishya that acquired by performing the duties laid down for his order, and in the Shudra that acquired by serving the three other orders, however small it may be, is worthy of praise, and when spent for the acquisition of virtue yields great benefits. The Shudra is said to be the constant servitor of the three other orders.

sn: क्षत्रधर्मा वैश्यधर्मा नावृत्तिः पतते द्विजः। शूद्रधर्मा यदा तु स्यात् तदा पतति वै द्विजः॥
en: If the Brahmana, when hard-pressed for a living, performs the duties of either the Kshatriya or the Vaishya, he does not fall off from virtue. When, however, the Brahmana performs the duties of the lowest order, then does he certainly fall off.

sn: वाणिज्यं पाशुपाल्यं च तथा शिल्पोपजीवनम्। शूद्रस्यापि विधीयन्ते यदा वृत्तिर्न जायते॥
en: When the Shudra is unable to secure his living by service of the three other orders, then it is lawful for him to follow trade, tending of cattle, and the practice of the mechanical arts.

sn: रङ्गावतरणं चैव तथा रूपोपजीवनम्। मद्यमांसोपजीव्यं च विक्रयं लोहचर्मणोः॥ अपूर्विणा न कर्तव्यं कर्म लोके विगर्हितम्। त्यजतो धर्म इति श्रुतिः॥
en: Appearance on the stage and disguising oneself in various forms, exhibition of puppets, the sale of spirits and meat, and trading in iron and leather, should never be adopted for purposes of a living by one who had never before been engaged in those callings every one of which is regarded as censurable in the world. We have heard that if one engaged in them can renounce them, he acquires great merit.

sn: संसिद्धः पुरुषो लोके यदाचरति पापकम्। मदेनाभिप्लुतमनास्तच्च न ग्राह्यमुच्यते॥
en: When one who has become successful in life acts sinfully on account of his mind being filled with pride, his acts under such circumstances can never pass for authority.

sn: कृतपूर्वं तु महान् श्रूयन्ते हि पुराणेषु प्रजा धिग्दण्डशासनाः। दान्ता धर्मप्रधानाश्च न्यायधर्मानुवृत्तिकाः॥
en: It is heard in the Puranas that formerly mankind were self-controlled, that they valued virtue greatly, that the practices they followed for livelihood were all agreeable to propriety and the injunctions laid down in the scriptures; and that the only punishment that was necessary for chastising them when they did wrong was merely the deprecation of their deeds.

sn: धर्म एव सदा नृणामिह राजन् प्रशस्यते। धर्मवृद्धा गुणानेव सेवन्ते हि नरा भुवि॥
en: At the time of which we speak, O king, Virtue, and nothing else, was much praised among men. Having achieved great progress in virtue, men in those days adored only all good qualities that they saw.

sn: तं धर्ममसुरास्तात नामृष्यन्त जनाधिप। विवर्धमानाः क्रमशस्तत्र तेऽन्वाविशन् प्रजाः॥
en: The Asuras, however, O child, could not bear that virtue, which prevailed in the world. Multiplying the Asuras entered the bodies of inen.

sn: तासां दर्पः समभवत् प्रजानां धर्मनाशनः। दर्पात्मनां ततः पश्चात् क्रोधस्तासामजायत।॥
en: Then was pride generated in men which is so destructive of virtue. From pride originated arrogance, and from arrogance originated anger.

sn: ततः क्रोधाभिभूतानां वृत्तं लज्जासमन्वितम्। ह्रीश्चैवाप्यनशद् राजंस्ततो मोहो व्यजायत॥
en: When men thus became overwhelmed with anger, modesty and shame disappeared from them, and then they were possessed by carelessness.

sn: ततो मोहपरीतास्ता नापश्यन्त यथा पुरा। परस्परावमर्दैन वर्धयन्त्यो यथासुखम्॥
en: Afflicted by carelessness, they could no longer see as before, and as the consequence thereof they began to assail one another and thereby gain riches without any compunction.

sn: ताः प्राप्य तु स धिग्दण्डो न कारणमतोऽभवत्। ततोऽभ्यगच्छन् देवांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चावमन्य ह॥
en: When men became such, the punishment of mere depreciation on transgressors could produce no effect. Men, showing no respect of either the gods or Brahmanas, began to indulge their senses to their fill.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु देवा देववरं शिवम्। अगच्छन् शरणं धीरं बहुरूपं गुणाधिकम्॥
en: At that time the gods repaired to that foremost of god, viz., Shiva, possessed of patience of multiform aspect and endued with the foremost of qualities and sought his protection.

sn: तेन स्म ते गगनगाः सपुराः पातिताः क्षितौ। विधाप्येकेन बाणेन देवाप्यायिततेजसा॥
en: The gods gave him their conjoined energy, and thereupon the great god, with a single arrow killed on the Earth those three Asuras, viz., Desire, Anger, and Cupidity, who were staying in the sky, along with their very dwellers.

sn: तेषामधिपतिस्त्वासीद् भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। देवतानां भयकरः स हतः शूलपाणिना॥
en: The dreadful king those Asuras, endued with terrific prowess, who had struck the gods with terror, was also killed by Mahadeva armed with the lance.

sn: तस्मिन् हतेऽथ स्वं भावं प्रत्यपद्यन्त मानवाः। प्रापद्यन्त च वेदान् वै शास्त्राणि च यथा पुरा॥
en: When this king of the Asuras was killed men once more gained their proper natures, and once more began to study the Vedas and the other scriptures as in days of yore.

sn: ततोऽभिषिच्य राज्येन देवानां दिवि वासवम्। सप्तर्षयश्चान्वयुञ्जन् नराणां दण्डधारणे॥
en: Then the seven ancient Rishis came forward and installed Vasava as the king of the gods and the ruler of heaven. And they took upon themselves the task of holding the rod of punishment over mankind.

sn: सप्तर्षीणामथोर्ध्वं च विपृथु म पार्थिवः। राजानः क्षत्रियाश्चैव मण्डलेषु पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: After the seven Rishis came king Viprithu and many other kings, all belonging to the Kshatriya order for separately ruling separate classes of human beings.

sn: महाकुलेषु ये जाता वृद्धाः पूर्वतराश्च ये। तेषामप्यासुरो भावो हृदयान्नापसर्पति॥
en: There were, in those ancient times, certain clderly men from whose minds all wicked feelings did not disappear.

sn: तस्मात् तेनैव भावेन सानुषङ्गेण पार्थिवाः। आसुराण्येव कर्माणि न्यसेवन भीमविक्रमाः॥
en: Hence, on account of that wicked state of their minds and of those incidents connected with it, there appeared many kings of dreadful prowess who began to perform only such acts as were fit for Asuras.

sn: प्रत्यतिष्ठंश्च तेष्वेव तान्येव स्थापयन्त्यपि। भजन्ते तानि चाद्यापि ये बालिशतरा नराः॥
en: Those human beings, who are very foolish follow those wicked acts, establish them as authorities, and practise them to this day.

sn: तस्मादहं ब्रवीमि त्वां राजन् संचिन्त्य शास्त्रतः। संसिद्धाधिगमं कुर्यात् कर्म हिंसात्मकं त्यजेत्॥
en: Therefore, O king, I say, you, have reflected properly with the help of the scriptures, that one should avoid all acts that are fraught with injury or malice and try to acquire a knowledge of the Soul.

sn: न संकरेण द्रविणं प्रचिन्वीयाद् विचक्षणः। धर्मार्थं न्यायमुत्सृज्य न तत् कल्याणमुच्यते॥
en: The man endued with wisdom would not seek riches for the performance of religions rites by unfair and immoral ways. Wealth aquired by such means can never yield benefits.

sn: स त्वमेवंविधो दान्तः क्षत्रिय: प्रियबान्धवः। प्रजा भृत्यांश्च पुत्रांश्च स्वधर्मेणानुपालय॥
en: Do you, then, become a Kshatriya of this kind! Do you restrain your senses, be kind to your friends, and cherish, according to the duties of your order, your subjects, servants, and children.

sn: इष्टानिष्टसमायोगे वैरं सौहार्दमेव च। अथ जातिसहस्राणि बहूनि परिवर्तते॥
en: Through the union of both prosperity and adversity, there arise friendships and enmities. Thousands and thousands of existences are continually revolving, and in every mode of individual Soul's existence these must take place.

sn: तस्माद् गुणेषु रज्येथा मा दोषेषु कथंचन। निर्गुणोऽपि हि दुर्बुद्धिरात्मन: सोऽतिरज्यते॥
en: Therefore, be attached to good qualities of every sort, but never to faults. Such is the nature of good qualities that if the most foolish person, shorn of every virtue, hears himself praised for any good quality, he becomes filled with joy.

sn: मानुषेषु महाराज धर्माधर्मो प्रवर्ततः। न तथान्येषु भूतेषु मनुष्यरहितेष्विह॥
en: Virtue and sin exist, O king, only among men. These do not exist among other creatures.

sn: धर्मशीलो नरो विद्वानीहकोऽनीहकोऽपि वा। आत्मभूतः सदा लोके चरेद् भूतान्यहिंसया॥
en: One should, therefore, whether in need of food and other necessaries of life or above such need, be of virtuous disposition, acquire knowledge, always consider all creatures as his own self, and abstain totally from inflicting any kind of injury.

sn: यदा व्यपेतहल्लेखं मनो भवति तस्य वै। नानृतं चैव भवत तदा कल्याणपृच्छति॥
en: When one's mind becomes shorn of desire, and when all Darkness is removed from it, it is then that one acquires what is auspicious.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: पराशर उवाच एष धर्मविधिस्तात गृहस्थस्य प्रकीर्तितः। तपोविधिं तु वक्ष्यामि तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: Parashara said I have now described to you the ordained duties of a householder. I shall now describe to you the ordinances about penances. Hear me as I describe that subject.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: प्रायेण च गृहस्थस्य ममत्वं नाम जायते। सङ्गागतं नरश्रेष्ठ भावै राजसतामसैः॥
en: It is generally seen, O king. that on account of sentiments fraught with Darkness and Ignorance, the senses of mine begotten by attachment, originates in the heart of householder.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: गृहाण्याश्रित्य गावश्च क्षेत्राणि च धनानि च। दाराः पुत्राश्च भृत्याश्च भवन्तीह नरस्य वै॥
en: Becoming a householder, one acquires kine, fields, wealth of diverse sorts, wives, children, and servants.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: एवं तस्य प्रवृत्तस्य नित्यमेवानुपश्यतः। रागद्वेषौ विवर्धेते ह्यनित्यत्वमपश्यतः॥
en: One who follows this mode of life continually casts his eye upon these objects. Under these circumstances, one's attachments and aversions multiply, and one ceases to consider unreal possessions as eternal and indestructible.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: रागद्वेषाभिभूतं च नरं द्रव्यवशानुगम्। मोहजाता रतिर्नाम समुपैति नराधिप॥
en: When a person becomes possessed by attachment and aversion, and gives way to the control of worldly objects, the desire of enjoyment then seizes him, originating from carelessness, O king.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: कृतार्थं भोगिनं मत्वा सर्वो रतिपरायणः। लाभं ग्राम्यसुखादन्यं रतितो नानुपश्यति॥
en: Considering that person as blessed who has the largest share of enjoyments in this world, the man devoted to enjoyment does not, on account of his attachment thereto, see that there is any other happiness save what depends upon the gratification of the senses.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: ततो लोभाभिभूतात्मा संगाद् वर्धयते जनम्। पुष्ट्यर्थं चैव तस्येह जनस्यार्थं चिकीर्षति॥
en: Overwhelmed with cupidity that originates from such attachment, he then tries to multiply the number of his relatives and attendants, and for pleasing these latter he tries to increase his wealth by every means in his power.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: स जानन्नपि चाकार्यमर्थार्यं सेवते नरः। बालस्नेहपरीतात्मा तत्क्षयाच्चानुतप्यते॥
en: Filled with affection for children, such a person then commits, for the sake of acquiring riches, evil deeds, and yields to grief if his wealth belost.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: ततो मानेन सम्पन्नो रक्षन्नात्मपराजयम्। करोति येन भोगी स्यामिति तस्माद् विनश्यति॥
en: Having acquired honours and always guarding against the defeat of his plans, he follows such means as would satisfy his desire of enjoyment. At last he meets with destruction as the inevitable result of the conduct he follows.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: तथा हि बुद्धियुक्तानां शाश्वतं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्। अन्विच्छतां शुभं कर्म नराणां त्यजतां सुखम्॥
en: It is well known, however, that true happiness is theirs who are endued with intelligence, who are Brahmavadins, who try to perform only auspicious and beneficial acts, and who abstain from all acts which are optional and originate from desire only.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: स्नेहायतननाशाच्च धननाशाच्च पार्थिव। आधिव्याधिप्रतापाच्च निर्वेदमुपगच्छति॥
en: From loss of all such objects in which are centred our affections, from loss of riches, O king, and from the oppression of physical diseases and mental anguish a person falls into despair.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: मिर्वेदादात्मसम्बोधः सम्बोधाच्छास्त्रदर्शनम्। शास्त्रार्थदर्शनाद् राजस्तप एवानुपश्यति॥
en: From this despair originates an awakening of the soul. From such an awakening proceeds study of the Scriptures. From contemplation of the meaning of the Scriptures, O king, one sees the value of penance.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: दुर्लभो हि मनुष्येन्द्र नरः प्रत्यवमर्शवान्। यो वै प्रियसुखे क्षीणे तपः कर्तुं व्यवस्यति॥
en: A person endued with the knowledge of what is essential and what accidental, O king, is very rare,-a man who tries to practise penances, under the conviction that the happiness one enjoys from the possession of such agreeable objects as wives and children brings on ultimately misery.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: तपः सर्वगतं तात हीनस्यापि विधीयते। जितेन्द्रियस्य दान्तस्य स्वर्गमार्गप्रवर्तकम्॥
en: Penances, O child, are for all. They are ordained for even the lowest order of men, Penances lead the self-controlled man who has mastered all his senses to the way to heaven.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: प्रजापतिः प्रजाः पूर्वमसृजत् तपसा विभुः। क्वचित् क्वचिद् ब्रह्मपरो व्रतान्यास्थाय पार्थिव॥
en: It was through penances that the powerful Lord of all creatures, O king, practising vows at particular intervals, created all existent objects.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: आदित्या वसवो रुद्रास्तथैवाग्न्यश्विमारुताः। विश्वेदेवास्तथा साध्याः पितरोऽथ मरुद्गणाः॥ यक्षराक्षसगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्चान्ये दिवौकसः। संसिद्धास्तपसा तात ये चान्ये स्वर्गवासिनः॥
en: The Aditya's, the Vasus, the Rudras, Agni, the Ashvins, the Maruts, the Vishvedevas, the Saddhyas, the Pitris, the Maruts, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the other Inhabitants of heaven, and indeed, all other celestials whatever, O child, have all become successful through their penances.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: ये चादौ ब्राह्मणाः सृष्टा ब्रह्मणा तपसा पुरा। ते भावयन्तः पृथिवीं विचरन्ति दिवं तथा॥
en: Those Brahmanas whom Brahman created at the beginning, succeeded through their penances in honouring not the Earth alone but the heaven also in which they moved about at pleasure.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: मर्त्यलोके च राजानो ये चान्ये गृहमेधिनः। महाकुलेषु दृश्यन्ते तत् सर्वं तपसः फलम्॥
en: In this world of men, they who are kings and those others who are householders born in high families, have all become what they are on account of their penances.,

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: कौशिकानि च वस्त्राणि शुभान्याभरणानि च। वाहनासनपानानि तत् सर्वं तपसः फलम्॥
en: The silken dresses they put on the excellent ornaments that decorate their persons, the animals and vehicles they ride, and the seats they use are all the outcome of their penances.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: मनोऽनुकूलाः प्रमदा रूपवत्यः सहस्रशः। वासः प्रासादपृष्ठे च तत् सर्वं तपसः फलम्॥
en: Thousands of many charming and beautiful damsels, that they enjoy, and their residence in palaces, are all on account of their penances.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: शयनानि च मुख्यानि भोज्यानि विविधानि च। अभिप्रेतानि सर्वाणि भवन्ति शुभकर्मिणाम्॥
en: The righteous persons enjoy various sorts of costly beds and sweet viands,

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: नाप्राप्यं तपसः किंचित् त्रैलोक्येऽपि परंतप। उपभोगपरित्यागः फलान्यकृतकर्मणाम्॥
en: There is nothing in the three worlds, O scorcher of enemies, that penances cannot bring in. Even those who are shorn of true knowledge acquire Renunciation through their penances.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: सुखितो दुःखितो वापि नरो लाभं परित्यजेत्। अवेक्ष्य मनसा शास्त्रं बुद्ध्या च नृपसत्तम॥
en: Whether in rich circumstances or miserable, a person should renounce cupidity, meditating on the scriptures, with the help of his mind and understanding, O best of kings.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: असंतोषोऽसुखायेति लोभादिन्द्रियसम्भ्रमः। ततोऽस्य नश्यति प्रज्ञा विद्येवाभ्यासवर्जिता।॥
en: Discontent produces misery. Cupidity brings on stupefaction of the senses. The senses being stupefied, one's wisdom is lost like knowledge not kept up by continued application.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: नष्टप्रज्ञो यदा तु स्यात् तदा न्यायं न पश्यति। तस्मात् सुखक्षये प्राप्ते पुमानुग्रं तपश्चरेत्॥
en: When one's wisdom is lost, he cannot discriminate what is proper from what is improper. Hence, when one's happiness is destroyed he should practise the austerest of penances.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: यदिष्टं तत् सुखं प्राहुद्देष्यं दुःखमिहेष्यते। कृताकृतस्य तपस: फलं पश्यस्व यादृशम्॥
en: Wheat is agreeable is called happiness. What is disagreeable is called misery. Happiness is the outcome of penances practisted. When they are not practised, the outcome is misery. See the fruits of practising and abstaining from penances.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: नित्यं भद्राणि पश्यन्ति विषयांश्चोपभुञ्जते।। प्राकाश्यं चैव गच्छन्ति कृत्वा निष्कल्मषं तपः॥
en: By practising pure penances, people always enjoy auspicious consequences of every sort, enjoy all good things, and acquire great fame.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: अप्रियाण्यवमानांश्च दुःखं बहुविधात्मकम्। फलार्थी तत्फलं त्यक्त्वा प्राप्नोति विषयात्मकम्॥
en: He, however, who, by abandoning (pure penances), undertakes penances from desire of fruit, suffers from many disagreeable consequences, and disgrace and sorrow of all sorts, as the fruits thereof, all of which originate from worldly possessions.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: धर्मे तपसि दाने च विचिकित्सास्य जायते। स कृत्वा पापकान्येव निरयं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Despite the desirability of practising virtue, penances, and gifts, the desire for doing all sorts of forbidden acts originates in his mind. By thus perpetrating various sorts of sinful deeds, he goes to hell.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: सुखे तु वर्तमानो वै दुःखे वापि नरोत्तमा सुवृत्ताद् यो न चलते शास्त्रचक्षुः स मानवः॥
en: That person, O best of men, who, in both happiness and misery, does deviate from the duties ordained for him, is said to have the scriptures for his eye.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: इषुप्रपातमात्रं हि स्पर्शयोगे रतिः स्मृता। रसने दर्शने घ्राणे श्रवणे च विशाम्पते।॥
en: It is said that the pleasure one gets from the gratification of his senses of touch, tongue, sight, smell, and hearing, O king, lasts only so long as an arrow shot off the bow takes in falling down upon the Earth.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: ततोऽस्य जायते तीव्रा वेदना तक्षयात् पुनः। अबुधा न प्रशंसन्ति मोक्षं सुखमनुत्तमम्॥
en: Upon the termination of the pleasure, which is fickle, on suffers the most acute pain. It is only the senseless that do not speak highly of happiness of Liberation which is peerless.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: ततः फलार्थं सर्वस्य भवन्ति ज्यायसे गुणाः। धर्मवृत्त्या च सततं कामार्थाभ्यां न हीयते॥
en: Seeing the misery consequent upon the gratification of the senses, the wise cultivate the virtues of tranquillity and self-control for the purpose of acquiring Liberation. On account of righteous conduct, riches and pleasure can never succeed in afflicting them.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: अप्रयत्नागताः सेव्या गृहस्थैविषयाः सदा। प्रयत्नेनोपगम्यश्च स्वधर्म इति मे मतिः॥
en: Householders may, without any compunction, enjoy riches and other possessions which are acquired with Exertion. About the duties of their order, I think, they should satisfy them with the help of Exertion.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: मानिनां कुलजातानां नित्यं शास्त्रार्थचक्षुषाम्। क्रियाधर्मविमुक्तानामशक्त्या संवृतात्मनाम्॥
en: The practice of those who are honoured, who are born in high families, and who have their eyes always turned towards the meaning of the Scriptures, is incapable of being followed by those who are sinful and who have uncontrolled minds.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: क्रियमाणं यदा कर्म नाशं गच्छति मानुषम्। तेषां नान्यदृते लोके तपसः कर्म विद्यते॥
en: All acts that are done by man under the influence of pride, meet with destruction. Therefore, there is no other act, for the respectable and the truly righteous, in this world to do than penance.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: सर्वात्मनानुकुर्वीत गृहस्थः कर्मनिश्चयम्। दाक्ष्येण हव्यकव्यार्थं स्वधर्मे विचरन् नृप।॥
en: As regards, those householders, however, who are addicted to acts, they should, with their whole hearts, perform acts. Following the duties of their order, O king, they should with diligence and assiduity celebrate sacrifices and other religious rites.

description: The ordinances about penance's as described by Parasara
sn: यथा नदीनदाः सर्वे सागरे यान्ति संस्थितम्। एवमाश्रमिणः सर्वे गृहस्थे यान्ति संस्थितिम्॥
en: Indeed, as all rivers, male and female, go in the end to the Ocean, so men belonging to all the other orders have the householders for their refuge.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: जनक उवाच वर्णो विशेषवर्णानां महर्षे केन जायते। एतदिच्छाम्यहं ज्ञातुं तद् ब्रूहि वदतां वरा॥
en: Janaka said Whence, O great Rishi, does this difference of colour arise among men of the different orders? I wish to know this. Tell me this, O foreinost of speakers.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: यदेतज्जायतेऽपत्यं स एवायमिति श्रुतिः। कथं ब्राह्मणतो जातो विशेषग्रहणं गतः॥
en: The Shrutis say that the offspring one begets is his own self. Originally sprung from Brahman, all the inhabitants of the Earth should have been Brahmanas. Sprung from Brahmanas, why have men begun to perform works distinguished from those of Brahmanas.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: पराशर उवाच एवमेतन्महाराज येन जातः स एव सः। तपसस्त्वपकर्षेण जातिग्रहणतां गतः॥ सुक्षेत्राच्च सुबीजाच्च पुण्यो भवति सम्भवः। अतोऽन्यतरतो हीनादवरो नाम जायते॥
en: Parashara said It is as you say, O king! The offspring begotten by one is none else than the begetter himself. Because men have deviated from penance, this distribution into classes of different colours has taken place. When the soil and the seed is good, the offspring produced become meritorious. If, however, the soil and seed are inferior, the offspring that will be born will be inferior.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: वक्त्राद् भुजाभ्यामूरुभ्यां पद्भ्यां चैवाथ जज्ञिरे। सृजतः प्रजापतेर्लोकानिति धर्मविदो विदुः॥
en: Persons well read in the scriptures know that when the Lord of all creatures began to create the worlds, some creatures originated from his mouth, some from his arms, some from his thighs, and some from his feet.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: मुखजा ब्राह्मणास्तात बाहुजाः क्षत्रियाः स्मृताः। उरुजा धनिनो राजन् पादजाः परिचारकाः॥
en: Those who came out of his mouth, O child, were called Brahmanas. Those who originated from his arms were called Kshatriyas. Those, O king, sprang from his thighs, and some from his feet.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: चतुर्णामेव वर्णानामागमः पुरुषर्षभ। अतोऽन्ये त्वतिरिक्ता ये ते वै संकरजाः स्मृताः॥
en: Only these four orders of men, O king, were thus created. They who belong to classes besides these are said to have originated from an intermixture of these.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: क्षत्रियातिरथाम्बष्ठा उग्रा वैदेहकास्तथा। श्वपाकाः पुल्कसाः स्तेना निषादाः सूतमागधाः॥ अयोगाः करणा व्रात्याश्चाण्डालाच नराधिप। एते चतुर्थ्यो वर्णेभ्यो जायन्ते वै परस्परात्॥
en: The Kshatriyas called Atirathas, Amvashthas, Ugras, Vaidehas, Shvapakas, Pukasas, Stenas, Nishadas, Sutas, and Chandalas, O monarch, have all originated form the four original castes by intermixture with one another.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: जनक उवाच ब्रह्मणैकेन जातानां नानात्वं गोत्रतः कथम्। बहूनीह हि लोके वै गोत्राणि मुनिसत्तम॥
en: Janka said When all have originated from Brahman alone, how did human beings become divergent of race? O best of ascetics, numberless diversity of races is seen in this world.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: यत्र तत्र कथं जाताः स्वयोनि मुनयो गताः। शुद्धयोनौ समुत्पन्ना वियोनौ च तथा परे॥
en: How could, men devoted to penances acquire the dignity of Brahmanas, though of indiscriminate origin? Indeed, those born in pure wombs and those in impure, all became Brahmanas.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: पराशर उवाच राजन्नेतद् भवेद् ग्राह्यमपकृष्टेन जन्मना। महात्मनां समुत्पत्तिस्तपसा भावितात्मनाम्॥
en: O king, that status of great persons who succeeded in purifying their souls by penances could not be regarded as affected by their low births.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: उत्पाद्य पुत्रान् मुनयो नृपते यत्र तत्र ह। स्वेनैव तपसा तेषामृषित्वं विदधुः पुनः॥
en: Great Rishi, O monarch, by begetting children in indiscriminate wombs, gave them the dignity of Rishis by means of their power of asceticism.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: पितामहश्च मे पूर्वमृष्यशृङ्गश्च काश्यपः। वेदस्ताण्ड्यः कृपश्चैव कक्षीवान् कमठादयः॥ यवक्रीतश्च नृपते द्रोणच वदतां वरः। आयुर्मतङ्गो दत्तश्च दुपदो मत्स्य एव च॥ एते स्वां प्रकृति प्राप्ता वैदेह तपसोऽऽश्रयात्। प्रतिष्ठिता वेदविदो दमेन तपसैव हि॥
en: My grandfather Vashishtha, Rishyashringa, Kashyapa, Veda, Tandya, Kripa, Kakshivat, Kamatha, and others, and Yavakrita, O king, and Drona, that foremost of speakers, and Ayu, and Matanga and Datta, and Drupada, and Matsya-all these, O king of the Videhas, gained their respective positions through penance as the means.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: मूलगोत्राणि चत्वारि समुत्पन्नानि पार्थिव। अङ्गिराः कश्यपश्चैव वसिष्ठो भृगुरेव च॥
en: Originally only four families arose, O king viz., Angiras, Kashyapa, Vashishtha and Bhrigu.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: कर्मतोऽन्यानि गोत्राणि समुत्पन्नानि पार्थिव। नामधेयानि तपसा तानि च ग्रहणं सताम्॥
en: On account of acts and behaviour, O king, many other families came into existence in time. The names of those families have originated from the penances of those who have founded them. Good people use them.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: जनक उवाच विशेषधर्मान् वर्णानां प्रबूहि भगवन् मम। ततः सामान्यधर्माश्च सर्वत्र कुशलो ह्यसि॥
en: Janaka said Tell me, O holy one, the especial duties of the several castes. Tell me also with their common duties are. You know everything.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: पराशर उवाच प्रतिग्रहो याजनं च तथैवाध्यापनं नृप। विशेषधर्मा विप्राणां रक्षा क्षत्रस्य शोभना॥
en: Parashara said Taking gifts, officiating at the sacrifices of others, the teaching of pupils, O king, are the especial duties of the Brahmanas. The protection of the other castes is the special duty of the Kshatriya.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: कृषिश्च पाशुपाल्यं च वाणिज्यं च विशामपि। द्विजानां परिचर्या च शूद्रकर्म नराधिप॥
en: Agriculture, cattle-tending, and trade are the duties, of the Vaishyas. While service of the (three) twice-born classes is the duty, 0 king, of the Shudras.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: विशेषधर्मा नृपते वर्णानां परिकीर्तिताः। धर्मान् साधारणांस्तात विस्तरेण शृणुष्व मे॥
en: I have now told you what the especial duties are of the four castes, O king. Hear, now, O child as I tell you what the common duties are of all the four castes.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: आनृशंस्यमहिंसा चाप्रमादः संविभागिता। श्राद्धकर्मातिथेयं च सत्यमक्रोध एव च॥ स्वेषु दारेषु संतोषः शौचं नित्यानसूयता। आत्मज्ञानं तितिक्षा च धर्माः साधारणा नृप॥
en: Compassion, abstention from injury, carefulness, giving to others what is due to them, Shraddhas in honour of departed manes, hospitality to guests, truthfulness, subjugation of anger, contentedness with one's own married wives, purity, freedom from malice, knowledge of Self, and Renunciation,-these duties, O king are common to all the castes.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: ब्राह्मणा: क्षत्रिया वैश्यास्त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः। अत्र तेषामधीकारो धर्मेषु द्विपदां वर॥
en: Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas,these are the three twice-born orders, They have all an equal right to the performance of these dutics, O foremost of men.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: विकर्मावस्थिता वर्णाः पतन्ते नृपते त्रयः। उन्नमन्ति यथासन्तमाश्रित्येह स्वकर्मसु॥
en: These three castes following the duties Other than those sanctioned for them, suffer indignity, O king, as they go up and acquire great merit by taking for their model some righteous individual of their respective classes who duly satisfies his own duties.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: न चापि शूद्रः पततीति निश्चयो न चापि संस्कारमिहार्हतीति वा। श्रुतिप्रवृत्तं न च धर्ममाप्नुते न चास्य धर्मे प्रतिषेधनं कृतम्॥
en: The Shudra never falls down; nor is he worthy of any of the rites of regeneration. The course of duties originating from the Vedas is not his. He is not interdicted, however, from practising the thirteen duties which are common to all the castes.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: वैदेह कं शूद्रमुदाहरन्ति द्विजा महाराज श्रुतोपपन्नाः। अहं हि पश्यामि नरेन्द्र देवं विश्वस्य विष्णु जगतः प्रधानम्॥
en: O king of the Videhas, Brahmanas learned in the Vedas, O king, regard a (virtutous) Shudra as equal to Brahman himself. I, however, O king, regard such a Shudra as the effulgent Vishnu of the universe, the foremost one in all the worlds.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: सतां वृत्तमधिष्ठाय निहीना उद्दिधीर्षवः। मन्त्रवर्जं न दुष्यन्ति कुर्वाणाः पौष्टिकी: क्रियाः॥
en: Persons of the lowest caste, desiring to root out the evil passions, may follow the conduct of the good; and, while so acting, they may acquire great merit by performing all rites that lead to advancement, omitting the Mantras which are to be uttered by the other castes while performing the self-same ceremonies.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: यथा यथा हि सद्वृत्तमालम्बन्तीतरे जनाः। तथा तथा सुखं प्राप्य प्रेत्य चेह च मोदते।॥
en: Wherever persons of the lowest caste follow the conduct of the good, they succeed in acquiring happiness on account of which they are able to pass their time in happiness both in this world and the next.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: जनक उवाच किं कर्म दूषयत्येनमथो जातिर्महामुने। संदेहो मे समुत्पन्नस्तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Janaka said O great ascetic, is man sullied by his deeds or is he stained by the order or class in which he is born? A doubt has arisen in my mind. You should expound this to me.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: पराशर उवाच असंशयं महाराज उभयं दोषकारकम्। कर्म चैव हि जातिश्च विशेषं तु निशामय॥
en: Parashara said Forsooth, O king, both, viz., acts and birth, are sources of demerit. Listen now to their difference.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: जात्या च कर्मणा चैव दुष्टं कर्म न सेवते। जात्या दुष्टश्च य: पापं न करोति स पूरुषः॥
en: That man who, though sullied by birth, does not coinmit sin, abstains from sin notwithstanding birth and acts.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: जात्या प्रधानं पुरुषं कुर्वाणं कर्म धिक्कृतम्। कर्म तद् दूषयत्येनं तस्मात् कर्म न शोभनम्॥
en: If, however, a person of superior birth perpetrates censurable deeds, such acts pollute him. Hence, of the two, viz., acts and birth, acts pollute man.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: जनक उवाच कानि कर्माणि धाणि लोकेऽस्मिन् द्विजसत्तम। न हिंसन्तीह भूतानि क्रियमाणानि सर्वदा॥
en: Janaka said What are those righteous acts in this world, 0 best of all twice-born ones, the accomplishment of which does not inflict any injury upon other creatures?

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: पराशर उवाच शृणु मेऽत्र महाराज यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। यानि कर्माण्यहिंस्राणि नरं त्रायन्ति सर्वदा॥
en: Parashara said Hear from me, O king, about what you ask, viz.., those acts free from injury which always rescue man.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: संन्यस्याग्नीनुदासीनाः पश्यन्ति विगतज्वराः। नैःश्रेयसं कर्मपथं समारुह्य यथाक्रमम्॥ प्रश्रिता विनयोपेता दमनित्याः सुसंशिताः। प्रयान्ति स्थानमजरं सर्वकर्मविवर्जिताः॥
en: Those who, keeping aside their domestic fires, have freed themselves from all worldly attachments, become freed from all anxieties. Gradually getting up step by step, in the path of Yoga, they at last see the stage of highest happiness. Gifted with faith and humility, always practising self-control, possessed of keen intelligence, and abstaining from all acts, they acquire eternal happiness.

description: The origin of the difference of colour amongst different orders. The birth of various castes
sn: सर्वे वर्णा धर्मकार्याणि सम्यक् कृत्वा राजन् सत्यवाक्यानि चोक्त्वा। त्यक्तवाधर्म दारुणं जीवलोके यान्ति स्वर्ग नात्र कार्यो विचारः॥
en: All classes of men, O king, by duly doing virtuous acts, by speaking the truth, and by abstaining from sin, in this world, go up to heaven. There is no doubt in this.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: पराशर उवाच पिता सखायो गुरवः स्त्रियश्च न निर्गुणानां हि भवन्ति लोके। अनन्यभक्ता: प्रियवादिनश्च हिताश्च वश्याश्च भवन्ति राजन्॥
en: Parashara said The father, the friends, the preceptors, and the wishes of the preceptors of men who are shorn of devotion, are unable to give to those men the merits derivable from devotion. Only they who are firmly devoted to such elders, who speak what is agreeable to them, who speek their well-being, and who are submissive to them in conduct, can acquire the merit to devotion.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: पिता परं दैवतं मानवानां मातुर्विशिष्टं पितरं वदन्ति। ज्ञानस्य लाभं परमं वदन्ति जितेन्द्रियार्थाः परमाप्नुवन्ति॥
en: That father is the highest of gods with his children. It is said that the father is superior to the mother. The acquirement of Knowledge is are considered as the hightest acquisition. They who have subjugating the objects of the senses, acquire what is highest.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: रणाजिरे यत्र शराग्निसंस्तरे नृपात्मजो घातमवाप्य दह्यते। प्रयाति लोकानमरैः सुदुर्लभान्। निषेवते स्वर्गफलं यथासुखम्॥
en: That Kshatriya prince, who going to the battle-field, receives wounds amid fiery arrows shooting in all directions and burns therewith, certainly goes to regions which unattainable by the very gods and, arrived there enjoys the happiness of heaven in perfect contentiment.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: श्रान्तं भीतं भ्रष्टशस्त्रं रुदन्तं पराङ्मुखं पारिबहश्च हीनम्। अनुद्यन्तं रोगिणं याचमानं न वै हिंस्याद् बालवृद्धौ च राजन्॥
en: A Kshatriya should not, O king, strike one who is fatigued, or one who is terrified, or one who has been disarmed, or one who is weeping, or one who is reluctant to fight, or one who is unequipped with mail and cars and horse and infantry, or one who has ceased to exert in the fight, or one who is ill, or one who cries for quarter. Or one who is of tender years, or one who is old.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: पारिबहः सुसंयुक्तमुद्यतं तुल्यतां गतम्। अतिक्रमेत् तं नृपतिः संग्रामे क्षत्रियात्मजम्॥
en: A Kshatriya should, in battle, fight one of his order, who is equipped with mail and cars and horse and infantry who is ready for battle, and who is a compeer.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: तुल्यादिह वधः श्रेयान् विशिष्टाच्चेति निश्चयः। निहीनात् कातराच्चैव कृपणाद् गर्हितो वधः॥
en: Death at the hands of one who is equal or of a superior is praiseworthy, but not that at the hands of one that is low, or of one who is a coward, or of one who is a wretch. This is well known.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: पापात् पापसमाचारनिहीनाच्च नराधिप। पाप एव वधः प्रोक्तो नरकायेति निश्चयः॥
en: Death at the hands of one who is sinful, or of one who is of low birth and wicked conduct, O king is infamous and leads to hell.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: न कश्चित् त्राति वै राजन् दिष्टान्तवशमागतम्। सावशेषायुषं चापि कश्चिन्नैवापकर्षति॥
en: One whose lease of life has run out, cannot be saved by any body. Likewise, one whose lease of life has not run out can never be killed by any one.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: स्निग्धैश्च क्रियमाणानि कर्माणीह निवर्तयेत्। हिंसात्मकानि सर्वाणि नायुरिच्छेत् परायुषा॥
en: One should prevent his affectionate elders from doing to his such acts as done by menials, as also all such acts as can injure others. One should never wish to extend his own life by taking the lives of others.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: गृहस्थानां तु सर्वेषां विनाशमभिकासताम्। निधनं शोभनं तात पुलिनेषु क्रियावताम्॥
en: When they sacrifice their lives, it is laudable for all householders observing the duties of men living in sacred places to give up their lives on the banks of sacred rivers.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: आयुषि क्षयमापन्ने पञ्चत्वमुपगच्छति। तथा ह्यकारणाद् भवति कारणैरुपपादितम्॥
en: When one lease of life is over, his body dissolved into the five elements. Sometimes this occurs suddenly and some times it is brought about by (natural) causes.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: तथा शरीरं भवति देहाद् येनोपपादितम्। अध्वानं गतकशायं प्राप्तश्चायं गृहाद् गृहम्॥
en: He who having obtained a body, destroys it himself becomes invested with another body of a similar nature. Though set on the path of Liberation, he yet becomes a traveller and acquires another body like a person going from one room into another.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: द्वितीयं कारणं तत्र नान्यत् किंचन विद्यते। तद् देहं देहिनां युक्तं पञ्चभूतेषु वर्तते॥
en: About such a man's attainment of a second body the only cause is his accidental death. There is no second cause. That new body which embodied creatures obtain, comes into existence and becomes attached to Rudras and Pishachas.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: शिरास्नायवस्थिसंघातं बीभत्सामेध्यसंकुलम्। भूतानामिन्द्रियाणां च गुणानां च समागमम्॥ त्वगन्तं देहमित्याहुर्विद्वांसोऽध्यात्मचिन्तकाः। गुणैरपि परिक्षीणं शरीरं मर्त्यतां गतम्॥
en: Learned men, conversant with spiritual science say that the body is a compound of arteries and sinews and bones and much repulsive and impure matter and a compound of essences, and the senses and the objects of the senses born of desire, all having an outer cover of skin close to them. Shorn of beauty and other accomplishments, this compound, through force of the desires of a pristine life, assumes a human forin.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: शरीरिणा परित्यक्तं निश्चेष्टं गतचेतनम्। भूतैः प्रकृतिमापन्नस्ततो भूमौ निमज्जति॥
en: Left off by the owner, the body becomes inanimate and motionless. Indeed, when the principal ingredients return to their respective natures, the body is mixed up with the dust.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: भावितं कर्मयोगेन जायते तत्र तत्र ह। इदं शरीरं वैदेह म्रियते यत्र यत्र ह।
en: Caused by its union with deeds, this body reappears under circumstances determined by its deeds. Indeed O king of the Videhas, under whatever circumstances this body is dissolved, its next birth, determined by the these circumstances, is seen to enjoy and endure the fruits of all its pristine deeds.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: तत्स्वभावोऽपरो दृष्टो विसर्गः कर्मणस्तथा॥ न जायते तु नृपते कंचित् कालमयं पुनः।
en: Individual Soul after dissolution of the body is inhabited, does not, O king, take birth in a different body at once.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: परिभ्रमति भूतात्मा द्यामिवाम्बुधरो महान्॥ स पुनर्जायते राजन् प्राप्येहायतनं नृप।
en: ones It roves through the sky for sometime take a spacious cloud. Getting a new receptacle, O king, it then takes birth again.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: मनसः परमो ह्यात्मा इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः॥ विविधानां च भूतानां जङ्गमाः परमा नृपा
en: The Soul is above the mind. The mind is above the senses. Mobile creatures, again, are foremost of all created objects.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: जङ्गमानामपि तथा द्विपदाः परमा गताः॥ द्विपदानामपि तथा द्विजा वै परमाः समृताः।
en: Amongst mobile creatures the two legged are superior. Amongst two-legged creatures, those that are are twice-born are superior.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: द्विजानामपि राजेन्द्र प्रज्ञावन्तः परा मताः। प्राज्ञानामात्मसम्बुद्धाः सम्बुद्धानाममानिनः॥
en: Amongst those that are twice-born they who are endued with wisdom are superior. Amongst them who are endued with wisdom they that have succeeded in acquiring a knowledge of the soul are superior. Amongst those who are endued with a knowledge of the soul, those who are endued with humility are superior.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: जातमन्वेति मरणं नणामिति विनिश्चयः। अन्तवन्ति हि कर्माणि सेवन्ते गुणतः प्रजाः॥
en: Death follows birth in all men. This is settled. Creatures, influenced by the qualities of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance, pursue acts which have an end.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: आपन्ने तूत्तरां काष्ठां सूर्ये यो निधनं व्रजेत्। नक्षत्रे च मुहूर्ते च पुण्ये राजन् स पुण्यकृत्॥ अयोजयित्वा क्लेशेन जनं प्लाव्य च दुष्कृतम्। मृत्युनाऽऽत्मकृते नेह कर्म कृत्वाऽऽत्पशक्तिभिः॥
en: That man is considered as righteous who meets with dissolution when the Sun is in the northern declension, and at a time and under a constellation both of which are sacred and auspicious, He is righteous who, having purified himself of all sins and performed all his acts according to the best of his might and having abstained from giving pain to any man, meets with death when it comes.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: विषमुटबन्धनं दाहो दस्युहस्तात् तथा वधः। दंष्ट्रिभ्यश्च पशुभ्यश्च प्राकृतो वध उच्यते॥
en: The death that one meets with by taking poision, by hanging, by burning, at the hands of robbers and at the teeth of animals, is said to be an infamous one.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: न चैभिः पुण्यकर्माणो युज्यन्ते चाभिसंधिजैः। एवंविधैश्च बहुभिरपरैः प्राकृतैरपि॥
en: Those man who are righteous never meet with such or similar deaths even if they be afflicted with mental and physical diseases of the most painful sort.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: ऊर्ध्वं भित्त्वा प्रतिष्ठन्ते प्राणाः पुण्यवतां नृप। मध्यतो मध्यपुण्यानामधो दुष्कृतकर्मणाम्॥ रज्ञानतुल्यः पुरुषस्य राजन्। येनावृतः कुरुते सम्प्रयुक्तो घोराणि कर्माणि सुदारुणानि॥
en: The lives of the pious, O king, piercing through the Sun, ascend into the regions of Brahman. The lives of those who are both righteous and sinful rove in the middle regions. The lives of those who are sinful sink into the lowest depths. There is one only enemy (of man) and not another. That enemy is at one with Ignorance, O king. Overwhelmed by it, is led to perpetrate frightful and exceedingly cruel deeds.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: प्रबाधनार्थं श्रुतिधर्मयुक्तान्। वृद्धानुपास्य प्रभवेत यस्य। प्रयत्नसाध्यो हि स राजपुत्र प्रज्ञाशरेणोन्मथितः परैति॥
en: That enemy for resisting which one should display his energy waiting upon the aged according to the duties laid down in the Shrutis,-~-that enemy which cannot be Overcome except by steady endeavours,-meets with destruction, O king, only when it is crushed by the arrows of wisdom. One

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: अधीत्य वेदं तपसा ब्रह्मचारी यज्ञाज्यशक्त्या संनिगृह्येह पञ्च। वनं गच्छेत् पुरुषो धर्मकामः श्रेयः स्थित्वा स्थापयित्वा स्ववंशम्॥
en: The man desirous of acquiring merit should at first study the Vedas and practise penances, becoming a Brahimacharin. He should next, becoming a householder, perform the usual Sacrifices. Establishing his race, he should then enter the forest, controlling his senses, and desirous of acquiring Liberation.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: उपभोगैरपि त्यक्तं नात्मानं सादयेन्नरः। चण्डालत्वेऽपि मानुष्यं सर्वथा तात शोभनम्॥
en: One should never emaciate himself by abstaining from every enjoyment. Of all births, that of a human being is preferable even if one has to become a Chandala.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: इयं हि योनिः प्रथमा यां प्राप्य जगतीपते। आत्मा वै शक्यते त्रातुं कर्मभिः शुभलक्षणैः॥
en: Indeed, O king, that order of birth (viz., humanity) is the foremost, since by becoming a human being one succeeds in rescuing his self by meritorious acts.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: कथं न विप्रणश्येम योनितोऽस्या इति प्रभो। कुर्वन्ति धर्मं मनुजा: श्रुतिप्रामाण्यदर्शनात्॥
en: Men always perform righteous acts, O lord, guided by the authority of the Shrutis, so that they may not deviate from the status of humanity.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: यो दुर्लभतरं प्राप्य मानुष्यं द्विषते नरः। धर्मावमन्ता कामात्मा भवेत्स खलु वञ्च्यते॥
en: That man who, having been born as a man that is so difficult of attainment, indulges in malice, disregards righteousness and gives way :o desire, is certainly betrayed by his desires.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: यस्तु प्रीतिपुरोगेन चक्षुषा तात पश्यति। दीपोपमानि भूतानि यावदर्थान्न पश्यति॥ सान्त्वेनानप्रदानेन प्रियवादेन चाप्युत। समदुःखसुखो भूत्वा स परत्र महीयते॥
en: That man who regards all creatures impartially guided by affection, considering them worthy of being cherished with loving, aid, who disregards all sorts of wealth, who offers them consolation, gives them food, addresses them in sweet words, and who rejoices in their happiness and grieves in their sorrows, has never to suffer misery in the next world.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: दानं त्यागः शोभना मूर्तिरद्भ्यो भूतप्लाव्यं तपसा वै शरीरम्। सरस्वतीनैमिषपुष्करेषु ये चाप्यन्ये पुण्यदेशाः पृथिव्याम्॥
en: Repairing to the Sarasvati, the Naimisha forest, the Pushkara lake, and the other sacred spots on Earth, one should make gifts, practise renunciation, render his aspect amiable, O king, and purify his body with baths and penances.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: गृहेषु येषामसवः पतन्ति तेषामथो निर्हरणं प्रशस्तम्। यानेन वै प्रापणं च श्मशाने शौचेन नूनं विधिना चैव दाहः॥
en: Those men who meet with death within their houses should have their bodies cremated. Their bodies bodies should should be be taken to the crematorium on cars and there they should be burnt according to the rites of purification that have been laid down in the scriptures,

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: इष्टिः पुष्टिर्यजनं याजनं च दानं पुण्यानां कर्मणां च प्रयोगः। शक्त्या पित्र्यं यच्च किंचित् प्रशस्तं सर्वाण्यात्मार्थे मानवोऽयं करोति॥
en: Religious rites, beneficial ceremonies, the performance of sacrifices, officiation at the sacrifices of others, gifts, the doing of other meritorious deeds, the performance according to the best of his power, of all that has been ordained in in the case of his deceased ancestors,-all these one does for benefiting his own self.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: धर्मशास्त्राणि वेदाश्च षडङ्गानि नराधिप। श्रेयसोऽर्थे विधीयन्ते नरस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥
en: O king! All the scriptures of righteousness and the Vedas with six angas proceed for the welfare of sinless one.

description: Discourse on Kshatriya duties and death
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतद् वै सर्वमाख्यातं मुनिना सुमहात्मना। विदेहराजाय पुरा श्रेयसोऽर्थे नराधिप॥
en: Bhishma continued All this was said by that great sage to the king of the Videhas, O king, in days of yore for his well-being.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: भीम उवाच पुनरेव तु पप्रच्छ जनको मिथिलाधिपः। पराशरं महात्मानं धर्मे परमनिश्चयम्॥
en: Daksha said Once again Janaka, the king of Mithila, asked the great Parashara gifted with certain knowledge regarding all duties.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: जनक उवाच किं श्रेयः का गतिर्ब्रह्मन् किं कृतं न विनश्यति। क्व गतो न निवर्तेत तन्मे ब्रूहि महामते॥
en: Janaka said What yields good? What is the best path (for living creatures)? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that spot going where one has not to return? Tell me all this, O you of great intelligence.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: पराशर उवाच असङ्ग श्रेयसो मूलं ज्ञानं चैव परा गतिः। चीर्णं तपो न प्रणश्येद्वापः क्षेत्रे न नश्यति॥
en: Parashara said Dissociation is the root of what is good. Knowledge is the greatest path. Penances practised are never destroyed. Gifts also, made to worthy persons, are not lost.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: छित्त्वाधर्ममयं पाशं यदा धर्मेऽभिरज्यते। दत्त्वाभयकृतं दानं तदा सिद्धिमवाप्नुते॥
en: When one, snapping the fetters of sin, begins to take pleasure in virtue, and when one makes that highest of all gifts, viz., the promise of all harmlessness to all creatures, then does one acquire success.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: यो ददाति सहस्राणि गवामश्वशतानि च। अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यः सदा तमभिवर्तते॥
en: He who gives away thousands of kine and hundreds of horses, and who promises harmlessness to all creatures receives in return the promise of harmlessness from all.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: वसन् विषयमध्येऽपि न वसत्येव बुद्धिमान्। संवसत्येव दुर्बुदिरसत्सु विषयेष्वपि॥
en: One may live in the midst of all sorts or riches and cnjoyment, yet, if blessed with intelligence, one does not live in them; while he who is shorn of intelligence lives wholly in objects of enjoyment which unsubstantial.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: नाधर्मः श्लिष्यते प्राज्ञं पयः पुष्करपर्णवत्। अप्राज्ञमधिकं पापं श्लिष्यते जतुकाष्ठवत्॥
en: Sin cannot attach to a wise man as water cannot drench the leaves of the lotus. Sin sticks more firmly to him who is without attachment as lac and wood stick firmly to each other.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: नाधर्मः कारणापेक्षी कर्तारमभिमुञ्चति। कर्ता खलु यथाकालं ततः समभिपद्यते॥ न भिद्यन्ते कृतात्मान आत्मप्रत्ययदर्शिनः।
en: Sin, which cannot be dissipated except by endurance of its fruits, never leaves the doer. The doer, when the time comes, has to suffer the consequences thereof. They, however, who are of purified souls and who realise the cxistence of Brahma, are never afflicted by the fruits of their deeds. are even

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: बुद्धिकर्मेन्द्रियाणां हि प्रमत्तो यो न बुद्ध्यते। शुभाशुभे प्रसक्तात्मा प्राप्नोति सुमहद् भयम्॥
en: Careless in about one's senses of knowledge and of action, one who is not conscious of his wicked deeds, and whose heart is attached to both good and bad, becomes afflicted with great fear.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: वीतरागो जितक्रोधः सम्यग् भवति यः सदा। विषये वर्तमानोऽपि न स पापेन युज्यते॥
en: One who at all times becomes entirely freed from attachments and who completely subdues the passion of anger, is never sullied by sin even if he lives in the enjoyment of worldly objects.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: मर्यादायां धर्मसेतुर्निबद्धो नैव सीदति। पुष्टस्रोत इवासक्तः स्फीतो भवति संचयः॥
en: As a dyke set across a river, if not washed away, makes the waters thereof to swell up, so the man who, without being attached to objects of pleasure, creates the dyke of virtue whose materials consist of the limitations set down in the scriptures, has never to wane away. On the other hand, his merits and penances, increase.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: यथा भानुगतं तेजो मणिः शुद्धः समाधिना। आदत्ते राजशार्दूल तथा योगः प्रवर्तते।॥
en: As the pure gem absorbs and attracts to itself, according to the natural law, the rays of the Sun, so, O foremost of kings, does Yoga proceed by help of rapt attention.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: यथा तिलानामिह पुष्पसंश्रयात् पृथक्पृथग्याति गुणोऽतिसौम्यताम्। तथा नराणां भुवि भावितात्मनां यथाऽऽश्रयं सत्त्वगुणः प्रवर्तते॥
en: As sesame seeds, for being always with sweet-scented flowers, become in respect of quality very sweet, so the quality of Goodness arises in men proportionate to the extent of their association with persons of purified souls.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: जहाति दारांश्च जहाति सम्पदः पदं च यानं विविधाश्च याः क्रिया:। स्तदास्य बुद्धिर्विषयेषु भिद्यते॥
en: When one becomes desirous of living in heaven, he abandons his wives and riches and rank and vehicles and various sorts of good deeds. indeed, when one gets such a bent of mind, his understanding is said to be dissociated from the objects of the senses.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: प्रसक्तबुद्धिर्विषयेषु यो नरो न बुध्यते ह्यात्महितं कथंचन। स सर्वभावानुगतेन चेतसा नृपाभिषेणेव झषो विकृष्यते॥
en: That man who, with understanding attached to the objects of the senses, becomes blind to what is for his real well-beings, is dragged by his heart which runs after all earthly objects, like a fish by the bait of meat.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: संघातवन्मर्त्यलोकः परस्परमपाश्रितः। कदलीगर्भनि:सारो नौरिवाप्सु निमज्जति॥
en: Like the body that is made up of different limbs and organs, all mortal creatures exist depending upon one another. They are weak like the pith of the banana plant. They sink in the world's ocean like a boat.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: निश्चितो न चापि मृत्युः पुरुषं प्रतीक्षते। सदा हि धर्मस्य क्रियैव शोभना यदा नरो मृत्युमुखेऽभिवर्तते॥
en: There is no fixed time for the acquisition of virtue. Death waits for no man. When man is constantly running towards the jaws of Death, the doing of pious deeds is proper at all times.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: यथान्धः स्वगृहे युक्तो ह्यभ्यासादेव गच्छति। तथा युक्तेन मनसा प्राज्ञो गच्छति तां गतिम्॥
en: Like a blind man who, with attention, can move about his own house, the wise man, with mind fixed on Yoga, can proceed along the road.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: मरणं जन्मनि प्रोक्तं जन्म वै मरणाश्रितम्। अविद्वान् मोक्षधर्मेषु बद्धो भ्रमति चक्रवत्। न धर्मकाल: पुरुषस्य
en: It has been said that death originates from birth. Birth is subject to the control of death. One unacquainted with the course of the duties of Liberation revolves like a wheel between birth and death, unable to free himself from that fate.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: बुद्धिमार्गप्रयातस्य सुखं त्विह परत्र च॥ विस्तराः क्लेशसंयुक्ताः संक्षेपास्तु सुखावहाः। परार्थं विस्तराः सर्वे त्यागमात्महितं विदुः॥
en: One who walks along the road recommended by the understanding acquires happiness both in this world and the next. Many of them are fraught with misery; while the Few yield happiness. Fruits represented by Nescience form the Many. Renunciation yields the soul's happiness.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: यथा मृणालानुगतमाशु मुञ्चति कर्दमम्। तथाऽऽत्मा पुरुषस्येह मनसा परिमुच्यते॥
en: As the lotus stalk quickly leaves the mire attached to it, so the Soul can quickly renounce the mind.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: मनः प्रणयतेऽऽत्मानं स एनमभियुञ्जति। युक्तो यदा स भवति तदा तं पश्यते परम्॥
en: It is the mind that at first inclines the Soul to Yoga. The latter then merges the former into itself. When the Soul gains success in Yoga, it then sees itself invested with qualities.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: परार्थे वर्तमानस्तु स्वं कार्यं योऽभिमन्यते। इन्द्रियार्थेषु संयुक्तः स्वकार्यात् परिमुच्यते॥
en: Engaged amid the objects of the senses, one who considers such engagement to be his employment falls away from his true employment on account of such devotion to those objects.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: अधस्तिर्यग्गतिं चैव स्वर्गे चैव परां गतिम्। प्राप्नोति स्वकृतैरात्मा प्राज्ञस्येहेतरस्य च॥
en: The soul of the wise man acquires, through its pious deeds, a state of great happiness in heaven, while that of the man who is not endued with wisdom sinks very low or is born among intermediate creatures.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: मृण्मये भाजने पक्वे यथा वै नश्यति द्रवः। तथा शरीरं तपसा तप्तं विषयमश्नुते॥
en: As a liquid substance, if kept in a baked earthen pot, does not escape therefrom but remains undiminished similarly, one's body with which one had practised penances enjoys (without rejecting) all objects of pleasure.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: विषयानुश्नुते यस्तु न स भोक्ष्यत्यसंशयम्। यस्तु भोगांस्त्यजेदात्मा स वै भोक्तुं व्यवस्यति॥
en: Verily, that man who enjoys earthly objects can never be liberated. That man, however, who renounces such objects, succeeds in enjoying great happiness hereafter.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: नीहारेण हि संवीतः शिश्नोदरपरायणः। जात्यन्ध इव पन्थानमावृतात्मा न बुद्ध्यते॥
en: Like one suffering from blindness and, therefore, incapable of seeing his way, the sensualist, with soul confined in an opaque case, seems to be surrounded by a mist and cannot see (the true object).

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: वणिग् यथा समुद्राद् वै यथार्थं लभते धनम्। तथा मार्णवे जन्तोः कर्मविज्ञानतो गतिः॥
en: As merchants, going across the sea, make profits according to their capital, so creatures, in this world of men, attain to ends proportionate to their respective deeds.

description: What yields good. What is the best path? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that place from which there is no return? Parasara's replies
sn: अहोरात्रमये लोके जरारूपेण संसरन्। मृत्युर॑सति भूतानि पवनं पन्नगो यथा॥
en: Like a snake devouring air, Death walks in this world made up of days and nights in the form of Decrepitude and devours all ceatures.
