en: A perfect adept in that department of knowledge which is about the Soul and gifted with sure conclusions about all branches of that science, as Mairtravaruni, that foremost of Rishis, was seated, the king, approaching him with joined hands, asked him in humble words, well said and sweet and shorn of all controversial spirit, this question,-O holy one, I wish to hear of Supreme and Eternal Brahma by attaining to which men of wisdom have not to return.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: यच्च तत् क्षरमित्युक्तं यत्रेदं क्षरते जगत्। यच्चाक्षरमिति प्रोक्तं शिवं क्षेम्यमनामयम्॥
en: I wish also to know that which is called Destructible and That into which this universe goes when destroyed. Indeed, what is That which is said to be indestructible. Auspicious, wholesome and free from all sorts of evil.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच श्रूयतां पृथिवीपाल क्षरतीदं यथा जगत्। यन्न क्षरति पूर्वेण यावत्कालेन वाप्यथ॥
en: Hear, O king, as to how this universe is destroyed, and of That which was never destroyed and which will never be destroyed at any time.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: युगं द्वादशसाहस्रं कल्पं विद्धि चतुर्युगम्। दशकल्पशतावृत्तमहस्तद् ब्राह्ममुच्यते॥
en: Twelve thousand years make a cycle. Four such cycles, taken a thousand times, make a Kalpa which measures one day of Brahman.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: रात्रिश्चैतावती राजन् यस्यान्ते प्रतिबुद्ध्यते। सृजत्यनन्तकर्माणं महान्तं भूतमग्रजम्॥ मूर्तिमन्तममूर्तात्मा विश्वं शम्भुः स्वयम्भुवः। अणिमा लघिमा प्राप्तिरीशानं ज्योतिरव्ययम्॥ सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत् सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्। सर्वतःश्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति॥
en: Brahman's night also, O king, is of the same measure. When Brahman himself is destroyed, Shambhu of formless soul and to whom the Yoga attributes of lightness, heaviness, etc., naturally stick, awakes, and once more creates that First of all creatures, possessed of huge proportions, of infinite deeds, endued with form, and at one with the universe. That Shambhu is otherwise called Ishana. He is pure Effulgence, and is above all decay, having his hands and feet stretching on all sides with eyes and head and mouth cverywhere, and with ears also in every place. That Being exists, possessing the entire universe.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: हिरण्यगर्भो भगवानेष बुद्धिरिति स्मृतः। महानिति च योगेषु विरिञ्चिरिति चाप्यजः॥
en: The eldest-born Being is called Hiranyagarbha. This holy one has been called the Understanding. In the Yoga scriptures, He is called the Great, and Virinchi, and the Unborn.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: सांख्ये च पठ्यते शास्त्रे नामभिर्वहुधात्मकः। विचित्ररूपो विश्वात्मा एकाक्षर इति स्मृतः॥
en: In the Sankhya system, He is described by diverse names, and considered as having Infinity for his Soul. Of various forms and constituting the soul of the universe, He is considered as One and Indestructible.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: वृतं नैकात्मकं येन कृतं त्रैलोक्यमात्मना। तथैव बहुरूपत्वाद् विश्वरूप इति स्मृतः॥
en: The three worlds of numberless ingredients have been created by Him without help from any source and have been overwhelmed by him. On account of His manifold forins, He is said to be of universal form.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: एष वै विक्रियापन्नः सृजत्यात्मानमात्मना। अहङ्कारं महातेजाः प्रजापतिमहंकृतम्॥
en: Undergoing changes He creates Himself. Gifted with great energy, He first creates Consciousness and that Great Being called Prajapati endued with Consciousness.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: अव्यक्ताद् व्यक्तमापन्नं विद्यासगं वदन्ति तम्। महान्तं चाप्यहङ्कारमविद्यासर्गमेव च॥
en: The Manifest is created from the Unmanifest. This is called by the learned the Creation of Knowledge. The creation of (Virat) and Consciousness, by Hiranyagarbha, is the Creation of Ignorance.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: अविधिश्च विधिश्चैव समुत्पन्नौ तथैकतः। विद्याविद्येति विख्याते श्रुतिशास्त्रार्थचिन्तकैः॥
en: Allotment of attributes and the destruction thereof, called respectively by the names of Ignorance and Knowledge by persons learned in the Shrutis, then arose, referring to this, that, or the other of the three.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: भूतसर्गमहङ्कारात् तृतीयं विद्धि पार्थिवा अहङ्कारेषु सर्वेषु चतुर्थं विद्धि वैकृतम्॥
en: Know, O king, that the creation of the elements from Consciousness is the third. In all the kinds of Consciousness is the fourth creation which originates from modification of the third.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: वायुयोतिरथाकाशमापोऽथ पृथिवी तथा। शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसो गन्धस्तथैव च॥
en: This fourth creation consists of Wind and Light and Ether and Water and Earth, with their properties of sound, touch, form, taste, and scent. arose

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: एवं युगपदुत्पन्नं दशवर्गमसंशयम्। पञ्चमं विद्धि राजेन्द्र भौतिकं सर्गमर्थवत्॥
en: This aggregate of ten arose, forsooth, at the same time. The fifth creation, O king, is that which has originated, from combinations of the principal elements.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: श्रोत्रं त्वक् चक्षुषी जिह्वा घ्राणमेव च पञ्चमम्। वाक् च हस्तौ च पादौ च पायुर्मेदूं तथैव च॥
en: This comprises the ear, the skin, the eyes, the tongue, and the nose forming the fifth, and speech, and the two hands, and the two legs, and the lower canal, and the organs of generation.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि चैतानि तथा कर्मेन्द्रियाणि च। सम्भूतानीह युगपन्मनसा सह पार्थिव॥
en: The first five of those form the organs of knowledge, and the last five the organs of action. All these, with mind, simultaneously, O king.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: एषा तत्त्वचतुर्विंशा सर्वाकृतिषु वर्तते। यां ज्ञात्वा नाभिशोचन्ति ब्राह्मणास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥
en: These form the twenty-four topics that exist in the forms of all living creatures. By understanding these properly. these properly. Brahmanas endued with insight into the truth have never to give way to sorrow.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: एतद् देहं समाख्यातं त्रैलोक्ये सर्वदेहिषु। वेदितव्यं नरश्रेष्ठ सदेवनरदानवे॥ सयक्षभूतगन्धर्वे सकिन्नरमहोरगे। सचारणपिशाचे वै सदेवर्षिनिशाचरे॥ सदंशकीटमशके सपूतिकृमिमूषिके। शुनि श्वपाके चैणे ये सचाण्डाले सपुल्कसे॥ हस्त्यश्वखरशार्दूले सवृक्षे गवि चैव ह। यच्च मूर्तिमयं किंचित् सर्वत्रैतन्निदर्शनम्॥ जले भुवि तथाऽऽकाशे नान्यत्रेति विनिश्चयः। स्थानं देहवतामासीदित्येवमनुशुश्रुम॥
en: In the three worlds a combination of these, called body, is possessed by all embodied Creatures. Indeed, O king, a combination of those is known as such in gods and men and Danavas, in Yakshas and spirits and Gandharvas, and Kinnaras and great snakes, and Charanas and Pishachas, in celestial Rishis and Rakshasas, in biting flies, and worins, and gnats, and vermin born of filth and rats, and dogs and Shvapakas and Chaineyas and Chandalas and Pukkasas, in elephants and horse and asses and tigers, and trees, and kine. Whatever other creatures exist in water or ether or on earth, for there is on other place in which creatures exist as we have heard, have this combination.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: कृत्स्नमेतावतस्तात क्षरते व्यक्तसंज्ञितम्। अहन्यहनि भूतात्मा ततः क्षर इति स्मृतः॥
en: All these, O sire, included within the class called Manifest, are seen to be destroyed day after day. Hence, all creatures begotten by union of these twenty-four are said to be destructible.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: एतदक्षरमित्युक्तं क्षरतीदं यथा जगत्। जगन्मोहात्मकं प्राहुरव्यक्ताद् व्यक्तसंज्ञकम्॥
en: This then is the Indestructible. And since the universe, which is made up of Manifest and Unmanifest, is destroyed, therefore, it is said to be Destructible.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: महांश्चैवाग्रजो नित्यमेतत् क्षरनिदर्शनम्। कथितं ते महाराज यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: The Very Being called Mahan who is the first born is always spoken of as an instance of the Destructible. I have now told you, O king, all that you had asked me.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: पञ्चविंशतिमो विष्णुर्निस्तत्त्वस्तत्त्वसंज्ञितः। तत्त्वसंश्रयणादेतत् तत्त्वमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: Above the twenty-four topics already referred to is the twenty-fifth called Vishnu. That Vishnu, on account of the absence of all qualities, is not a topic though as that which permeates all the topics, he has been called so by the wise.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: यन्मय॑मसृजद् व्यक्तं तत्तन्मूर्त्यधितिष्ठति। चतुर्विंशतिमोऽव्यक्तो ह्यमूर्तः पञ्चविंशकः॥
en: Since that which is destructible has caused all this that is Manifest, therefore, all this is gifted with form. The twenty-fourth, which is Nature, is said to lord over all this. The twentyfifth, which is Vishnu, is formless and, therefore, cannot be said to lord over the universe.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: स एव हृदि सर्वासु मूर्तिष्वातिष्ठतेऽऽत्मवान्। केवलश्चेतनो नित्यः सर्वमूर्तिरमूर्तिमान्॥
en: It is that Unmanifest, which, when endued with body lives in the hearts of all creatures having body. As regards eternal Consciousness, although he is shorn of attributes and without form, yet he assumes all forins.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: सर्गप्रलयधर्मिण्या असर्गप्रलयात्मकः। गोचरे वर्तते नित्यं निर्गुणं गुणसंज्ञितम्॥
en: Uniting with Nature which has has the attributes of birth and death, he also assumes the attributes of birth and death. And on account of such union he becomes an object of perception and though in reality shorn of all attributes yet he coines to be invested therewith.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: एवमेष महानात्मा सर्गप्रलयकोविदः। विकुर्वाणः प्रकृतिमानभिमन्यत्यबुद्धिमान्॥
en: It is in this way that the Soul, becoming united with Nature and invested with Ignorance, undergoes changes and becomes conscious of Self.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: तमःसत्त्वरजोयुक्तस्तासु तास्विह योनिषु। नियते प्रतिबुद्धित्वादबुद्धजनसेवनात्॥
en: Uniting with the qualities of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance, he becomes at one with various creatures belonging to various orders of Being, on account of his forgetfulness and his waiting upon Ignorance.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: सहवासविनाशित्वान्नान्योऽहमिति मन्यते। योऽहं सोऽहमिति ह्युक्त्वा गुणानेवानुवर्तते॥
en: On account of his birth and death originating from the fact of living in union with Nature, he thinks himself to be no other than what he apparently is, Knowing himself as this or that, he follows the qualities of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: तमसा तामसान् भावान् विविधान् प्रतिपद्यते। रजसा राजसांश्चैव सात्त्विकान् सत्त्वसंश्रयात्॥
en: Under the influence of Ignorance, he comes by various kinds of conditions which are affected by Ignorance. Under the influences of Darkness and Goodness he attains likewise to conditions which are affected by Darkness and Goodness.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: शुक्ललोहितकृष्णानि रूपाण्येतानि त्रीणि तु। सर्वाण्येतानि रूपाणि यानीह प्राकृतानि वै॥
en: There are three colours in all viz., White, Red, and Dark. All those colours belong to Nature.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: तामसा निरयं यान्ति राजसा मानुषानथ। सात्त्विका देवलोकाय गच्छन्ति सुखभागिनः॥
en: Through Ignorance one goes to hell. Through Darkness one attains to the status of humanity. Through Goodness people ascend to the regions of the gods and partake of great happiness.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: निष्कैवल्येन पापेन तिर्यग्योनिमवाप्नुयात्। पुण्यपापेन मानुष्यं पुण्येनैकेन देवताः॥
en: By sticking to sin continuously one sinks into the intermediate order of beings. By acting both virtuously and sinfully one comes by the status of humanity. By acting only righteously, one attains to the status of the gods.

description: How this universe is destroyed. That which was never destroyed and will never be destroyed
sn: एवमव्यक्तविषयं क्षरमाहुर्मनीषिणः। पञ्चविंशतिमो योऽयं ज्ञानादेव प्रवर्तते॥
en: In this way the twenty-fifth, viz., (the Indestructible), the wise say, by union with the unmanifest, becomes changed into (destructible). By means of knowledge, however, the Indestructible appears in His true nature.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच एवमप्रतिबुद्धत्वादवुद्धमनुवर्तते। देहाद् देहसहस्राणि तथा समभिपद्यते॥
en: Vasistha said Thus on account of his forgetfulness the Soul follows Ignorance and acquires thousands of bodies one after another.

sn: तिर्यग्योनिसहस्रेषु कदाचिद् देवतास्वपि। उपपद्यति संयोगाद् गुणैः सह गुणक्षयात्॥
en: He attains to thousands of births among the intermediate orders and sometimes among the very gods on account his union with qualities.

sn: मानुषत्वाद् दिवं याति दिवो मानुष्यमेव च। मानुष्यान्निरयस्थानमानन्त्यं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: From the status of humanity he goes to heaven and from heaven he returns to humanity, and from humanity he sinks into hell for many long years.

sn: कोशकारो यथाऽऽत्मानं कीट: समवरुन्धति। सूत्रतन्तुगुणैर्नित्यं तथायमगुणो गुणैः॥
en: As the worm that make the cocoon does itself completely on all sides by means of the threads it weaves itself, so the Soul, though in reality above all qualities, invests himself on all sides with qualities.

sn: द्वन्द्वमेति च निर्द्वन्द्वस्तासु तास्विह योनिषु। शीर्षरोगेऽक्षिरोगे च दन्तशूले गलग्रहे॥ जलोदरे तृषारोगे ज्वरगण्डे विषूचके। श्वित्रकुष्ठेऽग्निदग्धे च सिध्मापस्मारयोरपि॥ यानि चान्यानि द्वन्द्वानि प्राकृतानि शरीरिषु। उत्पद्यन्ते विचित्राणि तान्येषोऽप्यभिमन्यते॥
en: Though above both happiness and misery, it is thus that he subjects himself to happiness and misery. It is thus also that, though above all discases, the Soul considers himself to be afflicted by headache, opthalmia, toothache, affections of the throat, abdominal dropsy, burning thirst, enlargement of glands, cholera, vitiligo, leprosy, burns, asthma, phthisis, epilepsy, and various other diseases from which embodied creatures suffer.

sn: तिर्यग्योनिसहस्रेषु कदाचिद् देवतास्वपि। अभिमन्यत्यभीमानात् तथैव सुकृतान्यपि॥
en: Considering himself, through error, as born among thousands of creatures in the intermediate orders of being, the sometimes among the gods, he suffer misery and enjoys the fruits of his good deeds.

sn: शुक्लवासाश्च दुर्वासाः शायी नित्यमधस्तथा। मण्डूकशायी च तथा वीरासनगतस्तथा॥ चीरधारणमाकाशे शयनं स्थानमेव च। इष्टकाप्रस्तरे चैव कण्टकप्रस्तरे तथा॥ भस्मप्रस्तरशायी च भूमिशय्या तलेषु च। वीरस्थानाम्बुपके च शयनं फलकेषु च॥ विविधासु च शय्यासु फलगृङ्ख्यान्वितस्तथा। मुञ्जमेखलनग्नत्वं क्षौमकृष्णाजिनानि च॥ शाणीवालपरीधानो व्याघ्रचर्मपरिच्छदः। सिंहचर्मपरीधानः पट्टवासास्तथैव च॥ फलक परिधानश्च तथा कण्टकवस्त्रधृका कीटकावसनश्चैव चीरवासास्तथैव च॥ वस्त्राणि चान्यानि बहून्यभिमन्यत्यबुद्धिमान्। भोजनानि विचित्राणि रत्नानि विविधानि च॥
en: Invested with Ignorance he considers himself as dressed sometimes in white cloth and sometimes in full dress of four pieces, or as lying on floors or with hands and feet contracted like those of frogs, or as seated upright in the position of meditation, or as clad in rags or as lying or sitting under the canopy of heaven or within palaces bult of bricks and stone or on rugged stones or on ashes or bare stones or on the naked earth or on beds or on battle-fields or in water or in mire or on wooden planks or on various sorts of beds; or, moved by desire of fruit, he considers himself as clad in a piece of cloth made of grass or as totally naked or as dressed in silk or in skin of the black antelope or in cloth made of flax or in sheep-skin or in tiger-skin or in lion-skin or in hemp fabric, or in barks of birch or in cloths made of the produce of prickly plants, or in vestures made of threads woven by worms or of tattered rags or in various other sorts of cloth too numerous to mention. The soul considers himself also as wearing various sorts of ornaments and gems, or as eating various sorts of food.

sn: एकरात्रान्तराशित्वमेककालिकभोजनम्। चतुर्थाष्टमकालश्च षष्ठकालिक एव च॥ घड्रात्रभोजनश्चैव तथैवाष्टाहभोजनः। सप्तरात्रदशाहारो द्वादशाहिकभोजनः॥ मासोपवासी मूलाशी फलाहारस्तथैव च। वायुभक्षोऽम्बुपिण्याकदधिगोमयभोजनः॥ गोमूत्रभोजनश्चैव शाकपुष्पाद एव च। शैवालभोजनश्चैव तथाऽऽवामेन वर्तयन्॥ वर्तयन् शीर्णपणैश्च प्रकीर्णफलभोजनः। विविधानि च कृच्छ्राणि सेवते सिद्धिकासया॥
en: He considers himself as sometimes eating at intervals of one night, or once at the same hour every day, or as at the fourth, the sixty, and the eight hour every day, or as once in six or seven or cight nights, or as once in ten or twelve days, or as once, in a month, or as eating only roots, or fruits, or as living upon air or water alone, or on cakes of sesame husk, or curds or cowdung, or the urine of the cow or potherbs or flowers or moss or raw food, or as living on falled leaves of trees or fruits that have dropped down and lie scattered on the ground, or various other sorts of food, moved by the desire of acquiring ascetic success.

sn: चान्द्रायणानि विधिवल्लिङ्गानि विविधानि च। चातुराश्रम्यपन्थानमाश्रयत्यपथानपि॥ उपाश्रमानण्यपरान् पाषण्डान् विविधानपि। विविक्ताच शिलाच्छायास्तथा प्रस्रवणानि च॥ पुलिनानि विविक्तानि विविक्तानि वनानि च। देवस्थानानि पुण्यानि विविक्तानि सरांसि च॥ विविक्ताश्चापि शैलानां गुहा गृहनिभोपमाः। विविक्तानि च जप्यानि व्रतानि विविधानि च॥ नियमान् विविधांश्चापि विविधानि तपांसि च। यज्ञांश्च विविधाकारान् विधींश्च विविधांस्तथा॥
en: The Soul considers himself as following the observance of Chandrayana according to the rites laid down in the scriptures, or various other vows and observances, and the courses of duty laid down for the four modes of life, and even prohibitions of duty, and the duties of other subsidiary modes of life set down the four principal ones, and even various kinds of practices that distinguish the wicked and sinful. The Soul considers himself as enjoying lonely places and the charming shades of mountains and the cool vicinity of springs and fountains, and solitary river banks and secluded forests, and sacred pilgrimages, and lakes and waters remote from the busy haunts of men, and linely mountain caves giving the accommodation that houses and palaces afford. The Soul consider himself as reciting of different kinds of secret Mantras or as observing different vows and rules and various sorts of penances, and sacrifices of many sorts, and rites of diverse sorts.

sn: वणिक्पथं द्विजं क्षत्रं वैश्यशूद्रांस्तथैव च। दानं च विविधाकारं दीनान्धकृपणादिषु॥
en: The Soul considers himself as following sometimes the ways of traders and merchants and the practices of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras, and gifts of various sorts to those who are poor or blind or helpless.

sn: अभिमन्यत्यसम्बोधात् तथैव त्रिविधान् गुणान्। सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चैव धर्मार्थो काम एव च॥
en: On account of his being invested with Ignorance, the Soul adopts the different qualities of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance, and Righteousness and riches and pleasure.

sn: प्रकृत्याऽऽत्मानमेवात्मा एवं प्रविभजत्युतः। स्वधाकारवषट्कारौ स्वाहाकारनमस्क्रियाः॥ याजनाध्यापनं दानं तथैबाहुः प्रतिग्रहम्। यजनाध्ययने चैव यच्चान्यदपि किंचन॥
en: Under the influence of Nature, the Soul, undergoing changes himself, observes and follows and practises all these and considers himself as such. Indeed, the Soul considers himself as employed in the utterance of the sacred Mantras Svaha, Svadha and Vashat, and in saluting those he considers as his elders; in officiating in the sacrifices and studying the scriptures, and doing all other acts and rites of this sort.

sn: जन्ममृत्युविवादे च तथा विशसनेऽपि च। शुभाशुभमयं सर्वमेतदाहुः क्रियापथम्॥
en: The Soul considers himself as connected with birth and death and quarrels and destruction. All these, the learned say form the path of acts good and bad.

sn: प्रकृतिः कुरुते देवी भवं प्रलयमेव च। दिवसान्ते गुणानेतानभ्येत्यैकोऽवतिष्ठते॥ रश्मिजालमिवादित्यस्तत् तत्काले नियच्छति। एवमेषोऽसकृत्पूर्वं क्रीडार्थमभिमन्यते॥ आत्मरूपगुणानेतान् विविधान् हृदयप्रियान्। एवमेतां विकुर्वाणः सर्गप्रलयधर्मिणीम्॥ क्रियां क्रियापथे रक्तस्त्रिगुणां त्रिगुणाधिपः। क्रियां क्रियापथोपेतस्तथा तदिति मन्यते॥
en: It is the goddess Nature who causes birth and death. When the time comes for Universal Dissolution, all existent objects and qualities are withdrawn by the Supreme Soul which then exists alone like the Sun withdrawing at evening all his rays; and when the time comes for Creation. He once more creates and spreads them out like the Sun shedding his rays when morning comes. Thus the Soul, for the sake of spol, repeatedly considers himself invested with all these conditions, which are his own forms and qualities infinite in number, and agrecable to himself. It is thus that the Soul, though really above the three qualities, becomes attached to the path of acts and creates by modification nature invested with the conditions of birth and death and at once with all acts and conditions which are characterised by the three qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance. Arrived at the path of action, the Soul considers particular acts as possessing particular characteristics and productive of particular ends.

sn: प्रकृत्या सर्वमेवेदं जगदन्धीकृतं विभो। रजसा तमसा चैव व्याप्तं सर्वमनेकधा॥
en: O king, the whole of this universe has been blinded by Nature and all things have been variously overwhelmed (through Nature by the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance).

sn: एवं द्वन्द्वान्यथैतानि समावर्तन्ति नित्यशः। ममैवैतानि जायन्ते धावन्ते तानि मामिति॥
en: It is on account of the Soul being invested by Nature that these pairs of opposites, productive of happiness and woe, again and again come. It is on account of this Ignorance that individual Soul considers these sorrows to be his and imagines them as following him.

sn: निस्तर्तव्यान्यथैतानि सर्वाणीति नराधिप। मन्यतेऽयं ह्यबुद्धत्वात् तथैव सुकृतान्यपि।॥ भोक्तव्यानि मयैतानि देवलोकगतेन वै। इहैव चैनं भोक्ष्यामि शुभाशुभफलोदयम्॥
en: Indeed, O king, through that Ignorance it is that Individual Soul imagines he should anyhow cross those sorrows, and that he should, going into the regions of the gods, enjoy the happiness that await all his good deeds. it is through Ignorance that he thinks he should enjoy and suffer these delights and these miserics here in this world.

sn: सुखमेव तु कर्तव्यं सकृत् कृत्वा सुखं मम। यावदन्तं च मे सौख्यं जात्यां जात्यां भविष्यति॥
en: Through Ignorance Individual Soul thinks,-I should secure my happiness. By continually doing good deeds, I may enjoy happiness in this life till its close and shall be happy in all future lives.

sn: भविष्यति च मे दुःखं कृतेनेहाप्यनन्तकम्। महद् दुःखं हि मानुष्यं निरये चापि मज्जनम्॥
en: Through, again the evil deeds I do in this life I may suffer unending misery. The status of humanity is full of great misery, for from it one sinks into hell.

sn: निरयाच्चापि मानुष्यं कालेनैष्याम्यहं पुनः मनुष्यत्वाच्च देवत्वं देवत्वात् पौरुषं पुनः॥ मनुष्यत्वाच्च निरयं पर्यायेणोपगच्छति। य एवं वेत्ति नित्यं वै निरात्माऽऽत्मगुणैर्वृतः॥ तेन देवमनुष्येषु निरये चोपपद्यते। ममत्वेनावृतो नित्यं तत्रैव परिवर्तते।॥
en: From hell, it will take many long years before I can return to the status of humanity. From humanity I shall attain of the status of the gods. From that superior status I shall have to return to humanity and thence to sink into hell once more.—One who always consider this combination of the principal elements and the senses, with the reflection of consciousness in it, to be thus invested with the characteristics of the Soul, has again and again to walk among gods and human beings and to sink into hell. Being always invested with the idea of mineness, Individual Soul has to go through a round of such births.

sn: सर्गकोटिसहस्राणि मरणान्तासु मूर्तिषु। य एवं कुरुते कर्म शुभाशुभफलात्मकम्॥ स एव फलमाप्नोति त्रिषु लोकेषु मूर्तिमान्। प्रकृति कुरुते कर्म शुभाशुभफलात्मकम्। प्रकृतिश्च तद श्नाति त्रिषु लोकेषु कामगा॥ तिर्यग्योनिमनुष्यत्वं देवलोके तथैव च। त्रीणि स्थानानि चैतानि जानीयात् प्रकृतानि ह॥ अलिङ्गां प्रकृति त्वाहुर्लिङ्गैरनुमिमीमहे। तथैव पौरुषं लिङ्गमनुमानाद्धि मन्यते॥
en: Millions upon millions of births have to be gone through by Individual Soul in the successive forms he assumes, all of which are liable to death. He who does acts in this way, which are all full of good and bad fruits, has in the three worlds to assume successive forms and to enjoy and suffer fruits corresponding therewith. It is Nature that causes good and bad acts; and it is Nature that enjoys and suffers the fruits thereof in the three worlds. Indeed, Nature follows the course of acts. The status of the intermediate beings, of humanity, and of the gods, all originate from Nature. Nature has been said to be shorn of all qualities. Her existence is proved by her acts.

sn: स लिङ्गान्तरमासाद्य प्राकृतं लिङ्गमव्रणः। व्रणद्वाराण्यधिष्ठाय कर्मण्यात्मनि मन्यते॥ श्रोत्रादीनि तु सर्वाणि पञ्चकर्मेन्द्रियाण्यथ। वागादीनि प्रवर्तन्ते गुणेष्विह गुणैः सह॥ अहमेतानि वै सर्वं मय्यतानीन्द्रियाणि ह। निरिन्द्रियो हि मन्येत व्रणवानस्मि निर्बणः॥ अलिङ्गो लिङ्गमात्मानमकालः कालमात्मनः।
en: Similarly, Soul, though without attributes himself, has his existence proved by the acts which the body does when it receives his reflection. Although the Soul is not subject to changes of any kind, and is the active principle that sets Nature in motion, yet entering a body which is united with the senses of knowledge and action. He considers all the acts of those senses as his own. The five senses of knowledge beginning with the ear, and those of action beginning with speech, uniting with the qualities of Goodness and Darkness and Ignorance become engaged in numerous objects. Individual Soul imagines that it is he who does the deeds of his life and that the senses of knowledge and action belong to him, although in reality he has no senses. Indeed, though having no body, he imagines that he has a body. Though shorn of qualities, he considers himself as endued therewith, the though above Time, imagines himself to be under Time's control.

sn: असत्त्वं सत्त्वमात्मानमतत्त्वं तत्त्वमात्मनः॥ अमृत्युर्मृत्युमात्मानमचरश्चरमात्मनः।
en: Though having no understanding, he still considers himself as endued with it, and though above the four and twenty topics, considers himself as one included among them. Though deathless, he still considers himself as subject to death, and though motionless regards himself as having motion.

sn: अक्षेत्रः क्षेत्रमात्मानमसर्गः सर्गमात्मनः॥ अतपास्तप आत्मानमगतिर्गतिमात्मनः।
en: Though not possessed of a material body, he still considers himself as possessed of one; and though unborn, he still regards himself as having birth. Though above penances, he still considers as engaged in penances, and though he has no end he still considers himself as liable to attain to ends.

sn: अभवो भवमात्मानमभयो भयमात्मनः॥ अक्षरः क्षरमात्मानमबुद्धिस्त्वभिमन्यते॥
en: Though not gifted with motion and birth, he still considers himself as endued with both, and though above fear, still considers himself as subject to fear. Though Indestructible, he still considers himself Destructible. Invested with Ignorance, the Soul thus thinks of himself.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच एवमप्रतिबुद्धत्वादबुद्धजनसेवनात्। सर्गकोटिसहस्राणि पतनान्तानि गच्छति॥
en: Yudhishthira said It is thus, on account of his Ignorance and his association with others who are invested with Ignorance, that Individual Soul passes through millions and millions of births every one of which has dissolution in the end.

sn: धाम्ना धामसहस्राणि मरणान्तानि गच्छति। तिर्यग्योनिमनुष्यत्वे देवलोके तथैव च।॥
en: On account of his transformation into Intelligence invested with Ignorance, Individual Soul goes to millions of abodes, every one of which is liable to end in Jostruction, among intermediate beings and men and the gods.

sn: चन्द्रमा इव भूतानां पुनस्तत्र सहस्रशः। लीयतेऽप्रतिबुद्धत्वादेवमेष ह्यबुद्धिमान्॥ कला पञ्चदशी योनिस्तद्धाम प्रतिबुध्यते। नित्यमेतद् विजानीहि सोमं वै षोडशी कलाम्॥
en: On account of Ignorance, Individual Soul like the Moon, has to wax and wane thousands and thousands of times. This is truly the nature of Individual Soul when invested with Ignorance. Know that the Moon has in reality full sixteen portions. Only fifteen of these are subject to increase and decrease. The sixteenth remains constant. after the manner of the Moon, Individual Soul too has full appear and disappear. The sixteenth is subject to no change.

sn: कलायां जायतेऽजस्रं पुनः पुनरबुद्धिमान्। धाम तस्योपयुञ्जन्ति भूय एवोपजायते॥
en: Invested with Ignorance, Individual Soul repeatedly and continually takes birth in the fifteen portions, named above. With the etemai and immutable portion of Individual Soul the principal elements become united and this union takes place repeatedly.

sn: षोडशी तु कला सूक्ष्मा स सोम उपधार्यताम्। न तूपयुज्यते देवैर्देवानुपयुनक्ति सा॥
en: That sixteenth portion is subtile. It should be known as Soma. It is never upheld by the senses. On the other hand, the senses are upheld by it.

sn: एतामक्षपयित्वा हि जायते नृपसत्तम। सा ह्यस्य प्रकृतिर्दृष्टा तत्क्षयान्मोक्ष उच्यते॥
en: Since those sixteen portions are the cause of the birth of creatures, creatures can never, O king, take birth without their help. They are called Nature. The destruction of Jiva's liability to be united with nature is called Liberation.

sn: तदेव षोडशकलं देहमव्यक्तसंज्ञकम्। ममायमिति मन्वानस्तत्रैव परिवर्तते॥ पञ्चविंशो महानात्मा तस्यैवाप्रतिबोधनात्। विमलस्य विशुद्धस्य शुद्धाशुद्धनिषेवणात्॥ अशुद्ध एव शुद्धात्मा तादृग् भवति पार्थिव। अबुद्धसेवनाच्चापि बुद्धोऽऽप्यबुद्धतां व्रजेत्॥
en: The Principle of Greatness, which is the twenty-fifth, if it regards that body of sixteen portions called the Unmanifest, has to assume it repeatedly. On account of not knowing. That which is stainless and pure, and for its devotion to what is the outcome of a combination of both Pure and Impure, the Soul, which is, in reality, pure, becomes, O king, Impure. Indeed, on account of its devotion to ignorance, Individual soul though characterised by Knowledge, becomes repeatedly associated with Ignorance.

sn: तथैवाप्रतिबुद्धोऽपि विज्ञेयो नृपसत्तम। प्रकृतेस्त्रिगुणायास्तु सेवनात् त्रिगुणो भवेत्॥
en: Though, O king, free from error of every sort, yet on account of its devotion to the three qualities of Nature, it becomes endued with those attributes.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: जनक उवाच अक्षरक्षरयोरेष द्वयोः सम्बन्ध इष्यते। स्त्रीपुंसोऽपि भगवन् सम्बन्धस्तद्वदुच्यते॥
en: Janaka said O holy one, it has been said that the relation between male and female is like that which exists between the Indestructible and the Destructible.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: ऋते तु पुरुषं नेह स्त्री गर्भ धारयत्युत। ऋते स्त्रियं न पुरुषो रूपं निवर्तयेत् तथा॥
en: Without a male, a female can never conceive. Without a female, a male also can never create a form.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: अन्योन्यस्याभिसम्बन्धादन्योन्यगुणसंश्रयात्। रूपं निर्वर्तयत्येतदेवं सर्वासु योनिषु॥ ये
en: On account of their union with each other, and each depending upon the qualities of the other, forms are seen to spring up. This is the case with all orders of being.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: रत्यर्थमभिसम्बन्धादन्योन्यगुणसंश्रयात्। ऋतौ निर्वय॑ते रूपं तद् वक्ष्यामि निदर्शनम्॥
en: Through each other's union for purposes of (sexual) intercourse, and through each depending upon the qualities of the other, forms (of living creatures) flow in seasons. I shall tell you the indications thereof.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: गुणाः पुरुषस्येह ये च मातृगुणास्तथा। अस्थि स्नायुश्च मज्जा च जानीम: पितृणो गुणाः॥
en: Hear what the qualities are which belong to the father and what those are which belong to mother. Bones, sinews, and marrow, O twiceborn one, we know, originate from the father.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: त्वङ्मांसं शोणितं चेति मातृजान्यपि शुश्रुम। एवमेतद् द्विजश्रेष्ठ वेदे शास्त्रे च पठ्यते॥
en: Skin, flesh, and blood, we hear, originate from the mother. Even this, O foremost of twice-born ones, is what may be read of in the Veda and other scriptures.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: प्रमाणं यत् स्ववेदोक्तं शास्त्रोक्तं यच्च पठ्यते। वेदशास्त्रद्वयं चैव प्रमाणं तत् सनातनम्॥
en: Whatever is read as said in the Vedas and in other scriptures is considered as authority. The authority, again, of the Vedas and other scriptures, is eternal.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: अन्योन्यगुणसंरोधादन्योन्यगुणसंश्रयात्। एवमेवाभिसम्बद्धौ नित्यं प्रकृतिपूरुषो॥ पश्यामि भगवंस्तस्मान्मोक्षधर्मो न विद्यते। अथवानन्तरकृतं किंचिदेव निदर्शनम्॥
en: If Nature and Soul be always united together in this way by each opposing and cach depending on the other's qualities, I see, O holy one, that Liberation cannot exist. You, O holy one, are gifted with spiritual vision so that you see all things as if they are present before your eyes. If, therefore, there be any direct evidence of the existence of Liberation, do speak of it to me.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: तन्ममाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन प्रत्यक्षो ह्यसि सर्वदा। मोक्षकामा वयं चापि काङ्क्षामो यदनामयम्। अदेहमजरं नित्यमतीन्द्रियमनीश्वरम्॥
en: We are desirous of acquiring Liberation. Indeed, we wish to acquire That which is auspicious, bodiless, not subject to decrepitude, eternal, beyond the perception of the senses, and having nothing superior to it.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच यदेतदुक्तं भवता वेदशास्त्रनिदर्शनम्। एवमेतद् यथा चैतन्निगृह्णाति तथा भवान्॥
en: Vashishtha said What you say about the characteristics of the Vedas and the other scriptures is even so. You understand those marks in the way in which they should be understood.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: धार्यते हि त्वया ग्रन्थ उभयोर्वेदशास्त्रयोः। न च ग्रन्थस्य तत्त्वज्ञो यथातत्त्वं नरेश्वर॥
en: O lord of kings, you only understand aright the texts of the Vedas and other scriptures without understanding the true senses or meaning of those texts, remembering them fruitlessly.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: यो हि वेदे च शास्त्रे च ग्रन्थधारणतत्परः। न च ग्रन्थार्थतत्त्वज्ञस्तस्य तद्धारणं वृथा॥ भारं स वहते तस्य ग्रन्थस्यार्थं न वेत्ति यः। यस्तु ग्रन्थार्थतत्त्वज्ञो नास्य ग्रन्थागमो वृथा॥
en: Indeed, one who remembers a work without understanding their meaning, is said to carry an useless load. He, however, who understands the true meaning of a treatise, is said to have studied that work to purpose.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: ग्रन्थस्यार्थस्य पृष्टः संस्तादृशो वक्तुमर्हति। यथा तत्त्वाभिगमनादर्थं तस्य स विन्दति॥
en: Asked about the meaning of a text, one should communicate that meaning which he has understood by a careful study.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: न यः संसत्सु कथयेद् ग्रन्थार्थं स्थूलबुद्धिमान्। स कथं मन्दविज्ञानो ग्रन्थं वक्ष्यति निर्णयात्॥
en: That person of dull intelligence who refuses to explain the meanings of text in the midst of an assemblage of the learned, that person of foolish understanding, never succeeds in explaining the meaning aright.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: निर्णयं चापि छिद्रात्मा न तं वक्ष्यति तत्त्वतः। सोपहासात्मतामेति यस्माच्चैवात्मवानपि॥
en: An ignorant wight, going to explain the true meaning of treatises, incurs ridicule. Even those endued with a knowledge of the Soul have to incurs ridicule on such occasions.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: तस्मात् त्वं शृणु राजेन्द्र यथैतदनुदृश्यते। याथातथ्ये सांख्येषु योगेषु च महात्मसु॥
en: Listen now to me, O king, as to how the subject of Liberation has been explained among the great persons conversant with the Sankhya and the Yoga Systems of Philosophy.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: यदेव योगाः पश्यन्ति सांख्यैस्तदनुगम्यते। एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स बुद्धिमान्॥
en: That which the Yogins behold is exactly what the Sankhyas strive after to attain. He who sees the Sankhya and the Yoga Systems to be one and the same is said to be gifted with intelligence.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: त्वङ्मांसं रुधिरं मेदः पित्तं मज्जा च स्नायु च। अथ चैन्द्रियकं तात तद् भवानिदमाह माम्॥
en: Skin, flesh, blood, fat, bile, marrow, and sinews, and these senses, which you were speaking to me, exist.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: द्रव्याद् द्रव्यस्य निर्वृत्तिरिन्द्रियादिन्द्रियं तथा। देहाद् देहमवाप्नोति बीजाद् बीजं तथैव च॥
en: Objects originate from objects; the senses from the senses. From body one acquires a body, as a seed is obtained from seed.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: निरिन्द्रियस्याबीजस्य निर्द्रव्यस्याप्यदेहिनः। कथं गुणा भविष्यन्ति निर्गुणत्वान्महात्मनः॥
en: When the Supreme Being is without senses, without seed, without matter, without body, He must be divested of all qualities; and on account of His being so, how, indeed, can He have qualities of any kind?

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: गुणा गुणेषु जायन्ते तत्रैव निविशन्ति च। एवं गुणा: प्रकृतितो जायन्ते निविशन्ति च।॥
en: Ether and other qualities originate from the qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance, and disappear in the end in them. Thus the qualities arise from Nature and disappear in Nature.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: त्वमांसं रुधिरं मेदः पित्तं मज्जास्थि स्नायु च। अष्टौ तान्यथ शुक्रेण जानीहि प्राकृतानि वै॥
en: Skin, flesh, blood, fat, bile, marrow, bones, and sinews,-these eight, that are made of Nature, know, O king, may sometimes be produced by the vital seed alone (of the male).

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: पुमांश्चैवापुमांश्चैव त्रैलिङ्गचं प्राकृतं स्मृतम्। न वापुमान् पुमांश्चैव स लिङ्गीत्यभिधीयते॥
en: The Individual Soul and the universe are said to both partake of Nature characterised by the three qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance. The Supreme Soul is different from both the Individual Soul and the universe.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: अलिङ्गात् प्रकृतिर्लिङ्गैरुपालभ्यति सात्मजैः। यथा पुष्पफलैर्नित्यमृतवोऽमूर्तयस्तथा॥
en: As the seasons, though having no forms, are nevertheless inferred from the appearance of particular fruits and flowers, similarly, Nature, though formless, is inferred from the Principles of Greatness and the rest that originate from it.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: एवमप्यनुमानेन ह्यलिङ्गमुपलभ्यते। पञ्चविंशतिमस्तात लिङ्गेषु नियतात्मकः॥
en: Thus, from the existence of Consciousness in body, the Supreme Soul, shorn of all qualities whatever and perfectly stainless, is inferred.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: अनादिनिधनोऽनन्तः सर्वदर्शी निरामयः। केवलं त्वभिमानित्वाद् गुणेषु गुण उच्यते॥
en: Without beginning and destruction, without end, the seer of all things, and auspicious, that Soul, only on account of its Oneness with the body and other qualities, comes to be taken as invested with qualities.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: गुणा गुणवतः सन्ति निर्गुणस्य कुतो गुणाः। तस्मादेवं विजानन्ति ये जना गुणदर्शिनः॥
en: Those persons who are truly conversant with qualities know that only objects endued with qualities can have attributes but that That which is above all qualities can have none.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: यदा त्वेष गुणानेतान् प्राकृतानभिमन्यते। तदा स गुणहान्य तं परमेवानुपश्यति॥
en: When the Individual Soul conquers all qualities born of Nature and which it assumes under mistake, only then does it see the Supreme Soul.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: यत् तद् बुद्धेः परं प्राहुः सांख्या योगाश्च सर्वशः। बुद्ध्यमानं महाप्राज्ञमबुद्धपरिवर्जनात्॥ अप्रबुद्धमथाव्यक्तं सगुणं प्राहुरीश्वरम्। निर्गुणं चेश्वरं नित्यमधिष्ठातारमेव च॥ प्रकृतेश्च गुणानां च पञ्चविंशतिकं बुधाः। सांख्ययोगे च कुशला बुध्यन्ते परमैषिणः॥
en: Only the highest Rishis conversant with the Sankhya and the Yoga Systems know that Supreme Soul which Sankhyas and Yogins and believers in all other Systems say is beyond the Understanding, which is considered as Knower and endued with the highest wisdom on account of its renouncing all consciousness of identi-fication with nature, which is above the attribute of Ignorance or Error, which is Unmanifest, which is beyond all attributes, which is called the Supreme, which is dissociated from all attributes, which ordains all things, which is Eternal and Immutable, which overrules Nature and all her attributes, and which, getting over twenty-four topics of enquiry, forms the twenty-fifth.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: यदा प्रबुद्धा ह्यव्यक्तमवस्थाजन्मभीरवः। बुध्यमानं प्रबुध्यन्ति गमयन्ति समं तदा॥
en: When men of knowledge, who stand in fear of birth, of the several states of living consciousness, and of death, succeed in knowing the Unmanifest, they succeed in understanding the Supreme Soul at the same time.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: एतन्निदर्शनं सम्यगसम्यगनिदर्शनम्। बुध्यमानाप्रबुद्धानां पृथपृथगरिंदम्॥
en: An intelligent man considers the unity of the Individual Soul with the Supreme Soul as consistent with the scriptures and as perfectly correct; while the man shorn of intelligence considers the two as different from each other. This forms the distinction between the man of intelligence and the man that is shorn of it.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: परस्परेणैतदुक्तं क्षराक्षरनिदर्शनम्। एकत्वमक्षरं प्राहुर्नानात्वं क्षरमुच्यते॥
en: The Characteristics of both the Destructible and Indestructible have now been said to you. The indestructible is Oneness or Unity, while multiplicity or variety is said to be the Destructible.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: पञ्चविंशतिनिष्ठोऽयं यदा सम्यक् प्रवर्तते। एकत्वं दर्शनं चास्य नानात्वं चाप्यदर्शनम्॥
en: When one begins to study and understand property the twenty-five topics of enquiry, one then understands that the oneness of the Soul is consistent with the scriptures and its multiplicity is what is opposed to them.

description: Individual soul, Nature and Supreme Soul
sn: तत्त्वनिस्तत्त्वयोरेतत् पृथगेव निदर्शनम्। पञ्चविंशतिसगं तु तत्त्वमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥ निस्तत्त्वं पञ्चविंशस्य परमाहुर्निदर्शनम्। सर्गस्य वर्गमाधारं तत्त्वं तत्त्वात् सनातनम्॥
en: These are the several characteristics of what is included in the list of topics is beyond that number and forms and twenty-sixth. The study or comprehension of created things according to their aggregates (of five) is the study and comprehension of topics. Above these is That which is eternal.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: जनक उवाच नानात्वैकत्वमित्युक्तं त्वयैतदृषिसत्तम। पश्याम्येतद्धि संदिग्धमेतयोर्वे निदर्शनम्॥
en: Janaka said You have, O foremost of Rishis, said that Unity is the attribute of that which is Indestructible and variety or multiplicity is the attribute of what is known as Destructible. I have not, however, clearly understood the nature of these two. Doubts are still in my mind.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: तथा बुद्धप्रबुद्धाभ्यां बुद्ध्यमानस्य चानघ। स्थूलबुद्ध्या न पश्यामि तत्त्वमेतन्न संशयः॥
en: Ignorant men consider the Soul as endued with multiplicity. They, however, who are endued with knowledge and wisdom consider the Soul to be one and the same. I, however, have a very dull understanding. I am, therefore, unable to understand how all this can take place.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: अक्षरक्षरयोरुक्तं त्वया यदपि कारणम्। तदप्यस्थिरबुद्धित्वात् प्रणष्टमिव मेऽनघ॥
en: I have almost forgotten the causes also that you have attributed to the unity and the multiplicity of the Indestructible and the Destructible on account of the restlessness of my understanding.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: तदेतच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि नानात्वैकत्वदर्शनम्। बुद्धं चाप्रतिबुद्धं च बुध्यमानं च तत्त्वतः॥ विद्याविद्ये च भगवान्नक्षरं क्षरमेव च। साङ्ख्यं योगं च कार्येन पृथक् चैवापृथक् च ह॥
en: I, therefore, wish to hear you once more discourse to me on those subjects of unity and multiplicity, on him who is gifted with knowledge, on what is shorn of knowledge, on Individual Soul, Knowledge, Ignorance, on Indestructible, Destructible, and the Sankhya and the Yoga systems, in detail and separately and agreeable to the truth.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच हन्त ते सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यदेतदनुपृच्छसि। योगकृत्यं महाराज पृथगेव शृणुष्व मे॥
en: Vashishtha said I shall tell you what you ask. Listen, however, to me, O king, as I explain to you the practices of Yoga separately.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: योगकृत्यं तु योगानां ध्यानमेव परं बलम्। तच्चापि द्विविधं ध्यानमाहुर्विद्याविदो जनाः॥
en: Contemplation, which forms an obligatory practice with Yogins, is their highest power, Those conversant with Yoga say that that Contemplation is of two sorts.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: एकाग्रता च मनसः प्राणायामस्तथैव च। प्राणायामस्तु सगुणो निर्गुणो मनसस्तथा॥
en: One is the concentration of the mind, and the other is called Pranayama (suppression of vital airs). Pranayama is said to be real; while concentration of mind is unsubstantial to it.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: मूत्रोत्सर्गपुरीषे च भोजने च नराधिप। त्रिकालं नाभियुञ्जीत शेषं युञ्जीत तत्परः॥
en: Excepting the three times when a man passes urine and stools and eats, one should devote his entire time to contemplation.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यो निवर्त्य मनसा शुचिः। दशद्वादशभिर्वापि चतुर्विंशात् परं ततः॥ संचोदनाभिर्मतिमानात्मानं चोदयेदथ। तिष्ठन्तमजरं तं तु यत् तदुक्तं मनीषिभिः॥
en: Withdrawing the senses from their objects by the help of the mind, one gifted with intelligence, having made oneself pure, should, according to the twenty-two modes of transmitting the Prana breath, unite the Individual Soul with That which is above the four and twentieth topic which is regarded by the wise as living in every part of the body and as above decay and destruction.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: तैश्चात्मा सततं ज्ञेय इत्येवमनुशुश्रुम। व्रतं ह्यहीनमनसो नान्यथेति विनिश्चयः॥
en: It is by means of those twenty-two modes that the Soul may always be known. It is certain that this practice of Yoga is his whose mind is never possessed by evil passions. It is not any other person's.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: विमुक्तः सर्वसङ्गेभ्यो लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः। पूर्वरात्रेऽपररात्रे धारयीत मनोऽऽत्मनि॥ स्थिरीकृत्येन्द्रियग्राम मनसा मिथिलेश्वर। मनो बुद्ध्या स्थिरं कृत्वा पाषाण इव निश्चलः॥
en: Freed from all attachments, abstemious in diet, and controlling all the senses, one should fix his mind on the Soul, during the first and the last part of the night, after having, O king of Mithila, stopped the functions of all the senses, quieted the mind by the understanding, and assumed a posture as motionless as that of stone.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: स्थाणुवच्चाप्यकम्पः स्याद् गिरिवच्चापि निश्चलः। बुद्ध्या विधिविधानज्ञास्तदा युक्तं प्रचक्षते॥
en: When men of knowledge, conversant with the rules of Yoga, become as fixed as a stake of wood, and as immovable as a mountain, then they are said to be in Yoga.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: न शृणोति न चाघ्राति न रंस्यति न पश्यति। न च स्पर्श विजानाति न संकल्पयते मनः॥ न चाभिमन्यते किंचिन्न न बुध्यति काष्ठवत्। तदा प्रकृतिमापनं युक्तमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: When one does not hear, and smell and taste, and see; when one does not feel any touch; when one's mind is perfectly free from every purpose; when one is not conscious of any thing, when one cherishes no thought, when one becomes like a piece of wood, then is he called by the wise to be in perfect Yoga.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: निर्वाते हि यथा दीप्यन् दीपस्तद्वत् प्रकाशते। निर्लिङ्गोऽविचलश्चोर्ध्वं न तिर्यग् गतिमाप्नुयात्॥
en: At such a time one shines like a limp that burns in a place where blows no wind; at such a time one becomes freed even from his subtile form, and perfectly at one with Brahma. When one acquires such progress, he has no longer to ascend or to fall among intermediate beings.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: तदा तमनुपश्येत यस्मिन् दृष्टे न कथ्यते। हृदयस्थोऽन्तरात्मेति ज्ञेयो ज्ञस्तात मद्विधैः। ॥
en: When persons like ourselves say that there has been a complete identification of Knower, the Known, and Knowledge, then is the Yogin said to see the Supreme Self.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: विधूम इव सप्तार्चिरादित्य इव रश्मिमान्। वैद्युतोऽग्निरिवाकाशे दृश्यतेऽऽत्मा तथाऽऽत्मनि॥
en: While in Yoga, the Supreme Soul shows itself in the Yogin's heart like a burning fire, or like the bright Sun or like the lightning's spark in the firmament.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: ये पश्यन्ति महात्मानो धृतिमन्तो मनीषिणः। ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मयोनिस्था ह्ययोनिममृतात्मकम्॥ तदेवाहुरणुभ्योऽणु तन्महद्भ्यो महत्तरम्। तत् तत्त्वं सर्वभूतेषु ध्रुवं तिष्ठन् न दृश्यते॥
en: That Supreme Soul which is Unborn and which is the essence of nectar, which is seen by great Brahmanas gifted with intelligence and wisdom and conversant with the Vedas, is subtiler than what is subtile and greater than what is great. That Soul, though living in all creatures, is not seen by them.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: बुद्धिद्रव्येण दृश्येत मनोदीपेन लोककृत्। महतस्तमसस्तात पारे तिष्ठन्नतामसः॥
en: The Creator of the worlds, He is seen only by a person gifted with wealth of intelligence when helped by the lamp of the mind. He lives on the other shore of the Darkness and is above the Ishvara.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: स तमोनुद इत्युक्तः सर्वज्ञैर्वेदपारगैः। विमलो वितमस्कश्च निर्लिङ्गोऽलिङ्गसंज्ञितः॥
en: Persons conversant with the Vedas and endued with omniscience call Him the remover of Darkness, stainless, above Darkness, and with and without attributes.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: योग एष हि योगानां किमन्यद् योगलक्षणम्। एवं पश्यं प्रपश्यन्ति आत्मानमजरं परम्॥
en: This is what is called the Yoga of Yogins. What else is the mark of Yoga? By such practices do Yogins succeed in seeing the Supreme Soul that is above destruction and decay.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: योगदर्शनमेतावदुक्तं ते तत्त्वतो मया। सांख्यज्ञानं प्रवक्ष्यामि परिसंख्यानदर्शनम्॥
en: This much that I have told you in detail is about the Science of Yoga. I shall now describe to you that Sankhya philosophy by which the Supreme Soul is seen through the gradual destruction of mistakes.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: अव्यक्तमाहुः प्रकृतिं परां प्रकृतिवादिनः। तस्मान्महत् समुत्पन्नं द्वितीयं राजसत्तम॥
en: The Sankhyas, whose System is built on Nature, say that Nature, which is Unmanifest, is the foremost. From Nature they say, O king, the second principle called Greatness is produced.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: अहङ्कारस्तु महतस्तृतीयमिति नः श्रुतम्। पञ्चभूतान्यहङ्कारादाहुः सांख्यात्मदर्शिनः॥
en: We have heard that from Greatness originates the third principle called Consciousness. The Sankhyas blessed with sight of the Soul say that from Consciousness originate the five subtile essences of sound, form, touch, taste, and scent.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: एताः प्रकृतयश्चाष्टौ विकारावापि षोडश। पञ्च चैव विशेषा वै तथा पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि च॥
en: All these eight they call by the name of Nature. The changes of these eight are sixteen in number. They are the five gross essences of ether, light, earth, water and wind, and the ten senses of action and of knowledge including the mind.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: एतावदेव तत्त्वानां सांख्यमाहुर्मनीषिणः। सांख्ये विधिविधानज्ञा नित्यं सांख्यपथे रताः॥
en: Wise men devoted to the Sankhya path and conversant with all its ordinances, and dispensations consider these twenty-four topics as including the whole range of Sankhya enquiry. One

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: यस्माद् यदभिजायेत तत् तत्रैव प्रलीयते। लीयन्ते प्रतिलोमानि सृज्यन्ते चान्तरात्मना॥
en: What is produced becomes merged in the producing cause. Created by the Supreme Soul after another, these principles are destroyed in a reverse order.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: अनुलोमेन जायन्ते लीयन्ते प्रतिलोमतः। गुणा गुणेषु सततं सागरस्योर्मयो यथा।॥
en: Al every new Creation, the qualities start into being in the lateral order, and (when Destruction comes) they merge in a reverse order, like the waves of the ocean disappearing in the ocean from which they originate.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: सर्गप्रलय एतावान् प्रकृतेर्नृपसत्तम। एकत्वं प्रलये चास्य बहुत्वं च यदासृजत्॥
en: O best of kings, this is the manner in which the Creation and the Destruction of Nature takes place. The Supreme Being is all that remains when Universal destruction takes place; and it is He who assumes various forms when Creation beings.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: एवमेव च राजेन्द्र विज्ञेयं ज्ञानकोविदैः। अधिष्ठातारमव्यक्तमस्याप्येतत्रिदर्शनम्॥
en: This is evern so, O king, as ascertained by men of knowledge. It is Nature that causes the Over-presiding Soul to thus assume diversity and revert back to unity. Nature also herself has the same marks.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: एकत्वं च बहुत्वं च प्रकृतेरर्थतत्त्ववान्। एकत्वं प्रलये चास्य बहुत्वं च प्रवर्तनात्॥
en: One fully conversant with the nature of the topics of enquiry knows that Nature also assumes the same sort of diversity and unity, for when Destruction comes she reverts into unity and when Creation takes place she assumes diversity of form.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: बहुधाऽऽत्मा प्रकुर्वीत प्रकृति प्रसवात्मिकाम्। तच्च क्षेत्रं महानात्मा पञ्चविंशोऽधितिष्ठति।॥
en: The soul makes Nature, which contains the principles of production or growth, assume various forms. Nature is called Kshetra (or soil). Above the twenty-four topics or principles is the Sour which is Great. It presides over that Nature or Kshetra.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: अधिष्ठातेति राजेन्द्र प्रोच्यते यतिसत्तमैः। अधिष्ठानादधिष्ठाता क्षेत्राणामिति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: Hence, O great king, the foremost Yatis say that the Soul is the Presider. Indeed, we have heard that on account of the Soul's presiding over all Kshetras. He is called the Presider.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: क्षेत्रं जानाति चाव्यक्त क्षेत्रज्ञ इति चोच्यते। आव्यक्तिके पुरे शेते पुरुषश्चेति कथ्यते॥
en: And because, He knows that Unmanifest Kshetra, He is, therefore, also called Kshetrajna. And because also Soul enters into Unmanifest Kshetra (viz., the body), therefore is He called Purusha.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: अन्यदेव च क्षेत्रं स्यादन्यः क्षेत्रज्ञ उच्यते। क्षेत्रमव्यक्तमित्युक्तं ज्ञाता वै पञ्चविंशकः॥
en: Kshetra is something quite different from Kshetrajna. Kshetra is Unmanifest. The Soul, which is above the twenty-four principles, is called the Knower.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: अन्यदेव च ज्ञानं स्यादन्यज्ज्ञेयं तदुच्यते। ज्ञानमव्यक्तमित्युक्तं ज्ञेयो वै पञ्चविंशकः॥
en: Knowledge and the objects known are different from each other. Knowledge, again, has been said to be Unmanifest while the object of knowledge is the Soul which is above the twenty-four principles.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: अव्यक्त क्षेत्रमित्युक्तं तथा सत्त्वं तथेश्वरः। अनीश्वरमतत्त्वं च तत्त्वं तत् पञ्चविंशकम्॥
en: The Unmanifest is called Kshetra, understanding, and also the supreme Lord; while Purusha, which is the twenty-fifth principle has nothing superior to it and is not a principle.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: सांख्यदर्शनमेतावत् परिसंख्यानुदर्शनम्। सांख्याः प्रकुर्वते चैव प्रकृतिं च प्रचक्षते॥
en: This much, O king, is an account of the Sankhya philosophy. The Sankhyas call Nature the cause of the universe, and merging all the are grosser principles into the Intelligence beyind the Supreme Soul.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: तत्त्वानि च चतुर्विंशत् परिसंख्याय तत्त्वतः। सांख्याः सह प्रकृत्या तु निस्तत्त्वः पञ्चविंशकः॥
en: Rightly studying the twenty-four topics along with Nature, and determining their true nature, the Sankhyas succeed in seeing. That which is the twenty-four topics or principles.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: पञ्चविंशोऽप्रकृत्यात्मा बुध्यमान इति स्मृतः। यदा तु बुध्यतेऽऽत्मानं तदा भवति केवलः॥
en: Individual Soul in reality is that very Soui which is above Nature and the four and twenty topics. When he succeeds in knowing that Supreme Soul by dissociating himself from Nature, he then becomes at one with the Supreme Soul.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: सम्यग्दर्शनमेतावद् भाषितं तव तत्त्वतः। एवमेतद् विजानन्तः साम्यतां प्रति यान्त्युत॥
en: I have now told you everything about the Sankhya System truly. Those who conversant with this philosophy acquire tranquillity.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: सम्यनिदर्शनं नाम प्रत्यक्षं प्रकृतेस्तथा। गुणतत्त्वान्यथैतानि निर्गुणोऽन्यस्तथा भवेत्॥
en: Indeed, as men whose understandings are subject to error directly perceive all objects of the senses, so men freed from error have directly known Brahma.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: न त्वेवं वर्तमानानामावृत्तिर्विद्यते पुनः। विद्यतेऽक्षरभावत्वादपरं परमव्ययम्॥
en: They who acquire that state have never to return to this world after the dissolution of their bodies; while as regards those who are said to be liberated in this life, power, concentration, and immutability, become theirs, on account of their having attained to the nature of the Indestructible.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: पश्येरन्नैकमतयो न सम्यक् तेषु दर्शनम्। ते व्यक्तं प्रतिपद्यन्ते पुनः पुनररिंदम्॥
en: They who see this universe as many are said to see incorrectly. These men are blind to Brahma. O chastiser of enemies, such persons have again and again to return to the world and assume bodies.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: सर्वमेतद् विजानन्तो नासर्वस्य प्रबोधनात्। व्यक्तीभूता भविष्यन्ति व्यक्तस्य वशवर्तिनः॥
en: They who are conversant with all that has been said above become endued with omniscient, and accordingly when they pass from this body no longer become subject to the subjection of any more physical frames.

description: The practices of Yoga and the nature of the Supreme Soul
sn: सर्वमव्यक्तमित्युक्तमसर्वः पञ्चविंशकः। य एनमभिजानन्ति न भयं तेषु विद्यते॥
en: All things, have been said to be the result of the Unmanifest. The Soul, which is the twentyfifth, is above all things. They who know the Soul have no fear of coming back to the world.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच सांख्यदर्शनमेतावदुक्तं ते नृपसत्तम। विद्याविद्ये त्विदानी मे त्वं निबोधानुपूर्वशः॥
en: I have thus described you the Sankhya Philosophy. Listen now to me as I tell you what is Vidya (Knowledge) and what is Avidya (Nescience), one after the other.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: अविद्यामाहुरव्यक्तं सर्गप्रलयधर्मि वै। सर्गप्रलयनिर्मुक्तां विद्यां वै पञ्चविंशकः॥
en: The learned say that that Nature which is subject to Creation and Destruction, is called Avidya; while Purusha (Soul), who is freed from the attributes of Creation and Destruction and who is above the twenty-four topics or principles, is called Vidya.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: परस्परस्य विद्यां वै त्वं नबोधानुपूर्वशः। यथोक्तमृषिभिस्तात सांख्यस्याभिनिदर्शनम्॥
en: Listen to me first as I Tell you what is Vidya among success sets of other things, as explained in the Sankhya Philosophy. essences

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: कर्मेन्द्रियाणां सर्वेषां विद्यां बुद्धीन्द्रियं स्मृतम्। बुद्धीन्द्रियाणां च तथा विशेषा इति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: Among the senses of knowledge and those of action, the senses of knowledge are said to from what is known as Vidya. Of the senses of knowledge and their objects, the former form Vidya.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: विशेषाणां मनस्तेषां विद्यामाहुर्मनीषिणः। मनसः पञ्च भूतानि विद्या इत्यभिचक्षते॥
en: Of objects of the senses and the mind, the wise have said that the mind forms Vidya. Of mind and the five subtile essences, the five subtile essences form Vidya.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: अहङ्कारस्तु भूतानां पञ्चानां नात्र संशयः। अहङ्कारस्य च तथा बुद्धिर्विद्या नरेश्वरा६॥
en: Of the five subtile and Consciousness, Consciousness forms vidya. Of Consciousness and Greatness the latter O king, is Vidya.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: विद्या प्रकृतिरव्यक्तं तत्त्वानां परमेश्वरी। विद्या ज्ञेया नरश्रेष्ठ विधिश्च परमः स्मृतः॥
en: Of all the principles beginning with Greatness, and Nature, it is Nature, which is unmanifest and supreme, that is called Vidya. Of Nature, and that called Creator which is Supreme, the latter should be known as Vidya.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: अव्यक्तस्य परं प्राहुर्विद्यां वै पञ्चविंशकम्। सर्वस्य सर्वमित्युक्तं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानस्य पार्थिव॥
en: Above Nature is the twenty-fifth (Soul) who should be known as Vidya. Of all Knowledge, that which is the Object of Knowledge has been said to be the Unmanifest, O king.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: ज्ञानमव्यक्तमित्युक्तं ज्ञेयो वै पञ्चविंशकः। तथैव ज्ञानमव्यक्तं विज्ञाता पञ्चविंशकः॥ विद्याविद्यार्थतत्त्वेन मयोक्ता ते विशेषतः।
en: Again, Knowledge has been said to be Unmanifest, and the Object of knowledge to be what is above the four and twenty. Once more, Knowledge has been said to be Unmanifest, and the Knower is what is above the four and twenty. I have now told you what is truly the meaning of Vidya and Avidya.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: अक्षरं च क्षरं चैव यदुक्तं तन्निबोध मे॥ उभावेवाक्षरावुक्तावुभावतानवनक्षरौ।
en: Listen now to me as I tell you that has been said about the Indestructible and the Destructible. Both Individual Soul and Nature have been said to be Indestructible, and both of them have been said to be Destructible.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: कारणं तु प्रवक्ष्यामि याथातथ्यं तु ज्ञानतः॥ अनादिनिधनावेतावुभावेवेश्वरौ मतौ।
en: I shall tell you the reason of this correctly as I have understood it. Both Nature and Individual Soul are without beginning and without end. Both of them are considered as supreme.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: तत्त्वसंज्ञावुभावेतौ प्रोच्येत ज्ञानचिन्तकैः॥ सर्गप्रलयधर्मत्वादव्यक्तं प्राहुरक्षरम्। तदेतद् गुणसर्गाय विकुर्वाणं पुनः पुनः॥
en: Those who are endued with knowledge say that both are to be called principles. On account of its attributes of Creation and Destruction, the Unmanifest is called Indestructible. That Unmanifest becomes repeatedly modified for the purpose of creating the principles.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: गुणानां महदादीनामुत्पत्तिश्च परस्परम्। अधिष्ठानात् क्षेत्रमाहुरेतत्तत् पञ्चविंशकम्॥
en: And because the principles beginning with Greatness are produced by Purusha (Soul) as well, and because also Purusha and the Unmanifest mutually depend upon each other, therefore is Purusha also, the twenty-fifth, called Kshetra.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: यदा तु गुणजालं तदव्यक्तात्मनि संक्षिपेत्। तदा सह गुणैस्तैस्तु पञ्चविंशो विलीयते॥
en: When the Yogin withdraws and merges all the principles into the Unmanifest Soul (or Brahma), then the twenty-fifth (viz., Soul or Purusha) also, with all those principles, disappears into it.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: गुणा गुणेषु लीयन्ते तदैका प्रकृतिर्भवेत्। क्षेत्रज्ञोऽपि यदा तात तत्क्षेत्रे सम्प्रलीयते॥ तदा क्षरत्वं प्रकृतिर्गच्छते गुणसंश्रिता! निर्गुणत्वं च वैदेह गुणेष्वप्रतिवर्तनात्॥
en: When the principles become merged each into its creator, then the one that remains is Nature. When Soul, too, O son, becomes merged into his own producing cause, then Nature with all the principles in it becomes subject to destruction and attains also to the condition of being without attributes on account of her dissociation from all principles.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: एवमेव च क्षेत्रज्ञः क्षेत्रज्ञानपरिक्षये। प्रकृत्या निर्गुणस्त्वेष इत्येवमनुशुश्रुम॥
en: Thus it is that Soul, when his knowledge of Soil disappears, becomes, by his nature, shorn of qualities. We have heard it.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: क्षरो भवत्येष यदा तदा गुणवतीमथ। प्रकृति त्वभिजानाति निर्गुणत्वं तथाऽऽत्मनः॥
en: We he becomes destructible he then assurnes attributes. When, however, he gains his own real nature, he then succeeds in understanding his own condition of being really shorn of qualities.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: तदा विशुद्धो भवति प्रकृतेः परिवर्जनात्। अन्योऽहमन्येयमिति यदा बुध्यति बुद्धिमान्॥
en: By shaking off Nature and beginning to realise that he is different from her, the intelligent Soul then comes to be regarded as pure and stainless.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: तदैष तत्त्वतामेति न चापि मिश्रतां व्रजेत्। प्रकृत्या चैव राजेन्द्र मिश्रो ह्यन्यश्च दृश्यते॥
en: When Individual Soul ceases to exist in a state of union with Nature, then does he become at one with Brahima. When however, he exists united with Nature, he then, O king, seems to be different from Brahma.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: यदा तु गुणजालं तत् प्राकृतं वै जुगुप्सते। पश्यते च परं पश्यं तदा पश्यन्न संत्यजेत्॥
en: Indeed, when Individual Soul shows no affection for Nature and her principles, he then succeeds in seeing the Supreme and having once seen Him wishes not to lose that happiness.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: किं मया कृतमेतावद् योऽहं कालमिमं जनम्। मत्स्यो जालं हविज्ञानादनुवर्तितवानिह॥
en: When the Knowledge of truth comes to him, Individual Soul begins to lament thus:-Alas, how foolishly have I acted by falling through ignorance into this frame composed of nature like a fish entangled in a net.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: अहमेव हि सम्मोहादन्यमन्यं जनाज्जनम्। मत्स्यो यथोदकज्ञानादनुवर्तितवानहम्॥
en: Alas, through Ignorance, I have inigrated from body to body like a fish from water to water thinking that water along is the element in which it can dwell.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: मत्स्योऽन्यत्वं यथाज्ञानादुदकान्नाभिमन्यते। आत्मानं तद्वदज्ञानादन्यत्वं नैव वेदम्यहम्॥
en: Indeed, like a fish that does not know anything else than water to be its element, I also have never known anything else than children and wives to be my own!

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: ममास्तु धिगबुद्धस्य योऽहं मग्नमिमं पुनः। अनुवर्तितवान् मोहादन्यमन्यं जनाज्जनम्॥
en: Fie on me that, through ignorance, am repeatedly passing from body to body in forgetfulness.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: अयमत्र भवेद् बन्धुरनेन सह मे क्षमम्। साम्यमेकत्वमायातो यादृशस्तादृशस्त्वहम्॥
en: The Supreme Soul alone is my friend. I can make friendship with Him. Whatever be my nature and whoever I may be, I am capable to be like Him and can become at one with Him.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: तुल्यतामिह पश्यामि सदृशोऽहमनेन वै। अयं हि विमलो व्यक्तमहमीदृशकस्तथा॥
en: I see my similarity with Him. I am, indeed, like Him. He is pure. It is clear that I am of the same nature.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: योऽहमज्ञानसम्मोहादज्ञया सम्प्रवृत्तवान्। ससङ्गयाहं नि:सङ्गः स्थितः कालमिमं त्वहम्॥
en: Through Ignorance and stupefaction, I have becoine associated with Inanimate Nature. Though really shorn of attachments, I have passed this long time in a state of attachment with Nature.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: अनयाहं वशीभूतः कालमेतं न बुद्धवान्। उच्चमध्यमनीचानां तामहं कथमवासे॥
en: Alas, by her was I so long controlled without having been able to know it. Various are the forms,-high, middling, and low,-that Nature assumes. Oh, how shall I like in those forms?

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: समानयानया चेह सह वासमहं कथम्। गच्छाम्यबुद्धभावत्वादेषेदानीं स्थिरो भवे॥
en: How shall I live conjointly with her? On account of my ignorance I repair to her companionship. I shall now be fixed.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: सहवासं न यास्यामि कालमेतद्धि वञ्चनात्। वञ्चितोऽस्म्यनया यद्धि निर्विकारो विकारया॥
en: I shall no longer keep her company. For having passed so long a time with her, I should think that I was so long imposed on by her, for myself being really freed form change, how could I keep company with one who is subject to change.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: न चायमपराधोऽस्या ह्यपराधो ह्ययं मम। योऽहमत्राभवं सक्तः पराङ्मुखमुपस्थितः॥
en: She cannot be held responsible for this. The responsibility is mine, since turning away from the Supreme Soul became of my own accord attached to her,

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: ततोऽस्मि बहुरूपासु स्थितो मूर्तिष्वमूर्तिमान्। अमूर्तश्चापि मूर्तात्मा ममत्वेन प्रधर्षितः॥
en: On account of that attachment, myself, though without form in reality, had to live in various forms. Indeed, though without forın by nature I become endued with forms on account of my notion of Egoism, and thereby insulted and distressed.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: तासु तास्विह योनिषु। निर्ममस्य ममत्वेन किं कृतं तासु तासु च॥ प्राक् कृतेन ममत्वेन योनीषु वर्तमानेन नष्टसंज्ञेन चेतसा। न ममात्रानया कार्यमहंकारकृतात्मया॥ आत्मानं बहुधा कृत्वा येयं भूयो युनक्ति माम्। इदानीमेघ बुद्धोऽसि निर्ममो निरहंकृतः॥
en: On account of my idea of mineness concerning the results of Nature, I am forced to take birth in various orders of Being. Alas, though really shorn of Egoism, yet on account of affecting it, what various evil acts have been perpetrated by me in those orders in which I was born while I remained in them with a soul that had lost all knowledge! I have nothing to do with him who, with essence made up of consciousness, divides himself into many pieces and who tries to unite me with them. It is only now that I have been awakened and have understood that I am by nature without egoism and without that consciousness which creates the forms of Nature that invest me all around.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: ममत्वमनया नित्यमहंकारकृतात्मकम्। अपेत्याहमिमां हित्वा संश्रयिष्ये निरामयम्॥
en: Renouncing Egoism which I always have regarding her and whose essence is made up of consciousness, and leaving Nature herself, I shall take refuge in Him, who is auspicious.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: अनेन साम्यं यास्यामि नानयाहमचेतया। क्षेमं मम सहानेन नैकत्वमनया सह॥
en: I shall be united with Him, and not will Nature which is inanimate. If I unite with Hiin, it will do me good. I have no similarity of nature with Nature.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: एवं परमसम्बोधात् पञ्चविंशोऽनुबुद्धवान्। अक्षरत्वं नियच्छेत त्यक्त्वा क्षरमनामयम्॥
en: The twenty-fifth (viz., Individual Soul), when he thus succeeds in understanding the Supreme, becomes able to able to cast off the Destructible and at one with the Indestructible and which is the essence of all that is auspicious.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: अव्यक्तं व्यक्तधर्माणं सगुणं निर्गुणं तथा। निर्गुणं प्रथमं दृष्टवा तादृग् भवति मैथिल॥
en: Shorn of qualities in his true nature and in reality Unmanifest, Individual Soul becomes invested with what is Manifest and assumes qualities. When he succeeds in seeing what is without qualities, and which is the origin of the Unmanifest, he becomes, O king of Mithila, at one with the same.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: अक्षरक्षरयोरेतदुक्तं तव निदर्शनम्। मयेह ज्ञानसम्पन्नं यथाश्रुतिनिदर्शनात्॥
en: I have now told you according to what I have heard, as to how knowledge that is subtile, pure and certain, originates. Do you listen to me.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: निःसंदिग्धं च सूक्ष्मं च विबुद्ध विमलं यथा। प्रवक्ष्यामि तु ते भूयस्तन्निबोध यथाश्रुतम्॥
en: Now I again speak as I heard about that soul which is so tiny, awakened and pure.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: सांख्ययोगौ मया प्रोक्तौ शास्त्रद्वयनिदर्शनात्। यदेव शास्त्रं सांख्योक्तं योगदर्शनमेव तत्॥
en: I have already described to you, what the Sankhya and the Yoga Systems are as expounded in their respective scriptures. Verily, the science that has been explained in Sankhya treatises is at one with what has been laid down in the Yoga scriptures.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: प्रबोधनकरं ज्ञानं सांख्यानामवनीपते। विस्पष्टं प्रोच्यते तत्र शिष्याणां हितकाम्यया॥
en: The knowledge, 0 king, which the Sankhyas preach, is capable of awakening every one. In the Sankhya scriptures, that Knowledge has been explained very clearly for the behoof of disciples.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: बृहच्चैवमिदं शास्त्रमित्याहुर्विदुषो जनाः। अस्मिश्च शास्त्रे योगानां पुनर्वेदे पुरःसरः॥
en: The learned say that this Sankhya System is very extensive. Yogins have respect for that System as also for the Vedas.

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: पञ्चविंशात् परं तत्त्वं पठ्यते न नराधिप। सांख्यानां तु परं तत्त्वं यथावदनुवर्णितम्॥
en: In the Sankhya System no topic or principle above the twenty-fifth is admitted. That which the Sankhyas consider as their highest principle has been duly described (by me).

parva: MOKSHADHARMA PARVA) — Continued. Description of Vidya (Knowledge) and Avidya (Nescience
sn: बुद्धमप्रतिबुद्धत्वाद् बुध्यमानं च तत्त्वतः। बुध्यमानं च बुद्धं च प्राहुर्योगनिदर्शनम्॥
en: In the Yoga philosophy, it is said that Brahma, which is the essence of knowledge without the second, becomes the Individual Soul only when invested with Ignorance. In the Yoga Scriptures, therefore, both Brahma and Individual Soul are spoken of.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच अथ बुद्धमथाबुद्धमिमं गुणविधिं शृणु। आत्मानं बहुधा कृत्वा तान्येव प्रविचक्षते॥
en: Vashishtha said Listen now to me as I describe to you the Buddha (Enlightened to the Supreme Self) and Abuddha (Individual Soul) which is the dispensation of the qualities, Assuming many forms the Supreme Soul, becoming Individual Soul, regards all those forms as real.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: एतदेवं विकुर्वाणो बुध्यमानो न बुध्यते। गुणान् धारयते ह्येष सृजत्याक्षिपते तदा॥
en: On account of such transformations Individual Soul fails to understand the Supreme Soul, for he has the three qualities and creates and withdraws into himself what he creates.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: अजस्रं त्विह क्रीडार्थं विकरोति जनाधिप। अव्यक्तबोधनाच्चैव बुध्यमानं वदन्त्यपि॥
