en: Carelessly for his sport, O king, does Individual Soul undergo changes and because he is capable of understanding the called action of the Unmanifest, therefore he is the Comprehender.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: न त्वेव बुध्यतेऽव्यक्तं सगुणं तात निर्गुणम्। कदाचित् त्वेव खल्वेतदाहुरप्रतिबुद्धकम्॥
en: The Unmanifest or Nature can at no time comprehend Brahma which is really without qualities even when it shows itself with qualities. Hence is Nature called Unintelligent.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: बुध्यते यदि वाक्यक्तमेतद् वै पञ्चविंशकम्। बुध्यमानो भवत्येव सङ्गात्मक इति श्रुतिः। अनेनाप्रतिबुद्धेति वदन्त्यव्यक्तमच्युतम्॥ अव्यक्तबोधनाच्चापि बुध्यमानं वदन्त्युत।
en: There is a declaration of the Shrutis that is ever Nature does succeed in knowing the twenty fifth, she then becomes at one with the Individual Soul who is united with her. On account of this Individual Soul or Purusha, who is not manifest and which in his real nature is not subject to changes, comes to be called as the Unawakened or Ignorant.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: पञ्चविंशं महात्मानं न चासावपि बुध्यते॥ षड्विशं विमलं बुद्धमप्रमेयं सनातनम्। स तु तं पञ्चविंशं च चतुर्विंशं च बुध्यते॥
en: Indeed, because the twenty-fifth can comprehend the Unmanifest, he is, therefore, called Comprehender. He cannot, however readily, comprehened the twenty-sixth, which is pure, which is Knowledge without duality, which is immeasurable, and which is eternal. The twenty-sixth, however, can know both the Individual Soul and Nature, numbering the twenty-fifth and the twenty-fourth respectively.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: दृश्यादृश्ये ह्यनुगतं स्वभावे महाद्युते। अव्यक्तमत्र तद् ब्रह्म बुध्यते तात केवलम्॥
en: O you of great effulgence, only wise men know that Brahma which is Unmanifest, which is in its real nature to all that is seen and unseen, and which, O son, is the one independent essence in the universe,

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: केवलं पञ्चविंशं च चतुर्विंशं न पश्यति। बुध्यमानो यदाऽऽत्मानमन्योऽहमिति मन्यते॥
en: When Individual Soul considers himself different from what he truly is, it is only then that lie fails to know the Supreme Soul and himself and Nature with which he is united.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: तदा प्रकृतिमानेष भवत्यव्यक्तलोचनः। बुध्यते च परां बुद्धिं विशुद्धाममलां यदा॥
en: When Individual Soul succeeds in understanding Nature then he is said to be restored to his true nature and then does he attain to that high understanding which is pure and stainless.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: षड्विंशो राजशार्दूल तथा बुद्धत्वमाव्रजेत्। ततस्त्यजति सोऽव्यक्तं सर्गप्रलयधर्मि वै॥
en: When Individual Soul succeeds, O foremost of kings, in attaining to that excellent understanding, he then attains to that Pure Knowledge which is called the twenty-sixth (or Brahma). He then casts off the Unmanifest or Nature which has the attributes of Creation and Destruction.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: निर्गुणः प्रकृति वेद गुणयुक्तामचेतनाम्। ततः केवलधर्माऽसौ भवत्यव्यक्तदर्शनात्॥
en: When Individual Soul know Nature which is unintelligent and subject to the action of the three qualities of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance, he then becomes shorn of qualities himself. On account of his thus understanding the Unmanifest, he succeeds in acquiring the nature of the Supreme Soul.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: केवलेन समागम्य विमुक्तोऽऽत्मानमाप्नुयात्। एतत् तु तत्त्वमित्याहुर्निस्तत्त्वमजरामरम्॥
en: The Learned say that when he is feed from the qualities and united in nature with the Supreme Soul, then does Individual Soul become at one with that Soul. The Supreme Soul, is called the Real as well as Not Real, and is above decay and destruction.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: तत्त्वसंश्रयणादेतत् तत्त्ववन्न च मानद। पञ्चविंशति तत्त्वानि प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: O giver of honours, the Soul, though it has the body for its resting place, yet it cannot be said to have acquired the nature of those principles. The wise say that there are five and twenty principles in all.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: न चैष तत्त्ववांस्तात निस्तत्त्वस्त्वेष बुद्धिमान्। एष मुञ्चति तत्त्वं हि क्षिप्रं बुद्धस्य लक्षणम्॥
en: Indeed, O son, the Soul not to be considered as possessed of any of the principles. Endued with Intelligence, it is above the principles. It renounces quickly even that principle which is the mark of Knowledge.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: षड्विंशोऽहमिति प्राज्ञो गृह्यमाणोऽजरामरः। केवलेन बलेनैव समतां यात्यसंशयम्॥
en: When Individual Soul comes to regard himself as the twenty-sixth which is divested of decay and destruction, it is then that, forsooth, he succeeds by his own force in attaining to similarity with the twenty-sixth.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: षड्विंशेन प्रबुद्धेन बुध्यमानोऽप्यबुद्धिमान्। एतन्नानात्वमित्युक्तं सांख्यश्रुतिनिदर्शनात्॥
en: Though awakened by the twenty-sixth which is Pure Intelligence, Individual Soul still becomes subject to Ignorance. This is the cause of Jiva's multifariousness as explanied in the Shrutis and the Sankhya scriptures.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: चेतनेन समेतस्य पञ्चविंशतिकस्य ह। एकत्वं वै भवत्यस्य यदा बुद्ध्या न बुध्यते॥
en: When Individual Soul, who is endued with consciousness, loses all Consciousness of a distinct or individual self, then does he, losing his multifariousness, resume his Oneness.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: बुध्यमानोऽप्रबुद्धेन समतां याति मैथिल। सङ्गधर्मा भवत्येष निःसङ्गात्मा नराधिप।॥
en: O king, of Mithila, when Individual Soul, who is found to be in union with happiness and misery and who is seldom free from the consciousness of self, becomes identified with the Supreme Soul which transcends understanding, then does he becomes freed from virtue and vice.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: निःसङ्गात्मानमासाद्य षड्विंशकमजं विभुम्। विभुस्त्यजति चाव्यक्तं यदा त्वेतद् विबुद्ध्यते॥
en: Indeed, when Individual soul attaining to the twenty-sixth which is Unborn and Powerful and which is shorn of all attachments, succeeds in comprehend it thoroughly, he himself becomes possessed of power and entirely renounces the Unmanifest or Nature.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: चतुर्विंशमसारं च षड्विंशस्य प्रबोधनात्। एष ह्यप्रतिबुद्धश्च बुध्यमानश्च तेऽनघ॥ प्रोक्तो बुद्धश्च तत्त्वेन यथाश्रुतिनिदर्शनात्। नानात्वैकत्वमेतावद् द्रष्टव्यं शास्त्रदर्शनात्॥
en: For understanding the twenty-sixth, the twenty-four principles seem to Individual soul to be unreal. I have thus told you, O sinless one, according to the indications of the Shrutis the nature of the Unintelligent, and of Individual Soul, as also of that which is Pure knowledge, agreeably to the truth. Guided by the scriptures, variety and oneness are thus to be understood.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: मशकोदुम्बरे यद्वदन्यत्वं तद्वदेतयोः। मत्स्योदके यथा तद्वदन्यत्वमुपलभ्यते॥
en: The difference between the gnat and the Udumvara, or that between the fish and water, illustrates the difference between the Individual Soul and the Supreme Soul.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: एवमेवावगन्तव्यं नानात्वैकत्वमेतयोः। एतद्धि मोक्ष इत्युक्तमव्यक्तज्ञानसंहितम्॥
en: The Multiplicity and Oneness of these two are to be understood thus. This is called Liberation, viz., this comprehension of oneself as something distinct from Unintelligent or Unmanifest Nature.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: पञ्चविंशतिकस्यास्य योऽयं देहेषु वर्तते। एष मोक्षयित्वयेति प्राहुरव्यक्तगोचरात्॥
en: The twenty-fifth, which lives in the bodies of living creatures, should be liberated making him know the Unmanifest or the Supreme Soul which is above the understading.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: सोऽयमेवं विमुच्येत नान्यथेति विनिश्चयः। परेण परधर्मा च भवत्येष समेत्य वै॥
en: Indeed, that twenty-fifth is capable of acquiring Liberation in this way only and not through any other means. Though insooth different from the body in which he lives for the time being, he partakes of the nature of that body on account of his union with it.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: विशुद्धधर्मा शुद्धेन बुद्धेन च स बुद्धिमान्। विमुक्तधर्मा मुक्तेन समेत्य पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Uniting with what is Pure, he becomes Pure. Uniting with the Intelligent, he becomes Intelligent. By uniting, O foremost of men, with one that is Liberate he becomes Liberated.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: वियोगधर्मिणा चैव विमुक्तात्मा भवत्यथा विमोक्षिणा विमोक्षश्च समेत्येह तथा भवेत्॥
en: By uniting with one who is shorn of all attachments, he becomes freed from all attachments. By uniting with one striving after Liberation, he himself partaking of the nature of his companion, strives after Liberation.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: शुचिकर्मा शुचिश्चैव भवत्यमितदीप्तिमान्। विमलात्मा च भवति समेत्य विमलात्मना॥
en: By uniting with one of pure acts, he becomes pure and of pure acts and endued with blazing effulgence. By uniting with one of pure soul, he becomes of pure soul himself.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: केवलात्मा तथा चैव केवलेन समेत्य वै। स्वतन्त्रश्च स्वतन्त्रेण स्वतन्त्रत्वमवाप्नुते॥
en: By uniting with the One independent Soul, he becomes One and Independent. Uniting with One that is dependent on One's Own Self, he attains to the same nature and acquires Independence.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: एतावदेतत् कथितं मया ते तथ्यं महाराज यथार्थतत्त्वम्। अमत्सरत्वं परिगृह्य चार्थं सनातनं ब्रह्म विशुद्धमाद्यम्॥
en: O monarch, I have duly told you all this that is perfectly true. Candidly have I described to you this subject, viz., the Eternal, Pure and Prime Brahma.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: नावेदनिष्ठस्य जनस्य राजन् प्रदेयमेतत् परमं त्वया भवेत्। विधिसमानाय विबोधकारणं प्रबोधहेतोः प्रणतस्य शासनम्॥
en: You may communicate this high knowledge, capable of awakening the soul, to that person, O king, who though not a master of the Vedas is, nevertheless, humble and has a keen desire for acquiring the knowledge of Brahma.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: न देयमेतच्च तथानृतात्मने शठाय क्लीबाय न जिह्मबुद्धये। न पण्डितज्ञानपरोपतापिने देयं तु देयं च निबोध यादृशे॥
en: It should never be given to one who speaks falsehood, or one who is cunning or roguish, or one who has no strength of mind, or one who is of crooked understanding, or one who is jealous of men of knowledge, or one who pains others. Listen to me as I say who they are to whom this knowledge may safely be given.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: श्रद्धान्वितायाथ गुणान्विताय परापवादाद् विरताय नित्यम्। विशुद्धयोगाय बुधाय नित्यं क्रियावते च क्षमिणे हिताय॥ विविक्तशीलाय विधिप्रियाय विवादहीनाय बहुश्रुताय) विजानते चैव न चाहितक्षमे दमे च शक्ताय शमे च देयम्॥
en: It should be given to one who has faith, or one who has merit, or one who does not speak ill of others, or one who is given to penances from the purest of motives, or one who is endued with knowledge and wisdom, or one who performs sacrifices and other rites laid down in the Vedas, or one who has a forgiving nature, or one who feels compassion on and does good to all crcatures; or one who is fond of living in privacy and solitude, or one who is fond of performing all acts laid down in the scriptures, or one who does not like to quarrel, or one who is endued with great learning, or one having wisdom, or one possessed of forgiveness and self-control and tranquillity of soul.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: मेतत् परं ब्रह्म विशुद्धमाहुः। न श्रेयसा योक्ष्यति तादृशे कृतं धर्मप्रवक्तारमपात्रदानात्॥
en: This high knowledge of Brahma should never be given to one who has not such qualifications. It has been said that by giving this knowledge to one who is not considered a worthy recipient, no advantage or good fruit can arise.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: पृथ्वीमिमां यद्यपि रत्नपूर्णां दद्यान्न देयं त्विदमव्रताय। जितेन्द्रियायैतदसंशयं ते भवेत् प्रदेयं परमं नरेन्द्र॥
en: This great knowledge should never be given, even if he gives in exchange the whole Earth full of gems and riches of every sort, to one that is not obscrvant of any vows and restraints. Forsooth, however, O king, this knowledge should be imparted to one who has conquered his senses.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: कराल मा ते भयमस्तु किञ्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं ब्रह्म परं त्वयाद्या यथावदुक्तं परमं पवित्रं विशोकमत्यन्तमनादिमध्यम्॥
en: O Karala, do not entertain any fear since you have heard all this regarding high Brahma from the to-day! I have described to you duly the high and holy Brahma that is without beginning and middle, and that is capable of removing all kinds of sorrow.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: अगाधजन्मामरणं च राजन् निरामयं वीतभयं शिवं च। ज्ञानस्य तत्त्वार्थमिदं विदित्वा॥
en: Seeing Brahma whose sight is capable of doing away with both birth and death, O king, which is full of auspiciousness, which removes all fear, and which yields the highest benefit, and having acquired this essence of all knowledge, renounce all error and stupefaction to-day.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: द्धिरण्यगर्भाद् गदतो नराधिप। प्रसाद्य यत्नेन तमुग्रचेतसं सनातनं ब्रह्म यथाद्य त्वया।॥ वै पृष्टस्त्वया चास्मि यथा नरेन्द्र यथा मयेदं त्वयि चोक्तमद्य। तथावाप्तं ब्रह्मणो मे नरेन्द्र महाज्ञानं मोक्षविदां परायणम्॥
en: I had acquired this knowledge from the eternal Hiranyagarbha himself, O king, who communicated it to me for my having carefully pleased that great Being of very superior Soul. Asked by you to-day, I have, O king, communicated the knowledge of eternal Brahma to you, just as I had myself gained it from my teacher. Indeed, this great knowledge which is the refuge of all persons conversant with Liberation has been given to you exactly as I had it from Brahman himself.”

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतदुक्तं परं ब्रह्म यस्मान्नावर्तते पुनः। पञ्चविंशो महाराज परमर्षिनिदर्शनात्॥
en: Bhishma said I have thus told you of high Brahma, just as the great Rishi had said, by attaining to which the Twenty-fifth (Individual Soul) has never to return.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: पुनरावृत्तिमाप्नोति परं ज्ञानमवाप्य च। नावबुध्यति तत्त्वेन बुध्यमानोऽजरामरम्॥
en: On account of his knowing truly the Supreme Soul which is not subject to decay and death, Individual Soul is obliged to frequently return to the world. When, however, Individual Soul succeeds in acquiring that high knowledge, he has no longer to return.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: एतन्निःश्रेयसकरं ज्ञानं ते परमं मया। कथितं तत्त्वतस्तात श्रुत्वा देवर्षितो नृप॥
en: Having heard it, O king, from the celestial Rishi, I have, O son, given to you that great knowledge which yields the highest good.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: हिरण्यगर्भादृषिणा वसिष्ठेन महात्मना। वसिष्ठादृषिशार्दूलान्नारदोऽवाप्तवानिदम्॥
en: This knowledge acquired from Hiranyagarbha by the great Rishi Vashishtha. was From that foremost of Rishis, viz., Vashishtha, it was acquired by Narada.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: नारदाद् विदितं मह्यमेतद् ब्रह्म सनातनम्। मा शुचः कौरवेन्द्र त्वं श्रुत्वैतत् परमं पदम्॥
en: From Narada I have acquired that knowledge which is truly at one with the eternal Brahma. Having heard this discourse of great import, couched in excellent words, do not, O foremost of the Kurus, give way any longer to greaf.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: येन क्षराक्षरे वित्ते भयं तस्य न विद्यते। विद्यते तु भयं तस्य यो नैतद् वेत्ति पार्थिव॥
en: That man who knows the Destructible and the Indestructible, become freed from fear. He, indeed, O king, is compelled to entertain fear who is shorn of this knowledge.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: अविज्ञानाच्च मूढात्मा पुनः पुनरुपाद्रवत्। प्रेत्य जातिसहस्राणि मरणान्तान्युपाश्नुते॥
en: On account of Ignorance, the man of foolish soul hath repeatedly to return to this world. Indeed, after death he has to be born in thousands and thousands of orders of Being, every one of which meets with Death in the end.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: देवलोकं तथा तिर्यड्मनुष्यमपि चाश्नुते। यदि शुध्यति कालेन तस्मादज्ञानसागरात्॥
en: Now in the world of the gods, now among men, and now among intermediate orders of Being, he has to appear again and again. If in course of time he succeeds in crossing that Ocean of Ignorance in which he is sunk, he then succeeds in avoiding completely re-birth and attaining to oneness with the Supreme Soul.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: (उत्तीर्णोऽस्मादगाधात् स परमाप्नोति शोभनम्।) अज्ञानसागरो घोरो ह्यव्यक्तोऽगाध उच्यते। अहन्यहनि मज्जन्ति यत्र भूतानि भारत॥
en: The Ocean of Ignorance is dreadful. It is bottomless and called the Unmanifest. 0 Bharata, day after day, creatures are seen to fall and sink in that Ocean.

description: The Supreme Soul and the Individual Soul
sn: यस्मादगाधादव्यक्तादुत्तीर्णस्त्वं सनातनात्। तस्मात् त्वं विरजाश्चैव वितमस्कश्च पार्थिव॥
en: Since you, O king, have been freed from that eternal and limitless Ocean of Ignorance, you have, therefore, become freed from Darkness and also Ignorance.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: भीष्म उवाच मृगयां विचरन् कश्चिद् विजने जनकात्मजः। वने ददर्श विप्रेन्द्रमृषि वंशधरं भृगोः॥
en: Bhishma said Once on a time a king of Janaka's family while roaming in the uninhabited forest in pursuit of deer, saw a superior Brahmana or Rishi of Bhrigu's race.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: उपासीनमुपासीनः प्रणम्य शिरसा मुनिम्। पश्चादनुमतस्तेन पप्रच्छ वसुमानिदम्॥
en: Bowing with his head to the Rishi who was seated at his ease, king Vasuman sat near him and with his permission put to him this question:भगवन् किमिदं श्रेयः प्रेत्य चापीह वा भवेत्।

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: पुरुषस्याधुवे देहे कामस्य वशवर्तिनः॥
en: O holy one, what yields the highest benefit, both in this world and in the next, to man who has an unsuitable body and who is the slave of his desires?

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: सत्कृत्य परिपृष्टः सन् सुमहात्मा महातपाः। निजगाद ततस्तस्मै श्रेयस्करमिदं वचः॥
en: Duly respected by king, and and thus questioned, that great Rishi endued with ascetic merit, then said these words to him which were highly beneficial.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: ऋषिरुवाच मनसोऽप्रतिकूलानि प्रेत्य चेह च वाञ्छसि। भूतानां प्रतिकूलेभ्यो निवर्तस्व यतेन्द्रियः॥
en: see If you seek both here and hereafter what is agreeable to your mind, do you then, with controlled senses, abstain from doing what is disagreeable to all creatures.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: धर्म सतां हितः पुंसां धर्मश्चैवाश्रयः सताम्। धर्माल्लोकास्त्रयस्तात प्रवृत्ता: सचराचराः॥
en: Virtue is beneficial to them that are good. Virtue is the refuge of the good. From virtue have originated the three worlds with their mobile and immobile creatures.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: स्वादुकामुक कामानां वैतृष्ण्यं किं न गच्छसि। मधु पश्यसि दुर्बुद्धे प्रपातं नानुपश्यसि॥
en: O you, who are eagerly desirous of enjoying all agreeable objects, how is it that you are not yet satiated with objects or desire? You the honey, O you of little understanding, but are blind to the fall.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: यथा ज्ञाने परिचयः कर्तव्यस्तत्फलार्थिना। तथा धर्मे परिचयः कर्तव्यस्तत्फलार्थिना॥
en: As one desirous of acquiring the fruits of knowledge, should busy himself with the acquisition of knowledge, so one desirous of acquiring the fruits of Virtue should be busy with the acquisition of Virtue.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: असता धर्मकामेन विशुद्धं कर्म दुष्करम्। सता तु धर्मकामेन सुकरं कर्म दुष्करम्॥
en: If a wicked men, from desire of virtue, tries to do a pure and stainless act, the fulfilment of his desire becomes impossible. If, on the other hand, a good man, moved by the desire of acquiring virtue, tries to do an act that is even difficult, its accomplishment becomes easy for him.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: वने ग्राभ्यसुखाचारो यथा ग्राम्यस्तथैव सः। ग्रामे वनसुखाचारो यथा वनचरस्तथा।॥
en: If, while living in the forest, one acts in such a way as to enjoy all the pleasures of living amongst men in towns, one comes to be regarded not as a forest recluse but as an inhabitant of towns. Likewise, if one while living in towns, acts in such a way as to enjoy the happiness of a forest life, one is regarded not as a inhabitant of towns but as a forest recluse.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: मनोवाक्कायिके धर्मे कुरु श्रद्धां समाहितः। निवृत्तौ वा प्रवृत्तौ वा सम्प्रधार्य गुणागुणान्॥
en: Ascertaining the merits of the religion of Karma and that of Abstention therefrom, do you, with concentrated senses, be devoted to the practices of virtue in thought, word, and deed.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: नित्यं च बहु दातव्यं साधुभ्यश्चानसूयता। प्रार्थितं व्रतशौचाभ्यां सत्कृतं देशकालयोः॥
en: Judging of the propriety of time and place, purified by the observance of vows and other purifying rites, and solicited, do you, without malice, make large gifts to the good.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: शुभने विधिना लब्धमर्हाय प्रतिपादयेत्। क्रोधमुत्सृज्य दद्याच्च नानुतप्येन्न कीर्तयेत्॥
en: Acquiring riches by fare means, one should give it away to worthy persons. One should make gifts, renouncing anger; and having made gifts one should never yield to sorrow nor proclaim those gifts with his own mouth.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: अनृशंसः शुचिर्दान्तः सत्यवागार्जवे स्थितः। योनिकर्मविशुद्धश्च पात्रं स्याद् वेदविद् द्विजः॥
en: The Brahmana who is full of mercy, who is pure, who has his senses under control, who is truthful in speech, who is full of candour, and whose birth is pure, has been considered as a person deserving of gifts.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: सत्कृता चैकपत्नी च जात्या योनिरिहेष्यते। ऋग्यजुः सामगो विद्वान् षट्कर्मा पात्रमुच्यते॥
en: A person is said to be pure in birth when he is born of a mother who has only one husband and who is of the same caste with him. Indeed, such a Brahmana, knowing the three Vedas, viz., Rich, Yajush, and Saman, endued with learning, only observant of the six duties, has been considered as deserving of gifts.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: स एव धर्मः सोऽधर्मस्तं तं प्रति नरं भवेत्। पात्रकर्मविशेषेण देशकालाववेक्ष्य च॥
en: Virtue becomes sin and sin becomes virtue, according to the nature of the doer, of time, and of place.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: लीलयाल्पं यथा गात्रात् प्रमृज्यात् तु रजः पुमान्। बहुयत्नेन च महत् पापनिर्हरणं तथा॥
en: Sin is renounced like the fifth on one's body,-a little with a little exertion, and a great quantity when the exertion is greater.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: विरिक्तस्य यथा सम्यग् घृतं भवति भेषजम्। तथा निर्हतदोषस्य प्रेत्य धर्मः सुखावहः॥
en: A person, after clearing his bowels, should lake clarified butter, butter, which acts most beneficially on his system. Likewise, when one has freed himself of all faults and busies himself with the acquisition of virtue, that Virtue in the next world, brings on the highest happiness.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: मानसं सर्वभूतेषु वर्तते वै शुभाशुभम्। अशुभेभ्य: सदाऽऽक्षिप्य शुभेष्वेवावतारयेत्॥
en: Good and evil thoughts are in the minds of all creatures. Withdrawing the mind from cvil thoughts, it should always be bent towards good thoughts.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: सर्वं सर्वेण सर्वत्र क्रियमाणं च पूजय। स्वधर्मे यत्र रागस्ते कामं धर्मो विधीयताम्॥
en: One should always respect the practices of his own caste. Do you try, therefore, to act in such a way that you may have faith in the practices of your own caste.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: अधृतात्मन् धृतौ तिष्ठ दुर्बुद्धे बुद्धिमान् भव। अप्रशान्तः प्रशाम्य त्वमप्राज्ञः प्राज्ञवच्चर॥
en: O you who are endued with an impatient soul, follow the practice of patience. O you of a foolish understanding try to be possessed of intelligence. Shorn of tranquillity, try to be tranquil, and shorn of wisdom as you are, try to act wisely.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: तेजसा शक्यते प्राप्तुमुपाय: सहचारिणा। इह च प्रेत्य च श्रेयस्तस्य मूलं धृतिः परा॥
en: He who is in the company of the righteous, succeeds, by his own energy, in acquiring the means of doing what is beneficial for him both here and hereafter. Verily, the root of that benefit is unflinching firmness.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: राजर्षिरधृतिः स्वर्गात् पतितो हि महाभिषः। ययातिः क्षीणपुण्योऽपि धृत्या लोकानवाप्तवान्।॥
en: The royal sage Mahabhisha, for want of this firinness, fell from heaven. Yayati, also, though his merits had become exhausted succeeded in regaining regions of happiness through his firmness.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: तपस्विनां धर्मवतां विदुषां चोपसेवनात्। प्राप्स्यसे विपुलां बुद्धि तथा श्रेयोऽभिपत्स्यसे॥
en: You are sure to acquire great intelligence, as also what is for your highest good by seeing virtuous and learned persons endued with ascetic merit.

description: The discourse between Vasuman and the Brahmana about what is of the highest good to a man both in this world and the next
sn: भीष्म उवाच स तु स्वभावसम्पन्नस्तच्छ्रुत्वा मुनिभाषितम्। विनिवर्त्य मनः कामाद् धर्मे बुद्धिं चकार ह॥
en: Hearing these words of the sage, king Vasuman, having good disposition, withdrawing his mind from the pursuits of desire, set it upon the acquisition of virtue. a

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धर्माधर्मविमुक्तं यद् विमुक्तं सर्वसंशयात्। जन्ममृत्युविमुक्तं च विमुक्तं पुण्यपापयोः॥ यच्छिवं नित्यमभयं नित्यमक्षरमव्ययम्। शुचि नित्यमनायासं तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: You should, O grandfather, describe to me what is freed from duty and its reverse, what is freed from every doubt, what is above birth and death, as also virtue and sin, what is auspiciousness, what is eternal fearlessness, what is Eternal and Indestructible, and Immutable, what is always Pure, and what is ever free from exertion.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि इतिहासं पुरातनम्। याज्ञवल्क्यस्य संवादं जनकस्य च भारत॥ याज्ञवल्क्यमृषिश्रेष्ठं दैवरातिर्महायशाः। पप्रच्छ जनको राजा प्रश्न प्रश्नविदां वरम्॥
en: Bhishma said O Bharata, referring to this matter I shall recite to you the old discourse between Yajnavalkya and Janaka. Once on a time the famous king Daivarati of Janaka's race, truthfully understanding the meaning of all questions, put this question to Yajnavalkya, that foremost of Rishis.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: जनक उवाच कतीन्द्रियाणि विप्रर्षे कति प्रकृतयः स्मृताः। किमव्यक्तं परं ब्रह्म तस्माच्च परतस्तु किम्॥ प्रभवं चाप्ययं चैव कालसंख्यां तथैव च। वक्तुमर्हसि विप्रेन्द्र त्वदनुग्रहकाङ्क्षिणः॥
en: Janaka said ( regenerate Rishi, how many kinds of senses are there? How many kinds also are there of Nature? What is the Unmanifest and highest Brahma? What is higher than Brahmana? What is Birth and what Death? What are the limits of Age? You should, O foremost of Brahmanas, describe all these subjects to me who seek your favour.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: अज्ञानात् परिपृच्छामि त्वं हि ज्ञानमयोनिधिः। तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि सर्वमेतदसंशयम्॥
en: I am ignorant while you are an Ocean of knowledge. Hence, I ask you. Verily, I wish to hear you describe all these subject.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच श्रूयतामवनीपाल यदेतदनुपृच्छसि। योगानां परमं ज्ञानं सांख्यानां च विशेषतः॥
en: Hear, O king, what I say in answer to these questions of yours. I shall give you the high knowledge which Yogins prize, and especially that which is possessed by the Sankhyas.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: न तवाविदितं किंचिन्मां तु जिज्ञासते भवान्। पृष्टेन चापि वक्तव्यमेष धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: Nothing is unknown to you. Still you ask me. One, however, who is questioned, should answer. This is the eternal practice.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: अष्टौ प्रकृतयः प्रोक्ता विकाराश्चापि षोडश। तत्र तु प्रकृतीरष्टौ प्राहुरध्यात्मचिन्तकाः॥
en: Eight principles have been called by the name of Nature, while sixteen have been called changes. Of Manifest, there are seven. These are of views of those persons who are conversant with the spiritual science.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: अव्यक्तं च महान्तं च तथाहङ्कार एव च। पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम्॥ एताः प्रकृतयस्त्वष्टौ विकारानपि मे शृणु। श्रोत्रं त्वक्चैव चक्षुश्च जिह्वा घ्राणं च पञ्चमम्॥ शब्दः स्पर्शच रूपं च रसो गन्धस्तथैव च। वाक् च हस्तौ च पादौ च पायुर्मेद्रं तथैव च॥
en: The Unmanifest, Greatness, Consciousness and the five subtile elements of Earth, Wind, Ether, water, and Light, these eight are known by the name of Nature. Listen now to the enumeration of those called changes. They are the ear, the skin, the eye, the tongue' and the nose; and sound, touch, form, taste, and scent, as also speech, the two arins, the two feet, the lower duct (within the body), and the organ of pleasure.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: एते विशेषा राजेन्द्र महाभूतेषु पञ्चसु। बुद्धीन्द्रियाण्यथैतानि सविशेषाणि मैथिल॥
en: The ten commencing with sound, and originating from the five great principles, are called Vishesha. The five senses of knowledge are called Savishesha, O king of Mithila.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: मनः षोडशकं प्राहुरध्यात्मगतिचिन्तकाः। त्वं चैवान्ये च विद्वांसस्तत्त्वबुद्धिविशारदाः॥
en: Persons conversant with the spiritual science consider the Mind as the sixteenth. This is agreeable to your own views as also to those of other learned men well acquainted with the truths about principles.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: अव्यक्ताच्च महानात्मा समुत्पद्यति पार्थिव। प्रथमं सर्गमित्येतदाहुः प्राधानिकं बुधाः॥
en: From the Unmanifest, O king, originates the Greatness. The learned say this to be the first creation relating to Nature.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: महतश्चाप्यहङ्कार उत्पन्नो हि नराधिप। द्वितीयं सर्गमित्याहुरेतद् बुद्ध्यात्मकं स्मृतम्॥
en: From Greatness, O king of men, originates Consciousness. This has been designated the second creation having the Understanding for its essence.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: अहङ्काराच्च सम्भूतं मनो भूतगुणात्मकम्। तृतीयः सर्ग इत्येष आहङ्कारिक उच्यते॥
en: From Consciousness has originated the Mind which is the essence of sound and the others that are the qualities of ether and the rest. This is the third creation, relating to Consciousness.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: मनसस्तु समुद्भूता महाभूता नराधिप। चतुर्थं सर्गमित्येतन्मानसं विद्धि मे मतम्॥
en: From Mind have originated the great elements, O king! This is the fourth creation called mental.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसो गन्धस्तथैव च। पञ्चमं सर्गमित्याहुभौतिकं भूतचिन्तकाः॥
en: Persons conversant with the principal elements hold that Sound and Touch and Form and Taste and Scent are the fifth creation, relating to the Great elements.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: चक्षुश्च जिह्वा घ्राणं च पञ्चमम्। सर्गं तु षष्ठमित्याहुर्बहुचिन्तात्मकं स्मृतम्॥
en: The creation of the Ear, the Skin, the Eye, the Tongue, and the Scent, forms the sixth and is considered as having for its essence multiplicity of thought.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: अधः श्रोत्रेन्द्रियग्राम उत्पद्यति नराधिप। सप्तमं सर्गमित्याहुरेतदैन्द्रियकं स्मृतम्॥
en: The senses that come after the Ear and the others then originate, O king. This is called seventh creation and relates to the senses of knowledge.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: श्रोत्रं त्व त्वक् चैव ऊर्ध्वं स्रोतस्तथा तिर्यगुत्पद्यति नराधिप। अष्टमं सर्गमित्याहुरेतदार्जवकं स्मृतम्॥
en: Then, O king, come the vital air that rises upwards and those that go downwards. This is the eighth creation and called Arjjva (straight).

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: तिर्यस्रोतस्त्वधःस्रोत उत्पद्यति नराधिप। नवमं सर्गमित्याहुरेतदार्जवकं बुधाः॥
en: Then come those vital airs which move transversely in the lower parts of the body and also that called Apana passing downwards. This, the ninth creation, is also called Arjjava, O king.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: एतानि नव सर्गाणि तत्त्वानि च नराधिप। चतुर्विंशतिरुक्तानि यथाश्रुतिनिदर्शनात्॥
en: These nine kinds of creation, and these principles, O king, which are twenty-four in number, are described to you according to what has been laid down in the scriptures.

description: The origin of the principles of the Sankhya System
sn: अत ऊर्ध्वं महाराज गुणस्यैतस्य तत्त्वतः। महात्मभिरनुप्रोक्तां कालसंख्यां निबोध मे॥
en: After this, O king, listen to me as I tell you the durations of time as said by the learned regarding these principles or attributes.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच अव्यक्तस्य नरश्रेष्ठ कालसंख्यां निबोध मे। पञ्चकल्पसहस्राणि द्विगुणान्यहरुच्यते॥
en: Yajnavalkya said Listen to me, O foremost of men, as I tell you what the duration of time is about the Supreme Purusha. Ten thousand Kalpas are said to form a single day of his.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: रात्रिरेतावती चास्य प्रतिबुद्धो नराधिप। सृजत्योषधिमेवाग्रे जीवनं सर्वदेहिनाम्॥
en: The duration of his night is equal. When his night passes, he awakes, O king, and first crcates herbs and plants which form the sustenance of all embodied creatures.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: ततो ब्रह्माणमसृजद्धिरण्याण्डसमुद्भवम्। सा मूर्तिः सर्वभूतानामित्येवमनुशुश्रुम॥
en: He then creates Brahman who originates from a golden egg. That Brahman is the form of all created things, as we have heard.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: संवत्सरमुषित्वाण्डे निष्क्रम्य च महामुनिः। संदधे स महीं कृत्स्नां दिवमूर्ध्वं प्रजापतिः॥
en: Having lived for one whole year within that egg, the great ascetic Brahman, called also Prajapati came out of it and created the whole Earth, and the Heaven above.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: द्यावापृथिव्योरित्येष राजन् वेदेषु पठ्यते। तयोः शकलयोर्मध्यमाकाशमकरोत् प्रभुः॥
en: The lord then, it is seen in the Vedas, O king, placed the sky between Heaven and Earth.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: एतस्यापि च संख्यानं वेदवेदाङ्गपारगैः। दशकल्पसहस्राणि पादोनान्यहरुच्यते॥
en: The wise men, conversant in the study of Vedas said that it is seven thousand and five hundred Kalpas that form the day of Brahman.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: रात्रिमेतावतीं चास्य प्राहुरध्यात्मचिन्तकाः। सृजत्यहङ्कारमृषिर्भूतं दिव्यात्मकं तथा॥
en: Persons conservant with spiritual science hold that his night also is of an equal duration. Brahman, called Great, then creates Consciousness called element and endued with excellent essences.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: चतुरश्चापरान् पुत्रान् देहात् पूर्वं महानृषिः। ते वै पितॄणां पितरः श्रूयन्ते राजसत्तम॥
en: Before creating any physical bodies out of the ingredients called the chief elements, Mahan or Brahma, endued with penances created four others called his sons. They are the fathers of the original fathers, O best of kings as we have heard.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: देवाः पितॄणां च सुता देवैर्लोकाः समावृताः। चराचरा नरश्रेष्ठ इत्येवमनुशुश्रुमा॥
en: We have also heard, O king, that the senses (of knowledge) along with the four inner faculties, have originated from the Pitris, and that the entire universe of mobile and immobile Beings has been filled with those Great elements.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: परमेष्ठी त्वहङ्कारः सृजन् भूतानि पञ्चधा। पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम्॥
en: The powerful Consciousness created the five elements. These are Earth, Wind, Ether, Water, and Light as the fifth.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: एतस्यापि निशामाहुस्तृतीयमिह कुर्वतः। पञ्चकल्पसहस्राणि तावदेवाहरुच्यते॥
en: This Consciousness from whom originates the third creation, has five thousand Kalpas for his night, and his day is of equal duration.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसो गन्धस्तथैव च। एते विशेषा राजेन्द्र महाभूतेषु पञ्चसु॥
en: Sound, Touch, Form. Taste, and Scent,-these five are called Vishesha. They inhere into the five great elements.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: यैराविष्टानि भूतानि अहन्यहनि पार्थिव। अन्योन्यं स्पृहयन्त्येते अन्योन्यस्य हिते रताः॥ अन्योन्यमतिवर्तन्ते अन्योन्यस्पर्धिनस्तथा। ते वध्यमाना ह्यन्योन्यं गुणैर्हारिभरव्ययैः॥ इहैव परिवर्तन्ते तिर्यग्योनिप्रवेशिनः।
en: All creatures, 0 king, continually permeated by these five, seek one another's companionship, become subservient to one another, and challenging one another, get over one another; and actuated by those immutable and seductive principles, creatures kill one another and rove in this world, entering into numerous intermediate orders of Being.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: त्रीणि कल्पसहस्राणि एतेषामहरुच्यते॥ रात्रिरेतावती चैव मनसश्च नराधिप। मनश्चरति राजेन्द्र चारितं सर्वमिन्द्रियैः :॥ न चेन्द्रियाणि पश्यन्ति मन एवानुपश्यति।
en: Three thousands of Kalpas form their day. Their night also is the same. The Mind roves over all things, O king, guided by the Senses. The Senses do not perceive anything. It is the Mind that perceives through them.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: चक्षुः पश्यति रूपाणि मनसा तु न चक्षुषा॥ मनसि व्याकुले चक्षुः पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति।
en: The Eye sees forms when helped by the Mind is distracted, the Eye cannot see fully even the object before it.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: तथेन्द्रियाणि सर्वाणि पश्यन्तीत्यभिचक्षते॥ न चेन्द्रियाणि पश्यन्ति मन एवात्र पश्यति।
en: It is commonly said that the Senses perceive. This is not true, for it is the Mind that perceives through the Senses.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: मनस्युपरते राजनिन्द्रियोपरमो भवेत्॥ न चेन्द्रियव्युपरमे मनस्युपरमो भवेत्। एवं: मनःप्रधानानि इन्द्रियाणि प्रभावयेत्॥
en: When the activity of the Mind, is stopped, the activity of the Senses is also stopped. One should thus consider the Senses to be under the control of the Mind.

description: The duration of time of the Supreme Purusha
sn: इन्द्रियाणां तु सर्वेषामीश्वरं मन उच्यते। एतद् विशन्ति भूतानि सर्वाणीह महायशः॥
en: Indeed, the Mind is said to be the Lord of all the Senses. O you of great fame, these are all the twenty elements in the Universe.

sn: याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच तत्त्वानां सर्वसंख्या च कालसंख्या तथैव च। मया प्रोक्ताऽऽनुपूर्वेण संहारमपि मे शृणु॥
en: I have, one after another, told you the order of the creation, with their total number, of the various principles, as also the extent of the duration of each. Hear as I tell you of their destruction.

sn: यथा संहरते जन्तून् ससर्ज च पुनः पुनः। अनादिनिधनो ब्रह्मा नित्यश्चाक्षर एव च॥
en: Listen to me how Brahman, who is eternal and undeteriorating, and who is without beginning and without end, repeatedly creates and destroys all created objects.

sn: अहःक्षयमथो बुद्ध्वा निशि स्वप्नमनास्तथा। चोदयामास भगवानव्यक्तोऽहंकृतं नरम्॥
en: When his day expires and night comes, he seeks sleep. At such a time the unmanifest and holy one moves the Being called Maharudra, who is conscious of his great powers.

sn: ततः शतसहस्रांशुरव्यक्तेनाभिचोदितः। कृत्वा द्वादशधाऽऽत्मानमादित्यो ज्वलदग्निवत्॥
en: Urged by the unmanifest, that Being, assuming the form of the Sun of hundreds of thousands of rays, divides himself into a dozen parts each resembling a burning fire.

sn: चतुर्विधं महीपाल निर्दहत्याशु तेजसा। जरायुजाण्डजस्वेदजोद्भिज्जं च नराधिप॥
en: He then consumes with his energy, O king, without any loss of time, the four sorts of created beings, viz., viviparous, oviparious, filth-born, and vegetable.

sn: एतदुन्मेषमात्रेण विनष्टं स्थाणु जङ्गमम्। कूर्मपृष्ठसमा भूमिर्भवत्यथ समन्ततः॥
en: Within, the twinkling of the eye all mobile and immobile creatures being thus destroyed, the Earth becomes on all sides, bare as a tortoise shell.

sn: जगद् दग्ध्वामितबलः केवलां जगतीं ततः। अम्भसा बलिना क्षिप्रमापूरयति सर्वशः॥
en: Having burnt everything on the face of the Earth, Rudra of incomparable might, then quickly fills the bare Earth with Water, possessed of great force.

sn: ततः कालाग्निमासाद्य तदम्भो याति संक्षयम्। विनष्टेऽम्भसि राजेन्द्र जाज्वलत्यनलो महान्॥
en: He then creates the cycle-fire which dries up that Water. The Water disappearing, the great element of Fire continues to blaze dreadfully.

sn: तमप्रमेयोऽतिबलं ज्वलमानं विभावसुम्। ऊष्माणं सर्वभूतानां सप्तार्चिषमथाञ्जसा॥ भक्षयामास भगवान् वायुरष्टात्मको बली। विचरन्नमितप्राणस्तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधस्तथा॥
en: Then comes the powerful Wind of iinmeasurable force, in his eight forms, who devours speedily that blazing fire of transcendent force, possessed of seven flames, and al one with the heat that exists in every crcature. Having devoured that fire, the Wind passes in every direction, upwards, downwards and transversely.

sn: तमप्रतिबलं भीममाकाशं ग्रसतेऽऽत्मना। आकाशमप्यभिनदन्मनो ग्रसति चाधिकम्॥
en: Then Space of inmeasurable existent devours that Wind of transcendent power. Then mind cheerfully devours that immeasurable Space.

sn: मनो ग्रसति भूतात्मा सोऽहंकारः प्रजापतिः। अहंकारं महानात्मा भूतभव्यभविष्यवित्॥
en: Then that Lord of all creatures, viz., Consciousness, who is the Soul of everything, devours the Mind. Consciousness in his turn, is devoured by the Great Soul who is conversant with the Past, the Present, and the Future.

sn: तमप्यनुपमात्मानं विश्वं शम्भुः प्रजापतिः। अणिमा लघिमा प्राप्तिरीशानो ज्योतिरव्ययः॥
en: The incomparable Universe is then devoured by Shambhu, that Lord of all things in whom exist the lordly powers of Anima, Laghima, Prapti, etc., and who is considered as Supreme and pure Effulgence that is Iminutable.

sn: सर्वत:पाणिपादान्तः सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखः। सर्वतःश्रुतिमाँल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति॥
en: His hands and feet extend over every part his eyes and head and face are everywhere, his reach every places, and he exists possessing all things.

sn: हृदयं सर्वभूतानां पर्वणाङ्गुष्ठमात्रकः। अथ ग्रसत्यनन्तो हि महात्मा विश्वमीश्वरः॥
en: He is the heart of all creatures. He measures a digit of the thumb. That Infinite and Supreme Soul that Lord of all, thus devours the Universe. cars

sn: ततः समभवत् सर्वमक्षयाव्ययमव्रणम्। भूतभव्यभविष्याणां स्रष्टारमनघं तथा॥
en: After this, what remains is the Undeteriorating and the Immutable One who is without shortcoming of any sort, who is the Creator of the Past, the Present, and the Future; and who is perfectly faultless.

sn: एषोऽप्ययस्ते राजेन्द्र यथावत् समुदाहृतः। अध्यात्ममधिभूतं च अधिदैवं च श्रूयताम्॥
en: I have thus, O king, duly told you of Destruction. I shall now describe to you the subject of Adhyatma (Spiritual), Adhibhuta (Eternal) and Adhidaivata (Accidental).

sn: याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच पादावध्यात्ममित्याहुब्राह्मणास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः। गन्तव्यमधिभूतं च विष्णुस्तत्राधिदैवतम्॥
en: Brahmanas well read in the subjects of enquiry speak of the two feet as Spiritual, the act of walking as Elemental and Vishnu as Accidental.

sn: पायुरध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथा तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः। विसर्गमधिभूतं च मित्रस्तत्राधिदैवतम्॥
en: The lower duct is Spiritual; its function of throwing out the excreta is Elemental, and Mitra (Surya) is the Accidental.

sn: उपस्थोऽध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथा योगप्रदर्शिनः। अधिभूतं तथाऽऽनन्दो दैवतं च प्रजापतिः॥
en: The organ of generation is called Spiritual. Its agreeable function is called Elemental and Prajapati is its Accidental.

sn: हस्तावध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथा संख्यानदर्शिनः। कर्तव्यमधिभूतं तु इन्द्रस्तत्राधिदैवतम्॥
en: The hands are Spiritual; their function as represented by acts is Elemental; and Indra is the Accident of those limbs.

sn: वागध्यात्ममिति प्राहुर्यथा श्रुतिनिदर्शिनः। वक्तव्यमधिभूतं तु वह्निस्तत्राधिदैवतम्॥
en: The organs of speech are spiritual; the words uttered by them are Elemental; and Agni is their Accidental.

sn: चक्षुरध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथा श्रुतिनिदर्शिनः। रूपमत्राधिभूतं तु सूर्यश्चाप्यधिदैवतम्॥
en: The eye is Spiritual; vision or form is its Elemental, and Surya is the Accidental of that organ.

sn: श्रोत्रमध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथा श्रुतिनिदर्शिनः। शब्दस्तत्राधिभूतं तु दिशश्चात्रधिदैवतम्॥
en: The car is Spiritual; sound is Elemental; and the points of the compass are its Accidental.

sn: जिह्वामध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथा श्रुतिनिदर्शिनः। रस एवाधिभूतं तु आपस्तत्राधिदैवतम्॥
en: The tongue is Spiritual; taste is its Elemental; and Water is its Accidental.

sn: घ्राणमध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथा श्रुतिनिदर्शिनः। गन्ध एवाधिभूतं तु पृथिवी चाधिदैवतम्॥
en: The sense of scent is Spiritual; odor is its elemental; and Earth is its Accidental.

sn: त्वगध्यात्ममिति प्राहुस्तत्त्वबुद्धिविशारदाः। स्पर्शमेवाधिभूतं तु पवनश्चाधिदैवतम्॥
en: The skin is Spiritual; touch is its Elemental; and Wind is its Accidental.

sn: मनोऽध्यात्ममिति प्राहुर्यथा शास्त्रविशारदाः। मन्तव्यमधिभूतं तु चन्द्रमाश्चाधिदैवतम्॥
en: Mind has been called Spiritual that with which the Mind is employed is Elemental; and the moon is its Accidental.

sn: अहंकारिकमध्यात्ममाहुस्तत्त्वनिदर्शिनः। अभिमानोऽधिभूतं तु रुद्रश्चात्राधिदैवतम्॥
en: Ahankara is Spiritual; that which is to be vanity is its Elemental; and Rudra is its Accidental.

sn: बुद्धिरध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथावदभिदर्शिनः। बोद्धव्यमधिभूतं तु क्षेत्रज्ञश्चाधिदैवतम्॥
en: Buddhi is Spiritual; that which is to be understood is its Elemental; and Soul is its Accidental.

sn: एषा ते व्यक्तितो राजन् विभूतिरनुदर्शिता। आदौ मध्ये तथान्ते च यथातत्त्वेन तत्त्ववित्॥
en: I have thus truly expounded to you, O king, with its details taken individually. The power of the supreme in the beginning, the middle, and the end, O you, who are fully conversant with the nature of the original principles.

sn: प्रकृतिर्गुणान् विकुरुते स्वच्छन्देनात्मकाम्यया। क्रीडार्थे तु महाराज शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Nature, cheerfully and of her own accord, as if for sport, O king produces, by undergoing changes herself, thousands and thousands of combinations of her original qualities.

sn: यथा दीपसहस्राणि दीपान्माः प्रकुर्वते। प्रकृतिस्तथा विकुरुते पुरुषस्य गुणान् बहून्॥
en: As men can light thousands of lamps from but a single lamp, similarly Nature, by change, multiplies into thousands of existent objects the (three) qualities of Purusha.

sn: सत्त्वमानन्द उद्रेकः प्रीतिः प्राकाश्यमेव च। सुखं शुद्धित्वमारोग्यं संतोषः श्रद्दधानता॥ अकार्पण्यमसंरम्भः क्षमा धृतिरहिंसता। समता सत्यमानृण्यं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्॥ शौचमार्जवमाचारमलौल्यं हृद्यसम्भ्रमः। इष्टानिष्टवियोगानां कृतानामविकत्थना॥ दानेन चात्मग्रहणमस्पृहत्वं परार्थता। सर्वभूतदया चैव सत्त्वस्यैते गुणाः स्मृताः॥
en: Patience, joy, prosperity, satisfaction, brightness of all faculties, happiness, purity, health, contentment, faith, liberality, mercy, forgiveness, firinness, benevolence, equanimity, truth, satisfaction of obligations, mildness, modesty, calmness, external purity, simplicity, observance of obligatory rites, dispassionateness, fearlessness of heart, disregard for good and evil as also for pristine deeds,-appropriation of objects only when acquired by gift, the absence of cupidity, regard for the interests of others, mercy for all crcatures, these have been said to be the characteristics of the quality of Goodness.

sn: रजोगुणानां संघातो रूपमैश्चर्यविग्रहो। अत्यागित्वमकारुण्यं सुखदुःखोपसेवनम्॥ परापवादेषु रतिर्विवादानां च सेवनम्। अहंकारमसत्कारश्चिन्ता वैरोपसेवनम्॥ परितापोऽभिहरणं ह्रीनाशोऽनार्जवं तथा। भेदः परुषता चैव कामः क्रोधो मदस्तथा॥ दर्पो द्वेषोऽतिवादश्च ऐते प्रोक्ता रजोगुणाः। तामसानां तु संघातं प्रवक्ष्याम्युपधार्यताम्॥
en: The characteristics of the quality of Darkness are pride of personal beauty, assertion of supremacy, war, disinclination to give, absence of mercy, enjoyment and enduring of happiness and misery, pleasure in speaking ill of others, habit of quarrelling, pride, discourtesy, anxiety, hostilities, sorrow, appropriation of others' properties, shamelessness, crookedness, disunion, roughness, lust, anger, pride, assertion of superiority, malice and calumny. These originate from the quality of Darkness. I shall now tell you of qualities which originate Ignorance.

sn: मोहोऽप्रकाशस्तामिसमन्धतामिस्रसंज्ञितम्। मरणं चान्धतामिस्र तामिदं क्रोध उच्यते॥
en: They are stupefaction of judgement, obscuration of every faculty, darkness, blind darkness. Darkness means death, and blind darkness means anger.

sn: तमसो लक्षणानीह भक्षणाद्यभिरोचनम्। भोजनानामपर्याप्तिस्तथा पेयेष्वतृप्तता॥ गन्धवासो विहारेषु शयनेष्वासनेषु च। दिवास्वप्नेऽतिवादे च प्रामदेषु च वै रतिः॥ नृत्यवादित्रगीतानामज्ञानाच्छ्रद्दधानता। द्वेषो धर्मविशेषाणामेते वै तामसा गुणाः॥
en: Besides these, the other marks of Ignorance are greediness for food, ceaseless appetite for both food and drink, taking pleasure in scents and dresses and sports and beds and seats and sleep during the day and calumny and all sorts of acts proceeding from carelessness, taking pleasure, in dancing and instrumental and vocal music, and aversion for every sort of religion. These, indeed, are the characteristics of Ignorance.

sn: याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच एते प्रधानस्य गुणास्त्रयः पुरुषसत्तम। कृत्स्नस्य चैव जगतस्तिष्ठन्त्यनपगाः सदा॥
en: These three, O foremost of men, are the qualities of Nature. These belong to all things of the universe.

sn: अव्यक्तरूपो भगवान् शतधा च सहस्रधा। शतधा सहस्रधा चैव तथा शतसहस्रधा॥ कोटिशश्च करोत्येष प्रत्यगात्मानमात्मना।
en: The uninanifest Purusha endued with the six Yoga qualities transforms himself by himself into hundreds and thousands and millions and millions of forms.

sn: सात्त्विकस्योत्तमं स्थानं राजसस्येह मध्यमम्॥ तामसस्याधमं स्थान प्राहुरध्यात्मचिन्तकाः।
en: Those that are conversant with the spiritual science say that to the quality of Sattva is assigned a high, to Rajas a middling, and to Tamas, a low place in the universe.

sn: केवलेनेह पुण्येन गतिमूर्ध्वामवाप्नुयात्॥ पुण्यपापेन मानुष्यमधर्मेणाप्यधोगतिम्।
en: By the help of unmixed virtue one acquires a high end. Through virtue mixed with sin one acquires the status of humanity. While through unmixed sin one is visited by a vile end.

sn: द्वन्द्वमेषां त्रयाणां तु संनिपातं च तत्त्वतः॥ सत्त्वस्य रजसश्चैव तमसश्च शृणुष्व मे।
en: Listen now to me, king, as I speak to you of the intermixture of the three qualities of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas.

sn: सत्त्वस्य तु रजो दृष्टं रजसश्च तमस्तथा॥ तमसश्च तथा सत्त्वं सत्त्वस्याव्यक्तमेव च।
en: Sometimes Rajas is seen mixed with Sattva Tamas also exists with Rajas. With Tamas may also be seen Sattva. Also Sattva and Rajas and Tamas may be seen existing together and in cqual parts. They then form the Nature.

sn: अव्यक्तः सत्त्वसंयुक्तो देवलोकमवाप्नुयात्॥ रजःसत्त्वसमायुक्तो मानुषेषु प्रपद्यते। रजस्तमोभ्यां संयुक्तस्तिर्यग्योनिषु जायते॥ राजसैस्तामसैः सत्त्वैर्युक्तो मानुषमाप्नुयात्।
en: When the Purusha becomes endued with only Sattva, he aquires the region of the gods. Endued with both Sattva and Rajas, he is born as a man. Endued with Rajas and Tamas, he is born the intermediate order of Being. Endued with all three, viz., Sattva and Rajas and Tamas, he becomes a man.

sn: पुण्यपापवियुक्तानां स्थानमाहुर्महात्मनाम्। शाश्वतं चाव्ययं चैवमक्षयं चामृतं च तत्॥
en: Those great persons who are above both virtue and sin, attain, it is said, to that place which is eternal, immutable, undecaying, and immortal.

sn: ज्ञानिनां सम्भवं श्रेष्ठं स्थानमव्रणमच्युतम्। अतीन्द्रियमबीजं च जन्ममृत्युतमोनुदम्॥
en: Men of knowledge go by very superior births and their place is faultless and undecaying, transcending the perception of the senses, free from ignorance above birth and death, and full of light that removes all sorts of darkness,

sn: अव्यक्तस्थं परं यत् तत् पृष्टस्तेऽहं नराधिप। स एष प्रकृतिस्थो हि तत्स्थ इत्यभिधीयते॥
en: You had asked me about the nature of the supreme living in the Unmanifest, Purusha. I shall tell you. He is said to live in His own nature without partaking of the nature of Prakriti.

sn: अचेतना चैव मता प्रकृतिश्चापि पार्थिव। एतेनाधिष्ठिता चैव सृजते संहरत्यपि॥
en: Nature, O king, is inanimate and unintelligent. When presided over by Purusha (Soul) then only can she create and destroy.

sn: जनक उवाच अनादिनिधनावेतावुभावेव महामते। अमूर्तिमन्तावचलावप्रकम्प्यगुणागुणौ॥
en: Both Nature and Soul, O you of great intelligence, are without beginning and without end. Both of them are without end. Both of them are without form. Both of them are undeteriorating.

sn: अग्राह्यावृषिशार्दूल कथमेको ह्यचेतनः। चेतनावांस्तथा चैकः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति भाषितः॥
en: Both of them, again, cannot be comprehended. How then, O foremost of Rishis, can it be said that one of them is inanimate and unintelligent? How, is the other said to be animate and intelligent? And why is the latter called Kshetrajna (Soul).

sn: त्वं हि विप्रेन्द्र कात्स्येंन मोक्षधर्ममुपाससे। साकल्यं मोक्षधर्मस्य श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: You, O foremost of Brahmanas, are a master of the entire religion of Liberation. I wish to hear fully of the religion of Liberation.

sn: अस्तित्वं केवलत्वं च विनाभावं तथैव च। दैवतानि च मे ब्रूहि देहं यान्याश्रितानि वै॥ तथैवोत्क्रामिणः स्थानं देहिनो वै विपद्यतः। कालेन यद्धि प्राप्नोति स्थानं तत् प्रब्रवीहि मे॥
en: Do you describe to me then the existence and Oneness of Soul, of his separateness from Nature, of the gods which attach to the body, of the place to which embodied creatures go when they die, and that place to which they may ultimately, in course of time, be able to go.

sn: सांख्यज्ञानं च तत्त्वेन पृथग्योगं तथैव च। अरिष्टानि च तत्त्वानि वक्तुमर्हसि सत्तम। विदितं सर्वमेतत् ते पाणावामलकं यथा॥
en: Tell me, also, of the Knowledge expounded in the Sankhya system, and of the Yoga system separately. You also speak of the predicaments of death, O best of men. All these subjects are well known to you even as an embolic myrobalan in your hand. Tell me, also, of the Knowledge expounded in the Sankhya system, and of the Yoga system separately. You also speak of the predicaments of death, O best of men. All these subjects are well known to you even as an embolic myrobalan in your hand.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच न शक्यो निर्गुणस्तात गुणीकर्तुं विशाम्पते। गुणवांश्चाप्यगुणवान् यथातत्त्वं निबोध मे॥
en: That which is without qualities, O son, can never be explained by assigning qualities to it. Listen, however, to me as I explain to you what is endued with qualities and what is devoid of them.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: गुणैर्हि गुणवानेन निर्गुणश्चागुणस्तथा। प्राहुरेवं महात्मानो मुनयस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥
en: Great Munis conversant with the truth about principles say that when Soul seizes qualities like a crystal catching the reflection of a red flower, he is said to be possessed of qualities; but when freed from qualities like the crystal freed from reflection, he is seen in his real nature, which is as above all qualities.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: गुणस्वभावस्त्वव्यक्तो गुणान् नैवातिवर्तते। उपयुङ्क्ते च तानेव स चैवाज्ञः स्वभावतः॥
en: Unmanifest Nature is by her nature endued with qualities. She cannot transcends them. Shorn of intelligence by nature she becomes attached to qualities.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: अव्यक्तस्तु न जानीते पुरुषो ज्ञः स्वभावतः। न मत्तः परमोऽस्तीति नित्यमेवाभिमन्यते॥
en: Unmanifest Nature cannot know anything, while Purusha, by his nature, is endued with knowledge.—There is nothing higher than myself, the Soul is always conscious of it.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: अनेन कारणेनैतदव्यक्तं स्यादचेतनम्। नित्यत्वाच्चाक्षरत्वाच्च क्षरत्वान्न तदन्यथा।॥
en: Therefore the unmanifest Nature, although by nature inanimate and unintelligent, still becomes animate and intelligent on account of her union with the Soul who is Eternal and Indestructible instead of remaining in her own nature owing to her destructibility.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: यदाज्ञानेन कुर्वीत गुणसर्ग पुनः पुनः। यदाऽऽत्मानं न जानीते तदाऽऽत्मापि न मुच्यते॥
en: When Soul, through ignorance, repeatedly becomes associated with qualities, he fails to understand his own real nature and therefore he fails to acquire Liberation.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: कर्तृत्वाच्चापि सर्गाणां सर्गधर्मा तथोच्यते। कर्तृत्वाच्चापि योगानां योगधर्मा तथोच्यते॥ कर्तृत्वात् प्रकृतीनां च तथा प्रकृतिधर्मिता॥
en: On account of the Soul's Supremacy over the principles that originate from Nature he is said to partake of the nature of those principles. On account also of his agency in the matter of creation, he is said to possess the quality of creation. On account of his agency in the matter of Yoga, he is said to possess the quality of Yoga. For his Supremacy over those particular principles know by the name of Nature, he is said to possess the character of Nature.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: कर्तृत्वाच्चापि बीजानां बीजधर्मा तथोच्यते। गुणानां प्रसवत्वाच्च प्रलयत्वात् तथैव च।॥
en: For his agency in the matter of creating the seeds, he is said to partake of the nature of those seeds. And because he causes the several principles or qualities to come into being, he is, therefore, said to be subject to decay and destruction.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: उपेक्षत्वादनन्यत्वादभिमानाच्च केवलम्। मन्यन्ते यतयः सिद्धा अध्यात्मज्ञा गतज्वराः। अनित्यं नित्यमव्यक्तं व्यक्तमेतद्धि शुश्रुम॥
en: On account, again, of his being the witness of everything, and on account, also of there being nothing else than he, as also for his consciousness of oneness with Nature, Yatis endued with ascetic success, conversant with the spiritual science, and freed from fever of every sort, consider him as existing by himself without a second, immutable, unmanifest, unstable, and manifest.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: अव्यक्तैकत्वमित्याहुर्नानात्वं पुरुषे तथा। सर्वभूतदयावन्तः केवलं ज्ञानमास्थिताः॥
en: This is what we have heard. Those Sankhyas, however, that depend upon Knowledge only and the practice of mercy for all creatures, say that it is Nature which is Ore but souls are many.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: अन्यः स पुरुषोऽव्यक्तस्त्वध्रुवो ध्रुवसंज्ञकः। यथा मुञ्ज इषीकाणां तथैवैतद्धि जायते॥
en: As a matter of fact, Soul is different from Nature which though unstable, still appears as stable. As a blade of reed is different from its outer cover, so is Soul different from Nature.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: अन्यच्च मशकं विद्यादन्यच्चोदुम्बरं तथा। न चोदुम्बरसंयोगैर्मशकस्तत्र लिप्यते॥
en: Indeed, the worm that lies within the Udumvara should be known as different from the Udumvara, Though existing with the Udumvara, the worm is not to be considered as forming a part of the Udumvara.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: अन्य एव तथा मत्स्यस्तदन्यदुदकं स्मृतम्। न चोदकस्य स्पर्शेन मत्स्यो लिप्यति सर्वशः॥
en: The fish is separate from the water in which it lives, and the water is separate from the fish that lives in it. Though the fish and water exist together, yet it is never drenched by water.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: अन्यो ह्यग्निरुखाप्यन्या नित्यमेवमवेहि भोः। न चोपलिप्यते सोऽग्निरुखासंस्पर्शनेन वै॥
en: The fire that lies in an earthen saucepan is separate from the earthen saucepan, and the saucepan is separate from the fire it contains. although the fire exists in and with the saucepan, yet it is not to be considered as constituting any part of it.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: पुष्करं त्वन्यदेवात्र तथान्यदुदकं स्मृतम्। न चोदकस्य स्पर्शेन लिप्यते तत्र पुष्करम्॥
en: The lotus-leaf that lies afloat on a piece of water is separate from the piece of water on which it floats. Because it exists with water it does not form a portion of the water.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: एतेषां सहवासं च निवासं चैव नित्यशः। याथातथ्येन पश्यन्ति न नित्यं प्राकृता जनाः॥
en: The eternal existence of those objects in and with those mentioned, is never correctly understood by ordinary mortals.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: ये त्वन्यथैव पश्यन्ति न सम्यक् तेषु दर्शनम्। ते व्यक्तं निरयं घोरं प्रविशन्ति पुनः पुनः॥
en: They who see Nature and Soul in any other light are said to possess an incorrect vision. It is certain that they have repeatedly to sink into dreadful hell.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: सांख्यदर्शनमेतत् ते परिसंख्यानमुत्तमम्। एवं हि परिसंख्याय सांख्याः केवलतां गताः॥
en: I have thus told you the philosophy of the Sankhyas, that excellent science by which all things have been correctly determined. Ascertaining the nature of Soul and Nature in this way, the Sankhyas acquire Liberation.

description: What is with qualities and what is without qualities
sn: ये त्वन्ये तत्त्वकुशलास्तेषामेतन्निदर्शनम्। अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि योगानामनुदर्शनम्॥
en: I have also told of the systems of those others who are conversant with the great principles of the universe. I shall now describe to you the science of the Yogins,

sn: याज्ञवक्ल्य उवाच सांख्यज्ञानं मया प्रोक्तं योगज्ञानं निबोध मे। यथाश्रुतं यथादृष्टं तत्त्वेन नृपसत्तम॥
en: Yajnavalkya said, I have already spoken to you of the science of the Sankhyas. Hear now as I truly describe the science of the Yogins as heard and seen my me, O best of kings. are

sn: नास्ति सांख्यसमं ज्ञानं नास्ति योगसमं बलम्। तावुभावेकचर्यो तावुभावनिधनौ स्मृतौ॥
en: There is no Knowledge like that of the Sankhyas. There is no power like that of Yoga. These two prescribe the same practices, and both are considered as capable of leading to Liberation.

sn: पृथक् पृथक् प्रपश्यन्ति येऽप्यबुद्धिरता नराः। वयं तु राजन् पश्याम एकमेव तु निश्चयात्॥
en: Those men who not blest with intelligence consider the Sankhya and the Yoga systems to be different from each other. We, however, O king, regard them as one and the same, according to the conclusion to which we have arrived.

sn: यदेव योगाः पश्यन्ति तत् सांख्यैरपि दृश्यते। एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स तत्त्ववित्॥
en: What the Yogins have in view is the very same which the Sankhyas also have in view. He who sees both the Sankhya and the Yoga systems to be one and the same is to be considered as truly conversant with the principles that ordain the universe.

sn: रुद्रप्रधानानपरान् विद्धि योगानरिंदम्। तेनैव चाथ देहेन विचरन्ति दिशो दश॥
en: Know, O king, that the vital airs and the senses are the chief instruments for practising Yoga. By only regulating those vital airs and the senses, Yogins go everywhere at their will.

sn: यावद्धि प्रलयस्तात सूक्ष्मेणाष्टगुणेन ह। योगेन लोकान् विचरन् सुखं संन्यस्य चानघ।॥
en: When the gross body is destroyed, Yogins, gifted with subtile bodies possessed of the eight Yoga powers wander over the universe, enjoying all sorts of happiness, O sinless one.

sn: वेदेषु चाष्टगुणिनं योगमाहुर्मनीषिणः। सूक्ष्ममष्टगुणं प्राहुर्नेतरं नृपसत्तम॥
en: The wise have, in the scriptures, spoken of Yoga as giving eight sorts of power. They have spoken of Yoga as gifted with eight limbs.

sn: द्विगुणं योगकृत्यं तु योगानां प्राहुरुत्तमम्। सगुणं निर्गुणं चैव यथा शास्त्रनिदर्शनम्॥
en: Indeed, O king, they have not spoken of any other sort of Yoga. It has been said that the practices of Yogins, excellent as those are of two sorts. Those two sorts, according to the characteristics described in the scriptures, are practices endued with attributes and those freed from attributes.

sn: धारणं चैव मनसः प्राणायामश्च पार्थिव। एकाग्रता च मनसः प्राणायामस्तथैव च॥
en: The concentration of the mind together with the regulation of the vital airs. O king, is one sort. The concentration of the mind along with subjugation of the senses, is of another sort. The first kind of Yoga is said to be that possessed of qualities; the second kind is said to be that freed from qualities.

sn: प्राणायामो हि सगुणो निर्गुणं धारयेन्मनः। यद्यदृश्यति मुञ्चन् वै प्राणान् मैथिलसत्तम। वाताधिक्यं भवत्येव तस्मात् तं न समाचरेत्।।१०
en: The, again, Regulation of the Vital air is Yoga with qualities. In Yoga without qualities, the mind, freed from its functions, should be fixed. Only the regulation of the vital air which is said to be endued with qualities should, in the first instance, be practised, for, O king of Mithila, if the vital air be exhaled without mentally thinking upon a definite image, the wind in the neophyte's system will increase to his great injury.

sn: निशायाः प्रथमे यामे चोदना द्वादश स्मृताः। मध्ये स्वप्नात् परे यामे द्वादशैव तु चोदनाः॥
en: In the first period of the night, twelve ways of suppressing the vital air are recommended. After sleep, in the last period of the night, other twelve ways of doing the same have been laid down.

sn: तदेवमुपशान्तेन दान्तेनैकान्तशीलिना। आत्मारामेण बुद्धेन योक्तव्योऽऽत्मा न संशयः॥
en: Forsooth, one endued with tranquillity, of controlled senses, living in retirement, rejoicing in one's in one's own self, and fully conversant with the meaning of the scriptures, should fix his Soul.

sn: पञ्चानामिन्द्रियाणां तु दोषानाक्षिप्य पञ्चधा। शब्दं रूपं तथा स्पर्श रसं गन्धं तथैव च॥ प्रतिभामपवर्गं च प्रतिसंहृत्य मैथिल। इन्द्रियग्राममखिलं मनस्यभिनिवेश्य ह॥
en: Removing the five faults of the five sense, viz., (withdrawing them from their objects of) sound, form, touch, taste, and scent, and removing those conditions called Pratibha and Apavanga, O king, of the Mithilas, all the senses should be fixed upon the mind.

sn: मनस्तथैवाहंकारे प्रतिष्ठाप्य नराधिप। अहंकार तथा बुद्धौ बुद्धिं च प्रकृतावपि॥
en: The mind should then be fixed on Consciousness, O king; Consciousness should next be fixed on Intelligence, and Buddhi should then be fixed on Nature.

sn: एवं हि परिसंख्याय ततो ध्यायन्ति केवलम्। विरजस्कमलं नित्यमनन्तं शुद्धमव्रणम्॥ तस्थुषं पुरुषं नित्यमभेद्यमजरामरम्। शाश्वतं चाव्ययं चैव ईशानं ब्रह्म चाव्ययम्।॥
en: Thus merging these one after another, Yogins meditate on the Supreme Soul which is One, which is freed from Darkness, which is Immutable and Infinite and Pure and without defect, and without blemish, who is Eternal Soul, who is unchangeable, who is Indivisible, who is without decay and death, who is everlasting who is above decrease, and which is Immutable Brahma.

sn: युक्तस्य तु महाराज लक्षणान्युपधारय। लक्षणं तु प्रसादस्य यथा तृप्तः सुखं स्वपेत्॥
en: Listen, now, O king, to the marks of one that is Yoga. All the marks of cheerful contentment that are his who is sleeping in contentment are seen in the person, that is in Samadhi.

sn: निर्वाते तु यथा दीपो ज्वलेत् स्नेहसमन्वितः। निश्चलोखंशिखस्तद्वद् युक्तमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: The person in contemplation, the wise hold looks like the fixed and upward flame of a lamp that is full of oil and that burns in a spot where there is no air.

sn: पाषाण इव मेघोत्थैर्यथा बिन्दुभिराहतः। नालं चालयितुं शक्यस्तथा युक्तस्य लक्षणम्॥
en: He is like a rock which is incapable of being moved in the last by even a heavy downpour from the clouds.

sn: शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैर्विविधैर्गीतवादितैः। क्रियमाणैर्न कम्पेत युक्तस्यैतन्निदर्शनम्॥
en: He is incapable of being moved by the sound of couchs and drums, or by songs, or the sound of hundreds of musical instruments beat or blown together. Even this is the characteristic of one in contemplation.

sn: तैलपात्रं यथा पूर्ण कराभ्यां गृह्य पुरुषः। सोपानमारुहेद् भीतस्तय॑मानोऽसिपाणिभिः॥ संयतात्मा भयात् तेषां न पात्राद् बिन्दुमुत्सृजेत्। तथैवोत्तरमागम्य एकाग्रमनसस्तथा॥ स्थिरत्वादिन्द्रियाणां तु निश्चलत्वात् तथैव च। एवं युक्तस्य तु मुनेर्लक्षणान्युपलक्षयेत्॥
en: As a man of cool courage and determination, while going up a flight of steps with a vessel full of oil in his hands, does not spill even a drop of the liquid if terrified and threatened by person armed with weapons, so the Yogin, when his his mind has been concentrated and when he sees the Supreme Soul in contemplation, does not, of account of the entire stoppage of the functions of his senses at such a time, move in the slightest degree. Even these should be known to be the marks of the Yogin while he is in contemplation.

sn: स्वयुक्तः पश्यते ब्रह्म यत् तत्परममव्ययम्। महतस्तमसो मध्ये स्थितं ज्वलनसंनिभम्॥
en: While in contemplation, the Yogin sees Brahma which is Supreme and Immutable, and which is situated like a burning Effulgence in the midst of thick Darkness.

sn: एतेन केवलं याति त्यक्त्वा देहमसाक्षिकम्। कालेन महता राजश्रुतिरेषां सनातनी॥
en: It is by this means that he acquires, after many years, Liberation after renouncing this inanimate body. Even this is what the eternal Shruti says.

sn: एतद्धि योगं योगानां किमन्यद् योगलक्षणम्। विज्ञाय तद्धि मन्यन्ते कृतकृत्या मनीषिणः॥
en: This is called the Yoga of the Yogins. What else is it? Knowing it, they who are gifted with wisdoin consider themselves as crowned with Success.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच तथैवोत्क्रममाणं तु शृणुष्वावहितो नृप। पद्भ्यामुत्क्रममाणस्य वैष्णवं स्थानमुच्यते॥
en: Yajnavalkya said Listen now to me, with attention, O king, as to what the places are to which those who die have to go. If the Individual soul escapes through the feet, it is said that the man goes to the region of Vishnu.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: जवाभ्यां तु वसून् देवानाप्नुयादिति न श्रुतम्। जानुभ्यां च महाभागान् साध्यान् देवानवाप्नुयात्॥
en: If through the calves, it has been heard by us that the man goes to the regions of the Vasus. If through the knees, he acquires the companionship of those gods who are called Sadhyas.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: पायुनोत्क्रममाणस्तु मैत्रं स्थानमवाप्नुयात्। पृथिवीं जधनेनाथ उरुभ्यां च प्रजापतिम्॥
en: If through the lower duct, the man acquires the regions of Mitra. If through the posteriors, the man returns of the Earth, and if through the things to the region of Patriarch.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: पार्श्वभ्यां मरुतो देवान् नाभ्यामिन्द्रत्वमेव च। बाहुभ्यामिन्द्रमेवाहुरुरसा रुद्रमेव च॥
en: If through the flanks, the man acquires the regions of the Maruts, and if through the nostrils, to the region of the Moon. If through the arms, the man goes to the region of Indra, and if through the chest, to that of Rudra.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: ग्रीवया तु मुनिश्रेष्ठं नरमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्। विश्वेदेवान् मुखेनाथ दिशः श्रोत्रेण चाप्नुयात्॥
en: If through the neck, the man goes to the excellent region of that foremost of ascetics known as Nara. If through the mouth, the man acquires the region of the Vishvedevas, and if through the ears, to the region of the gods presiding over the several points of the horizon.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: घ्राणेन गन्धवहनं नेत्राभ्यामग्निमेव च। भूभ्यां चैवाश्विनौ देवौ ललाटेन पितृनथ॥
en: If through the nose, the man acquires the region of the Wind-god; and if through the eyes, to the region of Agni. If through this brows, the man goes to the region of the Ashvins; and if through the forehead, to that of the departed manes.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: ब्रह्माणमाप्नोति विभुं मूर्धा देवाग्रजं तथा। एतान्युत्क्रमणस्थानान्युक्तानि मिथिलेश्वर।॥
en: If through the crown of the head, the man goes to the region of the powerful Brahman, that foremost of the gods. I have thus told you, O king of Mithila, the several places to which men go according to the manner in which their individual souls escape from their bodies.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: अरिष्टानि प्रवक्ष्यामि विहितानि मनीषिभिः। संवत्सरवियोगस्य सम्भवन्ति शरीरिणः॥
en: I shall now tell you the presaging marks, as laid down by the wise, of those who have but one year to live.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: योऽरुन्धतीं न पश्येत दृष्टपूर्वां कदाचन। तथैव ध्रुवमित्याहुः पूर्णेन्दुं दीपमेव च॥ खण्डाभासं दक्षिणतस्तेऽपि संवत्सरायुषः।
en: One who, having previously seen the fixed star called Arandhati, cannot see it, or that other star called Dhruva, or one that sees the full Moon or the flame of a burning lamp to be broken towards the south, has but one year to live.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: परचक्षुषि चात्मानं ये न पश्यन्ति पार्थिव॥ आत्मच्छायाकृतीभूतं तेऽपि संवत्सरायुषः।
en: Those men, O king, who can no longer behold their own images reflected in the eyes of others, have but one year to live.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: अतिद्युतिरतिप्रज्ञा अप्रज्ञा चाद्युतिस्तथा॥ प्रकृतेर्विक्रियापत्तिः पण्मासान्मृत्युलक्षणम्।
en: One who being gifted with lustre loses it, or being endued with wisdom loses it,-indeed, one whose inward and outward nature is thus metamorphosed,-has but six months more to live.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: दैवतान्यवजानाति ब्राह्मणैश्च विरुद्ध्यते॥ कृष्णश्यावच्छविच्छायः षण्मासान्मृत्युलक्षणम्।
en: He who disregards the gods, or falls out with the Brahmanas, or one who being naturally of a dark colour become pale of hue, has but six months more to live.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: ऊर्णनाभेर्यथा चक्रं छिद्रं सोमं प्रपश्यति॥ तथैव च सहस्रांशुं सप्तरात्रेण मृत्युभाक्।
en: One who sees the lunar disc full of holes like spider's web, or one who sees the solar disc to have similar holes, has but one week more to live.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: शवगन्धमुपाघ्राति सुरभिं प्राप्य यो: नरः॥ देवतायतनस्थस्तु सप्तरात्रेण मृत्युभाक्।
en: One who, when smelling sweet scents in places of Worship, perceives them to be as offensive as the smell of dead bodies, has but one week more to live.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: कर्णनासावनमनं दन्तदृष्टिविरागिता॥ संज्ञालोपो निरूष्मत्वं सद्योमृत्युनिदर्शनम्।
en: The depression of the nose or of the cars, the discolour of the teeth or of the eyes, the loss of all consciousness, and the loss also of all animal magnetism, are symptoms indicating death that very day.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: अकस्माच्च स्रवेद् यस्य वाममक्षि नराधिप।॥ मूर्धतश्चोत्पतेद् धूमः सद्योमृत्युनिदर्शनम्।
en: If, without any ostensible cause tears suddenly flow from one's left eye, and if vapours be seen to issue from his head, it is a sure mark that the man will die before that day is over.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: एतावन्ति त्वरिष्टानि विदित्वा मानवोऽऽत्मवान्॥ निशि चाहनि चात्मानं योजयेत् परमात्मनि।
en: on Knowing all these presaging symptoms, the man of purified soul should day and night unite his soul with the Supreme Soul.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: प्रतीक्षमाणस्तत्कालं यत्कालं प्रेतता भवेत्॥ अथास्य नेष्टं मरणं स्थातुमिच्छेदिमां क्रियाम्। सर्वगन्धान रसांश्चैव धारयीत नराधिप।१९।।
en: Thus should he go on till the day comes for his death. If, however, instead of wishing to die he wishes to live in this world, he renounces all enjoyments,-0 king, and lives in abstinence. He thus conquers death by uniting his Soul with the Supreme Soul.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: ससांख्यधारणं चैव विदितात्मा नरर्षभ। यजेच्च मृत्यु योगेन तत्परेणान्तरात्मना॥
en: Indeed, the man who is gifted with knowledge of the Soul, O king, follows the practises recommended by the Sankhyas and conquers death by uniting his Soul with Supreme Soul.

description: The places to which the dead go
sn: गच्छेत् प्राप्याक्षयं कृत्स्नमजन्म शिवमव्ययम्। शाश्वतं स्थानमचलं दुष्प्रापमकृतात्मभिः॥
en: At last, he acquires what is entirely indestructible, which is without birth, which is auspicious, and immutable, and eternal, and stable, and which is incapable of being acquired by men of impure souls.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच अव्यक्तस्थं परं यत् तत् पृष्टस्तेऽहं नराधिप। परं गुह्यमिमं प्रश्नं शृणुष्वावहितो नृप॥
en: Yajnavalkya said You have asked me, O king, of that Supreme Brahma which lives in the Unmanifest. Your question relates to a deep mystery. Listen to me with rapt attention, O king.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: यथाऽऽर्षेणेह विधिना चरतावनतेन ह। मयाऽऽदित्यादवाप्तानि यजूंषि मिथिलाधिप॥
en: Having behaved humbly according to the ordinances laid down by the Rishis I obtained the Yajushes, O king, from the Sun-god.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
