sn: महता तपसा देवस्तपिष्णुः सेवितो मया। प्रीतेन चाहं विभुना सूर्येणोक्तस्तदानघ॥ वरं वृणीष्व विप्रर्षे यदिष्टं ते सुदुर्लभम्। तत् ते दास्यामि प्रीतात्मा मत्प्रसादो हि दुर्लभः॥
en: With the hardest penances i formerly adored the heat-giving god. O sinless one, pleased with me, the powerful Sun, addressed me, saying, O regenerate Rishi, pray for the boon you covet, however difficult it may be of acquisition. I shall, with cheerful mind, grant it to you. It is very difficult to make me grant grace.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततः प्रणम्य शिरसा मयोक्तस्तपतां वरः। यजूंषि नोपयुक्तानि क्षिप्रमिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: Bowing to him with my head, I addressed that foremost of heat-giving luminaries thus, I have no knowledge of the Yajushes. I wish to know them forthwith.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततो मां भगवानाह वितरिष्यामि ते द्विज। सरस्वतीह वाग्भूता शरीरं ते प्रवेक्ष्यति॥
en: The holy one, thus solicited, told ine,-I shall grant you the Yajushes. Made up of the essence of speech, the goddess of learning Sarasvati will enter into your person.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततो मामाह भगवानास्यं स्वं विवृतं कुरु। विवृतं च ततो मेऽऽस्यं प्रविष्टा च सरस्वती॥
en: The god then ordered me to open my mouth. I did as I was cominanded. The goddess Sarasvati then entered into my body, O sinless one.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततो विदह्यमानोऽहं प्रविष्टोऽम्भस्तदानघ। अविज्ञानादमर्षाच्च भास्करस्य महात्मनः॥
en: At this, I began to burn. Unable to suffer the pain I plunged into river. Not understanding what the great Sun had done for a me for my well-being, I became even angry with him.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततो विदह्यमानं मामुवाच भगवान् रविः। मुहूर्तं सह्यतां दाहस्तत: शीतीभविष्यति॥
en: While I was burning with the energy of the goddess, the holy Sun told me.-Do you suffer this burning sensation for only a little time. That will soon come to an end and you will be cool.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: शीतीभूतं च मां दृष्ट्वा भगवानाह भास्करः। प्रतिष्ठास्यति ते वेदः सखिलः सोत्तरो द्विज॥
en: Indeed, I became cool. Beholding me restored to ease, the Maker of light said to me,-The whole Vedas, with its appendix, together with the Upanishads, will appear in you by inward light, О twice-born one.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: कृसनं शतपथं चैव प्रणेष्यसि द्विजर्षभ। तस्यान्ते चापुनर्भावे बुद्धिस्तव भविष्यति॥
en: You will also edit the entire Satapathas, O foremost of twice-born ones. After that, your understanding will turn to the path of Liberation.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: प्राप्स्यसे च यदिष्टं तत् सांख्ययोगेप्सितं पदम्। एतावदुक्त्वा भगवानस्तमेवाभ्यवर्तत॥
en: You will also acquire that end which is desirable and which is coveted by both Sankhyas and Yogins. Having said so, the divine Sun proceeded to the setting hills.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततोऽनुव्याहृतं श्रुत्वा गते देवे विभावसौ। गृहमागत्य संहृष्टोऽचिन्तयं वै सरस्वतीम्॥
en: Hearing his last words, and after he had departed from where I was, I came home in joy and then remembered the goddess Sarasvati.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततः प्रवृत्तातिशुभा स्वरव्यञ्जनभूषिता। ओङ्कारमादितः कृत्वा मम देवी सरस्वती॥
en: Thought of by me, the auspicious Sarasvati appeared immediately before my eyes, adorned with all the vowels and the consonants and having placed the syllable OM in the van.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततोऽहमयं विधिवत् सरस्वत्यै न्यवेदयम्। तपतां च वरिष्ठाय निषण्णस्तत्परायणः॥
en: was I then, according to the ordinance, offered to the goddess the usual Arghya, and dedicated another to the Sun, that foremost of all heatgiving gods. Doing this duty I took my seat, devoted to both those gods.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततः शतपथं कृत्स्नं सरहस्यं ससंग्रहम्। चक्रे सपरिशेषं च हर्षेण परमेण ह॥
en: Thereupon the entire Satapatha Brahmanas, with all their mysteries and with all their abstracts as also their appendices, appeared of themselves before my minds-eye, at which I became filled with great joy.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: कृत्वा चाध्ययन तेषां शिष्याणां शतमुत्तमम्। विप्रियार्थं सशिष्यस्य मातुलस्य महात्मनः॥
en: I then taught them to a hundred competent disciples and thereby did what disagreeable to my great maternal uncle (Vaishampayana) with the disciples round him.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततः सशिष्येण मया सूर्येणेव गभस्तिभिः। व्यस्तो यज्ञो महाराज पितुस्तव महात्मनः॥
en: Then, shining in the midst of my disciples like the Sun himself with his rays, I took the management of the Sacrifice, of your noble father, O king.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: मिषतो देवलस्यापि ततोऽर्धं हृतवानहम्। स्ववेददक्षिणायार्थे विमर्दे मातुलेन ह॥
en: In that Sacrifice, a quarrel arose between me and my maternal uncle as to who should be allowed to take the sacrificial fee that was paid for the recitation of the Vedas. In the very presence of Deval, I took half of that fee.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: सुमन्तुनाथ पैलेन तथा जैमिनिना च वै। पित्रा ते मुनिभिश्चैव ततोऽहमनुमानितः॥
en: Your father and Sumanta and Paila and Jaimini and other ascetics all agreed to that arrangement.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: दश पञ्च च प्राप्तानि यजूंष्यर्कान्मयानध। तथैव रोमहर्षेण पुराणमवधारितम्॥
en: I had thus got from the Sun the five times ten Yajushes, O king. I then studied the Puranas with Romaharshan.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: बीजमेतत् पुरस्कृत्य देवीं चैव सरस्वतीम्। सूर्यस्य चानुभावेन प्रवृत्तोऽहं नराधिप॥ कर्तुं शतपथं चेदमपूर्वं च कृतं मया। यथाभिलषितं मार्ग तथा तच्चोपपादितम्॥
en: Keeping before me those Mantras and the goddess Sarasvati, I then, O king, helped by the inspiration of the Sun, set myself to compile the excellent Satapatha Brahmanas, and succeeded in performing the task never before undertaken by any one else. That path which I has wished to take, has been taken by me and I have also taught it to my disciples.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: शिष्याणामखिलं कृत्स्नमनुज्ञातं ससंग्रहम्। सर्वे च शिष्याः शुचयो गताः परमहर्षिताः॥
en: Indeed I gave to my disciples the whole of those Vedas with their abstracts. Pure in mind and body, all those disciples have, on account of my instructions, become filled with joy.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: शाखाः पञ्चदशेमास्तु विद्या भास्करदेशिताः। प्रतिष्ठाप्य यथाकामं वेद्यं तदनुचिन्तयम्॥
en: Having established this knowledge consisting of fifty branches which I had acquired from the Sun, I now meditate on the great object of that knowledge (viz., Brahma).

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: किमत्र ब्रह्मण्यमृतं किं च वेद्यमनुत्तमम्। चिन्तयं स्तत्र चागत्य गन्धर्वो मामपृच्छत॥ विश्वावसुस्ततो राजन् वेदान्तज्ञानकोविदः। चतुर्विंशास्ततोऽपृच्छत् प्रश्नान् वेदस्य पार्थिव॥ पञ्चविंशतिमं प्रश्नं पप्रच्छान्वीक्षिकी तदा। विश्वाविश्वं तथाश्वाश्वं मित्रं वरुणमेव च॥
en: The Gandharva Vishvavasu, a master of the Vedanta Shastra, desirous, O king, of ascertaining what is good for the Brahmanas in this knowledge and what truth is in it, and what is the excellent object of this knowledge, once catechised me. He put to me altogether twentyfour questions, O king, regarding the Vedas. Finally, he put to me a question, numbered twenty-fifth which relates to ratioscination. These questions are as follow:-What is universe and what is non-universe? What is Ashva and what Ashva? What is Mitra? What is Varuna?

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं तथा ज्ञोऽज्ञः कस्तपा अतपास्तथा। सूर्यातिसूर्य इति च विद्याविद्ये तथैव च॥ वेद्यावेद्यं तथा राजन्नचलं चलमेव च। अपूर्वमक्षयं क्षय्यमेतत् प्रश्नमनुत्तमम्॥
en: What is Knowledge? What is the object of knowledge? What is Unintelligent? What is Intelligent? Who is Ka? Who is endued with the principle of change? Who is not endued with the same What is he that devours the Sun and what is the Sun? What is Vidya and what is Avidya? What is Vedya and Avedya? What is Immobile and Mobile? What is without beginning, what is indestructible, and what is Destructible? These were the transcendental questions put to me by that foremost of Gandharvas.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: अथोक्तश्च महाराज राजा गन्धर्वसत्तमः। पृष्टवाननुपूर्वेण प्रश्नमर्थविदुत्तमम्॥
en: After king Vishvavasu, that foremost of Gandharvas, had asked me these questions one after another, I answered them duly.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: मुहूर्तमुष्यतां तावद् यावदेवं विचिन्तये। बाढमित्येव कृत्वा च तूष्णीं गन्धर्व आस्थितः॥
en: At first, however, I told him,-Wait for a short time, till I reflect on your questions!—the Gandharva agreed to it, and sat in silence.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ततोऽनुचिन्तयमहं भूयो देवी सरस्वतीम्। मनसा स च मे प्रश्नो दध्नो घृतमिवोद्धतम्॥
en: I then thought once again of the goddess Sarasvati in my mind. The replies then to those questions naturally originated in my mind like butter from curds.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: तत्रोपनिषदं चैव परिशेषं च पार्थिव। मध्नामि मनसा तात दृष्ट्वा चान्वीक्षिकी पराम्॥
en: Keeping in view the high science of inferential ratioscination, I churned with my mind, O Monarch, the Upanishads and the supplementary works relating to the Vedas.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: चतुर्थी राजशार्दूल विद्यैषा साम्परायिकी। उदीरिता मया तुभ्यं पञ्चविंशादधिष्ठिता।॥
en: I then expounded to him the fourth science that deals with Liberation, O foremost of kings, and on which I have already discoursed to thee, and which is based upon the twenty-fifth, viz., Individual Soul.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: अथोक्तस्तु मया राजन् राजा विश्वावसुस्तदा। श्रूयतां यद् भवानस्मान् प्रश्न सम्पृष्टवानिह॥
en: Having said all this, O king, to king Vishvavasu, I then addressed him, saying, Listen now to the answers that I give to your several questions.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: विश्वाविश्वेति यदिदं गन्धर्वेन्द्रानुपृच्छसि। विश्वाव्यक्तं परं विद्याद् भूतभव्यभयंकरम्॥
en: I now dealt with the question which, O Gandharva, you ask, viz.,-what is Universe and what is Not-universe?—The Universe is Unmanifest and original Nature endued with the principles of birth and death which are terrible.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: त्रिगुणं गुणकर्तृत्वादविश्वो निष्कलस्तथा। अश्वश्चाश्वा च मिथुनमेवमेवानुदृश्यते॥ अव्यक्तं प्रकृति प्राहुः पुरुषेति च निर्गुणम्। तथैव मित्रं पुरुषं वरुणं प्रकृति तथा॥
en: It is, besides, possessed of the three qualities on account of its producing principles all of which are fraught with those attributes. That which is Not-universe is Purusha shorn of all attributes. By Ashva and Ashva are meant the female and the male. Similarly, Mitra is Soul, the Varuna is Nature.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ज्ञानं तु प्रकृति प्राहुर्तेयं निष्कलमेव च। अज्ञश्च ज्ञश्च पुरुषस्तस्मान्निष्कल उच्यते॥
en: Knowledge, again, is said to be Nature, while the object to be know is called Soul. The Ignorant and the Knowing or Intelligent and both Soul without attributes.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: कस्तपा अतपाः प्रोक्तः कोऽसौ पुरुष उच्यते। तपास्तु प्रकृति प्राहुरतपा निष्कलः स्मृतः॥
en: You have asked what is Kah, who is endued with change, and who is unendued therewith. I answer, Kah is Soul. That which is endued with change is Nature. He who is not endued therewith is Soul.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: तथैवावेद्यमव्यक्तं वेद्यः पुरुष उच्यते। चलाचलमिति प्रोक्तं त्वया तदपि मे शृणु॥
en: Likewise is called the unknowable is Nature; and that which is called Knowable is Soul.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: चलां तु प्रकृति प्राहुः कारणं क्षयसर्गयोः। आक्षेपसर्गयोः कर्ता निश्चलः पुरुषः स्मृतः॥
en: You have asked me about the Mobile and the Immobile. Hear my answer That which is mobile is Nature, which, undergoing changes, forms the cause of Creation and Destruction, The Immobile is Soul, for without himself undergoing changes he assists at Creation and Destruction.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: तथैव वेद्यमव्यक्तमवेद्यः पुरुषस्तथा। अज्ञावुभौ ध्रुवौ चैव अक्षयौ चाप्युभावपि॥ अजौ नित्यावुभौ प्राहुरध्यात्मगतिनिश्चयाः॥
en: What is Knowable is Nature; while what is Unknowable is Soul. Both Nature and Soul are said to be unintelligent, stable, indestructible, unborn and eternal, according to the decision of the philosophers who know the spiritual science.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: अक्षयत्वात् प्रजनने अजमत्राहुरव्ययम्। अक्षयं पुरुषं प्राहुः क्षयो ह्यस्य च विद्यते॥
en: On account of the indestructibility of Nature in the matter of Creation, Prakriti, which is unborn, is considered as not subject to decay destruction. Soul, again, is indestructible and unchangeable.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: गुणक्षयत्वात् प्रकृतिः कर्तृत्वादक्षयं बुधाः। एषा तेऽऽन्वीक्षिकी विद्या चतुर्थी साम्परायिकी॥
en: The qualities of Nature are destructible, but not Nature herself. The learned, therefore, call Nature indestructible. By undergoing changes Nature works as the cause of Creation. The results appear and disappear, but not original Nature. Hence also is Nature called indestructible. Thus have I told you the conclusions of the fourth Science based on the principles of inference and having Liberation for its end.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: विद्योपेतं धनं कृत्वा कर्मणा नित्यकर्मणि। एकान्तदर्शना वेदाः सर्वे विश्वावसो स्मृताः॥
en: Having acquired by the science of inference and by serving preceptors, the Richs, the Samans, and the Yajushes, all the or obligatory rites should be observed and all the Vedas read with reverence, O Vishvavasu,

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: जायन्ते च प्रियन्ते च यस्मिन्नेते यतश्च्युताः। वेदार्थं ये न जानन्ति वेद्यं गन्धर्वसत्तम॥ साङ्गोपाङ्गानपि यदि यश्च वेदानधीयते। वेदवेद्यं न जानीते वेदभारवहो हि सः॥
en: O foremost of Gandharvas, they who study the Vedas with all their branches from which all things originate and into which all things merge when destruction sets in, and which is the one object whose knowledge the Vedas seek to preach,-indeed, they who have no acquaintance with what the Vedas seek to establish,-study the Vedas uselessly and carry their burthen of such study in vain.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: यो घृतार्थी खरीक्षीरं मथेद् गन्धर्वसत्तम। विष्ठां तत्रानुपश्येत न मण्डं न च वै घृतम्॥
en: If a person seeking butter churns the milk of the she-ass, without finding what he seeks he simply finds a substance of foul smell like ordure.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: तथा वेद्यमवेद्यं च वेदविद्यो न विन्दति। स केवलं मूढमतिर्ज्ञानभारवहः स्मृतः॥
en: Similarly if one, having read the Vedas, fails to know what is Nature and what is Soul, one only proves his own foolishness of understanding and carries a useless load.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: द्रष्टव्यौ नित्यमेवैतो तत्परेणान्तरात्मना। तथास्य जन्मनिधने न भवेतां पुनः पुनः॥
en: One should, with devoted attention, think on both Nature and Soul, so that he may avoid repeated birth and death.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: अजस्रं जन्मनिधनं चिन्तयित्वा त्रयीमिमाम्। परित्यज्य क्षयमिह अक्षयं धर्ममास्थितः॥
en: Thinking upon the incident of one's repeated births and deaths and avoiding the religion of acts which merely yield destructible results, one should follow the eternal religion of Yoga.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: यदानुपश्यतेऽत्यन्तमहन्यहनि काश्यप। तदा स केवलीभूतः षड्विंशमनुपश्यति॥
en: O Kashyapa, if one continuously reflects on the nature of the Individual Soul and its connection with the Supreme Soul, he then succeeds in divesting him of all attributes and in seeing the Supreme Soul.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: अन्यश्च शाश्वतोऽव्यक्तस्तथान्यः पञ्चविंशकः। तस्य द्वावनुपश्येतां तमेकमिति साधवः॥
en: The Eternal and Unmanifest Supreme Soul is considered by men of foolish understandings as distinct from the Individual Soul. They are really wise who see both these as truly one and the same.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ते नैतन्नाभिनन्दन्ति पञ्चविंशकमच्युतम्। जन्ममृत्युभयाद् योगाः सांख्याश्च परमैषिणः॥
en: Frightened at repeated births and deaths, the Sankhyas and Yogins consider the Individual Soul and the Supreme Soul to be one and the same.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: विश्वावसुरुवाच पञ्चविशं यदेतत् ते प्रोक्तं ब्राह्मणसत्तम। तथा तन्न तथा चेति तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Vishvavasu then said You have, O foremost of Brahmanas, said that Individual Soul is indestructible and truly undistinguished from the Supreme Soul. This, however, is difficult to understand. You should once more explain this subject to me.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: जैगीषव्यस्यासितस्य देवलस्य मया श्रुतम्। पराशरस्य विप्रर्वार्षगण्यस्य धीमतः॥ भृगोः पञ्चशिखस्यास्य कपिलस्य शुकस्य च। गौतमस्यार्टिषेणस्य गर्गस्य च महात्मनः॥ नारदस्यासुरेश्चैव पुलस्त्यस्य च धीमतः। सनत्कुमारस्य ततः शुक्रस्य च महात्मनः॥ कश्यपस्य पितुश्चैव पूर्वमेव मया श्रुतम्। तदनन्तरं च रुद्रस्य विश्वरूपस्य धीमतः॥ दैवतेभ्यः पितृभ्यश्च दैतेयेभ्यस्ततस्ततः। प्राप्तमेतन्मया कृत्स्नं वेद्यं नित्यं वदन्त्युत॥
en: I have heard discourses on this subject from Jaigishavya, Asita, Devala, the regenerate sage Parashara, the intelligent Varshaganya, Bhrigu, Panchashikha, Kapila, Shuka, Gautama, Arshtisena, the great Garga, Narada, Asuri, the intelligent Paulastya, Sanatkumara, the great Shukra, and my father Kashyapa. Subsequently I heard this from Rudra and the intelligent Vishvarupa several of the gods, the Pitris, and the Daityas. I have gained all that they say, for they generally describe that eternal object of all knowledge.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: तस्मात् तद् वै भवबुद्ध्या श्रोतुमिच्छामि ब्राह्मण। भवान् प्रबर्हः शास्त्राणां प्रगल्भश्चातिबुद्धिमान्॥
en: I wish, however, to hear what you say on those subjects with the help of your intelligence. You are the foremost of all persons, and a learned learned lecturer on the scriptures, and gifted with great intelligence.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: न तवाविदितं किंचिद् भवाञ्चतिनिधिः स्मृतः। कथ्यते देवलोके च पितृलोके च ब्राह्मण॥
en: There is nothing which you do not know. You are an ocean of the Shrutis, as described, O Brahmana, in the world of both the gods and the departed manes.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ब्रह्मलोकगताश्चैव कथयन्ति महर्षयः। पतिश्च तपतां शश्वदादित्यस्तव भाषिता॥
en: The great Rishi living in the region of lords and who is said to be eternal lord of all luminaries, is your preceptor.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: सांख्यज्ञानं त्वया ब्रह्मन्नवाप्तं कृत्स्नमेव च। तथैव योगशास्त्रं च याज्ञवल्क्य विशेषतः॥
en: O Yajnavalkya, you have acquired the entire science, O Brahmana, of the Sankhyas, as also the scriptures of the Yogins in particular.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: निःसंदिग्धं प्रबुद्धस्त्वं बुध्यमानश्चराचरम्। श्रोतुमिच्छामि तज्ज्ञानं घृतं मण्डमयं यथा॥
en: Forsooth, you are enlightened, fully conversant with the mobile and immobile universe. I wish to hear you describe that knowledge, which is compared to clarified butter having solid grains.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच कृत्स्नधारिणमेव त्वां मन्ये गन्धर्वसत्तम। जिज्ञाससे च मां राजंस्तन्निबोध यथाश्रुतम्॥
en: Yajnavalkya said You are, O foremost of Gandharvas, capable of comprehending every knowledge. As, however, you ask me, do you hear me then explain to you according as I myself have obtained it from my preceptor.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: अबुध्यमानां प्रकृति बुध्यते पञ्चविंशकः। न तु बुध्यति गन्धर्व प्रकृतिः पञ्चविंशकम्॥
en: Nature, which is unintelligent, is apprehended by Individual Soul, however, cannot be apprehended by Nature, 0 Gandharva.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: अनेन प्रतिबोधेन प्रधानं प्रवदन्ति तत् सांख्ययोगाश्च तत्त्वज्ञा यथाश्रुतिनिदर्शनात्॥
en: In consequence of Individual Soul being reflected in Nature, the latter is called Pradhana by Sankhyas and Yogins conversant with the original principles as laid down in the Shrutis.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: पश्यंस्तथैव चापश्यन् पश्यत्यन्य: सदानघ। षड्विंशं पञ्चविंशं च चतुर्विंशं च पश्यति॥
en: O sinless one, the other, seeing, sees the Nature and the Soul; not seeing, it sees the Supreme Soul.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: न तु पश्यति पश्यंस्तु यश्चैनमनुपश्यति। पञ्चविंशोऽभिमन्येत नान्योऽस्ति परतो मम॥
en: The Souls thinks that there is nothing higher than itself. In sooth, however, though seeing it does not see the Supreme Self which sees it.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: न चतुर्विंशको ग्राह्यो मनुजैर्ज्ञानदर्शिभिः। मत्स्यश्चोदकमन्वेति प्रवर्तेत प्रवर्तनात्॥
en: The wise should never think that the Nature is at one with the Soul which has a real and independent existence. The fish live in water. It goes there impelled by its own nature.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: यथैव बुध्यते मत्स्यस्तथैषोऽप्यनुबुध्यते। स स्नेहात् सहवासाच्च साभिमानाच्च नित्यशः॥ स निमज्जति कालस्य यदैकत्वं न बुध्यते। उन्मज्जति हि कालस्य समत्वेनाभिसंवृतः॥
en: As the fish, though living in the water, is to be considered as separate from it, similarly is the Soul to be apprehended, i.e., though the Soul exists in a state of contact with the Nature, it is, however, in its real nature, separate form, and independent of Nature, When overwhelmed with the consciousness of Self, and when unable to understand its identity with the Supreme Soul, on account of the illusion that covers it, of its co-existence with Nature, and of its own manner of thinking, the Individual Soul always sinks down, but when freed from such consciousness it goes upwards.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: यदा तु मन्यतेऽन्योऽहमन्य एष इति द्विजः। तदा स केवलीभूतः षड्विंशमनुपश्यति॥
en: When the Individual Soul succeeds in apprehending that it is one, and Nature with which it lives is another, then only does it, O twice-born one, succeed in seeing the Supreme Soul and attaining to the condition of Oneness with the universe.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: अन्यश्च राजन्नवरस्तथान्यः पञ्चविंशकः। तत्स्थानाच्चानुपश्यन्ति एक एवेति साधवः॥
en: The Supreme is one, O king, and the Individual Soul is another. On account of the Supreme overlying the Individual Soul, the wise consider both to be one and the same.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ते नैतन्नाभिनन्दन्ति पञ्चविंशकमच्युतम्। जन्ममृत्युभयाद् भीता योगाः सांख्याश्च काश्यप।॥ षड्विंशमनुपश्यन्तः शुचयस्तत्परायणाः। यदा स केवलीभूतः षड्विंशमनुपश्यति। तदा स सर्वविद् विद्वान् न पुनर्जन्म विन्दति॥ एवमप्रतिबुद्धश्च बुध्यमानश्च तेऽनघ। बुद्धश्चोक्तो यथातत्त्वं मया श्रुतिनिदर्शनात्॥ पश्यापश्यं यो न पश्येत् क्षेम्यं तत्त्वं च काश्यप। केवलाकेवलं चाद्यं पञ्चविशं परं च यत्॥
en: For these reasons, Yogins and followers of the Sankhya system of philosophy, terrified by birth and death, blessed with sight of the Supreme Soul, pure in body and mind, and devoted to the Supreme Soul, do not welcome the Individual Soul as indestructible. When one sees the Supreme Soul and losing all consciousness of individuality becomes at one with the Supreme, he then becomes omniscient, and possessed of such omniscience he becomes freed from the obligation of rebirth. I have thus described to you truly, O sinless one, about Nature which is unintelligent, and Individual Soul which is gifted with intelligence, and the Supreme Soul which is gifted with omniscience, according to the marks laid down in the Shrutis. That man who does not see any difference between the knower and the known, and between knowledge and the known, is both Kevala and not-Kevala, is the original cause of the universe, is both Individual Soul and the Supreme Soul.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: विश्वावसुरुवाच तथ्यं शुभं चैतदुक्तं त्वया विभो सम्यक् क्षेम्यं दैवताद्यं यथावत्। स्वस्त्यक्षयं भवतश्चास्तु नित्यं बुद्ध्या सदा बुद्धियुक्तं मनस्ते॥
en: Vishvavasu said 0 powerful one, you have duly and adequately expounded what is the origin of all the gods and which produces Liberation. You have said what is true and excellent. May you enjoy inexhaustible blessings, and may your mind be ever united with intelligence.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच एवमुक्त्वा सम्प्रयातो दिवं स विभ्राजन् वै श्रीमता दर्शनेन। दृष्टश्च तुष्ट्या परयाभिनन्द्य प्रदक्षिणं मम कृत्वा महात्मा॥
en: Yajnavalkya said Having said those words, the king of Gandharvas proceeded towards heaven, shining in resplendence of beauty. Before leaving me, the great one duly honoured me by going round my body, and I found him, highly pleased.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ये ब्रह्मादीनां खेचराणां क्षितौ च चाधस्तात् संवसन्ते नरेन्द्र। तत्रैव तदर्शनं दर्शयन् वै सम्यक् क्षेम्यं ये पथं संश्रिता वै॥
en: He inculcated the science he had learnt from me to those celestials that live in the regions of Brahman and other gods, unto those who live on Earth, to also the dwellers of the nether regions, and to them who had adopted the path of Liberation, O king.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: सांख्याः सर्वे सांख्यधर्मे रताश्च तद्वद् योगा योगधर्मे रताश्च। स्तेषामेतदर्शनं ज्ञानदृष्टम्॥
en: The Sankhyas are devoted to the practices of their system. The Yogins are devoted to the practices of their system. There are others who are desirous of acquiring Liberation. To these latter this science yields palpable fruits.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ज्ञानान्मोक्षो जायते राजसिंह नास्त्यज्ञानादेवमाहुर्नरेन्द्र। तस्माज्ज्ञानं तत्त्वतोऽन्वेषितव्यं येनात्मानं मोक्षयेज्जन्ममृत्योः॥
en: O foremost of kings, Liberation originates from Knowledge. Without Knowledge it can never be acquired. The wise have said it, O king. Hence, one should try his best for acquiring true Knowledge in all its particulars, by which one may succeed in freeing oneself from birth and death.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: प्राप्य ज्ञानं ब्राह्मणात् क्षत्रियाद् वा वैश्याच्छूद्रादपि नीचादनीक्ष्णम्। श्रद्धातव्यं श्रद्दधानेन नित्यं न श्रद्धिनं जन्ममृत्यू विशेताम्॥
en: Acquiring knowledge from a Brahmana or a Kashtriya or Vaishya or even a Shudra who is of low birth, one having faith should always show respect for such knowledge. Birth and death cannot attack one who has faith. arose

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: सर्वे वर्णा ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मजाश्च सर्वे नित्यं व्याहरन्ते च ब्रह्मा तत्त्वं शास्त्रं ब्रह्मबुद्ध्या ब्रवीमि सर्वं विश्वं ब्रह्म चैतत् समस्तम्॥
en: All orders of men are Brahmanas. All originate from Brahman. All All men utter Brahma. Helped by an understanding that is derived from and directed to Brahma, I preach this science treating of Nature and Soul. Indeed this whole universe is Brahma.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ब्रह्मास्यतो ब्राह्मणाः सम्प्रसूता बाहुभ्यां वै क्षत्रियाः सम्प्रसूताः। नाभ्यां वैष्याः पादतश्चापि शूद्राः। सर्वे वर्णा नान्यथा वेदितव्याः॥
en: From the mouth of Brahman originated the Brahmanas; from his arms, the Kshatriyas; from his navel, the Vaishyas, and from his feet, the Shudras. All the orders should be considered as differing from one another.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: अज्ञानतः कर्मयोनि भजन्ते तां तां राजंस्ते तथा यान्त्यभावम्। तथा वर्णा ज्ञानहीनाः पतन्ते घोरादज्ञानात्प्राकृतं योनिजालम्॥
en: Actuated by Ignorance, all men meet with death and go, O king, by birth which is the cause of acts. Shorn of Knowledge, all orders of men, dragged by terrible Ignorance, fall into varied orders of being on account of the principles that originate from Nature.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: तस्माज्ज्ञानं सर्वतो मार्गितव्यं सर्वत्रस्थं चैतदुक्तं मया ते। तत्स्थो स्तस्मै नित्यं मोक्षमाहुर्नरेन्द्र॥
en: Therefore, all should, by every means, try to acquire Knowledge. I have told you that every person is entitled to took for its acquisition. One who is endued with Knowledge, as Brahmana. Others, are possessed of knowledge. Hence, this science of a Liberation is always open to them all. The Wise, O king, have said this.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: यत् ते पृष्टं तन्मया चोपदिष्ट याथातथ्यं तद्विशोको भवस्व। राजन् गच्छस्वैतदर्थस्य पारं सम्यक् प्रोक्तं स्वस्ति ते त्वस्तु नित्यम्॥
en: The questions you had put to me, have all been answered by me according to the truth. Do you, therefore, renounce all grief. Go you to the other end of this enquiry. Your questions were good. Blessings on your head for ever.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: भीष्म उवाच स एवमनुशास्तस्तु याज्ञवल्क्येन धीमता। प्रीतिमानभवद् राजा मिथिलाधिपतिस्तदा॥
en: Thus instructed by the intelligent Yajanavalkya, the king of Mithila become filled with joy.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: गते मुनिवरे तस्मिन् कृते चापि प्रदक्षिणम्। दैवरातिर्नरपतिरासीनस्तत्र मोक्षवित्॥ गोकोटिं स्पर्शयामास हिरण्यं तु तथैव च। रत्नाञ्जलिमथैकं च ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ तदा॥
en: The king honoured that foremost of ascetics by going round his body. Dismissed by the king, he left his court. King Daivarati, having acquired the knowledge of the religion of Liberation, took his seat, and touching a million kine and a quantity of gold, of gems and jewels, gave them away to a number of Brahmanas.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: विदेहराज्यं च तदा प्रतिष्ठाप्य सुतस्य वै। यतिधर्ममुपासंश्चाप्यवसन्मिथिलाधिपः॥
en: Installing his son in the sovereignty of the Videhas, the old king began to lead the life of a Yati.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: सांख्यज्ञानमधीयानो योगशास्त्रं च कृत्स्नशः। धर्माधर्मं च राजेन्द्र प्राकृतं परिगर्हयन्॥
en: Taking no notice of all ordinary duties, the king began to study the science of the Sankhyas and the Yogins in full.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: अनन्त इति कृत्वा स नित्यं केवलमेव च। धर्माधर्मों पुण्यपापे सत्यासत्ये तथैव च॥ जन्ममृत्यू च राजेन्द्र प्राकृतं तदचिन्तयत्। व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्य कर्मेदमिति नित्यं नराधिप॥
en: Considering himself to the Infinite, he began to reflect on only the Eternal and Independent One. He renounced all ordinary duties, Virtue and Vice, Truth and Falsehood, Birth and Death, and all other things relating to the principles produced by Nature.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: पश्यन्ति योगाः सांख्याश्च स्वशास्त्रकृतलक्षणाः। इष्टानिष्टविमुक्तं हि तस्थौ ब्रह्म परात्परम्॥
en: Both Sankhyas and Yogins, according to the teachings of their sciences, consider this universe as the outcome of the action of the Manifest and the Unmanifest.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: नित्यं तदाहुर्विद्वांसः शुचि तस्माच्छुचिर्भव। दीयते यच्च लभते दत्तं यच्चानुमन्यते॥
en: The learned say that Brahma is freed from good and evil, is self-dependent, the highest of the high, Eternal, and Pure. Do you, therefore, O king, become Pure.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ददाति च नरश्रेष्ठ प्रतिगृह्णाति यच्च ह। ददात्यव्यक्त इत्येतत् प्रतिगृह्णाति तच्च वै॥ आत्मा ह्येवात्मनो ह्येकः कोऽन्यस्तस्मात्परो भवेत्। एवं मन्यस्व सततमन्यथा मा विचिन्तय॥
en: The giver, the receiver of the gift, the gift itself, and that what is ordered to be given away, are all to be deemed as the unmanifest Soul. The Soul is the Soul's possession. Who, therefore, can be a stranger to one? Do you think always in this way. Never think otherwise.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: यस्याव्यक्तं न विदितं सगुणं निर्गुणं पुनः। तेन तीर्थानि यज्ञाश्च सेवितव्या विपश्चिता॥
en: He who does not know what is Nature possessed of qualities and what is Soul transcending qualities, only he, not possessed as he is of knowledge, repairs to sacred waters and cerebrates sacrifices.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: न स्वाध्यायैस्तपोभिर्वा यज्ञैर्वा कुरुनन्दन। लभतेऽव्यक्तिकं स्थानं ज्ञात्वा व्यक्तं महीयते॥
en: Not by study of the Vedas, not by penances, not by sacrifices, O son of Kuru, can one acquire the status of Brahma. Only when one succeeds in apprehending the Supreme or Unmanifest, he is respected.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: तथैव महतः स्थानमाहङ्कारिकमेव च। अहङ्कारात् परं चापि स्थानानि समवाप्नुयात्॥
en: They who wait upon Mahat acquires the regions of Mahat. They who wait upon Consciousness, go to the spot that belongs to Consciousness. They who wait upon what is higher, acquire higher places.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: ये त्वव्यक्तात् परं नित्यं जानते शास्त्रतत्पराः। जन्ममृत्युविमुक्तं च विमुक्तं सदसच्च यत्॥
en: Those persons learned in the scriptures, who succeed in apprehending eternal Brahma which is higher than Unmenifest nature, can acquire that which is above birth and death, which is free from qualities, and which is both existent and non-existent.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: एतन्मयाऽऽप्तं जनकात् पुरस्तात् तेनापि चाप्तं नृप याज्ञवल्क्यात्। ज्ञानं विशिष्टं न तथा हि यज्ञा ज्ञानेन दुर्गं तरते न यज्ञैः॥
en: I got all this knowledge from Janaka. The latter had got it from Yajnavalkya. Knowledge is very superior. Sacrifices cannot compare with it. With the help of Knowledge one succeeds in crossing the world's ocean which is beset with difficulties and dangers. One can never cross that by means of sacrifices.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: दुर्गं जन्म निधनं चापि राजन् न भौतिकं ज्ञानविदो वदन्ति यज्ञैस्तपोभिर्नियमैर्ऋतैश्च दिवं समासाद्य पतन्ति भूमौ॥
en: Birth and death, and other obstacles, O king, men of knowledge say, one cannot get over by ordinary exertion. Men acquire heaven through sacrifices, penances, observances. But they have again to drop down therefrom on the Earth. vows, and

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: तस्मादुपासस्व परं महच्छुचि शिवं विमोक्षं विमलं पवित्रम्। मुपास्य वै तत्त्वमृषिर्भविष्यसि॥
en: Do you, therefore, worship with reverence that which is Supreme, most pure, blessed, stainless, and sacred, and which is above all states. By apprehending Soul, O king, and by celebrating the Sacrifice which consists in the acquisition of Knowledge, you will really be wise.

description: Yajnavalka's attainment of knowledge. He describes the manifest and unmanifest
sn: यदुपनिषदमुपाकरोत् तथासौ जनकनृपस्य पुरा हि याज्ञवल्क्यः। च्छुभममृतत्वमशोकमर्च्छति॥
en: In former time, Yajnavalkya did that good to king Janaka which comes from a study of the Upanishads. The Eternal and Immutable Supreme was the subject which the great Rishi had described to the king of Mithila. It enabled him to attain to that Brahma which is auspicious and immortal, and which is above all sorts of sorrows.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ऐश्वर्यं वा महत् प्राप्य धनं वा भरतर्षभ। दीर्घमायुरवाप्याथ कथं मृत्युमतिक्रमेत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said Having acquired great power and great riches, and having obtained a long period of life, how many one succeed in shunning death?

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: तपसा वा सुमहता कर्मणा वा श्रुतेन वा। रसायनप्रयोगैर्वा कैर्नाप्नोति जरान्तकौ॥
en: By which of these means viz., penances, or the performance of the various acts, or by knowledge of the Shrutis, or the application of medicines, can one succeed in avoiding decrepitude and death.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। भिक्षोः पञ्चशिखस्येह संवादं जनकस्य च॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old narrative of Panchashikha who was a Bhikshu in his practices and Janaka.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: वैदेहो जनको राजा महर्षि वेदवित्तमम्। पर्यपृच्छत् पञ्चशिखं छिन्नधर्मार्थसंशयम्॥
en: Once on a time, Janaka, the king of Videhas, questioned the great Rishi Panchashikha, who was the foremost of all persons conversant with the Vedas and who had all his doubts removed about the object and meaning of all duties.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: केन वृत्तेन भगवन्नतिकामेज्जरन्तकौ। तपसा वाथ बुद्ध्या वा कर्मणा वा श्रुतेन वा॥
en: The King said By what conduct, O holy one, may one get over Decrepitude and Death? Is it by penances, or by the understanding, or by religious practices, or by study and knowledge of the scriptures.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: एवमुक्तः स वैदेहं प्रत्युवाचापरोक्षवित्। निवृत्तिर्न तयोरस्ति नानिवृत्तिः कथञ्चन॥
en: Thus addressed by the king of the Videhas the learned Panchashikha, conversant with all invisible things, answered saying, Nothing can prevent two (viz., decrepitude and death); nor is it true that these cannot be prevented under any circumstances.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: न हहानि निवर्तन्ते न मासा न पुनः क्षपाः। सोऽहं प्रपद्यतेऽध्वानं चिराय ध्रुवमध्रुवः॥
en: Neither days, nor nights, nor months, cease to go on. Only that man who, though transitory, follows the eternal path succeeds in avoiding birth and death.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: सर्वभूतसमुच्छेदः स्रोतसेवोह्यते सदा। ऊह्यमानं निमज्जन्तमप्लवे कालसागरे॥
en: Destruction overtakes all creatures. All creatures seem to be ceaselessly borne along the endless current of time. Those that are borne along the endless current of time which is without a vessel and which in infested by those two powerful alligators, viz., decrepitude and death, sink down without anybody coming to their help.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: जरामृत्युमहाग्राहे न कश्चिदभिपद्यते। नैवास्य कश्चिद् भवति नासौ भवति कस्यचित्॥
en: As one is swept along that current, one does not find any friend for help and one does not feel any interest for any one else.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: पथि सङ्गतमेवेदं दारैरन्यैश्च बन्धुभिः। नायमत्यन्तसंवासो लब्धपूर्वो हि केनचित्॥
en: One meets with wives and other friends only on his road. One had never before enjoyed this sort of companionship with any one for any length of time.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: क्षिप्यन्ते तेन तेनैव निष्टनन्तः पुनः पुनः। कालेन जाता याता हि वायुनेवाभ्रसंचयाः॥
en: Creatures, as they are carried along the current to time, become again and again are drawn towards one another like clouds moved by the wind meeting one another with loud noise.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: जरामृत्यू हि भूतानां खादितारौ वृकाविव। बलिनां दुर्बलानां च हस्वानां महतामपि॥
en: Like wolves, descrepitude and death are devourers of all creatures. Indeed, they devour the strong and the weak, the short and the tall.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: एवंभूतेषु भूतात्मा नित्यभूतोऽध्रुवेषु च। कथं हि हृष्येज्जातेषु मृतेषु च कथं ज्वरेत्॥
en: Among creatures, therefore, which are all so fickle only the Soul exists eternally. Why should he, then, rejoice when creatures are born and why should he grieve when the die.

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: कुतोऽहमागतः कोऽस्मि क्व गमिष्यामि कस्य वा। कस्मिन् स्थितः क्व भविता कस्मात्किमनुशोचसि।।१४।
en: Whence have I come? Who am I? Where shall I go? Whose am I? Before what do I rest? What shall I be? Why then do you grieve for what?

description: How a man can avoid death and decrepitude. The narrative of Panchashika
sn: द्रष्टा स्वर्गस्य कोऽन्योऽस्ति तथैव नरकस्य च। आगमांस्त्वनतिक्रम्य दद्याच्चैव यजेत च॥
en: Who else than you will see heaven or hell? Hence, without throwing aside the scriptures, one should make gifts and celebrate sacrifices.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अपरित्यज्य गार्हस्थ्यं कुरुराजर्षिसत्तम। कः प्राप्तो विनयं बुद्ध्या मोक्षतत्त्वं वदस्व मे॥
en: Yudhishthira said. Without giving up the domestic mode of life, O royal sage of Kuru's race, who ever acquired Liberation which is the annihilation of the Understanding? Do tell me this.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: संन्यस्यते यथाऽऽत्मायं व्यक्तस्यात्मा यथा च यत्। परं मोक्षस्य यच्चापि तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: How may the gross and the subtile form be renounced? Do you also, O grandfather, tell me what the supreme excellence of Liberation is.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। जनकस्य च संवाद सुलभायाश्च भारत॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Janaka and Sulabha, O Bharata!

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: संन्यासफलिकः कश्चिद् बभूव नृपतिः पुरा। मैथिलो जनको नाम धर्मध्वज इति श्रुतः॥
en: Formerly there was a king of Mithila, of the name of Dharmadhyaja, of Janaka's race. He was given to the religion of Renunciation,

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: स वेदे मोक्षशास्त्रे च स्वे च शास्त्रे कृतश्रमः। इन्द्रियाणि समाधाय शशास वसुधामिमाम्॥
en: He was well conversant with the Veda, with the scriptures on Liberation, and with the scriptures dealing with royal duties. Governing his senses, he ruled this Earth.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तस्य वेदविदः प्राज्ञाः श्रुत्वा तां साधुवृत्तताम्। लोकेषु स्पृहयन्त्यन्ये पुरुषाः पुरुषेश्वर॥
en: Hearing of his good conduct in the world, many wise men, well-conversant with wisdom, O foremost of men, wished to imitate him.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अथ धर्मयुगे तस्मिन् योगधर्ममनुष्ठिता। महीमनुचचारैका सुलभा नाम भिक्षुकी॥
en: In the saine golden age, a woman by name sulabha, belonging to the mendicant order, practised the duties of Yoga and travelled over the entire Earth.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तया जगदिदं कृत्स्नमटन्त्या मिथिलेश्वरः। तत्र तत्र श्रुतो मोक्षे कथ्यमानस्त्रिदण्डिभिः॥
en: In course of her wanderings over the Earth, Sulabha heard from many ascetics of different places that the king of Mithila was given to the religion of Liberation.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सातिसूक्ष्मां कथा श्रुत्वा तथ्यं नेति ससंशया। दर्शने जातसंकल्पा जनकस्य बभूव ह॥
en: Hearing this report about king Janaka and desirous of learning whether it was true or not, Sulabha became desirous of seeing Janaka.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तत्र सा विप्रहायाथ पूर्वरूपं हि योगतः। अबिभ्रदनवद्याङ्गी रूपमन्यदनुत्तमम्॥
en: Abandoning, by her Yoga powers, her former body and features, Sulabha assumed the most perfect features and peerless beauty.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: चक्षुर्निमेषमात्रेण लघ्वस्त्रगतिगामिनी। विदेहानां पुरी सुभूर्जगाम कमलेक्षणा॥
en: In the twinkling of an eye and with the speed of the quickest arrow the fair browed lady having eyes like lotus-petals went to the capital of the Videhas.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सा प्राप्य मिथिलां रम्यां प्रभूतजनसंकुलाम्। भैक्ष्यचर्यापदेशेन ददर्श मिथिलेश्वरम्॥
en: Arrived at the metropolis of Mithila having a large population, she adopted the guise of a mendicant and appeared before the king.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: राजा तस्याः परं दृष्ट्वा सौकुमार्यं वपुस्तदा। केयं कस्य कुतो वेति बभूवागतविस्मयः॥
en: The king, beholding her delicate form, became filed with wonder and enquired who she was, whose she was, and whence she came.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: ततोऽस्याः स्वागतं कृत्वा व्यादिश्य च वरासनम्। पूजितां पादशौचेन वरान्नेनाप्यतर्पयत्॥
en: Welcoming her, he assigned her an excellent seat, honoured her by offering water to wash her feet, and pleased her with excellent refreshments.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अथ भुक्तवती प्रीता राजानं मन्त्रिभिर्वृतम्। सर्वभाष्यविदां मध्ये चोदयामास भिक्षुकी॥
en: Refreshed duly and pleased with the rites of hospitality offered to her, Sulabha, the female mendicant, urged the king, who was encircled by his ministers and seated in the midst of learned scholars, (to speak out his fidelity to the religion of Liberation).

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सुलभा त्वस्य धर्मेषु मुत्तो नेति ससंशया। सत्त्वं सत्त्वेन योगज्ञा प्रविवेश महीपतेः॥
en: Doubting whether Janaka has succeeded in acquiring Liberation by following the religion of Renunciation, Sulabha, gifted with Yogapower, entered the understanding of the king by her own understanding.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: नेत्राभ्यां नेत्रयोरस्य रश्मीन् संयम्य रश्मिभिः। सा स्म तं चोदयिष्यन्ती योगबन्धैर्बबन्ध ह॥
en: Controlling, by means of the rays of light that came out from her own eyes, the rays issuing from the eyes of the king, the lady, desirous of ascertaining the truth, bound up king Janaka with Yoga fetters,

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: जनकोऽप्युत्स्मयन् राजा भावमस्या विशेषयन्। प्रतिजग्राह भावेन भावमस्या नृपोत्तम॥
en: Own Priding himself upon his invincibleness and defeating the intentions of Sulabha, that best of kings seized her resolution with his own resolution.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तदेकस्मिन्नधिष्ठाने संवादः श्रूयतामयम्। छत्रादिषु विमुक्तस्य मुक्तायाश्च त्रिदण्डके॥
en: The king, in his subtile form, had no royal umbrella and sceptre. The lady Sulabha, in hers, was without the threefold stick. Both staying then in the same form, thus conversed with each other. Listen to that conversation as it took place between the king and Sulabha.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: जनक उवाच भगवत्याः क्व चर्येयं कृता क्व च गमिष्यसि। कस्य च त्वं कुतो वेति पप्रच्छैनां महीपतिः॥
en: Janaka said O holy lady, to what course of conduct are you given? Whose are you? Whence have you come? After finishing your business here, where will you go?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: श्रुते वयसि जातौ च सद्भावो नाधिगम्यते। एष्वर्थेषूत्तरं तस्मात् प्रवेद्यं मत्समागमे॥
en: No one can, without questioning, determine another's proficiency in the scriptures, or age, or order of birth. You should, therefore, answer these questions of mine, when you have come to me.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: छत्रादिषु विशेषेषु मुक्तं मां विद्धि तत्त्वतः। स त्वां सम्मन्तुमिच्छामि मानार्हा हि मतासि मे॥
en: Know that I am truly shorn of all vanity about my royal umbrella and sceptre. I wish to know you thoroughly. You are deserving, I think, of my respect.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यस्माच्चैतन्मया प्राप्तं ज्ञानं वैशेषिकं पुरा। यस्य नान्यः प्रवक्तास्ति मोक्षं तमपि मे शृणु॥
en: Do you hear me as I describe to you Liberation, for there is none else who describe to you that subject. Hear me also as I tell you who that person is from whom in days of yore I acquired this distinguishing knowledge.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: पराशरसगोत्रस्य वृद्धस्य सुमहात्मनः। भिक्षोः पञ्चशिखंस्याहं शिष्यः परमसम्मतः॥
en: I am the beloved disciple of the great and venerable Panchashikha, belonging to the mendicant order, or Parasara's family.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सांख्यज्ञाने च योगे च महीपालविधौ तथा। त्रिविधे मोक्षधर्मेऽस्मिन् गताध्वा छिन्नसंशयः॥
en: My doubts have been removed and I am fully conversant with the Sankhya and the Yoga systems, and the ordinances about sacrifices and other rites, which form the three well known paths of Liberation.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: स यथाशास्त्रदृष्टेन मार्गेणेह परिभ्रमन्। वार्षिकांश्चतुरो मासान् पुरा मयि सुखोषितः॥
en: Wandering over the Earth and following path that is pointed out by the scriptures, the learned Panchashika formerly lived happily in my abode for four months during the rains.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तेनाहं सांख्यमुख्येन सुदृष्टार्थेन तत्त्वतः। श्रावितस्त्रिविधं मोक्षं न च राज्याद्धि चालितः॥
en: That foremost of Sankhyas described to me, according to the truth, and in an intelligible manner suited to my understanding, the several kinds of means for acquiring Liberation. He did not, however, order me to give up my kingdom.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सोऽहतामखिलां वृत्तिं त्रिविधां मोक्षसंहिताम्। मुक्तरागश्चराम्येकः पदे परमके स्थितः॥
en: Freed from attachments, and fixing my Soul on Supreme Brahma, and unaffected by companionship, I live, practising in all its minute details that threefold conduct which is laid down in treatises on Liberation.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: वैश्राग्यं पुनरेतस्य मोक्षस्य परमो विधिः। ज्ञानादेव च वैराग्यं जायते येन मुच्यते॥
en: Renunciation in the highest prescribed for Liberation. Renunciation, by which one becomes freed, emanate from Knowledge.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: ज्ञानेन कुरुते यत्तं यत्नेन प्राप्यते महत्। महद् द्वन्द्वप्रमोक्षाय सा सिद्धिर्या वयोऽतिगा।॥
en: From Knowledge originates the endeavour after Yoga, and through that exertion one acquires knowledge of Self. Through means knowledge of Self one gets over joy and grief. That enables one to transcend death and acquire great success.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सेयं परमिका बुद्धेः प्राप्ता निर्द्वन्द्वता मया। इहैव गतमोहेन चरता मुक्तसङ्गिना।॥
en: That high intelligence has been acquired by me, and accordingly I have not over all pairs of opposites. Even in this life I have been freed from stupefaction and have got over all attachments.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यथा क्षेत्रं मृदूभूतमद्भिराप्लावितं तथा। जनयत्यङ्कुरं कर्म नृणां तद्वत् पुनर्भवम्॥
en: As a soil, saturated with water and softened thereby, causes the seed to sprout forth, similarly, the acts of men cause rebirth.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यथा चोत्तापितं बीजं कपाले यत्र तत्र वा। प्राप्याप्यकुरहेतुत्वमबीजत्वान्न जायते॥ तद्वद् भगवतानेन शिखा प्रोक्तेन भिक्षुणा। ज्ञानं कृतमबीजं मे विषयेषु न जायते॥
en: As a seed, fried on a pan or otherwise, becomes unfit to sprout forth although the power for sprouting lies there, similarly my understanding having been freed from the productive principle formed by desire, by the instructions of the holy Panchashikha of the mendicant order, it no longer gives its fruit in the form of attachment to the objects of the senses.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: नाभिरज्यति कस्मिश्चिन्नानर्थे न परिग्रहे। नाभिरज्यति चैतेषु व्यर्थत्वाद् रागरोषयोः॥
en: I never experience love for my wife or hate for my enemies. Indeed, I keep aloof from both, making the fruitlessness of attachment and anger.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यश्च मे दक्षिणं बाहुं चन्दनेन समुक्षयेत्। सव्यं वास्यापि यस्तक्षेत् समावेतावुभौ मम॥
en: I regard both person impartially, viz., him who smears my right hand with sandal-paste and him who wounds my left.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सुखी सोऽहमवाप्तार्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः। मुक्तसङ्गः स्थितो राज्ये विशिष्टोऽन्यैस्त्रिदण्डिभिः॥
en: Having attained my object, I am happy, and consider in the same light a clod of earth, a piece of stone, and a lump of gold. I am shorn of all attachments, though am engaged in ruling a kingdom. On account of all this I am better known over all bearers of triple sticks.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: मोक्षे हि त्रिविधा निष्ठा दृष्टान्यैर्मोक्षवित्तमैः। ज्ञानं लोकोत्तरं यच्च सर्वत्यागश्च कर्मणाम्॥
en: Some foremost of men who are conversant with the Liberation say that Liberation has a triple path. Some consider Knowledge having all things of the world for its object as the means of Liberation. Some hold that the total renunciation of acts is the means thereof.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: ज्ञाननिष्ठां वदन्त्येके मोक्षशास्त्रविदो जनाः। कर्मनिष्ठां तथैवान्ये यतयः सूक्ष्मदर्शिनः॥
en: Another class of persons conversant with the scriptures Liberation say that Knowledge is the only means. Others, viz., Yatis, gifted with subtile vision; hold that acts form the means.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: प्रहायोभयमप्येव ज्ञानं कर्म च केवलम्। तृतीयेयं समाख्याता निष्ठा तेन महात्मना॥
en: The great Panchashikha, discarding both the opinion about knowledge and acts, considered the third as the only means or path of Liberation.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यमे च नियमे चैव कामे द्वेषे परिग्रहे। माने दम्भे तथा स्नेहे सदृशास्ते कुटुम्बिभिः॥
en: If house-holders be endued with selfrestraint, and control over the senses, they become the equals of Sannyasins. If, on the other hand, Sannyasins be endued with desire and aversion and wives and honour and pride and affection, they become like householders.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: त्रिदण्डादिषु यद्यस्ति मोक्षो ज्ञानेन कस्यचित्। छत्रादिषु कथं न स्यात् तुल्यहेतौ परिग्रहे॥
en: If one can acquire Liberation by means of knowledge, then may Liberation exist in triple sticks. Why then may Liberation not exist in the umbrella and the sceptre as well, especially when the reason in taking up the triple stick and the scepture is the same.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: येन येन हि यस्यार्थः कारणेनेह कर्मणि। तत्तदालम्बते सर्वः स्वे स्वे स्वार्थपरिग्रहे॥
en: One becomes attached to all those things and acts which are necessary for him for the sake of his own self for particular reasons.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: दोषदर्शी तु गार्हस्थ्ये यो व्रजत्याश्रमान्तरे। उत्सृजन् परिगृहंश्च सोऽपि सङ्गान्न मुच्यते॥
en: If a person, seeing the faults of the domestic mode of life, renounce it for adopting another mode, he cannot, for such rejection and adoption, he considered as one who is at once freed from all attachments.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: आधिपत्ये तथा तुल्ये निग्रहानुग्रहात्मके। राजभिर्भिक्षुकास्तुल्या मुच्यन्ते केन हेतुना॥
en: Sovereignty is fraught with the rewarding and the punishing of others. The life of a mendicant is equally fraught with the same. When, therefore, mendicants are like kings in this respect, why would mendicants only acquire Liberation, and not kings?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अथ सत्याधिपत्येऽपि ज्ञानेनैवेह केवलम्। मुच्यन्ते सर्वपापेभ्यो देहे परमके स्थिताः॥
en: Not withstanding the possession of sovereignty, therefore, one becomes purged of all sins by means of knowledge alone, living in Supreme Brahma.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: काषायधारणं मौण्ड्यं त्रिविष्टब्यं कमण्डलुम्। लिङ्गान्युत्पथभूतानि न मोक्षायेति मे मतिः॥
en: The putting on of brown cloths shaving of the head, bearing of the triple stick, and the water-pitcher, these are the external signs of one's mode of life. These are useless in helping one to acquire Liberation.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यदि सत्यपि लिङ्गेऽस्मिन् ज्ञानमेवात्र कारणम्। निर्मोक्षायेह दुःखस्य लिङ्गमानं निरर्थकम्॥
en: When, despite the adoption of these emblems of a particular mode of life, Knowledge along becomes the cause of one's Liberation from sorrow, it would appear that the adoption of mere emblems is absolutely useless.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अथवा दुःखशैथिल्यं वीक्ष्य लिङ्गे कृता मतिः। किं तदेवार्थसामान्यं छत्रादिषु न लक्ष्यते॥
en: Or, if, seeing the mitigation of sorrow in it, you have adopted these emblems of Sanyasa, why then should not the mitigation of sorrow be seen in the umbrella and the sceptre which I use.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: आकिंचन्ये न मोक्षोऽस्ति किंचन्ये नास्ति बन्धनम्। किंचन्ये चेतरे चैव जन्तुर्ज्ञानेन मुच्यते॥
en: Liberation does not exist in poverty; nor is bondage to be seen in riches. One acquires Liberation through Knowledge only, whether one is poor or rich.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तस्माद् धर्मार्थकामेषु तथा राज्यपरिग्रहे। बन्धनायतनेष्वेषु विद्ध्यबन्धे पदे स्थितम्॥
en: For these reasons, know that I am living in a state of freedom, though outwardly engaged in the enjoyment of religion, wealth, and pleasure, in the form of kingdom and wives, which form a field of bondage.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: राज्यैश्वर्यमयः पाशः स्नेहायतनबन्धनः। मोक्षाश्मनिशिते नेह च्छिन्नस्त्यागासिना मया॥
en: I have cut off the fetters formed by kingdom and riches, and the bondage of attachments, which the sword of Renunciation whetted on the the stone of the of the scriptures describing Liberation.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सोऽहमेवंगतो मुक्तो जातास्थस्त्वयि भिक्षुकि। अयथार्थं हि ते वर्णं वक्ष्यामि शृणु तन्मम॥
en: As regard myself then, I tell you that I have become freed in this way. O mendicant lady, I entertain an affection for you. But that should not prevent me from telling you that your conduct does not tally with the practices of the mode of life, which you have adopted.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सौकुमार्यं तथा रूपं वपुरग्र्यं तथा वयः। तवैतानि समस्तानि नियमश्चेति संशयः॥
en: Under formation of the body is highly delicate. You have beauty. You have an exceedingly shapely form. You are young. You have all these, and you have also subjugation of the senses. I doubt it verily. ine as

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यच्चाप्यननुरूपं ते लिङ्गस्यास्य विचेष्टितम्। मुक्तोऽयं स्यान्न वेति स्याद् धर्षितो मत्परिग्रहः॥
en: You have stopped up my body for ascertaining as to whether I am really liberated or not. This åct of yours does not tally with that mode of life whose emblems you carry.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: न च कामसमायुक्ते युक्तेऽप्यस्ति त्रिदण्डके। न रक्ष्यते त्वया चेदं न मुक्तस्यास्ति गोपना॥
en: The triple stick is unfit for a Yogin who has desire. As regards yourself, you do not adhere to your stick. As regards those who are freed, they should protect themselves from fall.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: मत्पक्षसंश्रयाच्चायं शृणु यस्ते व्यतिक्रमः। आश्रयन्त्याः स्वभावेन मम पूर्वपरिग्रहम्॥
en: Listen now to to what your transgression has been on account of your contact with me and your having entered into my gross body with the help of your understanding.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: प्रवेशस्ते कृतः केन मम राष्ट्रे पुरेऽपि वा। कस्य वा संनिकर्षात् त्वं प्रविष्टा हृदयं मम॥
en: Why have you entered into my kingdom or my palace? At whose sign have you entered heart.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: वर्णप्रवरमुख्यासि ब्राह्मणी क्षत्रियस्त्वहम्। नावयोरेकयोगोऽस्मि मा कृथा वर्णसंकरम्॥
en: You belong to the foremost of all the orders, being, as you are, a Brahmana woman. As regards myself whoever, I am a Kshatriya. There is no union for us two. Do not help to cause an intermixture of races.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: वर्तसे मोक्षधर्मेण त्वं गार्हस्थ्येऽहमाश्रमे। अयं चापि सुष्टस्ते द्वितीयोऽऽश्रमसंकरः॥
en: You follow the duties that lead to Liberation. I am a householder. This act of yours, therefore, is another evil you have committed, for it produces an unnatural union of two opposite modes of life.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सगोत्रां वासगोत्रां वा न वेद त्वां न वेत्थ माम्। सगोत्रमाविशन्त्यास्ते तृतीयो गोत्रसंकरः॥
en: into my I do not know whether you belong to my own family or do not belong to it. As regards yourself also, you do not know who I am. If you are of my own Gotra, you have by entering into my body, produced another evil,-viz., or unnatural union.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अथ जीवति ते भर्ता प्रोषितोऽप्यथवा क्वचित्। अगम्या परभार्येति चतुर्थो धर्मसंकरः॥
en: If, again, your husband be alive and living in an distant place, your union with me has produced the fourth evil of sinfulness, for you are not one whom I may lawfully marry.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सा त्वमेतान्यकार्याणि कार्यापेक्षा व्यवस्यसि। अविज्ञानेन वा युक्ता मिथ्याज्ञानेन वा पुनः॥
en: Do you commit all these sinful deeds, actuated by the motive of performing a particular object? Do you do these from ignorance or from perverted intelligence.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अथवापि स्वतन्त्रासि स्वदोषेणेह कर्हिचित्। यदि किंचिच्छ्रुतं तेऽस्ति सर्वं कृतमनर्थकम्॥
en: If, again, on account of your evil nature you have thus become thoroughly independent or unrestrained in your conduct, I tell you that if you have any knowledge of the scriptures, you will understand that everything you have done has been productive of evil.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: इदमन्यच्चतुर्थं ते भावस्पर्शविघातकम्। दुष्टाया लक्ष्यते लिङ्गं विवृण्वत्याप्रकाशितम्॥
en: A third fault touches you on account of these acts of yours, a fault that is destructive of peace of mind. By trying to show your superiority, the indication of a wicked woman is seen in you.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: न मय्येवाभिसंधिस्ते जयैषिण्या जये कृतः। येयं मत्परिषत् कृत्स्ना जेतुमिच्छसि तामपि॥
en: Desirous of asserting your victory as you are, it is not myself alone whom you wish to defeat, for it is plain that you wish to win a victory over even the whole of my court.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तथाहतस्ततश्च त्वं दृष्टिं स्वां प्रतिमुञ्चसि। मत्पक्षप्रतिघाताय स्वपक्षोद्भावनाय च॥
en: By loO king thus towards all these meritorious Brahmanas, it is clear that you wish to humiliate them all the glorify yourself.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: साम स्वेनामर्षजेन त्वमृद्धिमोहेन मोहिता। भूयः सृजसि योगांस्त्वं विषामृतमिवैकताम्॥
en: Stupefied by your pride of Yoga power that has been born of your jealousy, you have caused a union of your understanding with mine and thereby have really mingled together nectar with poision.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: इच्छतोरत्र यो लाभः स्त्रीसोरमृतोपमः। अलाभश्चापि रक्तस्य सोऽपि दोषो विषोपमः॥
en: The union, again, of man and woman, when each seek the other, is sweet as nectar. That association, however, of man and woman when the latter, herself coveting, cannot get an individual of the opposite sex that does not seek her, is, instead of being a merit, only a fault that is as noxious as poison.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: मा स्पाक्षीः साधु जानीष्व स्वशास्त्रमनुपालय। कृतेयं हि विजिज्ञासा मुक्तो नेति त्वया मम।
en: Do not continue to touch me. Know that I am righteous. Do you act according to your own scriptures. Your enquiry, viz., whether I am or I am not liberated, has been finished.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: एतत सर्वं प्रतिच्छन्नं मयि नार्हसि गुहितुम्॥७० सा यदि त्वं स्वकार्येण यद्यन्यस्य महीपतेः। तत् त्वं सत्रप्रतिच्छन्ना मयि नार्हसि गुहितुम्॥
en: You should not conceal from me all your secret motives. You should not who thus disguise yourself, conceal from me what your object is, that is, whether this call of yours has been prompted by the desire of accomplishing some object of your own or whether you have come for accomplishing the object of some other king.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: न राजानं मृषा गच्छेन्न द्विजातिं कथंचन। न स्त्रियं स्त्रीगुणोपेतां हन्युह्येते मृषा गताः॥
en: One should never appear deceitfully before a king; nor before a Brahmana; nor before his wife when that wife is possessed of every wifely virtue. Those who appear in deceitful guise before these three very soon meet with destruction.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: राज्ञां हि बलमैश्वर्यं ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदां बलम्। रूपयौवनसौभाग्यं स्त्रीणां बलमनुत्तमम्॥
en: The power of kings consists in their sovereignty. The power of Brahmanas wellversed in the Vedas is in the Vedas. Women hold a high power on account of their beauty and youth and blessedness.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अत एतैर्बलैरेव बलिनः स्वार्थमिच्छता। आर्जवेनाभिगन्तव्या विनाशाय ह्यनार्जवम्॥
en: These are powerful in the possession of these powers. He, therefore, who seeks to accomplish his own object should always approach these three with sincerity and openmindedness, Insincerity and deceit cannot yield success.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सा त्वं जातिं श्रुतं वृत्तं भावं प्रकृतिमात्मनः। कृत्यमागमने चैव वक्तुमर्हसि तत्त्वतः॥
en: You should, therefore, inform me of the order to which you belong by birth, of your learning and conduct and disposition and nature, as also of the object with which you have come here.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्येतैरसुखैर्वाक्यैरयुक्तैरसमञ्जसैः। प्रत्यादिष्टा नरेन्द्रेण सुलभा न व्यकम्पत॥
en: Bhishma said Though chastised by the king in these unpleasant, improper, and ill-applied words, the lady Sulabha was not at all abashed.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: उक्तवाक्ये तु नृपतौ सुलभा चारुदर्शना। ततश्चारुतरं वाक्यं प्रचक्रामाथ भाषितुम्॥
en: After the king had said these words, the beautiful Sulabha then gave vent to the following words in reply which were more handsome than her person.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सुलभोवाच नवभिनवभिश्चैव दोषैर्वाग्बुद्धिदूषणैः। अपेतमुपपन्नार्थमष्टादशगुणान्वितम्॥
en: O king, speech should always be free from the nine verbal faults and the nine faults of judgement. It should also, while setting forth the meaning with clearness, be possessed of the eighteen well-known merits.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सौक्षम्यं सांख्यक्रमौ चोभौ निर्णयः सप्रयोजनः। पञ्झैतान्यर्थजातानि वाक्यमित्युच्यते नृप।॥
en: Ambiguity, determination of the faults and merits of premises and conclusions, weighing the respective strength or weakness of those faults and merits, establishment of the conclusion, and the element of persuasiveness or otherwise that belongs to the conclusion thus arrived at,-these five characteristics belonging to the sense-form the authoritativeness of what is said.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: एषामेकैकेशोऽर्थानां सौम्यादीनां स्वलक्षणम्। शृणु संसार्यमाणानां पदार्थपदवाक्यतः॥
en: Listen now to the characteristics of these requirements beginning with ambiguity, one after another, as I explain them according to the combinations.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयेषु भिन्नेषु यदा भेदेन वर्तते। तत्रातिशायिनी बुद्धिस्तत् सौक्ष्म्यमिति वर्तते॥
en: When knowledge rests on difference from one another, and when the understanding rests upon many points one after another, the combination of words is said to be sullied by ambiguity.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: दोषाणां च गुणानां च प्रमाणं प्रविभागतः। कंचिदर्थमभिप्रेत्य सा संख्येत्युपधार्यताम्॥
en: By ascertainment called Sankhya, is meant the determination, by elimination, of faults or merits, adopting tentative meanings.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: इदं पूर्वमिदं पश्चाद् वक्तव्यं यद् विवक्षितम्। क्रमयोगं तमप्याहुर्वाक्यं वाक्यविदो जनाः॥
en: Krama, or weighing the relative strength or weakness of the faults or merits, consists in settling the propriety of the priority or subsequence of the words used in sentence. This is the meaning of the word Krama as held by person who can explain sentences or texts.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: धर्मकामार्थमोक्षेषु प्रतिज्ञाय विशेषतः। इदं तदिति वाक्यान्ते प्रोच्यते स विनिर्णयः॥
en: Conclusion is the final determination after this examination of what has been said on the subject of religion, pleasure, profit, and Liberation, in respect of what it particularly is that has been said in the text.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: इच्छाद्वेषाभवैर्दुःखैः प्रकर्षो यत्र जायते। तत्र या नृपते वृत्तिस्तत् प्रयोजनमिष्यते॥
en: The sorrow begotten by wish or hatred multiplies itself greatly. The conduct, O king, that one follows in such a matter is called Prayojanam.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तान्येतानि यथोक्तानि सौक्ष्यादीनि जनाधिप। एकार्थसमवेतानि वाक्यं मम निशामय॥
en: Take it for granted, O king, at my word, that these marks of Ambiguity and the others, vhen occurring together, make a complete and intelligible sentence.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: उपेतार्थमभिन्नार्थं न्यायवृत्तं न चाधिकम्। नाश्लक्ष्णं न च संदिग्धं वक्ष्यामि परमं ततः॥ न गुर्वक्षरसंयुक्तं पराङ्मुखसुखं न च। नानृतं न त्रिवर्गेण विरुद्धं नाप्यसंस्कृतम्॥ न न्यूनं कष्टशब्दं वा विक्रमाभिहितं न च। न शेषमनु कल्पेन निष्कारणमहेतुकम्॥
