en: The words I shall utter will have senses, be free from ambiguity, logical, free from tautology, smooth, certain, free from bombast, agreeable, or sweet truthful, not inconsistent with the three-1 old objects of life, refined not elliptical or imperfect, shorn of harshness or difficulty of comprehension, characterised by due order, not far-fetched in sense, corrected with one another as cause and effect, and each having a specific object.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: कामात् क्रोधाद् भयाल्लोभाद् दैन्याच्यानार्यकात् तथा। ह्रीतोऽनुक्रोशतो मानान्न वक्ष्यामि कथंचन॥
en: I shall not tell you anything, actuated by desire or anger or fear or cupidity or abjectness or deceipt or shame or mercy or pride.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: वक्ता श्रोता च वाक्यं च सदा त्वविकलं नृप। सममेति विवक्षायां तदा सोऽर्थः प्रकाशते॥
en: When the speaker, the hearer, and the words said, perfectly agree with one another in course of a speech, then does the sense or meaning come out very clearly.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: वक्तव्ये तु यदा वक्ता श्रोतारमवमन्य वै। स्वार्थमाह परार्थं तत् तदा वाक्यं न रोहति॥
en: When about what is to be said, the speaker does not care for the understanding of the hearer by uttering words whose meaning is understood by himself, then, however good those words may be, they cannot be comprehended by the hearer.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अथ यः स्वार्थमुत्सृज्य परार्थं प्राह मानवः। विशङ्का जायते तस्मिन् वाक्यं तदपि दोषवत्॥
en: That speaker, again, who, without caring for his own meaning, uses words that are of excellent sound and sense, creates only erroneous impressions in the mind of the hearer. Such words in such matters are certainly faulty.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यस्तु वक्ता द्वयोरर्थमविरुद्धं प्रभाषते। श्रोतुश्चैवात्मनश्चैव स वक्ता नेतरो नृप॥
en: That speaker, however, who uses words that are, while expressing his own meaning, intelligible to the hearer as well, is a true speaker. No other man deserves the name.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तदर्थवदिदं वाक्यमुपेतं वाक्यसम्पदा। अविक्षिप्तमना राजन्नेकाग्रः श्रोतुमर्हसि॥
en: You should, therefore, O king, hear with rapt attention these words of mine, fraught with meaning and endued with wealth of sound.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: कासि कस्य कुतश्चेति त्वयाहमभिचोदिता। तत्रोत्तरमिदं वाक्यं राजन्नेकमनाः शृणु॥
en: You have asked me who I am, whose I am, whence I am coming, etc. Listen now to me, O king, with full mind, as I answer these questions of yours.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यथा जतु च काष्ठं च पांसवश्चोदबिन्दवः। संश्लिष्टानि तथा राजन् प्राणिनामिह सम्भवः॥
en: As lac and wood, as grains of dust and drops of water, exist mixed up when brought together, so are the existence of all creatures.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: शब्दः स्पर्शो रसो रूपं गन्थः पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि च। पृथगात्मान आत्मानं संश्लिष्टा जतुकाष्ठवत्॥
en: Sound, touch, taste, form, and scent, these, and the senses, though different in their essences, exist yet in a state of unison like lac and wood.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: न चैषां चोदना काचिदस्तीत्येष विनिश्चयः। एकैकस्येह विज्ञानं नास्त्यात्मनि तथा परे॥
en: It is again well known that nobody asks any of these, saying, who are you? Each of them also has no knowledge either of itself or of the others.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: न वेद चक्षुश्चक्षुष्टुं श्रोत्रं नात्मनि वर्तते। तथैव व्यभिचारेण न वर्तन्ते परस्परम्॥
en: The eye cannot see itself. The ear cannot hear itself. The eye, again, cannot satisfy the functions of any of the other senses, or can any of the senses satisfy the functions of any sense except its own.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: प्रश्लिष्टं च न जानन्ति यथाऽऽप इव पांसवः। बाह्यानन्यानपेक्षन्ते गुणांस्तानपि मे शृणु॥
en: If all of them even combine together, even then they can not know their own-selves as dust and water mingled together can not know each other though existing together. In order to perform their respective functions, they await the contact of external objects.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: रूपं चक्षुः प्रकाशश्च दर्शने हेतवस्त्रयः। यथैवात्र तथान्येषु ज्ञानज्ञेयेषु हेतवः॥
en: The eye, form, and light, form the three requisites of the action called Seeing. The same holds good about the action of the other senses and the ideas which is their result.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: ज्ञानज्ञेयान्तरे तस्मिन् मनो नामापरो गुणः। विचारयति येनायं निश्चये साध्वसाधुनि॥
en: Then, again, between the functions of the senses and the ideas which are their result, the mind is an entity quite separate from the senses and is considered to have an action of its own. With its aid one distinguishes what is existent from what is non-existent for arriving at certainty.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: द्वादशस्त्वपरस्तत्र बुद्धिर्नाम गुणः स्मृतः। येन संशयपूर्वेषु बोद्धव्येषु व्यवस्यति॥
en: With the five senses of knowledge and five senses of action, the mind makes a total of eleven. The twelfth is the Understanding. When doubt originates about what is to be known, the Understanding comes forward and sets at rest all doubts,

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अथ द्वादशके तस्मिन् सत्त्वं नामापरो गुणः। महासत्त्वोऽल्पसत्त्वो वा जन्तुर्येनानुमीयते॥
en: After the twelfth, Sattva is another principle numbering the thirteenth. With its aid creatures are distinguished as possess more of it or less of it in their constitutions,

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अहं कर्तेति चाप्यन्यो गुणस्तत्र चतुर्दशः। ममायमिति येनायं मन्यते न ममेति च॥
en: After this, Consciousness (of self is an other principle.) It helps one to apprehend self as distinguished from what is not self.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अथ पञ्चदशो राजन् गुणस्तत्रापरः स्मृतः। पृथक्कलासमूहस्य सामग्र्यं तदिहोच्यते॥ गुणस्त्वेवापरस्तत्र संघात इव षोडशः। प्रकृतिर्व्यक्तिरित्येतौ गुणौ यस्मिन् समाश्रितौ॥
en: Desire is the fifteenth principle, O king, the whole universe. The sixteenth principle is Avidya or nescience. To it are attached the seventeenth and the eighteenth principles called Nature and Manifestation.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सुखासुखे जरामृत्यू लाभालाभौ प्रियाप्रिये। इति चैकोनविंशोऽयं द्वन्द्वयोग इति स्मृतः॥
en: Happiness and sorrow, decrepitude and death, gain and loss, the agreeable and the disagreeable,-these form the nineteenth principle and are called pairs of opposites.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: ऊर्ध्वं चैकोनविंशत्या कालो नामापरो गुणः। इतीमं विद्धि विंशत्या भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययम्॥
en: Beyond the nineteenth principle is another, viz., Time, called the twentieth. Know that the births and deaths of all creatures are owing to the action of this twentieth principle.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: विशश्वैष संघातो महाभूतानि पञ्च च। सदसद्भावयोगौ तु गुणावन्यौ प्रकाशकौ॥ इत्येवं विंशकश्चैव गुणाः सप्त च ये स्मृताः। विधिः शुक्रं बलं चेति त्रय एते गुणाः परे॥ विंशतिर्दश चैवं हि गुणाः संख्यानतः स्मृताः। समग्रा यत्र वर्तन्ते तच्छरीरमिति स्मृतम्॥
en: These twenty exist together, Besides these,. the five Great primary elements, and existence and non-existence, bring up the number to twenty-seven. Beyond these, there are three others, named Vidhi, Shukra, and Bala, that make the number thirty. That is which these thirteen principles occur is said to be body.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अव्यक्तं प्रकृतिं त्वासां कलानां कश्चिदिच्छति। व्यक्तं चासां तथा चान्यः स्थूलदर्शी प्रपश्यति॥ अव्यक्तं यदि वा व्यक्तं द्वयीमथ चतुष्टयीम्। प्रकृतिं सर्वभूतानां पश्यन्त्यध्यात्मचिन्तकाः॥
en: Whether the Unmanifest or the Manifest be their cause, or whether the two be considered as their cause, or, fourthly, whether the four together be the cause, they that are conversant with spiritual science behold Nature as the cause of all creatures.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: येयं प्रकृतिरव्यक्ता कलाभिर्व्यक्ततां गता। अहं च त्वं च राजेन्द्र ये चाप्यन्ये शरीरिणः॥
en: That Nature which is Unmanifest, becomes manifest in the form of these principles. Myself, yourself, O king, and all others that are gifted with body, are the result of that Nature.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: बिन्दुन्यासादयोऽवस्थाः शुक्रशोणितसम्भवाः। यासामेव निपातेन कललं नाम जायते॥
en: Embryonic conditions are due to the mixture of the vital seed and blood. On account of insemination the result which first appears is called by the name of 'Kalala.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: कललाद् बुद्बुदोत्पत्तिः पेशी च बुबुदात् स्मृता। पेश्यास्त्वङ्गाभिनिर्वृत्तिर्नखरोमाणि चाङ्गतः॥
en: From 'Kalala' originates bubble. From 'Budbuda' originates what is called 'Peshi.' From 'Peshi' that stage originates in which the various limbs are seen. From this last stage appear nails and hair.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सम्पूर्णे नवमे मासि जन्तोर्जातस्य मैथिल। जायते नामरूपत्वं स्त्री पुमान् वेति लिङ्गतः॥
en: When the ninth months is gone, O king of Mithila, the creature takes its birth so that, its sex being known, it is called a boy or girl.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: जातमात्रं तु तद्रूपं दृष्ट्वा ताम्रनखाङ्गुलि। कौमारं रूपमापन्नं रूपतो नोपलभ्यते॥
en: When the creature comes out of the womb, the form it presents is such that its nails and fingers seem to be of the colour of burnished copper. The next stage is called infancy, when the forin that was seen at the time of birth becomes metamorphosed.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: कौमाराद् यौवनं चापि स्थावीर्यं चापि यौवनात्। अनेन क्रमयोगेन पूर्वं पूर्वं न लभ्यते॥
en: From infancy youth is reached, and from youth, old age. As the creature advances from one stage into another, the from shown in the previous stage becomes changed.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: कलानां पृथगर्थानां प्रतिभेदः क्षणे क्षणे। वर्तते सर्वभूतेषु सौक्ष्म्यात् तु न विभाव्यते॥
en: The constituent elements of the body, which serve various functions in the general economy, undergo change every moment in every creature. Those changes, however, are so minute that they cannot be marked.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: न चैषामत्ययो राजल्लँक्ष्यते प्रभवो न च। अवस्थायामवस्थायां दीपस्येवार्चिषो गतिः॥
en: The birth of particles, and their death, in each successive stage, cannot be marked, O king, even as one cannot mark the changes in the flame of a burning lamp.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तस्याप्येवंप्रभावस्य सदश्वस्येव धावतः। अजस्रं सर्वलोकस्य कः कुतो वा न वा कुतः॥ कस्येदं कस्य वा नेदं कुतो वेदं न वा कुतः। सम्बन्धः कोऽस्ति भूतानां स्वैरप्यवयवैरिह॥
en: When such is the state of the bodies of all creatures,-i.e., when what is called the body is changing continually like the rapid motion of a house of good mettle,-who then has come whence or not whence, or whose is it or whose is it not, or whence does it not arise? What connection does there exist between creatures and their own bodies?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यथाऽऽदित्यान्मणेश्चापि वीरुद्भ्यश्चैव पावकः। जायन्त्येवं समुदयात् कलानामिव जन्तवः॥
en: As fire is generated from the contact of flint with iron, or from two sticks of wood when rubbed against each other, so are creatures created from combination of the (thirty) principles already named.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: आत्मन्येवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं यथा त्वमनुपश्यसि। एवमेवात्मनाऽऽत्मानमन्यस्मिन् किं न पश्यसि॥
en: Indeed, as you yourself see your own body in your body and as you yourself see your soul in your own soul, why is it that you do not see your own body and your own soul in the bodies and souls of others.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यद्यात्मनि परस्मिश्च समतामध्यवस्यसि। अथ मां कासि कस्येति किमर्थमनुपृच्छसि॥
en: If it is true that you see an identity with yourself and others, why then did you ask me who I am and whose?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: इदं मे स्यादिदं नेति द्वन्द्वैर्मुक्तस्य मैथिल। कासि कस्य कुतो वेति वचनैः किं प्रयोजनम्॥
en: If it is true that you have, O King, been freed from the knowledge of duality which says-this is mine and this other is not mine, then what use is there with such questions as Who are you, whose are you, and whence do you come?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: रिपौ मित्रेऽथ मध्यस्थे विजये संधिविग्रहे। कृतवान् यो महीपालः किं तस्मिन् मुक्तलक्षणम्।।१३०
en: What marks of Liberation can be said to take place in that king who acts as others act towards enemies and allies and neutrals and in victory and trace and war?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: त्रिवर्ग सप्तधा व्यक्तं यो न वेदेह कर्मसु। सङ्गवान् यस्त्रिवर्गेण किं तस्मिन् मुक्तलक्षणम्॥
en: What inarks of Liberation are in him who do not know the true nature of the three-fold objects of life as shown in seven ways in all acts and who, on that account, is attached to that three-fold objects?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: प्रिये वाप्यप्रिये वापि दुर्बले बलवत्यपि। यस्य नास्ति समं चक्षुः किं तस्मिन् मुक्तलक्षणम्॥१३२
en: What marks of Liberation exist in him who cannot look impartially on the agreeable, on the weak, and the strong? Unworthy as you are of it, your pretence to Liberation should be suppressed by your counsellors.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तदयुक्तस्य ते मोक्षे योऽभिमानो भवेन्नृप। सुहृद्धिः संनिवार्यस्तेऽविरक्तस्येव भेषजम्॥
en: This your attempt to acquire Liberation is like the use of medicine by a patient who indulges in all sorts of forbidden food and practices.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तानि तानि तु संचिन्त्य सङ्गस्थानान्यरिंदम। आत्मनाऽऽत्मनि सम्पश्येत् किमन्यन्मुक्तलक्षणम्॥
en: O chastiser of enemies, thinking of wives and other sources of attachment, one should see these in his own soul. What else can be considered as the indication of Liberation.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: इमान्यन्यानि सूक्ष्माणि मोक्षमाश्रित्य कानिचित्। चतुरङ्गप्रवृत्तानि सङ्गस्थानानि मे शृणु॥
en: Listen now to me as I speak fully of these and certain other minute sources of attachment belonging to the four-well-known acts to which you are still fettered though you profess yourself to have adopted the religion of Liberation.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: य इमां पृथिवीं कृत्स्नामेकच्छत्रां प्रशास्ति ह। एक एव स वै राजा पुरमध्यावसत्युत॥
en: That man who has to rule the entire world must, indeed, be a single king without a second. He is obliged to live in only a single palace.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तत्पुरे चैकमेवास्य गृहं यदधितिष्ठति। गृहे शयनमप्येकं निशायां यत्र लीयते॥
en: In that palace he has again only one sleeping 'room. In that room he has, again, only one bed on which at night he is to lie down.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: शय्यार्धं तस्य चाप्यत्र स्त्रीपूर्वमधितिष्ठति। तदनेन प्रसङ्गेन फलेनैवेह युज्यते॥
en: Half that bed again he is obliged to give to his Queen. This may serve as an example of how little the king's share is of all he is said to possess.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: एवमेवोपभोगेषु भोजनाच्छादनेषु च। गुणेषु परिमेयेषु निग्रहानुग्रहं प्रति॥
en: This is the case with his objects of enjoyment, with the food he eats, and with the dresses he puts on. He is thus attached to a very limited share of all things. He is, again, attached to the duties of rewarding and punishing.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: परतन्त्रः सदा राजा स्वल्पेष्वपि प्रसज्जते। संधिविग्रहयोगे च कुतो राज्ञः स्वतन्त्रता॥
en: The king always depends on others. He enjoys a very small share of all he is supposed to possess, and to that small share he is compelled to be attached. In the matter also of peace and war, the king is not independent?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: स्त्रीषु क्रीडाविहारेषु नित्यमस्यास्वतन्त्रता। मन्त्रे चामात्यसमितौ कुतस्तस्य स्वतन्त्रता॥
en: In the matter of women, of sports and other sports of enjoyment, the king's inclinations are greatly limited. In the matter of taking advice and in the assembly of his councellors what independence can the king be said to have.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यदा ह्याज्ञापयत्यन्यांस्तत्रास्योक्ता स्वतन्त्रता। अवशः कार्य ते तत्र तस्मिंस्तस्मिन् क्षणे स्थितः।।१४२
en: When, indeed, he passes orders on other men, he is said to be perfectly independent. But the moment after, in the several matters of his orders, his independence is limited by the very men whom he has ordered.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: स्वप्नकामो न लभते स्वप्तुं कार्यार्थिभिर्जनैः। शयने चाप्यनुज्ञातः सुप्त उत्थाप्यतेऽवशः॥
en: If the king wishes to sleep, he cannot satisfy his desire, resisted by those who have something to do with him. He must sleep when allowed, and while sleeping he is compelled to wake up for attending to those who have urgent business with him.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: स्नाह्यालभ पिब प्राश जुहुध्यग्नीन् यजेत्यपि। ब्रवीहि शृणु चापीति विवश: कार्यते परैः॥
en: Bathe, touch, drink, eat, pour libations on the fire, celebrate sacrifices, speak, hear,these are the words which kings have to hear from others and hearing them have to serve those that utter them.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अभिगम्याभिगम्यैवं याचन्ते सततं नराः। न चाप्युत्सहते दातुं वित्तरक्षी महाजनान्॥
en: Men come in numbers to the king and pray to him for gifts. Being, however, the protector of the general treasury, he cannot make gifts even to the most worthy.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: दाने कोषक्षयोऽप्यस्य वैरं चास्याप्रयच्छतः। क्षणेनास्योपवर्तन्ते दोषा वैराग्यकारकाः॥
en: If he makes gifts, the treasury becomes exhausted. If he does not, disappointed solicitors regard him inimically. He becomes vexed and as the outcome of this, misanthropy possesses his mind.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: प्राज्ञाशूरांस्तथैवाढ्यानेकस्थानपि शङ्कते। भयमप्यभये राज्ञो यैश्च नित्यमुपास्यते॥
en: If many wise and heroic and rich men live together, the king's mind begins to be filled with distrust. Even when there is no cause of fear, the king fears those who always wait upon and adore him.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तथा चैते प्रदुष्यन्ति राजन् ये कीर्तिता मया। तथैवास्य भयं तेभ्यां जायते पश्य यादृशम्॥
en: Those I have mentioned, O king, also find fault with him. See, how the king's fears may originate from even them.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सर्वः स्वे स्वे गृहे राजा सर्वः स्वे स्वे गृहे गृही। निग्रहानुग्रहान् कुर्वंस्तुल्यो जनक राजभिः॥
en: Then again all men are kings in their own houses. All men, again, in their own houses are householders. Like kings, O Janaka, all men in their own houses punish and reward.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: पुत्रा दारास्तथैवात्मा कोशो मित्राणि संचयाः। परैः साधारणा ह्येते तैस्तैरेवास्य हेतुभिः॥१५०॥
en: Like kings others also have sons and wives and their own selves and treasuries and friends and stores. In these respects the king does not differ from other men.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: हतो देशः पुरं दग्धं प्रधानः कुञ्जरो मृतः। लोकसाधारणेष्वेषु मिथ्याज्ञानेन तप्यते॥
en: The country is ruined, the city is burnt by fire,-the foremost of elephants is dead, at all this the king grieves like others, little thinking that these impressions are all owing to ignorance and mistake.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अमुक्तो मानसैर्दुःखैरिच्छाद्वेषभयोद्भवैः। शिरोरोगादिभी रोगैस्तथैवाभिनियन्तृभिः॥
en: The king is seldom freed from mental sorrows caused by desire and aversion and fear. He is generally afflicted also by headaches and various other diseases.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: द्वन्द्वैस्तैस्तैस्त्वपहतः सर्वतः परिशङ्कितः। बहुप्रत्यर्थिकं राज्यमुपास्ते गणयन्निशाः॥
en: The king is afflicted by all pairs of opposites. He is alarmed at everything. Indeed, beset with enemies and obstacles as kingdom is, the king, while he enjoys it, passes sleepless nights.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तदल्पसुखमत्यर्थं बहुदुःखमसारवत्। तृणाग्निज्वलनप्रख्यं फेनबुबुदसंनिभम्॥
en: Sovereignty, therefore, is blessed with a small share of happiness. The misery with which it is full is very great. It is as unreal as burning flames fed by straw or the bubbles of froth seen on the surface of water.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: को राज्यमभिपद्येत प्राप्य चोपशमं लभेत्। ममेदमिति यच्चेदं पुरं राष्ट्रं च मन्यसे।१५५॥
en: Who is there that would like to obtain sovereignty, or having acquired sovereignty can hope to acquire tranquillity? You know this kingdom and this palace as yours.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: बलं कोशममात्यांश्च कस्यैतानि न वा नृप। मित्रामात्यपुरं राष्ट्रं दण्डः कोशो महीपतिः॥ सप्ताङ्गस्यास्य राज्यस्य त्रिदण्ड्यस्येव तिष्ठतः। अन्योन्यगुणयुक्तस्य कः केन गुणतोऽधिकः॥
en: You think also this army, this treasury, and these counsellors as yours. Whose, however, in sooth are they, and whose are they not? Allies, ministers, capital, provinces, punishment, treasury, and the king,—these seven which form the limbs of a kingdom exist, depending upon one another, like three sticks standing with one another's help. The merits of each are shown by the merits of the others. Which of them can be said to be superior to the rest?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तेषु तेषु हि कालेषु तत्तदङ्गं विशिष्यते। येन यत् सिध्यते कार्यं तत् प्राधान्याय कल्पते॥
en: Some particular ones are regarded as superior to the rest when some important purpose is served through their agency. Superiority, for the time being, is said to belong to that one whose efficacy is thus seen.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सप्ताङ्गश्चैव संघातस्त्रयश्चान्ये नृपोत्तम। सम्भूय दशवर्गोऽयं भुङ्क्ते राज्यं हि राजवत्॥
en: The seven limbs already mentioned, O best of kings, and the three others, forming ten, supporting one another, are said to enjoy the kingdom like the king himself.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यश्च राजा महोत्साहः क्षत्रधर्मे रतो भवेत्। स तुष्येद् दशभागेन ततस्त्वन्यो दशावरैः॥
en: That king who is gifted with great energy and who is firmly attached to Kshatriya duties, should be satisfied with only a tenth part of the produce of the subject's field.Other kings are seen to be satisfied with less than a tenth part of such produce.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: नास्त्यसाधारणो राजा नास्ति राज्यमराजकम्। राज्येऽसति कुतो धर्मो धर्मेऽसति कुतः परम्॥
en: There is no one who possessed the kingly office without some one else possessing it in the world, and there is no kingdom without a king. If there be no kingdom, there can be no virtue and if there be no virtue, whence can Liberation arise.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: योऽप्यत्र परमो धर्मः पवित्रं राजराज्ययोः। पृथिवी दक्षिणा यस्य सोऽश्वमेधेन युज्यते॥
en: Merit of the most sacred and the highest order is associated with kings and kingdoms. By ruling a kingdom well, a king acquires the merit of a Horse-sacrifice with the whole Earth given away as sacrificial gift.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: साहमेतानि कर्माणि राजदुःखानि मैथिल। समर्था शतशो वक्तुमथवापि सहस्रशः॥
en: O king of Mithila, I can mention hundreds and thousands of faults like these that belong to kings and kingdoms.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: स्वदेहेनाभिषङ्गो मे कुतः परपरिग्रहे। न मामेवंविधां युक्तामीदृशं वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Then, again, when I have no real connection with even my body, how then can I be said to have any connection with the bodies of others? You cannot charge me with having tried to engender an inter-mixture of castes.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: ननु नाम त्वया मोक्षः कृत्स्नः पञ्चशिखाच्छ्रुतः। सोपाय: सोपनिषदः सोपासङ्गः सनिश्चयः॥
en: Have you heard the religion of Liberation in all its bearings from the lips of Panchashikha, together with its means, it methods, its practises, and its conclusion?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तस्य ते मुक्तसङ्गस्य पाशानाक्रम्य तिष्ठतः। छत्रादिषु विशेषेषु पुनः सङ्गः कथं नृप॥
en: If you have prevailed over all your bonds and freed yourself from all attachments, may I ask you, O king, why you preserve your connections still with this umbrella and those other appendages of royalty.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: श्रुतं ते न श्रुत मन्ये मृषा वापि श्रुतं श्रुतम्। अथवा श्रुतसंकाशं श्रुतमन्यच्छ्रुतं त्वया॥
en: I think that you have not listened to the scriptures, or, you have listened to them without any advantage, or, perhaps, you have listened to some other books loO king like the scriptures.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: अथापीमासु संज्ञासु लौकिकीषु प्रतिष्ठसे। अभिषङ्गावरोधाभ्यां बद्धस्त्वं प्राकृतो यथा॥
en: It appears that you are endued with only worldly knowledge, and that like an ordinary man of the world, you are bound by the fetters of touch and wives and mansions and the like.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: सत्त्वेनानुप्रवेशो हि योऽयं त्वयि कृतो मया। किं तवापकृतं यत्र यदि मुक्तोऽसि सर्वशः॥
en: If be true that you have been freed from all fetters, what harm then have I done you by entering your body with only my Intellect?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: नियमो ह्येषु वर्णेषु यतीनां शून्यवासिता। शून्यमावेशयन्त्या च मया किं कस्य दूषितम्॥
en: The practice with Yatis is to live in uninhabited or deserted adodes. What harm them have I done to whom by entering your understanding which is indeed shorn of true knowledge?

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: न पाणिभ्यां न बाहुभ्यां पादोरुभ्यां च चानघ। न गात्रावयवैरन्यैः स्पृशामि त्वां नराधिप॥
en: I have not touched you, O king, with my hands, or arms, or feet, or thighs, O sinless One, or with any other part of the body.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: कुले महति जातेन ह्रीमता दीर्घदर्शिना। नैतत्सदसि वक्तव्यं सद्वासद्वा मिथः कृतम्॥
en: You are born in a great family. You have modesty. You have foresight. Whether the act has been good or bad, my entrance into your person has been a private one, concerning us two only. Was it not unfair for you to proclaim that private act before all your ministers.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: ब्राह्मणा गुरवश्चेमे तथा मान्या गुरूत्तमाः। त्वं चाथ गुरुरप्येषामेवमन्योन्यगौरवम्॥
en: All these Brahmanas deserve respect. They are foremost of preceptors. You also are worthy of their respect, being their king. Doing them respect, you are entitled to receive reverence from them.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: तदेवमनुसंदृश्य वाच्यावाच्यं परीक्षता। स्त्रीपुंसोः समवायोऽयं त्वया वाच्यो न संसदि॥
en: Thinking on all this, it was not proper for you to proclaim before these foremost of men the fact of this union between two persons of opposite sexes, if indeed, you are really acquainted with the rules of propriety about speech.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यथा पुष्करपर्णस्थं जलं तत्पर्णमस्पृशत्। तिष्ठत्यस्पृशती तद्वत् त्वयि वत्स्यामि मैथिल॥
en: O king of Mithila, I am living in you without touching you at all even like a drop of water on a lotus leaf that rests on it without drenching it in the least.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यदि वाप्यस्पृशन्त्या मे स्पर्श जानासि कञ्चन। ज्ञानं कृतमबीजं ते कथं तेनेह भिक्षुणा॥
en: If, despite this, you still feel my touch, how can it be believed that through the instructions of the mendicant Panchashika, your knowledge has become disassociated from the sensual objects.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: स गार्हस्थ्याच्च्युतश्च त्वं मोक्षं चानाप्य दुर्विदम्। उभयोरन्तराले वै वर्तसे मोक्षवार्तिकः॥
en: You have, it is evident, deviated from the domestic mode of life, but you have not yet acquired Liberation that is so difficult to acquire. You live between the two, pretending that you have reach the goal of Liberation.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: न हि मुक्तस्य मुक्तेन ज्ञस्यैकत्वपृथक्त्वयोः। भावाभावसमायोगे जायते वर्णसंकरः॥
en: The contact of one that is liberated with another that has been so, or of Soul with Nature, cannot lead to an intermingling which you fear.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: वर्णाश्रमाः पृथक्त्वेन दृष्टार्थस्यापृथक्त्विनः। नान्यदन्यदिति ज्ञात्वा नान्यदन्यत्र वर्तते॥
en: Only those who consider the Soul to be at one with the body, and who think the several orders and modes of life to be really different from one another, commit the inistake of supposing an intermingling to be possible. My body is different from yours. But my soul is not different from your soul. When I am able to realise this, I have not the least doubt that my understanding is really not living in yours, though I have entered into you by Yoga.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: पाणौ कुण्डं तथा कुण्डे पयः पयसि मक्षिका। आश्रिताश्रययोगेन पृथक्त्वेनाश्रिताः पुनः॥
en: A pot is carried in the hand. In the pot there is milk. On the milk is a fly. Though the hand and pot, the pot and milk, and the milk and the fly, cxist together, yet they are all different from each other.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: न तु कुण्डे पयोभावः पयश्चापि न मक्षिका। स्वयमेवाप्नुवन्त्येते भावा ननु पराश्रयम्॥
en: The pot does not assume the nature of the milk. Nor does the milk partake the nature of the fly. The condition of each is in dependent of itself, and can never be changed by the condition of that other with which it may for the time being exist.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: पृथक्त्वादाश्रमाणां च वर्णान्यत्वे तथैव च। परस्परपृथक्त्वाच्च कथं ते वर्णसंकरः॥
en: Simnilarly, colour and practices, though they may exist together with and in a person that is liberated, do not really belong to him. How then can an intermingly of orders be possible on account of this union of myself with you.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: नास्मि वर्णोत्तमा जात्या न वैश्या नावरा तथा। तव राजन् सवर्णास्मि शुद्धयोनिरविप्लुता॥
en: Then, again, I am not superior to you in colour. Nor am I a Vaishya, nor a Shudra, I am, O king, of the same caste with you, born of a pure family.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: प्रधानो नाम राजर्षिर्व्यक्तं ते श्रोत्रमागतः। कुले तस्य समुत्पन्नां सुलभा नाम विद्धि माम्॥
en: There was a royal sage named Pradhana. It is clear that you have heard of him. I am born in his family, and my name is Sulabha.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: द्रोणश्च शत्शृङ्गश्च चक्रद्वारश्च पर्वतः। मम सत्रेषु पूर्वेषां चिता मघवता सह॥
en: In the sacrifices performed by my ancestors, the foremost of the gods, viz., Indra, used come, accompanied by Drona, Shatashringa, and Chakradvara.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: साहं तस्मिन् कुले जाता भर्तर्यसति मविधे। विनीता मोक्षधर्मेषु चराम्येका मुनिव्रतम्।।१८६।
en: Born in such a family, it was found that no fitting husband could be found for me. Instructed then in the religion of Liberation, I wander over the Earth alone, practising asceticism. to

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: नास्मि सत्रप्रतिच्छन्ना न परस्वापहारिणी। न धर्मसंकरकरी स्वधर्मेऽसि धृतव्रता॥
en: I am not a hypocrite with regard to the life of Renunciation I follow; I am not a thief that appropriates others properties. I am not a confuser of the practices of the different castes. I am firm in the practices of the mode of life I follow.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: नास्थिरा स्वप्रतिज्ञायां नासमीक्ष्य प्रवादिनी। नासमीक्ष्यागता चेह त्वत्सकाशं जनाधिप॥
en: I am firm and steady in my vows. I never utter any word without thinking of its fitness. I did not come to you, without having thought properly, O king!

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: मोक्षे ते भावितां बुद्धिं श्रुत्वाहं कुशलैषिणी। तव मोक्षस्य चाप्यस्य जिज्ञासार्थमिहागता॥
en: Having heard that your understanding has been purified by the religion of Liberation, I came here from desire of some good. Indeed, it was for enquiring of you about Liberation that I had come.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: न वर्गस्था ब्रवीम्येतत् स्वपक्षपरपक्षयोः। मुक्तो व्यायच्छते यश्च शान्तौ यश्च न शाम्यति॥
en: I do not say so for glorifying myself and humiliating my opponents. But I say it, out of sincerity only. What I say is that he who is liberated never vaunts that intellectual superiority which one shows by logical discussions for the sake of victory. He, on the other hand, is really liberated who devotes himself to Brahima, that sole seat of peace.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: यथा शून्ये पुरागारे भिक्षुरेकां निशां वसेत्। तथाहं त्वच्छरीरेऽस्मिन्निमां वत्स्यामि शर्वरीम्॥
en: As a person of the mendicant order lives for only one night in an emphy house, similarly, I shall live for this one night in your body.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: साहं मानप्रदानेन वागातिथ्येन चार्चिता। सुप्ता सुशरणं प्रीता श्वो गमिष्यामि मैथिल॥
en: You have honoured me with both words and other offers that are due from a host to a guest. Having slept this one night in your body, O king of Mithila, which is as it were my own chamber now, tomorrow I shall go.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्येतानि स वाक्यानि हेतुमन्त्यर्थवन्ति च। श्रुत्वा नाधिजगौ राजा किञ्चिउदन्यदतः परम्॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words fraught with excellent sense and with reason, king Janaka could not replay thereto.

description: The excellence of Liberation; one can acquire it in domestic mode of life. The discourse between Janaka and Sulabha
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्येतानि स वाक्यानि हेतुमन्त्यर्थवन्ति च। श्रुत्वा नाधिजगौ राजा किञ्चिउदन्यदतः परम्॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words fraught with excellent sense and with reason, king Janaka could not replay thereto.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं निर्वेदमापन्नः शुको वैयासकिः पुरा। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: Yudhishthira said How was Shuka the son of Vyasa, in days of yore, won over to Renunciation? I wish to hear you recite the story. My curiosity about it is irrepressible.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: अव्यक्तव्यक्ततत्त्वानां निश्चयं बुद्धिनिश्चयम्। वक्तुमर्हसि कौरव्य देवस्याजस्य या कृतिः॥
en: You should, O you of Kuru's race, describe to me on the conclusions about the Unmanifest, the Manifest, and of the Truth (or Brahma) that is in, but unattached to, them, as also of the acts of self-create Narayana, as they are known to you.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: भीष्म उवाच प्राकृतेन सुवृत्तेन चरन्तमकुतोभयम्। अध्याप्य कृस्त्नं स्वाध्यायमन्वशाद् वै पिता सुतम्॥
en: Bhishma said Seeing his son Shuka living fearlessly as ordinary men do in practices that are regarded innocent by them, Vyasa taught him the entire Vedas and then discoursed to him one day in following manner.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: व्यास उवाच धर्मं पुत्र निषेवस्व सुतीक्ष्णौ च हिमातपौ। क्षुत्पिपासे च वायुंच जय नित्यं जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Vyasa said O son, becoming the master of your senses, do you conquer extreme cold and extreme heat, hunger and thirst, and the wind also, and having controlled them, do you practise virtue.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: सत्यमार्जवमक्रोधमनसूयां दमं तपः। अहिंसां चानृशंस्यं च विधिवत् परिपालय॥
en: Do you duly observe truth and sincerity, and freedom from anger and malice, and selfcontrol and penances, and the duties of benevolence and mercy.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: सत्ये तिष्ठ रतो धर्मे हित्वा सर्वमनार्जवम्। देवतातिथिशेषेण मात्रां प्राणस्य संलिह॥
en: Rest you on truth, firmly devoted to virtue, renouncing all sorts of insincerity and deceit. Do you support your life on the remnants of food after feeding gods and guests.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: फेनमात्रोपमो देहे जीवे शकुनिवत् स्थिते। अनित्ये प्रियसंवासे कथं स्वपिषि पुत्रक॥
en: Your body is as fickle as the froth on the surface of water. The Individual Soul is sitting unattached in it as a bird on a tree. The companionship of all agreeable objects is transitory. Why then, O son, do you sleep in such forgetfulness?

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: अप्रमत्तेषु जाग्रत्सु नित्ययुक्तेषु शत्रुषु। अन्तरं लिप्समानेषु बालस्त्वं नावबुध्यसे॥
en: Your enemies are careful and awake and ever-ready (to assail you) and always watchful of their opportunity. Why are you so foolish as not to know this?

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: अहःसु गण्यमानेषु क्षीयमाणे तथाऽऽयुषि। जीविते लिख्यमाने च किमुत्थाय न धावसि॥
en: As the days are going one after another, and period of your life is being decreased. Indeed, when your life is being continually shortened, why do you not run to preceptors?

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: ऐहलौकिकमीहन्ते मांसशोणितवर्धनम्। पारलौकिककार्येषु प्रसुप्ता भृशनास्तिकाः॥
en: Only they who have no faith, set their hearts on worldly things that have the only effect of increasing flesh and blood. They do not care for the next world.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: धर्माय येऽभ्यसूयन्ति बुद्धिमोहान्विता नराः। अपथा गच्छतां तेषामनुयाताऽपि पीड्यते॥
en: Those men who are stupefied by erroneous understandings show a hatred for virtue. The man who follows those misguided persons that have taken to devious and wrong paths is afflicted equally with them.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: ये तु तुष्टाः श्रुतिपरा महात्मानो महाबलाः। धर्म्य पन्थानमारूढास्तानुपास्स्व च पृच्छ च॥
en: They, however, who are contented, devoted to the scriptures, gifted with high souls, and possessed of great might, follow the path of virtue. Do you wait upon them with respect and seek instruction from them.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: उपधार्य मतं तेषां बुधानां धर्मदर्शिनाम्। नियच्छ परया बुद्ध्या चित्तमुत्पथगामि वै॥
en: Do you act according to the instructions received from those wise men whose eyes are set upon virtue. With understanding purified by such instructions and made superior, do you then control your heart which is ever ready to deviate from the right course.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: आद्यकालिकया बुद्ध्या दूरे श्व इति निर्भयाः। सर्वभक्ष्या न पश्यन्ति कर्मभूमिमचेतसः॥
en: They who always think about the present, who fearlessly consider the tomorrow as something quite remote,-they who do not observe any restrictions about food-are really senseless wights who fail to understand that this world is only a field of probation.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: धर्मं निःश्रेणिमास्थाय किंचित् किंचित् समारुह। कोषकारवदात्मानं वेष्टयन्नानुबुध्यसे॥
en: Going to the flight of steps formed by Virtue. Do you ascend those steps one after another. At present you are like a worm which weaves its cocoon round itself and thereby closes up all means of escape.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: नास्तिकं भिन्नमर्यादं कूलपातमिव स्थितम्। वामतः कुरु विस्रब्यो नरं वेणुमिवोद्धृतम्॥
en: Do you shun unhesitatingly, the atheist who transgresses all restraints, who is situated like a house by the side of a dreadful and encroaching current, and who seems to stand like a bamboo with its head erect in pride.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: कामं क्रोधं च मृत्युं च पञ्चेन्द्रियजला नदीम्। नावं धृतिमयीं कृत्वा जन्मदुर्गाणि संतर॥
en: Do you with the raft of Yoga cross the ocean of the world those whose five senses constitute its waters, having Desires and Anger and Death for its fierce monsters, and birth for its votex.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: मृत्युनाभ्याहते लोके जरया परिपीडिते। अमोघासु पतन्तीषु धर्मपोतेन संतर॥
en: Do you cross, with the raft of Virtue, the world that is affected by Death and afflicted by Decrepitude, and upon which the thunder-bolts formed by days and nights and falling incessantly.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: तिष्ठन्तं च शयानं च मृत्युरन्वेषते यदा। निर्वृत्तिं लभते कस्मादकस्मान्मृत्युनाशितः॥
en: When Death is seeking you at every moment, it is certain that Death may get you for his victim at any time. Whence will you get your rescue.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: संचिन्वानकमेवेनं कामानामवितृप्तकम्। वृकीवोरणमासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति॥
en: Like the she-wolf snatching away a lamb, Death snatches away one who is still engaged in acquiring wealth and still unsatisfied in the enjoyment of pleasures.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: क्रमशः संचितशिखो धर्मबुद्धिमयो महान्। अन्धकारे प्रवेष्टव्यं दीपो यत्नेन धार्यताम्॥
en: When you are destined to enter into the dark, do you hold up the blazing lamp or righteous understanding and whose flame has been sufficiently kept.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: सम्पतन् देहजालानि कदाचिदिह मानुषे। ब्राह्मण्यं लभते जन्तुस्तत् पुत्र परिपालय॥
en: Getting by various forms one after another in the world of men, a creature acquires the status of Brahmanhood with great difficulty. You have acquired that status. Do you then, O son, try to maintain it.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: ब्राह्मणस्य तु देहोऽयं न कामार्थाय जायते। इह क्लेशाय तपसे प्रेत्य त्वनुपमं सुखम्॥
en: A Brahmana has not been born for the gratification of senses. On the other hand, his body, for being subjected to mortification and penances in this world so that he may enjoy peerless happiness in the next world.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: स्तल्लब्ध्वा न रतिपरेण हेलितव्यम्। स्वाध्याये तपसि दमे च नित्ययुक्तः क्षेमाथीं कुशलपर: सदा यतस्व॥
en: The status of Brahmanhood is acquired by long-continued and austere penances. Having gained that status one should never waste his time in the gratification of his senses. Always engaged in penances and self-control and desirous of what is for your well being, do you live and act, devoted to peace and tranquillity.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: अव्यक्तप्रकृतिरयं कलाशरीरः सूक्ष्मात्मा क्षणत्रुटिशो निमेषरोमा। ऋत्वास्यः समबलशुक्लकृष्णनेत्रो मासाङ्गो द्रवति वयोहयो नराणाम्॥
en: The life, of every man, is like a horse. The nature of that horse unmanifest. The elements from its body. Its nature is highly subtile. Kshanas, and Trutis, and Nimeshas are the hair on its body. The twilight's form its shoulderjoints. The lighted and the dark fortnights form its two equally powerful eyes. Months are its other limbs. That horse is running incessantly.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा प्रसृतमजस्रमुग्रवेगं गच्छन्तं सततमिहाव्यपेक्षमाणम्। चक्षुस्ते यदि न परप्रणेतृनेयं धर्मे ते भवतु मनः परं निशाम्य॥
en: If your eyes be not blind, seeing then that horse continually moving forward in its invisible course, do you set your heart on virtue, after hearing what your preceptors have 10 say about the next world.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: ये चात्र प्रचलित धर्म कामवृत्ताः क्रोशन्तः सततमनिष्टसम्प्रयोगाः। क्लिश्यन्तः परिगतवेदनाशरीरा बह्वीभिः सुभृशमधर्मकारणाभिः॥
en: They who deviate from virtue and who act carelessly, who always show malice towards others and take to evil ways, are obliged to take bodies in the regions of Yama and suffer various afflictions on account of their various sinful deeds.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: राजा सदा धर्मपर: शुभाशुभस्य गोप्ता समीक्ष्य सुकृतिनां दधाति लोकान्। बहुविधमपि चरति प्रविशति सुखमनुपगतं निखद्यम्॥
en: That king who is given to virtue and who protects and punishes the good and the wicked with discrimination, acquires the regions of the men of righteous deeds. By doing various good acts, he acquires such happiness as is faultless and as is incapable of being attained to by going through even thousands of births.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: श्वानो भीषणकाया अयोमुखानि वयांसि बलगृध्रकुलपक्षिणां च संघाः। नुदमुपरतं विशसन्ति॥
en: Dreadful dogs, crows or iron beaks, flocks of ravens and vultures and other birds, and blood-sucking worms, attacks the man who disobeys the commands of his parents and preceptors when he goes to hell after death.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: मर्यादा नियताः स्वयम्भुवा य इहेमा: प्रभिनत्ति दशगुणा मनोऽनुगत्वात्। विपिनमवगाह्य स पापः॥
en: That sinful wretch who, on account of his carelessness, transgresses the ten boundaries that have been fixed by the Self-create himself, is obliged to pass his time in great inisery in the wild deserts situated in the dominions of Death.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: यो लुब्धः सुभृशं प्रियानृतश्च मनुष्य: सततनिकृतिवञ्चनाभिरति: स्यात्। उपनिधिभिरसुखकृत्स परमनिरयगो भृशमसुखमनुभवति दुष्कृतकर्मा॥
en: That man who is sullied with cupidity, who is fond of falsehood, who always takes pleasure in deception and cheating, and who does injuries to others by practising hypocrisy and deception, has to go to deep hell and suffer great misery and afflictions for his acts of iniquity.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: मवगाढोऽसिपत्रवनभिन्नगात्रः। परशुवनशयो निपतितो वसति च महानिरये भृशातः॥
en: Such a man is compelled to bathe in the broad river called Vaitarani whose waters are scalding, to enter into a forest of trees whose leaves are as sharp as swords, and then to lie down on a bed of axes. He has thus to pass his days in dreadful hell in great misery.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: महापदानि कत्थसे न चाप्यवेक्षसे परम्। चिरस्य मृत्युकारिकामनागतां न बुध्यसे॥
en: You see only the regions of Brahman and other gods, but you cannot see what is the highest. Alas, you are ever blind also to what brings Death on its train.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: प्रयायतां किमास्यते समुत्थितं महद् भयम्। अतिप्रमाथि दारुणं सुखस्य संविधीयताम्॥
en: Follow the path of Liberation. Why do you delay? A frightful terror, destructive of your happiness, is before you: Do you take prompt mcasures for acquiring Liberation.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पुरा मृत: प्रणीयते यमस्य राजशासनात्। त्वमन्तकाय दारुणैः प्रयत्नमार्जवे कुरु॥
en: Soon after death you are sure to be taken before Yama at his behest. For acquiring happiness in the next world, try to acquire virtue by the practice of difficult and austere vows.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पुरा समूलबान्धवं प्रभुईरत्यदुःखवित्। तवेह जीवितं यमो न चास्ति तस्य वारकः॥
en: The powerful Yama does not care for the sufferings of others, very soon takes the lives of all persons, that is, of yourself and your friends. there is none capable of resisting him.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पुराभिवाति मारुतो यमस्य यः पुरःसरः। पुरैक एव नीयसे कुरुष्व साम्परायिकम्॥
en: Very soon the wind of Yama will blow before you. Very soon will you be taken alone to that fearful presence. Do you then achieve what will be for your behoof there.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पुरा स हि क्व एव ते प्रवाति मारुतोऽन्तकः। पुरा च विभ्रमन्ति ते दिशो महाभयागमे॥
en: Where now is that Death-wind which will blow before you very soon? Very soon will the points of the horizon, when that time arrives, begin to whirl before your eyes.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: श्रुतिश्च संनिरुध्यते पुरा त्वेह पुत्रका समाकुलस्य गच्छतः समाधिमुत्तमं कुरु॥
en: O son, soon will your Vedas disappear from you as you go helplessly into that dread presence. Do you, therefore, think of Yoga abstraction which is endued with great excellence.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: शुभाशुभे पुरा कृते प्रमादकर्मविप्लुते। स्मरन् पुरा न तप्यसे निधत्स्व केवलं निधिम्॥
en: Do you try to attain that one only treasure so that you may not have to grieve at the recollection of your pristine deeds good and bad all of which are marked by mistake.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पुरा जरा कलेवरं विजर्जरीकरोति ते। बलाङ्गरूपहारिणी निधत्स्व केवलं निधिम्॥
en: Decrepitude very soon weakens your body and robs you of your strength and limbs and beauty. Do you, therefore, seek that one only treasure.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पुरा शरीरमन्तको भिनत्ति रोगसारथिः। प्रसह्य जीवितक्षये तपो महत् समाचर॥
en: Very soon the Destroyer, having Disease as his charioteer, will with a strong hand, for taking your life, pierce and break your body. Do you, therefore, practise austere penances.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पुरा वृका भयंकरा मनुष्यदेहगोचराः। अभिद्रवन्ति सर्वतो यतस्व पुण्यशीलने॥
en: Very soon will those terrible wolves that live within your body, attack from all sides. Do you try, therefore, to achieve acts acts of righteousness.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पुरान्धकारमेककोऽनुपश्यसि त्वरस्व वै। पुरा हिरण्यमयान् नगान् निरीक्षसेऽद्रिमूर्धनि॥
en: Very soon will you, all alone, see a thick darkness, and very soon will you see golden trees on the top of the hill. Do you, therefore, hurry to achieve acts of righteousness.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पुरा कुसङ्गत्तानि ते सुहन्मुखाश्च शत्रवः। विचालयन्ति दर्शनाद् घटस्व पुत्र यत्परम्॥
en: Very soon will those evil companions and enemies of yours, (viz., the senses), dressed as friends swerve you from correct vision. Do you, then, O son, try to achieve that which is of the highest good.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: धनस्य यस्य राजतो भयं न चास्ति चोरतः। मृतं च यन्न मुञ्चति समर्जयस्व तद् धनम्॥
en: Do you acquire that wealth which has no fear from either kings or thieves, and which one has not to renounce even at Death.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: न तत्र संवियुज्यते स्वकर्मभिः परस्परम्। यदेव यस्य यौतकं तदेव तत्र सोऽश्नुते॥
en: Acquired by one's own deeds, that wealth has never to be distributed among partners. Each enjoys that wealth which each has acquired for himself.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: परत्र येन जीव्यते तदेव पुत्र दीयताम्। धनं यदक्षरं ध्रुवं समर्जयस्व तत् स्वयम्॥
en: O son, give that to others by which they may be able to live in the next world. Do you also try to acquire that wealth which is indestructible and durable.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: न यावदेव पच्यते महाजनस्य यावकम्। अपक्व एव यावके पुरा प्रलीयसे त्वर॥
en: Do not think that you should first enjoy all sorts of pleasures and then try to acquire Liberation, for before; you are satiated with enjoyment you may meet with Death. Do you, in view of this, hasten to do acts of goodness.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: न मातृपुत्रबान्धवा न संस्तुतः प्रियो जनः। अनुव्रजन्ति संकटे व्रजन्तमेकपातिनम्॥
en: Neither mother, nor son, nor relatives, nor dear friends even when begged with honours, accompany the man that dies. One alone has to go to the regions of Yama.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: यदेव कर्म केवलं पुरा कृतं शुभाशुभम्। तदेव पुत्र सार्थिकं भवत्यमुत्र गच्छतः॥
en: Only those deeds, good and bad, that one did before death follow the man who goes to the other world.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: हिरण्यरत्नसंचयाः शुभाशुभेन संचिताः। न तस्य देहसंक्षये भवन्ति कार्यसाधकाः॥
en: The gold and gems that one has acquired by good and bad means do not do any good to man after death.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: परत्रगामिकस्य ते कृताकृतस्य कर्मणः। न साक्षि आत्मना समो नृणामिहास्ति कश्चन॥
en: There is no witness, of men who have gone to the next world, better than the soul, of all acts done and undone in life.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: मनुष्यदेहशून्यकं भवत्यमुत्र गच्छतः। प्रविश्य बुद्धिचक्षुषा प्रदृश्यते हि सर्वशः॥
en: The Yogins when they enter the sky of their hearts, see by Yoga intelligence that the destruction of body sets in when Individual Soul enters into the witness-Chaitanya.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: इहाग्निसूर्यवायवः शरीरमाश्रितास्त्रयः। त एव तस्य साक्षिणो भवन्ति धर्मदर्शिनः॥
en: Even here, the god of Fire, the Sun, and the Wind,-these three live in the body. These, seeing as they do all the practices of one's life, become his witnesses.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: अहर्निशेषु सर्वतः स्पृशत्सु सर्वचारिषु। प्रकाशगूढवृत्तिषु स्वधर्ममेव पालय॥
en: Days and Nights,—the former marked by the virtue of showing all things and the latter marked by the virtue of conccaling all things.-are running continually and touching all things. Do you, therefore, satisfy the duties of your own order.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: अनेकपारिपन्थिके विरूपरौद्रमक्षिके। स्वमेव कर्म रक्ष्यतां स्वकर्म तत्र गच्छति॥
en: The road in the other world is full of many foes and of many repulsive and terrible insects and worms. Do you take care of your own acts, for only acts will accompany you along that road.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: न तत्र संविभज्यते स्वकर्मणा परस्परम्। तथा कृतं स्वकर्मजं तदेव भुज्यते फलम्॥
en: There one has not to share his deeds with others, but every one enjoys or suffers the fruits of those acts which every one has himself performed.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: यथाप्सरोगणाः फलं सुखं महर्षिभिः सह। तथाऽऽनुवन्ति कर्मजं विमानकामगामिनः॥
en: As Apsaras and great Rishis acquires fruits of great happiness, similarly men of righteous deeds, acquire in the other world cars of transcendent brightness that go everywhere at the will of the riders.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: यथेह यत् कृतं शुभं विपाप्मभिः कृतात्मभिः। तदाप्नुवन्ति मानवास्तथा विशुद्धयोनयः॥
en: Men of pure deeds and purified souls and pure birth acquire in the next world fruits commensurate with their own righteous deeds in this life.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: प्रजापतेः सलोकतां बृहस्पतेः शतक्रतोः। व्रजन्ति ते परां गतिं गृहस्थधर्मसेतुभिः॥
en: By walking along the high road formed by the duties of domesticity, men acquire happy ends by acquiring the region of Prajapati or Brihaspati or of him of a hundred sacrifices.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: सहस्रशोऽप्यनेकशः प्रवक्तुमुत्सहाम ते। अबुद्धिमोहनं पुनः प्रभुर्निनाय पावकः॥
en: I can give you thousands and thousands of instructions. Know, however, that the powerful cleanser keeps all foolish persons in the Dark.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: गता त्रिरष्टवर्षता ध्रुवोऽसि पञ्चविंशकः। कुरुष्व धर्मसंचय वयो हि तेऽतिवर्तते॥
en: You have passed twenty-four years. You are now full twenty-five years of age. Your years are passing away. Begin now to husband virtue.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पुरा करोति सोऽन्तकः प्रमादगोमुखां चमूम्। यथागृहीतमुत्थितस्त्वरस्व धर्मपालन॥
en: The Destroyer that lives within error and carelessness will very soon deprive your senses of their respective powers. Do you, before that takes place, hasten to discharge your duties, relying on your body alone.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: यथा त्वमेव पृष्ठतस्त्वमग्रतो गमिष्यसि। तथा गतिं गमिष्यतः किमात्मना परेण वा॥
en: When it is your duty to go along that road in which your self only shall be in front and yourself only in the rear, what need then have you with either your body or your wife and children?

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: यदेकपातिनां सतां भवत्यमुत्र गच्छताम्। भयेषु साम्परायिकं निधत्स्व केवलं निधिम्॥
en: When men have to go alone and without companions to the region of Yama, it is clear that in view of such a situation of terror, you should try to acquire that one only treasure.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: सकूलमूलबान्धवं प्रभुहरत्यसङ्गवान्। न सन्ति यस्य वारकाः कुरुष्व धर्मसंनिधिम्॥
en: The powerful Yama, not caring for the sufferings of others, snatches away the friends and relatives of one's race by the very roots. There is no one who can resist him. Do you, therefore, seek to acquire virtue.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: इदं निदर्शनं मया तवेह पुत्र साम्प्रतम्। स्वदर्शनानुमानतः प्रवर्णितं कुरुष्व तत्॥
en: I impart to you these lessons, O son, that are all at one with the scriptures I follow. Do you, therefore, seek to acquire virtue.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: दधाति यः स्वकर्मणा ददाति यस्य कस्यचित्। अबुद्धिमोहजैर्गुणैः स एक एव युज्यते॥
en: He who maintains his body by performing the duties laid down for his own order, and who makes gifts for acquiring whatever fruits may attach to such acts, becomes freed from the consequences begotten by ignorance and errror.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: श्रुतं समस्तमश्नुते प्रकुर्वतः शुभाः क्रियाः। तदेतदर्थदर्शनं कृतज्ञमर्थसंहितम्॥
en: The knowledge which a man of pious deeds acquires from Vedic sayings leads to omniscience. That omniscience is at on with the science of the highest object of human acquisition. Instructions, given to the grateful, become beneficial.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: निबन्धनी रज्जुरेषा या ग्रामे वसतो रतिः। छित्त्वैतां सुकृतो यान्ति नैनां छिन्दन्ति दुष्कृतः॥
en: The pleasure that one takes in living amidst the dwellings of men is truly a fast-blinding cord. Snapping that cord, men of righteous deeds go to regions of great happiness. Wicked men, however, cannot break that fetter.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: किं ते धनेन किं बन्धुभिस्ते किं ते पुत्रैः पुत्रक यो मरिष्यसि। आत्मानमन्विच्छ गुहां प्रविष्टं पितामहास्ते क्व गताश्च सर्वे॥
en: What use have you of riches, O son, or of relatives, or of children, since you have to die? Do you engage in seeking for your soul which is hidden in a cave. Where have all your grandfathers gone?

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्ने चापराह्निकम्। न हि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतं वास्य न वाकृतम्॥
en: Do that today which you would keep for tomorrow. Do that in the forenoon which you would keep for the afternoon. Death does not wait for any one, to seen whether one has or has not done his task.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: अनुगम्य विनाशान्ते निवर्तन्ते ह बान्धवाः। अग्नौ प्रक्षिप्य पुरुषं ज्ञातयः सुहृदस्तथा॥ नास्तिकान् निरनुक्रोशान् नरान् पापमते स्थितान्। वामतः कुरु विस्रब्धं परं प्रेप्सुरतन्द्रितः॥
en: Following the body after one's death, one's relatives and kinsmen and friends return placing it on the funeral pyre. Do you unhesitatingly shun those who are men sceptics, who are destitute of mercy, and who are given to wicked ways, and do you try to seek, without listlessness or apathy, that which is for your greatest good.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: एवमभ्याहते लोके कालेनोपनिपीडिते। सुमहद् धैर्यमालम्ब्य धर्मं सर्वात्मना कुरु॥
en: When, therefore, the world is thus assailed by Death, do you, with your whole heart, achieve virtue, helped all the while by unswerving patience.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: अथेमं दर्शनोपायं सम्यग् यो वेत्ति मानवः। सम्यक् स्वधर्मं कृत्वेह परत्र सुखमश्नुते॥
en: That man who is well conversant with the means of acquiring Liberation and who duly satisfies the duties of his order, certainly acquires great happiness in the next world.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: न देहभेदे मरणं विजानता न च प्रणाशः स्वनुपालिते पथि। धर्मं हि यो वर्धयते स पण्डितो य एव धर्माच्च्यवते स मुह्यति॥
en: There is no destruction for you who do not recognise death in the attainment of a different body and who do not deviate from the path of the pious. He who increases the stock of virtue is truly wise. He, on the other hand, who deviates from virtue is said to be fool.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: प्रयुक्तयोः कर्मपथि स्वकर्मणो: फलं प्रयोक्ता लभते यथाकृतम्। निहीनकर्मा निरयं प्रपद्यते त्रिविष्टपं गच्छति धर्मपारगः॥
en: One who is engaged to the accomplishment of good deeds, attains to heaven and other rewards as the fruits of those acts; but he who is addicted to wicked deeds has to sink in hell.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: सोपानभूतं स्वर्गस्य मानुष्यं प्राप्य दुर्लभम्। तथाऽऽत्मानं समादध्याद् भ्रश्यते न पुनर्यथा॥
en: Having acquired the status of humanity, so difficult of getting, that is the stepping stone to heaven, one should fix his soul on Brahma so that he may not fall away once more.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: यस्य नोक्रामति मति: स्वर्गमार्गानुसारिणी। तमाहुः पुण्यकर्माणमशोच्यं पुत्रबान्धवैः॥
en: That man whose understanding, directed to the path of heaven, does not deviate therefrom, is considered by the wise as truly a man of virtue and when he dies his friends should indulge in grief.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: यस्य नोपहता वुद्धिर्निश्चये ह्यवलम्बते। स्वर्गे कृतावकाशस्य नास्ति तस्य महद् भयम्॥
en: That man whose understanding is not firm and which is directed to Brahma and who has attained to heaven, becomes freed from a great fear.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: तपोवनेषु ये जातास्तत्रैव निधनं गताः। तेषामल्पतरो धर्मः कामभोगानजानताम्॥
en: That who are born in asylums of ascetics and who die there, do not acquire much mnerit by abstaining all their life from enjoyments and the indulgence of desire.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: यस्तु भोगान् परित्यज्य शरीरेण तपश्चरेत्। न तेन किंचिन्न प्राप्तं तन्मे बहु मतं फलम्॥
en: He, however, who though possessed of objects of enjoyment renounces them and practices penances, succeeds in acquiring everything. The fruits of the penances of such a inan are, I think, much greater.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: मातापितृसहस्राणि पुत्रदारशतानि च। अनागतान्यतीतानि कस्य ते कस्य वा वयम्॥
en: Ever one had and will have in this world mothers and fathers and sons and wives, by hundreds and thousands. Who, however, were they and whose are we?

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: अहमेको न मे कश्चिन्नाहमन्यस्य कस्यचित्। न तं पश्यामि यस्याहं तन्न पश्यामि यो मम॥
en: I am quite alone. I have no one whom I may call mine. Nor do I belong to any one else, I do not see that person whose I am, nor do I see him whom I may call mine.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: न तेषां भवता कार्यं न कार्यं तव तैरपि। स्वकृतैस्तानि यातानि भवांश्चैव गमिष्यति॥
en: They have nothing to do with you. You have nothing to do with them. All creatures take birth according to their pristine deeds. You also shall have to go hence determined by your own deeds.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: इह लोके हि धनिनां स्वजन: स्वजनायते। स्वजनस्तु दरिद्राणां जीवतामपि नश्यति॥
en: It is seen in this world that the friends and followers of persons in affluence behaved towards them with devotion. The friends and followers, however, of the poor fall away during even the life-time of the poor.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: संचिनोत्यशुभं कर्म कलत्रापेक्षया नरः। तत: क्लेशमवाप्नोति परत्रेह तथैव च॥
en: Man commits numerous evil deeds for the sake of his wife. From those evil deeds he suffers much distress both in this world and in the next.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: पश्यति च्छिन्नभूतं हि जीवलोकं स्वकर्मणा। तत् कुरुष्व तथा पुत्र कृत्स्नं यत् समुदाहृतम्॥
en: The wise man sees the world of life devastated by the deed performed by every living being. Do you, therefore, O son, act according to all the instructions I have delivered to you.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: तदेतत् सम्प्रदृश्यैव कर्मभूमिं प्रपश्यतः। शुभान्याचरितव्यानि परलोकमभीप्सता॥
en: Seeing this world to be only a field of action, the man endued with true vision, should, from desire of happiness in the next world, do acts that are good.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: मासर्तुसंज्ञापरिवर्तकेण सूर्याग्निना रात्रिदिवेन्धनेन। स्वकर्मनिष्ठाफलसाक्षिकेण भूतानि काल: पचति प्रसह्य॥
en: Exerting his irresistible power, Time cooks all creatures, with the help of his ladle formed by months and seasons, the sun for his fire, and days and nights for his fuel, they being the witnesses of the fruits of every act done by every creature.

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: धनेन किं यन्न ददाति नाश्नुते। बलेन किं येन रिपुं न बाधते। श्रुतेन किं येन न धर्ममाचरेत् किमात्मना यो न जितेन्द्रियो वशी॥
en: For what object is that wealth which is not given away and which is not enjoyed? For what purpose is that strength which is not used in resisting or subjugating one's enemies? For what purpose is that knowledge of the scriptures which does not move one to deeds of virtue? And for what purpose is that soul which does not control the senses and abstain from evil deeds?

description: How Sukha was won over to Renunciation
sn: भीष्म उवाच इदं द्वैपायनवचो हितमुक्तं निशम्य तु। शुको गतः परित्यज्य पितरं मोक्षदेशिकम्॥
en: Bhishma said-Having heard these wholesome words spoken by the Island-born (Vyasa), "Shuka, leaving his father, proceeded to seek a preceptor who could teach him the religion of Liberation.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यद्यस्ति दत्तमिष्टं वा ततस्तप्तं तथैव च। गुरूणां वापि शुश्रूषा तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said If there is any efficacy in gifts, in sacrifices, in penances, well done, and in dutiful services done to preceptors and other reverend elders, do you, O grandfather, speak of the same to me.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: भीष्म उवाच आत्मनानर्थयुक्तेन पापे निविशते मनः। स कर्म कलुषं कृत्वा क्लेशे महति धीयते॥
en: Bhishma said An understanding associated with evil, makes the mind fall into sin. In this state one stains his deeds, and then falls into great distress.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: दुर्भिक्षादेव दुर्भिक्षं क्लेशात् क्लेशं भयाद् भयम्। मृतेभ्यः प्रमृता यान्ति दरिद्राः पापकर्मिणः॥
en: Those who are of sinful deeds, have to take birth as persons of very poor circumstances, They pass from famine to famine, from pain to pain, from fear to fear. They are more dead than those who are dead.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: उत्सवादुत्सवं यान्ति स्वर्गात स्वर्ग सुखात् सुखम्। श्रद्दधानाश्च दान्ताश्च धनस्था: शुभकारिणः॥
en: Possessed of affluence, persons having faith, who are self-controlled, and who are devoted to righteous deeds, go from joy to joy, from heaven to heaven, from happiness to happiness.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: व्यालकुञ्जरदुर्गेषु सर्पचौरभयेषु च। हस्तावापेन गच्छन्ति नास्तिकाः किमतः परम्॥
en: The unbelievers have to pass, with groping hands, through regions full of beasts of prey and elephants and pathless tracts full of snakes and robbers and other causes of fear. What more need be said of these?

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: प्रियदेवातिथेयाश्च वदान्याः प्रियसाधवः। क्षेम्यमात्मवतां मार्गमास्थिता हस्तदक्षिणम्॥
en: They, on the other hand, who have reverence for gods and guests, who are liberal, who have respect for good men, and who makes gifts in sacrifices, have for theirs the path that belongs to men of purified and subdued souls.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: पुलाका इव धान्येषु पूत्यण्डा इव पक्षिषु। तद्विधास्ते मनुष्येषु येषां धर्मो न कारणम्॥
en: Those who are not pious should not be counted among men even as grains without kennel are not counted among grain and a6 cockroaches are not counted among birds.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: सुशीघ्रमपि धावन्तं विधानमनुधावति। शेते सह शयानेन येन येन यथा कृतम्॥
en: The acts that one does, follow him even when he runs fast. Whatever act one does, lie down with the doer when the doer lays himself down.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: उपतिष्ठति तिष्ठन्तं गच्छन्तमनुगच्छति। करोति कुर्वतः कर्म च्छायेवानुविधीयते॥
en: Indeed, the sins one commits, sin when the doer sits, and run when he runs. The sin acts when the doer acts, and, in deed, follow the doer like his shadow.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: येन येन यथा यद् यत्पुरा कर्म सुनिश्चितम्। तत् तदेकतरो भुङ्क्ते नित्यं विहितमात्मना॥
en: Whatever the acts one does by whatever means and under whatever circumstances, are sure to be enjoyed and suffered by the doer in his next life.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: स्वकर्मफलनिक्षेपं विधानपरिरक्षितम्। भूतग्राममिमं कालः समन्तादपकर्षति॥
en: From every side Time is always dragging all creatures, following the rule about the distance to which they are thrown and which is commensurate with their deeds.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: अचोद्यमानानि यथा पुष्पाणि च फलानि च। स्वं कालं नातिवर्तन्ते तथा कर्म पुरा कृतम्॥
en: As flowers and fruits, without being compelled, never allow their proper time to pass away without making their appearance, so the acts one has done in past life appear at the proper time.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: सम्मानश्चावमानश्च लाभालाभौ क्षयोदयौ। प्रवृत्ता विनिवर्तन्ते विधानान्ते पदे पदे॥
en: Honour and dishonour, profit and loss, destruction and growth, are seen to set in. No one can resist them. None of them is everlasting for it must disappear in the end.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: आत्मना विहितं दुःखमात्मना विहितं सुखम्। गर्भशय्यामुपादाय भुज्यते पौर्वदेहिकम्॥
en: The sorrows one suffers is the outcome of his deeds. The happiness one enjoys originates from his deeds. From the time when one lies within the mother's womb one begins to enjoy and suffer his pristine deeds.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: बालो युवा वा वृद्धश्च यत् करोति शुभाशुभम्। तस्यां तस्यामवस्थायां भुङ्क्ते जन्मनि जन्मनि॥
en: Whatever acts good and bad one does in childhood, youth, or old age, one enjoys and suffer their consequences in his next life in similar ages.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम्। तथा पूर्वकृतं कर्म कर्तारमनुगच्छति॥
en: As the calf recognises its dam even when the latter may stand among thousands of her kind, similarly the acts done by one in his past life come to him in the next life although he may live among thousands of his species.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: मलिनं हि यथा वस्त्रं पश्चाच्छुद्ध्यति वारिणा। उपवासैः प्रतप्तानां दीर्घं सुखमनन्तकम्॥
en: As a piece of dirty cloth is whitened by being washed in water, similarly the righteous, purified by continuous exposure to the fire of fasts and penances at last acquire eternal happiness.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: दीर्घकालेन तपसा सेवितेन महामते। धर्मनिर्धूतपापानां संसिध्यन्ते मनोरथाः॥
en: O you of great intelligence, the desires and purposes of those whose sins have been purged off by long-continued penances wellperformed, become fruitful.

description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: शकुनानामिवाकाशे मत्स्यानामिव चोदके। पदं यथा न दृश्येत तथा पुण्यकृतां गतिः॥
en: The path of the righteous cannot be discerned even as that of birds in the sky or that of fishes in the water.
