description: The efficacy of gifts, sacrifice and penance's
sn: अलमन्यैरुपालब्धैः कीर्तितैश्च व्यतिक्रमैः। पेशलं चानुरूपं च कर्तव्यं हितमात्मनः॥
en: There is no need of speaking ill of others; nor of reciting the instances of their failure. On the other hand, one should always do what is delightful, sweet, and beneficial to his own self.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं व्यासस्य धर्मात्मा शुको जज्ञे महातपाः। सिद्धिं च परमां प्राप्तस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, how the great Shuka of austere penances took birth as the son of Vyasa, and how did he succeed in acquiring the highest success?

sn: कस्यां चोत्पादयामास शुकं व्यासस्तपोधनः। न ह्यस्य जननी विद्मं जन्म चायं महात्मनः॥
en: Upon what woman did Vyasa, having asceticism for his wealth, beget that son of his? We do not know who was Shuka's mother, nor do we know anything of the birth of that great ascetic.

sn: कथं च बालस्य सत: सूक्ष्मजाने गता मतिः। यथा नान्यस्य लोकेऽस्मिन् द्वितीयस्येह कस्यचित्॥
en: How was it that, when he was a mere boy, his mind became bent to the knowledge of the subtile? Indeed, in this world no second person can be seen in whom such marks could be seen at so early an age.

sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण महामते। न हि मे तृप्तिरस्तीह शृण्वतोऽमृतमुत्तमम्॥
en: I wish to hear all this in full, you of great intelligence. I am never satiated with hearing your excellent and nectar-like words.

sn: माहात्म्यमात्मयोगं च विज्ञानं च शुकस्य ह। यथावदानुपूर्येण तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Tell me, grandfather, in their due order, of the greatness, and the knowledge of Shuka and of his union with the (Supreme) Soul!

sn: भीष्म उवाच न हायनैर्न पलितैर्न वित्तैर्न न बन्धुभिः। ऋषयश्चक्रिरे धर्म योऽनूचानः स नो महान्॥
en: The Rishis did not make merit depend upon years of decrepitude or riches or friends. They said that he amongst them was great who studied the Vedas.

sn: तपोमूलमिदं सर्वं यन्मां पृच्छसि पाण्डवः तदिन्द्रियाणि संयम्य तपो भवति नान्यथा॥
en: All this that you have asked has penances for its root. That penance, again, O son of Pandu, originates from the subjugation of the senses.

sn: इन्द्रियाणां प्रसङ्गेन दोषमृच्छत्यसंशयम्। संनियम्य तु तान्येव सिद्धिमाप्नोति मानवः॥
en: Forsooth, one incurs fault by letting loose his senses. It is only by controlling them that one succeeds in acquiring success.

sn: अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य वाजपेयशतस्य च। योगस्य कलया तात न तुल्यं विद्यते फलम्॥
en: The merit of a thousand Horse-sacrifices or a hundred Vajapeyas is not equal to even a sixteenth part of the merit of Yoga.

sn: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि जन्मयोगफलं तथा। शुकस्याश्यां गतिं चैव दुर्विदामकृतात्मभिः॥
en: I shall, now, recite to you the circumstances of Shuka's birth, the fruits he acquired of his penances, and the foremost end he achieved. These are the topics which persons of uncleansed souls cannot understand.

sn: मेरुशृङ्गे किल पुरा कर्णिकारवनायुते। विजहार महादेवो भीमैर्भूतगणैर्वृतः॥
en: Once on a time on the summit of Meru adorned with Karnikara flowers, Mahadeva sported, in company of his followers, the terrible spirits.

sn: शैलराजसुता चैव देवी तत्राभवत् पुरा। तत्र दिव्यं तपस्तेपे कृष्णद्वैपायनस्तदा॥
en: The daughter of the king of mountains, viz., the goddess Parvati, was also there. There near that summit, the Island-born (Vyasa) practised extraordinary austerities.

sn: योगेनात्मानमाविश्य योगधर्मपरायणः। धारयन् स तपस्तेपे पुत्रार्थं कुरुसत्तम॥
en: O best of the Kuru, given to the practices of Yoga, the great ascetic, withdrawing himself by Yoga into his own soul, and engaged in concentration, practised many austerities for the sake of a son.

sn: अग्नेर्भूमेरपां वायोरन्तरिक्षस्य वा विभो। धैर्येण सम्मितः पुत्रो मम भूयादिति स्म ह॥
en: The prayer he offered to the great God was,-~O powerful one, let me have a son that will have the might of Fire and Earth and Weather and Wind and Ether.

sn: संकल्पेनाथ योगेन दुष्प्रापमकृतात्मभिः। वरयामास देवेशमास्थितस्तप उत्तमम्॥
en: Engaged in the austerest of penances the Island-born Rishi begged of that great God, who cannot be approached by persons of impure souls, by his Yoga.

sn: अतिष्ठन्मारुताहारः शतं किल समाः प्रभुः। आराधयन्महादेवं बहुरूपमुमापतिम्॥
en: The powerful Vyasa remained there for a hundred years, living on air alone, engaged in worshipping many formed Mahadeva, the lord ofUma.

sn: तत्र ब्रह्मर्षयश्चैव सर्वे राजर्षयस्तथा। लोकपालाश्च लोकेशं साध्याश्च बहुभिः सह।॥ आदित्याश्चैव रुद्राश्च दिवाकरनिशाकरौ। वसवो मरुतश्चैव सागरा: सरितस्तथा॥ अश्विनौ देवगन्धर्वास्तथा नारदपर्वतौ। विश्वावसुश्च गन्धर्वः सिद्धाश्चाप्सरसस्तथा॥
en: There were all the twice-born Rishis and royal sages and the Regents of the world and the Sadhyas along with the Vasus, and the Adityas, the Rudras, and the Sun and the Moon, and the Maruts, and the Oceans, and the rivers, and the Ashvins, the Deities, the Gandharvas, and Narada, and Parvata, and the Gandharva Vishvavasu, and the Siddhas, and the Apsaras.

sn: तत्र रुद्रो महादेवः कर्णिकारमयीं शुभाम्। धारयाणः स्रज भाति ज्योत्स्नामिव निशाकरः॥
en: There Mahadeva, called also Rudra, sat, adorned with an excellent garland of Karnikara flowers, and effulgent like the Moon with his rays.

sn: तस्मिन् दिव्ये वने रम्ये देवदेवर्षिसंकुले। आस्थितः परमं योगमृषिः पुत्रार्थपच्युतः॥
en: In those delightful and celestial forests populous with gods and heavenly Rishis, the great Rishi remained, engaged in high Yogacontemplation, for getting a son.

sn: न चास्य हीयते प्राणो न ग्लानिरुपजायते। त्रयाणामपि लोकानां तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: His strength suffered no decrease, nor did he feel any pain. There at the three worlds were much surprised.

sn: जटाश्च तेजसा तस्य वैश्वानरशिखोपमाः। प्रज्वलन्त्यः स्म दृश्यन्ते युक्तस्यामिततेजसः॥
en: While the Rishi, gifted with immeasurable energy, sat in Yoga, his mattered locks, on account of his energy, were seen to blaze like flames of fire.

sn: मार्कण्डेयो हि भगवानेतदाख्यातवान् मम! स देवचरितानीह कथयामास मे सदा॥
en: I heard to this from the illustrious Markandeya. He used always to recite to me the acts of the gods.

sn: एता अद्यापि कृष्णस्य तपसा तेन दीपिताः। अग्निवर्णा जटास्तात प्रकाशन्ते महात्मनः॥
en: It is for this that the matted locks of the great Vyasa, thus enblazed by his energy on that occasion, seem to this day to be gifted with the hue of fire.

sn: एवंविधेन तपसा तस्य भक्त्या च भारत। महेश्वरः प्रसन्नात्मा चकार मनसा मतिम्॥
en: Pleased with such penances and such devotion, O Bharata, of the Rishi, the great God resolved to grant him his wish.

sn: उवाच चैवं भगवांस्त्र्यम्बकः प्रहसन्निव। एवंविधस्ते तनयो द्वैपायन भविष्यति॥
en: Smiling with pleasure, the three-eyed god addressed him and said,-O Island-born one, you will have a son after your heart.

sn: यथा ह्यग्निर्यथा वायुर्यथा भूमिर्यथा जलम्। यथा च खं तथा शुद्धो भविता ते सुतो महान्॥
en: Endued with greatness, he shall be as pure as Fire, as Wind, as Earth, as Water, and as Space.

sn: तद्भावभावी तबुद्धिस्तदात्मा तदपाश्रयः। तेजसाऽऽवृत्य लोकांस्त्रीन् यशःप्राप्स्यति ते सुतः।।२९।
en: He will be conscious of his being Brahma's self ; his understanding and soul shall be devoted to Brahma, and he shall completely depend upon Brahma so as to be at one with.

sn: भीष्म उवाच स लब्ध्वा परमं देवाद् वरं सत्यवतीसुतः। अरणी सहिते गृह्य ममन्थाग्निचिकीर्षया॥
en: Bhishma said Having got this high boon from the great God, the son of Satyavati, was one day engaged in rubbing his sticks for making a fire.

sn: अथ रूपं परं राजन् बिभ्रती स्वेन तेजसा। घृताची नामाप्सरसमपश्यद् भगवानृषिः॥
en: While thus engaged, the illustrious Rishi, O king, saw the . Apsara Ghritachi, who, on account of her energy, was then possessed of great beauty.

sn: ऋषिरप्सरसं दृष्ट्वा सहसा काममोहितः। अभवद् भगवान् व्यासो वने तस्मिन् युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Seeing the Apasara in those woods, the illustrious Rishi Vyasa, O Yudhisthira, became suddenly possessed by desire.

sn: सा च दृष्ट्वा तदा व्यासं कामसंविग्नमानसम्। शुकी भूत्वा महाराज घृताची समुपागमत्॥
en: The Apsara, seeing the Rishi's heart smitten with desire, changed herself into a she-parrot and came to that spot.

sn: तामप्सरसं दृष्ट्वा रूपेणान्येन संवृताम्। शरीरजेनानुगदः सर्वगात्रातिगेन ह॥
en: Although he saw the Apsara disguised in another form, the desire that had arisen in the Rishi's heart spread itself over every part of his body.

sn: स तु धैर्येण महता निगृह्णन् हृच्छयं मुनिः। न शशाक नियन्तुं तद् व्यास: प्रविसृतं मनः॥ भावित्वाच्चैव भावस्य घृताच्या वपुषा हृतः।
en: Inviting all his patience, the ascetic tried to suppress that desire. With all his efforts, however, Vyasa could not control his agitated mind. On account of the inevitability of what was to take place the Rishi's heart was drawn by Ghritachi's beauty.

sn: यत्नान्नियच्छतस्तस्य मुनेरग्निचिकीर्षया॥ अरण्यामेव सहसा तस्य शुक्रमवापतत्।
en: He tried his best for making a fire for suppressing his emotion, but despite all his efforts his vital seed came out in the wood.

sn: सोऽविशंकेन मनसा तथैव द्विजसत्तमः॥ अरणी ममन्थ ब्रह्मर्षिस्तस्यां जज्ञे शुको नृप।
en: That best of twice-born ones, however O king, continued to rub his stick without feeling any scruples for what had taken place. From the seed that feil, was born a son to him called Shuka.

sn: शुक्रे निर्मथ्यमाने स शुको जज्ञे महातपाः॥ परमर्षिर्महायोगी अरणीगर्भसम्भवः
en: On account of this incident about his birth, he came to be called by the name of Shuka. : Indeed, it was thus that great ascetic, that foremost of Rishis and highest of Yogins, was born from the two sticks.

sn: यथाध्वरे समिद्धोऽग्नि ति हव्यमुदावहम्॥ तथारूप: शुको जज्ञे प्रज्वलन्निव तेजसा।
en: As in a sacrifice a blazing fire spreads its effulgence all around when libations of clarified butter are poured upon it, similarly did Shuka take his birth, blazing with effulgence on account of his own energy.

sn: बिभ्रत् पितुश्च कौरव्य रूपवर्णमनुत्तमम्॥ बभौ तदा भावितात्मा विधूम इव पावकः।
en: Assuming the excellent form and hue of his father, Shuka, O son of Kuru, of purified Soul, shone like a smokeless fire.

sn: तं गङ्गा सरितां श्रेष्ठा मेरुपृष्ठे जनेश्वर॥ स्वरूपिणी तदाभ्येत्य तर्पयामास वारिणा।
en: O king, coming to the breast of Meru, in her own embodied form, the foremost of rivers, viz., Ganga, bathed Shuka with her waters.

sn: अन्तरिक्षाच्च कौरव्य दण्डः कृष्णाजिनं च ह॥ पपात भूमिं राजेन्द्र शुकस्यार्थे महात्मनः।
en: There fell from the sky, O son of Kuru, an ascetic's stick and a dark deer skin for the use, O king, of the great Shuka.

sn: जेगीयन्ते स्म गन्धर्वा ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः॥ देवदुन्दुभयश्चैव प्रावाद्यन्त महास्वनाः।
en: The Gandharvas sang repeatedly and the various clans of Apsaras danced; and celestial kettle drums of loud sound began to bcat.

sn: विश्वावसुश्च गन्धर्वस्तथा तुम्बुरुनारदौ॥ हाहा हूहूच गन्धर्वी तुष्टवुः शुकसम्भवम्।
en: The Gandharvas Vishvavasu, and Tumvuru, and Narada, and those other Gandharvas called by the name of Haha, and Huhu, eulogised the birth of Shuka.

sn: तत्र शक्रपुरोगाश्च लोकपालाः समागताः॥ देवा देवर्षयश्चैव तथा ब्रह्मर्षयोऽपि च।
en: There the regents of the world headed by Indra, as also the gods and the celestial and the regenerate Rishis.

sn: दिव्यानि सर्वपुष्पाणि प्रववर्ष च मारुतः॥ जङ्गमाजङ्गमं चैव प्रहृष्टमभवज्जगत्।
en: The Wind-god poured there showers of celestial flowers. The entire universe, mobile and immobile, became filled with joy.

sn: तं महात्मा स्वयं प्रीत्या देव्या सह महाद्युतिः॥ जातमात्रं मुनेः पुत्र विधिनोपानयत् तदा।
en: The great and the highly effulgent Mahadeva, accompanied by the Goddess, and moved by affection, came there and soon after the birth of the Muni's son invested him with the sacred thread.

sn: तस्य देवेश्वरः शक्रो दिव्यमद्भुतदर्शनम्॥ ददौ कमण्डलु प्रीत्या देववासांसि वा विभो।
en: Shakra, the king of the gods, gave him, from affection, a celestial pitcher of excellent form, and some celestial dresses.

sn: हंसाच शतपत्राश्च सारसाश्च सहस्रशः॥ प्रदक्षिणमवर्तन्त शुकाश्चाषाश्च भारत।
en: Thousands of Swans and Shatapatras and cranes, and many parrots and Chasas, O Bharata, wheeled over his head.

sn: आरणेयस्ततो दिव्यं प्राप्य जन्म महाद्युतिः॥ तत्रैवोवास मेधावी व्रतचारी समाहितः।
en: Highly effulgent and intelligent Shuka, having obtained his birth from the two sticks, continued to live there, practising many vows and fasts.

sn: उत्पन्नमात्रं तं वेदाः सरहस्या: ससंग्रहाः॥ उपतस्थुर्महाराज यथास्य पितरं तथा।
en: As soon as Shuka was born, the Vedas, with all their mysteries and all their abstracts, came for living in him, O king, even as they live in his father.

sn: बृहस्पतिं च वत्रे स वेदवेदाङ्गभाष्यवित्॥ उपाध्यायं महाराज धर्ममेवानुचिन्तयन्।
en: For all that, Shuka, selected Brihaspati, who was a master of all the Vedas together with their branches and commentaries, for his preceptor, remembering universal practice.

sn: सोऽधीत्य निखिलान् वेदान् सरहस्यान् ससंग्रहान्।।२४ इतिहासं च कात्स्र्येन राजशास्त्राणि वा विभो। गुरवे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा समावृत्तो महामुनिः।।२५। उग्रं तयः समारेभे ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः।
en: Having read all the Vedas together with all their mysteries and abstracts, as also all the histories and the science of polity, O powerful king, the great ascetic returned home, after giving his preceptor the tuition-fee. Adopting the vow of celibacy, he then bagan to practise the austerest penances, concentrating all his attention thereon.

sn: देवतानामृषीणां च बाल्येऽपि स महातपाः। सम्मन्त्रणीयो मान्यश्च ज्ञानेन तपसा तथा॥
en: Even in his childhood, he became an object of reverence with the gods and Rishis for his knowledge and penances.

sn: न त्वस्य रमते बुद्धिराश्रमेषु नराधिप। त्रिषु गार्हस्थ्यमूलेषु मोक्षधर्मानुदर्शिनः॥
en: The mind of the great ascetic, O king, found pleasure in the three modes of life, keeping in view, as he did, the Religion of Liberation.

sn: भीष्म उवाच स मोक्षमनुचिन्त्यैव शुकः पितरमभ्यगात्। प्राहाभिवाद्य च गुरुं श्रेयोऽर्थी विनयान्वितः॥ मोक्षधर्मेषु कुशलो भगवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे। यथा मे मनसः शान्तिः परमा सम्भवेत् प्रभो॥
en: Bhishma said “Thinking of Liberation, Shuka approached his father, and possessed as he was of humility and desirous of acquiring his highest good, he saluted his great preceptor and said,-You are well-versed in the Religion of Liberation. Do you, O illustrious one, describe it to me, so that I may enjoy supreme tranquillity of mind, O powerful one.

sn: श्रुत्वा पुत्रस्य तु वचः परमर्षिरुवाच तम्। अधीष्व पुत्र मोक्षं वै धर्मांच विविधानपि॥
en: Hearing these words of his son, the great Rishi said to him,-Do you study, O son, the Religion' of Liberation and all the various duties of life.

sn: पितुर्नियोगाज्जग्राह शुको धर्मभृतां वरः। योगशास्त्रं च निखिलं कापिलं चैव भारत॥
en: At the command of his father, Shuka, that foremost of all righteous men, mastered all the books on Yoga, O Bharata, as also the Science of Kapila.

sn: स तं ब्राह्मया श्रिया युक्तं ब्रह्मतुल्यपराक्रमम्। मेने पुत्रं यदा व्यासो मोक्षधर्मविशारदम्॥ उवाच गच्छेति तदा जनकं मिथिलेश्वरम्। स ते वक्ष्यति मोक्षार्थं निखिलं मिथिलेश्वरम्॥
en: When Vyasa saw his son to be endued with the resplendence of the Vedas, and the energy of Brahman, and fully conversant with the Religion of Liberation, he addressed him, saying,-Go you to Janaka the king of Mithila. The king of Mithila will tell you everything for your Liberation.

sn: पितुर्नियोगमादाय जगाम मिथिलां नृप। प्रष्टुं धर्मस्य निष्ठां वै मोक्षस्य च परायणम्॥
en: Bearing the command of his father, O king, Shuka, proceeded to Mithila for enquiring of its king about the truth of duties and the Refuge of Liberation.

sn: उक्तश्च मानुषेण त्वं पथा गच्छेत्यविस्मितः। न प्रभावेण गन्तव्यमन्तरिक्षचरेण वै॥
en: Before he started, his father further told him,-Do you go there be that path which ordinary human beings follow. Do not have recourses to your Yoga-power for proceeding through the skies. At this Shuka was not at all surprised.

sn: आर्जवेणैव गन्तव्यं न सुखान्वेषिणा तथा। नान्वेष्टव्या विशेषास्तु विशेषा हि प्रसङ्गिनः॥
en: He was further told that he should proceed there with simplicity and not from desire of pleasure.-Along your way do not seek for friends and wives, since friends and wives are causes of attachment to the world.

sn: अहंकारो न कर्तव्यो याज्ये तस्मिन् नराधिपे। स्थातव्यं च वशे तस्य स ते छेत्स्यति संशयम्॥
en: Although the king of Mithila is one in whose sacrifices we officiate, still you should not indulge in any feeling of superiority while living with him. You should live under his direction and in obedience to him. He will remove your doubts.

sn: स धर्मकुशलो राजा मोक्षशास्त्रविशारदः। याज्यो मम स यद् ब्रूयात् तत् कार्यमविशङ्कया॥
en: That king is well versed in all duties and well acquainted with the Scriptures on Liberation. He is one for whom I officiate in sacrifices. You should, unhesitatingly, do what he orders.

sn: एवमुक्तः स धर्मात्मा जगाम मिथिलां मुनिः। पद्भ्यां शक्तोऽन्तरिक्षण क्रान्तुं पृथ्वी ससागराम्॥
en: Thus instructed, the pious Shuka proceeded to Mithila on foot although he was able to go through the skies over the whole Earth with her seas.

sn: स गिरीश्चाप्यतिक्रम्य नदीतीर्थसरांसि च। बहुव्यालमृगाकीर्णा ह्यटवीश्च वनानि च॥ मेरोहरेश्च द्वे वर्षे वर्ष हैमवतं ततः। क्रमेणैवं व्यतिक्रम्य भारतं वर्षमासदत्॥
en: Crossing many hills and mountains, many rivers, many waters and lakes, and many woods and forests full of beasts of prey and other animals, crossing the two insular continents of Meru and Hari successively and next the continent of Himavat, he came at last to the continent known by the name of Bharata.

sn: स देशान् विविधान् पश्यंश्चीनहूणनिषेवितान्। आर्यावर्तमिमं देशमाजगाम महामुनिः॥
en: Having seen many countries inhabited by Chins and Huns, the great ascetic at last reached Aryavarta.

sn: पितुर्वचनमाज्ञाय तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन्। अध्वानं सोऽतिचक्राम खेचरः खे चरन्निवा१६॥
en: In obedience to the commands of his father and bearing them constantly in his mind, he gradually passed along his way on the Earth like a bird passing through the air.

sn: पत्तनानि च रम्याणि स्फीतानि नगराणि च। रत्नानि च विचित्राणि पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति॥
en: Passing through many charming towns and populous cities, he saw various kinds of wealth without waiting to observe them.

sn: उद्यानानि च रम्याणि तथैवायतनानि च। पुण्यानि चैव रत्नानि सोऽत्यकामदथाध्वगः॥
en: On his way he passed through many charming gardens and planes and many sacred waters.

sn: सोऽचिरेणैव कालेन विदेहानाससाद ह। रक्षितान् धर्मराजेन जनकेन महात्मना॥
en: Before much time had passed he reached the country of the Videhas that was protected by the virtuous and great Janaka.

sn: तत्र ग्रामान् बहून पश्यन् बबनरसभोजनान्। पल्लीघोषान् समृद्धांश्च बहुगोकुलसंकुलान्॥
en: There he saw many populous villages, and many kinds of food and drink and viands and houses of cowherds swelling with men and inany herbs of cattle.

sn: स्फीतांश्च शालियवसैहँससारससेवितान्। पद्मिनीभिश्च शतशः श्रीमतीभिरलङ्कृतान्॥
en: He saw many fields abounding with paddy and barley and other grain, and many lakes and waters inhabited by swans and cranes and adorned with beautiful lotuses.

sn: स विदेहानतिक्रम्य समृद्धजनसेवितान्। मिथिलोपवनं रम्यमाससाद समृद्धिमत्॥
en: Passing through the Videha country full of rich people, he arrived at the delightful gardens of Mithila rich with many sorts to trees.

sn: हस्त्यश्वरथसंकीर्णं नरनारीसमाकुलम्। पश्यन्नपश्यन्निव तत् समतिकामदच्युतः॥
en: Abounding with elephants and horses and cars, and peopled by men and women, he passed through them without caring to see the things that were presented to his eye.

sn: मनसा तं वहन् भारं तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन्। आत्मारामः प्रसन्नात्मा मिथिलामाससाद ह॥
en: Bearing that caution in his mind and continually thinking of it, Shuka of cheerful soul and taking delight in internal survey only, reached Mithila at last.

sn: तस्या द्वारं समासाद्य निःशङ्कः प्रविवेश हा तापि द्वारपालास्तमुग्रवाचा न्यषेधयन्॥
en: Arrived at the gate, he sent word through the guards, he reached the king's palace and entered it without any-hesitation. The gatekeepers prevented him with harsh words.

sn: तथैव च शुकस्तत्र निर्मन्युः समतिष्ठत। चातपाध्वसंतप्तः क्षुत्पिपासाश्रमान्वितः॥ प्रताम्यति ग्लायति वा नापैति च तथाऽऽतपात्।
en: Thereat, Shuka, without any anger, stopped and waited. Neither the sun nor the long distance he had walked had tried him in the least. Neither hunger, nor thirst, nor the exertion he had made, had weakened him. The heat of the Sun had not scorched or pained or distressed him in any way.

sn: तेषां तु द्वारपालानामेकः शोकसमन्वितः॥ मध्यं गतमिवादित्यं दृष्ट्वा शुकमवस्थितम्।
en: Among those porters there was one who felt mercy for him, seeing him staying there like the midday Sun in his effulgence.

sn: पूजयित्वा यथान्यायमभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः॥ प्रावेशयत् ततः कक्ष्यां द्वितीयां राजवेश्मनः।
en: Adoring him in due form and saluting him properly, with joined hands he conducted him to the first chamber of the palace.

sn: तत्रासीनः शुकस्तात मोक्षमेवान्वचिन्तयत्॥ छायायामातपे चैव समदर्शी महाद्युतिः।
en: Seated there, Shuka, O son, began to think of Liberation only. Gifted with equality he considered impartially a shaded spot and one exposed to the Sun's rays.

sn: तं मुहूर्तादिवागम्य राज्ञो मन्त्री कृताञ्जलिः॥ प्रावेशयत्ततः कक्ष्यां तृतीयां राजवेश्मनः।
en: Soon after, the king's minister, coming to that place with joined hands, conducted him to the second chamber of the palace.

sn: तत्रान्तःपुरसम्बद्धं महच्चैत्ररथोपमम्॥ सुविभक्तजलाक्रीडं रम्यं पुष्पितपादपम्।
en: That chamber led to a spacious garden which formed a part of the inner apartments of the palace. It looked like a second Chaitraratha. Beautiful pools of water were here and there at regular intervals. Delightful trees, all of which were in their flowering season, were in that garden.

sn: शुकं प्रावेशयन्मन्त्री प्रमदावनमुत्तमम्॥ स तस्यासनमादिश्य निश्चक्राम ततः पुनः।
en: Bevies of damsels, of celestial beauty, were in attendance. The minister led Suka from the second chamber to that charming spot. commanding those ladies to give the ascetic a seat, the minister left him there.

sn: तं चारुवेषाः सुश्रोण्यस्तरुण्यः प्रियदर्शनाः॥ सूक्ष्मरक्ताम्बरधरास्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः।
en: Those well-dressed well-dressed damels were of beautiful features, possessed to excellent hips, young in years, clad in red dresses of fine texture, and decked with many ornaments of burnished gold.

sn: संलापोल्लापकुशला नृत्यगीतविशारदाः॥ स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिण्यो रूपेणाप्सरसां समाः।
en: They well-skilled in sweet conversation and maddening revelry, and consummate mistresses of the arts of dancing and singing. Always opening their lips with smiles, they were like the very Apsaras in beauty.

sn: कामोपचारकुशला भावज्ञाः सर्वकोविदाः॥ परं पञ्चाशतं नार्यो वारमुख्याः समाद्रवन्।
en: Well-skilled in all the acts of dalliance, capable of reading the thoughts of men upon whom they wait, endued with every accomplishment, fifty damsels, of a very high order and of east virtue, surrounded the ascetic.

sn: पाद्यादीनि प्रतिग्राह्य पूजया परयार्चयन्॥ कालोपपन्नेन तदा स्वाद्वन्नेनाभ्यतर्पयन्।
en: Presenting him with water for washing his feet, and adoring him respectfully with the were offer of usual articles, they pleased him with excellent viands agreeable to the season.

sn: तस्य भुक्तवतस्तात तदन्तःपुरकाननम्॥ सुरम्यं दर्शयामासुरेकैकश्येन भारत।
en: After he had eaten, those damsels then, one after another, singly conducted him through the grounds, showing him every objection of interest, O Bharata.

sn: क्रीडन्त्यश्च हसन्त्यश्च गायन्त्यश्चापिताः शुभम्॥ उदारसत्त्वं सत्त्वज्ञाः स्त्रियः पर्यचरंस्तथा।
en: Sporting and laughing and singing, those ladies conversant with the thoughts of all men, entertained that ascetic of noble soul.

sn: आरणेयस्तु शुद्धात्मा निःसंदेहः स्वकर्मकृत्॥ वश्येन्द्रियो जितक्रोधो न हृष्यति न कुप्यति।
en: The pure-souled ascetic born in the firesticks, performing all his duties unhesitatingly, having all his senses under complete control, and a thorough master of his anger, was neither pleased nor angered at all this.

sn: तस्मै शय्यासनं दिव्यं देवाह रत्नभूषितम्॥ स्पास्तरणसंकीर्णं ददुस्ता: परमस्त्रियः। पादशौचं तु कृत्वैव शुकः संध्यामुपास्य च॥ निषसादासने पुण्ये तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन्।
en: Then those foremost of beautiful women offered him an excellent seat. Washing his feet and other limbs, Shuka said his evening prayers, sat on that excellent seat, and began to think of the object for which he had come there.

sn: पूर्वरात्रे तु तत्रासौ भूत्वा ध्यानपरायणः॥ मध्यरात्रे यथान्यायं निद्रामाहारयत् प्रभुः।
en: In the first part of the night, he gave himself of Yoga. The powerful ascetic, passed the middle part of the night in sleep.

sn: ततो मुहूर्तादुत्थाय कृत्वा शौचमनन्तरम्॥ स्त्रीभिः परिवृतो धीमान् ध्यानमेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: Very soon waking up from his sleep, he performed the necessary rites of cleansing his body, and though surrounded by those beautiful ladies, he once again devoted himself to Yoga.

sn: अनेन विधिना काणि स्तदहःशेषमच्युतः। तां च रात्रिं नृपकुले वर्तयामास भारत॥
en: It was in this way, O Bharata, that the son of the Island-born Krishna passed the latter part of that day and the whole of that night in the mansion of king Janaka.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः स राजा जनको मन्त्रिभिः सह भारत। पुरः पुरोहितं कृत्वा सर्वाण्यन्तःपुराणि च॥
en: Bhishma said The next morning, king Janaka, O Bharata, accompanied by his minister and the whole household, came to Shuka, preceded by his priest.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: आसनं च पुरस्कृत्य रत्नानि विविधानि च। शिरसा चार्घ्यमादाय गुरुपुत्रं समभ्यगात्॥
en: Bringing with him rich seats and various sorts of jewels and gems, and bearing the ingredients of the Arghya on his own head, the king approached the son of his reverend preceptor.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: स तदाऽऽसनमादाय बहुरत्नविभूषितम्। स्पर्धास्तरणसंस्तीर्णं सर्वतोभद्रमृद्धिमत्॥ पुरोधसा संगृहीतं हस्तेनालभ्य पार्थिवः। प्रददौ गुरुपुत्राय शुकाय परमार्चितम्॥
en: The king, taking with his own hands, from the hands of his priest, that seat adorned with many gems, covered with an excellent sheet, beautiful in all its parts and dearly costly, presented it with great respect to his preceptor's son Shuka.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: तत्रोपविष्टं तं कार्ष्णि शास्त्रतः प्रत्यपूजयत्। पाद्यं निवेद्य प्रथममर्थ्य गां च न्यवेदयत्॥
en: After the son of Krishna had taken his seat on it, the king adored him according to prescribed rites. At first offering him water to wash his feet, he then presented him the Arghya and kine.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: स च तां मन्त्रवत्पूजां प्रत्यगृह्णाद् यथाविधि। प्रतिगुह्य तु तां पूजां जनकाद् द्विजसत्तमः॥ गां चैव समनुज्ञाय राजानमनुमान्य च। पर्यपृच्छन्महातेजा राज्ञः कुशलमव्ययम्॥
en: The ascetic accepted that worship offered with due rites and Mantras. That foremost of twice-born ones, having thus accepted the worship offered by the king, and taking the kine also that were presented to him, then saluted the king, gifted with great energy, he next enquired after the king's welfare and prosperity.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: अनामयं च राजेन्द्र शुकः सानुचरस्य ह। अनशिष्टस्तु तेनासौ निषसाद सहानुगः॥
en: Indeed, O king, Shuka asked about the welfare of the king's followers and officers also. Receiving Shuka's permission, Janaka sat down with all his followers.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: उदारसत्त्वाभिजनो भूमौ राजा कृताञ्जलिः। कुशलं चाव्ययं चैव पृष्ट्वा वैयासकिं नृपः। किमागमनमित्येवं पर्यपृच्छत पार्थिवः॥
en: Having a high soul and possessed of high birth, the king with joined hands, sat down on the bare ground and enquired after the wellbeing and unabated prosperity of Vyasa's son. The king then asked his guest the object of his visit.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: शुक उवाच पित्राहमुक्तो भद्रं ते मोक्षधर्मार्थकोविदः। विदेहराजो याज्यो मे जनको नाम विश्रुतः॥
en: Shuka said Blessed be you, my father told me that his client, the king of the Videhas, known all over the world by the name of Janaka, is well-versed in the Religion of Liberation.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: तत्र गच्छस्व वै तूर्णं यदि ते हृदि संशयः। प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा स ते च्छेत्स्यति संशयम्॥
en: He ordered me to come to him forthwith, if I had any doubts to be solved in the Religion of either Action or Renunciation. He gave me to understand that the king of Mithila would remove all my doubts.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: सोऽहं पितुर्नियोगात् त्वामुपप्रष्टुमिहागतः। तन्मे धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ यथावद् वक्तुर्महसि॥
en: I have, therefore, come come here at the command of my father, for the purpose of receiving instruction from you. You should, O foremost of all righteous persons, instruct me!

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: किं कार्यं ब्राह्मणेनेह मोक्षार्थश्च किमात्मकः। कथं च मोक्षः प्राप्तव्यो ज्ञानेन तपसाथवा॥
en: What are the duties of a Brahmana, and what is the essence of those duties that have Liberation for their object. How, also, is Liberation to be acquired. Is it to be acquired by the help of Knowledge or by that Penances?

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: जनक उवाच यत् कार्यं ब्राह्मणेनेह जन्मप्रभृति तच्छृणु। कृतोपनयनस्तात भवेद् वेदपरायणः॥
en: Janaka said Hear what the Duties are of a Brahmana from the time of his birth. After his investiture, O son, with the sacred thread, he should give his attention to the study of the Vedas.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: तपसा गुरुवृत्त्या च ब्रह्मचर्येण वा विभो। देवतानां पितॄणां चाप्यनृणो ह्यनसूयकः॥
en: By practising penances and dutifully serving his preceptor, and observing the duties of Brahmacharya, O powerful one, he should satisfy the debt be owes to the gods, and the Pitris, and renounce all malice.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: वेदानधीत्य नियतो दक्षिणामपवर्त्य च। अभ्यनुज्ञामथ प्राप्य समावर्तेत वै द्विजः॥
en: Having read the Vedas with close attention, and controlled his senses, and having given his preceptor the tuition-fee, he should, with the order of his preceptor, return home.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: समावृत्तश्च गार्हस्थ्ये स्वदारनिरतो वसेत्। अनसूयुर्यथान्यायमाहिताग्निस्तथैव च॥
en: Coming back home, he should follow the domestic mode of life and marry a wife, confine himself to her, and live freeing himself from every sort of malice, and having established his domestic fire.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: उत्पाद्य पुत्रपौत्रं तु वन्याश्रमपदे वसेत्। तानेवाग्नीन् यथाशास्त्रमर्चयन्नतिथिप्रियः॥
en: Living as a householder, he should procreate sons and grandsons. After that, he should retire to the forest, and continue to adore the same fires and entertain guests with cordial hospitality.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: स वनेऽग्नीन् यथान्यायमात्मन्यारोप्य धर्मवित्। निर्द्वन्द्वो वीतरागात्मा ब्रह्माश्रमपदे वसेत्॥
en: Living virtuously in the forest, he should, at last, establish his fire in his soul, and freed from all pairs of opposites, and renouncing all attachments, he should pass his days in the anchorite-mode of life, which is otherwise called the mode of Brahma.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: शुक उवाच उत्पन्ने ज्ञानविज्ञाने निर्द्वन्द्वे हृदि शाश्वते। किमवश्यं निवस्तव्यमाश्रमेषु भवेत् त्रिषु॥
en: Shuka said If one acquires an understanding cleansed by study of the scriptures and true conceptions of all things, and if the heart succeeds in freeing itself permanently from the effects of all pairs of opposites, is it still necessary for such a person to follow one after another, the three modes of life called Brahmacharya, Garahastya, and Vanaprastha.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: एतद् भवन्तं पृच्छामि तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति। यथा वेदार्थतत्त्वेन ब्रूहि मे त्वं जनाधिप॥
en: This is what I ask you. You should me. Indeed, O king, do tell me this according to the true meaning of the Vedas.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: जनक उवाच न विना ज्ञानविज्ञाने मोक्षस्याधिगमो भवेत्। न विना गुरुसम्बन्धं ज्ञानस्याधिगमः स्मृतः॥
en: Janaka said It is impossible to aquire Liberation without the help of an understanding purified by the study of the scriptures and without that true conception of all things which is known by the name of Vijnana, again, without that cleansed understanding, one cannot get a Preceptor.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: प्लावयिता तस्य ज्ञानं प्लव इहोच्यते। विज्ञाय कृतकृत्यस्तु तीर्णस्तदुभयं त्यजेत्॥
en: The Preceptor is the helmsman, and Knowledge is the Boat. After having got that Boat, one becomes successful. Indeed, having crossed the Ocean, one may renounce both.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: अनुच्छेदाय लोकानामनुच्छेदाय कर्मणाम्। पूर्वैराचरितो धर्मश्चातुराश्रम्यसंकटः॥
en: For preventing the destruction of all the worlds, and for preventing the destruction of deeds, the duties belonging to the four modes of life were practised by the wise of old.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: अनेन क्रमयोगेन बहुजातिषु कर्मणाम्। हित्वा शुभाशुभं कर्म मोक्षो नामेह लभ्यते॥
en: By renouncing acts, good and bad, according to this order of acts, one succeeds, in course of many births, in acquiring Liberation.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: भावितैः करणैश्चायं बहुसंसारयोनिषु। आसादयति शुद्धात्मा मोक्षं वै प्रथमाश्रमे॥
en: That man who, through penances, practised in many births, succeeds in acquiring purified mind and understanding, and soul, certainly becomes able to acquire Liberation in even the very first mode.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: तमासाद्य तु मुक्तस्य दृष्टार्थस्य विपश्चितः। त्रिष्वाश्रमेषु को न्वर्थो भवेत् परमभीप्सतः॥
en: When, having acquired cleansed understanding, Liberation becomes his, and on account thereof be becomes possessed of knowledge of all visible things, what desirable object is there to attain by following the three other modes of life? a

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: राजसांस्तामसांश्चैव नित्यं दोषान् विवर्जयेत्। सात्त्विकं मार्गमास्थाय पश्येदात्मानमात्मना॥
en: One should always renounce faults produced by the qualities of Rajas and Tamas. Following the path of Sattva, one should see Self by Self.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि। सम्पश्यन्नोपलिप्येत जले वारिचरो यथा॥
en: Seeing one's Self in all creatures and all creatures in one's self, one should live like acquatic animals living in water without being drenched by it.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: पक्षिवत् प्रवणादूर्ध्वममुत्रानन्त्यमश्नुते। विहाय देहान्निर्मुक्तो निर्द्वन्द्वः प्रशमं गतः॥
en: He who succeeds in getting over all pairs of opposites and resisting their influence, succeeds in renouncing all attachments, and acquires infinite happiness in the next world, going there like a bird soaring into the sky from below.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: अत्र गाथाः पुरा गीताः शृणु राज्ञा ययातिना। धार्यन्ते या द्विजैस्तात मोक्षशास्त्रविशारदैः॥
en: Regarding it, there is a saying sung of old by king Yayati, and remembered, O sire, by all persons conversant with the Scriptures dealing with Liberation.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: ज्योतिरात्मनि नान्यत्र सर्वजन्तुषु तत् समम्। स्वयं च शक्यते द्रष्टुं सुसमाहितचेतसा॥
en: The effulgent ray exists in one's Soul and not any where else. It exists equally in all creatures. One can see it himself if his heart be given to Yoga.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: न बिभेति परो यस्मान्न बिभेति पराच्च यः। यश्च नेच्छति न द्वेष्टि ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा।॥
en: When a person lives in such a way that another is not filled with fear on seeing him, and when a person is not himself filled with fear on seeing others, when a person ceases to cherish desire and malice, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: यदा भावं न कुरुते सर्वभूतेषु पापकम्। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When a person ceases to cherish a sinful attitude towards all creatures in thought, word, and deed, he is then said to attain to Brahima.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: संयोज्य मनसाऽऽत्मानमीणूंमुत्सृज्य मोहनीम्। त्यक्त्वा कामं च मोहं च तदा ब्रह्मत्वमश्नुते॥
en: By controlling the mind and the soul, by renouncing malice that stupefies the mind, and by throwing off desire and stupefaction, one is said to attain to Brahma.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: यदा श्राव्ये च दृश्ये च सर्वभूतेषु चाप्ययम्। समो भवति निर्द्वन्द्वो ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When a person assumes an equality of attitude about all objects of hearing and vision, as also about all living creatures, and gets over all pairs of opposites, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: यदा स्तुतिं च निन्दां च समत्वेनैव पश्यति। काञ्चनं चायसं चैव सुखं दुःखं तथैव च।॥ शीतमुष्णं तथैवार्थमनर्थं प्रियमप्रियम्। जीवितं मरणं चैव ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When a person regards impartially praise and dispraise, gold and iron, happiness and misery, heat and cold, good and evil, the agreeable and the disagreeable, life and death, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: प्रसार्येह यथाङ्गानि कूर्मः संहरते पुनः। तथेन्द्रियाणि मनसा संयन्तव्यानि भिक्षुणा॥
en: One following the duties of the mendicant order should restrain his senses and the mind like a tortoise withdrawing its outstretched limbs.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: तमःपरिगतं वेश्म यथा दीपेन दृश्यते। तथा बुद्धिप्रदीपेन शक्य आत्मा निरीक्षितुम्॥
en: As a house covered with darkness, is capable of being seen with the help of a lighted lamp, similarly can the soul be seen with the help of the lamp of the understanding.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: एतत् सर्वं च पश्यामि त्वयि बुद्धिमतां वर। यच्चान्यदपि वेत्तव्यं तत्त्वतो वेद तद् भवान्॥
en: O foremost of intelligent persons, I see that all this knowledge that I am imparting to you, lives in you. Whatever else should be known by one desirous of learning the Religion of Liberation, is already known to you.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: ब्रह्मर्षे विदितश्चासि विषयान्तमुपागतः। गुरोस्तव प्रसादेन तव चैवोपशिक्षया॥
en: O regenerate Rishi, I am convinced that through the mercy of your preceptor and through the instructions you have received, you have already transcended all objects of the senses.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: तस्यैव च प्रसादेन प्रादुर्भूतं महामुने। ज्ञानं दिव्यं ममापीदं तेनासि विदितो मम॥
en: O great ascetic, through the grace of your father, I have acquired omniscience, and hence I have succeeded in knowing you.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: अधिकं तव विज्ञानमधिका च गतिस्तव। अधिकं तव चैश्वर्यं तच्च त्वं नावबुध्यसे॥
en: Your knowledge is much greater than what you think it to be. Your perceptions also that result from intuition, are much greater than what you think them to be. Your power also is much greater than you are conscious of.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: बाल्याद् वा संशयाद् वापि भयाद् वाप्यविमोक्षजात्। उत्पन्ने चापि विज्ञाने नाधिगच्छति तां गतिम्॥
en: Whether in consequence of your tender age, or of the doubts you have not been able to remove, or of the fear that is due to be unattainment of Liberation, you are conscious of that Knowledge due to Intuition, although it has originated in your mind.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: व्यवसायेन शुद्धेन मद्विधैश्छिन्नसंशयः। विमुच्य हृदयग्रन्थीनासादयति तां गतिम्॥
en: After one's doubts have been removed by persons like us, one succeeds in opening the knots of one's heart, and, then, by a righteous endeavour, acquires, and becomes conscious of, that Knowledge. not one

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: भवांश्चोत्पन्नविज्ञानः स्थिरबुद्धिरलोलुपः। व्यवसायादृते ब्रह्मनासादयति तत्परम्॥
en: As regards yourself, you are one that has already acquired knowledge. Your intelligence is steady and tranquil. You are free from covetousness. For all that, O Brahmana, one never succeed, without endeavour in attaining to Brahma, which is the highest object of acquisition.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: नास्ति ते सुखदुःखेषु विशेषो नासि लोलुपः। नौत्सुक्यं नृत्यगीतेषु न राग उपजायते॥
en: You see no difference between happiness and misery. You are not covetous. You have no desire for dancing and song. You have no attachments.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: न बन्धुष्वनुबन्धस्ते न भयेष्वस्ति ते भयम्। पश्यामि त्वां महाभाग तुल्यलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनम्॥
en: You have no attachment to friends. You have no fear in things which fill with fear. O blessed one, I see that you consider equally a lump of gold and a clod of Earth.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: अहं त्वामनुपश्यामि ये चाप्यन्ये मनीषिणः। आस्थितं परमं मार्गमक्षयं तमनामयम्॥
en: Myself and other persons endued with wisdom, see you established in the highest and indestructible path of peace.

description: The conversation between Shuka and Sanaka
sn: यत् फलं ब्राह्मणस्येह मोक्षार्थश्च यदात्मकः। तस्मिन् वै वर्तसे ब्रह्मन् किमन्यत् परिपृच्छसि॥
en: O Brahmana, you discharge the duties of Brahmana and enjoy the fruit which should be his, and which is at one with the essence of the object represented by Liberation. What else have you to enquire of me?

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं कृतात्मा कृतनिश्चयः। आत्मनाऽऽत्मानमास्थाय दृष्ट्वा चात्मानमात्मना।॥
en: Bhishma said Having heard these words of king Janaka, Shuka of purified soul and settled conclusions began to stay in his Soul by his Soul, having of course seen Self by Self.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: कृतकार्यः सुखी शान्तस्तूष्णीं प्रायादुदङ्मुख। शैशिरं गिरिमुद्दिश्य सधर्मा मातरिश्वनः॥ एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु देवर्षि रदस्तथा।
en: His object being fulfilled he became happy and tranquil, and without further questioning Janaka, he proceeded northwards to the mountains of Himavat with the speed of the wind and like the wind.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: हिमवन्तमियाद् द्रष्टुं सिद्धचारणसेवितम्॥ तमप्सरोगणाकीर्णं शान्तस्वननिनादितम्। किन्नराणां सहस्रैश्च भृङ्गराजैस्तथैव च॥ मद्गुभिः खजरीटैच विचित्रैर्जीवजीवकैः॥ चित्रवर्णैर्मयूरैश्च केकाशतविराजितैः।
en: Those mountains were full of various clans of Apsaras and echoed with many soft sounds. Filled with thousands of Kinnaras and Bhringarajas, it was adorned, besides, with many Madgus and Khanjaritas and many Jivajivakas of variegated colour. And there were many peacocks also of gorgeous hues, uttering their shrill but melodious cries.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: राजहंससमूहैश्च कृष्णैः परभृतैस्तथा॥ पक्षिराजो गरुत्मांश्च यं नित्यमधितिष्ठति।
en: Many bevies of swans also, and many flights of gladdened coils, too, adorned the place. The king of birds, viz., Garuda, live on that suimit constantly.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: चत्वारो लोकपालाश्च देवाः सर्षिगणास्तथा॥ तत्र नित्यं समायान्ति लोकस्य हितकाम्यया।
en: The four Regents of the world, the gods, and various classes of Rishis, used always to come there from desire of doing good to the world.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: विष्णुना यत्र पुत्रार्थे तपस्तप्तं महात्मना॥ तत्रैव च कुमारेण बाल्ये क्षिप्ता दिवौकसः।
en: It was there that the great Vishnu had practised the severest penances for the object of getting a son.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: शक्तिय॑स्ता क्षितितले त्रैलोक्यमवमन्य वै॥ तत्रोवाच जगत् स्कन्दः क्षिपन् वाक्यमिदं तदा। योऽन्योऽस्ति मत्तोऽभ्यधिको विप्रा यस्याधिकं प्रियाः।। यो ब्रह्मण्यो द्वितीयोऽस्ति त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान्। साऽभ्युद्धरत् त्विमां शक्तिमथवा कम्पयत्विति॥ तच्छ्रुत्वा व्यथिता लोकाः क इमामुद्धरेदिति।
en: It was there that the commander-in-chief of the gods named Kumara, in his younger days, disregarding the three worlds with all the inhabitants, threw down his dart, piercing the Earth therewith. Throwing down his dart, Skanda, addressing the universe, said, If there be any person who is superior to me in might, or who holds Brahmanas to be dearer, or who can equal me in devotion to the Brahmanas and the Vedas, or who is endued with energy like me, let him draw up this dart or at least shake it!-Hearing this challenge, the three worlds became stricken with anxiety, and all creatures asked one another, saying-who will raise this dart?

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: अथ देवगणं सर्वं सम्भ्रान्तेन्द्रियमानसम्॥ अपश्यद् भगवान् विष्णुः क्षिप्तं सासुरराक्षसम्। किं त्वत्र सुकृतं कार्यं भवेदिति विचिन्तयन्॥ अनामृष्य ततः क्षेपमवैक्षत च पावकिम्।
en: Vishnu saw all the gods and Asuras and Rakshasas to be greatly troubled in mind. He thought of what should be done under the circumstances. Without being able to bear that challenge regarding the hurling of the dart, he directed his eyes towards Skanda, the son of the Fire-god.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: सम्प्रगृह्य विशुद्धात्मा शक्तिं प्रज्वलितां तदा॥ कम्पयामास सव्येन पाणिना पुरुषोत्तमः।
en: The pure Vishnu caught hold of the burning dart with his left hand, and began to shake it.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: शक्त्यां तु कम्प्यमानायां विष्णुना बलिना तदा॥ मेदिनी कम्पिता सर्वा सशैलवनकानना।
en: When the dart was being thus shaken by the highly powerful Vishnu, the whole Earth with her mountains, forests, and seas, shook with the dart.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: शक्तेनापि समुद्धर्तुं कम्पिता साभवत् तदा॥ रक्षिता स्कन्दराजस्य धर्षणा प्रभविष्णुना।
en: Although Vishnu was fully capable to raise the dart, still he contented himself with only shaking it. In this, the powerful lord only kept the honour of Skanda intact.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: तां कम्पयित्वा भगवान् प्रह्लादमिदमब्रवीत्॥ पश्य वीर्यं कुमारस्य नैतदन्यः करिष्यति।
en: Having shaken it himself, the divine Vishnu, addressing Prahlada, said,-see the might of Kumara! None else in the universe can raise this dart.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: सोऽमृष्यमाणस्तद्वाक्यं समुद्धरणनिश्चितः॥ जग्राह तां तदा शक्तिं न चैनां न व्यकम्पयत्।
en: Unable to bear this, Prahlada determined to raise the dart. He caught it, but was unable to shake it at all.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: नादं महान्तं मुक्त्वा स मूछितो गिरिमूर्धनि॥ विह्वल: प्रापतद् भूमौ हिरण्यकशिपोः सुतः।
en: Uttering a loud cry, he dropped down on the hill-top in a swoon. Indeed, the son of Hiranyakashipu dropped down on the Earth.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: तत्रोत्तरां दिशं गत्वा शैलराजस्य पार्श्वतः॥ तपोऽतप्यत दुर्धर्षं तात नित्यं वृषध्वजः।
en: Going towards the northern side of those grand mountains, Mahadeva, having the bull for his emblem, had practised the austerest penances.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: पावकेन परिक्षिप्तं दीप्यता यस्य चाश्रमम्॥ आदित्यपर्वतं नाम दुर्धर्षमकृतात्मभिः।
en: The asylum where Mahadeva had practised those austerities is encompassed on all sides with a burning fire. Unapproachable by person of impure souls, that mountain is known by the name of Aditya.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: न तत्र शक्यते गन्तुं यक्षराक्षसदानवैः॥ दशयोजनविस्तारमग्निज्वालासमावृतम्।
en: There is a fiery girdle all around it, of ten Yojanas in width and it is incapable of being approached by Yakshas and Rakshasas and Danavas.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: भगवान् पावकस्तत्र स्वयं तिष्ठति वीर्यवान्॥ सर्वान् विघ्नान् प्रशमयन् महादेवस्य धीमतः। दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं हि पादेनैकेन तिष्ठतः॥
en: The illustrious God of Fire, endued with mighty energy, lives there in embodied form engaged in removing all obstacles from the side of Mahadeva of great wisdom who remained there for thousand celestial years, standing on one foot.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: देवान् संतापयंस्तत्र महादेवो महाव्रतः। ऐन्द्रीं तु दिशमास्थाय शैलराजस्य धीमतः॥
en: Living on the side of that foremost of mountains, Mahadeva of great vows scorched the gods greatly.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: विविक्ते पर्वततटे पाराशर्यो महातपाः। वेदानध्यापयामास व्यास: शिष्यान् महामतिः॥
en: At the foot of those mountains, in a retired spot, Parashara's son of great ascetic merit, viz., Vyasa, taught the Vedas to his disciples.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: सुमन्तुं च महाभागं वैशम्पायनमेव च। जैमिनि च महाप्राज्ञं पैलं चापि तपस्विनम्॥
en: Those disciples were the highly blessed Sumanta, Vaishampayana, Jaimini of great wisdom, and Paila of great ascetic merit.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: यत्र शिष्यैः परिवृतो व्यास आस्ते महातपाः। तत्राश्रमपदं रम्यं ददर्श पितुरुत्तमम्।
en: Shuka went to that charming asylum where his father, the great ascetic Vyasa, was living surrounded by his disciples.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: आरणेयो विशुद्धात्मा नभसीव दिवाकरः। अथ व्यास: परिक्षिप्तं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्॥ ददृशे सुतमायान्तं दिवाकरसमप्रभम्।
en: Seated in his asylum, Vyasa saw his son approach like a burning fire of scattered flames, or resembling the Sun himself in effulgence.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: असज्जमा वृक्षेषु शैलेषु विषयेषु च। योगयुक्तं महात्मानं यथा बाणं गुणच्युतम्।॥
en: As Shuka approached, he did not seem to touch the trees or the rocks of the mountain. Perfectly dissociated from all objects of the senses, and engaged in Yoga, the great ascetic came, resembling in speed an arrow shot off a bow.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: सोऽभिगम्य पितुः पादावगृह्णादरणीसुतः। यथोपजोषं तैश्चापि समागच्छन्महामुनिः॥
en: Born on the fire-sticks, Shuka approaching his father, touched his feet. With due formalities he then accosted the disciples of his father.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: ततो निवेदयामास पित्रे सर्वमशेषतः। शुको जनकराजेन संवादं प्रीतमानसः॥
en: With great cheerfulness he then described in full to his father all the particulars of his conversation with king Janaka.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: एवमध्यापयशिष्यान् व्यासः पुत्रं च वीर्यवान्। उवास हिमवत्पृष्ठे पाराशर्यो महामुनिः॥
en: After the arrival of his powerful son, Vyasa, the son of Parashara, continued to live there on the Himavat, engaged in teaching his disciples, and his son.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: ततः कदाचिच्छिष्यास्तं परिवार्यावतस्थिरे। वेदाध्ययनसम्पन्नाः शान्तात्मानो जितेन्द्रियाः॥
en: One day as he was seated his disciples, all well-read in the Vedas, having their senses under control, and gifted with tranquil souls, sat themselves around him.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: वेदेषु निष्ठां सम्प्राप्य साङ्गेष्वपि तपस्विनः। अथोचुस्ते तदा व्यासं शिष्याः प्राञ्जलयो गुरुम्॥
en: All of them had perfectly mastered the Vedas with their branches. All of them were observant of penances. With joined hands they addressed their preceptor in the following words.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: शिष्या ऊचुः महता तेजसा युक्ता यशसा चापि वर्धिताः। एकं त्विदानीमिच्छामो गुरुणानुग्रहं कृतम्॥
en: We have, through your favour, been ended with great energy. Our fame, also has spread. There is one favour that we pray you to grant us.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: इति तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मर्षिस्तानुवाच हा उच्यतामिति तद् वत्सा यद् वः कार्यं प्रियं मया॥
en: Hearing these words of theirs, the twiceborm Rishi answered them, saying,-You sons, tell me what that boon is which you want me to grant you.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: एतद् वाक्यं गुरोः श्रुत्वा शिष्यास्ते हष्टमानसाः। पुनः प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा प्रणम्य शिरसा गुरुम्॥ ऊचुस्ते सहिता राजन्निदं वचनमुत्तमम्। यदि प्रीत उपाध्यायो धन्याः स्मो मुनिसत्तम॥
en: Hearing this answer of their preceptor, the disciples became filled with joy. Bending their heads once more low to their preceptor, and joining their hands, all of them simultaneously, said, O king, these excellent words: If our preceptor has been gratified with us, then, O best of sages, we are sure to be successful.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: काङ्क्षामस्तु वयं सर्वे वरं दातुं महर्षिणा। षष्ठः शिष्यो न ते ख्यातिं गच्छेदत्र प्रसीद नः॥
en: We all solicit you, O great Rishi, to grant us a boon. Do you show us favour. Let no sixth disciple succeed in acquiring fame.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: चत्वारस्ते वयं शिष्या गुरुपुत्रश्च पञ्चमः। इह वेदाः प्रतिष्ठेरन्नेषः नः कासितो वरः॥
en: We are four. Our preceptor's son forms the fifth. Let the Vedas shine in only us five! This is the boon that we pray for.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: शिष्याणां वचनं श्रुत्वा व्यासो वेदार्थतत्त्ववित्। पराशरात्मजो धीमान् परलोकार्थचिन्तकः॥ उवाच शिष्यान् धर्मात्मा धन॑ नैःश्रेयसं वचः। ब्राह्मणाय सदा देयं ब्रह्म शुश्रूषवे तथा॥
en: Hearing these words of his disciples, Vyasa, the son of Parashara, endued with great intelligence, well conversant with the meanings of the Vedas, endued with a pious soul, and always engaged in thinking of objects that grant benefits on a person in the next world, said to his disciples these righteous words, fraught with great benefit:-The Vedas should always be given to him, who is a Brahmana, or to him who is desirous of listening to Vedic instructions, by him who eagerly wishes to acquire a residence in the region of Brahman.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: ब्रह्मलोके निवासं यो ध्रुवं समभिकासते। भवन्तो बहुलाः सन्तु वेदो विस्तार्यतामयम्॥
en: Do ye multiply. Let the Vedas spread. The Vedas should never be given to one who has not formally become a disciple. Nor should they be given to one who does not observe good vows. Nor should they be given to one who is of one impure soul.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: नाशिष्ये सम्प्रदातव्यो नाव्रते नाकृतात्मनि। एते शिष्यगुणा: सर्वे विज्ञातव्या यथार्थतः॥
en: These should be known as the proper accomplishments of persons who can be accepted as disciples. No science should be given to one without a proper examination of one's character.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: नापरीक्षितचारित्रे विद्या देया कथंचन। यथा हि कनकं शुद्धं तापच्छेदनिकर्षणैः॥
en: As pure gold is tested by heat, cutting, and rubbing, similarly disciples should be tested by their birth and accomplishments.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: परीक्षेत तथा शिष्यानीक्षेत् कुलगुणादिभिः। न नियोज्याश्च वः शिष्या अनियोगे महाभये॥
en: You should never give disciples tasks to which they should not be set, or tasks which are full of dangers. One's knowledge is always proportionate to his understanding and diligence in study.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: यथामति यथापाठं तथा विद्या फलिष्यति। सर्वस्तरतु दुर्गाणि सर्वो भद्राणि पश्यतु॥ श्रावयेच्चतुरो वर्णान् कृत्वा ब्राह्मणमग्रतः।
en: Let all disciples master all difficulties, and let all of them be crowned with success. You are competent to expound the scriptures to persons of all the castes. Only ye should, while delivering instructions address a Brahmana, first of all.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: वेदस्याध्ययनं हीदं तच्च कार्यं महत् स्मृतम्॥ स्तुत्यर्थमिह देवानां वेदाः सृष्टाः स्वयम्भुवा।
en: These are the rules about the study of the Vedas. This again is considered as a high task. The Vedas were created by the Self-create for the purpose of praising the gods therewith.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: यो निर्वदेत सम्मोहाद् ब्राह्मणं वेदपारगम्॥ सोऽभिध्यानाद् ब्राह्मणस्य पराभूयाद संशयम्।
en: That man who, through stupefaction of intellect, speaks ill of a Brahmana well-read in the Vedas, is certain to meet with humiliation on account of such evil-speaking.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: यश्चाधर्मेण विब्रूयाद् यश्चाधर्मेण पृच्छति॥ तयोरन्यतरः प्रति विद्वेषं चाधिगच्छति।
en: He who, disregarding all rules of virtue, seeks knowledge, and he who, disregarding the rules of virtue, communicates knowledge, both of them fall off and instead of that love which should exist instead of that love which should exist between preceptor and disciple, such questioning and such communication are sure to create distrust and suspicion.

description: The study of Self by Self
sn: एतद् वः सर्वमाख्यातं स्वाध्यायस्य विधिं प्रति। उपकुर्याच्च शिष्याणामेतच्च हृदि वो भवेत्॥
en: I have now told you everything about the way in which the Vedas should be studied and taught. You should treat your disciples thus, remembering these instructions.”

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं व्यासशिष्या महौजसः। परिषस्वजिरे तदा॥ अन्योन्यं हृष्टमनसः
en: "Hearing these words of their preceptor, Vyasa's disciples gifted with great energy, became filled with the joy and embraced one another.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: उक्ताः स्मो यद् भगवता तदात्वायतिसंहितम्। तन्नो मनसि संरूढं करिष्यामस्तथा च तत्॥
en: Addressing one another, these said,-We will remember and act according to what has been said by our illustrious preceptor in view of our future well-being.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: अन्योन्यं संविभाष्यैवं सुप्रीतमनसः पुनः। विज्ञापयन्ति स्म गुरुं पुनर्वाक्यविशारदाः॥ शैलादस्मान्महीं गन्तुं कासितं नो महामुने। वेदान नेकथा कर्तुं यदि ते रुचितं प्रभो॥
en: Having said this to one another with gladdened hearts, the disciples of Vyasa, who were consummate masters of words, once more addressed their preceptor and said,-If it pleases you, O powerful one we wish to get down from this mountain to the Earth, O great ascetic, for the object of sub-dividing the Vedas.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: शिष्याणां वचनं श्रुत्वा पराशरसुतः प्रभुः। प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्॥ क्षितिं वा देवलोकं वा गम्यतां यदि रोचते। अप्रमादश्च वः कार्यो ब्रह्म हि प्रचुरच्छलम्॥
en: Hearing these words of his disciples, the powerful son of Parashara, replied them in these wholesome words which were fraught, besides, with virtue and profit.-You may go to the Earth or to the regions of the gods as ye like. You should always be careful, for the Vedas are such that they are always liable to be misunderstood.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: तेऽनुज्ञातास्ततः सर्वे गुरुणा सत्यवादिना। जग्मुः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा व्यासं मूर्धाभिवाद्य च॥
en: Permitted by their preceptor of truthful speech, the disciples left him after going round him and bowing their heads to him.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: अवतीर्य महीं तेऽथ चातुर्होत्रमकल्पयन्। संयाजयन्तो विप्रांश्च राजन्यांश्च विशस्तथा॥
en: Descending upon the Earth they celebrated the Agnishtoma and other sacrifices; and they began to officiate at the sacrifices of Brahinanas and Kshatriyas and Vaishyas.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: पूज्यमाना द्विजैर्नित्यं मोदमाना गृहे रताः। याजनाध्यापनरताः श्रीमन्तो लोकविश्रुताः॥
en: Happily spending their days in the domestic mode of life, they were treated by the Brahmanas with great reverence. Possessed of great fame and prosperity, they were engaged in teaching and officiating in sacrifices.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: अवतीर्णेषु शिष्येषु व्यासः पुत्रसहायवान्। तूष्णीं ध्यानपरो धीमानेकान्ते समुपाविशत्।१०।।
en: After his disciples had departed, Vyasa remained in his hermitage, with only his son in his company. Passing his days in anxious thoughtfulness, and great Rishi, endued with wisdom, kept silent, sitting in a retired corner of the asylum.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: तं ददर्शाश्रमपदे नारदः सुमहातपाः। अथैनमब्रवीत् काले मधुराक्षरया गिरा॥
en: At that time Narada of great ascetic merit came there for seeing Vyasa, and addressing him, said these words of sweet sound.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: भो भो ब्रह्मर्षिवासिष्ठ ब्रह्मघोषो न वर्तते। एको ध्यानपरस्तूष्णीं किमास्से चिन्तयन्निव।॥
en: Narada said O twice-born Rishi of Vashistha's family, why are Vedic sounds silent now? Why are you sitting silent and alone, engaged in meditation like one engrossed in thought?

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: ब्रह्मघोषैविरहितः पर्वतोऽयं न शोभते। रजसा तमसा चैव सोमः सोपप्लवो यथा॥
en: Alas, destitute of Vedic sound, this mountain has lost its beauty, as the Moon shorn of splendour when possessed by Rahu or covered with dust.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: न भ्राजते यथापूर्वं निषादानामिवालयः। देवर्षिगणजुष्टोऽपि वेदध्वनिनिराकृतः॥
en: Though inhabited by the celestial Rishis, yet shorn of Vedic sounds, the mountain no longer appears beautiful now but resembles a village of Nishadas.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: ऋषयश्च हि देवाश्च गन्धर्वाश्च महौजसः। वियुक्ता ब्रह्मघोषेण न भ्राजन्ते यथा पुरा॥
en: The Rishis, the gods, and the Gandharvas, too, no longer shine as before on account of being deprived of Vedic sound.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा कृष्णद्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत्। महर्षे यत् त्वया प्रोक्तं वेदवादविचक्षण॥ एतन्मनोऽनुकूलं मे भवानर्हति भाषितुम्। सर्वज्ञः सर्वदर्शी च सर्वत्र च कुतूहली॥
en: Hearing these words of Narada the Islandborn Krishna answered, saying,-0 Great Rishi, O you who are conversant with the sayings of the Vedas, all that you have said is agreeable to me, and you should say it to me! You are omniscient. You have seen everything. Your curiosity knows all things.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: त्रिषु लोकेषु यद् भूतं सर्वं तव मते स्थितम्। तदाज्ञापय विप्रचे ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते॥
en: You know everything in the three words. Do you, then, Otwice-born Rishi, order me.0, tell me what I am to do.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: यन्मया समनुष्ठेयं ब्रह्मर्षे तदुदाहर। विमुक्तस्येहं शिष्यैर्मे नातिहृष्टमिदं मनः॥
en: Tell me, O twice-born Rishi, what should now be done by me. Separated from my disciples, my mind has become very dispirited.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: नारद उवाच अनाम्नायमला वेदा ब्राह्मणस्याव्रतं मलम्। मलं पृथिव्या वाहीका: स्त्रीणां कौतूहलं मलम्॥
en: Narada said The fault of the Vedas is the suspension of their recitation. The fault of the Brahmanas is their non-observance of vows. The Vahika race is the stain of the Earth. Curiosity is the fault of women.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: अधीयतां भवान् वेदान् सार्धं पुत्रेण धीमता। विधुन्वन् ब्रह्मघोषेण रक्षाभयकृतं तमः॥
en: Do you with your intelligent son recite the Vedas, and do you with the echoes of Vedic sounds remove the fears of the Rakshasas.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: भीष्म उवाच नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा व्यासः परमधर्मवित्। तथेत्युवाच संहृष्टो वेदाभ्यासदृढव्रतः॥
en: Bhishma continued Hearing these words of Narada, Vyasa, the best of all persons knowing duties and firmly devoted to Vedic recitation, became filled with joy and answered Narada, saying,-So be it.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: शुकेन सह पुत्रेण वेदाभ्यासमथाकरोत्। स्वरेणोच्चैः स शैक्ष्येण लोकानापूरयन्निव॥
en: With his son Shuka, be began to recite the Vedas in a loud sweet voice, observing all the rules of ortheopy and, as it were, filling the three worlds with that sound.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: तयोरभ्यसतोरेव नानाधर्मप्रवादिनोः। वातोऽतिमात्रं प्रववौ समुद्रानिलवेजितः॥
en: One day as father and son, who knew well the ordinances of duties, were engaged in reciting the Vedas, a violent wind arose as if moved by the gales that blow on the bosom of the ocean.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: ततोऽनध्याय इति तं व्यासः पुत्रमवारयत्। शुको वारितमात्रस्तु कौतूहलसमन्वितः॥
en: Understanding from this incident that the hour was not suited to sacred recitation, Vyasa immediately ordered his son to stop the recitation. Shuka, thus forbidden by his father, became filled with curiosity.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: अपृच्छत् पितरं ब्रह्मन् कुतो वायुरभूदयम्। आख्यातुमर्हति भवान् वायोः सर्वं विचेष्टितम्॥
en: He asked his father saying,-0 twice-born one, whence is this Wind? You should tell me everything about the conduct of the Wind.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: शुकस्यैतद् वचः श्रुत्वा व्यासः परमविस्मितः। अनध्यायनिमित्तेऽस्मिन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing this question of Shuka, Vyasa became filled with wonder. He answered Shuka by telling him that that was an omen which showed that the recitation of the Vedas should be stopped.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: दिव्यं ते चक्षुरुत्पन्नं स्वयं ते निर्मलं मनः। तमसा रजसा चापि त्यक्तः सत्त्वे व्यवस्थितः॥
en: You have acquired spiritual vision. Your mind too has, of itself, became purged off all impurities. You have been freed from the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance. You live now in the quality of Goodness.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: आदर्श स्वामिव च्छायां पश्यस्यात्मानमात्मना। व्यस्यात्मनि स्वयं वेदान् बुद्ध्या समनुचिन्तय॥
en: You see now your Soul with your Soul as one sees his own shadow in a mirror. Staying yourself on your own Soul, do you reflect on the Vedas.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: देवयानचरो विष्णोः पितृयाणश्च तामसः। द्वावेतौ प्रेत्य पन्थानौ दिवं चाधश्च गच्छतः॥
en: The path of the Supreme Soul is called the path of the gods. The path that is made up of the quality of Ignorance is called the path of Pitris. These are the two paths in the world hereafter. By one, people go to heaven. By the other people go to hell.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे च यत्र संवान्ति वायवः। सप्तैते वायुमार्गा वै तान् निबोधानुपूर्वशः।॥
en: The winds blow, on the Earth's surface and in the sky. There are seven courses in which they blow. Listen to me as I describe them one after another.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: तत्र देवगणाः साध्या महाभूता महाबलाः। तेषामप्यभवत् पुत्रः समानो नाम दुर्जयः॥
en: The body has the senses. The senses are ruled over by the Sadhyas and many great beings of great strength. These gave birth to an invincible son named Samana.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: उदानस्तस्य पुत्रोऽभूद् व्यानस्तस्याभवत् सुतः। अपानश्च ततो ज्ञेयः प्राणश्चापि ततोऽपरः॥
en: From Samana originated a son calle Udana. From Udana originated Vyana. From Vyana arose Apana, and lastly from Apana originated the wind called Prana.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: अनपत्योऽभवत् प्राणो दुर्धर्षः शत्रुतापनः। पृथक् कर्माणि तेषां ते प्रवक्ष्यामि यथातथम्॥
en: That invincible scorcher of all enemies, vis., Prana, became barren. I shall now recite to you the different functions of those winds.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: प्राणिनां सर्वतो वायुश्चेष्टां वर्तयते पृथक्। प्राणनाच्चैव भूतानां प्राण इत्यभिधीयते॥
en: The wind is the root of the various functions of all living creatures, and because living creatures are enabled to live by it, therefore is the wind called Prana (or life).

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: प्रेरयत्यभ्रसंघातान् धूमजांचोष्मजांश्च यः। प्रथमः प्रथमे मार्गे प्रवहो नाम योऽनिलः॥ अम्बरे स्नेहमभ्येत्य विद्युयश्च महाद्युतिः।
en: That wind which is the first in the above number and which is known by the name of Pravaha (Samana) drives, along the first course, masses of clouds born of smoke and heat. Passing through the sky, and coming into contact with the water in the clouds, that wind shows itself in effulgence among the darts of lightening.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: आवहो नाम संवाति द्वितीयः श्वसनो नदन्॥ उदयं ज्योतिषां शश्वत् सोमादीनां करोति यः। अन्तर्देहेषु चोदानं यं वदन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: The second wind, called Avaha blows with a loud noise. It is this wind that make Soma and the other luminaries rise and appear. Within the body that wind is called Udana by the wise.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: यश्चतुर्थ्य: समुद्रेभ्यो वायर्धारयते जलम्। उद्धत्याददते चापो जीमूतेभ्योऽम्बरेऽनिलः॥ योऽद्भिः संयोज्य जीमूतान् पर्जन्याय प्रयच्छति। उद्वहो नाम बंहिष्ठस्तृतीयः स सदागतिः॥
en: That wind which drinks up water from the four oceans, and having sucked it up gives it to the clouds in the sky and which, having given it to the clouds, presents them to the gods of rain, is third in the number and known by the name of Udvaha.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: समूह्यमाना बहुधा येन नीताः पृथग् घनाः। वर्षमोक्षकृतारम्भास्ते भवन्ति घनाघनाः॥ संहता येन चाविद्धा भवन्ति नदतां नदाः। रक्षणार्थाय सम्भूता मेघत्वमुपयान्ति च॥ योऽसौ वहति भूतानां विमानानि विहायसा। चतुर्थः संवहो नाम वायुः स गिरिमर्दनः॥
en: That wind which supports the clouds and divides them into various parts which melts them for pouring rain and once more solidifies them, which is perceived as the sound of roaring clouds, which exists for the preservation of the world by itself assuming the form of the clouds, which carries the cars of all celestials along the sky, is known by the name of Samvaha. The fourth in the number, it is gifted with great strength so that it is capable of rending the very mountains.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: दारुणोत्पातसंचारो नभसः स्तनयित्नुमान्। पञ्चमः स महावेगो विवहो नाम मारुतः॥ येन वेगवता रुग्णा रूक्षेण रुवता नगान्। वायुना सहिता मेघास्ते भवन्ति बलाहकाः॥
en: That wind causes portends of many sorts and creates roaring sounds in the sky. It is known by the name of Vivaha. The fifth wind has great force and speed. It is dry and roots out and breaks down all trees. Existing with it, the clouds are called Valahaka.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: यस्मिन् पारिप्लवा दिव्या वहन्त्यायो विहायसा। पुण्यं चाकाशगङ्गायास्तोयं विष्टभ्य तिष्ठति॥
en: The sixth wind carries all celestial waters in the sky and prevents them from falling down. Keeping the sacred waters of the celestial Ganga, that wind blows preventing them from having a downward course.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: दुरात् प्रतिहतो यस्मिन्नेकरश्मिर्दिवाकरः। योनिरंशुसहस्रस्य येन भाति वसुन्धरा॥
en: Obstructed by the wind from a distance, the Sun, which is really the root of a thousand rays, and which lights up the world, appears as a luminous body of but one ray.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: यस्मादाप्यायते सोमो निधिर्दिव्योऽमृतस्य च। षष्ठः परिवहो नाम स वायुर्जयतां वरः॥
en: Through the action of that wind, the Moon, after waning increases again till he shows his full disc. That wind is known, O foremost of ascetics, by the name of Parivaha.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: सर्वप्राणभृतां प्राणान् योऽन्तकाले निरस्यति। यस्य वानुवर्तेते मृत्युवैवस्वतावुभौ॥ सम्यगन्वीक्षतां बुद्ध्या शान्तयाध्यात्मनित्यया। ध्यानाभ्यासाभिरामाणां योऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते॥ यं समासाद्य वेगेन दिशोऽन्तं प्रतिपेदिरे। दक्षस्य दशपुत्राणां सहस्राणि प्रजापतेः॥ येन स्पृष्टः पराभूतो यात्येव न निवर्तते। परावहो नाम परो वायुः स दुरतिक्रमः॥
en: That wind which takes away the life of all living creatures when the proper time comes, whose path is followed by Death and Surya's son Yama, which becomes the source of that immortality becomes the source of the immortality which is acquired by the Yogins of subtile sight who are always engaged in Yogameditation, by whose help the thousands of grandsons of Daksha, that lord of creatures, by his ten sons, succeeded in days of yore in reaching the ends of the universe, whose touch enables one to acquire Liberation by freeing himself from the obligation of returning to the world, that wind is called by the name of Paravaha. The foremost of all winds, it cannot be resisted by any body.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: एवमेते दितेः पुत्रा मारुताः परमाद्भुताः। अनारतं ते संवान्ति सर्वगाः सर्वधारिणः॥
en: Wonderful are these winds all of whom are the sons of Diti. Capable of going everywhere and upholding all things, they blow all around you without being attached to you at any time.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: एतत् तु महदाश्चर्यं यदयं पर्वतोत्तमः। कम्पितः सहसा तेन वायुनातिप्रवायता॥
en: This, however, is greatly wonderful, viz., that this foremost of mountains should thus be suddenly shaken by that wind which has begun to below.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: विष्णोनि:श्वासवातोऽयं यदा वेगसमीरितः। सहसोदीर्यते तात जगत् प्रव्यथते तदा॥
en: This wind is the breath of Vishnu's nostrils. When moved with speed, it begins to blow with great vehemence at which the whole universe becomes agitated.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: तस्माद् ब्रह्मविदो वेदान् नाधीयन्तेऽतिवायति। वायोर्वायुभयं ह्युक्तं ब्रह्म तत्पीडितं भवेत्॥
en: Hence, when the wind begins to blow with violence, persons knowing the Vedas do not recite the Vedas, The Vedas are a form of wind. If uttered with vehemence, the external wind becomes agitated.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं पराशरसुतः : प्रभुः। उक्त्वा पुत्रमधीष्वेति व्योमगङ्गामगात् तदा॥
en: Having said these words, the powerful son of Parashara ordered his son to go on with his Vedic recitation. He then left that place for plugging into the waters of the celestial Ganga." recite the Vedas, The Vedas are a form of wind. If uttered with vehemence, the external wind becomes agitated.

description: The suspension of the Vedas. The disciples of Vyasa go down for sub-dividing them
sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं पराशरसुतः : प्रभुः। उक्त्वा पुत्रमधीष्वेति व्योमगङ्गामगात् तदा॥
en: Having said these words, the powerful son of Parashara ordered his son to go on with his Vedic recitation. He then left that place for plugging into the waters of the celestial Ganga."

sn: भीष्म उवाच एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शून्ये नारदः समुपागमत्। शुकं स्वाध्यायनिरतं वेदार्थान् वक्तुमीप्सितान्॥
en: Bhishma said "After Vyasa had left the spot, Narada, passing through the sky, came to Shuka engaged in studying the scriptures The celestial Rishi came for the object of asking Shuka the meaning of certain parts of the Vedas.

sn: देवर्षि तु शुको दृष्ट्वा नारदं समुपस्थितम्। अर्थ्यपूर्वेण विधिना वेदोक्तेनाभ्यपूजयत्॥
en: Seeing the celestial Rishi Narada arrived at his asylum, Shuka adored him by offering him the Arghya according to the rites laid down in the Vedas.

sn: नारदोऽथाब्रवीत् प्रीतो ब्रूहि धर्मभृतां वर। केन त्वां श्रेयसा वत्स योजयामीति हृष्टवत्॥
en: Pleased with the honours conferred upon him, Narada addressed Shuka, saying.-Tell me, O foremost of pious men, how, O dear child, may I acccomplished what is for your highest good.

sn: नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शुकः प्रोवाच भारत। अस्मॅिल्लोके हितं यत् स्यात् तेन मां योक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Hearing these words of Narada, Shuka said to him, O Bharata, these words:-You should instruct me about what may be beneficial to me!

sn: नारद उवाच तत्त्वं जिज्ञासतां पूर्वमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्। सनत्कुमारो भगवानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Narada said In days of yore the illustrious Sanatkumara had said these words to certain Rishis of purified souls who had gone to him for enquiring after the truth.

sn: नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति सत्यसमं तपः। नास्ति रागसमं दुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम्॥
en: There is no eye like that of knowledge. There is no penance like the practice of truth. There is no sorrow like attachment. There is no happiness like renunciation.

sn: निवृत्तिः कर्मणः पापात् सततं पुण्यशीलता। सवृत्तिः समुदाचारः श्रेय एतदनुत्तमम्॥
en: Abstention from sinful deeds, steady practice of virtue, good conduct, the due observance of all religious duties,—these form the highest good.

sn: मानुष्यमसुखं प्राप्य यः सज्जति स मुह्यति। नालं स दुःखमोक्षाय संयोगो दुःखलक्षणम्॥
en: Having acquired the status of humanity which is mixed with sorrow, he who becomes attached to it, becomes stupefied; such a man never succeeds in freeing himself from sorrow. Attachment is a mark of sorrow.

sn: सक्तस्य बुद्धिश्चलति मोहजालविवर्धनी। मोहजालावृतो दुःखमिह चामुत्र सोऽश्नुते॥
en: The understanding of a person who is attached to earthly object becomes more and more entangled in the net of stupefaction. The man who becomes entangled in the net of stupefaction comes by sorrow both in this world and in the next.

sn: सर्वोपायात् तु कामस्य क्रोधस्य च विनिग्रहः। कार्यः श्रेयोऽर्थिना तौ हि श्रेयोघातार्थमुद्यतौ॥
en: One should, by every means in his power, control both desire and anger if one tries to acquire what is for his good. Those two originate for only destroying his good.

sn: नित्यं क्रोधात् तपो रक्षेच्छ्रियं रक्षेच्च मत्सरात्। विद्यां मानावमानाभ्यामात्मानं तु प्रमादतः॥
en: One should always protect his penances from anger, and his prosperity from pride. One should always protect his knowledge from honour and dishonour, and his soul from error.

sn: आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः क्षमा च परमं बलम्। आत्मज्ञानं परं ज्ञानं न सत्याद् विद्यते परम्॥
en: Mercy is the highest virtue. Forgiveness is the highest power. The knowledge of self is the highest knowledge. There is nothing higher than truth.

sn: सत्यस्य वचनं श्रेयः सत्यादपि हितं वदेत्। यद् भूतहितमत्यन्तमेतत् सत्यं मतं मम॥
en: It is always meet to speak the truth. It is better again to speak what is wholesome than to speak what is true. I hold that that is truth which is filled with the greatest benefit to all creatures.

sn: सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी निराशीनिष्परिग्रहः। येन सर्वं परित्यक्तं स विद्वान् स च पण्डितः॥
en: That man is said to be truly learned and truly endued with wisdom who renounces every act, who never indulges in hope, who is perfectly dissociated from all worldly surroundings, and who has renounced everything that belongs to the world.

sn: इन्द्रियैरिन्द्रियार्थान् यश्चरत्यात्मवशैरिह। असज्जमानः शान्तात्मा निर्विकारः समाहितः॥ आत्मभूतैरतद्भूतः सह चैव विनैव च। स विमुक्तः परं श्रेयो नचिरेणाधितिष्ठति॥
