en: That person who, without being attached thereto, enjoys all objects of sense with the help of senses which are completely under his control, who is endued with a tranquil soul, who is never moved by joy or sorrow, who is engaged in Yoga-meditation, who lives with the gods presiding over his senses and dissociated also from them, and who, though gifted with a body, never considers himself as identifiable with it, becomes liberated and very soon acquires what is his highest good.

sn: अदर्शनमसंस्पर्शस्तथासम्भाषणं सदा। यस्य भूतैः सह मुने स श्रेयो विन्दते परम्॥
en: One who never sees others, never touches others, never talks with others, soon, O ascetic, acquires what is for his highest good.

sn: न हिंस्यात् सर्वभूतानि मैत्रायणगतश्चरेत्। नेदं जन्म समासाद्य वैरं कुर्वीत केनचित्॥
en: One should not injure any creature. On the other hand, one should treat with friendliness to all. Having acquired the status of humanity, one should never treat inimically to any one.

sn: आकिञ्चन्यं सुसंतोषो निराशीस्त्वमचापलम्। एतदाहुः परं श्रेय आत्मज्ञस्य जितात्मनः॥
en: A perfect disregard for all (worldly) things, perfect contentment, abandonment of hope of every sort, and patience,-these form the highest good of one who has governed his senses and acquired a knowledge of self.

sn: परिग्रहं परित्यज्य भव तात जितेन्द्रियः। अशोकं स्थानमातिष्ठ इह चामुत्र चाभयम्॥
en: Renouncing all attachments, O child, do you master all your senses, and thereby acquire happiness both in this world and in the next.

sn: निरामिषा न शोचन्ति त्यजेदामिषमात्मनः। परित्यज्यामिषं सौम्य दुःखतापाद् विमोक्ष्यसे॥
en: They who are free from cupidity have never to suffer any sorrow. One should, therefore, renounce all cupidity from one's soul. By renouncing cupidity, O amiable and blessed one, you will be able to liberate yourself from sorrow and pain.

sn: तपोनित्येन दान्तेन मुनिना संयतात्मना। अजितं जेतुकामेन भाव्यं सङ्गेष्वसङ्गिना॥
en: One who wishes to conquer that which is unconquerable should live giving himself up to penances, to self-control, to taciturnity, to a subjugation of the soul. Such a person should live in the midst of attachments without being attached thereto.

sn: गुणसङ्गेष्वनासक्त एकचर्यारतः सदा। ब्राह्मणो नचिरादेव सुखमायात्यनुत्तमम्॥
en: That Brahmana who lives in the midst of attachments without being attached to them and who always lives in seclusion, very soon acquires the highest happiness.

sn: द्वन्द्वारामेषु भूतेषु य एको रमते मुनिः। विद्धि प्रज्ञानतृप्तं तं ज्ञानतृप्तो न शोचति॥
en: That man who lives alone in happiness in the midst of creatures who are seen to find pleasure in leading lives of sexual union, should be known to be a person whose thirst has been satisfied by knowledge. It is well known that that man whose thirst has been satisfied by knowledge has never to grieve.

sn: शुभैर्लभति देवत्वं व्यामिश्रैर्जन्म मानुषम्। अशुभैश्चाप्यधो जन्म कर्मभिर्लभतेऽवशः॥
en: One acquires the status of the god my means of good deeds; the status of humanity by means of acts which are good and bad; while by acts which are purely wicked, one helplessly falls down among the lower animals.

sn: तत्र मृत्युजरादुःखैः सततं समभिद्रुतः। संसारे पच्यते जन्तुस्तत्कथं नावबुद्ध्यसे॥
en: Always attacked by sorrow and decrepitude and death, a living creature is being cooked in this world. Do you not know it?

sn: अहिते हितसंज्ञस्त्वमधुवे ध्रुवसंज्ञकः। अनर्थे चार्थसंज्ञस्त्वं किमर्थं नावबुद्ध्यसे॥
en: You generally consider that to be beneficial which is really injurious; that to be certain which is really uncertain; and that to be desirable and good which is undesirable and not good. Alas, why do you not form a correct apprehension of these?

sn: संवेष्ट्यमानं बहुभिर्मोहात् तन्तुभिरात्मजैः। कोषकार इवात्मानं वेश्यन् नावबुध्यसे॥
en: Like a silkworm that covers itself in its own cocoon, you are continually covering yourself in a cocoon made of your own numberless deeds born of stupefaction and mistake. Alas, why do you not form a correct apprehension of your situation?

sn: अलं परिग्रहेणेह दोषवान् हि परिग्रहः। कृमिर्हि कोषकारस्तु बध्यते स परिग्रहात्॥
en: No need of attaching yourself to earthly objects. Attachment to earthly objects produces evil. The silk-worm that forms a cocoon round itself is at last destroyed by its own deed.

sn: पुत्रदारकुटुम्बेषु सक्ताः सीदन्ति जन्तवः। सर:पङ्कार्णवे मग्ना जीर्णा वनगजा इव॥
en: Those persons who become attached to sons and wives and relatives meet with destruction in the end, as wild elephants sunk in the mire of a lake are by and by weakened till overtaken by Death,

sn: महाजालसमाकृष्टान् स्थले मत्स्यानिवोद्धृतान्। स्नेहजालसमाकृष्टान् पश्य जन्तून् सुदुःखितान्॥
en: See, all creatures that allow themselves to be dragged by the net of affection become subject to great grief as fishes on land, dragged thereto by means of large nets.

sn: कुटुम्बं पुत्रदारांश्च शरीरं संचयाश्च ये। पारक्यमधुवं सर्वं किं स्वं सुकृतदुष्कृतम्॥
en: Relatives, sons, wives, the body itself, and all properties amassed with care, unsubstantial and of no use in the next world. Only acts, good and bad, that one does, follow him to the other world.

sn: यदा सर्वं परित्यज्य गन्तव्यमवशेन ते। अनर्थे किं प्रसक्तस्त्वं स्वमर्थं नानुतिष्ठसि॥
en: When it is certain that you shall have to go helplessly to the other world, leaving behind all these things, alas, why do you then allow yourself to be attached to such worthless unsubstantial things, without attending to what forms your real and durable wealth?

sn: अविश्रान्तमनालम्बमपाथेयमदैशिकम्। तमःकान्तारमध्वानं कथमेको गमिष्यसि॥
en: The path which you shall have to pass through is without resting places of any sort. There is no support along that way which one may catch for maintaining oneself. The country are through which it passes is unknown and undiscovered. It is, again, covered with thick darkness. Alas, how will you go along that way without being supplied with the necessary expenses?

sn: न हि त्वां प्रस्थितं कश्चित् पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यति। सुकृतं दुष्कृतं च त्वां यास्यन्तमनुयास्यति॥
en: When you shall go along that road, nobody will follow you. Only your deeds, good and bad, will follow you when you shall leave his world for the next.

sn: विद्या कर्म च शौचं न ज्ञानं च बहुविस्तरम् अर्थार्थमनुसार्यन्ते सिद्धार्थश्च विमुच्यते॥
en: One seeks the real object by means of learning, acts, purity and great knowledge. When that foremost of objects is acquired, one becomes liberated.

sn: निबन्धनी रज्जुरेषा या ग्रामे वसतो रतिः। छित्त्वैतां सुकृतो यान्ति नैनां छिन्दन्ति दुष्कृतः॥
en: The desire that one feels for living in the midst of human dwellings is like a binding fetter. They that are of good deeds succeed in snapping that fetter and freeing themselves. Only men of wicked deeds do not succeed in breaking them.

sn: रूपकूलां मनःस्रोतां स्पर्शद्वीपां रसावहाम्। गन्धपङ्का शब्दजला स्वर्गमार्गदुरावहाम्॥ क्षमारित्रां सत्यमयीं धर्मस्थैर्यवटारकाम्। त्यागवाताध्वगां शीघ्रां नौतार्यां तां नदी तरेत्॥
en: The river of life is dreadful. Personal beauty or form forms is banks. The mind is the speed of its current. Touch forms its island. Taste forms its waters. That particular part of it which leads towards heaven is beset with great difficulties. Body is the boat by which one must cross that river. Forgiveness is the oar by which it is to be moved. Truth is the ballast that keeps that boat steady. The practice of virtue is the rope that is to be put to the mast for dragging that boat along difficult waters. Charity or gift forms the wind that moves the sails of that boat. Bifted with swift speed, it is with that boat that one must cross the river of life.

sn: त्यज धर्ममधर्म च तथा सत्यानृते त्यज। उभे सत्यानृते त्यक्त्वा येन त्यजसि तं त्यज।॥
en: Renounce both virtue and vice, and truth and falsehood. Having renounced truth and falsehood, do you cast off that by which these are to be shaken off.

sn: त्यज धर्ममसंकल्पादधर्म चाप्यलिप्सया। उभे सत्यानृते बुद्ध्या बुद्धिं परमनिश्चयात्॥
en: By casting off all purpose, do you renounce virtue; do you cast off sin also by renouncing all desire. With the help of the understanding, do you renounce truth and falsehood; and, at last, do you renounce the understanding itself by knowledge of the highest subject.

sn: अस्थिस्थूणं स्नायुयुतं मांसशोणितलेपनम्। चर्मावनद्धं दुर्गन्धि पूर्ण मूत्रपुरीषयोः॥ जराशोकसमाविष्टं रोगायतनमातुरम्। रजस्वलमनित्यं च भूतावासमिमं त्यज॥
en: Do you renounce this body having bones for its pillars; sinews for its binding strings and cords; flesh and blood for its outer plaster; the skin for its outer case; full of urine and faeces and, therefore, sending forth a bad smell; exposed to the attacks of decrepitude and sorrow; forming the seat of disease and weakened by pain; predominated by the quality of Darkness; not permanent or durable, and which serves as the habitation of the indwelling creature.

sn: इदं विश्वं जगत् सर्वमजगच्चापि यद् भवेत्। महाभूतात्मकं सर्वं महद् यत् परमाश्रयात्॥
en: This entire universe of matier, and that which is called Mahat or Buddhi, are formed of great elements. That which is called Mahat is due to the action of the Supreme.

sn: इन्द्रियाणि च पञ्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा। इत्येष सप्तदशको राशिरव्यक्तसंज्ञकः॥
en: The five senses, the three qualities of Tamas, Sattva, and Rajas,-these make up seventeen.

sn: सर्वैरिहेन्द्रियार्थश्च व्यक्ताव्यक्तैर्हि संहितः। चतुर्विंशक इत्येष व्यक्ताव्यक्तमयो गणः॥
en: These seventeen, which are known by the name of the Unmanifest, with all those that are called Manifest, viz., the five objects of the five senses, with Consciousness and the Understanding, constitute the well-known twenty-four.

sn: एतैः सर्वैः समायुक्तः पुमानित्यभिधीयते। त्रिवर्गं तु सुखं दुःखं जीवितं मरणं तथा॥ य इदं वेद तत्त्वेन स वेद प्रभवाप्ययौ। पारम्पर्येण बोद्धव्यं ज्ञानानां यच्च किञ्चन॥
en: When endued with those twenty-four possessions, one comes to be called by the name of Jiva or Individual Soul. He who knows the three-fold objects as also happiness and sorrow and life and death, truly and in all their details, is said to know growth and decay All objects of knowledge, should be known by and by.

sn: इन्द्रियैर्गृह्यते यद् यत् तत् तद् व्यक्तमिति स्थितिः। अव्यक्तमिति विज्ञेयं लिङ्गग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम्॥
en: All objects that are perceived by the senses are called Manifest. Whatever objects are above the senses and are apprehended by means only of their marks are said to be Unimanifest.

sn: इन्द्रियैर्नियतैर्देही धाराभिरिव तर्प्यते। लोके विततमात्मानं लोकांश्चात्मनि पश्यति॥
en: By controlling the senses, one acquires great gratification, like a thirsty and parched traveller at a sweet shower of rain. Having restrained the senses one sees one's soul spread out for embracing all objects, and all objects in one's soul.

sn: परावरदृशः शक्तिर्ज्ञानमूला न नश्यति। पश्यतः सर्वभूतानि सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा॥
en: Having its roots in knowledge, the power is never lost of the man who (thus) sees the Supreme in his soul,-of the man, who always sees all creatures in all conditions.

sn: सर्वभूतस्य संयोगो नाशुभेनोपपद्यते। ज्ञानेन विविधान् क्लेशानतिवृत्तस्य मोहजान्॥
en: He who, by the help of knowledge, gets over all sorts of pain begotten of mistake stupefaction, never catches any evil by coming into contact with all creatures.

sn: लोके बुद्धिप्रकाशेन लोकमार्गो न रिष्यते। अनादिनिधनं जन्तुमात्मनि स्थितमव्ययम्॥ अकर्तारममूर्तं च भगवानाह तीर्थवित्। यो जन्तुः स्वकृतैस्तैस्तैः कर्मभिनित्यदुःखितः॥ स दुःखप्रतिघातार्थं हन्ति जन्तूननेकधा। ततः कर्म समादत्ते पुनरन्यन्नवं बहु॥
en: Such a man, his understanding being fully shown, never finds fault with the course of conduct that prevails in the world. One conversant with Liberation says that the Supreme Soul is without beginning and without end; that it takes birth as all creatures; that it resides in the Individual Soul; that it is inactive, and without form. Only that man who meets with grief on account of his own misdeeds, kills numerous creatures for the purpose of preventing that grief. On account of such sacrifices, the performers have to go through re-births and have necessarily to perform numberless deeds on all sides.

sn: तप्यतेऽथ पुनस्तेन भुक्त्वापथ्यमिवातुरः। अजस्रमेव मोहान्धो दुःखेषु सुखसंज्ञितः॥
en: Such a man, blinded by mistake, and considering that to be happiness which is really a source of grief, is continually rendered unhappy like a sick person who eats bad food.

sn: बध्यते मथ्यते चैव कर्मभिर्मन्थवत् सदा। ततो निबद्धः स्वां योनि कर्मणामुदयादिह॥
en: Such a man is pressed and grinded by his deeds like any substance that is churned. Fettered by his deeds he obtains re-birth, the order of his life being determined by the character of his deeds.

sn: परिभ्रमति संसारं चक्रवद् बहुवेदनः। स त्वं निवृत्तबन्धुस्तु निवृत्तश्चापि कर्मतः॥
en: Suffering many kinds of torture, he passes through a repeated round of re-births like a wheel that turns ceaselessly. You have, however, snapped asunder all your fetters. You abstain from all deeds.

sn: सर्ववित् सर्वजित् सिद्धो भव भावविवर्जितः। संयमेन नवं बन्धं निवर्त्य तपसो बलात्। सम्प्राप्ता बहवः सिद्धिमप्यबाधां सुखोदयाम्॥
en: Possessed of oinniscience and the master of all things, may you be successful, and do you become freed from all existent objects. Through subjugation of their senses and the power of their penances, many persons, having destroyed the fetters of action, acquired great success and uninterrupted happiness.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: नारद उवाच अशोकं शोकनाशार्थं शास्त्रं शान्तिकरं शिवम्। निशम्य लभते बुद्धिं तां लब्ध्वा सुखमेधते॥
en: Narada said By listening to such sacred scriptures, as bring about tranquillity, as remove grief, and as yield happiness, one acquired (a pure) understanding, and, having acquired it; obtains to great happiness.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: शोकस्थानसहस्राणि भयस्थानशतानि च। दिवसे दिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम्॥
en: A thousand causes of sorrow, a hundred causes of fear, from day to day, attack one who is shorn of understanding but not one who is endued with wisdom and learning.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: तस्मादनिष्टनाशार्थमितिहासं निबोध मे। तिष्ठते चेद् वशे बुद्धिर्लभते शोकनाशनम्॥
en: Do you, therefore, listen to some old narratives as I recount them to you, for the object of removing your sorrow, If one can subjugate his understanding, he is sure to acquire happiness.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: अनिष्टसम्प्रयोगाच्च विप्रयोगात् प्रियस्य च। मनुष्या मानसैर्दुःखैर्युज्यन्ते स्वल्पबुद्धयः॥
en: By accession of what is undesirable and dissociation from what is agreeable, only men of little intelligence yield to mental sorrow.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: द्रव्येषु समतीतेषु ये गुणास्तान् न चिन्तयेत्। न तानाद्रियमाणस्य स्नेहबन्धः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: When things are passed, one should not grieve, thinking of their merits. He who thinks of such past things with affection can never liberate himself.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: दोषदर्शी भवेत् तत्र यत्र रागः प्रवर्तते। अनिष्टवर्धितं पश्येत् तथा क्षिप्र विरज्यते॥
en: One should always try to find out the faults of those things to which one becomes attached, One should always consider such things to be fraught with much evil, By doing so, one should soon free him therefrom.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: नार्थो न धर्मो न यशो योऽतीतमनुशोचति। अप्यभावेन युज्येत तच्चास्य न निवर्तते।॥
en: The man who grieves for what is past, cannot acquire either riches or religious merit or fame. What exists no longer cannot be acquired. When such things go away, they do not return.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: गुणैर्भूतानि युज्यन्ते वियुज्यन्ते तथैव च। सर्वाणि नैतदेकस्य शोकस्थानं हि विद्यते॥
en: Creatures sometimes acquire and sometimes lose earthly objects. No man in this world can be grieved by all the events that befall him.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: मृतं वा यदि वा नष्टं योऽतीतमनुशोचति। दुःखेन लभते दु:खं द्वावनों प्रपद्यते॥
en: Dead or lost, he who grieves for what is gone only gets sorrow for sorrow. Instead of one sorrow, he gets two.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: नाश्रु कुर्वन्ति ये बुद्ध्या दृष्ट्वा लोकेषु संततिम्। सम्यक् प्रपश्यतः सर्वं नाश्रुकर्मोपपद्यते॥
en: Those men who, seeing the course of life and death in the world with the help of their intelligence, do not shed tears, are said to see properly. Such persons have never to shed tears.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते। यस्मिन् न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुचिन्तयेत्॥
en: When any such calamity comes, which creates either their physical or mental grief, as is incapable of being prevented by even his best endeavours, one should cease to think on it with sorrow.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: भैषज्यमेतद् दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत्। चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते॥
en: Not to think of it is the panacea for sorrow. By thinking of it, one can never remove it; on the other hand, by thinking upon sorrow, one only increases it.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः। एतद् विज्ञानसामर्थ्य न बालैः समतामियात्॥
en: Mental sorrow should be destroyed by wisdom; while physical sorrow should be removed by medicines. This is the power of knowledge. One should not, in such matters, act like men of little understandings.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: अनित्यं यौवनं रूपं जीवितं द्रव्यसंचयः। आरोग्यं प्रियसंवासो गृध्येत् तत्र न पण्डितः॥
en: Youth, beauty, life, hoarded riches, health, association with those that are loved, these all are fickle. One endued with wisdom should never covet them.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: न जानपदिकं दुःखमेकः शोचितुमर्हति। अशोचन् प्रतिकुर्वीत यदि पश्येदुपक्रमम्॥
en: One should not lament individually for a sorrowful incident that concerns an entire community. Instead of indulgence in grief when it comes, one should try to avert it and apply a remedy as soon as he finds the opportunity for doing it.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: सुखाद् बहुतरं दुःखं जीविते नात्र संशयः। स्निग्धत्वं चेन्द्रियार्थेषु मोहान्मरणमप्रियम्॥
en: There is no doubt that in this life misery is much greater than that of happiness. There is no doubt in this that all men show attachment for objects of the senses and that death is considered as disagreeable.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: परित्यजति यो दुःखं सुखं वाप्युभयं नरः। अभ्येति ब्रह्म सोऽत्यन्तं न तं शोचन्ति पण्डिताः।१७।।
en: That man who renounces both joy and sorrow, is said to attain to Brahma. When such a man dies, men of wisdom never indulge in any grief for him.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: त्यज्यन्ते दुःखमर्था हि पालने न च ते सुखाः। दुःखेन चाधिगम्यते नाशमेषां न चिन्तयेत्॥
en: There is pain in spending wealth. There is pain in protecting it. There is pain in acquiring it. Hence, when one's wealth is lost, he should not grieve for it.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: अन्यामन्यां धनावस्थां प्राप्य वैशेषिकी नराः। अतृप्ता यान्ति विध्वंसं संतोषं यान्ति पण्डिता॥
en: Men of little understandings, in their efforts to acquire different grades of wealth, lose their contentment and at last die broken-hearted. Wise men, however, are always contented.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः। संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं हि जीवितम्॥
en: All combinations are sure to end in dissolution. All things that are high are destined to fall down and become low. Union is sure to end in disunion, and life is certain to end in death.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: अन्तो नास्ति पिपासायास्तुष्टिस्तु परमं सुखम्। तस्मात् संतोषमेवेह धनं पश्यन्ति पण्डिताः॥
en: Thirst can never be satiated. Contentment is the greatest happiness. Hence, wise men regard contentment as the most valuable wealth.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: निमेषमात्रमपि हि वयो गच्छन्न तिष्ठति। स्वशरीरेष्वनित्येषु नित्यं किमनुचिन्तयेत्॥
en: One's lease of life is running continually. It stops not in its course for even a single moment. When one's body itself is not durable, what other thing is there which one should consider as durable?

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: भूतेषु भावं संचिन्त्य ये बुद्ध्वा मनस: परम्। न शोचन्ति गताध्वानः पश्यन्तः परमां गतिम्॥
en: Those persons who, meditating on the nature of all creatures and, concluding that it is beyond the grasp of the mind, direct their attention to the highest path, and, starting, acquire a fair progress in it, have not to indulge in sorrow.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: संचिन्वानकमेवैनं कामानामवितृप्तकम्। व्याघ्रः पशुमिवासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति।॥
en: Like a tiger seizing and running away with its prey, Death seizes and runs away with the man, who is engaged in such occupation and which is still not satiated with objects of desire and enjoyment.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: तथाप्युपायं सम्पश्येद् दुःखस्य परिमोक्षणम्। अशोचन् नारभेच्चैव मुक्तश्चाव्यसनी भवेत्॥
en: One should always try to liberate himself from sorrow. One should try to remove sorrow by beginning his work with cheerfulness, that is without indulging, in sorrow, having freed himself from a particular sorrow, one should act in such a way as to keep sorrow at a distance by abstaining from all shortcomings of conduct.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: शब्दे स्पर्शे च रूपे च गन्धेषु च रसेषु च। नोपभोगात् परं किंचिद् धनिनो वाधनस्य च॥
en: The rich and the poor alike find nothing in sound and touch and form and scent and taste, after the immediate enjoyment thereof.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: प्राक्सम्प्रयोगाद् भूतानां नास्ति दुःखं परायणम्। विप्रयोगात् तु सर्वस्य न शोचेत् प्रकृतिस्थितः॥
en: Before union, creatures never suffer sorrow. Hence, one who has not deviated from his original nature, never grieves when that union comes to an end.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: धृत्या शिश्नोदरं रक्षेत् पाणिपादं च चक्षुषा। चक्षुःश्रोत्रे च मनसा मनो वाचं च विद्यया॥
en: One should control his sexual appetite and the stomach with the help of patience. One should protect his hands and feet with the help of the eye. One's eyes and ears and the other senses, should be protected by the mind. One's mind and speech should be governed with the help of wisdomn.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: प्रणयं प्रतिसंहृत्य संस्तुतेष्वितरेषु च। विचरेदसमुन्नद्धः स सुखी स च पण्डितः॥
en: Renouncing love and affection for persons that are known as well as for those that are unknown, one should act with humility. Such a person is said to be endued with wisdom, and such a one surely finds happiness.

description: Narada preaches the importance of Yoga and knowledge of Self
sn: अध्यात्मरतिरासीनो निरपेक्षो निरामिषः। आत्मनैव सहायेन यश्चरेत् स सुखी भवेत्॥
en: That man who is pleased with his own Soul, who is given to Yoga, who depends upon nothing out of self, who is without cupidity, and who acts without the help of anything but his self, succeeds in acquiring happiness.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: नारद उवाच सुखदुः दुःखविपर्यासो यदा समनुपद्यते। नैनं प्रज्ञा सुनीतं वा त्रायते नापि पौरुषम्॥
en: Narada said When the changes of happiness and sorrow appear or disappear, they cannot be prevented by either wisdom or policy or exertion.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: स्वभावाद् यलमातिष्ठेद् यत्नवान् नावसीदति। जरामरणरोगेभ्यः प्रियमात्मानमुद्धरेत्॥
en: Without suffering himself to deviate from his true nature, one should try his best for protecting his own Self. He who makes such care and exertion, has never to to perish. Considering Self as something dear, one should always try to rescue himself from decrepitude death, and disease.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: रुजन्ति हि शरीराणि रोगाः शारीरमानसाः। सायका इव तीक्ष्णाग्राः प्रयुक्ता दृढधन्विभिः॥
en: Metal and physical ailments afflict the body, like keen-pointed arrows discharged from the bow by a strong bowman.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: व्यथितस्य विधित्साभिस्ताम्यतो जीवितैषिणः। अवशस्य विनाशाय शरीरमपकृष्यते॥
en: The body of a person who is tortured by thirst, who is moved by agony, who is perfectly helpless, and that is desirous of prolonging his life, is dragged towards destruction.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: स्रवन्ति न निवर्तन्ते स्रोतांसि सरितामिव। आयुरादाय मर्त्यानां राज्यहानि पुनः पुनः॥
en: Days and nights are continually running, carrying away in their current the periods of life of all human beings. Like currents of rivers, these flow ceaselessly without ever returning.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: व्यत्ययो ह्ययमत्यन्तं पक्षयोः शुक्लकृष्णयोः। जातान् माजरयति निमेषान् नावतिष्ठते॥
en: The continued succession of the lighted and the dark fortnights is destroyed all mortal creatures without stopping for even a moment in this work.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: सुखदुःखानि भूतानामजरो जरयत्यसौ। आदित्यो ह्यस्तमभ्येति पुनः पुनरुदेति च॥
en: Rising and setting day after day, the Sun, who is himself undecaying, is perpetually coO king the joys and sorrows of all men.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: अदृष्टपूर्वानादाय भावानपरिशङ्कितान्। इष्टानिष्टान् मनुष्याणामस्तं गच्छन्ति रात्रयः॥
en: The nights are continually going away, taking with them the good and bad incidents that befall man, that depend on destiny, and that are unexpected by him.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: योऽयमिच्छेद् यथाकामं कामानां तदवाप्नुयात्। यदि स्यान्न पराधीनं पुरुषस्य क्रियाफलम्॥
en: If the fruits of men's deeds were not dependent on other circumstances, then one would acquire whatever object he would long for.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: संयताश्च हि दक्षाश्च मतिमन्तश्च मानवाः। दृश्यन्ते निष्फलाः संतः प्रहीणाः सर्वकर्मभिः॥
en: Even men of controlled senses, of cleverness, and of intelligence, if destitute of acts, never succeed in acquiring any fruits.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: अपरे बालिशा: सन्तो निर्गुणाः पुरुषाधमाः। आशीभिरप्यसंयुक्ता दृश्यन्ते सर्वकामिनः॥
en: Other, though shorn of intelligence and accomplishments of any sort, and who are really the lowest of men, are seen, even when they do not wish for success, to be crowned with the fruition of all their desires.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: भूतानामपरः कश्चिद्धिंसायां सततोत्थितः। वञ्चनायां च लोकस्य स सुखेष्वेव जीर्यते॥
en: Some one else, who is always ready to injure all creatures, and who is engaged in imposing on all the world, is seen to languish in happiness.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: अचेष्टमानमासीनं श्री: कञ्चिदुपतिष्ठते। कश्चित् कर्मानुसृत्यान्यो न प्राप्यमधिगच्छति॥
en: Some one who sits idly, acquires great prosperity; while another, by working earnestly, is seen to miss desirable fruits almost within his reach.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: अपराधं समाचक्ष्व पुरुषस्य स्वभावतः। शुक्रमन्यत्र सम्भूतं पुनरन्यत्र गच्छति॥
en: Do you ascribe it as one of the faults of man! The seminal fluid, originating in one's nature from sight of one person, goes to another person.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: तस्य योनौ प्रयुक्तस्य गर्भो भवति वा न वा। आम्रपुष्पोपमा यस्य निवृत्तिरुपलभ्यते॥
en: When given to the womb, it sometimes produces an embryo and sometimes fails. When sexual intercourse fails, it resembles a mango tree that puts forth a great many flowers without, however, producing a single fruit.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: केषाञ्चित् पुत्रकामानामनुसंतानमिच्छताम्। सिद्धौ प्रयतमानानां न चाण्डमुपजायते॥
en: As regards some men who are desirous of having offspring and who, for the fruition of their object, work earnestly, they fail to procreate an embryo in the womb.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: गर्भाच्चोद्विजमानानां क्रुद्धादाशीविषादिव। आयुष्माजायते पुत्रः कथं प्रेत इवाभवत्॥
en: Some person, again, who fears the birth of an embryo as one fears a snake of deadly poison, finds, a long-lived son born to him and sources who seems to be his own self return to the stages through which he has passed.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: देवानिष्ट्वा तपस्तप्त्वा कृपणैः पुत्रगृद्धिभिः। दश मासान् परिधृता जायन्ते कुलपांसनाः॥
en: Many persons with strong desire for children, and cheerless on that account, after sacrificing to many gods and practising severe austerities, at last beget children, duly borne for ten long months, that prove to be veritable wretches of their race.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: अपरे धनधान्यानि भोगांश्च पितृसंचितान्। विपुलानभिजायन्ते लब्धास्तैरेव मङ्गलैः॥
en: Others, who have been obtained by virtue of such blessed rites and observances, at once acquires riches and grain and various other of enjoyment acquired and accumulated by their fore fathers.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: अन्योन्यं समभिप्रेत्य मैथुनस्य समागमे। उपद्रव इवाविष्टो योनि गर्भः प्रपद्यते॥
en: In an act of sexual intercourse, when two persons of opposite sexes come into contact with one another, the embryo takes birth in the womb, like a calamity attacking the mother.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: शीघ्रं परशरीराणि च्छिन्नबीजं शरीरिणम्। प्राणिनं प्राणसंरोधे मांस.श्लेष्मविवेष्टितम्॥
en: Very soon after suspension of the vital airs, other physical forms possess that embodied creature whose gross body has been destroyed but whose deeds have all been performed with that gross body, made of flesh and phlegm.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: निर्दग्धं परदेहेऽपि परदेहं चलाचलम्। विनश्यन्तं विनाशान्ते नावि नावमिवाहितम्॥
en: Upon the destruction of the body, another body which is as much destructible as the one which is destroyed, is kept ready for the burnt and destroyed creature even as one boat goes to another for transferring to itself the passengers of the other.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: सङ्गत्या जठरे न्यस्तं रेतोबिन्दुमचेतनम्। केन यत्नेन जीवन्तं गर्भ त्वमिह पश्यसि॥
en: By sexual intercourse, a drop of the seminal fluid that is inanimate, is cast into the womb. I ask you, through whose or what care is the embryo kept alive?

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: अन्नपानानि जीर्यन्ते यत्र भक्षाश्च भक्षिताः। तस्मिन्नेवोदरे गर्भ: किं नान्नमिव जीर्यते॥
en: That part of the body into which the food that is eaten goes and where it is digested, is the place where the embryo lives, but it is not disgested there.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: गर्भे मूत्रपुरीषाणां स्वभावनियता गतिः। धारणे वा विसर्गे वा न कर्ता विद्यते वशः॥
en: In the womb, amid urine and faeces, one's sojourn is governed by Nature. The born creature is not free in the matter or residence therein or escape therefrom. In fact, in these respects, he is perfectly helpless.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: स्रवन्ति हुंदराद् गर्भा जायमानास्तथा परे। आगमेन तथान्येषां विनाश उपपद्यते॥
en: Some embryos fall from the womb. Some come out alive. While as regards some, they are destroyed in the womb, after being quickened with life, on account of some other bodies being ready for them.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: एतस्माद् योनिसम्बन्धाद् यो जीवन् परिमुच्यते। प्रजां च लभते काञ्चित् पुनर्द्वन्द्वेषु सज्जति॥
en: That man who, in an act of sexual intercourse, injects the seminal fluid, obtains from it a son or daughter. The offspring thus obtained, when the time comes, takes part in a similar act of sexual intercourse.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: स तस्य सहजातस्य सप्तमी नवमीं दशाम्। प्राप्नुवन्ति ततः पञ्च न भवन्ति गतायुषः॥
en: When the lease of a person's life ends, the five primal elements of his body attain to the seventh and the ninth stages and they cease to be. The person, however, suffers no change.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: नाभ्युत्थाने मनुष्याणां योगाः स्युर्नात्र संशयः। व्याधिभिश्च विमथ्यन्ते व्याधैः क्षुद्रमृगा इव॥
en: Forsooth, when persons are attacked by diseases as little animals assailed by hunters, they then lose the power of rising up and moving about.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: व्याधिभिर्मथ्यमानानां त्यजतां विपुलं धनम्। वेदनां नापकर्षन्ति यतमानाश्चिकित्सकाः॥
en: If when men are attacked by diseases, they wish to spend even immense riches, physicians with their best efforts fail to lessen their sufferings.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: ते चातिनिपुणा वैद्याः कुशलाः सम्भृतौषधाः। व्याधिभिः परिकृष्यन्ते मृगा व्याधैरिवार्दिताः॥
en: Even physicians, who are well-skilled and expert in their science and well-equipt with excellent medicines, are themselves attacked by disease like animals assailed by hunters.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: ते पिबन्तः कषायांश्च सपौषि विविधानि च। दृश्यन्ते जरया भग्ना नगा नागैरिवोत्तमैः॥
en: Even if men drink many astringents and various sorts of medicated ghee, they are seen to be broken by decrepitude like trees by strong elephants.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: के वा भुवि चिकित्सन्ते रोगार्तान् मृगपक्षिणः। श्वापदानि दरिद्रांश्च प्रायो नार्ता भवन्ति ते॥
en: When animals and birds and beasts of prey and poor men are attacked by diseases, who treats them with medicines? Indeed, these are not seen to be ill.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: घोरानपि दुराधर्षान् नृपतीनुग्रतेजसः। आक्रम्याददते रोगाः पशून् पशुगणा इव॥
en: Like larger animals attacking smaller ones, diseases are seen to attack even dreadful kings of fierce energy and invincible prowess.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: इति लोकमनाक्रन्दं मोहशोकपरिप्लुतम्। स्रोतसा सहसाऽऽक्षिप्तं ह्रियमाणं बलीयसा॥
en: All men, deprived of the power of even uttering cries of pain, and overwhelmed by error and grief, are seen to be carried away along the dreadful current into which they have been thrown.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: न धनेन न राज्येन नोग्रेण तपसा तथा। स्वभावमतिवर्तन्ते ये नियुक्ताः शरीरिणः॥
en: Embodied creatures, even when trying to conquer it with the help of wealth, of sovereign power, or of the austerest penances. men

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: न म्रियेरन् न जीर्येरन् सर्वे स्युः सर्वकामिनः। नाप्रियं प्रति पश्येयुरुत्थानस्य फले सति॥
en: If all attempts men make were successful then men would never die, would never be subject to decrepitude, would never meet with any disagreeable thing, and lastly would have all their wishes fructified.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: उपर्युपरि लोकस्य सर्वो गन्तुं समीहते। यतते च यथाशक्ति न च तद् वर्तते तथा॥
en: All desire to acquire gradual superiority of position. To satisfy this wish they try their very best. The result however, does not agree with their wish.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तांश्च मत्तान् मद्यमदेन च। अप्रमत्ताः शठाञ्छूरा विक्रान्ताः पर्युपासते॥
en: Even men who are perfectly careful, who are honest, and brave and endued with prowess, are seen to worship men intoxicated with the pride of wealth and with even alcoholic stimulants.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: क्लेशाः परिनिवर्तन्ते केषाञ्चिदसमीक्षिताः। स्वं स्वं च पुनरन्येषां न किंचिदधिगम्यते।॥
en: Some men are seen whose calamities vanish before even these are seen by them. Others there are who are seen to possess no riches but who are free from misery of every sort.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: महच्च फलवैषम्यं दृश्यते कर्मसंधिषु। वहन्ति शिबिकामन्ये यान्त्यन्ये शिबिकागताः॥
en: A great disparity is seen about the fruits that wait upon conjunctions of acts. Some are seen to carry vehicles on their shoulders, while some are seen to ride on them.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: सर्वेषामृद्धिकामानामन्ये रथपुरःसुराः। मनुष्याश्च गतस्त्रीकाः शतशो विविधस्त्रियः॥
en: All men desirous of riches and prosperity. A few only have cars dragged in their processions. Some there are who cannot get a single wife when their first married ones are dead; while others have hundreds of wives.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: द्वन्द्वारामेषु भूतेषु गच्छन्त्येकैकशो नराः। इदमन्यत् पदं पश्य मात्र मोहं करिष्यसि॥
en: are Misery and happiness are the two things which exist side by side. Men have either misery or happiness. See this is a subject of wonder! Do you, however, allow yourself to be stupefied by error at such a sight.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: त्यज धर्ममधर्मं च उभे सत्यानृते त्यज। उभे सत्यानृते त्यक्त्वा येन त्यजसि तं त्यज॥
en: Renounce both virtue and sin! Renounce also truth and falsehood! Having renounced both truth and falsehood, do you then cast off that with whose help you shall cast off the former.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: एतत् ते परमं गुह्यमाख्यातमृषिसत्तम। येन देवाः परित्यज्य मर्त्यलोकं दिवं गताः॥
en: O best of Rishis, I have now told you what is a great mystery! With the help of such instructions, the gods succeeded in leaving the Earth for becoming dwellers of heaven.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शुकः परमबुद्धिमान्। संचिन्त्य मनसा धीरो निश्चयं नाध्यगच्छत॥
en: Hearing these words of Narada, Shuka, gifted with great intelligence and possessed of tranquillity of mind, reflected upon the drift of the instructions he received, but could not deterinine any thing.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: पुत्रदारैर्महान् क्लेशो विद्याम्नाये महाञ्च्छ्रमः। किं नु स्याच्छाश्वतं स्थानमल्पक्लेशं महोदयम्॥
en: He understood that one suffers great misery on account of children and wives; that one has to work hard for the acquisition of science and Vedic lore. He, therefore, asked himself, saying,-What is that situation which is eternal and which is free from all sorts of misery but in which there is great prosperity?

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: ततो मुहूर्तं संचिन्त्य निश्चितां गतिमात्मनः। परावरज्ञो धर्मस्य परां नैःश्रेयसी गतिम्॥
en: Thinking for a moment upon the course ordained for him, Shuka, who was well acquainted with the beginning and the end of all duties, determined to attain to the highest end which is full of happiness.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: कथं त्वहमसंश्लिष्टो गच्छेयं गतिमुत्तमाम्। नावर्तेयं यथा भूयो योनिसंकरसागरे॥
en: He questioned himself, saying,-How shall I, cutting off all attachments and becoming perfectly free, acquire that excellent end? How, indeed, shall I acquire that excellent situation whence there is no return into the ocean of various sorts of birth.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: परं भावं हि काङ्क्षामि यत्र नावर्तते पुनः। सर्वसङ्गान् परित्यज्य निश्चितो मनसा गतिम्॥
en: I wish to come by that condition of existence whence there is no return! Renouncing all kinds of attachments, arrived at certainty by mental retrospection, I shall acquire that end.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: तत्र यास्यामि यत्रात्मा शमं मेऽधिगमिष्यति। अक्षयश्चाव्ययश्चैव यत्र स्थास्यामि शाश्वतः॥
en: I shall acquire that situation in which your Soul will have tranquillity, and when I shall be able to live for good without being subject to decrepitude or change.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: न तु योगमृते शक्या प्राप्तुं सा परमा गतिः। अवबन्धो हि बुद्धस्य कर्मभिर्नोपपद्यते॥
en: It is, however, certain that that high end cannot be acquired without the help of Yoga. One who has acquired the state of perfect knowledge and enlightenment never comes by low attachments through deeds.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: तस्माद् योगं समास्थाय त्यक्त्वा गृहकलेवरम्। वायुभूतः प्रवेक्ष्यामि तेजोराशिं दिवाकरम्॥
en: I shall, therefore, have recourse to Yoga, and renouncing this body which is my present residence, I shall change myself into a wind and enter that mass of effulgence which is represented by the sin.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: न ह्येष क्षयतां याति सोमः सुरगणैर्यथा। कम्पितः पतते भूमिं पुनश्चैवाधिरोहति॥
en: When Individual Soul enters that mass of effulgence, he no longer suffers like Soma who, with the gods, upon the exhaustion of merit, drops down on the Earth and having once more acquired sufficient merit returns to heaven.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: क्षीयते हि सदा सोमः पुनश्चैवाभिपूर्यते। नेच्छाम्येवं विदित्वैते ह्रासवृद्धी पुनः पुनः॥
en: The Moon is always seen to decrease and once more increase. Seeing this decrease and increase that go on repeatedly, I do not wish to have a form of existence in which there are such changes.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: रविस्तु संतापयते लोकान् रश्मिभिरुल्बणैः। सर्वतस्तेज आदत्ते नित्यमक्षयमण्डलः॥ अतो मे रोचते गन्तुमादित्यं दीप्ततेजसम्।
en: The Sun warms all the worlds by means of his rays. His disc never suffers any diminution. Remaining unchanged, he drinks energy from all things. Hence, I wish to go into the Sun of blazing effulgence.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: अत्र वत्स्यामि दुर्धर्षो निःशङ्केनान्तरात्मना॥ सूर्यस्य सदने चाहं निक्षिप्येदं कलेवरम्।
en: There I shall live, invincible by all, and in my inner soul freed from all fear, having renounced this body of mine in the solar region.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: ऋषिभिः सह यास्यामि सौरं तेजोऽतिदुःसहम्॥ आपृच्छामि नगान् नागान् गिरिमुर्वी दिशो दिवम्। देवदानवगन्धर्वान् पिशाचोरगराक्षसान्॥। लोकेषु सर्वभूतानि प्रवेक्ष्यामि न संशयः।
en: I shall enter with the great Rishis the unbearable energy of the Sun, I declare to all creatures, these trees, these elephants, these mountains, the Earth herself, the several cardinal points, the sky, the gods, the Danavas, the Gandharvas, the Pishachas, Uragas, and the Rakshasas, that I shall enter all creatures in the world.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: पश्यन्तु योगवीर्यं मे सर्वे देवाः सहर्षािभिः॥६ अथानुज्ञाप्य तमृर्षि नारदं लोकविश्रुतम्।
en: Let all the gods with the Rishis, witness my Yoga power to-day.-Having said these words, Shuka, informed the illustrious Narada of his intention.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: तस्मादनुज्ञां सम्प्राप्य जगाम पितरं प्रति॥ सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं कृष्णद्वैपायनं मुनिम्। शुकः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा कृष्णमापृष्टवान् मुनिम्॥
en: Obtaining Narada's permission, Shuka then went to where his father was. Arrived before him, the great Muni, viz., the great and Islandborn Krishna, Shuka circumambulated him and addressed him the usual enquiries.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: श्रुत्वा चर्षिस्तद् वचनं शुकस्य प्रीतो महात्मा पुनराह चैनम्। भो भो पुत्र स्थीयतां तावदद्य यावच्चक्षुः प्रीणयामि त्वदर्थे॥
en: Hearing of Shuka's intention, the great Rishi became highly pleased. Addressing him the great Rishi said,-0 son, O dear son, do you stay here to-day so that I may see you for some time for gratifying my eyes.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: निरपेक्षः शुको भूत्वा नि:स्नेहो मुक्तसंशयः। मोक्षमेवानुसंचिन्त्य गमनाय मनो दधे॥
en: Shuka, however, paid no heed to that request. Freed from affection and all doubt, he began to think only of Liberation, and set his heart on the journey.

description: The eternal situation free from sorrows. Suka leaves his house
sn: पितरं सम्परित्यज्य जगाम मुनिसत्तमः। कैलासपृष्ठं विपुलं सिद्धसंघनिषेवितम्॥
en: Leaving his father, that foremost of Rishis then went to the spacious breast, of Kailasa which was inhabited by numbers of ascetics crowned with success.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: भीष्म उवाच गिरिशृङ्ग समारुह्य सुतो व्यासस्य भारत। समे देशे विविक्ते स निःशलाक उपाविशत्॥
en: Bhishma said. Having got upon the summit of the mountain, O Bharata, the son of Vyasa sat down upon a level place free from blades of grass and secluded.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: धारयामास चात्मानं यथाशास्त्रं यथाविधि। पादप्रभृतिगात्रेषु क्रमेण क्रमयोगवित्॥
en: According to the direction of the scriptures and to the ordinances laid down, that ascetic, who knew the successive processes of Yoga, held his soul first in one place and then in another, beginning from his feet and proceeding through all the limbs.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: ततः स प्राङ्मुखो विद्वानादित्ये नचिरोदिते। पाणिपादं समादाय विनीतवदुपाविशत्॥
en: Then when the Sun, had not risen long, Shuka sat, with his face turned towards the East, and hands and feet drawn in an humble posture.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: न तत्र पक्षिसंघातो न शब्दो नातिदर्शनम्। यत्र वैयासकिधीमान् योक्तुं समुपचक्रमे॥
en: In that spot where the intelligent son of Vyasa sat prepared to practise Yoga, there were no flocks of birds, no sound, and no sight that was repulsive or fearful.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: स ददर्श तदाऽऽत्मानं सर्वसंगविनिःसृतम्। प्रजहास ततो हासं शुकः सम्प्रेक्ष्य तत्परम्॥
en: He then saw his own Soul freed from all attachments. Seeing that highest of all things, he laughed in joy.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: स पुनर्योगमास्थाय मोक्षमार्गोपलब्धये। महायोगेश्वरो भूत्वा सोऽत्यकामद् विहायसम्॥
en: He once more set himself to Yoga for acquiring the path of Liberation. Becoming the great master of Yoga he got over the element of ether.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: ततः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा देवर्षि नारदं ततः। निवेदयामास च तं स्वं योगं परमर्षये।॥
en: He then went round the celestial Rishi Naradas, and informed him of the fact of his having begun to practise the highest Yoga.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: शुक उवाच दृष्टो मार्गः प्रवृत्तोऽस्मि स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु तपोधन। त्वत्प्रसादाद् गमिष्यामि गतिमिष्टां महाद्युते॥
en: I have succeeded in seeing the path (of Emancipation). I have addressed myself to it. Blessed be you, O you having penances for your wealth. I shall through your favour, O you of great splendour, acquire an end that is highly desirable.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: नारदेनाभ्यनुज्ञात: शुको द्वैपायनात्मजः। अभिवाद्य पुनर्योगमास्थायाकाशमाविशत्॥
en: Bhishma said Having received the order of Naradas, Shuka the son of the Island-born Vyasa saluted the celestial Rishi and once more set himself to Yoga and entered the element of ether.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: कैलासपृष्ठादुत्पत्य स पपात दिवं तदा। अन्तरिक्षचरः श्रीमान् वायुभूतः सुनिश्चितः॥
en: Ascending then from the breast of the Kailasa mountain, he soared into the sky. Capable of passing through the sky, the blessed Shuka of fixed conclusion, then made himself at one with the element of Wind.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: तमुद्यन्तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं वैनतेयसमद्युतिम्। ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि मनोमारुतरंहसम्॥
en: As that foremost of twice-born ones, effulgent like Garuda, was passing through the skies with the speed of the wind or thought, all creatures directed their eyes towards him.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: व्यवसायेन लोकांस्त्रीन् सर्वान् सोऽथ विचिन्तयन्। आस्थितो दीर्घमध्वानं पावकार्कसमप्रभः॥
en: Gifted with the splendour of fire or the Sun, Shuka then considered the three worlds as one Brahma, and went along that lengthy path.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: तमेकमनसं यान्तमव्यग्रमकुतोभयम्। ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि जङ्गमानि चराणि च॥
en: Indeed, all creatures, mobile and immobile, cast their eyes upon him as he went with rapt attention, and a tranquil and fearless soul.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: यथाशक्ति यथान्यायं पूजां वै चक्रिरे तदा। पुष्पवर्षेच दिव्यैस्तमवचक्रुर्दिवौकसः॥
en: All creatures, according to the ordinance and according to their power, adored him with respect. The celestials poured showers of celestial flowers upon him.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मिताः सर्वे गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः। ऋषयश्चैव संसिद्धाः परं विस्मयमागताः।१५॥
en: Seeing hiin, all the tribes of Apsaras and Gandharvas became filled with wonder. The Rishis also, that were crowned with success, became equally surprised.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: अन्तरिक्षगतः कोऽयं तपसा सिद्धिमागतः। अध:कायोर्ध्ववक्त्रश्च नेत्रैः समभिरज्यते॥
en: And they asked themselves,Who is this one who has acquired success by his penances? With looks withdrawn from his own body but turned upwards, he is delighting us all with his glances.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: ततः परमधर्मात्मा त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः। भास्करं समुदीक्षन् स प्राङ्मुखो वाग्यतोऽगमत्॥ शब्देनाकाशमखिलं पूरयन्निव सर्वशः।
en: Of highly righteous soul and celebrated throughout the three worlds, Shuka went silently, his face turned towards the East and look directed towards the Sun. As he went, along he seemed to fill the entire sky with an all-pervading noise.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा दृष्ट्वा सर्वाप्सरोगणाः॥ सम्भ्रान्तमनसो राजन्नासन् परमविस्मिताः।
en: Seeing him coming in that way, all the tribes of the Apsaras, struck with fear O king, became filled with surprise. Heáeçet[eDeYerle-ees Ye=MeceglHeÂguueesdeveeim~19~~

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: दैवतं कतमं ह्येतदुत्तमां गतिमास्थितम्। सुनिश्चितमिहायाति विमुक्तमिव निःस्पृहम्॥
en: Headed by Panchachuda and others, they looked at Shuka with eyes expanded by surprise. And they asked one one another, saying,-What god is this one who has acquired such a high end? Forsooth, he comes here, freed from all attachments and desire.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: ततः समभिचक्राम मलयं नाम पर्वतम्। उर्वशी पूर्वचित्तिश्च यं नित्यमुपसेवतः॥
en: Shuka then went to the Malaya mountains where Urvashi and Purvachitti used to always live.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: तस्य ब्रह्मर्षि पुत्रस्य विस्मयं ययतुः परम्। अहो बुद्धिसमाधानं वेदाभ्यासरते द्विजे॥ अचिरेणैव कालेन नभश्चरति चन्द्रवत्। पितृशुश्रूषया बुद्धिं सम्प्राप्तोऽयमनुत्तमाम्॥
en: Both of them, seeing the energy of the son of the great twice-born Rishi, became filled with wonder. And they said,-Wonderful is this concentration of attention of a twice-born youth who was accustomed to the recitation and study of the Vedas! Soon will he pass through the entire sky like the Moon. It was by dutiful service and humble ministrations towards his father that he gained this excellent understanding.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: पितृभक्तो दृढतपा: पितुः सुदयितः सुतः। अनन्यमनसा तेन कथं पित्रा विसर्जितः॥
en: He is firmly devoted his father, endued with austere penances, and is very much loved by his father. Alas, why has he been dismissed by his inattentive father to go along a way whence no one returns.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: उर्वश्या वचनं श्रुत्वा शुकः परमधर्मवित्। उदैक्षत दिशः सर्वा वचने गतमानसः॥ सोऽन्तरिक्षं महीं चैव सशैलवनकाननाम्। विलोकयामास तदा सरांसि सरितस्तथा।॥
en: Hearing these words of Urvashi, and attending to their meaning, Shuk:a, that foremost of all persons conversant with duties, looked on all sides, and once more saw the entire sky, the whole Earth with her mountains and waters and forests, and also all the lakes and rivers.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: ततो द्वैपायनसुतं बहुमानात् समन्ततः। कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वा निरीक्षन्ते स्म देवताः॥
en: All the gods also, of both sexes, joining their hands, paid respect to the son of Island bonr Rishi and looked act him with wonder and reverence.

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: अब्रवीत् तास्तदा वाक्यं शुकः परमधर्मवित्। पिता यद्यनुगच्छेन्मां क्रोशमानः शुकेति वै॥ ततः प्रतिवचो देयं सवेरेव समाहितः। एतन्मे स्नेहतः सर्वे वचनं कर्तुमर्हथ॥
en: Shuka, addressing all of them, that foremost of all pious men, said these words-If my father follow me and repeatedly call after me by my name, do all of you in a body return him an answer for me. Moved by the affection all of you have for me, do you satisfy this request of mine!

description: The practice of yoga by Suka
sn: शुकस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा दिशः सर्वाः सकाननाः। समुद्राः सरितः शैलाः प्रत्यूचुस्तं समन्ततः॥ यथाऽऽज्ञापयसे विप्र बाढमेवं भविष्यति। ऋषेळहरतो वाक्यं प्रतिवक्ष्यामहे वयम्॥
en: Hearing these words of Shuka, all the points of the horizon, all the forests, all the seas, all the rivers, and all the mountains answered him from all sides, saying,.-We accept your command, O twice-born one! It shall be as you say! It is thus that we answer the words spoken by the Rishi.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं ब्रह्मर्षिः सुमहातपाः। प्रातिष्ठत शुकः सिद्धिं हित्वा दोषांश्चतुर्विधान्॥
en: Bhishma said “Having spoken in this way, the twice-born Rishi of austere penances, viz., Shuka, lived on his success, renouncing the four sorts of faults.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: तमो हृष्टविधं हित्वा जहौ पञ्चविधं रजः। ततः सत्त्वं जहौ धीमांस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Renouncing also the eight kinds of Tamas, he dismissed the five kinds of Rajas. Gifted with great intelligence, he the renounced the attribute of Sattva. All this seemed extremely wonderful.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: ततस्तस्मिन् पदे नित्ये निर्गुणे लिङ्गवर्जिते। ब्रह्मणि प्रत्यतिष्ठत् स विधूमोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन्॥
en: He then lived in that eternal station which is shorn of attributes, freed from every indication, that is, in Brahma, shining like a smokeless fire.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: उल्कापाता दिशा दाहो भूमिकम्पस्तथैव च। प्रादुर्भूतः क्षणे तस्मिंस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Meteors began to shoot. The points of the horizon seemed to be ablaze. The Earth trembled. All these phenomena seemed extremely wonderful.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: दुमाः शाखाश्च मुमुचुः शिखराणि च पर्वताः। निर्घातशब्दैश्च गिरिहिमवान् दीर्यतीव ह॥
en: The trees began to throw off their branches and the mountains their summits. Loud peals were heard that seemed to rive the Himavat mountains.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: न बभासे सहस्रांशुर्न जज्वाल च पावकः। ह्रदाश्च सरितश्चैव चुक्षुभुः सागरास्तथा॥
en: The Sun seemed at that moment to be shorn of effulgence. Fire refused to burn forth. The lakes and rivers and seas were all moved.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: ववर्ष वासवस्तोयं रसवच्च सुगन्धि च। ववौ समीरणश्चापि दिव्यगन्धवहः शुचिः॥
en: Vasava poured showers of rain of excellent taste and smell. A pure breeze began to blow, carrying excellent taste and smell. A pure breeze began to blow, carrying excellent perfumes.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: स शृङ्गे प्रथमे दिव्ये हिमवन्मेरुसम्भवे। संश्लिष्टे श्वेतपीते द्वे रुक्मरूप्यमये शुभे॥
en: Shuka, as he went through the sky, saw two beautiful summits, one belonging to Himavat and another to Meru. These were side by side with each other. One of them was made of gold and was, therefore, yellow; the other was white, being made of silver.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: शतयोजनविस्तारे तिर्यगूर्वं च भारत। उदीची दिशमास्थाय रुचिरे संददर्श ह॥
en: Each of them, O Bharata, was a hundred Yojanas in height and of the same breath. Indeed, as Shuka went towards the north, he beheld those two beautiful summits,

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: सोऽविशङ्केन मनसा तदैवाभ्यपतच्छुकः। ततः पर्वतशृङ्गे द्वे सहसैव द्विधाकृते॥
en: With a fearless heart he dashed against those two summits that were close to each other. Unable to bear the force, the summits were suddenly rent in two parts.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: अदृश्येतां महाराज तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्। ततः पर्वत शृङ्गाभ्यां सहसैव विनिःसृतः॥ न च प्रतिजघानास्य स गति पर्वतोत्तमः। ततो महानभूच्छब्दो दिवि सर्वदिवौकसाम्॥
en: The spectacle, O monarch, was extremely wonderful to look at. Shuka pierced through those summits, for they were unable to stop his onward course. At this a loud noise was made in heaven by the dwellers thereof.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: गन्धर्वाणामृषीणां च ये च शैलनिवासिनः। दृष्ट्वा शुकमतिक्रान्तं पर्वतं च द्विधाकृतम्॥ साधु साध्विति तत्रासीन्नादः सर्वत्र भारत।
en: The Gandharvas and the Rishis also and others who lived in that mountain sent up loud cheers at the sight of the mountain being rent in two and Shuka passing through it. Indeed, O Bharata, a loud noise was heard everywhere at that moment, saying,-Excellent, Excellent.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: स पूज्यमानो देवैश्च गन्धर्वैर्ऋषिभिस्तथा।॥ यक्षराक्षससंघेश्च विद्याधरगणैस्तथा।
en: He was worshipped by the Gandharvas and the Rishis, by Yakhas and Rakshasas, and by all tribes of the Vidyadharas.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: दिव्यैः पुष्पैः समाकीर्णमन्तरिक्षं समन्ततः॥ आसीत् किल महाराज शुकाभितपने तदा।
en: The entire sky became covered with celestial flowers showered from heaven at that moment when Shuka thus cut through that impenetrable barrier, O king.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: ततो मन्दाकिनी रम्यामुपरिष्टादभिव्रजन्॥ शुको ददर्श धर्मात्मा पुष्पितदुमकाननाम्।
en: The pious Shuka then saw from a high region the extremely beautiful celestial river Mandakini, running below through a region adorned by many flowering groves and forests.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: तस्यां क्रीडन्त्यभिरतास्ते चैवाप्सरसां गणाः॥ शून्याकारं निराकाराः शुकं दृष्ट्वा विवाससः।
en: In these waters many beautiful Apsaras were playing. Seeing Shuka who was bodiless, those naked aerial beings felt no shame.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: तं प्रक्रामन्तमाज्ञाय पिता स्नेहसमन्वितः॥ उत्तमा गतिमास्थाय पृष्ठतोऽनुससार ह।
en: Learning that Shuka had undertaken his great journey, his father Vyasa, filled with affection, followed him behind along the same aerial path.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: शुकस्तु मारुतादूर्ध्वं गति कृत्वान्तरिक्षगाम्॥ दर्शयित्वा प्रभावं स्वं ब्रह्मभूतोऽभवत् तदा।
en: Meanwhile Shuka, passing through thai region of the sky which is above the region of the wind, showed his Yoga-power and identified himself with Brahma.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: महायोगगतिं त्वन्यां व्यासोत्थाय महातपाः॥ निमेषान्तरमात्रेण शुकाभिपतनं ययौ।
en: Following the subtile path of high Yoga, Vyasa of austere penances, reached within the twinkling of the eye that place whence Shuka first started.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: स ददर्श द्विधा कृत्वा पर्वताग्रं शुकं गतम्॥ शशंसुर्ऋषयस्तत्र कर्म पुत्रस्य तत् तदा।
en: Proceeding along the same way, Vyasa saw the mountain summit rent in two parts and through which Shuka has passed. Meeting the Island-born ascetic, the Rishis began to describe to him the achievements of his own.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: ततः शुकेति दीर्पण शब्देनाक्रन्दितस्तदा॥ स्वयं पित्रा स्वरेणोच्चैस्त्रील्लोकाननुनाद्य वै।
en: Vyasa, however, began to lament, loudly naming his son and causing the three worlds to resound with the noise he made.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: शुकः सर्वगतो भूत्वा सर्वात्मा सर्वतोमुखः। :॥ प्रत्यभाषत धर्मात्मा भो शब्देनानुनादयन्।
en: Meanwhile, the pious Shuka, who had entered all things, had become the soul of all things, and had acquired omnipresence, answered his fathers by uttering the monosyllable BHO in the form of an echo.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: तत एकाक्षरं नादं भोरित्येव समीरयन्॥ प्रत्याहरज्जगत् सर्वमुच्चैः स्थावरजङ्गमम्।
en: Thereat, the entire universe of mobile and immobile creatures, uttering the monosyllable BHO, echoed the answer of Shuka.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: ततः प्रभृति चाद्यापि शब्दानुच्चारितान् पृथक्॥ गिरिगह्वरपृष्ठेषु व्याहरन्ति शुकं प्रति।
en: Thereforward, when sounds are made in mountain-caves or on mountain-breasts, the latter, as if in answer to Shuka, still echo them.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: अन्तर्हितः प्रभावं तु दर्शयित्वा शुकस्तदा॥ गुणान् संत्यज्य शब्दादीन् पदमभ्यगमत् परम्।
en: Having renounced all the attributes of sound, etc., and showing his Yoga-power in the manner of his disappearance, Shuka in this way acquired the highest station.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: महिमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा पुत्रस्यामिततेजसः॥ निषसाद गिरिप्रस्थे पुत्रमेवानुचिन्तयन्।
en: Seeing that glory and power of his son of immeasurable energy, Vyasa sat down on the breast of the mountain and began to think of his son sorrowfully.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरे क्रीडन्तोऽप्सरसां गणाः॥ आसाद्य तमृषि सर्वाः सम्भ्रान्ता गतचेतसः।
en: Seeing the Rishi seated there, the Apsaras who were sporting on the banks of the celestial river Mandakini, became all moved with shame and dispirited.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: जले निलिल्यिरे काश्चित् काश्चिद् गुल्मान् प्रपेदिरे।।२९ वसनान्याददुः काश्चित् तं दृष्ट्वा मुनिसत्तमम्।
en: Some of them, to hide their nakedness, plunged into the river, and some entered the groves hard by, and some quickly took up their clothes, at seeing the Rishi.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: तां मुक्ततां तु विज्ञाय मुनिः पुत्रस्य वै तदा।॥ सक्ततामात्मनश्चैव प्रीतोऽभूद् व्रीडितश्च ह॥
en: Seeing these movements, the Rishi understood that his son had been liberated from all attachments, but that he himself was not freed therefrom. At this he became filled with both joy and shame.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: तं देवगन्धर्ववृतो महर्षिगणपूजितः। पिनाकहस्तो भगवानभ्यागच्छत शंकरः॥
en: As Vyasa was seated there, the auspicious god Shiva, armed with trident, surrounded on all sides by many gods and Gandharvas and worshipped of all the great Rishis, came there.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: तमुवाच महादेवः सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वचः। पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तं कृष्णद्वैपायनं तदा॥
en: Consoling the Island-born Rishi who was burning with grief on account of his son, Mahadeva said these words to him

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: अग्नेर्भूमेरपां वायोरन्तरिक्षस्य चैव ह। वीर्येण सदृशः पुत्रः पुरा मत्तस्त्वया वृतः॥
en: You had formerly solicited from me a son endued with the energy of Fire, of Water, of Wind, and of Ether.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: स तथालक्षणो जातस्तपसा तव सम्भृतः। मम चैव प्रसादेन ब्रह्मतेजोमयः शुचिः॥
en: Procreated by your penances, the son that was born to you was of that very sort. Proceeding from my favour, he was pure and full of Brahma-energy.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: स गतिं परमां प्राप्तो दुष्प्रापामजितेन्द्रियैः। दैवतैरपि विप्रर्षे तं त्वं किमनुशोचसि॥
en: He has acquired the highest end-an end that is, which none can acquire who has not completely mastered his senses, nor by even any of the gods, why then, O twice-born Rishi, do you grieve for that son?

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: यावत् स्थास्यन्ति गिरयो यावत् स्थास्यन्ति सागराः। तावत् तवाक्षया कीर्तिः सपुत्रस्य भविष्यति॥
en: As long as the hills will last, as long as the ocean will last, so long will the fame of your son continue.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: छायां स्वपुत्रसदृशी सर्वतोऽनपगां सदा। द्रक्ष्यसे त्वं च लोकेऽस्मन् मत्प्रसादान्महामुने॥
en: Through my favour, O great Rishi, you will see in this world a shadowy form resembling your son, moving by the side and never leaving you for a single moment!

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: सोऽनुनीतो भगवता स्वयं रुद्रेण भारत। छायां पश्यन् समावृत्तः स मुनिः परया मुदा॥
en: Thus favoured by the illustrious Rudra himself, O Bharata, the Rishi saw a shadow of his son by his side. He came back from that place, filled with joy at this.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: इति जन्म गतिश्चैव शुकस्य भरतर्षभ। विस्तरेण समाख्याता यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: I have now told you, O chief of Bharata's race, everything regarding the birth and life of Shukra about which you had asked me.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: एतदाचष्ट मे राजन् देवर्षिर्नारदः पुरा। व्यासश्चैव महायोगी संजल्पेषु पदे पदे॥
en: The celestial Rishi Narada and the great Yogin Vyasa had again and again told all this to me in days of yore when the subject was suggested in course of conversation.

description: Suka passes through the mountain to Mandakini. Vyasa follows him. Mahadeva consoles him describing the origin of Suka
sn: इतिहासमिमं पुण्यं मोक्षधर्मोपसंहितम्। धारयेद् यः शमपरः स गच्छेत् परमां गतिम्॥
en: That person devoted to tranquillity who hears this sacred history directly connected with the subject of Liberation is sure to acquire the highest end.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच गृहस्थो ब्रह्मचारी वा वानप्रस्थोऽथ भिक्षुकः। य इच्छेत् सिद्धिमास्थातुं देवतां कां यजेत सः॥
en: If a man be a house-holder or Brahmacharin, a hermit or a mendicant, and if he wishes to acquire success, what god should he worship?

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: कुतो ह्यस्य ध्रुवः स्वर्गः कुतो नैःश्रेयसं परम्। विधिना केन जुहुयाद् दैव पित्र्यं तथैव च॥
en: Whence can he surely acquire heaven and whence that which is of the highest benefit? According to what ordinances should he perform the Homa in honour of the gods and the departed manes?

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: मुक्तश्च कां गतिं गच्छेन्मोक्षचैव किमात्मकः। स्वर्गतश्चैव किं कुर्याद् येन न च्यवते दिव॥
en: What is the end to which one goes when he becomes Liberated? What is the essence of Liberation? What should one do, so that he, having attained to heaven, would not have to drop down thence?

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: देवतानां च को देवः पितॄणां च पिता तथा। तस्मात् परतरं यच्च तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Who is the God of the gods? And who is the Pitri of the Pitris? Who is He who is superior to him who is the God of the gods and the Pitri of the Pitris? Tell me all this, O Grandfather?"

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच गूढं मां प्रश्नवित् प्रश्नं पृच्छसे त्वमिहानघ। न ह्येतत् तर्कया शक्यं वक्तुं वर्षशतैरपि॥
en: Bhishma said "O you who are well acquainted with the art of questioning, this question which you have put to me, O pure one, is one which is enveloped in deep mystery. One cannot answer it with the help of logic even if one were to try for a hundred years.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: ऋते देवप्रसादाद् वा राजन् ज्ञानागमेन वा। गहनं ह्येदाख्यानं व्याख्यातव्यं तवारिहन्॥
en: Without the favour of Narayana, O king, or an acquisition of high knowledge, this question of yours cannot be answered. Though this subject is filled with deep mystery, I shall yet, O destroyer of enemies, explain it to you?

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। नारदस्य च संवादमृषेर्नारायणस्य च॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Narada and the Rishi Narayana.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: नारायणो हि विश्वात्मा चतुर्मूर्तिः सनातनः। धर्मात्मजः सम्बभूव पितैवं मेऽभ्यभाषत॥ कृते युगे महाराज पुरा स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे। नरो नारायणश्चैव हरिः कृष्णः स्वयम्भुवः॥
en: I heard it from my father that in the golden age, O king, during the epoch of the Self-create Manu, the eternal Narayana, the Soul of the universe, was born as the son of Dharma in a quadrupie form, viz., as Nara, Narayana, Hari, and the Self-create Krishna.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: तेषां नारायणनरौ तपस्तेपतुरव्ययौ। बदर्याश्रममासाद्य शकटे कनकामये॥
en: Amongst them all, Narayana and Nara practised severest austerities by going to the Himalayan retreat known by the name of Vadari, and riding on their golden cars.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: अष्टचक्रं हि तद् यानं भूतयुक्तं मनोरमम्। तत्राद्यौ लोकनाथौ तौ कृशौ धमनिसंततौ॥ तपसा तेजसा चैव दुर्निरीक्ष्यौ सुरैरपि। यस्य प्रसादं कुर्वाते स देवौ द्रष्टुमर्हति॥
en: Each of those cars had eight wheels, and was made up of the five primal elements, and supremely beautiful. Those original regents of the world who had taken birth as the sons of Dharma, became extremely emaciated in body on account of the austerities they practised. Indeed, for those austerities and for their energy, the very gods were unable to look at them. Only that god to whom they were kind could see them.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: नूनं तयोरनुमते हृदि हृच्छयचोदितः। महामेरोगिरेः शृङ्गात् प्रच्युतो गन्धमादनम्॥
en: Forsooth, with his heart given to them, and moved by a longing desire to see them, Narada dropped down on Gandhamadana from a summit of the high mountains of Meru and walked over all the world.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: नारदः सुमहद्भूतं सर्वलोकानचीचरत्। तं देशमगमद् राजन् बदर्याश्रममाशुगः॥
en: Endued with great speed, he at last went to that spot whereon was situate the retreat of Vadari. Moved by curiosity he entered that retreat at the hour of Nara's and Narayana's performing their daily rites.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: तयोराह्निकवेलायां तस्य कौतूहलं त्वभूत्। इदं तदास्पदं कृत्स्नं यस्मिल्लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः॥ सदेवासुरगन्धर्वाः सकिन्नरमहोरगाः।
en: He said to himself,-This is truly the retreat of that Being in whom are placed all the worlds including the gods, the Asuras, the Gandharvas, the Kinnaras, and the great snakes.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: एका मूर्तिरियं पूर्वं जाता भूयश्चतुर्विधा॥ धर्मस्य कुलसंताने धर्मादेभिर्विवर्धितः।
en: There was only one forin of this great Being before. That form took birth in four forms for the multiplication of the race of Dharma which have been reared by that god.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: अहो ह्यनुगृहीतोऽद्य धर्म एभिः सुरैरह॥ नरनारायणाभ्यां च कृष्णेन हरिणा तथा।
en: How wonderful it is that Dharma has thus been honoured by these four great gods, viz., Nara, Narayana, Krishna and Hari.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: अत्र कृष्णो हरिश्चैव कस्मिंश्चित् कारणान्तरे॥ स्थितौ धर्मोत्तरौ होतो तथा तपसि धिष्ठितौ।
en: In this spot Krishna and Hari lived formerly. The other two, however, viz., Nara and Narayana, are now living here performing penances for the object of increasing their merit.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: एतौ हि परमं धाम कानयोराह्निकक्रिया॥ पितरौ सर्वभूतानां दैवतं च यशस्विनौ। कां देवतां तु यजतः पितॄन् वा कान् महामती॥
en: These two are the highest refuge of the universe. What can be the nature of the daily rites these two perform? They are the fathers of all creatures and the illustrious gods of all beings. Gifted with great intelligence, what is that god whom these two adore? Who are those Pitris whom these two Pitris of all beings worship.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: इति संचिन्त्य मनसा भक्त्या नारायणस्य तु। सहसा प्रादुरभवत् समीपे देवयोस्तदा॥
en: Thinking of this mentally, and filled with devotion towards Narayana, Narada suddenly appeared before those two gods.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: कृते दैवे च पित्र्ये च ततस्ताभ्यां निरीक्षितः। पूजितश्चैव विधिना यथाप्रोक्तेन शास्त्रतः॥
en: After those two gods had finished their adorations to their deities and the Rishis, they looked at the celestial Rishi arrived at their asylum. The latter was honoured with those eternal rites that are laid down in their scriptures.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यमपूर्वं विधिविस्तरम्। उपोपविष्टः सुप्रीतो नारदो भगवानृषिः॥
en: Seeing that extraordinary conduct of the two original gods in themselves adoring other deities and Pitris, the illustrious Rishi Narada took his seat there, well pleased with the honours he had received.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: नारायणं संनिरीक्ष्य प्रसन्नेनान्तरात्मना। नमस्कृत्वा महादेवमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: With a cheerful soul he looked at Narayana, and bowing to Mahadeva he said these words.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: नारद उवाच वेदेषु सपुराणेषु साङ्गोपाङ्गेषु गीयसे। त्वमजः शाश्वतो धाता मातामृतमनुत्तमम्॥ प्रतिष्ठितं भूतभव्यं त्वयि सर्वमिदं जगत्।
en: In the Vedas and the Puranas in the auxiliary and sub-auxiliary treaties, you are sung with respect! You are unborn and eternal! you are the Creator! You are the mother of the universe! You are the embodiment of Immortality and you are the foremost of all things. The Past and the Future, indeed, the entire universe has been placed on you.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: चत्वारो ह्याश्रमा देव सर्वे गार्हस्थ्यमूलकाः॥ यजन्ते त्वामहरहर्नानामूर्तिसमास्थितम्।
en: The four modes of life,olord, of which the domestic is the first, continually sacrifice to you who are of diverse forms.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: पिता माता च सर्वस्य जगतः शाश्वतो गुरुः। कं त्वद्य यजसे देवं पितरं कं न विद्महे॥
