en: You are the father and the mother and the eternal preceptor of the universe. We know not who is that god or that Pitri to whom you are sacrificing to-day.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: श्री भगवानुवाच अवाच्यमेतद् वक्तव्यमात्मगुह्यं सनातनम्। तव भक्तिमतो ब्रह्मन् वक्ष्यामि तु यथातथम्॥
en: This topic is one regarding which nothing should be said. It is an ancient ministry. Your devotion to me is very great. Hence, O twiceborn one, I shall describe it to you according to the truth.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: यत् तत् सूक्ष्ममविज्ञेयमव्यक्तमचलं ध्रुवम्। इन्द्रियैरिन्द्रियार्थश्च सर्वभूतैश्च वर्जितम्॥ स ह्यन्तरात्मा भूतानां क्षेत्रज्ञश्चेति कथ्यते। त्रिगुणव्यतिरिक्तो वै पुरुषश्चेति कल्पितः॥
en: That which is minute, which is inconceivable, unmanifest, immobile, durable dissociated from the senses and the objects of the senses, as well as the (five) elements,—that is called the in-dwelling Soul of all existent creatures. That is known by the name of Kshetrajna. Transcending the three qualities of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas, that is regarded as Purusha in the scriptures.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: तस्मादव्यक्तमुत्पन्नं त्रिगुणं द्विजसत्तम। अव्यक्ता व्यक्तभावस्था या सा प्रकृतिरव्यया॥
en: From him has originated the unmanifest, O foremost of twice-born ones, endued with the three qualities of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. Though really unmanifest, she is called indestructible Nature and lives in all manifest forins.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: तां योनिमावयोर्विद्धि योऽसौ सदसदात्मकः। आवाभ्यां पूज्यतेऽसौ हि दैवे पित्र्ये च कल्प्यते॥
en: Know that from her we two have originated. That all-pervading Soul, which is made of all existent and non-existent things, is worshipped by us. Even He is what we adore in all those rites that we perform in honour of the gods and the departed manes.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: नास्ति तस्मात् परोऽन्यो हि पिता देवोऽथवा द्विज। आत्मा हि नः स विज्ञेयस्ततस्तं पूजयावहे॥
en: There is no higher god, or father than He, O twice-born one! He should be known as our Soul. It is Him that we adore.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: तेनैषा प्रथिता ब्रह्मन् मर्यादा लोकभाविनी। दैवं पित्र्यं च कर्तव्यमिति तस्यानुशासनम्॥
en: This course of duties followed by men has, O twice-born one, been laid down by Him. It is his ordinance that we should duly perform all the rites laid down regarding the gods and the departed manes.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: ब्रह्मा स्थाणुर्मनुर्दक्षो भृगुर्धर्मस्तपो यमः। मरीचिरङ्गिराऽत्रिश्च पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः॥ वसिष्ठः परमेष्ठी च विवस्वान् सोम एव च। कर्दमश्चापि यः प्रोक्तः क्रोधो विक्रीत एव च॥ एकविंशतिरुत्पन्नास्ते प्रजापतयः स्मृताः। तस्य देवस्य मर्यादां पूजयन्तः सनातनीम्॥
en: Brahman, Sthanu, Manu, Daksha, Bhrigu, Dharma, Yama, Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vashishtha, Parameshthi, Vivaswat, Shoma, Karddama, Kroda, Avak, and Krita, these twenty-one persons called Patriarchs, were first born. All of them obeyed the eternal law of the Supreme God.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: दैवं पित्र्यं च सततं तस्य विज्ञाय तत्त्वतः। आत्मप्राप्तानि च ततः प्राप्नुवन्ति द्विजोत्तमाः॥
en: Observing all the rites, in full, that were laid down in honor of the gods and the departed manes, all those foremost of twice-born ones acquired all those objects which they sought.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: स्वर्गस्था अपि ये केचित् तान् नमस्यन्ति देहिनः। ते तत्प्रसादाद् गच्छन्ति तेनादिष्टफलां गतिम्॥
en: The bodiless dwellers of heaven, itself bow to that Supreme God and through His favour they acquire those fruits and that end which he ordains for them.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: ये हीनाः सप्तदशभिर्गुणैः कर्मभिरेव च। कला:पञ्चदश त्यक्त्वा ते मुक्ता इति निश्चयः॥
en: This is the injunction of the scriptures that those persons who are freed from these seventeen attributes, who have renounced all facts, and who are divested of the fifteen elements which form the gross body, are said to be Liberated.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: मुक्तानां तु गतिर्ब्रह्मन् क्षेत्रज्ञ इति कल्पिता। स हि सर्वगुणश्चैव निर्गुणश्चैव कथ्यते॥
en: The ultimate end of the Liberated is called by the name of Kshetrajna. He is considered as both possessed of, and freed from, all the attributes.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: दृश्यते ज्ञानयोगेन आवां च प्रसृतौ ततः। एवं ज्ञात्वा तमात्मानं पूजयावः सनातनम्॥
en: He can be apprehended by knowledge alone. We two have originated from Him. Knowing him in that way, we worship that eternal soul of all things.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: तं वेदाश्चाश्रमाश्चैव नानामतसमास्थिताः। भक्त्या सम्पूजयन्त्याशु गतिं चैषां ददाति सः॥
en: The Vedas and all the modes of life, though marked by diversities of opinion, all adore Him with devotion. It is he who, inclined to show favour, confers on them high ends fraught with happiness.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: ये तु तद्भाविता लोके ह्येकान्तित्वं समास्थिताः। एतदभ्यधिकं तेषां यत् ते तं प्रविशन्त्यत्॥
en: Those persons in this world who, filled with His spirit, become fully and conclusively devoted to him, acquire much higher end, for they succed in entering Him and becoming merged in his self.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: इति गुह्यसमुद्देशस्तव नारद कीर्तितः। भक्त्या प्रेम्णा च विप्रर्षे अस्मद्भक्त्या च ते श्रुतः॥
en: I have now, O Narada, described to you what is highly mysterious, moved by the live I bear for you four devotion to me. Indeed, on account of that devotion which you profess towards me, you have succeeded in listening to this my discourse.

description: Who is the God of gods. The discourse between Narada and Rishi Narayana on this subject
sn: इति गुह्यसमुद्देशस्तव नारद कीर्तितः। भक्त्या प्रेम्णा च विप्रर्षे अस्मद्भक्त्या च ते श्रुतः॥
en: I have now, O Narada, described to you what is highly mysterious, moved by the live I bear for you four devotion to me. Indeed, on account of that devotion which you profess towards me, you have succeeded in listening to this my discourse.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: भीष्म उवाच स एवमुक्तो द्विपदां वरिष्ठो नारायणेनोत्तमपूरुषेण। जगाद वाक्यं द्विपदां वरिष्ठं नारायणं लोकहिताधिवासम्॥
en: Bhishma said "Addressed by Narayana, that foremost of beings, in these words, Narada, the foremost of men, then said these words to Narayana for the behoof of the world.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: नारद उवाच यदर्थमात्रप्रभवेण जन्म कृतं त्वया धर्मगृहे चतुर्धा! तत्साध्यतां लोकहितार्थमद्य गच्छामि द्रष्टुं प्रकृतिं तवाद्याम्॥
en: Narada said Let that object be fulfilled for which you, O Self-born Being, have taken birth in four forms in the house of Dharma! I shall now go for seeing your original nature.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: पूजां गुरूणां सततं करोमि परस्य गुह्यं न तु भिन्नपूर्वम्। वेदाः स्वधीता मम लोकनाथ तप्तं तपो नानृतमुक्तपूर्वम्॥
en: I always adore my elders. I have never given out the secrets of others. O lord of the universe, I have studied the Vedas carefully. I have practised austere penances. I have never spoken a falsehood.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: गुप्तानि चत्वारि यथागमं मे शत्रौ च मित्रे च समोऽस्मि नित्यम्। तं चादिदेवं सततं प्रपन्न एकान्तभावेन वृणोम्यजस्रम्॥
en: As laid down in the scriptures, I have always protected the four that should be protected. I always treat impartially friends and enemies. Wholly and surely given to Him, that first of gods, viz., the Supreme Soul, I incessantly worship Him.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: एभिर्विशेषैः परिशुद्धसत्त्व: कस्मान्न पश्येयमनन्तमीशम्। तत्पारमेष्ठ्यस्य वचो निशम्य नारायणः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता॥ गच्छेति तं नारदमुक्तवान् स सम्पूजयित्वाऽऽत्मविधिक्रियाभिः। ततो विसृष्टः परमेष्ठिपुत्रः सोऽभ्यर्चयित्वा तमृर्षि पुराणम्॥
en: Having purified my soul by these specially meritorious acts, why shall I not succeed in seeing that Infinite Lord of the universe?-Hearing these words of Parameshthi's son, Narayana, that protector of the scriptures, said to him, saying,-Go, O Narada!—Before sending him away, however, the great god adored the celestial Rishi with those rites and ceremonies which have been laid down in the scriptures by himself. Narada also duly honoured the ancient Rishi Narayana. After such honours had been exchanged, the son of Parameshthi left that spot.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: स्ततोऽधिमेरौ सहसा निलिल्ये। मेकान्तमासाद्य गिरेः स शृङ्गे॥
en: Endued with high Yoga-power, Narada suddenly soared into the sky and reached the summit of the mountains of Meru. Proceeding to a secluded spot on that summit, the great ascetic took rest for a short time.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: आलोकयन्नुत्तरपश्चिमेन ददर्श चाप्यद्भुतमुक्तरूपम्। क्षीरोदधेर्योत्तरतो हि द्वीपः श्वेतः स नाम्ना प्रथितो विशालः॥
en: He then caste his eyes towards the northwestern direction and saw an exceedingly wonderful spectacle. Towards the north, in the ocean of Milk, there is a large island named the White Island.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: मेरोः सहस्रः स हि योजनानां द्वात्रिंशतोर्ध्वं कविभिनिरुक्तः। अनिन्द्रियाश्चानशनाश्च तत्र निष्पन्दहीनाः सुसुगन्धिनस्ते॥
en: The learned say that its distance from the mountains of Meru is greater than thirty-two thousands Yojanas. The inhabitants of that realin have no senses. They live without food. Their eyes are winkless. They always send forth excellent perfumes.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: श्चक्षुर्मुषः पापकृतां नराणाम्। वज्रास्थिकायाः सममानोन्माना दिव्यावयवरूपाः शुभसारोपेताः॥
en: Their complexions are white. They are purged off of all sins. They blast the eyes of those sinners that look at them. Their bones and bodies are as hard as adamant. They consider honour and dishonour equally. They all look as if they are of divine origin. All of them are endued with auspicious marks and great strength.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: छत्राकृतिशीर्षा मेघौघनिनादाः सममुष्कचतुष्का राजीवच्छतपादाः। षष्ट्या दन्तैर्युक्ताः शुक्लैरष्टाभिर्दष्ट्राभिर्ये जिह्वाभिर्ये विश्ववक्त्रं लेलिह्यन्ते सूर्यप्रख्यम्॥११
en: Their heads seem to be like umbrellas. Their voices are deep like that of the clouds. Each of them have four testes. The soles of their feet have hundreds of lines. They had sixty white teeth, and eight small ones. They had many tongues. With those tongues they seemed to lick the very Sun whose face is turned towards all sides.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: देवं भक्त्या विश्वोत्पन्न यस्मात् सर्वे लोकाः सम्प्रसूताः। वेदा धर्मा मुनयः शान्ता देवाः सर्वे तस्य निसर्गः॥
en: Indeed, they seemed to be capable of devouring that great god from whom has originated the entire universe, the Vedas, the duties, and the ascetics possessing the quality of tranquillity.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अनिन्द्रिया निराहारा अनिष्पन्दाः सुगन्धिनः। कथं ते पुरुषा जाताः का तेषां गतिरुत्तमा॥
en: Yudhishthira said are “O grand-father, you have said that those beings have no senses, that they do not eat anything for maintaining their lives; that their eyes are winkless, and that they always emit excellent perfumes. I ask, how were they born? What also is the superior end which they acquire?

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: ये च मुक्ता भवन्तीह नरा भरतसत्तम। तेषां लक्षणमेतद्धि तच्छ्वेतद्वीपवासिनाम्॥
en: O chief of Bharata's race, the characteristics of those men that become liberated the same as those by which the inhabitants of the White Island are distinguished?

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: तस्मान्मे संशयं छिन्धि परं कौतूहलं हि मे। त्वं हि सर्वकथारामस्त्वां चैवोपाश्रिता वयम्॥
en: Do you remove my doubts! The curiosity I feel is very great. You are the repository of all histories and narratives. As regards ourselves, we entirely depend on you for knowledge and instruction.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: भीष्म उवाच विस्तीर्णैषा कथा राजन् श्रुता मे पितृसंनिधौ। यैषा तव हि वक्तव्या कथासारो हि सा मता॥
en: Bhishma said "This narrative, O king, which I have heard from my father, is extensive. I shall now recite it to you. Indeed, it is considered as the cream of all narratives.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: राजोपरिचरो नाम बभूवाधिपतिर्भुवः। आखण्डलसखः ख्यातो भक्तो नारायणं हरिम्॥
en: There was, in days of yore, a king on Earth, Uparichara, by name. He was known to be the friend, of Indra the king of gods. He was devoted to Narayana called also by the name of Hari.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: धार्मिको नित्यभक्तश्च पितुर्नित्यमतन्द्रितः। साम्राज्यं तेन सम्प्राप्तं नारायणवरात् पुरा॥
en: He used to discharge all the duties laid down in the scriptures. Ever devoted to his father, was always ready for action. He acquired sovereignty of the world on account of a boon he had obtained from Narayana.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: सात्वतं विधिमास्थाय प्राक् सूर्यमुखनिःसृतम्। पूजयामास देवेशं तच्छेषेण पितामहान्॥
en: Following the Satvata ritual that had been declared in days of yore by the Sun himself, king Uparichara used to adore the God of gods, and after his worship was over, to adore the Grandfather of the universe.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: पितृशेषेण विप्रांश्च संविभज्याश्रितांश्च सः! शेषान्नभुक् सत्यपरः सर्वभूतेष्वहिंसकः॥
en: After adoring the departed manes, he adored the Brahmanas. He then divided the offerings among those who depended on him. With the remnant after serving those, the king satisfied his own hunger. Given to truth, the king abstained from doing any injury to any creature.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: सर्वभावेन भक्तः स देवदेवं जनार्दनम्। अनादिमध्यनिधनं लोककर्तारमव्ययम्॥
en: With his entire soul, the king was devoted to that God of gods, viz., Janardana, who is without beginning and middle and end, who is Creator of the universe, and who is without decay of any sort.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: तस्य नारायणे भक्तिं वहतोऽमित्रकर्षिणः। एकशय्यासनं देवो दत्तवान् देवराट् स्वयम्॥
en: Seeing the devotion to Narayana of that destroyer of foes, the divine king of the gods himself shared with him his own seat and bed.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: आत्मराज्यं धनं चैव कलत्रं वाहनं तथा। यत्तद्भागवतं सर्वमिति तत् प्रोक्षितं सदा॥
en: His kingdom and riches and wives and animals were all considered by him as obtained from Narayana. He, therefore, offered all his belongings to that great god.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: काम्यनैमित्तिका राजन् यज्ञियाः परमक्रियाः। सर्वाः सात्वतमास्थाय विधि चक्रे समाहितः॥
en: Adopting the Satvata ritual, king Uparichara, with concentrated soul, used to perform all his sacrificial acts and observances, both optional and obligatory.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: पाञ्चरात्रविदो मुख्यास्तस्य गेहे महात्मनः। प्रायणं भगवत्प्रोक्तं भुञ्जते वाग्रभोजनम्॥
en: Many foremost Brahmanas, well conversant with the Pancharatra ritual, used to eat before all others the food offered to the god Narayana in the palace of that illustrious king.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: तस्य प्रशासतो राज्यं धर्मेणामित्रघातिनः। नानृता वाक् समभवन्मनो दुष्टं न चाभवत्॥
en: As long as that destroyer of enemies continued to rule his kingdom piously, no falsehood ever escaped his lips and no evil thought ever entered his mind.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: न च कायेन कृतवान् स पापं परमण्वपि। ये हि ते ऋषयः ख्याताः सप्त चित्रशिखण्डिनः॥ तैरेकमतिभिर्भूत्वा यत् प्रोक्तं शास्रमुत्तमम्। वेदैश्चतुर्भिः समितं कृतं मेरौ महागिरौ॥ आस्यैः सप्तभिरुद्गीण लोकधर्ममनुत्तमम्। मरीचिरत्र्यङ्गिरसौ पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः। वसिष्ठश्च महातेजास्ते हि चित्रशिखण्डिनः॥ सप्त प्रकृतयो ह्येतास्तथा स्वायम्भुवोऽष्टमः। एताभिर्धार्यते लोकस्ताभ्यः शास्त्रं विनिःसृतम्॥
en: With his limbs he never perpetrated even the slightest crime. The seven celebrated Rishis, viz., Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vashishtha, who passed by the name of Chitra-shikhandins, uniting together on the breast of that foremost of mountains, viz., Meru, promulgated an excellent work on duties and observances which were consistent with the four Vedas. The contents of that work were uttered by seven mouths, and fomed the best compendium of human duties and obsevances. Known, as already stated, by the name of ChitraShikhandins, those seven Rishis form the seven elements, and the Self-born Manu, who is the eighth in the number, formed original Nature. These eight keep up the universe, and it was these eight who promulgated the treatise referred to.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: एकाग्रमनसो दान्ता मुनयः संयमे रताः। भूतभव्यभविष्यज्ञाः सत्यधर्मपरायणाः॥
en: With their senses and minds under complete subjugation and ever given to Yoga, these eight ascetics, with concentrated souls, fully know the Past, the Present and the Future, and are devoted to the Religion of Truth.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: इदं श्रेय इदं ब्रह्म इदं हितमनुत्तमम्। लोकान् संचिन्त्य मनसा ततः शास्त्रं प्रचक्रिरे॥
en: This is good, This is Brahma,—-This is highly beneficial,-reflecting thus in their minds, those Rishis created the worlds, and the science of morality and duty that governs those worlds.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: तत्र धर्मार्थकामा हि मोक्षः पश्चाच्च कीर्तितः। मर्यादा विविधाश्चैव दिवि भूमौ च संस्थिताः॥
en: In that work the authors discoursed on Religion and Profit and Pleasure, and subsequently on Liberation also. The various restrictions and limitations were also laid down in it for the Earth as also for Heaven.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: आराध्य तपसा देवं हरिं नारायणं प्रभुम्। दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं वै सर्वे ते ऋषिभिः सह॥
en: They wrote that work after having adored with penances the powerful and illustrious Narayana called also Hari, for a thousand divine years, in company with many other Rishis.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: नारायणानुशास्ता हि तदा देवी सरस्वती। विवेश तानृषीन् सर्वाल्लोकानां हितकाम्यया॥
en: Pleased with their penances and adoration, Narayana ordered the goddess of speech, viz., Sarasvati, to enter into the bodies of those Rishis. The goddess, for the behoof of the worlds, did what she ordered.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: ततः प्रवर्तिता सम्यक् तपोविद्भिर्द्विजातिभिः। शब्दे चार्थे च हेतो च एषा प्रथमसर्गजा॥
en: On account of the entrance of the goddess of speech into their bodies, those Rishis, well conversant with penances, succeeded in composing that foremost of works in respect of words, senses and reason.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: आदादेव हि तच्छास्त्रमोंकारस्वरपूजितम्। ऋषिभिः श्रावितं यत्र तत्र कारुणिको ह्यसौ॥
en: Having composed that work sanctified with the syllable OM, the Rishis first of all read it to Narayana, who heard them from kindness.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: ततः प्रसन्नो भगवाननिर्दिष्टशरीरगः। ऋषीनुवाच तान् सर्वानदृश्यः पुरुषोत्तमः॥ कृतं शतसहस्रं हि श्लोकानादिमुत्तमम्। लोकतन्त्रस्य कृत्स्नस्य यस्माद् धर्मः प्रवर्तते।॥
en: The illustrious and bodiless Narayana became highly pleased with what he heard. That foremost of all Beings then addressed those Rishis in an incorporeal voice and said,-Excellent is this work that you have composed containing a hundred thousand verses. The duties and observances of all the worlds will originate from this your work.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: प्रवृत्तौ च निवृत्तौ च यस्मादेतद् भविष्यति। यजुर्ऋक्सामभिर्जुष्टमथर्वांगिरसैस्तथा॥
en: Perfectly following the four Vedas, viz., the Yajushes, the Richs, the Samans, and the Atharvans of Angiras, this work of yours will be an authority in all the worlds with regard to both Work and Renunciation.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: यथा प्रमाणं हि मया कृतो ब्रह्मा प्रसादतः। रुद्रश्च क्रोधजो विप्रा यूयं प्रकृतयस्तथा॥
en: According to the authority of the scriptures I have created Brahman from the attribute of Grace, Rudra from my anger, and yourselves, ye Brahmanas, as representing the elements.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वायुभूमिरापोऽग्निरेव च। सर्वे च नक्षत्रगणा यच्च भूताभिशब्दितम्॥ अधिकारेषु वर्तन्ते यथास्वं ब्रह्मवादिनः। सर्वे प्रमाणं हि यथा तथा तच्छास्त्रमुत्तमम्॥ भविष्यति प्रमाणं वै एतन्मदनुशासनम्। तस्मात् प्रवक्ष्यते धर्मान् मनुः स्वायम्भुवः स्वयम्॥
en: The Sun, and the Moon, Wind, and Earth, and Water and Fire, all the stars and planets and constellations, all else that is called by the name of creatures, and utterers of Brahma, all live and act in their respective spheres and are all respected as authorities. This work which you have composed shall be regarded by all persons, as a work of the highest authority. This is my order. Guided by this treatise, the Self-created Manu himself will declare to the world its duties and observances.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: उशना बृहस्पतिश्चैव यदोत्पन्नौ भविष्यतः। तदा प्रवक्ष्यतः शास्त्रं युष्मन्मतिभिरुद्धृतम्॥
en: When Ushanas and Brihaspati will be born, they also will promulgate their respective work on morality and religion, guided by and quoting from this your work.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: स्वायम्भुवेषु धर्मेषु शास्त्रे चौशनसे कृते। बृहस्पतिमते चैव लोकेषु प्रतिचारिते॥ युष्मत्कृतमिदं शास्त्रं प्रजापालो वसुस्ततः। बृहस्पतिसकाशाद् वै प्राप्स्यते द्विजसत्तमाः॥
en: After the publication of his work by the Self-born Manu and of that by Ushanas, and after the publication of the work also by Brihaspati, this science composed by you will be acquired by king Vasu. Indeed, you foremost of twice-born ones, that king will acquire this knowledge of this work from Brihaspati.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: स हि सद्भावितो राजा मद्भक्तश्च भविष्यति। तेन शास्त्रेण लोकेषु क्रियाः सर्वाः करिष्यति॥
en: Filled with all good thoughts, that king will become deeply devoted to me. Guided by this work, he will perform all his religious deeds and observance.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: एतद्धि युष्मच्छास्त्राणां शास्त्रमुत्तमसंज्ञितम्। एतदर्थ्यं च धर्म्यं च रहस्यं चैतदुत्तमम्॥
en: Verily, this work composed by you will be the foremost of all works on morality and religion. Excellent as it is, this work is full of instructions for acquiring both Riches and Religious merit, and is full of mysteries.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: अस्य प्रवर्तनाच्चैव प्रजावन्तो भविष्यथ। स च राजश्रिया युक्तो भविष्यति महान् वसुः॥
en: For the publication of this treatise, you will be progenitors of an extensive family! King Uparichara also will become endued with greatness and prosperity.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: संस्थिते तु नृपे तस्मिशास्त्रमेतत् सनातनम्। अन्तर्धास्यति तत् सर्वमेतद् वः कथितं मया॥
en: Upon the death, however, of that king, this eternal work will disappear from the world. I all this.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनमदृश्यः पुरुषोत्तमः। विसृज्य तानृषीन् सर्वान् कामपि प्रसृतो दिशम्॥
en: Having said these words to all those Rishis, the invisible Narayana left them and went to some place that was not known to them.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: ततस्ते लोकपितरः सर्वलोकार्थचिन्तकाः। प्रावर्तयन्त तच्छास्त्रं धर्मयोनि सनातनम्॥
en: Then those progenitors of the world, those Rishis who conferred their thoughts on the worldly ends, duly promulgated that work which is the eternal origin of all duties and observances.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: उत्पन्नेऽङ्गिरसे चैव युगे प्रथमकल्पिते। साङ्गोपनिषदं शास्त्रं स्थापयित्वा बृहस्पतौ॥
en: Subsequently, when Brihaspati was born in Angiras's family in the golden age, those seven Rishis charged him with the task of tell you promulgating their work which was consistent with the Upanishads and the several branches of the Vedas.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: जग्मुर्यथेप्सितं देशं तपसे कृतनिश्चयाः। धारणाः सर्वलोकानां सर्वधर्मप्रवर्तकाः॥
en: The themselves who were upholders of the universe and the first promulgators of duties and religious observances, then went to the place they chose, determined to practise penances." promulgating their work which was consistent with the Upanishads and the several branches of the Vedas.

description: Narada goes to see Narayana born in the house of Dharma. The Characteristics of liberated men
sn: जग्मुर्यथेप्सितं देशं तपसे कृतनिश्चयाः। धारणाः सर्वलोकानां सर्वधर्मप्रवर्तकाः॥
en: The themselves who were upholders of the universe and the first promulgators of duties and religious observances, then went to the place they chose, determined to practise penances."

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततोऽतीते महाकल्पे उत्पन्नेऽङ्गिरसः सुते। बभूवुर्निर्वृता देवा जाते देवपुरोहिते॥
en: Bhishma said Then, upon the expiration of the great cycle, when the celestial priest Brihaspati was born in the family of Angiras, all the gods became very happy.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: बृहद् ब्रह्म महच्चेति शब्दाः पर्यायवाचकाः। एभिः समन्वितो राजन् गुणैर्विद्वान् बृहस्पतिः॥
en: The words Vrihat, Brahma, and Mahat all carry the same significance. The celestial priest, O king, came to be called Brihaspati because he was gifted with all these accomplishments.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: तस्य शिष्यो बभूवाग्यो राजोपरिचरो वसुः। अधीतवांस्तदा शास्त्रं सम्यक् चित्रशिखण्डिजम्॥
en: King Uparichara, otherwise called Vasu, became a disciple of Brihaspati and soon became the greatest of his disciples. Admitted as such, he began of study from his preceptor that science which was composed by the seven Rishis who were known by the name of Chitrashikhandins.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: स राजा भावितः पूर्वं दैवेन विधिना वसुः। पालयामास पृथिवीं दिवमाखण्डलो यथा॥
en: With soul purified by sacrifices and other religious rites, he governed the Earth like Indra ruling the Heaven.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: तस्य यज्ञो महानासीदश्वमेधो महात्मनः। बृहस्पतिरुपाध्यायस्तत्र होता बभूव ह॥
en: The illustrious king celebrated a great Horse-sacrifice in which his preceptor Brihaspati became the priest offering libation.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: प्रजापतिसुताश्चात्र सदस्याश्चाभवंस्त्रयः। एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितश्चैव महर्षयः॥ धनुषाख्योऽथ रैभ्यश्च अर्वावसुपरावसू। ऋषिर्मेधातिथिश्चैव ताण्ड्यश्चैव महानृषिः॥ ऋषिः शान्तिर्महाभागस्तथा वेदशिराश्च यः। ऋषिश्रेष्ठश्च कपिल: शालिहोत्रपिता स्मृतः॥ आद्यः कठस्तैत्तिरिश्च वैषम्पायनपूर्वजः। कण्वोऽथ देवहोत्रश्च एते षोडश कीर्तिताः॥
en: The sons of Prajapati themselves, viz., Ekata, Dvita, and Trita became the priests watching the proceedings. There were others also who became Sadasyas in that sacrifice, viz., Dhanusha, Rajvya, Arvavasu, Paravasu, the Rishi Medhatithi, the great Rishi Tandya, the blessed Rishi Shanti, Vedashiras the foremost of Rishis, viz., Kapila, who was the father of Shalihotra, the first Kalpa, Tittiri the elder brother of Vaishampayana, Kanwa, and Devahotra, forming in all sixteen,

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: सम्भूताः सर्वसम्भारास्तस्मिन् राजन् महाक्रतौ। न तत्र पशुघातोऽभूत् स राजैवं स्थितोऽभवत्॥
en: In that great sacrifice, O king, all the necessary articles were collected. No animals were killed in it. The king had ordained it so.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: अहिंस्रः शुचिरक्षुद्रो निराशीः कर्मसंस्तुतः। आरण्यकपदोद्भूता भागास्तत्रोपकल्पिताः॥
en: He was full of mercy. Of pure and liberal mind, he had renounced all desire, and was well-conversant with all rites. The necessary articles of that sacrifice were the productions of the forest.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: प्रीतस्ततोऽस्य भगवान् देवदेवः पुरातनः। साक्षात् तं दर्शयामास सोऽदृश्योऽन्येन केनचित्॥
en: The ancient God of gods (viz., Hari), became highly pleased with the king on account of that sacrifice. Incapable of being seen by any one else, the great God appeared before his worshipper.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: स्वयं भागमुपाघ्राय पुरोडाशं गृहीतवान्। अदृश्येन हृतो भागो देवेन हरिमेधसा॥
en: Accepting by taking its scent, the share offered to him he himself took up the Purodasha (clarified butter with cakes of powdered barley). The great God took up the offerings without being seen by any one.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: बृहस्पतिस्ततः क्रुद्धः स्रुचमुद्यम्य वेगितः। आकाशं जन् स्रुचः पातै रोषादश्रूण्यवर्तयत्॥
en: At this, Brihaspati became angry. Taking up the ladle he hurled it violently at the sky, and began to shed tears in anger.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: उवाच चोपरिचरं मया भागोऽयमुद्यतः। ग्राह्यः स्वयं हि देवेन मत्प्रत्यक्षं न संशयः॥
en: Addressing king Uparichara he said,-Here, I place this as Narayana's share of the sacrificial offerings! Forsooth, he shall take it before my eyes.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उद्यता यज्ञभागा हि साक्षात् प्राप्ताः सुरैरिह। किमर्थमिह न प्राप्तो दर्शनं स हरिविभुः॥
en: Yudhishthira said In the great sacrifice of Uparichara, all the gods appeared in their respective forms for partaking of the sacrificial offerings and were seen by all. Why is it that the powerful Hari only acted otherwise by invisibly taking his share?

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः स तं समुद्भूतं भूमिपालो महान् वसुः। प्रसादयामास मुनि सदस्यास्ते च सर्वशः॥
en: Bhishma said When Brihaspati yielded to anger, the great king Vasu and all his Sadasyas sought to pacify the great Rishi.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: ऊचुश्चैनमसम्भ्रान्ता न रोषं कर्तुमर्हसि। नैष धर्मः कृतयुगे यस्त्वं रोषमचीकृथाः॥
en: With cool heads, all of them said to Brihaspati,-You should not yield to anger. In this golden age, this anger to which you have yielded should not be the characteristic of any one.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: अरोषणो ह्यसौ देवो यस्य भागोऽयमुद्यतः। न शक्यः स त्वया द्रष्टुमस्माभिर्वा बृहस्पते॥
en: The great god for whom the share of the sacrificial offerings was designed by you, is himself free from anger! He is incapable of being seen either by ourselves or by you, O Brihaspati.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: यस्य प्रसादं कुरुते स वैतं द्रष्टुमर्हति। एकतद्वितत्रिताश्चोचुस्ततश्चित्रशिखण्डिनः॥
en: Only he can see Him to whom He becomes gracious!—Then the Rishis Ekata, Dvita, and Trita, who were all conversant with the science of morality and duties compiled by the seven Rishis, addressed that assembly and began the following narration.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: वयं हि ब्रह्मणः पुत्रा मानसाः परिकीर्तिताः। गताः निःश्रेयसार्थं हि कदाचिद् दिशमुत्तराम्॥
en: We are the sons of Brahman, begotten by his will. Once on a time we went to the north for the acquisition of our highest good.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: तप्त्वा वर्षसहस्राणि चरित्वा तप उत्तमम्। एकपादाः स्थिताः सम्यक् काष्ठभूताः समाहिताः॥
en: Having practised penances for thousands of years and acquired a great ascetic merit, we again stood on only one foot like fixed rods of wood.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: मेरोरुत्तरभागे तु क्षीरोदस्यानुकूलतः। स देशो यत्र नस्तप्तं तपः परमदारुणम्॥
en: The country where we practised these austerest of penances, lies to the north of the mountains of Meru and on the shores of the ocean of milk.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: कथं पश्येम हि वयं देवं नारायणात्मकम्। वरेण्यं वरदं तं वै देवदेवं सनातनम्॥ कथं पश्येम हि वयं देवं नारायणं त्विति। अथ व्रतस्यावभृथे वागुवाचाशरीरिणी॥ स्निग्धगम्भीरया वाचा प्रहर्षणकरी विभो।
en: The object we had in mind was how to see the divine Narayana in his own form. Upon the termination of our penances and after we had performed the final ablutions, we heard an incorporeal voice, O powerful Brihaspati, deep like that of the clouds and exceedingly melodious and filling the heart with joy.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: सुतप्तं वस्तपो विप्राः प्रसन्नेनान्तरात्मना॥ यूयं जिज्ञासवो भक्ताः कथं द्रक्ष्यथ तं विभुम्।
en: The voice said You Brahmanas, you have performed well these penances with cheerful souls! Devoted to Narayana, you try to know how you may succeed in seeing that god of great power.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: क्षीरोदधेरुत्तरतः श्वेतद्वीपो महाप्रभः॥ तत्र नारायणपरा मानवाश्चन्द्रवर्चसः।
en: On the northern shores of the ocean of milk there is an island called White Island. The men that dwell in that island have complexions as white as the rays of the Moon and that are devoted to Narayana.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: एकान्तभावोपगतास्ते भक्ताः पुरुषोत्तमम्॥ ते सहस्रार्चिषं देवं प्रविशन्ति सनातनम्।
en: Worshippers of that foremost of all Beings, they are devoted to Him with their whole minds. They all enter that eternal and illustrious god of a thousand rays.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: अनिन्द्रिया निराहारा अनिष्पन्दाः सुगन्धिनः॥ एकान्तिनस्ते पुरुषाः श्वेतद्वीपनिवासिनः। गच्छध्वं तत्र मुनयस्तत्रात्मा मे प्रकाशितः॥
en: They are shorn of senses. They do not live on any sort of food. Their eyes are winkless. Their bodies always emit a sweet smell. Indeed, the inhabitants of White Island believe and adore only one God. Go there, ye ascetics, for there I have revealed myself.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: अथ श्रुत्वा वयं सर्वे वाचं तामशरीरिणीम्। यथाख्यातेन मार्गेण तं देशं प्रतिपेदिरे॥
en: All of us, hearing these invisible words, proceeded by the way said to the country described.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: प्राप्य श्वेतं महाद्वीपं तच्चित्तास्तद्दिदृक्षवः। ततोऽस्मदृष्टिविषयस्तदा प्रतिहतोऽभवत्॥
en: Eagerly desirous of seeing Him and our hearts full of Him, we reached that large island called White Island. Arrived there, we could see nothing. Indeed our vision was blinded by the energy of the great god and accordingly we could not see Him.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: न च पश्याम पुरुषं तत्तेजोहृतदर्शनाः। ततो नः प्रादुरभवद् विज्ञानं देवयोगजम्॥
en: At this, the idea, due to the grace of the great God Himself, sprung in our minds that one who had not practised sufficient penances could not soon see Narayana.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: न किलातप्ततपसा शक्यते द्रष्टुमञ्जसा। ततः पुनर्वर्षशतं तप्त्वा तात्कालिकं महत्॥ व्रतावसाने च शुभान् नरान् ददृशिरे वयम्।
en: Under the influence of this idea we once more began to practise some severe austerities, suited to the time and place, for a hundred years. Upon the termination of our vows, we saw a number of men of auspicious marks.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: श्वेतांश्चन्द्रप्रतीकाशान् सर्वलक्षणलक्षितान्॥ नित्याञ्जलिकृतान् ब्रह्म जपतः प्रागुदङ्मुखान्।
en: All of them were white and looked like the Moon and were erdued with every sort of blessedness. Their hands were always joined in prayer. The faces of some were turned towards the North and of some to East. They were engaged in silently meditating on Brahma.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: मानसो नाम स जपो जप्यते तैर्महात्मभिः॥ तेनैकाग्रमनस्त्वेन प्रीतो भवति वै हरिः।
en: The recitation performed by those great persons was a mental Yapa. On account of their hearts, having been entirely fixed upon Him, Hari became highly gratified with them.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: याभवन्मुनिशार्दूल भाः सूर्यस्य युगक्षये॥ एकैकस्य प्रभा तादृक् साभवन्मानवस्य ह।
en: The effulgence that came out of the persons of those men resembled, O foremost of ascetics, the splendours which the sun assumed when the time comes for the dissolution of the universe.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: तेजोनिवासः स द्वीप इति वै मेनिरे वयम्॥ न तत्राभ्यधिकः कश्चित् सर्वे ते समतेजसः।
en: Indeed, we thought that that Island was the seat of all Energy. All the denizens were perfectly equal in energy. There was no superiority or inferiority there among them.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: अथ सूर्यसहस्रस्य प्रभां युगपदुत्थिताम्॥ सहसा दृष्टवन्तः स्म पुनरेव बृहस्पते।
en: We then suddenly saw once more a light arise that seemed to be the concentrated effulgence of a thousand Sons, O Brihaspati.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: सहिताश्चाभ्यधावन्त ततस्ते मानवा दुतम्॥ कृताञ्जलिपुटा हृष्टा नम इत्येव वादिनः।
en: The denizens in a body, ran towards that light, with hands joined in reverential attitude, full of joy, and uttering the one word Salutation.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: ततो हि वदतां तेषामश्रौष्म विपुलं ध्वनिम्॥ बलिः किलोपहियते तस्य देवस्य तैनरैः।
en: We then heard a very loud noise uttered by all of them together. It appeared that those men were engaged in offering a sacrifice to the great God.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: वयं तु तेजसा तस्य सहसा हृतचेतसः॥ न किंचिदपि पश्यामो हतचक्षुर्बलेन्द्रियाः।
en: As regards ourselves, we were suddenly deprived of our senses by his Energy. Shorn of vision and strength and all the senses, we could not behold or feel anything.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: एकस्तु शब्दो विततः श्रुतोऽसमाभिरुदीरितः॥ जितं ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष नमस्ते विश्वभावन।
en: We only heard a loud sound uttered by the collected denizens. It said,-Victory to you, O you have eyes like lotus petals! Salutation to you, O Creator of the universe.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: नमस्तेऽस्तु हृषीकेश महापुरुषपूर्वज॥ इति शब्दः श्रुतोऽस्माभिः शिक्षाक्षरसमन्वितः।
en: Salutation to you, O Hrishikesha, O foremost of Beings, O First-born! This was the sound we heard, uttered distinctly and in accordance with the rules of orthoepy.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वायुः सर्वगन्धवहः शुचिः॥ दिव्यान्युवाह पुष्पाणि कर्मण्याश्चौषधीस्तथा।
en: Meanwhile, a fragrant and pure breeze blew, carrying perfumes of celestial flowers, and of certain herbs and plants that were necessary on the occasion.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: तैरिष्टः पञ्चकालज्ञैर्हरिरेकान्तिभिर्नरै॥ भक्त्या परमया युक्तैर्मनोवाक्कर्मभिस्तदा।
en: Those men, gifted with great devotion, having hearts full of reverence, conversant with the ordinances laid down in the Pancharatra, were then adoring the great god with mind, word, and deed.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: नूनं तत्रागतो देवो यथा तैर्वागुदीरिता॥ वयं त्वेनं न पश्यामो मोहितास्तस्य मायया।
en: Forsooth, Hari appeared in that place whence the sound we heard originated. As regards ourselves, stupefied by His illusion, we could not behold Him.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: मारुते संनिवृत्ते च बलौ च प्रतिपादिते॥ चिन्ताव्याकुलितात्मानो जाता: स्मोऽङ्गिरसां वर।
en: After the breeze has ceased and the sacrifice had been over, our hearts became stricken with anxiety, O foremost one of Angiras's race.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: मानवानां सहस्रेषु तेषु वै शुद्धयोनिषु॥ अस्मान् न कश्चिन्मनसा चक्षुषा वाप्यपूजयत्।
en: As we stood among those thousands of men all of whom were of pure birth, no one honoured us with a glance or a nod.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: तेऽपि स्वस्था मुनिगणा एकभावमनुव्रताः॥ नास्मासु दधिरे भावं ब्रह्मभावमनुष्ठिताः।
en: Those ascetics, all of whom were cheerful and filled with devotion and who were all are practising the Brahma-frame of mind, showed no feeling for us.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: ततोऽस्मान् सुपरिश्रान्तां स्तपसा चातिकर्शितान्॥ उवाच स्वस्थं किमपि भूतं तत्राशरीरकम्।
en: We had been greatly tired. Our penances had einaciated us. At that time, a bodiless Being addressed us from the sky and said to us

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: देव उवाच दृष्टा वः पुरुषाः श्वेताः सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जिताः॥ दृष्टो भवति देवेश एभिर्दृष्टैद्विजोत्तमैः।
en: These white men, who are divested of all external senses, competent to see (Narayana). Only those foremost of twice-born persons whom these white men honoured with their looks, can see the great God.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: गच्छध्वं मुनयः सर्वे यथागतभितोऽचिरात्॥ न स शक्यस्त्वभक्तेन द्रष्टुं देवः कथंचन।
en: Go hence, ye Munis, to the place from where you have come! That great Deity is incapable of being ever seen by one who has no devotion.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: कामं कालेन महता एकान्तित्वमुपागतः॥ शक्यो द्रष्टुं स भगवान् प्रभामण्डलदुर्दशः। महत् कार्यं च कर्तव्यं युष्माभिर्द्विजसत्तमाः॥
en: Incapable of being seen on account of his dazzling effulgence, that illustrious Deity can be seen only by those person who succeed, in course of long time, in devoting themselves wholly and solely to Him. O foremost of twiceborn ones, you have a great duty to perform.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: इतः कृतयुगेऽतीते विपर्यासं गतेऽपि च। वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे विप्राः प्राप्ते त्रेतायुगे पुनः॥ सुराणां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं सहाया वै भविष्यथा
en: After the expiration of this the golden age, when the Treta age comes in course of the Vivasvat cycle, a great calamity will befall the world. You Munis, you shall then have to help the gods.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: ततस्तदद्भुतं वाक्यं निशम्यैवामृतोपमम्॥ तस्य प्रसादात् प्राप्ताः स्मो देशमीप्सितमञ्जसा।
en: no Having heard this wonderful words that were sweet as nectar, we soon returned to the place we desired, through the favour of that great Deity.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: एवं सुतपसा चैव हव्यकव्यैस्तथैव च॥ देवोऽस्माभिर्न दृष्टः स कथं त्वं द्रष्टुमर्हसि।
en: When with the help of even such austere penances of offerings devoutly given in sacrifices, we could not see the great Deity, how, indeed, can you except to see Him so easily?

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: नारायणो महद्भूतं विश्वसृग्धव्यकव्यभुक॥ अनादिनिधनोऽव्यक्तो देवदानवपूजितः।
en: Narayana is a Great Being. he is the Creator of the universe. He is worshipped in sacrifices with offerings of clarified butter and other food dedicated with the help of Vedic Mantras. He has no beginning and end. He is Unmanifest. Both the gods and the Danavas adore Him.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: एवमेकतवाक्येन द्वितत्रितमतेन च॥ अनुनीतः सदस्यैश्च बृहस्पतिरुदारधीः। समापयत् ततो यज्ञं दैवतं समपूजयत्॥
en: Induced by these words spoken by Ekata and approved by his companions, viz., Dvita and Trita, and solicited also by the other Sadasyas, the great Brihaspati terminated that sacrifice after duly offering the accustomed adorations to the gods.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: समाप्तयज्ञो राजापि प्रजां पालितवान् वसुः। ब्रह्मशापाद् दिवो भ्रष्टः प्रविवेश महीं ततः॥
en: Having completed his great sacrifice, king Uparichara, also, began to rule his subjects piously. At last, renouncing his body, he ascended to heaven. After sometime, through the curse of the Brahmanas, he dropped down from those happy regions and sank deep into the bowels of the Earth.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: स राजा राजशार्दूल सत्यधर्मपरायणः। अन्तर्भूमिगतश्चैव सततं धर्मवत्सलः॥
en: King Vasu, O foremost of kings, was always devoted to the true religion. Although sunk deep into the bowels of the Earth, his devotion to virtue did not decrease.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: नारायणपरो भूत्वा नारायणजपं जपन्। तस्यैव च प्रसादेन पुनरेवोत्थितस्तु सः॥
en: Ever devoted to Narayana, and ever reciting sacred Mantras having Narayana for their god, he once more ascended to heaven through Narayana's favour.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the description of the White Island
sn: महीतलाद् गतः स्थानं ब्रह्मणः समनन्तरम्। परां गतिमनुप्राप्त इति नैष्ठिकमञ्जसा॥
en: Getting up from the bowels of the Earth, king Vasu, on account of the very highest end that he attained, proceeded to a spot which is even higher than the region of Brahman himself.”

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यदा भगवतोऽत्यर्थमासीद् राजा महान् वसुः। किमर्थं स परिभ्रष्टो विवेश विवरं भुवः॥
en: Yudhishthira said When the great king Vasu was so wholly devoted to Narayana, why then did he drop down from heaven and why again had he to sink beneath the surface of Earth?

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। ऋषीणां चैव संवादं त्रिदशानां च भारत॥
en: Regarding it is cited an old discourse, O Bharata, between the Rishis and the gods.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: अजेन यष्टव्यमिति प्राहुर्देवा द्विजोत्तमान्। स च च्छागोऽप्यजो ज्ञेयो नान्यः पशुरिति स्थितिः॥
en: Once on a time, addressing many foremost of Brahmanas the gods said to them that sacrifices should be performed by offering up Ajas as victims. The word Aja means the goat and no other animal.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: ऋषय ऊचुः बीजैर्यज्ञेषु यष्टव्यमिति वै वैदिकी श्रुतिः। अजसंज्ञानि बीजानि च्छागं नो हन्तुमर्हथ॥
en: The Rishis said The Veda declares that in sacrifices the offerings should consist of seeds. Seeds are called Ajas. You should not kill goats.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: नैष धर्मः सतां देवा यत्र वध्येत वै पशुः। इदं कृतयुगं श्रेष्ठं कथं वध्येत वै पशुः॥
en: O gods, that cannot be the religion of good and pious people in which the destruction of animals is sanctioned. This, again, is the golden age. How can animals be killed in this epoch of righteousness?

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: भीष्म उवाच तेषां संवदतामेवमृषीणां विबुधैः सह। मार्गागतो नृपश्रेष्ठस्तं देशं प्राप्तवान् वसुः॥ अन्तरिक्षचरः श्रीमान् समग्रबलवाहनः।
en: Bhishma said While this conversation was going on between the Rishis and the gods, that foremost of kings, viz., Vasu, was seen to come that way. Gifted with great prosperity, the king was coming through the sky, accompanied by his troops and vehicles and animals.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा सहसाऽऽयान्तं वसुं ते त्वन्तरिक्षगम्॥ ऊचुर्द्विजातयो देवानेष च्छेत्स्यति संशयम्।
en: Seeing king Vasu coming there through the skies, the Brahmanas addressing the gods, said,-This one will dispell our doubts.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: यज्वा दानपतिः श्रेष्ठः सर्वभूतहितप्रियः॥ कथंस्विदन्यथा ब्रूयादेष वाक्यं महान् वसुः।
en: He celebrates sacrifices. He is liberal in making gifts. He always seeks the well being of all creatures. How, indeed, will the great Vasu speak otherwise.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: एवं ते संविदं कृत्वा विबुधा ऋषयस्तथा॥ अपृच्छन् सहिताभ्येत्य वसु राजानमन्तिकात्।
en: Having thus spoken each other, the gods and the Rishis quickly approached king Vasu and asked him, saying,-0 king, with what should one celebrate sacrifices?

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: भो राजन् केन यष्टव्यमजेनाहोस्विदौषधैः॥ एतन्नः संशयं छिन्धि प्रमाणं नो भवान् मतः।
en: Should one sacrifice with the goat or with herbs and plants? Do you remove this doubt of ours! We select you as our judge in this matter.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: स तान् कृताञ्जलिर्भूत्वा परिपप्रच्छ वै वसुः॥ कस्य वै को मतः कामो ब्रूत सत्यं द्विजोत्तमाः।
en: Thus accosted by them, Vasu joined his hands in humility and said to them,-Tell me truly, ye foremost of Brahmanas, what opinion is held by you individually in this matter?

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: ऋषय ऊचुः धान्यैर्यष्टव्यमित्येव पक्षोऽस्माकं नराधिप।।१२। देवानां तु पशुः पक्षो मतो राजन् वदस्व नः।
en: The Rishis said The opinion held by us, O king, is that sacrifices should be celebrated with grain! The gods, however, hold that sacrifices should be celebrated with animals. Do you judge between us and tell us which of these opinions is correct.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: भीष्म उवाच देवानां तु मतं ज्ञात्वा वसुना पक्षसंश्रयात्॥ छागेनाजेन यष्टव्यमेवमुक्तं वचस्तदा।
en: Bhishma said Learning the opinion of the gods, Vasu, moved by partiality for them, said that sacrifices should be celebrated with animals.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: कुपितास्ते ततः सर्वे मुनयः सूर्यवर्चसः॥ ऊचुर्वसुं विमानस्थं देवपक्षार्थवादिनम्। सुरपक्षो गृहीतस्ते यस्मात् तस्माद् दिवः पत॥ अद्यप्रभृति ते राजन्नाकाशे विहता गतिः। असाच्छापाभिघातेन महीं भित्त्वा प्रवेक्ष्यसि॥ (विरुद्धं वेदसूत्राणामुक्तं यदि भवेन्नृप। वयं विरुद्धवचना यदि तत्र पतामहे।।)
en: At this answer, all the Rishis, effulgent like the Sun, became very angry. Addressing Vasu who was seated on his car and who had supported the deities, they said to him,-Since you have unfairly sided with the gods, do you fall down from heaven! From this day, O king, you shall lose the power of passing through the sky! Through our curse, you shall sink deep below the surface of the Earth.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: ततस्तस्मिन् मुहूर्तेऽथ राजोपरिचरस्तदा। अधो वै सम्बभूवाशु भूमेर्विवरगो नृप॥
en: After the Rishis had said these words, king Uparichara immediately dropped down, O king, and went down a hole in the Earth. At the command, however,. of Narayana, Vasu's memory did not leave him.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: स्मृतिस्त्वेनं न हि जहौ तदा नारायणाज्ञया। देवास्तु सहिताः सर्वे वसोः शापविमोक्षणम्॥
en: To the good fortune of Vasu, the gods, pained at the curse imprecated on him by the Brahmanas, began to think anxiously as to how that curse might be removed.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: चिन्तयामासुरव्यग्राः सुकृतं हि नृपस्य तत्। अनेनास्मत्कृते राज्ञा शापः प्राप्तो महात्मना॥
en: They said, This great king has been cursed for our sake. We, dwellers of heaven, should unite together for doing what is good to him in return for what he has done to us.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: अस्य प्रतिप्रियं कार्यं सहितै! दिवौकसः। इति बुद्ध्या व्यवस्याशु गत्वा निश्चयमीश्वराः॥ ऊचुः संहष्टमनसो राजोपरिचरं तदा। ब्रह्मण्यदेवभक्तस्त्वं सुरासुरगुरुर्हरिः॥ कामं स तव तुष्टात्मा कुर्याच्छापविमोक्षणम्।
en: Having speedily determined this in their minds with the help of reflection, the gods went where king Uparichara was. Arrived before him, they addressed his, saying,-You are devoted to the great God of the Brahmanas (viz., Narayana)! That great Lord of both the gods and the Asuras, pleased with you, will save you from the curse that has been imprecated upon you.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: मानना तु द्विजातीनां कर्तव्या वै महात्मनाम्॥ अवश्यं तपसा तेषां फलितव्यं नृपोत्तम।
en: It is proper, however, that the great Brahmanas should be honoured. Verily, O best of kings, their penances should bear fruits.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: यतस्त्वं सहसा भ्रष्ट आकाशान्मेदिनीतलम्॥ एकं त्वनुग्रहं तुभ्यं दद्मो वै दद्मो वै नृपसत्तमा यावत् त्वं शापदोषेण कालमासिष्यसेऽनघ।॥
en: Indeed, you have already fallen down from the sky on the Earth! We wish, however, O best of kings, to show you a favour. As long as you, O sinless one, will live in this hole, so long you will receive (due sustenance).

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: भूमेर्विवरगो भूत्वा तावत् त्वं कालमाप्स्यसि। यज्ञेषु सुहुतां विप्रैर्वसोर्धारां समाहितैः॥ प्राप्स्यसेऽस्मदनुध्यानान्मा च त्वां ग्लानिरस्पृशत्।
en: You will get those streaks of clarified butter which Brahmanas with concentrated minds pour in sacrifices along with sacred Mantras, and which are called by the name of Vasudhara! Indeed, weakness or distress shall hot affect you.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: न क्षुत्पिपासे राजेन्द्र भूमेश्छिद्रे भविष्यतः॥ वसोर्धाराभिपीतत्वात् तेजसाऽऽप्यायितेन च। स देवोऽस्मद्वरात् प्रीतो ब्रह्मलोकं हि नेष्यति॥
en: While living, O king of kings, in the hole of the Earth, neither hunger nor thirst shall assail you for you will drink those streaks of clarified butter called Vasudhara. Your energy also shall continue unabated. By virtue of this our boon that we grant you, the God of gods, viz., Narayana, will be pleased with you, and He will take you hence to the region of Brahman.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: एवं दत्त्वा वरं राज्ञे सर्वे ते च दिवौकसः। गताः स्वभवनं देवा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः॥
en: Having granted these boons to the king, the dwellers of heaven, as also all those Rishis having penances for wealth, returned each to his respective place.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: चक्रे वसुस्ततः पूजां विष्वक्सेनाय भारत। जप्यं जगौ च सततं नारायणमुखोद्गतम्॥
en: Then Vasu, O Bharata, began to worship the Creator of the universe and to recite silently those sacred Mantras that had come out of Narayana's mouth in days of yore.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: तत्रापि पञ्चभिर्यज्ञैः पञ्चकालानरिंदम। अयजद्धरिं सुरपतिं भूमेर्विवरगोऽपि सन्॥
en: Although living in a pit of the Earth, the king still adored Hari, the Lord of all the gods in the well-known five-sacrifices that are celebrating five times every day, O destroyer of enemies.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: ततोऽस्य तुष्टो भगवान् भक्त्या नारायणो हरिः। अनन्यभक्तस्य सतस्तत्परस्य जितात्मनः॥
en: On account of these adorations of his, Narayana, otherwise called Hari, became highly gratified with him who thus showed himself to be entirely devoted to Him. Who entirely depended upon Him as his sole refuge, and who had completely mastered his senses.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: वरदो भगवान् विष्णुः समीपस्थं द्विजोत्तमम्। गरुत्मन्तं महावेगमाबभाषेप्सितं तदा॥
en: The illustrious Vishnu, that giver of boons, then addressed the fleet Garuda, that foremost of birds, who waited upon Him as his servant, and said these desirable words.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: द्विजोत्तम महाभाग पश्यतां वचनान्मम। सम्राट् राजा वसुर्नाम धर्मात्मा संशितव्रतः॥ ब्राह्मणानां प्रकोपेन प्रविष्टो वसुधातलम्।
en: O foremost of birds, O you who are highly blessed, listen to what I say. There is a great king named Vasu who is of righteous soul and rigid vows! Through the anger of the Brahmanas, he has dropped into a pit of the Earth.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: मानितास्ते तु विप्रेन्द्रास्त्वं तु गच्छ द्विजोत्तम॥
en: The Brahmanas have been sufficiently honoured. Do you go to that king now.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: भूमेर्विवरसंगुप्तं गरुडेह ममाज्ञया। अधश्चरं नृपश्रेष्ठं खेचरं कुरु मा चिरम्॥
en: At my behest, O Garuda, go to that foremost of kings, viz., Uparichara, who is now living in a hole of the Earth and incapable of any longer passing through the sky, and bring him up forthwith into the sky.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: गरुत्मानथ विक्षिप्य पक्षौ मारुतवेगवान्। विवेश विवरं भूमेर्यत्रास्ते पार्थिवो वसुः॥
en: Hearing these words of Vishnu, Garuda, spreading his wings and going with the speed of the wind, entered that pit in the Earth in which king Vasu was residing.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: तत एनं समुत्क्षिप्य सहसा विनतासुतः। उत्पपात नभस्तूर्णं तत्र चैनममुञ्चत॥
en: All on a sudden taking the king up, the son of Vinata soared into the sky and there released the king from his beaks.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते संजज्ञे राजोपरिचरः पुनः। सशरीरो गतश्चैव ब्रह्मलोकं नृपोत्तमः॥
en: At that moment, king Uparichara once more acquired his divine form and re-entered the region of Brahman.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: एवं तेनापि कौन्तेय वाग्दोषाद् देवताज्ञया। प्राप्ता गतिरवस्तात् तु द्विजशापान्महात्मना॥
en: It was the way, O son of Kunti, that that great king first dropped down through the curse of the Brahmanas for a faulty speech, and once more got up to heaven at the behest of the great God (Vishnu).

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: केवलं पुरुषस्तेन सेवितो हरिरीश्वरः। ततः शीघ्रं जहौ शापं ब्रह्मलोकमवाप च॥
en: Only the powerful Lord Hari, that foremost of all Beings, was devoutly adored by him. It was for this devout worship that the king succeeded very soon in freeing himself from the curse imprecated upon him by the Brahmanas and in regaining the blessed regions of Brahman.

description: The discussion whether goats should be sacrificed. The fall of King Vasu
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं सम्भूता मानवा यथा। नारदोऽपि यथा श्वेतं द्वीपं स गतवानृषिः। तत् ते सर्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमना नृप।॥
en: Bhishma said I have thus told you everything regarding the origin of the spiritual sons of Brahman. Listen to me with rapt attention, for I shall now describe to you how the celestial Rishi Narada had proceeded in days of yore to White Island."

description: Narada worships Narayana in the White Island
sn: भीष्म उवाच प्राप्य श्वेतं महाद्वीपं नारदो भगवानृषिः। ददर्श तानेव नराश्वेतांश्चन्द्रसमप्रभान्॥
en: Bhishma said "Arrived at the spacious kingdom called White Island, the illustrious Rishi saw those same white men effulgent like the sun.

description: Narada worships Narayana in the White Island
sn: पूजयामास शिरसा मनसा तैश्च पूजितः। दिदृक्षुर्जप्यपरमः सर्वकृच्छ्रगतः स्थितः॥
en: Adored by them, the Rishi worshipped them in return by bending his head and respecting them in his mind. Desirous of seeing Narayana, he began to live there, attentively engaged in the silent recitation of Mantras sacred to him, and practising the most difficult VOWS.

description: Narada worships Narayana in the White Island
sn: भूत्वैकाग्रमना विप्र उर्ध्वबाहुः समाहितः। स्तोत्रं जगौ स विश्वाय निर्गुणाय गुणात्मने॥
en: With rapt mind, the twice-born Rishi, with arms upraised, stood in Yoga, and then sang the following hymn to the Lord of the universe, Him, viz., who is at once the soul of attributes and divested of ali attributes.

पृश्निगर्भप्रवृत्त १६७ प्रवृत्तवेदक्रिय १६८ अज १६९ सर्वगते १७० सर्वदर्शिन् १७१ अग्राह्य १७२ अचल १७३ महाविभूते १७४ माहात्म्यशरीर १७५ पवित्र १७६ महापवित्र १७७ हिरण्यमय १७८ बृहत् १७९ अप्रतळ १८० अविज्ञेय १८१ ब्रह्मण्य १८२ प्रजासर्गकर १८३ प्रजानिधनकर १८४ महामायाधर १८५ चित्रशिखण्डिन् १८६ वरप्रद १८७ पुरोडाशभागहर १८८ गताध्वर १८९ छिन्नतृष्ण १९० छिन्नसंशय १९१ सर्वतोवृत्त १९२ निवृत्तिरूप १९३ ब्राह्मणरूप १९४ ब्राह्मणप्रिय १९५ विश्वमूर्ते १९६ महामूर्ते १९७ बान्धव १९८ १९९ ब्रह्मण्यदेव भक्तोऽहं त्वां दिदृक्षुरेकान्तदर्शनाय २०० नमो भक्तवत्सल नमः॥
en: Narada said “Salutation to you, O God of gods, O you that are freed from all acts! You are he who is divested of all attributes, who is the Witness of all the worlds, who is called Soul, who is the foremost of all Beings, who is Infinite, who is called Purusha, who is the great Purusha, who is the foremost of all Purushas, who is the soul of the three attributes, who is called the Foremost, who is Amrita (nectar), who is called Immortal, who is called Ananta (Sesha), who is Space, who is without beginning, who is both Manifest and Unmanifest as existent and not-existent things, who is said to have his home in Truth, who is the first of gods (Narayana), who is the giver of riches, who is at one with Daksha and other Lords of the Creation, who is the Ashvatha and other big trees, who is the four-headed Brahman, who is the Lord of all created Beings, who is the Lord of Speech, who is the Lord of universe, who is the all-pervading Soul, who is the Sun, who is the breath called Prana, who is the King of the waters, who is at one with the King, who is at one with the Regents of the quarters, who is the refuge of the universe when it is dissolved in the final destruction, who is unrevealed, who is the giver of the Vedas to Brahman, who is at one with the sacrifices and Vedic studies acquired by Brahmanas with the help of their bodies, who is at one with the four principal orders of the gods, who is every one of those four orders, who is endued with effulgence, who is endued with great effuigence, who is he to whom the seven largest offerings in sacrifices are presented with the Gayatri and other sacred Mantras, who is Yama, who is Chitragupta and the other attendants of Yama, who is called the wife of Yama who is that order of the gods called Tushita, who is that other order called Maha-Tushita, who is the Death, who is desire and all diseases that have been created for helping the advent of Death, who is health and freedom from disease, who is subject to desire and passions, who is free from desire and passions, who is Infinite as shown in species and forms, who is he who is punished, who is he who is the punisher, who is all the lesser sacrifices, who is all the larger sacrifices, who is all the priests, who is the origin of all sacrifices, who is fire, who is the very heart of all sacrifices, who is he that is sung sacrifices, who takes those shares of the sacrificial offerings which are presented to him, who is the embodiment of the five sacrifices, who is the maker of the five divisions of time, who is incapable of being understood except by those scriptures which are called Pancharatra, who never shrinks from anything, who is undefeated, who is only Mind, who is known only by name, who is the Lord of Brahman himself, who has finished all the vows and observances mentioned in the Vedas, who is the swan, who is the great swan, who is the foremost of swans, who is the in yoga, who is the embodiment of the Sankhya philosophy, who lives in all Individual Souls, who lives in every heart, who lives in every sense, who floats on the ocean-water, who lives in the Vedas, who lies on the lotus, who is the Lord of the universe, and whose troops go on all sides for protecting his worshippers! You take birth as all creatures! You are the origin of the universe! Your mouth is fire! You are that fire which passes through the waters of the ocean, coming out all the while from an Equine head! You are the sanctified butter which is poured into the sacrificial fire! You are the cardriver! You are Vashat! You are the syllable OM! You are Penances! You are Mind! You are butter! You are the Sun! You are the Elephants which are stationed in the four cardinal points! You light up the cardinal points of the compass. You light up the subsidiary points also! You are the Equine head! You are the first three Mantras of the Rigveda! You are the protector of all the castes! You are the five fires! You are He who has thrice lighted the sacrificial fire called Nachi! You are the refuge of the Vedas, having six limbs! You are the foremost of those Brahmanas who are engaged in singing the Samans in sacrifices and other religious rites. You are Pragjyotish. And you are he who sings the first Saman! You are the observer of those vows which depend upon the Vedas and which are observed by singers of Saman! You are the embodiment of the Upanishad called by the name of Atharvashiras. You are he who is the subject-matter of the of the five foremost of scriptures! You are called the preceptor who subsists only on the froth of water. You are a Valikhilya. You are the embodiment of him who has not deviated from Yoga. You are the embodiment of correctness of judgement or reasoning. You are the beginning of the cycles, you are the middle of the cycles, and you are their end! You are Akhandala. You are the two Rishis Prachina-garbha and Kaushika! You are Purustuta, you are Puruhuta, you are the designer of the universe. You have the universe for your form. Infinite are your motions. Your bodies are infinite! You are without end and are are are without beginning, and without middle. Your middle is unmanifest. Your end is unmanifest. You have vows for your residence. You live in the ocean. You have your home in Fame, in Penances, in Self-control, in Prosperity, in Knowledge, in grand feats, and in Everything belonging to the universe! You are Vasudeva. You are the grantor of every wish. You are the monkey that carried Rama on his shoulders. You are the great Horsc-sacrifice. You partake of offerings made in great sacrifices! You are the grantor of boons, of happiness, of wealth. You are devoted to Hari! You are Restraint of the senses. You are vows and observances, You are mortifications, you severe mortifications, you very severe mortifications. You are he who practises vows and religious and other pious rites. You are freed from all mistakes. You a Brahmacharin. You took birth in the womb of Prishni. You are are he from whom have originated all Vedic rites and acts. You originated all Vedic rites and acts. You are unborn. You pervade all things. Your eyes are on all things. You must not be apprehended by the senses. You are not subject to decay. You are endued with great power. Your body is inconceivably vast. You are holy, you are very holy. You are golden. You are vast. You are beyond the range of logic or argument. You are unknowable. You are the foremost of Causes. You are the Creator of all creatures and you are their destroyer. You are the possessor of great powers of illusion. You are called Chittrashikhandin. You are the giver of boons. You partake of the sacrificial offerings. You have acquired the merit of all sacrifices. You are he who has been freed from all doubts. You are omnipresent. You are of the form of a Brahmana. You are fond of Brahmanas. You have the universe for your form. Your form is very huge. You are the greatest friend. You are kind to all your worshippers. You are the great god of the Brahmanas. I am your devoted disciple. I am desirous of seeing you. Salutations to you who are of the form of Liberation."

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवं स्तुतः स भगवान् गुस्तिथ्यैश्च नामभिः। तं मुनि दर्शयामास नारदं विश्वरूपधृक्॥
en: Bhishma said Thus sung with names that were not known to others, the Divine Narayana having the universe for his form appeared before the ascetic Narada.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: किंचिच्चन्द्राद् विशुद्धात्मा किंचिच्चन्द्राद् विशेषवान्। कृशानुवर्णः किंचिच्च किंचिद्धिष्ण्याकृतिः प्रभुः॥
en: His form was some what purer than the moon and differed from the moon in some particulars. He somewhat resembled a burning fire in complexion. The powerful Lord was somewhat of the form of Vishti,

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: शुकपत्रनिभः किंचित् किंचित्स्फटिकसंनिभः। नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यो जातरूपप्रभः क्वचित्॥
en: He looked in some respects like the feathers of the parrot, and in some a collection of pure crystal. He resembled in some respects a hill of antimony and in some a mass of pure gold.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: प्रवालाङ्कुरवर्णश्च श्वेतवर्णस्तथा क्वचित्। क्वचित् सुवर्णवर्णाभो वैदूर्यसदृशः क्वचित्॥
en: His complexion somewhat resembled the coral when first formed, and was somewhat white. That complexion resembled in some respects the colour of gold and in some that of the lapis lazulus.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: नीलवैदूर्यसदृश इन्द्रनीलनिभः क्वचित्। मयूरग्रीववर्णाभो मुक्ताहारनिभः क्वचित्॥
en: It resembled in some respects the colour of the blue lapis lazulus and in some that of sapphire. It resembled in some respects of colour of the peacock's neck, and in some that of a string of pearls.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: एतान् बहुविधान् वर्णान् रूपैर्बिभ्रत्सनातनः। सहस्रनयनः श्रीमाञ्छतशीर्षः सहस्रपात्॥
en: Bearing these various sorts of hues on his body the eternal Deity appeared before Narada. He had a thousand eyes and was endued with great beauty. He had a hundred heads and a hundred feet.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सहस्रोदरबाहुश्च अव्यक्ता इति च क्वचित्। ओङ्कारमुद्गिरन् वक्त्रात् सावित्री च तदन्वयाम्॥
en: He had a thousand stomachs and a thousand arms. He seemed to be still inconceivable to the mind. With one of his mouths he uttered the syllable OM and then the Gayatri following OM.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: शेषेभ्यश्चैव वक्त्रेभ्यश्चतुर्वेदान् गिरन् बहून्। आरण्यकं जगौ देवो हरिर्नारायणो वशी॥
en: With mind under complete mastery, the great God, called by the names of Hari and Narayana, by his other mouths, many in nụmber, uttered many Mantras from the four Vedas which are known by the name of Aranyaka.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: वेदि कमण्डलुं शुभ्रान् मणीनुपानहौ कुशान्। अजिनं दण्डकाष्ठं च ज्वलितं च हुताशनम्॥
en: The Lord of all the gods, the great God who is worshipped in sacrifices, held in his hands a sacrificial altar, a Kamandalu, a few white gems, a pair of shoes, a bundle of Kusha blades, a deer-skin, a tooth-stick, and a little burning fire.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: धारयामास देवेशो हस्तैर्यज्ञपतिस्तदा। तं प्रसन्नं प्रसन्नात्मा नारदो द्विजसत्तमः॥
en: With a cheerful heart, that foremost of twice-born one viz., Narada, controlling speech, bowed to the great God and worshipped Him.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: वाग्यतः प्रणतो भूत्वा ववन्दे परमेश्वरम्। तमुवाच नतं मूर्धा देवानामादिरव्ययः॥
en: The first of all the gods, who is free from decay, said the following words to him whose head was still bent low in veneration.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितश्चैव महर्षयः। इमं देशमनुप्राप्ता मम दर्शनलालसाः॥
en: The Holy One said The great Rishis, Ekata, Dvita, and Trita, came to this country from desire of seeing me.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: न च मां ते ददृशिरे न च द्रक्ष्यति कथश्चन। ऋते ौकान्तिकश्रेष्ठात् त्वं चैवैकान्तिकोत्तमः॥
en: Their wishes, however, were not fulfilled. Excepting those who are devoted to with wholly and solely, no else can see me. As regards you, you are verily the foremost of all persons devoted to me with all their souls.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: ममैतास्तनवः श्रेष्ठा जाता धर्मगृहे द्विज। तास्त्वं भजस्व सततं साधयस्व यथागतम्॥
en: These are my bodies, the best ones that I assume. These were born, O twice-born one, in the house of Dharma. Do you worship them always, and do you perform those rites that are laid down in the ordinances in connexion with that worship.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: वृणीष्व च वरं विप्र मत्तस्त्वं यदिहेच्छसि। प्रसन्नोऽहं तवायेह विश्वमूर्तिरिहाव्ययः॥
en: O Brahmana, do you ask of me the boons you wish! I am pleased with you to-day and I appear to you now in my universal form as freed from decay and deterioration!

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: नारद उवाच अद्य मे तपसो देव यमस्य नियमस्य च। सद्यः फलमवाप्तं वै दृष्टो यद् भगवान् मया॥
en: Narada said Since, O holy one, I have to-day succeeded in seeing you, I think that I have acquired forthwith the fruits of my penances, O God, of my self-restraint, and of all the vows and observances that I have practised.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: वर एष ममात्यन्तं दृष्टस्त्वं यत् सनातनः। भगवन् विश्वदृक् सिंहः सर्वमूर्तिमहान् प्रभुः॥
en: This, indeed, is the highest boon you have granted me for you have appeared before me to-day, O Eternal Lord! You, O holy one, have the universe for your eye! You are the Lion. Your form is identifiable with everything! Possessed of power you, O Lord, are vast and infinite.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
