sn: भीष्म उवाच एवं संदर्शयित्वा तु नारदं परमेष्ठिनम्। उवाच वचनं भूयो गच्छ नारद मा चिरम्॥
en: Bhishma said Having thus appeared before Narada the son of Parameshthi, the great God addressed that ascetic and said,-Go hence, O Narada, and do not delay!

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: इमे ह्यनिन्द्रियाहारा मद्भक्ताश्चन्द्रवर्चसः। एकाग्राश्चिन्तयेयुर्मी नैषां विघ्नो भवेदिति॥
en: These worshippers of mine, having moonlike complexions, are divested of all senses and do not live upon any kind of food. They are, again, all Liberated! With minds wholly concentrated upon me, people should think of me. Such worshippers will never meet with any obstacles.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सिद्धा ह्येते महाभागाः पुरा ह्येकान्तिनोऽभवन्। तमोरजोभिर्निर्मुक्ता मां प्रवेक्ष्यन्त्यसंशयम्॥
en: These men have all acquired ascetic success and are highly blessed. In day of yore they became entirely devoted to me. They have becn freed from the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance. Forsooth, they are competent to enter me and become merged into my Self.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: न दृश्यश्चक्षुषा योऽसौ न स्पृश्यः स्पर्शनेन च। न घेयश्चैव गन्धेन रसेन च विवर्जितः॥ सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चैव न गुणास्तं भजन्ति वै। यश्च सर्वगतः साक्षी लोकस्यात्मेति कथ्यते॥ भूतग्रामशरीरेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति। अजो नित्यः शाश्वतश्च निर्गुणो निष्कलस्तथा॥ द्विादशेभ्यस्तत्त्वेभ्यः ख्यातो यः पञ्चविंशकः। पुरुषो निष्क्रियश्चैव ज्ञानदृश्यश्च कथ्यते॥ यं प्रविश्य भवन्तीह मुक्ता वै द्विजसत्तमाः। स वासुदेवो विज्ञेयः परमात्मा सनातनः॥
en: He who cannot be seen with the eye, touched with the sense of touch, smelt with the sense of scent, and who is beyond the sense of taste, He whom the three qualities of goodness. Darkness, and Ignorance do not touch, who permeates all things and is the one Witness of the universe, and who is described as the Soul of the entire universe, He who is not destroyed upon the destruction of the bodies of all created things, who is unborn and unchangeable and eternal, who is freed from all qualities, who is indivisible and entire, He who is above the twenty-four topics of enquiry and is considered the Twenty-fifth, who is called by the name of Twenty-fifth, who is called by the name of Purusha, who is inactive, and who is said to be apprehended by Knowledge alone, He into whom the foremost of twice-born ones enter and become liberated, He is the eternal Supreme Soul and is known by the name of Vasudeva.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: पश्य देवस्य माहात्म्यं महिमानं च नारद। शुभाशुभैः कर्मभिर्यो न लिप्यति कदाचन॥
en: See, O Narada, the greatness and power of that God! He is never affected by good or bad deeds.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति गुणानेतान् प्रचक्षते। यत्ते सर्वशरीरेषु तिष्ठन्ति विचरन्ति च॥
en: Satvata, Rajas, and Tamas, are said to be the three (original) qualities. These live and act in the bodies of all creatures.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: एतान् गुणांस्तु क्षेत्रज्ञो भुङ्क्ते नैभिः स भुज्यते। निर्गुणो गुणभुक् चैव गुणस्रष्टा गुणाधिकः॥
en: The Individual Soul, called Kshetrajna, enjoys and suffers the action of these three qualities. He, however, is above them and they cannot touch Him. Freed from these qualities, He is again their enjoyer and sufferer. Having created them Himself, He is above them all.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: जगत्प्रतिष्ठा देवर्षे पृथिव्यप्सु प्रलीयते। ज्योतिष्यापः प्रलीयन्ते ज्योतिर्वायौ प्रलीयते॥ खे वायुः प्रलयं याति मनस्याकाशमेव च। मनो हि परमं भूतं तदव्यक्ते प्रलीयते॥
en: O celestial Rishi, the Earth, which is the refuge of the universe, disappears into water. Water disappears into Fire and Fire into Wind. Wind disappears into Ether, and Ether into Mind. Mind is a great creature, and it disappears into Unmanifest Nature.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: अव्यक्तं पुरुषे ब्रह्मन् निष्क्रिये सम्प्रलीयते। नास्ति तस्मात् परतरः पुरुषाद् वै सनातनात्॥
en: Unmanifest Nature, 0 Brahmana, disappears into Inactive Purusha (Soul). There is nothing higher than Purusha (Soul) which is Eternal.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: नित्यं हि नास्ति जगति भूतं स्थावरजङ्गमम्। ऋते तमेकं पुरुषं वासुदेवं सनातनम्॥
en: There is nothing among mobile and immobile things in the universe which is immutable, except Vasudeva, the eternal Purusha.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सर्वभूतात्मभूतो हि वासुदेवो महाबलः। पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम्॥ ते समेता महात्मानः शरीरमिति संज्ञितम्। तदा विशति यो ब्रह्मन्नदृश्यो लघुविक्रमः॥ उत्पन्न एव भवति शरीरं चेष्टयन् प्रभुः। न विना धातुसंघातं शरीरं भवति क्वचित्॥
en: Endued with great power, Vasudeva is the Soul of all creatures. Earth, Wind, Ether, Water, and Fire forming fifth, are primal clephants of great power. Mingling together they form the body. Possessed of subtile prowess and invisible to all eyes, O Brahmana, the powerful Vasudeva then enter that combination of the five principal elements called body. Such entrance is called his birth, and taking birth He makes the body move about and act. Without a combination of the five principal elements, 110 body can ever be formed.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: न च जीवं विना ब्रह्मन् वायवश्चेष्टयन्त्युत। स जीवः परिसंख्यातः शेषः संकर्षणः प्रभुः॥
en: Without, again, the entrance of Individual Soul into the body, the mind living within it cannot cause it move and act. He that enters the body is possessed of great power and is called Individual. He is known also by other names, viz., Shesha and Sankarshana.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: तस्मात् सनत्कुमारत्वं योऽलभत् स्वेन कर्मणा। यस्मिश्च सर्वभूतानि प्रलयं यान्ति संक्षयम्॥ स मनः सर्वभूतानां प्रद्युम्न परिपठ्यते।
en: He who takes his his rise, from that Sankarshana, by his own acts, Sanatkumara, and in whom all creatures merge when the universal dissolution sets in, is the Mind of all creatures and is called by the name of Praddyumna.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: तस्मात् प्रसूतो यः कर्ता कारणं कार्यमेव च।॥ न च जीवं विना ब्रह्मन् वायवश्वेश्यन्त्युत। तस्मात् सर्वं सम्भवति जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्। सोऽनिरुद्धः स ईशानो व्यक्तः स सर्वकर्मसु॥
en: From Him originates. He who is the Creator, and who is both Cause and Effect. From this last, everything, viz., the mobile and immobile universe, originates. This one is called Aniruddha. He is otherwise called Ishana and He is manifest in all deeds.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: यो वासुदेवो भगवान् क्षेत्रज्ञो निर्गुणात्मकः। ज्ञेयः स एव राजेन्द्र जीव: संकर्षणः प्रभुः॥
en: That illustrious one, viz., Vasudeva, who is called Kshetrajna, (Soul) and who is freed from qualities, should, O king of kings, be known as the powerful Sankarshana, when He takes birth as (Individual Soul).

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: संकर्षणाच्च प्रद्युम्नो मनोभूतः स उच्यते। प्रद्युम्नाद् योऽनिरुद्धस्तु सोऽहंकारः स ईश्वरः॥
en: From Sankarshana originates Praddyumna who is called “Mind-begotten." From Praddymuna is He who is Aniruddha. He is Consciousness, He is Ishvara (Supreme Lord).

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: मत्तः सर्वं सम्भवति जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्। अक्षरं च क्षरं चैव सच्चासच्चैव नारद॥
en: It is from me that the entire mobile and immobile universe originates. It is from me, O Narada, that the indestructible and the destructible, the existent and the non-existent, originates.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: गुरुः। मां प्रविश्य भवन्तीह मुक्ता भक्तास्तु ये मम्। अहं कि पुरुषो ज्ञेयो निष्क्रियः पञ्चविंशकः॥
en: They who are devoted to me enter into me and become liberated. I am known as Purusha. Without acts, I am the Twenty-fifth.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: निर्गुणो निष्कलश्चैव निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः। एतत् त्वा न विज्ञेयं रूपवानिति दृश्यते॥ इच्छन् मुहूर्तान्नश्येयमीशोऽहं जगतो
en: Getting over qualities, I am entire and indivisible. I am above all pairs of opposite and shorn of all attachments. This, O Narada, you will fail to understand. You see me as having a form. If I wish, I can dissolve this form in a moment. I am the Supreme Lord and the Preceptor of the universe.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: माया ह्येषा मया सृष्टा यन्मां पश्यसि नारद॥ सर्वभूतगुणैर्युक्तं नैव त्वं ज्ञातुमर्हसि। मयैतत् कथितं सम्यक् तव मूर्तिचतुष्टयम्॥
en: What you see of me, ONarada, is merely an illusion of mine. I now appear to be possessed of the attributes of all created things. You are not competent to know me. I have shown to you duly my fourfold form. I am, O Narada, the doer, I am Cause, and I am Effect.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: अहं हि जीवसंज्ञातो मयि जीवः समाहितः। नैव ते बुद्धिरत्राभूद् दृष्टो जीवो मयेति वै॥
en: I am the sum-total of all living creatures. All living creatures have their refuge in me, Do not think that you have seen the Individual Soul.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: अहं सर्वत्रगो ब्रह्मन् भूतग्रामान्तरात्मकः। भूतग्रामशरीरेषु नश्यत्सु न नशाम्यहम्॥
en: I pervade all things, O Brahmana, and am the inner Soul of all creatures. When the bodies of all creatures, however, are destroyed, I am not destroyed.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सिद्धा हि ते महाभागा नरा ह्येकान्तिनोऽभवन्। तमोरजोभ्यां निर्मुक्ताः प्रवेक्ष्यन्ति च मां मुने॥
en: Those highly blessed men who, having acquired ascetic success, become entirely devoted to me, become freed from the qualities of both Darkness and Ignorance and succeed, therefore, in entering me, O great ascetic.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: हिरण्यगर्भो लोकादिश्चतुर्वक्त्रोऽनिरुक्तगः। ब्रह्मा सनातनो देवो मम बह्वर्थचिन्तकः॥
en: He called Hiranyagarbha, who is the beginning of the world, who has four faces, who cannot be understood with the help of the Nirukta, who is otherwise called Brahman, who is an eternal god, is engaged in loO king after many of my works.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: ललाटाच्चैव मे रुद्रो देवः क्रोधाद् विनिःसृतः। पश्यैकादश मे रुद्रान् दक्षिणं पार्श्वमास्थितान्॥
en: The god Rudra, born of my anger, originated from my forehead. See, the eleven Rudras are increasing on the right side of my person.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: द्वादशैव तथाऽऽदित्यान् वामपार्वे समास्थितान्। अग्रतश्चैव मे पश्य वसूनष्टौ सुरोत्तमान्॥ नासत्यं चैव दस्रं च भिषजौ पश्य पृष्ठतः। सर्वान् प्रजापतीन् पश्य पश्य सप्त ऋषींस्तथा॥
en: The twelve Adityas are on the left side of my person. See the eight Vasus, those foremnost of gods, are in my front, and see, Nasatya and Dasra, those two celestial physicians, are in the rear. See also in my body all the Prajapatis and see the seven Rishis Also.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: वेदान् यज्ञांश्च शतशः पश्यामृतमथौषधीः। तपांसि नियमांश्चैव यमानपि पृथग्विधान्॥
en: See also the Vedas, all the Sacrifices numbering by hundreds, the Amrita (nectar), and all the (medicinal) herbs and plants, and Penances, and vows and observances of various sorts.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: तथाष्टगुणमैश्वर्यमेकस्थं पश्य मूर्तिमत्। श्रियं लक्ष्मी च कीर्तिं च पृथिवीं च ककुदिनीम्॥
en: See also in me the eight attributes of power, viz., those particularly called the Lordly powers, living all together in my body in their united and embodied form. See also Shree and Lakshmi, and Kirti, and the Earth with her hump.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: वेदानां मातरं पश्य मत्स्थां देवीं सरस्वतीम्। ध्रुवं च ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठ पश्य नारद खेचरम्॥
en: See the goddess Sarasvati, that mother of the Vedas, living in me! See, O Narada, Dhruva, that foremost of luminaries ranging in the sky.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: अम्भोधरान् समुद्रांश्च सरांसि सरितस्तथा। मूर्तिमन्तः पितृगणांश्चतुरः पश्य सत्तम॥ त्रींश्चैवेमान् गुणान् पश्य मत्स्थान् मूर्तिविवर्जितान्।
en: See also all the Oceans, those receptacles of water, and lakes, and rivers. See, also, O best of men, the four foremost ones amongst the Pitris in their embodied forms. See also, living in me, the three qualities (of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas) which are formless.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: देवकार्यादपि मुने पितृकार्यं विशिष्यते॥ देवानां च पितॄणां च पिता ह्येकोऽहमादितः।
en: The acts done in honour of the departed mane are superior to those done in honour of the gods. I am the Pitri of the both the gods and the Pitris, and am existing from the beginning.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: अहं हयशिरा भूत्वा समुद्रे पश्चिमोत्तरे॥ पिबामि सुहुतं हव्यं कव्यं च श्रद्धयान्वितम्।
en: Becoming the Equine-head I pass through the Western and the Northern ocean and drink sacrificial libations duly poured with Mantras and solid sacrificial food offered with respect and devotion.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: मया सृष्टः पुरा ब्रह्मा मां यज्ञमयजत् स्वयम्॥ ततस्तस्मिन् वरान् प्रीतो दत्त्वानसम्यनुत्तमान्।
en: In ancient times I created Brahman who himself worshipped me in sacrifices. Pleased with him on that account I granted him many excellent boons.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: मत्पुत्रत्वं च कल्पादौ लोकाध्यक्षत्वमेव च॥ अहंकारकृतं चैव नाम पर्यायवाचकम्।
en: I said to him that in the beginning of the cycle he would be born to me as my son, and the sovereignty of all the worlds would he enjoy, and various names will be given to diverse objects on account of the Ahankara, i. e., egoism, coming into existence.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: त्वया कृतां च मर्यादा नातिक्रस्यति कश्चन॥ त्वं चैव वरदो ब्रह्मन् वरेप्सूनां भविष्यसि। सुरासुरगणानां च ऋषीणां च तपोधन॥
en: I also told him that none would ever violate the limits and boundaries he would lay down, and, further that he would be the giver of boons to persons who would solicit him for the same.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: पितॄणां च महाभाग सततं संशितव्रत। विविधानां च भूतानां त्वमुपास्यो भविष्यसि॥
en: I further assured him that he would be an object of worship with all the gods and Asuras, all the Rishis and Pitris, and the various creatures forming the creation.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: प्रादुर्भावगतश्चाहं सुरकार्येषु नित्यदा। अनुशास्यस्त्वया ब्रह्मन् नियोज्यश्च सुतो यथा।॥
en: I also gave him to understand that I would always appear for performing the business of the gods and for that I would allow myself to be commanded by him even as a son by his father.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: एतांश्चान्यांश्च रुचिरान् ब्रह्मणेऽमिततेजसे। अहं दत्त्वा वरान् प्रीतो निवृत्तिपरमोऽभवम्॥
en: Granting these and other highly agreeable boons to Brahman of great energy on account of my being propitiated with him I adopted the course dictated by Renunciation.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: निर्वाणं सर्वधर्माणां निवृत्तिः परमा स्मृता। तस्मान्निवृत्तिमापन्नश्चरेत् सर्वाङ्गनिर्वृतः॥
en: The highest Renunciation is the annihilation of all duties and acts. Hence, by adopting Renunciation one should act in complete happiness.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: विद्यासहायवन्तं च आदित्यस्थं समाहितम्। कपिलं प्राहुराचार्याः सांख्यनिश्चितनिश्चयाः॥
en: Learned preceptors, with settled conclusions deducted from the truths of the Sankhya philosophy, have spoken of me as Kapila endued with the power of knowledge, living within the effulgence of the Sun, and concentrated in Yoga.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: हिरण्यगर्भो भगवानेष च्छन्दसि सुष्टुतः। सोऽहं योगरतिर्ब्रह्मन् योगशास्त्रेषु शब्दितः॥
en: In the Vedas I have been repeatedly hymned as the illustrious Hiranyagarbha. In the Yoga-Shastras, O Brahmana, I have been spoken of as one who find pleasure in Yoga.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: एषोऽहं व्यक्तिमागत्य तिष्ठामि दिवि शाश्वतः। ततो युगसहस्रान्ते संहरिष्ये जगत् पुनः॥
en: I am eternal. Assuming a form that is manifest, I live at present, in the sky. At the end of a thousand cycles, I shall once more withdraw the universe into myself.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: कृत्वाऽऽत्मस्थानि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च। एकाकी विद्यया सार्धं विहरिष्ये जगत् पुनः॥
en: Having withdrawn all creatures, mobile and immobile, into myself, I shall exist all alone with Knowledge only as my companion.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: तयो भूयो जगत् सर्वं करिष्यामीह विद्यया। अस्मिन् मूर्तिश्चतुर्थी या सासृजज्छेषमव्ययम्॥
en: After the lapse of ages I shall again create the universe, with the help of that Knowledge. My fourth form creates the indestructible Shesha.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: स हि संकर्षणः प्रोक्तः प्रद्युम्नं सोऽप्यजीजनत्। प्रद्युम्नादनिरुद्धोऽहं सर्गो मम पुनः पुनः॥
en: That Shesha is called by the name of Sankarshana. Sankarshana creates Praddyumna. From Praddyumna I take birth myself as Aniruddha. I Aniruddha. I create (myself) repeatedly.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: अनिरुद्धात् तथा ब्रह्मा तन्नाभिकमलोद्भवः। ब्रह्मणः सर्वभूतानि चराणि स्थावराणि च॥
en: From Aniruddha originates Brahman. The latter is born from Aniruddha's navel. From Brahman originate all mobile and immobile creatures.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: एतां सृष्टिं विजानीहि कल्पादिषु पुनः पुनः। यथा सूर्यस्य गगनादुदयास्तमने इह॥
en: Know that Creation originates in this way repeatedly at the beginning of every cycle. Creation and destruction succeed each other like sunrise and sunset in this world.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: नष्टे पुनर्बलात् काल आनयत्यमितद्युतिः। तथा बलादहं पृथ्वी सर्वभूतहिताय वै॥ सत्त्वैराक्रान्तसर्वाङ्गां नष्टां सागरमेखलाम्। आनयिष्यामि स्वस्थानं वाराहं रूपमास्थितः॥ हिरण्याक्षं वधिष्यामि दैतेयं बलगवितम्।
en: Then, again, as Time, gifted with great energy, forcibly brings back the Sun after his disappearance, similarly I shall, assuming the form of a boar and displaying my strength, bring back the Earth with her belt of seas to her own position for the behoof of all creatures when she becomes submerged in water. I shall then kill the son of Diti, named Hiranyagarbha, elated with pride of strength.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: नारसिंहं वपुः कृत्वा हिरण्यकशिपुं पुनः॥ सुरकार्ये हनिष्यामि यज्ञघ्नं दितिनन्दनम्।
en: Assuming the form then of a Manlion, I shall, for doing good to the gods, kill Hiranyakasipu, the son of Diti, who will be a great destroyer of sacrifices.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: विरोचनस्य बलवान् बलिः पुत्रो महासुरः॥ अवध्यः सर्वलोकानां सदेवासुररक्षसाम्। भविष्यति स शक्रं वा स्वराज्याच्चयावयिष्यति॥
en: Virochana will have a powerful son named Vali. The entire universe consisting of gods, Asuras, and Rakshasas will not be able to kill that great Asura. He will hurl Shakra from the sovereignty of the universe.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: त्रैलोक्येऽपहते तेन विमुखे च शचीपतौ। अदित्यां द्वादशादित्यः सम्भविष्यामि कश्यपात्॥ (जटी गत्वा यज्ञसदः स्तूयमानो द्विजोत्तम। यज्ञस्तवं करिष्यामि श्रुत्वा प्रीतो भवेद् बलिः।। किमिच्छसि वटो बृहीत्युक्तो याचे महद् वरम्। दीयतां त्रिपदीमात्रमिति याचे महासुरम्।। स दद्यान्मयि सम्प्रीतः प्रतिषिद्धश्च मन्त्रिभिः। यावज्जलं हस्तगतं त्रिभिर्विक्रमणैर्वृतम्।।)
en: When after defeating the Lord of Shachi, that Asura will possess the sovereignty of the three worlds, I shall take birth in Aditi's womb, by Kashyapa, as the twelfth Aditya.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: ततो राज्यं प्रदास्यामि शक्रायामिततेजसे। देवताः स्थापयिष्यामि स्वस्वस्थानेषु नारद॥
en: I shall restore it to Indra of immeasurable splendour, and replace the gods, O Narada, in their respective stations,

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: बलिं चैव करिष्यामि पातालतलवासिनम्। दानवं च बलिं श्रेष्ठमवध्यं सर्वदैवतैः॥
en: As regards Vali, that foremost of Danavas, who is to be unslayable by all the gods, I shall cause him to live in the nether regions.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: त्रेतायुगे भविष्यामि रामो भृगुकुलोद्वहः। क्षत्रं चोत्सादयिष्यामि समृद्धबलवाहनम्॥
en: In the Treta age I shall take birth as Rama in the race of Bhrigu, and root out the Kshatriyas who will become proud of their strength and riches.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: संध्यांशे समनुप्राप्ते त्रेताया द्वापरस्य च। अहं दाशरथी रामो भविष्यामि जगत्पतिः॥
en: Towards the end of Treta and the beginning of Dvapara, I shall take birth as Rama the son of Dasharatha in Ikshvaku's race.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: त्रितोपघाताद् वैरूप्यमेकतोऽथ द्वितस्तथा। प्राप्स्येते वानरत्वं हि प्रजापति सुतावृषी॥
en: At that time, the two Rishis, viz., the two sons of Prajapati, called by the names of Ekata and Dvita, will on account of the injury done by them to their brother Trita, have to take birth as monkeys, losing the beauty of the human forin.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: तयोर्ये त्वन्वये जाता भविष्यन्ति वनौकसः। महाबला महावीर्याः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमाः॥ ते सहाया भविष्यन्ति सुरकार्ये मम द्विज।
en: Those monkeys that shall take birth in the race of Ekata and Dvita, shall become endued with great power and mighty energy and will equal Shakra himself in power. All those monkeys, O twice-born one, will become my allies for performing the work of the gods.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: ततो रक्षः :पति घोरं पुलस्त्यकुलपांसनम्॥ हरिष्ये रावणं रौद्रं सगणं लोककण्टकम्।
en: I shall then kill the dreadful king of the Rakshasas, that wretch of Pulastya's race, viz., the fierce Ravana, that thorn of all worlds, together with all his children and followers.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: द्वापरस्य कलेश्चैव संधौ पार्यवसानिके॥ प्रादुर्भाव: कंसहेतोर्मथुरायां भविष्यति।
en: At the junction the Dvapara and the Kali ages, I shall again appear in the world taking birth in city of Mathura for the purpose of killing Kansa.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: तत्राहं दानवान् हत्वा सुबहून् देवकण्टकान्॥ कुशस्थली करिष्यामि निवेशं द्वारकां पुरीम्।
en: There, after killing numberless Danavas that will be as thorns in the side of the gods, I shali take up my residence in Kushasthali at the city of Dwaraka.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: वसानस्तत्र वै पुर्यामदितेर्विप्रियंकरम्॥ हनिष्ये नरकं भौमं मुरं पीठं च दानवम्।
en: While living in that city I shall kill the Asura Naraka the chief of the Earth,-him, that is, who will do an injury to Aditi, as also some other Danavas of the names of Muru and Pitha.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: प्राग्ज्योतिषं पुरं रम्यं नानाधनसमन्वितम्॥ कुशस्थली नयिष्यामि हत्वा वै दानवोत्तमम्।
en: Killing also another foremost of Danavas, viz., the kill of Pragjyotisha, I shall transplant that delightful city furnished with various kinds of wealth into Dwaraka.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: महेश्वरमहासेनौ बाणप्रियहितैषिणौ॥ पराजेष्याम्यथायुक्तौ देवौ लोकनमस्कृतौ।
en: I shall then defeat the two gods adored of all the deities, viz., Maheshvara and Mahasena, who will become fond of the Danava Vana and do him various good offices and who will try their best for that worshipper of theirs.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: ततः सुतं बलेर्जित्वा बाणं बाहुसहस्रिणम्॥ विनाशयिष्यामि ततः सर्वान् सौभनिवासिनः।
en: Defeating next the son of the Danava Vali, viz., Bana, who will be possessed a thousandarms, I shall next destroy all the inhabitants of the Danava city called Saubha.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: यः कालयवनः ख्यातो गर्गतेजोऽभिसंवृतः॥ भविष्यति वधस्तस्य मत्त एव द्विजोत्तम।
en: I shall next, O foremost of Brahmanas, bring about the death of Kalayavana, a Danava who will be endued with great power on account of his being equipt with the energy of Gargya.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: जरासंधश्च बलवान् सर्वराजविरोधनः॥ भविष्यत्यसुरः स्फीतो भूमिपालो गिरिव्रजे। मम बुद्धिपरिस्पन्दाद् वधस्तस्य भविष्यति॥
en: A proud Asura will appear as a king at Girivraja, of the name of Jarasandha, who will fall out with all the other kings of the world. His death will be brought about by me through some one else guided by my intelligence.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: शिशुपालं वधिष्यामि यज्ञे धर्मसुतस्य वै। समागतेषु बलिषु पृथिव्यां सर्वराजसु॥ वासविः सुसहायो वै मम त्वेको भविष्यति।
en: I shall next kill Shisupala in the sacrifice of king Yudhishthira the son of Dharma, into which sacrifice all the kings of the world will bring tribute. In some of these works, only Arjuna, the son of Vasava, will become my assistant.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: युधिष्ठिरं स्थापयिष्ये स्वराज्ये भ्रातृभिः सह॥ एवं लोका वदिष्यन्ति नरनारायणावृषी। उद्युक्तौ दहतः क्षत्रं लोककार्यार्थमीश्वरौ॥ कृत्वा भारावतरणं वसुधाया यथेप्सितम्। सर्वसात्वतमुख्यानां द्वारकायाश्च सत्तम॥ करिष्ये प्रलयं घोरमात्मज्ञातिविनाशनम्।
en: I shall place Yudhishthira with all his brothers in his ancestral kingdom. People will call me and Arjuna as Narayana and Nara, when, endued with power, we two, putting forth our strength, shall kill a large number of Kshatriyas, for doing good to the world. Having lightened the load of the Earth according to our pleasure, I shall merge all the principal Satvatas, as also Dwaraka, my favourite city, into my own self, recollecting my all-einbracing Knowledge.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: कर्माण्यपरिमेयाणि चतुर्मूर्तिधरो ह्यहम्॥ कृत्वा लोकान् गमिष्यामि स्वानहं ब्रह्मसत्कृतान्।
en: Having four forms, I shall, in this way, perform many feats of great prowess, and attain at last to those regions of happiness created by me and honoured by all the Brahmanas.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: हंस: कूर्मश्च मत्स्यश्च प्रादुर्भावा द्विजोत्तम॥ वराहो नरसिंहश्च वामनो राम एव च। रामो दाशरथिश्चैव सात्वतः कल्किरेव च॥
en: Appearing in the forms of a swan, a tortoise, a fish, O foremost of twice-born ones, I shall then appear as a boar, then as a manlion, then as a dwarf, then as Rama of Bhrigu's race, then as Rama the son of Dasharatha, then as Krishna the scion of the Satvata race, and lastly as Kalki.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: यदा वेदश्रुतिर्नष्टा मया प्रत्याहृता पुनः। सवेदाः सश्रुतीकाश्च कृताः पूर्वं कृते युगे॥
en: When the Vedas disappeared from the world, I brought them back. The Vedas, were re-created by me in the Krita age.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: अतिक्रान्ताः पुराणेषु श्रुतास्ते यदि वा क्वचित्। अतिक्रान्ताश्च बहवः प्रादुर्भावा ममोत्तमाः॥
en: They have once more disappeared or may only be partially heard here and there in the Puranas. Many of my best incarnations also in the world have become facts of the past.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: लोककार्याणि कृत्वा च पुनः स्वां प्रकृतिं गताः। न ह्येतद् ब्रह्मणा प्राप्तमीदृशं मम दर्शनम्॥ यत् त्वया प्राप्तमद्येह एकान्तगतबुद्धिना। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं ब्रह्मन् भक्तिमतो मया॥ पुराणं च भविष्यं च सरहस्यं च सत्तम।
en: Having secured the good of the worlds in those forms in which I appeared, they have reentered into my own Nature. Brahman (the Creator) himself never saw me in this form of mine, which you, O Narada, have seen to-day on account of your entire devotion to me. I have now said to you, who are devoted to me wholly, everything, O Brahmana. . I have described to you my ancient appearances and future ones also, O best of inen, together with ail their mysteries.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवं स भगवान् देवो विश्वमूर्तिधरोऽव्ययः॥ एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं तत्रैवान्तर्दधे पुनः।
en: Bhishma said ‘The holy and illustrious god, of universal and immutable form, having said these words to Narada, disappeared there and then.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: नारदोऽपि महातेजाः प्राप्यानुग्रहमीप्सितम्॥ सरनारायणौ द्रष्टुं बदर्याश्रममाद्रवत्।
en: Having won the high favour that he had solicited, Narada also, gifted with great energy, then proceeded in all haste to the retreat called Vadari, for seeing Nara and Narayana.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: इदं महोपनिषदं चतुर्वेदसमन्वितम्॥ सांख्ययोगकृतं तेन पञ्चरात्रानुशब्दितम्। नारायणमुखोद्गीतं नारदोऽश्रावयत् पुनः॥ ब्रह्मणः सदने तात यथादृष्टं यथाश्रुतम्।
en: This great Upanishad quite of a piece with the four Vedas, and the Sankhya-Yoga, and called by him by the name of the Pancharatra Scriptures and recited by Narayana himself with his own mouth, was repeated by Narada before a large audience in the residence of Brahman (his sire) in exactly the same way in which Narayana had recited it and in which he had heard it from his own lips."

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एतदाश्चर्यभूतं हि माहात्म्यं तस्य धीमतः॥ किं वै ब्रह्मा न जानीते यतः शुश्राव नारदात्।
en: Yudhishthira said “Was not Brahman. the Creator of all things, acquainted with this wonderful discourse of the glory of Narayana gifted with intelligence that he heard it from the lips of Narada?

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: पितामहोऽपि भगवांस्तस्माद् देवादनन्तरः॥ कथं स न विजानीयात् प्रभावममितौजसः।
en: Is the illustrious Grandfather of all the worlds any way different from or inferior to the great Narayana? How then it is that he was unacquainted with the power of Narayana of great energy?"

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: भीष्म उवाच महाकल्पसहस्राणि महाकल्पशतानि च॥ समतीतानि राजेन्द्र सर्गाश्च प्रलयाश्च ह।
en: Bhishma continued "Hundreds and thousands of great cycles, hundreds and thousands of Creations and Dissolutions, O king of kings, have been over and become events of the past.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सर्गस्यादौ स्मृतो ब्रह्मा प्रजासर्गकरः प्रभुः॥ जानाति देवप्रवरं भूयश्चातोऽधिकं नृप।
en: In the beginning of every Creation, Brahman, endued with great power and who creates all things, is remembered by Narayana). Brahman knows well, O king, that Narayana, that foremost of all gods is very much superior to him.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: परमात्मानमीशानमात्मनः प्रभवं तथा॥ ये त्वन्ये ब्रह्मसदने सिद्धसंघाः समागताः। तेभ्यस्तच्छावयामास पुराणं वेदसम्मितम्॥ तेषां सकाशात् सूर्यस्तु श्रुत्वा वै भावितात्मनाम्। आत्मानुगामिनां राजन् श्रावयामास वै ततः॥ षट् षष्टिर्हि सहस्राणि ऋषीणां भावितात्मनाम्।
en: He knows that Narayana is the Supreme Soul, that He is the Supreme Lord, that He is Creator of Brahman himself. Narada recited this very ancient narrative which is perfectly consistent with the Vedas, to that assembly of Rishis crowned with ascetic success that came to the abode of Brahman. The gods Surya, having heard that narrative from those Rishis crowned with ascetic success, repeated it to the sixty-six thousands of Rishis, O king, of purified souls, that follow in his train.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सूर्यस्य तपतो लोकान् निर्मिता ये पुरः सराः॥ तेषामकथयत् सूर्यः सर्वेषां भावितात्मनाम्।
en: And the Sun, the deity that imparts heat to all the worlds, repeated that narrative to those Beings also, of purified souls, that have been created (by Brahman) for always travelling in the van of the Sun.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सूर्यानुगामिभिस्तात ऋषिभिस्तैर्महात्मभिः॥ मेरौ समागता देवाः श्राविताश्चेदमुत्तमम्।
en: The great Rishis who follow in the Sun's train, O son, repeated that excellent narrative to the deities assembled on the breast of Meru.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: देवानां तु सकाशाद् वै ततः श्रुत्वासितो द्विजः॥ श्रावयामास राजेन्द्र पितॄणां मुनिसत्तमः।
en: The best of ascetics, viz., the regener: Asita, then, having heard the narrative from the gods, repeated it to the Pitris, O king of kings.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: मम चापि पिता तात कथयामास शान्तनुः॥ ततो मयापि श्रुत्वा च कीर्तितं तव भारत।
en: I heard it from my father Shantanu, O son, who recited it to me formerly. Myself having heard it from my father, I have repeated it to you, O Bharata.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सुरैर्वा मुनिभिर्वापि पुराणं यैरिदं श्रुतम्॥ सर्वे ते परमात्मानं पूजयन्ते समन्ततः।
en: Gods and ascetics, they who have heard this excellent old narrative which is a Purana, all worship the Supreme Soul.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: इदमाख्यानमार्षेयं पारम्पर्यागतं नृप॥ नावासुदेवभक्ताय त्वया देयं कथंचन।
en: This discourse, belonging to the Rishis and thus handed down from one to another, should not, O king, be communicated by you to any one who is not a worshipper of Vasudeva.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: मत्तोऽन्यानि च ते राजन्नुपाख्यानशतानि वै॥ यानि श्रुतानि सर्वाणि तेषां सारोऽयमुद्धृतः।
en: This narrative, O king, is really the cream of the hundreds of other discourses that you have heard from me.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सुरासुरैर्यथा राजन् निर्मथ्यामृतमुद्धतम्॥ एवमेतत् पुरा विप्रैः कथामृतमिहोद्धृतम्।
en: In days of yore, O king, the gods and the Asuras, in a body, churned the Ocean and raised the Ambrosia. Similarly the Brahmanas, in a body in days of yore, churned all the scriptures and raised this narrative, which resembles nectar.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: यश्चेदं पठते नित्यं यश्चेदं शृणुयान्नरः॥ एकान्तभावोपगत एकान्तेषु समाहितः। प्राप्य श्वेतं महाद्वीपं भूत्वा चन्द्रप्रभो नरः॥ स सहस्रार्चिषं देवं प्रविशेन्नात्र संशयः।
en: He who frequently reads this narrative, and he who frequently listens to it with rapt attention, in a secluded spot, and filled with devotion, succeeds, being possessed of lunar complexion, in living in the spacious insular continent known by the name of White Island. Forsooth, such a man succeeds in entering into Narayana of a thousand rays.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: मुच्येदार्तस्तथा रोगाच्छ्रुत्वेमामादितः कथाम्॥ जिज्ञासुर्लभते कामान् भक्तो भक्तगतिं व्रजेत्।
en: By listening to this narrative from the beginning, a sick person becomes freed from his disease. The man who simply desires to read or listen to this discourse, gets the fruition of all his wishes. By reading or listening to it. The devoted worshipper acquires the high end reserved for devoted worshippers.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: त्वयापि सततं राजन्नभ्यर्च्यः पुरुषोत्तमः॥ स हि माता पिता चैव कृत्स्नस्य जगतो गुरुः।
en: You also, O king, should always adore and worship that foremost of all Beings. He is the father and the mother of all creatures, and He is an object of reverence to the entire universe.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: ब्रह्मण्यदेवो भगवान् प्रीयतां ते सनातनः॥ युधिष्ठिर महाबाहो महाबुद्धिर्जनार्दनः।
en: Let the illustrious and Eternal God of the Brahmanas, Viz., Janarddana of great intelligence, be pleased with you, O Yudhisthira of mighty arms.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वैतदाख्यानवरं धर्मराड् जनमेजय॥ भ्रातरश्चास्य ते सर्वे नारायणपराऽभवन्।
en: Vaishampayana said Having listened to this best of discourses, O Janamejaya, king Yudhisthira the just, and all his brothers became devoted to Narayana.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: जितं भगवता तेन पुरुषेणेति भारत॥ नित्यं जप्यपरा भूत्वा सरस्वतीमुदीरयन्।
en: And all of them, O Bharata, silently meditating upon Narayana (from that day), uttered these words for His glorification, viz., Victory to that holy and illustrious Being.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: यो ह्यस्माकं गुरुश्रेष्ठः कृष्णद्वैपायनो मुनिः॥ जगौ परमकं जप्यं नारायणमुदीरयन्।
en: He, again, who is our best of preceptors, viz., the Island-born Krishna, devoted to penances, sung, uttering the word Narayana, that great Mantra which is worthy of being silently.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: गत्वान्तरिक्षात् सततं क्षीरोदममृताशयम्॥ पूजयित्वा च देवेशं पुनरायात् स्वमाश्रमम्।
en: Passing through the sky to the Ocean of milk, which is always the abode of nectar, and adoring the great God there, be returned to his own hermitage.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं नारदोक्तं मयेरितम्॥ पारम्पर्यागतं ह्येतत् पित्रा मे कथितं पुरा।
en: Bhishma continued I have now recounted to you the discourse that was recited by Narada. That narrative has come down from person to person from very ancient times. I heard it from my father who formerly recounted it to me.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: सौतिरुवाच एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं वैशम्पायन कीर्तितम्॥ जनमेजयेन तच्छ्रुत्वा कृतं सम्यग् यथाविधि।
en: Suta said I have now told you all that Vaishampayana recounted to Janamejaya. Having listened to Vaishampayana's narration, king Janamejaya severe duly satisfied all his duties according to the scriptural ordinances.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: यूयं हि तप्ततपसः सर्वे च चरितव्रताः॥ सर्वे वेदविदो मुख्या नैमिषारण्यवासिनः।
en: You have have all practised very penances and observed many high and excellent vows. Living in this sacred forest of Naimisha, you are foremost of all persons conversant with the Vedas.

description: Narayana appears before Narada and tells him that those who have implicit faith in Narayana become liberated. His various incarnations are also described
sn: शौनकस्य महासत्रं प्राप्ताः सर्वे द्विजोत्तमाः॥ यजध्वं सुहुतैर्यज्ञैः शाश्वतं परमेश्वरम्। पारम्पर्यागतं ह्येतत् पित्रा मे कथितं पुरा॥
en: You foremost of twice-born ones, you all have come to this great sacrifice of Shaunaka. Do you all worship that Eternal and Supreme Lord of the universe in excellent sacrifices, properly pouring libations of clarified butter to the fire with the help of Mantras and dedicating the same to Narayana. As for myself, I heard this excellent discourse which has come down from generation to generation, from my father who recited it to me formerly.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: शौनक उवाच कथं स भगवान् देवो यज्ञेष्वग्रहरः प्रभुः। यज्ञधारी च सततं वेदवेदाङ्गवित् तथा॥
en: Saunaka said is that illustrious god, viz., the powerful Narayana, who is a master of the Vedas and their branches, at once the doer and the enjoyer of sacrifices?

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: निवृत्तं चास्थितो धर्मं क्षमी भागवतः प्रभुः। निवृत्तिधर्मान् विदधे स एव भगवान् प्रभुः॥
en: Endued with forgiveness, he has adopted, again, the Religion of Renunciation. Indeed, it is that holy and powerful one who has himself laid down the duties of Renunciation.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: कथं प्रवृत्तिधर्मेषु भागार्हा देवताः कृताः। कथं निवृत्तिधर्माश्च कृता व्यावृत्तबुद्धयः॥
en: Why then has he made many of the gods the takers of shares in sacrifices which, of course, are all due to the Religion of Action. Why has he again created some with an opposite disposition, for they follow the ordinances of the Religion of Renunciation.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: एतं नः संशयं सौते छिन्थि गुह्यं सनातनम्। त्वया नारायणकथाः श्रुता वै धर्मसंहिताः॥
en: Do you, O Suta, remove this doubt of ours. This doubt seems to be eternal and is filled with great mystery. You have heard all discourses on Narayana, which are consistent with the (other) scriptures.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: सौतिरुवाच जनमेजयेन यत् पृष्टः शिष्यो व्यासस्य धीमतः। तत् तेऽहं कथयिष्यामि पौराणं शौनकोत्तम॥
en: O excellent Saunaka, I shall recount to you what Vaishampayana, the disciple of the intelligent Vyasa, said when questioned on these very topics by king Janamejaya.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: श्रुत्वा माहात्म्यमेतस्य देहिनां परमात्मनः। जनमेजयो महाप्राज्ञो वैशम्पायनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having heard the discourse on the glory of Narayana who is the Soul of all embodied creatues, Janamejaya, gifted with great intelligence and wisdom, asked Vaishampayana about these very topics.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: जनमेजय उवाच इमे सब्रह्मका लोकाः ससुरासुरमानवाः। क्रियास्वभ्युदयोक्तासु सक्ता दृश्यन्ति सर्वशः॥
en: The whole world of Being, with Brahman, the gods, the Asuras, and human beings are seen to be deeply attached to acts which yield prosperity.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: मोक्षश्चोक्तस्त्वया ब्रह्मन् निर्वाणं परमं सुखम्। ये तु मुक्ता भवन्तीह पुण्यपापविवर्जिताः॥ ते सहस्रर्चिषं देवं प्रविशन्तीह शुश्रुम्।
en: Liberation has, O twice-born one, been described by you to be the highest happiness and to consist of the cessation of existence. They who being shorn of both merit and demerit, become liberated, succeed, we hear, in entering the great God of a thousand rays.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: अयं हि दुरनुष्ठेयो मोक्षधर्मः सनातनः॥ यं हित्वा देवताः सर्वा हव्यकव्यभुजोऽभवन्।
en: It seems to be, O Brahmana, that the eternal religion of Liberation is highly difficult of observance. Turning away from it, all the gods have become enjoyers of the libations of clarified butter poured with Mantras on sacrificial fires and other offerings presented to them by similar means.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: किं च ब्रह्मा च रुद्रश्च शक्रश्च बलभित् प्रभुः॥ सूर्यस्ताराधिपो वायुरग्निर्वरुण एव च। आकाशं जगती चैव ये च शेषा दिवौकसः॥ प्रलयं न विजानन्ति आत्मनः परिनिर्मितम्। ततस्तेनास्थिता मार्ग ध्रुवमक्षरमव्ययम्॥
en: Then, again, Brahman, and Rudra, the powerful Sakra the killer of Vala, the Sun, the Lord of the stars, the Wind-god, the god of fire, the god of the Waters, Infinite Space, the Universe too and the rest of the dwellers of heaven,-these, it seems do not know the way of securing an annihilation of conscious existence that is encompassed by one's own efforts.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: स्मृत्वा कालपरीमाणं प्रवृत्तिं ये समास्थिताः। दोषः कालपरीमाणे महानेष क्रियावताम्॥
en: Hence, perhaps, they have not followed the path which is certain, indestructible, and immutable. Hence, perhaps turning away from that path, they have adopted the Religion of Action which leads to conscious existence that is measured by time.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: एतन्मे संशयं विप्र हृदि शल्यमिवार्पितम्। छिन्धीतिहासकथनात् परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: This, indeed, is one great defeat of those who are wedded to acts, for all their rewards are for the time being. This doubt, O twiceborn one, exists in my heart like a dagger! Tear it out by recounting to me some discourses of old on this subject. Great is my curiosity to listen to you.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: कथं भागहराः प्रोक्ता देवताः क्रतुषु द्विज। किमर्थं चाध्वरे ब्रह्मन्निज्यन्ते त्रिदिवौकसः॥
en: Why, O twice-born one, have the gods been said to be takers of their respective shares of sacrificial offerings presented to them with the help of Mantras in sacrifices of various kinds? Why, again, are the dwellers of heaven worshipped in sacrifices?

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: ये च भागं प्रगृह्णन्ति यज्ञेषु द्विजसत्तम। ये यजन्तो महायज्ञैः कस्य भागं ददन्ति वै॥
en: And, O best of twice-born ones to whom do they, who partake of offerings in sacrifices performed to their honour, themselves make offerings when they perform great sacrifices?

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अहो गूढतमः प्रश्नस्त्वया पृष्टो जनेश्वर। नातप्ततपसा ह्येष नावेदविदुषा तथा॥ नापुराणविदा चैव शक्यो व्याहर्तुमञ्जसा।
en: The question you have put to me, O king, relates to a deed mystery. No man can quickly answer it who has not practised penances, and who is not acquainted with the Puranas.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि यन्मे पृष्टः पुरा गुरुः॥ कृष्णद्वैपायनो व्यासो वेदव्यासो महानृषिः।
en: I shall, however, answer you by reciting to you what my preceptor the Island-born Krishna, otherwise called Vyasa, the great Rishi who has divided the Vedas, had said to us on a former occasion when questioned by us.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: सुमन्तुजैमिनिश्चैव पैलश्च सुदृढव्रतः॥ अहं चतुर्थः शिष्यो वै पञ्चमश्च शुकः स्मृतः।
en: Sumanta, and Jaimini, and Paila of firm vows, and myself as the fourth, and Shuka. as the fifth, were disciples of the illustrious Vyasa.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: एतान् समागतान् सर्वान् पञ्च शिष्यान् दमान्वितान्॥२० शौचाचारसमायुक्ताञ्जिक्रोधाञ्जितेन्द्रियान्। वेदानध्यापयामास महाभारतपञ्चमान्॥
en: We, five in all, endued with self-control and purity of observances, had completely mastered anger and controlled our senses. Our preceptor used to teach us the Vedas having the Mahabharata for their fifth.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: मेरौ गिरिवरे रम्ये सिद्धचारणसेविते। तेषामभ्यस्यतां वेदान् कदाचित् संशयोऽभवत्।॥ एष वै यस्त्वया पृष्टस्तेन तेषां प्रकीर्तितः। ततः श्रुतो मया चापि तवाख्येयोऽद्य भारत॥
en: Once on a time, on the breast of that foremost of mountains, viz., the delightful Meru, inhabited by Siddhas and Charanas while we were engaged in reading the Vedas, this very doubt sprang in our minds, that has been given vent to by you to-day. We, therefore, asked our preceptor about it. It heared the answer that our preceptor made. I shall now recount that answer to you, O Bharata.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: शिष्याणां वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वाज्ञानतमोनुदः। पराशरसुतः श्रीमान् व्यासो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the words that were addressed to him by his disciples, that remover of all sorts of darkness represented by ignorance, viz., the blessed Vyasa the son of Parashara, said these words:मया हि सुमहत् तप्तं तपः परमदारुणम्।

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च जानीयामिति सत्तमाः॥
en: I have practised the austerest of penances. You best of men, I am fully conversant with the Past, the Present, and the Future.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: तस्य मे तप्ततपसो निगृहीतेन्द्रियस्य च। नारायणप्रसादेन क्षीरोदस्यानुकूलतः॥ त्रैकालिकमिदं ज्ञानं प्रादुर्भूतं यथेप्सितम्।
en: On account of those penances of mine and of the control under which I kept my senses, while I lived on the shores of the ocean of milk, Narayana became pleased with me. As the result of the great God's gratification, this omniscience about the Past, the Present, and Future that was desired by me, sprang in my inind.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: तच्छृणुध्वं यथान्यायं वक्ष्ये संशयमुत्तमम्॥ यथा वृत्तं हि कल्पादौ दृष्टं मे ज्ञानचक्षुषा।
en: Listen now to me as I describe to you, in due order, this great doubt that has perplexed your minds. I have, with the eye of knowledge, seen, all that took place in the beginning of the aeon.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: परमात्मेति यं प्राहुः सांख्ययोगविदो जनाः॥ महापुरुषसंज्ञां स लभते स्वेन कर्मणा। तस्मात् प्रसूतमव्यक्तं प्रधानं तं विदुर्बुधाः॥
en: He whom both the Sankhyas and the Yogins call by the name of the Supreme Soul, comes to be regarded as the foremost Purusha on account of his own deeds. From Him originate Prakriti that is called the unmanifest or Pradhana by the learned.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: अव्यक्ताद् व्यक्तमुत्पन्नं लोकसृष्ट्यर्थमीश्वरात्। अनिरुद्धो हि लोकेषु महानात्मेति कथ्यते॥
en: From the powerful Unmanifest sprang, for the creation of all the worlds, he that is called Aniruddha. That Aniruddha is known among all creatures by the name of the Great Soul.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: योऽसौ व्यक्तत्वमापन्नो निर्ममे च पितामहम्। सोऽहंकार इति प्रोक्तः सर्वतेजोमयो हि सः॥
en: It is that Aniruddha who, becoming manifest, created the Grandfather Brahman. Aniruddha is known by another name, viz., consciousness, and is gifted with every sort of energy.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम्। अहंकारप्रसूतानि महाभूतानि पञ्चधा॥
en: Earth, Wind, Ether, Water, and Fire numbering the fifth—these are the five Great Creatures that have originated from Consciousness.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: महाभूतानि सृष्ट्वैव तान् गुणान् निर्ममे पुनः। भूतेभ्यश्चैव निष्पन्ना मूर्तिमन्तश्च ताशृणु॥
en: Having created the Great Creatures he then created their qualities. Combining the Great Creatures, he then created various embodied Beings. Hear me as I describe them to you.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: मरीचिरङ्गिराचात्रिः पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः। वसिष्ठश्च महात्मा वै मनुः स्वायम्भुवस्तथा॥ ज्ञेयाः प्रकृतयोऽष्टौ ता यासु लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः।
en: Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, the great Vashistha, and the Self-created Manu,-these should be known as the eight elements. Upon these depend all the worlds.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: वेदवेदाङ्गसंयुक्तान् यज्ञान् यज्ञाङ्गसंयुतान्॥ निर्ममे लोकसिद्ध्यर्थं ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः। अष्टाभ्यः प्रकृतिभ्यश्च जातं विश्वमिदं जगत्।॥
en: Then the Grandfather of all the worlds, viz., Brahman, created, for the success of all creatures, the Vedas with all their branches as also the sacrifices with their limbs. From these eight elements have originated this vast universe.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: रुद्रो रोषात्मको जातो दशान्यान् सोऽसृजत् स्वयम्। एकादशैते रुद्रास्तु विकारपुरुषाः स्मृताः॥
en: Then originated Rudra from the principle of anger. Taking birth, he created ten others like him. These eleven Rudras are called by name of Vikara-Purushas.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: ते रुद्राः प्रकृतिश्चैव सर्वे चैव सुरर्षयः। उत्पन्ना लोकसिद्ध्यर्थं ब्रह्माणं समुपस्थिताः॥
en: The Rudras, the Prakritis, and the several celestial Rishis, having come into existence approached Brahman, with the object of upholding the universe and its work.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: वयं सृष्टा हि भगवंस्त्वया च प्रभविष्णुना। येन यस्मिन्नधीकारे वर्तितव्यं पितामह॥
en: Addressing the Grandfather, they said,-We have been created, O holy one, by you, O you of great power. Tell us, O Grandfather, which of us should be vested with what jurisdiction.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: योऽसौ त्वयाभिनिर्दिष्टो ह्यधिकारोऽर्थचिन्तकः। परिपाल्यः कथं तेन साहंकारेण कर्तृणा॥
en: What jurisdictions have been created by you for supervising what particular affairs? Which of us should, gifted with what sort of consciousness, shall take charge of which of these?

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: प्रदिशस्व बलं तस्य योऽधिकारार्थचिन्तकः। एवमुक्तो महादेवो देवांस्तानिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Do you ordain also to each of us the measure of strength that we are to have for satisfying the duties duties of our our respective jurisdictions.-Thus addressed by them, the great god replied to them in the following way.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच साध्वहं ज्ञापितो देवा युष्माभिर्भद्रमस्तु वः। ममाप्येषा समुत्पन्ना चिन्ता या भवतां मता॥
en: Brahman said You have done well, ye gods, in speaking to me of this matter. Blessed be you all! I was thinking of this very subject that has drawn your attention.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: लोकत्रयस्य कृत्स्नस्य कथं कार्यः परिग्रहः। कथं बलक्षयो न स्याद् युष्माकं ह्यात्मनश्च मे॥
en: How should the three words be maintained and kept agoing? How should your strength and mine be taken advantage of for the accomplishment of that object.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: इतः सर्वेऽपि गच्छामः शरणं लोकसाक्षिणम्। महापुरुषमव्यक्तं स नो वक्ष्यति यद्धितम्॥
en: Let all of us, leaving this place, go that unmanifest and foremost of Beings who is the witness of the world, for seeking his protection. He will tell us what is for our behoof.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: ततस्ते ब्रह्मणा सार्धमृषयो विबुधास्तथा। क्षीरोदस्योत्तरं कूलं जग्मुर्लोकहितार्थिनः॥
en: After this, those gods and Rishis, with Brahman, went to the northern shores of the ocean of milk, desirous of doing good to the three worlds.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: ते तपः समुपातिष्ठन् ब्रह्मोक्तं वेदकल्पितम्। स महानियमो नाम तपश्चर्यासु दारुणः॥
en: Arrived there, they began to practise those austere penances that are said by Brahman in the Vedas. Those austerest of penances are known by the name of Mahaniyama.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: ऊर्ध्वा दृष्टिर्बाहवश्च एकाग्रं च मनोऽभवत्। एकपादाः स्थिताः सर्वे काष्ठभूताः समाहिताः॥
en: They stood there with mind fixed, immovable as stakes of wood, and with eyes upturned and arms raised upward.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं ते तपस्तप्त्वा सुदारुणम्। शुश्रुवुर्मधुरां वाणी वेदवेदाङ्गभूषिताम्॥
en: For a thousand divine years they were engaged in those severe penances. At the conclusion of that time they heard these sweet words in harmony with the Vedas and their branches.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच भो भोः सब्रह्मका देवा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः। स्वागतेनाय॑ वः सर्वाश्रावये वाक्यमुत्तमम्॥
en: The Blessed and Holy One said You gods and Rishis having asceticism for wealth with Brahman in your company, honouring you all with welcome, I say to you these words.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: विज्ञातं वो मया कार्यं तच्च लोकहितं महत्। प्रवृत्तियुक्तं कर्तव्यं युष्मत्प्राणोपबृंहणम्॥
en: I know what is in your hearts! Verily, your thoughts are for the behoof of the three worlds. I shall multiply your energy and strength, investing the same with disposition for work.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: सुतप्तं च तपो देवा ममाराधनकाम्यया। भोल्यथास्य महासत्त्वास्तपसः फलमुत्तमम्॥
en: You gods, well have you practised these penances from desire of worshipping me. You foremost of Beings, enjoy now the excellent fruits of those austerities which you have practised.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: एष ब्रह्मा लोकंगुरुर्महाललोकपितामहः। यूयं च विबुधश्रेष्ठा मां यजध्वं समाहिताः॥
en: This Brahman is the Lord of all the words. Gifted with power, he is the Grandfather of all creatures. You also are foremost of gods. Do you all, with concentrated minds, celebrate sacrifices for my glory.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: ते सर्वे भागान् कल्पयध्वं यज्ञेषु मम नित्यशः। तथा श्रेयोऽभिधास्यामि यथाधीकारमीश्वराः॥
en: In those sacrifices which you will perform, do ye always give me a part of the sacrificial offerings. I shall then, ye lords of creation, assign to each of you your respective spheres and ordain what will be for your behoof.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वैतद् देवदेवस्य वाक्यं हृष्टतनूरुहाः। ततस्ते विबुधाः सर्वे ब्रह्मा च महर्षयः॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Hearing these words of that God of gods, all those gods and great Rishis and Brahman became filled with such delight that the hair on their bodies stood erect.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: वेददृष्टेन विधिना वैष्णवं क्रतुमाहरन्। तस्मिन् सत्रे सदा ब्रह्मा स्वयं भागमकल्पयत्॥
en: They immediately made arrangements for a sacrifice in honour of Vishnu according to the Vedic ordinances. In that sacrifice, Brahman himself assigned a portion of the offerings to Vishnu.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: देवा देवर्षयश्चैव स्वं स्वं भागमकल्पयन्। ते कार्तयुगधर्माणो भागाः परमसत्कृताः॥
en: Similarly the gods and the celestial Rishis also, dedicated similar portions each to the great God. The portions, thus offered with great respect to Vishnu, were about both the quantity and the quality of the articles used, according to the ordinances laid down for the Krita age.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: प्राहुरादित्यवर्णं तं पुरुषं तमसः परम्। बृहन्तं सर्वगं देवमीशानं वरदं प्रभुम्॥
en: The gods and the Rishis and Brahman, in that sacrifice, worshipped the great God as one having the complexion of the Sun, as the foremost of Beings, situate beyond the reach of Ignorance, vast, pervading all things, the Supreme Lord of all, the giver of boons, and endued with power.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: ततोऽथ वरदो देवस्तान् सर्वानमरान् स्थितान्। अशरीरो बभाषेदं वाक्यं खस्थो महेश्वरः॥
en: Thus worshipped by them the boon-giving and great God, invisible and bodiless, addressed those assembled celestials from heaven and said to them

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: येन यः कल्पितो भागः स तथा मामुपागतः। प्रीतोऽहं प्रदिशाम्यद्य फलमावृत्तिलक्षणम्॥
en: I have received the offerings dedicated by you in this sacrifice. I am pleased with all of you. I shall confer rewards on you that will, however, be fraught with ends from where there will be return.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: एतद् वो लक्षणं देवा मत्प्रसादसमुद्भवम्। स्वयं यज्ञैर्यजमानाः समाप्तवरदक्षिणैः॥ युगे युगे भविष्यध्वं प्रवृत्तिफलभागिनः।
en: This shall be your distinctive characteristic, ye gods, from this day, on account of my favours and kindness for you. Celebrating sacrifices in every cycle, with large presents, you will become enjoyers of fruits born of Action.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: यज्ञैर्ये चापि यक्ष्यन्ति सर्वलोकेषु वै सुराः॥ कल्पयिष्यन्ति वो भागांस्ते नरा वेदकल्पितान्।
en: You gods, those men also that will celebrate sacrifices, according to the Vedic ordinances, will give to all of you, shares of their sacrificial offerings.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: यो मे यथा कल्पितवान् भागमस्मिन् महाक्रतौ॥ स तथा यज्ञभागार्हो वेदसूत्रे मया कृतः।
en: In the Veda-sutras I make him the receiver of a share like that which he has himself offered one in this sacrifice.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: यूयं लोकान् भावयध्वं यज्ञभागफलोचिताः॥ सर्वार्थचिन्तका लोके यथाधीकारनिर्मिताः।
en: Created to superintend the affairs of your respective jurisdictions, do you uphold the worlds according to your strength as dependent on the shares you receive in those sacrifices.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: याः क्रियाः प्रचरिष्यन्ति प्रवृत्तिफलसत्कृताः॥ आभिराप्यायितबला लोकान् वै धारयिष्यथा
en: Indeed, receiving strength from those rites and observances that will be in vogue in the several worlds, originating from the fruits of action, do ye continue to uphold the affairs of those worlds.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: यूयं हि भाविता यज्ञैः सर्वयज्ञेषु मानवैः॥ मां ततो भावयिष्यध्वमेषा वो भावना मम।
en: Strengthened by the sacrifices that will be celebrated by men, ye will strengthen me. These are the thoughts that I cherish for you

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: इत्यर्थं निर्मिता वेदा यज्ञाश्चौषधिभिः सह॥ एभिः सम्यक् प्रयुक्तैर्हि प्रीयन्ते देवताः क्षितौ।
en: It is for this that I have created the Vedas and sacrifices and plants and herbs. Duly served with these by human beings on Earth, the gods will be pleased.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: निर्माणमेतद् युष्माकं प्रवृत्तिगुणकल्पितम्॥ मया कृतं सुरश्रेष्ठा यावत्कल्पक्षयादिह। चिन्तयध्वं लोकहितं यथाधीकारमीश्वराः॥
en: You foremost of gods, till the end of this aeon, I have ordained your creation, making your constitutions depend upon the result of the religion of Action. You foremost of Beings, do you then, about your respective jurisdictions, engage yourselves in seeking the welfare of the three worlds.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: मरीचिरनिराश्चात्रिः पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः। वसिष्ठ इति सप्तैते मानसा निर्मिता हि ते॥
en: Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasistha,-these seven Rishis have been created by the fiat of the will.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: एते वेदविदो मुख्या वेदाचार्याश्च कल्पिताः। प्रवृत्तिधर्मिणश्चैव प्राजापत्ये च कल्पिताः॥
en: These will become the foremost of all persons versed in the Vedas. In fact, they will become the preceptors of the Vedas. They will follow the Religion of Action, for they have been intended to devote themselves to the act of procreating children.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: अयं क्रियावतां पन्था व्यक्तीभूतः सनातनः। अनिरुद्ध इति प्रोक्तो लोकसर्गकरः प्रभुः॥
en: This is the eternal path of creatures engaged in acts and observances. The powerful Lord who is charged with the creation of all the worlds is called Aniruddha.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: सनः सनत्सुजातश्च सनकः ससनन्दनः। सनत्कुमारः कपिल: सप्तमश्च सनातनः॥ सप्तैते मानसाः प्रोक्ता ऋषयो ब्रह्मणः सुताः। स्वयमागतविज्ञाना निवृत्ति धर्ममास्थिताः॥
en: Sana, Sanatsujata, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatkumara, Kapila, and Sanatana,—these seven Rishis are known as the spiritual sons of Brahman. Their knowledge comes to them of itself. These seven follow the Religion of Renunciation.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: एते योगविदो मुख्या: सांख्यज्ञानविशारदाः। आचार्या धर्मशास्त्रेषु मोक्षधर्मप्रवर्तकाः॥
en: They are the foremost of all persons conversant with Yoga. They have a profound knowledge of the Sankhya philosophy. They are teachers of the scriptures on duty and it is they who introduce the duties of the Religion of Renunciation and cause them flow in the worlds.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: यतोऽहं प्रसृतः पूर्वमव्यक्तात् त्रिगुणो महान्। तस्मात् परतरो योऽसौ क्षेत्रज्ञ इति कल्पितः॥
en: From Nature has sprung Consciousness and the three great qualities. Transcending Nature is called Soul.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: सोऽहं क्रियावतां पन्थाः पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभः। यो यथा निर्मितो जन्तुर्यस्मिन् यस्मिश्च कर्मणि॥ प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा तत्फलं सोऽश्नुते महत्। एष लोकगुरुर्ब्रह्मा जगदादिकरः प्रभुः॥
en: That Soul is myself. The path of those who follow acts is fraught with return. One cannot, by that path, reach the place whence there is no return. Different creatures have been created with different objects. Some are intended for the Path of Action and some for that of Renunciation. One enjoys the the reward, according to the path that he follows. This Brahman is the lord of all the worlds. Endued with power, it is he who creates the universe.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: एष माता पिता चैव युष्माकं च पितामहः। मयानुशिष्टो भविता सर्वभूतवरप्रदः॥
en: He is your mother and father, and he is your grandfather. At my behest, he will grant boons to all creatures.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: अस्य चैवात्मजो रुद्रो ललाटाद् यः समुत्थितः। ब्रह्मानुशिष्टो भविता सर्वभूतधरः प्रभुः॥
en: His son Rudra, who has originated from his brow at his behest, will, gifted with power, uphold all created beings.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: गच्छध्वं स्वानधीकारांश्चिन्तयध्वं यथाविधि। प्रवर्तन्तां क्रियाः सर्वाः सर्वलोकेषु मा चिरम्॥
en: Go you to your respective jurisdictions, and seek, according to the ordinances, the welfare of the world! Let all the scriptural acts flow in all the worlds. Let there be no delay in this.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: प्रदिश्यन्तां च कर्माणि प्राणिनां गतयस्तथा। परिनिष्ठितकालानि आयूषीह सुरोत्तमाः॥
en: You foremost of gods, do ye ordain the acts of all creatures and the ends that they are come by. Do ye also set the limits of the lives of all creatures.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: इदं कृतयुगं नाम कालः श्रेष्ठः प्रवर्तितः। अहिंस्या यज्ञपशवो युगेऽस्मिन् न तदन्यथा॥
en: This present cycle that is going on is the foremost of all epochs and should be known by the name of Krita. In this cycle living creatures should not be celebrated. It should be as I ordain and let it not be otherwise.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: चतुष्पात् सकलो धर्मो भविष्यत्यत्र वै सुराः। ततस्त्रतायुगं नाम त्रयी यत्र भविष्यति॥
en: In this age, ye celestials, virtue will flourish in full. After this age will come the cycle called Treta. The Vedas, in that cycle, will lose one quarter. Only three of them will exist.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: प्रोक्षिता यत्र पशवो वधं प्राप्स्यन्ति वै मखे। यत्र पादश्चतुर्थो वै धर्मस्य न भविष्यति॥
en: In the sacrifices that will be celebrated in that age, animals, after dedication with the help of sacred Mantras, will be killed. As regards virtue, again, it will lose one quarter; only three quarters thereof will remain.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: ततो वै द्वापरं नाम मिश्रः कालो भविष्यति। द्विपादहीनो धर्मश्च युगे तस्मिन् भविष्यति॥
en: On the termination of the Treta, will come the mixed Yoga known by the name of Dvapara. In that cycle, virtue will lose two quarters and only two quarters thereof will remain.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: ततस्तिष्येऽथ सम्प्राप्ते युगे कलिपुरस्कृते। एकपादस्थितो धर्मो यत्र तत्र भविष्यति॥
en: Upon the termination of Dvapara, the cycle that will set in will be called Tish, and it will come with Kali walking in the van. Virtue will lose full three quarters. Only a quarter thereof will exist in all places.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: देवा देवर्षयश्चोचुस्तमेवंवादिनं गुरुम्। एकपादस्थिते धर्मे यत्र क्वचन गामिनि॥ कथं कर्तव्यमस्माभिर्भगवंस्तद् वदस्व नः।
en: When the great God said these words, the gods and the celestial Rishis addressed him and said,-If only a fourth part of virtue is to exist in that age in every place, tell us, O Holy One, where shall we then go and what shall we do?

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच यत्र वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च तपः सत्यं दमस्तथा॥ अहिंसाधर्मसंयुक्ताः प्रचरेयुः सुरोत्तमाः। स वो देशः सेवितव्यो मा वोऽधर्मः पदा स्पृशेत्।।८९
en: You foremost of gods, ye should, in that age, go to such places where the Vedas and Sacrifices and Penances and Truth and selfcontrol, accompanied by duties fraught with mercy for all creatures, will still continue. Sin will never be able to affect you at all.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: व्यास उवाच तेऽनुशिष्टा भगवता देवाः सर्षिगणास्तथा। नमस्कृत्वा भगवते जग्मुर्देशान् यथेप्सितान्॥
en: Vyasa said Thus commanded by the great God, the gods with all the Rishis bowed their heads to him and then proceeded to the places they desired.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
sn: गतेषु त्रिदिवौकःसु ब्रह्मैकः पर्यवस्थितः। दिदृक्षुर्भगवन्तं तमनिरुद्धतनौ स्थितम्॥
en: After the celestiats had left that place, only Brahman remained there, desirous of seeing the great Deity then living in the form of Aniruddha.

description: The creation of Rudras etc. The Religion of Renunciation
