en: Following the path pointed out by Vamadeva, the great Rishi Panchala, through my favour obtained from that eternal Being the rules of the division of syllables and words, Indeed, Galava, born in the Vabhravya race, having acquired high ascetic success and obtained a boon from Narayana, compiled the rules about the division of syllables and words and those about emphasis and accent in utterance, and appeared as the first scholar who became conversant with those two subjects. Repeatedly thinking of the sorrow of birth and death, Kundarika and king Brahmadatta attained to that property which is acquired by persons devoted to Yoga, in course of seven births, through my favour.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: पुराहमात्मजः पार्थ प्रथितः कारणान्तरे॥ धर्मस्य कुरुशार्दूल ततोऽहं धर्मजः स्मृतः।
en: In days of yore, O Partha, I was, for some reason, born as the son of Dharma, O Kuruchief, and owing to such birth of mind I was celebrated under the name of Dharmaja.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: नरनारायणौ पूर्वं तपस्तेपतुरव्ययम्॥ धर्मयानं समारूढौ पर्वते गन्धमादने।
en: I took birth in two forms, viz., as Nara and Narayana. Riding on the car that helps the performance of scriptural and other duties, I practised, in those two forms, eternal austerities on the breast of Gandhamadana,

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: तत्कालसमये चैव दक्षयज्ञो बभूव ह॥ न चैवाकल्पयद् भागं दक्षो रुद्रस्य भारत।
en: At that time the great sacrifice of Daksha took place. Daksha, however, in that sacrifice of his, refused to dedicate a share to Rudra, O Bharata, of the sacrificial offerings.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: ततो दधीचिवचनाद् दक्षयज्ञमपाहरत्॥ ससर्ज शूलं कोपेन प्रज्वलन्तं मुहुर्मुहुः।
en: Moved by the sage Dadhichi, Rudra destroyed that sacrifice. He hurled a flaming dart.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: तच्छूलं भस्मसात्कृत्वा दक्षयज्ञं सविस्तरम्॥ आवयोः सहसागच्छद् बदर्याश्रममन्तिकात्।
en: That dart, having consumed all the articles of Daksha's sacrifice, came with great force towards us at the retreat of Badari.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: वेगेन महता पार्थ पतन्नारायणोरसि॥ ततस्तत् तेजसाऽऽविष्टाः केशा नारायणस्य ह। बभूवुर्मुञ्जवर्णास्तु ततोऽहं मुञ्जकेशवान्॥
en: With great violence the dart then dropped upon the chest of Narayana. Attacked by the violence of that dart, the hair on the head of Narayana became green. In fact, on account of this change in the colour of my hair I came to be called by the name of Munjakesha.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: तच्च शूलं विनिर्धूतं हुंकारेण महात्मना। जगाम शंकरकरं नारायणसमाहतम्॥ अथ रुद्र उपाधावत् तावृषी तपसान्वितौ।
en: Driven off by an exclamation of Hun which Narayana uttered, this dart, losing its power, returned to Shankara's hands. At this, Rudra became greatly enraged and as the outcome thereof he rushed towards the Rishis Nara and Narayana gifted with the power of severe austerities.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: तत एनं समुद्भूतं कण्ठे जग्राह पाणिना॥ नारायणः स विश्वात्मा तेनास्य शितिकण्ठता।
en: Narayana then seized the rushing Rudra with his hand by the throat. Caught by Narayana, the lord of the universe, Rudra's throat changed colour and became dark. From that time forth Rudra came to be called by the name of Shitikantha.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: अथ रुद्रविघातार्थमिषीका नर उद्धरन्॥ मन्त्रैश्च संयुयोजाशु सोऽभवत् परशुर्महान्।
en: In the meantime Nara, for destroying Rudra, took up a blade of grass and inspired it with Mantras. The blade of grass, thus inspired, was converted into a powerful battle-axe.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: क्षिप्तश्च सहसा तेन खण्डनं प्राप्तवास्तदा॥ ततोऽहं खण्डपरशुः स्मृतः परशुखण्डनात्।
en: Nara suddenly hurled that battle-axe at Rudra but it broke into pieces. For that weapon thus breaking into pieces, I came to be called by the name of Khandaparashu.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: अर्जुन उवाच अस्मिन् युद्धे तु वार्ष्णेय त्रैलोक्यशमने तदा॥ को जयं प्राप्तवांस्तत्र शंसैतन्मे जनार्दन।
en: Arjuna said In the battle capable of encompassing the destruction of the three worlds, who acquired the victory, O Janarddana, do you tell me this.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच तयोः संलग्नयोर्युद्धे रुद्रनारायणात्मनोः॥ उद्विग्नाः सहसा कृत्स्नाः सर्वे लोकास्तदाभवन्।
en: The Blessed and Holy One said When Rudra and Narayana thus fought all the universe became suddenly stricken with anxiety.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: नागृह्णात् पावकः शुभं मखेषु सुहुतं हविः॥ वेदा न प्रतिभान्ति स्म ऋषीणां भावितात्मनाम्।
en: The god of fire ceased to accept duly poured in sacrifices with the help of Vedic Miantras. The Vedas no longer shone by inward light in the minds of the Rishis of purified souls.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: देवान् रजस्तमश्चैव समाविविशतुस्तदा॥ वसुधा संचकम्पे च नभश्च विचचाल ह।
en: The quality of Darkness and Ignorance possessed the gods. The Earth shook. The vault of the sky seemed to divide in two parts.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: निष्प्रभाणि च तेजांसि ब्रह्मा चैवासनच्युतः॥ अगाच्छोषं समुद्रश्च हिमवांश्च व्यशीर्यत।
en: All the luminaries became deprived of their effulgence. The Creator, Brahman, himself dropped from his seat. The Ocean himself became dry. The mountains of Himavat became riven.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: तस्मिन्नेवं समुत्पन्ने निमित्ते पाण्डुनन्दन॥ ब्रह्मा वृतो देवगणैर्ऋषिभिश्च महात्मभिः। आजगामाशु तं देशं यत्र युद्धमवर्तत॥ सोऽञ्जलिप्रग्रहो भूत्वा चतुर्वक्त्रो निरुक्तगः।
en: When such dreadful portents appeared everywhere, O son of Pandu, Brahman, attended by all the gods and the great Rishis, soon come to the place where the battle was going on. The four-headed Brahman, capable of being understood with the help of only the Niruktas, joined his hands and addressing Rudras, saidउवाच वचनं रुद्रं लोकानामस्तु वै शिवम्॥

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: न्यस्यायुधानि विश्वेश जगतो हितकाम्यया।
en: Let good happen to the three worlds. Throw down your weapons, O lord of the universe, for doing good to the world.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: यदक्षरमथाव्यक्तमीशं लोकस्य भावनम्॥ कूटस्थं कर्तृ निर्द्वन्द्वमकर्तेति च यं विदुः। व्यक्तिभावगतस्यास्य एका मूर्तिरियं शुभा॥ नरो नारायणश्चैव जातौ ,धर्मकुलोद्वहौ।
en: That which is indestructible, immutable, supreme, the origin of the universe, uniform, and the supreme actor, that which is above all pairs of opposites, and inactive, has, chosing to be shown, been pleased to assume this one blessed form. This Nara and Narayana have taken birth in the race of Dharma.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: तपसा महता युक्तौ देवश्रेष्ठौ महाव्रतौ॥ अहं प्रसादजस्तस्य कुतश्चित् कारणान्तरे।
en: The foremost of all gods, these two are observers of the highest vows and gifted with the severest penances. Through some reason best known to Him. I myself have originated from the quality of His Grace.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: त्वं चैव क्रोधजस्तात पूर्वसर्गे सनातनः॥ मया च सार्धं वरद विबुधैश्च महर्षिभिः। प्रसादयाशु लोकानां शान्तिर्भवतु मा चिरम्॥
en: Eternal as you are, for you have ever existed since all the past creations, you too have originated from His anger. With myself then, these gods, and all the great Rishis, do you worship this displayed form of Brahma and let peace be to all the worlds forthwith!

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: ब्रह्मणा त्वेवमुक्तस्तु रुद्रः क्रोधाग्निमुत्सृजन्। प्रसादयामास ततो देवं नारायणं प्रभुम्। शरणं च जगामाद्यं वरेण्यं वरदं प्रभुम्॥
en: Thus addressed by Brahman, Rudra iminediately renounced the fire of his anger and began to please the illustrious and powerful Narayana. Indeed, he soon placed himself at the disposal of the worshipful, boongiving, and powerful Narayana.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: ततोऽथ वरदो देवो जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः। प्रीतिमानभवत् तत्र रुद्रेण सह संगतः॥
en: That boon-giving god who has his anger and the senses under control, became soon pleased and reconciled with Rudra.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: ऋषिभिर्ब्रह्मणा चैव विबुधैश्च सुपूजितः। उवाच देवमीशानमीशः स जगतो हरिः॥
en: Well-worshipped by the Rishis, by Brahmana, and by all the gods the great God, the Lord of the universe, otherwise called by the name of Hari, then addressed the illustrious

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: यस्त्वां वेत्ति स मां वेत्ति यस्त्वामनु स मामनु। नावयोरन्तरं किंचिन्मा तेऽभूद् बुद्धिरन्यथा॥
en: He who knows you knows me. He who follows you follows me! There is no difference between you and me. Do you never think otherwise.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: अद्यप्रभृति श्रीवत्सः शूलाको मे भवत्वयम्। मम पाण्यङ्कितश्चापि श्रीकण्ठस्त्वं भविष्यसि॥
en: The mark made by your lance on my chest will from this day put on the form of a beautiful whirl, and the mark of my hand on your throat will also assume a beautiful shape on account of which you shall, from this day forth, be called by the name of Shreekantha.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच एवं लक्षणमुत्पाद्य परस्परकृतं तदा। सख्यं चैवातुलं कृत्वा रुद्रेण सहितावृषी॥ तपस्तेपतुरव्यग्रौ विसृज्य त्रिदिवौकसः। एष ते कथितः पार्थ नारायणजयो मृधे॥
en: Having mutually caused such marks on each other's body, the two Rishis Nara and Narayana thus made friends with Rudra and sending away the gods, once more began to practise penances with a tranquil souls. I have thus told you, O son of Pritha, how in that battle which occurred in days of yore between Rudra and Narayana, the latter got the victory.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: नामानि चैव गुह्यानि निरुक्तानि च भारत। ऋषिभिः कथितानीह यानि संकीर्तितानि ते॥
en: I have told you the many secret names by which Narayana is called, and what the meanings, O Bharata, are of those names, which, as I have told you the Rishis have bestowed upon the great God.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: एवं बहुविधै रूपैश्चरामीह वसुन्धराम्। ब्रह्मलोकं च कौन्तेय गोलोकं च सनातनम्॥ मया त्वं रक्षितो युद्धे महान्तं प्राप्तवाञ्जयम्।
en: In this way, O son of Kunti, assuming various forms do I rove at will, through the Earth, the region of Brahman himself, and that other high and eternal region of happiness called Goloka. Protected by me in the great battle, you have acquired a great victory.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: यस्तु ते सोऽग्रतो याति युद्धे सम्प्रत्युपस्थिते॥ तं विद्धि रुद्र कौन्तेय देवदेवं कपर्दिनम्।
en: That Being whom, at the time of all your battles, you saw stalking in your van, know, O son of Kunti, is no other than Rudra, that god of gods, otherwise called by the name of Kaparddin.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: कालः स एव कथितः क्रोधजेति मया तव॥ निहतास्तेन वै पूर्वं हतवानसि यान् रिपून्।
en: He is otherwise known by the name of Kala and should be known as one that has originated from my anger. The enemies whom you have killed were all, in the first instance, killed by him.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: अप्रमेयप्रभावं तं देवदेवमुमापतिम्। नमस्व देवं प्रयतो विश्वेशं हरमक्षयम्॥
en: Do you bend your head to that god of gods, the lord of Uma, gifted with immeasurable power. With concentrated soul, do you bend your head to that illustrious Lord of the universe, that indestructible god, otherwise called by the name of Hara.

description: The attainment of uniformity by Agni and Soma-the birth of gods, Manus etc.
sn: यश्च ते कथितः पूर्वं क्रोधजेति पुनः पुनः। तस्य प्रभाव एकाग्रे यच्छ्रुतं ते धनंजय॥
en: He is none else than that god who, I have repeatedly said to you, has originated from my anger. You have before this, heard, O Dhananjaya, of the power and energy which live in him.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: शौनक उवाच सौते सुमहदाख्यानं भवता परिकीर्तितम्। यच्छ्रुत्वा मुनयः सर्वे विस्मयं परमं गताः॥
en: Saunaka said O Sauti, excellent is this discourse which you have recounted. Varily, these ascetics, having heard it, have all been filled with surprise.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: सर्वाश्रमाभिगमनं सर्वतीर्थावगाहनम्। न तथा फलदं सौते नारायणकथा यथा।॥
en: It is said, O Sauti, that a discourse that has Narayana for its subject is more fruitful of merit than sojourns to all the sacred retreats and ablutions performed in all the sacred waters on the Earth.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: पाविताङ्गाः स्म संवृत्ताः श्रुत्वेमामादितः कथाम्। नारायणाश्रयां पुण्यां सर्वपापप्रमोचनीम्॥
en: Having listened to this discourse of yours that has Narayana for its theme, that is sacred and capable of purifying one of every sin, all of us have certainly become holy.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: दुर्दर्शो भगवान् देवः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः। सब्रह्मकैः सुरैः कृत्स्नैरन्यैश्चैव महर्षिभिः॥
en: Worshipped of all the worlds, that illustrious and foremost of gods is incapable of being seen by the gods with Brahman numbering among them and all the Rishis.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: दृष्टवान् नारदो यत्तु देवं नारायणं हरिम्। नूनमेतद्ध्यनुमतं तस्य देवस्य सूतज॥
en: That Narada was able to see of Narayana, otherwise called Hari, was owing, O son of Suta, to the especial favour of that divine and powerful Lord.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: यद् दृष्टवान् जगन्नाथमनिरुद्धतनौ स्थितम्। यत् प्राद्रवत् पुनर्भूयो नारदो देवसत्तमौ॥ नरनारायणौ द्रष्टुं कारणं तद् ब्रवीहि मे।
en: When, however, the celestial Rishi Narada had succeeded in seeing the Supreme Lord of the universe as residing in the form of Aniruddha, why did he again proceed so speedily (to the retreat of Vadari) for seeing those two foremost of gods, viz., Nara and Narayana? Do you, O Sauti, tell us the reason of Narada's conduct.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: सौतिरुवाच तस्मिन् यज्ञे वर्तमाने राज्ञः पारिक्षितस्य वै॥ कर्मान्तरेषु विधिवद् वर्तमानेषु शौनक। कृष्णद्वैपायनं व्यासमृर्षि वेदनिधिं प्रभुम्॥ परिपप्रच्छ राजेन्द्रः पितामहपितामहम्।
en: Sauti said During the continuance of his Sacrifice, Janamejaya, the royal son of Parikshit, taking advantage of an interval in the sacrificial rites, and when all the learned Brahmanas were resting, O Shaunaka, that king of kings, addressed the grand-father of his grand-father, viz., the Island-born Rishi Krishna, otherwise called Vyasa, that ocean of Vedic learning, that foremost of ascetics gifted with power, and said these words.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: जनमेजय उवाच श्वेतद्वीपान्निवृत्तेन नारदेन सुरर्षिणा॥ ध्यायता भगवद्वाक्यं चेष्टितं किमतः परम्।
en: Janamejaya said After the celestial Rishi Narada had come beck from White-Island, reflecting, as he came, on the words spoken to him by the holy Narayana, what, indeed, did that great ascetic next do?

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: बदर्याश्रममागम्य समागम्य च तावृषी॥ कियन्तं कालमवसत् कां कथां पृष्टवांश्च सः।
en: Arrived at the retreat known by the name of Vadari on the breast of the Himavat mountains, and seeing the two Rishis Nara and Narayana who were practising severe austerities at that place, how long did Narada live there and what were the subjects of conversation between him and the two Rishis?

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: इदं शतसहस्राद्धि भारताख्यानविस्तरात्॥ आमन्थ्य मतिमन्थेन ज्ञानोदधिमनुत्तमम्।
en: This discourse on Narayana, that is really an ocean of knowledge, has been raised by your intelligent self by churning that vast history called Bharata which consists of a hundred thousand Verses,

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: नवनीतं यथा दध्मो मलयाच्चन्दनं यथा॥ आरण्यकं च वेदेभ्य ओषधिभ्योऽमृतं यथा। समुद्धृतमिदं ब्रह्मन् कथामृतमिदं तथा॥ तपोनिधे त्वयोक्तं हि नारायणकथाश्रयम्।
en: As butter is raised from curds, sandal-wood from the mountains of Malaya, the Aranyakas from the Vedas, and ambrosia from all the medicinal herbs, similarly, O ocean of austerities, has this discourse that is like ambrosia and that has Narayana for its object, been raised by you, O Brahmana, from various histories and Puranas existing in the world.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: स ईशो भगवान् देवः सर्वभूतात्मभावनः॥ अहो नारायणं तेजो दुर्दर्श द्विजसत्तम।
en: Narayana is the Supreme Lord. Illustrious and gifted with great power. He is the soul of all creatures. Indeed, O foremost of twice-born ones, the energy of Narayana is irresistible.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: यत्राविशन्ति कल्पान्ते सर्वे ब्रह्मादय: सुराः॥ ऋषयश्च सगन्धर्वा यच्च किंचिच्चराचरम्।
en: At the end of the aeon, all the gods having Brahman for their foremost, all Rishis with the Gandharvas, and all things mobile and immobile, enter into Narayana.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: न ततोऽस्ति परं मन्ये पावनं दिवि चेह च॥ सर्वाश्रमाभिगमनं सर्वतीर्थावगाहनम्। न तथा फलदं चापि नारायणकथा यथा॥ सर्वथा पाविताः स्मेह श्रुत्वेमामादितः कथाम्। हरेविश्वेश्वरस्येह सर्वपापप्रणाशनीम्॥ न चित्रं कृतवांस्तत्र यदार्यो मे धनंजयः। वासुदेवसहायो यः प्राप्तवाञ्जयमुत्तमम्॥ न चास्य किंचिदप्राप्यं मन्ये लोकेष्वपि त्रिषु। त्रैलोक्यनाथो विष्णुः स यथाऽऽसीत् साह्यकृत् स वै। धन्याश्च सर्व एवासन् ब्रह्मस्ते मम पूर्वजाः। हिताय श्रेयसे चैव येषामसीज्जनार्दनः॥ तपसाथ सुदृश्यो हि भगवाल्लोकपूजितः।
en: I think, therefore, that there is nothing holier on earth or in heaven and nothing higher than Narayana. A sojourn to all the sacred places on Earth, and ablutions performed in all were the sacred waters, do not produce so much merit as a discourse that has Narayana for its subject. Having listened to this discourse from the beginning,-this discourse on Hari, the lord of the universe, which dissipates all sins, we feel that we have been purged off of all our sins, and sanctified entirely. Nothing wonderful was done by my ancestor Dhananjaya whose was the victory in the great battle on Kurukshetra, for it should be remembered that he had Vasudeva for his friend. I think that that person could have nothing unattainable in the three-worlds, who had for his friend Vishnu himself, that great Lord of the universe! Highly fortunate and and commendable those ancestors of mine, since they had Janarddana himself for superintending their temporal and spiritual prosperity. Worshipped of all the worlds, the holy Narayana is capable of being seen with the help of austerities alone.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: यं दृष्टवन्तस्ते साक्षाच्छ्वत्साकविभूषणम्॥ तेभ्यो धन्यतरचैव नारदः परमेष्ठिजः।
en: They, however, succeeded in seeing Narayana adorned with the beautiful mystic mark. More fortunate than my ancestors was the celestial Rishi Narada the the son of Prameshthi.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: न चाल्पतेजसमृर्षि वेद्म नारदमव्ययम्॥ श्वेतद्वीपं समासाद्य येन दृष्टः स्वयं हरिः।
en: Indeed, I think that Narada, who is above all destruction, was gifted with great energy, for going to White-Island he had succeeded in seeing the person of Hari.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: देवप्रसादानुगतं व्यक्तं तत् तस्य दर्शनम्॥ तद् दृष्टवांस्तदा देवमनिरुद्धतनौ स्थितम्।
en: Indeed, it is clear that the sight he had got of the Supreme Lord was owing to only the favour of that Being. Fortunate was Narada inasmuch as he had succeeded in seeing Narayana as existing in the form of Aniruddha. agiru TTG: TECL 7:118411

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: नरनारायणौ द्रष्टुं किं तु तत् कारणं मुने।
en: Having seen Narayana in that form, why did Narada hasten once more to the hermitage of Vadari for seeing Nara and Narayana! What was the reason, O ascetic of this step taken by Narada?

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: श्वेतद्वीपानिवृत्तश्च नारदः परमेष्ठिजः॥ बदरीमाश्रमं प्राप्य समागम्य च तावृषी। कियन्तं कालमवसत् प्रश्नान् कान् पृष्टवांश्च ह॥ श्वेतद्वीपादुपावृत्ते तस्मिन् वा सुमहात्मनि। किमब्रूतां महात्मानौ नरनारायणावृषी॥ तदेतन्मे यथातत्त्वं सर्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि।
en: How long also did Narada the son of Prameshthi, after his return from White Island and arrival at Vadari and meeting with the two Rishis Nara and Narayana, reside there, and what conversation had he with them? What did those two great and foremost of Rishis say to him? You should tell me all this.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच नमो भवगते तस्मै व्यासायामिततेजसे॥ यस्य प्रसादाद् वक्ष्यामि नारायणकथामिमाम्।
en: Vaishampayana said Salutations to the holy Vyasa of incomparable energy. Through his favour; I shall recite this narrative having Narayana for its theme.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: प्राप्य श्वेतं महाद्वीपं दृष्ट्वा च हरिमव्ययम्॥ निवृत्तो नारदो राजंस्तरसा मेरुमागमत्। हृदयेनोद्वहन् भारं यदुक्तं परमात्मना॥
en: Arrived at White Island Narada saw the immutable Hari. Leaving that place, he speedily went, O king, to the mountains of Meru, remembering those weighty words which the Supreme Lord had said to him. Arrived at Meru he became filled with wonder at the thought, O king, of what he had done.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: पश्चादस्याभवद् राजन्नात्मनः साध्वसं महत्। यद् गत्वा दूरमध्वानं क्षेमी पुनरिहागतः॥ मेरोः प्रचक्राम ततः पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्।
en: And he said to himself,-'How wonderful is it! The journey I have done is a long one! Having gone to such a distance, I have returned safe and sound!' From the mountains of Meru he then went towards Gandhamadana.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: निपपात च खात् तूर्णं विशाला बदरीमनु॥ ततः स ददृशे देवौ पुराणावृषिसत्तमौ। तपश्चरन्तौ सुमहदात्मनिष्ठौ महाव्रतौ॥
en: Passing through the skies he speedily got down upon that extensive retreat known by the name of Vadari. There he saw those ancient gods, viz., those two foremost of Rishis, (called Nara and Narayana) performing penances, observing high vows, and depending upon their own selves.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: तेजसाभ्यधिको सूर्यात् सर्वलोकविरोचनात्। श्रीवत्सलक्षणौ पूज्यौ जटामण्डलधारिणौ॥
en: Both of those adorable persons bore on their chests the mystic marks called Shrivatsa, and both had matted locks on their heads. And an account of the effulgence with which they illumined the world they seemed to surpass the very Sun in energy.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: जालपादभुजौ तौ तु पादयोश्चक्रलक्षणौ। व्यूढोरस्कौ दीर्घभुजौ तथा मुष्कचतुष्किणौ॥
en: The palms of each bore the mark called the swan's foot. The soles of their feet bore the mark of the discus. Their chests were very broad; their arms extended to their knees. Each of them had four shoulder joints.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: षष्टिदन्तावष्टदंष्ट्रौ मेघौघसदृशस्वनौ। स्वास्यौ पृथुललाटौ च सुभ्र सुहनुनासिकौ॥
en: Each of them had sixty teeth and four arms. The voice of each was as deep as the roaring of the clouds. Their faces were highly beautiful, their foreheads broad, their brows fair, their cheeks well-formed, and their noses acquiline.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: आतपत्रेण सदृशे शिरसी देवयोस्तयोः। एवं लक्षणसम्पन्नौ महापुरुषसंज्ञितौ॥
en: The heads of those two gods were large and round, resembling open umbrellas. Endued with these marks, they were certainly very superior persons in appearance.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा नारदो हृष्टस्ताभ्यां च प्रतिपूजितः। स्वागतेनाभिभाष्याथ पृष्टश्चानामयं तथा॥ बभूवान्तर्गतमतिर्निरीक्ष्य पुरुषोत्तमौ। सदोगतास्तत्र ये वै सर्वभूतनमस्कृताः॥ श्वेतद्वीपे मया दृष्टास्तादृशावृषिसत्तमौ।
en: Seeing them Narada became filled with joy. He saluted them with respect and was saluted by them in return. They received the celestial Rishi, saying Welcome,' and made the ordinary enquiries. Seeing those two foremost of Beings, Narada began to think within himself, — These two foremost of Rishis that are respected by all creatures seem to be very like, in appearance, to those persons, worshipped of all beings, whom I have seen in White-Island.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: इति संचिन्त्य मनसा कृत्वा चाभिप्रदक्षिणम्॥ स चोपविविशे तत्र पीठे कुशमये शुभे।
en: Thinking thus, he went round them both and then sat down on the excellent seat made of Kusha grass that had been offered to him.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: ततस्तौ तपसां वासौ यशसां तेजसामपि॥ ऋषी शमदमोपेतौ कृत्वा पौर्वाह्निकं विधिम्।
en: After this, those two Rishis that were the abode of penances, of famous deeds, and of energy,-those ascetics that were gifted with tranquillity of heart and self-control, performed their morning rites.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: पश्चान्नारदमव्यग्रौ पाद्यार्थ्याभ्यामथार्चतः॥ पीठयोचोपविष्टौ तौ कृतातिथ्याह्निको नृप।
en: They then, without anxious hearts, adored Narada with water to wash his feet and the usual articles of the Arghya. Having performed their morning rites and the observances necessary for receiving their guest, they sat down on the two seats made of wood.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: तेषु तत्रोपविष्टेषु स देशोऽभिव्यराजत॥ आज्याहुतिमहाज्वालैर्यज्ञवाटो यथाग्निभिः।
en: When those two Rishis sat, that place began to shine with peculiar beauty even as the sacrificial altar shines with beauty on account of the sacred fires when libations of clarified butter are poured upon them.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: अथ नारायणस्तत्र नारदं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ सुखोपविष्टं विश्रान्तं कृतातिथ्यं सुखस्थितम्।
en: Then seeing Narada refreshed from fatigue and seated at his ease and well-pleased with the rites of hospitality he had received, Narayana said these words.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: नरनारायणावूचतुः। अपीदानी स भगवान् परमात्मा सनातनः॥ श्वेतद्वीपे त्वया दृष्ट आवयोः प्रकृतिः परा।
en: Have you seen in White Island the Supreme Soul, who is eternal and divine, and who is the high source whence we have originated.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: नारद उवाच दृष्टो मे पुरुषः श्रीमान् विश्वरूपधरोऽव्ययः॥ सर्वे लोका हि तत्रस्थास्तथा देवाः सहर्षिभिः।
en: Narada said are I have seen that beautiful Being who is immutable and who has universe for his form! In Hiin live all the worlds, and all the gods with the Rishis.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: अद्यापि चैनं पश्यामि युवां पश्यन् सनातनौ।॥ यैर्लक्षणैरुपेतः स हरिरव्यक्तरूपधृक्। तैर्लक्षणैरुपेतौ हि व्यक्तरूपधरौ युवाम्॥ दृष्टौ युवां मया तत्र तस्य देवस्य पार्श्वतः।
en: Even now I see that Being in seeing you two who eternal. Those marks and indications that characterise Hari himself of unmanifest form, characterise you two who are endued with manifest forms. Verily, I see both of you by the side of that great God.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: इहैव चागतोऽस्म्पद्य विसृष्टः परमात्मना॥ को हि नाम भवेत् तस्य तेजसा यशसा श्रिया। सदृशस्त्रिषु लोकेषु ऋते धर्मात्मजौ युवाम्॥
en: Dismissed by the Supreme Soul, I have come here to-day. In energy, fame and beauty, who else in the three worlds can equal Him than you two who have been born in the race of Dharma.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: तेन मे कथितः कृत्स्नो धर्मः क्षेत्रज्ञसंज्ञितः। प्रादुर्भावाश्च कथिता भविष्या इह ये यथा।॥
en: He has told me the entire list of duties referring to Soul. He has also told me of all those incarnations which he will, in the future, have in this world.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: तत्र ये पुरुषाः श्वेताः पञ्चेन्द्रियविवर्जिताः। प्रतिबुद्धाश्च ते सर्वे भक्ताश्च पुरुषोत्तमम्॥ तेऽर्चयन्ति सदा देवं तैः सार्धं रमते च सः।
en: The inhabitants, of White Island whom I have seen, are all shorn of the five senses that the ordinary persons have. All of them are of awakened souls, endued as they are with true knowledge. They are, again, entirely devoted to the foremost of Beings, viz., the Supreme Lord of the universe. They always engaged in adoring that great God, and the latter always sports with them.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: प्रियभक्तो हि भगवान् परमात्मा द्विजप्रियः॥ रमते सोऽय॑मानो हि सदा भागवतप्रियः।
en: The holy and Supreme Soul is always fond of those who are devoted to him. He is fond also of the twice-born ones. Always fond of those who are devoted to Him. He sports with those worshippers of His.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: विश्वभुक् सर्वगो देवो माधवो भक्तवत्सलः॥ स कर्ता कारणं चैव कार्यं चातिबलद्युतिः।
en: Enjoying the universe, pervading everything, the illustrious Madhava is ever affectionate towards his worshippers. He is the Actor; he is the Cause; and He is the Effect. He is gifted with omnipotence and immeasurable, effulgence.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: हेतुश्चाज्ञा विधानं च तत्त्वं चैव महायशाः॥ तपसा योज्य सोऽऽत्मानं श्वेतद्वीपात् परं हि यत्। तेज इत्यभिविख्यातं स्वयंभासावभासितम्॥ शान्तिः सा त्रिषु लोकेषु विहिता भावितात्मना।
en: He is the Cause whence all things proceed. He is the embodiment of all the scriptural injunction. He is the embodiment of all themes. He is endued with great fame. Uniting Himself with penances, He has lighted Himself with a splendour which is said to represent an energy that is higher than (what is in) White Island. Of soul purified by penances, He has ordained Peace and Tranquillity in the three worlds.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: एतया शुभया बुद्ध्या नैष्ठिकं व्रतमास्थितः॥ न तत्र सूर्यस्तपति न सोमोऽभिविराजते। न वायुर्वाति देवेशे तपश्चरति दुश्चरम्॥
en: With such an auspicious understanding, he observes a very superior vow which is the embodiment of holiness. The Sun warms not and Soma does not adorn the region where he lives practising austerest penances. There the wind blows not.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: वेदीमष्टनलोत्सेधां भूमावास्थाय विश्वकृत्। एकपादस्थितो देव उर्ध्वबाहुरुदङ्मुख॥
en: Having made an altar measuring eight fingers breadth, the illustrious Creator of the universe is practising penances there, standing on one foot, with arms upraised, and with face directed towards the East.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: साङ्गानावर्तयन् वेदांस्तपस्तेपे सुदुश्चरम्। यद् ब्रह्मा ऋषयश्चैव स्वयं पशुपतिश्च यत्॥ शेषाश्च विबुधश्रेष्ठा दैत्यदानवराक्षसाः। नागाः सुपर्णा गन्धर्वाः सिद्धा राजर्षयश्च ये॥ हव्यं कव्यं च सततं विधियुक्तं प्रयुञ्जते। कृत्स्नं तु तस्य देवस्य चरणावुपतिष्ठति॥
en: Reciting the Vedas with their branches, he is practising the severest austerities. Whatever libations of clarified butter or meat are poured on the sacrificial fire according to the ordinances of Brahman, by the Rishis, by Pashupati himself, by the rest of the principal gods, by the Daityas, the Danavas, and the Rakshasas, Nagas, Garuda bird, Gandharvas, Siddhas and foremost of the sages and whatever sacrificial oblation are offered, all reach the feet of that great god.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: याः क्रियाः सम्प्रयुक्ताश्च एकान्तगतबुद्धिभिः। ताः सर्वाः शिरसा देवः प्रतिगृह्णाति वै स्वयम्॥
en: Whatever rites and religious acts are performed by persons whose souls are entirely given to him, are all received by that great God on his head.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: न तस्यान्यः प्रियतरः प्रतिबुद्धैर्महात्मभिः। विद्यते त्रिषु लोकेषु ततोऽस्यैकान्तिकं गतः॥
en: No one is dearer to him in the three worlds than those persons who are enlightened and possessed of great souls. Dearer even than those persons is one who is entirely devoted to him.

description: Why did Narada succeed in seeing Narayana? Why did he go to see Nara and Narayana
sn: इह चैवागतस्तेन विसृष्टः परमात्मना। एवं मे भगवान् देवः स्वयमाख्यातवान् हरिः। आसिष्ये तत्परो भूत्वा युवाभ्यां सह नित्यशः॥
en: Dismissed by him who is the Supreme Soul, I am coming here. This is what the illustrious and holy Hari has himself said to me. I shall henceforth live with you two, devoted to Narayana in the form of Anirudhha.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: नरनारायणावूचतुः धन्योऽस्यनुगृहीतोऽसि यत् ते दृष्टः स्वयं प्रभुः। न हि तं दृष्टवान् कश्चित् पद्मयोनिरपि स्वयम्॥
en: Nara and Narayana said You deserve very high encomiums, and highly favoured have you been, since you have seen the powerful Narayana himself. None else, not even Brahman himself who has sprung from the primal lotus, has been able to see him.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: अव्यक्तयोनिर्भगवान् दुर्दर्शः पुरुषोत्तमः। नारदैतद्धि नौ सत्यं वचनं समुदाहृतम्॥
en: That foremost of Purushas, gifted with power and holiness, is of unmanifest origin and incapable of being seen. These words that we say to you are very true, O Narada!

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: नास्य भक्तात् प्रियतरो लोके कश्चन विद्यते। ततः स्वयं दर्शितवान् स्वमात्मानं द्विजोत्तम॥
en: There exists no one in the universe who is dearer to him than one that worships him with devotion. It is, therefore, O best of twice-born ones, that he showed himself to you!

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: तपो हि तप्यतस्तस्य यत् स्थान परमात्मनः। न तत् सम्प्राप्नुते कश्चिदृते ह्यावां द्विजोत्तम॥
en: No one can go to that realm where the Supreme Soul resides practising penances, except we two, O foremost of twice-born ones.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: या हि सूर्यसहस्रस्य समस्तस्य भवेद् द्युतिः। स्थानस्य सा भवेत् तस्य स्वयं तेन विराजता॥
en: On account of that places being adorned by Him, Its splendour resembles the effulgence of a thousand Suns collected together.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: तस्मादुत्तिष्ठते विप्र देवाद् विश्वभुवः पतेः। क्षमा क्षमावतां श्रेष्ठ यया भूमिस्तु युज्यते॥
en: From that illustrious Being, O Brahmana, from Him who is the origin of the Creator of the universe, O foremost of all persons gifted with forgiveness, originates the attribute of forgiveness which attaches to the Earth.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: तस्माच्चोत्तिष्ठते देवात् सर्वभूतहिताद् रसः। आपो हि तेन युज्यन्ते द्रवत्वं प्राप्नुवन्ति च॥
en: It is from that illustrious Being whose attributes are for the good of all beings, that Rasa (Taste) has flown. The attribute of Rasa belongs to the waters which are, again, liquid.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: तस्मादेव समुद्भूतं तेजो रूपगुणात्मकम्। येन संयुज्यते सूर्यस्ततो लोके विराजते॥
en: It is from Him that Heat or Light has flown, having the attribute of Form or vision for its soul. It belongs to the Sun on account of which the Sun becomes able to shine and give heat.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: तस्माद् देवात् समुद्भूतः स्पर्शस्तु पुरुषोत्तमात्। येन स्म युज्यते वायुस्ततो लोकान् विवात्यसौ॥
en: It is from that illustrious and foremost of Beings that Touch also has originated. It belongs to the Wind, on account of which the Wind moves about in the world producing the sensation of Touch.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: तस्माच्चोत्तिष्ठते शब्दः सर्वलोकेश्वरात् प्रभोः। आकाशं युज्यते येन ततस्तिष्ठत्यसंवृतम्॥
en: It is from that powerful Lord of the entire universe that that Sound has arisen. It belongs to Ether, which, therefore, exists uncovered and unconfined.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: तस्माच्चोत्तिष्ठते देवात् सर्वभूतगतं मनः। चन्द्रमा येन संयुक्तः प्रकाशगुणधारणः॥
en: It is from that illustrious Being that Mind, which pervades all Beings, has originated. It belongs to the Moon, on account of which the Moon has come to be invested with the attribute of showing all the things.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: यद्धृतोत्पादकं नाम तत् स्थानं वेदसंज्ञितम्। विद्यासहायो यत्रास्ते भगवान् हव्यकव्यभुक्॥
en: That spot where the divine Narayana, that cater of the libations and other offerings made in sacrifices lives with Knowledge alone for his companion, has, in the Vedas, been called by the name of the productive cause of all things known as Sat.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: ये हि निष्कलुषा लोके पुण्यपापविवर्जिताः। तेषां वै क्षेममध्वानं गच्छतां द्विजसत्तम॥
en: The path that is theirs, O foremost of twiceborn ones, that are stainless and that are freed from both virtue and sin, is fraught with auspiciousness and happiness.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: सर्वलोकतमोहन्ता आदित्यो द्वारमुच्यते। आदित्यदग्धसर्वाङ्गा अदृश्याः केनचित् क्वचित्॥
en: The Sun, who is the remover of the darkness of all the worlds, is said to be the door. Entering the Sun, the bodies of such persons consumed by his fire. They then become invisible for after that they cannot be beheld by any one at any time.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: परमाणुभूता भूत्वा तु तं देवं प्रविशन्त्युत। तस्मादपि च निर्मुक्ता अनिरुद्धतनौ स्थिताः॥
en: Reduced into invisible atoms, they then enter into Narayana. Passing out from him also, they enter into the form of Aniruddha.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: मनोभूतास्ततो भूत्वा प्रद्युम्नं प्रविशन्त्युत। प्रद्युम्नाच्चापि निर्मुक्ता जीवं संकर्षणं ततः॥ विशन्ति विप्रप्रवरा: सांख्या भागवतैः सह। ततस्त्रैगुण्यहीनास्ते परमात्मानमञ्जसा॥ प्रविशन्ति द्विजश्रेष्ठाः क्षेत्रज्ञं निर्गुणात्मकम्। सर्वावासं वासुदेवं क्षेत्रज्ञं विद्धिं तत्त्वतः॥
en: Losing all physical attributes altogether and changed into mind alone, they then enter into Pradyumna. Passing out of Pradyumna, those foremost of twice-born ones, including both those who are conversant with Sankhya philosophy and those who are devoted to the Supreme God, then enter Sankarshana who is otherwise called Individual Soul. After inis, divested of the three primal qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance, those foremost of twice-born ones speedily enter the Supreme Soul otherwise called Kshetrajna and which itself is above the three primal qualities. Know that Vasudeva is He called Kshetrajna. Verily should you know that, that Vasudeva is the residence or original refuge of all things in the universe.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: समाहितमनस्काश्च नियताः संयतेन्द्रियाः। एकान्तभावोपगता वासुदेवं विशन्ति ते॥
en: Only they whose mind are concentrated, who observe all sorts of restraint, whose senses are restrained, and who are devoted with their whole souls, succeed in entering Vasudeva.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: आवामपि च धर्मस्य गृहे जातौ द्विजोत्तम। रम्यां विशालामाश्रित्य तप उग्रं समास्थितौ॥
en: We two, O foremost to twice-born ones, have taken birth in the house of Dharma. Living in this charming and spacious herinitage, we are practising the austerest penances.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: ये तु तस्यैव देवस्य प्रादुर्भावाः सुरप्रियाः। भविष्यन्ति त्रिलोकस्थास्तेषां स्वतीत्यथो द्विज॥
en: We are thus employed, O twice-born one, moved by the desire of benefiting those manifestations of the Supreme God, dear to all the celestials, that will appear in the three worlds.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: विधिना स्वेन युक्ताभ्यां यथापूर्वं द्विजोत्तम। आस्थिताभ्यां सर्वकृच्छ्रे व्रतं सम्यगनुत्तमम्॥
en: In accordance, one after another, which such ordinances as are extraordinary and as apply to us two only, O best of twice-born ones, we are duly observing all excellent and high vows fraught with the austerest penances.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: आवाभ्यामपि दृष्टस्त्वं श्वेतद्वीपे तपोधन। समागतो भगवता संजल्पं कृतवांस्तथा॥
en: You, O celestial Rishi having penances for your wealth were seen by us in White Island when you were there. Having met with Narayana, you have formed a particular resolution.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: सर्वं हि नौ संविदितं त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे। यद् भविष्यति वृत्तं वा वर्तते वा शुभाशुभम्। सर्वं स ते कथितवान् देवदेवो महामुने॥
en: In the three worlds consisting of mobile and immobile Beings, there is nothing that we do not know. Of good or evil that will occur or has occurred or is occurring, that God of gods, O great ascetic, has informed you.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा तयोर्वाक्यं तपस्युगे च वर्ततोः। नारदः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा नारायणपरायणः॥
en: Vaishampayana continued Having heard these words of Nara and Narayana both of whom were practising the austerest penances, the celestial Rishi Narada joined his hands in respect and became entirely devoted to Narayana.

description: Nara and Narayana said to Narada that for his devotion the Great God showed himself to him
sn: जजाप विधिवन्मन्त्रान् नारायणगतान् बहून्। दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं हि नरनारायणाश्रमे॥ अवसत् स महातेजा नारदो भगवानृषिः। तमेवाभ्यर्चयन् देवं नरनारायणौ च तौ॥
en: He passed his time in mental recitation, with due observances, numberless sacred Mantras that are approved by Narayana. Adoring the Supreme Deity Narayana, and worshipping those two ancient Rishis also that had taken birth in the house of Dharma, the illustrious Rishis Narada, gifted with great energy, continued to live, thus engaged, in that retreat, called Vadari, on the breast of Himavat, belonging to Nara and Narayana, for thousand divine years. a worshipping those two ancient Rishis also that had taken birth in the house of Dharma, the illustrious Rishis Narada, gifted with great energy, continued to live, thus engaged, in that retreat, called Vadari, on the breast of Himavat, belonging to Nara and Narayana, for thousand divine years. a

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य नारदः परमेष्ठिजः। दैवं कृत्वा यथान्यायं पित्र्यं चक्रे ततः परम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said On one occasion, while living in the hermitage of Nara and Narayana, Narada the son of Prameshthi, having duly performed the rites and observances in honour of the gods, began to perforin thereafter the rites in honour of the departed manes.

sn: ततस्तं वचनं प्राह ज्येष्ठो धर्मात्मजः प्रभुः। क इज्यते द्विजश्रेष्ठ दैवे पित्र्ये च कल्पिते॥ त्वया मतिमतां श्रेष्ठ तन्मे शंस यथागमम्। किमेतत् क्रियते कर्म फलं वास्य किमिष्यते॥
en: Beholding him thus prepared, the eldest son of Dharma, viz., the powerful Narayana, addressed him, saying,-Whom you adoring, O foremost of twice-born ones, by these rites and the observances in connection with the gods and the departed means. O foremost of all persons gifted with intelligence, tell me this, agreeably to the scriptures. What is this that you are doing? What also are the fruits desired by you of those rites which you are performing. are

sn: नारद उवाच त्वयैतत् कथितं पूर्वं दैवं कर्तव्यमित्यपि। दैवतं च परो यज्ञः परमात्मा सनातनः॥
en: Narada said You said to me formerly that rites and observances in honour of the gods should be performed. You said that the rites in honour of the gods from the highest sacrifice and are equivalent to the worship of the Eternal and Supreme Soul.

sn: ततस्तद्भावितो नित्यं यजे वैकुण्ठमव्ययम्। तस्माच्च प्रसृतः पूर्वं ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः॥
en: Thus instructed, I always sacrifice in honour of the eternal and iminutable Vishnu through these rites that I perform in adoring the gods. It is from that Supreme Deity that Brahman, the Grandfather of all the worlds, sprang in days of yore.

sn: मम वै पितरं प्रीतः परमेष्ठ्यप्यजीजनत्। अहं संकल्पजस्तस्य पुत्रः प्रथमकल्पितः॥
en: That Brahman, otherwise called Prameshthi, filled with cheerfulness, caused my father (Daksha) to come into being. I was the son of Brahman, created before all others, by his will.

sn: यजामि वै पितृन् साधो नारायणविधौ कृते। एवं स एव भगवान् पिता माता पितामहः॥
en: Orighteous and illustrious one, I am performing these rites in honour of the departed manes for the sake of Narayana and according to those ordinances that have been ordained by himself. The illustrious Narayana is the father, mother, and grandfather.

sn: इज्यते पितृयज्ञेषु तथा नित्यं जगत्पतिः। श्रुतिश्चाप्यपरा देवी पुत्रान् हि पितरोऽयजन्॥
en: In all sacrifices performed in honour of the departed manes, it is that Lord of the universe who is worshipped. On one occasion, the gods, who were father, taught their children the Shrutis.

sn: वेदश्रुतिः प्रणष्टा च पुनरध्यापिता सुतैः। ततस्ते मन्त्रदाः पुत्राः पितृत्वमुपपेदिरे॥
en: Having lost their knowledge of the Shrutis, and father had to acquire it again from those sons to whom they had come municated it. On account of this incident, the sons, who had thus to communicate the Mantras to their father, acquired the status of fathers.

sn: वै नूनं पुरैतद् विदितं युवयोर्भावितात्मनोः। पुत्राश्च पितरश्चैव परस्परमपूजयन्॥
en: Forsooth, what the gods did on that occasion is well known to you two. Sons and fathers had thus to adore each other.

sn: त्रीन् पिण्डान् न्यस्य पृथव्यां पूर्वं दत्त्वा कुशानिति। कथं तु पिण्डसंज्ञां ते पितरो लेभिरे पुरा॥
en: Having first spread some blades of Kusha grass, the gods and the departed manes placed three funeral cakes thereon and thus adored each other. I wish to know, however, the reason why the departed manes in days of yore acquired the name of Pindas.

sn: नरनारायणावूचतुः इमां हि धरणी पूर्वं नष्टां सागरमेखलाम्। गोविन्द उज्जहाराशु वारां रूपमास्थितः।१२।।
en: Nara and Narayana said The Earth, in days of yore, with her belt of seas, disappeared from the view. Govinda, taking the form of a gigantic boar, raised her up.

sn: सापयित्वा तु धरणी स्वे स्थाने पुरुषोत्तमः। जलकर्दमलिप्ताङ्गो लोककार्यार्थमुद्यतः॥
en: Having replaced the Earth in her former position, that foremost of Purushas, his body smeared with water and mud, began to do what was necessary for the world and its inhabitants.

sn: प्राप्ते चाह्निककाले तु मध्यदेशगते रवौ। दंष्ट्राविलग्नांस्त्रीन् पिण्डान् विधाय सहसा प्रभुः।१४॥ स्थापयामास वै पृथ्वयां कुशानास्तीर्य नारद। स तेष्वात्मानमुद्दिश्य पित्र्यं चक्रे यथाविधि॥
en: When the Sun reached the meridian, and the hour, therefore, came for saying the morning prayers, the powerful Lord, suddenly shaking off thrce balls of mud from his tusk, placed them upon the Earth, O Narada, having previously spread powerful Vishnu dedicated those balls of mud to his own self, according to the rites laid down in the eternal ordinance.

sn: संकल्पयित्वा त्रीन् पिण्डान् स्वेनैव विधिना प्रभुः। आत्मगात्रोष्मसम्भूतैः स्नेहगर्भस्तिलैरपि॥ प्रोक्ष्यापसव्यं देवेशः प्राङ्मुखः कृतवान् स्वयम्। मर्यादास्थापनार्थं च ततो वचनमुक्तवान्॥
en: Regarding the three balls of mud that the powerful Lord had shaken off from his tusks as funeral cakes, he then, with sesame seeds that arose from the heat of his own body, himself performed the rite of dedication, sitting with face turned towards the East. That foremost of gods then, moved by the desire of establishing rules of conduct for the inhabitants of the three worlds, said these words.

sn: वृषाकपिरुवाच अहं हि पितरः स्रष्टुमुद्यतो लोककृत् स्वयम्। यस्य चिन्तयतः सद्यः पितृकार्यविधीन् परान्॥
en: I am the Creator of the worlds. I ain determined to create those that are to be called departed manes.-Saying these words, he began to think of those high ordinances that should regulate the rites to be performed in honour of the departed manes.

sn: दंष्ट्राभ्यां प्रविनिर्धूता ममैते दक्षिणां दिशम्। आश्रिता धरणी पिण्डास्तस्मात् पितर एव ते॥
en: While thus doing, he beheld that the three balls of mud, shaken off his tusk, had fallen towards the South. He then said to himself,—These balls, shaken off my tusk, have fallen on the Earth towards the south of her surface! Led by this, I declare that these should be known henceforth by the name of departed manes.

sn: त्रयो मूर्तिविहीना वै पिण्डमूतिधरास्त्विमे। भवन्तु पितरो लोके मया सृष्टाः सनातनाः॥
en: Let these three that are of no particular shape, and that are only round, come to be considered as Pitris in the world! Thus do I create the eternal Pitris.

sn: पिता पितामहश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहः। अहमेवात्र विज्ञेयस्त्रिषु पिण्डेषु संस्थितः॥
en: I am the father, the grandfather and the great grandfather, and I should be considered as living in these three Pindas.

sn: नास्ति मत्तोऽधिः कश्चित् को वान्योऽयॊ मया स्वयम् को वा मम पिता लोके अहमेव पितामहः॥
en: There is no one that is superior to me. Who is there whom I myself may adore with rites? Who, again, is iny father in the universe? I myself am my grandfather.

sn: पितामहपिता चैव अहमेवात्र कारणम्। इत्येतदुक्त्वा वचनं देवदेवो वृषाकपिः॥ वराहपर्वते विप्र दत्त्वा पिण्डान् सविस्तरान्। आत्मानं पूजयित्वैव तत्रैवादर्शनं गतः॥
en: I am, indeed, the Grandfather and the father, I am the one cause! Having said these words, that God of gods, viz., He called Vrishakapi, offered those funeral cakes, O learned Brahmana, on the breast of the Varaha mountains, with elaborate rites. By those rites. He adored His own self, and having finished the adoration, disappeared there and then.

sn: एषा तस्य स्थितिविप्र पितरः पिण्डसंज्ञिताः। लभन्ते सततं पूजां वृषाकपिवचो यथा॥
en: Hence the Pitris are called Pinda. This is the root of the designation. According to the words given vent to by Vrishakapi at that time, the Pitris receive the worship offered by all.

sn: ये यजन्ति पितॄन् देवान् गुरूंश्चैवातिथींस्तथा। गाश्चैव द्विजमुख्यांश्च पृथिवीं मातरं यथा॥ कर्मणा मनसा वाचा विष्णुमेव यजन्ति ते! अन्तर्गतः स भगवान् सर्वसत्त्वशरीरगः॥
en: They who celebrate sacrifices in honour of and adore the departed manes, the gods, the preceptor or other reverend senior, guests arrived at the house, kine, superior Brahmanas, the goddess Earth, and their mothers, in thought, word, and deed, and said to adore and sacrifice to Vishnu himself. Entering the bodies of all existent creatures, the illustrious Lord is the Soul of all things.

sn: समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु ईश्वरः सुखदुःखयोः। महान् महात्मा सर्वात्मा नारायण इति श्रुतिः॥
en: Unaffected by happiness or misery, His attitude towards all is equal. Gifted with greatness, and of great soul, Narayana has been said to be the soul of all things in the universe.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वैतन्नारदो वाक्यं नरनारायणेरितम्। अत्यन्तं भक्तिमान् देवे एकान्तित्वमुपेयिवान्॥
en: Having heard these words of Nara and Narayana, the Rishi Narada became filled with devotion towards the Supreme Being. Indeed, with his whole soul he gave himself up to Narayana.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: प्रोष्य वर्षसहस्रं तु नरनारायणाश्रमे। श्रुत्वा भगवदाख्यानं दृष्ट्वा च हरिमव्ययम्॥ हिमवन्तं जगामाशु यत्रास्य स्वक आश्रमः।
en: Having lived for a full thousand years in the hermitage of Nara and Narayana, having seen the immutable Hari, and heard the excellent discourse having Narayana for its theme, the celestial Rishi went to his own hermitage on the breast of Himavat.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: तावपि ख्याततपसौ नरनारायणावृषी॥ तस्मिन्नेवाश्रमे रम्ये तेपतुस्तप उत्तमम्।
en: Those foremost of ascetics, viz., Nara and Narayana, however, continued to live in their charming hermitage of Vadari, practising the severest austerities.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: त्वमप्यमितविक्रान्तः पाण्डवानां कुलोद्वहः॥ पावितात्माद्य संवृत्तः श्रुत्वेमामादित: कथाम्।
en: You are born in the race of the Pandavas. You are of immeasurable energy. O perpetuator of the race of the Pandavas, having listened to this discourse on Narayana from the beginning, you have, in sooth been purged off of all your sins and your soul has been sanctified.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: नैव तस्यापरो लोको नायं पार्थिवसत्तम॥ कर्मणा मनसा वाचा यो द्विष्याद् विष्णुमव्ययम्।
en: Neither this world nor the next world is for him, O best of kings, who hates instead of loving and respecting the immutable Hari.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: मज्जन्ति पितरस्तस्य नरके शाश्वती: समा:॥ यो द्विष्याद् विबुधश्रेष्ठं देवं नारायणं हरिम्।
en: The ancestors of that person who hates Narayana, who is the foremost of gods, and is otherwise called Hari, sink into hell for good.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: कथं नाम भवेद् द्वेष्य आत्मा लोकस्य कस्यचित्॥ आत्मा हि पुरुषव्याघ्र ज्ञेयो विष्णुरिति स्थितिः।
en: O foremost of men, Vishnu is the soul of all beings. How, then can Vishnu be heated, for in hating him one would hate his own self.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: य एष गुरुरस्माकमृषिर्गन्धवतीसुतः॥ तस्माच्छ्रुतं मया चेदं कथितं च तवानघ॥
en: He who is our preceptor, viz., the Rishi Vyasa, the son of Gandhavati, has himself recited this narrative to us about the glory of Narayana, that glory which is the highest and which is immutable. I heard it from him and have recited it to you exactly as I heard it, O sinless one.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: नारदेन तु सम्प्राप्तः सरहस्य: संसग्रहः। एष धर्मो जगन्नाथात् साक्षान्नारायणानृप॥
en: This religion, with its mysteries and its abstract of details, was won by Narada, O king, from that Lord of the universe, viz., Narayana himself.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: एवमेष महान् धर्मः स ते पूर्वं नृपोत्तम। कथितो हरिगीतासु समासविधिकल्पितः॥
en: Even such are the particulars of this great religion. I have, before this, O foremost of kings, explained it to you in the Hari-Gita, with a brief reference to its ordinances.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: कृष्णद्वैपायनं व्यासं विद्धि नारायणं भुवि। को ह्यन्यः पुरुषव्याघ्र महाभारतकृद् भवेत्॥ धर्मान्नानाविधांश्चैव को ब्रूयात्तमृते प्रभुम्॥
en: Know that the Island-born Krishna, otherwise called Vyasa, is Narayana on Earth. Who else than he, O foremost of kings, could compile such a work as the Mahabharata? Who else than that powerful Rishi could describe the diverse kinds of duties and religion for the। observance and adoption of men.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: वर्ततां ते महायज्ञो यथा संकल्पितस्त्वया। संकल्पिताश्वमेधस्त्वं श्रुतधर्मश्च तत्त्वतः॥
en: You are bent upon celebrating a great sacrifice. Let that sacrifice of yours be celebrated! Having listened to the various kinds of duties and religions, let your Horsesacrifice go on.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: सौतिरुवाच एतत् तु महदाख्यानं श्रुत्वा पार्थिवसत्तमः। ततो यज्ञसमाप्यर्थं क्रियाः सर्वाः समारभत्॥
en: Sauti said Having heard this great discourse, that best of kings began all those rites that are laid down in the ordinance, for the completion of his great sacrifice.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: नारायणीयमाख्यानमेतत् ते कथितं मया। पृष्टेन शौनकाद्येह नैमिषारण्यवासिषु॥
en: Accosted by you, O Shaunaka, I have duly recounted to you and all these Rishis who inhabit the Naimisha forest, that great discourse having Narayana for theme.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: नारदेन पुरा राजन् गुरवे मे निवेदितम्। ऋषीणां पाण्डवानां च शृण्वतोः कृष्णभीष्मयो॥
en: Formerly Narada had recounted it to my preceptor before many Rishis and the son of Pandu and in the presence of Krishna and Bhishma also.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: स हि परमगुरुर्जनभुवनपतिः पृथुधरणिधरः श्रुतिविनयनिधिः। स्तव भवतु गतिर्हरिरमरहितः॥
en: The Supreme god Narayana is the Lord of all the foremost of Rishis, and of the three worlds. He is the upholder of Earth herself of huge proportions. He is the receptacle of the Shruti's and of the quality of humility. He is the great receptacle of all those ordinances that should be practised for acquiring tranquillity of heart, as also of all those who go by the name of Yama. He is always accompanied by the foremost of twice-born ones. Let that great god be your refuge.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: असुरवधकरस्तपसां निधिः। सुमहतां यशसां च भाजनम्। ऽभयदो मखभागहरोऽस्तु शरणं स ते॥
en: Hari ever does what is agreeable and beneficial to the dwellers of heaven. He is always the killer of such Asuras. He is the receptacle of penances. He is endued with great fame. He is the killer of the Daityas known by the name of Madhu and Kaitabha. He is the ordainer of the ends that are gained by persons acquainted with and observant of scriptural and other duties. He removes the fears of all persons. He takes the foremost of those offerings which are offered in sacrifices. He is your refuge and protection.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: त्रिगुणो विगुणश्चतुरात्मधरः पूर्तेश्योश्च फलभागहरः। विदधातु नित्यमजितोऽतिचलो गतिमात्मगां सुकृतिनामृषीणाम्।॥
en: He is endued with attributes. He is endued with four-fold form. He shares the merits originating from the dedication of tanks and the observance of similar religious rites. Undefeated and gifted with great power, it is He who always ordains the end, approachable by the Soul alone, of Rishis of pious deeds.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: तं लोकसाक्षिणमजं पुरुशं पुराणं रविवर्णमीश्वरं गतिं बहुशः। प्रणमध्वमेकमनसो यतः सलिलोद्भवोऽपि तमृषि प्रणतः॥
en: He is the witness of the worlds. He is unborn. He is the one ancient Purusha. Endued with solar complexion, He is the Supreme Lord, and He is the refuge of all. Do all of you bow your heads to Him since He who originated from the water (viz., Narayana himself) bends his head to Him.

description: The birth of Brihaspati; the descripton of the White Isand.
sn: स हि लोकयोनिरमृतस्य पदं सूक्ष्म परायणमचलं हि पदम्। तत्सांख्योगिभिरुदार वृतं बुद्ध्या यतात्मभिरिदं सनातनम्॥
en: He is the origin of the universe. He is that Being who is called Eternal. He is Minute. He is the refuge upon whom all things depend. He is the one Being who is immutable. The Sankhyas and Yogins, of controlled souls, hold him who is eternal in their understanding.

sn: शौनक उवाच श्रुतं भगवतस्तस्य माहात्म्यं परमात्मनः। जन्म धर्मगृहे चैव नरनारायणात्मकम्॥
en: Shaunaka said I heard from you the glory of the divine and Supreme Soul. I have heard also of the birth of Supreme God in the house of Dharma, in the form of Nara and Narayana.

sn: महावराहसृष्टा च पिण्डोत्पत्तिः पुरातनी। प्रवृत्तौ च निवृत्तौ च यो यथा परिकल्पितः॥
en: I have also heard from you the origin of the Pinda (funeral cake), from the mighty Boar. I have heard from you about those gods and Rishis that were ordained for the religion of Action and of those that were ordained for the Religion of Renunciation.

sn: तथा च नः श्रुतो ब्रह्मन् कथ्यमानस्त्वयानघ। हव्यकव्यभुजो विष्णुरुदक्पूर्वे महोदधौ॥ यच्च तत् कथितं पूर्वं त्वया हयशिरो महत्। तच्च दृष्टं भगवता ब्रह्मणा परमेष्ठिना॥
en: You have also, O twice-born one, described to us other topics. You have said also to us of that huge form, with the Divine head, of Vishnu, the eater of the libations and other offerings made in sacrifices,-the form, viz., cast. That form was seen by the illustrious Brahman, otherwise known by the name of Parameshthi.

sn: किं तदुत्पादितं पूर्वं हरिणा लोकधारिणा। रूपं प्रभावं महतामपूर्वं धीमतां वर॥
en: What, however, were the real features, and what the energy, the like of which among all great objects had never appeared before, of that form which Hari, the upholder of the universe, showed at that time.

sn: दृष्ट्वा हि विबुधश्रेष्ठमपूर्वममितौजसम्। तदश्वशिरसं पुण्यं ब्रह्मा किमकरोन्मुने॥
en: What did Brahman, do, 0 ascetic, after having beheld that foremost of gods, him whose like had never been witnessed before, him who was of incomparable energy, him who had the Equine head, and him who was Sacredness itself?

sn: एतन्नः संशयं ब्रह्मन् पुराणं ज्ञानसम्भवम्। कथयस्वोत्तममते महापुरुषनिर्मितम्॥ पाविताः स्म त्वया ब्रह्मन् पुण्यां कथयता कथाम्।
en: O twice-born one, this doubt has occurred to us with respect to this ancient subject of knowledge. O you of foremost intelligence, why did the Supreme Deity put on that form and show himself in it to Brahman? You have, forsooth, sanctified us by describing to us these various sacred topics.

sn: सौतिरुवाच कथयिष्यामि ते सर्वं पुराणं वेदसम्मितम्॥ जगौ यद् भगवान् व्यासो राज्ञः पारिक्षितस्य वै।
en: Sauti said I shall recount to you that ancient history, which is quite of a piece with the Vedas, and which the illustrious Vaishampayana recited to the son of Parikshit on the occasion of the great Snake-sacrifice.

sn: श्रुत्वाश्वशिरसो मूर्ति देवस्य हरिमेधसः॥ उत्पन्नसंशयो राजा एतदेवमचोदयत्।
en: Having heard the account of the great form of Vishnu, that had a horse-head, the royal son of Parikshit too had entertained the same doubt and put the same questions to Vaishampayana.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच यत्तद् दर्शितवान् ब्रह्मा देवं हयशिरोधरम्॥ किमर्थं तत् समभवत् तन्ममाचक्ष्व सत्तम।
en: Janamejaya said Tell me, O best of men, why did Hari appear in that powerful form, having a horsehead and which Brahman, the Creator, saw on the shores of the great northern Ocean on the occasion referred to by yourself?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच यत् किंचिदिह लोके वै देहसत्त्वं विशाम्पते॥ सर्वं पञ्चभिराविष्टं भूतैरीश्वरबुद्धिभिः।
en: Vaishampayana said All existent objects, O king, in this world, are the outcome of a combination of the five principal elements, a cornbination due to the intelligence of the Supreme Lord.

sn: ईश्वरो हि जगत्स्रष्टा प्रभुर्नारायणो विराट्॥ भूतान्तरात्मा वरदः सगुणो निर्गुणोऽपि च।
en: The powerful Narayana, endued with infinity, is the Supreme Lord and Creator of the universe. He is the inner Soul of all things, and the giver of boons. Shorn of qualities, he is again possessed of them.

sn: भूतप्रलयमत्यन्तं शृणुष्व नृपसत्तम॥ धरण्यामथ लीनायामप्सु चैकार्णवे पुरा।
en: Listen now, O best of kings, to me as I recount to you, how the Destruction of all things is encompassed. A first, the element of Earth becomes merged in Water and nothing then is seen except one vast expanse of Water on all sides.

sn: ज्योतिर्भूते जले चापि लीने ज्योतिषि चानिले॥ वायौ चाकाशसंलीने आकाशे च मनोऽनुगे।
en: Water then merges into Fire, and Fire into Wind. Wind then merges into Ether, and Ether, in its turn, merges into Mind.

sn: व्यक्ते मनसि संलीने व्यक्त चाव्यक्ततां गते।॥ अव्यक्ते पुरुषं याते पुंसि सर्वगतेऽपि च।
en: Mind merges into the Manifest. The Manifest merges into the Unmanifest (or Nature). The Unmanifest (or Nature) merges into Purusha (Soul) and Purusha merges into the Supreme Soul (or Brahma).

sn: तम एवाभवत् सर्वं न प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥ तमसो ब्रह्म सम्भूतं तमोमूलामृतात्मकम्।
en: Then Darkness covers the universe, and nothing can be seen. From that primal Darkness originates Brahma. Darkness is primeval and immortal.

sn: तद्विश्वभावसंज्ञान्तं पौरुषी तनुमाश्रितम्॥ सोऽनिरुद्ध इति प्रोक्तस्तत् प्रधानं प्रचक्षते।
en: Brahma that originates from primeval Darkness develops into the idea of the universe, and assumes the form of Purusha. Such Purusha is called Aniruddha. Shorn of sex, it is called otherwise by the name of Pradhana

sn: तदव्यक्तभिति ज्ञेयं त्रिगुणं नृपसत्तम॥ विद्यासहायवान्देवो विष्वक्सेनो हरिः प्रभुः।
en: That is also known by the name of Manifest, or the combination of the three qualities, O best of kings! He exists with Knowledge alone for his companion. That illustrious and powerful Being is otherwise called by the name of Vishvaksena or Hari.

sn: अप्स्वेव शयनं चक्रे निद्रायोगमुपागतः॥ जगतश्चिन्तयन् सृष्टिं चित्रां बहुगुणोद्भवाम्।
en: Entering into Yoga-sleep, he lays himself down on the waters. He then thinks of the Creation of the Universe of various phenomena and qualities.

sn: तस्य चिन्तयतः सृष्टिं महानात्मगुणः स्मृतः॥ अहंकारस्ततो जातो ब्रह्मा स तु चतुर्मुखः।
en: While engaged in thinking of Creation, he recollects his own great qualities. From this originates the four-faced Brahman representing the Consciousness of Aniruddha.

sn: हिरण्यगर्भो भगवान् सर्वलोकपितामहः॥ पद्येऽनिरुद्धात् सम्भूतस्तदा पद्मनिभेक्षणः।
en: The illustrious Brahman, otherwise called Hiranyagarbha, is the Grandfather of all the worlds. Having eyes like lotus petals, he takes birth within the Lotus that originates from (the navel of) Aniruddha.

sn: सहस्रपत्रे द्युतिमानुपविष्टः सनातनः॥ ददृशेऽद्भुतसंकाशो लोकानापोमयान् प्रभुः।
en: Seated on that Lotus, the illustrious, powerful, and eternal Brahman of wonderful form saw that the waters were on all sides.

sn: सत्त्वस्थः परमेष्ठी स ततो भूतगणान् सृजन्॥ पूर्वमेव च पद्मस्य पत्रे सूर्यांशुसप्रभे। नारायणकृतौ विन्दू अपामास्तां गुणोत्तरौ॥ तावपश्यत् स भगवाननादिनिधनोऽच्युतः।
en: Following the quality of Goodness, Brahman, otherwise called Parameshthi, then began to create the universe. In the primeval Lotus that was effulgent like the Sun, two drops of water had been grown by Narayana that were fraught with great merit. The illustrious Narayana, without beginning and without end, and above destruction, cast his eyes on those two drops of water,

sn: एकस्तत्राभवद् विन्दुर्मध्वाभो रुचिरप्रभः॥ स तामसो मधुर्जातस्तदा नारायणाज्ञया। कठिनस्त्वपरो विन्दुः कैटभो राजसस्तु स॥
en: One of those two drops of water, very beautiful and bright, looked like a drop of honey. From that drop originates, at the behest of Narayana, a Daitya of the name of Madhu made up of the quality of Ignorance. The other drop of water within the Lotus was very hard. From it originated the Daitya Kaitabha made up of the quality of Darkness.

sn: तावभ्यधावतां श्रेष्ठौ तमसा रजसान्वितौ। बलवन्तौ गदाहस्तौ पद्मनालानुसारिणौ॥
en: Endued thus with the qualities of Ignorance and Darkness, the two Daityas possessed of might and armed with maces, immediately after their birth, began to rove within that huge primeval Lotus.

sn: ददृशातेऽरविन्दस्थं ब्रह्माणममितप्रभम्। सृजन्तं प्रथमं वेदांश्चतुरस्चारुविग्रहान्॥
en: They saw within it Brahman of incomparable effulgence, engaged in creating the four Vedas, each gifted with the most charming form.

sn: ततो विग्रहवन्तौ तौ वेदान् दृष्ट्वासुरोत्तमौ। सहसा जगृहतुर्वेदान् ब्रह्मणः पश्यतस्तदा॥
en: Those two foremost of Asuras, having bodies, seeing the four Vedas, suddenly seized them in the very presence of their Creator.

sn: अथ तौ दानवश्रेष्ठौ वेदान् गृह्य सनातनान्। रसां विविशतुस्तूर्णमुदक्पूर्वे महोदधौ॥
en: Having seized the eternal Vedas, the two powerful Danavas, quickly dived into the ocean of waters which they saw and proceeded to its bottom.

sn: ततो हृतेषु वेदेषु ब्रह्मा कश्मलमाविशत्। ततो वचनमीशानं प्राह वेदैविनाकृतः॥
en: Seeing the Vedas forcibly taken away from him, Brahman became stricken with grief. Robbed of the Vedas thus, Brahman then addressed the Supreme Lord in these words.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच वेदा मे परमं चक्षुर्वेदा मे परमं बलम्। वेदा मे परमं धाम वेदा मे ब्रह्म चोत्तरम्॥
en: Brahman said The Vedas form my great eyes! The Vedas are my great strength! The Vedas are my great refuge! The Vedas are my high Brahma.

sn: मम वेदा हृताः सर्वे दानवाभ्यां बलादितः। अन्धकारा हि मे लोका जाता वेदैविनाकृताः॥
en: All the Vedas, however, have been by force taken away from me by the two Danavas! Deprived of the Vedas, the world I have created have become covered with darkness.

sn: वेदानृते हि कुर्यां लोकानां सृष्टिमुत्तमाम्। अहो बत महद् दुःखं वेदनाशनजं मम॥
en: Without the Vedas, how shall I succeed in starting my Creation? Alas, great is the grief I suffer for the loss of the Vedas.

sn: प्राप्तं दुनोति हृदयं तीव्र शोकपरायणम्। को हि शोकार्णवे मग्नं मामितोऽद्य समुद्धरेत्॥ वेदांस्तांश्चानयेन्नष्टान् कस्य चाहं प्रियो भवे।
en: My heart is aching. It has become the seat of a great sorrow. Who is there who will save me from this ocean of grief in which I am sunk for the loss I have suffered? Who is there who will bring me the Vedas I have lost? Who is there who will take mercy on me?

sn: इत्येवं भाषमाणस्य ब्रह्मणो नृपसत्तम॥ हरेः स्तोत्रार्थमुद्भूता बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतां वर। ततो जगौ परं जप्यं साञ्जलिप्रग्रहः प्रभुः॥
en: While Brahman was saying these words, O best of kings, the resolution suddenly arose in his mind, O foremost of intelligent persons, for singing the praises of Hari in these words. The powerful Brahman then, with hands joined in reverence, and seizing the feet of his progenitor, sang this highest of hymns in honour of Narayana.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच ॐनमस्ते ब्रह्महृदय नमस्ते मम पूर्वज। लोकाद्य भुवनश्रेष्ठ सांख्ययोगनिधे प्रभो॥ व्यक्ताव्यक्तकराचिन्त्य क्षेमं पन्थानमास्थित।
en: Brahman said I bow to you, O heart of Brahman! I bow to you who has been born before me! You are the origin of the universe! You are the foremost of all abodes. You, O powerful one, are the ocean of Yoga with all its branches. You are the Creator of both what is Manifest and what is Unmanifest! You travel the path of great auspiciousness!

sn: विश्वभुक् सर्वभूतानामन्तरात्मन्नयोनिज। अहं प्रसादजस्तुभ्यं लोकधाम स्वयम्भुवः॥ त्वत्तो मे मानसं जन्म प्रथमं द्विजपूजितम्। चाक्षुषं वै द्वितीयं मे जन्म चासीत् पुरातनम्॥
en: You are the consumer of the universe. You are the inner self of all creatures. You are without any origin. You are the refuge of the universe. You are self create, for you have no origin. As for myself, I have originated from your Cheerfulness. From you have I derived my birth. My first birth from you, which is considered sacred by all twice-born ones, was due to your will. My second birth in days of yore was from your eyes.

sn: त्वत्प्रसादात् तु मे जन्म तृतीयं वाचिकं महत्। त्वत्तः श्रवणनं चापि चतुर्थं जन्म मे विभो॥
en: Through your favour, my third birth was from your speech. My fourth birth, O powerful Lord, was from your ears.

sn: नासिक्यं चापि मे जन्म त्वत्तः परममुच्यते। अण्डजं चापि मे जन्म त्वत्तः षष्ठं विनिर्मितम्॥
en: My fifth birth, excellent in all ways, was from your nose, O Lord. My sixth birth was, through you, from an egg.

sn: इदं च सप्तमं जन्म पद्मजन्मेति वै प्रभो। सर्गे सर्गे ह्यहं पुत्रस्तव त्रिगुणवर्जित॥
en: This is my seventh birth. It has taken place, O Lord, within this Lotus. At each Creation I take birth from you as your son, O you who are shorn of the three qualities.

sn: प्रथितः पुण्डरीकाक्ष प्रधानगुणकल्पितः। त्वमीश्वरः स्वभावश्च स्वयम्भूः पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: Indeed, O lotus-eyed one, I take birth as your eldest son, made up of the foremost of three qualities, Sattva. You are endued with that nature which is Supreme. You originate from yourself.

sn: त्वया विनिर्मितोऽहं वै वेदचक्षुर्वयोतिगः। ते मे वेदा हताश्चक्षुरन्धो जातोऽस्मि जागृहि॥ ददस्व चढूंषि मम प्रियोऽहं ते प्रियोऽसि मे।
en: I have been created by you. The Vedas are my eyes. Hence, I am above Time. Those Vedas, which form my eyes, have been taken away from me. I have, therefore, become blind. Do you awake from this Yoga-sleep. Give me back my eye. I am dear to you and you are dear to me.

sn: एवं स्तुतः स भगवान् पुरुषः सर्वतोमुखः॥ जहौ निद्रामथ तदा वेदकार्यार्थमुद्यतः। ऐश्वर्येण प्रयोगेण द्वितीयां तनुमास्थितः॥
en: Thus landed by Brahman, the illustrious Purusha, with face turned towards every side, then renounced his sleep, resolved to recover the Vedas. Applying his Yoga-power, he put on a second form.

sn: सुनासिकेन कायेन भूत्वा चन्द्रप्रभस्तदा। कृत्वा हयशिरः शुभ्रं वेदानामालयं प्रभुः॥
en: His body, have an excellent nose, became as bright as the Moon. He assumed an equine head of great lustre, that head which was the abode of the Vedas.

sn: तस्य मूर्धा समभवद् द्यौः सनक्षत्रतारका। केशाश्चास्याभवन् दीर्घा रवेरंशुसमप्रभाः॥
en: The sky, with all its luminaries and constellations, became the crown of his head. His locks of hair were long and flowing, and had the sheen of the solar rays.

sn: कर्णावाकाशपाताले ललाटं भूतधारिणी। गङ्गा सरस्वती श्रोण्यौ भ्रुवावास्तां महोदधी॥
en: The regions above and below became his two ears. The Earth became his forehead. The two rivers Ganga and Sarasvati became his two eye-brows,

sn: चक्षुषी सोमसूर्यो ते नासा संध्या पुनः स्मृता। ॐकारस्त्वथ संस्कारो विद्युज्जिह्वा च निर्मिता॥
en: The Sun and the Moon became his two eyes. The twilight became his nose. The syllable OM became his memory and intelligence. The lightning became his tongue.

sn: दन्ताश्च पितरो राजन् सोमपा इति विश्रुताः। गोलोको ब्रह्मलोकश्च ओष्ठावास्तां महात्मनः॥ ग्रीवा चास्याभवद् राजन् कालरात्रिर्गुणोत्तरा।
en: The Soma-drinking departed manes became, it is said, his teeth. The two regions of happiness viz., Goloka and Brahmaloka, became his upper and lower lips. The dreadful night after universal destruction, and that is above the three qualities, became his neck.

sn: एतद्धयशिरः कृत्वा नानामूर्तिभिरावृतम्॥ अन्तर्दधौ स विश्वेशो विवेश च रसां प्रभुः।
en: Having put on this form endued with the equine head and having various things for its various limbs, the Lord of the universe disappeared then and there, and went to the nether regions. was

sn: रसां पुनः प्रविष्टश्च योगं परममास्थितः॥ शैक्ष्यं स्वरं समास्थाय उद्गीतं प्रासृजत् स्वरम्।
en: Having reached those regions he began Yoga. Adopting a voice governed by the rules of the science called Shiksha, he began to chant Vedic Mantras,

sn: स स्वरः सानुनादी च सर्वशः स्निग्ध एव च॥ बभूवान्तर्महीभूतः सर्वभूतगुणोदितः।
en: His pronunciation distinct and reverberated through the air, and was sweet the sound of his voice filled the nether region from end to end. Gifted with the properties of all elements it yielded great benefits.

sn: ततस्तावसुरौ कृत्वा वेदान् समयबन्धनान्।५६॥ रसातले विनिक्षिप्य यतः शब्दस्ततो दुतौ।
en: The two Asuras, making a compact with the Vedas about the time when they would return to take them up again, threw them down in the nether region, and ran towards the spot hence those sounds seemed to come.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राजन् देवो हयशिरोधरः॥ जग्राह वेदानखिलान् रसातलगतान् हरिः।
en: Meanwhile, O king, the Supreme Lord with the equine head, otherwise called Hari, who was himself in the nether region, took up all the Vedas.

sn: प्रादाच्च ब्रह्मणे भूयस्ततः स्वां प्रकृतिं गतः॥ स्थापयित्वा हयशिर उदक्पूर्वे महोदधौ। वेदानामालयं चापि बभूवाश्वशिरास्ततः॥
en: Returning to where Brahman was living, he gave the Vedas to him. Having restored the Vedas to Brahman, the Supreme Lord once more returned to his own nature. The Supreme Lord also established his form with the horsehead in the north-eastern region of the great ocean. Having established him who was the abode of the Vedas, he once more became the horse-headed from that he was.

sn: अथ किंचिदपश्यन्तौ दानवौ मधुकैटभौ। पुनराजग्मतुस्तत्र वेगितौ पश्यतां च तौ॥ यत्र वेदा विनिक्षिप्तास्तत् स्थानं शून्यमेव च।
en: The two Danavas Madhu and Kaitabha, not finding the person from whom those sounds came, speedily returned there. They cast their eyes around but saw that the spot on which they had thrown the Vedas was vacant.

sn: तत उत्तममास्थाय वेगं बलवतां वरौ॥ पुनरुत्तस्थतुः शीघ्रं रसानामालयात् तदा।
en: Proceeding quickly those two foremost of powerful Beings, rose from the nether region.

sn: ददृशाते च पुरुषं तमेवादिकरं प्रभुम्॥ श्वेतं चन्द्रविशुद्धाभमनिरुद्धतनौ स्थितम्।
en: Returning to where the primeval Lotus was that had given them birth, they saw the powerful Being, the original Creator, living in the form of Aniruddha of fair complexion and endued with a moon-like splendour.

sn: भूयोऽप्यमितविक्रान्तं निद्रायोगमुपागतम्॥ आत्मप्रमाणरचिते अपामुपरि कल्पिते।
en: Of immeasurable prowess, he was under Yoga-sleep, his body stretched on the waters and occupying a space as vast as itself.

sn: शयने नागभोगाढ्ये ज्वालामालासपावृते॥ निष्कल्मषेण सत्त्वेन सम्पन्नं रुचिरप्रभम्।
