en: Highly effulgent and endued with the pure quality of Goodness, the body of the Supreme Lord lay on the excellent hood of a snake that seemed to throw out flames of fire for the resplendence attaching to it.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा दानवेन्द्रौ तौ महाहासममुञ्चताम्॥ उचतुश्च समाविष्टौ रजसा तमसा च तौ। अयं स पुरुषः श्वेतः शेते निद्रामुपागतः॥ अनेन नूनं वेदानां कृतमाहरणं रसात्।
en: Seeing the Lord thus lying, the two foremost of Danavas roared out a loud laugh. Having the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance, they said. This is that Being of white complexion. He is no lying asleep. Forsooth, this one has brought the Vedas away from the nether region.

sn: कस्यैष को नु खल्वेष किं न स्वपिति भोगवान्॥ इत्युच्चारितवाक्यौ तौ बोधयामासतुर्हरिम्।
en: Whose is he? Who is he? Why is he thus asleep on the hood of a snake? Saying these words, the two Danavas awakened Hari from his Yoga-sleep.

sn: युद्धार्थिनौ हि विज्ञाय विबुद्धः पुरुषोत्तमः॥ निरीक्ष्य चासुरेन्द्रौ तौ ततो युद्धे मनो दधे।
en: The foremost of Beings, (viz., Narayana), thus awakened understood that the two Danavas intended to fight with him. Seeing the two foremost of Asuras prepared to battle with him, he also wished to satisfy that desire of theirs.

sn: अथ युद्धं समभवत् तयोर्नारायणस्य वै॥ रजस्तमोविष्टतनू तावुभौ मधुकैटभौ। ब्रह्मणोपचितिं कुर्वन् जघान मधुसूदनः॥
en: Thereupon an encounter took place between those two and Narayana. The Asuras Madhu and Kaitabha were embodiments of the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance. Narayana killed them both for pleasing Brahman. He thence passed by the name of Madhusudana (slayer of Madhu).

sn: ततस्तयोर्वधेनाशु वेदापहरणेन च। शोकापनयनं चक्रे ब्रह्मणः पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: Having brought about the destruction of the two Asuras and restored the Vedas to Brahman, the Supreme Being removed the sorrow of Brahman.

sn: ततः परिवृतो ब्रह्मा हरिणा वेदसत्कृतः। निर्ममे स तदा लोकान् कृत्स्नान् स्थावरजङ्गमान्॥
en: Helped then by Hari and assisted by the Vedas, Brahman created all worlds with their mobile and immobile creatures.

sn: दत्त्वा पितामहाया यां मतिं लोकविसर्गिकीम्। तत्रैवान्तर्दधे देवो यत एवागतो हरिः॥
en: After this, Hari, giving to the Grandfather intelligence of the foremost order regarding the Creation, disappeared there and then for going to the place he had come from.

sn: तौ दानवौ हरिहत्वा कृत्वा हयशिरस्तनुम्। पुनः प्रवृत्तिधर्मार्थं तामेव विदधे तनुम्॥
en: It was thus that Narayana, having assumed the form equipped with the horse-head, killed the two Danavas Madhu and Kaitabha. Once more, however, he assumed the same form for making the Religion of Action to prevent the universe.

sn: एवमेव महाभागो बभूवाश्वशिरा हरिः। पौराणमेतत् प्रख्यातं रूपं वरदमैश्वरम्॥
en: Thus did the blessed Hari assume in days of yore that grand form having the horse-head. This, of all his forms, endued with power, is celebrated as the most ancient.

sn: यो ह्येतद् ब्राह्मणो नित्यं शृणुयाद् धारयेत वा। न तस्याध्ययनं नाशमुपगच्छेत् कदाचन॥
en: That person who frequently listens or mentally recites this history of the assumption by Narayana of the form with the horse-head, will never forget his Vedic or other learning.

sn: आराध्य तपसोग्रेण देवं हयशिरोधरम्। पाञ्चालेन क्रमः प्राप्तो देवेन पथि देशिते॥
en: Having worshipped with the austerest penances the illustrious god with the horsehead, the Rishi Panchala acquired the science of Karma by going along the path pointed out by the god (Rudra).

sn: एतद्धयशिरो राजन्नाख्यानं तव कीर्तितम्। पुराणं वेदसमितं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: I have thus recounted to you, O king, the old story of Hayashiras, agreeable to the Vedas, about which you had asked me.

sn: यां यामिच्छेत् तनुं देवः कर्तुं कार्यविधौ क्वचित्। तां तां कुर्याद् विकुर्वाणः स्वयमात्मानमात्मना।॥
en: Whatever forms the Supreme Deity wishes to assume with a view to the governing of the affairs of the universe, he assumes immediately by his own inherent powers.

sn: एष वेदनिधिः श्रीमानेष वै तपसो निधिः। एष योगश्च सांख्यं च ब्रह्म चाग्र्यं हविर्विभुः॥
en: The Supreme God, endued with every prosperity, is the receptacle of the Vedas. He is the receptacle of Penances also. The powerful Hari is Yoga. He is the embodiment of the Sankhya philosophy. He is that foremost Brahma of which we hear.

sn: नारायणपरा वेदा यज्ञा नारायणात्मकाः। तपो नारायणपरं नारायणपरा गतिः॥
en: The Vedas are the soul of Narayana, all sacrifices are the form of Narayana, Penances are Narayana and the highest end is also Narayana.

sn: नारायणपरं सत्यमृतं नारायणात्मकम्। नारायणपरो धर्मः पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभः॥
en: Truth has Narayana for its refuge. Rita has Narayana for its soul. The Religion of Renunciation in which there is no return, had Narayana for its high region.

sn: प्रवृत्तिलक्षणश्चैव धर्मो नारायणात्मकः। नारायणात्मको गन्धो भूमौ श्रेष्ठतमः स्मृतः॥
en: The other Religion which has Action for its root, has equally Narayana for its Soul. The foremost of all the qualities that belong to the element of Earth is scent. Scent has Narayana for its soul.

sn: अपां चापि गुणा राजन् रसा नारायणात्मकाः। ज्योतिषां च परं रूपं स्मृतं नारायणात्मकम्॥
en: The properties of Water, O king, are called the Tastes. These Tastes have Narayana for their soul. The foremost property of Fire is form. Form also has Narayana for its soul.

sn: नारायणात्मकश्चापि स्पर्शो वायुगुणः स्मृतः। नारायणात्मकश्चैव शब्द आकाशसम्भवः॥
en: Touch, which is the property of Wind, is also said to have Narayana for its soul. Sound, which is a property of Air, has, like the others, Narayana for its soul.

sn: मनश्चापि ततो भूतमव्यक्तगुणलक्षणम्। नारायणपरः कालो ज्योतिषामयनं च यत्॥
en: Mind also, which is the property of Nature, has Narayana for its soul. Time which is measured by the motion to the celestial luminaries has similarly Narayana for its soul.

sn: नारायणपरा कीर्तिः श्रीश्च लक्ष्मीश्च देवताः। नारायणपरं सांख्यं योगो नारायणात्मकः॥
en: The presiding gods of Fame, of Beauty, and of Prosperity, have the same Supreme Deity for their soul. Both the Sankhya philosophy and Yoga have Narayana for their soul.

sn: कारणं पुरुषो ह्येषां प्रधानं चापि कारणम्। स्वभावश्चैव कर्माणि दैवं येषां च कारणम्॥
en: The Supreme Being is the cause of all this, as Soul. He is, again, the cause of everything, as Nature.

sn: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम्। विविधा च तथा चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम्॥
en: He is the basis on which all things depend. He is the doer or agent, and He is the cause of that variety in the universe. He is the various kinds of power which act in the universe. Fifthly, he is that all controlling unseen power of which people speak.

sn: पञ्चकारणसंख्यातो निष्ठा सर्वत्र वै हरिः। तत्त्वं जिज्ञासमानानां हेतुभिः सर्वतोमुखैः॥
en: Those engaged in investigating the several subjects of enquiry with the help of such reasons as are of wide application, consider Hari to be at one with the five reasons referred to above and as the final refuge of all things.

sn: तत्त्वमेको महायोगी हरिर्नारायणः प्रभुः। ब्रह्मादीनां स लोकानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्॥ सांख्यानां योगिनां चापि यतीनामात्मवेदिनाम्। मनीषितं विजानाति केशवो न तु तस्य ते॥
en: Indeed, the powerful Narayana, endued with the highest Yoga-power, is the one subject of (enquiry). Keshava perfectly knows the thoughts of men including Brahman and the great Rishis, of those that are Sankhyas and Yogins, of those that are Yatis, and of those, generally, that are conversant with the Soul, but none of these can know what his thoughts are.

sn: ये केचित् सर्वलोकेषु दैवं पित्र्यं च कुर्वते। दानानि च प्रयच्छन्ति तप्यन्ते च तपो महत्॥ सर्वेषामाश्रयो विष्णुरैश्वरं विधिमास्थितः। सर्वभूतकृतावसो वासुदेवेति चोच्यते॥
en: Whatever acts are performed in honour of the gods or the departed manes, whatever gifts are made, whatever penances are performed, have Vishnu for their refuge,-Vishnu who is established upon his own supreme ordinances. He is named Vasudeva because of his being the adobe of all creatures.

sn: महाविभूतिर्गुणवर्जिताख्यः। गुणैश्च संयोगमुपैति शीघ्र कालो यथर्तावृतुसम्प्रयुक्तः॥
en: He is immutable. He is Supreme. He is the. foremost of Rishis. He is endued with the highest power. He is said to be above the three qualities. As Time assumes marks when it manifests itself in the form of successive seasons, so He, though really shorn of qualities, assumes qualities (for manifesting Himself).

sn: नैवास्य विन्दन्ति गतिं महात्मनो न चागतिं कश्चिदिहानुपश्यति। ज्ञानात्मका: सन्ति हि ये महर्षयः पश्यन्ति नित्यं पुरुषं गुणाधिकम्॥
en: Even the high-souled do not succeed in understanding his motions. Only those foremost of Rishis who have knowledge for their Souls, succeed in seeing in their hearts that Purusha who is above all qualities,

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: जनमेजय उवाच अहो होकन्तिनः सर्वान् प्रीणाति भगवान् हरिः। विधिप्रयुक्तां पूजां च गृह्णाति भगवान् स्वयम्।।।।
en: Janamejaya said The illustrious Hari becomes favourite to them who are whole-mindedly devoted to him. He accepts also all adoration that is offered to Him according to the ordinance.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: ये तु दग्धेन्धना लोके पुण्यपापविवर्जिताः। तेषां त्वयाभिनिर्दिष्टा पारम्पर्यागता गतिः॥
en: Of those persons who have freed themselves from desire, and that are shorn of both merit and demerit, you have spoken of the Knowledge they attain, as handed down from preceptor to preceptor, as the end they acquire.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: चतुर्थ्यां चैव ते गत्यां गच्छन्ति पुरुषोत्तमम्। एकान्तिनस्तु पुरुषा गच्छन्ति परमं पदम्॥
en: Such persons always acquire that end which is the fourth, viz., the essence of the foremost of Purushas or Vasudeva,-through the three others. Those persons, however, who are devoted to Narayana with their whole minds at once acquire the highest end.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: नूनमेकान्तधर्मोऽयं श्रेष्ठो नारायणप्रियः। अगत्वा गतयस्तिस्रो यद् गच्छत्यव्ययं हरिम्॥
en: Forsooth, the Religion of Devotion is superior (to that of Knowledge) and is very dear to Narayana. These, without passing through the three successive stages at once attain to the immutable Hari.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: सहोपनिषदान् वेदान् ये विप्राः सम्यगास्थिताः। पठन्ति विधिमास्थाय ये चापि यतिधर्मिणः॥ तेभ्यो विशिष्टां जानामि गतिमेकान्तिनां नृणाम्। केनैष धर्मः कथितो देवेन ऋषिणापि वा॥
en: The end that is attained by Brahmanas, who, practising due observances, study the Vedas with the Upanishads according to the rules laid down for such study, and by those who follow the Religion of Yatis, is inferior, I think, to that attained by persons devoted whole-mindedly to Hari, Who first promulgated this Religion of Devotion? Was it some god or some Rishi who declared it.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: एकान्तिनां च का चर्या कदा चोत्पादिताविभो। एतन्मे संशयं छिन्धि परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: What are the practices of those practices begin? I have doubts on those subjects. Do you dispell them. Great is my curiosity to her you explain the several points.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच समुपोढेष्वनीकेषु कुरुपाण्डवयोर्मधे। अर्जुने विमनस्के च गीता भगवता स्वयम्॥ अगतिश्च गतिश्चैव पूर्वं ते कथिता मया। गहनो ह्येष धर्मो वै दुर्विज्ञेयोऽकृतात्मभिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said, "When the diverse detachments of the Pandava and the Kuru armies were drawn up in battle array and when Arjuna became dispirited, the holy one himself explained the question of what is the end and what is not the end attained by persons of different characters. I have before this recited to you the words of the holy one. It is difficult to understand the religion preached by the holy one on that occasion. Men of impure souls cannot apprehend it at all.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: सम्मितः समावेदेन पुरैवादियुगे कृतः। धार्यते स्वयमीशेन राजन् नारायणेन च॥
en: Having created this religion in days of yore, viz., in the golden age, in perfect accordance with the Samans, it is borne, O king, by the Supreme Lord, viz., Narayana, himself.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: एतदर्थं महाराज पृष्टः पार्थेन नारदः। ऋषिमध्ये महाभागः शृण्वतोः कृष्णभीष्मयोः॥
en: This very subject was ushered by the highly blessed Partha to Narada in the midst of the Rishis and in the presence of Krishna and Bhishma.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: गुरुणा च मयाप्येष कथितो नृपसत्तम। यथा तत् कथितं तत्र नारदेन तथा शृणु॥
en: My preceptor, viz., the Island-born Krishna heard what Narada said. Receiving it from the celestial Rishis, O best of kings, my preceptor gave it to me in exactly the same way in which he had got it from the celestial Rishi. I shall now recount it to you, O king, in the same way as it has been received from Naradas. Listen, therefore, to me.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: यदासीन्मानसं जन्म नारायणमुखोद्गतम्। ब्रह्मणः पृथिवीपाल तदा नारायणः स्वयम्॥ तेन धर्मेण कृतवान् दैवं पित्र्यं च भारत। फेनपा ऋषयश्चैव तं धर्म प्रतिपेदिरे॥
en: In that cycle when the Creator Brahman, O king, took his birth in the mind of Narayana and came out from the latter's mouth, Narayana himself, performed, O Bharata, his divine and ancestral rites in accordance with this religion. Those Rishis who live upon the froth of water then got it from Narayana.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: वैखानसाः फेनपेभ्यो धर्मं तं प्रतिपेदिरे। वैखानसेभ्यः सोमस्तु ततः सोऽन्तर्दधे पुनः॥
en: From the froth-eating Rishis, this religion was gained by the Rishis, named Vaikhanasas. From the Vaikhanasas Soma got it. Afterwards, it disappeared from the universe.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: यदासीच्चाक्षुषं जन्म द्वितीयं ब्रह्मणो नृप। तदा पितामहेनैव सोमाद् धर्मः परिश्रुतः॥
en: After the second birth of Brahman, viz., when he originated from the eyes of Narayana, O king, the Grandfather (that is, Brahman) then received this religion from Soma.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: नारायणात्मको राजन् रुद्राय प्रददौ च तम्। ततो योगस्थितो रुद्रः पुरा कृतयुगे नृप।॥ बालखिल्यानृषीन् सर्वान् धर्ममेतदपाठयत्। अन्तर्दधे ततो भूयस्तस्य देवस्य मायया॥
en: Having received it thus, Brahman gave this religion, which has Narayana for its soul, to Rudra. In the golden age of that ancient Kalpa, Rudra, devoted to Yoga, 0 king, communicated it to all those Rishis called Valkhilyas. Through the illusion of Narayana, it once more disappeared from the universe.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: तृतीयं ब्रह्मणो जन्म यदासीद् वाचिकं महत्। तत्रैष धर्मः सम्भूतः स्वयं नारायणानृप॥
en: In the third birth of Brahman which was from the speech of Narayana, this religion once more sprang up, O king, from Narayana himself.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: सुपर्णो नाम तमृषिः प्राप्तवान् पुरुषोत्तमात्। तपसा वै सुतप्तेन दमेन नियमेन च।॥
en: Then a Rishi named Suparna acquired it from that foremost of Beings.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: त्रिः परिक्रान्तवानेतत् सुपर्णो धर्ममुत्तमम्। यस्मात् तस्माद् व्रतं ह्येतत् त्रिसौपर्णमिहोच्यते॥
en: The Rishi Suparna used to recite this excellent religion, three times during the day. Therefore it passed by the name of Trisauparna in the world.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: ऋग्वेदपाठपठितं व्रतमेतद्धि दुश्चरम्। सुपर्णाच्चाप्यधिगतो धर्म एष सनातनः॥ वायुना द्विपदां श्रेष्ठ कथितो जगदायुषा। वायोः सकाशात् प्राप्तश्च ऋषिभिर्विघसाशिभिः॥
en: This religion has been referred to in the Rigveda. The duties it enjoins are extremely difficult of observance. From the Rishi Suparna, this eternal religion was acquired, O foremost of men, by the wind god, that sustainer of the lives of all creatures in the universe. The god of wind communicated it to such Rishis as live upon the remnants of sacrificial offerings after feeding guests and others.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: ततो महोदधिश्चैव प्राप्तवान् धर्ममुत्तमम्। अन्तर्दधे ततो भूयो नारायणसमाहितः॥
en: From those Rishis this excellent religion was acquired by the great Ocean. It once more disappeared from the universe and became merged into Narayana.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: यदा भूयः श्रवणजा सृष्टिरासीन्महात्मनः। ब्रह्मणः पुरुषव्याघ्र तत्र कीर्तयतः शृणु॥
en: In the next birth of the great Brahman when he originated from the ear of Narayana, listen, O king, to what took place in that aeon.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: जगत्स्रष्टुमना देवो हरिनारायणः स्वयम्। चिन्तयामास पुरुषं जगत्सर्गकरं प्रभुम्॥
en: The illustrious Narayana, otherwise called Hari, when he was bent upon Creation, thought of a Being who would be powerful enough to create the universe.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: अथ चिन्तयतस्तस्य कर्णाभ्यां पुरुषः स्मृतः। प्रजासर्गकरो ब्रह्मा तमुवाच जगत्पतिः॥
en: While thinking of this, a Being originated from his ears capable to create the universe. The Lord of all called him by the name of Brahman..

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: सृज प्रजाः पुत्र सर्वा मुखतः पादतस्तथा। श्रेयस्तव विधास्यामि बलं तेजश्च सुव्रत॥
en: Addressing Brahman, the Supreme Narayana said,—Do you, O son, create all kinds of creatures from your mouth and feet. O you of excellent vows, I shall do what will be good for you, for I shall impart to you both energy and strength sufficient to make you competent for this work.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: धर्मं च मत्तो गृह्णीष्व सात्वतं नाम नामतः। तेन सृष्टं कृतयुगं स्थापयस्व यथाविधि॥
en: Do you receive also from me this excellent religion known by the name of Satvata. Helped by that religion do you create the golden age and ordain it duly.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: ततो ब्रह्मा नमश्चक्रे देवाय हरिमेधसे। धर्मं चाम्यं स जग्राह सरहस्यं ससंग्रहम्॥ आरण्यकेन सहितं नारायणमुखोद्भवम्। उपदिश्य ततो धर्मं ब्रह्मणेऽमिततेजसे॥ त्वं कर्ता युगधर्माणां निराशी:कर्मसंज्ञितम्। जगाम तमसः पारं यत्राव्यक्तं व्यवस्थितम्॥
en: Thus addressed, Brahman bowed his head to the illustrious Harimedhas and received from him that foremost of all religions with all its mysteries and abstract of details, together with the Aranyakas,-the religion which originated from the mouth of Narayana. Narayana then instructed Brahman of incomparable energy in that religion, and addressing him, said,-You are the creator of the duties that are to be observed in the respective cycles! Having said. this to Brahman, Narayana disappeared and went to that place which is beyond the reach of Ignorance, where the unmanifest resides, and which is known by the name of acts without desire of fruits.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: ततोऽथ वरदो देवो ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः। असृजत् स ततो लोकान् कृत्स्नान् स्थावरजङ्गमान्॥
en: After this, the boon-giving Brahman, the Grandfather of the worlds, created the different worlds with all their mobile and immobile creatures.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: ततः प्रावर्तत तदा आदौ कृतयुगं शुभम्। ततो हि सात्वतो धर्मो व्याप्य लोकानवस्थितः॥
en: The age that first began was highly auspicious and came to be called by the name of Krita. In that age, the religion of Sattva existed, in the entire universe.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: तेनैवाद्येन धर्मेण ब्रह्मा लोकविसर्गकृत्। पूजयामास देवेशं हरि नारायणं प्रभुम्॥
en: With the help of that primeval religion of virtue, Brahman, the Creator of all the worlds, adored the Lord of all the gods, viz., the powerful Narayana otherwise called Hari.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: धर्मप्रतिष्ठाहेतोश्च मनुं स्वारोचिषं ततः। अध्यापयामास तदा लोकानां हितकाम्यया॥
en: For the propagation then of that religion and desirous of benefiting the worlds, Brahman then instructed that Manu who is known by the name of Swarochish in that religion.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: ततः स्वरोचिवः पुत्रं स्वयं शङ्खपदं नृप। अध्यापगत् पुराव्यग्रः सर्वलोकपतिर्विभुः॥
en: Svarochish-Manu, that Lord of all the worlds, that foremost of all persons gifted with power, then cheerfully gave the knowledge of that religion to his own son, O king, who was known by the name of Shankhapada.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: ततः शङ्खपदश्चापि पुत्रमात्मजमौरसम्। दिशां पालं सुवर्णाभमध्यापयत भारत। सोऽन्तर्दधे ततो भूयः प्राप्ते त्रेतायुगे पुनः॥
en: The son of Manu, viz., Shankhapada, imparted the knowledge of that religion to his own son Suvarnabha who was the Regent of the cardinal and subsidiary points. When, upon the expiration of the Krita Yoga, the Treta came, that religion once more disappeared from the world.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: नासिक्ये जन्मनि पुरा ब्रह्मणः पार्थिवोत्तम। धर्ममतं स्वयं देवो हरिर्नारायणः प्रभुः॥ तज्जगादारविन्दाक्षो ब्रह्मणः पश्यतस्तदा। सनत्कुमारो भगवांस्तत: प्राधीतवान् नृप॥
en: In a subsequent birth of Brahman, O best of kings, viz., that which was derived from the nose of Narayana, O Bharata, the illustrious and powerful Narayana or Hari having eyes like lotus petals, himself sang this religion in the presence of Brahman. Then the son of Brahman, created by his will, viz., Sanatkumara, studied this religion.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: सनत्कुमारादपि च वीरणो वै प्रजापतिः। कृतादौ कुरुशार्दूल धर्ममेतदधीतवान्॥
en: From Santakumara, the Prajapati Virana, in the beginning of the Krita age, O foremost of Kurus, obtained this religion.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: वीरणचाप्यधीत्यैनं रैभ्याय मुनये ददौ। रैभ्यः पुत्राय शुद्धाय सुव्रताय सुमेधसे॥ कुक्षिनाम्ने स प्रददौ दिशां पालाय धर्मिणे। ततोऽप्यन्तर्दधे भूयो नारायणमुखोद्भवः॥
en: Having studied it in this way, Virana taught it to the ascetic Raivya. Raivya, in his turn, gave it to his son of pure soul, good vows, and great intelligence viz., Kukshi, that righteous Regent to the cardinal and subsidiary points. After this, that religion born of the mouth of Narayana, once more disappeared from the world.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: अण्डजे जन्मनि पुनर्ब्रह्मणे हरियोनये। एष धर्मः समुद्भूतो नारायणमुखात् पुनः॥
en: In the next birth of Brahman, viz., that which he derived from an egg which originated from Hari, this religion once more issued from the mouth of Narayana.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: गृहीतो ब्रह्मणा राजन् प्रयुक्तश्च यथाविधि। अध्यापिताश्च मुनयो नाम्ना बर्हिषदो नृप॥
en: It was received by Brahman, O king, and practised duly in all its details by him. Brahman then gave it, O king, to those Rishis who are known by the name of Varhishada.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: बर्हिषद्भ्यश्च सम्प्राप्तः सामवेदान्तगं द्विजम्। ज्येष्ठं नामाभिविख्यातं ज्येष्ठसामव्रतो हरिः॥
en: From the Barhishadas it was acquired by a Brahmana well-versed in the Sama-Veda, and known by the name of Jeshthya. And because he was well-versed in the Samans, therefore was he known also by the name of Jeshthyasamavrata-Hari.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: ज्येष्ठाच्चाप्यनुसंक्रान्तो राजानमविकम्पनम्। अन्तर्दधे ततो राजन्नेष धर्मः प्रभो हरेः॥
en: From the Brahmana known by the name of Jeshthya, this religion was obtained by a king of the name of Avikampana. After this, that religion, derived from the powerful Hari, once more disappeared from the world.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: यदिदं सप्तमं जन्म पद्मजं ब्रह्मणो नृप। तत्रैव धर्मः कथितः स्वयं नारायणेन ह॥ पितामहाय शुद्धाय युगादौ लोकधारिणे। पितामहश्च दक्षाय धर्ममेतं पुरा ददौ॥
en: During the seventh birth of Brahman from the lotus, O king, that sprang from the navel of Narayana, this religion was once more preached by Narayana himself, to the Grandsire of pure soul, the Creator of all the worlds, in the beginning of this Kalpa. The Grandfather gave it in days of yore to Daksha.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: ततो ज्येष्ठे तु दौहित्रे प्रादाद् दक्षो नृपोत्तम। आदित्ये सवितुर्येष्ठे विवस्थाजगृहे ततः॥
en: Daksha, in his turn, gave it to the eldest of all the sons of his daughters, O monarch, viz., Aditya, who is senior in age to Savitri. From Aditya, Vivasvat got it.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: त्रेतायुगादौ च ततो विवस्वान् मनवे ददौ। मनुश्च लोकभूत्यर्थं सुतायेक्ष्वाकवे ददौ॥
en: In the beginning of the Treta Yuga, Vivasvat gave the knowledge of this religion to Manu. Manu, for the protection and support of all the worlds, then gave it to his son Ikshvaku.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: इक्ष्वाकुणा च कथितो व्याप्य लोकानवस्थितः। गमिष्यति क्षयान्त च पुनर्नारायणं नृप॥
en: Promulgated by Ikshvaku, that religion overspreads the whole world. When the universal destruction sets in, it will once more return to Narayana and be merged in Him.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: यतीनां चापि यो धर्मः स ते पूर्वं नृपोत्तमा कथितो हरिगीतासु समासविधिकल्पितः॥
en: The religion which is followed and practised by the Yatis, has, O best of kings, been described to you before this in the Harigita, with all its ordinances in brief.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: नारदेन सुसम्प्राप्तः सरहस्यः ससंग्रहः। एष धर्मो जगन्नाथात् साक्षान्नारायणान्नृप॥
en: The celestial Rishi Narada got it from that Lord of universe, viz., Narayana himself, O king, with all its mysteries and abstract of details.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: एवमेष महान् धर्म आद्यो राजन् सनातनः। दुर्विज्ञेयो दुष्करश्च सात्वतैर्धार्यते सदा॥
en: Thus, O king, this foremost of religions is primeval and eternal. Incapable of being understood easily and highly difficult of being pervaded by the quality of godness.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: धर्मज्ञानेन चैतेन सुप्रयुक्तेन कर्मणा। अहिंसाधर्मयुक्तेन प्रीयते हरिरीश्वरः॥
en: It is by means of acts that are wellperformed and done with a perfect knowledge of duties,-acts, that is, in which there is nothing of injury to any creature,-that Hari the Supreme Lord became pleased.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: एकव्यूहविभागो वा क्वचिद् द्विर्गृहसंज्ञितः। त्रियूँहश्चापि संख्यातश्चतुर्दूहश्च दृश्यते॥
en: Some persons worship Narayana as endued with only one form, viz., that O Aniruddha. Some worship Him as endued with two forms, viz., that of Aniruddha and Pradyumna. Some adore Him as having three forms, viz., Aniruddha, Pradyumna and Sankarshana. A fourth section adore him as having four forms, viz., Aniruddha, Pradyumna, Shankarshana, and Vasudeva.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: हरिरेव हि क्षेत्रज्ञो निर्ममो निष्कलस्तथा। जीवश्च सर्वभूतेषु पञ्चभूतगुणातिगः॥
en: Hari is Himself the Kshetrajna (Soul). He is without parts. He is the Individual Soul in all creatures, getting over the five primal elements.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: मनश्च प्रथितं राजन् पञ्चेन्द्रियसमीरणम्। एष लोकविधिधीमानेष लोकविसर्गकृत्॥
en: He is the Mind, O king, that directs and governs the five senses. Gifted with the highest intelligence, He is the Ordainer of the universe, and the Creator thereof.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: अकर्ता चैव कर्ता च कार्य कारणमेव च। यथेच्छति तथा राजन् क्रीडते पुरुषोऽव्ययः॥
en: He is both active and inactive. He is both Cause and Effect. He is the one immutable Soul, who sports as He likes, O king.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: एष एकान्तधर्मस्ते कीर्तितो नृपसत्तम। मया गुरुप्रसादेन दुर्विज्ञेयोऽकृतात्मभिः॥
en: Thus have I recounted to you the Religion of Devotion, O best of kings, which cannot be comprehended by persons of impure souls but which I acquired through the favour of my preceptor.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: एकान्तिनो हि पुरुषा दुर्लभा बहवो नृप। यद्येकान्तिभिराकीर्णं जगत् स्यात् कुरुनन्दन॥ अहिंसकैरात्मविद्भिः सर्वभूतहिते रतैः। भवेत् कृतयुगप्राप्तिराशी: कर्मविवर्जिताः॥
en: Persons are very rare, O king, who are devoted whole-mindedly to Narayana. If, O son of Kuru's race, the world has been full of such persons, who are full of universal mercy, who are possessed of the knowledge of the soul, and who are always busy with doing good to others, then the Krita age would have begun and all men would have undertaken works without desire of fruit.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: एवं स भगवान् व्यासो गुरुर्मम विशाम्पते। कथयामास धर्मज्ञो धर्मराज्ञे द्विजोत्तमः॥ ऋषीणां संनिधौ राजशृण्वतोः कृष्णभीष्मयोः। तस्याप्यकथयत् पूर्वं नारदः सुमहातपाः॥
en: It was even thus, O king, that foremost of twice-born ones, viz., the illustrious Vyasa, my preceptor, well-versed in all duties, described to king Yudhishthira the just this religion of Devotion, in the presence of many Rishis and in the hearing of Krishna and Bhishma. He had got it from the celestial Rishi Narada having penances for wealth.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: देवं परमकं ब्रह्म श्वेतं चन्द्राभमच्युतम्। यत्र चैकान्तिनो यान्ति नारायणपरायणाः॥
en: Those persons who are whole-mindedly devoted to Narayana in the end, that greatest of gods, identical with Brahma, pure in complexion, effulgent like the moon, and immutable.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: जनमेजय उवाच एवं बहुविधं धर्मं प्रतिबुद्धैर्निषेवितम्। न कुर्वन्ति कथं विप्रा अन्ये नानाव्रते स्थिताः॥
en: I see that those twice-born ones whose souls have been awakened, pactise various kinds of duties. Why it is that other Brahmanas do not practise those duties but observe other kinds of vows and rites?

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तिस्रः प्रकृतयो राजन् देहबन्धेषु निर्मिताः। सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चैव भारत॥
en: Three kinds of disposition, O king, have been created about all embodied creatures, viz., that which appertains to the quality of goodness, that which appertains to the quality of Darkness, and lastly that which appertains to the quality of Ignorance, O Bharata.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: देहबन्धेषु पुरुषः श्रेष्ठः कुरुकुलोद्वह। सात्त्विकः पुरुषव्याघ्र भवेन्मोक्षाय निश्चितः॥
en: As regards embodied creatures, perpetuator of Kuru's race, that person is the foremost who follows the quality of Goodness, for, O foremost of men, it is certain that he will acquire Liberation.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: अत्रापि स विजानाति पुरुषं ब्रह्मवित्तमम्। नारायणपरो मोक्षस्ततो वै सात्त्विकः स्मृतः॥
en: It is with the help of this very quality of Goodness that one endued therewith succeeds in understanding the person who is conversant with Brahma. As regards Liberation, it is entirely dependent upon Narayana. Hence it is that Liberation is considered as made up of the quality of Goodness.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: मनीषितं च प्राप्नोति चिन्तयन् पुरुषोत्तमम्। एकान्तभक्तिः सततं नारायणपरायणः॥
en: By thinking of the foremost of Beings, the man who is devoted whole-mindedly to Narayana, gains great wisdom.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: मनीषिणो हि ये केचिद् यतयो मोक्षधर्मिणः। तेषां विच्छिन्नतृष्णानां योगक्षेमवहो हरिः॥
en: Those persons who are possessed of wisdom, who follow the practices of Yatis and the Religion of Liberation,-those persons whose thirst has been satisfied_always find that Hari favours them with the fruition of their desire.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: जायमानं हि पुरुष यं पश्येन्मधुसूदनः। सात्त्विकस्तु स विज्ञेयो भवेन्मोक्षे च निश्चितः॥
en: That man subject to birth (and death) upon whom Hari casts a kind eye should be known as gifted with the quality of Goodness and devoted to the acquisition of Liberation.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: सांख्ययोगेन तुल्यो हि धर्म एकान्तसेवितः। नारायणात्मके मोक्षे ततो यान्ति परां गतिम्॥
en: The religion followed by a person who is devoted whole-mindely to to Narayana is considered as similar or equal in merit to the system of the Sankhyas.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: नारायणेन दृष्टस्तु प्रतिबुद्धो भवेत् पुमान्। एवमात्मेच्छया राजन् प्रतिबुद्धो न जायते॥
en: By following that religion one acquires the highest end by attaining to Liberation which has Narayana for its soul. That person upon whom Narayana looks with mercy succeeds in becoming awakened.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: राजसी तामसी चैव व्यामिश्रे प्रकृती स्मृते। तदात्मकं हि पुरुषं जायमानं विशाम्पते॥
en: No one, O king, can become awakened through his own wishes. That nature which partakes of both Darkness and Ignorance is said to be mixed.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: प्रवृत्तिलक्षणैर्युक्तं नावेक्षति हरिः स्वयम्।
en: Hari never casts a kind eye upon the person subject to birth who has such a mixed nature and who has, on that account the principle of action in him.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: पश्यत्येनं जायमानं ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः॥ रजसा तमसा चैव मानसं समभिप्लुतम्।
en: Only Brahman, the Grandfather of the worlds, cares for the person who is subject to me birth the death because of his mind being overwhelmed with the two inferior qualities of Darkness and Ignorance.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: कामं देवा ऋषयश्च सत्त्वस्था नृपसत्तम॥ हीनाः सत्त्वेन शुद्धेन ततो वैकारिकाः स्मृताः।
en: Forsooth, the gods and the Rishis are endued with the qualities of Goodness, best of kings! But then they who are divested of that quality in its subtile form are always considered to be of mutable nature.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं वैकारिको गच्छेत् पुरुषः पुरुषोत्तमम्॥ वद सर्वं यथादृष्टं प्रवृत्तिं च यथाक्रमम्।
en: Janamejaya said, How can one who is subject to change succeed in attaining to that foremost of Being? Do tell me all this, which is, no doubt, know to you! Do you describe to also of Renunciation in due order.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सुसूक्ष्मं सत्त्वसंयुक्तं संयुक्तं त्रिभिरक्षरैः॥ पुरुषः पुरुषं गच्छेनिष्क्रियः पञ्चविंशकः।
en: Vaishampayana sajd— When it becomes able to abstain entirely from acts, the twenty-fifth, i.e., the Individual Soul, succeeds in attaining to the foremost of Beings which is highly subtile, which is invested with the quality of Goodness, and which is highly of Goodness, and which is fraught with the essence symbolised by the three letters of the alphabet (viz., A. U. and M.)

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: एवमेकं सांख्ययोगं वेदारण्यकमेव च॥ परस्पराङ्गान्येतानि पाञ्चरात्रं च कथ्यते। एष एकान्तिनां धर्मो नारायणपरात्मकः॥
en: The Sankhya system, the Aranyaka-Veda, and the Pancharatra scriptures, are all identical and form parts of one whole. This is the religion of those who are devoted whole. mindedly to Narayana—the religion that has Narayana for its Soul.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: स्तमेव राजनपुनराविशन्ति। इमे तथा ज्ञानमहाजलौघा नारायणं वै पुनराविशन्ति॥
en: As waves of the ocean, rising from the ocean, rush away from it only to return to it in the long run so various sorts of knowledge, originating from Narayana, return to Narayana in the end.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: एष ते कथितो धर्मः सात्वतः कुरुनन्दन। कुरुरुष्वैनं यथान्यायं यदि शक्तोऽसि भारत्॥
en: I have thus explained to you, O son of Kuru's race, what the religion of Goodness is. If you be qualified for it, O Bharata, do you practise that religion duly.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: एवं हि स महाभागो नारदो गुरवे मम। श्वेतानां यतिनां चाह एकान्तगतिमव्ययाम्॥
en: Thus did the highly-blessed Narada explain to my preceptor.-the Island-born Krishna-the eternal and immutable course called Ekanta, followed by the Whites as also by Yatis.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: व्यासश्चकथयत् प्रीत्या धर्मपुत्राय धीमते। स एवायं मया तुभ्यमाख्यातः प्रसृतो गुरोः॥
en: Pleased with Dharma's son Yudhisthira, Vyasa imparted this religion to king Yudhisthira the just who was endued with great intelligence. Derived from my preceptor I have also communicated it to you.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: इत्थं हि दुश्चरो धर्म एष पार्थिवसत्तम। यथैव त्वं तथैवान्ये भवन्तीह विमोहिताः॥
en: O best of kings, this religion is, for these reasons, highly difficult of practice. Others, hearing it, become as much stupefied as you have allowed yourself to be.

description: The practices of men who are devoted to Narayana
sn: कृष्ण एव हि लोकानां भावनो मोहनस्तथा। संहारकारकश्चैव कारणं च विशांपते॥
en: It is Krishna who is the protector of the universe and its beguiler. It is He who is the destroyer and the cause, O king.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: जनमेजय उवाच सांख्यं योगः पाञ्चरात्रं वेदारण्यकमेव च। ज्ञानान्येतानि ब्रह्मर्षे लोकेषु प्रचरन्ति ह॥
en: The Sankhya System, the Pancharatra Scriptures, and the Aranyaka-Vedas—these different systems of knowledge or religion,-0 twice-born Rishi, are current in the world.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: किमेतान्येकनिष्ठानि पृथनिष्ठानि वा मुने। प्रब्रूहि वै मया पृष्टः प्रवृत्तिं च यथाक्रमम्॥
en: Do all these systems preach the same course of duties, or are the courses of duties preached by them, O ascetic, different from one another? Accosted by me, do you describe to me on Renunciation in due order!

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच जज्ञे बहुशं परमत्युदारं यं द्वीपमध्ये सुतमात्मयोगात्। पराशरात् सत्यवती महर्षि तस्मै नमोऽज्ञानतमोनुदाय॥
en: Vaishampayana said I bow to that great Rishi who is the remover of Darkness, and whom Satyavati bore to Parashara in the midst of an island, who is endued with great knowledge and great liberality of soul.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: पितामहाद् यं प्रवदन्ति षष्ठं महर्षिमायविभूतियुक्तम्। नारायणस्यांशजमेकपुत्रं द्वैपायनं वेद महानिधानम्॥
en: The learned say that he is the origin of the Grandfather Brahman; that he is the sixth form of Narayana; that he is the foremost of Rishis; that he is endued with the power of Yoga; that as the only son of his parents he is an incarnate part of Narayana; and that, born under extraordinary circumstances on an Island, he is the undecaying receptacle of the Vedas.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: रायणो ब्रह्ममहानिधानम्। ससर्ज पुत्रार्थमुदारतेजा व्यासं महात्मानमजं पुराणम्॥
en: In the Krita age, Narayana, of great power and might energy, created him as his son. Verily, the great Vyasa is unborn and ancient and is the undecaying receptacle of the Vedas.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: जनमेजय उवाच त्वयैव कथितं पूर्वं सम्भवे द्विजसत्तम। वसिष्ठस्य सुतः शक्तिः शक्तिपुत्रः पराशरः॥ पराशरस्य दायादः कृष्णद्वैपायनो मुनिः।
en: Janamejaya said, O best of twice-born ones, it was you who said before this that the Rishi Vashishtha had a son named Shakti and that Shakti had a son named Parashara, and that Parashara begot a son named the Island-born Krishna gifted with great ascetic merit.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: भूयो नारायणसुतं त्वमेवैनं प्रभाषसे॥ किमतः पूर्वजं जन्म व्यासस्यामिततेजसः। कथयस्वोत्तममते जन्म नारायणोद्भवम्॥
en: You tell me again that Vyasa is the son of Narayana. I ask was it in some former birth that Vyasa of great energy had originated from Narayana? O you of great intelligence, do tell me of that birth of Vyasa from Narayana!

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वेदार्थान् वेत्तुकामस्य धर्मिष्ठस्य तपोनिधेः। गुरोर्मे ज्ञाननिष्ठस्य हिमवत्पाद आसतः॥
en: Desirous of understanding the meaning of the Shrutis, my preceptor, that sea of penances, who is greatly devoted to the observance of all scriptural duties and the acquisition of knowledge, lived for sometime in a particular region of the Himavat mountains.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: कृत्वा भारतमाख्यानं तप:श्रान्तस्य धीमतः। शुश्रूषां तत्परा राजन् कृतवन्तो वयं तदा॥ सुमन्तुजैमिनिश्चैव पैलश्च सुदृढव्रतः। अहं चतुर्थः शिष्यो वै शुकोव्यासात्मजस्तथा॥
en: Gifted with great intelligence, he became fatigued with his penances on account of the great strain on his energies made by the composition of the Mahabharata. At that time, Sumanta and Jaimini and Paila of firm vows and myself as the fourth, and Shuka his own son, were his disciples. All of us, O king, seeing the fatigfue of our preceptor, waited dutifully upon him, engaged in doing all that was necessary for removing that fatigue of his.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: एभिः परिवृतो व्यास: शिष्यैः पञ्चभिरुत्तमैः। शुशुभे हिमवत्पादे भूतैर्भूतपतिर्यथा॥
en: Surrounded by these disciples of his, Vyasa shone on the breast of the Himavat mountains like the Lord of all the goblins, viz., Mahadeva, in the midst of those ghostly attendants of his.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: वेदानावर्तयन् साङ्गान् भारतार्थांश्च सर्वशः। तमेकमनसं दान्तं युक्ता वयमुपास्महे॥
en: Having recapitulated the Vedas with all their branches as also the meanings of all the Verses in the Mahabharata, one day, with rapt attention, all of us approached our preceptor who, having mastered his senses, was at time engaged in thought.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: कथान्तरेऽथ कस्मिंश्चित् पृष्टोऽस्माभिर्द्विजोत्तमः। वेदार्थान् भारतार्थांश्च जन्म नारायणात् तथा॥
en: Availing ourselves of an interval in the conversation, we asked that foremost of twiceborn ones to explain to us the meanings of the Vedas and of the Verses in the Mahabharata and describe to us the events as well of his own birth from Narayana.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: स पूर्वमुक्त्वा वेदार्थान् भारतार्थांश्च तत्त्ववित्। नारायणादिदं जन्म व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: Conversant as he was with all subjects of enquiry, he at first described to us the interpretations of the Shrutis and the Mahabharata, and then began to narrate to us the following events regarding his birth from Narayana.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: शृणुध्वमाख्यानवरमिदमायमुत्तमम्। आदिकालोद्भवं विप्रास्तपसाधिगतं मया॥
en: Vyasa said Listen, ye disciples to this foremost of narratives, to this best of histories that concerns the birth of a Rishi. Belonging to the Krita age, this discourse has become known to me through my penances, ye twice-born ones.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: प्राप्ते प्रजाविसर्गे वै सप्तमे पद्मसम्भवे। नारायणो महायोगी शुभाशुभविवर्जितः॥ ससृजे नाभितः पूर्वं ब्रह्माणममितप्रभः। ततः स प्रादुरभवदथैनं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: On the occasion of the seventh creation, viz., that which was due to the primeval Lotus, Narayana, gifted, with the austerest penances, getting over both good and evil, and possessed of peerless splendour, at first created Brahman, from his navel. After Brahman had come into being, Narayana addressed him, saying,

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: मम त्वं नाभितो जातः प्रजासर्गकरः प्रभुः। सृज प्रजास्त्वं विविधा ब्रह्मन् सजडपण्डिताः॥
en: You have originated from my navel. Gifted with power of creation, do you begin to create diverse kinds of creatures, rational and irrational.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: स एवमुक्तो विमुखश्चिन्ताव्याकुलमानसः। प्रणम्य वरदं देवमुवाच हरिमीश्वरम्॥
en: Thus addressed by his Creator, Brahman, with mind stricken with anxiety, felt the difficulty of his task and became reluctant to do what he was ordered to do. Bowing his head to the boon-giving and illustrious Hari, the Lord of the universe, Brahman said these words to him,

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: का शक्तिर्मम देवेश प्रजाः स्रष्टुं नमोऽस्तु ते। अप्रज्ञावानहं देव विधत्स्व यदनन्तरम्॥
en: I bow to you, O Lord of the gods, but I ask what power have I to create various creatures? I have no wisdom. Do you ordain what should be ordained in view of this.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: स एवमुक्तो भगवान् भूत्वाथान्तर्हितस्ततः। चिन्तयामास देवेशो बुद्धिं बुद्धिमतां वरः॥
en: Thus addressed by Brahman, the Lord of the universe, viz., Narayana, disappeared there and then from Brahman's view, the foremost of all being gifted with intelligence, viz., the Supreme Lord, then thought of Intelligence.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: स्वरूपिणी ततो बुद्धिरुपतस्थे हरि प्रभुम्। योगेन चैनां निर्योगः स्वयं नियुयुजे तदा॥
en: Possessed of form that resembled immediately appeared before the powerful Hari. Himself above all Yoga, Narayana then, with Yoga, applied the goddess of Intelligence properly.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: स तामैश्वर्ययोगस्थां बुद्धिं गतिमती सतीम्। उवाच वचनं देवो बुद्धिं वै प्रभुरव्ययः॥
en: The illustrious and powerful and immutable Hari, addressed the goddess of Intelligence who was gifted with activity and goodness and all the power of Yoga, said to her these words-

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: ब्रह्माणं प्रविशस्वेति लोकसृष्ट्यर्थसिद्धये। ततस्तमीश्वरादिष्टा बुद्धिः क्षिप्रं विवेश सा॥
en: For the accomplishment of the work of creating all the words do you enter into Brahman!-Ordered thus by the Supreme Lord, Intelligence immediately entered Brahman.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: अथैनं बुद्धिसंयुक्तं पुनः स ददृशे हरिः। भूयश्चैव वचः प्राह सृजेमा विविधाः प्रजाः॥
en: When Hari saw that Brahman had become united with Intelligence, He once addressed him, saying,-Do you now create various creatures.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: बाढमित्येव कृत्वासौ यथाऽऽज्ञां शिरसा हरेः। एवमुक्त्वा स भगवांस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥ प्राप चैनं मुहूर्तेन संस्थानं देवसंज्ञितम्। तां चैव प्रकृति प्राप्य एकीभावगतोऽभवत्॥
en: Replying to Narayana by uttering the word— Yes,-Brahman reverently accepted the order of his progenitor. Narayana then disappeared from Brahman's view, and in a more moment repaired to his own place known by the name of Light or Effulgence. Coming back to His own disposition, Hari resolved Himself into His one universal nature.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: अथास्य बुद्धिरभवत् पुनरन्या तदा किला सृष्टाः प्रजा इमाः सर्वा ब्रह्मणा परमेष्ठिना॥ दैत्यदानवगन्धर्वरक्षोगणसमाकुला। जाता हीयं वसुमती भाराकान्ता तपस्विनी।॥
en: After the work of Creation, however, had been done by Brahman, another thought arose in the mind of Narayana. Indeed,. He thought thus,-Brahman, otherwise called Parameshthi, has created all these creatures, consisting of Daityas and Danavas and Gandharvas and Rakshasas. The helpless Earth has become loaded with the weight of creatures.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: बहवो बलिनः पृथ्व्यां दैत्यदानवराक्षसाः। भविष्यन्ति तपोयुक्ता वरान् प्राप्स्यन्ति चोत्तमान्॥
en: Many among the Daityas and Danavas and Rakshsas on Earth will become gifted with great strength. Possessed of penances, they will at various times succeed in acquiring many excellent boons.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: अवश्यमेव तैः सर्वैर्वरदानेन दर्पितैः। बाधितव्याः सुरगणा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः॥
en: Elated with pride and power on account of those boons they will succeed in acquiring, they will oppress and afflict the gods and the Rishis endued with ascetic power.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: तत्र न्याय्यमिदं कर्तुं भारावतरणं मया। अथ नानासमुद्भूतैर्वसुधायां यथाक्रमम्॥
en: It is, therefore, proper that I should now and then lighten the burden of the Earth, by assuming various forms one after another as occasion would require.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: निग्रहेण च पापानां साधूनां प्रग्रहेण च। इयं तपस्विनी सत्या धारयिष्यति मेदिनी॥
en: I shall perform this task by punishing the wicked and supporting the righteous. The Earth, which is the embodiment of Truth, will succeed in bearing her burden of creatures.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: मया ह्येषा हि ध्रियते पातालस्थेन भोगिना। मया धृता धारयति जगद् विश्वं चराचरम्॥ तस्मात् पृथ्व्याः परित्राणं करिष्ये सम्भवं गतः।
en: Assuming the form of a powerful snake I myself have to uphold the Earth in empty space. Supported by me thus, she will support the entire universe of creatures mobile and immobile. Incarnated on the Earth, therefore, in different forms, I shall have to save her at such time from danger.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: एवं स चिन्तयित्वा तु भगवान् मधुसूदनः॥ रूपाण्यनेकान्यसृजत् प्रादुर्भावे भवाय सः।
en: Having thought thus, the illustrious killer of Madhu created various forms in his mind in which to appear from time to time for performing the proposed task.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: वाराहं नारसिंह च वामनं मानुषं तथा॥ एभिर्मया निहन्तव्या दुर्विनीताः सुरारयः।
en: Assuming the form of a Boar, of a Manlion, of a Dwarf, and of human beings, I shall suppress or kill such enemies of the gods as will become wicked and ungovernable.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: अथ भूयो जगत्स्रष्टा भोःशब्देनानुनादयन्॥ सरस्वतीमुच्चचार तत्र सारस्वतोऽभवत्।
en: After this, the Prime Creator of the universe once more uttered the syllable BHO, causing the atmosphere to resound with it. From this syllable of speech arose a Rishi named Sarasvat.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: अपान्तरतमा नाम सुतो वाक्सम्भवः प्रभुः॥ भूतभव्यभविष्यज्ञः सत्यवादी दृढव्रतः।
en: The son, thus born of the Speech of Narayana, also passed by the name of Apantara-tamas. Endued with great power, he was fully conversant with the past, the present, and the future. Firm in the observance of vows, he was truthful in speech.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: तमुवाच नतं मूर्धा देवानामादिरव्ययः॥ वेदाख्याने श्रुतिः कार्या त्वया मतिमतां वर।
en: To that Rishi who, after birth, had bowed his head to Narayana, the latter, who was the original Creator of all the gods and possessed of immutable nature, said those words-You should bestow your attention on the distribution of the Vedas, O foremost of all persons gifted with intelligence.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: तस्मात् कुरु यथाऽऽज्ञप्तं ममैतद् वचनं मुने॥ सेन भिन्नास्तदा वेदा मनोः स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे।
en: Do you, therefore, O ascetic, do what I command you!-In obedience to this command of the Supreme Lord from whose Speech the Rishi Apantaratamas came into being, the latter, in that Kalpa which is named from the Self-born Manu, distributed and arranged the Vedas.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: ततस्तुतोष भगवान् हरिस्तेनास्य कर्मणा॥ तपसा च सुतप्तेन यमेन नियमेन च।
en: For that act of the Rishi, the illustrious Hari became pleased with him, as also for his wellperformed penances, his and observances, and his control of the senses or passions.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: मन्वन्तरेषु पुत्रत्वमेवमेव प्रवर्तकः॥ भविष्यस्यचलो ब्रह्मन्नप्रधृष्यश्च नित्यशः।
en: Addressing him, Narayana said,-At each cycle of Manu, O son, you will act thus about the Vedas. You shall on account of this act of yours, be immutable, O twice-born one, and incapable of being excellent by any one.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: पुनस्तिष्ये च सम्प्राप्ते कुरवो नाम भारताः॥ भविष्यन्ति महात्मानो राजानः प्रथिता भुवि।
en: When the Kali age will set in, certain princes of Bharata's line, named Kauravas, will take their birth from you. They will be celebrated over Earth as great princes ruling over powerful kingdoms.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: तेषां त्वत्तः प्रसूतानां कुलभेदो भविष्यति॥ परस्परविनाशार्थ त्वामृते द्विजसत्तम।
en: Born of you, dissension's will break out among them for their destruction at one another's hands during your absence, O foremost of twice-born ones.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: तत्राप्यनेकधा वेदान् भेत्स्यते तपसान्वितः॥ कृष्णे युगे च सम्प्राप्ते कृष्णवर्णो भविष्यसि।
en: In that age also, gifted with austere penances, you will divide the Vedas into various classes. Indeed, in that dark age, your complexion will become dark.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: धर्माणां विविधानां च कर्ता ज्ञानकरस्तथा। भविष्यसि तपोयुक्तो न च रागाद् विमोक्ष्यसे।॥
en: You will made various kinds of duties of flow and various kinds of knowledge also. Although gifted with austere penances, yet you shall never be able to free yourself from desire and attachment to the world.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: वीतरागश्च पुत्रस्ते परमात्मा भविष्यति। महेश्वरप्रसादेन नैतद् वचनमन्यथा॥
en: Your son, however, will be freed from every attachment like the Supreme Soul, through the favour of Mahadeva. It will not be otherwise.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: यं मानसं वै प्रवदन्ति विप्राः पितामहस्योत्तमबुद्धियुक्तमा वसिष्ठमयं च तपोनिधानं यस्यातिसूर्यं व्यतिरिच्यते भाः॥ तस्यान्वये चापि ततो महर्षिः पराशरो नाम महाप्रभावः। पिता स ते वेदनिधिर्वरिष्ठो महातपा वै तपसो निवासः॥ कानीनगर्भः पितृकन्यकायां तस्मादृषेस्त्वं भविता च पुत्रः॥
en: He whom learned Brahmanas call the mindbegotten son of the Grandfather, viz., Vashishtha gifted with great intelligence and like an ocean of penances, and whose splendour excells that of the Sun himself, will be the progenitor of a family in which a great Rishi of the name of Parashara, endued with mighty energy and prowess, will take his birth. That foremost of persons, that ocean of Vedas, that habitation of penances, will become your father. You shall take your birth as the son of a maiden living in the house of her father, through an act of sexual union with the great Rishi Parashara.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: भूतभव्यभविष्याणां छिन्नसर्वार्थसंशयः। ये ह्यतिक्रान्तकाः पूर्वं सहस्रयुगपर्ययाः॥ तांश्च सर्वान् मयोद्दिष्टान् द्रक्ष्यसे तपसान्वितः। पुनर्द्रक्ष्यसि चानेकसहस्रयुगपर्ययान्॥
en: You will entertain no doubts about the meanings of things past, present, and future. Gifted with penances and instructed by me, you will see the incidents of a thousands and thousands of ages long past away. You will see through thousands and thousands of ages also in the future.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: अनादिनिधनं लोके चक्रहस्तं च मां मुने। अनुध्यानान्मम मुने नैतद् वचनमन्यथा।॥
en: You shall in that birth, see me, O ascetic,—me who am without birth and death,-incarnated on Earth armed with the discus. All this will happen to you, O ascetic, through the merit that you will acquire for your continued devotion to me. These words of mine will never be otherwise.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: भविष्यति महासत्त्व ख्यातिश्चाप्यतुला तव। शनैश्चरः सूर्यपुत्रो भविष्यति मनुर्महान्॥
en: You shall be one of the foremost of creatures. Great shall be your fame. The Sun's son Shani (Saturn) will in a future cycle, take birth as the great Manu of that period.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: तस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे चैव मन्वादिगणपूर्वकः। त्वमेव भविता वत्स मत्प्रसादान्न संशयः॥
en: During that period, O son, you shall, as regards merits, be superior to even the Manus of the several periods. Forsooth, you will be so through my favour.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: यत्किचिद् विद्यते लोके सर्वं तन्मद्विचेष्टितम्। अन्यो ह्यन्यं चिन्तयति स्वच्छन्दं विदधाम्यहम्॥
en: Whatever exists in the world is the result of my exertion. The thoughts of others may not tally with their deeds. As regards myself, however, I always ordain what I think, without the least obstacles.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: एवं सारस्वतमृषिमपान्तरतमं तथा। उक्त्वा वचनमीशानः साधयस्वेत्यथाब्रवीत्॥ सोऽहं तस्य प्रसादेन देवस्य हरिमेधसः। अपान्तरतमा नाम ततो जातोऽऽज्ञया हरेः। पुनश्च जातो विख्यातो वसिष्ठकुलनन्दनः॥
en: Having said these words to the Rishi Apantaratamas, otherwise called by the name of Sarasvat, the Supreme Lord sent him away, saying to him,-Go!-I am he that was born as Apantaratamas through the behest of Hari. Once more have I taken birth as the celebrated Krishna-Dvaipayana, a delighter of the race of Vashishtha.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: तदेतत् कथितं जन्म मा पूर्वकमात्मनः। नारायणप्रसादेन तथा नारायणांशजम्॥
en: I have thus told, you my dear disciples, the circumstances of my own pristine birth which was due to the favour of Narayana in so much that I was a very part of Narayana himself.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: मया हि सुमहत् तप्तं तपः परमदारुणम्। पुरा मतिमतां श्रेष्ठाः परमेण समाधिना॥
en: You foremost of intelligent persons, I practised, in days of yore, the austerest penances, with the help of the highest abstraction of the mind.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: एतद् वः कथितं सर्वं यन्मां पृच्छत पुत्रकाः। पूर्वजन्म भविष्यं च भक्तानां स्नेहतो मया॥
en: You sons, actuated by my great love for yourselves who are devoted to me with reverence, I have told you everything about what you wished to know from me. viz., my first birth in days gone by and that other birth subsequent to it.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एष ते कथितः पूर्वं सम्भवोऽस्मद्गुरोर्नृप। व्यासस्याक्लिष्टमनसो यथा पृष्टः पुनः शृणु॥
en: Vaishampayana said I have thus described to you, O king, the circumstances about the former birth of our revered preceptor, viz., Vyasa of unsullied mind, as asked by you! Listen to me once again!

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: सांख्यं योगः पाञ्चरात्रं वेदाः पाशुपतं तथा। ज्ञानान्येतानि राजर्षे विद्धि नामामतानि वै॥
en: There are various kinds of religion, O royal sage, who go by various names such as Sankhya, Yoga, the Panch-ratra, Vedas, and Pashupati.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: सांख्यस्य वक्ता कपिलः परमर्षिः स उच्यते। हिरण्यगर्भो योगस्य वेत्ता नान्यः पुरातनः॥
en: The promulgator of the Sankhya religion is said to be the great Rishi Kapila. The primeval Hiranyagarbha, and none else, is the promulgator of the Yoga system.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: अपान्तरतमाश्चैव वेदाचार्यः स उच्यते। प्राचीनगर्भ तमृषि प्रवदन्तीह केचन॥
en: The Rishi Apantaratamas is said to be the preceptor of the Vedas, some call that Rishi by the name of Prachina-garbha.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: उमापतिर्भूतपति: श्रीकण्ठो ब्रह्मणः सुतः। उक्तवानिदमव्यग्रो ज्ञानं पाशुपतं शिवः॥
en: The religion known by the name of Pashupata was promulgated by the Lord of Uma, that lord of all creatures, viz., the cheerful Shiva, otherwise known by the name of Shreekantha, the son of Brahman.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: पाञ्चरात्रस्य कृत्स्नस्य वेत्ता तु भगवान् स्वयम्। सर्वेषु च नृपश्रेष्ठ ज्ञानेष्वेतेषु दृश्यते॥ यथागमं यथाज्ञानं निष्ठा नारायणः प्रभुः। न चैनमेवं जानन्ति तमोभूता विशाम्पते॥
en: The illustrious Narayana is himself the promulgator of the religion, contained in the Pancharatra Scriptures. In all these religions, O foremost of kings, it is seen that the powerful Narayana is the one sole object of exposition. According to the scriptures of these religions and the extent of knowledge they contain, Narayana is the one sole object of adoration they preach. Those persons whose vision, O king, blinded by darkness, cannot understand that Narayana is the Supreme Soul pervading the entire universe.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: तमेव शास्त्रकर्तारः प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः। निष्ठां नारायणमृर्षि नान्योऽस्तीति वचो मम॥
en: Those wise persons who are the authors of the scriptures say that Narayana, who is a Rishi, is the one object of respectful adoration in the universe, I say that there is no other being like Him.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: नि:संशयेषु सर्वेषु नित्यं वसति वै हरिः। ससंशयान् हेतुबलान् नाध्यावसति माधवः॥
en: The Supreme God, called by the name of Hari, lives in the hearts of those who have are are succeeded in removing all doubts. Madhava never lives in the hearts of those who are under the sway of doubt and who would dispute away everything with the help of false logic.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: पाञ्चरात्रविदो ये तु यथाक्रमपरा नृप। एकान्तभावोपगतास्ते हरि प्रविशन्ति वै॥
en: They who conversant with the Pancharatra Scriptures, who are duly observant of the duties laid down therein, and who are whole-mindedly devoted to Narayana, succeed in entering into Narayana.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: सांख्यं च योगं च सनातने द्वे वेदाश्च सर्वे निखिलेन राजन्। सर्वैः समस्तैर्ऋषिभिर्निरुक्तो नारायणो विश्वमिदं पुराणम्॥
en: The Sankhya and the Yoga Systems are eternal. All the Vedas, again, O king, are eternal. The Rishis, in all these systems or religion, have said that this universe existing from ancient times is Narayana's self.

description: The story that Vyasa was Narayan's son
sn: शुभाशुभं कर्म समीरितं यत् प्रवर्तते सर्वलोकेषु किञ्चित्। तस्मादृषेस्तद्भवतीति विद्याद् दिव्यन्तरिक्षे भुवि चाप्सु चेति॥
en: You should know that whatever acts, good or bad, laid down in the Vedas and occurring in heaven and Earth, the sky between, and the waters, are all made by that ancient Rishi Narayana.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच वहवः पुरुषा ब्रह्मन्नुताहो एक एव तु। को ह्यत्र पुरुषः श्रेष्ठः को वा योनिरिहोच्यते॥
en: Janamejaya said O twice-born one, are there many souls or is there only one? Who, in the universe, is the foremost of Souls? What, again, is said to be the source of all things?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वहवः पुरुषा लोके सांख्ययोगविचारणे। नैतदिच्छन्ति पुरुषमेकं कुरुकुलोद्वह॥
en: Vaishampayana said, In the Sankhya and the Yoga Systems many are the Souls spoken of. O preceptor of Kuru's race, those who follow these systems do not wish to assert that there is but one Purusha in the universe.

sn: बहूनां पुरुषाणां च यथैका योनिरुच्यते। तथा तं पुरुषं विश्वव्याख्यास्यामि गुणाधिकम्॥ नमस्कृत्वा च गुरवे व्यासाय विदितात्मने। तपोयुक्ताय दान्ताय वन्द्याय परमर्षये॥
en: Similarly in scriptures in which the many Souls are said to have one origin in the Supreme Soul, it may be said that this entire universe is at one with that one Soul of superior attributes. I shall explain this now, after bowing to my preceptor Vyasa, that foremost of Rishis, who is conversant with the soul, endued with penances, self-controlled, and worthy of respectful adoration.

sn: इदं पुरुषसूक्तं हि सर्ववेदेषु पार्थिव। ऋतं सत्यं च विख्यातमृषिसिंहेन चिन्तितम्॥
en: This speculation on Purusha, O king, occurs in all the Vedas. It is well-known to be at one with Rita and Truth. The foremost of Rishis, viz., Vyasa, has thought upon it.

sn: उत्सर्गेणापवादेन ऋषिभिः कपिलादिभिः। अध्यात्मचिन्तामाश्रित्य शास्त्रााण्युक्तानि भारत॥
en: Having occupied themselves with reflection on what is called the spiritual science, various Rishis, O king, having Kapila for their first, have declared their opinions on this subject both generally and particularly.

sn: समासतस्तु यद् व्यासः पुरुषैकत्वमुक्तवान्। तत् तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रसादादमितौजसः॥
en: Through the favour of Vyasa of great energy, I shall explain to you what Vyasa has said in brief on this question of the Oneness of Soul.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। ब्रह्मणा सह संवादं त्र्यम्बकस्य विशाम्पते॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Brahman, O king, and the Three-eyed Mahadeva.

sn: क्षीरोदस्य समुद्रस्य मध्ये हाटकसप्रभः। वैजयन्त इति ख्यातः पर्वतप्रवरो नृप॥
en: In the midst of the Ocean of milk, there is a very huge mountain of great effulgence like that of gold, known, O king, by the name of Vaijayanta.

sn: तत्राध्यात्मगति देव एकाकी प्रविचिन्तयन्। वैराजसदनान्नित्यं वैजयन्तं निषेवते॥
en: Going there all alone, from his own abode of great splendour and happiness, the illustrious god Brahman used very often to pass his time, engaged in thinking on the course of spiritual science.

sn: अथ तत्रासतस्तस्य चतुर्वक्त्रस्य धीमत। ललाटप्रभवः पुत्रः शिव आगाद् यदृच्छया॥
en: While the four-headed Brahman of great intelligence, as seated there, his son Mahadeva, who had originated from his forehead, met him one day in course of his travel through the universe.

sn: आकाशेन महायोगी पुरा त्रिनयनः प्रभुः। ततः खानिपपाताशु धरणीधरमूर्धनि॥
en: In days of yore, the Three-eyed Shiva endued with power and high Yoga, while proceeding along the sky, saw Brahman seated on that mountain and, therefore, dropped down quickly on its top.

sn: अग्रतश्चाभवत् प्रीतो ववन्दे चापि पादयोः। तं पादयोर्निपतितं दृष्ट्वा सव्येन पाणिना॥
en: With a cheerful heart he appeared before his progenitor and adored his feet. Seeing Mahadeva prostrated at his feet, Brahman took him up with his left hand.

sn: उत्थापयामास तदा प्रभुरेकः प्रजापतिः। उवाच चैनं भगवांश्चिरस्यागतमात्मजम्॥
en: Having thus raised Mahadeva up, Brahman, that powerful and one Lord of all creatures, then addressed his son, whom he met after long time in those words.

sn: पितामह उवाच स्वागतं ते महाबाहो दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि मेऽन्तिकम्। कच्चित् ते कुशलं पुत्र स्वाध्यायतपसोः सदा॥ नित्यमुग्रतपास्त्वं हि ततः पृच्छामि ते पुनः॥
en: The Grandfather said Welcome are you, O you of mighty arms! By good luck I see you after such a long time before me. I hope, O son, that everything is right with your penances, and your Vedic studies and recitations. You always observe the austerest penances. hence I ask you about the progress and well-being of those penances of yours.

sn: रुद्र उवाच त्वत्प्रसादेन भगवन् स्वाध्यायतपसोर्मम। कुशलं चाव्ययं चैव सर्वस्य जगतस्त्वथ॥
en: Rudra said O Illustrious One, through your grace, all is well with my penances and Vedic studies. It is all right, again, with universe.

sn: चिरदृष्टो हि भगवान् वैराजसदने मया। ततोऽहं पर्वतं प्राप्तस्त्विमं त्वत्पादसेवितम्॥
en: I saw your illustrious self a long while ago in your own home of happiness and effulgence! I am coming thence to this mountain that is not the habitation of your feet.

sn: कौतूहलं चापि हि मे एकान्तगमनेन ते। नैतत् कारणमल्पं हि भविष्यति पितामह॥
en: My mind is filled up with great curiosity for your thus coming into such a secluded mind from your usual religion of happiness and splendour. There must be great reason, O Grandfather, for such an act.

sn: किं नु तत्सदनं श्रेष्ठं क्षुत्पिपासाविवर्जितम्। सुरासुरैरध्युषितं ऋषिभिश्चरामितप्रभैः॥ गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च सततं संनिषेवितम्। उत्सृज्येम गिरिवरमेकाकी प्राप्तवानसि॥
en: Your own foremost of abodes is free from the pains of hunger and thirst and inhabited by both gods and Asuras, by Rishis of great splendour, as also by Gandharvas and Apsaras. Leaving such a spot of happiness, you live alone in this foremost of mountains. The cause of this cannot but be weighty.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच वैजयन्तो गिरिवरः सततं सेव्यते मया। अत्रैकाग्रेण मनसा पुरुषश्चिन्त्यते विराट्॥
en: This foremost of mountains, called Vaijayanta, is always my abode. Here, with concentrated mind, I meditate on the one universal Soul of infinite proportions.

sn: रुद्र उवाच वहवः पुरुषा ब्रह्मंस्त्वया सृष्टाः स्वयम्भुवा। सृज्यन्ते चापरे ब्रह्मन् स चैकः पुरुषो विराट॥
en: Rudra said Self-create you are. Many are the Souls that haven been created by you. Others again, O Brahman, are being created by you. The Infinite Soul, however, of whom you speak, is one and single.

sn: को ह्यसौ चिन्त्यते ब्रह्मस्त्वयैकः पुरुषोत्तमः। एतन्मे संशयं ब्रूहि महत् कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: Who is that foremost of Souls, O Brahman, that is being meditated by you? Great is my curiosity about it. Do you kindly remove the doubt that has possessed my mind!

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच बहवः पुरुषाः पुत्र त्वया ये समुदाहृताः। एवमेतदतिक्रान्तं द्रष्टव्यं नैवमित्यपि॥
en: Brahman said O son, many are those Souls of whom you speak. The one Soul, however, of whom I am thinking, transcends all Souls and is invisible.

sn: आधारं तु प्रवक्ष्यामि एकस्य पुरुषस्य ते। बहूनां पुरुषाणां स यथैका योनिरुच्यते॥ तथा तं पुरुषं विश्वं परमं सुमहत्तमम्। निर्गुणं निर्गुणा भूत्वा प्रविशन्ति सनातनम्॥
en: The many Souls that exist in the universe constitute the basis upon which that one Soul slands; and since that one Soul is said to be the source whence all the innumerable Purushas have originated, hence all the latter, if they succeed in divesting themselves of attributes, become competent to enter into that one Soul who is at one with the universe, who is supreme, who is the foremost of the foremost, who is eternal, and who is himself divested of and is above all qualities. 77977 Ryt fagd TH

sn: सुमहत्तमम्। निर्गुणं निर्गुणा भूत्वा प्रविशन्ति सनातनम्॥
en: The many Souls that exist in the universe constitute the basis upon which that one Soul slands; and since that one Soul is said to be the source whence all the innumerable Purushas have originated, hence all the latter, if they succeed in divesting themselves of attributes, become competent to enter into that one Soul who is at one with the universe, who is supreme, who is the foremost of the foremost, who is eternal, and who is himself divested of and is above all qualities.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच शृणु पुत्र यथा ह्येष पुरुषः शाश्वतोऽव्ययः। अक्षयश्चाप्रमेयश्च सर्वगश्च निरुच्यते॥
en: Brahman said Listen, O son, as to how that Soul is indicated. He is eternal and immutable. He is undecaying and immeasurable. He pervades all things.

sn: न स शक्यस्त्वया द्रष्टुं मयान्यैर्वापि सत्तम। सगुणो निर्गुणो विश्वोज्ञानदृश्योह्यसौ स्मृतः॥
en: O best of all creatures, that soul cannot be seen by you or me, others. Those who are endued with the understanding and the senses but shorn of self-control and tranquillity of soul cannot see him. The Supreme Soul is said to be one that can be seen with the help of knowledge alone.

sn: अशरीरः शरीरेषु सर्वेषु निवसत्यसौ। वसन्नपि शरीरेषु न स लिप्यति कर्मभिः॥
en: Though shorn of body, He lives in every body. Though living, again, in bodies He is never touched by the acts done by those bodies.

sn: ममान्तरात्मा तव च ये चान्ये देहिसंज्ञिताः। सर्वेषां साक्षिभूतोऽसौ न ग्राह्यः केनचित् क्वचित्॥
en: He is my inner soul. He is your inner soul. He is the omniscient Witness living within all embodied creatures and engaged in marking their acts. No one can grasp or comprehend him at any time.

sn: विश्वमूर्धा विश्वभुजो विश्वपादाक्षिनासिकः। एकश्चरति क्षेत्रेषु स्वैरचारी यथासुखम्॥
en: The universe is the crown of his head. The universe is his arms. The universe is his feet. The universe is his eyes. The universe is his nose. Alone and singly, he passed through all bodies, unrestrained by any limitations on his will and as best as it likes him.

sn: क्षेत्राणि हि शरीराणि बीजं चापि शुभाशुभम्। तानि वेत्ति स योगात्मा ततः क्षेत्रज्ञ उच्यते॥
en: Kshetriya is another name for body. And because he knows all bodies as also all good and bad acts, therefore, he, who is the soul of Yoga, is called by the name of Kshetrajna.

sn: नागतिर्न गतिस्तस्य ज्ञेया भूतेषु केनचित्। सांख्येन विधिना चैव योगेन च यथाक्रमम्॥ चिन्तयामि गतिं चास्य न गतिं वेधि चोत्तराम्। यथाज्ञानं तु वक्ष्यामि पुरुषं तु सनातनम्॥ तस्यैकत्वं महत्त्वं च स चैकः पुरुषः स्मृतः। महापुरुषशब्दं स बिभत्र्येकः सनातनः॥
en: No one succeeds in perceiving how he enters into embodied creatures and how he goes out of them. According to the Sankhya mode, as also with the help of Yoga and the due observance of the ordinances prescribed by it, I am engaged in thinking of the cause of that Soul, but, alas, I am unable to comprehend that cause, excellent as it is. I shall, however, according to the extent of my knowledge describe to you that eternal Soul and his Oneness and supreme greatness. The learned speak of him as the one Soul. That one eternal Being deserves the appellation of the great Supreme Purusha.

sn: एको हुताशो बहुधा समिध्यते एकः सूर्यस्तपसो योनिरेका। एको वायुर्बहुधा वाति लोके महोदधिश्चाम्भसां योनिरेकः। स्तं निर्गुणं पुरुषं चाविशन्ति।॥
en: Fire is an element, but it may be seen to burn up in a thousand places under thousand different circumstances. The Sun is one and single, but his rays extend over the wide universe. Penances are of various kinds, but they have one common origin whence they have originated. The Wind is one, but it blows in various forms in the world. The great Ocean is the one parent of all the waters in the world seen under various circumstances. Shorn of qualities, that one Soul is the universe shown in infinitude. Originating from him, the infinite universe enters into that one Soul again who is above all qualities, when the time for its destruction comes.

sn: हित्वा गुणमयं सर्वं कर्म हित्वा शुभाशुभम्। उभे सत्यानृते त्यक्त्वा एवं भवति निर्गुणः॥
en: By renouncing the consciousness of body and the senses, by renouncing all acts good and bad, by renouncing both truth and falsehood, one succeeds in divesting oneself of qualities.

sn: अचिन्त्यं चापि तं ज्ञात्वा भावसूक्ष्मं चतुश्यम्। विचरेद् योऽसमुन्नद्धः स गच्छेत् पुरुषं शुभम्॥
en: The person who realises that inconceivable Soul and comprehends his subtile existence in the four-fold of Aniruddha, Pradyumna, Sankarshana, and Vasudeva, and who, on account of such comprehension, acquires perfect tranquillity of heart, succeeds in entering into, and identifying himself with, that one auspicious Soul.

sn: एवं हि परमात्मानं केचिदिच्छन्ति पण्डिताः। एकात्मानं तथाऽऽत्मानमपरे ज्ञानचिन्तकाः॥
en: Some persons endued with learning speak of Him as the Supreme Soul. Others hold Him as the One Soul. A third class of learned men describe Him as the Soul.

sn: तत्र य: परमात्मा हि स नित्यं निर्गुणः स्मृतः। स हि नारायणो ज्ञेयः सर्वात्मा पुरुषो हि सः॥
en: The truth is that He who is the Supreme Soul is always shorn of qualities. He is Narayana. He is the Universal Soul, and He is the One Purusha. He is never affected by the fruits of deeds as the leaf of the lotus is never drenched by the water one may throw upon it.

sn: न लिप्यते फलैश्चापि पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा। कर्मात्मा त्वपरो योऽसौ मोक्षबन्धैः स युज्यते॥
en: The acting Soul is different. That Soul is sometimes engaged in acts and when it succeeds in renouncing acts acquires Liberation or identity with the Supreme Soul.

sn: स सप्तदशकेनापि राशिना युज्यते च सः। एवं बहुविधः प्रोक्तः पुरुषस्ते यथाक्रमम्॥
en: The acting Soul is endued with the seventeen possessions. Thus is it said that there are innumerable kinds of Souls in due order.

sn: यत् तत्कृत्स्नं लोकतन्त्रस्य धाम वेद्यं परं बोधनीयं स बोद्धा। मन्ता मन्तव्यं प्राशिता प्राशनीयं घ्राता प्रेयं स्पर्शिता स्पर्शनीयम्॥
en: In sooth, however, there is but one Soul. He is the abode of all the ordinances in the universe. He is the highest object of knowledge. He is at once the knower and the object to be known. He is at once the thinker and the object of thought. He is the eater and the food that is eaten. He is the smeller and the scent that is smelled. He is at once he that touches and the object that is touched.

sn: द्रष्टा द्रष्टव्यं श्राविता श्रावणीयं ज्ञाता ज्ञेयं सगुणं निर्गुणं च। यद् वै प्रोक्तं तात सम्यक् प्रधानं नित्यं चैतच्छाश्वतं चाव्ययं च॥
en: He is the agent that sees and the object that is seen. He is the hearer and the object that is heard. He is the conceiver and the object conceived. He is possessed of qualities and is free from them. He is that, O son, which is named Pradhana (Nature), enduring, eternal, and immutable.

sn: यद् वै सूते धातुराद्यं विधानं तद् वै विप्राः प्रवदन्तेऽनिरुद्धम्। यद् वै लोके वैदिकं कर्म साधु आशीर्युक्तं तद्धि तस्यैव भाव्यम्॥
en: He it is who creates the prime ordinance about Dhatri himself. Learned Brahmanas call Him by the name of Aniruddha. Whatever acts of excellent merits and blessings, originate in the world from the Vedas, have been caused by Him.

sn: देवाः सर्वे मुनयः साधु शान्तास्तं प्राग्वंशे यज्ञभागैर्यजन्ते। अहं ब्रह्मा आद्य ईशः प्रजानां तस्माज्जातस्त्वं च मत्तः प्रसूतः॥ मत्तो जगज्जङ्गमं स्थावरं च सर्वे वेदाः सरहस्या हि पुत्र॥
en: All the gods, and all the Rishis, gifted with tranquil souls, occupying their places on the altar, dedicate to Him the first share of their sacrificial offerings. I that am Brahman, the primeval master of all creatures, have come into being from Him, and you have sprung from me. From me has originated the universe with all its mobile and immobile creatures, and all the Vedas, O son, with their mysteries.

sn: चतुर्विभक्तः पुरुषः स क्रीडति यथेच्छति। एवं स भगवान् स्वेन ज्ञानेन प्रतिबोधितः॥
en: Divided into four parts, (viz., Aniruddha, Pradyumna, Sankarshana, and Vasudeva), He sports as He pleases. That illustrious and divine Lord is such, awakened by His Own knowledge.

sn: एतत् ते कथितं पुत्र यथावदनुपृच्छतः। सांख्यज्ञाने तथा योगे यथावदनुवर्णितम्॥
en: I have thus answered you, O son, according to your questions, and according to the way in which the matter is explained in the Sankhya System and the Yoga Philosophy."

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धर्माः पितामहेनोक्ता मोक्षधर्माश्रिताः शुभाः। धर्ममाश्रमिणां श्रेष्ठं वक्तुमर्हति मे भवान्।॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have, O grandfather, described to us the duties belonging to the Religion of Liberation. You should now tell us what the foremost duties are of persons belonging to the several modes of life.

sn: भीष्म उवाच सर्वत्र विहितो धर्मः स्वर्गः सत्यफलं महत्। बहुद्वारस्य धर्मस्य नेहास्ति विफला क्रिया॥
en: Bhishma said “The duties ordained with regard to every mode of life are capable, if well performed, of leading to heaven and the high fruit of Truth. Duties have many doors, and none of the practices enjoined by them fails to produce the desired effect.

sn: यस्मिन् यस्मिनश्च विषये यो यो याति विनिश्चयम्। स तमेवाभिजानाति नान्यं भरतसत्तम॥
en: Whoever adopts a class of duties with steady and firm faith, praises the duties adopted by him to the exclusion of the rest, О chief of Bharata's race.

sn: इमां च त्वं नरव्याघ्र श्रोतुमर्हसि मे कथाम्। पुरा शक्रस्य कथितां नारदेन महर्षिणा॥
en: This particular subject, however, which you wish me to describe was in days of yore the subject of conversation between the celestial Rishi Narada and the king of the gods, viz., Indra.

sn: महर्षिारदो राजन् सिद्धस्त्रैलोक्यसम्मतः। पर्येति क्रमशो लोकान् वायुरव्याहतो यथा॥
en: The great Rishi Narada, O king, adored of all the world, has been crowned with success. He wanders through all the worlds unimpeded, like the all-pervading wind itself.

sn: स कदाचिन्महेष्वास देवराजालयं गतः। सत्कृतश्च महेन्द्रेण प्रत्यासन्नगतोऽभवत्॥
en: Once upon a time he went to the abode of Indra. Duly honoured by the king of the gods, he sat close to his host.

sn: तं कृतक्षणमासीनं पर्यपृच्छच्छचीपतिः। महर्षे किंचिदाश्चर्यमस्ति दृष्टं त्वयानघ॥
en: Seeing him seated at his ease and free from exhaustion, the husband of Shachi addressed him, saying,-O great Rishi, is there any thing wonderful that has been seen by you, O sinless one?

sn: यदा त्वमपि विप्रर्षे त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्। जातकौतूहलो नित्यं सिद्धश्चरसि साक्षिवत्॥
en: O twice-born Rishi, crowned with ascetic success, you walk about moved by curiosity, through the universe of mobile and immobile objects, seeing all things.

sn: न ह्यस्त्यविदितं लोके देवर्षे तव किंचन। श्रुतं वाप्यनुभूतं वा दृष्टं वा कथयस्व मे॥
en: O celestial Rishi, there is nothing in the universe which you do not know. Do you tell me, therefore, of any wonderful event which you may have seen, or heard of, or felt.

sn: तस्मै राजन् सुरेन्द्राय नारदो वदतां वरः। आसीनायोपपन्नाय प्रोक्तवान् विपुलां कथाम्॥
