en: Thus questioned, Narada, that foremost of speakers, O king, then began to recite to the king of the gods the extensive history that follows.

sn: यथा येन च कल्पेन स तस्मै द्विजसत्तमः। कथां कथितवान् पृष्टस्तथा त्वमपि मे शृणु॥
en: Listen now to me as I recount that story which Narada told before Indra. I shall describe it in the same way in which the celestial Rishi had described it, and for the same purpose that he had in view.”

sn: भीष्म उवाच आसीत् किल नरश्रेष्ठ महापद्ये पुरोत्तमे। गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तीरे कश्चिद् विप्रः समाहितः।
en: Bhishma said "In a beautiful town called by the name of Mahapadma which was situate on the southern side of the river Ganga, there lived, O best of men, a Brahmana of concentrated Soul.

sn: सौम्यः सोमान्वये वेदे गताध्वा छिन्नसंशयः। धर्मनित्यो जितक्रोधो नित्यतृप्तो जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Born in the family of Atri, he was amiable by nature. All his doubts had been removed and he was well conversant with the path he was to follow. Ever practising the duties of religion, he had a complete hold over his passion. Always contented, he was the perfect master of his senses.

sn: तपःस्वाध्यायनिरतः सत्यः सज्जनसम्मतः। न्यायप्राप्तेन वित्तेन स्वेन शीलेन चान्वितः॥
en: Given to penances and the study of the Vedas, he was respected by all good men. He acquired riches by fair means and his conduct in all things tallied with the mode of life he led and the order to which he belonged.

sn: ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिविपुले सत्त्वाद्याश्रयसम्मिते। कुले महति विख्याते विशिष्टां वृत्तिमास्थितः॥
en: The family to which the belonging was large and famous. He had many kinsmen and relatives, and many children and wives. His conduct was always respectable and faultless.

sn: स पुत्रान् बहुलान् दृष्ट्वा विपुले कर्मणि स्थितः। कुलधर्माश्रितो राजन् धर्मचर्यास्थितोऽभवत्॥
en: Observing that he had many children, the Brahmana began to perform religious acts on a large scale. His religious observances, O king, were according to the customs of his own family.

sn: ततः स धर्मं वेदोक्तं तथा शास्त्रोक्तमेव चा शिष्टाचीर्णं च धर्मं च त्रिविधं चिन्त्य चेतसा॥
en: The Brahmana thought that there were three kinds of duties laid down for observances. There were, first, the duties ordained in the Vedas about the order in which he was born and the mode of life he was leading. There were, secondly, the duties sanctioned in the scriptures, viz., those especially called the Dharmashastras. And, thirdly, there were those duties that eminent and revered men of ancient times have followed, through not laid down either in the Vedas or the Scriptures.

sn: किन्नु मे स्याच्छुभं कृत्वा किं कृतं किं परायणम्। इत्येवं खिद्यते नित्यं न च याति विनिश्चयम्॥
en: Which of these duties should I follow? Which of thein, again, followed by me, are likely to produce my benefit? Which, indeed, should be my refuge? Thoughts like these always troubled him. He could not solve his doubts.

sn: तस्यैवं खिद्यमानस्य धर्मं परममास्थितः। कदाचिदतिथिः प्राप्तो ब्राह्मणः सुसमाहितः॥
en: While troubled with such thoughts, a Brahmana of concentrated soul and observant of every superior religion, came to his house as a guest.

sn: स तस्मै सक्रियां चक्रे क्रियायुक्तेन हेतुना। विश्रान्तं सुसमासीनमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The house-holder duly respected his guest according to those ordinances of worship that are laid down in the scriptures. Seeing his guest refreshed and seated at ease, the host addressed him in the following words.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच समुत्पन्नाभिधानोऽस्मि वाङ्माधुर्येण तेऽनघ। मित्रत्वमभिपन्नस्त्वं किंचिद् वक्ष्याम तच्छृणु॥
en: The Brahmana said Osinless One, I have become greatly attached to you on account of the sweetness of your conversation. You have become my friend. Listen to me, for I wish to say something to you.

sn: गृहस्थधर्मं विप्रेन्द्र कृत्वा पुत्रगतं त्वहम्। धर्म परमकं कुर्यां को हि मार्गो भवेद् द्विज॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, making over the duties of a house-holder to my son, I wish to satisfy the highest duties of man. What, O twice-born one, should be my path?

sn: अहमात्मानमास्थाय एक एवात्मनि स्थितिम्। कर्तुं काङ्क्षामि नेच्छामि बद्धः साधारणैर्गुणैः॥
en: Relying upon the soul, I wish to acquire existence in the One Soul. Alas, fettered by the bonds of attachment, I have not the heart to actually perform that task.

sn: यावदेतदतीतं मे वयः पुत्रफलाश्रितम्। तावदिच्छामि पाथेयमादातुं पारलौकिकम्॥
en: And since the best portion of my life has passed away as house-holder, I wish to devote the remaining part of my life in acquiring the means of defraying the expenses of my journey in respect of the time to come.

sn: अस्मिन् हि लोकसम्भारे परं पारमभीप्सतः। उत्पन्ना मे मतिरियं कुतो धर्ममयः प्लवः॥
en: The desire has originated in my mind of crossing the ocean of the world. Alas, whence shall I get the vessel of religion?

sn: संयुज्यमानानि निशम्य लोके निर्यात्यमानानि च सात्त्विकानि। दृष्ट्वा तु धर्मध्वजकेतुमाला प्रकीर्यमाणामुपरि प्रजानाम्॥ न मे मनो रज्यति भोगकाले दृष्ट्वा यतीन्प्रार्थयतः परत्र। तेनातिथे बुद्धिबलाश्रयेण धर्मेण धर्मे विनियुक्ष्व मां त्वम्॥
en: Hearing that the very gods are persecuted and made to suffer the fruits of their deeds, and seeing the rows of Yama's standards and flags floating over the heads of all creatures, my hearts fails to derive pleasure from the various objects of pleasure with which it comes into contact. Seeing also that the Yatis depend for their maintenance upon alms obtained in course of their rounds of mendicancy. I have no respect for the religion of the Yatis as well. O my reverend guest, do you, helped by that religion which is founded upon the basis of intelligence and reason, make me observe a particular course of duties and observances.

sn: सोऽतिथिर्वचनं तस्य श्रुत्वा धर्माभिभाषिणः। प्रोवाच वचनं श्लक्ष्णं प्राज्ञो मधुरया गिरा॥
en: Bhishma said, Gifted with great wisdom, the guest hearing this speech of his host which was consistent with virtue, said these sweet words in melodious voice.

sn: अतिथिरुवाच अहमप्यत्र मुह्यामि ममाप्येष मनोरथः। न च संनिश्चयं यामि बहुद्वारे त्रिविष्टपे॥
en: The Guest said I also am confounded about this subject. The same thought occupies my mind. I am unable to arrive at certainty of conclusion. Heaven has many doors.

sn: केचिन्मोक्षं प्रशंसन्ति केचिद् यज्ञफलं द्विजाः। वानप्रस्थाश्रयाः केचिद् गार्हस्थ्यं केचिदास्थिताः॥
en: There are some that speak highly of Liberation. Some twice-born persons praise the fruits acquired by the by the performance of sacrifices. Some there are who take refuge in the forest mode of life. Some, again, follow the domestic mode of life.

sn: राजधर्माश्रयं केचित् केचिदात्मफलाश्रयम्। गुरुधर्माक्षयं केचित्केचिद् वाक्संयमाश्रयम्॥
en: Some depend upon the merits attainable by an observance of the royal duties. Some depend upon the fruits of that culture which consists in the control of the soul, Some think that the merits originating from a dutiful obedience to preceptors and seniors efficacious. Some follow control of speech. are

sn: मातरं पितरं केचिच्छुश्रूषन्तो दिवं गताः। अहिंसया परे स्वर्ग सत्येन च तथा परे॥
en: Some, by waiting dutifully upon their mothers and fathers, have gone to heaven. Some have ascended to heaven by practising the duty of mercy, and some by practising Truth.

sn: आहवेऽभिमुखाः केचिनिहतास्त्रिदिवं गताः। केचिदुव्रतैः सिद्धाः स्वर्गमार्ग समाश्रिताः॥
en: Some rush to battle, and sacrificing their lives, have attained to heaven. Some again, acquiring success by practising the vow called Unccha, are following the path of heaven.

sn: केचिदध्ययने युक्ता वेदव्रतपराः शुभाः। बुद्धिमन्तो गताः स्वर्गं तुष्टात्मानो जितेन्द्रियाः॥
en: Some have given themselves up to the study of the Vedas. Endued with auspiciousness and wedded to such study, these men, gifted with intelligence, and tranquil souls, and having their senses under complete control, attain to heaven.

sn: आर्जवेनापरे युक्ता निहतानार्जवर्जनैः। ऋजवो नाकपृष्ठे वै शुद्धात्मानः प्रतिष्ठिताः॥
en: Others, marked by simplicity and truth, have been killed by wicked men. Gifted with pure souls, such men to truth and simplicity, have become respected inhabitants of heaven.

sn: एवं बहुविधैर्लोकधर्मद्वारैरनावृतैः। ममापि मतिराविग्ना मेघलेखेव वायुना॥
en: In this world, it is seen, that men go to heaven through a thousand doors of duty, all standing wide open. My understanding has been troubled by your question, like a cloud before the wind.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: अतिथिरुवाच उपदेशं तु ते विप्र करिष्येऽहं यथाक्रमम्। गुरुणा मे यथाख्यातमर्थतत्त्वं तु मे शृणु॥
en: The Guest said-For all that, O Brahmana, I shall try to instruct you duly. Listen to me as I recount to you what I have heard from my preceptor.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: यत्र पूर्वाभिसर्गे वै धर्मचक्र प्रवर्तितम्। नैमिषे गोमतीतीरे तत्र नागाह्वयं पुरम्॥
en: In that place whence in course of a former creation, the wheel of virtue was set in motion, in that forest which is known by the name of Naimisha, and which is situate on the banks of the Gomati, there is a city called Nagapura.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: समग्रैस्त्रिदशैस्तत्र इष्टमासीद् द्विजर्षभ। योन्द्रातिक्रमं चक्रे मान्धाता राजसत्तमः॥
en: There, in that region, all the gods, asscmbled a grand sacrifice. There the foremost of earthly kings, Mandhatri, defeated Indra, the king of the gods.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: कृताधिवासो धर्मात्मा तत्र चक्षुःश्रवा महान्। पद्मनाभो महानागः पद्म इत्येव विश्रुतः॥
en: A powerful Naga, of righteous soul, lives in the city that stands in that region. That great Naga is known by the name of Padmanabha or Padma.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: स वाचा कर्मणा चैव मनसा च द्विजर्षभ। प्रसादयति भूतानि त्रिविधे वर्त्मनि स्थितः॥
en: Walking in the three-fold path (of acts, knowledge, and adoration), he pleases all creatures in thought, word, and deed.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: साम्ना भेदेन दानेन दण्डेनेति चतुर्विधम्। विषमस्थं समस्थं च चक्षुर्ध्यानेन रक्षति॥
en: Thinking upon all things with great care, he protects the virtuous and punishes the wicked by following the four-fold policy on conciliation, creating dissensions, making gifts or giving bribes, and using force.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तमतिक्रम्य विधिना प्रष्टुमर्हसि कासितम्। स ते परमकं धर्मं न मिथ्या दर्शयिष्यति॥
en: Going there, you should put to him the questions you wish. He will show you truly what the highest religion is.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: स हि सर्वातिथि गो बुद्धिशास्त्रविशारदः। गुणैरनुपमैर्युक्तः समस्तैराभिकामिकैः॥
en: That Naga is always fond of guests. Gifted with great intelligence, he is well conversant with the Scriptures. He possesses all desirable virtues the like of which are not to be seen in any other person.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: प्रकृत्या नित्यसलिलो नित्यमध्ययने रतः। तपोदमाभ्यां संयुक्तो वृत्तेनानवरेण च॥
en: By nature he does those duties which are performed with or in water. He is given to the study of the Vedas. He is endued with penances and self-control. He has great riches.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: यज्वा दानपतिः क्षान्तो वृत्ते च परमे स्थितः। सत्यवागनसूयुश्च शीलवानियतेन्द्रियः।१०॥
en: He celebrates sacrifices, makes gifts, abstains from doing injury, and practises forgiveness. His conduct is in every way good. Truthful in speech and shorn of malice, his conduct is good and his senses are under proper control.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: शेषान्नभोक्ता वचनानुकूलो हितार्जवोत्कृष्टकृताकृतज्ञः। अवैरकृद् भूतहिते नियुक्तो गङ्गाह्रदाम्भोऽभिजनोपपन्नः॥
en: He eats after feeding all his guests and attendants. He is kind of speech. He has knowledge of what is good and what is simple and right and what is censurable. He takes an account of what he does and what he leaves undone. He never acts with hostility towards any one. He is always engaged in doing what is good to all creatures. He belongs to a family which is as pure and stainless as the water of a lake in the midst of the Ganges.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अतिभारोऽथ तस्यैव भारावतरणं महत्। पराश्वासकरं वाक्यमिदं मे भवतः श्रुतम्॥
en: I have heard these words of yours that are so consoling, with as much satisfaction as is experienced by a person heavily loaded when that load is taken off his head or shoulders.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: अध्वक्लान्तस्य शयनं स्थानक्लान्तस्य चासनम्। तृषितस्य च पानीयं क्षुधार्तस्य च भोजनम्॥ ईप्सितस्येव सम्प्राप्तिरन्नस्य समयेऽतिथेः। एषितस्यात्मनः काले वृद्धस्यैव सुतो यथा॥ मनसा चिन्तितस्येव प्रीतिस्निग्धस्य दर्शनम्। प्रह्लादयति मां वाक्यं भवता यदुदीरितम्॥ दत्तचक्षुरिवाकाशे पश्यामि विमृशामि च।
en: The pleasure which a traveller who has made a long journey on foot feels when he lies down on a bed, that which a person feels when he finds a seat after having stood for a long time for want of room, or that which is felt by a thirsty person when he finds a glass of cool water, or that which is felt by a hungry man when he finds good food set before him, or that which a guest feels when a dish of desirable food is placed before him at the proper time, or that which is felt by an old men when after long coveting he gets a son, or that which is felt by one when meeting with a dear friend or relative about whom he had become highly anxious, resembles that which I have been filled on account of these words given vent to by you.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: प्रज्ञानवचनाद्योऽयमुपदेशो हि मे कृतः॥ बाढमेवं करिष्यामि यथा मे भाषते भवान्।
en: Like a person with upturned look I have heard what has fallen from your lips and am thinking upon their meaning. With these wise words of yours, you have truly instructed me!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: इमां हि रजनीं साधो निवसस्व मया सह॥ प्रभाते यास्यति भवान् पर्याश्वस्तः सुखोषितः। असौ हि भगवान् सूर्यो मन्दरश्मिरवाङ्मुखः॥
en: Yes, I shall do what you have ordered me to do. You may go tomorrow carily in the morning, passing the night happily with me and removing your fatigue by such rest. See, the rays of the divine Sun have been partially dimmed and the god of day is going in his downward course!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततस्तेन कृतातिथ्यः सोऽतिथिः शत्रुसूदन। उवास किल तां रात्रिं सह तेन द्विजेन वै॥
en: Bhishma continued Hospitably treated by that Brahmana, the learned guest, O destroyer of enemies, passed that night in the company of his host.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: चतुर्थधर्मसंयुक्तं तयोः कथयतोस्तदा। व्यतीता सा निशा कृत्स्ना सुखेन दिवसोपमा॥
en: Indeed, both of them passed the night happily, conversing cheerfully with each other on the subject of the duties of the fourth mode of life, viz., Sannyasa. So engrossing was their conversation that the night passed away as if it were day.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ततः प्रभातसमये सोऽतिथिस्तेन पूजितः। ब्राह्मणेन यथाशक्त्य स्वकार्यमभिकाङ्क्षता॥
en: When morning came, the guest was adored with due rites by the Brahmana, who was bent upon doing what was considered by him to be beneficial for himself.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ततः स विप्रः कृतकर्मनिश्चयः कृताभ्यनुज्ञः स्वजनेन धर्मकृत्। यथोपदिष्टं भुजगेन्द्रसंश्रयं जगाम काले सुकृतैकनिश्चयः॥
en: Having dismissed his guest, the virtuous Brahmana, determined to achieve his purpose, took leave of his kinsmen and relatives, and started in due time for the abode of that foremost of Nagas, with heart firmly directed towards it.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: भीष्म उवाच स वनानि विचित्राणि तीर्थानि च सरांसि च। अभिगच्छन् क्रमेण सम कंचिन्मुनिमुपस्थितः॥
en: Proceeding by many charming forests and lakes and sacred waters, the Brahmana at last arrived at the asylum of a certain ascetic.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तं स तेन यथोद्दिष्टं नागं विप्रेण ब्राह्मणः। पर्यपृच्छद् यथान्यायं श्रुत्वैव च जगाम सः॥
en: Going there, he enquired of him, in proper words, about the Naga of whom he had heard from his guest, and instructed by him he pursued his journey.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: सोऽभिगम्य यथान्यायं नागायतनमर्थवित्। प्रोक्तवाहमस्मीति भोःशब्दालंकृतं वचः॥
en: With a clear idea of the object of his journey the Brahman then reached the house of the Naga. Entering it duly, he announced his arrival in proper words, saying,-Ho! who is there! I am a Brahmana come here as a guest!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तत् तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा रूपिणी धर्मवत्सला। दर्शयामास तं विप्रं नागपत्नी पतिव्रता॥
en: Hearing these words, the chaste wife of the Naga, endued with great beauty and devoted to the observance of all duties, showed herself.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: सा तस्मै विधिवत् पूजां चक्रे धर्मपरायणा। स्वागतेनागतं कृत्वा किं करोमीति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Always attentive to the duties of hospitality, she adored the guest with due rites, and welcoming him, said,-What can I do for you?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच विश्रान्तोऽभ्यर्चितश्चास्मि भवत्या श्लक्ष्णया गिरा। द्रष्टुमिच्छामि भवति देवं नागमनुत्तमम्॥
en: The Brahmana said O lady, I am sufficiently honoured by you with the sweet words you have said unto me. The fatigue of the journey has also been removed. I wish, O blessed lady, to see your excellent husband.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: एतद्धि परं कार्यमेतान्मे परमेप्सितम्। अनेन चार्थेनाम्यद्य सम्प्राप्त: पन्नागाश्रमम्॥
en: This is my great object. This is the one object of my desire. It is for this reason that I have come to-day to the house of the Naga your husband.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: नागभार्योवाच आर्यः सूर्यरथं वोढुं गतोऽसौ मासचारिकः। सप्ताष्टभिर्दिनैविप्र दर्शयिष्यत्यसंशयम्॥
en: The Wife of the Naga said Reverend Sir, my husband has gone to drag the car of the Sun for a month. O learned Brahmana, he return in fifteen days, and will, forsooth, appear before you.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: एतद्विदितमार्यस्य विवासकरणं तव। भर्तुर्भवतु किं चान्यत् क्रियतां तद् वदस्व मे॥
en: I have thus told you the reason of my husband's absence from home. Be that as it may, what else is there that I can do for you? Tell me this.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अनेन निश्चयेनाहं साध्वि सम्प्राप्तवानिह। प्रतीक्षन्नागमं देवि वत्स्याप्यस्मिन् महावने॥
en: The Brahmana said O chaste lady, I have come here with the object of seeing your husband. O reverend dame, I shall live in the adjacent forest, waiting for his return.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: सम्प्राप्तस्यैव चाव्यग्रमावेद्योऽहमिहागतः। ममाभिगमनं प्राप्तो वाच्यश्च वचनं त्वया॥
en: When your husband returns, do kindly tell him that I have arrived at this place actuated by the desire of seeing him. You should also inform me of his return when that event takes place.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: अहमप्यत्र वत्स्यामि गोमत्याः पुलिने शुभे। कालं परिमिताहारो यथोक्तं परिपालयन्॥
en: O blessed lady, I shall, till then, live on the banks of the Gomati, waiting for his return and living restricted diet.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ततः स विप्रस्तां नागी समाधाय पुनः पुनः। तदेव पुलिनं नद्याः प्रययौ ब्राह्मणर्षभः॥
en: Having said this repeatedly to the wife of the Naga, the foremost of Brahmanas went to the banks of the Gomati for living there till the time of Naga's return. O blessed lady, I shall, till then, live on the banks of the Gomati, waiting for his return and living restricted diet.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ततः स विप्रस्तां नागी समाधाय पुनः पुनः। तदेव पुलिनं नद्याः प्रययौ ब्राह्मणर्षभः॥
en: Having said this repeatedly to the wife of the Naga, the foremost of Brahmanas went to the banks of the Gomati for living there till the time of Naga's return.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: भीष्म उवाच अथ तेन नरश्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मणेन तपस्विना। निराहारेण वसता दुःखितास्ते भुजङ्गमाः॥
en: Bhishma said These Nagas of that city became greatly distressed when they saw that that Brahmana, devoted to the practice of penances, continued to live in the forest, entirely abstaining from food, in expectation of the arrival of the Naga king.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: सर्वे सम्भूय सहिता ह्यस्य नागस्य बान्धवाः। भ्रातरस्तनया भार्या ययुस्तं ब्राह्मणं प्रति॥
en: All the kinsmen and relatives of the great Naga, including his brothers and children and wife, assembling together, went to the spot where the Brahmana was living.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तेऽपश्यन् पुलिने तं वै विविक्ते नियतव्रतम्। समासीनं निराहारं द्विजं जप्यपरायणम्॥
en: Arrived on the banks of the Gomati, they saw that twice-born one seated in a solitary place, abstaining from food of every sort, observant all the while of excellent vows, and engaged in silently reciting certain Mantras.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ते सर्वे समतिक्रम्य विप्रमभ्यर्च्य चासकृत्। ऊचुर्वाक्यमसंदिग्धमातिथेयस्य बान्धवाः॥
en: Approaching the Brahmana and offering him due adorations, the kinsmen and relatives of the great Naga said to him these candid words.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: षष्ठो हि दिवसस्तेऽद्य प्राप्तस्येह तपोधन। न चाभिभाषसे किंचिदाहारं धर्मवत्सल॥
en: O Brahmana having asceticism, for your riches, that is the sixth day of your arrival here, but you speak no word about your food, O twice-born one you are devoted to virtue.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: अस्मानभिगतश्चासि वयं च त्वामुपस्थिताः। कार्यं चातिथ्यमस्माभिर्वयं सर्वे कुटुम्बिनः॥
en: You have come to us. We too are here in attendance upon you. It is absolutely necessary that we should do the duties of hospitality by you. We are all relations of the Naga king with whom you have business.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: मूलं फलं वा पर्ण वा पयो वा द्विजसत्तम्। आहारहेतोरन्नं वा भोक्तुमर्हसि ब्राह्मण॥
en: Roots or fruit, leaves, or water, or rice or meat, O best of Brahmanas, you should take for food.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: त्यक्ताहारेण भवता वने निवसता त्वया। बालवृद्धमिदं सर्वं पीड्यते धर्मसंकटात्॥
en: For your living in this forest under such circumstances of total abstention from food, the whole community of Nagas young and old is being aggrieved, since this your fast implies negligence on our part to discharge the duties of hospitality.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: न हि नो भ्रूणहा कश्चिज्जातापद्यनृतोऽपि वा। पूर्वाशी वा कुले ह्यस्मिन् देवतातिथिबन्धुषु॥
en: We have none amongst us who has been guilty of Brahmanicide. None of us has been guilty of Brahmanicide. None of us has ever lost a son immediately after birth. No one has been born in our race who has eaten before serving the gods or guests or relatives arrived at his house.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच उपदेशेन युष्माकमाहारोऽयं कृतो मया। द्विरूनं दशरात्रं वै नागस्यागमनं प्रति॥
en: The Brahmana said On account of these solicitations of you all, I may be considered to have broken my fast. Eight days remain when the king of the Nagas will return.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: यद्यष्टरात्रेऽतिक्रान्ते नागमिष्यति पन्नगः। तदाहारं करिष्यामि तन्निमित्तमिदं व्रतम्॥
en: If, on the expire of the eighth night hence, the king of the Nagas do not come back, I shall then break this fast by eating. Indeed, this vow of abstaining from all food that I am observing is on account of my respect for the Naga king.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: कर्तव्यो न च संतापो गम्यतां च यथागतम्। तन्निमित्तमिदं सर्वं नैतद् भेत्तसुमिहार्हथ॥
en: You should not grieve for what I am doing. Do you all return to whence you came. This my vow is on his account. You should not do anything on account of which this my vow may be broken.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ते तेन समनुज्ञाता ब्राह्मणेन भुजङ्गमाः। स्वमेव भवनं जग्मुरकृतार्था नरर्षभ॥
en: The assembled Nagas, thus addressed by Brahmana, were sent away by him, whereupon, O forcmost of men, they returned to their respective quarters.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: भीष्म उवाच अथ काले बहुतिथे पूर्णे प्राप्तो भुजङ्गमः। दत्ताभ्यनुज्ञः स्वं वेश्म कृतकर्मा विवस्वता॥
en: Bhishma said Upon the expire of full fifteen days, the Naga king (Padmanabha), having finished his task of dragging the car of the Sun and obtained the latter's permission, returned to his own house.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तं भार्याप्युपचक्राम पादशौचादिभिर्गुणैः। उपपन्नां च तां साध्वीं पन्नगः पर्यपृच्छत॥ अथ त्वमसि कल्याणि देवतातिथिपूजने। पूर्वमुक्तेन विधिना युक्ता युक्तेन मत्समम्॥
en: Seeing him return, his wife approached him quickly for washing his feet and dutifully satisfying other tasks of a similar nature. Having performed these tasks, she sat by his side. The Naga then, refreshed from fatigue, addressed his dutiful and chaste wife, saying, I hope, my dear wife, that during my absence you have not neglected to adore the gods and guests according to the instructions I gave you, and according to the ordinances laid down in the scriptures.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: न खल्वस्यकृतार्थेन स्त्रीबुद्ध्या मार्दवीकृता। मद्वियोगेन सुश्रोणि विमुक्ता धर्मसेतुना॥
en: I hope, without yielding to that impure understanding which is natural to persons of your sex, you have, during my absence from home, been firm in the observance of the duties of hospitality. I trust that you have not gone beyond the barriers of duty and virtue.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: नागभार्योवाच शिष्याणां गुरुशुश्रूषा विप्राणां वेदधारणम्। भृत्यानां स्वामिवचनं राज्ञो लोकानुपालनम्॥ सर्वभूतपरित्राणं क्षत्रधर्म इहोच्यते। वैश्यानां यज्ञसंवृत्तिरातिथेयसमन्विता॥
en: The duty of disciples is to wait respectfully upon their preceptor for doing his bidding; that of Brahmanas is to study the Vedas and bear them in memory; that of servants is to obey the commands of their masters; that of the king is to protect his people by supporting the good and punishing the wicked. It is said that the duties of a Kshatriya are the protection of all creatures from wrong and oppression.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: विप्रक्षत्रियवैश्यानां शुश्रूषा शूद्रकर्म तत्। गृहस्थधर्मो नागेन्द्र सर्वभूतहितैषिता॥
en: The duty of the Shudra is to serve with humility persons of the twice-born orders, viz., Brahmanas and Kshatriyas and Vaishyas. The religion of the house-holder, O king of the Nagas, consists in doing good to all creatures.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: नियताहारता नित्यं व्रतचर्या यथाक्रमम्। धर्मो हि धर्मसम्बन्धादिन्द्रियाणां विशेषतः॥
en: Frugality of fare and observance of vows in due order, form merit (for persons of all classes) on account of the connection that exists between the senses and the duties religion.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: अहं कस्य कुतो वापि कः को मे ह भवेदिति। प्रयोजनमतिनित्यमेवं मोक्षाश्रमे वसेत्॥
en: Who am I? Whence have I come? What are others to me and what am I to others?—these are the thoughts to which the mind should ever be given by him who leads that course of life which leads to Liberation.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: पतिव्रतात्वं भार्यायाः परमो धर्म उच्यते। तवोपदेशान्नागेन्द्र तच्च तत्त्वेन वेद्मि वै॥
en: Chastity and obedience to the husband from the highest duty of wife. Through your instruction, O king of Nagas, I have learnt this well.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: साहं धर्मं विजानन्ती धर्मनित्ये त्वयि स्थिते। सत्पथं कथमुत्सृज्य यास्यामि विपथं पथः॥
en: I, therefore, that am well versed in my duty, and that have you for my husband,—you who are devoted to virtue,-O, why shall I, falling off from the path of duty, tread along the path of disobedience and sin?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: देवतानां महाभाग धर्मचर्या न हीयते। अतिथीनां च सत्कारे नित्युक्तास्म्यतन्द्रिता।॥
en: During your absence from home, the adorations to the gods have not suffered in any respect. I have also, without the slightest negligence, performed the duties of hospitality towards persons arrived as guests in your house.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: सप्ताष्टदिवसास्त्वद्य विप्रस्येहागतस्य वै। तच्च कार्यं न मे ख्याति दर्शनं तव काङ्क्षति॥
en: Fifteen days ago a Brahmana has come here. He has not given out his object to me. He wishes to see you.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: गोमत्यास्त्वेष पुलिने त्वदर्शनसमुत्सुकः। आसीनो वर्तयन् ब्रह्म ब्राह्मणः संशितव्रतः॥
en: Living on the banks of the Gomati, he is anxiously expecting your return. Of rigid vows, that Brahmana is sitting there, engaged in the recitation of Brahma.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: अहं त्वनेन नागेन्द्र सत्यपूर्वं समाहिता। प्रस्थाप्यो मत्सकाशं स सम्प्राप्तो भुजगोत्तमः॥
en: O king of the Nagas, I have made a promise to him that I would send you to him as soon as you would return to your house.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा महाप्राज्ञ तत्र गन्तुं त्वमर्हसि। दातुमर्हसि वा तस्य दर्शनं दर्शनश्रवः॥
en: Hearing these words of men, O best of Nagas, you should go there. O you who hear with your eyes, you should great to that twiceborn person the object that has brought him here.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: नाग उवाच अथ ब्राह्मणरूपेण कं तं समनुपश्यसि। मानुषं केवलं विप्रं देवं वाथ शुचिस्मिते॥
en: The Naga said O you of sweet smiles, for whom have you taken that Brahmana? Is he really a human being or is he some god that has come here in the disguise of a Brahmana?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: को हि मां मानुषः शक्तो द्रष्टकामो यशस्विनि। संदर्शनरुचिर्वाक्यमाज्ञापूर्वं वदिष्यति॥
en: O you of great fame, who is there ainong men who would be desirous of seeing are or that would be competent for the purpose? Can a human being, desiring to see me, leave such a command with you about sending me to him for paying him a visit at the place where he is living?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: सुरासुरगणानां च देवर्षीणां च भाविनि। ननु नागा महावीर्याः सौरसेयास्तरस्विनः॥
en: Amongst the gods and Asuras and celestial Rishis, O amiable lady, the Nagas are endued with great energy. Having great speed, they are endued again with excellent fragrance.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: वन्दनीयाश्च वरदा वयमप्यनुयायिनः। मनुष्याणां विशेषेण नावेक्ष्या इति मे मतिः॥
en: They derseve to be adored. They are capable of granting boons. Indeed, we too deserve to be followed by others. I tell you, O lady, that we cannot be seen by human beings.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: नागभार्योवाच आर्जवेन विजानामि नासौ देवोऽनिलाशन। एकं तस्मिन् विजानामि भक्तिमानतिरोषण॥
en: Judging by his simplicity and candour I know that that Brahmana is not any god who lives on air. O you of great anger, I also know this, viz., that he respects you with all his heart.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: स हि कार्यान्तराकाङ्क्षी जलेप्सुः स्तोकको यथा। वर्ष वर्षप्रियः पक्षी दर्शनं तव कासति॥
en: He seeks the accomplishment of some object that depends upon your help. As the bird called Chataka, which if fond of rain, waits in earnest expectation of a shower, so is that Brahmana waiting is expectation of a meeting with you.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: हित्वा त्वद्दर्शनं किंचिद् विनं न प्रतिपालयेत्। तुल्यऽप्याभिजने जातो न कश्चित् पर्युपासते॥
en: Let no calamity befall him on account of his inability to obtain a sight of you. No person born like you in a respectable family can be considered to remain respectable by neglecting a guest arrived at his house.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तद्रोषं सहजं त्यक्त्वा त्वमेनं द्रष्टुमर्हसि। आशाच्छेदेन तस्याद्य नात्मानं दग्धुमर्हसि॥
en: Renouncing that anger which is natural to you, you should go and see that Brahmana. You should not allows yourself to be consumed by disappointing that Brahmana.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: आशया ह्यभिपन्नानामकृत्वाचप्रमार्जनम्। राजा वा राजपुत्रो वा भ्रूणहत्यैव युज्यते॥
en: The king or the prince, by refusing to wipe the tears of persons who come to him from hopes of relief, commits the sin of foeticide. By abstaining from speech one acquire wisdom.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: मौने ज्ञानफलावाप्तिर्दानेन च यशो महत्। वाग्मित्वं सत्यवाक्येन परत्र च महीयते॥
en: By practising gifts one acquires great fame. By observing truthfulness of speech, one acquire the fit of eloquence and comes to be respected in heaven.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: भूप्रदानेन च गतिं लभत्याश्रमसम्मिताम्। न्याय्यस्यार्थस्य सम्प्राप्तिं कृत्वा फलमुपाश्नुते॥
en: By giving away land one acquires that high end which is ordained for Rishis leading the sacred mode of life. By acquiring riches through fair means one succeeds in acquiring many desirable fruits.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: अभिप्रेतामसंश्लिष्टां कृत्वा चात्महितां क्रियाम्। न याति निरयं कश्चिदिति धर्मविदो विदुः॥
en: By doing in full what is good for oneself, one can avoid going to hell. This is what the righteous say.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: नाग उवाच अभिमानैर्न मानो मे जातिदोषेण वै महान्। रोषः संकल्पजः साध्वि दग्धो वागग्निना त्वया॥
en: The Naga said I had no arrogance. On account, however, of my birth, my pride was considerable. Of anger which is born of desire, O blessed lady, I have none. It has all been consumed by the fire of your excellent instructions.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: न च रोषादहं साध्वि पश्येयमधिकं तमः। तस्य वक्तव्यतां यान्ति विशेषेण भुजङ्गमाः॥
en: I do not see, O blessed lady, any darkness that is thicker than anger. On account, however of the Nagas having excess of anger, they have become objects of reproach with all persons.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: रोषस्य हि वशं गत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्। तथा शक्रप्रतिस्पर्धी हतो रामेण संयुगे॥
en: By yielding to the influence of anger, the ten-headed Ravan of great prowess, became the rival Shakra and was for that reason killed by Rama in battle.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: अन्तःपुरगतं वत्सं श्रुत्वा रामेण निर्हतम्। धर्षणारोषसंविग्नाः कार्तवीर्यसुता हताः॥
en: Hearing that the Rishi Rama of Bhrigu's race had entered the inner apartments of their palace for bringing away the calf of the Homa cow of his father, the sons of Karttavirya, yielding to anger, took such entry as an insult to their royal house, and as the result thereof, they met with destruction at the hands of Rama.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: जामदग्न्येन रामेण सहस्रनयनोपमः। संयुगे निहतो रोषात् कार्तवीर्यो महाबलः॥
en: Indeed, Karttavirya of great strength, resembling the thousand-eyed Indra himself, on account of his having yielded to anger, was killed in battle by Rama of Jamadagni's race.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तदेष तपसां शत्रुः श्रेयसां विनिपातकः। निगृहीतो मया रोषः श्रुत्वैवं वचनं तव॥
en: Verily, O amiable lady, at your words I have controlled my anger, that enemy of penances, that destroyer of all that is beneficial for himself.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: आत्मानं च विशेषेण प्रशंसाम्यनपायिनी। यस्य मे त्वं विशालाक्षि भार्या गुणसमन्विता॥
en: I praise my own self greatly since, O largeeyed one, I am fortunate enough to have you as my wife,-you who are possessed of every virtue and who have inexhaustible merits.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: एष तत्रैव गच्छामि यत्र तिष्ठत्यसौ द्विजः। सर्वथा चोक्तवान् वाक्यं स कृतार्थः प्रयास्यति॥
en: I shall now proceed to that spot where the Brahmana is living. I shall certainly address that Brahmana in proper words, and he shall certainly go hence, his wishes being done.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: भीष्म उवाच स पन्नगपतिस्तत्र प्रययौ ब्राह्मणं प्रति। तमेव मनसा ध्यायन् कार्यवत्तां विचारयन्॥
en: Bhishma said Having said these words to his dear wife, the king of the Nagas proceeded to in exposition of an interview with him. As wondered as to that the business could be that had brought him to the Naga city.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तमतिक्रम्य नागेन्द्रो मतिमान् स नरेश्वर। प्रोवाच मधुरं वाक्यं प्रकृत्या धर्मवत्सलः॥ भो भो क्षाम्याभिभाषे त्वां न रोषं कर्तुमर्हसि। इह त्वमभिसम्प्राप्तः कस्यार्थे किं प्रयोजनम्॥
en: Arrived before him, O king of men, that foremost of Nagas, devoted by his nature to virtue, addressed his guest in sweet words, saying,-0 Brahmana, do not give way to anger. I address you in peace! Do not be angry! For whom have you come here? What is your object?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: आभिमुख्यादभिक्रम्य स्नेहात् पृच्छामि ते द्विजा विविक्ते गोमतीतीरे कं वा त्वं पर्युपाससे॥
en: Coming to you, I ask you in love, O twiceborn one! Whom do you worship in this retired spot on the banks of the Gomati?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच धर्मारण्यं हि मां विद्धि नागं द्रष्टुमिहागतम्। पद्मनाभं द्विजश्रेष्ठ तत्र मे कार्यमाहितम्॥
en: The Brahmana said Know that my name is Dharmaranya; and that I have come here for seeing the Naga Padamanabha, O foremost O all twice-born persons! With him I have some business!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तस्य चाहमसांनिध्ये श्रुतवानस्मि तं गतम्। स्वजनात् तं प्रतीक्षामि पर्जन्यमिव कर्षकः॥
en: I have heard that he is not at home and that, therefore, I am not now near his present habitation. Like a Chataka waiting in expectation of the clouds, I am waiting for him whom I consider as dear to me!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तस्य चाक्लेशकरणं स्वस्तिकारसमाहितम्। आवर्तयामि तद् ब्रह्म योगयुक्तो निरामयः॥
en: For removing all evil from him and bringing about what is good to him, I am engaged in reciting the Vedas till he comes and am in Yoga and passing my time happily!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: नाग उवाच अहो कल्याणवृत्तस्त्वं साधुः सज्जनवत्सलः। अवाच्यस्त्वं महाभाग परं स्नेहेन पश्यसि॥
en: The Naga said-Indeed, your conduct is highly good. Pious you are and devoted to the well being of all pious persons, O highly blessed Brahmana, every praise is due to you? You see the Naga with eyes of affection.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: अहं स नागो विप्रर्षे यथा मां विन्दते भवान्। आज्ञापय यथा स्वैरं किं करोमि प्रियं तव॥
en: I am that Naga, O learned Rishi, whom you seek! Do you order me, as you wish, in respect of what is agreeable to you and what I should do for you!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: भवन्तं स्वजनादस्मि सम्प्राप्तं श्रुतवानहम्। अतस्त्वां स्वयमेवाहं द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो द्विज॥
en: Having heard from any wife that you are here, I have to come this spot, O twice-born one, for seeing you!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: सम्प्राप्तश्च भवानद्य कृतार्थः प्रतियास्यति। विस्रब्यो मां द्विजश्रेष्ठ विषये योक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: When you come here, you are certain to return hence with your object fulfilled. You should, O foremost of twice-born persons, cmploy me to any task with all confidence!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: वयं हि भवता सर्वे गुणक्रीता विशेषतः। यस्त्वमात्महितं त्यक्त्वा मामेवेहानुरुध्यसे॥
en: All of us have certainly been purchased by you with your merits, since you disregarding what is for your own good, has employed your time in seeking the well-being of ourselves!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच आगतोऽहं महाभाग तव दर्शनलालसः। कंचिदर्थमनर्थज्ञः प्रष्टुकामो भुजङ्गम्॥
en: The Brahmana said O highly blessed Naga, I have come here, actuated by the desire of seeing you! I have come here, ignorant as I am with all things, for asking you about something, O snake!

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: अहमात्मानमात्मस्थो मार्गमाणोऽऽत्मनो गतिम्। वासार्थिनं महाप्रज्ञं चलच्चित्तमुपास्मि ह॥
en: Relying on the Soul, I wish to attain to the Supreme Soul which is the end of the Individual Soul. I am neither attached to, nor dissociated from, the world.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: प्रकाशितस्त्वं स्वगुणैर्यशोगर्भगभस्तिभिः। शशाङ्ककरसंस्पर्श«द्यैरात्मप्रकाशितैः॥
en: You shine with the effulgence of your own merits covered by fame,-with an effulgence that is as sweet as that of the moon.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तस्य मे प्रश्नमुत्पन्नं छिन्धि त्वमनिलाशन। पश्चात् कार्यं वदिष्यामि श्रोतुमर्हति तद् भवान्॥
en: O you who subsist on air only, do you first answer a question that I wish to put to you! Afterwards I shall inform you of the object with which I have come here.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ब्राह्मणः उवाच विवस्वतो गच्छति पर्ययेण वोढुं भवांस्तं रथमेकचक्रम्। आश्चर्यभूतं यदि तत्र किंचिद् दृष्टं त्वया शंसितुमर्हसि त्वम्॥
en: The Brahmana said You go for dragging the one-wheeled car of Vivasvat according to your turn. You should describe to me anything wonderful that you may have seen in those regions through which you pass.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: नाग उवाच आश्चर्याणामनेकानां प्रतिष्ठा भगवान् रविः। यतो भूताः प्रवर्तन्ते सर्वे त्रैलोक्यसम्मताः॥
en: The Naga said, The divine Sun is the refuge or home of numberless wonders. All the creatures that inhabit the three worlds have sprung from the Sun.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: यस्य रश्मिसहस्रेषु शाखास्विव विहंगमाः। वसन्त्याश्रित्य मुनयः संसिद्धा दैवतैः सह॥
en: Numberless Munis, crowned with ascetic success, together with all the gods, live in the rays of the Sun like birds perching on the branches of trees.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: यतो वायुर्विनिःसृत्य सूर्यरश्म्याश्रितो महान्। विजृम्भत्यम्बरे तत्र किमाश्चार्यमतः परम्॥
en: What, again, can be more wonderful than this that the powerful Wind, emanating from the Sun, takes refuge in his rays and thence yawns over universe?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: विभज्य तं तु विप्रर्षे प्रजानां हितकाम्यया। तोयं सृजति वर्षासु किमाश्चर्यमत: परम्॥
en: What can be more wonderful than this, O twice-born Rishi, that the Sun, dividing the Wind into many parts from desire of doing good to all creatures, creates rain that falls in the rain sea on?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: यस्य मण्डलमध्यस्थो महात्मा परमत्विषा। दीप्तः समीक्षते लोकान् किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्॥
en: What can be more wonderful than this the Supreme Soul, from within the solar disc, himself bathed in burning effulgence, looks upon the universe?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: शुक्रो नामासितः पादो यश्च वारिधरोऽम्बरे। तोयं सृजति वर्षासु किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्॥
en: What can be more wonderful than this that the Sun has a black ray which, changes itself into clouds charged with rain and pours showers of rain when the season comes?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: योऽष्टमासांस्तु शुचिना किरणेनोक्षितं पयः। प्रत्यादत्ते पुनः काले किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्॥
en: What can be more wonderful than this that drinking up for eight months the rain he pours down he pours it down again in the rainy season.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: यस्य तेजोविशेषेषु स्वयमात्मा प्रतिष्ठितः। यतो बीजं मही चेयं धार्यते सचराचरा॥
en: In certain rays of the Sun, the Soul of the universe said to live. From Him is the seed of all things, and it is He that supports the earth with all her mobile and immobile creatures.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: यत्र देवो महाबाहुः शाश्वतः पुरुषोत्तमः। अनादिनिधनो विप्र किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्॥
en: What can be more wonderful, O Brahmana, than this, that the foremost of Purushas, eternal and mighty-armed, endued with great effulgence, eternal, and without beginning and without end, lives in the Sun?

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: आश्चर्याणामिवाश्चर्यमिदमेकं तु मे शृणु। विमले यन्मया दृष्टमम्बरे सूर्यसंश्रयात्॥
en: Listen, however, to one thing I shall tell you now. It is the wonder of wonders. I have seen it in the clear sky, on account of my nearless to the Sun.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: पुरा मध्याह्नसमये लोकांस्तपति भास्करे। प्रतदित्यप्रतीकाशः सर्वतः समदृश्यत्॥
en: In former times, one day at the hour of noon, while the Sun was shining in all his glory and giving heat to everything we saw a Being coming towards the Sun, who seemed to shine with effulgence that was equal to that of the Sun himself.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: स लोकांस्तेजसा सर्वान् स्वभासा निर्विभासयन्। आदित्याभिमुखोऽभ्येति गगनं पाटयन्निव॥
en: Making all the worlds shine up with his glory and filling them with his energy, he came, as I have already told you towards the Sun, rending the sky, as it were, for passing through it.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: हुताहुतिरिव ज्योतिर्व्याप्य तेजोमरीचिभिः। अनिर्देश्येन रूपेण द्वितीय इव भास्करः॥
en: The rays that came out of his body seemed to resemble the blazing effulgence of libations of clarified butter poured into the sacrificial fire. On account of his energy and splendour he could not he looked at. His form seemed to be indescribable. Indeed, he appeared to us to be like a second Sun.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तस्याभिगमनप्राप्ती हस्तौ दत्तौ विवस्वता। तेनापि दक्षिणो हस्तो दत्तः प्रत्यर्चितार्थिना॥
en: As soon as he came near the Sun extended his two hands. For honouring the Sun in return, he also extended his right-hand.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ततो भित्त्वैव गगनं प्रविष्टो रश्मिमण्डलम्। एकीभूतं च तत् तेजः क्षणेनादित्यतां गतम्॥
en: The latter the then, piercing through the sky, entered into the Sun's disc. Mingling then with the Sun's energy, he seemed to be changed into the Sun's self.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: तत्र नः संशयो जातस्तयोस्तेजः समागमे। अनयोः को भवेत् सूर्यो रथस्थो योऽयमागतः॥
en: When the two energies thus met together, we were so confounded that we could not any longer make out which was which. Indeed, we could not make out who was the Sun whom we bore on his car, and who was Being that we had seen coming through the sky.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ते वयं जातसंदेहाः पर्यपृच्छामहे रविम्। क एष दिवमाक्रम्य गतः सूर्य इवापरः॥
en: Filled with confusion, we then addressed the Sun, saying,-O illustrious one, who is this Being who has mixed himself with you and has been charged into your second self.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: सूर्य उवाच नैष देवोऽनिलसखो नासुरो न च पन्नगः। उच्छवृत्तिव्रते सिद्धो मुनिरेव दिवं गतः॥
en: This Being is not the god of the fire, he is not an Asura. Nor is he a Naga. he is a Brahmana who has attained to heaven on account of his having been crowned with success in the observance of the vow called Unccha.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: एष मूलफलाहारः शीर्णपर्णाशनस्तथा। अभक्षो वायुभक्षश्च आसीद् विप्रः समाहितः॥
en: This person had lived upon fruit and roots and upon the fallen leaves of trees. He had sometimes lived upon water, and sometimes upon air alone, passing his devas with concentrated soul.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: भवश्चानेन विप्रेण संहिताभिरभिष्टुतः। स्वर्गद्वारे कृतोद्योगो येनासौ त्रिदिवं गतः॥
en: The god Mahadeva had been propitiated by him with constant recitation of the Samhitas. he had tried to perform those deeds which lead to heaven. Through the merits of those acts he had now attained to heaven.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: असङ्गतिरनाकाङ्क्षी नित्यमुच्छशिलाशनः। सर्वभूतहिते युक्त एष विप्रो भुजङ्गम॥
en: Without riches and without desire of any king he had observed the vow called Unccha with regard to his food. This learned Brahmana, ye Nagas, had been devoted to the good of all creatures.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: न हि देवा न गन्धर्वा नासुरा न च पन्नगाः। प्रभवन्तीह भूतानां प्राप्तानामुत्तमां गतिम्॥ एतदेवंविधं दृष्टमाश्चर्यं तत्र मे द्विज।
en: Neither gods, nor Gandharvas, nor Asuras, nor Nagas, can be considered as superior to those creatures who attain to this excellent end of coming into the solar disc. Even such, 0 twice-born one, was the wonderful incident that I saw on that occasion.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: संसिद्धो मानुष: कामं योऽसौ सिद्धगतिं गतः। सूर्येण सहितो ब्रह्मन् पृथिवीं परिवर्तते॥
en: That Brahmana, who was crowned with success by the observance of the Unccha vow and who thus obtained an end that persons crowned with ascetic success gain. to this day, Otwice-born one, goes round the Earth, staying in the disc of the Sun. crowned with ascetic success gain. to this day, Otwice-born one, goes round the Earth, staying in the disc of the Sun.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच आश्चर्यं नात्र संदेहः सुप्रीतोऽस्मि भुजङ्गमा अन्वर्थोपगतैर्वाक्यैः पन्थानं चास्मि दर्शितः॥
en: Forsooth, this is highly wonderful, ONaga. I have been highly pleased by listening to you. By these words of yours that are fraught with subtile meaning, you have shown me the way I am to follow.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि साधो भुजगसत्तम। स्मरणीयोऽस्मि भवता सम्प्रेषणनियोजनैः॥
en: Blessed be you, I wish to depart hence, O best of Nagas. You should remember me now and then and enquire after me sending your servants.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: नाग उवाच अनुक्त्वा हृद्गतं कार्यं क्वेदानीं प्रस्थितौ भवान्। उच्यदां द्विज यत् कार्यं यदर्थं त्वमिहागतः॥
en: The Naga said The object that brought you here is still in your mind, for you have not as yet given it out to me. Where then will you go? Tell me, O twice-born one, what should be done by me, and what that object is which brought you here.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: उक्तानुक्ते कृते कार्ये मामामन्त्र्य द्विजर्षभ। मया प्रत्यभ्यनुज्ञातस्ततो यास्यसि सुव्रत॥
en: After the fulfilment of your business, whatever it is, expressed or unexpressed in speech, you may depart, O foremost of twiceborn persons, saluting me and dismissed by me cheerfully, O you of excellent vows.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: न हि मां केवलं दृष्ट्वा त्यक्त्वा प्रणयवानिह। गन्तुमर्हसि विप्रर्षे वृक्षमूलगतो यथा॥
en: You have conceived a friendship for me. O twice-born Rishi, you should not depart from this place after having only seen me, yourself sitting under the shade of this tree.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: त्वयि चाहं द्विजश्रेष्ठ भवान् मयि न संशयः। लोकोऽयं भवतः सर्वः का चिन्ता मयि तेऽनघ॥
en: You have become dear to me and I have become dear to you. All the persons in this city are yours. What objection then, O sinless one, you have to pass some time in my house.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच एवमेतन्महाप्राज्ञ विदितात्मन् भुजङ्गम। नातिक्रान्तास्त्वया देवाः सर्वथै व यथातथम्॥
en: The Brahmana said It is even so, O you of great wisdom, O Naga, who have acquired a knowledge of the Soul. It is very true that the gods are not superior to you in any respect.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: स एव त्वं स एवाहं योऽहं स तु भवानपि। अहं भवांश्च भूतानि सर्वे यत्र गताः सदा॥
en: He that is yourself is varily myself, as that is myself is truly yourself. Myself, yourself, and all other creatures, shall all have to enter into the Supreme Soul.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: आसीत् तु मे भोगपते संशयः पुण्यसंचये। सोऽहमुच्छव्रतं साधो चरिष्याम्यर्थसाधनम्॥
en: A doubt had entered my mind, O king of Nagas, in the matter of the best means for acquiring virtue or merit. That doubt has been removed by your discourse, for I have learnt the value of the Unccha vow.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma
sn: एष मे निश्चयः साधो कृतं कारणमुत्तमम्। आमन्त्रयामि भद्रं ते कृतार्थोऽस्मि भुजङ्गम॥
en: I shall hence follow that yow which is so very efficacious in producing beneficial consequences. That, O blessed one, has become my certain conclusion now, based on good reasons. I take your leave. Blessing to you. My object has been done, ONaga.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma.
sn: भीष्म उवाच स चामव्योरगश्रेष्ठं ब्राह्मणः कृतनिश्चयः। दीक्षाकाङ्क्षी तदा राजश्च्यवनं भार्गवं श्रितः।१॥
en: Bhishma said Having saluted that foremost of Nagas in this way, the Brahmana, firmly resolved to follow the Unccha mode of life, went O king, to Chyavana of Bhrigu's race, from desire of being formally instructed and initiated in that VOW.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma.
sn: स तेन कृतसंस्कारो धर्ममेवाधितस्थिवान्। तथैव च कथामेतां राजन् कथितवांस्तदा॥ भार्गवेणापि राजेन्द्र जनकस्य निवेशने। कथैषा कथिता पुण्या नारदाय महात्मने॥
en: Chyavana performed the initiating rites of the Brahmana and formally initiated him into the Unccha mode of life. The son of Bhrigu,.0 king, recited this history to king Janaka in his palace. King Janaka, in his turn, described it to the celestial Rishi Narada of high soul.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma.
sn: नारदेनापि राजेन्द्र देवेन्द्रस्य निवेशने। कथिता भरतश्रेष्ठ पृष्टेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा॥
en: The celestial Rishi Narada too of pure acts going on one occasion to the house of Indra the king of the gods, gave to Indra this history upon being asked by him.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma.
sn: देवराजेन च पुरा कथितैषा कथा शुभा। समस्तेभ्यः प्रशस्तेभ्यो विप्रेभ्यो वसुधाधिप।॥
en: The king of the gods, having acquired it thus from Narada, recited this blessed history to an assembly of all the foremost Brahmanas, O king.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma.
sn: यदा च मम रामेण युद्धमासीत् सुदारुणम्। वसुभिश्च तदा राजन् कथेयं कथिता मम॥
en: On the occasion, again, of my dreadful fight with Rama of Bhrigu's race the celestial Vasus, O king, had recited this history.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma.
sn: पृच्छमानाय तत्त्वेन मया चैवोत्तमा तव। कथेयं कथिता पुण्या धा धर्मभृतां वर॥
en: Asked by you, O foremost of pious men, I have recited this history that is excellent and sacred and endued with great merit.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma.
sn: यदयं परमो धर्मो यन्मां पृच्छसि भारत। आसीद् धीरो ह्यनाकासी धर्मार्थकरणे नृप॥
en: You had asked me about that which forms the highest duty, O king. This history is my answer to your query. A brave men he was, O king. This history is my answer to your query. A brave man he was, O king, who followed the practice of the Unccha vow in this way, without desiring for any fruit.

description: The story of the Naga king Padma.
sn: स च किल कृतनिश्चयो द्विजो भुजगपतिप्रतिदेशितात्मकृत्यः यमनियमसहो वनान्तरं परिगणितोञ्छशिलाशनः प्रविष्टः॥
en: Firmly resolved, that Brahmana, instructed by the king of Nagas in this way about his duty, followed the practice of restraint and self control, an living upon such food as the allowed the Uccha vow, proceeded to another forest.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वती व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्।।
en: Having saluted Narayana and Nara the best of male beings as also Sarasvati, the goddess of learning let us cry success.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: युष्ठिर उवाच शमो बहुविधाकारः सूक्ष्म उक्तः पितामह। न च मे हृदये शान्तिरस्ति श्रुत्वेदमीदृशम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, peace of mind has been described to be subtile and of various forms. I have heard all your discourses, but have not still been able to acquire tranquillity of mind.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: अस्मिन्नर्थे बहुविधा शान्तिरुक्ता पितामह। स्वकृते का नु शान्तिः स्याच्छमाद् बहुविधादपि॥
en: Various means of quieting the mind have been described by you, O sire, but how can peace of mind be acquired from only a knowledge of the different sorts of tranquillity, when I myself have been the means of bringing all this about?

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: शराचितशरीरं हि तीव्रव्रणमुदीक्ष्य च। शर्म नोपलभे वीर दुष्कृतान्येव चिन्तयन्॥
en: Seeing your body covered with arrows and bad sores, I cannot get, O hero, any peace of mind. thinking of the evils I have done.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: रुधिरेणावसिक्ताङ्गं प्रस्रवन्तं यथाचलम्। त्वां दृष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्र सीदे वर्षास्विवाम्बुजम्॥
en: Seeing your body, O bravest of the brave, covered with blood, like a hill covered with water from its springs, I am perishing with grief as the lotus in the rainy season.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: अतः कष्टतरं किं नु मत्कृते यत् पितामहः। इमामवस्थां गमितः प्रत्यमित्रै रणाजिरे॥
en: What can be more painful than this, that, for me, you, O grandfather have been reduced to this condition by my people fighting against their enemies on the battlefield.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: तथा चान्ये नृपतयः सहपुत्राः सबान्धवाः। मत्कृते निधनं प्राप्ताः किं नु कष्टतरं ततः॥
en: Other princes also, with their sons and kinsmen, have been killed on my account. Alas, what can be more painful than this?

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: वयं हि धार्तराष्ट्राश्च कालमन्युवंशगताः। कृत्वेदं निन्दितं कर्म प्राप्स्यामः कां गतिं नृप।॥
en: Tell us, O prince, what will befall us and the sons of Dhritarashtra, who, impelled by fate and anger, have done this hateful act.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: इदं तु धार्तराष्ट्रस्य श्रेयो मन्ये जनाधिप। इमामवस्थां सम्प्राप्तं यदसौ त्वां न पश्यति॥
en: O king, I think the son of Dhritarashtra is fortunate, because he does not see you in this condition.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: सोऽहं तव ह्यन्तकरः सुहृद्वधकरस्तथा। न शान्तिमधिगच्छामि पश्यंस्त्वां दुःखितं क्षितौ॥
en: But I, who am the cause of your death as well as of that of our friends, am denied all peace of mind by seeing you on the naked earth in this miserable plight.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: दुर्योधनो हि समरे सहसैन्यः सहानुजः। निहतः क्षत्रधर्मेऽस्मिन् दुरात्मा कुलपांसनः॥
en: The wicked Duryodhana, the most infamous of his family has, with all his soldiers and his brothers, died in battle, performing Kshatriya duties.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: न स पश्यति दुष्टात्मा त्वामद्य पतितं क्षितौ। अतः श्रेयो मृतं मन्ये नेह जीवितमात्मनः॥
en: That wicked man does not see you lying on the ground! Verily, for this reason, I would prefer death to life.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: अहं हि समरे वीर गमितः शत्रुभिः क्षयम्। अभविष्यं यदि पुरा सह भ्रातृभिरच्युत॥ न त्वामेवं सुदुःखार्तमद्राक्षं सायकार्दितम्। नूनं हि पापकर्माणो धात्रा सृष्टाः स्म हे नृप॥
en: O hero, who never forsook virtue, had I with my brothers met with death before this at the hands of our enemies on the battlefield, I would not have seen you in this pitiful condition, so pierced with arrows! Surely, O prince, the Maker had created us to commit evil deeds.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: अन्यस्मिन्नपि लोके वै यथा मुच्येम किल्बिषात्। तथा प्रशाधि मां राजन् मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम्॥
en: O king, if you wish to do me good, do you then instruct me in such a way that I may be purged of this sin in even another world.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: भीष्म उवाच परतन्त्रं कथं हेतुमात्मानमनुपश्यसि। कर्मणां हि महाभाग सूक्ष्मं ह्येतदतान्द्रियम्॥
en: Bhishma said Why, O fortunate one, do you regard your soul, which is dependent, to be the cause of your deeds? Its inaction is subtle and imperceptible to the senses.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। संवादं मृत्युगौतम्योः काललुब्धकपन्नगैः॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old story of the conversation between Mrityu and Gautami with Kala and the Fowler and the serpent.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: गौतमी नाम कौन्तेय स्थविरा शमसंयुता। सर्पण दष्टं स्वं पुत्रमपश्यद्गतचेतनम्॥
en: There was, O son of Kunti, an old lady named Gautami, who was endued with great patience and peace of mind. One day she found her son dead on account of having been bitten by a serpent.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: अथ तं स्नायुपाशेन बद्ध्वा सर्पममर्षितः। लुब्धकोऽर्जुनको नाम गौतम्याः समुपानयत्॥
en: An angry fowler, named Arjunaka, bound the serpent with a string and brought it before Gautami.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: स चाब्रवीदयं ते स पुत्रहा पन्नगाधमः। ब्रूहि क्षिप्रं महाभागे वध्यतां केन हेतुना॥
en: He then said to her. This wretched serpent has been the cause of your son's death. O blessed lady! Tell me quickly how this wretch is to be killed!

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: अग्नौ प्रक्षिप्यतामेष च्छिद्यतां खण्डशोऽपि वा। न ह्ययं बालहा पापश्चिरं जीवितुमर्हति॥
en: Shall I throw it into the fire or shall I cut it into pieces? This infamous killer of a child should not live longer!

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: गौतम्युवाच विसृजैनमबुद्धिस्त्वमवध्योऽर्जुनक त्वया। को ह्यात्मानं गुरुं कुर्यात् प्राप्तव्यमविचिन्तयन्॥
en: Gautami replied Do you, O Arjunaka of little understanding, set free this serpent! It should not be killed by you. Who is so foolish as not to care for the inevitable destiny that awaits him and make himself heavy for sinking into sin?

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: प्लवन्ते धर्मलघवो लोकऽम्भसि यथा प्लवाः। मज्जन्ति पापगुरवः शस्त्रं स्कन्नमिवोदके॥
en: Those who have made themselves light by performing virtuous deeds, manage to cross the sea of the world as a ship crosses the ocean. But those who have loaded themselves with sin sink into the bottom, as an arrow thrown into the water.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: हत्वा चैनं नामृत: स्यादयं मे जीवत्यस्मिन् कोऽत्ययः स्यादयं ते। अस्योत्सर्गे प्राणयुक्तस्य जन्तोर्मृत्योर्लोकं को नु गच्छेदनन्तम्॥
en: By killing this serpent, this my boy will not revive, and by letting it live, no harm will be caused to you. Who would go to the endless regions of Death by killing this living creature?

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: लुब्धक उवाच जानाम्यहं देवि गुणागुणज्ञे सर्वार्तियुक्ता गुरवो भवन्ति। स्वस्थस्यैते तूपदेशा भवन्ति तस्मात् क्षुद्रं सर्पमेनं हनिष्ये।॥
en: The fowler said I know, O lady, who know the difference between, right and wrong that great persons are pained at the miseries of all creatures. But these words which you have uttered carry instruction for only a selfcontained person. Therefore, I must kill this serpent.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: शमार्थिनः कालगतिं वदन्ति सद्यः शुचं त्वर्थविदस्त्यजन्ति। श्रेयःक्षयं शोचति नित्यमोहात् तस्माच्छुचं मुञ्च हते भुजङ्गे॥
en: Those who value peace of mind, attribute everything to the course of Time as the cause, but practical men soon pacify their grief. People, through perpetual error, fear loss of beatitude. Therefore, O lady, remove your grief by having this serpent killed (by me).

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: गौतम्युवाच आतिनैवं विद्यतेऽस्मद्विधानां धर्मात्मानः सर्वदा सज्जना हि। दीशे नाहं पन्नगस्य प्रमाथे॥
en: Gautami replied People like us are never pained. Good men have their souls always bent on virtue. The death of the boy was predestined: therefore, I cannot approve of the destruction of this serpent.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: न ब्राह्मणानां कोपोऽस्ति कुतः कोपाच्च यातनाम्। मार्दवारक्षम्यतां साधो मुच्यतामेष पन्नगः॥
en: Brahmanas do not cherish resentment, because resentment leads to pain. Do you, O Goodman, forgive and set free this serpent out of mercy.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: लुब्धक उवाच ल्लभ्यो लाभ्यः स्याद् बलिभ्यः प्रशस्तः। कालाल्लाभो यस्तु सत्यो भवेत श्रेयोलाभः कुत्सितेऽस्मिन्न ते स्यात्॥
en: The fowler replied Let us acquire great and inexhaustible merit in the next worlds by destroying (this creature), as a man gains great merit, and confers it on his victim as well, by sacrifice upon the altar! Merit is won by killing an enemy: by killing this despicable creature, you will acquire great and true merit in the next world.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: गौतम्युवाच का नु प्राप्तिर्गृह्य शत्रु निहत्य का कामाप्तिः प्राप्य शत्रु न मुक्त्वा। कस्मात् सौम्याहं न क्षमे नो भुजङ्गे मोक्षार्थं वा कस्य हेतोर्न कुर्याम्॥
en: Gautami replied What good is there in torturing and destroying an enemy, and what good is acquired by not setting free an enemy in our power? Therefore. O you of kind face, why should we not forgive this serpent and try to acquire merit by setting it free.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: लुब्धक उवाच अस्मादेकाद् बहवो रक्षितव्या नैको बहुभ्यो गौतमि रक्षितव्यः। कृतागसं धर्मविदस्त्यजन्ति सरीसृपं पापमिमं जहि त्वम्॥
en: The fowler replied A great number (of creatures)should be safeguarded against this one, instead of this single creature being protected. Virtuous men quit the vicious: do you, therefore, destroy the wicked creature.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: गौतम्युवाच नास्मिन् हते पन्नगे पुत्रको मे सम्प्राप्स्यते लुब्धक जीवितं वै। गुणं चान्यं नास्य वधे प्रपश्ये तस्मात् सर्प लुब्धक मुञ्च जीवम्॥
en: Gautami replied By killing this serpent, my son, O fowler, will not regain his life, nor do I see that any other end will be attained by its death: therefore, do you, O fowler, set this living serpent free.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: लुब्धक उवाच वृत्रं हत्वा देवराट् श्रेष्ठभाग वै यज्ञं हुत्वा भागमवाप चैव। शूली देवो देववृत्तं चर त्वं क्षिप्रं सर्प जहि मा भूत्ते विशङ्का॥
en: The fowler said By destroying Vritra, Indra got the best portion (of sacrificial offerings), and by destroying a sacrifice Mahadeva secured his share of sacrificial offerings: do you, therefore, kill this serpent forthwith without any misgivings whatsoever.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: भीष्म उवाच असकृत् प्रोच्यमानापि गौतमी भुजगं प्रति। लुब्धकेन महाभागा पापे नैवाकरोन्मतिम्॥ ईषदुच्छ्वसमानस्तु कृच्छ्रात् संस्तभ्य पन्नगः। उत्ससर्ज गिरं मन्दां मानुषीं पाशपीडितः॥
en: Bhishma said Although repeatedly urged on by the fowler for the destruction of the serpent, the great Gautami did nor bend her mind to that sinful deed. Painfully fettered with the cord, sighing a little and keeping up its composure with great difficulty, the serpent then uttered these words slowly, in a human voice.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: सर्प उवाच कोन्वर्जुनक दोषोऽत्र विद्यते मम बालिश। अस्वतन्त्रं हि मां मृत्युर्विवशं यदचूचुदत्॥
en: The serpent said O foolish Arjunaka, what is my fanlt? I have no will of my own, and am not independent! Death sent me on this work.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: तस्यायं वचनाद् दष्टो न कोपेन न काम्यया। तस्य तत्किल्बिषं लुब्ध विद्यते यदि किल्बिषम्॥
en: By his order have I bitten this child, and not out of any anger or option an my part. Therefore, if there be any sin in this, O fowler, the sin is his.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: लुब्धक उवाच यद्यन्यवशगेनेदं कृतं ते पन्नगाशुभम्। कारणं वै त्वमप्यत्र तस्मात् किल्बिषी॥
en: The fowler said If you have committed this evil, urged thereto by another, the sin is your also as you are an instrument in the act.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: मृत्पात्रस्य क्रियायां हि दण्डचक्रादयो यथा। कारणत्वे प्रकल्प्यन्ते तथा त्वमपि पन्नग॥
en: As in the making of an earthen pot the potter's wheel and rod and other things are all considered as causes, so are you, O serpent.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: सर्प उवाच किल्विषी चापि मे वध्यः किल्बिषी चासि पन्नग। आत्मानं कारणं ह्यत्र त्वमाख्यासि भुजङ्गम॥ सर्व एते ह्यस्ववशा दण्डचक्रादयो यथा। तथाऽहमपि तस्मान्मे नैष दोषो मतस्तव॥
en: The serpent said He who is guilty should be killed by me, You, O serpent, are guilty! Indeed you confess it. As all these, vis., the porter's wheel, rod, and other things, are not independent causes, so I am not an independent cause! Therefore, this is no fault of mine, you should admit it.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: अथवा मतमेतत्ते तेऽप्यन्योन्यप्रयोजकाः। कार्यकारणसन्देहो भवत्यन्योन्यचोदनात्॥
en: If you hold otherwise, then these are to be considered as causes working with one another. For thus working with one other, a doubt springs up about their relation as cause and effect.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: एवं सति न दोषो मे नास्मि वध्यो न किल्बिषी। किल्विषं समवाये स्यान्मन्यसे यदि किल्विषम्॥
en: Such being the case, it is no fault of mine, nor should I be killed on this account, nor am I guilty of any sin! Or, if you think that there is sin, the sin lies in the aggregate of causes.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: लुब्धक उवाच कारणं यदि न स्याद् वै न कर्ता स्यास्त्वमप्युत। विनाशकारणं त्वं च तस्माद् वध्योऽसि मे मतः॥
en: The fowler said If you are neither the principal cause nor the agent in this matter: you are still the cause of the death. Therefore, I think you should be killed.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: असत्यपि कृते कार्यं नेह पन्नग लिप्यते। तस्मान्नात्रैव हेतुः स्याद् वध्यः किं बहु मन्यसे॥
en: If, O serpent, you think that when an evil deed is done the doer is not implicated therein, then there can be no cause in this matter: but having done this, you should surely be killed. What more do you think?

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: सर्प उवाच कार्याभावे क्रिया न स्यात् सत्यसत्यपि कारणे। तस्मात् समेऽस्मिन् हेतौ मे वाच्यो हेतुर्विशेषतः॥
en: The serpent said Whether any prime cause exists or not, no effect is done without an (intermediate) act. Therefore, causation being of no importance in either case, my act as the cause should be considered in full.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: अन्यः प्रयोगे स्यादत्र किल्बिषी जन्तुनाशने।॥ यद्यहं कारणत्वेन मतो लुब्धक तत्त्वतः।
en: If, O fowler, you consider me truly, to be the cause then the sin of this act of killing a living being rests on the shoulders of another who led me to do this.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: लुब्धक उवाच वध्यस्त्वं मम दुर्बुद्धे बालघाती नृशंसकृत्। भाषसे किं बहु पुनर्वध्यः सन् पन्नगाधम॥
en: The fowler said You don't deserve life, O foolish one, why do you then exchange so many words, O wretched serpent? You should be killed by me. You have done a heinous crime by killing this infant.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: सर्प उवाच यथा हवींषि जुह्वाना मखे वै लुब्धकर्विजः। न फलं प्राप्नुवन्त्यत्र फलयोगे तथा ह्यहम्॥
en: The serpent said O fowler, as the priests officiating at a sacrifice do not gain the merit of the act by offering oblations of clarified butter to the fire, so should I be considered in this matter.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: भीष्म उवाच तथा ब्रुवति तस्मिंस्तु पन्नगे मृत्युचोदिते। आजगाम ततो मृत्युः पन्नगं चाब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Bhishma continued The serpent directed by Death having said this, Death himself appeared there and addressing the serpent said:

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: मृत्युरुवाच प्रचोदितोऽहं कालेन पन्नग त्वामचूचुदम्। विनाशहेतुर्नास्य तमहं न प्राणिनः शिशोः॥
en: Mrityu said Guided by Kala, I, O serpent, sent you on this mission, and neither are you nor am I the cause of this child's death.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: यथा वायुर्जलधरान् विकर्षति ततस्ततः। तद्वज्जलदवत् सर्प कालस्याहं वशानुगः॥
en: As the clouds are driven hither and thither by the wind I, am, O serpent, moved by Kala.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: सात्त्विका राजसाश्चैव तामसा ये च केचन। भावाः कालात्मकाः सर्वे प्रवर्तन्ते ह जन्तुषु॥
en: All influences of Sattwa, or Rajas, or Tamas, originate from Kala as they work in all creatures.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: जङ्गमाः स्थावराश्चैव दिवि वा यदि वा भुवि। सर्वे कालात्मकाः सर्प कालात्मकमिदं जगत्॥
en: All creatures, mobile and immobile, in heaven, or earth, are pervaded by the influence of Kala. The whole universe, O serpent, is permeated by this same influence of Kala.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: प्रवृत्तयश्च लोकेऽस्मिंस्तथैव च निवृत्तयः। तासां विकृतयो याश्च सर्वं कालात्मकं स्मृतम्॥
en: All acts in this world and all abstentions, as also all their changes, are owing to be influenced by Kala.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: आदित्यश्चन्द्रमा विष्णुरापो वायुः शतक्रतुः। अग्नि: स्वं पृथिवी मित्रः पर्जन्यो वसवोऽदितिः।।५५
en: The Sun, Soma, Vishnu, Water, Wind, the god of a hundred sacrifices, Fire, Sky, Earth, Mitra and Parjanaya, Aditi, and the Vasus, Rivers and Oceans, all existent and nonexistent objects, are created and destroyed by Kala.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: सरितः सागराचैव भावाभावौ च पन्नग। सर्व कालेन सृज्यन्ते ह्रियन्ते च पुनः पुनः॥ एवं ज्ञात्वा कथं मां त्वं सदोषं सर्प मन्यसे। अथ चैवंगते दोघे मयि त्वमपि दोषवान्॥
en: Knowing this, why do you, O serpent, consider me blameable? If I am to be blamed for this, you are also blameable.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: सर्प उवाच निर्दोषं दोषवन्तं वा न त्वां मृत्यो ब्रवीम्यहम्। त्वयाहं चोदित इति ब्रवीम्येतावदेव तु॥
en: The serpent said I do not, O Mrityu, blame you, nor do I set you free from all blame. I only say that I am directed and influenced by you.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: यदि काले तु दोषोऽस्ति यदि तत्रापि नेष्यते। दोषो नैव परीक्ष्यो मे न ह्यत्राधिकृता वयम्॥
en: If Kala is to be blamed, or, it is not for me to find the fault. We have nor right to do so.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: निर्मोक्षस्त्वस्य दोषस्य मया कार्या यथा तथा। मृत्योरपि न दोषः स्यादिति मेऽत्र प्रयोजनम्॥
en: As it is my duty to absolve myself from this blame, so it is my duty to see that Mrityu is not blamed.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: भीष्म उवाच सर्पोऽथार्जुनकं प्राह श्रुतं ते मृत्युभाषितम्। नानागसं मां पाशेन संतापयितुमर्हसि॥
en: Bhishma continued Then the serpent, addressing Arjunaka said, 'You have heard what Mrityu has said. Therefore, it is not proper for you to torment me, who am innocent, by fettering me with this rope

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: लुब्धक उवाच मृत्योः श्रुतं मे वचनं तव चैव भुजङ्गम। नैव तावददोषत्वं भवति त्वयि पन्नग॥
en: The fowler said I have heard, you, O serpent, as well as the words of Mrityu, but these, O serpent, do not set you free from all blame.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: मृत्युस्त्वं चैव हेतुर्हि बालस्यास्य विनाशने। उभयं कारणं मन्ये न कारणमकारणम्॥
en: Mrityu and you are the causes of this child's death. I regard both of you to be the cause and I do not call that to be the cause which is not truly so.
