description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: धिमृत्युं च दुरात्मानं क्रूरं दुःखकरं सताम्। त्वां चैवाहं वधिष्यामि पापं पापस्य कारणम्॥
en: Accursed be the wicked and vengeful Death that causes misery to the good! I shall also kill you who are sinful and engaged in sinful deeds.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: मृत्युरुवाच विवशौ कालवशगावावां निर्दिष्टकारिणौ। नावां दोषेण गन्तव्यौ यदि सम्यक् प्रपश्यसि॥
en: Mrityu said We both are not free, but are dependent on Kala, and are ordained to do our appointed work. You will not blame us if you do consider this matter thoroughly.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: लुब्धक उवाच युवामुभौ कालवशौ यदि मे मृत्युपन्नगौ। हर्षक्रोधौ यथा स्यातामेतदिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: The fowler said If you both, O serpent and Mrityu, depend on Kala. I am curious to know how pleasure and anger are caused.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: मृत्युरुवाच या काचिदेव चेष्टा स्यात् सर्वा कालप्रचोदिता। पूर्वमेवैतदुक्तं हि मया लुब्धक कालतः॥ तस्मादुभौ कालवशावावां निर्दिष्टकारिणौ। नावां दोषेण गन्तव्यौ त्वया लुब्धक कर्हिचित्॥
en: Mrityu said Everything is done under the influence of Kala. I have said it before, O fowler, that Kala is the cause of all and therefore we both, acting under the influence of Kala, do our appointed work and, therefore, O fowler, we two should not be blamed by you.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: भीष्म उवाच अथोपगम्य कालस्तु तस्मिन् धर्मार्थसंशये। अब्रवीत् पन्नगं मृत्यु लुब्धं चार्जुनकं तथा॥
en: Bhishma said Then Kala arrived there where ethics were being discussed, and spoke thus to the serpent and Mrityu and the fowler Arjunaka assembled together.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: काल उवाच न ह्यहं नाप्ययं मृत्यु यं लुब्धक पन्नगः। किल्बिषी जन्तुमरणे न वयं हि प्रयोजकाः॥
en: Kala said Neither Mrityu, nor this serpent, nor I, O fowler, am guilty of the death of any creature. We are merely the immediate causes of the event. O Arjunaka, the Karma of this child was the exciting cause of our action in this matter.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: अकरोद् यदयं कर्म तन्नोऽर्जुनक चोदकम्। विनाशहेतुर्नान्योऽस्य वध्यतेऽयं स्वकर्मणा॥
en: There was no other cause by which this child met its death. It was killed by the result of its own Karma.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: यदनेन कृतं कर्म तेनायं निधनं गतः। विनाशहेतुः कर्मास्य सर्वे कर्मवशा वयम्॥
en: It has met 'with death as the result of its pristine Karma. Its Karma has been the root of its destruction. We all are subject to our respective Karma.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: कर्मदायादवाँल्लोकः कर्मसम्बन्धलक्षणः। कर्माणि चोदयन्तीह यथान्योन्यं तथा वयम्॥
en: Karma is a help to salvation as sons are and Karma also expresses virtue and vice in man. We impell one another even acts urge one another.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: यथा मृत्पिण्डतः कर्ता कुरुते यद् यदिच्छति। एवमात्मकृतं कर्म मानवः प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: As men make from a lump of clay whatever they wish to make, so do men come by various results out of Karma.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: यथाच्छायातयौ नित्यं सुसम्बद्धौ निरन्तरम्। तथा कर्म च कर्ता च सम्बद्धावात्मकर्मभिः॥
en: As light and shadow are connected with each other, so are men related to Karma through their own deeds.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: एवं नाहं न वै मृत्यु सर्पो न तथा भवान्। न चेयं ब्राह्मणी वृद्धा शिशुरेवात्र कारणम्॥
en: Therefore, neither are you, nor am I, nor Mrityu, nor the serpent, nor this old Brahmana lady, is the cause of this child's death.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: तस्मिंस्तथा ब्रुवाणे तु ब्राह्मणी गौतमी नृप। स्वकर्मप्रत्ययाँल्लोकान् मत्वाऽर्जुनकमब्रवीत्॥
en: He himself is the cause here. Upon Kala, O king, explaining the matter thus, Gautami, convinced in her mind that men suffer according to their actions, spoke thus to Arjunaka.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: गौतमी उवाच नैव कालो न भुजगो न मृत्युरिह कारणम्। स्वकर्मभिरयं बालः कालेन निधनं गतः॥
en: Gautami said Neither Kala, nor Mrityu, nor the serpent, is the cause here. This child has met with death as the result of its own Karma,

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: मया च तत् कृतं कर्म येनायं मे मृतः सुतः। यातु कालस्तथा मृत्युर्मुञ्चार्जुनक पन्नगम्॥
en: I too have so acted that my son has died. Let now Kala and Mrityu retire from there, and do you too, O Arjunaka, set this serpent free.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो यथागतं जग्मुर्मृत्युः कालोऽथ पन्नगः। अभूद् विशोकोऽर्जुनको विशोका चैव गौतमी॥
en: Bhishma continued Then Kala and Mrityu and the serpent returned to their respective places, and Gautami became consoled in mind as also the fowler.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: एतच्छुत्वा शमं गच्छ मा भूः शोकपरो नृप। स्वकर्मप्रत्ययाँल्लोकान् सर्वे गच्छन्ति वै नृप॥
en: Having heard all this, O king, do you forego all grief, and acquire peace of mind! Men attain to heaven or hell as the result of their own Karma.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: नैव त्वया कृतं कर्म नापि दुर्योधनेन वै। कालेनैतत् कृतं विद्धि निहता येन पार्थिवाः॥
en: This evil has neither been of your own creation, nor of Duryodhana's! That these king's of Earth have all been killed, is the work of Kala.

description: Yudhishthira's despondency at the death of his relatives. The story of Mrityu, Gautami, Kala, the fowler, the serpent etc.
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येतद् वचनं श्रुत्वा बभूव विगतज्वरः। युधिष्ठिरो महातेजाः पप्रच्छेदं च धर्मवित्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard all this, the powerful and pious Yudhishthira became consoled in mind, and again enquired as follows.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामह महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद। श्रुतं मे महदाख्यानमिदं मतिमतां वर॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O wisest of men, O you who are learned in all the scriptures, I have heard, this great story, O foremost of intelligent men!

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: भूयस्तु श्रोतुमिच्छामि धर्मार्थसहितं नृप। कथ्यमानं त्वया किञ्चित् तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: I am desirous of again listening to the recital of some history full of religious instruction, and you should satisfy me.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: केन मृत्युर्गृहस्थेन धर्ममाश्रित्य निजितः। इत्येतत् सर्वमाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेनापि च पार्थिव॥
en: O king, tell me if any householder has ever succeeded in conquering Death by the practice of virtue! Do you recite this to me in full.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। यथा मृत्युर्गृहस्थेन धर्ममाश्रित्य निर्जितः॥
en: Bhishma said This ancient history is narrated describing the subject of the conquest, by a householder, of Death, by the practice of virtue.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: मनोः प्रजापते राजनिक्ष्वाकुरभवत् सुतः। तस्य पुत्रशतं जज्ञे नृपतेः सूर्यवर्चसः॥
en: The Prajapati Manu had a son, O king, named Ikshvaku. That king, illustrious as the Sun, begat a hundred sons.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: दशमस्तस्य पुत्रस्तु दशाश्वो नाम भारत। माहिष्मत्यामभूद् राजा धर्मात्मा सत्यविक्रमः॥
en: His tenth son, O Bharata, was named Dashashva, and this virtuous prince of infallible prowess became the king of Mahismati.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: दशाश्वस्य सुतस्त्वासीद् राजा परमधार्मिकः। सत्ये तपसि दाने च यस्य नित्यं रतं मनः॥
en: Dashashva's son, o king, was a pious prince whose mind was continually devoted to the practice of truth and charity and devotion.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: मदिराश्व इति ख्यातः पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपतिः। धनुर्वेदे च वेदे च निरतो योऽभवत् सदा॥
en: He was known by the name of Madirashva and ruled the Earth as her master. He was continually given to the study of the Vedas as also of the science of arms.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: मदिराश्वस्य पुत्रस्तु द्युतिमान् नाम पार्थिवः। महाभागो महातेजा महासत्त्वो महाबलः॥
en: Madirashva's son was the king named Dyutimat who was ended with great good fortune and power and strength and energy.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: पुत्रो द्युतिमतस्त्वासीद् राजा परमधार्मिकः। सर्वलोकेषु विख्यातः सुवीरो नाम नामतः॥
en: Dyutimat's son was the highly devout and pious king who was celebrated in all the worlds by the name of Suvira. His soul was intent on religion and he possessed riches like another Indra the king of the gods.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: धर्मात्मा कोषवांश्चापि देवराज इवापरः। सुवीरस्य तु पुत्रोऽभूत् सर्वसंग्रामदुर्जयः॥
en: Suvira too had a son who was invincible in battle, and who was the best of all warriors and known by the name of Sudurjaya.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: स दुर्जय इति ख्यातः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। दुर्जयस्येन्द्रवपुषः पुत्रोऽश्विसदृशद्युतिः॥
en: And Durjaya too, endued with a body like that of Indra, had a son who was radiant with the effulgence of fire. He was the great king named Duryodhana who was one of the foremost of royal sages.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: दुर्योधनो नाम महान् राजा राजर्षिस्तमः। तस्येन्द्रसमवीर्यस्य संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनः॥
en: Indra used to pour rain profusely in the kingdom of this king, who never fled from the battle field and was gifted with valour like unto Indra himself.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: विषये वासवस्तस्य सम्यगेव प्रवर्षति। रत्नैर्धनैश्च पशुभिः सस्येश्चापि पृथग्विधैः॥
en: The cities and the kingdom of this king were filled with wealth and gems and cattle and various sorts of grain.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: नगरं विषयश्चास्य प्रतिपूर्णस्तदाभवत्। न तस्य विषये चाभूत् कृपणो नापि दुर्गतः॥
en: There was no miser in his kingdom nor any person afflicted with distress or suffering from poverty. Nor was there in his kingdom any person who was weak in body or afflicted with disease.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: व्याधितो वा कृशो वाऽपि तस्मिन् नाभृन्नरः क्वचित्। सुदक्षिणो मधुरवागनसूयुर्जितेन्द्रियः। धर्मात्मा चानृशंसश्च विक्रान्तोऽथाविकस्थनः॥
en: This king was very intelligent, mild in speech, without envy, a master of his passions, of a righteous soul, full of mercy, gifted with prowess, and not given to boasting.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: यज्वा च दान्तो मेधावी ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यसङ्गरः। न चावमन्ता दाता च वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः॥
en: He celebrated sacrifices, and was selfcontrolled and intelligent, devoted to Brahmanas and Truth. He never humiliated others, and was charitable, and wellread in the Vedas and the Vedanta.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तं नर्मदा देवनदी पुण्या शीतजला शिवा। चकमे पुरुषव्याघ्रं स्वेन भावेन भारत।॥
en: Auspicious and sacred and of cool waters, the celestial stream Narmada, in her own nature, O Bharata, courted him.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तस्यां जज्ञे तदा नद्यां कन्या राजीवलोचना। नाम्ना सुदर्शना राजन् रूपेण च सुदर्शना॥
en: He begot upon that river, a lotus eyed daughter, named Sudarshana, who was, O king, gifted with great beauty.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तादृग्रूपा न नारीषु भूतपूर्वा युधिष्ठिर। दुर्योधनसुता यादृगभवद् वरवर्णिनी॥
en: No woman, O Yudhishthira, had been born before, who was so very beautiful as that excellent lady the daughter of Duryodhana.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तामग्निश्चकमे साक्षाद् राजकन्यां सुदर्शनाम्। भूत्वा च ब्राह्मणो राजन् वरयामास तं नृपम्॥
en: The god Agni himself courted the beautiful princess Sudarshana, and assuming the shape of a Brahmana, O king, sought her hand from the king.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: दरिद्रश्चासवर्णश्च ममायमिति पार्थिवः। न दित्सति सुतां तस्मै तां विप्राय सुदर्शनाम्॥
en: The king was reluctant to give his daughter in marriage to the Brahmana who was poor and not of equal rank with himself.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: ततोऽस्य वितते यज्ञे नष्टोऽभूद्धव्यवाहनः। ततःसुदुःखितो राजा वाक्यमाह द्विजांस्तदा॥
en: Thereupon Agni disappeared from his great sacrifice. The king, grieved at heart, then addressed the Brahmanas, saying,

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: दुष्कृतं मम किं नु स्याद् भवतां वा द्विजर्षभाः। येन नाशं जगामाग्निः कृतं कुपुरुषेष्विव॥
en: What sin have, I you excellent Brahmanas, or you, have committed, that Agni should disappear from this sacrifice, as good done to wicked men vanishes from their estimation.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: न ह्यल्पं दुष्कृतं नोऽस्ति येनाग्नि शमागतः। भवतां चाथवा मह्यं तत्त्वेनैतद् विमृश्यताम्॥
en: Indeed, we have committed a great iniquity for which Agni has thus disappeared! Either you have committed the sin, or I. Do you fully enquire into the matter.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तत्र राज्ञो वचः श्रुत्वा विप्रास्ते भरतर्षभ। नियता वाग्यताश्चैव पावकं शरणं ययुः॥
en: Then hearing the king's words, O foremost prince of Bharata's race, the Brahmanas, controlling speech, sought with concentrated faculties the help of the god of fire.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तान् दर्शयामास तदा भगवान् हव्यवाहनः। स्वं रूपं दीप्तिमत् कृत्वा शरदर्कसमद्युतिः॥
en: The divine carrier of oblations, effugent as the autumnal Sun, appeared before them, covering his self in glorious refulgence.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: ततो महात्मा तानाह दहनो ब्राह्मणर्षभान्। वरयाम्यात्मनोऽर्थाय दुर्योधनसुतामिति॥
en: The great Agni then addressed those excellent Brahmanas, saying, I seek the daughter of Duryodhana for my own self.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: ततस्ते कल्पमुत्थाय तस्मै राज्ञे न्यवेदयन्। ब्राह्मणा विस्मिताः सर्वे यदुक्तं चित्रभानुना॥
en: At this, all those Brahmanas were struck with surprise and rising on the morrow, they told the king what had been said by the firegod.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: ततः स राजा तच्छुत्वा वचनं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्। अवाप्य परमं हर्षं तथेति प्राह बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Hearing the words of those Brahmavadins, the wise king was delighted at heart, and said, Be it so! The king sought a boon of Do you, O Agni, be pleased to remain always with us here!

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: अयाचत च तं शुल्कं भगवन्तं विभावसुम्। नित्यं सांनिध्यमिह ते चित्रभानो भवेदिति॥ तमाह भगवानग्निरेवमस्त्विति पार्थिवम्। ततः सांनिध्यमद्यापि माहिष्मत्यां विभावसोः॥
en: Be it so! said the divine Agni to that king. For this reason Agni has always been present in the kingdom of Mahismati to this day, and was seen by Sahadeva in his conquering expedition to the south.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: दृष्टं हि सहदेवेन दिशं विजयता तदा। ततस्तां समलंकृत्य कन्यामाहृतवाससम्॥ ददौ दुर्योधनो राजा पावकाय महात्मने। प्रतिजग्राह चाग्निस्तु राजकन्यां सुदर्शनाम्॥ विधिना वेददृष्टेन वसोर्धारामिवाध्वरे। तस्या रूपेण शीलेन कुलेन वपुषा श्रिया॥ अभवत् प्रीतिमानग्निर्गर्भे चास्या मनो दधे। तस्याः समभवत्पुत्रो नाम्नाऽऽग्नेयः सुदर्शनः॥
en: Then the king gave his daughter, dressed in new raiments and decked with jewels, to the great god, and Agni too accepted, according to Vedic rites, the princess Sudarshana as his bride, as he accepts libations of clarified butter at sacrifices. Agni was well pleased with her look, her beauty, grace, character, and nobility of birth, and thought of begetting offspring upon her. And she soon gave birth to a son by Agni, of the name of Sudarshana.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: सुदर्शनस्तु रूपेण पूर्णेन्दुसदृशोपमः। शिशुरेवाध्यगात् सर्वं परं ब्रह्म सनातनम्॥
en: Sudarshana, also, was, as beautiful as the full moon, and even in his childhood he acquired a knowledge of the supreme and eternal Brahma.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: अथौघवान् नाम नृपो नृगस्यासीत् पितामहः। तस्याथौघवती कन्या पुत्रश्चौवरथोऽभवत्॥
en: There was also a king named Oghavat, who was the grandfather of Nriga. He had a daughter named Oghavati, and a son, too, of the name of Ogharatha born to him.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तामोघवान् ददौ तस्मै स्वयमोघवतीं सुताम्। सुदर्शनाय विदुषे भार्यार्थं देवरूपिणीम्॥
en: King Oghavat gave his daughter Oghavati, beautiful as a goddess, 10 the learned Sudarshana, for wife.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: स गृहस्थाश्रमरतस्तया सह सुदर्शनः। कुरुक्षेत्रेऽवसद् राजन्नोघवत्या समन्वितः॥
en: Sudarshana, o king, leading the domestic mode of life with Oghavati, used to live in Kurukshetra with her.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: गृहस्थश्चावजेष्यामि मृत्युमित्येव स प्रभो। प्रतिज्ञामकरोद् धीमान् दीप्ततेजा विशाम्पते।॥
en: This intelligent prince of fiery energy took the vow, O lord, of conquering Death by leading the life of a householder.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तामथौघवतीं राजन् स पावकसुतोऽब्रवीत्। अतिथेः प्रतिकूलं ते न कर्तव्यं कथंचन॥
en: The son of Agni, O king, said to Oghavati Do you never act against the wishes of those who seek our hospitality.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: येन येन च तुष्येत नित्यमेव त्वयाऽतिथिः। अप्यात्मनः प्रदानेन न ते कार्या विचारणा॥
en: You should ungrudgingly welcome the guests, even if you have to offer your own body.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: एतद् व्रतं मम सदा हृदि सम्परिवर्तते। गृहस्थानां च सुश्रोणि नातिथेर्विद्यते परम्॥
en: O beautiful one, I always remember this vow, since for householders, there is no higher virtue than hospitality to guests.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: प्रमाणं यदि वामोरु वचस्ते मम शोभने। इदं वचनमव्यग्रा हृदि त्वं धारयेः सदा॥
en: Do you always remember without ever doubting it, if my words be any authority with you.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: निष्क्रान्ते मयि कल्याणि तथा संनिहितेऽनघे। नातिथिस्तेऽवमन्तव्यः प्रमाणं यद्यहं तव॥
en: O sinless and blessed one, if you have any faith in me, do you never disregard a guest whether I be at your side or at a distance from you.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तमब्रवीदोघवती तथा मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः। न मे त्वद्वचनात् किंचिन्न कर्तव्यं कथंचन॥
en: Oghavati placing her clasped hands on her forehead, replied, saying, I shall leave nothing indone of what you order me.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: जिगीषमाणस्तु गृहे तदा मृत्युः सुदर्शनम्। पृष्ठतोऽन्वगमद् राजन् रन्ध्रान्वेषी तदा सदा॥
en: Then, O king, desiring to overreach Sudarshana, Mrityu began to watch him for Ginding out his short comings.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: इध्मार्थं तु गते तस्मिन्नग्निपुत्रे सुदर्शने। अतिथिळह्मणः श्रीमांस्तामाहौघवतीं तदा॥
en: Once on a time, when the son of Agni went out fetch fuel from the forest, a graceful Brahmana sought the hospitality of Oghavati with these words.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: आतिथ्यं कृतमिच्छामि त्वयाऽद्य वरवर्णिनि। प्रमाणं यदि धर्मस्ते गृहस्थाश्रमसम्मतः॥
en: O beautiful lady, if you have any faith in the virtue of hospitality as laid down for householders, then I would request you to extend the rites of hospitality to me today.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: इत्युक्ता तेन विप्रेण राजपुत्री यशस्विनी। विधिना प्रतिजग्राह वेदोक्तेन विशाम्पते॥
en: Thus addressed by that Brahmana, O king, the illustrious princess welcomed him according to the rites laid down in the Vedas.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: आसनं चैव पाद्यं च तस्मै दत्त्वा द्विजातये। प्रोवाचौघवती विप्रं केनार्थः किं ददामि ते॥
en: Having offered him a seat, and water to wash his feet, she enquired, saying, What is your business? What can I offer you?

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तामब्रवीत् ततो विप्रो राजपुत्री सुदर्शनाम्। त्वया ममार्थः कल्याणि निर्विशङ्कतदाचर॥
en: The Brahmana said to her, my business is with your body, O blessed one! Do you act accordingly without any hesitation whatever.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: यदि प्रमाणं धर्मस्ते गृहस्थाश्रमसम्मतः। प्रदानेनात्मनो राज्ञि कर्तुमर्हसि मे प्रियम्॥
en: If the duties prescribed for householders be acceptable to you, do you, O princess, satisfy me by offering up your body to me.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: स तया छन्द्यमानोऽन्यैरीप्सितैर्नृपकन्यया। नान्यमात्मप्रदानात् स तस्या ववे वरं द्विजः॥
en: Though tempted by the princess witi, offers of various other things, the Brahmana, however, did not seek the Brahmana, however, did not seek any thing else than the offer of her own person.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: सा तु राजसुता स्मृत्वा भर्तुर्वचनमादितः। तथेति लज्जमाना सा तमुवाच द्विजर्षभम्॥
en: Finding him determined, that lady, recollecting the directions given to her by her husband, but filled with shame, said to that excellent Brahmana Be it so.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: ततो विहस्य विप्रर्षिः सा चैवाथ विवेश ह। संस्मृत्य भर्तुर्वचनं गृहस्थाश्रमकाङ्क्षिणः॥
en: Recollecting the words of her husband who was desirous of acquiring the virtue of householders, she cheerfully approached the i twiceborn Rishi.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: अथेध्मानमुपादाय स पावकिरुपागमत्। मृत्युना रौद्रभावेन नित्यं बन्धुरिवान्वितः॥
en: Meanwhile, the son of Agni, having collected fuel, returned to his home. Mrityu, with his dreadful and inexorable nature, was always by his side, as one attends upon his devoted friend.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: ततस्त्वाश्रममागम्य स पावकसुतस्तदा। तां व्याजहारौघवतीं क्वासि यातेति चासकृत्॥
en: When the son of Pavaka returned to his own asylum, he called out for Oghavati by name, and repeatedly exclaimed Where are you gone?

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तस्मै प्रतिवचः सा तु भर्त्रे न प्रददौ तदा। कराभ्यां तेन विप्रेण स्पृष्टा भर्तृव्रता सती॥
en: But the chaste lady, devoted to her husband, being then in the arms of that Brahmana, gave no reply to her husband.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: उच्छिष्टाऽस्मीति मन्वाना लज्जिता भर्तुरेव च। तूष्णीं भूताऽभवत् साध्वी चोवाचाथ किंचन॥
en: Indeed, considering herself sullied, that chaste woman became speechless, overcome with shame.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: अथ तां पुनरेवेदं प्रोवाच स सुदर्शनः। क्व सा साध्वी क्व सा याता गरीयः किमतो मम।।
en: Sudarshana, addressing her again, exclaimed Where can my chaste wife be? Where has she gone? Nothing can be so very important to me than this.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: पतिव्रता सत्यशीला नित्यं चैवार्जवे रता। कथं न प्रत्युदेत्यद्य स्मयमाना यथा पुरा॥
en: Why does not that simple and truthful lady, devoted to her husband, alas reply as she used to do before with sweet smiles.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: उटजस्थस्तु तं विप्रः प्रत्युवाच सुदर्शनम्। अतिथिं विद्धि सम्प्राप्तं ब्राह्मणं पावके च माम्।।६४। अनया छन्द्यमानोऽहं भार्यया तव सत्तम। तैस्तैरतिथिसत्कारैर्ब्रह्मन्नेषाा वृता मया॥ अनेन विधिना सेयं मामर्छति शुभानना। अनुरूपं यदनान्यत् तद् भवान् कर्तुमर्हति॥
en: Then that Brahmana, who was within the hut, thus replied to Sudarshana Know, O son of fire, that a Brahmana guest has arrived, and though tempted by your wife with various other offers of welcome, I have, O best of Brahmanas, desired only her body and this fair lady is engaged in welcoming me with due rites! You can do whatever you think proper on this occasion.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: कूटमुद्ररहस्तस्तु मृत्युस्तं वै समन्वगात्। हीनप्रतिज्ञमत्रैनं वधिष्यामीति चिन्तयन्॥
en: Armed with the iron club, death pursued the Rishi at that moment, desirous of bringing about the destruction of one who would, he thought, deviate from his promise.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: सुदर्शनस्तु मनसा कर्मणा चक्षुषा गिरा। त्यक्तेति॒स्त्यक्तमन्युश्च स्मयमानोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ सुरतं तेऽस्तु विप्राय्य प्रीतिर्हि परमा मम। गृहस्थस्य हि धर्मोऽत्र्यः सम्प्राप्तातिथिपूजनम्॥
en: Sudarshana was struck with wonder, but renouncing all, jealousy and anger by look, word, deed, or thought, said Do you enjoy yourself, O Brahmana! It is a great pleasure to me! A householder acquires the highest merit by honouring a guest.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: अतिथिः पूजितो यस्य गृहस्थस्य तु गच्छति। नान्यस्तस्मात् परो धर्म इति प्राहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: The learned say that to the householders, there is no higher merit than what comes from a guest leaving his house after having been duly honoured by him.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: प्राणा हि मम दाराश्च यच्चानद् विद्यते वसु। अतिथिभ्यो मया देयमिति मे व्रतमाहितम्॥
en: My life, my wife and all my earthly belongings, are all dedicated to the use of my guests! This is the vow that I have taken.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: नि:संदिग्धं यथा वाक्यमेतन्मे समुदाहृतम्। तेनाहं विप्र सत्येन स्वयमात्मानमालभे॥
en: As I have truly made this statement, by that truth, O Brahmana, I shall acquire the knowledge of Self.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम्। बुद्धिरात्मा मनः कालो दिशश्चैव गुणा दश॥ नित्यमेव हि पश्यन्ति देहिनां देहसंश्रिताः। सुकृतं दुष्कृतं चापि कर्म धर्मभृतां वर॥
en: O foremost of the virtuous, the five elements, viz., fire, air, earth, water, and sky, and the mind, the intellect and the Soul, and time and space and the ten organs of sense, are all in the bodies of men and always witness the good and evil deeds of men.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: यथैषा नानृता वाणी मयाऽद्य समुदीरिता। तेन सत्येन मां देवाः पालयन्तु दहन्तु वा॥
en: This truth I have spoken today, and let the gods bless me for it or destroy me if I have spoken an untruth.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: ततो नादः समभवद् दिक्षु सर्वासु भारत। असकृत् सत्यमित्येवं नैतन्मिथ्येति सर्वतः॥
en: At this, O Bharata, there arose from all sides, in repeated echoes, a voice, crying This is true, this is not false.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: उटजात् तु ततस्तस्मान्निश्रकाम स वै द्विजः। वपुषा द्यां च भूमिं च व्याप्य वायुरिवोद्यतः॥ स्वरेण विप्रः शैक्षेण त्रीन्लोकाननुनादयन्। उवाच चैनं धर्मज्ञं पूर्वमामन्त्र्य नामतः॥ ते
en: Then that Brahmana came out of the hovel, and like the wind rising and covering both Earth and sky, and making the three worlds echo with Vedic recitations, and calling that virtuous man by name, and congratulating him, said:

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: धर्मोऽहमस्मि भद्रं ते जिज्ञासार्थं तवानघ। प्राप्तः सत्यं च ज्ञात्वा प्रीतिर्मे परमा त्वयि॥
en: O sinless one, I am Dharma! All glory to you! I came here, O truthloving one, to try you, and I am well pleased with you by knowing you to be virtuous.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: विजितश्च त्वया मृत्युर्योऽयं त्वामनुगच्छति। रन्ध्रान्वेषी तव सदा त्वया धृत्या वशी कृतः॥
en: You have controlled and conquered Death who always has pursued you, seeking your shortcomings.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: न चास्ति शक्तिस्त्रैलोक्ये कस्यचित् पुरुषोत्तम। पतिव्रतामिमां साध्वीं तवोद्वीक्षितुमप्युत॥
en: O best of men, no one in the three worlds has the power to insult, even with looks, this chaste lady devoted to her husband, far less to touch her body.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: रक्षिता त्वद्गुणैरेषा पतिव्रतगुणैस्तथा। अधृष्या यदियं ब्रूयात् तथा तन्नान्यथा भवेत्॥
en: She has been saved from contamination by your virtue and by her own chastity. There can be nothing against what this proud lady will say.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: एषा हि तपसा स्वेन संयुक्ता ब्रह्मवादिनी। पावनार्थं च लोकस्य सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा भविष्यति॥
en: This Brahmavadin, gifted with austere penances, shall, for the salvation of the world, be changed into a powerful river.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: अर्धेनौघवती नाम त्वामधेनानुयास्यति। शरीरेण महाभाग योगो ह्यस्या वशे स्थितः॥
en: And you will acquire all the worlds in this your body, and because the science of Yoga is within her control, this highly blessed lady will follow you with only half her body, and with the other half will she be celebrated as the river Oghavati.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: अनया सह लोकांश्च गन्ताऽसि तपसार्जितान्। यत्र नावृत्तिमभ्येति शाश्वतांस्तान् सनातनान्॥
en: And you will acquire with her all the worlds that are acquired by penances.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: अनेन चैव देहेन लोकांस्त्वमभिपत्स्यसे। निर्जितश्च त्वया मृत्युरैश्वर्ये च तवोत्तमम्॥
en: You will acquire even in this material body those eternal and everlasting worlds from which none return.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: पञ्चभूतान्यतिक्रान्तः स्ववीर्याञ्च मनोजवः गृहस्थधर्मेणानेन कामक्रोधौ च ते जितौ॥
en: You have conquered Death, "and acquired the highest happiness and by your own power (of mind), attaining to the speed of thought, you have transcended the five elements.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: स्नेहो राश्च तन्द्री च मोहो द्रोहश्च केवलः। तव शुश्रूषया राजन् राजपुत्र्या विनिर्जिताः॥
en: By thus following the duties of a householder, you have conquered your passions, desires, and anger and this princess, O best of virtuous men, has by serving you, conquered affliction, desire, illusion, enmity and lassitude of mind.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: भीष्म उवाच शुल्कानां तु सहस्त्रेण वाजिनां रथमुत्तमम्। युक्तं प्रगृह्य भगवान् वासवोऽप्याजगाम तम्॥
en: Bhishma said Then, riding in a fine chariot drawn by a thousand white steeds, the glorious Vasava approached that Brahmana.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: मृत्युरात्मा च लोकाश्च जिता भूतानि पञ्च च। बुद्धिः कालो मनो व्योम कामक्रोधौ तथैव च॥
en: Therefore, O best of men, do you remember that a to householder there is no greater god than the guest.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: तस्माद् गृहाश्रमस्थस्य नान्यद् दैवतमस्ति वै। ऋतेऽतिथिं नरव्याघ्र मनसैतद् विचारय॥ अतिथिः पूजितो यद्धि ध्यायते मनसा शुभम्। न तत् क्रतुशतेनापि तुल्यमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: The learned say that the blessings of an honoured guest are more fruitful than the merit of a hundred sacrifices.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: पात्रं त्वतिथिमासाद्य शीलाढ्यं यो न पूजयेत्। स दत्त्वा दुष्कृतं तस्मै पुण्यमादाय गच्छति॥
en: Whenever a deserving guest seeks the hospitality of a householder and is not respected by him, he takes away all the virtues of the latter giving him his sins.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: एतत् ते कथितं पुत्र मयाऽऽख्यानमनुत्तमम्। यथा हि विजितो मृत्युर्गृहस्थेन पुराभवत्॥
en: I have now recited to you, my son, this excellent story as to how Death was conquered in days of yore by a householder.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यमिदमाख्यानमुत्तमम्। बुभूषताभिमन्तव्यं सर्वदुश्चरितापहम्॥
en: The recital of this excellent story gives glory, fame, and longevity. The man who seeks worldly prosperity should consider it as powerful in removing all evil.

description: The story of Sudarshana and Oghavati. How death was conquered by a householder
sn: इदं यः कथयेद् विद्वानहन्यहनि भारत। सुदर्शनस्य चरितं पुण्याँल्लोकानवाप्नुयात्॥
en: And, O Bharata, the learned man who daily recites this story of the life of Sudarshana acquires blessed regions.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्राह्मण्यं यदि दुष्प्राप्यं त्रिभिर्वर्णैर्नराधिप। कथं प्राप्तं महाराज क्षत्रियेण महात्मना॥ विश्वामित्रेण धर्मात्पन् ब्राह्मणत्वं नरर्षभ। श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वेन तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said If, O prince, it is so very difficult for the other three castes to acquire Brahmanahood, how then did the great Vishvasmitra, O king, though a Kshatriya, acquire the status of a Brahmana? I desire to know this, O sire! Therefore, do you truly describe this matter to me.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: तेन ह्यमितवीर्येण वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः। हतं पुत्रशतं सद्यस्तपसाऽपि पितामह॥
en: O Sire, by virtue of his austerities that powerful man destroyed in a moment the hundred sons of the great Vasishtha.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: यातुधानाश्च बहवो राक्षसास्तिग्मतेजसः। मन्युनाऽऽविष्टदेहेन सृष्टाः कालान्तकोपमाः॥
en: While under the influence of ire, he created numberless evil spirits and Rakshasas of great vigour and resembling the great destroyer Kala himself.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: महान् कुशिकवंशश्च ब्रह्मर्षिशतसंकुलः। स्थापितो नरलोकेऽस्मिन् विद्वद्ब्राह्मणसंस्तुतः॥
en: The great and learned family of Kushika, containing hundreds of twiceborn sages in it and highly spoken of by the Brahmanas, was founded in this world of men by him.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: ऋचीकस्यात्मजश्चैव शुनःशेपो महातपाः। विमोक्षितो महासत्रात् पशुतामप्युपागतः॥
en: Having been sought to be killed as an animal in the great sacrifice of Amvarisha, Shunashepha of austere penances the son of Richika acquired his deliverance through Vishvamitra.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: हरिश्चन्द्रक्रतौ देवांस्तोषयित्वाऽऽत्मतेजसा। पुत्रतामनु सम्प्राप्तो विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः॥
en: Having pleased the gods at a sacrifice Harishchandra became a son of the wise Vishvamitra.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: नाभिवादयते ज्येष्ठं देवरातं नराधिप। पुत्राः पञ्चाशदेवापि शप्ताः श्वपचतां गताः॥
en: For not having honoured their eldest brother Devarat, the other fifty brothers of his were imprecated, and all of them became Chandalas.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: त्रिशङ्कुर्वन्धुभिर्मुक्त ऐक्ष्वाकः प्रीतिपूर्वकम्। अवाशिरा दिवं नीतो दक्षिणामाश्रितो दिशम्॥
en: When abandoned by his friends, and hanging with his head down wards in the lower regions, Trisanku, the son of Ikshaku, was translated to heaven at the pleasure of Vishvamitra.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: विश्वामित्रस्य विपुला नदी देवर्षिसेविता। कौशिकी च शिवा पुण्या ब्रह्मर्षिसुरसेविता॥
en: Vishvamitra had a large river, named Kaushiki, that was frequented by celestial Rishis. This sacred and suspicious river was frequented by the celestials and twiceborn Rishis.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: तपोविनकरी चैव पञ्चचूडा सुसम्मता। रम्भा नामाप्सराः शापाद् यस्य शैलत्वमागता॥
en: For disturbing his devotions, the famous celestial nymph Rambha, having fine bracelets, was cursed and changed into a rock.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: तथैवास्य भयाद् बद्ध्वा वसिष्ठः सलिले पुरा। आत्मानं मज्जयन् श्रीमान् विपाशः पुनरुत्थितः॥
en: From fear of Vishvamitra the glorious Vasishtha, in days of yore, binding himself with creepers, threw himself down into a river and again rose released from his fetters,

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: तदाप्रभृति पुण्या हि विपाशाऽभून्महानदी। विख्याता कर्मणा तेन वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः॥
en: On account of this, that large and sacred river became thenceforth famous by the name of Vipasha.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: वाग्भिश्च भगवान् येन देवसेनाग्रगः प्रभुः। स्तुतः प्रीतमनाश्चासीच्छापाञ्चैनममुञ्चत॥ ध्रुवस्यौत्तानपादस्य ब्रह्मर्षीणां तथैव च। मध्यं ज्वलति यो नित्यमुदीचीमाश्रितो दिशम्॥
en: He prayed to the glorious and powerful Indra who was pleased with him and freed him from a curse. Remaining on the northern side of the sky, he sheds his lustre from a position in the midst of the seven twiceborn Rishis, and Dhruva the son of Uttanpada.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: तस्यैतानि च कर्माणि तथान्यानि च कौरव। क्षत्रियस्येत्यतो जातमिदं कौतूहलं मम॥
en: These and many others are his feats. O descendant of Kuru, my curiosity has been kindled in this respect, because they were performed by a Kshstriya.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: किमेतदिति तत्त्वेन प्रब्रूहि भरतर्षभ। देहान्तरमनासाद्य कथं स ब्राह्मणोऽभवत्॥
en: Therefore, O foremost one of Bharata's race do you relate this matter to me truly! How without renouncing his body and taking another body of flesh could he become a Brahmana?

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: एतत् तत्त्वेन मे तात सर्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि। मतङ्गस्य यथातत्त्वं तथैवैतद् वदस्व मे॥
en: Do you, O sire, truly describe this matter to me as you have described to me the story of Matanga.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: स्थाने मतङ्गा ब्राह्मण्यं नालभद् भरतर्षभ। चण्डालयोनौ जातो हि कथं ब्राह्मण्यमाप्तवान्॥
en: Matanga was born as a Chandala, and could not acquire Brahmanahood, but how could this man acquire the status of a Brahmana?

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: किमेतदिति तत्त्वेन प्रब्रूहि भरतर्षभ। देहान्तरमनासाद्य कथं स ब्राह्मणोऽभवत्॥
en: Therefore, O foremost one of Bharata's race do you relate this matter to me truly! How without renouncing his body and taking another body of flesh could he become a Brahmana?

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: एतत् तत्त्वेन मे तात सर्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि। मतङ्गस्य यथातत्त्वं तथैवैतद् वदस्व मे॥
en: Do you, O sire, truly describe this matter to me as you have described to me the story of Matanga.

description: The story of Vishvamitra as being promoted from a Kshatriya to a Brahmana
sn: स्थाने मतङ्गा ब्राह्मण्यं नालभद् भरतर्षभ। चण्डालयोनौ जातो हि कथं ब्राह्मण्यमाप्तवान्॥
en: Matanga was born as a Chandala, and could not acquire Brahmanahood, but how could this man acquire the status of a Brahmana?

sn: भीष्म उवाच श्रूयतां पार्थ तत्त्वेन विश्वामित्रो यथा पुरा। ब्राह्मणत्वं गतस्तात ब्रह्मर्षित्वं तथैव च॥
en: Bhishma said Listen truly in full, O son of Pritha, how, in days of yore, Vishvamitra acquired the status of a Brahmana, as also of a Brahmana Rishi!

sn: भरतस्यान्वये चैवाजमीढो नाम पार्थिवः। बभूव भरतश्रेष्ठ यज्वा धर्मभृतां वरः॥
en: There was O foremost of Bharata's descendants, in the family of Bharata, a king named Ajamida, who celebrated many sacrifices and was the best of all virtuous men.

sn: तस्य पुत्रो महानासीज्जह्वर्नाम नरेश्वरः। दुहितृत्वमनुप्राप्ता गङ्गा यस्य महात्मनः॥
en: His son was the great king named Jahnu. Ganga was the daughter of this great prince.

sn: तस्यात्मजस्तुल्यगुणः सिधुद्वीपो महायशाः। सिन्धुद्वीपाच्च राजर्षिर्बलाकाश्वो महाबलः॥
en: The far-fained and equally virtuous Sindhudvipa was the son of this prince. From Sindhudvipa sprang the great royal sage Valakashva.

sn: वल्लभस्तस्य तनयः साक्षाद्धर्म इवापरः। कुशिकस्तस्य तनयः सहस्त्राक्षसमद्युतिः॥
en: His son was named Vallabha who was like a second Dharina incarnate. His son was Kushika who was illustrious like the thousandeyed Indra.

sn: कुशिकस्यात्मजः श्रीमान् गाधिर्नाम जनेश्वरः। अपुत्रः प्रसवेनार्थी वनवासमुपावसत्॥
en: Kushika's son was the illustrious king Gadhi who, being childless and wishing to have a son born to him, went to the forest.

sn: कन्या जज्ञे सुतात् तस्य वने निवसतः सतः। नाम्ना सत्यवती नाम रूपेणाप्रतिभा भुवि॥
en: While living there, a daughter was born to him. She was called Satyavati, and she was peerless in beauty on Earth.

sn: तां वज्र भार्गवः श्रीमांश्च्यवनस्यात्मसम्भवः। ऋचीक इति विख्यातो विपुले तपसि स्थितः॥
en: The illustrious son of Chyavana, known by the name of Richika, of the family of Bhrigu, gifted with austere penance's, sought the hand of this lady.

sn: स तां न प्रददौ तस्मै ऋचीकाय महात्मने। दरिद्र इति मत्वा वै गाधिः शत्रुनिबर्हणः॥
en: Thinking him to be poor, Gadhi, the destroyer of his enemies, did not bestow her in marriage upon the great Richika.

sn: प्रत्याख्याय पुनर्यातमब्रवीद् राजसत्तमः। शुल्कं प्रदीयतां मह्यं ततो वत्स्यसि मे सुताम्॥
en: But when the latter, thus dismissed, was going away, the excellent king, addressing him, said If you can give me a marriage dower you will have my daughter as your wife!

sn: ऋचीक उवाच किं प्रयच्छामि राजेन्द्र तुभ्यं शुल्कमहं नृप। दुहितुर्ब्रह्यसंसक्तो माऽभूत् तत्र विचारणा॥ चन्द्ररश्मिप्रकाशानां हयानां वातरंहसाम्। एकतः श्यामकर्णानां सहस्रं देहि भार्गव॥
en: Richika said What dower, O king, shall I offer you for the hand of your daughter? Tell me truly, without any hesitation whatsoever! Gadhi said, O Descendant of Bhrigu, give me a thousand horses quickcoursing as the wind, and possessing the colour of moonbeams, and each having one ear black.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः स भृगुशार्दूलश्च्यवनस्यात्मजः प्रभुः। अब्रवीद् वरुणं देवमादित्यं पतिमम्भसाम्॥ एकतः श्यामकर्णानां हयानां चन्द्रवर्चसाम्। सहस्रं वातवेगानां भिक्षे त्वां देवसत्तम॥
en: Bhishma said Then that powerful son of Chyavana who was the foremost of Bhrigu's family, besought the god Varuna, the son of Aditi, who was the lord of all the waters. O best of gods, I pray to you io give me a thousand horses, all fleet like the wind and having complexion as effulgent as the moon's, but each having one ear black.

sn: तथेति वरुणो देव आदित्यो भृगुसत्तमम्। उवाच यत्र ते च्छन्दस्तत्रोत्थास्यन्ति वाजिनः॥ ध्यातमात्र ऋचीकेन हयानां चन्द्रवर्चसाम्। गङ्गाजलात् समुत्तस्थौ सहस्रं विपुलौजसाम्॥
en: The god Varuna, the son of Aditi, said to that scion Bhrigu's race Be it so! Whenever you will seek, the horses shall come. As soon as Richika thought of them, there came from the waters of Ganga a thousand highborn horses, as effulgent as the moon.

sn: अदूरे कान्यकुब्जस्य गङ्गायास्तीरमुत्तमम्। अश्वतीर्थे तदद्यापि मानवैः परिचक्ष्यते॥
en: Not far from Kanyakuvja, the sacred bank of Ganga is still famous among men as Ashvatirtha on account of the appearance of those horses.

sn: ततो वै माधये तात सहस्रं वाजिनां शुभम्। ऋचीकः प्रददौ प्रीतः शुल्कार्थं तपतां वरः॥
en: Then Richika, that best of ascetics, pleased in mind, gave those thousand excellent horses to Gadhi as the marriage gift.

sn: ततः स विस्मितो राजा गाधिः शापभयेन च। ददौ तां समलंकृत्य कन्यां भृगुसुताय वै॥
en: King Gadhi, stricken with wonder and fearing to be cursed, gave his daughter, adorned with jewels, to that son of Bhrigu.

sn: जग्राह विधिवत् पाणिं तस्या ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमः। सा च तं पतिमासाद्य परं हर्षमवाप ह॥
en: That foremost of twiceborn Rishis accepted her hand in marriage according to due rites. The princes too was wellpleased at seeing herself the wife of that Brahmana.

sn: स तुतोष च ब्रह्मर्षिस्तस्या वृत्तेन भारत। छन्दयामास चैवैनां वरेण वरवर्णिनीम्॥
en: That foremost of twiceborn Rishis, O Bharata, was well pleased with her conduct and expressed a desire to grant her a boon.

sn: मात्रे तत् सर्वमाचख्यौ सा कन्या राजसत्तम। अथ तामब्रवीन्माता सुतां किंचिदवाङ्मुखी॥ ममापि पुत्रि भर्ता ते प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हति। अपत्यस्य प्रदानेन समर्थश्च महातपाः॥
en: The princess, O excellent king, communicated this to her mother. The mother said to the daughter that stood before her with downcast eyes You should, O my daughter, secure a favour for me also from your husband. That sage of austere penances is competent to grant a boon to me, the boon, viz., of the birth of a son to mc.

sn: ततः सा त्वरितं गत्वा तत् सर्वं प्रत्यवेदयत्। मातुश्चिकीर्षितं राजन् ऋचीकस्तामथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Then, O king, returning speedily to her husband Richika, the princess described to him all that had been wished for by her mother.

sn: गुणवन्तमपत्यं सा अचिराज्जनयिष्यति। मम प्रसादात् कल्याणि माऽभूत् ते प्रणयोऽन्यथा॥२५
en: By my favour, O blessed one, she will soon give birth to a son gifted with every virtue! May your request be fulfilled!

sn: तव चैव गुणश्लाघी पुत्र उत्पत्स्यते महान्। अस्मद्वंशकरः श्रीमान् सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Of you too shall be born a powerful and glorious son who, gifted with virtue, shall perpetuate my race. Truly do I say this to you.

sn: ऋतुस्नाता च साऽश्वत्थं त्वं च वृक्षमुदुम्बरम्। परिष्वजेथाः कल्याणि तत एवमवाप्स्यथः॥
en: When you two shall bathe in your season, she shall embrace a pepul tree, and you, O excellent lady, shall embrace a fig tree, and by so doing you shall have the fruition of your desires.

sn: चरुद्वयमिदं चैव मन्त्रपूतं शुचिस्मिते। त्वं च सा चोपभुञ्जीतं ततः पुत्राववाप्स्यथः॥
en: O sweetlysmiling lady, both she and you shall have to partake of these two sacrificial offerings (charu) consecrated with hymns, and then you shall get sons.

sn: ततः सत्यवती हृष्टा मातरं प्रत्यभाषत। यदृचीकेन कथितं तच्चाचख्यौ चरुद्वयम्॥
en: Thereat, Satyavati, pleased at heart, told her mother all that had been said by Richika as also of the two balls of charu.

sn: तामुवाच ततो माता सुतां सत्यवती तदा। पुत्रि पूर्वोपपन्नायाः कुरुष्व वचनं मम॥
en: Then the mother, addressing her daughter Satyavati, said: O daughter, as I deserve greater respect from you than your husband, do you obey my words.

sn: भळ य एष दत्तस्ते चर्मन्त्रपुरस्कृतः। एनं प्रयच्छ मह्यं त्वं मदीयं त्वं गृहाण च॥
en: Do you give me the charu, duly consecrated with hymns, which your husband has given you, and yourself take, the one that has been intended for me.

sn: व्यत्यासं वृक्षयोश्चापि करवाव शुचिस्मिते। यदि प्रमाणं वचनं मम मातुरनिन्दिते॥
en: O sweetlysmiling one of pure character, if you have any reverence for my word, let us change the trees respectively intended for us.

sn: स्वमपत्यं विशिष्टं हि सर्व इच्छत्यनाविलम्। व्यक्तं भगवता चात्र कृतमेवं भविष्यति॥
en: Every one wishes to possess an excellent and pure son. The illustrious Richika too must have acted from the same motive in this matter as will appear in the long run.

sn: ततो मे त्वच्चरौ भावः पादपे च सुमध्यमे। कथं विशिष्टो भ्राता मे भवेदित्येव चिन्तय॥
en: Therefore, O beautiful girl, my heart is bent upon your charu and tree, and you too should also try to secure an excellent brother for yourself.

sn: तथा च कृतवत्यौ ते माता सत्यवती च सा। अथ गर्भावनप्राप्ते उभे ते वै युधिष्ठिर॥
en: The mother and the daughter Satyavati having acted thus, they both, O Yudhishthira, became big with child.

sn: दृष्ट्वा गर्भमनुप्राप्तां भार्यो स च महानृषिः। उवाच तां सत्यवती दुर्मना भृगुसत्तमः॥
en: Finding his wife quick with child, that great Rishi, the descendant of Bhrigu, became pleased at heart, and addressing her, said:

sn: व्यत्यासेनोपयुक्तस्ते चरुर्व्यक्तं भविष्यति। व्यत्यास: पादपे चापि सुव्यक्तं कृतः शुभे॥
en: O excellent lady, you have not done well in exchanging the charu as will soon be seen. It is also clear that you have changed the trees.

sn: मया हि विश्वं यद्ब्रह्म त्वच्चरौ संनिवेशितम्। क्षत्रवीर्यं च सकलं चरौ तस्या निवेशितम्॥
en: I had put the entire accuinulated energy of Brahma in your charu and Kshatriya energy in the charu of your mother.

sn: त्रैलोक्यविख्यातगुणं त्वं विप्रं जनयिष्यसि। सा च क्षत्रं विशिष्टं वै तत एतत् कृतं मया॥
en: I had so settled that you would give birth to a Brahmana whose virtues would be famous throughout the three worlds, and that she would give birth to an excellent Kshatriya.

sn: व्यत्यासस्तु कृतो यस्मात् त्वया मात्रा च ते शुभे। तस्मात् ब्राह्मणं श्रेष्ठं माता ते जनयिष्यति॥ क्षत्रियं तूप्रकर्माणं त्वं भद्रे जनयिष्यसि। न हि ते तत् कृतं साधु मातृस्नेहेन भाविनि॥ ते
en: But now, O excellent lady, as you have changed the order (of the charu so), your mother give birth to an excellent Brahmana, and you too, O excellent lady, will give birth to a Kshatriya of dreadful deeds. You have not done well, O lady, by doing this out of affection for your mother.

sn: सा श्रुत्वा शोकसंतप्ता पपात वरवर्णिनी। भूमौ सत्यवती राजन् छिन्नेव रुचिरा लता॥
en: Hearing this, O king, the excellent lady Satyavati, filled with sorrow, dropped upon the ground like a beautiful creeper cut in two parts.

sn: प्रतिलभ्य च सा संज्ञां शिरसा प्रणिपत्य च। उवाच भार्या भर्तारं गाधेयी भार्गवर्षभम्॥ प्रसादयन्त्यां भार्यायां मयि ब्रह्मविदां वर। प्रसादं कुरु विप्रर्षे न मे स्यात् क्षत्रियः सुतः॥
en: Regaining her senses and bowing to her lord with head (bent), the daughter of Gadhi said to her husband, that foremost one of Bhrigu's race'O twiceborn Rishi, O you who are foremost amongst those versed in Brahma, have mercy on me, your wife, who is thus appeasing you and so order that a Kshatriya son may not be born to me.

sn: कामं ममोग्रकर्मा वै पौत्रो भवितुमर्हति। स्यात् सुतो ब्रह्मन्नेष मे दायतां वरः॥
en: Let my grandson be such a one as will be farnous for his dreadful feats if it be your desire, but not my son, O Brahmana! Do you grant me this favour.

sn: एवमस्त्विति होवाच स्वां भार्यो सुमहातपाः। ततः सा जनयामास जमदग्निं सुतं शुभम्॥
en: Be it so, said that Rishi of austere penances to his wife and then, O king, she gave birth to a blessed son named Jamadagni.

sn: विश्वामित्रं चाजनयद् गाधिभार्या यशस्विनी। ऋषेः प्रसादाद् राजेन्द्र ब्रह्मर्षेब्रह्मवादिनम्॥
en: The famous wife of Gadhi too gave birth to the twiceborn Rishi Vishvamitra versed in the knowledge of Brahma, by favour of that Rishi.

sn: ततो ब्राह्मणतां यातो विश्वामित्रो महातपाः। न तु मे तथर्षिः सैन्धवायनः॥ क्षत्रियः सोऽप्यथ तथा ब्रह्मवंशस्य कारकः॥
en: The highly pious Vishvamitra, though a Kshatriya, gained the dignity of a Brahmana and became the founder of a race of Brahmanas.

sn: तस्य पुत्रा महात्मानो ब्रह्मवंशविवर्धनाः। तपस्विनो ब्रह्मविदो गोत्रकार एव च॥
en: His sons became great progenitors of many race of Brahmanas who were given to austere penances, learned in the Vedas, and founders of many clans.

sn: मधुच्छन्दश्च भगवान् देवरातश्च वीर्यवान्। अक्षीणश्च शकुन्तश्च भ्रुः कालपथस्तथा॥ याज्ञवल्क्यश्च विख्यातस्तथा स्थूणो महाव्रतः। उलूको यमदूतश्च वल्गुजङ्घश्च भगवान् गालवश्च महानृषिः। ऋषिर्वज्रस्तथा ख्यातः सालंकायन एव च॥ लीलाढ्यो नारदश्चैव तथा कूर्चामुखः स्मृतः। वादुलिर्मुसलश्चैव वक्षोग्रीवस्तथैव च॥
en: The worshipful Madhuchchhanda and the powerful Devrat, Akshina, Shakunta, Vabhru, Kalapatha, the celebrated Yajnavalkya, Sthuna of great vows, Uluka, Mudgala, and the sage Saindhavayana, the illustrious Valgujangha and the great Rishi Galava, Ruchi, the celebrated Vajra, as also Salankayana, Liladhya, and Narada, the one known as Kurchamukha, and Vahuli Mushala as also Vakshogriva.

sn: आंघ्रिको नैकदृक् चैव शिलायूपः शितः शुचिः। चक्रको मारुतन्तव्यो वातमोऽथाश्वलायनः॥ श्यामायनोऽश्च गार्यश्च जाबालिः सुश्रुतस्तथा। कारीषिरथ संश्रुत्यः परपौरवतन्तवः॥ महानृषिश्च कपिलस्तथर्षिस्ताडकायनः। तथैव चोपगहनस्तथर्षिश्चासुरायणः॥ मार्दमर्षिर्हिरण्याक्षो जङ्गारिर्बाभ्रवायणिः। भूतिर्विभूतिः सूतश्च सुरकृत् तु तथैव च॥ अरालि चिकाचैव चाम्पेयोज्जयनौ तथा। नवतन्तुर्बकनखः सेयनो यतिरेव च॥ अम्भोरुहश्चास्मत्स्यः शिरीषी चाथ गार्दभिः। उर्जयोनिरुदापेक्षी नारदी च महानृषिः॥ विश्वामित्रात्मजाः सर्वे मुनयो ब्रह्मवादिनः। तथैव क्षत्रियो राजन् विश्वामित्रो महातपाः॥ ऋचीकेनाहितं ब्रह्म परमेतद् युधिष्ठिर। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं तत्त्वेन भरतर्षभ॥ विश्वामित्रस्य वै जन्म सोमसूर्याग्नितेजसः।
en: Anghrika, Naikadrik, Shilayupa, Shita, Suchi, Chakraka, Marutantavya, Vataghna, Ashvalayana and Shyamayana, Gargya, and Javali, as also Sushruta, Karishi, Sangshrutya, and Par Paurava, and Tantu, the great sage Kapila, Tarakayana, Upagahana, Asurayani, Margama, Hiranyaksha, Janghari, Bhavravayani, and Suti, Bibhuti, Suta, Surakrit, Arani, Nachika, Champeya, Ujjayana, Navatantu, Vakanakhs, Sayana, Vati, Ambhoruha, Amatsyhin, Shirishin, Gardhavi, Urjjayoni, Udapekshin, and the great Rishi Naradin these ascetics were all sons of Vishvamitra and were versed in the knowledge of Brahma. O king Yudhishthira, the greatly austere and pious Vishvamitra, although a Kshatriya, became a Brahmana for Richika having placed the energy of supreme Brahma (in the charu), O foremost prince of Bharata's family! I have now described to you, in full, the story of the birth of Vishvamitra who was gifted with the birth of Vishvamitra who was gifted with the energy of the sun, the moon, and the firegod.

sn: यत्र यत्र च संदेहो भूयस्ते राजसत्तम। तत्र तत्र च मां ब्रूहि च्छेत्तास्मि तव संशयम्॥
en: 0 best of kings, if you have any doubt about any other subject, please let me know it, so that I may remove it.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आनृशंस्यस्य धर्मज्ञ गुणान् भक्तजनस्य च। श्रोतुमिच्छामि धर्मज्ञ तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said O you who know the truths of religion, I wish to hear of the merits of religion, I wish to hear of the merits of mercy, and of the marks of devout men! Do you, O sire, describe them to me.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। वासवस्य च संवादं शुकस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: Bhishma said “Regarding it, this ancient legend, the story of Vasava and the great Shuka, is cited as an illustration.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: विषये काशिराजस्य ग्रामानिष्क्रम्य लुब्धकः। सविषं काण्डमादाय मृगयामास वै मृगम्॥
en: In the dominion of the king of Kashi, a fowler, having poisoned arrows with him, went out of his village on hunting expedition in search of antelopes.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: तत्र चामिषलुब्धेन लुब्धकेन महावने। अविदूरे मृगान् दृष्ट्वा बाणः प्रतिसमाहितः॥
en: Desirous of getting meat, when in a big forest in pursuit of the chase, he saw a drove of antelopes near at hand, and shot his arrow at one of them.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: तेन दुर्वारितास्त्रेण निमित्तचपलेषुणा। महान् वनतरुस्तत्र विद्धो मृगजिघांसया॥
en: The arrow of that fowler of irresistible arms, shot for the destruction of the antelope, missing its aim, pierced a powerful foresttree.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: स तीक्ष्णविषदिग्धेन शरेणातिवलात् क्षतः। उत्सृज्य फलपत्राणि पादपः शोषमागतः॥
en: The tree, pierced with that arrow covered with dreadful poison, withered away, shedding its leaves and fruits.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: तस्मिन् वृक्षे तथाभूते कोटरेषु चिरोषितः। न जहाति शुको वासं तस्य भक्त्या वनस्पतेः॥
en: The tree having thus withered, a parrot which had lived in a hollow of its trunk all his life, did not leave his nest out of affection for that lordly tree.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: निष्प्रचारो निराहारो ग्लान: शिथिलवागपि। कृतज्ञः सह वृक्षण धर्मात्मा सोऽप्यशुष्यत॥
en: Motionless starving, silent and sorrowful, that grateful and virtuous parrot also withered away with the tree.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: तमुदारं महासत्त्वमतिमानुषचेष्टितम्। समदुःखसुखं दृष्ट्वा विस्मित: पाकशासनः॥
en: The conqueror of Paka (Indra) was filled with wonder upon seeing that great and generous bird thus uninfluenced by misery or happiness and possessing extraordinary resolution.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: ततश्चिन्तामुपगतः शक्रः कथमयं द्विजः। तिर्यग्योनावसम्भाव्यमानृशंस्यमवस्थितः॥
en: Then Shakra thought, How could this bird come to possess such humane and generous feelings which cannot be seen in one of the lower animal creation?

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: अथवा नात्र चित्रं हि अभवद् वासवस्य तु। प्राणिनामपि सर्वेषां सर्वं सर्वत्र दृश्यते॥
en: There is nothing wonderful in the matter, for all crcatures are seen to show kindly and generous feelings towards others.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: ततो ब्राह्मणवेषेण मानुषं रूपमास्थितः। अवतीर्य महीं शक्रस्तं पक्षिणमुवाच ह॥
en: Assuming then the shape of a Brahmana, Shakra went on the Earth and addressing the bird, said:

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: शुक भो पक्षिणां श्रेष्ठ दाक्षेयी सुप्रजा त्वया। पृच्छे त्वां शुकमेनं त्वं कस्मान्न त्यजसि दुमम्॥
en: O Suka, O best of birds, the granddaughter of Daksha has become blessed (by having you as her offspring)! I ask you, why do you not leave this withered tree?

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: अथ पृष्टः शुकः प्राह मूर्धा समभिवाद्य तम्। स्वागतं देवराज त्वं विज्ञातस्तपसा मया॥
en: Thus accosted, the Shuka bowed to him and thus replied: Welcome to you, O king of the gods, I have recognised you by the merit of my austere penances.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: ततो दशशताक्षेण साधु साध्विति भाषितम्। अहो विज्ञानमित्येवं मनसा पूजितस्ततः॥
en: Well-done, well-done! said the thousandeyed god. Then the latter lauded him in his mind, saying 0, how wonderful is the knowledge which he possesses.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: तमेवं शुभकर्माणं शुकं परमधार्मिकम्। विजानन्नपि तां प्रीतिं पप्रच्छ बलसूदनः॥
en: Although the destroyer of Vala knew that parrot to be of a greatly virtuous character and meritorious in action, he still enquired of him about the reason of his love for the tree.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: निष्पत्रमफलं शुष्कमशरण्यं पतत्रिणाम्। किमर्थं सेवसे वृक्षं यदा महदिदं वनम्॥ अन्येऽपि बहवो वृक्षाः पत्रसंच्छन्नकोटराः। पर्याप्तसंचारा विद्यन्तेऽस्मिन् महावने॥
en: This tree is withered and it is without leaves and fruits, and is unfit to be the refuge of birds. Why do you then cling to it? This forest too is vast and in this wilderness there are numberless other good trees whose hollows are covered with leaves and which you can choose freely and to your heart's content.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: गतायुषमसामर्थ्य क्षीणसारं हतश्रियम्। विमृश्य प्रज्ञया धीर जहीमं स्थविरं दुमम्॥
en: patient one, displaying proper discrimination in your wisdom, do you leave this old tree that is dead and useless and shorn of all its leaves and no longer capable of any good.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: भीष्म उवाच तदुपश्रुत्य धर्मात्मा शुकः शक्रेण भाषितम्। शुभाः पर्या सुदीर्घमतिनिःश्वस्य दीनो वाक्यमुवाच ह॥ अनतिक्रमणीयानि दैवतानि शचीपते। यत्राभवत् तव प्रश्नस्तन्निबोध सुराधिप॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words of Shakra, the virtuous Shuka, heaved a deep sigh, and sorrowfully replied to him, saying O husband of Sachi, and chief of the gods, the ordinances of the gods should always be obeyed. Do you hear of the reason of the thing about which you have asked me.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: अस्मिन्नहं दुमे जातः साधुभिश्च गुणैर्युतः। बालभावेन संगुप्तः शत्रुभिश्च न धर्षितः॥
en: Here, within this tree, was I born and here in this tree have all the good traits of my character been developed, and here in this tree was I protected in my infancy from the attacks of my enemies.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: किमनुक्रोश्य वैफल्यमुत्पादयसि मेऽनघ। आनृशंस्याभियुक्तस्य भक्तस्यानन्यगस्य च॥
en: O sinless one, why are you, in your kindness, interfering with the principle of my conduct in life? I am merciful and devoutly intent on virtue, and firm in conduct.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: अनुक्रोशो हि साधूनां महद्धर्मस्य लक्षणम्। अनुक्रोशश्च साधूनां सदा प्रीतिं प्रयच्छति॥
en: Kindliness of feeling is the highest test of virtue amongst the good, and this same merciful and humane feeling is the source of eternal happiness to the virtuous,

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: त्वमेव दैवतैः सर्वैः पृच्छसे धर्मसंशयात्। अतस्त्वं देवदेवानामाधिपत्ये प्रतिष्ठितः॥
en: All the gods ask you to remove their doubts in religion, and for this reason, O lord, you have been elected their king.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: नार्हसे मां सहस्त्राक्ष दुमं त्याजयितुं चिरात्। समर्थमुपजीव्येमं त्यजेयं कथमद्य वै॥ तस्य वाक्येन सौम्येन हर्षित: पाकशासनः। शुकं प्रोवाच धर्मात्मा आनृशंस्येन तोषितः॥
en: You should not, O thousandeyed one, advise me now to leave this tree for good. When it was capable of good, it supported my life. How can I leave it now? Pleased with these wellmeant words of the parrot, the virtuous destroyer of Paka, thus said to him:I am pleased with your humane and merciful disposition.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: वरं वृणीष्वेति तदा स च वने वरं शुकः। आनृशंस्यपरो नित्यं तस्य वृक्षस्य सम्भवम्॥
en: Do you ask a boon of me. At this, the merciful parrot craved this boon of him, saying Let this tree revive.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: विदित्वा च दृढां भक्तिं तां शुके शीलसम्पदम्। प्रीतः क्षिप्रमथो वृक्षममृतेनावसिक्तवान्॥
en: Knowing the great attachment of the parrot to that tree and great high character, Indra, wellpleased, caused the tree to be quickly sprinkled over with nectar.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: ततः फलानि पत्राणि शाखाश्चापि मनोहराः। शुकस्य दृढभक्तित्वाच्छ्रीमतां प्राप स दुमः॥ शुकश्च कर्मणा तेन आनृशंस्यकृतेन वै। आयुषोऽन्ते महाराज प्राप शक्रसलोकताम्॥
en: Then that tree became revived and grand through the penanres of the parrot, and the latter, too, O great king, at the end of his life, acquired the companionship of Shakra by virtue of that act of mercy.

description: The merits of mercy and the marks of devout men. The story of Vasava and the great Suka
sn: एवमेव मनुष्येन्द्र भक्तिमन्तं समाश्रितः। सर्वार्थसिद्धिं लभते शुकं प्राप्य यथा द्रुमः॥
en: Thus, o king, by communion and companionship with the pious, people acquire all the objects of their desire even as the tree did through its companionship with the parrot."

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामह महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद। दैवे पुरुषकारे च किंस्विच्छ्रेष्ठतरं भवेत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said Of Exertion and Destiny, tell me O learned sire who are versed in all the scriptures, which is the more potent?

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। वसिष्ठस्य च संवादं ब्रह्मणश्च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said This ancient story of the conversation of Vasishtha and Brahman. O Yudhishthira, explain this matter.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: दैवमानुषयोः किंस्वित् कर्मणोः श्रेष्ठमित्युत। पुरा वसिष्ठो भगवान् पितामहमपृच्छत॥
en: In days of yore the worshipful Vasishta enquired of Brahman as to which among these two, viz., the Karma of a creature acquired in this life, or that acquired in pristine lives (and called Destiny), is the more powerful in shaping his life.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: ततः पद्मोद्भवो राजन् देवदेवः पितामहः। उवाच मधुरं वाक्यमर्थवद्धेतुभूषितम्॥
en: Then, O king, the great god Brahman, who had originated from the primeval lotus. answered him in these sweet and wellreasoned pregnant words.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच नाबीजं जायते किंचिन्न बीजेन विना फलम्। बीजाद् बीजं प्रभवति बीजादेव फलं स्मृतम्॥
en: Brahmana said Nothing springs into existence without seed. Without seed, fruits do not grow. From seeds originate other seeds. Hence are fruits known to be sprung from seeds.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: यादृशं वपते बीजं क्षेत्रमासाद्य कर्षकः। सुकृते दुष्कृते वापि तादृशं लभते फलम्॥
en: According to the good or bad seed that the husbandman sows in his field, he reaps good or bad fruits.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: यथा बीजं विना क्षेत्रमुप्तं भवति निष्फलम्। तथा पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति॥
en: As, unsown with seed, the soil, through tilled, becomes fruitless, so, without personal Exertion, Destiny is of no use.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: क्षेत्रं पुरुषकारस्तु दैवं बीजमुदाहृतम्। क्षेत्रबीजसमायोगात् ततः सस्यं समृद्ध्यते॥
en: One's own deeds are like the soil, and Destiny is compared to the seed. The harvest grows from the union of the soil and seed.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: कर्मणः फलनिर्वृत्तिं स्वयमश्नाति कारकः। प्रत्यक्षं दृश्यते लोके कृतस्यापकृतस्य च॥ शुभेन कर्मणा सौख्यं दुःखं पापेन कर्मणा। कृतं फलति सर्वत्र नाकृतं भुज्यते क्वचित्॥
en: It is seen every day in the world that the doer reaps the fruit of his good and evil acts; that happiness results from goods deeds, and pain is the outcome of evil ones; that acts, when done, always fructify; and that, if not done, no fruit arises.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: कृती सर्वत्र लभते प्रतिष्ठां भाग्यसंयुताम्। अकृती लभते भ्रष्टः क्षते क्षारावसेचनम्॥
en: A man of (good) act gains merits with good fortune, while and idler loses his estate, and reaps evil like the infusion of alkaline matter injected into a wound.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: तपसा रूपसौभाग्यं रत्नानि विविधानि च। प्राप्यते कर्मणा सर्वे न दैवादकृतात्मना॥
en: By firm application, one acquires beauty, fortune, and all sorts of riches. Everything can be obtained by Exertion: but nothing can be gained through Destiny only, by a man who lacks personal Exertion.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: तथा स्वर्गश्च भोगश्च निष्ठा या च मनीषिता। सर्वं पुरुषकारेण कृतेनेहोपलभ्यते॥
en: One attains to heaven, and all the object of enjoyment, as also the fulfilment of his heart's desires, by wellapplied personal Exertion.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: ज्योतींषि त्रिदशा नागा यक्षाश्चन्द्राकमारुताः। सर्वे पुरुषकारेण मानुष्याद् देवतां गताः॥
en: All the luminaries in the sky, all the gods, the Nagas, and the Rakshasas, as also the Sun and the Moon and the Winds, have acquired their high status by evolution from man's status, by dint of their own action.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: अर्थो वा मित्रवर्गा वा ऐश्वर्यं वा कुलान्वितम्। श्रीश्चापि दुर्लभा भोक्तुं तथैवाकृतकर्मभिः॥
en: Riches, friends, prosperity coming down from generatica to generation, as also the sweets of life, are difficult of attainment by those who want Exertion.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: शौचेन लभते विप्रः क्षत्रियो विक्रमेण तु। वैश्यः पुरुषकारेण शूद्रः शुश्रूषया श्रियम्॥
en: The Brahmana acquires prosperity by holy living, the Kshatriya by prowess, the Vaishya by manly exertion, and the Shudra by service.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: नादातारं भजन्त्यर्था न क्लीबं नापि निष्क्रियम्। नाकर्मशीलं नाशूरं तथा नैवातपस्विनम्॥
en: The stingy, the impotent, or the idler do not acquire riches and other objects of enjoyment. Nor are these ever acquired by the man who is not active or inanly or devoted to the exercise of religious austerities.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: येन लोकास्त्रयः सृष्टा दैत्याः सर्वाश्च देवताः। स एष भगवान् विष्णुः समुद्रे तप्यते तपः॥
en: Even he, the worshipful Vishnu, who created the three worlds with the Daityas and all the gods, even He is engaged in austere penances in the heart of the deep.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: स्वं चेत् कर्मफलं न स्यात् सर्वमेवाफलं भवेत्। लोको दैवं समालक्ष्य उदासीनो भवेन्ननु॥
en: If one's Karma bore no fruit, then all actions would become fruitless and depending on desting men should become idlers.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: अकृत्वा मानुषं कर्म यो दैवमनुवर्तते। वृथा श्राम्यति सम्प्राप्य पतिं क्लीबमिवाङ्गना॥
en: He who, without following the human modes of action follows Destiny only, acts in vain, like the woman who has an impotent husband.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: न तथा मानुषे लोके भयमस्ति शुभाशुभे। तथा त्रिदशलोके हि भयमन्येन जायते॥
en: The apprehension of good or evil in this world is not Destiny be unfavourable as his apprehension of the same in the other world if Exertion be wanting while here. SO great if

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: कृतः पुरुषकारस्तु दैवमेवानुवर्तते। न दैवमकृते किंचित् कस्यचिद् दातुमर्हति॥
en: Man's powers, if properly applied only follow his Destiny, but Destiny alone cannot produce any good where Exertion is wanting.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: यथा स्थानान्यनित्यानि दृश्यन्ते दैवतेष्वपि। कथं कर्म विना दैवं स्थास्यति स्थापयिष्यतः॥
en: When it is seen that even in the celestial regions, the position of the gods themselves is unstable, how would the gods maintain their own position or that of other of others without proper Karma.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: न दैवतानि लोकेऽस्मिन् व्यापार यान्ति कस्यचित्। व्यासङ्गं जनयन्त्युग्रमात्माभिभवशङ्कया।॥
en: The gods do not always approve of the good actions of others in this world, for, fearing their own defeat, they try to thwart the acts of others.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: ऋषीणां देवतानां च सदा भवति विग्रहः। कस्य वाचा ह्यदैवं स्याद्यतो दैवं प्रवर्तते॥
en: There is a constant rivalry between the gods and the Rishis, and if they all have to go through their Karma, still it can never be said that there is no such thing as Destiny, for it is the latter that introduces all Karma.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: कथं तस्य समुत्पत्तिर्यतो दैवं प्रवर्तते। एवं त्रिदशलोकेऽपि प्राप्यन्ते बहवो गुणाः॥
en: How does Karma originate, if Destiny is the principal motive power of human action? By this means, many virtues are accumulated in the celesiial regions.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः। आत्मैव ह्यात्मन: साक्षी कृतस्याप्यकृतस्य च।॥
en: One's own self is his friend and his enemy too, as also the witness of one's good and evil deeds.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: कृतं चाप्यकृतं किंचित् कृते कर्मणि सिद्ध्यति। सुकृतं दुष्कृतं कर्म न यथार्थे प्रपद्यते॥
en: Good and evil appear through Karma. Good and evil acts do not produce sufficient results.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: देवानां शरणं पुण्यं सर्वं पुण्यैरवाप्यते। पुण्यशीलं नरं प्राप्य किं दैवं प्रकरिष्यति॥
en: Virtue is the refuge of the gods, and by virtue everything is acquired. Destiny thwarts not the man who has acquired virtue and righteousness.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: पुरा ययातिर्विभ्रष्टश्च्यावितः पतितः क्षितौ। पुनरारोपितः स्वर्गं दौहित्रैः पुण्यकर्मभिः॥
en: In days of yore, Yayati, falling from his high position in heaven, descended on the Earth but was again restored to the celestial regions by the good deeds of his pious grandsons.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: पुरूरवाश्च राजर्षिर्द्विजैरभिहितः पुरा। ऐल इत्यभिविख्यातः स्वर्गं प्राप्तो महीपतिः॥
en: The royal sage Pururavas, well known as the descendant of lla, attained to heaven through the intercession of the Brahmanas.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: अश्वमेधादिभिर्यज्ञैः सत्कृत: कोसलाधिपः। महर्षिशापात् सौदासः पुरुषादत्वमागतः॥
en: Saudasa, the king of Koshala, though dignified by the performance of Ashvamedha and other sacrifices, came by the status of a maneating Rakshasa, through the course of a great Rishi.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: अश्वत्थामा च रामश्च मुनिपुत्रौ धनुर्धरौ। न गच्छतः स्वर्गलोकं सुकृतेनेह कर्मणा॥
en: Ashvatthaman and Rama, though both warriors and Sons of Ascetics, failed to acquired heaven by virtue of their own actions in this world.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: वसुर्यज्ञशतैरिष्ट्वा द्वितीय इव वासवः। मिथ्याभिधानेनैकेन रसातलतलं गतः॥
en: Vasu, though he celebrated a hundred sacrifices, like a second Vasava, was sent to the nethermost regions, for making a single false statement.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: बलिवैरोचनिर्बद्धो धर्मपाशेन दैवतैः। विष्णोः पुरुषकारेण पातालसदनः कृतः॥
en: Bali, the son of Virochana, virtuous bound by his promise, was sent to the regions under the Earth, by the prowess of Vishnu.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
