sn: शक्रस्योद्रम्य चरणं प्रस्थितो जनमेजयः। द्विजस्त्रीणां वधं कृत्वा किं दैवेन न वारितः॥
en: Was not Janamejaya, who followed the footprints of Shakra, for slaying a Brahmana woman, checked and put down by the gods?.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: अज्ञानाद् ब्राह्यणं हत्वा स्पृष्टो बालवधेन च। वैशम्पायनविप्रर्षिः किं दैवेन न वारितः॥
en: Was not the twiceborn Rishi Vaishampayana too, who killed a Brahmana in ignorance, and was polluted by the slaughter of a child, put down by the gods?

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: गोप्रदानेन मिथ्या च ब्राह्मणेभ्यो महामखे। पुरा नृगश्च राजर्षिः कृकलासत्वमागतः॥
en: In days of yore the royal sage Nriga became changed into a lizard. He had made gifts of kine into the Brahmanas at his great sacrifice, but this did not help him.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: धुन्धुमारश्च राजर्षिः सत्रेष्वेव जरां गतः। प्रीतिदायं परित्यज्य सुष्वाप स गिरिव्रजे॥
en: The royal sage Dhundhumara was possessed by decrepitude even while engaged in celebrating his sacrifices, and foregoing all the merits thereof the merits thereof he fell asleep at Girivraja.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: पाण्डवानां हृतं राज्यं धार्तराष्ट्रैर्महाबलैः। पुनः प्रत्याहृतं चैव न दैवाद् भुजसंश्रयात्॥
en: The Pandavas too regained their lost kingdom, of which they had been deprived by the powerful sons of Dhritarashtra, not through the influence of the Fates, but by recourse of their own heroism.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: तपोनियमसंयुक्ता मुनयः संशितव्रताः। किं त दैवबलाच्छापमुत्सृजन्ते न कर्मणा॥
en: Do the ascetics of rigid vows, and given to the practice of austere penances, denounce their curses by the help of any supernatural power or only in the exercise of their own power attained by individual acts?

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: पापमुत्सृजते लोके सर्वं प्राप्य सुदुर्लभम्। लोभमोहसमापन्नं न दैवं चायते नरम्॥
en: If possessed by the wicked, all the good which is gained with difficulty in this world, is soon lost to them. Destiny does not help the man that is full of spiritual ignorance and avarice.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: यथाग्निः पवनोद्भूतः सुसूक्ष्मोऽपि महान् भवेत्। तथा कर्मसमायुक्तं दैवं साधु विवर्धते॥
en: Even as small fire, when fanned by the wind, becomes highly powerful, so does Destiny, when helped by individual Exertion, becomes greatly potent.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: यथा तैलक्षयाद् दीपः प्रह्रासमुपगच्छति। तथा कर्मक्षयाद् दैवं प्रहासमुपगच्छति॥
en: As by the diminution of oil in the lamp its light is put out, so does the influence of Destiny, by the abatement of one's acts.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: विपुलमपि धनौघं प्राप्य भोगान् स्त्रियो वा पुरुष इह न शक्तः कर्महीनो हि भोक्तम्। सुनिहितमपि चार्थं दैवतै रक्ष्यमाणं पुरुष इह महात्मा प्राप्नुते नित्ययुक्तः॥
en: Having obtained riches, and woman and all the enjoyments of this world, the, man who is not hardworking is unable to enjoy them long, but the great man, diligent in Exertion, can find riches buried deep in the Earth and watched over by the Fates.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: व्ययगुणमपि साधुं कर्मणा संश्रयन्ते भवति मनुजलोकाद् देवलोको विशिष्टः। बहुतरसुसमृद्ध्या मानुषाणां गृहाणि। पितृवनभवनाभं दृश्यते चामराणाम्॥
en: The good man who is prodigal is sought by the gods for his good conduct, the celestial world being better than the world of men, but the house of miser though full of riches is looked upon by the gods as the house of the dead.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: न च फलति विकर्मा जीवलोक न दैवं व्यपनयति विमार्गं नास्ति दैवे प्रभुत्वम्। गुरुमिव कृतमय्यं कर्म संयाति दैवं नयति पुरुषकारः संचितस्तत्र तत्र॥
en: The inan who does not cxert himself is never contented in this world, nor can Destiny change the course of a man who has gone wrong. There is no power inherent in Destiny. As the pupil follows the preceptor, so does one's action, guided by Destiny, follows his own personal exertion. Where one's own exertion is displayed, there only Destiny, shows its hand.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं मया वै मुनिसत्तम। फलं पुरुषकारस्य सदा संदृश्य तत्त्वतः॥
en: best of ascetics, I have thus described all the merits of personal Exertion, having always known in their true significance.

description: Exertion and destinywhich is more powerful. Conversation between Brahman and Vasishtha
sn: अभ्युत्थानेन दैवस्य समारब्धेन कर्मणा। विधिना कर्मणा चैव स्वर्गमार्गमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: By the influence of Destiny, and by showing personal Exertion, do men attain to heaven. The combined help of Destiny and Exertion, becomes fruitful.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कर्मणां च समस्तानां शुभानां भरतर्षभ। फलानि महतां श्रेष्ठ प्रब्रूहि परिपृच्छतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O best of Bharata's family and the foremost of great men, I wish to know what the fruits are of good deeds! Do you enlighten me.

sn: भीष्म उवाच हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि यन्मां पृच्छसि भारत। रहस्यं यदृषीणां तु तच्छृणुष्व युधिष्ठिर। या गतिः प्राप्यते येन प्रेत्यभावे चिरेप्सिता॥
en: Bhishma said I shall tell you what you have asked. Do you, O Yudhishthira, listen to this which forms the secret knowledge of the Rishis.

sn: येन येन शरीरेण यद्यत् कर्म करोति यः। तेन तेन शरीरेण तत्तत् फलमुपाश्नुते॥
en: Listen to me as I explain what the long coveted ends, are which befall men after death. The fruits of whatever actions are performed by creatures in whatever bodies or forms of existence, are reaped by the doers while crcatures perform good or evil acts, they reap the fruits there of in similar states of succeeding lives. No act done with the help of the five organs of sensual perception, is ever lost.

sn: यस्यां यस्यामवस्थायां यत् करोति शुभाशुभम्। तस्यां तस्यामवस्थायां भुङ्क्ते जन्मनि जन्मनि॥ न नश्यति कृतं कर्म सदा पञ्चेन्द्रियैरिह। ते ह्यस्य साक्षिणो नित्यं षष्ठ आत्मा तथैव च॥ चक्षुर्दद्यान्मनो दद्याद् वाचं दद्याच्च सूनृताम्। अनुव्रजेदुपासीत स यज्ञः पञ्चदक्षिणः॥ यो दद्यादपरिक्लिष्टमन्नमध्वनि वर्तते। श्रान्तायादृष्टपूर्वाय तस्य पुण्यफलं महत्॥
en: The five sensual organs and the immortal soul which is the sixth, are its witnesses. One should devote his eye (to the service of others); one should devote his heart (to the same); one should utter sweet words: one should also follow and worship (one's guest). This is the sacrifice with five gifts. He who offers good food to the unknown, and tired traveller, fatigued by a long journey, acquires great merit.

sn: स्थण्डिलेषु शयानानां गृहाणि शयनानि च। चीरवल्कलसंवीते वासांस्याभरणानि च॥
en: Those who use the sacrificial platform as their only bed, obtain palatial mansions and beds (in subsequent births). He who wears only rags and barks of trees for dress, gets good apparel and ornaments.

sn: वाहनानि च यानानि योगात्मनि तपोधने। अग्नीनुपश्यानस्य राज्ञः पौरुषमेव च॥
en: One possessed of penances and having his soul on Yoga, gets vehicles and riding animals. The king who lics down by the side of the sacrificial fire, acquires vigour and valour.

sn: रसानां प्रतिसंहारे सौभाग्यमनुगच्छति। आमिषप्रतिसंहारे पशून् पुत्रांश्च विन्दति॥
en: The man who casts off the enjoyment of all delicacies, acquires prosperity, and he who abstains from animal food, obtains children and cattle.

sn: अवाशिरास्तु यो लम्बेदुदवासं च यो वसेत्। सततं चैकशायी य: स लभेतेप्सितां गतिम्॥
en: He who lies down with his head downwards, or who lives in water, or who lives secluded and alone in the practice of Brahmacharya, acquires all the desired ends.

sn: पाद्यमासनमेवाथ दीपमन्नं प्रतिश्रयम्। दद्यादतिथिपूजार्थं स यज्ञः पञ्चदक्षिणः॥
en: He who gives shelter to a guest and welcomes him with water to wash his feet as also with food, light and bed, acquires the merits of the sacrifice with the five gifts.

sn: वीरासनं वीरशय्यां वीरस्थानमुपागतः। अक्षयास्तस्य वै लोकाः सर्वकामगमास्तथा।॥
en: He who on the battlefield, lays himself down as a warrior on a warrior's bed, goes to those eternal regions where all the objects of desire are fulfilled.

sn: धनं लभेत दानेन मौनेनाज्ञां विशाम्पते। उपभोगांश्च तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण जीवितम्॥
en: A man, O king, acquires riches who makes charitable gifts. One gets obedience to one's command by the vow of silence all the enjoyments of life by practice of austerities, long life by Brahmacharya, and beauty, prosperity and immunity from discase by abstaining from injury to others.

sn: रूपमैश्वर्यमारोग्यमहिंसाफलमश्नुते। फलमूलाशिनो राज्यं स्वर्ग: पर्णाशिनां भवेत्॥
en: Those who live on fruits and roots only, acquire Sovereignty, those who live on only leaves of trees acquire Residence in heaven.

sn: प्रायोपवेशिनो राजन् सर्वत्र सुखमुच्यते। गवाढ्यः शाकदीक्षायां स्वर्गगामी तृणाशनः॥
en: A man, O king, is said to acquire happiness, by abstention from food. By eating herbs alone, one gets cows. By living on grass, one acquires the celestial regions.

sn: स्त्रियस्त्रिषवणं स्नात्वा वायुं पीत्वा क्रतुं लभेत्। स्वर्ग सत्येन लभते दीक्षया कुलमुत्तमम्॥
en: By avoiding all intercourse with his wife and making ablutions three times a day and by inhaling the air only for purposes of maintenance one acquires the merit of a sacrifice. Heaven is gained by the practice of truth, and nobility of birth by sacrifices.

sn: सलिलाशी भवेद् यस्तु सदाग्निः संस्कृतो द्विजः। मनुं साधयतो राज्यं नाकपृष्ठमनाशके॥
en: The Brahmana of pure practices who lives on water only, and performs the Agnihotra continually, and recites the Gayatri, acquires a kingdom. By abstaining from food or by restricting it, one acquires residence in heaven.

sn: उपवासं च दीक्षायामभिषेकं च पार्थिव। कृत्वा द्वादश वर्षाणि वीरस्थानाद् विशिष्यते॥
en: O king, by avoiding all but the prescribed diet while celebrating sacrifices, and by making pilgrimage for twelve years, one acquires a place better than the abodes reserved for heroes.

sn: धीत्य सर्ववेदान् वै सद्यो दुःखाद् विमुच्यते। मानसं हि चरन् धर्मं स्वर्गलोकमुपाश्नुते।।२
en: By reading all the Vedas, is immediately freed from misery, and by practising virtue in thought, one acquires the heavenly regions.

sn: या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः। योऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम्।।
en: That man who shakes off the longing for happiness and material comforts-a thirst that is difficult of conquest by the foolish and which does not abate with the decline of physical vigour and which clings to him like a dreadful disease,-is able to secure happiness.

sn: यथा धेनुसहस्त्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम्। एवं पूर्वकृतं कर्म कर्तारमनुगच्छति॥
en: As the young calf is able to recognise its dam from among a thousand cows, so do the pristinc deeds of a man follow him.

sn: अचोद्यमानानि यथा पुष्पाणि च फलानि च। स्वकालं नातिवर्तन्ते तथा कर्म पुरा कृतम्॥
en: As the flowers and fruits of a tree, unmoved by apparent influences, never miss their proper one season, so does Karma done in a pristine existence bring about its fruits in proper time.

sn: जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः केशा दन्ता जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः। चक्षुःश्रोत्रे च जीर्येते तृष्णैका न तु जीर्यते॥
en: With age, man's hair grows grey; his teeth become loose; his eyes and ears too become dim in action; but the only thing that does not decline is his desire for enjoyments.

sn: येन प्रीणाति पितरं तेन प्रीतः प्रजापतिः। प्रीणाति मातरं येन पृथिवी तेन पूजिता॥ येन प्रीणात्युपाध्यायं तेन स्याद् ब्रह्म पूजितम्। सर्वे तस्यादृता धर्मा यस्यैते त्रय आदृताः। अनादृतास्तु यस्यैते सर्वास्तस्याफला: क्रियाः॥
en: Prajapati is pleased with those deeds which please one's father, and the Earth is pleased with those acts which please one's mother, and Brahma is pleased with those acts which please one's mother, and Brahma is adored with those acts that please one's preceptor. Virtue is honoured by him who honours these three. The acts of those who despise these three do not help them.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भीष्मस्यैतद् वचः श्रुत्वा विस्पताः कुरुपुङ्गवाः। आसन् प्रहृष्टमनसः प्रीतिमन्तोऽभवंस्तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said The princes of the line of Kuru became filled with surprise upon listening to this speech of Bhishma. All of them became pleased in mind and overpowered with joy.

sn: यन्मन्त्रे भवति वृथोपयुज्यमाने यत् सोमे भवति वृथाभिषूयमाणे। यच्चाग्नौ भवति वृथाभिहूयमाने तत् सर्वं भवति वृथाभिधीयमाने॥
en: As Mantras applied for gaining victory, or the performance of the Soma sacrifice made without proper gifts, or oblations poured on the fire without proper hymns, become fruitless and produce evil results, so sin and evil results originate from falsehood.

sn: इत्येतदृषिणा प्रोक्तमुक्तवानस्मि यद् विभो। शुभाशुभफलप्राप्तौ किमतः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: O prince, I have thus described to you this doctrine of the fruition of good and evil deeds, as recounted by the Rishis of old. What else do you wish to hear. O prince, I have thus described to you this doctrine of the fruition of good and evil deeds, as recounted by the Rishis of old. What else do you wish to hear.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच के पूज्या: के नमस्कार्याः कान् नमस्यसि भारत। एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व येभ्यः स्पृहयसे नृप॥
en: Yudhishthira said Who are deserving of adoration? Who are they to whom one may bow? Who are they, O Bharata, to whom you would lower your head? Who, again, are they whom you like? Tell me all this, O prince.

sn: उत्तमापद्रतस्यापि यत्र ते वर्तते मनः। मनुष्यलोके सर्वस्मिन् यदमुत्रेह चाप्युत॥
en: What is that upon which your mind turn when affliction overwhelms you. Do you describe to me what is beneficial here, that is, in this region of human beings, as also hereafter.

sn: भीष्म उवाच स्पृहयामि द्विजातिभ्यो येषां ब्रह्म परं धनम्। येषां स्वप्रत्ययः स्वर्गस्तपः स्वाध्यायसाधनम्॥
en: Bhishma said I like those twiceborn persons whose highest wealth is Brahma, whose heaven is their knowledge of the soul, and whose penances are formed by their diligent study of the Vedas.

sn: येषां बालाश्च वृद्धाश्च पितृपैतामहीं धुरम्। उद्वहन्ति न सीदन्ति तेभ्यो वै स्पृहयाम्यहम्॥
en: My heart longs for those in whose family persons young and old diligently bear the, ancestral burthens without languishing under them.

sn: विद्यास्वभिविनीतानां दान्तानां मृदुभाषिणाम्। श्रुतवृत्तोपपन्नानां सदाक्षरविदां सताम्॥ संसत्सु वदतां तात हंसानामिव संघशः। मङ्गल्यरूपा रुचिरा दिव्यजीमूतनिःस्वनाः॥ सम्यगुच्चरिता वाचः श्रूयन्ते हि युधिष्ठिर। शुश्रूषमाणे नृपतौ प्रेत्य चेह सुखावहाः॥
en: Brahmanas well-trained in several branches of knowledge, self-controlled, mild-speeched, conversant with the scriptures, well-bchaved, possessed of the knowledge of Brahma, and righteous in conduct, discourse in respectable assemblies like flights of swans. They in a voice deep as the muttering of clouds give vent to auspicious, sweet, excellent, and wellpronounced words, O Yudhishthira. In the courts of monarchs, they spoke these words fraught with happiness both temporal and spiritual, themselves being received with honour and attention and served with respect by those kings.

sn: ये चापि तेषां श्रोतारः सदा सदसि सम्मताः। विज्ञानगुणसम्पन्नास्तेभ्यश्च स्पृहयाम्यहम्॥
en: Indeed, my heart longs after them who endued with knowledge and all desirable attributes, and honoured by others, listen to such words when uttered in assemblies or the courts of kings.

sn: सुसंस्कृतानि प्रयताः शुचीनि गुणवन्ति च। ददत्यन्नानि तृप्त्यर्थं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो युधिष्ठिर॥
en: My heart, O king, always yearns after them who, for the satisfaction of Brahmanas, O Yudhishthira, give to them, with devotion, food that is well-cooked and clean and wholesome.

sn: ये चापि सततं राजंस्तेभ्यश्च स्पृहयाम्यहम्। शक्यं ह्येवाहवे योद्धं न दातुमनसूयितम्॥
en: It is easy to fight in battle, but not so to make a gift without pride or vanity.

sn: शूरा वीराच शतशः सन्ति लोके युधिष्ठिर। येषां संख्यायमानानां दानशूरो विशिष्यते॥
en: In this world, O Yudhishthira, there are hundreds of brave men and heroes. While counting them, he who is a hero in gifts should be considered as superior.

sn: धन्यःस्यां यद्धहं भूयः सौम्य ब्राह्मणकोऽपि वा। कुले जातो धर्मगतिस्तपोविद्यापरायणः॥
en: O amiable one, if I had been even a vulgar Brahmana I would have considered myself as very great, not to speak of one born in a good family, gifted with righteousness of conduct, and given to penances and learning.

sn: मे त्वत्तः प्रियतरो लोकेऽस्मिन् पाण्डुनन्दन। त्वत्तश्चापि प्रियतरा ब्राह्मणा भरतर्षभ॥
en: There is no one, O son of Pandu, in this world, who is dearer to me than you, O chief of Bharats's race, but Brahmans are dearer to me than you.

sn: यथा मम प्रियतमास्त्वत्तो प्रियाः कुरूत्तम। तेन सत्येन गच्छेयं लोकान् यत्र स शान्तनुः॥
en: And since, O best of the Kurus, the Brahmanas are very much dearer to me than you, it is by that truth that I expect to go to all those regions of happiness which have been gained by my father Shantanu.

sn: न मे पिता प्रियतरो ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तथाभवत्। न मे पितुः पिता वापि ये चान्येऽपि सुहृज्जनाः।।१५
en: Neither my father, nor my grandfather, nor any one else connected with me by blood, is dearer to me than the Brahmanas.

sn: न हि मे वृजिनं किंचिद् विद्यते ब्राह्मणेष्विह। अणु वा यदि वा स्थूलं विद्यते साधुकर्मसु॥
en: I do not expect any fruit, small or great, from my adoration of the Brahmanas.

sn: कर्मणा मनसा वापि वाचा वापि परंतप। यन्मे कृतं ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तेनाद्य न तपाम्यहम्॥
en: On account of what I have done to the Brahmanas in thought, word, and deed, I do not feel any pain now.

sn: ब्रह्मण्य इति मामाहस्तया वाचाऽस्मि तोषितः। एतदेव पवित्रेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः परमं स्मृतम्॥
en: People used to call me as one devoted to the Brahmanas. This address always pleased me highly. To do good to the Brahmanas is the most sacred of all sacred duties.

sn: पश्यामि लोकानमलाञ्छुचीन् ब्राह्मणयायिनः। तेषु मे तात गन्तव्यमह्नाय च चिराय च॥
en: I see many regions of beatitude waiting for me who have respectfully followed the Brahmanas. Very soon shall I go to these regions for good, O son.

sn: यथा भर्नाश्रयो धर्मः स्त्रीणां लोके युधिष्ठिर। स देवः सा गतिर्नान्या क्षत्रियस्य तथा द्विजाः॥
en: In this world, O Yudhishthira, the duties of women depend upon their husbands. To a woman, verily, the husband is the god and he is the highest end for which she should try. As the husband to wife, so are the Brahmanas to Kshatriyas.

sn: क्षत्रियः शतवर्षी च दशवर्षी द्विजोत्तमः। पितापुत्रौ च विज्ञेयौ तयोर्हि ब्राह्मणो गुरुः॥
en: If there be a Kshatriya hundred years old and a good Brahmana child of only ten years, the latter should be considered as a father and the former as a son, for among the two, the Brahmana is superior.

sn: नारी तु पत्यभावे वै देवरं कुरुते पतिम्। पृथिवी ब्राह्मणालाभे क्षत्रियं कुरुते पतिम्॥
en: A woman, in the absence of her husband, takes his younger brother for her lord; so the Earth, not having obtained Brahmana, made the Kshatriya her king.

sn: पुत्रवच्च ततो रक्ष्या उपास्या गुरुवच्च ते। अग्निवच्चोपचर्या वै ब्राह्मणाः कुरुसत्तम॥
en: The Brahmanas should be protected like sons and adored like fathers or preceptors. Indeed, O best of the Kurus, they served reverentially as people wait with respect upon their sacrificial or Homa fires.

sn: ऋजून् सतः सत्यशीलान् सर्वभूतहिते रतान्। आशीविषानिव क्रूद्धान् द्विजान् परिचरेत् सदा॥
en: The Brahmanas are gifted with simplicity and righteousness. They are given to truth. They are always engaged in the behalf of all creatures. Yet when angry they are like snakes of dreadful venom. They should, for these reasons, be always waited upon and served with respect and humility.

sn: तेजसस्तपसश्चैव नित्यं बिभ्येद् युधिष्ठि। उभे चैते परित्याज्ये तेजश्चैव तपस्तथा॥
en: One should, O Yudhishthira, always fear these two, viz., Energy and Penances. Both these should be shirked or kept at a distance.

sn: व्यवसायस्तयोः शीघ्रमुभयोरेव विद्यते। हन्युः क्रुद्धा महाराज ब्राह्मणा ये तपस्विनः॥
en: The effects of both are quick, There is this superiority, however, of Penances, viz., that Brahmanas gifted with Penances, O king, can, if angry, kill the object of their anger.

sn: भूयः स्यादुभयं दत्तं ब्राह्मणाद् यदकोपनात्। कुर्यादुभयतः शेषं दत्तशेषं न शेषयेत्॥
en: Even greatest Energy and Penances, become neutralised if applied against a Brahmana who has conquered anger. If the two that is, Energy and Penances-be set against each other, then both of them would be destroyed. Again when Energy, is set against Penances, it is sure to be destroyed without leaving a remnant. Penances applied against Energy cannot be destroyed completely.

sn: दण्डपाणिर्यथा गोषु पालो नित्यं हि रक्षयेत्। ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्म च तथा क्षत्रियः परिपालयेत्॥
en: As the herdsman, stick in hand, protects the herd, so should the Kshatriya always protect the Vedas and the Brahmanas.

sn: पितेव पुत्रान् रक्षेथा ब्राह्मणान् धर्मचेतसः। गृहे चैषामवेक्षेथाः किंस्विदस्तीति जीवनम्॥
en: The Kshatriya should protect all pious Brahmanas as a father protects his sons. He should always look after the houses of the Brahmanas for finding out that the means of subsistence may not be wanting.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्राह्मणानां तु ये लोकाः प्रतिश्रुत्य पितामह। न प्रयच्छन्ति मोहात् ते के भवन्ति महाद्युते॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O you of great splendour, what do those men become who, through stupefaction of intellect, do not make gifts to Brahmanas after having promised to make those gifts?

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: एतन्मे तत्त्वतो ब्रूहि धर्मे धर्मभृतां वर। प्रतिश्रुत्य दुरात्मानो न प्रयच्छन्ति ये नराः॥
en: O foremost of all righteous persons, do tell me what the duties are in this matter. Indeed, what becomes the end of those wicked men who do not give after having promised to give.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: भीष्म उवाच यो न दद्यात् प्रतिश्रुत्य स्वल्पं वा यदि वा बहु। आशास्तस्य हताः सर्वाः क्लीबस्येव प्रजाफलम्॥
en: Bhishma said The person who, after having promised, does not give, be it little or much, has the mortification to witness his hopes frustrated like the hopes of a eunuch about children.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: यां रात्रिं जायते जीवां यां रात्रिं च विनश्यति। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे यद् यत् सुकृतं तस्य भारत।॥ यच्च तस्य हतं किंचिद् दत्तं वा भरतर्षभ। तपस्तप्तमथो वापि सर्वं तस्योपहन्यते॥
en: Whatever good acts such a person does between the day of his birth and that of his death, O Bharata, whatever libations he pours on the sacrificial fire, whatever gifts he makes, o chief of Bharata's race, and whatever penances he performs, all becomes useless.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: अथैतद् वचनं प्राहुर्धर्मशास्त्रविदो जनाः। निशम्य भरतश्रेष्ठ बुद्धया परमयुक्तया।॥
en: They who conversant with the scriptures hold this as their opinion, arriving at it, О chief of the Bharatas, with the help of a well-ordered understanding.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: अपि चोदाहरन्तीमं धर्मशास्त्रविदो जनाः। अश्वानां श्यामकर्णानां सहस्त्रेण स मुच्यते।।७।
en: Persons conversant with the scriptures also opine that such a man may be purified by giving away a thousand horses with dark ears. are

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। शृगालस्य च संवादं वानरस्य च भारत॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between a jackal and an ape.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: तौ सखायौ पुरा ह्यास्तां मानुषत्वे परंतप। अन्यां योनि समापन्नौ शार्गाली वानरी तथा॥
en: While both were human beings, O scorcher of enemies, they were intimate friends. After death one of them became a jackal and the other an ape.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: ततः परासून् खादन्तं शृगालं वानरोऽब्रवीत्। श्मशानमध्ये सम्प्रेक्ष्य पूर्वजातिमनुस्मरन्॥
en: Seeing the jackal one day eating an animal car-case in the midst of a crematorium, the ape, remembering his own and his friend's pristine birth as human beings, addressed him, saying,

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: किं त्वया पापकं पूर्वं कृतं कर्म सुदारुणम्। यस्त्वं श्मशाने मृतकान् पूतिकानत्सि कुत्सितान्॥
en: Verily, what dreadíul sin did you commit in your pristine birth on account of which you are obliged in this birth to feed in a crematorium upon such repulsive food as the putrid car-case of an animal?

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच शृगालो वानरं तदा। ब्राह्मणस्य प्रतिश्रुत्य न मया तदुपाहतम्॥
en: Thus addressed the jackal replied to the ape, saving Having promised to give to a Brahmana I did not make him the gift.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: तत्कृते पापकी योनिमापन्नोऽस्मि प्लवङ्गम। तस्मादेवंविधं भक्ष्यं भक्षयामि बुभुक्षितः॥
en: It is for that sin, O ape, that I have fallen into this wretched state of existence. It is for that reason that, when hungry, I am obliged to cat such food.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: भीष्म उवाच शृगालो वानरं प्राह पुनरेव नरोत्तम। किं त्वया पातकं कर्म कृतं येनासि वानरः॥
en: Bhishma said The jackal then, O best of men, addressed the monkey and said What sin did you commit for which you have become an ape.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: वानर उवाच सदा चाहं फलाहारो ब्राह्मणानां प्लवङ्गमः। तस्मान्न ब्राह्मणस्वं तु हर्तव्यं विदुषा सदा। समं विवादो मोक्तव्यो दातव्यं स प्रतिश्रुतम्॥
en: The ape said In my former life I used to eat the fruits belonging to Brahmanas. Hence have I become an ape. Hence it is clear that one endued with intelligence and learning should never take what belongs to Brahmanas. As one should abstain from this, one should avoid also all quarrels with Brahmanas. Having promised, one should certainly make the promised gift lo them.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्येतद् ब्रुवतो राजन् ब्राह्मणस्य मया श्रुतम्। कथां कथयतः पुण्यां धर्मज्ञस्य पुरातनीम्॥
en: Bhishma said I heard this, O king, from my preceptor while he was discoursing upon the subject of Brahmanas. I heard this from that pious person when he recounted the old and sacred declarations of this topic.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: श्रुतश्चापि मया भूयः कृष्णस्यापि विशाम्पते। कथां कथयतः पूर्वं ब्राह्मणं प्रति पाण्डव॥
en: I heard this from Krishna also, o king, while he was discoursing, O son of Pandu, upon Brahmanas.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: न हर्तव्यं विप्रधनं क्षन्तव्यं तेषु नित्यशः। बालाश्च नावमन्तव्या दरिद्राः कृपणा अपि॥
en: The property of a Brahmana should never be taken. They should always be let alone. Poor, or miserly, or young in years, they should never be dishonored.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: एवमेव च मां नित्यं ब्राह्मणाः संदिशन्ति वै। प्रतिश्रुत्य भवेद् देयं नाशा कार्या द्विजोत्तमे॥
en: The Brahmanas always taught me this. Having promised to make them a gift, the gift should be made. A superior Brahmana should never be disappointed in his expectations. an

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: ब्राह्मणो ह्याशया पूर्वं कृतया पृथिवीपते। सुसमिद्धो यथा दीप्तः पावकस्तद्विधः स्मृतः॥
en: A Brahmana, O king, in whom expectation has been raised, has, O king, been said to be like a burning fire.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: यं निरीक्षेत संक्रुद्ध आशया पूर्वजातया। प्रदहेच्च हि तं राजन् कक्षमक्षय्यभुग यथा॥
en: That man upon whom a Brahmana with raised expectations looks, is sure, O king, to be reduced to ashes as a heap of straw is capable of being consumed by a burning fire.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: स एव हि यदा तुष्टो वचसा प्रतिनन्दति। भवत्यगदसंकाशो विषये तस्य भारत॥
en: When the Brahmana, gratified by the king, addresses the king in delightful and affectionate words, he becomes, O Bharata, a source of great good to the king, for he continucs to live in the kingdom like a physician fighting against various ills of the body.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: पुत्रान् पौत्रान् पशुंश्चैव बान्धवान् सचिवांस्तथा। पुरं जनपदं चैव शान्तिरिष्टेन पोषयेत्॥
en: Such a Brahimana is sure to maintain peacefully the sons and grandsons and animals and relatives and ministers and other officers and the city and the provinces of the king.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: एतद्धि परमं तेजो ब्राह्मणस्येह दृश्यते। सहस्त्रकिरणस्येव सवितुर्धरणीतले॥
en: Such is the energy of the Brahimana, like to that of the thousand-rayed Sun himself, on the Earth.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: तस्माद् दातव्यमेवेह प्रतिश्रुत्य युधिष्ठिर। यदीच्छेच्छोभनां जाति प्राप्तुं भरतसत्तम॥
en: Therefore, O Yudhishthira, if one wishes to come by a respectable or happy order of being in his next birth, he should, having made the promise to a Brahmana, certainly satisfy it by actually making the gift to him.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: ब्राह्मणस्य हि दत्तेन ध्रुवं स्वर्गो ह्यनुत्तमः। शक्यः प्राप्तुं विशेषेण दानं हि महती क्रिया॥
en: By making gifts to a Brahmana one is sure to acquire the highest heaven. Verily, the making of gifts is the highest of deeds that one can perform.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: इतो दत्तेन जीवन्ति देवताः पितरस्तथा। तस्माद् दानानि देयानि ब्राह्मणेभ्यो विजानता॥
en: The gods and the departed manes are supported by the gifts one makes to a Brahmana. Hence one endued with knowledge should ever make gifts to the Brahmanas.

description: The end of persons who fail to make gifts to the Brahmanas after having promised them. The story of the jackal and ape
sn: महद्धि भरतश्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मणस्तीर्थमुच्यते। वेलायां न तु कस्यांचिद् गच्छेद् विप्रो ह्यपूजितः।।२८
en: O chief of the Bharatas, the Brahmana is considered as the highest object to whom gifts should be made. At no time should a Brahmana be received without due adoration.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मित्रसौहार्दयोगेन उपदेशं करोति यः। जात्याऽधरस्य राजर्षेर्दोषस्तस्य भवेन्न वा॥
en: Yudhishthira said I wish to know, O royal sage, whether any sin is committed by one who from interested or disinterested friendship delivers instructions to a person of a low order of birth.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: एतदिच्छामि तत्त्वेन व्याख्यातुं वै पितामह। सूक्ष्मा गतिर्हि धर्मस्य यत्र मुह्यन्ति मानवाः॥
en: O grandfather, I wish to hear this explained to me in full. The course of duty is highly subtile. Men are often seen to be stupefied about that course.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि शृणु राजन् यथाक्रमम्। ऋषीणां वदतां पूर्वं श्रुतमासीत् यथा पुरा॥
en: Bhishma said About it, o king, I shall recite to you, in due order, what I heard certain Rishis say in days of yore.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: उपदेशो न कर्तव्यो जातिहीनस्य कस्यचित्। उपदेशे महान् दोष उपाध्यायस्य भाष्यते॥
en: Instruction should not be given to one who belongs to a low or degraded caste. It is said that the preceptor who delivers instruction to such a person commits great sin.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: निदर्शनमिदं राजन् शृणु मे भरतर्षभ। दुरुक्तवचने राजन् यथापूर्वं युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Listen to me, O chief of Bharatas, as I recite to you, O Yudhishthira, this incident which took place in days of yore, o king, of the evil consequences of imparting of instruction to a lowborn person fallen into distress.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: ब्रह्माश्रमपदे वृत्तं पाश्र्वं हिमवतः शुभे। तत्राश्रमपदं पुण्यं नानावृक्षगणायुतम्॥
en: The incident which I shall describe, took place in the hermitage of certain twice born sages which stood on the auspicious breast of Himavat. There, on the breast of that king of mountains, was a sacred asylum adorned with trees of various kinds.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: नानागुल्मलताकीर्णं मृगद्विजनिषेवितम्। सिद्धचारणसंयुक्तं रम्यं पुष्पितकाननम्॥
en: Overgrown also with various species of crecpers and plants, it was the resort of many animals and birds. Inhabited by Siddhas and Charanas also, it was highly delightful on account of the woods that flowered there at every scason.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: व्रतिभिर्बहुभिः कीर्णं तापसैरुपसेवितम्। ब्राह्मणैश्च महाभागैः सूर्यज्वलनसंनिभैः॥
en: Many Brahmacharins lived there, and many herimits. Many Brahmanas lived there, who were highly blessed and who resembled the sun or the fire in energy and effulgence.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: नियमव्रतसम्पन्नैः समाकीर्णं तपस्विभिः। दीक्षितैर्भरतश्रेष्ठ यताहारैः कृतात्मभिः॥
en: Ascetics of various kinds, observant of various restraints and vows, as also others, O king of the Bharatas, who had gone through initiatory rites and were frugal in fare and possessed of purified souls, lived there.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: तपोध्ययनघोषैश्च नादितं भरतर्षभ। वालखिल्यैश्च बहुभिर्यतिभिश्च निषेवितम्॥
en: Large numbers of Valikhilyas and inany who observed the vow of Sanyasa also, used to live there. On account of all this, the hermitage resounded with the recitation of the Vedas and the sacred Mantras uttered by its dwellers.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: तत्र कश्चित् समुत्साहं कृत्वा शूद्रो दयान्वितः। आगतो ह्याश्रमपदं पूजितश्च तपस्विभिः॥
en: Once upon a time a Shudra endued with mercy for all creatures, ventured to come into that herinitage. Arrived at that retreat, he was duiy honoured by all the ascetics.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: तांस्तु दृष्ट्वा मुनिगणान् देवकल्पान् महौजसः। विविधां वहतो दीक्षां सम्प्राहष्यत भारत॥
en: Seeing those ascetics of diverse classes who were endued with great energy, that resembled the gods, and who were observing diverse kinds of initiation, O Bharata, the Shudra became highly pleased at heart.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: अथास्य बुद्धिरभवत् तपस्ये भरतर्षभ। ततोऽब्रवीत् कुलपतिं पादौ संगृह्य भारत॥ भवत्प्रसादादिच्छामि धर्म वक्तुं द्विजर्षभ। तन्मां त्वं भगवन् वक्तुं प्रव्राजयितुमर्हसि॥
en: Seeing everything, ( chief of Bharata's race, the Shudra felt inclined to devote himself to the practice of penances. Touching the feet of the head of the order, O Bharata, he said to hiin. Through your favour, O foremost of twice born persons, I wish to learn the duties of religion. You should, o illustrious one, describe to me those duties and introduce me into a life of Renunciation.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: वर्णावरोऽहं भगवन् शूद्रो जात्यास्मि सत्तम। शुश्रूषां कर्तुमिच्छामि प्रपन्नाय प्रसीद मे॥
en: I am certainly inferior in colour, O illustrious one, for I am by caste a Shudra, O best of men! I wish to wait upon and serve you here. Be pleased with me who humbly seek your shelter.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: कुलपतिरुवाच न शक्यमिह शूद्रेण लिङ्गमाश्रित्य वर्तितुम्। आस्यतां यदि ते बुद्धिः शुश्रूषानिरतो भव॥ शुश्रूषया पराँल्लोकानवाप्स्यसि न संशयः॥
en: The Kulapati said It is impossible that a Shudra should live here following the life of Renunciation. If it pleases you, you may stay here and serve us. Forsooth, by such service you shall acquire many regions of great happiness.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु मुनिना स शूद्रोऽचिन्तयन्नृप। कथमत्र मया कार्यं श्रद्धा धर्मपरा च मे॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by the ascetic, the Shudra began to think in his mind, o king How should I now act? I have great reverence for those religious duties which lead to merit.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: विज्ञातमेवं भवतु करिष्ये प्रियमात्मनः। गत्वाऽऽश्रमपदाद् दूरमुटजं कृतवास्तु सः॥
en: Let this, however, be settled, that I shall do what would be for my behoof. Proceeding to a spot that was distant from that hermitage, he inade a hut of the twigs and leaves of trees.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: तत्र वेदी च भूमिं च देवतायतनानि च। निवेश्य भरतश्रेष्ठ नियमस्थोऽभवन्मुनिः॥
en: Erecting also a sacrificial platform and making a little room for his sleep, and some platforms for the use of the gods, he began, O chief of the Bharatas, to lead a life governed by rigid observances and vows and to practise penances, abstaining entirely from speech.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: अभिषेकांश्च नियमान् देवतायतनेषु च। बलिं च कृत्वा हत्वा च देवतां चाप्यपूजयत्॥
en: He began to perform ablutions thrice a day, observe other vows, make sacrifices to the gods, pour libations on the sacrificial fire, and adore and worship the gods in this way.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: संकल्पनियमोपेतः फलाहारो जितेन्द्रियः। नित्यं संनिहिताभिस्तु ओषधीभिः फलैस्तथा॥ अतिथीन् पूजयामास यथावत् समुपागतान्। एवं हि सुमहान् कालो व्यत्यकामत तस्य वै॥
en: Governing all carnal desires, living sparingly upon fruits and roots, governing all his senses, he daily welcomed and entertained all that came to his hermitage as guests, offering them herbs and fruits which grew in abundance around. In this way he passed a very long time in that hermitage of his.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: अथास्य मुनिरागच्छत् संगत्या वै तमाश्रमम्। सम्पूज्य स्वागतेनर्षि विधिवत् समतोषयत्॥
en: One day an ascetic came to that Shudra's asylum for making his acquaintance. The Sudra welcomed and adored the Rishi with due rites, and pleased him highly.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: अनुकूला: कथाः कृत्वा यथागतमपृच्छता ऋषिः परमतेजस्वी धर्मात्मा संशितव्रतः॥
en: Possessed of great energy, and a righteous soul, that Rishi of rigid vows conversed with his host on many agreeable subjects and informed him of the place whence he had come.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: एवं सुबहुशस्तस्य शूद्रस्य भरतर्षभ। सोऽगच्छदाश्रममृषिः शूद्रं द्रष्टुं नरर्षभ॥
en: In this way, O chief of the Bharatas, that Rishi, O best of men, came into the hermitage of the Shudra in numerable times for seeing him.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: अथ तं तापसं शूद्रः सोऽब्रवीद् भरतर्षभ। पितृकार्यं करिष्यामि तत्र मेऽनुग्रहं कुरु॥
en: On one of these occasions the Shudra, O king, addressing the Rishi, said I wish to perform the rites that are ordained for the Pitris. Do you show me kindness in this matter.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: बाढमित्येव तं विप्र उवाच भरतर्षभ। शुचिर्भूत्वा स शूद्रस्तु तस्यर्षेः पाद्यमानयत्॥ अथ दर्भाश्च वन्यांश्च ओषधीर्भरतर्षभ। पवित्रमासनं चैव वृषी च समुपानयत्॥
en: Very well the Brahmana said in reply to him, O king. Then, purifying himself by a bath, the Shudra brought water for the Rishi to wash his feet, and he also brought some Kusha grass, and wild herbs and fruits, and a sacred seat. and the seat called Vrishi.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: अथ दक्षिणमावृत्य वृषी चरमशैर्षिकीम्। कृतामन्यायतो दृष्ट्वा तं शूद्रमृषिरब्रवीत्॥ कुरुष्वैतां पूर्वशीर्षां भवांश्चोदङ्मुखः शुचिः। स च तत् कृतवान् शूद्रः सर्वं यदृषिरब्रवीत्॥
en: The Vrishi, however, was placed by the Shudra towards the south, with its head turned to the west. Seeing this and knowing that it was against the ordinance, the Rishi addressed the Shudra, saying Place the Vrishni with its head turned towards the East and having purified yourself, do you sit with your face turned towards the north.The Shudra did everything as the Rishi directed.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: यथोपदिष्टं मेधावी दर्भा_दि यथातथम्। हव्यकव्यविधिं कृत्स्नमुक्तं तेन तपस्विना॥ ऋषिणा पितृकार्यं च स च धर्मपथे स्थितः। पितृकार्यं कृते चापि विसृष्टः स जगाम ह॥ अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य स तप्यन् शूद्रतापसः। वने पञ्चत्वमगमत् सुकृतेन च तेन वै॥ अजायत महाराजवंशे स च महाद्युतिः। तथैव स ऋषिस्तात कालधर्ममवाप ह॥
en: Endued with great intelligence, and practising righteousness, the Shudra received every direction, about the Sraddha, as laid down in the ordinance, from that Rishi gifted with penances, marking the manner of spreading the Kusha grass, and placing the Arghyas, and as regards the rites to be observed in the matter of the libations to be poured and the food to be offered. After the rites in honour of the Pitris had been finished, the Rishi, was sent away the Shudra, whercupon he returned to his own abode. After a long time, the whole of which he passed practising such penances and vows, the Shudra ascetic died in the those woods. On account of I the merit he acquired by those practices, the Shudra, in his next life, was born in the family of a great king, and in time became possessed of great splendour. The twiceborn Rishi also, when the time came, paid his debt to Nature.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: पुरोहितकुले विप्र आजातो भरतर्षभ। एवं तौ तत्र सम्भूतावुभौ शूद्रमुनी तदा॥
en: In his next life, O chief of Bharata's race, he was born in the family of a priest. Thus those two, viz., that Shudra who had passed a life of penances and that twiceborn Rishi who had out of kindness given the former some instructions in the matter of the rites performed in honour of the Pitris, became reborn, the one as the son of a royal race and the other as the member of a priestly family.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: क्रमेण वर्धितौ चापि विद्यासु कुशलावुभौ॥ अथर्ववेदे वेदे च बभूवर्षिः सुनिष्ठितः।
en: Both of them began to grow and both gained great knowledge in the usual branches of study. The Brahmana became well versed in the Vedas as also in the Atharvans.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: कल्पप्रयोगे चोत्पन्ने ज्योतिषे च परं गतः॥ सांख्ये चैव परा प्रीतिस्तस्य चैवं व्यवर्धत।
en: The reborn Rishi gained great perfection in all sacrifices ordained in the Sutras, of the Vedanga which deals with religious rites and observances, astrology and astronomy. He took great pleasure in the Sankhya philosophy too.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: पितर्युपरते चापि कृतशौचस्तु पार्थिव॥ अभिषिक्तः प्रकृतिभी राजपुत्रः स पार्थिवः।
en: Meanwhile, the reborn Shudra who had become a prince, when his father the king died, performed his last rites; and after he had purified himself by performing all the obsequial rites, he was installed by the subjects of his father as their king on his paternal throne.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: अभिषिक्तेन स ऋषिरभिषिक्तः पुरोहितः॥ स तं पुरोधाय सुखमवसद् भरतर्षभ।
en: But soon after his own installation as king, he installed the rebora Rishi as his priest. Having made the Brahmana his priest, the king began to pass his days happily.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: राज्यं शशास धर्मेण प्रजाश्च परिपालयन्॥ पुण्याहवाचने नित्यं धर्मकार्येषु चासकृत्। उत्स्मयन् प्राहसच्चापि दृष्ट्वा राजा पुरोहितम्॥ एवं स बहुशो राजन् पुरोधसमुपाहसत्।
en: He ruled his kingdom piously and protected and maintained all his subject. Every day, however, the king, seeing his priest on the occasion of receiving benedictions from him as also of the performance of religious and other sacred rites, smiled or laughed loudly. In this way, O king, the reborn Shudra who had become a king, laughed at seeing his priest on numberless occasions.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: लक्षयित्वा पुरोधास्तु बहुशस्तं नराधिपम्॥ उत्स्मयन्तं च सततं दृष्ट्वासौ मन्युमाविशत्।
en: The priest, marking that the king always smiled or laughed whenever he happened to look at him, became angry.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: अथ शून्ये पुरोधास्तु सह राज्ञा समागतः॥ कथाभिरनुकूलाभी राजानं चाभ्यरोचयत्।
en: On one occasion he met the king in a place where there was nobody present. He pleased the king by agreeable conversation.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्नरेन्द्रं स पुरोधा भरतर्षभ॥ वरमिच्छाम्यहं त्वेकं दत्तं महाद्युते॥
en: Taking advantage of that moment, О chief of Bharata's race, the priest addressed the king, saying you of great splendour, I pray you to grant me a single boon.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: राजोवाच वराणां ते शतं दद्यां किं बतैकं द्विजोत्तम। स्नेहाच्च बहुमानाच्च नास्त्यदेयं हि मे तव॥
en: The king said Of boons, O best of twiceborn persons, I am ready to grant you a hundred, what do you say then of one only? From the affection I have for you and the reverence in which I hold you, there is nothing that I cannot give you.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: पुरोहित उवाच एकं वै वरमिच्छामि यदि तुष्टोऽसि पार्थिव। प्रतिजानीहि तावत् त्वं सत्यं यद् वद नानृतम्॥
en: The priest said I wish to have only one boon, if, O king, you have been pleased with me. Promise that you would tell me the truth, instead of any untruth.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: भीष्म उवाच बाढमित्येव तं राजा प्रत्युवाच युधिष्ठिर। यदि ज्ञास्यामि वक्ष्यामि अजानन् न तु संवदे॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by the priest, O Yudhishthira, the king said to himSo be it! If I know what you would ask me, I shall certainly tell you truly. If, on the other hand, I do not know it, I shall not say anything.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: पुरोहित उवाच पुण्याहवाचने नित्यं धर्मकृत्येषु चासकृत्। शान्तिहोमेषु च सदा किं त्वं हससि वीक्ष्य माम्॥५०
en: The priest said Every day, on occasions of receiving benedictions from me, when, again, I am engaged in the performance of religious rites, on your behalf, on occasions also of the Homa and other rites of propitiation, why do you laugh upon seeing me?

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: सव्रीडं वै भवति हि मनो मे हसता त्वया। कामया शापितो राजन् नान्यथा वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Seeing you laugh at me on all occasions, my mind shrinks with shame, I have made you promise, O king, that you would answer me truly. You should not tell an untruth.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: सुव्यक्तं कारणं ह्यत्र न ते हास्यमकारणम्। कौतूहलं मे सुभृशं तत्त्वेन कथयस्व मे॥
en: There must be some grave reason for your conduct. Your laughter cannot be causeless. I have great curiosity to know the reason. Do you speak truly to me.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: राजोवाच एवमुक्ते त्वया विप्र यदवाच्यं भवेदपि। अवश्यमेव वक्तव्यं शृणुष्वैकमना द्विज॥
en: The king said While you have thus accosted me, o twiceborn one, I am bound to enlighten you even if the matter be one that should not be given out to you! I must tell you the truth. Do you listen to me with rapt attention, O twiceborn one.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: पूर्वदेहे यथा वृत्तं तन्निबोध द्विजोत्तमा जाति स्मराम्यहं ब्रह्मन्नवधानेन मे शृणु॥
en: Listen, O foremost of twiceborn persons, to me as I give out to you what took place (to us) in our pristine births. I remember that birth. Do you listen to me with concentrated mind.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: शूद्रोऽहमभवं पूर्वं तापसो भृशसंयुतः। ऋषिरुग्रतपास्त्वं च तदाभूद् द्विजसत्तम॥
en: In my former life I was a Shudra engaged in the practice of severe penances. You, O best of twiceborn persons, were a Rishi of austere penances.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: प्रीयता हि तदा ब्रह्मन् ममानुग्रहबुद्धिना। पितृकार्यं त्वया पूर्वमुपदेशः कृतोऽनघ॥
en: O sinless one, pleased with me, and moved by the desire of doing me good, you, O Brahmana, were pleased to give me certain instruction about the rites I performed in honour of my departed manes.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: बृस्यां दर्भेषु हव्ये च कव्ये च मुनिसत्तम। एतेन कर्मदोषेण पुरोधास्त्वमजायथाः॥
en: You instructed me about the manner of spreading the Vrishi and the Kusha blades and of offering libations and meat and other food, O foremost of ascetics. On account of this transgression of yours you are born as a priest.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: अहं राजा च विप्रेन्द्र पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्। मत्कृतस्योपदेशस्य त्वयावाऽऽप्तमिदं फलम्॥
en: I have taken birth as a king, O foremost of Brahinanas. See the changes that Time encompasses. You have reaped this fruit on account of your having instructed me.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: एतस्मात् कारणाद् ब्रह्मन् प्रहसे त्वां द्विजोत्तम। न त्वां परिभवन् ब्रह्मन् प्रहसामि गुरुभवान्॥
en: It is for this reason, O Brahmana, that I smile at seeing you, O foremost of twiceborn persons. I do not certainly laugh at you from desire of disregarding you. You are my preceptor.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: विपर्ययेण मे मन्युस्तेन संतप्यते मनः। जातिं स्मराम्यहं तुभ्यमतस्त्वां प्रहसामि वै॥
en: I am really very sorry at this change of condition. My heart burns at the thought. I remember our former births, hence do I laugh at seeing you.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: एवं तवोग्रं हि तप उपदेशेन नाशितम्। पुरोहितत्वमुत्सृज्य यतस्व त्वं पुनर्भवे॥
en: Your austere penances were all destroyed by the instructions you gave me. Removing your present office of priest, do you try to regain a superior birth.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: इतस्त्वमधमामन्यां मा योनि प्राप्स्यसे द्विजा गृह्यतां द्रविणं विप्र पूतात्मा भव सत्तम॥
en: Do you exert so that you may not obtain in your next life a birth meaner than your present one. Take as much riches as you wish, O learned Brahmana, and purify your soul, O best of men.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो विसृष्टो राज्ञा तु विग्रो दानान्यनेकशः। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ वित्तं भूमि ग्रामांश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Bhishma continued Dismissed by the king, the Brahmana made many gifts, to persons of his own order, of riches and land and villages.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: कृच्छ्राणि चीर्वा च ततो यथोक्तानि द्विजोत्तमैः। तीर्थानि चापि गत्वा वै दानानि विविधानि च॥
en: He observed many rigid and severe vows as laid down by the foremost of Brahmanas. He sojourned to many sacred waters and made many gifts to Brahmanas in those places.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: दत्वा गाश्चैव विप्रेभ्यः पूतात्माऽभवदात्मवान्। तमेव चाश्रमं गत्वा चचार विपुलं तपः॥
en: Making gifts of kine to persons of the twiceborn order, his soul became purified and he succeeded in gaining a knowledge of it. Going to that very asylum where he had lived in his former birth, he practised very severe penances.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: ततः सिद्धिं परां प्राप्तो ब्राह्मणो राजसत्तम। सम्मतश्चाभवत् तेषामाश्रमे तन्निवासिनाम्॥
en: As the result of all this, O foremost of kings, that Brahmana gained the highest success. He became an object of respect with all the ascetics who lived in that asylum.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: एवं प्राप्तो महत्कृच्छ्रमृषिः सन्नृपसत्तम। ब्राह्मणेन न वक्तव्यं तस्माद् वर्णावरे जने॥
en: In this way, O best of kings, that twice born Rishi fell into great distress. The Brahmana should, therefore, never give instructions to Shudras.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: (वर्जयेददुपदेशं च सदैव ब्राह्मणो नृप। उपदेशं हि कुर्वाणो द्विजः कृच्छ्रमवाप्नुयात्।। नेषितव्यं सदा वाचा द्विजेन नृपसत्तम। न च प्रव्यक्तव्यमिह किञ्चिद् वर्णावरे जने॥)
en: Hence, O king, the Brahmana should avoid delivering instructions to such as are lowborn, for it was by giving instructions to a lowborn person a Brahmana came to grief. O best of kings, the Brahmana should never desire to acquire instruction from, or impart instruction to, a person who belongs to the lowest order.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: ब्राह्मणा: क्षत्रिया वैश्यास्त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः। एतेषु कथयन् राजन् ब्राह्मणो न प्रदुष्यति॥
en: Brahmanas and Kshatriyas and Vaishyas, these three orders, are considered as twice born. By delivering instruction to these, a Brahmana does not commit any sin.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: तस्मात् सद्भिर्न वक्तव्यं कस्यचित् किंचिदग्रतः। सूक्ष्मा गतिर्हि धर्मस्य दुर्जेया ह्यकृतात्मभिः॥
en: They, therefore, who are good, should never discourse on any subject, for giving any instruction, before persons of the inferior caste. The course of morality is highly subtle and incapable of being understood by persons of uncleansed soul.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: तस्मान्मौनेन मुनयो दीक्षां कुर्वन्ति चादृताः। दुरुक्तस्य भयाद् नाभाषन्ते च किंचन॥
en: It is for this reason that ascetics adopt the vow of silence, and, honoured by all, pass through initiation without speaking a single word, For fear of saying what is incorrect or what may offend, ascetics never utter a single word.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: धार्मिका गुणसम्पन्नाः सत्यार्जवसमन्विताः। दुरुक्तवाचाभिहितैः प्राप्नुवन्तीह दुष्कृतम्॥
en: Even men who are righteous and endued with every accomplishment, and truth and simplicity of conduct, have been known to commit great sin on account of words spoken improperly.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: उपदेशो न कर्तव्यः कदाचिदपि कस्यचित्। उपदेशाद्धि तत् पापं ब्राह्मण: समवाप्नुयात्॥
en: Instruction should never be given on anything to any person. If on account of the instructions given, the instructed cominit any sin, that sin attaches to the Brahmana who gave the instruction.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: विमृश्य तस्मात् प्राज्ञेन वक्तव्यं धर्ममिच्छता। सत्यानृतेन हि कृत उपदेशो हिनस्ति हि॥
en: The wise man, therefore, who wishes to acquire merit, should always act with wisdom. That instruction which is given in exchange for money always sullies the instructor.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: वक्तव्यमिह पृष्टेन विनिश्चित्य विनिश्चयम्। स चोपदेशः कर्तव्यो येन धर्ममवाप्नुयात्॥
en: Requested by others, one should say only what is correct after determining it with the help of reflection. One should give instruction in such a way that one may, by giving it, acquire merit.

description: Whether any sin is committed if a person give instructions to a lowcaste person. The story of a Brahmana and a Shudra
sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातमुपदेशकृते मया। महान् केशो हि भवति तस्मान्नोपदिशेदिह॥
en: I have thus told you everything about instructions very often persons become plunged into great afflictions on account of giving instruction. Hence it is proper that one should abstain from giving instruction to others.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कीदृशे पुरुषे तात स्त्रीषु वा भरतर्षभ। श्री: पद्मा वसते नित्यं तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, in what kind of man or woman, O chief of the Bharatas, does the goddess of Prosperity always live.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्णयिष्यामि यथावृत्तं यथाश्रुतम्। रुक्मिणी देवकीपुत्रसंनिधौ पर्यपृच्छत॥
en: Bhishma said About it, I shall describe to you what took place and what I have heard. Once on a time, the princess Rukmini put this question in the presence of Devaki's son.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: नारायणस्याङ्गतां ज्वलन्ती दृष्ट्वा श्रियं पद्मसमानवर्णाम्। कौतूहलाद् विस्मितचारु नेत्रा पप्रच्छ माता मकरध्वजस्य॥
en: Seeing ihe goddess of Prosperity, shining with beauty and gifted with the hue of the lotus, the mother of Pradyumna having the emblem of Makara on his banner, filled with curiosity, said these words.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: कानीह भूतान्युपसेवसे त्वं संतिष्ठसे कानिव सेवसे त्वम्। तानि त्रिलोकेश्वरभूतकान्ते तत्त्वेन मे ब्रूहि महर्षिकल्पे॥
en: Who are those beings whom you help and whom you serve? Who, again, are those whom you do not serve? O you who are dear to him who is the lord of all creatures, tell me this truly, O you who are equal to a great Rishi in penances and power.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: एवं तदा श्रीरभिभाष्यमाणा देव्या समक्षं गरुडध्वजस्य। उवाच वाक्यं मधुराभिधानं मनोहरं चन्द्रमुखी प्रसन्ना॥
en: Thus addressed by the princess, the goddess of Prosperity, with a face beautiful like the moon, and, actuated by grace in the presence of the deity having the emblem of Garuda on his banner, said these words in reply which were sweet and charming.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: श्रीरुवाच वसामि नित्यं सुभगे प्रगल्भे दक्षे नरे कर्मणि वर्तमाने। अक्रोधने देवपरे कृतज्ञे जितेन्द्रिये नित्यमुदीर्णसत्त्वे॥
en: Shree said O blessed lady, I always live with him who is eloquent, active, attentive to business, free from anger, given to the adoration of the gods, endued with gratitude, has his passions under complete restraint, and is highminded in everything.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: नाकर्मशीले पुरुषे वसामि न नास्तिके साङ्गरिके कृतघ्ने। न भिन्नवृत्ते न नृशंसवर्णे न चापि चौरे न गुरुष्वसूये॥
en: I never live with one who does not attend to business, who is an unbeliever, who causes an intermixture by his lustful habit, who is ungrateful, who is of impure deeds, who uses harsh and cruel words, who is a thief, and who cherishes malice towards his preceptors and other elders.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: ये चाल्पतेजोबलसत्त्वमानाः क्लिश्यन्ति कृप्यन्ति च यत्र तत्र। न चैव तिष्ठामि तथाविधेषु नरेषु संगुप्तमनोरथेषु॥
en: I never live in those persons who are gifted with little energy, strength, life, and honour, who are distressed at every, trifle, and who always indulge in anger. Nor do I ever live with those who think in one way and act in a different way.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: यश्चात्मनि प्रार्थयते न किञ्चिद् यश्च स्वभावोपहतान्तरात्मा। तेष्वल्पसंतोषपरेषु नित्यं नरेषु नाहं निवसामि सम्यक्॥
en: I never live also with him who never wishes for any acquisition for imself, or him who is so blinded as to rest satisfied with the lot in which he finds himself without any exertion, or with those who are contented with small gains.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: स्वधर्मशीलेषु च धर्मविस्तु वृद्धोपसेवानिरते च दान्ते। कृतात्मनि क्षान्तिपरे समर्थे क्षान्तासु दान्तासु तथाबलासु॥
en: I live with those who perform the duties of their own order, or those who are conversant with the duties of virtue, or those who are given to the service of the aged, or those who have their passions under restraint, or those that are gifted with purified souls, or those who observe the virtue of forgiveness, or those who are able and prompt in action, or with such women as are forgiving and self-controlled.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: सत्यस्वभावार्जवसंयुत्तासु वसामि देवद्विजपूजिकासु॥ प्रकीर्णभाण्डामनपेक्ष्यकारिणी सदा च भर्तुः प्रतिकूलवादिनीम्॥
en: I live with those women also who are given to truth and sincerity and who adore the gods. I do not live with those women also who do not look after household furniture and provisions scattered all around the house, and who always ulter words against the wishes of their husbands.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: मेवंविधां तां परिवर्जयामि। पापामचोक्षामवलेहिनीं च व्ययेतधैर्य कलहप्रिया च।।१२।
en: I always avoid those women who are fond of the houses of other people and who have no modesty. On the other hand, I live with those women who are devoted to their husbands, who are blessed in conduct, and who are always adorned with ornaments and well-clad.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: निद्राभिभूतां सततं शयानां एवंविधां तां परिवर्जयामि। सत्यासु नित्यं प्रियदर्शनासु सौभाग्ययुक्तासु गुणान्वितासु॥ वसामि नारीषु पतिव्रतासु कल्याणशीलासु विभूषितासु। यानेषु कन्यासु विभूषणेषु यज्ञेषु मेघेषु च वृष्टिमत्सु॥ वसामि फुल्लासु च पद्मिनीषु नक्षत्रवीथीषु च शारदीषु। गजेषु गोष्ठेषु तथाऽऽसनेषु सर:सु फुल्लोत्पलपङ्कजेषु।।१५।
en: I always live with those women who are truthful in words, who are handsome and lovely in appearance, who are blessed and whe are gifted with all accomplishments. I always avoid such women who are sinful and unclean or impure, who always lick the corners of their mouths, who have no patience or fortitude, and who are fond of dispute and quarrelling; who are indolent and sleepy and always inclined to lie down. I always live in conveyances and the animals that drag them, in maidens, in ornaments and good dresses, in sacrifices, in clouds charged with rain, in full-blown lotises. and in those stars that covers the autumnal sky. I live in elephants, in the cowpeng in good seats, and in lakes adorned with full-bloun lotuses.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: नदीषु हंसस्वननादितासु क्रौञ्चावघुष्टस्वरशोभितासु। विकीर्णकूलद्रुमराजितासु तपस्विसिद्धद्विजसेवितासु।।१६।
en: I live also in such rivers as pass by with sweet murinurs, melodious with the music of cranes, having banks adorned with row of various trees, and resorted to by Brahmanas and ascetics.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: वसामि नित्यं सुबहूदकासु सिंहैर्गजैश्चाकुलितोदकासु। मत्ते गजे गोवृषभे नरेन्द्र सिंहासने सत्पुरुषेषु नित्यम्।।१७।
en: I always live in those rivers also which havo deep and extensive waters rendered turbid by lions and elephants plunging into them for bathing or satisfying their thirst. I live also in angry elephants, in bulls, in kings, on the throne, and in good men.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: यस्मिन् जनो हव्यभुजं जुहोति गोब्राह्मणं चार्चति देवताश्च। काले च पुष्पैर्बलयः क्रियन्ते तस्मिन् गृहे नित्यमुपैमि वासम्॥
en: I always live in that house in which the inmate pours libations on the sacrificial fire and adore kine, Brahmanas, and the gods. I live in that house where at the proper time offerings are made, to the gods, of flowers in course of worship.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: स्वाध्यायनित्येषु सदा द्विजेषु क्षत्रे च कृष्याभिरते सदैव। वैश्ये च धर्माभिरते वसामि शूद्रे शुश्रूषणनित्ययुक्ते॥
en: I always live in such Brahmanas as are given to the study of the Vedas, in Kshatriyas devoted to the observance of virtue, in Vaishyas devoted to cultivation, and in Shudras devoted to the service of the three upper castes.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: नारायणे त्वेकमना वसामि सर्वेण भावेन शरीरभूता। तस्मिन् हि धर्मः सुमहान् निविष्टो ब्रह्मण्यता चात्र तथा प्रियत्वम्॥
en: I live, with a heart firm and unshaken, in Narayana, in my embodied self. In Him exists virtue, full and perfect, devotion to the Brahmanas, and the quality of goodness.

description: The kind of person in whom prosperity dwells. The conversation between Rukmini and the goddess Shree
sn: नाहं शरीरेण वसामि देवि नैवं मया शक्यमिहाभिधातुम्। भावेन यस्मिन् निवसामि पुंसि स वर्धते धर्मयशोर्थकामैः॥
en: Can I not say, O lady, that I do not live in my embodied form? That person in whom I live in spirit increases in virtue and fame and wealth and object of desire.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच स्त्रीपुंसयोः सम्प्रयोगे स्पर्शः कस्याधिको भवेत्। एतस्मिन् संशये राजन् यथावद् वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said You should, O king, tell me truly which of the two, viz., man or woman, gets the greater pleasure from an act of union with each other. Kindly remove my doubt it.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। भंगास्वनेन शक्रस्य तथा वैरमभूत् पुरा॥
en: Bhishma said To illustrate this question, the old discourse between Bhangasvana and Shakra is cited in this connection.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: पुरा भंगास्वनो नाम राजर्षिरतिधार्मिकः। अपुत्रः पुरुषव्याघ्र पुत्रार्थं यज्ञमाहरत्॥
en: In days of old there lived a king name Bhangasvana. He was very pious and was known as a royal sage. He was, however, childless, O king, and, therefore, made a sacrifice from desire of getting a son.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: अग्निष्टुतं स राजर्षिरिन्द्रद्विष्टं महाबलः। प्रायश्चित्तेषु मर्त्यानां पुत्रकामेषु चेष्यते॥
en: The sacrifice which that powerful king celebrated was Agnishtuta, which on account of the god of fire being alone worshipped in it, is always disliked by Indra. Yet it is the sacrifice that is desired by men when for the object of getting children they seek to purify themselves of their sins.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: इन्द्रो ज्ञात्वा तु तं यज्ञं महाभागः सुरेश्वरः। अन्तरं तस्य राजर्षेरन्विच्छनियतात्मनः॥
en: Learning that the king was desirous of performing the Agnishtuta, the highly blessed king of the gods, viz., Indra, began from that moment to look for the shortcomings of that royal sage to well controlled soul.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: न चैवास्यान्तरं राजन् स ददर्श महात्मनः। कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य मृगयां गतवान् नृपः॥
en: Despite, all his careful watch Indra, however, O king, could not find any shortcomings on the part of the great king. Sometimes after, one day, the king went on a hunting expedition.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: इदमन्तरमित्येव शक्रो नृपममोहयत्। एकाश्वेन च राजर्षिर्धान्त इन्द्रेण मोहितः॥
en: Saying to himself, this, indeed, is an opportunity, Indra stupefied th, king. The king went alone on his horse, confounded, because of the king of the gods having stupefied his senses.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: न दिशाऽविन्दत नृपः क्षुत्पिपासादितस्तदा। इतश्चेतश्च वै राजन् श्रमतृष्णान्वितो नृप॥
en: Stricken with hunger and thirst, the king's confusion was so great that he could not see the cardinal points. Indeed, stricken with thirst, he began to rove about.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: सरोऽपश्यत् सुरुचिरं पूर्णं परमवारिणा। सोऽवगाह सरस्तात पाययामास वाजिनम्॥
en: He then saw a lake that was highly beautiful and was full of transparent water. Descending from his horse, and plunging into the lake, he made his animal to drink.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: अथ पीतोदकं सोऽश्वं वृक्षे बद्ध्वा नृपोत्तमः। अवगाह्य ततः स्नातस्तत्र स्त्रीत्वमवाप्तवान्॥
en: Tying his horse then, whose thirst had been satisfied, to a tree, the king plunged into the lake again for doing his ablutions. To his surprise he found that he was metamorphosed by virtue of the waters, into a woman.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: आत्मानं स्त्रीकृतं दृष्ट्वा वीडितो नृपसत्तमः। चिन्तानुगतसर्वात्मा वयाकुलेन्द्रियचेतनः॥
en: Seeing himself thus changed in respect of sex itself, the king became filled with shame. With his senses and mind completely agitated, he began to think thus with his whole heart.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: आरोहिष्ये कथं त्वश्वं कथं यास्यामि वै पुरम्। इष्टेनाग्निष्टुता चापि पुत्राणां शतमौरसम्॥ जातं महाबलानां मे तान् प्रवक्ष्यामि किं त्वहम्। दारेषु चात्मकीयषु पौरजानपदेषु च॥
en: Alas, how shall I ride my horse? How return to my capital? On account of the Agnishtuta sacrifice I have got a hundred sons all gifted with great strength, and all children of my own loins! Alas, thus changed, what shall I say to them? What shall I say to my wives, my relatives and wellwishers, and my subjects of the city and the provinces?

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: मृदुत्वं च तनुत्वं च विक्लवत्वं तथैव च। स्त्रीगुणा ऋषिभिः प्रोक्ता धर्मतत्त्वार्थदर्शिभिः॥
en: Rishis versed in the truths of duty and religion and other matters say that mildness and softness and susceptibility to extreme agitation are the characteristics of women, and that activity, hardness, and energy are the characteristics of men. Alas, my manliness is gone! For why has femininity possessed me? On account of this change of sex, how shall I succeed in riding my horse again?

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: व्यायामे कर्कशत्वं च वीर्यं च पुरुषे गुणाः। पौरुषं विप्रनष्टं वै स्त्रीत्वं कनापि मेऽभवत्॥
en: Having thought thus the king, with great exertion, mounted his horse and returned to his capital, changed though he had been into a woman.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: स्त्रीभावात् पुनरश्वं तं कथमारोढुमुत्सहे। महता त्वथ यत्नेन आरुह्याश्वं नराधिपः॥
en: Seeing that extraordinary change his sons and wives and servants, and his subject of the city and the provinces were extremely amazed.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: पुनरायात् पुरं तात स्त्रीकृतो नृपसत्तमः। पुत्रा दाराश्च भृत्याश्च पौरजानपदाश्च ते॥
en: Then addressing them all, that royal sage, that foremost of orators, said, I had gone out on a hunting expedition, accompanied by a large army. Losing all knowledge of the cardinal points I entered a thick and dreadful forest, moved by the fates.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: किंत्विदं विति विज्ञाय विस्मयं परमं गताः। अथोवाच स राजर्षिः स्त्रीभूतो वदतां वरः॥ मृगयामस्मि निर्याता बलैः परिवृतो दृढम्। उद्भ्रान्तः प्राविशं घोरामटवीं दैवचोदितः।॥
en: In that terrible forest, I became very much thirsty and lost my senses. I then saw a beautiful lake abounding with fowl of all sorts.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: अटव्यां च सुघोरायां तृष्णा” नष्टचेतनः। सरः सुरुचिरप्रख्यमपश्यं पक्षिभिर्वृतम्॥ तत्रावगाढः स्त्रीभूतो दैवेनाहं कृतः पुराः। नामगोत्राणि चाभाष्य दाराणां मन्त्रिणां तथा॥
en: Plunging into that lake for performing my ablutions, I was changed into a woman! Summoning then his wives and counsellors, and all his sons by their names, that best of kings changed into a woman said to them these words: Do you enjoy this kingdom happily. About myself, I shall go to the forest, you sons.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: आह पुत्रांस्ततः सोऽथ स्त्रीभूतः पार्थिवोत्तमः। सम्प्रीत्या भुज्यतां राज्यं वनं यास्यामि पुत्रकाः॥
en: Having said thus to his children, the king went to the forest. Arrived there, she arrived at a hermitage inhabited by an ascetic.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
sn: एवमुक्त्वा पुत्रशतं वनमेव जगाम ह। गत्वा चैवाश्रमं सा तु तापसं प्रत्यपद्यत॥ तापसेनास्य पुत्राणामाश्रमेष्वभवच्छतम्। अथ साऽऽदाय तान् सर्वान् पूर्वपुत्रानभाषत।॥
en: By that ascetic the changed monarch gave birth to a hundred sons. Taking all those children of hers, she went to where her former children were, and addressing the latter, said, You are the children of my loins while I was a man. These are my children given birth to by me in this state of change. Sons, do you all enjoy my kingdom together, like brothers born of the saine parents.

description: -continued Whether man or woman gets greater pleasure from an act of union
