description: -continued The story of Indra and Matanga
sn: तदेवं शोकहर्षी तु कामद्वेषौ च पुत्रका अतिमानातिवादौ च प्रविशेते द्विजाधमम्॥
en: While wandering in that existence, joy and grief, desire and hatred vanity and evil speech, scck to enter into him and make a wretch of him.

description: -continued The story of Indra and Matanga
sn: तांश्चज्जयति शत्रून् स तदा प्राप्नोति सद्गतिम्। अथ ते वै जयन्त्येनं तालाग्रादिव पात्यते॥
en: If he succeeds in subjugating those foes, he then acquires a high end. If, on the other hand, those enemies succeed in subjugating him, he falls down from that high position like a person falling down on the ground from the high top of a palmyra tree.

description: -continued The story of Indra and Matanga
sn: मतङ्ग सम्प्रधायँवं यदहं त्वामचूचुदम्। वृणीष्व काममन्यं त्वं ब्राह्मण्यं हि सुदुर्लभम्॥
en: Knowing this for certain, O Matanga that I say to you do you name some other boon, for the status of a Brahmana is incapable of being acquired by you.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्तो मतङ्गस्तु संशितात्मा यतव्रतः। सहस्रमेकपादेन ततो ध्याने व्यतिष्ठत॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by Indra, Matanga refused to hear what he was commanded. On the other hand, with regulated vows and purified soul, he practised austerer penances by standing on one foot for a thousand years, being deeply engaged in Yoga-meditation.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: तं सहस्रावरे काले शक्रो द्रष्टुमुपागमत्। तदेव च पुनर्वाक्यमुवाच बलवृत्रहा॥
en: After a thousand years had passed away, Shakra once more came to see him. Indeed the destroyer of Vala and Vritra laid to him the same words.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: मतङ्ग उवाच इदं वर्षसहस्रं वै ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः। अतिष्ठमेकपादेन ब्राह्मण्यं प्राप्नुयां कथम्॥
en: Matanga said I have passed these thousand years, standing on one foot, with soul engaged in meditation and in the observance of the vow of celibacy. Why is it that I have not yet succeeded in acquiring the dignity of a Brahmana?

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: शक्र उवाच चण्डालयोनौ जातेन नावाप्यं वै कथंचन। अन्यं कामं वृणीष्व त्वं मा वृथा तेऽस्त्वयं श्रमः॥ एवमुक्तो मतङ्गस्तु भृशं शोकपरायणः। अध्यतिष्ठद्गयां गत्वा सोऽङ्गुष्ठेन शतं समाः॥
en: Shakra said One born as a Chandala cannot, by any means, acquire the dignity of a Brahmana. Do you, therefore, name some other boon so that all this labour of yours may not prove futile! Thus addressed by the king of the celestials, Matanga became filled with grief. He went to Gaya, and passed there a century of years, standing all the while on one foot.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: सुदुर्वहं वहन् योगं कृशो धमनिसंततः। त्वगस्थिभूतो धर्मात्मा स पपातेति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: On account of the observance of such Yoga which was extremely difficult to bear, he became very much emaciated and his arteries and veins became swollen and visible. He was reduced to only skin and bones. We have heard that righteous person, while practising those austerities at Gaya, dropped down on the ground from sheer exhaustion.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: तं पतन्तमभिदुत्य परिजग्राह वासवः। वराणामीश्वरो दाता सर्वभूतहिते रतः॥
en: Seeing him falling down the lord and giver of boons, engaged in the behoof of all creatures viz., Vasava, speedily came to that spot and held him fast.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: शक्र उवाच मतङ्ग ब्राह्मणत्वं ते विरुद्धमिह दृश्यते। ब्राह्मण्यं दुर्लभतरं संवृतं परिपन्थिभिः॥
en: Shakra said It seems, O Matanga , that the dignity of a Brahmana which you seek is illsuited to you. That dignity is incapable of being acquired by you. Indeed in your case, it is beset with many dangers.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: पूजयन् सुखपाप्नोति दुःखमाप्नोत्यपूजयन्। ब्राह्मणः सर्वभूतानां योगक्षेमसमर्पिता॥
en: A person by adoring a Brahmana acquires happiness; while by abstaining from such worship, he gets grief and misery. The Brahmana is as regards all creatures, the giver of what they prize or covet and the protector of what they already have.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽनुतृप्यन्ते पितरो देवतास्तथा। ब्राह्मणः सर्वभूतानां मतङ्ग पर उच्यते॥
en: It is through the Brahmanas that the departed manes and the deities become pleased. The Brahmana, O Matanga, is said to be the foremost of all created Beings. The Brahmana grants all objects which are desired and in the way they are desired.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: ब्राह्मणः कुरुते तद्धि यथा यद् यच्च वाञ्छति। बह्वीस्तु संविशन् योनीर्जायमानः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Passing through numberless orders of being and undergoing repeated rebirths, one succeeds in some subsequent birth in acquiring the dignity of a Brahmana.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: पर्याये तात कस्मिंश्चिद् ब्राह्मण्यमिह विन्दति। तदुत्सृज्येह दुष्प्रापं ब्राह्मण्यमकृतात्मभिः॥
en: That dignity is really incapable of being obtained by persons of impure souls. Do you, therefore, relinquish the idea Do you name some other boon. The particular boon which you seek is incapable of being granted to you.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: मतङ्ग उवाच अन्यं वरं वृणीष्व त्वं दुर्लभोऽयं हि ते वरः। किं मां तुदसि दुःखार्तं मृतं मारयसे च माम्॥
en: Matanga said Stricken as I am with grief, why, O Shakra, do you afflict me further? You are striking one that is already dead, by this conduct. I do not pity you who having acquired the dignity of a Brahmana fail to retain it.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: त्वां तु शोचामि यो लब्वा ब्राह्मण्यं न बुभूषसे। ब्राह्मण्यं यदि दुष्प्रापं त्रिभिर्वर्णैः शतक्रतो॥ सुदुर्लभं सदावाप्य नानुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः। यः पापेभ्यः पापतमस्तेषामधम एव सः॥
en: Those who having won the dignity of a Brahmana that, like wealth, is so difficult to acquire, do not seek to keep it up, must be considered as the most wretched in this world. Indeed, they are the most sinful of all creatures.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: ब्राह्मण्यं यो न जानीते धनं लब्वेव दुर्लभम्। दुष्प्रापं खलु विप्रत्वं प्राप्तं दुरनुपालनम्॥
en: Forsooth, the dignity of a Brahmana is highly difficult to attain, and being attained, is difficult to maintain, it is capable of removing every sort of grief. Alas, having got it men do not always seek to keep it up.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: दुरावापमवाप्यैतन्नानुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः। एकारामो ह्यहं शक्र निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः॥
en: When even such persons are considered as Brahmanas, why is it that I, who am pleased with my own self, who am superior to all pairs of opposites, who am dissociated from all worldly objects, who am observant of the duty of mercy towards all creatures and of selfcontrol of conduct, should be considered worthy of that dignity?

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: अहिंसादममास्थाय कथं नार्हामि विप्रताम्। दैवं तु कथमेतद् वै यदहं मातृदोषतः॥
en: not How unfortunate I am, O Purandara, that through the sin of my mother I have been reduced to this plight, although I am not unrighteous in my conduct?

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: एतामवस्थां सम्प्राप्तो धर्मज्ञः सन् पुरंदर। नूनं दैवं न शक्यं हि पौरुषेणातिवर्तितुम्॥
en: Forsooth, Destiny is incapable of being warded off or conquered by individual exertion since, O lord, I am unable to acquire, despite these.persistent attempts of mine the object for the acquisi.ion of which I am trying.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: यदर्थे यत्नवानेव न लभे विप्रतां विभो। एवंगते तु धर्मज्ञ दातुमर्हसि मे वरम्।॥
en: When such is the case, O righteous one, you should grant me some other boon if, indeed, I have become worthy of your favour or if I have a little of merit!

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच यदि तेऽमनुग्राह्यः किंचिद् वा सुकृतं मम। वृणीष्वेति तदा प्राह ततस्तं बलवृत्रहा॥
en: Bhishma said The destroyer of Vala and Vritra then said to him Do you name the boon! Thus urged by the great Indra, Matanga said the following words

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: मतङ्ग उवाच चोदितस्तु महेन्द्रेण मतङ्गः प्राब्रवीदिदम्। यथा कामविहारी स्यां कामरूपी विहङ्गमः॥
en: Matanga said Gifted with the power of assuming any form at will, let me be able to journey through the skies and let me enjoy whatever pleasures I may wish for. And let me also have the willing worship of both Brahmanas and Kshatriyas.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: ब्रह्मक्षत्राविरोधेन पूजां च प्राप्नुयामहम्। यथा ममाक्षया कीर्तिर्भवेच्चापि पुरंदर॥
en: I bow to you by bending my head, O god! You should do that also by which my fame, O Purandara, may live eternally in the world!

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: शक्र उवाच कर्तुमर्हसि तद् देव शिरसा त्वां प्रसादये। छन्दोदेव इति ख्यातः स्त्रीणां पूज्यो भविष्यसि॥
en: Shakra said You will be celebrated as the deity of a particular measure of verse and you will get the worship of all women. Your fame, O son, shall become peerless in the three worlds.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: कीर्तिश्च तेऽतुला वत्स त्रिषु लोकेषु यास्यति। एवं तस्मै वरं दत्त्वा वासवोऽन्तरधीयत॥
en: Having granted him these boons, Vasava disappeared there and then. Matanga also renouncing his lifebreaths, acquired a high place.

description: The story of Indra and Matanga on the subject
sn: प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा मतङ्गोऽपि सम्प्राप्तः स्थानमुत्तमम्। एवमेतत् परं स्थानं ब्राह्मण्यं नाम भारत। तच्च दुष्प्रापमिह वै महेन्द्रवचनं यथा॥
en: You may thus see, O Bharata that the dignity of a Brahmana is very high. That dignity is incapable of being acquired here as said by the great Indra himself.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतं मे महदाख्यानमेतत् कुरुकुलोद्वह। सुदुष्प्रापं यद् ब्रवीषि ब्राह्मण्यं वदतां वरा॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have heard this great description, 0, perpetuater of Kuru's race. You, O foremost of eloquent men, have said that the dignity of a Brahmana is greatly difficult of acquisition.

sn: विश्वामित्रेण च पुरा ब्राह्मण्यं प्राप्तमित्युत। श्रूयते वदसे तच्च दुष्प्रापमिति सत्तम॥
en: It is heard, however, that in former times the dignity of a Brahmana had been acquired by Vishvamitra. You, however, O best of men, tell us that dignity is incapable of being won.

sn: वीतहव्यश्च नृपतिः श्रुतो मे विप्रतां गतः। तदेव तावद् गाङ्गेय श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं विभो॥
en: I have also heard that formerly king Vitahavya had succeeded in acquiring the dignity of a Brahmana. O powerful one, I wish to hear, O son of Ganga, the story of king Vitahavya's promotion.

sn: सकेन कर्मणा प्राप्तो ब्राह्मण्यं राजसत्तमः। वरेण तपसा वापि तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: By what acts did that best of kings succeed in acquiring the dignity of a Brahmana? Was it through some boon or was it through the virtue of penances? You should tell me everything.

sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु राजन् यथा राजा वीतहव्यो महायशाः। राजर्षिर्दुर्लभं प्राप्तो ब्राह्मण्यं लोकसत्कृतम्॥
en: Bhishma said Hear, O king, how the highly illustrious royal sage Vitahavya succeeded formerly in acquiring the dignity of a Brahmana that is so difficult to attain and that is held in such high esteem by all the world.

sn: मनोर्महात्मनस्तात प्रजा धर्मेण शासतः। बभूव पुत्रो धर्मात्मा शर्यातिरिति विश्रुतः॥
en: While the great Manu in days of yore was employed in ruling righteously his subjects, he obtained a son of righteous soul who become celebrated under the name of Sharyati.

sn: तस्यान्ववाये द्वौ राजन् राजानौ सम्वभूवतुः। हैहयस्तालजंघश्च वत्सस्य जयतां वर॥
en: In Sharyati's family, O monarch, two kings were born viz., Haihaya and Talajangha. Both of them were sons of Vatsa, O foremost of victorious kings.

sn: हैहयस्य तु राजेन्द्र दशसु स्त्रीषु भारत। शतं बभूव पुत्राणां शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम्॥
en: Haihaya, O monarch, had ten wives. Upon them he beget, O Bharata, hundred sons all of whom were heroes who never returned from the battle field.

sn: तुल्यरूपप्रभावाणां बलिनां युद्धशालिनाम्। धनुर्वेदे च वेदे च सर्वत्रैव कृतश्रमाः॥
en: All of them resembled one another in features and prowess. All of them were gifted with great strength and all of them were possessed of great skill in battle. They all studied the Vedas and the science of weapons thoroughly.

sn: काशिष्वपि नृपो राजन् दिवोदासपितामहः। हर्यश्व इति विख्यातो बभूव जयतां वरः॥
en: In Kashi also, O monarch, there was a king who was the grandfather of Divodasa. The foremost of victorious men, he passed by the name of Haryashva.

sn: स वीतहव्यदायादैरागत्य पुरुषर्षभ। गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये संग्रामे विनिपातितः॥
en: The sons of king Haihaya, O chief of men, invaded the kingdom of Kashi, and advancing to the country that lies between the rivers Ganga and Yamuna fought a battle with king Haryashva and killed him in it.

sn: तं तु हत्वा नरपति हैहयास्ते महारथाः। प्रतिजग्मुः पुरी रम्यां वत्सानामकुतोभया:॥
en: Having killed king Haryashva thus, the sons of Haihaya, those great car warriors fearlessly returned to their own charming city in the country of the Vatsas.

sn: हर्यश्वस्य च दायादः काशिराजोऽभ्यषिच्यता सुदेवो देवसंकाशः साक्षाद् धर्म इवापरः॥
en: Meanwhile Haryashva's son Sudeva who looked like a celestial in splendour and who was a second god of virtue, was installed on the throne of Kashi as its king.

sn: स पालयामास महीं धर्मात्मा काशिनन्दनः। तैर्वीतहव्यैरागत्य युधि सर्वैर्विनिर्जितः॥
en: The delighter of Kashi, the righteous-souled prince ruled his kingdom for some time when the hundred sons of Vitihavya once more attacked his territories and defeated him in battle.

sn: तमथाजौ विनिर्जित्य प्रतिजग्मुर्यथागतम्। सौदेवस्त्वथ काशीशो दिवोदासोऽभ्यषिच्यत॥
en: Having defeated king Sudeva thus, the victors returned to their own city. After this, Divodasa, the son of Sudeva, became installed on the throne of Kashi as its king.

sn: दिवोदासस्तु विज्ञाय वीर्यं तेषां यतात्मनाम्। वाराणसी महातेजा निर्ममे शक्रशासनात्॥
en: Understanding the prowess of those great princess viz., the sons of Vitihavya, king Divodasa, gifted with great energy, rebuilt and fortified the city of Varanasi at the command of Indra.

sn: विप्रक्षत्रियसम्बाधां वैश्यशूद्रसमाकुलाम्। नैकद्रव्योच्चयवती समृद्धविपणापणाम्॥ गङ्गाया उत्तरे कूले वप्रान्ते राजसत्तमा गोमत्या दक्षिणे कूले शक्रस्येवामरावतीम्॥
en: The territories of Divodasa were full of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. and they teemed with all sorts of articles and provisions, and were adorned with prosperous shops and marts. Those territories O best of kings, extended northwards from the banks of Ganga to the southern Banks of Gomati, and resembled a second Amaravati (the city of Indra).

sn: तत्र तं राजशार्दूलं निवसन्तं महीपतिम्। आगत्य हैहया भूयः पर्थधावन्त भारत॥
en: The Haihayas once again, O Bharata, attacked that foremost of kings as he ruled his kingdom.

sn: स निष्क्रम्य ददौ युद्धं तेभ्यो राजा महाबलः। देवासुरसमं घोरं दिवोदासो महाद्युतिः॥
en: The powerful king Divodasa gifted with great splendour, issuing out of his capital, gave them battle. The engagement between the two parties terrible like the encounter in days of old between the celestials and the Asuras.

sn: स तु युद्धे महाराज दिनानां दशतीर्दश। हतवाहनभूयिष्ठस्ततो दैन्यमुपागमत्॥
en: King Divodasa fought the enemy for a thousand days at the end of which, having lost a large number of followers and animals, he became greatly distressed.

sn: हतयोधस्ततो राजन् क्षीणकोशश्च भूमिपः। दिवोदासः पुरीं त्यक्त्वा पलायनपरोऽभवत्॥
en: King Divodasa, O king, having lost his army and seeing his treasury exhausted left his capital and fled away.

sn: गत्वाऽऽश्रमपदं रम्यं भरद्वाजस्य धीमतः। जगाम शरणं राजा कृताञ्जलिररिन्दम॥
en: Going to the charming herinitage of the wise Bharadvaja, the king, O chastiser of foes, joining his hands in respect sought the Rishi's protection.

sn: तमुवाच भरद्वाजो ज्येष्ठः पुत्रो बृहस्पतेः। पुरोधाः शीलसम्पन्नो दिवोदासं महीपतिम्॥ किमागमनकृत्यं ते सर्वे प्रब्रूहि मे नृप। यत् ते प्रिय तत् करिष्ये न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा।।२५
en: Seeing king Divodasa before him, the eldest son of Brihaspati, viz., Bharadvaja of excellent conduct, who was the monarch's priest, said to him What is the reason of your coming here? Tell me everything, o king! I shall do that which is agreeable to you, without any scruple.

sn: राजोवाच भगवन् वैतहव्यैर्मे युद्धे वंशः प्रणाशितः। अहमेकः परियूनो भवन्तं शरणं गतः॥
en: The king said O holy one, the sons of Vitahavya have killed all the children and men of my house. I only have escaped with life, totally discomfited by the enemy, I seek refuge with you.

sn: शिष्यस्नेहेन भगवंस्त्वं मां रक्षितुमर्हसि। एकशेषः कृतो वंशो मम तैः पापकर्मभिः॥
en: You should, O holy one, protect me with such affection as you have for a disciple! Those princes of sinful deeds have killed my whole family, leaving myself only alive.

sn: भीष्म उवाच तमुवाच महाभागो भरद्वाजः प्रतापवान्। न भेतव्यं न भेतव्यं सौदेव व्येतु ते भयम्॥
en: Bhishma said Bharadvaja of great energy said to him who pleaded so piteously Do not fear! Do not fear! O son of Sudeva, let your fears be gone.

sn: अहमिष्टिं करिष्यामि पुत्रार्थं ते विशाम्पते। वीतहव्यसहस्राणि येन त्वं प्रहरिष्यसि॥
en: son on I shall perform a sacrifice, O monarch, in order that you may have a son through whom you will be able to smite thousand upon thousands of Vitahavya's party.

sn: तत इष्टिं चकारर्षिस्तस्य वै पुत्रकामिकीम्। अथास्य तनयो जज्ञे प्रतर्दन इति श्रुतः॥
en: After this, the Rishi performed a sacrifice with the object of bestowing a Divodasa. As the result thereof, to Divodasa was born a son named Pratarddana.

sn: स जातमात्रो ववृधे समाः सद्यस्त्रयोदश। वेदं चापि जगौ कृत्स्नं धनुर्वेदं च भारत॥
en: As soon as he was born, he grew into a child of full three and ten years, and quickly mastered the entire Vedas and the whole sciences of arms.

sn: योगेन च समाविष्टो भरद्वाजेन धीमता। तेजो लोक्यं स संगृह्य तस्मिन् देशे समाविशत्॥३२
en: Helped by his Yoga powers, the highly intelligent Bharadvaja had entered into the prince. Indeed, collecting all the energy of the objects of the universe, Bharadvaja caused it to enter the body of prince Pratarddana.

sn: तत: स कवची धन्वी स्तूयमानः सुरर्षिभिः। वन्दिभिर्वन्द्यमानश्च बभौ सूर्य इवोदितः॥
en: Casing his person in shining mail and armed with the bow, Pratarddana, his praises lauded by bards and the celestial Rishi, shone resplendent like the Sun.

sn: स रथी बद्धनिस्त्रिंशो बभौ दीप्त इवानलः। प्रययौ स धनुर्छन्वन् खड्गी चर्मी शरासनी॥
en: Mounted on his car and with the scimitar tied to his belt, he shone like a burning fire. With scimitar and shield and whirling his shield, as he went, he proceeded to the presence of his father.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा परमं हर्षे सुदेवतनयो ययौ। मेने च मनसा दग्धान् वैतहव्यान् स पार्थिवः॥
en: Seeing the prince, the son of Sudeva, viz., king Divodasa become filled with joy. Indeed, the old king thought the sons of his enemy Vitahavya as already killed.

sn: ततोऽसौ यौवराज्ये च स्थापयित्वा प्रतर्दनम्। कृतकृत्यं तदाऽऽत्मानं स राजा अभ्यनन्दत॥
en: Divodasa then installed his son Pratarddana as the heirapparent, and considering himself crowned with success became highly happy.

sn: ततस्तु वैतहव्यानां वधाय स महीपतिः। पुत्रं प्रस्थापयामास प्रतर्दनमरिंदमम्॥
en: After this, the old king commanded that chastiser of foes, viz., prince Pratarddana, to march against the sons of Vitahavya and kill them in battle.

sn: सरथः स तु संतीर्य गङ्गामाशु पराक्रमी। प्रययौ वीतहव्यानां पुरी परपुरंजयः॥
en: Gifted with great prowess Pratarddana, that subjugator of hostile cities, speedily crossed Ganga on his car and proceeded against the city of the Vitahavyas.

sn: वैतहव्यास्तु संश्रुत्य रथघोषं समुद्धतम्। निर्ययुर्नगराकारै रथैः पररथारुजैः॥
en: Hearing the clatter of the wheels of his car, the sons of Vitahavya riding on their own cars that looked fortified citadels and that were capable of destroying hostile vehicles, issued out of their city.

sn: निष्क्रम्य ते नरव्याघ्रा दंशिताश्चित्रयोधिनः। प्रतर्दनं समाजग्मुः शरवर्षेरुदायुधाः॥
en: Coming out of their capital. those foremost of men., viz., the sons of Vitahavya, who were all skilful warriors cased in mail rushed with uplifted weapons towards Pratarddana, covering him with showers of arrows.

sn: शस्त्रैश्च विविधाकारै रथौरैच युधिष्ठिर। अभ्यवर्षन्त राजानं हिमवन्तमिवाम्बुदाः॥
en: Surrounding him with numberless cars, O Yudhishthira, the Vitahavyas poured upon Pratarddana showers of weapons of various sorts like the clouds pouring torrents of rain on the breast of Himavat.

sn: अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य तेषां राजा प्रतर्दनः। जघान तान् महातेजा वज्रानलसमैः शरैः॥
en: Baffling their weapons with his own, prince Pratarddana gifted with great energy killed them all with arrows that resembled the thunder bolt of Indra.

sn: कृत्तोत्तमाङ्गास्ते राजन् भल्लैः शतसहस्रशः। अपतन् रुधिरार्द्राङ्गा निकृत्ता इव किंशुकाः॥
en: Their heads cut off, O king, with hundreds and thousands of broad headed arrows, the warriors of Vitahavya dropped down with blood dyed bodies like Kinshuka trees felled on every side by woodmen with their axes.

sn: हतेषु तेषु सर्वेषु वीतहव्यः सुतेष्वथा प्राद्रवन्नगरं हित्वा भृगोराश्रममप्युत॥
en: After all his warriors and sons had been killed in battle, king Vitahavya fled away from his capital to the hermitage of Bhrigu.

sn: ययौ भृगुं च शरणं वीतहव्यो नराधिपः। अभयं च ददौ तस्मै राज्ञे राजन् भृगुस्तदा॥
en: Indeed, arrived there the royal fugitive sought refuge with Bhrigu. The Rishi Bhrigu, O monarch, assured the defeated king of his protection.

sn: अथानुपदमेवाशु तत्रागच्छत् प्रतर्दनः। स प्राप्य चाश्रमपदं दिवोदासात्मजोऽब्रवीत्॥ भो भो केऽत्राश्रमे सन्ति भृगोः शिष्या महात्मनः। द्रष्टुमिच्छे मुनिमहं तस्याचक्षत मामिति॥
en: Pratarddana followed in the footsteps of Vitahavya. Arrived at the Rishi's hermitage, the son of Divodasa said in a loud voice Ho, listen ye disciples of the great Bhrigu that may happen to be present! I wish to see the sage, Go and inform him of this.

sn: स तं विदित्वा तु भृगुनिश्चक्रामाश्रमात् तदा। पूजयामास च ततो विधिना नृपसत्तमम्॥
en: Knowing that it was Pratarddana who had come, the Rishi Bhrigu himself came out of his hermitage and adored that best of kings according to due rites.

sn: उवाच चैन राजेन्द्र किं कार्यं ब्रूहि पार्थिव। स चोवाच नृपस्तस्मै यदागमनकारणम्॥
en: Addressing him then, the Rishi said: Tell me, o king, what is your business! The king, at this informed the Rishi of the reason of his arrival.

sn: राजोवाच अयं ब्रह्मन्नितो राजा वीतहव्यो विसर्ग्यताम्। तस्य पुत्रैर्हि मे कृत्स्नो ब्रह्मन् वंशःप्रणाशितः॥
en: The king said King Vitahavya has come here, O Brahmana! Do you surrender him. His sons, O Brahmana, had destroyed my family.

sn: उत्सादितश्च विषयः काशीनां रत्नसंचयः। एतस्य वीर्यदृप्तस्य हतं पुत्रशतं मया॥
en: They had devastated the territories and the wealth of the Kashis. Those hundred sons, however, of this king proud of his power, have all been killed by me.

sn: अस्येदानी वधादद्य भविष्याम्यनृणः पितुः। तमुवाच कृपाविष्टो भृगुर्धर्मभृतां वरः॥ नेहास्ति क्षत्रियः कश्चित् सर्वे हीमे द्विजातयः। एतत् तु वचनं श्रुत्वा भृगोस्तथ्यं प्रतर्दनः॥ पादावुपस्पृश्य शनैः प्रहृष्टो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। एवमप्यस्मि भगवन् कृतकृत्या न संशयः॥ य एष राजा वीर्येण स्वजातिं त्याजितो मया। अनुजानीहि मां ब्रह्मन् ध्यायस्व च शिवेन माम्।।५५
en: By killing that king himself I shall today satisfy the debt I owe to my father! To him that foremost of righteous men, viz., the Rishi Bhrigu, stricken with mercy, replied by saying There is no Kshatriya in this hermitage. They who are here, are all Brahmanas! Hearing these words of Bhrigu, that must he thought be consonant with truth Pratarddana touched the Rishi's feet slowly and filled with joy said By this, O holy one, I am forsooth crowned with success, since this king becomes divested of the very order of his birth on account of my prowess! Give me your permission O Brahmana, to leave you and let me solicit you to pray for my wellbeing.

sn: त्याजितो हि मया जातिमेष राजा भृगूद्वह। ततस्तेनाभ्यनुज्ञातो ययौ राजा प्रतर्दनः॥ यथागतं महाराज मुक्त्वा विषमिवोरगः। भृगोर्वचनमात्रेण स च ब्रह्मर्षितां गतः॥
en: cause. This king, O founder of the family that goes by your name becomes divested of the very order of his birth, on account of my might! Dismissed by the Rishi Bhrigu, king Pratarddana then left that hermitage, and went to the place he had come from, having, in the way I have described, voinited forth the poison of specch even as a snake vomits forth its real poison. Meanwhile, king Vitahavya, acquired the dignity of the twice born sage by virtue of the worth only of Bhrigu.

sn: वीतहव्यो महाराज ब्रह्मवादित्वमेव च। तस्य गृत्समदः पुत्रो रूपेणेन्द्र इवापरः॥
en: And he acquired also a complete mastery of all the Vedas through the same Vitahavya had a son named Gritsamada who in beauty of person was a second Indra.

sn: शक्रस्त्वमिति यो दैत्यैर्निगृहीतः किलाभवत्। ऋग्वेदे वर्तते चाग्र्या श्रुतिर्यस्य महात्मनः॥ यत्र गृत्समदो राजन् ब्राह्मणैः स महीयते। स ब्रह्मचारी विप्रर्षिः श्रीमान् गृत्समदोऽभवत्॥
en: Once on a time the Daityas afflicted him much taking him for none else than Indra. With regard to that great Rishi, there is this foremost of Shrutis in the Richs viz., There where Gritsamada is, O Brahmana, he is held in high respect by all twice born persons! Gifted with great intelligence, Gritsamada became a twice born Rishi in the observance of Brahmacharya.

sn: पुत्रो गृत्समदस्यापि सुचेता अभवद् द्विजः। वर्चाः सुतेजसः पुत्रो विहव्यस्तस्य चात्मजः॥
en: Gritsamada had a regenerate son of the name of Sutejas. Sutejas had a son of the name of Varchas and the son of Varchas was known by the name of Vihavya.

sn: विहव्यस्य तु पुत्रस्तु वितत्यस्तस्य चात्मजः। वितत्यस्य सुतः सत्यः संतः सत्यस्य चात्मजः॥
en: Vihavya had a own begotten son who was named Vitatya, and Vitatya had a son of name Satya. Satya had a son of name Santa.

sn: श्रवास्तस्य सुतश्चर्षिः श्रवसश्चाभवत् तमः। तमसश्च प्रकाशोऽभूत् तनयो द्विजसत्तमः। प्रकाशस्य च वागिन्द्रो बभूव जयतां वरः॥
en: Santa had a son viz., the Rishi Shravas. Shravas begot a son named Tama. Tama begot a son named Prakasha who was a very great Brahmana.

sn: तस्यात्मजश्च प्रमितिर्वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः। घृताच्यां तस्य पुत्रस्तु रुरुर्नामोदपद्यत॥
en: Prakasha had a son named Vagindra who was the foremost of all silent reciters of sacred Mantras. Vagindra begot a son named Pramati who was a perfect master of all the Vedas and their auxiliaries. Pramati begot upon the Apsara Ghritachi a son who was named Ruru.

sn: प्रमद्वरायां तु रुरोः पुत्रः समुदपद्यत। शुनको नाम विप्रर्षिर्यस्य पुत्रोऽथ शौनकः॥
en: Ruru begot a son upon his wife Pramadvara. That son was the regenerate Rishi Shunaka. Shunaka begot a son who is named Shaunaka.

sn: एवं विप्रत्वमगमद् वीतहव्यो नराधिपः। भृगोः प्रसादाद् राजेन्द्र क्षत्रियः क्षत्रियर्षभ॥
en: It was thus, O foremost of monarchs that king Vitahavya, though a Kshatriya by the order of his birth, acquired the dignity of a Brahmana, O chief of Kshatriyas, through the grace of Bhrigu.

sn: तथैव कथितो वंशो मया गार्समदस्तव। विस्तरेण महाराज किमन्यदनुपृच्छसि॥
en: I have also told you the genealogy of the race that originated from his son Gritsamada. What else would you ask?

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच के पूज्या वै त्रिलोकेऽस्मिन् मानवा भरतर्षभ। विस्तरेण तदाचक्ष्व न हि तृप्यामि कथ्यतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said What men, O chief of Bharata's race are worthy of homage in the three worlds? Tell me this in detail, I am never satiated with hearing you describe these topics.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। नारदस्य च संवादं वासुदेवस्य चोभयोः॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Narada and Vasudeva.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: नारदं प्राञ्जलिं दृष्ट्वा पूजयानं द्विजर्षभान्। केशवः परिपप्रच्छ भगवन् कान् नमस्यसि॥ बहुमानपरस्तेषु भगवन् यान् नमस्यसि। शक्यं चेच्छ्रोतुमस्माभिर्बुह्येतद् धर्मवित्तम॥
en: Seeing Narada on one occasion adoring many foremost of Brahmanas with joined hands, Keshava addressed him, saying Whom do you worship? Whom amongst these Brahmanas, O holy one, do you worship with so great respect? If it is capable of being heard by me, I wish then to hear it. Do O foremost of righteous men, tell me this.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: नारद उवाच शृणु गोविन्द यानेतान् पूजयाम्यरिमर्दन। त्वत्तोऽन्यः कः पुमाल्लोके श्रोतुमेतदिहार्हति॥
en: Narada said Hear, O Govinda, as to who those are whom I am adoring, Ogrinder of enemies What other person is there in the world who is worthier than you to hear this?

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: वरुणं वायुमादित्यं पर्जन्यं जातवेदसम्। स्थाणुं स्कन्दं तथा लक्ष्मी विष्णुं ब्रह्माणमेव च॥
en: I adore them o powerful one, who constantly worship Varuna and Vayu and Aditya, and Parjanya and the deity of Fire and Sthanu and Skanda and Lakshmi and Vishnu and the Brahmanas, and the lord of speech, and the Moon, and the Waters, and the Earth and the goddess Sarasvati,

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: वाचस्पतिं चन्द्रमसमपः पृथ्वी सरस्वतीम्। सततं ये नमस्यन्ति तान् नमस्याम्यहं विभो॥ तपोधनान् वेदविदो नित्यं वेदपरायणान्। महार्हान् वृष्णिशार्दूल सदा सम्पूजयाम्यहम्।।८
en: O foremost of Vrishni's race, I always adore those Brahmanas who are are endued with penances, who are conversant with the Vedas who are always given to Vedic study, and who are possessed of great worth.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: अभुक्त्वा देवकार्याणि कुर्वते येऽविकत्थनाः। संतुष्टाश्च क्षमायुक्तास्तान् नमस्याम्यहं विभो॥
en: O powerful one, I bow down my head to those persons who are freed from boastfulness, who perform with an empty stomach, the rites in honour of the deities, who are always contended with what they have, and who are gifted with forgiveness.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: सम्यग् यजन्ति ये चेष्टीः क्षान्ता दान्ता जितेन्द्रियाः। सत्यं धर्मे क्षितिं गाश्च तान् नमस्यामि यादव।॥
en: I adore them, O Yadava, who are performers of sacrifices, who are forgiving in nature, and selfcontrolled, who are masters of their own senses, who worship truth and virtue, and who give away land and kine to good Brahmanas.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: ये वै तपसि वर्तन्ते वने मूलफलाशनाः। असंचयाः क्रियावन्तस्तान् नमस्यामि यादव॥
en: I bow to them, O Yadava, who are devoted to the observance of penances, who live in forests, who live upon fruits and roots who never store anything for the morrow, and who perform all the acts and rites laid down in the scriptures.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: ये भृत्यभरणे शक्ताः सततं चातिथिव्रताः। भुञ्जते देवशेषाणि तान् नमस्यामि यादव।॥
en: I bow to them, O Yadava, who feed and cherish their servants who are always hospitable to guests and who eat only the residue of what is offered to the deities.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: ये वेदं प्राप्य दुर्धर्षा वाग्मिनो ब्रह्मचारिणः। याजनाध्यापने युक्ता नित्यं तान् पूजयाम्यहम्॥
en: I worship them who have become irresistible by studying the Vedas, who are eloquent in discoursing on the scriptures, who are observant of the vow of Brahmacharya, and who are always devoted to the duties of officiating at the sacrifices of others and of teaching disciples.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: प्रसन्नहृदयाश्चैव सर्वसत्त्वेषु नित्याः। आपृष्ठतापात् स्वाध्याये युक्तास्तान् पूजयाम्यहम्।।१४
en: I adore them that are endued with mercy towards all creatures and who study the Vedas till their back are heated by the Sun.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: गुरुप्रसादे स्वाध्याये यतन्तो ये स्थिरव्रताः। शुश्रूषवोऽनसूयन्तस्तान् नमस्यामि यादव॥
en: I bow to them, O Yadava, who try to acquire the grace of their preceptors, who labour in the acquisition of their Vedas, who are firm in the observance of vows, who wait with dutiful obedience, upon their preceptors and seniors, and who are free from malice and envy.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: सुव्रता मुनयो ये च ब्राह्मणाः सत्यसंगराः। वोढारो हव्यकव्यानां तान् नमस्यामि यादव॥
en: I bow to them, O Yadava, who are observant of excellent vows, who practise silence, who have knowledge of Brahma, who are firm in truth, who are givers of libations of clarified butter and oblations of meat.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: भैक्ष्यवर्यासु निरताः कृशा गुरुकुलाश्रयाः। निर्धना ये तु तान् नमस्यामि यादव।॥
en: I bow to them, O, Yadava, who live upon elemosynary alms, who are emaciated for want of adequate food and drink, who have lived in the houses of their preceptors, who are averse to and destitute of all enjoyments and who are poor in Earthly possessions.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: निर्ममा निष्प्रतिद्वन्द्वा निहीका निष्प्रयोजनाः। ये वेदं प्राप्य दुर्धर्षा वाग्मिनो ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
en: I bow to them, O Yadava, who have no affection for things of this Earth, who do not quarrel with others, who do not clothe themselves, who have no wants, who have become irresistible through the acquisition of the Vedas, eloquent in the exposition of virtue, and that are utterers of Brahma.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: अहिंसानिरता ये च ये च सत्यव्रता नराः। दान्ताः शमपराश्चैव तान् नमस्यामि केशव॥ निःसुखा
en: I bow to them who are given to the practice of the duty of mercy towards all creatures who are firm in the observance of truth, who are self controlled, and who are peaceful in their conduct.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: देवतातिथिपूजायां युक्ता ये गृहमेधिनः। कपोतवृत्तयो नित्यं तान् नमस्यामि यादव॥
en: I bow to them, O Yadava who are devoted to the worship of gods and guests, who are observant of the domestic mode of life and that follow the practice of pigeons about collecting their food.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: येषां त्रिवर्गः कृत्येषु वर्तते नोपहीयते। शिष्टाचारप्रवृत्ताश्च तान् नमस्याम्यहं सदा॥
en: I always bow to those persons, who while doing all their works have an eye on the threefold objects of life, and who are observant of truth and righteous behaviour.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: ब्राह्मणाः श्रुतसम्पन्ना ये त्रिवर्गमनुष्ठिताः। अलोलुपाः पुण्यशीलास्तान् नमस्यामि केशव॥
en: I bow to them, O Keshava, who are conversant with Brahma, who are gifted with knowledge of the Vedas, who are attentive to the threefold objects of life, who are free from cupidity, and who are righteous in their behaviour.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: अब्भक्षा वायुभक्षाश्च सुधाभक्षश्च ये सदा। व्रतैश्च विविधैर्युक्तास्तान् नमस्यामि माधव॥
en: I bow to them, O Madhava, who live upon water only, or upon air alone, or upon the residue of the food that is offered to deities and guests, and who practise all sorts of excellent VOWS.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: अयोनीनग्नियोनींश्च ब्रह्मयोनींस्तथैव च। सर्वभूतात्मयोनींश्च तान् नमस्याम्यहं सदा॥
en: I always adore them who have no wives, who have wives and the domestic fire, who are the refuge of the Vedas, and who are the refuge of all creatures in the universe.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: नित्यमेतान् नमस्यामि कृष्ण लोककरानृषीन्। लोकज्येष्ठान् कुलज्येष्ठांस्तमोघ्नॉल्लोकभास्करान्॥
en: I always bow to those Rishis. O Krishna, who are the creators of the universe, who are the elders of the universe, who are the eldest members of the race or the family, who are dispellers of the darkness of ignorance, and who are the best of all persons in the universe.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: तस्मात् त्वमपि वार्ष्णेय द्विजान् पूजय नित्यदा। पूजिताः पूजनार्हा हि सुखं दास्यन्ति तेऽनघ।॥
en: For these reasons, do you also O scion of Vrishni's race, adore every day those twiceborn persons of whom I speak. Worthy as they are of reverent worship, they will when adored confer happiness on you, O sinless one,

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: अस्मिल्लोके सदा ह्येते परत्र च सुखप्रदाः। चरन्ते मान्यमाना वै प्रदास्यन्ति सुखं तव।॥
en: Those persons of whom I speak are always givers of happiness in this world as well as in the next. Respected by all, they move about in this world, and, if adored by you are sure to grant you happiness.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: ये सर्वातिथयो नित्यं गोषु च ब्राह्मणेषु च। नित्यं सत्ये चाभिरता दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: They who are hospitable to all persons who come to them as guests, and who are always devoted to Brahmanas and kine as also to truth succeed in crossing all calamities and impediments.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: नित्यं शमपरा ये च तथा ये चानसूयकाः। नित्यस्वाध्यायिनो ये च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: They who are always devoted to peacefulness of conduct as also they who are shorn of malice and envy, and they who are always attentive to the study of the Vedas, succeed in crossing all calamities and impediments.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: सर्वान् देवान् नमस्यन्ति ये चैकं वेदमाश्रिताः। श्रद्दधानाश्च दान्ताश्च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: They who bow to all the deities, they who follow one Veda as their refuge, they who are possessed of faith and are self controlled, succeed in crossing all calamities and impediments.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: तथैव विप्रप्रवरान् नमस्कृत्य यतव्रताः। भवन्ति ये दानरता दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: They who adore the foremost of Brahmanas with reverence and are firm in the observance of excellent vows and practise the virtue of charity succeed in crossing all calamities and impediments.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: तपस्विनश्च ये नित्यं कौमारब्रह्मचारिणः। तपसा भावितात्मानो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: They who are engaged in the practice of penances, they who are always observant of the vow of celibacy, and they whose souls have been purified by penances, succeed in crossing all calamities and impediments.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: देवतातिथिभृत्यानां पितॄणां चार्चने रताः। शिष्टान्नभोजिनो ये च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: The who are devoted to the worship of the gods and guests and dependants as also of the departed manes and they who eat the residue of the food that is offered to deities departed manes guests and dependants succeed in crossing all calamities and impediments.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: अग्निमाधाय विधिवत् प्रणता धारयन्ति ये। प्राप्ताः सोमाहुतिं चैव दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥
en: They who, having lighted the domestic fire, duly keep it burning and adore it with reverence, and they who have duly poured libations in Somasacrifices, succeed in crossing all calamities and impediments.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: मातापित्रोणुरुषु च सम्यग् वर्तन्ति ये सदा। यथा त्वं वृष्णिशार्दूलेत्युक्त्वैवं विरराम सः॥
en: They who behave properly towards their mothers and fathers and preceptors and other elders even as you, O foremost of the Vrishnis, do behave, (succeed in crossing all calamities and impediments)! Having said these words the celestial Rishi ceased speaking.

description: The discourse between Narada and Vasudeva
sn: भीष्म उवाच तस्मात् त्वमपि कौन्तेय पितृदेवद्विजातिथीन्। सम्यक् पूजयसे नित्यं गतिमिष्टामवाप्स्यसि॥
en: Bhishma continued For these reasons, do you also, O son of Kunti, always adore with reverence the deities the departed manes the Brahmanas and guests arrived at your palace, and as the outcome of such conduct you are to acquire a desirable end! sure the departed manes the Brahmanas and guests arrived at your palace, and as the outcome of such conduct you are to acquire a desirable end! sure

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामह महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद। त्वत्तोऽहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि धर्मे भरतसत्तम॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O you of great wisdom, O you who are conversant with all branches of knowledge, I wish to hear you discourse on topics connected with duty and Virtue.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: शरणागतं ये रक्षन्ति भूतग्रामं चतुर्विधम्। किं तस्य भरतश्रेष्ठ फलं भवति तत्त्वतः॥
en: Tell me truly, O chief of Bharata's race, what the merits are of those persons who grant protection to living creatures of the four castes when these pray for protection.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: इदं शृणु महाप्राज्ञ धर्मपुत्र महायशः। इतिहासं पुरावृत्तं शरणार्थे महाफलम्॥
en: Bhisham said: O Dharma's son of great wisdom and widespread fame, listen to this old, history regarding the great merit of granting protection to others when protection is humbly sought.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: प्रपात्यमान: श्येनेन कपोतः प्रियदर्शनः। वृषदर्भ महाभागं नरेन्द्रं शरणं गतः॥
en: Once on a time, a beautiful pigeon, pursued by a hawk dropped down from the skies and sought the protection of the highly blessed king Vrishadarbha.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: स तं दृष्ट्वा विशुद्धात्मा त्रासादङ्कमुपागतम्। आश्वास्याश्वसिहीत्याह न तेऽस्ति भयमण्डज॥
en: The pure-souled, king beholding the pigeon take refuge in his lap from fear, comforted him, saying, Be comforted, O bird! You have no fear!

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: भयं ते सुमहत् कस्मात् कुत्र किं वा कृतं त्वया। येन त्वमिह सम्प्राप्तो विसंज्ञो भ्रान्तचेतनः॥
en: Whence have you taken such great fright? What and where have you done it in consequence of which you have lost your senses in fear and are more dead than alive?

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: नवनीलोत्पलापीडचारुवर्ण सुदर्शन। दाडिमाशोकपुष्पाक्ष मा त्रसस्वाभयं तव॥
en: Your colour, O beautiful bird, resembles that of a fresh blown blue lotus. Your eyes are of the hue of the pomegranate or the Ashoka flower! Do not fear, I command you, be comforted!

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: मत्सकाशमनुप्राप्तं न त्वां कश्चित् समुत्सहेत्। मनसा ग्रहणं कर्तुं रक्षाध्यक्षपुरस्कृतम्॥
en: When you have sought my protection, know that no one will have the courage to even think of catching you, who have such a protector to take care of your body.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: काशिराज्यं तदद्यैव त्वदर्थं जीवितं तथा। त्यजेयं भव विश्रब्धः कपोत न भयं तव॥
en: I shall, for your sake give up today the very kingdom of the Kashis and, if necessary my life too! Be comforted, therefore, do no fear, O pigeon.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: श्येन उवाच ममैतद् विहितं भक्ष्यं च राजंस्त्रातुमर्हसि। अतिक्रान्तं च प्राप्तं च प्रयत्नाच्चोपपादितम्॥
en: The hawk said This bird has been ordained to be my food. You should not, O king, protect him from me! I have pursued this bird and have got him. Indeed, with great exertion have I got at him at last.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: मासं च रुधिरं चास्य मज्जा मेदश्च मे हितम्। परितोषकरो ह्येष मम मास्याग्रतो भव॥
en: His flesh and blood and marrow and fat will be of great good to me. This bird will be the means of pleasing me greatly. Do not, O king place yourself between him and me in this way.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: तृष्णा मे बाधतेऽत्युग्रा क्षुधा निर्दहतीव माम्। मुञ्चैनं न हि शक्ष्यामि राजन् मन्दयितुं क्षुधाम्॥
en: I have been possessed by a terrible thirst and hunger is knawing my bowels, Release the bird and cast him off. I am unable to bear the pains of hunger any longer.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: मया ह्यनुसृतो ह्येष मत्पक्षनखविक्षतः। किंचिदुच्छ्वासनिःश्वासं न राजन् गोप्तुमर्हसि॥
en: I pursued him as my prey. See, his body is bruised and torn by me with my wings and talons. Look his breath has become very weak. You should not, O king, protect him from me!

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: यदि स्वविषये राजन् प्रभुस्त्वं रक्षणे नृणाम्। खेचरस्य तृषार्तस्य न त्वं प्रभुरथोत्तम॥
en: In the exercise of that power which properly belongs to you, you are indeed, competent to interfere in protecting human beings when sought to be destroyed by human beings. But you have no power over a skyranging bird stricken with thirst.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: यदि वैरिषु भृत्येषु स्वजनव्यवहारयोः। विषयेष्विन्द्रयाणां च आकाशे मा पराक्रम॥
en: Your power may extend over your enemies, your servants, your relatives, the disputes that take place between your subjects. Indeed it may extend over every part of your dominions and over also your own senses. Your power, however, does, not extend over the sky.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: प्रभुत्वं हि पराक्रम्य सम्यक् पक्षहरेषु ते। यदि त्वमिह धर्मार्थी मामपि द्रष्टुमर्हसि॥
en: Displaying your prowess over such enemies as act against your wishes, you may establish your rule over them. Your rule, however, does not extend over the skyranging birds. Indeed if you have been desirous of acquiring merit (by protecting this pigeon), It is your duty to look at me also!

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: भीष्म उवाच श्रुत्वा श्येनस्य तद् वाक्यं राजर्षिविस्मयं गतः। सम्भाव्य चैनं तद्वाक्यं तदर्थी प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words of the hawk, the royal sage became stricken with wonder. Without disregarding these words of his, the king, desirous of attending to his comforts, replied to him, saying the following words.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: राजोवाच गोवृषो वा वराहो वा मृगो वा महिषोऽपि वा। त्वदर्थमद्य क्रियतां क्षुधाप्रशमनाय ते॥
en: The king said Let a bovine bull or boar or deer or buffalo be dressed today for your sake! Do you satisfy your hunger on such food today.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: शरणागतं न त्यजेयमिति मे व्रतमाहितम्। न मुञ्चति ममाङ्गानि द्विजोऽयं पश्य वै द्विज॥
en: Never to leave one who has sought my protection is my firm vow. See, O bird, this bird does not leave my lap!

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: श्येन उवाच न वराहं न चोक्षाणं न चान्यान् विविधान् द्विजान्। भक्षयामि महाराज किमन्यायेन तेन मे॥ यस्तु मे विहितो भक्ष्यः स्वयं देवैः सनातनः। श्येनाः कपोतान् खादन्ति स्थितिरेषा सनातनी॥
en: The hawk said I do not, O king, eat the flesh of the boar or the ox or of any of the various kinds of fowl. What need have I of food of this or that kind? My business is with that food which has been eternally ordained for beings of my order? Hawks feed on pigeons. This is the eternal ordinance.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: उशीनर कपोते तु यदि स्नेहस्तवानघ। ततस्त्वं मे प्रयच्छाद्य स्वमांसं तुलया धृतम्॥
en: O sinless Ushinara, if you feel such affection for this pigeon do you then give me flesh from your own body, of weight equal to that of this pigeon.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: राजोवाच महाननुग्रहो मेऽघ यस्त्वमेवमिहात्थ माम्। बाढमेव करिष्यामीत्युक्त्वासौ राजसत्तमः॥ उत्कृत्योत्कृत्य मांसानि तुलया समतोलयत्। अन्तःपुरे ततस्तस्य स्त्रियो रत्नविभूषिताः॥ हाहाभूता विनिष्क्रान्ताः श्रुत्वा परमदुःखिताः। तासां रुदितशब्देन मन्त्रिभृत्यजनस्य च॥
en: The king said Great is the favour you show me today by speaking to me thus. Yes, I shall do what you bid. Having said this that best of kings began to cut off his own flesh and weigh it in a balance against the pigeon. Meanwhile in the inner apartments of the palace, the queen adorned with jewels and gems, hearing what was taking place, uttered exclamations of woe and came out, stricken with grief.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: बभूव सुमहान् नादो मेघगम्भीरनि:स्वनः। निरुद्धं गगनं सर्वं शुभं मेघैः समन्ततः॥
en: On account of those cries of the ladies as also of the ministers and servants a noise deep as the muttering of the clouds arose in the palace. The sky that had been very clear became covered with thick clouds on all sides.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: मही प्रचलिता चासीत् तस्य सत्येन कर्मणा। स राजा पार्श्वतश्चैव बाहुभ्यामूरुतश्च यत्॥ तानि मांसानि संच्छिद्य तुलां पूरयतेऽशनैः। तथापि च समस्तेन कपोतेन बभूव ह॥
en: The Earth began to tremble, as the consequence of that act of truth which the monarch did. The king began to cut off the flesh from his sides from his arms, and from his thighs, and quickly fill one of the scales for weighing it against the pigeon. For all that, the pigeon continued to weigh heavier.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: अस्थिभूतो यदा राजा निर्मासो रुधिरस्रवः। तुलां ततः समारूढः स्वं मांसक्षयमुत्सृजन्॥
en: When at last the king became a skeleton of bones, without any flesh, and covered with blood he wished to give up his whole body and, therefore, ascended the scale in which he had placed the flesh that he had previously cut off.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: ततः सेन्द्रास्त्रयो लोकास्तं नरेन्द्रमुपस्थिताः। भेर्यश्चाकाशगैस्तत्र वादिता देवदुन्दुभिः॥
en: At that time, the three worlds, headed by Indra, came to that spot for seeing him. Celestial kettledrums and various other drums were struck and played upon by invisible beings belonging to the sky.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: अमृतेनावसिक्तश्च वृषदर्भो नरेश्वरः। दिव्यैश्च सुसुखैर्माल्यैरभिवृष्टः पुनः पुनः॥
en: King Vrishadarbha was bathed in a shower of nectar that was poured upon him. Garlands of celestials flowers, of sweet fragrance and touch, were also showered upon him copiously again and again.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: देवगन्धर्वसंघातैरप्सरोभिश्च सर्वतः। नृत्तश्चैवोपगीतश्च पितामह इव प्रभुः॥
en: The deities and Gandharvas and Apsaras in large bands began to sing and dance around him even as they sing and dance around the Grandfather Brahman.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: हेमप्रसादसम्बाधं मणिकाञ्चनतोरणम्। स वैदूर्यमणिस्तम्भं विमानं समधिष्ठितः॥
en: The king then ascended a celestial car that excelled a mansion made entirely of gold, that had arches made of gold and gems and that was adorned with columns made of lapis lazuli.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: स राजर्षिर्गत: स्वर्ग कर्मणा तेन शाश्वतम्। शरणागतेषु चैवं त्वं कुरु सर्वं युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Through the merit of his act the royal sage Shivi proceeded to eternal Heaven. Do you also, O Yudhishthira, act thus towards those who seek your protection.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: भक्तानामनुरक्तानामाश्रितानां च रक्षिता। दयावान् सर्वभूतेषु परत्र सुखमेधते॥
en: He who protects those who are devoted to him those who are attached to him from love and affection and those who depend upon him, and who has mercy for all creatures succeeds in acquiring great happiness hereafter.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: साधुवृत्तो हि यो राजा सवृत्तमनुतिष्ठति। किं न प्राप्तं भवेत् तेन सव्याजेनेह कर्मणा॥
en: That king who is of righteous conduct and who is observant of honesty and integrity, succeeds by his acts of sincerity in acquiring every valuable reward.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: स राजर्षेर्विशुद्धात्मा धीरः सत्यपराक्रमः। काशीनामीश्वरः ख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु कर्मणा॥
en: The royal sage Shivi, of pure soul and gifted with great wisdom and unbaffled prowess, that king of the Kashis, became celebrated over the three worlds for his virtuous deeds.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: योऽप्यन्यः कारयेदेवं शरणागतरक्षणम्। सोऽपि गच्छेत तामेव गतिं भरतसत्तमा॥
en: Anybody who would protect in the same way a seeker for protection, would certainly acquire the same happy end, best of the Bharatas.

description: Merits of persons granting protection to living creatures
sn: इदं वृत्तं हि राजर्षेवृषदर्भस्य कीर्तयन्। पूतात्मा वै भवेल्लोके शृणुयाद् यश्च नित्यशः॥
en: He who recites this history of the royal sage Vrishadarbha is sure to become purged of every sin, and the person who hears this history recited by another is sure to acquire the same result.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं राज्ञः सर्वकृत्यानां गरीयः स्यात् पितामह। कुर्वन् किं कर्म नृपतिरुभौ लोकौ समश्नुते॥
en: Yudhishthira Said Which act, O grandfather is the foremost of all those that have been laid down for a king? What is that act by doing which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतद् राज्ञः कृत्यतममभिषिक्तस्य भारत। ब्राह्मणानामनुष्ठानमत्यन्तं सुखमिच्छता॥
en: Bhishma said Even this, viz., the worship of the Brahmanas, is the foremost of all those deeds, O Bharata, which have been laid down for a king duly installed on the throne if, indeed, he is desirous of acquiring great happiness.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: कर्तव्यं पार्थिवेन्द्रेण तथैव भरतर्षभ। श्रोत्रियान् ब्राह्मणान् वृद्धान् नित्यमेवाभिपूजयेत्॥
en: Even this is what the foremost of all kings should do. Know this well, O chief of Bharata's race. The king should always adore with reverence all righteous Brahmanas possessed of Vedic learning.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: पौरजानपदांश्चापि ब्राह्मणांश्च बहुश्रुतान्। सान्त्वेन भोगदानेन नमस्कारैस्तथार्चयेत्॥
en: The king should, with bows sweet speeches and gifts of all articles of enjoyment, adore all Brahmanas endued with great learning who may live in his city or provinces.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: एतत् कृत्यतमं राज्ञो नित्यमेवोपलक्षयेत्। यथाऽऽत्मानं यथा पुत्रांस्तथैतान् प्रतिपालयेत्॥
en: This is the foremost of all acts laid down for the king. Indeed, the king should always keep his eyes fixed on this. He should protect and cherish these, even as he protects his own self or his own children.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: ये चाप्येषां पूज्यतमास्तान् दृढं प्रतिपूजयेत्। तेषु शान्तेषु तद् राष्ट्र सर्वमेव विराजते॥
en: The king should adore with greater reverence those amongst the Brahmanas who may be worthy of it. When such men are freed from all anxiety, the whole kingdom shines in beauty.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: ते पूज्यास्ते नमस्कार्या भान्यास्ते पितरो यथा। तेष्वेव यात्रा लोकानां भूतानामिव वासवे॥
en: Such individuals are worthy of adoration. The king should bow his head to such individuals. Indeed, they should be honoured, even as one honours his father and grandfather. The course of conduct followed by men, depends upon them as the existence of all creatures depends upon Vasava.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: अभिचारैरुपायैश्च दहेयुरपि चेतसा। निःशेषं कुपिताः कुर्युरुयाः सत्यपराक्रमाः॥
en: Having prowess incapable of being baffled and gifted with great energy, such men if enraged are capable of reducing the entire kingdom to ashes by only their will or by acts of incantation, or by other means.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: नान्तमेषां प्रपश्यामि न दिशश्चाप्यपावृताः। कुपिताः समुदीक्षन्ते दावेष्वग्निशिखा इव ॥
en: I do not see anything that can destroy them. Their power seems to be uncontrolled, being capable of reaching to the last end of the universe. When angry, their looks fall upon men and things like a burning flame of fire upon a forest. are

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: बिभ्यत्येषां साहसिका गुणास्तेषामतीव हि। कूपा इव तृणच्छन्ना विशुद्धा द्यौरिवापरे॥
en: The most courageous men are struck with fear at their name. Their virtues and powers are extraordinary and immeasurable. Some amongst them are like wells and pits with mouths covered by grass and creepers, while others resemble the sky shorn of clouds and darkness.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: प्रसह्यकारिणः केचित् कार्पासमृदवो परे। सन्ति चैषामतिशठास्तथैवान्ये तपस्विनः॥
en: Some amongst them of dreadful dispositions. Some are as mild and soft in disposition as cotton. Some amongst them are very cunning. Some amongst them are given to the practice of penances.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: कृषिगोरक्ष्यमप्येके भैक्ष्यमन्येऽप्यनुष्ठिताः। चौराश्चान्येऽनृताश्चान्ये तथान्ये नटनर्तकाः॥
en: Some amongst them are employed in agricultural pursuits. Some amongst them are engaged in the keep of kine. Some amongst them live upon eleemosynary alms. Some amongst them are even thieves. Some amongst them are found of creating quarrels and disputes. Some again, amongst them are actors and dancers.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: सर्वकर्मसहाश्चान्ये पार्थिवेष्वितरेषु च। विविधाकारयुक्ताश्च ब्राह्मणा भरतर्षभ॥
en: Some amongst them are competent to perform all feats ordinary and extraordinary. The Brahmanas, O chief of Bharata's race, are of various aspects and conduct.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: नानाकर्मसु रक्तानां बहुकर्मोपजीविनाम्। धर्मज्ञानां सतां तेषां नित्यमेवानुकीर्तयेत्॥
en: One should always sing the praises of the Brahmanas who are conversant with all duties, who are righteous of conduct, who are given to various kinds of acts, and who are seen to derive their sustenance from various callings.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: पितॄणां देवतानां च मनुष्योरगरक्षसाम्। पुराप्येते महाभागा ब्राह्मणा वै जनाधिप॥
en: The Brahmanas, O king, who are highly blessed are older in respect of their origin than the departed manes, the deities human beings, the Snakes, and the Rakshasas.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: नैते देवैर्न पितृभिर्न गन्धर्वैर्न राक्षसैः। नासुरैर्न पिशाचैश्च शक्या जेतुं द्विजातयः॥
en: These twice born persons are incapable of being defeated by the deities or the departed manes, or the Gandharvas or the Rakshasas, or the Asuras or the Pishachas.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: अदैवं दैवतं कुर्युर्दैवतं चाप्यदैवतम्। यमिच्छेयुः स राजा स्याद् यो नेष्टः स पराभवेत्।।१७
en: The Brahmanas are competent to make him a god, that is not a god. They can, again, divest one who is a deity of his status as such. He becomes a king, whom they wish to make a king. He on the other hand, is crushed whom they do not love or like.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: परिवादं च ये कुयुर्ब्राह्मणानामचेतसः। सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते राजन् विनश्येयुर्न संशयः॥
en: I tell you truly, O king, that those foolish persons, forsooth, meet with destruction who caluminate the Brahmanas and utter their dispraise.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: निन्दाप्रशंसाकुशलाः कीर्त्यकीर्तिपरायणाः। परिकुप्यति ते राजन् सततं द्विषतां द्विजाः॥
en: Expert in praise and dispraise, and themselves the origin or cause of other people's fame and ignominy, the Brahmanas, O king, always become angry with those who seek to injure others.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: ब्राह्मणा यं प्रशंसन्ति पुरुषः स प्रवर्धते। ब्राह्मणैर्यः पराकृष्टः पराभूयात् क्षणाद्धि सः॥
en: That man whom the Brahmanas praise succeeds in becoming prosperous. That man who is censured and renounced by the Brahmanas soon meets with discomfiture.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: शका यवनकाम्बोजास्तास्ताः क्षत्रियजातयः। वृषलत्वं परिगता ब्राह्मणानामदर्शनात्॥
en: It is on account of the absence of Brahmanas from among them that the Shakas, the Yavanas, the Kamvojas and other Kshatriya tribes have become fallen and degraded into Shudras.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: द्राविडाश्च कलिङ्गाश्च पुलिन्दाश्चाप्युशीनराः। कोलिसर्पा माहिषकास्तास्ताः क्षत्रियजातयः॥ वृषलत्वं परिगता ब्राह्मणानामदर्शनात्। श्रेयान् पराजयस्तेभ्यो न जयो जयतां वर॥
en: The Dravidas, the Kalingas, the Pulindas the Ushinaras, the Kolisarpas, the Mahishakas, and other Kshatriyas, have, on account of the absence of Brahmanas from among their midst, become degraded into Shudras. Defeat from them is preferable to victory, O foremost of victorious persons.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: यस्तु सर्वमिदं हन्याद् ब्राह्मणं च न तत्समम्। ब्रह्मवध्या महान् दोष इत्याहुः परमर्षयः॥
en: One killing all other living creatures in this world does not commit a sin so heinous as that of killing a single Brahmana. The great Rishis have said that Brahmanicide is a heinous sin.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: परिवादो द्विजातीनां न श्रोतव्यः कथंचन। आसीताधोमुखस्तूष्णीं समुत्थाय व्रजेच्च वा॥
en: One should never utter the dispraise or calumny of the Brahmanas. Where the dispraise of Brahmanas is uttered, one should sit with face hanging down or leave that place.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: न स जातोऽजनिष्यद् वा पृथिव्यामिह कश्चन। यो ब्राह्मणविरोधेन सुखं जीवितुमुत्सहेत्॥
en: That man has not as yet been born in this world or will not take birth here who has been or will be able to pass his life happily after quarrelling with the Brahmanas.

description: The deed by which a king succeeds in enjoying both this world and the next
sn: दुर्ग्राह्यो मुष्टिना वायुर्दुःस्पर्शः पाणिना शशी। दुर्धरा पृथिवी राजन् दुर्जया ब्राह्मणा भुवि॥
en: One cannot seize the wind with his hands. One cannot touch the moon with his hand. One cannot support the earth on his arms. Similarly, O king, one is not able to defeat the Brahmanas in this world,

sn: भीष्म उवाच ब्राह्मणानेव सततं भृशं सम्परिपूजयेत्। एते हि सोमराजान ईश्वराः सुखदुःखयोः॥
en: Bhishma said One should always offer the most respectful adoration to the Brahmanas. They have Soma for their king, and they it is who confer happiness and misery upon others.

sn: एते भौगैरलङ्कारैरन्यैश्चैव किमिच्छकैः। सदा पूज्या नमस्कारै रक्ष्याश्च पितृवन्नृपैः॥ ततो राष्ट्रस्य शान्तिर्हि भूतानामिव वासवात्।
en: They, O king, should always be cherished and protected as one cherishes and protect his own father and grandfather, and should be adored with bows and gifts of food and ornaments and other articles of enjoyment as also with such things as they may wish for. The peace and happiness of the kingdom originate from such respect shown to the Brahmanas even as the peace and happiness of all living creatures come from Vasava the king of the gods.

sn: जायतां ब्रह्मवर्चस्वी राष्ट्रे वै ब्राह्मणः शुचिः॥ महारथश्च राजन्य एष्टव्यः शत्रुतापनः।
en: Let Brahmanas of pure conduct and Brahmaeffulgence be born in a kingdom. Kshatriya also who are splendid carwarriors and that are capable of defeating all enemies, should be desired.

sn: ब्राह्मणं जातिसम्पन्नं धर्मज्ञं संशितव्रतम्॥ वासयेत गृहे राजन् न तस्मात् परमस्ति वै।
en: This was said to me by Narada. There is nothing higher, O king, than this viz., the act of making a Brahmana of good birth, having a knowledge of morality and righteousness, and steadfast in the observance of excellent vows, live in his mansion. Such an act yields every sort of blessing.

sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्यो हविर्दत्तं प्रतिगृह्णन्ति देवताः॥ पितरः सर्वभूतानां नैतेभ्यो विद्यते परम्।
en: The sacrificial offerings given Brahmanas reach the very gods who accept them. Brahmanas are the fathers of all creatures. There is nothing higher than a Brahmana.

sn: आदित्यश्चन्द्रमा वायुरापो भूरम्बरं दिशः॥ सर्वे ब्राह्मणमाविश्य सदानमुपभुञ्जते। न तस्याश्नन्ति पितरो यस्य विप्रा न भुञ्जते॥
en: The Sun, the Moon, the Wind, the Water, the Earth, the Sky and the points of the compass, all enter the body of the Brahmana and take what the Brahmana eats. In that house where Brahmanas do not eat, the departed manes refuse to eat.

sn: देवाश्चाप्यस्य नाश्नन्ति पापस्य ब्राह्मणद्विषः। ब्राह्मणेषु तु तुष्टेषु प्रीयन्ते पितरः सदा॥
en: The gods also never eat in the house of the wretch who hates the Brahmanas. When the Brahmanas are pleased, the departed manes are also pleased.

sn: तथैव देवता राजन् नात्र कार्या विचारणा। तथैव तेऽपि प्रीयन्ते येषां भवति तद्धविः॥
en: The deities also become pleased when the Brahmanas are pleased. There is no doubt in this. They who give away the sacrificial Havi to the Brahmanas become themselves pleased.

sn: न च प्रेत्य विनश्यन्ति गच्छन्ति च परां गतिम्। येन येनैव हविषा ब्राह्मणांस्तर्पयेन्नरः॥ तेन तेनैव प्रीयन्ते पितरो देवतास्तथा। ब्राह्मणादेव तद् भूतं प्रभवन्ति यतः प्रजाः॥
en: Such men never meet with destruction. Indeed, they succeed in acquiring great ends. Those particular offerings in sacrifices with which one pleases the Brahmanas, go to please both the departed manes and the deities. The Brahmana is the cause of that sacrifice whence all created things have originated.

sn: यतश्चायं प्रभवति प्रेत्य यत्र च गच्छति। वेदेष मार्ग स्वर्गस्य तथैव नरकस्य च॥
en: The Brahmana is acquainted with that from which this universe has originated and to which, when apparently, destroyed it. returns. Indeed, the Brahmana knows the path that leads to the celestial region and the other path which leads to the opposite place.

sn: आगतानागते चोभे ब्राह्मणो द्विपदां वरः। ब्राह्मणो भरतश्रेष्ठ स्वधर्मं चैव वेद यः॥
en: The Brahmana is conversant with that which has taken place and that which will take place. The Brahmana is the foremost of all twolegged beings. The Brahmana, O chief of the Bharatas, is fully conversant with those duties which have been laid down for his order.

sn: ये चैनमनुवर्तन्ते ते न यान्ति पराभवम्। न ते प्रेत्य विनश्यन्ति गच्छन्ति न पराभवम्॥
en: Those persons who follow the Brahmanas are never defeated. They never meet with destruction even after death. Indeed, victory is always theirs.

sn: यद् ब्राह्मणमुखात् प्राप्तं प्रतिगृह्णन्ति वै वचः। भूतात्मानो महात्मानस्ते न यान्ति पराभवम्॥
en: Those great persons indeed, those persons who have subdued their souls, who accept the words that fall from the lips of the Brahmanas, are never defeated. Victory always becomes theirs.

sn: क्षत्रियाणां प्रतपतां तेजसा च बलेन च। ब्राह्मणेष्वेव शाम्यन्ति तेजांसि च बलानि च।॥
en: The energy of those Kshatriyas who scorch everything with their energy and might, when they encounter the Brahmanas, become neutralised.

sn: भृगवस्तालजंघाश्च नीपानाङ्गिरसोऽजयन्। भरद्वाजो वैहतव्यानैलांश्च भरतर्षभ॥
en: The Bhrigus conquered the Talajanghas. The sons of Angiras conquered the Nipas. Bharadvaja conquered the Vitahavyas as also the Alias, O chief of Bharata's race. and power

sn: चित्रा युधांश्चाप्यजयन्नेते कृष्णाजिनध्वजाः। प्रक्षिप्याथ च कुम्भान् वै पारगामिनमारभेत्॥
en: Although all these Kshatriyas were capable of using various arms, yet the Brahmanas named, owning only black deer-skins for their emblems, succeeded in conquering them effectually. Bestowing the Earth upon the Brahmanas and illuminating both the worlds by the brilliance of such an act, one should accomplish acts through which one may succeed in acquiring the end of all things.

sn: यत् किंचित् कथ्यते लोकेश्रूयते पठ्यतेऽपि वा। सर्वं तद् ब्राह्मणेष्वेव गूढोऽग्निरिव दारुषु॥
en: Like. fire concealed within wood, everything that is said or heard or read in this world, lies in the Brahmana.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। संवादं वासुदेवस्य पृथिव्याश्च भरतर्षभ॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old history of the conversation between Vasudeva and the Earth, O chief of Bharata's race.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच मातरं सर्वभूतानां पृच्छे त्वां संशयं शुभे। केनस्वित् कर्मणा पापं व्यपोहति नरो गृही॥
en: Vasudeva said O mother, of all creatures, O auspicious goddess, I wish to ask you for a solution of this doubt of mine! By what act does a man living like a householder succeed in cleansing all his sins.?

sn: पृथ्वी उवाच ब्राह्मणानेव सेवेत पवित्रं ह्येतदुत्तमम्। ब्राह्मणान् सेवमानस्य रजः सर्वं प्रणश्यति। अतो भूतिरतः कीर्तिरतो बुद्धिः प्रजायते॥
en: The Earth said One should serve the Brahmanas. This conduct is purifying and excellent. All the impurities are destroyed of that man who serves the Brahmanas with respect.

sn: महारथश्च राजन्य एष्टव्यः शत्रुतापनः। इति मां नारदः प्राह सततं सर्वभूतये॥
en: From this (conduct) arises prosperity. From this arises fame. From this originates intelligence or knowledge of the soul. A Kshatriya, by this conduct, becomes a powerful carwarrior and a destroyer of foes and succeeds in winning great fame.

sn: ब्राह्मणं जातिसम्पन्नं धर्मज्ञं संशितं शुचिम्। अपरेषां परेषां च परेभ्यश्चैव येऽपरे॥
en: Even this is what Narada said to me, viz., that one should always respect a Brahmana that is well born, of rigid vows, and conversant with the scriptures, if one wishes every kind of prosperity.

sn: ब्राह्मणा यं प्रशंसन्ति स मनुष्यः प्रवर्धते। अथ यो ब्राह्मणान् क्रुष्टः पराभवति सोऽचिरात्॥२५
en: That man really grows in prosperity who is praised by the Brahmanas who are higher than those who are regarded superior to all men high or low.

sn: यथा महार्णवे क्षिप्त आमलोष्टो विनश्यति। तथा दुश्चरितं सर्वं पराभावाय कल्पते॥
en: That man who speaks ill of the Brahmanas soon meets with discomfiture, even as a clod of unbaked earth, meets with destruction when thrown into the sea.

sn: पश्य चन्द्रे कृतं लक्ष्म समुद्रो लवणोदकः। तथा भगसहस्रेण महेन्द्रः परिचिह्नितः॥
en: Similarly, all acts that are hurtful to the Brahmanas, to bring about discomfiture and ruin. Look at the dark spots on the Moon and the salt waters of the ocean.

sn: तेषामेव प्रभावेण सहस्रनयनो ह्यसौ। शतक्रतुः समभवत् पश्य माधव यादृशम्॥
en: The great Indra had at one time been marked all over with a thousand sexmarks. It was through the power of the Brahmanas that those marks were metamorphosed into as many eyes.

sn: इच्छन् कीर्तिं च भूतिं च लोकांश्च मधुसूदन। ब्राह्मणानुमते तिष्ठेत् पुरुषः शुचिरात्मवान्॥
en: See, O Madhava, how all these things took place. Desiring fame and prosperity and are sure various regions of beatitude in the next world, a person of pure conduct and soul should, O destroyer of Madhu, live in obedience to the dictates of the Brahmanas.

sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्येतद् वचनं श्रुत्वा मेदिन्या मधुसूदनः। साधु साध्विति कौरव्य मेदिनीं प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing those words of the goddess Earth, the destroyer of Madhu, O you of Kuru's race, said, Excellent, Excellent! and honoured the goddess in due form.

sn: एतां श्रुत्वोपमां पार्थ प्रयतो ब्राह्मणर्षभान्। सततं पूजयेथास्त्वं ततः श्रेयोऽभिपत्स्यसे॥
en: Having heard this discourse between the goddess Earth and Madhava, do you, O son of Pritha, always, with rapt soul, adore all superior Brahmanas. Doing this, you will surely obtain what is highly beneficial for you.

sn: भीष्म उवाच जन्मनैव महाभागो ब्राह्मणो नाम जायते। नमस्यः सर्वभूतानामतिथिः प्रसृत्ताग्रभुक्॥
en: Bhishma said O blessed king, a Brahmana, by birth alone becomes an object of worship with all creatures and entitled, as guests, to eat the first portion of all cooked food.

sn: सर्वार्थाः सुहृदस्तात ब्राह्मणाः सुमनोमुखाः। गीर्भिर्मङ्गलयुक्ताभिरनुध्यायन्ति पूजिताः॥
en: From them come all the great objects of life. They are the friends of all creatures in the universe. They are again the mouths of all the gods (for food poured into their mouths is eaten by the deities). Adored with respect, they wish its prosperity by uttering words fraught with auspiciousness.

sn: सर्वान्नो द्विषतस्तात ब्राह्मणा जातमन्यवः। गीर्भिर्दारुणयुक्ताभिरभिध्यासुरपूजिताः॥
en: Disregarded by our enemies, let them be engaged with these, and let thein wish evil to those detractors of theirs, imprecating them with severe curses.

sn: अत्र गाथाः पुरागीताः कीर्तयन्ति पुराविदः। सृष्ट्वा द्विजातीन् धाता हि यथापूर्वं समादधत्॥
en: About it, persons conversant with ancient history repeat the following verses sung of old respecting how in ancient times the Creator, after having created the Brahmanas, laid down their duties.

sn: न चान्यदिह कर्तव्यं किञ्चिदूर्ध्वं यथाविधि। गुप्तो गोपायते ब्रह्मा श्रेयो वस्तेन शोभनम्॥
en: A Brahmana should never do anything else than what has been laid down for him. Protected they should protect others. By acting thus, they are sure to acquire what is for their behoof.

sn: स्वमेव कुर्वतां कर्म श्रीर्वा ब्राह्मी भविष्यति। प्रमाणं सर्वभूतानां प्रग्रहाश्च भविष्यथ॥
en: By doing those acts that are laid down for them, they are sure to acquire Brahma prosperity You shall become the exemplas of all creatures, and reins for controlling them.

sn: न शौद्रं कर्म कर्तव्यं ब्राह्मणेन विपश्चिता। शौद्रं हि कुर्वतः कर्म धर्मः समुपस्थ्यते॥
en: A Brahmana endued with learning should never do that which is laid down for the Shudras. By doing such acts, a Brahmana loses his merit.

sn: श्रीश्च बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च विभूतिश्च प्रतापिनी। स्वाध्याये चैव माहात्म्यं विपुलं प्रतिपत्स्यते॥
en: By Vedic study he is sure to acquire prosperity, intelligence, energy and power competent to scorch all things, as also glory of the most superior kind.

sn: हुत्वा चाहवनीयस्थं महाभाग्ये प्रतिष्ठिताः। अग्रभोज्याः प्रसूतीनां श्रिया ब्राह्मयानुकल्पिताः॥
en: By offering oblations of clarified butter to the deities, the Brahmanas acquire high blessedness, become worthy of taking the precedence of even children in the matter of all kinds of cooked food, and gifted with Brahma prosperity.

sn: श्रद्धया परया युक्ता ह्यनभिद्रोहलब्धया। दमस्वाध्यायनिरताः सर्वान् कामानवाप्स्यथ॥
en: Endued with faith that is fraught with mercy towards all creatures, and devoted to self-control and the study of the Vedas, you shall acquire the fruition of all your desires.

sn: यच्चैव मानुषे लोके यच्च देवेषु किञ्चन। सर्वे तु तपसा साध्यं ज्ञानेन नियमेन च॥
en: Whatever things exist in the world of men, whatever things exist in the region of the celestials, can all be achieved and acquired with the help of penances and knowledge and the observance of vows and restraints.

sn: इत्येवं ब्रह्मगीतास्ते समाख्याता मयानघ। विप्राणामनुकम्पार्थं तेन प्रोक्तं हि धीमता॥
en: I have thus recited to you, O sinless one, the verses that were sung by Brahmana himself. Gifted with supreme intelligence and wisdom, the Creator himself ordained this through mercy for the Brahmanas.

sn: भूयस्तेषां बलं मन्ये यथा राज्ञस्तपस्विनः। दुरासदाश्च चण्डाश्च रभसाः क्षिप्रकारिणः॥
en: The power of those amongst them who are devoted to penances is equal to the power of kings. They are, indeed, irresistible, fierce, fleet like lightning and exceedingly quick in what they do.

sn: सन्त्येषां सिंहसत्त्वाश्च व्याघ्रसत्त्वास्तथापरे। वराहमृगसत्त्वाश्च जलसत्त्वास्तथापरे॥
en: There are amongst them those who are possessed of might of lions and those who are possessed of the might of tigers. Some of them are gifted with the might of boars, some of the deer and some of crocodiles.

sn: सर्पस्पर्शसमाः केचित् तथान्ये मकरस्पृशः। विभाष्यघातिनः केचित् तथा चक्षुर्हणोऽपरे॥
en: Some there are amongst them whose touch resembles that of snakes of dreadful poison, and some whose bite resembles that of sharks. Some amongst them are capable of bringing about by words only the destruction of those that are opposed to them; and some are competent to destroy by a look only of their eyes.

sn: सन्ति चाशीविषसमाः सन्ति मन्दास्तथापरे। विविधानीह वृत्तानि ब्राह्मणानां युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Some among them, as already said, are like snakes of dreadful poison, and some that are gifted with very mild dispositions. The dispositions, O Yudhishthira, of the Brahmanas, are of various kinds.

sn: मेकला द्राविडा लाटाः पौण्ड्राः कान्वशिरास्तथा। शौण्डिका दरदा दार्वाश्चौराः शबरबर्बराः॥
en: The Mekalas, the Dravidas, the Lathas, the Paundras, the Knowashiras, the Shaundikas, the Daradas, the Darvas, Darvas, the Chauras, Shavaras, the Varvaras, the Kiratas, the Yavanas and numerous other tribes of Kshatriyas, have degenerated into the status of Shudras through the anger of the Brahmanas.

sn: किराता यवनाश्चैव तास्ताः क्षत्रियजातयः। वृषलत्वमनुप्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाममर्षणात्॥ ब्राह्मणानां परिभवादसुराः सलिलेशयाः। ब्राह्मणानां प्रसादाच्च देवाः स्वर्गनिवासिनः॥
en: On account of their having disregarded the Brahmanas, the Asuras have been obliged to take refuge in the depths of the ocean. Through the favour of the Brahmanas, the celestials have become denizens of the happy regions of Heaven.

sn: अशक्यं स्प्रष्टुमाकाशमचाल्यो हिमवान् गिरिः। अधार्या सेतुना गङ्गा दुर्जया ब्राह्मणा भुवि॥
en: The element of other is incapable of being touched. The Himavat mountains, incapable of being moved from their root. The current of Ganga is incapable of being resisted by a dam. The Brahmanas are incapable of being governed.

sn: न ब्राह्मणविरोधेन शक्या शास्तुं वसुन्धरा। ब्राह्मणा हि महात्मानो देवानामपि देवताः॥
en: Kshatriyas are incapable of ruling the Earth without securing the good will of Brahmanas. are The Brahmana are great. They are the deities of the very deities.

sn: तान् पूजयस्व सततं दानेन परिचर्यया। यदीच्छसि महीं भोक्तुमिमां सागरमेखलाम्॥
en: Do you always adore them with gifts and obedient services, if, indeed, you desire to enjoy the sovereignty of the whole Earth encircled by seas.

sn: प्रतिग्रहेण तेजो हि विप्राणां शाम्यतेऽनघ। प्रतिग्रहं ये नेच्छेयुस्तेभ्यो रक्ष्यं त्वया नृप॥
en: The energy and power of Brahmanas, o sinless one, become abated by the acceptance of gifts. You should protect your family, O king, from those Brahmanas who do not desire to accept gifts.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। शक्रशम्बरसंवाद तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर।।।।
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old history of the discourse between Shakra and Shambara. Do you listen to it, О Yudhishthira.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: शको ह्यज्ञातरूपेण जटी भूत्वा रजोगुणः। विरूपं रथमास्थाय प्रश्न पप्रच्छ शम्बरम्॥
en: Once upon a time Shakra, assuming the guise of an ascetic with matted locks on his head and body covered with ashes all over, rode on an ugly car and went to the Asura Shambara.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: शक्र उवाच केन शम्बर वृत्तेन स्वजात्यानधितिष्ठसि। श्रेष्ठं त्वां केन मन्यन्ते तद् वै प्रब्रूहि तत्त्वतः॥
en: Shakra said Through what conduct, O Shambara, you have been able to become the head of your family? Why do all people consider you as superior? Do you tell me this truly and fully.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: शम्बर उवाच नासूयामि यदा विप्रान् ब्राह्ममेव च मे मतम्। शास्त्राणि वदतो विप्रान् सम्मन्यामि यथासुखम्॥
en: Shambara said I never entertain any ill feelings towards the Brahmanas. Whatever instructions they give, I accept with unqualified reverence. When the Brahmanas are engaged in explaining the scriptures, I listen to them with great happiness.
