description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: श्रुत्वा च नावजानामि नापराध्यामि कर्हिचित्। अभ्याभ्यनुपृच्छामि पादौ गृह्णामि धीमताम्॥
en: Having heard their interpretations I never disregard them. Nor do I ever offend against the Brahmanas in any way. I always adore intelligent Brahmanas. I always seek information from them. I always adore their feet.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: ते विश्रब्धाः प्रभाषन्ते सम्पृच्छन्ते च मां सदा। प्रमत्तेष्वप्रमत्तोऽस्मि सदा सुप्तेषु जागृमि॥
en: Approaching me with confidence, they always address me with affection and enquire after my wellbeing. If they ever happen to be careless, I am always careful. If they happen to sleep, I always remain awake.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: ते मां शास्त्रपथे युक्तं ब्रह्मण्यमनसूयकम्। समासिञ्चन्ति शास्तारः क्षौद्रं मध्विव मक्षिकाः॥
en: Like bees drenching the cells of the comb with honey, the Brahmanas, who are my zstructors and rulers, always drench me with the nectar of knowledge who am always devoted to the path pointed out by the scriptures, wlw am devoted to the Brahmanas and who am perfectly shorn of malice or evil passion.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: यच्च भाषन्ति संतुष्टास्तच्च गृह्णामि मेधया। समाधिमात्मनो नित्यमनुलोममचिन्तयम्॥
en: I always accept with cheerful hearts whatever they say. Helped by memory and understanding. I am always careful of my own faith in them and I always think of my own inferiority to them.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: सोऽहं वागग्रमृष्टानां रसानामवलेहकः। स्वजात्यानधितिष्ठामि नक्षत्राणीव चन्द्रमा:॥
en: I always lick the nectar that is at the end of their tongue, and it is for this reason that I occupy a position far above that of all others of my family like the Moon transcending all the stars.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: एतत् पृथिव्याममृतमेतच्चक्षुरनुत्तमम्। यद् ब्राह्मणमुखाच्छास्त्रमिह श्रुत्वा प्रवर्तते॥
en: The scriptural interpretations which fall from the lips of the Brahmanas and listening to which every wise man acts in the world, form nectar on Earth and may, also be likened to most excellent.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: एतत् कारणमाज्ञाय दृष्ट्वा देवासुरं पुरा। युद्धं पिता मे हृष्टात्मा विस्मितः समपद्यत॥
en: Seeing the battle between the celestials and the Asuras in days of old, and understanding the power of the instructions that fell from the Brahmanas, my father became filled with delight and wonder.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: दृष्ट्वा च ब्राह्मणानां तु महिमानं महात्मनाम्। पर्यपृच्छत् कथममी सिद्धा इति निशाकरम्॥
en: Seeing the power of great Brahmanas, my father asked the Moon the question-How do the Brahmanas acquire success?

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: सोम उवाच ब्राह्मणास्तपसा सर्वे सिध्यन्ते वाग्बलाः सदा। भुजबीर्याश्च राजानो वागस्त्राश्च द्विजातयः॥
en: Soma said The Brahmanas become crowned with success by virtue of their penances. Their strength consists in speech. The power of Kshatriyas is in their arms. The Brahmanas, however, have words for their weapons.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: प्रणवं चाप्यधीयीत ब्राह्मीर्दुर्वसतीर्वसन्। निर्मन्युरपि निर्वाणो यदि स्यात् समदर्शनः॥
en: Undergoing the discomforts of a residence into the house of his preceptor, the Brahmana should study the Vedas or at least the Pranava. Freeing himself of anger and renouncing earthly attachments, he should become a Yati, regarding all things and all creatures with equal eyes.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: अपि च ज्ञानसम्पन्नः सर्वान् वेदान् पितुर्गुहे। श्लाघमान इवाधीयाद् ग्राम्य इत्येव तं विदुः॥
en: If remaining in the house of his father he masters all the Vedas and acquiring great knowledge acquires a position that should command respect, people still condemn him as untravelled or home-keeping.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: भूमिरेतौ निगिरति सर्पो बिलशयानिव। राजानं चाप्ययोद्धारं ब्राह्मणं चाप्रवासिनम्॥
en: Like a snake swallowing mice, the Earth swallows up these two, viz., a king that is unwilling to fight and a Brahmana who is reluctant to leave home for acquiring knowiedge.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: अभिमानः श्रियं हन्ति पुरुषस्याल्पमेधसः। गर्भेण दुष्यते कन्या गृहवासेन च द्विजः॥
en: Pride destroys the prosperity of persons of little wit. A maiden, if she conceives, becomes stained. A Brahmana incurs reproach by remaining at home.

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: इत्येतन्मे पिता श्रुत्वा सोमादद्भुतदर्शनात्। ब्राह्मणान् पूजयामास तथैवाहं महाव्रतान॥
en: This is what my father heard from the revered Soma. My father, on account of this, began to adore and respect the Brahmanas. Like him, I also worship and adore all Brahmanas of high vows!

description: The conversation between Shakra and Shamvara on the same subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच श्रुत्वैतद् वचनं शक्रो दाग्वेन्द्रमुखाच्च्युतम्। द्विजान् सम्पूजयामास महेन्द्रत्वमवाप च ॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words that fell from the mouth of that prince of Danavas, Shakra began to adore the Brahmanas, and as a result thereof he succeeded in acquiring the kingship of the celestials.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अपूर्वश्च भवेत् पात्रमथवापि चिरोषितः। दूरादभ्यागतं चापि किं पात्रं स्यात् पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Which among these three persons, O grandfather should be regarded as the best for making gifts, viz., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known to the giver for a long time, or one who comes to the giver from a long distance?

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: भीष्म उवाच क्रिया भवति केषांचिदुपांशुव्रतमुत्तमम्। यो यो याचेत यत् किञ्चित् सर्वं दद्याम इत्यपि॥
en: Bhishma said All these are equal. The fitness of some consists in their soliciting alms for celebrating sacrifices or for paying the preceptor's fee or for maintaining their wives and children. The fitness of some, for receiving gifts, consists in their following the vow of wandering over the Earth, never soliciting anything but receiving when given. We should also give to one what one seeks.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: अपीडयन् भृत्यवर्गमित्येवमनुशुश्रुम। पीडयन् भृत्यवर्गं हि आत्मानमपकर्षति॥
en: We should however, make gifts without afflicting those who depend upon us. This is what we have heard. By afflicting one's dependants, one afflicts his own self.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: अपूर्वं भावयेत् पात्रं यच्चापि स्याच्चिरोषितम्। दूरादभ्यागतं चापि तत्पात्रं च विदुर्बुधाः॥
en: The stranger, one, that is who has come for the first time, should be considered as a proper object of gifts. He who is familiar and wellknown and has been living with the giver, should also be considered in the same light. The learned know that he too who comes from a distant place should be considered in an equal light.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अपीडया च भूतानां धर्मस्याहिंसया तथा। पात्रं विद्यात् तु तत्त्वेन यस्मै दत्तं न संतपेत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said It is true that we should make gifts to others without afflicting any one and without going against the ordinances of scriptures. One should, however, correctly determine who the person is that should be considered as a proper object for making gifts. He should be such that the gift itself, when made over to him, may not grieve.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: भीष्म उवाच ऋत्विक् पुरोहिताचार्याः शिष्यसम्बन्धिबान्धवाः। सर्वे पूज्याश्च मान्याश्च श्रुतवन्तोऽनसूयकाः॥
en: Bhishma said If the Ritvij, the Purohita, the preceptor, the Acharya, the disciple, the relative (by marriage), and kinsmen, happen to be endued with learning and free from malice, then should they be considered worthy of respect and adoration.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: अतोऽन्यथा वर्तमानाः सर्वे नार्हन्ति सत्क्रियाम्। तस्मान्नित्यं परीक्षेत पुरुषान् प्रणिधाय वै॥
en: Those persons who do not possess such qualifications cannot be considered as worthy of gifts or hospitality. Hence, one should with deliberation examine persons who one meets.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: अक्रोधः सत्यवचनमहिंसा दम आर्जवम्। अद्रोहोऽनभिमानश्च ह्रीस्तितिक्षा दमः शमः॥ यस्मिन्नेतानि दृश्यन्ते न चाकार्याणि भारत। स्वभावतो निविष्टानि तत्पात्रं मानमर्हति॥
en: Absence of anger, truthfulness of speech, abstention from injury, sincerity, peacefulness of conduct, the absence of pride, modesty, renunciation, selfcontrol and tranquillity or contentment of soul he in whom these are by nature, and in whom there are no wicked acts, should be considered as a proper object. Such a person deserves honours.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: तथा चिरोषितं चापि सम्प्रत्यागतमेव च। अपूर्वं चैव पूर्वं च तत्पात्रं मानमर्हति॥
en: Whether the person be one who is wellknown and familiar or one who has come newly, whether he has or has not been seen before, if he happens to possess these qualifications, he should be considered as worthy of honors and hospitality.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: अव्यवस्था च वेदानां शास्त्राणां चाभिलङ्घनम्। अव्यवस्था च सर्वत्र एतान्नाशनमात्मनः॥
en: He who denies the authority of the Vedas, or tries to show that the scriptures should be disregarded, or approves of all breaches of control in society, simply brings about his own ruin.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: भवेत् पण्डितमानी यो ब्राह्मणो वेदनिन्दकः। आन्वीक्षिकी तर्कविद्यामनुरक्तो निरर्थिकाम्॥ हेतुवादान् ब्रुवन् सत्सु विजेताहेतुवादिकः। आक्रोष्टा चातिवक्ता च ब्राह्मणानां सदैव हि॥ सर्वाभिशङ्की मूढच बालः कटुकवागपि। बोद्धव्यस्तादृशस्तात नरं श्वानं हि तं विदुः॥
en: That Brahinana who is proud of his learning, who speaks ill of the Vedas or who is given to the science of useless disputation, or who is desirous of acquiring victory in disputations) in assemblies of good men by disproving the reasons that exist for morality and religion and attributing everything to chance, or who indulges in censuring and reproaching others who reproves Brahmanas, or who is suspicious of all persons, or who is foolish and bereft of judgment, or who is bitter of speech, should be known to be as hateful as a dog.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: यथा श्वा भषितुं चैव हन्तुं चैवावसज्जते। एवं सम्भाषणार्थाय सर्वशास्त्रवधाय च॥
en: As a dog, meets others, barking the while and seeking to bite, such a person is even so, for he spends his breath in vain and tries to destroy the authority of all the scriptures.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: लोकयात्रा च द्रष्टव्या धर्मश्चात्महितानि च। एवं नरो वर्तमानः शाश्वतीर्घते समाः॥
en: or Those practices that support society, the duties of virtue, and all those acts which yield benefit to one's own self, should be attended to. A person that lives, attending to these, becomes prosperous for good.

description: Which of the three is the proper party to make gifts, vis., one who is a thorough stranger, or one who is living with and known for a long time, or one who comes from a long distance
sn: ऋणमुन्मुच्य देवानामृषीणां च तथैव च। पितॄणामथ विप्राणामतिथीनां च पञ्चमम्॥ पर्यायेण विशुद्धेन सुविनीतेन कर्मणा। एवं गृहस्थ: कर्माणि कुर्वन् धर्मान्न हीयते॥
en: By satisfying the debt one owes to the deities by performing sacrifices, that to the Rishis by studying the Vedas, that to the departed manes by procreating children, that to the Brahmanas by making presents to them, and that to guests by feeding them, in due order, and with purity of motive, and properly attending to the ordinances of the scriptures, a householder does not fall away from virtue.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच स्त्रीणां स्वभावमिच्छामि श्रोतुं भरतसत्तम। स्त्रियो हि मूलं दोषाणां लघुचित्ता हि ताः स्मृताः॥१
en: Yudhishthira said O best of the Bharatas, I wish to hear you describe the disposition of women. Women are said to be the root of all evil. They are all considered as highly frail.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। नारदस्य च संवादं पुंश्चल्या पञ्चचूडया॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old history of the discourse between the celestial Rishi Narada and the (celestial) courtezan Panchachuda.

sn: लोकाननुचरन् सर्वान् देवर्षिर्नारदः पुरा। ददर्शाप्सरसं ब्राह्मीं पञ्चचूडामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: Once in ancient times, the celestial Rishi Narada, having roamed over all the world, met the Apsara Panchachuda of faultless, beauty, having her residence in the region of Brahman.

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा चारुसर्वाङ्गी पप्रच्छाप्सरसं मुनिः। संशयो हृदि कश्चिन्मे ब्रूहि तन्मे सुनध्यमे॥
en: Seeing the Apsara every limb of whose body was highly beautiful, the ascetic addressed her, saying Oyou of slender waist, I have a doubt in my mind. Do you explain it!

sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्ताथ सा विप्रं प्रत्युवाचाथ नारदम्। विषये सति वक्ष्यामि समर्थे मन्यसे च माम्॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by the Rishi, the Apsara said to him If the subject is one which is known to me and if you consider me competent to speak on it, I shall certainly say what is in my mind.

sn: नारद उवाच न त्वामविषये भद्रे नियोक्ष्यामि कथंचन। स्त्रीणां स्वभावमिच्छामि त्वत्तः श्रोतुं वरानने॥
en: Narada said O amiable one, I shall not certainly ask you for any task that is beyond your power. O you of beautiful face, I wish to hear from you of the disposition of women.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य देवर्षेरप्सरोत्तमा। प्रत्युवाच न शक्ष्यामि स्त्री सती निन्दितुं स्त्रियः॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words of the celestial Rishi, that foremost of Apsaras replied to him, saying I am unable being myself a woman to speak ill of women.

sn: विदितास्ते स्त्रियो याश्च यादृशाश्च स्वभावतः। न मामर्हसि देवर्षे नियोक्तुं कार्य ईदृशे॥
en: You know what women are and with what nature they are gifted. You should not, O celestial Rishi, set me to such a task.

sn: तामुवाच स देवर्षिः सत्यं वद सुमध्यमे। मृषावादे भवेद् दोषः सत्ये दोषो न विद्यते॥
en: It is very To her the celestial Rishi said true, O you of slender waist! One commits sin by speaking what is untrue. In saying however, what is true, there can be no sin.

sn: इत्युक्ता सा कृतमतिरभवच्चारुहासिनी। स्त्रीदोषाञ्छाश्वतान् सत्यान् भाषितुं सम्प्रचक्रमे॥
en: Thus addressed by him, the Apsara Panchachuda of sweet smiles consented to answer Narada's question. She then addressed herself to mention what the true and eternal shortcomings are of women.

sn: पञ्चचूड़ उवाच कुलीना रूपवत्यश्च नाथवत्यश्च योषितः। मर्यादासु न तिष्ठन्ति स दोषः स्त्रीषु नारद॥
en: Panchachuda said Even if highborn and gifted with beauty and possessed of protectors women wish to transgress the restraints assigned to them. This fault truly attaches them, O Narada.

sn: न स्त्रीभ्यः किञ्चिदन्यद् वै पापीयस्तरमस्ति वै। स्त्रियो हि मूलं दोषाणां तथा त्वमपि वेत्थ ह॥
en: There is nothing else that is more sinful than women. Verily, women are the root of all evils. That is certainly known to you, O Narada.

sn: समाज्ञातानृद्धिमतः प्रतिरूपान् वशे स्थितान्। पतीनन्तरमासाद्य नालं नार्यः प्रतीक्षितुम्॥
en: Women even when having husbands of fame and wealth, of handsome features and completely obedient to them, are prepared to disregard them if they get the opportunity.

sn: असद्धर्मस्त्वयं स्त्रीणामस्माकं भवति प्रभो। पापीयसो नरान् यद् वै लज्जां त्यक्त्वा भजामहे॥१४
en: This, O powerful one, is a sinful disposition with us women, casting off modesty, we seek the companionship of men of sinful habits and intentions.

sn: स्त्रियं हि यः प्रार्थयते संनिकर्ष च गच्छति। ईषच्च कुरुते सेवां तमेवेच्छन्ति योषितः॥
en: Women show a liking for those men who court them, who approach their presence and who respectfully serve them to even a slight extent.

sn: अनर्थित्वान्मनुष्याणां भयात् परिजनस्य च। मर्यादायाममर्यादाः स्त्रियस्तिष्ठन्ति भर्तृषु॥
en: Through want of solicitation by persons of the other sex, or fear of relatives, women, who are naturally impatient of all control, do not transgress those that have been ordained for them, and remain by the side of their husbands.

sn: नासां कश्चिदगम्योऽस्ति नासां वयसि निश्चयः। विरूपं रूपवन्तं वा पुमानित्येव भुजते॥
en: There is none whom they cannot admit to their favours. They never consider about the age of the person they are prepared to favour. Ugly or handsome, if only the person happens to belong to the opposite sex, women are ready to enjoy his companionship.

sn: न भयान्नाप्यनुक्रोशान्नार्थहेतोः कथंचन। न ज्ञातिकुलसम्बन्धात् स्त्रियस्तिष्ठन्ति भर्तृषु॥
en: That women remain faithful to their husbands is due not to their fear of sin, nor to mercy, nor to riches, nor to the affection that originates in their hearts for kinsmen and children.

sn: यौवने वर्तमानानां मृष्टाभरणवाससाम्। नारीणां स्वैरवृत्तीनां स्पृहयन्ति कुलस्त्रियः॥
en: Women living in the respectable families envy the condition of those members of their sex who are young and welladorned with jewels and gems and that lead a free life.

sn: याश्च शश्वद् बहुमता रक्ष्यन्ते दयिताः स्त्रियः। अपि ताः सम्प्रसज्जन्ते कुब्जान्धजडवामनैः॥
en: Even those women who are loved by their husbands and treated with great respect, are seen to confer their favours upon men who are humpbacked, who are blind, who are idiots or who are dwarfs.

sn: पङ्गुष्वथ च देवर्षे ये चान्ये कुत्सिता नराः। स्त्रीणामगम्यो लोकेऽस्मिन् नास्ति कश्चिन्महामुने।।२१
en: Women may be seen to like the companionship of even those men who are inert or those men who are ugly to look at, O great Rishi, there is no man in this world whom women may consider as unfit for companionship!

sn: यदि पुंसां गतिर्ब्रह्मन् कथंचित्रोपपद्यते। अप्यन्योन्यं प्रवर्तन्ते न हि तिष्ठन्ति भर्तृषु॥ अलाभात् पुरुषाणां हि भयात् परिजनस्य च। वधबन्धभयाच्चापि स्वयं गुप्ता भवन्ति ताः॥
en: Through inability to obtain persons of the opposite sex, or fear of relatives or fear of death and imprisonment, women remain, of themselves under control.

sn: चलस्वभावा दुःसेव्या दुर्गाह्या भावतस्तथा। प्राज्ञस्य पुरुषस्येह यथा वाचस्तथा स्त्रियः॥
en: They are highly fickle, for they always hanker after new companions. On account of their nature being unintelligible, they are incapable of being kept in obedience by loving treatment. Their nature is such that they are incapable of being controlled when bent upon transgression. Indeed, women are like the words uttered by the wise.

sn: नाग्निस्तृप्यति काष्ठानां नापगानां महोदधिः। नान्तकः सर्वभूतानां न पुंसां वामलोचनाः॥
en: Fire is never satiated with fuel. Ocean can never be filled with the waters that the rivers bring to him. The destroyer is never satiated with killing even all living creatures. Likewise, women are never satiated with men.

sn: इदमन्यच्च देवर्षे रहस्यं सर्वयोषिताम्। दृष्ट्वैव पुरुषं हृद्यं योनिः प्रक्लिद्यते स्त्रियाः॥
en: This, O celestial Rishi, is another mystery about women. As soon as they see a man of beautiful and charming features, unfailing signs of desire appear on their body.

sn: कामानामपि दातारं कर्तारं मनसां प्रियम्। रक्षितारं न मृष्यन्ति स्वभतार्रमलं स्त्रियः॥
en: They never show sufficient regard for even such husbands as satisfy all their wishes, as always do what is agreeable to them, and as protect them from want and danger.

sn: न कामभोगान् विपुलान् नालंकारान् न संश्रयान्। तथैव बहु मन्यन्ते यथा रत्यामनुग्रहम्॥
en: Women never prize even profuse articles of enjoyment or ornaments or other delightful things so much as they do the companionship of persons of the opposite sex,

sn: अन्तकः पवनो मृत्युः पातालं वडवामुखम्। क्षुरधारा विषं सर्पो वह्निरित्येकत: स्त्रियः॥
en: The destroyer, the god of wind, death the nether regions, the equine mouth that roves through the ocean, vomiting ceaseless flames of fire, the sharpness of the razor, dreadful poison, the snake and Fire all these exist in a state of union in the woman.

sn: यतश्च भूतानि महान्ति पञ्च यतश्च लोका विहिता विधात्रा। स्तदैव दोषाः प्रमदासु नारद॥
en: Indeed from that eternal Brahma whence the five great elements have originated whence the Creator Brahman has ordained the universe and whence, indeed, men have sprung, have women sprung into existence. At that time, again, ONarada, when women were created, these faults that I have described were planted in them.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच इमे वै मानवा लोके स्त्रीषु सज्जन्त्यभीक्ष्णशः। मोहेन परमाविष्टा देवसृष्टेन पार्थिव॥
en: Yudhishthira said Overcome by the illusion of the divine Being, all men, O king in this world, are seen to attach themselves to women.

sn: स्त्रियश्च पुरुषेष्वेव प्रत्यक्षं लोकसाक्षिकम्। अत्र मे संशयस्तीवो हृदि सम्परिवर्तते।॥
en: Likewise, women, too, are seen to attach themselves to men. All this is seen taking place everywhere in the world. I have a doubt on this subject.

sn: कथमासां नराः सङ्गं कुर्वते कुरुनन्दन। स्त्रियो वा केषु रज्यन्ते विरज्यन्ते च ताः पुनः॥
en: Why, O delighter of the Kurus, do men still attach themselves to women? Who, again, are those men with whom are women highly pleased, and who are they with whom they are displeased.

sn: इति ताः पुरुषव्याघ्र कथं शक्यास्तु रक्षितुम्। प्रमदाः पुरुषेणेह तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: You should, O chief of men, explain to me how men are capable of protecting women?

sn: एता हि रममाणास्तु वञ्चयन्तीह मानवान्। न चासां मुच्यते कश्चित् पुरुषो हस्तमागतः॥
en: While men take pleasure in women and sport with them, women, it seems, are engaged in imposing upon men. Then, again, if a man once falls into their hands, it is difficult for him to escape from them. Like kine ever liking pastures new, women like new men one after another.

sn: गावो नवतृणानीव गृह्णन्त्येता नवं नवम्। शम्बरस्य च या माया माया या नमुचेरपि॥
en: The women have in them the sum total of that illusion which the Asura Shambara possessed, that illusion which the Asura Namuchi possessed, that illusion which Bali or Kumbhinasi had.

sn: बलेः कुम्भीनसेश्चैव सर्वास्ता योषितो विदुः। हसन्तं प्रहसन्त्येता रुदन्तं प्ररुदन्ति च॥
en: If man laughs, women laugh. If man weeps, they weep. If the opportunity requires, they receive the man who is disagreeable to them with sweet words.

sn: अप्रियं प्रियवाक्यैश्च गृह्णते कालयोगतः। उशना वेद यच्छास्त्रं यच्च वेद बृहस्पतिः॥
en: That science of policy which the preceptor of the Asuras knew, that science of policy which the preceptor of the celestials, viz., Brihaspati, knew, is not deeper or more subtile than what woman's intelligence. Indeed, how can women, therefore, be restrained by men?

sn: स्त्रीबुद्ध्या न विशिष्येत नास्तु रक्ष्याः कथं नरैः। अनृतं सत्यमित्याहुः सत्यं चापि तथानृतम्॥
en: They make a lie appear as truth, and a truth, appear as a lie. They who can do this I ask, O hero how can they be governed by persons of the opposite sex?

sn: इति यास्ताः कथं वीर संरक्ष्याः पुरुषैरिह। स्त्रीणां बुद्ध्यर्थनिष्कर्षादर्थशास्त्राणि शत्रुहन्॥
en: It appears to me that Brihaspati and othur great thinkers, O destroyer of enemies evolved the science of policy from observation of the understanding of women.

sn: बृहस्पतिप्रभृतिभिर्मन्ये सद्भिः कृतानि वै। सम्पूज्यमानाः पुरुषैर्विकुर्वन्ति मनो नृप॥
en: Whether treated by men, with respect or with hatred, women are seen to turn the heads and agitate the hearts of men.

sn: अपास्ताश्च तथा राजन् विकुर्वन्ति मनः स्त्रियः। इमाः प्रजा महाबाहो धार्मिक्य इति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: Living creatures, O you of mighty arms are virtuous. Even this is what we have heard. Treated with love and respect or otherwise women are seen to deserve censure for their conduct towards men.

sn: सत्कृतासत्कृताश्चापि विकुर्वन्ति मनः सदा। कस्ताः शक्तो रक्षितुं स्यादिति मे संशयो महान्।।१३
en: This great doubt fills my mind, viz., when their conduct is such, what man is there that can restrain them within the limits of virtue? Do you explain this to me, O highly blessed scion of Kuru's race.

sn: तथा ब्रूहि महाभाग कुरूणां वंशवर्धन। यदि शक्या कुरुश्रेष्ठ रक्षा तासां कदाचन। कर्तुं वा कृतपूर्वं वा तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: You should tell me, O chief of Kuru's race, whether women are truly capable of being governed within the limits prescribed by the scriptures or whether any one before our time did really succeeded in so controlling them.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमेव महाबाहो नात्र मिथ्यास्ति किंचन। यथा ब्रवीषि कौरव्य नारी प्रति जनाधिप॥
en: Bhishma said It is true what you say, O you of mighty arms. There is nothing untrue in all this that you say, O you of Kuru's race, on the subject of women, O monarch!

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि इतिहासं पुरातनम्। यथा रक्षा कृता पूर्वं विपुलेन महात्मना॥
en: About it I shall recite to you the old history of how in days of yore the great Vipula had succeeded in restraining women within the limits laid down for them.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: प्रमदाश्च यथा सृष्टा ब्रह्मणा भरतर्षभ। यदर्थं तच्च ते तात प्रवक्ष्यामि नराधिप।॥
en: I shall also tell you, O king, how women were created by the Grandfather Brahman and the object for which they were created by him.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: न हि स्त्रीभ्यः परं पुत्र पापीयः किंचिदस्ति वै। अग्निर्हि प्रमदा दीप्तो मायाश्च मयजा विभो॥
en: There is no creature more sinful, O son, than woman. Woman is a burning fire. She is the illusion, o king, that the Daitya Maya created.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: क्षुरधारा विषं सर्पो वह्रिरित्येकतः स्त्रियः। प्रजा इमा महाबाहो धार्मिक्य इति नः श्रुतम्॥ स्वयं गच्छन्ति देवत्वं ततो देवानियाद् भयम्।
en: She is the sharp edge of the razor. She is poison. She is a snake. She is fire. She is verily, all these in a body. We have heard that all human beings beings are characterised by righteousness, and that they, in course of natural progress and improvement, attain to the dignity of god. This circumstance alarmed the celestials.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: अथाभ्यगच्छन् देवास्ते पितामहमरिंदम॥ निवेद्य मानसं चापि तूष्णीमासन्नधोमुखाः।
en: They, therefore, O chastiser of foes, assembled together and went to the Grandfather. Informing Him of what was in their minds, they stood silent before him with downcast eyes.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तेषामन्तर्गतं ज्ञात्वा देवानां स पितामहः॥ मानवानां प्रमोहार्थे कृत्या नार्योऽसृजत् प्रभुः।
en: Having learnt what was in the hearts of the celestials, the powerful Grandfather created women with the help of an Atharvan rite.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: पूर्वसर्गे तु कौन्तेय साध्व्यो नार्य इहाभवन्॥ असाध्व्यस्तु समुत्पन्नाः कृत्याः सर्गात् प्रजापतेः। ताभ्यः कामान् यथाकामं प्रादाद्धि स पितामहः॥
en: In a former creation, O son of Kunti, women were all virtuous. Those however, that sprang from this creation by Brahman with the help of an illusion, became sinful. The Grandfather bestowed upon them the desire of enjoying all kinds of carnal pleasure.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: ताः कामलुब्धाः प्रमदाः प्रबाधन्ते नरान् सदा। क्रोधं कामस्य देवेशः सहायं चासृजत् प्रभुः॥
en: Tempted by the desire of enjoyment, they began to pursue persons of the other sex. The powerful lord of the deities created Anger as the companion of Lust.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: असज्जन्त प्रजाः सर्वाः कामक्रोधवशं गताः। न च स्त्रीणां क्रियाः काश्चिदिति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः।।११
en: Persons of the male sex, yielding to the power of Lust and Anger, sought the companionship of women. Women have no especial acts laid down for them. This is the ordinance that was laid down.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: निरिन्द्रिया ह्यशास्त्राश्च स्त्रियोऽनृतमिति श्रुतिः। शय्यासनमलंकारमन्नपानमनार्यताम्॥ दुर्वाग्भावं रतिं चैव ददौ स्त्रीभ्यः प्रजापतिः। न तासां रक्षणं शक्यं कर्तुं पुंसा कथंचन॥ अपि विश्वकृता तात कुतस्तु पुरुषैरिह।
en: The Shruti declares that women are gifted with the most powerful senses that they have no scriptures to follow, and that they are living lies. Beds, seats, ornaments, food and drink and the absence of all that is respectable and righteous, indulgence in disagreeable words, and love of sexual companionship these were bestowed by Brahman upon women. Men are quite unable to restrain them within limits.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: वाचा च वधबन्धैर्वा क्लेशैर्वा विविधैस्तथा॥ न शक्या रक्षितुं नार्यस्ता हि नित्यमसंयताः।
en: The Creator himself is incapable of keeping them within proper limits, what need then be said of men?

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: इदं तु पुरुषव्याघ्र पुरस्ताच्छुतवानहम्॥ यथा रक्षा कृता पूर्वं विपुलेन गुरुस्त्रियाः।
en: This, O chief of men, I heard in former days viz., how Vipula had succeeded in protecting his preceptor's wife in ancient times.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: ऋषिरासीन्महाभागो देवशर्मेति विश्रुतः॥ तस्य भार्या रुचिर्नाम रूपेणासदृशी भुवि।
en: There was in days of yore a highly blessed Rishi of the name of Devasharman of great fame. He had a wife of name Ruchi, who was peerless on Earth in beauty.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तस्या रूपेण सम्मत्ता देवगन्धर्वदानवाः॥ विशेषेण तु राजेन्द्र वृत्रहा पाकशासनः।
en: Her loveliness intoxicated every one among the celestials and Gandharvas and Danavas. The chastiser of Paka, viz., Indra, the destroyer of Vritra, O king, was in particular enamoured of her and coveted her body.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: नारीणां चरितज्ञश्च देवशर्मा महामुनिः॥ यथाशक्ति यथोत्साहं भार्यां तामभ्यरक्षत।
en: The great ascetic Devasharman fully knew the disposition of women. He therefore, to the best of his power and energy, protected her.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: पुरन्दरं च जानीते परस्त्रीकामचारिणम्॥ तस्माद् बलेन भार्याया रक्षणं स चकार ह।
en: The Rishi knew that Indra had not scruples in seeking the companionship of other people's wives. It was therefore, that he used to protect his wife, putting forth all his power.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: स कदाचिदृषिस्तात यज्ञं कर्तुमनास्तदा॥ भार्यासंरक्षणं कार्यं कथं स्यादित्यचिन्तयत्।
en: Once on a time. O son, the Rishi became desirous of celebrating a sacrifice. He began to think of how (during his own absence from home) his wife could be protected.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: रक्षाविधानं मनसा स संचिन्त्य महातपाः॥ आहूय दयितं शिष्यं विपुलं प्राह भार्गवम्।
en: Gifted with high ascetic merit, he at last hit upon the course he should adopt. Summoning his favourite disciple whose name was Vipula and who was of Bhrigu's family, he said as follows.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: देवशर्मन् उवाच यज्ञकारो गमिष्यामि रुचिं चेमां सुरेश्वरः॥ यतः प्रार्थयते नित्यं तां रक्षस्व यथाबलम्।
en: Devasharman said I shall leave home in order to celebrate a sacrifice. The king of the celestials always covets this Ruchi of mine. Do you, during my absence, protect her, displaying all your power.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: अप्रमत्तेन ते भाव्यं सदा प्रति पुरन्दरम॥ स हि रूपाणि कुरुते विविधानि भृगूत्तम।
en: You shall pass your time carefully in view of Purandara. O foremost one of Bhrigu's race, that Indra assumes various forms.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तो विपुलस्तेन तपस्वी नियतेन्द्रियः॥ सदैवोग्रतपा राजन्नग्न्यर्कसदृशद्युतिः। धर्मज्ञः सत्यवादी च तथेति प्रत्यभाषत। पुनश्चेदं महाराज पप्रच्छ प्रस्थितं गुरुम्॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by his preceptor, the ascetic Vipula, with senses restrained, always engaged in severe penances, possessed of the splendour, O king, of fire or the sun, conversant with all the duties of virtue, and ever truthful in speech, answered him, saying So be it! Once more, however, as his preceptor was about to start, Vipula asked him in these words.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: विपुल उवाच कानि रूपाणि शक्रस्य भवन्त्यागच्छतो मुने। वपुस्तेजश्च कीदृग्वै तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Vipula said Tell me, O Muni, what forms does Shakra assume when he comes. Of what kinds is his body and what is his energy? You should tell me all this.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः स भगवांस्तस्मै विपुलाय महात्मने। आचचक्षे यथातत्त्वं मायां शक्रस्य भारत।॥
en: Bhishma said The illustrious Rishi then truly described to the great Vipula all the illusions of Shakra, O Bharata.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: देवशर्मन् उवाच बहुमायः स विप्रर्षे भगवान् पाकशासनः। तांस्तान् विकुरुते भावान् बहूनथ मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: Devasharman said The powerful chastiser of Paka, . regenerate Rishi, is full of illusion. Every moment he assumes those forms that he chooses.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: किरीटी वज्रधृग् धन्वी मुकुटी बद्धकुण्डलः॥ भवत्यथ मुहूर्तेन चण्डालसमदर्शनः।
en: Sometimes he wears a diadem and holds the thunderbolt. Sometimes, armed with the thunder bolt and wearing a crown on his head, he adorns himself with earrings. In a moment he changes himself into the shape and aspect of Chandala.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: शिखी जटी चीरवासाः पुनर्भवति पुत्रक॥ बृहच्छरीश्च पुनश्चीरवासाः पुनः कृशः।
en: Sometimes he appears with coronal locks on his head; soon again, O son, he shows himself with matted locks, his person being clad in rags. Sometimes he assumes a goodly and huge frame. The next moment he changes himself into one of emaciated limbs and clad in rags. as

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: गौरं श्यामं च कृष्णं च वर्णं विकुरुते पुनः॥ विरूपो रूपवांश्चैव युवा वृद्धस्तथैव च।
en: Sometimes he becomes fair, sometimes darkish, sometimes dark of complexion. Sometimes he becomes ugly and sometimes beautiful. Sometimes he appears as young and sometimes as old.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियश्चैव वैश्यः शूद्रस्तथैव च॥ प्रतिलोमोऽनुलोमश्च भवत्यथ शतक्रतुः।
en: Sometimes he appears as a Brahmana, sometimes as a Kshatriya, sometimes as a Vaishya, and sometimes as a Shudra. Indeed, he of a hundred sacrifices appears at times as a person born of impure caste, that is, as the son of a superior father by an inferior mother or of an inferior father by a superior mother.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: शुकवायसरूपी च हंसकोकिलरूपवान्॥ सिंहव्याघ्रगजानां च रूपं धारयते पुनः।
en: Sometimes he appears a parrot, sometimes as a crow, sometimes as a swan and sometimes as a koel. He assumes the forms also of a lion, a tiger or an elephant.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: दैवं दैत्यमथो राज्ञां वपुर्धारयतेऽपि च॥ अकृशो वायुभग्नाङ्गः शकुनिर्विकृतस्ताया।
en: Sometimes he appears as a god, sometimes as a Daitya and sometimes he assumes the guise of a king. Sometimes he appears as fat and plump, sometimes as one whose limbs have been broken by the disordered wind in the system, sometimes as a bird, and sometimes as one of an exceedingly ugly form.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: चतुष्पाद् बहुरूपश्च पुनर्भवति बालिशः॥ मक्षिकामशकादीनां वपुर्धारयतेऽपि च।
en: Sometimes he appears as a quadruped. Capable of assuming any form, he sometimes appears as an idiot shorn of all intelligence. He assumes also the forms of flies and gnats.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: न शक्यमस्य ग्रहणं कर्तुं विपुल केनचित्॥ अपि विश्वकृता तात येन सृष्टमिदं जगत्।
en: O Vipula, no one can make him out on account of these numberless disguises that he is capable of assuming. The very Creator of the universe is not equal to that feat.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: पुनरन्तर्हितः शक्रो दृश्यते ज्ञानचक्षुषा॥ वायुभूतश्च स पुनर्देवराजो भवत्युत।
en: He makes himself invisible when he likes. He is incapable of being seen except with the eye of knowledge. The king of the celestials sometimes changes himself into the wind.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: एवं रूपाणि सततं कुरुते पाकशासनः॥ तस्माद् विपुल यत्नेन रक्षेमां तनुमध्यमाम्।
en: The chastiser of Paka always assumes these disguises. Do you therefore, O Vipula protect this slender-waisted wife of mine with great care. intent upon

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: यथा रुचिं नावलिहेद् देवेन्द्रो भृगुसत्तम॥ क्रतावुपहिते न्यस्तं हविः श्वेव दुरात्मवान्।
en: O foremost one of Bhrigu's race, do you take every care for seeing that the king of the celestials may not defile this wife of mine like a wretched dog licking the Havi kept in view of a sacrifice.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: एवमाख्याय च मुनिर्यज्ञकारोऽगमत् तदा॥ देवशर्मा महाभागस्ततो भरतसत्तम।
en: Having said these words, the highly blessed ascetic viz., Devasharman, celebrating a sacrifice, started from his abode, O chief of the Bharatas.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: विपुलस्तु वचः श्रुत्वा गुरोश्चिन्तामुपेयिवान्॥ रक्षां च परमां चक्रे देवराजान्महाबलात्।
en: Hearing these words of his preceptor, Vipula began to think, I shall certainly protect this lady in every respect from the powerful king of the celestials.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: किं नु शक्यं मया कुर्ते गुरुदाराभिरक्षणे॥ मायावा हि सुरेन्द्रोऽसौ दुर्धर्षश्चापि वीर्यवान्।
en: But what should be the means? What can I do for protecting the wife of my preceptor? The king of the celestials is endued with large powers of illusion. Gifted with great energy, he is difficult of being resisted.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: नापिधायाश्रमं शक्यो रक्षितुं पाकशासनः॥ उटजं वा तथा ह्यस्य नानाविधसरूपता।
en: Indra cannot be kept out by enclosing this retreat of ours or fencing this yard, since he is capable of assuming numberless forms.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: वायुरूपेण वा शक्रो गुरुपत्नी प्रधर्षयेत्॥ तस्मादिमां सम्प्रविश्य रुचिं स्थास्येऽहमद्य वै।
en: Assuming the form of the wind, the king of the celestials may assault the wife of my preceptor. The best course, therefore, for me, would be to enter the body of this lady and remain there.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: अथवा पौरुषेणेयं न शक्या रक्षितुं मया॥ बहुरूपो हि भगवाञ्छूयते पाकशासनः।
en: By displaying my prowess I shall not be able to protect the lady, for the powerful chastiser of Paka, it has been heard by me, is capable of assuming any form he likes.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: सोऽहं योगबलादेनां रक्षिष्ये पाकशासनात्॥ गात्राणि गात्रैरस्याहं सम्प्रवेक्ष्ये हि रक्षितुम्।
en: I shall, therefore, protect this one from Indra by my Yogapower. For satisfying my object I shall with my body enter the body of this lady.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: यधुच्छिष्टामिमां पत्नीमद्य पश्यति मे गुरुः॥ शप्स्यत्यसंशयं कोपाद् दिव्यज्ञानो महातपाः।
en: If my preceptor on return, sees his wife defiled, he will, forsooth, curse me through anger, for endued with great ascetic merit, he is gifted with spiritual vision.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: न चेयं रक्षितुं शक्या यथान्या प्रमदा नृभिः॥ मायावी हि सुरेन्द्रोऽसावहो प्राप्तोऽस्मि संशयम्।
en: This lady is incapable of being protected in the way in which other women are protected by men, since the king of the celestials is gifted with large powers of illusion. Alas, the situation is very critical.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: अवश्यं करणीयं हि गुरोरिह हि शासनम्॥ यदि त्वेतदहं कुर्यामाश्चर्ये स्यात् कृतं मया।
en: The command of my preceptor should certainly be obeyed by me. If, therefore, I protect her by my Yogapower, the feat will be considered by all as a wonderful one.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: योगेनाथ प्रवेशो हि गुरुपल्याः कलेवरे॥५ एवमेव शरीरेऽस्या निवत्स्यामि समाहितः।
en: By my Yogapower therefore, I shall enter the body of my preceptor's lady. I shall live within her and yet not touch her body like a drop of water on a lotus leaf which lies on it yet does not drench it at all.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: असक्तः पद्मपत्रस्थो जलबिन्दुर्यथाचलः॥ निर्मुक्तस्य रजोरूपान्नापराधो भवेन्मम। यथा हि शून्यां पथिकः सभामध्यावसेत् पथि॥ तथाद्यावासयिष्यामि गुरुपत्न्याः कलेवरम् एवमेव शरीरेऽस्या निवत्स्यामि समाहितः॥
en: If I be free from the touch of passion, I cannot incur any sin by doing what I wish to do. As a traveller, in course of his sojourn, takes up his quarters (for a while) in any empty house he finds, I shall, similarly live, this day within the body of my preceptor's lady. Indeed, with mind rapt up in Yoga, I shall live today in this lady's body.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: इत्येवं धर्ममालोक्य वेदवेदांश्च सर्वशः। तपश्च विपुलं दृष्ट्वा गुरोरात्मन एव च।॥ इति निश्चित्य मनसा रक्षां प्रति स भार्गवः। अन्वतिष्ठत् परं यत्नं यथा तच्छृणु पार्थिव॥
en: Giving his best consideration to these points of virtue, thinking of all the Vedas and their branches and with eye directed to the penances which his preceptor had and which he himself also was possessed of, and having settled in his mind, with a view only to protect the lady, to enter her body by Yogapower, Vipula of Bhrigu's race, took great care (for accomplishing his object. Listen now to me, O king, as I recite to you what he did.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: गुरुपत्नीं समासीनो विपुलः स महातपाः। उपासीनामनिन्द्यागी कथाभिः समलोभयत्॥
en: Gifted with great penances, Vipula sat himself down by the side of his preceptor's wife as she of faultless features was sitting in her cottage. Vipula then began to discourse to her for bringing her over to the cause of virtue and truth.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: नेत्राभ्यां नेत्रयोरस्या रशिंम संयोज्य रश्मिभिः। विवेश विपुलः कायमाकाशं पवनो यथा॥
en: Directing his eyes then to hers and uniting the rays of light that came out from her organs of vision with those that issued from his, Vipula entered the lady's body even as the element of wind enters that of ether or space.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: लक्षणं लक्षणेनैव वदनं वदनेन च। अविचेष्टन्नतिष्ठद् वै छायेवान्तहितो मुनिः॥
en: Penetrating her eyes with his eyes and her face with his face, Vipula lived, without moving within her invisibly, like her shadow.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: ततो विष्टभ्य विपुलो गुरुपल्याः कलेवरम्। उवास रक्षणे युक्तो न च सा तमबुद्ध्यता॥
en: Restraining every part of the lady's body, Vipula continued to live within her, intent on protecting her from Indra. The lady herself knew nothing of this.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: यं कालं नागतो राजन् गुरुस्तस्य महात्मनः। क्रतुं समाप्य स्वगृहं तं कालं सोऽभ्यरक्षत॥
en: It was in this way, o king, that Vipula continued to protect the lady till the time of his great preceptor's return after accomplishing the sacrifice which he had gone out to perform.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः कदाचिद् देवेन्द्रो दिव्यरूपवपुर्धरः। इदमन्तरमित्येवमभ्यगात् तमथाश्रमम्॥
en: Bhishma said One day the king of the celestials assuming a form of divine beauty, came to the hermitage of the Rishi, thinking that the opportunity he had been expecting had at last come.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: रूपमप्रतिमं कृत्वा लोभनीयं जनाधिप। दर्शनीयतमो भूत्वा प्रविवेश तमाश्रमम्॥
en: Indeed, O king, having assumed a form peerless in beauty and highly tempting to women and highly agreeable to look at, Indra entered the ascetic's asylum.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: स ददर्श तमासीनं विपुलस्य कलेवरम्। निश्चेष्टं स्तब्धनयनं यथा लेख्यगतं तथा॥
en: He beheld the body of Vipula staying in a sitting posture, immovable as a stake and with eyes shorn of vision, like a picture drawn on the canvas.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: रुचिं च रुचिरापाङ्गी पीनश्रोणिपयोधराम्। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षीं सम्पूर्णेन्दुनिभाननाम्॥
en: And he beheld also Ruchi, seated there, adorned with eyes whose ends were highly beautiful, possessed of full and round hips, and having a deep and swelling bosom. Her eyes were large and expansive like lotus petals and her face was as beautiful and sweet as the full moon.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: सा तमालोक्य सहसा प्रत्युत्थातुमियेष ह। रूपेण विस्मिता कोऽसीत्यथ वक्तुमिवेच्छती॥
en: Seeing Indra come in that guise, the lady wished to rise up and welcome him. Her wonder having been excited at the peerless beauty of form which the person possessed, she very much wished to ask him as to who he was.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: उत्थातुकामा तु सती विष्टब्धा विपुलेन सा। निगृहीता मनुष्येन्द्र न शशाक विचेष्टितुम्॥
en: Although however, she wished to rise up and welcome him, yet her limbs having been restrained by Vipula who was living within her, she failed, O king, to do what she wished. In fact, she was unable, to move from the place where she sat.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तामाबभाषे देवेन्द्रः साम्ना परमवल्गुना। त्वदर्थमागतं विद्धि देवेन्द्रं मां शुचिस्मिते॥
en: The king of the celestials then addressed her in sweet words uttered with a sweet voice.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: क्लिश् मानमनङ्गेन त्वत्संकल्पभवेन ह। तत् सम्प्राप्तं हि मां सुभु पुरा कालोऽतिवर्तते॥
en: Indeed he said O you of sweet smiles, know that I am Indra, arrived there for your sake! Know, O sweet lady that I am afflicted by the god of love provoked by your thoughts. O you of beautiful brows, I have come to you. Time passes away.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तमेवंवादिनं शक्रं शुश्राव विपुलो मुनिः। गुरुपल्ल्याः शरीरस्थो ददर्श त्रिदशाधिपम्॥
en: These words that Indra spoke were heard by the ascetic Vipula. Remaining within the body of his preceptor's wife, he saw everything that took place.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: न शशाक च सा राजन् प्रत्युत्थातुमनिन्दिता। वक्तुं च नाशकद् राजन् विष्टब्धा विपुलेन सा॥
en: The lady of faultless beauty, though she heard what Indra said, was, however, unable to rise up for welcoming or honouring the king of the celestials. Her senses restrained by Vipula she could make no reply.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: आकारं गुरुपत्यास्तु स विज्ञाय भृगूद्वहः। निजग्राह महातेजा योगेन बलबत् प्रभो॥
en: Judging from the marks afforded by the body of his preceptor's wife that she was not reluctant to receive Indra with kindness, that scion of Bhrigu's race, of mighty energy restrained her limbs and senses all the more effectually, O king, by his Yogapowers.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: बबन्ध योगबन्धैश्च तस्याः सर्वेन्द्रियाणि सः। तां निर्विकारां दृष्ट्वा तु पुनरेव शचीपतिः॥ उवाच वीडितो राजस्तां योगबलमोहिताम्। एह्येहीति ततः सा तु प्रतिवक्तुमियेष तम्॥
en: With Yogafetters he bound up all her senses. Seeing her seated without any mark of agitation on her body, the husband of Sachi, abashed a little once more addressed that lady who was stupefied by the Yogapowers of her husband's disciple, in these words Come, come, O sweet lady! Then the lady tried to answer him. Vipula however, restrained the words that she intended to utter,

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: स तां वाचं गुरोः पत्न्या विपुलः पर्यवर्तयत्। भो: किमागमने कृत्यमिति तस्यास्तु निःसृता॥
en: The words therefore, that actually dropped from her lips were What is the reason of your coming here? These words adorned with grammatical refinements, came out of her mouth that was as beautiful like the moon.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: वक्त्राच्छशाङ्कसदृशाद् वाणी संस्कारभूषणा। वीडिता सा तु तद्वाक्यमुक्त्वा परवशा तदा॥
en: Subject to the influence of another, she gave vent to these words, but became rather ashamed for uttering them. Hearing her, Purandara became highly disspirited.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: पुरन्दरश्च तत्रस्थो बभूव विमना भृशम्। स तद्वैकृतमालक्ष्य देवराजो विशाम्पते॥
en: Observing that awkward result, the king of the celestials, O monarch, having a thousand eyes, saw everything with his spiritual eye.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: अवैक्षत सहस्राक्षस्तदा दिव्येन चक्षुषा। स ददर्श मुनिं तस्याः शरीरान्तरगोचरम्॥
en: He then saw the ascetic living within the body of the lady. Indeed, the ascetic remained within the body of his preceptor's wife like an image or reflection on a mirror.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: प्रतिबिम्बमिवादशे गुरुपल्याः शरीरगम्। स तं घोरेण तपसा युक्तं दृष्ट्वा पुरन्दरः॥
en: Seeing the ascetic gifted with the terrible power of penances, Purandara, O king, fearing the Rishi's curse, trembled in fear.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: प्रावेपत सुसंत्रस्तः शापभीतस्तदा विभो। विमुच्य गुरुपत्नीं तु विपुलः सुमहातपाः। स्वकलेवरमाविश्य शक्रं भीतमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Vipula then gifted with great ascetic power, left the body of his preceptor's wife and returned to his own body that was lying near. Then he addressed the terrified Indra in the following words.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: विपुल उवाच अजितेन्द्रिय दुर्बुद्धे पापात्मक पुरन्दर। न चिरं पूजयिष्यन्ति देवास्त्वां मानुषास्तथा॥
en: Vipula said O wicked Purandara, O you of sinful mind, o wretch who have no control over your senses, neither the deities nor human beings will worship you for any length of time.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: किं तु तद्विस्मृतं शक न तन्मनसि ते स्थितम्। गौतमेनासि यन्मुक्तो भगाङ्कपरिचिह्नितः॥
en: Have you forgotten it, O Shakra does it not still dwell in your remembrance that Gautama had cursed you on account of which your body became disfigured with a thousand sexmarks, which owing to the Rishi's mercy, were after words changed into so many eyes.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: जाने त्वां बालिशमतिमकृतात्मानमस्थिरम्। मयेयं रक्ष्यते मूढ गच्छ पाप यथागतम्॥
en: I know that you are of an exceedingly foolish understanding that, your soul is impure and that you are of an exceedingly fickle mind. O fool, know that this lady is being protected by me. O sinful wretch, return whence you came.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: नाहं त्वामद्य मूढात्मन् दहेयं हि स्वतेजसा। कृपायमानस्तु न ते दग्धुमिच्छामि वासव॥
en: you of foolish soul, I do not reduce you today into ashes with my energy. Indeed, I am filled with mercy for you. It is for this that I do not, O Vasava, wish to burn you.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: स च घोरतमो धीमान् गुरुस्त्वं पापचेतसम्। दृष्ट्वा त्वां निर्दहेदद्य क्रोधदीप्तेन चक्षुषा॥
en: My preceptor gifted with great intelligence, is possessed of terrible power. With eyes blazing with anger, he would, if he saw you, have burnt your sinful self today.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: नैवं तु शक्र कर्तव्यं पुनर्मान्याच ते द्विजाः। मा गम: ससुतामात्यः क्षयं ब्रह्मबलार्दितः॥
en: You should not, O Shakra, do its like again. The Brahmanas should be respected by you. See that you do not, with your sons and counsellors, meet with destruction, afflicted by the power of the Brahmanas.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: अमरोऽस्मीति यबुद्धि समास्थाय प्रवर्तसे। मावमंस्था न तपसा नसाध्यं नाम किंचन॥
en: You think that you are an immortal and that, therefore, are at liberty to act thus. Do not, however, dishonour the Brahmanas. Know that there is nothing unattainable by penance.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: भीष्म उवाच तच्छुत्वा वचनं शक्रो विपुलस्य महात्मनः। अकिंचिदुक्त्वा व्रीडार्तस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words of the great Vipula, Shakra without saying anything, and covered with shame, disappeared.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: मुहूर्तयाते तस्मिंस्तु देवशर्मा महातपाः। कृत्वा यज्ञं यथाकाममाजगाम स्वमाश्रमम्॥
en: A moment after he had gone away, Devasharman of great ascetic merit, having accomplished the sacrifice, he had intended to perform, returned to his own hermitage.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: आगतेऽथ गुरौ राजन् विपुल: प्रियकर्मकृत्। रक्षितां गुरवे भार्यां न्यवेदयदनिन्दिताम्॥
en: When his preceptor returned, Vipula who had done a good deed, gave to him his wife of faultless beauty whom he had successfully protected against the machination of Indra.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: अभिवाद्य च शान्तात्मा स गुरुं गुरुवत्सलः। विपुलः पर्युपातिष्ठद् यथापूर्वमशङ्कितः॥
en: O tranquil soul and full of respect for his preceptor, Vipula respectfully saluted him and stood before him with a fearless heart.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: विश्रान्ताय ततस्तस्मै सहासीनाय भार्यया। निवेदयामास तदा विपुलः शक्रकर्म तत्॥
en: After his preceptor had rested a while and when he was seated with his wife on the same seat, Vipula told him everything that Shakra had done.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तच्छुत्वा स मुनिस्तुष्टो विपुलस्य प्रतापवान्। बभूव शीलवृत्ताभ्यां तपसा नियमेन च॥
en: Hearing these words of Vipula, that foremost of Munis, gifted with great prowess, became highly pleased with him for his conduct and disposition, his penances and his observances.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: वियुलस्य गुरौ वृत्तिं भक्तिमात्मनि तत्प्रभुः। धर्म च स्थिरतां दृष्ट्वा साधु साध्वित्यभाषत।॥
en: Observing Vipula's conduct towards himself his preceptor and his devotion also and marking his steadiness in virtue, the powerful Devasharman exclaimed-Excellent, excellent.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: प्रतिलभ्य च धर्मात्मा शिष्यं धर्मपरायणम्। वरेणच्छन्दयामास देवशर्मा महामतिः॥
en: The pious Devasharman receiving his virtuous disciple with a sincere welcome, honoured him with a boon.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: स्थितिं च धर्मे जग्राह स तस्माद् गुरुवत्सलः। अनुज्ञातश्च गुरुणा चचारानुत्तमं तपः॥
en: Indeed, Vipula, steady in virtue, obtained from his preceptor the boon that he would never swerve or fall away from virtue. Dismissed by his preceptor he left his house and practised the most severe austerities.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तथैव देवशर्मापि सभार्यः स महातपाः। निर्भयो बलवृत्रमाच्चचार विजने वने।॥
en: Devasharman also of severe penances, with his wife, began from that day to live in those solitary woods, perfectly fearless of him who had killed Vala and Vritra.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: भीष्म उवाच विपुलस्त्वकरोत् तीव्र तपः कृत्वा गुरोर्वचः। तपोयुक्तमथात्मानममन्यत स वीर्यवान्॥
en: Bhishma said Having satisfied his preceptor's command, Vipula practised the most severe penances. Gifted with great energy, he at last regarded himself as endued with sufficient ascetic merit.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: स तेन कर्मणा स्पर्धन् पृथिवीं पृथिवीपते। चचार गतभीः प्रीतो लब्धकीतिवरो नृप॥
en: Priding himself upon the feat he had performed, he he wandered fearlessly and contentedly over the Earth, O monarch, honoured by all as one possessed of great fame for what he had done.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: उभौ लोकौ जितौ चापि तथैवामन्यत प्रभुः। कर्मणा तेन कौरव्य तपसा विपुलेन च॥
en: The powerful Bhargava thought that he had conquered both the worlds by that feat of his as also by his severe penances.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: अथ काले व्यतिक्रान्ते कस्मिंश्चित् कुरुनन्दन। रुच्या भगिन्या आदान प्रभूतधनधान्यवत्॥
en: After sometime, O delighter of the Kurus, the time came for a ceremony of gifts to take place with respect to the sister of Ruchi. Profuse wealth and corn were to be given away in it.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु दिव्या काचिद् वराङ्गना। बिभ्रती परमं रूपं जगामाथ विहायसा॥
en: Meanwhile a certain celestial damsel, gifted with great beauty, was passing through the skies.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तस्याः शरीरात् पुष्पाणि पतितानि महीतले। तस्याश्रमस्याविदूरे दिव्यगन्धानि भारत॥
en: From her body as she passed through the sky, some flowers dropped down on the Earth. Those flowers of celestial fragrance fell on spot not far from the hermitage of Ruchi's husband.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तान्यगृह्णात् ततो राजन् रुचिर्ललितलोचना। तदा निमन्त्रकस्तस्या अङ्गेभ्यः क्षिप्रमागमत्॥
en: As the flowers lay scattered on the ground, they were picked up by Ruchi of beautiful eyes. Soon after an invitation came to Ruchi from the country of the Angas.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तस्या हि भगिनी तात ज्येष्ठा नाम्ना प्रभावती। भार्या चित्ररथस्याथ बभूवाङ्गेश्वरस्य वै॥
en: The sister, referred to above, of Ruchi, named Prabhavati was the wife of Chitraratha the king of the Angas.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: पिनह्य तानि पुष्पाणि केशेषु वरर्णिनी। आमन्त्रिता ततोऽगच्छद् रुचिरङ्गपतेर्गृहम्॥
en: Ruchi, of great beauty, having attached those flowers to her hair, went to the palace of the king of the Angas to answer the invitation she had received,

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: पुष्पाणि तानि दृष्ट्वा तु तदाङ्गेन्द्रवराङ्गना। भगिनी चोदयामास पुष्पार्थे चारुलोचना॥
en: Seeing those flowers on her hair, the queen of the Angas having beautiful eyes, urged her sister to obtain some for her.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: सा भत्रे सर्वमाचष्ट रुचिः सुरुचिरानना। भगिन्या भाषितं सर्वमृषिस्तच्चाभ्यनन्दत॥
en: Ruchi of beautiful face, speedily informed her husband of that request of her sister. The Rishi accepted the prayer of his sisterinlaw.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: ततो विपुलमानाय्य देवशर्मा महातपाः। पुष्पार्थे चोदयामास गच्छ गच्छेति भारत॥
en: Summoning Vipula into his presence, Devasharman of severe penances commanded his disciple to bring him some flowers of the same sort, saying Go, go.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: विपुलस्तु गुरोर्वाक्यमविचार्य महातपाः। स तथेत्यब्रवीद् राजंस्तं च देशं जगाम ह॥
en: Accepting unhesitatingly the order of his preceptor, the great ascetic Vipula. O king, answered So be it! and then proceeded to that spot whence the lady Ruchi had picked up the flowers that were wanted by her sister.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: यस्मिन् देशे तु तान्यासन् पतितानि नभस्तलात्। अम्लानान्यपि तत्रासन् कुसुमान्यपराण्यपि॥
en: Arrived at that place where the flowers had fallen from the sky, Vipula saw some others still lying scattered. They were all as fresh as if they had been newly plucked from the plants. None of them had faded away.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: स ततस्तानि जग्राह दिव्यानि रुचिराणि च। प्राप्तानि स्वेन तापसा दिव्यगन्धानि भारत॥
en: He took up those exquisitely beautiful celestial flowers. Possessed of celestial fragrance, O Bharata, Vipula got them there as the result of his severe penances.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: सम्प्राप्य तानि प्रीतात्मा गुरोर्वचनकारकः। तदा जगाम तूर्णं च चम्पां चम्पकमालिनीम्॥
en: The accomplisher of his his preceptor's command, having obtained them, he felt great delight and started quickly for the city of Champa adorned with festoons of Champaka flowers.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: स वने निर्जने तात ददर्श मिथुनं नृणाम्। चक्रवत् परिवर्तन्तं गृहीत्वा पाणिना करम्॥
en: As he went on, he saw on his way a human couple moving in a circle hand in hand.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तत्रैकस्तूर्णमगमत् तत्पदे च विवर्तयन्। एकस्तु न तदा राजश्चक्रतुः कलहं ततः॥
en: One of them made a rapid step and thereby destroyed the cadence of the movement. Therefore, O king, a dispute arose between them.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: त्वं शीघ्रं गच्छसीत्येकोऽब्रवीन्नेति तथा परः। नेति नेति च तौ राजन् परस्परमथोचतुः॥
en: Indeed, one of them charged the other, saying You have taken a quicker step! The other answered No, Indeed, as each held his own opinion obstinately, each. O king asserted what the other denied, and denied what the other asserted.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तयोर्विस्पर्धतोरेवं शपथोऽयमभूत् तदा। सहसोद्दिश्य विपलुं ततो वाक्यमथोचतुः॥
en: While thus quarrelling with each other with great assurance, an oath was then heard among them. Indeed, each of them suddenly named Vipula in what they uttered.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: आवयोरनृतं प्राह यस्तस्याभूद् द्विजस्य वै। विपुलस्य परे लोके या गतिः सा भवेदिति॥
en: Their oath was this That one among us two who speaks falsely, shall, in the next world, meet with the end which will be the twiceborn Vipula's.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु विपुलो विषण्णवदनोऽभवत्। एवं तीव्रतापाश्चाहं कष्टश्चायं परिश्रमः॥ मिथुनस्यास्य किं मे स्यात् कृतं पापं यथा गतिः। अनिष्टा सर्वभूतानां कीर्तितानेन मेऽद्य वै॥
en: Hearing these words of theirs, Vipula's face became very sad. He began to commune with himself, I have practised severe penances. The dispute between this couple is hot. To me, again, it is painful. What sin have I committed that both these persons should refer to my end in the next world as the most painful one among those reserved for all creatures?

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: एवं संचिन्तयन्नेव विपुलो राजसत्तम। अवाङ्मुखो दीनमना दध्यौ दुष्कृतमात्मनः॥
en: Thinking thus, Vipula, O best of kings, hung down his head, and with a dispirited mind began to recollect what sin he had done.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: ततः षडन्यान् पुरुषानक्षैः काञ्चनराजतैः। अपश्यद् दीव्यमानान् वै लोभहर्षान्वितांस्तथा॥ कुर्वतः शपथं तेन यः कृतो मिथुनेन तु। विपुलं वै समुद्दिश्य तेऽपि वाक्यमथाब्रुवन्॥
en: Proceeding a little way he saw six other men playing with dice made of gold and silver. Engaged in play, those individuals seerned to him to be so excited that the hairs on their bodies stood erect. They also were heard by Vipula to take the same oath that he had already heard the first couple to take. Indeed, their words had reference in the same way to Vipula.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: लोभमास्थाय योऽस्माकं विषमं कर्तुमुत्सहेत्। विपुलस्य परे लोके या गतिस्तामवाप्नुयात्॥
en: He, amongst us who, led by cupidity, will act in an unfair way, shall meet with that end which is reserved for Vipula in the next world.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: एतच्छुत्वा तु विपुलो नापश्यद् धर्मसंकरम्। जन्मप्रभृति कौरव्य कृतपूर्वमथात्मनः॥
en: Hearing these words, however, Vipula, although he tried earnestly to recollect, could not remember any sin of his from even his earliest years, O you of Kuru's race.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: सम्प्रदध्यौ तथा राजन्नग्नावग्निरिवाहितः। दह्यमानेन मनसा शापं श्रुत्वा तथाविधम्॥
en: Indeed, he began to burn like a fire placed in the midst of another fire. Hearing that curse, his mind burnt with grief.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तस्य चिन्तयतस्तात बढ्यो दिननिशा ययुः। इदमासीन्मनसि स रुच्या रक्षणकारितम्॥
en: In this state of anxiety a long time was passed. At last he recollected the manner in which he had acted in protecting his preceptor's wife from the machinations of Indra.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: लक्षणं लक्षणेनैव वदनं वदनेन च। विधाय न मया चोक्तं सत्यमेतद् गुरोस्तथा॥
en: I had entered the body of that lady, placing limb within limb, face within face. Although I had acted in this way, I did not yet tell my preceptor the truth.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: एतदात्मनि कौरव्य दुष्कृतं विपुलस्तदा। अमन्यत महाभाग तथा तच्च न संशयः॥
en: This was the sin, O you of Kuru's race, which Vipula recollected in himself. Indeed, O blessed king, forsooth, that was the sin which he had actually committed.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: स चम्पां नगरीमेत्य पुष्पाणि गुरवे ददौ। पूजयामास च गुरुं विधिवत् स गुरुप्रियः॥
en: Coming to the city of Champa, he gave the flowers to his preceptor. Devoted to superiors and seniors, he adored his preceptor in due form.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: भीष्म उवाच तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य शिष्यं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्। देवशर्मा महातेजा यत् तच्छृणु जनाधिप॥
en: Bhishma said Seeing his disciple returned from his mission, Devasharman of great energy addressed him in words which I shall recite to you, O king.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: देवशर्मन् उवाच किं ते विपुल दृष्टं वै तस्मिन् शिष्य महावने। ते त्वां जानन्ति विपुल आत्मा च रुचिरेव च॥
en: Devasharman said What have you seen, O Vipula, in course of your journey. O disciple, through the great forest? Then whom you have seen knew, you, O Vipula. I, as also my wife Ruchi, know how you had acted in the matter of protecting Ruchi.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: विपुल उवाच ब्रह्मर्षे मिथुनं किं तत् के च ते पुरुषा विभो। ये मां जानन्ति तत्त्वेन यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि।॥
en: Vipula said O twiceborn Rishi, who are those two whom I first saw? Who also are those other six whom I saw afterwards? All of them know me. Who indeed, are they to whom you prefer in your speech to me?

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: देवशर्मन् उवाच यद् वै तन्मिथुनं ब्रह्मन्नहोरात्रं हि विद्धि तत्। चक्रवत् परिवर्तेत तत् ते जानाति दुष्कृतम्॥
en: Devasharman said The first couple, O twiceborn one, whom you saw, are, Day and Night. They are ceaselessly moving like a circle. Both of them know the sin you have committed.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: ये च ते पुरुषा विप्र अक्षैर्दीव्यन्ति हृष्टवत्। ऋतूंस्तानभिजानीहि ते ते जानन्ति दुष्कृतम्॥
en: Those other men (six in number) whom, O learned Brahmana, you saw playing cheerfully at dice, are the six Seasons. They also are acquainted with your sins.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: न मां कश्चिद् विजानीत इति कृत्वा न विश्वसेत्। नरो रहसि पापात्मा पापकं कर्म वै द्विज॥
en: Having committed a sin secretly, no sinful man should cherish the assuring thought that his sin is known only to himself and not to any one else.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: कुर्वाणं हि नरं कर्म पापं रहसि सर्वदा। पश्यन्ति ऋतवश्चापि तथा दिननिशेऽप्युत॥
en: When a man commits a sinful deed in secret, the Seasons as also Day and Night see it always.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तथैव हि भवेयुस्ते लोकाः पापकृतो यथा। कृत्वा नाचक्षतः कर्म मम तच्च यथाकृतम्॥
en: Those regions that are reserved for the sinful shall be yours. What you had done, you did not tell me. That your sin was not known to any one, was your belief, and this conviction had filled you with joy.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: ते त्वां हर्षस्मितं दृष्ट्वा गुरोः कर्मानिवेदकम्। स्मारयन्तस्तथा प्राहुस्ते यथा श्रुतवान् भवान्॥
en: You did not inform your preceptor of the whole truth, choosing to hide from him a substantial portion. The Seasons, and Day and Night whom you have heard speak thus, thought it proper to remind you of your sin.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: अहोरात्रं विजानाति ऋतवश्चापि नित्यशः। पुरुषे पापकं कर्म शुभं वा शुभकर्मिणः॥
en: Day and Night and the Seasons, do know all the good and the bad deeds, that are in a man.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तत् त्वया मम यत् कर्म व्यभिचाराद् भयात्मकम्। नाख्यातमिति जानन्तस्ते त्वामाहुस्तथा द्विज॥
en: They spoke to you in that way, O twice born one, because they have full knowledge of what you had done but which you had not the courage to inform me of, fearing you had done wrong.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तेनैव हि भवेयुस्ते लोकाः पापकृतो यथा। कृत्वा नाचक्षत: कर्म मम यच्च त्वया कृतम्॥
en: For this reason you will visit the regions that are reserved for the sinful. You did not tell me what you had done.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: त्वयाशक्या च दुर्वृत्त्या रक्षितुं प्रमदा द्विजा न च त्वं कृतवान् किंचिदतः प्रीतोऽस्मि तेन ते॥
en: You were fully capable, O twiceborn one, of protecting my wife whose disposition, by nature is sinful. In doing what you did, you did not commit any sin I was for this, pleased with you.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: यदि त्वहं त्वां दुर्वृत्तमद्राक्षं द्विजसत्तम। शपेयं त्वामहं क्रोधान्न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा॥
en: O best of Brahmanas, if I had known you to have acted wickedly, I would, without hesitation, have cursed you entirely.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: सज्जन्ति पुरुषे नार्य:पुंसां सोऽर्थश्च पुष्कलः। अन्यथारक्षतः शापोऽभविष्यत् ते मतिश्च मे॥
en: Women become united with men, Such union, is very desirable with men. You had, however, protected my wife in a different spirit. If you had acted otherwise, I would have cursed. Even this is what I think.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: रक्षिता च त्वया पुत्र मम चापि निवेदिता। अहं ते प्रीतिमांस्तात स्वस्थः स्वर्गं गमिष्यसि॥
en: You had, O son, protected my wife I have known the manner in which you had done it as if you had yourself informed me of it. I have,O son, become pleased with you. Relieved of all anxiety, you shall go to heaven.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: इत्युक्त्वा विपुलं प्रीतो देवशर्मा महानृषिः। मुमोद स्वर्गमास्थाय सहभार्यः सशिष्यकः॥
en: Having said these words to Vipula, the great Rishi Devasharman, ascended to Heaven with his wife and his disciple and began to pass his time there in great happiness.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: इदमाख्यातवांश्चापि ममाख्यानं महामुनिः। मार्कण्डेयः पुरा राजन् गङ्गाकूले कथान्तरे॥
en: In course of conversation, o king, on a former occasion, the great ascetic Markandeya had described to me this history on the banks of Ganga.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: तस्माद् ब्रवीमि पार्थ त्वां स्त्रियो रक्ष्याः सदैव च। उभयं दृश्यते तासु सततं साध्वसाधु च॥
en: I therefore, recite it to you. Women should always be protected by you. Amongst them both kinds are to be seen, that is those who are virtuous and those who are not so.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: स्त्रियः साध्व्यो महाभागाः सम्मता लोकमातरः। धारयन्ति महीं राजन्निमां सवनकाननाम्॥
en: The virtuous women are highly blessed. They are the mothers of the universe. They, it is, o king, that keep up the Earth with all her waters and forests.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: असाध्व्यश्चापि दुर्वृत्ताः कुलनाः पापनिश्चयाः। विज्ञेया लक्षणैर्दुष्टैः स्वगात्रसहजैर्नृप॥
en: Those women who are sinful, who are of wicked conduct, who are the destroyer of their race, and who are wedded to sinful purposes, are capable of being ascertained by marks, expressive of the evil that is in them, which appear, O king, on their persons.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: एवमेतासु रक्षा वै शक्या कर्तुं महात्मभिः। अन्यथा राजशार्दूल न शक्या रक्षितुं स्त्रियः॥
en: It is thus that great persons are capable of protecting women. They cannot, O foremost of kings, be protected in any other way.

description: The creation of woman and the object thereof. The story of Vipula and Devasharman
sn: एता हि मनुजव्याघ्र तीक्ष्णास्तीक्ष्णपराक्रमाः। नासामस्ति प्रियो नाम मैथुने सङ्गमेति यः॥
en: Women, O king are fierce. They are gifted with fierce prowess. They have none whom they love or like, so much as them that have sexual intercourse with them.
