en: As the cub of a tiger resembles its father and dam in form and in stripes or spots, so a person cannot but show the circumstance of his origin.

description: The duties of persons born in mixed castes
sn: कुले स्रोतसि संच्छन्ने यस्य स्याद् योनिसंकरः। संश्रयत्येव तच्छीलं नरोऽल्पमथवा बहु॥
en: However secret may one's birth be, if that birth happens to be impure, its character or nature is sure to show itself slightly or largely.

description: The duties of persons born in mixed castes
sn: आर्यरूपसमाचारं चरन्तं कृतके पथि। सुवर्णमन्यवर्णं वा स्वशीलं शास्ति निश्चये॥
en: A person may for purposes of his own, choose to follow an insincere path, practising such conduct as seems to be pious. His own nature, however, in the matter of those acts that he does, always announces whether he belongs to a good caste or to a different one.

description: The duties of persons born in mixed castes
sn: नानावृत्तेषु भूतेषु नानाकर्मरतेषु च। जन्मवृत्तसमं लोके सुश्लिष्टं न विरज्यते॥
en: Creatures in the world are gifted with various kinds of disposition. They are, again, seen to be employed in various kinds of acts. Amongst creatures thus engaged, there is nothing that is so good or valuable as pure birth and righteous conduct.

description: The duties of persons born in mixed castes
sn: शरीरमिह सत्त्वेन न तस्य परिकृष्यते। ज्येष्ठमध्यावरं सत्त्वं तुल्यसत्त्वं प्रमोदते॥
en: If a person be born in a low caste, good understanding originating from a study of the scriptures fails to rescue his body from low acts. Absolute goodness of understanding is of different degrees. It may be high, middling, and low. Even if it appears in a person of low birth, it disappears like autumnal clouds without producing any result. On the other hand, goodness of understanding which, according to its measure, has ordained the position in which the person is born, shows itself in his deeds.

description: The duties of persons born in mixed castes
sn: ज्यायांसमपि शीलेन विहीनं नैव पूजयेत्। अपि शूद्रं च धर्मज्ञं सद्वृत्तभिपूजयेत्॥
en: If a person happens to belong to a superior caste but still if he happens to be divested of good conduct, he should receive no respect or worship. One may adore even a Shudra if he knows his duties and is of good conduct.

description: The duties of persons born in mixed castes
sn: आत्मानमाख्याति हि कर्मभिर्नरः सुशीलचारित्रकुलैः शुभाशुभैः। प्रणष्टमप्याशु कुलं तथा नरः पुनः प्रकाशं कुरुते स्वकर्मतः॥
en: A person proclaims himself by his own good and bad deeds and by his good or bad nature and race of birth. If ones' race of birth happens to be degraded for any reason, one soon raises it and makes it resplendent and famous by his deeds.

description: The duties of persons born in mixed castes
sn: योनिष्वेतासु सर्वासु संकीर्णास्वितरासु च। यत्रात्मानं न जनयेद् बुधस्तां परिवर्जयेत्॥
en: For these reasons the wise should avoid those women among these various castes mixed, upon whom they should not beget children.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्रूहि तात कुरुश्रेष्ठ वर्णानां त्वं पृथक् पृथक। कीदृश्यां कीदृशाश्चापि पुत्राः कस्य च के च ते॥
en: Yudhishthira said Describe to us, O sire, the orders and classes separately, what kind of son is begotten on what women, who is entitled to have whom for sons, and what kinds of sons are there.

sn: विप्रवादाः सुबहवः श्रूयन्ते पुत्रकारिताः। अत्र नो मुह्यतां राजन् संशयं छेत्तुमर्हसि॥
en: It is known that disputes frequently take place about sons. You should, O king, remove the doubts of our mind. Indeed, we are stupefied about this subject.

sn: भीष्म उवाच आत्मा पुत्रश्च विज्ञेयस्तस्यानन्तराश्च यः। निरुक्तजश्च विज्ञेयः सुतः प्रसृतजस्तथा॥
en: Bhishma said One's own begotten son considered as his own self. The son that is begotten upon one's wife by a person whom he has invited for it, if called Niruktaja. The son that is begotten upon one's wife by somebody without his permission, is Prasritaja.

sn: पतितस्य तु भार्याया भर्ना सुसमवेतया। तथा दत्तकृतौ पुत्रावध्यूढच तथापरः॥
en: The son begotten upon his own wife by a person degraded from his positions is called Patitaja. There are two other, sons, viz., the son given, and the son made. There is another called Adhyuda.

sn: षडपध्वंसजाश्चापि कानीनापसदास्तथा। इत्येते वै समाख्यातास्तान् विजानीहि भारत॥
en: The son born of a maiden in her father's house is called Kanina. Besides these, there are six kinds of sons called Apadhwansaja and six others that are called Apasadas. These are the several kind of sons mentioned in the scriptures, know, O Bharata. are

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच षडपध्वंसजाः के स्युः के वाप्यपसदास्तथा। एतत् सर्वं यथातत्त्वं व्याख्यातुं मे त्वमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said Who the six that are called Apadhvansaja? Who also are the Apasadas? You should fully explain all this to me.

sn: भीष्म उवाच त्रिषु वर्णेषु ये पुत्रा ब्राह्मणस्य युधिष्ठिर। वर्णयोश्च द्वयोः स्यातां यौ राजन्यस्य भारत।॥ एको विड्वर्ण एवाथ तथात्रैवोपलक्षितः। घडपध्वंसजास्ते हि तथैवासपदाशृणु॥
en: Bhishma said The sons that a Brahmana begets upon wives taken from the three inferior castes, those begotten by a Kshatriya upon wives taken from the two castes inferior to his own, O Bharata, and the sons that a Vaishya begets upon a wife taken from the one caste that is inferior to his,-are all called Apadhvansas. ! They are, as thus explained, of six kinds. Listen now to me as I tell you who the Apasadas are.

sn: चाण्डालो व्रात्यवैद्यौ च ब्राह्मण्यां क्षत्रियासु च। वैश्यायां चैव शूद्रस्य लक्ष्यन्तेऽपसदास्त्रयः॥
en: The son that a Shudra begets upon a Brahmani woman is called a Chandala. Begotten upon a Kshatriya woman by a person of the Shudra order, the son is called a Vratye.। He who is born of a Vaishya woman by a Shudra father is called a Vaidya. These three kinds of sons are called Apasada.

sn: मागधो वामकश्चैव द्वौ वैश्यस्पोलक्षितौ। ब्राह्मण्यां क्षत्रियायां च क्षत्रियस्यैक एव तु॥
en: The Vaishya, by knowing a woman of the Brahmana order, begets a son that is called a Magadha, while the son that he begets upon a Kshatriya woman is called a Vamaka, The। Kshatriya can beget but one kind of son of upon a woman of a superior caste.

sn: ब्राह्मण्यां लक्ष्यते सूत इत्येतेऽपसदाः स्मृताः। पुत्रा ह्येते न शक्यन्ते मिथ्याकर्तुं नराधिप॥
en: Indeed, the son begotten by a Kshatriya upon a Brahmana woman, is called a Suta. These three also are called Apasadas. It cannot be said, O king, that these six kinds of sons are no sons.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच क्षेत्र केचिदेवाहुः सुतं केचित्तु शुक्रजम्। तुल्यावेतौ सुतौ कस्य तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Some say that one's son is he, who is born in his soil. Some, on the other hand, say that one's son is he who has been begotten from his seed. Are both these kinds of sons equal? Whose, again, is the son to be? Do you tell me, this, O grandfather.

sn: भीष्म उवाच रेतजो वा भवेत् पुत्रस्त्यक्तो वा क्षेत्रजो भवेत्। अध्यूढः समयं भित्त्वेत्येतदेव निबोध मे॥
en: Bhishma said His is the son from whose seed he has sprung. If, however, the owner of the seed discards the son born of it, such son then becomes his upon whose wife he has been begotten. The same rule applies to the son called Adhyuda. He belongs to the person from whose seed he has sprung. If, however, the owner of the seed forsakes him, he becomes the son of the husband of his mother. Know this is what the law declares.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच रेतजं विद्य वै पुत्रं क्षेत्रजस्यागमः कथम्। अध्यूढं विद्म वै पुत्रं भित्त्वा तु समयं कथम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said We know that the son becomes his from whose seed he has taken birth. Whence does the husband of the woman who gives birth to the son derive his right to the latter? Likewise the son called Adhyuda should be known to be the son of him from whose seed he has sprung. How can they be the sons of others on account of the engagement about owning and rearing them having been broken?

sn: भीष्म उवाच आत्मजं पुत्रमुत्पाद्य यस्त्यजेत् कारणान्तरे। न तत्र कारणं रेतः स क्षेत्रस्वामिनो भवेत्॥
en: Bhishma said Fie who, having begotten a son of his own loins: forsakes him for some reason or other, cannot be considered as the father of such son, for vital seed only cannot create sonship. Such son must be held to belong to the person who is the master of the soil.

sn: पुत्रकामो हि पुत्रार्थं यां वृणीते विशाम्पते। क्षेत्रजं तु प्रमाणं स्यान्न वै तत्रात्मजः सुतः॥
en: When a man, desiring to have a son, marries a girl quick with child, the son born of his wife must belong to him, for it is the fruit of his own soil. The person from whose vital seed the son has sprung, can have no right to such son.

sn: अन्यत्र क्षेत्रजः पुत्रो लक्ष्यते भरतर्षभ। न ह्यात्मा शक्यते हन्तुं दृष्टान्तोपगतो ह्यसौ॥
en: The son who is born in one's soil but not begotten by the owner, O chief of Bharata's race, bears all the marks of the father that has actually begotten him. The son thus born is incapable of concealing the evidences of physiognomy. He is at He is at once known by eyesight.

sn: क्वचिच्च कृतकः पुत्रः संग्रहादेव लक्ष्यते। न तत्र रेतः क्षेत्रं वा यत्र लक्ष्येत भारत॥
en: As regards the son made, he is sometimes considered as the child of the person who has made him a son and who brings him up. In his case, neither the vital seed of which he has been born nor the soil in which he has been born, becomes the cause of sonship.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कीदृशः कृतकः पुत्रः संग्रहादेव लक्ष्यते। शुक्रं क्षेत्रं प्रमाणं वा यत्र लक्ष्यं न भारत॥
en: Yudhishthira said What kind of son is that who is said to be a made son and whose sonship originates from the fact of his being taken and reared, and in whose case neither the vital seed nor the soil of birth, O Bharata, is caused as the cause of sonship.

sn: भीष्म उवाच मातापितृभ्यां यस्त्यक्तः पथि यस्तं प्रकल्पयेत्। न चास्य मातापितरौ ज्ञायेतां स हि कृत्रिमः॥
en: Bhishnia said When one takes up and rears a son who has been cast off on the road by his father and mother, and when the person thus taking and rearing him cannot find out his parents after search, he becomes the father of such son and the latter becomes what is called his made son.

sn: अस्वामिकस्य स्वामित्वं यस्मिन् सम्प्रति लक्ष्यते। यो वर्ण: पोषयेत् तं च तद्वर्णस्तस्य जायते॥
en: Not having anybody to own him, he becomes his who rcars hiin. Such son, again, comes to be considered as belonging to that castes to which his owner or rearer belongs.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथमस्य प्रयोक्तव्यः संस्कारः कस्य वा कथम्। देया कन्या कथं चेति तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said How should the purifactory rites of such a person be performed? In whose case that sort of rites are to be performed? With what girl should he be married? Tell me all this, O grandfather.

sn: भीष्म उवाच आत्मवत् तस्य कुर्वीत संस्कारं स्वामिवत् तथा। त्यक्तो मातापितृभ्यां यः सवर्ण प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Bhishma said The rites of purification for such a son should be performed according to the usage of the person himself who rears him, for, renounced by his parents, such son gets the caste of the person who takes him and rears him.

sn: तद्गोत्रबन्धुजं तस्य कुर्यात् संस्कारमच्युत। अथ देया तु कन्या स्यात् तद्वर्णस्य युधिष्ठिर।॥
en: Indeed, O you of unfading glory, the rearer should perform all the purificatory rites for such son according to the practices of his own family and kinsmen. As regards the girl also, O Yudhishthira, that should be bestowed in marriage upon such a son, she should belong to the caste of the rearer himself.

sn: संस्कर्तुं वर्गगोत्रं च मातृवर्णविनिश्चये। कानीनाध्यूढजौ वापि विज्ञेयौ पुत्र किल्बिषौ॥
en: All this is to be done only when the caste of the son's true mother cannot be learnt. Among sons, he who is born of a maiden and he who is born of a mother who had conceived before her marriage but brought nim forth subsequent to that act, are considered as very disgraceful and degraded.

sn: तावपि स्वाविव सुतौ संस्कार्याविति निश्चयः। श्रेत्रजो वाप्यपसदो येऽध्यूढास्तेषु चाप्युत॥ आत्मवद् वै प्रयुञ्जीरन् संस्कारान् ब्राह्मणादयः। धर्मशास्त्रेषु वर्णानां निश्चयोऽयं प्रदृश्यते॥ एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: Even these two, however, should receive the same rites of purification that sanctioned for the sons begotten by the father in lawful marriage. In respect of the son who becomes his fathers on account of his birth in the father's soil, and of those sons who are called Apsadas, and those conceived by the wife in her maidenhood but brought forth after marriage, Brahmanas and others should apply the same rites of purification that are in vogue in their own castes. These are the conclusions that are seen in the scriptures about the different castes. I have thus told you everything of your questions. What else do you wish to hear?

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दर्शने कीदृशः स्नेहः संवासे च पितामह। महाभाग्यं गवां चैव तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said What is the nature of the compassion or pity that is felt at seeing the misery of another? What is the nature of that compassion or sympathy that one feels for another on account of his living in the companionship of that other? What is the nature of the supreme blessedness of kine? You should, O grandfather explain all this to me.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: भीष्म उवाच हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि पुरावृत्तं महाद्युते। नहुषस्य च संवादं महर्षेश्च्यवनस्य च॥
en: Bhishma said I shall, O you of great effulgence, recite to you in this connection an ancient narrative of a conversation between Nahusha and the Rishi Chyavana.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: पुरा महर्षिश्च्यवनो भार्गवो भरतर्षभ। उदावासकृतारम्भो बभूव स महाव्रतः॥
en: Formerly, O chief of Bharata's race, the great Rishi Chyavana of Bhrigu's race, always practising high vows, became desirous of leading for sometime the mode of life called Udavasa, and sed himself to commence it.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: निहत्य मानं क्रोधं च प्रहर्षं शोकमेव च। वर्षाणि द्वादश मुनिर्जलवासे धृतव्रतः॥
en: Renouncing pride, anger, joy and grief, the ascetic, pledging himself to observe that vow, set himself to live for twelve years, according to the rules of Udavasa.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: आदधत् सर्वभूतेषु विश्रम्भं परमं शुभम्। जलेचरेषु सर्वेषु शीतरश्मिरिव प्रभुः॥
en: The Rishi inspired all creatures with trust. And he inspired similar confidence in all creatures living in water. The powerful ascetic resembled the Moon himself in his conduct to all.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: स्थाणुभूतः शुचिर्भूत्वा दैवतेभ्यः प्रणम्य च। गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये जलं सम्प्रविवेश ह॥
en: Bowing to all the deities and having purged himself of all sins, he entered the water at the confluence of Ganga and Yamuna, and stood there like an inanimate post of wood.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: गङ्गायमुनयोर्वेगं सुभीमं भीमनिःस्वनम्। प्रतिजग्राह शिरसा वातवेगसमं जवे॥
en: Placing his head against it, he bore the fierce and roaring current of the two rivers united together,—the current whose speed resembled that of the wind itself.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: गङ्गे च यमुने चैव सरितश्च सरांसि च। प्रदक्षिणमृर्षि चक्रुर्न औनं पर्यपीडयन्॥
en: Ganga and Yamuna, however, and the other rivers and lakes, whose waters unite together at the confluence at Prayaga, instead of afflicting the Rishi, went beyond him.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: अन्तर्जलेषु सुष्वाप काष्ठभूतो महामुनिः। ततश्चोर्ध्वस्थितो धीमानभवद् भरतर्षभ॥
en: Assuming the attitude of a wooden post, the great Muni sometimes laid himself down in the water and slept at ease. And sometimes, O chief of Bharata's race the intelligent sage stood erect.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: जलौकसां स सत्त्वानां बभूव प्रियदर्शनः। उपाजिघ्रन्त च तदा तस्योष्ठं हृष्टमानसाः॥
en: He became quite agreeable to all creatures living in water. Without the least fear, all these used to smell the Rishi's lips.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: तत्र तस्यासतः कालः समतीतोऽभवन्महान्। ततः कदाचित् समये कस्मिंश्चिन्मत्स्यजीविनः॥
en: In this way, the Rishi passed a long time at that grand confluence of waters. One day, some fishermen came there.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: तं देशं समुपाजग्मुर्जालहस्ता महाद्युते। निषादा बहवस्तत्र मत्स्योद्धरणनिश्चयाः॥
en: With nets in their hands, O you of great effuigence, those men came where the Rishi was. They were many in number and all of them were bent upon catching fish.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: व्यायता बलिनः शूराः सलिलेष्वनिवर्तिनः। अभ्याययुश्च तं देशं निश्चिता जालकर्मणि॥
en: Well-formed and broadchested, gifted with great strength and courage, and never returning in fear from water, those men who lived upon the earning by their nets, came there, resolved to catch fish.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: जालं ते योजयामासुनिःशेषेण जनाधिप। मत्स्योदकं समासाद्य तदा भरतसत्तम॥
en: Arrived at that water which, contained many fish, those fishermen, O chief of the Bharatas, tied all their nets together.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: ततस्ते बहुभिर्योगैः कैवर्ता मत्स्यकाक्षिणः। गङ्गायमुनयोर्वारि जालैरभ्यकिरंस्ततः॥
en: Desirous of fish, of fish, those innumerable Kaivartas, united together and surrounded a portion of the waters of Ganga and Yamuna with their nets.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: जालं सुविततं तेषां नवसूत्रकृतं तथा। विस्तारायामसम्पन्नं यत् तत्र सलिलेऽक्षिपन्॥
en: Indeed, they threw upon the water their net which was made of new strings, capable of covering a large space, and having sufficient length and breadth.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: ततस्ते सुमहच्चैव बलवच्च सुवर्तितम्। अवतीर्य ततः सर्वे जालं चकृषिरे तदा॥
en: Getting down into the water, all of them began to drag with great force that net which was very large and had been wellspread over a large space.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: अभीतरूपाः मंहृष्टा अन्योन्यवशवर्तिनः। बबन्धुस्तत्र मत्स्यांश्च तथान्यान् जलचारिणः॥
en: All of them were free from fear, cheerful, and fully determined to do one another's bidding. They had succeeded in catching a large number of fish and other aquatic animals.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: तथा मत्स्यैः परिवृतं च्यवनं भृगुनन्दनम्। आकर्षयन्महाराज जालेनाथ चदृच्छया॥
en: And as they dragged their net, o king, they easily dragged up Chyavana the son of Bhrigu, along with a large number of fish.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: नदीशैवलदिग्धाङ्गं हरिश्मश्रुजटाधरम्। लग्नैः शङ्खनखैर्गात्रे क्रोडैश्चित्रैरिवार्पितम्॥
en: His body was overgrown with the rivermoss. His beard and matted locks had become green. And all over his body could be seen conchs and other mollusca attached with their heads.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: तं जालेनोद्धृतं दृष्ट्वा ते तदा वेदपारगम्। सर्वे प्राञ्जलयो दाशा: शिरोभिः प्रापतन् भूवि॥
en: Seeing that Rishi who was a master of the Vedas dragged up by them from the water, all the fishermen stood with joined hands and then laid themselves low on the ground and repeatedly bent their heads.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: परिखेदपरित्रासाज्जालस्याकर्षणेन च। मत्स्या बभूवुफ्पन्नाः स्थलसंस्पर्शनेन च॥
en: Through fear and pain caused by the dragging to the net, and on account of their being brought upon the land, the fishes caught in the net died.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: स मुनिस्तत् तदा दृष्ट्वा मत्स्यानां कदनं कृतम्। नभूव कृपयाविष्टो निःश्वसंश्च पुनः पुनः॥
en: Seeing that great onslaught of fishes, the ascetic became filled with compassion and sighed repeatedly.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: मत्स्य पुरुष उवाच अज्ञानाद् यत् कृतं पापं प्रसादं तत्र नः कुरु। करवाम प्रियं किं ते तन्नो ब्रूहि महामुने॥
en: The fishermen said We have perpetrated this sin unwillingly. Be pleased with us! What wish of yours shall we fulfil? Command us, ogreat ascetic.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तो मत्स्यमध्यस्थश्च्यवनो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। यो मेऽद्य परमः कामस्तं शृणुध्वं समाहिताः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by them, Chyavana, from among that mass of fishes around him, said Do you with rapt attention hear what my most cherished wish is.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: प्राणोत्सर्ग विसर्ग वा मत्स्यैर्यास्यामम्यहं सह। संवासान्नोत्सहे त्यक्तुं सलिलेऽध्युषितानाहम्॥
en: I shall either die with these fishes or do ye sell me with them. I have lived with them for a long time within the water. I do not wish to leave them at such a time!

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: इत्युक्तास्ते निषादास्तु सुभृशं भयकम्पिताः। सर्वे विवर्णवदना नहुषाय न्यवेदयन्॥
en: When he said these words to them, the fishermen became greatly terrified. With pale faces they went to king Nahusha and informed him of all that had occurred.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: भीष्म उवाच नहुषस्तु ततः श्रुत्वा च्यवनं तं तथागतम्। वरितः प्रययौ तत्र सहामात्यपुरोहितः॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing the strait into which Chyavana was reduced, King Nahusha speedily went there, accompanied by his ministers and priest.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: शौचं कृत्वा यथान्यायं प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतो नृपः। आत्मानमाचचक्षे च च्यवनाय महात्मने॥
en: Having purified himself duly, the king, with joined hands and rapt attention, introduced himself to the great Chyavana.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: अर्चयामास तं चापि तस्य राज्ञः पुरोहितः। सत्यव्रतं महात्मानं देवकल्पं विशाम्पते॥
en: The king's priest then adored with due ceremonies that Rishi, O king, who was observant of the vow of truth and gifted with a great soul, and who resembled a god himself.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: नहुष उवाच करवाणि प्रियं किं ते तन्मे ब्रूहि द्विजोत्तम। सर्वं कर्तास्मि भगवान् यद्यपि स्यात् सुदुष्करम्॥
en: Nahusha said Tell, me, O best of twiceborn ones, what act shall we do that may be pleasing to you? However difficult that deed may be, there is nothing, O holy one, that I shall not be able to do at your command.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: च्यवन उवाच श्रमेण महता युक्ताः कैवर्ता मत्स्यजीविनः। मम मूल्यं प्रयच्छेभ्यो मत्स्यानां विक्रयैः सह॥
en: Chyavana said These men who live by catching fish, have all been exhausted with fatigue. Do you pay them the price that may be fixed upon me along with value of these fish.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: हुष उवाच सहस्रं दीयतां मूल्यं निषादेभ्यः पुरोहित। निष्क्रयार्थे भगवतो यथाऽऽह भृगुनन्दनः॥
en: Nahusha said Let my priest give to these Nishadas a thousand coins as price for buying this sacred one as he himself has ordered.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: च्यवन उवाच सहस्रं नाहमर्हामि किं वा त्वं मन्यसे नृप। सदृशं दीयतां मूल्यं स्वबुद्ध्या निश्चयं कुरु॥
en: Chyavana said A thousand coins is not my price. The question depends upon your discretion. Give them a fair price, setting with your discretion. Give them a fair price, settling with your own intelligence what it should be.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: नहुष उवाच सहस्राणां शतं विप्र निषादेभ्यः प्रदीयताम्। स्यादिदं भगवन् मूल्यं किं वान्यन्मन्यते भवान्॥
en: Nahusha said Let, О learned Brahmana, a hundred thousand coins be given to these Nishadas. Shall this be your price, O holy one, or do you think otherwise.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: च्यवन उवाच नाहं शतसहस्रेण निमेयः पार्थिवर्षभ। दीयतां सदृशं मूल्यममात्यैः सह चिन्तय॥
en: Chyavana said I should not be bought with a hundred thousand coins, O best of kings! Let a proper price be given to these! Do you consult with your ministers.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: नहुष उवाच कोटिः प्रदीयतां मूल्यं निषादेभ्यः पुरोहित। यदेतदपि नो मूल्यमतो भूयः प्रदीयताम्॥
en: Nabusha said Let my priest give to these Nishadas a crore of coins. If even this does not cover your value, let more be paid to them.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: च्यवन उवाच राजन् नार्हाम्यहं कोटि भूयो वापि महाद्युते। सदृशं दीयतां मूल्यं ब्राह्मणैः सह चिन्तय॥
en: Chyavana said O king, I am not with a crore of coins or even more. Let that price be given to these men which would be fair or proper. Do you consult with the Brahmanas.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: नहुष उवाच अर्धं राज्यं समग्रं वा निषादेभ्यः प्रदीयताम्। एतन्मूल्यमहं मन्ये किं वान्यन्मन्यसे द्विज॥
en: Nahusha said Let half my kingdom or even the whole be given away to these Nishadas. I think that would be your price. What, however, do you think twiceborn one?

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: च्यवन उवाच अर्धं राज्यं समग्रं च मूल्यं नार्हामि पार्थिव। सदृशं दीयतां मूल्यमृषिभिः सह चिन्त्यताम्॥
en: Chyavana said I do not deserve to be purchased with half your kingdom or even the whole of it, O king! Let that price which is proper be given to these men. Do you consult with the Rishis!

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: भीष्म उवाच महर्षेर्वचनं श्रुत्वा नहुषो दुःखकर्शितः। स चिन्तयामास तदा सहामात्यपुरोहितः॥
en: Bhishma continued Hearing these words of the great Rishi, Nahusha became stricken with great sorrow. With his ministers and priest he began to think on the matter.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: तत्र त्वन्यो वनचरः कश्चिन्मूलफलाशनः। नहुषस्य समीपस्थो गविजातोऽभवन्मुनिः॥
en: There then came to king Nahusha an ascetic living in the forest and subsisting upon fruit and roots and born of cow.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: स तमाभाष्य राजानमब्रवीद् द्विजसत्तमः। तोषमिपम्यहं क्षिप्रं यथा तुष्टो भविष्यति॥
en: That best of twiceborn persons, addressing the king, O monarch, said these words-I shall soon satisfy you. The Rishi also will be satisfied.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: नाहं मिथ्यावचो ब्रूयां स्वैरेष्वपि कुतोऽन्यथा। भवतो यदहं ब्रूयां तत्कार्यमविशङ्कया॥
en: I shall never speak a falsehood, no, not even in jest, what then need I say of other occasions? You should unhesitatingly do what I bid you.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: नहुष उवाच ब्रवीतु भगवान् मूल्यं महर्षेः सदृशं भृगोः। परित्रायस्व मामस्मद्विषयं च कुलं च मे॥
en: Nahusha said Do you, O illustrious one, say what the value is of that great Rishi of Bhrigu's race. O, save me from this terrible difficulty, save my kingdom and save my family

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: हन्याद्धि भगवान् क्रुद्धस्त्रैलोक्यमपि केवलम्। किं पुनर्मां तपोहीनं बाहुवीर्यपरायणम्॥
en: If the holy Chyavana become angry, he would destroy the three worlds; what need I say then of my poor self who is destitute of penances and who depends upon the power only of his arms.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: अगाधाम्भसि मग्नस्य सामात्यस्य सऋत्विजः। प्लवो भव महर्षे त्वं कुरु मूल्यविनिश्चयम्॥
en: O great Rishi, do you become the raft to us who have all fallen into a fathomless deep with all our counsellors and our priest. Do you settle what the value should be of the Rishi!

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: भीष्म उवाच गविजातः प्रतापवान्। नहुषस्य वचः श्रुत्वा उवाच हर्षयन् सर्वानमात्यान् पार्थिवं च तम्॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words of Nahusha, the ascetic born of a cow and gifted with great energy spoke thus, gladdening the monarch with all his counsellors:

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: अनया महाराज द्विजा वर्णेषु चोत्तमाः। गावश्च पुरुषव्याघ्र गौर्मूल्यं परिकल्प्यताम्॥
en: Brahmanas, O king, belong to the foremost of the four castes. No value, however great, can be fixed upon them. Kine also are invaluable. Therefore, O king, do you regard a cow as the value of the Rishi!

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: नहुषस्तु ततः श्रुत्वा महर्षेर्वचनं नृप। हर्षेण महता युक्तः सहामात्यपुरोहितः॥
en: Hearing these words of the great Rishi, Nahusha became, O king, filled with joy along with all his counsellors and priest.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: अभिगम्य भृगोः पुत्रं च्यवनं संशितव्रतम्। इदं प्रोवाच नृपते वाचा संतर्पयन्निव॥
en: Proceeding then to Bhrigu's son Chyavana of rigid vows, he addressed him thus O monarch, for satisfying him to the best of his power.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: नहुष उवाच उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ विप्रर्षे गवा क्रीतोऽसि भार्गव। एतन्मूल्यमहं मन्ये तव धर्मभृतां वर॥
en: Nahusha said Rise, rise, O twiceborn Rishi, you have been purchased, O son of Bhrigu, with a cow as your price! O foremost of righteous persons, even this, I think, is your price!

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: च्यवन उवाच उत्तिष्ठाम्येष राजेन्द्र सम्यक् क्रीतोऽस्मि तेऽनघ। गोभिस्तुल्यं न पश्यामि धनं किंचिदिहाच्युत॥
en: Chyavana said Yes, O king of kings, I do rise up. I have been properly purchased by you, O sinless ore. I do not, O you of unfading glory, see any riches that is equal to kine.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: कीर्तनं श्रवणं दानं दर्शनं चापि पार्थिव। गवां प्रशस्यते वीर सर्वपापहरं शिवम्॥
en: To speak of kine, to hear others speak of then, to make gifts of kine, and to see kine, O king, are acts, that are all praised, O hero, and that are highly auspicious and purifying.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: गावो लक्ष्म्याः सदा मूलं गोषु पाप्मा न विद्यते। अन्नमेव सदा गावो देवानां परमं हविः॥
en: Kine are always the root of prosperity. There is no fault in kine. Kine always give the best food, in the form of Havi, to the deities.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: स्वाहाकारवषट्कारौ गोषु नित्यं प्रतिष्ठितौ। गावो यज्ञस्य नेत्र्यो वै तथा यज्ञस्य ता मुखम्॥
en: The sacred Mantras, Svaha and Vashat, are always established upon kine. Kine are the chief conductresses of Sacrifices. They form the mouth of Sacrifice.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: अमृतं ह्यव्ययं दिव्यं क्षरन्ति च वहन्ति च। अमृतायतनं चैताः सर्वलोकनमस्कृताः॥
en: They bear and yield excellent and strength giving ambrosia. They receive the adoration of all the worlds and are considered as the source of nectar.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: तेजसा वपुषा चैव गावो वह्निसमा भुवि। गावो हि सुमहत् तेजः प्राणिनां च सुखप्रदाः॥
en: On Earth, kine resemble fire in energy and form. Indeed, kine represent high energy, and are conferreres of great happiness upon all creatures.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: निविष्टं गोकुलं यत्र श्वासं मुञ्चति निर्भयम्। विराजयति तं देशं पापं चास्यापकर्षति॥
en: That country where, kine placed by their owners, breathe fearlessly, shines in beauty. The sins also of that country are all removed.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: गावः स्वर्गस्य सोपानं गावः स्वर्गेऽपि पूजिताः। गाव: कामदुहो देव्यो नान्यत् किंचित् परं स्मृतम्।।
en: Kine form the stairs leading to Heaven. Kine are worshipped in Heaven itself. Kine are goddesses that can give everything and grant every wish. There is nothing else in the world that is so high or so superior.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्येतद् गोषु मे प्रोक्तं माहात्म्यं भरतर्षभ। गुणैकदेशवचनं शक्यं पारायणं न तु॥
en: Bhishma said This is what I say to you on the subject of the glory and superiority of kine, O chief of Bharata's race. I am competent to describe a part only of the merits of the kine. I have not the ability to exhaust the subject.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: निषाद उवाच दर्शनं कथनं चैव सहास्माभिः कृतं मुने। सतां साप्तपदं मैत्रं प्रसादं नः कुरु प्रभो॥
en: The Nishadas said O ascetic, you have seen us and have also spoken with us, It has been said that friendship, with the good, depends upon only seven words. Do you then, O lord, show us your favour.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: हवींषि सर्वाणि यथा [पभुङ्क्ते हुताशनः। एवं त्वमपि धर्मात्मन् पुरुषाग्निः प्रतापवान्॥
en: The blazing sacrificial fire eats all the oblations of clarified butter poured upon it. Of pious soul, and gifted with great energy, you are among men, a blazing fire in energy.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: प्रसादयामहे विद्वन् भवन्तं प्रणता वयम्। अनुग्रहार्थमस्माकमियं गौः प्रतिगृह्यताम्॥
en: We propitiate you, O you of great learning. We surrender ourselves to you. Do you, for showing us favour, take back from us this cow.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: च्यवन उवाच कृपणस्य च यच्चक्षुर्मुनेराशीविषस्य च। नरं समूलं दहति कक्षमग्निरिव ज्वलन्।॥
en: Chyavana said The eye of a poor or distressed person, the eye of an ascetic, or the eye of a snake of dreadful poison, consume a man with his very roots even as a fire, that burning with the aid of the wind and consumes a stack of dry grass or straw.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: प्रतिगृह्णामि वो धेनुं कैवर्ता मुक्तकिल्बिषाः। दिवं गच्छत वै क्षिप्रं मत्स्यैः सह जलोद्भवैः॥
en: I shall accept the cow that you wish to present me-You fishermen, freed from every sin, go ye to heaven forthwith, with these fishes also that you have caught with your nets.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततस्तस्य प्रभावात् ते महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः। निषादास्तेन वाक्येन सह मत्स्यैर्दिवं ययुः॥
en: Bhishma said After this, on account of the energy of that great Rishi of purified soul, those fishermen along with all those fish, through virtue of those words that he had uttered, went to heaven.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: ततः स राजा नहुषो विस्मितः प्रेक्ष्य धीवरान्। आरोहमाणांस्त्रिदिवं मत्स्यांश्च भरतर्षभ॥
en: Seeing the fishermen ascending to heaven with those fishes in their company, became filled with wonder, O chief of Bharata's race.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: ततस्तौ गविजश्चैव च्यवनश्च भृगूद्वहः। वराभ्यामनुरूपाभ्यां छन्दयामासतु पम्॥
en: After this, the two Rishis, viz., the one born of a cow and the other who was Chyavana of Bhrigu's race, pleased king Nahusha by granting him many boons.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: ततो राजा महावीर्यो नहुषः पृथिवीपतिः। परमित्यब्रवीत् प्रीतस्तदा भरतसत्तम॥
en: Then the highly energetic king Nahusha that lord of all the Earth, filled with joy, O best of the Bharatas, said-Sufficient.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: ततो जग्राह धर्मे स स्थितिमिन्द्रनिभो नृपः। तथेति चोदितः प्रीतस्तावृषी प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: Like a second, Indra the king of the celestials, he accepted the boon about his own steadiness in virtue. The Rishis having granted him the boon, the delighted king adored them both with great respect.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: समाप्तदीक्षश्च्यवनस्ततोऽगच्छत् स्वमाश्रमम्। गविजश्च महातेजाः स्वमाश्रमपदं ययौ॥
en: As regards Chyavana, his vow having been completed, he returned to his own hermitage. The Rishi who had taken his birth from the cow, and who was gifted with great energy, also proceeded to his own hermitage.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: निषादाश्च दिवं जग्मुस्ते च मत्स्या जनाधिप। नहुषोऽपि वरं लब्वा प्रविवेश स्वकं पुरम्॥
en: The Nishadas all ascended to heaven, as also the fishes they had caught, O king, king Nahusha too, having got those valuable boons, entered his own city.

description: The nature of compassion and pity. The discourse between Nahusha and Chyavana
sn: एतत्ते कथितं तात यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। दर्शने यादृशः स्नेहः संवासे वा युधिष्ठिर॥ महाभाग्यं गवां चैव तथा धर्मविनिश्चयम्। किं भूयः कथ्यतां वीर किं ते हदि विवक्षितम्॥
en: I have thus, O son, told you everything about what you had asked me. The affection that is caught by the sight alone of others as also by the fact of living with them, O Yudhishthira, and the high blessedness of kine too, and the ascertainment of true virtue, are the subject I have described. Tell me, O hero what else is in your mind.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच संशयो मे महाप्राज्ञ सुमहान् सागरोपमः। तं मे शृणु महाबाहो श्रुत्वा व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said O you of great wisdom, 'I have a doubt which is very great and which is as vast as the ocean itself. Listen to it, O mightyarmed one, and having learnt what it is, you should explain it to me.

sn: कौतूहलं मे सुमहज्जामदग्न्यं प्रति प्रभो। रामं धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठं तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: I have a great curiosity about Jamadagni's son, O lord, viz., Rama, that foremost of all pious persons. you should satisfy that curiosity.

sn: कथमेष समुत्पन्नो रामः सत्यपराक्रमः। कथं ब्रह्मर्षिवंशोऽयं क्षत्रधर्मा व्यजायत॥
en: How was Rama born who was gifted with prowess incapable of being baffled? He belonged by birth to a family of twice born Rishis. How did he become a follower of Kshatriya practices?

sn: तदस्य सम्भवं राजन् निखिलेनानुकीर्तय। कौशिकाच्च कथं वंशात् क्षत्राद् वै ब्राह्मणो भवेत्॥४
en: Do you then, O king, recite to me in full the circumstances of Rama's birth. How also did a son of the race of Kushika, who was Kshatriya become a Brahmana?

sn: अहो प्रभावः सुमहानासीद् वै सुमहात्मनः। रामस्य च नरव्याघ्र विश्वामित्रस्य चैव हि॥
en: Great, indeed, was the power of the highsouled Rama, O chief of men, as also of Vishvamitra.

sn: कथं पुत्रानतिक्रम्य तेषां नप्तृष्वथाभवत्। एष दोषः सुतान् हित्वा तत्त्वं व्याख्यातुमर्हसि।॥
en: Why did the grandson of Richika instead of his son become a Kshatriya? Why also did the grandson of Kushika and not his son become a Brahmana? Why did such untoward incidents befall the grandsons of both, instead of their sons? You should explain the truth of these circumstances.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीपमितिहासं पुरातनम्। च्यवनस्य च संवादं कुशिकस्य च भारत॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited an old history of the discourse between Chyavana and Kushika, O Bharata!

sn: एतं दोषं पुरा दृष्ट्वा भार्गवश्च्यवनस्तदा। आगामिनं महाबुद्धिः स्ववंशे मुनिसत्तमः॥
en: Gifted with great intelligence, Chyavana of Bhrigu's race, that best of ascetics, saw (with his spiritual eye) the stain that would affect his own race.

sn: निश्चित्य मनसा सर्वं गुणदोषबलाबलम्। दग्धुकामः कुलं सर्वं कुशिकानां तपोधनः॥
en: Reflecting upon the merits and faults of that incident, as also its strength and weakness, Chyavana having asceticism for his wealth, became desirous of consuming the race of the Kushikas.

sn: च्यवनः समनुप्राप्य कुशिकं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। वस्तुमिच्छा समुत्पन्ना त्वया सह ममानघ॥
en: Going then to the presence of king Kushika, Chyavana said to him,—o sinless one, the desire has arisen in my heart of living with you for sometime.

sn: कुशिक उवाच भगवन् सहधर्मोऽयं पण्डितैरिह धार्यते। प्रदानकाले कन्यानामुच्यते च सदा बुधैः॥
en: Kushika said O holy one, to live together is a deed which the learned ordain for girls wheir these are given away. The wise always speak of the practice in such connection only.

sn: यत्तु तावदतिक्रान्तं धर्मद्वारं तपोधन। तत्कार्यं प्रकरिष्यामि तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: O Rishi having asceticism for your wealth, the residence which you seek with me is not sanctioned by the ordinance. Yet, however opposed to the dictates of duty and virtue, I shall do what you may be pleased to order.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अथासनमुपादाय च्यवनस्य महामुनेः। कुशिको भार्यया सार्धमाजगाम यतो मुनिः॥
en: Bhishma said Ordering a seat to be placed for the great ascetic Chyavana, king Kushika, accompanied by his wife, stood before him.

sn: प्रगृह्य राजा भृङ्गारं पाद्यमस्मै न्यवेदयत्। कारयामास सर्वाश्च क्रियास्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Bringing a little jar of water, the king offered him water for washing his feet. He then through his servants, caused all the rites to be duty performed in honour of his illustrious guest.

sn: ततः स राजा च्यवनं मधुपर्क यथाविधि। ग्राहयामास चाव्यग्रो महात्मा नियतव्रतः॥
en: The illustrious Kushika, who was observant of restraints and vows, then cheerfully presented, in due forms, the ingredients consisting of honey and the other things, to the great Rishi and asked him to accept the same.

sn: सत्कृत्य तं तथा विप्रमिदं पुनरथाब्रवीत्। भगवन् परवन्तौ स्वो ब्रूहि किं करवावहे॥
en: Having welcomed and honoured the learned Brahmana thus, the king once more addressed him and saidWe two await your orders! Command us what we are to do for you, O holy one.

sn: यदि राज्यं यदि धनं यदि गाः संशितव्रत। यज्ञदानानि च तथा ब्रूहि सर्वं ददामि ते॥
en: If it is our kingdom or riches or kine, O you of rigid vows, or all articles that are given away in sacrifices, which you want, tell us the word and we shall bestow all upon you.

sn: इदं गृहमिदं राज्यमिदं धर्मासनं च ते। राजा त्वमसि शाध्युर्वीमहं तु परवांस्त्वयि॥
en: This palace, this kingdom, this seat of justice, are at your disposal. You are the master of all these! Do you rule the Earth! As regards myself, I depend entirely upon you.

sn: एवमुक्ते ततो वाक्ये च्यवनो भार्गवस्तदा। कुशिकं प्रत्युवाचेदं मुदा परमया युतः॥
en: Addressed in these words by the king, Chyavana of Bhrigu's race, filled with great joy, said to Kushika these words in reply.

sn: च्यवन उवाच न राज्यं कामये राजन् न धनं न य योषितः। न च गा न च वै देशान् न यज्ञं श्रूयतामिदम्॥
en: Chyavana said I do not, O king covet your kingdom, nor your riches, nor the damsels you have nor your kine, nor your provinces, nor articles needed for sacrifice! Do you listen to me.

sn: नियमं किंचिदारप्स्ये युवयोर्यदि रोचते। परिचर्योऽस्मि यत्ताभ्यां युवाभ्यामविशङ्कया॥
en: If it pleases you and your wife, I shall begin to observe a certain vow. I wish you and your me during that period unhesitatingly.

sn: एवमुक्ते तदा तेन दम्पती तौ जहर्षतुः। प्रत्यब्रूतां च तमृषिमेवमस्त्विति भारत॥
en: consort to serve Thus addressed by the Rishi, the king and the queen became filled with delight, O Bharata, and answered him, saying-Be it so, O Rishi.

sn: अथ तं कुशिको दृष्टः प्रावेशयदनुत्तमम्। गृहोद्देशं ततस्तस्य दर्शनीयमदर्शयत्॥
en: Pleased with the Rishi's words, the king led him to an apartment of the place. It was an excellent one, agreeable to see. The king showed him everything in that room.

sn: राजोवाच इयं शय्या भगवतो यथाकाममिहोप्यताम्। प्रयतिष्यावहे प्रीतिमाहर्तुं ते तपोधन।॥
en: The king said This, O holy one, is your bed. Do you live here as you please! O you having asceticism for your wealth, myself and my queen shall try our best to give you every comfort and every pleasure.

sn: अथ सूर्योऽतिचक्राम तेषां संवदतां तथा। अथर्षिश्चोदयामास पानमन्नं तथैव च॥
en: While they were thus conversing with each other, the sun was over the meridian. The Rishi ordered the king to bring him food and drink.

sn: तमपृच्छत् ततो राजा कुशिकः प्रणतस्तदा। किमन्नजातमिष्टं ते किमुपस्थापयाम्यहम्॥
en: Bowing to the Rishi, King Kushika asked him, saying-What kind of food is liked by you? What food, indeed, shall be brought for you.

sn: ततः स परया प्रीत्या प्रत्युवाच नराधिपम्। औपपत्तिकमाहारं प्रयच्छेस्वेति भारत॥
en: Filled with joy, the Rishi answered that king, O Bharata, saying-Let food that is proper be given to me.

sn: तद्वचः पूजयित्वा तु तथेत्याह स पार्थिवः। यथोपपन्नमाहारं तस्मै प्रादाज्जनाधिप॥
en: Receiving these words with respect, the king said,-So be it!-and then offered to the Rishi food of the proper kind.

sn: ततः स भुक्त्वा भगवान् दम्पती प्राह धर्मवित्। स्वप्तुमिच्छाम्यहं निद्रा बाधते मामिति प्रभो॥
en: Having finished his meals, the holy Chyavana, knowing every duty, addressed the king and the queen, saying I wish to sleep, O powerful one, sleep hinders me now.

sn: ततः शय्यागृहं प्राप्य भगवानृषिसत्तमः। संविवेश नरेशस्तु सपत्नीकः स्थितोऽभवत्।॥
en: Proceeding thence to a room that had been got ready for him, that best of Rishis then laid himself down upon a bed. The king and the queen sat down.

sn: न प्रबोध्योऽस्मि संसुप्त इत्युवाचाथ भार्गवः। संवाहितव्यौ मे पादौ जागृतव्यं च तेऽनिशम्॥
en: The Rishi told them-Do not, while I sleep, awake me! Do you keep yourself awake and continually press my feet as long as I sleep.

sn: अविशङ्कस्तु कुशिकस्तेथेत्येवाह धर्मवित्। न प्रबोधयतां तौ च दम्पती रजनीक्षये॥ यथादेशं महर्षस्तु शुश्रूषापरमौ तदा। बभूवतुर्महाराज प्रयतावथ दम्पती॥
en: Kushika, conversant with every duty, unhesitatingly, saidSo be it! Indeed, the king and the queen kept themselves awake all night, duty engaged in tending and serving the Rishi in the manner directed the royal pair, O king, accomplished the Rishi's order with earnestness and attention.

sn: ततः स भगवान् विप्रः समादिश्य नराधिपम्। सुष्वापैकेन पाइँन दिवसानेकविंशतिम्॥
en: Meanwhile the holy Brahmana, having thus commanded the king, slept soundly, without changing his posture or turning even once, for one and twenty days.

sn: स तु राजा निराहारः सभार्य: कुरुनन्दन। पर्युपासत तं हृष्टश्च्यवनाराधने रतः॥
en: The king, O delighter of the Kurus, abstaining from food, along with his wife, sat joyfully the whole time, engaged in tending and serving the Rishi.

sn: भार्गवस्तु समुत्तस्थौ स्वयमेव तपोधनः। अकिंचिदुक्त्वा तु गृहानिश्चक्राम महातपाः॥
en: On the expiration of one and twenty days, the son of Bhrigu rose of his own accord. The great ascetic then went out of the room, without speaking to thein at all.

sn: तमन्वगच्छतां तौ च क्षुधितौ श्रमकर्शितौ। भार्यापती मुनिश्रेष्ठस्तावेतौ नावलोकयत्॥
en: Famished and toilworn, the king and the queen followed him, but that foremost of Rishis did not please to cast a single look upon any of them.

sn: तयोस्तु प्रेक्षतोरेव भार्गवाणां कुलोद्वहः। अन्तर्हितोऽभूद् राजेन्द्र ततो राजापतत् क्षितौ॥
en: Proceeding a little way, the son of Bhrigu disappeared in the very sight of the royal pair. At this, the king struck with grief, drooped down on the Earth.

sn: स मुहूर्तं समाश्वस्य सह देव्या महाद्युतिः। पुनरन्वेषणे यत्नमकरोत् परमं तदा॥
en: Comforted. he up soon, and accompanied by his queen, the king possessed of great splendour, began to search everywhere for the Rishi. rose

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच तस्मिन्नन्तर्हिते विप्रे राजा किमकरोत् तदा। भार्या चास्य महाभागा तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said After the Rishi had disappeared, what did the king do and what also his highly-blessed wife? Tell me this O grandfather.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अदृष्ट्वा स महीपालस्तमृषि सह भार्यया। परिश्रान्तो निववृते वीडितो नष्टचेतनः॥
en: Bhishma said Not seeing the Rishi, the king, Stricken with shame, toilworn, and losing his senses, returned to his palace, accompanied by his queen.

sn: स प्रविश्य पुरी दीनो नाभ्यभाषत किंचन। तदेव चिन्तयामास च्यवनस्य विचेष्टितम्॥
en: Entering his mansion in a dejected spirit, The spoke not a word with any one. He thought only of that conduct of Chyavana.

sn: अथ शून्येन मनसा प्रविश्य स्वगृहं नृपः। ददर्श शयने तस्मिन् शयानं भृगुनन्दनम्।॥
en: With a despairing heart he then went to his room. There he beheld the son of Bhrigu stretched as before on his bed.

sn: विस्मितौ तमृषि दृष्ट्वा तदाश्चर्ये विचिन्त्य च। दर्शनात् तस्य तु तदा विश्रान्तौ सम्बभूवतुः॥
en: Seeing the Rishi there, they wondered much. Indeed, they began to think upon that very strange incident. The sight of the Rishi removed their fatigue.

sn: यथास्थानं च तौ स्थित्वा भूयस्तं संववाहतुः। अथापरेण पार्बेन सुष्वाप स महामुनिः॥
en: Seated once more by his side, they again began to gently press his feet as before. Meanwhile the great ascetic continued to sleep soundly as before. Only, he now lay on another side.

sn: तेनैव च स कालेन प्रत्यबुद्ध्यत वीर्यवान्। न च तौ चक्रतुः किंचिद् विकारं भयशङ्कितौ॥
en: Gifted with great energy, he thus passed another twentyone days. Moved by fear, the royal pair showed no change in their attitude or sentiment towards the Rishi.

sn: प्रतिबुद्धस्तु स मुनिस्तौ प्रोवाच विशाम्पते। तैलाभ्यङ्गो दीयतां मे स्त्रास्येऽहमिति भारत॥
en: Awaking then from his sleep the ascetic addressed the king and the queen, saying-do you rub my body with oil, I wish to have a bath.

sn: तौ तथेति प्रतिश्रुत्य श्रुधितौ श्रमकर्शितौ। शतपाकेन तैलेन महार्हेणोपतस्थतुः॥
en: Famishing and toilworn though they were, forthwith they volunteered their services and soon approached the Rishi with a rich oil that had been prepared by boiling it a hundred times.

sn: ततः सुखासीनमृर्षि वाग्यतौ संववाहतुः। न च पर्याप्तमित्याह भार्गवः सुमहातपाः॥
en: While the Rishi was seated at his ease, the king and the queen, silently, continued to rub him. Gifted with great ascetic merit, the son of Bhrigu did not once utter the word Sufficient.

sn: यदा तौ निर्विकारौ तु लक्ष्यामास भार्गवः। तत उत्थाय सहसा स्नानशालां विवेश ह॥
en: Bhrigu's son however saw that the royal pair were totally unmoved. Rising up all on a sudden, he entered the bath room.

sn: क्लृप्तमेव तु तत्रासीत् स्नानीयं पार्थिवोचितम्। असत्कृत्य च तत् सर्वं तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥ स मुनिः पुनरेवाथ नृपतेः पश्यतस्तदा। नासूयां चक्रतुस्तौ च दम्पती भरतर्षभ॥
en: The various articles necessary for a bath and such as were fit for a king's use, were ready there. Without using, any of those articles, the Rishi once more disappeared there and then by his Yogapower, before king Kushika (and his wife). This, however, O chief of Bharatas, failed to disturb the equanimity of the royal pair.

sn: अथ स्नातः स भगवान् सिंहासनगतः प्रभुः। दर्शयामास कुशिकं सभार्यं कुरुनन्दन॥
en: The next time the powerful Rishi was seen seated, after a bath, on the throne. It was from that place that he then showed himself to the king and the queen, O delighter of the Kurus.

sn: संहृष्टवदनो राजा सभार्यः कुशिको मुनिम्। सिद्धमन्नमिति प्रबो निर्विकारो न्यवेदयत्॥
en: With a cheerful face, king Kushika, together with his wife, then offered the Rishi cooked food with great respect. Gifted with wisdom, and with heart totally unmoved, Kushika made this offer.

sn: तपस्वी उवाच आनीयतामिति मुनिस्तं चोवाच नराधिपम्। स राजा समुपाजह्वे तदन्नं सह भार्यया।॥
en: The Ascetic said Let the food be brought. Assisted by his wife, the king soon brought there the food.

sn: मासंप्रकारान् विविधाशाकानि विविधानि च। वेसवारविकारांश्च पानकानि लघूनि च॥
en: There were various kinds of meat and different preparations also thereof. There was a great variety of vegetables also and potherbs.

sn: रसालापूपकांश्चित्रान् मोदकानथ खाण्डवान्। रसान् नानाप्रकारांश्च वन्यं च मुनिभोजनम्॥
en: There were juicy cakes too among those dishes and several agreeable kinds of confectionery, and solid preparations of milk. Indeed, the viands were different in kinds and taste. Among them there were also some foodforest produces-such as ascetics liked and took.

sn: फलानि च विचित्राणि राजभोज्यानि भूरिशः। बदरेङ्गुदकाश्मर्यभल्लातकफलानि च॥
en: Various sweet fruits fit to be eaten by kings, were also there. There were Vadaras and Ingudas and Kahsmaryyas and Bhallatakas.

sn: गृहस्थानां च यद् भोज्यं यच्चापि वनवासिनाम्। सर्वमाहारयामास राजा शापभयात् ततः॥
en: The food that was offered contained such things as are taken by householders, as also such things as arc taken by the forest dwellers. Through fear of the Rishi's curse, the king had caused all kinds of food to be gathered and got ready for his guest.

sn: अथ सर्वमुपन्यस्तमग्रतश्च्यवनस्य तत्। ततः सर्वं समानीय तच्च शय्यासनं मुनिः॥ वस्त्रैः शुभैरवच्छाद्य भोजनोपस्करैः सह। सर्वमादीपयामास च्यवनो भृगुनन्दनः॥
en: All this food, brought from the kitchen, was placed before Chyavana. A seat was also placed for him and a bed too was spread. The dishes were then caused to be covered with white cloths. Soon, however, Chyavana of Bhrigu's race put fire to all the things and reduced them to ashes.

sn: न च तौ चक्रतुः क्रोधं दम्पती सुमहामती। तयोः सम्प्रेक्षतोरेव पुनरन्तर्हितोऽभवत्॥
en: Gifted with great intelligence, the royal pair showed no anger at this conduct of the Rishi, who once more, after this, disappeared before the very eyes of the king and the queen.

sn: तथैव च स राजर्षिस्तथौ तां रजनीं तदा। सभार्यो वाग्यत: श्रीमान् न च कोपं समाविशत्।।२४
en: The royal sage Kushika thereupon stood there in the same posture for the whole night, with his wife by his side, and without speaking a word. Gifted with great prosperity, he did not yield to wrath.

sn: नित्यसंस्कृतमन्नं तु विविधं राजवेश्मनि। शयनानि च मुख्यानि परिषेकाश्च पुष्कला:॥ वस्त्रं च विविधाकारमभवत् समुपार्जितम्। न शशाक ततो द्रष्टुमन्तरं च्यवनस्तदा॥
en: Every day, good and pure food of various sorts, excellent beds, profuse articles needed for bath, and cloths of various sorts, were collected and kept ready in the palace for the Rishi. Indeed, Chyavana could not find any fault in the conduct of the king.

sn: पुनरेव च विप्रर्षिः प्रोवाच कुशिकं नृपम्। सभार्यो मां रथेनाशु वह यत्र ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: Then addressing king Kushika, the twice born Rishi said to him, “Do you with your spouse, yoke yourself to a car and take me on it wherever I shall direct."

sn: तथेति च प्राह नृपो निर्विशङ्कस्तपोधनम्। क्रीडारथोऽस्तु भगवन्नुत सांग्रामिको रथः॥
en: Unhesitatingly, the king answered Chyavana having asceticism for wealth, saying-So be it! And he further enquired of the Rishi, asking-Which car shall I bring? Shall it be my pleasure car for making pleasure journeys or, shall it be my war-chariot?

sn: इत्युक्तः स मुनी राज्ञा तेन हृष्टेन तद्वचः। च्यवनः प्रत्युवाचेदं हृष्टः परपुरंजयम्॥ सज्जीकुरु रथं क्षिप्रं यस्ते सांग्रामिको मतः। सायुधः सपताकश्च शक्तीकनकयष्टिमान्॥ किङ्किणीस्वननिर्घोषो युक्तस्तोरणकल्पनैः। जाम्बूनदनिबद्धश्च परमेषुशतान्वितः॥
en: Thus addressed by the delighted and contented King, the ascetic said to him-Do you promptly get ready that chariot with which you attack hostile cities! cities! Indeed, that warchariot of yours, with every weapon, with its standard and flags, its darts and javelins and golden columns and poles, should be made ready. Its rattle resembles the tinkling of bells. It is adorned with numberless arches made of pure gold. It is always furnished with hundreds of high and excellent weapons!

sn: ततः स तं तथेत्युक्त्वा कल्पयित्वा महारथम्। भार्यां वामे धुरि तदा चात्मानं दक्षिणे तथा॥ त्रिदण्डं वज्रसूच्यग्रं प्रतोदं तत्र चादधत्।
en: The king said So be it, and soon made his great warchariot ready. And he yoked his wife thereto on the left and his own self on the right, And the king placed on the chariot, among its other articles, the goad which had three handles and which had a point hard as adamant and sharp as the needle.

sn: सर्वमेतत् तथा दत्त्वा नृपो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥ भगवन् क्व रथो यातु ब्रवीतु भृगुनन्दन।
en: Having placed every article upon the car, the king said to the Rishi-O holy one, where shall the chariot proceed? O let the son of Bhrigu issue his order.

sn: यत्र वक्ष्यसि विप्रर्षे तत्र यास्यति ते रथः।३४॥ एवमुक्तस्तु भगवान् प्रत्युवाचाथ तं नृपम्। इत: प्रभृति यातव्यं पदकं पदकं शनैः॥ श्रमो मम यथा न स्यात् तथा मच्छन्दचारिणौ।
en: This your chariot shall proceed to the place which you may be pleased to direct! Thus addressed, the holy' man replied to the king, saying-Let the car go hence, dragged slowly, step by step. Obeying my will, do you two proceed in such a way that I may not feel any exhaustion.

sn: सुसुखं चैव वोढव्यो जनः सर्वश्च पश्यतु॥ नोत्सार्याः पथिकाः केचित् तेभ्यो दास्ये वसु ह्यहम्।
en: I should be borne away pleasantly, and let all your people see this march that I make through their midst. No person that comes to me, as I proceed along the road, should be driven away. I shall distribute riches among all.

sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च ये कामानर्थयिष्यन्ति मां पथि॥ सर्वान् दास्याम्यशेषेण धनं रत्नानि चैव हि।
en: To the Brahmanas who may approach me on the way, I shall grant their wishes and bestow upon all of the them gems and riches without stint.

sn: क्रियतां निखिलेनैतन्मा विचारय पार्थिव॥ तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा भृत्यांस्तथाब्रवीत्। यद् यद् ब्रूयान्मुनिस्तत्तत् सर्वं देयमशङ्कितैः॥ ततो रत्नान्यनेकानि स्त्रियो युग्यमजाविकम्। कृताकृतं च कनकं गजेन्द्राचाचलोपमाः॥ अन्वगच्छत तमृषि राजामात्याश्च सर्वशः।
en: Let all this be done, O king, and do not entertain any scruples!-Hearing these words of the Rishi, the king called his servants and told them-Ye should without any fear, give away whatever the ascetic will command. Then profuse jewels and gems and beautiful women, and pairs of sheep, and coined and uncoined gold, and huge elephants resembling, hills or mountain summits, and all the ministers of the king, began to follow the Rishi as he was carried on that chariot.

sn: हाहाभूतं च तत् सर्वमासीन्नगरमार्तवत्॥ तौ तीक्ष्णाग्रेण सहसा प्रतोदेन प्रतोदितौ। पृष्ठे विद्धौ कटे चैव निर्विकारो तमूहतुः॥
en: Cries of Oh and Alas arose from every part of the city which was plunged in grief at that extraordinary spectacle. The Rishi struck the king and the queen suddenly with that goad having a sharp point. Though thus struck on the back and the cheeks, the royal pair still showed no sign of agitation. On the other hand they continued to carry the Rishi on as before.

sn: वेपमानौ निराहारौ पञ्चशदात्रकर्षितौ। कथंचिदूहतुर्वीरौ दम्पती तं रथोत्तमम्॥
en: Trembling from head to foot, for no food had passed their lips for fifty nights, and exceedingly weak, the heroic pair somehow succeeded in dragging that excellent chariot.

sn: बहुशो भृशविद्धौ तौ स्रवन्तो च क्षतोद्भवम्। ददृशाते महाराज पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥
en: Repeatedly and deeply cut by the goad, the royal pair became covered with blood. Indeed, O king, they then looked like a couple of Kinshuka trees in the flowering season.

sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा पौरवर्गस्तु भृशं शोकसमाकुलः। अभिशापभयत्रस्तो न च किंचिदुवाच ह॥
en: Seeing the plight to which their king and queen had been reduced, the citizens became afflicted with great grief. Filled with fear of the curse of the Rishi, they kept silent under their misery.

sn: द्वन्द्वशश्चाब्रुवन् सर्वे पश्यध्वं तपसो बलम्। क्रुद्धा अपि मुनिश्रेष्ठं वीक्षितुं नेह शक्नुमः॥
en: Collected in masses they said to each other-See the might of penances! Although all of us are angry, we are still unable to look at the Rishi.

sn: अहो भगवतो वीर्यं महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः। राज्ञश्चापि सभार्यस्य धैर्यं पश्यत यादृशम्॥
en: Great is the energy of the holy Rishi of purified soul! See also the endurance of the king and his royal spouse.

sn: श्रान्तावपि हि कृच्छ्रेण रथमेनं समूहतुः। न चैतयोर्विकारं वै ददर्श भृगुनन्दनः॥
en: Though exhausted with fatigue and hunger, they are still carrying the car! The son of Bhrigu, despite the misery he caused to Kushika and his queen, could see no sign of dissatisfaction or agitation in them.

sn: ततः स निर्विकारौ तु दृष्ट्वा भृगुकुलोद्वहः। वसु विश्राणयामास यथा वैश्रवणस्तथा॥
en: Bhishma said The perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, seeing the king and the queen totally unmoved, began to distribute wealth very largely as if he were a second Lord of Treasures.

sn: तत्रापि राजा प्रीतात्मा यथादिष्टमथाकरोत्। ततोऽस्य भगवान् प्रीतो बभूव मुनिसत्तमः॥
en: At this deed also, king Kushika showed no mark of dissatisfaction. He did as the Rishi ordered. Seeing all this, that illustrious and best of ascetics became pleased.

sn: अवतीर्य रथश्रेष्ठाद् दम्पती तौ मुमोच ह। विमोच्य चैतौ विधिवत् ततो वाक्यमुवाच ह॥
en: Descending from that excellent car, he unharnessed the royal pair. Having freed them, he addressed them duty.

sn: स्निग्धगम्भीरया वाचा भार्गवः सुप्रसन्नया। ददानि वां वरं श्रेष्ठं तं ब्रूतामिति भारत॥
en: Indeed the son of Bhrigu, in a soft, deep, and delighted voice, saidI am ready to give an excellent boon to you both.

sn: सुकुमारौ च तौ विद्धौ कराभ्यां मुनिसत्तमः। पस्पर्शामृतकल्पाभ्यां स्नेहाद् भरतसत्तम॥
en: Delicate as they were, their bodies had been pierced with the goad. Moved by affection, that best of ascetics softly touched them with his hands, whose healing virtues resembled those of ambrosia itself, O chief of the Bharatas.

sn: अथाब्रवीन्नृपो वाक्यं श्रमो नास्त्यावयोरिह। विश्रान्तौ च प्रभावात् ते उचतुस्तौ तु भार्गवम्॥
en: Then the king answered Myself and my wife have felt no exhaustion Indeed, all their fatigue had been removed through the power of the Rishi, and hence it was that the king could say so to the Rishi.

sn: अथ तौ भगवान् प्राह प्रहृष्टश्च्यवनस्तदा। न वृथा व्याहृतं पूर्वं यन्मया तद् भविष्यति॥
en: Pleased with their conduct, the illustrious Chyavana said to them I have never before spoken falsehood; It must, therefore be as I have said.

sn: रमणीयः समुद्देशो गङ्गातीरमिदं शुभम्। किंचित्कालं व्रतपरो निवत्स्यामीह पार्थिव॥
en: This spot on the banks of Ganga is very charming and auspicious. I shall, observing a vow, live for a little while here, O king.

sn: गम्यतां स्वपुरं पुत्र विश्रान्तः पुनरेष्यसि। इहस्थं मां सभार्यस्त्वं द्रष्टासि श्वो नराधिप॥
en: Do you return to your city. You are exhausted! You shall come again. Tomorrow, O king, you shall returning with your wife, see me here.

sn: न च मन्युस्त्वया कार्यः श्रेयस्ते समुपस्थितम्। यत् काक्षितं हृदिस्थं ते तत्सर्वं हि भविष्यति॥
en: You should not give to anger or grief. The time is come when you shall reap a great reward! That which is coveted by you and which is in your heart will indeed be done.

sn: इत्येवमुक्तः कुशिकः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना। प्रोवाच मुनिशार्दूलमिदं वचनमर्थवत्॥
en: Thus addressed by the Rishi, king Kushika, with a pleased heart, replied to the Rishi in these pregnant words.

sn: न मे मन्युर्महाभाग पूतो स्वो भगवंस्त्वया। संवृतौ यौवनस्थौ स्वो वपुष्मन्तौ बलान्वितौ॥
en: I have entertained no anger or grief, O highly blessed one! We have been cleansed and sanctified by you, O holy one! We have once more become youthful. See our bodies have become greatly beautiful and possessed of great strength.

sn: प्रतोदेन व्रणा ये मे सभार्यस्य त्वया कृताः। तान् न पश्यामि गात्रेषु स्वस्थोऽस्मि सह भार्यया।।६१
en: I do not any longer see those wounds that were caused by you on our bodies with your good! Verily, with my wife, I am in good health.

sn: इमां च देवीं पश्यामि वपुषाप्सरसोपमाम्। श्रिया परमया युक्तां यथा दृष्टा पुरा मया।॥
en: I see my goddess become as beautiful in body as an Apsara. Indeed, she is endued with as much beauty and splendour as she had ever been before.

sn: तव प्रसादसंवृत्तमिदं सर्वं महामुने। नैतच्चित्रं तु भगवंस्त्वयि सत्यपराक्रम॥
en: All this, O great ascetic, is due to your favour, Indeed, there is nothing wonderful in all this, O holy Rishi of power ever unbaffled.

sn: इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचैनं कुशिकं च्यवनस्तदा। आगच्छेथाः सभार्यश्च त्वमिहेति नराधिप॥
en: Thus addressed by the king, Chyavana said to him – You shall, with your wife, return here tomorrow, O king.

sn: इत्युक्तः समनुज्ञातो राजर्षिरभिवाद्य तम्। प्रययौ वपुषा युक्तो नगरं देवराजवत्॥
en: With these words, the royal sage Kushika was sent away. Saluting the Rishi, the king, endued with a handsome body, returned to his capital like a second king of the celestials.

sn: तत एनमुपाजग्मुरमात्याः सपुरोहिताः। बलस्था गणिकायुक्ताः सर्वाः प्रकृतयस्तथा॥
en: The counsellors then, with the priest, came out to welcome him. His troops also and the dancing women and all his subjects, did the same.

sn: तैर्वृतः कुशिको राजा श्रिया परमया ज्वलन्। प्रविवेश पुरं हृष्टः पूज्यमानोऽथ बन्दिभिः॥
en: Surrounded by them all, King Kushika, shining in beauty and splendour, entered his city, with a delighted heart, and his praises were sung by bards and encomiasts.

sn: ततः प्रविश्य नगरं कृत्वा पौर्वाह्निकी: क्रियाः। भुक्त्वा सभार्यो रजनीमुवास स महाद्युतिः॥
en: Having entered his city and performed all his morning rites, he ate with his wife. Gifted with great splendour, the king then passed the night happy.

sn: ततस्तु तौ नवमभिवीक्ष्य यौवनं परस्परं विगतरुजाविवामरौ। ननन्दतुः शयनगतौ वपुर्धरौ श्रिया युतौ द्विजवरदत्तया तदा॥
en: Each saw the other to be possessed of fresh youthfulness. All their sufferings and pains having ceased, they saw each other to resemble a celestial, Gifted with the splendour they had got as a boon from that foremost of Brahmanas, and possessed of exceedingly lovely features and beautiful forms, both of them passed a happy night in their bed.

sn: स्तपोधनो वनमभिराममृद्धिमत्। मनीषया बहुविधरत्नभूषितं ससर्ज यन्न पुरि शतक्रतोरपि॥
en: In the interval spreader of the feats of Bhrigu's race, viz., the Rishi having penances for his wealth, converted by his Yogapower, that charming wood on the bank of Ganga into a retreat full of wealth of every kind and adorned with every variety of jewels and gems on account of which it excelled in beauty and splendour the very abode of the king of the celestials.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः स राजा रात्र्यन्ते प्रतिबुद्धो महामनाः। कृतपूर्वाह्निकः प्रायात् सभार्यस्तद् वनं प्रति॥
en: Bhishma said When that night passed away, the great king Kushika awoke and performed his morning rites. Accompanied by his wife he then went towards that forest which the Rishi had selected for his residence.

sn: ततो ददर्श नृपतिः प्रासादं सर्वकाञ्चनम्। मणिस्तम्भसहस्राढ्यं गन्धर्वनगरोपमम्॥
en: Arrived there, the king saw a palatial inansion made entirely of gold. Having a thousand columns each of which was made of gems and precious stones, it looked like a mansion belonging to the Gandharvas.

sn: तत्र दिव्यानभिप्रायान् ददर्श कुशिकस्तदा। पर्वतान् रूप्यसानूंश्च नलिनीश्च सपङ्कजाः॥ चित्रशालाश्च विविधास्तोरणानि च भारत। शाद्वलोपचितां भूमिं तथा काञ्चनकुट्टिमाम्॥
en: Kushika saw in every part of that building signs of celestial design. And he saw hills with charming valleys, and lakes with lotuses on their bosom; and mansions full of rich and curious articles, and gateways and arches, O Bharata, and the king beheld many open glades and open spots carpeted with grass, and resembling fields of gold.

sn: सहकारान् प्रफुल्लांश्च केतकोद्दालकान् वरान्। अशोकान् सहकुन्दांश्च फुल्लांश्चैवातिमुक्तकान्॥
en: And he saw many Sahakaras adorned with blossoms, and Ketakas and Uddalakas, and Dhavas, and Ashokas and blossoming Kundas, and Atimuktas.

sn: चम्पकांस्तिलकान् भव्यान् पनसान् वञ्जुलानपि। पुष्पितान् कर्णिकारांश्च तत्र तत्र ददर्श ह॥
en: And he saw there many Champakas and Tilakas and Bhavyas and Panasas and Vyanjulas and Karnikaras adorned with flowers.

sn: श्यामान् वारणपुष्पांश्च तथाष्टपदिका लताः। तत्र तत्र परिक्लृप्ता ददर्श स महीपतिः॥
en: And the king saw many Shyamas and Varanapushpas and the creepers called Astapadika, all clipt properly and beautifully.

sn: रम्यान् पद्मोत्पलधरान् सर्वर्तुकुसुमांस्तथा। विमानप्रतिमांश्चापि प्रासादान् शैलसंनिभान्॥
en: And the king saw trees on which lotuses of various species bloomed in all their beauty, and some of which bore flowers of every season. And he saw also many mansions that looked like celestial cars or like beautiful mountains.

sn: शीतलानि च तोयानि क्वचिदुष्णानि भारत। आसनानि विचित्राणि शयनप्रवराणि च॥ पर्यङ्कान् रत्नसौवर्णान् परास्तिरणावृतान्। भक्ष्यं भोज्यमनन्तं च तत्र तत्रोपकल्पितम्॥
en: And at some places, O Bharata, there were tanks and lakes full of cool water and at others were those that were full of warm or hot water. And there were various kinds of excellent seats and costly beds and bedsteads made of gold and gems and overlaid with beautiful cloths and carpets. There were profuse viands and edibles, all well dressed and ready for use.

sn: वाणीवादाञ्छुकांश्चैव सारिकान् भृङ्कराजकान्। कोकिलाञ्छतपत्रांश्च सकोयष्टिककुक्कुभान्॥ मयूरान् कुक्कुटांश्चापि दात्यूहान् जीवजीवकान्। चकोरान् वानरान् हंसान् सारसांश्चक्रसाह्वयान्॥
en: And there were talking parrots, she-parrots, Bhringarajas, Kokilas, Shatapatras with Koyashtikas and Kukkubhas, and peacocks and cocks and Datyuhas and Jivajivakas and Chakoras and monkeys and swans and Sarasas and Chakravakas.

sn: समन्ततः प्रमुदितान् ददर्श सुमनोहरान्। क्वचिदप्सरसा संघान् गन्धर्वाणां च पार्थिव॥
en: Here and there he saw bevies of rejoicing Apsaras and conclaves of happy Gandharva, O monarch.

sn: कान्ताभिरपरांस्तत्र परिष्वक्तान् ददर्श ह। न ददर्श च तान् भूयो ददर्श च पुनर्नृपः॥
en: And he saw other Gandharvas at other places rejoicing with their dear wives. The king sometimes saw these sights and sometimes could not see them.

sn: गीतध्वनि सुमधुरं तथैवाध्यापनध्वनिम्। हंसान सुमधुरांश्चापि तत्र शुश्राव पार्थिवः॥
en: The king heard also sweet notes of Vocal music and the sweet voices of preceptors engaged in lecturing their disciples on the Vedas and the Scriptures. And the king also heard the harinonious notes of the geese sporting in the lakes.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वात्यद्भुतं राजा मनसाचिन्तयत् तदा। स्वप्नोऽयं चित्तविभ्रंश उताहो सत्यमेव तु॥
en: Seeing such highly wonderful spectacles, the king began to reflect inwardly, saying-ls this a dream? Or, is all this due to an alienation of my mind? Or is it all real.

sn: अहो सह शरीरेण प्राप्तोऽस्मि परमां गतिम्। उत्तरान् वा कुरून पुण्यानथवाप्यमरावतीम्॥
en: O, I have, without renouncing my body, attained to the beatitude of Heaven. This land is cither the sacred country of the UttaraKurus, or the abode, called Amaravati, of the king of the celestials.

sn: किंचेदं महदाश्चर्यं सम्पश्यामीत्यचिन्तयत्। एवं संचिन्तयन्नेव ददर्श मुनिपुङ्गवम्॥
en: 0, what are these wonderful spectacles that I see! Reflecting thus, the king at last saw that foremost of Rishis.

sn: तस्मिन् विमाने सौवर्णे मणिस्तम्भसमाकुले। महार्हे शयने दिव्ये शयानं भृगुनन्दनम्॥
en: In that golden palace having columns made of jewels and gems, the son of Bhrigu lay stretched on a costly and excellent bed.

sn: तमभ्ययात् प्रहर्षेण नरेन्द्रः सह भार्यया। अन्तर्हितस्ततो भूयश्च्यवनः शयनं च तत्॥
en: With his wife by his side, the king approached, with an exulting heart, the Rishi as he lay on that bed. Chyavana, however, speedily disappeared at this, with the bed itself upon which he lay.

sn: ततोऽन्यस्मिन् वनोद्देशे पुनरेव ददर्श तम्। कौश्यां वृस्यां समासीनं जपमानं महाव्रतम्॥
en: The king then saw the Rishi at another part of that forest, seated on a mat made of Kusha grass, and mentally engaged in the recital of some high Mantras.

sn: एवं योगबलाद् विप्रो मोहयामास पार्थिवम्। क्षणेन तद् वनं चैव ते चैवाप्सरसां गणाः॥ गन्धर्वाः पादपाश्चैव सर्वमन्तरधीयत।
en: Through his Yoga-power, thus did that Brahmana stupefy the king. In a moment that charming forest, those bevies of Apsaras, those bands of Gandharvas, those beautiful trees, all disappeared.

sn: निःशब्दमभवच्चापि गङ्गाकूलं पुनर्नृप॥ कुशवल्मीकभूयिष्ठं बभूव च यथा पुरा।
en: The bank of Ganga became as silent as usual, and appeared as before covers with Kusha grass and anthills.

sn: ततः स राजा कुशिकः सभार्यस्तेन कर्मणा॥ विस्मयं परमं प्राप्तस्तद् दृष्ट्वा महदद्भुतम्।
en: Having seen that highly wonderful spectacle and its quick disappearance also, king Kushika, with his wife, became filled with wonder.

sn: ततः प्रोवाच कुशिको भार्यां हर्षसमन्वितः॥ पश्य भद्रे यथा भावाश्चित्रा दृष्टाः सुदुर्लभाः।
en: With a delighted heart, the king addressed his wife saying, see, O amiable one, the various agreeable scenes and sights, occurring nowhere else, which we two have just seen.

sn: प्रसादाद् भृगुमुख्यस्य किमन्यत्र तपोबलात्॥ तपसा तदवाप्यं हि यत् तु शक्यं मनोरथैः।
en: All this is due to the favour of Bhrigu's son and the power of his penances. By penances one attains all which cherishes in his imagination.

sn: त्रैलोक्यराज्यादपि हि तप एव विशिष्यते॥ तपसा हि सुतप्तेन शक्यो मोक्षस्तपोबलात्। अहो प्रभावो ब्रह्मर्षेश्च्यवनस्य महात्मनः॥ इच्छयैष तपोवीर्यादन्याँल्लोकान् सृजेदपि।
en: Penances are superior to even the kingdom of the three worlds. With penances wellperformed, Liberation itself may be acquired. Mark the power of the great and celestial Rishi Chyavana derived from his penances! He can. at his pleasure, create even other'worlds.

sn: ब्राह्मणा एव जायेरन् पुण्यवाग्बुद्धिकर्मणः॥ उत्सहेदिह कृत्वैव कोऽन्यो वै च्यवनादृते।
en: Only Brahmanas are born in this world for uttering and understanding sacred deeds. Who else save Chyavana could do all this?

sn: ब्राह्मण्यं दुर्लभं लोके राज्यं हि सुलभं नरैः॥ ब्राह्मण्यस्य प्रभावाद्धि रथे युक्तौ स्वधुर्यवत्।
en: Sovereignty may be acquired easily. But the dignity of a Brahmana is not attainable. It was through the power of a Brahmana that we were harnessed to a car like wellbroken animals.

sn: इत्येवं चिन्तयानः स विदितश्च्यवनस्य वै॥ सम्प्रेक्ष्योवाच नृपति क्षिप्रमागम्यतामिति।
en: These thoughts that passed through the king's mind, became known to Chyavana. Ascertaining the king's thoughts, the Rishi addressed him and saidCome here quickly.

sn: इत्युक्तः सहभार्यस्तु सोऽभ्यगच्छन्महामुनिम्॥ शिरसा वन्दनीयं तमवन्दत च पार्थिवः।
en: Thus addressed, the king and the queen approached the great ascetic, and bending their heads they adored him who were worthy of adoration.

sn: तस्याशिषः प्रयुज्याथ स मुनिस्तं नराधिपम्॥ निषीदेत्यब्रवीद् धीमान् सान्त्वयन् पुरुषर्षभः।
en: Uttering a benediction upon the king, the Rishi, gifted with great intelligence, O king, comforted the king and saidSit down on that seat.

sn: ततः प्रकृतिमापन्नो भार्गवो नृपते नृपम्॥ उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा तर्पयन्निव भारत। राजन् सम्यग् जितानीह पञ्च पञ्च स्वयं त्वया।।३५ मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि कृच्छ्रान्मुक्तोऽसि तेन वै।
en: After this, O monarch, the son of Bhrigu, without guile or insincerity of any sort, pleased the king with many soft words, and then saido king, you have completely subjugated the five organs of action and the five organs of knowledge with the mind as their sixth. For this you have come out unhurt from the fiery ordeal I had prepared for you.

sn: सम्यगाराधितः पुत्र त्वया प्रवदतां वर॥ न हि ते वृजिनं किंचित् सुसूक्ष्ममपि विद्यते।
en: I have been properly honoured and adored, O son, by you, O foremost of all persons gifted with speech. You have no sin, not even a minute one, in you.

sn: अनुजानीहि मां राजन् गमिष्यामि यथागतम्॥ प्रीतोऽस्मि तव राजेन्द्र वस्श्च प्रतिगृह्यताम्।
en: Give me leave, o king, for I shall now proceed to the place I came from. I have been highly pleased with you, O king. Pray accept the boon I am ready to give!

sn: कुशिक उवाच अग्निमध्ये गतेनेव भगवन् संनिधौ मया।॥ वर्तितं भृगुशार्दूल यन्न दग्धोऽस्मि तद् बहु।
en: Kushika said Before you, O holy one, I have stood like one staying in the midst of a fire. That I have not yet, O chief of Bhrigu's race, been reduced to ashes is sufficient.

sn: एष एव वरो मुख्यः प्राप्तो मे भृगुनन्दन॥ यत् प्रीतोऽसि मया ब्रह्मन् कुलं त्रातं च मेऽनघ।
en: Even this is the highest boon that I have got, O delighter of Bhrigu! That you have been pleased by me, O Brahmana, and that I have succeed in rescuing my race from destruction, O sinless one, are in my case the best boons.

sn: एष मेऽनुग्रहो विप्र जीविते च प्रयोजनम्॥ एतद् राज्यफलं चैव तपसश्च फलं मम।
en: This I consider, O learned Brahmana, as a distinct mark of your favour. The object of my life has been accomplished. Even this is what I consider the very object of my sovereignty. This is the highest fruit of my penances.

sn: यदि त्वं प्रीतिमान् विप्र मयि वै भृगुनन्दन॥ अस्ति मे संशयः कश्चित् तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: If, O learned Brahmana, you have been pleased with me, O delighter of Bhrigu, then do you remove some doubts which are in my mind.

sn: च्यवन उवाच वरश्च गृह्यतां मत्तो यश्च ते संशयो हृदि। तं प्रब्रूहि नरश्रेष्ठ सर्वं सम्पादयामि ते॥
en: Chyavana said Do you accept a boon from me. Do you also, O king, tell me what the doubt is that is in your mind. I shall certainly accomplish all your purposes.

sn: कुशिक उवाच यदि प्रीतोऽसि भगवंस्ततो मे वद भार्गव। कारणं श्रोतुमिच्छामि मद्गृहे वासकारितम्॥
en: Kushika said If you have been pleased with me, O holy one, do you then, O son of Bhrigu, teil me your object in living in my palace for sometime, for I wish to hear it. What was your object in sleeping on the bed I assigned you for, one and twenty days continuously, without changing sides.

sn: शयनं चैकपाāन दिवसानेकविंशतिम्। अकिंचिदुक्त्वा गमनं बहिश्च मुनिपुङ्गवा॥
en: O foremost of ascetics, what also was your object, again in going out of the room without speaking a single word.

sn: अन्तर्धानमकस्माच्च पुनरेव च दर्शनम्। पुनश्च शयनं विप्र दिवसानेकविंशतिम्॥
en: Why did you, again, without any reason, disappear and once more become visible? Why, O learned Brahmana, did you again lay yourself down on the bed, and sleep, as before, for one and twenty days.

sn: तैलाभ्यक्तस्य गमनं भोजनं च गृहे मम। समुपानीय विविधं यद् दग्धं जातवेदसा॥
en: Why did you go out after you were rubbed by us with oil for your bath? Why, also, after having made various kinds of food in my palace to be collected, did you consume them with fire?

sn: निर्याणं च रथेनाशु सहसा यत् कृतं त्वया। धनानां च विसर्गस्य वनस्यापि च दर्शनम्॥
en: What was the cause of your sudden journey through my city on the car? What was your object in giving away so much riches? What was your motive in showing us the wonders of the forest created by your Yogapower.

sn: प्रासादानां बहूनां च काञ्चनानां महामुने। पणिविद्रुमपादानां पर्याणां च दर्शनम्॥
en: What, indeed, was your motive in showing, O great ascetic, so many palaces made of gold and so many bedsteads supported on posts of jewels and gems?

sn: पुनश्चादर्शनं तस्य श्रोतुमिच्छामि कारणम्। अतीव ह्यत्र मुह्यामि चिन्तयानो भृगूद्वह॥
en: Why also did all these wonders disappear from our sight? I wish to hear the cause of all this. Thii.king of all these acts of yours, O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, I became stupefied.

sn: न चैवात्राधिगच्छामि सर्वस्यास्य विनिश्चयम्। एतदिच्छामि कार्येन सत्यं श्रोतुं तपोधन॥
en: I cannot comprehend your motive. ( you having penances for wealth, I wish to hear the truth about all those acts of yours in full.

sn: च्यवन उवाच शृणु सर्वमशेषेण यदिदं येन हेतुना। न हि शक्यमनाख्यातुमेवं पृष्टेन पार्थिव॥
en: Chyavana said Listen to me as I tell you fully the reasons which had moved me in all these acts of mine. Asked by you, O king, I cannot refuse to enlighten you.

sn: पितामहस्य वदतः पुरा देवसमागमे। श्रुतवानस्मि यद् राजस्तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: In days of yore, on one occasion, when the deities had assembled together, the Grandfather Brahman said some words. I heard them, O king, and shall now repeat them to you.
