sn: ब्रह्मक्षत्रविरोधेन भविता कुलसंकरः। पौत्रस्ते भविता राजंस्तेजोवीर्यसमन्वितः॥
en: On account of a quarrel between Brahmana and Kshatriya energy, there will occur an intermixture in my race. Your grandson, O king, will become endued with great energy and power.

sn: ततस्ते कुलनाशार्थमहं त्वां समुपागतः। चिकीर्षन् कुशिकोच्छेदं संदिधक्षुः कुलं तव॥
en: Hearing this, I came here resolved to exterminate your race. Indeed, I came, O Kushika, seeking the utter extermination of your family, in fact, for reducing to ashes all your descendants.

sn: ततोऽहमागम्य पुरे त्वामवोचं महीपते। नियम कंचिदारप्स्ये शुश्रूषा क्रियतामिति॥
en: Moved by this motive I came to your palace, O monarch, and said to you I shall observe some vow. Do you attend upon me and serve me dutifully.

sn: न च ते दुष्कृतं किंचिदहमासादयं गृहे। तेन जीवसि राजर्षे न भवेथास्त्वमन्यथा॥
en: While living, however, in your house, I could not see any shortcomings in you. It is for that reason, O royal sage, that you are still alive, for otherwise you would have by this been dead.

sn: एवं बुद्धिं समास्थाय दिवसानेकविंशतिम्। सुप्तोऽस्मि यदि मां कश्चिद् बोधयेदिति पार्थिव॥
en: It was with this resolution that I slept for twentyone days in the hope that somebody would awake me before I arose out of my own accord.

sn: यदा त्वया सभार्येण संसुप्तो न प्रबोधितः। अहं तदैव ते प्रीतो मनसा राजसत्तम॥
en: You, however, with your wife, did not awake me. Even then, O best of kings, I became delighted with you.

sn: उत्थाय चास्मि निष्क्रान्तो यदि मां त्वं महीपते। पृच्छेः क्व यास्यसीत्येवं शपेयं त्वामिति प्रभो॥
en: Rising from my bed I went out of the chamber without speaking to any of you. I did this, O king, in the hope that you would ask me and thus I would have an opportunity of cursing you.

sn: अन्तर्हितः पुनश्चास्मि पुनरेव च ते गृहे। योगमास्थाय संसुप्तो दिवसानेकविंशतिम्॥
en: I then disappeared, and again showed myself in the room of your palace, and once more following Yoga slept for one and twenty days.

sn: क्षुधितौ मामसूयेथां श्रमाद् वेति नराधिप। एवं बुद्धिं समास्थाय कर्शितौ वां क्षुधा मया।॥
en: My motive was this. Exhausted with toil and hunger you two would be angry with me and do what would be unpleasant to me. It was from this motive that I caused yourself and your wife to be afflicted with hunger.

sn: न च तेऽभूत् सुसूक्ष्मोऽपि मन्युर्मनसि पार्थिव। सभार्यस्य नरश्रेष्ठ तेन ते प्रीतिमानहम्॥
en: In your heart, however, O king, the slightest feeling of anger or vexation did not rise. For this, O king, I became highly pleased with you.

sn: भोजनं च समानाय्य यत् तदा दीपितं मया। क्रुद्ध्येथा यदि मात्सर्यादिति तन्मर्षितं च मे॥
en: When I caused various kinds of food to be brought and then set fire to them, I hoped that yourself with your wife would yield to anger at the sight. Even that act, however, of mine was tolerated by you.

sn: ततोऽहं रथमारुह्य त्वामवोचं नराधिप। सभार्यो मां बहस्वेति तच्च त्वं कृतवांस्तथा॥ अविशङ्को नरपते प्रीतोऽहं चापि तेन ह। धनोत्सर्गेऽपि च कृते न त्वां क्रोधः प्रधर्षयत्॥
en: I then ascended the car, o king, and addressed you, saying Do you with your wife bear me! You did what I ordered, without the least scruple, O king! I became delighted at this. The gifts of riches I made could not excite your anger.

sn: ततः प्रीतेन ते राजन् पुनरेतत् कृतं तव। सभार्यस्य वनं भूयस्तद् विद्धि मनुजाधिप॥
en: Pleased with you, O king, I created with the help of my Yogapower that forest which yourself with your wife did see here. Listen, O king, to the object I had.

sn: प्रीत्यर्थं तव चैतन्मे स्वर्गसंदर्शनं कृतम्। यत् वे वनेऽस्मिन् नृपते दृष्टं दिव्यं निदर्शनम्॥
en: For pleasing you and your qucen I made you to have a glimpse of Heaven, All those things which you have seen in these woods, O king, are a foretaste of Heaven.

sn: स्वर्णोद्देशस्त्वया राजन् सशरीरेण पार्थिव। मुहूर्तमनुभूतोऽसौ सभार्येण नृपोत्तम॥
en: O best of kings, for a little while I made you and your wife behold, in even your, earthly bodies, some sights of Heaven.

sn: निदर्शनार्थं तपसो धर्मस्य च नराधिप। तत्र याऽऽसीत् स्पृहा राजंस्तच्चापि विदितं मया॥२८
en: All this was done for showing the power of penances and the reward that is in store for virtue. The desire that arose in your heart, O monarch, at sight of those delightful objects, is known to me.

sn: ब्राह्मण्यं काक्षसे हि त्वं तपश्च पृथिवीपते। अवमन्य नरेन्द्रत्वं देवेन्द्रत्वं च पार्थिव॥
en: You became desirous of obtaining the dignity of a Brahmana and the merit of penances, O king, disregarding the sovereignty of the Earth, nay, the sovereignty of very Heaven.

sn: एवमेतद् यथाऽऽत्य त्वं ब्राह्मण्यं तात दुर्लभम्। ब्राह्मणे सति चर्षित्वमृषित्वे च तपस्विता।॥
en: You thought this, O king. The status of a Brahmana is highly difficult to get; having become a Brahmana, it is highly difficult to obtain the status of a Rishi; having become a Rishi it is difficult to become an ascetic.

sn: भविष्यत्येष ते कामः कुशिकात् कौशिको द्विजः। तृतीयं पुरुषं तुभ्यं ब्राह्मणत्वं गमिष्यति॥
en: I tell you that your desire will be fulfilled. From you, O Kushika, will originate a Brahmana who shall be called after your name. The person that will be the third in descent from you shall obtain the status of a Brahmana.

sn: वंशस्ते पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ भृगूणामेव तेजसा। पौत्रस्ते भविता विप्रस्तपस्वी पावकद्युतिः॥
en: Through the energy of the Bhrigus, your grandson, O king, will be an ascetic gifted with the splendour of fire.

sn: यः स देवमनुष्याणां भयमुत्पादयिष्यति। त्रयाणामेव लोकानां सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: He shall always strike all men, indeed, the inhabitants of the three worlds, 'vith fear. I tell you the truth.

sn: राजर्षे यत् ते मनसि वर्तते। तीर्थयात्रां गमिष्यामि पुरा कालोऽभिवर्तते।॥
en: O royal sage, do you accept the boon that is now in your mind. I shall soon start for a sojourn to all the sacred water, Time is expiring.

sn: कुशिक उवाच एष एव वरो मेऽद्य यस्त्वं प्रीतो महामुने। भवत्वेतद् यथाऽऽत्य त्वं भवेत् पौत्रो ममानघ॥ वरं गृहाण
en: Kushika said This, O great ascetic, is a high boon in my case, for you have been pleased with me! Let that take place which you have said! Let my grandson become a Brahmana, O sinless one.

sn: ब्राह्मण्यं मे कुलस्यास्तु भगवन्नेष मे वरः। पुनश्चाख्यातुमिच्छामि भगवन् विस्तरेण वै॥
en: Indeed, Let the dignity of Brahmanahood attach to my family, O holy one! This is the boon I pray for! I wish to once more ask you in full, O holy one.

sn: कथमेष्यति विप्रत्वं कुलं मे भृगुनन्दन। कश्चासौ भविता बन्धुर्मम कश्चापि सम्मतः॥
en: In what way, O delighter of Bhrigu, will the dignity of Brahmanahood attach to my family? Who will be my friend? Who will have my affection and respect?

sn: अवश्यं कथनीयं मे तवैतन्नरपुङ्गव। यदर्थं त्वाहमुच्छेत्तुं सम्प्राप्तो मनुजाधिप॥
en: I should certainly, O king, tell you everything about the circumstance for which, O monarch, I came hither for exterminating your race.

sn: भृगूणां क्षत्रिया याज्या नित्यमेतज्जनाधिप। ते च भेदं गमिष्यन्ति दैवयुक्तेन हेतुना॥
en: This is wellknown, o king, that the Kshatriyas should always have the help of the sons of Bhrigu in the matter of sacrifices. Through an irresistible decree of destiny, the Kshatriyas and the Bhargavas will quarrel,

sn: क्षत्रियाश्च भृगून् सर्वान् वधिष्यन्ति नराधिप। आ गर्भादनुकृन्तन्तो दैवदण्डनिपीडिताः॥
en: The Kshatriyas, o king, will kill all the descendants of Bhrigu. By an ordinance of fate, they will root out the race of Bhrigu, not sparing even infants in their mothers wombs.

sn: तत उत्पत्स्यतेऽस्माकं कुले गोत्रविवर्धनः। उर्वो नाम महातेजा ज्वलनार्कसमद्युतिः॥
en: There will then be born in Bhrigu's race a Rishi of the name of Urva. Gifted with great energy, he will in splendour certainly resemble fire or the sun.

sn: स त्रैलोक्यविनाशाय कोपाग्निं जनयिष्यति। महीं सपर्वतवनां यः करिष्यति भस्मसात्॥
en: He will cherish such anger as will be sufficient to consume the three worlds. He will be competent to reduce the whole Earth with all her mountains and forests into ashes.

sn: कंचित् कालं तु वह्निं च स एव शमयिष्यति। समुद्रे वडवावको प्रक्षिप्य मुनिसत्तमः॥
en: For a little while he will put out the flames of that fiery rage, throwing it into the Mare's mouth that wanders through the ocean.

sn: पुत्रं तस्य महाराज ऋचीकं भृगुनन्दनम्। साक्षात् कृत्स्नो धनुर्वेदः समुपस्थास्यतेऽनघ।॥ क्षत्रियाणामभावाय दैवयुक्तेन हेतुना। स तु तं प्रतिगृह्मैव पुत्रे संक्रामयिष्यति॥ जमदग्नौ महाभागे तपसा भावितात्मनि। स चापि भृगुशार्दूलस्तं वेदं धारयिष्यति॥
en: He will have a son of the name of Richika. The whole science of arms, O sinless one, on its embodied form, will come to him, for the extermination of the entire Kshatriya caste, through a decree of Destiny. Receiving that science by inward light, he will, by Yogapower, communicate it to his son, the highly blessed Jamadagni of purified soul. That foremost of Bhrigu's race will bear that science in his mind.

sn: कुलात् तु तव धर्मात्मन् कन्यां सोऽधिगमिष्यति। उद्भावनार्थं भवतो वंशस्य नृपसत्तम॥
en: O you of righteous soul, Jamadagni will marry a girl, taking her from your race, for spreading its glory, O chief of the Bharatas.

sn: गाधेर्दुहितरं प्राप्य पौत्रीं तव महातपाः। ब्राह्मणं क्षत्रधर्माणं पुत्रमुत्पादयिष्यति॥
en: Having obtained for wife the daughter of Gadhi and your granddaughter, O king, that great ascetic will beget a twiceborn son gifted with Kshatriya accomplishments.

sn: क्षत्रियं विप्रकर्माणं बृहस्पतिमिवौजसा। विश्वामित्रं तव कुले गाधेः पुत्रं सुधार्मिकम्॥
en: In your race will be born a son, a Kshatriya gifted with the virtues of a Brahmana. Possessed of great virtue, he will be the son of Gadhi. Known by the name of Vishvamitra, he will in energy come to be considered as the equal of Brihaspati himself, the preceptor of the celestials.

sn: तपसा महता युक्तं प्रदास्यति महाद्युते। स्त्रियौ त कारणं तत्र परिवर्ते भविष्यतः॥
en: The illustrious Richika will grant this son to your race, this Kshatriya who will be endued with high penances. Two women will be the cause in the matter of this exchange of sons.

sn: पितामहनियोगाद् वै नान्यथैतद् भविष्यति। तृतीये पुरुषे तुभ्यं ब्राह्मणत्वमुपैष्यति॥ भविता त्वं च सम्बन्धी भृगूणां भावितात्मनाम्।
en: All this will take place at the command of the Grandfather. It will never be otherwise. The status of Brahmanahood will attach to one who is third in descent from you. You shall become a relative of the Bhargavas!

sn: भीष्म उवाच कुशिकस्तु मुनेर्वाक्यं च्यवनस्य महात्मनः॥ श्रुत्वा हृष्टोऽभवद् राजा वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह।
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words of the great ascetic Chyavana, king Kushika became filled with joy, and answered as followएवमस्त्विति धर्मात्मा तदा भरतसत्तम॥

sn: पुनरेव नराधिपम्। वरार्थं चोदयामास तमुवाच स पार्थिवः॥ बाढमेवं करिष्यामि कामं त्वत्तो महामुने।
en: Indeed, O best of the Bharatas, he saidSo be it! Gifted with high energy, Chyavana once more addressed the king, and urged him to accept a boon from himself. The king replied, Very well. From you, O great ascetic, I shall obtain the fruition of my wish.

sn: च्यवनस्तु महातेजाः ब्रह्मभूतं कुलं मेऽस्तु धर्मे चास्य मनो भवेत्॥ एवमुक्तस्तथेत्येवं प्रत्युक्त्वा च्यवनो मुनिः। अभ्यनुज्ञाय नृपति तीर्थयात्रा ययौ तदा॥ एतत् ते कथितं सर्वमशेषेण मया नृप। भृगूणां कुशिकानां च अभिसम्बन्धकारणम्॥
en: Let my family become invested with the dignity of Brahmanahood, and let it always set its heart upon virtue. The ascetic Chyavana, thus solicited, granted the king's prayer, and bidding farewell to the king, started on his intended sojourn to the sacred waters. I have now told you everything, O Bharata, relating to your questions, viz., how the Bhrigus and the Kushikas became connected with each other by marriage.

sn: यथोक्तमृषिणा चापि तदा तदभवन्नृप। जन्म रामस्य च मुनेर्विश्वामित्रस्य चैव हि॥
en: Indeed, O king, everything took place as the Rishi Chyavana had said. The birth of Rama (of Bhrigu's race) and of Vishvamitra (of Kushika's race) happened in the way that Chyavana had said,

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मुह्यामीव निशम्याध चिन्तयानः पुनः पुनः। हीनां पार्थिवसंघातैः श्रीमद्भिः पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said I am stupefied, O grandfather, to hear your words! Thinking that the Earth is now destitute of a very large number of kings all of whom were gifted with great prosperity, my heart becomes filled with grief.

sn: प्राप्य राज्यानि शतशो महीं जित्वाथ भारत। कोटिशः पुरुषान् हत्वा परितप्ये पितामह॥
en: Having conquered the Earth and acquired hundreds of kingdoms, O Bharata, I turn with grief, O grandfather, at the thought of the millions of men I have killed.

sn: का नु तासां वरस्त्रीणां समवस्था भविष्यति। या हीनाः पतिभिः पुत्रैर्मातुलैर्भ्रातृभिस्तथा॥
en: Alas, what will the condition be of those foremost ladies who have been deprived by us of husbands and sons and maternal uncles and brothers?

sn: वयं हि तान् कुरून् हत्वा ज्ञातींश्च सुहृदोऽपि वा। अवाक्शीर्षाः पतिष्यामो नरके नात्र संशयः॥
en: Having killed those Kurus our kinsmen, that is, and our friends and wellwisherswe shall have to sink in hell with heads hanging downwards. There is no doubt of this.

sn: शरीरं योक्तुमिच्छामि तपसोग्रेण भारत। उपदिष्टमिहेच्छामि तत्त्वतोऽहं विशाम्पते॥
en: I wish, O Bharata, to afflict my body with, severe, penances. With that end in view, O king. I wish to receive instructions from you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरस्य तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा भीष्मो महामनाः। परीक्ष्य निपुणं बुद्ध्या युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said The great Bhishma, hearing these words of Yudhishthira, reflected upon them acutely with the help of his understanding, and addressed Yudhishthira in reply.

sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु वक्ष्यामि यत् त्वयि। या गतिः प्राप्यते येन प्रेत्यभावे विशाम्पते॥
en: Bhishma said Hear what I say to you. It is highly wonderful and is a great mystery. The subject is the ends that creatures acquire after death as the rewards of particular acts or courses of conduct they follow.

sn: तपसा प्राप्यते स्वर्गस्तपसा प्राप्यते यशः। आयुः प्रकृर्षो भोगाश्च लभ्यन्ते तपसा विभो॥
en: One goes to Heaven by penances. By penances one acquires fame. By penances, O mighty king, one lives long and gets all articles of enjoyment.

sn: रहस्यमद्भुतं चैव ज्ञानं विज्ञानमारोग्यं रूपं सम्पत् तथैव च। सौभाग्यं चैव तपसा प्राप्यते भरतर्षभ।॥
en: By penances one acquires knowledge, science, health and freedom from disease, beauty of person, prosperity and blessedness, O chief of Bharata's race.

sn: धनं प्राप्नोति तपसा मौनेनाज्ञां प्रयच्छति। उपभोगांस्तु दानेन ब्रह्मचर्येण जीवितम्॥ अहिंसायाः फलं रूपं दीक्षाया जन्म वै कुले। फलमूलाशिनां राज्यं स्वर्गः पर्णाशिनां भवेत्॥
en: By penances one acquires riches. By observing the vow of silence one succeeds in bringing the whole world under his sway. By making gifts one gets all kinds of enjoyable articles. By observing the rite of Diksha one acquires birth in a good and high family. Those who spend their lives living upon only fruits and roots succeed in acquiring kingdom and sovereignty. Those who live upon the leaves of plants and trees as their food succeed in going to Heaven.

sn: पयोभक्षो दिवं याति दानेन द्रविणाधिकः। गुरुशुश्रूषया विद्या नित्यश्राद्धेन संततिः॥
en: One who live upon water only attains to Heaven. By making gifts one simply increases his wealth. By serving with reverence his preceptor, acquires learning. By performing Shraddhas every day in honour of his Departed Manes, one acquires a large number of children.

sn: गवाढ्यः शाकदीक्षाभिः स्वर्गमाहुस्तृणाशिनाम्। स्त्रियस्त्रिषवणं स्नात्वा वायुं पीत्वा क्रतुं लभेत्॥
en: By observing Diksha upon potherbs and vegetables, one acquires a large number of kine. Those who live upon grass and straw succeed in going to Heaven. By bathing thrice every day with necessary rites, one acquires a large number of waves. By drinking the air alone, one acquires residence in the regions of Prajapati.

sn: नित्यस्नायी भवेद् दक्षः संध्ये तु द्वे जपन् द्विजः। मरूं साधयतो राजन् नाकपृष्ठमनाशके॥
en: one The Brahmana who bathes every day and recites sacred Mantras in the two twilights, becomes possessed of the position of Daksha himself. By adoring the deities in a forest or desert, one acquires a kingdom or sovereignty, and by observing the vow of relinquishing the body by a long fast, one goes to the celestial region.

sn: स्थण्डिले शयमानानां गृहाणि शयनानि च। चीरवल्कलवासोभिर्वासांस्याभरणानि च।॥
en: One having penances for wealth and always passing his days in Yoga obtains good beds and seats and Vehicles. Renouncing the body by entering a burning fire, one becomes an object of respect in the region of Brahman.

sn: शय्यासनानि यानानि योगयुक्ते तपोधने। अग्निप्रवेशे नियतं ब्रह्मलोके महीयते॥
en: Those who lie on the hard and bare ground acquire houses and beds. Those who clothe themselves in rags and barks get good dresses and ornaments.

sn: रसानां प्रतिसंहारात् सौभाग्यमिह विन्दति। आमिषप्रतिसंहारात् प्रजा ह्यायुष्मती भवेत्॥
en: By avoiding the several agreeable tastes one succeeds in winning great prosperity. By abstaining from meat and fish, one gets longlived children.

sn: उदवासं वसेद् यस्तु स नराधिपतिर्भवेत्। सत्यवादी नररेष्ठ दैवतैः सह मोदते॥
en: One who passes sometime in Udavasa, mode of life, becomes the very lord of the celestial region. The man who speaks the truth, O best of men, succeeds in sporting happily with the celestials themselves.

sn: कीर्तिर्भवति दानेन तथाऽऽरोग्यमहिंसया। द्विजशुश्रूधया राज्यं द्विजत्वं चापि पुष्कलम्॥
en: By making gifts one acquires great fame on account of his high achievements. By abstention from cruelty, one acquires health and freedom from disease. By serving the Brahmanas with respect, one acquires kingdom and sovereignty, and the high position of a Brahmana.

sn: पानीयस्य प्रदानेन कीर्तिर्भवति शाश्वती। अन्नस्य तु प्रदानेन तृप्यन्ते कामभोगतः॥
en: By making gifts of water and other drinks, one acquires eternal fame on account of high achievements. By making gifts of food, one acquires various articles of enjoyment.

sn: सान्त्वदः सर्वभूतानां सर्वशोकैर्विमुच्यते। देवशुश्रूषया राज्यं दिव्यं रूपं नियच्छति॥
en: One who gives peace to all creatures, (by refraining to do them any injury), becomes freed from every region. By serving the gods, one obtains a kingdom and celestial beauty,

sn: दीपालोकप्रदानेन चक्षुष्मान् भवते नरः। प्रेक्षणीयप्रदानेन स्मृति मेधां च विन्दति।॥
en: By presenting lights at places which are dark and frequented by men, one acquires a good eyesight. By giving away good and beautiful objects, one acquires a good memory and understanding.

sn: गन्धमाल्यप्रदानेन कीर्तिर्भवति पुष्कला। केशश्मश्रु धारयतामग्र्या भवति संततिः॥
en: By distributing scents and garlands, one acquires farreaching fame. Those who abstain from shaving off their hair and beards, get excellent children.

sn: उपवासं च दीक्षां च अभिषेकं च पार्थिव। कृत्वा द्वादशवर्षाणि वीरस्थानाद् विशिष्यते॥
en: By observing fasts and initiation and baths, O Bharata, for twelve years one acquires a region which is superior to that attainable by unreturning heroes.

sn: दासीदासमलङ्करान् क्षेत्राणि च गृहाणि च। ब्रह्मदेयां सुतां दत्त्वा प्राप्नोति मनुजर्षभ॥
en: By conferring one's daughter on an eligible bridegroom according to the Brahma form, one gets, O best of men, male and female slaves and ornaments and fields and houses.

sn: क्रतुभिश्चोपवासैश्च त्रिदिवं याति भारत। लभते च शिवं ज्ञानं फलपुष्पप्रदो नरः॥
en: By celebrating sacrifices and observing fasts, one goes to the celestial region, O Bharata. The man who gives away fruits and flowers succeeds in gaining sacred knowledge.

sn: सुवर्णशृङ्गैस्तु विराजितानां गवां सहस्रस्य नरः प्रदानात्। मित्येवमाहुर्दिवि देवसंघाः॥
en: The man who gives away a thousand kine with horns bedecked with gold, succeeds in acquiring Heaven. This has been declared by the very deities in a celestial assemblage.

sn: प्रयच्छते यः कपिलां सवत्सां कांस्योपदोहां कनकाग्रशृङ्गीम्। तैस्तैर्गुणैः कामदुहास्य भूत्वा नरं प्रदातारमुपैति सा गौः॥
en: One who gives away a Kapila cow with her calf, with a brazen pot for milking, with horns bedecked with gold, and possessed of various other accomplishments, obtains the fruition of all his desires from that cow.

sn: स्तावत् कालं प्राप्य स गोप्रदानात्। मासप्तमं तारयते परत्र॥
en: Such a person, on account of that act of gift, lives in the celestial region for as many years as there are hairs on the body of the cow and rescues in the next world his sons and grandsons and all his family to the seventh degree.

sn: सदक्षिणां काञ्चनारुशृङ्गी कांस्योपदोहां द्रविणोत्तरीयाम्। धेनुं तिलानां ददतो द्विजाय लोका वसूनां सुलभा भवन्ति॥
en: That man gets to the regions of the Vasus who gives away a cow with horns beautifully decorated with gold, accompanied with a brazen jar for milking, along with a piece of cloth embroidered with gold, a measure of sesame and a sum of money as gift.

sn: स्वकर्मभिर्मानवं संनिरुद्धं तीव्रान्धकारे नरके पतन्तम्। महार्णवे नौरिव वायुयुक्ता दानं गवां तारयते परत्र॥
en: A gift of kine rescues the giver in the next world when he finds himself falling into the deep darkness of hell and fettered by his own deeds in this world, like a boat with sails that have caught the air rescuing a person drowning in the ocean.

sn: यो ब्रह्मदेयां तु ददाति कन्यां भूमिप्रदानं च करोति विप्रे। ददाति चान्नं विधिवच्च यश्च स लोकमाप्नोति पुरंदरस्य॥
en: He who confers a daughter according to the Brahma form upon an eligible person, or who makes a gift of land to a Brahmana, or who gives food according to due rites, succeeds in attaining to the region of Indra.

sn: नैवेशिकं सर्वगुणोपपन्नं ददाति वै यस्तु नरो द्विजाय। स्वाध्यायचारित्र्यगुणान्विताय तस्यापि लोकाः कुरुघूत्तरेषु॥
en: That man who presents a house, furnished with every sort of furniture to Brahmana given to Vedic studies and endued with every accomplishment and good behaviour, lives in the country of UttaraKurus.

sn: धुर्यप्रदानेन गवां तथा वै लोकानवाप्नोति नरो वसूनाम्। स्वर्गाय चाहस्तु हिरण्यदानं ततो विशिष्टं कनकप्रदानम्॥
en: By making gifts of draft bullocks, a person acquires the region of the Vasus. Gift of gold secures Heaven. Gift of pure gold yields greater merit still.

sn: छत्रप्रदानेन गृहं वरिष्ठं यानं तथोपानहसम्प्रदाने। वस्त्रप्रदानेन फलं स्वरूपं गन्धप्रदानात् सुरभिर्नरः स्यात्॥
en: By making gift of an umbrella, one acquires a palatial residence. By making gift of a pair of sandals or shoes, one acquires good cars, The reward of cloths, is personal beauty, and by making gifts of scents, one gets a fragrant body in next life.

sn: पुष्पोपगं वाथ फलोपंग वा यः पादपं स्पर्शयते द्विजाया सश्रीकमृद्धं बहुरत्नपूर्ण लभत्ययत्नोपगतं गृहं वै॥
en: One who gives flowers and fruits and plants and trees to a Brahmana, acquires, without any toil, a palatial residence containing beautiful women and plenty of riches.

sn: भक्ष्यानपानीयरसप्रदाता सर्वान् समाप्नोति रसान् प्रकामम्। प्रतिश्रयाच्छादनसम्प्रदाता प्राप्नोति तान्येव न संशयोऽत्र॥
en: The giver of food and drink of different tastes and other articles of enjoyment succeeds in acquiring profuse supply of such articles. The giver, again, of houses and cloths get articles of a similar nature. There is no doubt in this.

sn: स्रग्धूपगन्धाननुलेपनानि स्नानानि माल्यानि च मानवो यः। स्तथाभिरूपश्च नरेन्द्र लोके॥
en: That person who makes gifts of garlands and incense and scents and unguents and the articles needed by men after a bath, and garlands to Brahmanas, becomes freed from cvery disease and, possessed of personal beauty, sports in joy in the region reserved for great kings.

sn: बीजैरशून्यं शयनैरुपेतं दद्याद् गृहं यः पुरुषो द्विजाय। पुण्याभिरामं बहुरत्नपूर्ण लभत्यधिष्ठानवरं स राजन्॥
en: That man, O king, who presents to a Brahmana a house that is stored with grain, furnished with beds, full of riches, auspicious, and delightful, acquires a palatial residence.

sn: सुगन्धचित्रास्तरणोपधानं दद्यान्नरो यः शयनं द्विजाय। रूपान्वितां पक्षवती मनोज्ञां भार्यामयत्नोपगतां लभेत् सः।
en: He who gives to a Brahmana a good bed perfumed with fragrant scents, covered with an excellent sheet, and pillows, gets without any effort on his part a beautiful wife, belonging to a respectable family and of agreeable manners.

sn: पितामहस्यानवरो वीरशायी भवेन्नरः। नाधिकं विद्यते यस्मादित्याहुः परमर्षयः॥
en: The man who takes to a hero's bed on the field of battle becomes the equal of the Grandfather Brahman himself. There is no end that is higher than this. Even this is what the great Rishis have said,

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रीतात्मा कुरुनन्दनः। नाश्रमेऽरोचयद् वासं वीरमार्गाभिकाझ्या॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words of his grandfather, Yudhishthira, the delighter of the Kurus, became anxious to get the end reserved for heroes and no longer expressed any disgust for leading a domestic mode of life.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरः प्राह पाण्डवान् पुरुषर्षभा पितामहस्य यद् वाक्यं तद् वो रोचत्विति प्रभुः।।४३
en: Then, O foremost of men, Yudhishthira, addressing all the other sons of Pandu, said to them Let the words which our grandfather has said, command your faith.'

sn: ततस्तु पाण्डवाः सर्वे द्रौपदी च यशस्विनी। युधिष्ठिरस्य तद् वाक्यं बाढमित्यभ्यपूजयन्॥
en: At this, all the Pandavas with the famous Draupadi amongst them, highly spoke of the words of Yudhishthira and said, yes.'

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आरामाणां तडागानां यत् फलं कुरुपुङ्गवा तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि त्वत्तोऽद्य भरतर्षभ॥
en: Yudhishthira said I wish, O Bharata, chief to hear from you what the rewards are, O best of the Kurus, of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: भीष्म उवाच सुप्रदर्शा बलवती चित्रा धातुविभूषिता। उपेता सर्वभूतैश्च श्रेष्ठा भूमिरिहोच्यते॥
en: Bhishma said A piece of land on a best sight, fertile, situate in the midst of charming adorned with various kinds of metals, and inhabited by all sorts of creatures, Is considered as the foremost of spots.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तस्याः क्षेत्रविशेषाश्च तडागानां च बन्धनम्। औदकानि च सर्वाणि प्रवक्ष्याम्यनुपूर्वशः॥
en: A particular portion of such land should be chosen for digging a tank. I shall tell you, in due order, the different kinds of tanks. I shall also tell you what kinds of tanks. I shall also tell you what the merits also are of the digging of tanks.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तडागानां च वक्ष्यामि कृतानां चापि ये गुणाः। त्रिषु लाकेषु सर्वत्र पूजनीयस्तडागवान्॥
en: The man who causes a tank to be dug becomes entitled to the respect and adoration of the three worlds.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: अथवा मित्रसदनं मैत्रं मित्रविवर्धनम्। कीर्तिसंजननं श्रेष्ठं तडागानां निवेशनम्॥
en: A tank full of water is as agreeable and beneficial as the house of a friend. It is gratifying to the Sun himself. It also helps the growth of the celestials. It is the foremost of all things that lead to fame.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: धर्मस्यार्थस्य कामस्य फलमाहुर्मनीषिणः। तडागसुकृतं देशे क्षेत्रमेकं महाश्रयम्॥ चतुर्विधानां भूतानां तडागमुपलक्षयेत्। तडागानि च सर्वाणि दिशन्ति श्रियमुत्तमाम्॥
en: The wise have said that the excavation of a tank brings on Virtue, Profit and Pleasure. A tank is said to be properly excavated, if it is made on a piece of land that is inhabited by respectable persons. A tank is said to be necessary for all the four purposes of living creatures. Thanks, again, are considered as forming the excellent beauty of a country.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: देवा मनुष्यगन्धर्वा: पितरोरगराक्षसाः। स्थावराणि च भूतानि संश्रयन्ति जलाशयम्॥
en: The celestials, human beings, Gandharvas. Departed Manes Uragas, Rakshasas, and even immobile beings, all resort to a tank full of water as their refuge.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तस्मात् तांस्ते प्रवक्ष्यामि तडागे ये गुणाः स्मृताः। या च तत्र फलावाप्तिर्ऋषिभिः समुदाहृता॥
en: I shall, therefore, recite to you the merits attached to tanks as described by great Rishis, and the rewards in store for persons who cause them to be excavated.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: वर्षाकाले तडागे सलिलं यस्य तिष्ठति। अग्निहोत्रफलं तस्य फलमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: The wise have said that man acquires the merit of an Agnihotra sacrifice in whose tank water is held in the season of rains.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: शरत्काले तु सलिलं तडागे यस्य तिष्ठति। गोसहस्रस्य स प्रेत्य लभते फलमुत्तमम्॥
en: The high reward in the world that is reaped by the person who makes a gift of a thousand kine is acquired by that man in whose tank water is held in the season of autumn.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: हेमन्तकाले सलिलं तडागे यस्य तिष्ठति। स वै बहुसुवर्णस्य यज्ञस्य लभते फलम्॥
en: That person in whose tank water lics in the cold season acquires the merit of the wight who performs a sacrifice with profuse gifts of gold.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तु यस्य वै शैशिरे काले तडागे सलिलं भवेत्। तस्याग्निष्टोमयज्ञस्य फलमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: That person in whose tank water lies in the season of dew, acquires, the wise have said, the merits of an Agnishtoma sacrifice.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तडागं सुकृतं यस्य वसन्ते तु महाश्रयम्। अतिरात्रस्य यज्ञस्य फलं स समुपाश्नुते॥
en: That man in whose wellmade tank water lies in the season of spring, acquires the merit of the Atiratra sacrifice.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: निदाघकाले पानीयं तडागे यस्य तिष्ठति। वाजिमेधफलं तस्य फलं वै मुनयो विदुः॥
en: That man in whose tank water lies in the season of summer, wins, the Rishi say, the merits of a horsesacrifice.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: स कुलं तारयेत् सर्वं यस्य खाते जलाशये। गावः पिबन्ति सलिलं साधवश्च नराः सदा॥
en: That man rescues his whole race in whose tank kine are seen to satisfy their thirst and from which pious men draw their water.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तडागे यस्य गावस्तु पिबन्ति तृषिता जलम्। मृगपक्षिमनुष्याच सोऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत्॥
en: That man in whose tank kine satisfy their thirst as also other animals and birds, and human being, gains the merits of of a horsesacrifice.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: यत् पिबन्ति जलं तत्र स्नायन्ते विश्रमन्ति च। तडागे यस्य तत् सर्वं प्रेत्यानन्त्याय कल्पते।॥
en: Whatever quantity of water is drunk from one's tank and whatever quantity is taken therefrom by others for purposes of bathing, all become stored for the benefit of the excavater of the tank and he enjoys the same eternally in the next world.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: दुर्लभं सलिलं तात विशेषेण परत्र वै। पानीयस्य प्रदानेन प्रीतिर्भवति शाश्वती॥
en: Water, especially in the other world, is difficult to get, O son. A gift of drink yields eternal happiness.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तिलान् ददत पानीयं दीपान् ददत जाग्रत। ज्ञातिभिः सह मोदध्वमेतत् प्रेत्य सुदुर्लभम्॥
en: Make gifts of sesame here. Make gifts of water. Do you also give lamps. While alive and awake, do you sport happily with kinsmen. These are acts which you shall not be able to achieve in the other world.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: सर्वदानैर्गुरुतरं सर्वदानैर्विशिष्यते। पानीयं नरशार्दूल तस्माद् दातव्यमेव हि॥
en: The gift of drink, O chief of men, is superior to every other gift. In point of merit, it is superior to all other gifts. Therefore, do you make gifts of water.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: एवमेतत् तडागस्य कीर्तितं फलमुत्तमम्। अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि वृक्षाणामवरोपणम्॥
en: Thus have the Rishis described the high merits of the excavation of tanks, I shall now describe to you the planting of trees.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: स्थावराणां च भूतानां जातयः षट् प्रकीर्तिताः। वृक्षगुल्मलतावल्ल्यस्त्वक्सारास्तृणजातयः॥
en: Of immobile objects, six classes have been spoken. They are Vrikshas, Gulmas, Latas, Vallis, Tvaksaras, and Trinas of diverse kinds.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: एता जात्यस्तु वृक्षाणां तेषां रोपे गुणस्त्विमे। कीर्तिश्च मानुषे लोके प्रेत्य चैव फलं शुभम्॥
en: These are the several kinds of vegetables. Listen now to the merit of their planting, By planting trees one acquires fame in the world of men and auspicious rewards in the next world.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: लभते नाम लोके च पितृभिश्च महीयते। देवलोके गतस्यापि नाम तस्य न नश्यति॥
en: Such a man is applauded and respected in the world of the Departed Manes. Such a man's name does not die even when he goes to live in the world of celestials.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: अतीतानागते चोभे पितृवशं च भारत। तारयेद् वृक्षरोपी च तस्माद् रोपयेत्॥
en: The man who plants trees rescues the ancestors and descendants of both his paternal and maternal lines. Do you, therefore, plant trees, O Yudhishthira.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तस्य पुत्रा भवन्त्येत पादपा नात्र संशयः। परलोकगतः स्वर्ग लोकांश्चात्पोति सोऽव्ययान्॥
en: The trees that a man plants become the planter's children. There is no doubt in this, Departing from this world, such a man goes to the celestial region, Indeed, he enjoys many cternal regions of bliss.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: पुष्पैः सुरगणान् वृक्षाः फलैचापि तथा पितॄन्। छायया चातिथिं तात पूजयन्ति महीरुहः॥
en: Trees please the deities by their flowers; the Departed Manes by their fruits; and all guests and strangers by the shadow they afford.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: किन्नरोरगरक्षांसि देवगन्धर्वमानवाः। तथा ऋषिगणाश्चैव संश्रयन्ति महीरुहान्॥
en: Kinnaras, Uragas, Rakshasas, deities Gandharvas, and human beings, as also Rishis, all resort to trees as their refuge.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: पुष्पिताः फलवन्तश्च तर्पयन्तीह मानवान्। वृक्षदं पुत्रवद् वृक्षास्तारयन्ति परत्र तु॥
en: Trees that bear flowers and fruits please all men. The planter of trees is saved in the next world by the trees he plants like children saving their own father.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तस्मात् तडागे सवृक्षा रोप्याः श्रेयोऽर्थिना सदा। पुत्रवत् परिपाल्याश्च पुत्रास्ते धर्मतः स्मृताः॥
en: Therefore, the man who is desirous of achieving his own good, should plant trees by the side of tanks and rear them like his own children. The trees which a man plants are, according to both reason and the scriptures, the children of the planter.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तडागकृद् वृक्षरोपी इष्टयज्ञश्च यो द्विजः। एते स्वर्गे महीयन्ते ये चान्ये सत्यवादिनः॥
en: That Brahmana who excavates a tank, and he who plants trees, and he who performs sacrifices, are all adored in the celestial region as men who are devoted to truth fullness of speech.

description: The rewards of the planting of trees and the digging of tanks
sn: तस्मात् तडागं कुर्वीत आरामांश्चैव रोपयेत् यजेच्च विविधैर्यज्ञैः सत्यं च सततं वदेत्॥
en: Hence, one should cause tanks to be excavated and trees to be planted, adore the deities in diverse sacrifices, and speak the truth.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यानीमानि बहिर्वेद्यां दानानि परिचक्षते। तेभ्यो विशिष्टं किं दानं मतं ते कुरुपुङ्गव॥
en: Yudhishthira said Amongst all those gifts mentioned in the work other than the Vedas, which gift, О chief of Kuru's race, is the most superior in your opinion?

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: कौतूहलं हि परमं तत्र मे विद्यते प्रभो। दातारं दत्तमन्वेति यद् दानं तत् प्रचक्ष्व मे॥
en: O powerful one, great is my curiosity in this matter. Do you describe to me that gift which follows the giver to the next world?

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: भीष्म उवाच अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो व्यसने चाप्यनुग्रहः। यच्चाभिलषितं दद्यात् तृषितायाभिचायते॥ दत्तं मन्येत यद् दत्त्वा तद् दानं श्रेष्ठमुच्यते। दत्तं दातारमन्वेति यद् दानं भरतर्षभ॥
en: Bhishma said An assurance to all creatures of love and affection and abstention from every sort of injury, acts of kindness and favour done to a person in distress, gifts, of articles made to one who solicits with thirst and agreeable to the solicitor's wishes, and whatever gifts are made without the giver's ever thinking of them as gifts made by him, form, O chief of Bharata's race, the highest and best of gifts.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: हिरण्यदानं गोदानं पृथिवीदानमेव च। एतानि वै पवित्राणि तारयन्त्यपि दुष्कृतम्॥
en: Gift of gold, gift of kine, and gift of earth,-these are considered as sincleansing. They rescue the giver from his evil deeds.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: एतानि पुरुषव्याघ्र साधुभ्यो देहि नित्यदा। दानानि हि नरं पापान्मोक्षयन्ति न संशयः॥
en: O king, do you always make such gifts, to the righteous. Forsooth, gifts rescue the giver from all his sins.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: यद् यदिष्टतमं लोके यच्चास्य दयितं गृहे। तत् तद् गुणवते देयं तदेवाक्षयमिच्छता॥
en: That person who wishes to make his gifts eternal, should always give to persons gifted with necessary qualifications whatever articles are desired by all and whatever things are the best in his house.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: प्रियाणि लभते नित्यं प्रियदः प्रियकृत् तथा। प्रियो भवति भूतानामिह चैव परत्र च॥
en: The man who makes gifts of agreeable things and who does to others what is agreeable to others, always succeeds in getting things that are agreeable to himself. Such a person certainly becomes agreeable to all, both here and hereafter.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: याचमानमभीमानादनासक्तमकिंचनम्। यो नार्चति यथाशक्ति स नृशंसो युधिष्ठिर॥
en: That man, O Yudhishthira, is a cruel wight, who, through vanity, does not, to the extent of his means, attend to the wishes of the poor and helpless who solicit assistance.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: अमित्रमपि चेद् दीनं शरणैषिणमागतम्। व्यसने योऽनुगृह्णाति स वै पुरुषसत्तमः॥
en: He is, indeed, the foremost of men who shows favour to even an helpless enemy fallen into distress when such enemy comes and prays for help.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: कृशाय कृतविद्याय वृत्तिक्षीणाय सीदते। अपहन्यात् क्षुधां यस्तु न तेन पुरुषः समः॥
en: No man is equal to him who satisfies the hunger of a person who is emaciated, possessed of learning, destitute of the means of support, and weakened by misery.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: क्रियानियमितान् साधून् पुत्रदारैश्च कर्शितान्। अयाचमानान् कौन्तेय सर्वोपायैर्निमन्त्रयेत्॥
en: One should always, O son of Kunti, remove by ever ineans in his power, the distress of the pious observant of vows and acts, who though having no sons and wives and plunged into misery, do not yet solicit others for any kind of help.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: आशिषं ये न देवेषु न च मत्र्येषु कुर्वते। अर्हन्तो नित्यसंतुष्टास्तथा लब्धोपजीविनः॥ आशीविषसमेभ्यश्च तेभ्यो रक्षस्व भारत। तान् युक्तरुपजिज्ञास्यस्तथा द्विजवरोत्तमान्॥
en: Those persons who do not utter blessings upon the deities and men, who are worthy of respect and always contented, and who live upon such alms as they get without begging, are considered as veritable snakes of virulent poison. Do you, O Bharata, always protect yourself from them by making gifts to them. They are capable to make the foremost of Ritwijas. You are to find them out by means of your spies and agents.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: कृतैरावसथैर्नित्यं सप्रेष्यैः सपरिच्छदैः। निमन्त्रयेथाः कौरव्य सर्वकामसुखावहैः॥
en: You should honour those men by gifts of good houses furnished with every necessary article, with slaves and servants, with good dresses and vestments, O son of Kuru, and with all articles bringing on pleasure, and happiness.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: यदि ते प्रतिगृह्णीयुः श्रद्धापूतं युधिष्ठिर। कार्यमित्येव मन्वाना धार्मिकाः पुण्यकर्मिणः॥
en: Righteous men of righteous deeds should make such gifts, moved by the desire that it is their duty to act in that way and not from desire of reaping any regards therefrom. Indeed, good men should act in this way so that the virtuous described above might not, O Yudhishthira, feel any disinclination to accept those gifts sanctified by devotion and faith.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: विद्यास्नाता व्रतस्नाता ये व्यपाश्रित्य जीविनः। गूढस्वाध्यायतपसो ब्राह्मणाः संशितव्रताः॥
en: There are persons bathed in learning and bathed in vows. Without depending upon anybody they get their means of living. These Brahmanas of rigid vows are given to Vedic study and penances without proclaiming their practices to any one. men

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: तेषु शुद्धेषु दान्तेषु स्वदारपरितोषिषु। यत् करिष्यसि कल्याणं तत् ते लोके युधाम्पते॥
en: Whatever gifts you may make to those persons of pure conduct, of thorough mastery over their senses, and always contented with their own married wives, are sure to acquire for you a merit that will accompany you in all the worlds into which you may go.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: यथाग्निहोत्रं सुहुतं सायं प्रातर्द्विजातिना। तथा दत्तं द्विजातिभ्यो भवत्यथ यतात्मसु।॥
en: One reaps the same merit by making gifts to twiceborn persons of controlled souls which one acquires by properly pouring libations to the sacred fire morning and evening.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: एष ते विततो यज्ञः श्रद्धापूतः सदक्षिणः। विशिष्टः सर्वयज्ञेभ्यो ददतस्तात वर्तताम्॥
en: This is the sanctified spread out for you, a sacrifice that is sanctified by devotion and faith and that is accompanied with Dakshina! It is superior to all other sacrifices. Let that sacrifice ceaselessly flow from you as you give away.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: निवापदानसलिलस्तादृशेषु युधिष्ठिर। निवसन् पूजयंश्चैव तेष्वानृण्यं नियच्छिति॥
en: Performed in view of such men, O Yudhishthira, a sacrifice in which the water that is sprinkled for dedicating gifts forms the oblations in honour of the Departed Manes, and devotion and worship rendered to such superior men, serves to free one of the debts he owes to the deities.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: य एवं नैव कुप्यन्ते न लुभ्यन्ति तृणेष्वपि। त एव नः पूज्यतमा ये चापि प्रियवादिनः॥
en: Those persons who do not give way to anger and who never desire to take even a blade of grass belonging to others, as also they who are of sweet speech, deserve to receive from us the most respectful adorations.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: एते न बहु मन्यन्ते न प्रवर्तन्ति चापरे। पुत्रवत् परिपाल्यास्ते नमस्तेभ्यस्तथाभयम्॥
en: Such persons and others never pay their regards to the giver. Nor do they try for obtaining gifts. They should, however, be maintained by givers as they maintain their own sons. I bend my head to them. From them also proceeds fearlessness.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्या मृदुब्रह्मधरा हि ते। क्षात्रेणापि हि संसृष्टं तेजः शाम्यति वै द्विजे॥
en: Ritwijas, Priests and Preceptors, when well-read in the Vedas and when behaving mildly towards disciples, become such. Forsooth, Kshatriya energy loses its force upon a Brahmana when it meets him.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: अस्ति मे बलवानस्मि राजास्मीति युधिष्ठिर। ब्राह्मणान् मा च पर्यश्रीर्वासोभिरशनेन च॥
en: Thinking that you are a king, that you are gifted with great power, and that you have riches do, not, O Yudhishthira, enjoy your affluence without giving anything to the Brahmanas.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: यच्छोभार्थं बलार्थं वा वित्तमस्ति तवानघ। तेन ते ब्राह्मणाः पूज्याः स्वधर्ममनुतिष्ठता॥
en: Observing the duties of your own caste, do you adore the Brahmanas with whatever riches you have, O sinless one, for purposes of adornment or sustaining your power.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: नमस्कार्यास्तथा विप्रा वर्तमाना यथातथम्। यथासुखं यथोत्साह ललन्तु त्वयि पुत्रवत्॥
en: Let the Brahmanas live in whatever way they like. You should always bend your head to them with respect. Let them always rejoice in you as your children, living happily and according to their wishes.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: को ह्यक्षयप्रसादानां सुहृदामल्पतोषिणाम्। वृत्तिमहत्यवक्षेप्तुं त्वदन्यः कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Who else save you, O best of the Kurus, can provide the means of livelihood for such Brahmana gifted with eternal contentment, as are your wellwishers, and as are pleased with only a little?

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: यथा पत्याश्रयो धर्मः स्त्रीणां लोके सनातनः। सदैव सा गतिर्नान्या तथास्माकं द्विजातयः॥
en: As women have one eternal duty, in this world, viz., dependence upon, and the obedient service of their husbands, and as such duty as are forms their only end, so is the service of Brahmanas our eternal duty and end.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: यदि नो ब्राह्मणास्तात संत्यजेयुरपूजिताः। पश्यन्तो दारुणं कर्म सततं क्षत्रिये स्थितम्॥ अवेदानामयज्ञानामलोकानामवर्तिनाम्। कस्तेषां जीवितेनार्थस्त्वां विना ब्राह्मणाश्रयम्॥
en: If on seeing cruelties and other sinful deeds in Kshatriyas, the Brahmanas, O son, unhonoured by us leave us all, I say, of what use would life be to us, in the absence of all contact with the Brahmanas, especially as we shall then have to carry on our existence without being able to study the Vedas, to celebrate sacrifices, to hope for worlds of bliss hereafter, and to perform great deeds?

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि यथा धर्मं सनातनम्। राजन्यो ब्राह्मणान् राजन् पुरा परिचचार ह॥
en: I shall, about it, tell you what the eternal practice is. Formerly, O king, the Kshatriyas used to serve the Brahmanas.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: वैश्यो राजन्यमित्येव शूद्रो वैशमति श्रुतिः। दूराच्छूद्रेणोपचर्यो ब्राह्मणोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन्॥
en: The Vaishya likewise used in those days to adore the Kshatriya, and the Shudra to adore the Vaishya. This is what is heard. The Brahmana was like a burning fire. Without being able to touch him or approach his presence, the Shudra used to serve the Brahmana from a distance.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: संस्पर्शपरिचर्यस्तु वैश्येन क्षत्रियेण च। मृदुभावान् सत्यशीलान् सत्यधर्मानुपालकान्॥
en: It was only the Kshatriya and the Vaishya who could serve the Brahmana hy touching his bcdy or approaching his presence. The Brahmanas are gifted with a mild disposition. They are truthful in conduct. They are followers of the true religion.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: आशीविषानिव क्रुद्धास्तानुपाचरत द्विजान्। अपरेषां परेषां च परेभ्यश्चापि ये परे॥
en: When angry, they are like snakes of drcadful poison. Such being their nature, do you, O Yudhishthira, serve and attend them with obedience and respect. The Brahmanas are superior to those who are higher than the high and the low.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: क्षत्रियाणां प्रतपतां तेजसा च बलेन च। ब्राह्मणेष्वेव शाम्यन्ति तेजांसि च तपांसि च॥
en: The energy and penances of those Kshatriyas who blaze forth with energy and power, become powerless and neutralised when they come in in contact with the Brahmanas.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: न मे पिता प्रियतरो न त्वं तात तथा प्रियः। न मे पितुः पिता राजन् न चात्मा न च जीवितम्।।
en: My father himself is not dearer to me than the Brahmanas. My mother is not dearer to me than they. My grandfather, O king, is not dcarer, my own life is not dearer, O king, to me than the Brahmanas.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: त्वत्तश्च मे प्रियतरः पृथिव्यां नास्ति कश्चन। त्वत्तोऽपि मे प्रियतरा ब्राह्मणा भरतर्षभ॥
en: On Earth there is nothing, O Yudhishthira, that is dearer to me than you. But, O chief of Bharata's race, the Brahmanas are dearer to me than even you.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: ब्रवीमि सत्यमेतच्च यथाहं पाण्डुनन्दन। तेन सत्येन गच्छेयं लोकान् यत्र च शान्तनुः॥
en: I tell you truly, O son of Pandu! I swear by this truth, by which I hope to acquire all those blissful regions that have been Shantanu's.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: पश्येयं च सतां लोकाञ्छुचीन् ब्रह्मपुरस्कृतान्। तत्र मे तात गन्तव्यमह्नाय च चिराय च॥
en: I see those sacred regions with Brahma shining conspicuously before them. I shall go there, O son, and live in them eternally.

description: A description of the gifts which fellows the giver to the next world
sn: सोऽहमतादृशाल्लोकान् दृष्ट्वा भरतसत्तम। यन्मे कृतं ब्राह्मणेषु न तप्ये तेन पार्थिव॥
en: Seeing these regions. O best of the Bharatas. I am filled with joy at the thought of all these acts which I have done in aid and honour of the Brahmanas, O king.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यौ च स्यातां चरणेनोपपन्नौ यौ विद्यया सदृशौ जन्मना चा मयाचमानाय च याचते च॥।॥
en: Yudhishthira said To which of two Brahmanas, when both happen to be equally pure in conduct, equally, gifted with learning and purity, of birth and blood, but differing from each other in only this, viz., the one solicits and the other does not-I ask O grandfather, would a gift be more meritorious?

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: भीष्म उवाच श्रेयो वै याचतः पार्थ दानमाहुरयाचते। अर्हत्तमो वै धृतिमान् कृपणादधृतात्मनः॥
en: Bhishma said It has been said, O son of Pritha, that a gift made to an unsoliciting person yields greater merit than one made to a person who begs. One endued with contentment is certainly more deserving than that person who is shorn of that virtue and is, therefore, helpless amidst the storms and buffets of the world.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: क्षत्रियो रक्षणधृतिर्ब्राह्मणोऽनर्थनाधृतिः। ब्राह्मणो धृतिमान् विद्वान् देवान् प्रीणाति तुष्टिमान्॥३
en: The firmness of a Kshatriya consists in the protection he gives to others. The firmness of a Brahmana consists in his refusal to beg. The Brahmana endued with steadiness and learning and contentment gladdens the celestials.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: याच्यमाहुरनीशस्य अभिहारं च भारत। उद्वेजयन्ति याचन्ति सदा भूतानि दस्युवत्॥
en: The wise have said that an act of begging on the part of a poor man is a great reproach. Thosc persons who solicit others are said to annoy the world like thieves and robbers.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: प्रियते याचमानो वै न जातु म्रियते ददत्। ददत् संजीवयत्येनमात्मानं च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: The person who solicits is said to meet with death. The giver, however, is said not to meet with death. The giver is said to give life to him who solicits. By an act of gift, O Yudhishthira, the giver is said to rescue his own self also.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मो याचते यत् प्रदीयते। अयाचतः सीदमानान् सर्वोपायैर्निमन्त्रयेत्॥
en: Mercy is a very high virtue. Led by niercy people make gifts to those who solicit. Those, however, who do not beg but are sunk into poverty and distress, should be respectfully invited for receiving help.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: यदि वै तादृशा राष्ट्रान् वसेयुस्ते द्विजोत्तमाः। भस्मच्छन्नानिवाग्नीस्तान् बुध्येथास्त्वं प्रयत्नतः॥
en: If such Brahmanas, who must be considered as the foremost of their order, live in your kingdom, you should consider them as fire covered with ashes.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: तपसा दीप्यमानास्ते दहेयुः पृथिवीमपि। अपूज्यमानाः कौरव्य पूजार्हास्तु तथाविधाः॥
en: Burning with penances, they are capable of consuming the whole Earth. Such persons, O son of Kuru's race though not generally adored, should still he considered as worthy of adoration in every way.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: पूज्या हि ज्ञानविज्ञानतपोयोगसमन्विताः। तेभ्यः पूजां प्रयुञ्जीथा ब्राह्मणेभ्यः परंतप॥
en: Gifted with knowledge and spiritual vision and penances and Yoga, such persons always deserve our adoration. O scorcher of enemies, do you always offer adoration to such Brahmanas.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: ददद् बहुविधान् दायानुपागच्छन्नयाचताम्। यदग्निहोत्रे सुहुते सायंप्रातर्भवेत् फलम्॥
en: One should go of his own accord to those foremost of Brahmanas who do not solicit any body and make gifts to them of various kinds of wealth in abundance. The merit that comes from properly pouring libations on the sacred fire every morning and evening, is acquired by are the person who makes gifts to a Brahmana endowed with learning, with the Vedas, and with high and excellent vows.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: विद्यावेदव्रतवति तद्दानफलमुच्यते। विद्यावेदव्रतस्नातानव्यापाश्रयजीविनः॥ गूढस्वाध्यायतपसो ब्राह्मणान् संशितव्रतान्। कृतैरावसथैर्हद्यैः सप्रेष्यैः सपरिच्छदैः॥
en: You should, O son of Kunti, invite those foremost of Brahmanas, who are cleansed by learning and the Vedas and vows, who live, in independence, whose Vedic studies and penances concealed without being announced from the house top, and who observe excellent vows, and honour them with gifts of well-built and charming houses containing servitors and robes and furniture, and all other articles of pleasure and enjoyment.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: निमन्त्रयेथाः कौरव्य कामैश्चान्येर्द्विजोत्तमान्। अपि ते प्रतिगृह्वीयुः श्रद्धोपेतं युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Knowing all duties and possessed of minute vision, those foremost of Brahmanas, O Yudhishthira, may accept the gifts offered to them with devotion and respect, thinking, that they should not refuse and disappoint the giver.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: कार्यमित्येव मन्वाना धर्मज्ञाः सूक्ष्मदर्शिनः। अपि ते ब्राह्मणा भुक्त्वा गताः सोद्धरणान् गृहान्।।
en: You should invite those Brahmanas whose wives wait for their return like tillers in expectation of rain. Having fed them well, you should present additional food to them so that upon their return home their expectant wives might be able to distribute that food among their children who had clamoured for food but who had been consoled with promises.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: येषां दाराः प्रतीक्षन्ते पर्जन्यमिव कर्षकाः। अन्नानि प्रातःसवने नियता ब्रह्मचारिणः॥
en: Brahmacharins of controlled senses, O son, by eating at one's house in the forenoon, cause the three sacrificial fires to be pleased with the householder at whose house they eat.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: ब्राह्मणास्तात भुञ्जनास्त्रेताग्निं प्रीणयन्त्युत। माध्यन्दिनं ते सवनं ददतस्तात वर्तताम्॥ ।
en: Let the sacrifice of gift proceed in your house at midday, O son, and do you also distribute kine and gold and dresses. By acting thus, you are sure to please the king of the celestials himself.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: गोहिरण्यानि वासांसि तेनेन्द्रः प्रीयतां तव। तृतीयं सवनं ते वै वैश्वदेवं युधिष्ठिर॥
en: That would constitute your third sacrifice, O Yudhishthira, in which offerings are made to the deities, the Departed Manes and the Brahmanas. By such sacrifice you are sure to please the Vishvedevas.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: यद् देवेभ्यः पितृभ्यश्च विप्रेभ्यश्च प्रयच्छसि। अहिंसा सर्वभूतेभ्यः संविभागश्च भागशः॥
en: Let mercy to all creatures, giving to all creatures what is due to them, controlling the senses, renunciation, firmness, and truth, form the final bath of that sacrifice which is formed by gift.

description: The preference of gift one who solicits and to one who does not
sn: दमस्त्यागो धृतिः सत्यं भवत्यवभृथायते। एष ते विततो यज्ञः श्रद्धापूतः सदक्षिणः॥
en: This is the sacrifice that is spread out for you-a sacrifice which is sanctified by devotion and faith, and who has a large sacrificial gift attached to it. This sacrifice which is formed by gift is superior to all other sacrifices. O son, let this sacrifice be always celebrated by you.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दानं यज्ञः क्रिया चेह किंस्वित् प्रेत्य महाफलम् कस्य ज्यायः फलं प्रोक्तं कीदृशेभ्यः कथं कदा॥ एतदिच्छामि विज्ञातुं याथातथ्येन भारत। विद्वन् जिज्ञासमानाय दानधर्मान् प्रचक्ष्व मे॥
en: Yudhishthira said I wish to know fully, O Bharata, where one get the high reward of gifts and sacrifices. Are those rewards acquired here or hereafter? Which amongst these two (viz., Gift and Sacrifice) yields superior merit? To whom should gifts be made? In what manner are gifts and sacrifices to be made? When also are they to be made? I ask you this, O learned sire? Do you discourse to me on the duty of gifts!

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: अन्तर्वेद्यां च यद् दत्तं श्रद्धया चानृशंस्यतः। किंस्विन्नैःश्रेयसं तात तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Do you tell me, O grandfather, what brings on the highest reward, viz., gifts made from the sacrificial platform or those made out of that place?

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: भीष्म उवाच रौद्रं कर्म क्षत्रियस्य सततं तात वर्तते। तस्य वैतानिकं कर्म दानं चैवेह पावनम्॥
en: Bhishma said O son, a Kshatriya is generally engaged in decds of fierceness. In his case, sacrifices and gifts, are considered as cleansing or sanctifying him.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: न तु पापकृतां राज्ञां प्रतिगृह्णन्ति साधवः। एतस्मात् कारणाद् यज्ञैर्यजेद् राजाऽऽप्तदक्षिणैः॥
en: The good and righteous, do not accept the gifts of persons of the royal order, who perpetrate sinful deeds. Therefore, the king should celebrate sacrifices with profuse gifts in the form of Dakshina.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: अथ चेत् प्रतिगृह्वीयुर्दद्यादहरहर्नृपः। श्रद्धामास्थाय परमां पावनं ह्येतदुत्तमम्॥
en: If the good and righteous would accept the gifts made to them, the Kshatriya, O king, should continually make gifts with devotion and faith to them. Gifts yield great merit, and are highly cleansing.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: ब्राह्मणांस्तर्पयन् द्रव्यस्ततो यज्ञे यतव्रतः। मैत्रान् साधून् वेदविदः शीलवृत्ततपोर्जितान्॥
en: Observing vows, one should celebrate sacrifices and please with wealth, such Brahmanas as are friends of all creatures, endued with righteousness, conversant of the Vedas, and pre-eminent for acts, conduct and penances.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: यत् ते ते न करिष्यन्ति कृतं ते न भविष्यति। यज्ञान् साधय साधुभ्यः स्वाद्वन्नान् दक्षिणावतः॥
en: If such Brahmanas do not accept your gifts, no merit will become yours. Do you celebrate sacrifices with profuse Dakshina, and make gifts of good and agreeable food to the righteous.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: इष्टं दत्तं च मन्येथा आत्मानं दानकर्मणा। पूजयेथा याजयूकांस्तवाप्यंशो भवेद् यथा॥
en: By making an act of gift you should consider yourself as performing a sacrifice. You should, with gifts, worship those Brahmanas who perform sacrifices. By doing this you will acquire a share in the merits of those sacrifices of theirs.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: प्रजावतो भरेथाश्च ब्राह्मणान् बहुकारिणः। प्रजावांस्तेन भवति यथा जनयिता तथा॥
en: You should support such Brahmanas as have children and as are capable of sending people to heaven. By acting thus, you are sure to get a large progeny-in fact, as large a progeny as the Prajapati himself.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: यावतः साधुधर्मान् वै सन्तः संवर्धयन्त्युत। सर्वस्वैश्चापि भर्तव्या नरा ये बहुकारिणः॥
en: The righteous support and advance the cause of virtue. One should, by giving up his all, support such men as also those who do good to all creatures.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: समृद्धः सम्प्रयच्छ त्वं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो युधिष्ठिर। धेनूरनडूहोऽन्नानि च्छत्रं वासांस्युपानहौ॥
en: Yourself being rich, do you, Yudhishthira, make gifts to Brahmans of kine and bullocks and food and umbrellas and robes and sandals or shoes.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: आज्यानि यजमानेभ्यस्तथानानि च भारत। अश्ववन्ति च यानानि वेश्मानि शयनानि च॥
en: Do you give to sacrificing Brahmanas clarified butter as also food, and cars and vehicles with horses harnessed thereto, and dwelling houses and mansions and beds.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: एते देया व्युष्टिमन्तो लघूपायाश्च भारत। अजुगुप्सांश्च विज्ञाय ब्राह्मणान् वृत्तिकर्शितान्॥
en: Such gifts yield prosperity and affluence to the giver, and are considered as pure, O Bharata. Those Brahmanas who are not censurable for anything they do, and who have no means of support assigned to them, should be found out.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: उपच्छन्नं प्रकाशं वा वृत्त्या प्रतिपालयेत् राजसूयाश्वमेधाभ्यां श्रेयस्तत् क्षत्रियान् प्रति॥
en: Covertly or publicly, do you maintain such Brahmanas by giving to them the means of support. Such conduct always gives higher benefit to Kshatriyas than the Rajasuya and the Horse-Sacrifices.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: एवं पापैर्विनिर्मुक्तस्त्वं पूतः स्वर्गमाप्स्यसि। संचयित्वा पुनः कोशं यद् राष्ट्र पालयिष्यसि॥
en: Purged off of sin, you are sure of attaining to Heaven. Filling your treasury, you should do good to your kingdom.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: तेन त्वं ब्रह्मभूयत्वमवाप्स्यसि धनानि च। आत्मनश्च परेषां च वृत्तिं संरक्ष भारत॥
en: By such conduct you are sure to acquire immense riches, and become a Brahman (in your next life). Do you, O Bharata, protect your own means as also the means of others people's livelihood.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: पुत्रवच्चापि भृत्यान् स्वान् प्रजाश्च परिपालय। योगः क्षेमश्च ते नित्यं ब्राह्मणेष्वस्तु भारत॥
en: Do you support your servants as your own children. Do you, O Bharata, protect the Brahmanas in the enjoyment of what they have and make gifts, to them of such articles as they have not.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: तदर्थं जीवितं तेऽस्तु मा तेभ्योऽप्रतिपालनम्। अनर्थो ब्राह्मणस्यैष यद् वित्तनिचयो महान्॥
en: Let your life be devoted to the Brahmanas. Let it never be said that you do not grant protection to the Brahmanas. Much wealth, when possessed by a Brahmana; becomes a source of evil to himn.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: श्रिया ह्यभीक्ष्णं संवासो दर्पयेत् सम्प्रमोहयेत्। ब्राह्मणेषु प्रमूढेषु धर्मो विप्रणशेद् ध्रुवम्। धर्मप्रणाशे भूतानामभावः स्यान्न संशयः॥
en: Constant association with riches and prosperity is sure to fill him with pride and cause him to be stupefied. If the Brahmanas become stupefied and steeped in folly., virtue and duties are sure to suffer destruction. Forsooth, if virtue and duty come to an end, it will lead to the destruction of all creatures.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: यो रक्षिभ्यः सम्प्रदाय राजा राष्ट्रं विलुम्पति। यज्ञे राष्ट्राद् धनं तस्मादानयध्वमिति ब्रुवन्॥
en: That king who having amassed riches makes it over to his treasury officers and guards, and then begins to again plunder his kingdom, saying to his officers-Do you bring me as much riches as you can extort from the kingdom.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: यच्चादाय तदाज्ञप्तं भीतं दत्तं सुदारुणम्। यजेद् राजा न तं यज्ञं प्रशंसन्त्यस्य साधवः॥
en: And who spends the riches that is thus collected at his behest under circumstances of fear and cruelty, in the performance of sacrifices, should know that those sacrifices of his, are never highly spoken of by the pious.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: अपीडिताः सुसंवृद्धा ये ददत्यनुकूलतः। तादृशेनाप्युपायेन यष्टव्यं नोद्यमाहृतैः॥
en: The king should celebrate scarifices with such money as is willingly paid to his treasury by prosperous and unpersecuted subjects. Sacrifices should never be celebrated with money got with severity and extortion.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: यदा परिनिषिच्येत निहितो वै यथाविधि। तदा राजा महायज्ञैर्यजेत बहुदक्षिणैः॥
en: The king should then celebrate great sacrifices with large presents in the shape of Dakshina, when on account of his being devoted to the behoof of his subjects the latter bathe him with copious showers of riches brought willingly by them for the purpose.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: वृद्धबालधनं रक्ष्यमन्धस्य कृपणस्य च। न खातपूर्वं कुर्वीत न रुदन्ती धनं हरेत्॥
en: The king should protect the riches of those that are old, of those that are minors, of those that are blind, and of those that are otherwise disqualified. The king should never take any money from his people, if they, in a season of drought, succeed in growing any corn with the help of water obtained from wells. Nor should he take any wealth from weeping women.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: हतं कृपणवित्तं हि राष्ट्र हन्ति नृपश्रियम्। दद्याच्च महतो भोगान् क्षुद्भयं प्रणुदेत् सताम्॥
en: The riches taken from the poor and the helpless is sure to destroy the kingdom and prosperity of the king. The king should always present to the righteous all enjoyable articles in abundance. He should certainly remove the fear of famishing which those men may have.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: येषां स्वादूनि भोज्यानि समवेक्ष्यन्ति बालकाः। नाश्नन्ति विधिवत् तानि किं तु पापतरं ततः॥
en: There are no men more sinful than those upon whose food children look wistfully without being able to eat them duly,

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: यदि ते तादृशो राष्ट्रे विद्वान् सीदेत् क्षुधा द्विजः। भ्रूणहत्यां च गच्छेथाः कृत्वा पापमिवोत्तमम्॥
en: If within your kingdom any learned Brahinana dies with hunger like any of those children, you shall then incur the sin of focticide for having allowed such an act.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: धिक् तस्य जीवितं राज्ञो राष्ट्रे यस्यावसीदति। द्विजोऽन्योवा मनुष्योऽपि शिबिराह वचो यथा॥
en: King Shivi himself had said this, viz.-Fie on that king in whose kingdom a Brahmana or even any other man starves.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: यस्य स्म विषये राज्ञः स्नातकः सीदति क्षुधा। अवृद्धिमेति तद्राष्ट्रं विन्दते सहराजकम्॥
en: That kingdom in which a Brahmana of the Snataka class starves, becomes overwhelmed with adversity. Such a kingdom with its king also incurs reproach.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: क्रोशन्त्यो यस्य वै राष्ट्राधियन्ते तरसा स्त्रियः। क्रोशतां पतिपुत्राणां मृतोऽसौ न च जीवति॥
en: That king is more dead than alive in whose kingdom women are easily abducted from their husbands and sons uttering cries and groans of indignation and grief.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: अरक्षितारं हर्तारं विलोप्तारमनायकम्। तं वै राजकलिं हन्युः प्रजाः सन्ना निघृणम्॥
en: The subjects should arm themselves for killing that king who does not protect them who simply plunders their riches, who confounds all distinctions who is incapable of taking their lead, who is without mercy, and who is considered as the most sinful of kings.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: अहं वो रक्षितेत्युक्त्वा यो न रक्षति भूमिपः। स संहत्य निहन्तव्यः श्वेव सोन्माद आतुरः॥
en: That king who tells his people that he is their protector but who does not or is unable to protect them, should be killed by his subjects in a body like a dog that is affected with the rabies and has become mad.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: पापं कुर्वन्ति यत् किंचित् प्रजा राज्ञा हरक्षिताः। चतुर्थं तस्य पापस्य राजा विन्दति भारत॥
en: A fourth part of whatever sins are committed by the subjects visits that king who does not protect, О Bharata.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: अथाहुः सर्वमेवैति भूयोऽमिति निश्चयः। चतुर्थे मतमस्माकं मनोः श्रुत्वानुशासनम्॥
en: Some authorities say that the whole of those sins visits such a king. Others are of opinion that a half thereof visits him. Bearing in mind, However, the saying of Manu, it is our opinion that a fourth part of such sins visits the unprotecting king.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: शुभं वा यच्च कुर्वन्ति प्रजा राज्ञा सुरक्षिताः। चतुर्थं तस्य पुण्यस्य राजा चाप्नोति भारत॥
en: That king, O Bharata, O Bharata, who affords protection to his subjects gets fourth part of whatever merits his subjects win by living under his protection.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: जीवन्तं त्वानुजीवन्तु प्रजाः सर्वा युधिष्ठिर। पर्जन्यमिव भूतानि महादुममिवाण्डजाः॥
en: Do you, O Yudhishthira, act in such a way that all your subjects, may seek refuge with you as long as you are alive, as all creatures seek the refuge, of the god of rain or as the birds seek the refuge of a large tree.

description: The rewards of gifts in this world and in the next
sn: कुबेरमिव रक्षांसि शतक्रतुमिवामराः। ज्ञातयस्त्वानुजीवन्तु सुहृदश्च परंतप॥
en: Let all your kinsmen and all your friends and well-wishers, O scorcher of enemies, seek refuge with you as the Rakshasas seek Kubera or the gods seek Indra as theirs.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच इदं देयमिदं देयमितीयं श्रुतिरादरात्। बहुदेयाश्च राजानः किंस्विद् दानमनुत्तमम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said People accept with respect the sayings of the Shrutis which say-This is to be given. This other thing is to be given! As regards kings, again, they make gifts of various things to various men. What, however, O grandfather is the best or foremost of all gifts?

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: भीष्म उवाच अतिदानानि सर्वाणि पृथिवीदानमुच्यते। अचला ह्यक्षया भूमिर्दोग्ध्री कामानिहोत्तमान्॥
en: Bhishma said Of all kinds of gifts, the gift of earth is said to be the first. earth is immovable and indestructible. It is capable of giving to him who possesses it all the best things upon which he may like to have.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: दोग्ध्री वासांसि रत्नानि पशून् व्रीहियवांस्तथा। भूमिदः सर्वभूतेषु शाश्वतीरेधते समाः॥
en: It gives dresses and vestments, jewels and gems, animals, paddy, and barley. Amongst all creatures, the giver of earth grows rich for ever and ever.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: यावद् भूमेरायुरिह तावद् भूमिद एधते। न भूमिदानादस्तीह परं किंचिद् युधिष्ठिर॥
en: As long as the earth lasts, so long does the giver thereof grow rich. There is no gift that is higher, O Yudhishthira, than the gift of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अप्यल्पं प्रददुः सर्वे पृथिव्या इति नः श्रुतम्। भूमिमेव ददुःसर्वे भूमि ते भुञ्जते जनाः॥
en: we have heard that all men have given a little quantity of earth. All men have made gifts of earth, hence all men enjoy a little of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: स्वकर्मैवोपजीवन्ति नरा इह परत्र च। भूमिभूतिर्महादेवी दातारं कुरुते प्रियम्॥
en: Whether in this or in the next world, all creatures live subject to their own deeds. Earth is Prosperity's self. She is a powerful goddess. She makes him her lord who makes gifts of her in this life to her people.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: य एतां दक्षिणां दद्यादक्षयां राजसत्तम। पुनर्नरत्वं सम्प्राप्य भवेत् स पृथिवीपतिः॥
en: That person, O best of kings, who gives away earth, which is indestructible, as gift, is born in next life as a man and becomes also a lord of Earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: यथा दानं तथा भोग इति धर्मेषु निश्चयः। संग्रामे वा तनुं जह्याद् दद्याच्च पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: The quantity of one's enjoyment in this life is equal to one's gifts in a pristine life. This is the conclusion pointed out by the scriptures. For a Kshatriya should either give away the Earth in gift or renounce his life in battle.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: इत्येतत् क्षत्रबन्धूनां वदन्ति परमां श्रियम्। पुनाति दत्ता पृथिवी दातारमिति शुश्रुम॥
en: This is the highest source of prosperity to Kshatriyas. We have heard that earth, when given away, cleanses and sanctifies the giver.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अपि पापसमाचारं ब्रह्मघ्नमपि चानृतम्। सैव पापं प्लावयति सैव पापात् प्रमोचयेत्॥
en: The man who is of sinful conduct who is guilty of Brahmanicide and of falsehood, is purified by a gift of earth. Indeed, such a gift rescues even such a sinner from all his sins.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अपि पापकृतां राज्ञां प्रतिगृह्णन्ति साधवः। पृथिवीं नान्यदिच्छन्ति पावनं जननी यथा॥
en: The virtuous accept gifts of earth only and no other thing from sinful kings. Like one's mother, earth, when given away, purifies the giver and the taker.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: नामास्याः प्रियदत्तेति गृह्यं देव्याः सनातनम्। दानं वाप्यथवाऽऽदानं नामास्याः प्रथमं प्रियम्॥
en: This is an eternal and secret name of earth. viz., Priyadatta. Given away or accepted in gift, the name that is dear to her is Priyadatta.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: य एतां विदुषे दद्यात् पृथिवीं पृथिवीपतिः। पृथिव्यामेतदिष्टं स राजा राज्यमितो व्रजेत्॥
en: The gift of earth is desirable. That king who makes a gift of earth to a learned Brahmana, gets from that gift a kingdom.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: पुनश्चासौ जनिं प्राप्य राजवत् स्यान्न संशयः। तस्मात् प्राप्यैव पृथिवीं दद्याद् विप्राय पार्थिवः॥
en: Upon being born again in this world, such a man, forsooth, attains to a position equal to that of a king. Hence, a king, as soon as he gets carth, should make gifts of earth to the Brahmanas.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: नाभूमिपतिना भूमिरधिष्ठेया कथंचन। न चापात्रेण वा ग्राह्या दत्तेदाने न चाचरेत्॥
en: None but a lord of Earth can make gifts of carth. Nor should one who is not a worthy person accept a gift of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: ये चान्ये भूमिमिच्छेयुः कुर्युरेवं न संशयः। यः साधोभूमिमादत्ते न भूमि विन्दते तु सः॥
en: They who desire carth should act thus. That person who takes away earth belonging to a pious person never gets any earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: भूमिं दत्त्वा तु साधुभ्यो विन्दते भूमिमुत्तमाम्। प्रेत्य चेह च धर्मात्मा सम्प्राप्नोति महद् यशः॥
en: By making gifts of earth to the righteous, one gets good carth. Of virtuous soul, such a giver acquires great fame both in this world and in the next.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: यस्य विप्रास्तु शंसन्ति साधोभूमि सदैव हि। न तस्य शत्रवो राजन् प्रशंसन्ति वसुन्धराम्॥
en: That pious king about whom the Brahmanas say——We live on earth given to us by him, is such that his very enemies cannot utter the least reproach about his kingdom.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: यत् किंचित् पुरुषः पापं कुरुते वृत्तिकर्शितः। अपि गोचर्ममात्रेण भूमिदानेन पूयते॥
en: Whatever sins a man commits from want of the means of livelihood, are all washed off by gift of only so much earth as is covered by a cowhide.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: येऽपि संकीर्णकर्माणो राजानो रौद्रकर्मिणः। तेभ्यः पवित्रमाख्येयं भूमिदानमनुत्तमम्॥
en: Those kings who are mean in their acts or are of fierce deeds, should be taught that gift of earth is highly purifying and is at the same time the highest gift.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अल्पान्तरमिदं शश्वत् पुराणा मेनिरे जनाः। यो यजेताश्वमेधेन दद्याद् वा साधवे महीम्॥
en: The ancients thought that there is always very little difference between the man who celebrates a Horse-Sacrifice and him who makes a gift of earth to one who is righteous.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अपि चेत्सुकृतं कृत्वा शङ्करन्नपि पण्डिताः। अशक्यमेकमेवैतद् भूमिदानमनुत्तमम्॥
en: The learned doubt the acquision of merit which all other pious acts yield. The only act about which they are dead certain, is the of earth which, indeed, is the foremost of all gifts.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: सुवर्ण रजतं वस्त्रं मणिमुक्तावसूनि च। सर्वमेतन्महाप्राज्ञो ददाति वसुधां ददत्।॥
en: The wise man who makes gifts of earth, gives away all these, viz, gold, silver cloth, gems and pearls and precious stones.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: तपो यज्ञः श्रुतं शीलमलोभः सत्यसंधता। गुरुदैवतपूजा च एता वर्तन्ति भूमिदम्॥
en: Penances, sacrifice, Vedic learning, good conduct, absence of cupidity, firmness in truth, adoration of elders, preceptors, and the deities, all these live in him who makes a gift of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: भूर्तृनिःश्रेयसे युक्तास्त्यक्तात्मानो रणे हताः। ब्रह्मलोकगताः सिद्धा नातिक्रामन्ति भूमिदम्॥
en: They who ascend to the region of Brahman by renouncing their lives in battle after having fought without any consideration for themselves for securing the behoof of their masters, even they are unable to go above the merit of those who make gifts of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: यथा जनित्री स्वं पुत्रं क्षीरेण भरते सदा। अनुगृह्णाति दातारं तथा सर्वरसैर्मही॥
en: As the mother always nourishes her own child with milk from her breast, so does earth please with all the tastes the person that makes a gift of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: मृत्युर्वैकिङ्करो दण्डस्तमो वह्निः सुदारुणः। घोराश्च दारुणा: पाशा नोपसर्पन्ति भूमिदम्॥
