en: Mrityu, Vaikinkara, Danda, Tama, Fire, who is highly fierce, and all heinous and terrible sins are incapable of touching the person who makes a gift of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: पितूंश्च पितृलोकस्थान् देवलोकाच्च देवताः। संतर्पयति शान्तात्मा यो ददाति वसुन्धराम्॥
en: That man of tranquil soul who makes a gift of earth pleases (by that act) the Departed Manes living in their region and the deities also hailing from the region that is theirs.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: कृशाय म्रियमाणाय वृत्तिग्लानाय सीदते। भूमि वृत्तिकरी दत्त्वा सत्री भवति मानवः॥
en: The man who makes a gift of earth to one who is weak and cheerless and destitute of the mcans of life and famishing with weakness, and who thereby supplies one with the means of sustenance, deserves the honour and merit of celebrating a sacrifice.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: यथा धावति गौर्वत्सं सवन्ती वत्सला पयः। एवमेव महाभाग भूमिर्भवति भूमिदम्॥
en: As an affectionate cow runs towards her half, with full udders dropping milk, similarly the highly blessed Earth, runs towards the person who makes a gift of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: फालकृष्टां महीं दत्त्वा सबीजां सफलामपि। उदीर्णं वापि शरणं यथा भवति कामदः॥
en: That man who makes to a Brahmana a gift of earth which has been titled, or sown with seeds, or which contains standing crops, or a palace well furnished with every necessary article, succeeds in becoming the accomplisher of the wishes of everybody.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: ब्राह्मणं वृत्तिसम्पन्नमाहिताग्निं शुचिव्रतम्। नरः प्रतिग्राह्य महीं न याति परमापदम्॥
en: The man who makes a Brahmana having the means of life, possessing a domestic fire and of pure vows and practices, accept a gift of earth, never falls into any danger or distress.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: यथा चन्द्रमसो वृद्धिरहन्यहनि जायते। तथा भूमिकृतं दानं सस्ये सस्ये विवर्धते॥
en: As the moon increases day by day, so the merit of a gift of earth increases every time such earth produces crops.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अत्र गाथा भूमिगीताः कीर्तयन्ति पुराविदः। याः श्रुत्वा जामदग्त्येन दत्ता भूः काश्यपाय वै॥
en: Those persons conversant with ancient history sing this verse regarding the gift of earth. Heaving that verse Jamadagni's son (Rama) gave away the whole Earth to Kashyapa.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: मामेवादत्त मां दत्त मां दत्त्वा मामवाप्स्यथ। अस्मिल्लोके परे चैव तद् दत्तं जायते पुनः॥
en: The verse to which I refer is this. Receive me in gift. Give me away. By giving me away, you (O giver) will obtain me again! That which is given away in this life is reacquired in the next.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: य इमां व्याहृतिं वेद ब्राह्मणो वेदसम्मिताम्। श्राद्धस्य क्रियमाणस्य ब्रह्मभूयं स गच्छति॥
en: That Brahmana who recites this great saying of the Vedas at the time of a Shraddha get the highest reward.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: कृत्यानामधिशस्तानामरिष्टशमनं महत्। प्रायश्चित्तं महीं दत्त्वा पुनात्युभयतो दश॥
en: A gift of earth is a great expiation for the sin of those powerful men who perform Atharvan rites for injuring others. Indeed, by making a gift of earth one rescues ten generations of his paternal and maternal families.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: पुनाति य इदं वेद वेदवादं तथैव च। प्रकृतिः सर्वभूतानां भूमिर्वैश्वानरी मता॥
en: That person who knows this Vedic saying about the merits of a gift of earth, succeeds in rescuing ten generations of both his paternal and maternal families. Earth is the original source of all creatures. It has been said that the god of fire is the presiding genius of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अभिषिच्यैव नृपति श्रावयेदिममागमम्। यथा श्रुत्वा महीं दद्यान्नादद्यात् साधुतश्च ताम्॥
en: After the coronation ceremony has been performed of a king, this Vedic saying should be recited to him, so that he may make gifts of earth and may never take away earth from a pious person.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: सोऽयं कृत्स्नो ब्राह्मणार्थो राजार्थचाप्यसंशयः। राजा हि धर्मकुशलः प्रथमं भूतिलक्षणम्॥
en: Forsooth, the entire wealth owned by the king belongs to the Brahmanas. A king knowing well the science of duty and morality the first requisite of the kingdom's prosperity.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अथ येषामधर्मज्ञो राजा भवति नास्तिकः। न ते सुखं प्रबुध्यन्ति न सुखं प्रस्वपन्ति च॥
en: Those people whose king is unrighteous and atheistic in conduct and belief, can never be happy. Such people can never sleep or wake in peace.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: सदा भवन्ति चोद्विग्नास्तस्य दुश्चरितैर्नराः। योगक्षेमा हि बहवो राष्ट्र नास्याविशन्ति तत्॥ अथ येषां पुन: प्राज्ञो राजा भवति धार्मिकः। सुखं ते प्रतिबुध्यन्ते सुसुखं प्रस्वपन्ति च॥
en: On account of his deeds of wickedness his subjects become always filled with anxiety. Protection of what the subjects already have and new acquisitions by fair means are events that are not seen in the kingdom of such a king. Those people, again, who have a wise and righteous king, sleep happily and wake up in happiness.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: तस्य राज्ञः शुभै राज्यैः कर्मभिर्निर्वृता नराः। योगक्षेमेण वृष्ट्या च विवर्धन्ते स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: By the blessed and righteous acts of such a king, his subjects, become shorn of anxiety. The subjects, restrained from wicked deeds, grow in prosperity through their own conduct. Capable of keeping what they have, they go on making new acquisitions.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: स कुलीन: स पुरुषः स बन्धुः स च पुण्यकृत्। स दाता स च विक्रान्तो यो ददाति वसुन्धराम्॥
en: That king who makes gifts of earth, is considered as wellborn. He is considered as a man. He is a friend. He is righteous in his acts. le is a giver. He is considered as possessing prowess.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: आदित्या इव दीप्यन्ते तेजसा भुवि मानवाः। ददन्ति वसुधां स्फीतां ये वेदविदुषि द्विजे॥
en: Those men who make gifts of ample and fertile earth to Brahmanas knowing the Vedas, always shine in the world, on account of their energy, like so many suns.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: यथा सस्यानि रोहन्ति प्रकीर्णानि महीतले। तथा कामाः प्ररोहन्ति भूमिदानसमार्जिताः॥
en: As seeds scattered on the soil grow, and yield a goodly crop, so all one's wishes become successful on account of his making gifts of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: आदित्यो वरुणो विष्णुर्ब्रह्मा सोमो हुताशनः। शूलपाणिश्च भगवान् प्रतिनन्दन्ति भूमिदम्॥
en: The Sun, Varuna, Vishnu, Brahmana, the Moon, the FireGod and the illustrious and tridentbearing Mahadeva, all praise the man who makes a gift of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: भूमौ जायन्ति पुरुषा भूमौ निष्ठां व्रजन्ति च। चतुर्विधो हि लोकोऽयं योऽयं भूमिगुणात्मकः॥
en: Living creatures originate from Earth and it is to the Earth that they return when they disappear. Living creatures which are divided into four classes have Earth for their primordial essence.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: एषा माता पिता चैव जगतः पृथिवीयते। नानया सदृशं भूतं किंचिदस्ति जनाधिप।॥
en: The Earth is both the mother and father of the universe of creatures, O king. There is no element, O king, that can compare with Earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। बृहस्पतेश्च संवादमिन्द्रस्य च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: About it is cited the old discourse between the celestial preceptor Brihaspati and Indra the kung of Heaven, O Yudhishthira.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: इष्ट्वा क्रतुशतेनाथ महता दक्षिणावता। मघवा वाग्विदां श्रेष्ठं पप्रच्छेदं बृहस्पतिम्॥
en: Having worshipped Vishnu in a hundred sacrifices each of which was famous for plentiful gifts, Maghavat put this question to Brihaspati, that foremost of all orators.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: मघवा उवाच भगवन् केन दानेन स्वर्गत: सुखमेधते। यदक्षयं महाघु च तद् ब्रूहि वदतां वर॥
en: Maghavat said O illustrious one, by what gift does one succeed in coming to the celestial region and acquiring beatitude? O foremost of speakers, do you tell me of that gift which yields high and eternal merit.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तः स सुरेन्द्रेण ततो देवपुरोहितः। बृहस्पतिवृहत्तेजाः प्रत्युवाच शतक्रतुम्॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by the king of the celestials, the preceptor of the gods, viz., Brihaspati of great energy, said these words in reply to him of a hundred sacrifices.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: बृहस्पति उवाच सुवर्णदानं गोदानं भूमिदानं च वृत्रहन्। दददेतान् महाप्राज्ञः सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: Brihaspati said Gift of gold, gift of kine, and gift of earth, by these, O destroyer of Vritra, one becomes cleansed, O you of great wisdom, of all sins.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: न भूमिदानाद् देवेन्द्र परं किंचिदिति प्रभो। विशिष्टमिति मन्यामि यथा प्राहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: There is no gift, O king of the celestials, higher than the gift of earth, O powerful one. I consider this gift as the most superior, according to what has been declared by the wise.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: ये शूरा निहता युद्धे स्वर्याता रणगृद्धिनः। सर्वे ते विबुधश्रेष्ठ नातिक्रामन्ति भूमिदम्॥
en: Those heroes who, fearless of battle, give their lives in battle with enemies, come to Heaven. How high sover their end, none of them can get over the giver of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: भर्तुनिःश्रेयसे युक्तास्त्यक्तात्मानो रणे हताः। ब्रह्मलोकगता मुक्ता नातिक्रामन्ति भूमिदम्॥
en: Those men who, disregarding their bodies, give their lives in battle while working for the behoof of their masters, ascend to the region of Brahman himself. But even they are unable to get over the giver of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: पञ्च पूर्वा हि पुरुषाः षडन्ये वसुधां गताः। एकादश ददद्भूमि परित्रातीह मानवः॥
en: By making a gift of earth one rescues these eleven, viz., five generations of ancestors and six generations of descendants.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: रत्नोपकीर्णा वसुधां यो ददाति पुरंदर। स मुक्तः सर्वकलुषैः स्वर्गलोके महीयते॥
en: That person, O Purandara, who makes a gift of earth rich with jewels and gems becomes purged off of all his sins and is highly respected in the celestial region.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: महीं स्फीतां ददद् राजन् सर्वकामगुणान्विताम्। राजाधिराजो भवति तद्धि दानमनुत्तमम्॥
en: If a person, O king, makes a gift of rich and fertile earth that is capable of granting every wish he succeeds in attaining to the position of a king of kings (in his next life). A gift of earth, therefore, is the foremost of all gifts.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: सर्वकामसमायुक्तां काश्यपी यः प्रयच्छति। सर्वभूतानि मन्यन्ते मां ददातीति वासव॥
en: That person, O Vasava, who makes a gift of earth capable of satisfying every wish with fruition is considered as making a gift of every object in the world,

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: सर्वकामदुधां धेनुं सर्वकामगुणान्विताम्। ददाति यः सहस्राक्ष स्वर्ग याति स मानवः॥
en: That man who gives away a cow endued with every accomplishment and granting the fruition of every desire, succeeds O you of a thousand eyes, in attaining the celestial region.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: मधुसर्पिःप्रवाहिण्यः पयोदधिवहास्तथा। सरितस्तर्पयन्तीह सुरेन्द्र वसुधाप्रदम्॥
en: The giver of earth, O king of the celestials, is pleased when he comes to Heaven by hundreds of rivers which run honey an i ghee and milk and curds,

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: भूमिप्रदानान्नृपतिर्मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषात्। न हि भूमिप्रदानेन दानमत्यद् विशिष्यते॥
en: A king, by making gifts of earth, is purged off of all his sins. There is no gift, therefore, which is superior to the gift of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: ददाति यः समुद्रान्तां पृथिवीं शस्त्रनिर्जिताम्। तं जनाः कथयन्तीह यावद् भवति गौरियम्॥
en: That king who gives away the Earth bounded by the ocean, after having conquered it with the help of his weapons, is talked of by all men and his memory lasts as long as the mountains last on the surface of Earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: पुण्यामृद्धिरसां भूमिं यो ददाति पुरंदर। न तम्य लोकाः क्षीयन्ते भूमिदानगुणान्विताः॥
en: Gifted as he is with merits that belong to the gift of earth, the region of happiness reserved for the person who makes gift of such earth as is auspicious and rich with every taste, never become exhausted.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: सर्वदा पार्थिवेनेह सततं भूतिमिच्छता। भूर्देया विधिवच्छक पात्रे सुखमभीप्सुना॥
en: That king, O Shakra, who wishes to have prosperity and who wishes to acquire happiness for himself, should always make gifts of earth, with due rites, to worthy persons.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अपि कृत्वा नरः पापं भूमि दत्त्वा द्विजातये। समुत्सृजति तत् पापं जीर्णो त्वचमिवोरगः॥
en: If after committing numerous sins a person makes gifts of carth to the twiceborn class, he leaves off all those sins like a snake casting off its slough.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: सागरान् सरितः शैलान् काननानि च सर्वशः। सर्वमेतन्नरः शक्र वसुधां ददत्॥
en: The person who makes a gift of earth is said to make gifts of everything, that is, of seas and rivers and mountains and forests.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: तडागान्युदपानानि स्रोतांसि च सरांसि च। स्नेहान् सर्वरसांश्चैव ददाति वसुधां ददत्॥
en: By making a gift of earth, the person is said to give away lakes and tanks and wells and rivers. On account of the moisture of earth, one is said to give away articles of various tastes by making a gift of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: ओषधीयम्सम्पन्ना नगान् पुष्पफलान्वितान्। काननोपलशैलांश्च ददाति वसुधां ददत्॥
en: The man who makes a gift of earth is considered as giving away herbs and plants possessed of high and efficacious virtues, trees adorned with flowers and fruit, charming forests, and hillocks.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अग्निष्टोमप्रभृतिभिरिष्ट्वा च स्वाप्तदक्षिणैः। त तत्फलमवाप्नोति भूमिदानाद् यदश्नुते॥
en: The merit which a person acquires by making a gift of earth is incapable of being acquired by the performance of even such great sacrifices as the Agnishtoma and others with profuse gifts in the shape of Dakshina.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: दाता दशानुगृह्णाति दश हन्ति तथा क्षिपन्। पूर्वदत्तां हरन् भूमिं नरकायोपगच्छति॥
en: The giver of earth, it has been already said, rescues ten generations of both his paternal and maternal families. Likewise, by taking away earth that was given away, one sinks himself into hell and casts ten generations of both one's paternal and maternal lines into the same place of misery.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: न ददाति प्रतिश्रुत्य दत्त्वापि च हरेत् तु यः। स बद्धो वारुणैः पाशैस्तप्यते मृत्युशासनात्॥
en: That man who having promised to make a gift of earth does not actually make it, or who having made a gift resumes it, has to pass a long time, in great misery on account of being tied with the noose of Varuna at the command of Death.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: आहिताग्निं सदायज्ञं कृशवृत्तिं प्रियातिथिम्। ये भजन्ति द्विजश्रेष्ठं नोपसर्पन्ति ते यमम्॥
en: Those men have never to go to Yama who honour and adore those foremost of Brahmanas who pour libations every day on their domestic fire, who are always always engaged in the performance of sacrifices, who have scanty means of livelihood, and who receive with hospitality every guest seeking shelter in their houses.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: ब्राह्मणेष्वनृणीभूतः पार्थिवः स्यात् पुरंदर। इतरेषां तु वर्णानां तारयेत् कृशदुर्बलान्॥
en: The king, O Purandara, should free himself from the debt he owes to the Brahmanas and protect the helpless and the weak of the other castes.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: नाच्छिन्द्यात् स्पर्शितां भूमि परेण त्रिदशाधिप। ब्राह्मणस्य सुरश्रेष्ठ कृशवृत्तेः कदाचन॥
en: The king should never resume, O chief of gods, earth that has been given away by another to a Brahmana. O king, of the celestials, who is destitute of the means of life.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: यथाश्रु पतितं तेषां दीनानामथ सीदताम्। ब्राह्मणानां हृते क्षेत्रे हन्यात् त्रिपुरुषं कुलम्॥
en: The tears that would drop from the eyes of such cheerless and destitute Brahmaras on account of their lands being resumed, are capable of destroying the ancestors and descendants to the third generation of the resumer.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: भूमिपालं च्युतं राष्ट्राद् यस्तु संस्थापयेन्नरः। तस्य वासः सहस्राक्ष नाकपृष्ठे महीयते॥
en: That man who reinstates a king driven away from his kingdom, gets residence in Heaven and is much honoured by the denizens thereof.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: इक्षुभिः संततां भूमिं यवगोधूमशालिनीम्। गोऽश्ववाप्तनपूर्णां वा बाहुवीर्यादुपार्जिताम्॥ निधिगर्भो ददद् भूमिं सर्वरत्नपरिच्छदाम्। अक्षयाँल्लभते लोकान् भूमिसत्रं हि तस्य तत्॥
en: That king who succeeds in making gifts of earth with such crops standing thereon as sugarcane or barley or wheat, or with kine and horses and other draft cattle, earth that has been acquired with the might of the giver's arms, that has mineral in its bowels and that is covered with every kind of wealth on the surface, acquires unending regions of happiness in the next world, and such a king it is that is said to celebrate the earthsacrifice.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: विधूय कलुषं सर्वं विरजाः सम्मतः सताम्। लोके महीयते सद्भिर्यां ददाति वसुन्धराम्॥
en: That king who makes a gift of earth is purged off of every sin and, therefore, is pure and liked by the righteous. In this world he is highly honoured and praised by all righteous men.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: यथाप्सु पतितः शक्र तैलविन्दुर्विसर्पति। तथा भूमिकृतं दानं सस्ये सस्ये विवर्धते॥
en: The merit of a gift of earth increases every time the earth given away bears crops for the benefit of the owner, as a drop of oil, falling upon water, is seen to extend on every side, and cover the watery surface.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: ये रणाग्रे महीपालाः शूराः समितिशोभनाः। वध्यन्तेऽभिमुखाः शक्र ब्रह्मलोकं व्रजन्ति ते॥
en: Those heroic kings and ornaments of assemblies who give their lives in battle with faces towards the foe, attain, O Shakra, to the region of Brahman.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: नृत्यगीतपरा नार्यो दिव्यमाल्यविभूषिताः। उपतिष्ठन्ति देवेन्द्र तथा भूमिप्रदं दिवि॥
en: Beautiful ladies skilled in music and dancing and adorned with garlands of celestial flowers, approach, O king of the deities, the giver of earth as he comes to Heaven departing from the Earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: मोदते च सुखं स्वर्गे देवगन्धर्वपूजितः। यो ददाति महीं सम्यग् विधिनेह द्विजातये॥
en: That king who makes gifts of Earth with due rites to persons of the twiceborn order, sports in bliss in the celestial regions, worshipped all the while by the celestials and Gandharvas.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: शतमप्सरसश्चैव दिव्यमाल्यविभूषिताः। उपतिष्ठन्ति देवेन्द्र ब्रह्मलोके धराप्रदम्॥
en: One hundred Apsaras, adorned with celestial garlands, approach, O king of the deities, the giver of earth as he ascends to the region of Brahman.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: उपतिष्ठन्ति पुण्यानि सदा भूमिप्रदं नरम्। शङ्खभद्रासनं छत्रं वराश्वा वरवाहनम्॥
en: Sweetscented flowers, an excellent conch and excellent seat, an umbrella and excellent horses with good vehicles, are always ready for the person who makes gifts of earth.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: भूमिप्रदानात् पुष्पाणि हिरण्यनिचयास्तथा। आज्ञा सदाप्रतिहता जयशब्दा वसूनि च॥
en: By making gifts of earth a king can always command fragrant flowers and heaps of gold. Heaving all kinds of wealth, the commands of such a king can never be disobeyed anywhere and cries of victory welcome him wherever he may go.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: भूमिदानस्य पुण्यानि फलं स्वर्गः पुरंदर। हिरण्यपुष्पाश्चौषध्य: कुशकाञ्चनशाद्वलाः॥
en: The rewards of the gifts of earth consist of residence in the celestial region, O Purandara, and gold, and flowers, and plants and herbs of medicinal virtue, and Kusha and mineral wealth and verdant grass.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अमृतप्रसवां भूमिं प्राप्नोति पुरुषो ददत्। नास्ति भूमिसमं दानं नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः। नास्ति सत्यसमो धर्मो नास्ति दानसमो निधिः॥
en: A person by making a gift of earth wins in his next lifenectargiving earth. There is no gift equal to a gift of earth. There is none worthy of greater respect than the mother. There is no duty higher than truth. There is no riches more valuable than that which is given away.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: एतदाङ्गिरसाच्छ्रुत्वा वासवो वसुधामिमाम्। वसुरत्नसमाकीर्णां ददावाङ्गिरसे तदा॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words from the son of Angiras, Vasava made a gift to him of the whole Earth with all her jewels and gems and all her riches.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: य इदं श्रावयेच्छ्राद्धे भूमिदानस्य सम्भवम्। न तस्य रक्षसां भागो नासुराणां भवत्युत॥
en: If these verses describing the merit of the gifts of earth be recited on the occasion of a Shraddha, neither Rakshasas nor Asuras can succeed in getting any share of the offering made in it.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: अक्षयं च भवेद् दत्तं पितृभ्यस्तन्न संशयः। तस्माच्छ्राद्धेष्विदं विद्वान् भुञ्जतः श्रावयेद् द्विजान्।।
en: Forsooth, the offerings one makes to the departed manes at such a Shraddha become unending. Hence on occasions of Shraddhas, the learned man should recite these verses on the subject of the merits of the gifts of earth, in the presence and hearing of the invited Brahmanas when engaged in eating.

description: A description of the best of all gifts
sn: इत्येतत् सर्वदानानां श्रेष्ठमुक्तं तवानघ। मया भरतशार्दूल किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: I have thus, O chief of the Bharatas, described to you that gift which is the foremost of all gifts. What else do you wish to hear?

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कानि दानानि लोकेऽस्मिन् दातुकामो महीपतिः। गुणाधिकेभ्यो विप्रेभ्यो दद्याद् भरतसत्तम॥ केन तुष्यन्ति ते सद्यः किं तुष्टाः प्रदिशन्ति च। शंस मे तन्महाबाहो फलं पुण्यकृतं महत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said When a king wishes to make gifts in this world, what, indeed, are those gifts which he should make, O best of the Bharatas, to such Brahmanas as are endued with superior accomplishments? What gift is that by which the Brahmanas become readily pleased? What fruits do they give in return? O you of powerful arms, tell me what is the high reward which can be won through the merit of gifts.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: दत्तं किं फलवद् राजनिह लोके परत्र च। भवत: श्रोतुमिच्छामि तन्मे विस्तरतो वद॥
en: What gifts, O king; yield rewards both in this world and in the next? I wish to hear all this from you. Do you describe to me all this in detail.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: भीष्म उवाच इममर्थं पुरा पृष्टो नारदो देवदर्शनः। यदुक्तवानसौ वाक्यं तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: Bhishma said These very questions were formerly put by me to Narada. Hear me as I recite to you what that celestial sage had told me in reply.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: नारद उवाच अन्नमेव प्रशंसन्ति देवा ऋषिगणास्तथा। लोकतन्त्रं हि संज्ञाश्च सर्वमन्ने प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Narada said The celestials and all the Rishis speak highly of food. The course of the world and the intellectual faculties have all been fixed on food.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नेन सदृशं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति। तस्मादन्नं विशेषेण दातुमिच्छन्ति मानवाः॥
en: There has never been, nor will be, any gift equal to the gift of food. Hence, men always wish particularly to make gifts of food.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नमूर्जस्करं लोके प्राणाश्चान्ने प्रतिष्ठिताः। अन्नेन धार्यते सर्वं विश्वं जगदिदं प्रभो॥
en: In this world, food is the root of energy and strength. The vital airs are established on food. It is food that keeps up the wide universe, O powerful one.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नाद् गृहस्था लोकेऽस्मिन् भिक्षवस्तापसास्तथा। अन्नाद् भवन्ति वै प्राणा: प्रत्यक्षं नात्र संशयः॥
en: All classes of men, householders and mendicants and ascetics, live upon food. The vital airs depend upon food. There is no doubt in this.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: कुटुम्बिने सीदते च ब्राह्मणाय महात्मने। दातव्यं भिक्षवे चान्नमात्मनो भूतिमिच्छता॥
en: Afflicting one's relatives, one, if desirous of his own prosperity, should make gifts of food to a great Brahmana or a person of the mendicant order.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: ब्राह्मणायाभिरूपाय यो दद्यादन्नमर्थिने। विदधाति निधिं श्रेष्ठं पारलौकिकमात्मनः॥
en: That man who makes a gift of food to an accomplished Brahmana who begs the same, secures for himself in the next world wealth of great value.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: श्रान्तमध्वनि वर्तन्तं वृद्धपर्हमुपस्थितम्। अर्चयेद् भूतिमन्विच्छन् गृहस्थो गृहमागतम्॥
en: The householder who seeks his own prosperity should receive with respect a deserving old man who is worn out with toil while proceeding on his way far from home, when such a man come to the householder's house.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: क्रोधमुत्पतितं हित्वा सुशीलो वीतमत्सरः। अन्नदः प्राप्नुते राजन् दिवि चेह च यत्सुखम्॥
en: That man who, shorn of irrepressible anger and becoming righteous in nature and freed from malice, makes gifts of food, is sure to acquire happiness, O king, both in this world and in the next.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: नावमन्येदभिगतं न प्रणुद्यात् कदाचन। अपि वपाके शुनि वा न दानं विप्रणश्यति॥
en: The householder should never disregard the man who comes to his place, nor should he insult him by sending him away. A gift of food made to even a Chandala or a dog is never lost.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: यो दद्यादपरिक्लिष्टमन्नमध्वनि वर्तते। आर्तायादृष्टपूर्वाय स महद्धर्ममाप्नुयात्॥
en: That man who makes a gift of clean food to a person on the way who is fatigued and unknown to the giver, is sure to win great merit.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: पितॄन् देवानृषीन् विप्नानतिथींश्च जनाधिप। यो नरः प्रीणयत्यन्नस्तस्य पुण्यफलं महत्॥
en: The man who pleases with gifts of food the departed manes, the deities, the Rishis, the Brahmanas, and guests arrived at his house, wins great merit.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: कृत्वातिपातकं कर्म यो दद्यादन्नमर्थिने। ब्राह्मणाय विशेषेण न स पापेन मुह्यते॥
en: That person who having committed even a heinous crime makes a gift of food to one who solicits, or to a Brahmana in special, is never stupefied by that heinous sin.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: ब्राह्मणेष्वक्षयं दानमन्नं शूद्रे महाफलम्। अन्नदानं हि शूद्रे च ब्राह्मणे च विशिष्यते॥
en: A gift of food made to a Brahmana becoines eternal. One made to a Shudra yields great merit. This is the difference between the merits of the gifts of food made to Brahmanas and Shudras.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: न पृच्छेद् गोत्रचरणं स्वाध्यायं देशमेव च। भिक्षितो ब्राह्मणेनेह दद्यादन्नं प्रयाचितः॥
en: Solicited by a Brahmana, one should not enquire about his family or conduct or Vedic learning. Asked for food, one should give food to him who asks.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नदस्यान्नवृक्षाश्च सर्वकामफलप्रदाः। भवन्ति चेह चामुत्र नृपतेर्नात्र संशयः॥
en: There is no doubt in this, O king, that he who makes gifts of food gets both in this world and in the next many trees giving food and every other object of desire.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: आशंसन्ते हि पितरः सुवृष्टिमिव कर्षकाः। अस्माकमपि पुत्रो वा पौत्रे वान्नं प्रदास्यति॥
en: Like cultivators expecting auspicious showers of rain, the departed manes always expect that their sons and grandsons would present food to them.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: ब्राह्मणो हि महद्भूतं स्वयं देहीति याचति। अकायो वा सकामो वा दत्त्वा पुण्यमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: The Brahmana is a great being. When he comes into one's house and solicits, saying, Give me!the owner of the house, whether actuated or not by the desire of gaining merit, is sure to win great merit by listening to that prayer.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: ब्राह्मणः सर्वभूतानामतिथिः प्रसृताग्रभुक्। विप्रा यदधिगच्छन्ति भिक्षमाणा गृहं सदा॥ सत्कृताश्च निवर्तन्ते तदतीव प्रवर्धते। महाभागे कुले प्रेत्य जन्म चाप्नोति भारत॥
en: The Brahmana is the guest of all creatures in the universe. He is entitled to the first part of every food. That house increases in prosperity to which the Brahmanas go from desire of getting alms and from which they return honoured on account of their desires being satisfied. The owner of such a house is born in his next life in a family, O Bharata, that has all the comforts and luxuries of life.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: दत्त्वा त्वन्नं नरो लोके तथा स्थानमनुत्तमम्। नित्यं मिष्टान्नदायी तु स्वर्गे वसति सत्कृतः॥
en: A man, by making gifts of food in this world, is sure to acquire an excellent place hereafter. He who makes gifts of sweet meats and all food that is sweet, gains a residence in heaven where he is honoured of all the deities and other denizens. inan

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नं प्राणा नराणां हि सर्वमन्ने प्रतिष्ठितम्। अन्नदः पशुमान् पुत्री धनवान् भोगवानपि॥
en: Food forms the life-breaths of men. Everything rests upon food. He who makes gifts of food gets many animals, many children, profuse riches (in other shape), and all articles of comfort and luxury in profusion.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: प्रणवांश्चापि भवति रूपवांश्च तथा नृप। अन्नदः प्राणदो लोके सर्वदः प्रोच्यते तु सः॥
en: The giver of food is said to be the giver of life. Indeed, he is said to be the giver of everything. Hence, O king, such a acquires both strength and personal grace in this world.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नं हि दत्त्वातिथये ब्राह्मणाय यथाविधि। प्रदाता सुखमाप्नोति दैवतैश्चापि पूज्यते॥
en: If food be given duly to a Brahmana come to one's house as a guest, the giver acquires great happiness, and is adored by the very celestials.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: ब्राह्मणो हि महद्भूतं क्षेत्रभूतं युधिष्ठिर। उप्यते तत्र तद् बीजं तद्धि पुण्यफलं महत्॥
en: The Brahmana, O Yudhishthira, is a great Being. He is also a fertile field. Whatever seed is sown on that field yields an abundant crop of merit.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: प्रत्यक्षं प्रीतिजननं भोक्तुनुर्भवत्युत। सर्वाण्यन्यानि दानानि परोक्षफलवन्त्युत॥
en: A gift of food readily yields the happiness of both the giver and the receiver. All other gifts produce unseen fruits.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नाद्धि प्रसवं यान्ति रतिरन्नाद्धि भारत। धर्मार्थावन्नतो विद्धि रोगनाशं तथान्नतः॥
en: From food originate creatures. From food springs happiness and joy, O Bharata, Know that virtue and wordly profit both spring from food. The cure of disease or health also comes from food.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नं ह्यमृतमित्याह पुराकल्पे प्रजापतिः। अन्नं भुवं दिवं खं च सर्वमन्ने प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: In a former Age, the Lord of all creatures said that food is ambrosia or the source of immortality. Food is Earth, Food is Heaven, Food is the Sky. Everything rests on food.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नप्रणाशे भिद्यन्ते शरीरे पञ्च धातवः। बलं बलवतोऽपीह प्रणश्यत्यन्नहानितः॥
en: In the absence of food, the five elements that form the body cease to exist in a state of unison. From want of food the strength of even the strongest man is seen to fail.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: आवाहाश्च विवाहाश्च यज्ञाश्चान्नमृते तथा। निवर्तन्ते नरश्रेष्ठ ब्रह्म चात्र प्रलीयते॥
en: Invitation and marriages and sacrifices all cease for want of food. The very Vedas disappear when there is no food.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नतः सर्वमेतद्धि यत् किंचित् स्थाणु जङ्गमम्। त्रिषु लोकेषु धर्मार्थमन्नं देयमतो वुधैः॥
en: All the mobile and iminobile creatures of the universe depend on food. Virtue and, worldly profit, in the three worlds, depend on food. Hence the wise should make gifts of food.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नदस्य मनुष्यस्य बलमोजो यशांसि च। कीर्तिश्च वर्धते शश्वत् त्रिषु लोकेषु पार्थिव॥
en: The strength, energy, fame and achievements of the man who makes gifts of food, always multiply themselves in the three worlds, O king.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: मेघेवूय संनिधत्ते प्राणानां पवनः पतिः। तच्च मेघगतं वारि शक्रो वर्षति भारत॥
en: The deity of wind, places above the clouds (the water drawn by the Sun). The water thus taken to the clouds is caused by Shakra to be poured upon the Earth, O Bharata.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: आदत्ते च रसान् भौमानादित्यः स्वगभस्तिभिः वायुरादित्यतस्तांश्च रसान् देवः प्रवर्षति॥
en: The Sun, by means of his rays, draws up the moisture of the Earth. The god of wind cause the moisture to fall down from the Sun.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: तद् यदा मेघतो वारि पतितं भवति क्षितौ। तदा वसुमती देवी स्निग्धा भवति भारत॥
en: When the water comes down from the clouds upon the Earth, the goddess Earth become moist, О Bharata.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: ततः सस्यानि रोहन्ति येन वर्तयते जगत्। मांसमेदोऽस्थिशुक्राणां प्रादुर्भावस्ततः पुनः॥
en: Then do people sow various kinds of crops upon whose outturn the universe of creatures depends. It is from the food thus produced that the flesh, fat, bones and vital seed of all beings originate.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: सम्भवन्ति ततः शुक्रात् प्राणिनः पृथिवीपते। अग्नीषोमौ हि तच्छुक्रं सृजतः पुष्यतश्च ह॥
en: From the vital seed thus made, O king, spring various kinds of living creatures. Agni and Soma, living within the body, create and maintain the vital seed.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: एवमन्नाद्धि सूर्यश्च पवनः शुक्रमेव च। एक एव स्मृतो राशिस्ततो भूतानि जज्ञिरे॥
en: Thus from food, the Sun and the god of wind and the vital seed spring and act. All these are said to form one element or quantity, and it is from these that all creatures originate.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: प्राणान् ददाति भूतानां तेजश्च भरतर्षभ। गृहमभ्यागतायाऽथ यो दद्यादन्नमर्थिने॥
en: That man who gives unto one who comes to his house and begs it, is said, O chief of the Bharatas, to contribute both life and energy to living creatures.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: भीष्म उवाच नारदेनैवमुक्तोऽहमदामन्नं सदा नृप। अनसूयुस्त्वमप्यन्नं तस्माद् देहि गतज्वरः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by Narada, O king, I have always made gifts of food. Do you also, therefore, freed from malice and with a cheerful heart, make gifts of food.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: दत्त्वान्नं विधिवद् राजन् विप्रेभ्यस्त्वमिति प्रभो। यथावदनुरूपेभ्यस्ततः स्वर्गमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: By making gifts of food, O king, worthy Brahinanas with due rites, you may be sure, O powerful one, of attaining to Heaven.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अन्नदानां हि ये लोकास्तांस्त्वं शृणु जनाधिप। भवनानि प्रकाशन्ते दिवि तेषां महात्मनाम्॥
en: Hear me, O king, as I tell you what the regions are reserved for those who make gifts of food. The mansions of those great persons shine with resplendence in the regions of Heaven.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: तारासंस्थानि रूपाणि नानास्तम्भान्वितानि च। चन्द्रमण्डलशुभ्राणि किंकिणीजालवन्ति च॥ तरुणादित्यवर्णानि स्थावराणि चराणि च।
en: Bright as the stars in the sky, and supported upon many columns, white as the disc of the moon, and adorned with many tinkling bells, and rosy like the newly risen sun, those palaces are either fixed or movable.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: अनेकशतभौमानि सान्तर्जलचराणि च॥ वैदूर्यार्कप्रकाशानि रौप्यरुक्ममयानि च।
en: Those mansions are filled with hundreds and hundreds of things and animals that live on land and as many things and animals living in water. Some of them are effulgent like lapis lazuli and some are resplendent like the Sun. Some of them are made of silver and some of gold.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: सर्वकामफलाश्चापि वृक्षा भवनसंस्थिताः॥ वाप्यो वीथ्यः सभाः कूपा दीर्घिकाश्चैव सर्वशः।
en: Within those mansions are many trees capable of satisfying every desire of the inmates. Many tanks and roads and halls and wells and lakes are all there.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: घोषवन्ति च यानानि युक्तान्यथ सहस्रशः॥ भक्ष्यभोज्यमयाः शैला वासांस्याभरणानि च।
en: Thousands of vehicles with horses and other animals harnessed thereto and with wheels whose caltter is always loud, are all there. Mountains of food and all enjoyable articles and heaps of cloths and ornaments are also there.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: क्षीरं स्रवन्ति सरितस्तथा चैवानपर्वताः॥ प्रसादाः पाण्डुराभ्राभाः शय्याश्च काञ्चनोज्ज्वला:।
en: Numerous rivers that run milk, and hills of rice and other edibles, are also there. Indeed, many palatial residences loO king like white clouds, with many beds of golden splendour, are in those regions.

description: The fruits of gifts to Brahmana and others. The replies of Narada
sn: तान्यन्नदाः प्रपद्यन्ते तस्मादन्नप्रदो भव॥ एते लोकाः पुण्यकृता अन्नदानां महात्मनाम्। तस्मादनं प्रयत्नेन दातव्यं मानवैर्भुवि॥
en: All these are won by those men who make gifts of food in this world. Do you, therefore, become a giver of food. Indeed these are the regions reserved for those great and righteous persons who make gifts of food in this world. For these reasons, men should always make gifts of food in this world.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतं मे भवतो वाक्यमन्नदानस्य यो विधिः। नक्षत्रयोगस्येदानी दानकल्पं ब्रवीहि मे।।।।
en: Yudhishthira said I have heard your discourse about the ordinances for the gift of food. Do you describe to me now about the conjunctions of the planets and the stars in relation to the subject of making gifts.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। देवक्याश्चैव संवादं महर्षेर्नारदस्य च॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is recited this ancient discourse between Devaki and Narada, that foremost of Rishis.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: द्वारकामनुसम्प्राप्तं नारदं देवदर्शनम्। पप्रच्छेदं वचः प्रश्नं देवकी धर्मदर्शनम्॥
en: Once on a time when Narada of godlike features and knowing every duty arrived at Dwaraka, Devaki asked him this question.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: तस्याः सम्पृच्छमानाया देवर्षि रदस्ततः। आचष्ट विधिवत् सर्वं तच्छणुष्व विशाम्पते॥
en: The celestial Rishi Narada replied to her question in the following words. Do you hear as I recite them.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: नारद उवाच कृत्तिकासु महाभागे पायसेन ससर्पिषा। संतर्घ्य ब्राह्मणान् साधूल्लोकानाप्नोत्यनुत्तमान्॥
en: Narada said By pleasing, O blessed lady, worthy Brahmanas with pudding mixed with ghee, under the constellation Krittika, one acquires regions of great happiness.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: रोहिण्यां प्रसृतैर्मार्गेमांसैरन्नेन सर्पिषा। पयोऽन्नपानं दातव्यमनृणार्थे द्विजातये॥
en: Under the constellation Rohini, one should, for freeing himself from the debt he owes to the Brahmanas, make gifts to them of many handfuls of venison along with rice and clarified butter and milk, and other kinds of edibles and drinks.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: दोग्ध्रीं दत्त्वा सवत्सां तु नक्षत्रे सोमदैवते। गच्छन्ति मानुषाल्लोकात् सर्वलोकमनुत्तमम्॥
en: One giving away a cow with a calf under the constellation called Somadevata (or Mrigashiras), proceeds from this human region to a region in Heaven of great felicity.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: आर्द्रायां कृसरं दत्त्वा तिलमिश्रमुपोषितः। नरस्तरति दुर्गाणि क्षुरधारांश्च पर्वतान्॥
en: One undergoing a fast and giving away Krishara mixed with sesame, gets over all difficulties in the next world, including those mountains with rocks sharp as razors.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: पूपान् पुनर्वसौ दत्त्वा तथैवान्नानि शोभने। यशस्वी रूपसम्पन्नो बह्वनो जायते कुले॥
en: By making gifts, O beautiful lady, of cakes and other food under the constellation Punarvasu, one gets personal beauty and great fame and takes birth in his next life in a family in which there is profuse food.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: पुष्येण कनकं दत्त्वा कृतं वाकृतमेव च। अनालोकेषु लोकेषु सोमवत् स विराजते॥
en: Making a gift of wrought or unwrought gold, under the constellation Pushya, one shines like the Moon himself in regions of surrounding darkness.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: आश्लेषायां तु यो रूप्यमृषभं वा प्रयच्छति। स सर्वभयनिर्मुक्तः सम्भवानधितिष्ठति॥
en: He who makes a gift, gift, under under the constellation Ashlesha, of silver or a bull, becomes freed from every fear and acquires riches and prosperity.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: मघासु तिलपूर्णानि वर्धमानानि मानवः। प्रदाय पुत्रपशुमानिह प्रेत्य च मोदते॥
en: By making a gift, under the constellation Megha, of earthen dishes filled with sesame, one gets children and animals in this world and acquires happiness in the next.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: फल्गुनीपूर्वसमये ब्राह्मणानामुपोषितः। भक्ष्यान् फाणित संयुक्तान् दत्त्वा सौभाग्यमृच्छति॥१३
en: By making gifts, while fasting, to Brahmanas, under the constellation called PurvaPhalguni, of food mixed with Phanita, the reward is great prosperity both here and hereafter.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: घृतक्षीरसमायुक्तं विधिवत् षष्टिकौदनम्। उत्तराविषये दत्त्वा स्वर्गलोके महीयते॥
en: By making a gift, under the constellation called UttaraPhalguni, of clarified butter and milk with rice called Shashthika, one wins great honours in Heaven.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: यद् यत् प्रदीयते दानमुत्तराविषये नरैः। महाफलमनन्तं तद् भवतीति विनिश्चयः॥
en: Whatever gifts are made by men under the constellation of Uttara-Phalguni yield great merit, which, again, becomes unending. This is very certain.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: हस्ते हस्तिरथं दत्त्वा चतुर्युक्तमुपोषितः। प्राप्नोति परमॉल्लोकान् पुण्यकामसमन्वितान्॥
en: Observing a fast, the person who makes, under the constell.tion Hasta, a gift of a car with four elephants, acquires regions of great happiness that are capable of granting the fruition of every wish.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: चित्रायां वृषभं दत्त्वा पुण्यगन्धांश्च भारत। चरन्त्यप्सरसां लोके रमन्ते नन्दने तथा॥
en: By making a gift, under the constellation Chitra, of a bull and of good perfumes, one sports in bliss in regions of Apsaras like the deities sporting in the garden of Nandana.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: स्वात्यामथ धनं दत्त्वा यदिष्टतममात्मनः। प्राप्नोति लोकान् स शुभानिह चैव महद् यशः॥
en: By making gifts of riches under the constellation Svati, one acquires such excellent regions as one desires and wins, besides great fame.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: विशाखायामनड्वाहं धनुं दत्त्वा च दुग्धदाम्। सप्रासङ्गं च शकटं सधान्यं वस्त्रसंयुतम्॥ पितॄन् देवांश्च प्रीणाति प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते। न च दुर्गाण्यवाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति॥
en: By making gifts, under the constellation Vishakha, of a bull, and a cow giving profuse milk, a cart full of paddy, with a Prasanga for covering the same, and also cloths for wear, a person pleases the departed manes and the deities and acquires external merit in the other world. Such a person never meets with any calamity and certainly reaches Heaven.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: दत्त्वा यथोक्तं विप्रेभ्यो वृत्तिमिष्टां स विन्दति। नरकादींश्च संक्लेशान् नाप्नोतीति विनिश्चयः॥
en: By making gifts the Brahmanas of whatever articles they want, one acquires such means of subsistence as he wishes, and becomes rescued from Hell and every calamity that befall sinners after death. This is the certain conclusion of the scriptures.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: अनुराधासु प्रावारं वरानं समुपोषितः। दत्त्वा युगशतं चापि नरः स्वर्गे महीयते॥
en: By making gifts, under the constellation Anuradha, of embroidered cloth and other dresses and of food, observing a fast all the while, one becomes honoured in Heaven for a hundred cycles.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: कालशाकं तु विप्रभ्यो दत्त्वा मर्त्यः समूलकम्। ज्येष्ठायामृद्धिमिष्टां वै गतिमिष्टां स गच्छति॥
en: By making a gift under the constellation Jyeshtha, of the potherb called Kalashaka with the roots, one acquires great prosperity as also such an end as is desirable.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: मूले मूलफलं दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणेभ्यः समाहितः। पितॄन् प्रीणयते चापि गतिमिष्टां च गच्छति॥
en: By making to Brahmanas a gift under the constellation Mula, of fruits and roots, with a controlled soul, one pleases the departed manes and attains to a desirable end.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: अथ पूर्वास्वषाढार दधिपात्राण्युपोषितः। कुलवृत्तोपसम्पन्ने ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे॥ पुरुषो जायते प्रेत्य कुले सुबहुगोधने। उदमन्थं ससर्पिष्कं प्रभूतमधिफाणितम्। दत्त्वोत्तरास्वषाढासु सर्वकामानवाप्नुयात्॥
en: By making, under the constellation Purvashadha, a gift, to a Brahmana knowing the Vedas and of good family and conduct, of cups filled with curds, while observing a fast, one is born in his next life in a family having abundant kine. One secures the fruition of every desire, by making gifts, under the constellation Uttarashadha, of jugs full of barleywater, with clarified butter and juice of sugarcane in abundance.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: दुग्धं त्वभिजिते योगे दत्त्वा मधुघृतप्लुतम्। धर्मनित्यो मनीषिभ्यः स्वर्गलोके महीयते॥
en: By making a gift, under the conjunction called Abhijit, of milk with loney and ghee unto men of wisdom, a righteous person attains to Heaven and becomes an object of adoration and honour there.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: श्रवणे कम्बलं दत्त्वा वस्त्रान्तरितमेव वा। श्वेतेन याति यानेन स्वर्गलोकानसंवृतान्॥
en: By making, under the conjunction Shravana, a gift of blankets or other cloth of thick texture, one passes freely through every region of happiness, riding on a white car of pure resplendence.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: गोप्रयुक्तं धनिष्ठासु यानं दत्त्वा समाहितः। वस्त्रराशिधनं सद्यः प्रेत्य राज्यं प्रपद्यते॥
en: By making with a controlled soul under the constellation Dhanishtha a gift of a car with bulls yoked thereto, or masses of cloths and riches, one at once acquires Heaven in his next life.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: गन्धानछतभिषायोगे दत्त्वा सागुरुचन्दनान्। प्राप्नोत्यप्सरसा संघान् प्रेत्य गन्धांश्च शाश्वतान्॥
en: By making gifts, under the constellation Shatabhisha, of perfumes with Aquilaria Agallocha and sandal wood, one acquires in the next world the companionship of Apsaras as also eternal perfumes of various sorts.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: पूर्वाभाद्रपदायोगे राजमाषान् प्रदाय तु। सर्वभक्षफलोपेतः स वै प्रेत्य सुखी भवेत्॥
en: By making gifts, under the constellation Purva Bhadrapada, of Rajamasha, one acquires great happiness in next life and comes by a profuse supply of every kind of food and fruits.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: औरभ्रमुत्तरायोगे यस्तु मांसं प्रयच्छति। स पितॄन् प्रीणयति वै प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते॥
en: One who makes, under the constellation Uttara, a gift of mutton, pleases the departed manes by such an act and acquires unending merit in the next world.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: कांस्योपदोहनां धेनुं रेवत्यां यः प्रयच्छति। सा प्रेत्य कामानादाय दातारमुपतिष्ठति॥
en: If one makes a gift, under the constellation Revati, of a cow with a vessel of white copper for milking her, the cow so given away approaches him in the next world, ready to grant the fruition of every desire.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: रथमश्वसमायुक्तं दत्त्वाश्विन्यां नरोत्तमः। हस्त्यश्वरथसम्पन्ने वर्चस्वी जायते कुले॥
en: By making a gift, under the constellation Ashvini, of a car with horses yoked thereto, one is born in his next life in a family possessing abundant elephants and horses and cars and becomes gifted with great energy.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: भरणीषु द्विजातिभ्यस्तिलधेनुं प्रदाय वै। गा: सुप्रभूताः प्राप्नोति नरः प्रेत्य यशस्तथा॥
en: By making, under the constellation Bharani, a gift to the Brahmanas of kine and. sesame, one attains in his next life great fame and abundant kine.

description: The ordinances of the gifts of food
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्येष लक्षणोद्देशः प्रोक्तो नक्षत्रयोगतः। देवक्या नारदेनेह सा स्नुषाभ्योऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Bhishma said Thus did Narada describe to Devaki the subject of what gifts should be made under what constellations. Devaki herself, having heard this account related it in her turn to her daughters-in-law.

sn: भीष्म उवाच सर्वान् कामान् प्रयच्छन्ति ये प्रयच्छन्ति काञ्चनम्। इत्येवं भगवानत्रिः पितामहसुतोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhishma said The illustrious Atri, the son of the Grandfather Brahman, said, They who make gifts of gold are said to make gifts of every thing in the world.

sn: पवित्रमथ चायुष्यं पितॄणामक्षयं च तत्। सुवर्णं मनुजेन्द्रेण हरिश्चन्द्रेण कीर्तितम्॥
en: King Harishchandra said that the gift of gold washes off sins, leads to long life, and yields inexhaustible merit to the departed means.

sn: पानीयं परमं दानं दानानां मुनरब्रवीत्। तस्मात् कूपांश्च वापीश्च तडागानि च खानयेत्॥
en: Manu has said that a gift of drink is the best of all gifts: therefore should a man cause wells and tanks and lakes to be excavated.

sn: अर्धं पापस्य हरति पुरुषस्येह कर्मणः। कूपः प्रवृत्तपानीयः सुप्रवृत्तश्च नित्यशः॥
en: A well full of water and from which various creatures draw water, is said to take off half the sinful deeds of the person who has excavated it.

sn: सर्वं तारयते वंशं यस्य खाते जलाशये। गावः पिवन्ति विप्राश्च साधवश्च नराः सदा॥
en: The entire family of a person is rescued from hell and sin in whose well or tank or lake kine and Brahmanas and pious people constantly satisfy their thirst.

sn: निदाघकाले पानीयं यस्य तिष्ठत्यवारितम्। स दुर्गं विषमं कृत्स्नं न कदाचिदवाप्नुते॥
en: That man gets over every sort of calamity from whose well or tank every one draws water without restraint during the summers season.

sn: बृहस्पतेर्भगवतः पूष्णाश्चैव भगस्य च। अश्विनोश्चैव बढेश्च प्रीतिर्भवति सर्पिषा॥
en: Clarified butter is said to please the illustrious Brihaspati, Pushan, Bhaga, the twin Ashvins, and the god of fire.

sn: परमं भेषजं ह्येतद् यज्ञानामेतदुत्तमम्। रसानामुत्तमं चैतत् फलानां चैतदुत्तमम्॥
en: Clarified butter is possessed of high medicinal virtues. It is a high requisite of Sacrifice. It is the best of all liquids. The merit a gift of clarified butter yields is very superior.

sn: फलकामो यशस्कामः पुष्टिकामश्च नित्यदा। घृतं दद्याद् द्विजातिभ्यः पुरुषः शुचिरात्मवान्॥
en: That man who wishes for the reward of happiness in the next world, who wishes for the fame and prosperity, should with a purified heart and having purified himself, make gifts of clarified butter to the Brahmanas.

sn: घृतं मासे आश्वयुजि विप्रेभ्यो यः प्रयच्छति। तस्मै प्रयच्छतो रूपं प्रीतौ देवाविहाश्विनौ॥
en: The twin Ashvins, pleased, confer personal beauty upon that man who makes gifts of clarified butter to the Brahmanas in the month of Ashvin.

sn: पायसं सर्पिषा मिश्रं द्विजेभ्यो यः प्रयच्छति। गृहं तस्य न रक्षांसि धर्षयन्ति कदाचन॥
en: Rakshasas never invade the house of that man who makes gifts to the Brahmans of pudding mixed with clarified butter.

sn: पिपासया न म्रियते सोपच्छन्दश्च जायते। न प्राप्नुयाच्च व्यसनं करकान् यः प्रयच्छति॥
en: That man never dies of thirst who makes gifts to the Brahmanas of jars filled with water. Such a person gets every necessary of life in profusion, and has never to suffer from any calamity or distress.

sn: प्रयतो ब्राह्मणाने यः श्रद्धया परया युतः। उपस्पर्शनषड्भागं लभते पुरुषः सदा॥
en: That man, who with great devotion and controlled senses makes gifts to the foremost of Brahmanas, is said to take a sixth part of the merits acquired by the Brahmanas by their penances.

sn: यः साधनार्थं काष्ठानि ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयच्छति। प्रतापनार्थं राजेन्द्र वृत्तवद्भ्यः सदा नरः॥ सिद्ध्यन्त्यर्थाः सदा तस्य कार्याणि विविधानि च। उपर्युपरि शत्रूणां वपुषा दीप्यते च सः॥
en: That man who makes presents, to Brahmanas having the means of life, of firewood for purposes of coO king as also for enabling them to drive cold, finds all his purposes and all his acts successful. Such a one is seen to shine over all his enemies.

sn: भगवांश्चापि सम्प्रीतो वह्निर्भवति नित्यशः। न तं त्यजन्ति पशवः संग्रामे च जयत्यपि॥
en: The illustrious god of fire becomes pleased with such a man. As another reward, he never becomes divested of cattle, and he is sure to win victory in battle.

sn: पुत्राञ्छ्रियं च लभते यश्छत्रं सम्प्रयच्छति। न चक्षुर्व्याधिं लभते यज्ञभागमथाश्नुते॥
en: The man who makes a gift of an umbrella gets children and great prosperity. Such a person never suffers from any eyedisease. The merits also that originate from the performance of a sacrifice become his.

sn: निदाघकाले वर्षे वा यश्छत्रं सम्प्रयच्छति। नास्य कश्चिन्मनोदाहः कदाचिदपि जायते।
en: That man who makes a gift of an umbrella in the season of summer or rains, has never to suffer from any heartburning on any account.

sn: कृच्छ्रात् स विषमाच्चैव क्षिप्रं मोक्षमवाप्नुते॥ प्रदानं सर्वदानानां शकटस्य विशाम्पते। एवमाह महाभागः शण्डिल्यो भगवानृषिः॥
en: Such a man quickly succeeds in freeing himself from every difficulty and obstacle. The highly blessed and illustrious Rishi Shandilya had said that of all gifts, the gift of a car, O king, is the greatest.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दह्यमानाय विप्राय यः प्रयच्छत्युपानहौ। यत्फलं तस्य भवति तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said I wish to hear, O grandfather what the merits are of that person who makes the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana whose feet are burning or being scorched by hot sands while walking.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: भीष्म उवाच उपानही प्रयच्छेद् यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः समाहितः। मर्दते कण्टकान् सर्वान् विषमान्निस्तरत्यपि॥
en: Bhishma said The man who gives to the Brahmanas sandals for the protection of their feet, succeeds in crushing all thorns and gets over every sort of difficulty.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: स शत्रूणामुपरि च संतिष्ठति युधिष्ठिर। यानं चाश्वतरीयुक्तं तस्य शुभं विशाम्पते॥ उपतिष्ठति कौन्तेय रौप्यकाञ्चनभूषितम्। शकटं दम्यसंयुक्तं दत्तं भवति चैव हि॥
en: Such a man, O Yudhishthira, stands over the heads of all his enemies, cars of pure splendour, with mules yoked thereto and made of gold and silver, O monarch, approach him. He who makes a gift of sandals is said to acquire the merit of making the gift of a car with well-broken horses yoked thereto.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यत् फलं तिलदाने च भूमिदाने च कीर्तितम्। गोदाने चान्नदाने च भूयस्तद् ब्रूहि कौरव॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me fully once more, O grand father, of the merits of gifts of sesame and land, and of kine and food.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणुष्व मम कौन्तेय तिलदानस्य यत् फलम्। निशम्य च यथान्यायं प्रयच्छ कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Bhishma said Hear, O son of Kunti, what the merits are of the gift sesame. Hearing me, do you then, O best of the Kurus, make gifts of sesame according to the rites.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: पितॄणां परमं भोज्यं तिलाः सृष्टाः स्वयम्भुवा। तिलदानेन वै तस्मात् पितृपक्षः प्रमोदते॥
en: Sesame seeds were created by the Self create Brahmana as the best food for the departed manes. Hence, gifts sesame seeds always please the departed manes greatly.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: माघमासे तिलान् यस्तु ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयच्छति। सर्वसत्त्वसमाकीर्णं नरकं स न पश्यति॥
en: The man who makes gifts of sesame seeds in the month of Magha, to the Brahmanas, has never to see Hell which is full of all dreadful creatures.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: सर्वसत्रैश्च यजते यस्तिलैर्यजते पितॄन्। न चाकामन दातव्यं तिलश्राद्धं कदाचन॥
en: He who worship the departed manes with offerings of sesame seeds is considered as worshipping the deities in all the sacrifices. One should never make a Shraddha with offerings of sesames seeds without entertaining some purpose.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: महर्षेः कश्यपस्यैते गात्रेभ्यः प्रसृतास्तिलाः। ततो दिव्यं गता भावं प्रदानेषु तिलाः प्रभो॥
en: Sesame seeds sprang from the limbs of the great Rishi Kashyapa. Hence in the matter of gifts, they have come to be considered as possessed of great efficacy.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: पौष्टिका रूपदाश्चैव तथा पापविनाशनाः। तस्मात् सर्वप्रदानेभ्यस्तिलदानं विशिष्यते॥
en: Sesame seeds confer both prosperity and personal beauty cleanse the giver of all his sins. It is for this reason that the gift of sesame seeds is superior to the gift of every other article.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: आपस्तम्बश्च मेधावी शङ्खश्च लिखितस्तथा। महर्षिौतमश्चापि तिलदानैर्दिवं गताः॥
en: The highly intelligent Apastamva, Shankha and Likhita, and the great Rishi Gautama, have all gone to the celestial region by having made gifts of sesame seeds.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: तिलहोमरता विप्राः सर्वे संयतमैथुनाः। समा गव्येन हविषा प्रवृत्तिषु च संस्थिताः॥
en: Those Brahmanas who make Homa with offerings of sesame, abstain from sexual intercourse, and are observant of the religion of Acts, are considered as equal to vaccine Havi.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: सर्वेषामिति दानानां तिलदानं विशिष्यते। अक्षयं सर्वदानानां तिलदानमिहोच्यते॥
en: The gift of sesame seeds is superior to all gifts. Amongst all gifts, the gift of sesame is considered as yielding unending merit.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: उच्छिन्ने तु पुरा हव्ये कुशिकर्षिः परंतपः। तिलैरग्नित्रयं हत्वा प्राप्तवान् गतिमुत्तमाम्॥
en: Formerly when Havi (clarified butter) on one occasion could not be procured, the Rishi Kushika, O scorcher of enemies made offerings of sesame seeds to his three sacrificial fires and succeeded in acquiring an excellent end.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: इति प्रोक्तं कुरुश्रेष्ठ तिलदानमनुत्तमम्। विधानं येन विधिना तिलानामिह शस्यते॥
en: I have thus said to you, O chief of the Kurus, what the regulations are about the excellent gift of sesame seeds. It is on account of these regulations that the gift of sesame seeds has come to be considered as fraught with very superior merit.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: अत उर्ध्वं निबोधेदं देवानां यष्टुमिच्छताम्। समागमे महाराज ब्रह्मणा वै स्वयम्भुवा॥
en: After this, listen to what I would say. Once on a time the gods, desirous of making a Sacrifice, went, O king, to the presence of the Self-create Brahman.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: देवाः समेत्य ब्रह्माणं भूमिभागे यियक्षवः। शुभं देशमयाचन्त यजेम इति पार्थिव॥
en: Having met Brahman, desirous as they were of celebrating a sacrifice on the Earth, they begged him for a piece of sacred earth, saying, We want it for our sacrifice.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: देवा ऊचुः भगवंस्त्वं प्रभुर्भूमेः सर्वस्य त्रिदिवस्य च। यजेमहि महाभाग यज्ञं भवदनुज्ञया॥
en: The deities said O illustrious one, you are the lord of all the Earth as also of all the gods! With your permission, O highly blessed one, we wish to perform a sacrifice.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: नाननुज्ञातभूमिर्हि यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते। त्वं हि सर्वस्य जगतः स्थावरस्य चरस्य च॥
en: The person who has not got by lawful means the earth whereon to make the sacrificial altar, acquires not the merit of the sacrifice he performs.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: प्रभुर्भवसि तस्मात्त्वं समनुज्ञातुमर्हसि। ददानि मेदिनीभागं भवद्भ्योऽहं सुरर्षभाः॥
en: You are the Lord of all the universe consisting of its mobile and immobile objects. Therefore, you should grant us a piece of earth for the sacrifice we wish to make.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच यस्मिन् देशे करिष्यध्वं यज्ञान् काश्यपनन्दनाः।
en: Brahman said You foremost of gods, I shall give you a piece of earth whereon, you sons of Kashyapa, you shall celebrate your intended sacrifice.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: देवा ऊचुः भगवन् कृतकार्याः स्म यक्ष्महे स्वाप्तदक्षिणैः॥ इमं तु देशं मुनयः पर्युपासन्ति नित्यदा।
en: The gods said Our wishes, O holy one, have become successful. We shall celebrate our sacrifice even here with large gifts. Let, however, the ascetics always worship this piece of Earth.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: ततोऽगस्त्यश्च कण्वश्च भृगुरत्रिर्वृषाकपिः॥ असितो देवलश्चैव देवयज्ञमुपागमन्।
en: Then there came to that place Agastya, Kanva, Bhrigu, Atri, and Vrishakapi, Asita and Devala.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: ततो देवा महात्मान ईजिरे यज्ञमच्युतम्॥ तथा समापयामासुर्यथाकालं सुरर्षभाः।
en: The great deities then. O you of unfading glory, celebrated their sacrifice. Those foremost of gods finished it in due time.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: त इष्टयज्ञस्त्रिदशा हिमवत्यचलोत्तमे॥ पष्ठमंशं क्रतोस्तस्य भूमिदानं प्रचक्रिरे।
en: Having completed that sacrifice of theirs on the breast of that foremost of mountains, viz., Himavat, the celestials attached to the gift of earth a sixth part of the merit originating from their sacrifice.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: प्रादेशमात्रं भूमेस्तु यो दद्यादनुपस्कृतम्॥ न सीदति स कृच्छ्रेषु न च दुर्गाण्यवाप्नुते।
en: The man who makes a gift of even a span of carth with reverence and faith, has never to suffer from any difficulty and has never to meet with any calamity.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: शीतवातातपसहां गृहभूमि सुसंस्कृताम्॥ प्रदाय सुरलोकस्थः पुण्यान्तेऽपि न चाल्यते।
en: By making a gift of a house that prevents cold, wind, and sun, and that stands upon a piece of clean land, the giver attains to the region of the celestials and does not fall down cven when his merit becomes exhausted.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: मुदितो वसति प्राज्ञः शक्रेण सह पार्थिव॥ प्रतिश्रयप्रदानाच्च सोऽपि स्वर्गे महीयते।
en: By making a gift of a house to live in, the giver, cndued with wisdom, lives, O king, happily in the company of Shakra, Such a person receives great honours in the celestial region.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: अध्यापककुले जातः श्रोत्रियो नियतेन्द्रियः॥ गृहे यस्य वसेत् तुष्टः प्रधानं लोकमश्नुते।
en: That person in whose house a Brahmana of controlled senses, wellread in the Vedas, and belonging by birth to a family of preceptors, lives in contentment, succeeds in attaining to and enjoying a region of great happiness.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: तथा गवार्थे शरणं शीतवर्षसहं दृढम्॥ आसप्तमं तारयति कुलं भरतसत्तम।
en: Likewise, O best of the Bharatas, by giving away a shed for the shelter of kine that can prevent cold and rain and that is substantial in structure, the giver rescues seven generations of his race.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: क्षेत्रभूमिं ददल्लोके शुभां श्रियमवाप्नुयात्॥ रत्नभूमिं प्रदद्यात् तु कुलवंशं प्रवर्धयेत्।
en: By giving away a piece of earth fit for cultivation the giver acquires great prosperity. By giving a piece of earth containing mineral riches, the giver advances his family.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: न चोषरां न निर्दग्धां महीं दद्यात् कथंचन॥ न श्मशानपरीतां च न च पापनिषेविताम्।
en: One should never give away carth that is barren or that is burnt; nor should one give away any earth that is near a crematorium, or that has been possessed and enjoyed by a sinful person before such gift.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: पारक्ये भूमिदेशे तु पितॄणां निर्वपेत् तु यः॥ तद्भूमिं वापि पितृभिः श्राद्धकर्म विहन्यते।
en: When a man performs a Shraddha in honour of the departed manes on earth belonging to another person, the departed manes render both the gift of that earth and the Shraddha itself fruitless.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: तस्मात् क्रीत्वा महीं दद्यात् स्वल्पामपि विचक्षणः॥ पिण्डः पितृभ्यो दत्तो वै तस्यां भवति शाश्वतः।
en: Hence, a wise man should buy even a small piece of earth and make a gift of it, The funeral cake that is offered to one's ancestors on earth that has been duly purchased, becomes endless.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: अटवीपर्वताश्चैव नद्यस्तीर्थानि यानि च॥ सर्वाण्यस्वामिकान्याहुन हि तत्र परिग्रहः।
en: Forests, mountains, rivers, and Tirthas, are considered as having no owners. No earth need be bought here for performing Shraddhas.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: इत्येतद् भूमिदानस्य फलमुक्तं विशाम्पते॥ अतः परं तु गोदानं कीर्तयिष्यामि तेऽनघ।
en: This has been said, O king, on the subject of the merits of making gifts of earth. After this, O sinless one, I shall describe to you the। subject of the gift of kine.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: गावोऽधिकास्तपस्विभ्यो यस्मात् सर्वेभ्य एव च।।३७ तस्मान्महेश्वरो देवस्तपस्ताभिः सहास्थितः।
en: Kine are considered as superior to all the ascetics. And therefore, the divine Mahadeva practised penances in their company.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: ब्राह्मे लोके वसन्त्येताः सोमेन सह भारत॥ यां तो ब्रह्मर्षयः सिद्धाः प्रार्थयन्ति परां गतिम्।
en: Kine, O Bharata, live in the region of Brahman, in the company of Soma. Forming, as it does the highest end, the twiceborn Rishis, crowned with success, try to attain to that very region.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: पयसा हविषा दना शकृता चाथ चर्मणा॥ अस्थिभिश्चोपकुर्वन्ति शृङ्गैर्वालैश्च भारत।
en: Kine benefit human beings with milk, clarified butter, curd, dung, skin, bones, horns, and hair, O Bharata.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: नासां शीतातपौ स्यातां सदैताः कर्म कुर्वते॥ न वर्षविषयं वापि दुःखमासां भवत्युत।
en: Kine do not feel cold or heat. They always work. Even the rainy season cannot affect them at all.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: ब्राह्मणैः सहिता यान्ति तस्मात् पारमकं पदम्॥ एकं गोब्राह्मणं तस्मात् प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः।
en: And since kine attain to the highest end, in the company of Brahmanas, therefore do the wise say that kine and Brahmanas are equal.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: रन्तिदेवस्य यज्ञे ता: पशुत्वेनोपकल्पिताः॥ अतश्चर्मण्वती राजन् गोचर्मभ्यः प्रवर्तिता।
en: Formerly king Rantideva celebrated a grand sacrifice in which an immense number of kine were offered up and killed. From the juice that was secreted by the skins of the slain animals, a river was formed that passed by the name of Charmanvati.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: पशुत्वाच्च विनिर्मुक्ताः प्रदानायोपकल्पिता:॥ ता इमा विप्रमुख्येभ्यो यो ददाति महीपते। निस्तरेदापदं कृच्छ्रां विषमस्थोऽपि पार्थिव॥ गवां सहस्रदः प्रेत्य नरकं न प्रपद्यते।
en: Kine no longer are animals fit for sacrifice. They now are animals fit for gift. That king who presents kine to foremost of Brahmanas, O king, is sure to get over every danger even if he falls into it. The man who presents a thousand kine has not to go to hell,

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: सर्वत्र विजयं चापि लभते मनुजाधिप॥ अमृतं वै गवां क्षीरमित्याह त्रिदशाधिपः।
en: Such a person, O king, wins victory everywhere. The very king of the celestials had said that the milk of kine is nectar.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: तस्माद् ददाति यो धेनुममृतं स प्रयच्छति॥ अग्नीनामव्ययं ह्येतद्धौम्यं वेदविदो विदुः।
en: Therefore, one who presents a cow is considered as making a gift of nectar. Persons, wellread in the Vedas, have declared that the clarified butter manufactured from cow's milk, is the very best of all libations poured upon the sacrificial fire.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: तस्माद् ददाति यो धेनुं स हौम्यं सम्प्रयच्छति॥ स्वर्गो वै मूर्तिमानेष वृषभं यो गवां पतिम्। विप्रे गुणयुते दद्यात् स वै स्वर्गे महीयते॥ प्राणा वै प्राणिनामेते प्रोच्यन्ते भरतर्षभ।
en: Therefore, the man, who presents a cow, is considered as making a gift of a libation for sacrifice. A bull is the embodiment of Heaven. He who makes the gift of a bull to a qualified Brahmana, receives great honours in the celestial region. Kine, O chief of Bharata's race, are said to be the vital airs of living creatures.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: तस्माद् ददाति यो धेनुं प्राणानेष प्रयच्छति॥ गावः शरण्या भूतानामिति वेदविदो विदुः।
en: Therefore, the man who makes the gift of a cow, is said to make the gift of vital airs. Persons, conversant with the Vedas, have said that kine are the great refuge of living creatures.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: तस्माद् ददाति यो धेनुं शरणं सम्प्रयच्छति॥ न वधार्थं प्रदातव्या न कीनाशे न नास्तिके। गोजीविने न दातव्या तथा गौर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: The man, who makes the gift of a cow, is considered as making the gifts of what is the high refuge of all creatures. The cow should never be given away for slaughter; nor should the cow be given to a tiller of the soil; nor should the cow be given away to an atheist. The cow should not also, chief of the Bharatas, be given to one who se occupations is the keep of kine.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: ददत् स तादृशानां वै नरो गां पापकर्मणाम्। अक्षयं नरकं यातीत्येवमाहुर्महर्षयः॥
en: The wise have said that the person, who gives away the cow to any of such sinful persons, has to sink in eternal Heli.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: न कृशां नापवत्सां वा वथ्यां रोगान्वितां तथा। न व्यङ्गां न परिश्रान्तां दद्याद् गां ब्राह्मणाय वै॥
en: One should never give to a Brahmana a cow that is lean, or that produces dead calves, or that is barren, or that is diseased, or that is defective of limb, or that is worn out with toil.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: दशगोसहस्रदो हि शक्रेण सह मोदते। अक्षयाँल्लभते लोकान् नरः शतसहस्रशः॥
en: The man, who gives away ten thousand kine, attains to Heaven and sports in bliss in the company of Indra. The man, who makes gifts of kine by hundred thousands, wins many regions of eternal happiness.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: इत्येतद् गोप्रदानं च तिलदानं च कीर्तितम्। तथा भूमिप्रदानं च शृणुष्वाने च भारत॥
en: Thus have I recited to you the merits of the gift of kine and of sesame, as also of the gift of earth. Listen now to me as I describe to you the gift of food, O Bharata.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: अन्नदानं प्रधानं हि कौन्तेय परिचक्षते। अन्नस्य हि प्रदानेन रन्तिदेवो दिवं गतः॥
en: The gift of food, O son of Kunti, is considered as a very superior gift. Formerly king Rantideva ascended to the celestial region by having made gifts of food.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: श्रान्ताय क्षुधितायानं यः प्रयच्छति भूमिपः। स्वायम्भुवं महत् स्थानं स गच्छति नराधिप॥
en: That king, who makes a gift of food to one who is toil-worn and hungry, acquires the regions of supreme happiness belonging to the Self-create.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: न हिरण्यैर्न वासोभिर्नान्यदानेन भारत। प्राप्नुवन्ति नराः श्रेयो यथा ह्यन्नप्रदाः प्रभो॥
en: Men cannot, by gifts of gold and dresses and of other things, win that happiness which givers of food succeed in wining, O you of great power.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: अन्नं वै प्रथमं द्रव्यमन्नं श्रीश्च परा मता। अन्नात् प्राणः प्रभवति तेजो वीर्यं बलं तथा॥
en: Food is, indeed, the first article. Food is considered as the highest prosperity. It is from food that life originates as also energy and prowess and strength.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: सद्यो ददाति यश्चान्नं सदैकाग्रमना नरः। न स दुर्गाण्यवाप्नोतीत्येवमाह पराशरः॥
en: He, who always makes gifts of food, with attention, to the righteous, never suffers any distress. This has been said by Parashara.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: अर्चयित्वा यथान्यायं देवेभ्योऽन्नं निवेदयेत्। यदन्ना हि नरा राजंस्तदन्नास्तस्य देवताः॥
en: Having adored the deities duly food should be first dedicated to them. It has been said, O king that the kind of food that is taken by particular men is taken also by the gods those men worship.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: कौमुदे शुक्लपक्षे तु योऽन्नदानं करोत्युत। स संतरति दुर्गाणि प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते॥
en: That man, who makes gifts of food in light half of the month of Kartika, succeeds in getting over every difficulty here and acquires endless happiness hereafter.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: अभुक्त्वातिथये चान्नं प्रयच्छेद् यः समाहितः। स वै ब्रह्मविदां लोकान् प्राप्नुयाद् भरतर्षभ॥
