en: That man, who makes a gift of food to a hungry guest arrived at his house, acquires all those regions, O chief of Bharata's race, that are reserved for persons acquainted with Brahman.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: सुकृच्छ्रामापदं प्राश्चानदः पुरुषस्तरेत्। पापं तरति चैवेह दुष्कृतं चापकर्षति॥
en: The man, who makes gifts of food, is sure to get over every difficulty and distress. Such a person gets over every sin and purges himself of every evil act.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: इत्येदन्नदानस्य तिलदानस्य चैव ह। भूमिदानस्य च फलं गोदानस्य च कीर्तितम्॥
en: I have thus described to you the merits of making gifts of food, of sesame, of earth, and of kine. person gets over every sin and purges himself of every evil act.

description: The merits of the gift of a pair of sandals to a Brahmana. The gifts of sesame, land, kine, gold, &c.
sn: इत्येदन्नदानस्य तिलदानस्य चैव ह। भूमिदानस्य च फलं गोदानस्य च कीर्तितम्॥
en: I have thus described to you the merits of making gifts of food, of sesame, of earth, and of kine.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतं दानफलं तात यत् त्वया परिकीर्तितम्। अन्नदानं विशेषेण प्रशस्तमिह भारत॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have heard, O sire, of the merits of the different kinds of gift which you have described to me. I understand, O Bharata, that the gift of food is especially praiseworthy and superior.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: पानीयदानमेवैतत् कथं चेह महाफलम्। इत्येतच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि विस्तरेण पितामह॥
en: What, however, are the great merits of making gifts of drink. I wish to hear of this in full, O grandfather.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: भीष्म उवाच हन्त ते वर्तयिष्यामि यथावद् भरतर्षभ। गदतस्तन्ममाघेह शृणु सत्यपराक्रम॥
en: Bhishma said I shall, O chief of Bharata's race. relate to you this subject. Listen to ine, O you of unbaffled prowess, as I speak to you.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: पानीयदानात् प्रभृति सर्वं वक्ष्यामि तेऽनघ। यदन्नं यच्च पानीयं सम्प्रदायाश्नुते नरः॥ न तस्मात् परमं दानं किंचिदस्तीति मे मनः। अन्नात् प्राणभृतस्तात प्रवर्तन्ते हि सर्वशः॥
en: I shall, O sinless one, describe to you gifts beginning with that of drink. The merit that a man wins by making gifts of food and of drink is such that the like of it, I think, is incapable of being acquired by any other gift. There is no gift, superior to that of either food or drink. It is from food that all living creatures are able to exist.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: तस्मादन्नं परं लोके सर्वलोकेषु कथ्यते। अन्नाद् बलं च तेजश्च प्राणिनां वर्धते सदा॥
en: Therefore, food is considered as a very superior object in all the worlds. From food the strength and energy of living creatures continually increase.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: अन्नदानमतस्तस्माच्छ्रेष्ठमाह प्रजापतिः। सावित्र्या ह्यपि कौन्तेय श्रुतं ते वचनं शुभम्॥
en: Hence, the master of all creatures has himself said that the gift of food is a very superior gift. You have heard, O son of Kunti, what the auspicious words are of Savitri herself.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: यतश्च यद् यथा चैव देवसत्रे महामते। अन्ने दत्ते नरेणेह प्राणा दत्ता भवन्त्युत॥
en: You know why those words were said what those words were, and how they were said in course of the sacred Mantras, O you of great intelligence. A man, by making a gift of food, really makes a gift of life itself.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: प्राणदानाद्धि परमं न दानमिह विद्यते। श्रुतं हि ते महाबाहो लोमशस्यापि तद्वचः॥
en: There is no gift in this world which is superior to the gift of life. You are not unacquainted with this saying of Lomasha, O you of mighty arms.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: प्राणान् दत्त्वा कपोताय यत् प्राप्तं शिबिना पुरा। तां गतिं लभते दत्त्वा द्विजस्यान्न विशाम्पते॥
en: The end that was attained to formerly by king Shivi on account of his having granted life to the pigeon is acquired by him, O king, who makes a gift of food to a Brahmana.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: तस्माद् विशिष्टां गच्छन्ति प्राणदा इति नः श्रुतम्। अन्नं वापि प्रभवति पानीयात् कुरुसत्तम।
en: Hence, we have heard that they who give life attain to very superior regions of happiness in after life. Food, O best of the Kurus, may or may not be superior to drink.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: नीरजातेन हि बिना न किंचित् सम्प्रवर्तते॥ नीरजातश्च भगवान् सोमो ग्रहगणेश्वरः।
en: Nothing can exist without the help of what comes from water. The very lord of all the planets, viz., the illustrious Soma, has originated from water.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: अमृतं च सुधा चैव स्वाहा चैव स्वधा तथा॥ अन्नौषध्यो महाराज वीरुधश्च जलोद्भवाः।
en: Ambrosia and Suddha and Svadha and milk, as also every sort of food, the deciduous herbs, O king, and creepers originate from water.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: यतः प्राणभृतां प्राणा: सम्भवन्ति विशाम्पते॥ देवानाममृतं ह्यन्नं नागानां च सुधा तथा।
en: From these, O king, the vital airs of all living creatures flow. The deities have nectar for their food. The Nagas have Sudha.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: पितॄणां च स्वधा प्रोक्ता पशूनां चापि वीरुधः॥ अन्नमेव मनुष्याणां प्राणानाहुर्मनीषिणः।
en: The departed manes have Svadha for their. The animals have herbs and plants for their food. The wise have said that rice, etc., form the food of human beings.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: तच्च सर्वं नरव्याघ्र पानीयात् सम्प्रवर्तते॥ तस्मात् पानीयदानाद् वै न परं विद्यते क्वचित्।
en: All these, O king originate from water. Hence, there is nothing superior to the gift of water or drink.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: तच्च दद्यान्नरो नित्यं यदीच्छेद् भूतिमात्मनः॥ धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं जलदानमिहोच्यते।
en: If a person wishes to get prosperity for himself, he should always make gifts of drink. The gift of water is considered as very laudable. It brings on great fame and bestows long life on the giver.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: शत्रूश्चाप्यधि कौन्तेय सदा तिष्ठति तोयदः॥ सर्वकामानवाप्नोति कीर्तिं चैव हि शाश्वतीम्।
en: The giver of water, O son of Kunti, always stands over the heads of his enemies. Such a person obtains the fruition of all his desires and acquires everlasting fame.

description: The merits of the gifts of drink
sn: तोयदो मनुजव्याघ्र प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्चाति पापेभ्यश्च प्रमुच्यते॥ स्वर्ग गत्वा महाद्युते। अक्षयान् समवाप्नोति लोकानित्यब्रवीन्मनुः॥
en: The giver, O king, becomes purged of every sin and obtains unending happiness hereafter as he proceeds to the celestial region. O you of great splendour. Manu himself has said that such a person acquires regions of endless bliss in the other world.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच तिलानां कीदृशं दानमथ दीपस्य चैव हि। अन्नानां वाससां चैव भूय एव ब्रवीहि मे॥
en: Yudhishthira said Do you describe to me once again. O grandfather, the merit's of the gifts of sesame and of lamps for lighting darkness, as also of food and clothes.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। ब्राह्मणस्य च संवादं यमस्य च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma Said : Regarding it, O Yudhishthira, is recited the discourse that took place forinerly between a Brahmana and Yama.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: मध्यदेशे महान् ग्रामो ब्राह्मणानां बभूव ह। गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये यामुनस्य गिरेरधः॥
en: In the region lying between the rivers Gangs and Yamuna, at the foot of the hills called Yamuna, there was a large town peopled by Brahmanas.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: पर्णशालेति विख्यातो रमणीयो नराधिप। विद्वांसस्तत्र भूयिष्ठा ब्राह्मणाश्चावसंस्तथा।॥
en: The town was known by the name of Parnashala and was very charming, O king. A large number of learned Bralımanas lived in it.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: अथ प्राह यम: कंचित् पुरुषं कृष्णवाससम्। रक्ताक्षमूर्ध्वरोमाणं काकजङ्घाक्षिनासिकम्॥ गच्छ त्वं ब्राह्मणग्रामं ततो गत्वा तमानय। अगस्त्यं गोत्रतश्चापि नामतश्चापि शर्मिणम्॥
en: One day, Yama, the king of the dead, commanded a messenger of his, who was clad in black, having bloodred eyes and hair standing erect, and possessed of feet, eyes, and nose all of which resembled those of a crow, saying, Go you to the town inhabited by Brahmanas and bring here the person known by the name of Sharmin and born in the race of Agastya.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: शमे निविष्टं विद्वांसमध्यापकमनावृतम्। मा चान्यमानयेथास्त्वं सगोत्रं तस्य पार्श्वतः॥
en: He is intent on mental tranquillity and gifted with learning. He teaches the Vedas and his practices are wellknown. Do not bring me another person belonging to the same race and living in the same neighbourhood.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: स हि तादृग्गुणस्तेन तुल्योऽध्ययनजन्मना। अपत्येषु तथा वृत्ते समस्तेनैव धीमता॥
en: This other man I want is equal to him in virtues, study and birth. As for children and conduct, this other reassembles the intelligent Sharmin.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: तमानय यथोद्दिष्टं पूजा कार्या हि तस्य वै। स गत्वा प्रतिकूलं तच्चकार यमशासनम्॥
en: Do you bring the individual I want. He should be adored with respect. The messenger, doing there, did the very reverse of what he had been ordered to do.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: तमाक्रम्यानयामास प्रतिषिद्धो यमेन यः। तस्मै यमः समुत्थाय पूजां कृत्वा च वीर्यवान्॥
en: Attacking that person, he brought him who had been forbidden by Yama to be brought. Endued with great energy, Yama rose up on seeing the Brahmana and adored him duly.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: प्रोवाच नीयतामेष सोऽन्य आनीयतामिति। एवमुक्ते तु वचने धर्मराजेन स द्विजः॥ उवाच धर्मराजानं निर्विण्णोऽध्ययनेन वै। यो मे कालो भवेच्छेषस्तं वसेयमिहाच्युत॥
en: The king of the dead then ordered him messenger, saying Let this one be taken back, and let the other one be brought to me.When the great judge of the dead said these words, that Brahmana addressed him and said I have finished my study of the Vedas and am no longer attached to the world. Whatever period may yet remain of my life, I wish to pass, living here, O you of unfading glory.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: यम उवाच नाहं कालस्य विहितं प्राप्नोमीह कथंचन। यो हि धर्मं चरति वै तं तु जानामि केवलम्॥
en: Yama said I cannot determine the exact period, ordained by Time, of one's life, and hence, unurged by Time, I cannot allow one to live here. I take note of the acts of virtue (or otherwise) that one does in the world.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: गच्छ विप्र त्वमद्यैव आलयं स्व महाद्युते। ब्रूहि सर्वं यथा स्वैरं करवाणि किमच्युत॥
en: Do you, O learned Brahmana of great splendour, return forthwith to your house. Tell me what also is in your mind and what I can do for you, O you of unfading glory.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच यत् तत्र कृत्वा सुमहत् पुण्यं स्यात् तद् ब्रवीहि मे। सर्वस्य हि प्रमाणं त्वं त्रैलोक्यस्यापि सत्तम॥
en: Brahmana said Do you tell me what those acts are by doing which one may acquire great merit. O best of all beings, you are the foremost of authorities in the three worlds.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: यम उवाच शृणु तत्त्वेन विप्रर्षे प्रदानविधिमुत्तमम्। तिलाः परमकं दानं पुण्यं चैवेह शाश्वतम्॥
en: Yama said Do you hear, O twiceborm Rishi, the excellent ordinances about gifts. The gift of sesame seeds is a very superior gift. It yields everlasting merit.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: तिलाश्च सम्प्रदातव्या यथाशक्ति द्विजर्षभ। नित्यदानात् सर्वकामांस्तिला निवर्तयन्त्युत॥
en: O foremost of twiceborn ones, one should make gifts of as much sesame as one can. By making gifts of sesame every day, one is sure to acquire the fruition of his desires.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: तिलान् श्राद्धे प्रशंसन्ति दानमेतद्ध्यनुत्तमम्। तान् प्रयच्छस्व विप्रेभ्यो विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: The gift of sesame at Shraddhas is highly spoken of. The gift of sesame is a very superior gift. Do you make gifts of sesame to the Brahmanas according to the rites laid down in the scriptures.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: वैशाख्यां पौर्णमास्यां तु तिलान् दद्याद् द्विजातिषु। तिला भक्षयितव्याश्च सदा त्वालम्भनं च तैः॥
en: One should, on the day of the full moon of the month of Vaishakha, make gifts of sesame to the Brahmanas. They should also be made to cat and to touch sesame on every occasion that one can afford.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: कार्यं सततमिच्छद्भिः श्रेयः सर्वात्मना गृहे। तथाऽऽपः सर्वदा देयाः पेयाश्चैव न संशयः॥
en: They, who are desirous of seeing their wellbeing, should with their whole minds do this in their houses. Forsooth, men should likewise make gifts of water and set up resting places for the distribution of drinking water.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: पुष्करिण्यस्तडागानि कूपांश्चैवात्र खानयेत्। एतत् सुदुर्लभतरमिहलोके द्विजोत्तम॥
en: One should make tanks and lakes and wells to be excavated. Such acts are rare in the world, O best of twice born persons.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: आपो नित्यं प्रदेयास्ते पुण्यं ह्येतदनुत्तमम्। प्रपाश्च कार्या दानार्थं नित्यं ते द्विजसत्तम। भुक्तेऽप्यन्नं प्रदेयं तु पानीयं वै विशेषतः॥
en: Do you always make gifts of water. This act is full great merit, О best of twice born persons, for making such gifts you should put up resting places along the roads for the distribution of water. After one has eaten, the gift to one should especially be made of water for drink.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्ते स तदा तेन यमदूतेन वै गृहान्। नीतश्च कारयामास सर्वं तद् यमशासनम्॥
en: Bhishma said After Yama had said these words to him, the messenger who had borne him from his house conveyed him back to it. The Brahmana, on his return, obeyed the instructions he had received.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: नीत्वा तं यमदूतोऽपि गृहीत्वा शर्मिणं तदा। ययौ स धर्मराजाय न्यवेदयत चापि तम्॥
en: Having thus conveyed him back to his abode, the messenger of Yama fetched Sharmin who had really been sought by Yama. Taking Sharmin to him, he informed his inaster.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: तं धर्मराजो धर्मज्ञं पूजयित्वा प्रतापवान्। कृत्वा च संविदं तेन विससर्ज यथागतम्॥
en: Endued with great energy, the judge of the dead adored that pious Brahmana, and having conversed with him for some time dismissed him for being taken back to his house.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: तस्यापि च यमः सर्वमुपदेशं चकार ह। प्रेत्यैत्य च ततः सर्वं चकारोक्तं यमेन तत्॥
en: To him also Yama gave same instructions. Sharmin too, returning to the world of men, did all that Yama had said.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: तथा प्रशंसते दीपान् यमः पितृहितेप्सया। तस्माद् दीपप्रदो नित्यं संतारयति वै पितॄन्।॥
en: Like the gift of water, Yama, from desire of doing good to the departed manes, applauds the gift of lamps to light dark places, for it is considered as benefiting the departed manes.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: दातव्याः सततं दीपास्तस्माद् भरतसत्तमा देवतानां पितॄणां च चक्षुष्यं चात्मनां विभो॥
en: Hence, O best of the Bharatas, one should always give lamps for lighting dark places. The giving of lamps increases the power of vision, of the deities, the Pitris, and one's own self.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: रत्नदानं च सुमहत् पुण्यमुक्तं जनाधिप। यस्तान् विक्रीय यजते ब्राह्मणो ह्यभयंकरम्॥
en: It has been said, O king, that the gift of gems is a very great gift. The Brahmana, who having accepted a gift of gems, sells the same for celebrating a sacrifice, commits no sin.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: यद् वै ददाति विप्रेभ्यो ब्राह्मणः प्रतिगृह्य वै। उभयोः स्यात् तदक्षय्यं दातुरादातुरेव च॥
en: The Brahmana, who having accepted a gift of gems, makes a gift of them to Brahmanas, wins endless merit himself and confers endless merit upon him from whom he had originally received them.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: यो ददाति स्थितः स्थित्यां तादृशाय प्रतिग्रहम्। उभयोरक्षयं धर्मं तं मनुः प्राह धर्मवित्॥
en: Knowing every duty, Manu himself has said that he who, observant of proper control makes a gift of gems to a Brahmana observant of proper restraints, wins inexhaustible merit himself and confers inexhaustible merit upon the recipient.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: वाससां सम्प्रदानेन स्वदारनिरतो नरः। सुवस्त्रश्च सुवेषश्च भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम॥
en: The man, who is content with his own married wife and who makes a gift of dresses, acquires an excellent complexion and excellent dresses for himself.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: गाव: सुवर्णं च तथा तिलाश्चैवानुवर्णिताः। बहुशः पुरुषव्याघ्र वेदप्रामाण्यदर्शनात्॥
en: I have told you, O foremost of men, What the merits are of gifts of kine, of gold and of sesame, according to various precepts of the Vedas and the scriptures.

description: The gifts of sesame and lamps
sn: विवाहांश्चैव कुर्वीत पुत्रानुत्पादयेत च। पुत्रलाभो हि कौरव्य सर्वलाभाद् विशिष्यते॥
en: One should marry and procreate offspring upon one's married wives. Of all acquistions, O son of Kuru's race, that of sons is considered the foremost.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भूय एवं कुरुश्रेष्ठ दानानां विधिमुत्तमम्। कथयस्व महाप्राज्ञ भूमिदानं विशेषतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Do you, O foremost one of Kuru's family, describe to me once again the excellent ordinances about gifts, with especial reference, O you of great wisdom, to the gift of earth.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: पृथिवीं क्षत्रियो दद्याद् ब्राह्मणायेष्टिकर्मिणे। विधिवत् प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न त्वन्यो दातुमर्हति॥
en: A Kshatriya should make gifts of earth to a pious Brahmana; such a Brahmana should accept the gift with due rites. None else, however save a Kshatriya can make gifts of Earth.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: सर्ववर्णस्तु यच्छक्यं प्रदातुं फलकाक्षिभिः। वेदे वा यत् समाख्यातं तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: You should now tell me what those objects are that persons of all classes can freely give if actuated by the desire of acquiring merit. You should also tell me what has been said in the Vedas on this subject.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: भीष्म उवाच तुल्यानामानि देयानि त्रीणि तुल्यफलानि च। सर्वकामफलानीह गावः पृथ्वी सरस्वती॥
en: Bhishma said There are three gifts that pass by the same name and that yield equal merits. Indeed, these three confer the fruition of every desire. The three objects whose gifts are of such a character are kine, earth, and knowledge.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: यो ब्रूयाच्चापि शिष्याय धां ब्राह्मीं सरस्वतीम्। पृथिवीगोप्रदानाभ्यां तुल्यं स फलमश्नुते॥
en: That person, who tells his disciple words of good meaning drawn from the Vedas, acquires merit equal to that which is acquired by making gifts of earth and kine.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: तथैव गाः प्रशंसन्ति न तु देयं ततः परम्। संनिकृष्टफलास्ता हि लघ्वाश्च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Likewise are kine praised. There is no object of gift higher than they. Kine are supposed to confer merit forthwith. They are also, O Yudhishthira, such that a gift of them cannot but yield great merit.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: मातरः सर्वभूतानां गावः सर्वसुखप्रदाः। वृद्धिमाकाक्षत नित्यं गावः कार्याः प्रदक्षिणाः॥
en: Kine are the mothers of all creatures. They grant every sort of happiness. The person, who seeks his own prosperity, should always make gifts of kine.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: संताड्या न तु पादेन गवां मध्ये न च व्रजेत्। मङ्गलायतनं देव्यस्तस्मात् पूज्याः सदैव हि॥
en: No one should kick at kine or pass through the midst of kine. Kine are goddesses and homes of auspiciousness. Therefore they always deserve worship.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: प्रचोदनं देवकृतं गवां कर्मसु वर्तताम्। पूर्वमेवाक्षरं चान्यदभिधेयं ततः परम्॥
en: Formerly, the deities, while tilling the earth whereon they celebrated a sacrifice, used the a god for striking the bullocks yoked to the plough. Hence, in cultivating earth for such a purpose, one may, without incurring censure or sin, apply the goad to bullocks. In other acts, however, bullocks should never be struck with the goad of the whip.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: प्रचारे वा निवाते वा बुधो नोद्वेजयेत गाः। तृषिता ह्यभिवीक्षन्त्यो नरं हन्युः सबान्धवम्॥
en: When kine are grazing or lying down, no one should tease them in any way. When thirsty and they do not get water, kine, by merely loO king at such a person, can destroy him with all his relatives and friends.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: पितृसद्मानि सततं देवतायतनानि च। पूयन्ते शकृता यासां पूतं किमधिकं ततः॥
en: What creatures can be more sacred than kine when with the very dung of kine aitars, whereon Shraddhas are performed in honour of the departed manes, of those whereon the deities are adored, are cleansed and sanctified.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: घासमुष्टिं परगवे दद्यात् संवत्सरं यः। अकृत्वा स्वयमाहारं व्रतं तत् सार्वकामिकम्॥
en: That man who, before eating himself, gives every day, for a year only a handful of grass to a cow belonging to another, is considered as practising a vow or observance which bestows the fruition of every desire.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: तु स हि पुत्रान् यशोऽर्थं च श्रियं चाप्यधिगच्छति। नाशयत्यशुभं चैव दुःस्वप्नं चाप्यपोहति॥
en: Such a person acquires children and fame and wealth and prosperity, and removes all evils and bad dreams.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच देयाः किंलक्षणा गावः काश्चापि परिवर्जयेत्। कीदृशाय प्रदातव्या न देयाः कीदृशाय च॥
en: Yudhishthira said What should be the marks of those kine that deserve to be given away? What are those kine that should be looked over in the matter of gifts? What should be the characters of those persons to whom should kine be given? Who, again, are those to whom kine should not be given?

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: भीष्म उवाच असवृत्ताय पापाय लुब्धायानृतवादिने। हव्यकव्यव्यपेताय न देया गौः कथंचन॥
en: Bhishma said A cow should never be given to one who is not pious in conduct, or one that is sinful, or one that is covetous, or one who is a liar, or one who does not make offerings to the departed manes and celestials.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: भिक्षवे बहुपुत्राय श्रोत्रियायाहिताग्नये। दत्त्वां दशगवां दाता लोकानाप्नोत्यनुत्तमान्॥
en: A person, by making a gift of ten kine to a Brahmana learned in the Vedas, poor in earthly riches, possessed of many children, and owning a domestic fire, attains numerous regions of great happiness.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: यश्चैव धर्मं कुरुते तस्य धर्मफलं च यत्। सर्वस्यैवांशभाग् दाता तं निमित्तं प्रवृत्तयः॥
en: When a man performs any meritorious act, assisted by what he has got in gift from another, he acquires portion of that merit.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: यश्चैवमुत्पादयते यश्चैनं त्रायते भयात्। यश्चास्य कुरुते वृत्तिं सर्वं ते पितरस्त्रयः॥
en: He who procreates a person, he who rescues a person, and he who assigns the means of livelihood to a person, are considered as the three fathers.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: कल्मषं गुरुशुश्रूषा हन्ति मानो महद् यशः। अपुत्रतां त्रयः पुत्रा आवृत्तिं दश धेनवः॥
en: Services dutifully done to the preceptor destroys sin. Pride destroys even great fame. The possession of three children removes the reproach of childlessness, and the possession of ten kine removes the reproach of poverty.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: वेदान्तनिष्ठस्य बहुश्रुतस्य प्रज्ञानतृप्तस्य जितेन्द्रियस्य। शिष्टस्य दान्तस्य यतस्य चैव भूतेषु नित्यं प्रियवादिनश्च॥ न्मृदुश्च शान्तो ह्यतिथिप्रियश्च। वृत्तिं द्विजायातिसृजेत तस्मै यस्तुल्यशीलश्च सपुत्रदारः॥
en: To one who is devoted to the Vedanta, who is gifted with great learning, who has been filled with wisdom, who has a complete mastery over his senses, who observes the restraints laid down in the scriptures, who has withdrawn himself from all worldly attachments, to him who says agreeable words to all creatures, to him who would never do an evil act even when actuated by hunger, to one who is mild or possessed of a peaceful disposition, to one that is hospitable to all guests, to such a Brahmana, should a man, possessed of similar conduct and having children and wives, assign the means of livelihood.

description: The gifts of earth. Vedic injunctions on the objects of gift
sn: शुभे पात्रे ये गुणा गोप्रदाने तावान् दोषो ब्राह्मणस्वापहारे। सर्वावस्थं ब्राह्मणस्वापहारो दाराश्चैषां दूरतो वर्जनीयाः॥
en: The merit of the gift of kine to a worthy person is exactly equal to the sin of robbing a Brahmana of what belongs to him. Under all circumstances anything belonging to Brahmana should be avoided and his wives kept at a distance. a

sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्रैव कीर्त्यते सद्भिाह्मणस्वाभिमर्शने। नृगेण सुमहत् कृच्छ्रे यदवाप्तं कृरूद्वह।॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it, O perpetuator of Kuru race, is recited by the righteous the narrative of the great calamity that befell king Nriga on account of his taking what had belonged to a Brahmana.

sn: निविशन्त्यां पुरा पार्थ द्वारवत्यामिति श्रुतिः। अदृश्यत महाकूपस्तृणवीरुत्समावृतः॥
en: Sometime before, certain youths of Yudu's race, while searching for water, came to a large well covered with grass and creepers.

sn: प्रयत्नं तत्र कुर्वाणास्तस्मात् कूपाज्जलार्थिनः। श्रमेण महत. युक्तास्तस्मिंस्तोये सुसंवृते॥ ददृशुस्ते महाकायं कृकलासमवस्थितम्। तस्य चोद्धरणे यत्नमकुर्वंस्ते सहस्रशः॥
en: Desirous of drawing water from it, they worked hard for removing the creepers they covered its mouth. After the mouth had been cleaned, they saw within the well a very large lizard living within it. The youths nade strong and repeated efforts for rescuing the lizard from that plight.

sn: प्रग्रहैश्चर्मपट्टैश्च तं बद्ध्वा पर्वतोपमम्। नाशक्नुवन् समुद्धर्तुं ततो जग्मुर्जनार्दनम्॥
en: Resembling a very hill in size, the lizard was sought to be freed by cords and leather tongs. Not succeeding in their attempts, the youths then went to Janardana.

sn: खमावृत्योदपानस्य कृकलासः स्थितो महान्। तस्य नास्ति समुद्धर्तेत्येतत् कृष्णे न्यवेदयन्॥
en: Addressing him they said— Covering the entire space of a well, there is a very large lizard to be seen. Despite our best efforts we have not succeeded in rescuing it from that plight. This was what they said to Krishna.

sn: माधव उवाच स वासुदेवेन समुद्धृतश्च पृष्टश्च कार्यं निजगाद राजा। नृगस्तदाऽऽत्मानमथो न्यवेदयत् पुरातनं यज्ञसहस्रयाजिनम्॥
en: Madhava spoke Vasudeva then went there and took out the lizard and questioned it as who it was. The lizard said that it was the soul of king Nriga who had flourished in days of yore and who had celebrated many sacrifices.

sn: तथा ब्रुवाणं तु तमाह माधवः शुभं त्वया कर्म कृतं न पापकम्। कथं भवान् दुर्गतिमीदृशीं गतो नरेन्द्र तद् ब्रूहि किमेतदीदृशम्॥
en: To the lizard that said those words "You had done many pious deeds. You committed no sin. Why then, O king, have you come by such a distressful end? Do you explain what is this and why has it been caused?"

sn: शतं सहस्राणि गवां शतं पुन: पुनः शतान्यष्टशतायुतानिा त्वया पुरा दत्तमितीह शुश्रुम नृप द्विजेभ्यः क्व तु तद् गतं तव॥
en: We have heared that you did repeatedly make gifts to the Brahmanas numerable kine. Why, therefore, have you come by this end.

sn: नृगस्ततोऽब्रवीत् कृष्णं ब्राह्मणस्याग्निहोत्रिणः। प्रोषितस्य परिभ्रष्टा गौरेका मम गोधने॥
en: Nriga then replied to Krishna, saying, On one occasion a cow belonging to a Brahmana who regularly adored his domestic fire, escaping from the owner's house while he was absent from home, entered my flock.

sn: गवां सहस्र संख्याता तदा सा पशुपैर्मम। सा ब्राह्मणाय दत्ता प्रेत्यार्थमभिकाइक्षता॥
en: The keepers of my cattle included that cow in their list of a thousand. In time that cow was given away by me to a Brahmana, wishing for liappiness in heaven.

sn: मे अपश्यत् परिमार्गश्च तां गां परगृहे द्विजः। ममेयमिति चोवाच ब्राह्मणो यस्य साभवत्॥
en: The true owner, returning home, sought for his lost cow and at last found it in the house of another. Finding her, the owner said, “This cow is mine."

sn: तावुभौ समनुप्राप्तौ विवदन्तो भृशज्वरौ। भवान् दाता भवान् हर्तेत्यथ तौ मामवोचताम्॥
en: The other person contested his claim, till both, growing wroth came to me. Addressing me, one of them said, You gave this cow. The other one said You have robbed me of this cow because she is inine.

sn: शतेन शतसंख्येन गवां विनिमयेन वै। याचे प्रतिग्रहीतारं स तु मामब्रवीदिदम्॥ देशकालोपसम्पन्ना दोग्ध्री शान्तातिवत्सला। स्वादुक्षीरप्रदा धन्या मम नित्यं निवेशने॥ कृतं च भरते सा गौर्मम पुत्रमपस्तनम्। न सा शक्या मया दातुमित्युक्त्वा स जगाम ह॥१६
en: I then begged the Brahmana to whom I had given that cow, to return the gift in exchange for hundreds and hundreds of other kine. Without yielding to my earnest solicitation, he addressed me saying, The cow I have got is well suited to time and place. She gives profuse inilk, besides being very quiet and very fond of us. The milk she gives is very sweet. She is lauded in my house. She is nourishing, besides, a weak child of mine that has just been born. I cannot, therefore, part with her. Having said these words, the Brahmana went away.

sn: ततस्तमपरं विप्रं याचे विनिमयेन वै। गवां शतसहस्रं हि तत्कृते गृह्यतामिति॥
en: I then begged the other Brahmana offering him an exchange, and saying-Do you take a hundred thousand kine for this one cow.

sn: न राज्ञां प्रतिगृह्णामि शक्तोऽहं स्वस्य मार्गणे। सैव गौर्दीयतां शीघ्रं ममेति मधुसूदन॥
en: The Brahmana, however, replied to me saying I do not accept gifts from Kshatriyas. I am able to support myself without aid. Do you then forthwith, give me that very cow which was mine. Thus, O slayer of Madhu, did that Brahmana speak to me.

sn: रुक्ममश्वांश्च ददतो रजतस्यन्दनांस्तथा। न जग्राह ययौ चापि तदा स ब्राह्मणर्षभः॥
en: I then offered to make gifts to him of gold and silver and horses and cars. That foremost of Brahmanas refused to accept any of these gifts and departed.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु चोदितः कालधर्मणा। पितृलोकमहं प्राप्य धर्मराजमुपागमम्॥
en: Meanwhile, urged by Time's irresistible power, I had to depart from this world. Going to the region of the departed manes I was taken before Yama the king of the dead.

sn: यमस्तु पूजयित्वा मां ततो वचनमब्रवीत्। नान्तः संख्यायते राजंस्तव पुण्यस्य कर्मणः॥
en: Adoring me duly, Yama addressed me saying-The end cannot be determined, O king, of your righteous deeds.

sn: अस्ति चैव कृतं पापमज्ञानात् तदपि त्वया। चरस्व पापं पश्चाद् वा पूर्वं वा त्वं यथेच्छसि॥
en: There is, however, a little sin which was unconsciously committed by you. Do you suffer the punishment for that sin now or afterwards as you like.

sn: रक्षितास्मीति चोक्तं ते प्रतिज्ञा चानृता तव। ब्राह्मणस्वस्य चादानं द्विविधस्ते व्यतिक्रमः॥
en: You had sworn that you would protect (all persons in the enjoyment of their own). This oath of yours was not rigidly kept by you. You took also what belonged to a Brahmana. This has been the twofold sin, you have perpetrated.

sn: पूर्वं कृच्छ्रे चरिष्येऽहं पश्चाच्छुभमिति प्रभो। धर्मराजं ब्रुवन्नेवं पतितोऽस्मि महीतले॥
en: I answered, saying-I shall first suffer the distress of punishment, and when that is over, I shall enjoy the happiness that is in store for me, O lord! After I had said these words to the king of the dead, I dropped down on the Earth.

sn: अश्रौषं पतितश्चाहं यमस्योच्चैः प्रभाषतः। वासुदेवः समुद्धर्ता भविता ते जनार्दनः॥
en: Though fallen down I still could hear the words that Yama said to me very loudly. Those words were-Janardana the son of Vasudeva, will save you.

sn: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रान्ते क्षीणे कर्मणि दुष्कृते। प्राप्स्यसे शाश्वतान्लोकाञ्जितान् स्वेनैव कर्मणा।।२६
en: Upon the completion of a full thousand years, when your sin will be dissipated you shall then attain to many regions of unending happiness that have been acquired by you through your own pious deeds.

sn: कूपेऽऽत्मानमधःशीर्षमपश्यं पतितश्च ह। तिर्यग्योनिमनुप्राप्तं न च मामजहात् स्मृतिः॥
en: Falling down I found myself, with head downwards, within this well changed into a creature of the intermediate order, Memory, however, did not leave me.

sn: त्वया तु तारितोऽस्म्यद्य किमन्यत्र तपोबलात्। अनुजानीहि मां कृष्ण गच्छेयं दिवमद्य वै॥
en: By you I have been saved today. What else can it testify than the power of your penances? Let me have your permission, O Krishna. I wish to ascend to the celestial region.

sn: अनुज्ञात: स कृष्णेन नमस्कृत्य जनार्दनम्। दिव्यमास्थाय पन्थानं ययौ दिवमरिंदमः॥
en: Permitted then by Krishna, king Nriga bowed his head to him and then mounted a celestial car and went to Heaven.

sn: ततस्तस्मिन् दिवं याते नृगे भरतसत्तम। वासुदेव इमं श्लोकं जगाद कुरुनन्दन॥
en: After Nriga had thus proceeded to the celestial region, O best of the Bharatas, Vasudeva recited this Verse, O delighter, of the Kurus.

sn: ब्राह्मणस्वं न हर्तव्यं पुरुषेण विजानता। ब्राह्मणस्वं हृतं हन्ति नृगं ब्राह्मणगौरिव॥
en: No one should knowingly misappropriate anything belonging to a a Brahmana. The property of Brahmana, if take, destroys the taker even as the Brahmana's cow destroyed king Nriga!

sn: सतां समागमः सद्भिर्नाफलः पार्थ विद्यते। विमुक्तं नरकात् पश्य नृगं साधुसमागमात्॥
en: I tell you, again O Partha, that a meeting with the good never proves furtile. See king Nriga was rescued from Hell through a meeting of his with one that is good.

sn: प्रदानफलवत् तत्र द्रोहस्तत्र तथाफलः। अपचारं गवां तस्माद् वर्जयेत युधिष्ठिर।॥
en: As a gift yields merit, so an act of spoliation brings on to demerit. Hence also, O Yudhishthira one should avoid doing any injury to kine.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दत्तानां फलसम्प्राप्तिं गवां प्रब्रूहि मेऽनघ। विस्तरेण महाबाहो न हि तृष्यामि कथ्यताम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O sinless one, do you describe to me more fully the merits of making gifts of kine. O you of mighty arms, I am never satiated with your words.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। ऋषेरुद्दालकेर्वाक्यं नाचिकेतस्य चोभयोः॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old discourse between the Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: ऋषिरुद्दालकिर्दीक्षामुपगम्य ततः सुतम्। त्वं मामुपचरस्वेति नाचिकेतमभाषत॥
en: Once on a time the Rishi Uddalaki, gifted with great intelligence, approaching his son Nachiketa, said to him, Do you wait upon and serve me.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: समाप्ते नियमे तस्मिन् महर्षिः पुत्रमब्रवीत्। उपस्पर्शनसक्तस्य स्वाध्यायाभिरतस्य च॥ इध्मा दर्भाः सुमनसः कलशश्चातिभोजनम्। विस्मृतं मे तदादाय नदीतीरादिहाव्रज॥
en: Upon the completion of the vow he had observed, the great Rishi once more said to his son, Engaged in performing my ablutions and deeply busy with my Vedic study, I have forgotten to bring with me the firewood, the Kusha blades, the flowers, the waterjar, and the potherbs I had collected. Bring me those things from the riverbank.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: गत्वानवाप्य तत् सर्वं नदीवेगसमाप्लुतम्। न पश्यामि तदित्येवं पितरं सोऽब्रवीन्मुनिः॥
en: The son went there, but found all the articles washed away by the current. Returning to his father, he said “I do not see the things."

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: क्षुत्पिपासाश्रमाविष्टो मुनिरुद्दालकिस्तदा। यमं पश्येति तं पुत्रमशपत् स महातपाः॥
en: Stricken as he then was by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, the Rishi Uddalaki of great ascetic merit, in a sudden anger cursed his son, saying, meet with Yama today.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: तथा स पित्राभिहतो वाग्वज्रेण कृताञ्जलिः। प्रसीदेति ब्रुवन्नेव गतसत्त्वोऽपतद् भुवि॥
en: Thus struck by his father with the thunder of his speech, the son, with joined hands, said, “Be pleased with me. Soon, however, he dropped down on the earth dead.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: नाचिकेतं पिता दृष्ट्वा पतितं दुःखमूच्छितः। किं मया कृतमित्युक्त्वा निपपात महीतले॥
en: Seeing Nachiketa prostrated upon the earth, his father become senseless with grief. He, too, exclaiming, Alas, what have I done! dropped down on the earth.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: तस्य दुःखपरीतस्य स्वं पुत्रमनुशोचतः। व्यतीतं तदहःशेषं सा चोग्रा तत्र शर्वरी॥
en: Filled with grief as he bewailed for his son, the rest of that day passed away and night came.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: पित्र्येणाश्रुप्रपातेन नाचिकेतः कुरूद्वह। प्रास्पन्दच्छयने कौश्ये वृष्ट्या सस्यमिवाप्लुतम्॥
en: Then Nachiketa, O son of Kuru's race, drenched by the tears of his father, showed signs of returning life as he lay on a mat of Kusha grass. His regaining of life under the tears of his father resembled the sprouting forth of seeds when drenched with good showers.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: स पर्यपृच्छत् तं पुत्रं क्षीणं पर्यागतं पुनः। दिव्यैर्गन्धैः समादिग्धं क्षीणस्वप्नमिवोत्थितम्॥
en: The son, just restored to life, was still weak. His body was smeared with scents and the looked like one just awaking from a deep sleep. The Rishi asked hiin, saying.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: अपि पुत्र जिता लोकाः शुभास्ते स्वेन कर्मणा। दिष्ट्या चासि पुनः प्राप्तो न हि ते मानुषं वपुः।।१३
en: Have you, O son, acquired auspicious regions by your own deeds? By good luck, you have been restored to me. Your body does not seem to be human.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: प्रत्यक्षदर्शी सर्वस्य पित्रा पृष्टो महात्मना। स तां वार्ता पितुर्मध्ये महर्षीणां न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Thus asked by his great father. Nachiketa who had seen every thing with his own eyes, answered thus in the midst of the Rishis.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: कुर्वन् भवच्छासनमाशु यातो ह्यहं विशालां रुचिरप्रभावाम्। वैवस्वतीं प्राप्य सभामपश्यं सहस्रशो योजनहेमभासम्॥
en: In obedience to your command I proceeded to the vast region of Yama which is possessed of a charming effulgence. There I saw a palatial mansion which extended for thousands of Yojanas and emitted a golden splendour on every part.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: दृष्ट्वैव मामभिमुखमापतन्तं देहीति स शासनमादिदेश। वैवस्वतोऽादिभिरहणैश्च भवत्कृते पूजयामास मां सः॥
en: As soon as Yama saw me approaching with face towards him, he ordered his attendants, saying, Give him a good seat. Indeed the king of the dead, for your sake, adored me with the Arghya and other ingredients.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: ततस्त्वहं तं शनकैरवोचं वृतः सदस्यैरभिपूज्यमानः। प्राप्तोऽस्मि ते विषयं धर्मराज लोकानों यानहं तान् विधत्सव॥
en: Thus adored by Yama and seated in the midst of his counsellors, I then asked him mildly, I have come to your house, O judge of the dead. Do you assign me those regions which I deserve for my acts.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: यमोऽब्रवीन्मां न मृतोऽसि सौम्य यमं पश्येत्याह स त्वां तपस्वी। पिता प्रदीप्ताग्निसमानतेजा न तच्छक्यमनृतं विप्र कर्तुम्॥
en: Yama then answered me, saying, You are not dead, ( amiable one. Gifted with penances, your father said to you meet with Yama. The energy of your father is like that of a burning fire. I could not possibly falsify that speech of his.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: दृष्टस्तेऽहं प्रतिगच्छस्व तात शोचत्यसौ तव देहस्य कर्ता। ददानि किं चापि मन:प्रणीतं प्रियातिधेस्तव कामान् वृणीष्व॥
en: You have seen me. Do you go hence, O child. The author of your body is bewailing for you. You are my dear guest. What wish of yours shall I fulfil? Solicit the fruition of whatever desire you may have.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: तेनैवमुक्तस्तमहं प्रत्यवोचं प्राप्तोऽस्मि ते विषयं दुर्निवर्त्यम्। इच्छाम्यहं पुण्यकृतां समृद्धान् लोकान् द्रष्टुं यदि तेऽहं वरार्हः॥
en: Thus addressed by him, I replied to the king of the dead, saying, I have arrived within your territory from which no traveller ever returns. If I am worthy of your attentions, I wish, O king of the dead, to see those regions of great prosperity and happiness that have been reserved for doers of virtuous deeds.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: तु यानं समारोप्य मां स देवो वाहैर्युक्तं सुप्रभं भानुमत् तत्। संदर्शयामास तदात्मलोकान् सर्वोस्तथा पुण्यकृतां द्विजेन्द्र॥
en: Thus addressed by me, Yama made me mount a vehicle effulgent as the Sun and to which were yoked many excellent horses. Taking me on that car, he showed me, O foremost of twice born ones, all those charming regions that are reserved for the pious.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: अपश्यं तत्र वेश्मानि तैजसानि महात्मनाम्। नानासंस्थानरूपाणि सर्वरत्नमयानि च॥
en: I saw in those regions many effulgent palaces intended for great persons. Those mansions are of various forns and are adorned with every kind of gems.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: चन्द्रमण्डलशुभ्राणि किङ्किणीजालवन्ति च। अनेकशतभौमानि सान्त लवनानि च।॥
en: Bright as the lunar disc, they are ornamented with rows of tinkling bells, Hundreds among them are many storied. Within them are charming groves and gardens and transparent pools of water.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: वैदूर्यार्कप्रकाशनि रूप्यरुक्ममयानि च। तरुणादित्यवर्णानि स्थावराणि चराणि च॥
en: Effulgent like lapis lazuli and the Sun, and made of silver and gold, their colour resembles that of the morning Sun. Some of them are fixed and soine movable.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: भक्ष्यभोज्यमयान्शैलान् वासांसि शयनानि च। सर्वकामफलांश्चैव वृक्षान् भवनसंस्थितान्॥
en: Within them are many hills of foods any enjoyable articles, and dresses and beds in abundance. Within them are many trees capable of granting the fruition of every desire.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: नद्यो वीथ्यः सभा वाप्यो दीर्घिकाश्चैव सर्वशः। घोषवन्ति च यानानि युक्तान्यथ सहस्रशः॥
en: There are also many rivers and roads and spacious halls and lakes and large tanks. Thousands of cars with rattling wheels may be seen there, having excellent horses yoked to them.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: क्षीरस्रवा वै सरितो गिरीश्च सर्पिस्तथा विमलं चापि तोयम्। नदृष्टपूर्वान् सुबहूनपश्यम्॥
en: Many rivers of milk, many hills of clarified butter and large pieces of transparent water are there. Indeed, I saw many such regions never seen by me before, of happiness and joy, approved by the king of dead.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: मवोचं वै प्रभविष्णुं पुराणम्। क्षीरस्यैताः सर्पिषश्चैव नद्यः शश्वत्स्रोताः कस्य भोज्याः प्रदिष्टा॥
en: Seeing all those objects, I addressed the ancient and powerful judge of the dead, saying For whose use and enjoyment have these rivers with eternal currents of milk and clarified butter been ordained?

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: यम उवाच यमोऽब्रवीद् विद्धि भोज्यास्त्वमेता ये दातारः साधवो गोरसानाम्। अन्ये लोकाः शाश्वता वीतशोकैः समाकीर्णा गोप्रदाने रतानाम्॥
en: Yama said These rivers of milk and clarified butter are for the enjoyment of those pious persons who make gifts in the world of men. Other eternal worlds there are which are filled with such palaces free from every sort of sorrow. These are reserved for th« se persons who make gift of kine.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: न त्वेतासां दानमात्रं प्रशस्तं पात्रं कालो गोविशेषे विधिश्च। ज्ञात्वां देयं विप्र गवान्तरं हि दुःखं ज्ञातुं पावकादित्यभूतम्॥
en: The mere gift of kine is not laudable. There are considerations of fitness or otherwise about the person to whom kine should be given, the time for making those gifts, the kind of kine and rites that should be observed in making the gifts. Gifts of kine should be made after knowing the qualifications of both Brahmanas and the kine themselves. Kine should not be given to one in whose house they are likely to suffer from fire or the sun.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: स्वाध्यायवान् योऽतिमात्रं तपस्वी वैतानस्थो ब्राह्मणः पात्रमासाम्। कृच्छ्रोत्सृष्टाः योषणाभ्यागताश्च द्वारैरेतैर्गोविशेषाः प्रशस्ताः॥
en: That Brahmana, who is endued with Vedic learning, who is of austere penances, and who celebrates sacrifices, is considered as worthy of receiving kine in gift. Those kine which have been saved from distressful situations, or which have been given by poor householders from want of sufficient means to feed and cherish them, are for these reasons, counted as of great value.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: तिस्रो राज्यस्त्वद्भिपोष्य भूमौ तृप्ता गावस्तर्पितेभ्यः प्रदेयाः। स्त्र्यहं दत्त्वा गोरसैर्वर्तितव्यम्॥
en: Abstaining from all food and subsisting upon water alone for three nights and sleeping the while on the naked earth, one should, having properly fed the kine intended to be given away, give them to Brahmanas after having pleased them also (with other gifts).

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: दत्त्वा धेनुं सुव्रता कांस्यदोहां कल्याणवत्सामलायिनी च। स्तावद् वर्षाण्यश्नुते स्वर्गलोकम्॥
en: The kine, given away, should be accompanied by their calves. They should, again, be such as to bring forth good calves at the proper They should be accompanied with other articles. Having completed the gift, the giver should live for three days on only milk and abstaining from food of every other kind.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: तथानड्वाहं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रदाय दान्तं धुर्यं बलवन्तं युवानम्। कुलानुजीव्यं वीर्यवन्तं बृहन्तं भुङ्क्ते लोकान् सम्मितान् धेनुदस्य॥
en: He, who gives a good cow that brings forth good calves at proper time, and that does not fly away from the owner's house, and accompanies such gifts with a vessel of white brass for milking her, enjoys the divine happiness for as many years as are measured by the number of hairs on the animal's body. He who gives a bull to a Brahmana, that is wellbroken and capable of carrying loads, strong and young in years, disinclined to do any mischief, largesized and powerful enjoys those regions, approved of the righteous, that are reserved for givers of kine.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: गोषु क्षान्तं गोशरण्यं कृतज्ञं वृत्तिग्लानं तादृशं पात्रमाहुः। वृद्धे ग्लाने सम्भ्रमे वा महार्थे कृष्यर्थं वा होम्यहेतोः प्रसूत्याम्॥ गुर्वर्थं वा बालपुष्ट्याभिषणां गां वै दातुं देशकालोऽविशिष्टः। अन्तर्ज्ञाताः सक्रयज्ञानलब्धाः प्राणक्रीता निर्जिता यौतकाच॥
en: He is considered as a proper person for receiving a cow in gift who is known to be mild towards kine, who takes kine for his refuge, who is grateful, and who has no means of livelihood assigned to him. When an old man becomes ill, or when a famine takes place or when a Brahmana intends to celebrate a sacrifice, or when one wishes to till for agriculture, or when one gets a son through the efficacy of a Home performed for the purpose, or for the use of one's preceptor, or for the sustenance of a child, one should give away a loved cow. These are the considerations that are spoken highly of about place and time. The kine worthy of being given away are those that give profuse milk, or those which wellknown, or those that have been acquired as honoraria for learning, or those that have been purchased for price, or those that have been obtained in exchange by offering other living are creatures, or those that have been got by prowess of arms, or those that have been got as marriagedower.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: नचिकेता उवाच श्रुत्वा वैवस्वतवचस्तमहं पुनरब्रुवम्। अभावे गोप्रदातॄणां कथं लोकान् हि गच्छति॥
en: Nachiketa said Hearing these words of Vaivasvata, the Regent of the dead, I once more addressed him, saying What are those objects by giving which, when kine cannot be had, givers may yet go to regions reserved for men making gifts of kine.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: ततोऽब्रवीद् यमो धीमान् गोप्रदानपरां गतिम्। गोप्रदानानुकल्पं तु गामृते सन्ति गोप्रदाः॥
en: Accosted by me, the wise Yama answered, explaining further what the end is which one wins by making gifts of kine. He said, In the absence of kine, a person by making gifts of the substitute of kine, acquires the merit of making gifts of kine.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: अलाभे यो गवां दद्याद् घृतधेनुं यतव्रतः। तस्यैता घृतवाहिन्यः क्षरन्ते वत्सला इव॥
en: If in the absence of kine, one makes a gift of a cow made of clarified butter, observant of a vow the while, one gets for one's use these rivers of clarified butter all of which approach one like an affectionate mother approaching her loved child.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: घृतालाभे तु यो दद्यात् तिलधेनुं यतव्रतः। स दुर्गात् तारितो धेन्वा क्षीरनद्यां प्रमोदते॥
en: If in absence of even a cow made of clarified butter, one makes a gift of a cow made of sesame seeds, observing a vow the while, one succeeds with the help of that cow to get over all calamities in this world and to enjoy great happiness hereafter from these rivers of milk that you see.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: तिलालाभे तु यो दद्याज्जलधेनुं यतव्रतः। स कामप्रवहां शीतां नदीमेतामुपाश्नुते॥
en: If a cow made of sesame seeds, is not available, one makes a gift of a cow made of water, he succeeds in coming to these happy regions and enjoying this river of cool and transparent water, that can grant the fruition of every desire.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: एवमेतानि मे तत्र धर्मराजो न्यदर्शयत्। दृष्ट्वा च परमं हर्षमवापमहमच्युत॥
en: The king of the dead explained to me all this while I was his guest, and, O you of unfading glory, great was the joy that I felt on seeing all the wonders he showed me.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: निवेदये चाहमिमं प्रियं ते क्रतुर्महानल्पधनप्रचारः। प्राप्तो मया तात स मत्प्रसूतः। प्रपत्स्यते वेदविधिप्रवृत्तः॥
en: I shall now tell you what would certainly be agreeable to you. I have now got a great sacrifice whose performance does not require much riches. That sacrifice may be said to originate from me, O sire. Others will obtain it also. It is not quite of a piece with the ordinances of the Vedas.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: शापो ह्ययं भवतोऽनुग्रहाय प्राप्तो मया यत्र दृष्ट्वा यमो वै। दानव्युष्टिं तत्र दृष्ट्वा महात्मन् नि:संदिग्धान् दानधर्मोश्चरिष्ये॥
en: The curse that you had imprecated on me was no curse but was in sooth a blessing, since it enabled me to see the great king of the dead. There I have seen what the rewards are of gifts. I shall henceforth, O you of great soul, practise the duty of gift without any doubt about its rewards.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: इदं च मामब्रवीद् धर्मराजः पुनः पुनः सम्प्रहृष्टो महर्षे दानेन यः प्रयतोऽभूत् सदैव विशेषतो गोप्रदानं च कुर्यात्॥
en: And, O great Rishi, the righteous Yama, filled with joy, repeatedly told me. One who, by making repeated gifts, has succeeded in acquiring purity of mind should then make gift of kine in particular.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: शुद्धो ह्यर्थो नावमन्यस्व धर्मान् पात्रे देयं देशकालोपपन्ने। तस्माद् गावस्ते नित्यमेव प्रदेया मा भूच्च ते संशयः कश्चिदत्र॥
en: The subject is fraught with sanctity. Do you never disregard the duties of gifts. Gifts, again, should be made to worth persons, when time and place are suitable. Do you, therefore, always make gifts of kine. Never entertain any doubt about it.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: एताः पुरा ह्यददन्नित्यमेव शान्तात्मानो दानपथे निविष्टाः। स्ते वै दानं प्रददुश्चैव शक्त्या॥
en: Devoted to the path of gifts, formerly many great persons used to make gifts of kine. Fearing to practise austere penances, they made gifts according to their power.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: काले च शक्त्या मत्सरं वर्जयित्वा शुद्धात्मानः श्रद्धिनः पुण्यशीलाः। दत्त्वा गां वै लोकममुं प्रपन्ना देदीप्यन्ते पुण्यशीलास्तु नाके॥
en: In time they shook off all sentiments of pride and vanity, and purified their souls. Engaged in performing Shraddhas in honour of the departed manes and in all religious acts of righteousness, they used to make, according to their power, gifts of kine, and as the reward of those acts they have attained to the celestial region and are shining in effulgence for such virtue.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: एतद् दानं न्यायलब्धं द्विजेभ्यः पात्रे दत्तं प्रापणीयं परीक्ष्य। काम्याष्टम्या वर्तितव्यं दशाह रसैर्गवां शकृता प्रस्रवैर्वा॥
en: One should, on the eighth day of the moon that is known by the name of Kamyashtami, make gifts a kine, properly got, to the Brahinanas, after determining the fitness of the recipients. After making the gift, one should then live for ten days together upon only the milk of kine, their dung and their urin ..

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: र्वेदावाप्तिर्गोयुगस्य प्रदाने। तीर्थावाप्तिर्गोप्रयुक्तप्रदाने पापोत्सर्गः कपिलायाः प्रदाने॥
en: The merit that one acquires by making a gift of a bull is equal to that of the divine cow. By making a gift of a couple of kine one gains, as the reward thereof, a mastery of the Vedas. By making a gift of cars and vehicles with kine yoked thereto, one wins the merit of baths in sacred water. By making a gift of a cow of the Kapila kine, one becomes purged of all his sins.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: गामप्येकां कपिलां सम्प्रदाय न्यायोपेतां कलुषाद् विप्रमुच्येत्। गवां रसात् परमं नास्ति किंचिद् गवां प्रदानं सुमहद् वदन्ति॥
en: Indeed by giving away even a single cow of the Kapila kine that has been acquired by fair means, one becomes purged of all his sins. There is nothing higher than the milk which is given by kine. The gift of a cow is truly considered as a very superior gift.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: गावो लोकांस्तारयन्ति क्षरन्त्यो गावश्चान्नं संजनयन्ति लोके। यस्तं जानन गवां हार्दमेति स वै गन्ता निरयं पापचेताः॥
en: Kine, by giving milk, rescue all the worlds from calamity. It is kine, again, that produce the food upon which creatures live. One who, knowing the extent of the service that kine do, does not entertain in his heart love for kine, is a sinner who is sure to sink in Hell.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: यैस्तद् दत्तं गोसहस्रं शतं वा दशार्धं वा दश वा साधुवत्सम्। अप्येका वै साधवे ब्राह्मणाय सास्यामुष्मिन् पुण्यतीर्था नदी वै॥
en: If one gives a thousand or a hundred or ten or five kine, indeed, if one gives to a pious Brahmana even a single cow which brings forth good calves at proper seasons, he is sure to see that cow approach him in Heaven in the form of a river of sacred water capable of granting the fruition of every desire.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: प्राप्त्या पुष्ट्या लोकसंरक्षणेन गावस्तुल्याः सूर्यपादैः पृथिव्याम्। स्तस्माद् गोदः सूर्य इवावभाति॥
en: About prosperity and the growth that kine confer, in the matter also of the protection that kine grant to all creatures of the Earth, kine are equal to the very rays of the Sun that fall on the Earth. The word that signifies the cow means also the rays of the Sun. The giver of a cow begets a very large progeny inhabiting a large part of the Earth. Hence, he who gives a cow shines like a second Sun in effulgence.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: गुरुं शिष्यो वरयेद् गोप्रदाने स वै गन्ता नियतं स्वर्गमेव। विधिज्ञानं सुमहान् धर्म एष विधिं ह्याद्यं विधयः संविशन्ति॥
en: The disciple should, in the matter of making gifts of kine, select his preceptor. Such a disciple is sure to go to Heaven every time. The selection of a preceptor is considered as a high duty by persons knowing the ordinances. This is, indeed, the initial ordinance. All other ordinances depend upon it.

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: इदं दानं न्यायलब्धं द्विजेभ्यः पात्रे दत्त्वा प्रापयेथाः परीक्ष्य। त्वय्याशंसन्त्यमरा मानवाश्च वयं चापि प्रसृते पुण्यशीले॥
en: Selecting, after examination, a fit person among the Brahmanas, one should make to him the gift of a cow that has been acquired by fair means, and having made the gift make him accept it. The deities and men and ourselves also, in wishing good to others, say, Let the merits of gifts be yours on account of your virtue?

description: The merits of the gifts of kine. The discourse between Rishi Uddalaki and Nachiketa
sn: इत्युक्तोऽहं धर्मराजं द्विजर्षे धर्मात्मानं शिरसाभिप्रणम्य। अनुज्ञातस्तेन वैवस्वतेन प्रत्यागमं भगवत्पादमूलम्॥
en: Thus did the judge of the dead speak to me, O twiceborn Rishi. I then bowed my head to the righteous Yama. Getting his permission I left his kingdom and have now come to the sole of your feet.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उक्तं ते गोप्रदानं वै नाचिकेतमृषि प्रति। माहात्म्यमपि चैवोक्तमुद्देशेन गवां प्रभो॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have O grandfather, describe to me the topic of gifts of kine in speaking of the Rishi Nachiketa You have also, related O powerful one, the efficacy and preeminence of that act.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: नृगेण च महदुःखमनुभूतं महात्मना। एकापराधदज्ञानात् पितामह महामते॥
en: You have also told me O grandfather, of great intelligence, the exceedingly painful character of the misfortune that befell the great king Nriga on account of a single transgression of his.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: द्वारवत्यां यथा चासौ निविशन्त्यां समुद्धतः। मोक्षहेतुरभूत् कृष्णस्तदप्यवधृतं मया।॥
en: He had to live for a long time at Dvaravati (in the form of a mighty lizard) and how Krishna became the instrument of his rescue from that miserable condition.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: किं त्वस्ति मम संदेहो गवां लोकं प्रति प्रभो। तत्त्वतः श्रोतुमिच्छामि गोदा यत्र वसन्त्युत॥
en: I have, however one doubt. About the regions of kine. I wish to hear particularly about those regions which are reserved for the residence of persons who make gifts of kine.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। यथापृच्छत् पद्मयोनिमेतदेव शतक्रतुः॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old discourse between him who sprang from the primeval lotus and him who performed a hundred sacrifices.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: शक्र उवाच स्वर्लोकवासिनां लक्ष्मीमभिभूय स्वयार्चिषा। गोलोकवासिनः पश्ये व्रजतः संशयोऽत्र मे॥
en: Shakra said I see, O grandfather, that those who live in the region of kine transcend by their effulgence the prosperity of the celestial dwellers and pass them by. This has created a doubt in my mind.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: कीदृशा भगवॅल्लोका गवां तद् ब्रूहि मेऽनघ। यानावसन्ति दातार एतदिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: Of what kind, O holy one, are the regions of kine? Tell me all about them, O sinless one. Indeed, what is the nature of those regions that are inhabited by givers of kine? I wish to know this.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: कीदृशाः किंफलाः किंस्वित् परमस्तत्र को गुणः। कथं च पुरुषास्तत्र गच्छन्ति विगतज्वराः॥
en: Of what kind are those regions? What fruits do they yield? What is the highest object there which the inhabitants thereof succeed in acquiring? What are its virtues. How also do men, shorn of anxiety, succeed in going to those regions?

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: कियत्कालं प्रदानस्य दाता च फलमश्नुते। कथं बहुविधं दानं स्यादल्पमपि वा कथम्॥
en: For what period does the giver of a cow enjoy the fruits of his gift? How may persons make gifts of many kine and how may they make gifts of a few kine?

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: बह्वीनां कीदृशं दानमल्पानां वापि कीदृशम्। अदत्त्वा गोप्रदाः सन्ति केन वा तच्च शंस मे॥
en: What are the merits of the gifts of many kine and what those of the gifts of a few only. How also do persons become givers of kine without really giving any kine? Do you tell me all this.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: कथं वा बहुदाता स्यादल्पदात्रा समः प्रभो। अल्पप्रदाता बहुदः कथं स्वित् स्यादिहेश्वर॥
en: How does one making gifts of even many kine, O powerful lord, become the equal of one who has made gifts of only a few kine? How also does one who has made gifts of only few kine equal one who has made gifts of many kine?

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: कीदृशी दक्षिणा चैव गोप्रदाने विशिष्यते। एतत् तथ्येन भगवन् मम शंसितुमर्हसि॥
en: What kind of present is considered and distinguished for preeminence in the matter of gifts of kine? You should, O holy one, describe to me all this according to truth.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: पितामह उवाच योऽयं प्रश्नस्त्वया पृष्टो गोप्रदानादिकारितः। नास्ति प्रष्टास्ति लोकेऽस्मिंस्त्वत्तोऽन्योहि शतक्रतो॥१
en: The grandfather said The questions you have put to me about kine, beginning with their gift, are such that there is none else in the three world, O you of a hundred sacrifices, who could put them.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: सन्ति नानाविधा लोका यांस्त्वं शक्र न पश्यसि। पश्यामियानहं लोकानेकपत्न्यश्च याः स्त्रियः॥
en: There are many kinds of regions, O Shakra, which are invisible to even you. Those regions are seen by me. O Indra,, as also by those women who are chaste and who have been devoted to only one husband.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: कर्मभिश्चापि सुशुभैः सुव्रता ऋषयस्तथा। सशरीरा हि तान् यान्ति ब्राह्मणाः शुभबुद्धयः॥
en: Rishis observe excellent vows, by means of their deeds of virtue and piety and Brahmanas of righteous souls, succeed in going there in even their human bodies.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: शरीरन्यासमोक्षेण मनसा निर्मलेन च। स्वप्नभूतांश्च ताल्लोकान् पश्यन्तीहापि सुव्रताः॥
en: Men who perform excellent vows see those regions which resemble the bright creations of dreams helped by their purified minds and by that (temporary) liberation which succeeds the loss of one's consciousness of body.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: ते तु लोकाः सहस्राक्ष शृणु यादृग्गुणान्विताः। न तत्र क्रमते कालो न जरा न च पावकः॥ तथा नास्त्यशुभं किंचिन्न व्याधिस्तत्र न क्रमः।
en: O you, of a thousand eyes, hear me as I tell you what the attributes are of those regions. There the very course of Time is stopped. Decrepitude is not there nor Fire which is omnipresent in the universe. There is slightest transgression does not take place, nor disease, nor weakness of any sort.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: यद् यच्च गावो मनसा तस्मिन् वान्छन्ति वासव॥ तत् सर्वं प्राप्नुवन्ति स्म मम प्रत्यक्षदर्शनात्।
en: The kine which live there, O Vasava, acquire the fruition of every desire which they cherish in their hearts. I have direct experience of what I say to you.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: कामगाः कामचारिण्यः कामात् कामांश्च भुञ्जते॥ वाप्यः सरांसि सरितो विविधानि वनानि च। गृहाणि पर्वताश्चैव यावद्र्व्यं च किंचन॥ मनोज्ञं सर्वभूतेभ्यः सर्वतन्त्रं प्रदृश्यत। ईदृशाद् विपुलाल्लोकान्नास्ति लोकस्तथाविधः॥
en: Capable of going everywhere at will and actually going from place to place with ease, they enjoy the fruition of desire after desire as it arises in their minds. Lakes, tanks, rivers, forests of diverse kinds, mansions, hills and all kinds of delightful objects are to be seen there. There is no region of happiness that is superior to any of these of which I speak.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: तत्र सर्वसहाः क्षान्ता वत्सला गुरुवर्तिनः। अहङ्कारैर्विरहिता यान्ति शक्र नरोत्तमाः॥
en: All those foremost of men, O Shakra, who are forgiving to all creatures, who endure everything, who are full of love for all things, who render dutiful obedience to their preceptors, and who are freed from pride and vanity, go to those regions of supreme happiness.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: यः सर्वमांसानि न भक्षयीत पुमान् सदा भावितो धर्मयुक्तः। मातापित्रोरर्चिता सत्ययुक्तः शुश्रूषिता ब्राह्मणानामनिन्द्यः।॥ अक्रोधनो गोषु तथा द्विजेषु धर्मे रतो गुरुशुश्रूषकश्चा यावज्जीवं सत्यवृत्ते रतश्च दाने रतो यः क्षमी चापराधे॥ मृदुर्दान्तो देवपरायणश्च सर्वातिथिश्चापि तथा दयावान्। ईदृग्गुणो मानवस्तं प्रयाति लोकं गवां शाश्वतं चाव्ययं च॥
en: He who abstains from every kind of flesh, who is possessed of a pure heart, who is gifted with righteousness, who worships his parents with respect, who is endued with truthfulness of speech and conduct, who attends with obedience upon the Brahmanas, who is faultless in conduct, who never behaves with anger towards kine and towards the Brahmanas, who performs every duty, who serves his preceptors with reverence, who is devoted for his whole life to truth and to gifts, and who is always forgiving towards all transgressions against himself, who is mild and selfcontrolled, who is full of respect for the celestials, who is hospitable to all guests, who is gifted with mercy, indeed, he who is adorned with these attributes, succeeds in attaining to the eternal region of kine.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: न पारदारी पश्यति लोकमेतं न वै गुरुघ्नो न मृषा सम्प्रलापी। सदा प्रवादी ब्राह्मणेष्वात्तवैरो दोषैरेतैर्यश्च युक्तो दुरात्मा॥ न मित्रधुड्नैकृतिकः कृतघ्नः शठोऽनृजुर्धर्मविद्वेषश्च। न ब्रह्महा मनसापि प्रपश्येद् गवां लोकं पुण्यकृतां निवासम्॥
en: He who is sullied with adultery, sees not such a region; nor he who is a destroyer of his preceptor; nor he who speaks falsely or indulges in idle vaunts; nor he who always disputes with others; nor he who acts with hostility towards the Brahmanas. Indeed, that wicked man who is sullied with such faults cannot even see these regions of happiness; nor he who injures his friends, nor he who is guileful; nor he who is ungrateful; nor he who is a cheat; nor he who is crooked in conduct; nor he who is a disregarder of religion nor he who is a slayer of Brahmanas. Such man cannot see in ever Imagination the region of kine that is the abode of only the pious.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं निपुणेन सुरेश्वर। गोप्रदानरतानां तु फलं शृणु शतक्रतो॥
en: I have told you everything particularly about the regions of kine, O king of the celestials. Hear now, O you of a hundred sacrifices, the merit of persons who are engaged in making gifts of kine.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: दायाद्यलब्धैरथैयो गाः क्रीत्वा सम्प्रयच्छति। धर्मार्जितान् धनैः क्रीतान् स लोकानाप्नुतेऽयान्॥
en: He who makes gifts of kine, after purchasing them with money obtained by inheritance or acquired by fair means, attains, as the fruit of such an act, to many regions of endless happiness.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: यो वै द्यूतेधनं जित्वा गाः क्रीत्वा सम्प्रयच्छति। स दिव्यमयुतं शक्र वर्षाणां फलमश्नुते॥
en: He who makes a gift of a cow, having acquired it with money, won at dice, enjoys happiness, O Shakra, for ten thousand celestial years.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: दायाद्याद्याः स्म वै गावो न्यायपूर्वैरुपार्जिताः। प्रदद्यात् ताः प्रदातॄणां सम्भवन्त्यपि च धुवाः॥
en: He who acquires a cow as his share of ancestral riches is said to acquire her legitimately. Such a cow may be given away. They who make gifts of kine so acquired, obtain innumerable endless regions of eternal happiness.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: प्रतिगृह्य तु यो दद्याद् गाः संशुद्धेन चेतसा। तस्यापीहक्षियाल्लोकान् ध्रुवान् विद्धि शचीपते।।२०
en: That person who having acquired a cow in gift makes a gift of her with a pure heart, succeeds, forsooth, O lord of Sachi, in Obtaining eternal regions of beatitude.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: जन्मप्रभृति सत्यं च यो ब्रूयानियतेन्द्रियः। गुरुद्विजसहः क्षान्तस्तस्य गोभिः समा गतिः॥
en: That person who with controlled senses speaks the truth from his birth and who endures everything at the hands of his preceptor and of the Brahmanas, and who practises forgiveness, gains an end that is equal to that of kine.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: न जातु ब्राह्मणो वाच्यो यदवाच्यं शचीपते। मनसा गोषु न दुह्येद् गोवृत्तिर्गोऽनुकल्पकः॥
en: Improper words, O lord of Shachi, should never be addressed to a Brahmana. One, again, should not, in even his mind, do an injury to a cow. One should in his conduct, imitate the cow, and show mercy towards the cow.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: सत्ये धर्मे च निरतस्तस्य शक्र फलं शृणु। गोसहस्रेण समिता तस्य धेनुर्भवत्युत॥
en: Hear, O Shakra, of the fruits which truthful persons enjoy. If such a person gives away a single cow, that becomes thousandfold.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: क्षत्रियस्य गुणैरेतैरपि तुल्यफलं शृणु। तस्यापि द्विजतुल्या गौर्भवतीति विनिश्चयः॥
en: If Kshatriya endued with such qualifications, makes a gift of a single cow, his merit equals that of a Brahmana's That single cow, listen, O Shakra, which such a Kshatriya gives away produces as much merit as the single cow that a Brahmana gives away does under similar circumstances. This is the issue of the scriptures.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: वैश्यस्यैते यदि गुणास्तस्य पञ्चशतं भवेत्। शूद्रस्यापि विनीतस्य चतुर्भागफलं स्मृतम्॥
en: If a Vaishya, endued with similar accomplishments, were to make a gift of a single cow, that cow would equal five hundred kine. If a Shudra endued with humility were to make a gift of a cow, such cow would be equal to a hundred and twenty five kine. one COW a a

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: एतच्चैनं योऽनुतिष्ठेत युक्तः सत्ये रतो गुरुशुश्रूषया च। दक्षः क्षान्तो देवतार्थी प्रशान्तः शुचिर्बुद्धो धर्मशीलोऽनहंवाद॥ महत् फलं प्राप्यते स द्विजाय दत्त्वा दोग्ध्रीं विधिनानेन धेनुम्। नित्यं दद्यादेकभक्तः सदा च सत्ये स्थितो गुरुशुश्रूषिता च॥
en: Given to penances and truth, always in Scriptures through duliful services done to his preceptor, gifted with forgiving nature, engaged in the adoration of the deities, possessed of a tranquil soul, pure, enlightened, observant of all duties, and freed from every sort of egotism, that man who makes a gift of a cow to a Brahmana, forsooth, acquires great merit through that act of his, viz., the gift, according to proper rites, of a cow giving profuse milk. Hence, one, with singleness of devotion, observant of truth, and engaged in humbly serving his preceptor, should always make gifts of kine.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: वेदाध्यायी गोषु यो भक्तिमांश्च नित्यं दत्त्वा योऽभिनन्देत गाश्च। आजातितो यश्च गवां नमेत इदं फलं शक्र निबोध तस्य॥
en: Hear, O Shakra, what the merit is of that person who, duly studying the Vedas, shows respect for kine, who always becomes glad on seeing kine, and who since his birth always bows his head to kine.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: यत् स्यादिष्ट्वा राजसूये फलं तु यत् स्यादिष्ट्वा बहुना काञ्चनेन। एतत् तुल्यं फलमप्याहुरग्र्यं सर्वे सन्तस्त्वृषयो ये च सिद्धाः॥
en: The merit which one wins by celebrating the Rajasuya sacrifice, the merit that one acquires by making gifts of heaps of gold, that high merit is acquired by a person who shows such respect for kine. Virtuous Rishis and great persons crowned with success have said so.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: योऽग्रं भक्तं किंचिदप्राश्य दद्याद् गोभ्यो नित्यं गोव्रती सत्यवादी। शान्तोऽलुब्धो गोसहस्रस्य पुण्यं संवत्सरेणाप्नुयात् सत्यशीलः॥
en: Given to truth, possessed of a tranquil soul, free from cupidity, always truthful in speech, and behaving with respect towards kine with the steadiness of a vow, the man who, for a whole year, before himself taking any food, regularly presents some food to kine, acquires the merit, by such an act, of the gift of a thousand kine.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: यदेकभक्ततदश्नीयाद् दद्यादेकं गवां च यत्। दशवर्षाण्यनन्तानि गोव्रती गोऽनुकम्पकः॥
en: That man who takes only one meal a day and who gives away the entire quantity of his other meal to kine, that man, who thus respects kine with the steadiness of a vow and shows such mercy towards them, enjoys for ten years unlimited happiness.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: एकेनैव च भक्तेन यः क्रीत्वा गां प्रयच्छति। यावन्ति तस्या रोमाणि सम्भवन्ति शतक्रतो॥
en: That man who takes himself only one meal a day and with the other meal saved for some time purchases a cow and makes a gift of it, acquires, through that gift, O you of a hundred sacrifices, the eternal merit of the gift of as many kine as there are hairs on the body of that single cow so given away.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: तावत् प्रदानात् स गवां फलमाप्नोति शाश्वतम्। ब्राह्मणस्य फलं हीदं क्षत्रियस्य तु वै शृणु॥
en: These are sayings about the merits that Brahmanas acquire by making gifts of kine. Listen now to the merits that Kshatriyas may acquire. It has been said that a Kshatriya, by purchasing a cow in this manner and making a gift of it to a Brahmana, acquires great happiness for five years. A Vaishya, by such conduct, wins only half the merit of a Kshatriyas, and a Shudra, by such conduct, wins half the merit that a Vaishya does.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: पञ्चवार्षिकमेवं तु क्षत्रियस्य फलं स्मृतम्। ततोऽर्धेन तु वैश्यस्य शूद्रो वैश्यार्धतः स्मृतः॥
en: That man who sells himself and with the proceeds thereof purchases kini and gives them away to Brahmanas, enjoys happiness in Heaven for as long a period as kin are seen on Earth.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: यश्चात्वविक्रयं कृत्वा गाः क्रीत्वा सम्प्रयच्छति। यावत् संदर्शयेद् गां वै स तावत् फलमश्नुते॥ रोम्णि रोम्णि महाभाग लोकाश्चास्याऽक्षयाः स्मृताः। संग्रामेष्वर्जयित्वा तु यो वै गाः सम्प्रयच्छति। आत्मविक्रयतुल्यास्ताः शाश्वता विद्धि कौशिक॥३६ अभावे यो गवां दद्यात् तिलधेनुं यतव्रतः। दुर्गात् स तारितो धेन्वा क्षीरनद्यां प्रमोदते॥
en: It has been said, O highly blessed one, that a region of eternal happiness exists in every hair of such kine as are purchased with the proceeds obtained by selling oneself. That man who having acquired kine by battle makes gifts of them, acquires as much merit as he who makes gifts of kine after having bought the same with the proceeds of selling oneself. That man who, in the absence of kine, makes a gift of a cow made of sesame seeds, controlling his senses the while, is saved by such a cow from every sort of calamity or distress. Such a man sports in great happiness.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: न त्वेवासां दानमात्रं प्रशस्तं पात्रं कालो गोविशेषे विधिश्च। कालज्ञानं विप्र गवान्तरं हि दुःखं ज्ञातुं पावकादित्यभूतम्॥
en: The mere gift of kine is not fraught with merit. The considerations of worthy recipients, of time, of the kind of kine, and of the ritual to be observed, should be seen. One should determine the proper time for making a gift of kine. One should also determine the distinctive qualifications of both Brahmanas and of kine themselves. Kine should not be given to one in whose house they are likely to suffer from fire or the sun.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: स्वाध्यायाढ्यं शुद्धयोनि प्रशान्तं वैतानस्थं पापभीरूं बहुज्ञम्। गोषु क्षान्तं नातितीक्ष्णं शरण्यं वृत्तिग्लानं तादृशं पात्रमाहुः॥
en: One who is rich in Vedic learning, who is of pure birth, who is gifted with a tranquil soul, who is given to the celebration of sacrifices, who fears the perpetration of sin, who is gifted with varied knowledge, who is compassionate towards kine, who is mild in conduct, who gives protection to all who seek it of him, and who has no means of livelihood assigned to him, is considered as a proper person for receiving a gift of kine.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: वृत्तिग्लाने सीदति चातिमात्रं कृष्यर्थे वा होम्यहेतोः प्रसूतेः। गुर्वर्थं वा बालसंवृद्धये वा धेनुं दद्याद् देशकालेऽविशिष्टे॥
en: To a Brahmana who has no means of livelihood to him while he is want of food for purposes of agriculture, for a child born on account of Homa, for the purposes of his preceptor, for the sustenance of a child born should a cow be given. Indeed, the gift should be made at a proper time and in a proper place.

description: The end of persons who make gifts of kine
sn: अन्तर्ज्ञाताः सक्रयज्ञानलब्धाः प्राणैः क्रीतास्तेजसा यौतकाश। कृच्छ्रोत्सृष्टाः पोषणाभ्यागताश्च द्वारैरेतैर्गोविशेषः प्रशस्ताः॥
