en: The trees there yield sweet fruits. Indeed, those trees are always bedecked with excellent flowers and fruits. Those flowers, O best of twiceborn persons, have celestial fragrance.

sn: सर्वा मणिमयी भूमिः सर्वकाञ्चनवालुकाः। सर्वर्तुसुखसंस्पर्शा निष्पङ्का नीरजाः शुभा॥
en: The entire soil of that region is formed of gems. The sands there are all gold. The climate there possesses the excellencies of every season. There is no mire, no dust. It is, indeed, highly sacred.

sn: रक्तोत्पलवनैश्चैव मणिखण्डैर्हिरण्मगैः। तरुणादित्यसंकाशैर्भान्ति तत्र जलाशयाः॥
en: The rivers there shine in resplendence for the red lotuses blossoming upon their bosoms, and for the jewels, gems and gold that are on their banks and which display the effulgence of the morning Sun

sn: महार्हमणिपत्रैश्च काञ्चनप्रभकेसरैः। नीलोत्पलविमित्रैश्च सरोभिर्बहुपङ्कजैः॥
en: There are many lakes also on whose breasts are many lotuses, mixed here and there with Nymphoea stellata, and having their petals made of costly gems, and their filaments goldhued.

sn: करवीरवनैः फुल्लैः सहस्रावर्तसंवृतैः। संतानकवनैः फुल्लैर्वृक्षैश्च समलंकृताः॥
en: They are also bedecked with flowering forests of the Nerium odorum with thousands of beautiful creepers twining round them, as also with forests of Santanakas bearing flowers.

sn: निर्मलाभिश्च मुक्ताभिर्मणिभिश्च महाप्रभैः। उद्भूतपुलिनास्तत्र जातरूपैश्च निम्नगाः॥
en: There are rivers whose banks are variegated with many bright pearls and shining gems and gold.

sn: सर्वरत्नमयैश्चित्रैरवगाढा दुमोत्तमैः। जातरूपमयैश्चान्यैर्हताशनसमप्रभैः॥
en: Parts of those regions are covered with excellent trees that are decked with jewels and gems of every sort. Some of them are made of gold and some of them are effulgent like fire.

sn: सौवर्णा गिरयस्तत्र मणिरत्नशिलोच्चयाः। सर्वरत्नमयैर्भान्ति शृङ्गैश्चारुभिरुच्छ्रितैः॥
en: There stand many mountains made of gold, and many hills made of jewels and gems. These shine in beauty on account of their tall summits made of all sorts of gems.

sn: नित्यपुष्पफलास्तत्र नगाः पत्ररथाकुलाः। दिव्यगन्धरसैः पुष्पैः फलैश्च भरतर्षभ॥
en: The trees that bedeck those regions always put forth flowers and fruits, and are always covered with dense foliage. The flowers always yield a celestial fragrance and the fruits are greatly sweet, О chief of Bharata's race.

sn: रमन्ते पुण्यकर्माणस्तत्र नित्यं युधिष्ठिर। सर्वकामसमृद्धार्था निःशोका गतमन्यवः॥
en: The righteous persons, O Yudhishthira, always sport there happily. Freed from grief and anger, they spend their time there, crowned with the fruition of every desire.

sn: विमानेषु विचित्रेषु रमणीयेषु भारत। मोदन्ते पुण्यकर्माणो विहरन्तो यशस्विनः॥
en: Pious and illustrious persons sport there happily, moving from place to place, O Bharata, on delightful and highly beautiful cars.

sn: बलवान् बली। उपक्रीडन्ति तान् राजन्शुभाश्चाप्सरसां गणाः। एताल्लोकानवाप्नोति गां दत्त्वा वै युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bevies of celestial nymphs always amuse there, with music and dance. Indeed, Yudhishthira, a person goes to such regions as the fruit of his making gifts of kine.

sn: येषामधिपतिः पूषा मारुतो ऐश्वर्ये वरुणो राजा नाममात्रं युगन्धरः॥ सुरूपा बहुरूपाश्च विश्वरूपाश्च मातरः। प्रजापत्यमिति ब्रह्मन् जपेन्नित्यं यतव्रतः॥
en: Those regions which are owned by Pushan, and the Maruts of great power, are acquired by givers of kine. In riches the royal Varuna is considered as preeminent. The giver of kine acquires riches like that of Varuna himself. One should, with the steadiness of a vow, daily recite these Mantras sung by Prajapati himself, vizYugandharah, Surupali, Bahurupah, Vishvarupah, and Matara.

sn: गाश्च शुक्षूषते यश्च समन्वेति च सर्वशः। तस्मै तुष्टाः प्रयच्छन्ति वरानपि सुदुर्लभान्॥
en: He who serves kine with respect and who follows them with humility, succeeds in getting many invaluable boons from kine who become pleased with him.

sn: दुह्येन मनसा वापि गोषु नित्यं सुखप्रदः। अर्चयेत सदा चैव नमस्कारैश्च पूजयेत्॥
en: One should never, even in his heart, injure, kine. One should indeed, always confer happiness on them. One should always respect kine and adore them, by bending low his head.

sn: दान्तः प्रीतमना नित्यं गवां व्युष्टिं तथाश्नुते। त्र्यहमुष्णं पिबेन्मूत्रं त्र्यहमुष्णं पिबेत् पयः॥
en: He who does this, controlling his senses all the while and filled with cheerfulness, succeeds in acquiring that happiness which is enjoyed by kine. One should for three day drink the hot urine of the cow. For the next three days one should drink the hot milk of the cow.

sn: गवामुष्णं पयः पीत्वा त्र्यहमुष्णं घृतं पिबेत्। त्र्यहमुष्णं घृतं पीत्वा वायुभक्षो भवेत् व्यहम्॥
en: Having thus drunk for three days hot milk, one should next drink hot clarified butter for three days. Having thus drunk hot clarified butter for three days, one should live for the next three days on air only.

sn: येन देवाः पवित्रेण भुञ्जते लोकमुत्तमम्। यत् पवित्रं पवित्राणां तद् घृतं शिरसा वहेत्॥
en: Thatsacred thing by whose help the celestials enjoy regions of happiness, that which is most sacred of all sacred things, viz., clarified butter, should then be carried on the head.

sn: घृतेन जुहुयादग्निं घृतेन स्वस्ति वाचयेत्। घृतं प्राशेद् घृतं दद्याद् गवां पुष्टिं तथाश्नुते॥
en: With the help of clarified butter, one should pour libations on the sacred fire. By making gifts of clarified butter, one should make the Brahmanas utter benedictions on oneself. One should eat clarified butter and make gifts of clarified butter. As the reward of this conduct, one may then acquire that prosperity, which belongs to kine.

sn: निर्हतैश्च यवैर्गोभिर्मासं प्रश्रितयावकः। ब्रह्महत्यासमं पापं सर्वमेतेन शुध्यते॥
en: That man who, for a month, lives upon the gruel of barley picked up every day from cowdung, becomes purged of sins as heinous as Brahmanicide.

sn: पराभवाच्च दैत्यानां देवैः शौचमिदं कृतम्। ते देवत्वमपि प्राप्ताः संसिद्धाश्च महाबलाः॥
en: After their defeat at the hands of the demons, the deities practised this expiation, It was on account of this expiation that they succeeded in regaining their position as celestials. Indeed, it was through this that they regained their strength and became successful.

sn: गाव: पवित्राः पुण्याश्च पावनं परमं महत्। ताश्च दत्त्वा द्विजातिभ्यो नरः स्वर्गमुपाश्नुते॥
en: Kine are sacred. They are embodiments of virtue. They are high and most efficacious purifiers of all. By making gifts of kine to the Brahmanas one acquires the celestial region.

sn: गवां मध्ये शुचिर्भूत्वा गोमती मनसा जपेत्। पूताभिरद्भिराचम्य शुचिर्भवति निर्मलः॥
en: Living in a pure state, in the midst of kine, one should mentally recite those sacred Mantras named Gomati, after touching pure water. By doing this, one becomes purified.

sn: अग्निमध्ये गवां मध्ये ब्राह्मणानां च संसदि। विद्यादेवव्रतस्नाता ब्राह्मणाः पुण्यकर्मिणः॥ अध्यापयेरन्शिष्यान् वै गोमतों यज्ञसम्मिताम्। त्रिरात्रापोषितो भूत्वा गोमती लभते वरम्॥
en: Brahmanas of righteous deeds, who have been purified by knowledge, study of the Vedas, and observance of vows, should, only in the midst of sacred fires or kine or conclaves of Brahmanas, impart to their disciples a knowledge of the Gomati Mantras which are in every way like a sacrifice. One should observed a fast for three nights for receiving the boon formed by a knowledge of the meaning of the Gomati Mantras.

sn: पुत्रकामश्च लभते पुत्रं धनमथापि वा। पतिकामा च भर्तारं सर्वकामांश्च मानवः॥
en: The man who wishes to get a son may cbtain it by worshipping these Mantras, He who wishes to acquire riches may have his desire fulfilled by worshipping these Mantras. The girl desirous of having a good husband may have her wish fulfilled by the same means. In fact, one may acquire the fruition of every desire he may cherish, by worshipping these sacred Mantras.

sn: गावस्तुष्टाः प्रयच्छन्ति सेविता वै न संशयः। एवमेता महाभागा यज्ञियाः सर्वकामदाः। रोहिण्य इति जानीहि नैताभ्यो विद्यते परम्॥
en: When kine are pleased with the service one renders them, they are, forsooth, capable of granting the fruition of every desire. Even so, kine are highly blessed. They are the essential articles of sacrifices. They are grantors of every wish. Know that there is nothing superior to kine.

sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तः स महातेजाः शुकः पित्रा महात्मना। पूजयामास गां नित्यं तस्मात् त्वमपि पूजय॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by his great father, Shuka, gifted with great energy, began from that time to adore kine every day. Do you also, O son, act thus.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मया गवां पुरीषं वै श्रिया जुष्टमिति श्रुतम्। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं संशयोऽत्र पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have heard that the dung of the cow is gifted with prosperity. I wish to hear how this has been occasioned. I have doubts, O grand father which you should remove.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। गोभिर्नृपेह संवादं श्रिया भरतसत्तम॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old story, O king of the conversation between kine and godless of prosperity, O best of the Bharatas.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: श्रीः कृत्वेह वपुः कान्तं गोमध्येषु विवेश ह। गावोऽथ विस्मितास्तस्या दृष्ट्वा रूपस्य सम्पदम्॥
en: Once on a time, assuming a very beautiful form, the goddess Shree entered a herd of kine. Sceing her beauty the kine became filled with wonder.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: गौ उवाच कासि देवि कुतो वा त्वं रूपेणाप्रतिभा भुवि। विस्मिताः स्म महाभागे तव रूपस्य सम्पदा॥
en: The kine said Who are you, O goddess? Whence have you become nonpareil on Earth for beauty? O highly blessed goddess, we have been filled with wonder at your beauty.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: इच्छाम त्वां वयं ज्ञातुं कात्वं क्व च गामिष्यसि। तत्त्वेन वरवर्णाभे सर्वमेतद् ब्रवीहि नः॥
en: We wish to know who you are. Who indeed, are you? Where will you proceed? O vou of very great beauty, do tell us in detail all We wish to know!

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: श्री उवाच लोककान्तास्मि भद्रं वः श्री माहं परिश्रुता। मया दैत्याः परित्यक्ता विनष्टाः शाश्वतीः समाः॥६
en: Shree said Blessed be you, I am dear to all creatures. Indeed. I am known by the name of Shree. Forsaken by me, the demons have been lost for ever.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: मयाभिपन्ना देवाश्च मोदन्ते शाश्वतीः समाः। इन्द्रो विवस्वान् सोमश्च विष्णुरापोऽग्निरेव च॥
en: The celestials, viz., Indra, Vivasvat, Soma, Vishnu, Varuna, and Agni, having obtained me, are sporting happily and will do so for ever.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: मयाभिपन्नाः सिध्यन्ते ऋषयो देवतास्तथा। यान् नाविशाम्यहं गावस्ते विनश्यन्ति सर्वशः॥
en: Indeed, the Rishis and the celestials, only when they are endued with me, become successful. You kine, those beings meet with destruction into whom I do not enter.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च मया जुष्टाः सुखान्विताः। एवं प्रभावं मां गावो विजानीत सुखप्रदाः॥
en: Virtue, Prosperity, and Pleasure, only when endued with me, become sources of happiness. You kine, who are givers of sources of happiness, know that I am gifted with such energy.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: इच्छामि चापि युष्मासु वस्तुं सर्वासु नित्यदा। आगत्य प्रार्थ ये युष्माञ्छ्रीजुष्टा भवताऽथ वै॥
en: I wish to always live in every one of you. Going to your presence, I solicit you. Be all of you gifted with Shree.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: गाव ऊचुः अध्रुवा चपला च त्वं सामान्या बहुभिः सह। न त्वामिच्छाम भद्रं ते गम्यतां यत्र रंस्यसे॥
en: The kine said You are fickle and restless. You allow yourself to be enjoyed by many persons. We do not wish to have you! Blessed be you, go wherever you like.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: वपुष्मन्त्यो वयं सर्वाः किमस्माकं त्वयाद्य वै। यथेष्टं गम्यतां तत्र कृतकार्या वयं त्वया।॥
en: As regards ourselves, all of us have good forms. What need have we with you? Go wherever you like. You have already pleased us greatly.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: श्रीरुवाच किमेतद् वः क्षमं गावो यन्मां नेहाभिनन्दथ। न मां सम्प्रति गृह्णीध्वं कस्ताद् बै दुर्लभां सतीम्।।१३
en: Shree said Is it proper with you, you kine, that you do not welcome me? I am difficult of being attained. Why then do you not accept me?

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: सत्यं च लोकवादोऽयं लोके चरति सुव्रताः। स्वयं प्राप्ते परिभवो भवतीति विनिश्चयः॥
en: It appears, you creatures of excellent vows, that the popular proverb is true, viz., that it is certain that when one comes to another of this own accord and without being sought, he is not much respected.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: महदुग्रं तपः कृत्वा मां निषेवन्ति मानवाः। देवदानवगन्धर्वाः पिशाचोरगराक्षसाः॥
en: The gods, the Danavas, the Gandharvas, the Pishachas, the Uragas, the Rakshasas, and human being succeed in getting me only after practising the severest austerities.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: प्रभाव एष वो गावः प्रतिगृह्णीत मामिह। नावमन्या ह्यहं सौम्यास्त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे॥
en: You who have such energy, do you take me! You amiable ones, I am never dishonoured by any one in the three worlds of mobile and immobile creatures.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: गाव ऊचुः नावमन्यामहे देवि न त्वां परिभवामहे। अध्रुवा चलचित्तासि ततस्त्वां वर्जयामहे॥
en: The kine said We do not disregard you, O goddess! We do not slight you! You are fickle and of a very restless heart. It is for this only that we take leave of you.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: बहुना च किमुक्तेन गम्यतां यत्र वाञ्छसि। वपुष्मन्त्यो वयं सर्वाः किमस्माकं त्वयानघे॥
en: What need of much talk? Go wherever you like. All of us have excellent forms. What need have we with you, O sinless one?

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: श्रीरुवाच अवज्ञाता भविष्यामि सर्वलोकस्य मानदाः। प्रत्याख्यानेन युष्माकं प्रसादः क्रियतां मम॥
en: Shree said You givers of honours, renounced by you thus, I shall certainly be an object of disregard with all the world? Do you show me grace.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: महाभागा भवत्यो वै शरण्याः शरणागताम्। परित्रायन्तु मां नित्यं भजमानामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: You are all highly blessed, You are ever ready to grant protection to those who seek your protection. I have come to you soliciting your refuge. I have no fault. Do you rescue me.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: माननामहमिच्छामि भवत्यः सततं शिवाः। अप्येकाङ्गेश्वधे वस्तुमिच्छामि च सुकुत्सिते॥
en: Know that I shall always be devoted to you! I wish to live in any part of your bodies, however repulsive it may be. Indeed, I wish to live even in you rectum.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: न वोऽस्ति कुत्सितं किंचिदङ्गवालक्ष्यतेऽनघाः। पुण्या: पवित्राः सुभगा ममादेशं प्रयच्छथ॥
en: You sinless ones, I do not see that you have any part in your bodies that may be considered as repulsive, for you are sacred, and purifying, and highly blessed! Do you, however, grant my prayer. Do you tell me in which part of your bodies shall I live.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: भीष्म उवाच वसेयं यत्र वो देहे तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हथ। एवमुक्तास्ततो गावः शुभाः करुणवत्सलाः। सम्मत्र्य सहिताः सर्वाः श्रियमूचुनराधिप॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by Shree, the kine, always auspicious and bent on showing kindness to all who are devoted to them, parleyed with one another, and then addressing Shree, said to her, O king, these words.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: गौ उवाच अवश्यं मानना कार्या तवास्माभिर्यशास्विनि। शकृन्मूत्रे निवस त्वं पुण्यमेतद्धि नः शुभे॥
en: The kine said you of great fame, it is certainly desirable that we should honour you! Do you live in our urine and dung. Both these are sacred, O goddess.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: श्रीरुवाच दिष्ट्या प्रसादो युष्माभिः कृतो मेऽनुग्रहात्मकः। एवं भवतु भद्रं वः पूजितास्मि सुखप्रदाः॥
en: Shree said By good luck, you have shown me much favour. Let it be even as you say! Blessed by you all, I have really been honoured by you, you givers of happiness.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवं कृत्वा तु समयं श्रीर्गोभिः सह भारत। पश्यन्तीनां ततस्तासां तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Bhishma said Having, O Bharata, made this contract with kine, Shree there and then, before those kine, disappeared.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: एवं गोशकृतः पुत्र माहात्म्यं तेऽनुवर्णितम्। माहात्म्यं च गवां भूयः श्रूयतां गदतो मम॥
en: I have thus told you, O son, the glory of the dung of kine. I shall once again describe to you the glory of kine. Do you listen to me. Bhishma said Having, O Bharata, made this contract with kine, Shree there and then, before those kine, disappeared.

description: The merits of cowdung. The conversation between kine and the goddess of prosperity
sn: एवं गोशकृतः पुत्र माहात्म्यं तेऽनुवर्णितम्। माहात्म्यं च गवां भूयः श्रूयतां गदतो मम॥
en: I have thus told you, O son, the glory of the dung of kine. I shall once again describe to you the glory of kine. Do you listen to me.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ये च गां सम्प्रयच्छन्ति हतशिष्टाशिनश्च ये। तेषां सत्राणि यज्ञाश्च नित्यमेव युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said on They who make gifts of kine, and who live upon the remnants of things offered as libations the sacred fire, are considered, O Yudhishthira as always performing sacrifices of kind.

sn: ऋते दधि घृतेनेह न यज्ञः सम्प्रवर्तते। तेन यज्ञस्य यज्ञत्वमतो मूलं च कथ्यते॥
en: No sacrifice can be performed without the help of curds and clarified butter. The very character as sacrifice which sacrifices have, depends upon clarified butter. Hence clarified butter is considered as the very root of sacrifice.

sn: दानानामपि सर्वेषां गवां दानं प्रशस्यते। गावः श्रेष्ठाः पवित्राश्च पावनं ह्येतदुत्तमम्॥
en: Of all kinds of gifts, the gift of kine is spoken highest of. Kine are the foremost of all things. Themselves sacred, they are the best of purifier.

sn: पुष्ट्यर्थमेताः सेवेत शान्त्यथर्मपि चैव ह। पयोदधिघृतं चासां सर्वपापप्रमोचनम्॥
en: People should cherish kine for getting prosperity and even peace. The milk, curds, and clarified butter that kine yield are capable of purifying one from every kind of sin.

sn: गावस्तेजः पर प्रोक्तमिह लोके परत्र च। न गोभ्यः परमं किंचित् पवित्रं भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Kine are said to represent the highest energy both in this world and the next. There is nothing that is more sacred or purifying than kine, O chief of the Bharatas.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। पितामहस्य संवादमिन्द्रस्य च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Regarding it is recited the ancient discourse between the Grandfather and chief of the celestials.

sn: पराभूतेषु दैत्येषु शक्रस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरः। प्रजाः समुदिताः सर्वाः सत्यधर्मपरायणाः॥
en: After the demons had been defeated and Shakra had become the lord of the three worlds, all creatures grew prosperous and became devoted to the true religion.

sn: अथर्षयः सगन्धर्वाः किन्नरोरगराक्षसाः। देवासुरसुपर्णाश्च प्रजानां पतयस्तथा॥ पुर्यपासन्त कौन्तेय कदाचिद् वै पितामहम्। नारदः पर्वतश्चैव विश्वावसुर्हहाहुहूः॥ दिव्यतानेषु गायन्तः पर्युपासन्त तं प्रभुम्। तत्र दिव्यानि पुष्पाणि प्रावहत् पवनस्तदा॥
en: Then, on one occasion, the Rishis, the Gandharvas, the Kinnaras, the Uragas, the Rakshasas, the Deities, the Asuras, the winged crcatures, and the Prajapatis, O you of Kuru's race, ali assembled together and worshipped the Grandfather. There were Narada and Parvata and Vishvavasu and HahaHuhu, who sang celestial songs for worshipping that powerful lord of all creatures. The god of wind bore there the fragrance of celestial flowers.

sn: आजहुर्ऋतवश्चापि सुगन्धीनि पृथक् पृथक्। तस्मिन् देवसमावाये सर्वभूतसमागमे॥ दिव्यवादित्रसंघुष्टे दिव्यस्त्रीचारणावृते। इन्द्रः पप्रच्छ देवेशमभिवाद्य प्रणम्य च॥ देवानां भगवन् कस्माल्लोकेशानां पितामह। उपरिष्टाद् गवां लोक एतदिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: The Seasons also, in their embodied forms, bore the fragrance of flowers peculiar to each, to that assemblage of celestials, that gathering of all creatures of the universe, where celestial maidens danced and sang in accompaniment with celestial music. In the midst of that assembly, Indra, saluting the Lord of all the celestial and bowing his head to him with respect, asked him, saying, I wish, O Grandfather, to know why the region of kine is higher, O holy one, than the region of the celestials themselves who are the lords of all the worlds.

sn: किं तपो ब्रह्मचर्यं वा गोभिः कृतमिहेश्वर। देवानामुपरिष्टाद् यद् वसन्त्यरजसः मुखम्॥
en: What austerities, what Brahmacharya, O lord, did kine perform on account of which they are able to live happily in a region that is even above that of the celestials.

sn: ततः प्रोवाच ब्रह्मा तं शक्रं बलनिषूदनम्। अवज्ञातास्त्वया नित्यं गावो बलनिषूदन॥
en: Thus addressed by Indra, Brahman said to the destroyer of Bala, You have always, O destroyer of Bala, disregarded kine.

sn: तेन त्वमासां माहात्म्यं न वेत्सि शृणु यत् प्रभो। गवां प्रभावं परमं माहात्म्यं च सुरर्षभ॥
en: Hence, you are not acquainted with glorious pereminence of kine. Listen now to me, o powerful one, as I explain to you the great energy and glorious pereminence of kine, O king of the celestials.

sn: यज्ञाझं कथिता गावो यज्ञ एव च वासव। एताभिश्च विना यज्ञो न वर्तेत कथंचन॥
en: Kine have been said to be the limbs of sacrifice. They represent sacrifice itself, O Vasava! Without them there can be no sacrifice.

sn: धारयन्ति प्रजाश्चैव पयसा हविषा तथा। एतासां तनयाश्चापि कृषियोगमुपासते॥ जनयन्ति च धान्यानि बीजानि विविधानि च।
en: With their milk and the Havi produced therefrom, they sustain all creatures. Their male children are engaged in helping the cultivation and thereby produce various kinds of paddy and other seeds.

sn: ततो यज्ञाः प्रवर्तन्ते हव्यं कव्यं च सर्वशः॥ पयोदधिधृतं चैव पुण्याश्चैताः सुराधिप। वहन्ति विविधान् भारान् क्षुत्तृष्णापरिपीडिताः॥
en: From them originate sacrifices and Havya and Kavya, and milk and curds and clarified butter. Hence, O chief of the celestials, kine are sacred. Stricken with hunger and thirst, they carry various burthens.

sn: मुनींश्च धारयन्तीह प्रजाश्चैवापि कर्मणा। वासवाकूटवाहिन्यः कर्मणा सुकूतेन च॥
en: Kine support ascetics. They sustain all creatures by various acts. O Vasava, kine are guileless in their conduct on account of such conduct and of many wellperformed acts, they are able to live always in regions that are even above ours.

sn: उपरिष्टात् ततोऽस्माकं वसन्त्येताः सदैव हि। एवं ते कारणं शक्र निवासकृतमद्य वै॥
en: I have thus explained to you today, O you of a hundred sacrifices, the reason, O Shakra, of kine living in a place that is high above that of the celestials.

sn: गवां देवोपरिष्टाद्धि समाख्यातं शतक्रतो। एता हि वरदत्ताश्च वरदाश्चापि वासव॥
en: Kine got many excellent forms, O Vasava, and are themselves givers of boons. They are called Surabhis. Of sacred deeds and gifted with many auspicious marks they are highly purifying.

sn: सुरभ्यः पुण्यकर्मिण्यः पावनाः शुभलक्षणाः। यदर्थं गां गताश्चैव सुरभ्यः सुरसत्तम॥
en: Listen to me also, O destroyer of Bala, as I tell you in full the reason why kine, the children of Surabhi, have descended on the Earth, O best of the celestials.

sn: तच्च मे शृणु कार्येन वदतो बलसूदन। पुरा देवयुगे तात देवेन्द्रेषु महात्मसु॥ त्रिलोकाननुशासत्सु विष्णौ गर्भत्वमागते। अदित्यास्तप्यमानायास्तपो घोरं सुदुश्चरम्॥
en: Formerly , O son, when in the golden age the great Danavas became lords of the three worlds, Aditi performed the severest austerities and got Vishnu within her womb. Indeed, O chief of the celestials, she had stood upon one leg for many long years, desirous of having a son.

sn: पुत्रार्थममरश्रेष्ठ पादेनैकेन नित्यदा। तां तु दृष्ट्वा महादेवीं तप्यमानां महत्तपः॥ दक्षस्य दुहिता देवी सुरभी नाम नामतः। अतप्यत तपो घोरं हृष्टा धर्मपरायणा॥ कैलासशिखरे रम्ये देवगन्धर्वसेविते। व्यतिष्ठदेकपादेन परमं योगमास्थिता॥ दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च। संतप्तास्तपसा तस्या देवाः सर्षिमहोरगाः॥
en: Seeing the great goddess Aditi thus practising the severest austerities, the daughter of Daksha, viz., the illustrious Surabhi, herself given to virtue likewise practised very severe austerities upon the breast of the charming mountains of Kailasa that are resorted to by both the celestials and the Gandharvas. Established on the highest Yoga, she also stood upon the leg for eleven thousand years. The celestials with the Rishis and the great Nagas all became scorched with the severity of her penances. Going there with me, all of them began of worship that auspicious goddess.

sn: तत्र गत्वा मया सार्धं पर्युपासन्त तां शुभाम्। अथाहमब्रुवं तत्र देवीं तां तपसान्विताम्॥
en: I then addressed that goddess gifted with penances, and said, O goddess, O you of faultless conduct, for what purpose do you practise such severe austerities,

sn: किमर्थं तप्यसे देवि तपो घोरमनिन्दिते। प्रीतस्तेऽहं महाभागे तपसानेन शोभने॥
en: O highlyblessed one, I am pleased with your penances, O beautiful one! Do you, O goddess, beg what boon you wish to have. I shall grant you whatever, you may ask! These were my words to her, O Purandara.

sn: वरयस्व वरं देवि दातास्मीति पुरंदर।॥ वरेण भगवन् मह्यं कृतं लोकपितामह। एष एव वरो मेऽद्य यत् प्रीतोऽसि ममानघ।॥ तामेवं ब्रुवती देवीं सुरभिं त्रिदशेश्वर। प्रत्यब्रुवं यद् देवेन्द्र तन्निबोध शचीपते॥
en: Thus addressed by me, Surabhi answered me, saying, I have no need O grandfather of boons. O sinless one, that you have been pleased with me is a great boon to me. To the illustrious Surabhi, O chief of the celestials, who said so to me, O lord of Sachi, I answered thus, O goddess, I have been highly pleased with this your freedom from cupidity and desire, and with these penances of yours, O you of beautiful face. I therefore, grant you the boon of immortality.

sn: अलोभकाम्यया देवि तपसा च शुभानने। प्रसन्नोऽहं वरं तस्मादमरत्वं ददामि ते॥
en: You will live in a region that is higher than the three worlds, through my favour. That region shall be known to all by the name of Goloka.

sn: त्रयाणामपि लोकानामुपरिष्टान्निवत्स्यसि। मत्प्रसादाच्च विख्यातो गोलोकः सम्भविष्यति॥
en: Your offspring, ever engaged in doing good deeds, will live in the world of men, In fact, O highly blessed one, your daughters will live there.

sn: मानुषेषु च कुर्वाणाः प्रजा: कर्म शुभास्तव। निवत्स्यन्ति महाभागे सर्वा दुहितश्च ते॥ मनसा चिन्तिता भोगास्वत्वया वै दिव्यमानुषाः। यच्च सर्वं सुखं देवि तत् ते सम्पत्स्यते शुभे॥
en: You will readily get all kinds of enjoyment, celestial and human, that you may think of. You will get whatever happiness exists in the celestial region, O blessed one! The regions, O you of a hundred eyes, that are Surabhi's are replete with means for the satisfaction of every desire, Neither Death, nor Decrepitude, nor fire, can overcome its inhabitants.

sn: तस्या लोकाः सहस्राक्ष सर्वकामसमन्विताः। न तत्र क्रमते मृत्युर्न जरा न च पावकः॥
en: No illluck, O Vasava exists there, many charining forests and delightful ornaments and objects of beauty may be seen there.

sn: न दैवं नाशुभं किंचिद् विद्यते तत्र वासव। तत्र दिव्यान्यरण्यानि दिव्यानि भवनानि च॥ विमानानि सुयुक्तानि कामगानि च वासव। ब्रह्मचर्येण तपसा यत्नेन च दमेन च॥
en: There may be seen many beautiful cars, all excellently equipt and which move at the will of the rider, O Vasava. O you having eyes like lotus petals, it is only by celibacy, by penances, by Truth, by self-control, by gifts, by various kinds of righteous deeds, by sojourns lo sacred waters, in fact, by severe austerities and righteous deeds well-performed, that one can attain to Goloka.

sn: दानैश्च विविधैः पुण्यैस्तथा तीर्थानुसेवनात्। तपसा महता चैव सुकृतेन च कर्मणा॥
en: You had asked me, O Shakra and I have answered you in full. O destroyer of Asuras, you should never disregard kine!

sn: भीष्म उवाच शक्यः समासादयितुं गोलोकः पुष्करेक्षण। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं मया शक्रानुपृच्छते॥
en: Bhishma said learing these words of the self-creale Brahman, O Yudhishthira, Shakra of a thousand eyes began from that time to adore kine every day and to show them the greatest respect.

sn: न ते परिभवः कार्यो गवामसुरसूदन॥ एतच्छ्रुत्वा सहस्राक्षः पूजयामास नित्यदा। गाश्चक्रे बहुमानं च तासु नित्यं युधिष्ठिर॥ एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं पावनं च महाद्युते। पवित्रं परमं चापि गवां माहात्म्युमुत्तमम्॥ कीर्तितं पुरुषव्याघ्र सर्वपापविमोचनम्। य इदं कथयेन्नित्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः समाहितः॥ हव्यकव्येष यज्ञेषु पितृकार्येषु चैव ह। सार्वकामिकमक्षय्यं पितृस्तस्योपतिष्ठते॥
en: I have thus told you everything about the purifying character of kine, O you of great splendour. I have expounded to you the sacred and high pre-eminence and glory of kine, that is capable of purifying one from every sin, O chief of men. That man who with senses withdrawn from every other object will recite this account to Brahmanas, on occasions when Havya and Kavya are offered, or at sacrifices, or on occasions of worshipping the departed in succeeds conferring upon his ancestors an endless happiness fraught with the fruition of every desire.

sn: गोषु भक्तश्च लभते यद् यदिच्छति मानवः। स्त्रियोऽपि भक्ता या गोषु ताश्च काममवाप्नुयुः॥
en: The man who is devoted to kine succeeds in getting the fruition of every desire of his. Indeed, even those women who are devoted 10 kine succeed in securing the fulfilment of every desire of theirs.

sn: पुत्रार्थी लभते पुत्रं कन्यार्थी तामवाप्नुयात्। धनार्थी लभते वित्तं धर्मार्थी धर्ममाप्नुयात्॥
en: He who wishes for sons obtains them. He who desires daughters obtains them. He who desires riches succeeds in acquiring wealth, and he who desires religions merit succeeds in winning it.

sn: विद्यार्थी चाप्नुयाद् विद्यां सुखार्थी प्राप्नुयात् सुखम्। न किंचिद् दुर्लभं चैव गवां भक्तस्य भारत॥
en: He who desires knowledge acquires it, and he who desires happiness succeeds in acquiring happiness. Indeed, O Bharata, there is nothing which one devoted to kine cannot obtain. l at

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उक्तं पितामहेनदं गवां दानमनुत्तमम्। विशेषेण नरेन्द्राणामिह धर्ममवेक्षताम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have, O grandfather, expounded to me the highly meritorious gift of kine. In the case of kings performing their duties, that gift is most meritorious.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: राज्यं हि सततं दुःखं दुर्धरं चाकृतात्मभिः। भूयिष्ठं च नरेन्द्राणां विद्यते न शुभा गतिः॥
en: Sovereignty is always painful. It is incapable of being borne by persons of impure souls. Generally kings fail to acquire auspicious ends.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: पूयन्ते तत्र नियतं प्रयच्छन्तो वसुन्धराम्। सर्वे च कथिता धर्मास्त्वया मे कुरुनन्दन॥
en: By always making, however, gifts of earth, they succeed in purifying themselves. You have, O prince of Kuru's race, describe to me many duties.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: एवमेव गवामुक्तं प्रदानं ते नृगेण ह। ऋषिणा नाचिकेतेन पूर्वमेव निदर्शितम्॥
en: You have described to me the gifts of kine formerly made by king Nriga. The Rishi Nachiketa, in ancient times, had described the merits of this act.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: वेदोपनिषदश्चैव सर्वकर्मसु दक्षिणाः। सर्वक्रतुषु चोद्दिष्टं भूमिर्गावोऽथ काञ्चनम्॥
en: The Vedas and the Upanishads also have laid down that in all sacrifices, in fact, in all sorts of religious rites, the sacrificial present should be earth or kine or gold.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तत्र श्रुतिस्तु परमा सुवर्णं दक्षिणेति वै। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं पितामह यथातथम्॥
en: The Shrutis, however, declare that of all presents, gold is very superior and is, indeed, the best. I wish, O grandfather, to hear you describe truly this subject.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: किं सुवर्णं कथं जातं कस्मिन् काले किमात्मकम्। किं दैवं किं फलं चैव कस्माच्च परमुच्यते॥
en: What is gold? How did it spring up? When did it come into existence? What is its essence? Who is its presiding god? What are its fruits. Why is it considered as the foremost of all things?

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: कस्माद् दानं सुवर्णस्य पूजयन्ति मनीषिणः। कस्माच्च दक्षिणार्थं तद् यज्ञकर्मसु शस्यते॥
en: Why do wise men applaud the gift of gold? Why is gold considered as the best of presents in all sacrifices?

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: कस्माच्च पावनं श्रेष्ठं भूमेर्गोभ्यश्च काञ्चनम्। परमं दक्षिणार्थे च तद् ब्रवीहि पितामह॥
en: Why also is gold considered as a purifier superior to earth itself and kine? Why, indeed, is it considered so superior as a sacrificial present? Do you, O grandfather, describe to me all this.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु राजन्नवहितो बहुकारणविस्तरम्। जातरूपसमुत्पत्तिमनुभूतं च यन्मया।॥
en: Bhishma said Listen, O king, with rapt attention to me as I recite to you in detail the circumstances connected with the origin of gold as understood by me.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: पिता मम महातेजाः शान्तनुर्निधनं गतः। तस्य दित्सुरहं श्राद्धं गङ्गाद्वारमुपागमम्॥
en: When my highly energetic father Shantanu died, I proceeded to Gangadvara for performing his Shraddha.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तत्रागम्य पितुः पुत्र श्राद्धकर्म समारभम्। माता मे जाह्नवी चात्र साहाय्यमकरोत् तदा॥
en: Arrived there I began the Shraddha of my father. My mother Janhavi coming there, gave me great assistance.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: ततोऽग्रतस्ततः सिद्धानुपवेश्य बहूनृषीन्। तोयप्रदानात् प्रभृति कार्याण्यहमथारभम्॥
en: Inviting many ascetics crowned with success and making them take their seats before me, I began the preliminary rites consisting of gifts of water and of other things.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तत् समाप्य यथोद्दिष्टं पूर्वकर्म समाहितः। दातुं निर्वपणं सम्यग् यथावदहमारभम्॥
en: Having with concentrated mind performed all preliminary rites as laid down in the scriptures, I began to duly offer the obsequial cake.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: ततस्तं दर्भविन्यासं भित्त्वा सुरुचिरागदः। प्रलम्बाभरणो बाहुरुदतिष्ठद् विशाम्पते॥
en: I then saw, O king, that a beautiful arm, adorned with armlets and other ornaments, rose a up, piercing the ground, through the blades of Kusha grass which I had spread.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तमुत्थितमहं दृष्ट्वा परं विस्मयमागमम्। प्रतिग्रहीता साक्षान्मे पितेति भरतर्षभ॥
en: Seeing that arm rise from the ground, I became stricken with wonder. Indeed, O chief of Bharata's race, I thought that my father had come himself for accepting the cake I was about to offer.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: ततो मे पुनरेवासीत् संज्ञा संचिन्त्य शास्त्रतः। नायं वेदेषु विहितो विधिहस्त इति प्रभो॥ पिण्डो देयो नरेणेह ततो मतिरभून्मम। साक्षान्नेह मनुष्यस्य पिण्डं हि पितरः क्वचित्॥ गृह्णन्ति विहितं चेत्थं पिण्डो देयः कुशेष्विति। ततोऽहं तदनादृत्य पितुर्हस्तनिदर्शनम्॥ शास्त्रप्रमाण्यसूक्ष्मं तु विधिं पिण्डस्य संस्मरन्। ततो दर्भेषु तत् सर्वमददं भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Reflecting then, by the light of the scriptures. I became convinced that the ordinance is in the Vedas that the cake should not be presented to the hand of him whose Shraddha is performed. My conviction was that the obsequial cake should never be presented in this world by a man to the visible hand of the nan whose obsequial rites are performed. The departed Manes do not come in their visible forms for taking the cake. On the other hand, the ordinance lays down that it should be presented on the blades of Kusha grass spread the earth for the purpose. I then, disregarding that hand which was the mark of may father's presence, and recollecting the true ordinance of the scriptures regarding to mode of presenting the cake, offered the entire cake, O chief of the Bharatas, upon those blades of Kusha grass that were spread before me.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: शास्त्रमार्गानुसारेण तद् विद्धि मनुजर्षभ। तत: सोऽन्तर्हितो बाहुः पितुर्मम जनाधिप॥
en: Know, O king, that what I did was perfectly consistent with the scriptural ordinance. After this, the arm of my father, O monarch, vanished, in our very sight. on more

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: ततो मां दर्शयामासुः स्वप्नान्ते पितरस्तथा। प्रीयमाणास्तु मामूचुः प्रीताः स्म भरतर्षभ।॥ विज्ञानेन तवानेन यन्न मुह्यसि धर्मतः। त्वया हि कुर्वता शास्त्रं प्रमाणमिह पार्थिव॥
en: On that night as I slept, the departed Manes appeared to me in a dream. Pleased with me they said, O chief of Bharata's race, these words, We have been pleased with you, for the mark you have shown today of your adherence to the ordinance. It has pleased us to see that you have not deviated from the injunctions of the scriptures. The scriptural ordinance, followed by you, has become authoritative, O king.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: आत्मा धर्मः श्रुतं वेदाः पितरश्चर्षिभिः सह। साक्षात् पितामहो ब्रह्मा गुरवोऽथ प्रजापतिः॥ प्रमाणमुपनीता वै स्थिताश्च न विचालिताः। तदिदं सम्यगारब्धं त्वयात्र भरतर्षभ॥
en: By such conduct you have honoured and maintained the authority of yourself, the scriptures, the Vedas, the Pitris and the Rishis, the Grandfather Brahman himself, and those elders, viz., the Prajapatis. Adherence to the scriptures has been upheld. You have today, O chief of the Bharatas, acted very properly.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: किं तु भूमेगंवां चार्थे सुवर्णं दीयतामिति। एवं वयं च धर्मज्ञ सर्वे चास्मत्पितामहाः॥ पाविता वै भविष्यन्ति पावनं हि परं हि तत्। दशपूर्वान् दशैवान्यांस्तथा संतारयन्ति ते॥ सुवर्णं ये प्रयच्छन्ति एवं मत्पितरोऽब्रुवन्। ततोऽहं विस्मितो राजन् प्रतिबुद्धो विशाम्पते॥
en: You have made gifts of earth and kine. Do you make gifts of gold. The gift of gold is very purifying. O you that are wellconversant with duties, know that by such acts both ourselves and our forefathers will all be purged of all our sins. Such gifts rescue both ancestors, and descendants of tenth degree of the person who makes them! These were the words that my ancestors, appearing to me in a dream, said to me. I then awoke, o king, and become filled with wonder.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: सुवर्णदानेऽकरवं मतिं च भरतर्षभ। इतिहासमिमं चापि शृणु राजन् पुरातनम्॥
en: Indeed, O chief of Bharata's race, I determined upon making gifts of gold, Listen now, O king, to this old history.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: जामदग्न्यं प्रति विभो धन्यमायुष्यमेव च। जामदग्न्येन रामेण तीव्ररोषान्वितेन वै॥ त्रिःसप्तकृत्व: पृथिवी कृता निःक्षत्रिया पुरा। ततो जित्वा महीं कृत्स्ना रामो राजीवलोचनः॥ आजहार क्रतुं वीरो ब्रह्मक्षत्रेण पूजितम्। वाजिमेधं महाराज सर्वकामसमन्वितम्॥
en: It is highly praiseworthy, and it gives longevity to a man who listens to it. It was first recited to Rama the son of Jamadagni. Formerly Jamadagni's son Rama, existed with great anger, rooted out the Kshatriyas from off the face of the Earth for twentyone times. Having subjugated the entire Earth, the heroic Rama having cyes like lotus petals began to make preparations for celebrating a Horse Sacrifice, O king, that is lauded by all Brahmanas and Kshatriyas and that is capable of granting the fruition of every desire.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: पावनं सर्वभूतानां तेजोद्युतिविवर्धनम्। विपाप्मा च स तेजस्व तेन क्रतुफलेन च॥
en: That sacrifice purifies all creatures and increases the energy and splendour of those who succeed in celebrating it. Gifted with great energy, Rama, by the celebration of that sacrifice, became sinless.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: नैवात्मनोऽथ लघुतां जामदग्न्योऽध्यगच्छत। स तु क्रतुवरेणेष्वा महात्मा दक्षिणावता॥
en: Having, however, celebrated that foremost of sacrifices, the great Rama could not acquire perfect lightness of heart.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: पप्रच्छागमसम्पन्नानृषीन् देवांश्च भार्गवः। पावनं यत् परं नृणामुग्रे कर्मणि वर्तताम्॥ तदुच्यतां महाभागा इति जातघृणोऽब्रवीत्। इत्युक्ता वेदशास्त्रज्ञास्तमूचुस्ते महर्षयः॥ राम विप्राः सक्रियन्तां वेदप्रामाण्यदर्शनात्। भूयश्च विप्रर्षिगणाः प्रष्टव्याः पावनं प्रति॥
en: Going to Rishis conversant with every branch of learning as also the celestials, Rama of Bhrigu's race questioned them. Filled with repentance and mercy, he addressed them, saying, highly blessed ones, do you declare that which purifies men engaged in terrific deeds? Thus addressed by him, those great Rishis, fully read in the Vedas and the scriptures, answered him, saying, ( Rama, guided by the authority of the Vedas, do you honour all learned Brahmanas. Acting thus for sometime, do you once more ask the twice born Rishis as to what should be done by you for purifying yourself.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: यद् ब्रूयूमहाप्राज्ञास्तच्चैव समुदाचर। ततो वसिष्ठं देवर्षिमगस्त्यमथ काश्यपम्॥ तमेवार्थं महातेजाः पप्रच्छ भृगुनन्दनः। जाता मतिर्मे विप्रेन्द्राः कथं पूयेयमित्युत॥
en: Follow the advice which those highly wise persons would give! Going then to Vashishtha and Agastya and Kashyapa, that delighter of the Bhrigus, gifted with great energy, asked them the very question, You foremost of Brahmanas, even this is the wish that has originated in my heart. How, indeed, can I purify myself.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: केन वा कर्मयोगेन प्रदानेनेह केन वा। यदि वोऽनुग्रहकृता बुद्धिर्मा प्रति सत्तमाः।
en: wa urah fos wafafa autetar:118011 By what acts and rites may this be engendered? Or, if by gifts, what is that article by giving away which this wish of mine may be satisfied, O foremost of righteous persons, if you are bent upon doing me a favour, then do tell me, you who have asceticism for wealth, what is that by which I may succeed in purifying myself!

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: ऋषय ऊचुः गाश्च भूमिं च वित्तं च दत्त्वेह भृगुनन्दन। पापकृत् पूयते मर्त्य इति भार्गव शुश्रुम॥
en: The Rishis said O delighter of the Bhrigus, the mortal that has committed sin becomes purified by making gifts of kine, of earth, and of riches. This is what we have heard.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: अन्यद् दानं तु विप्रर्षे श्रूयतां पावनं महत्। दिव्यमत्यद्भुताकारमपत्यं जातवेदसः॥
en: There is another gift that is considered as a great purifier. Listen to us, O twiceborn Rishi, as we discourse on it! That article is excellent and is wonderful to look at and is, besides, the offspring of Fire

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: दग्ध्वा लोकान् पुरा वीर्यात् सम्भूतमिह शुश्रुम। सुवर्णमिति विख्यातं तद् ददत् सिद्धिमेष्यसि॥
en: Formerly the god Agni burnt all the world. We have heard that from his seed sprung gold of bright complexion. It passed by the name of the goodcomplexioned. By making gifts of gold you are sure to have your wish fulfilled.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: ततोऽब्रवीद् वसिष्ठस्तं भगवान् संशितव्रतः। शृणु राम यथोत्पन्नं सुवर्णमनलप्रभम्॥
en: Then the illustrious Vashishtha in especial, of rigid vows, addressing him, said, Hear, O Rama, how gold, which is effulgent like fire, first came into being .

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: फलं दास्यति ते यत्तु दाने परमिहोच्यते। सुवर्णं यच्च यस्माच्च यथा च गुणवतमम्॥
en: That gold will confer merit on you. Ini matters of gifts, gold is highly spoken of. I shall also tell you what is gold, whence it has come, and how it has come to be endued with superior attributes.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तन्निबोध महाबाहो सर्वं निगदतो मम। अग्नीषोमात्मकमिदं सुवर्णं विद्धि निश्चये॥
en: Listen to me, O you of mighty arms, as I describe these subjects. Know this as certain that gold is of the essence of Fire and Moor.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: अजोऽग्निवरुणो मेषः सूर्योऽश्व इति दर्शनम्। कुञ्जराश्च मृगा नागा महिषाश्चासुरा इति॥ कुक्कुटाश्च वराहाश्च राक्षसा भृगुनन्दन। इडा गावः पयः सोमो भूमिरित्येव च स्मृतिः॥
en: The goat is Fire, the sheep is Varuna; the horse is the Sun; elephants are Nagas; buffaloes are Asuras; cocks and boars are Rakshasas; O delighter of the Bhrigus; earth is sacrifice, kine, water, and Soma. These are the declarations of the Smritis.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: जगत् सर्वं च निर्मथ्य तेजोराशिः समुत्थितः। सुवर्णमेभ्यो विप्रर्षे रत्नं परममुत्तमम्॥
en: Churning the entire universe, a mass of energy was found. That energy is gold. Hence, O twiceborn Rishi, compared to all these objects gold is surely superior. It is a valuable thing, high and excellent.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: एतस्मात् कारणाद् देवा गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसाः। मनुष्याश्च पिशाचाश्च प्रयता धारयन्ति तत्॥
en: It is therefore that the celestial and Gandharvas and Uragas and Rakshasas and human beings and Pishachas hold it with care.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: मुकुटैरङ्गदयुतैरलंकारैः पृथग्विधैः। सुवर्णविकृतैस्तत्र विराजन्ते भृगूत्तम॥
en: All these beings, O son of Bhrigu's race, shine in splendour, with the help of gold, after converting it into crowns and armlets and various ornaments.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तस्मात् सर्वपवित्रेभ्यः पवित्रं परमं स्मृतम्। भूमेगोभ्योऽथ रत्नेभ्यस्तद् विद्धि मनुजर्षभा॥
en: It is also for this reason that gold is considered as the most purifying of all cleansing things such as earth and kine and all other kinds of riches, O king.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: पूथिवीं गाश्च दत्त्वेह यच्चान्यदपि किंचन। विशिष्यते सुवर्णस्य दानं परमकं विभो॥
en: The gift of gold, O powerful king, is the highest gift. It is superior to the gift of earth, of kine, and of all other things.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: अक्षयं पावनं चैव सुवर्णममराते। प्रयच्छ द्विजमुख्येभ्यः पावनं ह्येतदुत्तमम्॥
en: O you who are effulgent like an immortal, gold is an eternal purifier. Do you make gifts of it to the foremost of Brahmanas as it is the foremost of purifying things.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: सुवर्णमेव सर्वासु दक्षिणासु विधीयते। सुवर्णे ये प्रयच्छन्ति सर्वदास्ते भवन्त्युत॥
en: Of all kinds of presents, gold is the best. They who make gifts of gold are said to be givers of all things,

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: देवतास्ते प्रयच्छन्ति ये सुवर्णं ददत्यथ। अग्निगर्हि देवताः सर्वाः सुवर्णं च तदात्मकम्॥
en: Indeed, they who make gifts of gold are considered as givers of celestials. Agni is all the deities in one, and gold has Agni for its essence.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तु तस्य तस्मात् सुवर्णं ददता दत्ताः सर्वाः स्म देवताः। भवन्ति पुरुषव्याघ्र न ह्यतः परमं विदुः॥
en: Hence it is that the person who makes gift of gold gives away all the celestials. Hence, O king, there is no gift higher than the gift of gold.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच भूय एव च माहात्म्यं सुवर्णस्य निबोध मे। गदतो मम विप्रर्षे सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वर॥
en: Vashishtha said Hear once more, O twice born Rishi, as I describe the superiority of gold, O foremost of all wielders weapons.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: मया श्रुतमिदं पूर्वं पुराणे भृगुनन्दन। प्रजापतेः कथयतो यथान्यायं वै॥
en: I heard this formerly in the Purana, O son of Bhrigu's race. It represents the speech of Prajapati himself.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: शूलपाणेर्भगवतो रुद्रस्य च महात्मनः। गिरौ हिमवति श्रेष्ठे तदा भृगुकुलोद्वह॥ देव्या विवाहे निवृत्ते रुद्राण्या भृगुनन्दन। समागमे भगवतो देव्या सह महात्मनः॥ तत: सर्वे समुद्विग्ना देवा रुद्रमुपागमन्। ते महादेवमासीनं देवीं च वरदामुमाम्॥ प्रसाद्य शिरसा सर्वे रुद्रमूचुर्भृगूद्वह। अयं समागमो देव देव्या सह तवानघ॥ तपस्विनस्तपस्विन्या तेजस्विन्याऽतितेजसः। अमोघतेजास्त्वं देव देवी चेयमुमा तथा॥
en: After the marriage was over of the illustrious and great Rudra armed with the trident, O son Bhrigu's race, with the goddess who became his consort, on the breast of that foremost of mountains, viz., Himavat, the illustrious and great deity wished to unite himself with the goddess. Thereupon all the celestials, stricken with anxiety, approached Rudra. Bending their heads with respect and pleasing Mahadeva and his boon-giving consort Uma, both of whom were seated together, they addressed Rudra, O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, saying, This union, O illustrious and sinless one, of you with the goddess, is a union of an ascetic with another. Indeed, it is the union, O lord, of one energetic person with another equally so. You, O illustrious one, are of irresistible energy. The goddess Uma also is gifted with energy that is equally irresistible.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: अपत्यं युवयोर्देव बलवद् भविता विभो। तन्नूनं त्रिषु लोकेषु न किञ्चिच्छेषयिष्यति॥
en: The offspring that will result from a union like this, will, forsooth, O illustrious deity, be gifted with very great might. Indeed, powerful lord, that offspring will consume all things in the three worlds without leaving a residue.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तदेभ्यः प्रणतेभ्यस्त्वं देवेभ्यः पृथुलोचन। वरं प्रयच्छ लोकेश त्रैलोक्यहितकाम्यया॥
en: Do you then, O lord of all the universe, O you having large eyes, grant to these celestials prostrated before you, a boon from desire of benefiting the three worlds.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: अपत्यार्थं निगृह्वीष्व तेजः परमकं विभो। त्रैलोक्यसारौ हि युवां लोकं संतापयिष्यथः॥
en: Do you, O powerful one, restrain this great energy of yours may become the seed of offspring. Indeed, that energy is the essence of all forces in the three worlds. You two, by an act of congress, are sure of scorch the universe.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तदपत्यं हि युवयोर्देवानभिभवेद् ध्रुवम्। न हि ते पृथिवी देवी न च द्यौर्न दिवं विभो॥ नेदं धारयितुं शक्ताः समस्ता इति मे मतिः। तेज:प्रभावनिर्दग्धं तस्मात् सर्वमिदं जगत्॥
en: Your offspring will certainly be able of afflict the celestials. Neither the goddess Earth, nor the Sky, nor Heaven, O powerful one, nor all of them together, will be able to bear your energy, we firmly believe. The entire universe yours which is certain to be burnt through the force of your energy.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तस्मात् प्रसादं भगवन् कर्तुमर्हसि नः प्रभो। न देव्यां सम्भवेत् पुत्रो भवतः सुरसत्तम। धैर्यादेव निगृह्णीष्व तेजो ज्वलितमुत्तमम्॥
en: You should, O powerful one, show us favour, O illustrious deity. That favour consists in your not begetting a son, O foremost of the celestials, upon the goddess Uma. Do you, patiently govern your fiery and powerful energy.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: इति तेषां कथयतां भगवान् वृषभध्वजः। एवमस्त्विति देवांस्तान् विप्रर्षे प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: To the deities that said so, the holy Mahadeva having the bull for his sign, O twiceborn Rishi, answered, saying, So be it!

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: इत्युक्त्वा चोर्ध्वमनयद् रेतो वृषभवाहनः। उर्ध्वरेताः समभवत् ततः प्रभृति चापि सः॥ रुद्राणीति ततः क्रुद्धा प्रजोच्छेदे तदा कृते। देवानथाब्रवीत् तत्र स्त्रीभावात् परुषं वचः॥
en: Having said so, the deity that has the bull for his vehicle, drew up his vital seed. From that time he passed by the name of Urddharetas (one that has drawn up the vital seed). At this attempt of the celestials to stop procreation, the consort of Rudra became highly wroth. On account of her being the opposite sex, she used hard words. On account of her being the opposite sex, she used hard words.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: यस्मादपत्यकामो वै भर्ता मे विनिवर्तितः। सुरा यूयमनपत्या भविष्यथ॥
en: Since you have opposed my lord in procreating an offspring when he was desirous of procrcating one upon me, as the result of this act, you celestials, you all shall become sonless.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: प्रजोच्छेदो मम कृतो यस्माद् युष्माभिरद्य वै। तस्मात् प्रजा वः स्वगमा: सर्वेषां न भविष्यति॥
en: Indeed, since you have opposed the birth of an offspring from me, therefore, you shall have no offspring of your own When this curse was imprecated.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: तस्मात् सर्वे पावकस्तु न तत्रासीच्छापकाले भृगूद्वह। देवा देव्यास्तथा शापादनपत्यास्ततोऽभवन्॥
en: O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, the deity of fire was not there. It is on account of this curse of the goddess that the deities have become childless.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: रुद्रस्तु तेजोऽप्रतिमं धारयामास वै तदा। प्रस्कन्नं तु ततस्तस्मात् किंचित्तत्रापतद् भुवि॥
en: Rudra begged them, held in himself his energy of incomparable power. A small quantity, however, that came out o this body dropped on the Earth.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: उत्पपात तदा वह्वौ ववृधे चाद्भुतोपमम्। तेजस्तेजसि संयुक्तमात्मयोनित्वमागतम्॥
en: That seed, falling on the Earth, leaped into a burning fire and there began to grow most wonderfully.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः। असुरस्तारको नाम तेन संतापिता भृशम्॥ आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा मरुतोऽथाश्विनावपि। साध्याश्च सर्वे संत्रस्ता दैतेयस्य पराक्रमात्॥
en: The energy of Rudra, coming in contact with another energy of great power, became une with it in essence. Mean while, all the celestials headed by Indra were scorched by the Asura named Taraka. The Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Maruts, the Ashvins, and the Saddhyas all became greatly afflicted on account of the prowess of that son of Diti.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: स्थानानि देवतानां हि विमानानि पुराणि च। ऋषीणां चाश्रमाश्चैव बभूवुरसुरैर्हताः॥
en: All the regions of the celestials, their beautiful cars, and their palaces, and the asylums of the Rishis, we.e snatched away by the Asuras.

description: An account of gold and its gifts
sn: ते दीनमनसः सर्वे देवता ऋषयश्च ये। प्रजग्मुः शरणं देवं ब्रह्माणमजरं विभुम्॥
en: Then the celestials and the Rishis, with depressed hearts, sought the protection of the illustrious and powerful Brahman of unfading glory.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: भगवानुवाच असुरस्तारको नाम त्वया दत्तवरः प्रभो। सुरानृषीश्च क्लिश्नाति वधस्तस्य विधीयताम्॥
en: The Deities said The Asura named Taraka who has received boons from you, O powerful one, is assailing the celestials and the Rishis. Let his death be ordained by you.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तस्माद् भयं समुत्पन्नमस्माकं वै पितामह। परित्रायस्व नो देव न ह्यन्या गतिरस्ति नः॥
en: O Grandfather, we fear him greatly. O illustrious one, do you save us! We have no other refuge than you.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ब्राह्मोवाच समोऽहं सर्वभूतानामधर्मं नेह रोचये। हन्यतां तारकः क्षिप्रं सुरर्षिगणबाधिता॥
en: Brahman said I treat all creatures equally, I cannot however, approve of sin, Let Taraka, that enemy of the celestials and Rishis, be speedily destroyed.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: वेदा धर्माश्च नोच्छेदं गच्छेयुः सुरसत्तमाः। विहितं पूर्वमेवात्र मया वै व्येतु वो ज्वरः॥
en: The Vedas and the eternal duties shall not be rooted out, you foremost of celestials, I have ordained what is proper, in this matter. Let the anxiety of your hearts be removed.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: देवा ऊचुः वरदानाद् भगवतो दैतयो बलगर्वितः। दैवैर्न शक्यते हन्तुं स कथं प्रशमं व्रजेत्॥
en: The Celestials said For your having granted him boons, that son of Diti has been proud of his power. He is incapable of being killed by the deities. How then will his death be engendered?

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: स हि नैव स्म देवानां नासुराणां न रक्षसाम्। वध्य: स्यामिति जग्राह वरं त्वत्तः पितामह॥
en: The boon which, O Grandfather, he has obtained from you is that he should not be killed by celestials or Asuras or Rakshasas.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: देवाश्च शप्ता रुद्राण्या प्रजोच्छेदे पुराकृते। न भविष्यति वोऽपत्यमिति सर्वे जगत्पते॥
en: The celestials have also been cursed by the wife of Rudra on account of their attempt of step propagation. The curse imprecated by her has been, O lord of the universe, this viz., that they are not to have any offspring.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच हुताशनो न तत्रासीच्छापकाले सुरोत्तमाः। स उत्पदयितापत्यं वधाय त्रिदशद्विषाम्॥ तद् वै सर्वानतिक्रम्य देवदानवराक्षसान्। मानुषानथ गन्धर्वान् नागानथ च पक्षिणः॥ अस्त्रेणामोघपातेन शक्त्यां तं घातयिष्यति। यतो वो भयमुत्पन्नं ये चान्ये सुरशत्रवः॥
en: Brahman said You foremost of celestials, Agni was not there at the time the curse was given by the goddess. He will beget a child for the destruction of the enemies of the gods. Superior to all the deities, Danavas, Rakshasas, human beings, Gandharvas. Nagas and feathery creatures, the son of Agni with his dart, which in his hands, will be a weapon incapable of being baffled if once hurled at the enemy, will destroy Taraka whom you fear. Indeed, all other enemies of yours will also be killed by him.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: सनातनो हि संकल्पः काम इत्यभिधीयते। रुद्रस्य तेजः प्रस्कन्नमग्नौ निपतितं च यत्॥
en: Will is eternal. That Will is known by the name of Kama and is at one with Rudra's seed a portion of which fell into the burning form of Agni.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तत्तेजोऽग्निर्महद्भूतं द्वितीयमिति पावकम्। वधार्थं देवशत्रूणां गङ्गायां जनयिष्यति॥
en: That energy, which is a powerful substance, and which resembles a second Agni, will be cast by Agni into Ganga for producing a child upon her in order to bring about the destruction of the enemies of the gods.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: स तु नावाप तं शापं नष्टः स हुतभुक् तदा। तस्माद् वो भयहृद् देवाः समुत्पत्स्यति पावकिः॥१३
en: Agni did not come within the range of Uma's curse. The eater of sacrificial libations was not present there when the curse was imprecated.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अन्विष्यतां वै ज्वलनस्तथा चाद्य नियुज्यताम्। तारकस्य वधोपायः कथितो वै मयानघाः॥
en: Let the god of fire, therefore, be searched out. Let him now be set to this task. You sinless ones, I have told you the means for the destruction of Taraka.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: न हि तेजस्विनां शापास्तेजःसु प्रभवन्ति वै। बलान्यतिबलं प्राप्य दुर्बलानि भवन्ति वै॥
en: The curses of the energetic cannot produce any effect upon the energetic. Forces, when they come into contact with a stronger force, become weakened.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: हन्यादवध्यान् वरदानपि चैव तपस्विनः। संकल्पाभिरुचिः काम: सनातनतोऽभवत्॥
en: They who are endued with penances can destroy even the boongiving deities who are indestructible. Will, or Like, or Desire sprang in former times and is the most eternal of all creatures.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: जगत्पतिरनिर्देश्यः सर्वगः सर्वभावनः। हृच्छयः सर्वभूतानां ज्येष्ठो रुद्रादपि प्रभुः॥
en: Agni is the Lord of the universe. He is incapable of being apprehended or described. Capable of going every where and present in all things he is the Creator of all beings. He lives in the hearts of all creatures, Gifted with great power, He is older than Rudra himself.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अन्विष्यतां स तु क्षिप्रं तेजोराशिर्हताशनः। स वो मनोगतं कामं देवः सम्पादयिष्यति॥ एतद् वाक्यमुपश्रुत्य ततो देवा महात्मनः। जग्मुः संसिद्धसंकल्पाः पर्येषन्तो विभावसुम्॥
en: Let that eater of sacrificial libations, who is mass of energy, be found out. That illustrious deity will fulfil this desire of your hearts, Hearing these word of the Grandfather, the great gods then proceeded to find out to the god of fire with cheerful hearts on account of their purpose having been crowned with success. possessed

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ततस्त्रैलोक्यमृषयो व्यचिन्वन्त सुरैः सह। काङ्क्षन्तो दर्शनं वह्नः सर्वे तद्गतमानसाः॥
en: The gods and the Rishis then searched every portion of the three worlds their hearts being busy with the thought of Agni and eagerly desiring to see him.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: परेण तपसा युक्ताः श्रीमन्तो लोकविश्रुताः। लोकानन्वचरन् सिद्धाः सर्व एव भृगूत्तम॥
en: Gifted with penances, of prosperity celebrated over all the worlds, those great ones, all crowned with ascetic success, sojourned over every part of the universe, O foremost one of Bhrigu's race.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: नष्टमात्मनि संलीनं नाधिजग्मुर्हताशनम्। ततः संजातसंत्रासानग्निदर्शनलालसान्॥ जलेचरः क्लान्तमनास्तेजसाग्नेः प्रदीपितः। उवाच देवान् मण्डूको रसातलतलोत्थितः॥ रसातलतले देवा वसत्यग्निरिति प्रभो। संतापादिह सम्प्राप्तः पावकप्रभवादहम्॥
en: They could not find out the eater of sacrificial libations who had concealed himself by merging his self into self. At this time, a frog, living in water, got on the surface from the nethermost regions, with cheerless heart on account of having been scorched by the energy of Agni. The little creature addressed the celestials who had become stricken with fear and who had became stricken with fear and who were all very eager to see the god of fire, saying, You gods, Agni is now living in the nethermost regions. Scorched by the energy of that god and unable to bear in longer, I have come here.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: स संसुप्तो जले देवा भगवान् हव्यवाहनः । अपः संसृज्य तेजोभिस्तेन संतापिता वयम्॥
en: The illustrious bearer of sacrificial offerings ye gods, is now under the waters. He has created a mass of waters within which he is living. All of us have been scorched by his energy.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तस्य दर्शनमिष्टं वो यदि देवा विभावसोः। तत्रैवमधिगच्छध्वं कार्यं वो यदि वह्निना॥
en: If, ye gods, you wish to see himif you have any business with him, go to him there.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: गम्यतां साधयिष्याप्तो वयं ह्यग्निभयात् सुराः। एतावदुक्त्वा मण्डूकस्त्वरितो जलमाविशत्॥
en: As regards ourselves, we shall fly from this place, O celestials, from fear of Agni! Having said this much, the frog dived into the water.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: हुताशनस्तु बुबुधे मण्डूकस्य च पैशुनम्। शशाप स तमासाद्य न रसान् वेत्स्यसीति वै॥
en: The eater of sacrificial libations came to know of the treachery of the frog. Coming to that animal, he cursed the whole race, saying, You will be deprived of the organ of taste.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तं वै संयुज्य शापेन मण्डूकं त्वरितो ययौ। अन्यत्र वासाय विभुर्न चात्मानमदर्शयत्॥
en: Having made this curse on the frog, he left spot immediately for living else, where. Indeed the powerful celestial did not show himself.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: देवास्त्वनुग्रहं चक्रुर्मण्डूकानां भृगूत्तम। यत्तच्छृणु महाबाहो गदतो मम सर्वशः॥
en: Seeing the condition to which the frogs were reduced for having done them a service, the celestials o best of the Bhrigus, showed favour to those creatures. I shall tell you everything about it. Do you hear me, O mightyarmed hero.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: देवा ऊचुः अग्निशापादजिह्वापि रसज्ञानबहिष्कृताः। सरस्वती बहुविधां यूयमुच्चारयिष्यथ॥
en: The Deities said Though deprived of tongues through the curse of Agni and, therefore of the sensation of taste, you will be able to utter various kinds of words.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: बिलवासं गतांश्चैव निराहारानचेतसः। गतासूनपि संशुष्कान् भूमिः संधारयिष्यति॥
en: Living within holes, deprived of food, shorn of consciousness, wasted and dried up, and more dead than alive, the Earth will yet hold you all.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तमोघनायामपि वै निशायां विचरिष्यथ। इत्युक्त्वा तांस्ततो देवाः पुनरेव महामिमाम्॥ परीयुर्व्वलनस्यार्थे न चाविन्दन् हुताशनम्।
en: You shall also be able to move about at nighttime when everything is covered with thick darkness! Having said this to the frogs, the celestials once more journeyed over every part of the Earth for finding out the god of fire. Despite all their endeavours however, they could not find him out.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अथ तान् द्विरदः कश्चित् सुरेन्द्रद्विरदोपमः॥ अश्वत्थस्थोऽग्निरित्येवमाह देवान् भृगूद्वह।
en: Then, O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, an elephant, as large and powerful as the elephant of Shakra addressed the gods, sayingAgni is now living within this Ashvattha tree!

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: शशाप ज्वलनः सर्वान् द्विरदान् क्रोधमूच्छितः॥ प्रतीपा भवतां जिह्वा भवित्रीति भृगूद्वह।
en: Worked up with anger, Agni cursed all the elephants, O descendent of Bhrigu, sayingYour tongues will be bent back.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: इत्युक्त्वा निःसृतोऽश्वत्थादग्निर्वारणसूचितः। प्रविवेश शमीगर्भमथ वह्निः सुषुप्सया॥
en: Having been pointed out by the elephants, the God of Fire cursed all elephants thus and then went away and entered the heart of the Shami tree for living within it for sometime.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अनुग्रहं तु नागानां यं चक्रुः शृणु तं प्रभो। देवा भृगुकुलश्रेष्ठ प्रीत्या सत्यपराक्रमाः॥
en: Listen now, O powerful hero, what favour was shown to the elephants, O foremost one of Bhrigu's race; by the celestials of unbaffled prowess who were all pleased with the service one of their representatives had rendered them.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: देवा ऊचुः प्रतीपया जिह्वयापि सर्वाहारं करिष्यथ। वाचं चोच्चारयिष्यध्वमुच्चैरव्यञ्जिताक्षराम्॥
en: The Deities said With the help of even your tongues bent inwards you shall be able to eat all things, and with even those tongues you shall be able to utter cries which will only be indistinct. Having blessed the elephants thus, the inhabitants of the celestial region once more began to search Agni.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: इत्युक्त्वा पुनरेवाग्निमनुसझुर्दिवौकसः। अश्वत्यान्निःसृतश्चाग्निः शमीगर्भमुपाविशत्॥
en: Indeed, having come out of the Ashvattha tree, the God of Fire had entered the heart of Shami,

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: शुकेन ख्यापितो विप्र तं देवाः समुपाद्रवन्। शशाप शुकमग्निस्तु वाग्विहीनो भविष्यसि॥
en: This new residence of Agni was made known by a parrot. The gods there upon went there. Enraged with the conduct of the parrot, the God of Fire cursed the whole parrot race, saying, You shall from this day be deprived of the power of speech.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: जिह्वामावर्तयामास तस्यापि हुतभुक् तथा। दृष्ट्वा तु ज्वलनं देवाः शुकमूचुर्दयान्विताः॥ भविता न त्वमत्यन्तं शुकत्वे नष्टवागिति। आवृत्तजिह्वस्य सतो वाक्यं कान्तं भविष्यति॥
en: Indeed, the eater of sacrificial offerings turned up the tongues of all the parrots. Seeing Agni at the place pointed out by the parrot, and beholding the curse imprecated upon him, the gods, moved by mercy for the poor creature. blessed him, saying, on account of your being a parrot, you shall not be wholly deprived of the power of speech. Though your tongue has been turned backwards, yet you will only be able to speak the letter K.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: बालस्येव प्रवृद्धस्य कलमव्यक्तमद्भुतम्। इत्युक्त्वा तं शमीगर्भे वह्निमालक्ष्य देवताः॥ तदेवायतनं चक्रुः पुण्यं सर्वक्रियास्वपि। ततः प्रभृति चाप्यग्निः शमीगर्भेषु दृश्यते॥
en: Like that of a child or an old man, your words shall be sweet and indistinct and wonderfulHaving said these words to the parrot, and seeing the god of fire within the heart of the Shami, the gods made Shami wood a sacred fuel fit for producing fire in all religious rites. It was from that time that fire is seen to live in the heart of the Shami.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: उत्पादने तथोपायमभिजग्मुश्च मानवाः। आपो रसातले यास्तु संस्पृष्टाश्चित्रभानुना॥
en: Men began to consider the Shami as a proper means for producing fire (in sacrifices). The waters that are in the nether most regions had come into contact with the god of fire.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ताः पर्वतप्रस्रवणैरूष्मां मुञ्चन्ति भार्गव। पावकेनाधिशयता संतप्तास्तस्य तेजसा॥
en: Those heated waters, O you of Bhrigu's race, are vomited forth by the mountain springs. On account, of Agni's having lived in them for sometime, they became hot through his power.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अथाग्निर्देवता दृष्ट्वा बभूव व्यथितस्तदा। किमागमनमित्येवं तानपृच्छत पावकः॥
en: Meanwhile Agni, seeing the gods, became grieved. Addressing the celestials, he asked them, Why have you come here?

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तमूचुर्विबुधाः सर्वे ते चैव परमर्षयः। त्वां नियोक्ष्यमहे कार्यं तद् भवान् कर्तुमर्हति॥ कृते च तस्मिन् भविता तवापि समुहान् गुणः॥
en: To him the celestials and the great Rishis said, We wish to engage you in a particular work. You should perform it. When done, it will redound greatly to your credit.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अग्निरुवाच ब्रूत यद् भवतां कार्यं कर्तास्मि तदहं सुराः। भवतां तु नियोज्योऽस्मि मा वोऽत्रास्तु विचारणा।।५०
en: Agni said Tell me what your business is. I shall, O gods accomplish it. I am always willing to do anything for you. Do not, hesitate, therefore, to command me.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: देवा ऊचुः असुरस्तारको नाम ब्रह्मणो वरदर्पितः। अस्मान् प्रबाधते वीर्याद् वधस्तस्य विधीयताम्॥
en: The celestials said There is an Asura of the name of Taraka who has been filled with pride on account of the boon he has obtained from Brahman. By his power he is able to oppose and discomfit us. Do you bring about his destruction.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: इमान् देवगणांस्तात प्रजापतिगणांस्तथा। ऋषींचापि महाभाग परित्रायस्व पावक॥
en: O sire, do you rescue these celestials, these Prajapatis, and these Rishis, O highly blessed Pavaka.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अपत्यं तेजसा युक्तं प्रवीरं जनय प्रभो। यद् भयं नोऽसुरात् तस्मान्नाशयेद्धव्यवाहन॥
en: O powerful one, do you beget a heroic son possessed of your power, who will remove, O bearer of sacrificial libations, our fears from that Asura.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: शप्तानां नो महादेव्या नान्यदस्ति परायणम्। अन्यत्र भवतो वीर्यं तस्मात् त्रायस्व नः प्रभो॥
en: We have been cursed by the great goddess Uma. There is nothing else than your power which can be our refuge now. Do you, therefore, O powerful deity, rescue us all.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: इत्युक्तः स तथेत्युक्त्वा भगवान् हव्यवाहनः। जगामाथ दुराधर्षो गङ्गां भागीरथी प्रति॥
en: Thus addressed, the illustrious and irresistible bearer of sacrificial libations answered, saying, Be it so! and he then proceeded towards Ganga otherwise called Bhagirathi.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तया चाप्यभवन्मिश्रो गर्भे चास्यादधे तदा। ववृधे स तदा गर्भः कक्षे कृष्णगतिर्यथा।॥
en: He knew her and caused her to conceive. Indeed, in the womb of Ganga the seed of Agni began to grow even as Agni himself grows.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तेजसा तस्य देवस्य गङ्गा विह्वलचेतना। संतापमगमत् तीव्र सोढुं सा न शशाक ह॥
en: With the energy of that god, Ganga became greatly moved at heart. Indeed, she suffered great distress and became unable to bear it.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: आहिते ज्वलनेनाथ गर्भे तेजः समन्विते। गङ्गायामसुरः कश्चिद् भैरवं नादमानदत्॥
en: When the deity of fire cast his seed gifted with great energy into the womb of Ganga, a certain Asura uttered a terrific roar.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अबुद्धिपतितेनाथ नादेन विपुलेन सा। वित्रस्तोद्धान्तनयना गङ्गा विनुतलोचना॥
en: On account of that dreadful roar uttered by the Asura for purposes of his own, Ganga became very much terrified and her eyes rolled in fear and betrayed her agitation.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: विसंज्ञा नाशकद् गर्भं वोढुमात्मानमेव च। सा तु तेजःपरीताङ्गी कम्पयन्तीव जाह्नवी॥
en: Shorn of consciousness, she could not bear her body and the seed within her womb. The daughter of Janhu, carrying the energy of the illustrious god, began to tremble.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: उवाच ज्वलनं विप्र तदा गर्भबलोद्धता। ते न शक्तास्मि भगवंस्तेजसोऽस्य विधारणे॥
en: Overwhelmed with the energy of the seed she held in her womb, O learned Brahmana, she then addressed the god of fire, saying, I cannot any longer, O illustrious one, bear your seed in my womb.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: विमूढास्मि कृतानेन न मे स्वास्थ्यं यथा पुरा। विह्वला चास्मि भगवंश्चेतो नष्टं च मेऽनघ॥
en: Indeed, I am overcome with weakness by this seed of yours. The health I had in days before, is no longer mine. I have been greatly agitated, O illustrious one, and my heart is dead within me, O sinless one.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: धारणे नास्य शक्ताहं गर्भस्य तपतां वर। उत्स्रक्ष्येऽहमिमं दुःखान्न तु कामात् कथंचन॥
en: O foremost of all persons gifted with penances, I cannot bear your seed any longer. I shall throw it off, induced by the distress that has befallen me, and not by caprice.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: न तेजसोऽस्ति संस्पर्शो मम देव विभावसो। आपदर्थे हि सम्बन्धः सुसूक्ष्मोऽपि महाद्युते॥
en: There has been no actual contact of my body with your seed, O illustrious deity of fire. Our union, having for its cause the distress that has befallen the celestials, has been subtile and not of the flesh, O highly effulgent one.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: यदत्र गुणसम्पन्नमितरद् वा हुताशन। त्वय्येव तदहं मन्ये धर्माधर्मी च केवलौ॥
en: Whatever merit or otherwise they may be in this deed, O eater of sacrificial offerings, must belong to you. indeed, I think, you will be visited by virtue or sin of this deed.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तामुवाच ततो वह्निर्धार्यतां धार्यतामिति। गर्भो मत्तेजसा युक्तो महागुणफलोदयः ॥
en: To her the god of fire said, Do you carry the seed. Do, indeed, bear the foetus endued with my power. It will produce great results.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: शक्ता ह्यसि महीं कृत्स्नां वोढुं धारयितुं तथा। न हि ते किंचिदप्राप्यमन्यतो धारणादृते॥ सा वह्निना वार्यमाणा देवैरपि सरिद्वरा। समुत्ससर्ज तं गर्भं मेरौ गिरिवरे तदा॥
en: You are, indeed, capable of bearing the entire Earth. You will gain nothing by not holding this energy. That foremost of rivers, though thus dissuaded by the deity of fire as also by all the other celestials, cast off the seed on the breast of Meru, that foremost of all mountains.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: समर्था धारणे चापि रुद्रतेजःप्रधर्षिता। नाशकत् तं तदा गर्भ संधारयितुमोजसा॥
en: Capable of bearing that seed, yet oppressed by the power of Rudra, she could not hold that seed longer on account of its burning energy.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: सा समुत्सृज्य तं दुःखाद् दीप्तवैश्वाना, नम्। दर्शयामास चाग्निस्तं तदा गङ्गां भृगूद्वह॥ पप्रच्छ सरितां श्रेष्ठां कच्चिद् गर्भः सुखोदयः। कीदृग्वर्णोऽपि वा देवि कीदृग्रूपश्च दृश्यते। तेजसा केन वा युक्तः सर्वमेतद् ब्रवीहि मे॥
en: After she had cast it off, through sheer distress, that burning seed having the splendour of fire, O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, Agni saw her, and asked that foremost of rivers, Is it all right with the foetus you have cast off? Of what complexion has it been, O goddess? Of what form does it look? With what energy does it seem to be gifted? Do you tell me all about it.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: गङ्गा उवाच जातरूपः स गर्भो वै तेजसा त्वमिवानघ। सुवर्णो विमलो दीप्तः पर्वतं चावभासयत्॥
en: Ganga said The foetus is of goldhue. In energy it is like you, O sinless one! Of an excellent colour, perfectly stainless, and burning with splendour, it has lighted the entire mountain.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: पद्मोत्पलविमिश्राणां ह्रदानामिव शीतलः। गन्धोऽस्य स कदम्बानां तुल्यो वै तपतां वर॥
en: O foremost of all persons gifted with penances, the fragrance of it resembles the cool perfume that is scattered by lakes adorned with lotuses.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तेजसा तस्य गर्भस्य भास्करस्येव रश्मिभिः। यद् द्रव्यं परिसंसृष्टं पृथिव्यां पर्वतेषु च॥ तत् सर्वं काञ्चनीभूतं समन्तात् प्रत्यदृश्यत। पर्यधावत शैलांश्च नदीः प्रस्रवणानि च॥
en: With the splendour of that foetus everything around it seemed to be changed into gold as all things on mountain and low land seem to be changed into gold by the rays of the Sun.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: व्यादीपयंस्तेजसा च त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्। एवंरूपः स भगवान् पुत्रस्ते हव्यवाहन। सूर्यवैश्वानरसमः कान्त्या सोम इवापरः॥
en: The splendour of that foetus, spreading far and wide, falls upon mountains and rivers and springs. It seems that the three worlds, with all their mobile and immobile creatures, are being lighted up by it. Such is your child, O illustrious bearer of sacrificial offerings. Like the Sun or your blazing self, in beauty it is like second Soma!

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु सा देवी तत्रैवान्तरधीयता पावकश्चापि तेजस्वी कृत्वा कार्यं दिवौकसाम्॥ जगामेष्टं ततो देशं तदा भार्गवनन्दन।
en: Having said these words, the goddess-disappeared. The highly energetic god of fire also, having performed the business of the celestials, proceeded to the place he liked, O delighter of the Bhrigus.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: एतैः कर्मगुणैर्लोके नामाग्नेः परिगीयते॥ हिरण्यरेता इति वै ऋषिभिर्विबुधैस्तथा। पृथिवी च तदा देवी ख्याता वसुमतीति वै॥
en: It was on account of the result of this act that the Rishis and the celestials bestowed the name of Hiranyaretas upon the gods of fire. . And because the Earth held that seed she also came to be called by the name of Vasumati.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: स तु गर्भो महातेजा गाङ्गेयः पावकोद्भवः। दिव्यं शरवणं प्राप्य ववृधेऽद्भुतदर्शनः॥
en: Meanwhile, that foetus, which had originated from the god of fire and been held for a time by Ganga, having fallen on a forest of reeds, began to grow and at last assumed a wonderful form.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ददृशुः कृत्तिकास्तं तु बालार्कसदृशद्युतिम्। पुत्रं वै ताश्च तं बालं पुपुषुः स्तन्यविस्रवैः॥
en: The presiding goddess of the constellation Krittika saw that form resembling the rising Sun.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ततः स कार्तिकेयत्वमवाप परमद्युतिः। स्कन्नत्वात् स्कन्दतां चापि गुहावासाद् गुहोऽभवत्।।
