en: She henceforth began to bring up that child as her son with the milk of her breast. For this reason that highly effulgent child came to be called Kartikeya after her name.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: एवं सुवर्णमुत्पन्नमपत्यं जातवेदसः। तत्र जाम्बूनदं श्रेष्ठं देवानामपि भूषणम्॥
en: And because he grew from seed that fell out of Rudra's body, he came to be called Skanda. The incident also of his birth having taken place in the forest of reeds, concealed from every body's view, gave him the name of Guha. It was thus that gold came into existence as the offspring of the god of fire.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ततः प्रभृति चाप्येतज्जातरूपमुदाहृतम्। रत्नानामुत्तमं रत्नं भूषणानां तथैव च॥
en: Hence it is that gold came to be regarded as the foremost of all things and the ornament of the very gods. It was from this incident that gold came to be called by the name of Jatarupam.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: पवित्रं च पवित्राणां मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम्। यत् सुवर्णं स भगवानग्निरीशः प्रजापतिः॥
en: It is the foremost of all precious things, and among ornaments also it is the foremost. The purifier among all purifying things it is the most sacred of all sacred objects.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: पवित्राणां पवित्रं हि कनकं द्विजसत्तमाः। अग्नीषोमात्मकं चैव जातरूपमुदाहृतम्॥
en: Gold is truly the illustrious Agni, the Lord of all things, and the foremost of all Prajapatis. The most sacred of all sacred things if gold, O foremost of twiceborn ones. Indeed, gold is said to have for its essence Agni and Soma.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच अपि चेदं पुरा राम श्रुतं मे ब्रह्मदर्शनम्। पितामहस्य यद् वृत्तं ब्रह्मणः परमात्मनः॥
en: Vashishtha said Formerly I also heard this history, O Rama, called Brahmadarshana, about the achievement of the Grandfather Brahman who is at one with the Supreme Soul.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: देवस्य महतस्तात वारुणीं बिभ्रतस्तनुम्। ऐश्वर्ये वारुणे राम रुद्रस्येशस्य वै प्रभो॥ आजग्मुर्मुनयः सर्वे देवाश्चाग्निपुरोगमाः। यज्ञाङ्गानि च सर्वाणि वषट्कारश्च मूर्तिमान्॥
en: To a sacrifice performed formerly by that foremost of gods, viz., the Lord of Rudra, O you of great power, who on that occasion had assumed the form of Varuna, there came the ascetics and all the celestials headed by Agni. There also came to that sacrifice all the sacrificial limbs (in their embodied forms), and the Mantra called Vashat in his embodied forin.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: मूर्तिमन्ति च सामानि यजूंषि च सहस्रशः। ऋग्वेदश्चागमत् तत्र पदक्रमविभूषितः॥
en: All the Samans also and all the Yajushas, in thousands and in their embodied forms, came there. The Rig Veda also came there, adorned with the rules of orthoepy.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: लक्षणानि स्वराः स्तोभा निरुक्तं सुरपतयः। ओङ्कारश्चावसन्नेत्रे निग्रहप्रग्रहौ तथा॥
en: The Lakshnanas, the Svaras, the stotras, the Niruktas, the Notes arranged in rows, and the syllable Om, as also Nigraha and Pragraha, all came there and lived in the eye of Mahadeva.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: वेदाश्च सोपनिषदो विद्या सावित्र्यथापि च। भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च दधार भगवान् शिवः॥
en: The Vedas with the Upanishads, Vidya, and Savitri, as also, the Past, the Present, and the Future, all came there and were held by the illustrious Shiva.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: संजुहावात्मनाऽऽत्मानं स्वयमेव तदा प्रभो। यज्ञं च शोभयामास बहुरूपं पिनाकधृत्॥
en: The powerful Lord of All then poured libations himself into his own self. Indeed, the holder of Pinaka caused that Sacrifice of multifarious form to look highly beautiful.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: द्यौर्नभः पृथिवी खं च तथा चैवैष भूपतिः। सर्वविद्येश्वरः श्रीमानेष चापि विभावसुः॥
en: He is Heaven, Sky, Earth, and the Welkin. He is called the Lord of the Earth. He is the Lord whose rule is acknowledged by all obstacles. He is gifted with Shree and He is at one with the God of Fire.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: एष ब्रह्मा शिवो रुद्रो वरुणोऽग्निः प्रजापतिः। कीर्त्यते भगवान् देवः सर्वभूतपतिः शिवः॥
en: That illustrious god is called by various names. He is Brahman, Shiva, Rudra, Varuna, Agni and Prajapati, He is the auspicious Lord of all creatures.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तस्य यज्ञः पशुपतेस्तपः क्रतव एव च। दीक्षा दीप्तव्रता देवी दिशश्च सदिगीश्वराः॥ देवपत्न्यश्च कन्याश्च देवानां चैव मातरः। आजग्मुः सहितास्तत्र तदा भृगुकुलोद्वह॥
en: Sacrifice, Penance, all the rites, the goddess Diksha burning with rigid observances, the several Points with the presiding deities, the consorts of all the deities, their daughters, and the celestials mothers, all came to Pashupati, O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, together in a body.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: यज्ञं पशुपतेः प्रीता वरुणस्य महात्मनः। स्वयम्भुवस्तु ता दृष्ट्वा रेतः समपतद् भुवि॥
en: Seeing that sacrifice of the great Mahadeva who had assumed the form of Varuna, all of them became highly pleased. Seeing the celestial ladies of great beauty, the seed of Brahman came out and dropped upon the Earth.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तस्य शुक्रस्य विस्पन्दान् पांसून् संगृह्य भूमितः। प्रास्यत् पूषा कराभ्यां वै तस्मिन्नेव हुताशने॥
en: On account of the seed having fallen on the dust, the Sun took up that dust mixed with the particles of seed from the Earth with his hands and cast it into the sacrificial fire.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ततस्तस्मिन् सम्प्रवृत्ते सत्रे ज्वलितपावके। ब्रह्मणो जुह्वतस्तत्र प्रादुर्भावो बभूव ह॥
en: Meanwhile, the sacrifice with the sacred fire of burning flames was commenced and it is went on. Brahman was pouring libations on the fire. While thus engaged, the Grandfather became worked up with desire.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: स्कन्नमात्रं च तच्छुक्रं स्रवेण परिवृज्ञ सः। आज्यवन्मन्त्रतश्चापि सोऽजूहांद् भृगुनन्दन॥
en: As soon as the seed came out, he took it up with the sacrificial ladle and poured it as a libation of clarified butter, O delighter of the Bhrigus with the necessary Mantras, on the burning fire.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ततः स जनयामास भूतग्रामं च वीर्यवान्। तस्य तत् तेजसस्तस्माज्जज्ञे लोकेषु तैजसम्॥
en: From that seed, Brahman of great power caused the four orders of creatures to come into being. That seed of the Grandfather was endued with the three qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance. From that element in it which represented the quality of Goodness, sprang all mobile creatures gifted with the principle of action.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तमसस्तामसा भावा व्यापि सत्त्वं तथोभयम्। स गुणस्तेजसो नित्यस्तस्य चाकाशमेव च॥
en: From the element of Ignorance in it. sprang all immobile creatures. The quality of Goodness, however, which lived in that seed, entered both kinds of existence. That quality of Goodness is of the nature of Light. It is eternal and of it is unending Space.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: सर्वभूतेषु च तथा सत्त्वं तेजस्तथोत्तमम्। शुक्रे हुतेऽग्नौ तस्मिंस्तु प्रादुरासंस्त्रयः प्रभो॥
en: In all the creatures the quality of Goodness is present and is at one with that light which shows what is right and what is wrong. When the seed of Brahman was thus poured as a libation on that sacrificial fire, there came from it, O powerful one, three beings into existence.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: पुरुषा वपुषा युक्ताः स्वैः स्वैः प्रसवजैर्गुणैः। भृगित्येव भृगुः पूर्वमङ्गारेभ्योऽङ्गिराभवत्॥
en: They were three male persons, gifted with bodies that partook of the nature of the circumstances from which they respectively originated. One arose first from the fire (called Bhrik) and hence he passed by the name of Bhrigu. A second came from the burning charcoals and hence he passed the name of Angirasa.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अङ्गारसंश्रयाच्चैव कविरित्यपरोऽभवत्। सह ज्वालाभिरुत्पन्नो भृगुस्तस्माद् भृगुः स्मृतः।।१०६
en: The third originated from a heap of extinguished charcoals and he passed by the name of Kavi. It has been already said that the first came out with flames issuing from his body and hence he was called Bhrigu,

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: मरीचिभ्यो मरीचिस्तु मारीचः कश्यपो ह्यभूत्। अङ्गारेभ्योऽङ्गिरास्तात वालखिल्याः कुशोच्चयात्।।
en: From the rays of the sacrificial fire originated another called Marichi. From Marichi (afterwards) sprang Kashyapa. It has been already said that from the (burning) charcoals originated Angiras. The dwarf Rishis called Valikhillyas originated from the blades of Kusha grass spread out in that sacrifice.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अत्रैवानेति च विभो जातमत्रिं वदन्त्यपि। तथा भस्मव्यपोहेभ्यो ब्रह्मर्षिगणसम्मताः॥ वैखानसाः समुत्पन्नास्तप:श्रुतगुणेप्सवः। अश्रुतोऽस्य समुत्पन्नावश्विनौ रूपसम्मतौ॥ शेषाः प्रजानां पतयः स्रोतोभ्यस्तस्य जज्ञिरे।
en: From the same blades of Kusha grass, O you of great power originated Atri. From the ashes of the fire originated the twiceborn Rishis, viz., the Vaikhanashas, endued with penances and given to Vedic learning and all of excellent qualities. From the eyes of Agni originated the twin Ashvins endued with great beauty. At last, from his ears, originated the Prajapatis.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ऋषयो रोमकूपेभ्यः स्वेदाच्छन्दो बलान्मनः॥ एतस्मात् कारणादाहरग्निः सर्वास्तु देवताः। ऋषयः श्रुतसम्पन्ना देवप्रामाण्यदर्शनात्॥ यानि दारुणि निर्यासास्ते मासाः पक्षसंज्ञिताः। अहोरात्रा मुहूर्ताश्च पित्तं ज्योतिश्च दारुणम्॥ रौद्रं लोहितमित्याहुलॊहितात् कनकं स्मृतम्। तन्मैत्रमिति विज्ञेयं धूमाच्च वसवः स्मृताः॥ अर्चिषो याच ते रुद्रास्तथाऽऽदित्या महाप्रभाः। उद्दिष्टास्ते तथाङ्गारा ये धिष्ण्येषु दिवि स्थिताः।।११४
en: The Rishis originated the pores of Agni's body. From his sweat originated Chhandas, and from his strength originated Mind. Therefore Agni has been said to be all the celestials in his individual self, by Rishis endued with Vedic learning, guided by the authority of the Vedas. The pieces of wood that keep alive the flumes of Agni are considered as the Months. The juices the fuel yields form the Fortnights. . The liver of Agni is called the Day and Night, and his fierce light is called the Muhurtas, The blood of Agni is considered as the source of the Rudras. From his blood originated the goldhued celestials called the Maitradevatas. . From his smoke originated the Vasus. From his flames originated the Rudras as also the (twelve) Adityas of great effulgence. . The Planets and Constellations and other stars that have been set in their respective orbits in the sky, are considered as the (burning) charcoals of Agni.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: आदिकर्ता च लोकस्य तत्परं ब्रह्म तध्रुवम्। सर्वकामदमित्याहुस्तद्रहस्यमुवाच ह॥ ततोऽब्रबीन्महादेवो वरुणः पवनात्मकः। मम सत्रमिदं दिव्यमहं गृहपतिस्त्विह॥ त्रीणि पूर्वाण्यपत्यानि मम तानि न संशयः। इति जानीत खगमा मम यज्ञफलं हि तत्॥
en: The first Creator of the universe declared Agni to be Supreme Brahma and Eternal, and the giver of all desires. This is indeed, a mystery, After all these births had taken place, Mahadeva who had assumed the form of Varuna (for his sacrifice) and who had Pavana for his soul, said, This excellent Sacrifice is minc. I am the Grahapati in it. The three beings that first originated from the sacrificial fire are mine! Forsooth, they should be considered as my children. Know this, you gods who range through the skies! They are the fruits of this Sacrifice.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: मदङ्गेभ्यः प्रसूतानि मदाश्रयकृतानि च। ममैव तान्यपत्यानि वरुणो दवद्यात्मकः॥
en: "Agni said, These children have originated from my limbs. They have all depended upon me as the cause of their being. They should, therefore, be considered as my children. Mahadeva in the form of Varuna has erred in this matter.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अथाब्रवील्लोकगुरुर्ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः। ममैव तान्यपत्यानि मम शुक्र हुतं हि तत्॥
en: After this, the Master of all the worlds, the Grandfather of all creatures, viz., Brahman, then said, These children are mine! The seed which I poured upon the sacrificial fire was mine.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अहं कर्ता हि सत्रस्य होता शुक्रस्य चैव ह। यस्य बीजं फलं तस्य शुक्रं चेत् कारणं मतम्।।१२०
en: I am the performer of this Sacrifice. I poured on the sacrificial fire, the seed that came out of myself. He who has planted the seed always enjoys the fruit. The principal cause of these births is my seed.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ततोऽब्रुवन् देवगणाः पितामहमुपेत्य वै। कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वे शिरोभिरभिवन्द्य च॥ वयं च भगवन् सर्वे जगच्च सचराचरम्। तवैव प्रसवाः सर्वे तस्मादग्निर्विभावसुः॥ तरुणश्चेश्वरो देवो लभतां काममीप्सितम्। निसर्गाद् ब्रह्मणश्चापि वरुणो यादसाम्पतिः॥ जग्रह वै भृगु पूर्वमपत्यं सूर्यवर्चसम्। ईश्वरोऽङ्गिरसं चाग्नेरपत्यार्थमकल्पयत्॥
en: The celestial went to the Grandfather and having bowed their heads to him and jointed hands in respect, they said to him, All of us, O illustrious one, and the entire universe of mobile and immobilc creatures, are your offspring, O sire, let Agni of burning flames, and the illustrious and powerful Mahadeva who has, for this sacrifice, assumed the form of Varuna, have their wish. At these words, although bom of Brahman, the powerful Mahadeva in the form of Varuna, the king of all aquatic creatures received the firstborn one, viz., Bhrigu effulgent as the Sun, as his own child. The Grandfather then intended that Angirasa should become the son of Agni.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: पितामहस्त्वपत्यं वै कविं जग्राह तत्त्ववित्। तदा स वारुणः ख्यातो भृगुः प्रसवकर्मवित्॥
en: Knowing the truth, the Grandfather then took Kavi as his own son. Busy with procreating creatures for peopling the Earth, Bhrigu who is considered as a Prajapati thence came to be called as Varuna's offspring.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: आग्नेयस्त्वङ्गिराः श्रीमान् कविाह्मो महायशाः। भार्गवाङ्गिरसौ लोके लोकसंतानलक्षणौ॥
en: Gifted with every prosperity, Angirasa passed as the offspring of Agni, and the celebrated Kavi came to be known as the child of Brahman himself. Bhrigu and Angirasa, who had originated from the fire and the charcoals of Agni respectively, became the procreators of extensive races and tribes in the world,

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: एते हि प्रस्रवाः सर्वे प्रजानां पतयस्त्रयः। सर्वं संतानमेतेषामिढमित्युपधारय॥
en: Indeed, these three, viz., Bhrigu and Angirasa and Kavi, considered as Prajapati, are the progenitors of many races and tribes. All are the children of these three. Know this, o powerful hero.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: भृगोस्तु पुत्राः सप्तासन् सर्वे तुल्या भृगोर्गुणैः। च्यवनो वज्रशीर्षश्च शुचिरौर्वस्तथैव च॥ शुक्रो वरेण्यश्च विभुः सवनश्चेति सप्त ते। भार्गवा वारुणाः सर्वे येषां वंशे भवानपि॥
en: Bhrigu beget seven sons all whom became equal to him in merits and qualities. Their names are Chyavana, Vajrashirshan, Suchi, Urva, Shukra, that giver of boons, Vibhu and Savana. These are the seven. They are children of Bhrigu and are hence Bhargavas. They are also called Varunas on account of their ancestor Bhrigu having been adopted by Mahadeva in the form of Varuna. You belong to the race of Bhrigu.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अष्टौ चाङ्गिरसः पुत्रा वारुणास्तेऽप्युदाहताः। बृहस्पतिरुतथ्यश्च पयस्यः शान्तिरेव च॥ घोरो विरूपः संवर्तः सुधन्वा चाष्टमः स्मृतः। एतेऽष्टौ वह्रिजाः सर्वे ज्ञाननिष्ठा निरामयाः॥
en: Angirasa begot eight sons. They also are known as Varunas. Their names are Brihaspati, Utatthya, Payasya, Shanti, Dhira, Virupa, Samvarta, and Sudhanvan the eighth. These eight are considered also as the children of Agni. Freed from every evil, they are devoted to knowledge only.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ब्रह्मणस्तु कवेः पुत्रा वारुणास्तेऽप्युदाहृताः। अष्टौ प्रसवजैर्युक्ता गुणैर्ब्रह्मविदः शुभाः॥
en: The sons of Kavi who was adopted by Brahman himself are also known as Varunas. Eight in number all of them became progenitors of races and tribes. Auspicious by nature, they all knew Brahma.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: कविः काव्यश्च घृष्णुश्च बुद्धिमानूशना तथा। भृगुश्च विरजाश्चैव काशी चोग्रश्च धर्मवित्॥
en: The names of the eight sons of Kavi are Kavi, Kavya, Dhrishnu, Ushanas endued with great intelligence, Bhrigu, Viraja, Kashi, and Ugra knowing every duty.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अष्टौ कविसुता ह्येते सर्वमेभिर्जगत् ततम्। प्रजापतय एते हि प्रजाभागैरिह प्रजाः॥
en: These are the eight sons of Kavi. By them the whole world has been peopled. They are all called Prajapatis, and they have procreated many offspring.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: एवमङ्गिरसश्चैव कवेश्च प्रसवान्वयैः। भृगोश्च भृगुशार्दूल वंशजैः सततं जगत्॥
en: Thus, O chief of Bhrigu's race, has the whole world been peopled with the children of Angirasa, and Kavi and Bhrigu,

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: वरुणश्चादितो विप्र जग्राह प्रभुरीश्वरः। कविं तात भृगुं चापि तस्मात् तौ वारुणो स्मृतौ।।
en: The powerful and supreme Lord Mahadeva in the form of Varuna which he had assumed for this sacrifice had first, О learned Brahmana, adopted both Kavi and Angirasa. Hence, these two are considered as of Varuna.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: जग्राहाङ्गिरसं देवः शिखी तस्माद्हताशनः। तस्मादाङ्गिरसा ज्ञेयाः सर्व एव तदन्वयाः॥
en: After that the eater of sacrificial libations, viz., the god of fire, adopted of Angirasa. Hence, all the children of Angirasa are known as belonging to the race of Agni.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ब्रह्मा पितामहः पूर्वं देवताभिः प्रसादितः। इमे नः संतरिष्यन्ति प्रजाभिर्जगतीश्वराः॥
en: The Grandfather Brahman was, formerly propitiated by all the deities who said to him, Let these lords of the universe save us all.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: सर्वे प्रजानां पतयः सर्वे चातितपस्विनः। त्वत्प्रसादादिमं लोकं तारयिष्यन्ति साम्प्रतम्॥
en: Let all of them become progenitors of offspring. Let all of them become endued with penances. Through your favour, let all these rescue the world.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तथैव वंशकर्तारस्तव तेजोविवर्धनाः। भवेयुर्वेदविदुषः सर्वे च कृतिनस्तथा॥
en: Let them become procreators and extenders of races and tribes and let them increase your power. Let all of them become thorough masters of the Vedas and let them be performers of great deeds.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: देवपक्षचराः सौम्याः प्रजापत्या महर्षयः। आप्नुवन्ति तपश्चैव ब्रह्मचर्ये परं तथा॥
en: Let all of them be friends to the divine cause. Indeed, let all of them become gifted with auspiciousness. Let become founders of extensive races and tribes and let them be great Rishis. Let all of them be gifted with great penances and let all of them be devoted to high celibacy'.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: सर्वे हि वयमेते च तवैव प्रसवः प्रभो। देवानां ब्राह्मणानां च त्वं हि कर्ता पितामह॥
en: All of us, as also all these, are your offspring, O you of great power. You, O Grandfather, are the Creator of both the celestials and the Brahmanas.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: मारीचमादितः कृत्वा सर्वे चैवाथ भार्गवाः। अपत्यानीति सम्प्रेक्ष्य क्षमयाम पितामह॥
en: Marichi is your first offspring. All these also that are called Bhargavas are your progeny. LoO king at this fact, O Grandfather, we shall all help and support one another.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ते त्वनेनैव रूपेण प्रजनिष्यन्ति वै प्रजाः। स्थापयिष्यन्ति चात्मानं युगादिनिधने तथा॥ इत्युक्तः स तदा तैस्तु ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः। तथेत्येवाब्रवीत् प्रीतस्तेऽपि जग्मुर्यथागतम्॥
en: All these shall, thus, multiply their progeny and establish yourself at the beginning of each one after the universal destruction. Thus addressed by them, Brahman, the grandfather of all the worlds, said to them, So be it! I am pleased with you all! Having said so to the celestials, he proceeded to the place he had come from.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: एवमेतत् पुरा वृत्तं तस्य यज्ञे महात्मनः। देवश्रेष्ठस्य लोकादौ वारुणीं बिभ्रतस्तनुम्॥
en: This is what took place in days of your in that sacrifice of the great Mahadeva, that foremost, one of all the celestials, in the beginning of creation, when he for the purposes of his sacrifice had assumed the form of Varuna.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अग्निर्ब्रह्मा पशुपतिः शर्वो रुद्रः प्रजापतिः। अग्नेरपत्यमेतद् वै सुवर्णमिति धारणा॥
en: Agni is Brahman. He is Pashupati. He is Sarva. He is Rudra. He is Prajapati. It is wellknown that gold is the offspring of Agni.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अग्न्यभावे च कुरुते वह्निस्थानेषु काञ्चनम्। जामदग्न्य प्रमाणज्ञो वेदश्रुतिनिदर्शनात्॥
en: When fire is not to be had, gold is used as a substitute. Guided by the marks of the auditions of the Veda, one who is conversant with authorities and who knows the identity of gold with fire, acts thus.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: कुशस्तम्बे जुहोत्यग्निं सुवर्णे तत्र च स्थिते। बल्मीकस्य वपायां च कर्णे वाजस्य दक्षिणे॥ शकटो। परस्याप्सु ब्राह्मणस्य करे तथा। हते प्रीतिकरीमृद्धिं भगवांस्तत्र मन्यते॥
en: Putting a piece of gold on some blades of Kusha grass spread out on the ground, the sacrificer pours libations upon it. If libations are poured upon also the pores of an anthill, upon the right ear of a goat, upon a piece of level earth, upon the waters of a Tirtha, or on the hand of a Brahmana, the illustrious god of fire becomes pleased and considers it as a source of his own advancement as also that of the celestials through his.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तस्मादग्निपराः सर्वे देवता इति शुश्रुम। ब्रह्मणो हि प्रभूतोऽग्निरग्नेरपि च काञ्चनम्॥
en: Hence, it is that we have heard that all the celestials consider Agni as their refuge and are devoted to him. Agni originated from Brahman, and from, Agni originated gold.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तस्माद् ये वै प्रयच्छन्ति सुवर्णे धर्मदर्शिनः। देवतास्ते प्रयच्छन्ति समस्ता इति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: Hence, we have heard that those virtuous persons who make gifts of gold are considered as giving away all the deities.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तस्य चातमसो लोका गच्छतः परमां गतिम्। स्वलॊके राजराज्येन सोऽभिषिच्येत भार्गव॥
en: The man who makes gifts of gold acquires a very high end. Regions of burning effulgence are his. Indeed, O Bhargava, he becomes installed as the king of kings in the celestial region.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: आदित्योदयसम्प्राप्ते विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम्। ददाति काञ्चनं यो वै दुःस्वप्नं प्रतिहन्ति सः॥
en: That person who, at sunrise, makes a gift of gold according to the ordinance and with proper Mantras, succeeds in warding off the evils foreshadowed by ominous dreams.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ददात्युदितमात्रे यस्तस्य पाप्मा विधूयते। मध्याह्ने ददतो रुक्मं हन्ति पापमनागतम्॥
en: The man who, as soon as the Sun has risen, makes a gift of gold becomes purged of all his sins. He who makes a gift of gold at midday destroys all his future sins.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ददाति पश्चिमां संध्या यः सुवर्णे यतव्रतः। ब्रह्मवाय्वग्निसोमानां सालोक्यमुपयाति सः॥
en: He who, with controlled soul, makes a gift of gold at the second twilight succeeds in living with Brahman and the god of wind and Agni and Soma in their respective regions.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: सेन्द्रेषु चैव लोकेषु प्रतिष्ठां विन्दते शुभाम्। इह लोके यशः प्राप्य शान्तपाप्मा च मोदते॥
en: Such a man acquires fame in regions of great happiness that belong to Indra himself. Acquiring great fame in this world also, and purged of all his sins, he sports on joy and happiness.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: ततः सम्पद्यतेऽन्येषु लोकेष्वप्रतिमः सदा। अनावृतगतिश्चैव कामचारो भवत्युत॥
en: Such a man acquires many other regions of happiness and becomes peerless for glory and fame. His course perfectly unobstructed he succeeds in going every where at will.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: न च क्षरति तेभ्यश्च यशैश्चैवाप्नुते महत्। सुवर्णमक्षयं दत्त्वा लोकांश्चाप्नोति पुष्कलान्॥
en: He has never to fall down from the regions which he acquires, and the glory he attains to, becomes very great. Indeed, by making gifts of gold one acquires numberless regions of a happiness all of which he enjoys for good.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: यस्तु संजनयित्वाग्निमादित्योदयनं प्रति। दद्याद् वै व्रतमुद्दिश्य सर्वकामान् समश्नुते॥
en: That man who, having lighted a fire at sunrise, makes gifts of gold in view of the observance of a particular vow, succeeds in acquiring the fruition of all his desires.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: अग्निमित्येव तत् प्राहुः प्रदानं च सुखावहम्। यथेष्टगुणसंवृत्तं प्रवर्तकमिति स्मृतम्॥
en: It has been said that gold is at one with Agni. The gift of gold, therefore, yields great happiness. The gift of gold leads to the possession of those merits and qualities that are desired, and purifies the heart.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: एषा सुवर्णस्योत्पत्तिः कथिता ते मयानघ। कार्तिकेयस्य च विभो तद् विद्धि भृगुनन्दन॥
en: I have thus told you, O sinless one, the origin of gold. O you of power, know how Kartikeya grew up, O delighter of Bhrigu's race.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: कार्तिकेयस्तु संवृद्धः कालेन महता तदा। देवैः सेनापतित्वेन वृतः सैन् गूद्वह॥
en: After a long time Kartikeya grew up. He was then, O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, chosen by all the celestials with Indra at their head, as the commanderinchief of the celestial forces.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: जघान तारकं चापि दैत्यमन्यांस्तथासुरान्। त्रिदशेन्द्राज्ञया ब्राँल्लोकानां हितकाम्यया॥
en: He killed the Daitya Taraka as also many other Asuras, at the command of the king of the celestials, O Brahmana, and moved also by the desire of benefiting all the worlds.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: सुवर्णदाने च मया कथितास्ते गुणा विभो। तस्मात् सुवर्णे विप्रेभ्यः प्रयच्छ ददतां वर॥
en: I have also, O you of great power, described to you the merits of making gifts of gold. Do you, therefore, O foremost of all speakers, make gifts of gold.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तः स वसिष्ठेन जामदग्न्यः प्रतापवान्। ददौ सुवर्णे विप्रेभ्यो व्यमुच्यत च किल्बिषात्॥१६६
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by Vashishtha, Jamadagni's son of great power then made gifts of gold to the Brahmanas and became cleansed of his sins.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं सुवर्णस्य महीपते। प्रदानस्य फलं चैव जन्म चास्य युधिष्ठिर॥
en: I have thus, told you, O king, everything about the merits of the gifts of gold and about its origin also, O Yudhishthira.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तस्मात् त्वमपि विप्रेभ्यः प्रयच्छ कनकं बहु। ददत्सुवर्णे नृपते किल्बिषाद् विप्रमोक्ष्यसि॥
en: Do you also, therefore, make profuse gift of gold to the Brahmanas. Indeed, O king, by making such gifts of gold, you will surely be purged of all you sins.

description: The coloquies of the deities on the subject
sn: तस्मात् त्वमपि विप्रेभ्यः प्रयच्छ कनकं बहु। ददत्सुवर्णे नृपते किल्बिषाद् विप्रमोक्ष्यसि॥
en: Do you also, therefore, make profuse gift of gold to the Brahmanas. Indeed, O king, by making such gifts of gold, you will surely be purged of all you sins.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उक्ताः पितामहेनेह सुर्णस्य विधानतः। विस्तरेण प्रदानस्य ये गुणाः श्रुतिलक्षणाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have, O grandfather described to me fully the merits of the gift of gold according to the ordinances laid down in the scriptures and the Veda.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: यत्तु कारणमुत्पत्तेः सुवर्णस्य प्रकीर्तितम्। स कथं तारकः प्राप्तो निधनं तद् ब्रवीहि मे॥
en: You have also described the origin of gold. Do you tell me now how Taraka met with destruction.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: उक्तं स देवतानां हि अवध्य इति पार्थिव। कथं तस्याभवन्मृत्युर्विस्तरेण प्रकीर्तय॥
en: You have, said, O king, that Asura had become unslayable by the gods. Do you tell me fully how his destruction was brought about.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: एतादिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं त्वत्तः कुरुकुलोद्वह। कात्स्येन तारकवधं परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: Operpetuator of Kuru's race, I wish to hear this from you, I mean the details of Taraka's destruction. Great is my curiosity to hear the narrative.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: भीष्म उवाच विपन्नकृत्या राजेन्द्र देवता ऋषयस्तथा। कृत्तिकाश्चोदयामासुरपत्यभरणाय वै॥
en: Bhishma said The gods and the Rishis, O king reduced to great distress, urged the six Krittikas to rear that child.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: न देवतानां काचिद्धि समर्था जातवेदसः। एता हि शक्तास्तं गर्भं संधारयितुमोजसा॥
en: Amongst the celestial ladies there were none, except these, who could by their power, bear the seed of Agni in their wombs.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: षण्णां तासां ततः प्रीत: पावको गर्भधारणात्। स्वेन तेजोविसर्गेण वीर्येण परमेण च॥
en: The god of fire became highly pleased with those goddesses for their readiness to sustain the conception caused by the seed of Agni which was gifted with his own great power.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: तास्तु षट् कृत्तिका गर्भे पुपुषुर्जातवेदसः। षट्सु वर्त्मसु तेजोऽन्गेः सकलं निहितं प्रभो॥
en: When the energy of Agni, O king, was divided into six parts and placed within the channels, the six Krittikas began to nourish the portion that each held in her womb.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: ततस्ता वर्धमानस्य कुमारस्य महात्मनः। तेजसाभिपरीताङ्ग्यो न क्वचिच्छम लेभिरे॥
en: As the great Kumara, however, began to grow within their wombs their bodies being possessed by his energy, they could not get peace anywhere.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: ततस्तेजःपरीताङ्ग्यः सर्वाः काल उपस्थिते। समं गर्भे सुषुविरे कृत्तिकास्तं नरर्षभ॥
en: Filled with energy as their bodies were, the time at last came for delivery. All of them, it so happened, O prince of men, delivered simultaneously.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: ततस्तं षडधिष्ठानं गर्भमेकत्वमागतम्। पृथिवी प्रतिजग्राह कार्तस्वरसमीपतः॥
en: Though held in six different wombs, yet when all the parts, as they came out, united into one. The goddess Earth held the child, taking it up from a mass of gold.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: स गर्भो दिव्यसंस्थानो दीप्तिमान् पावकप्रभः। दिव्यं शरवणं प्राप्य ववृधे प्रियदर्शनः॥
en: Indeed, the child, possessed of a beautiful form, shone like the god of Fire. Of beautiful features, he began to grow in a charming forest of reeds.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: ददृशुः कृत्तिकास्तं तु बालमर्कसमद्युतिम्। जातस्नेहाच्च सौहार्दात् पुपुषुः स्तन्यविस्रवैः॥
en: The six Krittikas saw that child of theirs loO king like the morning Sun. Filled with affection for him, indeed, loving him very much, they began to rear him with their milk.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: अभवत् कार्तिकेयः स त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे। स्कन्नत्वात् स्कन्दतां प्राप्तो गुहावासाद् गुहोऽभवत्।।
en: On account of his having been born of the Krittikas and reared by them, he was known in the three worlds by the name of Kartikeya. Having originated from the seed which had fallen off from Rudra he was named Skanda, and because of his birth in a solitary forest of reeds he was called Guha.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: ततो देवास्त्रयस्त्रिंशद् दिशश्च सदिगीश्वराः। रुद्रो धाता च विष्णुश्च यमः पूषार्यमा भगः॥ अंशो मित्रश्च साध्याश्च वासवो वसवोऽश्विनौ। आपो वायुर्नभश्चन्द्रो नक्षत्राणि ग्रहा रविः॥ पृथग्भूतानि चान्यानि यानि देवार्पणानि वै। आजग्मुस्तेऽद्भुतुं द्रष्टुं कुमारं ज्वलनात्मजम्॥
en: The thirtythree gods, the points of the compass together with their presiding deities, and Rudra, Dhatri, Vishnu, Yama, Pushan, Aryaman, Bhaga, Angsha Mitra, the Sadhyas, Vasava, the Vasus, the Ashvins, the Waters, the Wind, the Firmament, Chandramas and all the Constellations and the Planets and the Sun, and all the Richs and Samans and Yajushes in their embodied forms, came there to see that wonderful child who was the son of the god of Fire.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: ऋषयस्तुष्टुवुश्चैव गन्धर्वाश्च जगुस्तथा। षडाननं कुमारं तु द्विषडक्षं द्विजप्रियम्॥
en: The Rishis sang hymns of praise and the Gandharvas sang in honour of that child called Kumara of six heads, twelve eyes, and greatly devoted to the Brahmanas.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: पीनांसं द्वादशभुजं पावकादित्यवर्चसम्। शयानं शरगुल्मस्थं दृष्ट्वा देवाः सहर्षिभिः॥ लेभिरे परमं हर्ष मेनिरे चासुरं हतम्। ततो देवाः प्रियाण्यस्य सर्व एव समाहरन्॥
en: His shoulders were broad, and he had twelve arms, and the splendour of his body resembled that of fire and Aditya. As he lay stretched on a clump of heath, the gods with the Rishis, seeing him, became filled with great joy and considered the great Asura as already Killed. The celestials then began to bring him various kinds of toys and articles that could amuse him.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: क्रीडत: क्रीडनीयानि ददुः पक्षिगणाश्च ह। सुपर्णोऽस्य ददौ पुत्रं मयूरं चित्रबर्हिणम्॥
en: As he played like a child, various sorts of toys and birds were given to him. Garuda of excellent feathers gave to him a child of his, viz., a peacock having plumes of variegated colour.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: राक्षसाश्च ददुस्तस्मै वराहमहिषावभौ। कुक्वुटं चाग्निसंकाशं प्रददावरुणः स्वयम्॥
en: The Rakshasas gave to him a boar and a buffalo. Aruna himself gave him cock of fiery splendour.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: चन्द्रमाः प्रददौ मेषमादित्यो रुचिरां प्रभाम्। गवां माता च गा देवी ददौ शतसहस्रशः॥
en: The Moon gave him a sheep, and the Sun gave him some dazzling rays of his. The mother of all kine, viz., Surabhi, gave him kine by hundreds and thousands.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: छागमग्निर्गुणापेतमिला पुष्पफलं बहु। सुधन्वा शकटं चैव रथं चामितकूबरम्॥
en: Agni gave him a goat having many good qualities. Ila gave him profuse flowers and fruits. Sudhanvan gave him a riding chariot and a car of the great Kubera.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: वरुणो वारुणान् दिव्यान् सगजान् प्रददौ शुभान्। सिंहान् सुरेन्द्रो व्याघ्रांश्च द्विपानन्यांश्च पक्षिणः॥ श्वापदांश्च बहून् घोरांश्छत्राणि विविधानि च। राक्षसासुरसंघाश्च अनुजग्मुस्तमीश्वरम्॥
en: Varuna gave him many auspicious and good products of the Ocean, with some elephants. The king of the celestials gave him lions and tigers and pards and various kinds of the birds of the air, and inany terrible beasts of prey and many umbrellas also. Many Rakshasas and Asuras began to follow that powerful child.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: वर्धमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा प्रार्थयामास तारकः। उपायैर्बहुभिर्हन्तुं नाशकच्चापि तं विभुम्॥
en: Seeing the son of Agni grow up, Taraka sought, by various means, to bring about his destruction, but could not do anything to that powerful deity.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: सैनापत्येन तं देवाः पूजयित्वा गुहालयम्। शशंसुर्विप्रकारं तं तस्मै तारककारितम्॥
en: The gods in time invested Agni's son born a solitary forest with the command of their arıy. And they also informed him of the oppressions made upon them by the Asura Taraka.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: स विवृद्धो महावीर्यो देवसेनापतिः प्रभुः। जघानामोघया शक्त्या दानवं तारकं गुहः॥
en: The commanderinchief of the celestial army grew up and became possessed of great energy and power. In time Guha killed Taraka, with his irresistible dart.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: तेन तस्मिन् कुमारेण क्रीडता निहतेऽसुरे। सुरेन्द्रः स्थापितो राज्ये देवानां पुनरीश्वरः॥
en: Indeed, Kumara killed the Asura as easily as if in sport. Having brought about the destruction of Taraka the reestablished the king of the celestials in his sovereignty of the three worlds.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: स सेनापतिरेवाथ बभौ स्कन्दः प्रतापवान्। ईशो गोप्ता च देवानां प्रियकृच्छङ्करस्य च॥
en: Gifted with mighty power, the celestial general shone in beauty and splendour. The powerful Skanda became the protector of the celestials and did what was agreeable to Shankara.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: हिरण्यमूर्तिर्भगवानेष एव च पावकिः। सदा कुमारो देवानां सैनापत्यमवाप्तवान्॥
en: The illustrious son of Pavaka had a golden form. Indeed, Kumara is always the leader of the celestial arms.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: तस्मात् सुवर्णं मङ्गल्यं रत्नमक्षय्यमुत्तमम्। सहजं कार्तिकेयस्य वह्नस्तेजः परं मतम्॥
en: Gold is the powerful energy of the god of fire and was born with Kartikeya. Hence is gold highly sacred, valuable, and excellent and has unending merit.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: एवं रामाय कौरव्य वसिष्ठोऽकथयत् पुरा। तस्मात् सुवर्णदानाय प्रयतस्व नराधिप॥
en: Thus, O son of Kuru's race, did Vasishtha recite formerly this topic to Rama of Bhrigu's race. Do you, therefore, O king of men, try to make gifts of gold.

description: The history of the destruction of Taraka
sn: रामः सुवर्णं दत्त्वा हि विमुक्तः सर्वकिल्विषैः। त्रिविष्टपे महत् स्थानमवापासुलभं नरैः॥
en: By making gifts of gold, Rama became purged of all his sins, and finally acquired a high place in Heaven that is unattainable by other men.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य धर्मात्मन् धर्माः प्रोक्ता यथा त्वया। तथैव मे श्राद्धविधिं कृत्स्नं प्रब्रूहि पार्थिव॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have described to me, you of righteous soul, the duties of the four castes. Do you, similarly, O king, describe to me now all the ordinances regarding the Shraddha.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठरेणैवमुक्तो भीष्मः शान्तनवस्तदा। इमं श्राद्धविधिं कृत्स्नं वक्तुं समुपचक्रमे॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by Yuthishthira, the son of Shantanu began of recite to him the following ritual, consistent with the ordinances, of the Shraddha.

sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणुष्वावहितो राजञ्छ्राद्धकर्मविधिं शुभम्। धन्यं यशस्यं पुत्रीयं पितृयज्ञं परंतप॥
en: Bhishma said Listen, O king, with rapt attention, to me as I describe to you the ritual of the Shraddha. or That ritual is auspicious, laudable, productive of fame and progeny, and is considered as a sacrifice, O scorcher of enemies, in honour of the departed Manes.

sn: देवासुरमनुष्याणां गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम्। पिशाचकिन्नराणां च पूज्या वै पितरः सदा॥
en: Gods or Asuras human beings, Gandharvas or Uragas or Rakshasas, Pishachas or Kinnaras, every one should always adore the departed Manes.

sn: पितॄन् पूज्यादितः पश्चाद्देवतास्तर्पयन्ति वै। तस्मात् तान् सर्वयज्ञेन पुरुषः पूजयेत् सदा॥
en: It is seen that people adore the departed Manes first, and please the celestials next by offering them their worship. Hence, one should always adore the departed Manes with every care.

sn: अन्वाहार्ये महाराज पितॄणां श्राद्धमुच्यते। तस्माद् विशेषविधिना विधिः प्रथमकल्पितः॥
en: It is said, O king, that the Shraddha perforined in honour of the departed Manes is performable afterwards. But this general rule has a special restraint.

sn: सर्वेष्वहःसु प्रीयन्ते कृते श्राद्धे पितामहाः। प्रवक्ष्यामि तु ते सर्वास्तिथ्यातिथ्यगुणागुणान्॥
en: The (deceased) grandfather become gratified with the Shraddha that may be performed on any day. I shall, however, tell you now what the merits and demerits are of the respective lunar days.

sn: येष्वहःसु कृतैः श्राद्धैर्यत् फलं प्राप्यतेऽनघ। तत् सर्वे कीर्तयिष्यामि यथावत् तन्निबोध मे॥
en: I shall describe to you, O sinless one, what fruits are attained on what days by performing the Shraddha. Do you listen to me with rapt attention.

sn: पितॄनगे प्रतिपदि प्राप्नुयात् सुगृहे स्त्रियः। अभिरूपप्रजायिन्यो दर्शनीया बहुप्रजाः॥
en: By worshipping the departed Manes on the first day of the light fortnight, one obtains in his abode beautiful wives capable of producing many children all endued with desirable accomplishments.

sn: स्त्रियो द्वितीयां जायन्ते तृतीयायां तु वाजिनः। चतुर्थ्यो क्षुद्रपशवो भवन्ति बहवो गृहे॥
en: By performing the Shraddha on the second day of the light fortnight, one gets many daughters. By performing on the third day, one acquires many horses. By performing it on the fourth day, one gets a large herd of smaller arimals in his house.

sn: पञ्चम्यां बहवः पुत्रा जायन्ते कुर्वतां नृप। कुर्वाणास्तु नराः षष्ठ्यां भवन्ति द्युतिभागिनः॥
en: They, O king, who perform the Shraddha on the fifth day, get many sons. Those men who perform the Shraddha on the sixth day, acquire great splendour.

sn: कृषिभागी भवेच्छ्राद्धं कुर्वाण: सप्तमी नृप। अष्टम्यां तु प्रकुर्वाणो वाणिज्ये लाभमाप्नुयात्॥
en: By performing it on the seventh day, O king, one wins great fame. By performing it on the eighth day one, secures great profits in commercial pursuits.

sn: नवम्यां कुर्वतः श्राद्धं भवत्येकशफं बहु। विवर्धन्ते तु दशमी गावः श्राद्धान् विकुर्वतः॥
en: By performing it on the ninth day, one, acquires many animals of uncloven hoofs. By performing it on the tenth day, one acquires many valuable kine.

sn: कुप्यभागी भवेन्मर्त्यः कुर्वन्नेकादशीं नृप। ब्रह्मवर्चस्विनः पुत्रा जायन्ते तस्य वेश्मनि॥
en: By performing it on the eleventh day one gets valuable cloths and utensils. Such a man also gets many sons all of whom become endued with Brahma splendour.

sn: द्वादश्यामीहमानस्य नित्यमेव प्रदृश्यते। रजतं बहुवित्तं च सुवर्णं च मनोरमम्॥
en: By performing the Shraddha on the twelfth day, one always sees if he desires various sorts of beautiful silver and gold articles.

sn: ज्ञातीनां तु भवेच्छेष्ठः कुर्वञ्छ्राद्धं त्रयोदशीम्। अवश्यं तु युवानोऽस्य प्रमीयन्ते नरा गृहे॥ युद्धभागी भवेन्मर्त्यः कुर्वञ्छ्राद्धं चतुर्दशीम्। अमावास्यां तु निर्वापात् सर्वकामानवाप्नुयात्॥
en: on By performing the Shraddha the thirteenth day, one reigns supreme over his kinsmen. Forsooth, all the young men in the family of him who performs the Shraddha on the fourteenth day die. Such a man becomes entangled in war. By performing the Shraddha on the day of the new moon, one gets the fruition of every desire.

sn: कृष्णपक्षे दशम्यादौ वर्जयित्वा चतुर्दशीम्। श्राद्धकर्मणि तिथ्यस्तु प्रशस्ता न तथेतराः॥
en: In the dark fortnight, all the days beginning with the tenth, Icaving only the fourteenth day out, are good days for the performance of the Shraddha. Other days of that fortnight are not SO.

sn: यथा चैवापरः पक्षः पूर्वपक्षाद् विशिष्यते। तथा श्राद्धस्य पूर्वाह्वादपराह्वो विशिष्यते॥
en: Then, again, as the dark fortnight is better than the light one, so the afternoon of the day is better than the forenoon for the Shraddha.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किंस्विद् दत्तं पितृभ्यो वै भवत्यक्षयमीश्वर। किं हविश्चिररात्राय किमानन्त्याय कल्पते॥
en: Yudhishthira said O you of great power, tell me what that object is which if dedicated to the departed Manes, becomes inexhaustible! What Havi, again, (if offered) lasts for all time? What, indeed, is that which becomes eternal?

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: भीष्म उवाच हवींषि श्राद्धकल्पे तु यानि श्राद्धविदो विदुः। तानि मे शृणु काम्यानि फलं चैव युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Bhishma said Hear me, O Yudhishthira, what those Havis are which persons conversant with the ritual of the Shraddha consider as suitable for the Shraddha and what the fruits are of each.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: तिलैब्रीहियवैरिद्धिर्मूलफलैस्तथा। दत्तेन मासं प्रायन्ते श्राद्धेन पितरो नृप॥
en: With sesame seeds, rice, barley, Masha water, root and fruits, if given at Shraddhas, the departed Manes, O king, remain pleased for a month.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: वर्धमानतिलं श्राद्धमक्षयं मनुरब्रवीत्। सर्वेष्वेव तु भोज्येषु तिलाः प्राधान्यतः स्मृताः॥
en: Manu has said that if a Shraddha is performed with profuse sesame, such Shraddha becomes inexhaustible. Of all sorts of food, sesame seeds are considered as the best.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: द्वौ मासौ तु भवेत्तृप्तिर्मत्स्यैः पितृगणस्य ह। त्रीन्मासानाविकेनाहुश्चतुर्मासं शशेन ह॥
en: With fishes offered at Shraddhas, the departed Manes remain pleased for two months. With mutton they remain pleased for three months and with the flesh of the hare for four.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: आजेन मासान्ग्रीयन्ते पञ्चैव पितरो नृप। वाराहेण तु षण्मासान् सप्त वै शाकुलेन तु॥
en: With the flesh of the goat, o king, they remain pleased for five months, with becon for six months, and with the flesh of birds for seven.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: मासानष्टौ पार्षतेन रौरवेण नव प्रभो। गवयस्य तु मांसेन तृप्तिः पितॄणां माहिषेण तु॥
en: With venison got from those deer that are called Prishata, they remain pleased for eight months, and with that obtained from the Ruru for nine months, and with the meat of the Gavaya for ten months.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: गव्येन दत्तं श्राद्धे तु संवत्सरमिहोच्यते। यथा गव्यं तथा युक्तं पायसं सर्पिषा सह॥ वाध्रीणसस्य मांसेन तृप्ति दशवार्षिकी॥
en: With the meat of the buffalo they remain pleased for eleven months. With beef presented at the Shraddha, they remain pleased for a full year. Payas mixed with clarified butter is as much as acceptable to the departed Manes as beef. With the meat of the Vadhrinasa the Pitris remained pleased for twelve years.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: आनन्याय भवेद्दत्तं खङ्गमांसं पितृक्षये। कालशाकं च लौहं चाप्यानन्त्यं छाग उच्यते।
en: The flesh of the Rhinoceros, offered to the departed Manes on the anniversaries of the lunar days on which they died, becomes endless. The potherb called Kalashaka, the petals of the Kanchana flower, and meat of the goat also, thus offered, prove inexhaustible.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: गाथाश्चाप्यत्र गायन्ति पितृगीता युधिष्ठिर। सनत्कुमारो भगवान् पुरा मय्यभ्यभाषत॥
en: Regarding it, O Yudhishthira, there are some Verses, originally sung by the departed Manes, that are now sung (in the world). Sanatkumara communicated them to me former days.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: अपि नः स्वकुले जायाद् यो नो दद्यात्त्रयोदशीम्। मधासु सर्पिःसंयुक्तं पायसं दक्षिणायने॥
en: He who has taken birth in our race, should give us Payasa mixed with clarified butter on the thirteenth day (of the dark fortnight), under the constellation Magha, during the Sun's southward course.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: आजेन वापि लौहेन मघास्वेव यतव्रतः। हस्तिच्छायासु विधिवत् कर्णव्यजनवीजितम्॥
en: One born in our race, should under the constellation Magha, as if in the observance of a vow, offer the meat of goat or the petals of the Kanchana flower. One should also offer us, with due rites, Payasa mixed with clarified butter, dedicating it on a spot covered by the shadow of an elephant.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: एष्टव्या बहवः पुत्रा योकोऽपि गयां व्रजेत्। यनासौ प्रथितो लोकेष्वक्षय्यकरणो वटः॥
en: Many sons should be coveted so that even one may go to Gaya, where stands the banian that is celebrated over all the worlds and that makes all offerings made under its branches endless.

description: Eternal gifts to the departed manes
sn: आपो मूलं फलं मांसम्मनं वापि पितृक्षये। यत् किंचिन्मधुसम्मिश्रं तदानन्त्याय कल्पते।॥
en: Even a little of water, roots, fruits, meat, and rice, mixed with honey, if offered on the anniversary of the day of death, becomes endless.

sn: भीष्म उवाच यमस्तु यानि श्राद्धानि प्रोवाच शशविन्दवे। तानि मे शृणु काम्यानि नक्षत्रेषु पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: Bhishma said Hear me, O Yudhishthira, as I tell you what those optional Shraddhas are that should be performed under the different constellations and that were first spoken of by Yama of king Shashabindu.

sn: श्राद्धं यः कृत्तिकायोगे कुर्वीत सततं नरः। अग्नीनाधाय सापत्यो यजेत विगतज्वरः॥
en: That man who always perforins the Shraddha under the constellation Krittika, is considered as performing a sacrifice after establishing the sacred fire. Such a person, freed from fever, goes to Heaven with his children.

sn: अपत्यकामो रोहिण्यां तेजस्कामो मृगोत्तमे। क्रूरकर्मा ददच्छ्राद्धमार्द्रायां मानवो भवेत्॥
en: He who is desirous of children should perform the Shraddha under the constellation Rohini, while he who is desirous of power should do it under the constellation Mrigashiras. By performing the Shraddha under the constellation Ardra, a man becomes the doer of terrific deeds.

sn: धनकामो भवेन्मर्त्यः कुर्वञ्छ्राद्धं पुनर्वसौ। पुष्टिकामोऽथ पुष्येण श्राद्धमीहेत मानवः॥
en: A man, by performing the Shraddha under Punarvasu, makes much gain by agriculture. The man who is desirous of growth and advancement should perform the Shraddha under Pushya.

sn: आश्लेषायां ददच्छ्राद्धं धीरान् पुत्रान् प्रजायते। ज्ञातीनां तु भवेच्छ्रेष्ठो मघासु श्राद्धमावपन्॥
en: By doing it under the constellation Ashlesha one begets heroic children. By doing it under the Maghas onc gains superiority over kinsmen.

sn: फल्गुनीषु ददच्छ्राद्धं सुभगः श्राद्धदो भवेत्। अपत्यभागुत्तरासु हस्तेन फलभाग् भवेत्॥
en: By doing it under the (prior) Phalgunis, one gains good fortune. By doing the Shraddha under the later Phalgunas one gets many children; while by performing it under Hasta, one gets the fruition of his wishes.

sn: चित्रायां तु ददच्छ्राद्धं लभेद् रूपवतः सुतान्। स्वातियोगे पितॄनर्च्य वाणिज्यमुपजीवति॥
en: By performing it under the constellation Chitra one gets beautiful children. By doing it under the constellation Svati, one makes much profit by trade.

sn: बहुपुत्रो विशाखासु पुत्रमीहन् भवेन्नरः। अनुराधासु कुर्वाणो राजचक्र प्रवर्तयेत्॥
en: The man who desires children, acquires the fruition of his desire by performing the Shraddha under the constellation Vishakha. By doing it under Anuradha, one becomes an Emperor.

sn: आधिपत्यं व्रजेन्मयो ज्येष्ठायामपवर्जयन्। नरः कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ ऋद्धो दमपुरःसरः॥
en: By making offerings in honour of the departed Manes Manes under the constellation Jeshthya, with devotion and humility, one acquires sovereignty, O foremost one of Kuru's race.

sn: मूले त्वारोग्यमृच्छेत यशोऽऽषाढासु चोत्तमम्। उत्तरासु त्वषाढासु वीतशोककश्चरेन्महीम्॥
en: By doing the Shraddha under Mula, one gains health, and by doing it under the prior Ashada, one acquires excellent fame. By performing it under the later Ashada, one succeeds in travelling over the whole world, freed from every sorrow.

sn: श्राद्धं त्वभिजिता कुर्वन् भिषक्सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात्। श्रवणेषु ददच्छ्राद्धं प्रेत्य गच्छेत् स सद्गतिम्॥
en: By doing it under the constellation Abhijit, one acquires great knowledge. By doing it under Shravana, one, after death, attains to a very high end.

sn: राज्यभागी धनिष्ठायां भवेत नियतं नरः। नक्षत्रे वारुणे कुर्वन् भिषक्सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: The man who performs the Shraddha under the constellation Dhanistha becomes a king. By doing it under the constellation presided over by Varuna (viz., Shatavisha), one becomes a successful physician.

sn: पूर्वप्रोष्ठपदाः कुर्वन् बहून् विन्दत्यजाविकान्। उत्तरासु प्रकुर्वाणो विन्दते गाः सहस्रशः॥
en: By performing the Shraddha under the constellation of the prior Bhadrapada, one acquires many goats and sheep: while by doing it under the later Bhadrapada, one acquires thousands of kine.

sn: बहुकुप्यकृतं वित्तं विन्दते रेवतीं श्रितः। अश्विनीष्वश्वान् विन्देत भरणीष्वायुरुत्तमम्॥
en: By performing the Shraddha under the constellation Revati, one acquires many utensils of white brass and copper. By doing it under Ashvini, one acquires many horses, while under Bharani, one live long.

sn: इमं श्राद्धविधिं श्रुत्वा शशबिन्दुस्तथाकरोत्। अक्लेशेनाजयच्चापि मही सोऽनुशशास ह॥
en: Listening to these ordinances about the Shraddha king Shashabindu acted accordingly, and succeeded in easily conquering and ruling the whole Earth.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कीदृशेभ्यः प्रदातव्यं भवेच्छ्राद्धं पितामह। द्विजेभ्यः कुरुशार्दूल तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said. You should, O foremnost one of Kuru's race, tell me to what kind of Brahmanas, O grandfather, should the offers made at Shraddhas, be given away.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: भीष्म उवाच ब्राह्मणान् न परीक्षेत क्षत्रियो दानधर्मवित्। दैवे कर्मणि पित्र्ये तु न्यायमाहुः परीक्षणम्॥
en: Bhishma said The Kshatriya who is conversant with the ordinances about gift, should never examine Brahmanas. In all matters, however, relating to the worship of the deities and the departed Manes, an examination has been said to be proper.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: देवताः यूजयन्तीह दैवेनैवेह तेजसा। उपेत्य तस्माद् देवेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यो दापयेन्नरः॥
en: The deities are adored on Earth by men only when they are filled with devotion originating from the celestials themselves. Hence, one should, approaching them, make gifts to all Brahmanas, respecting such gifts as are made to the celestial themselves.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: श्राद्धे त्वथ महाराज परीक्षेद् ब्राह्मणान् बुधः। कुलशीलवयोरूपैर्विद्ययाभिजनेन च॥
en: In Shraddhas, however, O king, the man of intelligence should examine the Brahmanas. Such examination should be about their birth, conduct, age, appearance, and learning.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: तेषामन्ये पङ्क्तिदूषास्तथान्ये पङ्क्तिपावनाः। अपाङ्क्तेयास्तु ये राजन् कीर्तयिष्यामि तान् शृणु॥
en: Amongst the Brahmanas there are some who pollute the line and some who purify it. Listen to me, O king, as I tell you those Brahmanas are that should be excluded from the line.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: कितवो भ्रूणहा यक्ष्मी पशुपालो निराकृतिः। ग्रामप्रेष्यो वार्धषिको गायनः सर्वविक्रयी।॥ अगारदाही गरदः कुण्डाशी सोमविक्रयी। सामुद्रिको राजभृत्यस्तैलिकः कूटकारकः॥ पित्रा विवदमानश्च यस्य चोपपतिहे। अभिशस्तस्तथा स्तेनः शिल्पं यश्चोपजीवति॥ पर्वकारच सूची च मित्रधुक पारदारिकः। अवतानामुपाध्यायः काण्डपृष्ठस्तथैव च॥ श्वभिश्च यः परिक्रामेद् यः शुना दष्ट एव च। परिवित्तिश्च यश्च स्याद् दुश्चर्मा गुरुतल्पगः॥ कुशीलवो देवलको नक्षत्रैर्यश्च जीवति। ईदृशैर्ब्राह्मणैर्भुक्तमपाङ्क्तेयैर्युधिष्ठिर।॥ रक्षांसि गच्छते हव्यमित्याहुर्ब्रह्मवादिनः।
en: He who is wily, or he who is guilty of foeticide, or he who is ill of consumption, or he who keeps animals, or he who has no Vedic study, or is a common servant of a village, or lives upon usury, or he who is a singer, or he who sells all articles, or he who is guilty of arson, or he who is a poisoner, or he who is a pimp by profession, or he who sells Soma, or he who teaches palmistry, or he who is in the employ of the king, or he who is a seller or oil, or he who is a cheat and false swearer, or he who has quarrel with his father, or he who tolerates a paramour of his wife, or he who has been cursed, or he who is a theif, or he who lives by some mechanical art, or he who puts on disguises, or he who is deceitful in his conduct, or he who is hostile to those he calls his friends, or he who is an adulterer, or he who is a preceptor of Shudras, or he who has taken up the profession of arms, or he who wanders with dogs (for hunting), or he who has been bit by a dog, or he who has married before his older brothers, or he who scems to have undergone circumcision, he who violates the bed of his preceptor, he who is an actor or mime, he who lives by setting up an idol, and he who lives by calculating the conjunctions of stars and planets and asterisms, are considered as fit to be excluded from the line. Persons knowing the Vedas say that the offerings made at Shraddhas, if eaten by such Brahmanas, jo to fill the stomachs of Rakshasas, O Yudhishthira.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: श्राद्धं भुक्त्वा त्वधीयीत वृषलीतल्पगश्च यः॥ पुरीषे तस्य ते मासं पितरस्तस्य शेरते। सोमविक्रयिणे विष्ठा भिषजे पूयशोणितम्॥
en: That person who having eaten at a Shraddha does not abstain that day from Vedic studies, or who has known that day a Shudra woman, must know that his departed Manes on account of such deeds of his, have to lie for a month on his own excreta.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: नष्टं देवलके दत्तमप्रतिष्ठं च वाधुषे। यत्तु वाणिजके दत्तं नेह नामुत्र तद् भवेत्॥ भस्मनीव हुतं हव्यं तथा पौनर्भवे द्विजे। ये तु धर्मव्यपेतेषु चारित्रापगतेषु च। हव्यं कव्यं प्रयच्छन्ति तेषां तत्प्रेत्य नश्यति॥
en: The offerings made at Shraddhas if presented to a Brahmana who sells wine, become converted into human excreta; if presented to a Brahmana who practises as a physician, they become converted into puss and blood; if presented to one who lives by setting up an idol, they fail to produce any fruit; if presented to one who lives upon usury, they lead to infamy; if presented to one who is engaged in trade, they become productive of no fruits cither in this world or in the next. If presented to a Brahmana who is born of a widowed mother, they become as fruitless as libations poured on ashes.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: ज्ञानपूर्वं तु ये तेभ्यः प्रयच्छन्त्यल्पबुद्धयः। पुरीषं भुञ्जते तेषां पितरः प्रेत्य निश्चयः॥
en: They who present the Havya and Kavya to such Brahmanas who do not perform the duties ordained for them and who do not observe those rules of good conduct that persons of their order should observe, find such presents productive of no merits hereafter.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: एतानिमान् विजानीयादपाङ्क्तेयान् द्विजाधमान्। शूद्राणामुपदेशं च ये कुर्वन्त्यल्पचेतसः॥
en: That littlewitted man who makes gifts of such articles to such men knowing their dispositions, obliges, by such conduct, his departed Manes to eat human excreta in the next world.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: षष्टिं काणः शतं षण्ढः श्वित्री यावत्प्रपश्यति। पड्क्त्यां समुपविष्टायां तावद् दूषयते नृप॥
en: You should know that these wretched Brahmanas deserve to be excluded from the line. Those Brahmanas also of little energy who are engaged in instructing Shudras belong to the same class.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: यद् वेष्टितशिरा भुङ्क्ते यद् भुङ्क्ते दक्षिणामुखः। सोपानत्कश्च यद् भुङ्क्ते सर्वे विद्यात् तदासुरम्॥
en: A Brahmana who is blind stains sixty individuals of the line, one who is destitute of manly powers stains a hundred; while one who is afflicted with white leprosy stains as many as he looks upon, O king.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: असूयता च यद् दत्तं यच्च श्रद्धाविवर्जितम्। सर्वं तदसुरेन्द्राय ब्रह्मा भागमकल्पयत्॥
en: Whatever offerings made at Shraddhas are eaten by one with his head wrapped round with a cloth, whatever is eaten by one with face southwards, and whatever is eaten with shoes or sandals on, all goes to please the Asuras.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: श्वानश्च पतिदूषाश्च नावेक्षेरन् कथंचन। तस्मात् परिसृते दद्यात् तिलांश्चान्ववकीरयेत्॥
en: Whatever, again is given with malice, and whatever is given without respect, have been ordained by Brahman himself as the portion of the king of Asuras (viz., Bali.)

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: तिलैर्विरहितं श्राद्धं कृतं क्रोधवशेन च। यातुधानाः पिशाचाश्च विप्रलुम्पन्ति तद्धविः॥
en: Dogs, and such Brahmanas as are polluters of lines, should not be suffered to look upon the offerings made at Shraddhas performed at a place that is properly hedged around or concealed from the view. That spot should also be covered with sesame seeds.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: अपाक्तो यावतः पाङ्क्तान् भुजानानुपश्यति। तावत्फलाद् भ्रंशयति दातारं तस्य बालिशम्॥
en: That Shraddha which is done without sesame seeds, or that which is done by a person in anger, has its Havi robbed by Rakshasas and Pishachas.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: इमे तु भरतश्रेष्ठ विज्ञेयाः पङ्क्तिपावनाः। ये त्वतस्तान् प्रवक्ष्यामि परीक्षस्वेह तान् द्विजान्।।२४
en: According to the number of Brahmanas seen by one who deserves to be excluded from the line, is the loss of merit he causes of the foolish perforiner of the Shraddha who invites him to the feast.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: विद्यावेदव्रतस्नाता ब्राह्मणाः सर्व एव हि। सदाचारपराश्चैव विज्ञेयाः सर्वपावनाः॥ पातेयांस्तु प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञेयास्ते पतितपावनाः। त्रिणाचिकेत: पञ्चाग्निस्त्रिसुपर्णः षडङ्गवित्॥ ब्रह्मदेयानुसंतानश्छन्दोगो ज्येष्ठसामगः। मातापित्रोर्यश्च वश्यः श्रोत्रियो दशपूरुषः॥ ऋतुकालाभिगामी च धर्मपत्नीषु यः सदा। वेदविद्याव्रतस्नातो विप्रः पङ्क्तिं पुनात्युत॥
en: I shall now, O chief of Bharata's race, tell you who are purifiers of the line. Do you find them out by examination. All those Brahmanas who are purified by knowledge, Vedic study, vows and observances and they who are of good and righteous conduct, should be known as purifiers of everything. I shall now tell you who deserve to sit in the line. You should know them to be such whom I shall mark out presently. He who is conversant with the three Nachiketas, he who has set up the five sacrificial fires, he who knows the five Suparnas, he who knows the six branches (called Angas) of the Veda, he who is a descendant of fathers who were engaged in teaching the Vedas and is himself engaged in teaching, he who is well conversant with the Prosody, he who is acquainted with the Jeshthya Saman, he who is obedient to his parents, he who is conversant with the Vedas, and whose ancestors have been so for ten generations, he who knows only his married wives and this at their seasons, and he who has been purified by knowledge, by the Veda, and by vows and observances, even such a Brahmana, purifies the line.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: अथर्वशिरसोऽध्येता ब्रह्मचारी यतव्रतः। सत्यवादी धर्मशीलः स्वकर्मनिरतश्च सः॥ ये च पुण्येषु तीर्थेषु अभिषेककृतश्रमाः। मखेषु च समन्त्रेषु भवन्त्यवभृथप्लुताः॥ अक्रोधना ह्यचपलाः क्षान्ता दान्ता जितेन्द्रियाः। सर्वभूतहिता ये च श्राद्धेष्वेतान् निमन्त्रयेत्॥ एतेषु दत्तमक्षय्यमेते वै पङ्क्तिपावनाः। इमे परे महाभागा विज्ञेयाः पङ्क्तिपावनाः॥
en: He who reads the Atharvashiras, who is given to the observance of Brahmacharya practices, and who is steady in the observance of righteous vows, who is truthful and of pure conduct, and who duly satisfies the duties laid down for his order, they also who have undergone fatigue and labour for bathing in the sacred waters, who have done the final bath after celebrating sacrifices sacrifices with proper Mantras, who are freed from anger, who are not restless, who are endued with forgiveness, who are self controlled masters of their senses, and they who are devoted to the behoof of all creatures, these should be invited to Shraddhas. arent HTATET EN: Partaga:1

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: ये चेतिहासं प्रयता: श्रावयन्ति द्विजोत्तमान्॥
en: Anything given to these, becomes endless. These, indeed, are purifiers of lines. There are others also, highly blessed, who should be considered as purifiers of the line.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: ये च भाष्यविदः केचिद् ये च व्याकरणे रताः। अधीयते पुराणं ये धर्मशास्त्राण्यथापि च॥
en: They are are Yatis and those who are conversant with the religion of Emancipation, and they who are devoted to Yoga and they who properly observe excellent vows, and they who, with collected mind, recite (sacred) histories to fcremost of Brahmanas.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: अधीत्य च यथान्यायं विधिवत् तय कारिणः। उपपन्नो गुरुकुले सत्यवादी सहस्रशः॥ अग्र्याः सर्वेषु वेदेषु सर्वप्रवचनेषु च। यावदेते प्रपश्यन्ति पड्क्त्यास्तावत्पुनन्त्युत॥
en: They who conversant with commentaries, they also who are given to grammatical studies, they who study the Puranas and they who study, the Dharmashastras, and having studied them act up to the standard laid down in them, he who has lived in the house of his preceptor, he who if truthful in speech, he who is a giver of thousands, they that are foremost in Vedic lore and (in the knowledge of) the scriptural and are philosophical aphorisms, these purity the lines as far they look at it.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: ततो हि पावनात्पङ्क्त्याः पङ्क्तिपावन उच्यते। क्रोशादर्घतृतीयाच्च पावयेदेक एव हि॥ ब्रह्मदेयानुसंतान इति ब्रह्मविदो विदुः। अनृत्विगनुपाध्यायः स चेदग्रासनं व्रजेत्॥
en: And because they purity all who sit in the line, therefore are they called purifiers of lines. Utterers of Brahma say that even a single person who happens to be the descendant of ancestors who were teachers of the Veda and who is himself a Vedic teacher, purifies full seven miles around him.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: ऋत्विग्भिरभ्यनुज्ञातः पङ्क्त्या हरति दुष्कृतम्। अथ चेद् वेदवित् सर्वैःपङ्क्तिदोषैर्विवर्जितः॥
en: If he who is not a Ritvik and that is not a Vedic teacher takes the foremost seat in a Shraddha, with even the permission of the other Ritviks there present, he is said to take the sins of all who may be sitting in the line.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: न च स्यात् पतितो राजन् पङ्क्तिपावन एव सः। तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन परीक्ष्यामन्त्रयेद् द्विजान्॥
en: If, on the other hand, he happens to be conversant with the Vedas and freed from all those faults which are considered as capable of polluting the line, he shall not, o king, be considered as fallen, Such a man would then be really a purifier of the line.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: स्वकर्मनिरतानन्यान् कुले जातान् बहुश्रुतान्। यस्य मित्रप्रधानानि श्राद्धानि च हवींषि च॥
en: For these reasons, O king, you should properly examine the Brahinanas before inviting them to Shraddhas. You should invite only such among them as are devoted to the duties laid down for their order, and as are born in good families, and as are gifted with great learning.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: यस्य मित्रप्रधानानि श्राद्धानि च हवींषि च। न प्रीणन्ति पितॄन् देवान् स्वर्गं च न स गच्छति।।४१
en: He who performs Shraddhas for feeding only his friends and whose Havi does not please the celestials and the departed Manes, fails to ascend to Heaven.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: यश्च श्राद्ध कुरुते सङ्गत्तानि न देवयानेन पथा स याति। स वै मुक्तः पिप्पलं बन्धनाद् वा स्वर्गाल्लोकाच्च्यवते श्राद्धमित्रः॥ तस्मान्मित्रं श्राद्धकृन्नाद्रियेत दद्यान्मित्रेभ्यः संग्रहार्थं धनानि। यन्मन्यते नैव शत्रु न मित्रं तं मध्यस्थं भोजयेद्धव्यकव्य॥
en: He who collects his friends and relatives only on the occasion of the Shraddha he performs, fails to proceed (after death) by the celestial path. The man who converts the Shraddha he performs, into an occasion for only collecting his friends, never succeeds in ascending to Heaven. The man who converts the Shraddha into an occasion for treating his friends, becomes alienated from Heaven even like a bird dissociated from the perch when the chain tying it breaks.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: न चावता प्राप्नुयाद् बीजभागम्। न चेह नामुत्र फलं ददाति॥
en: Therefore, he who performs a Shraddha should not honour his friends. He may make gifts of riches to them on other occasions by collecting them together. The Havi and the Kavi offered at Shraddhas should be served to them who are neither friends nor enemies but are only indifferent or neutral.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: ब्राह्मणो हनधीयानस्तृणाग्निरिव शाम्यति। तस्मै श्राद्धं न दातव्यं न हि भस्मनि हूयते॥
en: As seed sown on a barren soil does not sprout forth, or as one who has not sown does not get a share of the produce, so that Shraddha the offerings in which are eaten by an unworthy person, yields no fruit either in this : world or in the next.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: सम्भोजनी नाम पिशाचदक्षिणा सा नैव देवान् न पितृनुपैति। इहैव सा भ्राम्यति हीनपुण्या शालान्तरे गौरिव नष्टवत्सा॥
en: That Brahmana who is destitute of Vedic study, is like a fire made by burning grass or straw; and becomes soon put out even like such a fire. The offerings inade at Shraddhas should not be given to him even as libations should not be poured on the ashes of the sacrificial fire.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: यथाग्नौ शान्ते घृतमाजुहोति तन्नैव देवान् न पितृनुपैति। तथा दत्तं नर्तने गायने च यां चानृते दक्षिणामावृणोति॥
en: When the offerings made at Shraddhas are exchanged by the performers with one another, they become Pishacha presents. Such offerings please neither the gods nor the departed Manes, Instead of reaching the other world, they wander about even here like a cow which has lost her calf wandering about within the fold.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: उभौ हिनस्ति न भुनक्ति चैषा या चानृते दक्षिणा दीयते वै। आघातिनी गर्हितैषा पतन्ती तेषां प्रेतान् पातयेद् देवयानात्॥
en: As those libations of clarified butter that are poured upon the extinguished ashes of a sacrificial fire never reach either the gods or the departed Manes, similarly a gift that is inade to a dancer or a singer or a Dakshina presented to a lying or deceitful person, yields no merit.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: ऋषीणां समये नित्यं ये चरन्ति युधिष्ठिर। निश्चिताः सर्वधर्मज्ञास्तान् देवा ब्राह्मणान् विदुः॥४९
en: The present that is given to a lying or deceitful person destroys both the giver and the receiver without benefiting them in any way. Such a present is destructive and highly censurable. The Pitris of the person making it have to fall down form the celestial path.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: स्वाध्यायनिष्ठा ऋषयो ज्ञाननिष्ठास्तथैव च। तपोनिष्ठाश्च बोद्धव्याः कर्मनिष्ठाश्च भारत॥
en: The gods know thein to he Brahmanas who always walk, O Yudhishthira, within the limits set up by the Rishis who know all duties, and who have a firm faith in their efficacy.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: कव्यानि ज्ञाननिष्ठेभ्यः प्रतिष्ठाप्यानि भारत। तत्र ये ब्राह्मणान् केचिन्न निन्दन्ति हि ते नराः॥
en: Those Brahmanas who are given to Vedic study, to knowledge, to penances, and to acts, O Bharata, should be known as Rishis.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: ये तु निन्दन्ति जल्पेषु न ताञ्छ्राद्धेषु भोजयेत्। ब्राह्मणा निन्दिता राजन् हन्युस्त्रैपुरुषं कुलम्॥
en: The offerings made at Shraddhas, should be given to those who are devoted to knowledge. Indeed, they are to be considered as men who never speak ill of the Brahmanas.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: वैखानसानां वचनमृषीणां श्रूयते नृप। दूरादेव परीक्षेत ब्राह्मणान् वेदपारगान्॥
en: Those men should never be fed on occasions of Shraddhas who speak ill of Brahmanas in course of conversation in the midst of conclaves. If Brahmanas, O king, be vilified, they would destroy three generations of the calumniator.

description: A description of Brahmanas to whom offers should be made as the time of Shraddhas
sn: प्रियो वा यदि वा द्वेष्यस्तेषां तु श्राद्धमावपेत्। यः सहस्रं सहस्राणां भोजयेदनृतान् नरः। एकस्तान्मन्त्रवित् प्रीतः सर्वानर्हति भारत॥
en: This is saying, O king, of the Vaikhanasa Rishis. Brahmanas knowing the Vedas should be examined from a distance. Whether one likes them or not, one should give to such Brahmanas the offerings made at Shraddhas. That man who feeds thousands upon thousands of unworthy Brahmanas acquires merit that is attainable by feeding even one Brahmana if the latter happens to be endued with a knowledge of the Vedas, o Bharata!

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच केन संकल्पितं श्राद्धं कस्मिन् काले किमात्मकम्। भृग्वगिरसिके काले मुनिना कतरेण वा॥
en: Yudhishthira said By whom was the Shraddha first conceived and at what time? What also is its substance? In the time when the world was inhabited by only the descendants of Bhrigu and Angirasa who was the Muni who established the Shraddha?

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: कानि श्राद्धानि वानि कानि मूलफलानि च। धान्यजात्यश्च का वास्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: What deeds should not be done at Shraddha? What are those Shraddhas in which fruits and roots are to be offered? What kinds also of paddy should be avoided in Shraddhas? Tell me all this, O grandfather.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: भीष्म उवाच यथा श्राद्धं सम्प्रवृत्तं यस्मिन् काले यदात्मकम्। येन संकल्पितं चैव तन्मे शृणु जनाधिप॥
en: Bhishma said Listen to me, O kine, as I tell you how the Shraddha was introduced, the time of such introduction, the essence of the rite, and the ascetic who conceived it.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: स्वायम्भुवोऽत्रिः कौरव्य परमर्षिः प्रतापवान्। तस्य वंशे महाराज दत्तात्रेय इति स्मृतः॥
en: Form the SelfCreate Brahman sprang Atri, O you of Kuru's race. In Atri's family was born a Muni named Dattatreya.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: दत्तात्रेयस्य पुत्रोऽभून्निमि म तपोधनः। निमेश्चाप्यभवत् पुत्रः श्रीमान्नाम श्रिया वृतः॥
en: Dattatreya got a son named Nimi having asceticism for wealth. Nimi got a son named Shrimat who was gifted with great beauty of person.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रान्ते स कृत्वा दुष्करं तपः। कालधर्मपरीतात्मा निधनं समुपागतः॥
en: Upon the expiration of a full thousand years, Shrimat having practised the practised the severest austerities, yielded to the influence of Time and departed from this world.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: निमिस्तु कृत्वा शौचानि विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा। संतापमगमत् तीवं पुत्रशोकपरायणः॥
en: His father Nimi, having performed the purificatoy rites according to sanctioned rites, because stricken with great grief, thinking continually of the loss of his son.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: अथ कृत्वोपहार्याणि चतुर्दश्यां महामतिः। तमेव गणयशोकं विरात्रे प्रत्यबुध्यत॥
en: Thanking of that cause of sorrow, the great Nimi collected together various agreeable objects on the fourteenth day of the moon. The next morning he rose from bed.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: तस्यासीत् प्रतिबुद्धस्य शोकेन व्यथितात्मनः। मनः संवृत्य विषये बुद्धिर्विस्तारगामिनी॥
en: Stricken as his heart was with grief, as he rose from sleep that day he succeeded in withdrawing it from the one object upon which it had been working. His mind became busy with other matters.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: ततः संचिन्तयामास श्राद्धकल्पं समाहितः। यानि तस्यैव भोज्यानि मूलानि च फलानि च॥ उक्तानि यानि चान्नानि यानि चेष्टानि तस्य ह। तानि सर्वाणि मनसा विनिश्चित्य तपोधनः॥
en: With rapt attention he then conceived the idea of a Shraddha. All those articles of his own fond, containing fruits and roots, and all those kinds of staple grains which he liked, were carefully thought of by that sage having penances for wealth.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: अमावास्यां महाप्राज्ञो विप्रानानाय्या पूजितान्। दक्षिणावर्तिकाः सर्वा बृसीः स्वयमथाकरोत्॥
en: On the day of the New Moon he invited a number of worthy Brahmanas. Gifted with great wisdom, Nimi made them sit on seats and honoured them by going round thein.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: सप्त विप्रांस्ततो भोज्ये युगपत् समुपानयत्। ऋते च लवणं भोज्यं श्यामाकानं ददौ प्रभुः॥
en: Approaching seven such Brahmanas whom he had brought to his house together, the powerful Nimi gave them food consisting of Shyamaka rice, unmixed with salt.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: दक्षिणाग्रास्ततो दर्भा विष्टरेषु निवेशिताः। पादयोश्चैव विप्राणां ये त्वन्नमुपभुञ्जत॥
en: Towards the feet of those Brahmanas engaged in eating the food that was served to them a number of Kusha blades was spread out, on the seats they occupied, with the tops of the blades directed towards the south.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: कृत्वा च दक्षिणाग्रान् वै दर्भान् स प्रयतः शुचिः। प्रददौ श्रीमतः पिण्डान् नामगोत्रमुदाहरन्।॥
en: With a pure body and mind and with rapt attention, Niini, having placed those blades of sacred grass in the way indicated, offered cakes of rice to his dead son, uttering his name and family.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: तत् कृत्वा स मुनिश्रेष्ठो धर्मसंकरमात्मनः। पश्चात्तापेन महता तप्यमानोऽभ्यचिन्तयत्॥
en: Having done this, that foremost of ascetics became filled with regret at the idea of having done a deed that had not been laid down in any of the scriptures. Indeed, filled with regret, he began to think of what he had done.

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: अकृतं मुनिभिः पूर्वं किं मयेदमनुष्ठितम्। कथं नु शापेन न मां दहेयुर्ब्राह्मणा इति॥
en: Never done before by the ascetics, alas, what have I done! How shall I avoid being cursed by the Brahmanas?

description: The history and particular rites of a Shraddha
sn: ततः संचिन्तयामास वंशकर्तारमात्मनः। ध्यातमात्रस्तथा चात्रिराजगाम तपोधनः॥
en: He then thought of the original founder of his race. As soon as he was thought of, Atri having penances for wealth came there.
