sn: नाभाग उवाच अनृतं भाषतु सदा सद्भिश्चैव विरुध्यतु। शुल्केन तु ददत्कन्यां यस्ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Nabhaga said Let him who has stolen your stalks always speak untruth and quarrel with those who are pious. Let him bestow his daughter in marriage after accepting a pecuniary satisfaction offered by his soninlaw.

sn: कविरुवाच पद्भ्यां स गां ताडयतु सूर्ये च प्रतिमेहतु। शरणागतं संत्यजतु यस्ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Kavi said Let him who has stolen your stalks be guilty of striking a cow with his foot. Let him pass urine, facing the sun! Let him renounce the person who seeks shelter at his hands.

sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच करोतु भृतकोऽवर्षं राज्ञश्चास्तु पुरोहितः। ऋत्विगस्तु ह्ययाज्यस्य यस्ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Vishvamitra said Let him who has stolen your stalks become a servant who acts deceitfully towards his master! Let him be the priest of a king! Let him officiate as the sacrificial priest of one who should not be assisted at his sacrifices!

sn: पर्वत उवाच ग्रामे चाधिकृतः सोऽस्तु खरयानेन गच्छतु। शुनः कर्षतु वृत्त्यर्थे यस्ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Parvata said Let him who has stolen your stalks be the head of a village. Let him make journeys on asses. Let him leash hounds for maintenance.

sn: भरद्वाज उवाच सर्वपापसमादानं नृशंसे नानृते च यत्। तत् तस्यास्तु सदा पापं यस्ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Bharadvaja said Let him who has stolen your stalks be guilty of all the transgressions of him who is cruel in conduct and untruthful in speech.

sn: अष्टक उवाच स राजास्त्वकृतप्रज्ञः कामवृत्तश्च पापकृत्। अधर्मेणाभिषास्तूर्वी यस्ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Ashtaka said Let him who has stolen your stalks be a king shorn of wisdom, capricious and sinful in his conduct, and disposed to rule the Earth impiously.

sn: गालव उवाच पापिष्ठेभ्यो ह्यनर्हिः स नरोऽस्तु स्वपापकृत्। दत्त्वा दानं कीर्तयतु यस्ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Galava said Let him who has stolen your stalks be more infamous than a sinful man. Let him be sinful in his deeds towards his kinsmen and relatives. Let him proclaim the gifts he makes to others.

sn: अरुन्धती उवाच श्वश्र्वापवाद वदतु भर्तुर्भवतु दुर्मनाः। एका स्वादु समश्नातु या ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Arundhati said Let her who has stolen your stalks speak ill of her motherinlaw. Let her dislike her husband. Let her eat alone any good food that comes to her house.

sn: बालखिल्या ऊचुः एकपादेन वृत्त्यर्थं ग्रामद्वारे स तिष्ठतु। धर्मज्ञस्त्यक्तधर्मास्तु यस्ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: The Balakhilyas said Let him who has stolen your stalks stand on one foot at the entrance of a village. Let him, while knowing all duties, be guilty of every transgression.

sn: शुनःसख उवाच अग्निहोत्रमनादृत्य स सुखं स्वपतु द्विजः। परिव्राट् कामवृत्तोऽस्तु यस्ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Shunasakha said Let him who has stolen your stalks be a Brahmana who sleeps happily having neglected his daily Homa. Let him, after becoming a religious mendicant, act in any way he likes, without observing any control.

sn: सुरभ्युवाच बालजेन निदानेन कांस्यं भवतु दोहनम्। दुह्यते परवत्सेन या ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Surabhi said Let her who has stolen your stalks be milked, with he, (hind) legs bound with a rope of human hair, and with the help of a calf not her own, and, while milked, let her be held in vessel of white brass.

sn: भीष्म उवाच र्नानाविधैर्बहुभिः कौरवेन्द्र। सहस्राक्षो देवराट् सम्प्रहृष्टः समीक्ष्य तं कोपनं विप्रमुख्यम्॥
en: Bhishma said After the Rishis and the royal sages had taken various oaths, O Kuru king, the thousand eye chief of the celestials, filled with joy, looked at the angry Rishi Agastya.

sn: अथाब्रवीन्मघवा प्रत्ययं स्वं समाभाष्य तमृषि जातरोषम्। ब्रह्मर्षिर्देवर्षिनृपर्षिमध्ये यं तं निबोधेह ममाद्य राजन्॥
en: Addressing the Rishi who was very angry at the disappearance of his lotus stalks, Indra thus declared what was passing in his mind. Hear, O king, the words Indra spoke in the midst of those twiceborn and celestial Rishis and royal sages.

sn: शक्र उवाच अध्वर्यवे दुहितरं ददातु छन्दोगे वा चरितब्रह्मचर्ये। अथर्वणं वेदमधीत्य विप्रः स्नायीत यः पुष्करमाददाति॥
en: Shakra said Let him who has stolen your stalks acquire the merit of him who bestows his daughter in marriage upon a Brahmana who has duly observed the vow of Brahmacharya or who has duly studied the Samans and the Yajushes. Let him also have the merit of one who takes the final bath after completing his study of the Atharva Veda.

sn: सर्वान् वेदानधीयीत पुण्यशीलोऽस्तु धार्मिकः। ब्रह्मणः सदनं यातु यस्ते हरति पुष्करम्॥
en: Let him who has stolen your stalks acquire the mcrit of having studied all the Vedas. Let him be observant of all duties and rightcous in his conduct. Indeed, let him go to the region of Brahman.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच आशीर्वादस्त्वया प्रोक्तः शपथो बलसूदन। दीयतां पुष्करं मह्यमेष धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: Agastya said You have, O destroyer of Vala, uttered a benediction instead of a course. Give them to me, for that is eternal duty.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच न मया भगवॅल्लोभाद्भुतं पुष्करमद्य वै धर्मांस्तु श्रोतुकामेन हतं न क्रोद्भुमर्हसि॥
en: Indra said O holy one, I did not remove your stalks, moved by cupidity. Indeed, I removed them from desire of hearing this assembly recite what the duties are that we should observe. You should not yield to anger.

sn: धर्मश्रुतिसमुत्कर्षो धर्मसेतुरनामयः। आर्षो वै शाश्वतो नित्यमव्ययोऽयं मया श्रुतः॥
en: Duties are the foremost of Shrutis. Duties form the eternal path. I have listened to this discourse of the Rishis (on duties) that is eternal and immutable, and that is above all change.

sn: तदिदं गृह्यतां विद्वन् पुष्करं द्विजसत्तम। अतिक्रमं मे भगवन् क्षन्तुमर्हस्यनिन्दित॥
en: Do you then, foremost of learned Brahmanas, take back these stalks of yours. O holy one, you should forgive my transgression, (you who are free from every fault.

sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तः स महेन्द्रेण तपस्वी कोपनो भृशम्। जग्राह पुष्करं धीमान् प्रसन्नश्चाभवन्मुनिः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by the king of the celestials, the ascetics viz., Agastya, who had been very angry, took back his stalks. Gifted with intelligence, the Rishi became cheerful.

sn: प्रययुस्ते ततो भूयस्तीर्थानि वनगोचराः। पुण्येषु तीर्थेषु तथा गात्राण्याप्लावयन्त ते॥
en: After this, those dwellers of the forest went to various other sacred waters. Indeed, going to those sacred waters they performed their ablutions everywhere.

sn: आख्यानं य इदं युक्तः पठेत् पर्वणि पर्वणि। न मूर्ख जनयेत् पुत्रं न भवेच्च निराकृतिः॥
en: The man who reads this discourse with rapt attention on every Parva day, will not beget an ignorant and wicked son. He will never be shorn of fearing

sn: न तमापत् स्पृशेत् काचिद् विज्वरो न जरावहः। विरजाः श्रेयसा युक्तः प्रेत्य स्वर्गमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: No calamity will ever befall him. He will, besides, be free from every sort of sorrow. He will never suffer from decrepitude and decay. Freed from stains and evil of every sort, and gifted with merit, he is sure to acquire Heaven,

sn: यश्च शास्त्रमधीयीत ऋषिभिः परिपालितम्। स गच्छेद् ब्रह्मणो लोकमव्ययं च नरोत्तम॥
en: He who studies this Shastra observed by the Rishis, is sure, O king, to attain to the eternal region of Brahman that is full of happiness.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यदिदं श्राद्धकृत्येषु दीयते भरतर्षभ। छत्रं चोपानही चैव केनैतत् सम्प्रवर्तितम्॥ कथं चैतत् समुत्पन्नं किमर्थं चैव दीयते। न केवलं श्राद्धकृत्ये पुण्यकेष्वपि दीयते॥ बहुष्वपि निमित्तेषु पुण्यमाश्रित्य दीयते। एतद् विस्तरशो ब्रह्मन् श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O chief of Bharata's race. by whom was the custom of giving umbrellas and sandals at Shraddhas introduced? Why was it introduced and for what purpose are those gifts made? They are given not only at Shraddhas, but also at other religious rites. They are given on many occasions with the view of winning religious merit. I wish to know, in full, O twiceborn one, the true meaning of this practice.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु राजन्नवहितश्छत्रोपानहविस्तरम्। यथैतत् प्रथितं लोके यथा चैतत् प्रवर्तितम्॥
en: Bhishma said Do you, O prince, attentively listen to the details I shall recite about the custom of giving away umbrellas and shocs at religious rites, and as to how and by whom it was introduced.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: यथा चाक्षय्यतां प्राप्तं पुण्यतां च यथा गतम्। सर्वमेतदशेषेण प्रवक्ष्यामि नराधिप॥
en: I shall also tell you in full, O prince, how it acquired the force of a permanent observance and how it came to be considered as a meritorious act.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: जमदग्नेश्च संवादं सूर्यस्य च महात्मनः। पुरा स भगवान् साक्षाद्धनुषाक्रीडयत् प्रभो॥
en: I shall in this connection, recite the conversation between Jamadagni and the great Sun. Formerly the illustrious Jamadagni, O powerful king, of Bhrigu's race, was engaged in practising with his bow.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: संधाय संधाय शरांश्चिक्षेप किल भार्गवः। तान् क्षिप्तान् रेणुका सर्वांस्तस्येषून्दीप्ततेजसः॥ आनीय सा तदा तस्मै प्रादादसकृदच्युत। अथ तेन स शब्देन ज्यायाश्चैव शरस्य च॥ प्रहृष्टः सम्प्रचिक्षेप सा च प्रत्याजहार तान्। ततो मध्याह्नमारूढे ज्येष्ठामूले दिवाकरे॥ स सायकान् द्विजो मुक्त्वा रेणुकामिदमब्रवीत्। गच्छानय विशालाक्षि शरानेतान् धनुश्च्युतान्॥
en: Taking his aim, he shot arrow after arrow. His wife Renuka used to pick up the arrows when he shot and repeatedly bring them back to that descendant, gifted with the burning energy of Bhrigu's race. pleased with the whizzing noise of his arrows and the twang of his bow, he amused himself thus by repeatedly shooting his arrows which Renuka brought back to him, One day, at noontide, O monarch, was in that month when the Sun in Jyesthamula, the Brahmana, having shot all his arrows, said to Renuka, O largeeyed lady, go and fetch me the arrows I have shot from my bow.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: यावदेतान् पुनः सुभ्र क्षिपामीति जनाधिए। सा गच्छन्त्यन्तरा छायां वृक्षमाश्रित्य भामिनी॥ तस्थौ तस्या हि सन्तप्तं शिरः पादौ तथैव च। स्थिता सा तु मुहूर्तं वै भर्तुः शापभयाच्छुभा॥ ययावानयितुं भूयः सायकानसितेक्षणा। प्रत्याजगाम च शरांस्तानादाय यशस्विनी॥ सा वै खिन्ना सुचार्वङ्गी पद्भ्यां दुःखं नियच्छती। उपाजगाम भर्तारं भयाद् भर्तुः प्रवेपती॥
en: O you of beautiful eyebrows, I shall again shoot them with my bow! The lady proceeded on her errand but was compelled to sit under the shade of a tree, on account of her head and feet being scorched by the heat of the Sun. The black eyed and graceful Renuka, having rested for only a moment, feared the curse of her husband and, therefore began to collect and bring back the arrows. Taking them with her, the celebrated lady of beautiful features came back, distressed in mind and her feet smarting with pain. Trembling with fear, she approached her husband.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: सतामृषिस्तदा क्रुद्वो वाक्यमाह शुभाननाम्। रेणुके किं चिरेण त्वमागतेति पुनः पुनः॥
en: The Rishis, stricken with anger, repeatedly addressed his fairfaced wife, saying, O Renuka, why have you been so late in returning?

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: रेणुकोवाच शिरस्तावत् प्रदीप्तं मे पादौ चैव तपोधन। सूर्यतेजोनिरुद्धाऽहं वृक्षच्छायां समाश्रिता॥
en: Renuka said O you, having penances for wealth, my hand and feet were scorched by the rays of the Sun! Oppressed by the heat, I took shelter under the shade of a tree!

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: एतस्मात् कारणाद् ब्रह्मश्चिरायैतत् कृतं मया। एतच्छ्रुत्वा मम विभो मा क्रुधस्त्वं तपोधन॥
en: with me. This . has been the cause of the delay! Informed of the cause, do you, O lord, cease to be angry

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: जमदग्निरुवाच अद्यैनं दीप्तकिरणं रेणुके तव दुःखदम्। शरैर्निपातयिष्यामि सूर्यमस्त्राग्नितेजसा॥
en: Jamadagni said O Renuka, this very day shall I destroy, with the fiery energy of my weapons, the star of the day with his burning rays, who has afflicted you thus.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: भीष्म उवाच स विस्फार्य धनुर्दिव्यं गृहीत्वा च शरान् बहून्। अतिष्ठत् सूर्यमभितो यतो याति ततो मुखः॥
en: Bhishma said Drawing his celestial bow, and taking up many arrows, Jamadagni stood, turning his face towards the Sun and watching him as he moved on.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: अथ तं प्रेक्ष्य सन्नद्धं सूर्योऽभ्येत्य तथाब्रवीत्। द्विजरूपेण कौन्तेय किं ते सूर्योऽपराध्यते॥
en: Then O son of Kunti, seeing him ready for fight, the Sun approached him in the guise of a Brahmana, and said to him, What has the Sun done to offend you?

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: आदत्ते रश्मिभिः सूर्यो दिवि तिष्ठंस्ततस्ततः। रसं हृतं वै वर्षासु प्रवर्षति दिवाकरः॥
en: Passing through the sky, he draws up the moisture from the Earth and in the form of rains he pours it down once more on her.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: ततोऽन्नं जायते विप्र मनुष्याणां सुखावहम्। अन्नं प्राणा इति यथा वेदेषु परिपठ्यते॥
en: It is through this, O twiceborn one, that the food of human beings springs up, food that is so agreeable to them! The Vedas say that it is food that forms the vital airs.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: अथाभ्रेषु निगूढच रश्मिभिः परिवारितः। सप्तद्वीपानिमान् ब्रह्मन् वर्षेणाभिप्रवर्षति॥
en: O Brahmana, hidden in the clouds and encompassed by his rays, the Sun drenches the seven insular continents with showers of rain.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: ततस्तदौषधीनां च वीस्थां पुष्पपत्रजम्। सर्वं वर्षाभिनिवृत्तमनं सम्भवति प्रभो॥
en: O powerful one, the moisture, thus poured, spreading itself into the leaves and fruits of vegetables and herbs, is changed into food.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: जातकर्माणि सर्वाणि व्रतोपनयनानि च। गोदानानि विवाहाश्च तथा यज्ञसमृद्धयः॥ शास्त्राणि दानानि तथा संयोगा वित्तसंचयाः। अन्नतः सम्प्रवर्तन्ते तथा त्वं वेत्थ भार्गव॥
en: O son of Bhrigu, the rites consequent on birth, religious observances, investiture with the sacred thread, gifts of kine, marriage, all articles in view of sacrifices, the rules for the governance of men, gifts all sorts of union, and the acquisition of riches, originate from food! You know this well!

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: रमणीयानि यावन्ति यावदारम्भिकाणि च। सर्वमन्नात् प्रभवति विदितं कीर्तयामि ते॥
en: All the good and sweet things in the universe, and all the efforts made by living creatures, originate from food. I duly recite what is well known to you! Indeed, you fully know all that I have said.

description: The introduction of umbrellas and sandals as gifts of Shraddhas
sn: सर्वं हि वेत्थ विप्र त्वं यदेतत् कीर्तितं मया। प्रसादये त्वां विप्रर्षे किं ते सूर्य निपात्य वै॥
en: Do you therefore, O twiceborm Rishi, appease your anger! What will you gain by annihilating the Sun?

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवं प्रयाचति तदा भास्करे मुनिसत्तमः। जगदग्निर्महातेजाः किं कार्यं प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: Yudhishthira said What did that foremost of ascetics, viz., Jamadagni gifted with great energy, do when thus besought by the Sun?

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: भीष्म उवाच स तथा याचमानस्य मुनिरग्निसमप्रभः। जमदग्निः शमं नैव जगाम कुरुनन्दन॥
en: Bhishma said O descendant of Kuru, inspite of all the prayers of the Sun, the sage Jamadagni, effulgent like fire, continued to cherish his anger.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: ततः सूर्यो मधुरया वाचा तमिदमब्रवीत्। कृताञ्जलिर्विप्ररूपी प्रणम्यैनं विशाम्पते।॥ चलं निमित्तं विप्रर्षे सदा सूर्यस्य गच्छतः। कथं चलं भेत्स्यसि त्वं सदा यान्तं दिवाकरम्॥
en: Then, O king, the Sun, in the guise of a Brahmana, bowed his head to him and addressed him, with clasped hands, in these sweet words, O twiceborn Rishi, the Sun is always moving! How shall you pierce the Lord of day who is continually moving forward?

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: जमदग्निरुवाच स्थिरं चापि चलं चापि जाने त्वां ज्ञानचक्षुषा। अवश्यं विनयाधानं कार्यमद्य मया तव॥
en: Jamadagni said With the eye of knowledge I know you to be both moving and motionless! I shall surely read you a lesson this day.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: मध्याह्ने वै निमेषार्धं तिष्ठसि त्वं दिवाकर। तत्र भेत्स्यामि सूर्य त्वां न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा॥
en: At midday you appear to stay in the firmament for a moment. It is then, O Sun, that I shall pierce you with my arrows! There is no swerving from this resolution of mine.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: सूर्य उवाच असंशयं मां विप्रर्षे भेत्स्यसे धन्विनां वर। अपकारिणं मां विद्धि भगवञ्छरणागतम्॥
en: Surya said O twiceborn Rishi, forsooth, you know me, O best of archers! But, O holy one, though I have offended, see I pray for your protection.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः प्रहस्य भगवान् जगदग्निरुवाच तम्। न भीः सूर्य त्वया कार्या प्रणिपातगतो ह्यसि॥
en: Bhishma said At this, the worshipful Jamadagni smilingly addressed the Sun, saying, O Sun, when you have sought my protection, you have nothing to fear.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: ब्राह्मणेष्वार्जवं यच्च स्थैर्यं च धरणीतले। सौम्यतां चैव सोमस्य गाम्भीर्यं वरुणस्य च॥ दीप्तिमग्नेः प्रभां मेरोः प्रतापं तपनस्य च। एतान्यतिक्रमेद् यो वै स हन्याच्छरणागतम्॥
en: He would get over the simplicity that exists in Brahmanas, the stability that exists in the Earth, the mildness existing in the Moon, the gravity existing in Varuna, the effulgence existing in Agni, the brightness of Meru, and the heat of the Sun, who would kill a suppliant for protection.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: भवेत् स गुरुतल्पी च ब्रह्महा च स वै भवेत्। सुरापानं स कुर्याच्च यो हन्याच्छरणागतम्॥
en: The man who can kill a suppliant is capable of violating the bed of his preceptor, of killing ! a Brahmana and of drinking alcohol.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: एतस्य त्वपनीतस्य समाधि तात चिन्तय। यथा सुखगमः पन्था भवेत् त्वद्रश्मिभावितः॥
en: Do you, therefore, think of some remedy for this evil, by which people may be relieved when heated by your rays.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतावदुक्त्वा स तदा तूष्णीमासीद् भृगूत्तमः। अथ सूर्योऽददत् तस्मै छत्रोपानहमाशु वै॥
en: Bhishma said So saying, that exceilent descendant of Bhrigu remained silent for some time, and the Sun immediately gave him an umbrella and a pair of sandals,

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: सूर्य उवाच महर्षे शिरसस्त्राणं छत्रं मद्रश्मिवारणम्। प्रतिगृह्णष्व पद्भ्यां च त्राणार्थं चर्मपादुके॥
en: Surya said Do you, O great Rishi, take this umbrella with which the head may be protected and my rays warded off. This pair of sandals is made of leather for the protection of the feet.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: अद्यप्रभृति चैवेह लोके सम्प्रचरिष्यति। पुण्यकेषु च सर्वेषु परमक्षय्यमेव च॥
en: From this day the gift of these articles in all religious rites shall be established as a custom.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: भीष्म उवाच छत्रोपानहमेतत् तु सूर्येणैतत् प्रवर्तितम्। पुण्यमेतदभिख्यातं त्रिषु लोकेषु भारत॥
en: Bhishma said This custom of giving umbrella and shoes was introduced by the Sun. O descendant of Bharata, these gifts are regarded meritorious in the three worlds.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: तस्मात् प्रयच्छ विप्रेषु छत्रोपानहमुत्तमम्। धर्मस्तेषु महान् भावी न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा॥
en: Do you, therefore, give away umbrellas and shoes to Brahmanas. I have no doubt that you will then acquire great religious merit by the deed.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: छत्रं हि भरतश्रेष्ठ यः प्रदद्याद् द्विजातये। शुभ्रं शतशलाकं वै स प्रेत्य सुखमेधते॥ स शक्रलोके वसति पूज्यमानो द्विजातिभिः। अप्सरोभिश्च सततं देवैश्च भरतर्षभ॥
en: O foremost one of Bharata's race, he who gives away a white umbrella with a hundred ribs to a Brahmana, acquires eternal happiness after death and lives the region of Indra, respected by Brahmanas, Apsaras, and Devas.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: दह्यमानाय विप्राय यः प्रयच्छत्युपानहौ। स्नातकाय महाबाहो संशिताय द्विजातये॥ सोऽपि लोकानवाप्नोति दैवतैरभिपूजितान्। गोलोके स मुदा युक्तो वसति प्रेत्य भारत॥
en: O powerful one, he who gives shoes to Snataka Brahmanas as also to Brahmanas practising the rites of religion whose feet have become sore with the heat of the Sun, acquires regions coveted by the very celestials. Such a man, O Bharata, lives happily in the highest Heaven after his death.

description: Jamadagni's attempt to destroy the sun
sn: एतत् ते भरतश्रेष्ठ मया कात्स्न्येन कीर्तितम्। छत्रोपानहदानस्य फलं भरतसत्तम॥
en: O foremost one of Bharata's race. I have thus recited to you, in full the merits of giving away shoes and umbrellas at religious ceremonies.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच गार्हस्थ्यं धर्ममखिलं प्रब्रूहि भरतर्षभ। ऋद्धिमाप्नोति किं कृत्वा मनुष्य इह पार्थिव॥
en: Yudhishthira said O foremost one of Bharata's race, do you describe to me all the deities of the household mode and tell me all that a man should do in order to acquire prosperity in this world.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि पृरावृत्तं जनाधिप। वासुदेवस्य संवादं पृथिव्याश्चैव भारत॥
en: Bhishma said O Bharata, I shall, in this connection, recite to you the old story of Vasudeva and the goddess Earth.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: संस्तुत्य पृथिवीं देवीं वासुदेवः प्रतापवान्। पप्रच्छ भरतश्रेष्ठ मां त्वं यत् पृच्छसेऽद्य वै॥
en: The powerful Vasudeva, O excellent prince of Bharata's race, after singing the praises of the goddess Earth, accosted her about this very subject that you have required about.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: वासुदेव उवाच गार्हस्थ्यं धर्ममाश्रित्य मया वा मद्विधेन वा। किमवश्यं धरे कार्यं किं वा कृत्वा कृतं भवेत्॥
en: Vasudeva said Having adopted the domestic mode of life, what acts should I, or one like me, do and how are such acts to yield success. man

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: पृथ्वी उवाच ऋषयः पितरो देवा मनुष्याश्चैव माधव। इज्याश्चैवार्चनीयाश्च यथा चैव निबोध मे॥
en: The Goddess Earth said O Madhava, the Rishis, the celestials the departed Manes, and men should be adored, and sacrifices should be performed by a householder.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: सदा यज्ञेन देवाश्च सदाऽऽतिथ्येन मानुषाः। छन्दतश्च यथा नित्यमर्हान् भुञ्जीत नित्यशः॥
en: Do you also learn this from me that the celestials are always pleased with sacrifices, and are pleased with hospitality. Therefore, the householder should please them with such objects as they desire.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: तेन पषिगणाः प्रीता भवन्ति मधुसूदन। नित्यमग्निं परिचरेदभुक्त्वा बलिकर्म च॥
en: By such acts, O destroyer of Madhu Rishis also are pleased. The householders, abstaining from food, should daily attend to his sacred fire and to his sacrificial offerings.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: कुर्यात् तथैव देवा वै प्रीयन्ते मधुसूदन। कुर्यादहरहः श्राद्धमन्नाद्येनोदकेन च॥ पयोमूलफलैर्वापि पितॄणां प्रीतिमाहरन्। सिद्धान्नाद् वैश्वदेवं वै कुर्यादग्नौ यथाविधि॥ अग्नीषोमं वैश्वदेवं धान्वन्तर्यमनन्तरम्। प्रजानां पतये चैव पृथग्योमो विधीयते॥
en: The celestials, O destroyer of Madhu, are pleased with such deeds. The householder should daily offer oblations of food and water, or of fruits, roots and water, for the satisfaction of the departed Manes, and give boiled food to the Vishvedevas, and oblations of clarified butter to Agni, Soma, and Dhanvantari.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: तथैव चानुपूर्वेण बलिकर्म प्रयोजयेत्। दक्षिणायां यमायेति प्रतीच्यां वरुणाय च॥ सोमाय चाप्युदीच्यां वै वास्तुमध्ये प्रजापतेः। धन्वन्तरे:प्रागुदीच्यां प्राच्यां शक्राय माधव॥
en: He should offer separate and distinct oblations of Prajapati. He should make sacrificial offerings duly; to Yama in the South, to Varuna in the West, to Soma in the North, to Prajapati within the homestead, to Dhanvantari in the North East, and to Indra in the East.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: मनुष्येभ्य इति प्राहुर्बलिं द्वारि गृहस्य वै। मरुद्भ्यो दैवतेभ्यश्च बलिमन्तर्गृहे हरेत्॥
en: He should offer food to men at the entrance of his house. These, O Madhava, are known as the Bali offerings. The Bali should be offered to the Maruts and the deities in the interior of one's house.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: तथैव विश्वेदेवेभ्यो बलिमाकाशतो हरेत्। निशाचरेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो बलिं नक्तं तथा हरेत्॥
en: To the Vishvedevas it should be offered in open air, and to the Rakshasas and evil spirits the offerings should be made at night.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: एवं कृत्वा बलिं सम्यग् दद्याद् भिक्षां द्विजाय वै। अलाभे ब्राह्मणस्याग्नावग्रमुद्धृत्य निक्षिपेत्॥
en: After making these offerings, the householder should make offerings to Brahmanas, and if no Brahmana be present, the first portion of the food should be thrown into the fire.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: यदा श्राद्धं पितृभ्योऽपि दातुमिच्छेत मानवः। तदा पश्चात् प्रकुर्वीत निवृत्ते श्राद्धकर्मणि॥
en: When a man wishes to offers Shraddha to his ancestors, he should, when the Shraddha ceremony is donc, please his ancestors and then make the Bali offerings duly.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: पितॄन् संतर्पयित्वा तु बलिं कुर्याद् विधानतः। वैश्वदेवं ततः कुर्यात् पश्चाद् ब्राह्मणवाचनम्॥
en: He should then make offerings to the Vishwedevas. He should next invite Brahmanas, and then properly entertain guests arrived at his house, with food.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: ततोऽन्नेन विशेषेण भोजयेदतिथीनपि। अर्चापूर्व महाराज ततः प्रीणाति मानवान्॥
en: By this act, O prince, are guests pleased. He who does not live in the house long, or, having come, goes away after a short time, is called guest.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: अनित्यं हि स्थितो यस्मात् तस्मादतिथिरुच्यते। आचार्यस्य पितुश्चैव सख्युराप्तस्य चातिथेः॥ इदमस्ति गृहे मह्यमिति नित्यं निवेदयेत्।
en: To his preceptor, to his father, to his friend and to a guest, a householder should say, I have got this in my house to offer you today! And he should offer it accordingly every day.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: ते यद् वदेयुस्तत् कुर्यादिति धर्मो विधीयते॥ गृहस्थः पुरुषः कृष्ण शिष्टाशी च सदा भवेत्।
en: The house holder should do whatever they would order him to do. This is the established custom. The householder, O Krishna should take his food the last of all, after having offered food to all of them.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: राजत्विजं स्नातकं च गुरुं श्वशुरमेव च।॥ अर्चयेन्मधुपर्केण परिसंवत्सरोषितान्।
en: The householder should adore with offerings of honey, etc., his king his priest, his preceptor, and his fatherinlaw, as also Snataka Brahmanas even if they were to live in his house for whole year.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: श्वभ्यश्च श्वपचेभ्यश्च वयोभ्यश्चावपेद् भुवि। वैश्वदेवं हि नामैतत् सायंप्रातर्विधीयते॥
en: In the morning as well as in the evening, food should be offered on the ground to dogs, the cooks for dogs and birds. This is called the Vaishvedeva offerings.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: एतांस्तु धर्मान् गार्हस्थ्यान् यः कुर्यादनसूयकः। स इहर्षिवरान् प्राण्य प्रेत्य लोके महीयते॥
en: The householder, who performs these ceremonies with mind shorn of passion, obtains the blessings of the Rishis in this world, and after death acquires the heavenly regions.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: भीष्म उवाच इति भूमेर्वचः श्रुत्वा वासुदेवः प्रतापवान्। तथा चकार सततं त्वमप्येवं सदाचर॥
en: Bhishma said Having heard all this from the goddess Earth, the powerful Vasudeva acted accordingly. Do you also act in the same way.

description: Duties of the Domestic Mode of Life
sn: एतद् गृहस्थधर्मं त्वं चेष्टमानो जनाधिप। इहलोके यशः प्राप्य प्रेत्य स्वर्गमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: By performing these duties of a householder. O king, you shall acquire fame in this world and Heaven after death?

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आलोकदानं नामैतत् कीदृशं भरतर्षभ। कथमेतत् समुत्पन्नं फलं वा तद् ब्रवीहि मे।॥
en: Yudhishthira said Of what kind is the gift of light, О chief of Bharata's race? How did this gift originate? What are the merits of it? Do you tell me all this.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। मनोः प्रजापतेर्वादं सुवर्णस्य च भारत॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it, O Bharata, is recited the old discourse between Manu, that lord of creatures, and Suvarna,

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: तपस्वी कश्चिदभवत् सुवर्णो नाम भारत। वर्णतो हेमवर्णः स सुवर्ण इति पप्रथे॥
en: These was formerly an ascetic, O Bharata named Suvarna. His complexion was like that of gold and hence he was called Suvarna.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: कुलशीलगुणोपेतः स्वाध्याये च परंगतः। बहून् सुवंशप्रभवान् समतीतः स्वकैर्गुणैः॥
en: Gifted with good birth, good conduct and good qualities, he had mastered all the Vedas. Indeed, by the accomplishments he possessed, he succeeded in excelling many persons of noble birth.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: स कदाचिन्मनुं विप्रो ददर्शोपससर्प च। कुशलप्रश्नमन्योन्यं तौ चोभौ तत्र चक्रतुः॥
en: One day that learned Brahmana beheld Manu, the lord of all creatures, and approached him. Meeting each other, they made the usual polite enquires.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: ततस्तौ सत्यसंकल्पौ मेरौ काञ्चनपर्वते। रमणीये शिलापृष्ठे सहितौ संन्यषीदताम्॥
en: Both of them were in the truth. Having met each other, they sat down on charming breast of the golden mount Meru.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: तत्र तौ कथयन्तौ स्तां कथा नानाविधाश्रयाः। ब्रह्मर्षिदेवदैत्यानां पुराणानां महात्मनाम्॥
en: Seated there they began to talk with each other on various subjects about the great deities and twiceborn Rishis and Daityas of ancient times.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: सुवर्णस्त्वब्रवीद् वाक्यं मनुं स्वायम्भुवं प्रति। हितार्थं सर्वभूतानां प्रश्न मे वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Then Suvarna addressing the Selfcreate Manu, said these words:You should answer one question of mine for the behoof of all creatures.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: सुमनोभिर्यदिज्यन्ते दैवतानि प्रजेश्वर। किमेतत् कथमुत्पन्नं फलं योगे च शंस मे॥
en: O lord of all creatures, the celestials are scen to be adored with presents of flowers and other good scents. What is this? How has this practice come into operation? What also are the merits of it? Do you describe this subject to me.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: मनुरुवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। शुक्रस्य च बलेश्चैव संवादं वै महात्मनोः॥
en: Manu said Regarding it is recited the oid discourse between Shukra and the great (Daitya) Bali.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: बलेवैरोचनस्येह त्रैलोक्यमनुशासतः। समीपमाजगामाशु शुक्रो भृगुकुलोद्वहः॥
en: Once on a time, Shukra of Bhrigu's race approached Bali the son of Virochana while he was ruling the three worlds.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: तमादिभिरभ्यर्च्य भार्गवं सोऽसुराधिपः। निषसादासने पश्चाद् विधिवद् भूरिदक्षिणः॥
en: Having adored the descendant of Bhrigu with the Arghya, the king of the Asuras, that profuse giver of sacrificial presents, sat down after his guest had seated himself.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: कथेयमभवत् तत्र त्वया या परिकीर्तिता। सुमनोधूपदीपानां सम्प्रदाने फलं प्रति॥ ततः पप्रच्छ दैत्येन्द्रः कवीन्द्रं प्रश्नमुत्तमम्॥
en: This very subject which you have introduced regarding the merits of the gift of flowers and incense and lamps, came up on the occasion. Indeed the king of the Daityas put this high question of Shukra that most learned of all ascetics.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: बलि उवाच सुमनोधूपदीपानां किं फलं ब्रह्मवित्तम। प्रदानस्य द्विजश्रेष्ठ तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Bali said O foremost of all persons conversant with Brahma, what, indeed, is the merit of giving flowers and incense and lamps? You should, O foremost of Brahmanas, describe this to me.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: शुक्र उवाच तपः पूर्वं समुत्पन्नं धर्मस्तस्मादनन्तरम्। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे चैव वीरुदोषध्य एव च॥
en: Shukra said Penance first sprang into existence. Afterwards came religion. In the interval many creepers and herbs sprang up.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: सोमस्यात्मा च बहुधा सम्भूतः पृथिवीतले। अमृतं च विषं चैव ये चान्ये तृणजातयः॥
en: Their species were innumerable. All of them have the Moon for their lord. Some of these creepers and herbs came to be considered as Ambrosia and some came to be considered as Poison. Others that were neither this nor that formed one class.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: अमृतं मनसः प्रीतिं सद्यस्तृप्तिं ददाति च। मनो ग्लपयते तीव्र विषं गन्धेन सर्वशः॥
en: That is Ambrosia which gives immediate pleasure and joy to the mind. That is Poison which tortures the mind greatly by its smell.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: अमृतं मङ्गलं विद्धि महद्विषममङ्गलम्। ओषध्यो ह्रामृतं सर्वा विषं तेजोऽग्निसम्भवम्॥
en: men Know again that Ambrosia is highly auspicious and that Poison Poison is highly inauspicious. All the herbs are Ambrosia. Poison is born of the energy of fire.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: मनो ह्लादयते यस्माच्छ्रियं चापि दधाति च। तस्मात् सुमनसः प्रोक्ता नरैः सुकृतकर्मभिः॥
en: Flowers please the mind and confer prosperity. Hence of pious deeds bestowed the name Sumanas on thein.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: देवताभ्य: सुमनसो यो ददाति नरः शुचिः। तस्य तुष्यन्ति वै देवास्तुष्टाः पुष्टिं ददत्यपि॥
en: That man who in a state of purity offers flowers to the celestials finds that the celestials become pleased with him, and as the result of such satisfaction confer prosperity upon him.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: यं यमुद्दिश्य दीयेरन् देवं सुमनसः प्रभो। मङ्गलार्थं स तेनास्य प्रीतो भवति दैत्यप॥
en: O king of the Daityas, those celestials to whom worshippers offer flowers, O lord, uttering their names the while, become pleased with the offerers on account of their devotion.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: ज्ञेयास्तूग्राश्च सौम्याश्च तेजस्विन्यश्च ताः पृथक्। ओषध्यो बहुवीर्या हि बहुरूपास्तथैव च।॥
en: The (deciduous) herbs are of various kinds and possess different qualities. They should be classed as fierce, mild, and powerful.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: यज्ञियानां च वृक्षाणामयज्ञीयान् निबोध मे। आसुराणि च माल्यानि दैवतेभ्यो हितानि च॥
en: Listen to me as I tell you which tress are useful for purposes of sacrifice and which are not so. Hear also what garlands are acceptable to Asuras, and what are beneficial when offered to the celestials.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: रक्षसामुरगाणां च यक्षाणां च तथा प्रियाः। मनुष्याणां पितॄणां च कान्तायास्त्वनुपूर्वशः॥
en: I shall also set forth in due order what garlands are killed by the Rakshasas, what by the Uragas, what by the Yakshas, what by human beings, and what by the departed Manes, in proper order.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: वन्या ग्राम्याश्चेह तथा कृष्टोप्ताः पर्वताश्रयाः। अकण्टकाः कण्टकिनो गन्धरूपरसान्विताः॥
en: Flowers are of various kinds. Some are wild, some are from iress which grow in the midst of human dwellings; some belong to trees which never grow unless planted on wellcultivated soil; some are from trees growing on mountains,; some are from trees which are not prickly; and some from tress which are prickly. Fragrance, beauty of form and taste also make grounds of classification.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: द्विविधो हि स्मृतो गन्ध इष्टोऽनिष्टश्च पुष्पजः। इष्टगन्धानि देवानां पुष्पाणीति विभावय॥
en: The scent of flowers is of two kinds, agreeable and disagreeable. Those flowers which have sweet smell should be offered to the celestials.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: अकण्टकानां वृक्षाणां श्वेतप्रायाश्च वर्णतः। तेषां पुष्पाणि देवानामिष्टानि सततं प्रभो॥
en: The flowers of trees which have no thorns are generally white in colour. Such flowers are always acceptable to the celestials, O lord.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: जलजानि च माल्यानि पद्मादीनि च यानि वै। गन्धर्वनागयक्षेभ्यस्तानि दद्याद् विचक्षणः॥
en: A wise man should offer garlands red of aquatic flowers, such as the lotus and the like, to the Gandharvas and Nagas and Yakshas.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: ओषध्यो रक्तपुष्पाश्च कटुकाः कण्टकान्विताः। शत्रूणामभिचारार्थमाथर्वेषु निदर्शिताः॥
en: Such plants and herbs as produce red flowers, as have been scent, and as are prickly, have been laid down in the Atharvans as fit for all acts of incantation for injuring enemies.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: तीक्ष्णवीर्यास्तु भूतानां दुरालम्भाः सकण्टकाः। रक्तभूयिष्ठवर्णाश्च कृष्णाश्चैवोपहारयेत्॥
en: Such flowers as have keen energy, as are painful to the touch, as grow on trees and plants having thorns, and as are either bloodyred or black, should be offered to (evil) spirits an unearthly beings.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: मनोहृदयनन्दिन्यो विशेषमधुराश्च याः। चारुरूपाः सुमनसो मानुषाणां स्मृता विभो॥
en: Such flowers as please the mind and heart, as are very agreeable when pressed, and as are of beautiful form, have been said, O lord, to be worthy of being offered to men.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: न तु श्मशानसम्भूता देवतायतनोद्भवाः। संनयेत् पुष्टियुक्तेषु विवाहेषु रहःसु च॥
en: Such flowers as grow on cemeteries and crematoria, or in places dedicated to the celestials, should not be brought and used for marriage and other rites having growth and prosperity for their object, or for acts of pleasure in secrecy.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: गिरिसानुरुहाः सौम्या देवानामुपपादयेत्। प्रोक्षिताऽभ्युक्षिताः सौम्या यथायोग्यं यथास्मृति।।३४
en: Such flowers as grow on mountains and in vales, and as are beautiful to look at and sweetscented; should be offered to the celestials. Sprinkling them with sandal paste, such sweet flowers should be duly offered according to the scriptural ordinances.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: गन्धेन देवास्तुष्यन्ति दर्शनाद् यक्षराक्षसाः। नागाः समुपभोगेन त्रिभिरेतैस्तु मानुषाः॥
en: The celestials become pleased with the scent of flowers; the Yakshas and Rakshasas with their sight; the Nagas with their touch; and human beings with all three, viz., scent, sight, and touch.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: सद्यः प्रीणाति देवान् वै ते प्रीता भावयन्त्युत। संकल्पसिद्धा मानामीप्सितैश्च मनोरमैः॥
en: Flowers, when offered to the celestials please them immediately. They are capable of accomplishing every object by merely wishing its accomplishment. As such, when pleased with devotees offering them flowers, they cause all the objects cherished by their worshippers to be immediately achieved.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: प्रीताः प्रीणन्ति सततं मानिता मानयन्ति च। अवज्ञातावधूताश्च निर्दहन्त्यधमान् नरान्॥
en: Pleased, they gratify their worshippers. Honoured they make their worshippers enjoy all honors. Disregarded and insulted, they make those vilest of men to be ruined and consumed.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: अत उर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि धूपदानविधेः फलम्। धूपांश्च विविधान् साधूनसाधूंश्च निबोध मे॥
en: I shall, after this, speak to you of the merits of the ordinances about the gift of incense. Know, O king of Asuras, that incenses are of various sorts. Some of them are auspicious and some inauspicious.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: निर्यासा: सारिणश्चैव कृत्रिमाश्चैव ते त्रयः। इष्टोऽनिष्टो भवेद् गन्धस्तन्मे विस्तरशः शृणु॥
en: Some incenses consists of exudations. Some are made of fragrant wood set on fire. And some are artificial, being made by the hand, of various articles mixed together. Their scent is of two sorts, viz., agreeable and disagreeable. Listen to me as I describe the subject fully.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: निर्यासाः सल्लकीवा देवानां दयिताऽस्तु ते। गुग्गुलुः प्रवरस्तेषां सर्वेषामिति निश्चयः॥
en: All exudations except that of the Boswellia serrata are agreeable to the celestials. It is, however, certain that the best of all cxudations is that of the Balsamodendron Mukul.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: अगुरुः सारिणां श्रेष्ठो यक्षराक्षसभोगिनाम्। दैत्यानां सल्लकीयश्च काङ्गतो यश्च तद्विधः॥
en: Of all Dhupas of the Sari class, the Aquilaria Agallocha is the best. It is very acceptable to the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, and Nagas. The exudation of the Boswellia serratta, and others of the same class, are much acceptable to the Daityas.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: अथ सर्जरसादीनां गन्धैः पार्थिव दारवैः। फाणितासवसंयुक्तर्मनुष्याणां विधीयते॥
en: Dhupas made of the exudation of the Shorea robusta and the Pinus deodara, mixed with various spirits of strong scent, are, O king, acceptable to human beings.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: देवदानवभूतानां सद्यस्तुष्टिकरः स्मृतः। येऽन्ये वैहारिकास्तत्र मानुषाणामिति स्मृताः॥
en: Such Dhupas are said to immediately please the celestials, the Danavas, and spirits. Besides these, there are many other kinds of Dhupas used by men for purposes of pleasure or enjoyment.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: य एवोक्ताः सुमनसां प्रदाने गुणहेतवः। धूपेष्वपि परिज्ञेयास्त एव प्रीतिवर्धनाः॥
en: The offer of flowers and the gift of such Dhupas as yield gratification are equal in merits.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: दीपदाने प्रवक्ष्यामि फलयोगमनुत्तमम्। यथा येन यदा चैव प्रदेया यादृशाश्च ते॥
en: I shall now speak of the merits of the gift of Jights, and who may give them at what time and in what manner, and what should be the kind of lights that should be offered.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: ज्योतिस्तेजः प्रकाशं वाप्यूर्ध्वगं चापि वर्ण्यते। प्रदानं तेजसां तस्मात् तेजो वर्धयते नृणाम्॥
en: Light is said to be energy and fame and goes upwards. Hence the gift of light, which is energy, increases the energy of men.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: अन्धन्तमस्तमिस्रं च दक्षिणायनमेव च। उत्तरायणमेतस्माज्ज्योतिर्दानं प्रशस्यते॥
en: There is a hell named Andhatamas. The period also of the Sun's southward course is considered as dark. For avoiding that hell and the darkness of this period, one should give lights during that period when the Sun is in northern solstice. Such an act is highly spoken of by the good.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: यस्मादूर्ध्वगमेतत् तु तमसश्चैव भेषजम्। तस्मादूर्ध्वगतेर्दाता भवेदत्रेति निश्चयः॥
en: Since, again, light has an upward course and is considered as a remedy for darkness, therefore one should give lights. This is the conclusion of the scriptures.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: देवास्तेजस्विनो ह्यस्मात् प्रभावन्तः प्रकाशकाः। तामसा राक्षसाश्चैव तस्माद् दीपः प्रदीयते॥
en: It is by giving lights that the celestials have become gifted with beauty, energy, and resplendence. By abstention from such a deed, the Rakshasas have become gifted with the opposite attributes. Hence, one should always give lights.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: आलोकदानाच्चक्षुष्मान् प्रभायुक्तो भवेन्नरः। तान् दत्त्वा नोपहिंसेत न हरेनोपनाशयेत्॥
en: By giving lights a man becomes gifted with keen vision and resplendence. Onc who gives lights should not be looked with jealousy by others. Lights, again, should not be stolen, nor put out when given by others.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: दीपहर्ता भवेदधस्तमोगतिरसुप्रभः। दीपप्रदः स्वर्गलोके दीपमालेव राजते॥
en: One who steals a light becomes blind. Such a man has to grope through darkness and becomes shorn of resplendence. One who gives lights shines in beauty in the celestial regions like a row of lights,

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: हविषा प्रथमः कल्पो द्वितीयश्चौषधीरसैः। वसामेदोऽस्थिनिर्यासैन कार्वः युष्टिमिच्छता॥
en: Among lights, the best are those in which clarified butter is burnt. Next in order are those in which the juice of deciduous herbs is burnt. One seeking prosperity and growth should never burn fat or marrow or the juice that comes from the bones of creatures.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: गिरिप्रपाते गहने चैत्यस्थाने चतुष्पथे। दीपदानं भवेन्नित्यं य इच्छेद् भूतिमात्मनः॥
en: The who desires his aggrandisement and prosperity should always give lights at descents from mountains, in roads through forests and inaccessible regions, under sacred tress standing in the midst of human dwellings, and in crossings of streets.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: कुलोद्योतो विशुद्धात्मा प्रकाशत्वं च गच्छति। ज्योतिषां चैव सालोक्यं दीपदाता नरः सदा॥
en: The man who gives lights always illumines his race, acquires purity of soul and effulgence of form. Indeed, such a man, after death, lives in the company of the luminous bodies in the sky.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: बलिकर्मसु वक्ष्यामि गुणान् कर्मफलोदयान्। देवयक्षोरगनृणां भूतानामथ रक्षसाम्॥
en: I shall now describe to you the merits, with the fruits they bring about, of Bali offerings man own made to the celestials, the Yakshas, the Uragas, human beings, spirits and Rakshasas.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: येषां नाग्रभुजो विप्रा देवतातिथिबालकाः। राक्षसानेव तान् विद्धि निर्विशङ्कानमगलान्॥
en: Those unscrupulous and wicked men who eat without First serving Brahmanas and celestials and guests and children, should be known as Rakshasas,

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: तस्मादग्रं प्रयच्छेत देवेभ्यः प्रतिपूजितम्। शिरसा प्रयतश्चापि हरेद् बलिमतन्द्रितः॥
en: Hence, one should first offer the food one has got ready to the celestials after having adored them duly with controlled senses and rapt attention. One should offer the Bali to the celestials, bending his head in respect.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: गृह्णन्ति देवता नित्यमाशंसन्ति सदा गृहान्। बाह्याश्चागन्तवो येऽन्ये यक्षराक्षसपन्नगा:॥
en: The celestials are always supported by food that householders offer. They bless such houses in which offerings are made to them. The Yakshas and Rakshasas and Pannagas, as also guests and all houseless persons, are supported by the food offered by householders.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: इतो दत्तेन जीवन्ति देवताः पितरस्तथा। ते प्रीताः प्रीणयन्तेनमायुषा यशसा धनैः॥
en: Indeed, the celestials and the departed, Manes derive their sustenance from such offerings. Pleased with such offerings they please the offerer in return with longevity and fame and riches.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: बलयः सह पुष्पैस्तु देवानामुपहारयेत्। दधिदुग्धमयाः पुण्याः सुगन्धाः प्रियदर्शनाः॥
en: Clean food, of sweet scent and look, mixed with milk and curds, should, along with flowers, be offered to the celestials.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: कार्या रुधिरमासांढ्या बलयो यक्षरक्षसाम्। सुरासवपुरस्कारा लाजोल्लापिकभूषिताः॥
en: The Balis that should be offered to Yakshas and Rakshasas should be rich with blood and meat, with wines and spirits accompanying, and adorned with friend paddy.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: नागानां दयिता नित्यं पद्मोत्पलविमिश्रिताः। तिलान् गुडसुसम्पन्नान् भूतानामुपहारयेत्॥
en: Balis mixed with lotuses and Utpalas are very acceptable to the Nagas. Sesame seeds, boiled in raw sugar, should he offered to the spirits and other unearthly Beings.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: अग्रदाताग्रभोगी स्याद् बलवीर्यसमन्वितः। तस्मादग्रं प्रयच्छेत देवेभ्यः प्रतिपूजितम्॥
en: He who never takes any food without first giving a part of it to the Brahmanas and celestials and guests, becomes entitled to first portions of food. Such a man becomes gifted with strength and energy. Hence one should never take any food without first offering a portion thereof to the celestial after adoring them with respect.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: ज्वलन्त्यहरहो वेश्म याचास्य गृहदेवताः। ताः पूज्या भूतिकामेन प्रसृताग्रप्रदायिना॥
en: One's house always shines in beauty on account of the household deities that live in it. Hence, he who desires his own advancement and prosperity should adore the household gods by offering them the first portion of every food.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: इत्येतदसुरेन्द्राय काव्यः प्रोवाच भार्गवः। सुवर्णाय मनुः प्राह सुवर्णो नारदाय च॥
en: Thus did the learned Kavi oi Bhrigu's race discourse to Bali the chief of the Asuras. That discourse was next recited by Manu to the Rishi Suvarna. Suvarna, in his turn, recited it to Narada.

description: The history of the gift of light
sn: नारदोऽपि मयि प्राह गुणानेतान् महाद्युते। त्वमप्येतद् विदित्वेह सर्वमाचर पुत्रक॥
en: The celestial Rishi Narada recited to me merits of the several acts mentioned. Informed of those merits, do you, O son, perform the several acts mentioned.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतं मे भरतश्रेष्ठ पुष्पधूपप्रदायिनाम्। फलं बलिविधाने च तद् भूयो वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have, O chief of the Bharatas, heard what the merits which presenters of flowers and lincense and lights acquire. I have heard you speak also of the merits of a due observance of the ordinances in respect of the presentation of the Bali. You should, O grandfather, discourse to me once more on this subject.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: धूपप्रदानस्य फलं प्रदीपस्य तथैव च। बलयश्च किमर्थं वै क्षिप्यन्ते गृहमेधिभिः॥
en: Indeed, tell me. O Sire once more of the merits of presenting incense and lights. Why Balis offered the ground by householders. are on

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। नहुषस्य च संवादमगस्त्यस्य भृगोस्तथा॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is recited the old discourse between Nahusha and Agastya and Bhrigu.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: नहुषो हि महाराज राजर्षिः सुमहातपाः देवराज्यमनुप्राप्तः सुकृतेनेह कर्मणा॥
en: The royal sage Nahusha, O monarch, having penances for wealth, acquired the sovereignty of the celestial region by his own good deeds.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: तत्रापि प्रयतो राजन् नहुषस्त्रिदिवे वसन्। मानुषीश्चैव दिव्याश्च कुर्वाणो विविधाः क्रियाः॥
en: With controlled senses, O king, he lived in the celestial region, engaged in doing diverse acts of both human an celestial nature.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: मानुष्यस्तत्र सर्वा:स्म क्रियास्तस्य महात्मनः। प्रवृत्तस्त्रिदिवे राजन् दिव्याश्चैव सनातनाः॥
en: From that great kuig flowed various kinds of human acts and various kinds of celestial deeds, also, O king.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: अग्निकार्याणि समिधः कुशाः सुमनसस्तथा। बलयश्चान्नलाजाभिषूपनं दीपकर्म च॥ सर्वं तस्य गृहे राज्ञः प्रावर्तत महात्मनः। जपयज्ञान्मनोयज्ञास्त्रिदिवेऽपि चकार सः॥
en: The various rites with respect to the sacrificial fire, the collection of sacred fuel and of Kusha grass, as also of flowers, and the presentation of Bali consisting of food adorned with fried paddy, and the offer of incense and of light, all there, O monarch, occurred daily in the house of that great king while he lived in the celestial region. Indeed, though living in the celestial region. he celebrated the sacrifice of recitation and the sacrifice of meditation.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: देवानभ्यर्चयच्चापि विधिवत् स सुरेश्वरः। सर्वानेव यथान्यायं यथापूर्वमरिन्दम॥
en: And, O chastiser of foes, Nahusha, although he had become the king's of the deities, yet adored all the deities, as he used to do formerly, with due rites and ceremonies.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: अथेन्द्रोऽहमिति ज्ञात्वां अहंकारं समाविशत्। सर्वाश्चैव क्रियास्तस्य पर्यहीयन्त भूपतेः॥
en: Sometime after, Nahusha realised his position as the king of the deities. This filled him with pride. From that time all his deeds were suspended.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: स ऋषीन् वाहयामास वरदानमदान्वितः। परिहीणक्रियश्चैव दुर्बलत्वमुपेयिवान्॥
en: Filled with pride on account of the boon he had received from all the celestials, Nahusha caused the very Rishis to bear hiin on their shoulders. On account, however, of his abstention from all religious acts, his energy began to wane.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: तस्य वाहयतः कालो मुनिमुख्यास्तपोधनान्। अहंकाराभिभूतस्य सुमहानभ्यवर्तत॥
en: The time was very long for which Nahusha, filled with arrogance, continued to employ the foremost of Rishis, having penances for wealth, as the bearers of his vehicles.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: अथ पर्यायशः सर्वान् वाहनायोपचक्रमे। पर्यायश्चाप्यगस्त्यस्य समपद्यत भारत॥
en: He make the Rishis perform by turns this humiliating work. The day came when it was Agastya's turn to carry the vehicle, O Bharata.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: अथागत्य महातेजा भृगुर्ब्रह्मविदां वरः। अगस्त्यमाश्रमस्थं वै समुपेत्येदमब्रवीत्॥ एवं वयमसत्कारं देवेन्द्रस्यास्य दुर्मतेः। नहुषस्य किमर्थं वै मर्षयाम महामुने॥
en: At that time, Bhrigu, that foremost of all persons conversant with Brahma went to Agastya while the latter was seated in his hermitage, and addressing him said, O great ascetic, why should we patiently suffer such indignities inflicted on us by this wicked Nahusha who has become the king of the deities.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: अगस्त्य उवाच कथमेष मया शक्यः शप्तुं यस्य महामुने। वरदेन वरो दत्तो भवतो विदितश्च सः॥
en: Agastya said How can, succeed in cursing Nahusha, O great Rishi? You know how the Boongiving (Brahman) himself has given Nahusha the best of boons.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: यो मे दृष्टिपथं गच्छेत् स मे वश्यो भवेदिति। इत्यनेन वरं देवो याचितो गच्छता दिवम्॥
en: Coming to the celestial region, the boon that Nahusha prayed for, was that, whoever would come within the range of his vision would, deprived of all energy, come within his control.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: एवं न दग्धः स मया भवता च न संशयः। अन्येनाप्यषिमुख्येन न दग्धो न च पातितः॥
en: The selfborn Brahman granted him this boon, and it is therefore that neither yourself nor I have been able to consume him. Forsooth, it is for this reason that none one else amongst the foremost of Rishis has been able to consume or throw him down from his elevated position.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: अमृतं चैव पानाय दत्तमस्मै पुरा विभो। महात्मना तदर्थं च नास्माभिर्विनिपात्यते॥
en: Formerly, O lord, nectar was given by Brahman to Nahusha for drinking. Therefore we can do nothing to him.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: प्रायच्छत वरं देवः प्रजानां दुःखकारणम्। द्विजेष्वधर्मयुक्तानि स करोति नराधमः॥
en: The great god, it appears, gave that boon to Nahusha for plunging all creatures into grief. That wretched behaves most unrighteously towards the Brahmanas.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: तत्र यत्प्राप्तकालं नस्तद् ब्रूहि वदतां वर। भवांश्चापि यथा ब्रूयात् तत्कर्तास्मि न संशयः॥
en: O foremost of all speakers, tell us what should be done under the circumstances. Forsooth, I shall do what you will advise. man

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: भृगु उवाच पितामहनियोगेन भवन्तं सोऽहमागतः। प्रतिकर्तुं बलवति नहुषे दैवेमोहिते॥
en: Bhrigu said It is at the command of the Grandfather that I have come to you with the view of counteracting the power of Nahusha who is gifted with great energy but who has been stupefied by fatc.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: अद्य हि त्वां सुदुर्बुद्धी रथे योक्ष्यति देवराट्। अद्यैनमहमुद्वृत्तं करिष्येऽनिन्द्रमोजसा॥
en: That exceedingly wicked being who has become the king of the celestials, will today yoke you to his car. With the help of my power I shall today hurl him down from his position as Indra on account of his having transcended all restraints.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: अद्येन्द्र स्थापयिष्यामि पश्यतस्ते शतक्रुतम्। संचाल्य पापकर्माणमैन्द्रात् स्थानात् सुदुर्मतिम्॥
en: I shall today, in your very sight, reestablish the true Indra in his position, him, viz., who has celebrated a hundred horse sacrifices, having hurled the wicked and sinful Nahusha from that seat.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: अद्य चासौ कुदेवेन्द्रस्त्वां पदा धर्षयिष्यति। दैवोपहतचित्तत्वादात्मनाशाय मन्दधीः॥
en: That impious king of the celestials will today insult you by a kick, on account of his understanding being afflicted by fate and for bringing about his own downfall.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: व्युत्क्रान्तधर्मं तमहं घर्षणामर्षितो भृशम्। अहिर्भवस्वेति रुषा शप्स्ये पापं द्विजदुहम्॥
en: Euraged at such an insult I shall today curse that sinful wretch, that enemy of the Brahmanas, who has transcended all restrains, saying, Be you metamorphosed into a snake.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: तत एनं सुदुर्बुद्धिं धिक्शब्दाभिहतत्विषम्। धरण्यां पातयिष्यामि पश्यतस्ते महामुने॥
en: Before your eyes, O great ascetic, I shall today hurl down on the Earth the wicked Nahusha who shall be deprived of all power on account of the cries of Fie that will be uttered from all sides.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: नहुषं पापकर्माणमैश्वर्यबलमोहितम्। यथा च रोचते तुभ्यं तथा कर्तास्म्यहं मुने॥
en: Indeed, I shall hurl down Nahusha today, that sinful man, who has, besides, been stupefied by lordship and power. I shall do this, if you like it, О ascetic.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु भृगुणा मैत्रावरुणिरव्ययः। अगस्त्यः परमप्रीतो बभूव विगतज्वरः॥
en: Thus addressed by Bhrigu, Mitravaruna's son Agastya of unfading power and glory, became highly pleased and freed from every anxiety.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं वै स विपन्नश्च कथं वै पातितो भुवि। कथं चानिन्द्रतां प्राप्तस्तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Yudhishthira said How was Nahusha plunged into distress? How was he hurled down on the Earth? How, indeed, was he deprived of the sovereignty of the celestials? You should recite everything to me.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवं तयोः संवदतोः क्रियास्तस्य महात्मनः। सर्वा एव प्रवर्तन्ते या दिव्या याश्च मानुषीः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus did those two Rishis, viz., Bhrigu and Agastya, talk with each other, I have already told you how Nahusha, when he first become the king of the celestials, acted in a proper way. Indeed, that great royal sage performed all human and celestial deeds.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: तथैव दीपदानानि सर्वोपकरणानि वै। बलिकर्म च यच्चान्यदुत्सेकाश्च पृथग्विधाः॥ सर्वे तस्य समुत्पन्ना देवेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः। देवलोके नृलोके च सदाचारा बुधैः स्मृताः॥
en: Nahusha who had become the king of the celestials, made gifts of light, and properly deserved all other rites of a similar nature, the due presentation of Balis, and all rites as are performed on especially sacred days. Pious acts are always done by wise men, in both the world of men and that of the celestials, Indeed, O foremost of kings, if such acts are observed, householders always succeed in acquiring prosperity and aggrandisement.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: ते चेद् भवन्ति राजेन्द्र ऋद्ध्यन्ते गृहमेधिनः। धूपप्रदानैर्दीपैश्च नमस्कारैस्तथैव च॥
en: Even such is the effect of the gift of lamps and of incense, as also of bows and prostrations, to the celestials.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: यथा सिद्धस्य चान्नस्य ग्रहायाग्रं प्रदीयते। बलयश्च गृहोद्देशे अतः प्रीयन्ति देवताः॥
en: When food is cooked, the first portion thereof should be offered to a Brahmana. The particular offerings called Bali should also be presented to the household gods. The deities become pleased with such gifts.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: यथा च गृहिणस्तोषो भवेद् वै बलिकर्मणि। तथा शनगुणा प्रीतिर्देवतानां प्रजायते॥
en: It is also well known that the measure of gratification which the celestials derive from such offerings is a hundred times as great as that which the householder himself gets from making them.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: एवं धूपप्रदानं च दीपदानं च साधवः। प्रयच्छन्ति नमस्कारैर्युक्तमात्मगुणावहम्॥
en: Pious and wise persons make offering of incense and lights, accompanying them with bows and prostrations. Such acts always yield advancement and prosperity to those that do them.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: स्नानेनादिश्च यत् कर्म क्रियते वै विपश्चिता। नमस्कारप्रयुक्तेन तेन प्रीयन्ति देवताः॥
en: Those rites which the learned perform in course of their ablutions, and with the help of waters, accompanied with bows to the gods, always contribute to the satisfaction of the celestials.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: पितरश्च महाभागा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः। गृह्याश्च देवताः सर्वाः प्रीयन्ते विधिनार्चिताः॥
en: When adored with proper rites, the highlyblessed departed Manes, Rishis having asceticism for wealth, and the household deities, all become pleased.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: इत्येतां बुद्धिमास्थाय नहुषः स नरेश्वरः। सुरेन्द्रत्वं महत् प्राप्य कृतवानेतदद्भुतम्॥
en: Filled with such ideas, Nahusha, that great king, when he obtained the sovereignty of the celestials, observed all these rites and duties fraught with great glory.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य भाग्यक्षय उपस्थिते। सर्वमेतदवज्ञाय कृतवानिदमीदृशम्॥
en: Sometime after, the good fortune of Nahusha decreased, and as the outcome of it, he neglected all these observances and began to act in defiance of all control in the manner I have already described.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: ततः स परिहीणोऽभूत् सुरेन्द्रो बलदर्पतः। धूपदीपोदक विधिं न यथावच्चकार ह॥
en: The king of the celestials, on account of his abstention from observing the ordinances about the offers of incense and light, began to decline in power.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: ततोऽस्य यज्ञविषयो रक्षोभिः पर्यबध्यत। अथागस्त्यमृषिश्रेष्ठं वाहनायाजुहाव ह॥
en: His sacrificial rites and presents were obstructed by Rakshasas. It was at this time that Nahusha yoked that foremost of Rishis, viz., Agastya, to his car.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: द्रुतं सरस्वतीकूलात् स्मयन्निव महाबलः। ततो भृगुर्महातेजा मैत्रावरुणिमब्रवीत्॥
en: Possessed of great strength Nahusha smiling all the while, set that great Rishi speedily to the task, commanding him to bear the vehicle from the banks of the Sarasvati. At this time, Bhrigu, possessed of great energy, addressed the son of Mitravaruna, saying:

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: निमीलय स्वनयने जटां यावद् विशामि ते। स्थाणुभूतस्य तस्थाय जटां प्राविशदच्युतः॥ भृगुः स सुमहातेजाः पातनाय नृपस्य च। ततः स देवराट प्राप्तस्तमृर्षि वाहनाय वै॥
en: Do you shut your eyes till I enter into the matted locks on your head. Having said this, Bhrigu of unfading glory and great energy entered into the matted locks of Agastya who stood still like a wooden post, for hurling king Nahusha from the throne of Heaven. Soon after Nahusha saw Agastya approach him for bearing his car.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: ततोऽगस्त्यः सुरपतिं वाक्यमाह विशाम्पते। योजयस्वेति मां क्षिप्रं कं च देशं वहामि ते॥
en: Seeing the king of the celestials, Agastya addressed him, saying, Do you yoke me to your vehicle forthwith! To what region shall I bear you.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: यत्र वक्ष्यसि तत्र त्वां नयिष्यामि सुराधिप। इत्युक्तो नहुषस्तेन योजयामास तं मुनिम्॥
en: O lord of the celestials, I shall bear you to the spot which you may be pleased to direct! Thus addressed by him. Nahusha caused the ascetic to be yoked to his car.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: भृगुस्तस्य जटान्तस्थो बभूव हृषितो भृशम्। न चापि दर्शनं तस्य चकार स भृगुस्तदा।॥
en: Bhrigu, who was living within the matted locks of Agastya, became highly pleased at this act of Nahusha. He took care not to look at Nahusha.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: वरदानप्रभावज्ञो नहुषस्य महात्मनः। न चुकोप तदाऽगस्त्यो युक्तोऽपि नहुषेण वै॥
en: Fully acquainted with the power which the illustrious Nahusha had acquired on account of the boon which Brahman had granted him, Bhrigu acted thus. Agastya also though treated by Nahusha in this way, did not yield to anger.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: तं तु राजा प्रतोदेन चोदयामास भारत। न चुकोप स धर्मात्मा ततः पादेन देवराट्॥ अगस्त्यस्य तदा क्रुद्धो वामेनाभ्यहनच्छिरः। तस्मिन्शिरस्यभिहते स जटान्तर्गतो भृगुः॥ शशाप बलवत्क्रुद्धो नहुषं पापचेतसम्। यस्मात् पदाऽऽहतः कोधाच्छिरसीमं महामुनिम्॥ तस्मादाशु महीं गच्छ सर्पो भूत्वा सुदुर्मते। इत्युक्तः स तदा तेन सर्पो भूत्वा पपात ह॥ अदृष्टेनाथ भृगुणा भूतले भरतर्षभ। भृगुं हि यदि सोऽद्रक्ष्यन्नहुषः पृथिवीपते॥ न च शक्तोऽभविष्यद् वै पातने तस्य तेजसा। स तु तैस्तैः प्रदानैश्च तपोभिर्नियमैस्तथा॥ पतितोऽपि महाराज भूतले स्मृतिमानभूत्। प्रसादयामास भृगु शापान्तो मे भवेदिति॥
en: Then, O Bharata, king Nahusha urged Agastya on with his goad. The pious Rishi did not still yield to anger. The lord of the celestials, himself enraged, then struck Agastya on the head with his left foot. When the Rishi was thus struck on the head, Bhrigu, who was living within Agastya's matted locks became incensed and cursed the sinful Nahusha, saying, Since you have struck with your foot on the head of this great Rishi, do you, therefore, fall down on the Earth, changed into a snake, O wretch of wicked understanding! Thus, imprecated by Bhrigu who had not been seen Nahusha, forthwith became transformed into a snake and dropped down on the Earth, O chief of Bharata's race! If, O monarch, Nahusha had seçn Bhrigu, the latter would not then have succeeded, by his power, in hurling the forner down on the Earth. On account of the various gifts that Nahusha had made, as also his penances and religious observances, though hurled down on the Earth. O king, he succeeded in keeping his memory. He then began to propitiate Bhrigu with a view to get rid of the curse.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: ततोऽगस्त्यः कृपाविष्टः प्रसादयत तं भृगुम्। शापान्तार्थं महाराज स च प्रादात् कृपान्वितः॥
en: Agastya also, filled with mercy joined Nahusha in pacifying Bhrigu for the termination of the curse. At last Bhrigu felt mercy for Nahusha and arranged for the working out of the curse.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: भृगु उवाच राजा युधिष्ठिरो नाम भविष्यति कुलोद्वहः। स त्वां मोक्षयिता शापादित्युक्त्वान्तरधीयत॥
en: Bhrigu said There will appear a king (on Earth) of the name of Yudhishthira, the foremost of his race. He will rescue you from this curse! Having said this, the Rishi disappeared from the presence of Nahusha.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: अगस्त्योऽपि महातेजाः कृत्वा कार्यं शतक्रतोः। स्वमाश्रमपदं प्रायात् पूज्यमानो द्विजातिभिः॥
en: Agastya also, of great energy, having thus performed the business of the true Indra, that arbitrator of a hundred sacrifices, returned to his hermitage, adored of all members of the regenerate order.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: नहुषोऽपि त्वया राजंस्तस्माच्छापात् समुद्धृतः। जगाम ब्रह्मभवनं पश्यतस्ते जनाधिप॥
en: You have, o king rescued Nahusha from Bhrigu's curse. Rescued by you, he ascended to the region of Brahman before your eyes.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: तदा स पातयित्वा तं नहुषं भूतले भृगुः। जगाम ब्रह्मभवनं ब्रह्मणे च न्यवेदयत्॥
en: As regards, Bhrigu, having hurled Nahusha on the Earth, he went to the region of Brahman and informed the Grandfather of it.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: ततः शक्रं समानाय्य देवानाह पितामहः। वरदानान्मम सुरा नहुषो राज्यमाप्तवान्॥
en: The Grandfather having called Indra back, addressed the celestials, saying, You celestials, through the boon I had granted him, Nahusha had obtained the sovereignty of Heaven.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: स चागस्त्येन क्रुद्धेन भ्रंशितो भूतलं गतः। न च शक्यं विना राज्ञा सुरा वर्तयितुं क्वचित्॥
en: Deprived, however, of that sovereignty by the enraged Agastya, he has been hurled on the Earth, O celestials, you will not succeed in living without a king.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: तस्मादयं पुनः शक्रो देवराज्येऽभिषिच्यताम् एवं सम्भाषमाणं तु देवाः पार्थ पितामहम्॥ एवमस्त्विति संदृष्टाः प्रत्यूचुस्तं नराधिप। सोऽभिषिक्तो भगवता देवराज्ये च वासवः॥ ब्रह्मणा राजशार्दूल यथापूर्वं व्यरोचत। एवमेतत् पुरावृत्तं नहुषस्य व्यतिक्रमात्॥
en: Do you, therefore, once more install Indra as the king of Heaven. The celestials filled with joy, O son of Pritha, replied to the Grandsire, who said so to them, saying, So be it. Brahman then, O best of kings, installed Indra in the sovereignty of Heaven. Made once more the king of the celestials, Vasava began to shine in beauty and resplendence. This is what took place forinerly through the transgressions of Nahusha.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: स च तैरेव संसिद्धो नहुषः कर्मभिः पुनः। तस्माद् दीपाः प्रदातव्याःसायं वै गृहमोधिभिः॥
en: On account, however, of the merits he had acquired through deeds of the kind I have mentioned, Nahusha succeeded in once more regaining his lost position. Hence, when evening comes, householders should give lights.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: दिव्यं चक्षुरवाप्नोति प्रेत्य दीपस्य दायकः। पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतीकाशा दीपदाश्च भवन्त्युत॥
en: The giver of lights is sure to win celestial vision after death. Givers of light become as resplendent as the full moon.

description: The merits of the gifts of light, incense, &c. The discourse between Nahusha and Agastya on the subject
sn: यावदक्षिनिमेषाणि ज्वलन्ते तावती: समाः। रूपवान् बलवांश्चापि नरो भवति दीपदः॥
en: The giver of lights becomes gifted with beauty of form and strength for years corresponding with the number of twinkles for which the lights given by him burn or blaze.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्राह्मणस्वानि ये मन्दा हरन्ति भरतर्षभ। नृशंसकारिणो मूढाः क्व ते गच्छन्ति मानवाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Where do those foolish, wretched, and sinful men go, O king, who steal misappropriate such articles as belong to Brahmanas? or

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। चाण्डालस्य च संवादं क्षाबन्धोश्च भारत॥
en: Bhishma said I shall, about it, O Bharata, recite to you the conversation between a Chandala and a low Kshatriya.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: वृद्धरूपोऽसि चाण्डाल बालवच्च विचेष्टसे। श्वखराणां रज:सेवी कस्मादुद्विजसे गवाम्॥
en: This Kshatriya said You seem, O Chandala, to be old in years, but your conduct appears to be like that of a boy! Your body is besmeared with the dust raised by dogs and asses, but without minding thal dust you are anxious about the little drops of milk that have fallen upon you persons.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: साधुभिर्गर्हितं कर्म चाण्डालस्य विधीयते। कस्माद् गोरजसाध्वस्तमपां कुण्डे निषिञ्चसि॥
en: It is plain that such acts as are censured by the pious are ordained for the Chandala. Why, indeed, do you seek to wash off the spots of milk from your body.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: चाण्डाल उवाच ब्राह्मणस्य गवां राजन् हियतीनां रजः पुरा। सोममुध्वंसयामास तं सोमं येऽपिबन् द्विजाः॥ दीक्षितश्च स राजापि क्षिप्रं नरकमाविशत्। सह तैर्याजकैः सर्वैर्ब्रह्मस्वमुपजीव्य तत्॥
en: The Chandala said Formerly, O king, certain kine belonging to a Brahmana were stolen, While they were being carried away, some milk from their udders dropped upon a number of Soma plants that grew by the roadside. Those Brahmanas who drank the juice of the plants thus bedewed with milk, as also the king who celebrated the sacrifice in which that Soma was drunk, had to sink in hell. Indeed, for having thus appropriated something belonging to a Brahmana, the king with all the Brahmanas who had helped him had to go to hell.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: येऽपि तत्रापिबन् क्षीरं घृतं दधि च मानवाः। ब्राह्मणाः सहराजन्याः सर्वे नरकमाविशन्॥
en: All those men also, Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, who drank milk or clarified butter or curds, in the palace of the king who had stolen the Brahmana's kine, had to fall into hell.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: जनस्ताः पयसा पुत्रांस्तथा पौत्रान् विधुवन्तीः। पशूनवेक्षमाणाश्च साधृवृत्तेन दम्पती॥
en: The stolen kine also, shaking their bodies, killed with their milk the sons and grandsons of those who had stolen them, as also the king and the queen although the latter treated the animals, with great care and attention.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: अहं तत्रावसं राजन् ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः। तासां मे रजसा ध्वस्त भैक्षमासीन्नराधिप॥
en: As for myself, O king, I used to live the life of a celibate in that place where these kine were placed after they had been stolen away. The food I had got by begging became sprinkled over with the milk of those kine.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: चाण्डालोऽहं ततो राजन् भुक्त्वा तदभवं नृप। ब्रह्मस्वहारी च नृपः सोऽप्रतिष्ठां गतिं ययौ।॥
en: Having taken that food, O Kshatriya, I have, in this life, become a Chandala. The king who had stolen the kine belonging to a Brahmana came by a wretched end.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: तस्माद्धरेन विप्रस्वं कदाचिदपि किंचन। ब्रह्मस्वं रजसा ध्वस्तुं भुक्त्वा मां पश्य यादृशम्॥
en: Hence, one should never steal or appropriate anything belonging to a Brahmana. Mark, to what state I am reduced on account of my having eaten food that had been sprinkled over with milk belonging to a Brahmana.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: तस्मात् सोमोऽप्यविक्रेयः पुरुषेण विपश्चिता। विक्रयं त्विह सोमस्य गर्हयन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: It is for this reason that Soma plants should never be destroyed by wise men. They who sell the Soma plant are held in low esteem by the wise.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: ये चैनं क्रीणते तात ये च विक्रीणते जनाः। ते त वैवस्वतं प्राप्य रौरवं यान्ति सर्वशः॥
