en: Indeed, O son, they who purchase Soma and they who sell it, both sink in the hell called Raurava after death.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: सोमं तु रजसा ध्वस्तं विक्रीणन् विधिपूर्वकम्। श्रोत्रियो वाधुषी भूत्वा न चिरं स विनश्यति॥
en: That man who, possessing a knowledge of the Vedas, duly sells Soma, becomes in his next life a usurer and speedily meets with destruction.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: नरकं त्रिंशतं प्राप्य स्वविष्ठामुपजीवति। श्रुचर्यामभिमानं च सखिदारे च विप्लवम्॥ तुलया धारयन् धर्ममभिमान्यतिरिच्यते। श्वानं वै पापिनं पश्य विवर्णं हरिण कृशम्॥
en: For threehundred times he has to sink into hell and become changed into an animal which subsists upon human excreta. Serving a low person, pride, and rape upon a friend's wife, if weighed against one another in a balance, would show that pride, which is above all restraints, is the heaviest. Mark this dog, so sinful and disagreeably pale and lean.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: अभिमानेन भूतानामिमां गतिमुपागतम्। अहं वै विपुले तात कुले धनसमन्विते॥ अन्यस्मिजन्मनि विभो ज्ञानविज्ञानपारगः। अभवं तत्र जानानो ह्येतान् दोषान् मदात् सदा॥ संरब्ध एव भूतानां पृष्ठमांसमभक्षयम्। सोऽहं तेन च वृत्तेन भोजनेन च तेन वै॥ इमामवस्थां सम्प्राप्तः पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्। आदीप्तमिव चैलान्तं भ्रमरिव चार्दितम्॥ धावमानं सुसंरब्धं पश्य मां रजसान्वितम्। स्वाध्यायैस्तु महात्पापं हरन्ति गृहमेधिनः॥ दानैः पृथग्विधैश्चापि यथा प्राहुर्मनीषिणः। तथा पापकृतं विप्रमाश्रमस्थं महीपते॥ सर्वसङ्गविनिर्मुक्तं छन्दांस्युत्तारयन्त्युत। अहं हि पापयोन्यां वै प्रसूतः क्षत्रियर्षभ। निश्चयं नाधिगच्छामि कथं मुच्येयमित्युत॥
en: It is through pride that living creatures come by such a miserable end. As for myself, I was born in a large family in a former birth of mine, O lord, and I was a perfect master of all branches of knowledge and al the sciences. I knew the immensity of all these faults, but moved by pride, I became blinded and ate the i meat attached to the vertebral columns of animals. On account of such conduct and such food, I have come by this state. Mark, the। reverses engendered by Time! Like a person whose cloth has caught fire at one end, or who is pursued by bees, see, I am running, filled with fear, and smeared with dust! The householders are rescued from all sins by a study of the wise. O Kshatriya, a sinful Brahmana becomes rescued from all his sins by a study of the Vedas, if he becomes a forestreclusc and abstains from attachment of every kind. O chief of Kshatriyas, I am, in this life, born in sinful caste.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: जातिस्मरत्वं च मम केनचित् पूर्वकर्मणा। शुभेन येन मोक्षं वै प्राप्तुमिच्छाम्यहं नृप।॥
en: I cannot see clearly how I may succeed in purifying myself from all sins. On account of some meritorious deed of a former life, I have not lost the memory of my previous births.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: त्वमिमं सम्प्रपन्नाय संशयं ब्रूहि पृच्छते। चाण्डालत्वात् कथमहं मुच्येयमिति सत्तम॥
en: O king, I throw myself on your mercy! I ask you. Do you remove my doubt. By what auspicious course of conduct should I wish to acquire my liberation? O foremost of men, by what means shall I succeed in getting rid of my Chandalahood.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: राजन्य उवाच चाण्डाल प्रतिजानीहि येन मोक्षमवाप्स्यसि। ब्राह्मणार्थे त्यजन् प्राणान् गतिमिष्टामवाप्स्यसि॥
en: The Kshatriya said Know, O Chandala, the means by which you may be able to acquire liberation. By renouncing your life for the sake of a Brahmana, you may come by a desirable end.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: दत्त्वा शरीरं क्रव्याद्भयो रणाग्नौद्विजहेतुकम्। हत्वा प्राणान् प्रमोक्षस्ते नान्यथा मोक्षमर्हसि॥
en: By throwing your body on the fire of battle as a libation to the beasts and birds of prey for the sake of a Brahmana, indeed, by renouncing your life thus, you may achieve liberation. By no other means will you succeed in acquitting it.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तः स तदा तेन ब्रह्मस्वार्थे परंतप। हत्वा रणमुखे प्राणान् गतिमिष्टामवाप ह॥
en: Bhishma said Thus accosted, that Chandala, O scorcher of enemies, poured his lifebreaths as a libation on the fire of battle for the sake of protecting a Brahmana's riches and as the result of that act attained to a very desirable end.

description: The end of a person stealing a Brahmana's goods. The conversation between a Chandala and a lowcaste Kshtriya on the subject
sn: तस्माद् रक्ष्यं त्वया पुत्र ब्रह्मस्वं भरतर्षभ। यदीच्छसि महाबाहो शाश्वतीं गतिमात्मनः॥
en: Hence, O son, you should always protect the property of the Brahmanas, if, O chicf of Bharata's race, you wish, O you of mighty arms, an end consisting of eternal happiness. Hence, O son, you should always protect the property of the Brahmanas, if, O chicf of Bharata's race, you wish, O you of mighty arms, an end consisting of eternal happiness.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एके लोकाः सुकृतिनः सर्वे त्वाहो पितामह। तत्र तत्रापि भिन्नास्ते तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, it has been said that all righteous men attain to the same region after death. It is true, O Bharata, that there is difference of position among them?

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: भीष्म उवाच कर्मभिः पार्थनानात्वं लोकानां यान्ति मानवाः। पुण्यान् पुण्यकृतो यान्ति पापान पापकृतो नराः॥
en: Bhishma said By different acts, O son of Pritha, men acquire different regions. They who are righteous in conduct acquire blissful regions, while they who are sinful acquire miserable regions.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। गौतमस्य मुनेस्तात संवादं वासवस्य च॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old discourse, O son, between the ascetic Gautama and Vasava.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: ब्राह्मणौ गौतमः कश्चिन्मृदुर्दान्तो जितेन्द्रियः। महावने हस्तिशिशुं परिधूनममातृकम्॥
en: A certain Brahmana named Gautama, mild and selfcontrolled and with all his senses under complete control, saw an infant elephant that had lost his mother and that was highly cheerless on that account.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा जीवयामास सानुक्रोशो धृतव्रतः। स तु दीर्पण कालेन बभूवातिबलो महान्॥
en: Full of mercy and steady in the observance of his vows, the ascetic nursed that infant animal. After a long time the little beast grew up into a large and powerful elephant.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: तं प्रभिन्नं महानागं प्रस्रुतं पर्वतोपमम्। धृतराष्ट्रस्य रूपेण शक्रो जग्राह हस्तिनम्॥
en: One day, Indra, in the guise of king Dhritarashtra, scized that powerful clephant which was as huge as a hill and from whose rent temples the juice was trickling down.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: ह्रियमाणं तु तं दृष्ट्वा गौतमः संशितव्रतः। अभ्यभाषत राजानं धृतराष्ट्र महातपाः॥ मा मेऽहार्षीहस्तिनं पुत्रमेनं दुःखात् पुष्टं धृतराष्ट्राकृतज्ञ। मैत्रं सतां सप्तपदं वदन्ति मित्रद्रोहो मैव राजन् स्पृशेत् त्वाम्॥
en: Seeing the elephant dragged away, the great ascetic Gautama of rigid vows said to king Dhritarashta, O ungrateful Dhritarashtra, do not rob me of this elephant. It is considered by me as a son and I have reared it with much pain. It is said that between the pious, friendship if formed by merely the exchange of seven words. You should see, O king, that the sin of injuring a friend does not affect you,

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच इध्मोदकप्रदातारं शून्यपालं ममाश्रमे। विनीतमाचार्यकुले सुयुक्तं गुरुकर्मणि॥ शिष्टं दान्तं कृतज्ञं च प्रियं च सततं मम। न मे विक्रोशतो राजन् हर्तुमर्हसि कुञ्जरम्॥
en: Gautamia said You should not, O king, take away by force this elephant which brings me my fuel and water, which protects my hermitage when I am away, which is exceedingly docile and obedient to his instructor, which carefully does what his preceptor commands, which is mild and wellbroken, and which is grateful and very dear to me. Indeed, you should not take it away without caring for my protestalions and cries.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच गवां सहस्रं भवते ददानि दासीशतं निष्कशतानि पञ्च! अन्यच्च वित्तं विविधं महर्षे किं ब्राह्मणस्येह गजेन कृत्यम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said I shall give you a thousand kine, a hundred maidservants, and five hundred pieces of gold. I shall also, O great Rishi, give you various other kinds of wealth. What use can Brahmanas have with elephant?

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच तवैव गावो हि भवन्तु राजन् दास्यः सनिष्का विविधं च रत्नम्। अन्यच्च वित्तं विविधं नरेन्द्र किं ब्राह्मणस्येह धनेन कृत्यम्॥
en: Gautama said Keep O king, your kine and maid servants and coins of gold and various gems and various other kinds of riches. What, o king, have Brahmanas to do with riches.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ब्राह्मणानां हस्तिभिर्नास्ति कृत्यं राजन्यानां नागकुलानि विप्रा स्वं वाहनं नयतो नास्त्यधर्मो नागश्रेष्ठं गौतमास्मान्निवर्त॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Brahmanas have no use for elephants. Indeed, O learned Brahmana, elephants are intended for Kshatriyas. In taking away an animal, viz., this foremost of elephants, for my use, I cannot be considered as committing any sin. Do you cease obstructing me thus, o Gautama.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच यत्र प्रेत: यत्र प्रेतो नन्दति पुण्यकर्मा शोचते पापकर्मा। स्तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये॥
en: Gautama said O illustrious king, going even to that region of Yama where the pious live happily and the sinful in grief, I shall take from you this my elephants.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ये निष्क्रिया नास्तिका श्रद्दधानाः पापात्मान इन्द्रियार्थे निविष्टाः। यमस्य ते यातनां प्राप्नुवन्ति परं गन्ता धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र॥
en: Dhritarashtra said They who are destitute of religious acts, they who have no religious faith and are atheists, they who are sinful and are always engaged in pleasing their appetites only they have to go to the region of Yama and suffer the misery he inflicts. Dhritarashtra shall go to a higher region and not there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच वैवस्वती संयमनी जनानां यत्रानृतं नोच्यते यत्र सत्यम्। यत्राबला बलिनं यातयन्ति तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये॥
en: Gautama said Men are restrained in the region of Yama. No falsehood can be told there. Only truth prevails in that place. There the weak persecute the strong. Going there I shall compel you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ज्येष्ठां स्वसारं पितरं मातरं च यथा शत्रु मदमत्ताश्चरन्ति। तथाविधानामेष लोको महर्षे परं गन्ता धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Only those persons who, intoxicated with pride, treat their eldest sister and father and mother as enemies, have to go, O great ascetic, to such a region. I shall go to a higher region. Indeed, Dhritarashtra shall not have to go there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच मन्दाकिनी वैश्रवणस्य राज्ञो महाभागा भोगिजनप्रवेश्या। गन्धर्वयक्षैरप्सरोभिश्च जुष्टा तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये॥
en: Gautama said Those highly blessed ones go to the region called Mandakini, of king Vaishravana for enjoying joy and comfort. There live Gandharvas and Yakshas and Apsaras. Going even there, O kine, I shall compel you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अतिथिव्रताः सुव्रता ये जना वै प्रतिश्रयं ददति ब्राह्मणेभ्यः। शिष्टाशिनः संविभज्याश्रितांश्च मन्दाकिनी तेऽपि विभूषयन्ति॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Those persons who consider hospitality to guests as a vow, who observe good vows, who give shelter to Brahmanas, and who eat what remains after distribution among his dependants, adorn the region called Mandakini of Kubera. I shall not go there, for a higher region is reserved for me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच मेरोरग्रे यद् वनं भाति रम्यं सुपुष्पितं किन्नरीगीतजुष्टम्। सुदर्शना यत्र जम्बूर्विशाला तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये॥
en: Gautama said If you go to those charming woods, decked with flowers, which stand on the summit of Meru, which echo with the melodious notes of Kinnaris, and which are graced with beautiful Jamvus of wide spreading branches, I shall proceed even there and compell you to yield up this elephant to me. Dhritarashtra said

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ये ब्राह्मणा मृदवः सत्यशीला बहुश्रुताः सर्वभूताभिरामाः। येऽधीयते सेतिहासं पुराणं मध्वाहुत्या जुह्वति वै द्विजेभ्यः॥ तथाविधानामेष लोको महर्षे परं गन्ता धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र। यद् विद्यते विदितं स्थानमस्ति तद् ब्रूहि त्वं त्वरितो ह्येष यामि॥
en: Those Brahmanas who have mild dispositions, who are devoted to truth, who are endued with scriptural knowledge, who are compassionate to all creatures, who study, the Puranas with all the histories, who pour libations on the sacred fire and make gifts of honcy to the Brahmanas, go to such regions, O great Rishi! I shall go to a higher region. Indeed, Dhritarashtra shall not go there. If you are acquainted with any other wellknown region of happiness, speak to me, for I shall go even there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच सुपुष्पितं किन्नरराजजुष्टं प्रियं वनं नन्दनं नारदस्य। गन्धर्वाणामप्सरसां च शश्वत् तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये॥
en: Gautama said If you go to the woods owned by Narada and held dear by him, which are adorned with flowers and which echo with the melodious songs of the prince of Kinnaras, and which are the eternal habitation of Gandharvas an Apsaras. I shall follow you there and compell you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ये नृत्यगीते कुशला जनाः सदा ह्ययाचमानाः सहिताश्चरन्ति। तथाविधानामेष लोको महर्षे परं गन्ता धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र॥
en: Dhritarashtra said They who never beg, they who cultivate music and dancing, and always move about happily, proceed to such regions. O great Rishi, I shall go to a region which is higher. Indeed Dhritarashtra shall not have to go there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच यत्रोत्तराः कुरवो भान्ति रम्या देवैः सार्धं मोदमाना नरेन्द्र। यत्राग्नियौनाश्च वसन्ति लोका अब्योनयः पर्वतयोनयश्च॥ यत्र शक्रो वर्षति सर्वकामान् यत्र स्त्रियः कामचारा भवन्ति। यत्र चा नास्ति नारीनराणां तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये॥
en: Gautama said If you go that region where the Uttara Kurus blaze in beauty and pass their days happily, O king, in the company of the very celestials, where those beings who originate from fire, those who originate from water, and those who originate from mountains, live happily, and where Shakra rains down the fruition of every desire, and where women live in perfect freedom, uncotrolled by rules of any kind regulating their conduct or motions, and where there is no feeling of jealousy among both the sexes, if you go there, even there shall I go and compel you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ये सर्वभूतेषु निवृत्तकामा अमांसादा न्यस्तदण्डाश्चरन्ति। न हिंसन्ति स्थावरं जङ्गमं च भूतानां ये सर्वभूतात्मभूताः॥ निराशिषो निर्ममा वीतरागा लाभालाभे तुल्यनिन्दाप्रशंसाः। तथाविधानामेष लोको महर्षे परं गन्ता धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Those men who are freed from desire for all articles of enjoyment, who abstain from meat, who never take up the rod of punishment, and never inflict the least harm on mobile and immobile creatures, who have formed themselves the soul of all creatures, who never accost others by pronouncing blessings upon them, who are entirely freed from the idea of mineness, who are shorn of attachments for every thing, who view profit and loss as also praise and blame in equal light, only those men, O great Rishi, go to such regions. I shall go to a higher region. Indeed, Dhritarashtra shall not go there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच ततोऽपरे भान्ति लोकाः सनातनाः सुपुण्यगन्धा विरजा वीतशोकाः। स्तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये॥
en: Gautama said Next to these shine in beauty those eternal regions, full of excellent perfumes which are free from passions of every kind and which are destitute of sorrow. These forin the abode of the great king Soma. If you go there, even there shall I proceed and compell you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ये दानशीला न प्रतिगृह्यते सदा न चाप्यर्थोश्चाददते परेभ्यः। येषामदेयमर्हते नास्ति किंचित् सर्वातिथ्या: सुप्रसादा जनाश्च॥ ये क्षन्तारो नाभिजल्पन्ति चान्यान् सत्रीभूताः सततं पुण्यशीलाः। तथाविधानामेष लोको महर्षे परं गन्ता धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Those men who always make gifts without receiving any gift, who never accept any service from others, who possess nothing which they cannot give to a worthy person, who are hospitable to all creatures, who are inclined to show favour to every one, who are of for giving dispositions, who never speak ill of others, who protect all creatures by covering them with mercy, and who are always righteous in their conduct, only those men, O great Rishi, go to such regions. I shall go to a higher region. Indeed, Dhritarashtra shall not go there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच ततोऽपरे भान्ति लोकाः सनातना विरजसो वितमस्का विशोकाः। स्तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये।॥
en: Gautama sajd Next to these shine in beauty other regions that are eternal free from passion and Darkness and sorrow, and which lie at the foot of the great SunGod. If you go there, even there shall I go and compell you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच स्तपस्विनः सुव्रताः सत्यसंधाः। आचार्याणामप्रतिकूलभाषिणो नित्योत्थिता गुरुकर्मस्वचोद्याः॥ तथाविधानामेष लोको महर्षे विशुद्धानां भावितो वाग्यतानाम्। सत्ये स्थितानां वेदविदां महात्मनां परं गन्ता धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Those man who attentively study the Vedas, who are given to the service of their preceptors, who observe penances and excellent vows, who are firm in truth, who never utter words of disobedience or enmity to their preceptors, who are always alert, and ever ready in the service of elders and preceptors, they go, O great Rishi, to such regions, they who are pure who are gifted with cleansed souls, who are of controlled speech, who arc firm in truth and who are well versed in the Vedas. I shall proceed to a higher region. Indeed, Dhritarashtra shall not go there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच ततोऽपरे भान्ति लोकाः सनातनाः सुपुण्यगन्धा विरजा विशोकाः। स्तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये॥
en: Gautama said Next to those are the eternal regions which shine in beauty, which are full of excellent perfumes, which are free from passion, and which are destitute of every sorrow. They form the abode of the great king Varuna. If you proceed there, even there shall I go and compell you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच चातुर्मास्यैर्ये यजन्ते जनाः सदा तथेष्टीनां दशशतं प्राप्नुवन्ति। ये चाग्निहोत्रं जुह्वति श्रद्दधाना यथाम्नायं त्रीणि वर्षाणि विप्राः॥ सुधारिणां धर्मधुरे महात्मनां यथोदिते वर्त्मनि सुस्थितानाम्। धर्मात्मनामुद्वहतां गतिं तां परं गन्ता धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Those men who adore the celestials by observing the vow called Chaturmasya, who perform a hundred and ten sacrifices, who pour libations every day on their sacred fire with devotion and faith for three years according to the ordinances declared in the Vedas, who perform without hesitation of all duties, who walk steadily along the way trod by the pious, who steadily sustain the course of conduct followed by the righteousshould, only they go to such region, I shall go to a higher region. Indeed, Dhritarashtra shall not go there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच इन्द्रस्य लोका विरजा विशोका दुरन्वयाः कांसिता मानवानाम्। तस्याहं ते भवने भूरितेजसो राजन्निमं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये॥
en: Gautama said Above them are the regions of Indra, free from passion and sorrow, which are difficult of access and coveted by all men. Going even to the abode of indra himself of great energy, I shall, O king, compel you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच शतवर्षजीवी यश्च शूरो मनुष्यो वेदाध्यायी यश्च यज्वाऽप्रमत्तः। एते सर्वे शक्रलोकं व्रजन्ति परं गन्ता धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र॥
en: Dhritarashtra said He who lives for a hundred years, who is gifted with heroism, who studies the Vedas and who celebrates sacrifices with devotion, indeed, such men proceed to the region of Shakra. I shall go to a higher region, Indeed, Dhritarashtra shall not go there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच प्रजापत्याः सन्ति लोका महान्तो नाकस्य पृष्ठे पुष्कला वीतशोकाः। मनीषिताः सर्वलोकोद्भवानां तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये।॥
en: Gautama said Above the firmament are the regions of the Prajapatis, of superior happiness, abounding in every happiness, and shorn of sorrow. Belonging to those powerful ones from whom the creation has originated, they are coveted by all persons. If you go there, even their shall I go and compel you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ये राजानो राजसूयाभिषिक्ता धर्मात्मानो रक्षितारः प्रजानाम्। स्तेषां लोका धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Those kings who have bathed upon the termination of the Rajasuya sacrifice, who are gifted with righteous souls, who have protected their subjects properly, and who have washed their limbs with purified water upon the termination of the Horsesacrifice, go to such regions. Indeed Dhritarashtra shall not go there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच ततः परं भान्ति लोकाः सनातनाः सुपुण्यगन्धा विरजा वीतशोकाः। तस्मिन्नहं दुर्लभे चाप्यधृष्ये गवां लोके हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये॥
en: Gautama said Next to those, shine in beauty those eternal regions, full of delicious perfumes, freed from passion, and transcending all sorrow. Those are the regions of kine, very hard to get in, where oppression can never be. If you go there, I shall go even there and compell you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यो गोसहस्री शतदः समां समां गवां शती दश दद्याच्च शक्त्या। तथा दशभ्यो यश्च दद्यादिहैका पञ्चभ्यो वा दानशीलस्तथैकाम्॥ ये जीर्यन्ते ब्रह्मचर्येण विप्रा ब्राह्मीं वाचं परिरक्षन्ति चैव। स्ते तत्र मोदन्ति गवां निवासे॥
en: Dhritarashtra said He who, having a thousand kine, gives away a hundred kine every year, or having a hundred kine gives away ten every year to the best of his power, or possessing only ten or even five kine gives away therefrom one cow, and they who give a mature old age practising the vow of celibacy all their days, who obey the injunctions of the Vedas, and who, gifted with energy of mind, go to sacred waters and shrines, live happily in the region of kine.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: प्रभासं मानसं तीर्थे पुष्कराणि मह्वत्सरः। पुण्यं च नैमिषं तीर्थे बाहुदां करतोयिनीम्॥ गयां गयशिरश्चैव विपाशां स्थूलवालुकाम्। कृष्णां गङ्गां पञ्चनदं महाह्रदमथापि च॥ गोमती कौशिकी पम्पां महात्मानो धृतव्रताः। सरस्वतीदृषद्वत्यौ यमुनां ये तु यान्ति च॥ तत्र ते दिव्यसंस्थाना दिव्यमाल्यधराः शिवाः। प्रयान्ति पुण्यगन्धाढ्या धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र वै॥
en: They who go to Prabhasa and Manasa, the lakes of Pushkara, the large lake called Mahatsara the sacred forest of Naimisha, Vahuda, Karatoya, Ganga, Gayashiras, Vipasha, Sthulavaluka, Krishna, the five rivers (of the Punjab), the extensive lake called Mahahrada, Gomati, Kaushiki, Champa, Sarasvati, Drishadvati, and Yamuna, indeed those illustrious Brahmanas, firm in the observance of vows, who go to these sacred waters, go to the regions of which you speak. Gifted with celestial bodies and adorned with celestial garlands, those blessed individuals, always emitting the sweetest perfumes, go to the regions of joy. Indeed, Dhritarashtra shall not go there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच यत्र शीतभयं नास्ति न चोष्णभयमण्वपि। न क्षुत्पिपासे न ग्लानिर्न दुःखं न सुखं तथा॥ न द्वेष्यो न प्रियः कश्चिन्न बन्धुर्न रिपुस्तथा। न जरामरणे तत्र न पुण्यं न च पातकम्॥
en: Gautama said Next to these are regions where there is no fear of the least cold or heat, no hunger, no thirst, no pain, no sorrow, no joy, no one who is agreeable or disagreeable, no friend, and no enemy, no decrepitude and no death, and where there is neither virtue nor sin.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: तस्मिन् विरजसि स्फीते प्रज्ञासत्त्वव्यवस्थिते। स्वयंभुभवने पुण्ये हस्तिनं मे प्रदास्यसि॥
en: Going, even to that region which is freed from passion, which is full of happiness, and where there is wisdom and the quality of Sattwa, indeed, going to even that sacred abode of the selfcreate Brahman, I shall compel you to yield up this elephant to me.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच निर्मुक्ताः सर्वसङ्गैर्ये कृतात्मानो यतव्रताः। अध्यात्मयोगसंस्थानैर्युक्ताः स्वर्गगतिं गताः॥ ते ब्रह्मभवनं पुण्यं प्राप्नुवन्तीह सात्त्विकाः। न तत्र धृतराष्ट्रस्ते शक्यो द्रष्टुं महामुने॥
en: Dhritarashtra said They who are shorn of all attachments, who are gifted with purified souls, who steadily observe the foremost vows, who are given to Yoga which is the outcome of the pacification of the mind, and who have acquired the happiness of Heaventhose persons possessed of the quality of Sattwacome to the sacred region of Brahman. O great ascetic, you shall not be able to discover Dhritarashtra there.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच रथन्तरं यत्र बृहच्च गीयते यत्र वेदी पुण्डरीकैस्तृणोति। यत्रोपयाति हरिभिः सोमपीथी तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये।॥
en: Gautama said There where the foremost of Rathantaras is sung, where altars are covered with the sacred Kusha blades, for the celebration of Pundarika sacrifices, there where Soma drinking Brahmanas sojourn on cars drawn by excellent horses, going even there I shall compel you to yield up this elephant.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: बुध्यामि त्वां वृत्रहणं शतक्रतुं व्यतिक्रमन्तं भुवनानि विश्वा। दकार्थं ते मनसोऽभिषङ्गात्॥
en: I think you are the destroyer of Vritra, viz., the god who has celebrated a hundred sacrifices, engaged in passing through all the regions of the universe. I hope I have not through mental weakness, committed any fault by the words I have addressed you.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: शतक्रतुरुवाच मन्वागमं परिवादे गजस्या तस्माद् भवान् प्रणतं मानुशास्तु ब्रवीषि यत् तत् करवाणि सर्वम्॥
en: The God of a hundred sacrifices said Yes, I am Maghavat. I come on earth for seizing this elephant. I bow to you. Do you command me. I shall immediately accomplish all that you may be pleased to say.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच श्वेतं करेणुं मम पुत्रं हि नागं यं मेऽहार्षीर्दशवर्षाणि बालम्। स्तमेव मे देहि सुरेन्द्र नागम्॥
en: Gautama said Do you give me, O king, of the celestials, this white elephant that is so young, for it is only ten years of age. I have raised it as a child of my own. Living in this forest, it has grown under my eye and has been to me a dear companion. Do you set free this my child that you have seized and wish to take away.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: शतक्रतु उवाच अयं सुतस्ते द्विजमुख्य नाग आगच्छति त्वामभिवीक्षमाणः। पादौ च ते नासिकयोपजिघ्रते श्रेयो ममाध्याहि नमश्च तेऽस्तु॥
en: The god of a hundred sacrifices said This elephant that has been a son, to you, O foremost of Brahmanas, comes to you loO king wistfully at you. See, it smells your feet with its nostrils. My salutations to you. Do you pray for my wellbeing.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: गौतम उवाच शिवं सदैवेह सुरेन्द्र तुभ्यं ध्यायामि पूजां च सदा प्रयुञ्ज। ममापि त्वं शक्र शिवं ददस्व त्वया दत्तं प्रतिगृह्णामि नागम्॥
en: Gautama said O king, of the celestials, I do always think of your good. I always offer you worship. Do you also, O Shakra, impart your blessings to me. Given by you, I accept this elephant.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: शतक्रतुरुवाच येषां वेदा निहिता वै गुहायां मनीषिणां सत्यवतां महात्मनाम्। तेषां त्वयैकेन महात्मनास्मि वृद्धस्तस्मात् प्रीतिमांस्तेऽहमद्य॥
en: The God of a hundred sacrifices said Amongst all those great and foremost of Rishis, who firmly follow truth and who have the Vedas planted in their heart, you alone have been able to recognise me. Therefore I am exceedingly pleased with you.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: हन्तैहि ब्राह्मण क्षिप्रं सह पुत्रेण हस्तिना। त्वं हि प्राप्तुं शुभाँल्लोकानह्नाय च चिराय च॥
en: Do you, therefore, O Brahmana, come with me speedily, accompanied by this your son. You are worthy of going to various regions of great happiness, without the delay of even a single day.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: भीष्म उवाच स गौतमं पुरस्कृत्य सह पुत्रेण हस्तिना। दिवमाचक्रमे वज्री सद्भिः सह दुरासदम्॥
en: Bhishma said Having said these words, the holder of the thunderbolt, taking Gautama with him and placing him before, along with his son, viz., that elephant, went to Heaven, that is difficult of attainment by even the pious.

description: The various ends of righteous persons after death. The discourse between Goutama and Vasava
sn: इदं यः शृणुयान्नित्यं यः पठेद् वा जितेन्द्रियः। स याति ब्रह्मणो लोकं ब्राह्मणो गौतमो यथा॥
en: He who would listen to this history every day or would recite it, controlling his senses all the while, will go to the region of Brahman even as Gautama himself. the while, will go to the region of Brahman even as Gautama himself.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दानं बहुविधाकारं शान्तिः सत्यमहिंसितम्। स्वदारतुष्टिश्चोक्ता ते फलं दानस्य चैव यत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have described to us the various kinds of gifts, tranquillity of soul, Truth, mercy, contentment with one's married wife, and the merits of gift.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: पितामहस्य विदितं किमन्यत् तपसो बलात्। तपसो यत्परं तेऽद्य तन्नो व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: You know very well, O grandfather, that there is nothing whose power is superior to that of Penances. You should explain to us what forms the highest penance.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: भीष्म उवाच तपः प्रचक्षते यावत् तावल्लोको युधिष्ठिर। मतं ममात्र कौन्तेय तपो नानशनात् परम्॥ अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। भगीरथस्य संवादं ब्रह्मणश्च महात्मनः॥
en: Bhishma said I tell you, O Yudhishthira, that one acquires a regions of happiness according to the nature of penances he practises. This is what I hold, O son of Kunti, that there is no Penance superior to abstention from food. Regarding it is recited the ancient discourse between Bhagiratha and the illustrious Brahman.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: अतीत्य सुरलोकं च गवां लोकं च भारत। ऋषिलोकं च सोऽगच्छद् भगीरथ इति श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard, O Bharata, that Bhagiratha attained to that region which is superior to that of the celestials of kine, and of the Rishis.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: तं तु दृष्ट्वा वचः प्राह ब्रह्मा राजन् भगीरथम्। कथं भगीरथागास्त्वमिमं लोकं दुरासदम्॥
en: Seeing this, O monarch, the Grandfather Brahman, addressing Bhagirama, said, How, O Bhagiratha, have you attained to this region that is so hard to get at.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: न हि देवा न गन्धर्वा न मनुष्या भगीरथ। आयान्त्यतप्ततपसः कथं वै त्वमिहागतः॥
en: Neither the celestials, nor Gandharvas, nor mankind, o Bhagiratha, succeed in coming here without having performed the severest austerities. How, indeed, have you come by this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: भगीरथ उवाच निष्काणां वै ह्यददं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः शतं सहस्राणि सदैव दानम्। ब्राह्यं व्रतं नित्यमास्थाय विद्वन् न त्वेवाहं तस्य फलादिहागाम्॥
en: Bhagiratha said I used to make gifts of hundred thousands of gold coins to the Brahmanas practising the vow of celibacy all the while. It is not by dint of the merit of those, gifts, O learned one, that I have acquired this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: नेकादशैकादशकान् क्रतूंश्च। ज्योतिष्टोमानां च शतं यदिष्टं फलेन तेनापि च नागतोऽहम्॥
en: I celebrated the Ekaratri (onenight's) sacrifice (consisting of fasts and gifts) for ten times, and the Pancharatri (fivenights) sacrifices for as many times. I performed eleven times the Ekadashratri sacrifice. I performed a hundred times the great sacrifices of Jyotishtoma. It is not, however, through the merits of those sacrifices that I have acquired this region of happiness.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: यच्चावसं जाह्नवीतीरनित्यः शतं समास्तप्यमानस्तपोऽहम्। अदां च तत्राश्वतरीसहस्रं नारीपुरं न च तेनाहमागाम्॥
en: For a hundred years I lived continuously by the side of the sacred Jahnavi, all the while performed the severest austerities. There I made gifts to the Brahmanas of thousands of males and numberless female slaves.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: दशायुतानि चाश्वानां गोऽयुतानि च विंशतिम्। पुष्करेषु द्विजातिभ्यः प्रादां शतसहस्रशः॥
en: By the side of the Pushkara lake I made gifts to the Brahmanas, for a hundred thousand times, a hundred thousand horses, and two hundred thousand kine.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: सुवर्णचन्द्रोत्तमधारिणीनां कन्योत्तमानामददं सहस्रम्। षष्टिं सहस्राणि विभूषितानां जाम्बूनदैराभरणैर्न तेन॥
en: I also gave away a thousand women of great beauty, each adorned with golden moons, and sixty thousand more, decked with ornaments of pure gold. It is not, however, through the merits of those deeds that I have succeeded in acquiring these regions.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: स्वेकैकशो दश गा लोकनाथ। समानवत्साः पयमा समन्तिताः सुवर्णकांस्योपदुहा न तेन॥
en: O lord of the universe, performing those sacrifices known as Gosava, I gave away ten Arvudas of kine, presenting each Brahmana with ten kine, each of whom was accompanied with her calf, each of whom gave milk at the time, and with each of whom were given a vessel of gold and one white brass for milking her.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: आप्तोर्यामेषु नियतमेकैकस्मिन् दशाददम्। गृष्टीनां क्षीरदात्रीणां रोहिणीनां शतानि च॥
en: Celebrating many Soma sacrifices, I gave away to cach Brahinana ten kine each of whom gave milk, and each of whom had brought forth only her first calf, besides making presents to them of hundreds of kine belonging to that kind which is known by the name of Rohini.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: दोग्ध्रीणां वै गवां चापि प्रयुतानि दशैव ह। प्रादां दशगुणं ब्रह्मन् न तेनाहमिहागतः॥
en: I also gave away to the Brahmanas twice ten Prayutas of other kine, all giving milk, It is not through the merit of those gifts, O Brahman, that I have succeeded in acquiring to this region of happiness.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: वाजिनां बाह्निजातानामयुतान्यददं दशा कर्काणां हेममालानां न च तेनाहमागतः॥
en: I also gave away a hundred thousand horses of the Valhika breed, all of white complexion, and adorned with garlands of gold. It is not, however, through the merits of those deeds that I have acquired this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: कोटीश्च काञ्चनस्याष्टौ प्रादां ब्रह्मन् दशान्वहम्। एकैकस्मिन् क्रतौ तेन फलेनाहं च चागतः॥
en: I gave also eight crores of golden coins to the Brahmanas, O Brahmana, and another ten crores also in each sacrifice that I celebrated. It is not, however, through the merits of those deeds that I have acquired this region of happiness.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: वाजिनां श्यामकर्णानां हरितानां पितामह। प्रादां हेमस्रजां ब्रह्मन् कोटीर्दश च सप्त च॥
en: I also gave away seventeen crors of horses, O Grandfather, each of green colour, each having black ears, and each adorned with garlands of gold.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: ईषादन्तान् महाकायान् काञ्चनस्रग्विभूषितान्। पद्मिनो वै सहस्राणि प्रादां दश च सप्त च॥
en: I also gave away seventeen thousand huge elephants having teeth as large as ploughshares, each having those whirls on its body, which are called Padmas, and each bedecked with garlands of gold.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: अलंकृतानां देवेश दिव्यैः कनकभूषणैः। रथानां काञ्चनाङ्गानां सहस्राण्यददं दशा॥
en: I gave away ten thousand cars, Grandfather, whose parts were made of gold, and which were adorned with various ornaments of gold.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: सप्त चान्यानि युक्तानि वाजिभिः समलंकृतः। दक्षिणावयवाः केचिद् वेदैर्ये सम्प्रकीर्तिताः॥
en: vast sum I also gave away seven thousand other cars with horses yoked to each. All the horses that were yoked to them were adorned with omaments of gold. Those cars represented the presents of a sacrifice and were of exactly that kind which is indicated in the Vedas.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: वाजपेयेषु दशसु प्रादां तेष्वपि चाप्यहम्। शक्रतुल्यप्रभावाणामिज्यया विक्रमेण ह॥
en: In the ten great Vajapeya sacrifices that I celebrated I gave away a thousand heroes each gified with the power of Indra himself, judged by their prowess and the sacrifices they had celebrated.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: सहस्रं निष्ककण्ठानामददं दक्षिणामहम्। विजित्य भूपतीन् सर्वानथैरिष्ट्वा पितामह॥ अष्टभ्यो राजसूयेभ्यो न च तेनाहमागतः।
en: Spending a of money, O Grandfather, and celebrating eight Rajasuya Sacrifices. I gave away to the Brahmanas who officiated in them, a thousand kings whose necks were adorned with garlands of gold, after having defeated them in battle. It is not, however, through the merits of those deeds that I have acquired this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: स्रोतश्च यावद्गङ्गायाश्छन्नमासीज्जगत्पते॥ दक्षिणाभिः प्रवृत्ताभिर्मम नागां च तत्कृते। वाजिनां च सहस्रे द्वे सुवर्णशतभूषित॥ वरं ग्रामशतं चाहमेकैकस्य त्रिधाददम्।
en: In those sacrifices, O Lord of the universe, I made presents as profuse as the stream of Ganga herself. Each Brahmana I gave two thousand elephants decked with gold, as many horses adorned with golden ornaments, and a hundred villages of the best kind.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: तपस्वी नियताहारः शममास्थाय वाग्यतः॥ दीर्घकालं हिमवति गङ्गायाश्च दुरुत्सहाम्। मूर्धा धारां महादेवः शिरसा यामधारयत्। न तेनाप्यहमागच्छं फलेनेह पितामह॥
en: Indeed, I gave these thrice to each Brahmana obscrvant of penances, living on regulated dict, adopting tranquillity of soul, and controlling speech, I lived for a long time on the breast of Himavat by the side of that Ganga whose irresistible current was borne by Mahadeva on his head. It is not through the merit of these deeds, O grandfather, that I have acquired this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: शम्याक्षेपैरयजं यच्च देवान् साद्यस्कानामयुतैश्चापि यत्तत्। त्रयोदशद्वादशाहैश्च देव सपौण्डरीकान्न च तेषां फलेन॥
en: Throwing the Shami, I worshipped the gods in numberless such sacrifices as are completed in course of single day, and such others as take twelve days for completing, and others still as can be completed in thirteen days, besides many Pundarikas. I have not acquired this region through the merits of any of those sacrifices.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: अष्टौ सहस्राणि ककुह्मिनामहं शुक्लर्षभाणामददं द्विजेभ्यः। एकैकं वै काञ्चनं शृंगमेभ्यः पत्नीश्चैषामददं निष्ककण्ठीः॥
en: I gave to the Brahmanas eight thousands of white bulls, each possessed of a beautiful hump, and each having one of its horns covered with gold. To them I also gave beautiful wives whose necks were adorned with chains of gold.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: हिरण्यरत्नानिचयानददं रत्नपर्वतान्। धनधान्यसमृद्धाश्च ग्रामाश्चान्ये सहस्रशः॥
en: I also gave away inasses of gold and wealth of other kinds. I gave away hills of gems and valuable stones. I gave away Villages, thousands in number and filled with wealth and corn.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: शतं शतानां गृष्टीनामददं चायतन्द्रितः। इष्ट्वा कैर्महायज्ञै ाह्मणेभ्यो न तेन च॥
en: With all my senses about me, I gave away the Brahmanas a hundred thousand kine each of whom had brought forth only her first calf, at many great sacrifices which I celebrated. It i is not, however, through the merits of those। deeds that I have acquired this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: द्विादशाहैरश्वमेधैश्च देव। स्तेषां फलेनेह च चागतोऽस्मि।॥
en: I worshipped the celestials in a sacrifice that is completed in eleven days. Twice I worshipped them in sacrifices that are completed in twelve days. I worshipped ther, also many a time in the Horsesacrifices. I performed the Arkayana sacrifice sixteen times, it is not through the merits of those deeds that I have acquired this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: निष्कैककण्ठमददं योजनायतं तद्विस्तीर्णं काञ्चपादपानाम्। वनं वृतानां रत्नविभूषितानां न चैव तेषामागतोऽहं फलेन।।
en: I also gave each Branis. 17 a forest of Kanchana trees extending for Yojana on every side, and with each tree adorned with jewels and gems. It is not through the merits of that deed that I have acquired this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: मक्रोधनोऽकरवं त्रिंशतोऽब्दान्। शतं गवामष्टशतानि चैव दिने दिने ह्यददं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः॥
en: For thirty years, with heart perfectly freed from anger, I observed the Turayana vow that has very superior merit, and gave away to the Brahmanas every day nine hundred kine.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: पयस्विनीनामथ रोहिणीनां तथैवान्याननडुहो लोकनाथ। प्रादां नित्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सुरेश नेहागतस्तेन फलेन चाहम्॥
en: Indeed, O Lord of the universe, every one of those kine belonged to the Rohini species and gave milk at the time I gave them away. It is not through the merits of those deeds, O king of the deities, that I have acquired this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: त्रिंशदग्नीनहं ब्रह्मनयजं यच्च नित्यदा। अष्टाभिः सर्वमेधैश्च नरमेधैश्च सप्तभिः॥
en: a I adored thirty fires, O Brahman, every day. I worshipped the celestials in eight sacrifices in which the fat of all animals was poured on the fire. I worshipped them in seven sacrifices in which the fat of human beings was poured on the fire.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: दशभिर्विश्वजिद्भिश्च शतैरष्टादशोत्तरैः। न चैव तेषां देवेश फलेनाहमिहागमम्॥
en: ored them in thousand and livcrtyeight Vishvajit sacrifices. It is not through the merits of those sacrifices, O king of all the celestials, that I have acquired this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: सरवां बाहुदायां च गङ्गायामथ नैमिषे। गवां शतानामयुतमददं न च तेन वै॥
en: On the banks of Sarayu and Vahuda and Ganga, as also in the forest of Naimisha, I gave away millions of kine to the Brahmanas. It is not through the merits of those deeds that I have acquired this region.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: इन्द्रेण गुह्यं निहितं वै गुहायां यद्भार्गवस्तपसेहाभ्यविन्दत्। जाज्वल्यमानमुशनस्तेजसेह तत्साधयामासमहं वरेण्य॥
en: The vow of fast had been known to Indra. He had, however, kept it a secret. Shukra, the descendent of Bhrigu, gained a knowledge of it by means of spiritual sight acquired through penances. Burning with energy as he does, it is Ushanas who first made it known to the universe. I observed that vow, O boongiving Deity.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: ततो मे ब्राह्मणास्तुष्टास्तस्मिन् कर्मणि साधिते। सहस्रमृषयश्चासन् ये वै तत्र समागताः॥
en: When I finished that very superior vow, the Brahmanas became all pleased with me. A thousand Rishis came there.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: उक्तस्तैरस्मि गच्छ त्वं ब्रह्मलोकमिति प्रभो। प्रीतेनोक्तसहस्रेण ब्राह्मणानामहं प्रभो। इमं लोकमनुप्राप्तो मा भूत् तेऽत्र विचारणा॥
en: All those Brahmanas and Rishis, O powerful lord, pleased with me, said, do you go to the region of Brahman! It is on account of the merits of that vow that I have succeeded in acquiring this region of very superior happiness. There is no doubt in this.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: कामं यथावद्विहितं विधात्रा पृष्टेन वाच्यं तु मया यथावत्। तपो हि नान्यच्चानशनान्मतं मे नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद।
en: Asked by the Supreme Creator of all things, I have duly explained the merits of the vow of fast. In my opinion, there is no penance higher than fast. I bow to you, o foremost of all the celestials. Be propitiated with me.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तवन्तं ब्रह्मा तु राजानं स भगीरथम्। पूजयामास पूजाहँ विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: Bhishma said King Bhagiratha, who had said so and who was worthy of every honour, was, on the conclusion of his speech, honoured by Brahman according to the rites ordained for that purpose.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: तस्मादनशनैर्युक्तो विप्रान् पूजय नित्यदा। विप्राणां वचनात् सर्वं परत्रेह च सिध्यति॥
en: Do you, therefore, O Yudhishtira, observe the vow of fast and adore the Brahmanas every day. The words uttered by Brahmanas can do every things both in this world and in the next.

description: The highest penance described. The discourse between Bhagiratha and Brahma
sn: वासोभिरन्नैर्गोभिश्च शुभैनैवेशिकैरपि। शुभैः सुरगणैश्चापि स्तोष्या एव द्विजास्तथा। एतदेव परं गुह्यमलोभेन समाचर॥
en: Indeed, the Brahmanas should ever be pleased with gifts of dresses and food and whitecomplexioned kine and good dwelling houses and palaces. The very celestials should please the Brahmanas. Freeing yourself from cupidity, do you practice this vow of very superior merit that is not known to all.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच शतायुरुक्तः पुरुषः शतवीर्यश्च जायते। कस्मान्नियन्ते पुरुषा बाला अपि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Man, it is said, is gifted with a period of life extending for a hundred years, and with great energy and power. Why then, O grandfather, do human beings die even in their youth?

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: आयुष्मान् केन भवति अल्पायुर्वाऽपि मानवः। केन वा लभते कीर्ति केन वा लभते श्रियम्॥
en: By what does a man become longlived, and by what is his life shortened? Through what does a man acquire the fame that depends upon great deeds? Through what does one acquire wealth and prosperity?

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण जपहोमैस्तथौषधैः। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Is it by penances, or celibacy or silent recitation of sacred Mantras, or drugs? Is it by his deeds, or mind, or speech? Do you explain to me this, O grandfather.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्र तेऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि यन्मां त्वमनुपृच्छसि। अल्पायुर्येन भवति दीर्घायुर्वाऽपि मानवः॥
en: Bhishma said I shall tell you what you ask me. In fact, I shall tell you what the reason is for which one becomes short lived, and what the reason is for which one becomes longlived.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: येन वा लभते कीर्तिं येन वा लभते श्रियम्। यथा वर्तयन् पुरुषः श्रेयसा सम्प्रयुज्यते॥
en: I shall also explain to you the reason for which one succeeds in winning the fame that depends on great deeds, and the reason for which one succeeds in acquiring riches and prosperity. Indeed, I shall enlighten you about the manner in which one must live in order to be possessed of what is good for him. one own

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: आचाराल्लभते ह्यायुराचराल्लभते श्रियम्। आचारात् कीर्तिमाप्नोति पुरुषः प्रेत्य चेह च॥
en: It is by conduct that one acquires a long life, and it is by conduct that one acquires riches and prosperity. Indeed, it is by conduct that one acquires the fame that depends upon great deeds both in this world and in the next.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: दुराचारो हि पुरुषो नेहायुर्विन्दते महत्। त्रसन्ति यस्माद् भूतानि तथा परिभवन्ति च॥
en: The man whose conduct is improper or wicked never acquires a long life. All creatures fear such a man and are oppressed by him.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: तस्मात् कुर्यादिहाचारं यदीच्छेद् भूतिमात्मनः। अपि पापशरीरस्य आचारो हन्त्यलक्षणम्॥
en: If, therefore, wishes his advancement and prosperity, one should, in this world, follow the path of rightcousness and conduct himself properly. Good conduct succeeds in removing the inauspiciousness and misery of even one that is sinful.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: आचारलक्षणो धर्मः सन्तश्चारित्रलक्षणाः। साधूनां च यथावृत्तमेतदाचारलक्षणम्॥
en: Virtue is singled out by conduct. The good and virtuous are so on account of the conduct they follow. The marks, again, of good conduct are afforded by the deeds of those that are good Or righteous.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अप्यदृष्टं श्रवादेव पुरुषं धर्मचारिणम्। भूतिकर्माणि कुर्वाणं तं जनाः कुर्वते प्रियम्॥
en: People regard that who righteously and who does good acts even if they only hear of him without actually seeing him.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: ये नास्तिका निष्क्रियाश्च गुरुशास्त्राभिलंघिनः। अधर्मज्ञा दुराचारारते भवन्ति गतायुधः॥
en: The atheists they who are destitute of all acts, they who are disobedient to preceptors and violate the injunctions of the scriptures, they who are unacquainted with and, therefore, unobservant of duties, and they who are wicked of conduct, become shortlived. man acts

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: विशीला भिन्नमर्यादा नित्यं संकीर्णमैथुनाः। अल्पायुषो भवन्तीह नरा निरयगामिनः॥
en: They who are of improper conduct, they who violate all restraints, they who are unscrupulous about sexual congress, become shortlived here and have to go to Hell hereafter.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: सर्वलक्षणहीनोऽपि समुदाचारवान् नरः। श्रद्वधानोऽनसूयुश्च शतं वर्षाणि जीवति॥
en: Even those men live for a hundred years who, though destitute of all accomplishments, follow propriety and righteousness of conduct and become endued with faith and freed from malice.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अक्रोधनः सत्यवादी भूतानामविहिसंकः। अनसूयुरजिह्मश्च शतं वर्षाणि जीवति॥
en: He who is free from anger, who is truthful in speech, who never does any injury to any creature in the universe, who is shorn of malice and crookedness and insincerity, succeeds in living for a hundred years.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: लोष्ठमर्दी तृणच्छेदी नखखादी च यो नरः। नित्योच्छिष्ट: संकुसुको नेहायुर्विन्दते महत्॥
en: He who always breaks little clods of carth, or tears up the grass that grows under his feet, or cuts off his nails with his teeth, or is always impure, or very restless, never succeeds in living long.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: ब्राह्म मुहूर्ते बुध्येत धर्मार्थो चानुचिन्तयेत्। उत्थायाचम्य तिष्ठेत पूर्वो संध्यां कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: One should wake up from sleep at the hour known as the Brahma Muhurta and then think of both religion and worldly profit. Getting up from bed, one should then wash his face and mouth, and joining his hands in an attitude of respect, then say the morning prayers.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: एवमेवापरां संध्या समुपासीत वाग्यतः। नेक्षेतादित्यमुद्यन्तं नास्तं यान्तं कदाचन॥
en: In this way, one should when evening sets in say his evening prayers also, controlling speech the while. One should never look at the rising sun, nor at the setting sun.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: नोपसृष्टं न वारिस्थं न मध्यं नभसो गतम्। ऋषयो नित्यसंध्यत्वाद् दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुवन्॥
en: Nor should one look at the sun when he is in eclipse; nor at his image in the water, nor at midday when he is at the meridian. The Rishis, on account of their worshipping the two twilight's, with great regularity succeeded in acquiring longevity.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: तस्मात् तिष्ठेत् सदा पूर्वो पश्चिमां चैव वाग्यतः। ये न पूर्वामुपासन्ते द्विजाः संध्यां न पाश्चिमाम्॥ सर्वोस्तान् धार्मिको राजा शूद्रकर्माणि कारयेत्। परदारा न गन्तव्या सर्ववर्णेषु कर्हिचित्॥
en: Hence one should controlling speech, say his prayers regularly at the two twilight's. As regards those Brahmanas who do not say their prayers at the two twilight's, a righteous king should set them to perform such deeds as are ordained for the Shudras. Persons of every caste should never have sexual congress with other people's wives.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: न हीदृशमनायुष्यं लोके किंचन विद्यते। यादृशं पुरुषस्येह परदारोपसेवनम्॥
en: There is nothing that shortens life so: cffcctually as sexual union with other people's wives.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: यावन्तो रोमकूपाः स्युः स्त्रीणां गात्रेषु निर्मिताः। तावद् वर्षसहस्राणि नरकं पर्युपासते॥
en: The adulterer shall have to live in Hell for as many thousand years as the number of pores on the bodies of the women with whom he may cominit the offence.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: प्रसाधनं च केशानामञ्जनं दन्तधावनम्। पूर्वाह्न एव कार्याणि देवतानां च पूजनम्॥
en: One should dress one's hair, apply collyrium to one's eyes, and wash one's teeth, as also worship the celestials in the forenoon.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: पुरीषमूत्रे नोदीक्षेन्नाधितिष्ठेत् कदाचन। नातिकल्यं नातिसायं न च मध्यन्दिने स्थिते॥ नाज्ञातैः सह गच्छेत नैको न वृषलैः सह। पन्था देयो ब्राह्मणाय गोभ्यो राजभ्य एव च॥ वृद्धाय भारतप्ताय गर्भिण्यै दुर्बलाय च। प्रदक्षिणं च कुर्वीत परिज्ञातान् वनस्पतीन्॥ चतुष्पथान् प्रकुर्वीत सर्वानेव प्रदक्षिणान्। मध्यन्दिने निशाकाले अर्धरात्रे च सर्वदा॥ चतुष्पथं न सेवेत उभे संध्ये तथैव च। उपानही च वस्त्रं च धृतमन्यैर्न धारयेत्॥
en: One should not gaze at urine or faeces, or tread on it or touch it with one's feet. One should not see out on a journey at early dawn, or at midday, or in the evening twilight, or with a companion that is unknown, or with a Shudra, or alone. While passing along a road, one should standing aside, always give way to a Brahmana, to kine, to kings, to an old man, to one that is loaded with a burthen, to a woman big with child, or to one that is weak. When one meets a large tree that is known, one should walk round it. One should also, when coming upon the crossing of four roads, walk round it before pursuing his journey. At midday, or at midnight, or at night in general, or at the two twilight's, one should not proceed the crossings of the four roads. One should never wear sandals or clothes that have been worn by another.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: ब्रह्मचारी च नित्यं स्यात् पादं पादेन नाक्रमेत्। अमावास्यां पौर्णमास्यां चतुर्दश्यां च सर्वशः॥ अष्टम्यां सर्वपक्षाणां ब्रह्मचारी सदा भवेत्। आक्रोशं परिवादं च पैशुन्यं च विवर्जयेत्॥
en: One should always observe the vow of celibacy, and should never cross his legs. One should observe the vow of celibacy on the day of the new moon, as also, on that of the full moon, as also on the eighth lunar day of both fortnights. One should never cat the flesh of animals not killed in sacrifices. One should never eat the flesh of the back of an animal. One should avoid censuring and calumniating others, as also all kinds of deceitful conduct.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: नारुन्तुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत। ययास्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत न तां वदेद् रुशती पापलोक्याम्॥
en: One should never cut others with wordy arrows. Indeed, one should never utter any cruel speech. One should never accept anything in gift from a person who is low and vulgar. One should never utter such words as pain other people or as are inauspicious or as are sinful.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: वाक्सायका वदनान्निष्पतन्ति यैराहतः शोचति रात्र्यहानि। परस्य वा मर्मसु ये पतन्ति तान् पण्डितो नावसृजेत् परेषु॥
en: Wordy arrows fall from the mouth. Pierced therewith, the victim grieves day and night. The wise man should never shoot them for cutting the vitals of other people.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: रोहते सायकैर्विद्धं वनं परशुना हतम्। वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम्॥
en: A forest, pierced with arrows or cut down with the axe, grows again. The man, however, who is pierced with words unwisely spoken, becomes the victim of wounds that fester and bring on death.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: कर्णिनालीकनाराचान् निर्हरन्ति शरीरतः। वाक्शल्यस्तु न निहर्तुं शक्यो हृदिशयो हि सः॥३४
en: Barbed arrows and Nalikas and broadheaded arrows are capable of being extracted from the body. Wordy arrows, however, are incapable of being extracted, for they lie einbedded in the very heart.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: हीनाङ्गानतिरिक्ताङ्गान् विद्याहीनान् विगर्हितान्। रूपद्रविणहीनांश्च सत्त्वहीनांश्च नाक्षिपेत्॥
en: One should not taunt a person who is defective of a limb or who has a limb in excess. or one who is shorn of learning, or one who is niserable, or one who is ugly or poor, or one who is shorn of strength.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: नास्तिक्यं वेदनिन्दां च देवतानां च कुत्सनम्। द्वेषस्तम्भोऽभिमानं च तैक्ष्ण्यं च परिवर्जयेत्॥
en: One should avoid atheism, vilifying the Vedas, censuring the celestials, malice, pride, arrogance, and harshness.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: परस्य दण्डं नोद्यच्छेत् क्रद्धो नैनं निपातयेत्। अन्यत्र पुत्राच्छिष्याच्च शिक्षार्थं ताडनं स्मृतम्॥
en: One should not angrily, take up the rod of punishment for laying it upon another. Only the son or the pupil, it has been said, can be mildly reprimanded for purposes of instruction.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: न ब्राह्मणान् परिवदेन्नक्षत्राणि न निर्दिशेत्। तिथिं पक्षस्य न ब्रूयात् तथास्यायुर्न रिष्यते॥
en: One should not vilify Brahmanas; nor should point at the stars with one's fingers. If asked, one should not say what the lunation is on a particular day. By telling it, his life becomes shortened.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: कृत्वा मूत्रपुरीषे तु रथ्यामाक्रम्य वा पुनः। पादप्रक्षालनं कुर्यात् स्वाध्याये भोजने तथा॥
en: Having answered calls of nature or having walked over a road, one should wash his feet. One should also wash his feet before sitting to recite the Vedas or to eat any food.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: त्रीणि देवाः पवित्राणि ब्राह्मणानामकल्पयन्। अदृष्टमद्भिर्निर्णिक्तं यच्च वाचा प्रशस्यते॥
en: These are the three things which are considered as pure and sacred by the celestials and as such fit for the Brahmana's use, viz., that whose impurity is unknown, that which has been washed in water, and that which has been well spoken of.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: संयावं कृसरं मांसं शष्कुलीं पायसं तथा। आत्मार्थं न प्रकर्तव्यं देवार्थं तु प्रकल्पयेत्॥
en: Samayava, Krishana, meat, Shashakuli, and Payasa should never be cooked for one's ownself. Whenever cooked, these should be offered to the celestials.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: नित्यमग्निं परिचरेद् भिक्षां दद्याच्च नित्यदा। वाग्यतो दन्तकाष्ठं च नित्यमेव समाचरेत्॥
en: One should attend every day to his sacred fire. One should every day give alms. One should, controlling speech the while, clean his teeth with the tooth-stick.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: न चाभ्युदितशायी स्यात् प्रायश्चित्ती तथा भवेत्। मातापितरमुत्थाय पूर्वमेवाभिवादयेत्॥ आचार्यमथवाप्यन्यं तथायुर्विन्दते महत्। वर्जयेद् दन्तकाष्ठानि वर्जनीयानि नित्यशः॥
en: One should never be in bed when the sun is up. If one fails any day to be up with the sun, he should then perform an expiation. Rising from bed, one should first salute his parents, and preceptors, or other elders worthy of respect. By so doing one acquires a long life. The toothstick should be thrown off when done with, and a new one should be used every day.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: भक्षयेच्छास्त्रदृष्टानि पर्वस्वपि विवर्जयेत्। उदङ्मुखश्च सततं शौचं कुर्यात् समाहितः॥
en: One should eat food which is not forbidden in the scriptures, abstaining from food of every kind on days of the new moon and the full moon. One should, with senses controlled, answer calls of nature, facing the north.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अकृत्वा देवपूजां च नाचरेद् दन्तधावनम्। अकृत्वा देवपूजां च नाभिगच्छेत् कदाचन। अन्यत्र तु गुरुं वृद्धं धार्मिकं वा विचक्षणम्॥ अवलोक्यो न चादर्शो मलिनो बुद्धिमत्तरैः।
en: One should not adore the celestials without having first washed his teeth. Without also adoring the celestials first, one should never repair to any person except his preceptor or one who is old in years or one who is righteous or one who is wise. Wise men should never see themselves in an unnolished or dirty mirror.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: न चाज्ञातां स्त्रियं गच्छेद् गर्भिणी वा कदाचन॥ उदक्शिरा न स्वपेत तथा प्रत्यक्शिरा न च।
en: One should never know a woman that is unknown or with one that is big with child.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: प्राक्शिरास्तु स्वपेद् विद्वानथवा दक्षिणाशिराः॥ न भग्ने नावशीर्णे च शयने प्रस्वपीत च।
en: One should never sleep with head turned towards the north or the west. One should not lie down upon a broken bedstead.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: नान्तर्धाने न संयुक्ते न च तिर्यक् कदाचन॥ न चापि गच्छेत् कार्येण समयाद् वापि नास्तिकैः।
en: One should not sleep on a bed without having examined it first with the help of a light. Nor should one sleep on a bed with another by his side. One should never sleep in a transverse direction. One should never make agreement with atheists or do anything in conjunction with them. an one

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: आसनं तु पदाऽऽकृष्य न प्रसज्जेत् तथा नरः॥ न नग्न: कर्हिचित् स्नायान्न निशायां कदाचन।
en: One should never drag a seat with the foot and sit on it. One should never bathe in a nude state nor at night.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: स्नात्वा च नावमृज्येत गात्राणि सुविचक्षणः॥ न चानुलिम्पेदस्नात्वा स्नात्वा वासो न निधुनेत्।
en: An intelligent person should never allow his limbs to be rubbed or pressed after bathing. One should never smear unguents upon his body without having first gone through bath. Having bathed, one should never wave his cloth in the air.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: न चैवार्द्राणि वासांसि नित्यं सेवेत मानवः॥ सजश्च नावकृष्येत न बहिर्धारयीत च।
en: One should not wear wet clothes every day. One should never take off his body the garlands of flowers one may wear, Nor should wear such garlands over his outer garments.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: उदक्यया च सम्भाषां न कुर्वीत कदाचन॥ नोत्सृजेत पुरीषं च क्षेत्रे ग्रामस्य चान्तिके।
en: One should never even talk with a woman during the period of her menses. One should not answer a call of nature on a field or at place too near an inhabited village.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: उभे मूत्रपुरीषे तु नाप्से कुर्यात् कदाचन॥ अन्नं बुभुक्षमाणस्तु त्रिर्मुखेन स्पृशेदपः।
en: One should never answer a call of nature on a piece of water. One should first wash his mouth, thrice with water before eating any food.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: भुक्त्वा चान्नं तथैव त्रिर्द्धिः पुनः परिमार्जयेत्॥ प्राङ्मुखो नित्यमश्रीयाद् वाग्यतोऽन्नमकुत्सयन्।
en: Having finished his meals, one should wash his mouth thrice with water and twice again. One should eat, with face turned east wards, his food, controlling speech the while and without censuring the food that is caten.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: प्रस्कन्दयेच्च मनसा भुक्त्वा चाग्निमुपस्पृशेत्॥ आयुष्यं प्राङ्मुखो भुडक्ते यशस्य दक्षिणामुखः।
en: One should always leave a residue of the food that is placed before one for eating. Having finished his meals, one should mentally touch fire. If one eats with face turned eastwards, he becomes longlived. By eating with face turned south wards, one acquires great fame.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: धन्यं पश्चान्मुखे भुङ्क्ते ऋतं भुङ्क्ते उदङ्मुखः॥ अग्निमालभ्य तोयेन सर्वान् प्राणानुपस्पृशेत्।
en: By eating with face turned westwards, one acquires great riches. By eating with face turned northwards, one becomes truthful in specch. Having finished his meals, one should wash all the upper holes of one's body with water.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: गात्राणि चैव सर्वाणि नाभिं पाणितले तथा॥ नाधितिष्ठेत् तुषं जातु केशभस्मकपालिकाः।
en: Likewise, all the limbs, the navel, and the palms of the hands should be washed with water. One should never sit upon husk of corn or upon hair, or upon ashes, or upon bones.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अन्यस्य चाप्यवस्नातं दूरतः परिवर्जयेत्॥ शान्तिहोमांश्च कुर्वीत सावित्राणि च धारयेत्।
en: One should, never use the water that has been used by another for bathing. One should always perform the Homa for propitiating the celestials, and recite the Savitri Mantras.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: निषण्णश्चापि खादेत न तु गच्छन् कदाचन॥ मूत्रं नोत्तिष्ठता कार्यं न भस्मनि न गोव्रजे।
en: One should always eat in a seated posture. One should never eat while walking. One should never answer a call of nature standing. One should never answer a call of nature on ashes or in a cowpen.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: आर्द्रपादस्तु भुञ्जीत नार्द्रपादस्तु संविशेत्॥ आर्द्रपादस्तु भुजानो वर्षाणां जीवते शतम्।
en: One should wash his feet before sitting to one's meals. One should never sit or lie down for slecp with wet feet. One who sits to his meals after having washed his feet, lives for a century.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: त्रीणि तेजांसि नोच्छिष्ट आलभेत कदाचन॥ अग्निं गां ब्राह्मणं चैव तथा ह्यायुर्न रिष्यते।
en: One should never touch these three things, while one is in an impure state, viz., fire, a cow and a Brahmana. By observing this rule one lives long.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: त्रीणि तेजांसि नोच्छिष्ट उदीक्षेत कदाचन॥ सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ चैव नक्षत्राणि च सर्वशः।
en: One should not, while he is in an impure state, cast one's eyes on these three things, viz., the sun, the moon and the stars.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: ऊर्ध्वं प्राणा ह्युत्क्रामन्ति यूनः स्थविर आयति॥ प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादाभ्यां पुनस्तान् प्रतिपद्यते।
en: The lifebreaths of a young man go up wards, when an old and venerable person comes to his house. He gets them back by standing up and properly saluting the guest.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अभिवादयीत वृद्धांश्च दद्याच्चैवासनं स्वयम्॥ कृताञ्जलिरुपासीत गच्छन्तं पृष्ठतोऽन्वियात्।
en: Old men should always be saluted. One should, upon seeing them, offer seats with his own hand. After the old man has taken his seat, a person should sit and remain with hands joined in respect. When an old man goes along the road, one should always follow him instead of walking ahead.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: न चासीतासने भिन्ने भिन्नकांस्यं च वर्जयेत्॥ नैकवस्त्रेण भोक्तव्यं न नग्नः स्नातुमर्हति।
en: One should never sit on a torn or broken seat. One should, without using it any longer, throw away a broken vessel of white brass. One should, never eat without a piece of upper garinent covering his body. One should never bathe in a nude state.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: स्वप्तव्यं नैव नग्नेन न चोच्छिष्टोऽपि संविशेत्॥ उच्छिष्टो न स्पृशेच्छीर्षं सर्वे प्राणास्तदाश्रयाः।
en: One should never sleep in a naked state. One should never even touch the remnants of other people's dishes and plates. One should never, while he is in an impure state, touch another's head, for it is said in the scriptures that the vital airs are all concentrated in the head.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: केशग्रहं प्रहारांश्च शिरस्येतान् विवर्जयेत्॥ न संहताभ्यां पाणिभ्यां कण्डूयेदात्मनः शिरः।
en: One should never strike another on the heads or seize another by the hair. One should prol join his hand together for scratching his head.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: न चाभीक्ष्णं शिरःस्नायात् तथा यायुर्न रिष्यते॥ शिरःस्नातस्तु तैलैश्च नाङ्गं किंचिदपि स्पृशेत्।
en: One should not, while bathing, repeatedly dip his head in water. By so doing one shortens one's life. One who has bathed by dipping the head in water should not, afterwards put oil to any part of his body.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: तिलसृष्टं न चाश्नीयात् तथास्यायुर्न रिष्यते॥ नाध्यापयेत् तथोच्छिष्टो नाधीयीत कदाचन।
en: One should never take his mcals without cating some sesame. One should never teach (the Vedas or any scriptures) at a time when he is impure. Nor should onc study while is impure.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: वाते च पूतिगन्धे च मनसापि न चित्नयेत्॥ अत्र गाथा यमोद्गीताः कीर्तयन्ति पुराविदः। आयुरस्य निकृन्तामि प्रजास्तस्याददे तथा॥ उच्छिष्टो यः प्राद्रवति स्वाध्यायं चाधिगच्छति। यश्चानध्यायकालेऽपि मोहादभ्यस्यति द्विजः॥ तस्य वेदः प्रणश्येत आयुश्च परिहीयते।
en: When a storm rises or a bad smell spreads itself in the atmosphere, he should never think of the Vedas. Persons knowing ancient history recite a Gatha sung by Yama in days of yore. He who runs while impure or studies the Veda under similar circumstances, indeed, that twice born Brahman who studies the Veda at forbidden times loses his Veda and shortens his life.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: तस्माद् युक्तो ह्यनध्याये नाधीयीत कदाचन॥ प्रत्यादित्यं प्रत्यनलं प्रति गां च प्रति द्विजान्। ये मेहन्ति च पन्थानं ते भवन्ति गतायुषः॥ उभे मूत्रपुरीषे तु दिवा कुर्यादुदङ्मुखः।
en: Hence, one should never study the Veda with rapt altention at forbidden times. They who answer a call of nature, with face towards the sun or towards a burning fire, or towards a cow, or towards a twice born person, or on the road, become shortlived. At day time both calls of nature should be answered with face turned towards the north.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: दक्षिणाभिमुखो रात्रौ तथा ह्यायुर्न रिष्यते॥ त्रीन् कृशान् नावजानीयाद् दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः। ब्राह्मणं क्षत्रियं सर्प सर्वे ह्याशीविषास्त्रयः॥ दहत्याशीविषः क्रद्धो यावत् पश्यति चक्षुषा।
en: At night, those calls should be answered facing the south. By so doing one does not shorten his life. One who wishes to live long should never disregard or insult any of these three, however weak or emaciated they may appear to be, viz., the Brahmana, the Kshatriya, and the snake. All three are gifted with dreadful poison. The snake, of angry, burns the victim with only a look of its eye.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: क्षत्रियोऽपि दहेत् क्रूद्धो यावत् स्पृशति तेजसा॥ ब्राह्मणस्तु कुलं हन्याद् ध्यानेनावेक्षितेन च।
en: The Kshatriya also, if angry, burns the object of his anger, as soon as he sees him, with his energy. The Brahmana, stronger than any of these two, destroys, not only the object of his anger but his entire family as well, not by looks alone but by thought also.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: तस्मादेतत् त्रयं यत्नादुपसेवेत पण्डितः॥ गुरुणा चैव निर्बधो न कर्तव्यः कदाचन।
en: A wise man should, therefore, tend these three carefully. One should never engage in any disputation with his preceptor.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अनुमान्यः प्रसाद्यश्च गुरुः क्रद्धो युधिष्ठिर॥ सम्यङ्गमिथ्या प्रवृत्तेऽपि वर्तितव्यं गुराविह।
en: O Yudhishthira, if the preceptor becomes angry, he should always be pacified with due honors. If the preceptor is entirely in the wrong, still one should follow and honour him.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: गुरुनिन्दा दहत्यायुर्मनुष्याणां न संशयः॥ दूरादावसथान्मूत्रं दूरात् पादावसेचनम्।
en: Forsooth, calumnious sayings against the preceptor always consume the lives of those who utter them. One should always answer a call of nature at a spot far distant from his dwelling place. One should wash his feet at a distance from his dwelling place.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: उच्छिष्टोत्सर्जनं चैव दूरे कार्यं हितैषिणा॥ रक्तमाल्यं न धार्य स्याच्छुक्लं धार्य तु पण्डितैः।
en: One should always throw the remnants of his dishes and plates at a spot distant from his dwelling place. Indeed, he who wishes for his own behoof should do all this. One should not wear garlands of red flowers. Indeed, the wise should wear garlands of white flowers.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: वर्जयित्वा तु कमलं तथा कुवलयं प्रभो॥ रक्तं शिरसि धार्य तु तथा वानेयमित्यपि।
en: Rejecting the lotus and the lily, O you of great might, one may bear on his head, however, a flower that is red, even if it be an aquatic one.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: काञ्चनीयापि माला या न सा दुष्यति कर्हिचित्।।८४ स्नातस्य वर्णकं नित्यमाई दद्याद् विशाम्पते।
en: A garland of gold can never become impure. After one has bathed, O king, he should use perfumes mixed with water.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: विपर्ययं न कुर्वीत वाससो बुद्धिमान् नरः॥ तथा नान्यधृतं धार्य न चापदशमेव च।
en: One should never wear his upper garment for covering the lower limbs or the lower garments for covering the upper ones. Nor should one wear clothes used by another. One should not, again, wear a piece of cloth that has not its fringes.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अन्यदेव भवेद् वासः शयनीये नरोत्तम॥ अन्यद् रथ्यासु देवानामायामन्यदेव हि।
en: When one goes to bed, O king, he should wear a different piece of cloth. When passing along a road, one should wear a different piece of cloth. So also, when adoring the celestials, one should wear a different piece of cloth.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: प्रियङ्गुचन्दनाभ्यां च बिल्वेन तगरेण च॥ पृथगेवानुलिम्पेत केसरेण च बुद्धिमान्।
en: The intelligent man should smear his limbs with unguents made of Priyangu, sandal wood, Bilva, Tagara, and Keshara.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: उपवासं च कुर्वीत स्नातः शुचिरलंकृतः॥ पर्वकालेषु सर्वेषु ब्रह्मचारी सदा भवेत्।
