en: In observing a fast, one should purify himself by a bath, and adorn his body with ornaments and unguents. One should always abstain from sexual union on days of the full moon and the new moon.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: समानमेकपात्रे तु भुजेन्नान्नं जनेश्वर॥ नालीढया परिहतं भक्षयीत कदाचन।
en: One should never, O king, eat off the same plate with another even if he be of his own or equal rank. Nor should one ever eat any food that has been prepared by a woman in her menses.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: तथा नोद्धृतसाराणि प्रेक्ष्यते नाप्रदाय च॥ न संनिकृष्टे मेधावी नाशुचेर्न च सत्सु च।
en: One should never eat any food or drink any liquid whose essence has been taken off. Nor should one eat anything without giving a part thereof to persons who wistfully gaze at the food that one happens to take. The intelligent man should never sit near an impure person. Nor should one sit near persons who are foremost in virtue.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: प्रतिषिद्धान्नधर्मेषु भक्ष्यान् भुञ्जीत पृष्ठतः॥ पिप्पलं च वटं चैव शणशाकं तथैव च। उदुम्बरं न खादेच्च भवार्थी पुरुषोत्तमः॥ न पाणौ लवणं विद्वान् प्राश्नीयान्न च रात्रिषु।
en: All food that is forbidden in religious rites should never be taken even on other occasions. The fruits of the Ficus religiosa and the Ficus Bengalensis as also the leaves of the Crotolaria Juncea, and the fruits of the Ficus glomerata, should never be eaten by one who seeks his own good. The flesh of goats, of kine, and the peacock, should never be eaten. One should also abstain from dried flesh and all flesh that is stale. The intelligent man should never eat any salt, taking it up with his hand.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: दधिसक्तून् न भुञ्जीत वृथा मासं च वर्जयेत्॥ सायंप्रातश्च भुञ्जीत नान्तराले समाहितः।
en: Nor should he eat curds and flour of fried barley at night. One should abstain also from flesh of animals not killed in sacrifices. One should, with rapt attention, eat once on the morning and once in the evening, abstaining entirely from all food in the interval.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: वालेन तु न भुञ्जीत परश्राद्धं तथैव च॥ वाग्यतो नैकवस्त्रश्च नासंविष्टः कदाचन।
en: One should never eat any food in which he may find out a hair. Nor should one eat at the Shraddha of an enemy. One should eat silently; one should never eat without covering his body with an upper garment, and without sitting down.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: भूमौ सदैव नाश्नीयान्नानासीनो न शब्दवत्॥ तोयपूर्वं प्रदायान्नमतिथिभ्यो विशाम्पते। पश्चाद् भुजीत मेधावी न चाप्यन्यमना नरः॥ समानमेकपक्त्यां तु भोज्यमनं नरेश्वर। विषं हालाहलं भुङ्क्ते योऽप्रदाय सुहृज्जने॥ पानीयं पायसं सक्तून् दधिसर्पिमधून्यपि। निरस्य शेषमन्येषां न प्रदेयं तु कस्यचित्॥ भुजानो मनुजव्याघ्र चैव शङ्कां समाचरेत्।
en: One should never eat any food placing it on the naked ground. One should never eat except in a sitting posture. One should never make any noise while eating. The intelligent man should first offer water and then food to one who has become his guest, and after liaving served the guest thus, should then take his meals himself. He who sits down to dinner in a line with friends and himself eats any food without giving thereof to his friends, is said to eat dreadful poison. As regards water and Payasa and flour of fried barley and curds and clarified butter and honey, one should never, after drinking or eating these, offer the residue thereof to others. One should never, O King, eat any foot hesitatingly.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: दधि चाप्यनुपानं वै न कर्तव्यं भवार्थिना॥ आचम्य चैकहस्तेन परिप्लाव्यं तथोदकम्।
en: One seeking one's own good, should never drink curds finishing his meal. After the meal is finished, one should wash his mouth and face with the (right) hand only, and taking a little water should then dip the toe of the right food in it.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अङ्गुष्ठं चरणस्याथ दक्षिणस्यावसेचयेत्॥ पाणिं मूर्ध्नि समाधाय स्पृष्ट्वा चाग्निं समाहितः।
en: After washing, one should touch the crown of his head with the (right) hand. With rapt attention, one should next touch fire.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: ज्ञातिश्रेष्ठ्यमवाप्नोति प्रयोगकुशलो नरः॥ अद्भिःप्राणान् समालभ्य नाभिं पाणितले तथा।
en: The man who knows how to observe all these ordinances carefully carefully succeeds in acquiring the foremost place among kinsmen. One should, after finishing his meals, wash his nose and eyes and ears and navel and both hands with water.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: स्पृशंश्चैव प्रतिष्ठेत च चाप्याट्टैण पाणिना॥ अङ्गुष्ठस्यान्तराले च ब्राह्यं तीर्थमुदाहृतम्।
en: One should not, however, keep his hands wet. Between the tip and the root of the thumb is situate the sacred Tirtha known by the name of Brahma.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: कनिष्ठिकायाः पश्चात् तु देवतीर्थमिहोच्यते॥ अङ्गुष्ठस्य च यन्मध्यं प्रदेशिन्याश्च भारत। तेन पित्र्याणि कुर्वीत स्पृष्ट्वापो न्यायतः सदा॥ परापवादं न ब्रूयानाप्रियं च कदाचन।
en: On the back of the little finger, it is said, is situate the Devatirtha. The intervening space between the thumb and the forefinger, Bharata, should be used for performing the Pitri rites, after touching water according to the ordinance. One should never vilify other people. Nor should one ever utter anything that is disagreeable.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: न मन्युः कश्चिदुत्पाद्यः पुरुषेण भवार्थिना॥ पतितैस्तु कथां नेच्छेद् दर्शनं च विवर्जयेत्।
en: The man who desires his own good, should never seek to bring on himself the wrath of others. One should never seek to talk with an outcaste. The very sight of such a personi should be shunned.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: संसर्ग च न गच्छेत तथाऽऽयुर्विन्दते महत्॥ न दिवा मैथुनं गच्छेन्न कन्यां न च बन्धकीम्।
en: One should never come in contact with degraded person. By avoiding such contact one succeeds in acquiring a long life. One should never indulge in sexual intercourse at day time. Nor should one know a maiden, or a harlot nor a barren woman.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: न चास्नातां स्त्रियं गच्छेत् तथायुर्विन्दते महत्॥ स्वे स्वे तीर्थे समाचम्य कार्ये समुपकल्पिते। त्रिः पीत्वाऽऽपो द्विः प्रमृज्य कृतशौचो भवेन्नरः।। इन्द्रियाणि सकृत्स्पृश्य त्रिरभ्युक्ष्य च मानवः।
en: One should never know a woman who has not bathed after the expiry of her menses. By avoiding such acts one succeeds in acquiring a long life. After washing the several limbs directed, in view of religious acts, one should wash his lips thrice, and once more twice. By doing this, one becomes purified and fit for religious rites. The several organs of sense should each be washed once, and water should also be sprinkled over the entire body.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: कुर्वीत पित्र्यं दैवं च वेददृष्टेन कर्मणा॥ ब्राह्मणार्थे च यच्छौचं तच्च मे शृणु कौरव। पवित्रं च हितं चैव भोजनाद्यंन्तयोस्तथा॥ सर्वशौचेषु ब्राह्मण तीर्थेन समुपस्पृशेत् निष्ठीव्य तु
en: Having done this, one should perforin the adoration of the departed Manes and celestials, according to the ordinances of Vedas. Listen to me, O you of Kuru's race, as I tell you what purification is cleansing and beneficial for a Brahmana. Before beginning to eat and after finishing the meal, and in all deeds requiring purification, the Brahmana should rinse his mouth with water placed on the limb called the Brahmatirtha.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: तथा क्षुत्त्वा स्पृश्यापो हि शुचिर्भवेत्॥ वृद्धो ज्ञातिस्तथा मित्रं दरिद्रो यो भवेदपि। गृहे वासयितव्यास्ते धन्यमायुष्यमेव च॥ गृहे पारावता धन्याः शुकाश्च सहसारिकाः।
en: After ejecting any matter from the throat or spitting, one should wash his mouth before he can become pure. A kinsman who happens to be old, or a friend who happens to be poor, should be accommodated in one's house and his comforts looked after as if he were a member of the family. By doing this, one succeeds in winning both fame and longevity. To keep pigeons as also parrots both male and female, in one's house is highly blessed.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: गृहेष्वेते न पापाय तथा वै तैलपायिकाः॥ उद्वीपकाश्च गृध्राश्च कपोता भ्रमरास्तथा। निवेशेयुर्यदा तत्र शान्तिमेव तदाऽऽचरेत्। अमङ्गल्यानि चैतानि तथाक्रोशो महात्मनाम्॥ महात्मनोऽतिगुह्यानि न वक्तव्यानि कर्हिचित्। अगम्याश्च न गच्छेत राज्ञः पत्नी सखीस्तथा॥
en: If these live in one's house, they succeed in removing calamity. The same is the case with cockroaches. If fireflies and vultures and woodpigeons and bees enter a house and live in it, acts of propitiating the celestials should be performed. These are creatures of evil omen, as also ospreys. One should never give out the secrets of great men; one should never have sexual union with a forbidden woman. Nor should one ever have such union with the consort of a king or with women who are the friends of qucens.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: वैद्यानां बालवृद्धानां भृत्यानां च युधिष्ठिर। बन्धूनां ब्राह्मपानां च तथा गारणिकस्य च॥ सम्बन्धिनां च राजेन्द्र तथाऽऽयुर्विन्दते महत्। ब्राह्मणस्थपतिभ्यां च निर्मितं यन्निवेशनम्॥ तदावसेत् सदा प्राज्ञो भवार्थी मनुजेश्वर। संध्यायां न स्वपेद् राजन् विद्यां न च समाचरेत्।।
en: One should never make friends with physicians, or with children, or with persons who are old, or with one's servants, O Yudhishthira. One should always provide for friends, for Brahmanas and for such as seek his protection. By doing this, O king, one acquires a long life. A wise man should live in such a house as has been constructed with the help of a Brahmana and an engineer skilled in his calling, if, indeed, O king, he seeks for his own behoof. One should not, O king, sleep at the evening twilight. Nor should one study at such hour for acquiring any any branch of knowledge.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: न भुञ्जीत च मेधावी तथायुर्विन्दते महत्। नक्तं न कुर्यात् पित्र्याणि भुक्त्वा चैव प्रसाधनम्।।११९
en: An intelligent man should never eat also at such an hour. By acting thus, one acquires a long life. One should never perform any act in honour of the departed Manes at night time. One should not adorn his body after finishing his meals.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: पानीयस्य क्रिया नक्तं न कार्या भूतिमिच्छता। वर्जनीयाश्चैव नित्यं सक्तवो निशि भारत॥
en: One should not bathe at night, if he seeks his own aggrandisement. One should also, O Bharata, always abstain from the flour of fried barley at night.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: शेषाणि चैव पानानि पानीयं चापि भोजने। सौहित्यं न च कर्तव्यं रात्रौ न च समाचरेत्॥
en: The residue of food and drink, as also the flowers with which one has adored the celestials, should never be used. Inviting a guest at night, one should never, with excessive courtesy, compel him to eat to his fill. Nor should one cat to his fill, at night.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: द्विजच्छेदं न कुर्वीत भुक्त्वा न च समाचरेत्। महाकुले प्रसूतां च प्रशस्ता लक्षणैस्तथा॥ वयःस्थां च महाप्राज्ञः कन्यामावोढुमर्हति। अपत्यमुत्पाद्य ततः प्रतिष्ठाप्य कुलं तथा॥ पुत्राः प्रदेया ज्ञानेषु कुलधर्मेषु भारत। कन्या चोत्पाद्य दातव्या कुलपुत्राय धीमते॥
en: One should not kill a bird (for eating it), especially after having fed it, A wise man should espouse a maiden born in a high family, gifted with auspicious marks, and of full age. Begetting children upon her and thus perpetuating his race by that means, one should make over his sons to a good preceptor for being educated generally, O Bharata, as also in the especial customs of the family, O monarch. The daughters that one may beget should be married to youths of respectable families, who are again possessed of intelligence.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: पुत्रा निवेश्याश्च कुलाद् भृत्या लभ्याश्च भारत। शिरःस्नातोऽथ कुर्वीत दैवं पित्र्यमथापि च॥
en: Sons should also be settled and a portion of the family inheritance given to them, O Bharata, as their provision. One should bathe by dipping his head in water before he sits down to perform any act in honour of the departed Manes or the deities.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: नक्षत्रे न च कुर्वीत यस्मिन् जातो भवेन्नरः। न प्रोष्ठपदयोः कार्यं तथाग्नेये च भारत॥
en: One should never perform a Shraddha under the constellation of his nativity. No Shraddha should be performed under any of the Bhadrapadas (prior or later), nor under the constellation Krittika, O Bharata.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: दारुणेषु च सर्वेषु प्रत्यरिं च विवर्जयेत्। ज्योतिषे यानि चोक्तानि तानि सर्वाणि वर्जयेत्।।१२७
en: The Shraddha should never be performed under any of those constellations that are considered as dreadful (such as Ashlesha, etc.,) and any of those that upon calculation, seem to be hostile. Indeed, in this matter, all these constellations should be avoided which are forbidden in astrology.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: प्राङ्मुख: श्मश्रुकर्माणि कारयेत् सुसमाहितः। उदङ्मुखो वा राजेन्द्र तथायुर्विन्दते महत्॥
en: One should sit facing either the east or the north while being shaved by a barber. By so doing, O great king, one succeeds in living long.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: परिवादं न च ब्रूयात् परेषामात्मनस्तथा। परिवादो धर्माय प्रोच्यते भरतर्षभ॥
en: One should neither 'vilify others reproach himself for, O chief of the Bharatas, it is said that calumny is sinful whether of others or of oneself.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: वर्जयेद् व्यंगिनीं नारी तथा कन्यां नरोत्तमा समा? व्यंगितां चैव मातुः स्वकुलजां तथा॥
en: In marrying, one should avoid a woman who is deficient of any limb. A maiden too, if such, should also be avoided. A woman of the same Pravars should also be avoided; as also one who is ill-formed in body; as also one who has been born in the race to which one's mother belongs. nor

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: वृद्धां प्रव्रजितां चैव तथैव च पतिव्रताम्। तथा निकृष्टवर्णां च वर्णोत्कृष्टां च वर्जयेत्॥ अयोनि च वियोनि च न गच्छेत विचक्षणः।
en: A wise man should never know a woman who is old, or one who has given up the domestic mode of life for entering the forest mode, or one who is faithful to her husband or one whose organs of generation are not healthy or well-formed.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: पिङ्गलां कुष्ठिनीं नारी न त्वमुद्दोढुमर्हसि॥ अपस्मारिकुले जातां निहीनां चापि वर्जयेत्। श्वित्रिणां च कुले जातां क्षयिणां मनुजेश्वर॥ लक्षणैरन्विता या च प्रशस्ता या च लक्षणैः। मनोज्ञां दर्शनीयां च तां भवान् वोढुमर्हति॥ महाकुले निवेष्टव्यं सदृशे वा युधिष्ठिर।
en: You should not marry a woman who is of a yellow colour, or one who is attacked with leprosy, or onc born in a family in which there has been epilepsy, or one that is low in birth and habits, or one that is born in a family in which the disease called leprosy has appeared, or one belonging by birth to a family in which there are early deaths. Only that maiden who is gifted with auspicious indications, and who is accomplished for all sorts of qualifications, who is agrecable and beautiful, should be married. One should marry, O Yudhishthira, in a family who is higher or at least equal to his OW1l.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अवरा पतिता चैव न ग्राह्या भूतिमिच्छता॥ अग्नीनुत्पाद्य यत्नेन क्रियाः सुविहिताश्च याः। वेदे च ब्राह्मणैः प्रोक्तास्ताश्च सर्वाः समाचरेत्।।१३६ न चेा स्त्रीषु कर्तव्या रक्ष्या दाराश्च सर्वशः।
en: One who is desirous of his own prosperity, should never marry a woman who is of an inferior caste or who has fallen away from the caste of her birth. Carefully lighting up the fire, one should perform all those acts which have been ordained and declared in the Vedas or by the Brahinanas. One should never seek to injure women. Wives should always be protected.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अनायुष्या भवेदीर्ध्या तस्मादीलुं विवर्जयेत्॥ अनायुष्यं दिवा स्वप्नं तथाभ्युदितशायिता।
en: Malice always shortens life. Hence, one should always abstain from entertaining malice. Sleep at day time shortens life. To sleep after the sunrise shortens life.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: प्रगे निशामाशु तथा नैवोच्छिष्टाः स्वपन्ति वै॥ पारदार्यमनायुष्यं नापितोच्छिष्टता तथा।
en: They who sleep at any of the twilight's, or at nightfall, or who go to sleep in, a state of impurity, have their lives shortened. Adultery always shortens life. One should not remain in a state of impurity after shaving.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: यत्नतो वै न कर्तव्यमभ्यासश्चैव भारत॥ संध्यायां च न भुञ्जीत न स्नायेन्न तथा पठेत्। प्रयतश्च भवेत् तस्यां न च किंचित् समाचरेत्॥ ब्राह्मणान् पूजयेच्चापि तथा स्नात्वा नराधिप।
en: One should, O Bharata, carefully abstain from reading or reciting the Vedas, and eating, and bathing at eventide. When the evening twilight sets in one should collect his senses for meditation, without doing any act. One should, O king, bathe and then adore the Brahinanas.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: देवांश्च प्रणमेत् स्नातो गुरुश्चाप्यभिवादयेत्॥ अनिमन्त्रितो न गच्छेत यज्ञं गच्छेत दर्शकः। अनर्चिते ह्यनायुष्यं गमनं तत्र भारत॥ न चैकेन परिव्रज्यं न गन्तव्यं तथा निशि।
en: Indeed, one should bathe before adoring the celestials and reverentially saluting the preceptor. One should never go to a sacrifice unless invited. Indeed, one may go there without an invitation, if he wishes to only see how the sacrifice is conducted. If one goes to a sacrifice without an invitation and if one does not on that account, receive proper adoration from the sacrificer, his life becomes shortened. One should never go alone on a journey to foreign parts. Nor should one ever go alone to any place at night.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अनागतायां संध्यायां पश्चिमायां गृहे वसेत्॥ मातुः पितुर्गुरूणां च कार्यमेवानुशासनम्। हितं चाप्यहितं चापि न विचार्यं नरर्षभ॥ धनुर्वेदे च वेदे च यत्नः कार्यो नराधिप।
en: Before evening sets in, one should return to his house and remain within it. One should always obey the commands of his parents and preceptor, without at all judging whether those commands are good or not. One should, O king, attend carefully of the Vedas and the military science.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: हस्तिपृष्ठेऽश्वपृष्ठे च रथचर्यासु चैव ह॥ यत्नवान् भव राजेन्द्र यत्नवान् सुखमेधते।
en: Do then, O king, carefully attend to the practice of riding an elephant, a horse and a warchariot. The man who attends to these with care, succeeds in acquiring happiness.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अप्रधृष्यश्च शत्रूणां भृत्यानां स्वजनस्य च॥ प्रजापालनयुक्तश्च न क्षतिं लभते क्वचित्।
en: Such a king succeeds in becoming unconquerable by enemies, and govern his servants and kinsmen without any of them being able to subjugate him. The king who attains to such a position and who carefully attends to the duty of protecting his subjects, has never to incur any loss.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: युक्तिशास्त्रं च ते ज्ञेयं शब्दशास्त्रं च भारत॥ गान्धर्वशास्त्रं च कला: परिज्ञेया नराधिप।
en: You should, O king, be proficient in logic, as also the science of words, the science of music and the four and the sixty branches of knowledge known by the name of Kala.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: पुराणमितिहासाश्च तथाख्याऽऽनानि यानि च॥ महात्मनां च चरितं श्रोतव्यं नित्यमेव ते।
en: One should every day hear the Puranas and the histories and all the other narratives that cxist, as also the biographies of all great men.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: पत्नी रजस्वला या च नाभिगच्छन्न चाह्वयेत्॥ स्नातां चतुर्थे दिवसे रात्रौ गच्छेद् विचक्षणः।
en: When one's wife is in her season, one should never know her, nor even summon her for conversation. A wise man may take her into his company on the fourth day after the bath of purification.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: पञ्चमे दिवसे नारी षष्ठेऽहनि पुमान् भवेत्॥ एतेन विधिना पत्नीमुपगच्छेत पण्डितः।
en: If one holds sexual union on the fifth day from the first appearance of the cataminal flow he gets a daughter. By holding it on the sixth day, he gets a son. A wise man should, in the matter of sexual intercourse attend to this rule.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिमित्राणि पूजनीयानि सर्वशः॥ यष्टव्यं च यथाशक्ति यज्ञैर्विविधदक्षिणैः।
en: Kinsmen and relatives by marriage and friends should all be treated with respect. One should, to the best of his power, worship the celestials in sacrifices, giving away various kinds of articles as sacrificial presents.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: अत उर्ध्वमरण्यं च सेवितव्यं नराधिप॥ एष ते लक्षणोद्देश आयुष्याणां प्रकीर्तितः।
en: After the period laid down for the domestic mode of life, one should, O king, become a hermit. I have thus told you briefly all the characteristics of persons who succeed in living long.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: शेषस्त्रविद्यवृद्धेभ्यः प्रत्याहार्यो युधिष्ठिर॥ आचारो भूतिजनन आचारः कीर्तिवर्धनः।
en: What I have not told you should be heard by you from the mouths of persons well-versed in the three Vedas, O Yudhishthira. You should know that conduct is the root of prosperity. Conduct increases fame.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: आचाराद् वर्धते ह्यायुराचारो हन्त्यलक्षणम्॥ आगमानां हि सर्वेषामाचारः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते।
en: It is conduct which prolongs life. It is conduct which destroys all calamitics and evils. Conduct has been said to be superior 10 all the branches of knowledge.

description: Why a man becomes long:, or short lived
sn: आचारप्रभवो धर्मो धर्मादायुर्विवर्धते॥ एतद् यशस्यमायुष्यं स्वयं स्वस्त्ययनं महत्। अनुकम्प्य सर्ववर्णान् ब्रह्मणा समुदाहृतम्॥
en: It is conduct which begets virtue, and it is virtue which prolongs life. Conduct gives fame, long life, and Heaven. Conduct is the most efficacious rite of propitiating the celestials. The self-create Brahman himself has said that one should show mercy to all orders of men.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यथा ज्येष्ठः कनिष्ठेषु वर्तेत भरतर्षभ। कनिष्ठाश्च यथा ज्येष्ठे वर्तेरंस्तद् ब्रवीहि मे॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O chief of Bharata's race, how the eldest brother should treat his younger brothers, and how the younger brothers should behave towards their eldest brother.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ज्येष्ठवत् तात वर्तस्व ज्येष्ठोऽसि सततं भवान्। गुरोर्गरीयसी वृत्तिर्या च शिष्यस्य भारत॥
en: Bhishma said Do you, O son, always behave towards your younger brothers as their eldest brother should. You are always the eldest of all these your brothers. You should always treat your younger brothers in the way in which a preceptor treats his disciples.

sn: न गुरावकृतप्रज्ञे शक्यं शिष्येण वर्तितुम्। गुरोहिं दीर्घदर्शित्वं यत् तच्छिष्यस्य भारत॥
en: If the preceptor happens to happens the disciple cannot possibly behave towards him in a respectful or proper way. If the preceptor is possessed of purity and good conduct, the disciple also succeeds in acquiring conduct of the same kind, O Bharata.

sn: अन्धः स्यादन्धवेलायां जडः स्यादपि वा बुधः। परिहारेण तद् ब्रूयाद् यस्तेषां स्याद् व्यतिक्रमः॥
en: The eldest brother should at times not notice the acts of his younger brothers, and though possessed of wisdom should at times act as if he does not understand their acts. If the younger brothers be guilty of any sin, the eldest brother should correct them by indirect ways and means.

sn: प्रत्यक्षं भिन्नहृदया भेदयेयुः कृतं नराः। श्रियाभितप्ताः कौन्तेय भेदकामास्तथारयः॥
en: If there be good understanding among brothers and if the oldest brother seeks to correct his younger brothers by director ostensible means, persons who are enemies, O son of Kunti, who feel pain on seeing such good understanding and who, therefore, always seek to bring about a disunion, try to disunite the brothers and sow dissension among them.

sn: ज्येष्ठः कुलं वर्धयति विनाशयति वा पुनः। हन्ति सर्वमपि ज्येष्ठः कुलं यत्रावजायते॥
en: It is the eldest brother who increases the prosperity of the family or destroys it entirely. If the eldest brother happens to be not gifted with sense and wicked in conduct, he encompasses the destruction of the whole family.

sn: अथ वो विनिकुर्वीत ज्येष्ठो भ्राता यवीयसः। अज्येष्ठः स्यादभागश्च नियम्यो राजभिश्च सः॥
en: That eldest brother who injures his younger brothers ceases to be considered as the eldest and forfeits his share in the family property and deserves to be checked by the king.

sn: निकृती हि नरो लोकान् पापान् गच्छत्यसंशयम्। विदुलस्येव तत् पुष्पं मोघं जनयितुः स्मृतम्॥
en: That man who acts deceitfully, has, forsooth, to go to the regions of grief and every kind of evil. The birth of such a person is of no avail like the flowers of the cane.

sn: सर्वानर्थः कुले यत्र जायते पापपूरुषः। अकीर्ति जनयत्येव कीर्तिमन्तर्दधाति च॥
en: That family in which a sinful person is born becomes subject to every evil. Such a person brings about infamy, and all the good deeds of the family disappear.

sn: सर्वे चापि विकर्मस्था भागं नार्हन्ति सोदराः। नाप्रदाय कनिष्ठेभ्यो ज्येष्ठः कुर्वीत यौतकम्॥
en: Such among the brothers as are addicted to wicked deeds forfeit their shares of the family property. In such a case, the eldest brother may appropriate the entire joint property without giving any portion thereof to his younger brothers.

sn: अनुपघ्नन् पितुर्दायं जंघाश्रमफलोऽध्वगः। स्वयमीहितलब्धं तु नाकामो दातुमर्हति॥
en: If the eldest brother makes any money, without using the paternal property and by going to a distant place he may appropriate for his own use, such wealth without giving any share thereof to his younger brothers.

sn: भ्रातृणामविभक्तानामुत्थानमपि चेत् सह। न पुत्रभागं विषमं पिता दद्यात् कदाचन॥
en: If brothers wish (during the lifetime of their father) to partition the family property, the father should give equal shares to all his sons.

sn: न ज्येष्ठो वावमन्येत दुष्कृतः सुकृतोऽपि वा। यदि स्त्री यद्यवरजः श्रेयश्चेत् तत् तदाचरेत्॥
en: If the eldest brother happens to be a vicious man and without any accomplishments, he inay be disregarded by his younger brothers. If the wife or the younger brother happens to be sinful, her or his good must still be looked alier.

sn: धर्मं हि श्रेय इत्याहुरिति धर्मविदो जनाः। दशाचार्यानुपाध्याय उपाध्यायान् पिता दश॥
en: Persons conversant with the efficacy of righteousness hold that virtue is the highest good. The Upadhyaya is superior to even ten Acharyyas. The father is equal to ten Upadhyayas.

sn: दश चेव पितॄन् माता सर्वां वा पृथिवीमपि। गौरवेणाभिभवति नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः॥
en: The mother is equal to ten fathers or even the whole Earth. There is no senior equal to the mother. Indeed, she is above all in respect of the reverence due to her.

sn: माता गरीयसी यच्च तेनैतां मन्यते जनः। ज्येष्ठो भ्राता पितृसमो मृते पितरि भारत॥
en: It is, therefore, that people regard the mother to deserve so much respect. After the demise of the father, O Bharata, the eldest brother should be considered as the father.

sn: स ह्येषां वृत्तिदाता स्यात् स चैतान् प्रतिपालयेत्। कनिष्ठास्तं नमस्येरन् सर्वे छन्दानुवर्तिनः॥ तमेव चोपजीवरेन् यथैव पितरं तथा।
en: It is the eldest brother who should assign to them their means of support and protect and maintain them. All the younger brothers should bow to him and obey his command. Indeed, they should depend upon him, as they did upon their father during his lifetime.

sn: शरीरमेतौ सृजतः पिता माता च भारत॥ आचार्यशास्ता या जाति: सा सत्या साजरामरा।
en: So far as the body is concerned, O Bharata, it is the father and the mother who creates it. That birth, however, which the Acharya ordains, is considered as the true birth which is really unfading and immortal.

sn: ज्येष्ठा मातृसमा चापि भगिनी भरतर्षभ॥ भ्रातुर्भार्या च तद्वत् स्याद् यस्या बाल्ये स्तनं पिबेत्।।
en: The eldest sister, O chief of Bharata's race, is like a mother. The wife of the eldest brother also is like the mother, for the younger brother, in infancy receives nursing from her.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां म्लेच्छानां च पितामह। उपवासे मतिरियं कारणं च न विद्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, all the orders of men, including the very Mlechchhas, are naturally disposed to observe fasts. We, however, do not know the reason thereof.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: ब्रह्मक्षत्रेण नियमाश्चर्तव्या इति नः श्रुतम्। उपवासे कथं तेषां कृत्यमस्ति पितामह॥
en: We have heard that only Brahmanas and Kshatriyas should observe the vow of fasts. How, O grandfather, are the other castes to be taken as acquiring any merit by the observance of fasts?

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: नियमांश्चोपवासांश्च सर्वेषा ब्रूहि पार्थिव। आप्नोति कां गतिं तात उपवासपरायणः॥
en: How have vows and fasts come to be observed by persons of all castes, O king? What is that end which one devoted to the observance of fasts, acquires?

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: उपवासः परं पुण्यमुपवासः परायणम्। उपोष्येह नरश्रेष्ठ किं फलं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: It has been said that fasts are greatly meritorious and that fasts are a great refuge. O king, what is the fruit that is acquired in this world by the man who observes fasts?

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: अधर्मान्मुच्यते केन धर्ममाप्नोति वा कथम्। स्वर्गे पुण्यं च लभते कथं भरतसत्तम॥
en: By what means is one purged of his sins? By what means does one acquire virtue. By what means, O best of the Bharatas, does one succeed in acquiring Heaven and merit.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: उपोष्य चापि किं तेन प्रदेय स्यानराधिप। धर्मेण च सुखार्थोल्लभेद् येन ब्रबीहि तम्॥
en: After having observed a fast, what should one give away, O king? O tell me, what those duties are by which one may succeed in acquiring objects leading to happiness.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ब्रुवाणं कौन्तेयं धर्मज्ञं धर्मतत्त्ववित्। धर्मपुत्रमिदं वाक्यं भीष्मः शान्तनवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Kunti's son begotten by the deity of Dharma, who was conversant with every duty and who said so to him, Shantanu's son, Bhishma, who knew every duty, answered in the following words.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: भीष्म उवाच इदं खलु मया राजन् श्रुतमासीत् पुरातनम्। उपवासविधौ श्रेष्ठा गुणा ये भरतर्षभ॥
en: Bhishma said Formerly, O king, I heard of these high merits O chief of Bharata's race, as belonging to the observance of fasts according to the ordinance.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: ऋषिमङ्गिरसं पूर्वं पृष्टवानस्मि भारत। यथा मां त्वं तथैवाहं पृष्टवांस्तं तपोधनम्॥
en: I had, O Bharata, asked the Rishi Angirasa of great ascetic merit, the very same questions which you have asked me today.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: प्रश्चमतं मया पृष्टो भगवानग्निसम्भवः। उपवासविधिं पुण्यमाचष्ट भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Accosted by me thus, the illustrious Rishi, who originated from the sacrificial fire, answered me even thus about the observance of fasts according to the ordinance.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: अङ्गिरा उवाच ब्रह्मक्षत्रे त्रिरात्रं तु विहितं कुरुनन्दन। द्विस्त्रिरात्रमथैकाहं निर्दिष्टं पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Angirasa said Fasts for three nights together, ordained for Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, O delighter of the Kurus. Indeed, O king, a fast for one night, for two nights, and for three nights may be observed by them.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: वैश्याः शूद्राश्च यन्मोहादुपवासं प्रचक्रिरे। त्रिरात्रं या द्विरात्रं वा तयोर्तुष्टिर्न विद्यते॥
en: Fast for one night is ordained for Vaishyas and Shudras. If they observe fasts for two or three nights by mistake, such fasts never bring on their advancement.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: चतुर्थभक्तक्षपणं वैश्ये शूद्रे विधीयते। त्रिरात्रं न तु धर्मज्ञैर्विहितं धर्मदर्शिभिः॥
en: Fasts for two nights have been ordained for Vaishyas and Shudras (on certain special occasions). Fasts for three nights, however, have not been ordained for them by persons knowing duties.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: पञ्चम्यां वापि षष्ठ्यां च पौर्णमास्यां च भारत। उपोष्य एकभक्तेन नियतात्मा जितेन्द्रियः॥ क्षमावान् रूपसम्पन्नः श्रुतवांश्चैव जायते। नानपत्यो भवेत् प्राज्ञो दरिद्रो वा कदाचन॥
en: The wise man who, with his senses and soul under restraint, O Bharata, fasts, by abstaining from one of the two meals, on the fifth and the sixth days of the moon as also on the day of the full moon, becomes gifted with forgiveness and personal beauty and knowledge of scriptures. Such a person never becomes childless and poor.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: यजिष्णुः पञ्चमी षष्ठी कुले भोजयते द्विजान्। अष्टमीमथ कौरव्य कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दशीम्॥ उपोष्य व्याधिरहितो वीर्यवानभिजायते। मार्गशीर्षं तु यो मासमेकभक्तेन संक्षिपेत्॥ भोजयेच्च द्विजाशक्त्या स मुच्येद् व्याधिकिल्बिशैः। सर्वकल्याणसम्पूर्ण: सर्वोषधिसमन्वितः॥
en: He who celebrates sacrifices for worshipping the deities on the fifth and the sixth days of the moon, becomes superior to all the members of his family and succeeds in feeding a large number of Brahmanas. He who observes fasts on the eighth and the fourteenth days of the dark fortnight, becomes freed from diseases and possessed of great energy. The man who abstains from one meal every day throughout the month called Margashirsha, should, with respect and devotion, feed a number of Brahmanas. By so doing he becomes freed from all his sins. Such a man becomes gifted with prosperity, and all sorts of grain become his.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: उपोष्य व्याधिरहितो वीर्यवानभिजायते। कृषिभागी बहुधनो बहुधान्यश्च जायते॥
en: He becomes gifted with energy. In fact, such a person reaps profuse harvest from his fields, acquires great riches and much corn.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: पौषमासं तु कौन्तेय भक्तेनैकेन यः क्षिपेत्। सुभगो दर्शनीयश्च यशोभागी च जायते॥
en: That man, O son of Kunti, who passes the whole month of Pausha abstaining every day from one of two meals, becomes a gainer of good fortune and pleasant features and great fame.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: माघं तु नियतो मासमेकभक्तेन यः क्षिपेत्। श्रीमत्कुले ज्ञातिमध्ये स महत्त्वं प्रपद्यते॥
en: He who passes the whole month of Magha, abstaining every day from one of the two mcals, is born in a high family and attains to a position of eminence among his kinsmen.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: भगदैवतमासं तु एकभक्तेन यः क्षिपेत्। स्त्रीषु वल्लभतां याति वश्याश्चास्य भवन्ति ताः।।२२
en: He who passes the whole month of Bhagadaivata, confining himself every day to only one meal, becomes a favourite with women who, indeed, readily acknowledge his sway.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: चैत्रं तु नियतो मासमेकभक्तेन यः क्षिपेत्। सुवर्णमणिमुक्ताढ्ये कुले महति जायते॥
en: He who passes the whole of the month of Chaitra, taking every day one meal only, is born in high family and becomes rich in gold, gems, and pearls.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: निस्तरेदेकभक्तेन वैशाख यो जितेन्द्रियः। नरो वा यदि वा नारी ज्ञातीनां श्रेष्ठतां व्रजेत्॥
en: The person, whether male or female, who passes the month of Baishakha, taking himself or herself every day one meal, and keeping his or her senses under restraint, succeeds in attaining to a position of eminence among kinsmen.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: ज्येष्ठामूलं तु यो मासमेकभक्तेन संक्षिपेत्। ऐश्वर्यमतुलं श्रेष्ठं पुमान् स्त्री वा प्रपद्यते॥
en: The person who passes the month of Jaishthya taking himself every day one meal, succeeds in acquiring a position of eminence and great riches. If a woman, she reaps the same reward.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: आषाढमेकभक्तेन स्थित्वा मासमतन्द्रितः। बहुधान्यो बहुधनो बहुपुत्रश्च जायते॥
en: He who passes the month of Ashada, taking himself one meal a day and with senses steadily concentrated upon his duties, becomes possessed of much corn, great riches and large progeny.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: श्रावणं नियतो मासमेकभक्तेन यः क्षिपेत्। यत्र तत्राभिषेकेण युज्यते ज्ञातिवर्धनः॥
en: He who passes the month of Sravana, taking himself one meal a day receives the honors of Abhisheka wherever he may happen to live, and attains to a position of eminence among kinsmen whom he supports.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: प्रौष्ठपदं तु यो मासमेकाहारो भवेन्नरः। गवाढ्यं स्फीतमचलमैश्वर्यं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: That man who takes himself only one meal a day for the whole month of Proshthapada, becomes possessed of great riches.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: तथैवाश्वयुजं मासमेकभक्तेन यः क्षिपेत्। मृजावन् वाहनाढ्यश्च बहुपुत्रश्च जायते॥
en: The man who passes the month of Ashvin, taking himself one meal a day, becomes pure in soul and body, possessed of many animals and vehicles and large progeny.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: कार्तिकं तु नरो मासं यः कुर्यादेकभोजनम्। शूरश्च बहुभार्यश्च कीर्तिमांश्चैव जायते॥
en: He who passes the month of Kartika, taking himself one meal every day, becomes possessed of heroism, many wives and great fame.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: इति मासा नरव्याघ्र क्षिपतां परिकीर्तिताः। तिथीनां नियमा ये तु शृणु तानपि पार्थिव॥
en: I have now told you, O king, what the fruits are that are obtained by men by observing fasts for the two and ten months in detail. Listen now, O king, to me as I tell you what the rules are about the lunar days.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: पक्षे पक्षे गते यस्तु भक्तमश्नशति भारत। गवाढ्यो बहुपुत्रश्च बहुभार्यः स जायते॥
en: The man who, abstaining from it every day, takes rice at the termination of every fortnight becomes possessed of a great many kine, a large progeny, and a long life.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: मासि मासि त्रिरात्राणि कृत्वा वर्षाणि द्वादश। गणाधिपत्यं प्राप्नोति निःसपत्नमनाविलम्॥
en: He whọ observes fasts for three nights every month and acts thus for two and ten years, acquires a position of eminence among his kinsmen and friends, without a rival to contest his claim and without any anxiety caused by any one trying to rise to the same height.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: एते तु नियमाः सर्वे कर्तव्या: शरदो दश। द्वे चान्ये भरतश्रेष्ठ प्रवृत्तिमनुवर्तता॥
en: These rules which I speak of, O chief of Bharata's race, should be observed for twelve years. Be disposed to do it.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: यस्तु प्रातस्तथा सायं भुजानो नान्तरा पिबेत्। अहिंसानिरतो नित्यं जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्॥ षभिः स वषैर्नृपते सिध्यते नात्र संशयः। अग्निष्टोमस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः॥
en: That man who eats once in the forenoon and once after evening and abstains from drinking at the interval, and who shows mercy towards all creatures, and pours libations of clarified butter on his sacred fire every day, acquires success, O king, in six years. There is no doubt in this. Such a man acquires the merit of the Agnishtoma sacrifice.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: अधिवासे सोऽप्सरसां नृत्यगीतविनादिते। रमते स्त्रीसहस्राढ्ये सुकृती विरजो नरः॥
en: Gifted with merit and freed from every sort of stain, he acquires the region of the Apsaras which echo with the sound of songs and dance, and passes his days in the company of a thousand highly beautiful ladies.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: तप्तकाञ्चनवर्णाभं विमानमधिरोहति।
en: He rides on a car of the colour of melted gold and receives great honours in the region of Brahma.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रं च ब्रह्मलोके महीयते॥ तत्क्षयादिह चागम्य माहाम्यं प्रतिपद्यते। यस्तु संवत्सरं पूर्णमेकाहारो भवेन्नरः॥ अतिरात्रस्य यज्ञस्य स फलं समुपाश्नुते। दशवर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गे च स महीयते॥
en: After the exhaustion of that merit, such a person returns to Earth and acquires elevated position. That man who passes one whole year, taking himself every day only one meal, acquires the merit of the Atiratra sacrifice. He ascends to Heaven after death and receives great honours there.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: तत्क्षयादिह चागम्य माहात्म्यं प्रतिपद्यते। यस्तु संवत्सरं पूर्णं चतुर्थं भक्तमश्नुते॥ अहिंसानिरतो नित्यं सत्यवाग् विजितेन्द्रियः। वाजपेयस्य यज्ञस्य स फलं समुपाश्नुते॥
en: Upon the termination of that merit he returns to the Earth and acquires a position of eminence. He who passes one whole year fasting for three days in succession and taking food on every fourth day, and abstaining from injury from every sort, adhering to truthfulness of speech, and keeping his senses under control, acquires the merit of the Vajapeya sacrifice.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: दशवर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते। षष्ठे काले तु कौन्तेय नरः संवत्सरं क्षिपन्॥ अश्वमेधस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः। चक्रवाकप्रयुक्तेन विमानेन स गच्छति॥
en: Such a person ascends to Heaven after death and receives great honours there. That man, O son of Kunti, who passes a whole year observing fasts for five days and taking food on only the sixth day, gains the merit of Horse sacrifice. The chariot he rides, is drawn by Chakravakas.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: यत्वारिंशत् सहस्राणि वर्षाणां दिवि मोदते। अष्टमेन तु भक्तेन जीवन् संवत्सरं नृप॥ गवामयस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः। हंससारसयुक्तेन विमानेन स गच्छति॥
en: Such a man enjoys every kind of happiness in Heaven for full forty thousand years. He who passes a whole year observing fasts for seven days and taking food on only every eighth day, gains the merit of the Gavamaya sacrifice. The chariot he rides, is drawn by swans and cranes.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: पञ्चाशतं सहस्राणि वर्षाणां दिवि मोदते। पक्षे पक्षे गते राजन् योऽश्नीयाद् वर्षमेव तु॥ षण्मासानशनं तस्य भगवानङ्गिराऽब्रवीत्। षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि दिवमावसते च सः॥
en: Such a person enjoys all kinds of happiness in Heaven for fifty thousand years. He who passes a whole year, o king, taking food only at intervals of a fortnight, gains the merit of a continuous fast for six months. This has been said by the illustrious Angirasa himself. Such a man Lives in Heaven for sixty thousand years.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: वीणानां वल्लकीनां च वेणूनां च विशाम्पते। सुघोषैर्मधुरैः शब्दैः सुप्तः स प्रतिबोध्यते॥
en: He is roused every morning from his bed by the sweet notes of Vinas and Vallakis and flutes, O king.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: संवत्सरमिहैकं तु मासि मासि पिबेदपः। फलं विश्वजितस्तात प्राप्नोति स नरो नृप॥
en: He who passes a whole year, drinking only a little water at the termination of every month, acquires, O king, the merit of the Vishvajit sacrifice.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: सिंहव्याघ्रप्रयुक्तेन विमानेन स गच्छति। सप्ततिं व सहस्राणि वर्षाणां दिवि मोदते॥
en: Such a man rides a chariot drawn by lions and tigers. He lives in Heaven for seventy thousand years in the enjoyment of every sort of happiness.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: मासादूर्ध्वं नरव्याघ्र नोपवासो विधीयते। विधि त्वनशनस्याहुः पार्थ धर्मविदो जनाः॥
en: No fast for more than a month, O king, has been ordained. Even this, O son of Pritha, is the ordinance about fasts that has been declared by sages conversant with duties.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: अनार्तो व्याधिरहितो गच्छेदनशनं तु यः। पदे पदे यज्ञफलं स प्राप्नोति न संशयः॥
en: That man who, unafflicted by discase and free from every malady, observes a fast, indeed acquires, at every step the merits of Sacrifices.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: दिवं हंसप्रयुक्तेन विमानेन स गच्छति। शतं वर्षसहस्राणां मोदते स दिवि प्रभो॥
en: Such a man ascends to Heaven on a car drawn by swans. Gifted with power, he enjoys every sort of happiness in Heaven for a hundred years.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: शतं चाप्सरस: कन्या रमयन्त्यपि तं नरम्। आर्तो वा व्याधितो वापि गच्छेदनशनं तु यः॥
en: A hundred Apsaras of the most beautiful features, wait upon, and sport with him.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: शतं वर्षसहस्राणां मोदते स दिवि प्रभो। काञ्चीनूपुरशब्देन सुप्तश्चैव प्रबोध्यते॥
en: He is roused from his bed every morning by the sound of the Kanchis and the Nupuras of those ladies.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: सहस्रहंसयुक्तेन विमानेन तु गच्छति। स गत्वा स्त्रीशताकीर्णं रमते भरतर्षभ॥
en: Such a person rides on a car drawn by a thousand swans. Living, again, in a region teeming with hundreds of the most beautiful ladies, he passes his time in great joy.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: क्षीणस्याप्यायनं दृष्टं क्षतस्य क्षतरोहणम्। व्याधितस्यौषधग्रामः क्रुद्धस्य च प्रसादनम्॥ दुःखितस्यार्थमानाभ्यां दुःखानां प्रतिषेधनम्। न चैते स्वर्गकामस्य रोचन्ते सुखमेधसः॥
en: The person who seeks Heaven, does not want strength when he becomes weak, or the cure of wounds when he is wounded, or the administration of medicine when he is ill, or soothings, by others when he is angry, or the mitigation, by the expenditure of money, of sorrows caused by poverty.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: अतः स कामसंयुक्त विमाने हेमसंनिभे। रमते स्त्रीशतकीर्णं पुरुषोऽलंकृतः शुचिः॥
en: Leaving this world, where he suffers all sorts of privations, he proceeds to Heaven and rides on cars bedecked with gold, his body adorned with all sorts of ornaments. There in the midst of hundreds of beautiful ladies, he enjoys all sorts of pleasure and happiness, cleansed of every sin.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: स्वस्थः सफलसंकल्प: सुखी विगतकल्मषः। अनश्चन् देहमुत्सृज्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः॥
en: Indeed, abstaining from food and enjoyments in this world, he renounces this body and ascends to Heaven as the fruit of his penances, There purged of all his sins, he enjoys health and happiness and all his wishes become crowned with success.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: बालसूर्यप्रतीकाशे विमाने हेमवर्चसि। वैदूर्यमुक्ताखचिते वीणामुरजनादिते॥ पताकादीपिकाकीर्णं दिव्यकघण्टानिनादिते। स्त्रीसहस्रानुचरिते स नरः सुखमेधते॥
en: Such a person rides on a celestials car of golden colour, effulgent like the morning sun, set with pearls and lapis lazuli, resounding with the music of Vinas and Murajas, adorned with banners and lamps, and echoing with the sounds of celestial bells.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: यावन्ति रोमकूपाणि तस्य गात्रेषु पाण्डव। तावन्त्येव सहस्राणि वर्षाणां दिवि मोदते॥
en: Such a person enjoys all sorts of happiness in Heaven for as many years as there are pores in his body.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: नास्ति वेदात् परं शास्त्रं नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः। न धर्मात् परमो लाभस्तपो नानशनात् परम्॥
en: There is no Shastra superior to the Veda. There is no person more worthy of respect than the mother. There is no acquisition superior to that of virtue, and no penance superior to fast.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्यः परं नास्ति पावनं दिवि चेह च। उपवासैस्तथा तुल्यं तपःकर्म न विद्यते॥
en: There is nothing, more sacred, in Heaven or Earth, than Brahmanas. Similarly there is no penance that is superior to the observance of fasts.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: उपोष्य विधिवद् देवास्त्रिदिवै प्रतिपेदिरे। ऋषयश्च परां सिद्धिमुपवासैरवाप्नुवन्॥
en: It was by fasts that the celestials have succeeded in becoming dwellers of Heaven. It is by fasts that the Rishis have acquired high success.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: दिव्यवर्षसहस्राणि विश्वामित्रेण धीमता। क्षान्तमेकेन भक्तेन तेन विप्रत्वमागतः॥
en: Vishvamitra passed a thousand celestial years, taking one meal a day, and as the consequence thereof acquired the status of a Brahmana.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: च्यवनो जमदग्निश्च वसिष्ठो गौतमो भृगुः। सर्व एव दिवं प्राप्ताः क्षमावन्तो महर्षयः॥
en: Chyavana, Jamadagni, Vasishtha, Gautama and Bhriguall these great Rishis gifted with the virtue of forgivenesshave attained to Heaven through the observance of fasts.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: इदमङ्गिरसा पूर्वं महर्षिभ्यः प्रदर्शितम्। यः प्रदर्शयते नित्यं न स दुःखमवाप्नुते॥
en: Forinerly Angirasa declared so to the great Rishis. The man who teaches another the merit of fasts, has never to suffer any sort of misery.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: इमं तु कौन्तेय यथाक्रमं विधि प्रवर्तितं ह्यङ्गिरसा महर्षिणा। पठेच्च यो वै शृणुयाच्च नित्यदा न विद्यते तस्य नरस्य किल्बिषम्॥
en: The ordinances about fasts, in their due order, O son of Kunti, have originated from the great Rishi Angirasa. The man who daily reads these ordinances or hears them read, becomes freed from all sins.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men
sn: र्न चास्य दोषैरभिभूयते मनः। वियोनिजानां च विजानते रुतं ध्रुवां च कीर्तिं लभते नरोत्तमः॥
en: Not only is such a person freed from every calamity, but his mind rises above all sorts of shortcomings. Such a person succeeds in understanding the sounds of all creatures other than human, and acquiring eternal fame, becomes the foremost of men.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामहेन विधिवद् यज्ञाः प्रोक्ता महात्मना। गुणाश्चैषां यथातथ्यं प्रेत्य चेह च सर्वशः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, you have duly described to us the subject of Sacrifices, including the merits in full that attach to them both here and hereafter.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: न ते शक्या दरिद्रेण यज्ञाः प्राप्तुं पितामह। बहूपकरणा यज्ञा नानासम्भारविस्तराः॥
en: It should be remembered, however, O grandfather, that Sacrifices are incapable of being celebrated by poor men, for these require a large store of various articles.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: पार्थिवै राजपुत्रैर्वा शक्याः प्राप्तुं पितामह। नार्थन्यूनैरवगुणैरेकात्मभिसंहतैः॥
en: Indeed, O grandfather, the merit attaching to Sacrifices can be acquired by only kings and princes. That merit is incapable of being acquired by those who have no wealth and power and who live alone and are helpless.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: यो दरिद्रैरपि विधिः शक्यः प्राप्तुं सदा भवेत्। अर्थन्यूनैरवगुणैरेकात्मभिरसंहतैः॥ तुल्यो यज्ञफलैरेतैस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह।
en: Do you tell, us O grandfather, what the ordinances are about those acts that are fraught with merit equal to what belongs to Sacrifices and which, therefore, are capable of being performed by poor men.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: भीष्म उवाच इदमङ्गिरसा प्रोक्तमुपवासफलात्मकम्॥ विधिं यज्ञफलैस्तुल्यं तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर। यस्तु कल्यं तथा सायं भुजानो नान्तरा पिबेत्॥
en: Bhishma said Listen, O Yudhishthira! Those ordinances that I have told you of, those, viz., that were first promulgated by the great Rishis Angirasa, and that have reference to meritorious fasts for their soul, are considered as equal to Sacrifices.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: अहिंसानिरतो नित्यं जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। षड्भिरेव स वषैस्तु सिध्यते नात्र संशयः॥ तप्तकाञ्चनवर्णं च विमानं लभते नरः। देवस्त्रीणामधीवसे नृत्यगीतनिनादिते॥ प्राजापत्ये वसेत् पद्मं वर्षाणामग्निसंनिभे।
en: That man who takes one meal in the forenoon and one at night, without taking any food or drink during the interval and who observes this regulation for a period of six years successively abstaining all the while from injuring any creature and regularly pouring libations on his sacred fire every day, attains, forsooth, to success. Such a man acquires hereafter a car of the colour of heated gold, and acquires a residence, for millions of years, in the region of Prajapati, in the company of celestial ladies, that ever echoes with the sound of music and dance, and shines with the effulgence of fire.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: त्रीणि वर्षाणि यः प्राशेत् सततं त्वेकभोजनम्॥ धर्मपत्नीरतो नित्यमग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्।
en: He who passes three years, taking one meal a day and abstaining all the while from intercourse with any other woman except his own married wife, attains to the merit of the Agnishtoma sacrifice.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: यज्ञं बहुसुवर्णं वा वासवप्रियमाचरेत्॥ सत्यवान् दानशीलश्च ब्रह्मण्यश्चानसूयकः। क्षान्तो दान्तो जितक्रोधः स गच्छति परां गतिम्॥ पाण्डुराभ्रप्रतीकाशे विमाने हंसलक्षणे। द्वे समाप्ते ततः पद्मे सोऽप्सरोभिर्वसेत् सह॥ द्वितीये दिवसे यस्तु प्राश्नीयादेकभोजनम्। सदा द्वादशमासांस्तु जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्॥ अग्निकार्यपरो नित्यं नित्यं कल्यप्रबोधनः। अग्निष्टोमस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः॥
en: Such a man is considered as having performed a Sacrifice, with plenty of gifts in gold, that is dear to Vasava himself. By practising truthfulness of speech, making gifts, respecting the Brahmanas, avoiding malice, becoming forgiving and self controlled and conquering anger, a man acquires the highest end. Riding on a car of the colour of white clouds that is drawn by swans, he lives, for millions and millions of years, in the company of Apsaras. Fasting for a whole day and taking only one meal on the second day, he who pours libations upon his sacred fire for the period of a whole year, indeed, he who observes such a fast and attends every day to his fire and rises every day from bed before sunrise, acquires the merit of the Agnishtoma sacrifice. Such a man acquires a car drawn by swans and cranes.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: हंससारसयुक्तं च विमानं लभते नरः। इन्द्रलोके च वसते वरस्त्रीभिः समावृतः॥ तृतीये दिवसे यस्तु प्राचीयादेकभोजनम्। सदा द्वादशमासांस्तु जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्॥ अग्निकार्यपरो नित्यं नित्यं कल्यप्रबोधनः। अतिरात्रस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्॥
en: up from Surrounded by the most beautiful ladies, he lives in the region of Indra. That man who takes only one meal every third day, and pours libations every day on his sacred fire for a period of a whole year, indeed, he who thus attends to his fire every day and wakes sleep every morning before sun rise, acquires the high merit of the Atiratra sacrifice. He acquires a car drawn by peacocks and swans and cranes.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: मयूरहंसयुक्तं च विमानं लभते नरः। सप्तर्षीणां सदा लोके सोऽप्सरोभिर्वसेत् सह॥
en: Proceeding to the region of the seven Rishis, he lives there, surrounded by Apsaras of great beauty. It is wellknown that such residence lasts for full three Padmas of years.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: निवर्तनं च तत्रास्य त्रीणि पद्यानि वै विभुः। दिवसे यश्चतुर्थे तु प्राश्नीयादेकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। वाजपेयस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्॥
en: Fasting for three days successively, he who takes only one meal every fourth day, and pours libations every day on his sacred fire, acquires the great merit of the Vajapeya sacrifice. The car he acquires is graced by highly beautiful celestial ladies who have Indra for their father.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: इन्द्रकन्याभिरूढं च विमानं लभते नरः। सागरस्य च पर्यन्ते वासवं लोकमावसेत्॥
en: He lives in the region, of Indra for millions and millions of years, and enjoys great happiness by witnessing the sports of the king of the gods.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: देवराजस्य च क्रीडां नित्यकालमवेक्षते। दिवसे पञ्चमे यस्तु प्राश्नीयादेकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासांस्तु जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। अलुब्धः सत्यवादी च ब्रह्मण्यश्चाविहिंसकः॥ अनसूयुरपापस्थो द्वादशाहफलं लभेत्।
en: Fasting for four days successively he who eats only one meal every fifth day, and pours libations on the sacred fire every day for a the period of a whole year, and who lives without cupidity, telling the truth, respecting the Brahmanas, abstaining from every sort of injury, and avoiding malice and sin, acquires the merit of the Vajapeya sacrifice.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: जाम्बूनदमयं दिव्यं विमानं हंसलक्षणम्॥ सूर्यमालासमाभासमारोहेत् पाण्डुरं गृहम्।
en: The car he rides, is made of gold and drawn by swans and effulgent like many suns rising together. He acquires, besides, a palatial building of pure white.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: आवर्तनानि चत्वारि तथा पद्मानि द्वादश॥ शराग्निपरिमाणं च तत्रासौ वसते सुखम्।
en: He lives there happily for full one and fifty Padmas of years.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: दिवसे यस्तु षष्ठे वै मुनिः प्राशेत भोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। सदा त्रिषवणस्नायी ब्रह्मचार्यनसूयकः॥ गवां मेधस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्।
en: He who fasting for five days, takes food only on the sixth day, and pious libations on his sacred fire every day for one year, and who performs three ablutions in course of the day for purifying himself and saying his prayers and paying his adoration, and who leads a celibate life, divested of malice in his conduct, acquires the merit of the Gomedha sacrifice.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: अग्निज्वालासमाभासं हंसबहिणसेवितम्॥ शातकुम्भसमायुक्तं साधयेद् यानमुत्तमम्।
en: He acquires an excellent car adorned with pure gold, effulgent like a blazing fire and drawn by swans and peacocks.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: तथैवाप्सरसामङ्के प्रतिसुप्तः प्रबोध्यते॥ नूपुराणां निनादेन मेखलानां च नि:स्वनैः।
en: He sleeps on the lap of Apsaras and is awakened every morning by the melodious sound of Nupuras and Kanchis.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: कोटीसहस्रं वर्षाणां त्रीणि कोटिशतानि च॥ पद्मान्यष्टादश तथा पताके द्वे तथैव च।
en: He leads such a happy life for ten thousand millions of years and three thousand millions besides and eight and ten Padmas and two Patakas.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: अयुतानि च पञ्चाशदृक्षचर्मशतस्य च॥ लोम्नां प्रमाणेन समं ब्रह्मलोके महीयते।
en: Such a man lives also, honoured by all, in the region of Brahma for as many years as there are hairs on the bodies of five thousand bears.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: दिवसे सप्तमे यस्तु प्राश्नीयादेकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। सरस्वती गोपयानो ब्रह्मचर्ये समाचरन्॥ सुमनोवर्णकं चैव मधुमासं च वर्जयन्। पुरुषो मरुतां लोकमिन्द्रलोकं च गच्छति॥
en: Fasting for six days, he who takes only one meal every seventh day and pours libations on the sacred fire every day, for a full year, controlling speech all the while and observing the vow of celibacy and abstaining from the use of flowers and unguents and honey and meat, acquires the region of the Maruts and of Indra. Crowned with the fruition of every wish as it originates in the mind, he is waited upon and adored by celestial ladies.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: तत्र तत्र हि सिद्धार्थो देवकन्याभिरर्च्यते। फलं बहुसुवर्णस्य यज्ञस्य लभते नरः॥
en: He acquires the merits of a sacrifice in which profuse gold is given away. Proceeding to the regions named, he lives there for numberless years in the enjoyment of greatest happiness.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: संख्यामतिगुणां चापि तेषु लोकेषु मोदते। यस्तु संवत्सरं क्षान्तो भुङ्क्तेऽहन्यष्टमे नरः॥ देवकार्यपरो नित्यं जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। पौण्डरीकम्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्॥
en: He who shows mercy to all and fasting for seven days eats on every eighth day for whole year, and, pouring libations every day on the sacred fire, worship the celestials, regularly, acquires the great merits of the Paundarika sacrifice. The car he rides is lotus-hued.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: पद्मवर्णनिभं चैव विमानमधिरोहति। कृष्णाः कनकगौर्यश्च नार्यः श्यामास्तथापराः॥
en: on car Forsooth, such a man acquires also a large number of young and beautiful ladies, some having complexions that are dark, some with complexions that are gold, and some that are Shyamas, whose looks and gestures are of the most agreeable kind.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: वयोरूपविलासिन्यो लभते नात्र संशयः। यस्तु संवत्सरं भुङ्क्ते नवमे नवमेऽहनि॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्॥
en: He who fasts for eight days and takes only one meal on every ninth day for one full year, and pours libations on the sacred fire every day, wine the great merits of a thousand Horse sacrifices. The car he rides in Heaven is beautiful like a lotus.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: पुण्डरीकप्रकाशं च विमानं लभते नरः। दीप्तसूर्याग्नितेजोभिर्दिव्यमालाभिरेव च॥
en: He always journeys, that accompanied by the daughters of Rudra bedecked with celestial garlands and gifted with the effulgence of the midday sun or of fires of burning flames.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: नीयते रुद्रकन्याभिः सोऽन्तरिक्षं सनातनम्। अष्टादश सहस्राणि वर्षाणां कल्पमेव च॥
en: Acquiring the regions of Rudra, he lives there in great happiness for number less years.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: कोटीशतसहस्रं च तेषु लोकेषु मोदते। यस्तु संवत्सरं भुङ्क्ते दशाहे वै गते गते॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै जुह्वानो जातवेदसम् ब्रह्मकन्यानिवासे च सर्वभूतमनोहरे॥ अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्।
en: He who fasts for nine days and takes only one meal every tenth day for a whole year, and pours libations on his sacred fire every day, gains the high merit of a thousand Horse sacrifices and attains to the companionship of Brahmana's daughters whose beauty charm the hearts of all creatures.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: रूपवत्यश्च तं कन्या रमयन्ति सनातनम्॥ नीलोत्पलनिभैर्वर्ण रक्तोत्पलनिभैस्तथा। विमानं मण्डलावर्तमावर्तगहनाकुलम्॥
en: These ladies, possessed of such beauty, and some of them possessed of colour of the lotus and some like that of the same flower of the blue variety, always keep him in joy. He acquires a beautiful car which moves in beautiful circles and which looks like the dense cloud called Avarta, resemble also an ocean wave.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: सागरोर्मिप्रतीकाशं लभेद् यानमनुत्तमम्। विचित्रमणिमालाभिर्नादितं शङ्खनिःस्वनैः॥
en: That car resounds with the constant tinkle of rows of pearls and gems, and the melodious sound of conchs, and is adorned with columns made of crystals and diamonds, as also with an altar constructed of the same minerals.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: स्फाटिकैर्वज्रसारैश्च स्तम्भैः सुकृतवेदिकम्। आरोहति महद् यानं हंससारसनादितम्॥
en: He rides such a car, drawn by swans and cranes, and lives for millions and millions of years in great happiness in Heaven.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: एकादशे तु दिवसे यः प्राप्ते प्राशते हविः। सदा द्वादशमासान् वै जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्॥ परस्त्रियं नाभिलषेद् वाचाथ मनसापि वा। अनृतं च न भोषेत मातापित्रोः कृतेपि वा॥ अभिगच्छेन्महादेवं विमानस्थं महाबलम्। अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्॥
en: He who fasts for ten days and cats only clarified butter on every eleventh day for one full year and pours libations on his sacred fire every day, who never, in word or thought, seeks the company of other people's wives and who never utters a false hood even for the sake of his mother and father, succeeds in seeing Mahadeva of great power seated on his car. Such a person acquires the great merit of a thousand Horse sacrifices.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: स्वायम्भुवं च पश्येत विमानं समुपस्थितम्। कुमार्यः काञ्चनाभासा रूपवत्यो नयन्ति तम्॥
en: He sees the car of the Selfcreate Brahman himself approach for taking him on it. He rides on it, accompanied by celestial ladies gifted with great beauty, and complexions as effulgent as that of pure gold.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: रुद्राणां तमधीवासं दिवि दिव्यं मनोहरम्। वर्षाण्यपरिमेयानि युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभः॥
en: Gified with the blazing splendour of the cycle fire, he lives for many years in a celestial mansion in Heaven, full of every happiness.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: कोटीशतसहस्रं च दशकोटिशतानि च। रुद्रं नित्यं प्रणमते देवदानवसम्मतम्॥
en: For those numberless years he experiences the joy of bending his head in respect to Rudra worshipped by the celestials and Danavas.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: स तस्मै दर्शनं प्राप्तो दिवसे दिवसे भवेत् दिवसे द्वादशे यस्तु प्राप्ते वै प्राशते हविः॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै सर्वमेधफलं लभेत्। आदित्यद्वादशं तस्य विमानं संविधीयते॥
en: Such a person sees every day the great god. That man who having fasted for eleven days, cats only a little clarified butter on the twelfth, and acts thus for a whole year, succeeds in acquiring the merits of all the Sacrifices. The car he rides, is effulgent like a dozen suns.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: मणिमुक्ताप्रवालैश्च महाहरुपशोभितम्। हंसमालापरिक्षिप्तं नागवीथीसमाकुलम्॥ मयूरैश्चक्रवाकैश्च कूजद्भिरुपशोभितम्। अटैटर्महद्भिः संयुक्तं ब्रह्मलोके प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Adorned with costly gems and pearls and corals, embellished with rows of swans and snakes and peacocks and Chakravakas uttering their melodious notes, and beautified with large domes, is the quarter to which he attains in the region of Brahman.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: नित्यमावसथं राजन् नरनारीसमावृतम्। ऋषिरेवं महाभागस्त्वगिरा प्राह धर्मवित्॥
en: That house, O king, is always filled with men and women. This is what the highly blessed Rishi Angirasa, knowing every duty, said.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: त्रयोदशे तु दिवसे प्राप्ते यः प्राशते हविः। सदा द्वादशमासान् वै देवसत्रफलं लभेत्॥
en: That man who having fasted twelve days, eats a little clarified butter on the thirteenth, and acts thus for a whose year, succeeds in acquiring the merits of the divine sacrifice.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: रक्तपद्मोदयं नाम विमानं साधयेन्नरः। जातरूपप्रयुक्तं च रत्नसंचयभूषितम्॥
en: Such a man gets a car of the colour of the new-blown lotus, adorned with pure gold and heaps of jewels and gems.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: देवकन्याभिराकीर्णं दिव्याभरणभूषितम्। पुण्यगन्धोदयं दिव्यं वायव्यैरुपशोभितम्॥
en: He goes to the regions of the Maruts which are full of celestial ladies, which are adorned with every kind of celestial ornament, which are filled with celestial perfumes, and which contain every element of happiness,

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: तत्र शंकुपताके द्वे युगान्तं कल्पमेव च। अयुतायुतं तथा पद्मं समुद्रं च तथा वसेत्॥
en: That resolute resides in the abode of Brahma for the period counted as two Shankha, two Mahapadma, a Kalpa, four ages, ten crore and four Padma years.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: गीतगन्धर्वघोषैश्च भेरीपणवनिःस्वनैः। सदा प्रह्लादितस्ताभिर्देवकन्याभिरिज्यते॥
en: Soothed with the sound of music and the sweet voice of Gandharvas and the sounds and blare of drums and Panavas, he is constantly pleased by celestial ladies of great beauty.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: चतुर्दशे तु दिवसे यः पूर्णे प्राशते हविः। सदा द्वादशमासांस्तु महामेधफलं लभेत्॥
en: That man who having fasted for thirteen days, eats a little clarified butter on the fourteenth day, and acts thus for a full year, acquires the merits of the Mahamedha sacrifice.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: अनिर्देश्यवयोरूपा देवकन्याः स्वलंकृताः। मृष्टतप्ताङ्गदधरा विमानैरुपयान्ति तम्॥
en: Celestial ladies of indescribable beauty, and whose age cannot be determined for they look ever young, adorned with every ornament and with armlets of blazing effulgence, wait upon him with many cars and follow him in his journeys.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: कलहंसविनिर्घोषैपुराणां च निःस्वनैः। काञ्चीनां च समुत्कर्षैस्तत्र तत्र निबोध्यते॥
en: He is waked every morning from his bed by the melodious note of swans, the tinkle of Nupuras, and the highly agreeable jingle of Kanchis. Indeed, he lives in a superior house, waited upon by such celestial ladies, for years as countless as the sands on the shores of Ganga.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: देवकन्यानिवासे च तस्मिन् वसति मानवः। जाह्नवीवालुकाकीर्णं पूर्णे संवत्सरं नरः॥ यस्तु पक्षे गते भुङ्क्ते एकभक्तं जितेन्द्रियः। सदा द्वादशमासान् जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्॥ राजसूयसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्। यानमारोहते दिव्यं हंसबहिणसेवितम्॥
en: That man who, keeping his senses under restraint, fasts for a fortnight and takes only one meal on the sixteenth day, and acts thus for a whole year, pouring libations every day on his sacred fire, acquires the great merits of a thousand Rajasuya sacrifices. The car he rides, is highly beautiful and is drawn by swans and peacocks.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: मणिमण्डलकैश्चित्रं जातरूपसमावृतम्। दिव्याभरणशोभाभिर्वरस्त्रीभिरलंकृतम्॥ एकस्तम्भं चतुर सप्तभौमं सुमङ्गलम्। वैजयन्तीसहनैश्च शोभितं गीतनि:स्वनैः॥ दिव्यं दिव्यगुणोपेतं विमानमधिरोहति। मणिमुक्ताप्रवालैश्च भूषितं वैद्युतप्रभम्॥
en: Riding on such a car which is, besides, adorned with garlands of pearls and the purest gold and graced with bevies of celestial ladies decked with ornaments of every sort, having one column and four arches and seven altars exceedingly auspicious, having thousand of banners and echoing with the sound of music, celestial and celestial attributes, set with gems and pearls and corals, and effulgent like lightning, such a man lives in Heaven for a thousand cycles, having elephants and rhinoceroses for dragging that car of his.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: वेसद् युगसहस्रं च खगजरवाहनः। षोडशे दिवसे प्राप्ते यः कुर्यादेकभोजनम्॥
en: That man who having fasted for fifteen days takes one meal on the sixteenth day and acts thus for one whole year, acquires the merits of the Soma sacrifice.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: सदा द्वादशमासान् वै सोमयज्ञफलं लभेत्। सोमकन्यानिवासेषु सोऽध्यावसति नित्यशः॥
en: Proceeding to the celestial region, he lives in the company of Soma's daughters. His body fragrant with unguents whose perfumes are as sweet as those of Soma himself, he acquires the power of going immediately to any place he likes.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: सौम्यगन्धानुलिप्तश्च कामकारगतिर्भवेत्। सुदर्शनाभिर्नारीभिर्मधुराभिस्तथैव च॥
en: Seated on his car he is waited upon by beautiful damsels of agreeable manners, and commands all articles of enjoyment.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: अर्च्यते वै विमानस्थः कामभोगैश्च सेव्यते। फलं पद्मशतप्रख्यं महाकल्पं दशाधिकम्॥
en: He enjoys such happiness upto the period of one hundred Padma years as longer as ten Mahakalpa and four ages.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: आवर्तनानि चत्वारि साधयेच्चाप्यसौ नरः। दिवसे सप्तदशमे यः प्राप्ते प्राशते हविः॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। स्थानं वारुणमैन्द्रं च रौद्रं वाप्यधिगच्छति॥ मारुतौशनसे चैव ब्रह्मलोकं स गच्छति।
en: That man who having fasted for sixteen days, eats a little clarified butter on the seventeenth day, and acts thus for a whole year, pouring libations every day on his sacred fire, proceeds to the regions of Varuna and Indra and Rudra and the Maruts and Ushanas and Brahman himself.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: तत्र दैवतकन्याभिरासनेनोपचर्यते॥ भूर्भुवं चापि देवर्षि विश्वरूपमवेक्षते।
en: There he is waited upon by celestial ladies and sees the celestial Rishi called Bhurbhuva and sees the entire universe.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: तत्र देवाधिदेवस्य कुमार्यो रमयन्ति तम्॥ द्वात्रिंशद् रूपधारिण्यो मधुरा: समलंकृताः।
en: The daughters of the king of the dcities gladden him there. Those damsels, of agreeable manners and adorned with every ornament, are capable of assuming thirty-two forms.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: चन्द्रादित्यावुभौ यावद् गगने चरतः प्रभो॥ तावच्चरत्यसौ धीरः सुधामृतरसाशनः।
en: As long as the Sun and Moon move in the sky, so long does that wise man live in those regions of happiness, living upon the succulence of ambrosia and nectar.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: अष्टादशे यो दिवसे प्राश्नीयादेकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै सप्तलोकान् स पश्यति।
en: That man who having fasted for seventeen days, takes only one meal on the eighteenth day, and acts thus for a whose year, succeeds! in seeing the seven regions of the universe.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: रथैः सनन्दिघोषैश्च पृष्ठतः सोऽनुगम्यते॥ देवकन्याधिरूढस्तु भ्राजमानैः स्वलंकृतैः।
en: While making his journeys on his car, he is always followed by a large train of cars producing the most agreeable rattle and ridden by celestial ladies shining with ornaments and beauty.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: व्याघ्रसिंहप्रयुक्तं च मेघस्वननिनादितम्॥ विमानमुत्तमं दिव्यं सुसुखी ह्यधिरोहति।
en: Enjoying the greatest happiness, the car he rides, is celestial and endued with the greatest beauty. It is drawn by lions and tigers, and produces ratile as deep as the muttering of the clouds.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: तत्र कल्पसहस्रं स कन्याभिः सह मोदते॥ सुधारसं च भुञ्जीत अमृतोपममुत्तमम्।
en: He lives in such happiness for a thousand aeons, living with celestial ladies upon ambrosia that is as sweet as nectar itself.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: एकोनविंशतिदिने यो भुङ्क्ते एकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै सप्तलोकान् स पश्यति।
en: That man who having fasted, for eighteen days, eats only one meal on the nineteenth day and acts thus for a full year, succeeds in perceiving all the seven regions of the universe.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: उत्तमं लभते स्थानमप्सरोगणसेवितम्॥ गन्धर्वैरुपगीतं च विमानं सूर्यवर्चसम्।
en: The region to which he attains is peopled by various tribes of Apsaras and resounds with the sweet note of Gandharvas. The car he rides is effulgent like the sun.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: तत्रामरवरस्त्रीभिर्मोदते विगतज्वरः॥ दिव्याम्बरधरः श्रीमानयुतानां शतं शतम्।
en: His heart shorn of every anxiety, he is waited upon by the foremost of celestial ladies. Decked with celestial garlands, and possessed of beauty, he lives in such happiness for millions and millions of years.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: पूर्णेऽथ विशे दिवसे यो भुङ्क्ते ह्येकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासांस्तु सत्यवादी धृतव्रतः। अमांसाशी ब्रह्मचारी सर्वभूतहिते रतः॥ स लोकान् विपुलान् रम्यानादित्यानामुपाश्नुते।
en: That man who having fasted for nineteendays, eats only one meal on every twentieth day, and acts thus for a full year, observing all thie while truthfulness of speech and observance of other (excellent) rituals, abstaining also froin meat, leading a celibate life and devoted to the behoof of all creatures, acquires the extensive regions of great happiness, belonging to the Adityas.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च दिव्यमाल्यानुलेपनैः॥ विमानैः काञ्चनैर्हद्यैः पृष्ठतश्चानुगम्यते।
en: While making his journeys on his own car, he is followed by a large train of cars ridden by Gandharvas and Apsaras decked with celestial garlands and perfumes.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: एकविंशे तु दिवसे यो भुङ्क्ते ह्येकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। लोकमौशनसं दिव्यं शक्रलोकं च गच्छति॥ अश्विनोर्मरुतां चैव सुखेष्वभिरतः सदा।
en: That man who having fasted for twenty days, takes a single meal on the (wenty first day, and acts thus for a full year, pouring libations every day on his sacred fire, acquires the regions of Ushanas and Shakra, of the Ashvins and the Maruts, and lives there in uninterrupted happiness of great measure.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: अनभिज्ञश्च दुःखानां विमानवरमास्थितः॥ सेव्यमानो वरस्त्रीभिः क्रीडत्यमरवत् प्रभुः।
en: Unacquainted with all sorrows; he rides the foremost of cars for making his journeys, and waited upon by foremost of celestial ladies, and possessed of power, he sports in joy like a celestial himself.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: द्वाविंशे दिवसे प्राप्ते यो भुङ्क्ते ह्येकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। अहिंसानिरतो धीमान् सत्यवागनसूयकः॥ लोकान् वसूनामाप्नोति दिवाकरसमप्रभः।
en: That man who having fasted for twentyone day, and acts thus for a full year, pouring libations on his sacred fire every day, abstaining from injuring any creature, observing truthfulness of speech, and freed from malice, acquires the regions of the Vasus and becomes endued with solar effulgence.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: कामचारी सुधाहारो विमानवरमास्थितः॥ रमते देवकन्याभिर्दिव्याभरणभूषितः।
en: Gifted with the power of going every where that will, living upon nectar, and riding on the foremost of cars, his body decked with celestial ornaments, he sports in joy in the company of celestial ladies.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: त्रयोविंशे तु दिवसे प्राशेद् यस्त्वेकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासांस्तु मिताहारो जितेन्द्रियः। वायोरुशनसश्चैव रुद्रलोकं च गच्छति॥ कामचारी कामगमः पूज्यमानोऽप्सरोगणैः।
en: That man who having fasted for twentytwo days, takes a single meal on the twenty third day, and acts thus for a full year, thus regulating his diet and keeping his senses under restraint acquires the regions of the wind God of Ushanas and of Rudras. Capable of going everywhere at will, and always roving at will, he is adored by various tribes of Apsaras. man

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: अनेकगुणपर्यन्तं विमानवरमास्थितः॥ रमते देवकन्याभिर्दिव्याभरणभूषितः।
en: Riding on the foremost of cars and his body decked with celestial ornaments, he sports for numberless years in great happiness in the company of celestial ladies.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: चतुर्विंशे तु दिवसे यः प्राप्ते प्राशते हविः॥ सदा द्वादशमासांश्च जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। आदित्यानामधीवासे मोदमानो वसेच्चिरम्॥ दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरो दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनः।
