en: That who having fasted for twentythree days eats a little clarified butter on the twentyfourth day, and acts thus for a full year, pouring libations on his sacred fire, lives for countless years in great happiness in the regions of the Adityas, his body decked with celestial dresses and garlands and celestial perfumes and unguents.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: विमाने काञ्चने दिव्ये हंसयुक्ते मनोरमे॥ रमते देवकन्यानां सहस्रैरयुतैस्तथा।
en: Riding on an excellent car, made of gold and gifted with great beauty and drawn by swans, he sports in joy in the company of thousands and thousands of celestial ladies.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: पञ्चविंशे तु दिवसे यः प्राशेदेकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासांस्तु पुष्कलं यानमारूहेत्।
en: That man who having fasted for twenty four days, takes a single meal on the twentyfifth day, and acts thus for full year, Succeeds in getting a car of the foremost kind, full of every object of enjoyment.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: सिंहव्याघ्रप्रयुक्तस्तु मेघनिःस्वननादितैः॥ स रथैर्नन्दिघोषैश्च पृष्ठतो ह्यनुगम्यते। देवकन्यासमारूढैः काञ्चनैर्विमलैः शुभैः॥ विमानमुत्तमं दिव्यमास्थाय सुमनोहरम्। तत्र कल्पसहस्रं वै वसते स्त्रीशतावृते॥ सुधारसं चोपजीवनमृतोपममुत्तमम्।
en: He is followed in his journeys by a large train of cars drawn by lions and tigers, and producing a sound as deep as the muttering of the clouds ridden by celestial ladies, and all made of pure gold and endued with great beauty. Himself riding on an excellent celestial car endued with great beauty, he lives in those regions for a thousand aeons, in the company of hundreds of celestial ladies and living upon ambrosia that is sweet as nectar itself.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: षड्विंशे दिवसे यस्तु प्रकुर्यादेकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासांस्तु नियतो नियताशनः। जितेन्द्रियो वीतरागो जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्॥ स प्राप्नोति महाभागः पूज्यमानोऽप्सरोगणैः। सप्तानां मरुतां लोकान् वसूनां चापि सोऽश्नुते॥१११ विमानैः स्फाटिकैर्दिव्यैः सर्वरत्नैरलंकृतैः। गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च पूज्यमानः प्रमोदते॥ द्वे युगानां सहस्रे तु दिव्ये दिव्येज तेजसा।
en: That man who having fasted for twentyfive days, takes only one meal on the twenty sixth day, and acts thus för a full year in the observance of such a regulation about diet, keeping his senses under restraint, freed from attachment, and pouring libations every day on his sacred fire, that blessed man, adored by the Apsaras, acquires the regions of the seven Maruts and the Vasus. When making his journeys, he is followed by a large train of cars made of excellent crystal and adorned with all sorts of geins, and ridden by Gandharvas and Apsaras who show him every honour. He lives in those regions, in enjoyment of such happiness, and gifted with celestial energy, for two thousand cycles.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: सप्तविंशेऽथ दिवसे यः कुर्यादेकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासांस्तु जुह्वानो जातवेदसम्। फलं प्राप्नोति विपुलं देवलोके च पूज्यते॥ अमृताशी वसंस्तत्र स वितृष्णः प्रमोदते।
en: That man who having fasted for twentysix days eats a single meal on the twentyseventh day, and acts thus for a full year, pouring libations every day on his sacred fire, acquires great merit and proceeding to the celestial region, receives honours from the deities, Living there he subsists on nectar freed from thirst of every kind, and enjoying every happiness.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: देवर्षिचरितं राजन् राजर्षिभिरनुष्ठितम्॥ अध्यावसति दिव्यात्मा विमानवरमास्थितः।
en: His soul purified of every dross and making his journeys on a celestial car of great beauty, he lives there, O king, acting like the celestial Rishis and the royal sages.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: स्त्रीभिर्मनोभिरामाभी रममाणो मदोत्कटः॥ युगकल्पसहस्राणि त्रीण्यावसति वै सुखम्।
en: Gifted with great energy, he lives there in great happiness in the company of celestial ladies of highly agreeable manners, for three thousand cycles and aeons.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: योऽष्टाविंशे तु दिवसे प्राश्नीयादेकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासांस्तु जितात्मा विजितेन्द्रियः। फलं देवर्षिचरितं विपुलं समुपाश्नुते॥ भोगवांस्तेजसा भाति सहस्रांशुरिंवामलः।
en: That man who having fasted for twenty seven days, takes a single meal on the twentyeighth day, and acts thus for a full year, with soul and senses under perfect restraint, acquires very great merit, which, in fact, is equal to what is acquired by the celestial Rishis. Having every article of enjoyment, and gifted with great energy, he shines with the effulgence of the midday sun.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: सुकुमार्यश्च नार्यस्तं रममाणाः सुवर्चसः॥ पीनस्तनोरुजघना दिव्याभरणभूषिताः। रमयन्ति मनःकान्ते विमाने सूर्यसंनिभे॥ सर्वकामगमे दिव्ये कल्पायुतशतं समाः।
en: Sportive ladies of the most delicate features and gifted with splendour of complexion, having deep bosoms, tapering thighs and full and round hips, decked with celestial ornaments, please him with their company while he rides on a delightent and excellent car effulgent like the sun and equipped with every article of enjoyment for thousands and thousands of aeons.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: एकोनत्रिंशे दिवसे यः प्राशेदेकभोजनम्॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै जुह्वानो सत्यव्रतपरायणः। तस्य लोका: शुभा दिव्या देवराजर्षिपूजिताः॥ विमानं सूर्यचन्द्राभं दिव्यं समधिगच्छति। जातरूपमय युक्तं सर्वरत्नसमन्वितम्॥ अप्सरोगणसम्पूर्ण गन्धर्वैरभिनादितम्।
en: That man who having fasted for twentyeight days, takes a single meal on the twentyninth day, and acts thus for a full year, observing all the while truthfulness of speech, acquires auspicious regions of great happiness that are adored by celestial Rishis and royal sages. The car he obtains is effulgent like the sun and the moon made of pure gold and adorned with every sort of gem, ridden by Apsaras and Gandharvas singing melodiously.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: तत्र चैनं शुभा नार्यो दिव्याभरणभूषिताः॥ मनोऽभिरामा मधुरा रमयन्ति मदोत्कटाः।
en: Thereon he is attended by auspicious ladies adorned with celestial ornaments of every sort. Gifted with sweet dispositions and agreeable features, and endued with great energy, se gladden him with their company.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: भोगवांस्तेजसा युक्तो वैश्वानरसमप्रभः॥ दिव्यो दिव्येन वपुषा भ्राजमान इवामरः।
en: Endued with every article of enjoyment and with great energy, and possessed of the splendour of a burning fire, he shines like a celestial, with a celestial form having every excellence.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: वसूनां मरुतां चैव साध्यानामश्विनोस्तथा॥ रुद्राणां च तथा लोकं ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति।
en: The regions he attains are those of the Vasus and the Maruts, of the Saddhyas and the Ashvins, of the Rudras and of Brahman himself.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: यस्तु मासे गते भुङ्क्ते एकभक्तं शमात्मकः॥ सदा द्वादशमासान् वै ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नुयात्।
en: That man who having fasted for a full month, takes a single meal on the first day of the following month, and acts thus for a full year, loO king on all things impartially, attains to the regions of Brahman himself.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: सुधारसकृताहारः श्रीमान् सर्वमनोहरः॥ तेजसा वपुषा लक्ष्म्या भ्राजते रश्मिवानिव।
en: There he lives upon ambrosia. Gifted with a beautiful form highly agreeable to all, he shines with energy and prosperity like the sun himself of a thousand rays.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरो दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनः॥ सुखेष्वभिरतो भोगी दुःखानामविजानकः।
en: Devoted to yoga and adorned with celestial dresses and garlands and smeared with celestial pertumes and unguents, he passes his time in great happiness, not experiencing the least sorrow. He shines on his car attended by ladies that blaze forth with effulgence emitted by themselves.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: स्वयंप्रभाभिर्नारीभिर्विमानस्थो महीयते॥ रुद्रदेवर्षिकन्याभिः सततं चाभिपूज्यते।
en: Those ladies the daughters of the celestial Rishis and the Rudras, worship him with veneration.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: नानारमणरूपाभि नारागाभिरेव च॥ नानामधुरभाषाभिर्नानारतिभिरेव च।
en: Capable of assuming various forms that are highly delightful and highly agreeable, their speech is characterized by various kinds of sweetness, and they are able to please the person they wait upon in various kinds of ways.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: विमाने गगनाकारे सूर्यवैदूर्यसंनिभे॥ पृष्ठतः सामसंकाशे उदर्के चाम्रसवन्निभे। दक्षिणायां तु रक्ताभे अधस्ताचीलमण्डले॥ ऊर्ध्वं विचित्रसंकाशे नैको वसति पूजितः।
en: While making his journeys, he rides on a car that looks like the sky itself in colour, In his rear are cars which look like the Moon; before him are those which resemble the clouds; on his right are cars that are red; below him are those that are blue and above, him are those that are of variegated colour. He is always worshipped by those who wait upon him.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: यावद् वर्षसहस्रं वै जम्बुद्वीपे प्रवर्षति॥ तावत् संवत्सराः प्रोक्ता ब्रह्मलोकेऽस्य धीमतः।
en: Gifted with great wisdom, he lives in the region of Brahman for as many years as are measured by the drops of rain that fall in course of a thousand years on the insular continent of Jamvudvipa.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: विपुषश्चैव यावन्त्यो निपतन्ति नभस्तलात्॥ वर्षासु वर्षतस्तावन्निवसत्यमरप्रभः।
en: Indeed, gifted with the effulgence a deity, he lives in that region of unalloyed happiness for as many years as the drops of rain which fall upon the Earth in the rainy season.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: मासोपवासी वर्षस्तु दशभिः स्वर्गमुत्तमम्॥ महर्षित्वमथासाद्य सशरीरगतिर्भवेत्
en: The man who having fasted for a whole month, eats on the first day of the following months and acts thus for ten years, acquires the status of a great Rishi. He has not to undergo any change of form while going to the celestial region for enjoying the rewards of his deeds in this life.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: मुनिर्दान्तो जितक्रोधो जितशिश्चोदरः सदा॥ जुह्वन्नग्नीश्च नियत: संध्योपासनसेविता।
en: Indeed, this is the status which one acquires by controlling speech, practising self-denial, subjugating anger, sexual appetite, and the desire to eat, pouring libations on the sacred fire, and regularly worshipping the twotwilight's.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: बहुभिर्नियमैरवं शुचिरश्नाति यो नरः॥ अभ्रावकाशशीलश्च तस्य भानोरिव त्विषः।
en: That man who purifies hiinself by the observance of these and similar vows and practices, and who eats in this way, becomes as pure as other and gifted with solar effulgence.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: दिवं गत्वा शरीरेण स्वेन राजन् यथामरः॥ स्वर्गे पुण्यं यथाकाममुपभुङ्क्ते तथाविधः।
en: Such a man, o king proceeding to the celestial region in even his own corporeal frame, enjoys all the, happiness that is there like a celestial at his will.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: एष ते भरतश्रेष्ठ यज्ञानां विधिरुत्तमः॥ याख्यातो ह्यानुपूर्वेण उपवासफलात्मकः।
en: I have thus told you, O chief of the Bharatas, what the excellent ordinances are as son about sacrifices, one ' after another, dependent upon the fruits of fasts.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: दरिद्रैर्मनुजैः पार्थ प्राप्तं यज्ञफलं यथा॥ उपवासानिमान् कृत्वा गच्छेच्च परमां गतिम्। देवद्विजातिपूजायां रतो भरतसत्तम॥ उपवासविधिस्त्वेष विस्तरेण प्रकीर्तितः।
en: Poor men, O of Pritha, may, nevertheless, acquire the fruits thereof (by the observance of fasts). By observing these fasts, even a poor man may acquire the highest end, O foremost one of Bharata's race, devoting himself all the while besides, to the worship of the celestials and the Brahinanas. I have thus recited to you in full the ordinance about fasts.

description: Ordinances equivalent to sacrifices for poor men.
sn: नियतेष्वप्रमत्तेषु शौचवत्सु महात्मसु॥ दम्भद्रोहनिवृत्तेषु कृतबुद्धिषु भारत। अचलेष्वप्रकम्पेषु मा ते भूदत्र संशयः॥
en: Do not entertain any doubt about those men who so observe vows, who are so hecdful and pure and great, who are so freed from pride and malice, who are endued with such devoted understandings, and who pursue their end with such firinness and fixity of purpose without ever deviating from their path.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यद् वरं सर्वतीर्थानां तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह। यत्र चैव परं शौचं तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, o grandfather of that which is considered as the foremost of all Tirthas. Indeed, you should expound to me what that Tirtha is which conduces to the greatest purity.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: भीष्म उवाच सर्वाणि खलु तीर्थानि गुणवन्ति मनीषिणः। यत्तु तीर्थं च शौचं च तन्मे शृणु समाहितः॥
en: Bhishma said Forsooth, all Tirthas are possessed of merit. Listen, however, with attention to me as I tell you what the Tirtha, the cleanser, is of men gifted with wisdom.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: अगाधे विमले शुद्ध सत्यतोये धृतिहदे। स्नातव्यं मानसे तीर्थे सत्त्वमालम्ब्य शाश्वतम्॥
en: Following eternal Truth one should bathe in the Tirtha called Manasa, which is unfathomable, stainless, and pure, and which has Truth for its waters and the understanding for its lake.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: तीर्थशौचमनर्थित्वमार्जवं सत्यमार्दवम्। अहिंसा सर्वभूतानामानृशंस्यं दमः शमः॥
en: The fruits, in the form of cleansing, that one gains by bathing in the Tirtha, are freedom from cupidity, sincerity, truthfulness, mildness, mercy, abstention from injuring any creature, selfcontrol, and tranquillity.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: निर्मला निरहंकारा निर्द्वन्द्वा निष्परिग्रहाः। शुचयस्तीर्थभूतास्ते ये भैक्ष्यमुपभुञ्जते॥
en: Those men who are freed from attachments, who are shorn of pride, who are above all pairs of opposites, who have no wives and children and houses and gardens, etc., who are gifted with purity, and who live upon the alms given to them by others, are considered as Tirthas.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: तत्त्ववित्त्वनहंबुद्धिस्तीर्थप्रवरमुच्यते। शौचलक्षणमेतत् ते सर्वत्रैवान्ववेक्षतः॥
en: He who knows the truths of all things and who is freed from the idea of mineness, is said to be the highest Tirtha. In finding out the marks of purity, your gaze should ever be directed towards these qualities.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: रजस्तमः सत्त्वमथो येषां निधोतमात्मनः। शौचाशौचसमायुक्ताः स्वकार्यपरिमार्गिणः॥ सर्वत्यागेष्वभिरताः सर्वज्ञाः समदर्शिनः। शौचेन वृत्तशौचार्थास्तु तीर्थाः शुचयश्च ये॥
en: Those persons from whose souls the qualities of goodness, darkness, and ignorance have been washed off, they who, not caring for purity and impurity, pursue the ends they have proposed to themselves, they who have renounced everything, they who are possessed of omniscience and gifted with universal sight, and they who are of pure conduct, are considered as Tirthas possessing the purifying power.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: नोदकक्लिन्नगावस्तु स्नात इत्यभिधीयते। स स्नातो यो दमस्नात:स बाह्याभ्यन्तरःशुचिः॥
en: That man whose limbs only are wet with water is not considered as one that is washed. He, on the other hand, is considered as washed who has washed himself by selfdenial. Even such a person is said to be pure both internally and externally.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: अतीतेष्वनपेक्षा ये प्राप्तेष्वर्थेषु निर्ममाः। शोचमेव परं तेषां येषां नोत्पद्यते स्पृहा॥
en: They who never busy themselves with what is past, they who feel no attachment for present acquisitions, indeed, they who are free from desire, are said to be possessed of the highest purity.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: प्रज्ञानं शौचमेवेह शरीरस्य विशेषतः। तथा निष्किंचनत्वं च मनसश्च प्रसन्नता॥
en: Knowledge is said to form the especial purity of the body. So also freedom from desire, and cheerfulness of mind.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: वृत्तशौचं मनःशौचं तीर्थशौचमतः परम्। ज्ञानोत्पन्नं च यच्छौचं तच्छौचं परमं स्मृतम्॥
en: Purity of conduct forms the purity of the mind. The purity that one acquires by ablutions in sacred waters is considered as inferior. Indeed that purity which originates from knowledge, is considered as the best.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: मनसा च प्रदीप्तेन ब्रह्मज्ञानजलेन च। स्नाति यो मानसे तीर्थे तत्स्नानं तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥
en: Those ablutions which one performs with a burning mind in the waters of the knowledge of Brahma in the Tirtha called Manasa, are the true ablutions for truth knowing persons.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: समारोपितशौचस्तु नित्यं भावसमाहितः। केवलं गुणसम्पन्नः शुचिरेव नरः सदा॥
en: That man who is endued with true purity of conduct and who is always given to the preservation of a proper attitude to wards all, indeed, he who is gifted with attributes and merit, is considered as truly pure.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: शरीरस्थानि तीर्थानि प्रोक्तान्येतानि भारत। पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानि पुण्यानि शृणु तान्यपि॥
en: These that I have mentioned have been said to be the Tirthas of the body. Listen to me as I tell you what those sacred Tirthas are that are situate on the Earth also.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: शरीरस्य यथोद्देशाः शुचयः परिकीर्तिताः। तथा पृथिव्या भागाश्च पुण्यानि सलिलानि च॥
en: As special attributes of the body have been said to be sacred, so there are particulars spots on Earth as well, and particular waters, which are considered sacred.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: कीर्तनाच्चैव तीर्थस्य स्नानाच्च पितृतर्पणात्। धुनन्ति पापं तीर्थेषु ते प्रयान्ति सुखं दिवम्॥
en: By reciting the names of the Tirthas, by performing ablutions there, and by offering oblations to the departed Manes in those places, one's sins are dissipated. Those men whose sins are thus dissipated, succeed in acquiring the celestial region, when they leave this world.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: परिग्रहाच्च साधूनां पृथिव्याश्चैव तेजसा। अतीव पुण्यभागास्ते सलिलस्य च तेजसा॥
en: On account of their association with pious persons through the special efficacy of the earth itself, of those spots and of particular waters, there are certain portions of the Earth that have come to be considered as sacred.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: मनसश्च पृथिव्याश्च पुण्यास्तीर्थास्तथापरे। उभयोरेव यःस्नायात् स सिद्धिं शीघ्रमाप्नुयात्॥
en: The mental Tirthas are separate and distinct from those of the Earth. That person who bathes in both acquires success forthwith.

description: The foremost and purest of all Tirthas described
sn: यथा बलं क्रियाहीनं क्रिया वा बलवर्जिता। नेह साधयते कार्य समायुक्ता तु सिध्यति॥ एवं शरीरशौचेन तीर्थशौचेन चान्वितः। शुचिः सिद्धिमवाप्नोति द्विविधं शौचमुत्तमम्॥
en: As strength without exertion, or exertion without strength can never perform anything, singly, and as these, when combined, can do all things, so one that becomes gifted with the purity that is contributed by the Tirthas in the body as also by that which is contributed by the Tirthas on the Earth, becomes truly pure and acquires success. That purity which is derived from both sources is the best.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सर्वेषामुपवासानां यच्छ्रेयः सुमहत्फलम्। यच्चाप्यसंशयं लोके तन्मे त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said You should, O grandfather, tell me what is the highest, the most beneficial, and the most certain fruit of all sorts of fasts in this world.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु राजन् यथा गीतं स्वयमेव स्वयम्भुवा। यत् कृत्वा निर्वृतो भूयात् पुरुषो नात्र संशयः॥
en: Bhishma said Listen, O king, to what was recited by the selfcreate himself and by doing which a person, forsooth, acquires the highest happiness.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: द्वादश्यां मार्गशीर्षे तु अहोरात्रेण केशवम्। अाश्वमेधं प्राप्नोति दुष्कृतं चास्य नश्यति॥
en: That man who fasts on the twelfth day of the moon in the month called Margashira and adores Krishna as Keshava for the whole day and night, acquires the merits of the Horse sacrifice and becomes purged off of all his sins.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: तथैव पौषमासे तू पूज्यो नारायणेति च। वाजपेयमवाप्नोति सिद्धिं च परमां व्रजेत्॥
en: He who, similarly, fasts on the twelfth day of the moon in the month of Pausha and adores Krishna as Narayana, for the whole day and night, acquires the merits of the Vajapeya sacrifice and the highest success.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: अहोरात्रेण द्वादश्यां माघमासे तु माधवम्। राजसूयमवाप्नोति कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत्॥
en: He who fasts on the twelfth day of the moon in the month of Magha and adores Krishna, as Madhava, for the whole day and night, acquires the merits of the Rajasuya sacrifice, and rescues his own family.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: तथैव फाल्गुने मासि गोविन्देति च पूजयन्। अतिरात्रमवाप्नोति सोमलोकं च गच्छति॥
en: He who fasts on the twelfth day of the moon in the month of Phalguna and adores Krishna as Govinda, for the whole day and night, acquires the merit of the Atiratra sacrifice and goes to the region of soma.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: अहोरात्रेण द्वादश्यां चैत्रे विष्णुरिति स्मरन्। पौण्डरीकमवाप्नोति देवलोकं च गच्छति॥
en: He who fasts on the twelfth day of the moon in the month of Chaitra and adores Krishna as Vishnu, for the whole day and night acquires the merit of the Pundarika sacrifice and proceeds to the region of the celestials.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: वैशाखमासे द्वादश्यां पूजयन् मधुसूदनम्। अग्निष्टोममवाप्नोति सोमलोकं च गच्छति॥
en: By observing a similar fast on the twelfth day of the month of Vaishakha and adoring Krishna as the destroyer of Madhur for the whole day and night one acquires the merits of the Agnishtoma sacrifice and proceeds to the region of soma.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: अहोरात्रेण द्वादश्यां ज्येष्ठे मासि त्रिविक्रमम्। गवां मेधमवाप्नोति अप्सरोभिश्च मोदते॥
en: By observing a fast on the twelfth lunar day in the month of Jaishtha and adoring Krishna as him who had covered the universe with three steps of his, one acquires the merits of the Gomedha sacrifice and sports with the Apsaras in great happiness.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: आषाढे मासि द्वादश्यां वामनेति च पूजयन्। नरमेधमवाप्नोति पुण्यं च लभते महत्॥
en: By observing a fast on the twelfth day of the moon in the month of Ashada and adoring Krishna as the Dwarf, one acquires the merits of the Naramedha sacrifice and sports in happiness with the Apsaras.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: अहोरात्रेण द्वादश्यां श्रावणे मासि श्रीधरम्। पञ्चयज्ञानवाप्नोति विमानस्थश्च मोदते॥
en: By observing a fast for the twelfth lunar day of the month of Shravana and adoring Krishna for day and night as Shrecdhara, one acquires the merits of the sacrifice called Panchayajna and acquires a beautiful car in the celestial region where on he sports in joy.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: तथा भाद्रपदे मासि हृषीकेशेति पूजयन्। सौत्रामणिमवाप्नोति पूतात्मा भवते च हि॥
en: By observing a fast on the twelfth day of the moon in the month of Bhadrapada and adoring Krishna as Hrishikesha for the whole day and night, one acquires the merits of the sautramani sacrifice and becomes purged off of all sins.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: द्वादश्यामाश्विने मासि पद्मनाभेति चार्चयन्। गोसहस्रफलं पृण्यं प्राप्नुयान्नात्र संशयः॥
en: By observing a fast for the twelfth day of the moon in the month of Ashvin and adoring Krishna as Padmanabha, onc acquires forsooth, the merits of that sacrifice in which a thousand kine are given away.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: द्वादश्यां कार्तिके मासि पूज्य दामोदरेति च। गवां यज्ञमवाप्नोति पुमान् स्त्री वा न संशयः॥
en: By observing a fast for the twelfth day of the moon in the month of Kartika and adoring Krishna as Damodara, one acquires forsooth, the combined merits of all the sacrifices.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: अर्चयेत् पुण्डरीकाक्षमेवं संवत्सरं तु यः। जातिस्मरत्वं प्राप्नोति विन्द्याद् बहु सुवर्णकम्॥
en: He who, in this way worship Krishna for a whole year as Pundarikaksha, acquires the power of recollecting the incidents of his pristine births and acquires much wealth in gold.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: अहन्यहनि तद्भावमुपेन्द्रं योऽधिगच्छति। समाप्ते भोजयेद् विप्रानथवा दापयेद् घृतम्॥ अतः परं नोपवासो भवतीति विनिश्चयः। उवाच भगवान् विष्णुः स्वयमेव पुरातनम्॥
en: Likewise he who adores Krishna every day as Upendra, acquires oneness with him. After Krishna has been adored thus, one should, at the conclusion of his vow, feed a number of Brahmanas or make gifts of clarified butter to them. The illustrious Vishnu, that ancient Being, has himself said that there is no fast which possesses superior merits.

description: The most beneficial fruit of all fasts
sn: उवाच भगवान् विष्णुः स्वयमेव पुरातनम्॥
en: Likewise he who adores Krishna every day as Upendra, acquires oneness with him. After Krishna has been adored thus, one should, at the conclusion of his vow, feed a number of Brahmanas or make gifts of clarified butter to them. The illustrious Vishnu, that ancient Being, has himself said that there is no fast which possesses superior merits.

description: The means for acquiring beauty, prosperity, good tempor and happiness
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शरतल्पगतं भीष्मं वृद्धं कुरुपितामहम्। उपगम्य महाप्राज्ञः पर्यपृच्छद् युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Approaching Bhishma venerable in years viz., Bhishma, who was then lying on his bed of arrows, the highly wise Yudhishthira put the following questions.

description: The means for acquiring beauty, prosperity, good tempor and happiness
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अङ्गानां रूपसौभाग्यं प्रियं चैव कथं भवेत्। धर्मार्थकामसंयुक्तः सुखभागी कथं भवेत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said How, O grandfather does one acquire beauty of form and prosperity and sweetness of disposition? How, indeed, does one acquire religious meril and wealth and pleasure? How does one win happiness?

description: The means for acquiring beauty, prosperity, good tempor and happiness
sn: भीष्म उवाच मार्गशीर्षस्य मासस्य चन्द्रे मूलेन संयुते। पादौ मूलेन राजेन्द्र जंघायामथ रोहिणीम्॥ अश्चिन्यां सक्थिनी चैव उरू चाषाढयोस्तथा। गुह्यं तु फाल्गुनी विद्यात् कृत्तिका कटिकास्तथा।॥ नाभिं भाद्रपदे विद्याद् रेवत्यामक्षिमण्डलम्। पृष्ठमेव धनिष्ठासु अनुराधोत्तरास्तथा॥ बाहुभ्यां तु विशाखासु हस्तौ हस्तेन निर्दिशेत्। पुनर्वस्वङ्गुली राजन्नाश्लेषासु नखास्तथा॥ ग्रीवां ज्येष्ठा च राजेन्द्र श्रवणेन तु कर्णयोः। मुखं पुष्येण दानेन दन्तोष्ठौ स्वातिरुच्यते॥ हासं शतभिषां चैव मघां चैवाथ नासिकाम्। नेत्रे मृगशिरो विद्याल्ललाटे मित्रमेव तु॥ भरण्यां तु शिरो विद्यात् केशानार्दो नराधिप। समाप्ते तु घृतं दद्याद् ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे॥
en: Bhishma said In the month of Margashira, when the inoon comes in conjunction with the asterism called Mula, when his two feet are united with that very asterism, O king, when Rohini is in his calf, when his knee-joints are in Ashvini, and his thighs are in the two Ashadas when Phalguni makes his anus, and Krittika his waist, when his navel is in Bhadrapada, his ocular region in Revati, and his back on the Dhanishthas, when Anuradha makes his belly, when with his two arms he reaches the Vishakhas, when his two hands are indicated by Hasta, when Punarvasu, O king, makes his fingers, Ashlesha his nails when Jyeshtha makes his neck when Shravana makes his ears, and Pushya his mouth when Svati is said to make his teeth and lips, when Shatabhisha is his smile and Magha his nose, when Mrigashiras is known to be in his eye, and Chitra in his forehead, when his head is in Bharani, when Ardra forms his hair, o king, the vow called Chandravrata should be taken in hand. Upon the termination of that vow, gifts of clarified butter should be made 10 Brahmanas conversant with the Vedas.

description: The means for acquiring beauty, prosperity, good tempor and happiness
sn: सुभगो दर्शनीयश्च ज्ञानभाग्यथ जायते। जायते परिपूर्णाङ्गः पौर्णमास्येव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: As the fruit of that vow one acquires prosperity, personal beauty and that good luck which brings about knowledge. Indeed, onc becomes on account of such a vow, as full of attribute as the full Moon hiinself.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पितामहं महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद। श्रोतुमिच्छामि मानां संसारविधिमुत्तमम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said o grandfather, O greatly wise one, conversant with all the scriptures, I wish to know those excellent ordinances by which mortals have to travel through their rounds of rebirth.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: केन वृत्तेन राजेन्द्र वर्तमाना नरा भुवि। प्राप्नुवन्त्युत्तमं स्वर्गे कथं च नरकं नृप॥
en: What is that conduct by following which O king, men succeed in acquiring high heaven and what is that conduct by which one sinks in Hell?

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: मृतं शरीरमुत्सृज्य काष्ठलोष्टसमं जनाः। प्रयान्त्यमुं लोकमितः को वै ताननुगच्छति॥
en: When renouncing the dead body that is as inert as a piece of wood or clod of earth people proceed to the other world, what are those which follow them there?

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: भीष्म उवाच अयमायाति भगवान् बृहस्पतिरुदारधीः। पृच्छैनं सुमहाभागमेतद् गुह्यं सनातनम्॥
en: Bhishma said Yonder comes the illustrious and highly intelligent Brihaspati. Do you ask his blessed self. The subject is an eternal mystery.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: नैतदन्येन शक्यं हि वक्तुं केनचिदद्य वै। वक्ता बृहस्पति समो न ह्यन्यो विद्यते क्वचित्॥
en: None else is capable of explaining the matter. There is no speaker like Brihaspati.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तयोः संवदतोरेवं पार्थमाङ्गेययोस्तदा। आजगाम विशुद्धद्वात्मा नाकपृष्ठाद् बृहस्पतिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said While the son of Pritha and the son of Ganga were thus conversing with each other, there came at the spot from the sky the illustrious Brihaspati of purified soul.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततो राजा समुत्थाय धृतराष्ट्रपुरोगमः। पूजामनुपमा चक्रे सर्वे ते च सभासदः॥
en: King Yudhishthira, and all others, headed by Dhritarashtra, stood up and received Brihaspati with proper honours. Excellent was the worship they offered to the preceptor of the celestials.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततो धर्मसुतो राजा भगवन्तं बृहस्पतिम्। उपगम्य यथान्यायं प्रश्न पप्रच्छ तत्त्वतः॥
en: Then approaching the illustrious Brihaspati, Dharma's royal son, Yudhishthira, asked him the question in proper form, desirous of knowing the truth.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भगवन् सर्वधर्मज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद।
en: Yudhishthira said O illustrious one, you are conversant with all duties and all the scriptures. Do you tell me what is truly the friend of mortal creatures?

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: मर्त्यस्य कः सहायो वै पिता माता सुतो गुरुः॥ ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिवर्गश्च मित्रवर्गस्तथैव च। मृतं शरीरमुत्सृज्य काष्ठलोष्टसमं जनाः॥
en: Is the father, or mother, or son, or preceptor, or kinsmen, or relatives, or those called friends, that may be said to truly form the friend of a mortal creature? One goes to the next world, leaving his dead body that is like a piece of wood or a clod of earth. Who is it that follows him there?

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच गच्छन्त्यमुत्र लोकं वै क एनमनुगच्छति। एकः प्रसूयते राजन्नेक एव विनश्यति॥
en: Brihaspati said One is born alone, o king, and one dies alone; one crosses alone the difficulties one meets with, and one alone meets whatever misery falls to his lot.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: धर्म:सहायश्च एकस्तरति दुर्गाणि गच्छत्येकस्तु दुर्गतिम्। असहाय: पिता माता तथा भ्राता सुतो गुरुः॥ ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिवर्गश्च मित्रवर्गस्तथैव च। मृतं शरीरमुत्सृज्य काष्ठलोष्टसमं जनाः॥ मुहूर्तमिव रोदित्वा ततो यान्ति पराङ्मुखः।
en: One has really no companion in these deeds. The father the mother, the brother, the son the preceptor kinsmen, relatives and friends, leaving the dead body as if it were a piece of wood or a clod of earth, after having mourned for only a moment, all turn away from it and mind their own affairs.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: तैस्तच्छरीरमुत्सृष्टं धर्म एकोऽनुगच्छति॥ तस्माद् सेवितव्यः सदा नृभिः।
en: Only virtue follows the body that is thus left by them all. It is therefore, plain, that virtue is the only friend and that virtues only should be sought by all.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: प्राणी धर्मसमायुक्तो गच्छेत् स्वर्गगतिं पराम्॥ तथैवाधर्मसंयुक्तो नरकं चोपपद्यते।
en: A virtuous man would acquire that high end which is formed by Heaven. If sinful he goes to hell.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: तस्मान्यायागतैरथैर्धर्मे सेवेत पण्डितः॥ धर्म एको मनुष्याणां सहाय: परिलौकिकः।
en: Hence, an intelligent man should always seek to acquire virtue through wealth acquired by fair means. Virtue is the one only friend whichcrcatures have in the next world.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: लोभान्मोहादनुक्रोशाद् भयाद् वाप्यबहुश्रुतः॥ नरः करोत्यकार्याणि परार्थं लोभमोहितः।
en: Moved by cupidity, or stupefaction, or mercy, or fear, one shorn of knowledge is seen to do unfair deeds, for sake of even another, his judgement thus stupefied by cupidity.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च त्रितयं जीविते फलम्॥ एतत् त्रयमवाप्तव्ययधर्मपरिवर्जितम्।
en: Virtue, wealth, and pleasure, these three form the fruit of life. Onc should win these three by means of being free from impropriety and sin.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतं भगवतो वाक्यं धर्मयुक्तं परं हितम्॥ शरीरनिचयं ज्ञातुं बुद्धिस्तु मम जायते।
en: Yudhishthira said I have carefully heard the words spoken by your illustrious self, these words that are fraught with virtue, and that are highly beneficial, I wish now to know of the state of the body (after death.)

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: मृतं शरीर हि नृणां सूक्ष्ममव्यक्ततां गतम्॥ अचक्षुर्विषयं प्राप्तं कथं धर्मोऽनुगच्छति।
en: The dead body of man becomes subtile and unmanifest. It becomes invisible. How is it possible for virtue to follow it?

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिर्मनोऽन्तगः॥ बुद्धिरात्मा च सहिता धर्मं पश्यन्ति नित्यदा। प्राणिनामिह सर्वेषां साक्षिभूता निशानिशम्॥ एतैश्च सह धर्मोऽपि तं जीवमनुगच्छति।
en: Brihaspati said Earth, Wind Ether, Water, Light, mind, Yama (the king of the dead), Understanding, the soul, as also day and Night, all together witness the merits of all living creatures. With these, virtue follows the creature (When dead.)

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: त्वगस्थिमांसं शुक्रं च शोणितं च महामते॥ शरीरं वर्जयन्त्येते जीवितेन विवर्जितम्
en: When the body becomes bereft of life, skin, bones flesh, the vital seed, and blood, leave it simultaneously.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततो धर्मसमायुक्तः प्राप्नुते जीव एव हि॥ ततोऽस्य कर्म पश्यन्ति शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्। देवताः पञ्चभूतस्थाः किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: Gifted with merit (and demerit) individual soul (after the destruction of this body) comes by another body. After the attainment by individual soul of that body the presiding deities of the five elements once more witness all his deeds, good and bad.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततो धर्मसमायुक्तः स जीव: सुखमेधते। इहलोके परे चैव किं भूयः कथयामि ते॥
en: What else do you wish to hear? If gifted with virtue, individual soul enjoys happiness. What other subject, belonging to this or the other world shall I describe to you?

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच तद् दर्शितं भगवता यथा धर्मोऽनुगच्छति। एतत् तु ज्ञातमिच्छामि कथं रेतः प्रवर्तते॥
en: Yudhishthira said Your illustrious self has explained how virtuc follows individual soul. I wish to know how the vital seed is originated.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: बृहस्पति रुवाच अन्नमश्नन्ति यद् देवाः शरीरस्था नरेश्वर। पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिर्मनस्तथा॥ ततस्तृप्तेषु राजेन्द्र तेषु भूतेषु पञ्चसु। मनःषष्ठेषु शुद्धात्मन् रेतः सम्पद्यते महत्॥
en: Brihaspati said The food that these gods, O king, who live in the body viz Earth, Wind, Ether, Water, Light and Mind, cat, pleases them. When those five elements become pleased, O monarch with Mind numbering as their sixth, their vital seed then becomes generated, O you of purified Soul.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततो गर्भ: सम्भवति श्लेषात् स्त्रीपुंसयोर्नृप। भूयः किं श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: When an act of union takes place between male and female, the vital seed comes out and causes conception. I have thus explained to you what you had asked. When else do you wish to hear.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आख्यातं मे भगवता गर्भः संजायते यथा। यथा जातस्तु पुरुषः प्रपद्यति तदुच्यताम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have, O illustrious one, said how conception takes piace. Do you explain how the individual soul that takes birth, grows.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं आसन्नमात्रः पुरुषस्तैर्भूतैरभिभूयते। विप्रयुक्तश्च तैर्भूतैः पुनर्यात्यपरां गतिम्॥ सर्वभूतसमायुक्तः प्राप्नुते जीव एव हि।
en: Brihaspati said As soon as individual soul enters the vital seed, he becomes overwhelmed by the elements already mentioned. When individual soul become disunited therewith, he is said to attain to the other end (viz., death).

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततोऽस्य कर्म पश्यन्ति शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्। देवताः पञ्चभूतस्था: किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: Gifted with these elements, the individual soul comes by a body. The deities that preside over those elements, witness all his deeds, good and bad. What else do you wish to hear.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच त्वगस्थिमांसमुत्सृज्य तैश्च भूतैर्विवर्जितः। जीवःस भगवन् क्वस्थः सुखदुःखे समश्नुते॥
en: Yudhishthira said Living off skin, bone and flesh, and becoming destitute of all those elements, in what does individual soul reside, O illustrious one, for enjoying and suffering happiness and imisery?

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच जीवः कर्मसमायुक्तः शीघ्रं रेतस्त्वमागतः। स्त्रीणां पुष्पं समासाद्य सूते काले भारत॥
en: Brihaspati said Endued with all his acts, individual soul quickly enters the vital seed, and availing of the menstrual flow of women, takes birth in time, O Bharata.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: यमस्य पुरुषैः क्लेशं यमस्य पुरुषैर्वधम्। दुःखं संसारचक्रं च नरः क्लेशं स विन्दति॥
en: After birth individual soul receives woe and death from the messengers of Yama. Indeed, he goes through misery and a painful round of rebirth.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: इहलोके च स प्राणी जन्मप्रभृति पार्थिव। सुकृतं कर्म वै भुक्ते धर्मस्य फलमाश्रितः॥
en: Endued with life, O king, individual soul in this world, from the moment of his birth, enjoys and suffers his own (pristine deeds), depending upon virtue (and its reverse).

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: यदि धर्म यथाशक्ति जन्मप्रभृति सेवते। ततः स पुरुषो भूत्वा सेवते नित्यदा सुखम्॥
en: If individual soul according to the best of his power, follows virtue from the day of his birth, he them succeeds in enjoying uninterruptedly, when reborn, happiness.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: अथान्तरा तु धर्मस्पाप्यधर्ममुपसेवते। सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं स जीवोऽप्यधिगच्छति॥
en: If, on the other hand, without following virtue without interruption, he acts sinfully, he reaps happiness at first as the reward of his virtue and suffers misery after that.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: अधर्मेण समायुक्तो यमस्य विषयं गतः। महद् दुःखं समासाद्य तिर्यग्योनौ प्रजायते॥
en: Endued with sin, individual soul has to go the dominions of Yama and suffering great misery there he has to take birth in an intermediate order of being.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: कर्मणा येन येनेह यस्यां योनौ प्रजायते। जीवो मोहसमायुक्तस्तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥ यदेतदुच्यते शास्त्रे सेतिहासे च च्छन्दसि। यमस्य विषयं घोरं मया लोकः प्रपद्यते॥
en: Listen to me as I tell you, what the different acts are by doing which individuals soul, Stupefied by folly, has to take birth in different orders of being, as declared in the Vedas, the scriptures, and the histories, Mortals have to go to the dreadful regions of Yama.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: इह स्थानानि पुण्यानि देवतुल्यानि भूपते। तिर्यग्योन्यतिरिक्तानि गतिमन्ति च सर्वशः॥
en: There are, again, places in those regions that are worse than those which are occupied by animals and birds. In those regions, O king there are places which are fraught with every merit and which are worthy on that account of being the habitations of the very celestials.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: यमस्य भवने दिव्ये ब्रह्मलोकसमे गुणैः। कर्मभिर्नियतैर्बद्धो जन्तुर्दुःखान्युपाश्नुते॥
en: Creatures, fettered by their deeds, suffer various kinds of misery. Indeed, there are places of these kinds in the abode of Yama which is equal to the region of Brahman himself in merits.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: येन येन तु भावेन कर्मणा पुरुषो गतिम्। प्रयाति परुषां घोरां तत्ते वक्ष्याम्यत: परम्॥
en: If a twice born person having studied the four Vedas, becomes stupefied by folly and accepts a gift from a fallen man, he has then 10 take birth in the order of asses.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: अधीत्य चतुरो वेदान् द्विजो मोहसमन्वितः। पतितात् प्रतिगृह्याथ खरयोनौ प्रजायते॥
en: I shall after this tell you what those acts and dispositions are on account of which a person acquires an end that is fraught with great misery and terror.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: खरो जीवति वर्षाणि दस पञ्च च भारत। खरो मृतो बलीवर्दः सप्त वर्षाणि जीवति॥
en: He has to live as an ass for fifteen years, Shaking off his assinine form, he has next to take birth as an ox and which state he has to live for seven years.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: बलीवर्दो मृतश्चापि जायते ब्रह्मराक्षसः। ब्रह्मरक्षश्च मासांस्त्रीस्ततो जायति ब्राह्मणः॥
en: Throwing off his bovine forın, he has next to take birth as a Rakshasa of the twice born order. Living as a Rakshasa of the twice born order for three months, he then regains his status of a Brahmana.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: पतितं याजयित्वा तु कृतियोनौ प्रजायते। तत्र जीवति वर्षाणि दश पञ्च च भारत॥
en: A Brahmana, by officiating at the sacrifice of a degraded person, has to take birth as a vile worm. In this form he has to live for fifteen years, O Bharata.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: कृमिभावाद् विमुक्तस्तु ततो जायति गर्दभः। गर्दभः पञ्च वर्षाणि पञ्च वर्षाणि सूकरः॥
en: Freed from his worm birth, he is next born as an ass. As an ass he has to live for five years, and then as a hog, in which state also he has to reinain for as many years.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: कुक्कुटः पञ्च वर्षाणि पञ्च वर्षाणि जम्बुकः। श्रा वर्षमेकं भवति ततो जायति मानवः॥
en: After that he is born as a cock, and living for five years in that form, he is born as a jackal and lives for as many years in that state. He is then born as a dog, and living thus for a ycar he regains his manhood.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: उपाध्यायस्य यः पापं शिष्यः कुर्यादबुद्धिमान्। स जीव इह संसारांस्त्रीनाप्नोति न संशयः॥
en: That foolish disciple who offends his preceptor by injuring him, has certainly to undergo three changes in this world.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: प्राश्वा भवति राजेन्द्र ततः क्रव्यात्ततः खरः। ततः प्रेतः परिक्लिष्टः पश्चाज्जायति ब्राह्मणः॥
en: Such a person, o king, has in the first instance to become a dog. He has then to become a beast of prey, and then an ass. Living his assinine form he has to wander for sometime in great, misery as a spirit. After the expiration of that time, he is born as a Brahmana.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: मनसापि गुरोर्भार्यां यः शिष्यो याति पापकृत्। स उग्रान् प्रैति संसारानधर्मेणेह चेतसा॥
en: That sinful disciple who even in thought knows the wife of his preceptor, has, on account of such a sinful heart, to undergo many dreadful shapes in this world.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: वयोनौ तु स सम्भूतस्त्रीणि वर्षाणि जीवति। तत्रापि निधनं प्राप्तः कृमियोनौ प्रजायते॥
en: First taking birth in the canine order he has to live for three years. Throwing off the canine forin when death comes, he is born as a vile vermin.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: कृमिभावमनुप्राप्तो वर्षमेकं तु जीवति। ततस्तु निधनं प्राप्तो ब्रह्मयोनौ प्रजायते॥
en: In this form he has to live for a year. Renouncing that form he succeeds in regaining his status as a human being of the twice born order.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: यदि पुत्रसमं शिष्यं गुरुर्हन्यादकारणे। आत्मनः कामकारेण सोऽपि हिंस्रः प्रजायते॥
en: If the preceptor kills, without reason, his disciple who is even as a son to him, he has on account of such a wilful deed of sin on his part, to take birth as a beast of prey.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: पितरं मातरं चैव यस्तु पुत्रोऽवमन्यते। सोऽपि राजन् मृतो जन्तुः पूर्वं जायेत गर्दभः॥
en: That son who disregards his father and mother, O king, is born after renouncing his human form as an ass.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: गर्दभत्वं तु सम्प्राप्य दशवर्षाणि जीवति। संवत्सरं तु कुम्भीरस्ततो जायेत मानवः॥
en: Assuming the assinine form he has to live for ten years. After that he is born as a crocodile, in which form he has to live for a year. After that he regains the human forin.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: पुत्रस्य मातापितरौ यस्य रुष्टावुभावपि। गुर्वपध्यानतः सोऽपि मृतो जायति गर्दभः॥
en: That son with whom his parents become angry has on account of his evil thoughts towards them, to take birth as an ass.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: खरो जीवति मासांस्तु दश श्वा च चतुर्दश। बिडालः सप्तमासांस्तु ततो जायति मानवः॥
en: As an ass he has to live for ten months. He is next born as a dog and has to remain as such for fourteen months. After that he is born as a cat and living in that form for seven months he regains his human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: मातापितरावाश्य सारिकः सम्प्रजायते। ताडयित्वा तु तावेव जायते कच्छपो नृप॥
en: Having spoken ill of parents one is born as a Sarika. Striking them one is born, O king as a tortoise.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: कच्छपो दश वर्षाणि त्रीणि वर्षाणि शल्यकः। व्यालो भूत्वा च षण्मासांस्ततो जायति मानुषः॥
en: Living as a tortoise for ten years, he is born as a porcupine. After that he has to take birth as a snake, and living for six months in that form he regains human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: भर्तृपिण्डमुपाश्नन् यो राजद्विष्टानि सेवते। सोऽपि मोहसमापन्नो मृतो जायति वानरः॥
en: That man who, while living upon the food that his royal master supplies, commits deeds injurious to the interests of his master, stupefied by folly, has, after death, to take birth as a monkey.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: वानरो दश वर्षाणि पञ्च वर्षाणि मूषिकः। श्वाथ भूत्वा तु षण्मा सांस्ततो जायति मानुषः॥
en: For ten years he has to live as a monkey, and after that for five years as a mouse. After that he is born as a dog, and living in that form for six months he succeeds in regaining his human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: न्यासापहर्ता तु नरो यमस्य विषयं गतः। संसाराणां शतं गत्वा कृमियोनौ प्रजायते॥
en: That man who misappropriates what is deposited with him in trust, has to undergo a hundred births. He at last takes birth as a vile worm.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: तत्र जीवति वर्षाणि दश पञ्च च भारत। दुष्कृतस्य क्षयं कृत्वा ततो जायति मानुषः॥
en: In that order he has to live for fifteen years, O Bharata. Upon the exhaustion of his sin in this way, he succeeds in regaining his human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: असूयको नरश्चापि मृतो जायति शार्ङ्गकः। विश्वासहर्ता तु नरो मीनो जायति दुर्मतिः॥
en: That man who has malice towards others, has, after death, to take birth as a sharngaka. That wicked man who becomes guilty of breach of trust has to take birth as a fish.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: भूत्वा मीनोऽष्ट वर्षाणि मृतो जायति भारत। मृगस्तु चतुरो मासांस्ततश्छागः प्रजायते॥
en: Living as a fish for eight years he is born, O Bharata, as a deer. Living as a deer for four months he is next born as a goat.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: छागस्तु निधनं प्राप्य पूर्ण संवत्सरे ततः। कीटः संजायते जन्तुस्ततो जायति मानुषः॥
en: After the expiration of a full year, he renounces his goatish body, and is then born as a worm. After that he succeeds in regaining his human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: धान्यान् यवास्तिलान् माषान् कुलत्थान् सर्षपांश्चणान् कलापानथ मुद्गांश्च गोधूमानतसींस्तथा॥ सस्यस्यान्यस्य हर्ता च मोहाज्जन्तुरचेतनः। स जायते महाराज मूषिको निरपत्रपः॥
en: That shameless insensate man who, through stupefaction, steals paddy, barley sesame, Masha, Kulattha, oil seeds, oats Kalaya, Mudga, wheat, Atasi, and other kinds of corn, is born as a mouse.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततः प्रेत्य महाराज मृतो जायति सूकरः। सूकरो जातमात्रस्तु रोगेण म्रियते नृप।॥
en: After leading the life for sometime, he is next born as a hog. As soon as he is born as a hog he has to die of diseasc.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: श्वा ततो जायते पूढः कर्मणा तेन पार्थिव। भूत्वा श्वा पञ्च वर्षाणि ततो जायति मानवः॥
en: On account of his sin, that foolish man has next to take birth as a dog, O king. Living as a dog for five years, he then regains his human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: परदाराभिमर्श तु कृत्वा जायति वै वृकः। श्वा शृगालस्ततो गृध्रो व्याल:कंको बकस्तथा॥
en: Having committed an act of adultery with the wife of another man, one is born as a wolf. After that he has to assume the forms of a dog and jacka! and vulture. He has next to take birth as a snake and then as a Kanka (a bird of prey) and then as a crane.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: भ्रातुर्भार्यो तु पापात्मा यो धर्षयति मोहितः। पुस्कोकिलत्वमाप्नोति सोऽपि संवत्सरं नृप॥
en: That sinful wight who out of foolishness, knows his brother's wife, has to take birth as a male Coel and to live in that form for a whole year, O king.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: सखिभार्यां गुरोर्भार्यां राजभार्यां तथैव च। प्रधर्षयित्वा कामाया मृतो जायति सूकरः॥
en: He who, through lust, knows the wife of a friend, or the wife of preceptor, or the wife of his king, has after death to take the form of a hog.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: सूकरः पञ्च वर्षाणि दश वर्षाणि श्वाविधः। बिडालः पञ्च वर्षाणि दश वर्षाणि कुक्कुटः॥
en: He has to live in this form for five years and then to assume that of a wolf for ten years. For the next five years he has to live as a cat and then for the next ten years as a cock.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: पिपीलकस्तु मासांस्त्रीन् कीट:स्यान्मासमेव तु। एतानासाद्य संसारान् कृमियोनौ प्रजायते॥ तत्र जीवति मासांस्तु कृमियोनौ चतुर्दश। ततोऽधर्मक्षयं कृत्वा पुनर्जायति मानवः॥
en: He is next born as an ant, for three months and then as a worm for a month. Having undergone these births, he has next to live as a vile worm for fourteen years. When his sin becomes exhausted by such punishment, he at last regains the human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: उपस्थिते विवाहे तु यज्ञे दानेऽपि वा विभो। मोहात् करोति यो विघ्नं स मृतो जायते कृमिः॥
en: When a marriage is about to take place a sacrifice or an act of gifts is about to be made, O you of great power the man who puts in any impediment has to take birth in his next life as a vile worm.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: कृमिर्जीवति वर्षाणि दश पञ्च च भारत। अधर्मस्य क्षयं कृत्वा ततो जायति मानवः॥
en: Assuming such a form he has to live, O Bharata, for fifteen years. When his sin is exhausted by such suffering, he regains the human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: पूर्वं दत्त्वा तु यः कन्यां द्वितीये दातुमिच्छति। सोऽपि राजन् मृतो जन्तुः कृमियोनौ प्रजायते॥
en: Having once bestowed his daughter in marriage upon a person, he who seeks to bestow her again upon a second husband, is compelled, O king, to take birth among vile worms.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: तत्र जीवति वर्षाणि त्रयोदश युधिष्ठिर। अधर्मसंक्षये युक्तस्ततो जायति मानवः॥
en: Assuming such a form, O Yudhishthira, he has to live for thirteen years. Upon the exhaustion of his sin by such sufferance, he regains the human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: देवकार्यमकृत्वा तु पितृकार्यमथापि वा। अनिर्वाप्य समश्चन् वै मृतो जायति वायसः॥
en: He who eats without having performed the rites in honour of the celestials or those in honour of the departed Manes or without having offered (even) oblations of water to both the Rishis and the departed Manes has to take birth as a crow.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: वायसः शतवर्षाणि ततो जायति कुक्कुटः। जायते व्यालकश्चापि मासं तस्मात् तु मानुषः॥
en: Living as a crow for a hundred years, he next assumes the forin of a cock. His next change is that of a snake for a month. After this he regains the human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ज्येष्ठं पितृसमं चापि भ्रातरं योऽवमन्यते। सोऽपि मृत्युमुपागम्य क्रौञ्चयोनौ प्रजायते॥
en: He who disregards his eldest brother who is like a father, has, after death, to take birth as a crane.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: क्रौञ्चो जीवति वर्षे तु ततो जायति चीरकः। ततो निधनमापन्नो मानुषत्वमुपाश्नुते॥
en: Having assumed that form he has to live in it for two years. Renouncing that form at the conclusion of that period, he regains the human forin.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: वृषलो ब्राह्मणीं गत्वा कृमियोनौ प्रजायते। ततः सम्प्राप्य निधनं जायते सूकरः पुनः॥
en: That Shudra who knows a Brahmani woman has after death, to take birth as hog.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: सूकरो जातमात्रस्तु रोगेण म्रियते नृप। श्वा ततो जायते मूढः कर्मणा तेन पार्थिव॥
en: As soon as he takes birth in that order he dies of disease, O king. The wretch has next to take birth as a dog, O king, on account of that sinful deed.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: श्वा भूत्वा कृतकर्माऽसौ जायते मानुषस्ततः। तत्रापत्यं समुत्पाद्य मृतो जायति मूषिकः॥
en: Renouncing his canine form he regains, upon the exhaustion of his sin, the human form. The Shudra who begets offspring upon a Brahmani woman, leaving off his human form, is born again as a mouse. man

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: कृतघ्नस्तु मृतो राजन् यमस्य विषयं गतः। यमस्य पुरुषैः क्रुद्धैर्वधं प्राप्नोति दारुणम्॥
en: The who becomes guilty of ingratitude, O king, has to go to the regions of Yama and there to suffer very painful and severe treatment at the hands of the emissaries, provoked to fury of the grim king of the dead.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: दण्डं समुन्दरं शूलमग्निकुम्भं च दारुणम्। असिपत्रवनं घोरवालुकं कूटशाल्मलीम्॥ एताश्चान्याश्च बह्वीश्च यमस्य विषयं गतः। यातनाः प्राप्य तत्रोग्रास्ततो वध्यति भारत॥
en: Clubs with heavy hammers and mallets sharppointed lances heated jars, dreadful sword blades heated sands, thorny Shalmalisthese and many other engines of torture such a man has to suffer in the regions of Yama, O Bharata,

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततो हतः कृतघ्नः स तत्रोग्रैर्भरतर्षभ। संसारचक्रमासाद्य कृमियोनौ प्रजायते॥
en: O chief of Bharata's race, having suffered such dreadful treatment in the regions of the grim king of the dead, the ungrateful person has to return to this world and take birth among vile vermin.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: कृमिर्भवति वर्षाणि दश पञ्च च भारत। ततो गर्भं समासाद्य तत्रैव म्रियते शिशुः॥
en: He has to live as a vile vermin for a period of fifteen years, O Bharata. He has then to enter the womb and dic prematurely before birth.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततो गर्भशतैर्जन्तुर्बहुभिः सम्प्रद्यते। संसारांश्च बहून् गत्वा ततस्तिर्यक्षु जायते॥
en: After this that person has to enter the womb a hundred times successively. Indeed, having undergone a hundred rebirths, he at last is born as a creature in some interinediate order between man and inanimate nature.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततो दुःखमनुप्राप्य बहु वर्षगणानिह। अपुनर्भवसंयुक्तस्तत: कूर्मः प्रजायते॥
en: Having suffered misery for a great many years, he has to take birth as hairless tortoise.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: दधि हत्वा बकश्चापि प्लवो मत्स्यानसंस्कृतान्। चोरयित्वा तु दुर्बुद्धिर्मधु दंशः प्रजायते॥
en: A person who steals curds is born as a crane. One becomes a monkey by stealing raw fish. That intelligent man who steals honey, is born as a gadfly.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: फलं वा मूलकं हृत्वा अपूपं वा पिपीलिकाः। चोरयित्वा च निष्पावं जायते हलगोलकः॥
en: By stealing fruits or roots or cakes, one becomes an ant. By stealing Nishpava, one becomes a Halagolaka.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: पायसं चोरयित्वा तु तित्तिरित्वमवाप्नुते। हृत्वा पिष्टमयं पूपं कुम्भोलूकः प्रजायते॥
en: By stealing Payasa, one becomes, in his next birth, a Tittiri bird. By stealing cakes, one becomes a screechowl.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: अयो हत्वा तु दुर्बुद्धिर्वायसो जायते नरः। कांस्यं हत्वा तु दुर्बुद्धिरेरितो जायते नरः॥
en: That littlewitted man who steals iron has to take birth as a cow. That man who steals white brass, is born as a bird of the Harita spccies.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: राजतं भाजनं हृत्वा कपोतः सम्प्रजायते। हृत्वा तु काञ्चनं भाण्डं कृमियोनौ प्रजायते॥
en: By stealing a silver vessel, one becomes a pigeon. By stealing a golden vessel, one has to take birth as a vile veriin.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: पत्रोर्णं चोरयित्वा तु कृकलत्वं निगच्छति। कौशिकं तु ततो हत्वा नरो जायति वर्तकः॥
en: By stealing a piece of silken cloth, one becomes a Krikara. By stealing a piece of cloth made of red silk, one becomes a Vartaka.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: अंशुकं चोरयित्वा तु शुको जायति मानवः। चोरयित्वा दुकूलं तु मृतो हंसः प्रजायते॥
en: By stealing a picce of muslin, one becomes a parrot. By stealing a piece of cloth that is of fine texture one becomes a swan after renouncing his human body.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: क्रौञ्चः कासिकं हृत्वा मृतो जायति मानवः। चोरयित्वा नरः पटें त्वाविकं चैव भारत॥ क्षौमं च वस्त्रमादाय शशो जन्तुः प्रजायते। वर्णान् हृत्वा तु पुरुषो मृतो जायति बर्हिणः॥
en: By stealing a piece of cotton cloth, one becomes a Krauncha bird after renouncing his human body, and O Bharata, stealing a shoulder sheet of cloth, garment made of sheep wool and a piece of linen, one is born as a hare. By stealing different sorts of colouring matter, one is born as a peacock.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: हृत्वा रक्तानि वस्त्राणि जायते जीवजीवकः। वर्णकादींस्तथा गन्धांश्चोरयित्वेह मानवः॥ छुच्छन्दरित्वमाप्नोति राजञ्लोभपरायणः। तत्र जीवति वर्षाणि ततो दश च पञ्च च॥
en: By stealing a piece of red cloth one is born as a bird of the Jivajivaka species. By stealing unguents (such as sandalpaste) and perfumes in this world, the avaricious man, O king, is born as a mole. Assuming the form of a mole one has to live in it for fifteen years.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: अधर्मस्य क्षयं गत्वा ततो जायति मानुषः। चोरयित्वा पयश्चापि बलाका सम्प्रजायते॥
en: After the exhaustion of his sin by such suffering he regains the human form. By stealing milk, one becomes a crane.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: यस्तु चोरयते तैलं नरो मोहसमन्वितः। सोऽपि राजन् मृतो जन्तुस्तैलपायी प्रजायते॥
en: That inan, king, who through stupefaction of the understanding, steals oil, is born, after renouncing this body, as an animal who lives upon oil as his form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: अशस्त्रं पुरुषं हत्वा सशस्त्र: पुरुषाधमः। अर्थार्थी यदि वा वैरी स मृतो जायते खरः॥
en: That wretch who, himself wellarmed, kills another while that other is unarined, for getting his riches or out of hostile feelings, has, after renouncing his human body, to take birth as an ass.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: खरो जीवति वर्षे द्वे ततः शस्त्रेण वध्यते। स मृतो मृगयोनौ तु नित्योद्विग्नोऽभिजायते॥
en: Assuming that assinine form, he has to live for a period of two years and then he is killed by a weapon, Renouncing his assinine body, he has to take birth, in his next life, as a deer always anxious (for fear of being killed.)

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: अधर्मस्य क्षयं कृत्वा मृगो वध्यति शस्त्रेण गते संवत्सरे तु सः। हतो मृगस्ततो मीनः सोऽपि जालेन बध्यते॥ मासे चतुर्थे सम्प्राप्ते श्वापदः सम्प्रजायते। श्वापदो दश वर्षाणि द्वीपी वर्षाणि पञ्च च॥
en: Upon the expiration of a year from the time of his birth as a deer, he is killed by a weapon. Thus renouncing his form of a deer, he next takes birth as a fish and dies on account of being dragged up in a net, on the expiration of the fourth month. He has next to take birth as a beasts of prey. He has to live in that form, for ten years and then he takes birth as a bird in which form he has to live for five years.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततस्तु निधनं प्राप्तः कालपर्यायचोदितः। ततो जायति मानुषः॥
en: Actuated by the change that is occasioned by time, he then renounces that form and, his sin having been exhausted, he regains the human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: स्त्रियं हत्वा तु दुर्बुद्धिर्यमस्य विषयं गतः। बहून् क्लेशान् समासाद्य संसारांश्चैव विंशतिम्॥११७
en: That man of little understanding who slays a woman has to go to the regions of Yama and to suffer various kinds of pain and misery. He then has to pass through full twentyone transformations.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ततः पश्चान्महाराज कृमियोनौ प्रजायते। कृमिर्विंशतिवर्षाणि भूत्वा जायति मानुषः॥
en: After that, О king, he has to take birth as a vile vermin. Living as a vermin for twenty years, he regains the human form.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: भोजनं चोरयित्वा तु मक्षिका जायते नरः। मक्षिकासंघवशगो बहून् मासान् भवत्युता। ११९ ।। ततः पापक्षयं कृत्वा मानुषत्वमवाप्नुते। धान्यं हत्वा तु पुरुषो लोमशः सम्प्रजायते॥
en: By stealing food, one has to take birth as a bee. Living for many months in the company of other bees, his sin become exhausted and he regains the human form. By stealing paddy, one becomes a cat.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: तथा पिण्याकसम्मिश्रमशनं चोरयेन्नरः। स जायते बभ्रुसमो दारुणो मूषिको नरः॥
en: That man who steals food mixed with sesame cakes is in his next birth born as a mouse large or small according to the largeness or smallness of the quantity stolen.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: दशन् वै मानुषान्नित्यं पापात्मा स विशाम्पते। घृतं हृत्वा तु दुर्बुद्धिः काकमद्गुः प्रजायते॥
en: He bites human beings every day and, therefore, becomes sinful and passes through a varied round of rebirths. That foolish man who steals clarified butter has to take birth as a gallinule.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: मत्स्यमांसमथो हृत्वा काको जायति दुर्मतिः। लवणं चोरयित्वा तु चिरिकाकः प्रजायते॥
en: That wicked man who steals fish has to take birth as a crow. By stealing salt one has to take birth as an imitating parrot.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: विश्वासेन तु निक्षिप्तं यो विनिहोति मानवः। स गतायुर्नरस्तात मत्स्ययोनौ प्रजायते॥
en: That man who misappropriates trust property, has to suffer a diminution in the period of his life and dying has to take birth ainong fishes.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: मत्स्ययोनिमनुप्राप्य मृतो जायति मानुषः। मानुषत्वमनुप्राप्य क्षीणायुरुपपद्यते॥
en: Having lived for sometime as a fish, he dies and regains the human form. Regaining, however, the human form he becomes short lived.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: पापानि तु नराः कृत्वा तिर्यग् जायन्ति भारत। न चात्मनः प्रमाणं ते धर्मे जानन्ति किंचन॥
en: Indeed having perpetrated sins, O Bharata, one has to take birth in an order intermediate between that of humanity and vegetables. Those people do not know the principles of virtue who take their own hearts for their guide.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: ये पापानि नराः कृत्वा निरस्यन्ति व्रतैः सदा। सुखदुःखसमायुक्ता व्यथितास्ते भवन्त्युत॥
en: Those men who commit various sinful deeds, and then scck to expiate them by continuous vows and observances of piety, enjoy happiness and suffer misery and live in great anxiety of heart.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: असंवासाः प्रजायन्ते म्लेच्छाश्चापि न संशयः। नराः पापसमाचारा लोभमोहसमन्विताः॥
en: Those sinful men who yield to the influence of cupidity and stupefaction, are surely born as Mlechchhas who are uriworthy of being associated with.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: वर्जयन्ति च पापानि जन्मप्रभृति ये नराः। अरोगा रूपवन्तस्ते धनिनश्च भवन्त्युत॥
en: Those men, on the other hand, who abstain from sin all their lives, become free from disease of every sort gifted with beauty of form, and possessed of riches.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: स्त्रियोऽप्येतेन कल्पेन कृत्वा पापमवाप्नुयुः। एतेषामेव जन्तूनां भार्यात्वमुपयान्ति ताः॥
en: Women also when they act in this way attain to births of the same kind. Indeed, they have to take births as the males of the animals I have mentioned.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: परस्वहरणे दोषाः सर्व एव प्रकीर्तिताः। एतद्धि लेशमात्रेण कथितं ते मयाऽनद्य॥
en: I have told you all the faults of the misappropriation of others' properties. I have described to you very briefly the subject, O sinless one.

description: The deeds by which one goes to heaven or hell
sn: अपरस्मिन् कथायोगे भूयः श्रोष्यसि भारत। एतन्मया महाराज ब्रह्मणो वदतः पुरा॥ सुरर्षीणां श्रुतं मध्ये पृष्टश्चापि यथातथम्। मयापि तच्च कार्थेन यथावदनुवर्णितम्। एतच्छुत्वा महाराज धर्मे कुरु मनः सदा॥
en: In connection with some other subject, O Bharata, you will again hear of those faults. I heard all this O king, Formerly from Bhrahman himself, and I asked all about it in a proper way, when he described it in the midst of the celestial Rishis. I have told you truly and in detail all that you had asked me. Having listened to all this,.o king, do you always set your heart on virtue.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अर्धमस्य गतिर्ब्रह्मन् कथिता मे त्वयाऽनघ। धर्मस्य तु गतिं श्रोतुमिच्छामि वदतां वर॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have told me, O twiceborn one, what the end is of virtue or sin, I wish now to hear, O foremost of speakers, of what the end is of virtue.

sn: कृत्वा कर्माणि पापानि कथं यान्ति शुभां गतिम्। कर्मणा च कृतेनेह केन यान्ति शुभां गतिम्॥
en: Having committed various sinful deeds, by what acts do people succeed in acquiring an auspicious end in this world? By what acts also, do people acquire auspicious end in the celestial region?

sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच कृत्वा पापानि कर्माणि अधर्मवशमागतः। मनसा विपरीतेन निरयं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Brihaspati said By committing sinful deeds with perverted mind, one gives way to the influence of sin, and accordingly goes to Hell.

sn: मोहादधर्मं यः कृत्वा पुनः समनुतप्यते। मन:समाधिसंयुक्तो न स सेवेते दुष्कृतम्॥ यथा यथा मनस्तस्य दुष्कृतं कर्म गर्हते। तथा तथा शरीर तु तेनाधर्मेण मुच्यते॥
en: That man who having perpetrated sinful deeds through stupefaction of mind, feels the pangs of repentance and sets his heart on meditation (of the deity), has not to suffer the consequences of his sins. One becomes freed from his sins inasmuch as he repents for them.

sn: यदि व्याहरते राजन् विप्राणां धर्मवादिनाम्। ततोऽधर्मकृतात् क्षिप्रमवादात् प्रमुच्यते॥
en: If one having committed a sin, O king, mentions it before Brahmanas conversant with a duties, he speedily becomes freed from the obloquy arising from his sin.

sn: यथा यथा नरः सम्यगधर्ममनुभाषते। समाहितेन मनसा विमुच्येत तथा तथा। भुजङ्ग इव निर्मोकात् पूर्वमुक्ताज्जरान्वितात्॥
en: Accordingly as one mentions his sins, fully or otherwise, with concentrated mind, he becomes cleansed there from fully or otherwise, like a snake freed from his diseased slough.

sn: दत्त्वा विप्रस्य दानानि विविधानि समाहितः। मन:समाधिसंयुक्तः सुगति प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: By making with a concentrated mind, gifts of various kinds to Brahmana, and concentrating the mind (on the deity), one attains to an auspicious end.

sn: प्रदानानि तु वक्ष्यामि यानि दत्त्वा युधिष्ठिर। नरः कृत्वाप्यकार्याणि ततो धर्मेण युज्यते॥
en: I shall now tell you what those gifts are, o Yudhishthira, by making which a person, even if guilty of having committed sinful deeds, may become gifted with merit.

sn: सर्वेषामेव दानानामन्नं श्रेष्ठमुदाहृतम्। पूर्वमन्नं प्रदातव्यमृजुना धर्ममिच्छता॥
en: Of all kinds of gifts, that of food is considered as the best. One desirous of acquiring merit should, with a sincere heart, make gifts of food.

sn: प्राणा ह्यन्नं मनुष्याणां तस्माज्जन्तुश्च जायते। अन्ने प्रतिष्ठितो लोकस्तस्मादनं प्रशस्यते॥
en: Food is the vital air of men. From it all creatures originate. All the worlds of living creatures are established upon food. Hence food is highly spoken of.

sn: अन्नमेव प्रशंसन्ति देवर्षिपितृमानवाः। अन्नस्य हि प्रदानेन रन्तिदेवो दिवं गतः॥
en: The deities Rishis, departed manes, and men, all praise food. Formerly king Rantideva, proceeded to the celestial region by making gifts of food.

sn: न्यायलब्धं प्रदातव्यं द्विजातिभ्योऽन्नमुत्तमम्। स्वाध्यायं समुपेतेभ्यः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना॥
en: Good food that has been acquired by fair means, should be given with a cheerful heart, lo Brahmanas possessed of Vedic learning.

sn: यस्य ह्यन्नमुपाश्नन्ति ब्राह्मणानां शतं दशं। हृष्टेन मनसा दत्तं न स तिर्यग्गतिर्भवेत्॥
en: That man, whose food, given with a cheerful heart, is taken by a is taken by a thousand Brahmanas, has never to take birth in an intermediate order.

sn: ब्राह्मणानां सहस्राणि दश भोज्य नरर्षभ। नरोऽधर्मात् प्रमुच्येत योगेष्वभिरतः सदा॥
en: A person, O king, by feeding ten thousand Brahmanas, becomes cleansed of sin and devoted to Yoga practices.

sn: भैक्ष्येणान्नं समाहृत्य विप्रो वेदपुरस्कृतः। स्वाध्यायनिरते विप्रे दत्त्वेह सुखमेधते॥
en: A Brahmana knowing the Vedas, by giving away food acquired by him as alms, to a Brahmana devoted to the study of the Vedas, succeeds in acquiring happiness here.

sn: अहिंसन् ब्राह्मणस्वानि न्यायेन परिपाल्य च। क्षत्रियस्तरसा प्राप्तमन्नं यो वै प्रयच्छति॥ द्विजेभ्यो वेदवृद्धेभ्यः प्रयत: सुसमाहितः। तेनोपोहति धर्मात्मन् दुष्कृतं कर्म पाण्डव॥
en: That Kshatriya who, without taking anything belonging to a Brahmana, protects his subjects lawfully, and makes gifts of food, obtained by his strength. to Brahmanas foremost in Vedic knowledge, with concentrated heart, succeeds by such conduci, O you of righteous soul in cleansing himself, O son of Pandu, of all his sinful deeds.

sn: षड्भागपरिशुद्धं च कृपेर्भागमुपार्जितम्। वैश्यो ददद् द्विजातिभ्यः पापेभ्यः परिमुच्यते॥
en: Thai Vaishya who divides the produce of his fields into six equal parts and makes of gift a one of those shares to Brahmanas, succeeds by such conduct in cleansing himself from every sin.

sn: अवाप्य प्राणसंदेहं कार्कश्येन समार्जितम्। अन्नं दत्त्वा द्विजातिभ्यः शूद्रः पापात्प्रमुच्यते॥
en: That Shudra who acquiring food by hard labour and at the risk of life itself, makes a gift of it to Brahmanas, becomes purged off of every sin.

sn: औरसेन बलेनान्नमर्जयित्वाविहिंसकः। यः प्रयच्छति विप्रेभ्यो न स दुर्गाणि पश्यति॥
en: That man who, by dint of his physical strength acquires food without doing any act of injury to any creature, and makes gift of it to Brahmanas, succeeds in avoiding all calamities.

sn: न्यायेनैवाप्तमन्नं तु नरो हर्षसमन्वितः। द्विजेभ्यो वेदवृद्धेभ्यो दत्त्वा पापात् प्रमुच्यते॥
en: A person by cheerfully making gifts of food acquired by fair means to Brahmans pereminent for Vedic learning, becomes purged off of all his sins.

sn: अन्नपूर्जस्करं लोके दत्त्वोर्जस्वी भवेन्नरः। सतां पन्थानमावृत्य सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: By treading in the path of the pious, one becomes freed from all sins, A person by making gifts of such food as creates great energy becomes himself endued with great energy.

sn: दानवद्भिः कृतः पन्था येन यान्ति मनीषिणः। ते हि प्राणस्य दातारस्तेभ्यो धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: The path made by charitable persons, is always trod by the wise. They who make gifts of food, are considered as givers of life. The merit they acquire by such gifts, is eternal.

sn: सर्वावस्थं मनुष्येण न्यायेनान्नमुपार्जितम्। कार्यं पात्रागतं नित्यमन्नं हि परमा गतिः॥
en: Hence, person should, under all circumstances, seek to acquire food by fair means, and having got it to make always gifts of it to worthy men. Food is the great support of living creatures.

sn: अन्नस्य हि प्रदानेन नरो रौद्रं न सेवते। तस्मादन्नं प्रदातव्यमन्यायपरिवर्जितम्॥
en: By making gifts of food, one has never to go to hell. Hence one should always make gifts of food, having got it by fair means. a

sn: यतेद् ब्राह्मणपूर्वं हि भोक्तुमन्नं गृही सदा। अवन्ध्यं दिवसं कुर्यादन्नदानेन मानवः॥
en: The householder should always try to eat after having made a gift of food to a Brahmana. Every man should make the day fruitful by making gifts of food.

sn: भोजयित्वा दशशतं नरो वेदविदां नृप। न्यायविद्धर्मविदुषामितिहासविदां तथा॥ न याति नरकं घोरं संसारांश्च न सेवते। सर्वकामसमायुक्तः प्रेत्य चाप्यश्नुते सुखम्॥
en: A person by feeding, O king a thousand Brahmanas who are all conversant with duties and the scriptures and the sacred histories, has not to go to Hell and to return to this world for going through rebirths. Gifted with the fruition of every desire he enjoys great happiness in the next world.

sn: एवं खलु समायुक्तो रमते विगतज्वरः। रूपवान् कीर्तिमांश्चैव धनवांश्चोपपद्यते॥
en: Gifted with such merit, he sports in happiness, freed from every anxiety, possessed of personal beauty and great fame and endued with wealth.

sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातमन्नदानफलं महत्। मूलमेतत् तु धर्माणां प्रदानानां च भारता॥
en: I have thus told you all about the great merit of gifts of food. This is the root of all virtue and merit, as also of all gifts, O Bharata.

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अहिंसा वैदिकं कर्म ध्यानमिन्द्रियसंयमः। तपोऽथ गुरुशुश्रूषा किं श्रेयः पुरुषं प्रति॥
en: Yudhishthira said Which amongst these is more efficacious to a person, namely abstention from injury, the observance of the Vedic, ritual, meditation, control over the senses, penances and obedient services rendered to the preceptors.

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: बृहस्पति रुवाच सर्वाण्येतानि धाणि पृथग्द्वाराणि सर्वशः। शृणु संकीर्त्यमानानि षडेव भरतर्षभ॥
en: Brihaspati said All these six are meritorious. They are different doors of virtue. I shall discourse upon them now. Do you listen to them O chief of the Bharatas!

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: हन्त निःश्रेयसं जन्तोरहं वक्ष्याम्यनुत्तमम्। अहिंसापाश्रयं धर्मं यः साधयति वै नरः॥
en: I shall tell you what forms the highest good of a human being. That man who practises the religion of universal mercy, acquires his highest good.

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: त्रीन् दोषान् सर्वभूतेषु निधाय पुरुषः सदा। कामक्रोधौ च संयम्य ततः सिद्धिमवाप्नुते॥
en: That man who keeps under restraint the three passions, viz., lust, anger and avarice by throwing them upon all creatures, acquires success.

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: अहिंसकानि भूतानि दण्डेन विनिहन्ति यः। आत्मनः सुखमन्विच्छन् स प्रेत्य न सुखी भवेत्॥
en: He who, for his own happiness, kills other innocent creatures with the rod of punishment never acquires happiness in the next world.

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: आत्मोपमस्तु भूतेषु यो वै भवति पुरुषः। न्यस्तदण्डो जितक्रोधः स प्रेत्य सुखमेधते॥
en: That man who considers all creatures as his own self, and treats them as his own self, laying aside the rod of punishment and completely controlling his anger, succeeds in acquiring happiness.

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्य सर्वभूतानि पश्यतः। देवाऽपि मार्गे मुह्यन्ति अपदस्य पदैषिणः॥
