en: in The very celestials who are desirous of a fixed habitation, become stupefied ascertaining the road of that person who forms himself the soul of all creatures and considers them all as his own self, for such a person leaves no track behind.

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: न तत् परस्य संदध्यात् प्रतिकूलं यदात्मनः। एष संक्षेपतो धर्मः कामादन्यः प्रवर्तते॥
en: One should never do that to another which he considers as injurious to his own self. This in brief, is the rule of virtue. One by acting in a different way by giving way to desire, becomes guilty of sin.

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: प्रत्याख्याने च दाने च सुखदुःखे प्रियाप्रिये। आत्मौपम्येन पुरुषः प्रमाणमधिगच्छति॥
en: In refusing and giving, in weal and woe, in the agrecable and the disagreeable, one should judge of their effects by considering his own self.

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: यथाऽपरः प्रक्रमते परेषु तथापरे प्रक्रमन्ते परस्मिन्। तथैव तेऽस्तूपमा जीवलोके यथा धर्मो नैपुणेनोपदिष्ट॥१०
en: When one injures another, the injured in return injures the injurer. Likewise, when one cherishes another, that other cherishes the cherisher. One should forin his own rule of conduct according to this, I have told you what virtue is even by this subtile way.

description: Noninjury, observance of Vedic rituals, meditation, controlling senses, penances, and obedience to the preceptors, — which of them is preferable
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा तं सुरगुरुर्धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। दिवमाचक्रमे धीमान् पश्यतामेव नस्तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana continued: The preceptor of the celestials endued with great intelligence, having said this to king, Yudhishthira the just, ascended upwards for proceeding to the celestial region before our eyes.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा शरतल्पे पितामहम्। पुनरेव महातेजाः पप्रच्छ वदतां वरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said After this, king, Yudhishthira gifted with great energy, and the foremost of eloquent men, addressed his grandfather lying on his bed of arrows, in the following words.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ऋषयो ब्राह्मणा देवाः प्रशंसन्ति महामते। अहिंसालक्षणं धर्म वेदप्रामाण्यदर्शनात्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O You of great intelligence, the Rishi and Brahmanas and the celestials led by the authority of the Vedas, all speak highly of the religion of mercy.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: कर्मणा मनुजः कुर्वन् हिंसा पार्थिवसत्तम। वाचा च मनसा चैव कथं दुःखात् प्रमुच्यते॥
en: But, o king, what I ask you is this how does a man who has perpetrated acts of injury to others in word, thought and deed, succeed in purifying himself from misery.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: भीष्म उवाच चतुर्विधेयं निर्दिष्टा ह्यहिंसा ब्रह्मवादिभिः। एकैकतोऽपि विभ्रष्टा न भवत्यरिसूदन॥
en: Bhishma said Brahmavadins have said that there are four kinds of mercy or abstention from injury. If even one of those four kinds be not observed. The religion of mercy, it is said, is not observed.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: यथा सर्वश्चतुष्याद् वै त्रिभिः पादै तिष्ठति। तथैवेयं महीपाल कारणैः प्रोच्यते त्रिभिः॥
en: As all quadruped animals are incapable of standing on three legs so the religion of mercy cannot stand if any of those four divisions or parts be wanting.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: यथा नागपदेऽन्यानि पदानि पदगामिनाम्। सर्वाण्येवापिधीयन्ते पदजातानि कौञ्जरे॥ एवं लोकेष्वहिंसा तु निर्दिष्टा धर्मतः पुरा। कर्मणा लिप्यते जन्तुर्वाचा च मनसापि च॥
en: As the footprints of all other animals are sunk in those of the elephant, so all other religions are said to be contained in that of mercy. A person becomes guilty of injury through acts, words, and thoughts.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: पूर्वं तु मनसा त्यक्त्वा तथा वाचाऽथ कर्मणा। न भक्षयति सो मांसं त्रिविधं स विमुच्यते॥
en: Discarding it mentally in the beginning, one should next discard it in word and thought. He who according to this rule, abstains from eating meat is said to be purified in a three fold way.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: विकारणं तु निर्दिष्टं श्रूयते ब्रह्मवादिभिः। मनो वाचि तथाऽऽस्वादे दोषा ह्येषु प्रतिष्ठिताः॥
en: It is heard that Brahmavadins point out three causes (for the sin of eating meat). That sin may attach to the mind, to words, and to deeds.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: न भक्षयन्त्यतो मांसं तपोयुक्ता मनीषिणः। दोषांस्तु भक्षणे राजन् मांसस्येह निबोध मे॥
en: It is therefore, that wise men who are gifted with penances refrain from eating meat. Listen to me, O king, as tell you what the faults are which attach to the eating of meat.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: पुत्रमांसोपमं जानन् खादते योऽविचक्षणः। मांसं मोहसमायुक्तः पुरुषः सोऽधमः स्मृतः॥
en: The meat of other animals is like the flesh of one's son. That foolish person, stupefied by folly, who eats meat is considered as the vilest of human beings.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: पितृमातृसमायोगे पुत्रत्वं जायते यथा। हिंसां कृत्वावशः पापो भूयिष्ठं जायते तथा॥
en: The union of father and mother produces children, Similarly the cruelty that a helpless and sinful wretch commits, produces its progeny of repeated rebirths fraught with great misery.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: रसं च प्रतिजिह्वाया ज्ञानं प्रज्ञायते यथा। तथा शास्त्रत्रेषु नियतं रागो ह्यास्वादिताद् भवेत्॥
en: As the tongue is the cause of sensation of taste, so, the scriptures declare, attachment proceeds from taste.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: संस्कृतासंस्कृताः पक्वा लवणालवणास्तथा। प्रजायन्ते यथा भावास्तथा चित्तं निरुध्यते॥
en: Well-dressed, cooked with salt or without salt, meat, in whatever form one may take it, by and by attracts the mind and enslaves it.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: भेरीमृदङ्गशब्दांश्च तन्त्रीशब्दांश्च पुष्कलान्। निषेविष्यन्ति वै मन्दा मांसभक्षाः कथं नराः॥
en: How will those foolish men who live upon meat succeed in listening to the sweet music of celestial drums and cymbals and lyres and harps?

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: अचिन्तितमनिर्दिष्टमसंकल्पितमेव च। रसवृद्ध्याभिभूता ये प्रशंसन्ति फलार्थिनः॥
en: They who eat meat highly speak of it, allowing themselves to be stupefied by its taste which they declare be something inconceivable, undesirable, and unimaginable.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: प्रशंसा ह्येव मांसस्य दोषकर्मफलान्विता॥ जीवितं हि परित्यज्य बहवः साधवो जनाः। स्वमासैः परमांसानि परिपाल्य दिवं गताः॥
en: Such pradise even of meat is sinful. Formerly, many pious men, by giving the flesh of their own bodies, protected the flesh of other creatures and as a result of such deeds of merit, have proceeded to the celestial region.

description: The purification of one who has injured others
sn: एवमेषा महाराज चतुर्भिः कारणैर्वृता। अहिंसा तव निर्दिष्टा सर्वधर्मानुसंहिता॥
en: In this way, O king, the religion of mercy is surrounded by four considerations. I have thus declared to you that religion which contains all other religions within it. to

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अहिंसा परमो धर्म इत्युक्तं बहुशस्त्वया। जातो नः संशयो धर्मे मांसस्य परिवर्जने। दोषो भक्षयतः कः स्यात् कश्चाभक्षयतो गुणः॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have told it many times that abstention from injury is the highest Religion. In Shraddhas, however, that are performed in honour of the departed Manes, persons for their own behoof, should make offerings of various kinds of meat. A doubt has, therefore, sprung in our mind about the duty of abstaining from meat. What are the sins that one commits by eating meat, and what are the merits that one acquires?

sn: हत्वा भक्षयतो वापि परेणोपहतस्य वा। हन्याद् वा यः परस्यार्थं क्रीत्वा वा भक्षयेन्नरः॥
en: You have said SO So while discoursing formerly upon the ordinances about Shraddhas. How can meat, however, be procured without killing a living creature? Your declarations, therefore, appear to me to be contradictory.

sn: एतदिच्छामि तत्त्वेन कथ्यमानं त्वयानघ। निश्चयेन चिकीर्षामि धर्ममेतं सनातनम्॥
en: What are the demerits of him who eats meat by himself slaying a living creature? What are the merits of him who eats the meat of animals, slain by others? What the merits or demerits of hini who kills a living creature for another? Or of him who eats meat buying it of others? I wish, O sinless one, that you should describe to me this subject in full. I wish to ascertain this eternal Religion with certainty.

sn: कथमायुरवाप्नोति कथं भवति सत्त्ववान्। कथमव्यङ्गतामेति लक्षण्यो जायते कथम्॥
en: How does one acquire longevity? How does onc acquire strength? How does one acquire faultlessness of limbs? Indeed, how does one become gifted with excellent marks?

sn: भीष्म उवाच मांसस्याभक्षणाद् राजन् यो धर्मः कुरुनन्दन। तन्मे शृणु यथातत्त्वं यथास्य विधिरुत्तमः॥
en: Bhishma said Listen to me, O scion of Kuru's race, what the merit is of abstention from meat. Listen to me as I declare to you what the excellent ordinances, in sooth, are on this subject.

sn: रूपमव्यङ्गतामायुर्बुद्धिं सत्त्वं बलं स्मृतिम्। प्राप्तुकामैनरैहिंसा वर्जिता वै महात्मभिः॥
en: Those great inen who desire beauty, faultessness of limbs, long life, understanding mental and physical strength, and memory should abstain from acts of injury.

sn: ऋषीणामत्र संवादो बहुशः कुरुनन्दन। बभूव तेषां तु मतं यत् तच्छृणु युधिष्ठिर।॥
en: Numberless discourses took place. between the Rishis on this subject, O scion of Kuru's race. Listen, O Yudhishthira, what their opinion was.

sn: यो यजेताश्वमेधेन मासि मासि यतव्रतः। वर्जयेन्मधु मांसं च सममेतद् युधिष्ठिर॥
en: The merit acquired by that person, O Yudhishthira, who, with the steadiness of a vow, worship the celestials every month in Horse sacrifices, is equal to him who discards honey and meat.

sn: सप्तर्षयो वालखिल्यास्तथैव च मरीचिपाः। अमांसभक्षणं राजन् प्रशंसन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: The highly wise seven celestial Rishis, the Valakhillyas, and those Rishi, who drink the rays of the sun, all speak highly of abstention from ineat.

sn: न भक्षयति यो मांसं न च हन्यान्न घातयेत्। तन्मित्रं सर्वभूतानां मनुः स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: The self-create Manu has said that man who does not eat meat, or who does not kill living creatures, or who does not cause them to be killed, is a friend of all creatures.

sn: अधृष्यः सर्वभूतानां विश्वास्यः सर्वजन्तुषु। साधूनां सम्मतो नित्यं भवेन्मांसं विवर्जयन्॥
en: Such a man is incapable of being oppressed by any creature. He enjoys the confidence of all living beings. He always enjoys, besides, the praise of the pious.

sn: स्वमांसं परमांसेन यो वर्धयितुमिच्छति। नारदः प्राह धर्मात्मा नियतं सोऽवसीदति॥
en: The virtuous Narada has said that that man who wishes to multiply his own flesh by eating the flesh of other creatures, meet with disaster.

sn: ददाति यजते चापि तपस्वी च भवत्यपि। मधुमांसनिवृत्त्येति प्राहु चैवं बृहस्पतिः॥
en: Brihaspati has said that that man who abstains from honey and meat, gains the merit of gifts and sacrifices and penances.

sn: मासि मास्यश्वमेधेन यो यजेत शतं समाः। न खादति च यो मांसं सममेतन्मतं मम॥
en: In my view, these two persons are equal viz.hc who worships the celestials every month in a Horse-sacrifice for a century and he who abstains from honey and meat.

sn: सदा यजति सत्रेण सदा दानं प्रयच्छति। सदा तपस्वी भवति मधुमांसविवर्जनात्॥
en: On account of abstention from meat, one is considered as one who always worships the celestials in sacrifices, or as one who always makes gifts to others, or as one who always practises the severest austerities.

sn: सर्वे वेदा न तत् कुर्युः सर्वे यज्ञाश्च भारत। यो भक्षयित्वा मांसानि पश्चादपि निवर्तते॥
en: That inan who having eaten meal, gives it up afterwards, wins merit by such a deed that is so great that a study of all the Vedas or a performance, O Bharata, of all the sacrifices, cannot give its like.

sn: दुष्करं च रसज्ञाने मांसस्य परिवर्जनम्। चर्तुं व्रतमिदं श्रेष्ठं सर्वप्राण्यभयप्रदम्॥
en: It is very difficult to abstain from meat after one has known itstaste. Indeed, it is extremely difficult for such a person to observe the great vow abstention from meat, a vow that assures every creature by removing all fear.

sn: सर्वभूतेषु यो विद्वान् ददात्यभयदक्षिणाम्। दाता भवति लोके स प्राणानां नात्र संशयः॥
en: That learned person who gives to all living creatures the gift of complete assurance, is forsooth, regarded as the giver of lifc-breaths in this world.

sn: एवं वै परमं धर्मे प्रशंसन्ति मनीषिणः। प्राणा यथाऽऽत्मनोऽभीष्टा भूतानामपि वै तथा॥
en: This is the high Religion which wise men esteem very highly. The vital airs of other creatures are as dear to them as those of his own self.

sn: आत्मौपम्येन मन्तव्यं बुद्धिमद्भिः कृतात्मभिः। मृत्युतो भयमस्तीति विदुषां भूतिमिच्छताम्॥
en: Men gifted with intelligence and purified souls should always treat others as they theinselves wish to be treated. It is seen that even those men who are endued with learning and who seek to acquire the greatest good in the shape of Liberation, are not free from of the fear of death.

sn: किं पुनर्हन्यमानानां तरसा जीवितार्थिनाम्। अरोगाणामपापानां पापैराँसोपजीविभिः॥
en: What necessity there be said those innocent and healthy creatures gifted with love of life, when they are sought to be killed by sinful wretches living by slaughter?

sn: तस्माद् विद्धि महाराज मांसस्य परिवर्जनम्। धर्मस्यायतनं श्रेष्ठं स्वर्गस्य च सुखस्य च॥
en: Therefore, O king, know that the discarding of meat is the highest refuge of Religion, of the celestial region, and of happiness.

sn: अहिंसा परमो धर्मस्तथाहिंसा परं तपः। अहिंसा परमं सत्यं यतो धर्मः प्रवर्तते।॥
en: Abstention from injury is the highest Religion. It is, again, the highest penance. It is also the highest truth from which all duty emanates.

sn: न हि मांसं तृणात् काष्ठादुपलाद् वापि जायते। हत्वा जन्तुं ततो मांसं तस्माद् दोषस्तु भक्षणे॥
en: Flesh cannot be had from grass or wood or stone. Unless a living creature is killed it cannot be procured. Hence is the fault in eating flesh.

sn: स्वाहास्वधामृतभुजो देवाः सत्यार्जवप्रियाः। क्रव्यादान् राक्षसान् विद्धि जिह्मानृत परायणान्।।२५।
en: The celestials, who live upon Svaha, Svadha, and nectar, are given to truth and sincerity. Those persons, however, who are for satisfying the sensation of taste, should be known as Rakshasas pervaded by the quality of Darkness.

sn: कान्तारेप्वथ घोरेषु दुर्गेषु गहनेषु च। रात्रावहनि संध्यासु चत्वरेषु सभासु च॥ उद्यतेषु च शस्त्रेषु मृगव्यालभयेषु च। अमांसभक्षणे राजन् भयमन्यैर्न गच्छति॥
en: That man who abstains from meat, is never put in fear, O king, by any creature, wherever hic may be, viz., in terrible forest or inaccessible fastnesses, by day or by night, or at the two twilight's, in the open squares of towns or in conclaves of men, from upraised weapons or in places where there is great fright from wild animals or snakes.

sn: शरण्यः सर्वभूतानां विश्वास्यः सर्वजन्तुषु। अनुद्वेगकरो लोके च चाप्युद्विजते सदा॥
en: All creatures seek his protection. He is trusted by all. He never causes any anxiety in others, and himself has never to become anxious,

sn: यदि चेत् खादको न स्यान्न तदा घातको भवेत्। घातकः खादकार्थाय तद् घातयति वै नरः॥
en: If there were nobody who ate flesh there would then be nobody to slay living creatures. The man who slays living creatures kills them for the sake of the person who eats flesh.

sn: अभक्ष्यमेतदिति वै इति हिंसा निवर्तते। खादकार्थमतो हिंसा मृगादीनां प्रवर्तते॥
en: If flesh were not considered as food, there would then be no destruction of living creatures. It is for the sake of the eater that the destruction of living creatures is carried on in the world.

sn: यस्माद् प्रसति चैवायुर्हिसकानां महाद्युते। तस्माद् विवजयेन्मांसं य इच्छेद् भूतिमात्मनः॥
en: Since, O you of great splendour, the period of life is shortened of persons who kills living creatures or cause them to be killed, it is clear that the person who seeks his own, behoof, I should give up meat altogether.

sn: त्रातारं नाधिगच्छन्ति रौद्राः प्राणिविहिंसकाः। उद्वेजनीया भूतानां यथा व्यालमृगास्तथा॥
en: Those dreadful persons who are engaged in the destruction of living creatures never find protectors when they are in need. Such persons should always be molested and punished even as beasts of prey.

sn: लोभाद् वा बुद्धिमोहाद् वा बलवीर्यार्थमेव च। संसर्गादथ पापानामधर्मरुचिता नृणाम्॥
en: Through cupidity or stupefaction of sense, for the sake of strength and energy, or through association with the sinful, men show tendency for committing sin.

sn: स्वमांसं परमांसेन यो वर्धयितुमिच्छति। उद्विग्नवासो वसति यत्र यत्राभिजायते॥
en: That man who seeks to multiply his own flesh by (eating) the flesh of others has to live in this world in great anxiety and after death has to take birth in indifferent races and families.

sn: धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं स्वर्ये स्वस्त्ययनं महत्। मांसस्याभक्षणं प्राहुर्नियताः परमर्षयः॥
en: High Rishis given to the observance of vows and self control have said that abstention from meat is worthy of praise, productive of fame and Heaven and a great satisfaction itself.

sn: इदं तु खलु कौन्तेय श्रुतमासीत् पुरा मया। मार्कण्डेयस्य वदतो ये दोषा मांसभक्षणे॥
en: This I heard forinerly, O son of Kunti, from Markandeya when that Rishi discoursed on the sins of eating flesh.

sn: यो हि खादति मांसानि प्राणिनां जीवितैषिणाम्। हतानां वा मृतानां वा यथा हन्ता तथैव सः॥
en: He who eats the flesh of animals are who desirous of living but who have been slain by either himself or others, commits the sin of slaughter for his this act of cruelty.

sn: धनेन क्रयिको हन्ति खादचोपभोगतः। घातको वधबन्धाभ्यामित्येष त्रिविधो वधः॥
en: He who purchases flesh, kills living crcatures through his money. He who eats flesh, kills living creatures through such act of caling. He who binds or seizes and actually kilis living creatures, is the slaughterer. These are the three sorts of slaughter, each of these three acts being so.

sn: अखादन्ननुमोदंश्च भावदोषेण मानवः। योऽनुमोदति हन्यन्तं सोऽपि दोषेण लिप्यते॥
en: He who does not himself eat flesh but approves of an act of slaughter, becomes stained with the sin of slaughter.

sn: अधृष्यः सर्वभूतानामायुष्मान् निरुजः सदा। भवत्यभक्षयन् मांसं दयावान् प्राणिनामिह॥
en: By abstaining from meat and showing mercy to all creatures one becomes incapable of being molested by any creature, and acquires longevity perfect health and happiness.

sn: हिरण्यदानैर्गोदानैर्भूमिदानैश्च सर्वशः। मांसस्याभक्षणे धर्मो विशिष्ट इति नः श्रुतिः॥
en: The merit won by abstaining from meat, we have heard is superior to that of one who makes presents of gold, of kine, and of land.

sn: खादकस्य कृते जन्तून् यो हन्यात् पुरुषाधमः। महादोषतरस्तत्र घातको न तु खादकः॥
en: If ong cats the meat that has been sanctified on account of its having been procured from animals dedicated in sacrifices and that have been killed for the purpose of feeding Brahmanas, one incurs a little fault. By behaving otherwise, one becomes stained with sin. That wretched man who kills living creatures for the sake of those who would eat them commits great sin. The eater's sin is not so great.

sn: इज्यायज्ञश्रुतिकृतैर्यो मागैरबुधोऽधमः। हन्याज्जन्तून् मांसगृध्नुः स वै नरकभाड्नरः॥
en: That wretched man who following the path of religious rites and sacrifices laid down in the Vedas, would kill a living creature from desire of eating its flesh, would certainly go to Hell. One should never eat meat of animals not dedicated in sacrifices and that are, therefore, killed uselessly, and that has not been offered to the gods and departed Manes with the help of the ordinances. There is not the least doubt that a person by eating such meat goes to Hell.

sn: भक्षयित्वापि यो मांसं पश्चादपि निवर्तते। तस्यापि सुमहान् धर्मो यः पापाद् विनिवर्तते॥
en: That man who having eaten flesh abstains from it afterwards acquires great merit on account of such abstention from sin.

sn: आहर्ता चानुमन्ता च विशस्ता क्रयविक्रयी। संस्कर्ता चापभोक्ता च खादकाः सर्व एव ते॥
en: He who arranges for obtaining flesh, he who approves of those arrangements, he who kills, he who, buys or sells, he who cooks, and he who eats, are all considered as caters of flesh.

sn: इदमन्यत्तु वक्ष्यामि प्रमाणं विधिनिर्मितम्। पुराणमृषिभिर्जुष्टं वेदेषु परिनिष्ठितम्॥
en: I shall now cite another authority, depending upon the saying of the ordainer himself, that is ancient, worshipped by the Rishis, and established in the Vedas.

sn: प्रवृत्तिलक्षणो धर्मः प्रजार्थिभिरुदाहृतः। यथोक्तं राजशार्दूल न तु तन्मोक्षकाक्षिणाम्॥
en: It has been said that religion which has acts for its marks, has been ordained for householders O chief of kings, and not for those men who are desirous of Liberation.

sn: य इच्छेत् पुरुषोऽत्यन्तमात्मानं निरुपद्रवम्। स वर्जयेत मांसानि प्राणिनामिह सर्वशः॥
en: That man who wishes to avoid disaster should abstain from the meat of every living creature.

sn: श्रूयते हि पुरा कल्पे नृणां व्रीहिपयः पशुः। येनायजन्त यज्वानः पुण्यलोकपरायणाः॥
en: It is heard that in the former Aeon persons, desirous of acquiring regions of merit hereafter, celebrated sacrifices with seeds, regarding such animals as dedicated by them.

sn: ऋषिभिः संशयं पृष्टो वसुश्चेदिपतिः पुरा। अभक्ष्यमपि मांसं यः प्राह भक्ष्यमिति प्रभा॥
en: Doubtful about the propriety of eating flesh, the Rishis asked Vasu the king of the Chedis, for removing their doubt. King Vasu, knowing that flesh should not be taken, answered that it was edible, O king.

sn: आकाशादवनि प्राप्तस्ततः स पृथिवीपतिः। एतदेव पुनश्चोक्त्वा विवेश धरणीतलम्॥
en: From that moment Vasu dropped down from the sky on the Earth. After this he once more repeated his opinion, with the result that he had to go down below the earth for it.

sn: इदं तु शृणु राजेन्द्र कीर्त्यमानं मयानध। अभक्षणे सर्वसुखं मांसस्य मनुजाधिप॥
en: Listen to me, O king of kings, as I tell you this, O sinless one, There is absolute happiness ! in abstaining from meat, O king.

sn: यस्तु वर्षशतं पूर्णे तपस्तप्येत सुदारुणम्। यश्चैव वर्जयेन्मांसं सममेतन्मतं मम॥
en: He who practises severe austerities for a century, and he who abstains from ineat, are both equally meritorious. This is my opinion.

sn: कौमुदे तु विशेषेण शुक्लपक्षे नराधिप। वर्जयेन्मधुमांसानि धर्मो ह्यत्र विधीयते॥
en: In the light half of the month of Kartika in especial, one should abstain from honey and mcat. It has been ordained, that there is great merit in it.

sn: चतुरो वार्षिकान् मासान् यो मांसं परिवर्जयेत्। चत्वारि भद्राण्यवाप्नोति कीर्तिमायुर्यशोबलम्॥
en: He who abstains from meat for the four months of the rainy season, acquires the blessed achievements, viz., longevity, fame and power.

sn: अथवा मासमेकं वै सर्व मांसान्यभक्षयन्। अतीत्य सर्वदुःखानि सुखं जीवेन्निरामयः॥
en: He who abstains for the whole month of Kartika from meat of every kind, gets over all sorts of woe and lives in complete happiness.

sn: वर्जयन्ति हि मांसानि मासश: पक्षशोऽपि वा। तेषां हिंसानिवृत्तानां ब्रह्मलोको विधीयते॥
en: They who abstain from flesh by either months or fortnights, have the region of Brahma ordained for them on account of their abstention from cruelty.

sn: मांसं तु कौमुदं पक्षं वर्जितं पार्थ राजभिः। सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्थैर्विदितार्थपरावरैः॥
en: Formerly many kings, O son of Pritha who had forined themselves the souls of all creatures and who has known the truths of all things viz., Soul and Not Soul, had abstained from flesh either for the whole of the month of Kartika or for the whole of the light fortnight in that month.

sn: नाभागेनाम्बरीषेण गयेन च महात्मना। आयुनाथानरण्येन दिलीपरघुपूरुभिः॥ कीर्तवीर्यानिरुद्धाभ्यां नहुषेण ययातिना। नृगेण विष्वगश्वेन तथैव शशबिन्दुना॥ युवनाश्वेन च तथा शिबिनौशीनरेण च। मुचुकुन्देन मान्धात्रा हरिश्चन्द्रेण वा विभो॥
en: They were Nabhaga, Ambarisha, the great Gaya, Ayu Anaranya, and Dilipa, Raghu, Pura, Kartavirya, Aniruddha, Nahusha, Yayati, Nriga, Vishvaksena, Shasabindu, Yunanashva, Shibi the son of Ushinara, Muchukunda, Mandhatri, and Harishchandra.

sn: सत्यं वदत मासत्यं सत्यं धर्म: सनातनः। हरिश्चन्द्रश्चरति वै दिवि सत्येन चन्द्रवत्॥
en: Do you always speak the truth. Never speak an untruth. Truth is an cternal duty. It is by truth that Harishchandra roves through the sky like a second Moon.

sn: श्येनचित्रेण राजेन्द्र सोमकेन वृकेण च। रैवते रन्तिदेवेन बसुना सृञ्जयेन च॥ एतैश्चान्यैश्च राजेन्द्र कृपेण भरतेन च। दुष्यन्तेन करूषेण रामालर्कनरैस्तथा॥ विरूपाश्वेन निमिना जनकेन च धीमता। ऐलेन पृथुना चैव वीरसेनेन चैव ह॥ इक्ष्वाकुणा शम्भुना च श्वेतेन सगरेण च। अजेन धुन्धुना चैव तथैव च सुबाहुना॥ हर्यश्वेन च राजेन्द्र क्षुपेण भरतेन च। एतैश्चान्यैश्च राजेन्द्र पुरा मांसं न भक्षितम्॥ ब्रह्मलोके च तिष्ठन्ति ज्वलमानाः श्रियान्विताः। उपास्यमाना गन्धर्वैः स्त्रीसहस्रसमन्विताः॥
en: These other kings also viz.,. Shyenchitra, O monarch, and Somaka, Vrika Raivata, Rantideva, Vasu, Srinjaya, Dushmanta, Karushma, Rama, Alarka, Nala, Virupashva, Nimi, intelligent Janaka, Aila, Prithu, Virasena, Ikshvaku, Shambhu, Shveta, Sagara Aja, Dhundhu, Subahu, Haryashva, Kashypa and Bharata, O monarch, did not eat flesh for the month of Kartika and therefore attained to the celestial region and gifted with prosperity, blaze forth with effulgence in the region of Brahmana, worshipped by Gandharvas and surrounded by a thousand beautiful ladies.

sn: तदेतदुत्तमं धर्ममहिंसाधर्मलक्षणम्। ये चरन्ति महात्मानो नाकपृष्ठे वसन्ति ते॥
en: Those great men who practise this excellent Religion which is marked out by abstention from injury, succeed in living in the celestial region.

sn: मधु मांसं च ये नित्यं वर्जयन्तीह धार्मिकाः। जन्मप्रभृति मद्यं च सर्वे ते मुनयः स्मृताः॥
en: Those pious inen who from the time of birth abstain from honey and meat and wine are considered as ascetics.

sn: इमं धर्मममांसादं यश्चरेच्छावयीत वा। अपि चेत् सुदुराचारो न जातु निरयं व्रजेत्॥
en: That man who practises this religion consisting of abstention from meat or who recites it for making others hear it, will never have to go to Hell even if he be a great wicked man.

sn: पठेद् वा य इदं राजञ्छृणुयाद् वाप्यभीक्ष्णशः। अमांसभक्षणविधि पवित्रमृषिपूजितम्॥ विमुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यः सर्वकामैर्महीयते। विशिष्टतां ज्ञातिषु च लभते नात्र संशयः॥
en: He, O king, who always reads these ordinances about abstention from meat, that are sacred and worshipped by the Rishis or hears it read becomes purged off of every sin and acquire a great happiness on account of the fruition of every desire. Forsooth, he acquires an eminent position among kinsmen.

sn: आपनश्चापदो मुच्येद् बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात्। मुच्येत्तथाऽऽतुरो रोगाद् दुःखान्मुच्येत दुःखितः।।७४
en: When afflicted with calanity, he immediately gets over it. When obstructed with obstacles, he succeeds in freeing himself from them with the utmost case. When suffering from a disease, he becomes quickly cured, and afflicted with sorrow he becomes liberated from it with greatest ease.

sn: तिर्यग्योनि न गच्छेत रूपवांश्च भवेन्नरः। ऋद्धिमान् वै कुरुश्रेष्ठ प्राप्नुयाच्च महद् यशः॥
en: Such a man has never to take birth in the intermediate order of animals or birds. Born in the order of men, he attains to great personal beauty. Gifted with great prosperity, O chief of Kuru's race, he acquires great fame as well.

sn: एतत्ते कथितं राजन् मांसस्य परिवर्जने। प्रवृत्तौ च निवृत्तौ च विधानमृषिनिर्मितम्॥
en: I have thus told you, O king, all that should be said about the subject of abstention from meat, together with the ordinances about both the religion of action and inaction as framed by the Rishis.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच इमे वै मानवा लोके नृशंसा मांसगृद्धिनः। विसृज्य विविधान् भक्ष्यान् महारक्षोगणा इव॥
en: Yudhishthira said Alas, those cruel men, who not caring for various other sorts of food, want only flesh, are really like great Rakshasa.

sn: अपूपान् विविधाकाराशाकानि विविधानि च। खाण्डवान् रसयोगान्न तथेच्छन्ति यथाऽऽमिषम्॥
en: Alas, they do not relish various kinds of cakes and diverse sorts of potherbs and various species of Khanda with juicy flavour so much as they do flesh.

sn: तत्र मे बुद्धिरत्रैव विषये परिमुह्यते। न मन्ये रसतः किञ्चिन्मांसतोऽस्तीति मे किञ्चन॥
en: I cannot understand this at all I think they feel that there is nothing so tasteful as mcat.

sn: तदिच्छामि गुणाश्रोतुं मांसस्याभक्षणे प्रभो। भक्षणे चैव ये दोषास्तांश्चैव पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: I wish therefore, O powerful one, to hear what the merits are of abstention from flesh and the sin about the eating of flesh, O chief of Bharata's race.

sn: सर्वं तत्त्वेन धर्मज्ञ यथावदिह धर्मतः। किं च भक्ष्यमभक्ष्यं वा सर्वमेतद् वदस्व मे॥
en: You know every duty. Describe to me, in full according to the ordinances on duty, this subject. Do tell me what indeed is edible and what inedible ?

sn: यथैतद् यादृशं चैव गुणा ये चास्य वर्जने। दोषा भक्षयतो येऽपि तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Tell me, O grandfather, what is flesh, of what substances it is the merits of abstention from it, and the sins for eating meat.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि भारत। न मांसात्परमं किञ्चिद्रसतो विद्यते भुवि॥
en: Bhishma said O mighty armed one, O Bharata, It is the same as you submit. There is nothing on Earth that is superior to meat in taste.

sn: क्षतक्षीणाभितप्तानां ग्राम्यधर्मरतात्मनाम्। अध्वना कर्शितानां च न मांसाद्विद्यते परम्॥
en: There is nothing that is more beneficial than meat to persons who are lean or weak, or afflicted with disease or addicted to sexual union or exhausted with travel.

sn: सद्यो वर्धयति प्राणान् पुष्टिमय्यां दधाति च। न भक्ष्योऽभ्यधिकः कश्चिन्मांसादस्ति परंतप॥
en: Meat quickly increases strength. It ordains great development. There is no food. O scorcher of enemies, that is superior to meat.

sn: विवर्जिते तु बहवो गुणाः कौरवनन्दन। ये भवन्ति मनुष्याणां तान् ये निगदतः शृणु॥
en: But, O delighter of Kurus, those who abstain from it win great merits. Listen to me as I describe it to you.

sn: स्वमांसं परमांसेन यो वर्धयितुमिच्छति। नास्ति क्षुद्रतरस्तस्मात् स नृशंसतरो नरः॥
en: That man who wishes to increase his own flesh by the meat of another living creature is such that there is none meaner and more cruel than he.

sn: न हि प्राणात् प्रियतरं लोके किंचन विद्यते। तस्माद् दयां नरः कुर्याद् यथाऽऽत्मनि तथा परे॥
en: In this world there is nothing that is dearer to a creature than his life. Hence, one should show mercy to the lives of others as he does to his own life.

sn: शुक्राच्च तात सम्भूतिर्मासस्येह न संशयः। भक्षणे तु महान् दोषो निवृत्त्या पुण्यमुच्यते॥
en: Forsooth, O son, flesh has its origin in the vital seed. There is great sin attaching to its eating, as, indeed, there is merit in abstaining from it.

sn: विधिना वेददृष्टेन तद्भुक्त्वेह न दुष्यति। यत्रार्थ पशवः सृष्टा इत्यपि श्रूयते श्रुतिः॥ अतोऽन्यथा प्रवृत्तानां राक्षसो विधिरुच्यते।
en: One does not, however, commit any sin by eating flesh sanctified according to the ordinances to the Vedas. The Shruti says that animal were created for sacrifice. They wlio eat flesh in any other way are said to follow Rakshasa practice.

sn: क्षत्रियाणां तु यो दृष्टो विधिस्तमपि मे शृणु॥ वीर्येणोपार्जितं मांसं यथा भुञ्जन्न दुष्यति।
en: Listen to me as I tell you what the ordinances is for the Kshatriyas. They do not commit any sin by eating flesh that has been acquired power.

sn: आरण्याः सर्वदैवत्याः सर्वशः प्रोक्षिता मृगाः॥ अगस्त्येन पुरा राजन् मृगया येन पूज्यते।
en: All wild deer have been dedicated to the celestials and the departed Manes in days of old, O king, by Agastya. Hence the hunting of dcer is not censured.

sn: नात्मानमपरित्यज्य मृगया नाम विद्यते॥ समतामुपसङ्गम्य भूतं हन्यन्ति हन्ति वा।
en: There can be no hunting without risk of one's own life. There is equality of risk between the killer and the killed. Either the animal is killed or it kills the hunter.

sn: अतो राजर्षयः सर्वे मृगयां यान्ति भारत॥ न हि लिप्यन्ति पापेन न चैतत्पातकं विदुः।
en: Hence, O Bharata, even royal sages take to hunting. By such conduct they do not become stained with sin. Indeed the practice is not considered sinful.

sn: न ह्यतः सदृशं किंचिदिह लोके परत्र च।॥ यत् सर्वेष्विह भूतेषु दया कौरवनन्दन।
en: There is nothing O, delighter of the Kurus, that is equal in point of merit, either in this world or in the next to the practice of mercy to all living creatures.

sn: न भयं विद्यते जातु नरस्येह दयावत:॥ दयावतामिमे लोका: परे चापि तपस्विनाम्।
en: A kind-hearted man seldom has to suffer from any fright. A gracious and austerious person enjoys equal pleasure in this world and the next.

sn: अहिंसालक्षणो धर्म इति धर्मविदो विदुः॥ यदहिंसात्मकं कर्म तत् कुर्यादात्मवान् नरः।
en: Persons conversant with duty say that Religion is worthy of being called Religion which is characterised by abstention from cruelty. The man of purified soul should do only such acts as have mercy for their soul.

sn: पितृदैवतयज्ञेषु प्रोक्षितं हविरुच्यते॥ अभयं सर्वमेतेभ्यो यो ददाति दयापरः।
en: That flesh which is dedicated in sacrifices performed in honour of the deities and the departed Manes is called Havi. That man who is given to mercy and who behaves with mercy towards others, has no fear to entertain from any creature.

sn: अभयं तस्य भूतानि ददतीत्यनुशुश्रुम॥ क्षतं च स्खलितं चैव पतितं कृष्टमाहतम्। सर्वभूतानि रक्षन्ति समेषु विषमेषु च॥ नैनं व्यालमृगा नन्ति न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः।
en: It is heard that all creatures abstain from causing any fear to such a creature. All creatures protect him when he is wounded or fallen down or prostrated or weakened or bruised. Indeed they do under all circumstances, whether he is on even uneven ground. Neither snakes nor wild animals neither Pishachas nor Rakshasas, ever kill him.

sn: मुच्यते भयकालेषु मोक्षयेद् यो भये परान्॥ प्राणदानात् परं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति।
en: When circumstances of fear originate, he becomes freed from fear who fees others from situations of fear. There has never been nor will there ever be, a gift which is superior to the gift of life.

sn: न ह्यात्मनः प्रियतरं किंचिदस्तीह निश्चितम्॥ अनिष्टं सर्वभूतानां मरणं नाम भारत।
en: In the world, there is nothing else so dear as one's life. Hence, as man wants to be graced by others; he should himself be gracious on others. O Bharata, as the body of all creatures starts shivering at the time of death, nobody wants to die. SO or

sn: मृत्युकाले हि भूतानां सद्यो जायति वेपथुः॥ जातिजन्मजरादुःखैर्नित्यं संसारसागरे। जन्तवः परिवर्तन्ते मरणादुद्विजन्ति च॥ गर्भवासेषु पच्यन्ते क्षाराम्लकटुकै रसैः। मूत्रस्वेदपुरीषाणां परुषैर्भृशदारुणैः॥ जाताश्चाप्यवशास्तत्र च्छिद्यमानाः पुनः पुनः। पाच्यमानाश्च दृश्यन्ते विवशा मांसगृद्धिनः॥ कुम्भीयाके च पच्यन्ते तां तां योनिमुपागताः।
en: When the time comes for Death, a trembling of the entire body is seen in all creatures. Undergoing birth in the uterus, decrepitude, and sufferings of all sorts, in this ocean of the world, living creature may be seen to be continually going forward and coming back. Every creatures is afflicted by death. While living in the uterus all creatures are cooked in the fluid juices, that are alkaline and sour and bitter, of urine and phlegm and faeces, juices which produce painful sensations and are difficult to bear. There in the uterus they have to live in a state of helplessness and are even repeatedly torn and pierced. They who are covetous of meat are seen to be repeatedly cooked in the uterus in such a state of helplessness. Going through all sorts of birth, they cooked in the Hell called Kumbhipaka.

sn: आक्रम्य मार्यमाणाश्च भ्राम्यन्ते वै पुनः पुनः॥ नात्मनोऽस्ति प्रियतरः पृथिवीमनुसृत्य ह।
en: They are assailed and killed and in this way have to travel again and again. There is nothing so dear to one as his life when one comes to this world.

sn: तस्मात् प्राणिषु सर्वेषु दयावानात्मवान् भवेत्॥ सर्वमांसानि यो राजन् यावज्जीवं न भक्षयेत्। स्वर्गे स विपुलं स्थानं प्राप्नुयानात्र संशयः॥ ये भक्षयन्ति मांसानि भूतानां जीवितैषिणाम्। भक्ष्यन्ते तेऽपि भूतैस्तैरिति मे नास्ति संशयः॥ मांसं भक्षयते यस्माद् भक्षयिष्ये तमप्यहम्। एतन्मांसस्य मांसत्वमनुबुद्ध्यस्व भारत।॥ घातको वध्यते नित्यं तथा वध्यति भक्षिता।
en: are Hence, a person of purified soul should be merciful to all living creatures. That man, O king, who abstains from every kinds of meat from his birth, forsooth, acquires a large space in the celestial region. They who eat the flesh of animals who are desirous of life. are themselves eaten by the animals they eat. This is my opinion. Since he has eaten me, I shall eat him in return, this O Bharata, forms the character as Mansa of Mansa. The destroyer is always slain. After him the eater meets with the same fate.

sn: आक्रोष्टा क्रुध्यते राजंस्तथा द्वेष्यत्वमाप्नुते॥ येन येन शरीरेण यद्यत् कर्म करोति यः। तेन तेन शरीरेण तत्तत् फलमुपाश्नुते॥
en: He who acts with hostility towards another becomes the victim of similar deeds done by that other. Whatever acts one does in whatever bodies, he has to suffer the consequences thereof in those bodies.

sn: अहिंसा परमो धर्मस्तथाऽहिंसा परो दमः। अहिंसा परमं दानमहिंसा परमं तपः॥ अहिंसा परमो यज्ञस्तथाहिंसा परं फलम्। अहिंसा परमं मित्रमहिंसा परमं सुखम्॥
en: Abstention from cruelty is the highest Religion. Abstention from cruelty is the greatest self-restraint. Abstention from cruelty is the highest gift. Abstention from cruelty is the highest penance. Abstention from cruelty is the highest sacrifice. Abstention from cruelty is the highest power. Abstention from cruelty is the greatest friend. Abstention from cruelty is the greatest happiness. Abstention from cruelty is the highest truth. Abstention from cruelty is the highest Shruti.

sn: सर्वयज्ञेषु वा दानं सर्वतीर्थेपु वाऽऽप्लुतम्। सर्वदानफलं वापि नैतत्तुल्यमहिंसया॥
en: Gifts made in all sacrifices, ablutions performed in all sacred waters, and the merit which one acquires from making all kinds of gifts mentioned in the scriptures all these do not equal abstention from cruelty in merit.

sn: अहिंस्रस्य तपोऽक्षय्यमहिंस्रो यजते सदा। अहिंस्रः सर्वभूतानां यथा माता यथा पिता॥
en: The penances of a man who abstains from cruelty are endless. The man who abstains from cruelty is considered as always perforining sacrifices. The man who abstains from cruelty is the father and mother of all creatures.

sn: एतत् फलमहिंसाया भूयश्च कुरुपुङ्गव। न हि शक्या गुणा वक्तुमपि वर्षशतैरपि॥
en: Even these, chief of Kuru's race, are some of the merits of abstention from cruelty. Altogether, the merits of it are so many that they are incapable of being exhausted even if one were to speak for a century.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अकामाश्च सकामाश्च ये हताः स्म महामृधे। कां गतिं प्रतिपन्नास्ते तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Wishing to die and wishing to live many persons surrender their lives in the great sacrifice (of battle). Tell me O grandfather what is the end that these attain to.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: दुःखं प्राणपरित्यागः पुरुषाणां महामृधे। जानासि त्वं महाप्राज्ञ प्राणत्यागं सुदुष्करम्॥ समृद्धौ वासमृद्धौ वा शुभे वा यदि वाऽशुभे। कारणं तत्र में ब्रूहि सर्वज्ञो ह्यसि मे मतः॥
en: To give up life in battle is fraught with sorrow for men. O you of great wisdom you know that to give up life if difficult for men whether they are rich or poor or are in happiness or misery. In my opinion you are gifted with omniscience. Do you tell me the reason of this.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: भीष्म उवाच समृद्धौ वासमृद्धौ वा शुभे वा यदि वाऽशुभे। संसारेऽस्मिन् समायाताः प्राणिनः पृथिवीपते॥
en: Bhishma said In prosperity or adversity in weal or woe, living creatures, O king, coming into this world, live according to a particular method.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: निरता येन भावेन तत्र मे शृणु कारणम्। सम्यक् चायमनुप्रश्नस्त्वयोक्तस्तु युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Listen to me as I explain the reason to you. The question you have put to me is indeed, excellent, O Yudhishthira!

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि पुरावृत्तमिदं नृप। द्वैपायनस्य संवादं कीटस्य च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Regarding it, О king, I shall explain to you the old discourse that took place formerly between the Dvaipayana Rishi and a crawling worm.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: ब्रह्मभूतश्चरन् विप्रः कृष्णद्वैपायन: पुरा। ददर्श कीटं धावन्तं शीघ्रं शकटवर्त्मनि॥
en: Formerly when that learned Brahmana, viz., the Krishna Dvaipayana having identified himself with Brahma, roamed over the world, he saw on a road over which cars used to pass a worm moving quickly.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: गतिज्ञः सर्वभूतानां भाषाज्ञश्च शरीरिणाम्। सर्वज्ञः स तदा दृष्ट्वा कीटं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The Rishi knew the of every creature and the language of every animal, Gifted with omniscience, he addressed the worm he saw in these words. course

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: व्यास उवाच कीटसंत्रस्तरूपोऽसि त्वरितश्चैव लक्ष्यसे। क्व धावसि तदाचक्ष्व कुतस्ते भयमागतम्॥
en: Vyasa said O worm, you appear to be greatly alarmed and to be in great haste. Tell me, where do you run and whence have you been afraid?

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: कीट उवाच शकटस्यास्य महतो घोषं श्रुत्वा भयं मम। आगतं वै महाबुद्धे स्वन एष हि दारुणः॥
en: The worm said I am stricken with fear on hearing the rattle of that large car. O you of great intelligence, it makes a fearful roar. It is almost come.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: श्रूयते न च मां हन्यादिति ह्यस्मादपक्रमे। श्वसतां च शृणोम्येनं गोपुत्राणां प्रतोद्यताम्॥
en: The sound is heard. Will it not kill me? I am flying away for this, I hear the sound of the bulls.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: वहतां सुमहाभारं संनिकर्षे स्वनं प्रभो। नृणां च संवाहयतां श्रूयते विविधः स्वनः॥
en: They are breathing hard under the whip of the driver, as they are carrying the heavy load. I hear also the various sound made by the men who are driving the bulls.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: श्रोतुमस्मद्विधनैष न शक्यः कीटयोनिना। तस्मादतिक्रमाम्येष भयादस्मात् सुदारुणात्॥
en: Creatures which like us are born as worms, cannot bear such sounds. It is therefore that I am flying from this situation of great fright.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: दुःखं हि मृत्युर्भूतानां जीवितं च सुदुर्लभम्। अतो भीत: पलायामि गच्छेयं नासुख सुखात्॥
en: Death is considered by all creatures as painful. Life is an acquisition difficult to make. Hence, I fly away in fear, I do not wish to pass from a state of weal to one of woe.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: भीष्म उवाच इत्युक्तः स तु तं प्राह कुत: कीट सुखं तव। मरणं ते सुखं मन्ये तिर्यग्योनौ तु वर्तसे॥
en: Bhishma said O worm, whence can be your happiness? You belong to the intermediate order of being. I think death would be of happiness to you.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: शब्दं स्पर्श रस गन्धं भोगांश्चोच्चवचान् बहून्। नाभिजानासि कीट त्वं श्रेयो मरणमेव ते॥
en: Sound touch, taste, scent, and various kinds of excellent enjoyments are unknown to you, O worm! I think death will prove a benefit to you.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: कीट उवाच सर्वत्र निरतो जीव इतश्चापि सुखं मम। चिन्तयामि महाप्राज्ञ तस्मादिच्छामि जीवितुम्॥
en: The Worm said A living creature however circumstanced he may be becomes attached to it. In even this order of being I am happy, I think, O you of great wisdom! It is for this that I wish to live.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: इहापि विषयः सर्वो यथादेहं प्रवर्तितः। मानुषाः स्थैर्यजाश्चैव पृथग्भोगा विशेषतः॥
en: In this condition every object of enjoyment exists for me according to the necessity of my body. Human beings and those creatures which originate from immobile objects have different enjoyments.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: अहमासं मनुष्यो वै शूद्रो बहुधनः प्रभो। अब्रह्मण्यो नृशसंश्च कदर्यो वृद्धिजीवनः॥
en: In my former life I was a human being. O powerful one, I was a wealthy Shudra. I was not devoted to the Brahmanas. I was cruel, vile in conduct, and a usurer.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: वाक्तीक्ष्णो निकृतिप्रज्ञो द्वेष्टा विश्वस्य सर्वशः। मिथ्याकृतोऽपि विधिना परस्वहरणे रतः॥
en: I was harsh in speech. I considered cunning as wisdom. I hated all creatures. Taking advantage of pretexts in agreements made between myself and others I used always to take away what belonged to others.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: भृत्यातिथिजनश्चापि गृहे पर्यशितो मया। मात्सर्यात् स्वादुकामेन नृशंसेन बुभुक्षता॥
en: Without feeding servants and guests arrived at my house, I used to fill, when hungry, my own stomach, proud, covetous of good food, cruel as I was.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: देवार्थं पितृयज्ञार्थमन्नं श्रद्धाऽऽहतं मया। न दत्तमर्थकामेन देयमन्नं पुरा किल॥
en: Greedy as I was of riches, I never dedicated, with faith and respect any food to the celestials and the departed Manes, although duty required me to dedicate food to them.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: गुप्तं शरणमाश्रित्य भयेषु शरणागताः। अकस्मात् ते मया त्यक्ता न त्राता अभयैषिणः॥
en: Those men who moved by fear, came to me, for seeking my help, I sent adrift without giving them any protection. I did not extend my help to those who came to me with prayers for removing their fear.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: धनं धान्यं प्रियान् दारान् यानं वासस्तथाद्भुतम्। श्रियं दृष्ट्वा मनुष्याणामसूयामि निरर्थकम्॥
en: I used to feel unreasonable envy at seeing other people's riches and corn, and wives held dear by them, and articles of drink, and good palaces.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: ईष्र्युः परसुखं दृष्ट्वा अन्यस्य च बुभूषकः। त्रिवर्गहन्ता चान्येषामात्मकामानुवर्तकः॥
en: Seeing the happiness of other I was filled with envy and I always wished them poverty. Acting thus which promised to crown my own wishes with fruition, I sought to destroy the virtue, riches, and pleasures of other people.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: नृशंसगुणभूयिष्ठं पुरा कर्म कृतं मया। स्मृत्वा तदनुतप्येऽहं हित्वा प्रियमिवात्मजम्॥
en: In that past life of mine, I committed various deeds moved by cruelty and such other passions. Recollecting those deeds I am filled with repentance and grief, as one is filled with grief at the loss of his dear son.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: शुभानां नाभिजानामि कृतानां कर्मणां फलम्। माता च पूजिता वृद्धा ब्राह्मणश्चार्चितो मया।॥
en: On account of those deeds of mine, I do not know what the fruits are of good deeds. I, however, adored my old mother and on one occasion adored a Brahmana.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: सकृज्जातिगुणोपेतः सङ्गत्या गृहमागतः। अतिथिः पूजितो ब्रह्मस्तेन मां नाजहात् स्मृतिः॥
en: Gifted with birth and accomplishments, that Brahmana, while travelling, came to my house once as a guest. I received him with respectful hospitality. One account of the merit of that deed my memory has not forsaken me.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: कर्मणा पुनरेवाहं सुखमागामि लक्षये। तच्छ्रोतुमहमिच्छामि त्वत्तः श्रेयस्तपोधन॥
en: I think that on account of that deed, I shall once more succeed in regaining happiness. O you having asceticism for wealth you know everything, Tell me please what is for my behoof.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: व्यास उवाच शुभेन कर्मणा यद्वै तिर्यग्योनौ न मुह्यसे। ममैव कीट तत् कर्म येन त्वं न प्रमुह्यसे॥
en: Vyasa said On account of a meritorious deed, Oworm, that you, though born in the intermediate order of being are not stupefied. For a deed of mine, Oworm you are not stupefied.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: अहं त्वां दर्शनादेव तारयामि तपोबलात्। तपोबलाद्धि बलवद् बलमन्यन्न विद्यते॥
en: On account of the power of my penances, I am able to rescue a being of sin by granting him sight only of my body. There is no stronger power than that of penances.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: जानामि पापैः स्वकृतैर्गतं त्वां कीट कीटताम्। अवाप्स्यसि पुनर्धर्मं धर्मं तु यदि मन्यसे॥
en: I know, O worm that you have taken birth in the order of worms through the evil deeds of your past life. If, however, you think of acquiring virtue and inerit, you may again attain to it.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: कर्म भूमिकृतं देवा भुञ्जते तिर्यगाश्च ये। धर्मोऽपि हि मनुष्येषु कामार्थश्च तथा गुणाः॥
en: Deities as well as beings crowned with ascetic success, enjoy suffer the consequence of deeds done by them in this field of action. Men perform acts of merit from desire of fruit. The very accomplishinents that one seeks to acquire are sought from desire of the happiness they will produce.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: वाग्बुद्धिपाणिपादैश्च व्यपेतस्य विपश्चितः। किं हास्यति मनुष्यस्य मन्दस्यापि हि जीवतः॥
en: Learned or ignorant (in a previous existence) the creature that is in this life, shorn of speech and understanding and hands and feet, is really shorn of everything. or

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: जीवन् हि कुरुते पूजां विप्राय: शशिसूर्ययोः। ब्रुवन्नपि कथां पुण्यां तत्र कीट त्वमेष्यसि॥
en: He who becomes a superior Brahmana worships while alive, the deities of the sun and the moon, uttering various sacred Mantras. O worm, you will come by that state of existence.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: गुणभूतानि भूतानि तत्र त्वमुपभोक्ष्यसे। तत्र तेऽहं विनेष्यामि ब्रह्म त्वं यत्र वैष्यसि॥
en: Acquiring that status you will enjoy all the clements converted into articles of enjoyinent. When you have acquired that state, I shall impart to you Brahma. Or, if you wish, I may place you in any other status.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: स तथेति प्रतिश्रुत्य कीटो वर्त्मन्यतिष्ठत। शकटो व्रजंश्च सुमहानागतश्च यदृच्छया॥
en: Agreeing to the words of Vyasa, the worm did not leave the road, but remained on it. Meanwhile, the large car which was coming ini that direction came there.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: चक्राक्रमेण भिन्नश्च कीट: प्राणान् मुमोच हा सम्भूतः क्षत्रियकुले प्रसादादमितौजसः॥ तमृषि द्रष्टुमगमत् सर्वास्वन्यासु योनिषु। वाविन्द्रोधावरहाणां तथैव मृगपक्षिणाम्॥ वपाकशूद्रवैश्यानां क्षत्रियाणां च योनिषु। एवमाभाष्य ऋषिणा सत्यवादिना। प्रतिस्मृत्याथ जग्राह पादौ मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: Torn to pieces by the assault of the wheels, the worm died. Born at last in the Kshatriya order through the grace of Vyasa of immeasurable power, he proceeded to see the great Rishi. He had, before becoming a Kshatriya, to pass through various orders of birth, such as hedgehog and Iguana and boar and dcer and bird, and Chandala and Shudra and Vaishya. Having given and account of his various changes to the truth-telling Rishi, and remembering the Rishi's kindness for him, the worm (now with joined hands fell at the Rishi's feet and touched them with his head.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: कीट उवाच इदं तदतुलं स्थानमीप्सितं दशभिर्गुणैः। यदहं प्राप्य कीटत्वमागतो राजपुत्रताम्॥ स कीट
en: The Worm said My present status is that great one which is coveted by all and which only persons having ten well known attribute, can get. Indeed, I who was formerly a worm have thus acquired the status of a prince.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: वहन्ति मामतिबला: कुञ्जरा हेममालिनः। स्यन्दनेषु च काम्बोजा युक्ताः परमवाजिनः॥
en: Elephants of great strength, decked with golden chains, carry me on their backs. To my cars are yoked Kamboja horses of High mettle.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: उष्ट्राश्वतरयुक्तानि यानानि च वहन्ति माम्। सबान्धवः सहामात्यश्चाश्नामि पिशितौदनम्॥
en: Numerous cars to which are attached camels and mules bear me. With all my relatives and friends I now eat food rich with meat.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: गृहेषु स्वनिवासेषु सुखेषु शयनेषु च। वराहेषु महाभाग स्वपामि च सुपूजितः॥
en: Adored by all, I sleep, O highly blessed one on rich beds in charming rooms to which disagreeable winds cannot blow.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: सर्वेष्वपररात्रेषु सूतमागधबन्दिनः। स्तुवन्ति मां यथा देवा महेन्द्रं प्रियवादिनः॥
en: Towards the dawn bards and encomiasts sing my praises even as the deities utter the agreeable praises of Indra their chief.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: प्रसादात् सत्यसंधस्य भवतोऽमिततेजसः। यदहं कीटतां प्राप्य सम्प्राप्तो राजपुत्रताम्॥
en: Through your favour who are firm in truth and gifted with immeasurable energy, I who was before a worin have now become a Kshatriya.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: नमस्तेऽस्तु महाप्राज्ञ किं करोमि प्रशाधि माम्। त्वत्तपोबलनिर्दिष्टमिदं ह्यधिगतं मया॥
en: I bow my head to you, O you of great wisdom. Do you command me as to what I should now do. Ordained by the power of your penances, I have come by this position.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: व्यास उवाच अर्चितोऽहं त्वया राजन् वाग्भिरद्य यदृच्छया। अद्य ते कीटतां प्राप्य स्मृतिर्जाता जुगुप्सिता॥
en: Vyasa said I have today been adored by you, O king, with various words expressive of respect. Changed into a worm your memory had become clouded. That memory has again appeared.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: न तु नाशोऽस्ति पापस्य यस्त्वयोपचितः पुरा। शूद्रेणार्थप्रधानेन नृशंसेनाततायिना॥
en: The sin you had committed in a pristine life, has not yet been dissipated that sin viz., which was acquired by you while you were a Shudra covetous of riches and cruel in conduct and hostile to the Brahmanas.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: मम ते दर्शनं प्राप्तं तच्च वै सुकृतं त्वया। तिर्यग्योनौ स्म जातेन मम चाभ्यर्चनात् तथा॥ इतस्त्वं राजपुत्रत्वाद् ब्राह्मण्यं समवाप्स्यसि। गोब्राह्मणकृते प्राणान् हुत्वाऽऽत्मानं रणाजिरे॥
en: You were able to obtain a sight of my body. That was an act of merit to you while you were a worm. On account of your having saluted and worshipped me, you shall rise higher for, from the Kshatriya order you shall rise to the status of a Brahinana, if only you die on the field of battle for the sake of kine or Brahmanas.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: राजपुत्र सुखं प्राप्य क्रतूंश्चैवाप्तदक्षिणान्। अथ मोदिष्यसे स्वर्गे ब्रह्मभूतोऽव्ययः सुखी॥
en: O prince, enjoying much happiness and celebrating many sacrifices with profuse presents, you shall attain to Heaven and, changed into eternal Brahma, you shall enjoy perfect beatitude.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: तिर्यग्योन्याः शूद्रतामभ्युपैति शूद्रो वैश्यं क्षत्रियत्वं च वैश्यः। वृत्तश्लाघी क्षत्रियो ब्राह्मणत्वं स्वर्ग पुण्यं ब्राह्मणः साधुवृत्तः॥
en: Those who take birth in the intermediate order become Shudras. The Shudra rises to the status of the Vaishya; and the Vaishya to that of the Kshatriya. The charge of the duties of his caste succeeds in acquiring the status of a Brahmana. The Brahmana, by following a righteous conduct, acquires Heaven which is full of happiness.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: भीष्म उवाच क्षत्रधर्ममनुप्राप्तः स्मरन्नेव च वीर्यवान्। त्यक्त्वा स कीटतां राजंश्चचार विपुलं तपः॥
en: Bhishma said Having renounced the status of a worm and taken birth as a Kshatriya of great energy, the person remembering his previous changes, O monarch began to practise severe austerities.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: तस्य धर्मार्थविदुषो दृष्ट्वा तद् विपुलं तपः। आजगाम द्विजश्रेष्ठः कृष्णद्वैपायनस्तदा॥
en: Seeing those severe austerities of the Kshatriya who was well conversant with religion and Profit, Krishna Dvaipayana, that foremost of Brahmanas, went to him.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: व्यास उवाच क्षानं देवव्रतं कीट भूतानां परिपालनम्। क्षात्रं देवव्रतं व्यायंस्ततो विप्रत्वमेष्यसि॥
en: Vyasa said The penances, O worm, of the Kshatriyas consist of the protection of all creatures. Consider these duties of the Kshatriya to be the penances laid down for you. You shall come by the status of a Brahmana.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: पाहि सर्वाः प्रजाः सम्यक् शुभाशुभविदात्मवान्। शुभैः संविभजन् कामैरशुभानां च पावनैः॥
en: Ascertaining what is right and what is wrong, and purifying your soul, do you duly cherish and protect all creatures, judiciously satisfying all good desires and correcting all that is unholy.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: आत्मवान् भव सुप्रीतः स्वधर्माचरणे रतः। क्षात्री तनुं समुत्सृज्य ततो विप्रत्वमेष्यसि॥
en: Be you of purified soul, be contented and be devoted to the practice of virtue. Acting thus, you will then, when you die, become a Brahmana.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: भीष्म उवाच सोऽप्यवरण्यमनुप्राप्य पुनरेव युधिष्ठिर। महर्षेर्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रजा धर्मेण पाल्य च॥
en: Bhishma said Although he had retired into the forest yet, O Yudhishthira, having heard the words of the great Rishi, he began to cherish and protect his subjects righteously.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: अचिरेणैव कालेन कीट: पार्थिवसत्तम। प्रजापालनधर्मेण प्रेत्य विप्रत्वमागतः॥
en: Soon O best of kings, that worm, on account of the duty of protecting his subjects became a Brahmana after renouncing his Kshatriya body.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: ततस्तं ब्राह्मणं दृष्ट्वा पुनरेव महायशाः। आजगाम महाप्राज्ञः कृष्णद्वैपायनस्तदा॥
en: Secing him changed into a Brahmana, the celebrated Rishi,viz.,. Krishna Dvaipayana of great wisdom came to him.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: व्यास उवाच भो भो ब्रह्मर्षभ श्रीमन् मा व्यथिष्ठाः कथंचन। शुभकृच्छुभयोनीषु पापकृत् पापयोनिषु॥ उपपद्यति धर्मज्ञ यथापापफलोपगम्।
en: Vyasa said ochief of Brahmanas, O blessed one, be not troubled. He who acts piously, comes by a respectable birth. He on the other hand, who acts impiously comes by a low and vile birth. O you who are conversant with virtue, one attains to misery according to the measure of his sin.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: तस्मान्मृत्युभयात् कीट मा व्यथिष्ठाः कथंचन।॥ धर्मलोपभयं ते स्यात् तस्माद् धर्मं चरोत्तमम्।
en: Therefore, O worm do not be troubled through fear of death. The only fear you should entertain is about the loss of virtue. Do you therefore, go on practising virtue.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: कीट उवाच सुखात् सुखतरं प्राप्तो भगवंस्त्वत्कृते ह्यहम्॥ धर्ममूलां श्रियं प्राप्य पाप्मा नष्ट इहाद्य मे।
en: The Worm said Through your favour, O Holy one, I have attained from happy to happier positions! Having obtained such prosperity as is established in virtue, I think my demerits have been lost.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: भीष्म उवाच भगवद्वचनात् कीटो ब्राह्मण्यं प्राप्य दुर्लभम्॥ अकरोत् पृथिवीं राजन् यज्ञयूपशताङ्किताम्।
en: Bhishma said The worin having at the command of the holy Rishi acquired the status of a Brahmana that is so difficult to attain, caused the Earth to be marked with a thousand sacrificial stakes.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: ततः सालोक्यमगमद ब्रह्मणो ब्रह्मवित्तमः॥ अवाप च पदं कीटः पार्थ ब्रह्म सनातनम्। स्वकर्मफलनिर्वृत्तं व्यासस्य वचनात् तदा॥
en: That foremost of all persons conversant with Brahma then gained a residence in the region of Brahman himself. Indeed, O son of Pritha, the worm acquired the highest status viz. that of eternal Brahma as the result of his own deeds done according to the counsels of Vyasa.

description: The end of persons dying in battlefield. The discourse between Dvaipayana and a worm
sn: तेऽपि यस्मात् प्रभावेण हताः क्षत्रियपुङ्गवाः। सम्प्राप्तास्ते गतिं पुण्यां तस्मान्मा शोच पुत्रक॥
en: Those foremost of Kshatriyas, also, who have renounced their lifebreaths, exerting their energy all the while have all acquired a meritorious end. Therefore, O king, do not mourn on their account.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच विद्या तपश्च दानं च किमेतेषां विशिष्यते। पृच्छामि त्वां सतां श्रेष्ठ तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Which amongst these three is superior, viz.,. knowledge, Penances, and Gifts? I ask foremost of pious men. Tell me this, O grandfather.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: भीष्म उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। मैत्रेयस्य च संवादं कृष्णद्वैपायनस्य च।॥
en: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old conversation between Maitreya and Krishna Dvaipayana.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: कृष्णद्वैपायनो राजन्नज्ञातचरितं चरन्। वाराणस्यामुपातिष्ठन्मैत्रेयं स्वैरिणीकुले॥
en: Once on a time Krishna Dvaipayana, O king, while wandering over the world in disguisc, proceeded to Varanasi and waited tipon Maitreya who belonged by birth to a race of ascetics.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: तमुपस्थितमासीनं ज्ञात्वा स मुनिसत्तम। अर्चित्वा भोजयामास मैत्रेयोऽशनमुत्तमम्॥
en: Seeing Vyasa arrive, that foremost of Rishis viz., Maitreya, gave him a seat and after adoring him with due rites, entertained him with excellent food.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: तदन्नमुत्तमं भुक्त्वा गुणवत् सार्वकामिकम्। प्रतिष्ठमानोस्मयत प्रीतः कृष्णो महामनाः॥
en: Having eaten that good food which was very wholesome and which gave every kind of ratification the great Krishna become highly pleased and as he sat there, he even laughed aloud.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: तमुत्स्मयन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य मैत्रेयः कृष्णमब्रवीत्। कारणं ब्रूहि धर्मात्मन् व्यस्मयिष्ठाः कुतश्च ते॥
en: Seeing Krishna laugh, Maitreya addressed him. saying Tell me, O Righteous souled one, what the reason is of your laughter! You are an ascetic, gifted with power to control your emotions. Great joy, it appears has come over yoll.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: तपस्विनो धृतिमतः प्रमोदः समुपागतः। एतत् पृच्छामि ते विद्वन्नभिवाद्य प्रणम्य च॥
en: Saluting you and adoring you with bent head, I ask you this viz., what the power is of my penances and what the high blessedness is that is yours.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: आत्मनश्च तपोभाग्यं महाभाग्यं तवेह च। पृथगाचरतस्तात पृथगात्मसुखात्मनोः। अल्पान्तरमहं मन्ये विशिष्टमपि चान्वयात्॥
en: The acts I do are different from those of yours. You are already emancipated though alive. I however am not yet freed. For all that, I think that there is not much difference between you and me. I am, again distinguished by birth.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: व्यास उवाच अतिच्छन्दातिवादाभ्यां स्मयोऽयं समुपागतः। असत्यं वेदवचनं कस्माद् वेदोऽनृतं वेदत्॥
en: Vyasa said This wonder that has filled me, has originated from an ordinance which appears like a hyperbole for the comprehension of the people. The declaration of the Vedas seems to be untrue. But why should the Vedas say an untruth?

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: त्रीण्येव तु पदान्याहुः पुरुषस्योत्तमं व्रतम्। न दुह्येच्चैव दद्याच्च सत्यं चैव परं वदेत्॥
en: It has been said that there are three roads which form the best vows of a man. One should never injure; one should always tell the truth; and one should make gift.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: इति वेदोक्तमृषिभिः पुरस्तात् परिकल्पितम्। इदानीं चैव नः कृत्यं पुरस्ताच्च परिश्रुतम्॥
en: The Rishis of old said this, following the ordinances laid down in the Vedas. These injunctions of yore, should certainly be followed by us even in our times.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: अल्पोऽपि तादृशो दायो भवत्युत महाफलः। तृषिताय च ते दत्तं हृदयेनानसूयता॥
en: Even a small gift, made under the circumstances laid down, yields great fruits. You have given a little water with a sincere heart to a thirsty man.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: तृषितस्तृषिताय त्वं दत्त्वैतद् दर्शनं मम। अजैषीमहतो लोकान् महायज्ञैरिव प्रभो॥
en: Yourself thirsty and hungry, you have by giving me such food, conquered many high regions of happiness, O powerful one, as one does by many sacrifices.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: ततो दानपवित्रेण प्रीतोऽस्मि तपसैव च। पुण्यस्यैव हि ते सत्त्वं पुण्यस्यैव च दर्शनम्॥
en: I am greatly delighted with your very sacred gift as also with your penances. Your power is that of virtue. Your appearance is that of virtue.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: पुण्यस्यैवाभिगन्धस्ते मन्ये कर्मविधानजम्। अधिकं मार्जनात् तात तथा चैवानुलेपनात्॥ शुभं सर्वपवित्रेभ्यो दानमेव परं द्विजा नो चेत् सर्वपवित्रेभ्यो दानमेव परं भवेत्॥
en: The fragrance of virtue, is about you. I think that all your acts are performed according to the ordinance. O son, gift is superior to ablutions in sacred waters and to the accomplishment of all Vedic vows. Indeed, O Brahmana, gift is inore auspicious than all religious rites. If it be not more meritorious than all religious rites, there can be no question about its superiority.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: यानीमान्युत्तमानीह वेदोक्तानि प्रशंससि। तेषां श्रेष्ठतरं दानमिति मे नात्र संशयः॥
en: All those rites laid down in the Vedas which you highly speak of, do not equal a gift for, gift is undoubtedly fraught with very superior merit.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: दानकृद्भिः कृतः पन्था येन यान्ति मनीषिणः। ते हि प्राणस्य दातारस्तेषु धर्मः प्रतिष्ठितः॥
en: The road that has been made by those men, who make gifts is the road that is trodden by the wise. They who make gifts are considered as givers of even the life-breaths. The duties that forin virtue are established in them.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: यथा वेदाः स्वधीताश्च यथा चेन्द्रियसंयमः। सर्वत्यागो यथा चेह तथा दानमनुत्तमम्॥
en: As the Vedas when well-studied, as the controlling of the senses, as a life of universal Renunciation, so is gift which is fraught with very superior merit.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: त्वं हि तात महाबुद्धे सुखमेष्यसि शोभनम्। सुखात् सुखतरप्राप्तिमाप्नुते मतिमान्नरः॥
en: You, O son will rise from joy to greater joy (for performing the duty of making gifts.). The intelligent man certainly rises from joy to greater joy.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: तन्नः प्रत्यक्षमेवेदमुपलभ्यमसंशयम्। श्रीमन्तः प्राप्नुवन्त्यर्थान् दानं यज्ञं तथा सुखम्॥
en: We have undoubtedly seen many instances of this men gifted with prosperity succeed in acquiring riches, making gifts celebrating sacrifices, and acquiring happiness as the result thereof.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: सुखादेव परं दुःखं दुःखादप्यपरं सुखम्। दृश्यते हि महाप्राज्ञ नियतं वै स्वभावतः॥
en: It is always observed, O you of great wisdom to happen naturally that happiness is followed by misery, and misery is followed by happiness.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: त्रिविधानीह वृत्तानि नरस्याहुर्मनीषिणः। पुण्यमन्यत् पापमन्यन्न पुण्यं न च पापकम्॥
en: Wise men have said that human beings in this world have three kinds of conduct. Some are righteous; some are sinful; and some are neither righteous nor sinful.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: न वृत्तं मन्यते तस्य मन्यते न च पातकम्। तथा स्वकर्मनिर्वृत्तं न पुण्यं न च पापकम्॥
en: The conduct of the person who is devoted to Brahman is not considered either way. His sins are never considered as sins. So also the man who is devoted to the duties laid down for him, is considered as neither pious nor sinful.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: यज्ञदानतपःशीला नरा वै पुण्यकर्मिणः। येऽभिद्रुह्यन्ति भूतानि ते वै पापकृतो जनाः॥
en: Those men who are devoted to sacrifices, gifts, and penances, are considered as pious. These, however who injure other creatures and are unfriendly to them are considered sinful.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: द्रव्याण्याददते चैव दुःखं यान्ति पतन्ति च। ततोऽन्यत् कर्म यत्किचिन्न पुण्यं न च पातकम्॥२६
en: There are some men who appropriate others properties. These certainly fall into Hell and meet with misery. All other acts that men do are indifferent, being considered as neither righteous nor sinful.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: रमस्वैधस्व मोदस्व देहि चैव यजस्व च। न त्वामभिभविष्यन्ति वैद्या न च तपस्विनः॥
en: Do you sport and grow and rejoice and make gifts and celebrated sacrifices. Neither men of knowledge nor those gifted with penances will then be able to get the better of you.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: रमस्वैधस्व मोदस्व देहि चैव यजस्व च। न त्वामभिभविष्यन्ति वैद्या न च तपस्विनः॥
en: Do you sport and grow and rejoice and make gifts and celebrated sacrifices. Neither men of knowledge nor those gifted with penances will then be able to get the better of you.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच मैत्रेयः कर्मपूजकः। अत्यन्तश्रीमति कुले जातः प्राज्ञो बहुश्रुतः॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed by Vyasa, Maitreya, who was a worshipper of deeds, who had been born in a family gifted with great prosperity, who was wise and endued with great learning said to him these words.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: मैत्रेय उवाच असंशयं महाप्राज्ञ यथैवात्थ तथैव तत्। अनुज्ञातश्च भवता किंचिद् ब्रूयामहं विभो॥
en: Maitreya said O you of great wisdom, it is what you have said O powerful one, with your permission I wish to say something.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: व्यास उवाच यद् यदिच्छसि मैत्रेय यावद् यावद् यथा यथा। ब्रूहि तत्त्वं महाप्राज्ञ शुश्रूषे वचनं तव॥
en: Vyasa said Whatever you wish to say, O Maitreya in what way so even, do you say, O man of great wisdom, for I wish to hear you.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: मैत्रेय उवाच निर्दोषं निर्मलं चैवं वचनं दानसंहितम्। विद्यातपोभ्यां हि भवान् भावितात्मा न संशयः॥
en: Maitreya said Your words on the subject of gift are faultless and pure. Forsooth, your soul has been purified by knowledge and penances.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: भवतो भावितात्मत्वाल्लाभोऽयं सुमहान् मम। भूयो बुद्ध्यानुपश्यामि सुसमृद्धतपा इव॥
en: On account of your soul being purified, even this is the great advantage I reap from it. With the help of my understanding I see that you are gifted with high penances.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: अपि नो दर्शनादेव भवतोऽभ्युदयो भवेत्। मन्ये भवत्प्रसादोऽयं तद्धि कर्म स्वभावतः॥
en: As regards ourselves we succeed in acquiring prosperity through only seeing personages like you. I think that is due to your favour and originates from the nature of my own acts.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: तपः श्रुतं च योनिश्चाप्यतेद् ब्राह्मण्यकारणम्। त्रिभिर्गुणैः समुदितस्ततो भवति वै द्विजः॥
en: Penances, knowledge of the Vedas, and birth in a pure family, these are the causes of the status which one acquires of a Brahmana. When one is possessed of these three qualities then does he coine to be called a twice born person.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: अस्मिंस्तृप्ते च तृप्यन्ते पितरो दैवतानि च। न हि श्रुतवतां किंचिदधिकं ब्राह्मणादृते॥
en: If the Brahmana be pleased, the departed Manes and the deities also are pleased. There is nothing superior to a Brahmana possessed of Vedic learning.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: अन्धं स्यात् तम एवेदं न प्रज्ञायेत किंचन। चातुर्वण्र्यं न वर्तेत धर्माधर्मावृतानृते॥
en: Without the Brahmana, all would be darkness. Nothing would be known. The four castes would not exist. The distinction between virtue and sin, Truth and Untruth, would disappear.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: यथा हि सुकृलभे क्षेत्रे फलं विन्दति मानवः। एवं दत्त्वा श्रुतवति फलं दाता समश्नुते॥
en: Men, when they sow on a wellcultivated field reap an abundant harvest. Even so one reaps great merit by making gifts to a Brahmana endued with great learning.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: ब्राह्मणश्चेन्न विन्देत श्रुतवृत्तोपसंहितः। प्रतिग्रहीता दानस्य मोघं स्याद् धनिनां धनम्॥
en: If there were no Brahmana gifted with Vedic learning and good conduct for accepting gifts, the wealth possessed by rich men would be useless.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: अदनविद्वान् हन्त्यन्नमद्यमानं च हन्ति तम्। तं चान्नं पाति यश्चान्नं स हन्ता हन्यतेऽबुधः॥
en: The ignorant Brahmana, by eating the food that is offered to him, destroys what he eats. The food also that is eaten destroys the eater. That is called food which is given away to a worthy man, in all other cases he who takes it, makes the donor's gift thrown away and the receiver is likewise ruined for his unduly taking it.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: प्रभुन्नमदन् विद्वान् पुनर्जनयतीश्वरः। स चान्नाज्जायते तस्मात् सूक्ष्म एष व्यतिक्रमः॥
en: The Brahmana endued with learning, becomes the subjugator of the food that he eats. Having eaten it, be begets other food. The ignorant man who eats the food offered to him, loses his right to the children he procreates for the latter become his whose food has enabled the progenitor to beget them. This is the shortcoming of persons eating other people's food when they have not the power to conquer that food.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: यदेव ददतः पुण्यं तदेव प्रतिगृह्णतः। न ह्येकचक्रं वर्तेत इत्येवमृषयो विदुः॥
en: The merit which the giver wins by making the gift is equal to what the taker acquires by accepting the food Both the giver and the taker depend equally upon each other. This is what the Rishis have said.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: यत्र वै ब्राह्मणाः सन्ति श्रुतवृत्तोपसंहिताः। तत्र दानफलं पुण्यमिह चामुत्र चाश्नुते॥
en: There where Brahmanas exist, gifted with Vedic learning and conduct people are enabled to acquire the sacred fruits of gifts and to enjoy them both in this world and the next.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: ये योनिशुद्धाः सततं तपस्यभिरता भृशम्। दानाध्ययनसम्पन्नास्ते वै पूज्यतमाः सदा॥
en: Those men who are of pure birth, who are devoted to penances and who make gifts and study the Vedas, are considered as worthy of the most respectful adoration

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: तैर्हि सद्धिः कृतः पन्थास्तेन यातो न मुह्यते। ते हि स्वर्गस्य नेतारो यज्ञवाहाः सनातनाः॥
en: It is those good men who have chalked out the path by treading on which one does not become stupefied. It is those men who take others to the celestial region. They are the Men who carry on their shoulders the burthen of Sacrifices and live for good.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्तः स भगवान् मैत्रेयं प्रत्यभाषत। दिष्ट्यैवं त्वं विजानासि दिष्ट्या ते बुद्धिरीदृशी॥
en: Bhishma said Thus addressed, the Holy one replied to Maitreya, saying, By good luck you are gifted with knowledge. By good luck your understanding is of this kind.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: लोको ह्यार्यगुणानेव भूयिष्ठं तु प्रशंसति। रूपमानवयोमानश्रीमानाचाप्यसंशयम्॥
en: Good men highly speak of righteous qualities. By your good luck you are not overwhelmed by personal beauty, youth and prosperity.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: दिष्ट्या नाभिभवन्ति त्वां दैवस्तेऽयमनुग्रहः। यत् ते भृशतरं दानाद् वर्तयिष्यामि तच्छृणु॥
en: This favour done to you is due to kindness of the celestials. Listen to me, as I describe to you what is even superior to gift.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: यानीहागमशास्त्राणि याश्च काश्चित् प्रवृत्तयः। तानि वेदं पुरस्कृत्य प्रवृत्तानि यथाक्रमम्॥
en: All scriptures, religious treatises, and rites that are seen in the world, have all originated from the Vedas, according to their due order.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: अहं दानं प्रशंसामि भवानपि तपःश्रुते। तपः पवित्रं वेदस्य तपः स्वर्गस्य साधनम्॥
