en: Following them I highly speak of gift. You highly speak of penances and Vedic learning. Penances are sacred. Penances are the means by which one may acquire the Vedas and the celestial region.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: तपसा महदाप्नोति विद्यया चेति नः श्रुतम्। तपसैव चापनुदेद् यच्चान्यदपि दुष्कृतम्॥
en: With the help of penances and of knowledge one acquires the highest fruits.; It is by penances that onc dissipates his sins and all else that is evil.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: यद् यद्धि किंचित् संधाय पुरुषस्तप्यते तपः। सर्वमेतदवाप्नोति विद्यया चेति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that with whatever purpose in view one performs performs one acquires the fruition thereof on account of those penances. The same may be said of knowledge.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: दुरन्वयं दुष्प्रधर्षं दुरापं दुरतिक्रमम्। सर्वे वै तपसाभ्येति तपो हि बलवत्तरम्॥
en: Whatever is difficult to do whatever is dificult to conquer whatever is difficult to attain, and whatever is difficult to cross, can all be done with the help of penances. Of all things, penaces are of very superior power.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: सुरापोऽसम्मतादायी भ्रूणहा गुरुतल्पगः। तपसा तरते सर्वमेनसश्च प्रमुच्यते॥
en: The man who drinks alcohol, or he who takes forcibly other men's properties, or he who is guilty of focticide, or he who violates the bed of his preceptor, succeeds in crossing with the help of penances. Indeed, one becomes purged off of all these sins through penances.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: सर्वविद्यस्तु चक्षुष्मानपि यादृशतादृशम्। तपस्विनं तथैवाहस्ताभ्यां कार्यं सदा नमः॥
en: One gifted with all knowledge and therefore, having true vision and an ascetic of whatever kind, are equal. One should always bow to these two.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: सर्वे पूज्याः श्रुतधनास्तथैव च तपस्विनः। दानप्रदाः सुखं प्रेत्य प्राप्नुवन्तीह च श्रियम्॥
en: All men who have the Vedas for their wealth should be adored. Likewise all men gifted with penances deserve to be adored. They who make gifts get happiness in the next world and much prosperity in this world.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: इमं च ब्रह्मलोकं च लोकं च बलवत्तरम्। अन्नदानैः सुकृतिनः प्रतिपद्यन्ति लौकिकाः॥
en: By making gifts of food righteous men of this world obtain both this world and that of Brahiman himself with many other regions of superior happiness.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: पूजिताः पूजयन्त्येते मानिता मानयन्ति च। स दाता यत्र यत्रैति सर्वतः सम्प्रणूयते॥
en: Those men who are worshipped by all, theinselves worship him who makes gifts. Those men who are honoured everywhere, themselves honour him who makes gifts. Wherever the giver goes, he hears himself his own praise.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: अकर्ता चैव कर्ता च लभते यस्य यादृशम्। यदि चोर्ध्वं यद्यधो वा स्वाल्लोकानभियास्यति॥
en: He who docs acts and he who omits to do them, gets each what is proportionate to his acts and omissions. Whether one lives in the upper regions or in the nether, one always acquires those places to which one becomes entitled by his deeds.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: प्राप्स्यसि त्वन्नपानानि यानि वाञ्छसि कानिचित्। मेधाव्यसि कुले जातः श्रुतवाननृशंसवान्॥
en: As regards yourself you will certainly obtain whatever food and drink you may covet, for you are gifted with intelligence, good birth, Vedic learning and mercy.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: कौमारचारी व्रतवान् मैत्रेय निरतो भव। एतद् गृहाण प्रथमं प्रशस्तं गृहमेधिनाम्॥
en: You are possessed of youth, O Maitreya! you are observant of vows. Be devoted to virtuc. Do you take instructions from me about thosc duties which you should first follow, the duties, viz., of householders.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: यो भर्ता वासितातुष्टो भर्तुस्तुष्टा च वासिता। यस्मिन्नेवं कुले सर्वे कल्याणं तत्र वर्तते॥
en: That house in which the husband is pleased with his married wife, and the wife pleased with her husband, all auspicious results ensue.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: अद्भिर्गात्रान्मलमिव तमोऽग्निप्रभया यथा। दानेन तपसा चैव सर्वपापमपोहति॥
en: As filth is washed away from the body with water, as darkness is removed by the light of fire, so is sin washed off by gifts and penances.

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि मैत्रेय गृहान् साधु व्रजाम्यहम्। एतन्मनसि कर्तव्यं श्रेय एवं भविष्यति॥
en: Bless you, O Maitreya, may you have palaces! I depart hence in peace. Do you remember what I have said. You shall then be able to reap many advantages!

description: Knowledge, penances and gifts, which of them is superior
sn: तं प्रणम्याथ मैत्रेयः कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्। स्वस्ति प्राप्नोतु भगवाननित्युवाच कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: Maitreya then walked round his illustrious guest and bowed his head to him, and joining his hands in respect said, Let blessing be to you also, O Holy one!

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सत्स्त्रीणां समुदाचारं सर्वधर्मविदां वर। श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं त्वत्तस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said O you who know all duties, I wish to hcar in full, what forms the excellent conduct of good and chaste women. Do you, O grandfather, describe this to me.!

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: भीष्म उवाच सर्वज्ञां सर्वतत्त्वज्ञां देवलोके मनस्विनीम्। कैकेयी सुमना नाम शाण्डिली पर्यपृच्छत॥ केन वृत्तेन कल्याणि समाचारेण केन वा। विधूय सर्वपापानि देवलोकं त्वमागता॥ हुताशनशिखेव त्वं ज्वलमाना स्वतेजसा। सुता ताराधिपस्येव प्रभया दिवमागता॥
en: Bhishma said Once on a time in the celestial region, a lady named Sumana of Kaikeya's race, addressing Shandili, gifted with great energy and conversant with the truth regarding everything and gifted with omniscience, said, By what conduct, O auspicious lady, by what course of deeds have you succeeded in acquiring the celestial region, purged off of every sin? You shine with your own energy like a flame of fire, You appear to be a daughter of the Lord of stars, come to Heaven in your own effulgence.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: अरजांसि च वस्त्राणि धारयन्ती गलक्लमा। विमानस्था शुभा भासि सहस्रगुणमोजसा॥
en: You put on dresses of pure white, and as quite cheerful and at your case. Scated on that celestial car, you shine, O auspicious dame, with energy multiplied a thousand fold.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: न त्वमल्पेन तपसा दानेन नियमेन वा। इमं लोकमनुप्राप्ता तवं हि तत्त्वं वदस्व मे॥
en: You have not, I understand, attained to this region of happiness by great penances and gifts and vows. Do you tell me the truth!

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: इति पृष्टा सुमनया मधुरं चारुहासिनी। शाण्डिली निभृतं वाक्यं सुमनामिदमब्रवीत्॥ नाहं कापायवसना नापि वल्कलधारिणी। च जटिला भूत्वा देवत्वमागता॥ अहितानि च वाक्यानि सर्वाणि परुषाणि च। अप्रमत्ता च भर्तारं कदाचिन्नाहमब्रुवम॥
en: Thus questioned swectly by Sumana, Stiandili of sweet smiles, addressing her fair interrogatrix, thus answered her silently. I did not wear yellow robes; nor barks of trees. I did not shave my head; nor did I keep matted locks on my head. It is not on account of these deeds that I have acquired the status of a celestial. I never carelessly addressed any harsh words to my husband.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: न च मुण्डा देवतानां पितॄणां च ब्राह्मणानां च पूजने। अप्रमत्ता सदा युक्ता श्वश्वशुरवर्तिनी॥
en: I was always devoted to the adoration of the celestials the departed Manes, and the Brahmanas. Always careful I waited upon and served my motherin law and father-in-law.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: पैशुन्ये न प्रवामि न ममैतन्मनोगतम्। अद्वारि न च तिष्ठामि चिरं न कथयामि च॥
en: This was my resolution that I should never act deceitfully. I never used of stay at the door of our house nor did I speak long with anybody.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: असद् वा हसितं किंचिदहितं वापि कर्मणा। रहस्यमरहस्यं वा न प्रवामि सर्वथा।॥
en: I never did any evil deed. I never laughed aloud; I never did any injury; I never gave out any secret. Thus did I myself act.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: कार्यार्थं निर्गतं चापि भार्तारं गृहमागतम्। आसनेनोपसंयोज्य पूजयामि समाहिता॥
en: When my husband, having left home upon any business, used to return, I always served him by giving him a seat, and adored him with respect.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: यदन्नं नाभिजानाति यद् भोज्यं नाभिनन्दति। भक्ष्यं वा यदि वा लेह्यं तत्सर्वे वर्जयाम्यहम्॥
en: I never ate food of any kind which was unknown to my husband and with which my husband was not pleased.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: कुटुम्बार्थं समानीतं यत्किञ्चित् कार्यमेव तु। प्रातरुत्थाय तत्सर्वं कारयामि करोमि च॥
en: Rising early in the morning I did and caused to be done whatever was brought about and required to be done for the sake of relatives and kinsmen.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: प्रवासं यदि मे याति भर्ता कार्येण केनचित्। मङ्गलैर्बहुभिर्यक्ता भवामि नियता तदा॥
en: When my husband leaves home for going to a distant place on any errand, I remained at home engaged in various kinds of auspicious deeds for blessing his enterprise.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: अञ्जनं रोचनां चैव स्नानं माल्यानुलेपनम्। प्रसाधनं च निष्क्रान्ते नाभिनन्दामि भर्तरि॥
en: During the absence of my husband I never use collyrium or ornaments; I never wash myself properly or use garlands and unguents or adorn my feet with lacdye or body with ornaments.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: नोत्थापयामि भर्तारं सुखसुप्तमहं सदा। आन्तरेष्वपि कार्येषु तेन तुष्यति मे मनः॥
en: When my husband sleeps in peace I never awake him even if important business wanted his attention. I was happy to sit by him lying asleep.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: नायासयामि भर्तारं कुटुम्बार्थेऽपि सर्वदा। गुप्तगुह्या सदा चास्मि सुसम्मृष्टनिवेशना॥
en: I never urged my husband to work hard for acquiring riches to support his family and relatives. I always kept secrets without giving them out to others. I used to always keep our premises clean.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: इमं धर्मपथं नारी पालयन्ती समाहिता। अरुन्धतीव नारीणां स्वर्गलोके महीयते॥
en: That woman who with rapt attention, follows her duty, receives profuse honors in the celestial region like a second Arundhati.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतदाख्याय सा देवी सुमनायै तपस्विनी। पतिधर्मे महाभागा जगामादर्शनं तदा॥
en: Bhishma said The illustrious and highly blessed Shandili, of pious conduct having said these words to Sumana on the subject of woman's duties towards her husband, disappeared there and then.

description: The conduct of good and chaste women
sn: यश्चेदं पाण्डवाख्यानं पठेत् पर्वणि पर्वणि। स देवलोकं सम्प्राप्य नन्दने स सुखी वसेत्॥
en: That man, O son of Pandu, who reads this discourse at every full moon and new moon, succeeds in acquiring the celestial region and enjoying great happiness in the bowers of Nandana.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच साम्नि चापि प्रादाने च ज्यायः किं भवतो मतम्। प्रब्रूहि भरतश्रेष्ठ यदत्र व्यतिरिच्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said In which is superior efficacy, conciliation or Gifts? Tell me, O chief of Bharata's race, which of these two is superior in efficacy.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: भीष्म उवाच साम्ना प्रसाद्यते कश्चिद् दानेन च तथा परः। पुरुषप्रकृतिं ज्ञात्वा तयोरेकतरं भजेत्॥
en: Bhishma said Some become pleased by Conciliation, while others are pleased by Gifts. Every man, according to his own nature, likes the one or the other.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: गुणांस्तु शृणु मे राजन् सान्त्वस्य भरतर्षभ। दारुणान्यपि भूतानि सान्त्वेनाराधयेद् यथा॥
en: Listen to me, O king, as I explain to you the merits of Conciliation, O chief of Bharata's race so that the most furious creatures may be cooled down by it.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। गृहीत्वा रक्षसा मुक्तो द्विजाति: कानेन यथा॥
en: Regarding it is cited the ancient narrative of how a Brahmana who had been seized in the forest by a Rakshasa, was freed.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: कश्चिद् वाग्बुद्धिसम्पन्नो ब्राह्मणो विजने वने। गृहीतः कृच्छ्रमापन्नो रक्षसा भक्षयिष्यता॥
en: A certain Brahmana, gifted with eloquence and intelligence fell into distress, for he was seized in a lone forest by a Rakshasa who wished to feed on him.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: स बुद्धिश्रुतिसम्पन्नस्तं दृष्ट्वातीव भीषणम्। सामैवास्मिन् प्रयुयुजे न मुमोह न विव्यथे॥
en: The Brahmana gifted as he was with understanding and learning was not at all moved. Without allowing himself to be stupefied at the sight of that terrible cannibal, he resolved to apply Conciliation and see its effect on the Rakshasa.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: रक्षस्तु वाचं सम्पूज्य प्रश्नं पप्रच्छ तं द्विजम्। मोक्ष्येसे ब्रूहि मे प्रश्न केनास्मि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Respectfully saluting the Brahmana with words, the Rakshasa put to him this question: You shall escape, but tell me why I am so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: मुहूर्तमथ संचिन्त्य ब्राह्मणस्तस्य रक्षसः। आभिर्गाथाभिरव्यग्रः प्रश्न प्रतिजगाद ह॥
en: Reflecting for a short time, the Brahmana accepted the question of the Rakshasa and replied in the following well spoken words.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच विदेशस्थो विलोकस्थो विना नूनं सुहृज्जनैः। विषयानतुलान् भुड्क्षे तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: The Brahman. said Living in a place distant from your house, moving in a sphere that is not your own, and deprived of the company of your friends and kinsmen, you are enjoying vast riches. It is, therefore, that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: नूनं मित्राणि ते रक्षः साधूपचरितान्यपि। स्वदोषादपरज्यन्ते तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Indeed, O Rakshasa, your friends thought welltreated by you are still not welldisposed towards you on account of their own vicious nature. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: धनैश्वर्याधिकाः स्तब्धास्त्वद्गुणैः परमावराः। अवजानन्ति नूनं त्वां तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: You are gifted with merit and wisdom and a wellcontrolled soul. Yet it is your lot to see others who have merit and wisdom honoured in preference to yourself. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: गुणवान् विगुणानन्यान् नूनं पश्यसि सत्कृतान्। प्राज्ञोऽप्राज्ञान् विनीतात्मा तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Persons having riches much greater than yours but inferior to you in merit, are indeed, disregarding you. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: अवृत्त्या क्लिश्यमानोऽपि वृत्त्युपायान् विगर्हयन्। माहात्म्याद् व्यथसे नूनं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Though distressed for want of the means of support yet you are actuated by the greatness of your mind to disregard such means as are open to you for getting your sustenance. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: सम्पीड्यात्मानमार्यत्वात् त्वया कश्चिदुपस्कृतः। जितं त्वां मन्यते साधो तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: On account of your virtuous nature you had deprived yourself for doing good to another. This person, O righteous Rakshasa, considers you deceived and defeated. It is for this that you are so pale and lean,

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: क्लिश्यमानान् विमार्गेषु कामक्रोधावृतात्मनः। मन्ये त्वं ध्यायसि जनांस्तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: I think you are grieving for those persons who with souls possessed by lust and anger, are suffering inisery in this world. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: प्रज्ञासम्भावितो नूनमप्रजैरुपसंहितः। हीयमानोऽसि दुर्वृत्तैस्तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Though wise, you are ridiculed by others who are entirely destitute of it. Persons of wicked conduct are vilifying you. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: नूनं मित्रमुखः शत्रुः कश्चिदार्यवदाचरन्। वञ्चयित्वा गतस्त्वां वै तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Indeed some enemy of yours, with a friendly tongue, coming to you behaved at first like a pious man and then has left you, beguiling you like a knave. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: प्रकाशार्थगतिर्नूनं रहस्यकुशलः कृती! तज्ज्ञैर्न पूज्यसे नूनं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: You are well conversant with the course of world's affairs. You are well skilled in all mysteries. You are gifted with power. Those who know you to be such do not yet respect and praise you. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: असत्स्वपि निविष्टेषु ब्रुवतो मुक्तसंशयम्। गुणास्ते न विराजन्ते तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Staying in the midst of bad men engaged together in some business, you had discoursed to them removing their doubts. Still they did not admit your superior merits. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: धनबुद्धिश्रुतैीन: केवलं तेजसान्वितः। महत् प्रार्थयसे नूनं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Indeed though destitute of riches and intelligence and Vedic learning you wish yet, with the help of your energy alonc, to accomplish something great. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: तष:प्रणिहितात्मानं मन्ये त्वारण्यकांक्षिणम्। बान्धवा नाभिनन्दन्ति तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: It appears that although you are resolved to practise severe austerities by retiring into the forest, yet your kinsmen are not favourably disposed towards this project of yours. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: इष्टभार्यस्य ते नूनं प्रातिवेश्यो महाधनः। युवा सुललित: कामी तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Some rich neighbour of yours, endued with youth and handsome features, covets your dear wife. It is for this that you aic so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: नूनमर्थवतां मध्ये तव वाक्यमनुत्तमम्। न भाति कालेऽभिहितं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: The words spoken by you, even when excellent in the midst of rich men, are not regarded by them as wise or well timed. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: दृढपूर्वं श्रुतं मूर्ख कुपितं हृदयप्रियम्। अनुनेतुं न शक्नोषि तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Some dear kinsman of yours, shorn of intelligence though repeatedly instructed in the scriptures has become angry. You have not been able to pacify him. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: नूनमांसजयित्वा त्वां कृत्ये कस्मिंश्चिदीप्सिते। कश्चिदर्थयते नित्यं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Indeed somebody, having first set you to the accomplishment of some object desirable to you, is now trying to deprive you of the fruit thereof. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: नूनं त्वां सुगुणैर्युक्तं पूजयानं सुहृध्रुवम्। ममार्थ इति जानीते तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Though possessed of excellent qualities and adored by all on that account, you are yet considered by your kinsmen as adored for their sakc and not for your own. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: अन्तर्गतमभिप्रायं नूनं नेच्छसि लज्जया। विवेक्तुं प्राप्तिशैथिल्यात् तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥२७
en: Indeed, through shame you are unable to give out some purpose in your heart, moved also by the inevitable delay that will take place in its accomplishment. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: नानाबुद्धिरुचो लोके मनुष्यान् नूनमिच्छसि। ग्रहीतुं स्वगुणैः सर्वांस्तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Indeed, you wish with the help of your intelligence, to control various persons with various kinds of understandings and inclinations. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: अविद्वान् भीरुरल्पार्थे विद्याविक्रमदानजम्। यशः प्रार्थयसे नूनं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Shorn of learning without courage, and without much riches you seek such fame as is won by knowledge and prowess and gifts. Indeed, it is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: चिराभिलषितं किंचित्फलमप्राप्तमेव ते। कृतमन्यैरपहतं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: You have not been able to get something which you have long been seeking for. Or, what you try to do is sought to be undone by soinebody else. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: नूनमात्मकृतं दोषमपश्यन् किंचिदात्मनः। अकारणेऽभिशप्तोऽसि तेनासि हरिण: कृशः॥
en: Indeed without being able to see any fault on your part, you have been cursed by somebody. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: साधून् गृहस्थान् दृष्ट्वा च तथा साधून् वनेचरान्। मुक्तांश्चावसथे सक्तांस्तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Having no wealth and accomplishments you try in vain to remove the grief of your friends and the sorrows of sorrowing men. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: सुहृदां दुःखमार्तानां न प्रमोक्ष्यसि हानिजम्। अलमर्थगुणैर्हीनं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Seeing virtuous persons living like householders, unrighteous persons living according to the forest mode, and liberated persons attached to domesticity and fixed abodes, you have become so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: धर्नामर्थ्य च काम्यं च काले चाभिहितं वचः। न प्रतीयन्ति ते नूनं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Indeed, your acts connected with Virtue. Profit, and Pleasure, as also the well-time words spoken by you do not produce fruit. It is for this that you are so pale and lean,

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: दत्तानकुशलैरर्थान् मनीषी संजिजीविषुः। प्राप्य वर्तयसे नूनं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Though gifted with wisdom, yet desirous of living, you live with wealth obtained by you in gift from somebody of evil conduct. It is for this that you are pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: पापान प्रवर्धतो दृष्ट्वा कल्याणानावसीदतः। ध्रुवं गर्हयसे नित्यं तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Seeing sinful persons multiplying on every side and virtue languishing, you are filled with grief. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: परस्परविरुद्धानां प्रियं नूनं चिकीर्षसि। सुहृदामुपरोधेन तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Urged by them you seek to please all your friends even when they are quarrelling and opposing one another. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: श्रोत्रियांश्च विकर्मस्थान् प्राज्ञांश्चाप्यजितेन्द्रियान्। मन्येऽनुध्यायसि जनांस्तेनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: Seeing persons gifted with Vedic learning engaged in improper deeds, and learned persons unable to keep their senses under control, you are filled with grief. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: एवं सम्पूजितं रक्षो विप्रं तं प्रत्यपूजयत्। सखायमकरोच्चैनं संयोज्याधैर्मुमोच ह॥
en: Thus praised the Rakshasa adored that learned Brahmana in return, and making him his friend and bestowing sufficient riches upon himn in gift, sent him away. Seeing persons gifted with Vedic learning engaged in improper deeds, and learned persons unable to keep their senses under control, you are filled with grief. It is for this that you are so pale and lean.

description: The efficacy of conciliation and gifts
sn: एवं सम्पूजितं रक्षो विप्रं तं प्रत्यपूजयत्। सखायमकरोच्चैनं संयोज्याधैर्मुमोच ह॥
en: Thus praised the Rakshasa adored that learned Brahmana in return, and making him his friend and bestowing sufficient riches upon himn in gift, sent him away.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच जन्म मानुष्यकं प्राप्य कर्मक्षेत्रं सुदुर्लभम्। श्रेयोऽर्थिना दरिद्रेण किं कर्तव्यं पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, how should a poor inan, desirous of achieving his own behoof, act after having acquired the status of humanity and come into this region of acts that is so difficult to acquire.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: दानानामुत्तमं यच्च देयं यच्च यथा यथा। मान्यान् पूज्यांश्च गाङ्गेय रहस्यं वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Tell me also what is the best of all gifts, and what should be given under what circumstances? Tell me, O son of Ganga, who are truly worthy of honour and adoration. You should describe these mysteries to us.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं पृष्टो नरेन्द्रेण पाण्डवेन यशस्विना। धर्माणां परमं गुह्यं भीष्मः प्रोवाच पार्थिवम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus accosted by that famous king, viz., the son of Pandu, Bhishma explained to that king these great mysteries about duty.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणुष्वावहितो राजन् धर्मगुह्यानि भारत। यथा हि भगवान् व्यासः पुरा कथितवान् मयि॥
en: Bhishma said Listen to me with rapt attention, O king, as I explain to you, O Bharata, these mysteries of duties as the holy Vyasa had explained them to me formerly.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: देवगुह्यमिदं राजन् यमेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। नियमस्थेन युक्तेन तपसो महतः फलम्॥
en: This subject is a mystery to the very celestials, O king. Yama of pure deeds, with the help of vows well observed and Yoga meditation, had acquired the knowledge of these mysteries as the high fruits of his penances.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: येन यः प्रीयते देवः प्रीयन्ते पितरस्तथा। ऋषयः प्रमथा: श्रीश्च चित्रगुप्तो दिशां गजाः॥ ऋषिधर्मः स्मृतो यत्र सरहस्यो महाफलः। महादानफलं चैव सर्वयज्ञफलं तथा॥ यश्चैतदेवं जानीयाज्ज्ञात्वा वा कुरुतेऽनघ। सदोषोऽदोषवांश्चेह तैर्गुणैः सह युज्यते॥
en: What pleases deity, what pleases the departed manes, the Rishis, the companions of Mahadeva, the goddess Shri Chitragupta, and the powerful Elephants which rule the cardinal points of the compass, what forms the religion of the Rishis, the religion viz., which has many mysteries and which yields high fruits, the merits of what are called great gifts, and the merits of all the sacrifices he who knows these, O sinless one, and knowing acts according to his knowledge, becomes freed from stains if he has stains and acquires the inerits indicated.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: दशसूनासमं चक्रं दशचक्रसमो ध्वजः। दशध्वजसमा वेश्या दशवेश्यासमो नृपः॥
en: One oilman is equal to ten butchers. Equal to ten oilmen is one drinker of alcohol. Equal to ten drinkers of alcohol is one harlot. Equal to ten harlots is a single king.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: अर्धेनैतानि सर्वाणि नृपतिः कथ्यतेऽधिकः। त्रिवर्गसहितं शास्त्रं पवित्रं पुण्यलक्षणम्॥ धर्मव्याकरणं पुण्यं रहस्यश्रवणं महत्। श्रोतव्यं धर्मसंयुक्तं विहितं त्रिदशैः स्वयम्॥
en: A great king is said to be equal to half of these all. Hence, one should not accept gifts from these. On the other hand, one should attend to the science, which is sacred and which has virtue for its marks, of the threefold objects of life. Amongst these, Wealth and Pleasure are naturally attractive. Hence one should, with rapt attention, listen to the sacred expositions of Religion, for the fruits of listening to the mysteries of Religion are very great. One should certainly hear every subject bearing on Religion as ordained by the celestials themselves.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: पितॄणां यत्र गुह्यानि प्रोच्यन्ते श्राद्धकर्मणि। देवतानां च सर्वेषां रहस्यं कथ्यतेऽखिलम्॥
en: In it is contained the ritual about the Shraddha in which have been declared the mysteries of the departed Manes. The mysteries about the deities have also been explained there.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: ऋषिधर्मः स्मृतो यत्र सरहस्यो महाफलः। महायज्ञफलं चैव सर्वदानफलं तथा॥
en: It contains the duties and practices, productive of great merit, of the Rishis also, together with the mysteries attaching to them. It contains an exposition of the merits of great sacrifices and all kinds of gifts.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: ये पठन्ति सदा मा येषां चैवोपतिष्ठति। श्रुत्वा च फलमाचष्टे स्वयं नारायणः प्रभुः॥
en: Those men who always read the scriptures about these subjects, those who bear them properly in their mind, and he who, having listened to them, follows them in practice, are all considered to be as holy and sinless as the powerful Narayana himself.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: गवां फलं तीर्थफलं यज्ञानां चैव यत् फलम्। एतत् फलमवाप्नोति यो नरोऽतिथिपूजकः॥
en: The merits of the gift of kine, those that belong to the performance of ablutions in sacred waters, those that are acquired by the celebration of sacrifices, all these are acquired by that man who treats guests with respect.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: श्रोतारः श्रद्दधानाश्च येषां शुद्ध च मानसम्। तेषां व्यक्त जिता लोकाः श्रद्दधनेन साधुना॥ मुच्यते किल्बिषाच्चैच न सा पापेन लिप्यते। धर्मे च लभते नित्यं प्रेत्य लोकगतो नरः॥
en: They who listen to these scriptures, they who are gifted with faith and they who have a pure heart, it is well known conquer many regions of felicity. Those pious men who are gifted with faith, become cleansed of all since and no sin can touch them. Such men always increase in virtue and succeed in attaining to the celestial region.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य देवदूतो यदृच्छया। स्थितो ह्यन्तर्हितो भूत्वा पर्यभाषत वासवम्॥
en: Once on a time a celestial messenger, coming to the court of Indra of his own accord, but remaining invisible, addressed the king of the deities in these words:

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: यौ तौ कामगुणोपेतावश्विनौ भिषजां वरौ। आज्ञयाहं तयोः प्राप्तः सनरान् पितृदैवतान्॥
en: At the command of Ashvini Kumars (the celestial physicians) and who are gifted with every desirable quality, I have come to this place where I see human beings the departed Manes and the celestials assembled together.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: कस्माद्धि मैथुनं श्राद्धे दातुर्भोक्तुश्च वर्जितम्। किमर्थं च त्रयः पिण्डाः प्रविभक्ताः पृथक् पृथक्।।
en: Why, indeed, is sexual intercourse interdicted for the man who performs a Shraddha and for him also who eats at a Shraddha? Why are three rice balls offered separately at a Shraddha?

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: प्रथमः कस्य दातव्यो मध्यमः क्व च गच्छति। उत्तरश्च स्मृतः कस्य एतदिच्छागि वेदितुम्॥
en: To whom should the first of those balls be offered? To whom should the second one be offered? And whose has it been said is the third or the remaining one? I wish to know all this!

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: श्रद्दधनेन दूतेन भाषितं धर्मसंहितम्। पूर्वस्थास्त्रिदशाः सर्वे पितरः पूज्य खेचरम्॥
en: After the celestial messenger had said these words connected with virtue and duty, the celestials who were seated towards the east and the departed Manes also, praising that ranger of the sky, began as follows:

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: पितर ऊचुः स्वागतं तेऽस्तु भद्रं ते श्रूयतां खेचरोत्तम। गूढार्थः परमः प्रश्नो भवता समुदीरितः॥
en: The Pitris said Welcome are you and blessings upon you! Do you listen, O best of all rangers of the sky! The question you have put is a high one and fraught with deep import.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: श्राद्धं दत्त्वा च भुक्त्वा च पुरुषो यःस्त्रियं व्रजेत्। पितरस्तस्य तं मासं तस्मिन् रेतसि शेरते।॥
en: The departed Manes of that man who indulges in sexual intercourse on the day he performs a Shraddha or eats at a Shraddha, have to lie for a whole month on his vital seed.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: प्रविभागं तु पिण्डानां प्रवक्ष्याम्यनुपूर्वशः। पिण्डो ह्यधस्ताद् गच्छंस्तु अप आविश्य भावयेत्।।
en: We shall explain the classification of the riccballs offered at a Shraddha, The first ricehall should be thought of as being thrown into the waters.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: पिण्डं तु मध्यमं तत्र पत्नी त्वेका समश्नुते। पिण्डस्तृतीयो यस्तेषां तं दद्याज्जातवेदसि॥
en: The second ball should be given to one of the wives to eat. The third ball should be thrown into the burning fire.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: एष श्राद्धविधिः प्रोक्तो यथा धर्मो न लुप्यते। पितरस्तस्य तुष्यन्ति प्रहृष्टमनसः सदा॥ प्रजा विवर्धते चास्य अक्षयं चोपतिष्ठति।
en: This is the ordinance about the Shraddha. This is the ordinance of the rites of religion. The Pitris of that man who acts according to this ordinance become pleased with him and remain always cheerful. The progeny of such a man increases and he always commands endless riches.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: देवदूत उवाच आनुपूर्वेण पिण्डानां प्रविभागः पृथक् पृथक्॥ पितॄणां त्रिषु सर्वेषां निरुक्तं कथितं त्वया।
en: The Celestial Messenger said You have explained the division of the ricc balls and their consignment one after another to the three, together with the reasons thereof.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: एक:समुद्धृतः पिण्डो ह्यधस्तात् कस्य गच्छति॥ कं वा प्रीणयते देवं कथं तारयते पितॄन।
en: Whom does that riceball which is thrown into the waters reach? How does it , by being so thrown please the deities, and how does it rescue the departed Manes?

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: मध्यमं तु तदा पत्नी भुङ्क्तेऽनुज्ञातमेव हि॥ किमर्थं पितरस्तस्य कव्यमेव च भुञ्जते।
en: The second ball is eaten by the wife. That has been laid down in the ordinance. How do the Pitris of that man become the eaters thereof?

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: अत्र यस्त्वन्तिमः पिण्डो गच्छते जातवेदसम्॥ भवते का गतिस्तस्य कं वा समनुगच्छति।
en: The last ball goes into the burning fire. How does that ball succeed in finding its way to you, or who is he to whom it goes?

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं पिण्डेषु त्रिषु श गतिः॥ फलं वृत्तिं च मार्गं च यश्चैनं प्रतिपद्यते।
en: I wish to hear this, that is, what are the ends attained by the balls offered at Shraddhas when thus disposed of by being thrown into the waters, given to the wife, and thrown into the burning fire.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: पितरः ऊचुः सुमहानेष प्रश्नो वै यस्त्वया समुदीरितः॥ रहस्यमद्भुतं चापि पृष्टाः स्म गगनेचर।
en: The Pitris said The question which you have asked is of deep import. It involves a mystery and is wonderful. We have been highly pleased with you, O rarger of the sky.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: एतदेव प्रशसंन्ति देवाश्च मुनयस्तथा॥ तेऽप्येवं नाभिजानन्ति पितृकार्यविनिश्चयम्।
en: The very celestials and the Munis applaud acts done in honour of the departed Manes. Even they do not know what the certain conclusions are of the ordinances about the acts done in honour of the Pitris.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: वर्जयित्वा महात्मानं चिरजीविनमुत्तमम्॥ पितृभक्तस्तु यो विप्रो वरलब्धो महायशाः।
en: Excepting the great, immortal and excellent Markandeya, that learned Brahmana of great fame, who is ever devoted to the Pitris, none amongst them is conversant with the mysteries of the ordinances about the Pitris.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: त्रयाणामपि पिण्डानां श्रुत्वा भगवतो गतिम्॥ देवदूतेन यः पृष्टः श्राद्धस्य विधिनिश्चयः।
en: Having heard from the holy Vyasa what the end is of the three riceballs offered at the Shraddha, as explained by the Pitris themselves in reply to the question of the celestial messenger, I shall explain the same to you. Do you hear, o king, what the conclusions are about the ordinances about the Shraddha.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: गतिं त्रयाणां पिण्डानां शृणुष्वावहितो मम॥ अपो गच्छति यो ह्यत्र शशिनं ह्येष प्रीणयेत्।
en: Listen with attention, O Bharata, to me as I explain what the end is of the three rice balls. That rice ball which goes into water is considered as pleasing the deity of the Moon.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: शशी प्रीणयते देवान् पितश्चैव महामते॥ भुङ्क्ते तु पत्नी यं चैषामनुज्ञाता तु मध्यमम्।
en: That deity being pleased, O you of great intelligence gratifies in return the other deities and the Pitris also with them. It has bean laid down that the second riceball should be eaten by the wife.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: पुत्रकामाय पुत्रं तु प्रयच्छन्ति पितामहाः॥ पिण्डो दीयते तन्निबोध मे।
en: The Pitris, who always wish for progeny, bestow children on the woman of the house. Listen now to me as I tell you what becomes of the rice ball that is thrown into the burning fire.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: पितरस्तेन तृष्यन्ति प्रीताः कामान् दिशन्ति च॥ एतत् ते कथितं सर्वे त्रिषु पिण्डेषु या गतिः।
en: With that ball the Pitris are pleased, and as the result thereof, grant the fruition of all desires to the person offering it. I have thus told you everything about the end of the three riceballs offered at the Shraddha and consigned to the three (viz. water, the spouse and the fire.)

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: ऋत्विग्यो यजमानस्य पितृत्वमनुगच्छति॥ हव्यवाहे तु यः तस्मिन्नहनि मन्यन्ते परिहार्ये हि मैथुनम्।
en: That Brahmana who becomes the priest at a Shraddha forins himself by that deed, the Pitri of the person performing ine Shraddha. Hence he should abstain that day from sexual intercourse with even his own wife.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: शुचिना तु सदा श्राद्धं भोक्तव्य खेचरोत्तम॥ ये मया कथिता दोषास्ते तथा स्युर्न चान्यथा।
en: O best of all rangers of the sky, the man who eats at a Shraddha should remain pure for that day. By acting otherwise one surely commits the sin I have indicated. It cannot be otherwise.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: तस्मात् स्नातः शुचिः क्षान्तः श्राद्धंभुञ्जीत वै द्विजः।। प्रजा विवर्धते चास्य यश्चैवं सम्प्रयच्छति।
en: Hence, the Brahmana who is invited to a Shraddha for eating the offerings should eat them after purifying himself by a bath and remain pious for that day by abstaining form every kind of injury or evil. The progeny of such a person multiplies and he also who feeds him gets the same reward.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो विद्युत्प्रभो नाम ऋषिराह महातपाः॥ आदित्यतेजसा तस्य तुल्यं रूपं प्रकाशते। स च धर्मरहस्यानि श्रुत्वा शक्रमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhishma said After the Pitris had said so, a Rishi of austere penances, named Vidyutprabha, whose form was effulgent like the Sun spoke.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: तिर्यग्योनिगतान् सत्त्वान् मा हिंसन्ति मोहिताः। कीटान् पिपीलिकान् सर्पान् मेषान् समृगपक्षिणः।। किल्बिषं सुबहु प्राप्ताः किंस्विदेषां प्रतिक्रिया। ततो देवगणाः सर्वे ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः॥
en: Having heard those mysteries of religion as explained by che Pitris, he addressed Shakra, saying, Stupefied by folly, men kill numerous creatures born in the intermediate orders, such as worms, ants, snakes, sheep, deer and birds. They commit a great sin by these acts. What, however, is the remedy?

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: पितरश्च महाभागाः पूजयन्ति स्म तं मुनिम्।
en: When this question was asked, all the gods and Rishis having penances for wealth and the highly blessed Pitris, praised that ascetic.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: शक्र उवाच कुरुक्षेत्रं गयां गङ्गां प्रभासं पुष्कराणि च॥ एतानि मनसा ध्यात्वा अवगाहेत् ततो जलम्। तथा मुच्यति पापेन राहुणा चन्द्रमा यथा॥
en: Shakra said Thinking in one's mind of Kurukshetra and Gaya and Ganga and Prabhasa and the lakes of Pushkara, one should dip his head in a piece of water.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: त्र्यहं स्नातंः स भवति निराहारश्च वर्तते। स्पृशते यो गवां पृष्ठं बालधिं च नमस्यति॥
en: By so doing he becomes purged off of all his sins like the Moon freed from Rahu. He should thus bathe for three days successively and then fast for every day.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: ततो विद्युत्प्रभो वाक्यमभ्यभाषत वासवम्। अयं सूक्ष्मतरो धर्मस्तं निबोध शतक्रतो॥
en: Besides this, he should touch (After bathing) the back of a cow and bow his head to her tail. Vidutprabha, after this, once more addressing Vasava said, I shall describe a rite that is more subtle. Listen to me, O you of a hundred sacrifices.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: घृष्टो वटकषायेण अनुलिप्तः प्रियंगुणा। क्षीरेण षष्टिकान् भुक्त्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: Rubbed with the astringent powder of the hanging roots of the banian and anointed with the oil of Priyangu, one should eat the Shashtika paddy mixed with milk. By so doing he becomes purged off all his sins.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: श्रूयतां चापरं गृह्यं रहस्यमृषिचिन्तितम्। श्रुतं मे भाषमाणस्य स्थाणोः स्थाने बृहस्पतेः॥
en: Listen now to another mystery unknown to many but which was discovered by the Rishis with the help of meditation. I heard it from Brihaspati while he recited it before Mahadeva.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: रुद्रेण सह देवेश तन्निबोध शचीपते। पर्वतारोहणं कृत्वा एकपादो विभावसुम्॥ निरीक्षेत निराहार उर्ध्वबाहुः कृताञ्जलिः। तपसा महता युक्त उपवासफलं लभेत्॥
en: O king of the celestials do you hear it with Rudra in your company, O lord of Shachi. If a person, ascending a mountain stands there on one foot, with arms upraised and joined together and abstaining from food, looks at a burning fire, he acquires the merits of severe penances and obtains the rewards of fasts.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: रश्मिभिस्तापितोऽर्कस्य सर्वपापमपोहति। ग्रीष्मकालेऽथ वा शीते एवं पापमपोहति॥
en: Heated by the rays of the Sun, he becomes purged off all his sins. One who acts thus in both the summer and the winter seasons becomes freed from every sin.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: ततः पापत् प्रमुक्तस्य द्युतिर्भवति शाश्वती। तेजसा सूर्यवद् दीप्तो भ्राजते सोमवत् पुनः॥
en: Purged off of every sin one acquires a splendour of complexion for all time. Such a man burns with energy like the Sun or shines in beauty like the Moon.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: मध्ये त्रिदशवर्गस्य देवराजः शतक्रतुः। उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं बृहस्पतिमनुत्तमम्॥
en: After this, the king of the celestials viz., he of a hundred sacrifices, seated in the midst of the gods then sweetly addressed Brihaspati, with these excellent words:

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: धर्मगुह्यं तु भगवन् मानुषाणां सुखावहम्। सरहस्याश्च ये दोषास्तान् यथावदुदीरय॥
en: O Holy One, do you describe those mysteries of religion which are fraught with happiness to human beings, and what the faults are which they commit, together with the mysteries of them.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: बृहस्पति रुवाच प्रतिमेहन्ति ये सूर्यमनिलं द्विषते च ये। हव्यवाहे प्रदीप्ते च समिधं ये न जुह्वति॥ बालवत्सां च ये धेनुं दुहन्ति क्षीरकारणात्। तेषां दोषान् प्रवक्ष्यामि तान् निबोध शचीपते॥
en: Brihaspati said They who pass urine, facing the sun, they who do not show respect for the wind, they who do not pour libations on the burning fire, they who milk a cow whose calf is very young, actuated by the desire of obtaining from her as much milk as possible, commit many sins. I shall describe what those faults are, O lord of Shachi, Do you hear me.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: भानुमाननिलश्चैव हव्यवाहश्च वासव। लोकानां मातरश्चैव गावः सृष्टाः स्वयम्भुवा॥ लोकांस्तारयितुं शक्ता मत्र्येष्वेतेषु देवताः। सर्वे भवन्तः शृण्वन्तु एकैकं धर्मनिश्चयम्॥
en: The Sun, Wind, the carrier of sacrificial oblations, O Vasava, and kine who are the mothers of all creatures, were created by the self-create himself, for rescuing all the worlds, O Shakra. These are the deities of human beings. Listen all the conclusions of religion.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: वर्षाणि षडशीति तु दुर्वत्ताः कुलपांसनाः। स्त्रियः सर्वाश्च दुर्वृत्ता:प्रतिमेहन्ति या रविम्॥
en: Those wicked men and wicked women who pass urine facing the Sun, live in great infamy for eighty six years.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: अनिलद्वेषिणः शक्र गर्भस्था च्यवते प्रजा। हव्यवाहस्य दीप्तस्य समिधं ये न जुह्वति।॥
en: That man, O Shakra, who cherishes no respect for the wind, gets children that come out prematurely from the womb of his wife. These men who do not pour libations on the burning fire, find that the fire, when they do light it up for such rites as they wish to perform refuses to eat their libations.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: अग्निकार्येषु वै तेषां हव्यं नाश्नाति पावकः। क्षीरं तु बालवत्सानां ये पिबन्तीह मानवाः॥
en: Those men who drink the milk of kire whose calves are very young, never get children for perpetuating their races.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: न तेषां क्षीरपाः केचिज्जायन्ते कुलवर्धनाः। प्रजाक्षयेण युज्यन्ते कुलवंशक्षयेण च॥
en: Such men see their children die and their families shrink. These are consequences of the acts referred to as observed by twice born persons, venerable for age in their respective families.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: एवमेतत् पुरा दृष्टं कुलवृद्धौर्द्विजातिभिः। तस्माद् वानि वानि कार्यं कार्यं च नित्यशः।।
en: Hence, one should always avoid that which has been interdicted and do only that which has been directed to be done, if one is desirous of securing his prosperity. This that I say to you is very true.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: भूतिकामेन म]न सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते। ततः सर्वा महाभाग देवताः समरुद्गणाः॥ ऋषयश्च महाभागाः पृच्छन्ति स्म पितूंस्ततः। पितरः केन तुष्यन्ति मर्त्यानामल्पचेतसाम्॥ अक्षयं च कथं दानं भवेच्चैवोर्ध्वदेहिकम्।
en: After the celestial preceptor had said this the highly blessed celestials, with the Maruts, and the highly blessed Rishis questioned the departed Manes saying, You Pitris with what acts of human beings, who are generally gifted with little understandings, do you become pleased? What gifts made in course of such rites as are performed for improving the position of deceased persons in the other world become inexhaustible in efficacy?

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: आनृण्यं वा कथं मा गच्छेयुः केन कर्मणा॥ एतदिच्छामहे श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि नः।
en: By doing what acts can men become freed from the debt they owe to their ancestors? We wish to hear this. Great is our curiosity.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: पितर ऊचुः न्यायतो वै महाभागाः संशयः समुदाहृतः॥ श्रूयतां येन तुष्यामो मानां साधुकर्मणाम्।
en: The Pitris said Yoy highly blessed ones, the doubt existing in your minds has been properly explained. Listen as we describe the deeds of righteous men with which we become pleased.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: नीलपण्डप्रमोक्षेण अमावास्यां तिलोदकैः :॥ वर्षासु दीपकैश्चैव पितॄणामनृणो भवेत्।
en: Blue hued bulls should be liberated. Gifts should be made to us, on the day of the new moon of sesame seeds and water. In the season of rains, lamps should be lighted. By these decds of men they can free themselves from the debt they owe to their ancestors.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: अक्षयं निळलीकं च दानमेतन्महाफलम्॥ अस्माकं परितोषश्च अक्षयः परिकीर्त्यते।
en: Such gifts never become vain. On the other hand they yield great and endless fruits. The gratification we derive from them is considered to be inexhaustible.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: श्रद्दधानाश्च ये मर्त्या आहरिष्यन्ति संततिम्॥ दुर्गात् ते तारयिष्यन्ति नरकात् प्रपितामहान्।
en: Those men who gifted with faith, beget offspring, rescue their deceased ancestors from imiserable Hell.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: पितॄणां भाषितं श्रुत्वा हृष्टरोमा तपोधनः॥ वृद्धगार्यो महातेजास्तानेवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। के गुणा नीलपण्डस्य प्रमुक्तस्य तपोधनाः॥ वर्षासु दीपदानेन तथैव च तिलोदकैः।
en: Hearing these words of the Pitris, Vriddha Gargya, endued with penances and high energy, became filled with wonder so that the hair on his body stood erect. Addressing them he said, Ye having penances for wealth, tell us what the merits are of setting free Bulls having blue complexions. What merits, again, are of the gifts of lamps in the season of rains and the gift of water with sesame seeds?

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: पितर ऊचुः नीलषण्डस्य लाङ्गुलं तोयमभ्युद्धरेद् यदि॥ षष्टिं वर्षसहस्राणि पितरस्तेन तर्पिता:।
en: The Pitris said If a bull of blue complexion upon being liberated raises a (small) quantity of water with its tail the Pitris become pleased with that water for full sixty thousand years.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: यस्तु शृङ्गगतं पदं कूलादूद्धृत्य तिष्ठति।॥ पितरस्तेन गच्छन्ति सोमलोकमसंशयम्।
en: The mud such a bull raises with its horns from the banks (of a river or lake) succeeds, forsooth, in sending the Pitris to the region of Soma.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: वर्षासु दीपदानेन शशिवच्छोभते नरः॥ तमोरूपं न तस्यास्ति दीपकं यः प्रयच्छति।
en: By giving lamps in the season of rains one shines with effulgence like Soma himself. The man who gives lamps is never subject to the quality of Darkness.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: अमावास्यां तु ये माः प्रयच्छन्ति तिलोदकम्॥ पात्रमौदुम्बरं गृह्य मधुमिश्रं तपोधन। कृतं भवति तैः श्राद्धं सरहस्यं यथार्थवत्॥ हृष्टपुष्टमनास्तेषां प्रजा भवति नित्यदा।
en: Those men who make gifts on the day of the new moon of sesame seeds and water, mixed with honey and using a vessel of copper, O you having penances for wealth, are considered as duly performing a Shraddha with all its mysteries. These men get children of sound health and cheerful minds.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: कुलवंशस्य वृद्धिस्तु पिण्डदस्य फलं भवेत्। श्रद्दधानस्तु यः कुर्यात् पितॄणामनृणो भवेत्॥
en: The merit acquired by the giver of the Pinda takes the forin of the growth of his family. Indeed, he who performs these acts with faith, becomes freed from the debt he owes to the ancestors.

description: The mystery of duties and gifts
sn: एवमेव समुद्विष्टः श्राद्धकालक्रमस्तथा। विधिः पात्रं फलं चैव यथावदनुकीर्तिमम्॥
en: Thus have been laid down the proper time for the performance of the Shraddha, the ordinances about the rites to be observed the proper person that should be fed at the Shraddha, and the merits that belong to it. I have described everything to you in due orders.

sn: भीष्म उवाच केन ते च भवेत् प्रीतिः कथं तुष्टिं तु गच्छसि। इति पृष्टः सुरेन्द्रेण प्रोवाच हरिरीश्वरः॥
en: Bhishma said The king of the celestials viz., Indra after the Pitris had ceased to speak addressed the powerful Hari, saying, O Lord what are those deeds which please you? How indeed do men succeed in pleasing you?

sn: विष्णु उवाच ब्राह्मणानां परीवादो मम विद्वेषणं महत्। ब्राह्मणैः पूजितैर्नित्यं पूजितोऽहं न संशयः॥
en: Vishnu said That which I greatly hate, is the detraction of Brahmanas. Forsooth, if the Brahmanas are adored I consider myself adored.

sn: नित्याभिवाद्या विप्रेन्द्रा भुक्त्वा पादौ तथात्मनः। तेषां तुष्यामि मानां यश्चक्रे च बलिं हरेत्॥
en: All superior Brahmanas should always be saluted with respect, after feeding them with hospitality. One should respect his own feet also (in the evening). I am pleased with men who act thus, as also with those who worship and make offerings to the whirl that is noticeable on cowdung.

sn: वामनं ब्राह्मणं दृष्ट्वा वराहं च जलोत्थिम्। उद्धृतां धरणीं चैव मूर्धा धारयते तु यः॥ न तेषामशुभं किंचित् कल्मषं चोपपद्यते। अश्वत्यं रोचनां गां च पूजयेद् यो नरः सदा॥ पूजितं च जगत् तेन सदेवासुरमानुषम्। तेन रूपेण तेषां च पूजां गृह्णामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: They who see a Brahmana that is a dwarf in stature, or a boar that has just risen from water and that bears on his head a quantity of mud taken up from the bank, have never to meet with any evil, They become freed from every sin. That man who adores every day the Ashvattha (Ficus religiosa) and the substance called Gorochana and the cow, is considered as adoring the whole universe with the celestials and Asuras and human beings. Indeed, staying within these, I accept in my own form the adoration that is offered to them.

sn: पूजा ममैषा नास्त्यन्या यावल्लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः। अन्यथा हि वृथा माः पूजयन्त्यल्पवुद्धयः॥ नाहं तत् प्रतिगृह्णामि न सा तुष्टिकरी मम॥
en: The worship that is offered to these is the adoration offered to me. This has been so as long as the worlds have been created. Those little witted men who adore me in a different way, worship me in vain, for the worship of that kind I never accept. Indeed, the worship of other kind is not at all pleasing to me.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच चक्रं पादौ वराहं च ब्राह्मणं चापि वामनम्। उद्धृतां धरणीं चैव किमर्थं त्वं प्रशंससि॥
en: Indra said Why do you speak highly of the circular marks on cowdung, the feet, the boar, the Brahmana that is a dwarf in stature and mud raised up from the soil?

sn: भवान् सृजति भूतानि भवान् संहरति प्रजाः। प्रकृतिः सर्वभूतानां समानां सनातनी॥
en: It is you who create all creatures and it is you who destroy them. You are the eternal nature of all transitory things.

sn: भीष्म उवाच सम्प्रहस्य ततो विष्णुरिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। चक्रेण निहता दैत्याः पद्भ्यां क्रान्ता वसुन्धरा॥
en: Bhishma said Hearing these words of Indra, Vishnu smiled a little and then said, It was with my circular disc that the Daityas were killed. It was with my two feet that the world was covered.

sn: वाराहं रूपमास्थाय हिरण्याक्षो निपातितः। वामनं रूपमास्थाय जितो राजा मया बलिः॥
en: Assuming the forin of a boar I killed Hiranyaksha. Assuming the form of a dwarf I conquered king Bali.

sn: परितुष्टो भवाम्येवं मानुषाणां महात्मनाम्। तन्मां ये पूजयिष्यन्ति नास्ति तेषां पराभवः॥
en: Those great men who adore these, gratify me. Indeed, they who worship me in these forms never meet with dcfeat.

sn: अपि वा ब्राह्मणं दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मचारिणमागतम्। ब्राह्मणाग्र्याहुतिं दत्त्वा अमृतं तस्य भोजनम्॥
en: If one, seeing a celibate a Brahmana arrived at one's house, offers to him the first portion of his food that belongs as of right to a Brahmana, and eats the residue he is considered as eating Amrita.

sn: ऐन्द्रीं संध्यामुपासित्वा आदित्याभिमुखः स्थितः। सर्वतीर्थेषु स स्नातो मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः॥
en: If one, after worshipping the moon-twilight, stands with face directed towards the Sun, he reaps the merit that belongs to the performance of ablutions in all Tirthas and becomes purged off of all sins.

sn: एतद् वः कथितं गुह्यमखिलेन तपोधनाः। संशयं पृच्छमानानां किं भूयः कथयाम्यहम्॥
en: You Rishis having penances for wealth, I have told you in detail what forms a great mystery. On what else shall I discourse to you? Tell me your doubts!

sn: बलदेव उवाच श्रूयतां परमं गुह्यं मानुषाणां सुखावहम्। अजानन्तो यदबुधाः क्लिश्यन्ते भूतपीडिताः॥
en: Baladeva said Listen now to another great mystery that yields happiness to men. Unacquainted with it, ignorant persons suffer much distress from other creatures.

sn: कल्य उत्थाय यो मर्त्यः स्पृशेद् गां वै घृतं दधि। सर्षपं च प्रियर्थं च कल्मषात् प्रतिमुच्यते॥
en: That man who rising early dawn, touches a cow, clarified butter and curds, as also mustard seeds and the larger variety thereof called Priyangu, becomes purged off of all his sins.

sn: भूतानि चैव सर्वाणि अग्रतः पृष्ठतोऽपि वा। उच्छिष्टं वापि च्छिद्रेषु वर्जयन्ति तपोधनाः॥
en: As regards Rishis having penances for wealth they always avoid all creatures both before and behind, as also all that is impure, while performing Shraddhas.

sn: देवा ऊचुः प्रगृह्यौदुम्बरं पात्रं तोयपूर्णमुदङ्मुखः। उपवासं तु गृह्णीयाद् यद् वा संकल्पयेद् व्रतम्॥ देवतास्तस्य तुष्यन्ति कामिकं चापि सिध्यति। अन्यथा हि वृथा मर्त्याः कुर्वते स्वल्पबुद्धयः॥
en: The Deities said If a person, taking a vessel of copper filling it with water and facing the East determines upon a fast or the observance of a particular vow, the celestials become pleased with him and all his wishes become crowned with fortune. By observing fasts or vows in any other way, littlewitted man gain nothing.

sn: उपवासे बलौ चापि ताम्रपात्रं विशिष्यते। बलिर्भिक्षा तथाऱ्या च पितॄणां च तिलोदकम्॥ ताम्रपात्रेण दातव्यमन्यथाऽहल्पफलं भवेत्। गुह्यमेतत् समुद्दिष्टं यथा तुष्यन्ति देवताः॥
en: In uttering the resolution about the observance of fasts and in making offerings to the celestials, the use of a vessel of copper is preferable. In presenting the offerings to the celestials in (giving and accepting) alms, in presenting the ingredients of the Argha, and in offering oblations of water mixed with sesame seeds to the departed Manes, a vessel of copper should be used. By doing these acts in any other way, one acquires little merit. These mysteries have been laid down about how the deities are pleased.

sn: धर्म उवाच राजपौरुषिके विप्रे घाण्टिके परिचारिके। गोरक्षके वाणिजके तथा कारुकुशीलवे॥ मित्रदुह्यनधीयाने यश्च स्याद् वृषलीपतिः। एतेषु दैवं पित्र्यं वा न देयं स्यात् कथंचन॥
en: Dharma said The offerings made in all rites in honour of the celestials and in those in honour of the departed Manes, should never be given away to a Brahmana who has accepted service under the king or who rings the bell or attends to minor duties in acts of worship or at Shraddhas, or who keeps kine or who drives a trade, or who follows some art as a profession, or who is an actor, or who quarrels with friends or who is destitute of Vedic studies, or who marries a Shudra woman.

sn: पिण्डदास्तस्य हीयन्ते न च प्रीणाति वै पितॄन्। अतिथिर्यस्य भग्नाशो गृहात् प्रतिनिवर्तते॥
en: The performer of the Shraddha who gives away such offerings to such a Brahmana, losses prosperity and multiplies not his race. He fails, again to gratify his Pitris by doing such an act.

sn: पितरस्तस्य देवाश्च अग्नयश्च तथैव हि। निराशा: प्रतिगच्छन्ति अतिथेरप्रतिग्रहात्॥
en: From the house of that person whence a guest returns unsatisfied, the Pitris, the deities, and the sacred fires, all return disappointed on account of such treatment of the guest.

sn: स्त्रीनैर्गोनैः कृतघ्नैश्च ब्रह्मघ्नैर्गुरुतल्पगेः। तुल्यदोषो भवत्येभिर्यस्यातिथिरनर्चितः॥
en: That man who does not perform the duties of hospitality towards the guest arrived at his house comes to be considered as equally sinful with those who are slayers of women or of kine, who are ungrateful towards benefactors, who are slayers of Brahmanas, or who are violators of the beds of their preceptors.

sn: अग्नि रुवाच पादमुद्यम्य यो मर्त्यः स्पृशेद् गाश्च सुदुर्मतिः। ब्राह्मणं वा महाभागं दीप्यमानं तथानलम्॥ तस्य दोषान् वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणुध्वं समाहिताः। दिवं स्पृशत्यशब्दोऽस्य त्रस्यन्ति पितरश्च वै॥ वैमनस्यं च देवानां कृतं भवति पुष्कलम्। पावकश्च महातेजा हव्यं न प्रतिगृह्णति॥
en: Agni said Listen you with rapt attention. I shall describe the demerits of that man of wicked understanding who lifts up his feet for striking therewith a cow or a highly blessed Brahmana or a burning fire. The infamy of such man spreads throughout the world and reaches the boundary of Heaven itself. His Pítris become filled with fear. The deities also become highly dissatisfied with him. Gifted with great energy, Fire refuses to accept the libations poured by him.

sn: आजन्मनां शतं चैव नरके पच्यते तु सः। निष्कृतिं च न तस्यापि अनुमन्यन्ति कर्हिचित्॥
en: For a hundred lives he has to rot in Hell. He is never rescued at any time.

sn: तस्माद् गावो न पादेन स्प्रष्टव्या वै कदाचन। ब्राह्मणश्च महातेजा दीप्यमानस्तथानलः॥ श्रद्वधानेन मर्येन आत्मनो हितमिच्छता। एते दोषा मया प्रोक्तास्त्रिषु यः पादमुत्सृजेत्॥
en: One should, therefore, never touch a cow with his feet or a Brahmana of high energy or a burning fire, if he is gifted with faith and seeks his own behoof. These are the demerits declared by me of one who lifts up his feet towards these three.

sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच श्रूयतां परमं गुह्यं रहस्यं धर्मसंहितम्। परमान्नेन यो दद्यात् पितॄणामौपहारिकम्॥ गजच्छायायां पूर्वस्यां कुतपे दक्षिणामुखः। यदा भाद्रपदे मासि भवते बहुले मघा॥ श्रूयतां तस्य दानस्य यादृशो गुणविस्तरः। कृतं तेन महच्छ्राद्धं वर्षाणीह त्रयोदश॥
en: Vishwamitra said Listen to a great mystery that is unknown to most of men and which is connected with religion. He, who offers to the departed manes, rice boiled in milk and sugar, sitting with face directed to the south at noontide, in the shade caused by an elephant's body in the month of Bhadrapada, under the constellation Magha, acquires great merits. Hear of those merits. The man who makes such an offering to the Pitris under such circumstances, is considered as performing a great Shraddha each year for thirteen years successively.

sn: गाव: ऊचुः बहुले समंगे ह्यकुतोऽभये च क्षेमे च सख्येव हि भूयसी च। यथा पुरा ब्रह्मपुरे सवत्सा शतक्रतोर्वज्रधरस्य यज्ञे।॥ भूयश्च या विष्णुपदे स्थिता ता विभावसोश्चापि पथे स्थिता या। देवाश्च सर्वे सह नारदेन प्रकुर्वते सर्वसहेति नाम॥ मन्त्रेणैतेनाभिवन्देत यो वै विमुच्यते पापकृतेन कर्मणा। लोकानवाप्नोति पुरंदरस्य गवां फलं चन्द्रमसो द्युतिं च
en: The Kine said That man becomes purged off of all his sins who worships a cow with these Mantras. viz., O Bahula, O Samanga, O you who are fearless everywhere, O you who are forgiving and full of auspiciousness, O friend, O source of all plenty, in the region of Brahman, formerly you were present with your calf in the sacrifice of Indra the holder of the thunderbolt! You were stationed in the sky and in the path of Agni! The celestials with Narada among them worshipped you on that occasion by calling you Sarvamsaha! Such a man attains to the region of Purandara. He acquires, besides, the merits that belong to kine, and the splendour of the Moon also.

sn: एतं हि मन्त्रं त्रिदशभिजुष्टं पठेत यः पर्वसु गोष्ठमध्ये। न तस्य पापं न भयं न शोकः सहस्रनेत्रस्य च याति लोकम्॥
en: Such a man becomes freed from every sin, every fear, every grief. At the end, he acquires residence in the happy region of the Thousand eyed Indra.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अथ सप्त महाभाग ऋषयो लोकविश्रुताः। वसिष्ठप्रमुखः सर्वे ब्रह्माणं पद्मसम्भवम्॥
en: Bhishma said After this, the highly blessed and illustrious seven Rishis headed by Vashishtha, rose and going round the Louts-born Brahman stood around him with hands joined in respect.

sn: प्रदक्षिणमभिक्रम्य सर्वे प्राञ्जलयः स्थिताः। उवाच वचनं तेषां वसिष्ठो ब्रह्मावित्तमः॥
en: Vashishtha, that foremost of all persons conversant with Brahma became their spokesman and put this question which conduces to the behoof of all creatures but especially to the Brahmanas and Kshatriyas.

sn: सर्वप्राणिहितं प्रश्न ब्रह्मक्षत्रे विशेषतः। द्रव्यहीनाः कथं मा दरिद्राः साधुवर्तिनः॥
en: By doing what acts may virtuous men who have no worldly belongings succeed in acquiring the merits of sacrifices?

sn: प्राप्नुवन्तीह यज्ञस्य फलं केन च कर्मणा। एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तेषां ब्रह्मा वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing this question of theirs the Grandfather Brahman began to say what follows.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अहो प्रश्नो महाभागा गूढार्थः परमः शुभः। सूक्ष्मः श्रेयांश्च मर्त्यानां भवद्भिः समुदाहृतः॥
en: Brahman said Excellent is this question, you highly blessed ones! It is at once auspicious and high and full of mystery. This question that you have put is subtile and conduces to the wellbeing of mankind.

sn: श्रूयतां सर्वमाख्यास्ये निखिलेन तपोधनाः। यथा यज्ञफलं मो लभते नात्र संशयः॥
en: You Rishis having penances for wealth, I shall recite everything to you in full. Do you listen with attention to what I say as to how men acquire the merits of sacrifices.

sn: पौषमासस्य शुक्ले वै यदा युज्येत रोहिणी। तेन नक्षत्रयोगेन आकाशशयनो भवेत्॥ एकवस्त्रः शुचिः स्नातः श्रद्दधानः समाहितः। सोमस्य रश्मयः पीत्वा महायज्ञफलं लभेत्॥
en: In the lighted fortnight of the month of Pausha, when the constellation Rohini is in conjunction, if one purifying himself by a bath lies, under the canopy of heaven clad in a single piece of cloth, with faith and rapt attention, and drinks the rays of the Moon, he wins the merits of great sacrifices,

sn: एतद् वः परमं गुह्यं कथितं द्विजसत्तमाः। यन्मां भवन्तः पृच्छन्ति सूक्ष्मतत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः॥
en: You foremost of twice born persons, this is a great mystery that I declare it to you in reply to your question, you who know the truths of all subjects. attention, and drinks the rays of the Moon, he wins the merits of great sacrifices,

sn: एतद् वः परमं गुह्यं कथितं द्विजसत्तमाः। यन्मां भवन्तः पृच्छन्ति सूक्ष्मतत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः॥
en: You foremost of twice born persons, this is a great mystery that I declare it to you in reply to your question, you who know the truths of all subjects.

sn: विभावसुरुवाच सलिलस्याञ्जलिं पूर्णमक्षताश्च घृतोत्तराः। सोमस्योत्तिष्ठमानस्य तज्जलं चाक्षतांश्च तान्॥ स्थितो ह्यभिमुखो मर्त्यः पौर्णमास्यां बलिं हरेत्। अग्निकार्यं कृतं तेन हुताश्चास्याग्नयस्त्रयः॥
en: Vibhavasu (The Sun) said : There are two offerings. One of these consists of a palmful of water and the other called Akshata consists of rice grains with clarified butter. One should on the day of the full moon, stand facing that bright orb and make to him the two offerings mentioned viz., a palmful of water and the rice grains with clarified butter called Akshata. The man who presents these offerings is said to worship his sacred fire. Indeed, he is considered as one who has poured libations the three (principal) fires.

sn: वनस्पतिं च यो हन्यादमावास्यामबुद्धिमान्। अपि टेकेन पत्रेण लिप्यते ब्रह्महत्यया।॥
en: That man of little understanding who cuts down a large tree on the day of the new moon, becomes sullied with the sin of Brahmanicide. By killing even a single leaf one commits that sin.

sn: दन्तकाष्ठं तु यः खादेदमावास्यामबुद्धिमान्। हिंसितश्चन्द्रमास्तेन पितरचोद्विजन्ति च॥
en: That foolish man who chews a toothbrush on the day of the new moon is considered as on injuring the god of the moon by such a deed. The departed Manes of such a person become annoyed with him.

sn: हव्यं न तस्य देवाश्च प्रतिगृह्णन्ति पर्वसु। कुप्यन्ते पितरश्चास्य कुले वंशोऽस्य हीयते॥
en: The celestials do not accept the libations poured by such a man on days of the full moon and the new moon. His departed Manes, become enraged with him and his family become extinct.

sn: श्रीरुवाच प्रकीर्णं भाजनं यत्र भिन्नभाण्डमथासनम्। योषितश्चैव हन्यन्ते कश्मलोपहते गृहे॥ देवताः पितरश्चैव उत्सवे पर्वणीषु वा। निराशा:प्रतिगच्छन्ति कश्मलोपहताद् गृहात्॥
en: Shree said The celestials and departed Manes leave that sinful house, in which eating and drinking vessels and seats and beds lie scattered and in which women are beaten. Without accepting the offerings made to them by the owners of such houses, the celestials and the departed Manes fly away from such a sinful house.

sn: अङ्गिरा उवाच यस्तु संवत्सरं पूर्णं दद्याद् दीपं करञ्जके। सुवर्चलामूलहस्तः प्रजा तस्य विवर्धते॥
en: Angirasa said The offspring of that man multiplies who stands every night for a full year under a Karanjaka tree with a lamp for lighting it and holds in his hands the roots of the Suvarchala plant.

sn: गार्ग्य उवाच आतिथ्यं सततं कुर्याद् दीपं दद्यात् प्रतिश्रये। वर्जयानो दिवा स्वापं न च मांसानि भक्षयेत्॥
en: Gargya said One should always do the duties of hospitality to his guests. One should give lamps in the hall or shed where sacrifices are celebrated. One should avoid sleep during the day, and abstain from all sorts of flesh or food. never

sn: गोब्राह्मणं न हिंस्याच्च पुष्कराणि च कीर्तयेत्। एष श्रेष्ठतमो धर्मः सरहस्यो महाफलः॥
en: One should injure kine and Brahmanas. One should always recite the names of the Pushkara lakes and the other sacred waters. Such a course of duty is the foremost. Even this forms a high religion with its mysteries. If observed in practice, it is sure lo yield great results.

sn: अपि क्रतुशतैरिष्ट्वा क्षयं गच्छति तद्धविः। न तु क्षीयन्ति ते धर्माः श्रद्दधानैः प्रयोजिताः॥
en: If a person celebrated even a hundred sacrifices, he is doomed to see the exhaustion of the merits belonging to the libations poured therein. The duties, however which I have mentioned are 'such that when observed by persons having faith their merit becomes endless.

sn: इदं च परमं गुह्यं सरहस्यं निबोधत। श्राद्धकल्पे च दैवे च तैर्थिके पर्वणीषु च॥ रजस्वला च या नारी वित्रिकापुत्रिका च या।
en: Listen to another great mystery unknown to many. The celestials do not eat the libations on occasions of Shraddhas and rites in their honour or on occasions of those rites which are performed on ordinary lunar days or on the especially sacred days of the full moon and the new moon, if they see a woman in her menses or one who is the daughter of a mother suffering from leprosy.

sn: एताभिश्चक्षुषा दृष्टं हविर्नाश्नन्ति देवताः॥ पितरश्च न तुष्यन्ति वर्षाण्यपि त्रयोदश।
en: The ancestors of the man who allows such a woman to come near to place where the Shraddha is being performed by him do not become pleased with him for thirteen years.

sn: शुक्लवासाः शुचिर्भूत्वाः ब्राह्मणान् स्वस्ति वाचयेत्। कीर्तयेद् भारतं चैव तथा स्यादक्षयं हविः॥
en: Clad in white clothes, and becoming pure in body and mind, one should invite Brahmanas and make them utter their benedictions. On such occasions one should also recite the 110W Bharata. It is by observing all these that the offerings made at Shraddhas become endless.

sn: धौम्य उवाच भिन्नभाण्डं च खट्वां च कुक्कुटं शुनकं तथा। अप्रशस्तानि सर्वाणि यश्च वृक्षो गृहेरुहः॥
en: Broken utensils broken bedsteads, cocks and dogs as also such trees as have grown within dwelling houses, are all in auspicious objects. Dhaumya said

sn: भिन्नभाण्डे कलिं प्राहुः खट्वायां तु धनक्षयः। कुक्कुटे शुनके चैव हविर्नाश्नन्ति देवताः। वृक्षमूले ध्रुवं सत्त्वं तस्माद् वृक्षं न रोपयेत्॥
en: In a broken utensil exists Kali himself, while in a broken bedstead is loss of money. When a cock or a dog is seen, the celestials do not eat the offerings made to them. Scorpions and snakes find shelter under the roots of a tree. Hence one should never plant a tree within his house.

sn: जमदग्निरुवाच यो यजेदश्वमेधेन वाजपेयशतेन ह। अवाशिरा वा लम्बेत सत्रं वा स्फीतमाहरेत्॥ न यस्य हृदयं शुद्धं नरकं स ध्रुवं व्रजेत्। तुल्यं यज्ञश्च सत्यं च हृदयस्य च शुद्धता॥
en: Jamadagni said That man whose heart is not pure is sure to go to Hell even if he worships the celestials in a Horse sacrifice or in hundred Vajapeya Sacrifices, or if he practises the severes austerities with head down most. Purity of heart is considered as equal to Sacrifices and Truth.

sn: शुद्धेन मनसा दत्त्वा सक्तुप्रस्थं द्विजातये। ब्रह्मलोकमनुप्राप्तः पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम्॥
en: A very barley with a pure heart to a Brahmana, acquired poor Brahmana by giving only a portion of powered the region of Brahman himself. This is a sufficient proof.

description: The observance of duties which produces happiness
sn: वायु रुवाच किंचिद् धर्मं प्रवक्ष्यामि मानुषाणां सुखावहम्। सरहस्याश्च ये दोषास्ताशृणुध्वं समाहिताः॥
en: Vayu said I shall recite some duties the observance of which produces happiness to mankind. Do you listen also with rapt attention, to certain transgressions upon which they depend.

description: The observance of duties which produces happiness
sn: अग्निकार्यं च कर्तव्यं परमान्नेन भोजनम्। दीपकश्चापि कर्तव्यः पितॄणां सतिलोदकः॥ एतेन विधिना मर्त्यः श्रद्दधानः समाहितः। चतुरो वार्षिकान् मासान् यो ददाति तिलोदकम्॥ भोजनं च यथाशक्त्या ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे। पशुबधशतस्येह फलं प्राप्नोति पुष्कलम्॥
en: That man who offers for the four months of the rainy season sesame and water (to the Pitris) and food, according to the best of his power to a Brahmana thoroughly expert in duties, who duly pours libations on the sacred fire, and makes offerings of rice boiled in sugared milk, who gives lamps in honor of the ancestors, with sesame and water, indeed he who does all this with faith and rapt attention, acquires all the merits of a hundred sacrifices in which animals are offered up to the celestials.

description: The observance of duties which produces happiness
sn: इदं चैवापरं गुह्यमप्रशस्तं निबोधत। अग्नेस्तु वृषलो नेता हविर्मूढाश्च योषितः॥ मन्यते धर्म एवेति स चाधर्मेण लिप्यते।
en: Listen to this other great mystery that is unknown to all. That man who thinks it all right when a Shudra lights up the fire upon which he is to pour libations or who does not see any fault when women who are incompetent to assist at Shraddhas and other rites are allowed to assist at them, commit a sin,

description: The observance of duties which produces happiness
sn: अग्नयस्तस्य कुप्यन्ति शूद्रयोनि स गच्छति॥ पितरश्च न तुष्यन्ति सह देवैर्विशेषतः।
en: The three sacrificial fires become enraged with such a person. In his next life he is born as a Shudra. His departed manes, together with the celestials are never pleased with him.

description: The observance of duties which produces happiness
sn: प्रायश्चित्तं तु यत् तत्र ब्रुवतस्तन्निबोध मे॥ यत् कृत्वा तु नरः सम्यक् सुखी भवति विज्वरः।
en: I shall now recite what the expiation's are which one must perform for purifying himself from such sins. Listen to me with attention. By performing those expiatory rites, one becomes happy and free from fever.

description: The observance of duties which produces happiness
sn: गवां मूत्रपुरीषेण पयसा च घृतेन च॥ अग्निकार्यं त्र्यहं कुर्यात्रिराहारः समाहितः।
en: Fasting all the while one should, for three days, with rapt attention pour libations, on the sacred fire, of the urine of the cow mixed with cowdung and milk and clarified butter.

description: The observance of duties which produces happiness
sn: ततः संवत्सरे पूर्णे प्रतिगह्णन्ति देवताः॥ हृष्यन्ति पितरश्चास्य श्राद्धकाल उपस्थिते।
en: The celestials accept the offerings of such a man on the expiration of a full year. His departed Manes also, when the time comes for him for performing the Shraddha, become pleased with him.

description: The observance of duties which produces happiness
sn: एष ह्यधर्मो धर्मश्च सरहस्यः प्रकीर्तितः॥ मानां स्वर्गकामानां प्रेत्य स्वर्गसुखावहः॥
en: I have thus recited what is righteous and what unrighteous, with all their unknown details, about human beings desirous of attaining to Heaven. Men who abstain from these sins or who having committed them perform the expiatory rites pointed out, succeed in attaining to the celestial region when they leave this world.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: लोमश उवाच परदारेषु ये सक्ता अकृत्वा दारसंग्रहम्। निराशाः पितरस्तेषां श्राद्धकाले भवन्ति वै॥
en: Lomasha said The departed Manes of those men vho, without having wives of their own know the wives of other people, are disappointed when the time for the Shraddha comes.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: परदाररतिर्यश्च यश्च वन्ध्यामुपासते। ब्रह्मस्वं हरते यश्च समदोषा भवन्ति ते॥
en: He who knows the wives of other people, he who indulges in sexual union with a barren woman and he who appropriates what belongs to a Brahmana, are equally sinful.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: असम्भाष्या भवन्त्येते पितॄणां नात्र संशयः। देवताः पितरश्चैषां नाभिनन्दन्ति तद्धविः॥
en: Forsooth, the departed Manes of such people cut them off without wishing to have any intercourse with them. The offerings they make fail to please the celestials and the departed Manes.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: तस्मात् परस्य वै दारांस्त्यजेद् वन्थ्यां च योषितम्। ब्रह्मस्वं हि नर्तव्यमात्मनो हितमिच्छता॥
en: Hence, one should always abstain from sexual union with women who are the lawful wives of others, as also with women who are barren. The man who seeks his own good, should not appropriate what belongs to a Brahmana.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: श्रूयतां चापरं गुह्यं रहस्यं धर्मसंहितम्। श्रद्दधानेन कर्तव्यं गुरूणां वचनं सदा॥
en: Listen now to another mystery unknown to all, about Religion. One should having faith, always do the command of his preceptor and other elders.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: द्वादश्यां पौर्णमास्यां च मासि मासि घृताक्षतम्। ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयच्छेत तस्य पुण्यं निबोधत॥
en: On the twelfth lunar day, as also on the day of the full moon, every month, one should make gifts to Brahmanas of clarified butter and of Akshata. Listen to me as I say what the measure is of the merit that such a person wins.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: सोमश्च वर्धते तेन समुद्रश्च महोदधिः। अश्वमेधचतुर्भागं फलं सृजाति वासवः॥
en: By such a deed one is said to increase Soma and the Ocean. Vasava, the king of the celestials confers upon him a fourth part of the merits of the Horse Sacrifice.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: दानेनतेन तेजस्वी वीर्यवांश्च भवेन्नरः। प्रीतश्च भगवान् सोम इष्टान् कामान् प्रयच्छति॥
en: By making such gifts, a person becomes gifted with great energy and prowess. Wellpleased with him, the divine Soma grants him the fruition of his desires.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: श्रूयतां चापरो धर्म: सरहस्यो महाफलः। इदं कलियुगं प्राप्य मनुष्याणां सुखावहः॥
en: Listen now to another duty, together with the foundation on which it depends, which yields great merits. In this age of Kali, that duty, if performed gives much happiness to men.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: कल्यमुत्थाय यो मर्त्यः स्नातः शुक्लेन वाससा। तिलपात्रं प्रयच्छेत ब्राह्मणेभ्यः समाहितः॥ तिलोदकं च यो दद्यात् पितॄणां मधुना सह। दीपकं कृसरं चैव श्रूयतां तस्य यत् फलम्॥
en: That man who, rising at dawn and purifying himself by a bath dresses himself in white clothes and with concentrated attention makes gifts to Brahmanas of vessels full of sesame seeds, who makes offerings to the departed Manes of water with sesame seeds and honey and who gives lamps as also the food called Krishara, acquires great merits. Listen to me as I say what those merits are:

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: तिलपात्रे फलं प्राह भगवान् पाकशासनः। गोप्रदानं च यः कुर्याद् भूमिदानं च शाश्वतम्॥ अग्निष्टोमं च यो यज्ञं यजेत बहुदक्षिणम्। तिलपात्रं सहैतेन समं मन्यन्ति देवताः॥
en: The divine chastiser of Paka has attributed these merits to the gift of vessels of copper and brass filled with sesame seeds. He who makes gifts of kine, he who makes gifts of land which yield eternal merit, he who performs the Agnishthoma sacrifice with profuse presents in the form of Dakshina to the Brahmanas are all considered by the celestials as acquiring merits equal to those which one acquires by making gifts of vessels filled with sesame seeds.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: तिलोदकं सदा श्राद्धे मन्यन्ते पितरोऽक्षयम्। दीपे च कृसरे चैव तुष्यन्तेऽस्य पितामहाः॥
en: Gifts of water with sesame seeds are considered by the departed Manes as yielding eternal gratification to them. The grandfathers all become highly pleased with gifts of lamps and Krishara.

description: The condition of men who know others wives
sn: स्वर्गे च पितृलोके च पितृदेवाभिपूजितम्। एवमेतन्मयोद्दिष्टमृषिदृष्टं पुरातनम्॥
en: I have thus recited the ancient ordinance, laid down by the Rishis that is highly spoken of by both the departed Manes and the celestials in their respective regions.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततस्त्वृषिगणाः सर्वे पितरश्च सदेवताः। अरुन्धतीं तपोवृद्धामपृच्छन्त समाहिताः॥
en: Bhishma said The diverse Rishis there assembled together with the departed Manes and the deities, then, with rapt attention, asked Arundhati who was gifted with great ascetic merit.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: समानशीला वीर्येण वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः। त्वत्तो धर्मरहस्यानि श्रोतुमिच्छामहे वयम्। यत्ते गुह्यतमं भद्रे तत् प्रभाषितुमर्हसि॥
