en: Having penances for wealth Arundhati was equal to her husband the highsouled Vasishtha in energy, for both in vows and conduct she was her husbands equal. Addressing her, they said, We wish to hear from you the mysteries of duty and religion. You should, O amiable lady, tell us what you consider as a great mystery.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: अरुन्धत्युवाच तपोवृद्धिर्मया प्राप्ता भवतां स्मरणेन वै। भवतां च प्रसादेन धर्मान् वक्ष्यामि शाश्वतान्॥ सगुह्यान् सरहस्यांश्च ताशृणुध्वमशेषतः। श्रद्दधाने प्रयोक्तव्या यस्य शुद्धं तथा मनः॥ अश्रद्दधानो मानी च ब्रह्महा गुरुतल्पगः। असम्भाष्या हि चत्वारो नैषां धर्मः प्रकाशयेत्॥
en: Arundhati said The great progress I have been able to make in penances is owing to your consideration for me in thus remembering my poor self. With your gracious permission I shall now describe duties that are eternal, and are great mysteries. I shall describe them with the causes on which they depend. Listen to me as I describe them to you in full. A knowledge of these should be communicated to him only who has faith or who has a pure heart. These four viz., he who is bereft of faith, he who is full of pride, he who is guilty of Brahmanicide, and he who violates the bed of his preceptor, should never be talked to. Religion and duty should never be communicated to them.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: अहन्यहनि यो दद्यात् कपिला द्वादशीः समाः। मासि मासि च सत्रेण यो यजेत सदा नरः॥ गवां शतसहस्रं च यो दद्याज्ज्येष्ठपुष्करे। न तद्धर्मफलं तुल्यमतिथिर्यस्य तुष्यति॥
en: The merits acquired by a person who gives way a Kapila cow every day for twelve years, or by a person who worships the deities every month in a sacrifice or by him who gives away hundreds of thousands o kine in the great Pushkara, do not equal those that are his with whom a guest is pleased. now

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: श्रूयतां चापरो धर्मो मनुष्याणां सुखावहः। श्रद्दधानेन कर्तव्यः सहरस्यो महाफलः॥
en: Listen to another duty whose observance yields happiness to mankind. It should be observed its secret ritual by a person having faith. Its merits are certainly high.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: कल्यमुत्थाय गोमध्ये गृह्य दर्भान् सहोदकान्। निषिञ्चेत गवां शृङ्गे मस्तकेन च तज्जलम्॥ प्रताच्छेत निराहारस्तस्य धर्मफलं शृणु। श्रूयन्ते यानि तीर्थानि त्रिषु लोकेषु कानिचित्॥ सिद्धचारणजुष्टानि सेवितानि महर्षिभिः। अभिषेकः समस्तेषां गवां शृङ्गोदकस्य च॥
en: Listen to what they are. If a person rising at dawn and taking with him a quantity of water and a few blades of Kusha grass, goes to a cowpen and arrived there, washes a cow's horns by sprinkling thereon that water with those blades of Kusha grass and then causes the water to drip down on his own head, he is considered, on account of such a bath, as one who has performed his ablutions in all the sacred waters that the wise have heard to exist in the three worlds and that are honored and resorted to by the Shiddhas and Charanas.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: साधु साध्विति चोद्दिष्टं दैवतैः पितृभिस्तथा। भूतैश्चैव सुसंहष्टैः पूजिता साप्यरुन्धती॥
en: After Arundhati had said these words all the deities and ancestors applauded her saying, Excellent, Excellent, Indeed all the beings there were highly pleased and all of them adored Arundhati.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: पितामह उवाच अहो धर्मो महाभागे सरहस्य उदाहृतः। वरं ददामि ते धन्ये तपस्ते वर्धतां सदा॥
en: Brahman said O highly blessed one, excellent is the duty that you have described together with its secret ritual. Praise be to you! I grant you a boon, viz., that your penances always may increase.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: यम उवाच रमणीया कथा दिव्या युष्मत्तो या मया श्रुता। श्रूयतां चित्रगुप्तस्य भाषितं मम च प्रियम्॥
en: Yama said I have heard from you an excellent and agrecable subject. Listen to what Chitragupta has said and what is agreeable to now me.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: रहस्यं धर्मसंयुक्तं शक्यं श्रोतुं महर्षिभिः। श्रद्दधानेन मन आत्मनो हितमिच्छता॥
en: Those words touch on duty with its secret ritual and are worthy of being heard by the great Rishis as also by men having faith and desirous of achieving their own good.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: न हि पुण्यं तथा पापं किंचिद् विनश्यति। पर्वकाले च यत् किंचिदादित्यं चाधितिष्ठति॥
en: Nothing is lost of either virtue or sin that is committed by creatures. On days of the full moon and the new moon, those acts are taken to the Sun where they rest.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: प्रेतलोकं गते म] तत् तत् सर्वे विभावसुः। प्रतिजानाति पुण्यात्मा तच्च तत्रोपयुज्यते॥
en: When a mortal goes into the regions of the dead the Sun witnesses all his deeds. He who is virtuous, acquires the fruits of his virtue there.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: किंचिद् धर्मं प्रवक्ष्यामि चित्रगुप्तमतं शुभम्। पानीयं चैव दीपं च दातव्यं सतलं तथा॥ उपानहौ च च्छत्रं च कपिला च यथातथम्। पुष्करे कपिला देया ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे॥
en: I shall now tell you of some auspicious duties that are approved of by Chitragupta. Water for drink, and lamps for lighting darkness, should always be given as also sandals and umbrellas and Kapila kine with due rites. In Pushkara especially, one should make the gift of a Kapila cow to a Brahmana conversant with the Vedas.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: अग्निहोत्रं च यत्नेन सर्वशः प्रतिपालयेत्। अयं चैवापरो धर्मचित्रगुप्तेन भाषितः॥
en: One should also always maintain his Agnihotra with great care. Here is another duty which was proclaimed by Chitragupta.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: फलमस्य पृथक्त्वेन श्रोतुमर्हन्ति सत्तमाः। प्रलयं सर्वभूतैस्तु गन्तव्यं कालपर्ययात्॥
en: The best of creatures should listen to what the merits are of that duty separately. In course of time every creature is destined to undergo dissolution.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: तत्र दुर्गमनुप्राप्ताः क्षुत्तृष्णापरिपीडिताः। दह्यमाना विपच्यन्ते न तत्रास्ति पलायनम्॥
en: The little witted meet with great distress in the regions of the dead, for they become stricken with hunger and thirst. Indeed, they have to rot there in pain. There is no escape for them from such a disaster.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: अन्धकारं तमो घोरं प्रविशन्त्यल्पबुद्धयः। तत्र धर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि येन दुर्गाणि संतरेत्॥
en: They have to enter into a thick darkness. I shall now tell you of those duties by discharging which one may succeed in getting Over such disasters.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: अल्पव्ययं महार्थं च प्रेत्य चैव सुखोदयम्। पानीयस्य गुणा दिव्याः प्रेतलोके विशेषतः॥
en: The performance of those duties costs every little but yields great merit. Indeed, such performance yields great happiness in the other world. The merits of the gift of water for drink, are excellent. In the next world, in especial, those merits are very great.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: तत्र पुण्योदका नाम नदी तेषां विधीयते। अक्षयं सलिलं तत्र शीतलं ह्यमृतोपमम्॥
en: A large river full of excellent water is ordained in the other world for them who make gifts of water for drink. Indeed, the water contained in that river is endless and cool and sweet as neetar.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: स तत्र गोयं पिबति पानीयं यः प्रयच्छति। प्रदीपस्य प्रदानेन श्रूयतां गुणविस्तरः॥
en: He who makes gifts of water in this world, drinks from that river in the next world when he goes there, listen now to the profuse merits accruing from the gift of lamps.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: तमोऽधकारं नियतं दीपदो न प्रपश्यति। प्रभां चास्य प्रयच्छन्ति सोमभास्करपावकाः॥
en: The man who gives lamps in this world has never to even see the thick darkness (of Hell). The Sun and the Moon and the God of Fire always give him their light when he goes to the other world.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: देवताश्चानुमन्यन्ते विमलाः सर्वतो दिशः। द्योतते च यथाऽऽदित्यः प्रेतलोकगतो नरः॥
en: The celestials ordain that on very side of such a person there should be burning light. Indeed, when the giver of lights goes to the world of the dead, he himself shines in pure effulgence like a second sun.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: तस्माद् दीपः प्रदातव्यः पानीयं च विशेषतः। कपिलां ये प्रयच्छन्ति ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे॥ पुष्करे च विशेषेण श्रूयतां तस्य यत् फलम्। गोशतं सवृषं तेन दत्तं भवति शाश्वतम्॥
en: Hence, one should give lights while here and water for drink in especial. Listen now to what the merits are of the person who makes the gift of a Kapila cow to a Brahmana knowing the Vedas, especially if the gift be made in Pushkara. Such a man is considered as having made a gift of a hundred kine with a bull a gift that yields eternal merit.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: पापं कर्म च यत् किंचिद् ब्रह्महत्यासमं भवेत्। शोधयेत् कपिला ह्येका प्रदत्तं गोशतं यथा॥
en: The gift of a single Kapila cow is capable cleansing whatever sins the giver may be guilty of even if those sins be as grave as Brahmanicide, for the gift of a single Kapila cow is considered as equal in merit to that of a hundred kine.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: तस्मात्तु कपिला देया कौमुद्यां ज्येष्ठपुष्करे। न तेषां विषमं किंचिन्न दु:खं न च कण्टकाः॥
en: Hence, one should give away a Kapila cow at that Pushkara which is considered as the senior, on the day of the full moon in the month o. Kartika. Men who succeed in making such a gift have never to meet with distress of any kind, or sorrow, or thorns giving pain.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: उपानहो च यो दद्यात् पात्रभूते द्विजोत्तमे। छत्रदाने सुखां छायां लभते परलोकगः॥
en: That man who gives away a pair of sandals to a superior Brahmana who is worthy of the gift, acquires similar merits. By giving away an umbrella, a person gets comfortable shade in the next world.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: न हि दत्तस्य दानस्य नाशोऽस्तीह कदाचन। चित्रगुप्तमतं श्रुत्वा हृष्टरोमा विभावसुः॥
en: A gift made to worthy person never goes for nothing. It is sure to yield agreeable results to the giver. Hearing these opinions of Chitragupta the Sun's hairs stood erect.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: उवाच देवताः सर्वाः पितूंश्चैव महाद्युतिः। श्रुतं हि चित्रगुप्तस्य धर्मगुह्यं महात्मनः॥
en: Gifted with great splendour, he addressed all the celestials and the departed Manes, saying, Ye have heard the mysteries about duty, as explained by the great Chitragupta.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: श्रद्दधानाश्च ये मर्त्या ब्राह्मणेषु महात्मसु। दानमेतत् प्रयच्छन्ति न तेषां विद्यते भयम्॥
en: Those human beings who gifted with faith, make these gifts to great Brahmanas, become freed from fear of every sort.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: धर्मदोषास्त्विमे पञ्च येषां नास्तीह निष्कृतिः। असम्भाष्या अनाचारा वर्जनीया नराधमाः॥
en: These five kinds of men sullied with vicious deeds have no escape. Indeed, these wretched men of sinful conduct, should never be talked to. Indeed they should always be avoided.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: ब्रह्महा चैव गोघ्नश्च परदाररतश्च यः। अश्रद्दधानश्च नरः स्त्रियं यश्चोपजीवति॥
en: Those five are he who is the destroyer of a Brahmana, he who is the destroyer of a cow, he who is addicted to sexual union with other people's wives, he who is bereft of faith (in the Vedas), and he who maintains himself by selling the virtue of his wife.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: प्रेतलोकगता ह्येते नरके पापकर्मिणः। पच्यन्ते वै यथा मीना: पूयशोणितभोजनाः॥
en: These men of sinful conduct when they go to the region of the dead rot in hell like worms which live upon puss and blood.

description: The mysteries of duty and religion
sn: असम्भाष्याः पितॄणां च देवानां चैव पञ्च ते। स्नातकानां च विप्राणां ये चान्ये च तपोधनाः॥
en: These five are avoided by the departed Manes, the celestials, the Snataka Brahmanas and other twice born persons who are given to the practice of penances.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः सर्वे महाभाग देवाश्च पितरश्च ह। ऋषयश्च महाभागाः प्रमथान् वाक्यमब्रुवन्॥ भवन्तो वै महाभागा अपरोक्षनिशाचराः। उच्छिष्टानशुचीन् क्षुद्रान् कथं हिंसथ मानवान्॥
en: Bhishma said Then all the highly blessed celestials and the departed Manes, and the highly blessed Rishis also, addressing the Pramathas, said, Ye are all highly blessed beings. Ye are invincible right rangers. Why do you afflict those men who are vile and impure and that are unclean?

sn: के च स्मृताः प्रतीघाता येन मर्त्यान् न हिंसथ। रक्षोनानि च कानि स्युर्यगृहेषु प्रणश्यथ। श्रोतुमिच्छाम युष्माकं सर्वमेतन्निशाचराः॥
en: What acts are considered as obstacles to your power? What indeed, are those acts on account of which you cannot afflict men? What are those acts that are destructive of Rakshasas and which prevent you from influencing the dwellings of men? Ye night rangers, we wish to hear all this from you.

sn: प्रथमा ऊचुः मैथुनेन सदोच्छिष्टाः कुते चैवाधरोत्तरे। मोहान्मांसानि खादेत वृक्षमूले च यः खपेत्॥ आमिषं शीर्षतो यस्य पादतो यश्च संविशेत्। तत उच्छिष्टकाः सर्वे बहुच्छिद्राश्च मानवाः॥
en: The Pramathas said Men are rendered unclean by acts of sexual intercourse. They who do not purify themselves after such deeds, they who insult their elders, they who from stupefaction eat different sorts of meat, the man also who sleeps at the foot of a tree, he who keeps any animal matter under his pillow while lying down for sleeps and who lies down or sleeps putting the head where his feet should be placed, or his feet where his feet should be placed, these men are considered by us as unclean. Indeed, these men have many holes.

sn: उदके चाप्यमेध्यानि श्लेष्माणं च प्रमुञ्चति। एते भक्ष्याश्च वध्याश्च मानुषा नात्र संशयः॥ एवं शीलसमाचारान् धर्षयामो हि मानवान्। श्रूयतां च प्रतीघातान् यैर्न शक्नुम हिंसितुम्॥
en: Those also are classed amongst those who throw their phlegm and other uncle and secretions into the water, Forsooth, these men deserve to be killed and eaten up by us. Indeed, we afflict those human beings who are endued with such conduct. Listen now to what those acts are which are considered as antidotes and on account of which we fail to do any injury on men.

sn: गोरोचनासमालम्भो वचाहस्तश्च यो भवेत्। घृताक्षतं च यो दद्यान्मस्तके तत्परायणः॥ ये च मांसं न खादन्ति तान् न शक्नुम हिसितुम्। यस्य चाग्निगृहे नित्यं दिवारात्रौ च दीप्यते॥ तरक्षोश्चर्म दंष्ट्राश्च तथैव गिरिकच्छपः। आज्यधूमो बिडालश्चच्छागः कृष्णोऽथ पिङ्गलः॥
en: Those men on whose body are marks of Gorochana, or who hold Vachas in their hands, or who make gifts of clarified butter with Akshata, or who place clarified butter and Akshata on their heads, or those who abstain from meat, are incapable of being afflicted by us. That man in whose house the sacred fire burns day and night without being ever extinguished or who keeps the skin or teeth of a wolf in his house or a hill-tortoise, or from whose house the sacrificial smoke is seen to curl upwards or who keeps a cat or a goat that is either tawny or black in colour, is free from our power.

sn: येषामेतानि तिष्ठन्ति गृहेषु गृहमेधिनाम्। तान्यधृष्याण्यगाराणि पिशिताशैः सुदारुणैः॥ लोकानस्मद्विधा ये च विचरन्ति यथासुखम्।
en: Those householders who keeps these things in their houses always find them free from the attacks of even the most dreadful spirit that live on carrion.

sn: तस्मादेतानि गेहेषु रक्षोनानि विशाम्पते। एतद् वः कथितं सर्वे यत्र वः संशयो महान्॥
en: Those beings also, that like us range through different words seeking pleasure, are unable to do any harm to such houses. Therefore, should men keep such articles in their houses as are destructive of Rakshasas. We have thus told you everything in solution of your great doubts.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः पद्मप्रतीकाशः पद्मोद्भूतः पितामहः। उवाच वचनं देवान् वासवं च शचीपतिम्॥ अयं महाबलो नागो रसातलचरो बली। तेजस्वी रेणुको नाम महासत्त्वपराक्रमः॥
en: Bhishma said After this, the Grandfather Brahman, sprung from the primeval lotus and resembling the lotus (in agreeableness and fragrance), addressed the celestials headed by Vasava, the husband of Sachi, Yonder sits the powerful Naga who lives in the nether regions Gifted with great strength and energy and with great prowess also, his name is Renuka. He is certainly a great being.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: अतितेजस्विनः सर्वे महावीर्या महागजाः। घरयन्ति महीं कृत्स्नां सशैलवनकाननाम्॥ भवद्भिः समनुज्ञातो रेणुकस्तान् महागजान्। धर्मगुह्यानि सर्वाणि गत्वा पृच्छतु तत्र वै॥ पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा ते देवा रेणुकं तदा। प्रेषयामासुरव्यग्रा यत्र ते धरणीधराः॥
en: Those powerful elephants of great energy and power, who hold the entire Earth with her hills, waters and lakes, should be seen by this Renuka at your request. Let Renuka go to them and ask them about the mysteries of religion or duty! Hearing these words of the Grandfather, the celestials wellpleased, sent (the elephant) Renuka to where those upholders of the world are.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: रेणुका उवाच अनुज्ञातोऽस्मि देवैश्च पितृभिश्च महाबलाः। धर्मगुह्यानि युष्माकं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः। कथयध्वं महाभागा यद् वस्तत्त्वं मनीषितम्॥
en: Going where those elephants are, Renuka address them, saying, Ye powerful creature have been commanded by the celestials and the departed Manes to question you about the mysteries of religion and duty! I desire to hear you discourse on that subject in detail. Ye highly blessed ones, do ye discourse on the subject as your wisdom may dictate.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: दिग्गजा ऊचुः कार्तिके मासि चाश्लेषा बहुलस्याष्टमी शिवा। तेन नक्षत्रयोगेन यो ददाति गुडौदनम्॥
en: Standing in the eight quarters, the elephants said, On the sacred eighth day of the dark fortnight in the month of Kartika when the constellation Ashlesha is in the ascendant, one should make gifts of treacle and rice.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: इमं मन्त्रं जपञ्छ्राद्धे यताहारो ह्यकोपनः। बलदेवप्रभृतयो ये नागा बलवत्तराः॥ अनन्ता ह्यक्षया नित्यं भोगिनः सुमहाबलाः। तेषां कुलोद्भवा ये च महाभूता भुजङ्गेमाः॥ ते मे बलिं प्रतीच्छन्तु बलतेजोऽभिवृद्धये। यदा नारायणः श्रीमानुज्जहार वसुंधराम्॥ तद् बलं तस्य देवस्य धरामुद्धरतस्तथा। एवमुक्त्वा बलिं तत्र वल्मीके तु निवेदयेत्॥ गजेन्द्रकुसुमाकीर्णं नीलवस्त्रानुलेपनम्।
en: an Renouncing anger, and living on regulated diet, one should make these offerings at a Shraddha, uttering these Mantras, Let Baladeva and other Nagas endued with great strength, let other powerful snakes of huge bodies that are indestructible and eternal and let all the other great snakes that have taken their birth in their family, inake vali offerings to me for the increase of my strength and energy. Indeed, let my strength be as great as that of the blessed Narayana when he raised the submerged Earth. Uttering these Mantras, one should make Bali offerings upon anthill. After sunset, offerings of raw sugar and rice should be made on anthill selected. The anthill should Previously be strewn with Gajendra flowers. Offerings should also be made of blue clothes and fragrant unguents.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: निर्वपेत् तं तु वल्मीके अस्तं याते दिवाकरे॥ एवं तुष्टास्ततः सर्वे अधस्ताद्भारपीडिताः। श्रमं तं नावबुध्यामो धारयन्तो वसुंधराम्॥
en: If offerings are made thus, those, beings that live in the nether regions, carrying the weight of the upper regions upon their heads or shoulders, become well pleased and gratified. As for ourselves, we also do not feel the exertion of upholding the Earth, on account of such offerings beings made to us.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: एवं मन्यामहे सर्वे भारार्ता निरपेक्षिणः। ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो वैश्यः शूद्रो वा यधुपोषितः॥
en: Afflicted with the burthen we bear, this is what we think (beneficial for men), without the slightest selfish end. By observing this rule for full year, fasting on each occasion, Brahmanas Kshatriyas, and Vaishays and Shudras, acquire great merits from such gifts.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: एवं संवत्सरं कृत्वा दानं बहुफलं लभेत्। वल्मीके बलिमादाय तन्नो बहुफलं मतम्॥
en: We think that the making of such Bali offerings on the anthill is really fraught with very superior merits.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: ये च नागा महावीर्यास्त्रिषु लोकेषु कृत्स्नशः। कृतातिथ्या भवेयुस्ते शतं वर्षाणि तत्त्वतः॥
en: a By making such offerings one is considered as doing the duties of hospitality or a hundred years to all the powerful elephants which exist in the three worlds.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: दिग्गजानां च तच्छ्रुत्वा देवता: पितरस्तथा। ऋषयश्च महाभागाः पूजयन्ति स्म रेणुकम्॥
en: Hearing these words of the powerful clephants, the celestials and the departed Manes and the highly blessed Rishis, all spoke highly of Renuka. By making such offerings one is considered as doing the duties of hospitality or a hundred years to all the powerful elephants which exist in the three worlds.

description: The mysteries of duty described by the elephant
sn: दिग्गजानां च तच्छ्रुत्वा देवता: पितरस्तथा। ऋषयश्च महाभागाः पूजयन्ति स्म रेणुकम्॥
en: Hearing these words of the powerful clephants, the celestials and the departed Manes and the highly blessed Rishis, all spoke highly of Renuka.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: महेश्वर उवाच सारमुद्धृत्य युष्माभिः साधुधर्म उदाहृतः। धर्मगुह्यमिदं मत्तः शृणुध्वं सर्व एव ह॥
en: Maheshvara said You have recited excellent duties from your Inemory. Listen all of you now to me as I declare some mysteries about religion and duty.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: येषां धर्माश्रिता बुद्धिः श्रद्दधानाश्च ये नराः। तेषां स्यादुपदेष्टव्यः सरहस्यो महाफलः॥
en: Only those persons whose understandings have been fixed on religion and who are endued with faith, should be instructed about those mysteries, of duty and religion that are fraught with high merits.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: निरुद्विगन्स्तु यो दद्यान्मासमेकं गवाह्निकम्। एकभक्तं तथाश्नीयाच्छूयतां तस्य यत् फलम्॥
en: Hear what the merits are that become his who, with heart shorn of anxiety, gives food every day, for a month, to kine, and contents himself with one meal a day throughout such period.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: इमा गावो महाभागाः पवित्रं परमं स्मृताः। त्रील्लोकान् धारयन्ति स्म सदेवासुरमानुषान्॥
en: The kinc are highly blessed. They are considered as the most sacred of all sacred things. Indeed, it is they who are upholding the three words with the celestials, Asuras and human beings.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: तासु चैव महापुण्यं शुश्रूषा च महाफलम्। अहन्यहनि धर्मेण युज्यते वै गवाह्निकः॥
en: Respectful services done to them, yield great merit and grave results. That man who every day gives food to kine daily, acquires accumulated religious merits.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: मया ह्येता ह्यनुज्ञाताः पूर्वमासन् कृते युगे। ततोऽहमनुनीतो वै ब्रह्मणा पद्मयोनिना॥
en: Formerly in the golden age, I had expressed my approval of these creatures, Afterwards Brahman, sprung from the primeval lotus, requested me (to show kindness towards kine).

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: तस्माद् ब्रजस्थानगतस्तिष्ठत्युपरि मे वृषः। रमेऽहं सह गोभिश्च तस्मात् पूज्याः सदैव ताः॥
en: It is therefore, that emblem of bull stands on my standard overhead. I always sport with kine. Hence, should kine be adored by all.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: महाप्रभावा वरदा वरं दधुरुपासिताः। ता गावोऽस्यानुमन्यन्ते सर्वकर्मसु यत् फलम्॥ तस्य तत्र चतुर्भागो यो ददाति गवाह्निकम्॥
en: Kine are endued with great power, They are givers of boons. If adored, they would grant boons. That person who gives food to kine even for a single day, receives from those beneficent creatures, for that deed, a fourth part of the merits he may acquire by all his good acts in life.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: स्कन्द उवाच ममाप्यनुमतो धर्मस्तं शृणुध्वं समाहिताः। नीलपण्डस्य श्रृंगाभ्यां मृत्तिकां तु यः॥ अभिषेकं त्र्यहं कुर्यात् तस्य धर्म निबोधता शोधयेदशुभं सर्वमाधिपत्यं परत्र च॥
en: Skanda said I shall now describe a duty that is approved of by me. Do ye listen to it with rapt attention. That person who takes a little earth from the horns of a bull of blue color, smears his body therewith for three days, and them performs his ablutions, wins great merits. Hear what those merits are. By such a deed he would wash away every stain and evil, and acquire sovereign sway hereafter.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: यावच्च जायते मर्त्यस्तावच्छूरो भविष्यति। इदं चाप्यपरं गुह्यं सरहस्यं निबोधत॥
en: Every time he is born in this world, he becomes celebrated for his heroism. Hear of another mystery unknown to all.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: प्रगृह्यौदुम्बरं पात्रं पक्वान्नं मधुना सहा सोमस्योत्तिष्ठमानस्य पौर्णमास्यां बलिं हरेत्॥
en: Taking a vessel of copper and placing therein some cooked food after having mixed it with honey, one should offer it as offerings to the rising Moon on the evening of the day when that luminary is at full.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: तस्य धर्मफलं नित्यं श्रद्दधाना निबोधता साध्या रुद्रास्तथादित्या विश्वेदेवस्तथाश्विनौ॥ मरुतो वसवश्चैव प्रतिगृहन्ति तं बलिम्। सोमश्च वर्धते तेन समुद्रश्च महोदधिः॥ एष धर्मो मयोद्दिष्टः सरहस्यः सुखावहः॥
en: Do you learn, with faith, what the merits are of the person who acts thus. The Saddhyas, the Rudras, the Adityas, the Vishvedevas, the twin Ashvins, the Maruts and the Vasus, all accept that offering. By such an offering, Soma increases as also ocean that great receptacle of waters. This duty that is declared by me and that is unknown to all, if performed, certainly yields great happiness.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: विष्णु उवाच धर्मगुह्यानि सर्वाणि देवतानां महात्मनान्। ऋषीणां चैव गुह्यानि यः पठेदाह्निकं सदा॥ शृणुयाद् वानसू युर्यः श्रद्दधानः समाहितः। नास्य विघ्नः प्रभवति भयं चास्य न विद्यते॥
en: Vishnu said That person who gifted with faith and freed from malice, listens every day with rapt attention to the mysteries about religion and duty that are preserved by the great deities and those mysteries also of the same kind that are preserved by the Rishis has never to succumb to any evil. Such a person becomes also freed from every fear.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: ये च धर्माः शुभाः पुण्याः सरहस्या उदाहृताः। तेषां धर्मफलं तस्य यः पठेत जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: That man who, with his senses under thorough restraint, reads these sections describing these auspicious and meritorious duties, together with their mysteries duties, that have been ascribed (by the previous speakers), acquires all the merits of their actual performance.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: नास्य पापं प्रभवति न च पापेन लिप्यते। पठेद् वा श्रावयेद् वापि श्रुत्वा वा लभते फलम्॥
en: Sin can never lord over him. Indeed, such a man can never be stained with faults of any sort. Indeed, one acquires profuse merits by reading these mysteries or by reciting them to others or by hearing them recited.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: भुञ्जते पितरो देवा हव्यं कव्यमथाक्षयम्। श्रावयंश्चापि विप्रन्द्रान् पर्वसु प्रयतो नरः॥
en: The celestials and the departed Manes eat for ever the Havi and the Kavi offered by such a creature. Both these, on account of the virtues of the offer, become inexhaustible. Even such is the merit of the person who, with rapt attention, recites these mysteries to foremost of Brahmanas, on days of the full moon or the new moon.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: ऋषीणां देवतानां च पितॄणां चैव नित्यदा। भवत्यभिमतः श्रीमान् धर्मेषु प्रयतः सदा॥
en: Such a person, on account of such a deed, becomes steady in the performance of all duties. He also enjoys personal beauty and prosperity. He succeeds, besides this in becoming the favourite for all time, of the Rishis and the celestials and the departed Manes.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: कृत्वापि पापकं कर्म महापातकवर्जितम्। रहस्यधर्मे श्रुत्वेमं सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: If a person becoines guilty of all sins except those which are classed as grave or heinous, he becomes purged off of them all by only listening to the recitation of these mysteries about religion and duty.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: भीष्म उवाच एतद् धर्मरहस्यं वै देवतानां नराधिप। व्यासोद्दिष्टं मया प्रोक्तं सर्वदेवनमस्कृतम्॥ पृथिवी रत्नसम्पूर्णा ज्ञानं चेदमनुत्तमम्। इदमेव ततः श्राव्यमिति मन्येत धर्मवित्॥
en: Bhishma said Even these, O king, are the mysteries about religion and duty living in the breasts of the deities. Held in high esteem by all the celestials and promulgated by Vyasa, they have now been declared by me for your behoof. One who is conversant with religion and duty thinks that this excellent knowledge is even superior to the entire. Earth full of riches and wealth.

description: Duties as described by Maheshvara and Skanda
sn: नाश्रद्दधानाय न नास्तिकाय न नष्टधर्माय न निघृणाय। न हेतुदुष्टाय गुरुद्विषे वा नानात्मभूताय निवेद्यमेतत्॥
en: This knowledge should not be given to one who has no faith or to one who is an atheist, or to one who has fallen away from the duties of his caste, or to one who is shorn of mercy, or to one who is given to the science of empty disputations, or to one who is hostile to his preceptors, or to one who thinks all creatures to be different from oneself.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच के भोज्या ब्राह्मणस्येह के भोज्याः क्षत्रियस्य ह। तथा वैश्यस्य के भोज्याः के शूद्रस्य च भारत॥
en: Yudhishthira said Who are those persons, O Bharata from whom a Brahman in this world may take his food? From whom may a Kshatriya, a Vaishya and a Shudra take their food respectively?

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: भीष्म उवाच ब्राह्मणा ब्राह्मणस्येह भोज्या ये चैव क्षत्रियाः। वैश्याश्चापि तथा भोज्याः शूद्राश्च परिवर्जिताः॥
en: Bhishma said A Brahmana may take his food from another Brahmana or from a Kshatriya or from a Vaishya but he must never take food from a Shudra.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्या भोज्या वै क्षत्रियस्य ह। वर्जनीयास्तु वै शूद्राः सर्वभक्षा विकर्मिणः॥
en: A Kshatriya may take his food from a Brahmana, a Kshatriya or a Vaishya. He must, however, not take food given by Shudras who are given to evil ways and who partake of all sorts of food without any hesitation.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: वैश्यास्तु भोज्या विप्राणां क्षत्रियाणां तथैव च। नित्याग्नयो विविक्ताश्च चातुर्मास्यरताश्च ये॥
en: Brahmanas and Kshatriyas can partake of food given by such Vaishyas as serve the sacred fire everyday as are faultless in character and as perform the VOW of Chaturmasya.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: शूद्राणामथ यो भुङ्क्ते स भुङ्क्ते पृथिवीमलम्। मलं नृणां स पिबति मलं भुङ्क्ते जनस्य च॥
en: But the man who accepts food from a Shudra, swallows the very abomination of the Earth and drinks the excretions of the human body, and partakes of the filth of all the world.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: शूद्राणां यस्तथा भुक्ते स भुङ्क्ते पृथिवीमलम्। पृथिवीमलमश्नन्ति ये द्विजाः शूद्रभोजिनः॥
en: He partakes of the very filth of the Earth who takes his food thus from a Shudra. Indeed, those Brahinanas who accept their food from Shudras, take the dirt of the Earth.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: शूद्रस्य कर्मनिष्ठायां विकर्मस्थोऽपि पच्यते। ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो वैश्यो विकर्मस्थश्च पच्यते॥
en: If one engages in the service of a Shudra, he is doomed to perdition though he may duly perform all the rites of his caste. A Brahmana a Kshatriya or a Vaishya, so engaging is doomed although given to the proper performance of religious rites.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: स्वाध्यायनिरता विप्रास्तथा स्वस्त्ययने नृणाम्। रक्षणे क्षत्रियं प्राहुर्वैश्यं पृष्ट्यर्थमेव च॥
en: It is said that a Brahmana's duty consists in studying the Vedas and seeking the behoof of humanity that a Kshatriyas duty consists in protecting men and that a Vaishyas promoting their material prosperity.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: करोति कर्म यद् वैश्यस्तद् गत्वा ह्युपजीवति। कृषिगोरक्ष्यवाणिज्यमकुत्सा वैश्यकर्माणि॥
en: A Vaishya lives by distributing the fruits of his own deeds and agriculture. The breeding of kine and trade are the legitimate duties in which a Vaishya may engage without fear of censure.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: शूद्रकर्म तु यः कुर्यादवहाय स्वकर्म च। स विज्ञेयो यथा शूद्रो न च भोज्य: कदाचन।॥
en: The man who gives up his own proper occupation and does that of a Shudra, should be regarded as a Shudra, and on no account should any food be accepted from him.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: चिकित्सकः काण्डपृष्ठः पुराध्यक्षः पुरोहितः। सांवत्सरो वृथाध्यायी सर्वे ते शूद्रसम्मिताः॥
en: Professors of medicine mercenary soldiers, the priest who acts as warder of the house, and persons who devote a whole year to study without any profit are all to be regarded as Shudras.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: शूद्रकर्मस्वथैतेषु यो भुङ्क्ते निरपत्रपः। अभोज्यभोजनं भुक्त्वा भयं प्राप्नोति दारुणम्॥ कुलं वीर्यं च तेजश्च तिर्यग्योनित्वमेव च। स प्रयाति यथा श्वा वै निष्क्रियो धर्मवर्जितः॥
en: And those who foolishly partake of food offered at ceremonials in a Shudra's house, suffer from a dreadful disaster. On account of partaking such forbidden food, they loose their family strength and energy, and acquire the status of lower animals degenerating to the position of dogs fallen in virtue and devoid of all religious observances.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: भुक्त चिकित्सकस्यान्नं तदनं च पुरीषवत्। पुंश्चल्यन्नं च मूत्रं स्यात् कारुकानं च शोणितम्॥१४
en: He who takes food from a physician, takes but an excrement; the food of a harlot is like urine; that of a skilled mechanic is like blood.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: विद्योपजीविनोऽन्नं च यो भुङ्क्ते साधुसम्मतः। तदप्यन्नं यथा शौद्रं तत् साधुः परिवर्जयेत्॥
en: If a good Brahmana takes the food of one who lives by his learning. he is considered as taking the food of a Shudra. All good men should avoid such food.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: विचनीयस्य यो भुङ्क्ते तमाहुः शोणितं ह्रदम्। पिशुनं भोजनं भुङ्क्ते ब्रह्महत्यासमं विदुः॥
en: The food of a person who is censured by all, is said to be like a drink from a pool of blood. The acceptance of food from a wicked person is as the killing of Brahmana.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: असत्कृतमवज्ञातं च भोक्तव्यं कदाचन॥ व्याधि कुलक्षयं चैव क्षिप्रं प्राप्नोति ब्राह्मणः।
en: One should not accept food if he is slighted and not received with due honors by the giver. A Brahmana, who does so, is soon possessed by disease, and his family soon becomes extinct.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: नगरीरक्षिणो भुङ्क्ते श्वपचप्रवणो भवेत्॥
en: By accepting food from the warder of a city, one degenerates to the status, of the lowest outcast.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: गोने च ब्राह्मणध्ने च सुरापे गुरुतल्पगे। भुक्त्वान्नं जायते विप्रो रक्षसां कुलवर्धनः॥
en: If a Brahmana accepts food from one who is guilty of slaying either a cow or a Brahmana, or from one who has committed adultery with his preceptor's wife, or from a drunkard, he helps to promote the family of Rakshasas.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: न्यासापहारिणो भुक्त्वा कृतने क्लीववर्तिनि। जायते शबरावासे मध्यदेशबहिष्कृते॥
en: By taking food from a eunuch or from an ungrateful person, or from one who has misappropriated money entrusted to his care, one is born in the country of the Sabaras situated beyond the limit of the middle country.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: अभोज्याश्चैव भोज्याश्च मया प्रोक्ता यथाविधि। किमन्यदद्य कौन्तेय मत्तस्त्वं श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: I have thus duly described to you the persons from whom food may be accepted and from whom it may not. Now tell me, O Kunti, what else do you wish to hear from me today. son of misappropriated money entrusted to his care, one is born in the country of the Sabaras situated beyond the limit of the middle country.

description: The law of diet-The position of various castes about that
sn: अभोज्याश्चैव भोज्याश्च मया प्रोक्ता यथाविधि। किमन्यदद्य कौन्तेय मत्तस्त्वं श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: I have thus duly described to you the persons from whom food may be accepted and from whom it may not. Now tell me, O Kunti, what else do you wish to hear from me today. son of

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उक्तास्तु भवता भोज्यास्तथाभोज्याश्च सर्वशः। अत्र में प्रश्नसंदेहस्तन्मे वद पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have told me fully of those from whom food may be taken and of those from whom it should not be taken?

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: ब्राह्मणानां विशेषेण हव्यकव्यप्रतिग्रहे। नानाविधेषु भोज्येषु प्रायश्चित्तानि शंस मे॥
en: But I have grave doubts on one points, Do you o Sire enlighten me; do you tell me what expiations a Brahmana should make upon accepting the different kinds of food, those especially offered in honour of the celestials and the oblations made to the departed Manes.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: भीष्म उवाच हन्त वक्ष्यामि ते राजन् ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम्। प्रतिग्रहेषु भोज्ये च मुच्यते येन पाप्मनः॥
en: Bhishma said I shall tell you, O prince, how great Brahmanas may be freed from all sins incurred by acccpting food from others.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: घृतप्रतिग्रहे चैव सावित्री समिदाहुतिः। तिलप्रतिग्रहे चैव सममेतद् युधिष्ठिर॥
en: In accepting clarified butter, the expiation is made by pouring oblations on the fire, reciting the Savitri hymn. In accepting sesamum, o Yudhishthira the same expiation has to be made.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: मांसप्रतिग्रहे चैव मधुनो लवणस्य च। आदित्योदयनं स्थित्वा पूतो भवति ब्राह्मणः॥
en: In accepting meat, or honey, or salt, a Brahmana becomes purged off of all sins by standing till the rising of the Sun.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: काञ्चनं प्रतिगृह्याथ जपमानो गुरुश्रुतिम्। कृष्णायसं च विवृतं धारयन् मुच्यते द्विजः॥ एवं प्रतिगृहीतेऽथ धने वस्त्रे तथा स्त्रियाम्। एवमेव नरश्रेष्ठ सुवर्णस्य प्रतिग्रहे॥
en: If a Brahmana accepts gold from any one, he becomes cleansed of all sins by silently reciting the great Gayatri, and by holding a piece of iron in his hand, before the public. In accepting money or clothes or women or gold, the purification is the same as before.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: अन्नप्रतिग्रहे चैव पायसेक्षुरसे तथा। इक्षुतैलपवित्राणां त्रिसंध्येऽप्सु निमज्जनम्॥
en: In accepting food, or rice boiled in milk and sugar, or sugarcane juice, or sugarcane, or oil or any sacred thing, one becomes purified by bathing thrice during the day, viz., at morning noon and evening.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: व्रीहौ पुष्पे फले चैव जले पिष्टमये तथा। यावके दधिदुग्धे च सावित्रीं शतशोऽन्विताम्॥
en: If one accepts paddy, flowers fruits, water half ripe barley, milk or curdled milk or anything made of meal or flour the expiation is done by reciting the Gayatri prayer a hundred times.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: उपानहौ च च्छत्रं च प्रतिगृौर्ध्वदेहिके। जपेच्छतं समायुक्तस्तेन मुच्येत पाप्मना॥
en: In accepting shoes or clothes at obsequial ceremonies, the sin is dissipated by reciting devoutly the same hymn a hundred times.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: क्षेत्रप्रतिग्रहे चैव ग्रहसूतकयोस्तथा। त्रीणि रात्राण्युपोषित्वा तेन पापाद् विमुच्यते॥
en: a The acceptance of the gift of land during an eclipse or during the period of impurity, is expiated by observing a fast during three successive nights.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: कृष्णपक्षे तु यः श्राद्धं पितॄणामश्नुते द्विजः। अन्नमेतदहोरात्रात् पूतो भवति ब्राह्मणः॥
en: The Brahmana who partakes of oblations offered to departed Manes, in course of the dark fortnight, is purified by fasting for a whole day and night.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: न च संध्यामुपासीत न च जाप्यं प्रवर्तयेत्। न संकिरेत् तदन्नं च ततः पूयेत ब्राह्मणः॥
en: Without performing his ablutions Brahmana should not recite his evening prayers nor engage in religious meditation, nor take his food a second time. By so doing he is purified.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: इर्थमपराह्ने तु पितॄणां श्राद्धमुच्यते। यथोक्तानां यदश्नीयुर्ब्राह्मणाः पूर्वकीर्तिताः॥
en: Therefore the Shraddha of departed Manes has been ordained to be performed in the afternoon and then the Brahmana who has been invited beforehand should be treated with food.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: मृतकस्य तृतीयाहे ब्राह्मणो योऽन्नमश्नुते। स त्रिवेलं समुन्मज्य द्वादशाहेन शुध्यति॥
en: The Brahmana who takes food at the house of a dead person on the third day after the death, is purified by bathing three times daily for twelve days.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: द्वादशाहे व्यतीते तु कृतशौचो विशेषतः। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो हविर्दत्त्वा मुच्यते तेन पाप्मना॥
en: After the expiration of twelve days, and performing the purification ceremonies duly, the sin is dissipated by giving clarified butter to Brahmanas.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: मृतस्य दशरात्रेण प्रायश्चित्तानि दापयेत्। सावित्रीं रैवतीमिष्टिं कूष्माण्डमघमर्षणम्॥
en: If a man takes any food in the house of a dead person, within ten days after the death, he should perform all the expiations before mentioned and should recite the Savitri hymn and perform the sin-destroying Ishti and Kushmanda penances.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: मृतकस्य त्रिरात्रे यः समुद्दिष्टे समश्नुते। सप्त त्रिषवणं स्नात्वा पूतो भवति ब्राह्मणः॥ सिद्धिमाप्नोति विपुलामापदं चैव नाप्नुयात्॥
en: The Brahmana who takes his food in the house of a dead person for three nights becomes purified by performing his ablutions thrice daily for seven days, and thus gains all the objects of his desire, and is never troubled by misfortunes.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: यस्तु शूद्रैः समश्नीयाद् ब्राह्मणोऽप्येकभोजने। अशौचं विधिवत् तस्य शौचमत्र विधीयते॥
en: The Brahmana who take his food in the company of Shudras, is purged from all impurities by duly performing the ceremonies of purifications.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: यस्तु वैश्यैः सहाश्नीयाद् ब्राह्मणोऽप्येकभोजने। स वै त्रिरात्रं दीक्षित्वा मुच्यते तेन कर्मणा॥
en: The Brahmana who takes his food in the company of Vaishyas, is purged off of all sins, by living on alms for three successive nights.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: क्षत्रियैः सह योऽश्नीयाद् ब्राह्मणोऽप्येकभोजने। आप्लुत: सह वासोभिस्तेन मुच्येत पाप्मना॥
en: If a Brahmana takes his food with Kshatriyas, he should perform expiation by bathing with his clothes on.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: शूद्रस्य तु कुलं हन्ति वैश्यस्य पशुबान्धवान्। क्षत्रियस्य श्रियं हन्ति ब्राह्मणस्य सुवर्चसम्॥
en: By eating with a Shudra on the same plate the Shudra loses his family prestige; the Vaishya by eating on the same plate with a Vaishya, loses his cattle and friends. The Kshatriya loses his prosperity; and the Brahmana, his effulgence and power.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: प्रायश्चित्तं च शान्तिं च जुहुयात् तेन मुच्यते। सावित्रीं रैवतीमिष्टिं कूष्माण्डमघमर्षणम्॥
en: In such cases expiations should be performed and propitiatory rites should be observed, and oblations offered to the celestials. The Savitri hymn should be recited and the Revati rites and Kushmanda penances should be performed for destroying the sin.

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: तथोच्छिष्टमथान्योन्यं सम्प्राशेन्नात्र संशयः। रोचना विरजा रात्रिर्मङ्गलालम्भनानि च॥
en: If any of the above four castes partake of food partly eaten by a person of any other caste, the expiation is forsooth, made by smearing the body with sacred articles like Rochana, Durba grass, and turmeric,

description: The expiation of a Brahmana disregarding the law
sn: तथोच्छिष्टमथान्योन्यं सम्प्राशेन्नात्र संशयः। रोचना विरजा रात्रिर्मङ्गलालम्भनानि च॥
en: If any of the above four castes partake of food partly eaten by a person of any other caste, the expiation is forsooth, made by smearing the body with sacred articles like Rochana, Durba grass, and turmeric,

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दानेन वर्ततेत्याह तपसा चैव भारत। तदेतन्मे मनोदुःखं व्यपोह त्वं पितामह। किंस्वित् पृथिव्यां ह्येतन्मे भवाञ्छंसितुमर्हति॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Bharata, O grandfather, you opine that a man attains to heaven by virtue of generousity and austerity, but my mind is doubtful on affirming the same. Kindly let me have an adequate solution. kindly tell me which of the two is better, viz., charity or devotion?

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु यैर्धर्मनिरतैस्तपसा भावितात्मभिः। लोका ह्यसंशयं प्राप्ता दानपुण्यरत्तैर्नृपः। :॥
en: Bhishma said Listen to me as I recite the names of the princes who having been devoted to virtue, and having purified their hearts by penances and practiced gifts and other acts of virtue, undoubtedly acquire the different celestial regions.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: सत्कृतश्च तथाऽऽत्रेयः शिष्येभ्यो ब्रह्म निर्गुणम्। उपदिश्य तदा राजन् गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: The Rishi Atreya respected of all, attained, O king, to the excellent celestial regions by importing the knowledge of the limitless Supreme Being to his pupils.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: शिबिरौशीनरः प्राणान् प्रियस्य तनयस्य च। ब्राह्मणार्थमुपाकृत्य नाकपृष्ठमितो गतः॥
en: By offering the life of his dear son, for the behoof of a Brahmana king Shibi the son of Ushinara was taken from this world to the celestial regions

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: प्रतर्दनः काशिपतिः प्रदाय तनयं स्वकम्। ब्राह्मणायातुलां कीर्तिमिह चामुत्र चाश्नुते॥
en: Pratardana the king of Kashi, secured to himself unique and eternal fame in this as well as in the other world by giving his son to a Brahmana.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: रन्तिदेवश्च सांकृत्यो वसिष्ठाय महात्मने। अy प्रदाय विधिवल्लेभे लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: Rantideva, the son of Sangakriti, attained to the highest heaven by duly making gifts to the great Vasishtha.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: दिव्यं शतशलाकं च यज्ञार्थं काञ्चनं शुभम्। छत्रं देवावृधो दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणायास्थितो दिवम्॥
en: Devavriddha, too went to the celestial region by giving a hundred ribbed and excellent golden umbrella to a Brahmana for a sacrifice.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: भगवानम्बरीषश्च ब्राह्मणायामितौजसे। प्रदाय सकलं राष्ट्र सुरलोकमवाप्तवान्॥
en: The worshipful Ambarisha too, has acquired the celestial region by making a gift of all his kingdom to a highly powerful Brahmana.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: सावित्रः कुण्डलं दिव्यं यानं च जनमेजयः। ब्राह्मणाय च गा दत्त्वा गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: King Janamejaya of the solar race, went to the highest heaven by making a gift of earrings, fine vehicles and cows to Brahmanas,

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: वृषादर्भिश्च राजर्षी रत्नानि विविधानि च। रम्यांश्चावसथान् दत्त्वा द्विजेभ्यो दिवमागतः॥
en: The Royal Sage Vrishadarvi went to the celestial region by making gifts of various jewels and beautiful houses to Brahmanas,

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: निमी राष्ट्रं च वैदर्भिः कन्यां दत्त्वा महात्मने। अगस्त्याय गतः स्वर्गे सपुत्रपशुबान्धवः॥
en: King Nimi of Vidarbha, acquired the celestial region with his sons, friends and cattle by giving his daughter and kingdom to the great Agastya.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: जामदग्न्यश्च विप्राय भूमिं दत्त्वा महायशाः। रामोऽक्षयांस्तथा लोकान् जगाम मनसोऽधिकान्॥१२
en: The illustrious Rama, the son of Jamadagni, acquired the eternal regions, far beyond his expectation by giving lands to Brahmanas.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: अवर्षति च पर्जन्ये सर्वभूतानि देवराट्। वसिष्ठो जीवयामास येन यातोऽक्षयां गतिम्॥
en: Vasishtha, the greatest of Brahmanas, saved all the creatures at a time of great drought when the Rain God did not bestow his grateful showers upon the Earth, and for this deed he has secured eternal bliss himself.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: रामो दाशरथिश्चैव हुत्वा यज्ञेषु वै वसु। स गतो ह्यक्षयाल्लोकान् यस्य लोके महद् यशः॥१४
en: The highlyillustrious Rama the son Dasharatha, acquired the eternal regions by making gifts of riches at sacrifices,

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: कक्षसेनश्च राजर्षिर्वसिष्ठाय महात्मने। न्यासं यथावत् संन्यस्य जगाम सुमहायशाः॥
en: The illustrious Royal Sage Kakshasena went to the celestial region by duly making over to the great Vasishtha the wealth which he had deposited with him.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: करन्धमस्य पौत्रस्तु मरुत्तोऽविक्षितः सुतः। कन्यामाङ्गिरसे दत्त्वा दिवमाशु जगाम सः॥
en: Forthwith Maruta the son of Avikshita and the grandson of Karandhama, by giving his daughter in marriage to Angirasa, went to the celestial regions.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: ब्रह्मदत्तश्च पाञ्चाल्यो राजा धर्मभृतां वरः। निधि शङ्खमनुज्ञाप्य जगाम परमां गतिम्॥
en: The highly devout king of Panchala, Brahmadatta, attained the blessed way by giving away a valuable conchshell.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: राजा मित्रसहश्चैव वसिष्ठाय महात्मने। मदयन्तीं प्रियां भार्यां दत्त्वा च त्रिदिवं गतः॥
en: King Mitrasaha ascended to Heaven by giving his favourite wife Madayanti to the great Vasishtha.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: मनोः पुत्रश्च सुद्युम्नो लिखिताय महात्मने। दण्डमुद्धृत्य धर्मेण गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: Sudyumna the son of Manu, attained to the most blessed regions by duly punishing the high souled Likhita.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: सहस्रचित्यो राजर्षिः प्राणानिष्टान् महायशाः। ब्राह्मणार्थे परित्यज्य गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: The celebrated Royal sage Sahasrachitta went to the blessed regions by sacrificing his dear life for a Brahmana.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: सर्वकामैश्च सम्पूर्णे दत्त्वा वेश्म हिरण्मयम्। मौन्द्रल्याय गतः स्वर्गे शतद्युम्नो महीपतिः॥
en: The king Satadyumna went to heaven by giving to Mudgala a golden palace filled with all the objects of desire.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: भक्ष्यभोज्यस्य च कृतान् राशयः पर्वतोपमान्। शाण्डिल्याय पुरा दत्त्वा सुमन्युर्दिवमास्थितः॥
en: Formerly, King Sumanyu by giving to Shandilya heaps of food resembling a hill, went to the celestial region.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: नाम्ना च द्युतिमान् नाम शाल्वराजो महाद्युतिः। दत्त्वा राज्यमृचीकाय गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: The Shalva prince Dyutimat of great effulgence attained to the highest regions by giving his kingdom to Richika.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: मदिराश्वश्च राजर्षिर्दत्त्वा कन्यां सुमध्यमाम्। हिरण्यहस्ताय गतो लोकान् देवैरधिष्ठितान्॥
en: The Royal Sage Madirashva went to the region of the celestials by giving his slender waisted daughter to Hiranyahasta.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: लोमपादश्च राजर्षिः शान्तां दत्त्वा सुतां प्रभुः। ऋष्यशृङ्गाय विपुलैः सर्वैः कामैरयुज्यत॥
en: The lordly Lomapada attained all the objects of his desire by giving his daughter Shanta in marriage to Rishyashringa.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: कौत्साय दत्त्वा कन्यां तु हंसी नाम यशस्विनीम्। गतोऽक्षयानतो लोकान् राजर्षिश्च भगीरथः॥
en: The Royal Bhagiratha went to the eternal regions by giving his famous daughter Hansi in marriage to Kautsa.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: दत्त्वा शतसहस्रं तु गवां राजा भगीरथः। सवत्सानां कोहलाय गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: King Bhagiratha acquired the most blessed regions by giving hundreds and thousands of kine with their young one to Kohala.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो दानेन तपसा च ह। युधिष्ठिर गताः स्वर्गे निवर्तन्ते पुनः पुनः॥
en: These and many other men, O Yudhishthira, have attained to the celestial region, by the merit of their charities and penances and they have also returned from there again and again.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: तेषां प्रतिष्ठिता कीर्तिर्यावत् स्थास्यति मेदिनी। गृहस्थैर्दानतपसा यैर्लोका वै विनिर्जिताः॥
en: Their fame will last as long as the world will last. I have related to you, O Yudhishthira, this story of those good householders, who have attained to eternal regions by virtue of their charities and penances.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: शिष्टानां चरितं ह्येतत् कीर्तितं मे युधिष्ठिर। दानयज्ञप्रजासगैरेते हि दिवमास्थिताः॥
en: These people have acquired the celestial region by their charities and by performing sacrifices and by procreating children.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: दत्त्वा तु सततं तेऽस्तु कौरवाणां धुरन्धर। दानयज्ञक्रियायुक्ता बुद्धिर्धर्मोपचायिनी॥
en: O foremost scion of Kuru's race, these men devoted their virtuous intellects to the celebration of sacrifices and charities by always performing acts of charity.

description: The superiority of charity and devotion
sn: यत्र ते नृपशार्दूल संदेहो वै भविष्यति। श्वः प्रभाते हि वक्ष्यामि संध्या हि समुपस्थिता॥
en: O powerful prince, as night has set in I shall explain to you in the morning whatever doubts may spring up in your mind.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतं मे भवतस्तात सत्यव्रतपराक्रमा दानधर्मेण महता ये प्राप्तास्त्रिदिवं नृपाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have heard from you. O sire, the names of those kings who have ascended to the celestial region. O you whose power is great in the observance of the vow of truth, by following the religion of gift.

sn: इमांस्तु श्रोतुमिच्छामि धर्मान् धर्मभृतां वर। दानं कतिविधं देयं किं तस्य च फलं लभेत्॥
en: How many kinds of gifts are there? What are the fruits of the several kinds of gifts respectively.

sn: कथं केभ्यश्च धर्म्य च दानं दातव्यमिष्यते। कैः कारणैः कतिविधं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: For what reasons what kinds of gifts made to what persons yield merits? Indeed, to what persons should what gifts be made? For what reasons are how many kinds of gifts to be made? I wish to hear all this in full.

sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु तत्त्वेन कौन्तेय दानं प्रति ममानघ। यथा दानं प्रदातव्यं सर्ववर्णेषु भारत॥
en: Bhishma said Listen, O son of Kunti, in full to me, O sinless one, as I describe the subject of gifts. Indeed, I shall tell you, Bharata, how gifts should be made to all the orders of men.

sn: धर्मादाद् भयात् कामात् कारुण्यादिति भारत। दानं पञ्चविधं ज्ञेयं कारणैर्निबोध तत्॥
en: Gifts are made from desire of merit, from desire of profit, from fear, from free choice, and from pity. O Bharata! Gifts, therefore, should be known to be of five sorts. Listen now to the reasons for which gifts are thus divided into five classes.

sn: इह कीर्तिमवाप्नोति प्रेत्य चानुत्तमं सुखम्। इति दानं प्रदातव्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽनसूयता॥
en: With mind shorn of malice, one should make gifts to Brahmanas, for by making gifts to them one wins fame in this world and great happiness in the next.

sn: ददाति वा दास्यति वा मह्यं दत्तमनेन वा। इत्यर्थिभ्यो निशम्यैव सर्वं दातव्यमर्थिने॥
en: He is in the habit of making gifts; or he will make gifts; or he has already made gifts to me. Hearing such words from solicitors, one gives away all kinds of riches to a particular solicitor.

sn: नास्याहं न मदीयोऽयं पापं कुर्याद् विमानितः। इति दद्याद् भयादेव इंढ मूढाय पण्डितः॥
en: I am not his, nor is he mine. If disregarded, he may injure me. From such motives of fear even a learned and wise man may make gifts to an ignorant wretch.

sn: प्रियो मेऽयं प्रियोऽस्याहमिति सम्प्रेक्ष्य बुद्धिमान्। वयस्यामैवमक्लिष्टं दानं दद्यादतन्द्रितः॥
en: This one is dear to me. I also am dear to him. Actuated by considerations like these, an intelligent person, freely and with alacrity, makes gifts to a friend.

sn: दीनश्च याचते चायमल्पेनापि हि तुष्यति। इति दद्याद् दरिद्राय कारुण्यादिति सर्वथा॥
en: The person who solicits me is poor. He is, again, satisfied with little. From considerations such as these, one should always make gifts to the poor, moved by pity.

sn: इति पञ्चविधं दानं पुण्यकीर्तिविवर्धनम्। यथाशक्त्या प्रदातव्यमेवमाह प्रजापतिः॥
en: These are the five sorts of gift. They increase the giver's merits and fame. The Lord of all creatures has said that one should always make gifts according to his power. a

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: युधिष्ठिर पितामह महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद। आगमैर्बहुभिः स्फीतो भवान् नः प्रवरे कुले॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, you are endued with great wisdom. Indeed, you are fully conversant with every branch of learning. In our great family you are the only individual who have mastered sciences.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: त्वत्तो धर्मार्थसंयुक्तमायत्यां च सुखोदयम्। आश्चर्यभूतं लोकस्य श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यरिंन्दम॥
en: I wish to hear from you discourses of Religion and Profit, which bring on happiness in the next world, and that are fraught with wonder to all creatures.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: अयं च कालः सम्प्राप्तो दुर्लभो ज्ञातिबान्धवैः। शास्ता च न हि नः कश्चित् त्वामृते पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: The time that has come is full of distress. The like of it does not generally come to kinsmen and friends. Indeed, except you, O foremost of men, we have now none else who can take the place of an instructor.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: यदि तेऽहमनुग्राह्यो भ्रातृभिः सहितोऽनघ। वक्तुमर्हसि नः प्रश्नं यत् त्वां पृच्छामि पार्थिव॥
en: If, O sinless one, I with my brothers deserve your labour, you should answer the questions I wish to ask you.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: अयं नारायणः श्रीमान् सर्वपार्थिवसम्मतः। भवन्तं बहुमानेन प्रश्रयेण च सेवते॥
en: This one is Narayana who is gifted with every prosperity and is honoured by all the kings. Even he waits upon you, showing you every indulgence and honoring you greatly.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: अस्य चैव समक्षं त्वं पार्थिवानां च सर्वशः। भ्रातृणां च प्रियार्थं मे स्नेहाद् भाषितुमर्हसि।॥
en: You should describe it to me, through affection, for my benefit as also for that of my brothers, in the presence of Vasudeva himself and of all these kings.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा स्नेहादागतसम्भ्रमः। भीष्मो भागीरथीपुत्र इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words of king Yudhishthira, Bhishma, the son of the river Ganges, filled with joy on account of his affection for the monarch and his brothers, said what follows.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: भीष्म उवाच अहं ते कथयिष्यामि कथामतिमनोहराम्। अस्य विष्णोः पुरा राजन् प्रभावो यो मया श्रुतः॥
en: Bhishma said I shall certainly recite to you discourses that are charming on the subject, o king, of the power of this Vishnu as displayed in days of yore and as I have heard (from my preceptors).

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: यश्च गोवृषभाङ्कस्य प्रभावस्तं च मे शृणु। रुद्राण्याः संश्यो यश्च दम्पत्योस्तं च मे शृणु।॥
en: Listen to me also as I describe the power of that great god who has a bull for his emblem. Listen to me as I describe also the doubt that filled the mind of the wife of Rudra and that of Rudra himself.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: व्रतं चचार धर्मात्मा कृष्णो द्वादशवार्षिकम्। दीक्षितं चागतौ द्रष्टुमुभौ नारदपर्वतौ॥ कृष्णद्वैपायनश्चैव धौम्यश्च जपतां वरः। देवलः काश्यपश्चैव हस्तिकाश्यप एव च॥
en: Once on a time the virtuous Krishna observed a vow extending for two and ten years. For seeing him who had performed the rite of initiation for the observance of his great vow, there came to that place. Narada and Parvata, and Krishna Dvaipayana and Dhaumya that foremost of silent reciters, Devala, Kashyapa, and Hastikashyapa.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: अपरे चर्षयः सन्तो दीक्षादमसमन्विताः। शिष्यैरनुगता: सिद्धैर्देवकल्पैस्तपोधनैः॥
en: Other Rishis also, gifted with initiation and self-restraint, followed by their disciples and accompanied by many Siddhas and many ascetics of great merit, came there.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: तेषामतिथिसत्कारमर्चनीयं कुलोचितम्। देवकीतनयः प्रीतो देवकल्पमकल्पयत्॥
en: The son of Devaki offered them such laudable honors of hospitality as are offered to the gods alone.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: हरितेषु सुवर्णेषु बर्हिष्केषु नवेषु च। उपोवविविशुः प्रीता विष्टेरेषु महर्षयः॥
en: Those great Rishis sat themselves down upon seats some of which were green and some were goldhued and some were made of the plumes of the peacock and some were perfectly new and fresh.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: कथाश्चक्रुस्ततस्ते तु मधुरा धर्मसंहिताः। राजर्षीणां सुराणां च ये वसन्ति तपोधनाः॥
en: Thus seated, they began to converse sweetly with one another on subjects of Religion and Duty as also with many royal sages and celestials.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: ततो नारायणं तेजो व्रतचर्येन्धनोत्थितम्। वक्त्रानिःसृत्य कृष्णस्य वह्निरद्भुतकर्मणः॥
en: At that time the energy, in the form of fire, of Narayana, rising from the fuel that consisted of the rigid observance of his vow, came out of the mouth of Krishna of wonderful deeds.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: सोऽग्निर्ददाह तं शैलं सदुमं सलताक्षुपम्। सपक्षिमृगसंघातं सश्वापदसरीसृपम्॥
en: That fire began to consume those mountains with their trees and creepers and little plants, as also with their birds and deer and beasts of prey and reptiles.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: मृगैश्च विविधाकारैर्हाहाभूतमचेतनम्। शिखरं तस्य शैलस्य मथितं दीनदर्शनम्॥
en: Soon the summit of that mountain presented a distressing and pitiful sight. Inhabited by animals of various kinds which began to utter cries of woe and pain, the summit soon became bereft of every living creature. more

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: स तु वहिर्महाज्वालो दग्ध्वा सर्वमशेषतः। विष्णो:समीप आगम्य पादौ शिष्यवदस्पृशत्॥
en: That fire of powerful flames, having consumed everything without living a residue, at last returned to Vishnu and touched his feet like a docile disciple.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: ततो विष्णुर्गिरिं दृष्ट्वा निर्दग्धमरिकर्शनः। सौम्यैदृष्टिनिपातैस्तं पुनः प्रकृतिमानयत्॥
en: That crusher of enemies, viz., Krishna, seeing that mountain burnt, cast a benignant look upon it and thereby brought it back to its former condition.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: तथैव स गिरिभूर्यः प्रपुष्पितलताद्रुमः। सपक्षिगणसंघुष्टः सश्वापदसरीसृपः॥
en: That mountain thereupon once becaine bedecked with flowering trees and creepers, and once more echoed with the notes and cries of birds and deer and animals of prey and reptiles.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: तमद्भुतमचिन्त्यं च दृष्ट्वा मुनिगणस्तदा। विस्मितो दृष्टरोमा च बभूवास्राविलेक्षणः॥
en: Seeing that wonderful and inconceivable spectacle, al the ascetics became filled with wonder. Their hair stood erect and their vision was disturbed with tears.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: ततो नारायणो दृष्ट्वा तानृषीन् विस्मयान्वितान्। प्रश्रितं मधुरं स्निग्धं पप्रच्छ वदतां वरः॥
en: Seeing those Rishis thus stricken with wonder, that foremost of speakers. Narayana, addressed them in these sweet and refreshing words:

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: किमर्थमृषिपूगस्य त्यक्तसङ्स्य नित्यशः। निर्ममस्यागमवतो विस्मयः समुपागतः॥
en: Why, indeed, has wonder filled the hearts of this collection of Rishis, these ascetics who are always free from attachment of every kind, who are divested of the idea of mineness, and who are fully conversant with every sacred science.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: एतन्मे संशयं सर्वे याथातथ्यमनिन्दिताः। ऋषयो वक्तुमर्हन्ति निश्चितार्थं तपोधनाः॥
en: These Rishis having penances for wealth and freed from every stain, should explain to me truly this doubt which has originated in my mind.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: ऋषिरुवाच भवान् विसृजते लोकान् भवान् संहरते पुनः। भवान् शीतं भवानुष्णं भवानेष च वर्षति॥
en: The Rishis said You are the creator of all the worlds, and the destroyer of them again. You are Winter, you are Summer, and you are the season of Rains.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: पृथिव्यां यानि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च। तेषां पिता त्वं माता त्वं प्रभुः प्रभव एव च॥
en: Of all the creatures, mobile and immobile, that exist on Earth, you are the father, you are the mother, you are the master, and you are the origin.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: एवं नो विस्मयकरं संशयं मधुसूदन। त्वमेवार्हसि कल्याण वक्तुं वह्नर्विनिर्गमम्॥
en: Even this, O destroyer of Madhu, is a matter of wonder and doubt with us. O source of all auspiciousness, you should explain to us that doubt, viz., the issue of fire from your mouth.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: ततो विगतसंत्रासा वयमप्यरिकशन। यच्छुतं यच्च दृष्टं नस्तत् प्रवक्ष्यामहे हरे॥
en: Our fears being removed, we shall then, O Hari, recite to you what we have heard and seen.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: वासुदेव उवाच एतद् वै वैष्णवं तेजो मम वक्त्राद् विनिःसृतम्। कृष्णवा युगान्ताभो येनायं मथितो गिरिः॥
en: Vasudeva said The fire that came out from my mouth and that resembles the all destroying Yuga Fire in splendour, and by which this mountain has been crushed and scorched is nothing else than the power of Vishnu.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: ऋषयश्चार्तिमापन्ना जितक्रोधा जितेन्द्रियाः। भवन्तो व्यथिताश्चासान् देवकल्पास्तपोधनाः॥
en: Ye Rishis, ye are persons who have governed anger, who have brought your senses under complete control, who are gifted with wealth of penances, and who are very gods in power. Yet you have allowed yourselves to be agitated and distressed.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: व्रतचर्यापरीतस्य तपस्विव्रतसेवया। मम वह्निः समुद्भूतो न वै व्यथितुमर्हथ॥
en: I am now engaged wholly with the observances about a rigid: vow. Indeed, on account of my observing the vows of an ascetic, a fire came out from my mouth. You should not allow yourselves to be agitated therefor.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: व्रतं चर्तुमिहायातस्त्वहं गिरिमिमं शुभम्। पुत्रं चात्मसमं वीर्ये तपसा लब्धुमागतः॥
en: It is for observing a rigid vow that I came to this charming and sacred mountain. The object that has brought me here is to acquire, by the help of penances, a son that would be my equal in power.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: ततो ममात्मा यो देहे सोऽग्निर्भूत्वा विनिः सृतः। गतश्च वरदं द्रष्टुं सर्वलोकपितामहम्॥
en: On account of iny penances, the Soul existing in my body became changed into fire and came out of my mouth. That fire had gone to see the boongiving Grandfather all the universe.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: तेन चात्मानुशिष्टो मे पुत्रत्वे मुनिसत्तमाः। तेजसोऽर्धेन पुत्रस्ते भवितेति वृषध्वजः॥
en: The Grandfather, ye foremost of ascetics, told my soul that the energy of the great god having the bull for his embalmer would take birth as my son.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: सोऽयं वह्निरुपागम्य पादमूले ममान्तिकम्। शिष्यवत् परिचर्यार्थं शान्तः प्रकृतिमागतः॥
en: That fire returning from its mission, has come back to me and approached my feet like a disciple desirous of attending to me dutifully. Indeed, renouncing its fury it has come back to its own proper nature.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: एतदेव रहस्यं वः पद्मनाभस्य धीमतः। मया प्रोक्तं समासेन न भी: कार्या तपोधनाः॥
en: I have thus told you, in brief, a mystery belonging to Him who has the lotus for the origin and who is gifted with great intelligence. Ye Rishis having penances for wealth, you should not yield to fear.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: सर्वत्र गतिरव्यग्रा भवतां दीर्घदर्शनात्। तपस्वितसंदीप्ता ज्ञानविज्ञानशोभिताः॥
en: You are gifted with farreaching vision. You can proceed to every place without any obstacle. Radiant with vows observed by ascetics, you are adorned with knowledge and science.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: यच्छुतं यच्च वो दृष्टं दिवि वा यदि वा भुवि। आश्चर्यं परमं किंचित् तद् भवन्तो ब्रुवन्तु मे॥
en: I now ask you to tell me something that is highly wonderful which you have heard of or seen on Earth or in the celestial region.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: तस्यामृतनिकाशस्य वाङ्भधोरस्ति मे स्पृहा। भवद्भिः कथितस्येह तपोवननिवासिभिः॥
en: I am anxious to taste the honey of words which will drop from your lips and which, I am sure, will be as sweet as a jet of nectar itself.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: यद्यप्यहमदृष्टं वो दिव्यमद्युतदर्शनम्। दिवि वा भुवि वा किंचित् परयाम्यमरदर्शनाः॥ प्रकृतिः सा मम परा न क्वचित् प्रतिहन्यते। न चात्मगतमैश्वर्यमाश्चर्यं प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: If I see anything on Earth or in the celestial region, which is highly delightful and wonderful but which is unknown to all of you, O god like Rishis, that is on account of my own supreme Nectar which is incapable of being obstructed by anything. Anything wonderful which I know by nature or by my own inspiration, ceases to appear wonderful to me.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: श्रद्धेयः कथितो ह्यर्थं: सज्जनश्रवणं गतः। चिरं तिष्ठति मेदिन्यां शैले लेख्यामिवार्पितम्॥
en: Anything, however, that is recited by pious persons and that is heard from those who are good, deserves to be accepted with respect and faith. Such discourses exist on Earth for a long time and will last like characters engraved on rocks.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: तदहं सज्जनमुखान्निःसृतं तत्समागमे। कथयिष्याम्यहमहो बुद्धिदीपकरं नृणाम्॥
en: I wish, therefore, to hear at this meeting of ourselves, something dropping from the lips of persons who are good and who cannot fail to be productive of good to men.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: ततो मुनिगणाः सर्वे विस्मिताः कृष्णसंनिधौ। नेत्रैः पद्मदलप्रख्यैरपश्यंस्तं जनार्दनम्॥
en: Hearing these words of Krishna, all those ascetics became filled with wonder. They began to look at Janardana with those eyes of theirs that were as beautiful and large as the petals of the lotus.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: वर्धयन्तस्तथैवान्ये पूजयन्तस्तथाऽपरे। वाग्भिर्ऋग्भूषितार्थाभिः स्तुवन्तो मधुसूदनम्॥
en: Some of them began to glorify him and some began to adore him with respect. Indeed, all of them then sang the praises of the destroyer of Madhu with words whose meanings were adorned with the eternal Richs.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: ततो मुनिगणाः सर्वे नारदं देवदर्शनम्। तदा नियोजयामासुर्वचने वाक्यकोविदम्॥
en: all those ascetics then appointed Narada, that foremost of all persons conversant with words, to satisfy the request of Vasudeva.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: मुनयः ऊचुः यदाश्चर्यमचिन्त्यं च गिरौ हिमवति प्रभो। अनुभूतं मुनिगणैस्तीर्थयात्रापरैर्मुने॥ तद् भवानृषिसंघस्य हितार्थं सर्वमादितः। यथा दृष्टं हृषीकेशे सर्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: The Ascetics said You should, O Narada, describe in full, from the beginning, to Hrishikesha, that wonderful and inconceivable incident which took place, O powerful one, on the mountains of Himavat and which, O 'ascetic, was seen by those of us who had gone there in course of our sojourn to the sacred waters. Indeed, for the behoof of all the Rishis here collected, you should recite that incident.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: एवमुक्तः स मुनिभिर्नारदो भगवान् मुनिः। कथयामास देवर्षिः पूर्ववृत्तामिमां कथाम्॥
en: Thus addressed by those ascetics, the celestial Rishi, viz., the divine Narada, then recited the following story whose incidents had ken place sometime before.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततो नारायणसुहन्नारदो भगवानृषिः। शङ्करस्योमया साधू संवादं प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Bhishma said Then Narada, that holy Rishi, that friend of Narayana, recited the following discourse that took place between Shankara and his wife Uma.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: नारद उवाच तपश्चचार धर्मात्मा वृषभाङ्कः सुरेश्वरः। पुण्ये गिरौ हिमवति सिद्धचारणसेविते॥
en: Narada said Once on a time the pious lord of all the celestials, viz., Mahadeva having bull for his emblem, practised severe penances on the sacred mountains of Himavat the resort of Siddhas and Charanas,

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: नानौषधियुते रम्ये नानापुष्पसमाकुले। अप्सरोगणसंकीर्णे भूतसंघनिषेविते॥
en: That charming mountain is overgrown with various kinds of herbs and adorned with various flowers. At that time they were inhabited by the different tribes of Apsaras and crowds of ghosts.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: तत्र देवो मुदा युक्तो भूतसंघशतैर्वृतः। नानारूपैर्विरूपैश्च दिव्यैरद्भुतदर्शनैः॥
en: There the great god sat, filled with joy, and encircled by hundreds of ghostly beings who presented various aspects to the eye of the beholder. Some of them were ugly and awkward, some were very beautiful, and some presented the most wonderful appearances.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: सिंहव्याघ्रगजप्रख्यैः सर्वजातिसमन्वितैः। क्रोष्टुकद्वीपिवदनैर्ऋक्षर्षभमुखैस्तथा॥ उलूकवदनैर्भीमैर्वृकश्येनमुखैस्तथा।
en: Some, had faces like the lion's, some like the tiger's, and some like the elephant's. In fact, the faces of those goblins presented every variety of animal faces. Some had faces resembling that of the jackal; some those of the pard's; some like the ape's; some like the bull's.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: नानावणैर्मंगमुखैः सर्वजातिसमन्वितैः॥
en: Some of them had faces like the owl's; some like the hawk's; some had faces like those of the deer.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: किंनरैर्यक्षगन्धर्वे रक्षोभूतगणैस्तथा। दिव्यपुष्पसमाकीर्णं दिव्यज्वालासमाकुलम्॥
en: The great god was also encircled by Kinnaras and Yakshas and Gandharvas and Rakshasas and various other created beings. The retreat of Mahadeva also abounded with celestial flowers and shone with celestial rays of light.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: दिव्यचन्दनसंयुक्तं दिव्यधूपेन धूपितम्। तत् सदो वृषभाङ्कस्य दिव्यवादिननादितम्॥
en: It was perfumed with celestial sandal and celestial incense was burnt on all sides. And it echoe with the sounds of celestial instruments.

description: Religion and profit, which bring on happiness in the next world. The history of Rudra and Uma
sn: मृदङ्गपणवोद्दष्टं शङ्भेरीनिनादितम्। नृत्यद्भिर्भूतसंघेश्च बहिणैश्च समन्ततः॥
en: Indeed, it resounded with the beat of Mridangas and Panavas, the blare of conchs and the sound of drums. It was full of goblins of diverse tribes that danced in joy and with peacocks also that danced with plumes outspread.
