sn: तेन विश्वं कृतमेतद्धि राजन् स जीवयत्यात्मनैवात्मयोनिः। ततो देवासुरान् मानवांश्च लोकानृषीश्चापि पितॄन् प्रजाश्चा समासेन विधिवत्प्राणिलोकान् सर्वान् सदा भूतपतिः सिसृक्षुः॥ शुभाशुभं स्थावरं जङ्गमं च विष्वक्सेनात् सर्वमेतत् प्रतीहि। यद वर्तते यच्च भविष्यतीह सर्वं ह्येतत् केशव त्वं प्रतीहि॥ मृत्युश्चैव प्राणिनामन्तकाले साक्षात् कृष्ण: शाश्वतो धर्मवाहः। भूतं च यच्चेह न विद्म किंचिद् विष्वक्सेनात् सर्वमेतत् प्रतीहि॥
en: Forsooth, O king, it is this Krishna who has created this universe. He has originated from his own self; it is he who causes all things to exist through his own power. He it is who has created the celestials, the Asuras, the human beings, the worlds, the Rishis, the departed manes and all creatures. Desirous of creating, that Lord of all creatures duly created the entire universe of life. Know that good and evil, mobile and immobile, have all originated from this one who is Vishvaksena. Whatever exists, and whatever will come into being, all is Keshava. This Krishna is also the death which overtakes all creatures when their end comes. He is eternal and it is he who upholds the cause of Virtue Whatever existed in the past, and whatever we do not know, indeed, all that also is this Vishvaksena.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: यत् प्रशस्तं च लोकेषु पुण्यं यच्च शुभाशुभम्। तत्सर्वं केशवोऽचिन्त्यो विपरीतमतः परम्॥
en: All that is noble and meritorious in the universe, all that is good and evil, is Keshava who is inconccivable. Hence, it is absurd to think of anything which is superior to Keshava.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: एतादृशः केशवाऽतश्च भूयो नारायणः परमश्चाव्ययश्च। मध्याद्यन्तस्य जगतस्तस्थुषश्च बुभूषतां प्रभवश्चाव्ययश्च॥
en: Keshava is such. More than this. He is Narayana, the highest of the high, immutable and undecaying. He is the cternal and changeless cause of the entire mobile and immobile universe with its beginning, middle, and end, as also of all creatures whose birth follows their wish.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्रूहि ब्राह्मणपूजायां व्युष्टिं त्वं मधुसूदन। वेत्ता त्वमस्य चार्थस्य वेद त्वां हि पितामहः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell us, O destroyer of Madhu, the prosperity which originates from the worship of the Brahmanas. You are a master of this subject. Indeed, our grandfather knows you.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: वासुदेव उवाच शृणुष्वावहितो राजन् द्विजानां भरतर्षभ। यथा तत्त्वेन वदतो गुणान् वै कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Vasudeva said Hear me, O king, with attention, O chief of Bharata's race, as I recite to you what the merits of the Brahmanas are, O foremost one of Kuru's race.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: द्वारवत्यां समासीनं पुरा मां कुरुनन्दन। प्रद्युन्म: परिपप्रच्छ ब्राह्मणैः परिकोपितः॥ किं फलं ब्राह्मणेष्वस्ति पूजायां मधुसूदन। ईश्वरत्वं कुतस्तेषामिहैव च परत्र च॥
en: Once on a time while I was scated at Dvaravati, O delighter of the Kurus, my son Pradyumna, enraged by certain Brahmanas, came to me and said, O destroyer of Madhu, what mcrit is there for adoring the Brahmanas. Whence is their lordship derived both in this world and in the next.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: सदा द्विजातीन् सम्पूज्य किं फलं तत्र मानद। एतद् ब्रूहि स्फुटं सर्वे सुमहान् संशयोऽत्र मे॥
en: O giver of honours, what rewards are gained by constantly adoring the Brahmanas? Kindly explain this clearly to me, for my mind is disturbed by doubts about this.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: इत्युक्ते वचने तस्मिन् प्रद्युम्नेन तथा त्वहम्। प्रत्यब्रुवं महाराज यत् तच्छृणु समाहितः॥
en: When Pradyuinna said, these words to me, I answered him as follows. Do you hear, O king, with rapt attention, what those words were.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: व्युष्टिं ब्राह्मणपूजायां रौक्मिणेय निबोध मे। एते हि सोमराजान ईश्वराः सुखदुःखयोः॥
en: O child of Rukmini, listen to me as I tell you what prosperity one may acquire by adoring the Brahmanas. When one tries to acquire the threefold objects of life (viz., Virtue, Profit and Pleasure). or Emancipation, or fame and prosperity, or the treatment and cure of disease, or the worship of the deities and the departed manes, he should take care to please the twiceborn ones. They are each a king Soma. They are the dispensers of happiness and misery.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: अस्मिल्लोकै रौक्मिणेय तथामुष्मिंश्च पुत्रका ब्राह्मणप्रमुखं सौम्यं न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा॥
en: O child of Rukmini, whether in this or in the next world, O son, everything agrecable has originated from the Brahmanas. I have no doubt in this.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: ब्राह्मणप्रतिपूजायामायुः कीर्तिर्यशो बलम्। लोका लोकेश्वराश्चैव सर्वे ब्राह्मणपूजकाः॥ त्रिवर्गे चापवर्गे च यश:श्रीरोगशान्तिषु। देवतापितृपूजासु संतोष्याश्चैव नो द्विजाः॥
en: From the adoration of the Brahinanas originate achievements and fame and strength. Men and the Regents of the universe, adore the Brahmanas. We should satisfy the Brahmanas for the sake of accomplishment on holy deeds, wealth and desires, for attainment of emancipation, fame, grace and health as also at the time of offering pray to gods and Pitris.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: तत्कथं वै नाद्रियेयमीश्वरोऽस्मीति पुत्रका मा ते मन्युर्महाबाहो भवत्वत्र द्विजान् प्रति॥
en: How then, O son, can we disregard them, thinking that we are lords of the Earth? O mighty armed onc, do not allow your anger to embrace the Brahmanas as its objeci.,

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: ब्राह्मणा हि महद्भूतमस्मिल्लोके परत्र चा भस्म कुयुर्जगदिदं क्रुद्धाः प्रत्यक्षदर्शिनः॥
en: In this as also the next world, Brahmanas are considered as great Beings. They have direct knowledge of everything in the universe. Verily, they are capable of reducing everything into ashes, if angry.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: अन्यानपि सृजेयुश्च लोकालोकेश्वरांस्तथा। कथं तेषु न वर्तेरन् सम्यग् ज्ञानात् सुतेजसः॥
en: They are capable of creating other worlds and other Regents of worlds. Why then should not persons gifted with energy and true knowledge treat thein with obcdience and respect?

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: अवसन्मद्गृहे तात ब्राह्मणो हरिपिङ्गलः। चीरवासा बिल्वदण्डी दीर्घश्मश्रुः कृशो महान्॥
en: Formerly in my house, O son, lived the Brahmana Durvasas whose complexion was green and tawny. Clad in rags, he had a stick made of the Bilva tree. His bcard was long and he was greatly emaciated.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: दीर्धेभ्यश्च मनुष्येभ्यः प्रमाणादधिको भुवि। स स्वैरं चरते लोकान् ये दिव्या ये च मानुषाः॥ इमां गाथां गायमानश्चत्वरेषु सभासु च। दुर्वाससं वासयेत् को ब्राह्मणं सत्कृतं गृहे।॥
en: He was taller in stature than the tallest man on Earth. Wandering over all the worlds of human beings and of the deities and other superior beings, he sang constantly among assemblies and in public squares. Who is there who would cause the Brahmana Durvasas to live in his house, doing the duties of hospitality towards him?

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: रोषणः सर्वभूतानां सूक्ष्मेऽप्यपकृते कृते। परिभाषां च मे श्रुत्वा को नु दद्यात् प्रतिश्रयम्॥
en: He becomes wroth with cvery one if he finds even the slightest transgression! Hearing this about my nature, who is there who will give me refuge?

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: यो मां कश्चिद् वासयीत न स मां कोपयेदिति। यस्मान्नाद्रियते कश्चित् ततोऽहं समवासयम्॥
en: Indeed, he who would give me shelter as a guest should not do anything to anger me! When I saw that no one ventured to give him shelter in his house, I invited him and made him live in my abode.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: स सम्भुङ्क्ते सहस्राणां बहूनामन्नमेकदा। एकदा सोऽल्पकं भुङ्क्ते न चैवैति पुनर्गृहान्॥
en: On certain days hic would cat the food sufficient for the needs of thousands of persons. On other days he would eat very little. On some days he would go out of my house and would not return.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: अकस्माच्च प्रहसति तथाकस्मात् प्ररोदिति। न चास्य वयसा तुल्यः पृथिव्यामभवत् तदा॥
en: He would sometimes laugh without any reason and sometimes cry uselessly At that time there was nobody on Earth a old as he.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: अथ स्वावसथं गत्वा स शय्यास्तरणानि च। कन्याश्चालंकृता दग्ध्वा ततो व्यपगतः पुनः॥
en: One day, entering the quarters which were given to him, he burnt all the beds and coveriets and all the welladorned damsels who were there for serving him. Doing this, he went Out.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: अथ मामब्रवीद् भूयः स मुनिः संशितव्रतः। कृष्ण पायसमिच्छामि भोक्तुमित्येव सत्वरः॥
en: Of highly praiseworthy vows, he met me shortly after this and addressing me, said, O Krishna, I wish to cal frumenty forthwith.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: तदैव तु मया तस्य चित्तज्ञेन गृहे जनः। सर्वाण्यन्नानि पानानि भक्ष्याश्चोच्चावचास्तथा॥
en: Having understood his mind previously. I had set my servams to prepare every kind of food and drink.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: भवन्तु सत्कृतानीह पूर्वमेव प्रचोदितः। ततोऽहं ज्वलमानं वै पायसं प्रत्यवेदयम्॥
en: Indeed, many excellent viands had been kept ready. As soon as I was asked, I caused hot frumenty to be brought and offered to the ascetic.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: तं भुक्त्वैव स तु क्षिप्रं ततो वचनमब्रवीत्। क्षिप्रमङ्गानि लिम्पस्व पायसेनेति स स्म ह॥
en: Having eaten some, he quickly said to me, O Krishna, take some of this frumenty and smear all your limbs with it.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: अविमृश्यैव च ततः कृतवानस्मि तत् तथा। तेनोच्छिष्टेन गात्राणि शिरश्चैवाभ्यमक्षयम्॥
en: Unhesitatingly I did as directed. Indeed, with the residuc of that frumenty I smeared my body and head.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: स ददर्श तदाभ्याशे मातरं ते शुभाननाम्। तामपि स्मयमानां स पायसेनाभ्यलेपयम्॥
en: The ascetic at that time saw your beautiful mother standing near. Laughing the while, he sineared her body also with that frumenty.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: मुनिः पायसदिग्धाङ्गी रथे तूर्णमयोजयत्। तमारुह्य रथं चैव निर्ययौ स गृहान्मम॥
en: The ascetic then caused your mother, whose body was sicared over with frumenty, to be yoked to a car without any delay. Ascending that car he started from my house.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: अग्निवर्णो ज्वलन् धीमान् स द्विजो रथधुर्यवत्। प्रतोदेनातुदद् वाला रुक्मिणी मम पश्यतः॥
en: Highly intelligent that Brahmana shone with effulgence like fire, and struck, before, me, my youthful Rukmini, as if she were an animal born to drag the cars of human beings.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: न च मे स्तोकमप्यासीद् दुःखीमीर्ष्याकृतं तदा। तथा स राजमार्गेण महता निर्ययौ बहिः॥
en: Secing this, I did not feel the slightest grief bom of malice or the desire to injure the Rishi. Having yoked Rukmini to the car, he went out, desirous of passing along the high road of the city.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्ये दाशार्हा जातमन्यवः। तत्राजल्पन् मिथः केचित् समाभाष्य परस्परम्॥ ब्राह्मणा एव जायेरन् नान्यो वर्णः कथंचन। को ह्येनं रथमास्थाय जीवेदन्यः पुमानिह॥
en: Secing that extraordinary spectacle, some Dasharhas, filled with anger, addressed one another and began to converse thus; Who else is there on Earth who would live afier having yoke Rukmini to a car! Indeed, let the world be filled with Bralımanas only! Let no other orders take birth here!

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: आशीविषविषं तीक्ष्णं ततस्तीक्ष्णतरो द्विजः। ब्रह्माशीविषदग्धस्य नास्ति कश्चिच्चिकित्सकः॥
en: The poison of a virulent snake greatly powerful. More powerful thc poison is a Brahmana. There is no physician for a person who has been bit or burn by the virulent snake of a Brahmana.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: तस्मिन् व्रजति दुर्धर्षे प्रास्खलद् रुक्मिणी पथि। तन्नामर्षयत श्रीमांस्ततस्तूर्णमचोदयत्॥
en: As the irresistible Durvasas proceeded on the car, Rukmini tottered on the road and frequently dropped down. At this the twiceborn Rishi became angry and began to urge Rukmini on by striking her with the whip.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: ततः परमसंक्रुद्धो रथात् प्रस्कन्ध स द्विजः। पदातिरुत्पथेनैव प्राद्रवद् दक्षिणामुखः॥
en: At last, filled with an irresistible passion, the Brahmana leaped down from the car, and fled towards the south, running on foot, over a pathless ground.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: तमत्पथेन धावन्तमन्वधावं द्विजोत्तमम्। तथैव पायसादिग्धः प्रसीद भगवन्निति॥
en: Seeing that foremost of Brahmanas, flying along the pathless ground, we followed him, although we were smeared with frumenty, exclaiming behind him, Be pleased with us, O holy onc.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: ततो विलोक्य तेजस्वी ब्राह्मणो मामुवाच ह। जितः क्रोधस्त्वया कृष्ण प्रकृत्यैव महाभुज॥
en: Gifted with great energy, the Brahmana, seeing me, said, O mightyarmed Krishna, you have subdued anger by the strength of your nature.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: न तेऽपराधमिह वै दृष्टवानस्मि सुव्रत। प्रीतोऽस्मि तव गोविन्द वृणु कामान् यथेप्सितान्।।३८
en: O you of excellent vows, I have not found the slightest fault in you. O Govinda, I have been highly pleased with you. Do you solicit the fruition of such desires as you please.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: प्रसन्नस्य च मे तात पश्य व्युष्टिं यथाविधि। यावदेव मनुष्याणामन्ने भावो भविष्यति॥ यथैवान्ने तथा तेषां त्वयि भावो भविष्यति। यावच्च पुण्या लोकेषु त्वयि कीर्तिर्भविष्यति॥
en: Behold duly, O son, what the power is of myself when I become pleased with any one. As long as celestials and human beings will continue to entertain a liking for food, so long will every one among them cherish the same liking for you that they cherish for their food. As long, again as there will be Virtue in the several worlds, so long will the fame of your deeds last.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: त्रिषु लोकेषु तावच्च वैशिष्ट्यं प्रतिपत्स्यसे। सुप्रियः सर्वलोकस्य भविष्यसि जनार्दन॥
en: Indeed, your distinction will last so long in the three worlds. O Janardana, agreeable you will be to all persons.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: यत्ते भिन्नं च दग्धं य यच्च किंचिद् विनाशितम्। सर्वं तथैव द्रष्टासि विशिष्टं वा जनार्दन॥
en: Whatever articles of yours have been broken or burnt or otherwise destroyed (by me). you will see restored, O Janardana, to their former state or they will reappear even in a better forin.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: यावदेतत् प्रलिप्तं ते गात्रेषु मधुसूदन। अतो मृत्युभयं नास्ति यावदिच्छसि चाच्युत॥
en: As long again, O) you of unfading glory, as you will wish to live, so long will you have no fear of death attacking you through such parts of your body as have been smeared with the frumenty I gave you.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: न तु पादतले लिप्ते कस्मात्ते पुत्रकाद्य वै। नैतन्मे प्रियमित्येवं स मां प्रीतोऽब्रवीत् तदा॥ इत्युक्तोऽहं शरीरं स्वं ददर्श श्रीसमायुतम्।
en: O son, why did you not smear that frumenty on the soles of your feet as well? By not doing it, you have acted in a way that is not approved by me. These were the words that he said, well pleased with me on that occasion. After he had ceased speaking, I saw that my body became gifted with great beauty and splendour.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: रुक्मिणी चाब्रवीत् प्रीत: सर्वस्त्रीणां वरं यश:।४५ कीर्ति चानुत्तमां लोके समवाप्स्यसि शोभने।
en: To Rukmini also, the Rishi, well pleased with her, said, O beautiful lady, you will be the foremost one of they sex in fame, and you will enjoy great glory, and achievements. You will never suffer from decrepitude or disease or loss of complexion.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: न त्वां जरा वा रोगो वा वैवयं चापि भाविनि।।४६ स्प्रक्ष्यन्ति पुण्यगन्धा च कृष्णमाराधयिष्यसि।
en: Every one will see you engaged in waiting upon Krishna, possessed as you already are with a fragrant odor which is always present in you.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: षोडशानां सहस्राणां वधूनां केशवस्य ह॥ वरिष्ठा च सलोक्या च केशवस्य भविष्यसि।
en: You will become the foremost of all wives, numbering sixteen thousand, of Keshava. At last, when the time comes for your departure from the world, you will acquire the inseparable companionship of Krishna hereafter.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: तव मातरमित्युक्त्वा ततो मां पुनरब्रवीत्॥ प्रस्थितः सुमहातेजा दुर्वासाग्निरिव ज्वलन्। एषैव ते बुद्धिरस्तु ब्राह्मणान्प्रति केशव॥ इत्युक्त्वा स तदा पुत्र तत्रैवान्तरधीयत।
en: Having said these words to your mother, the Rishi once more addressed me and uttering the following words, left the spot. Indeed, the Rishi Durvasa, shining like a fire, said, ) Keshava, may you be so disposed always towards the Brahmanas. After uttering these words, that Brahmana disappeared there and then before my eyes.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: तस्मिन्नन्तर्हिते चाहमुपांशुव्रतमाचरम्॥ यत्किचिद् ब्राह्मणो ब्रूयात् सर्वं कुर्यामिति प्रभो।
en: After his disappearance, I began to follow the vow of uttering certain Mantras silently without being heard by anybody. From that day I resolved to do whatever commands I should receive from the Brahmanas.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: एतद् व्रतमहं कृत्वा मात्रा ते सह पुत्रक॥ ततः परमहष्टात्मा प्राविशं गृहमेव च।
en: Having adopted this vow, O son, along with your mother, both of us, with hearts filled with joy re-entered our palace.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: प्रविष्टमात्रश्च गृहे सर्वं पश्यामि तनवम्॥ यद् भिन्नं यच्च वै दग्धं तेन विप्रेण पुत्रका
en: Entering our house I saw that everything which the Rishi had broken or burnt had reappeared fresh.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: ततोऽहं विस्मयं प्राप्तः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा नवं दृढम्॥ अपूजयं च मनसा रौक्मिणेय सदा द्विजान्।
en: Seeing those new articles, which had besides become more durable, I became stricken with wonder. O son of Rukmini, from that day forth I have always adored the Brahmanas in my mind.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: इत्यहं रौक्मिणेयस्य पृच्छतो भरतर्षभ॥ माहात्म्यं द्विजमुख्यस्य सर्वमाख्यातवांस्तदा।
en: This, O chief of Bharata's race, is what I said on that occasion about the greatness of those Brahmanas who are the foremost of their order.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: तथा त्वमपि कौन्तेय ब्राह्मणान् सततं प्रभो॥ पूजयस्व महाभागान् वाग्भिर्दानैश्च नित्यदा।
en: Do you also, O son of Kunti, adore the highly blessed Brahmanas every day with gifts of wealth and kind, O powerful one.

description: The prosperity following the worship of the Brahmanas
sn: एवं व्युष्टिमहं प्राप्तो ब्राह्मणस्य प्रसादजाम्। यच्च मामाह भीष्मोऽयं तत्सत्यं भरतर्षभ॥
en: It was thus that I won the prosperity I enjoy, the prosperity that is born of the favour of Brahmanas. Whatever, again, Bhishma has said of me, O chief of the Bharatas, is all true.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दुर्वाससः प्रसादात् ते यत् तदा मधुसूदन। अवाप्तमिह विज्ञानं तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said You should, O destroyer of Madhu, explain lo me that knowledge which you have acquired through the favour of Durvasas.

sn: महाभाग्यं च यत् तस्य नामानि च महात्मनः। तत् त्वत्तो ज्ञातुमिच्छामि सर्वं मतिमतां वर॥
en: O foremost of all persons having intelligence, I wish to know everything about the great blessedness and all the names of that great one truly and in detail!

sn: वासुदेव उवाच हन्त ते कीर्तयिष्यामि नमस्कृत्य कपर्दिने। यदवाप्तं मया राजच्छ्रेयो यच्चार्जितं यशः॥
en: Vasudeva said I shall recite to you the good which I have acquired and the fame which I have won through the favour of that great one. I shall describe to you the subject, after having bowed unto Kaparddin.

sn: प्रयतः प्रातरुत्थाय यदधीये विशाम्पते। प्राञ्जलिः शतरुद्रीयं तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: O king, listen to me as I recite to you that Shatarudriya which I repeat, with controlled senses, every morning after rising from bed.

sn: प्रजापतिस्तत् ससृजे तपसोऽन्ते महातपाः। शङ्कररत्वसृजत् तात प्रजा: स्थावरजङ्गमाः॥
en: The great lord of all creatures, viz., the Grandfather Brahman himself, having penances for riches, composed those Mantras, after having observed especial penances for some time. O sire, it is Shankara who created all the creatures in the universe, mobile and immobile.

sn: नास्ति किंचित्परं भूतं महादेवाद् विशाम्पते। इह त्रिष्वपि लोकेषु भूतानां प्रभावो हि सः॥
en: There is no being who is superior, O monarch, lo Mahadeva. He is the highest of all beings in the three worlds.

sn: न चैबोत्सहते स्थातुं कश्चिदने महात्मनः। न हि भूतं समं तेन त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते॥
en: There is no one who is capable of attending before the great Being. Indeed, there is no Being in the three worlds who is his equal.

sn: गन्धेनापि हि संग्रामे तस्य क्रुद्धस्य शत्रवः। विसंज्ञा हतभूयिष्ठा वेपन्ते च पतन्ति च॥
en: When he stands, filled with anger, on the field of battle, the very scent of his body deprives all foes of consciousness and they who are not killed tremble and fall down.

sn: घोरं च निनदं तस्य पर्जन्यनिनदोपमम्। श्रुत्वा विशीर्येद्धृदयं देवानामपि संयुगे॥
en: His roars are terrible, like the mutterings of clouds. Hearing those roars in battle, the very hearts of the celestials break in twain.

sn: यांश्च घोरेण रूपेण पश्येत् क्रुद्धः पिनाकधृत्। न सुरा नासुरा लोके न गन्धर्वा न पन्नगाः॥ कुपिते सुखमेधन्ते तस्मिन्नपि गुहागताः। प्रजापतेश्च दक्षस्य यजतो वितते क्रतौ॥ विव्याध कुपितो यज्ञं निर्भयस्तु भवस्तदा। धनुषा बाणमुत्सृज्य सघोषं विननाद च॥
en: When the holder of Pinaka becomes angry and assuming a terrible mien merely casts his eye upon deity, Asura, Gandharva, or snake, that individual cannot obtain peace of mind by taking shelter in the recesses of even a mountain cave. When that lord of all creatures, viz., Daksha, desirous of celebrating a sacrifice, spread his sacrifice out, the brave Bhava, yielding to anger (at Daksha's slight of him), pierced the Sacrifice. Shooting his arrow from his terrible bow, he roared aloud.

sn: ते न शर्म कुतः शान्ति विषादं लेभिरे सुराः। विद्धे च सहसा यज्ञे कुपिते च महेश्वरे॥
en: Indeed, when Maheshvara became angry and suddenly pierced with his arrow the embodied form of sacrifice, the celestials became filled with sorrow, losing happiness and tranquility of heart.

sn: तेन ज्यातलघोषेण सर्वे लोकाः समाकुलाः। बभूवुरवशाः पार्थ विषेदुश्च सुरासुराः॥
en: On account of the iwang of his bowstring the whole universe became agitated. The celestials and the Asuras, O son of Pritha, all became cheerless and stupefied.

sn: आपश्चुक्षुभिरे चैव चकम्पे च वसुन्धरा। व्यद्रवन् गिरयश्चापि द्यौः पफाल च सर्वशः॥
en: The Ocean rolled in agitation and the Earth trembled to her centre. The hills and mountains began to move from their bases and ran on all sides. The Vault of the sky became cracked.

sn: अन्धेन तमसा लोकाः प्रावृता न चकाशिरे। प्रणष्टा ज्योतिषां भाश्च सह सूर्येण भारत॥
en: All the worlds became covered with darkness. Nothing could be seen. The light of all the luminaries became darkened, along with that of the Sun himself, O Bharata.

sn: भृशं भीतास्ततः शान्तिं चक्रुः स्वस्त्ययनानि च। ऋषयः सर्वभूतानामात्मनश्च हितैषिणः॥
en: The great Rishis, stricken with fear and desirous of doing good to themselves and the universe, performed the usual usual rites of propitiation and peace.

sn: ततः सोऽभ्यद्रवद् देवान् रुद्रो रौद्रपराक्रमः। भगस्य नयने क्रुद्धः प्रहारेण व्यशातयत्॥
en: Meanwhile, Rudra of terrible prowess rushed against the celestials. Filled with anger, he tore out the eyes of Bhaga.

sn: पूषणं चाभिदुद्राव पादेन च रुषान्वितः। पुरोडाशं भक्षयतो दशनान् वै व्यशातयत्॥
en: Excited with anger, he attacked Pushan with his foot. He tore out the teeth of that god as he satemployed in cating the large sacrificial ball (called Purodasha).

sn: ततः प्रणेमुर्देवास्ते वेपमानाः स्म शङ्करम्। पुनश्च संदधे रुद्रो दीप्तं सुनिशितं शरम्॥
en: Trembling with fear, the celestials bent their heads to Shankara. Without being appeased, Rudra once more placed on his bowstring a sharp and blazing arrow.

sn: रुद्रस्य विक्रमं दृष्ट्वा भीता देवाः सहर्षिभिः। ततः प्रसादयामासुः शर्वं ते विबुधोत्तमाः॥
en: Seeing his prowess, the celestials and the Rishis became all alarmed. Those foremost of gods began to pacify him.

sn: जेपुश्च शतरुद्रीयं देवाः कृत्वाञ्जलिं तदा। संस्तूयमानस्त्रिदशैः प्रससाद महेश्वरः॥
en: Joining their hands in respect, they began to recite the Shata Rudriya Mantras. Thus lauded by the celestials, at last Maheshvara became gratified.

sn: रुद्रस्य भागं यज्ञे च विशिष्टं ते त्वकल्पयन्। भयेन त्रिदशा राजञ्छरणं च प्रपेदिरे॥
en: The deities then assigned a large share to him. Trembling with fear, O king, they sought refuge with him.

sn: तेन चैव हि तुष्टेन स यज्ञः संधितोऽभवत्। यद् यच्चापहृतं तत्र तत्तथैवान्वजीवयत्॥
en: When Rudra became pleased, the embodiment of sacrifice, which had been cut in twain, became once more united. Whatever limbs of his had been destroyed by the arrows of Mahadeva, became once more whole and sound.

sn: असुराणां पुराण्यासंस्त्रीणि वीर्यवतां दिवि। आयसं राजतं चैव सौवर्णमपि चापरम्॥
en: The Asuras gifted with great energy had formerly threc cities in the firmament. One of these had been, made of iron; one of silver; and the third of gold.

sn: नाशकत् तानि मघवा जेतुं सर्वायुधैरपि। अथ सर्वेऽमरा रुद्रं जग्मुः शरणमर्दिताः॥
en: With all his weapons, Maghavat the chief of the celestials, was unable to pierce those cities. Afflicted by the Asuras, all the celestials then sought the protection of the great Rudra.

sn: तत ऊचुर्महात्मानो देवाः सर्वे समागताः। रुद्र रौद्रा भविष्यन्ति पशवः सर्वकर्मसु॥
en: The highsouled celestials in a body addressed him, saying, O Rudra, the Asuras threaten to display their destructive influence in all deeds.

sn: जहि दैत्यान् सह पुरैर्लोकांस्त्रयस्व मानद। स तथोक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा कृत्वा विष्णुं शरोत्तमम्॥
en: Do you kill the demons and destroy their city for the protection of the three worlds, giver of honours! Thus accosted by them, he replied, saying, So be it! and then made Vishnu his excellent shafthcad.

sn: शल्यमग्निं तथा कृत्वा पुङ्गं वैवस्वतं यमम्। वेदान् कृत्वा धनुः सर्वान् ज्यां च सावित्रिमुत्तमाम्।।
en: He made the deity of fire his shaftrced, and the SunGod's son Yama the wings of that arrow. He made the Vedas his bow and the goddess Savittri his excellent bowstring.

sn: ब्रह्माणं सारथिं कृत्वा विनियुज्य च सर्वशः। त्रिपर्वणा त्रिशल्येन तेन तानि बिभेद सः॥
en: And he made the Grandfather Brahman his charioteer. Applying all these, he pierced the triple city of the Asuras with that arrow of his, consisting of three Parvans and three Shalyas.

sn: शरेणादित्यवर्णेन कालाग्निसमतेजसा। तेऽसुराः सपुरास्तत्र दग्धा रुद्रेण भारत॥
en: Indeed, O Bharata, the Asuras with their cities, were all burnt by Rudra with that arrow which had solar effulgence and whose energy resembled that of the fire which appcars at the end of the cycle for consuming all things.

sn: तं चैवाङ्कगतं दृष्ट्वा बालं पञ्चशिखं पुनः। उमा जिज्ञासमाना वै कोऽयमित्यब्रवीत् तदा॥
en: Seeing that Mahadeva changed into a child with five locks of hair lying on the lap of Parvati, the latter asked the celestials as to who he was.

sn: असूयतश्च शक्रस्य वज्रेण प्रहरिष्यतः। स वज्रं स्तम्भयामासं तं बाहुं परिघोपमम्॥
en: Seeing the child, Shakra became suddenly filled with jealousy and anger and determined to kill him with his thunder. The child, however, paralysed the arm, appearing like a mace of iron, of Indra with the thunderbolt in it.

sn: न सम्बुबुधिरे चैव देवास्तं भुवनेश्वरम्। सप्रजापतयः सर्वे तस्मिन् मुमुहुरीश्वरे॥
en: The celestials all became stupefied, and they could not understand that child was the Master of the universe. Indeed, all of them, along with the very Regents of the world, found their intellects stupefied about that child who was none else than the Supreme Being.

sn: ततो ध्यात्वा च भगवान् ब्रह्मा तममितौजसम्। अयं श्रेष्ठ इति ज्ञात्वा ववन्दे तमुमापतिम्॥
en: Then reflecting with the help of his penances, the Illustrious Grandfather Brahman found out that that child was the foremost of al! beings, the lord of Uma, Mahadeva of immeasurable prowess. He then lauded the Lord.

sn: ततः प्रसादयामासुरुमां रुद्रं च ते सुराः। बभूव स तदा बाहुर्बलहन्तुर्यथा पुरा॥ स चापि ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा दुर्वासा नाम वीर्यवान्। द्वारवत्यां मम गृहे चिरं कालमुपावसन्॥
en: The celestials also began to sing the praises of both Uma and Rudra. The arm (which had been paralysed) of the destroyer of Vala then became restored to its former state. That Mahadeva, taking birth as the highly energetic Brahmana Durvasas, lived for a long time at Dvaravati in my house.

sn: विप्रकारान् प्रयुक्ते स्म सुबहून् मम वेश्मनि। तानुदारतया चाहं चक्षमे चातिदुःसहान्॥
en: While living in my house he committed various mischief's. Thought difficult of being borne. I suffered them yet from magnanimity of heart.

sn: रुद्रः स च शिवः सोऽग्निः सर्वः स सर्वजित्। स चैवेन्द्रश्च वायुश्च सोऽश्विनौ स च विद्युतः॥
en: He is Rudra; he is Shiva; he is Agni; he is Sarva; he is the defeater of all; he is Indra, and Vayu, and the Ashvins and the god of lightning.

sn: स चन्द्रमाः स चेशानः स सूर्यो वरुणश्च सः। स काल: सोऽन्तको मृत्युः स यमो रात्र्यहानि च।। मासार्धमासा ऋतवः संध्ये संवत्सरश्च सः। स धाता स विधाता च विश्वकर्मा स सर्ववित्॥
en: He is the Moon; he is Ishana; he is the Sun; he is Varuna; he is Time; he is the Destroyer; he is death; he is the day and the Night; he is the fortnight; he is the seasons; he is the two twilghts; he is the year. He is Dhatri; and he is Vidhatri; and he is Vishwakarinan; and he knows all things.

sn: वै नक्षत्राणि गृहाश्चैव दिशोऽथ प्रदिशस्तथा। विश्वमूर्तिरमेयात्मा भगवान् परमद्युतिः॥
en: He is the cardinal points of the compass and the subsidiary points also. Of universal form, he is of great soul. The holy and illustrious Durvasas is of the colour of the celestials.

sn: एकधा च द्विधा चैव बहुधा च स एव हि। शतधा सहस्रधा चैव तथा शतसहस्रधा॥
en: He sometimes shows himself singly; sometimes divides himself into two parts; and sometimes shows himself in many a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand, forms.

sn: ईदृशः स महादेवो भूयश्च भगवानतः। न हि शक्या गुणा वक्तुमपि वर्षशतैरपि॥
en: Even such is Mahadeva. He is, again, that god who is unborn. In even a hundred years, one cannot exhaust his merits by rccounting them.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच युधिष्ठिर महाबाहो महाभाग्यं महात्मनः। रुद्राय बहुरूपाय बहुनाम्ने निबोध मे॥
en: Vasudeva said O mighiyarmed Yudhishthira, listen to me as I recite to you the many names of Rudra as also the high blessedness of that great one.

sn: वदन्त्यग्निं महादेवं तथा स्थाणुं महेश्वरम्। एकाक्षं त्र्यम्बकं चैव विश्वरूपं शिवं तथा॥
en: The Rishis describe Mahadeva as Agni, and Sthanu, and Maheshvara; as oneeyed, and threeeyed, of universal form, and Shiva or highly auspicious.

sn: द्वे तनू तस्य देवस्य वेदज्ञा ब्राह्मणा विदुः। घोरामन्यां शिवामन्यां ते तनू बहुधा पुनः॥
en: Brahmanas knowing the Vedas say that god has two forins. (One of these is terrible, and the other mild and auspicious. Those two forms, again, arc subdivided into many forms.

sn: उग्रा घोरा तनुर्यास्य सोऽग्निर्विद्युत् स भास्करः। शिवा सौम्या च या त्वस्य धर्मस्त्वापोऽथ चन्द्रमा:।।४
en: That form which is fierce and terrible is considered as identical with Agni and Lightning and the Sun. That other form which is mild and auspicious is identical with Virtue and Water and the Moon.

sn: आत्मनोऽर्धं तु तस्याग्निः सोमोऽध पुनरुच्यते। ब्रह्मचर्यं चरत्येका शिवा चास्य तनुस्तथा॥
en: Then, again, it is said that half his body is fire and half is the moon. That form of his which is mild and auspicious, is said to be engaged in the practice of the vow of celibacy.

sn: यास्य घोरतमा मूर्तिर्जगत् संहरते तथा। ईश्वरत्वान्महत्त्वाच्च महेश्वर इति स्मृतः॥
en: That other form of his which is highly terrible performs all the destructive operations in the universe. Because he is great and the Supreme Lord of all (Ishvara), therefore he is called Maheshivara.

sn: यन्निर्दहति यत्तीक्ष्णो यदुनो यत् प्रतापवान्। मांसशोणितमज्जादो यत् ततो रुद्र उच्यते॥
en: And because he burns and oppresses, is keen and fierce, and gifted with great energy, and is engaged in cating flesh and blood and marrow, that he is called Rudra.

sn: देवानां सुमहान् यच्च यच्चास्य विषयो महान्। यच्च विश्वं महत् पाति महादेवस्ततः स्मृतः॥
en: Because he is the foremost of all the celestials, and because his dominion and acquisitions are very extensive, and because he protects the vast universe, therefore is called Mahadeva.

sn: धूम्ररूपं च यत्तस्य धूर्जटीत्यत उच्यते। समेधयति यन्नित्यं सर्वान् वै सर्वकर्मभिः॥ मनुष्याशिवमन्विच्छंस्तस्मादेष शिवः स्मृतः। दहत्यूज़ स्थितो यच्च प्राणान् नृणां स्थिरश्च यत्।।१०
en: Because he is of the form or colour of smoke, therefore he is called Dhurjjali. Because by all his deeds he performs sacrifices for all and seeks the wellbeing of every creature, therefore he is called Shiva or the auspicious one. Living in the sky, he burns the lives of all creatures and is, besides, fixed in a particular path from which he does not deviate.

sn: स्थिरलिङ्गश्च यन्नित्यं तस्मात् स्थाणुरिति स्मृतः। यदस्य बहुधा रूपं भूतं भव्यं भवत्तथा॥
en: His emblem, again, is fixed and immovable for all time. He is, for these reasons, called Sthanu. He is also of multiform aspect. He is present, past, and future.

sn: स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव बहुरूपस्ततः स्मृतः। विश्वे देवाश्च यत्तस्मिन् विश्वरूपस्ततः स्मृतः॥
en: He is mobile and immobilc. For this he is called Vahurupa. Thc celestials called Vishvedevas live in his body. Ile is, for this, called Vishvarupa having an universal form.

sn: सहस्राक्षोऽयुताक्षो वा सर्वतोऽक्षिमयोऽपि वा। चक्षुषः प्रभवेत् तेजो नास्त्यन्तोऽथास्य चक्षुपाम्॥
en: He has a thousand eyes; or, he has numberless cyes; or, he has cycs on all sides and on every part of his body. His cncrgy comes out through his cyes. There is no end of his eyes.

sn: सर्वथा यत्पशून् पाति तैश्च यद् रमते सह। तेषामधिपतिर्यच्च तस्मात् पशुपतिः स्मृतः॥
en: Because he always nourishes all crcatures and sports also with them, and because he is their lord or master, therefore is he called Pashupati (the lord of all creatures).

sn: नित्येन ब्रह्मचर्येण लिङ्गमस्य यदा स्थितम्। महयत्यस्य लोकश्च प्रिय ह्येतन्महात्मनः॥
en: Because his emblem always observes the of Brahmacharya, all the worlds, therefore, adore it. This act of worship is said to please him highly.

sn: विग्रहं पूजयेद् यो वै लिङ्गं वापि महात्मनः। लिङ्गं पूजयिता नित्यं महतीं श्रियमश्नुते॥
en: If there is one who adorcs him by creating his image, and another who adores his emblem, the latter it is who wins great prosperity for ever. VOW

sn: ऋषयश्चापि देवाश्च गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्तथा। लिङ्गमेवार्चयन्ति स्म यत् तदूर्ध्वं समास्थितम्॥
en: The Rishis, the celestials, the Gandharvas, and the Apsaras, adore that emblem of his which is every erect and upraised.

sn: पूज्यमाने ततस्तस्मिन् मोदते स महेश्वरः। सुखं ददाति प्रीतात्मा भक्तानां भक्तवत्सलः॥
en: If his emblem is adored, Maheshvara becomes highly pleased with the adorer. Affectionate towards his devotees, he confers happiness upon them with a chcerful soui.

sn: एप एव श्मशानेषु देवो वसति निर्दहन्। यजन्ते ते जनास्तत्र वीरस्थाननिषेविणः॥
en: This great god loves to live in crematoria and there he burns and consumes all dead bodies. Those persons who celebrate sacrifices on such grounds attain at the end to the regions of heroes.

sn: विषयस्थः शरीरेषु स मृत्युः प्राणिनामिह। स च वायुः शरीरेषु प्राणापानशरीरिणाम्॥
en: Engaged in his proper duty, he it is who is considered as the Death who live in the bodies of all creatures. He is, again, those vital airs called Prana and Apana, in the bodies of all embodied creatures.

sn: तस्य घोराणि रूपाणि दीप्तानि च बहूनि च। लोके यान्यस्य पूज्यन्ते विप्रास्तानि विदुर्बुधाः॥
en: He has many burning and terrible forms. All those forms are adored in the world and are known to Brahmanas gifted with knowledge.

sn: नामधेयानि देवेषु वहून्यस्य यथार्थवत्। निरुच्यन्ते महत्त्वाच्च विभुत्वात् कर्मभिस्तथा॥
en: Amongst the gods he has many significant names. Indeed, the meanings of those names are derived from either his greatness or vastness, or his feats, or his conduct.

sn: वेदे चास्य विदुर्विप्राः शतरुद्रीयमुत्तमम्। व्यासेनोक्तं च यच्चापि उपस्थानं महात्मनः॥
en: The Brahmanas always recite the excellent ShataRudriya in his honour, thai is in the Vedas as also that which has been composed by Vyasa.

sn: प्रदाता सर्वलोकानां विश्वं चाप्युच्यते महत्। ज्येष्ठभूतं वदन्त्येनं ब्राह्मणा ऋषयोऽपरे॥
en: These provide all worlds with the desired things. This huge universe has been told as their own appearance. Indeed, the Brahmanas and Rishis call him the eldest of all beings.

sn: प्रथमो ह्येष देवानां मुखादग्निमजीजनत्। ग्रहैर्बहुविधैः प्राणान् संरुद्धानुत्सृजत्यपि॥
en: He is the first of all the celestials, and it was from his mouth that he created Agni. That great deity, ever willing to grant protection to all, never forsakes his suppliants.

sn: विमुञ्चति न पुण्यात्मा शरण्यः शरणागतान्। आयुरारोग्यमैश्वर्यं वित्तं कामांश्च पुष्कलान्।॥ स ददाति मनुष्येभ्यः स एवाक्षिपते पुनः। शक्रादिषु च देवेषु तस्यैश्वर्यमिहोच्यते॥
en: He would much rather give up his own life and suffer all possible afflictions himself. Long life, health and freedom from disease, affluence, wealth, various kinds of pleasures and enjoyinents, are conferred by him, and it is he also who snatches them away. The lordship and affluence that one sees in Shakra and the Other celestials are, indeed, his.

sn: स एव व्यापृतो नित्यं त्रैलोक्यस्य शुभाशुभे। ऐश्वर्याच्चैव कामानामीश्वरः पुनरुच्यते॥
en: It is he who is always engaged in all that is good and evil in the three worlds. On account of his fullest control over all objects of enjoyment he is called Ishvara.

sn: महेश्वरश्च लोकानां महतामीश्वरच सः। बहुभिर्विविधै रूपैर्विश्वं व्याप्तमिदं जगत्। तस्य देवस्य यद् वक्त्रं समुद्रे वडवामुखम्॥
en: Because he is the master of the vast universe, therefore he is called Maheshvara. The whole universe is pervaded by him in various forms. His mouth roars and burns the waters of the sea in the form of the huge mare's head.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तवति वाक्यं तु कृष्णे देवकिनन्दने। भीष्मं शान्तनवं भूयः पर्यपृच्छद् युधिष्ठिरः॥ निर्णये वा महाबुद्धे सर्वधर्मविदां वर। प्रत्यक्षमागमो वेति किं तयोः कारणं भवेत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said After Krishna, the son of Devaki, had said these words, Yudhishthira once more asked Bhishma the son of Shantanu, saying, O you of great intelligence, O foremost of all persons, knowing duties, which, indeed of the two, direct perception and the scriptures, is to be considered as authority for coming to a conclusion?

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: भीष्म उवाच नास्त्यत्र संशयः कश्चिदिति मे वर्तते मतिः। शृणु वक्ष्यामि ते प्राज्ञ सम्यक् तवं मेऽनुपृच्छसि॥ संशयः सुगमस्तत्र दुर्गमस्तस्य निर्णयः।
en: Bhishma said I think there is no doubt in this. Listen to me, O you of great wisdom. I shall answer you. The question you have asked is indeed proper. It is easy to entertain doubt. But the solution of that doubt is difficult.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: दृष्टं श्रुतमनन्तं हि यत्र संशयदशर्नम्॥ प्रत्यक्षं कारणं दृष्ट्वा हैतुकाः प्राज्ञमानिनः।
en: Numberless are the instances, about both direct perception and Shrutis in which doubts may originate. Certain persons, who take pleasure in the name of logicians, imagining themselves to be gifted with superior wisdom, affirm that direct perception is the only authority.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: नास्तीत्येवं व्यवस्यन्ति सत्यं संशयमेव च॥ तदयुक्तं व्यवस्यन्ति बालाः पण्डितमानिनः।
en: They assert that nothing, however true, exists which is not directly perceivable; or, at least, they doubt the existence of those objects. Such assertions however are absurd and they who make them are fools, whatever their pride of learning.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: अथ चेन्मन्यसे चैकं कारणं किं भवेदिति॥ शक्यं दीर्पण कालेन युक्तेनातन्द्रितेन च।
en: If, on the other hand, you entertain any doubt how the one indivisible Brahman could be the cause, I answer that one would understand it only after many years and with the help of Yoga practised assiduously.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: प्राणयात्रामनेकां च कल्पमानेन भारत॥ तत्परेणैव नान्येन शक्यं ह्येतस्य दर्शनम्।
en: Indeed, O Bharata, one who lives according to such means as present themselves, and one who is devoted, would be capable of understanding it. None else, truly, is competent for comprehending it.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: हेतूनामन्तमासाद्य विपुलं ज्ञानमुत्तमम्॥ ज्योतिः सर्वस्य लोकस्य विपुलं प्रतिपद्यते।
en: When one gets to the very end of reasons, he attains to that excellent and all comprehending knowledge—that vast mass of effulgence, which illumines all the universe (called Brahma).

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: न त्वेव गमनं राजन् हेतुतो गमनं तथा। अग्राह्यमनिबद्धं च वाचा सम्परिवर्जयेत्॥
en: That knowledge, O king, which is derived from can hardly be said to be knowledge. Such knowledge should rejected. It should be understood, that it is not defined or comprehended by the word. It should, therefore, be rejected.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच प्रत्यक्षं लोकतः सिद्धिर्लोक्श्चागमपूर्वकः। शिष्टाचारो बहुविधस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, which among these (four) is most authoritative, viz., direct reason be perception, Inference from observation, the science of scriptures, and various kinds of practices which distinguish the good.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: भीष्म उवाच धर्मस्य ह्रियमाणस्य बलवद्भिर्दुरात्मभिः। संस्था यत्नैरपि कृता कालेन प्रतिभिद्यते॥
en: Bhishma said While virtue is sought to be destroyed by wicked persons possessed of great power, it is capable of being protected for the time being by those who are good if they work with care and earnestness. Such protection, however, is of no use in the long run, for destruction does overtake virtue at the end.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: अधर्मो धर्मरूपेण तृणैः कूप इवावृतः। ततस्तैर्भिद्यते वृत्तं शृणु चैव युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Then, again, virtue often proves a mark for covering sin, like grass and straw covering the mouth of a deep pit and concealing it from the view. Hear, again, O Yudhishthira. On account of this, the practices of the good are interfered with and destroyed by the wicked.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: अवृत्ता ये तु भिन्दन्ति श्रुतित्यागपरायणाः। धर्मविद्वेषिणो मन्दा इत्युक्तस्तेषु संशयः॥
en: Those persons who are evildoers, who discard the Shrutis, indeed, those wicked persons who are haters of virtue destroy that good conduct, hence, doubts attach to direct perception, Inference, and good conduct.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: अतृप्यन्तस्तु साधूनां य एवागमबुद्धयः। परमित्येव संतुष्टास्तानुपास्व च पृच्छ च॥
en: Those, therefore, among the good who are possessed of understanding purified by the scriptures and who are ever contented, are to be considered as the foremost. Let those who are anxious and deprived of tranquility of soul, approach these. Indeed, O Yudhishthira, do you seek them and ask them for the solutions of your doubts.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: कामार्थो पृष्ठतः कृत्वा लोभमोहानुसारिणौ। धर्म इत्येव सम्बुद्धास्तानुपास्व च पृच्छ च॥
en: Disregarding both Pleasure and Profit which always follow cupidity and cherishing the condition that only virtues should be sought, do you, O Yudhishthira, wait upon and ask those persons.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: न तेषां भिद्यते वृत्तं यज्ञाः स्वाध्यायकर्म च। आचारः कारणं चैव धर्मश्चैकस्त्रयं पुनः॥
en: The conduct of those persons never goes wrong or meets with destruction, as also their sacrifices and Vedic study and rites. Indeed, these three, viz., good conduct, mental purity, and the Vedas together form virtue.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पुनरेव हि मे बुद्धिः संशये परिमुह्यति। अपारे मार्गमाणस्य परं तीरमपश्यतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, my understanding is once more stupefied by doubt. I am on this side of the ocean, engaged in searching after the ineans of crossing it. I do not, however, see the other shore of the ocean.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: वेदः प्रत्यक्षमाचारः प्रमाणं तत्रयं यदि। पृथक्त्वं लभ्यते चैषां धर्मश्चैकस्त्रयं कथम्॥
en: If these three, viz., the Vedas, direct perception and behaviour (or mental purity) together form what is to be considered as authority, it can be alleged that there is difference between each. Virtue then becomes really of three kinds although it is one and indivisible.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: भीष्म उवाच धर्मस्य ह्रियमाणस्य बलवद्भिर्दुरात्मभिः। यद्येवं मन्यसे राजंस्त्रिधा धर्मविचारणा॥
en: Bhishma said Virtue is sometimes seen to be destroyed by a wicked man of great power. If you think, O king, that virtue should really be of three sorts. I answer that your conclusion is supported by reason.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: एक एवेति जानीहि त्रिधा धर्मस्य दर्शनम्। पृथक्त्वे च न मे बुद्धिस्त्रयाणामपि वै तथा॥
en: The truth is that virtue is one and indivisible, although it is capable of being scen from three different points.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: उक्तो मार्गस्त्रयाणां च त तथैव समाचर। जिज्ञासा न तु कर्तव्या धर्मस्य परितर्कणात्॥
en: The paths, of those three, which form the foundation of virtue have each been laid down. Do you act according to the instructions laid down. You should never wrangle about virtue and then seek to have those doubts of yours removed.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: सदैव भरतश्रेष्ठ मा तेऽभूदत्र संशयः। अन्धो जड इवाशङ्की यद् ब्रवीमि तदाचर॥
en: O chief of the Bharatas, let no doubts like these ever take possession of your mind. Do you obey unhesitatingly what I say. Follow me like a blind man or like one who, having no sense himself, has to depend upon that of another.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधो दानमेतच्चतुष्टयम्। अजातशत्रो सेवस्व धर्म एष सनातनः॥
en: Abstention from injury, truth, absence of anger (or forgiveness), and liberality or gifts, these four, O king do you practise, for these four form eternal virtue.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: ब्राह्मणेषु च वृत्तिर्या पितृपैतामहोचिता। तामन्वेहि महाबाहो धर्मस्यैते हि देशिकाः॥
en: Do you also, O mightyarmed prince, follow that conduct towards the Brahmanas which is consistent with what has been observed towards them by your father and grandfather. These are the principal marks of virtue.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: प्रमाणमप्रमाणं वै यः कुर्यादबुधो जनः। न स प्रमाणतामों विवादजननो हि सः॥
en: That foolish wight, who would destroy the weight of authority by denying that to be a standard which has always been accepted as such, would himself fail to become an authority among men. Such a man becomes the cause of much sorrow in the world.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: ब्राह्मणानेव सेवस्व सत्कृत्य बहुमन्य च। एतेष्वेव त्विमे लोकाः कृत्स्ना इति निबोध तान्।।२६
en: Do you respect the Brahmanas and treat them with hospitality. Do you always serve them in this way. The universe rests on them. Do you understand them to be such.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ये च धर्ममसूयन्ते ये चैनं पर्युपासते। ब्रवीतु मे भवानेतत् क्व ते गच्छन्ति तादृशाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, what the respective ends are of those who hate virtue and of those who worship and observe it.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: भीष्म उवाच रजसा तमसा चैव समवस्तीर्णचेतसः। नरकं प्रतिपद्यन्ते धर्मविद्वेषिणो जनाः॥
en: Bhishma said Those men who hate virtue are said to have their hearts possessed by the qualities of passion and darkness. Such men have always to go to Hell.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: ये तु धर्म महाराज सततं पर्युपासते। सत्यार्जवपराः सन्तस्ते वै स्वर्गभुजो नराः॥
en: Those men, on the other hand, O king, who always observe virtue, those men who are given to truth and sincerity, are called good. They always enjoy the pleasures or happiness of the celestial region.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: धर्म एव गतिस्तेषामाचार्योपासनाद् भवेत्। देवलोकं प्रपद्यन्ते ये धर्मं पर्युपासते॥
en: On account of their waiting upon their preceptors with respect their hearts always turn towards virtue. Indeed they, who worship virtuc, attain to the region of the celestials.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: मनुष्या यदि वा देवाः शरीरमुपताप्य वै। धर्मिणः सुखमेधन्ते लोभद्वेषविवर्जिताः॥
en: Those individuals, whether men or celestials, who are shorn of cupidity and malice and who emaciate or afflict their bodies by the practice of austerities succeed, on account of the virtle which they thus acquire, to attain to great happiness.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: प्रथमं ब्रह्मणः पुत्रं धर्ममाहुर्मनीषिणः। धर्मिणः पर्युपासन्ते फलं पक्वमिवाशयः॥
en: The righteous always adore them with love and affection as a hungry man's stomach longs for ripe and sweet fruits.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच असतां कीदृशं रूपं साधवः किं च कुर्वते। ब्रवीतु मे भवानेतत् सन्तोऽसन्तश्च कीदृशाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said What are the marks of the wicked, and what are those deeds which the good do? Explain to me this, O holy one, Indeed, tell me what characteristics are of the good and the wicked.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: भीष्म उवाच दुराचाराश्च दुर्धर्षा दुर्मुखाश्चाप्यसाधवः। साधवः शील सम्पन्नाः शिष्टाचारस्य लक्षणम्॥
en: Bhishma said The wicked are evil in their practices, incapable of being governed by rules, and eviltongued. The good are, however, always good in their deeds. Indeed the acts these men do are considered as the characteristics of good deeds.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: राजमार्गे गवां मध्ये धान्यमध्ये च धर्मिणः। नोपसेवन्ति राजेन्द्र सर्ग मूत्रपूरीषयोः॥
en: The good or the righteous, O king, never answer the two calls of nature on the public road, or in the midst of a cowpen or on a field of paddy.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: पञ्चानामशनं दत्त्वा शेषमश्नन्ति साधवः। न जल्पन्ति च भुजाना न निद्रान्त्याईपाणयः॥
en: After feeding the five they take their own food. They never talk while eating, and never go to sleep with wet hands.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: चित्रभानुमनड्वाहं देवं गोष्ठं चतुष्पथम्। ब्राह्मणं धार्मिकं वृद्धं ये कुर्वन्ति प्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: Whenever they see any of the following, they go round them for showing them respect, viz., a burning fire, a bull, the image of a deity, a cowpen, a crossing place of four roads, and an old and virtuous Brahmana.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: वृद्धानां भारतप्तानां स्त्रीणां चक्रधरस्य च। ब्राह्मणानां गवां राज्ञां पन्थानं ददते च ये॥
en: Themselves standing aside they give the way to those that are old, those that are afflicted with burdens, ladies, those that hold high appointments in the village or town administration, Brahmanas, kine, and kings.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: अतिथीनां च सर्वेषां प्रेष्याणां स्वजनस्य च। तथा शरणकामानां गोप्ता स्यात् स्वागतप्रदः॥
en: The righteous or good man is he who protects his guests, servants and other dependants, his own relatives, and all those who seek his protection. Such a man always welcomes these with the usual polite enquiries.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: सायंप्रातर्मनुष्याणामशनं देवनिर्मितम्। नान्तरा भोजनं दृष्टमुपवासविधिर्हि सः॥
en: As ordained by the deities human beings should take their food twice a day. viz., morning and evening. During the interval one should not eat anything. By following this rule about cating, one is said to observe a fast.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: होमकाले यथा वह्निः कालमेव प्रतीक्षते। ऋतुकाले तथा नारी ऋतुमेव प्रतीक्षते॥
en: As the sacred fire waits for libations to be poured upon it when the hour for Homa arrives, so a woman, when her period is over, cxpects sexual union with her husband.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: नान्यदा गच्छते यस्तु ब्रह्मचर्ये च तत् स्मृतम्। अमृतं ब्राह्मणा गाव इत्येतत् त्रयमेकतः।
en: One, who never knows his wife at any other time except after the period of menses, is said lo observe the vow of Brahmacharya. Amrita (nectar), Brahmanas, and kine, these three are considered as equal.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: तस्माद् गोब्राह्मणं नित्यमर्चयेत यथाविधि॥ स्वदेशे परदेशे वाप्यतिथिं नोपवासयेत्।
en: Therefore one should adoren always Brahinanas and kines. One should never cause his guest to go without food whether he lives in his own country or in a foreign land.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: कर्म वै सफलं कृत्वा गुरूणां प्रतिपादयेत्॥ गुरूभ्यस्त्वासनं देयमभिवाद्याभिपूज्य च।
en: After completing his study one should give the due present to his preceptor. When one sees his preceptor, he should receive him with respect and adoring him present him a seat.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: गुरुमभ्यर्च्य वर्धन्ते आयुषा यशसा श्रिया॥ वृद्धान् नाभिभवेज्जातु न चैतान् प्रेषयेदिति।
en: By adoring his preceptor, one increases the period of his life as also his fame and prosperity. One should never censure the old, •nor send them on any business.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: नासीनः स्यात् स्थितेष्वेवमायुरस्य न रिष्यते॥ न नग्नामीक्षते नारी न नग्नान् पुरुषानपि। मैथुनं सततं गुप्तमाहारं च समाचरेत्॥ तीर्थानां गुरवस्तीर्थं चोक्षाणां हृदयं शुचि। दर्शनानां परं ज्ञानं संतोषः परमं सुखम्॥ सायं प्रातश्च वृद्धानां शृणुयात् पुष्कला गिरः।
en: One should never be seated when any one that is old is standing. By acting thus one protects the duration of his life. One should never cast his eyes on a naked woman, nor a naked man. One should never indulge in sexual congress except in privacy, One should eat also without being seen by others. Preceptors are the foremost of shrines, the heart is the foremost of all sacred objects; knowledge is the foremost of all objects of search; and contentment is the foremost of all happiness. Morning and evening one should listen to the grave counsels of the aged.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: श्रुतमाप्नोति हि नरः सततं वृद्धसेवया॥ स्वाध्याय भोजने चैव दक्षिणं पाणिमुद्धरेत्।
en: One acquires wisdom by constantly waiting upon the aged. While reading the Vedas or employed in eating, one should use his right hand.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी नित्यमिन्द्रियाणि तथैव च॥ संस्कृतं पायसं नित्यं यवागू कृसरं हविः। अष्टकाः पितृदैवत्या ग्रहाणामभिपूजनम्॥ श्मश्रूकर्मणि मङ्गल्यं क्षुतानामभिनन्दनम्। व्याधितानां च सर्वेषामायुषामभिनन्दनम्॥
en: One should always keep his speech and mind under perfect control, as also his senses. With wellcooked frumenty, Yavaka, Krishara, and Havi (clarified butter), one should adore the departed manes and the celestials in the Shraddha called Ashtaka. The same should be used in adoring the Planets. One should not undergo a shave without calling down a blessing upon himself. if one sneezes, one should be blessed by those present. All, who are ill or suffer from diseases, should be blessed. The extension of their lives should be prayed for.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: न जातु त्वमिति ब्रूयादापन्नोऽपि महत्तरम्। त्वंकारो वा वधो वेति विद्वत्सु स विशिष्यते॥
en: One should never address an eminent person familiarly. Under even the greatest difficulties one should never do this. To you such a person are degraded by such a manner of address.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: अवराणां समानानां शिष्याणां च समाचरेत्। पापमाचक्षते नित्यं हृदयं पापकर्मिणः॥
en: Such a word can be used to those who are inferior, or equal, or to disciples. A sinful man always speaks of the sins he has committed.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: ज्ञानपूर्वकृतं कर्म च्छादयन्ते ह्यसाधवः। ज्ञानपूर्वं विनश्यन्ति गूहमाना महाजने॥
en: Those men, who have deliberately committed sins, meet with destruction by trying to conceal them from the good. Indeed, the confirmed sinners try to conceal their sinful deeds from others.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: न मां मनुष्याः पश्यन्ति न मां पश्यन्ति देवताः। पापेनाभिहितः पापः पापमेवाभिजायते॥
en: Such persons think that their sins are seen neither by men nor the celestials. The sinful man, laden with his sins, takes birth in a miserable order of being.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: यथा वा षिको वृद्धिं दिनभेदे प्रतीक्षते। धर्मेण पिहितं पापं धर्ममेवाभिवर्धयेत्॥
en: The sins of such a man continually grow, even as the interest charged by an usurer daily multiplies itself. If having committed a sin, one seeks to have it covered by virtue, that sin becomes destroyed and leads to virtue instead of to other sins.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: यथा लवणमम्भोभिराप्लुतं प्रविलीयते। प्रायश्चित्तहतं पापं तथा सद्यः प्रणश्यति॥
en: If a quantity of water be poured upon salt, the latter is immediately dissolved. So when expiation is performed, sin is dissipated.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: तस्मात् पापं न गूहेत गूहमानं विवर्धयेत्। कृत्वा तत् साधुष्वाख्येयं ते तत् प्रशमयन्त्युत॥
en: For these reasons one should never conceal a sin. Concealed, it is sure to increase, Having committed a sin, one should confess it before the good. They would then destroy it forthwith.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: आशया संचितं द्रव्यं कालेनैवोपभुज्यते। अन्ये चैतत् प्रपद्यन्ते वियोगे तस्य देहिनः॥
en: If one does not enjoy in good time what he has stored with hope, the result is that the stored wealth passes into another man's hands after the death of him who has stored it.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: मानसं सर्वभूतानां धर्ममाहुर्मनीषिणः। तस्मात् सर्वाणि भूतानि धर्ममेव समासते॥
en: The wise have said that the mind of every creature is the true test of virtue Hence, all creatures in this world have an innate tendency to achieve virtue.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: एक एव चरेद् धर्मे न धर्मध्वजिको भवेत्। धर्मवाणिजका ह्येते ये धर्ममुपभुञ्जते॥
en: One should achieve virtue alone singlehanded. Indeed, one should not proclaim himself virtuous and walk with the standard of virtue upraised for purposes of show. They are said to be traders in virtue who practice it for enjoying its fruits.

description: The authority of direct perception, inference, the science of the scriptures
sn: अर्चेद् देवानदम्भेन सेवेतामायया गुरून्। निधिं निदध्यात् पारत्र्यं यात्रार्थे दानशब्दितम्॥
en: One should worship the celestials without giving way to sentiments of pride. Similarly, one should serve his preceptor without deceit. or One should make arrangements for securing to himself invaluable riches in the next world which consists in gifts made here to worthy; persons. One should make arrangements for securing to himself invaluable riches in the next world which consists in gifts made here to worthy; persons.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच नाभागधेयः प्राप्नोति धनं सुबलवानपि। भागधेयान्वितस्त्वर्थान् कृशो बालश्च विन्दति॥
en: Yudhishthira said It is seen that if a person happens to be unfortunate, he fails to acquire riches how greatsoever his strength. On the other hand, if he happens to be fortunate, he amasses riches, even if he be a weak or a foolish wight.

sn: नालाभकाले लभते प्रयत्नेऽपि कृते सति। लाभकालेऽप्रयत्नेन लभते विपुलं धनम्॥
en: When, again, the time does not come for acquisition, one cannot make an acquisition, even if he tries his best. When, however, the time comes for acquisition, one acquires great wealth without any exertion.

sn: कृतयत्नाफलाश्चैव दृश्यन्ते शतशो नराः। अयत्नेनैधमानाश्च दृश्यन्ते बहवो जनाः॥
en: Hundreds of men may be seen who gain no result even when they try their best. Many persons, again, are seen to make acquisitions without any exertion.

sn: यदि यत्नो भवेन्मर्त्यः स सर्वे फलमाप्नुयात्। नालभ्यं चोपलभ्येत नृणां भरतसत्तम॥ प्रयत्नं कृतवन्तोऽपि दृश्यन्ते ह्यफला नराः।
en: If riches were the result of exertion, then one could, with exertion, acquire it forthwith. Among men, that which is not to be attained, O chief of the Bharatas, is never attained. Men are seen to fail in gaining results even if they try their best.

sn: मार्गत्यायशतैरथानमार्गश्चापरः सुखी॥ अकार्यमसकृत् कृत्वा दृश्यन्ते ह्यधना नराः।
en: One may be seen to seek riches by hundreds of means (and yet failing to acquire it); while another, without at all seeking it, gets it. Men may be seen doing evil deeds continually (for wealth) and yet they do not gain it.

sn: धनयुक्ताः स्वकर्मस्था दृश्यन्ते चापरेऽधनाः॥ अधीत्य नीतिशास्त्राणि नीतियुक्तो न दृश्यते।
en: Others get wealth without doing any evil act whatever. Others, again, who follow the duties assigned to them by the scripture, are without wealth. One may be seen to be without any knowledge of the science of ethics and polity even after he has studied all the treatises on that science.

sn: अनभिज्ञश्च साचिव्यं गमित: केन हेतुना॥ विद्यायुक्तो ह्यविद्यश्च धनवान् दुर्मतिस्तथा।
en: One, again, may be seen appointed as the prime minister of a king without having at all studied the moral and political sciences. A learned man may be seen who has wealth. An ignorant man may be seen having wealth. Both kinds of men, again, may be seen who has wealth.

sn: यदि विद्यामुपाश्रित्य नरः सुखमवाप्नुयात्॥ न विद्वान् विद्यया हीनं वृत्त्यर्थमुपसंश्रयेत्।
en: If by the acquisition of learning one could acquire the happiness of riches then no man of learning could be found living, for the very means of his livelihood, under the protection of one shorn of learning.

sn: यथा पिपासां जयति पुरुषः प्राप्य वै जलम्॥ इष्टार्थो विद्यया ह्येव न विद्यां प्रजहेन्नरः।
en: Indeed, if one could obtain, by the acquisition of learning, all desirable objects like a thirsty individual having his thirst satisfied upon getting water, then none in this world would have shown idleness in acquiring learning.

sn: नाप्राप्तकालो म्रियते विद्धः शरशतैरपि। तृणाग्रेणापि संस्पृष्टः प्राप्ताकालो न जीवति॥
en: If one's time has not come, one does not die even if cut with hundreds of shafts. On the other hand, one dies if his hour has come, even if it be a blade of grass with which he is struck.

sn: भीष्म उवाच ईहमानः समारम्भान् यदि नासादयेद् धनम्। उग्रं तपः समारोहेन ह्यनुप्तं प्ररोहति॥
en: Bhishma said If one, by performing arduous works, fails to acquire wealth, he should then practise severe austeritics. Unless seeds be sown, no crops appear.

sn: दानेन भोगी भवति मेधावी वृद्धसेवया। अहिंसया च दीर्घायुरिति प्राहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: It is by making gifts that one gets numerous objects of enjoyment; one becomes endued with intelligence and wisdom by waiting upon the elders. The wise have said that one becomes longlived by practising the duty of abstention from cruelty to all creatures.

sn: तस्माद् दद्यान याचेत पूजयेद् धार्मिकानपि। सुभाषी प्रियकृच्छान्तः सर्वसत्त्वाविहिंसकः॥
en: Hence, one should make gifts and not solicit and one should adore individuals. Indeed one should be sweet-speeched towards all, and always do what is agreeable to others. One should seek to attain to purity; one should always abstain from doing injury 10 any crcature,

sn: यदा प्रमाणं प्रसवः स्वभावश्च सुखासुखे। दंशकीटपिपीलानां स्थिरो भव युधिष्ठिर॥
en: It is but proper, O Yudhishthira, that you should be possessed by peaceful sentiments, since their deeds and Nature are the ruling causes of happiness and misery to even insects and ants.

sn: भीष्म उवाच कार्यते यच्च क्रियते सच्चासच्च कृताकृतम्। तत्राश्वसीत सत्कृत्वा असत्कृत्वा न विश्वसेत्॥
en: Bhishma said If one does good deeds or causes others to do them, he should then expect to attain to the merits of virtue; likewise if one does evil deeds and causes others to do them, he should never expect to attain to the merits of virtue.

sn: काल एव सर्वकाले निग्रहानुग्रहौ ददत्। बुद्धिमाविश्य भूतानां धर्माधर्मो प्रवर्तते॥
en: At all times, it is Time, which entering the understanding of all creatures, sets them to deeds of virtue or sin and then confers happiness or misery upon them.

sn: यदा त्वस्य भवेद् बुद्धिर्धर्मार्थस्य प्रदर्शनात्। तदाश्वसीत धर्मात्मा दृढबुद्धिर्न विश्वसेत्॥
en: When a person, seeing the fruits of virtue understands virtue to be superior, it is then that he inclines towards virtue and puts faith in il. One, however, whose understanding is not firm, cannot place faith in it.

sn: एतावन्मात्रमेतद्धि भूतानां प्राज्ञलक्षणम्। कालयुक्तोऽप्युभयविच्छेषं युक्तं समाचरेत्॥
en: As regards faith in virtue, it is this. To place faith in virtue is the mark of the wisdom of all persons. One, who is acquainted with what should be done and what should not be done, with a view to opportuneness, should, with care and devotion, do what is right.

sn: यथा झुपस्थितैश्वर्याः प्रजायन्ते न राजसाः। एवमेवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पूजयन्तीह धार्मिकाः॥
en: Those virtuous men, who have in this life been blessed with riches acting of their own accord, take particular care of their souls so that they may not, in their next lives, have to take birth as persons with the quality of darkness predominating in them.

sn: न ह्यधर्मतयाधर्मे दद्यात् काल: कथंचन। तस्माद् विशुद्धमात्मानं जानीयाद् धर्मचारिणम्॥
en: Time can never make the cause of misery. One should, therefore, know that the soul which is virtuous is certainly pure.

sn: स्प्रष्टुमप्यसमर्थो हि ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्। अधर्म: संततो धर्मे कालेन परिरक्षितम्॥
en: As regards sin, it may be said that, even when it is very great it is incapable of even touching virtue which is always protected by time and which shines like a burning fire.

sn: कार्यावेतौ हि धर्मेण धर्मो हि विजयावहः। त्रयाणामपि लोकानामालोकः कारणं भवेत्॥
en: These are the two results achieved by virtue, viz., the purity of the soul and unsusceptibility of being touched by iniquity Indeed virtue is fraught with victory. Its effulgence is so great that it lights up the three worlds.

sn: न तु कश्चिन्नयेत् प्राज्ञो गृहीत्वैव करे नरम्। उच्यमानस्तु धर्मेण धर्मलोकभयच्छले॥
en: A wise man cannot catch holds of a sinful person and forcibly make him pious. When seriously urged to act piously the sinful only act with hypocrisy, moved by fear.

sn: शूद्रोऽहं नाधिकारो मे चातुराश्रम्यसेवने। इति विज्ञानमपरे नात्मन्युपदधत्युत॥
en: Even the righteous among the Shudras never betake themselves to such hypocrisy under the pretext that persons of the Shudra order are not permitted to live according to any of the four prescribed modes.

sn: विशेषेण च वक्ष्यामि चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य लिङ्गत्तः। पञ्चभूतशरीराणां सर्वेषां सदृशात्मनाम्॥
en: I shall tell you particularly what the duties truly are of the four castes. So far as their bodies concerned, the individuals, belonging to all the four casts, have five primal elements for heir constituent ingredients; they are all the same substance in this matter. are

sn: लोकधर्मे च धर्मे च विशेषकरणं कृतम्। यथैकत्वं पुनर्यान्ति प्राणिनस्तत्र विस्तरः॥
en: For all that, their practices relating to life or the world and the duties of virtue, vary despite these distinctions, and sufficient liberty of action is left to them by which all individuals may attain to an equality of condition.

sn: अध्रुवो हि कथं लोकः स्मृतो धर्मः कथं ध्रुवः। यत्र कालो ध्रुवस्तात तत्र धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: The regions of happiness which represent the results or rewards of virtue are not eternal, for they are destined to come to an end. Virtue, however, is eternal When the cause is eternal, why is the effect not so? The answer to this is as follows. Only that virtue is eternal which is not prompted by the desire of fruit or reward.

sn: सर्वेषां तुल्यदेहानां सर्वेषां सदृशात्मनाम्। कालो धर्मेण संयुक्तः शेष एव स्वयं गुरुः॥
en: All men are equal as regards their physical organism. All of them, again, have souls which are equal in nature. When dissolution comes, all else dissolves away. What remains is the desire for acquiring virtue. That, indeed, reappears (in next life) of itself.

sn: एवं सति न दोघोऽस्ति भूतानां धर्मसेवने। तिर्यग्योनावपि सतां लोक एव मतो गुरुः॥
en: When such is the result, the inequality of condition, seen among human beings, cannot be considered in any way anomalous. So also, it is seen that those crcatures that belong to the intermediate orders of existence are equally subject, about their acis, to the influence of example.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शरतल्पगतं भीष्मं पाण्डवोऽथ कुरूद्वहः। युधिष्ठिरो हितं प्रेप्सुरपृच्छत् कल्मषापहम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Desirous of acquiring the merit which destroys sins that perpetuator of Kuru's race, viz., Yudhishthira the son of Pandu, questioned Bhishma who was lying on a bed of arrows saying.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं श्रेयः पुरुषस्येह किं कुर्वन् सुखमेधते। विपाप्मा स भवेत् केन किं वा कल्मषनाशनम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said What, indeed, is beneficial for a person in this world? What is that by doing which one may acquire happiness? By what may one be purged of all his sins? Indeed, what is that which destroys sins?

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मै शुश्रूषमाणाय भूयः शान्तनवस्तदा। दैवं वंशं यथान्यायमाचष्ट पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Vaishampayana said On this subject, the royal son of Shantanu, ( foremost of men, duly recited the names of the celestials to Yudhishthira who was desirous of hearing.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: भीष्म उवाच अयं दैवतवंशो वै ऋषिवंशसमन्वितः। त्रिसंध्यं पठितः पुत्र कल्मषापहरः परः॥
en: Bhishma said O son, the following names of the celestials with those of the Rishis, if duly recited morning, noon, and evening, destroy all sins.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: यदह्ना कुरुते पापमिन्द्रियैः पुरुषश्चरन्। बुद्धिपूर्वमबुद्धिर्वा रात्रौ यच्चापि संध्ययोः॥ मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यः कीर्तयन् वै शुचिः सदा। नान्धो न बधिरः काले कुरुते स्वस्तिमान् सदा॥
en: Acting with the help of his senses, whatever sins one may commit by day or by night or by the two twilight's, willingly or unwillingly, one is sure to be cleansed therefrom and become thoroughly pure by reciting these names. One, man never that takes those names, has never to become blind or deaf indeed, by taking those names, one always succeeds in getting what is beneficial.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: तिर्यग्योनि न गच्छेच्च नरकं संकराणि च। न च दुःखभयं तस्य मरणे स न मुह्यति॥
en: Such a never takes birth in the intermediate order of being never goes to hell and never becomes a human being of any of the mixed castes. He has never to fear any calamity. When death comes, he becomes stupefied.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: देवासुरगुरुर्देवः सर्वभूतनमस्कृतः। अचिन्त्योऽथाप्यनिर्देश्यः सर्वप्राणो ह्ययोनिजः॥
en: The master of all the celestials and Apsaras, resplendent with effulgence, adored of all creatures, inconceivable, indescribable, the life of all living beings, and unborn is the Grandfather Brahman, that Lord of the universe. His chaste wife is Savittri. Then comes that origin of the Vedas, the creator Vishnu, otherwise called Narayana of immeasurable power.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: पितामहो जगन्नाथः सावित्री ब्रह्मणः सती। वेदभूरथ कर्ता च विष्णुर्नारायणः प्रभुः॥ उमापतिर्विरूपाक्षः स्कन्दः सेनापतिस्तथा। विशाखो हुतभुग् वायुश्चन्द्रसूर्यो प्रभाकरौ॥ शक्रः शचीपतिर्देवो यमो धूमोर्णया सह। वरुणः सह गौर्या च सह ऋद्ध्या धनेश्वरः॥ सौम्या गौः सुरभिर्देवी विश्रवाश्च महानृषिः। संकल्पः सागरो गङ्गा स्रवन्त्योऽथ मरुद्गणः॥ वालखिल्यास्तपः सिद्धाः कृष्णद्वैपायनस्तथा। नारदः पर्वतश्चैव विश्वावसुर्हहाहुहूः॥ तुम्बुरुश्चित्रसेनश्च देवदूतश्च विश्रुतः। देवकन्या महाभागा दिव्याश्चाप्सरसां गणाः॥ उर्वशी मेनका रम्भा मिश्रकेशी ह्यलम्बुषा। विश्वाची च घृताची च पञ्चचूडा तिलोत्तमा॥ आदित्या वसवो रुद्राः साश्विनः पितरोऽपि च। धर्मः श्रुतं तपो दीक्षा व्यवसाय: पितामहः॥ शर्वर्यो दिवसाश्चैव मारीचः कश्यपस्तथा। शुक्रो बृहस्पति मो बुधो राहुः शनैश्चरः॥ नक्षत्राण्यतवश्चैव मासाः पक्षाः सवत्सराः। वैनतेयाः समुद्राश्च कद्रुजाः पन्नगास्तथा॥ शतद्रुक्ष विपाशा च चन्द्रभागा सरस्वती। सिंधुश्च देविका चैव प्रभासं पुष्कराणि च॥ गङ्गा महानदी वेणा कावेरी नर्मदा तथा। कुलप्पुना विशल्या च करतोयाम्बुवाहिनी॥ सरयूर्गण्डकी चैव लोहितश्च महानदः। ताम्रारुणा वेत्रवती पर्णाशा गौतमी तथा॥ गोदावरी च वेण्या च कृष्णवेणा तथाद्रिजा। दृषद्वती च कावेरी चक्षुर्मन्दाकिनी तथा॥ प्रयागं च प्रभासं च पुण्यं नैमिषमेव च। तच्च विश्वेश्वरस्थानं यत्र तद्विमलं सरः॥ पुण्यतीर्थं सुसलिलं कुरुक्षेत्रं प्रकीर्तितम्। सिंधूत्तमं तपोदानं जम्बूमार्गमथापि च॥ हिरण्वती वितस्ता च तथा प्लक्षवती नदी। वेदस्मृतिर्वेदवती मालवाथाश्ववत्यपि॥ भूमिभागास्तथा पुण्या गङ्गाद्वारमथापि च। ऋषिकुल्यास्तथा मेध्या नद्य: सिंधुवहास्तथा॥ चर्मण्वती नदी पुण्या कौशिकी यमुना तथा। नदी भीमरथी चैव बाहुदा च महानदी॥ माहेन्द्रवाणी त्रिदिवा नीलिका च सरस्वती। नन्दा चापरनन्दा च तथा तीर्थमहाह्रदः॥ गयाथ फल्गुतीर्थ च धर्मारण्यं सुरैर्वृतम्। तथा देवनदी पुण्या सरश्च ब्रह्मनिर्मितम्॥ पुण्यं त्रिलोकविख्यातं सर्वपापहरं शिवम्। हिमवान् पर्वतश्चैव दिव्यौषधिसमन्वितः॥ विध्यो धातुविचित्राङ्गस्तीर्थवानौषधान्वितः। मेरुर्महेन्द्रो मलयः श्वेतश्च रजतावृतः॥ शृङ्गवान् मन्दरो नीलो निषधो दर्दुरस्तथा। चित्रकूटोऽजनाभश्च पर्वतो गन्धमादनः॥ पुण्यः सोमगिरिश्चैव तथैवान्ये महीधराः। दिशश्च विदिशश्चैव क्षितिः सर्वे महीरुहाः॥ विश्वेदेवा नभश्चैव नक्षत्राणि ग्रहास्तथा। पान्तु नः सततं देवा: कीर्तिताऽकीर्तिता मया॥
en: Then comes the three-eye Lord of Uma; then Scanda the commander in-chief of the celestial army, then Vishoka; then Agni the eater of sacrificial libations; then Vayu the god of wind; then Chandramas; then the sungod, gifted with effulgence; then the illustrious Shankra the husband of Sachi, and Yama with his wife Dhumorna; and Varuna with Gauri; Kubera the lord of riches, with his wife Riddhi; the amiable and illustrious cow Surabhi, the great Rishi Vishravas; Sankalpa, Ocean, Ganga; the other sacred Rivers, the Maruts; the Valakhilyas crowned with success of penances; the island-born Krishna, Narada, Parvata; Vishvavasu; the Hahas; the Huhus; Tumburu; Chitrasena; the celestial messenger; the highly blessed celestial maidens; the celestial Apsaras; Urvashi, Menaka, Ramba, Mishrakeshi, Almbusha, Vishvachi, Ghritachi, Panchchada, Tilottama, the Adityas, the Vasus, the Ashvins, the Pitris; Dharma, (Righteousness); Vedic learning, Penances, Diksha, Perseverance (in religious acts) the Grandfather, Day and Night, Kashyapa, the the son of Marichi, Shukra, Brihaspati, Mangala the son of Earth, Vudha, Rahu, Shanaishchara, the Constellations, the Seasons, the Months, the fortnights, the Year, Garuda the son of Vinata, the several Oceans, the sons of Kadru, viz., the Snakes, Shatarudra, Vipasha, Chandrabhaga, Sarasvati, Sindhu, Devika, Prabhasa, the lakes of Pushkara, Ganga, Mahanadi, Vena, Kaveri, Narmada, Kaulampuna, Vishalya, Karatoya, Ambuvahini, Saryu, Gandaki, the great river Lohita, Tamra, Aruna, Vetravati, Parnasa, Gautami, Godavari, Vena, Krisnnavena, Dvije, Drishdvati, Kaveri, Vankhu, Mandakini, Prayaga, Prabhasa, the sacred Naimisha, the spot sacred to Vishvaswera or Mahadeva, viz., Kashi, that lake of crystal water, Kurukshetra, full of many sacred waters, the foremost of oceans (viz., the ocean of milk), Penances, Gifts, Jambamarga, Hiranwati, Vitasta the river Plakshavati, Vadasmriti, Vedamati, Malava, on Ashvavati, all sacred spots Earth, Gangadvars, the sacred Rishikulya, the river Chitravaha, the Charmanwati, the sacred river Kaushiki, the Yamuna, the river Bhimarathi, the great river Vahuda, Mahendravani, Tridiva, Milika, Sarasvati, Nanda the other Nanda, the large sacred lake Gaya, Phalgutirtha, Dharmaranya (the sacred forest) inhabited by the celestials, the sacred celestial river, the lake created by the Grandfather Brahinan, which is sacred and celebrated over the three worlds and auspicious and capable of purifying all sins, the Himavat mountain having excellent herbs, the Vindhya mountain variegated with various kinds of metals, containing many Tirhas and evergrown with medicinal herbs, Meru, Mahendrs, Malays, Shveta gifted with silver, Shringavat, Mandara, Nila, Nishadha, Dardura,
