Chitrakuta, Anjanabha, the Gandhamadana mountains, the sacred Somagiri, the various other mountains, the cardinal points of the compass, the subsidiary points, the Earth, all the trees, the Vishvedevas, the Firmament, the Constellations, the Planets, and the Deities, let these all, named and unnamed, rescue and purify us.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: कीर्तयानो नरो ह्येतान् मुच्यते सर्वकिल्विषैः। स्तुवंश्च प्रतिनन्दंश्च मुच्यते सर्वतो भयात्॥
en: The man, who takes the names of these, becomes purged of all his sins. By singing their praises and pleasing them, one becomes freed from every fear.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: सर्वसंकरपापेभ्यो देवतास्तवनन्दकः। देवतानन्तरं विप्रांस्तपः सिद्धास्तपोऽधिकान्॥
en: Indeed, the man, who delights in singing the hymns in laudation of the deities, becomes purged of all such sins as lead to birth in impure orders.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: कीर्तितान् कीर्तयिष्यामि सर्वपापप्रमोचनान्। यवक्रीतोऽथ रैभ्यश्च कक्षीवानौशिजस्तथा॥ भृग्वङ्गिरास्तथा कण्वो मेधातिथिरथ प्रभुः। बी च गुणसम्पन्न: प्राची दिशमुपाश्रिताः॥
en: After this recital of the deities, I shall name those learned Brahmanas crowned with ascetic merit and success and capable of purifying one of every sin. They are Yavakrita and Raibhya and Kakshivat and Aushija, and Bhrigu and Angirasa and Kanva and the powerful Medhatithi, and Varhi endued with every accomplishment. These all belong to the Eastern region.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: भद्रां दिशं महाभागा उल्मुचुः प्रमुचुस्तथा। मुमुचुश्च महाभागः स्वस्त्यात्रेयश्च वीर्यवान्॥ मित्रावरुणयोः पुत्रस्तथागस्त्यः प्रतापवान्। दृढायुश्चोर्ध्वबाहुश्च विश्रुतावृषिसत्तमौ॥
en: Others, viz., Unmuchu, Pramuchu, Mumuchu, all highly blessed, the highly energetic Svastyatreya, the highly powerful Agastya, the son of Mitra and Varuna; Dridhayu and Urdhavahu, those two foremost and celebrated of Rishis, these live in the Southern quarter.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: पश्चिमां दिशमाश्रित्य य एधन्ते निबोध तान्। उषङ्गुः सह सोदर्यैः परिव्याधश्च वीर्यवान्॥ ऋर्षिर्दीर्घतमाश्चैव गौतमः काश्यपस्तथा। एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितश्चैव महानृषिः॥ अत्रेः पुत्रश्च धर्मात्मा तथा सारस्वतः प्रभुः। उत्तरां दिशमाश्रित्य य एधन्ते निबोध तान्॥
en: Listen now to me as I name those Rishis who live in the Western quarter. They are Ushangu with his uterine brothers, greatly energetic, Dirghatamas, Gautama, Kashyapa, Ekata, Dvita, Trita, the righteous-souled son of Atri (viz., Durvasa). and and the powerful Sarasvati, Listen now to me as I name those Rishis who adore the celestial in sacrifices, living in the Northern region.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: अत्रिर्वसिष्ठः शक्तिश्च पाराशर्यश्च वीर्यवान्। विश्वामित्रो भरद्वाजो जमदग्निस्तथैव च।॥ ऋचीकपुत्रो रामश्च ऋषिरौद्दालकिस्तथा। श्वेतकेतुः कोहलश्च विपुलो देवलस्तथा॥ देवशर्मा च धौम्यश्च हस्तिकाश्यप एव च। लोमशो नाचिकेतश्च लोकहर्षण एव च॥ ऋषिरुग्रश्चवाश्चैव भार्गवश्च्यवनस्तथा।
en: They are Atri, Vasishtha, Shakti, Parashara's son Vyasa of Great energy; Vishvamitra, Bharadvaja, Jamadagni, the son of Richika, Rama, Auddalaka, Shvetaketu, Kohala, Vipula, Devala Devasharian, Dhaumya, Hastikashyapa, Lomasha, Nachiketa, Lomaharshana, Ugrashravas, and Bhrigu's son Chyavana. This is the number of Rishis gifted with Vedic learning.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: एष वै समवायश्च ऋषिदेवसमन्वितः॥ आद्यः प्रकीर्तितो राजन् सर्वपापप्रमोचनः।
en: They are primeval Rishis, O king, whose names, if taken, are capable of purifying one of every sin. After this I shall recite the names of the principle kings.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: नृगो ययातिर्नहुषो यदुः पूरुश्च वीर्यवान्।॥ धुन्धुमारो दिलीपश्च सगरश्च प्रतापवान्। कृशाश्वो यौवनाश्वश्च चित्राश्वः सत्यवांस्तथा॥ दुष्यन्तो भरतश्चैव चक्रवर्ती महायशाः। पवनो जनकश्चैव तथा दृष्टरथो नृपः॥ रधुर्नरवरश्चैव तथा दशरथो नृपः। रामो राक्षसहा वीरः शशबिन्दुर्भगीरथः॥ हरिश्चन्द्रो मरुत्तश्च तथा दृढरथो नृपः। महोदर्यो डलर्कश्च ऐलश्चैव नराधिपः॥ करन्धमो नरश्रेष्ठः कध्मोरश्च नराधिपः। दक्षोऽम्बरीषः कुकुरो रैवतश्च महायशाः॥ कुरुः संवरणश्चैव मान्धाता सत्यविक्रमः। मुचुकुन्दश्च राजर्षिर्जगुर्जाह्नविसेवितः॥ आदिराजः पृथुर्वैन्यो मित्रभानुः प्रियङ्करः। त्रसदस्युस्तथा राजा श्वेतो राजर्षिसत्तमः॥ महाभिषश्च विख्यातो निमिराजा तथाष्टकः। आयुः क्षुपश्च राजर्षिः कक्षेयुश्च नराधिपः॥ प्रतर्दनो दिवोदासः सुदासः कोसलेश्वरः। ऐलो नलश्च राजर्षिर्मनुश्चैव प्रजापतिः॥ हविध्रश्च पृषध्रश्च प्रतीपः शान्तनुस्तथा। अजः प्राचीनबर्हिश्च तथेक्ष्वाकुर्महायशाः॥ अनरण्यो नरपतिर्जानुजंघस्तथैव च। कक्षसेनश्च राजर्षिर्ये चान्ये चानुकीर्तिताः॥
en: They are Nriga, Yayati, Nahusha, Yadu, highly energetic Puru, Sagara, Dhundhumara, Dilpa of great prowess, Krisashva, Yauvanashva, Chitrashva, Satyavat, Dushmanta, Bharata who became an illustrious Emperor over many kings, Dasharatha, the heroic Rama, that destroyer of Rakshas, Shashabindu, Bhagiratha, Harishchandra, Maruta, Dridharatha, the highly fortunate Alarka, Aila, Karandhama, that foremost of men, Kashmira, Daksha, Ambarisha, Kukura, highly illustrious Raivata, Kuru, Samvarana, Mandhatri of Unmitigated prowess, the royal sage Muchukunda, Jahnu who was much favoured by Janhavi (Ganga), the first (in point of time) of all kings, viz., Prithu the son of Vena, Mitrabhanu, Priyankara, Trasadasyu, Shveta that foremost of royal sages, the celebrated Mahabhisha, Nimi. Ashtaka, Ayu, the royal sage Kshupa, Kaksheyu, Pratarddana, Divodasa, Sudasa, Koshaleshvara, Aila, Nala, the royal sage Manu, that lord of all creatures, Havidhra, Prishadhra, Pratipa, Shantanu, Aja, the Senior Varhi, Ikshvaku of great fame, Anaranya, Janujangha the royal sage Kakshasena, and inany others not named (in history).

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: तल्यमुत्थाय यो नित्यं संध्ये द्वेस्तमयोदये। पठेच्छुचिरनावृत्तः स धर्मफलभाग् भवेत्॥
en: That man, who rising carly in the morning, takes the names of these kings at the two twilight's, viz., at sunset and sunrise, with a pure body and mind and without distracted attention, wins great religious merit.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: देवा देवर्षयश्चैव स्तुता राजर्षयस्तथा। पुष्टिमायुर्यशः स्वर्गे विधास्यन्ति ममेश्वराः॥
en: One should sing the praises of the celestial Rishis, and the royal sages and say, These lord of the creation will ordain my growth, longevity and fame.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: मा विनं मा च मे पापं मा च मे परिपन्थिनः। ध्रुवो जयो मे नित्यः स्यात् परत्र च शुभा गतिः।।६२।
en: Let no calamity visit me, let no sin define me, and let there be no opponents or enemies of mine. Forsooth, I will always have victory and an auspicious end hereafter.

description: The means of happiness. The source of wellbeing
sn: मा विनं मा च मे पापं मा च मे परिपन्थिनः। ध्रुवो जयो मे नित्यः स्यात् परत्र च शुभा गतिः।।६२।
en: Let no calamity visit me, let no sin define me, and let there be no opponents or enemies of mine. Forsooth, I will always have victory and an auspicious end hereafter.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच शरतल्पगते भीष्मे कौरवाणां धुरन्धरे। शयाने वीरशयने पाण्डवैः समुपस्थिते॥ युधिष्ठिरो महाप्राज्ञो भम पूर्वपितामहः। धर्माणामागमं श्रुत्वा विदित्वा सर्वसंशयान्॥
en: Janamejaya said When that foremost person among the Kauravas, viz., Bhishma was lying on a bed of arrows—a bed that is always coveted by heroes and when the Pandavas were sitting around him, my great Grandfather Yudhishthira of much wisdom, heard these expositions of mysteries about the subject of duty and had all his doubts removed.

sn: दानानां च विधिं श्रुत्वा च्छिन्नधर्मार्थसंशयः। यदन्यदकरोद् विप्र तन्मे शंसितुमर्हसि॥
en: He heard also what the ordinances are about gifts, and thus had all his doubts removed about the topics of virtue and wealth. You should, O learned Brahmana, tell me now what else did the great Pandava king do.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अभून्मुहूर्ते स्तिमितं सर्वं तद्राजमण्डलम्। तूष्णीभूते ततस्तस्मिन् पटे चित्रमिवार्पितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said When Bhishma became silent, the entire body of kings became perfectly silent. Indeed, they all sat motionless there, like figures painted on canvas.

sn: मुहूर्तमिव च ध्यात्वा व्यासः सत्यवतीसुतः। नृपं शयानं गाड्यमिदमाह वचस्तदा॥ राजन् प्रकृतिमापन्नः कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। सहितो भ्रातृभिः सर्वैः पार्थिवैश्चानुयायिभिः॥
en: Then Vyasa the son of Satyavati, having thought for a moment, addressed the royal son of Ganga, saying, O king, the Kuru king Yudhishthira has been restored to his own nature, with all his brothers and followers.

sn: उपास्ते त्वां नरव्याघ्र सह कृष्णेन धीमता। तमिमं पुरयानाय समनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: With highly intelligent Krishna by his side he bends his head in respect to you. You should give him leave for returning to the city.

sn: एवमुक्तो भगवता व्यासेन पृथिवीपतिः। युधिष्ठिरं सहामात्यमनुजज्ञे नदीसुतः॥
en: Thus addressed by the holy Vyasa, the royal son of Shantanu and Ganga dismissed Yudhishthira and his counsellors.

sn: उवाच चैन मधुरं नृपं शान्तनवो नृपः। प्रविशस्व पुरीं राजन् व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: Addressing his grandson in a sweet voice, the royal son of Shantanu, also said, Do you return to your city, O king, Let the fever of your heart be removed.

sn: यजस्व विविधैर्यज्ञैर्वबन्नेः स्वाप्तदक्षिणैः। ययातिरिव राजेन्द्र श्रद्धादमपुरःसरः॥
en: Do you adore the celestials in various sacrifices distinguished by large gifts of food and riches like Yayati himself, O foremost of kings, gifted with devotion and selfcontrol.

sn: क्षत्रधर्मरतः पार्थ पितॄन् देवांश्च तर्पय। श्रेयसा योक्ष्यसे चैव व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: Devoted to the practices of the Kshatriya do you, O son of Pritha, please the departed manes and the celestials. You shall then acquire great benefits. Indeed let the fever of your heart be removed.

sn: रञ्जयस्व प्रजाः सर्वाः प्रकृती: परिसान्त्वय। सुहृदः फलसत्कारैरर्चयस्व यथार्हतः॥
en: Do you please all your subjects. Do you assure them and establish peace among all. Do you also honour all your wellwishers with such rewards as they deserve.

sn: अनु त्वां तात जीवन्तु मित्राणि सुहृदस्तथा। चैत्यस्थाने स्थितं वृक्षं फलवन्तमिव द्विजाः॥
en: Let all your friends and wellwishers live, depending on you for their means, as birds live, depending for their means upon a full grown tree laden with fruits and standing on a sacred spot.

sn: आगन्तव्यं च भवता समये मम पार्थिव। विनिवृत्ते दिनकरे प्रवृत्ते चोत्तरायणे॥
en: When the hour comes for departure from this world, do you come here, O king, I shall relinquish my body when the Sun, stopping in his southward course, will begin to return northwards.

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा च कौन्तेयः सोऽभिवाद्य पितामहम्। प्रययौ सपरीवारो नगरं नागसाह्वयम्॥
en: The son of Kunti answered, 'So be it!' and saluted his grandfather with respect and then started with all his relatives and followers, for the city of Hastinapur.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र पुरस्कृत्य गान्धारी च पतिव्रताम्। सह तैर्ऋषिभिः सर्वैतृभिः केशवेन च॥ पौरजानपदैश्चैव मन्त्रिवृद्धैश्च पार्थिव। प्रविवेश कुरुश्रेष्ठः पुरं वारणसाह्वयम्॥
en: Headed by Dhritarashtra and also Gandhari who was greatly devoted to her husband and accompanied by the Rishis and Keshava as also by the citizens and the inhabitants of the country and by his counsellors, O monarch, that foremost one of Kuru's race entered the city of Hastinapur.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कुन्तीसुतो राजा पौरजानपदं जनम्। पूजयित्वा यथान्यायमनुजज्ञे गृहान् प्रति॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then having duly honoured the citizens and the inhabitants of the province, the royal son of Kunti dismissed them to their respective homes.

sn: सान्त्वयामास नारीश्च हतवीरा हतेश्वराः। विपुलैरर्थदानैः स तदा पाण्डुसुतो नृपः॥
en: The Pandava king then consoled those women, who had lost their heroic husbands and sons in the battle, with profuse gifts of wealth.

sn: सोऽभिषिक्तो महाप्राज्ञः प्राप्य राज्यं युधिष्ठिरः। अवस्थाप्य नरश्रेष्ठः सर्वाः स्वप्रकृतीस्तथा॥
en: Having recovered his kingdom, Yudhishthira caused himself to be duly installed on the throne. That foremost of men then assured all his subjects by various deeds of good will.

sn: द्विजेम्यो गुणमुख्येभ्यो नैगमेभयश्च सर्वशः। प्रतिगृह्याशिषो मुख्यास्तथा धर्मभृतां वरः॥
en: That foremost of righteous men set himself to acquire the substantial blessings of the Brahmanas, of the foremost inilitary officers, and the leading citizens.

sn: उषित्वा शर्वरी: श्रीमान् पञ्चाशनगरोत्तमे। समय कौवाग्यस्य सस्मार पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Having passed fifty nights in the capital, the blessed monarch recollected the time indicated by his grandfather as the hour of his departure from this world.

sn: स निर्ययौ गजपुराद् याजकैः परिवारितः। दृष्ट्वा निवृत्तमादित्यं प्रवृतं चोत्तरायणम्॥
en: Accompanied by a number of priests he then left the city of Hastinapur having seen that the sun ceasing to go southwards, had begun to proceed in his northward course.

sn: धृतं माल्यं च गन्धांश्च क्षौमाणि च युधिष्ठिरः। चन्दानागुरुमुख्यानि तथा कालीयकान्यपि॥ प्रस्थाप्य पूर्वं कौन्तेयो भीष्मसंस्करणाय वै। माल्यानि च वराहा॑णि रतानि विविधानि च॥
en: Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, took with bin a large quantity of clarified butter and floral garlands and scents and silken cloths and excellent sandal wood and Aquilaria Agallocha and dark cloewood, for cremating the body of Bhishma. Various kinds of rich garlands and gems also were among those stores.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र पुरस्कृत्य गान्धारी च यशस्विनीम्। मातरं च पृथां धीमान् भ्रातृ॑श्च पुरुषर्षभान्॥ जनार्दनेनानुगतो विदुरेण च धीमता। युयुत्सुना च कौरव्यो युयुधानेन वा विभो॥ महता राजभोगेन पारिबहेण संवृतः। स्तूयमानो महातेजा भीष्मस्याग्नाननुव्रजन्॥
en: Placing Dhritarashtra at the head and queen Gandhari celebrated for her virtues, and his own mother Kunti and all his brothers also the highly intelligent Yudhishthira, accompanied by Krishna and wise Vidura, as also by Yuyutsu and Yuyudhana, and by his other relatives and followers forming a large train, proceeded, his praises sung the while by culogists and bards. The sacrificial fires of Bhishma were also borne in the procession.

sn: निश्चकाम पुरात् तस्माद् यथा देवपतिस्तथा। आससाद कुरुक्षेत्र ततः शान्तनवं नृपः॥
en: Thus accompanied, the king started from his city like a second king of the celestials. Soon he came upon the spot where the son of Shantanu was still lying on his bed of arrows.

sn: उपास्यमानं व्यासेन पाराशर्येण धीमता। नारदेन च राजर्षे देवलेनासितेन य॥ हतशिष्टैर्नृपैश्चान्यैर्नानादेशसमागतः। रक्षिभिश्च महात्मानं रक्ष्यमाणं समन्ततः॥ शयानं वीरशयने ददर्श नृपतिस्ततः। ततो रथादवातीर्य भ्रातृभिः सह धर्मराट्॥ अभवाद्याथ कौन्तेयः पितामहमरिंदम। द्वैपायनादीन् विप्रांश्च तैश्च प्रत्यभिनन्दितः॥
en: He saw his grandfather waited upon with reverence by Parasharas intelligent, son Vyasa, by Narada, O royal sage, by Devala and Asita, and also by the surviving unslain kings assembled from various parts of the country. Indeed, the king saw that his great grandfather, as he lay on his heroic bed, was guarded on all sides by the warriors appointed for that duty. Getting down from his car, king Yudhishthira, with his brothers, saluted his grandfather, that chastiser of all enemies. They also saluted the Rishis with the Island-born Vyasa at their head. They were saluted in return by them.

sn: ऋत्विग्भिर्ब्रह्मकल्पैश्च भ्रातृभिः सह धर्मजः। आसाद्य शरतल्पस्थमृषिभिः परिवारितम्॥
en: Accompanied by his priests each of whom resembled the grandfather Brahman himself, as also by his brothers, Yudhishthira, of undecaying glory, then approach that spot whereon Bhishma lay on his bed of arrows surrounded by those reverend Rishis.

sn: अब्रवीद् भरतश्रेष्ठं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। भ्रातृभिः सह कौरव्यः शयानं निम्नगासुतम्॥ युधिष्ठिरोऽहं नृपते नमस्ते जाह्नवीसुत। शृणोषि चेन्महाबाहो ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते॥
en: Then king Yudhishthira the just with all his brothers, addressed that foremost one of Kuru's race, the son of the River Ganga, as he lay on that bed of his saying, I am Yudhishthira, O king. Salutations to thee, O son of the River Janhavi. If you hearest me still, O tell me what I am to do for thee.

sn: प्राप्तोऽस्मि समये राजन्नग्नीनादाय ते विभो। आचार्यान् ब्राह्मणांश्चैव ऋत्विजो भ्रातरश्च मे॥ पुत्रश्व ते महातेजा धृतराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः। उपस्थितः सहामात्यो वासुदेवश्व वीर्यवान्॥
en: Carrying with me thy sacrificial fires, I have come here, O king and wait upon thec at the hour appointed. Preceptors of all branches of learning, Brahmanas, Ritvijas, all iny brothers, thy son the king Dhritarashtra of great energy, are all here with my counsellors as also Vasudeva of great prowess.

sn: हतशिष्टाश्व राजानः सर्वं च कुरुजांगलाः। तान् पश्य नरशार्दूल समुन्मीलय लोचने॥
en: The remnant of unslain warriors, and all the denizens of Kurujangala, are also here, Opening the eyes, O chief of Kuru's race, do you see them.

sn: यच्चेह किंचित् कर्तव्ये तत्सर्वं प्रापितं मया। यथोक्तं भवता काले सर्वमेव च तत् कृतम्॥
en: Whatever should be done on this occasion have all been arranged and provided for by me. Indeed, at this hour which you hadst spoken of, all things have been kept in readiness.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु गाङ्गेयः कुन्तीपुत्रेण धीमता। ददर्श भारतान् सर्वान् स्थितान् सम्परिवार्य ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by the highly intelligent Kunti's son the son, of Ganga opened his eyes and all the Bharatas assembled there and stood around him.

sn: ततश्व तं बली भीष्मः प्रगृह्म विपुलं भुजम्। उद्यन्मेघस्वरो वाग्मी काले वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The mighty Bhishma then, taking the strong hand of Yudhishthira, addressed hiin, in a voice deep as that of the clouds.

sn: दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि कौन्तेय सहामात्यो युधिष्ठिर। परिवृत्तो हि भगवान् सहस्रांशुर्दिवाकरः॥
en: By good luck, O son of Kunti, you have come here with all your counsellors, O Yudhishthira. The thousandrayed maker of day, the holy Sun, has begun his northward course.

sn: अष्टपञ्चाशतं राज्यः शयानस्याद्य मे गताः। शरेषु निशिताग्रेषु यथा वर्षशत तथा॥
en: I have been lying on my bed here for fiftycight nights. Stretched these on shai ppointed arrows, I have felt this period to be as long as if it was a century.

sn: माघोऽयं समनुप्राप्तो मासः सौम्यो युधिष्ठिर। त्रिभागशेषः पक्षोऽयं शुक्लो भवितुमर्हति॥
en: O Yuthishthira, the lunar month of Magha has come. This is, again, the lighted fortnight and a fourth part of it ought by this (according to my calculations) be over.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु गाङ्गेयो धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। धृतराष्ट्रमथामन्ञ्य काले वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having said so to Yudhishthira the son of Dharma, Ganga's son Bhishma then saluted Dhritarashtra and said to him as follows.

sn: भीष्म उवाच राजन् विदितधर्मोऽसि सुनिर्णीतार्थसंशयः। बहुश्रुता हि ते विप्रा बहवः पर्युपासिताः॥
en: Bhishma said O king, you know well the duties. All your doubts, again, relating to the science of wealth, have been well solved. You have served many learned Brahmanas.

sn: वेदशास्राणि सर्वाणि धर्मोश्च मनुजेश्वर। वेदांश्च चतुरः सर्वान् निखिलेनानुबुद्ध्यसे॥
en: You know the subtile sciences connected with the Vedas, all the duties of religion, O king, and the whole of the four Vedas.

sn: न शोचितव्यं कौरव्य भवितव्यं हि तत् तथा। श्रुतं देवरहस्यं ते कृष्णद्वैपायनादपि॥
en: You should not grieve, therefore, O son of Kuru. That which was preordained has come to pass. It could not be otherwise. You have heard the mysteries relating to the deities from the lips of the Islandborn Rishi himself.

sn: यथा पाण्डोः सुता राजंस्तथैव तव धर्मतः। तान् पालय स्थितो धर्मे गुरुशुश्रूषणे रतान्॥
en: Yuthishthira and his brothers are morally as much your sons as are the sons of Pandu. Following the duties of religion, cherish and protect them. In their turn, they are always devoted to the service of their elders.

sn: धर्मराजो हि शुद्धात्मा निदेशे स्थास्यते तव। आनृशंस्यपरं ह्येनं जानामि गुरुवत्सलम्॥
en: King Yudhishthira, the just, is pure souled. He will always be obedient to you. I know that he is given to the virtue of mercy or abstention from injury. He is devoted to his elders and preceptors.

sn: तब पुत्रा दुरात्मानः क्रोधलोभपरायणाः। ईर्ष्याभिभूता दुर्वृत्तास्तान् न शोचितुमर्हसि॥
en: Your sons wore all wickedsouled. They were full of anger and cupidity. Overwhelmed by envy they were all of wicked conduct. You should not grieve for them.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं धृतराष्ट्र मनीषिणम्। वासुदेवं महाबाहुमभ्यभाषत कौरवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this much to Dhritarashtra of great wisdom, the Kuru chief then addressed Vasudeva of great arms.

sn: भीष्म उवाच भगवन् देवदेवेश सुरासुरनमस्कृत। त्रिविक्रम नमस्तुभ्यं शङ्खचक्रगदाधर॥
en: O holy one, O god of all gods O you adored by all the deities and Asuras, O you who didst cover the three worlds with three steps of thine, I bow unto thee, O wielder of the conch, the discus, and the mace.

sn: वासुदेवो हिरण्यात्मा पुरुषः सविता विराट्। जीवभूतोऽनुरूपस्त्वं परमात्मा सनातन॥
en: You are Vasudeva, you are of golden body, you are the one Purusha (or active agent), you are the creator (of the universe), You are of huge proportions. You are sentiency. You are subtle. You are the Supreme and Eternal Soul.

sn: त्रायस्व पुण्डरीकाक्ष पुरुषोत्तम नित्यशः। अनुजानीहि मां कृष्ण वैकुण्ठ पुरुषोत्तम॥ रक्ष्याश्च ते पाण्डवेया भवान् येषां परायणम्।
en: Do you, O lotuseyed one, save me, O foremost of all beings. Do you give me to permission, O Krishna, to depart from this world, O you who are supreme happiness, O foremost of all beings. You should always protect the sons of Pandu. You are, indeed, already their sole refuge.

sn: उक्तवानस्मि दुर्बुद्धिं मन्दं दुर्योधनं तदा॥ यतः कृष्णस्ततो धर्मो यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः।
en: Formerly, I spoke the foolish Duryodhana of wicked understanding that there is Virtue where Krishna is, and that there is victory where Virtue is.

sn: वासुदेवेन तीर्थेन पुत्र संशाम्य पाण्डवैः॥ संधानस्य परः कालस्तवेति च पुनः पुनः।
en: I further advised him that depending on Vasudeva as his refuge, he should make peace with the Pandavas, Indeed, I repeatedly told him, “This is the fittest time for you to make peace.'

sn: न च मे तद् वचो मूढः कृतवान् स सुमन्दधीः। घातयित्वेह पृथिवीं ततः स निधनं गतः॥
en: The foolish and wicked Duryodhana however did not do what I said. Having caused a great havoc on Earth, at last, he himself gave up his life.

sn: त्वां तु जानाम्यहं देवं पुराणमृषिसत्तमम्। नरेण सहितं देव वदर्यां सुचिरोषितम्॥
en: I know thee, O illustrious one, to be that ancient and best of Rishis who lived for many years in the company of Nara, in hermitage of Badari.

sn: तथा मे नारदः प्राह व्यासश्च सुमहातपाः। नरनारायणावेतौ सम्भूतौ मनुजेष्विति॥
en: The celestial Rishi Narada told me this, as also Vyasa of austere penances. Even they have said to me that, Thyself and Arjuna are the old Rishis Narayana and Nara born among men.

sn: स मां त्वमनुजानीहि कृष्ण मोक्ष्ये कलेवरम्। त्वयाह समनुज्ञातो गच्छेयं परमां गतिम्॥
en: Do you, O Krishna, grant me leave. I shall renounce my body. Permitted by thec, I shall attain to the highest end.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच अनुज्ञानामि भीष्म त्वां वसून् प्राप्नुहि पार्थिव। न तेऽस्ति वृजिनं किंचिदिहलोके महाद्युते॥
en: Vasudeva said I give you leave, O Bhishma, O king, to attain to the status of the Vasus. O you of great splendour, you have not been guilty of a single sin, in this world.

sn: पितृभक्तोऽसि राजर्षे मार्कण्डेय इवापरः। तेन मृत्युस्तव वशे स्थितो भृत्य इवानतः॥
en: O royal sage, you are devoted to your father. You are, therefore, like a second Markandeya. It is, therefore, that death depends upon your pleasure like a slave.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु गाङ्गेयः पाण्डवानिदमब्रवीत्। धृतराष्ट्रमुखांश्चपि सर्वोश्च सुहृदस्तथा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said these words, the son of Ganga once more addressed the Pandavas headed by Dhritarashtra, and other friends and wellwishers of his.

sn: प्राणानुत्स्रष्टुमिच्छामि तत्रानुज्ञातुमर्हथ। सत्येषु यतितव्यं वः सत्यं हि परमं बलम्॥
en: I wish to renounce my life. You should give me leave. You should strive for attaching to truth. Truth forms the highest power.

sn: आनृशंस्यपरैर्भाव्यं सदैव नियतात्मभिः। ब्रह्मण्यैर्धर्मशीलैश्च तपोनित्यैश्च भारताः॥
en: You should always live with Brahmanas of righteous conduct, devoted to penances, ever abstaining from cruel conduct, and who have their souls under restraint.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा सुहृदः सर्वान् सम्परिष्वज्य चैव हा पुनरेवाब्रवीद् धीमान् युधिष्ठिरमिदं वचः॥ ब्राह्मणाश्चैव ते नित्यं प्राज्ञाश्चैव विशेषतः। आचार्या ऋत्विजश्चैव पूजनीया जनाधिप॥
en: Having said these words to his friends and embraced them all, the intelligent Bhishma once more addressed Yudhishthira, saying, "O king, worship all Brahmanas, especially those who are gifted with wisdom, them who are preceptors, those who are priests capable of assisting at sacrifices.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा कुरुन् सर्वान् भीष्मः शान्तनवस्तदा। तूष्णीं बभूव कौरव्यः स मुहूर्तमरिंदम॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said so to all the Kurus, Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, remained silent for some time, O chastiscr of enemies.

sn: धारयामास चात्मानं धरणासु यथाक्रमम्। तस्योर्ध्वमगमन् प्राणाः संनिरुद्धा महात्मनः॥
en: He then held forth his lifebreaths successively in those parts of his body which are indicated in Yoga. The vital airs of that great one, restrained duly, then rose up.

sn: इदमाश्चर्यमासीच्च मध्ये तेषां महात्मनाम्। सहितैर्ऋषिभिः सर्वैस्तदा व्यासादिभिः प्रभो॥
en: Those parts of the body of Shantanu's son, on account of the adoption of Yoga from which the vital airs went up, became soreless one after another.

sn: यद्ययन्मुञ्चति गात्रं हि स शान्तनुसुतस्तदा। तत् तद् विशल्यं भवति योगयुक्तस्य तस्य वै॥
en: In the midst of those great persons, including those great Rishis headed by Vyasa, the sight seemed to be a strange one, O king.

sn: क्षणेन प्रेक्षतां तेषां विशल्यः सोऽभवत् तदा। तद् दृष्ट्वा विस्मिताः सर्वे वासुदेवपुरोगमाः॥ सह तैर्मुनिभिः सर्वैस्तदा व्यासादिभिर्नृप।
en: Within a short time, the eniire body of Bhishma became arrowless and soreless. Seeing it, all those great personages, headed by Vasudeva, and all the ascetics with Vyasa, became filled with wonder.

sn: संनिरुद्धस्तु तेनात्मा सर्वेष्वायतनेषु च॥ जगाम भित्त्वा मूर्धानं दिवमभ्युत्पपात ह।
en: The vital airs, restrained and unable to escape through any of the outlets, at last passed through the crown of the head and proceeded upwards to Heaven.

sn: देवदुन्दुभिनादश्च पुष्पवर्षेः सहाभवत्॥ सिद्धा ब्रह्मर्षयश्चैव साधु साध्विति हर्षिताः।
en: The celestial kettledrums began to play and floral showers were rained down. The Siddhas and regenerate Rishis, filled with delight, exclaimed, Excellent, Excellent.

sn: महोल्केव च भीष्मस्य मूर्धदेशाज्जनाधिप।॥ निःसृत्याकाशमाविश्य क्षणेनान्तरधीयता
en: The vital airs of Bhishma, piercing through the crown of his head, shot up through the sky like a large metcor and soon became invisible.

sn: एवं स राजशार्दूल नृपः शान्तनवस्तदा॥ समयुज्यत कालेन भरतानां कुलोद्वहः।
en: O great king, thus did Shantanu's son, that pillar of Bharata's race, unite himself with eternity.

sn: ततस्त्वादाय दारुणि गन्यांश्च विविधान् बहून्॥ चितां चक्रुर्महात्मान पाण्डवा विदुरस्तथा।
en: Then the great Pandavas and Vidura, taking a large quantity of wood and various kinds of fragrant scents, made a funeral pyre.

sn: युयुत्सुश्चपि कौरव्य प्रेक्षकास्त्वितरेऽभवन्॥ युधिष्ठिरच गाङ्गेयं विदुरश्च महामतिः। छादयामासतुरुभौ क्षौमैर्माल्यैश्च कौरवम्॥ धारयामास तस्याथ युयुत्सुच्छत्रमुत्तमम्।
en: Yuyutsu and others stood as spectators of the preparations. Then Yudhishthira and the great Vidura wrapped Bhishma body with silken cloth and floral garlands. Yuyutsu held an excellent uinbrella over it.

sn: चामरव्यजने शुभ्रे भीमसेनार्जुनावुभौ॥ उष्णीषे परिगृहीतां माद्रीपुत्रावुभौ तथा।
en: Bhimasena and Arjuna both held in their hands a couple of pure white yaktails. The two sons of Madri held two headgears in their hands.

sn: स्त्रियः कौरवनाथस्य भीष्मं कुरुकुलोद्वहम्॥ तालवृन्तान्युपादाय पर्यवीजन्त सर्वशः। ततोऽस्य विधिवच्चक्रुः पितृमेधं महात्मनः॥ यजनं बहुशश्चाग्नौ जगुः सामानि सामगाः।
en: Yudhishthira and Dhritarashtra stood at the feet of the body, taking up palmyra fans, the wives of the lord of the Kurus stood around the body and began to fan it softly. The Pitri sacrifice of the great Bhishma was then duly performed. Many libations were poured upon the sacred fire. The singers of Samans sang many Samans.

sn: ततश्चन्दनकाष्ठैश्च तथा कालीयकैरपि।॥ कालागुरुप्रभृतिभिर्गन्धैश्चोच्वाचैस्तथा। समवच्छाद्य गाङ्गेयं सम्प्रज्वाल्य हुताशनम्॥ अपसव्यमकुर्वन्त धृतराष्ट्रमुखाश्चिताम्।
en: Then covering the body of Ganga's son with sandal wood and black aloe and the dark wood and other fragrant fuel, and setting ire to the same, the Kurus, with Dhritarashtra and others, stood on the right side of the funeral pyre.

sn: संस्कृत्य च कुरुश्रेष्ठं गाङ्गेयं कुरुसत्तमाः॥ जग्मुर्भागीरथीं पुण्यामृषिजुष्टां कुरूद्वहाः।
en: Having thus cremated the body of the son of Ganga those foremost ones of Kuru's race proceeded the sacred Bhagirathi, accompanied by the Rishis.

sn: अनुगम्यमाना व्यासेन नारदेनासितेन च॥ कृष्णेन भरतस्त्रीभिर्ये च पौरा: सभागताः।
en: They were followed by Vyasa, Narada, Asita, Krishna, by the ladies of the Bharata family, as also by such of the citizens of Hastinapur as had come to the place.

sn: उदकं चक्रिरे चैव गाङ्गेयस्य महात्मनः॥ विधिवत् क्षत्रियश्रेष्ठाः स च सर्वो जनस्तदा।
en: to All of them, the foremost of the Kshatriyas, arrived at the sacred river, duly offered Oblations of water to the great son of Ganga.

sn: ततो भगीरथी देवी तनयस्योदके कृते॥ उत्थाय सलिलात् तस्माद् रूदती शोकविहला।
en: After those oblations of water had been offered by them to her son the goddess Bhagirathi, rose up from the river, weeping and distracted by sorrow.

sn: परिदेवयती नत्र कौरवानभ्यभाषत॥ निबोधत यथावृत्तमुच्यमानं मयाऽनघाः।
en: In the midst of her lamentations, she addressed the Kurus, saying, You sinless ones, listen to me as I say to you all that took place.

sn: राजवृत्तेन सम्पन्नः प्रज्ञयाऽभिजनेन च॥ सत्कर्ता कुरुवृद्धानां पितृभक्तो महाव्रतः।
en: Gitted with royal conduct and disposition, and endued with wisdom and high birth, my Son was the benefactor of all the elders of his family. He was devoted to his father and was of high vows.

sn: जामदग्न्येन रामेण यः पुरा न पराजितः॥ दिव्यैरस्त्रैर्महावीर्यः स हतोऽद्य शिखण्डिना।
en: He could not be defeated by even Rama of Jamadagni's race with his highly powerful celestial weapons; alas, that hero has been killed by Shikhandin.

sn: अश्मसारमयं नूनं हृदयं मम पार्थिवाः॥ अपश्यन्त्याः प्रियं पुत्रं यन्न दीर्यति मेऽद्य वै।
en: You kings, forsooth, my heart is made of adamant, for it does not break even at the disappearance of that son from my view.

sn: समेतं पार्थिवं क्षत्रं काशिपुर्या स्वयंवरे॥ विजित्यैकरथेनैव कन्याश्चायं जहार ह।
en: At the Svayamvara at Kashi, he defeated on a single car the assembled Kshatriyas and carried away the three princesses.

sn: यस्य नास्ति बले तुल्यः पृथिव्यामपि कश्चन॥ हतं शिखण्डिना श्रुत्वा न विदीर्येत यन्मनः। जामदग्न्यः कुरुक्षेत्रे युधि येन महात्मना॥ पीडितो नातियत्नेन स हतोऽद्य शिखण्डिना।
en: There was no one on Earth who equalled him in power; alas, my heart does not break upon hearing the slaughter of that son of mine by Shikhandin. Who, high souled one, afflicted the son of Jamadagni, in the field of Kuru with very little exertion, is slain today by Shikhandin.

sn: एवंविधं बहु तदा विलपन्तीं महानदीम्॥ आश्वासयामास तदा गङ्गां दामोदरो विभुः। समाश्वसिहि भद्रे त्वं मा शुचः शुभदर्शने।॥ गतः स परमं लोकं तव पुत्रो न संशयः।
en: Hearing the goddess of the great river thus bewail the powerful Krishna consoled her with many soothing words. Krishna said, “O amiable one, be comforted. Do not give way to sorrow, O you of beautiful features. Forsooth, your son has gone to the highest region of happiness.

sn: वसुरेष महातेजाः शापदोषेण शोभने॥ मानुषत्वमनुप्राप्तो नैनं शोचितुमर्हसि।
en: O nice lady! He was ihe great effulgent Vasu compaled to take birth as a man on account of the curse of the sage Vasistha. Hence, it is not fair to wail for him.

sn: स एष क्षत्रधर्मेण अयुध्यत रणाजिरे॥ धनञ्जयेन निहतो नैष देवि शिखण्डिना।
en: According to Kshatriya duties, he was killed by Dhananjaya on the field of battle while engaged in battle. He has not been killed, O goddess, by Shikhandin.

sn: भीष्मं हि कुरुशार्दूलमुद्यतेषु महारणे॥ न शक्त: संयुगे हन्तुं साक्षादपि शतक्रतुः।
en: The very king of the celestials himself could not kill Bhishma in battle when he stood with stretched bow in hand.

sn: स्वच्छन्दतस्तव सुतो गतः स्वर्गं शुभानने॥ न शक्ता विनिहन्तुं हि रणे तं सर्वदेवताः।
en: (you of beautiful face, your son has happily gone to to Heaven. All the gods assembled together could not kill him in battle.

sn: तस्मान्मा त्यं सरिच्छ्रेष्ठे शोचस्व कुरुनन्दनम्। वसूनेष गतो देवि पुत्रस्ते विज्वरा भव॥
en: Do not, therefore, O goddess Ganga, grieve for that son of Kuru's race. He was one of the Vasus, O goddess, your son has gone to Heaven. Let the fever of your heart be removed."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्ता सा तु कृष्णेन व्यासेन तु सरिद्वरा। त्यक्त्वा शोकं महाराज स्वं वार्यवततार हा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by Krishna that foremost of all rivers cast off her grief, O great king, and became consoled.

sn: सत्कृत्य ते तां सरितं ततः कृष्णमुखा नृप। अनुज्ञातास्तया सर्वे न्यवर्तन्त जनाधिपाः॥
en: O monarch, having honoured that goddess duly all the kings there present, headed by Krishna, received her permission to go away from her banks.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वतीं चैव ततो जयमुदीरयेत्॥
en: Having saluted Narayana and Nara the best of male beings as also the Goddess of Learning, let us shout about success.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कृतोदकं तु राजानं धृतराष्ट्र युधिष्ठिरः। पुरस्कृत्य महाबाहुरुत्तताराकुलेन्द्रियः॥ उत्तीर्य तु महाबाहुर्बाष्पव्याकुललोचनः। पपात तीरे गङ्गाया व्याधविद्ध इव द्विपः॥
en: Vaishampayana said After the king Dhritarashtra had offered libations of water, the mighty-armed Yudhishthira, with his senses bewildered, and keeping the former in his front, ascended the banks (of the river), and as his eyes which filled with tears, he dropt down on the tank of the Ganga like an elephant pierced by the hunter.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: तं सीदमानं जग्राह भीमः कृष्णेन चोदितः। मैवमित्यब्रवीच्चैनं कृष्णः परबलार्दनः॥
en: Then, asked by Krishna, Bhima pulled him up from sinking. This must not be so, said Krishna, the anihilator of hostile armies.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: तमार्तं पतितं भूमौ श्वसन्तं च पुनः पुनः। ददृशुः पार्थिवा राजन् धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: The Pandavas, O king, beheld Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma troubled, lying on the ground and also sighing again and again.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा दीनमनसं गतसत्त्वं नरेश्वरम्। भूयः शोकसमाविष्टाः पाण्डवाः समुपाविशन्॥
en: And seeing the king despondent and feeble, the Pandavas, over-laden with grief, sat down surrounding him.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: राजा तु धृतराष्ट्रश्च पुत्रशोकाभिपीडितः। वाक्यमाह महाबुद्धिः प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्नरेश्वरम्॥ उत्तिष्ठ कुरुशार्दूल कुरु कार्यमनन्तरम्।
en: And gifted with high intelligence and wise vision, king Dhritarashtra greatly afflicted with grief for his sons, addressed the king, saying, Rise up, O foremost of Kurus,

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: क्षत्रधर्मेण कौन्तेय जितेयमवनी त्वया॥ भुक्ष्व भोगान् भ्रातृभिश्च सुहृद्धिश्च मनोऽनुगान्।
en: You now fulfill your duties. O Kunti's son, you have conquered this Earth like the Kshatriyas. Do you now, O king enjoy her with your brothers and friends.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: शोचितव्यं न पश्यामि त्वया धर्मभृतां वर॥ शोचितव्यं मया चैव गान्धार्या च महीपते।
en: O foremost of the pious, I do not see why you should grieve. O king, having lost a century of sons like wealth got in a dream, it is Gandhari and I, who should raelly mourn.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: ययोः पुत्रशतं नष्टं स्वप्नलब्धं यथा धनम्॥ अश्रुत्वा हितकामस्य विदुरस्य महात्मनः।
en: Not having listened to the weighty words of the great Vidura, who sought our well-being, I, of perverse senses, (now) repent.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: वाक्यानि सुमहार्थानि परितप्यामि दुर्मतिः॥ उक्तवान् विदुरो यन्मां धर्मात्मा दिव्यदर्शनः।
en: The virtuous Vidura, gifted with divine insight, had told me, your family will be extinct for the sins of Duryodhana.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: दुर्योधनापराधेन कुलं ते विनशिष्यति॥ स्वस्ति चेदिच्छसे राजन् कुलस्य कुरु मे वचः। वध्यतामेष दुष्टात्मा मन्दो राजा सुयोधनः॥ कर्णश्च शकुनिश्चैव नैनं पश्यतु कर्हिचित्। द्यूतसंघातमप्येषामप्रमादेन वारय॥ अभिषेचय राजानं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। स पालयिष्यति वशी धर्मेण पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: O king, if you wish for the well being of your family, act according to my advice. Renounce this wicked king, Suyodhana, and let not either Karna or Shakuni by any means see him. Stop their gambling too, and anoint the pious king Yudhishthira. That one of controlled senses will righteously govern the Earth.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: अथ नेच्छसि राजानं कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। मेढीभूतः स्वयं राज्यं प्रतिगृह्णीष्व पार्थिव॥ समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु वर्तमानं नराधिप। अनुजीवन्तु सर्वे त्वां ज्ञातयो भ्रातृभिः सह।॥
en: If you would not have king Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, then, O monarch, you yourself, celebrating a sacrifice, take charge of the kingdom, and regarding all creatures impartially, ( king, you let your kinsmen, O you benefactor of your kindred, subsist on your bounty.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: एवं ब्रुवति कौन्तेय विदुरे दीर्घदर्शिनि। दुर्योधनमहं पापमन्ववर्त वृथामतिः॥
en: When, O Kunti's son, the far-sighted Vidura said this, foolishly I followed the wicked Duryodhana.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: अश्रुत्वा तस्य धीरस्य वाक्यानि मधुराण्यहम्। फलं प्राप्य महद् दुःखं निमग्नः शोकसागरे॥
en: Having paid no heed to the sweet words of that sedate one, I have obtained this powerful grief as a consequence, and have been plunged in an occan of misery.

description: Yudhishthira's grief and consolation by Dhritarashtra
sn: वृद्धौ हि तेऽद्य पितरौ पश्य नौ दुःखितौ नृप। न शोचितव्यं भवता पश्यामीह जनाधिप।॥
en: See your old father and mother, O king, plunged in misery. But, O master of men, I find no reason for your sorrow.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु राज्ञा स धृतराष्ट्रेण धीमता। तूष्णीं बभूव मेधावी तमुवाचाथ केशवः॥
en: Thus accosted by the intelligent king Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira, gifted with understanding, became calm. And then Keshava (Krishna) said to him.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: अतीव मनसा शोकः क्रियमाणो जनाधिप। संतापयति चैतस्य पूर्वप्रेतान् पितामहान्॥
en: If a person indulges excessively in sorrow for his departed manes he grieves them.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: यजस्व विविधैर्यज्ञैर्बहुभिः स्वाप्तदक्षिणैः। देवांस्तर्पय सोमेन स्वधया च पितॄनपि॥
en: Do you (now) celebrate many a sacrifice with suitable presents to the priests; and do you please the celestials with Soma juice and the manes of your forefathers, with their due food and drink.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: अतिथीनन्नपानेन कामैरन्यैरकिंचनान्। विदितं वेदितव्यं ते कर्तव्यमपि ते कृतम्॥
en: Do you also please your guests with meat and drink and the poor with gifts after their hearts. A person of your high intelligence should not act thus.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: श्रुताश्च राजधर्मास्ते भीष्माद् भागीरथीसुतात्। कृष्णद्वैपायनाच्चैव नारदाद् विदुरात्तथा॥
en: You knew what ought to be known, you have performed what ought to be donc, and you have heard the duties of the Kshatriyas, recit ed by Bhishma, the son of Bhagirathi, by Krishna Dvaipayana, Narada and Vidura.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: नेमामर्हसि मूढानां वृत्तिं त्वमनुवर्तितुम्। पितृपैतामहं वृत्तिमास्थाय धुरमुद्वह॥
en: Therefore you should not act like a stupid; but following the course of your forefathers, sustain the burthen (of the Empire).

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: युक्तं हि यशसा क्षात्रं स्वर्ग प्राप्तुमसंशयम्। न हि कश्चिद्धि शूराणां निहतोऽत्र पराङ्मुखः॥
en: It is proper that a Kshatriya should attain the celestial region for certain by his (own) renown. Of heroes, those who came to be killed never shall have to turn away.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: त्यज शोक महाराज भवितव्यं हि तत्तथा। न शक्यास्ते पुनर्द्रष्टुं त्वया येऽस्मिन् रणे हताः।८।
en: Renounce your grief, O powerful king. Indeed, what has taken place was destined to happen so. You can in no way see those that have been killed in this war.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: एतावदुक्त्वा गोविन्दो धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। विरराम महातेजास्तमुवाच युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Having said this to Yudhishthira, prince of the pious, the high-spirited Govinda stopped; and Yudhishthira answered him thus.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच गोविन्द मयि या प्रीतिस्तव सा विदिता मम सौहृदेन तथा प्रेम्णा सदा मय्यनुकम्पसे॥
en: O Govinda, Is know full well your fondness for me. You have ever favoured me with your love and friendship.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: प्रियं त मे तु मे स्यात् सुमहत्कृतं चक्रगदाधर। श्रीमन् प्रीतेन मनसा सर्वे यादवनन्दन॥ यदि मामनुजानीयाद् भवान् गन्तुं तपोवनम्।
en: And, O holder of the mace and the discus, O scion of Yudhu's race, O glorious one, if (now) do you gladly permit me to retire into the woods, then you would do what is greatly desired by me.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: न हि शान्तिं प्रपश्यामि पातयित्वा पितामहम्॥ कर्णं च पुरुषव्याघ्र संग्रामेष्वपलायिनम्।
en: After having killed my grandfather, and that foremost of men, Karna, who never fled from the field of battle, I find no peace.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: कर्मणा येन मुच्येयमस्मात् क्रूरादरिंदम॥ कर्मणा तद् विधत्स्वेह येन शुध्यति मे मनः।
en: Do you, O Janardana, so ordain that I may be feed from this heinous sin and that iny mind may be purified.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: तमेवं वादिनं पार्थं व्यासः प्रोवाच धर्मवित्॥ सान्त्वयन् सुमहातेजाः शुभं वचनमर्थवत्।
en: As Pritha's son was speaking thus, the highly energetic Vyasa, knowing the duties of life, soothing him, spoke these excellent words.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: अकृता ते मतिस्तात पुनर्बाल्येन मुह्यसे॥ किमाकारा वयं तात प्रलपामो मुहुर्मुहुः।
en: My child, your mind is not yet calmed; and therefore you are again stupefied by childish feelings. And wherefore, O child, do we over and over again throw our words to the winds?

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: विदिताः क्षत्रधर्मास्ते येषां युद्धेन जीविका॥ तथा प्रवृत्तो नृपतिर्नाधिबधेन युज्यसे।
en: You know the duties of the Kshatriyas, who live by warfare. A king who has done his duty, should not allow himself to be overwhelmed by grief.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: मोक्षधर्माश्च निखिला याथातथ्येन ते श्रुताः॥ असकृच्चापि संदेहाश्छिन्नास्ते कामजा मया।
en: You have faithfully listened to the entire doctrine of salvation; and I have repeatedly removed your misgivings originating from desire.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अश्रद्दधानो दुर्मेधा लुप्तस्मृतिरसि ध्रुवम्॥ मैवं भव न ते युक्तमिदमज्ञानमीदृशम्।
en: Vaishampayana said, But not paying due heed to what I have unfolded, you of perverse understanding have doubtless forgotten it clean. Be it not so. Such ignorance is not worthy of you.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: प्रायश्चित्तानि सर्वाणि विदितानि च तेऽनघ। राजधर्माश्च ते सर्वे दानधर्माश्च ते श्रुताः॥
en: O sinless one, you are cognizant of all kinds of expiation; and you have also heard of the virtues of kings, as well as the merits of gifts.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: स कथं सर्वधर्मज्ञः सर्वागमविशारदः। परिमुह्यसि भूयस्त्वमज्ञानादिव भारत॥
en: Wherefore then, O Bharata, knowing every form of morality and versed in all the Agamas, are you overwhelmed (with grief) as if from ignorance.

sn: व्यास उवाच युधिष्ठिर तव प्रज्ञा न सम्यगिति मे मतिः। न हि कश्चित्स्वयं मर्त्यः स्ववशः कुरुते क्रियाम्॥
en: Vyasa said. O Yudhishthira, your wisdom, I conceive, is not sufficient. None does a work by his own power.

sn: ईश्वरेण च युक्तोऽयं साध्वसाधु च मानवः। करोति पुरुषः कर्म तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: It is god who engages him in deeds, good or bad, O bestower of honour. What is the cause then for repentance?

sn: आत्मानं मन्यसे चाथ पापकर्माणमन्ततः। शृणु तत्र यथापापमपकृष्येत भारत॥
en: You consider yourself as having perpetrated impious deeds. Do you therefore, O Bharata, listen to the way in which sins, may be removed.

sn: तपोभिः क्रतुभिश्चैव दानेन च युधिष्ठिर। तरन्ति नित्यं पुरुषा ये स्म पापानि कुर्वते॥
en: O Yudhishthira, those who commit sins, can always free themselves from them through penance, sacrifice and gifts.

sn: यज्ञेन तपसा चैव दानेन च नराधिप। पूयन्ते नरशार्दूल नरा दुष्कृतकारिणः॥
en: O king, O foremost of men, sinful people are purified by sacrifice, austerities and charity.

sn: असुराश्च सुराश्चैव पुण्यहेतोर्मखक्रियाम्। प्रयतन्ते महात्मानस्तस्माद् यज्ञाः परायणम्॥
en: The great celestials and Asuras celebrate sacrifices for acquiring religious mcrit; and therefore sacrifices are of great importance.

sn: यज्ञैरेव महात्मानो बभूवुरधिकाः सुराः। ततो देवाः क्रियावन्तो दानवनभ्यधर्षयन्॥
en: It is through sacrifices that the great celestials had grown so wondrously powerful; and having celebrated rites did they defeat the Danavas.

sn: राजसूयाश्वमेधौ च सर्वमेधं च भारत। नरमेधं च नृपते त्वमाहर युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Do you, O Yudhishthira, prepare for the Rajasuya, and the Horse-Sacrifice, as well as. O Bharata, for the Sarvamedha and the Naramedha.

sn: यजस्व वाजिमेधेन विधिवद् दक्षिणावता। बहुकामान्नवित्तेन रामो दाशरथिर्यथा॥ यथा च भरतो राजा दौष्यन्तिः पृथिवीपतिः। शाकुन्तलो महावीर्यस्तव पूर्वपितामहः॥
en: And as Dasharatha's son, Rama or as Dushyanta's and Shakuntala's son your ancestor, the lord of the Earth, thc exceedingly powerful king Bharata, had done, do you according to the ordinance celebrate the HorseSacrifice with presents.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच असंशयं वाजिमेधः पावयेत् पृथिवीमपि। अभिप्रायस्तु मे कश्चित् तं त्वं श्रोतुमिहार्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira replied:-Undoubtedly, the Horse-Sacrifice purifics princes. But I have a purpose of which you should hear.

sn: इमं ज्ञातिवधं कृत्वा सुमहान्तं द्विजोत्तम। दानमल्पं न शक्नोमि दातुं वित्तं च नास्ति मे॥
en: Having caused this huge slaughter of kindred, I cannot, O best of the twice-born ones, dispense gifts even on a small scale, I have no riches to give.

sn: न तु बालानिमान् दीनानुत्सहे वसु याचितुम्। तथैवाईव्रणान् कृच्छ्रे वर्तमानान् नृपात्मजान्॥
en: Nor can I for riches solicit these young sons of kings, living wretchedly with their wounds yet green, and undergoing suffering.

sn: स्वयं विनाश्य पृथिवीं यज्ञार्थं द्विजसत्तम। करमाहारयिष्यामि कथं शोकपरायणः॥
en: How, O foremost of twice-born ones, having myself destroyed the Earth, can I, overwhelmed with sorrow, levy dues for celebrating a sacrifice?

sn: अत्र मे दुर्योधनापराधेन वसुधा वसुधाधिपाः। प्रनष्टा योजयित्वास्मानकी, मुनिसत्तम॥
en: Through Duryodhana's folly, O best of ascetics, the kings of the Earth have met with destruction, and we with ignominy.

sn: दुर्योधनेन पृथिवी क्षयिता वित्तकारणात्। कोशश्चापि विशीर्णोऽसौ धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्मतेः॥
en: Duryodhana had wasted the Earth for money; and the treasury of that wicked son of Dhritarashtra is empty.

sn: पृथिवी दक्षिणा चात्र विधिः प्रथमकल्पितः। विद्वद्भिः परिदृष्टोऽयं शिष्टो विधिविपर्ययः॥
en: (In this sacrifice), the Earth is the sacrificial gift; this is the rule that is prescribed in the first instance. The learned observe the usual reversal of this rule though sanctioned.

sn: न च प्रतिनिधि कर्तुं चिकीर्षामि तपोधन। भगवन् सम्यक् साचिव्यं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Nor, O ascetic, do I like to have a substitute. In this matter, O reverend sir, you should favour me with your advice.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु पार्थेन कृष्णद्वैपायनस्तदा। मुहूर्तमनुसंचिन्त्य धर्मराजानमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus addressed by Pritha's son, KrishnaDvaipayana, thinking for a while, spoke to the righteous king. This treasury, (now) exhausted, shall be full. O son of Pritha, in the mountain Himavan (Himalaya) there is gold which had been left behind by Brahmanas at the sacrifice of the great Marutia.

sn: कोशश्चापि विशीर्णोऽयं परिपूर्णो भविष्यति। विद्यते द्रविणं पार्थ गिरौ हिमवति स्थितम्॥ उत्सृष्टं ब्राह्मणैर्यज्ञे मरुत्तस्य महात्मनः। तदानयस्व कौन्तेय पर्याप्तं तद् भविष्यति॥
en: O son of Pritha, today your treasury is cmply but it is expected to be filled very soon. In the sacrifice of high souled Marutta at mountain Himavat, left riches, you should collect them which is sufficient for yourself.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं यज्ञे मरुत्तस्य द्रविणं तत् समाचितम्। कस्मिंश्च काले स नृपो बभूव वदतां वर॥
en: Yudhishthira asked: How in that sacrifice celebrated by Marutta, was so much gold collected? And, O foremost of speakers, when did he reign?

sn: व्यास उवाच यदि शुश्रूषसे पार्थ शृणु कारन्धमं नृपम्। यस्मिन् काले महावीर्यः स राजासीन्महाधनः॥
en: Vyasa said If, O Pritha's son, you are anxious to hear, about that king of the Karandhama line, then listen to me as I tell you when that highly powerful king having immense riches reigned.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच शुश्रूषे तस्य धर्मज्ञ राजर्षेः परिकीर्तनम्। द्वैपायन मरुत्तस्य कथां प्रबूहि मेऽनघ॥
en: Yudhishthira said O righteous one, I wish to hear the history of that royal sage Marutta. Do you ( Dvaipayana, describe this to me, O sinless one.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: व्यास उवाच आसीत् कृतयुगे तात मनुर्दण्डधरः प्रभुः। तस्य पुत्रो महाबाहुः प्रसन्धिरिति विश्रुतः॥
en: Vyasa said O child, in the golden age Manu was lord wielding the sceptre. His son was known under the name of Prasandhi.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: प्रसन्धेरभवत् पुत्रः क्षुप इत्यभिविश्रुतः। क्षुपस्य पुत्र इक्ष्वाकुर्महीपालोऽभवत् प्रभुः।॥
en: Prasandhi had a son named Kshupa. Kshupa's son was king Ikshvaku.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: तस्य पुत्रशतं राजन्नासीत् परधार्मिकम्। तांस्तु सर्वान् महीपालानिक्ष्वाकुरकरोत् प्रभुः॥
en: He, O king, had a hundred sons possessed of pre-eminent picty. And all of them were inade monarchs by king Ikshvaku.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: तेषां ज्येष्ठस्तु विंशोऽभूत् प्रतिमानं धनुष्मताम्। विंशस्य पुत्रः कल्याणो विविंशो नाम भारत॥
en: The eldest of them, Vinsha, became an ideal bowman. Vinsha's son, O Bharata, was the auspicious Vivinsha.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: विविंशस्य सुता राजन् बभूवुर्दश पञ्च च। सर्वे धनुषि विक्रान्ता ब्रह्मण्याः सत्यवादिनः॥ दानधर्मरताः शान्ताः सततं प्रियवादिनः। तेषां ज्येष्ठः खनीनेत्रः स तान् सर्वानपीडयत्॥
en: Vivinsha, O king, had fifteen sons; all of them powerful archers, respecting Brahmanas and speaking the truth, gentle and everspeaking fair. The eldest brother Khaninetra, oppressed all his brothers.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: खनीनेत्रस्तु विक्रान्तो जित्वा राज्यमकण्टकम्। नाशकद् रक्षितुं राज्यं नान्वरज्यन्त तं प्रजाः॥
en: And having conquered the entire kingdom shorn of all troubles, Khaninetra, could not retain his supremacy; nor were the people satisfied with him.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: तमपास्य च तद्राज्ये तस्य पुत्रं सुवर्चसम्। अभ्यषिञ्चन्त राजेन्द्र मुदिता ह्यभवंस्तदा॥
en: And dethroning him, they, O foremost of kings invested his son Suvarcha with the rights of sovereignty, and experiences joy.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: स पितुर्विक्रियां दृष्ट्वा राज्यान्निरसनं च तत्। नियतो वर्तयामास प्रजाहितचिकीर्षया।॥ ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवादी च शुचिः शमदमान्वितः। प्रजास्तं चान्वरज्यन्त धर्मनित्यं मनस्विनम्॥
en: Seeing the reverses of his father and his expulsion from the empire he was ever busy with encompassing the well-being of the people, being devoted to Brahman, speaking the truth, practising purity and controlling his senses and thoughts. And the subjects were well-pleased with that grcat one constant in virtue.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: तस्य धर्मप्रवृत्तस्य व्यशीर्यत् कोशवाहनम्। तं क्षीणकोशं सामन्ताः समन्तात् पर्यपीडयन्॥
en: But he being constantly engaged in virtuous Works, His treasures and vehicles became greatly reduced. And on his treasury having become exhausted, the feudatory princes gathered round him and began to gave him trouble.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: स पीड्यमानो बहुभिः क्षीणकोशाश्ववाहनः। आर्तिमाळुत् परां राजा सह भृत्यैः पुरेण च॥
en: Being thus oppressed by many enemies while his treasury, horses and vehicles were impoverished, the king suffered great tribulation along with his retainers and the citizens.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: न चैनमभिहन्तुं ते शक्नुवन्ति बलक्षये। सम्यग्वृत्तो हि राजा स धर्मनित्यो युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Although his power decreased greatly, yet the enemies could not kill the king, for his power, ( Yudhishthira, was established in virtue.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: यदा तु परमामातिं गतोऽसौ सपुरो नृपः। ततः प्रदध्मौ स करं प्रादुरासीत् ततो बलम्॥
en: And when he had reached the worst point of misery along with the citizens, he blew his hand, and from that there appeared a supply of forces.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: ततस्तानजयत् सर्वान् प्रातिसीमान् नराधिपान्। एतस्मात् कारणाद् राजन् विश्रुतः स करन्धमः॥
en: And then he defeated all the kings living along the borders of his dominions And from this incident, O king, he hath been celebrated as Karandhama.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: तस्य कारन्धमः पुत्रस्त्रेतायुगमुखेऽभवत्। इन्द्रादनवरः श्रीमान् देवैरपि सुदुर्जयः॥
en: His son, Karandhama was born at the commencement of the Treta age, equalling Indra himself, gifted with grace, and invincible even by the immortals.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: तस्य सर्वे महीपाला वर्तन्ते स्म वशे तदा। स हि सम्राडभूत् तेषां वृत्तेन च बलेन च॥
en: At that time all the kings were under his control; and alike by virtue of his riches and of prowess, he became their emperor.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: अविक्षिन्नाम धर्मात्मा शौर्येणेन्द्रसमोऽभवत्। यज्ञशीलो धर्मरतिकृतिमान् संयतेन्द्रियः॥
en: In short, the righteous king Avikshit became like Indra himself in Heroism; and he was given to sacrifices, delighted in virtue and held his senses under control.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: तेजसाऽऽदित्यसदृशः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः। बृहस्पतिसमो बुद्ध्या हिमवानिव सुस्थिरः॥
en: And in energy he resembled the sun and in patience, Earth herself; in intelligence, he was like Brihaspati, and in calmness the mountain Himavan himself.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: कर्मणा मनसा वाचा दमेन प्रशमेन च। मनांस्याराधयामास प्रजानां स महीपतिः॥
en: And that king pleased the hearts of his subjects by act, thought, speech, self control, and forbearance.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: य ईजे हयमेधानां शतेन विधिवत् प्रभुः। याजयामास सं विद्वान् स्वयमेवाङ्गिराः प्रभुः॥
en: The lords who celebrated hundreds of Horse-Sacrifices, and whom the powerful and learned Angira himself served as priest.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: तस्य पुत्रोऽतिचक्राम पितरं गुणवत्तया। मरुत्तो नाम धर्मज्ञश्चक्रवर्ती महायशाः॥ नागायुतसमप्राणः साक्षाद् विष्णुरिवापरः।
en: His son excelled his father in the possession of good qualities; named Marutta, that lord of kings was righteous and of great fame; having the power of ten thousand elephants, and like unto Vishnu's second self.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: स यक्ष्यमाणो धर्मात्मा शातकुम्भमयान्युत॥ कारयामास शुभ्राणि भाजनानि सहस्रशः। मेरू पर्वतमासाद्य हिमवत्पार्श्व उत्तरे॥ काञ्चनः सुमहान् पादस्तत्र कर्म चकार सः। ततः कुण्डानि पात्रीश्च पिठराण्यासनानि च।॥ चक्रुः सुवर्णकर्तारो येषां संख्या न विद्यते।
en: Desirous of celebrating a sacrifice, that virtuous king, coming to Mount Meru on the northern side of Himavat, made thousands of shining golden vessels to be forged. There on a huge golden hill he performed the rites. And goldsmiths made numberless basins and vessels and pans and seats.

description: The story of the Royal Sage Marutta
sn: तस्यैव च समीपे तु यज्ञवाटो बभूव ह॥ ईजे तत्र स धर्मात्मा विधिवत् पृथिवीपतिः। मरुत्तः सहितैः सर्वैः प्रजापालैनराधिपः॥
en: And the sacrificial ground was near this place. And that righteous king Marutta, with other princes, celebrated a sacrifice there.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: कथंवीर्यः समभवत् स राजा वदतां वर। कथं च जातरूपेण समयुज्यत स द्विज॥
en: Yudhishthira said O best of speakers, how that king waxed so powerful? And how, O twice-born one, did he get so much gold?

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: क्व च तत् साम्प्रतं द्रव्यं भगवन्नवतिष्ठते। कथं च शक्यमस्माभिस्तदवाप्तुं तपोधन॥
en: And where now, O reverend sire, is all his wealth? And, O ascetic, how can we secure the same?

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: व्यास उवाच असुराश्चैव देवाश्च दक्षस्यासन् प्रजापतेः। अपत्यं बहुलं तात संस्पर्धन्त परस्परम्॥ तथैवाङ्गिरस: पुत्रौ व्रततुल्यौ बभूवतुः। बृहस्पतिर्ब्रहत्तेजाः संवर्तश्च तपोधनः॥ तावतिस्पर्धिनौ राजन् पृथगास्तां परस्परम्। बृहस्पतिः स संवर्तं बाधते स्म पुनः पुनः॥
en: Vyasa thereupon said-As the numerous children of the Prajapati Daksha, the Asuras, and the Celestials challenged each other, so in the same way Angira's sons, the highly energetic Brihaspati and the ascetic. Samvarta, of equal vows, challenged each other, O king. Brihaspati began to worry Samvarta again and again. was

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: स बाध्यमान् सततं भ्रात्रा ज्येष्ठेन भारत। अर्थानुत्सृज्य दिग्वासा वनवासमरोचयत्॥
en: And always troubled by his elder brother, he, O Bharata, renouncing his riches, went to the forest, with nothing to cover his body except the open sky.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: वासवोऽप्यसुरान् सर्वान् विजित्य च निपात्य च। इन्द्रत्वं प्राप्य लोकेषु ततो वव्रे पुरोहितम्॥ पुत्रमङ्गिरसो ज्येष्ठं विप्रज्येष्ठं बृहस्पतिम्। याज्यस्त्वङ्गिरसः पूर्वमासीद् राजा करंधमः॥ वीर्येणाप्रतिमो लोके वृत्तेन च बलेन च। शतक्रतुरिवौजस्वी धर्मात्मा संशितव्रतः॥
en: (At that time), having defeated and destroyed the Asuras, and gained the sovereignty of the celestial regions, Vasava had appointed as his priest Angira's eldest son, that best of Brahmanas, Brihaspati. Formerly Angira the family-priest of king Karandhama; peerless among men in might, power and character; powerful like Shatakratu. righteous-souled and of rigid vows.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: वाहनं यस्य योधाश्च मित्राणि विविधानि च। शयनानि च मुख्यानि महार्हाणि च सर्वशः॥ ध्यानादेवाभवद् राजन् मुखवातेन सर्वशः। स गुणैः पार्थिवान् सर्वान् वशे चक्रे नराधिपः॥
en: O king, he had vehicles, and warriors, and many adherents, and beautiful and rich bedsteads, produced through mediation by the breath of his mouth. And by his native virtues, the king had brought all the princes under his control.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: संजीव्य कालमिष्टं च सशरीरो दिवं गतः। बभूव तस्य पुत्रस्तु ययातिरिव धर्मवित्॥ अविक्षिन्नाम शत्रुजित् स वशे कृतवान् महीम्। विक्रमेण गुणैश्चैव पितेवासीत् स पार्थिवः॥
en: And having lives as long as he desired, he ascended the celestial region in his bodily form. And his named Avikshitconqueror of enemies-righteous like Yayati, brought all the Earth under his sway. And both in merit and power the king resembled his father. son

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: तस्य वासवतुल्योऽभून्मरुत्तो नाम वीर्यवान्। पुत्रस्तमनुरक्ताभूत् पृथिवी सागरम्बरा॥
en: He had a son named Marutta, gifted with energy, and resembling Vasava himself. This earth clad in oceans felt herself attracted towards him.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: स्पर्धते स स्म सततं देवराजेन नित्यदा। वासवोऽपि मरुत्तेन स्पर्धते पाण्डुनन्दन॥
en: He always used to defy the king of the celestials; and, O son of Pandu, Vasava also defied Marutta.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: शुचिः स गुणवानासीन्मरुत्तः पृथिवीपतिः। यतमानोऽपि यं शक्रो न विशेषयति स्म ह॥
en: And Marutta-master of Earth-was pure and perfect. And despite his striving, Shakra could not prevail over him.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: सोऽशक्नुवन् विशेषाय समाहूय बृहस्पतिम्। उवाचेदं वचो देवैः सहितो हरिवाहनः॥
en: And unable to control him, he riding on the horse, along with the celestials summoning Brihaspati, spoke to him thus.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: बृहस्पते मरुत्तस्य मा स्म कार्षीः कथंचन। दैवं कर्माथ पित्र्यं वा कर्तासि मम चेत् प्रियम्॥ अहं हि त्रिषु लोकेषु सुराणां च बृहस्पते। इन्द्रत्वं प्राप्तवानेको मरुत्तस्तु महीपतिः॥
en: O Brihaspati, if we wish to do what is agreeable to me, do not perform priestly offices for Marutta on behalf of the celestials or the departed Manes. I have, O Brihaspati, obtained the sovereignty of the three worlds, while Marutta is merely the king of the Earth.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: कथं ह्यमयं ब्रह्मंस्त्वं याजयित्वा सुराधिपम्। याजयेर्मृत्युसंयुक्तं मरुत्तमविशङ्कया॥
en: How, O Brahmana, having acted as priest to the immortal king of the celestials, will you unhesitatingly act as a priest to Marutta subject to death?

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: मां वा वृणीष्व भद्रं ते मरुत्तं वा महीपतिम्। परित्यज्य मरुत्तं वा यथाजोषं भजस्व माम्॥
en: May you fare well. Either take up my side or that of the king, Marutta, or forsaking Marutta, gladly come over to me.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: एवमुक्तः स कौरव्य देवराज्ञा बृहस्पतिः। मुहूर्तमिव संचिन्त्य देवराजानमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus addressed by the king of the Brihaspati, thinking for a mc.nent, replied to the king of the celestials.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: त्वं भूतानामधिपतिस्त्वयि लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः। नमुचेर्विश्वरूपस्य निहन्ता त्वं बलस्य च॥
en: You are the Lord of creatures, and in you are the worlds established. And you have killed Namuchi Vishvarupa and Vala.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: त्वमाजहर्थ देवानामेको वीरश्रियं पराम्। त्वं बिभर्षि भुवं द्यां च सदैव बलसूदन॥
en: You, O hero, alone, bring about the highest prosperity of the celestials, and O slayer of Bala, you sustain the carth as well as the celestial region.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: पौरोहित्यं कथं कृत्वा तव देवगणेश्वर। याजयेयमहं मर्त्य मरुत्तं पाकशासन॥ समाश्वसिहि देवेन्द्र नाहं मर्त्यस्य कर्हिचित्। ग्रहीष्यामि स्रुवं यज्ञे शृणु चेदं वचो मम॥
en: How, O foremost of the celestials, having officiated as you priest, shall I, O destroyer of Paka, O lord of gods, be passions, I will not take ladle in men's sacrifice, serve a mortal prince and listen to what I say.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: हिरण्यरेता नोष्ण स्यात् परिवर्तेत मेदिनी। भासं तु न रविः कुर्यान्न तु सत्यं चलेन्मयि॥
en: Even if the god of fire cease to cause heat and warmth, or the earth change its nature, or the sun cease to give light, I shall never deviate from the truth.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच बृहस्पतिवचः श्रुत्वा शक्रो विगतमत्सरः। प्रशस्यैनं विवेशाथ स्वमेव भवनं तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said On hearing these words of Brihaspati, Indra became freed from his envious feelings, and then lauding him he repaired to his own palace.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: व्यास उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। बृहस्पतेश्च संवादं मरुत्तस्य च धीमतः॥
en: Vyasa said Regarding it is cited the ancient legend of Brihaspati and the wise Marutta.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: देवराजस्य समयं कृतमाङ्गिरसेन ह। श्रुत्वा मरुत्तो नृपतिर्यज्ञमाहारयत् परम्॥
en: On hearing of the agreement made by Angira's son Brihaspati with the king of the celestials, king Marutta made the necessary preparations for a great sacrifice.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: संकल्प मनसा यज्ञं करन्धमसुतात्मजः। बृहस्पतिमुपागम्य वाग्मी वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: (Marutta) having conceived the idea of a sacrifice in his mind the eloquent grandson of Karandhama went to Brihaspati and spoke to him thus.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: भगवन् यन्मया पूर्वमभिगम्य तपोधन। कृतोऽभिसंधिर्यज्ञस्य भवतो वचनाद् गुरो॥ तमहं यष्टुमिच्छामि संभाराः सम्भृताश्च मे। याज्योऽस्मि भवतः साधो तत्प्राप्नुहि विधत्स्व च॥
en: O worshipful ascetic, I have intended to celebrate the sacrifice which you did propose to me once on a previous occasion, according to your instructions, and I now wish to appoint you, as officiating pricst at this sacrifice, the materials whereof I have collected, O excellent one, you are our family-priest, therefore do you take those sacrificial things and celebrate the sacrifice yourself.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: बृहस्पति उवाच न कामये याजयितुं त्वामहं पृथिवीपते। वृतोऽस्मि देवराजेन प्रतिज्ञातं च तस्य मे॥
en: Brihaspati said O king, I do not wish to perform your। sacrifice, I have been appointed as priest by the King the Celestials and I have promised to him to act as such.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: मरुत्त उवाच पित्र्यमस्मि तव क्षेत्रं बहु मन्ये च ते भृशम्। तवास्मि याज्यतां प्राप्तो भजमानं भजस्व माम्॥
en: Marutta said You are our hereditary family-priest, and therefore I cherish great regard for you, and I have acquired the right of being helped at sacrifices by you, and therefore it is proper that you should officiate as priest at my sacrifice.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: बृहस्पति उवाच अमर्त्य याजयित्वाहं याजयिष्ये कथं नरम्। मरुत्त गच्छवा मा वा निवृत्तोऽस्म्यद्य याजनात्॥
en: Having, O Marutta, acted as priest to the celestials, how can I act as such to mortal men, and whether you do leave this place or stay here, I tell you I have ceased to act as priest to any but the celestials.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: न त्वां याजयिताऽस्म्यद्य वृणु यं त्वमिहेच्छसि। उपाध्यायं महाबाहो यस्ते यज्ञं करिष्यति॥
en: O you of mighty arms, I am unable to act as your priest now. And according to your own desire, you can appoint any one as your priest who will perform your sacrifice.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: व्यास उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु नृपतिर्मरुत्तो व्रीडितोऽभवत्। प्रत्यागच्छन् सुसंविग्नो ददर्श पथि नारदम्॥
en: Vyasa said Thus told, king Marutta became confounded with shame, and while returning home with his mind stricken with anxiety, he met Narada on his way,

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: देवर्षिणा समागम्य नारदेन स पार्थिवः। विधिवत् प्राञ्जलिस्तस्थावथैनं नारदोऽब्रवीत्॥ राजर्षे नातिहष्टोऽसि कच्चित् क्षेमं तवानघ। क्व गतोऽसि कुतश्चेदमप्रीतिस्थ मागतम्॥
en: And on seeing the divine Rishi Narada, that king stood before him with due salutation, and with his hands clasped together, and then Narada addressing him thus said, O royal sage, you appear to be not well-pleased in your mind, is all well with you, where have you been, O sinless one, and why is this your mental disquietude?

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: श्रोतव्यं चेन्मया राजन् ब्रूहि मे पार्थिवर्षभ। व्यपनेष्यामि ते मन्युं सर्वयत्नैर्नराधिप॥
en: And, O king, if there be no objection to your telling it to me, do you, O best O kings, disclose to me, so that, O prince, I may remove the disquietude of your mind with all my efforts.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तौ मरुत्तः स नारदेन महर्षिणा। विप्रलम्भमुपाध्यायात् सर्वमेव न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Vaishampayana continued : Thus addressed by the great Rishi Narada, king Marutta informed him of the refusal he had received from his religious preceptor.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: मरुत्त उवाच गतोऽस्म्याङ्गिरसः पुत्रं देवाचार्यं बृहस्पतिम्। यज्ञार्थमृत्विजं द्रष्टुं स च मां नाभ्यनन्दत॥
en: Marutta said Trying to find out a priest to officiate at my sacrifice, I went to that priest of the Immortals, Brihaspati, the son of Angirasa, but he did not choose to accept my offer.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: प्रत्याख्यातश्च तेनाहं जीवितुं नाद्य कामये। परित्यक्तश्च गुरुणा दूषितश्चास्मि नारद॥
en: Having met with this refusal from him, I have no desire to live any longer now, for by his abandoning me thus, I have, O Narada, become sullied with sin.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: व्यास उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु राज्ञा स नारदः प्रत्युवाच ह। आविक्षितं महाराज वाचा संजीवयन्निव॥
en: Vyasa said Thus told by that king, Narada, O powerful prince, made this reply to him with words which seemed to revive that son of Avikshit.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: नारद उवाच राजन्नङ्गिरसः पुत्रः संवर्तो नाम धार्मिकः। चङ्क्रमीति दिशः सर्वा दिग्वासा मोहयन्प्रजाः।।१८। तं गच्छ यदि याज्यं त्वां न वाञ्छति बृहस्पतिः। प्रसन्नस्त्वां महातेजाः संवर्तो याजयिष्यति॥
en: Narada said The virtuous son of Angirasa, Samvarla by name, is travelling over all the earth in a nude state to the amazement all creatures; do you, O prince, go to him, if Brihaspati does not wish to officiate at your sacrifice, the powerful Samvarta, if pleased with you, will perform your sacrifice.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: मरुत्त उवाच संजीविताऽहं भवता वाक्येनानेन नारद। पश्येयं क्व न संवर्तं शंस मे वदतां वर॥ कथं च तस्मै वर्तेयं कथं मां न परित्यजेत्। प्रत्याख्यातश्च तेनापि नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥
en: Marutta said I feel as if filled with new life, by these your words, O Narada, but O the best of speakers, do you tell me where I can find Samvarta, and how I can remain by his side, and how I ma to act so that he may not leave inc, for I do not wish to live if I mcet with a refusal from him also.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: नारद उवाच उन्मत्तवेषं विभ्रत् स चक्रमीति यथासुखम्। वाराणस्यां महाराज दर्शनेप्सुर्महेश्वरम्॥
en: Narada said Desirous of seeing Maheshvara, O prince, he roves about at his pleasure in the city of Varanasi dressed as a maniac.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: तस्या द्वारं समासाद्य न्यसेथाः कुणपं क्वचित्। तं दृष्ट्वा यो निवर्तेत संवर्तः स महीपते॥ तं पृष्ठतोऽनुगच्छेथा यत्र गच्छेत् स वीर्यवान्। तमेकान्ते समासाद्य प्राञ्जलिः शरणं व्रजेः॥
en: And having reached the gate of the city, you must place a dead body somewhere near it, and the man who shall turn away on seeing the dead body, do you, O prince, know that man to be Samvarta, and knowing him, do you follow his footsteps wherever that powerful man wishes to go, and finding him (at length) in a lonely place you must seek his protection with your hands clasped together.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: पृच्छेत् त्वां यदि केनाहं तवाख्यात इति स्म ह। ब्रूयास्त्वं नारदेनेति संवर्त कथितोऽसि मे॥
en: And if he acquire of you as to the person who has given you the information about his own self, do you tell him that Narada has informed you about Samvarta.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: स चेत् त्वामनुयुञ्जीत ममानुगमनेप्सया। शंसेथा वह्निमारूढं मामपि त्वमशङ्कया॥
en: And if he should ask you to follow me, you must tell him unhesitatingly that I have entered into the fire.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: व्यास उवाच स तथेति प्रतिश्रुत्य पूजयित्वा च नारदम्। अभ्यनुज्ञाय राजर्षिययौ वाराणसी पुरीम्॥ तत्र गत्वा यथोक्तं स पुर्या द्वारे महायशाः। कुणपं स्थापयामास नारदस्य वचः स्मरन्॥
en: Vyasa said Having signified his consent to the proposal of Narada, that royal sage after duly adoring him and with his permission, went to the city of Varanasi, and having reached there, that famous prince did as he had been asked, and remembering the words of Narada, he placed a dead body at the gate of the city.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: यौगपद्येन विप्रश्च पुरीद्वारमथाविशत्। ततः स कुणपं दृष्ट्वा सहसा संन्यवर्तत॥
en: And by coincidence, that Brahmana also entered the gate of the city at the same time. Then on seeing the dead body, he suddenly turned away.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: स तं निवृत्तमालक्ष्य प्राञ्जलि: पृष्ठतोऽन्वगात्। आविक्षितो महीपालः संवर्तमुपशिक्षितुम्॥
en: And on seeing him turn back, that prince, the son of Avikshit followed his footsteps with his hands joined together, and with a view to receive instruction from him.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: स च तं विजने दृष्ट्वा पासुंभिः कर्दमेन च। श्लेष्मणा चैव राजानं ष्ठीवनैश्च समाकिरत्॥
en: And then finding him in a lonely place, Samvarta covered the king with mud and ashes and phlegm and spittle.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: स तथा बाध्यमानो वै संवर्तेन महीपतिः। अन्वगादेव तमृषि प्राञ्जलिः सम्प्रसादयन्॥
en: And though thus worried and oppressed by Samvarta, the king followed that sage with his hands joined together in prayer and endeavouring to plcase him.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: ततो निवर्त्य संवर्तः परिश्रान्त उपाविशत्। शीतलच्छायमासाद्य न्यग्रोधं बहुशाखिनम्॥
en: At length overcome with fatigue, and reaching the cool shade of a fig tree with many branches, Samvarta desisted from his course and sat down at rest.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: संवर्त उवाच कथमस्मि त्वया ज्ञातः केन वा कथितोऽस्मि ते। एतदाचक्ष्व मे तत्त्वमिच्छसे चेन्मम प्रियम्॥
en: How nave you come to know me, and who has referred you to ine, do you tell this to me truly, if you desire me to do what is good to you.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: सत्यं ते ब्रुवतः सर्वे सम्पत्स्यन्ते मनोरथाः। मिथ्या च ब्रुवतो मूर्धा शतधा ते स्फुटिष्यति॥
en: And if you speak truly, you will gain all the objects of your hcart, and should you tell a lie, your head shall be cut into a hundred pieces.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: मरुत्त उवाच नारदेन भवान् मह्यमाख्यातो ह्यटता पथि। गुरुपुत्रौ ममेति त्वं ततो मे प्रीतिरुत्तमा॥
en: Marutta said I have been told by Narada, wandering on his way, that you are the son of our familypriest, and this (information) has bent my mind (towards you), with great satisfaction.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: संवर्त उवाच सत्यमेतद् भवानाह स मां जानाति सत्रिणम्। कथयस्व तदेतन्मे क्व न सम्प्रति नारदः॥
en: Samvarta said You have told this to me truly, he (Narada) knows me to be a performer of sacrifices, now tell me where is Narada living at present.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: मरुत्त उवाच भवन्तं कथयित्वा तु मम देवर्षिसत्तमः। ततो मामभ्यनुज्ञाय प्रविष्टो हव्यवाहनम्॥
en: Marutta said That king of celestial saints (Narada) having given me this information about you, and commended me to your care, has entered into the fire.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: व्यास उवाच श्रुत्वा तु पार्थिवस्यैतत् संवर्तः प्रमुदं गतः। एतावदहमप्येवं शक्नुयामिति सोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Vyasa said Hearing these words of the king Marutta, Samvarta was highly pleased, and he said-I too am perfectly able to do all that.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: ततो मरुत्तमुन्मत्तो वाचा निर्भर्त्सयन्निव। रुक्षया ब्राह्मणो राजन् पुनः पुनरथाब्रवीत्॥ वातप्रधानेन मया स्वचित्तवशवर्तिना। एवं विकृतरूपेण कथं याजितुमिच्छसि॥ भ्राता मम समर्थश्च वासवेन च संगतः। वर्तते याजने चैव तेन कर्माणि कारय॥
en: Then, O prince, that Brahmana, raving like a maniac, and continually scolding Marutta with rude words, again accosted him thus, I am afflicted with a brain disorder, and, I always act according to the fretful caprices of my own mind, why are you then bent upon having this sacrifice performed by a priest of such a peculiar nature; my brother is able to officiate at sacrifices, and he has gone over to Vasava (Indra), and is engaged in celebrating his sacrifices, do you therefore have your sacrifice performed by him.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: गार्हस्थ्यं चैव याज्याश्च सर्वा गृह्याश्च देवताः। पूर्वजेन ममाक्षिप्तं शरीरं वर्जितं त्विदम्॥ नाहं तेनाननुज्ञातस्त्वामाविक्षित कर्हिचित्। याजयेयं कथंचिद् वै स हि पूज्यतमो मम॥
en: My elder brother has taken away by force from me all my houschold articles and mystical gods, and sacrificing clients, and has now left to me only this physical body of mine, and, O son of Avikshit, as he deserves all respect from me, I cannot by any means officiate at you sacrifice, unless he permits me.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: स त्वं बृहस्पतिं गच्छ तमनुज्ञाप्य चाव्रज। ततोऽहं याजयिष्ये त्वां यदि यष्टुमिहेच्छसि॥
en: You must therefore go to Brihaspati first, and taking his permission you can return to me, if you have any desire to celebrate a sacrifice, and then only shall I officiate at your sacrifice.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: मरुत्त उवाच बृहस्पतिं गतः पूर्वमहं संवर्त तच्छृणु। न मां कामयते याज्यमसौ वासवकाम्यया॥
en: Marutta said Do you listen to me, O Samvarta, I did go to Brihaspati first, but wishing the patronage of Vasava, he did not wish to have me as his sacrificer.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: अमरं याज्यमासाद्य याजयिष्ये न मानुषम्। शक्रेण प्रतिषिद्धोऽहं मरुत्तं मा स्म याजयः॥ स्पर्धते हि मया विप्र सदा हि स तु पार्थिवः। एवमस्त्विति चाप्युक्तो भ्रात्रा ते बलसूदनः॥
en: He said, Having secured the priest-hood of the Immortals, I do not wish to act for the mortals, and, I have been forbidden by Shakra (Indra) to officiate at Marutta's sacrifice, as he told me that Marutta having become king, was always filled with a desire to rival him. And to this your brother agreed by saying to the destroyer of Vala (Indra), Be it so.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: स मामधिगतं प्रेम्णा याज्यत्वेन बुभूषति। देवराजं समाश्रित्य तद् विद्धि मुनिपुङ्गव॥
en: Know, O best of ascetics, that as he had succeeded in getting the protection of the King of the Celestials, I went to him with gratified heart, but he did not agree to act as my priest.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: सोऽहमिच्छामि भवता सर्वस्वेनापि याजितुम्। कामये समतिक्रान्तुं वासवं त्वत्कृतैर्गुणैः॥
en: And thus repulsed, I now wish to spend all I possess, to have this sacrifice performed by you, and to outstrip Vasava by the merit of your good offices.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: न हि मे वर्तते बुद्धिर्गन्तुं ब्रह्मन् बृहस्पतिम्। प्रत्याख्यातो हि तेनास्मि तथाऽनपकृते सति॥
en: As I have been repulsed by Brihaspati for no fault of mine, I have now no desire, O Brahmana, to go to him to scek his help in this sacrifice.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: संवर्त उवाच चिकीर्षसि यथाकामं सर्वमेतत् त्वयि ध्रुवम्। यदि सर्वानभिप्रायान् कर्ताऽसि मम पार्थिव॥ याज्यमानं मया हि त्वां बृहस्पतिपुरन्दरौ। द्विषतां समभिक्रुद्धावेतदेकं समर्थयेः॥
