en: Samvarta said I can certainly, O king, do all that you wish, if only you agree to do all that I shall ask you to do, but I apprehend that Brihaspati and Purandara (Indra) when they will learn that I am engaged in celebrating your sacrifice, will be filled with anger, and do all they can to injure you.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: स्थैर्यमत्र कथं मे स्यात् सत्त्वं निःसंशयं कुरु। कुपितस्त्वां न हीदानीं भस्म कुर्यां सबान्धवम्॥
en: Therefore, do you assure me of your steadfastness, so as to ensure my coolness and constancy as otherwise, if I am filled with anger against you, I shall reduce (destroy) you and your kindred to ashes.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: मरुत्त उवाच यावत् तपेत् सहस्रांशुस्तिष्ठेरंश्चापि पर्वताः। तावल्लोकान्न लभेयं त्यजेयं सङ्गतं यदि॥ विषयैः सङ्गत्तं चास्तु मा चापि शुभबुद्धित्वं लभेयमिह कर्हिचित्। त्यजेयं सङ्गतं यदि॥
en: Marutta said If ever I forsake you, may I never attain the blessed regions as long as the mountains shall exist, and the thousand rayed sun continue to pour heat; if I forsake you, may I never gain true wisdom, and remain for ever addicted to worldly (imaterial) works.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: संवर्त उवाच आविक्षित शुभा बुद्धिवर्ततां तव कर्मसु। याजनं हि ममाप्येव वर्तते हृदि पार्थिव॥ अभिधास्ये च ते राजन्नक्षयं द्रव्यमुत्तमम्। येन देवान् सगन्धर्वाशक्रं चाभिभविष्यसि॥
en: Samvarta said Listen, Son of Avikshit, excellent as is your inclination to perform this act, so too, O king, have I in my mind the ability to perform the sacrifice, I tell you, O king, that your good things will become imperishable, and that you shall lord it over Shakra and the Celestials with Gandharvas.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: न तु मे वर्तते बुद्धिर्धने याज्येषु वा पुनः। विप्रियं तु करिष्यामि भ्रातुश्चेन्द्रस्य चोभयोः॥
en: For myself, I have no wish to hoard riches or sacrificial presents; I shall only do what is disagrecable to both Indra and my brother.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuncd
sn: गमयिष्यामि शक्रेण समतामपि ते ध्रुवम्। प्रियं च ते करिष्यामि सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I shall certainly make you attain equality with Shakra, and I tell you truly that I shall do what is agreeable to you.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: संवर्त उवाच गिरेर्हिमवतः पृष्ठे मुजवान् नाम पर्वतः। तप्यते यत्र भगवांस्तपो नित्यमुमापतिः॥
en: Samvarta said There is a peak named Munjaban on the summits of the Himalaya mountains, where the worshipful husband of Uma (Mahadeva) is constantly practising austere penances.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: वनस्पतीनां मूलेषु शृङ्गेषु विषमेषु च। गुहासु शैलराजस्य यथाकामं यथासुखम्॥ उमासहायो भगवान् यत्र नित्यं महेश्वरः। आस्ते शूली महातेजा नानाभूतगणावृतः॥
en: There the powerful and worshipful god of great power accompanied by his wife Uma, and armed with his trident, and surrounded by wild goblins of many sorts, following his random wish or fancy, constantly lives in the shade of huge forest trees, or in the caves, or on the rugged peaks of the great mountain.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: तत्र रुद्राश्च साध्याश्च विश्वेऽथ वसवस्तथा। यमश्च वरुणश्चैव कुबेरश्च सहानुगः॥ भूतानि च पिशाचाश्च नासत्यावपि चाश्विनौ। गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव यक्षा देवर्षयस्तथा॥ आदित्या मरुतश्चैव यातुधानाश्च सर्वशः। उपासन्ते महात्मानं बहुरूपमुमापतिम्॥
en: And there the Rudras, the Saddhyas, the Vishvedevas, the Vasus, Yama, Varuna, and Kubera with all his followers, and the spirits and globins, and the two Ashvins, the Gandharvas, the Apsaras, the Yakshas, as also the celestial sages, the Sun Gods, as well as the gods presiding over the winds, and evil spirits of all sorts, adore the great lord of Uma, gifted with diverse characteristics.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: रमते भगवांस्तत्र कुबेरानुचरैः सह। विकृतैर्विकृताकारैः क्रीडद्भिः पृथिवीपते॥
en: And there, O king, the adorable god, sports with the wild and playful followers of Kubera, having weird and ghastly appearances.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: श्रिया ज्वलन् दृश्यते वै बालादित्यसमद्युतिः। न रूपं शक्यते तस्य संस्थानं वा कदाचन॥
en: Shining with its own splendour, that mountain looks resplendent as the morning sun.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: निर्देष्टुं प्राणिभिः कैश्चित् प्राकृतैर्मांसलोचनैः। नोष्णं न शिशिरं तत्र न वायुर्न च भास्करः॥
en: And no creature with his natural eyes made of flesh, can ever see its shape or figure, and neither heat nor cold prevails there, nor does the sun shine or the winds blow.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: न जरा क्षुत्पिपासे वा न मृत्युर्न भयं नृप। तस्य शैलस्य पार्श्वेषु सर्वेषु जयतां वर॥
en: And, O king, neither does senility, nor hunger, nor thirst nor death nor fear afflict any one there.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: धातवो जातरूपस्य रश्मयः सवितुर्यथा। रक्ष्यन्ते ते कुबेरस्य सहायैरुद्यतायुधैः॥
en: And, O foremost of conquerors, there exist mines of gold, resplendent as the solar rays on all sides of that mountain. And, O king, desirous of doing good to him, the attendants of Kubera protect these mines of gold from intruders, with uplifted arms.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: चिकीर्षद्भिः प्रियं राजन् कुबेरस्य महात्मनः। तस्मै भगवते कृत्वा नमः शर्वाय वेधसे॥ रुद्राय शितिकण्ठाय पुरुषाय सुवर्चसे। कपर्दिने करालाय हर्यणे वरदाय च॥ त्र्यक्ष्णे पूष्णो दन्तभिदे वामनाय शिवाय च। याम्यायाव्यक्तरूपाय सवृत्ते शङ्कराय च॥ क्षेम्याय हरिकेशाय स्थाणवे पुरुषाय च। हरिनेत्राय मुण्डाय क्रुद्धायोत्तरणाय च॥ भास्कराय सुतीर्थाय देवदेवाय रंहसे। उष्णीषिणे सुवक्त्राय सहस्राक्षाय मीढुषे॥ गिरिशाय प्रशान्ताय यतये चीरवाससे। बिल्वदण्डाय सिद्धाय सर्वदण्डधराय च॥ भृगव्याधाय महते धन्विनेऽथ भवाय च। वराय सोमवक्त्राय सिद्धमन्त्राय चक्षुषे॥ हिरण्यवाहवे राजन्नुग्राय पतये दिशाम्। लेलिहानाय गोष्ठाय सिद्धमन्त्राय वृष्णये॥ पशूनां पतये चैव भूतानां पतये नमः। वृषाय मातृभक्ताय सेनान्ये मध्यमाय च॥ सुवहस्ताय पतये धन्विने भार्गवाय च। अजाय कृष्णनेत्राय विरूपाक्षाय चैव ह॥ तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्राय तीक्ष्णाय वैश्वानरमुखाय च। महाद्युतयेऽनङ्गाय सर्वाय पतये विशाम्॥ विलोहिताय दीप्ताय दीप्ताक्षाय महौजसे। वसुरेतः सुवपुषे पृथवे कृत्तिवाससे॥ कपालमालिने चैव सुवर्णमुकुटाय च। महादेवाय कृष्णाय त्र्यम्बकायानघाय च॥ क्रोधनायानृशंसाय मृदवे बाहुशालिने। दण्डिने तप्तपसे तथैवाक्रूरकर्मणे॥ सहस्रशिरसे चैव सहस्रचरणाय च। नमः स्वधास्वरूपाय बहुरूपाय दंष्ट्रिणे॥ पिनाकिनं महादेवं महायोगिनमव्ययम्। त्रिशूलहस्तं वरदं त्र्यम्बकं भुवनेश्वरम्॥ त्रिपुरघ्नं त्रिनयनं त्रिलोकेशं महौजसम्। प्रभवं सर्वभूतानां धारणं धरणीधरम्॥ ईशानं शङ्करं सर्वे शिवं विश्वेश्वरं भवम्। उमापतिं पशुपतिं विश्वरूपं महेश्वरम्॥ विरूपाक्षं दशभुजं दिव्यगोवृषभध्वजम्। उग्र स्थाणुं शिव रौद्रं शर्वं गौरीशमीश्वरम्॥ शितिकण्ठमजं शुक्रं पृथु पृथुहरं वरम्। विश्वरूपं विरूपाक्षं बहुरूपमुमापतिम्॥ प्रणम्य शिरसा देवमनङ्गाङ्गहरं हरम्। शरण्यं शरणं याहि महादेवं चतुर्मुखम्॥
en: Come here, and appease that adorable god who is known by the name of Sarva, Bedha, Rudra, Shitikantha, Surupa, Suvarcha, Kapardi, Karala, Haryaksha, Varada, Tryaksha, Pushnodantabhid, Vamana, Shiva, Yamya, Avyaktarupa, Sadvritta, Shankara, Kshemya, Harihesha, Sthanu, Purusha, Harinetra, Munda, Krisha, Uttarana, Bhaskara, Sutirtha, Devadeva, Ranha, Ushnishi, Suvaktra, Sahasraksha, Midhvan, Girisha, Prashanta, Yata, Chiravasa, Vilvadanda, Siddha, Sarvadandadhara, Mriga, Vyadha, Mahan, Dhanesha, Bhava, Vara, Somavaktra, Siddhamantra, Chakshu. Hiranyabahu, Ugra, Dikpati, Lelihana, Goshtha, Vrishnu, Pashupati, Bhutapati, Vrisha, Matribhakta, Senani, Madhyama, Sruvahasta, Yati, Dhanvi, Bharagava, Aja, Krishnanetra, Virupaksha, Tikshnadanshtra, Tikslina, Vaishvanaramukha, Mahadyuti, Ananga, Sarva, Dikpati, Bilohita, Dipta, Diptaksha, Mahauja, Vasuretas, Suvapu, Prithu, Krittivasa, Kapalmali, Suvarnamukuta, Mahedeva, Krishna, Tryambaka, Anagha, Krodhana, Nrishansa, Mridu, Bahushali, Dandi, Taptatapa, Akrurakarma, Shasrashira, Sahasra-Charana, Svadhasva Rupa, VahuRupa, Danshtri, Pinaki, Mahadeva, MahaYogi, Avyaya, Trishulahasta, Varada, Tryambaka, Bhuvneshvara, Tripuraghna, Trinayana, Trilokesha, Mahaja, SarvabhutaPrabhava, Sarvabhuta-Drarana, Dharanidhara, Ishana Shankara, Sarva, Shiva, Vishveshvara, Bhava, Umapati, Pashupati, Vishvarupa, Mahesavara, Virupaksha, Dashabhuja, Vrishavadhvaja, Ugra, Sthanu, Shiva, Raudra, Sharva, Girisha, Ishvara, Sitikantha, Aja, Shukra, Prithu, Prithuhara, Vara, Vishvarupa, Virupaksha, Vahurupa, Umapati, Anangangahara, Hara, Sharanya, Mahadeva, Chaturmukha.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: एवं कृत्वा नमस्तस्मै महादेवाय रंहसे। महात्मने क्षितिपते तत्सुवर्णमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: There bowing to that deity, you must seck his protection. And thus, O prince, making your submission to that great Mahadeva of great energy, you will acquire that gold.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: सुवर्णमाहरिष्यन्तस्तत्र गच्छन्तु ते नराः। इत्युक्तः स वचस्तेन चक्रे कारन्धमात्मजः॥
en: And the men who go there thus, succeed in getting the gold. Thus instructed, Marutta, the son of Karandhama, did as he was advised.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: ततोऽतिमानुषं सर्वं चक्रे यज्ञस्य संविधिम्। सौवर्णानि च भाण्डानि संचक्रुस्तत्र शिल्पिनः॥
en: He made super-human arrangements for the celebration of his sacrifice. And artisans made golden Vessels for that sacrificc.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: बृहस्पतिस्तु तां श्रुत्वा मरुत्तस्य महीपतेः। समृद्धिपतिदेवेभ्य: संतापमकरोद् भृशम्॥ स तप्यमानो वैवयं कृशत्वं चागमत् परम्। भविष्यति हि मे शत्रुः संवर्तो वसुमानिति॥
en: And hearing of the prosperity of Marulta, eclipsing that of the gods, Brihaspati, too, became grcatly sorry at heart and, distressed at the thought that his rival Samvarta should become prosperous, became sick at heart, and the glow of his complexion left him, and his body became emaciated.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continued
sn: तं श्रुत्वा भृशसंतप्तं देवराजो बृहस्पतिम्। अधिगम्यामरवृतः प्रोवाचेदं वचस्तदा।॥
en: And when the king of the gods came to know that Brihaspati was much aggrieved, he went to him attended by the Immortals and spoke to him thus.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: इन्द्र उवाच कच्चित्सुखं स्वपिषि त्वं बृहस्पते कच्चिन्मनोज्ञाः परिचारकास्ते। कच्चिद्देवानां सुखकामोऽसि विप्र कच्चिद्देवास्त्वां परिपालयन्ति॥
en: Do you, O Brihaspati, sleep in peace, and do you like your servants, do you seek the welfare of the celestials, and do the celestials, O Brahmana, protect you.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: बृहस्पति उवाच सुखं शये शयने देवराज तथा मनोज्ञाः परिचारका मे। तथा देवानां सुखकामोऽस्मि नित्यं देवाश्च मां सुभृशं पालयन्ति॥
en: Brihaspati said I do sleep in peace, in my bed, O Lord of the celestials, and my servants are to iny liking, and I always seek the well being of the celestials, and they cherish me well.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: इन्द्र उवाच कुतो दुःखं मानसं देहजं वा पाण्डुर्विवर्णश्च कुतस्त्वमद्या आचक्ष्व मे ब्राह्मण यावदेतान् निहन्मि सर्वांस्तव दुःखकर्तृन्॥
en: Indra said Whence then is this pain, mental or physical, and why are you pale and changed in appearance at present, tell me, O Brahmana, who those people are, who have caused you pain, so that I may slay them all.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: बृहस्पति उवाच मरुत्तमाहुर्मघवन् यक्ष्यमाणं महायज्ञेनोत्तमदक्षिणेन। संवर्तो याजयतीति मे श्रुतं तदिच्छामि न स तं याजयेत॥
en: O Indra, I have heard that Marutta will celebrate a great sacrifice at which rich presents will be given by him (to Brahmanas) and that at his sacrifice Samvarta will act as the officiating priest, and, therefore, do I wish that he may not officiate as priest at that sacrifice.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: इन्द्र उवाच सर्वान् कामाननुयातोऽसि विप्र यस्त्वं देवानां मन्त्रवित्सुपुरोधाः। उभौ च ते जरामृत्यू व्यतीतौ किं संवर्तस्तव कर्ताऽद्य विप्र॥
en: Indra said-You, O Brahmana, has attained all the objects of your desire when you have become the excellent priest of the celestials, versed in all the sacred hymns, and have got over the influence of death and decrepitude, what can Samvarta do to you now?

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: बृहस्पति उवाच देवैः सह त्वमसुरान् प्रणुद्य जिघांससे चाप्युत सानुबन्धान्। यं यं समृद्धं पश्यसि तत्र तत्र दुःखं सपत्नेषु समृद्धिभावः॥ अतोऽस्मि देवेन्द्र विवर्णरूपः सपत्नो मे वर्धते तन्निशम्य। सर्वोपायैर्मघवन् संनियच्छ संवर्त वा पार्थिवं वा मरुत्तम्॥
en: Prosperity of al rival is always painful, and do you, therefore, with your attendant gods persecute the Asuras with their kith and kin, and slay the most prosperous among them; hence, O Lord of the gods, am I changed in appearance at the thought that my rival is prospering, therefore, O Indra, do you, by all means, restrain Samvarta and king Marutta.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: इन्द्र उवाच एहि गच्छ प्रहितो जातवेदो बृहस्पतिं परिदातुं मरुत्ते। स्तथाऽमरं चैव करिष्यतीति॥
en: Do you, O Jataveda, following my direction, go to king Maruttato present Brihaspati to him and say to him that this Brihaspati will officiate at his sacrifice and make him immortal.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: अग्नि उवाच अहं गच्छामि मघवन् दूतोऽद्य बृहस्पतिं परिदातुं मरुत्ते। वाचं सत्यां पुरुहूतस्य कर्तुं बृहस्पतेश्चापचितिं चिकीर्षुः॥
en: Agni said I shall presently, O worshipful one, go there, as your messenger, to present Brihaspati to king Marutta; and to make Indra's words true, and to show respect to Brihaspati, Agni departed.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: व्यास उवाच ततः प्रायाद् धूमकेतुर्महात्मा वनस्पतीन् वीरुधश्चाप्यमृद्नन्। कामाद्धिमान्ते परिवर्तमानः काष्ठातिगो मातरिश्वेव नर्दन्॥
en: Vyasa said Then the great Fire-God went on his errand, laying waste all the forests and trees, like the powerful wind, roaring and revolving at random at the end of the winter season.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: मरुत उवाच आश्चर्यमद्य पश्यामि रूपिणं वह्निमागतम्। आसनं सलिलं पाद्यं गां चोपानय वै मुने॥
en: Marutta said See! I find the Fire-God come in his own embodiment, this day, therefore, do you, O Muni, offer him a seat and water, and a cow and water for washing the feet.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: अग्नि उवाच आसनं सलिलं पाद्यं प्रतिनन्दामि तेऽनघ। इन्द्रेण तु समादिष्टं विद्धि मां दूतमागतम्॥
en: Agni said I accept your offerings of water, seat, and water for washing the feet, O sinless one, do you know me as the messenger of Indra, come to you as ordered by him.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: मरुत उवाच कच्चिच्छ्रीमान् देवराजः सुखी च कच्चिच्चास्मान् प्रीयते धूमकेतो। कच्चिद्देवा अस्य वशे यथावत् प्रब्रूहि त्वं मम कात्स्न्येन देव॥
en: Marutta said O Fire-God, is the glorious King of the Celestials happy, and is he pleased with us, and are the other celestials loyal to him? Do you enlighten me duly on all these matters.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: अग्नि उवाच शक्रो भृशं सुसुखी पार्थिवेन्द्र प्रीतिं चेच्छत्यजरां वै त्वया सः। देवाश्च सर्वे वशगास्तस्य राजन् संदेशं त्वं शृणु मे देवराज्ञः॥
en: Agni said O king, Shakra is perfectly happy, he is pleased with you, and wishes to make you free from decrepitude, and all the other gods are loyal to him, do you, O king, listen to the message of the King of the Celestials.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: यदर्थं मां प्राहिणोत् त्वत्सकाशं बृहस्पतिं परिदातुं मरुत्ते। अयं गुरुर्याजयतां नृप त्वां मर्यं सन्तममरं त्वां करोतु॥
en: And the object for which he has sent me to you is to present Brihaspati to Marutta; O prince, let this priest perform your sacrifice, and make you who are only a mortal, attain immortality.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: मरुत उवाच संवर्गोऽयं याजयिता द्विजो मां बृहस्पतेरञ्जलिरेष तस्य। न चैवासौ याजयित्वा महेन्द्र मर्यं सन्तं याजयन्नद्य शोभेत्॥
en: Marutta said This twice-born Brahmana Samvarta will perform your sacrifice, and I pray to Brihaspati, that he having acted as priest to Mahendra it does not appear well for him now to act as priest to mortal men.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: अग्नि उवाच ये वै लोका देवलोके महान्त सम्प्राप्स्यसे तान् देवराजप्रसादात्। नूनं स्वर्ग त्वं जयेः कीर्तियुक्तः॥
en: If this Brihaspati officiate as your priest, then you will by the blessings of the King of the Celestials attain the highest place in the celestial mansion and acquiring fame you will, forsooth, conquer the heavenly region.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: तथा लोका मानुषा ये च दिव्याः प्रजापतेश्चापि ये वै महान्तः। ते ते जिता देवराज्यं च कृत्स्नं बृहस्पतिर्याजयेच्चेन्नरेन्द्र॥
en: And, O king, if Brihaspati act as your priest you will be able to conquer all the regions inhabited by men, and the heavenly regions and all the highest regions created by Prajapati and even the entire kingdom of the celestials.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: संवर्त उवाच मा स्मैव त्वं पुनरागाः कथंचित् बृहस्पतिं परिदातुं मरुत्ते। मां त्वां धक्ष्ये चक्षुषा दारुणेन संक्रुद्धोऽहं पावक त्वं निबोध॥
en: You must never come again thus to present Brihaspati to Marutta; for know, O Pavaka, (Agni), if you do, I losing my temper, will burn you with my fierce evil eyes.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: व्यास उवाच र्दाहाद् भीतो व्यथितोऽश्वत्थपर्णवत्। तं वै दृष्ट्वा प्राह शक्रो महात्मा बृहस्पतेः संनिधौ हव्यवाहम्॥
en: Vyasa said Then fearing destruction by fire, and trembling like the leaves of the Ashvatha tree (Ficus religiosa), Agni returned to the gods, and the great Shakra seeing that carrier of oblations (Agni) in the company of Brihaspati said as follows:

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: इन्द्र उवाच यस्त्वं गतः प्रहितो जातवेदो बृहस्पतिं परिदातुं मरुत्ते। तत् किं प्राह स नृपो यक्ष्यमाण: कच्चिद् वचः प्रतिगृह्णाति तच्च॥
en: Indra said You, O Jatavada (Agni), went to present Brihaspati to Marutta according to my direction, now what did that sacrificing king say to you, and did he accept my command?

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: अग्नि उवाच न ते वाचं रोचयते मरुत्तो बृहस्पतेरञ्जलिं प्राहिणोत् सः। संवर्तो मां याजयितेत्युवाच पुनः पुनः स मया याच्यमानः॥
en: Agni said, Your message was not acceptable by Maruita and when urged by me, he clasping the hands of Brihaspati, said again and again, that Samvarta would act as his priest.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: उवाचेदं मानुषा ये च दिव्याः प्रजापतेर्ये च लोका महान्तः। तांश्चेल्लभेयं संविदं तेन कृत्वा तथापि नेच्छेयमिति प्रतीतः॥
en: And he also observed that he did not wish to attain the worldly and the heavenly regions, and all the highest regions of Prajapati, and that if he were so minded, he would accept the terms of Indra.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: इन्द्र उवाच पुनर्गत्वा पार्थिवं त्वं समेत्य वाक्यं मदीयं प्रापय स्वार्थयुक्तम्। स्त्वत्तो वज्रं सम्प्रहर्तास्मि तस्मै॥
en: Do you return to that king and meeting him, tell him these words of mine, full of meaning and if he obey them not, I shall strike him with my thunderbolt.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: अग्नि उवाच गन्धर्वराड् यात्वयं तत्र दूतो बिभेम्यहं वासव तत्र गन्तुम्। संरब्धो मामब्रवीत् तीक्ष्णरोषः संवर्तो वाक्यं चरितब्रह्मचर्यः॥ यद्यागच्छः पुनरेवं कथंचिद् बृहस्पतिं परिदातुं मरुत्ते। दहेयं त्वां चक्षुषा दारुणेन संक्रुद्ध इत्येतदवैहि शक्र॥
en: Agni said Let this king of the Gandharvas go there as your messenger, O Vasava, for I am afraid to go there myself, Know, O Shakra, that highly enraged Samvarta, addicted to ascetic practices, told me these words in anger, 'I shall burn you with my fierce evil eyes if you on any account come again here to present Brihaspati to king Marutta.'

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: शक्र उवाच त्वमेवान्यान् दहसे जातवेदो न हि त्वदन्यो विद्यते भस्मकर्ता। त्वत्संस्पर्शात् सर्वलोको बिभेति अश्रद्धेयं वदसे हव्यवाह॥
en: Shakra said Jataveda, it is you who burns all other things and there is none else who can reduce you to ashes; all the world is afraid to come in contact with you, O carrier of oblation, these words of yours are worthy of no credence.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: अग्नि उवाच दिवं राजन् पृथिवीं च सर्वा संवेष्टयेस्त्वं स्वबलेनैव शक्र। एवंविधस्येह सतस्तवासौ कथं वृत्रस्त्रिदिवं प्राग् जहा॥
en: You, O Shakra, have encompassed the dominion of the heaven and the earth and the sky by the strength of your own arms, but even thus how could Vritra (of old) wrest from you the sovereignty of the celestial regions?

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: इन्द्र उवाच न गण्डिकाकारयोगं करेऽj न चारिसोमं प्रपिवामि वह्ने। न क्षीणशक्तौ प्रहरामि वज्रं को मेऽसुखाय प्रहरेत मर्त्यः॥
en: Indra said I can reduce my enemies to submission and can even reduce the size of a mountain to an atom, if I will it. But, O Vahni, as I do not accept the libation of Soma drink if offered by an enemy, and as I do not strike the weak with my thunderbolt (Vritra got the better of me for a time) But who among mortals can live in peace by creating enmity with me.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: प्रव्राजयेयं कालकेयान् पृथिव्या मपाकर्षन् दानवानन्तरिक्षात्। दिवः प्रह्लादमवसानमानयं को मेऽसुखाय प्रहरेत मानवः॥
en: I have banished the Kalakeyas to the earth, and removed the Danavas from the celestial region, and have terminated the existence of Prahlada in heaven, can there be any man who can leave in peace by exciting my enmity.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: अग्नि उवाच यत्र शर्यातिं च्यवनो याजियिष्यन् सहाश्विभ्यां सोममगृह्णदेकः। तं त्वं क्रुद्धः प्रत्यषेधीः पुरस्ताच्छर्यातियज्ञं स्मर तं महेन्द्र।॥ वज्रं गृहीत्वा च पुरन्दर त्वं सम्प्राहार्षीश्च्यवनस्यातिघोरम्। मपागृह्णात् तपसा जातमन्युः॥
en: Agni said Do you, O Mahendra, remember that formerly when the sage Chyavana officiated at the sacrifice of Sharyati with the twin gods Ashvins, and himself appropriated the Soma offering alone, you were filled with anger, and when bent upon preventing preventing Sharyati's sacrifice, you did violently strike Chyavana with your thunderbolt, that Brahmana, O Purandara, yielding to anger, was able by the power of his devotions to seize and hold fast your hand with your thunderbolt in it.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: ततो रोषात् सर्वतो घोररूपं सपत्नं ते जनयामास भूयः। मदं नामासुरं विश्वरूपं यं त्वं दृष्ट्वा चक्षुषी संन्यमीलः॥ भीतः हनुरेका जगतीस्था तथैका दिवं गता महतो दानवस्य। सहस्रं दन्तानां शतयोजनानां सुतीक्ष्णानां घोररूपं बभूव।॥ वृत्ताः स्थूला रजतस्तम्भव दंष्ट्राश्चतस्रो द्वे शते योजनानाम्। ज्जिघांसया शूलमुद्यम्य घोरम्॥ अपश्यस्त्वं तं तदा घोररूपं सर्वे वै त्वां ददृशुर्दर्शनीयम्। यस्माद् प्राञ्जलिस्त्वं महर्षिमागच्छेथाः शरणं दानवघ्न॥
en: And in anger, he again created a terrible loO king enemy of yours, the Asura named Mada assuming all shapes, on seeing whom you did shut your eyes with fear, whose one huge jaw was placed on earth, and the other extended to the celestial regions, and who looked terrible with his thousand sharp teeth extending over a hundred Yojanas, and had four prominent ones thick a set, and shining like a pillar of silver, and extending over two hundred Yojanas. And when grinding his teeth he followed you with his terrible and uplifted pike with the object of slaying you, you on seeing that terrible monster, presented a (pitiful) sight to all the bystanders. Then, O destroyer of Danavas, overcome with fear of the monster, with your hands clasped in prayer, you did seek the protection of the great sage.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned
sn: क्षात्राद् बलाद् ब्रह्मवलं गरीयो न ब्रह्मतः किंचिदन्यद् गरीयः। सोऽहं जानन् ब्रह्मतेजो यथावन्न संवर्त जेतुमिच्छामि शक्र॥
en: The power of Brahmana,s O Shakra, is greater than that of the Kshatriyas, none are more powerful than Brahmanas and knowing duly, as I do, the power of Brahmanas I do not, O Shakra, wish to quarrel with Samvarta.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: इन्द्र उवाच एवमेतद् ब्रह्मबलं गरीयो न ब्राह्मणात् किंचिदन्यद् गरीयः। आविक्षितस्य तु बलं न मृष्ये वज्रमस्मै प्रहरिष्यामि घोरम्॥
en: The power of Brahmanas is, indeed great and there are more powerful than Brahmanas, but I can never bear patiently the insolent pride of Avikshita's son, and so shall I grind him with my thunderbolt.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: धृतराष्ट्र प्रहितो गच्छ मरुत्तं संवर्तेन संगतं तं वदस्व। बृहस्पतिं त्वमुपशिक्षस्व राजन् वज्रं वा ते प्रहरिष्यामि घोरम्॥
en: Therefore, O Dhritarashtra, according to my direction go to king Marutta, attended by Samvarta, and deliver this now to him-do you, O prince, accept Brihaspati as your spiritual preceptor, as otherwise, I shall strike you with my dreadful thunderbolt.' do you

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: व्यास उवाच ततो गत्वा धृतराष्ट्रो नरेन्द्र प्रोवाचेदं वचनं वासवस्य॥
en: Vyasa said Then Dhritarashtra went to that monarch's court and delivered this news to him from Vasava.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच गन्धर्वं मां धृतराष्ट्रं निबोध त्वामागतं वक्तुकामं नरेन्द्र। ऐन्द्रं वाक्यं शृणु मे राजसिंह यत् प्राह लोकाधिपतिर्महात्मा॥ बृहस्पतिं याजकं त्वं वृणीष्व वज्रं वा ते प्रहरिष्यामि घोरम्। वचश्चेदेतन्न करिष्यसे मे प्राहैतदेतावदचिन्त्यका॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O king, know that I am Dhritarashtra the Gandharva, come here with the object of delivering to you the message of Indra, do you, O foremost of kings, listen to the words which the great lord of all the worlds meant for you, that one of incomprehensible deeds (Indra) only said this much do you accept Brihaspati as your officiating priest for the sacrifice, or if you do not comply with my request. I shall strike you with my dreadful thunderbolt.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: मरुत उवाच त्वं चैवैतद् वेत्थ पुरंदरच विश्वेदेवा वसवश्चाश्विनौ च। मित्रद्रोहे निष्कृतिर्नास्ति लोके महत् पापं ब्रह्महत्यासमं तत्॥
en: Marutta said-You, O Purandara, the Vishvadevas, the Vasus and the Ashvins you all know, that, in this world there is no escape for the results of playing false to a friend, it is a great sin like that of Brahminicide.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: बृहस्पतिर्याजयतां महेन्द्र देवश्रेष्ठं वज्रभृतां वरिष्ठम्। संवर्तो मां याजयिताऽद्य राजन् न ते वाक्यं तस्य वा रोचयामि॥
en: Let Brihaspati (therefore) officiate as priest to that Mahendra the supreme Deva (god), the highest one holding the thunderbolt, and, O prince, Samvarta will act as my priest, as neither his (Indra's) words, nor thine commend themselves to me.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: गन्धर्व उवाच घोरो नादः श्रूयतां वासवस्य नभस्तले गर्जतो राजसिंह। व्यक्तं वज्रं मोक्ष्यते ते महेन्द्रः क्षेमं राजंश्चिन्त्यतामेष कालः॥
en: The Gandharva said Do you, O foremost of kings, listen to the terrible war-cry, of Vasava roaring in the sky, assuredly and openly will Mahendra hurl his thunderbolt at you, do you, therefore, think of your well-being, for this is the time to do it.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: व्यास उवाच इत्येवमुक्तो धृतराष्ट्रेण राजन् श्रुत्वा नादं नदतो वासवस्य। तपोनित्यं धर्मविदां वरिष्ठं संवर्तं तं ज्ञापयामास कार्यम्॥
en: Vyasa said Thus addressed by Dhritarashtra, and hearing the of Vasava, the king communicated this news to Samvarta firm in devotion and the highest of all virtuous men. roar

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: मरुत उवाच दध्वा दूरं तेन न दृश्यतेऽद्या प्रपद्येऽहं शर्म विपेन्द्र त्वत्तः प्रयच्छ तस्मादभयं विप्रमुख्य॥
en: Marutta said Indeed this rain cloud floating in the air, indicates that Indra must be near at present, therefore, O prince of Brahmanas, I seek shelter from you, do you, O best of Brahmanas remove this fear of Indra from my mind.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: अयमायाति वै वज्री दिशो विद्योतयन् दशा अमानुषेण घोरेण सदस्यास्त्रासिता हि नः॥
en: The Holder of the Thunderbolt is coming encompassing the ten directions of space with his dreadful and super-human refulgence and my assistants at this sacrificial assembly have been filled with fear.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: संवर्त उवाच भयं शक्राद् व्येतु ते राजसिंह प्रणोत्स्येऽहं भयमेतत् सुघोरम्। संस्तम्भिन्या विद्यया क्षिप्रमेव मा भैस्त्वमस्याभिभवात् प्रतीतः॥
en: O foremost of kings, your fear of Shakra will soon be removed, and I shall soon remove this terrible pain by means of my magic (incantation), be calm and have no fear of being overpowered by Indra.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: अहं संस्तम्भयिष्यामि मा भैस्त्वं शक्रतो नृप। सर्वेषामेव देवानां क्षयितान्यायुधानि मे॥
en: You have nothing to fear from the God of a Hundred Sacrifices, I shall use my staying charms, O king, and the weapons of all the gods will avail them not.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: दिशो वज्रं व्रजतां वायुरेतु वर्षं भूत्वा वर्षतां काननेषु। आपः प्लवन्त्वन्तरिक्षे वृथा च सौदामनी दृश्यते मापि भैस्त्वम्॥ वह्निर्देवस्त्रातु वा सर्वतस्ते कामान् सर्वान् वर्षतु वासवो वा। वजं तथा स्थापयतां वधाय महाघोरं प्लवमानं जलौघैः॥
en: Let the lightning flash in all the directions, and the winds entering into the clouds pour down rain in the midst of the forests, and the water deluge the heavens and the flashes of lightning that are seen will avail not, you have nothing to fcar, let Vasava pour down the rains and plat his terrific thunderbolt where he will, floating among the masses of (clouds) for your destruction, for the god Vahni (Agni) will protect you in every way, and make you attain all the objects of your desire.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: मरुत उवाच घोरः शब्दः श्रूयते वै महास्वनो वज्रस्यैष सहितो मारुतेन। न मे स्वास्थ्यं जायते चाद्य विप्र॥
en: This dreadful crash of the thunderbolt together with the roaring of the winds, seem dreadful to my ears and my heart is stricken again and again, O Brahmana, and my peace of mind is gone at present.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: संवर्त उवाच वज्रादुग्राद् व्येतु भयं तवाद्य वातो भूत्वा हन्मि नरेन्द्र वज्रम्। भयं त्यक्त्वा वरमन्यं वृणीष्व कं ते कामं मनसा साधयामि॥
en: Samvarta said O king, the fear in your mind from this terrible thunderbolt will leave you immediately. I shall remove the thunder by the help of the winds, and setting aside all fear from your mind, do you accept a boon from me according to your heart's desire, and I shall do it for you.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: मरुत्त उवाच इन्द्रः साक्षात् सहसाभ्येतु विप्र हविर्यज्ञे प्रतिगृह्णातु चैव। स्वं स्वं धिष्ण्यं चैव जुषन्तु देवा हुतं सोमं प्रतिगृह्णन्तु चैव॥
en: Marutta said-I wish, O Brahmana, that Indra all of a sudden should come bodily at this sacrifice, and accept the oblation offered to him, and that all the other celestials also come and take their appointed shares of the offerings and accepts the libations of Soma offered to them.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: संवर्त उवाच अयमिन्द्रो हरिभिरायाति राजन् देवैः सर्वैस्त्वरितैः स्तूयमानः। मन्त्राहूतो यज्ञमिमं मयाद्य पश्यस्वैनं मन्त्रविसस्तकायम्॥
en: I have, by the power of my incantations, attracted Indra bodily to this sacrifice. See, O king, Indra coming with his horses, and adored by the other celestials hastening to this sacrifice.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: अग्निरुवाच ततो देवैः सहितो देवराजो रथे युक्त्वा तान् हरीन् वाजिमुख्यान्। राविक्षितस्याप्रमेयस्य सोमम्॥
en: Then the King of the Celestials attended by the other deities and riding in his chariot drawn by the most excellent horses, approached the sacrificial altar of that son of Avikshit and drank the Soma libations of that peerless king.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: तमायान्तं सहितं देवसंघैः प्रत्युद्ययौ सपुरोधा मरुत्तः। चक्रे पूजां देवराजाय चाश्यां यथाशास्त्रं विधिवत् प्रीयमाणः॥
en: And king Marutta with his priest rose to receive Indra coming with the host of celestials and well-pleased in mind, he welcomed the King of Deities with due and foremost honours according to the Shastras.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: संवर्त उवाच स्वागतं ते पुरुहूतेह विद्वन् यज्ञोऽप्ययं संनिहिते त्वयीन्द्र। शोशुभ्यते बलवृत्रघ्न भूयः पिबस्व सोमं सुतमुद्यतं मया।॥
en: Welcome to you, O Indra, by your presence here, I learned one, this sacrifice has been made grand, O destroyer of Vala, and Vritra, do you, again, drink this Soma juice produced by me today.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: मरुत्त उवाच शिवेन मां पश्य नमश्च तेऽस्तु प्राप्तो यज्ञः सफलं जीवितं मे। अयं यज्ञं कुरुते मे सुरेन्द्र बृहस्पतेरवरजो विप्रमुख्यः॥
en: Marutta said-Do you look with kindness upon me, I bow to you, O Indra, by your presence, my sacrifice has been perfected, and my life too blessed with good results. O Surendra, this excellent Brahmana, the younger brother of Brihaspati is engaged in celebrating my sacrifices.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: इन्द्र उवाच जानामि ते गुरुमेनं तपोधनं बृहस्पतेरनुजं तिग्मतेजसम्। यस्याह्वानादागतोऽहं नरेन्द्र प्रीतिर्मेऽद्य त्वयि मन्युः प्रनष्टः॥
en: Indra said I know your priest, this highly energetic ascetic, the younger brother of Brihaspati, at whose invitation I have come to this sacrifice, I am, o king, well-pleased with you, and my anger against you is gone.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: संवर्त उवाच यदि प्रीतस्त्वमसि वै देवराज तस्मात्स्वयं शाधि यज्ञे विधानम्। स्वयं सर्वान् कुरु भागान् सुरेन्द्र जानात्वयं सर्वलोकश्च देव॥
en: If, O King of the Celestials, you are pleased with us, do you yourself give all the directions for this sacrifice, and, O Surendra, yourself ordain the sacrificial portions (for the gods), so that, O god, all the world may know that it has been done by you.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: व्यास उवाच एवमुक्तस्त्वाङ्गिरसेन शक्रः समादिदेश स्वयमेव देवान्। सभाः नियन्तामावसथाश्च मुख्याः सहस्रशश्चित्रभूताः समृद्धाः॥ क्लृप्ताः स्थूणाः कुरुतारोहणानि गन्धर्वाणामप्सरसां च शीघ्रम्। यत्र नृत्येरन्नप्सरसः समस्ताः स्वर्गोपमः क्रियतां यज्ञवाटः॥
en: Vyasa said Thus addressed by the son of Angira, Shakra himself gave directions to all the celestials to erect the hall of assembly, and a thousand well-furnished excellent rooms loO king grand as in a canvass and quickly to complete the staircase massive and durable, for the ascent of the Gandharvas and Apsaras and to furnish that portion of the sacrificial ground reserved for the dance of the Apsaras, like the palace of Indra in the celestial region.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: इत्युक्तास्ते चक्रुराशु प्रतीता दिवौकसः शक्रवाक्यान्नरेन्द्र। ततो वाक्यं प्राह राजानमिन्द्रः प्रीतो राजन् पूज्यमानो मरुत्तम्॥ एष त्वयाहमिह राजन् समेत्य ये चाप्यन्ये तव पूर्वे नरेन्द्र। सर्वाश्चान्या देवता: प्रीयमाणा हविस्तुभ्यं प्रतिगृह्णन्तु राजन्॥
en: o king, thus directed, the renowned denizens of heaven quickly carried out the directions of Shakra. And then, O king, Indra well-pleased and worshipped, thus said to king Marutta, O prince, by associating with you at this sacrifice, your ancestors who have gone before you, as well as the other celestials have been highly pleased and accepted the oblations offered by you.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: आग्नेयं वै लोहितमालभन्तां वैश्वदेवं बहुरूपं हि राजन्। नीलं चोक्षाणं मध्यमप्यालभन्तां चलच्छिश्नं सम्प्रदिष्टं द्विजायाः॥
en: And now, O king, let the foremost of twiceborn ones, offer on the sacrificial altar a red bull belonging to the Fire-God and a sacred and duly consecrated blue bull with variegated skin, belonging to the Vishvedevas.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: ततो यज्ञो ववृधे तस्य राजन् यत्र देवाः स्वयमन्नानि जहः। यस्मिशक्रो ब्राह्मणैः पूज्यमानः सदस्योऽभूद्धरिमान् देवराजः॥
en: Then, O king, the sacrificial ceremony grew in splendour, wherein the celestials themselves collected the food, and Shakra the King of the a Celestials, possessed of horse, and adored by the Brahmanas, become all assistant at the sacrifice.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: ततः संवर्तश्चैत्यगतो महात्मा यथा वह्निः प्रज्वलितो द्वितीयः। हवींष्युच्चैराह्वयन् देवसंघान् जुहावाग्नौ मन्त्रवत् सुप्रतीतः॥
en: And then the great Samvarta ascending the altar, and loO king radiant as the second embodiment of the Burning Fire, loudly addressing the celestials with satisfaction, offered oblations of clarified butter to the fire with incantation of the sacred hymns.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: ततः पीत्वा बलभित् सोममयं ये चाप्यन्ये सोमपा देवसंघाः। सर्वेऽनुज्ञाताः प्रययुः पार्थिवेन यथाजोषं तर्पिताः प्रीतिमन्तः॥
en: And then the Destroyer of Vala first drank the Soma juice, and then the assembly of other celestials who drank Soma, and then in happiness and with the king's permission they returned home well-pleased and delighted.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: ततो राजा जातरूपस्य राशीन् पदे पदे कारयामास हृष्टः। द्विजातिभ्यो विसृजन् भूरि वित्तं रराज वित्तेश इवारिहन्ता॥
en: Then that king, the destroyer of his enemies, with a delighted heart, placed heaps of gold on various spots, and distributing the immense riches to the Brahmanas, he looked glorious like Kubera the King of Riches.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: ततो वित्तं विविधं संनिधाय यथोत्साहं कारयित्वा च कोषम्। अनुज्ञातो गुरुणा संनिवृत्य शशास गामखिलां सागरान्ताम्॥
en: And with a pleased heart, the king filled his treasury with different kinds of wealth, and with the permission of his spiritual preceptor he returned (to his kingdom) and continued to rule the entire kingdom extending to the limits of the sea.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: एवंगुण: सम्बभूवेह राजा यस्य क्रतो तत् सुवर्णं प्रभूतम्। तत् त्वं समादाय नरेन्द्र वित्तं यजस्य देवांस्तर्पयानो निवापैः॥
en: So virtuous in this world was that king, at whose sacrifice such an enormous quantity of gold was collected, and now, O prince you must collect that gold and adoring the gods with due rites, do you celebrate this sacrifice.

description: The Story of Marutta and Brihaspati continuned none
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो राजा पाण्डवो हृष्टरूप: श्रुत्वा वाक्यं सत्यवत्याः सुतस्य। मनश्चक्रे तेन वित्तेन यष्टुं ततोऽमात्यैर्मन्त्रयामास भूयः॥
en: Vaishmpayana said Then the Pandava prince Yudhishthira was delighted on hearing this speech of the son of Satyavati (Vyasa), and desirous of celebrating his sacrifice with those riches, he consulted again and again with his ministers.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: इत्युक्ते नृपतौ तस्मिन् व्यासेनाद्भुतकर्मणा। वासुदेवो महातेजास्ततो वचनमाददे॥ तं नृपं दीनमनसं निहतज्ञातिबान्धवम्। उपप्लुतमिवादित्यं सधूममिव पावकम्॥ निर्विण्णमनसं पार्थं ज्ञात्वा वृष्णिकुलोद्वहः। आश्वासयन् धर्मसुतं प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: When Vyasa of wonderful deeds had concluded his speech to the king, the highly powerful son of Vasudeva (Krishna) also addressed him. Knowing the king, the son of Pritha, afflicted in mind, and bereft of his relatives and kinsmen killed in battle, and appearing crest-fallen like the sun darkened by eclipse, or fire smothered by smoke, that support of the Vrishni race (Krishna), comforting the son of Dharma, tried to address him thus.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: वासुदेव उवाच सर्व जिह्यं मृत्युपदमार्जवं ब्रह्मणः पदम्। एतावान् ज्ञानविषयः किं प्रलापः करिष्यति॥
en: Vasudeva said All crookedness of heart brings on destruction, and all rectitude leads to Brahma. This and this only in the aim and object of all true wisdom, what can mental distraction do (to him).

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: नैव ते निष्ठितं कर्म नैव ते शत्रवो जिताः। कथं शत्रु शरीरस्थमात्मनो नावबुध्यसे॥
en: Your deed has not yet been destroyed nor have your enemies been subjugated, for you do not yet know the enemies that live within your own body.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि यथाधर्मं यथाश्रुतम्। इन्द्रस्य सह वृत्रेण यथा युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: I shall (therefore) relate to you truly as I have heard it, the story of the war of Indra with Vritra as It happened.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: वृत्रेण पृथिवी व्याप्ता पुरा किल नराधिप। दृष्ट्वा स पृथिवीं व्याप्तां गन्धस्य विषये हते॥ धराहरणदुर्गन्धो विषयः समपद्यत। शतक्रतुशुकोपाथ गन्धस्य विषये हृते॥ वृत्रस्य स ततः क्रुद्धो घोरं वज्रमवासृजत्।
en: Formerly, the Earth, O king, was encompassed by Vritra, and by this abstraction of earthly matter the seat of all smeil, there arose bad odours on all sides, and the Performer of a Hundred Sacrifices (Indra), being much incensed by this deed, hurled his thunderbolt at Vritra.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: स वध्यमानो वज्रेण सुभृशं भूरितेजसा॥ तोयं जग्राह विषयं ततः।
en: And being deeply wounded by the thunderbolt of powerful Indra, Vritra entered into the (waters), and by doing so, he destroyed their property.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: अप्सु वृत्रगृहीतासु रसे च विषये हते।॥ शतक्रतुरतिक्रुद्धस्तत्र वज्रमवासृजत्।
en: The waters being seized by Vritra, their liquid property left them. At this Indra became wroth and again smote him with his thunderbolt.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: स वध्यमानो वज्रेण तस्मिन्नमिततेजसा॥ विवेश सहसा ज्योतिर्जग्राह विषयं ततः।
en: And he (Vritra) smitten by the thunderbolt by the most powerful Indra went to the luminous matter and abstracted its inherent property.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: व्याप्ते ज्योतिषि वृत्रेण रूपेऽथ विषये हृते।॥ शतक्रतुरतिक्रुद्धस्तत्र वज्रमवासृजत्। स वध्यमानो वज्रेण तस्मिन्नमिततेजा॥ विवेश सहसा वायुं जग्राह विषयं ततः।
en: The luminous matter being over whelmed by Vritra and its property, colour and form being thereby lost, the angry Indra again hurled his thunderbolt at him. And thus wounded again by Indra of great power, Vritra entered all on a sudden into the gaseous matter, and thereafter made away with its inherent property.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: व्याप्ते वायौ तु वृत्रेण स्पर्शेऽथ विषये हृते॥ शतक्रतुरतिक्रुद्धस्तत्र वज्रमवासृजत्। स वध्यमानो वज्रेण तस्मिन्नमिततेजसा।॥ आकाशमभिदुद्राव जग्राह विषयं ततः। आकाशे वृत्रभूतेऽथ शब्दे च विषये हृते॥ शतक्रतुरभिक्रुद्धस्तत्र वज्रमवासृजत्।
en: And this matter being overpowered by Vritra and its property, touch being lost. Indra became again angry and flung his thunderbolt at him. And wounded therein by the powerful (Indra), he overwhelmed the ether, and took away its inherit property, and the ether being overwhelmed by Vritra, and its property, sound, being destroyed, the God of a Hundred Sacrifices highly enraged, again sinote him with his thunderbolt.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: स वध्यमानो वज्रेण तस्मिन्नमिततेजसा॥ विवेश सहसा शक्रं जग्राह विषयं ततः।
en: And thus smitten by the powerful Indra, he suddenly entered into his (Shakra's) body, and took away its essential attributes.

description: The story of Vritra and Indra
sn: तस्य वृत्रगृहीतस्य मोहः समभवन्महान्॥ रथन्तरेण तं तात वसिष्ठः प्रत्यबोधयत्। ततो वृत्रं शरीरस्थं जघान भरतर्षभ। शतक्रतुरदृश्येन वज्रेणेतीह नः श्रुतम्॥ इदं धन॑ रहस्यं वै शक्रेणोक्तं महर्षिषु। ऋषिभिश्च मम प्रोक्तं तन्निबोध जनाधिप।॥
en: And overtaken by Vritra, he was filled with great illusion. And, O venerable sir, the most powerful of Bharata's race, we have heard that Vasishtha comforted Indra and that the God of a Hundred Sacrifices killed Vritra in his body by means of his invisible thunderbolt, and know, O prince, that this religious mystery was recited by Shakra to the great sages, and they in turn told it to me.

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: वासुदेव उवाच द्विविधे जायते व्याधिः शारीरो मानसस्तथा। परस्परं तयोर्जन्म निर्द्वन्द्वं नोपपद्यते।।।।
en: There are two kinds of diseases, physical and mental. They are produced by the mutua? action of the body and mind on cach other, and they never originate without the interaction of the two.

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: शरीरे जायते व्याधिः शारीरः स निगद्यते। मानसे जायते व्याधिर्मानसस्तु निगद्यते॥
en: The disease that is produced in the body, is called physical, and that which is produced in the mind, is called mental.

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: शीतोष्णे चैव वायुश्च गुणा राजन् शरीरजाः। तेषां गुणानां साम्यं चेत् तदाहुः स्वस्थलक्षणम्॥
en: The cold, the warin (phlegm and bile) as well as the windy humours, O king, are the essential changes created in the physical body, and when these humours are equally distributed, and are present in due proportions, they indicate good health.

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: उष्णेन बाध्यते शीतं शीतेनोष्णं च बाध्यते। सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति त्रय आत्मगुणाः स्मृताः॥ तेषां गुणानां साम्यं चेत् तदाहुः स्वस्थलक्षणम्। तेषामन्यतमोत्सेके विधानमुपदिश्यते॥
en: The warm humour is influenced by the cold. and the cold by the warm. Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance are the attributes of the soul, and it is said by the learned, that their presence in equal parts, indicates health (of the mind). But if any of the three preponderate, some remedy is laid down.

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: हर्षेण बाध्यते शोको हर्षः शोकेन बाध्यते। कश्चिद् दुःखे वर्तमानः सुखस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छति। कश्चित् सुखे वर्तमानो दुःखस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छति॥
en: Happiness is overcome by sorrow, and sorrow by pleasure. Some people while afflicted by sorrow, wish to recall (past) happiness, while others, while in the enjoyment of happiness, wish to recall past sorrow.

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: स त्वं न दुःखी दुःखस्य न सुखी सुसुखस्य च। स्मर्तुमिच्छसि कौन्तेय किमन्यद् दुःखविभ्रमात्॥ अथवा ते स्वभावोऽयं येन पार्थावकृष्यसे। दृष्ट्वा सभागतां कृष्णामेकवस्त्रां रजस्वलाम्। मिषतां पाण्डवेयानां न तस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छसि॥ प्रव्राजनं च नगरादजिनैश्च विवासनम्। महारण्यनिवासश्च न तस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छसि॥ जटासुरात् परिक्लेशश्चित्रसेनेन चाहवः। सैन्धवाच्च परिक्लेशो न तस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छसि॥
en: But you, O son of Kunti, do nether wish to recall your sorrows nor your happiness, what else do you wish to recall barring this delusion of sorrow. Or, perchance, O son of Pritha, it is your innate nature, by which you are at present overpowered. You do not wish to recall to your mind the painful spectacle of Krishna standing in the hall of assembly with only one piece of cloth to cover her body, and while she was in her menses and before all the Pandavas. And it is not proper that you should brood over your departure from the city, and your exile with the hide of the antelope for your dress, and your wanderings in the great forest, nor should you recall to your mind the affliction from Jatasura, the fight with Chitrasena, and your troubles from the Saindhavas.

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: पुनरज्ञातचर्यायां कीचकेन पदा वधः। याज्ञसेन्यास्तथा पार्थ न तस्य स्मर्तुमिच्छसि॥ यच्च ते द्रोणभीष्माभ्यां युद्धमासीदरिंदम। मनसैकेन योद्धव्यं तत् ते युद्धमुपस्थितम्॥
en: Nor it is meet, O son of Pritha, and conqueror of your foes, that you should recall the incident of Kichaka's kicking Draupadi, during the period of your exile passed in absolute concealment, nor the incidents of the fight which took place between yourself and Drona and Bhishma. The time has now arrived, when you must fight which each must do single-handed with his mind.

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: तस्मादभ्युपगन्तव्यं युद्धाय भरतर्षभ परमव्यक्तरूपस्य पारं युक्त्या स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: Therefore, O chief of Bharata's race, you must now prepare to carry the struggle against your mind, and by dint of abstraction and the merit of your own Karma, you must reach the other side of the mysterious and unintelligible (mind).

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: यत्र नैव शरैः कार्यं न भृत्यैर्न च बन्धुभिः। आत्मनैकेन योद्धव्यं तत् ते युद्धमुपस्थितम्॥
en: In this war there will be no need for any weapons nor for friends nor attendants. The battle which is to be fought alone and singlehanded has now arrived for you.

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: तस्मिन्ननिर्जिते युद्धे कामवस्थां गमिष्यसि। एतज्ज्ञात्वा तु कौन्तेय कृतकृत्यो भविष्यसि॥
en: And if defeated in this struggle, you shall find yourself in the most wretched condition, and, O son of Kunti, knowing this, and acting accordingly, shall you attain success.

description: Mental and Physical Discases as described by Krishna
sn: एतां बुद्धिं विनिश्चित्य भूतानामागतिं गतिम्। पितृपैतामहे वृत्ते शाधि राज्यं यथोचितम्॥
en: And knowing this wisdom and the destiny of all creatures, and following the conduct of your forefathers do you duly govern your kingdom.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: वासुदेव उवाच न बाह्यं द्रव्यमुत्सृज्य सिद्धिर्भवति भारत। शारीरं द्रव्यमुत्सृज्य सिद्धिर्भवति वा न वा॥
en: Vasudeva said O foremost of Bharata's race, salvation is not attained by removing the external things (like kingdom, etc.), but by giving up things which satisfy the flesh (body).

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: बाह्यद्रव्यविमुक्तस्य शारीरेषु च गृङ्ख्यतः। यो धर्मो तत् सुखं चैव द्विषतामस्तु तत् तथा॥
en: The virtue and happiness which one attains who has renounced only the external objects, but who at the same time possessed by passions and weakness of the flesh, let these be the portion of our enemies.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: व्यक्षरस्तु भवेन्मृत्युस्त्र्यक्षरं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्। ममेति च भवेन्मृत्युर्न ममेति च शाश्वतम्॥
en: The word with two letters is Mrityu (death,) and the word with three letters is Shashvata Brahman, the eternal spirit. The consciousness of ego, or the state of being addicted to worldly objects is Death, and the absence of that feeling is immortality.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: ब्रह्ममृत्यू ततो राजन्नात्मन्येव व्यवस्थितौ।। अदृश्यमानौ भूतानि योधयेतामसंशयम्॥
en: And these two, Spirit and Death, O king, have their scats in the souls of all creatures, and remaining unseen, they, forsooth, rage war with each other.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: अविनाशोऽस्य सत्त्वस्य नियतो यदि भारत। भित्त्वा शरीरं भूतानामहिंसां प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: And if, O Bharata, it be true that no creature is ever killed, then one commits no sin for the death of a creature by destroying its body.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: लब्ध्वा हि पृथ्वी कृत्स्नां सहस्थावरजङ्गमाम्। ममत्वं यस्य नैव स्यात् किं तया स करिष्यति॥
en: Or What matters the world to a man, if having acquired the sovereignty of the entire earth with its mobile and immobile creation, he does not become attached to it.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: अथवा वसतः पार्थ वने वन्येन जीवतः। ममता यस्य द्रव्येषु मृत्योरास्ये स वर्तते॥
en: But if the man who having renounced the world, has adopted the forest mode of life, living on wild roots and edibles, O son of Pritha, has a craving for the earthly things, and is addicted to them, he may be said to bear death in his mouth.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: बाह्यान्तराणां शत्रूणां स्वभाव पश्य भारत। यन्न पश्यति तद् भूतमुच्यते स महाभयात्॥
en: Do you, O Bharata, watch and observe the character of your external and internal enemies. And the man who is able to perceive the nature of the eternal reality is able to get over the influence of the great fear (perdition).

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: कामात्मानं न प्रशंसन्ति लोके नेहाकामा काचिदस्ति प्रवृत्तिः। सर्वे कामा मनसोऽङ्गप्रभूता यान् पण्डितः संहरते विचिन्त्य॥ भूयो भूयो जन्मनोऽभ्यासयोगाद् योगी योगं सारमार्ग विचिन्त्य। दानं च वेदाध्ययनं तपश्च काम्यानि कर्माणि च वैदिकानि॥ व्रतं यज्ञान् नियमान् ध्यानयोगान् कामेन यो नारभते विदित्वा। यद् यच्चायं कामयते स धर्मो न यो धर्मो नियमस्तस्य मूलम्॥
en: Men do not like the conduct of those who are engrossed in earthly desires, and there is not deed without having a desire (at its root) and all desires are, as it were, the limbs of the mind. Therefore, wise men knowing this, control their desires. The Yogi who communes with the Supreme Spirit, knows Yoga to be the perfect way to salvation by reason of the practices of his many pristine births. And remembering that, what the soul wishes, is not conducive of piety and virtuc, but that the control of the desires is at the root of all true virtue, such men do not engage in the practice of charity, Vedic learning, asceticism, Vedic rites, whose object is attainment of earthly prosperity, ceremonies, sacrifices, religious rules and meditation, with the desires of securing any advantage thereby.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: अत्र गाथा: कामगीताः कीर्तयन्ति पुराविदः। शृणु संकीर्त्यमानास्ता अखिलेन युधिष्ठिर। नाहं शक्योऽनुपायेन हन्तुं भूतेन केनचित्॥
en: As an illustration of this truth, the sages, well-read in ancient learning, recite these verses called by the name of Kamagita, do you, Yudhishthira, listen to the recital of them in full.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: यो मां प्रयतते हन्तुं ज्ञात्वा प्रहरणे बलम्। तस्य तस्मिन् प्रहरणे पुनः प्रादुर्भवाम्यहम्॥
en: (Kama says), No creature is able to destroy me without following the proper methods (viz., subjugation of all desires and practice of Yoga, etc.)

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: यो मां प्रयतते हन्तुं यज्ञैर्विविधदक्षिणैः। जङ्गमेष्विव धर्मात्मा पुनः प्रादुर्भवाम्यहम्॥ यो मां प्रयतते नित्यं वेदैर्वेदान्तसाधनैः। स्थावरेष्विव भूतात्मा तस्य प्रादुर्भवाम्यहम्॥
en: If a man knowing my power, tries to destroy me by muttering prayers, etc., I prevail over him by deluding him with the belief that I am the ego within him. If he desire to destroy me by means of sacrifices with many presents, I deceive hiin by appearing in his mind as a most virtuous creature amongst the mobile creation, and if he wish to destroy me by mastering the Vedas and its auxiliaries, I overreach him by appearing to his mind to be the soul of virtue amongst the immobile creation.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: यो मां प्रयतते हन्तुं धृत्या सत्यपराक्रमः। भावो भवामि तस्याहं स च मां नावबुध्यते॥ यो मां प्रयतते हन्तुं तपसा संशितव्रतः। ततस्तपसि तस्याथ पुनः प्रादुर्भवाम्यहम्॥ यो मां प्रयतते हन्तुं मोक्षमास्थाय पण्डितः। तस्य मोक्षरतिस्थस्य नृत्यामि च हसामि च। अवध्यः सर्वभूतानामहमेकः सनातनः॥
en: And if the man whose strength lies in truth, wish to overcome me by patience, I appear to him as is mind, and thus he does not perceive my existence, and if the man of austere religious practices, wish to destroy me by means of asceticism, I appear in the dress of asceticism in his mind, and thus he is prevented from knowing me, and the man of learning, who with the object of attaining salvation wish to destroy me, I frolic and laugh in the face of such a man intent on salvation. I am the everlasting one without an equal, whom no creature can kill or destroy.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: तस्मात्त्वमपि तं कामं यज्ञैर्विविधदक्षिणैः। धर्मे कुरु महाराज तत्र ते स भविष्यति॥
en: Therefore, you too, O prince, divert your desires (Kama) to virtue, so that, by this means, you may attain what is for your good.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: यजस्व वाजिमेधेन विधिवद् दक्षिणावता। अन्यैश्च विविधैर्यज्ञैः समृद्धराप्तदक्षिणैः॥
en: Do you, therefore, make preparations for the due performance of ihe Horse Sacrifice with presents, and various other sacrifices of great splendour, and accompanied with presents.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: मा ते व्यथास्तु निहतान् बन्धून् वीक्ष्य पुनः पुनः। न शक्यास्ते पुनर्द्रष्टुं ये हताऽस्मिन् रणाजिरे॥
en: Let not, therefore, grief overpower you again, on seeing your friends lying killed on the battle-field. You cannot see the men killed in this battle alive again.

description: The Means of Salvation as described by Krishna
sn: स त्वमिष्ट्वा महायज्ञैः समृद्धैराप्तदक्षिणैः। कीर्ति लोके परां प्राप्य गतिमय्यां गमिष्यसि॥
en: Therefore, should you perform inagnificent sacrifices with presents, so that you may attain fame in this world, and reach the perfect way in the next.

description: The exhortation of the Rishis to Yudhishthira for going to Himalayas
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं बहुविधैर्वाक्यैर्मुनिभिस्तैस्तपोधनैः। समाश्वस्यत राजर्षिर्हतबन्धुर्युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Those great ascetics consoled the royal saint Yudhishthira, bereft of his friends with these words.

description: The exhortation of the Rishis to Yudhishthira for going to Himalayas
sn: सोऽनुनीतो भगवता विष्टरश्रवसा स्वयम्। द्वैपायनेन कृष्णेन देवस्थानेन वा विभुः॥ नारदेनाथ भीमेन नकुलेन च पार्थिव। कृष्णया सहदेवेन विजयेन च धीमता॥ अन्यैश्च पुरुषव्याप्रैाह्मणैः शास्त्रदृष्टिभिः। व्यजहाच्छोक्जं दुःखं संतापं चैव मानसम्॥
en: And, O monarch, that king exhorted by the worshipful Vishtarashraba himself, and by Dvaipayana (Vyasa), Krishna, Devasthana. Narada, Bhima, Nakula, Krishna (Draupadi), Sahadeva, and the sharp-witted Vijaya, as well as by other great men, and Brahmanas versed in the scriptures, became relieved of all mental suffering and sorrow originating from the death of his dear relations.

description: The exhortation of the Rishis to Yudhishthira for going to Himalayas
sn: अर्चयामास देवांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्च युधिष्टिाः। कृत्वाथ प्रेतकार्याणि बन्धूनां स पुनर्नृपः॥
en: And that king Yudhishthira after performing the obsequial ceremonies of his departed friends, and honouring the Brahmanas and the celestials, brought the kingdom of the earth with its girdle of oceans, under his sway.

description: The exhortation of the Rishis to Yudhishthira for going to Himalayas
sn: अन्वशासच्च धर्मात्मा पृथिवीं सागराम्बराम्। प्रशान्तचेताः कौरव्यः स्वराज्यं प्राप्य केवलम्। व्यासं च नारदं चैव तांश्चान्यानब्रवीन्नृपः॥
en: And having regained his kingdom, with a tranquil mind, that prince of Kuru's race thus addressed Vyasa, Narada and the other sages who were present.

description: The exhortation of the Rishis to Yudhishthira for going to Himalayas
sn: आश्वासितोऽहं प्राग्वृद्धैर्भवद्भिर्मुनिपुङ्गवैः। न सूक्ष्ममपि मे किंचिद् व्यलीकमिह विद्यते॥
en: I have been consoled by the words of so great, ancient and aged saints as your solves, and I have now no cause left for the least sorrow.

description: The exhortation of the Rishis to Yudhishthira for going to Himalayas
sn: अर्थश्च सुमहान् प्राप्तो येन यक्ष्यामि देवताः। पुरस्कृत्याद्य भवतः समानेष्यामहे मखम्॥
en: And likewise, I have attained great riches, with which I may adore the celestials, therefore, with your help, I shall now celebrate the sacrifice.

description: The exhortation of the Rishis to Yudhishthira for going to Himalayas
sn: हिमवन्तं त्वया गुप्ता गमिष्यामः पितामह। बह्वाश्चर्यो हि देशः स श्रूयते द्विजसत्तम॥ तथा भगवता चित्रं कल्याणं बहुभाषितम्। देवर्षिणा नारदेन देवस्थानेन चैव ह॥
en: O the best of the twice-borms, we have heard that those (Himalayan) regions are full of wonders, therefore, O Brahmana saint and grandfather do you so ordain that under your protection we may safely reach the Himalaya, mountains, the performance of my sacrifice being entirely within your control, and then the worshipful celestial saint Narada and Devasthana have also addressed exquisite and well meaning words for our behoof.

description: The exhortation of the Rishis to Yudhishthira for going to Himalayas
sn: नाभागधेयः पुरुषः कश्चिदेवंविधान् गुरून्। लभते व्यसनं प्राप्य सुहृदः साधुसम्मतान्॥
en: No unlucky man in times of great sorrow and distress, has ever the good fortune to secure the services of such preceptors and friends approved of all virtuous men.

description: The exhortation of the Rishis to Yudhishthira for going to Himalayas
sn: एवमुक्तास्तु राज्ञा सर्व अभ्यनुज्ञाप्य राजानं तथोभौ कृष्णफाल्गुनौ॥१२॥ पश्यतामेव सर्वेषां तत्रैवादर्शनं ययुः। ततो धर्मसुतो राजा तत्रैवोपाविशत् प्रभुः॥
en: Thus addressed by the king, those great saints, commending the king and Krishna and Arjuna to go the Himalayan regions, then and there vanished before the assembled multitude, and the king, the royal son of Dharma, then seated himself there for some time.

description: The exhortation of the Rishis to Yudhishthira for going to Himalayas
sn: ते एव महर्षयः। एवं नातिमहान् कालः स तेषां संन्यवर्तत। कुर्वतां शौचकार्याणि भीष्मस्य निधने तदा॥ महादानानि विप्रेभ्यो ददतामौर्ध्वदेहिकम्। भीष्मकर्णपुरोगाणां कुरूणां कुरुसत्तम॥ सहितो धृतराष्ट्रेण स ददावौर्ध्वदेहिकम्। ततो दत्त्वा बहुधनं विप्रेभ्यः पाण्डवर्षभः॥ धृतराष्ट्रं पुरस्कृत्य विवेश गजसाह्वयम्। स समाश्वास्य पितरं प्रज्ञाचक्षुषमीश्वरम्। अन्वशाद् वै स धर्मात्मा पृथिवीं भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: And the Pandavas then on account of the death of Bhishma, were engaged in celebrating his funeral ceremonies. And their tine, while thus engaged, seemed too long in passing, and performing the last rites for the bodies of Bhishma, Karna and other foremost Kauravas, they gave away large presents to Brahmanas. And then the foremost descendants of Kuru, again performed with Dhritarashtra the funeral rites, and having distributed profusc riches amongst the Brahmanas, the Pandava chief with Dhritarashtra in advance, entered the city of Hastinapur, and consoling his uncle, having eyes of wisdom, that virtuous prince continued to govern the earth with his brothers.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: जनमेजय उवाच विजिते पाण्डवेयैस्तु प्रशान्ते च द्विजोत्तम। राष्ट्रे किं चक्रतुर्वीरौ वासुदेवधनंजयौ॥
en: O best of the twice-borns, when the Pandavas had reconquered and pacified their kingdom, what did the two warriors Vasudeva and Dhananjaya do?

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विजिते पाण्डवै राजन् प्रशान्ते च विशाम्पते। राष्ट्र बभूवतुर्हष्टौ वासुदेवधनंजयौ॥ विजह्राते मुदा युक्तौ दिवि देवेश्वराविव। तौ वनेषु विचित्रेषु पर्वतेषु ससानुपु॥ तीर्थेषु चैव पुण्येषु पल्वलेषु नदीषु च। चक्रम्यमाणौ संहृष्टावश्विनाविव नन्दने॥
en: Vaishmpayana said. O king, Vasudeva and Dhananjaya were highly pleased when the Pandavas had succeeded in regaining and pacifying their kingdoms, and they deported themselves with great glcc, like Indra and his wife in the celestial regions, and amidst picturesque forest scenarios, and tablelands of mountains, and sacred places of pilgrimage, and lakes and rivers, they travelled with great pleasure like the two Ashvins in the Nandana garden of Indra.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: इन्द्रप्रस्थे महात्मानौ रेमतुः कृष्णपाण्डवौ। प्रविश्य तां सभां रम्यां विजह्राते च भारत॥
en: And, O Bharata, the great Krishna and the son of Pandu (Dhananjaya) entering the beautiful hall of assembly at Indraprastha, passed their time in great merriment.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: तत्र युद्धकथाश्चित्राः परिक्लेशांश्च पार्थिव। कथायोगे कथायोगे कथयामासतुः सदा॥
en: And there, O prince, they passed their time in describing the stirring incidents of the war, and the sufferings of their past lives.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: ऋषीणां देवतानां च वंशांस्तावाहतुः सदा। प्रीयमाणौ महात्मानौ पुराणावृषिसत्तमौ॥
en: And those two great ancient sages, pleased, recited the genealogy of the races of saints and gods.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: मधुरास्तु कथाचित्राश्चित्रार्थपदनिश्चयाः। निश्चप्रज्ञः स पार्थाय कथयामास केशवः॥
en: Then Keshava, knowing thc full significance of all matters, addressed Partha in sweet and beautiful words of excellent style and meaning.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तं ज्ञातीनां च सहस्रशः। कथाभिः शमयामास पार्थं शौरिर्जनार्दन॥
en: And then Janardana consoled the son of Pritha afflicted by the death of his sons, and thousands of other relatives.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: स तमाश्वास्य विधिवद् विज्ञानज्ञो महातपाः। अपहृत्यात्मनो भारं विशश्रामेव सात्वतः॥
en: And he of great ascetic merit and knowing the science of all things duly comforting him, rested for a while, as if a great burden had been removed from his own body.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: तत: कथान्ते गोविन्दो गुडाकेशमुवाच ह। सान्त्वयश्लक्ष्णया वाचा हेतुयुक्तमिदं वचः॥
en: Then Govinda (Krishna) comforting Arjuna with sweet speech, addressed these well reasoned words to himn.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: वासुदेव उवाच विजितेयं धरा कृत्स्रा सव्यसाचिन् परंतप। त्वद्वाहुबलमाश्रित्य राज्ञा धर्मसुतेन ह॥
en: Vasudeva said O Arjuna, the terror of your enemies, this cntire earth has been conquered by the king, the son of Dharma, depending on the power of your arms.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: असपत्नां महीं भुङ्क्ते धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनानुभावेन यमयोश्च नरोत्तम॥
en: And, O best of men, the virtuous king Yudhishthira now enjoys the sovereignty of the earth without a rival, by the power of Bhimasena and the twin brothers.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: धर्मेण राज्ञा धर्मज्ञ प्राप्तं राज्यमकण्टकम्। धर्मेण निहत: संख्ये स च राजा सुयोधनः॥ अधर्मरुचयो लुब्धाः सदा चाप्रियवादिनः। धार्तराष्ट्रा दुरात्मानः सानुबन्धा निपातिताः :॥ प्रशान्तामखिलां पार्थ प्रथिवीं पृथिवीपतिः। भुङ्क्ते धर्मसुतो राजा त्वया गुप्तः कुरुद्वह॥ रमे चाहं त्वया सार्धमरण्येष्वपि पाण्डव।
en: Oyou, who know what virtue is, it was by virtue alone, that the king has been able to regain his kingdom shorn of all enemies, and it was by the action of virtue, that king Suyodhana has been slain in battle, and, O son of Pritha and pillar of the Kuru race, the wicked sons sons of Dhritarashtra, avaricious, always rude in speech, and bent upon a sinful course of conduct, having been rooted out with their followers, the king, the son of Dharma and lord of the earth, now peaceably enjoys the cntire kingdom of the earth with your help, and I too, O son of Pandu, have been pleasantly passing away my time in your company, amidst woodland scenes.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: किमु यत्र जनोऽयं वै पृथा चामित्रकर्षण॥ यत्र धर्मसुतो राजा यत्र भीमो महाबलः। यत्र माद्रवतीपुत्रौ रतिस्तत्र परा मम॥
en: O terror of your enemies, what more need I tell you, but that where you and Pritha, and the king, the son of Dharma, and the powerful Bhimasena and the two sons of Madri are, there am I drawn with exquisite delight.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: तथैव स्वर्गकल्पेषु सभोद्देशेषु कौरव। रमणीयेषु पुण्येषु सहितस्य त्वयानघ॥ कालो महांस्त्वतीतो मे शूरसृनुमपश्यतः। बलदेवं च कौरव्य तथान्यान् वृष्णि पुगवान्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, in these delightful and sacred and celestial halls of assembly, a long time has gone away in your company without my seeing Vasudeva, Baladeva and other leaders of the Vrishni race.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: साऽहं गन्तुमभीप्सामि पुरीं द्वारावती प्रति। रोचतां गमनं मह्यं तवापि पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: And now I am desirous of going to the city of Dvaravati. Do you, therefore, O most courageous of me, assent to my departure.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: उक्तो बहुविधं राजा तत्र तत्र युधिष्ठिरः। सह भीष्मेण यद् युक्तमस्माभिः शोककारिते॥ शिष्टो युधिष्ठिरोऽस्माभिः शास्ता सन्नपि पाण्डवः। तेन तत् तु वचः सम्यग् गृहीतं सुमहात्मना॥
en: When king Yudhishthira was stricken heavily with sorrow, I with Bhishma, have recited to him many appropriate legends suited to the occasion with a view of dispelling his gricf, and the pliant and great Yudhishthira, though our sovereign, and versed in all learning, paid due heed to our words.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: धर्मपुत्रे हि धर्मज्ञे कृतज्ञे सत्यवादिनि। सत्यं धर्मो मतीश्चाग्र्या स्थितिश्च सततं स्थिरा॥
en: That son of Dharma honours truth, and is grateful and virtuous, therefore will his virtue, and good sense and the stability of his power always endure.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: तत्र गत्वा महात्मानं यदि ते रोचतेऽर्जुन। अस्मद्गमनसंयुक्तं वचो ब्रूहि जनाधिपम्॥
en: And now, O Arjuna, if it pleases you, do you go to that great prince and tell him of my desire to leave this place.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: न हि तस्याप्रियं कुर्यां प्राणत्यागेऽप्युपस्थिते। कुतो गन्तुं महाबाहो पुरी द्वारावतीं प्रति॥ सर्वं त्विदमहं पार्थ त्वत्प्रीतिहितकाम्पया। ब्रवीमि सत्यं कौरव्य न मिथ्यैतत् कथंचन॥ प्रयोजनं च निर्वृत्तमिह वासे ममार्जुन। धार्तराष्ट्रो हतो राजा सबल: सपदानुगः॥ पृथिवी च वशे तात धर्मपुत्रस्य धीमतः। स्थिता समुद्रवलया सशैलवनकानना॥ चिता रत्नैर्बहुविधैः कुरुराजस्य पाण्डव। धर्मेण राजा धर्मज्ञः पातु सर्वां वसुन्धराम्॥ उपास्यमानो बहुभिः सिद्धैश्चापि महात्मभिः। स्तूयमानश्च सततं वन्दिभिर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: For, O you of mighty arms, even if death comes to ine, I am reluctant to do anything that may displease him, what to speak of my going to the city of Dvaravati, O son of Pritha, and descendant of Kuru, I now tell you truly desiring to do only what is good and agreeable to you, and there can be nothing equivocal in it many way, that the necessity for my staying here no longer exists, when, O Arjuna, that monarch the son of Dhritarashtra, has been killed with his armies and attendants, and the earth, my friend, with its belt of seas, and its mountains and woods and forest, and the kingdom of the Kuru king filled with various gems, have passed under the control of that wise son of Dharma. And, O foremost prince of Bharata's race, may that virtuous prince govern the entire kingdom of the earth in virtue, and with the respect and approbation of numerous grcat Siddhas, and having his praises always extolled by the panegyrists.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: तं मया सह गत्वाद्य राजानं कुरु वर्धनम्। आपृच्छ कुरुशार्दूल गपनं द्वारका प्रति॥
en: Do you, O pride of Kuru's race, accompany me today to the king, the great advancer of the Kuru race, and sound him of my intended return to Dwraka.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: इदं शरीरं वसु यच्च मे गृहे निवेदितं पार्थ सदा युधिष्ठिरे। प्रियश्च मान्यश्च हि मे युधिष्ठिरः सदा कुरुणामधिपो महामतिः॥
en: As Yudhishthira the great king of the Kurus, always commands my love and respect, I have, O son of Pritha, placed this my body and all the riches that I have in my house, at his disposal.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: प्रयोजनं चापि निवासकारणे। न विद्यते मे त्वदृते नृपात्मज। स्थिता हि पृथ्वी तव पार्थ शासने गुरोः सुवृत्तस्य युधिष्ठिरस्य च॥
en: And, O prince, Partha (son of Pritha) when this earth has come under your control and that of the worshipful Yudhishthira of excellent character, there no longer remains any need for my staying here except for my love for you.

description: Krishna's desire of going to Dwarka
sn: इतीदमुक्तः स तदा महात्मना जनार्दनेनामितविक्रमोऽर्जुनः। जनार्दनं सम्प्रतिपूज्य पार्थिव॥
en: And, O king, when the redoubtable Arjuna had been thus addressed by the noble-hearted Janardana, he, showing all the honours due to him, sorrowfully replied by merely saying 'be it so'.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच सभायां वसतोस्तत्र निहत्यारीन् महात्मनोः। केशवार्जुनयोः का नु कथा समभवद् द्विज॥
en: Janamejaya said When the great Keshava and Arjuna after killing their enemies went to the assembly rooms what conversation, O twice-born one, took place between them?

sn: कृष्णेन सहितः पार्थ:स्वं राज्यं प्राप्य केवलम्। तस्यां सभायां दिव्यायां विजहार मुदा युतः॥
en: The son of Pritha (Arjuna), having recovered his own kingdom, spent his time gladly, without doing anything clse, in the company of Krishna, his heart filled with joy, in that palace of celestial beauty.

sn: तत्र कंचित् सभोद्देशं स्वर्णोद्देशसमं नृप। यदृच्छया तौ मुदितौ जग्मतुः स्वजनावृतौ॥
en: One day, those two listlessly went to a particular part of the palace that looked, O king, like a veritable portion of the celestial region. Themselves filled with joy, they were then surrounded by their relatives and attendants.

sn: ततः प्रतीतः कृष्णेन सहितः पाण्डवोऽर्जुनः। निरीक्ष्य तां सभां रम्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ विदितं मे महाबाहो संग्रामे समुपस्थिते। माहात्म्यं देवकीमातस्तच ते रूपमैश्वरम्॥
en: Pandu's son Arjuna, filled with joy in the company of Krishna, saw that delightful palace, and then addressed his companion, saying, 'O mighty-armed one, your greatness became known to me upon the approach of the battle. O son of Devaki, your form also, as the Lord of the universe, then became known to me.

sn: यत् तद् भगवता प्रोक्तं पुरा केशव सौहृदात्। तत् सर्वं पुरुषव्याघ्र नष्टं मे भ्रष्टचेतसः॥
en: What your holy self said to me at that time, O Keshava, through love, has all been forgotten by me, O chief of men, on account of the fickleness of my mind.

sn: मम कौतूहलं त्वस्ति तेष्वर्थेषु पुनः पुनः। भवांस्तु द्वारकां गन्ता नचिरादिव माधव॥
en: However, I have been curious again and again on the subject of those truths. You, too, O Madhava, will go to Dwraka soon.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु तं कृष्ण: फाल्गुनं प्रत्यभाषत। परिष्वज्य महातेजा वचनं वदतां वरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Thus addressed by him, Krishna of great energy, that foremost of speakers, embraced Phalguna and replied to him as follows.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच श्रावितस्त्वं मया गुह्यं ज्ञापितश्च सनातनम्। धर्मं स्वरूपिणं पार्थ सर्वलोकांश्च शाश्वतान्॥
en: Vasudeva said I made you listen to truths that are considered as mysteries. I conferred on you eternal truths. Indeed, I described to you Religion in its true form and on all the eternal regions.

sn: अबुद्ध्या नाग्रहीर्यस्त्वं तन्मे सुमहदप्रियम्। न च साद्य पुनर्भूयः स्मृति सम्भविष्यति॥
en: It is greatly disagreeable to me to learn that you did not, from folly, receive what I gave. The recollection of all that I told you on that occasion will not come to me now.

sn: नूनमश्रद्दधानोऽसि दुर्मेधा ह्यसि पाण्डव। न च शक्यं पुनर्वक्तुमशेषेण धनंजय॥
en: Forsooth, O son of Pandu, you are destitute of faith and your unde tanding is not good. It is impossible for me, U Dhananjaya, to repeat, in full, all that I said on that occasion.

sn: स हि धर्मः सुपर्याप्तो ब्रह्मणः पदवेदने। न शक्यं तन्मया भूयस्तथा वक्तुमशेषतः॥
en: That religion is more than sufficient for understanding Brahma. I cannot describe it again in detail.

sn: परं हि ब्रह्म कथितं योगयुक्तेन तन्मया। इतिहासं तु वक्ष्यामि तस्मिन्नर्थे पुरातनम्॥
en: I described to you, O Supreme Brahina having concentrated myself in Yoga. I shall now, however, recite to you an old history upon the same subject.

sn: यथा तां बुद्धिमास्थाय गतिमय्यां गमिष्यसि। शृणु धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ गदितं सर्वमेव मे॥
en: O foremost of all persons knowing duty, listen to everything I now say, so that, with an understanding adapted to my teaching, you may succeed in attaining to the highest end.

sn: आगच्छद् ब्राह्मणः कश्चित् स्वर्गलोकादरिंदम ब्रह्मलोकाच्च दुर्धर्षः सोऽस्माभिः पूजितोऽभवत्।।१५
en: O chastiser of enemies, on one occasion, a Brahmana came to us from the celestial regions. Of irresistible energy, he came from the regions of the grandfather. He was duly respected by us.

sn: अस्माभिः परिपृष्टश्च यदाह भरतर्षभ। दिव्येन विधिना पार्थ नच्छृणुष्वाविचारयन्॥
en: Listen, O son of Pritha, unhesitatingly to what he, O chief of Bharata's race, said, in answer to our enquiries, according to heavenly forms.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच मोक्षधर्मं समाश्रित्य कृष्ण यन्मामपृच्छथाः। भूतानामनुकम्पार्थं यत्मोहच्छेदनं विभो॥ तत् नेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावन्मधुसूदन। शृणुष्वावहितो भूत्वा गदतो मम माधव॥
en: Brahmana said That which you ask me, O Krishna, about the religion of Moksha (Emancipation), led by your compassion for all creatures, that, indeed, which destroys all delusion, O you gifted with Supreme power, I shall now tell you duly, O destroyer of Madhu. Do you listen with rapt attention as I discourse to you, O Madhava.

sn: कश्चिद् विप्रस्तपोयुक्तः काश्यपो धर्मवित्तमः। आससाद द्विजं कंचिद् धर्माणामागतागमम्॥
en: A Brahmana named Kashyapa, possessed of penances and the foremost of all persons knowing duties, came to a certain other Brahmana who had become conversant with all the mysteries of religion.

sn: गतागते सुबहुशो ज्ञानविज्ञानपारगम्। लोकतत्त्वार्थकुशलं ज्ञातार्थं सुखदुःखयोः॥
en: Indeed, the latter had mastered all the knowledge which the scriptures teach about the departure and reappearance of beings and possessed that direct knowledge of all things which Yoga gives. He was well-skilled in the truths of all subjects relating to the world. He has mastered the truth about pleasure and pain.

sn: जातीमरणतत्त्वज्ञं कोविदं पापपुण्ययौः। द्रष्टारमुच्चनीचानां कर्मभिर्देहिनां गतिम्॥
en: He knew the truth about birth and death, and understood the distinctions between merit and demerit. He had seen the ends attained to by embodied creatures high and low on account of their deeds.

sn: चरन्तं मुक्तवत्सिद्धं प्रशान्तं संयतेन्द्रियम्। दीप्यमानं श्रिया ब्राह्मया क्रममाणं च सर्वशः॥ अन्तर्धानगतिज्ञं च श्रुत्वा तत्त्वेन काश्यपः। तथैवान्तर्हितैः सिद्धैर्यान्तं चक्रधरैः सह॥ सम्भाषमाणमेकान्ते समासीनं च तैः सह। यदृच्छया च गच्छन्तमसक्तं पवनं यथा॥
en: He lived like one freed from the world. Crowned with ascetic success and gifted with perfect tranquillity of soul, he had all his senses under complete control. He seemed to shine with the resplendence of Brahma and capable of going everywhere at will. He knew the science of disappearing at will from before the eyes of all. He used to move about in the company of invisible Siddhas and celestial musicians. He used to sit and talk with them on some spot retired from the bustle of humanity. He was as unattached to all things as the wind Kashyapa having heard of him truly, wished to see him. Gifted with intelligence, that foremost of all Brahmanas approached the sage.

sn: तं समासाद्य मेधावी स तदा द्विजसत्तमः। चरणौ धर्मकामोऽस्य तपस्वी सुसमाहितः। प्रतिपेदे यथान्यायं दृष्ट्वा तन्महदद्भुतम्॥
en: Himself possessed of penances, Kashyapa, moved by the wish of acquiring merit, fell, with a rapt heart, at the feet of the sage when he had seen all those wonderful attributes.

sn: विस्मितश्चाद्भुतं दृष्ट्वा काश्यपस्तद् द्विजोत्तमम्। परिचारेण महत्ता गुरुं तं पर्यतोषयत्॥
en: Stricken with wonder at the sight of those extraordinary qualities, Kashyapa began to wait upon that foremost of all Brahmanas, with the dutiful respect of a disciple waiting upon his preceptor and succeeded in pleasing him.

sn: उपपन्नं च तत्सर्वं श्रुतचारित्रसंयुतम्। भावेनातोषयच्चैनं गुरुवृत्त्या परंतपः॥
en: By his devotion, O scorcher of enemies, rendering to him the obedience due from a disciplc to a preceptor, Kashyapa pleased that Brahmana who possessed all these qualities and was gifted besides with scriptural learning and excellent conduct.

sn: तस्मै तुष्टः स शिष्याय प्रसन्नो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। सिद्धिं परामभिप्रेक्ष्य शृणु मत्तो जनार्दन॥
en: Pleased with Kashyapa, the Brahmana one day addressed him cheerfully and spoke as follows, having the highest success in view. Listen to those words, O Janardana, as I repeat them.

sn: सिद्ध उवाच विविधैः कर्मभिस्तात पुण्ययोगैश्च केवलैः। गच्छन्तीह गतिं मर्त्या देवलोके च संस्थितिम्॥
