en: By various deeds, O son as also by the help of merit, mortal, creatures attain to diverse ends here and residence in Heaven.

sn: न क्वचित् सुखमत्यन्तं न क्वचिच्छाश्वती स्थितिः। स्थानाच्च महतो भ्रंशो दुःखलब्धात् पुनः पुनः॥
en: Nowhere one can enjoy the highest happiness; nowhere one can live for good. There are repeated falls from the highest regions acquired with such sorrow.

sn: अशुभा गतयः प्राप्ताः कष्टा मे पापसेवनात्। काममन्युपरीतेन तृष्णया मोहितेन च॥
en: On account of my indulgence in sin. I had to come by various miserable and inauspicious ends, filled as I was with lust and anger, and deluded by cupidity.

sn: पुनः पुनश्च मरणं जन्म चैव पुनः पुनः। आहारा विविधा भुक्ताः पीता नानाविधाः स्तनाः।।३२
en: I have repeatedly undergone death and rebirth. I have eaten various kinds of food, I have sucked at various breasts.

sn: मातरो विविधा दृष्टाः पितरश्च पृथग्विधाः। सुखानि च विचित्राणि दुःखानि च मयानघ।॥
en: I have seen various kinds of mothers, and various fathers dissimilar to one another. I have come by various kinds of happiness and misery, O sinless one.

sn: प्रियैर्विवासो बहुशः संवासश्चाप्रियैः सह। धननाशश्च सम्प्राप्तो लध्वा दुःखेन तद् धनम्॥
en: On various occasions have I been separated from what was agrecable and united with what was disagreeable. Having acquired wealth with great labour I have had to put up with its loss.

sn: अवमानाः सुकष्टाश्च राजतः स्वजनात् तथा। शारीरा मानसा वापि वेदना भृशदारुणाः॥
en: I have received from king and relatives insults and excessive misery. I have suffered from serve mental and physical pain.

sn: प्राप्ता विमाननाशोग्रा वधवन्धाश्च दारुणाः। पतनं निरये चैव यातनाश्च यमक्षये॥
en: I have undergone humiliations and death and imprisonment under circumstances of great severity. I have had falls into Hell and have suffered great lortures in the domains of Yama.

sn: जरा रोगाश्च सततं व्यसनानि च भूरिशः। लोकेऽस्मिन्ननुभूतानि द्वन्द्वजानि भृशं मया॥
en: I have, again and again, suffered from decrepitude and diseases, and from frequent and great calamities. In this world I have repeatedly suffered from all those afflictions which arise from a perception of all pairs of opposites.

sn: ततः कदाचिन्निर्वेदान्निराकाराश्रितेन य। लोकतन्त्रं परित्यक्तं दुःखार्तेन भृशं मया॥
en: After all this one day, laden with sorrow, despair came upon me. I took refuge in the Formless. Suffering from great distress, I gave up the world with all its joys and sorrows.

sn: लोकेऽस्मिन्ननुभूयाहमिमं मार्गमनुष्ठितः। ततः सिद्धिरियं प्राप्ता प्रसादादात्मनो मया।॥
en: Finding out then this path. I exercised myself in it in this world. Afterwards, through tranquillity of soul, I acquired the success you see.

sn: नाहं पुनरिहागन्ता लोकानालोकयाम्यहम्। आसिद्धेराप्रजासर्गादात्मनोऽपि गताः शुभाः॥
en: I shall not have to come to this world again. Indeed, till I attain to absorption into eternal Brahma, till, in fact, the final dissolution of the universe, I shall look on those happy ends that will be mine and on those beings and that form this universe.

sn: उपलब्धा द्विजश्रेष्ठ तथेयं सिद्धिरुत्तमाः इतः परं गमिष्यामि ततः परतरं पुनः॥
en: Having acquired this excellent success, I shall, after departing from this world, proceed to what is above it and thence to what is higher.

sn: ब्रह्मणः पदमव्यक्तं मा तेऽभूदत्र संशयः। नाहं पुनरिहागन्ता मर्त्यलोकं परंतप॥
en: Indeed, I shall come by the condition, which is unmanifest, of Brahma. Do not doubt this. O scorcher of enemies. I shall not return to this world of mortal creatures.

sn: प्रीतोऽस्मि ते महाप्राज्ञ ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते। यदीप्सुरुपपन्नस्त्वं तस्य कालोऽयमागतः॥
en: O you of great wisdom. I have become pleased with you. Tell me what I shall do for you. The time has come for the accomplishment of that purpose for which you have come here..

sn: अभिजाने च तदहं यदर्थं मामुपागतः। अचिरात् तु गमिष्यामि तेनाहं त्वामचूचुदम्॥
en: I know that object for which you have sought me. I shall soon depart from this world. Hence it is that I have given you this hint.

sn: भृशं प्रीतोऽस्मि भवतश्चारित्रेण विचक्षण। परिपृच्छस्व कुशलं भाषेयं यत् तवेप्सितम्॥
en: O you of great wisdom and experience, I have been highly pleased with you for your behaviour. Do you question me! I shall discourse on what is beneficial to you as desired by you.

sn: बहु मन्ये च ते बुद्धिं भृशं सम्पूजयामि च। येनाहं भवता बुद्धो मेधावी ह्यसि काश्यप॥
en: I think your intelligence is great, Indeed I speak highly of it, for it was with the help of that intelligence that you were able to recognise me. Surely, O Kashyapa, you are endued with great intelligence.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: वासुदेव उवाच ततस्तस्योपसंगृह्य पादौ प्रश्नान् सुदुर्वचान्। पप्रच्छ तांश्च धर्मान् स प्राह धर्मभृतां वरः॥
en: Touching the feet of that sage Brahmana asked him some very difficult questions. That foremost of all pious persons then described those duties that were referred to.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: कश्यप उवाच कथं शरीरं च्यवते कथं चैवोपपद्यते। कथं कष्टाच्च संसारात् संसरन् परिमुच्यते॥
en: Kashyapa said How does the body dissolve away, and how is another is acquired? How does one become liberated after passing through a repeated round of painful re-births?

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: आत्मा च प्रकृति मुक्त्वा तच्छरीरं विमुञ्चति। शरीरतश्च निर्मुक्तः कथमन्यत् प्रपद्यते॥
en: Enjoying Nature for sometime, how does the individual Soul cast off the particular body? How does the Individual Soul, freed from the body, attain to what is different from it, (viz., Brahman)?

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: कथं शुभाशुभे चायं कर्मणी स्वकृते नरः। उपभुङ्क्ते क्व वा कर्म विदेहस्यावतिष्ठते॥
en: How does a human being enjoy the good and bad deeds done by him? Where do the acts exist of one that is devoid of body?

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच एवं संचोदितः सिद्धः प्रश्नांस्तान् प्रत्यभाषत। आनुपूर्येण वार्ष्णेय तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: The Brahmana said Thus urged by Kashyapa, the Liberated Sage answered those questions one after another. Do you listen to me, O hero of the Vrishni race, as I recite to you the answers he gave.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: सिद्ध उवाच आयुः कीर्तिकराणीह यानि कृत्यानि सेवते। शरीरग्रहणे यस्मिंस्तेषु क्षीणेषु सर्वशः॥ आयुःक्षयपरीतात्मा विपरीतानि सेवते। बुद्धिावर्तते चास्य विनाशे प्रत्युपस्थिते॥
en: The Liberated Sage said, Upon the exhaustion of those deeds capable of prolonging life and bringing on fame which are done in a particular body that the Individual Soul assumes, the embodied Jiva, with the span of his life shortened, begins to do acts hostile to life and hcalth. On the approach of destruction, his understanding deviates from the proper course.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: सत्त्वं बलं च कालं च विदित्वा चात्मनस्तथा। अतिवेलमुपाश्नाति स्वविरुद्धान्यनात्मवान्॥
en: The man of inipure soul, after even a correct understanding of his constitution and strength and of the season of both his own life and of the year, begins to eat at irregular intervals and to eat such food as is hostile to him.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: यदायमतिकष्टानि सर्वाण्युपनिषेवते। अत्यथैमपि वा भुङ्क्ते न वा भुक्तो कदाचन॥
en: At such a time he does practices that are greatly harmful. He sometimes eats excessively and sometimes abstains altogether from food.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: दुष्टान्नामिषपानं च यदन्योन्यविरोधि च। गुरु चाप्यमितं भुङ्क्तं नातिजीर्णेऽपि वा पुनः॥
en: He eats bad food or bad meat or takes bad drinks, or food that has been made up of hostile ingredients. He eats food that is heavy and more than what is beneficial, or before the food previously taken, has been digested.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: व्यायाममतिमात्रं च व्यवायं चोपसेवते। सततं कर्मलाभाद् वा प्राप्तं वेगं विधारयेत्॥
en: He indulges in physical exercise and sexual pleasure in excess, or through avidity for work, suppresses the urgings of his corporeal organism even when they become pronounced.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: रसाभियुक्तमन्नं वा दिवा स्वप्नं च सेवते। अपक्वानागते काले स्वयं दोषान् प्रकोपयेत्॥
en: Or, he taken juicy food or indulges in sleep during daytime. Food that is not properly digested, of itself excites the faults, when the times comes.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: स्वदोषकोपनाद् रोगं लभते मरणान्तिकम्। अपि वोद्वन्धनादीनि परीतानि व्यवस्थति॥
en: From such excitement of the faults in his body, he gets disease ultimately bringing on death. Sometimes the person engages in unnatural deeds like strangling.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: तस्य तैः कारणैर्जन्तोः शरीरं च्यवते तदा। जीवितं प्रोच्यमानं तदृ यथावदुपधारय॥
en: Through these causes the living body of the creature dissolves away. Understand correctly the manner as I declare it to you.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: ऊष्मा प्रकुपितः काये तीव्रवायुसमीरितः। शरीरमनुपर्येत्य सर्वान् प्राणान् रुणद्धि वै॥
en: Urged on by the Wind which becomes violent, the heat in the body, becoming excited, and reaching every part of the body one after another, restrains all the vital airs.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: अत्यर्थं बलवानूष्मा शरीरे परिकोपितः। भिनत्ति जीवस्थानानि मर्माणि विद्धि तत्त्वतः॥
en: Know truly that excited all over the body, the heat becomes very strong, and pierces every vital part where life may be said to live.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: ततः सवेदनः सद्यो जीवः प्रच्यवते क्षरात्। शरीरं त्यजते जन्तुश्छिद्यमानेषु मर्मसु॥ वेदनाभिः परीतात्मा तद् विद्धि द्विजसत्तम। जातीमरणसंविग्नाः सततं सर्वजन्तवः॥
en: On account of this, the Individual Soul, feeling great pain, quickly takes leave of the body. Know, O foremost of twice-born ones, that when the vital parts of the body become thus afflicted, Individual Soul passes away from he body, suffering from great pain. All living creatures repeatedly suffer from birth and death.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: दृश्यन्ते संत्यजन्तश्च शरीराणि द्विजर्षभ। गर्भसंक्रमणे चापि मर्मणामतिसर्पणे॥ तादृशीमेव लभते वेदनां मानवः पुनः। भिन्नसंधिरथ क्लेदमद्भिः स लभते नरः॥
en: It is seen, O chief of Brahman's, that the pain which is felt by a person when renouncing his bodies is like to what is felt by him when first entering the womb or when coming out of it. His joints become almost dislocated and he derives much distress from the waters.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: यथा पञ्चसु भूतेषु सम्भूतत्वं नियच्छति। शैत्यात् प्रकुपित: काये तीव्रवायुसमीरितः॥
en: Moved by (another) violent wind, the wind in the body becomes excited through cold, and dissolves away the union of matter into its five primal elements.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: यः स पञ्चसु भूतेषु प्राणापाने व्यवस्थितः। स गच्छत्यूर्ध्वगो वायुः कृच्छ्रान्मुक्त्वा शरीरिणः॥२२
en: That wind which lives in the vital airs called Prana and Apana occurring within this compound of the five primal elements, rushes upwards, from a situation of distress, leaving the embodied creature.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: शरीरं च जहात्येवं निरुच्छ्वासश्च दृश्यते। स निरुष्मा निरुच्छ्वासो नि:श्रीको हतचेतनः॥
en: It is thus that the wind leaves the body. Then is seen breathlessness. The man then becomes destitute of heat, of breath, of beauty, and of consciousness.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: ब्रह्मणा सम्परित्यक्तो मृत इत्युच्यते नरैः। स्रोतोभियैर्विजानाति इन्द्रियार्थाशरीरभृत्॥
en: Deserted by Brahma, the person is said to be dead. By those canals through which he perceives all sensuous objects, the bearer of the body no longer perceives them.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: तैरेव न विजानाति प्राणानाहारसम्भवान्। तत्रैव कुरुते काये य: स जीवः सनातनः॥
en: The Individual Soul creates in the body in those canals the vital airs forned by the food.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: तथा यद्यद् भवेद् युक्तं संनिपाते क्वचित् क्वचित्। तत्तन्मर्म विजानीहि शास्त्रदृष्टं हि तत् तथा॥
en: The elements gathered together become in certain parts firmly united. Know that those parts are called the vitals of the body. It is said so in the Shastras.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: तेषु मर्मसु भिन्नेषु ततः स समुदीरयन्। आविश्य हृदयं जन्तोः सत्त्वं चाशु रुणद्धि वै॥
en: When those vital parts are cut, the Individual Soul, rising up, enters the heat of the living creature and restrains the principle of animation forthwith.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: ततः सचेतनो जन्तु भिजानाति किंचन। तमसा संवृतज्ञानः संवृतेष्वेव मर्मसु। स जीवो निरधिष्ठानचाल्यते मातरिश्वना॥
en: The creature then, though still possessed of consciousness, fails to know anything. The vital part being all worked up, the knowledge of the living creature becomes overwhelmed by darkness.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: ततः सतं महोच्छ्वासं भृशमुच्छ्वस्य दारुणम्। निष्क्रामन् कम्पयत्याशु तच्छरीरमचेतनम्॥ सजीव: प्रच्युतः कायात् कर्मभिः स्वैः समावृतः। अभितः स्वैः शुभैः पुण्यैः पापैर्वाप्युपपद्यते॥
en: The individual Soul then, who has been deprived of everything upon which to stay, is then agitated by the wind. He then, deeply breathing a long an painful breath, goes out speedily, making the inanimate body to tremble. Separated from the body, the Individual Soul, however, is surrounded by his deeds.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: ब्राह्मणा ज्ञानसम्पन्ना यथावच्छ्रुतनिश्चयाः। इतरं कृतपुण्यं वा तं विजानन्ति लक्षणैः॥ यथान्धकारे खद्योतं लीयमानं ततस्ततः। चक्षुष्मन्तः प्रपश्यन्ति तथा च ज्ञानचक्षुषः॥ पश्यन्त्येवंविधं सिद्धा जीवं दिव्येन चक्षुषा। च्यवन्तं जायमानं च योनि चानुप्रवेशितम्॥ तस्य स्थानानि दृष्टानि त्रिविधानीह शास्त्रतः। कर्मभूमिरियं भूमिर्यत्र तिष्ठन्ति जन्तवः॥
en: He becomes equipped on all sides with all his auspicious deeds of merit and with all his sins. Brahmanas gifted with knowledge and equipped with the certain conclusions of the scriptures, know him, from marks, as to whether he is possessed of merit or with its demerit. Even as men having eyes see the firefly appearing and disappearing in the midst of darkness, men having the eye of knowledge and crowned with success of penances, see, with spiritual vision, the Individual Soul as he leaves the body, as he is re-born, and as he enters the womb. It is seen that the Individual Soul has three regions assigned to him eternally.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: ततः शुभाशुभं कृत्वा लभन्ते सर्वदेहिनः। इहैवोच्चावचान् भोगान् प्राप्नुवन्ति स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: This world where creatures live is called the field of action. Performing acts, good or bad, all embodied creatures attain to the fruits thereof.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: इहैवाशुभकर्माणः कर्मभिर्निरयं गताः। अवाग्गतिरियं कष्टा यत्र पच्यन्ति मानवाः। तस्मात् सुदुर्लभो मोक्षो रक्ष्यश्चात्मा ततो भृशम्॥
en: On account of their own decds, creatures acquirc even here superior or inferiors enjoyments. Doers of evil deeds here, on ! account of those deeds of theirs, attain to hell.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: ऊर्ध्वं तु जन्तवो गत्वा येषु स्थानेष्ववस्थिताः। कीर्त्यमानानि तानीह तत्त्वतः संनिबोध मे॥
en: This condition of sinking with head downwards, in which creatures are boiled is one of great misery. It is such that a rescue therefrom is highly difficult. Indeed, one should try hard for saving himself from this misery.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा नैष्ठिकी बुद्धिं बुद्ध्येथाः कर्मनिश्चयम्। तारारूपाणि सर्वाणि यत्रैतच्चन्द्रमण्डलम्॥
en: Those regions where creatures live when they ascend from this world, I shall now declare truly. Do you listen to me attentively.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: यत्र विभ्राजते लोके स्वभासा सूर्यमण्डलम्। स्थानान्येतानि जानीहि जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम्॥
en: By listening to what I say, you will acquire firmness of understanding and a clear apprehension of deeds. Know that even those are the regions of all creatures of righteous deeds, viz., the stellar worlds that shine in the sky, the lunar disc, and the solar disc as well that shines in the universe in its own light.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: कर्मक्षयाच्च ते सर्वे च्यवन्ते वै पुनः पुनः। तत्रापि च विशेषोऽस्ति दिवि नीचोच्चमध्यमः॥
en: Upon the termination, again, of their merits, they fall away from those regions repeatedly. There is distinction of inferior, superior and middling happiness even in the celestial region.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: न च तत्रापि संतोषो दृष्ट्रा दीप्ततरां श्रियम्। इत्येता गतयः सर्वाः पृथक्ते समुदीरिताः॥
en: There is discontent at sight of prosperity more burning than one's own even in the celestial region. Even these are the goals which I have mentioned in full.

description: The dissolution of the body and the acquirement of another. The attainment of the soul to Brahman
sn: उपपत्तिं तु वक्ष्यामि गर्भस्याहमतः परम्। तथा तन्मे निगदतः शृणुष्वावहितो द्विज॥
en: I shall, after this, describe to you the attainment by the Individual Soul of the condition of residence in the womb. Do you hear me, with rapt attention, O twice-born one, as I speak to you.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच शुभानामशुभानां च नेह नाशोऽस्ति कर्मणाम्। प्राप्य प्राप्यानुपच्यन्ते क्षेत्रं क्षेत्र तथा तथा॥
en: The Brahmana said The acts, good and bad, that the Individual Soul, docs are not subject 10 destruction. Upon attainment of body after body, those deeds yield fruits corresponding with then.

sn: यथा प्रसूयमानस्तु फली दद्यात् फलं बहु। तथा स्याद् विपुलं पुण्यं शुद्धेन मनसा कृतम्॥
en: As a fruit bearing tree, when the scason for production comes, yields a large quantity of fruit, merit, achieved with a pure heart, likewise yields a large measure of happiness.

sn: पापं चापि तथैव स्यात् पापेन मनसा कृतम्। पुरोधाय मनो हीदं कर्मण्यात्मा प्रवर्तते॥
en: Similarly, sin, committed with a sinful heart, produces a large quantity of misery. The Individual Soul, placing the mind a head, performs action.

sn: यथा कर्मसमाविष्टः काममन्युसमावृतः। नरो गर्भ प्रविशति तच्चापि शृणु चोत्तरम्॥
en: Hear then how the Individual Soul, cquipped with all his deeds and overwhelmed with lust and anger, enters the womb.

sn: शुक्रं शोणितसंसृष्टं स्त्रिया गर्भाशयं गतम्। क्षेत्रं कर्मजमाप्नोति शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्॥
en: The vital seed, mixed with blood, enters the womb of females and becomes the held (of the Individual Soul), good or bad, born of (his) deeds.

sn: सौम्यादव्यक्तभावाच्च न च क्वचन सज्जति। सम्प्राप्य ब्राह्मणः कामं तस्मात् तद्ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्॥६
en: On account of his subtlety and the condition of being unmanifest, the Individual Soul does not become attached to anything even after coming by a body. Therefore, he is called Eternal Brahma.

sn: तद् बीजं सर्वभूतानां तेन जीवन्ति जन्तवः। स जीवः सर्वगात्राणि गर्भस्याविश्य भागशः॥ दधाति चेतसा सद्यः प्राणस्थानेष्ववस्थितः। तत: स्पन्दयतेऽङ्गानि स गर्भश्चेतनान्वितः॥
en: That (viz., Jiva or Brahma) is the seed of all crcatures. It is on account of Him that living creatures live. That the Individual Soul, cntering all the limbs of the foetus part by part, accepting the attribute of mind, and living within all the regions that belong to vital air, supports (life). On account of this, the foetus, becoming possessed of mind, begins to move its limbs.

sn: यथा लोहस्य नि:स्यन्दो निषिक्तो बिम्बविग्रहम्। उपैति तद् विजानीहि गर्भे जीवप्रवेशनम्॥
en: As liquefied iron, poured (into a mould), takes the form of the mould, so is the entrance of the Individual Soul into the foetus.

sn: लोहपिण्डं यथा वह्निः प्रविश्य ह्यतितापयेत्। तथा त्वमपि जानीहि गर्भे जीवापपादनम्॥
en: As fire, entering a mass of iron, heats it greatly, so is the manifestation of the Individual Soul in the foetus.

sn: यथा च दीपः शरणे दीप्यमानः प्रकाशते। एवमेव शरीराणि प्रकाशयति चेतना॥
en: As a lamp, burning in a room, discovers (all things within it), so does the mind discover the different limbs of the body.

sn: यद् यच्च कुरुते कर्म वा यदि वाशुभम्। पूर्वदेहकृतं सर्वमवश्यमुपभुज्यते॥
en: Whatever deeds, good or bad, the Individual Soul does in a former body, have certainly to be enjoyed or endured by him.

sn: पुनश्चान्यत् प्रचीयते। यावत् तन्मोक्षयागस्थं धर्मं नैवावबुध्यते॥
en: By such enjoyment and endurance former deeds are exhausted, and other deeds, again, accumulate, till the Individual Soul succeed in acquiring a knowledge of the duties included in that contemplation which leads to Liberation.

sn: तत्र कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि सुखी भवति येन वै। आवर्तमानो जातीषु यथान्योन्यास सत्तम॥
en: Regarding this, I shall tell you those deeds by which the individual Soul, O best of men, while passing through a repeated round of rebirths, becomes happy.

sn: दानं व्रतं ब्रह्मचर्यं यथोक्तं ब्रह्मधारणम्। दमः प्रशान्तता चैव भूतानां चानुकम्पनम्॥ संयमाश्चानृशंस्यं च परस्वादानवर्जनम्। व्यलोकानामकरणं भूतानां मनसा भुवि॥ ततस्तु क्षीयते चैव मातापित्रोश्च शुश्रूषा देवतातिथिपूजनम्। गुरुपूजा घृणा शौचं नित्यमिन्द्रियसंयमः॥ प्रवर्तनं शुभानां च तत् सतां वृत्तमुच्यते। ततो धर्मः प्रभवति यः प्रजाः पाति शाश्वतीः॥
en: Gifts, observances of austerity, celibacy, bearing Brahma according to the ordinances laid down, self-control, tranquility, mercy for all creatures, restraint of passions, abstention from cruelty as also from appropriating others properties, refraining from doing even mentally all deeds that are false and injurious to living creatures on the Earth, respectfully serving mother and father, honouring the celestials and guests, adoration of preceptors, pity, purity, constant control of all organs, and causing of all good deeds are said to form the conduct of the good. From observance of such conduct, originates virtue which protects all creatures eternally.

sn: एवं सत्सु सदा पश्येत् तत्राप्येषा ध्रुवा स्थितिः। आचारो धर्ममाचष्टे यस्मिशान्ता व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Such conduct one would always see among good persons. Indeed, such conduct lives there for good. That course of practices which persons of tranquil souls follow, indicates Virtue.

sn: तेषु तत् कर्म निक्षिप्तं यः स धर्मः सनातनः। यस्तं समभिपद्येत न स दुर्गतिमाप्नुयात्॥
en: Among them is thrown that course of practices which forms eternal Virtue. He who would follow virtue would never have to come by a miserable end.

sn: अतो नियम्यते लोकः प्रच्यवन् धर्मवर्त्मसु। यश्च योगी च मुक्तश्च स एतेभ्यो विशिष्यते॥
en: It is by the conduct of the good that the world is restrained in the paths of Virtue when it falls away, He who is a Yogin is Liberated, and is, therefore, distinguished above these (viz., the good).

sn: वर्तमानस्य धर्मेण शुभं यत्र यथा तथा। संसारतारणं ह्यस्य कालेन महता भवेत्॥
en: Deliverance from the world occurs, after a long time, of one who acts righteously and well on every occasion as he should.

sn: एवं पूर्वकृतं कर्म नित्यं जन्तु: प्रपद्यते। सर्वं तत्कारणं येन विकृतोऽयमिहागतः॥
en: A living creature thus always meets with his pristine deeds. All these deeds form the cause in consequence of which he comes into this world in a state different from his true form.

sn: शरीरग्रहणं चास्य केन पूर्वं प्रकल्पितम्। इत्येवं संशयो लोके तच्च वक्ष्याम्यत: परम्॥
en: There is a doubt in the world about this question. By what was the acceptance (by the individual Soul) of a body first determined.

sn: शरीरमात्मनः कृत्वा सर्वलोकपितामहः। त्रेलोक्यमसृजद् ब्रह्मा कृत्स्नं स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥
en: Having first formed a body of his own, the Grandfather of all the worlds viz., Brahman, then created the three worlds, of mobile and immobile creatures.

sn: ततः प्रधानमसृजत् प्रकृति स शरीरिणाम्। यया सर्वमिदं व्याप्तं यां लोके परमां विदुः॥
en: Having first himself taken a body, he then created Pradhana. That Pradhana is the material cause of all embodied creatures, by whom is all this covered, and whom all came to know as the greatest.

sn: इदं तत्क्षरमित्युक्तं परं त्वमृतमक्षरम्। त्रयाणां मिथुनं सर्वमेकैकस्य पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: This which is seen is said to be destructible; while the other is immortal and indestructible. This which (is seen) is said to be Kshara (the destructible); that, however, which is the other is the Iminortal (as also) Akshara (the Indestructible). Of each Purusha taken separately, the whole is duality among these three.

sn: असृजत् सर्वभूतानि पूर्वदृष्टः प्रजापतिः। स्थावराणि च भूतानि इत्येषा पौर्विकी श्रुतिः॥
en: Seen first (to appear in an embodied form). Prajapati (then) created all the primal elements and all immobile creatures. This is the ancient Shruti.

sn: तस्य कालपरीमाणमकरोत् स पितामहः। भूतेषु परिवृत्तिं च पुनरावृत्तिमेव च॥
en: Of that (acceptance of body), thc Grandfather put down a limit about time, and migrations among various creatures and return or re-birth.

sn: यथात्र कश्चिन्मेधावी दृष्टात्मा पूर्वजन्मनि। यत् प्रवक्ष्यामि तत् सर्वं यथावदुपपद्यते॥
en: All that I say is proper and correct, as a person who has intelligence and who has seen his Soul, would say on this subject of previous births.

sn: सुख दुःखे यथा सम्यगनित्ये यः प्रपश्यति। कायं चामेध्यसंघातं विनाशं कर्मसंहितम्॥ यच्च किंचित्सुखं तच्च दुःखं सर्वमिति स्मरन्। संसारसागरं घोरं तरिष्यति सुदुस्तरम्॥
en: That person who considers pleasure and pain as inconstant, which, indced, is the correct view, who regards the body as an unholy collection, and destruction as ordained in action, and who remembers that what little of pleasure there is, is really all pain, will succeed in crossing this terrible ocean of worldly migration which is so difficult to cross.

sn: जातीमरणरौगैश्च समाविष्टः प्रधानवित्। चेतनावत्सु चैतन्यं समं भूतेषु पश्यति॥
en: Though attacked by decrepitude and death and disease, he who understand Pradhana sees with an equal eye that Consciousness which lives in all beings gifted with Consciousness.

sn: निर्विद्यते ततः कृत्स्नं मार्गमाणः परं पदम्। तस्योपदेशं वक्ष्यामि याथातथ्येन सत्तम॥
en: Seeking the supreme seat, he then becomes utterly indifferent to all (other) things. O best of men, I shall now deliver instruction to you, according to truth, concerning this.

sn: शाश्वतस्याव्ययस्याथ यदस्य ज्ञानमुत्तमम्। प्राच्यमानं मया विप्र निबोधेदमशेषतः॥
en: Do you, O learned Brahmana, understand in full what form the excellent knowledge, as I declare it, of that indestructible seat.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच यः स्यादेकायने लीनस्तूष्णीं किंचिदचिन्तयन्। पूर्वं पूर्व परित्यज्य स तीर्णो बन्धनाद् भवेत्॥
en: Brahman said He who becomes immerged in the one receptacle (of all things), freeing himself from cven the thought of his own identity with all things, indeed, ccasing to things of even his own existencc-gradually renouncing one after another, will succeed in crossing his bonds.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: सर्वमित्रः सर्वसहः शमे रक्तो जितेन्द्रियः। व्यपेतभयमन्युश्च आत्मवान् मुच्यते नरः॥
en: That man who is the friend of all, who endures all, who is attached to tranquillity, who has conquered all his senses, who is shorn of fear and anger, and who is of controlled soul, succeeds in liberating himself.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु यश्चरेनियतः शुचिः। अमानी निरभीमानः सर्वतो मुक्त एव सः॥
en: He who treats all creatures as his ownself, who is restrained, pure, free froin vanity, and shorn of egoism, is considered as liberated from everything

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: जीवितं मरणं चोभे सुखदुःखे तथैव च। लाभालाभे प्रियद्वेष्ये यः समः स च मुच्यते॥
en: He also is libcrated who considers in the same light life and death, pleasure and pain, gain and loss, agreeable and disagrecable.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: न कस्यचित् स्पृहयते नावजानाति किंचन। निर्द्वन्द्वो वीतरागात्मा सर्वथा मुक्त एव सः॥
en: He is in every way liberated who does not covet others' properties, who never disregards any body, who is above all pairs of opposites, and whose soul is shorn of attachments.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: अनमित्रश्च निर्बधुरनपत्यश्च यः क्वचित्। त्यक्तधर्मार्थकामश्च निराकाक्षी च मुच्यते॥
en: He is liberated who has no enemy, no। kinsman, and no child, who has cast off religion, riches and pleasure, and who is freed from desire or cupidity.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: नैव धर्मी न चाधर्मी पूर्वोपचितहायकः। धातुक्षयप्रशान्तात्मा निर्द्वन्द्वः स विमुच्यते॥
en: He becomes liberated who acquires neither merit nor demerit, who casts off the merits and demerits accumulated in pristine births, who wastes the elements of his body for attaining to a tranquillised soul, and who gets over all pairs of opposites.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: अकर्मवान् विकासश्च पश्येज्जगदशाश्वतम्। अश्वत्थसदृशं नित्यं जन्ममृत्युजरायुतम्॥ वैराग्यबुद्धिः सततमात्मदोषव्यपेक्षकः। आत्मबन्धविनिर्मोक्षं स करोत्यचिरादिव॥
en: He who abstains from all deeds, who is free from desire or cupidity, who considers the universe as un-enduring or as like an Ashvatha tree, ever gifted with birth, death, and ! decrepitude, whose understanding is fixed on renunciation, and whose eyes are always directed towards his own faults, soon succeeds in freeing himself from the fetters that bind him.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: अगन्धमरसस्पर्शमशब्दमपरिग्रहम्। अरूपमनभिज्ञेयं दृष्ट्वाऽऽत्मानं विमुच्यते॥
en: He who sees his soul void of smell, of taste and touch, of sound, of belongings, of vision, and unknowable, becomes liberated.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: पञ्चभूतगुणैीनममूर्तिमदहेतुकम्। अगुणं गुणभोक्तारं यः पश्यति स मुच्यते॥
en: He who sces his soul shorn of the attributes of the five elements, to be without form and cause, to be really destitute of attributes though enjoying them, becomes liberated.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: विहाय सर्वसंकल्पान् बुद्ध्या शारीरमानसान्। शनैर्निर्वाणमाप्नोति निरिन्धन इवानलः॥
en: Abandoning, with the help of the understanding, all purposes relating to body and mind, one gradually attains to cessation of separate existence, like a fire unfed with fuel.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: सर्वसंस्कारनिर्मुक्तो निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः। तपसा इन्द्रियग्रामं यश्चरेन्मुक्त एव सः॥
en: One who is freed from all impressions, who is above all pairs of opposites, who is destitute of all belongings, and who uses all his senses under the guidance of penances, becomes liberated.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: विमुक्तः सर्वसंस्कारैस्ततो ब्रह्म सनातनम्। परमाप्नोति संशान्तमचलं नित्यमक्षरम्॥
en: Having become freed from all impressions, one then attains to Brahma which is Eternal and supreme, and tranquil, and stable, and enduring and indestructible.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि योगशास्त्रमनुत्तमम्। युञ्जन्तः सिद्धमात्मानं यथा पश्यन्ति योगिनः॥
en: After this I shall describe the science of Yoga than which there is nothing superior, and how Yogins, by concentration, sce the perfect soul.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: तस्योपदेशं वक्ष्यामि यथावत् तन्निवोध मे। यैरैश्चारयन्नित्यं पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि॥
en: I shall communicate the instructions about it duly. Do you learn from me those doors by which directing the soul within the body one sees that which is without beginning and end.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: इन्द्रियाणि तु संहृत्य मन आत्मनि धारयेत्। तीव्र तप्त्वा तपः पूर्वे मोक्षयोगं समाचरेत्॥
en: Withdrawing the senses from their objects, one should fix the mind upon the soul; having previously practised the severest austerities, one should practise that concentration of mind which leads to Liberation.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: तपस्वी सततं युक्तो योगशास्रमथाचरेत्। मनीषी मनसा विप्र पश्यन्नात्मानमात्मनि॥
en: Observant of penances and always practising concentration of mind, the learned Brahmana, gifted with intelligence, should observe the precepts of the Science of Yoga, seeing the soul in the body.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: य चेच्छक्नोत्ययं साधुर्योक्तुमात्मानमात्मनि। तत एकान्तशीलः स पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि॥
en: If the good man succeeds in concentrating the mind on the soul, he then, used to exclusive meditation, secs the Supreme Soul in his own soul.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: हि संयतः सततं युक्त आत्मवान् विजितेन्द्रियः। तथा य आत्मनाऽऽत्मानं सम्प्रयुक्तः प्रपश्यति॥
en: Self-controlled and always concentrated, and with all his senses completely conquered, the man of purified soul, on account of such complete concentration of mind, succeeds in seeing the soul by soul.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: यथा पुरुषः स्वप्ने दृष्ट्वा पश्यत्यसाविति। तथा रूपमिवात्मानं साधुयुक्तः प्रपश्यति॥
en: As a person seeing some unseen individual in a dream recognises him, saying. This is he, when he sees him after waking, similar.y the good man having seen the Supreme Soul in the deep contemplation of Samadhi recognises it upon waking from Samadhi.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: इषीकां च यथा मुजात् कश्चिनिष्कृष्य दर्शयेत्। योगी निष्कृष्य चात्मानं तथा पश्यति देहतः॥
en: As one sees the fibrous pith after extracting it from a blade of the Saccharum Munja, so the Yogin sees the Soul, extracting it from the body.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: मुजं शरीरमित्याहुरिषीकामात्मनि श्रिताम्। एतन्निदर्शनं प्रोक्तं योगविद्भिरनुत्तमम्॥
en: The body has been called the Saccharum Munja and the filbrons pith is called the Soul. This is the excellent illustration given by persons knowing Yoga.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: यदा हि युक्तमात्मानं सम्यक् पश्यति देहभृत्। न तस्येहेश्वरः कश्चित् त्रैलोक्यस्यापि यः प्रभुः।।२४
en: When the bearer of a body adequately sees the Soul in Yoga, he then has no one to master him, for he then becomes the lord of three worlds.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: अन्यान्याश्चैव तनवो यथेष्टं प्रतिपद्यते। विनिवृत्य जरां मृत्युं न शोचति न हृष्यति॥
en: He succeeds in assuming various bodies according as as he wishes. Turning away decrepitude and death, he neither grieves nor exalis.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: देवानामपि देवत्वं युक्तः कारयते वशी। ब्रह्म चाव्ययमाप्नोति हित्वा देहमशाश्वतम्॥
en: The self controlled man, concentrated in Yoga, can create (for himself) the godship of the very gods. Renouncing his transient body he attains to immutable Brahma.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: विनश्यत्सु च भूतेषु न भयं तस्य जायते। क्लिश्यमानेषु भूतेषु न स क्लिशति केनचित्॥
en: He does not fear even at on seçing all creatures falling victims to destruction. When all creatures are afflicted, he can never be afflicted by any one.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: दुःखशोकमयैोरैः सङ्गस्नेहसमुद्भवैः। न विचाल्यति युक्तात्मानिःस्पृहः शान्तमानसः॥
en: Devoid of desire and gifted with a tranquil mind, the person in Yoga is never affected by pain and sorrow and fear and the dreadful effects of attachment and affection.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: नैनं शस्त्राणि विध्यन्ते न मृत्युश्चास्य विद्यते। नातः सुखतरं किंचिल्लोके क्वचन दृश्यते॥
en: Weapons never pierce him; death does not exist for him. Nowhere in the world can be seen any one who is happier than he.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: सम्यग्युक्त्वा स आत्मानमात्मन्येव प्रतिष्ठते। विनिवृत्तजरादुःख सुखं स्वपिति चापि सः॥
en: Having adequately concentrated his soul, he lives firmly himself. Pruning off decrepitude and pain and pleasure, he sleeps at case.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: देहान्यथेष्टमभ्येति हित्वेमां मानुषीं तनुम्। निर्वेदस्तु न कर्तव्यो भुञ्जानेन कथंचन॥
en: Renouncing this human body he attains to (other) forms according to his pleasure. While one is enjoying the sovereignty that Yoga bestows, one should never fall away from devotion to Yoga.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: सम्यग्युक्तो यदाऽऽत्मानमात्मन्येव प्रपश्यति। तदैव न स्पृहयते साक्षादपि शतक्रतोः॥
en: When one, after adequate devotion to Yoga, sees the Soul in his ownself, he then ceases to have any regard for even him of a hundred sacrifices (India).

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: योगमेकान्तशीलस्तु यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु। दृष्टपूर्वी दिशं चिन्त्य यस्मिन् सनिवसेत् पुरे॥ पुनस्याभ्यन्तरे तस्य मनः स्थाप्यं न बाह्यतः। पुनस्याभ्यन्तरे तिष्ठन् यस्मिन्नावसथे वसेत्। तस्मिन्नावसथे धार्य सबाह्याभ्यन्तरं मनः॥ प्रचिन्त्यावसथे कृत्स्नं यस्मिन् काले स पश्यति। तस्मिन् काले मनश्चास्य न च किंचन बाह्यतः॥ सन्नियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं निर्घोषं निर्जने वने। कायमभ्यन्तरं कृत्स्नमेकाग्र: परिचिन्तयेत्॥ दन्तांस्तालु च जिह्वां च गलं ग्रीवां तथैव च। हृदयं चिन्तयेच्चापि तथा हृदयबन्धनम्॥
en: Hear now how one, habituating himself to exclusive meditation, succeeds in attaining to Yoga. Thinking of that points of the compass which has the Sun behind it, the mind should be fixed not outside, but in the interior of that palace in which one may happen to live. Livin within that palace the mind should then, with all it outward and inward (operations). see in that particular room in which one may live. At that time when, having deeply meditated one sees the All (viz., Brahma, the Soul of the Universe). there is then nothing external to Brahma where the mind may live. Controlling all the senses in a forest that is free from the noise and that is uninhabited, with mind fired thereon, one should meditate on the All both outside and inside his body. One should mediate on the teeth, the palate, the tongue, the throat, the neck likewise; one should also meditate on the heart and the ligatures of the heart.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच इत्युक्तः य मया शिष्यो मेधावी मधुसूदन। पप्रच्छ पुनरेवेमं मोक्षधर्मं सुदुर्वचम्॥
en: Thus addressed by me, that intelligent disciple, O destroyer of Madhu, once more asked me about this religion of Liberation that is so difficult to explain.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: भुक्तं भुक्तमिदं कोष्ठे कथमनं विपच्यते। कथं रसत्वं व्रजति शोणितत्वं कथं पुनः॥
en: How does this food that is eaten from time to time become digested in the stomach? How does it become changed into juice? How, again, into blood.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: तथा मांस च मेदश्च स्नाय्वस्थीनि च योषिति। कथमेतानि सर्वाणि शरीराणि शरीरिणाम्॥
en: How docs it nourish the flesh, the marrow, the sinews, the bones? How do all these limbs of embodied creatures grow?

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: वर्धते वर्धमानस्य वर्धते च कथं बलम्। निरोधानां निर्गमनं मलानां च पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: How does the strength grow of the growing man? How takes place the escape of all such elements as are not nutritive, and of all impurities separately?

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: कुतोवायं प्रश्वसिति उच्छ्वसित्यपि वा पुनः। कं च देशमधिष्ठाय तिष्ठेत्यात्मायमात्मनि॥
en: How does this one inhale and again, exhale? Staying upon what particular part does the Soul live in the body?

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: जीवः कथं वहति च चेष्टमान: कलेवरम्। किं वर्ण कीदृशं चैव निवेशयति वै पुनः॥
en: How does the Individual Soul, exerting himself, bear the body? Of what colour and of what kind is the body n which he lives again?

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: याथातथ्येन भगवन् वक्तुमर्हसि मेऽनघ। इति सम्परिपृष्टोऽहं तेन विप्रेण माधव॥
en: O' holy one, you should tell me all this accurately, O sinless one' Thus was I accosted by that learned Brahimana, O Madhava?

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: प्रत्यब्रुवं महाबाहो यथाश्रुतमरिंदम। यथा स्वकोष्ठे प्रक्षिप्य भाण्डं भाण्डमना भवेत्॥ तथा स्वकाये प्रक्षिप्य मनो द्वारैनिश्चलैः। आत्मानं तत्र मार्गेत प्रमादं परिवर्जयेत्॥
en: I replied to him. O you of mighty arms, as I myself had heard, O chastiser of all enemies! As onc, placi.:g some precious object in his store-room, should keep his mind on it, so placing the mind within one's own body, one should then, controlling all the senses, seek after the Soul, avoiding all carclessness.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: एवं सततमुद्युक्तः प्रीतात्मा न चिरादिव। आसादयति तद् ब्रह्म यद् दृष्ट्वा स्यात् प्रधानवित्।।४७
en: One should, becoming always assiduous in this way and pleased with his own self, within a very short time, attain to that Brahman by seeing which one would become conversant with Pradhana.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: न त्वसौ चक्षुषा ग्राह्यो न च सर्वैरपीन्द्रियैः। मनसैव प्रदीपेन महानात्मा प्रदृश्यते॥
en: He is not capable of being apprehended by the eye; nor even by all the senses. It is only with the lamp of the mind that the great Soul can be seell.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: सर्वतः पाणिपादान्तः सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखाः सर्वतःश्रुतिमाल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति॥
en: He has hands and feet on all sides; he has ears on all sides; he lives, pervading all things in this world.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: जीवो निष्क्रान्तमात्मानं शरीरात् सम्प्रपश्यति। स तमुत्सृज्य देहे धारयन् ब्रह्म केवलम्॥
en: The Individual Soul beholds the Soul as extracted from the body. Then renouncing Brahma as invested with form, by holding the mind in the body, he sees Brahma as freed from all qualities.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: आत्मानमालोकयति मनसा प्रहसन्निव। तदेवमाश्रयं कृत्वा मोक्ष याति ततो मयि॥
en: He sees the Soul with his mind, siniling as it were at the time. Depending upon that Brahma; he then attains to Liberation in me.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: इदं सर्वरहस्यं ते मया प्रोक्तं द्विजोत्तम। आपृच्छे साधयिष्यामि गच्छ विप्र यथासुखम्॥
en: O foremost of twice both oncs, all this mystery has now been declared by me. I ask your permission, for I shall leave this place. Do you (also) go wherever you like.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: इत्युक्तः स तदा कृष्ण मया शिष्यो महातपाः। अगच्छत यथाकामं ब्राह्मणः संशितव्रतः॥
en: Thus, addressed by me, O Krishna, on that occasion that disciple of mine, gifted with austere penances, that Brahmana of rigid vows, went away according to this pleasure.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: वासुदेव उवाच इत्युक्त्वा स तदा वाक्यं मां पार्थ द्विजसत्तमः। मोक्षधर्माश्रितः सम्यक् तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Vasudeva said O'son of Pritha having said these words to me, on that occasion, about the Religion of Emancipation, that best of Brahmanas disappeared then and there.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: कच्चिदेतत् त्वया पार्थ श्रुतमेकाग्रचेतसा। तदापि हि रथस्थस्त्वं श्रुतवानेतदेव हि॥
en: Have you heard this discourse, O son of Pritha, with mind directed solely to wards it? This you did hear on that occasion while you were on your car.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: नैतत् पार्थ सुविज्ञेयं व्यामिश्रेणेति मे मतिः। नरेणाकृतसंज्ञेन विशुद्धनान्तरात्मना।॥
en: I think, O son of Pritha, that this is difficult of being comprehended by one whose understanding is confused, or who has acquired no wisdom by study, or who eats food not suited to his body' or whose Soul is not purified.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: सुरस्यमिदं प्रोक्तं देवानां भरतर्षभ। कच्चिन्नेदं श्रुतं पार्थ मनुष्येणेह कर्हिचित्॥
en: O chief of Bharata's race, this is a great mystery among the celestials that has been declared. At no time or place; O son of Pritha, has this teen heard by man in this world.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: न ह्येतच्छ्रोतुमर्होऽन्यो मनुष्यस्त्वामृतेऽनघ। नैतदद्य सुविज्ञेयं व्यामिश्रेणान्तरात्मना॥
en: O sinless one, save yourself no other man is worthy of hearing it. It is not, at this time, capable of being easily understood by one whose inner soul is confused.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: क्रियावद्भिर्हि कौन्तेय देवलोकः समावृतः। . न चैतदिष्टं देवानां मर्त्यरूपनिवर्तनम्॥
en: The world of the celestials is filled, O son of Kunti, with those who follow the religion of actions. The cessation of the body is not liked by the celestials.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: पराहि सा गति पार्थं तद् ब्रह्म सनातनम्। यत्रामृतत्वं प्राप्नोति त्यक्त्वा देहं सदा सुखी॥
en: That goal, O son of Pritha, is the highest which is forined by eternal Brahman where (Onc, renouncing the body, attains to immortality and becomes always happy.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: इमं धर्मं समास्थाय येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः। स्त्रियो वैशयास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम्।।
en: By following this religion, even they who are of sinful birth, such as women and Vaishyas and Shudras, come by the highest goal.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पार्थ क्षत्रिया वा बहुश्रुताः। स्वधर्मरतयो नित्यं ब्रह्मलोकपरायणाः॥
en: What need be said then, O son of Pritha, of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas endued with great learning, always devoted to the duties of their own orders, and who are intent on the region of Brahma?

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: हेतुमच्चैतदुद्दिष्टमुपायाश्चास्य साधने। सिद्धि फलं च मोक्षश्च दुःखस्य च विनिर्णय॥
en: This has been laid down with the reasons; and also the means for its acquisition; and as complete attainment and fruit, viz., Liberation and the ascertainment of the truth about pain.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: नात परं सुख त्वन्यत् किंचित स्याद् भरतर्षभ। बुद्धिमाञ्श्रद्दधनश्च पराक्रान्तश्च पाण्डव॥ यः परित्यज्यते मर्यो लोकसारमसारवत्। एतैरुपायैः स क्षिप्रं परां गतिमवाप्नुते॥
en: O chief of Bharata's race, there is nothing else which yields happiness greater than is That mortal, O son of Pandu, who gifted with intelligence, and faith, and prowess, renounces unsubstantial what is considered substantial by the world, succeeds within a short time in obtaining the Supreme by these as as jeans.

description: The characteristics of a Liberated Person
sn: एतावदेव वक्तव्यं नातो भूयोऽस्ति किंचन। षण्मासान् नित्ययुक्तस्य योगः पार्थ प्रवर्तते॥
en: This is all that is to be said-there is nothing else which is higher than this. He, O son of Pritha, who devotes himself to its constant practice for a period of six months, succeeds in attaining to Yoga.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: वासुदेव उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। दम्पत्योः पार्थ संवादो योऽभवद् भरतर्षभ॥
en: Regarding it is cited the old narrative, O son of Pritha, of the discourse that took place between a married couple.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: ब्राह्मणी ब्राह्मणं कंचिज्ज्ञानविज्ञानपारगम्। दृष्ट्वा विविक्त आसीनं भार्या भर्तारमब्रवीत्॥ कं नु लोकं गमिष्यामि त्वामहं पतिमाश्रिता। न्यस्तकर्माणमासीनं कीनाशमविचक्षणम्॥
en: A certain Brahmana's wife, seeing the Brahmana, her husband, who was a complete master of every kind of knowledge and wisdom, seated in seclusion, said to him, Into what region shall I go, depending on you as my husband, you who are seated, having cast off all (religious) acts, who are harsh in your conduct towards me, and who undiscerning?

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: भार्याः पतिकृताँल्लोकानाप्नुवन्तीति नः श्रुतम्। त्वामहं पतिमासाद्य कां गमिष्यामि वै गतिम्॥
en: We have heard that a wife attains to those regions which are acquired by her husband. What, indeed, is the goal that I shall attain, having obtained you for my husband.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: एवमुक्तः स शान्तात्मा तामुवाच हसन्निव। सुभगे नाभ्यसूयामि वाक्यस्यास्य तवातघे॥
en: Thus questioned, that Brahmana of tranquil soul then said to her, smilingly, O blessed dame, I am not offended with these words of yours, O sinless one.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: ग्राह्यं दृश्यं च सत्यं वा यदिदं कर्म विद्यते। एतदेव व्यवस्यन्ति कर्म कर्मेति कर्मिणः॥
en: Whatever acts exist which are adopted with the help of others, which are seen and which are true, are done, as acts, by men, devoted to acts. are SO are

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: मोहमेव नियच्छन्ति कर्मणा ज्ञानवर्जिताः। नैष्कर्म्यं न च लोकेऽस्मिन् मुहूर्तमपि लभ्यते॥
en: Those persons who are destitute of knowledge, only store delusion by deeds. Freedom from acts, again, cannot even be momentarily attained in this world.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: कर्मणा मनसा वाचा शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्। जन्मादिमूर्तिभेदान्तं कर्म भूतेषु वर्तते॥
en: From birth to the attainment of a different form, action good or bad, and accomplished by deeds, mind, or speech, exists in all beings.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: रक्षोभिर्वघ्यमानेषु दृश्यद्रव्येषु वर्त्मसु। आत्मस्थमात्मना तेभ्यो दृष्टमायतनं मया॥
en: Those paths (of action) which characterised by visible objects (such as Somajuice and clarified butter for libations) being destroyed by Rakshasa, turning away from them I have perceived the scat (of the soul) that is in the body, with the help of the soul.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: यत्र तद् ब्रह्म निर्द्वन्द्वं यत्र सोमः सहाग्निना। व्यवायं कुरुते नित्यं धीरो भूतानि धारयन्॥
en: There lives Brahma transcending all pairs of opposites; there Soma with Agni; and there the mover of the under standing, (viz., Vayu) always moves, upholding all creatures.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: यत्र ब्रह्मादयो युक्तास्तदक्षरमुपासते। विद्वांसः सुव्रता यत्र शान्तात्मानो जितेन्द्रियाः॥
en: It is for that seat that the Grandfather Brahman and others, concentrated in Yoga, adorc thc Indestructible. It is for that seat that men of learning an excellent vows, of tranquil souls, and of senses completely controlled, strive.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: घ्राणेन न तदा यं नास्वाद्यं चैव जिह्वया। स्पर्शनेन तदस्पृश्यं मनसा त्ववगम्यते॥
en: That is not capable of being smelt by the sense of smell; nor tasted by the tongue; or touched by the organs of It is by the mind that that is attained.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: चक्षुषामविषह्यं च यत् किंचिच्छ्रवणात् परम्। अगत्वमरसस्मर्शमरूपाशब्दलक्षणम्॥
en: It is incapable of being conquered by the cye. It is above the sense of hearing. It is shorn of scent, taste, touch, and form as attributes.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: यतः प्रवर्तते तन्त्रं यत्र च प्रतितिष्ठति। प्राणोऽपान: समानश्च व्यानश्चोदार एव च॥ तत एव प्रवर्तन्ते तदेव प्रविशन्ति च। समानव्यानयोर्मध्ये प्राणापानौ विचेरतुः॥
en: It is that from which proceeds the wellordained universe, and it that upon which it depends. The vital airs called Prana, Apana, Samana, Vyana and Udana, flow from it, and it is that into which they again enter. The vital airs Prana and Apana move between Samana and Vyana.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: तस्मिल्लीने प्रलीयेत समानो व्यान एव च। अपान प्रणयोर्मध्ये उदानो व्याप्य तिष्ठति। तस्माच्छयानं पुरुषं प्राणापानौ न मुञ्चतः॥
en: When the soul sleeps, both Samana and Vyana are absorbed. Between Apana and Frana, Udana lives, pervading all.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: प्राणानामायतत्वेन तमुदानं प्रचक्षते। तस्मात् तपो व्यवस्यन्ति मन्दतं ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
en: Hence, Prana and Apana do not desert a sleeping person. On account of its controlling all the vital airs, the controlling breath is so called Udana.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: तेषामन्योन्यभक्षाणां सर्वेषां देहचारिणाम्। अग्निर्वैश्वानरो मध्ये सप्तधा दीव्यतेऽन्तरा॥ घ्राणं जिहा च चक्षुश्चत्वक् च श्रोत्रं च पञ्चमम्। मनो बुद्धिश्च सप्तैता जिह्वा वैश्वानरार्चिषः॥ प्रेयं दृश्यं च पेयं च स्पृश्यं श्रव्यं तथैव च। मन्तव्यमथ वोद्धव्यं ताः सप्त समिधो मम॥ घ्राता भक्षयिता द्रष्टा स्प्रष्टा श्रोता च पञ्चमः। मन्ता बोद्धा च सप्तैते भवन्ति परमविजः॥ प्रेये पेये च दृश्ये च स्पृश्ये श्रव्ये तथैव च। मन्तव्येऽप्यथ बोद्धव्ये सुभगे पश्य सर्वदा॥
en: Hence, utterers of Brahma practise penances which have myself for their goal. In the midst of all those vital airs which swallow up one another and move within the body, shines forth the fire called Vaishvanara made up of seven flames. The nose, the tongue, the eye, the skin, the car which numbers the fifth, the mind, and the understanding, these are the seven tongues of that Vaishvanara's flame. That which is smelt that which is seen, that which is drunk, that which is touched, as also that which is heard, that which is thought of, and that which is understood, these are the seven sorts of fuel for me. That which smells, that which eats, that which sces, that which touches, that which sees, that which touches, that which hears, numbering the fifth; that which thinks, and that which understands, these are the seven great officiating priests.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: हवींष्यग्निषु होतार: सप्तधा सप्त सप्तसु। सम्यक् प्रक्षिप्य विद्वांसो जनयन्ति स्वयोनिषु॥ पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम्। मनो बुद्धिश्च सप्तैता योनिरित्येव शब्दिताः॥ हविर्भूता गुणाः सर्वे प्रविशन्त्यग्निजं गुणम्। अन्तर्वासमुषित्वा च जायन्ते स्वासु योनिषु॥ तत्रैव च निरुध्यन्ते प्रलये भूतभावने। ततः संजायते गन्धस्ततः संजायते रसः॥
en: Mark, O blessed one, learned sacrificers duly casting seven libations in seven ways in the seven fires, viz., that which is smelt, that which is drunk, that which is smelt, that which is drunk, that which is seen, that which is touched, as also that which is heard, that which is thought of, and that which is understood, create them in their own wombs. Earth, Wind, Ether, Weather, and Light numbering as the fifth, Mind and Understanding, these seven are called wombs (of all things). All the attributes which form the sacrificial offerings, enter into the attribute that is born of the fire; and having lived within that dwelling become reborn in their respective wombs. There also, viz., in that which generates all beings, they remain absorbed during the period for which dissolution lasts.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: ततः संजायते रूपं ततः स्पर्शोऽभिजायते। ततः संजायते शब्दः संशयस्तत्र जायते। ततः संजायते निष्ठा जन्मैतत् सप्तधा विदुः॥
en: From that is produced smell, from that is produced taste, from that is produced colour, and from that is produced touch; from that is produced sound; from that originates doubt; and from that is produce a resolution. Thus is what is known as the sevenfold creation.

description: The discourse of the married couple. The description of Brahman
sn: अनेनैव प्रकारेण प्रगृहीतं पुरातनैः। पूर्णाहुतिभिरापूर्णास्त्रिभिः पूर्यन्ति तेजसा॥
en: It is thus that all this was comprehended by the ancients. By the three full and final libations, the full become full with light.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। निबोध दशहोतृणां विधानमथ यादृशम्॥
en: The Brahmana said Regarding it is cited the following ancient story. Do you understand, of what kind the institution is of the ten Hotris (sacrificing priests).

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: श्रोत्रं त्वक् चक्षुषी जिह्वा नासिका चरणौ करो। उपस्थं वायुरिति वा होतृणि दश भामिनि॥
en: The ear, the skin, the two eyes, the tongue, the nose, the two feet, the two hands, the genital organ, the lower duct, and speech, these, O beautiful one, are the ten sacrificing priests.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: शब्दस्पर्शी रूपरसौ गन्धो वाक्यं क्रिया गतिः। रेतोमूत्रपुरीषाणां त्यागो दश हवींषि च॥
en: Sound, touch, colour, taste, scent, speech, action, motion, and the discharge of vital seed, of urine, and of cxcreta, are the ten libations.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: दिशो वायू रविश्चन्द्रः पृथ्व्यग्नी विष्णुरेव च। इन्द्रः प्रजापतिर्मित्रमग्नयो दश भामिनि॥
en: The points of the compass, wind, Sun, Moon, earth, fire, Vishnu, Indra, Prajapati, and was Mitra, these, O beautiful one, are the ten (sacrificial) fires.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: दशेन्द्रियाणि होतृणि हवींषि दश भाविनि। विषया नाम समिधो हूयन्ते तु दशाग्निषु॥ चित्तं स्रुवश्च वित्तं च पवित्रं ज्ञानमुत्तमम्। सुविभक्तमिदं सर्वं जगदासीदिति श्रुतम्॥
en: The ten organs (of knowledge and action) are the sacrificing priests. The libations, O beautiful one, are ten. The objects of the senses are the fuel that are thrown into these ten fires, as also the mind, which is the ladle, and the wealth (viz., the good and bad acts of the sacrificer. What remains is the pure, highest knowledge. We have heard that all this universe well differentiated (from knowledge).

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: सर्वमेवाथ विज्ञेयं चित्तं ज्ञानमवेक्षते। रेतः शरीरभृत्काये विज्ञाता तु शरीरभृत्॥
en: All objects of knowledge are Mind. Knowledge only perceives it. The Individual Soul, encased in subtle form, lives within the gross body that is produced by the vital seed,

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: शरीरभृद् गार्हपत्यस्तस्मादन्यः प्रणीयते। मनचाहवनीयस्तु तस्मिन् प्रक्षिप्यते हविः॥
en: The bearer of the body is the Garhapatya fire. From that is produced another. Mind is the Ahavaniya fire. Into it is, poured the oblation.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: ततो वाचस्पतिर्जज्ञे तं मनः पर्यवेक्षते। रूपं भवति वैवर्णं समनुद्रवते मनः॥
en: From that was produced the Veda or Word), (then was born Mind); Mind (desirous of creation) sets itself on the Veda (or the Word). Then arises forin colour) undistinguished by particular colours. It runs towards the Mind. or

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: ब्राह्मण्युवाच कस्माद् वागभवत् पूर्वं कस्मात् पश्चान्मनोऽभवत्। मनसा चिन्तितं वाक्यं यदा समभिपद्यते॥
en: The Brahmana's wife said Why did Word first arise and why did Mind arise afterwards, seeing that Word comes into being after having been thought upon by Mind?

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: केन विज्ञानयोगेन मतिश्चित्तं समास्थिता। समुन्नीता नाध्यगच्छत् को वै तां प्रतिवाधते॥
en: Upon what authority can it be said that Mati (Prana) takes refuge in Mind. Why, again, in dreamless sleep, though separatcd from Mind, does not Prana apprehend (all objects)? What is that which controls it then?

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच तामपानः पतिर्भूत्वा तस्मात् प्रेषत्यपानताम्। तां गतिं मनसः प्राहुर्मनस्तस्मादपेक्षते॥
en: The Apana air, becoming the lord, on account of such lordship over it, makes it at one with itself. That restrained motion of the Prana air has been said to be the motion of the mind. Hence the mind depends upon Prana.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: प्रश्नं तु वाङ्मनसोर्मा यस्मात् त्वमनुपृच्छसि। तस्मात् ते वर्तयिष्यामि तयोरेव समाह्वयम्॥
en: But since you ask me a question about word and mind, I shall, therefore, describe to you a discourse between them.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: उभे वाङ्मनसी गत्वा भूतात्मानमपृच्छताम्। आवयोः श्रेष्ठमाचक्ष्व च्छिन्धि नौ संशयं विभो॥
en: Both Word and Mind, repairing to the Soul of matter, asked him, Do you say who amongst us is superior. Do you, O powerful one, remove our doubt.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: मन इत्येव भगवांस्तदा प्राह सरस्वती। अहं वै कामधुक् तुभ्यमिति तं प्राह वागथ॥
en: On that occasion, the holy one made this answer, The mind undoubtedly (is superior)! To him Word said, I great you the fruition of all your desires.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव विद्धयुभे मनसी मम। स्थावरं मत्सकाशे वै जङ्गमं विषये तव॥
en: The Brahmana said Know that I have two minds, immovable and movable. That which is immovable, is, indeed, with me; the movable is in your dominion.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: यस्तु तं विषयं गच्छेन्मन्त्रो वर्णः स्वरोऽपि वा। तन्मनो जगमो नाम तस्मादसि गरीयसी॥
en: That mind is indeed called movable which, in the form of Mantra, letter, or voice, is referrible to your dominion. Hence, you are superior.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: यस्मादपि समाधिस्ते स्वयमभ्येत्य शोभने। तस्मादुच्छ्वासमासाद्य प्रवक्ष्यामि सरस्वति॥
en: But since, coming of your own accord, O beautiful one, you enter into the engagement, therefore, filling myself with breath, I utter you.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: प्राणापानान्तरे देवी वाग् वै नित्यं स्म तिष्ठति। प्रेर्यमाणा महाभागे विना प्राणमपानती। प्रजापतिपुपाधावत् प्रसीद भगवन्निति॥
en: The goddess Word used always to live between Prana and Apana, But, O blessed one, sinking into Apana, though urged upwards, on account of becoming dissociated from Prana, she ran to Prajapati and said, Be pleased with ime, O holy one.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: ततः प्राणः प्रादुरभूद् वाचमाप्याययन् पुनः। तस्मा दुच्छ्वासमासाद्य न वाग् वदति कर्हिचित्।।२०
en: Then Prana appeared, once more fostering Word. Hence, Word, encountering deep exhalation, never utters anything.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: घोषिणी जातनिर्घोषा नित्यमेव प्रवर्तते। तयोरपि च घोषिण्या निर्घोषैव गरीयसी॥
en: Word always comes as endued with ulterance or unendued with it. Amongst those two. Word without utterance is superior to Word with utterance.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: गौरिव प्रसवत्यर्थान् रसमुत्तमशालिनी। सततं स्यन्दते ह्येषा शाश्वतं ब्रह्मवादिनी॥
en: Like a cow having milk, she yields various kinds of ineaning. This one always gives the Eternal (viz., Emancipation), speaking of Brahma.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: दिव्यादिव्यप्रभावेन भारती गौः शुचिस्मिते। एतयोरन्तरं पश्य सूक्ष्मयोः स्यन्दमानयो॥
en: O you of beautiful smiles, Word is a cow, on account of her power which is both divine and not divine. See the distinction of these two subtle forms of Word that flow.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: ब्राह्मण्युवाच अनुत्पन्नेषु वाक्येषु चोद्यमाना विवक्षया। किनु पूर्वं तदा देवी व्याजहार सरस्वती॥
en: What did the goddess of Word then say, formerly when, though moved by the wish to speak, speech could not come out?

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच प्राणेन या सम्भवते शरीरे प्राणादपानं प्रतिपद्यते च। उदानभूता च विसृज्य देहं व्यानेन सर्वं दिवमावृणोति॥
en: The Brahmana said The Word that is made in the body by Prana, then attains to Apana from Prana. Then changed into Udana and coming out of the body, it covers all the quarters, with Vyana.

description: The ten Hotris and two Minds
sn: ततः समाने प्रतितिष्ठतीह इत्येव पूर्वं प्रजजल्प वाणी। तस्मान्मनः स्थावरत्वाद् विशिष्टं तथा देवी जङ्गमत्वाद् विशिष्टा॥
en: After that, she lives in Samana. Even thus did Word formerly speak. Hence Mind, on account of being immovable, is distinguished, and the goddess Word, on account of being movable, is also distinguished.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। सुभगे सप्तहोतॄणां विधानमिह यादृशम्॥
en: The Brahmana said Regarding it is cited the ancient story, O blessed one, of what the institution is of the seven sacrificing priests.

sn: घ्राणश्चक्षुश्च जिह्वा च त्वक् श्रोत्रं चैव पञ्चमम्। मनो बुद्धिश्च सप्तैते होतारः पृथगाश्रिताः॥
en: The nose, the eye, the tongue, the skin, and the ear numbering the fifth, the mind, and the understanding, these are the seven sacrificing priests standing distinctly from one another.

sn: सूक्ष्मेऽवकाशे तिष्ठन्तो न पश्यन्तीतरेतरम्। एतान् वै सप्तहोतूंस्त्व स्वभावाद् विद्धि शोभने॥
en: Living in subtle space, they do not perceive one another. Do you, O beautiful one, know these sacrificing priests that are scven by their nature.

sn: ब्राह्मण्युवाच सूक्ष्मेऽवकाशे सन्तस्ते कथं नान्योन्यदर्शिनः। कथंस्वभावा भगवन्नेतदाचक्ष्व मे प्रभो॥
en: The Brahmana's wife said How is it that living in subtle space, these do not perceive one another? What are their (respective) natures, O holy one? Do you tell me this,Olord.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच गुणाज्ञानमविज्ञानं गुणज्ञानमभिज्ञता। परस्परं गुणानेते नाभिजानन्ति कर्हिचित्॥
en: Not knowing the qualities is ignorance; while knowledge of the qualities is knowledge. These seven never succeed in apprehending or knowing the qualitics of one another.

sn: जिह्वा चक्षुस्तथा श्रोत्रं वाङ्मनो बुद्धिरेव च। न गन्धानधिगच्छन्ति घ्राणस्तानधिगच्छति॥
en: The tongue, the eye, the ear too, the skin, the mind, and the understanding, do not succeed in apprehending smells. It is the nose alone which apprehends them.

sn: ध्राणं चक्षुस्तथा श्रोत्रं वाङ्मनो बुद्धिरेव च। न रसानधिगच्छन्ति जिह्वा तानधिगच्छति॥
en: The nose, the eye, the ear too, the skin, the mind, and the understanding, never succeed in apprehending tastes. The tonguc alone apprehends them. never

sn: घ्राण जिह्वा तथा श्रोत्रं वाङ्मनो बुद्धिरेव च। न रूपाण्यधिगच्छन्ति चक्षुस्तान्यधिगच्छति॥
en: The nose, the tongue. the ear also, the skin, the mind and the understanding, never succeed in apprehending colours. It is the eye alone which apprchends them.

sn: घ्राण जिह्वा ततश्चक्षुः श्रोत्रं बुद्धिर्मनस्तथा। न स्पर्शानधिगच्छन्ति त्वक् च तानधिगच्छति॥
en: The nose, the tongue, the eye too, the ear, the understanding, and the mind, succeed in apprehending sensations of touch. It is the skin alone that apprehends them.

sn: घ्राण जिह्वा च चक्षुश्च वाङ्मनो बुद्धिरेव च। न शब्दानधिगच्छन्ति श्रोत्रं तानधिगच्छति॥
en: The nose, the tongue, the eye, the skin, the mind, and the understanding, never succeed in apprehending sounds. It is the ear alone which apprehends them.

sn: घ्राण जिह्वा च चक्षुश्च त्वक् श्रोत्रं बुद्धिरेव च। संशयं नाधिगच्छन्ति मनस्नमधिगच्छति॥
en: The nose, the tongue, the cye, the skin, the car, and the understanding, never succeed in apprchending doubt. It is the mind which apprehends it.

sn: घ्राण जिह्वा च चक्षुश्च त्वक् श्रोत्रं मन एव च। न निष्ठामधिगच्छन्ति बुद्धिस्तामधिगच्छति॥
en: The nose, the tongue, the eye, the skin, the ear, and the mind, succeed in apprehending determination. It is the understanding alone which apprehends it.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। इन्द्रियाणां च संवादं मनसश्चैव भामिनि॥
en: Regarding it is cited, O beautiful lady, this ancient discourse between the senses and the mind. never

sn: मन उवाच नाघ्राति मामृते घ्राणं रसं जिह्वा न वेत्ति च। रूपं चक्षुर्न गृह्णाति त्वक् स्पर्श नावबुध्यते॥ न श्रोत्रं बुध्यते शब्दं मया हीनं कथंचन। प्रवरं सर्वभूतानामहमस्मि सनातनम्॥
en: The Mind said The nose does not smell without me. (Without me) the tongue does not apprchend taste. the eye does not perceive colour, the skin does not feel touchi, the car does not apprehend sound, when deprived of me. I am the eternal and foremost one among all the elements.

sn: अगाराणीव शून्यानि शान्तार्चिष इवाग्नयः। इन्द्रियाणि न भासन्ते मया होनानि नित्यशः॥
en: It always occurs that without inyself, the senses never shine, like habitations cmpty of inmates or fires whose flames have been quenched.

sn: काष्ठानीवाशुष्काणि यतमानैरपीन्द्रियैः। गुणार्थान् नाधिगच्छन्ति मामृते सर्वजन्तवः॥
en: Without me, all creatures cannot apprehend qualities and objects, with even the senses exerting themselves, as fuel that is wet and dry cannot catch fire.

sn: एवमेतद् भवेत् सत्यं यथैतन्मन्यते भवान्। ऋतेऽस्मानस्मादर्थोस्त्वं भोगान् भुङ्क्ते भवान् यदि।।
en: Hearing these words, the Senses said, This what you think would be true, if, you could enjoy pleasures without either ourselves or our objccts.

sn: यद्यस्मासु प्रलीनेषु तर्पणं प्राणधारणम्। भोगान् भुडक्ते भवान् सत्यं यथैतन्मन्यते तथा॥ अथवास्मासु लीनेषु तिष्ठत्सु विषयेषु च। यदि संकल्पमात्रेण भुङ्क्ते भोगान् यथार्थवत्॥
en: If, when we are no more, there be gratification and support of life, and a continuation of your enjoyments, then what you think would be true; or, if, when we are absorbed and objects are existing, you can't have your enjoyments by your desire alone, as truly as you have them with our help.

sn: अथ चेन्मन्यसे सिद्धिमस्मदर्थेषु नित्यदा। घ्राणेन रूपमादत्स्व रसमादत्स्व चक्षुषा॥
en: If, again, you consider your power over our objects to be always complete, do you then seize colour by the nose, and taste by the eye.

sn: श्रोत्रेण गधनादत्स्व स्पर्शानादत्स्व जिह्वया। त्वचा च शब्दमादत्स्व बुद्ध्या स्पर्शमथापि च॥
en: Do you also take smells by the car, and sensations of touch by the tongue. Do you also take sounds by the skin, and like wise touch by the understanding.

sn: बलवन्तो ह्यनियमा नियमा दुर्बलीयसाम्। भोगानपूर्वानादत्स्व नोच्छिष्टं भोक्तुमर्हति॥
en: The powerful do not acknowledge the control of any rules. Rulcs cxist only for the weak. Do you seize enjoyments unenjoyed before; you should not enjoy what has been tasted before (by others).

sn: यथा हि शिष्यः शास्तारं श्रुत्यर्थमभिधावति। ततः श्रुतमुपादाय श्रुत्यर्थमुपतिष्ठति॥ विषयानेवमस्माभिर्दर्शितानभिमन्यसे) अनागनानतीतांश्च स्वप्ने जागरणे तथा॥
en: As a disciple goes to a preceptor for the sake of the Shrutis, and then, having acquired the Shrutis, lives on their meaning, so do you regard as yours those objects which are shown by us, past or future, in sleep or in wakefulness.

sn: वैमनस्यं गतानां च जन्तूनामल्पचेतसाम्। अस्मदर्थे कृते कार्ये दृश्यते प्राणधारणम्॥
en: Of creatures, again, who have lillle intelligence, when their mind becomes distracted and checrless, life is seen to be upheld upon our objects discharging their functions.

sn: बहूनपि हि संकल्पान् मत्वा स्वजानुपास्य च। बुभुक्षया पीड्यमानो विषयानेव धावति॥
en: It is seen also that a creature, after having made many purposes and indulged in dreams, when afflicted by the desire to enjoy, runs to objects of sense alone.

sn: अगारमद्वारमिव प्रविश्य संकल्पभोगान् विषये निबद्धान्। प्राणक्षये शान्तिमुपैति नित्यं दारुक्षयेऽग्निलितो यथैव॥
en: One entering upon enjoyments depending on purposes alone and unconnected with actual objects of sense, always meets with death upon the exhaustion of the vital airs, like an enkindled fore upon the exhaustion of fuel.

sn: कामं तु नः स्वेषु गुणेषु सङ्गः कामं च नान्योन्यगुणोपलब्धिः। अस्मान् विना नास्ति तवोपलब्धि स्तावदृते त्वां न भजेत् प्रहर्षः॥
en: True it is that we have connections with our respectivc attributes; true it is, we have no knowledge of one anther's attributes. But without us you can have no perception. Without us no happiness can come to you. objects of sense, always meets with death upon the exhaustion of the vital airs, like an enkindled fore upon the exhaustion of fuel.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। सुभगे पञ्चहोतृणां विधानमिह यादृशम्॥
en: The Brahmana said Regarding it, О blessed lady, is cited the ancient story of what kind the institution is of the five sacrificing priests.

sn: प्राणापानावुदानश्च समानो व्यान एव च। पञ्चहोतूंस्तथैतान् वै परं भावं विदुर्बुधाः॥
en: The learned know this to be a great principle that Prana and Apana and Udana and Şamana and Vyana are the five sacrificing priests.

sn: ब्राह्मण्युवाच स्वभावात् सप्तहोतार इति मे पूर्विका मतिः। यथा वै पञ्चहोतारः परो भावस्तदुच्यताम्॥
en: The Brahmana's wife said I naturally believed that there are seven sacrificing priests. Let the great principle be declared to me as to how, indeed, the number is five of the sacrificing priests.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच प्राणेन सम्भृतो वायुरपानो जायते ततः। अपाने सम्भृते वायुस्ततो व्यानः प्रवर्तते॥
en: The Brahmana said The wind nursed y Prana afterwards takes birth in Apana. The wind nursed in Apana then becomes developed into Vyana.

sn: व्यानेन सम्भृतो वायुस्ततोदानः प्रवर्तते। उदाने सम्भृतो वायुः समानो नाम जायते॥
en: Nursed by Vyana, the wind is then developed into Udana. Nursed in Udana, the wind is then generated as Samana.

sn: तेऽपृच्छन्त पुरा सन्तः पूर्वजातं पितामहम्। यो नः श्रेष्ठस्तमाचक्ष्व स नः श्रेष्ठो भविष्यतिः॥
en: Those good beings formerly asked the first born Grandfather, saying, Do you say who amongst us is the foremost. He alone will be our chief.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच यस्मिन् प्रलीने प्रलयं व्रजन्ति सर्वे प्राणाः प्राणभृतां शरीरे। यस्मिन् प्रचीर्णे च पुनश्चरन्ति स वै श्रेष्ठो गच्छत यत्र कामः॥
en: Brahman said He upon whose extinction all the vital airs become extinct in the bodies of living creatures, he upon whose moving they move, is, indeed, the foremost. Do you go where you like.

sn: प्राण उवाच मयि प्रलीने प्रलयं व्रजन्ति सर्वे प्राणाः प्राणभृतां शरीरे। मयि प्रचीर्णे च पुनश्चरन्ति श्रेष्ठो ह्यहं पश्यत मां प्रलीनम्॥
en: Prana said Upon my extinction all the vital airs become extinct in the bodies of living creatures. Upon my moving they once more move. I am the foremost. Sce, I go into extinction.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच प्राणः प्रालीयत तत: पुनश्च प्रचचार ह। समानश्चाप्युदानश्च वचोऽव्रतां पुनः शुभे॥ न त्वं सर्वमिदं व्याप्य तिष्ठसीह यथा वयम्। न त्वं श्रेष्ठो हि नः प्राण अपानो हि वशे तव। प्रचचार पुनः प्राणस्तमपानोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: The Brahniana said Prana then became extinct and once more moved about. Then Saman and Udana also, O blessed one, said these words, You do not live here, pervading all this, as we do. You are not the foremost amongst us, O Prana! (Only) Apana is under your dominion! Prana then moved about, and to him Apana spoke.

sn: अपान उवाच पयि प्रलीने प्रलयं व्रजन्ति सर्वे प्राणाः प्राणभृतां शरीरे। मयि प्रचीर्णे च पुनश्चरन्ति श्रेष्ठो ह्यहं पश्यत मां प्रलीनम्॥
en: When I become extinct, all the vital airs become extinct in the bodies of living creatures. When I move about, they again move about. I am, therefore, the foremost, See, I go into extinction.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच व्यानश्च तमुदानश्च भाषमाणमथोचतुः। अपान न त्वं श्रेष्ठोऽसि प्राणो हि वशगस्तव॥
en: The Brahmana said To Apana who said so, both Vyana and Udana said, O Apana, you are not the foremost (Only) Prana is under your dominion.

sn: अपानः प्रचचाराथ व्यानस्तं पुनरब्रवीत्। श्रेष्ठोऽहमस्मि सर्वेषां श्रूयतां येन हेतुना॥
en: Then Apana began to move about, Vyana once more addressed him, saying I am the foremost of all. Listen, for what reason.

sn: मयि प्रलीने प्रलयं व्रजन्ति सर्वे प्राणाः प्राणभृतां शरीरे। मयि प्रचीर्णे च पुनश्चरन्ति श्रेष्ठो ह्यहं पश्यत मां प्रलीनम्॥
en: When I become extinct, all the vital airs become extinct in the bodies of living creatures. When I move about, they once more move about. I am (therefore) the foremost. Sce, I go into extinction.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच प्रालीयत ततो व्यान: पुनश्च प्रचचार ह। प्राणापानावुदानश्च समानश्च तमब्रुवन्। न त्वं श्रेष्ठोऽसि नो व्यान समानस्तु वशे तव॥ प्रचचार पुनर्व्यानः समानः पुनरब्रवीत्। श्रेष्ठोऽहमस्मि सर्वेषां श्रूयतां येन हेतुना॥ मयि प्रलीने प्रलयं व्रजन्ति सर्वे प्राणाः प्राणभृतां शरीरे। मयि प्रचीर्णे च पुनश्चरन्ति श्रेष्ठो ह्यहं पश्यत मां प्रलीनम्॥
en: Then Vyana became extinct and once more began to move about. At this, Prana and Apana and Udana and Samana Addressed him, saying. You are not the foremost among us, O Vyana! (Only) Samana is under your dominion. Vyana then began to move about and Saman said to him, I am the foremost of you all! Listen, for what reason. When I become extinct, all the vital airs become extinct in the bodies of living creatures. When I begin to move about, they once more move about. Hence, I am the forcmost. See, I become extinct.

sn: समानः प्रचचाराथ उदानस्तमुवाच ह। श्रेष्ठाऽहमस्मि सर्वेषां श्रूयतां येन हेतुना॥
en: Then Samana began to inovc about. To him Udana said, I am the foremost of all the vital airs. Listen, for what reason.

sn: मयि प्रलीने प्रलयं व्रजन्ति सर्वे प्राणा: प्राणभृतां शरीरे। मयि प्रचीर्णे च पुनश्चरन्ति श्रेष्ठो ह्यहं पश्यत मां प्रलीनम्॥
en: When I become extinct, all the vital airs become extinct in the bodies of living creatures. When I move about they once more move about. Hence, I am the foremost. Behold I become extinct.

sn: ततः प्रालीयतोदान: पुनश्च प्रचचार ह। प्राणापानौ समानश्च व्यानश्चैव तमब्रुवन्।। उदान न त्वं श्रेष्ठोऽसि व्यान एव वशे तव।॥
en: Then Udana, after having become extinct, began to once more move about. Prana and Apana and Samana and Vyana said to him, O Udana, you are not the foremost one among us. (Only) Vyana is under your dominion.

sn: व्राह्मण उवाच ततस्तानब्रवीद् ब्रह्मा समवेतान् प्रजापतिः। सर्वे श्रेष्ठा न वा श्रेष्ठाः सर्वे चान्योन्यधर्मिणः॥
en: The Brahmana said To them assembled together, the Lord of creatures, Brahman, said, You are all foremost and not foremost. You are all gified with the attributes of one another.

sn: सर्वे स्वविषये श्रेष्ठाः सर्वे चान्योन्यधर्मिणः। इति तानब्रवीत् सर्वान् समवेतान् प्रजापति॥
en: All are foremost in their own spheres, and all possess the attributes of one another! The Lord of all creatures, thus said to them, that were assembled together.

sn: एकः स्थिरश्चास्थिरश्च विशेषात् पञ्च वायवः। एक एव ममैवात्मा बहुधाप्युपचीयते॥
en: There is one that is unmoving, and one that is moving. On account of special attributes, there are five vital airs. My own self is one. That one accumulates into many forms.

sn: परस्परस्य सुहृदो भावयन्तः परस्परम्। स्वस्ति ब्रजत भद्रं वो धारयध्वं परस्परम्॥
en: Becoming friendly to one another, and pleasing one another, depart in depart in peace. Blessings to you, do you up hold one another.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। नातदस्य च संवादमृर्देवमतस्य च॥
en: The Brahmana said Regarding it is cited the ancient discourse between Narada and the Rishi Devamata.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: देवमत उवाच जन्तोः संजायमानर्थं किं नु पूर्वं प्रवर्तते। प्राणोऽपान: समानो वा व्यानो वोदान एव च।॥
en: Devamata said What, indeed, comes first into existence, of a creature that takes birth? Is it Prana, or Apana, or Samana, or Vyana, or Udana?

description: The first creation in a creature born
