sn: नारद उवाच येनायं सृज्यते जन्तुस्ततोऽन्यः पूर्वमेति तम्। प्राणद्वन्द्वं हि विज्ञेयं तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्च यत्॥
en: Narada said By whatever the creature is created, that first comes to him which is other. The vital airs are to be known as existing in pairs, viz., those which move transversely, upwards, and downwards.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: देवमत उवाच केनायं सृज्यते जन्तुः कश्चान्यः पूर्वमेति तम्। प्राणद्वन्द्वं च मे ब्रूहि तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्च यत्॥
en: Devamata said-By whom is a creature produced? Who (amongst) them comes first? Tell me what the pairs are of the vital airs, which move transversely, upwards, and downwards.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: नारद उवाच संकल्पाज्जायते हर्षः शब्दादपि च जायते। रसात् संजायते चापि रूपादपि च जायते॥
en: Narada said-From wish originates Pleasure. It also arise from sound. It arises also from taste; it arises too from colour.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: शुक्राच्छोणितसंसृष्टात् पूर्वं प्राणः प्रवर्तते। प्राणेन विकृते शुक्ते ततोऽपानः प्रवर्तते॥
en: From the semen, united with blood, first originates Prana. Upon the semen being modified by Prana, flows Apana.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: शुक्रात् संजायते चापि रसादपि च जायते। एतद् रूपमुदानस्य हर्षो मिथुनमन्तरा॥
en: Pleasure originates from the semen as well. It arises from taste also. This is the form (effect) of Udana. Pleasure is produced from union.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: कामात् संजायते शुक्रं शुक्रात् संजायते रजः। समानव्यानजनिते सामान्ये शुक्रशोणिते॥ प्राणापानाविदं द्वन्द्वमवाक् चोर्ध्वं च गच्छतः। व्यान: समानश्चैवोभौ तिर्यग् द्वन्द्वत्वमुच्यते॥
en: Semen is formed by desire. From desire is produced the menstrual flow. In the union of semen and blood, generated by Samana and Vyana, the pair that consists of Prana and Apana, enters, moving transversely and upwards. Vyana and Samana both form a pair which move transversely.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: अग्नि देवताः सर्वा इति देवस्य शासनम्। संजायते ब्राह्मणस्य ज्ञानं बुद्धिसमन्वितम्॥
en: Agni (fire) is all the celestials. This is the teaching of the Veda, The knowledge of Agni arises in a Brahmana, with intelligence,

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: तस्य धूमस्तमो रूपं रजो भस्मसु तेजसः। सर्वं संजायते तस्य यत्र प्रक्षिप्यते हविः॥
en: The smoke of that firc is of the form of Darkness. The quality that is known by the name of Passion is in it ashes. The quality of goodness originate from that portion of the fire into which the oblation is poured.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: सत्त्वात् समानो व्यानश्च इति यज्ञविदो विदुः। प्राणापानावाज्यभागौ तयोर्मध्ये हुताशनः॥
en: They who are conversant with sacrifices know that Samana and Vyana are from the quality of Goodness, Prana and Apana are portions of the oblation (of clarified butter). Between them is the Fire.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: एतद् रूपमुदानस्य परमं ब्राह्मणा विदुः। निर्द्वन्द्वमिति यत् त्वेतत् तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: That is the excellent form (or seat) of Udana, as the Brahmanas know. Listen as I say which is distinct from the pairs.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: अहोरात्रमिदं द्वन्द्वं तयोर्मध्ये हुताशनः। एतद् रूपमुदानस्य परमं ब्राह्मणा विदुः॥
en: Day and Night form a pair, Between them is the Fire. That is the cxcellent seat of Udana as the Brahinanas know.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: सच्चासच्चैव तद् द्वन्द्वं तयोर्मध्ये हुताशनः। एतद् रूपमुदानस्य परमं ब्राह्मणा विदुः॥
en: The existent and the non-existent form a pair. Between them is the Fire. That is the excellent scat of Udana as the Brahmanas know.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: ऊर्ध्वं समानो व्यानश्च व्यस्यते कर्म तेन तत्। तृतीयं तु समानेन पुनरेव व्यवस्यते॥
en: First is Saman. Then Vyana. The latter's function is managed through it (viz., Samana). Then, secondly, Samans, once more comes to work.

description: The first creation in a creature born
sn: शान्त्यर्थं व्यानमेकं च शान्तिर्ब्रह्म सनातनम्। एतद् रूपमुदानस्य परमं ब्राह्मणा विदुः॥
en: Only Vyana exists for tranquility. Tranquillity is eternal Brahma. This is the excellent scat of Udana as the Brahinanas know.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। चातुर्होत्रविधानस्य विधानमिह यादृशम्॥
en: The Brahmana said Regarding it is recited the ancient story of what the institution is of the Chaturhotra (sacrifice).

sn: तस्य सर्वस्य विधिवद् विधानमुपदिश्यते। शृणु मे गदतो भद्रे रहस्यमिदमद्भुतम्॥
en: The ordinances are now being duly declared in full. Listen to me, O fair lady, as I describe this wonderful mystery.

sn: करणं कर्म कर्ता च मोक्ष इत्येव भाविनि। चत्वार एते होतारो यैरिदं जगदावृतम्॥
en: The instrument, the action, the agent and liberation. These, O beautiful lady, are the four sacrificing pricsts by whom the universe is covered.

sn: हेतूनां साधनं चैव शृणु सर्वमशेषतः घ्राणं जिह्वा च चक्षुश्च त्वक् च श्रोत्रं च पञ्चमम्। मनो बुद्धिश्च सप्तैते विज्ञेया गुणहेतवः॥ गन्धो रसच रूपं च शब्दः स्पर्शश्च पञ्चमः। मन्तव्यमथ बोद्धव्यं सप्तैते कर्महेतवः॥ घ्राता भक्षयिता द्रष्टा वक्ता श्रोता च पञ्चमः। मन्ता बोद्धा च सप्तैते विज्ञेयाः कर्तृहेतवः॥ स्वगुणं भक्षयन्त्येते गुणवन्तः शुभाशुभम्।
en: Hear fully of causes. The noise, the tongue, the eye, the skin, the ear for the fifth, the mind and the understanding, these seven should be understood as the causes of qualities. Smell, taste, colour, sound, touch, numbering the fifth, the objects of the mind, and the objects of the understanding, these are the seven causes of action. He who smells, he who eats, he who sees, he who speaks, he who hears, numbering the lifth, he who thinks, and he who understands, these seven should be known as the causes of action. Endued with qualitics, these enjoy their own qualities, agrecable or disagrecable.

sn: अहं च निर्गुणोऽनन्तः सप्तैते मोक्षहेतवः॥ विदुषां बुध्यमानानां स्वं स्वं स्थानं यथाविधि। गुणास्ते देवताभूताः सततं भुञ्जते हविः॥ अदन्नन्नान्यथोऽविद्वान् ममत्वेनोपपद्यते।
en: As regards the soul, that is destitute of qualities. These seven are the causes of Liberation. With them who are learned and gifted with sufficient understanding, the qualities, which are in the position of celestials, eat the oblations, each in its proper place, and according to what has been ordained. The person who is shorn of learning, eating various kinds of food, becomes seized with the sense of egoism.

sn: आत्मार्थं पाचयन्ननं ममत्वेनोपहन्यते॥ अभक्ष्यभक्षणं चैव मद्यपानं च हन्ति तम्।
en: Digesting food for himself, he becomes ruined through the sense of egoism. The cating of food that should not be caten and the drinking of wine, ruin him.

sn: स चानं हन्ति तं चान्नं स हत्वा हन्यते पुनः॥ हन्ता ह्यन्नमिदं विद्वान् पुनर्जनयतीश्वरः।
en: He destroys the food (lic takes), and having destroyed that food he becomes destroyed himself. The learned man, however, giſted with power, destroys his food for reproducing it.

sn: न चान्नाज्जायते तस्मिन् सूक्ष्मो नाम व्यतिक्रमः॥ मनसा गम्यते यच्च यच्च वाचा निगद्यते। श्रोत्रेण श्रूयते यच्च चक्षुषा यच्च दृश्यते॥ स्पर्शेन स्पृश्यते यच्च घ्राणेन घ्रायते च यत्। मनःषष्ठानि संयम्य हवींष्येतानि सर्वशः॥ गुणवत्पावको मह्यं दीव्यतेऽत:शरीरगः।
en: The minutest sin does not arise in him from the food he takes. Whatever is thought of by the mind, whatever is uttered by words, whatever is heard by the ear, whatever is seen by the eye, whatever is touched by touch, whatever is smelt by the nosc, form oblations of clarified butter which should all, after controlling the senses with the mind numbering the sixth, be poured into that fire of high merits which burns within the body viz., the Soul.

sn: योगयज्ञः प्रवृत्ते मे ज्ञानवह्निप्रदोद्भवः। प्राणस्तोत्रोऽपानशस्त्रः सर्वत्यागसुदक्षिणः॥
en: The sacrifices formed by Yoga is going on as regards myself. The spring whence that sacrifice proceeds is that which gives the fire of knowledge. The upward vital air Prana is the Stotra of that sacrifice. The downward vital air Apana is its Shastra. The renunciation of everything is the excellent present of that sacrifice.

sn: कर्तानुमन्ता ब्रह्मात्मा होताध्वर्युः कृतस्तुतिः। ऋतं प्रशास्ता तच्छस्त्रमपवर्गोऽस्य दक्षिणा॥
en: Consciousness, Mind, and Understanding, which are all Brahma, are its Hotri, Adhvaryu, and Udgatri. The Prashastri, his Shastra, is truth. Cessation of separate existence (or Emancipation) is the Honorarium.

sn: ऋचश्चाप्यत्र शंसन्ति नारायणविदो जनाः। नारायणाय देवाय यदविन्दन् पशून् पुरा॥
en: People conversant with Narayana, recite some Richs on this subject. Formerly animals were offered to the divine Narayana.

sn: तत्र सामानि गायन्ति तत्र चाहुर्निदर्शनम्। देवं नारायणं भीरु सर्वात्मानं निबोध तम्॥
en: Then are sung some Samans. There is an authority on this subject. O timid one, know that the divine Narayana is the Soul of all.

sn: ऋचश्चाप्यत्र शंसन्ति नारायणविदो जनाः। नारायणाय देवाय यदविन्दन् पशून् पुरा॥
en: People conversant with Narayana, recite some Richs on this subject. Formerly animals were offered to the divine Narayana.

sn: तत्र सामानि गायन्ति तत्र चाहुर्निदर्शनम्। देवं नारायणं भीरु सर्वात्मानं निबोध तम्॥
en: Then are sung some Samans. There is an authority on this subject. O timid one, know that the divine Narayana is the Soul of all.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच एकः शास्ता न द्वितीयोऽस्ति शास्ता यो हृच्छयस्तमहमनुब्रवीमि। तेनैव युक्तः प्रवणादिवोदकं यथानियुक्तोऽस्मि तथा वहामि।।।।
en: The Brahmana said There is one Ruler. There is no second beside him. He who is Ruler lives in the heart. I shall speak now of him. Moved by Him, I move as directed like water along an inclined plane.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: एको गुरुर्नास्ति ततो द्वितीयो। यो हृच्छयस्तमहमनुब्रवीमि। तेनानुशिष्टा गुरुणा सदैव लोके द्विष्टाः पन्नगा: सर्व एव॥
en: There is one Preceptor. There is no second but him. He lives in the heart, and of him I shall now speak. Instructed by that preceptor, all snakes in the world are always possessed of feelings of enimity.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: एको बन्धुर्नास्ति ततो द्वितीयो यो हृच्छयस्तमहमनुब्रवीमि। तेनानुशिष्टा बान्धवा बन्धुमन्तः सप्तर्षयश्चैव दिवि प्रभान्ति॥
en: There is one kinsman. There is no second except him. He lives in the heart of him I shall now speak. Instructed by him, kinsmen become possessed of kinsmen, and the seven Rishis, O son of Pritha, shine in the sky.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: एक: श्रोता नास्ति ततो द्वितीयो यो हृच्छयस्तमहमनुब्रवीमि। तस्मिन् गुरौ गुरुवासं निरुष्य शक्रो गतः सर्वलोकामरत्वम्॥
en: There is one dispeller. There is no second but him. He lives in the heart. Of him I shall now speak. Having lived with that instructor, under the proper mode of living with an instructor, Shakra gained the sovereignty of all the worlds.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: एको द्वेष्टा नास्ति ततो द्वितीयो यो हृच्छयस्तमहमनुब्रवीमि। तेनानुशिष्टा गुरुणा सदैव लोके द्विष्टाः पन्नगाः सर्व एव॥
en: There is one enemy. There is no second but him. He lives in the heart. Of him I shall now speak. Instructed by that preceptor all snakes in the world are always possessed of feelings of enmity.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। प्रजापतौ पन्नगानां देवर्षीणां च संविदम्॥
en: Regarding it is cited the ancient story of the instruction of the snakes, the celestials, and the Rishis by the Lord of all creatures.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: देवर्षयश्च नागाश्चाप्यसुराश्च प्रजापतिम्। पर्यपृच्छन्नुपासीनाः श्रेयो नः प्रोच्यतामिति॥ तेषां प्रोवाच भगवाश्रेयः समनुपृच्छताम्। ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म ते श्रुत्वा प्राद्रवन् दिशः॥
en: The celestials and the Rishis, the snakes and the Asuras, seated around the Lord of all creatures, asked him, saying, Let that which is highly beneficial for us be said. To them who enquired about what is highly beneficial, the holy one uttered only the word Om, which is Brahma is one syllable. Hearing this, they ran away in various directions.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: तेषां प्रद्रवमाणानामुपदेशार्थमात्मनः। सर्याणां दंशने भावः प्रवृत्तः पूर्वमेव तु॥
en: Amongst them that thus ran in all directions from desire of sclf-instruction, the tendency for biting first arose in snakes.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: असुराणां प्रवृत्तस्तु दम्भभावः स्वभावजः। दानं देवा व्यवसिता दममेव महर्षयः॥
en: The tendency for ostentatious pride first arose in the Asuras. The celestials betook themselves to gifts, and the great Rishis to selfcontrol.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: एकं शास्तारमासाद्य शब्देनैकेन संस्कृताः। नाना व्यवसिताः सर्वे सर्पदेवर्पिदानवाः॥
en: Having gone to one tcacher, and having been instructed (refined) by one word, the snakes, the celestials, the Rishis, and the Danavas, all betook themselves to various different dispositions.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: शृणोत्ययं प्रोच्यमानं गृह्णाति च यथातथम्। पृच्छतस्तदतो भूयो गुरुरन्यो न विद्यते॥
en: It is that one who hears himself when speaking, and understands it duly. Once, again, is that heard from him when he speaks. There is no second preceptor.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: तस्य चानुमते कर्म ततः पश्चात् प्रवर्तते। गुरुर्बोद्धा च श्रोता च द्वेष्टा च हृदि निःसृतः॥
en: It is in obedience to his advice that action afterwards originates. The instructor, the apprehender, the hearer, and the enemy, are placed within the heart,

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: पापेन विचरल्लौके पापचारी भवत्ययम्। शुभेन विचरल्लौके शुभचारी भवत्युत॥
en: By acting sinfully in the world, it is he who becomes a person of sinful deeds. By acting auspiciously in the world, in is he who becomes a person of auspicious deeds.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: कामचारी तु कामेन य इन्द्रियसुखे रतः। ब्रह्मचारी सदैवैष य इन्द्रियजये रतः॥
en: It is he who becomes a person of controlled conduct by becoming addicted to the pleasures of sense, moved by desire. It is he who becomes a Brahmacharin by always devoting himself to the control of his senses.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: अपेतव्रतकर्मा तु केवलं ब्रह्मणि स्थितः। ब्रह्मभूतश्चरँल्लोके ब्रह्मचारी भवत्ययम्॥
en: It is he, again, who castes off vows and actions and takes refuge on Brahma alone. By moving in the world, identifying himself the while with Brahima, he becomes a Brahmacharin.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: ब्रह्मैव समिधस्तस्य ब्रह्माग्निर्ब्रह्मसम्भवः। आपो ब्रह्म गुरुर्बह्म स ब्रह्मणि समाहितः॥
en: Brahma is his fuel; Brahma is his fire; Brahma is his origin; Brahma is his water; Brahma is his preceptor; he is immerged in Brahma.

description: Countries, Provinces, mountains and rivers most sanctificd
sn: एतदेवेदृशं सूक्ष्मं ब्रह्मचर्यं विदुर्बुधाः। विदित्वा चान्वपद्यन्त क्षेत्रज्ञेनानुदर्शिताः॥
en: Brahmacharya is so subtle, understood by the wise. Having understood it, they followed it, instructed by the Kshetrajna. even as

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच संकल्पदंशमशकं शोकहर्षहिमातपम्। मोहान्धकारतिमिरं लोभव्याधिसरीसृपम्॥ विषयैकात्ययाध्वानं कामक्रोधविरोधकम्। तदतीत्य महादुर्ग प्रविष्टोऽस्मि महद् वनम्॥
en: The Brahmana said Having crossed that impassable fortress (of the world) which has purposes for its gadflies and mosquitoes, grief and joy for its cold and heat, heedlessness for its blinding darkness, cupidity and diseases for its reptiles, wealth for its own danger on the road, and lust and anger its robbers. I have entered the extensive forest (of Brahma).

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: ब्राह्मण्युवाच क्व तद् वनं महाप्राज्ञ के वृक्षाः सरितश्च काः। गिरयः पर्वताश्चैव कियत्यध्वनि तद् वनम्॥
en: The wife of the Brahmana said Where is that foremost, O you of great wisdom? What are its trces? What are its rivers? What its mountains and hills? How far is that forest?

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच नैतदस्ति पृथग्भाव: किंचिदन्यत् ततः सुखम्। नैतदस्त्यपृथग्भावः किंचिद् दुःखतरं ततः॥
en: The Brahmana said There exists nothing that is separate from it. There is nothing more delightful than it. There is nothing that is un-separated from it. There is nothing more afflicting than it.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: तस्माद्धस्वतरं नास्ति न ततोऽस्ति महत्तरम्। नास्ति तस्मात् सूक्ष्मतरं नास्त्यन्यत् तत्समं सुखम्॥
en: There is nothing smaller than that. There is nothing huger than that. There is nothing minuter than that. There is no happiness that can resemble it.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: न तत्राविश्य शोचन्ति न प्रहष्यन्ति च द्विजाः। न च बिभ्यति केषांचित् तेभ्यो बिभ्यति केचन॥
en: Twice-born persons. entering into it, at once get over both joy and sorrow. They (then) never stand in fear of any creature, nor does any creature stand in fear of them.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: तस्मिन् वने सप्त यहादुमाश्च फलानि सप्तातिथयश्च सप्त। सप्ताश्रमाः सप्त समाधयश्च दीक्षाश्च सप्तैतदरण्यरूपम्।।७।
en: In that forest are seven large trees, seven fruits, and seven guests. There are seven hermitages, (forms of) Yoga concentration, and seven (forms) of initiation. This is a description of that forest.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: पञ्चवर्णानि दिव्यानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च। सृजन्तः पादपास्तत्र व्याप्य तिष्ठन्ति तद् वनम्॥
en: The trees which stand filling that forest yield excellent flowers and fruits of five colours. seven

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: सुवर्णानि द्विवर्णानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च। सृजन्तः पादपास्तत्र व्याप्य तिष्ठन्ति तद् वनम्॥
en: The trees which stand there filling that forest, yield flowers and fruits which are of excellent colours and which are, besides of two kinds.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: सुरभीणि द्विवर्णानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च। सृजन्तः पादपास्तत्र व्याप्य तिष्ठन्ति तद् वनम्॥
en: The trees which stand there filling that forest, yield flowers and fruits of two colours.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: सुरभीण्येकवर्णानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च। सृजन्तः पादपास्तत्र व्याप्य तिष्ठन्ति तद् वनम्॥
en: The trees which stand there filling that forest, yield fragrant flowers and fruits of one colour.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: बहून्यव्यक्तवर्णानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च। विसृजन्तौ महावृक्षौ तद् वनं व्याप्य तिष्ठतः॥
en: The two trces which stand filling that forest, produce many flowers and fruits which are of unmanifest colours.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: एको वह्निः सुमना ब्राह्मणोऽत्र पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि समिधश्चात्र सन्ति। तेभ्यो मोक्षाः सप्त फलन्ति दीक्षा गुणाः फलान्यतिथयः फलाशाः॥
en: There is one fire here, possessed of a good mind. That is connected with Brahmana. The five senses are the fuel here. The seven forms of Libcration originating from them are the seven forms of Initiation. The qualities are the fruits, and the guests eat those fruits.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: आतिथ्यं प्रतिगृह्णन्ति तत्र तत्र महर्षयः। अर्चितेषु प्रलीनेषु तेष्वन्यद् रोचते वनम्॥
en: There, in various places, the great Rishis accept hospitality. When they, having been adored become annihilated, then another forest shines forth.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: प्रज्ञाक्षं मोक्षफलं शान्तिच्छायासमन्वितम्। ज्ञानाश्रयं तृप्तितोयमन्तःक्षेत्रज्ञभास्करम्॥
en: In that forest, Intelligence is the tree; Liberation is the fruit. Tranquillity is the shade of which it is possessed. It has knowledge for its resting house, contentment for its water, and the Kshetrajna for its sun.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: येऽधिगच्छन्ति तं सन्त स्तेषां नास्ति भयं पुनः। ऊर्वे चाधश्च तिर्यक् च तस्य नान्तोऽधिगम्यते॥
en: Its end cannot be determined upwards, downwards, or horizontally.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: स्त्ववाङ्मुखा भानुमत्यो जनित्र्यः। अर्ध्वं रसानाददते प्रजाभ्यः। सर्वान् यथा सत्यमनित्यता च॥
en: Seven females always live there, with faces downwards, endued with effulgence, and the cause of generation. They take up all the different tastes from all creatures, cven as inconstancy sucks up truth.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: तत्रैव प्रतितिष्ठन्ति पुनस्तत्रोपयन्ति च। सप्त सप्तर्षयः सिद्धा वसिष्ठप्रमुखैः सह॥
en: In that itself live, and from that emerge, the seven Rishis who are crowned with ascetic success, having Vasishtha for their foremost.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: यशो वर्थो भगश्चैव विजयः सिद्धतेजसः। एवमेवानुवर्तन्ते सप्त ज्योतींषि भास्करम्॥
en: Glory, effulgence, greatness, enlightenment; victory, perfection, and energy, these seven always follow this same like rays following the sun.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: गिरयः पर्वताश्चैव सन्ति तत्र समासतः। नद्यश्च सरितो वारि वहन्त्यो ब्रह्मसम्भवम्॥
en: Hills and mountains also exist there, in a body; and rivers and steams carrying waters in their course, waters that are born of Brahma.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: नदीनां सङ्गमश्चैव वैताने समुपह्वरे। स्वात्मतृप्ता यतो यान्ति साक्षादेव पितामहम्॥
en: And there is a confluence also of rivers in the secluded spot for sacrifice. Thence those who are contented with their own souls proceed to the Grandfather.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: कृशाशाः सुव्रताशाश्च तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषा:। आत्मन्यात्मानमाविश्य ब्रह्माणं समुपासते॥
en: They whose wishes have been reduced, whose wishes have been directed to excellent vows, and whose sins have been consumed by penances, merging themselves in their souls, succeed in attain to Brahma.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: शममप्यत्र शंसन्ति विद्यारण्यविदो जनाः। तदारण्यमभिप्रेत्य यथाधीरभिजायत॥
en: Tranquillity is lauded by those who are conversant with the forest of knowledge. Keeping that forest in view, they take birth so as not to lose courage.

description: The extensive forest of Brahma described
sn: एतदेवेदृशं पुण्यमरण्यं ब्राह्मणा विदुः। विदित्वा चानुतिष्ठन्ति क्षेत्रज्ञेनानुदर्शिना॥
en: Such is that sacred forest that is understood by Brahmanas, and understanding it, they live as directed by the Kshetrajna.

sn: व्राह्मण उवाच गन्धान् न जिघ्रामि न वेधि रसान् रूपं न पश्यामि न च स्पृशामि। न चापि शब्दान् विविधाशृणोमि न चापि संकल्पमुपैमि कंचित्॥
en: I do not smell scents. I do not get tastes. I do not see colours. I do not likewise hear the various sounds Nor do I entertain purposes of any kind.

sn: अर्थानिष्टान् कामयते स्वभाव: सर्वान् द्वेष्यान् प्रद्विषते स्वभावः। कामद्वेषावुद्भवतः स्वभावात् प्राणापानौ जन्तुदेहान्निवेश्य॥
en: It is Nature which desires such objects as are liked; it is Nature which hates such objects as are disliked. Desire and hatred originate from Nature, like the upward and the downward vital airs when should have entered animate bodies.

sn: तेभ्यश्चान्यांस्तेषु नित्यांश्च भावान् भूतात्मानं लक्षयेरशरीरे। तस्मिस्तिष्ठन्नास्मि सक्तः कथंचित् कामक्रोधाभ्यां जरया मृत्युना च॥
en: Separated from them are others; in them are eternal dispositions; Yogins would see in the body, the soul of all creatures. Living in that, I am never attached to anything through desire and anger, and decrepitude and death.

sn: नविद्विषाणस्य च सर्वदोषान्। स्तोयस्य बिन्दोरिव पुष्करेषु।॥
en: Not having any desire for any object of desire, and not having any hatred for any evil, there is not taint on my natures, as there is not taint of a drop of water on the lotus.

sn: नित्यस्य चैतस्य भवन्ति नित्या निरीक्ष्यमाणस्य बहुस्वभावान्। न सज्जते कर्मसु भोगजालं दिवीव सूर्यस्य मयूखजालम्॥ अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। अध्वर्युयतिसंवादं तं निबोध यशस्विनि॥
en: Of this fixed (principle) which looks upon various natures, they are fickle possessions. Though actions are performed, yet the collection of enjoyments does not attach itself to them, as the collection of rays of the sun does not attach to the sky. Regarding it is recited an ancient discourse between an Adhvarya and a Yati. Do you hear it, O glorious lady.

sn: प्रोक्ष्यमाणं पशुं दृष्ट्वा यज्ञकर्मण्यथाब्रवीत्। यतिरध्वर्युमासीनो हिंसेयमिति कुत्सयन्॥
en: Seeing an animal sprinkled with water at a sacrifice, a Yati said to the Adhvaryu sealed there these word sin censure, This is destruction of life.

sn: तमध्वर्युः प्रत्युवाच नायं छागो विनश्यति। श्रेयसा योक्ष्यते जन्तुर्यदि श्रुतिरियं तथा॥
en: To him the Adhvaryu replied. This goat will not be destroyed. The animal meets with great good, if the Vedic declaration on this subject be true.

sn: यो ह्यस्य पार्थिवो भाग-पृथिवीं स गमिष्यति। यदस्य वारिज किंचिदपस्तत् सम्प्रवेक्ष्यति॥
en: That part of this animal which is of earth will go to earth. That part of this one which is of water, will enter into water.

sn: सूर्ये चक्षुर्दिशः श्रोत्रं प्राणोऽस्य दिवमेव च। आगमे वर्तमानस्य न मे दोषाऽस्ति कश्चन॥
en: His eye will enter the sun; his ear will enter the various points of the horizon; his vital airs will enter the sky. I who follow the scriptures commit no sin.

sn: यतिरुवाच प्राणैर्वियोगे च्छागस्य यदि श्रेयः प्रपश्यसि। छागार्थे वर्तते यज्ञो भवतः किं प्रयोजनम्॥
en: The Yati said-If you see such good to the goat in this dissociation with (his) vital airs, then this sacrifice is for the goat. What need have you for it?

sn: अत्र त्वा मन्यतां भ्राता पिता माता सखेति च। मन्त्रयस्वैनमुन्नीय परवन्तं विशेषतः॥
en: Let the brother, father, mother, and friend give you their approval in this. Taking him (to them) do you consult them. This goat is cspccially dependent.

sn: एवमेवानुमन्येरस्तान् भवान् द्रष्टुमर्हति। तेषामनुमतं श्रुत्वा शक्या कर्तुं विचारणा॥
en: You should see them who can givc their consent in this. After hcaring their consent, the matter will become a worthy topic for consideration.

sn: प्राणा अप्यस्य छागस्य प्रापितास्ते स्वयोनिपु। शरीरं केवल शिष्टं निश्चेष्टमिति मे मतिः॥
en: The vital airs of this goat have been made to return to their respective sources. Only the inanimate body remains behind. This is what I think.

sn: इन्धनस्य तु तुल्येन शरीरेण विचेतसा। हिंसानिर्वेष्टुकामानामिन्धनं पशुसंज्ञितम्॥
en: Of those who wish to enjoy pleasure by means of the inanimate body (of an animal) which can be compared with fuel, the fuel (of sacrifice) is after all the animal himself.

sn: अहिंसा सर्वधर्माणामिति वृद्धानुशासनम्। यदहिस्रं भवेत् कर्म तत् कार्यमिति विद्महे॥
en: Abstention from cruelty is the foremost of all duties. This is the teaching of the elders. We know that no crucl action should be donc.

sn: अहिंसेति प्रतिज्ञेयं यदि वक्ष्याम्यतः परम्। शक्यं बहुविधं कर्तुं भवता कार्यदूषणम्॥
en: This is the proposition, viz., No destruction (of living creatures-If I say anything further, then various kinds of faulty actions are capable of being done by you.

sn: अहिंसा सर्वभूतानां नित्यमस्मासु रोचते। प्रत्यक्षतः साधयामो न परोक्षमुपास्महे॥
en: Always abstaining from cruelty to all creatures is what is lauded. We establish this from what is directly perceptible. We do not rely on what is beyond direct perception.

sn: अध्वर्युरुवाच भूमेर्गन्धगुणान् भुंक्षे पिबस्यापोमयान् रसान्। ज्योतिषां पश्यसे रूपं स्पृशस्यनिलजान् गुणान्॥ शृणोष्याकाशजाशब्दान् मनसा मन्यसे मतिम्। सर्वाण्येतानि भूतानि प्राणा इति च मन्यसे॥
en: The Adhvaryu said You enjoy the properties of smell which belong to the earth. You drink the tastes which belong to water. You see colours which belong to luminous bodies. You touch the properties which originate from wind, you hear the sounds which originate from ether. You think thoughts with the mind. All these entities, you hold, have life.

sn: प्राणादाने निवृत्तोऽसि हिंसायां वर्तते भवान्। नास्ति चेष्टा विना हिंसां किं वा त्वं मन्यसे द्विज।।२१
en: You do not then abstain from taking life. Really, you are engaged in slaughter. There can be no movement without destruction. Or, what do you think. O twice-born one.

sn: यतिरुवाच अक्षरं च क्षरं चैव द्वैधीभावोऽयमात्मनः। अक्षरं तत्र सद्भावः स्वभावः क्षर उच्यते॥
en: The Indestructible and the Destructible form the twofold manifestation of the soul. Of these the Indestructible is existent. The Destructible is said to be exceedingly nonexistent.

sn: प्राणो जिह्वा मनः सत्त्वं सद्भावो रजसा सह। भावैरेतैर्विमुक्तस्य निर्द्वन्द्वस्य निराशिषः॥ समस्य सर्वभूतेषु निर्ममस्य जितात्मनः। समन्तात् परिमुक्तस्य न भयं विद्यते क्वचित्॥
en: The vital air, the tongue, the mind, the quality of goodness, along with the quality of passion, are all existent. Of him who is freed from these existent objects, who is above all pairs of opposites, who does not cherish any expectation, who is alike to all creatures, who is freed from the idea of mineness, who has governed his self, and who is released from all his surroundings, no fear cxists from any source.

sn: अध्वर्युरुवाच सद्भिरेवेह संवासः कार्यो मतिमतां वर। भवतो हि मतं श्रुत्वा प्रतिभाति मतिर्मम॥
en: The Adhvaryu said O foremost of intelligent men, one should live with the good. Hearing your opinion my understanding shines with light.

sn: भगवन् भगवद्गुद्ध्या प्रतिपन्नो ब्रवीम्यहम्। व्रतं मन्त्रकृतं कर्तु पराधोऽस्ति मे द्विज॥
en: O illustrious one, I come to you, believing you to be a god; and I say I have no fault, O twice-born one, by performing these rites with the help of Mantras.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच उपपत्त्या यतिस्तूष्णीं वर्तमानस्ततः परम्। अध्वर्युरपि निर्मोहः प्रचचार महामखे।॥
en: The Brahmana said With this conclusion, the Yati remained silent after this. The Adhvaryu also went on with the great sacrifice, freed from delusion.

sn: एवमेतादृशं मोक्षं सुसूक्ष्मं ब्राह्मणा विदुः। विदित्वा चानुतिष्ठन्ति क्षेत्रज्ञेनार्थदर्शिना॥
en: The Brahmanas understand Liberation, which is exceedingly subtle, to be of this kind; and having understood it, they live accordingly, directed by the Kshetrajna, that seer of all topics.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: ब्राहाण उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। कार्तवीर्यस्य संवादं समुद्रस्य च भाविनि॥
en: The Brahmana said About it is cited the ancient story O lady, of the discourse between Kartavirya and the Ocean.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: कार्तवीर्यार्जुनो नाम राजा बाहुसहस्रवान्। येन सागरपर्यन्ता धनुषा निर्जिता मही॥
en: There was a king named Kartavirya-Arjuna who had a thousand arms. He conquered, with his bow, the Earth extending to the ocean.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: स कदाचित् समुद्रान्ते विचरन् बलदर्पितः। अवाकिरशरशतैः समुद्रमिति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that, once on a time, as he was walking on the shores of the sea, proud of his power, he showered hundreds of arrows on thal vast receptacle of water.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: तं समुद्रो नमस्कृत्य कृताञ्जलिरुवाच हा मा मुञ्च वीर नाराचान् ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते॥
en: The Ocean, bowing down to him, said, with joined hands, Do not, O hero. discharged your arrows (at me)! Say, what shall I do to you.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: मदाश्रयाणि भूतानि त्वद्विसृष्टैर्महेषुभिः। वध्यन्ते राजशार्दूल तेभ्यो देह्यभयं विभो॥
en: With these strong arrows shot by you, those creatures which have taken shelter in me are being killed, O foremost of kings! Do you, O lord, grant them security.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: अर्जुन उवाच मत्समो यदि संग्रामे शरासनधरः क्वचित्। विद्यते तं समाचक्ष्व यः समासीत मां मृधे॥
en: If any holder of the bow exists that is equal to me in battle, and that would stand against mc in the field, do you name him to me.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: समुद्र उवाच महर्षिर्जमदग्निस्ते यदि राजन् परिश्रुतः। तस्य पुत्रस्तवातिथ्यं यथावत् कर्तुमर्हति।॥
en: The Ocean said If you have heard, O king, of the great Rishi Jamadagni, his son is competent to duly receive you as a guest.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: ततः स राजा प्रययौ क्रोधेन महता वृतः। स तमाश्रममागम्य राममेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: Then that king proceeded, becoming highly irate. Arrived at that hermitage, he found Rama himself.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: स रामप्रतिकूलानि चकार सह बन्धुभिः। आयासं जनयामास रामस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: With his kinsmen he began to do many deeds while were hostile to Rama, and caused much trouble to that grcat hero.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: ततस्तेजः प्रजज्वाल रामस्यामिततेजसः। प्रदहन् रिपुसैन्यानि तदा कमललोचने।॥
en: Then the energy, which was immeasurable, of Rama shone forth, burning the troops of the enemy, O lotus-eyed one.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: ततः परशुमादाय स तं बाहुसहस्रिणम्। चिच्छेद सहसा रामो बहुशाखमिव दुमम्॥
en: Taking up his battle-axe, Rama suddenly displayed his power, and hacked that thousandarmed hero, like a tree of many branches.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: तं हतं पतितं दृष्ट्वा समेताः सर्वबान्धवाः। असीनादाय शक्तीश्च भार्गवं पर्यधावयन्॥
en: Seeing him killed and laid low on the earth, all his kinsmen, collected in a body, and taking up their darts rushed at Rama, who was then scated, from all sides.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: रामोऽपि धनुरादाय रथमारुह्य सत्वरः। विसृजशरवर्षाणि व्यधमत् पार्थिवं बलम्॥
en: Rama also, taking up his bow and quickly getting on his car, discharged showers of arrows and punished the army of the king.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: ततस्तु क्षत्रियाः केचिज्जामदग्न्यभयार्दिताः। विविशुर्गिरिदुर्गाणि मृगाः सिंहार्दिता इव॥
en: Then, some of the Kshatriyas, stricken with the terror of Jamadagni's son, entered mountain fastnesses, like deer afflicted by the lion.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: तेषां स्वविहितं कर्म तद्भयान्नानुतिष्ठताम्। प्रजा वृषलता प्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानामदर्शनात्॥
en: Of them that were unable, through feat of Rama, lo perform the duties ordained for their order, the progeny became Vrishalas owing to their inability to find Brahmanas.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: एवं ते द्रविडाऽऽभीरा: पुण्ड्राश्च शबरैः सह। वृषलत्वं परिगता व्युत्थानात् क्षत्रधर्मिणः॥
en: Thus the Dravidas and Adhiras and Pundars together with the Shavaras, became Vrishalas through those men who had Kshatriya duties assigned to them, following away (from them).

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: ततश्च हतवीरासु क्षत्रियासु पुनः पुनः। द्विजैरुत्पादितं क्षत्रं जामदग्न्यो न्यकृन्तत॥
en: Then the Kshatriyas that were begotten by the Brahmanas upon Kshatriya women who had lost their heroic children, were repeatedly destroyed by Jamadagni's son.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: एकविंशतिमेधान्ते रामं वागशरीरिणी। दिव्या प्रोवाच मधुरा सर्वलोकपरिश्रुता॥ राम राम निवर्तस्व के गुणं तात पश्यसि। क्षत्रबधूनिमान् प्राणैर्विप्रयोज्य पुनः पुनः॥
en: The destruction proceeded one and twenty times. At its conclusion a bodiless voice, sweet and coming from the celestial region, and which was heard by all people, spoke to Rama, O Rama, O Rama, stop! What merit do you see, O son, in thus destroying repeatedly these inferior Kshatriyas?

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: तथैव तं महात्मानमृचीकप्रमुखास्तदा। पितामहा महाभाग निवर्तस्वेत्यथाब्रुवन्॥
en: Thus, O blessed dame, his grandsires, headed by Richika, addressed that great one, saying, Do you, desist.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: पितुर्वधममृष्यंस्तु रामः प्रोवाच तानृषीन्। नार्हन्तीह भवन्तो मां निवारयितुमित्युत॥
en: Rama, however, unable to forgive the destruction of his father, replied to those Rishis, saying, you should not forbid me.

description: The discourse between Kartavirya, Arjuna and the Occan
sn: पितर ऊचुः नार्हसे क्षत्रबन्धुंस्त्वं निहन्तुं जयतां वरा नेह युक्तं त्वया हन्तुं ब्राह्मणेन सता नृपान्॥
en: The departed manes then said, O foremost of all victorious men, you should not kill these inferior Kshatriyas! It is not proper that your self, being a Brahmanas should kill these kings.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: पितर ऊचुः अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। श्रुत्वा च तत् तथा कार्यं भवता द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Regarding it is cited this old, history. Having heard it, you should act according to it, O foremost of all twice-born persons.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अलर्को नाम राजर्षिरभवत् सुमहातपाः। धर्मज्ञः सत्यवादी च महात्मा सुदृढव्रतः॥ ससागरान्तां धनुषा विनिर्जित्य महीमिमाम्। कृत्वा सुदुष्करं कर्म मनः सूक्ष्मे समादधे॥
en: There was a royal sage, named of Alarka gifted with the austerest of penances. He knew all duties, was truthful in speech, of high soul, and exceedingly firm in his vows. Having with his bow. conquered the whole earth extending to the seas, and thereby performed a highly difficult fear, he set his mind on that which is subtle.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: स्थितस्य वृक्षमूलेषु तस्य चिन्ता बभूव ह। उत्सृज्य सुमहत्कर्म सूक्ष्म प्रति महामते॥४॥
en: While sitting at the root of a tree, his thoughts, O you of great intelligence, abandoning all those great deeds, turned towards that which is subtle!

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अलर्क उवाच मनसो मे बलं जातं मनो जित्वा ध्रुवो जयः। अन्यत्र बाणान् धास्यामि शत्रुभिः परिवारितः॥
en: Alarka said My mind has become strong. Having conquered the mind, One's conquest becomes permanent. Though surrounded by enemies, I shall (henceforth) discharge my arrows at other objects.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: यदिदं चापलात् कर्म सर्वान् मोश्चिकीर्षति। मन:प्रति सुतीक्ष्णाग्रानहं मोक्ष्यामि सायकान्॥
en: Since on account of its unsteadiness, it sets all mortals to perform acts, I shall shoot very sharp-pointed arrows at the mind!

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: मन उवाच नेमे बाणास्तरिष्यन्ति मामलर्क कथंचन। तवैव मर्म भेत्स्यन्ति भिन्नमर्मा मरिष्यसि॥
en: The mind said These arrows, O Alarka, will never cut me through. They will pierce only your own vital parts. Your vital parts being picrced, you shall die.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अन्यान् बाणान् समीक्षस्व यैस्त्वं मां सूदयिष्यसि। तच्छुत्वाप्यविचिन्त्याथ ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Do you look out for other arrows with which 10 kill me! Hearing these words and reflecting upon them, he said as follows.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अलर्क उवाच आघ्राय सुबहून् गन्धां स्तानेव प्रतिगृध्यति। तस्माद् घ्राणं प्रति शरान् प्रतिमोक्ष्याम्यहं शितान्॥
en: Alarka said Smelling many perfumes, (the nose) desires after them only. Hence I shall throw my whcited arrows at the nose.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: घ्राण उवाच नेमे बाणास्तरिष्यन्ति मामलर्क कथंचन। तवैव मर्म भेत्स्यन्ति भिन्नमर्मा मरिष्यसि॥
en: The nose said-These arrows will never pass through me, O Alarka! They will pierce only your own vital parts, and your vital parts being pierced, you shall dic.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अन्यान् बाणान् समीक्षस्व यैस्त्वं मां सूदयिष्यसि। तच्छुत्वा स विचिन्त्याथ ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Do you look for other arrows with which to destroy me! Hearing these words and thinking upon them, he said as follows.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अलर्क उवाच इयं स्वादून् रसान् भुक्त्वा तानेव प्रतिगृध्यति। तस्माज्जिह्वां प्रति शरान् प्रतिमोक्ष्याम्यहं शितान्॥
en: Alarka said This one enjoying savoury tastes, hankers after them only. hence I shall discharge whetted arrows at the tongue.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: जिह्वोवाच नेमे बाणास्तरिष्यन्ति मामलर्क कथंचन। तवैव मर्म भेत्स्यन्ति भिन्नमर्मा मरिष्यसि॥
en: The tongue said These arrows, O Alarka, will not cut through me. They will only pierce your own vital parts and your vital parts being pierced, you shall dic.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अन्यान् बाणान् समीक्षस्व यैस्त्वं मां सूदयिष्यसि। तच्छुत्वा स विचिन्त्याथ ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Do you look for other arrows with which to kill me! Hearing these words and thinking upon them, he said as follows.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अलर्क उवाच स्पृष्ट्वा त्वग्विविधान् स्पर्शी स्तानेव प्रतिगृध्यति। तस्मात् त्वचं पाटयिप्ये विविधैः कङ्कपत्रिभिः॥
en: Alarka said The skin, touching various objects of touch, hankers after them only. Hence, I shall tear off the skin with various arrows equipt with the feathers of the Kanka.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: त्वगुवाच नेमे बाणास्तरिष्यन्ति मामलर्क कथंचन। तवैव मर्म भेत्स्यन्ति भिन्नमर्मा मरिष्यसि॥
en: The skin said These arrows will not, O Alarka, pass through me. They will pierce your own vital parts only, and your vital parts being pierced, you shall die.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अन्यान् बाणान् समीक्षस्व यैस्त्वं मां सूदयिष्यसि। तच्छुत्वा स विचिन्त्याथ ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Do you look for other arrows with which to kill me! Hearing these words and thinking on them, he said as follows.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अलर्क उवाच श्रुत्वा तु विविधाञ्शब्दांस्तानेव प्रतिगृध्यति। तस्माच्छ्रोत्रं प्रति शरान् प्रतिमुञ्चाम्यहं शितान्॥
en: Alarka said Hearing various sounds, (the ear) hankers after them only. Hence, I shall discharge wheticd shafts at the ear.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: श्रोत्रमुवाच नेमे बाणास्तरिष्यन्ति मामलर्क कथंचन। तवैव मर्म भेत्स्यन्ति ततो हास्यसि जीवितम्॥
en: The car said These arrows will not, O Alarka pass though ine. They will pierce your own vital parts only, and your vital parts being pierced, you shall die.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अन्यान् बाणान् समीक्षस्व यैस्त्वं मां सूदयिष्यसि। तच्छुत्वा स विचिन्त्याथ ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Do you then look for other arrows with which to kill me! Hearing these words and thinking upon them, he said as follows.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अलर्क उवाच दृष्ट्वा रूपाणि बहुशस्तान्येव प्रतिगृध्यति। तस्माच्चक्षुर्हनिष्यामि निशितैः सायकैरहम्॥
en: Alarka said Secing many colours, the eye longs for them only. Hence, I shall destroy the eye with sharp-pointed arrows.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: चक्षुरुवाच नेमे बाणास्तरिष्यन्ति मामलर्क कथंचन। तवैव मर्म भेत्स्यन्ति भिन्नमर्मा मरिष्यसि॥
en: Thc eye said, These arrows will not, O Alarka, pass through me at all. They will pierce your own vital parts lonely, and your vital parts being cut, you shall die.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अन्यान् बाणान् समीक्षस्व यैस्त्वं मां सूदयिष्यसि। तच्छुत्वा स विचिन्त्याथ ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Do you then look for other arrows with which to kill me! Hearing these words and reflecting upon them, he said as follows.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: अलर्क उवाच इयं निष्ठा बहुविधा प्रज्ञया त्वध्यवस्यति। तस्माद् बुद्धिं प्रति शरान् प्रतिमोक्ष्याम्यहं शितान्।।२४
en: Alarka said This forins many determinations with the help of ratiocination. Hence, I shall discharge whetted arrows at the understanding.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: बुद्धिरुवाच नेमे बाणास्तरिष्यन्ति मामलर्क कथंचन। तवैव मर्म भेत्स्यन्ति भिन्नमर्मा मरिष्यसि॥
en: These arrows will not, O Alarka, pass through me at all. They will pierce your vital parts only, and your vital parts being pierced, you shall die. Do you then look for other arrows with which to kill ine.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अन्यान् बाणान् समीक्षस्व यैस्त्वं मां सूदयिष्यसि।। ततोऽलर्कस्तपो घोरं तत्रैवास्थाय दुष्करम्। नाध्यगच्छत् परं शक्त्या बाणमेतेषु सप्तसु॥
en: The Brahmana said Then Alarka, engaging himself, even there, on penances difficult to perforin and greatly austere, failed to obtain, by the high power (of his penances) arrows for casting at these seven.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: सुसमाहितचेतास्तु स ततोऽचिन्तयत् प्रभुः। स विचिन्त्य चिरं कालमलर्को द्विजसत्तम॥ नाध्यगच्छत् परं श्रेयो योगान्मतिमतां वरः। स एकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा निश्चलो योगमास्थितः॥
en: Gifted with power, he then, with mind well concentrated, began to reflect. Then, O best of twice-born ones, Alarka, that foremost of intelligent men, having thought for a long time, could not obtain anything better than Yoga. Setting his mind on one object he remained perfectly still, engaged in Yoga.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: इन्द्रियाणि जघानाशु बाणेनैकेन वीर्यवान्। योगेनात्मानमाविश्य सिद्धिं परमिकां गतः॥
en: Gifted with energy, he speedily killed all the senses with one arrow, having entered by Yoga into his soul and thereby acquired the highest success.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: विस्मितश्चापि राजर्षिरिमां गाथां जगाद ह। अहो कष्टं यदस्माभिः सर्वं बाह्यमनुष्ठितम्॥
en: Stricken with wonder, that royal sage then sang this verse : Alas it is a pity that we should have performed all acts that are external.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: भोगतृष्णासमायुक्तः पूर्वं राज्यमुपासितम्। इति पश्चान्मया ज्ञातं योगान्नास्ति परं सुखम्॥
en: Alas, that we should have, gifted with the thirst for enjoyment, courted sovereignty before now! I have learnt this afterwards! There is no happiness that is higher than Yoga.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: इति त्वमनुजानीहि राम मा क्षत्रियान् जहि। तपो घोरमुपातिष्ठ ततः श्रेयोऽभिपत्स्यसे॥
en: Do you know this, O Rama! Cease, to kill the Kshatriyas! Do you practise the austerest of penances! You will then attain to what is good.

description: Alarka's discourse about controlling the various organs of the body
sn: इत्युक्तः स तपो घोरं जामदग्न्यः पितामहैः। आस्थितः सुमहाभागो ययौ सिद्धिं च दुर्गमाम्॥
en: Thus addressed by his grandfathers, Jamadagni's son performed the austcrest penances, and having practised then, that highly blessed one acquired that success which is difficult to recall.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच त्रयो वै रिपवो लोके नवधा गुणतः स्मृताः। प्रहर्षः प्रीतिरानन्दस्त्रयस्ते सात्त्विका गुणाः॥
en: The Brahmana said There are three enemies in the world. They are said to be minefield, according to their qualities. Exultation, satisfaction, and joy, these three qualities belong to Goodness.

sn: तृष्णा क्रोधोऽभिसंरम्भो राजसास्ते गुणाः स्मृताः। श्रमस्तन्द्रा च मोहश्च त्रयस्ते तामसा गुणाः॥
en: Cupidity, anger and hatred, these three qualitics said to belong Darkness. Lassitude, procrastination and delusion, these three qualities belong to Ignorance.

sn: एतान् निकृत्य धृतिमान् बाणसंधैरतन्द्रितः। जेतुं परानुत्सहते प्रशान्तात्मा जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Cutting these with showers of arrows, the intelligent man, free from idleness possessed of a tranquil soul, and with his senses under control, ventures to defeat others.

sn: अत्र गाथा: कीर्तयन्ति पुराकल्पविदो जनाः। अम्बरीषेण या गीता राज्ञा पूर्वं प्रशाम्यता॥
en: About it, persons conversant with ancient cycles recite some verses which were sung formerly by king Ambarisha who had acquired a tranquil soul.

sn: समुदीर्णेषु दोषेषु बाध्यमानेषु साधुषु। जग्राह तरसा राज्यमम्बरीषो महायशाः॥
en: When various kinds of faults were reigning supreme and when the righteous were afflicted, the illustrious Ambarisha put forth his strength for assuming sovereignty.

sn: स निगृह्यात्मनो दोषान् साधून् समभिपूज्य च। जगाम महतीं सिद्धिं गाथाश्चेमा जगाद ह॥
en: Subduing his own faults and adoring the righteous, he acquired great success and sang these verses.

sn: भूयिष्ठं विजिता दोषा निहताः सर्वशत्रवः। एको दोषो वरिष्ठश्च वध्यः स न हतो मया॥
en: I have controlled many faults. I have slain all enemies. But there is one, the greatest, vice which deserves to be destroyed but which has not been destroyed be me.

sn: यत्प्रयुक्तो जन्तुरयं वैतृष्ण्यं नाधिगच्छति। तृष्णात इह निम्नानि धावमानो न बुध्यते॥
en: Urged by that fault, this individual soul fails to attain to freedom from desire. Possessed by desire, one runs into ditches without knowing it.

sn: अकार्यमपि येनेह प्रयुक्तः सेवते नरः। तं लोभमसिभिस्तीक्ष्णैनिकृत्य सुखमेधते॥
en: Urged by that fault, one induigcs in forbidden deeds. Do you cut off, cut off, that cupidity with sharp-edged swords.

sn: लोभाद्धि जायते तृष्णा ततश्चिन्ता प्रवर्तते। स लिप्यमानो लभते भूयिष्ठं राजसान् गुणान्। तदवाप्तौ तु लभते भूयिष्ठं तामसान् गुणान्॥
en: From cupidity originates desire. From desire originates anxiety. The man who yields to desire acquires many qualities which bclong 10 Darkness,

sn: स तैर्गुणैः संहतदेहबन्धनः पुनः पुनजार्यति कर्म चेहते। जन्मक्षये भिन्नविकीर्णदेहो मृत्युं पुनर्गच्छति जन्मनैव॥
en: When these have been acquired, he gets many qualities which belong to ignorance. On account of the qualities, he repeatedly takes birth, with the fetters of body united, and is moved to action. Upon the expiration of life, with body becoming separated and scattered, he once mects with death which is due to birth itself.

sn: तस्मादेतं सम्यगवेक्ष्य लोभं निगृह्य धृत्याऽऽत्मनि राज्यमिच्छेत्। मात्मैव राजा विदितो यथावत्॥
en: Hence, duly understanding this, and governing cupidity by intelligence, one should desire for sovereignty in his soul. This is (true) sovereignty. There is no other sovereignty here. The soul properly understood, is the king.

sn: इति राज्ञाम्बरीषेण गाथा गीता यशस्विना। अधिराज्यं पुरस्कृत्य लोभमेकं निकृन्तता॥
en: Even these were thc verses sung by the illustrious king Ambarisha, on the subject of sovereignty which he kept before him, that king who had severed the one foremost fault, viz.. cupidity.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। ब्राह्मणस्य च संवादं जनकस्य च भाविनि॥
en: The Brahmana said Regarding it is cited the old discourse between a Brahmana and (king) Janaka.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: ब्राह्मणं जनको राजा सन्नं कस्मिंश्चिदागसि। विषये मे न वस्तव्यमिति शिष्ट्यर्थमब्रवीत्॥
en: King Janaka (on a certain occasion), desirous of punishing him said to a Brahmana who had become guilty of some offence, You shall not live within my dominions.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचाथ ब्राह्मणो राजसत्तमम्। यावांस्तव वशे स्थितः॥
en: Thus addressed, the Brahmana replied to that best of kings, saying. Tell me, O king, what the limits are of the territories subject to you.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: आचक्ष्व विषयं राजन् सोऽन्यस्य विषये राज्ञो वस्तुमिच्छाम्यहं विभो। वचस्ते कर्तुमिच्छामि यथाशास्त्रं महीपते॥
en: I wish, O lord, to live within the dominions of another king. Indeed, I wish to obey your command, O king, according to the scriptures.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: इत्युक्तस्तु तदा राजा ब्राह्मणेन यशस्विना। मुहुरुष्णं विनिःश्वस्य न किंचित् प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Thus addressed by that celebrated Brahmana, the king, hearing repeated and hou sighs, said not a word in reply.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: तमासीनं ध्यायमानं राजानममितौजसम्। कश्मलं सहसागच्छद् भानुमन्तमिव ग्रहः॥
en: Like the planet (Rahu) possessing the Sun, a cloudedness of understanding suddenly overwhelmed that king of incomparable energy as he sat plunged in thought.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: समाश्वास्य ततो राजा विगते कश्मले तदा। ततो मुहूर्तादिव तं ब्राह्मणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: When that cloudedness of understanding departed and the king became comforted, he spoke after a short time these words to that Brahmana.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: जनक उवाच पितृपैतामहे राज्ये वश्य जनपदे सति। विषयं नाधिगच्छामि विचिन्वन् पृथिवीमहम्॥
en: Although a (large) inhabited dominion is subject 10 me within this ancestral kingdom of mine, yield fail to find my dominion, searching through the whole Earth.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: नाधिगच्छं यदा पृथ्व्यां मिथिला मार्गिता मया। नाध्यगच्छं यदा तस्यां स्वप्रजा मार्गिता मया॥
en: When I could not find it on the Earth. I then Searched Mithila (for it). When I could not find it in Mithila, 1 then searched for it among my own children.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: नाध्यगच्छं तदा तस्यां तदा मे कश्मलोऽभवत्। ततो मे कश्मलस्यान्ते मतिः पुनरुपस्थिता॥
en: When I could not find it even there, a cloudedness of understanding came over me. After that cloudedness of understanding departed, intelligence came back to me.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: तदा न विषयं मन्ये सर्वो वा विषयो मम। आत्मायि चायं न मम सर्वा वा पृथिवी मम॥
en: Then I though that I have no dominion, or that everything is my dominion. This body is not mine, or the whole Earth is minc.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: यथा मम तथान्येषामिति मन्ये द्विजोत्तम। उष्यतां यावदुत्साहो भुज्यतां यावदुष्यते॥
en: At the same time, O best of twice bon persons, I think that that is as much mine as it is of others. Do you, therefore, live (here) as long as your choice leads you, and do you enjoy as long as you please.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: व्राह्मण उवाच पितृपैतामहे राज्ये वश्ये जनपदे सति। ब्रूहि कां मतिमास्थाय ममत्वं वर्जितं त्वया॥
en: When there is a large inhabited tract in your ancestral kingdom, tell me, depending upon what understanding, has the idea of mineness been got rid of by you.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: कां वै बुद्धिं समाश्रित्य सर्वो वै विषयस्तव। नावैषि विषयं येन सर्वो वा विषयस्तव॥
en: What also is that understanding depending upon which you have come to the conclusion that everything forms your dominion? What. indeed, is the notion through which you have no dominion, or everything is your dominion?

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: जनक उवाच अन्तवन्त इहावस्था विदिताः सर्वकर्मसु। नाध्यगच्छमहं तस्मान्ममेदमिति यद् भवेत्॥
en: Janaka said All conditions here, in all affairs, I understand, are liable to come to an end. Hence, I could not find that which should be called mine.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: कस्येदमिति कस्य स्वमिति बेदवचस्तथा। नाध्यगच्छमहं बुद्ध्या ममेदपिति यद् भवेत्॥
en: (Considering) whose is this, I thought of the Vedic text about anybody's property. I could not therefore, find, through my understanding, what should be (called) mine.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: एतां बुद्धिं समाश्रित्य ममत्वं वर्जितं मया। शृणु बुद्धिं च यां ज्ञात्वा सर्वत्र विषयो मम॥
en: Depending upon this notion. I got rid of the idea of mineness. Hear now what that notion is depending upon which I arrived at the conclusion that I have dominion everywhere.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: नाहमात्मार्थमिच्छामि गन्धान् ध्राणगतानपि। तस्मान्मे निर्जिता भूमिर्वशे तिष्ठन्ति नित्यदा॥
en: I do not wish for my own self those smells which are even in my nose. Therefore, the earth, subjugated by me, is always under me.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: नाहमात्मार्थमिच्छामि रसानास्येऽपि वर्ततः। आपो मे निर्जितास्तस्माद् वशे तिष्ठन्ति नित्यदा।।१९
en: I do not wish for my own self those tastes which exist in contact with even my tongue. Therefore, water, subjugated by me, is always under me.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: नाहमात्मार्थमिच्छामि रूपं ज्योतिश्च चक्षुषः। तस्मान्मे निर्जितं ज्योतिर्वशे तिष्ठन्ति नित्यदा॥
en: I do not wish for my own self the colour or light which belongs to my eye. Therefore, light subjugated by me, is always under me.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: नाहमात्मार्थमिच्छामि स्पर्शास्त्वचि गताश्च ये। तस्मान्मे निर्जितो वायुर्वशे तिष्ठन्ति नित्यदा॥
en: I do not wish for my own self those scrisations of touch which are in contact with even my skin. Therefore, the wind, subjugated by me, is always under me.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: नाहमात्मार्थमिच्छामि शब्दाश्रोत्रगतानपि। तस्मान्मे निर्जिताः शब्दे वशे तिष्ठन्ति नित्यदा॥
en: I do not wish for own self those sounds, which are in contact with even my car. Therefore, sounds, subjugated by me, are always under me.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: नाहमात्मार्थमिच्छामि मनो नित्यं मनोऽन्तरे। मनो मे निर्जितं तस्माद् वशे तिष्ठन्ति नित्यदा॥
en: I do not wish for my own self the mind that is always in my mind. Therefore the mind, subjugated by me, is under me.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: देवेभ्यश्च पितृभ्यश्च भूतेभ्योऽतिथिभिः सह। इत्यर्थे सर्व एवेति समारम्भा भवन्ति वै॥
en: All these acts of mine are for the sake of the celestials, the departed manes, the Bhuttas, together with guests.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: ततः प्रहस्य जनकं ब्राह्मणः पुनरब्रवीत्। तवज्जिज्ञासार्थमोह विद्धि मां धर्ममागतम्॥
en: The Brahmana then, smiling, once more said to Janaka, Know that I am Dharma, who come here today for examining you.

description: The means for destroying Egoism. The discourse of Janaka
sn: त्वमस्य ब्रह्मलाभस्य दुर्वारस्यानिवर्तिनः। सत्त्वनेमिनिरुद्धस्य चक्रस्यैकः प्रवर्तकः॥
en: You are indeed the one person for setting this wheel in motion, this wheel that has the quality of Goodness for its circumference, Brahma for its nave, and the understanding for its spokes, and which never turns back!

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच नाहं तथा भीरु चरामि लोके यथा त्वं मां तर्जयसे स्वबुद्ध्या। विप्रोऽस्मि मुक्तोऽस्मि वनेचरोऽस्मि गृहस्थधर्मा व्रतवांस्तथास्मि॥
en: The Brahmana said I do not, O timid one, move in this world in the manner which you, according to your own understanding, censure. I am a Brahmana endued with Vedic knowledge. I am liberated. I am a hermit, I follow the duties of a houscholder. I observe vows.

sn: नाहमस्मि यथा मां त्वं पश्यसे च शुभाशुभे। मया व्याप्तमिदं सर्वं यत् किंचिज्जगतीगतम्॥
en: I am not what you see me in good and bad deeds. I pervaded everything that exists in this universe.

sn: ये केचिज्जन्तवो लोके जङ्गमाः स्थावराश्च ह। तेषां मामन्तकं विद्धि दारूणामिव पावकम्॥
en: I am the destroyer of all crcatures that exist in the world, mobile or immobile, as fire destroys all kinds of wood.

sn: राज्यं पृथिव्यां सर्वस्यामथवापि त्रिविष्टपे। तथा बुद्धिरियं वेत्ति बुद्धिरेव धनं मम॥
en: Sovereignty over the whole Earth or over the Heaven can be compared with this knowledge of my oneness with the universe). This knowledge is my wcalth.

sn: एकः पन्था ब्राह्मणानां येन गच्छन्ति तद्विदः। गृहेषु वनवासेषु गुरुवासेषु भिक्षुषु॥
en: This is the one path for Brahmanas by which they who understand it proceed domesticity, or abodes in the forest, or residence with preceptors, among mendicants.

sn: लिङ्गैर्बहुभिरव्यौरेका बुद्धिरुपास्यते। नानालिङ्गाश्रमस्थानां येषां बुद्धिः शमात्मिका॥ ते भावमेकमायान्ति सरितः सागरं यथा।
en: With numerous unconfused symbols, only one knowledge is adored. Those who, whatever the symbols and modes of life which they follow, have acquired an understanding having tranquillity for its essence, attain to that one entity as numerous rivers all mecting the Ocean.

sn: बुद्ध्यायं गम्यते मार्गः शरीरेण न गम्यते। आद्यन्तवन्ति कर्माणि शरीरं कर्मबन्धनम्॥
en: This path can be trodden with the help of the understanding and not of the body. Actions have both beginning and end, and the body has actions for its fetters.

sn: तस्मात् ते सुभगे नास्ति परलोककृतं भयम्। तद्भावभावनिरता ममैवात्मानमेष्यसि॥
en: Hence, O blessed lady, you need have no fear about the world to come. With your heart intent upon the real object, it is my soul into which you will come!

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: ब्राह्मण्युवाच नेदमल्पात्मना शक्यं वेदितुं नाकृतात्मना। बहु चाल्पं च संक्षिप्तं विप्लुतं च मतं मम॥
en: The Brahmana's wife said This cannot be understood by a weakminded person as also by one whose soul has not been purified. My intelligence is very little, and contracted, and confused.

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: उपायं तं मम ब्रूहि येनैषा लभ्यते मतिः। तन्मन्ये कारणं त्वत्तो यत एषा प्रवर्तते।॥
en: Tell me the means by which the knowledge may be acquired. I wish to learn from you the source from which this knowledge comes.

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अरणी ब्राह्मणी विद्धि गुरुरस्योत्तरारणिः। तप:श्रुतेऽभिमन्थीतो ज्ञानाग्निर्जायते ततः॥
en: Know that intelligence about Brahma is the lower Arani; the preceptor is the upper Arani; penances and conversance with the scriptures are what make attrition. From this is originated the fire of knowledge.

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: ब्राह्मण्युवाच यदिदं ब्राह्मणो लिङ्गं क्षेत्रज्ञ इति संज्ञितम्। ग्रहीतुं येन यच्छक्यं लक्षणं तस्य तत् क्व नु।॥
en: The Brahmana's wife said About this symbol of Brahma, which is designated, Kshetrajna, where, indeed, is a description of it by which it is capable of being seized?

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अलिङ्गो निर्गुणश्चैव कारणं नास्य लक्ष्यते। उपायमेव वक्ष्यामि येन गृह्येत वा न वा॥
en: The Brahmana said He is without symbols, and without qualities. Nothing exists that may be you the considered as his cause. I shall, however, tell means by which he can be apprehended or not.

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: सम्यगुपायो दृष्टश्च भ्रमरैरिव लक्ष्यते। कर्मबुद्धिरवुद्धित्वाज्ज्ञानलिङ्गैरिवाश्रितम्॥
en: A good means may be found; which is perceived as by bees. That means consists of and understanding purified by action. Those whose understanding have not been so purified consider that entity, through their own ignorance, as invested with the properties of knowledge and others.

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: इदं कार्यमिदं नेति न मोक्षेषूपदिश्यते। पश्यतः शृण्वतो बुद्धिरात्मनो येषु जायते॥
en: It is not laid down that this should be done, or that this should not be donc, in the rules for acquiring Liberation, those that is, in which a knowledge of the soul originates only in him who sees and hears.

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: यावन्त इह शक्येरं स्तावन्तॊऽशान् प्रकल्पयेत्। अव्यक्तान् व्यक्तरूपानं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: One should understand as many parts, unmanifest and manifest, by hundreds and thousands, as one is capable of comprehending here.

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: सर्वान्नानार्थयुक्तांश्च सर्वान् प्रत्यक्षहेतुकान्। यतः परं न विद्यते ततोऽभ्यासे भविष्यति॥
en: Indeed, one should comprehend various objects of various significancies, and all objects of direct perception. Then will come, from practice, that above which nothing cxists.

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच ततस्तु तस्या ब्राह्मण्या मतिः क्षेत्रज्ञसंक्षये। क्षेत्रज्ञानेन परतः क्षेत्रज्ञेभ्यः प्रवर्तते॥
en: The holy one said Then the mind of the Brahmana's wife, upon the destruction of the Kshetrajna, became that which is beyond Kshctrajna, on account of the knowledge of Kshetra.

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: अर्जुन उवाच क्व नु सा ब्राह्मणी कृष्ण क्व चासौ ब्राह्मणर्पभः। याभ्यां सिद्धिरियं प्राप्ता तावुभौ वद मेऽच्युत॥
en: Arjuna said, Where, indeed, is that Brahmana's wife, O Krishna, and where is that foremost of Brahmanas, by both of whom was such success acquired. Tell me about them, O you of undecaying glory.

description: The Source of the Knowledge of Self
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच मनो मे ब्राह्मणं विद्धि बुद्धिं मे विद्धि ब्राह्मणीम्। क्षेत्रश्र इति यश्चोक्तः सोऽहमेव धनंजय॥
en: My mind is the Brahmana, and that my understanding is the Brahmana's wife. He who has been spoken of as Kshetrajna is I myself, O Dhananjaya.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: अर्जुन उवाच ब्रह्म यत्परमं ज्ञेयं तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि। भवतो हि प्रसादेन सूक्ष्मे मे रमते मतिः॥
en: Arjuna said You should explain Brahma to me, that which is the highest object of knowledge. Through your favour, my mind is delighted with these subtle disquisition's.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: वासुदेव उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। संवादं मोक्षसंयुक्तं शिष्यस्य गुरुणा सह॥
en: Vasudeva said Regarding it is recited the old discourse between a preceptor and his disciple on the subject of Brahma.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: कश्चिद् ब्राह्मणमासीनमाचार्यं संशितव्रतम्। शिष्यः प्रप्रच्छ मेधावी किंस्विच्छ्रेयः परंतप॥
en: Once on a time, O destroyer of enemics, an intelligent disciple questioned certain Brahmana of rigid vows who was preceptor, as a he was scated, saying-What, indeed, is the highest good?

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: भगवन्तं प्रपन्नोऽहं निःश्रेयसपरायणः। याचे त्वां शिरसा विप्र यद् ब्रूयां ब्रूहि तन्मम॥
en: Desirous of acquiring that which forms the highest good, I throw myself at your fect, O holy one! O learned Brahmana, I solicit you, bending my head, to explain to me what I ask.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: तभेवंवादिनं पार्थ शिष्यं गुरुरुवाच ह। सर्वे तु ते प्रवक्ष्यामि यत्र वै संशयो द्विज॥
en: To that disciple, O son of Pritha, who said So, the preceptor said, O twice-born one, I shall explain to you everything about which you may have any doubts.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: इत्युक्तः स कुरुश्रेष्ठ गुरुणा गुरुवत्सलः। प्राञ्जलिः परिपप्रच्छ यत्तच्छृणु महामते॥
en: Thus addressed, O foremost one of Kuru's race, by his preceptor, that disciple who was greatly devoted to his preceptor, spoke as follows, with joined hands. Do you hear what he said, O you of great intelligence.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: शिष्य उवाच कुतश्चाहं कुतश्च त्वं तत्सत्यं ब्रूहि यत्परम्। कुतो जातानि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च॥
en: Whence aim I? Whence are you? Explain that which is the highest truth. From what source have originated all creatures mobile and immobile?

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: केन जीवन्ति भूतानि तेषामायुश्च किं परम्। किं सत्य किं तपो विप्र के गुणाः सद्भिरीरिताः॥
en: By what do creatures live? What is the limit of their life? What is truth? What is penance, O learned Brahmana? What are called qualities by the good?

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: के पन्थान: शिवाश्च स्युः किं सुखं किं च दुष्कृतम्। एतान् मे भगवन् प्रश्चान् याथातथ्येन सुव्रत॥ वक्तुमर्हसि विप्रर्षे यथावदिह तत्त्वतः। त्वदन्यः कश्चन प्रश्चानेतान् वक्तुमिहार्हति॥
en: What paths are to be called auspicious? What is happiness? What is sin? O holy one, O you of excellent vows, you should answer these questions of mine, O learned Rishi, correctly, truly, and accurately. Who else is there in this world than you who is capable of answering these questions?

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: ब्रूहि धर्मविदां श्रेष्ठ परं कौतूहलं मम। मोक्षधर्मार्थकुशलो भवाँल्लोकेषु गीयते॥
en: Do you answer them, o foremost of all persons knowing duties! My curiosity is great. you are celebrated in all the worlds as one well-skilled in the duties about liberation.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: सर्वसंशयसंच्छेत्ता त्वदन्यो न च विद्यते। संसारभीरवश्चैव मोक्षकामास्तथा वयम्॥
en: There is none else save you who can remove all kinds of doubts. Afraid of worldly life, we have become desirous of acquiring Liberation.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: वासुदेव उवाच तस्मै सम्प्रतिपन्नाय यथावत् परिपृच्छते। शिष्याय गुणयुक्ताय शान्ताय प्रियवर्तिने॥ छायाभूताय दान्ताय यतते ब्रह्मचारिणे। तान् प्रश्नानब्रवीत् पार्थ मेधावी स धृतव्रतः। गुरुः कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ सम्यक् सर्वानरिंदम॥
en: Vasudeva said To that disciple who had humbly sought his instruction and put the questions duly. Who was devoted to his preceptor and endued with tranquillity, and who always acted in a manner that was agreeable (to his instructor), who lived so constantly by the side of his instructor as to have almost become his shadow, who was selfcontrolled and who had the life of a Yati and a Brahmacharin, O son of Pritha, that preceptor gifted with intelligence and observant of vows, duly explained all the questions, O foremost of Kuru's race, O chastiser of all enemies.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: गुरुरुवाच ब्रह्मणोक्तमिदं सर्वमृषिप्रवरसेवितम्। वेदविद्यां समाश्रित्य तत्त्वभूतार्थभावनम्॥
en: All this was declared by Brahman himself. Applauded and practised by the foreinost of Rishis, and depending on Vedic knowledge it involves a consideration of what forms the real entity.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: ज्ञानं त्वेव परं विद्यः संन्यासं तप उत्तमम्। यस्तु वेद निराबाधं ज्ञानतत्त्वं विनिश्चयात्। सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं स सर्वगतिरिष्यते॥ यो विद्वान् सहसंवासं विवासं चैव पश्यति। तथैवैकत्वनानात्वे स दुःखात् परिमुच्यते॥ यो न कामयते किंचिन्न किंचिदभिमन्यते। इहलोकस्थ एवैष ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते॥ प्रधानगुणतत्त्वज्ञः सर्वभूतविधानवित्। निर्ममो निरहङ्कारो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः॥ अव्यक्तबीजप्रभवो बुद्धिस्कन्धमयो महान्। महाहङ्कारविटप इन्द्रियाकुरकोटरः॥ महाभूतविशेषश्च विशेषप्रतिशाखवान्। सदापर्णः सदापुष्पः सदा शुभफलोदयः॥ अजीवः सर्वभूतानां ब्रह्मबीजः सनातनः। एतज्ज्ञात्वा च तत्त्वानि ज्ञानेन परमासिना॥ छित्त्वा चामरतां प्राप्य जहाति मृत्युजन्मनी।
en: We regard knowledge to be that highest object, and renunciation as the best penance. He who, certainly, knows the true object of knowledge which is incapable of being modified by circumstances, viz., the soul living in all creatures, succeeds in going wherever he likes and comes to be considered as the highest. That learned man who sees the residence of all things in one place and their severance as well, and who sees unity in diversity, succeeds in freeing himself from misery. He who does not long for anything and does not cherish the idea of mineness abut any thing, comes to be considered, although living in this world, as being at one with Brahina. He who knows the truth about the qualities of Nature, acquainted with the creation of all existent objects, divested of egoism, and without pride, succeeds, forsooth, in freeing himself. Understanding properly that great tree which has the unmanifest for its seed-sprout and the understanding for its trunk, and high consciousness of self for its branches, and the senses for the cells whence its twigs issue and the (five) great elements for its flower-buds, and the gross elements for its smaller boughs, which has leaves, which always puts forth flowers, and upon which all existent objects depend, whose seeds is Brahma, and which is eternal, and cutting all subjects with the sharp sword of knowledge, one acquires immortality and renounces birth and death.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: भूतभव्यभविष्यादि धर्मकामार्थनिश्चयम्। सिद्धसंघपरिज्ञातं पुराकल्पं सनातनम्॥ प्रवक्ष्येऽहं महाप्राज्ञ पदमुत्तममद्य ते। बुद्ध्वा यदिह संसिद्धा भवन्तीह मनीषिणः॥
en: The conclusions about the past, present, and future, etc., and religion, pleasure, and profit, which are all well known to Siddhas, which belong to remote ages, and which are, indeed, eternal, I shall declare to you. O you of great wisdom! These form what is called Good, Wise Men, understanding them in this world, acquire success.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: उपगम्यर्षयः पूर्वं जिज्ञासन्तः परस्परम्। प्रजापतिभरद्वाजौ गौतमो भार्गवस्तथा॥ वसिष्ठः कश्यपश्चैव विश्वामित्रोऽत्रिरेव च। मार्गान् सर्वान् परिक्रम्य परिश्रान्ताः स्वकर्मभिः॥२६
en: Formerly, the Rishis Brihaspati Bharadvaja, Gautama Bhargava, Vasishtha, Kashyapa, Vishvamitra and Atri, assembled together for the purpose of asking one another. They thus assembled together after having travelled over all paths and after they had got tired with the deeds each of them had done.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: ऋषिमाङ्गिरसं वृद्धं पुरस्कृत्य तु ते द्विजाः। ददृशुर्ब्रह्मभवने ब्रह्माणं वीतकल्मषम्॥
en: Those twice-born persons, headed by the sage son of Angirasa, proceeded to the region of the Grandfather. There they saw Brahman perfectly purged of all sin.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: तं प्रणम्य महात्मानं सुखासीनं महर्षयः। पप्रच्छुर्विनयोपेता नैःश्रेयसमिदं परम्॥
en: Bowing their heads to that great one who was seated at their ease, the great Rishis, gifted with humility, asked him this grave question about the highest good.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: कथं कर्म क्रियात् साधु कथं मुच्येत किल्बिषात्। के नो मार्गाः शिवाश्च स्युः किं सत्यं किं च दुप्कृतम्॥
en: How should a good man act? How would one be freed from sin? What paths are: auspicious for us? What is truth, and what is sin?

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: को चोभौ कर्मणां मार्गों प्राप्नुयुर्दक्षिणोत्तरौ। प्रलयं चापवर्गं च भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययौ॥
en: By what action are the two paths, northern and southern, obtained? What is destruction? What, Liberation? What is birth and what death of all existent objects?

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: इत्युत्ताः स मुनिश्रेष्ठैर्यदाह प्रपितामहः। तत् तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु शिष्य यथागमम्॥
en: I shall tell you. O disciple, what the Grandfather, thus addressed, said to them, according to the scriptures. Do you listen.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच सत्याद् भूतानि जातानि स्थावराणि चराणि च। तपसा तानि जीवन्ति इति तद् वित्त सुव्रताः। स्वां योनि समतिक्रम्य वर्तन्ते स्तेन कर्मणा॥
en: It is from Truth that all creatures, mobile and immobile, have been born. They live by penance (or action). Understand this, O you of excellent vows! On account of their own actions they live, transcending their own origin.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: सत्यं हि गुणसंयुक्तं नियतं पञ्चलक्षणम्॥ ब्रह्म सत्यं तपः सत्यं सत्यं चैव प्रजापतिः।
en: For Truth when united with qualities becomes always possessed of five marks. Brahman is Truth. Penance is truth. Prajapati is truth.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: सत्याद् भूतानि जातानि सत्यं भूतमयं जगत्॥ तस्मात् सत्यमया विप्रा नित्यं योगपरायणाः। अतीतक्रोधसंतापा नियता धर्मसेविन:॥ अन्योन्यनियतान् वैद्यान् धर्मसेतुप्रवर्तकान्। तानहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि शाश्वताल्लोकभावनान्॥ चातुर्विद्यं तथा वर्णाश्चातुराश्रमिकान् पृथक्।
en: It is from Truth that all creatures have originated. Truth is the universe of being. It is for this that Brahmanas who are always devoted to Yoga, who have got over anger and sorrow, and who always consider Religion as the causeway, take refuge in Truth. I shall now speak of those Brahmanas who are controlled by one another and endued with knowledge, of the orders, and of those who belong to the four modes of life.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: धर्ममेकं चतुष्पादं नित्यमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥ पन्थानं वः प्रवक्ष्यामि शिवं क्षेमकरं द्विजाः।
en: The wise say that Rcligion or duty is one, having four quarters. You twice born ones, I shall speak to you now of that path which is auspicious and yields good.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: नियतं ब्रह्मभावाय गतं पूर्वं मनीषिभिः॥ गदन्तस्तं मयाद्येह पन्थानं दुर्विदं परम्।
en: That path has constantly been trod over by wise men in order to acquirc an identity with Brahmana. I shall speak now of that path which is the highest and which is highly difficult of being understood.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: निबोधत महाभागा निखिलेन परं पदम्॥ ब्रह्मचारिकमेवाहुराश्रमं प्रथमं पदम्।
en: Do you understand, in all its fullness, you highly blessed ones, what is the highest set. The first step has been said to be the mode of life that belongs to Brahmacharins.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: गार्हस्थ्यं तु द्वितीयं स्याद् वानप्रस्थमतः परम्। ततः परं तु विज्ञेयमध्यात्मं परमं पदम्॥
en: The second step is domesticity. After this is the residence in the forcst. After that it should be known is the highest step, viz., that belongs to Adhyatma.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: ज्योतिराकाशमादित्यो वायुरिन्द्रः प्रजापतिः। नोपैति यावदध्यात्म तावदेतान् न पश्यति॥
en: Light, ether, sun, wind, Indra, and Prajapati, one sees these as long as one does not acquire Adhyatma.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: तस्योपायं प्रवक्ष्यामि पुरस्तात् तं निबोधत। फलमूलानिलभुजां मुनीनां वसतां वने।॥ वानप्रस्थं द्विजातीनां त्रयाणामुपदिश्यते। सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां गार्हस्थ्यं तद् विधीयते॥
en: I shall declare the means. Do you first understand them. The forest mode of life that is followed by ascetics living in the forest and subsisting upon fruits and roots and air is laid down for the three twice-born classes. The domestic mode of life is ordained for all the orders.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: श्रद्धालक्षणमित्येवं धर्मं धीराः प्रचक्षते। इत्येवं देवयाना वः पन्थानः परिकीर्तिताः। सद्भिरध्यासिता धीरैः कर्मभिर्धर्मसेतवः॥
en: The wise say that Religion or duty has Faith for its characteristic mark. Thus have I declared to you the paths leading to the celestials. They are adopted by the good and wise by their a 'ts. Those paihs are the causeways of picty.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: एतेषां पृथगध्यास्ते यो धर्मं संशितव्रतः। कालात् पश्यति भूतानां सदैव प्रभवाप्ययौ॥
en: That persons of rigid vows who follows any one of these modes separately, always succeeds in time to understand the production and destruction of all creatures.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
sn: अतस्तत्त्वानि वक्ष्यामि याथातथ्येन हेतुना। विषयस्थानि सर्वाणि वर्तमानानि भागशः॥
en: I shall now declarc, accurately and with reasons, the elements which live in parts in all objects.

description: An account of Brahman the highest object of Knowledge
