en: With vital seed drawn up and mind concentrated, one who is thus devoted, succeeds in conquering the celestial region. Having attained to the Highest seat, he has not to return to birth.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: संस्कृत: सर्वसंस्कारैस्तथैव ब्रह्मचर्यवान्। ग्रामान्निष्क्रम्य चारण्ये मुनिः प्रव्रजितो वसेत्॥
en: Cleansed by all purificatory rites and having lived as a Brahmacharin, one should next go out of his village and next live as an ascetic in the forest, having cast off (all attachments).

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: चर्मवल्कलसंवासी सायं प्रातरुपस्पृशेत्। अरण्यगोचरो नित्यं न ग्रामं प्रविशेत् पुनः॥
en: Clad in animal skins or barks of trees, he should perform his ablutions morning and evening. Always living within the forest, he should never return to an inhabited placc.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: अर्चयन्नतिथीन् काले दद्याच्चापि प्रतिश्रयम्। फलपत्रावरैर्मूलैः श्यामाकेन च वर्तयन्॥
en: Honouring guests when they come, he should give them shelter, and himself live upon fruits and leaves and common roots, and Shyamaka.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: प्रवृत्तमुदकं वायुं सर्वं वानेयमाश्रयेत्। प्राश्चीयादानुपूर्वेण यथादीक्षमतन्द्रितः॥
en: He should, without being idle, live on such water as he gets, and air, and all forest products. He should live upon these, in due order, according to the regulations of his initiation.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: समूलफलभिक्षाभिरर्चेदतिथिमागतम्। यद्भक्ष्यं स्यात्ततो दद्याद्भिक्षां नित्यमतन्द्रितः॥
en: He should honour the guest that comes to him with alms of fruits and roots. He should then, without idleness, always give whatever other food he may have.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: देवतातिथिपूर्वं च सदा प्राश्नीत वाग्यतः। अस्पर्धितमनाश्चैव लघ्वाशी देवताश्रयः॥
en: Controlling speech the while, he should eat after satisfying celestials and guests. His mind should be shorn of envy. He should eat little, and depend always on the celestials.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: दान्तो मैत्रः क्षमायुक्तः केशाश्मश्रु च धारयन्। जुह्वन् स्वाध्यायशीलश्च सत्यधर्मपरायणः॥
en: Self-controlled, practising universal mercy, and endued with forgiveness, he should wear both beard and hair. Celebrating sacrifices and devoting himself to the study of the scriptures, he should be steady in the observance of the duty of truth.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: शुचिदेहः सदा दक्षो वननित्यः समाहितः। एवं युक्तो जयेत् स्वर्ग वानप्रस्थो जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: With body always in a state of purity, gifted with cleverness, ever living in the forest, with concentrated mind, and senses, in subjection, a hermit, thus devoting himself, would conquer the celestial region.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: गृहस्थो ब्रह्मचारी च वानप्रस्थोऽथ वा पुनः। च इच्छेन्मोक्षमास्थातुमुत्तमा वृत्तिमाश्रयेत्॥
en: A houscholder, or Brahmacharin, or forestrecluse, who would wise to acquire Liberation, should have recourses to that which has been called the best course of conduct.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो दत्त्वा नैष्कर्म्यमाचरेत्। सर्वभूतसुखो मैत्र: सर्वेन्द्रिययतो मुनिः॥
en: Having granted to all creatures the pledge of utter abstention from harm, he should renounce all action, he should contribute to the happiness of all creatures, practise universal friendliness, govern all his senses, and be an ascetic.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: अयाचितमसंक्लृप्तमुपपन्नं यदृच्छया। कृत्वा प्राढे चरेद् भैक्ष्यं विधूमे भुक्तवज्जने॥
en: Living upon food got without asking and without trouble, and that has come to him spontaneously, he should make a fire. He should go for alins to a place whence smoke has ceased to curl up and where all the inhabitants have already eaten.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: वृत्ते शरावसम्पाते भक्ष्यं लिप्सेत मोक्षवित्। लाभेन च न हृष्येत नालाभे विमना भवेत्। न चातिभिक्षां भिक्षेत केवलं प्राणयात्रिकः॥
en: The person who is conversant with the conduct that leads to Liberation should seek for alms after the vessels (used in coO king) have been washed. He should never rejoice when he gets anything, and never lose heart if he gets nothing.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: यात्रार्थी कालपाकाङ्क्षश्चरेद् भैक्ष्यं समाहितः। लाभं साधारणं नेच्छेन्न भुञ्जीताभिपूजितः॥
en: Seeking just what is necessary for supporting life, he should, with concentrated mind, go about for alms, waiting for the proper time. He should not wish for carnings in common with others, nor eat when honoured.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: अभिपूजितलाभाद्धि विजुगुप्सेत भिक्षुकः। भुक्तान्यन्नानि तिक्तानि कषायकटुकानि च॥
en: The mendicant should conceal himself for avoiding gifts with honour. While eating, he should not eat the resident of another's dish, nor such food as is bitter, or astringent, or pungent.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: नास्वादयीत भुञ्जानो रसांश्च मधुरांस्तथा। यात्रामात्रं च भुञ्जीत केवलं प्राणधारणम्॥
en: He should not also eat such kinds of food as have a sweet taste. He should eat only so inuch as is necessary to keep him alive.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: असंरोधेन भूतानां वृत्तिं लिप्सेत मोक्षवित्। न चान्यमन्नं लिप्सेत भिक्षमाणः कथंचन॥ न संनिकाशयेद् धर्म विविक्ते चारजाश्चरेत्। शून्यागारमरण्यं वा वृक्षमूलं नदी तथा॥ प्रतिश्रयार्थ सेवेत पार्वती वा पुनर्गुहाम्। ग्रामैकरात्रिको ग्रीष्मे वर्षास्वेकत्र वा वसेत्॥
en: The person conversant with Liberation should obtain his livelihood without obstructing any creature. In his rounds of mendicancy he should never follow another. He should never show his piety; he should move about in a solitary place, freed from passion. As should, resort to either an empty house, or a forest, or the foot of some tree, or a river, or a mountain cave for shelter. In summer he should pass only one night in an inhabited place; in the rainy season he may live in one place.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: अध्वा सूर्येण निर्दिष्टः कीटवच्च चरेन्महीम्। दयार्थं चैव भूतानां समीक्ष्य पृथिवीं चरेत्॥
en: He should move about the world like a worm, having his path pointed out by the Sun. From mercy for creatures, he should walk on the Earth with his eyes directed towards it.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: संचयांश्च न कुर्वीत स्नेहवासं च वर्जयेत्। पूताभिरद्भिर्नित्यं वै कार्यं कुर्वीत मोक्षवित्॥
en: He should never amass riches and should avoid living with friends. The man knowing Liberation should every day do all his acts with pure water.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: उपस्पृशेदुद्भूताभिरद्धिश्च पुरुषः सदा। अहिंसा ब्रह्मचर्यं च सत्यमार्जवमेव च॥ अक्रोधश्चानसूया च दमो नित्यमपैशुनम्। अष्टस्वेतेषु युक्तः स्याद् व्रतेषु नियतेन्द्रियः॥
en: Such a man should always perform his ablutions with water that has been taken (from the river or tank). Abstention from harm, celibacy, truth, simplicity, freedom, from anger, freedom from decrying others, selfcontrol and habitual freedom from back-biting; with senses controlled, he should steadily pursue these eight vows.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: अपापमशठं वृत्तमजिह्यं नित्यमाचरेत्। जोषयेत सदा भोज्यं ग्रासमागतमस्पृहः॥
en: He should always practise a sinless mode of conduct, which is not deceptive or crooked. Shorn of attachments he should always make one who comes as a guest eat (at least) a morsel of food.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: यात्रामात्रं च भुञ्जीत केवलं प्राणयात्रिकम्। धर्मलब्धमथाश्नीयान्न काममनुवर्तयेत्॥
en: He should cat just enough for livelihood, the maintenance of life. He should eat only such food as has been got by fair means, and should not pursue the dictates of desire.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: ग्रासादाच्छादनादन्यन्न गृह्णीयात् कथंचन। यावदाहारयेत् तावत् प्रतिगृह्णीत नाधिकम्॥
en: He should never accept any other thing than food and clothing only. He should, again, accept only as much as he can cat and nothing more.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: परेभ्यो न प्रतिग्राह्यं न च देयं कदाचन। दैन्यभावाच्च भूतानां संविभज्य सदा बुधः॥
en: He should not be induced to accept gifts from others, nor should he make gifts to others. Owing to the helplessness of creatures, the wise man should always share with others.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: नाददीत परस्वानि न गृह्णीयादयाचितः। न किंचिद्विविषयं भुक्त्वा स्पृहयेत्तस्य वै पुनः॥
en: He should not misappropriate others belongings, nor should he take anything without being asked. He should not, having enjoyed anything, become so attached to it as to seek for it once more.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: मृदमापस्तथान्नानि पत्रपुष्पफलानि च। असंवृतानि गृह्णीयात् प्रवृत्तानि च कार्यवान्॥
en: One should take only earth, water, pebbles, leaves, flowers, and fruits, which are not owned by any body, as they come, when one wishes to do any act.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: न शिल्पजीविकां जीवेद्धिरण्यं नोत कामयेत्। न द्वेष्टा नोपदेष्टा च भवेच्च निरुपस्कृतः॥
en: One should not live by the occupation of an artisan, nor should he covet gold. One should not hate, nor teach; nor should one have any belongings.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: श्रद्धापूतानि भुञ्जीत निमित्तानि च वर्जयेत्। सुधावृत्तिरसक्तश्च सर्वभूतैरसंविदम्॥
en: One should eat only what is consecrated by faith, One should shun controversies. One should follow the nectarine course of conduct. One should never be attached to anything, and should never enter into relations of intimacy with any creature.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: आशीर्युक्तानि सर्वाणि हिंसायुक्तानि यानि च। लोकसंग्रहधर्मं च नैव कुर्यान्न कारयेत्॥
en: One should not perform, nor cause to perform, any such deed as involves expectation of fruit or destruction of life or the hoarding of riches or articles.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: सर्वभावानतिक्रम्य लघुमात्रः परिव्रजेत्। समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु स्थावरेषु चरेषु च॥
en: Rejecting all objects, content with a very little, one should move about (homeless), pursuing an equal conduct towards all creatures mobile and immobile.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: परं नोद्वजयेत् काचिन्न च कस्यचिदुद्विजेत्। विश्वास्यः सर्वभूतानामग्र्यो मोक्षविदुच्यते॥
en: One should never annoy another being; nor should one be annoyed with another. He who is trusted by all crcatures is considered as the foremost of those persons who understand Liberation.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: अनागतं च न ध्यायेन्नातीतमनुचिन्तयेत्। वर्तमानमुपेक्षेत कालाकाक्षी समाहितः॥
en: One should not think of the past nor feel anxious about the future. One should disregard the present, biding time, with fixed mind.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: न चक्षुषा न मनसा न वाचा दूषयेत् क्वचित्। न प्रत्यक्षं परोक्षं वा किंचिद् दुष्टं समाचरेत्॥
en: One should never defile anything by eye, mind, or speech. Nor should one do anything which is wrong, openly or in secret.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: इन्द्रियाण्युपसंहृत्य कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः। क्षीणेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्निरीहः सर्वतत्त्ववित्॥
en: Withdrawing his senses like the tortoise withdrawing its limbs, one should govern his senses and mind, cultivate a thoroughly peaceful understanding, and seek to master every subject.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: निर्द्वन्द्वो निर्नमस्कारो निःस्वाहाकार एव च। निर्ममो निरहङ्कारो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्॥
en: Freed from all pairs of opposites, never bending his head in respect, abstaining from the rites requiring the utterance of Svaha, one should be free from mineness, and egoism. with purified soul, one should never seek to acquire what one has not and protect what one has.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: निराशीर्निर्गुणः शान्तो निरासक्तो निराश्रयः। आत्मसङ्गी च तत्त्वज्ञो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः॥
en: Free from expectations shorn of qualities, endued with tranquility, one should be free from all attachments and should depend on one. Attached to one's Own self and understanding all subjects, one becomes, forsooth, liberated.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: अपादपाणिपृष्ठं तदशिरस्कमनूदरम्। प्रहीणगुणकर्माणं केवलं विमलं स्थिरम्॥ अगन्धमरसस्पर्शमरूपाशब्दमेव च। अनुगम्यमनासक्तममांसमपि चैव यत्॥ निश्चिन्तमव्ययं दिव्यं गृहस्थमपि सर्वदा। सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं ये पश्यन्ति न ते मृताः॥
en: Those who perceive the self, which is without hands and feet and back which is without head and without stomach, which is free from the action of all qualities, which is absolute, untainted, and stable, which is without smell, without taste and touch, without colour, and without sound, which is to be comprehended (by close study), which is unattached, which is without flesh, which is free from anxiety, unfading, and divine, and lastly which though living in a house resides in all creatures, succeed in escaping death.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: न तत्र क्रमते बुद्धिर्नेन्द्रियाणि न देवताः। वेदा यज्ञाच लोकाश्च न तपो न व्रतानि च।॥
en: There the understanding reaches not nor the senses, nor the celestials, nor the Vedas nor sacrifices, nor the regions (of superior bliss), nor penance nor vows.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: यत्र ज्ञानवतां प्राप्तिरलिङ्गग्रहणा स्मृता। तस्मादलिधर्मज्ञो धर्मतत्त्वमुपाचरेत्॥
en: The attainment to it by those who are endued with knowledge is said to be without comprehension of symbol. Hence the man who knows the properties of that which is shorn of symbols, should practise the truths of piety.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: गूढधर्माश्रितो विद्वान् विज्ञानचरितं चरेत्। अमूढो मूढरूपेण चरेद् धर्ममदूषयन्॥
en: The learned man, living as a householder, should adopt that conduct which is conformable to true knowledge. Though undeluded, he should practise piety like one that is deluded, without finding fault without it.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: यथैनमवमन्येरन् परे सततमेव हि। यथावृत्तश्चरेच्छान्तः सतां धर्मानकुत्सयन्॥
en: Without finding fault with the practices of the good, he should act in such a way for practising piety as may induce other to always disregard him.

description: The conduct of the Twice Born
sn: य एवं वृत्तसम्पन्नः स मुनिः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते। इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थांश्च महाभूतानि पञ्च च॥ मनो बुद्धिरहंकारमव्यक्तं पुरुषं तथा। एतत् सर्वं प्रसंख्याय यथावत् तत्त्वनिश्चयात्॥ ततः स्वर्गमवाप्नोति विमुक्तः सर्वबन्धनैः। एतावदन्तवेलायां परिसंख्याय तत्त्ववित्॥ ध्यायेदेकान्तमास्थाय मुच्यतेऽथ निराश्रयः। निर्मुक्तः सर्वसङ्गेभ्यो वायुराकाशगो यथा॥ क्षीणकेशो निरातङ्गस्तथेदं प्राप्नुयात् परम्॥
en: That man who is gifted with such a conduct is said to be the foremost of ascetics. The senses, the objects of the senses, the (five) great elements, mind, understanding, egoism, the unmanifest. Purusha also, after comprehending these duly with the help of correct inferences, one attains to the celestial region, released from all fetters. One conversant with the truth, understanding these at the time of the termination of his life, should mediate, exclusively resting on one point. Then, depending on none, none, one acquires Liberation. Freed from all attachments, like the wind in space, with his hoarded up means exhausted, without distress of any sort, he attains to the highest goal.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच संन्यासं तप इत्याहुवृद्धा निश्चितवादिनः। ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मयोनिस्था ज्ञानं ब्रह्म परं विदुः॥
en: Brahman said The ancients who always used to speak truth, say that Renunciation is penance. Brahmanas, living in that which has Brahma for its origin understand Knowledge to be high Brahma.

sn: अतिदूरात्मकं ब्रह्म वेदविद्याव्यपाश्रयम्। निर्द्वन्द्व निर्गुणं नित्यमचिन्त्यगुणमुत्तमम्॥
en: Brahma is very far off, and its attainment depends upon a knowledge of the Vedas. It is free from all pairs of opposites, it is shorn of all qualities; it is eternal; it is gifted with unthinkable qualities; it is supreme.

sn: ज्ञानेन तपसा चैव धीराः पश्यन्ति तत् परम्। निर्णिक्तमनसः पूता व्युत्क्रान्तरजसोऽमला:॥
en: It is by knowledge and penance that those gifted with wisdom see that which is the highest. Indeed, they who are of unsullied minds, who are purged of every sin, and who have transcended all passion and darkness (succeed in seeing it.)

sn: तपसा क्षेममध्वानं गच्छन्ति परमेश्वरम्। संन्यासनिरता नित्यं ये च ब्रह्मविदो जनाः॥
en: They who are always given to renunciation, and who are conversant with the Vedas, succeed in attaining to the supreme Lord who is at one with the path of happiness and peace, by the help of penance.

sn: तपः प्रदीप इत्याहुराचारो धर्मसाधकः। ज्ञानं वै परमं विद्यात् संन्यासं नृप उत्तमम्॥
en: Penance, it has been said, is light. Conduct leads to piety. Knowledge is said to be the highest. Renunciation is the best penance.

sn: यस्तु वेद निराधारं ज्ञानं नत्त्वविनिश्चयात्। सर्वभूनस्थमात्मानं स सर्वगतिरिष्यते॥
en: He who understands self through accurate determination of all subjects, undisturbed, which is at one with Knowledge, and which lives in all principles, succeeds in going everywhere.

sn: यो विद्वान् सहवासं च विवासं चैव पश्यति। तथैवैकत्वनानात्वे स दुःखात् प्रतिमुच्यते॥
en: That learned man who sees association and dissociation, and unity in diversity, is freed from misery.

sn: यो न कामयते किंचिन्न किंचिदवमन्यते। इहलोकस्थ एवैष ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते॥
en: He who never desires for anything, who despises nothing, becomes eligible, even when living in this world, for assimilation with Brahma.

sn: प्रधानगुणतत्त्वज्ञः सर्वभूतप्रधानवित्। निर्ममो निरहङ्कारो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः॥
en: He who is conversant with the truths about qualities of Greatness, and understands the Pradhana as existing in all principles, who is free from mineness and egoism, forsooth, becomes liberated.

sn: निर्द्वन्द्वो निर्नमस्कारो नि:स्वधाकार एव च। निर्गुणं नित्यमद्वन्द्वं प्रशमेनैव गच्छति॥
en: He who is freed from all pairs of opposites, who does not bend his head to any body, who has got over the rites of Svaha, succeeds by the help of tranquility alone in attaining to that which is free from pairs of opposites, which is eternal, and which is shom of qualities.

sn: हित्वा गुणमयं सर्वं कर्म जन्तुः शुभाशुभम्। उभे सत्यानृते हित्वा मुच्यते नात्र संशयः॥
en: Renouncing all action, good or bad, developed from qualities, and casting off both truth and falschood, a creature, forsooth, becomes liberated.

sn: अव्यक्तयोनिप्रभवो बुद्धिस्कन्धमयो महान्। महाहंकारविटप इन्द्रियाङ्करकोटरः॥ महाभूतविशालश्च विशेषयति शाखिनः। सदापत्रः सदापुष्पः शुभाशुभफलोदयः॥ आजीव्यः सर्वभूतानां ब्रह्मवृक्षः सनातनः। एनं छित्त्वा च भित्त्वा च तत्त्वज्ञानासिना बुधः॥ हित्वा सङ्गमयान् पाशान् मृत्युजन्मजरोदयान्। निर्ममो निरहङ्कारो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः॥
en: Having the unmanifest for the seed of its origin, with the understanding for its trunk, with the great principle of egoism for its collection of boughs, with the senses for the cavities of its little sprouts, with the (five) great elements for its large branches, the objects of the senses for this smaller branches, with leaves that are ever present, with flowers that always embellish it, and with fruits both agreeable and disagreeable always produced, is the eternal tree of Brahma which forins the support of all creatures. Cutting and piercing that tree with knowledge of truth as the sword, the wise man, abandoning the fetters which are made of attachment and which cause birth, decrepitude, and death, and freeing himself from mineness and egoism, forsooth, becomes liberated.

sn: द्वाविमौ पक्षिणौ नित्यौ संक्षेपौ चाप्यचेतनी। एताभ्यां तु परो योऽयश्चेतनावान् स उच्यते॥
en: These are the two birds, which are immutable, which are friends, and which should be known as unintelligent. That other who is different from these two is called the Intelligent.

sn: अचेतनः सत्त्वसंख्याविमुक्तः सत्त्वात् परं चेतयतेऽन्तरात्मा। र्गुणातिगो मुच्यते सर्वपापैः॥
en: When the inner self, which is shorn of knowledge of nature, which is (as it were) unintelligent, becomes conversant with that which is above nature, then, understanding the Kshetra, and gifted with an intelligence that is above all qualities and apprehends everything, becoming released from all sins.

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: केचिद् ब्रह्ममयं वृक्षं केचिद् ब्रह्मवनं महत्। केचित्तु ब्रह्म चाव्यक्त केचित् परमनामयम्।
en: Some consider Brahman as a tree. Some consider Brahma as a great forest. Some consider Brahina as unmanifest. Some consider it as transcendent and freed from every distress.

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: मन्यन्ते सर्वमप्येतदव्यक्तप्रभवाव्ययम्॥ उच्छ्वासमात्रमपि चेद् योऽन्तकाले समो भवेत्। आत्मानमुपसङ्गम्य सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते॥ निमेषमात्रमपि चेत् संयम्यात्मानमात्मनि। गच्छत्यात्मप्रसादेन विदुषां प्राप्तिमव्ययाम्॥ प्राणायामैरथ प्राणान् संयम्य स पुनः पुनः। दशद्वादशभिर्वापि चतुर्विंशात् परं ततः॥
en: They think that all this is produced from and absorbed into the unmanifest. He who, even for the short space of time covered by a single breath, when his end comes, becomes equable, attaining to the self, fits himself for immortality. Controlling the self in the self, even for the space of a wink, one goes, through the tranquility of the self, to that which forms the endless acquisition of those that are endued with knowledge. Restraining the vital airs again and again by controlling them according to the method called Pranayama (suppression of vital airs), by the ten or the twelve, he attains to that which is beyond the four and twenty.

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: एवं पूर्वं प्रसन्नात्मा लभते यद् यदिच्छति। अव्यक्तात् सत्त्वमुद्रिक्तममृतत्वाय कल्पते॥ सत्त्वात् परतरं नान्यत् प्रशंसन्तीह तद्विदः।
en: Thus having first acquired a tranquil soul, one attains to the fruition of all his desires. When the quality of Goodness predominates in what originates from the Unmanifest, it becomes fit for immortality. They who are conversant with Goodness speak highly of it, saying that there is nothing superior to Goodness.

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: अनुमानाद् विजानीमः पुरुषं सत्त्वसंश्रयम्। न शक्यमन्यथा गन्तुं पुरुषं द्विजसत्तमाः॥
en: By inference we know that the Purusha is dependent on Goodness. O best of twice-born ones, it is impossible to attain to Purusha by any other means.

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: क्षमा धृतिरहिंसा च समता सत्यमार्जवम्। ज्ञानं त्यागोऽथ संन्यासः सात्त्विकं वृत्तमिष्यते॥
en: Forgiveness, courage, abstention abstention from injury, equability, truth, sincerity, knowledge, gift, and renunciation, are said to be the marks of that course of conduct which arises out of Goodness.

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: एतेनैवानुमानेन मन्यन्ते वै मनीषिणः। सत्त्वं च पुरुषश्चैव तत्र नास्ति विचारणा॥
en: It is by this inference that the wise believe in the oneness of Purusha and Goodness. There is no doubt in this.

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: आहुरेके च विद्वांसो ये ज्ञानपरिनिष्ठिताः। क्षेत्रज्ञसत्त्वयोरैक्यमित्येतन्नोपपद्यते॥
en: Some learned men that are devoted to knowledge hold that Kshetrajna and Nature are one. This, however, is not correct.

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: पृथग्भूतं ततः सत्त्वमित्येतदविचारितम्। पृथग्भावश्च विज्ञेयः सहजश्चापि तत्त्वतः॥
en: If it said that Nature is different from Purusha, that also will indicate a want of consideration.

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: तथैवैकत्वनानात्वमिष्यते विदुषां नयः। मशकोदुम्बरे चैक्यं पृथक्त्वमपि दृश्यते॥
en: Distinction and association should be truly known. Unity and diversity are likewise laid down. That is the doctrine of the learned. Even both unity and diversity are seen in the gnat and Udumbara.

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: मत्स्यो यथान्यः स्यादप्सु सम्प्रयोगस्तथा तयोः। सम्बन्धस्तोयबिन्दूनां पण कोकनदस्य च॥
en: As a fish in water is different from it, so is the relation of the two (viz., Purusha and Nature). Indeed, their relation is like that of water drops on the leaf of the lotus,

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: गुरुरुवाच इत्युक्तवन्तस्ते विप्रास्तदा लोकपितामहम्। पुनः संशयमापना: पप्रच्छुर्मुनिसत्तमाः॥
en: The Preceptor said, Thus addressed, those learned Brahmanas, who were the foremost of men, felt some doubts and (therefore) they once questioned the Grandfather. more

description: The relation between Nature and Soul
sn: गुरुरुवाच इत्युक्तवन्तस्ते विप्रास्तदा लोकपितामहम्। पुनः संशयमापना: पप्रच्छुर्मुनिसत्तमाः॥
en: The Preceptor said, Thus addressed, those learned Brahmanas, who were the foremost of men, felt some doubts and (therefore) they once questioned the Grandfather. more

sn: ऋषय ऊचुः को वा स्विदिह धर्माणामनुष्ठेयतमो मतः। व्याहतामिव पश्यामो धर्मस्य विविधां गतिम्॥
en: The Rishis said Which among the duties is considered to be the most worthy of being performed? The various modes of duty, we sec, are contradictory.

sn: ऊर्ध्वं देहाद् वदन्त्येके नैतदस्तीति चापरे। केचित् संशयितं सर्वं नि:संशयमथापरे॥
en: Some say that it continues after the body is destroyed). Others say that it does not exist. Some say that everything is doubtful. Others have no doubts.

sn: अनित्यं नित्यमित्येके नास्त्यस्तीत्यपि चापरे। एकरूपं द्विधेत्येके व्यामिश्रमिति चापरे॥
en: Some say that the eternal (principle) is not eternal. Some say that it exists, and some that it exists not. Some say it is of one form, or twofold, and others that it is mixed.

sn: मन्यन्ते ब्राह्मणा एव ब्रह्मज्ञास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः। एकमेके पृथक् चान्ये बहुत्वमिति चापरे॥
en: Some Brahmanas who are conversant with Brahma and utterers of truth consider it to be one. Others, that is distinct; and others again that it is manifold.

sn: देशकालावुभौ केचिन्नैतदस्तीति चापरे। जटाजिनधराश्चान्ये मुण्डा केचिदसंवृताः॥
en: Some say that both time and space exist; others, that it is not so. Some bear matted locks on their heads and are clad in deer-skins. Others have shaven heads and go entirely naked.

sn: अस्नानं केचिदिच्छन्ति स्नानमप्यपरे जनाः। मन्यन्ते ब्राह्मणा देवा ब्रह्मज्ञास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥
en: Some abstain entirely from bathing and some are for bathing. Such differences of views may be seen among celestials and Brahmanas conversant with Brahma and gifted with perceptions of truth.

sn: आहारं केचिदिच्छन्ति केचिच्चानशने रताः। कर्म केचित् प्रशंसन्ति प्रशान्तिं चापरे जनाः॥
en: Some are for taking food; while some are given to fasts. Some speak highly of action. Others speak highly of perfect tranquility.

sn: केचिन्मोक्षं प्रशंसन्ति केचिद् भोगान् पृथग्विधान्। धनानि केचिदिच्छन्ति निर्धनत्वमथापरे। उपास्यसाधनं साधनं त्वेके नैतदस्तीति चापरे॥
en: Some applaud Liberation. Some, various sorts of enjoyments. Some desire various kinds of riches. Some, poverty. Some say that means should be resorted to. Others, that this is not so.

sn: अहिंसानिरताश्चान्ये केचिद्धिंसापरायणाः। पुण्येन यशसा चान्ये नैतदस्तीति चापरे॥
en: Some are given to a life of abstention from injury. Others are inclined to destruction. Some are for merit and glory. Others say that this is not so.

sn: सद्भावनिरताश्चान्ये केचित् संशयिते स्थिताः। दुःखादन्ये सुखादन्ये ध्यानमित्यपरे जनाः॥
en: Some are devoted to goodness. Others are established on doubt. Some are for pleasure. Some are for pain. Others people say that it is meditation.

sn: यज्ञमित्यपरे विप्राः प्रदानमिति चापरे। तपस्त्वन्ये प्रशंसन्ति स्वाध्यायमपरे जनाः॥
en: Other learned Brahmanas say that it is Sacrifice. Others, again, say that it is gift. Others speak highly of penances. Others, the study of the scriptures.

sn: एवं व्युत्थापिते धर्मे ज्ञानं संन्यासमित्येके स्वभावं भूतचिन्तकाः। सर्वमेके प्रशंसन्ति न सर्वमिति चापरे।॥
en: Some say that knowledge and renunciation (should be followed). Others who ponder on the elements, say that it is nature. Some speak too much of everything. Others, nothing.

sn: बहुधा विप्रबोधिते। निश्चयं नाधिगच्छामः सम्मूढाः सुरसत्तम॥
en: O foremost of the celestials, duty being thus confused and full of contradictions of various kinds, we are deluded and unable to arrive at any conclusion.

sn: इदं श्रेय इदं श्रेय इत्येवं व्युस्थितो जनः। यो हि यस्मिन् रतो धर्मे स तं पूजयते सदा॥
en: People stand up for acting, saying, This is good, This is good. He who follow a certain duty speaks highly of that duty as the best.

sn: तेन नोऽविहिता प्रज्ञा मनश्च बहुलीकृतम्। एतदाख्यातमिच्छामः श्रेयः किमिति सत्तम॥
en: Therefore our understanding breaks down and our mind is distracted. We, therefore, wish, O best of all beings, to know what is good.

sn: अतः परं तु यद् गुह्यं तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति। सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोश्चापि सम्बन्धः केन हेतुना॥
en: You should declare to us, after this, what is (so) mysterious, and what is the cause of the connection between the Soul and Nature.

sn: एवमुक्तः स तैर्विप्रैर्भगवाँलोकभावनः। तेभ्यः शशंस धर्मात्मा याथातथ्येन बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Thus addressed by those learned Brahmanas, the illustrious creator of the worlds, endued with great intelligence and possessed of a righteous soul, described to them accurately what they asked.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच हन्त वः संप्रवक्ष्यामि यन्मां पृच्छथ सत्तमाः। गुरुणा शिष्यमासाद्य यदुक्तं तन्निबोधत॥
en: Well then I shall describe to you what you ask. Learn what was told by a preceptor to a disciple who came to him.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: समस्तमिह तच्छ्रुत्वा सम्यगेवावधार्यताम्। अहिंसा सर्वभूतानामेतत् कृत्यतमं मतम्॥
en: Hearing it all, do you settle properly (what it should be). Abstention from injuring any creature is considered as the foremost of all duties.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: एतत् पदमनुद्विग्नं वरिष्ठं धर्मलक्षणम्। ज्ञानं निःश्रेय इत्याहुवृद्धा निश्चितदर्शिनः॥
en: That is the highest seat, shorn of anxiety and forming a mark of holiness. The ancients who had seen the certain truth, have said that knowledge is the highest happiness.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: तस्माज्ज्ञानेन शुद्धेन मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः। हिंसापराश्च ये केचिद् ये च नास्तिकवृत्तयः। लोभमोहसमायुक्तास्ते वै निरयगामिनः॥ आशीर्युक्तानि कर्माणि कुर्वते ये त्वतन्द्रिताः। तेऽस्मिल्लोके प्रमोदन्ते जायमानाः पुनः पुनः॥ कुर्वते ये तु कर्माणि श्रद्दधाना विपश्चितः। अनाशीर्योगसंयुक्तास्ते धीराः साघुदर्शिनः॥
en: Hence, one becomes freed of all sins by pure knowledge. they who are engaged in destruction and harm, they who are infidels in conduct, have to go to Hell on account of their being gifted with cupidity and delusion. Those who, without idleness, perform acts moved thereto by expectation, become repeatedly born in this world and sport in happiness. Those men who, gifted with learning and wisdom, perforın acts with faith, free from expectations, and possessed of concentration of mind, are said to perceive clearly.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्यथा। संयोगो विप्रयोगश्च तन्निबोधत सत्तमाः॥ विषयो विषयित्वं च सम्बन्धोऽयमिहोच्यते।
en: I shall, after this. describe how the association and the disassociation takes place of Soul and Nature. You best of men, listen. The relation here is said to be that betwcen the object and the subject.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: विषयी पुरुषो नित्यं सत्त्वं च विषयः स्मृतः॥ व्याख्यातं पूर्वकल्पेन मशकोदुम्बरं यथा। भुज्यमानं न जानीते नित्यं सत्त्वमचेतनम्। यस्त्वेवं तं विजानीते यो भुङ्क्ते यश्च भुज्यते॥
en: Purusha is always the subject; and Nature the object. It has been explained, by what has been said in a previous part of the discourse where it has been pointed out, that they exist after the manner of the gnat and the Udumbara,

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: नित्यं द्वन्द्वसमायुक्तं सत्त्वमाहुर्मनीषिणः। निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्कलो नित्यः क्षेत्रज्ञो निर्गुणात्मकः॥
en: An object of enjoyment as it is, Nature is unintelligent and knows nothing. He, however, who enjoys it, is said to know it, Soul being enjoyer, Nature is enjoyed.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: समं संज्ञानुगश्चैव स सर्वत्र व्यवस्थितः। उपभुङ्क्ते सदा सत्त्वमप: पुष्करपर्णवत्॥
en: The wise have said that Nature is always made up of pairs of opposites. Soul is, on the other hand, destitute of pairs of opposites, devoid of parts, eternal, and free, about its essence, from qualities.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: सर्वैरपि गुणैर्विद्वान् व्यतिषक्तो न लिप्यते। जलबिन्दुर्यथा लोलः पद्मिनीपत्रसंस्थितः॥
en: He lives in everything alike, and walks with knowledge. He always enjoys Nature as a lotus leaf (enjoys) water.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: एवमेवाप्यसंयुक्तः पुरुषः स्यान्न संशयः। द्रव्यमात्रमभूत् सत्त्वं पुरुषस्येति निश्चयः॥
en: Endued with knowledge, he is never tainted even if brought into contact with all the qualities.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: यथा द्रव्यं च कर्ता च संयोगोऽप्यनयोस्तथा। यथा प्रदीपमादाय कश्चित् तमसि गच्छति।
en: Forsooth, Purusha is unattached like the unsteady drop of water on the lotus leaf. This is the certain conclusion that Nature is the property of Purusha.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: तथा सत्त्वप्रदीपेन गच्छन्ति परमैषिणः॥ यावद् द्रव्यं गुणस्तावत् प्रदीपः सम्प्रकाशते।
en: The relation between these two (viz., Purusha and Nature) is like that existing between matter and its maker. As one goes into a dark place carrying a light with him, so those who wish for the Supreme proceed with the light of Nature. As long as matter and quality exist, so long the light shines.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: क्षीणे द्रव्ये गुणे ज्योतिरन्तर्धानाय गच्छति॥ व्यक्तः सत्त्वगुणस्त्वेवं पुरुषोऽव्यक्त इष्यते।
en: The flame, however, becomes put out when matter and quality (or oil and wick) are exhausted. Thus Nature is manifest; while Purusha is said to be unmanifest.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: एतद् विप्रा विजानीत हन्त भूयो ब्रवीमि वः॥ सहस्रेणापि दुर्मेधा न बुद्धिमधिगच्छति।
en: Understand this, you learned Brahmanas! Well, I shall now tell you something more. With even a thousand (explanations), one who has a bad understanding succeeds not in acquiring knowledge.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: चतुर्थेनाप्यथांशेन बुद्धिमान् सुखमेधते॥ एवं धर्मस्य विज्ञेयं संसाधनमुपायतः। उपायज्ञो हि मेधावी सुखमत्यन्तमश्नुते॥
en: One, however, who is gifted with intelligence succeeds in acquiring happiness, through only a fourth share (c: explanations). Thus should the accomplishment of duty be understood as dependent on means. For the intelligent man, having knowledge of means, succeeds in acquiring supreme happiness.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: यथाध्वानमपाथेयः प्रपन्नो मनुजः क्वचित्। क्लेशेन याति महता विनश्येदन्तरापि च॥ तथा कर्मसु विज्ञेयं फलं भवति वा न वा।
en: As some man travelling along a road without provisions of his journey, proceeds with great uneasiness and may even meet with destruction before he reaches the end of his journey, so should it be known that in deeds there may or may not be fruits.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: पुरुषस्यात्मनिःश्रेयः शुभाशुभनिदर्शनम्॥ यथा च दीर्घमध्वानं पद्भ्यामेव प्रपद्यते। अदृष्टपूर्वं सहसा तत्त्वदर्शनवर्जितः॥ तमेव च यथाध्वानं रथेनेहाशुगामिना। गच्छत्यश्वप्रयुक्तेन तथा बुद्धिमतां गतिः॥ ऊर्ध्वं पर्वतमारुह्य नान्ववेक्षेत भूतलम्।
en: The examination of what is agreeable and what disagrceable is one's own self, yields benefit. The progress in life of a man who is devoid of the perception of truth is like that of a man who rashly journey on a long road unseen before. The progress, however, of those who are gifted with intelligence, is like that of men who journey along the same road, riding on a car to which are yoked (fleet) horses and which moves with swiftness. Having ascended to the top of a mountain, one should not cast his eyes on the surface of the earth.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: रथेन रथिनं पश्य क्लिश्यमानमचेतनम्॥ यावद् रथपथस्तावद् रथेन स तु गच्छति।
en: Sceing a man, even though travelling on a car, afflicted and rendered insensible by pain, the inielligent man journeys on a car as long as there is a car-path.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: क्षीणे रथपदे विद्वान् रथमुत्सृज्य गच्छति॥ एवं गच्छति मेधावी तत्त्वयोगविधानवित्। परिज्ञाय गुणज्ञश्च उत्तरादुत्तरोत्तरम्॥
en: The learned man, when he sees the car-path end, abandons his car for going on. Thus does the intelligent man who knows the ordinances about truth and Yoga, proceed. Knowing the qualities, such man, proceeds, comprehending what is next and next.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: यथार्णवं महाघोरमप्लवः सम्प्रगाहते। बाहुभ्यामेव सम्मोहाद् वधं वाञ्छत्यसंशयम्॥ नावा चापि यथा प्राज्ञो विभागज्ञः स्वरित्रया। अश्रान्तः सलिले गच्छेच्छीघ्रं संतरते ह्रदम्॥ तीर्णो गच्छेत् परं पारं नावमुत्सृज्य निर्ममः।
en: As one who plunges, without a boat, into the terrible ocean, with only ones two arms, through delusion, undoubtedly wishes for a range. After destruction; while the wise man conversant with distinctions, goes into the water, with a boat having oars, and soon crosses the lake without fatigue, and having crossed it gets to the other shore and leaves off the boat, freed from the thought of mineness.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: व्याख्यातं पूर्वकल्पेन यथा रथपदातिनोः॥ स्नेहात् सम्मोहमापन्नो नावि दाशो यथा तथा।
en: This has been already explained by the illustration of the car and the pedestrian. One who has been overwhelmed by delusion on account of attachment, sticks to it like a fisherman to his boat.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: ममन्वेनाभिभूत: संस्तत्रैव परिवर्तते॥ नावं न शक्यपारुह्य स्थले विपरिवर्तितुम्।
en: Overcome by the idea of mineness, one wanders within its narrow embarking on a boat it is not possible in moving about on land.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: तथैव रथमारुह्य नाप्सु चर्या विधीयते॥ एवं कर्म कृतं चित्रं विषयस्थं पृथक् पृथक्।
en: Likewise, it is not possible in moving abut on water after one has got on a car. There are thus various actions about various objects.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: यथा कर्म कृतं लोके तथैतानुपद्यते॥ यनैव गन्धिनो रस्यं न रूपस्पर्शशब्दवत्। मन्यन्ते मुनयो बुद्ध्या तत् प्रधानं प्रचक्षते॥ तत्र प्रधानमव्यक्तमव्यक्तस्य गुणो महान्।
en: And as action is performed in this world, so does it result to those who perform them. That which is void of smell. void of taste, and void of touch and sound, that which is meditated upon by the sages with the help of their understanding is said to be Pradhana. Now, Pradhana is unmanifest. A development of the uninanife-t is Mahat.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: महत्प्रधानभूतस्य गुणोऽहंकार एव च॥ अहंकारात् तु सम्भूतो महाभूतकृतो गुणः।
en: A development of Pradhana when it has become Mahat is Egoism. From egoism emanates the great elements.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: पृथक्त्वेन हि भूतानां विषया वै गुणाः स्मृताः॥ बीजधर्मं तथाव्यक्तं प्रसवात्मकमेव च।
en: And from the great elements respectively, the objects of sense proceed. The unmanifest is of the nature of seed. It produced its essence.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: बीजधर्मो महानात्मा प्रसवश्चेति नः श्रुतम्॥ बीजधर्मस्त्वहंकारः प्रसवश्च पुनः पुनः।
en: We have heard that the great soul has the virtues of a seed, and that is a product. Egoism is of the nature of seed and is a product again and again.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: बीजप्रसवधर्माणि महाभूतानि पञ्च वै॥ बीजधर्मिण इत्याहुः प्रसवं च प्रकुर्वते। विशेषाः पञ्चभूतानां तेषां चित्तं विशेषणम्॥ तत्रैकगुणमाकाशं द्विगुणो वायुरुच्यते।
en: And the five great elements are of the nature of seed and products. The objects of the five great elements are gifted with the nature of seed, and yield products. These have intelligence for their property. Among them, space has one equality; wind is said to have two.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: त्रिगुणं ज्यातिरित्याहुरामश्चपि चतुर्गुणाः॥ पृथ्वी पञ्चगुणा ज्ञेया चरस्थावरसंकुला।
en: Light, it is said, is gifted with three qualities; and water as possessed of four qualities. Earth, consisting of mobile and immobile, should be known as possessed of five qualities.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: सर्वभूतकरी देवी शुभाशुभनिदर्शिनी॥ शब्दः स्पर्शस्तथा रूपं रसो गन्धश्च पञ्चमः। एते पञ्च गुणा भूमेर्विज्ञेया द्विजसत्तमाः॥ पार्थिवश्च सदा गन्धो गन्धश्च बहुधा स्मृतः।
en: She is a goddess who is the source of all entities and abounds with examples of the agreeable and the disagreeable.' Sound, likewise touch, colour, taste, and smell for the fifth, these are the five qualities of earth, O foremost of twice-born ones. Smell always belongs to carth, and smell is said to be of various kinds.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: तस्य गन्धस्य वक्ष्यामि विस्तरेण बहून् गुणान्॥ इष्टश्चानिष्टगन्धश्च मधुरोऽम्लः कटुस्तथा। निर्हारी संहतः स्निग्धो रूक्षो विशद एव च॥ एवं दशविधो ज्ञेयः पार्थिवो गन्ध इत्युत।
en: I shall describe at length the numerous qualities of smell. Smell is agreeable or disagreeable, sweet, sour, pungent, diffusive and compact, oily and dry, and clear. Thus smell, which belongs to the earth, should be known as of ten sorts.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: शब्दः स्पर्शस्तथा रूपं द्रवश्चापां गुणाः स्मृताः॥ रसज्ञानं तु वक्ष्यामि रसस्तु बहुधा स्मृतः।
en: Sound, touch, colour, and taste have been said to be the qualities of water. I shall now speak or the qualities of Taste. Taste has been said to be of various kinds.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: मधुरोऽम्लः कटुस्तिक्तः कषायो लवणस्तथा॥ एवं षड्विधविस्तारो रसो वारिमयः स्मृतः।
en: Sweet, sour, pungent, bitter, astringent, and saline likewise. Taste, which has been said to Belong to water, is thus of six varieties.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: शब्दः स्पर्शस्तथा रूपं त्रिगुणं ज्योतिरुच्यते॥ ज्योतिषश्च गुणो रूपं रूपं च बहुधा स्मृतम्।
en: Sound, touch, and colour, these are the three qualities of light. Colour is the quality of light, and colour is said to be of various sorts.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: शुक्लं कृष्णं तथा रक्तं नीलं पीतारुणं तथा॥ ह्रस्वं दीर्घ कृशं स्थूलं चतुरस्रं तु वृत्तवत्। एवं द्वादशविस्तार तेजसो रूपमुच्यते॥ विज्ञेयं ब्राह्मणैवृद्धर्धमेज्ञैः सत्यवादिभिः।
en: White, dark, red, blue, yellow, and grey also, and short long, minute, gross, square and circular, of these twelve varieties is colour which appertains to light. These should be understood by Brahmanas venerable for years, knowing duties, and truthful in speech.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: शब्दस्पर्शी च विज्ञेयौ द्विगुणो वायुरुच्यते॥ वायोश्चापि गुणः स्पर्शः स्पर्शश्च बहुधा स्मृतः।
en: Sound and touch should be known as the two qualities of wind. Touch has been said to be of various sorts.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: रूक्षः शीतस्तथैवोष्णः स्निग्धो विशद एव च।॥ कठिनश्चिक्कण: श्लक्ष्णः पिच्छिलो दारुणो मृदुः। एवं द्वादशविस्तारो वायव्यो गुण उच्यते॥ विधिवद् ब्राह्मणैः सिद्धधर्मस्तित्त्वदर्शिभिः॥
en: Rough, cold and hot, tender and clear, hard, oily, smooth, slippery, painful and soft, of twelve kinds is touch, which is the quality of wind, as said by Brahmanas crowned with success, knowing duties, and possessed of a sight of truth.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: तत्रैकगुणमाकाशं शब्द इत्येव च स्मृतः। तस्य शब्दस्य वक्ष्यामि विस्तरेण बहून् गुणान्॥
en: Now, space has only one quality, and that is said to be sound. I shall speak at length of the numerous qualities of sound.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: घडजर्षभः स गान्धारो मध्यमः पञ्चमस्तथा। अतः परं तु विज्ञेयो निषादो धैवतस्तथा। अष्टश्चानिष्टशब्दश्च संहतः प्रविभागवान्॥
en: Shadaja, Rishabha, together with Gandhara, Madhyama, and likewise Panchama; after this should be known Nishada, and then Daivata, besides these, there are agreeable sounds and disagreeable sounds compact, and of many ingredients.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: एवं दशविधो ज्ञेयः शब्द आकाशसम्भवः। आकाशमुत्तमं भूतमहंकारस्ततः परः॥
en: Sound which is born of space should thus be known to be of ten sorts. Space is the highest of the (five) elements. Egoism is above it.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: अहंकारात् परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा ततः परः। तस्मात् तु परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात् पुरुषः परः॥
en: Above egoism is understanding. Above understanding is the soul. Above the soul is the Unmanifest. Above the Unmanifest is Purusha.

description: Abstention from Injury. Association and disassociation of Soul and Naturc.
sn: परापरज्ञो भूतानां विधिज्ञः सर्वकर्मणाम्। सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा गच्छत्यात्मानमव्ययम्॥
en: One who knows which is superior and inferior among existent creatures, who is conversant with the ordinances about all deeds. and who forms himself the soul of all creatures, attains to the Unfading Soul.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच भूनानामथ पञ्चानां यथैषामीश्वरं मनः। नियमे च विसर्गे च भूतात्मा मन एव च॥
en: Since the mind is the ruler of these five elements, for controlling and bringing them forth, the mind, therefore, is the soul of the elements.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: अधिष्ठाता मनो नित्यं भूतानां महतां तथा। बुद्धिरैश्चर्यमाचष्टे क्षेत्रज्ञश्च स उच्यते॥
en: The mind always presides over the great elements. The understanding proclaims power, and is called the Soul.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: इन्द्रियाणि मनो युङ्क्ते सदश्वानिव सारथिः। इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिः क्षेत्रज्ञे युज्यते सदा॥
en: The mind yokes the senses, as a charioteer yokes good horses. The senses, the mind, and the understanding are always joined to the Soul.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: महदश्वसमायुक्तं बुद्धिसंयमनं रथम्। समारुह्य स भूतात्मा समन्तात् परिधावति॥
en: The individual soul, mounting the chariot to which big horses are yoked and which has the understanding for the reins, drives about on all sides.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: इन्द्रियग्रामसंयुक्तो मन:सारथिरेव च। बुद्धिसंयमनो नित्यं महान् ब्रह्ममयो स्थः॥
en: With all the senses attached to it (for steeds), with the mind for the charioteer, and the understanding for the eternal reins, exists thc great Brahma car.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: एवं यो वेत्ति विद्वान् वै सदा ब्रह्ममयं रथम्। स धीरः सर्वभूतेषु न मोहमधिगच्छति॥
en: Indeed, that man gifted with learning and wisdom who always understands the Brahmacharin this way, is never possessed by delusion in the midst of all entities.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: अव्यक्तादि विशेषान्तं सहस्थावरजङ्गमम्। सूर्यचन्द्रप्रभालोकं ग्रहनक्षत्रमण्डितम्॥ नदीपर्वतजालैश्च सर्वतः परिभूषितम्। विविधाभिस्तथा चाद्भिः सततं समलंकृतम्॥ आजीवं सर्वभूतानां सर्वप्राणभृतां गतिः। एतद् ब्रह्मवनं नित्यं तस्मिंश्चरति क्षेत्रवित्॥
en: This forest of Brahina begins with the unmanifest and ends with gross objects. It includes mobile and immobile objects, and gets, light from the radiance of the sun and the moon, and is decorated with planets and constellations. It is decked, again, on all sides with nets of rivers and mountains. It is always embellished likewise by various kinds of waters. It is the means of livelihood for all creatures. It is, again, the end of all living creatures. In that forest the Kshetrajna always moves about.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: लोकेऽस्मिन् यानि सत्त्वानि सानि स्थावराणि च। तान्येवाग्रे प्रलीयन्ते पश्चाद् भूतकृता गुणाः।
en: Whatever exist in this world, mobile and immobile, are the very first to be dissolved away. After this (are dissolved) those qualities which compose all entities.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: गुणेभ्यः पञ्चभूतानि एष भूतसमुच्छ्रय:॥ देवा मनुष्या गन्धर्वाः पिशाचासुरराक्षसाः। सर्वे स्वभावतः सृष्टा न क्रियाभ्यो न कारणात्॥ एते विश्वसृजो विप्रा जायन्तीह पुनः पुनः।
en: After the qualities (are dissolved) the five elements. Such is the gradation of entities. Celestials, men, Gandharvas, Pishachas, Asuras, (and) Rakshasa, have all originated from Nature, and not from actions, nor from a cause. The Brahmanas, who are creators of the universe are born here again and again.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: तेभ्यः प्रसूतास्तेष्वेव महाभूतेषु पञ्चसु। प्रलीयन्ते यथाकालमूर्मयः सागरे यथा॥
en: All that originates from them dissolves, when the time comes, in those very five great elements like billows in the ocean.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: विश्वसृग्भ्यस्तु भूतेभ्यो महाभूतास्तु सर्वशः। भूतेभ्यश्चापि पञ्चभ्यो मुक्तो गच्छेत् परां गतिम्॥
en: All the great elements are beyond those elements which form the universe. He who is released from those five clements goes to the highest goal.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: प्रजापतिरिदं सर्वं मनसैवासृजत् प्रभुः। तथैव देवानृषयस्तपसा प्रतिपेदिरे॥
en: The powerful Prajapati created all this by the mind only. Similarly Rishis attained to the status of celestials by the help of penance.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: तपसश्चानुपूर्येण फलमूलाशिनस्तथा। त्रैलोक्यं तपसा सिद्धाः पश्यन्तीह समाहिताः॥
en: Likewise, those who have acquired perfection, who capable of the concentration of Yoga, and who live on fruits and roots, likewise perceive the triple world by penance.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: औषधान्यगदादीनि नानाविद्याश्च सर्वशः। तयसैव प्रसिद्ध्यन्ति तपोमूलं हि साधनम्॥
en: Medicines and herbs and all the various sciences are acquired by means of penance alone, for all acquisition has penance for its were root.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: यदुरापं दुराम्नायं दुराधर्षं दुरन्वयम्। तत् सर्वं तपसा साध्यं तपो हि दुरतिक्रमम्॥
en: Whatever is difficult of acquisition, difficult to learn, difficult to defeat, difficult to pass through, can all be acquired by penance, for penance is irresistible.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: सुरापो ब्रह्महा स्तेयी भ्रूणहा गुरुतल्पगः। तयसैव सुतप्तेन मुच्यते किल्बिषात् ततः॥
en: One who drinks alcoholic liquors, one who kills a Brahmana, one who steals, one who destroys a foe us, one who violates one's preceptor's bed, becomes cleansed of such sin by penance well performed.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: मनुष्याः पितरो देवाः पशवो मृगपक्षिणः। यानि चान्यानि भूतानि सानि स्थावराणि च॥ तपः परायणा नित्यं सिद्ध्यन्ते तपसा सदा। तथैव तपसा देवा महामाया दिवं गताः॥
en: Human beings, departed manes, deities, (sacrificial) animal, beasts and birds, and all other creatures mobile and immobile, by always devoting themselves to penances, become successful by penance along. Similarly the celestials gifted with great powers of illusion, have attained to the celestial region.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: आशीर्युक्तानि कर्माणि कुर्वते ये त्वतन्द्रिताः। अहंकारसमायुक्तास्ते सकाशे प्रजापतेः॥
en: Those who without idleness perforın deeds with expectation, being full of egoism, approach the presence of Prajapati.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: ध्यानयोगेन शुद्धेन निर्ममा निरहंकृताः। आप्नुवन्ति महात्मानो महान्तं लोकमुत्तमम्॥
en: Those great ones, however, who are devoid of mineness and freed from egoism through the pure contemplation of Yoga, acquire the great and highest regions.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: ध्यानयोगमुपागम्य प्रसन्नमतयः सदा। सुखोपचयमव्यक्तं प्रविशन्त्यात्मवित्तमाः॥
en: Those who understand best the self, having acquired Yoga contemplation and having their minds always cheerful, into the unmanifest accumulation of happiness.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: ध्यानयोगादुपागम्य निर्ममा निरहंकृताः। अव्यक्तं प्रविशन्तीह महतां लोकमुत्तमम्॥
en: Those persons who are freed from egoism and who are re-born after having attained to the fullness of Yoga contemplation, enter into the highest region reserved for the great, viz., the Unmanifest.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: अव्यक्तादेव सम्भूतः समसंज्ञां गतः पुनः। तमोरजोभ्यां निर्मुक्तः सत्त्वमास्थाय केवलम्॥ निर्मुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यः सर्वं सृजति निष्कलम्। क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तं विद्याद् यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्॥
en: Born from that same unmanifest (principle) and attaining to the same once more, frecd from the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance and adhering to only the quality of Goodness, one becomes freed from every sin and creates all things. Such a one should be known to be Kshetrajna in perfection. He who knows him knows the Veda. enter to

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: चित्तं चित्तादुपागम्य मुनिरासीत संयतः। याच्चित्तं तन्मयो वश्यं गुह्यमेतत् सनातनम्॥
en: Attaining pure knowledge from (restraining) the mind, the ascetic should sit self-controlled. One necessarily becomes that on which one's mind is set. This is an eternal mystery.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: अव्यक्तादिविशेषान्तमविद्यालक्षणं स्मृतम्। निबोधत तथा हीदं गुणैर्लक्षणमित्युत॥
en: That which has the unmanifest for its beginning and gross qualities for its end, has been said to have Ne-science for its mark. But do you understand that whose nature is shorn of qualities.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: व्यक्षरस्तु भवेन्मृत्युस्त्र्यक्षरं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्। ममेति च भवेन्मृत्युन ममेति च शाश्वतम्॥
en: Of two syllables is Mrityu (death); of three syllable is the eternal Brahma Mineness is death, and the opposite of mineness is the eternal.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: कर्म केचित् प्रशंसन्ति मन्दबुद्धिरता नराः। ये तु वृद्धा महात्मानो न प्रशंसन्ति कर्म ते॥
en: Some who led by bad understanding speak highly of action. Those, however, who are numbered among the great ancients never speak highly of action.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: कर्मणा जायते जन्तुर्मूर्तिमान् षोडशात्मकः। पुरुषं प्रसतेऽविद्या तद् ग्राह्यममृताशिनाम्॥
en: By action is a creature born with body which is made up of the sixteen. (True) Knowledge swallows up Purusha. This is what is highly acceptable to eaters of ambrosia.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: तस्मात् कर्मसु नि:स्नेहा ये केचित् पारदर्शिनः। विद्यामयोऽयं पुरुषो न तु कर्ममयः स्मृतः॥
en: Therefore, those whose vision extends to the other end have no attachment to actions. This Purusha, however is full of knowledge and not full of action.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: य एवममृतं नित्यमग्राह्यं शश्वदक्षरम्। वश्यात्मानमसंश्लिष्टं यो वेद न मृतो भवेत्॥
en: He dies not who understands Him' who is immortal, immutable, incomprehensible, men are eternal and indestructible-Him who is the restrained Soul and who is above all attachments.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: अपूर्वमकृतं नित्यं य एनमविचारिणम्। य एवं विन्देदात्मानमग्राह्यममृताशनम्। अग्राह्योऽमृतो भवति स एभिः कारणैर्भुवः॥
en: He who thus understands the Soul to which there is nothing prior, which is uncreated, immutable, unconquered, and incomprehensible even to those who are eaters of nectar, certainly becomes himself incomprehensible and immortal through these means.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: आयोज्य सर्वसंस्कारान् संयम्यात्मानमात्मनि। स तद् ब्रह्म शुभं वेत्ति यस्माद् भूयो न विद्यते॥
en: Removing all impressions and controlling the soul in the soul, he understands that auspicious Brahma than which nothing greater exists.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: प्रसादे चैव सत्त्वस्य प्रसादं समवाप्नुयात्। लक्षणं हि प्रसादस्य यथा स्यात् स्वप्नदर्शनम्॥
en: Upon the understanding becoming clear, he succeeds in acquiring tranquillity. The mark of tranquillity is like that what takes place in a dream.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: गतिरेषा तु मुक्तानां ये ज्ञानपरिनिष्ठिताः। प्रवृत्तयश्च याः सर्वाः पश्यन्ति परिणामजाः॥
en: This is the end of those liberated ones who are intent on knowledge. They sees all those movements which are born of successive developments.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: एषा गतिर्विरक्तानामेष धर्मः सनातनः। एषा ज्ञानवतां प्राप्तिरेतद् वृत्तमनिन्दितम्॥
en: This is the end of those who are unattached to the world. This is the eternal practice. This is the acquisition of men of knowledge. This is the uncensured made of conduct.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: समेन सर्वभूतेषु निःस्पृहेण निराशिषा। शक्या गतिरियं गन्तुं सर्वत्र समदर्शिना॥
en: This end is capable of being attained by one who is alike to all creatures, who is without attachment, who is without expectations, and who looks equally on all things.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: एतद् वः सर्वमाख्यातं मया विप्रर्षिसत्तमाः। एवमाचरत क्षिप्रं ततः सिद्धिमवाप्स्यथ॥
en: I have now described everything to you, O foremost of twice-born Rishis! Do you act thus immediately, you will then acquire success.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: गुरुरुवाच इत्युक्तास्ते तु मुनयो गुरुणा ब्रह्मणा तथा। कृतवन्तो महात्मानस्ततो लोकमवाप्नुवन्॥
en: The Preceptor said, Thus addressed by the preceptor Brahman, those great sages acted accordingly and then attained to many happy regions.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: त्वमप्येतन्महाभाग मयोक्तं ब्रह्मणो वचः। सम्यगााचर शुद्धात्मंस्ततः सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: Do you also, O blessed one, duly act according to the words of Brahman as described by me, O you of pure soul. You will then acquire success.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: वासुदेव उवाच इत्युक्तः स तदा शिष्यो गुरुणा धर्ममुत्तमम्। चकार सर्वं कौन्तेय ततो मोक्षमवाप्तवान्॥
en: Thus instructed in the principles of high religion by the preceptor, the pupil. O son of Kunti, did everything accordingly and then attained to Liberation.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: कृतकृत्यश्च स तदा शिष्यः कुरुकुलोद्वह। तत् पदं समनुप्राप्तो यत्र गत्वा न शोचति॥
en: Having done all that he should have done, the pupil, O perpetuator of Kuru's race, attained to that seat going where one has not to grieve.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: अर्जुन उवाच को न्वसौ ब्राह्मणः कृष्ण कश्च शिष्योजनार्दन। श्रोतव्यं चेन्मयैतद् वै तत्त्वमाचक्ष्व मे विभो॥
en: Arjuna said Who, indeed, was was that Brahmana, O Krishna, and who the pupil, O Janardana! Truly, if am worthy of hearing it, do you then tell me, O Lord!

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: वासुदेव उवाच अहं गुरुर्महाबाहो मनः शिष्यं च विद्धि मे। त्वत्प्रीत्या गुह्यमेतच्च कथितं ते धनंजय॥
en: I am the preceptor, O mighty armed one, and know that the inind is my pupil. Through my affection for you. O Dhananjaya, I have described this mystery to you.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: मयि चेदस्ति ते प्रीतिर्नित्यं कुरुकुलोद्वह। अध्यात्ममेतच्छ्रुत्वा त्वं सम्यगाचर सुव्रत॥
en: If you have any love for me, O perpetuator of Kuru family, do you then, after having heard these instructions about the Soul, always act only, O you of excellent vows.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: ततस्त्वं सम्यगाचीर्णं धर्मेऽस्मिन्नरिकर्षण। सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो मोक्षं प्राप्स्यसि केवलम्॥
en: Then when this religion has been duly practised, O destroyer of foes, you will become freed from all your sins and attain to perfect liberation.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: पूर्वमप्येतदेवोक्तं युद्धकाल उपस्थिते। मया तव महाबाहो तस्मादत्र मनः कुरु॥
en: Formerly, when the hour of battle came, this very religion, O you of mighty-arins, was described by me. Do you, therefore, set your mind on it.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: मया तु भरतश्रेष्ठ चिरदृष्टः पिता प्रभुः। तमहं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि सम्मते तव फाल्गुन॥
en: And now, O chief of Bharata's race, it is long since that I saw the lord my father. I wish to see him again, with your leave, O Phalguna.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तवचनं कृष्णं प्रत्युवाच धनंजयः। गच्छावो नगरं कृष्ण गजसाह्वयमद्य वै॥
en: Dhananjaya replied to Krishna who had said so. We shall go today from this town to Hastinapur.

description: The mind and the Dissolution of the Body described
sn: समेत्य तत्र राजानं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। समनुज्ञाप्य राजानं स्वां पुरीं यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Meeting king Yudhishthira of virtuous soul there, and informing him you shall then go to your own city.

sn: ततोऽभ्यनोदयत् कृष्णो युज्यतामिति दारुकम्। मुहूर्तादिव चाचष्ट युक्तमित्येव दारुकः॥
en: After this, Krishna ordered, Daruka, saying, Let my car be yoked. Within a very short space of time Daruka informed (his master), saying, It has been yoked.

sn: तथैव चानुयात्रादि चोदयामास पाण्डवः। सज्जयध्वं प्रयास्यामो नगरं गजसाह्वयम्॥
en: The son of Pandu then ordered all his attendants, saying, 'Prepare your selves and be ready. We shall go today to Hastinapur.

sn: इत्युक्ताः सैनिकास्ते तु सज्जीभूता विशाम्पते। आचख्युः सज्जमित्येवं पार्थायामिततेजसे॥
en: Thus addressed, O king, the army got themselves ready, and informed Pritha's son of immeasurable energy, saying, Everything is ready.

sn: ततस्तौ रथमास्थाय प्रयातौ कृष्णपाण्डवौ। विकुर्वाणौ कथाश्चित्राः प्रीयमाणौ विशाम्पते॥
en: Then those two friends, viz., Krishna and the son of Pandu, ascended their car and proceeded on the journey, engaged in delightful conversation.

sn: रथस्थं तु महातेजा वासुदेवं धनंजयः। पुनरेवाव्रवीद् वाक्यमिदं भरतसत्तम॥
en: To Vasudeva seated on the car, the highly energetic Dhananjaya once more said these words, O chief of the Bharatas.

sn: त्वत्प्रसादाज्जयः प्राप्तो राज्ञा वृष्णिकुलोद्वह। नियताः शत्रवश्चापि प्राप्त राज्यमकण्टकम्॥६
en: O perpetuator of the Vrishni race, the king has got victory through your grace. All his enemies have been killed, and he has recovered his kingdom without a thorn in it.

sn: नाथवन्तश्च भवता पाण्डवा मधुसूदन। भवन्तं प्लमासाद्य तीर्णाः स्म कुरुसागरम्॥
en: O destroyer of Madhu, on you the Pandavas have got a powerful protector having obtained you for our raft we have crossed the Kuru ocean.

sn: विश्वकर्मन् नमस्तेऽस्तु विश्वात्मन् विश्वसत्तम। तथ त्वामभिजानामि यथा चाहं भवन्मतः॥
en: O you who have this universe for your handiwork, salutations to you, O Soul of the universe, O best of all beings in the universe. I know you in that measure in which I am approved by you.

sn: त्वत्तेजःसम्भवो नित्यं भूतात्मा मधुसूदन। रतिः क्रीडामयी तुभ्यं माया ते रोदसी विभो॥
en: O destroyer of Madhu, the soul of every creature is always born of your energy. Playful sport is yours. Earth and sky, O lord, are your illusion.

sn: त्वयि सर्वमिदं विश्वं यदिदं स्थाणु जङ्गमम्। त्वं हि सर्वं विकुरुषे भूतग्रामं चतुर्विधम्॥
en: This entire universe, consisting of mobile and iinmobile objects, is established on you. You create, by modification, the four orders of Being.

sn: पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षं च द्यां चैव मधुसूदन। हसितं तेऽमला ज्योत्स्रा ऋतवश्चेन्द्रियाणि ते॥
en: You create the Earth, the Sky, and Heaven, O Destroyer of Madhu. The stainless Lunar light is your smile. The seasons are your senses.

sn: प्राणो वायुः सततगः क्रोधो मृत्युः सनातनः। प्रसादे चापि पद्मा श्रीनित्यं त्वयि महामते॥
en: The ever-moving wind is your breath, and death, existing eternally is your anger. In your grace is the goddess of prosperity. Indeed, Shree is always established in you, O you of the highest intelligence.

sn: रतिस्तुष्टि तिः क्षान्तिर्मतिः कान्तिश्चराचरम्। त्वमेवेह युगसन्तेषु निधनं प्रोच्यसेऽनध॥
en: You the sport; you their contentment; you their intelligence, you their are are forgiveness, you their inclinations, you their beauty. You are the universe with its mobile and immobile objects. At the end of the age, it is you, O sinless one, who are called destruction.

sn: सुदीर्घेणापि कालेन न ते शक्या गुंणा मया। आत्मा च परमात्मा च नमस्ते नलिनेक्षण॥
en: I am incapable of reciting all your qualities in course of even a long period. You are the Soul and the Supreme Soul. I bow to you, O you of eyes like the (petals of the) lotus.

sn: विदितो मे सुदुर्धर्ष नारदाद् देवलात् तथा। कृष्णद्वैपायताच्चैव तथा कुरुपितामहात्॥ त्वयि सर्वे समासक्तं त्वमेवैको जनेश्वरः। यच्चानुग्रहसंयुक्तमेतदुक्तं त्वयानध॥ एतत् सर्वमहं सम्यगाचरिष्ये जनार्दन। इदं चाद्भुतमत्यन्तं कृतमस्मत्प्रियेप्सया॥ यत्पापो निहतः संख्ये कौरव्यो धृतराष्ट्रजः। त्वया दग्धं हि तत्सैन्यं मया विजितमाहवे॥
en: O you who are irresistible. I have learnt it from Narada and Devala and the island-born (Vyasa), and the Kuru grandfather also, that all this (universe) rests on you. You are the one Lord of all creatures. This, O sinless one, that you have described to me on account of your favour for myself, I shall duly accomplish in full, O Janardana! Highly wonderful is this which you have done from desire of doing what is agreeable to us, viz., the destruction in battle of the Kaurava (prince), the son of Dhritarashtra. That army had been burnt by you which I (subsequently) defeated in battle.

sn: भवता तत्कृतं कर्म येनावाप्तो जयो मया। दुर्योधनस्य संग्रामे तव बुद्धिपराक्रमैः॥ कर्णस्य च वधोपायो यथावत् सम्प्रदर्शितः। सैन्धवस्य च पापस्य भूरिश्रवस एव च॥
en: That feat was achieved by you on account of which victory became mine! By the power of your intelligence was shown the ineans by which was duly effected the destruction of Duryodhana in battle, as also of Karna, as of the sinful king of the Sindhus, and Bhurishravas.

sn: अहं च प्रीयमाणेन त्वया देवकिनन्दन। यदुक्तस्तत् करिष्यामि न हि मेऽत्र विचारणा॥
en: I shall accomplish all that which, O son of Devaki, pleased with me you have declared to myself. I do not entertain any doubt in this.

sn: राजानं च समासाद्य धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। चोदयिष्यामि धर्मज्ञ गमनार्थं तवानघ।॥
en: Going to king Yudhishthira of righteous soul, I shall, O sinless one, urge him to dismiss you, O you who are conversant with every duty.

sn: रुचितं हि ममैतत्ते द्वारकागमनं प्रभो। अचिरादेव द्रष्टा त्वं मातुलं मे जनार्दन॥
en: O lord, I approve of departure for Dwraka. You shall soon see my maternal uncle, O Janardana.

sn: बलदेवं च दुर्धर्षं तथान्यान् वृष्णिपुङ्गवान्। एवं सम्भाषमाणौ तौ प्राप्तौ वारणसाह्वयम्॥
en: You shall also see the irresistible Baladeva and other chiefs of the Vrishni race!' This conversing with each other, the two reached the city of Hastinapur.

sn: तथा विविशतुश्चोभौ सम्प्रहृष्टनराकुलम्। तौ गत्वा धृतराष्ट्रस्य गृहं शक्रगृहोपमम्॥
en: They then, with cheerful hearts, and without any anxiety, entered the palace of Dhritarashtra which resembled the mansion of Shakra.

sn: ददृशाते महाराज धृतराष्ट्रं जनेश्वरम्। विदुरं च महाबुद्धि राजानं च युधिष्ठिरम्॥ भीमसेनं च दुर्धर्षं माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ। धृतराष्ट्रमुपासीनं युयुत्सु चापराजितम्॥ गान्धारी च महाप्रज्ञां पृथां कृष्णां च भामिनीम्। सुभद्राद्याश्च ताः सर्वा भरतानां स्त्रियस्तथा॥
en: They then saw, O monarch king Dhritarashtra, and highly intelligent Vidura, and king Yudhishthira; and the irresistibly Bhimasena, and the two sons of Madri by Pandu; and king Dhritarashtra seated; and the unvanquished Yuyutsu; and Gandhari of great wisdom, and Pritha, and the beautiful Krishna, and the other ladies of Bharata's race with Subhadra for the first.

sn: ददृशाते स्त्रियः सर्वा गान्धारीपरिचारिकाः। ततः समेत्य राजानं धृतराष्ट्रमरिंदमौ॥ निवद्य नामधेये स्वे तस्य पादावगृह्णताम्। गान्धार्याश्च पृथायाश्च धर्मराजस्य चैव हि॥ भीमस्य च महात्मानौ तथा पादावगृह्णताम्। क्षत्तारं चापि संगृह्य पृष्ट्वा कुशलमव्ययम्॥
en: They also saw all these ladies who used to wait upon Gandhari. Then approaching king Dhritarashtra, those two chastisers of enemies announced their names and touched his feet. Indeed, those great ones also touched the feet of Gandhari and Pritha and king Yudhishthira the just, and Bhima. Embracing Vidura also, they enquired after his well-being.

sn: तैः सार्धं नृपतिं वृद्धं ततस्तौ पर्युपासताम्। ततो निशि महाराजो धृतराष्ट्र: कुरूद्वहान्॥ जनार्दनं च मेधावी व्यसर्जयत वै गृहान्। तेऽनुज्ञाता नृपतिना ययुः स्वं स्वं निवेशनम्॥
en: In the company of all those persons, Arjuna and Krishna then approached king Dhritarashtra (again). Night came and then the intelligent king Dhritarashtra dismissed all those perpetuators of Kurus' race as also Janardana for retiring to their respective rooms. Permitted by the king, all of them entered their respective apartments.

sn: धनंजयगृहानेव ययौ कृष्णस्तु वीर्यवान्। तत्रार्चितो यथान्यायं सर्वकामरूपस्थितः॥ कृष्णः सुष्वाप मेधावी धनंजयसहायवान्। प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां कृत्वा पौर्वाह्निकी क्रियाम्॥ धर्मराजस्य भवनं जग्मतुः परमार्चितौ। यत्रास्ते स सहामात्यो धर्मराजो महाबलः॥
en: Krishna of great energy proceeded to the apartments of Dhananjaya, Adored duly and furnished with every object of comfort and enjoyment, Krishna of great intelligence passed the night in happy sleep with Dhananjaya as his companion. When the night passed away and morning came, the two heroes, finishing their morning rites and adoring their persons properly proceeded to the palace of king Yudhishthira the just. There Yudhishthira the just, of great might, sat with his ministers.

sn: तौ प्रविश्य महात्मानौ तद् गृहं परमार्चितम्। धर्मराजं ददृशतुर्देवराजमिवाश्विनौ॥
en: The two great ones, entering that welladorned chamber, saw king Yudhishthira the just like the two Ashvins seeing the chief of the celestials.

sn: समासाद्य तु राजानं वार्ष्णेयकुरुपुङ्गवौ। निषीदतुरनुज्ञातौ प्रीयमाणेन तेन तौ॥
en: Meeting the king, he of Vrishni's race, as also that foremost hero of Kuru's race, getting the permission of Yudhishthira who was highly pleased with them, sat themselves down.

sn: ततः स राजा मेधावी विवक्षू प्रेक्ष्य तावुभौ। प्रोवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठो वचनं राजसत्तमः॥
en: Then the king, king, gifted gifted with great intelligence, seeing those two friends, became desirous of addressing them. Soon that best of kings, that foremost of speakers, addressed them in the following words.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच विवक्षू हि युवां मन्ये वीरौ यदुकुरुद्वहौ। बूतं कर्तास्मि सर्वे वां नचिरान्मा विचार्यताम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said You heroes, you foremost ones of Yadu's and Kuru's race, it appears that you two are desirous of saying something to me. Do you say what is in your mind. I shall soon satisfy it. Do not hesitate.

sn: इत्युक्तः फाल्गुनस्तत्र धर्मराजानमब्रवीत्। विनीतवदुपागम्य वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः॥
en: Thus addressed, Phalguna, well conversant with speech, hunibly approached king Yudhishthira the just and then said these words.

sn: अयं चिरोषितो राजन् वासुदेवः प्रतापवान्। भवन्तं समनुज्ञाप्य पितरं द्रष्टुमिच्छति॥
en: Highly powerful Vasudeva here, O sing, is long absent from home. He wishes, with your permission, to see his sire.

sn: स गच्छेदभ्यनुज्ञातो भवता यदि मन्यसे। आनर्तनगरी वीरस्तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: Let him go, if you think it proper, to the city of the Anaritas! You should, O hero, grant him permission.

sn: पुण्डरीकाक्ष भद्रं ते गच्छ त्वं मधुसूदन। पुरी द्वारवतीमद्य द्रष्टुं शूरसुतं प्रभो॥
en: O lotus-eyed one, blessed be you! O slayer of Madhu, do you go this very day to the city of Dvaravati of seeing, O powerful one, that foremost one of Sura's race.

sn: रोचते मे महाबाहो गमनं तव केशव। मातुलश्चिरदृष्टो मे त्वया देवी च देवकी॥
en: O mighty-armed Keshava, your departure is approved by me! You have not seen my maternal uncle as also the goddess Devaki for a long time.

sn: समेत्य मातुलं गत्वा बलदेवं च मानद। पूजयेथा महाप्राज्ञ मद्वाक्येन यथार्हतः॥
en: Meeting my maternal uncle and going to Baladeva also, O giver of honours, you well, O you of great wisdom, adore both of them at my word as they deserve.

sn: स्मरेथाश्चापि मां नित्यं भीमं च बलिना वरम्। फाल्गुनं सहदेवं च नकुलं चैव मानद॥
en: Do you also think of me daily as also of Bhima, that foremost of powerful men, and of Phalguna and Nakula and Sahadeva, O giver of honours.

sn: आनर्तानवलोक्य त्वं पितरं च महाभुज। वृष्णीश्च पुनरागच्छेर्हयमेधे ममानघ॥
en: Having seen the Anaritas, and your father, O mighty-armed one, and the Vrishnis, you will return to my horse sacrifice, O sinless one!

sn: स गच्छ रत्नान्यादाय विविधानि वसूनि च। यच्चाप्यन्यन्मनोज्ञं ते तदप्यादत्स्व सात्वत॥
en: you like. Do you then go, taking with you various kinds of gems and various sorts of wealth. Do you, O hero of the Satvata race, also take with you whatever else

sn: इयं च वसुधा कृत्स्ना प्रसादात् तव केशव। अस्मानुपगता वीर निहताश्चापि शत्रवः॥
en: It is through your grace, O Keshava that the whole Earth, O hero, has come under our sway and all our enemies have been killed.

sn: एवं ब्रुवति कौरव्ये धर्मराजे युधिष्ठिरे। वासुदेवो वरः पुंसामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: When king Yudhishthira the just of Kuru's race said so, Vasudeva, that foremost of men, said these words (in reply).

sn: तवैव रत्नानि धनं च केवलं धरा तु कृत्स्ना तु महाभुजाद्य वै। यदस्ति चान्यद् द्रविणं गृहे मम त्वमेव तस्येश्वर नित्यमीश्वरः॥
en: O mighty-armed one, all jewels and gems, all riches and the entire Earth, belong to you alone. Whatever wealth exists in my house, you, O lord, are always the owner thereof.

sn: तथेत्यथोक्तः प्रतिपूजितस्तदा गदाग्रजो धर्मसुतेन वीर्यवान्। पितृष्वसारं त्ववदद् यथाविधि सम्पूजितश्चाप्यगमत् प्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: To him Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, said, 'Be it so' and then duly adored (Krishna) the oldest brother, gifted with great energy, of Gada. Vasudeva then proceeded to his paternal aunt (Kunti). Duly honouring her, he circumbulated her body.

sn: तया स सम्यक् प्रतिनन्दितस्तत स्तथैव सर्वैर्विदुरादिभिस्तथा। विनिर्ययौ नागपुराद् गदाग्रजो रथेन दिव्येन चतुर्भुजः स्वयम्॥
en: He was properly accosted by her in return, and then by all the others having Vidura for their first. The four-arined eldest brother of Gada then started from Nagapura on his excellent car.

sn: रथे सुभद्रामधिरोप्य भाविनी युधिष्ठिरस्यानुमते जनार्दनः। पितृष्वसुश्चापि तथा महाभुजो विनिर्ययौ पौरजनाभिसंवृतः॥
en: Placing his sister, the lady Subhadra, on the car, the mighty-armed Janardana, then, with the permission of both Yudhishthira and (Kunti) his paternal aunt, started, accompanied by a large train of citizens.

sn: तमन्वयाद् वानरवर्यकेतनः ससात्यकिर्माद्रवतीसुतावपि। अगाधबुद्धिर्विदुरश्च माधवं स्वयं च भीमो गजराजविक्रमः॥
en: The hero who had the foremost of apes on his banner, as also Satyaki, and the two sons of Madravati, and Vidura of incomparable intelligence, and Bhima himself whose tread resembled that of a prince of elephants, all followed Madhava.

sn: निवर्तयित्वा कुरुराष्ट्रवर्धनां स्ततः स सर्वान् विदुरं च वीर्यवान्। जनार्दनो दारुकमाह सत्वरः प्रचोदयाश्वानिति सात्यकिं तथा॥
en: Janardana of great energy, causing all those cxtenders of the Kuru kingdom and Vidura also to return, addressed Daruka, and Satyaki, saying, 'urge the horses to speed.'

sn: ततो ययौ शत्रुगणप्रमर्दनः शिनिप्रवीरानुगतो जनार्दनः। दिवं तथाऽऽनर्तपुरी प्रतापवान्॥
en: Then that grinder of enemies, viz., Janardana of great prowess, accompanied by Satyaki, the foremost one of Shini's race, proceeded to the city of the Anarttas, after having killed all his enemies, like He of a hundred sacrifices proceeding to the celestial region.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: तथा प्रयान्तं वार्ष्णेयं द्वारकां भरतर्षभाः। परिष्वज्य न्यवर्तन्त सानुयात्रा परंतपाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said, As he of Vrishni's family was going to Dwraka, those foremost princes of Bharata's race, those chastisers of enemies, embraced him and fell back with their attendants.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: पुनः पुनश्च वार्ष्णेयं पर्यष्वजत फाल्गुनः। आ चक्षुर्विषयाच्चैनं स ददर्श पुनः पुनः॥
en: Phalguna repeatedly embraced the Vrishni hero and as long as he was within he range of eye-sight he repeatedly turned his eyes towards him.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: कृच्छ्रेणैव तु तां पार्थो गोविन्दे विनिवेशिताम्। संजहार ततो दृष्टि कृष्णश्चाप्यपराजितः॥
en: With great difficulty, the son of Pritha withdrew his look that had fallen on Govinda. The undefeated Krishna also (did the same).

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: तस्य प्रयाणे यान्यासन् निमित्तानि महात्मनः। बहून्यद्भुतरूपाणि तानि मे गदतः शृणु॥
en: The marks which were displayed on the occasion of the great one's departure, I shall now fully describe. Do you listen to me.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: वायुर्वेगेन महता रथस्य पुरतो ववौ। कुर्वत्रिःशर्करं मागं विरजस्कमकण्टकम्॥
en: The wind blew with great force before the car, clearing the path of sand grains and dust and thorns.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: ववर्षं वासवश्चैव तोयं शुचि सुगन्धि च। दिव्यानि चैव पुष्पाणि पुरतः शार्ङ्गधन्वनः॥
en: Vasava rained pure and fragrant showers and celestial flowers before the holder of Sharnga.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: स प्रयातो महाबाहुः समेषु मरुधन्वसु। ददर्शाथ मुनिश्रेष्ठमुत्तङ्कममितौजसम्॥
en: As the mighty-armed hero went on he came upon the desert ill-supplied with water. there a he saw that foremost of ascetics, named Utanka, of immeasurable energy.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: स तं सम्पूज्य तेजस्वी मुनि पृथुललोचनः। पूजितस्तेन च तदा पर्यपृच्छदनामय॥
en: The hero of large eyes and grcat energy adored that ascetic. He was then adored by the ascetic in return Vasudeva then enquired after his well-being.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: स पृष्टः कुशलं तेन सम्पूज्य मधुसूदनम्। उत्तङ्को ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठस्तत: पप्रच्छ माधवम्॥
en: That foremost of Brahmanas, viz., Utanka, politely accosted by Madhava, honoured him duly and then addressed him in these words.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: कच्चिच्छौरे त्वया गत्वा कुरुपाण्डवसद्म तत्। कृतं सौभ्रात्रमचलं तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: O Shaurin, having gone to the palaces of the Kurus and the Pandavas, have you succeeded in establishing durable understanding between them such as should exit between brothers? You should tell me every thing.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: अपि संधाय तान् वीरानुपावृत्तोऽसि केशव। सम्बन्धिनः स्वदयितान् सततं वृष्णिपुङ्गव॥
