en: Do you come, O Keshava, after having united them in peace, them who are your relatives and who are ever dear to you, O forcmost one of Vrishni's race.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: कच्चित् पाण्डुसुताः पच्च धृतराष्ट्रस्य चात्मजाः। लोकेषु विहरिष्यन्ति त्वया सह परंतप॥
en: Will the five sons of Pandu, and the children of Dhritarashtra, o destroyer of enemies, sport in the world in joy with you?

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: स्वराष्ट्रे ते च राजानः कच्चित् प्राप्स्यन्ति वै सुखम्। कौरवेषु प्रशान्तेषु त्वया नाथेन केशव॥
en: Will all the kings enjoy happiness in their respective kingdoms, on account of the pacification of the Kauravas brought about by you?

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: या मे सम्भावना तात त्वयि नित्यमवर्तत। अपि सा सफला तात कृता ते भरतान् प्रति॥
en: Has that trust, O son, which I had always reposed on you, borne fruit about the Kauravas?

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच कृतो यत्नो मया पूर्वे सौम्ये कौवान् प्रति। नाशक्यन्त यदा साम्ये ते स्थापयितुमञ्जसा॥ ततस्ते निधनं प्राप्ताः सर्वे ससुतबान्धवाः। न दिष्टमप्यतिक्रान्तुं शक्यं बुद्ध्या बलेन वा॥
en: I tried my test at first, for bringing about a good understanding, about the Kauravas. When I could not by any means establish them on peace, it happened that all of them, with their relatives and kinsmen, died. It is impossible to transgress destiny by either intelligence of power.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: महर्षे विदितं भूयः सर्वमेतत् तवानघ। तेऽत्यक्रामन् मतिं मह्यं भीष्मस्य विदुरस्य च॥
en: O great Rishi, O sinless one, this also cannot he unknown to you. They (the Kauravas) disregarded which Bhishma and Vidura gave them referring to me.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: ततो यमक्षयं जग्मुः समासाद्येतरेतरम्। पञ्चैव पाण्डवाः शिष्टा हतामित्रा हतात्मजाः। धार्तराष्ट्राश्च निहताः सर्वे ससुतबान्धवाः॥
en: Encountering one another they then becaine guests of Yama's palace. Only the five Pandavas form the remnant of the un-slain, all their friends and all their children having been destroyed. All the sons Dhritarashtra also, with thcir children and kinsmen, have been killed.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: इत्युक्तवचने कृष्णे भृशं क्रोधसमन्वितः। उत्तङ्क इत्युवाचैनं रोषादुत्फुल्ललोचनः॥
en: When Krishna had said these words, Utanka, filled with anger, and with eyes expanded in rage, addressed him in these words.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: यस्माच्छक्तेन ते कृष्ण न त्राताः कुरुपुङ्गवाः। सम्बन्धिनः प्रियास्तस्माच्छप्स्येऽहं त्वामसंशयम्॥
en: Since, though able, O Krishna, you did not rescue those foremost ones of Kuru's race, who were your relatives and, therefore, dear to you, I shall, forsooth, curse you.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: न च ते प्रसभं यस्मात् ते निगृह्य निवारिताः। तस्मान्मन्युपरीतस्त्वां शप्स्यामि मधुसूदन॥
en: Since you did not forcibly compel them to forbear, therefore, O destroyer of Madhu, I shall, filled with anger denounce a course on you.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: त्वया शक्तेन हि सता मिथ्याचारेण माधव। ते परीताः कुरुश्रेष्ठा नश्यन्तः स्म ह्यपेक्षिताः॥
en: It seems, O Madhava, that, though fully able (to save them), you were in different to these foremost of Kurus who, overwhelmed by insincerity and hypocrisy, have all met with destruction.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: वासुदेव उवाच शृणु मे विस्तरेणेदं यद् वक्ष्ये भृगुनन्दन। गृहाणानुनयं चापि तपस्वी ह्यसि भार्गव॥
en: O scion of Bhrigu's race listen, to what I say in full. Do you accept my apologies also. O you of Bhrigu's race you are an ascetic!

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: श्रुत्वा च मे तदध्यात्म मुञ्चेथाः शापमद्य वै। न च मां तपसाऽल्पेन शक्तोऽभिभवितुं पुमान्॥
en: After having heard my words about the soul, you may then utter your curse. No man is able, by a little ascetic merit, to put me down.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: न च ते तपसो नाशमिच्छामि तपतां वर। तपस्ते सुमहद्दीप्तं गुरवश्चापि तोषिताः॥
en: O foremost of ascetics, I do not wish to see the destruction of all your penances! You have a large measure of blazing penances. You have passed your preceptors and seniors.

description: The meeting of Krishna and Utanka
sn: कौमारं ब्रह्मचर्यं ते जानामि द्विजसत्तम। दुःखार्जितस्य तपसस्तस्मन्निच्छामि ते व्ययम्॥
en: O foremost of twice-born ones. I know that you have observed the rules of Brahmacharya from your infancy. I do not, therefore wish the loss or diminution of your penances acquired with so much pain!

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच ब्रूहि केशव तत्वेन त्वमध्यात्ममनिन्दितम्। श्रुत्वा श्रेयोऽभिधास्यामि शापं वा ते जनार्दन॥
en: Utanka said Do you, O Keshava, tell ine that faultless spiritual science. Having heard your discourse I shall ordain what is for your good or imprecate a curse to you O Janardana!

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: वासुदेव उवाच तमो रजश्च सत्वं च विद्धि भावान् मदाश्रयान्। तथा रुदान् वसून् वापि विद्धि मत्प्रभवान् द्विज॥
en: Vasudeva said Know that the three qualities of Ignorance, Darkness and Goodness exist, depending on me as their refuge. So also, O twice-born one, know that the Rudras and the Vasus have originated from me.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: मयि सर्वाणि भूतानि सर्वभूतेषु चाप्यहम्। स्थित इत्यभिजानीहि मा तेऽभूदत्र संशयः॥
en: In me are all creatures, and in all creatures do I exist know this. Let no doubt arise in your mind about this.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: तथा दैत्यगणान् सर्वान् यक्षगन्धर्वराक्षसान्। नागानप्सरसश्चैव विद्धि मत्प्रभवान् द्विज॥
en: So also, O twice-born one, know that all the tribes of the Daityas, all the Yakshas, Gandharvas, Rakshasas, Nagas, Apsaras, have originated from me.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: सदसच्चैव यत् प्राहुरव्यक्तं व्यक्तमेव च। अक्षरं च क्षरं चैव सर्वमेतन्मदात्मकम्॥
en: Whatever has been called existent and nonexistent, whatever is manifest, and notmanifest, whatever is destructible and indestructible, all have me for their soul.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: ये चाश्रमेषु वै धर्माश्चतुर्धा विदिता मुने। वैदिकानि च सर्वाणि विद्धि सर्वं मदात्मकम्॥
en: Those fourfold courses of duty which, O ascetic, are known to attach to the (four) modes of life, and all the Vedic duties, have me for their soul.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: असच्च सदसच्चैव यद् विश्वं सदसत् परम्। मत्तः परतरं नास्ति देवदेवात् सनातनात्॥
en: Whatever is non-existent, whatever is existent and non-existent, and whatever is above that which is existent and not existent, all these which form the universe-are from me. There is nothing higher (or beyond) me who am the eternal god of gods.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: ओङ्कारप्रमुखान् वेदान् विद्धि मां त्वं भृगूद्वह। यूपं सोमं चरुं होमं त्रिदशाप्यायनं मखे॥ होतारमपि हव्यं च विद्धि मां भृगुनन्दन। अध्वर्युः कल्पकश्चापि हविः परमसंस्कृतम्॥ उद्गाता चापि मां स्तौति गीतघोषैर्महाध्वरे। प्रायश्चित्तेषु मां ब्रह्मशान्तिमङ्गलवाचकाः॥ स्तुवन्ति विश्वकर्माणं सततं द्विजसत्तम।
en: O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, know that all the Veda beginning with the original syllable) One are at one with me. Know, O son of Bhrigu's race, that I am the sacrificial stake; I am the Soma (drunk in sacrifices); I am the Charu (cooked in sacrifices for being offered to the deities); I am the Homa (that is performed); I am those deeds which sacrificers perform for pleasing the celestials; I am even the pourer of the sacrificial libation; and I am the Havi or libation that is poured. I am the Adhvaryu. I am the Kalpaka; and I am the highly sanctified sacrificial Havi. It is me whom the Udgatri, in the great sacrifice, hymns by the sound of his songs. In all rites of expiation, O Brahmana, the utters of auspicious Mantras and bencdictions fraught with peace sing my praises who am the artificer, o foremost of twice-born ones, of the universe.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: मम विद्धि सुतं धर्ममग्रजं द्विजसत्तम॥ मानसं दयितं विप्र सर्वभूतदयात्मकम्।
en: Know, O best of twice-born persons, that Dharma is my eldest-born offspring, originated from my mind, O learned Brahmana, whose essence is for all creatures.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: तत्राहं वर्तमानैश्च निवृत्तैश्चैव मानवैः॥ बह्वीः संसरमाणो वै योनीर्वामि सत्तम। धर्मसंरक्षणार्थाय धर्मसंस्थापनाय च॥
en: Constantly changing myself, I take birth in various wombs. O best of men, for upholding that son of mine, with the help of men now existing in or departed from the world. Indeed, I do this for protecting Virtue and for establishing it.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: तैस्तैर्वेषैश्च रूपैश्च त्रिषु लोकेषु भार्गव। अहं विष्णुरहं ब्रह्मा शक्रोऽथ प्रभवाप्ययः॥
en: In those forms that I assume for the purpose, I am known, O son of Bhrigu's race, in the three worlds as Vishnu and Brahman and Shakra. I am the origin and I am the destruction of all things.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: भूतग्रामस्य सर्वस्य स्रष्टा संहार एव च। अधर्मे वर्तमानानां सर्वेषामहमच्युतः॥
en: I am the creator of al existent objects and I am their destroyer. Knowing no change myself, I am the destroyer of all those creatures that live in sinfulness.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: धर्मस्य सेतुं बनामि चलिते चलिते युगे। तास्ता योनीः प्रविश्याहं प्रजानां हितकाम्यया।॥
en: In every cycle I have to repair the causeway of Virtue, entering into various kinds of wombs from desire of doing good to my creatures.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: यदा त्वहं देवयोनौ वर्तामि भृगुनन्दना तदाहं देववत् सर्वमाचरामि न संशयः॥
en: When, O son of Bhrigu's race, I live in the order of the celestials, I then indeed, act in i every respect as a celestial.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: यदा गन्धर्वयोनौ वा वर्तामि भृगुनन्दना तदा गन्धर्ववत् सर्वमाचरामि न संशयः॥
en: When I live in the order of the Gandharvas, I then, O son of Bhrigu's race, act in every . respect as a Gandharva.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: नागयोनौ यदा चैव तथा वर्तामि नागवत्। यक्षराक्षसयोन्योस्तु यथावद् विचराम्यहम्॥ ।
en: When I live in the order of the Nagas I then act as a Naga, and when I live in the order of Yakshas or that of Rakshasas, I act after the manner of that order.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: मानुष्ये वर्तमाने तु कृपणं याचिता मया। न च ते जानसम्मोहा वचोऽगृहन्त मे हितम्॥
en: Born now in the order of men I must act a human being. I appealed to them (the Kauravas) most piteously. But stupefied as they were and deprived of their senses, they refused to take my words.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: भयं च महदुद्दिश्य त्रासिताः कुरवो मया। क्रुद्धेन भूत्वा तु पुनर्यथावदनुदर्शिताः॥
en: I frightened them, filled with anger referring to some great fear. But once more I showed themselves my usual human forin.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: तेऽधर्मेणेहं संयुक्ताः परीताः कालधर्मणा। धर्मेण निहता युद्धे गताः स्वर्गं न संशयः॥
en: Possessed as they were of unrighteousness, and assailed by the virtue of liine, all of them have been righteously killed in battle, and have, forsooth, gone to the celestial region.

description: Spiritual Science described by Krishna to Utanka
sn: लोकेषु पाण्डवाश्चैव गताः ख्याति द्विजोत्तम। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: The Pandavas also, O best of Brahmanas have acquired great fame. I have these told you all that you had asked me.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच अभिजानामि जगतः कर्तारं त्वां जनार्दन। नूनं भवत्प्रसादोऽयमिति मे नास्ति संशयः॥
en: Utanka said I know you, O Janardana, to be the creator of the universe. Forsooth, this knowledge that I have is the result of your grace towards me.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: चित्तं च सुप्रसन्नं मे त्वद्भावगतमच्युत। विपिवृत्तं च मे शापादिति विद्धि परंतप॥
en: O you of unfading glory, my heart is possessed of cheerful tranquility on account of its being devoted to you. Know, O chastiser of enemies, that my heart is no longer inclined to curse you.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: यदि त्वनुग्रहं कंचित् त्वत्तोऽर्हामि जनार्दन। द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं तन्निदर्शय॥
en: If, O Janardana, I deserve the least grace from you, do you then show me once your supreme form.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः स तस्मै प्रीतात्मा दर्शयामास तद् वपुः। शाश्वतं वैष्णवं धीमान् ददृशे यद् धनंजयः॥
en: Pleased with him, the holy one then showed Uttanka that eternal Vaishnava form which Dhananjaya of great intelligence had seen.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: स ददर्श महात्मानं विश्वरूपं महाभुजम्। सहस्रसूर्यप्रतिमं दीप्तिमत् पावकोपमम्॥ सर्वमाकाशमावृत्य तिष्ठन्तं सर्वतोमुखम्।
en: Utanka saw the greet Vasudeva of universal form, gifted with mighty-arms. The effulgence of that form was like that of a burning fire or a thousand suns. It stood before him filling all space. It had faces on every side.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा परमं रूपं विष्णोर्वैष्णवमद्भुतम्। विस्मयं च ययौ विप्रस्तं दृष्ट्वा परमेश्वरम्॥
en: Sceing that high and wonderful Vaishnava form of Vishnu, in fact, seeing the Supreme Lord in (that guise) the Brahmana Utanka became filled with wonder.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच विश्वकर्मन् नमस्तेऽस्तु विश्वात्मन् विश्वसम्भव। पद्भ्यां ते पृथिवी व्याप्ता शिरसा चावृतं नभः॥
en: Utanka said O you whose handiwork is the universe. I bow to you, O soul of the universe, O parent of all things! With your feet you have covered the entire Earth, and with your head you fill the firmament.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: द्यावापृथिव्योर्यन्मध्यं जठरेण तवावृतम्। भुजाभ्यामावृताश्चाशास्त्वमिदं सर्वमच्युत॥
en: That which lies between the Earth and the firmament has been filled by your stomach. All the points of the compass are covered by your arms. O you of unfading glory, you are all this.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: संहरस्व पुनर्देव रूपमक्षय्यमुत्तमम्। पुनस्त्वां स्वेन रूपेण द्रष्टुमिच्छामि शाश्वतम्॥
en: Do you withdraw this excellent and indestructible forin of yours. I wish to see you now in your own (human) form which too, is eternal.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: तमुवाच प्रसन्नात्मा गोविन्दो जनमेजय। वरं वृणीष्वेति तदा तमुत्तङ्कोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ पर्याप्त एष एवाद्य परस्त्वत्तो महाद्युते। यत् ते रूपमिदं कृष्णं पश्यामि पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: To him, O Janaimejaya, Govinda of contented spirit said these words, Do you ask for some boon! To him Utanka, however said this is a sufficient boon from you for the present, O you of great splendour, in that, O Krishna, I have seen this form of yours, O foremost of all beings!

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: तमब्रवीत् पुनः कुष्णो मा त्वमत्र विचारय। अवश्यमेतत् कर्तव्यममोघं दर्शनं मम॥
en: Krishna, however, once more said to him, 'Do not scruple in this matter! This must be done! A sight of my form cannot be fruitless!

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: अवश्यं करणीयं च यद्येतन्मन्यसे विभो। तोयमिच्छामि यत्रेष्टं मरुष्वेतद्धि दुर्लभम्॥
en: I must accomplish that, O lord, which you think should be done! I wish to have water wherever my wish for it may arise. Water is scarce in such deserts!

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: ततः संहृत्य तत् तेजः प्रोवाचोत्तङ्कमीश्वरः। एष्टव्ये सति चिन्त्योऽहमित्युक्त्वा द्वारकां ययौ॥
en: Withdrawing that energy, the Supreme Lord then said to Utanka, Whenever you will require water, think of me!' Having said so, he proceeded towards of Dwraka.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: ततः कदाचिद् भगवानुत्तङ्गस्तोयकांक्षया। तृषितः परिचक्राम मरौ सस्मार चाच्युतम्॥
en: Subsequently, one day, the illustrious Utanka, solicitous of water and greatly thirsty, wandered over the desert. In course of his wanderings he thought of Krishna of unfading glory.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: ततो दिग्वाससं धीमान् मातङ्ग मलपङ्किनम्। अपश्यत मरौ तस्मिश्वयूथपरिवारितम्॥
en: The intelligent Rishi then saw in that desert a naked hunter (of the Chandala class), all besmeared with dirt, surrounded by a pack of dogs.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: भीषणं बद्धनिस्त्रिंशं बाणकार्मुकधारिणम्। तस्याधः स्रोतसोऽपश्यद् वारि भूरिद्विजोत्तमः॥
en: Extremely fierce-loO king, he carried a sword and was armed with bow and arrows. That foremost of twice-born ones saw copious streams of water issuing from the urinary organs of that hunter.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: स्मरन्नेव च तं प्राह मातङ्गः प्रहसन्निव! एहुनङ्क प्रतीच्छस्व मनो वारि भृगूद्वह॥
en: As soon as Utanka had thought of Krishna, that hunter smilingly addressed him, saying, O Utanka, oyou or Bhrigu's race, do yoil accept this water from me.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: कृपा हि पे सुमहती त्वां दृष्ट्वा तृट्समाश्रितम्। इत्युक्तस्तेन स मुनिस्तत् तोयं नाभ्यनन्दत॥
en: Seeing you afflicted by thirst I have felt great mercy for you! Thus addressed by the hunter, the ascetic showed no inclination to accept that water.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: चिक्षेप च स तं धीमान् वाग्भिरुयाभिरच्युतम्। पुनः पुनश्च मानङ्गः पिबस्वेति तमब्रवीत्॥
en: The intelligent Utanka even began to blame Krishna of undecaying glory. The hunter, however again and again addressed the Rishi, saying, 'Drink!'

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: न चापिबत् स सक्रोधः क्षुभितेनानन्तरात्मना। ते स तथा निश्चयात् तेन प्रत्याख्यातो महात्मना॥ श्वभिः सह महाराज नत्रैवान्तरधीयता उत्तङ्कस्तं तथा दृष्ट्वा ततो वोडितमानस:॥
en: The ascetic refused to drink the water thus given. On the other hand, with heart stricken with hunger and thirst, he even became angry. Disregarded by the great Rishi through that conviction, the hunter, O king, with his pack of dogs, disappeared there and then. Seeing that disappearance, Utanka felt himself ashamed.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: मेने प्रलब्धमात्मानं कृष्णेनामित्रघातिना। अथ तेनैव मार्गेण शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः॥ आजगाम महाबुद्धिरुत्तङ्कश्चैनमब्रवीत्। न युक्तं तादृशं दातुं त्वया पुरुषसत्तमा॥ सलिलं विप्रमुख्येभ्यो मातङ्गस्रोतसा विभो। इत्युक्तवचनं तं तु महाबुद्धिर्जनार्दनः॥ उत्तङ्क श्लक्ष्णया वाचा सान्त्वयनिदमब्रवीत्। यादृशेनेह रूपेण योग्यं दातुं धृतेन वै॥ तादृशं खलु दत्तं यच्च त्वं नावबुध्यथा:। मया त्वदर्थमुक्तो वै वज्रपाणिः पुरंदरः॥
en: He even thought that Krishna, that destroyer of enemies, had beguiled him. Soon after, the holder of the conch and discus and mace, gifted with great intelligence, came to Utanka by the way (along which the hunter had come). Addressing Krishna, the Brahmana said, 'O foremost of beings, it was hardly propet for you to offer water to foremost of Brahmanas in the form of a hunter's urine, O lord! Utanka who said these words, Janardana of great intelligence replied, comforting him with many soft words, “That form which it was proper to assume for offering you water, in that form was water was water offered to you! But, alas, you could not understand it! The holder of the thunderbolt, Purandara, was requested by me for your sake.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: उत्तङ्कायामृतं देहि तोयरूपमिति प्रभुः। स मामुवाच देवेन्द्रो न मोऽमर्त्यतां व्रजेत्॥
en: My words to that powerful celestial were, Do you give nectar in the form of water to Utanka. The king of the celestials replied to me, saying, It is not meet that a mortal should become immortal!

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: अन्यमस्मै वरं देहीत्यसकृद् भृगुनन्दन। अमृतं देयमित्येव मयोक्तः स शचीपतिः॥
en: Let some other boon be granted to Utanka! O son of Bhrigu's race, these words were repeatedly addressed to me. The husband of Sachi, however, was once more requested by me in these words, viz., even nectar should be given to Utanka!

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: स मां प्रसाद्य देवेन्द्रः पुनरेवेदमब्रवीत्। यदि देरमवश्यं वै मातङ्गोऽहं महामते॥ भूत्वामृतं प्रदास्यामि भार्गवाय महात्मने। यद्येवं प्रतिगृह्णाति भार्गवोऽमृतमद्य वै॥ प्रदातुमेष गच्छामि भार्गवोऽस्यामृतं विभो। प्रत्याख्यातस्त्वहं तेन दास्यामि न कथंचन॥ स तथा समयं कृत्वा तेन रूपेण वासवः। उपस्थितस्त्वया चापि प्रत्याख्यातोऽमृतं ददत्॥ चाण्डालरूपी भगवान् सुमहांस्ते व्यतिक्रमः। यत् तु शक्यं मया कर्तुं भूय एव तवेप्सितम्॥
en: The king of the celestials, then comforting me, said, If, Oyou of great intelligence, nectar is to be given to him. I shall then assume the form of a hunter and give it to that great descendant of Bhrigu. If that son of Bhrigu accepts it thus, I then go to him, O lord, for giving it to him! If, however, he sends me away from disregard, I shall not then give it to him by any means.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: तोयेप्सा तव दुर्धर्षां करिष्ये सफलामहम्। येष्वहःसु च ते ब्रह्मन् सलिलेप्सा भविष्यति॥ तदा मरौ भविष्यन्ति जलपूर्णाः पयोधराः। रसवच्च प्रदास्यन्ति तोयं ते भृगुनन्दन॥ उत्तङ्कमेघा इत्युक्ताः ख्याति यास्यन्ति चापि ते॥
en: Having made this agreement with me, Vasava appeared before you, in that disguise, for giving thee nectar. You, however, did disregard him and send him away, seeing that the illustrious one had put on the guise of a Chandala. Thy fault has been great. Once more, about your desire. I am prepared to do what is in my power. Indeed, this painful thirst of yours, I shall arrange, shall be satisfied. On those days, o twice-born one, in which you will feel a desire for water, clouds wellcharged with water will rise over this desert. Those clouds, O son of Bhrigu's race, will give you savoury water to drink. Indeed, those clouds will become known in the world as Utanka-clouds.

description: Krishna shows his supreme form to Utanaka
sn: इत्युक्तः प्रीतिमान् विप्रः कृष्णेन स बभूव ह। अद्याप्युत्तङ्कमेघाच मरौ वर्षन्ति भारत॥
en: Thus addressed by Krishna, Utanka became Glad, and to this day, O Bharata, Utankaclouds (appear and) shower rain on arid deserts.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: जनमेजय उवाच उत्तङ्कः केन तपसा संयुक्तो वै महामनाः। यः शापं दातुकामोऽभूद् विष्णवे प्रभविष्णवे॥
en: Janamejaya said With what penances was the great Uttanka endued so that he entertained the wish to imprecate a curse on Vishnu himself, who is the source of all power?

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उत्तको महता युक्तस्तपसा जनमेजय। गुरुभक्तः स तेजस्वी नान्यत् किंचिदपूजयत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Janamejaya, Utanka was gifted with austere penances. He was devoted to his preceptor. Gifted with great energy, he abstained from adoring anybody else.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सर्वेषामृषिपुत्राणामेष आसीन्मनीरथः। औत्तङ्की गुरुवृत्तिं वै प्राप्नुयामेति भारत॥
en: All the children of the Rishis, O Bharata, entertained even this desire, viz., that their devotion to preceptors should be as great as that of Utanka.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: गौतमस्य तु शिष्याणां बहूनां जनमेजय। उत्तङ्केऽभ्यधिका प्रीतिः स्नेहश्चैवाभवत् तदा॥
en: Gautama's gratification with and affection for Utanka, among his numberless disciples, were every great, O Janamejaya.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: स तस्य दमशौचाभ्यां विक्रान्तेन च कर्मणा। सम्यक् चैवोपचारेण गौतमः प्रीतिमानभूत्॥
en: Indecd, Gautama was greatly pleased with the self-control and purity of conduct that marked out Utanka, and with his acts or prowess and the services he did to him.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: अथ शिष्यसहस्राणि समनुज्ञातवानृषिः। उत्तङ्क परया प्रीत्या नाभ्यनुज्ञातुमैच्छता
en: One after another, thousands of disciples received the preceptors' permission to return home. On account, however, of his great affection for Utanka, Gautama could not permit him to leave his hermitage.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: नं क्रमेण जरा तात प्रतिपेदे महामुनिम्॥ न चान्वबुध्यत तदा स मुनिर्गुरुवत्सलः।
en: Gradually, in course of time, O son, decrepitude overtook Utanka, that great ascetic. The ascetic, however, on account of his devotion to his prcccptor, was not conscious of it.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ततः कदाचिद् राजेन्द्र काष्ठान्यानयितुं ययौ॥ उत्तङ्कः काष्ठभारं च महान्तं समुपानयत्।
en: One day, he started, O king for fetching fuel for his preceptor. Soon after Utanka brought a heavy load of fuel.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: स नद्भाराभिभूतात्मा काष्ठभारमरिंदम॥ निचिक्षेप क्षितौ राजन् परिश्रान्तो बुभुक्षितः।
en: Toil-worn and hungry and afflicted by the load he carried on his head, O chastiser of enemies, he threw the load down on the Earth, O king.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: तस्य काष्ठे विलग्नाभूज्जटा रूप्यसमप्रभा।॥ ततः काष्ठैः सह तदा पपात धरणीतले।
en: One of his matted locks, white as silver, had become entangled with the load. Accordingly, when the load was thrown down, with in fell on the earth that matted lock of hair.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ततः स भारनिष्पिष्टः क्षुधाविष्टश्च भारत॥ दृष्ट्वा तां वयसोऽवस्थां रुरोदार्तस्वरस्तदा।
en: Oppressed as he had been by that load and overcome by hunger, O Bharata, Utanka, secing that sign of old age, began to bewail a loud from excess of sorrow.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ततो गुरुसुता तस्य पद्मपत्रनिभानना॥ जग्राहाश्रूणि सुश्रोणी करेण पृथुलोचना। पितुर्नियोगाद् धर्मज्ञा शिरसाऽवनता तदा॥ तस्या निपेततुर्दग्धौ करौ तैरश्रुबिन्दुभिः।
en: Knowing every duty, the daughter of his preceptor then who had cyes resembling lotus petals, and hips that were full and round, at the command her father, sought, with downcast face, to hold Utanka's tears in her hands. Her hands scemed to burn with those tear-drops that she held. Unable, accordingly, to hold them longer, she was compelled to throw them down on the earth.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: न हि तानश्रुपातांस्तु शक्ता धारयितुं मही॥ गौतमस्त्वव्रवीद् विप्रमुत्तङ्क प्रीतमानसः। कस्मात् तात तवाद्येह शोकोत्तरमिदं मनः। स स्वैरं ब्रूहि विप्रर्षे श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: The Earth herself was unable to hold those tear-drops of Utanka. With a pleased heart, Gautama then said to the twice-born Utanka, 'Why, O son, is your mind so afflicted with grief today? Tell me calmly and quietly, O learned Rishi, for I wish to hear it in full.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच भवद्गतेन मनसा भवन्त्रियचिकीर्षया। भवद्भक्तिगतेनेह भवद्भावानुगेन च॥ जरेय नावबुद्धा मे नाभिज्ञातं सुखं च मे। शतवर्षोषितं मां हि न त्वमभ्यनुजानिथा:॥
en: Utanka said With mind entirely devoted to you, and wholly bent upon doing what is agreeable to you, with my heart's devotion turned to you, and with thoughts entirely living on you, (I have lived nere till) decrepitude has overtaken me without my knowing it at all. I have not, again, known any happiness. Though I have lived with you for a century yet you have not granted me perinission to depart.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: भवता त्वभ्यनुज्ञाताः शिष्याः प्रत्यवरा मम। अपपन्ना द्विजश्रेष्ठ शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Many disciples of yours, who were my juniors, have, however, been permitted by you to return. Indeed, hundreds and thousands of foremost Brahmanas have, gifted with knowledge, bcen favoured with your permission.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: गौतम उवाच त्वत्प्रीतियुक्तेन मया गुरुशुश्रूषया तव। व्यतिक्रामन्महाकालो नावबुद्धो द्विजर्षभ॥
en: Gautama said Through my love and affection for you, and on account of your dutiful services to me, a long time has passed without my knowing it, O foremost of Brahmanas.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: किं त्वद्य यदि ते श्रद्धा गमनं प्रति भार्गव। अनुज्ञा प्रतिगृह्य त्वं स्वगृहान् गच्छ मा चिरम्॥
en: If, however, O you of Bhrigu's race, you desire to leave this place, do you go without delay, with my permission.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच गुर्वर्थं कं प्रयच्छामि ब्रूहि त्वं द्विजसत्तम। तमुपाहृत्य गच्छेयमनुज्ञातस्त्वया विभो॥
en: Utanka said What shall I present to my preceptor? Tell me this, O best of twice-born persons. Having brought it, I shall go hence, O lord, with your permission.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: गौतम उवाच दक्षिणा परितोषो वै गुरुणां सद्धिरुच्यते। तव ह्याचरतो ब्रह्मस्तुष्टोऽहं वै न संशयः॥
en: Gautama said The good say that the satisfaction of the preceptor is the final fee. Forsooth, O twiceborn one, I have been highly pleased with your conduct.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: इत्थं च परितुष्टं मां विजानीहि भृगूद्वह। युवा षोडशवर्षो हि यद्यद्य भविता भवान्॥ ददानि पत्नी कन्यां च स्वां ते दुहितरं द्विजा एतामृतेऽङ्गना नान्या त्वत्तेऽर्हति सेवितुम्॥
en: Know, O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, that I have been highly pleased with your conduct. Know, Operpetuator of Bhrigu's race, that I have been very much pleased with you for this. If you become a young man today of sixteen years, I shall confer on you, O twice-born years, I shall confer on you. O twice-born one, this my own daughter for becoming your wife. No other woman except this one is capable of waiting upon your energy.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ततस्तां प्रतिजग्राह युवा भूत्वा यशस्विनीम्। गुरुणा चाभ्यनुज्ञातो गुरुपत्नीमथाब्रवीत्॥ कं भवेत्य प्रयच्छामि गुर्वर्थे विनियुक्ष्व माम्। प्रियं हितं च काङ्क्षामि प्राणैरपि धनैरपि।॥
en: At these words of Gautama. Utanka once again became a youth and accepted that famous maiden for his wife. Receiving the permission of his preceptor, he then addressed his preceptor's wife, saying, What shall I give you as final fee for my preceptor? Do you command me. I wish to do, with riches, or even my life, what is agreeable and beneficial to you.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: यद् दुर्लभं हि लोकेऽस्मिन् रत्नमत्यातं महत्। तदानयेयं तपसा न हि मेऽत्रास्ति संशयः॥
en: Whatever gem, exceedingly wonderful and of great value, exists in this world, I shall bring for you with the help of my penances. I have no doubt in this.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: अहल्योवाच परितुष्टास्मि ते विप्र नित्यं भक्त्या तवानघ। पर्याप्तमेतद् भद्रं ते गच्छ तात यथेप्सितम्॥
en: I am highly pleased with you, O learned Brahmana, with your unceasing devotion, O sinless one. This is enough. Blessed be you, go wherever you like.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: उत्तङ्कस्तु महाराज पुनरेवाब्रवीद् वचः। आज्ञापयस्व मां मातः कर्तव्यं च तव प्रियम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Utanka, however, O king, once more said these words, Do you command me, O mother. It is proper that I should do something that is agreeable to you.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सौदासपल्या विधृते दिव्ये मणिकुण्डले। ते समानय भद्रं ते गुर्वर्थः सुकृतो भवेत्॥
en: Ahalya said Blessed be you, bring for me those celestial ear-rings which are worn by the wife of Saudasa. That which is due to your preceptor will then be well-discharged.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: स तथेति प्रतिश्रुत्य जगाम जनमेजय। गुरुपत्नीप्रियार्थं वै ते समानयितुं तदा॥
en: Replying her, 'So be it'. Utanka went away. O Janamejaya, determined upon bringing those ear-rings for doing what his preceptor's wife liked.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: स जगाम ततः शीघ्रमुत्तङ्कणे ब्राह्मणर्षभः। सौदास पुरुषादं वै भिक्षितुं मणिकुण्डले॥
en: That foremost of Brahmanas, Utanka, proceeded forthwith to Saudasa who had become a cannibal, in order to solicit the earrings from him.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: गौतमस्त्वब्रवीत् पत्नीमुत्तको नाद्य दृश्यते। इति पृष्टा तमाचष्ट कुण्डलार्थे गतं च सा॥
en: Gautama meanwhile said to his wife —'Utanka is not to be seen today. Thus addressed, she informed him how he had gone for fetching the jewelled ear-rings (of Saudasa's queen).

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ततः प्रोवाच पत्नीं स न ते सम्यगिदं कृतम्। शप्तः स पार्थिवो नूनं ब्राह्मणं तं वधिष्यति॥
en: At this, Gautama said, 'You have not acted wisely. Cursed (by Vasishtha), that king will, indeed, kill Utanka.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: अजानन्त्या नियुक्तः स भगवन् ब्राह्मणो मया। भवत्प्रसादान्न भयं किंचित् तस्य भविष्यति॥
en: Ahalya said Without knowing this, O holy one I have engaged Utanka in this task. He shall not, however, come by any danger through your grace.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: इत्युक्तः प्राह तां पत्नीमेवमस्त्विति गौतमः। उत्तोऽपि वने शून्ये राजानं तं ददर्श ह॥
en: Thus addressed by her, Gautama said, 'Let it be so.' Meanwhile, Utanka met king Saudasa in a deserted forest.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स नं दृष्ट्वा तथाभूतं राजानं घोरदर्शनम्। दीर्घश्मश्रुधरं नृणां शोणितेन समुक्षितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Seeing the king, who had become so, of frightful appearance, wearing a long beard smeared with the blood of human beings, the Brahmana Utanka, O king, did not become moved.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: चकार न व्यथां विप्रो राजा त्वेनमथाब्रवीत्। प्रत्युत्थाय महातेजा भयकर्ता यमोपमः॥ दिष्ट्या त्वमसि कल्याण षष्ठे काले ममान्तिकम्। भक्ष्यं मृगयमाणस्य सम्प्राप्तो द्विजसत्तम॥
en: That highly energetic monarch, inspiring terror in every breast and loO king like a second Yama, rising up addressed Utanka, saying, ‘By good luck, O best of Brahmanas, you have come to me at the sixth hour of the day when I am in search of food.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: राजन् गुर्वर्थिनं विद्धि चरन्तं मामिहागतम्। न च गुर्वर्थमुद्युक्तं हिंस्यमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: Utanka said O king, know that I have come here in course of my wanderings for the sake of my preceptor, The wise have said that while one is engaged for the sake of one's preceptor, one should not be injured.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: षष्ठे काले ममाहारो विहितो द्विजसत्तम। न शक्यस्त्वं समुत्स्रष्टुं क्षुधितेन मयाद्य वै॥
en: The king said O best of Brahmanas, food has been ordained for me at the sixth hour of the day. I am hungry. I cannot, therefore, allow you escape today.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: एवमस्तु महाराज समयः क्रियतां त मे। गुर्वर्थमभिनिवर्त्य पुनरेष्यामि ने वशम्॥
en: Utanka said Let it be so, O king! Let this agreement be made with me! After I have ceased to wander for my preceptor I shall once more come and put myself within your power.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: संश्रुतश्च मया योऽर्थो गुरवे राजसत्तम। त्वदधीनः स राजेन्द्र तं त्वां भिक्षे नरेश्वर॥
en: I have heard, O best of kings, that the object I seek for my preceptor is under your control, O king, therefore, O king I beg you for it.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ददासि विप्रमुख्येभ्यस्त्वं हि रत्नानि नित्यदा। दाता च त्वं नरव्याघ्र पात्रभूतः क्षिताविह। पात्रं प्रतिग्रहे चापि विद्धि मां नृपसत्तम॥
en: You every day give many foremost of gems to superior Brahmanas. You are a giver, O king, from whom gifts may be accepted. know that I too am a worthy object of charity present before you, O best of kings.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: उपाहृत्य गुरारर्थं त्वदायत्तमरिंदम। समयेनेह राजेन्द्र पुनरेष्यामि ते वशम्॥ सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि नात्र मिथ्या कथंचन। अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे स्वैरेष्वपि कुतोऽन्यथा।॥
en: Having accepted from you in gift that object for my preceptor, which is under your control, I shall, O king, on account of my agreement, once more come back to you and put myself under your power. I assure you truly of this. There is no falsehood in this. Never before have I spoken any falsehood, no not even in jest! What shall I say then of other occasions?

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सौदास उवाच यदि मत्तस्तवायत्तो गुर्वथैः कृत एव सः। यदि चास्मि प्रतिग्राह्यः साम्प्रतं तद् वदस्व मे॥१११!
en: If the object you seck for your preceptor is capable of being placed in your hands by me. If। I be considered as one from whom a gift may be accepted, do you then say what that object is!

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच प्रतिग्राह्यो मतो मे त्वं सदैव पुरुषर्षभ। सोऽहं त्वामनुसम्प्राप्तो भिक्षितुं मणिकुण्डले॥
en: Utanka said O foremost of men, O Saudasa, in my estimation you are a worthy person from whom gifts may be accepted. I have, therefore, come to you for begging of you the jewelled earrings (worn by your queen).

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: पत्न्यास्ते मम विप्रर्षे उचिते मणिकुण्डले। वरयार्थं त्वमन्यं वै तं ते दास्यामि सुव्रत॥
en: Saudasa said Those jewelled ear-rings, O learned and twice-born Rishi, belong to my wife. They should be asked from her. Do you therefore, solicit some other things froin me. I shall give it to you, O you of excellent vows!

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: अलं ते व्यपदेशेन प्रमाणा यदि ते वयम्। प्रयच्छ कुण्डले मह्यं सत्यवाग् भव पार्थिव॥
en: Utanka said If we be considered as any authority, do you cease then to urge this pretext. Do you give those jewelled ear-rings to me. Be truthful in speech, O king.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: इत्युक्तस्त्वब्रवीद् राजा तमुत्तकं पुनर्वचः। गच्छ मद्वचनाद् देवीं ब्रूहि देहीति सत्तम॥ सैवमुक्ता त्वया नूनं मद्वाक्येन शुचिव्रता। प्रदास्यति द्विजश्रेष्ठ कुण्डले ते न संशयः॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Thus addressed, the king once addressed Utanka and said to him, Do you, at my word, go to my venerable queen, O best of men, and ask her saying, Give!' She of pure Vows, thus begged by you will certainly, at my command, give you, O foremost of twice-born persons, those jewelled ear-rings of hers without doubt. more

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच क्व पत्नी भवतः शक्या मया द्रष्टुं नरेश्वर। स्वयं वापि भवान् पत्नी किमर्थं नोपसर्पति॥
en: Utanka said Where, O king, shall I be able to meet your queen? Why do you not yourself go to her?

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सौदास उवाच तां द्रक्ष्यति भवानद्य कस्मिंश्चिद् वननिर्झरे। षष्ठे काले न हि मया सा शक्या द्रष्टुमद्य वै॥
en: Saudasa said You will find hier today near a forest fountain. I cannot see her today as the sixth hour of the day has come.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उत्तङ्कस्तु तथोक्तः स जगाम भरतर्षभ। मदयन्तीं च दृष्ट्वा स ज्ञापयत् स्वप्रयोजनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Thus addressed, Utanka, O chief of Bharata's race, then left that place. Seeing Madayanti, he informed her of his object.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सौदासवचनं श्रुत्वा ततः सा पृथुलोचना। प्रत्युवाच महाबुद्धिमुत्तकं जनमेजय॥
en: Hearing the order of Saudasa, that lady of large eyes replied to the highly intelligent Utanka, O Janamejaya, in these words.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: एवमेतद् वद ब्रह्मन् नानृतं वदसेऽनघ। अभिज्ञानं तु किंचित् त्वं समानयितुपर्हसि॥
en: It is even so, Otwice-born one. You should, however, O sinless one, assure me that you do not say what is untrue! You should bring me some signet from my husband.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: इमे हि दिव्ये मणिकुण्डले मे देवाश्च यक्षाश्च महर्षयश्च। तैस्तैरुपायैरमहर्तुकामा श्छिद्रेषु नित्यं परितर्कयन्ति॥
en: These celestial ear-rings of mine, made of rich gems, are such that the celestials and Yakshas and great Rishis always watch for opportunities for taking them away.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: निक्षिप्तमेतद् भुवि पन्नगास्तु रत्नं समासाद्य परामशेयुः। यक्षास्तेथोच्छिष्टधृतं सुराश्च निद्रावशाद् वा परिधर्षयेयुः॥
en: If placed at any time on the Earth, this costly article would then be stolen by the Nagas. If worn by one who is impure on account of eating, it would then be taken away by the Yakshas. If the wearer falls asleep, the celestials would then take them away.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: छिद्रेष्वेतेष्विमे नित्यं ह्वियेते द्विजसत्तम। देवराक्षसनागानामप्रमत्तेन धार्यते॥
en: O best of Brahmanas, these ear-rings are capable of being taken away when such opportunities come, by celestials and Rakshasas and Nagas, if worn by a careless person.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: स्यन्देते हि दिवा रुक्मं रात्रौ च द्विजसत्तम। नक्तं नक्षत्रताराणां प्रभामाक्षिप्य वर्ततः॥
en: O best of twice-born ones, these ear-rings, day and night, always produce gold. At night, they shine brightly, attracting the rays of stars and constellations.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: एते ह्यमुच्य भगवन् क्षुत्पिपासाभयं कुतः। विषाग्निश्वापदेभ्यश्च भयं जातु न विद्यते॥
en: O holy one, if worn by any one, he would be freed from hunger and thirst and fear of every sort. The wearer of these ear-rings is freed also from the fear of poison and fire and every kind of danger.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ह्रस्वेन चैते आमुक्ते भवतो ह्रस्वके तदा। अनुरूपेण चामुक्ते जायेते तत्प्रमाणके॥
en: If wom by one of short stature, these become short. If worn by one of tall stature, these grow in size.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: एवंविधे ममैते वै कुण्डले परमार्चित। त्रिषु लोकेषु विज्ञाते तदभिज्ञानमानय॥
en: Even of such virtucs are these ear-rings of mine. they lauded and honoured everywhere. Indeed, they are known over the three worlds. Do you, therefore, bring inc some sign. are

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स मित्रसहमासाद्य अभिज्ञानमयाचत। तस्मै ददावभिज्ञानं स चेक्ष्वाकुवरस्तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Returning to king Saudasa who was always well-disposed towards all his friends, Utanka solicited him for some sign. That foremost one of Ikshaku's race then gave him a sign.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सौदास उवाच न चैवैषा गतिः क्षेम्या न चान्या विद्यते गतिः। एतन्मे मतमाज्ञाय प्रयच्छ मणिकुण्डले॥
en: Saudasa said This my present condition is intolerable. I do not see any refuge. Knowing this to be my wish, do you give away the jewelled ear-rings.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: इत्युक्तस्तामुत्तङ्कस्तु भर्तुर्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्। श्रुत्वा च सा तदा प्रादात् ततस्ते मणिकुण्डले॥
en: Thus addressed by the king, Utanka returned to the queen and reported to her the world of her husband. Hearing those words, the queen gave to Utanka her jewelled ear-rings.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: अवाप्य कुण्डले ते तु राजानं पुनरब्रवीत्। किमेतद् गुह्यवचनं श्रोतुमिच्छामि पार्थिव॥
en: Having got the ear-rings, Utanka returned to the king and said to him, 'I wish to hear, O king, what the meaning is of those mysterious words which you said as a sign to your queen.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सौदास उवाच प्रजानिसर्गाद् विप्रान् वै क्षत्रियाः पूजयन्ति ह। विप्रेभ्यश्चापि बहवो दोषाः प्रादुर्भवन्ति वै॥
en: Saudasa said Kshatriyas are seen to honour the Brahmanas from the very beginning of the creation. Towards the Brahmanas, however, many offences originate (on the part of the Kshatriyas).

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सोऽहं द्विजेभ्यः प्रणतो विप्राद् दोषमवाप्तवान्। गतिमन्यां न पश्यामि मदयन्तीसहायवान्॥
en: As for myself, I am always bent in humility before them. I am overtaken by a calamity through a Brahmana. Possessed of Madayanti, I do not see any other refuge.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: न चान्यामपि पश्यामि गतिं गतिमतां वर। स्वर्गद्वारस्य गमने स्थाने चेह द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Indeed, O foremost of all persons, having a high goal, I do not see any other refuge for myself in the matter of approaching the celestial gates or in continuing here, O best of twice-born ones.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: न हि राज्ञा विशेषेण विरुद्धेन द्विजातिभिः। शक्यं हि लोके स्थातुं वै प्रेत्य वा सुखमेधितुम्॥
en: It is impossible for a king that is hostile to Brahmanas to continue living in this world or in acquiring happiness in the next.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: तदिष्टे ते मया दत्ते एते स्वे मणिकुण्डले। यः कृतस्तेऽद्य समय: सफलं तं कुरुध्व मे॥
en: Hence have I given you these my jewelled ear-rings which were coveted by you. Do you now keep the agreement which you have made with me today.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच राजस्तथेह कर्तास्मि पुनरेष्यामि ते वशम्। प्रश्नं च कंचित् प्रष्टु त्वां निवृत्तेऽस्मि परंतप॥
en: Utanka said O king, I shall certainly carry out my promise. I shall truly return and place myself under your power. There is, however, a question, O scorcher of enemies which I wish to ask you.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ब्रूहि विप्र यथाकामं प्रतिवक्तास्मि ते वचः। छेत्तास्मि सशयं तेऽद्य न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा॥
en: Saudasa said Say, O learned Brahmana, what is in your mind. I shall certainly reply to your words. I shall remove whatever doubt may being your mind. I have no hesitation in this.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: प्राहुर्वाक्संयतं विप्रं धर्मनैपुणदर्शिनः। मित्रेषु यश्च विषमः स्तेन इत्येव तं विदुः॥
en: Utanka said Those who are skilled in the rules of duty, say that Brahmanas are of controlled speech. One who acts wrongly towards friends is considered as vile as a thief.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: स भवान् मित्रतामद्य सम्प्राप्तो मम पार्थिव। स मे बुद्धिं प्रयच्छस्व सम्मतां पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: You, again, O king, have become my friend today. Do you then, O foremost of men, give me such advice as is approved by the wise.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: अवाप्तार्थोऽहमद्येह भवांश्च पुरुषादकः। भवत्सकाशमागन्तुं क्षमं मम न वेति वै॥
en: As for myself, I have now obtained the fruition of my wishes. You, again, are a cannibal. Is it proper for me to return to you or not.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सौदास उवाच क्षमं चेदिह वक्तव्यं तव द्विजवरोत्तम। मत्समीपं द्विजश्रेष्ठ नागन्तव्यं कथंचन॥
en: Saudasa said If it is proper (for me), O foremost of superior Brahmanas, to say what you ask, I should then, O best of twice-born ones, tell you that you should never return to me.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: एवं तव प्रपश्यामि श्रेयो भृगुकुलोद्वह। आगच्छतो हि ते विप्र भवेन्मृत्युर्न संशयः॥
en: O perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, by acting thus, you will secure your well-being. If you return, O learned Brahmana, you will surely meet with death.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः स तदा राज्ञा क्षमं बुद्धिमतां हितम्। अनुज्ञाप्य स राजानमहल्यां प्रतिजग्मिवान्॥
en: Thus addressed by the intelligent king about what was beneficial for him, Utanka took leave of the king and set out for the presence of Ahalya.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: गृहीत्वा कुण्डले दिव्ये गुरुपल्याः प्रियंकरः। जवेन महता प्रायाद् गौतमस्याश्रमं प्रति॥
en: Desirous of doing what was agreeable to the wife of his preceptor, he took the ear-rings with him and started with great speed for reaching the hermitage of Gautama.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: यथा तयो रक्षणं च मदयन्त्यभिभाषितम्। तथा ते कुण्डले बद्ध्वा तदा कृष्णाजिनेऽनयत्॥
en: Protecting them even in the manner directed by Madayanti, that is, binding them within the folds of his black, deer-skin, he proceeded on his way.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: स कस्मिंश्चित् क्षुधाविष्टः फलभारसमन्वितम्। बिल्वं ददर्श विप्रर्षिरारुरोह च तं ततः॥
en: After he had proceeded for some distance, he became stricken with hunger. He there saw a Bilva tree covered down with the weight of (ripe) fruits. He climbed that tree.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: शाखामासज्य तस्यैव कृष्णाजिनमरिंदम। पातयामास बिल्वानि तदा स द्विजपुङ्गवः॥
en: Causing his deer-skin, O chastiser of enemies, to hang on a branch, that foremost of twice-born ones, then began to pluck some fruits.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: अथ पातयमानस्य बिल्वापहृतचक्षुषः। न्यपतंस्तानि बिल्वानि तस्मिन्नेवाजिने प्रभो॥ यस्मिंस्ते कुण्डले बद्धे तदा द्विजवरेण वै। बिल्वप्रहारैस्तस्याथ व्यशीर्यद् बन्धनं ततः॥
en: While he was engaged in plucking those fruits with eyes set towards them, some of them dropped, O king, on that deer-skin, in which those ear-rings had been carefully tied by that foremost of Brahmanas. With the strokes of the fruits, the know became loosened.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सकुण्डलं तदजिनं पपात सहसा तरोः। विशीर्णबन्धने तस्मिन् गते कृष्णाजिने महीम्॥ अपश्यद् भुजगः कश्चित् ते तत्र मणिकुण्डले।
en: Suddenly that deer-skin, with the ear-rings in it, dropped down. When the know being unfastened, the deer-skin fell down on the ground, a snake who was there saw those jewelled ear-rings.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ऐरावतकुलोद्भूतः शीघ्रो भूत्वा तदा हि सः॥ विदश्यास्येन वल्मीकं विवेशाथ स कुण्डले। ह्रियमाणे तु दृष्ट्वा स कुण्डले भुजगेन ह॥ पपात वृक्षात् सोद्वेगो दुःखात् परमकोपनः। स दण्डकाष्ठमादाय वल्मीकमखनत् तदा॥
en: That snake belonged to the race of Airavata. Promptly he took up the ear-rings in his mouth and then entered an ant-hill. Seeing the ear-rings taken by that snake, Utanka, filled with anger and in great anxiety of mind, came down from the tree. Taking his staff he began to pierce that ant-hill.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: अहानि त्रिंशदव्यग्रः पञ्च चान्यानि भारत। क्रोधामर्षाभिसतंप्तस्तदा ब्राह्मणसत्तमः॥
en: That best of Brahmanas, burning with anger and the desire for revenge, continually busied himself for thirty-five days in that work.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: तस्य वेगमसा तमसहन्ती वसुन्धरा। दण्डकाष्ठाभिनुन्नाङ्गी चचाल भृशमाकुला॥
en: The goddess Earth, unable to bear the force of Utanka's walking staff and with body torn therewith, became greatly anxious.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ततः खनत एवाथ विप्रर्धर्धरणीतलम्। नागलोकस्य पन्थानं कर्तुकामस्य निश्चयात्॥ रथेन हरियुक्तेन तं देशमुपजग्मिवान्। वज्रपाणिर्महातेजास्तं ददर्श द्विजोत्तमम्॥
en: To that twice-born Rishi then, who continued to dig the Earth from desire of making a path to the nether regions inhabited by the Nagas, the king of the celestial, armed with the thunder, came there, on his car drawn by green horses. Gifted with great energy, he saw that foremost of Brahmanas, as he sat there engaged in his task.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स तु तं ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा तस्य दुःखेन दुःखितः। उत्तङ्कमब्रवीद् वाक्यं नैतच्छक्यं त्वयेति वै॥
en: Vaishampayana continued : LoO king like a Brahmana stricken with the sorrow of Utanka, the king of the celestials addressed him, saying, 'This (purpose of thine) is impracticable of being accomplished.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: इतो हि नागलोको वै योजनानि सहस्रशः। न दण्डकाष्ठसाध्यं च मन्ये कार्यमिदं तव॥
en: The regions of the Nagas are thousands of Yojanas removed from this place. I think that your purpose is impossible of being achieved with your walking staff.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच नागलोके यदि ब्रह्मन् न शक्ये कुण्डले मया। प्राप्तुं प्राणान् विमोक्ष्यामि पश्यतस्तु द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Utanka said If, O Brahmana, the ear-rings be not recovered by me from the regions of the Nagas, I shall renounce my life-breaths before your eyes, O foremost of twice-born persons.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच यदा स नाशकत् तस्य निश्चयं कर्तुमन्यथा। वज्रपाणिस्तदा दण्डं वज्रास्त्रेण युयोज ह॥
en: Vaishmpayana said When the thunder-armed Indra could not divert Utanka from his purpose, he united the latter's walking staff with the force of thunder.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ततो वज्रप्रहारैस्तैर्दार्यमाणा वसुन्धरा। नागलोकस्य पन्थानमकरोज्जनमेजय॥
en: Then, O Janamejaya, the Earth, opening with those strokes having the force of thunder, gave way to the (nether) regions inhabited by the Nagas.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: स तेन मार्गेण तदा नागलोकं विवेश ह। ददर्श नागलोकं च योजनानि सहस्रशः॥
en: By that path Utanka entered the world of Nagas. He saw that that region lying thousands of Yojanas on all sides.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: प्राकारनिचयैर्दिव्यैर्मणिमुक्तास्वलंकृतैः। उपपन्नं महाभाग शातकुम्भमयैस्तथा॥
en: Indeed, O blessed one, it had many walls made of pure gold and decked with jewels and gems.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: वापी: स्फटिकसोपाना नदीश्च विमलोदकाः। ददर्श वृक्षांश्च बहून् नानाद्विजगणायुतान्॥
en: There were many flue tanks of water furnished with flights of stair-cases made of pure crystal, and many rivers of clear and transparent water. He saw also many trees with various species of birds perching on them.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: तस्य लोकस्य च द्वारं स ददर्श भृगूद्वहः। पञ्चयोजनविस्तारमायतं शतयोजनम्॥
en: That perpetuator of Bhrigu's race saw the gate of that region which was full five Yojanas high and a hundred Yojanas in width.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: नागलोकमुत्तङ्कस्तु प्रेक्ष्य दीनोऽभवत् तदा। निराशश्चाभवत् तत्र कुण्डलाहरणे पुनः॥
en: Seeing the regions of the Nagas, Utanka became very dispirited. Indeed, he despaired of getting back the ear-rings.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: तत्र प्रोवाच तुरगस्तं कृष्णश्वेतवालधिः। ताम्रास्यनेत्रः कौरव्य प्रज्वलन्निव तेजसा॥
en: Then there appeared to him a black horse with a white tail. His face and eyes were of a coppcry colour, O you of Kuru's race, and he secmed to blaze forth with energy.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: धमस्वापानमेतन्मे ततस्त्वं विप्र लप्स्यसे। ऐरावतसुतेनेह तवानीते हि कुण्डले॥
en: Addressing Uttanka, he said, 'Do you blew into the Apana duct of my body. You will then, O learned Brahmana, get back your ear-rings which have been taken away by a descendant of Airvata's race.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: मा जुगुप्सां कृथाः पुत्र त्वमत्रार्थे कथंचन। त्वयैतद्धि समाचीर्णं गौतमस्याश्रमे तदा।॥
en: Do not hate to do my order, O son. You did it often at the hermitage of Gautama in former days.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच कथं भवन्तं जानीयामुपाध्यायाश्रमं प्रति। यन्मया चीर्णपूर्वं हि श्रोतुमिच्छामि तद्ध्यहम्॥
en: Utanka said How did I know you in the asylum of my preceptor? Indeed, I wish to hear how I did in those days what you order me to do now.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: अश्व उवाच गुरोगुरुं मां जानीहि ज्वलनं जातवेदसम्। त्वया ह्यहं सदा विप्र गुरोरर्थेऽभिपूजितः॥ विधिवत् सततं विप्र शुचिना भृगुनन्दन। तस्मा यो विधास्यामि तवैवं कुरु मा चिरम्॥
en: The horse said Know, O learned Brahmana, that I am the preceptor of your preceptor, for I am the blazing Jatavedas (deity of fire). By you I was often adored for the sake of your preceptor, O child of Bhrigu's race, duly and with a pure heart and body. I shall therefore accomplish what is for your will-being. Do my bidding forthwith.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: इत्युक्तस्तु तथाकार्षीदुत्तङ्कश्चित्रभानुना। घृतार्चिः प्रीतिमांश्चापि प्रजज्वाल दिधक्षया॥
en: Thus addressed by the god of fire, Uttanka did as he was ordered. The deity then, pleased with him, blazed up for consuming everything.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ततोऽस्य रोमकूपेभ्यो धम्यतस्तत्र भारता घनः प्रादुरभूद् धूमो नागलोकभयावहः॥
en: From the pores of his body, O Bharata, on account of his very nature, a thick smoke came out threatening terrors to the world of Nagas.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: तेन धूमेन महता वर्धमानेन भारत। नागलोके महाराज न प्रज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: With that powerful and wide-spreading smoke, O Bharata, everything became covered with darkness, so that nothing, O king, could any longer be seen in the world of the Nagas.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: हाहाकृतमभूत् सर्वमैरावतनिवेशनम्। वासुकिप्रमुखानां च नागानां जनमेजय॥
en: Cries of woe were heard throughout the place of the Airavatas, uttered by the Nagas headed by Vasuki, O Janamejaya.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: न प्रकाशन्त वेश्मानि धूमरुद्धानि भारत। निहारसंवृतानीव वनानि गिरयस्तथा॥
en: Covered by that smoke, the places could no longer be seen, O Bharata. These resembled forests and hills overwhelmed by a thick frost.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ते धूमरक्तनयना वह्नितेजोऽभितापिताः। आजग्मुनिश्चयं ज्ञातुं भार्गवस्य महात्मनः॥
en: With eyes that were red on account of that smoke and afflicted by the energy of the god of fire, the Nagas came out of their palaces to the greet son of Bhrigu's race for determining what was the matter.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: श्रुत्वा च निश्चयं तस्य महर्षेरतितेजसः। सम्भ्रान्तनयनाः सर्वे पूजां चक्रुर्यथाविधि।॥
en: Having heard what the matter was from that ascetic of incomparable energy, all the Nagas, with fear depicted on their eyes, offered him their adorations according to due forms.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: सर्वे प्राञ्जलो नागा वृद्धबालपुरोगमाः। शिरोभिः प्रणिपत्योचुः प्रसीद भगवन्निति॥
en: Indeed, all the Nagas placing the old and the young ones before them, bowed to him with their heads and joining their hands addressed him, saying, 'Be pleased with us, O holy one.'

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: प्रसाद्य ब्राह्मणं ते तु पाद्यमर्थ्य निवेद्य च। प्रायच्छन् कुण्डले दिव्ये पन्नगाः परमार्चिते॥
en: Having pleased that Brahmana and offered him water to wash his feet and the ingredients of the Arghya (for honouring him), the Nagas gave him those celestial and highly-adored earrings.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: ततः स पूजितो नागैस्तदोत्तङ्कः प्रतापवान्। अग्निं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा जगाम गुरुसा तत्॥
en: Thus honoured by them, Utanka of great prowess, going round the god of fire, started for the hermitage of his preceptor,

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: स गत्वा त्वरितो राजन् गौतमस्य निवेशनम्। प्रायच्छत् कुण्डले दिव्ये गुरुपत्न्यास्तदानघ॥
en: Indeed, going quickly to Gautama's hermitage, O king, he presented those earrings to the wife of his preceptor, O sinless one.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: वासुकिप्रमुखानां च नागानां जनमेजय। सर्वे शशंस गुरवे यथावद् द्विजसत्तमः॥
en: That best of Brahmanas also told his preceptor everything about Vasuki and the other Nagas that had occurred.

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: एवं महात्मना तेन त्रील्लोकान् जनमेजय। परिक्रम्याहृते दिव्ये ततस्ते मणिकुण्डले॥
en: It was thus, O Janamejaya, that the great Utanka, having wandered through the three worlds, fetched, those jewelled ear-rings (for his preceptor's wife).

description: The story of Utanka and Saudasa
sn: एवंप्रभावः स मुनिरुत्तको भरतर्षभा परेण तपसा युक्तो यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: Of such prowess, O chief of Bharata's race, was the ascetic Utanka. So austere were the penances with which he was gifted. I have thus told you what you had asked me.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: जनमेजय उवाच उत्तङ्कस्य वरं दत्त्वा गोविन्दो द्विजसत्तम। अत ऊर्ध्वं महाबाहुः किं चकार महायशाः॥
en: Janamcjaya said After having conferred that boon on Utanka, O foremost of twice-born persons, what did the mighty-armed. Govinda of great celebrity next do?

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उत्तङ्कस्य वरं दत्त्वा प्रायात् सात्यकिना सह। द्वारकामेव गोविन्दः शीघ्रवेगैर्महाहयैः॥
en: Having granted that boon to Utanka, Govinda, accompanied by Satyaki, went to Dwraka on his car, drawn by his large quickcoursing horse.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: सरांसि सरितश्चैव वनानि च गिरीस्तथा। अतिक्रम्याससादाथ रम्यां द्वारवतीं पुरीम्॥
en: Passing many lakes and rivers and forests and hills, he at last came upon the charming city of Dvaravati.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: वर्तमाने महाराज महे रैवतकस्य च। उपायात् पुण्डरीकाक्षो युयुधानानुपस्तदा॥
en: It was at the time, O king, when the festival of Raivataka had begun, that he having eyes like lotus-petals arrived with Satyaki as his companion.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: अलंकृतस्तु स गिरि नारूपैर्विचित्रितैः। बभौ रत्नमयैः कोशैः संवृतः पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Adorned with many beautiful things and covered with various Koshas made of jewels and gems, the Raivataka hill shone, O king, with great splendour.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: काञ्चनस्रग्भिरग्र्याभिः सुमनोभिस्तथैव च। वासोभिश्च महाशैलः कल्पवृक्षैस्तथैव च॥ दीपवृक्षैश्च सौवर्णैरभीक्ष्णमुपशोभितः। गुहानिर्झरदेशेषु दिवाभूतो बभूव ह॥
en: That high mountain, decked with excellent garlands of gold and gay festoons of flowers, with many large trees which looked like the Kalpa trees of Indra's garden, and with many golden poles on which were lighted lamps, shone in beauty through day and night. By the caves and fountains the light was so great that it appeared like a broad day.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: पताकाभिर्विचित्राभिः सघण्टाभिः समन्ततः। पुम्भिः स्त्रीभिश्च संघुष्टः प्रगीत इव चाभवत्॥
en: On all sides beautiful flags waved on the air with little bells that jingled continuously. The entire hill resounded with the sweet songs of men and women.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: अतीव प्रेक्षणीयोऽभून्मेरुर्मुनिगणैरिव। मत्तानां हृष्टरूपाणां स्त्रीणां पुंसां च भारत॥ गायतां पर्वतेन्द्रस्य दिवस्पृगिव निःस्वनः। प्रमत्तमत्त सम्मत्तक्ष्वेडितोत्क्रुष्टसंकुलः॥
en: Raivataka presents a most delightful appearance like Meru with all his jewels and gems. Men and women excited and filled with delight, O Bharata, sang aloud. The swell of music which thus arose from that foremost of mountains appeared to touch the very heavens. Everywhere were heard spouts and loud whoops of men who were in all forms of excitement.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: तथा किलकिलाशब्दैर्भूधरोऽभून्मनोहरः। विपणापणवान् रम्यो भक्ष्यभोज्यविहारवान्॥
en: The cackle of thousands of voices made that mountain delightful and charming. It was adorned with many shops and stalls filled with various foods and enjoyable article.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: वस्त्रमाल्योत्करयुतो वीणावेणुमृदङ्गवान्। सुरामैरैयमिश्रेण भक्ष्यभोज्येन चैव ह॥
en: There were heaps of cloths and garlands, and the music of Vinas and flutes and Mridangas was heard everywhere. Food mixed with wines of various kinds was stored here and there.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: दीनान्धकृपणादिभ्यो दीयमानेन चानिशम्। बभौ परमकल्याणो महस्तस्य महागिरेः॥
en: Gifts were being continually given to those that were distressed, or blind or helpless. For all this, the festival of that mountain became highly auspicious.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: पुण्यावसथवान् वीर पुण्यकृद्भिर्निषेवितः। विहारो वृष्णिवीराणां महे रैवतकस्य ह॥
en: There were many sacred houses built on the breast of that mountain, O hero, within which lived many pious men. Even thus did the Vrishni heroes sport in that festival of Raivataka.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: स नगो वेश्मसंकीर्णो देवलोक इवाबभौ। तदा च कृष्ण सांनिध्यमासाद्य भरतर्षभ॥ शक्रसद्मप्रतीकाशो बभूव स हि शैलराट्। ततः सम्पूज्यमानः स विवेश भवनं शुभम्॥ गोविन्दः सात्यकिश्चैव जगाम भवनं स्वकम्। विवेश च प्रहृष्टात्मा चिरकालप्रवासतः॥ कृत्वा नसुकरं कर्म दानवेष्विव वासवः। उपायान्तं तु वार्ष्णेयं भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकास्तथा।॥ अभ्यगच्छन् महात्मानं देवा इव शतक्रतुम्।
en: Equipt with those palaces that mountain appeared like second Heaven. At the arrival Krishna, O chief of Bharata's race, that prince of mountains resembled the blessed mansion of Indra himself. Adored (by his relatives), Krishna then entered a beautiful palace. Satyaki also went to his own quarters with a delighted soul. Govinda entered his residence after a long absence, having accomplished deeds of great difficulty like Vasava amid the Danava host. The heroes of the Bhoja, Vrishni, and Andhaka races, all came forward to receive that great one like the deities advancing to receive the deity of a hundred sacrifices.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: स तानभ्यर्च्य मेधावी पृष्ट्वा च कुशलं तदा। अभ्यवादयत प्रीतः पितरं मातरं तदा॥
en: Gifted with great intelligence, he honoured them in return and enquired after their wellbeing. With a pleased heart he then saluted his father and mother.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: ताभ्यां स सम्परिष्वक्तः सान्त्वितश्च महाभुजः। उपोपविष्टैः सर्वैस्तैर्वृष्णिभिः परिवारितः॥
en: The mighty-armed hero was embraced by both of them and comforted too. He then took his seat with all the Vrishnis sitting around him.

description: The return of Krishna to dwarka
sn: स विश्रान्तो महातेजाः कृतपादावनेजनः। कथयामास तत्सर्वं पृष्टः पित्रा महाहवम्॥
en: Having washed his feet and removed his fatigue, Krishna of mighty energy, as he sat there, then described the chief events of the great battle in answer to the questions put to him by his father.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच श्रुतवानस्मि वार्ष्णेय संग्रामं परमाद्भुतम्। नराणां वदतां तत्र कथं वा तेषु नित्यशः॥
en: Vasudeva said O you of Vrishni's race, I have repeatedly heard men speaking of the wonderful battle.

sn: त्वं तु प्रत्यक्षदर्शी च रूपज्ञश्च महाभुजा तस्मात् प्रब्रूहि संग्रामं याथातथ्येन मेऽनघ॥
en: You however, O mighty-armed one, have seen it with your own eyes. Do you, therefore, O sinless one, describe the battle in full.

sn: यथा तदभवद् युद्धं पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। भीष्मकर्णकृपद्रोणशल्यादिभिरनुत्तमम्॥ अन्येषां क्षत्रियाणां च कृतास्त्राणामनेकशः। नानावेषाकृतिमतां नानादेशनिवासिनाम्॥
en: Indeed, tell me how that battle took place between the great Pandavas and Bhishma and Karna and Kripa and Drona and Shalya and others, between, in fact, numerous other Kshatriyas well-skilled in arms, differing from one another in conduct and dress and coming from various kingdoms.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः पुण्डरीकाक्षः पित्रा मातुस्तदन्तिके। शशंस कुरुवीराणां संग्रामे निधनं यथा।॥
en: Vaishmpayana said Thus addressed by his father, he having eyes like lotus-petals, described, in the presence of his mother also, how the Kaurava heroes had been killed in battle.

sn: अत्युद्धतानि कर्माणि क्षत्रियाणां महात्मनाम्। बहुलत्वान्न संख्यातुं शक्यान्यब्दशतैरपि॥
en: Vasudeva said-The feats were highly wonderful which were achieved by those great Kshatriyas. On account of their large number, they are incapable of being described in even hundreds of years.

sn: प्राधान्यतस्तु गदतः समासेनैव मे शृणु। कर्माणि पृथिवीशानां यथावदमरधुते॥
en: I shall, however, mention only the foremost of them. Do you listen, therefore, to me as I mention in brief those feats won by the kings of Earth, O you of godlike splendour.

sn: भीष्मः सेनापतिरभूदेकादशचभूपतिः। कौरव्यः कौरवेन्द्राणां देवानामिव वासवः॥
en: Bhishma of Kuru's race became the Commander-in-chief, having eleven divisions of the Kaurava princes under his command, like Vasava of the celestial forces.

sn: शिखण्डी पाण्डुपुत्राणां नेता सप्तचमूपतिः। बभूव रक्षितो धीमान् श्रीमता सत्यसाचिना॥
en: Highly intelligent Shikhandin, protected by the blessed Arjuna, became the leader of the seven divisions of the sons of Pandu.

sn: तेषां तदभवद् युद्धं दशाहानि महात्मनाम्। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च सुमहल्लोमहर्षणम्॥
en: The battle betwcen the Kurus and the Pandavas went on for ten days. It was so dreadful as to make one's hair stand erect.

sn: तत: शिखण्डी गाङ्गेयं युध्यमानं महाहवे। जघान बहुभिर्बाणैः सह गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: Then Shikhandin, in great battle, hciped by the holder of Gandiva, killed, with innumerable arrows, the son of Ganga, fighting bravely.

sn: अकरोत् स ततः कालं शरतल्पगतो मुनिः। अयनं दक्षिणं हित्वा सम्प्राप्ते चोत्तरायणे॥
en: Lying on abcd of arrows, Bhishma waited like an ascetic till the sun leaving his southwards path entered on his northerly course when that hero died.

sn: ततः सेनापतिरभूद् द्रोणोऽस्त्रविदुषां वरः। प्रवीरः कौरवेन्द्रस्य काव्यो दैत्यपतेरिव॥
en: Then Drona, that foremost of all persons conversant with arms, that greatest of men under Duryodhana, like Kavya himself of the lord of the Daityas, became the Commanderin-chief.

sn: अक्षौहिणीभिः शिष्टाभिर्नवभिर्द्विजसत्तमः। संवृतः समरश्लाघी गुप्तः कृपवृषादिभिः॥
en: That foremost of twice-born persons, ever boasting of his prowess in battle, was supported by the residue of the Kaurava-army consisting then of nine Akshauhinis, and protected by Kripa and Vrisha and others.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्त्वभून्नेता पाण्डवानां महास्त्रवित्। गुप्तो भीमेन मेधावी मित्रेण वरुणो यथा॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna familiar with many powerful weapons, and gifted with great intelligence, became became the leader of the Pandavas. He was protected by Bhima like Varuna protected by Mitra.

sn: स च सेनापरिवृतो द्रोणप्रेप्सुर्महामनाः। पितुर्निकारान् संस्मृत्य रणे कर्माकरोन्महत्॥
en: That great hero, always desirous of comparing his strength with Drona, supported by the Pandava-army, and recollecting the wrongs inflicted (by Drona) on his father (Drupada, the king of the Panchalas) performed great feats in battlc.

sn: तस्मिंस्ते पृथिवीपाला द्रोणपार्षतसंगरे। नानादिगागता वीराः प्रायशो निधनं गताः॥
en: In that battle between Drona and the son of Prishata, the kings assembled from various realms were nearly rooted out.

sn: दिनानि पञ्च तद् युद्धमभूत् परमदारुणम् ततो द्रोणः परिश्रान्तो धृष्टद्युम्नवशं गतः॥
en: That furious battle lasted for five days. At the conclusion of that period, Drona, exhausted, succumbed to Dhrishtadyumna.

sn: ततः सेनापतिरभूत् कर्णो दौर्योधने बले। अक्षौहिणीभिः शिष्टाभिर्वृतः पञ्चभिराहवे॥
en: After that, Karna became the Cominanderin-chief of Duryodhana's forces. He was supported in battle by the residue of the Kaurava-army which numbered five Akshauhinis.

sn: तिस्रस्तु पाण्डुपुत्राणां चम्वो बीभत्सुपालिताः। हतप्रवीरभूयिष्ठा बभूवुः समवस्थिताः॥
en: Of the sons of Pandu, there were then three Akshauhinis. After the destruction of innumerable heroes, protected by Arjuna, they came to battle.

sn: ततः पार्थं समासाद्य पतङ्ग इव पावकम्। पञ्चत्वमगमत् सौतिर्द्वितीयेऽहनि दारुणः॥
en: The Suta's son Karna, though a dreadful warrior, encountering Partha, came to his end on the second day, like an insect encountering a burning fire.

sn: हते कर्णे तु कौरव्या निरुत्साहा हतौजसः। अक्षौहिणीभिस्तिसृभिर्मद्रेशं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: After the fall of Karna, the Kauravas became dispirited, and lost all energy. Numbering three Akshaushinis, they gathered round the king of the Madras.

sn: हतवाहनभूयिष्ठाः पाण्डवाऽपि युधिष्ठिरम्। अक्षौहिण्या निरुत्साहाः शिष्टया पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Having lost many car-warriors and elephants and horsemen, the residue of the Pandava army, numbering one Akshauhini and overtaken with depression, supported by Yudhishthira.

sn: अवधीन्मद्रराजानं कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। तस्मिंस्तदादिवसे कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्॥
en: The Kuru king Yudhishthira, in the battle that took place, accomplished the most difficult feats and killed, before half the day was over, the king of the Madras.

sn: हते शल्ये तु शकुनि सहदेवो महात्मनाः। आहर्तारं कलेस्तस्य जघानामितविक्रमः॥
en: After the fall of Shalya, the great Sahadeva, of immeasurable prowess, killed Shakuni the man who had brought about the quarrel.

sn: निहते शकुनौ राजा धार्तराष्ट्रः सुदुर्मनाः। आपाक्रामद् गदापाणिर्हतभूयिष्ठसैनिकः॥
en: After the fall of Shakuni, the royal son of Dhritarashtra, whose army had suffered an extensive carnage and who on that account had become greatly dispirited, fled from the field, armed with his mace.

sn: तमन्वधावत् संक्रुद्धो भीमसेनः प्रतापवान्। हृदे द्वैपायने चापि सलिलस्थं ददर्श तम्॥
en: Then Bhimasena of great prowess, filled with anger, pursued him and discovered him within the waters of the Dvaipayana lake.

sn: हतशिष्टेन सैन्येन समन्तात् पर्यवार्य तम्। अथोपविविशुर्हष्टा हृदस्थं पञ्च पाण्डवाः॥
en: With the residue of their army, the Pandavas surrounded the lake and, filled with joy, met Duryodhana concealed within the waters.

sn: विगाह्य सलिलं त्वाशु बाग्बाणै शविक्षतः। उत्थाय स गदापाणियुद्धाय समुपस्थितः॥
en: Their wordy arrows, penetrating through the waters, pierced Duryodhana. Rising up from the lake, the latter approached the Pandavas, armed with his mace, desirous of battle.

sn: ततः स निहतो राजा धार्तराष्ट्रो महारणे। भीमसेनेन विक्रम्य पश्यतां पृथिवीक्षिताम्॥
en: Then, in the great battle that took place, the royal son of Dhritarashtra was killed by Bhimasena, displayed his great prowess, in the presence of many kings.

sn: ततस्तत् पाण्डवं सैन्यं प्रसुप्तं शिबिरे निशि। निहतं द्रोणपुत्रेण पितुर्वधममृष्यता॥
en: After this the residue of the Pandava-army, as it slept in the camp, was killed at night time by Drona's son who was unable to put up with the destruction of his father (at the hands of Dhrishtadyumna).

sn: हतपुत्रा हतबला हतमित्रा मया सह। युयुधानसहायेन पञ्च शिष्टास्तु पाण्डवाः॥
en: Their sons killed, their forces killed, their friends killed, only the five sons of Pandu, are alive with myself and Yuyudhana.

sn: सहैव कृपभोजाभ्यां द्रौणियुद्धादमुच्यत। युयुत्सुश्चापि कौरव्यो मुक्तः पाण्डवसंश्रयात्॥
en: With Kripa and and the Bhoja prince Kritavarman, the son of Drona represents the unkilled residuc of the Kaurava-army. Dhritarashtra's son Yuyutsu also has escaped slaughter on account of his having adopted the side of the Pandavas.

sn: निहते कौरवेन्द्रे तु सानुबन्धे सुयोधने। विदुरः संजयश्चैव धर्मराजमुपस्थितौ॥
en: Upon the destruction of the Kaurava-king Suyodhana with all his followers and allies, Vidura and Sanjaya have come to the presence of king Yudhishthira the just.

sn: एवं तदभवद् युद्धमहान्यष्टादश प्रभो। यत्र ते पृथिवीपाला निहताः स्वर्गमावसन्॥
en: Thus did that battle take place, O lord, for eighteen days. Many kings of Earth, killed therein, have ascended the celestial region.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शृण्वतां तु महाराज कथां तां लोमहर्षणाम्। दुःखशोकपरिक्लेशा वृष्णीनामभवंस्तदा।॥
en: Vaishampayana continued : The Vrishnis, as they heard, O king, that dreadful account became filled with grief and sorrow and pain.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कथयन्नेव तु सदा वासुदेवः प्रतापवान्। महाभारतयुद्धं तत्कथान्ते पितुरग्रतः॥ अभिमन्योर्वधं वीरः सोऽत्यक्रामन्महामतिः। अप्रियं वसुदेवस्य मा भूदिति महामतिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said After the great Vasudeva of great prowess had finished his narration of the great battle of the Bharatas before his father, it was plain that that hero had passed over the destruction of Abhimanyu. The motive of the great one was that his father might not hear what was highly unpleasant to him.

sn: मा दौहित्रवधं श्रुत्वा वसुदेवो महात्ययम्। दुःखशोकाभिसंतप्तो भवेदिति महामतिः॥
en: Indeed, the intelligent Krishna did not wish that his father Vasudeva should, on hearing the dreadful intelligence of the death of his daughter's son, be afflicted with sorrow and grief.

sn: सुभद्रा तु तमुत्क्रान्तमात्मजस्य वधं रणे। आचक्ष्व कृष्ण सौभद्रवमित्यपतद् भुवि॥
en: (His sister) Subhadra, noticing that the slaughter of her son had not been mentioned, addressed her brother, saying, Do you narrate the death of my son, O Krishna!-and dropped down on the earth (in a swoon).

sn: तामपश्यन्निपतितां वसुदेवः क्षितौ तदा। दृष्ट्वैव च पपातोळें सोऽपि दुःखेन मूर्छितः॥
en: Vasudeva saw his daughter fallen on the ground. As soon as he saw this, he also fell down, deprived of his senses by grief.

sn: ततः स दौहित्रवधदुःखशोकसमाहतः। वसुदेवो महाराज कृष्णं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥ ननु त्वं पुण्डरीकाक्ष सत्यवाग् भुवि विश्रुतः॥ यद् दौहित्रवधं मेऽद्य न ख्यापयसि शत्रुहन्।
en: (Regaining his senses) Vasudeva, afflicted with grief at the death of his daughter's son, O king, addressed Krishna, saying, O lotus-eyed one, you are famed on Earth for being truthful in speech. Why, however, O destroyer of enemies, do you not tell me today of the death of my daughter's son?

sn: तद् भागिनेयनिधनं तत्त्वेनाचक्ष्व मे प्रभो॥ सदृशाक्षस्तव कथं शत्रुभिर्निहतो रणे।
en: O powerful one, tell me in full of the destruction of your sister's son! Having eyes resembling thine, alas, how was he killed in battle by enemies.

sn: दुर्मरं बत वार्ष्णेय कालेऽप्राप्ते नृभिः सह॥ यत्र मे हृदयं दुःखाच्छतधा न विदीर्यते।
en: Since my heart does not from grief break into a hundred pieces, it seems, O you of the Vrishni race, that it does not die with men when its hour does not come.

sn: किमब्रवीत् त्वां संग्रामे सुभद्रां मातरं प्रति॥ मां चापि पुण्डरीकाक्ष चपलाक्षः प्रिबो मम।
en: Oh, at the time of his fall, what words did he give utterance to, addressing his mother? O lotus-eyed one, what did that darling of mine, having restless eyes, say to me?

sn: आहवं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा कच्चिन्न निहतः परैः॥ कच्चिन्मुखं न गोविन्द तेनाजौ विकृतं कृतम्।
en: I hope he has not been killed by eneinies while retreating from battle with his back towards them? I hope, O Govinda, that his face did not become cheerless while fighting?

sn: स हि कृष्ण महातेजाः श्लाघन्निव ममाग्रतः॥ बालभावेन विनयमात्मनोऽकथयत् प्रभुः।
en: He was possessed, O Krishna, of great energy. From a spirit of childishness, that powerful hero, boasting (of his prowess) in my presence, used to speak of his skill (in battle).

sn: कच्चिन्न निकृतो बालो द्रोणकर्णकृपादिभिः॥ धरण्यां निहतः शेते तन्ममाचक्ष्व केशव।
en: I hope that boy does not lie on the field, killed deceitfully by Drona and Karna and Kripa and others? Do you teli me this.

sn: स हि द्रोणं च भीष्मं च कर्णं च बलिनां वरम्॥ स्पर्धते स्म रणे नित्यं दुहितुः पुत्रको मम।
en: That son of my daughter always used to challenge Bhishma and that foremost of all powerful warriors, viz., Karna, in battle.

sn: एवंविधं बहु तदा विलपन्तं सुदुःखितम्॥ पितरं दुःखिततरो गोविन्दो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। न तेन विकृतं वक्त्रं कृतं संग्राममूर्धनि॥ न पृष्ठत: कृतश्चापि संग्रामस्तेन दुस्तरः।
en: His father who, from excess of grief, bewailed thus, Govinda, more afflicted than he, answered in these words, His face did not become cheerless as he fought in the van of battle. Dreadful though that battle was, he diu not turn his back upon it.

sn: निहत्य पृथिवीपालान् सहस्रशतसंघशः॥ खेदितो द्रोणकर्णाभ्यां दौःशासनिवशं गतः।
en: Having killed hundreds and thousands of kings of Earth, he was distressed by Drona and Karna and at last was killed by the son of Dushasana.

sn: एको होकेन सततं युध्यमाने यदि प्रभो॥ न स शक्येत संग्रामे निहन्तुमपि वज्रिणा।
en: If, O lord, he had been encountered, one to one, without intermission, he was incapable of being killed in battle by even the holder of the thunder-bolt.

sn: समाहृते च संग्रामात् पार्थे संशप्तकैस्तदा॥ पर्यवार्यत संक्रुद्धैः स द्रोणादिभिराहवे।
en: When his father Arjuna was withdrawn from the main body by the Samsaptakas, Abhimanyu was surrounded by the enraged Kaurava-heroes headed by Drona in battle.

sn: ततः शत्रुवधं कृत्वा सुमहान्तं रणे पितः॥ दौहित्रस्तव वार्ष्णेय दौःशासनिवशं गतः।
en: Then, O father, after he had killed a very large number of enemies in battle, your daughter's son at last succumbed to the son of Dushasana.

sn: नूनं च स गतः स्वर्गे जहि शोकं महामते॥ न हि व्यसनमासाद्य सीदन्ति कृतबुद्धयः।
en: Forsooth, he has gone to the celestial region! Kill this grief of thine, O you of great intelligence! They who who are of purified understandings never languish when they meet with any calamity.

sn: द्रोणकर्णप्रभृतयो येन प्रतिसमासिताः॥ रणे महेन्द्रप्रतिमाः स कथं नाप्नुयाद् दिवम्।
en: He by whom Drona and Karna and others were checked in battle, heroes who were equal to Indra himself in power, why would not he ascend to the celestial region.

sn: स शोकं जहि दुर्धर्ष मा च मन्युवशं गमः॥ शस्त्रपूतां हि स गतिं गतः परपुरंजयः।
en: O irresistible one, do you kill this grief of thine! Do not allow yourself to be swayed by anger. That conqueror of hostile cities has attained to that sanctified and which depends upon death at the edge of weapons.

sn: तस्मिंस्तु निहते वीरे सुभद्रेयं स्वसा मम॥ दुःखार्ताधो सुतं प्राप्य कुररीव ननाद ह।
en: After the fall of that hero, this my sister Subhadra, stricken with grief, bewailed aloud, when she saw Kunti, like a female as prey.

sn: द्रौपदी च समासाद्य पर्यपृच्छत दुःखिता॥ आर्ये क्व दारकाः सर्वे द्रष्टुमिच्छामि तानहम्।
