en: When she met Draupadi, she asked her in grief, O reverend lady, where are all our sons? I wish to see them.

sn: अस्यास्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वास्ताः कुरुयोषितः॥ भुजाभ्यां परिगृह्येनां चुक्रुशुः परमार्तवत्॥
en: Hearing her lamentations, all the Kauravaladies embraced her and wept sitting around her.

sn: उत्तरां चाब्रवीद् भद्रे भर्ता स क्व नु ते गतः। क्षिप्रमागमनं मह्यं तस्य त्वं वेदयस्व ह॥
en: Seeing (her daughter-in-law) Uttara, she said, O blessed girl, where has your husband gone? when he returns, do you without losing a moment apprise me of it.

sn: ननु नामाद्य वैराटि श्रुत्वा मम गिरं सदा। भवनान्निष्पतत्याशु कस्मान्नाभ्येति ते पतिः॥
en: Alas, O daughter of Virata, as soon he heard my voice, he used to come out of his chamber without the loss of a moment. Why does not your husband come out today.

sn: अभिमन्यो कुशलिनो मातुलास्ते महारथाः। कुशलं चाब्रुवन् सर्वे त्वां युयुत्सुमिहागतम्॥
en: Alas, O Abhimanyu, your maternal uncles, powerful car-warriors, are all hale. They used to bless you when they saw you come here prepared to go out for battle.

sn: आचक्ष्व मेऽद्य संग्रामं यथापूर्वमरिंदम। कस्मादेवं विलपतीं नाघेह प्रतिभाषसे॥
en: Do you tell me the incidents of battle today as before, O chastiser of enemies. Oh, why do you not answer me today, me who am weeping so bitterly?

sn: एवमादि तु वार्ष्णेय्यास्तस्यास्तत्परिदेवितम्। श्रुत्वा पृथा सुदुःखार्ता शनैर्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥ सुभद्रे वासुदेवेन तथा सात्यकिना रणे। पित्रा च लालितो बालः स हतः कालधर्मणा॥
en: Hearing these lamentations of this daughter of the Vrishni-race, Pritha, deeply stricken with grief, addressed her and slowly said, O Subhadra, though protected by Vasudeva and Satyaki and by his own father, your youthful son has yet been killed. That slaughter is due to the influence of Time.

sn: ईदृशो मर्त्यधर्मोऽयं मा शुचो यदुनन्दिनि। पुत्रो हि तव दुर्घर्षः सम्प्राप्तः परमां गतिम्॥
en: O daughter of Yadu's race, mortal your son was. Do not grieve. Irresistible in battle, your son has, forsooth, attained to the highest end.

sn: कुले महति जातासि क्षत्रियाणां महात्मनाम्। मा शुचश्चपलाक्षं त्वं पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणे॥
en: You are born in a high family of great Kshatriyas. Do not grieve, O you of restless glances, O girl of eyes like lotus petals!

sn: उत्तरां त्वमवेक्षस्व गुर्विणी मा शुचः शुभे। पुत्रमेषा हि तस्याशु जनयिष्यति भाविनी॥
en: Do you cast your eyes on Uttara, who is quick with child. O blessed lady do not give way to grief. This auspicious girl will soon bring forth a son to that hero!

sn: एवमाश्वासयित्वैनां कुन्ती यदुकुलोद्वह। विहाय शोकं दुर्धर्षे श्राद्धमस्य ह्यकल्पयत्॥ समनुज्ञाप्य धर्मज्ञं राजानं भीममेव च। यमौ यमोपमौ चैव ददौ दानान्यनेकशः॥ ततः प्रदाय बहीर्गा ब्राह्मणाय यदूद्वह। समाहृष्य तु वार्ष्णेयी वैराटीमब्रवीदिदम्॥ वैराटि नेह संतापस्त्वया कार्यो ह्यनिन्दिते। भर्तारं प्रति सुश्रोणि गर्भस्थं रक्ष वै शिशुम्॥
en: Having comforted her, thus, Kunti, knowing every duty, O perpetuator, of Yadu's race, casting off her grief, O irresistible one, made arrangements for Abhimanyu's obsequial rites, with the permission of king Yudhishthira and Bhima, and the twins (viz., Nakula and Sahadeva) who in prowess resembled Yama himself. She also made many presents to the Brahmanas, and bestowed upon them many kine, O perpetuator of Yadu's race. Then the Vrishni-dame (Kunti), comforted a little, addressed the daughter of Virata , saying, O faultless daughter of Virata, you should not grieve! For the sake of your husband, O you of round hips, protect the child in your womb.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततः कुन्ती विरराम महाद्युते। तामनुज्ञाप्य चैवेमां सुभद्रां समुपानयम्॥
en: Having said these words, O you of great splendour Kunti ceased. With her perinission I have brought Subhadra here.

sn: एवं स निधनं प्राप्तो दौहित्रस्तव मानद। संतापं त्यज दुधर्ष मा च शोके मनः कृथाः॥
en: It was thus, O giver of honours, that your daughter's son was killed. Cast off your burning grief, O irresistible one! Indeed, do not set your heart on sorrow. burning grief, O irresistible one! Indeed, do not set your heart on sorrow.

sn: एतच्छुत्वा तु पुत्रस्य वचः शूरात्मजस्तदा। विहाय शोकं धर्मात्मा ददौ श्राद्धमनुत्तमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard these words of his son, Vasudeva, that descendant of Shura, of righteous soul renouncing grief, made excellent obsequial offerings (to Abhimanyu).

sn: तथैव वासुदेवश्च स्वस्रीयस्य महात्मनः। दयितस्य पितुर्नित्यमकरोदौर्ध्वदेहिकम्॥
en: Vasudeva also performed those rites for the ascension (to Heaven) of his great nephew, that hero who was ever the darling of his father (Vasudeva).

sn: षष्टिं शतसहस्राणि ब्राह्मणानां महौजसाम्। विधिवद् भोजयामास भोज्यं सर्वगुणान्वितम्॥
en: He duly fod six millions of Brahmanas, gifted with great energy, with edibles possessed of every recommendation.

sn: आच्छाद्य च महाबाहुर्धनतृष्णामपानुदत्। ब्राह्मणानां तदा कृष्णस्तदभूल्लोमहर्षणम्॥ सुवर्णं चैव गाश्चैव शयनाच्छादनानि च। दीयमानं तदा विप्रा वर्धतामिति चाब्रुवन्॥
en: Presenting many clothes to them, Krishna satisfied the thirst for wealth of those Brahmanas. Wonderful were the heaps of gold, the number of kine and of beds and cloths, that were then given away. The Brahmanas loudly declared, Let (Krishna's wealth) increase.

sn: वासुदवोऽथ दाशार्हो बलदेवः ससात्यकिः। अभिमन्योस्तदा श्राद्धमकुर्वन् सत्यकस्तदा॥
en: Then Vasudeva of Dasharha's race, and Baladeva, and Satyaki, and Satyaka, each performed the obsequial rites of Abhimanyu.

sn: अतीत दुःखसंतप्ता न शमं चोपलेभिरे। तथैव पाण्डवा वीरा नगरे नागसाह्वये॥
en: Greatly stricken with grief, they could find no comfort. The same was the case with the sons of Pandu in the city of Hastinapure.

sn: नोपगच्छन्त वै शान्तिमभिमन्युविनाकृताः। सुबहूनि च राजेन्द्र दिवसानि विराटजा॥ नाभुङ्क्त पतिदुःखार्ता तदभूत् करुणं महत्। कुक्षिस्थ एव तस्याथ गर्भो वै सम्प्रलीयत॥
en: Deprived of Abhimanyu, they could get no peace of mind. The daughter of Virata, O king, for many days, totally abstained from all food, greatly afflicted by grief on account of the death of her husband. At this all her relatives, became plunged into excess of grief. They were all afraid that the embryo in her womb might be destroyed.

sn: आजगाम ततो व्यासो ज्ञात्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा। समागम्याब्रवीद् धीमान् पृथां पृथुललोचनाम्॥ उत्तरां च महातेजाः शोकः संत्यज्यतामयम्। भविष्यति महातेजाः पुत्रस्तव यशस्विनि॥ प्रभावाद् वासुदेवस्य मम व्याहरणादपि। पाण्डवानामयं चान्ते पालयिष्यति मेदिनीम्॥
en: Then Vyasa, ascertaining the state of things by his spiritual vision, arrived there. The highly intelligent Rishi, gifted with great energy, arrived (at the palace), addressed Pritha of large eyes, as also Uttara herself, saying, Let this grief be given up! O famous lady, a son gifted with great energy will be born to you, through the power of Vasudeva and at my word. That son will rule the Earth after the Pandavas.

sn: धनंजयं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य धर्मराजस्य शृण्वतः। व्यासो वाक्यमुवाचेदं हर्षयन्निव भारत॥ पौत्रस्तव महाभागो जनिष्यति महामनाः। पृथ्वीं सागरपर्यन्तां पालयिष्यति धर्मतः॥
en: Seeing Dhananjaya, he said to him in the hearing of king Yudhishthira, the just and pleasing him with his words, O Bharata, Your grandson, O highly blessed one, will become a great prince! He will righteously govem the whole Earth to the verge of the sea.

sn: तस्माच्छोकं कुरुश्रेष्ठ जहि त्वमरिकर्शन। विचार्यमत्र न हि ते सत्यमेतद् भविष्यति॥
en: Therefore, O foremost one of Kuru's race, renounce this grief, O mower of enemies! Do not doubt this! This will truly take place.

sn: यच्चापि वृष्णिवीरेण कृष्णेन कुरुनन्दन। पुरोक्तं तत् तथा भावा मा तेऽत्रास्तु विचारणा॥
en: That which was uttered by the Vrishni-hero on a former occasion, will, surely, happen! Do not think otherwise.

sn: विबुधानां गतो लोकानक्षयानात्मनिर्जितान्। न स शोच्यस्त्वया वीरो न चान्यैः कुरुभिस्तथा॥
en: As regards Abhimanyu, he has gone to the regions of the celestials, conquered by him with his own deeds. That hero should be grieved for by you or, indeed, by the other Kurus.

sn: एवं पितामहेनोक्तो धर्मात्मा स धनंजयः। त्यक्त्वा शोकं महाराज हृष्टरूपोऽभवत् तदा॥
en: Thus addressed by his grandfather, Dhananjaya of righteous soul, O king, renounced his grief and even became cheerful.

sn: पितापि तव धर्मज्ञ गर्भे तस्मिन् महामते। अवर्धत यथाकामं शुक्लपक्षे यथा शशी॥
en: Your father, O prince, who are conversant with all duties, began to grow in that womb. O you of great intelligence, like the Moon, in the lighted fortnight.

sn: ततः संचोदयामास व्यासो धर्मात्मजं नृपम्। अश्वमेघ प्रति तदा ततः सोऽन्तर्हितोऽभवत्॥
en: Then Vyasa urged the royal son of Dharma for celebrating the Horse-Sacrifice Having said so, he made himself invisible there and then.

sn: धर्मराजोऽपि मेधावी श्रुत्वा व्यासस्य तद् वचः। वित्तस्यानयने तात चकार गमने मतिम्॥
en: The intelligent king Yudhishthira, the just, hearing the words of Vyasa, set his mind on the journey for bringing wealth.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: जनमेजय उवाच श्रुत्वैतद् वचनं ब्रह्मन् व्यासेनोक्तं महात्मना। अश्वमेधं प्रति तदा किं भूयः प्रचकार ह॥
en: Janamejaya said Having heard these words, O twice-born one, that were spoken by the great Vyasa about the Horse-Sacrifice, what steps were taken by Yudhishthira.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: रत्नं च यन्मरुत्तेन निहितं वसुधातले। तदवाप कथं चेति तन्मे ब्रूहि द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Tell me, O foremost of twice-bom ones, how the king succeeded in obtaining the riches which Marutta had buried in the Earth!

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा द्वैपायनवचो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। भ्रातॄन् सर्वान् समानाय्य काले वचनमब्रवीत्॥ अर्जुनं भीमसेनं च माद्रीपुत्रौ यमावपि। श्रुतं वो वचनं वीरा: सौहृदाद् यन्महात्मना॥ कुरूणां हितकामेन प्रोक्तं कृष्णेन धीमता। तपोवृद्धेन महता सुहृदां भूतिमिच्छता॥ गुरुणा धर्मशीलेन व्यासेनाद्भुतकर्मणा। भीष्मेण च महाप्राज्ञा गोविन्देन च धीमता॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard the words of the Island-born ascetic king Yudhishthira the just, summoned all his brothers, viz., Arjuna and Bhimasena and the twin sons of Madri, in proper time and then said to them, You heroes, you have heard the words which the highly intelligent and great Krishna has said from his friendship for and the desire of doing good to the Kurus! Indeed you have heard those words that have been uttered by that ascetic of profuse penances, that great sage desirous of conferring prosperity on his friends, that preceptor of righteous conduct, viz., Vyasa of wonderful feats! You have heard what Bhishma also said, and what Govinda too of great intelligence has uttered.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: संस्मृत्य तदहं सम्यक् कर्तुमिच्छामि पाण्डवाः। आयत्यां च तदात्वे च सर्वेषां तद्धि नो हितम्॥
en: Remembering those words, you sons of Pandu, I wish to obey them duly! By obeying those words of theirs great blessedness will belong to all of you.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: अनुबधे च कल्याणं यद् वचो ब्रह्मवादिनः। इयं हि वसुधा सर्वा क्षीणरत्ना कुरुद्वहाः॥
en: Those words spoken by those utters of Brahma are certain (if obeyed) to produce considerable benefit. You perpetuators of Kuru's race, the Earth has become divested of her riches.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: तच्चाचष्ट तदा व्यासो मरुत्तस्य धनं नृपाः। यद्येतद् वो बहुमतं मन्यध्वं वा क्षमं यदि॥ तथा यथाऽऽह धर्मेण कथं वा भीम मन्यसे। इत्युक्तवाक्ये नृपतौ तदा कुरुकुलोद्वह॥ भीमसेनो नृपश्रेष्ठं प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्। रोचते मे महाबाहो यदिदं भाषितं त्वया॥ व्यासाख्यातस्य वित्तस्य समुपानयनं प्रति। यदि तत् प्राप्नुयामेह धनमाविक्षितं प्रभो॥ कृतमेव महाराज भवेदिति मतिर्मम। ते वयं प्रणिपातेन गिरीशस्य महात्मनः॥ तदानयाम भद्रं ते समभ्यर्च्य कपर्दिनम्। तद् वित्तं देवदेवेशं तस्यैवानुचरांश्च तान्॥ प्रसाद्यार्थमवाप्स्यामो नूनं वाग्बुद्धिकर्मभिः। रक्षन्ते ये च तद् द्रव्यं किन्नरा रौद्रदर्शनाः॥ ते च वश्या भविष्यन्ति प्रसन्ने वृषभध्वजे। श्रुत्वैवं वदतस्तस्य वाक्यं भीमस्य भारत॥ प्रीतो धर्मात्मजो राजा बभूवातीव भारत। अर्जुनप्रमुखाश्चापि तथेत्येवाब्रुवन् वचः॥
en: You kings, Vyasa, therefore, informed us of the wealth of Marutta. If you think that wealth abundant or sufficient, how shall we bring it? What, O Bhima, do you think about this? us When the king, O perpetuator of Kuru's race, said these words, Bhimasena, joining his hands, said these words in reply, The words you have said, O you of mighty arms, on the subject of bringing the riches indicated by Vyasa, are approved by me? If, O powerful one, we succeed in getting the riches kept there by the son of Avikshita, then this sacrifice, o king, purposed by will be easily accomplished! This is what I think. We shall, therefore, bowing our heads to the great Girisha, and off-ring duc adoration to that deity, bring that wealth. Blessed be you. Pleasing that god of gods as companions and followers, in words, thought, and deed, we shall, forsooth, obtain that wealth. Those Kinnaras of dreadful appcarance who are protecting that treasure will certainly veiled to us if the great deity having the bull for his sign, becomes pleased with us! Hearing these words uttered by Bhima, O Bharata, king Yudhishthira the son of Dharma, become highly pleased. The others, headed by Arjuna, at the same time, said, So be it.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: कृत्वा तु पाण्डवाः सर्वे रत्नाहरणनिश्चयम्। सेनामाज्ञापयामासुर्नक्षत्रेऽहनि च ध्रुवे॥
en: The Pandavas then, having resolved to bring that wealth, ordered their forced to march under the constellation Dhruva and on the day called by the same name.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: ततो ययुः पाण्डुसुता ब्राह्मणान् स्वस्ति वाच्य च। अर्चयित्वा सुरश्रेष्ठं पूर्वमेव महेश्वरम्॥
en: Making the Brahmanas utter benedictions on them, and having duly adored the great god Maheshvara, the sons of Pandu started on their enterprise).

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: मोदकैः पायसेनाथ मांसापूपैस्तथैव च। आशास्य च महात्मानं प्रययुर्मुदिता भृशम्॥
en: Pleasing that great deity with Modakas and frumenty and with cakes made of meat, the sons of Pandu started with cheerful hearts.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: तेषां प्रयास्यतां तत्र मङ्गलानि शुभान्यथा प्राहुः प्रहष्टमनसो द्विजण्या नागराश्च ते॥
en: While they thus started, the citizens, and many foremost of Brahmanas, with cheerful hearts, uttered auspicious blessings (on their heads).

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: ततः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य शिरोभिः प्रणिपत्य च। ब्राह्मणानग्निसहितान् प्रययुः पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥
en: The Pandavas, going round many Brahmanas who daily adored their fires, and bending their heads unto them, proceeded on their journey.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: समनुज्ञाप्य राजानं पुत्रशोकसमाहतम्। धृतराष्ट्रं सभार्यं वै पृथां च पृथुलोचनाम्॥ मूले निक्षिप्य कौरव्यं युयुत्सुं धृतराष्ट्रजम्। सम्पूज्यमानाः पौरैश्च ब्राह्मणैश्च मनीषिभिः॥
en: Taking the permission of king Dhritarashtra who was stricken with grief on account of the death of his sons, his queen (Gandhari), and Pritha also of large eyes, and keeping the Kaurava-prince Yuyutsu, the of Dhritarashtra, in the capital, they started, adored by the citizens and by many Brahmanas endued with great wisdom. son

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते प्रययुर्हष्टा: प्रहष्टनरवाहनाः। रथघोषेण महता पूरयन्तो वसुंधराम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said They then started with cheerful hearts, and accompanied by men and animals all of whom and which wcrc cqually cheerful. They filled the whole Earth with the loud clatter of their whecls.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: संस्तूयमानाः स्तुतिभिः सूतमागधवन्दिभिः। स्वेन सैन्येन संवीता यथादित्याः स्वरश्मिभिः॥
en: Their praises sung by eulogists and Sutas and Magadhas and bards, and supported by their own army, they appeared like so many Suns adorned with their own rays.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: पाण्डुरेणातपत्रेण ध्रियमाणेन मूर्धनि। बभौ युधिष्ठिरस्तत्र पौर्णमास्यामिवोडुराट्॥
en: With the white umbrella held over his head, king Yudhishthira shone with beauty like the lord of the stars on the night when he is at full.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: जयाशिषः प्रहृष्टानां नराणां पथि पाण्डवः। प्रत्यगृहाद् यथान्यायं यथावत् पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: That foremost of men, the eldest son of Pandu, accepted, with due forms, the blessings and cheers of his gladdened subjects as he went on his way.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: तथैव सैनिका राजन् राजानमनुयान्ति ये। तेषां हलहलाशब्दो दिवं स्तब्वा व्यतिष्ठत॥
en: About the soldiers who followed the king, their confused murmurs seemed to fill the entire sky.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: सरांसि सरितश्चैव वनान्युपवनानि च। अत्यक्रामन्महाराजो गिरिं चाप्यन्वपद्यत॥
en: That army crossed many lakes and rivers and forests and pleasure gardens. They at last came upon the mountains.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: तस्मिन् देशे च राजेन्द्र यत्र तद् द्रव्यमुत्तमम्। चक्रे निवेशनं राजा पाण्डवः सह सैनिकैः।
en: Arrived at that region where that wealth was buried. O king, Yudhishthira fixed his camp with all his brothers and troops.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: शिवे देशे समे चैव तदा भरतसत्तम॥ अग्रतो ब्राह्मणान् कृत्वा तपोविद्यादमान्वितान्। पुरोहितं च कौरव्य वेदवेदाङ्गपारगम्। आग्निवेश्यं च राजानो ब्राह्मणा: सपुरोधसः॥ कृत्वा शान्तिं यथान्यायं सर्वशः पर्यवारयन्। कृत्वा तु मध्ये राजानममात्यांश्च यथाविधि॥ षट्पदं नवसंख्यानं निवेशं चक्रिरे द्विजाः। मत्तानां वारणेन्द्राणां निवेशं च यथाविधि॥ कारयित्वा स राजेन्द्रो ब्राह्मणनिदमब्रवीत्। अस्मिन् कार्ये द्विजश्रेष्ठा नक्षत्रे दिवसे शुभे॥ यथा भवन्तो मन्यन्ते कर्तुमर्हन्ति तत् तथा। न न: कालात्ययो वै स्यादिहैव परिलम्बताम्॥ इति निश्चित्य विप्रेन्द्राः क्रियतां यदनन्तरम् श्रुत्वैतद् वचनं राज्ञो ब्राह्मणाः सपुरोधसः। इदमूचुर्वचो हृष्टा धर्मराजप्रियेप्सवः॥ अद्यैव नक्षत्रमहश्च पुण्यं यतामहे श्रेष्ठतमक्रियासु। नुपोष्यतां चापि भवद्भिरद्य॥
en: The region selected for the purpose, O chief of Bharata's race, was perfectly level and auspicious. There the king pitched his camp, placing in his van such Brahmanas as were gifted with penances and learning and selfcontrol, as also his priest Agniveshya, O you of Kurus' race, who was well-conversant with the Vedas and all their branches. Then the royal sons of Pandu, and the other kings, and the Brahmanas and priests well-skilled in sacrificial rites, having duly performed same propitiatory ceremonies, spread themselves all over that spot. Having duly placed the king and his ministers in the middle, the Brahinanas caused the camp to be pitched by laying out six roads and nine divisions. King Yudhishthira caused a separate encampment to be duly made for the infuriate elephants who accompanied his army. When everything was complete, he addressed the Brahmanas, saying, You foremost of Brahmanas, do that which you think should be done in view of the matter at hand. Indeed, let an auspicious day and constellation be fixed for it. Let not a long time pass away over our heads as we wait in suspense here. You foremost of learned Brahmanas, having formed this resolution, do what should be done after this! Hearing these words of the king, the Brahmanas with those amongst them who were well-skilled in the performance of religious rites, became filled with gladness and desirous of doing that was agrecable to king Yudhishthira the just, said these words in reply, This very day is an auspicious one with a auspicious constellation. We shall, therefore, try to celebrate those high rites we propose. We shall today, O king, live upon water alone. Do you all fast also today.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: श्रुत्वा तु तेषां द्विजशत्तमानां कृतोपवासा रजनी नरेन्द्रः। ऊषुः प्रतीताः कुशसंस्तरेषु यथाध्वरे प्रज्वलिता हुताशाः॥
en: Hearing those words of those foremost Brahmanas, the royal sons of Pandu passed that night, abstaining from all food, and lying confidently on beds of Kusha-grass, like burning fires in a sacrifice.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: ततो निशा सा व्यगमन्महात्मनां संशृण्वतां विप्रसमीरिता गिरः। ततः प्रभाते विमले द्विजर्षभा वचोऽब्रुवन् धर्मसुतं नराधिपम्॥
en: And the night wore away as they listened to the discourses of the learned Brahmanas. When the cloudless morning came, those foremost of Brahmanas addressed the royal son of Dharma, (saying as follows).

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: ब्राह्मणः ऊचुः क्रियतामुपहारोऽद्य त्र्यम्बकस्य महात्मनः। दत्त्वापहारं नृपते ततः स्वार्थं यतामहे।।।।
en: Let offerings be made to the great Mahadeva of three eyes. eyes. Having duly dedicated those offerings, O king, we shall then try to gain our objet.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषां ब्राह्मणानां युधिष्ठिरः। गिरीशस्य यथान्यायमुपहार मुपाहरत्॥
en: Hearing these words of those Brahmanas, Yudhishthira caused offerings to be duly made to that deity who loved to lie down on mountain-breasts.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: आज्येन तर्पयित्वाग्निं विधिवत्संस्कृतेन च। मन्त्रसिद्धं चक्रं कृत्वा पुरोधाः स ययौ तदा॥
en: Pleasing the (sacrificial) fire with (libations of) sanctified butter according to the ordinance, the priest (Dhaumya) cooked Charu with the aid of Mantras and performed the necessary rites.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: स गृहीत्वा सुमनसो मन्त्रपूता जनाधिप। मोदकैः पायसेनाथ मांसैश्चोपाहरद् बलिम्॥
en: He took up many flowers and sanctified them with Mantras, O king. With Modakas and frumenty and meat, he made offerings to the deity.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: सुनोभिश्च चित्राभिर्लाजैरुच्चावचैरपि। सर्वे स्विष्टतमं कृत्वा विधिवद् वेदपारगः॥
en: With various kinds of flowers and with fried paddy, of very superior kind, Dhaumya, well-versed in the Vedas, performed the remaining rites.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: किंकराणां ततः पश्चाच्चकार बलिमुत्तमम्। यक्षेन्द्राय कुबेराय मणिभद्राय चैव ह॥
en: He next presented offerings according to the ordinance to those ghostly beings who formed Mahadeva's train. And offerings were next made to Kubera the king of the Yakshas, and to Manibhadra also.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: तथान्येषां च यक्षाणां भूतानां पतयश्च ये। कृसरेण च मांसेन निवापैस्तिलसंयुतैः॥ ओदनं कुम्भशः कृत्वा पुरोधाः समुपाहरत्। ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सहस्राणि गवां दत्त्वा तु भूमिपः॥
en: To the other Yakshas also and to them who were the foremost ones among the ghostly companions of Mahadeva, the priest offered due adoration, having filled many jugs with food, with Krisharas and meat and Nivapas mixed with sesame seeds. The king gave away unto the Brahmanas thousands of kine.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: नक्तंचराणां भूतानां व्यादिदेश बलि तदा। धूपगन्धनिरुद्धं तत् सुमनोभिश्च संवृतम्॥ शुशुभे स्थानमत्यर्थ देवदेवस्य पार्थिव। कृत्वा पूजां तु रुद्रस्य गणानां चैव सर्वशः॥ ययौ व्यासं पुरस्कृत्य नृपो रत्ननिधि प्रति। पूजयित्वा धनाध्यक्षं प्रणिपत्याभिवाद्य च॥ सुमनोभिर्विचित्राभिरपूपैः कृसरेण च। शंखादींश्च निधीन् सर्वान् निधिपालांश्च सर्वशः॥ अर्चयित्वा द्विजाग्र्यान् स स्वस्ति वाच्य च वीर्यवान्। तेषां पुण्याहघोषेण तेजसा समवस्थितः॥ प्रीतिमान् स कुरुश्रेष्ठः खानयामास तद् धनम्। ततः पात्री: सकरका बहुरूपा मनोरमाः॥ भृङ्गराणि कटाहानि कलशान् वर्धमानकान्। बहूनि च विचित्राणि भाजनानि सहस्रशः॥ उद्धारयामास तदा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। तेषां रक्षणमप्यासीन्महान् करपुटस्तथा॥
en: He then directed the presentation, according to due rites, of offerings to those night-ranging beings (who live with Mahadeva). Surcharged, as it were, with the scent of Dhupas, and filled with the fragrance of flowers, that region, sacred to the deity of deities, O king, became highly delightful. Having performed the adoration of Rudra and of all the Ganas, the king, placing Vyasa ahead went towards the place where the treasure was buried. Once more adoring the Lord of riches, and bowing to hiin with respect and saluting himn properly, with various kinds of flowers and cakes and Krishara, having adored those foremost of gems, viz., Shankha and Nidhi and those Yakshas who are the lords of gems, and having adored many foremost of Brahmanas and caused them to utter blessings, the king gifted with great power, strengthened by the energy and the auspicious benedictions of those Brahmanas, caused that spot to be excavated. Then numerous vessels of various and delightful forms, Bhringaras, Katahas, Kalasas, Bardhamanakas, and innumerable Bhajanas of beautiful forms, were dug out by king Yudhishthira the just, The wealth thus dug out was placed in large has Karaput (wooden chests united with each other by chains or cords, and carried by bullocks or camels) for protection.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: नद्धं च भाजनं राजंस्तुलाधर्मभवन्नृप। वाहनं पाण्डुपुत्रस्य तत्रासीत् तु विशाम्पते॥
en: A portion of the wealth was caused to be carried upon the shoulders of men it stout balances of wood with baskets slung like scales at both ends. Indeed, O king, there were other methods of conveyance there for carrying away that wealth of the son of Pandu.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: षष्टिरुष्ट्रसहस्राणि शतानि द्विगुणा हयाः। वारणाश्च महाराज सहस्रशतसम्मिताः॥
en: There were sixty thousands of camels, and a hundred and twenty thousand horses, and of elephants, O king, there were one hundred thousand.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: शकटानि रथाश्चैव तावदेव करेणवः। खराणां पुरुषाणां च परिसंख्या न विद्यते॥
en: Of cars there were as many, and of carts too as many and of she elephants as many. Mules and men were of unlimited number.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: एतद् वित्तं तदभवद् यदुद्दघे युधिष्ठिरः। षोडशाष्टौ चतुर्विंशत्सहस्रं भारलक्षणम्॥
en: That wealth which Yudhishthira caused to be dug out was even so much. Sixteen thousand coins were placed on the back of each camel; cight thousand on each car; and twentyfour thousand on each elephant.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: एतेष्वादाय तद् द्रव्यं पुनरभ्यर्च्य पाण्डवः। महादेवं प्रति ययौ पुरं नागाह्वयं प्रति॥ द्वैपायनाभ्यनुज्ञातः पुरस्कृत्य पुरोहितम्। गोयुते गोयुते चैव न्यवसत् पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Having loaded these vehicles with that wealth and once more adoring the great deity Shiva, the son of Pandu started for the city of Hastinapur, with the perinission of the Islandborn Rishi, and placing his priest Dhaumya in the van. That foremost of men, viz., the royal son of Pandu, made short marches of four miles every day.

description: Yudhishthira's acquisition of wealth turned into earth by Marutta
sn: सा पुराभिमुखा राजन्नुवाह महती चमूः। कृच्छ्राद् द्रविणभारार्ता हर्षयन्ती कुरूद्वहान्॥
en: That powerful army, o king, afflicted with the weight they bore, returned, carrying that wealth, towards the capital, phasing the hearts of all those perpetuators of the Kuru-race.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु वासुदेवोऽपि वीर्यवान्। उपायाद् वृष्णिभिः सार्धं पुरं वारणसाह्वयम्॥
en: Meanwhile, the highly energetic Vasudeva, accompanied by the Vrishnis, came to the city of Hastinapur.

sn: समयं वाजिमेधस्य विदित्वा पुरुषर्षभः। यथोक्तो धर्मपुत्रेण प्रव्रजन् स्वपुरी प्रति॥
en: While leaving that city for returning to his own Dwraka, he had been requested by the son of Dharma to come back. Hence, knowing, that the tiine fixed for the Horse-Sacrifice had come, that foremost of men returned to Hastinapur.

sn: रौक्मिणेयेन सहितो युयुधानेन चैव ह। चारुदेष्णेन साम्बेन गदेन कृतवर्मणा॥ सारणेन च वीरेण निशठेनोल्मुकेन च। बलदेवं पुरस्कृत्य सुभद्रासहितस्तदा॥
en: Accompanied by the son Rukmini, by Yuyudhana, by Charudeshana, by Shamva by Gada, by Kritavarman, by the heroic Sarana, by Nishatha and by Un-mukha, Vasudeva came, with Baladeva at the head of the train, and with Subhadra also accompanying him.

sn: द्रौपदीमुत्तरां चैव पृथां चाप्यवलोककः। समाश्वासयितुं चापि क्षत्रिया निहतेश्वराः॥
en: Indeed, that hero came for seeing Draupadi, Uitara and Pritha and for comforting those renowned Kshatriya-ladies who had been bereft of many of their protectors.

sn: तानागतान् समीक्ष्यैव धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः। प्रत्यगृह्वाद् यथान्यायं विदुरश्च महामनाः॥
en: Seeing those heroes come, king Dhritarashtra, as also the great Vidura, received them with due honours.

sn: तत्रैव न्यवसत् कृष्णः स्वर्चितः पुरुषोत्तमः। विदुरेण महातेजास्तथैव च युयुत्सुना॥
en: That foremost of men, viz., Krishna of great energy, worshipped by Vidura and Yuyutsu, continued to live in the Kuru capital.

sn: वसत्सु वृष्णिवीरेषु तत्राथ जनमेजय। जज्ञे तव पिता राजन् परिक्षित् परवीरहा॥
en: It was while the Vrishni heroes, ) Janamejaya, were living in the Kuru-city, O king, that your father, that destroyer of hostile heroes, was born.

sn: स तु राजा महाराज ब्रह्मास्त्रेणावपीडितः। शवो बभूव निश्चेष्टो हर्षशोकविवर्धनः॥
en: The royal Parikshit, O monarch, afflicted by the Brahima-weapon of Ashvatthama), upon coming out of the womb, lay still and motionless for he had no life. By his birth he had pleased the citizens but soon piunged them into grief.

sn: हृष्टानां सिंहनादेन जनानां तत्र नि:स्वनः। प्रविश्य प्रदिशः सर्वाः पुनरेव व्युपारमत्॥
en: The citizens, learning of the birth of the prince, uttered a leonine shout. That noise proceeded to the utmost limit of every point of the compass. Soon, however, that noise ceased,

sn: ततः सोऽतित्वरः कृष्णो विवेशान्तःपुरं तदा। युयुधानद्वितीयो वै व्यथितेन्द्रियमानसः॥
en: Krishna, his senses and inind considerably affected, with Yuyudhana in his company, entered speedily the inner apartments of the palace.

sn: ततस्त्वरितमायान्तीं ददर्श स्वां पितृष्वसाम्। क्रोशन्तीमभिधावेति वासुदेवं पुनः पुनः॥
en: He saw his own paternal aunt (Kunti), coming, loudly weeping and calling upon him repeatedly.

sn: पृष्ठतो द्रौपदी चैव सुभद्रां च यशस्विनीम्। सविक्रोशं सकरुणं बान्धवानां स्त्रियो नृप॥
en: Behind her were Draupadi and the famous Subhadra, and the wives of the relatives of the Pandavas, all weeping piteously.

sn: ततः कृष्णं समासाद्य कुन्तिभोजसुता तदा। प्रोवाच राजशार्दूल बाप्पगद्गदया गिरा॥
en: Mecting Krishna, Kunti, that daughter of the Bhoja race, said to him in a voice choked with tears, Oforemost of monarchs.

sn: वासुदेव महाबाहो सुप्रजा देवकी त्वया। त्वं नो गतिः प्रतिष्ठा च त्वदायत्तमिदं कुलम्॥
en: O Vasudeva, O mighty-armed hero Devaki, by having borne you, has come to be considered as an excellent genetrix! You are our refuge and our glory! This race (of Pandu) depends upon you for its protector.

sn: यदुप्रवीर योऽयं ते स्वस्रीयस्यात्मजः प्रभो। अश्वत्थाम्ना हतो जातस्तमुज्जीवय केशव॥
en: O Yadava hero, O powerful one this child of your sister's son, has come, out of the womb, killed by Ashvatthama. O Keshava, do you révive him!

sn: त्वया ह्येतत् प्रतिज्ञातमैषीके यदुनन्दन। अहं संजीवयिष्यामि मृतं जातमिति प्रभो॥ सोऽयं जातो मृतस्तात पश्यैनं पुरुषर्षभ।
en: O delighter of the Yadavas, this was vowed by you, O powerful one, when Ashvatthaman had inspired the blade of grass into a Brahmaweapon of great energy! Indeed, O Keshava, your words were thcsc; I shall revive that child if he comes out of the womb dead!

sn: उत्तरां च सुभद्रां च द्रौपदीं मां च माधव॥ धर्मपुत्रं च भीमं च फाल्गुनं नकुलं तथा। सहदेवं च दुर्धर्ष सर्वान् नस्त्रातुमर्हसि॥
en: That child, O son, has been born deed! Sec him, O foremost of men. You should, O Madhava, rescue Uttara and Subhadra and Draupadi and myself, and Dharma's son (Yudhishthira), and Bhima and Phalguna, and Nakula and the irresistible Sahadeva.

sn: अस्मिन् प्राणा: समायत्ताः पाण्डवानां ममैव च। पाण्डोश्च पिण्डो दाशार्ह तथैव श्वशुरस्य मे॥ अभिमन्योश्च भद्रं ते प्रियस्य सदृशस्य च। प्रियमुत्पादयाद्य त्वं प्रेतस्यापि जनार्दन॥
en: In this child arc fettered the life-breaths of the Pandavas and myself! O you of the Dasharha-race, on him depends the obsequial cake of Pandu, as also of my father-in-law, and of Abhimanyu too, blessed be you, that favourite nephew of yours who was so very like you! Do you do today what will be beneficial to all these! I urge you earnestly, O Janardana.

sn: उत्तरा हि पुरोक्तं वै कथयत्यरिसूदन। अभिमन्योर्वचः कृष्ण प्रियत्वात् तन्न संशयः॥
en: Uttara, O destroyer of enemies, always repeats the words said to her by Abhimanyu. Forsooth, O Krishna, those words were highly agreeable to her.

sn: अब्रवीत् किल दाशार्ह वैराटीमा निस्तदा। मातुलस्य कुलं भद्रे तव पुत्रो गमिष्यति॥
en: O you of the Dasharha-race. Arjuna's son said to this daughter of Virata, Your son, O blessed girl, will go to my maternal uncles.

sn: गत्वा वृष्ण्यन्धककुलं धनुर्वेदं ग्रहीष्यति। अस्त्राणि च विचित्राणि नीतिशास्त्रं च केवलम्।।२४)
en: Taking up his quarters with the Vrishnis and Andhakas, he will obtain from them the science of arms, indeed, various wonderful weapons and the whole of the science of polities and morality.

sn: इत्येतत् प्रणयात् तात सौभद्रः परवीरहा। कथयामास दुर्घर्षस्तथा चैतन्न संशयः॥
en: These were the words, O son, that that destroyer of hostile heroes, viz., the son of Subhadra, that irresistible hero, said to Uttara from his love for her.

sn: तास्त्वां वयं प्रणम्येह याचामो मधुसूदन। कुलस्यास्य हितार्थं तं कुरु कल्याणमुत्तमम्॥
en: O destroyer of Madhu, bowing our heads to you, we pray you for making those words of Abhimanyu true! In view also of the time that has come, do you accomplish what is highly beneficial.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु वार्ष्णेयं पृथा पृथुललोचना। उच्छ्रित्य बाहू दुःखार्ता ताश्चान्याः प्रापतन् भुवि।।२७।'
en: Having said these words to that hero of the Vrishni's race, Pritha of large eyes, raised her arms upwards and with the other ladies in her company, dropped down on the Earth.

sn: अब्रुवश्च महाराज सर्वाः सास्राविलेक्षणाः। स्वस्रीयो वासुदेवस्य मृतो जात इति प्रभो॥
en: All of them, with eyes rendered muddy by tears, repeatedly explained, saying, Alas, the son of Vasudeva's nephew has been born dead.

sn: एवमुक्ते ततः कुन्ती पर्यगृह्णाज्जनार्दनः। भूमौ निपतितां चैनां सान्त्वयामास भारत॥
en: After Kunti had said so, Janardana took hold of her, O Bharata, and gently raising her from the Earth, comforted her as follows.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उत्थितायां पृथायां तु सुभद्रा भ्रातर तदा। दृष्ट्वा चुक्रोश दुःखार्ता वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ पुण्डरीकाक्ष पश्य त्वं पौत्रं पार्थस्य धीमतः। परिक्षीणेषु कुरुषु परिक्षीणं गतायुषम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said After Kunti had sat up, Subhadra, seeing her brother, began to weep aloud, and stricken with excessive grief, said, O you having eyes like lotus-petals, look at the grandson of Arjuna of great intelligence! Alas, the Kururace having been thinned, a child has been born that is feeble and dead.

sn: इषीका द्रोणपुत्रेण भीमसेनार्थमुद्यता। सोत्तरायां निपतिता विजये मयि चैव ह॥
en: The blade of grass, uplifted by Drona's son for bringing about the destruction of Bhimasena, fell upon Uttara and Vijaya and myself.

sn: सेयं विदीर्णे हृदये मयि तिष्ठति केशव। यन्न नश्यामि दुर्धर्ष सहपुत्रं तु तं प्रभो॥
en: Alas, that blade, O Keshava, is still existing (unexpected) in me, after having pierced my heart, since I do not, O irresistible hero, see this child with iny son.

sn: किं नु वक्ष्यति धर्मात्मा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनार्जुनौ चापि माद्रवत्याः सुतौ च तौ॥
en: What will the righteous-souled king Yudhishthira the just say? What will Bhimasena and Arjuna, and the two sons of Madravati also say?

sn: श्रुत्वाभिमन्योस्तनयं जातं च मृतमेव च। मुषिता इव वार्ष्णेय द्रोणपुत्रेण पाण्डवाः॥
en: Hearing that Abhimanyu's son was born and dead, the Pandavas, O you of Vrishni's race, will consider themselves as imposed upon by Ashvatthaman.

sn: अभिमन्युः प्रियः कृष्ण भ्रातृणां नात्र संशयः। ते श्रुत्वा किं नु वक्ष्यन्ति द्रोणपुत्रास्त्रनिर्जिताः॥
en: Abhimanyu, O Krishna, was, forsooth, the minion of all the Pandava-brother. Hearing this intelligence, what will those heroes, defeated by the weapon of Drona's son say?

sn: भवितातः परं दुःखं किं तदन्यज्जनार्दन। अभिमन्योः सुतात् कृष्ण मृताज्जातादरिंदम॥
en: Bowing grief, O Janardana, can be greater than this, viz., that Abhimanyu's son should be born and dead?

sn: साहं प्रसादये कृष्ण त्वामद्य शिरसा नता। पृथेयं द्रौपदी चैव ताः पश्य पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: Bowing to you with my head, O Krishna, I seek to please you today! See O foremost of men, these two standing here, viz., Pritha and Draupadi.

sn: यदा द्रोणसुतो गर्भान् पाण्डूनां हन्ति माधव। तदा किल त्वया द्रौणिः क्रुद्धनोक्तोऽरिमर्दन॥ अकामं त्वां करिष्यामि ब्रह्मबन्धो नराधम। अहं संजीवयिष्यामि किरीटितनयात्मजम्॥
en: When, O Madhava, the son of Drona tried to destroy the embryos even in the wombs of the ladies of the Pandavas, at that time, O grinder of enemies, you said in anger to Dronas son (even these words). O wretch of a Brahmana, O vilest of men I shall disappoint your wish! I shall revive the son of Kiritin's son.

sn: इत्येतद् वचनं श्रुत्वा जानानाहं बलं तव। प्रसादये त्वां दुर्धर्ष जीवतामभिमन्युजः॥
en: Hearing these words of yours and wellknowing your power, I seek to gratify you, O irresistible hero! Let the son of Abhimanyu be revived.

sn: यद्येतत् त्वं प्रतिश्रुत्य न करोषि वचः शुभम्। सकलं वृष्णिशार्दूल मृतां मामवधारय॥
en: If having pledged yourself previously you do not accomplish your auspicious vow, do you then know for certain, O chief of the Vrishni race, that I shall put an end to my life.

sn: अभिमन्योः सुतो वीर न संजीवति यद्ययम्। जीवति त्वयि दुर्धर्ष किं करिष्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: If, O hero, this son of Abhimanyu does not revive when you, O irresistible one, are alive and near, of what other use will you be to me?

sn: संजीवयैनं दुर्धर्ष मृतं त्वमभिमन्युजम्। सदृशाक्षसुतं वीर सस्यं वर्षन्निवाम्बुदः॥
en: Do you, therefore, O irresistible one, revive this son of Abhimanyu, this child who has eyes similar to his, even as a rain-charged cloud revives the lifeless crops (on a field).

sn: त्वं हि केशव धर्मात्मा सत्यवान् सत्यविक्रमः। स तां वाचमृतां कर्तुमर्हसि त्वमरिंदम॥
en: You, O Keshava, are righteous-souled, truthful, and of prowess incapable of being baffled. You should, O chastiser of enemies make your words truthful.

sn: इच्छन्नापि हि लोकांस्त्री जीवयेथा मृतानिमान्। किं पुनर्दयितं जातं स्वस्रीयस्यात्मजं मृतम्॥
en: If only you wish it, you can revive the three worlds (of being) if dead! What need, I say, therefore, of this darling child, born but dead, of your sister's son?

sn: प्रभावशास्मि ते कृष्ण तस्मात् त्वां याचयाम्यहम्। कुरुष्व पाण्डुपुत्राणामिमं परमनुग्रहम्॥
en: I know your power, O Krishna! Therefore do I solicit you! Do you show this great favour to the sons of Pandu.

sn: स्वसेति वा महाबाहो हतपुत्रेति वा पुनः। प्रपन्ना मामियं चेति दयां कर्तुमिहार्हसि॥
en: You should, O mighty-armed one, show mercy to this Uttara, or to me, thinking that I am your sister or even a mother who has lost her son, and one who has thrown herself upon your protection.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु राजेन्द्र केशिहा दुःखमूर्छितः। तथेति व्याजहारोच्चै दयन्निव तं जनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed, O king, the destroyer of Keshni, greatly possessed by sorrow answered, So be it! These words were uttered with sufficicnt loudness and they pleased all the inmates of the inner apartments of the place.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: वाक्येनतेन हि तदा तं जनं पुरुषर्षभः। ह्लादयामास स विभुर्धर्मार्ते सलिलैरवि॥
en: The powerful Krishna, that foremost of men, by uttering these words, pleased all the people assembled there, like one pouring cold water on a person afflicted with sweat.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: ततः स प्राविशत् तूर्णं जन्मवेश्म पितुस्तवा अर्चि पुरुषव्याघ्र सितैर्माल्यैर्यथाविधि॥ अपां कुम्भैः सुपूर्णश्च विन्यस्तैः सर्वतोदिशम्। घृतेन तिन्दुकालातैः सर्षपैश्च महाभुज॥ अस्त्रैश्च विमलैर्व्यस्तैः पावकैश्च समन्ततः। वृद्धाभिश्चापि रामाभिः परिचारार्थमावृतम्॥
en: He then quickly entered the lying in-room in which your father was born. It was duly sanctificd, O king, with many garlands, of while flowers; with many well-filled waterpots arranged on every side; with char-coal, soaked in clarified butter of Tinduka-wood, and mustard-seeds, o you of mighty arms; with shining weapons properly arranged and several fires on every side. And it was filled with many agreeable and aged dames summoned for waiting.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: दक्षैश्च परितो धीर भिषग्भिः कुशलैस्तथा। ददर्श च स तेजस्वी रक्षोनान्यपि सर्वशः॥ द्रव्याणि स्थापितानि स्म विधिवत् कुशलैर्जनैः। तथायुक्तं च तद् दृष्ट्वा जन्मवेश्म पितुस्तव॥
en: It was also surrounded by many well-skilled and clever physicians, O you of great intelligence! Gifted with great energy, he also beheld there all articles that are destructive of Rakshasas, duly placed by persons knowing the subject. Seeing the lying-in-room in which your father was born thus equipt, Hrishikesha became very glad and said, Excellent, Excellent!'

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: हटोऽभवद्धषीकेशः साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत्। तथा ब्रुवति वार्ष्णेये प्रहृष्टवदने तदा॥ द्रौपदी त्वरिता गत्वा वैराटी वाक्यमब्रवीत्। अयमायाति ते भद्रे श्वशुरो मधुसूदनः॥
en: When he of Vrishni's racc said so and presented such a chcerful look, Draupadi, going there quickly, addressed the daughter of Virata, saying, O blessed lady, here comes to you your father-in-law, the destroyer of Madhu, that ancient Rishi of inconceivable soul, that unvanquished one.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: पुराणर्षिरचिन्त्यात्मा समीपमपराजितः। सापि बाष्पकलां वाचं निगृहाश्रूणि चैव ह॥ सुसंवीताभवद् देवी देववत् कृष्णमीयुषी।
en: Virata's daughter, checking her tears said these words in a voice chocked with grief. Covering herself properly, the pincess waited for Krishna like the celestials reverentially waiting for him.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: सा तथा दूयमानेन हृदयेन तपस्विनी॥ दृष्ट्वा गोविन्दमायान्तं कृपणं पर्यदेवयत्।
en: The helpless lady with heart agitated by Sorrow, seeing Govinda coming, bewailed, saying :

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: पुण्डरीकाक्ष पश्यावां बालेन हि विनाकृतौ। अभिमन्युं च मां चैव हतौ तुल्यं जनार्दन॥
en: O lotus-eyed one, sce us two deprived of our child! O Janardana, both Abhimanyu and myself have been equally killed.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: वार्ष्णेय मधुहन् वीर शिरसा त्वां प्रसादये। द्रोणपुत्रास्त्रनिर्दग्धं जीवयैनं ममात्मजम्॥
en: o you of Vrishni's race, O destroyer of Madhu, I seek to please you by bending my head, O hero to you! Do you revive this child of mine who has been consumed by the weapon of Drona's son.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: यदि स्म धर्मराज्ञा वा भीमसेनेन वा पुनः। त्वया वा पुण्डरीकाक्ष वाक्यमुक्तमिदं भवेत्॥ अजानतीमिपीकेयं जनित्री हन्त्विति प्रभो। अहमेव विनष्टा स्यां नैतदेवंगते भवेत्॥
en: If king Yudhishthira the just, or Bhimasena, or yourself, O lotus-eyes one, had, on that occasion, said, Let the blade of grass destroy the unconscious mother, O powerful one, then I would have been destroyed and this would not have taken place.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: गर्भस्थस्यास्य बालस्य ब्रह्मास्त्रेण निपातनम्। कृत्वा नृशंसं दुर्बुद्धिौणिः किं फलमश्नुते॥
en: Alas, what benefit has been reaped by Drona's son by doing this cruel deed, viz., the destruction of the child in the womb by his Brahma-weapon.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: सा त्वां प्रसाद्य शिरसा याचे शत्रुनिबर्हणम्। प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यामि गोविन्द नायं संजीवते यदि॥
en: That self-same mother now seeks to please you, O slayer of enemies, by bending her head! Surely, O Govinda, I shall kill myself if this child does not revive.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: अस्मिन् हि बहवः साधो ये ममासन् मनोरथाः। ते द्रोणपुत्रेण हताः किं नु जीवामि केशव॥
en: In him, Orighteous one, I placed many expectations! Alas, when these have been frustrated by Drona's son, what necessity have I, O Keshava, to carry on the burden of life?

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: आसीन्मम मतिः कृष्ण पुत्रोत्सङ्गा जनार्दन। अभिवादयिष्ये हृष्टेति तदिदं वितथीकृतम्॥
en: I hoped, O Krishna, that with my child on my lap, O Janardana, I would salute you with respect! Alas, O Keshava, that hope has beelu destroyed.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: चपलाक्षस्य दायादे मृतेऽस्मिन् पुरुषर्षभ। विफला मे कृताः कृष्ण हृदि सर्वे मनोरथाः॥
en: O foremost of all beings at the death of this heir of Abhimanyu of restless eyes, all my hopes have been destroyed.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: चपलाक्षः किलातीव प्रियस्ते मधुसूदन। सुतं पश्य त्वमस्यैनं ब्रह्मास्त्रेण निपातितम्॥
en: Abhimanyu of restless eyes, O destroyer of Madhu, was exceedingly dear to you. Behold this child of his killed by the Brahma-weapon.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: कृतघ्नोऽयं नृशंसोऽयं यथास्य जनकस्तथा। यः पाण्डवीं श्रियं त्यक्त्वा गतोऽद्य यमसादनम्॥२२
en: This child is very ungrateful and very heartless, like his father, for, sce, disregarding the prosperity and affluence of the Pandavas, he has gone to Yama's house.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: मया चैतत् प्रतिज्ञातं रणमूर्धनि केशवा अभिमन्यौ हते वीर त्वामेष्याम्यचिरादिति।॥
en: I had, before this, vowed, O Keshava, that if Abhimanuyu fell on the field of battle, O hero, I would follow him immediately.

description: Krishna is requested to restore Abhimanyu's son to life
sn: तच्च नाकरवं कृष्ण नृशंसां जीवितप्रिया। इदानीं मां गतां तत्र किं नु वक्ष्यति फाल्गुनिः॥
en: I did not, however, keep my vow, cruel that I am and fond of life! If I go to him now, what indeed, will Phalguna's son say?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सैवं विलय करुणं सोन्मादेव तपस्विनी। उत्तरा न्यपतद् भूमौ कृपणा पुत्रगृद्धिनी॥
en: Vaishampayana said The helpless Uttara, desirous of getting back her child, having thus bewailed, dropped down in sorrow on the earth like demented creature.

sn: तां तु दृष्ट्वा निपतितां हतपुत्रपरिच्छदाम्। चुक्रोश कुन्ती दुःखार्ता सर्वाश्च भरतस्त्रियः॥
en: Sceing the princess fallen on the earth deprived of her son and with her body uncovered, Kunti as also all the (other) Bharata-ladies, deeply afflicted, began to weep aloud.

sn: मुहूर्तमिव राजेन्द्र पाण्डवानां निवेशनम्। अप्रेक्षणीयमभवदार्तस्वनविनादितम्॥
en: Resounding with the voice of lamentation the palace of the Pandavas, O king, was soon converted into a house of sorrow where nobody could remain.

sn: सा मुहूर्ते च राजेन्द्र पुत्रशोकाभिपीडिता। कश्मलाभिहता वीर वैराटी त्वभवत् तदा॥
en: Greatly stricken with grief on account of her son, Virata's daughter, O king, seemed to be struck down for sometime by sorrow and cheerlessness.

sn: प्रतिलभ्य तु सा संज्ञामुत्तरा भरतर्षभ। अङ्कमारोष्य तं पुत्रमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Regaining consciousness, O chief of Bharata's race, Uttara took up her child on her lap and said these words.

sn: धर्मज्ञस्य सुतः स त्वमधर्मे नावबुध्यसे। यस्त्वं वृध्णिप्रवीरस्य कुरुषे नाभिवादनम्॥
en: You are the child of one who knew every duty. Are you not conscious then of the sin you commit, since you do not salute this foremost one of the Vrishni's race?

sn: पुत्र गत्वा मम वचो ब्रूयास्त्वं पितरं त्विदम्। दुर्मरं प्राणिनां वीर कालेऽप्राप्ते कथंचन॥ याहं त्वया विनायेह पत्या पुत्रेण चैव ह। मर्तव्ये सति जीवामि हतस्वस्तिरकिंचना॥
en: O son, going to your father tell him these words of mine, viz., It is difficult for living creatures to die before their time comes, because through refit of you, my husband, and now deprived of my child also, I am yet alive when I should die, unendued as I am with everything auspicious and everything valuable.

sn: अथवा धर्मराज्ञाहमनुज्ञाता महाभुज। भक्षयिष्ये विषं घोरं प्रवेक्ष्ये वा हुताशनम्॥
en: O mighty-armed one, with the permission of king Yudhishthira the just. I shall swallow some dreadful poison or cast myself on the burning fire.

sn: अथवा दुर्मरं तात यदिदं मे सहस्रधा। पतिपुत्रविहीनाया हृदयं न विदीर्यते॥
en: O father, difficult of destruction is my heart since, though I am deprived of husband and child, that heart of mine does not brcak into a thousand pieces.

sn: उत्तिष्ठ पुत्र पश्येमां दुःखिता प्रपितामहीम्। आर्तामुपप्लुतां दीनां निमग्नां शोकसागरे॥
en: Rise, O son, and see this your afflicted great grandmother! She is deeply stricken with grief, bathed in tears, exceedingly cheerless, and plunged in an ocean of sorrow.

sn: आर्यांच पश्य पाञ्चालीं सात्वती च तपस्विनीम्। मां च पश्य सुदुःखार्तो व्याधविद्धां मृगीमिव॥
en: See the reverend princess of Panchala, and the helpless princess of the Sattata race! Look at myself, exceedingly afflicted with grief, and resembling a deer pierced by a hunter.

sn: उत्तिष्ठ पश्य वदनं लोकनाथस्य धीमतः। पुण्डरीकपलाशाक्षं पुरेव चपलेक्षणम्॥
en: Rise, O child, and look at the face of this king, who is gifted with great wisdom, and possessed of eyes like lotus-petals and resembling your father of restless glances.

sn: एवं विप्रलपन्तीं तु दृष्ट्वा निपतितां पुनः। उत्तरां तां स्त्रियः सर्वाः पुनरुत्थापयंस्ततः॥
en: Seeing Uttara, whey bewailed thus, fallen on the earth, all those ladies, raising her, caused her to sit up.

sn: उत्थाय च पुनधैर्यात् तदा मत्स्यपतेः सुता। प्राञ्जलिः पुण्डरीकाक्षं भूमावेवाभ्यवादयत्॥
en: Having sat up, the daughter of the king of the Matsyas, summoning her patience, joined her hands in respect and touched the earth with her head for saluting Keshava having eyes like lotus petals.

sn: श्रुत्वा स तस्या विपुलं विलापं पुरुषर्षभः। उपस्पृश्य ततः कृष्णो ब्रह्मास्त्रं प्रत्यसंहरत्॥
en: Hearing those heart-rending lamentations of hers, that foremost of persons touched water and withdrew the (force of the Brahmaweapon.

sn: प्रतिजज्ञे च दाशार्हस्तत्य जीवितमच्युतः। अब्रवीच्च विशुद्धात्मा सर्वे विश्रावयञ्जगत्॥ न ब्रवीम्युत्तरे मिथ्या सत्यमेतद् भविष्यति। एष संजीवयाम्येनं पश्यतां सर्वदेहिनाम्॥
en: That hero of undecaying glory, belonging to the race of the Dasharhas, promised to revive the child. Then he of pure soul, said these words in the hearing of the whole universe, 'O Uttara, I never utter a falsehood. My words will prove true. I shall revive this child before all creatures.

sn: नोक्तपूर्वं मया मिथ्या स्वैरेष्वपि कदाचन। न च युद्धात् परावृत्तस्तथा संजीवतामयम्॥
en: Never before have I uttered a falschood even in just. Never have I turned back from battle. (By the merit of those deeds) let this child revive.

sn: यथा मे दयितो धर्मो ब्राह्मणश्च विशेषतः। अभिमन्योः सुतो जातो मृतो जीवत्वयं तथा॥
en: As virtue is dear to me, as Brahmanas are especially dear to me, let Abhimanyu's son, who is born dead, revive.

sn: यथाहं नाभिजानामि विजये तु कदाचन। विराधं तेन सत्येन मृतो जीवत्वयं शिशुः॥
en: Never has a misunderstanding arisen between me and my friend Vijaya. Let this dead child revive by that truth.

sn: यथा सत्यं च धर्मश्च मयि नित्यं प्रतिष्ठितौ। तथा मृतः शिशुरयं जीवतादभिमन्युजः॥
en: As truth and virtue are always established in me, let this dead child of Abhimanyu revive.

sn: यथा कंसश्च केशी च धर्मेण निहतौ मया। तेन सत्येन बालोऽयं पुनः संजीवतामयम्॥
en: As Kansa and Keshi have been righteously killed by me, let this child revive today by that truth.

sn: इत्युक्तो वासुदेवेन स बालो भरतर्षभ। शनैः शनैर्महाराज प्रास्पन्दत सचेतनः॥
en: After these words uttered by Vasudeva, that child, O foremost one of Bharata's family, became animal and began gradually to move, O king. were

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ब्रह्मास्त्रं तु यदा राजन् कुष्णेन प्रतिसंहृतम्। तदा तद् वेश्म त्वत्पित्र तेजसाभिविदीपितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said, When the Brahma-weapon was withdrawn by Krishna, at that time, the lying in-room was lighted up by your father with his energy.

sn: ततो रक्षांसि सर्वाणि नेशुस्त्यक्त्वा गुहं तु तत्। अन्तरिक्षे च वागासीत् साधु केशव साध्विति॥
en: All the Rakshasas were forced to leave the room and many of them were killed. In the sky a voice was heard, saying, Excellent, O Keshava, Excellent.

sn: तदस्त्रं ज्वलितं चापि पितामहमगात् तदा। ततः प्राणान् पुनर्लेभे पिता तव नरेश्वर॥
en: The burning Brahma-weapon when returned to the Grandfather. Your father got back his, O king.

sn: व्यचेष्टत च बालोऽसौ यथोत्साहं यथाबलम्। बभूवुर्मुदिता राजंस्ततस्ता भरतस्त्रियः॥
en: The child began to move according to his energy and power. The Bharata-ladies became all filled with joy.

sn: ब्राह्मणान् वाचयामासुर्गोविन्दस्यैव शासनात्। ततस्ता मुदिताः सर्वाः प्रशाशंसुर्जनार्दनम्॥
en: At the command of Govinda, the Brahmanas were made to utter benedictions. All the ladies filled with joy, lauded Janardana.

sn: स्त्रियो भरतसिंहानां नावं लब्वेव पारगाः। कुन्ती द्रुपदपुत्री च सुभद्रा चोत्तरा तथा॥
en: Indeed, the wives of those Bharata-heroes, viz., Kunti and Drupada's daughter and Subhadra and Uttara, and the wives of other leading men, like (ship-wrecked) persons who have reached the shore after having got a boat, became greatly pleased.

sn: स्त्रियश्चान्या नृसिंहानां बभूवुर्हष्टमानसाः। तत्र मला नटाश्चैव ग्रन्थिकाः सौख्यशायिकाः॥ सूतमागधसंघाश्चाप्यस्तुवंस्तं जनार्दनम्। कुरुवंशस्तवाख्याभिराशीर्भिर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then wrestlers and actors and astrologers and those who enquire after the sleep (of princes), and bands of bards and eulogists all uttered the praises of Janardana, while ultering benedictions filled with the praises of the Kurus, O chief of the Bharatas.

sn: उत्थाय तु यथाकालमुत्तरा यदुनन्दनम्। अभ्यवादयत प्रीता सह पुत्रेण भारत॥
en: Uttara, rising up at the proper time, with a pleased heart and bearing her child in her arms, reverentially saluted the delighter of the Yadus.

sn: तस्य कृष्णो ददौ हृष्टो बहुरत्नं विशेषतः। तथान्ये वृष्णिशार्दूला नाम चास्याकरोत् प्रभुः॥ पितुस्तव महाराज सत्यसंधो जनार्दनः। परिक्षीणे कुले यस्माज्जातोऽयमभिमन्युजः॥ परिक्षिदिति नामास्य भवत्वित्यब्रवीत् तदा। सोऽवर्धते यथाकालं पिता तव जनाधिप॥ मनःप्रह्लादनश्चासीत् सर्वलोकस्य भारत। मासजातस्तु ते वीर पिता भवति भारत॥ अथाजग्मुः सुबहुलं रत्नमादाय पाण्डवाः। तान् समीपगताञ्श्रुत्वा निर्ययुर्वृष्णिपुङ्गवाः॥
en: Rejoicing greatly, Krishna made gifts to the child of many valuable gems. The other chiefs of the Vrishni-race, did the same. Then the powerful Janardana, firmly following truth, bestowed a name on the infant who was your father, O monarch. Since this child of Abhimanyu has been born at a time when this family has become nearly extinct, let his name be Parikshit.' This is what he said. Then your father, O king, began to grow, and please all the people, O Bharata. When your father was month old, O hero, the Pandavas returned to heir capital, bringing with them abundant riches. Hearing that the Pandavas were near, those foremost ones of the Vrishni-race went out.

sn: अलंचक्रुश्च माल्यौघैः पुरुषा नागसाह्वयम्। पताकाभिर्विचित्रार्ध्वजैश्च विविधैरपि॥
en: The citizens docked the city of Hastinapur with many garlands of flowers with beautiful pennons and standards of various kinds.

sn: वेश्मानि समलंचक्रुः पौराश्चापि जनेश्वर। देवतायतनानां च पूजाः सुविविधास्तथा॥ संदिदेशाथ विदुरः पाण्डुपुत्रप्रियेप्सया। राजमार्गाश्च तत्रासन् सुमनोभिरलंकृताः॥
en: The citizens also, O king, adorned their respective palaces. Desirous of doing what was beneficial to the sons of Pandu, Vidura ordered various kinds of adoration to be offered to the celestials established in their respective temples. The principal streets of the city were adorned with flowers.

sn: शुशुभे तत्पुरं चापि समुद्रौघनिभस्वनम्। नर्तकैश्चापि नृत्यद्भिर्गायकानां च निःस्वनैः॥ आसीद् वैश्रवणस्येव निवासस्तत्पुरं तदा। बन्दिभिश्च नरै राजन् स्त्रीसहायैश्च सर्वशः॥ तत्र तत्र विविक्तेषु समन्तादुपशोभितम्। पताका धूयमानाश्च समन्तापन्मातस्श्विना॥ अदर्शयन्निव तदा कुरून् वै दक्षिणोत्तरान्। अघोषयंस्तदा चापि पुरुषा राजधूर्गताः। सर्वराष्ट्रविहारोऽद्य रत्नाभरणलक्षणः॥
en: Indeed, the city was filled with the noise of thousands of voices which resembled the softened roar of distant ocean waves. With dancers all engaged in their business, and with the voice of singers, the (Kuru) city then resembled the palace of Vaishravana himself. Bards and culogists, O king, accompanied by beautiful women, were seen to adorn various retired spots in the city. The pennons were made by the wind to float gaily on every part of the city, as if bent upon showing the Kurus the southern and the northern points of the compass. All the officers also of the government loudly proclaimed that that was to be a day of rejoicing for the whole kingdom as a mark of the success of the enterprise for bringing a profusion of gems and other valuables.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तान् समीपगताश्रुत्वा पाण्डवान् शत्रुकर्शनः। वासुदेवः सहामात्यः प्रययौ ससुहृद्गणः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing that the Pandavas were near, that destroyer of enemies, viz., Vasudeva, accompanicd by his ministers, went out for seeing them.

sn: ते समेत्य यथान्यायं प्रत्युद्याता दिदृक्षया। ते समेत्य यथाधर्मं पाण्डवा वृष्णिभिः सह॥ विवुशः सहिता राजन् पुरं वारणसाह्वयम्।
en: They all proceeded forward to see and greeted them warnly. The Pandavas then, uniting with the Vrishnis according to the us usual formalities, together entered, O king, the city of Hastinapur.

sn: महतस्तस्य सैन्यस्य खुरनेमिस्वनेन ह॥ द्यावापृथिव्योः खं चैव सर्वमासीत् समावृतम्।
en: With the voices and the clatter of cars of that powerful host, the Earth and the sky, and the firmament itself, became of it were, entirely filled.

sn: ते कोशानग्रतः कृत्वा विविशेः स्वपुरं तदा॥ पाण्डवाः प्रीतमनसः सामात्याः ससुहणाः।
en: With rejoicing hearts, the Pandavas, accompanied by their officers and friends, entered the capital, placing that treasure in their van.

sn: ते समेत्य यथान्यायं धृतराष्ट्रं जनाधिपम्॥ कीर्तयन्तः स्वनामानि तस्य पादौ ववन्दिरे।
en: Going according to custom, to king Dhritarashtra first, they adored his feet, announcing their respective names.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रादनु च ते गान्धारी सुबलात्मजाम्॥ कुन्ती च राजशार्दूल तदा भरतसत्तम।
en: Those foremost ones of Bharata's race, O chief of kings, then paid their respectful salutations to Gandhari, the daughter of Subala, and to Kunti.

sn: विदुरं पूजयित्वा च वैश्यापुत्रं समेत्य च॥ पूज्यमानाः स्म ते वीरा व्यरोचन्त विशाम्पते।
en: They next adored (their uncle) Vidura and Yuyutsu, the son of Dhritarashtra by his Vaishya wife. Those heroes were then adored by others and they shone forth in beauty, O king.

sn: ततस्तत् परमाश्चर्यं विचित्रं महदद्भुतम्॥ शुश्रुवुस्ते तदा वीराः पितुस्ते जन्म भारत।
en: After this, O Bharata, those heroes heard the news of that highly wonderful and marvellous and glad some birth of your father.

sn: तदुपश्रुत्य तत् कर्म वासुदेवस्य धीमतः॥ पूजार्ह पूजयामासुः कृष्णं देवकिनन्दनम्।
en: Hearing of that feat of the highly intelligent Vasudeva, they all adored Krishna, the delighter of Devaki, who was every way worthy of adoration.

sn: ततः कतिपयाहस्य व्यास: सत्यवतीसुतः॥ आजगाम महातेजा नगरं नागसाह्वयम्।
en: Then, after a few days, Vyasa, the son of Satyavati, gifted with great cnergy, came to the city of Hastinapur.

sn: तस्य सर्वे यथान्यायं पूजाचंक्रुः कुरूद्वहाः॥ सह वृष्ण्यन्धकव्याघैरुपासांचक्रिरे तदा। तत्र नानाविधाकाराः कथाः समभिकीर्त्य वै॥
en: The perpctuators of Kuru's race adored the great Rishi according to the usual custom. Indeed, those heroes, with those foremost princes of the Vrihini and the Andhaka-races worshipped the sage.

sn: युधिष्ठिरो धर्मसुतो व्यासं वचनमब्रवीत्। भवत्प्रसादाद् भगवन् यदिदं रत्नमाहृतम्॥ उपयोक्तुं तदिच्छामि वाजिमेधे महाक्रतौ।
en: After having conversed on various topics, Dharma's son Yudhishthira addressed Vyasa and said, This treasure, O holy one, which has been brought through your favour, I desire to devote to that great Horse-Sacrifice.

sn: तमनुज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवता मुनिसत्तम। त्वदधीना वयं सर्वे कृष्णस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: 0 best of ascetics, I wish to have your permission. We are all, O Rishi, at your disposal, and at that of the great Krishna.

sn: व्यास उवाच अनुजानाभि राजंस्त्वां क्रियतां यदनन्तरम्। यजस्व वाजिमेधेन विधिवद् दक्षिणावता॥
en: Vyasa said I give you permission, O king, Do what should be done after this. Do you adore the deities duly by performing the Horse-Sacrifice with profuse gifts.

sn: अश्वमेधो हि राजेन्द्र पावनः सर्वपाप्मनाम्। तेनेष्ट्वा त्वं विपाप्मा वै भविता नात्र संशयः॥
en: The Horse-Sacrifice, O king, is a purifier of all sins. Forsooth, having adored the deities by that sacrifice you will surely be purged of all sins.

sn: इत्युक्तः स तु धर्मात्मा कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। अश्वमेधस्य कौरव्य चकाराहरणे मतिम्॥
en: Vaishmpayana said Thus addressed, the Kuru-King Yudhishthira of righteous soul, O monarch, began to make the necessary preparations for the Horse-Sacrifice.

sn: समनुज्ञाप्य तत् सर्वं कृष्णद्वैपायनं नृपः। वासुदेवमथाभ्येत्य वाग्मी वचनमब्रवीत्॥ देवकी सुप्रजा देवी त्वया पुरुषसत्तम। यद् ब्रूयां त्वां महाबाहो तत् कृथास्त्वमिहाच्युत॥
en: Having represented all this to the Islandborn Krishna, the king gifted with great eloquence, approached Vasudeva and said, 'O foremost of all beings, the goddess Devaki has, through you come to be considered as the most fortunate of mothers. O you of undercaying glory, do you perform what I shall now tell you, O mighty-armed one.

sn: त्वत्प्रभावार्जितान् भोगानश्नीम यदुनन्दन। पराक्रमेण बुद्ध्या च त्वयेयं निर्जिता पही।॥
en: O delighter of the Kurus, the various enjoyments we enjoy, have all been acquired are are through your power. The whole Earth has been subjugated by you with the help of your prowess and intelligence.

sn: दीक्षयस्व त्वमात्मानं त्वं हि नः परमो गुरुः। त्वयीष्टवति दाशार्ह विपाप्मा भविता ह्यहम्॥
en: Do you, therefore, cause yourself to undergo the rites of initiation. You are our highest preceptor and master. If you perform the sacrifice, O you of the Dasharha-race, I shall be purified from every sin.

sn: त्वं हि यज्ञोऽक्षरः सर्वस्त्वं धर्मस्त्वं प्रजापतिः। त्वं गतिः सर्वभूतानामिति मे निश्चिता मतिः॥
en: You Sacrifice! You the Indestructible! You are this All! You are Virtue! You are Prajapati! You are the goal of all creatures! This is iny certain conclusion.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच त्वमेवैतन्महाबाहो वक्तुमर्हस्यरिंदम। त्वं गतिः सर्वभूतानामिति मे निश्चिता मतिः॥
en: Vasudeva said O mighty-armed one, what you say is worthy of you, O chastiser of enemies! You are the goal of all creatures. This is my certain conclusion.

sn: त्वं चाद्य कुरुवीराणां धर्मेण हि विराजसे। गुणीभूताः स्म ते राजंस्त्वं नो राजा गुरुर्मतः॥
en: Of the heroes of the Kuru-race, you shine today in great glory for your virtue! They have all been cast into the shade, O king, by you! You are our king, and you are our senior.

sn: यजस्य मदनुज्ञातः प्राप्य एष क्रतुस्त्वया। युनक्तु नो भवान् कार्ये यत्र वाञ्छसि भारत॥ सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि सर्वे कर्तास्मि तेऽनघ।
en: With my approval freely granted, do you worship the celestials in the sacrifice suggested. Do you, O Bharata, appoint us to whatever task you like. Truly, do I pledge myself that I shall accomplish all, O sinless one, that you may bid me accomplish,

sn: भीमसेनार्जुनौ चैव तथा माद्रवतीसुतौ। इष्टवन्तो भविष्यन्ति त्वयीष्टवति पार्थिवे॥
en: Bhimasena and Arjuna and the two sons of Madravati will be sacrificing when you, O king, sacrifice Bhimasena and Arjuna and the two sons of Madravati will be sacrificing when you, O king, sacrifice

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु कृष्णेन धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। व्यासमामन्त्र्य मेधावी ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus addressed by Krishna, Yudhishthira, the of Dharma, gifted with great intelligence, saluted Vyasa and said these words:

sn: यदा कालं भवान् वेत्ति हयमेधस्य तत्त्वतः। दीक्षयस्व तदा मां त्वं त्वय्यायत्तो हि मे क्रतुः॥
en: Do you cause me to be initiated when the proper hour, as you truly know, come for that rite. This my sacrifice entirely depends on you. son

sn: व्यास उवाच अहं पैलोऽथ कौन्तेय याज्ञवल्क्यस्तथैव च। विधानं यद् यथाकालं तत् कर्तारो न संशयः॥
en: Vyasa said Myself, O son of Kunti, and Paila and Yajnavalkya, shall, undoubtedly, achieve every rite at the proper time.

sn: चैत्र्यां हि पौर्णमास्यां तु तव दीक्षा भविष्यति। सम्भाराः सम्भियन्तां च यज्ञार्थं पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: The rite of initiating you will be performed on the day of full moon belonging to the month of Chaitra. Let all the necessaries of the sacrifice, O foremost of men, be got ready.

sn: अश्वविद्याविदश्चैव सूता विप्राश्च तद्विदः। मेध्यमश्वं परीक्षन्तां तव यज्ञार्थसिद्धये॥
en: Let Sutas well-versed in the science of horses and let Brahmanas also possessed of the same learning, select, after examination, a worthy horse in order that your sacrifice may be completed.

sn: तमुत्सृज यथाशास्त्रं पृथिवीं सागराम्बराम्। स पर्येतु यशो दीप्तं तव पार्थिव दर्शयन्॥
en: Loosening the animal according to the injunctions of the scriptures, let him wander over the whole Earth with her belt of seas, showing your effulgent glory, O king.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः स तथेत्युक्त्वा पाण्डवः पृथिवीपतिः। चकार सर्वे राजेन्द्र यथोक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thius addressed (by the Rishi), Yudhishthira, the royal son of Pandu, answered, 'So be it!' and then, O monarch, he accomplished all that that utterer of Brahma had said.

sn: सम्भराश्चैव राजेन्द्र सर्वे संकल्पिताऽभवन्। स सम्भारान् समाहृत्य नृपो धर्मसुतस्तदा॥ न्यवेदयदमेयात्मा कृष्णद्वैपायनाय वै।
en: All the articles necessary for the sacrifice, O king, were duly procured. The royal son of Dharma, gifted with immeasurable soul, having procured all the necessaries, inforined the Island-born Krishna of it.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा व्यासो धर्मात्मजं नृपम्॥ यथाकालं यथायोगं सज्जाः स्म तव दीक्षणे।
en: Then the highly energetic Vyasa said to the royal son of Dharma, “As regards ourselves, we are all prepared to initiate you in view of the sacrifice.

sn: स्फ्यश्च कूर्चश्च सौवर्णो यच्चान्यदपि कौरव॥ तत्र योग्यं भवेत् किंचिद् रौक्मं तत् क्रियतामिति।
en: Let the Sphya and the Kurcha and all the other articles that, o you of Kuru's race, may be necessary for your sacrifice, be made of gold.

sn: अश्वश्चोत्सृज्यतामद्य पृथ्व्यामथ यथाक्रमम्। सुगुप्तं चरतां चापि यथाशास्त्रं यथाविधि॥
en: Let the horse also be loosened today, for wandering on the Earth, according to the ordinances of the scriptures. Let the animal, duly protected, wander over the Earth.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अयमश्वो यथा ब्रह्मन्नुस्तृष्टः पृथिवीमिमाम्। चरिष्यति यथाकामं तत्र वै संविधीयताम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said Let arrangements be made by you, O twiceborn one, about loosening this horse for enabling it to wander over the Earth at its will.

sn: पृथिवीं पर्यटन्तं हि तुरगं कामचारिणम्। कः पालयेदिति मुने तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: You should, O ascetic, say who will protect this horse while roaming over the Earth freely according to its will.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः स तु राजेन्द्र कृष्णद्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत्। भीमसेनादवरजः श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥ जिष्णुः सहिष्णुर्धष्णुश्च स एनं पालयिष्यति। शक्तः स हि महीं जेतुं निवातकवचान्तकः॥
en: Vaishampayana continued : Thus addressed (by king Yudhishthira), O king, the Island-born Krishna said, He who is born after Bhimasena, who is the foremost of all bowmen, who is called Jishnu, who is gifted with great patience and capable of overcoming all resistance, he will protect the horse. That destroyer of the Nivatakavachas can conquer the whole Earth.

sn: तस्मिन् वस्त्राणि दिव्यानि दिव्यं संहननं तथा। दिव्यं धनुश्चेषुधी च स एनमनुयास्यति॥
en: In him are all celestial weapons, His body is like that of a celestial in its powers of endurance. His bow and quivers are celestial. He will follow this horse.

sn: स हि धर्मार्थकुशलः सर्वविद्याविशारदः। यथाशास्त्रं नृपश्रेष्ठ चारयिष्यति ते हयम्॥
en: He is well-versed in both Religion and Profit. He is a master of all the sciences. O foremost of kings, he will, according to the scriptures, cause the horse to roam and graze at its will.

sn: राजपुत्रो महाबाहुः श्यामो राजीवलोचनः। अभिमन्योः पिता वीरः स एनं पालयिष्यति॥
en: son This mighty-armed prince, of dark colour, is endued with eyes resembling lotus petals. That hero, the father of Abhimanyu, will protect the horse,

sn: भीमसेनोऽपि तेजस्वी कौन्तेयोऽमितविक्रमः। समर्थो रक्षितुं राष्ट्र नकुलश्च विशाम्पते॥
en: Bhimasena also is gifted with great energy. That of Kunti is possessed of immeasurable power. He is competent to protect the kingdom, helped by Nakula, O monarch.

sn: सहदेवस्तु कौरव्य समाधास्यति बुद्धिमान्। कुटुम्बतन्त्रं विधिवत् सर्वमेव महायशाः॥
en: Gifted with great intelligence and fame, Sahadeva will, O you of Kuru's race, duly attend to all the relatives who have been invited to your capital.

sn: तत् तु सर्वे यथान्यायमुक्तः कुरुकुलोद्वहः। चकार फाल्गुनं चापि संदिदेश हयं प्रति॥
en: Thus addressed by the Rishi, that perpetuator of Kuru's race, viz., Yudhishthira, performed every injunction duly and appointed Phalguna to attend to the horse.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एह्यर्जुन त्वया वीर हयोऽयं परिपाल्यताम्। त्वम) रक्षितुं ह्येनं नान्यः कश्चन मानवः॥
en: Yudhishthira said Come, O Arjuna, let the horse, O hero, be protected by you. You alone are competent to protect it, and none else.

sn: ये चापि त्वं महाबाहो प्रत्युद्यान्ति नराधिपाः। तैविग्रहो यथा न स्यात् तथा कार्यं त्वयानघ॥
en: Those kings, O mighty-armed hero who will come forward to encounter you, try O sinless one, to avoid battles with them to the best of your power.

sn: आख्यातव्यश्च भवता यज्ञोऽयं मम सर्वशः। पार्थिवेभ्यो महाबाहो समये गम्यतामिति॥
en: You should also invite them all to this sacrifice of mine. Indeed, O mighty armed one, go forth but try to establish friendly relations with them.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा च धर्मात्मा भ्रातरं सव्यसाचिनम्। भीमं च नकुलं चैव पुरगुप्तौ समादधत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said so to his brother Savyasachi, the righteous-souled king Yudhishthira commanded Bhima and Nakula to protect the city.

sn: कुटुम्बतन्त्रे तदा सहदेवं युधां पतिम्। अनुमान्य महीपालं धृतराष्ट्र युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: With the permission of king Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira then set Sahadeva, that foremost of warriors, to wait upon all the invited guests.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: वैशम्प चाच दीक्षाकाले तु सम्प्राप्त सुमहर्विजः। विधिवद् दीक्षयामासुरश्वमेधाय पार्थिवम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said When the hour for initiation came, all those great Ritvijas duly initiated the king for the Horse-Sacrifice.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: कृत्वा स पशुबन्धांश्च दीक्षितः पाण्डुनन्दनः। धर्मराजो महातेजाः सहविभिळरोचत॥
en: Having finished the rites of binding the sacrificial animals, the son of Pandu, viz., king Yudhishthira the just, gifted with great energy, the initiation being over, shone with great splendour along with those Ritvijas.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: हयश्च हयमेधार्थं स्वयं स ब्रह्मवादिना। उत्सृष्टः शास्त्रविधिना व्यासेनामिततेजसा॥
en: The horse that was brought for the HorseSacrifice was let loose, according to the injunctions of the scriptures, by that utterer of Brahma, viz., Vyasa himself of great energy.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: स राजा धर्मराज राजन् दीक्षितो विबभौ तदा। हेममाली रुक्मकण्ठः प्रदीप्त इव पावकः॥
en: Then king Yudhishthira the just, O king, after the initiation, adorned with a garland of gold around his neck, shone like a burning fire.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: कृष्णाजिनी दण्डपाणिः क्षौमवासाः स धर्मजः। विवभौ द्युतिमान् भूयः प्रजापतिरिवाध्वरे॥
en: Having a black deer-skin for his upper garment, carrying a staff in hand, and wearing a cloth of red silk, the son of Dharina, gifted with great splendour, shone like a second Prajapati seated on the sacrificial after.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: तथैवास्यविजः सर्वे तुल्यवेषा विशाम्पते। बभूवुरर्जुनश्चापि प्रदीप्त इव पावकः॥
en: All his Ritvijas also, O king, were clad in similar dresses. Arjuna also shone like a burning fire.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: श्वेताश्वः कृष्णसारं तं ससाराश्वं धनंजयः। विधिवत् पृथिवीपाल धर्मराजस्य शासनात्॥
en: Dhananjaya, to whose car were yoked white horses, then duly prepared, O king, to follow that horse of the complexion of a black deer, at the command of Yudhishthira.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: विक्षिपन् गाण्डिवं राजन् बद्धगे गङ्गुलित्रवान्। तमश्वं पृथवीपाल मदा युक्तः ससार च॥
en: Repeatedly drawing his bow, named Gandiva, O king, and casing his hand in a fence made of iguana skin, Arjuna, O monarch, prepared to follow that those, O king, with a cheerful heart.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: आकुमारं तदा राजन्नागमत् तत्पुरं विभो। द्रष्टुकामं कुरुश्रेष्ठं प्रयास्यन्तं धनंजयम्॥
en: All Hastinapur, O king, with the very children, came out at that spot from desire of seeing Dhananjaya, that foremost of the Kurus, on the eve of his journey.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: तेषामन्योन्यसम्मादूष्मेव समजायत। दिदृक्षूणां हयं तं च तं चैव हयसारिणम्॥
en: So great was the crowd of spectators that came to see the horse and the prince who was to follow it, that on account of the pressure of bodies, it seemed a fire was created.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: ततः शब्दो महाराज दिशः खं प्रति पूरयन्। बभूव प्रेक्षतां नृणां कुन्तीपुत्रं धनंजयम्॥
en: Loud was the noise which arose from that crowd of men who assembled together for seeing Dhananjaya the son of Kunti, and it seemed to fill all the points of the compass and the entire sky.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: एष गच्छति कौन्तेय तुरगश्चैव दीप्तिमान्। यमन्वेति महाबाहुः संस्पृशन् धनुरुत्तमम्॥
en: And they said, There goes the son of Kunti, are there that horse of burning beauty. Indeed, the mighty-armed hero follows the horse, having armed himself with his excellent bow.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: एवं शुश्राव वदतां गिरो जिष्णुरुदारधीः। स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु व्रजारिष्टं पुनश्चैहीति भारत॥
en: These were the words which the intelligent Jishnu heard. The citizens also blessed him, saying, 'Let blessings be yours'. Go safely and return O Bharata.'

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: अथापरे मनुष्येन्द्र पुरुषा वाक्यमब्रुवन्। नैनं पश्याम सम्म धनुरेतत् प्रदृश्यते॥
en: Others, O chief of men, uttered these words :-'So great is the crowd that we do not see Arjuna. His bow, however, we see.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: एतद्धि भीमनिर्हादं विश्रुतं गाण्डिवं धनुः। स्वस्ति गच्छत्वरिष्टो वै पन्थानमकुतोभयम्॥
en: That is the celebrated bow Gaudiva of terrible twang. Blessed be you. let all dangers fly your path. Let fear nowhere inspire you.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: निवृत्तमेनं द्रक्ष्यामः पुनरेष्यति च ध्रुवम्। एवमाद्या मनुष्याणां स्त्रीणां च भरतर्षभ।॥ शुश्राव मधुरा वाचः पुनः पुनरुदारधीः। याज्ञवल्क्यस्य शिष्यश्च कुशलो यज्ञकर्मणि॥ प्रायात् पार्थेन सहितः शान्त्यर्थं वेदपारगः। ब्राह्मणाश्च महीपाल बहवो वेदपारगाः॥ अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं क्षत्रिवाश्च विशाम्पते। विधिवत् पृथिवीपाल धर्मराजस्य शासनात्॥
en: When he returns we shall see him, for it is certain that he will return. The great Arjuna repeatedly heard these and similar other sweet words of men and women, chief of the Bharatas. A disciple of Yajnavalkya, who was well-versed in all sacrificial rites, and who was a complete master of the Vedas, proceeded with Partha for performing auspicious rites in favour of the hero. Many Brahmanas also, O king, all knowing Vedas, well, and many Kshatriyas too, followed the great hero, at the command, O monarch, of Yudhishthira the just.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: पाण्डवैः पृथिवीमश्वो निर्जितामस्त्रतेजसा। चचार स महाराज यथादेशं च सत्तम॥
en: The horse then travelled, foremost of men, wherever he liked over the Earth already conquered by the Pandavas with the power of their weapons.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: तत्र युद्धानि वृत्तानि यान्यासन् पाण्डवस्य ह। तानि वक्ष्यामि ते वीर विचित्राणि महान्ति च॥
en: In course of the horse's wanderings, O king, many great and wonderful battles were fought between Arjuna and many kings. These I shall describe to you.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: स हयः पृथिवीं राजन् प्रदक्षिणमवर्तत। ससारोत्तरतः पूर्वं तन्निबोध महीपते॥
en: The horse, O king, travelled over the whole Earth. Know, O monarch, that from the north it turned towards the East.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: अवमृद्नन् स राष्ट्राणि पार्थिवानां हयोत्तमः। शनैस्तदा परिययौ श्वेताश्वश्च महारथः॥
en: Grinding the kingdoms of many kings that excellent horse wandered. And it was followed slowly by the great car-warrior Arjuna of white horses.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: तत्र संगणना नास्ति राज्ञामयुतशस्तदा। येऽयुध्यन्त महाराज क्षत्रिया हतबान्धवाः॥
en: O monarch, many Kshatriyas and kings, who fought with Arjuna on that occasion, were rendered miserable for having lost their kinsmen on the field of Kurukshetra.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: किराता यवना राजन् बहवोऽसिधनुर्धराः। म्लेच्छाश्चान्ये बहुविधाः पूर्वं ये निकृता रणे॥ आर्याश्च पृथिवीपालाः प्रहृष्टनरवाहनाः। समीयुः पाण्डुपुत्रेण बहवो युद्धदुर्मदाः॥
en: Many Kiratas also, O king, and Yavanas, all excellent bowmen, and various tribes of Mlechchas too, who had been discomfited before (by the Pandavas on the field of Kurukshetra), and many Aryan kings, possessed of soldiers and animals gifted with great alacrity, and all irresistible if fight, met the son of Pandu in battle.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: एवं वृत्तानि युद्धानि तत्र तत्र महीयते। अर्जुनस्य महीपालै नादेशसमागतैः॥
en: Thus took place innumerable battles in various countries, O monarch, between Arjuna and the kings of various realms who came to encounter him.

description: The horse is let loose and Yudhishthira is initiated
sn: यानि तूभयतो राजन् प्रतप्तानि महान्ति च। तानि युद्धानि वक्ष्यामि कौन्तेयस्य तवाऽनघ॥
en: I shall, O sinless king, describe to you those battles only which were the principal ones among all he fought.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: त्रिगतैरभवद् युद्धं कृतवैरैः किरीटिनः। महारथसमाज्ञातैर्हतानां पुत्रनप्तृभिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said A battle took place between the diademdecked (Arjuna) and the sons and grandsons of the Trigartas whose hostility the Pandavas had incurred before and all of whom were wellknown as powerful car-warriors.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: ते समाज्ञाय सम्प्राप्तं यज्ञियं तुरगोत्तमम्। विषयान्तं ततो वीरा दंशिताः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Having learn that, that foremost of horses, which was intended for the sacrifice, had come to their kingdom, those heroes, accoutring themselves in coats mail, surrounded Arjuna.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: रथिनो बद्धतूणीराः सदश्वैः तूणीरा: सदश्वैः समलंकृतैः। परिवार्य हयं राजन् ग्रहीतुं सम्प्रचक्रमुः॥
en: Mounted on their cars, drawn by excellent and well-decked steeds and with quivers on their backs, they surrounded that horse, O king, and tried to capture it.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: ततः किरीटी संचिन्त्य तेषां तत्र चिकीर्षितम्। वारयामास तान् वीरान् सान्त्वपूर्वमरिंदमः॥
