en: Thinking of that attempt of theirs, the diadem-decked Arjuna, forbade those heroes, with conciliatory words, ochastiser of enemies.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: तदनादृत्य ते सर्वे शरैरभ्यहनस्तदा। तमोरजोभ्यां संछन्नांस्तान् किरीटी न्यवारयत्॥
en: Disregarding Arjuna's message, they attacked him with their arrows. The diadem decked Arjuna resisted those warriors who were under the control of darkness and passion.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: तानब्रवीत् ततो जिष्णुः प्रहसन्निव भारत। निवर्तध्वमधर्मज्ञाः श्रेयो जीवितमेव च॥
en: Jishnu, addressed them smilingly and said, 'Desist, you unrighteous ones! Life is a blessing.'

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: स हि वीरः प्रयास्यन् वै धर्मराजेन वारितः। हतबान्धवा न ते पार्थ हन्तव्याः पार्थिवा इति॥
en: At the time of his starting, he had been earnestly ordered by king Yudhishthira the just not to kill those Kshatriyas whose kinsmen had been killed before on the field of Kurukshetra.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: स तदा तद् वचः श्रुत्वा धर्मराजस्य धीमतः। तान् निवर्तध्वमित्याह न न्यवर्तन्त चापि ते॥
en: Remembering these behest's of king Yudhishthira the just who was gifted with great intelligence, Arjuna asked the Trigartas to forbear. But they disregarded Arjuna's injunction.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: ततस्त्रिगर्तराजानं सूर्यवर्माणमाहवे। विचित्य शरजालेन प्रजहास धनंजयः॥
en: Then Arjuna defeated Suryavarman, the king of the Trigartas, in battle, by shooting countless arrows at him and laughed in scorn.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: ततस्ते रथघोषेण स्थनेमिस्वनेन च। पूरयन्तो दिशः सर्वा धनंजयमुपाद्रवन्॥
en: The Trigarta warriors, however filling the ten points with the sound of their cars and carwheels, rushed towards Dhananjaya.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: सूर्यवर्मा ततः पार्थे शराणां नतपर्वणाम्। शतान्यमुञ्चद् राजेन्द्र लध्वस्त्रमभिदर्शयन्॥
en: Then Suryavarman, showing great lightness of hand, pierced Dhananjaya with hundreds of straight arrows, O king!

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: तथैवान्ये महेष्वासा ये च तस्यानुयायिनः। मुमुचुः शरवर्षाणि धनंजयवधैषिणः॥
en: The other great bowmen, who followed the king and who were all desirous of bringing about the destruction of Dhananjaya, shot showers of arrows on him.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: स तान् ज्यामुखनिर्मुक्तैर्बहुभिः सुबहूशरान्। चिच्छेद पाण्डवो राजंस्ते भूमौ न्यपतंस्तदा॥
en: With numberless arrows shot from his own bowstring, the son of Pandu, O king, cut off those clouds of arrows upon which they fell down.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: केतुवर्मा तु तेजस्वी तस्यैवावरजो युवा। युयुधे भ्रातुराय पाण्डवेन यशस्विना॥
en: Gifted with great energy, Ketuvarman, the younger brother of Suryavarman, and gifted with youthful vigour, fought, for the sake of his brother, against Pandu's son endued with great fame.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य केतुवर्माणमाहवे। अभ्यन्निशितैर्वाणैर्बीभत्सुः परवीरहा।॥
en: Seeing Ketuvarman approaching towards him for battle, Bibhatsu, that destroyer of hostile heroes, killed him with many sharppointed arrows.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: केतुवर्मण्यभिहते धृतवर्मा महारथः। रथेनाशु समुत्पत्य शरैर्जिष्णुमवाकिरत्॥
en: Upon Ketuvarmana's fall, the powerful carwarrior Dlıritavarman, rushing on his car towards Arjuna, showered a perfect downpour of arrows on him.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: तस्य तां शीघ्रतामीक्ष्य तुतोषातीव वीर्यवान्। गुडाकेशो महातेजा बालस्य धृतवर्मणः॥
en: Seeing that lightness of hand shown by the youth Dhritavarman, Gudakesha of great energy and great prowess became highly pleased with him.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: न संदधानं ददृशे नाददानं च तं तदा। किरन्तमेव स शरान् ददृशे पाकशासनिः॥
en: The son of Indra could not see when the young warrior took out his arrows and when he placed them on his bowstring aiming at him. He only saw showers of arrows in the air.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: स तु तं पूजयामास धृतवर्माणमाहवे। मनसा तु मुहूर्तं वै रणे समभिहर्षयन्॥
en: For a brief space of time, Arjuna pleased his enemy and mentally admired his heroism and skill.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: तं पन्नगमिव क्रुद्धं कुरुवीरः स्मयन्निवा प्रीतिपूर्वं महाबाहुः प्राणैर्न व्यपरोपयत्॥
en: The Kuru hero, smiling the while, fought with that youth who took after an angry snake. The mighty-armed Dhananjaya, glad as he was in seeing the courage of Dhritavarman, did not take his life.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: स तथा रक्ष्यमाणो वै पार्थेनामिततेजसा। धृतवर्मा शरं दीप्त मुमोच विजये तदा॥
en: While, however, Partha of immeasurable energy fought mildly with him without wishing to kill him, Dhritavarman shot a burning arrow at him.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: स तेन विजयस्तूर्णमासीद् विद्धः करे भृशम्। मुमोच गाण्डिवं मोहात् तत् पपाताथ भूतले॥
en: Deeply pierced in the hand by that arrow, Vijaya became stupefied and his bow Gandiva dropped down on the Earth from his relaxed grasp.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: धनुषः पततस्तस्य सव्यसाचिकराद् विभो। बभूव सदृशं रूपं शक्रचापस्य भारत॥
en: The from of that bow, O king, when it fell from the grasp of Arjuna, resembled, O Bharata, that of the bow of Indra.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: तस्मिन् विपतिते दिवये महाधनुषि पार्थिवः। जहास सस्वनं हास धृतवर्मा महाहवे॥
en: When that great and celestial bow dropped down, O king, Dhritavarman laughed loudly in battle.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: ततो रोषार्दितो जिष्णुः प्रमृत्य रुधिरं करात्। धनुरादत्त तद् दिव्यं शरवर्ववर्ष च॥
en: At this, Jishnu, worked up with rage wiped the blood from his hand and once more taking up his bow, showered a perfect downpour of arrows.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: ततो हलहलाशब्दो दिवस्पृगभवत् तदा। नानाविधानां भूतानां तत्कर्माणि प्रशंसताम्॥
en: Then a loud and confused noise arose, filling the sky and touching the very heavens, as it were, from various creatures who spoke highly of that feat of Dhananjaya.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: ततः सम्प्रेक्ष्य संक्रुद्धं कालान्तकयमोपमम्। जिष्णुं त्रैगर्तका योधाः परीताः पर्यवारयन्॥ अभिसृत्य परीप्सार्थं ततस्ते धृतवर्मणः। परिववर्गुडाकेशं तत्राद्ध्यद् धनंजयः॥
en: Seeing Jishnu inflamed with wrath and loO king like Yama himself as he appears as the end of the cycle, the Trigarta warriors hastily surrounded him, rushing from their posts and desirous of rescuing Dhritavarman. Seeing himself surrounded by his enemies, Arjuna became more angry than before.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: ततो योधान् जघानाशु तेषां स दश चाष्ट च। महेन्द्रवज्रप्रतिमैरायसैर्बहुभिः शरैः॥
en: He then quickly despatched eighteen of their foremost warriors with many arrows of hard iron which resembled the arrows of the great Indra himself.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: तान् सम्प्रभग्नान् सम्प्रेक्ष्य त्वमाणो धनंजयः। शरैराशीविषाकारैर्जधान स्वनवद्धसन्॥
en: The Trigarta warriors then began to fly. Seeing them retreat, Dhananjaya, quickly shot many shafts at them which resembled angry snakes of dreadful poison, and laughed aloud.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: ते भग्नमनसः सर्वे त्रैगर्तकमहारथाः। दिशोऽभिदुद्रुवू राजन् धनंजयशरार्दिताः॥
en: The powerful car-warriors of the Trigarlas, with dispirited hearts, fled in all directions, greatly afflicted by Dhananjaya with his arrows.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: तमूचुः पुरुषव्याघ्रं संशप्तकनिषूदनम्। तवास्म किंकराः सर्वे सर्वे वै वशगास्तव॥
en: They then addressed that foremost of men, that destroyer of the Samsaptaka army, saying, 'We are your slaves! We yield to you.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: आज्ञापयस्व नः पाथै प्रह्वान् प्रेष्यानवस्थितान्। करिष्यामः प्रियं सर्वं तव कौरवनन्दन॥
en: Do you command us, O Partha! Lo, we wait here as the most docile of your servants! O delighter of the Kurus, we shall execute all your commands.'

description: The fight between Arjuna and Trigartas
sn: एतदाज्ञाय वचनं सर्वोस्तानब्रवीत् तदा। जीवितं रक्षत नृपाः शासनं प्रतिगृह्यताम्॥
en: Hearing these words expressive of their submission, Dhananjaya said them, 'Do you, O kings, save your lives, to and accept my dominion.'

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्राग्ज्योतिषमथाभ्येत्य व्यचरत् स हयोत्तमः। भगदत्तात्मजस्तत्र निर्ययौ रणकर्कशः॥
en: That foremost of horses then proceeded to the kingdom of Pragjyotisha and began to wander there. At this, Bhagadatta's son, who was greatly courageous in battle, came out.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: स हयं पाण्डुपुत्रस्य विषयान्तमुपागतम्। युयुधे भरतश्रेष्ठ वज्रदत्तो महीपतिः॥
en: King Vajradata, O chief of the Bharatas, finding the (sacrificial) horse arrived within his kingdom, fought (for detaining it).

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: सोऽभिनिर्याय नगराद् भगदत्तसुतो नृपः। अश्वमायान्तमुन्मथ्य नगराभिमुखो ययौ॥
en: The royal son of Bhagadatta, coming out of his city, afflicted the horse which was coming (and seizing it), marched back towards his own place.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: तमालक्ष्य महाबाहुः कुरूणामृषभस्तदा। गाण्डीवं विक्षिपस्तूर्णं सहसा समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Marking this, the mighty armed chief of the Kuru-race, speedily stretched his Gandiva, and suddenly rushed towards his enemy.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: ततो गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तैरिषुभिर्मोहितो नृपः। हयमुत्सृज्य तं वीरस्ततः पार्थमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Stupefied by the arrows shot from Gandiva, the heroic son of Bhagadatta, letting loose the horse, fled from Partha.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: पुनः प्रविश्य नगरं दंशितः स नृपोत्तमः। आरुह्य नागप्रवरं निर्ययौ रणकर्कशः॥
en: Once more entering his capital, that foremost of kings, irresistible in battle, cased himself in mail, and mounting on his prince of elephants, came out.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: पाण्डुरेणातपत्रेण ध्रियमाणेन मूर्धनि। दोधूयता चामरेण श्वेतेन च महारथः॥
en: That powerful car-warrior had a white umbrella held over his head, and was fanned with a milk-white yak-tails.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: ततः पार्थं समासाद्य पाण्डवानां महारथम्। आह्वयामास बीभत्सुं बाल्यान्मोहाच्च संयुगे॥
en: Moved by childishness and folly, he challenged Partha, the powerful car warrior of the Pandavas, famed for dreadful deeds in battle, to an encounter with him.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: स वारणं नगप्रख्यं प्रभिन्नकरटामुखम्। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धः श्वेताश्वं प्रति पार्थिवः॥
en: The enraged prince then urged towards Arjuna that elephant of his, which resembled a veritable mountain, and from whose temples and mouth came out streams of juice showing excitement.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: विक्षरन्तं महामेधं परवारणवारणम्। शास्त्रवत् कल्पितं संख्ये विवशं युद्धदुर्मदम्॥
en: Indeed, that elephant showered its secretions like a great mass of clouds pouring rain. Capable of resisting hostile feats of its own species, it had been equipped according to the ordinances of the treatises (on warelephants). Irresistible in battle, it had become so infuriate as to be beyond control.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: प्रचोद्यमानः स गजस्तेन राज्ञा महाबलः। तदाकडुशेन विबभावुत्पतिष्यन्निवाम्बरम्॥
en: Urged on by the prince with the iron-hook, that powerful elephant then scemed as if it would cut through the sky (like a flying hill).

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य क्रुद्धो राजन् धनंजयः। भूमिष्ठो वारणगतं योधयामास भारत॥
en: Seeing it advance towards him, o king, Dhananjaya, filled with anger and standing on the earth, O Bharata, met the prince on its back.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: वज्रदत्तस्ततः क्रुद्धो मुमोचाशु धनंजये। तोमरानग्निसंकाशाशलभानिव वेगितान्॥
en: Filled with anger, Vajradatta quickly shed at Arjuna a number of broad headed arrows gifted with the energy of fire and resembling (as they coursed through the air) a cloud of speedily moving locusts.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: अर्जुनस्तानसम्प्राप्तान् गाण्डीवप्रभवैः शरैः। द्विधा त्रिधा च चिच्छेद ख एव खगभैस्तदा॥
en: Arjuna, however, with arrows sped from Gandiva, cut off those arrows, come into tow, and some into three, pieces. He cut them off in the sky itself with those arrows of his passing through the sky.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: स तान् दृष्ट्वा तथा छिन्नांस्तोमरान् भगदत्तजः। इषूनसक्तांस्त्वरितः प्राहिणोत् पाण्डवं प्रति॥
en: The son of Bhagadatta, seeing his broadheaded arrows thus cut off, quickly sped at Arjuna a number of other arrows in a continuous line.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: ततोऽर्जुनस्तूर्णतरं रुक्मपुवानजिह्मगान्। प्रेष्यामास संक्रुद्धो भगदत्तात्मजं प्रति॥
en: Filled with anger at this, Arjuna more quickly than before, shot at Bhagadatta's son a number of straightly coursing arrows equipped with golden wings.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: स तैर्विद्धो महातेजा वज्रदत्तो महामृधे। भृशाहतः पपातोयॊ न त्वेनमजहात् स्मृतिः॥
en: Vajradatta of powerful energy, struck with great force and pierced with those arrows in that fierce encounter, fell down on the Earth. Consciousness, however, did not leave him.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: ततः स पुनरारुह्य वारणप्रवरं रणे। अव्यग्रः प्रेषयामास जयार्थी विजयं प्रति॥
en: Mounting on his prince of elephants again in the midst of that battle, the son of Bhagadatta, desirous of victory, very coolly shot a number of arrows at Arjuna.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: तस्मै बाणांस्ततो जिष्णुर्निर्मुक्ताशीविषोपमान्। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो ज्वलितज्वलनोपमान्॥
en: Filled with anger, Jishnu then shot at the prince a number of arrows which looked like burning flames of fire and which appeared to be so many snakes of dreadful poison.

description: The fight between Arjuna and Bhagadata
sn: स तैर्विद्धो महानागो विस्रवन् रुधिरं बभौ। गौरिकाक्तमिवाम्भोऽद्रिर्बहुप्रस्रवणं तदा।॥
en: Pierced therewith, the powerful elephant, emitting a large quantity of blood, looked like a mountain of many springs discharging rillets of water coloured with red chalk.

sn: एवं त्रिरात्रमभवत् तद् युद्धं भरतर्षभ। अर्जुनस्य नरेन्द्रेण वृत्रेणेव शतक्रतोः॥
en: Vaishampayana said — Thus went on that battle, O chief of the Bharatas, for three days between Arjuna and that prince like the encounter between him of a hundred sacrifices and Vritra.

sn: ततश्चतुर्थे दिवसे वज्रदत्तो महाबलः। जाहास सस्वनं हासं वाक्यं चेदमथाब्रवीत्॥ अर्जुनार्जुन तिष्ठस्व न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यसे। त्वां निहत्य करिष्यामि पितुस्तोयं यथाविधि॥
en: On the fourth day, Vajradatta of great power laughed loudly and addressing Arjuna, said these words :-Wait, wait, O Arjuna! You shall not excape me alive! Killing you I shall duly discharge the water-rite of my father.

sn: त्वया वृद्धो मम पिता भगदत्तः पितुः सखा। हतो वृद्धो मम पिता शिशुं मामद्य योधय॥
en: My aged father Bhagadatta, who was the friend of your father, was killed by you on account of his weight of years. Do you, however, fight me who am but a boy.

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा संक्रुद्धो वज्रदत्तो नराधिपः। प्रेषयामास कौरव्य वारणं पाण्डवं प्रति॥
en: Having said these words, O you of Kuru's race, king Vajradatta, filled with anger, urged his elephant towards the son of Pandu.

sn: सम्प्रेष्यमाणो नागेन्द्रो वज्रदत्तेन धीमता। उत्पतिष्यन्निवाकाशमभिदुद्राव पाण्डवम्॥
en: Urged on by the highly intelligent Vajradatta, that prince of elephants, as if desirous of cutting through the sky, rushed towards Dhananjaya.

sn: अग्रहस्तसुमुक्तेन शीकरेण स नागराट्। समौक्षत गुडाकेशं शैलं नीलमिवाम्बुदः॥
en: That best of elephants drenched Arjuna with a shower of juice emitted from the end of his trunk, like a mass of blue clouds drenching a hill with its down-pour.

sn: स तेन प्रेषितो राज्ञा मेघवद् विनदन् मुहुः। मुखाडम्बरसंहादैरभ्यद्रवत फाल्गुनम्॥
en: Indeed, urged on by the king, the elephant, repeatedly roaring like a cloud, rushed towards Phalguna, sending forth deep noise from its mouth.

sn: स नृत्यन्निव नागेन्द्रो वज्रदत्तप्रचोदितः। आससाद द्रुतं राजन् कौरवाणां महारथम्॥
en: Indeed urged on by Vajradatta that prince of elephants quickly moved towards the powerful car-warrior of the Kurus, with the tread of one that seemed to dance in excitement.

sn: तमायान्तमथालक्ष्य वज्रदत्तस्य वारणम्। गाण्डीवमाश्रित्य बली न व्यकम्पत शत्रुहा॥
en: Seeing that beast of Vajradatta advance towards him, that destroyer of enemies, viz., the powerful Dhananjaya, relaying on Gandiva, stood his ground without shaking with fear.

sn: चुक्रोध बलवच्चापि पाण्डवस्तस्य भूपतेः। कार्यविघ्नमनुस्मृत्य पूर्ववैरं च भारत॥
en: Recollecting what an obstacle Vajradatta was proving to the performance of his task, and remembering the old enmity of the house, the son of Pandu became greatly excited with rage against the king.

sn: ततस्तं वारणं क्रुद्धः शरजालेन पाण्डवः। निवारयामास तदा बेलेव मकरालयम्॥
en: Worked up with rage, Dhananjaya impeded the course of that beast with a shower of arrows like the shore resisting the surging sea.

sn: स नागप्रवरः श्रीमानर्जुनेन निवारितः। तस्थौ शरैर्विनुन्नाङ्गः श्वाविच्छललितो यथा।॥
en: That best of elephants and beautiful in appearance, thus impeded by Arjuna, stopped in its course, with body pierced with many an arrow, like a porcupine with its quills erect.

sn: निवारितं गजं दृष्ट्वा भगदत्तसुतो नृपः। उत्ससर्ज शितान् बाणानर्जुनं क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥
en: Seeing his elephant impeded in its course, the royal son Bhagadatta, deprived of sense by anger, shot many whetted arrows at Arjuna.

sn: अर्जुनस्तु महाबाहुः शरैररिनिघातिभिः। वारयामास तान् बाणांस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: The mighty-armed Arjuna baffled all those arrows with many foe-destroying arrows of his. The feat appeared to be exceedingly wonderful.

sn: ततः पुनरभिक्रुद्धो राजा प्राग्ज्योतिषाधिपः। प्रेषयामास नागेन्द्रं बलवत् पर्वतोपमम्॥
en: Once more the king of the Pragjyotishas, worked up with rage, forcibly urged his elephant, which resembled a mountain, at Arjuna.

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य बलवत् पाकशासनिः। नाराचमग्निसंकाशं प्राहिणोद् वारणं प्रति॥
en: Seeing the beast once more advancing towards him, Arjuna shot with great strength an arrow at it which resembled a veritable flame of fire.

sn: स तेन वारणो राजन् मर्मस्वभिहतो भृशम्। पपात सहसा भूमौ वज्ररुग्ण इवाचलः॥
en: Cut to the quick, O king, by the son of Pandu, the beast suddenly dropped down on the Earth like a mountain-summit loosened by a thunder-bolt.

sn: स पतशुशुभे नागो धनंजयशराहतः। विशन्निव महाशैलो महीं वज्रप्रपीडितः॥
en: Struck with Dhananjaya's arrow, the elephant, as it lay on the Earth, looked like a huge mountain-cliff lying on the ground, loosened by the bolt of Indra.

sn: तस्मिन् निपतिते नागे वज्रदत्तस्य पाण्डवः। तं न भेतव्यमित्याह ततो भूमिगतं नृपम्॥
en: When the elephant of Vajradatta was prostrated on the ground the so of Pandu, addressing the king who had fallen down with his beast, said, 'Do not fear.'

sn: अब्रवीद्धि महातेजाः प्रस्थितं मां युधिष्ठिरः। राजानस्ते न हन्तव्या धनंजय कथंचन॥
en: Indeed, Yudhishthira of great energy said to me while commissioning me for this task even these words, viz., You should not, O Dhananjaya, kill those kings (who may give you battle).

sn: सर्वमेतन्नरव्याघ्र भवत्येतावता कृतम्। योधाश्चापि न हन्तव्या धनञ्जय रणे त्वया॥
en: O foremost of men, you should consider your task as accomplished if only you disable those hostile kings! You should not also, O Dhananjaya, kill the warriors of those kings who may come forth to fight you.

sn: वक्तव्याश्चापि राजानः सर्वे सहसुहृज्जनैः। युधिष्ठिरस्याश्वमेधो भवद्भिरनुभूयताम्॥
en: They should be requested to come, with all their kinsmen and friends, to the HorseSacrifice of Yudhishthira.

sn: इति भ्रातृवचः श्रुत्वा न हन्मि त्वां नराधिप। उत्तिष्ठ न भयं तेऽस्ति स्वस्तिमान् गच्छ पार्थिव॥२४
en: Having heard these commands of my brother, I shall not kill you, O king! Rise up; let no fear be yours; return to your city safe and sound, O king.

sn: आगच्छेया महाराज परां चैत्रीमुपस्थिताम्। यदाश्वमेधो भविता धर्मराजस्य धीमतः॥
en: When the day of full moon in the month of Chaitra comes, you shall O great king, go to that sacrifice of king Yudhishthira the just, for it takes place. on that day!

sn: एवमुक्तः स राजा तु भगदत्तात्मजस्तदा। तथेत्येवाब्रवीद वाक्यं पाण्डवेनाभिनिर्जितः॥
en: Thus addressed by Arjuna the royal son of Bhagadatta, defeated by the son of Pandu, said, 'So be it.' that sacrifice of king Yudhishthira the just, for it takes place. on that day!

sn: एवमुक्तः स राजा तु भगदत्तात्मजस्तदा। तथेत्येवाब्रवीद वाक्यं पाण्डवेनाभिनिर्जितः॥
en: Thus addressed by Arjuna the royal son of Bhagadatta, defeated by the son of Pandu, said, 'So be it.'

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सैन्धवैरभवद् युद्धं ततस्तस्य किरीटिनः। हतशेषैर्महाराज हतानां च सुतैरपि॥
en: There took place a great battle between the diadem decked Arjuna and the hundreds of Saindhavas who still lived after the destruction of their clan.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: तेऽवतीर्णमुपश्रुत्य विषयं श्वेतवाहनम्। प्रत्युद्ययुरमृष्यन्तो राजानः पाण्डवर्षभम्॥
en: Hearing that he of white horses had entered their territories, those Kshatriyas came out against him, unable to bear that foremost one of Pandu's race.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: अश्वं च तं परामृश्य विषयान्ते विषोपमाः। न भयं चक्रिरे पार्थाद् भीमसेनादनन्तरात्॥
en: Those warriors who were as terrible as dreadful poison, finding the horse within their dominion, seized it without being filled with any fear of Partha who was the younger brother of Bhimasena.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: तेऽविदूराद् धनुष्पाणिं यज्ञियस्य हयस्य च। बीभत्सुं प्रत्यपद्यन्त पदातिनमवस्थितम्॥
en: Advancing against Bibhatsu who waited on foot, armed with his bow, upon the sacrificial horse, they attacked him from a near point.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ततस्ते तं महावीर्या राजानः पर्यवारयन्। जिगीषन्तो नरव्याघ्र पूर्वं विनिकृता युधि॥
en: Defeated in battle before, those Kshatriyas of great energy, moved by the desire of victory, surrounded that foremost of men.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ते नामान्यपि गोत्राणि कर्माणि विविधानि च। कीर्तयन्तस्तदा पार्थं शरवषैरवाकिरन्॥
en: Proclaiming their names and families and their various feats, they showered their arrows on Partha.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ते किरन्तः शरवातान् बारणप्रतिवारणान्। रणे जयमभीप्सन्तः कौन्तेयं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Pouring showers of arrows of such fierce energy as were capable of obstructing the course of hostile elephants, those heroes surrounded the son of Kunti, desirous of defeating him in battle.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ते समीक्ष्य च तं कृष्णमुग्रकर्माणमाहवे। सर्वे ययुधिरे वीरा रथस्थास्तं पदातिनम्॥
en: Themselves seated on cars, they fought Arjuna of dreadful feats who was on foot,

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ते तमाजन्जिरे वीरं निवातकवचान्तकम्। संशप्तकनिहन्तारं हन्तारं सैन्धवस्य च।॥
en: From every side they began to strike that hero, that destroyer of the Nivatakavachas, that destroyer of the Samsaptakas, that destroyer of the king of the Sindhus.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ततो रथसहस्रेण हयानामयुतेन च। कोष्ठकीकृत्य बीभत्सुं प्रहृष्टमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: Surrounding him on all sides as within a cage by means of a thousand cars and ten thousand horse, those brave warriors expressed their joy.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: तं स्मरन्तो वधं वीरा: सिन्धुराजस्य चाहवे। जयद्रथस्य कौरव्य समरे सव्यसाचिना॥ ततः पर्जन्यवत् सर्वे शरवृष्टीरवासृजन्। तै: कीर्णः शुशुभे पार्थो रविर्मेघान्तरे यथा॥
en: Recollecting the destruction by Dhananjaya of Jayadratha in battle, O you of Kuru's race, they poured heavy showers of arrows on that hero like a mass of clouds showering a heavy downpour. Overwhelmed with that arrow shower, Arjuna looked like the sun covered by a cloud.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: स शरैः समवच्छन्नश्चकाशे पाण्डवर्षभः। पञ्जरान्तरसंचारी शकुन्त इव भारत॥
en: That foremost son of Pandu, in the midst of that cloud of arrows, resembled a bird in the midst of an iron cage, O Bharata.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ततो हाहाकृतं सर्वं कौन्तेये शरपीडिते। त्रैलोक्यमभवद् राजन् रविरासीच्च निष्प्रभः॥
en: Seeing the son of Kunti thus afflicted with arrows, cries of oh and alas were uticred by the three worlds, and the Sun himself became shorn of his splendour.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ततो ववौ महाराज मारुतो लोमहर्षणः। राहुरग्रसदादित्यं युगपत् सोममेव च॥
en: Then, O king, a terrible wind began to blow, and Rahu swallowed up both the Sun and the Moon simultaneously.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: उल्काश्च जधिरे सूर्यं विकीर्यन्त्यः समन्ततः। वेपथुश्चाभवद् राजन् कैलासस्य महागिरेः॥
en: Many meteors struck the solar disc and then shot in different directions. The prince of mountains, viz., Kailasa, began to tremble.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: मुमुचुः श्वासमत्युष्णं दुःखशोकसमन्विताः। सप्तर्षयो जातभयास्तथा देवर्षयोऽपि च॥
en: The seven (celestial) Rishis, as also the other Rishis of Heaven, stricken with fear, and afflicted with grief and sorrow, breathed hot sights.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: शशं चाशु विनिर्भिद्य मण्डलं शशिनोऽपतत्। विपरीता दिशश्चापि सर्वा धूमाकुलास्तथा॥
en: Piercing through the sky, those meteors fell on the Lunar disc as well. All the points of the compass became filled with smoke and assumed a strange aspect.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: रासभारुणसंकाशा धनुष्मन्तः सविद्युतः। आवृत्य गगनं मेघा मुमुचुर्मोसशोणितम्॥
en: Reddish clouds, with flashes of lightning laying in their midst and the bow of Indra measuring them from side to side, suddenly covered the sky and poured flesh and bloods on the Earth.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: एवमासीत् तदा वीरे शरवर्षेण संवृते। फाल्गुने भरतश्रेष्ठ तद्युतमिवाभवत्।॥
en: Such was the aspect which all nature assumed when that hero was overwhelmed with showers of arrows. Indeed, when Phalguna, that foremost one among the Bharatas, was thus afflicted, those marvels were witnessed.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: तस्य तेनावकीर्णस्य शरजालेन सर्वतः। मोहात् पपात गाण्डीवमावापश्च करादपि।॥
en: Overwhelmed by that dense cloud of arrows, Arjuna became stupefied. The bow, Gandiva, fell down from his relaxed grip and his leathern hence also dropped down.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: तस्मिन् मोहमनुप्राप्ते शरजालं महत् तदा। सैन्धवा मुमुचुस्तूर्णं गतसत्त्वे महारथे॥
en: When Dhananjaya became stupefied, the Saindhava warriors once more shot forthwith at that senseless warrior, numberless other arrOWS.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ततो मोहसमापन्नं ज्ञात्वा पार्थं दिवौकसः। सर्वे वित्रस्तमनसस्तस्य शान्तिकृतोऽभवन्॥
en: Understanding that the son of Pritha was insensible, the celestials, with hearts stricken with fear, began to seek his well-being by uttering various benedictions.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ततो देवर्षयः सर्वे तथा सप्तर्षयोऽपि च। ब्रह्मर्षयश्च विजयं जेपुः पार्थस्य धीमतः॥
en: Then the celestial Rishis, the seven Rishis, and the twice-born Rishis, became engaged in silent recitations from desire of giving victory to the highly intelligent son of Pritha's.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ततः प्रदीपिते देवैः पार्थतेजसि पार्थिव। तस्थावचलवद् धीमान् संग्रामे परमास्त्रवित्॥
en: When at last the energy of Partha blazed forth through those deeds of the dwellers of the celestial region, that hero, who was conversant with celestial weapons of great efficacy, stood immovable like a hill.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: विचकर्ष धनुर्दिव्यं ततः कौरवनन्दनः। यन्त्रस्येवेह शब्दोऽभून्महांस्तस्य पुनः पुनः॥
en: The delighter of the Kurus then drew his celestial bow. And as he repeatedly stretched the bowstring, the twang that followed resembled the loud sound of some strong machine.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ततः स शरवर्षाणि प्रत्यमित्रान् प्रति प्रभुः। ववर्ष धनुषा पार्थो वर्षाणीव पुरंदरः॥
en: Like Purandara pouring rain, the powerful Arjuna then, with that bow of his, poured incessant showers of arrows on his enemies.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: ततस्ते सैन्धवा योधाः सर्व एव सराजकाः। नादृश्यन्त शरैः कीर्णाः शलभैरिव पादपाः॥
en: Pierced by those arrows, the Saindava warriors with their cuels became invisible like trees covered with locusts.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: तस्य शब्देन वित्रेसुर्भयार्ताश्च विदुद्रुवुः । मुमुचुश्चाश्रु शोकार्ताः शुशुचुश्चापि सैन्धवाः॥
en: Terror-stricken at the very sound of Gandiva and filled with consternation they fled away. In grief of hear they shed tears and cried aloud.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: तांस्तु सर्वान् नरव्याघ्रः सैन्धवान् व्यचरत् बली। अलातचक्रवद् राजशरजालैः समार्पयत्॥
en: The powerful warrior moved a midst that host of enemies with the celerity of a fiery wheel, all the time piercing those warriors with his arrows.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: तदिन्द्रजालप्रतिम बाणजालममित्रहा। विसृज्य दिक्षु सर्वासु महेन्द्र इव वज्रभृत्॥
en: Like the great Indra, the holder of the thunder-bolt, that destroyer of enemies viz., Arjuna, shot from his bow in every direction that shower of arrows which resembled a sight produced by magic.

description: The battle between Arjuna and the remaining Saindhavas
sn: मेघजालनिभं सैन्यं विदार्य शरवृष्टिभिः। विबभौ कौरवश्रेष्ठः शरदीव दिवाकरः॥
en: The Kaurava hero, piercing the hostile army with showers of arrows looked resplendent like the autumnal Sun when he disperses the clouds with his powerful rays. once

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो गाण्डीवभृच्छूरो युद्धाय समुपस्थितः। विबभौ युधि दुर्धर्षो हिमवानचलो यथा॥
en: Vaishampayana said The irresistible holder of Gandiva, ready for battle, stood immovable on the field like Himavat himself.

sn: ततस्ते सैन्धवा योधाः पुनरेव व्यवस्थिताः। व्यमुञ्चन्त सुसंरब्धाः शरवर्षाणि भारत॥
en: The Saindhava warriors, more rallying, showered in great rage repeated down-pours of arrows on him.

sn: तान् प्रहस्य महाबाहुः पुनरेव व्यवस्थितान्। ततः प्रोवाच कौन्तेयो मुमूर्षुश्लक्ष्णया गिरा।
en: The mighty-armed hero, laughing at his enemies, who had once more rallied but who were on the point of death, addressed them in these soft words.

sn: युध्यध्वं परया शक्त्या यतध्वं विजये मम॥ कुरुध्वं सर्वकार्याणि महद् वो भयमागतम्।
en: Do you fight to to best of your power and do you try to defeat me. Do you, however, accomplish all necessary deeds, for a great danger awaits you all.

sn: एष योत्स्यामि सर्वांस्तु निवार्य शरवागुराम्॥ तिष्ठध्वं युद्धमनसो दर्प शमयितास्मि वः।
en: See, I fight all of you, baffling your clouds of arrows! Bent as you are on battle, wait a little. I shall soon quell your pride.

sn: एतावदुक्त्वा कौरव्यो रोषाद् गाण्डीवभृत् तदा॥ ततोऽथ वचनं स्मृत्वा भ्रातुर्येष्ठस्य भारत।
en: The holder of Gandiva, having said these words in anger, recollected, however, the words, O Bharata, of his eldest brother.

sn: न हन्तव्या रणे तात क्षत्रिया विजिगीषवः॥ जेतव्याश्चेति यत् प्रोक्तं धर्मराज्ञा महात्मना। चिन्तयामास स तदा फाल्गुनः पुरुषर्षभः॥ इत्युक्तोऽहं नरेन्द्रेण न हन्तव्या नृपा इति। कथं तन्न मृषेदं स्याद् धर्मराजवचः शुभम्॥
en: Those words were :-You should not, O child, kill those Kshatriyas who will come against you for battle! They should, however, be defeated by you! That foremost of men, Phalguna, had been thus addressed by king Yudhishthira the just, of great soul. He, therefore, began to reflect thus. Thus was I commissioned by my by my brother. Warriors advancing against me should not be killed.

sn: न हन्येरंश्च राजानो राज्ञश्चाज्ञां कृता भवेत्। इति संचिन्त्य स तदा फाल्गुनः पुरुषर्षभः॥ प्रोवाच वाक्यं धर्मज्ञः सैन्धवान् युद्धदुर्मदान्।
en: I must act in such a way as not to falsify the words of king Yudhishthira the just. Having arrived at this conclusion, Phalguna, that foremost of men, then said to those Saindhavas who were all dreadful in battle, these words:

sn: श्रेयो वदामि युष्माकं न हिंसेयमवस्थितान्। यश्च वक्ष्यति संग्रामे तवास्मीति पराजितः॥
en: I say what is for your benefit. Though staying before me, I do not wish to kill you. He amongst you who will say to me that he has been defeated by me and that he is mine, will be spared by me.

sn: एतच्छुत्वा वचो मह्यं कुरुध्वं हितमात्मनः॥ ततोऽन्यथा कृच्छ्रगता भविष्यथ मयार्दिताः।
en: Having heard these words of mine, act towards me in that way which may best secure your well-being. By acting in a different way you will place yourselves in a situation of great fear and danger.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु तान् वीरान् युयुधे कुरुपुङ्गवः॥ अर्जुनोऽतीव संऋद्धः संक्रुद्धैर्विजिगीषुभिः।
en: Having said these words to those heroic warriors, the chief of the Kurus began to fight them. Arjuna was worked up with rage. His enemies, desirous of victory, were equally enraged.

sn: शतं शतसहस्राणि शराणां नतपर्वणाम्॥ मुमुचुः सैन्धवा राजस्तदा गाण्डीवधन्वनि।
en: The Saindhavas then, O king, shot hundreds and thousands of straight arrows at the wielder of Gandiva.

sn: शरानापततः क्रूरानाशीविषविषोपमान्॥ विच्छेद निशितैर्बाणैरन्तरा स धनंजयः।
en: Dhananjaya, with his own whetted arrows, cut off those arrows of sharp and terrible points, resembling stakes of dreadful poison, before could come up to him.

sn: छित्त्वा तु तानाशु चैव कङ्कपत्रशिलाशितान्॥ एकैकमेषां समरे बिभेद निशितैः शरैः।
en: Having off those sharp arrows bedecked with Kanka-feathers, Arjuna pierced each of the warriors opposed to him with a whetted arrow.

sn: ततः प्रासांश्च शक्तीश्च पुनरेव धनंजयम्॥ जयद्रथं हतं स्मृत्वा चिक्षिपुः सैन्धवा नृपाः।
en: The Saindhava Kshatriyas, recollecting that it was Dhananjaya who had killed their king Jayadarth, then hurled at him darts and javelins with great force.

sn: तेषां किरीटी संकल्पं मांघं चक्रे महाबलः॥ सर्वांस्तानन्तराच्छित्त्वा तदा चुक्रोश पाण्डवः।
en: The diadem-decked Dhananjaya of great power baffled their aim by cutting off all those weapons before any of them could reach him. At length the son of Pandu became highly angry.

sn: तथैवापततां तेषां योधानां जयगृद्धिनाम्॥ शिरांसि पातयामास भल्लैः संनतपर्वभिः।
en: With many straight and broad headed arrows, he cut off the heads of many of those warriors who were rushing at him from desire of victory.

sn: तेषां प्रद्रवतां चापि पुनरेवाभिधावताम्॥ निवर्ततां च शब्दोऽभूत् पूर्णस्येव महोदधेः।
en: Many fled, many rushed at Arjuna; many moved not; all of them, however, uttered such a loud noise that it resembled the roar of the Ocean,

sn: ते वध्यमानास्तु तदा पार्थेनामिततेजसा॥ यथाप्राणं यथोत्साहं योधयामासुरर्जुनम्।
en: As they were killed by Partha of immeasurable power, they fought him, each according to his strength and prowess.

sn: ततस्ते फाल्गुनेनाजौ शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ कृता विसंज्ञा भूयिष्ठाः क्लान्तवाहनसैनिकाः।
en: Their animals being all exhausted, Partha succeeded in depriving a large number of those warriors of their senses by means of his sharpest arrows in that battle.

sn: तांस्तु सर्वान् परिग्लानान् विदित्वा धृतराष्ट्रजा।॥ दुःशला बालमादाय नप्तारं प्रययौ तदा।
en: Then Dushala, their queen, the daughter of Dhritarastra, knowing that they were rendered cheerless by Arjuna, took her grandson in her arms and went to Arjuna.

sn: सुरथस्य सुतं वीरं रथेनाथागमत् तदा॥ शान्त्यर्थं सर्वयोधानामभ्यगच्छत पाण्डवम्।
en: The child was the son of Suratha (the son of Jayadratha). The brave prince proceeded to his maternal uncle on his car for the safety or all the Saindhava warriors.

sn: सा धनंजयमासाद्य सरोदार्तस्वरं तदा।॥ धनंजयोऽपि तां दृष्ट्वा धनुर्विससृजे प्रभुः।
en: The queen, arrived before Dhananjaya, began to weep in sorrow. Seeing her, the powerful Dhananjaya cast off his bow.

sn: समुत्सृज्य धनुः पार्थो विधिवद् भगिनीं तदा॥ प्राह किं करवाणीति सा च तं प्रत्युवाच ह। एष ते भरतश्रेष्ठ स्वस्रीयस्यात्मजः शिशुः॥ अभिवादयते पार्थ तं पश्य पुरुषर्षभ।
en: Leaving off his bow, Partha duly received his sister and enquired of her as to what he could do for her. The queen replied to him, saying, O chief of the Bharatas, this child is the son of your sister's son. He salutes you, O Partha. Look at him, O foremost of men.

sn: इत्युक्तस्तस्य पितरं स पप्रच्छार्जुनस्तथा॥ क्वासाविति ततो राजन् दुःशला वाक्यमब्रवीत्। पितृशोकाभिसंतप्तो विषादार्तोऽस्य वै पिता॥ पञ्चत्वमगमद् वीरो यथा तन्मे निशामय।
en: Thus addressed by her, Partha enquired after his son (Suratha), saying, Where is he? Dushala answered him, saying, Burning with grief on account of the destruction of his father, the heroic father of this child disd brokenheated. Listen from me as to how that hero was dead.

sn: स पूर्वं पितरं श्रुत्वा हतं युद्धे त्वयाऽनघ॥ त्वामागतं च संश्रुत्य युद्धाय हयसारिणम्। पितुश्च मृत्युदुःखार्तोऽजहात् प्राणान् धनंजय॥ प्राप्तो वीभत्सुरित्येव नाम श्रुत्वैव तेऽनघ। विषादातः पपातो। ममार च ममात्मजः॥ तं दृष्ट्वा पतितं तत्र ततस्तस्यात्मजं प्रभो। गृहीत्वा समनुप्राप्ता त्वामद्य शरणैषिणी॥ इत्युक्त्वाऽऽर्तस्वरं सा तु मुमोच धृतराष्ट्रजा।
en: O Dhananjaya, he had heard before that his father Jayadratha had been killed by you, o sinless one. Exceedingly afflicted with grief at this, and hearing of your arrival here as the follower and protector of this sacrificial horse, he at once fell down and gave up his life. Indeed, deeply afflicted with grief, as he was, as soon as he heard of your arrival, he gave up his life seeing him prostrate on the Earth, O lord, o took his intent son with me and have come to you, seeking your protection. Having said these words, the daughter of Dhritarashtra began to lament in deep sorrow.

sn: दीना दीनं स्थितं पार्थमब्रवीच्चाप्यधोमुखम्॥ स्वसारं समवेक्षस्व स्वस्त्रीयात्मजमेव च।
en: Arjuna stood before her great cheerlessness of heart. His face was turned towards the Earth. The cheerless sister then said to her brother, who was equally cheerless, these words : See your sister. See the child of your sister's son.

sn: कर्तुमर्हसि धर्मज्ञ दयां कुरुकुलोद्वह॥ विस्मृत्य कुरुराजानं तं च मन्दं जयद्रथम्।
en: O perpetuator of Kuru's race, O you who are fully conversant with every duty, you should show mercy to this child, forgetting the Kuru prince (Duryodhana) and the wicked Jayadratha. in

sn: अभिमन्योर्यथा जातः परिक्षित् परवीरहा॥ तथायं सुरथाज्जातो मम पौत्रो महाभुजः।
en: As that destroyer of hostile heroes, Parikshit, has been born of Abhimanyu, so has this mighty-armed child, my grandson, originated from Suratha.

sn: तमादाय नरव्याघ्र सम्प्राप्तास्मि तवान्तिकम्॥ शमार्थं सर्वयोधानां शृणु चेदं वचो मम।
en: Taking him with me, O king, I have come to you desirous of the safety of all the warriors! Do you listen to these words of mine.

sn: आगतोऽयं महाबाहो तस्य मन्दस्य पुत्रक॥ प्रसादमस्य बालस्य तस्मात् त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि।
en: This child of that wicked enemy of yours has now come to you, O mighty armed hero. You should, therefore, show mercy to this infant.

sn: एष प्रसाद्य शिरसा प्रशमार्थमरिंदम॥ याचते त्वां महाबाहो शमं गच्छ धनंजय।
en: O chastiser of enemies this intent seeks to please you by bending his head. He solicits you for peace! O mighty armed hero, be inclined to make peace.

sn: बालस्य हतबन्धोश्च पार्थ किंचिदजानतः॥ प्रसादं कुरु धर्मज्ञ मा मन्युवशमन्वगाः।
en: O you who know every duty, be pleased with the child whose friends and kinsmen have all been killed and who himself knows nothing of what has taken place. Do not yield to anger.

sn: तमनार्यं नृशंसं च विस्मृत्यास्य पितामहम्॥ आगस्कारिणमत्यर्थं प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि
en: Forgetting his disreputable and cruel grandfather, who offended against you so highly, it is but fit that you should extend your grace towards this child.

sn: एवं ब्रुवत्यां करुणं दुःशलायां धनंजयः॥ संस्मृत्य देवीं गान्धारीं धृतराष्ट्रं च पार्थिवम्।
en: Recollecting queen Gandhari and king Dhritarashtra, Dhananjaya, afflicted with grief, addressed Dushala who had said so to him, and answered her, censuring Kshatriya practices all the time.

sn: उवाच दुःखशोकातः क्षत्रधर्मं व्यगर्हयत्॥ यत्कृते वान्धवाः सर्वे मया नीता यमक्षयम्।
en: Fie on Duryodhana, that mean person covetous of kingdom and full of vanity! Alas, it was for him that all my kinsmen have been sent by me to the abode of Yama.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा बहु सान्त्वादिप्रसादमकराज्जयः॥ परिष्वज्य च तां प्रीतो विससर्ज गृहानं प्रति॥
en: Having said so, Dhananjaya comforted his sister and became inclined to make peace. Cheerfully, he embraced her and then dismissed her, asking her to return to her palace.

sn: दुःशला चापि तान् योधान् निवार्य महतो रणात्। सम्पूज्य पार्थं प्रययौ गृहानेव शुभानना॥
en: Dushala asked all her warriors to desert from that great battle, and adoring Partha, she of beautiful face returned towards her palace.

sn: एवं निर्जित्य तान् वीरान् सैन्धवान् स धनंजयः। अन्वधावत धावन्तं हयं कामविचारिणम्॥
en: Having defeated those heroes, viz., the Saindhavas, thus, Dhananjaya began to follow that horse which ranged at its will.

sn: ततो मृगमिवाकाशे यथा देवः पिनाकधृक्। ससार तं तथा वीरो विधिवद् यज्ञियं हयम्॥
en: The heroic Arjuna duly followed that sacrificial horse even as the divine holder of Pinaka had in days of yore followed the deer through the sky.

sn: स च वाजी यथेष्टेन तांस्तान् देशान् यथाक्रमम्। विचचार यथाकामं कर्म पार्थस्य वर्धयन्॥
en: The horse, at its will, passed through various kingdoms successively, multiplying the feats of Arjuna.

sn: क्रमेण स हयस्त्वेवं विचरन् पुरुषर्षभ। मणिपूरतेर्देशमुमायात् सहपाण्डवः॥
en: In course of time, O king, the horse wandering at its pleasure, at last arrived within the kingdom of Manipura, followed by the son of Pandu.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा तु नृपतिः प्राप्तं पितरं बभ्रुवाहनः। निर्ययौ विनयेनाथ ब्राह्मणार्थपुरःसरः॥
en: Hearing that his father Arjuna had arrived within his kingdom, the king of Manipura, Babhruvahana went out with humility, with a number of Brahmanas and some treasure in his van.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: मणिपूरेश्वरं त्वेवमुपयातं धनंजयः। नाभ्यनन्दत् स मेधावी क्षत्रधर्ममनुस्मरन्॥
en: Remembering, however, the duties of Kshatriyas, the highly intelligent Dhananjaya, seeing the king of Manipura arrive in that guise, did not approve of it.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: उवाच च स धर्मात्मा समन्युः फाल्गुनस्तदा। प्रक्रियेयं न ते युक्ता बहिस्त्वं क्षत्रधर्मतः॥
en: The righteous-souled Phalguna angrily said, Your conduct is not proper. You have certainly fallen away from Kshatriya duties.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: संरक्ष्यमाणं तुरगं यौधिष्ठिरमुपागतम्। यज्ञियं विषयान्ते मां नायौत्सी: किं नु पुत्रक॥
en: I have come here as the protector of Yudhishthira's sacrificial horse. Why, O son, will you not fight me, seeing that I have come within your territories?

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: धिक् त्वामस्तु सुदुर्बुद्धिं क्षत्रधर्मबहिष्कृतम्। यो मा युद्धाय सम्प्राप्तं साम्नैव प्रत्यगृह्णथाः॥
en: Fie on you, O you of foolish understanding, Fie on you who have deviated from Kshatriya duties! Fie on you who would receive me peacefully even though I have come here for fighting with you.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: न त्वया पुरुषार्थो हि कश्चिदस्तीह जीवता। यस्त्वं स्त्रीवद् यथाप्राप्तं मां साम्ना प्रत्यगृह्णथाः॥ यद्यहं न्यस्तशस्त्रस्त्वामागच्छेयं सुदुर्मते। प्रक्रियेयं भवेद् युक्ता तावत् तव नराधम॥ तमेवमुक्तं भ; तु विदित्वा पन्नगात्मजा। अमृष्यमाणा भित्त्वोर्वीमुलूपी समुपागमत्॥
en: In thus receiving me peacefully you act like a woman. O you of wretched understanding, if I had come to you, leaving aside my arms, then would this conduct of yours have been fit, O worst of men!" Learning that these words were addressed by her husband, the daughter of the Snake King, viz., Ulupi, unable to tolerate it, pierced through the Earth and came up there.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: सा ददर्श ततः पुत्रं विमृशन्तमधोमुखम्। संतय॑मानमसकृत् पित्रा युद्धार्थिना प्रभो॥ ततः सा चारुसर्वाङ्गी समुपेत्योरगात्मजा। उलूपी प्राह वचनं धन॑ धर्मविशारदम्॥
en: She saw her son standing there perfectly cheerless and with face hanging down. Indeed, the prince was repeatedly rebuked by his father who was desirous of battle with him, O monarch! The daughter of the Snake, possessed of beautiful limbs, viz., Ulupi, said these words consistent with righteousness and duty to the prince who himself was conversant with righteousness and duty.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: उलूपी मां निबोध त्वं मातरं पन्नगात्मजाम्। कुरुष्व वचनं पुत्र धर्मस्ते भविता परः॥ युध्वस्वैनं कुरुश्रेष्ठं पितरं युद्धदुर्मदम्। एवमेष हि ते प्रीतो भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: Know that I am your mother Ulupi that am the daughter of a snake. Do you perform my order, O son for you would then acquire great merit. Fight your father, this foremost one of Kuru's race, this hero who is irresistible in battle. Forsooth, he will then be pleased with you.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: एवं दुर्मर्षितो राजा स मात्रा बभ्रुवाहनः । मनश्चक्रे महातेजा युद्धाय भरतर्षभ।॥ संना काञ्चनं वर्म शिरस्त्राणं च भानुमत्। तूणीरशतसम्बाधमारुरोह रथोत्तमम्॥ सर्वोपकरणोपेतं युक्तमश्वैर्मनोजवैः। स चक्रोपस्करं श्रीमान् हेमभाण्डपरिष्कृतम्॥
en: Thus was king Babhruvahana incited against his father by his (step) mother. At last, gifted as he was with great energy, he made up his mind, O chief of the Bharatas, to fight Dhananjaya, Putting on his armour of bright gold and his shining head-dress, he got upon an excellent car which had hundreds of quivers ready on it. That car was equipped with necessaries for battle and had horses yoked to it which were fleet like the mind. It had excellent wheels and a strong Upashkara, and was adorned with golden ornaments of every sort.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: परमार्चितमुच्छ्रित्य ध्वजं सिंहं हिरण्मयम्। प्रययौ पार्थमुद्दिश्य स राजा बभ्रुवाहनः॥
en: Raising his standard which was decorated most beautifully and which bore the device of a lion in gold, the beautiful prince Babhruvahana proceeded against this father for battle.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: ततोऽभ्येत्य हयं वीरो यज्ञियं पार्थरक्षितम्। ग्राहयामास पुरुषैर्हयशिक्षाविशारदैः॥
en: Coming upon the sacrificial horse which was protected by Partha, the heroic prince caused it to be seized by persons well-versed in veterinary science.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: गृहीतं वाजिनं दृष्ट्वा प्रीतात्मा स धनंजयः। पुत्रं रथस्थं भूमिष्ठः संन्यवारयदाहवे॥
en: Seeing the horse seized, Dhananjaya become filled with joy. Standing on the earth, that hero began to oppose the advance of his son who was on his car.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: स तत्र राजा तं वीरं शरसंधैरनेकशः। अर्दयामास निशितैराशीविषविषोपमैः॥
en: The king afflicted the hero with repeated showers of arrows gifted with whetted points and resembling snakes of dreadful poison.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं पितुः पुत्रस्य चातुलम्। देवासुररणप्रख्यमुभयोः प्रीयमाणयोः॥
en: Incomparable was the battle which took place between the father and son. It resembled the battle between the celestials and the Asuras of old. Each was pleased with obtaining the other for an antagonist. arrow a

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: किरीटिनं प्रविव्याध शरेणानतपर्वणा। जत्रुदेशे नरव्याघ्र प्रहसन् बभ्रुवाहनः॥
en: Then Babhruvahana, laughing, cut the diadem-decked Arjuna, that foremost of men, in the shoulder with a straight arrow.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: सोऽभ्यगात् सह पुड्वेन वल्मीकमिव पन्नगः। विनिर्मिद्य च कौन्तेयं प्रविवेश महीतलम्॥
en: Equipped with feathers, that penetrated Arjuna's body like snake penetrating on an anthill. Piercing the son of Kunti through, the arrow went deep into the Earth.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: स गाढवेदनो धीमानालम्ब्य धनुरुत्तमम्। दिव्यं तेजः समाविश्य प्रमीत इव साऽभवत्॥
en: Feeling acute pain, the intelligent Dhananjaya rested awhile, supporting himself on his excellent bow. He stood, having recourse to his celestial energy and seemed externally like one dead.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: स संज्ञामुपलभ्याथ प्रशस्य पुरुषर्षभः। पुत्रं शक्रात्मजो वाक्यमिदमाह महाद्युतिः॥ साधु साधु महाबाहो वत्स चित्राङ्गदात्मजा सदृशं कर्म ते दृष्ट्वा प्रीतिमानस्मि पुत्रक॥
en: That foremost of men, then regaining consciousness, lauded his highly. Possessed of great splendour, the son of Shakra said, Excellent, Excellent, O mighty-armed one, O son of Chitrangada! O son, seeing this feat, so worthy of you, I am highly pleased son with you.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: विमुञ्चाम्येष ते बाणान् पुत्र युद्धे स्थिरो भव। इत्येवमुक्त्वा नाराचैरभ्यवर्षदमित्रहा॥
en: I shall now discharge these arrows at you, O son! Stand for fight (without running away). Having said these words, that destroyer of enemies shot a shower of arrows on the prince.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: तान् स गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तान् वज्राशनिसमप्रभान्। नाराचानच्छिनद् राजा भल्लैःसर्वास्त्रिधा द्विधा॥
en: King Babhruvahana, however, with his own broad-headed arrows, cut all those arrows, which were discharged from Gandiva and which resembled the thunderbolt of Indra in splendour, some in two, and some into three, parts.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: तस्य पार्थः शरैर्दिव्यैर्ध्वजं हेमपरिष्कृतम्। सुवर्णतालप्रतिमं क्षुरेणापाहरद् रथात्॥
en: Then the standard, decked with gold and resembling a golden Palmyra, on the king's car was cut off by Partha with some excellent arrows of his.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: हयांश्चास्य महाकायान् महावेगानरिंदम। चकार राजन् निर्जीवान् प्रहसन्निव पाण्डवः॥
en: The son of Pandu, laughing, next killed the king's horses of large size and great speed.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: स रथादवतीर्याथ राजा परमकोपनः। पदातिः पितरं क्रुद्धो योधयामास पाण्डवम्॥
en: Descending from his car, the king, worked up with rage, fought his father on foot.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: सम्प्रीयमाणः पार्थानामृषभः पुत्रविक्रमात्। नात्यर्थं पीडयामास पुत्रं वज्रधरात्मजः॥
en: Pleased with the prowess of his son, that foremost one of the sons of Pritha, viz., the son of the wielder of the thunderbolt, began to afflict him greatly.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: स मन्यमानो विमुखं पितरं बभ्रुवाहनः। शरैराशीविषाकारैः पुनरेवार्दयद् बली॥
en: The powerful Babhruvahana, thinking that his father was no longer able to face him, again afflicted him with many arrows resembling snakes of dreadful poison.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: ततः स बाल्यात् पितरं विव्याध हृदि पत्रिणा। निशितेन सुपुढेन बलवद् बभ्रुवाहनः॥
en: From a spirit of childishness he then vigorously cut his father in the breast with a whetted arrow having excellent wings.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: विवेश पाण्डवं राजन् मर्म भित्त्वातिदुःखकृत्। स तेनातिभृशं विद्धः पुत्रेण कुरुनन्दनः॥ महीं जगाम मोहार्तस्ततो राजन् धनंजयः। तस्मिन् निपतिते वीरे कौरवाणां धुरंधरे॥ सोऽपि मोहं जगामाथ ततश्चित्राङ्गदासुतः। व्यायम्य संयुगे राजा दृष्ट्वा च पितरं हतम्॥
en: That arrow, O king, penetrated the body of Pandu's son and reaching his very vitals caused him great pain. The delighter of the Kurus, Dhananjaya, deeply pierced therewith by his son, then dropped down in a swoon on the Earth, O king! When that hero, that bearer of the burthens of the Kurus, fell down, the son of Chitrangada also became unconscious. The latter's swoon was owing to his exertions in battle as also to his grief at seeing his father killed.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: पूर्वमेव स बाणौधैर्गाढविद्धोऽर्जुनेन ह। पपात सोऽपि धरणीमालिङ्ग्य रणमूर्धनि॥
en: He had been pierced deeply by Arjuna with clouds of arrows. He, therefore dropped down at the van of battle embracing the Earth.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: भर्तारं निहतं दृष्ट्वा पुत्रं च पतितं भुवि। चित्राड्दा परित्रस्ता प्रविवेश रणाजिरे॥
en: Hearing that her husband had been killed and that her son had fallen down on the Earth, Chitrangada, in great agitation of mind, went to the field of battle.

description: The arrival of Arjuna at Manipur, Hearing of the death of her husband and son, Chitrangada goes to the field
sn: शोकसंतप्तहृदया रुदती वेपती भृशम्। मणिपूरपतेर्माता ददर्श निहतं पतिम्॥
en: Her heart burning with sorrow, weeping piteously the while, and trembling all over, the mother of the king of Manipura saw her killed husband.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पान उवाच ततो बहुतरं भीरुर्विलप्य कमलेक्षणा। मुमोह दुःखसंतप्ता पपात च महीतले॥
en: Vaishampayana said That lady having eyes like lotus petals, having bewailed much, and burning with grief, at last lost her senses and dropped down on the Earth.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: प्रतिलभ्य च सा संज्ञां देवी दिव्यवपुर्धरा। उलूपी पन्नगसुतां दृष्ट्वेदं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ उलूपि पश्य भर्तारं शयानं निहतं रणे। त्वत्कृते मम पुत्रेण बाणेन समितिञ्जयम्॥
en: Regaining consciousness and seeing Ulupi, the daughter of the Snake-Chief, queen Chitrangada gifted with celestial beauty, said to her these words :-See, O Ulupi, our ever victorious husband killed in battle, through you, by my son of tender years.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: ननु त्वमार्यधर्मज्ञा ननु चासि पतिव्रता। यत्त्वत्कृतेऽयं पतितः पतिस्ते निहतो रणे॥
en: Do you know the practices of the respectable? Are you a wife devoted to you husband? It is through your deed, that your husband is land low, slain in battle.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: किंतु सर्वापराधोऽयं यदि तेऽद्य धनंजयः। क्षमस्व याच्यमाना वै जीवयस्व धनंजयम्॥
en: If Dhananjaya has offended against you in every respect, do you forgive him! I solicit you, do you revive that hero.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: ननु त्वमार्ये धर्मज्ञा त्रैलोक्यविदिता शुभे। यद् घातयित्वा पुत्रेण भर्तारं नानुशोचसि॥
en: O righteous lady, you know piety. You are, O blessed one, known (for your virtues) over the three worlds! How is it that having caused your husband to be killed by your son, you do not indulge in grief?

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: नाहं शोचामि तनयं हतं पन्नगनन्दिनि। पतिमेव तु शोचामि यस्यानिध्यमिदं कृतम्॥
en: O daughter of the Snake-Chief, I do not grieve for my killed son! I grieve for only my husband who has received this hospitality form his son.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्त्वा सा तदा देवीमुलूपी पन्नगात्मजाम्। भर्तारमभिगम्येदमित्युवाच यशस्विनी॥ उत्तिष्ठ कुरुमुख्यस्य प्रियमुख्य मम प्रिय। अयमश्वो महाबाहो मया ते परिमोक्षितः॥
en: Having said these words to the queenly Ulupi the daughter of the Snake-King, the illustrious Chitrangada went to where her husband lay on the Earth and addressing him, said, Rise, O dear husband, you occupy the King (Yudhishthira)! Here is that horse of yours! It has been liberated by me.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: ननु त्वया नाम विभो धर्मराजस्य यज्ञियः। अयमश्वोऽनुसर्तव्यः स शेष किं महीतले॥
en: Indeed, O powerful one, this sacrificial horse of king Yudhishthira the just, should be followed by you. Why then do you lie still on the Earth.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: त्वयि प्राणा ममायत्ता: कुरुणां कुरुनन्दन। स कस्मात् प्राणदोऽन्येषां प्राणान् संत्यक्तवानसि॥
en: My life-breaths depend on you, O delighter of the Kurus. How is it that he who is the ver of other people's life-breaths, renounces his own life-breaths today?

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: उलूपि साधु पश्येमं पतिं निपतितं भुवि। पुत्रं चेमं समुत्पाद्य घातयित्वा न शोचसि॥
en: See, O Ulupi, this beautiful form of your husband lying prostrate on the ground. How is it that you do not grieve, having cause him to be killed through your son whom you did excite with your words?

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: कामं स्वपितु बालोऽयं भूमौ मृत्युवशं गतः। लोहिताक्षो गुडाकेशो विजयः साधु जीवतु॥
en: It is fit that this boy should yield to the power of death and lie thus on the ground besides his own father. Oh, let Vijaya, let him that is called Gudakesha, let this hero with reddish eyes return to life.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: नापराधोऽस्ति सुभगे नराणां बहुभार्यता। प्रमदानां भवत्येष मा तेऽभूद् बुद्धिरीदृशी॥
en: O blessed lady, polygamy is no fault with men. Women only commit sin by taking more than one husband. Do not, therefore, cherish such thoughts (of vengeance).

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: सख्यं चैतत् कृतं धात्रा शश्वदव्ययमेव तु। सख्यं समभिजानीहि सत्यं सङ्गतमस्तु ते॥
en: This relationship was ordained by the Supreme Creator himself. It is besides, an eternal and unchangeable one. Do you attend to that relationship. Let your union (with Dhananjaya) be made true.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: पुत्रेण घातयित्वैनं पतिं यदि न मेऽद्य वै। जीवन्तं दर्शयस्यद्य परित्यक्ष्यामि जीवितम्॥
en: If, having killed your husband through your son, you do not revive him today before my eyes, I shall then renounce my own lifebreaths.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: साहं दुःखान्विता देवि पतिपुत्रविनाकृता। इहैव प्रायमाशिष्ये प्रेक्षन्त्यास्ते न संशयः॥
en: Forsooth, O reverend lady, afflicted as I am with grief and deprived as I am of both husband and son, I shall sit here today in Praya-vow before your presence.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्त्वा पन्नगसुतां सपत्नी चैत्रवाहनी। ततः प्रायमुपासीना तूष्णीमासीज्जनाधिप॥
en: Having said so to the daughter of the Snake-Chief, who was a co-wife with her to Arjuna, the princess Chatravahini sat in Praya, O king, restraining speech.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो विलप्य विरता भर्तुः पादौ प्रगृह्य सा। उपविष्टाभवद् दीना सोच्छ्वासं पुत्रमीक्षती॥
en: Vaishampayana said Ceasing to lament, the cheerless queen, taking upon her lap the feet of her husband, sat there, sighing heavily and desiring also for the restoration of her son to life.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: ततः संज्ञा पुनर्लध्वा स राजा बभ्रुवाहनः। मातरं तामथालोक्य रणभूमावथाब्रवीत्॥ इतो दुःखतरं किं नु यन्मे माता सुखैधिता। भूमौ निपतितं वीरमनुशेते मृतं पतिम्॥
en: King Babhruvahana then, regaining consciousness, saw his mother seated in that guise on the field of battle. Addressing her he said, What can be more painful than the sight of my mother, who has been brought up in luxury, lying on the naked Earth beside her heroic husband stretched thereon.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: निहन्तारं रणेऽरीणां सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्। मया विनिहतं संख्ये प्रेक्षते दुर्मरं बत॥
en: Alas, this destroyer of all enemies, this foremost of all wielders of weapons, has been killed by me in battle. It is clear that men do die, till their hour comes.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: अहोऽस्या हृदयं देव्या दृढं यन्न विदीर्यते। व्यूढोरस्कं महावाहुं प्रेक्षन्त्या निहतं पतिम्॥
en: Oh, the heart of this princess seems to be very hard since it does not break even on seeing her mighty-armed and broad-chested husband lying dead on the ground.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: दुर्मरं पुरुषेणेह मन्ये ह्यध्वन्यनागते। यत्र नाहं न मे माता विप्रयुज्येत जीवितात्॥
en: It is clear that one does not die till one's hour comes, since neither myself, nor my mother is deprived of life.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: हा हा धिक् कुरुवीरस्य संनाहं काञ्चनं भुवि। आविद्धं हतस्येह मया पुत्रेण पश्यत॥
en: Alas, alas, the golden coat of mail of this foremost hero of Kuru's race, killed by me, his son, knowingly, is lying on the ground, cut off from his body.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: भो भो पश्यत मे वीरं पितरं ब्राह्मणा भुवि। शयानं वीरशयने मया पुत्रेण पातितम्॥
en: Alas, you Brahmanas, see my heroic father lying prostrate on the Earth, on a hero's bed, killed by his son.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: ब्राह्मणा: कुरुमुख्यस्य ये मुक्ता हयसारिणः। कुर्वन्ति शान्ति कामस्य रणे योऽयं मया हतः॥
en: What benefit is done to this hero, killed by me in battle, by those Brahmanas who were commissioned to attend upon this foremost one of Kuru's race engaged in following the horse?

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: व्यादिशन्तु च किं विप्राः प्रायश्चित्तमिहाद्य मे। सुनृशंसस्य पापस्य पितृहन्तू रणाजिरे॥
en: Let the Brahmanas direct what expiation should now be done by me, a cruel and sinful wretch, who has killed his own father in battle.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: दुश्चरा द्वादशसमा हत्वा पितरमद्य वै। ममेह सुनृशंसस्य संवीतस्यास्य चर्मणा॥
en: Having killed my own father, I should, suffering every sort of misery, wonder over the Earth, cruel that I am, covering myself with his skin.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: शिर:कपाले चास्यैव युञ्जतः पितुरद्य मे। प्रायश्चितं हि नास्त्यन्यद्वन्वाऽद्य पितरं मम॥
en: Give me the two halves of my sire's head today, for there is no other expiation for me who have killed my own father.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: पश्य नागोत्तमसुते भर्तारं निहतं मया। कृतं प्रियं मया नेऽद्य निहत्य समरेऽर्जुनम्॥
en: See, O daughter of the foremost of Snakes, your husband killed by me. Indeed, by killing Arjuna in battle I have accomplished what is pleasant to you.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: सोऽहमद्य गमिष्यामि गतिं पितृनिषेविताम्। न शक्नोप्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानमहं धारयितुं शुभे॥
en: I shall today follow in the track by which my father has gone. O blessed one, I cannot comfort myself.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: सा त्वं मयि मृते मातस्तथा गाण्डीवधन्वनि। भव प्रीतिमती देवि सत्येनात्मानमालभे॥
en: Be happy today, O mother, seeing myself and the wielder of Gandiva both, embrace death today. I swear to you by truth itself.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्त्वा स ततो राजा दुःखशोकसमाहतः। उपस्पृश्य महाराज दुःखाद् वचनमब्रवीत्॥ शृण्वन्तु सर्वभूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च। त्वं च मातर्यथ सत्यं ब्रवीमि भुजगोत्तमे॥
en: Having said these words, the king, sorely afflicted with grief, O monarch, touched water, and exclaimed in sorrow, Let all creatures, mobile and immobile, listen to me! Do you also listen to me, O mother! I say the truth, O best of all daughters of the snakes.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: यदि नोत्तिष्ठति जयः पिता मे नरसत्तमः। अस्मिन्नेव रणोद्देशे शोषयिष्ये कलेवरम्॥
en: If this best of men, Jaya, my father does not rise up, I shall emaciate my own body, sitting on the field of battle.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: न हि मे पितरं हत्वा निष्कृतिर्विद्यते क्वचित्। नरकं प्रतिपत्स्यामि ध्रुवं गुरुवधार्दितः॥
en: Having killed my father, there is not rescue for me. Afflicted as I am with the sin of patricide, I shall, forsooth, have to sink in Hell.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: वीरं हि क्षत्रियं हत्वा गोशतेन प्रमुच्यते। पितरं तु निहत्यैवं दुर्लभा निष्कृतिर्मम॥
en: By killing a heroic Kshatriya one becomes cleansed by a gift of a hundred kine. By killing my father, however, so dreadful has been my sin that my rescue is impossible.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: एष एको महातेजाः पाण्डुपुत्रो धनंजयः। पिता च ममधर्मात्मा तस्य मे निष्कृतिः कुतः॥
en: This Dhanajaya, the son of Pandu, was the one hero gifted with mighty energy. Possessed of righteous soul, he was the creator of my being. How can I be rescued after having killed him?

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: इन्येवमुक्त्वा नृपते धनंजयसुतो नृपः। उपस्पृश्याभवत् तूष्र्णी प्रायोपेतो महामतिः॥
en: Having bewailed thus, the great son of Dhananjaya, king Babhruvahana, touched water and became silent, vowing to starve himself to death.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रायोपविष्टे नृपतौ मणिपूरेश्वरे तदा। पितृशोकसमाविष्टे सह मात्रा परंतप॥ उलूपी चिन्तयामास तदा संजीवनं मणिम्। स चोपातिष्ठत तदा पन्नगानां परायणम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said When the king of Manipura, that chastiser of enemies, afflicted with grief, along with his mother, sat down to starve himself to death, Ulupi then thought of the gem that has the virtue of reviving a dead man. The gem, the great refuge of the Snakes, thus thought of, arrived there.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: तं गृहीत्वा तु कौरव्य नागराजपतेः सुता। मन:प्रह्लादनीं वाचं सैनिकानामथाब्रवीत्॥
en: The daughter of the Prince of Snakes, taking it up, uttered these words which highly gladdened the combatants standing on the field.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: उत्तिष्ठ मा शुचः पुत्र नैव जिष्णुस्त्वया जितः। अजेयः पुरुषैरेष तथा देवैः सवासवैः॥
en: Rise up, O son! Do not grieve! Jishnu has not been vanquished by you! This hero is incapable of being defeated by men as also by the celestials headed by Vasva himself.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: मया तु मोहनी नाम मायैषा सम्प्रदर्शिता। प्रियार्थं पुरुषेन्द्रस्य पितुस्तेऽद्य यशस्विनः॥
en: I have exhibited this illusion, deceiving your senses, for the benefit of this foremost of men, viz., your illustrious father.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: जिज्ञासुह्येष पुत्रस्य बलस्य तव कौरवः। संग्रामे युद्ध्यतो राजन्नागतः परवीरहा।॥
en: O you of Kuru's race, desirous of ascertaining the prowess of yourself, his son, this destroyer of hostile heroes, O king, came here for fighting with you.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: तस्मादसि मया पुत्र युद्धाय परिचोदितः। मा पापमात्मनः पुत्र शङ्केथा ह्यण्वपि प्रभो॥
en: It was, therefore, O son, that you were urged by me to fight. O powerful king, O son, do not suspect that you have committed any, even the least, fault, by his challenge.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: ऋषिरेष महानात्मा पुराणः शाश्वतोऽक्षरः। नैनं शक्तो हि संग्रामे जेतुं शक्तोऽपि पुत्रक॥
en: He is a Rishi, of powerful soul, eternal and indestructible. O dear son, Shakra himself is incapable of defeating him in battle.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: अयं तु मे मणिर्दिव्यः समानीतो विशाम्पते। मतान् मृतान् पन्नगेन्द्रान् यो जीवयति नित्यदा॥
en: This celestial gem has been brought by me, O king. It always revives the snakes as often as they die.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: एनमस्योरसि त्वं च स्थापयस्व पितुः प्रभो। संजीवितं तदा पार्थं सत्वं द्रष्टासि पाण्डवम्॥
en: O powerful king, do you place this gem on the breast of your father. You shall then see the son of Pandu revive.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्तः स्थापयामास तस्योरसि मणिं तदा। पार्थस्यामिततेजाः स पितुः स्नेहादपापकृत्॥
en: Thus addressed, the prince who had committed no sin, moved by love for his father, then placed that gem on the breast of Pritha's son of incomparable energy.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: तस्मिन् न्यस्ते मणौ वीरो जिष्णुरुज्जीवितः प्रभुः। चिरसुप्त इवोत्तस्थौ मृष्टलोहितलोचनः॥
en: After the gem had been placed on his breast, the heroic and powerful Jishnu become revived. Opening his red eyes, he rose up like one who had slept long.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: तमुत्थितं महात्मानं लब्धसंज्ञं मनस्विनम्। समीक्ष्य पितरं स्वस्थं ववन्दे बभ्रुवाहनः॥
en: Seeing his father, the great hero of in exhaustible energy, restored to consciousness and quite at his case, Babhruvahana adored him with respect.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: उस्थिते पुरुषव्याघ्र पुनर्लक्ष्मीवति प्रभो। दिव्याः सुमनसः पुण्या ववृषे पाकशासनः॥
en: When that foremost of men, O powerful one, awake from the slumber of death with every auspicious sign of life the chastiser of Paka rained down celestial flowers.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: अनाहता दुन्दुभयो विनेदुर्मेघनिःस्वनाः। साधु साध्विति चाकाशे बभूव सुमहान् स्वनः॥
en: Kettle-drums struck by nobody, produced their music deep as the muttering of the clouds. A loud uproar was heard in the sky consisting of the words-Excellent, Excellent.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: उत्थाय च महाबाहुः पर्याश्वस्तो धनंजयः। बभ्रुवाहनमालिङ्ग्य समाजिघ्रत मूर्धनि॥
en: The mighty-armed Dhananjaya, rising up and well-comforted, embraced Babhruvahana and smelled his head.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: ददर्श चापि दूरेऽस्य मातरं शोककर्शिताम्। उलूप्या सहतिष्ठन्तीं ततोऽपृच्छद् धनंजयः॥ किमिदं लक्ष्यते सर्वे शाकविस्मयहर्षवत्। रणाजिरममित्रघ्न यदि जानासि शंस मे॥
en: He saw sitting at a distance from his son, this latter's mother stricken with grief, in the company of Ulupi. Dhanajaya asked, Why is it that every thing in the field of battle seems to bear the marks of grief, wonder and joy? If O destroyer of enemies, you know the cause, do you then tell me.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: जननी च किमर्थं ते रणभूमिमुपागता। नागेन्द्रदुहिता चेयमुलूपी किमिहागता॥
en: Why has your mother come to the field of battle? Why, also has Ulupi the daughter of the Prince of Snakes, come here?

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: जानाम्यहमिदं युद्धं त्वया मद्वचनात् कृतम्। स्त्रीणामागमने हेतुमहमिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: I know that you had fought this battle with me at my own command. I wish to know what the cause is which has brought out the ladies.

description: Ulipi, the daughter of Naga king also, goes there, She revives Arjuna
sn: तमुवाच तथा पृष्टो मणिपूरपतिस्तदा। प्रसाद्यशिरसा विद्वानुलूपी पृच्छ्यतामियम्॥
en: Thus questioned by Dhananjaya the intelligent king of Manipura gratified him by bending his head in respect, and then said, Let Ulupi be asked.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: अर्जुन उवाच किमागमनकृत्यं ते कौरव्यकुलनन्दिनि। मणिपूरपतेर्मातस्तथैव च रणाजिरे।।।।
en: What brings you here, O daughter (in-law) of Kuru's race, and what, also, is the cause of the arrival on the field of battle of her who is the mother of the king of Manipura?

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: कच्चित् कुशलकामासि राज्ञोऽस्य भुजगात्मजे। मम वा चपलापाङ्गि कच्चित् त्वं शुभमिच्छसि॥
en: Do you entertain friendly motives towards this king, O daughter of a snake? O you of restless glances, do you wish good to me too?

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: कच्चित् ते पृथुलश्रोणि नाप्रियं प्रियदर्शने। अकार्षमहमज्ञानादयं वा बभ्रुवाहनः॥
en: I hope, O you of ample hips, that neither I, nor this Babruvahana here, have, O beautiful lady, donc any injury to you unconsciously?

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: कच्चिन्नु राजपुत्री ते सपत्नी चैत्रवाहनी। चित्राङ्गदा वरारोहा नापराध्यति किंचन॥
en: Has Chitrangada of faultless limbs, descended from the line of Chitravahana, done you any wrong?

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: तमुवाचोरगपतेर्दुहिता प्रहसन्निवा न मे त्वमपराद्धोऽसि न हि मे बभ्रुवाहनः॥
en: To him, the daughter of the Prince of Snakes answered sinilingly, You have not offended me, nor has Babhruvahana done me any wrong.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: न जनित्री तथास्येयं मम या प्रेष्यवत् स्थिता। श्रूयतां यद् यथा चेदं मया सर्वं विचेष्टितम्॥
en: Nor this prince's mother who is always obedient to me as a hand-maid. Listen, how all this has been caused by me.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: न मे कोपस्त्वया कार्य: शिरसा त्वां प्रसादये। त्वत्प्रियार्थं हि कौरव्य कृतमेतन्मया विभो॥
en: You should not be angry with me. Indeed, I seek to please you by bending my head in respect. O you of Kuru's race, all this has been done by me for your good, O powerful one!

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: यत्तच्छृणु महाबाहो निखिलेन धनंजय। महाभारतयुद्धे यत् त्वया शान्तनवो नृपः॥ अधर्मेण हतः पार्थ तस्यैषा निष्कृतिः कृता। न हि भीष्मस्त्वया वीर युद्ध्यमानो हि पातितः॥
en: O mighty-armed Dhananjaya, Hear all that I have done. In the great battle of the BharataPrinces, you had killed the royal son of Shantanu by unfair ways. What I have done has expiated your sin. You did not overthrow Bhishma while fighting with you!

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: शिखण्डिना तु संयुक्तस्तमाश्रित्य हतस्त्वया। तस्य शान्तिमकृत्वा त्वं त्यजेथा यदि जीवितम्॥ कर्मणा तेन पापेन पतेथा निरये ध्रुवम्। एषा तु विहिता शान्तिः पुत्राद् यां प्राप्तवानसि।
en: He was engaged with Shikandin. Relying on him as your help, you did bring about the overthrow of Shantanu's son. Of you had died without having expiated your sin, you would then have fallen, forsooth, into Hell on account of that sinful deed of yours. Even this which you have got from your son is the expiation of that sin!

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: वसुभिर्वसुधापाल गङ्गया च महामते॥ पुरा हि श्रुतमेतत् ते वसुभिः कथितं मया।
en: Formerly, o king, I heard this said by the Vasus while they were in the company of Ganga, O you of great intelligence.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: गङ्गायास्तीरमाश्रित्य हते शान्तनवे नृप॥ आप्लुत्य देवा वसवः समेत्य च महानदीम्। इदमूचुर्वचो घोरं भागीरथ्या मते तदा॥ एष शान्तनवो भीष्मो निहतः सव्यसाचिना।
en: After the fall of Shantanu's son, those celestials, viz., the Vasus, coming to the banks of Ganga, bathed in her waters, and calling the goddess of that stream, they uttered these terrible words having the sanction of Bhagirati herself, viz., Shantanu's son Bhishma has been killed by Dhananjaya.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: अयुध्यमानः संग्रामे संसक्तोऽन्येन भाविनि। तदनेनानुषङ्गेण वयमद्य धनंजयम्॥
en: Indeed, O goddess, Bhishma then was engaged with another, and had ceased to fight. For this fault we shall today imprecate a curse on Dhananjaya!

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: शापेन योजयामेति तथास्त्विति च साब्रवीत्। तदहं पितुरावेद्य प्रविश्य व्यथितेन्द्रिया॥
en: To this, the goddess Ganga readily agreed, saying, Be it so! Hearing these words I became very much distressed and penetrating into the nether regions represented everything to my father.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: अभवं स च तच्छ्रुत्वा विषादमगमत् परम्। पिता त मे तु मे वसून् गत्वा त्वदर्थे समयाचत॥ पुनः पुनः प्रसाद्यैतांस्त एनमिदमब्रुवन्। पुत्रस्तस्य महाभाग मणिपूरेश्वरो युवा॥
en: Informed of what had taken place, my father became plunged in grief. Going to the Vasus, he begged them for your sake, again and again gratifying them by every means in his power. They then said to him, Dhananjaya has a highly blessed son who, youthful as he is, is the king of Manipura.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: स एनं रणमध्यस्थः शरैः पातयिता शुवि। एवं कृते स नागेन्द्र मुक्तशापो भविष्यति॥
en: He will, standing on the field of battle, cast Dhananjaya down on the Earth. When this will take place, O Prince of Snakes, Arjuna will be freed from our curse!

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: गच्छेति वसुभिश्चोक्तो मम चेदं शशंस सः। तच्छ्रुत्वात्वं मया तस्माच्छापादसि विमोक्षितः॥
