en: Do you return! Thus addressed by the Vasus, he came back and informed me of what had taken place. Having learnt all this, O hero, I have freed you from the curse of the Vasus in thus.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: न हि त्वां देवराजोऽपि समरेषु पराजयेत्। आत्मा पुत्रः स्मृतस्तस्मात् तेनेहासि पराजितः॥
en: The king of the celestials himself, incapable of defeating you in battle. The son is one's own self. It is for this that you have been defeated by him.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: न हि दोषो मम मतः कथं वा मन्यसे विभो। इत्येवमुक्तो विजयः प्रसन्नात्माब्रवीदिदम्॥ सर्वे मे सुप्रियं देवि यदेतत् कृतवत्यसि।
en: I cannot be held, O powerful one, to have committed any sin. How, indeed, would you hold me censurable? Thus addressed (by Ulupi), Vijaya became cheerful of heart and said to her, All this you have done, O goddess, is highly agreeable to me.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: इत्युक्त्वा सोऽब्रवीत् पुत्रं मणिपूरपतिं जयः॥ चित्राङ्गदायाः शृण्वत्याः कौरव्यदुहितुस्तदा। युधिष्ठिरस्याश्वमेधः परिचैत्री भविष्यति॥ तत्रागच्छेः सहामात्यो मातृभ्यां सहितो नृप॥
en: After this, Jaya addressed his son, the king of Manipura, and said to him in the hearing of Chitrangada, the daughter (-in-law) of Kuru's race, the Horse-Sacrifice of Yudhishthira will take place on the day of full moon in the coming month of Chaitra.Come there, O king, with your mother and your counsellors and officers!'

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: इत्येवमुक्तः पार्थन स राजा बभ्रुवाहनः। उवाच पितरं धीमानिदमस्राविलेक्षणः॥ उपयास्यामि धर्मज्ञ भवतः शासनादहम्। अश्वमेधे महायज्ञे द्विजातिपरिवेषकः॥
en: Thus addressed by Partha, king Babhruvahana of great intelligence, with tearful eyes, said these words to his father, 'O you who are conversant with every duty, I shall certainly go, at your command, to the great Horse-Sacrifice, and take upon myself the task of distributing food among the twice-born ones!

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: मम त्वनुग्रहार्थाय प्रविशस्व पुरं स्वकम्। भार्याभ्यां सह धर्मज्ञ मा भूत् तेऽत्र विचारणा॥
en: For, however, showing your grace towards me, do you enter your own city with your two wives. Do not cherish any scruple about this, O you who are fully acquainted with every duty!

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: उषित्वेह निशामेकां सुखं स्वभवने प्रभो। पुनरश्वानुगमनं कर्तासि जयतां वर॥
en: O lord, having lived for one night in your own palace in happiness, you may then follow the horse, O foremost of victorious warriors!

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: इत्युक्तः स तु पुत्रेण तदा वानरकेतनः। स्मयन् प्रोवाच कौन्तेयस्तदा चित्राङ्गदासुतम्॥ विदितं ते महाबाहो यथा दीक्षां चराम्यहम्। न स तावत् प्रवेक्ष्यामि पुरं ते पृथुलोचन॥
en: The ape-bannered son of Kunti, thus addressed by his son, answered the child Chitrangada, saying, You know, mighty-armed one, what vow I am observing? O you of large eyes, till the termination of this my vow, I cannot enter your city.

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: यथाकामं व्रजत्येष यज्ञियाश्वो नरर्षभा स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि न स्थानं विद्यते मम॥
en: O foremost of men, this sacrificial horse wanders at will. Blessings on you. I must go away. I have no place to rest for even a short while!

description: She gives an account of the whole thing
sn: स तत्र विधिवत् तेन पूजित: पाकशासनिः। भार्याभ्यामभ्यनुज्ञातः प्रायाद् भरतसत्तमः॥
en: The son of the chastiser of Paka then, duly adored by his son and obtaining the permission of his wives, left the spot and proceeded on his way.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स तु वाजी समुद्रान्तां पर्येत्य वसुधामिमाम्। निवृत्तोऽभिमुखो राजन् येन वारणसाह्वयम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said The (sacrificial) horse, having wandered over the entire Earth bounded by the ocean, then ceased and turned his face toward the city of Hastinapur.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: अनुगच्छंश्च तुरगं निवृत्तोऽथ किरीटभृत्। यदृच्छया समापेदे पुरं राजगृहं तदा॥
en: Following as he did that horse, the diademdecked Arjuna also turned his face towards the Kuru capital. Wandering at is will, the horse then came to the city of Rajagriha.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: तमभ्याशगतं दृष्ट्वा सहदेवात्मजः प्रभो। क्षत्रधर्मे स्थितो वीरः समरायाजुहाव ह॥
en: Seeing him arrived within his kingdom, O monarch, the heroic of Sahadeva, following Kshatriya duties, challenged him to battle.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: ततः पुरात् सनिष्क्रम्य रथी धन्वी शरी तली। मेघसन्धिः पदाति तं धनंजयमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Coming out of his city, Meghasandhi, mounted on his car and equipt with bow and arrows and leathern fence, rushed towards Dhananjaya who was on foot.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: आसाद्य च महातेजा मेघसन्धिर्धनंजयम्। बालभावान्महाराज प्रोवाचेदं न कौशलात्॥
en: Gifted with great energy, Meghasandhi, approaching Dhanajaya, O king, said these words from a spirit of childishness and without son any skill.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: किमयं चार्यते बाजी स्त्रीमध्य इव भारत। ह्यमेनं हरिष्यामि प्रयतस्व विमोक्षणे॥
en: This horse of yours, O Bharata, seems to move about, protected by women only! I shall take away the horse. Do you try to free him.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: अदत्तानुनयो युद्धे यदि त्वं पितृभिर्मम। करिष्यामि तवातिथ्यं प्रहर प्रहरामि च॥
en: Although my sires did not teach you in battle, I, however, shall do the duties of hospitality to you. Do you strike me, for I shall strike you.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचैनं प्रहसन्निव पाण्डवः। विनकर्ता मया वार्य इति मे व्रतमाहितम्॥ भ्रात्रा ज्येष्ठेन नृपते तवापि विदितं ध्रुवम्। प्रहरस्व यथाशक्ति न मन्युर्विद्यते मम॥
en: Thus addressed, the son of Pandu, smiling the while, answered him, saying, To resist him who obstructs me is the vow imposed on me by my eldest brother. Forsooth, O king, you know this. Do you strike me to the best of your power. I have no anger.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: इत्युक्तः प्राहरत् पूर्वे पाण्डवं मगधेश्वरः। किरन् शरसहस्राणि वर्षाणीव सहस्रदृक्॥
en: Thus addressed, the king of Magadha first struck the son of Pandu, showering his arrows on him like the thousand-eyed Indra showering a heavy downpour of rain.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: ततो गाण्डीवभृच्छूरो गाण्डीवप्रहितैः शरैः। चकार मोघांस्तान् बाणान् सयलान् भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then, Ochief of Bharata's race, the heroic wielder of Gandiva, with arrows shot of that excellent bow, baffled all the arrows shot carefully at him by his adversary.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: स मोघं तस्य बाणौधं कृत्वा वानरकेतनः। शरान् मुमोच ज्वलितान् दीप्तास्यानिव पन्नगान्॥१२
en: Having thus baffled that cloud of arrows, the ape-bannered hero shot a number of burning arrows at his enemy which resembled snakes with fiery mouths.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: ध्वजे पताकादण्डेषु रथे यन्त्रे हयेषु च। अन्येषु च रथाङ्गेषु न शरीरे न सारथौ॥
en: These arrows he shot at his flag and flagstaff and car and poles and yoke and the horses sparing the body of his-enemy and his cardriver.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: संरक्ष्यमाणः पार्थेन शरीरे सव्यसाचिना। मन्यमानः स्ववीर्यं तन्मागधः प्राहिणोच्छरान्॥
en: Though Partha who was capable of shooting with the bow with the left-hand (as well as the right) spared the body of the king of Magadha, yet the latter, thinking that his body was protected by his own prowess, discharged many arrows at Partha.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: ततो गाण्डीवधन्वा तु मागधेन भृशाहतः। बभौ वसन्तसमये पलाशः पुष्पितो यथा॥
en: The wielder of Gandiva, deeply struck by the king of Magadha, shone like a blossoming Palasha (Butea frondosa) in the season of spring.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: अवध्यमानः सोऽभयनन्मागधः पाण्डवर्षभम्। तेन तस्थौ य कौरव्य लोकवीरस्य दर्शने॥
en: Arjuna had no desire of killing the king of Magadha. It was for this that, having struck the son of Pandu, he succeeded in remaining before that foremost of heroes.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: सव्यसाची तु संक्रुद्धो विकृष्य बलवद् धनुः। हयांश्चकार निर्जीवान् सारथेश्च शिरोऽहरत्॥
en: Then Dhananjaya, becoming angry, drew his bow with great force, and killed his antagonist's horses and then struck off the head of his car-driver.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: धनुश्चास्य महच्चित्रं क्षुरेण प्रचकर्त ह। हस्तावापं पताकां च ध्वजं चास्य न्यपातयत्॥
en: With a razor-headed arruw he then cut off Meghasandhi's large and beautiful bow, and then his leathern fence. Then cutting off his flag and flag-staff, he caused it to fall down.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: स राजा व्यथितो व्यश्वो विधनुर्हतसारथिः। गदामादाय कौन्तेयमभिदुद्राव वेगवान्॥
en: The king of Magadha greatly afflicted, and deprived of horses and bow and driver, took up a mace and rushed with great speed at the son of Kunti.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: तस्यापतत एवाशु गदां हेमपरिष्कृताम्। शरैश्चकर्त बहुधा बहुभिर्गृध्रवाजितैः॥
en: Arjuna, then, with many arrows of his equipt with his vulturine feathers, cut off into pieces, that mace of his advancing enemy which was adorned with bright gold.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: सा गदा शकलीभूता विशीर्णमणिबन्धना। व्याली विमुच्यमानेव पपात धरणीतले॥
en: Thus cut off into pieces, that mace, with its jeweiled bonds and knots all severed, fell on the Earth, like a she-snake helplessly hurled down by somebody.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: विरथं विधनुष्कं च गदया परिवर्जितम्। सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् कपिकेतनः॥ पर्याप्तः क्षत्रधर्मोऽयं दर्शितः पुत्र गम्यताम्। बह्वेतत् समरे कर्म तव बालस्य पार्थिव॥
en: When his enemy became deprived of his car, his bow, and his mace, the ape-bannered hero then, comforting his cheerless enemy who had been observant of Kshatriya duties, said to him these words: O son, you have sufficiently shorn your adherence to Kshatriya duties. Go now. Great have been the feats, O king, which you have accomplished in battle although you are very young in years.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: युधिष्ठिरस्य संदेशो न हन्तव्या नृपा इति। तेन जीवसि राजंस्त्वमपराद्धोऽपि मे रणे।॥
en: The command I received from Yudhishthira was that kings who oppose me should not be killed. It is for this you live yet, O monarch, although you have offended me in battle.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: इति मत्वा तदात्मानं प्रत्यादिष्टं स्म मागधः। तथ्यमित्यभिगम्यैनं प्राञ्जलिः प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: Thus addressed, the king of Magadha considered himself defeated and spared. Thinking then that it was his duty to do so, he approached Arjuna and joining his hands in respect adored him.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: पराजितोऽस्मि भद्रं ते नाहं योधुमिहात्सहे। यद् यत् कृत्यं मया तेऽद्य तद् ब्रूहि कृतमेव तु॥
en: And he said, Defeated have I been by you! Blessed be you, I do not venture to continue the battle. Tell me what I am to do now for you! Consider your command as already carried out.'

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: तमर्जूनः समाश्वास्य पुनरेवेदमब्रवीत्। आगन्तव्यं परां चैत्रीमश्वमेधे नृपस्य नः॥
en: Comforting him again, Arjuna once more said to him. You should go to the HorseSacrifice of our king which takes place at the coming full moon of Chaitra.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: इत्युक्तः स तथेत्युक्त्वा पूजयामास तं हयम्। फाल्गुनं च युधि श्रेष्ठं विधिवत् सहदेवजः॥
en: Thus addressed by him, the son of Sahadeva said, So be it, and then duly adored that horse as also Phalguna, that foremost of warriors.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: ततो यथेष्टमगमत् पुनरेव स केसरी। ततः समुद्रतीरेण वङ्गान् पुण्ड्रान् सकोसलान्॥
en: The sacrificial horse then, having beautiful manes, proceeded at his will along the seacoast, going to the countries of the Bangas, the Pundras, and the Kosalas.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse homewards
sn: तत्र तत्र च भूरीणि म्लेच्छसैन्यान्यनेकशः। विजिग्ये धनुषा राजन् गाण्डीवेन धनंजयः॥
en: In those kingdoms Dhananjaya, with his bow Gandiva, O king, defeated numberless Mleccha armies one after another.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच मागधेनार्चितो राजन पाण्डवः श्वेतवाहनः। दक्षिणां दिशमास्थाय चारयामास तं हयम्॥
en: Vaishampayana continued : Adored by the king of Magadha, Pandu's son having white horses yoked to his car, proceeded along the south, following the (sacrificial) horse.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: ततः स पुनरावर्त्य हयः कामचरो बली। आससाद पुरीरम्यां चेदीनां शुक्तिसाह्वयाम्॥
en: Turning round in course of his wanderings at will, the strong horse came upon the beautiful city of the Chedis called after the oyster.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: शरभेणार्चितस्तत्र शिशुपालसुतेन सः। युद्धपूर्वं तदा तेन पूजया च महाबलः॥
en: Sharabha, the son of Shishupala, gifted with great strength, first met Arjuna in battle and then adored him with due honours.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: ततोऽर्चितो ययौ राजस्तदा स तुरगोत्तमः। काशीनगान् कोसलांश्च किरातानथ तेगणान्॥
en: Adored by him, O king, that best of horses then proceeded to the kingdom of the Kashis, the Angas, the Kosalas, the Kiratas, and the Tanganas.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: पूजां तत्र यथान्यायं प्रतिगृह्य धनंजयः। पुनरावृत्य कौन्तेयो दशार्णानगमत् तदा॥
en: Receiving due honours in all those kingdoms Dhananjaya turned his course. Indeed, the son of Kunti then proceeded to the country of the Dasharnas,

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: तत्र चित्राङ्गदो नाम बलवानरिमर्दनः। तेन युद्धमभूत् तस्य विजयस्यातिभैरवम्॥
en: The ruler of that people was Chitrangada who was gifted with great strength and was a crusher of enemies. Between him and Vijaya took place a very dreadful battle.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: तं चापि वशमानीय किरीटी पुरुषर्षभः। निषादराज्ञो विषयमेकलव्यस्य जग्मिवान्॥
en: Bringing him under his control the diademdecked Arjuna, that foremost of men, went to the kingdom of the Nishada king, viz., the son of Ekalavya.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: एकलव्यसुतश्चैनं युद्धेन जगृहे तदा। तत्र चक्रे निषादैः स संग्राम लोमहर्षणम्॥
en: The son of Ekalavya received Arjuna in battle! The encounter took place between the Kuru hero and the Nishadas was so furious as to make the hairs stand erect.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: ततस्तमपि कौन्तेयः समरेष्वपराजितः। जिगाय युधि दुर्धर्षो यज्ञविघ्नार्थमागतम्॥
en: Unvanquished in battle, the brave son of Kunti defeated the Nishada king who proved an impediinent to the sacrifice.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: स तं जित्वा महाराज नैषादि पाकशासनिः। अर्चितः प्रययौ भूयो दक्षिणं सलिलार्णवम्॥
en: Having subjugated the son of Ekalavya, O king, the son of Indra, duly adored by the Nishadas, then proceeded towards the southern Ocean.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: तत्रापि द्रविडैरान्नै रौद्रैर्माहिषकैरपि। तथा कोल्लगिरेयैश्च युद्धमासीत् किरीटिन:॥
en: In those regions battles took place between the diadem-decked hero and the Dravidas and Andhras and the dreadful Mahishakas and the hillmen of Kolwa.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: तांश्चापि विजयो जित्वा नातितीव्रण कर्मणा। तुरङ्गमवशेनाथ सुराष्ट्रानभितो ययौ॥
en: Subjugating those tribes without having to perform any terrific feats, Arjuna proceeded to the country of the Saurashtras, his footsteps guided by the horse.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: गोकर्णमथ चायाद्य प्रभासमपि जग्मिवान्। ततो द्वारवती रम्यां वृष्णिवीराभिमालिताम्॥
en: Arrived at Gokarna, he went thence to Prabhasa. Then he proceeded to the beautiful city of Dvaravati protected by the heroes of the Vrishni race.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: आससाद हयः श्रीमान् कुरुराजस्य यज्ञियः। तमुन्मथ्य हयश्रेष्ठं यादवानां कुमारकाः॥
en: When the beautiful sacrificial horse of the Kuru king reached Dvaravati, the Yadava youths, used force against that foremost of horses.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: प्रययुस्तांस्तदा राजन्नुग्रसेनो न्यवारयत्। ततः पुराद् विनिष्क्रम्य वृष्ण्यन्धकपतिस्तदा॥ सहितो वसुदेवेन मातुलेन किरीटिनः। तौ समेत्य कुरुश्रेष्ठ विधिवत्प्रीतिपूर्वकम्॥
en: King Ugrasena, however, soon went out and forbade those youths from doing what they thought. Then the king of the Vrislinis and the Andhakas, issuing out of his palace, with Vasudeva, the maternal uncle of Arjuna, in his company, cheerfully met the Kuru hero and received him with due rites.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: परया भारतश्रेष्ठ पूजया समवस्थितौ। ततस्ताभ्यामनुज्ञातो ययौ येन हयो गतः॥
en: The two elderly chiefs honoured Arjuna duly. Getting their permission, the Kuru prince then proceeded to where the horse he followed lied him.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: ततः स पश्चिमं देशं समुद्रस्य तदा हयः। क्रमेण व्यचरत् स्फीतं ततः पञ्चनदं ययौ॥
en: The sacrificial horse then proceeded along the coast of the western ocean and at last reached the country of the five waters full of population and prosperity.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: तस्मादपि स कौरव्य गन्धारविषयं हयः। विचचार यथाकामं कौन्तेयानुगतस्तदा॥
en: Thence, O king, the horse proceeded to the country of the Gandharas. Arrived there, it roamed at will, followed by the son of Kunti.

description: The return of the sacrificial horse to Dwarka
sn: ततो गान्धारराजेन युद्धमासीत् किरीटिनः। घोरं शकुनिपुत्रेण पूर्ववैरानुसारिणा॥
en: Then took place a dreadful battle between the diadem-decked hero and the king of the Gandharas, viz., the son of Shakuni, who had a bitter remembrance of the grudge his father bore to the Pandavas.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शकुनेस्तनयो वीरो गान्धराणां महारथः। प्रत्युद्ययौ गुडाकेशं सैन्येन महता वृतः॥ हस्त्यश्वरथयुक्तेन पताकाध्वजमालिना।
en: Vaishmpayana said The heroic son of Shakuni, who was a powerful car-warrior among the Gandharas, accompanied by a large army, proceeded against the Kuru hero of curly hair. That force contained elephants, horses and cars, and was adorned with many flags and banners.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: अमृष्यमाणास्ते योधा नृपस्य शकुनेर्वधम्॥ अभ्ययुः सहिताः पार्थं प्रगृहीतशरासनाः।
en: Unable to bear, and, therefore, burning to avenge, the destruction of their kin Shakuni. those warriors, armed with bows, rushed together at Partha.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: स तानुवाच धर्मात्मा बीभत्सुरपराजिताः॥ युधिष्ठिरस्य वचनं न च ते जगृहुर्हितम्।
en: The unvanquished Bibhatsu of virtuous soul addressed them peacefully, but they were reluctant to accept the beneficial words of Yudhishthira.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: वार्यमाणाऽपि पार्थेन सान्त्वपूर्वममर्पिताः॥ परिवार्य हयं जग्मुस्ततश्चक्रोध पाण्डवः।
en: Though forbidden by Partha with sweet words, they still gave themselves up to anger and surrounded the sacrificial horse. At this, the son of Pandu became filled with rage.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: ततः शिरांसि दीप्तायैस्तेषां चिच्छेद पाण्डवः॥ क्षुरैर्गाण्डपवनिर्मुक्तैर्नातियत्नादिवार्जुनः।
en: Then Arjuna, carelessly shooting from Gandiva many arrows with razor-like heads that blazed with splendour, cut off the heads of many Gandhara warriors.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: वध्यमानाः पार्थेन हयमुत्सृज्य सम्भ्रमात्॥ न्यवर्तन्त महाराज शरवर्षार्दिता भृशम्।
en: While thus killed by Partha, the Gandharas, O king, exceedingly afflicted, liberated the horse, moved by fear and desisted from battle.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: निरुध्यमानस्तैश्चापि गान्धारैः पाण्डुनन्दनः॥ आदिश्यादिश्य तेजस्वी शिरांस्येषां न्यपातयत्।
en: Resisted, however, by those Gandhara combatant who still surrounded him on all sides, the son of Pandu, gifted with great energy, cut off the heads of many, previously naming those whom he thus killed.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: वध्यमानेषु तेष्वाजौ गान्धारेषु समन्ततः॥ स राजा शकुनेः पुत्रः पाण्डवं प्रत्यवारयत्।
en: When the Gandhara warriors were thus being killed all around him in battle, the royal son of Shakuni came forward to resist the son of Pandu.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: तं युध्यमानं राजानं क्षत्रधर्मे व्यवस्थितम्॥ पार्थोऽब्रवीन मे वध्या राजानो राजशासनात्। अलं युद्धेन ते वीर न तेऽस्त्वद्य पराजयः॥
en: To the Gandhara king who was fighting with him, moved by Kshatriya duty, Arjuna said, I do not intend to kill the kings who fight with me, on account of the commands of Yudhishthira. O hero, Cease to fight with me. Do not scek defeat today.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: इत्युक्तस्तदनादृत्य वाक्यमज्ञानमोहितः। स शक्रसमकर्माणं समवाकिरदाशुगैः॥
en: Thus addressed, the son of Shakuni, stupefied by folly, disregarded that advice and covered with many swift shafts the Kuru hero who resembled Shakra hiinself in the feats he performed in battle.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: तस्य पार्थः शिरस्त्राणमर्धचन्द्रेण पत्रिणा। अपाहरदमेयात्मा जयद्रथशिरो यथा॥
en: Then Parhta, with a crescent-shaped arrow, cut off the head-gear of his enemies. Of immeasurable soul, he also caused that headgear to be borne along a great distance like the head of Jayadratha.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मयं जग्मुर्गान्धाराः सर्व एव ते। इच्छता तेन न हतो राजेत्यसि च तं विदुः॥
en: Seeing this feat, all the Gandhara warriors became stricken with wonder. They full well understood that Arjuna voluntarily spared their king.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: गान्धारराजपुत्रस्तु पलायनकृतक्षणः। ययौ तैरेव सहितस्त्रस्तैः क्षुद्रमृगरिव॥
en: The prince of the Gandharas then began to fly away from the field, followed by all his warriors who resembled a flock of frightened deer.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: तेषां तु तरसा पार्थस्तत्रैव परिधावताम्। प्रजहारोत्तमाङ्गानि भल्लैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: The Gandharas, through fear, lost their senses and wandered over the field, unable to escape. Arjuna, with his broadheaded arrows, cut off the heads of many.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: उच्छ्रितांस्तु भुजान् केचिन्नाबुध्यन्त शरैर्हतान्। शरैर्गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तैः पृथुभिः पार्थचोदितैः॥
en: Many there were who lost their arins on account of Arjuna's arrows, but so stupefied were they with fear that they were not aware of the loss of that limb. Indeed, the Gandhara army was greatly afflicted with those large arrows which Partha discharged from Gandiva.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: सम्भ्रान्तनरनागाश्वप्रपतद् विद्रुतं बलम्। हतविध्वस्तभूयिष्ठमावर्तत मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: That army, which then consisted of frightened men and elephants and horse, which lost many warriors and animals, and which had been disordered and routed, began to wander and wheel about the field again and again.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: नाभ्यदृश्यन्त वीरस्य केचिदग्रेऽग्यकर्मणः। रिपव: पात्यमाना वै ये सहेयुर्धञ्जयम्॥
en: Among those enemies who were thus being killed, none could be seen standing in front of the Kuru hero fained for foreinost of feats. No one could be seen who was able to bear the prowess of Dhananjaya.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: ततो गान्धारराजस्य मन्त्रिवृद्धपुरःसरा! जननी निर्ययौ भीता पुरस्कृत्यार्धमुत्तमम्॥
en: Then the mother of the king of the Gandharas, filled with fear, and with all the aged ministers of state, came out of her city, taking an excellent Arghya for Arjuna.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: सा न्यवारदव्यग्रं तं पुत्र युद्ध दुर्मदम्। प्रसादयामास च तं जिष्णुमक्लिष्टकारिणम्॥
en: She forbade her brave son of steady heart from fighting any longer, and pleased Jishnu who was never fatigued with toil.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: तां पूजयित्वा बीभत्सुः प्रसादमकरोत् प्रभुः। शकुनेश्चापि तनयं सान्त्वयन्निदमब्रवीत्॥ न मे प्रियं महाबाहो यत्ते बुद्धिरियं कृता। प्रतियोद्धुममित्रघ्न भ्रातैव त्वं ममानघ॥
en: The powerful Bibhatsu adored her and became inclined to show mercy towards the Gandharas. Comforting the son of Shakuni, he said, You have not, O mightyarmed hero, done what is agreeable to me by adopting these hostile measures! O destroyer of heroes, you are my brother, O sinless one.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: गान्धारी मातरं स्मृत्वा धृतराष्ट्रकृतेन च। तेन जीवसि राजंस्त्वं निहतास्त्वनुगास्तव॥
en: Recollecting my mother Gandhari, and for the sake of Dhritarashtra also, I have not taken your life. It is for this, o king, that you live still, Many of your followers, however, have been killed by me.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: मैवं भूः शाम्यतां वैरं मा ते भूद् बुद्धिरीदृशी। गच्छेयास्त्वं परां चैत्रीमश्वमेधे नृपस्य नः॥
en: Let not such a thing happen again. Let hostilities cease. Let not your understanding again go wrong. You should go to the HorseSacrifice of our king which takes place on the day of full moon of the month of Chaitra. still, Many of your followers, however, have been killed by me.

description: The battle between Arjuna and Gandhara king
sn: मैवं भूः शाम्यतां वैरं मा ते भूद् बुद्धिरीदृशी। गच्छेयास्त्वं परां चैत्रीमश्वमेधे नृपस्य नः॥
en: Let not such a thing happen again. Let hostilities cease. Let not your understanding again go wrong. You should go to the HorseSacrifice of our king which takes place on the day of full moon of the month of Chaitra.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वानुपयौ पार्थं हयं कामविहारिणम्। न्यवर्तत ततो वाजी येन नागाह्वयं पुरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said these words, Partha started, following the horse which roamed at will. The sacrificial horse then turned towards the road leading to the city of Hastinapur.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: तं निवृत्तं तु शुश्चाव चारणैव युधिष्ठिरः। श्रुत्वार्जुनं कुशलिनं स च हृष्टमनाऽभवत्॥
en: Yudhishthira heard from his intelligencebearers that the horse had turned back. And hearing also that Arjuna was hale and hearty, he became filled with joy.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: विजयस्य च तत् कर्म गान्धारविषये तदा। श्रुत्वा चान्येषु देशेषु स सुप्रीतोऽभवत् तदा॥
en: Hearing also the feats, performed by Vijaya in the country of the Gandharas as also in other kingdoms, the king became highly pleased.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु द्वादशी माघमासिकीम्। इष्टं गृहीत्वा नक्षत्रं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥ समानाय महातेजाः सर्वान् भ्रातृन् महीपतिः। भीमं च नकुलं चैव सहदेवं च कौरव॥ प्रोवाचेदं वचः काले तदा धर्मभृतां वरः। आमत्र्य वदतां श्रेष्ठो भीमं प्रहरतां वरम्॥
en: In the meantime, seeing that the twelfth day of the lighted fortnight in the month of Magha had come, and marking also that the constellation was favourable, high Yudhirshthira the just summoned all his brothers, viz., Bhima and Nakula and Sahadeva. Gifted with great energy, the king, o you of Kuru's race, that foremost of all persons knowing duties, said these words in proper time, Indeed, that foremost of all speakers, addressing Bhima, the first of all smiters, said,

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: आयाति भीमसेनासौ सहाश्वेन तवानुजः। यथा मे पुरुषाः प्राहुर्ये धनंजयसारिणः॥
en: Your younger brother (Arjuna), O Bhimasena, is returning with the horse. I have learnt this from those men who had followed Arjuna.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: उपस्थितश्च कालोऽयमभितो वर्तते हयः। मार्य च पौर्णमासीयं मास: शेषो वृकोदर॥
en: The time is come. The sacrificial horse is near. The day of full moon of the month of Magha is also near. The month is about to expire. O Vrikodara.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: प्रस्थाप्यन्तां हि विद्वांसो ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः। वाजिमेधार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं देशं पश्यन्तु यज्ञियम्॥
en: Let, therefore, learned Brahmanas knowing the Vedas look for a sacrificial spot for the celebration of the Horse-Sacrifice.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्तः स तु तच्चक्रे भीमो नृपतिशासनम्। हृष्टः श्रुत्वा गुडाकेशमायान्तं पुरुषर्षभम्॥
en: Thus addressed, Bhima obeyed the royal command He became very glad upon hearing that Arjuna of curly hair was about to retum.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: ततो ययौ भीमसेनः प्राज्ञैः स्थपतिभिः सह। ब्राह्मणानग्रतः कृत्वा कुशलान् यज्ञकर्मणि॥
en: Then Bhimna went out with a number of men knowing the rules of laying out sacrificial grounds and constructing buildings. And he took with him many Brahmanas well-versed in all the rites of sacrifices.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: तं स शालचयं श्रीमत् सप्रतोलीसुघट्टितम्। मापयामास कौरव्यो यज्ञवाट यथाविधि॥
en: Bhima selected a beautiful place and caused it to be duły measured out for laying the sacrificial compound. Numberless houses and mansions were constructed on it and high and broad roads also were laid cut.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: प्रासादशतसम्बाधं मणिप्रवरकुट्टिमम्। कारयामास विधिवद्धरत्नविभूषितम्॥
en: Soon enough the Kaurava hero filled that ground with hundreds of excellent palaces. The surface was levelled and made smooth with jewels and gems, and adorned with various golden structures.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: स्तम्भान् कनकचित्रांश्च तोरणानि बृहन्ति च। यज्ञायतनदेशेषु दत्त्वा शुद्धं च काननम्॥
en: Columns were raised, ornamented with bright gold an high and wide triumphal arches also were made on that sacrificial compound. All these were made of pure gold.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: अन्तःपुराणां राज्ञां च नानादेशसमीयुषाम्। कारयामास धर्मात्मा तत्र तत्र यथाविध॥
en: The righteous-souled prince also caused apartments to be duly constructed for the accommodation of ladies and of the numerous kings who, coming from many kingdoms, were expected to grace the sacrifice with their presence.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: ब्राह्मणानां च वेश्मानि नानादेशसमीयुषाम्। कारयामास कौन्तेयो विधिवत् तान्यनेकशः॥
en: The son of Kunti also caused many palaces to be duty erected for Brahmanas who were expected to come from various kingdoms.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: तथा सम्प्रेषयामास दूतान् नृपतिशासनात्। भीमसेनो महाबाहो राज्ञामक्लिष्टकर्मणाम्॥
en: Then the mighty-armed Bhimasena, at the command of the king, sent out messengers to the great kings of the Earth.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: ते प्रियार्थं कुरुपतेराययुर्नृपसत्तम। रत्नान्यने कान्यादाय स्त्रियोऽश्वानायुधानि च॥
en: Those best of kings came to the HorseSacrifice of the Kuru king for doing what was agreeable to him. And they brought many gems with them and many female slaves and horses and weapons.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: तेषां निविशतां तेषु शिबिरेषु महात्मनाम्। नर्दतः सागरस्येव दिवस्पृगभवत् स्वतः॥
en: The sounds which arose from those great kings who lived within those pavilions touched the very heavens and resembled the noise made by the roaring ocean.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: तेषामभ्यागतानां च स राजा कुरुवर्धनः। व्यादिदेशान्नपानानि शय्याश्चाप्यतिमानुषाः॥
en: King Yudhishthria, the delighter of the Kurus, assigned to the monarchs who thus came to his sacrifice various kinds of food and drink, and beds also of celestial beauty.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: वाहनानां च विविधाः शाला: शालीक्षुगोरसैः। उपेता भरतश्रेष्ठो व्यादिदेश स धर्मराट्॥
en: The chief of the Bharatas, viz., king Yudhishthria the just, assigned several stables well-filled with different kinds of corn and sugar-cane and milk to the animals.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: तथा तस्मिन् महायज्ञे धर्मराजस्य धीमतः। समाजग्मुर्मुनिगणा बहवो ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
en: To that great sacrifice of king Yudhishthira the just who was gifted with high intelligence, there also came a large number of ascetics all of whom were utterers of Brahma.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: ये च द्विजाति प्रवरास्तत्रासन् पृथिवीपते। समाजग्सुः सशिष्यास्तान् प्रतिजग्राह कौरवः॥
en: Indeed, O king, all the foremost ones among the twice born class that were then alive, came to that sacrifice, accompanied by their disciples. The Kuru king received them all.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: सर्वोश्च ताननुययौ यावदावसथान् प्रति। स्वयमेव महातेजा दम्भं त्यक्त्वा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: King Yudhishthira of great energy, renouncing all pride, himself followed all his guests to the pavilions that had been assigned for this residence.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: ततः कृत्वा स्थपतयः शिल्पिनोऽन्ये च ये तदा। कृत्स्नं यज्ञविधिं राज्ञो धर्मज्ञाय न्यवेदयन्॥
en: Then all the mechanics and engineers, having completed the arrangements of the sacrifice, informed king Yudhishthira of it.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा धर्मराजस्तु कृतं सर्वमतन्द्रितः। हृष्टरूपोऽभवद् राजा सह भ्रातृभिरादृतः॥
en: Hearing that everything was ready, king Yudhishthira the just, full of alertness and attention, became highly pleased along with his brothers all of whom honoured him duly.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिन् यज्ञे प्रवृत्ते तु वाग्मिनो हेतुवादिनः। हेतुवादान् बहूनाहुः परस्परजिगीषवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said When the great sacrifice of Yudhishthira began, many eloquent dialecticians started diverse propositions and disputed thereon, desirous of defeating one another.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: ददृशुस्तं नृपतयो यज्ञस्य विधिमुत्तमम्। देवेन्द्रस्येव विहितं भीमसेनेन भारता॥
en: The (invited) kings saw the excellent preparations of that sacrifice, resembling those of the king himself of the celestials, made, O Bharata, by Bhimasena.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: ददृशुस्तोरणान्यत्र शातकुम्भमयानि ते। शय्यासनविहारांश्च सुबहून् रत्नसंचयान्॥
en: They saw many triumphal arches made of gold, and many beds and seats and other articles of enjoyment and luxury, and crowds of men collected at different parts.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: घटान् पात्री: कटाहानि कलशान् वर्धमानकान्। न हि किंचिदसौवर्णमपश्यन् वसुधाधिपाः॥
en: There were also many jars and vessels and cauldrons and jugs and lids and covers. The invited kings saw nothing there that was not made of gold.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: यूपांश्च शास्त्रपठितान् दारवान् हेमभूषितान्। उपक्लृप्तान् यथाकालं विधिवद् भूरिवर्चसः॥
en: Many sacrificial stakes also were set up, made, according to he directions of the scriptures, of wood, and adorned with gold. Gifted with great effulgence, these were duly planted and dedicated (with (with scriptural Mantras).

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: स्थलजा जलजा ये च पशवः केचन प्रभो। सर्वानेव समानीतानपश्यंस्तत्र ते नृपाः॥
en: The kings, again, saw all animals of land and water, collected there on the occasion.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: पाश्चैव महिषीश्चैव तथा वृद्धस्त्रियोऽपि च। औदकानि च सत्त्वानि श्वापदानि वयांसि च॥ जरायुजाण्डजातानि स्वेदजान्युद्धिदानि च। पर्वतानूपजातानि भूतानि ददृशुश्च ते११३४॥
en: And they also saw many kine and many buffaloes and many old women, and many aquatic animals, many beasts of prey, and many species of birds, and many specimens of viviparous and oviparous creatures, and many that are fifth-born, and many belonging to the vegetable kingdom and many-animals and plants which live or grow on mountains.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: एवं प्रमुदितं सर्वे पशुगोधनधान्यतः। यज्ञवाटं नृपा दृष्ट्वा परं विस्मयमागताः॥
en: Seeing the sacrificial compound thus adorned with animals and kine and corn, the invited kings became filled with wonder.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: ब्राह्मणानां विशां चैव बहुमृष्टान्नमृद्धिमत्। पूर्णे शतसहस्त्रे तु विप्राणां तत्र भुञ्जताम्॥
en: Large masses of costly sweetmeats were kept ready for both the Brahmanas and the Vaishyas. And when the feeding was over of a hundred thousand Brahmanas, drums and cymbals were beat.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: दुन्दुभिर्मेघनिर्घोषो मुहुर्मुहुरताड्यत। विननादासकृच्चापि दिवसे दिवसे गते॥
en: And so large was the number fed that the sounds of drums and cymbals were heard again and again. Indeed, those sounds continued from day to day.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: एवं स ववृते यज्ञो धर्मराजस्य धीमतः। अन्नस्य सुबहून् राजनुत्सर्गान् पर्वतोपमान्॥
en: Thus was performed that sacrifice of the intelligent king Yudhishthira. Many hills of food. O king, were dedicated on the occasion. Many large tanks were seen of curds and many lakes of clarified butter.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: दधिकुल्याश्च ददृशुः सर्पिषश्च ह्रदान् जनाः। जम्बूद्वीपो हि सकलो नानाजनपदायुतः॥
en: In that great sacrifice, O monarch, was seen the entire population of Jamvudvipa, with all its kingdoms and provinces, collected together.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: राजन्नदृश्यतैकस्थो राजस्तस्य महामखे। जत्र जातिसहस्राणि पुरुषाणां ततस्ततः॥ गृहीत्वा भाजनान् जग्मुर्बहूनि भरतर्षभ। स्रग्विणश्चापि ते सर्वे सुमृष्टमाणकुण्डला:॥ पर्यवेषन द्विजातीस्ताशतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
en: Thousands of nations and races were there. A large number of men. O chief of Bharata's race, adorned with garlands and wearing bright ear-rings made of gold, taking numberless vessels in their hands, distributed the food to the twice-born classes by hundreds and thousands.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: विविधान्यन्नपानानि पुरुषा येऽनुयायिनः। ते वै नृपोपभोज्यानि ब्राह्मणानां ददुश्च ह॥
en: The attendants of the Pandavas gave away to the Brahmanas various kinds of food and drink which were, besides, so costly as to be worthy of being eaten and drunk by kings themselves. In that great sacrifice, O monarch, was seen the entire population of Jamvudvipa, with all its kingdoms and provinces, collected together.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: राजन्नदृश्यतैकस्थो राजस्तस्य महामखे। जत्र जातिसहस्राणि पुरुषाणां ततस्ततः॥ गृहीत्वा भाजनान् जग्मुर्बहूनि भरतर्षभ। स्रग्विणश्चापि ते सर्वे सुमृष्टमाणकुण्डला:॥ पर्यवेषन द्विजातीस्ताशतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
en: Thousands of nations and races were there. A large number of men. O chief of Bharata's race, adorned with garlands and wearing bright ear-rings made of gold, taking numberless vessels in their hands, distributed the food to the twice-born classes by hundreds and thousands.

description: The beginning of the Horse Sacrifice of Arjuna
sn: विविधान्यन्नपानानि पुरुषा येऽनुयायिनः। ते वै नृपोपभोज्यानि ब्राह्मणानां ददुश्च ह॥
en: The attendants of the Pandavas gave away to the Brahmanas various kinds of food and drink which were, besides, so costly as to be worthy of being eaten and drunk by kings themselves.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच समागतान् वेदविदो राज्ञश्च पृथिवीश्वरान्। दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरो राजा भीमसेनमभाषत॥ उपयाता नरव्याघ्रा य एते पृथिवीश्वराः एतेषां क्रियतां पूजा पूजार्हा हि नराधिपाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Seeing those kings-lords of Earth-all conversant with the Vedas, arrive, king Yudhishthira, addressing Bhimasena, said, O chief of men, let proper honors be paid to these kings who have come, for these foremost of men are all worthy of the highest honors.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्तः स तथा चक्रे नरेन्द्रेण यशस्विना। भीमसेनो महातेजा यमाभ्यां सह पाण्डवः॥
en: Thus addressed by the illustrious king Yudhishthira, Pandu's son Bhiinasena of mighty energy did as he was ordered, assisted by the twins.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: अथाभ्यगच्छद्गोविन्दो वृष्णिभिः सह धर्मजम्। बलदेवं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वप्राणभृतां वरः॥
en: The foremost of all men, viz., Govinda, came there, accompanied by the Vrishnis, and with Baladeva in the van.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: युयुधानेन सहितः प्रद्युम्नेन गदेन च। निशठेनाथ साम्बेन तथैव कृतवर्मणा।॥
en: He was accompanied by Yuyudhana and Pradyumna and Goda, and Nishatha and Shamba and Kritavarman.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: तेषामपि परां पूजां चक्रे भीमो महारथः। विविशुस्ते च वेश्मानि रत्नवन्ति च सर्वशः॥
en: The powerful car-warrior Bhima offered them the most respectful adoration. Those princes then entered the palaces, adorned with gems, which were assigned to them.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: युधिष्ठिरसमीपे तु कथान्ते मधुसूदनः। अर्जुनं कथयामास बहुसंग्रामकर्षितम्॥
en: At the end of a conversation he ad with Yudhishthira, the destroyer of Madhu referred to Arjuna who had been emaciated on account of many fights.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: स तं पप्रच्छ कौन्तेयः पुनः पुनररिंदमम्। धर्मजः शक्रजं जिष्णुं समाचष्ट जगत्पतिः॥
en: The son of Kunti repeatedly asked Krishna, that chastiser of enemies, about Arjuna. To Dharma's son, the lord of all the universe began to speak about Jishnu, the son of Shakra.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: आगमद् द्वारकावासी ममाप्तः पुरुषो नृप। योऽद्राक्षीत् पाण्डवश्रेष्ठ बहुसंग्रामकर्षितम्॥
en: O king, a confidential agent of mine living in Dwarka came to me. He had seen Arjuna, that foremost of Pandu's sons. Indeed, the latter has been very much emaciated with the fatigue of many battles,

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: समीपे च महाबाहुपाचष्ट च मम प्रभो। कुरु कार्याणि कौन्तेय हयमेधार्थसिद्धये॥
en: powerful monarch, that agent of mine inforned me that the mighty-armed hero is very near to us. You begin to celebrate your Horse-Sacrifice.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचैनं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। दिष्ट्या स कुशली जिष्णुरुपायाति च माधव॥
en: Thus addressed, king Yudhishthira the just said him, By good luck, O Madhava, Arjuna comes back safely!

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: यदिदं संदिदेशास्मिन् पाण्डवानां बलाग्रणी: तदा ज्ञातुमिहेच्छामि भवता यदुनन्दन॥
en: I wish to ascertain from you, O delighter of the Yadavas, what has been said in this matter by that mightiest of heroes amongs the sons of Pandu!

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्तो धर्मराजेन वृष्ण्यन्धकपतिस्तदा। प्रोवाचेदं वचो वाग्मी धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्॥ इदमाह महाराज पार्थवाक्यं स्मरन् नरः। वाच्यो युधिष्ठिरः कृष्ण काले वाक्यमिदं मम॥
en: Thus addressed by king Yudhishthira the just, the lord of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas, that foremost of eloquent men, said these words to that inonarch of righteous soul, My agent, reported the words of Partha thus to me, O great king, Yudhishthira, O Krishna, should be told these words of mine when the time comes!

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: आगमिष्यन्ति राजानः सर्वे वै कौरवर्षभ। प्राप्तानां महतां पूजा कार्या ह्येतत् क्षमं हि नः॥
en: O chief of the Kauravas, many kings will come (to your sacrifice)! When they arrive, high honours should be paid to them. This would, indeed, be worthy for us.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: इत्येतद्वचनाद् राजा विज्ञाप्यो मम मानद। यथा चात्ययिकं न स्याद् यदाहरणऽभवत्॥ कर्तुमर्हति तद राजा भवांश्चाप्यनुमन्यताम्। राजद्वषान्न नश्येयुरिमा राजन् पुनः प्रजाः॥
en: O giver of honours, the king should further be informed at iny request that he should do what is necessary for preventing a distinction similar to what occurred at the time of presenting the Arghya (on the occasion of the Rajasuya-Sacrifice). Let Krislina also approve of this. Let not, O king, through the ill-feeling of kings, the people be destroyed.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: इदमन्यच्च कौन्तेय वचः स पुरुषोऽब्रवीत्। धनंजयस्य नृपते तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: My man further reported, o king, these words of Dhananjaya, Listen as I repeat them.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: उपायास्यति यज्ञं नो मणिपूरपतिर्नृपः। पुत्रो मम महातेजा दयितो बभ्रुवाहनः॥
en: O monarch, the king of Manipura, my dear son Babhruvahana, will come at the sacrifice.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: तं भवान् मदपेश्चार्थ विधिवत् प्रतिपूजयेत्। स तु भक्तोऽनुरक्तश्च मम नित्यमिति प्रभो॥
en: Do you honour him duly for my sake, O powerful one, he is always attached and deeply devoted to me.

description: The arrival of a messenger from Arjuna
sn: इत्येतद् वचनं श्रुत्वा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। आभनन्द्यास्य तद् वाक्यमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing these words, king Yudhishthira the just approved of them and said as follows.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतं प्रियमिदं कृष्ण यत् त्वमर्हसि भाषितुम्। तन्येऽमृतरसं पुण्यं मनो ह्लादयति प्रभो॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have heard, O Krishna, your agreeable words, They are worthy of you. Gladsome and sweet as nectar are they. Indeed, they fill my heart with great joy, O powerful one.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: बहूनि किल युद्धानि विजयस्य नराधिपैः। पुनरासन् हृषीकेश तत्र तत्र च मे श्रुतम्॥
en: O Hrishikesha, I have heard that Vijaya has fought numberless battles with the kings of the Earth.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: किं निमित्तं स नित्यं हि पार्थः सुखविवर्जितः। अतीव विजयो धीमन्निति मे दूयते मनः॥
en: Why is Partha, always dissociated from ease and comfort? Vijaya is exceedingly intelligent. This, therefore, pains my heart very much.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: संचिन्तयामि कौन्तेयं रहो जिष्णुं जनार्दन। अतीव दुःखभागी स सततं पाण्डुनन्दनः॥
en: I always, O Janardana, think, when I am withdrawn from business, of Kunti's son Jishnu. The lot of that delighter of the Pandus is highly miserable.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: किं नु नस्य शरीरेऽस्ति सर्वलक्षणपूजिते। अनिष्टं लक्षणं कृष्ण येन दुःखान्युपाश्नुते॥
en: His body has every auspicious mark. What, however, O Krishna, is that sign in his excellent body for which he has always to suffer misery and discomfort?

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: अतीवासुखभोगी स सततं कुन्तिनन्दनः। न हि पश्यामि बीभत्सोर्निन्द्यं गात्रेषु किंचन। श्रोतव्यं चेन्मयै तद् वै तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: That son of Kunti has to bear a large share of misery. I do not see any censurable mark in his body. You should explain the cause to me if I deserve to hear it.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्तः स हृषीकेशो ध्यात्वा सुमहदुत्तरम्। राजानं भोजराजन्यवर्धनो विष्णुरब्रवीत्॥ न ह्यस्य नृपते किंचित् संश्लिष्टमुपलक्षये। ऋते पुरुषसिंहस्य पिण्डिकेऽस्याधिके यतः॥
en: Thus addressed, Hrishikesha, that enhancer of the glory of the Bhoja princes, having thought for long time, answered as follows:-I do not see any censurable mark in this prince, except that the cheek-bones of this foremost of men are a little too high.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: स ताभ्यां पुरुषव्याघ्रो नित्यमध्वसु वर्तते। न चान्यदनुपश्यामि येनासौ दुःखभाजनम्॥
en: For this that that foremost of men has always to be on the road. I really do not sce anything else for which he could be made so unhappy.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्तः पुरुषश्रेष्ठस्तदा कृष्णेन धीमता। प्रोवाच वृष्णिशार्दूलमेवमेतदिति प्रभो॥
en: Thus answered by the intelligent Krishna, that foremost of men, viz., kings, Yudhishthira, said to the chief of the Vrishnis that it was even SO.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: कृष्णा तु द्रौपदी कृष्णं तिर्यक् सासूयमैक्षत। प्रतिजग्राह तस्यास्तं प्रणयं चापि केशिहा॥ सख्युः सखा हृषीकेशः साक्षादिव धनंजयः।
en: The princess Draupadi, however, looked angrily and askance at Krishna. The destroyer of Keshi, viz., Hrishikesha, approved of that mark of love (for his friend) which the princess of Panchala, who also was his friend, showed.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: तत्र भीमादयस्ते तु कुरवो याजकाश्च ये॥ रेमुः श्रुत्वा विचित्रां तां धनंजयकथं शुभाम्।
en: Bhimasena and the other Kurus, including the sacrificial priests, who heard of the agrecable triumphs of Arjuna in course of his following the horse, became highly pleased.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: तेषां कथयतामेव पुरुषोऽर्जुनसंकथाः॥ उपायाद् वचनाद् दूतो विजयस्य महात्मनः।
en: While they were still engaged in talking about Arjuna a messenger came from that great hero bearing message from him.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: सोऽभिगम्य कुरुश्रेष्ठं नमस्कृत्य च बुद्धिमान्॥ उपायातं नरव्याघ्रं फाल्गुनं प्रत्यवेदयत्।
en: Going to the presence of the Kuru king, the intelligent messenger bowed his head in respect and informed him of the arrival of that foremost of men, viz., Phalguna.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: तच्छुत्वा नृपतिस्तस्य हर्षबाध्याकुलेक्षणः॥ प्रियाख्याननिमित्तं वै ददौ बहुधनं तदा।
en: On receipt of this news, tears of joy covered the king's eyes. Large gifts were made to the messenger for the very sweet tidings he had brought.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: ततो द्वितीये दिवसे महाशब्दो व्यवर्धत॥ आगच्छति नरव्याघ्ने कौरवाणां धुरंधरे।
en: On the second day forin that date, a loud din was heard when that foremost of men, tha chief of the Kurus camc.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: ततो रेणुः समुद्भूतो विवभौ तस्य वाजिनः॥ अभितो वर्तमानस्य यथोच्चैःश्रवसस्तथा।
en: as The dust raised by the hoofs of that horse as it walked close to Arjuna, looked as beautiful that raised by the celestial horse Uchchaishravas.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: तत्र हर्षकरी वाचो नराणां शुश्रुवेऽर्जुनः॥ दिष्ट्यासि पार्थकुशली धन्यो राजा युधिष्ठिरः।
en: And as Arjuna advanced, he heard many pleasing words uttered by the citizens. By good luck, O Partha, you are out of danger. Praise to king Yudhishthira.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: कोऽन्यो हि पृथिवीं कृत्स्ना जित्वा हि युधि पार्थिवान्। चारयित्वा हयश्रेष्ठमुपागच्छेदृतेऽर्जुनात्।
en: Who else than Arjuna could return after having caused the horse to wander over the whole Earth and after having defeated all the kings in battle?

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: ये व्यतीता महात्मानो राजानः सगरादयः॥ तेषामपीदृशं कर्म न कदाचन शुश्रुम।
en: We have not heard of such a feat having been done by even Sagara and other great kings of yore.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: नैतदन्ये करिष्यन्ति भविष्या वसुधाधिपाः॥ यत् त्वं कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ दुष्करं कृतवानसि।
en: Future kings also will never be able to perform so difficult a feat. O foremost one of Kuru's race, as this which you have done.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: इत्येवं वदतां तेषां पुंसां कर्णसुखा गिरः॥ शृण्वन् विवेश धर्मात्मा फाल्गुनो यज्ञसंस्तरम्।
en: Listening to such words, agrecable to the ear, of the citizens, the righteous souled Phalguna entered the sacrificial compound.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: ततो राजा सहामात्यः कृष्णश्च यदुनन्दनः॥ धृतराष्ट्र पुरस्कृत्य तं प्रत्युद्ययतुस्तदा।
en: Then king Yudhishthira with all his ministers, and Krishna, the delighter of the Yadus, placing Dhritarashtra in their van, went out for receiving Dhananjaya.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: सोऽभिवाद्य पितुः पादौ धर्मराजस्य धीमतः॥ भीमादींश्चापि सम्पूज्य पर्यध्वजत केशवम्।
en: Saluting the feet of his uncle (Dhritarashtra), and then of wise king Yudhishthira the just, and then adoring Bhima and others, he embraced Keshava.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: तैः समेत्यार्चितस्तांश्च प्रत्याथ यथा विधि॥ विशश्चाम महाबाहुस्तीरं लब्वेव पारगः। एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु स राजा बभ्रुवाहनः॥
en: Adored by them all and worshipping them in return according to due rites, the mightyarmed hero, accompanied by those princes, took rest like a ship-wrecked man tossed on the waves resting on reaching the shore.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: मातृभ्यां सहितो धीमान् कुरूनेव जगाम ह। तत्र वृद्धान् यथावत् स कुरूनन्यांश्च पार्थिवान्॥
en: Meanwhile the wise king Babhruvahana, accompanied by his mothers (Chitrangada and Ulupi), came to the Kuru capital.

description: Yudhishthira goes out to receive Arjuna
sn: अभिवाद्य महाबाहुस्तैश्चापि प्रतिनन्दितः। प्रविवेश पितामह्याः कुन्त्या भवनमुत्तमम्॥
en: The mighty-armed prince duly saluted all his elders of Kuru's race and the other kings present there, and was honored by them all in return, He then entered the excellent abode of his grandmother Kunti.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स प्रविश्य महाबाहुः पाण्डवानां निवेशनम्। पितामहीमभ्यवन्दत् साम्ना परमवल्गुना॥
en: Entering the palace of the Pandavas the mighty-armed prince saluted his grandmother in soothing and sweet words.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: ततश्चित्राङ्गदा देवी कौरव्यम्यात्मजापि च। पृथां कृष्णां च सहिते विनयेनोपजग्मतु॥ सुभद्रां च यथान्यायं याश्चान्याः कुरुयोषितः।
en: Then queen Chitrangada, and (Ulupi) the daughter of (the snake) Kauravya, together humbly approached Pritha and Krishna. They then met Subhadra and the other ladies of the Kuru race with due formalities.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: ददौ कुन्ती ततस्ताभ्यां रत्नानि विविधानि च॥ द्रौपदी च सुभद्रा च याश्चाप्यन्याऽददुः स्त्रियः।
en: Kunti gave them many gems and costly things. Draupadi and Subha 'ra and the other ladies of Kuru's race all made presents to them.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: ऊषतुस्तत्र ते देव्यौ महार्हशयनासने॥ सु पूजिते स्वयं कुन्त्या पार्थस्य हितकाम्यया।
en: The two ladies took up their residence there, using costly beds and seats, treated with affection and honor by Kunti herself from desire of doing what was agreeable to Partha.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: स च राजा महातेजाः पूजितो बभ्रुवाहनः॥ धृतराष्ट्रं महीपालमुपतस्थे यथाविधि।
en: King Babhruvahana of great energy, duly honored (by Kunti), then inet Dhritarashtra according to due rites.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: युधिष्ठिरं च राजानं भीमादींश्चापि पाण्डवान्॥ उपगम्य महातेजा विनयेनाभ्यवादयत्।
en: Going then to king Yudhishthira and Bhima and the other Pandavas the mighty prince of Munipura saluted them all with humility.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: स तैः प्रेम्या परिष्वक्तः पूजितश्च यथाविधि॥ धनं चास्मै ददुर्भूरि प्रीयमाणा महारथाः।
en: They all embraced him with great love and honored him duly. And those powerful carwarrior highly pleased with him, made large gifted of wealth to him.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: तथैव च महीपाल: कृष्णं चक्रगदाधरम्॥ प्रद्युम्न इव गोविन्दं विनयेनोपतस्थिवान्। तस्मै कृष्णो ददौ राज्ञे महार्हमतिपूजितम्॥
en: The king of Manipura then humbly approached Krishna, that hero armed with the discus and the mace, like a second Pradyumna approaching his father. Krishna gave to the king a very costly and excellent car adorned with gold and to which were yoked excellent horses.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: रथं हेमपरिष्कारं दिव्याश्वयुजमुत्तमम्। धर्मराजश्च भीमश्च फाल्गुनश्च यमौ तथा॥
en: Then king Yudhishthira the just, and Bhima, and Phalguna, and the twins, each separately honored him and made costly presents to him.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: पृथक् पृथक् च ते चैनं मानार्थाभ्यामयोजयन्। ततस्तृतीये दिवसे सत्यवत्यात्मजो मुनिः॥ युधिष्ठिरं समभ्येत्य वाग्मी वचनमब्रवीत्। अद्यप्रभृति कौन्तेय यजस्व समयो हि ते। मुहूर्तो यज्ञियः प्राप्तश्चोदयन्तीह याजकाः॥
en: On the third day, the sage Vyasa the son of Satyavati, that foremost of eloquent men, approaching Yudhishthira, said, From this day, O son of Kunti, do you begin your sacrifice. The time for it has come! The moment for undertaking the rite is at hand. The priests are urging you.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: अहीनो नाम राजेन्द्र क्रतुस्तेऽयं च कल्पताम्। बहुत्वात् काञ्चनाख्यस्य ख्यातो बहुसुवर्णकः॥
en: Let the sacrifice be performed in such a way that no limb may become defective. On account of the very large quantity of gold that is required for this sacrifice, it has come to be called the sacrifice of profuse gold.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: एवमत्र महाराज दक्षिणां त्रिगुणां कुरु। त्रित्वं व्रजतु ते राजन् ब्राह्मणा ह्यत्र कारणम्॥
en: Do you also, O great king, make the Dakshina of this sacrifice three times of what is enjoined. Let the merit of your sacrifice increase threefold. The Brahimanas competent for the purpose.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: त्रीनश्चमेधानत्र त्वं सम्प्राप्य बहुदक्षिणान्। ज्ञातिवध्याकृतं पापं प्रहास्यसि नराधिप॥
en: Acquiring the merits then of three HorseSacrifices, each with profuse presents, you shall be freed, O king, from the sin of having killed your kinsmen.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: पवित्रं परमं चैतत् पावनं चैतदुत्तमम्। यदाश्वमेधावभृथं प्राप्स्यसे कुरुनन्दन॥
en: The bath which one performs upon completion of the Horse-Sacrifice, O king, is highly powerful and productive of the highest merit. That merit will be yours, O king of Kuru's race. are

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: इत्युक्तः स तु तेजस्वी व्यासेनामितबुद्धिना। दीक्षां विवेश धर्मात्मा वाजिमेधाप्तये ततः॥
en: Thus addressed by Vyasa of incomparable intelligence, the righteous-souled Yudhishthria of great energy underwent the initiation for performance of the Horse-Sacrifice.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: ततो यज्ञं महाबाहुर्वाजिमेधं महाक्रतुम्। बह्वन्नदक्षिणं राजा सर्वकामगुणान्वितम्॥
en: The mighty-armed king then performed the great Horse-Sacrifice characterised by gifts of food and presents in profusion and capable of fructifying every desire and producing cvery merit.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: तत्र वेदविदो राजंश्चक्रुः कर्माणि याजकाः। परिक्रमन्तः सर्वज्ञा विधिवत् साधुशिक्षितम्॥
en: The priests, well-conversant with the Vedas, did every rite, duly, moving about in all directions. They were all well-trained, and possessed of omniscience.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: न तेषां स्खलितं किंचिदासीच्चाप्यकृतं तथा। क्रममुक्तं च युक्तं च चक्रुस्तत्र द्विजर्षभाः॥
en: In nothing was there any deviation from the ordinances, and nothing was done improperly. Those foremost of twice-born persons followed the procedure as laid down as it should be followed in those points about which no directions are given.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: कृत्वा प्रवर्ये धर्माख्यं यथावद् द्विजसत्तमाः। चक्रुस्ते विधिवद् राजंस्तथेवाभिषवं द्विजाः॥
en: Thosc best of twice-born ones, having first performed the rite called Pravargya otherwise called Dharma, then duly performed the rite of Abhishva, O king.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: अभिषूय ततो राजन् सोमं सोमपसत्तमाः। सवनान्यानुपूर्येण चक्रुः शास्त्रानुसारिणः॥
en: Those foremost of Soma-Drinkers, O monarch, extracting the juice of the Soma, then performed the Savana rite, following the injunctions of the scriptures.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: न तत्र कृपणः कश्चिन्न दरिद्रो बभूव ह। क्षुधितो दुःखितो वापि प्राकृतो वापि मानवः॥
en: Among those who came to that sacrifice none could be seen who was cheerless, none who was poor, none who was hungry, none who was plunged into grief, and none that seemed to be vulgar.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: भोजनं भोजनार्थिभ्यो दापयामास शत्रुहा। भीमसनो महातेजाः सततं राजशासनात्॥
en: Bhimasena of great energy, at the command of the king, caused food to be ceaselessly distributed among those who desired to eat.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: संस्तरे कुशलाश्चापि सर्वकार्याणि याजकाः। दिवसे दिवसे चक्रुर्यथाशास्त्रानुदर्शनात्॥
en: Following the injunctions of the scriptures, priests, well-versed in sacrificial rites of every kind, performed every day all the acts necessary to complete the great sacrifice.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: नाषडङ्गविदत्रासीत् सदस्यस्तस्य धीमतः। नाव्रतो नानुपाध्यायो न च वादाविचक्षणः॥
en: Amongst the Sadasyas of king Yudhishthira of great intelligence there was none who was not a master of the six branches of (Vedic) learning. There was none among them who was not an otserver of vows, none who was not an Upadhaya; none, who was not wellversed in dialectical disputations.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: ततो यूपोच्छ्ये प्राप्ते घड् बैल्वान् भरतर्षभ। खादिरान् बिल्वसमितांस्तावतः सर्ववर्णिनः॥
en: When the time came for erccting the sacrificial stake, O chief of Bharata's race, six stakes were set up which were made of Bilva, six which were made of Khadira, and six which were made of Sarvavarnin.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: देवदारुमयौ द्वौ तु यूपौ कुरुपतेर्मखे। श्लेष्मातकमयं चैकं याजका: समकल्पयन्॥
en: Two stakes were set up by the priest which were made of Devadaru in that sacrifice of the Kuru king, and one which was made of Shleshmataka.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: शोभार्थं चापरान यूपान् काञ्चनान् भरतर्षभ। स भीमः कारयामास धर्मराजस्य शासनात्॥
en: At the bchest of the king, Bhima caused some other stakes to be set up, for the sake of beauty only which were made of goid.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: ते व्यराजन्त राजर्षेर्वासोभिरुपशोभिताः। महेन्द्रानुगता देवा यथा सप्तर्षिभिर्दिवि।॥
en: Adorned with fine cloths supplied by the royal sage, those stakes shone there like Indra and the deities with the seven celestial Rishis standing around them in Heaven.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: इष्टका: काञ्चनीश्चात्र चयनार्थं कृताऽभवन्। शुशुभे चयनं तच्च दक्षस्येव प्रजापतेः॥
en: A number of golden bricks were made for making therewith a Chayana. The Chayana made resembled in beauty that which had been made for Daksha, the lord of creatures.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: चतुश्चित्यश्च तस्यासीदष्टादशकरात्मकः। स रुक्मपक्षो निचितस्त्रिकोणो गरुडाकृतिः॥
en: The Chayana measured eight and ten cubits and had four stories or lairs. A golden bird, of the shape of Garuda, was then made, having three angles.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: ततो नियुक्ताः पशवो यथाशास्त्रं मनीषिभिः। तं तं देवं समुद्दिश्य पक्षिणः पशवश्च ये॥
en: Following the injunctions of the scriptures, the priests endued with great learning then duly tied to the stakes both animals and birds, assigning each to its particular deity.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: ऋषभाः शास्त्रपठितास्तथा जलचराश्च ये। सर्वोस्तानभ्ययुजस्ते तत्राग्निचयकर्मणि॥
en: Bulls, possessed of such marks as are mentioned in the scriptures, and aquatic animals were properly tied to the stakes after the rites of the sacrificial fire had been performed.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: यूपेषु नियता चासीत् पशूनां त्रिशती तथा। अश्वरत्नोत्तरा यज्ञे कौन्तेयस्य महात्मनः॥
en: In that sacrifice of the great son of Kunti, three hundred animals were tied to the stakes set up, including that foremost of horses.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: स यज्ञः शुशुभे तस्य साक्षाद् देवर्षिसंकुलः। गन्धर्वगणसंगीतः प्रवृत्तोप्सरसां गणैः॥
en: That sacrifice looked greatly beautiful as if adorned with the celestial Rishis, with the Gandharvas singing in chorus and the various tribes of Apsaras dancing in merriment.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: स किंपुरुषसंकीर्णः किंनरैश्चोपशोभितः। सिद्धविप्रनिवासैश्च समन्तादभिसंवृतः॥
en: It teemed, besides, with Kimpurushas and was adorned with Kinnaras. All around it were houses of Brahinanas crowned with ascetic success.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: तस्मिन् सदसि नित्यास्तु व्यासशिष्या द्विजर्षभाः। सर्वशास्त्रप्रणेतारः कुशला यज्ञसंस्तरे॥
en: There were daily seen the disciples of Vyasa, those foremost of twice-born ones, who are compilers of all branches of learning, and well conversant with sacrificial rites.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: नारदश्च बभूवात्र तुम्बुरश्च महाद्युतिः। विश्वावसुश्चित्रसेनस्तथान्ये गीतकोविदाः॥
en: There was Narada, and there was Tunburu of great splendour. There were Vishvavasu and Chitrasena and others, all of whom were proficient in music.

description: The arrival of Babruvahana, Chitrangada and Ulupi
sn: गन्धर्वा गीतकुशला नृत्येषु च विशारदाः। रमयन्ति स्म तान् विप्रान् यज्ञकर्मान्तरेषु वै॥
en: At intervals of the sacrificial rites, those Gandharvas skilled in music and well-versed in dancing, used to please the Brahmanas who were engaged in the sacrifice.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रपयित्वा पशूनन्यान् विधिवद् द्विजसत्तमाः। तं तुरङ्गं यथाशास्त्रमालभन्त द्विजातयः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having cooked, according to due rites, the other excellent animals which were sacrificed, the priests then sacrificed, according to the injunctions of the scriptures, that horse (which had wandered over the whole world).

sn: ततः संश्रप्य तुरगं विधिवद् याजकास्तदा। उपसंवेशयन् राजंस्ततस्तां दुपदात्मजाम्।॥ कलाभिस्तिसृभी राजन् यथाविधि मनस्विनीम्।
en: After cutting that horse into pieces, according to scriptural directions, they caused Draupadi of great intelligence, who was possessed of the three requisites of Mantras, things, and devotion, to sit near the divided animal.

sn: उद्धृत्य तु वपा तस्य यथाशास्त्रं द्विजातयः॥ श्रपयामासुरव्यग्रा विधिवद् भरतर्षभ।
en: The Brahmanas then, with cool minds, taking up the marrow of that horse, cooked it duly, O chief of Bharata's race.

sn: तं वपाधूमगन्धं तु धर्मराजः सहानुजैः॥ उपजिघ्रद् यथाशास्त्रं सर्वपापापहं तदा।
en: King Yudhishthira the just, with all his younger brothers, then smelled, according to the scriptures, the smoke, capable of purging one from every sin, of the marrow that was thus cooked.

sn: शिष्टान्यङ्गानि यान्यासं स्तस्याश्वस्य नराधिप।॥ तान्यग्नौ जुहबु/राः समस्ताः षोडशार्विजः।
en: The remaining limbs, O king, of that horse, were poured into the fire by the sixteen sacrificial priests possessed of great wisdom.

sn: संस्थाप्यैवं तस्य राज्ञस्तं यज्ञं शक्रतेजसः॥ व्यासः स शिष्यो भगवान् वर्धयामासं तं नृपम्।
en: Having thus completed the sacrifice of that monarch who was gifted with the energy of Shakra himself, the illustrious Vyasa with his disciples eulogised the king greatly.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरः प्रादाद् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यथाविधि॥ कोटी: सहस्रं निष्काणां व्यासाय तु वसुंधराम्।
en: Then Yudhishthira gave away to the Brahmanas a thousand crores of golden nishkas, and to Vyasa he gave away the whole Earth.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य धरां राजन् व्यास: सत्यवतीसुतः॥ अब्रवीद् भरतश्रेष्ठं धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। वसुधा भवतस्त्वेषा संन्यस्ता राजसत्तम॥ निष्क्रयो दीयतां मह्यं ब्राह्मणा हि धनार्थिनः।
en: Satyavati's son Vyasa, having accepted the Earth, addressed that foremost one of Bharata's race, viz., king Yudhishthira the just, and said, O best of kings, the Earth which you have given me I return to you! Do you give me the purchasing value, for Brahmanas are desirous of wealth.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु तान् विप्रान् प्रत्युवाच महामनाः॥ भ्रातृभिः सहितो धीमान् मध्ये राज्ञां महात्मनाम्।
en: The great Yudhishthria of great intelligence staying with his brothers in the midst of the kings invited to his sacrifice, said to those Brahmanas:

sn: अश्वमेधे महायज्ञे पृथिवी दक्षिणा स्मृता॥ अर्जुनेन जिता चेयमृत्विग्भ्यः प्रापिता मया।
en: The Dakshina ordained in the scriptures for the great Horse-Sacrifice is the Earth, Hence, I have given away to the sacrificial priests the Earth conquered by Arjuna.

sn: वनं प्रवेक्ष्ये विप्राग्र्या विभजध्वं महीमिमाम्॥ चतुर्धा पृथिवीं कृत्वा चातुर्होत्रप्रमाणतः।
en: You foremost of Brahmanas, I shall enter the forest. Do you divide the Earth among yourselves! Indeed, do you divide the Earth into four parts according to what is done in the Chaturhotra-Sacrifice.

sn: नाहमादातुमिच्छामि ब्रह्मस्वं द्विजसत्तमाः॥ इदं नित्यं मनो विप्रा भ्रातृणां चैव मे सदा। इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंस्तु भ्रातरो द्रौपदी च सा॥ एवमेतदिति प्राहुस्तदभूल्लोमहर्षणम्।
en: You best of twice-born ones, I do not wish to appropriate what now belongs to the Brahmanas. This, you learned Brahmanas, has been the intention of myself and my brothers. When the king said these words, his brothers and Draupadi also said, Yes, it is even so. Grcat was the sensation created by this announcement.

sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षो धागासीत् साधु साध्विति भारत॥ तथैव द्विजसंघानां शंसतां विवभौ स्वनः।
en: Then, O Bharata, an invisible voice was heard in the sky, saying, 'Excellent, Excellent!' The murmurs, also, of crowd of Brahmanas as they spoke, arose.

sn: द्वैपायनस्तथा कृष्णः पुनरेव युधिष्ठिरम्॥ प्रोवाच मध्ये विप्राणामिदं सम्पूजयन् मुनिः। दत्तैषां भवता मह्यं तां ते प्रतिददाम्यहम्॥ हिरण्यं दीयतामेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धरास्तु ते।
en: The Island-born Krishna, highly applauding him, once more addressed Yudhishthira, before the Brahmanas, saying, "The Earth has been given by you to me!' I, however, give her back to you! Do you give to these Brahmanas gold. Let the Earth be yours!'

sn: ततोऽब्रवीद् वासुदेवो धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥ यथाऽऽह भगवान् व्यासस्तथा त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि।
en: Then Vasudeva, addressing king Yudhishthira the just, said, You should do as you are ordered by the illustrious Vyasa.'

sn: इत्युक्तः स कुरुश्रेष्ठः प्रीतात्मा भ्रातृभिः सह॥ कोटिकोटिकृतां प्रादाद् दक्षिणां त्रिगुणां क्रतोः।
en: Thus addressed, that foremost one of Kuru's race, along with all his brothers, became pleased and gave away millions of golden coins, in fact, trebling the Dakshina ordained for the Horse-Sacrifice,

sn: न करिष्यति तल्लोके कश्चिदन्यो नराधिपः॥ यत् कृतं कुरुराजेन मरुत्तस्यानुकुर्वता।
en: No other king will be able to accomplish what the Kuru king did on that occasion like Marutta.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य तु तद् रत्नं कृष्णद्वैपायनो मुनिः॥ ऋत्विग्भ्यः प्रददौ विद्वांश्चतुर्धा व्यभजंश्च ते।
en: Accepting that wealth, the Island-born sage, Krishna, of great learning, gave it to the sacrificial priests, dividing it into four parts.

sn: धरण्या निष्क्रयं दत्त्वा तद्धिरण्यं युधिष्ठिरः॥ धूतपापो जितस्वर्गो मुमुदे भ्रातृभिः सह।
en: Having paid that wealth as the price of the Earth, Yudhishthira, purged of his sins and assured of Heaven, rejoiced with his brothers.

sn: ऋत्विजस्तमपर्यन्तं सुवर्णनिचयं तथा॥ व्यभजन्त द्विजातिभ्यो यथोत्साहं यथासुखम्।
en: The sacrificial priests, having got that unlimited quantity of riches, distributed it among the Brahmanas gladly and according to the desire of each recipient.

sn: यज्ञवाटे च यत् किंचिद्धिरण्यं सविभूषणम्॥ तोरणानि च यूपांश्च घटान् पात्रीस्तथेष्टकाः।
en: The Brahmanas, also divided amongst themselves, according to Yudhishthira's permission, the various ornaments of gold which were in the sacrificial compound, including the triumphal arches, the stakes, the jars, and various kinds of vessels.

sn: युधिष्ठिराभ्यनुज्ञाताः सर्वं तद् व्यभजन् द्विजाः।।२५ अनन्तरं द्विजातिभ्यः क्षत्रिया जहिरे वसु।
en: After the Brahmanas had taken as much as they wished, the wealth that remained was taken away by Kshatriyas and Vaishyas and Shudras and various tribes of Mlecchas.

sn: तथा विट्शूद्र संघाश्च तथान्ये म्लेच्छजातयः॥ ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे मुदिता जग्मुरालयान्।
en: Thus pleased with presents inade by king Yudhishthira of great intelligence, the Brahmanas, filled with joy, returned to their respective abodes.

sn: तर्पिता वसुना तेन धर्मराजेन धीमता॥ स्वमंशं भगवान् व्यासः कुन्त्यै साक्षाद्धि मानतः।
en: The holy and illustrious Vyasa respectfully presented his own share, which was very large, of that gold to Kunti.

sn: प्रददौ तस्य महतो हिरण्यस्य महाद्युतिः॥ श्वशुरात् प्रीतिदायं तं प्राप्य सा प्रीतमानसा।
en: Receiving that gift of affection from her father-in-law, Pritha became pleased and devoted it to the performance of various acts of merit.

sn: चकार पुण्यकं तेन सुमहत् संघशः पृथा॥ गत्वा त्ववभृथं राजा विपाप्मा भ्रातृभिः सह।
en: King Yudhishthira, having bathed at the conclusion of his sacrifice and become purged of all his sins, shone in the midst of his brothers, honoured by all, like the king of the deitics in the midst of the dwellers of the celestial region.

sn: सभाज्यमानः शुशुभे महेन्द्रस्त्रिदशैरिव॥ पाण्डवाश्च महीपालैः समेतैरभिसंवृताः।
en: The sons of Pandu, surrounded by the assembled kings, looked as beautiful, O king, as the planets in the midst of the stars.

sn: अशोभन्त महाराज ग्रहास्तारागणैरिव॥ राजभ्योऽपि ततः प्रादाद् रत्नानि विविधानि च। गजानश्वानलं कारान् स्त्रियो वासांसि काञ्चनम्।।३२
en: To those kings they made presents of various jewels and gems, and elephants and horses and ornaments of gold, and female slaves and cloths and immense quantity of gold.

sn: तद् धनौघमपर्यन्तं पार्थः पार्थिवमण्डले। विसृजशुशुभे राजन् यथा वैश्रवणस्तथा ॥
en: Indeed, Prithas son, by distributing that untold riches among the invited kings, shone, O king, like Vaishravana, the lord of riches.

sn: आनीय च तथा वीरं राजानं बभ्रुवाहनम्। प्रदाय विपुलं वित्तं गृहान् प्रास्थापयत् तदा॥
en: Summoning next the heroic king Babhruvahana, Yudhishthira, gave to him various kinds of wealth in profusion and gave him permission to return home.

sn: दुःशलायाश्च तं पौत्रं बालकं भरतर्षभ। स्वराज्येऽथ पितुर्थीमान् स्वसुः प्रीत्या न्यवेशयत्।।३५
en: The son of Pandu, for pleasing his sister Dushala, established her infant grandson in his paternal kingdom.

sn: नृपतींश्चैव तान् सर्वान् सुविभक्तान् सुपूजितान्। प्रस्थापयामास वशी कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: The Kuru king Yudhishthira, having a full mastery over his senses, than dismissed the assembled kings all of whom had been properly classed and honoured by him.

sn: गोविन्दं च महात्मानं बलदेवं महाबलम्। तथान्यान् वृष्णिवीरांश्च प्रद्युम्नाद्यान् सहस्रशः॥ पूजयित्वा महाराज यथाविधि महाद्युतिः। भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजा प्रास्थापयदरिंदमः॥
en: The illustrious son of Pandu, that chastiser of foes, then duly adored the great Govinda and Baladeva of great power and the thousands of other Vrishni heroes having Pradyumna for their first. Assisted by his brothers, he then dismissed them for returning to Dwraka.

sn: एवं बभूव यज्ञः स धर्मराजस्य धीमतः। बबन्नधनरलौघः सुरामैरेयसागरः॥
en: Thus was celebrated that sacrifice of king Yudhishthira the just, which was distinguished by a profusion of flood and wealth and jewels and gems, and oceans of wines of different kinds.

sn: सर्पि:पङ्का ह्दा यत्र बभूवुश्चान्नपर्वताः। रसालाकर्दमा नद्यो बभूवुर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: There were lakes whose mire consisted of clarified butter and mountains of food. There were, also, O chief of Bharata's race, miry rivers made of drinks having the six kinds of taste.

sn: भक्ष्यखाण्डवरागाणां क्रिबतां भुज्यतां तथा। पशूनां बध्यतां चैव नान्तं ददृशिरे जनाः॥
en: Of men employed in making and eating the sweetmeats called Khandavaragas, and of animals killed for food, there was no end.

sn: मत्तप्रमत्तमुदितं सुप्रीतयुवतीजनम्। मृदङ्गशङ्खनादैश्च मनोरममभूत् तदा॥
en: The vast compound was filled with men inebriated with wine, and with young ladies filled with joy. The extensive grounds constantly echocd with the sounds of drums and the blare of conchs. With all these, the sacrifice became highly delightful.

sn: दीयतां भुज्यतां चेष्टं दिवारात्रमवारितम्। तं महोत्सवसंकाशं हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलम्॥ कथयन्ति स्म पुरुषा नानादेशनिवासिनः।
en: 'Let agreeable things be given away,' 'Let agreeable food be eaten.' These were the sounds which were repeatedly heard day and night in that sacrifice. It was like a great festival, full of rejoicing and contented men. People of various kingdoms speak of that sacrifice to this day.

sn: वर्षित्वा धनधाराभिः कामै रत्नै रसैस्तथा। विपाप्मा भरतश्रेष्ठः कृतार्थः प्राविशत् पुरम्॥
en: Having showered wealth in torrents, and various objects of desire, and jewels and gems, and drinks of various kinds, the foremost one of Bharata's race, purged of all his sins, and his purpose fulfilled, entered his capital. Having showered wealth in torrents, and various objects of desire, and jewels and gems, and drinks of various kinds, the foremost one of Bharata's race, purged of all his sins, and his purpose fulfilled, entered his capital.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच पितामह मे यज्ञे धर्मराजस्य धीमतः। यदाश्चर्यमभूत् किंचित् तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Janamejaya said. You should tell me of any wonderful incident which took place in the sacrifice of my grandsire.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रूयतां राजशार्दूल महदाश्चर्यमुत्तमम्। अश्वमेधे महायज्ञे निवृत्ते यदभूत् प्रभो॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hear, O chief of kings, of a most wonderful event which took place, O powerful monarch, at the conclusion of that great Horse-Sacrifice.

sn: तर्पितेषु द्विजाग्येषु ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिबन्धुषु। दीनान्धकृपणे वापि तदा भरतसत्तम॥ घुष्यमाणे महादाने दिक्षु सर्वासु भारत। पतत्सु पुष्पवर्षेषु धर्मराजस्य मूर्धनि॥ नीलाक्षस्तत्र नकुलो रुक्मपार्श्वस्तदानघ। वज्राशनिसमं नादममुञ्चद वसुधाधिप॥
en: On all the foremost of Brahmanas and all the kinsmen and relatives and friends, and all the poor, the blind, and the helpless ones, being gratified, O chief of Bharata's race, when the gifts made in profusion were being spoken of on all sides, indeed, when flowers were rained down on the head of king Yudhishthira the just, a blue-eyed mungoose, O sinless one, with one side of his body converted into gold, came there and spoke a voice that was as loud and deep as thunder.

sn: सकृदुत्सृज्य तन्नादं त्रासयानो मृगद्विजान्। मानुषं वचनं प्राह धृष्टो विलशयो महान्॥ सक्तुप्रस्थेन वो नायं यज्ञस्तुल्यो नराधिपाः। उच्छवृत्तेर्वदान्यस्य कुरुक्षेत्रनिवासिनः॥
en: Repeatedly uttering such deep sounds and thereby frightening all animals and birds, that proud dweller of a hole, with large body, spoke in a human voice and said, “You kings, this great sacrifice is not equal to a prastha of powdered daily given away by a liberal Brahmana of Kurukshetra who was observing the Unchcha vow.

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा नकुलस्य विशाम्पते। विस्मयं परमं जग्मुः सर्वे ते ब्राह्मणर्षभाः॥
en: Hearing these words of the mongoose, o king, all those foremost of Brahmanas became stricken with wonder.

sn: ततः समेत्य नकुलं पर्यपृच्छन्त ते द्विजाः। कुतस्त्वं समनुप्राप्तो यज्ञं साधुसमागमम्॥
en: Approaching the mongoose, they then asked him, saying, 'Whence have you come to this sacrifice this resort of the good and the pious?
