sn: किं बलं परमं तुभ्यं किं श्रुतं किं परायणम्। कथं भवन्तं विद्याम यो नो यज्ञं विगर्हसे।।१०
en: What is the extent of your power? What you learning? And what your refuge? How should we know you who thus censure this our sacrifice?

sn: अविलुप्यागमं कृत्स्नं विविधैर्यज्ञियैः कृतम्। यथागमं यथान्यायं कर्तव्यं च तथा कृतम्॥
en: Without having disregarded any portion of the scriptures, everything that should be done has been done here according to the scriptures and according to reason, with the help of various sacrificial rites.

sn: पूजार्हाः पूजिताश्चाव विधिवच्छास्त्रदर्शनात्। मन्त्राहुतिहुतश्चाग्निर्दत्तं देयममत्सरम्॥
en: Those who are deserving of adoration, have been duly adored here according to the way pointed out by the scriptures. Libations have bcen poured on the sacred fire with the help of proper Mantras. That which should be given, has been given away without pride.

sn: तुष्टा द्विजातयश्चात्र दानैर्बहुविधैरपि। क्षत्रियाश्च सुयुद्धेन श्राद्धैश्चापि पितामहाः॥
en: The twice-born class have been pleased with gifts of various kinds. The Kshatriyas have been pleased with battles fought according to just methods. The grandfathers have been pleased with Sharaddhas,

sn: पालनेन विशस्तुष्टाः कामैस्तुष्टा वरस्त्रियः। अनुक्रोशैस्तथा शूद्रा दानशेषैः पृथग्जनाः॥
en: The Vaishyas have been pleased by the protection offered to them, and many foremost of women have been pleased by accomplishing their desires. The Shudras have been pleased b y kind speeches, and others with the residue of the profuse wealth collected on the spot.

sn: ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिनस्तुष्टाः शौचेन च नृपस्य नः। देवा हविर्भिः पुण्यैश्च रक्षणैः शरणागताः॥
en: Kinsmen and relatives have been pleased by the purity of conduct shown by our king. The celestials have been pleased by libations of clarified butter and acts of merit, and dependents and followers by protection.

sn: यदत्र तथ्यं तद् ब्रूहि सत्यं सत्यं द्विजातिषु। यथाश्रुतं यथादृष्टं पृष्टो ब्राह्मणकाम्यया॥
en: That, therefore, which is true, do you truly declare to these Brahmanas. Indeed, do you declare what is according to the scriptures and to actual experience, asked by the Brahmanas who are eager to know.

sn: श्रद्धेयवाक्यः प्राज्ञस्त्वं दिव्यं रूपं बिभर्षि च। समागतश्च विप्रैस्त्वं तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Your words are creditable. You are wise. You have have, also, a celestial form. You have come into the midst of learned Brahmanas. You should explain yourself.'

sn: इति पृष्टो द्विजैस्तैः स प्रहसन् नकुलोऽब्रवीत्। नैषा मृषा मया वाणी प्रोक्ता दर्पण वा द्विजाः॥
en: Thus addressed by those twice-born persons, the mungoose, siniling, answered them as follows. “You twice-born ones, the words I have uttered are not false. Neither have I spoken them from pride.

sn: यन्मयोक्तमिदं वाक्यं युष्माभिश्चाप्युपश्रुतम्। सक्तुप्रस्थेन वो नायं यज्ञस्तुल्यो द्विजर्षभाः॥
en: You have all heard what I have said. You foremost of twice-born persons, this sacrifice is not equal in merit to the gift of a prastha of powdered barley.

sn: इत्यवश्यं मयैतद् वो वक्तव्यं द्विजसत्तमाः। शृणुताव्यग्रमनसः शंसतो मे यथातथम्॥
en: Forsooth, I should say this, O focmost of Brahmanas. Listen to me with rapt attention as I truly describe to you what took place.

sn: अनुभूतं च दृष्टं च यन्मयादुतमुत्तमम्। उच्छवृत्तेर्वदान्यस्य कुरुक्षेत्रनिवासिनः॥
en: Wonderful and excellent was the event that happened. It was seen by me and its consequences were felt by me. The incident relates to a liberal Brahmana living in Kurukshetra in the observance of the Unchcha VOW.

sn: स्वर्ग येन द्विजाः प्राप्तः सभार्यः ससुतस्नुषः। यथा चाघ शरीरस्य ममेदं काञ्चनीकृतम्॥
en: On account of that incident he attained to Heaven, O twice-born ones, along with his wife and son and daughter-in-law. And in consequence of what then took place half my body became changed into gold.

sn: नकुल उवाच हन्त वो वर्तयिष्यामि दानस्य फलमुत्तमम्। न्यायलब्धस्य सूक्ष्मस्य विप्रदत्तस्य यद् द्विजाः॥
en: The Mungoose continued : O twice-born ones, I shall presently tell you what the excellent fruit was of the gift, made by a Brahmana, of a very little measure (of powdered barley) acquired by fair means.

sn: धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे धर्मज्ञैर्बहुभिर्वृते। उच्छवृत्तिर्द्विजः कश्चित् कापोतिरभवत् तदा॥
en: On that righteous spot of ground known by the name of Kurukshetra, which is the habitation of many righteous persons, there lived a Brahmana observing the Unchcha vow. That mode of living is like that of the pigeon.

sn: सभार्यः सह पुत्रेण सस्नुषस्तपसि स्थितः। बभूव शुक्वृत्तः स धर्मात्मा नियतेन्द्रियः॥
en: He lived there with his wife and son and daughter-in-law and practiced penances. Of righteous soul and with senses completely controlled, he adopted the mode of living which is followed by a parrot.

sn: षष्ठे काले सदा विप्रो भुडन्तै तैः सह सुव्रतः। षष्ठे काले कदाचित् तु तस्याहारो न विद्यते॥ भुक्तेऽन्यस्मिन् कदाचित् स षष्ठे काले द्विजोत्तमः। कदाचिद् धर्मिणस्तस्य दुर्भिक्षे सति दारुणे॥ नाविद्यत तदा विप्राः संचयस्तन्निबोधता क्षीणौषधिसमावेशे द्रव्यहीनोऽभवत् तदा॥
en: Of excellent vows, he used to cat every day at the sixth division. If there was nothing to eat at the sixth division of the day, that excellent Brahmana would fast for that day and eat the next day at the sixth division. On one occasion, you Brahmanas, there took place a dreadful famine in the land. During that time there was nothing stored in the abode of that righteous Brahmana. The herbs and plants were all dried up and the whole kingdom became void of food-stores.

sn: काले कालेऽस्य सम्प्राप्ते नैव विद्येत भोजनम्। क्षुधापरिगताः सर्वे प्रातिष्ठन्त तदा तु ते॥
en: When the habitual hours came for eating, the Brahmana had nothing to eat. This happened day after day. All the members of his family were stricken with hunger but were obliged to pass the days as best they could.

sn: उच्छं तदा शुक्लपक्षे मध्यं तपति भास्करे। उष्णार्तश्च क्षुधार्तश्च विप्रस्तपसि संस्थितः॥
en: One day, in the month of Jyaishtha, while the Sun was in the meridian, the Brahman was engaged, in picking up grains of corn. Afflicted by heat and hunger, he was practicing this penance.

sn: उज्छमप्राप्तवानेव ब्राह्मणः क्षुच्छ्रमान्वितः। स तथैव क्षुधाविष्टः सार्धं परिजनेन ह॥
en: Unable to obtain of corn, the Brahmana soon became exhausted with hunger and toil. Indeed, with all the members of his family, he had no food to eat.

sn: क्षपयामास तं कालं कृच्छ्रप्राणो द्विजोत्तमः। अथ षष्ठे गते काले यवप्रस्थमुपार्जयन्॥
en: That best of Brahmanas passed the days in terrible suffering. One day, after the sixth division came, he succeeded in getting a prastha of barley.

sn: यवप्रस्थं तु तं सक्तूनकुर्वन्त तपस्विनः। कृतजप्याह्निकास्ते तु हुत्वा चार्नि यथाविधि॥ कुडवं कुडवं सर्वे व्यभजन्त तपस्विनः। अथागच्छद् द्विजः कश्चिदतिथिर्भुञ्जतां तदा।॥
en: That barley was then reduced by those ascetics to powder for making what is called Saktu of it. Having finished their silent recitations and other daily rites, and having duly poured libations on the sacred fire, those ascetics divided that little quantity of powdered barley amongst them selves so that the share of each came up to the measure of Kudava (twelve double handfuls). As they were about to sit down for cating, there came to their abode a guest.

sn: ते तं दृष्ट्वातिथिं प्राप्तं प्रहृष्टमनसोऽभवन्। तेऽभिवाद्य सुखप्रश्न पृष्ट्वा तमतिथि तदा॥
en: Seeing the person who came as a guest, all of them became highly pleased. Indeed, seeing him, they saluted him and made the usual inquiries of health and happiness.

sn: विशुद्धमनसो दान्ताः श्रद्धादमसमन्विताः। अनसूयवो विक्रोधाः साधवो वीतमत्सराः॥
en: They were of pure minds, self-controlled, and gifted with faith and control over the passions. Freed from malice, they all conquered anger. Possessed of piety, they were never pained at seeing other people's happiness.

sn: त्यक्तमानमदक्रोधा धर्मज्ञा द्विजसत्तमाः। स ब्रह्मचर्यं गोत्रं ते तस्य ख्यात्वा परस्परम्॥ कुटी प्रवेशयामासुः क्षुधार्तमतिथिं तदा। इदमर्थ्य च पाद्यं च वृसी चेयं तवानघ॥
en: They had renounced pride and haughtiness and anger. Indeed, they knew every duty, O foremost of twice-born ones! Informing their guest of their own penances and of the race or family to which they belonged, and ascertaining from him in return those particulars, they caused that hungry guest of theirs to enter their cottage. Addressing him they said, This is the Arghya for you. This water is for washing your feet. There are scattered some Kusha grass for your seat, O sinless one.

sn: शुचयः सक्तवश्चमे नियमोपार्जिताः प्रभो। प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भद्रं ते मया दत्ता द्विजर्षभ॥
en: Here is some clean Saktu acquired by lawful means, O powerful one! Given by us, O foremost of twice-born persons, do you accept it.

sn: इत्युक्तः प्रतिगृह्याथ सक्तूनां कुडवं द्विजः। भक्षयामास राजेन्द्र न च तुष्टि जगाम सः॥
en: Thus addressed by them, that Brahmana accepted the Kudava (twelve double handfuls) of powdered barley which was offered to him and ate it all. But his hunger, O king, was not satisfied with what he ate.

sn: स उच्छवृत्तिस्तं प्रेक्ष्य क्षुधापरिगतं द्विजम्। आहारं चिन्तयामास कथं तुष्टो भवेदिति॥
en: The Brahmana while observing the Unchcha vow, seeing that his guest's hunger was still unsatisfied, began to think of what other food he could place before him for pleasing him.

sn: तस्य भार्याब्रवीद् वाक्यं मद्भागो दीयतामिति। गच्छत्वेष यथाकामं परितुष्टो द्विजोत्तमः॥
en: Then his wife said to him. Let my share be given to him! Let this foremost of twice-born persons be pleased and let him then go wherever he will.

sn: इति ब्रुवन्तीं तां साध्वी भार्यां स द्विजसत्तमः। क्षुधापरिगतां ज्ञात्वा तान् सक्तून् नाभ्यनन्दत॥
en: Knowing that his chaste wife who said so, was herself stricken with hunger, that best of Brahmanas could not approve of her share of the powdered barley being given to the guest.

sn: आत्मानुमायो विद्वान् स तु विप्रर्षभस्तदा। जानन् वृद्धां क्षुधा” च श्रान्तां ग्लानां तपस्विनीम्।४४ त्वगस्थिभूतां वेपन्तीं ततो भार्यामुवाच ह। अपि कीटपतङ्गानां मृगाणां चैव शोभने॥ स्त्रियो रक्ष्याश्च पोषयाश्च न त्वेवं वक्तुमर्हसि। अनुकम्प्यो नरः पल्या पुष्टो रक्षित एव च॥
en: Indeed, that best of Brahmanas endued with learning, knowing from his own state that his aged, toil-worn, cheerless, and helpless wife was herself afflicted by hunger, and seeing that lady who had been emaciated into mere skin and bones, was quivering with weakness, addressed her and said, 'O beautiful one, with even animals, with even worms and insects, wives are fed and protected. You should not, therefore, say so. The wife treats her husband with kindness and feeds and protects him.

sn: प्रपतेद् यशसे दीप्तात् स च लोकान् न चाप्नुयात्। धर्मकामार्थकार्याणि शुश्रूषा कुलसंततिः॥
en: Everything connected with religion, pleasure, and wealth, careful nursing, offspring for perpetuating the race, are all dependent on the wife. Indeed, the merits of a person himself as also of his deceased ancestors depend also on her.

sn: दारेष्वधीनो धर्मश्च पितॄणामात्मनस्तथा। न वेत्ति कर्मतो भार्यारक्षणे योऽक्षमः पुमान्॥ अयशो महदाप्नोति नरकांश्चैव गच्छति।
en: The wife should know her husband by his deeds. Indeed, that man who fails to protect his wife, carns great infamy here and goes into Hell hereafter. Such a man falls down from even a position of great fame and never succeeds in acquiring happy regions hereafter.

sn: इत्युक्ता सा ततः प्राह धर्माथौ नौ समौ द्विज॥ सक्तुप्रस्थचतुर्भागं गृहाणेमं प्रसीद मे।
en: Thus addressed, she answered him, saying, O twice-born one, our religions acts and wealth are united. Do you take a fourth of this barley! Indeed, be pleased with me.

sn: सत्यं रतिश्च धर्मश्च स्वर्गश्च गुणनिर्जितः॥ स्त्रीणां पतिसमाधीनं कांक्षितं च द्विजर्षभ।
en: Truth, pleasure, religious merit, and Heaven, as acquirable by good qualities, of women, as also all the objects of their desire, O foremost of twice-born ones, depend on the husband.

sn: ऋतुर्मातुः पितुर्बीजं दैवतं परमं पतिः॥ भर्तुः प्रसादान्नारीणां रतिपुत्रफलं तथा।
en: In the production of children the mother contributes her blood. The father contributes his sced. The husband is the highest deity of the wife. Through the favour of the husband, women get both pleasure and offspring as the reward.

sn: पालनाद्धि पतिस्त्वं मे भर्तासि भरणाच्च मे॥ पुत्रप्रदानाद् वरदस्तस्मात् सक्तून् प्रयच्छ मे।
en: You are my Pati (lord) for the protection you give me. You are my Bhartri for the means of sustenance you give me. You are, again, boon-giver to me one account of your having presented me a son. Do you, therefore, take my share of the barley and give it to the guest.

sn: जरापरिगतो वृद्धः क्षुधार्तो दुर्बलो भृशम्॥ उपवास परिश्रान्तो यदा त्वमपि कर्शितः।
en: Overcome by decrepitude, you are of advanced years. Afflicted by hunger, you are greatly weakened. Worn out with fasts, you are very much emaciated.

sn: इत्युक्तः स तया सक्तून् प्रगृह्येदं वचोऽब्रवीत्॥ द्विज सक्तूनिमान भूयः प्रतिगृह्णीष्व सत्तम।
en: Thus addressed by her, he took her share of the powdered barley and addressing his guest, said, 'O twice-bom one, O best of men, do you accept this quantity of powdered barley as well.

sn: स तान् प्रगृह्य भुक्त्वा च र तुष्टिमगमद् द्विजः। तमुच्छवृत्तिरालक्ष्य ततश्चिन्तापरोऽभवत्॥
en: The Brahmana, having accepted that quantity, immediately ate it up, but his hunger was not yet satisfied. Secing him ungratified, the Brahmana in the observance of the Unchcha vow became thoughtful.

sn: सक्तूनिमान् प्रगृह्य त्वं देहि विप्राय सत्तम। इत्येव सुकृतं मन्ये तस्मादेतत् करोम्यहम्॥
en: His son then said to him 'O best of men, taking my share of the barley do you give it to the guest! I consider this act of mine as one of great merit. Therefore, I do it.

sn: भवान् हि परिपाल्यो मे सर्वदैव प्रयत्नतः। साधूनां काक्षितं यस्मात् पितुर्वृद्धस्य पालनम्॥
en: You should be always maintained by me with great care. Maintenance of the father is a duty which the good always covet.

sn: पुत्रार्थो विहितो ह्येष वार्धके परिपालनम्। श्रुतिरेषा हि विप्रर्षे त्रिषु लोकेषु शाश्वती॥
en: The maintenance of the father in his old age is the duty laid down for the son. This is the eternal Shruti (audition) current in the three worlds, O learned Rishi.

sn: प्राणधारणमात्रेण शक्यं कर्तुं तपस्त्वया। प्राणो हि परमो धर्मः स्थितो देहेषु देहिनाम्॥
en: By living on barely you are capable of practicing penances. The life-breath is the great deity which lives in the bodies of all embodied creatures.'

sn: पितोवाच अपि वर्षसहस्री त्वं बाल एव मतो मम। उत्पाद्य पुत्रं हि पिता कृतकृत्यो भवेत् सुतात्॥
en: The Father said If you attain to the age of even a thousand year, You will still seem to me to be only a little child. Having begotten a son, the father achieves success through him.

sn: बालानां क्षुद् बलवती जानाम्येतदहं प्रभो। वृद्धोऽहं धारयिष्यामि त्वं बली भव पुत्रका६१।।
en: O powerful me, I know that the hunger of children is very strong. I am old. I shall somehow succeed in holding my life-breaths. Do you, O son, become strong.

sn: न मां जीर्णेन वयसा पुत्र क्षुद् बाधतेऽपि च। दीर्घकालं तपस्तप्तं न मे मरणतो भयम्॥
en: Old and decrepit as I am, O son, hunger scarcely afflicts me. I have, again, for many years, practiced penances. I have no fear of death.

sn: पुत्र उवाच अपत्यमस्मि ते पुंसस्त्राणात् पुत्र इति स्मृतः। आत्मा पुत्रः स्मृतस्तस्मात् बाह्यात्मानमिहात्मना॥
en: The Son said-I am your offspring. The Shruti declare that one's offspring is called Putra, because one is rescued by him. One's own self, again, takes birth as his son. Do you, therefore, rescue yourself by your own self.

sn: पितोवाच रूपेण सदृशस्त्वं मे शीलेन च दमेन च। परीक्षितश्च बहुधा सक्तूनादह्यि ते सुत॥
en: The Father said In forin you are like me. In conduct and in self-control, also you are my like. You have been examined on various occasions by me. I shall, therefore, accept your share of the barley, O son!

sn: इत्युक्त्वाऽऽदाय तान् सक्तून् प्रीतात्मा द्विजसत्तमः। प्रहसन्निव विप्राय स तस्मै प्रददौ तदा॥
en: Having said this, that foremost of twiceborn persons cheerfully took his son's share of the barley and smilingly presented it to his twice-born guest.

sn: भुक्त्वा तानपि सक्तूत् स नैव तुष्टो बभूव ह। उच्छवृत्तिस्तु धर्मात्मा व्रीडामनुजगाम ह॥
en: Having eaten that barley also, the guest's hunger was not satisfied. The righteous-should host in the observance of the Unchcha vow became asharmed.

sn: तं वै वधूः स्थिता साध्वी ब्राह्मणप्रियकाम्यया। सक्तूनादाय संहृष्टा श्वशुरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ संतानात् तव संतानं मम विप्र भविष्यति। सक्तूनिमानतिथये गृहीत्वा सम्प्रयच्छ मे॥
en: Desirous of doing what was agreeable to him, his chaste daughter-in-law then, bearing her share of the barley, approached him and said, Through your son, O learned Brahmana, I shall obtain a son. Do you, therefore, take my share of the barley and give it to this guest.

sn: तव प्रसादान्निर्वृत्ता मम लोकाः किलाक्षयाः। पुत्रेण तानवाप्नोति यत्र गत्वा न शोचति॥
en: Through your grace, numerous regions of beatitude will be mine for eternity Through a grandson one obtains those regions going where one has not to suffer any kind of misery.

sn: धर्माद्या हि यथा त्रेता वह्निनेता तथैव च। तथैव पुत्रपौत्राणां स्वर्गस्त्रेता किलाक्षयः॥
en: Like the three-fold objects of life beginning with Religion, or the three-fold sacred fires, there is a triple aggregate of everlasting Heavens, depending upon the son, the grandson, and the great-grandson.

sn: पितृन्णात् तारयति पुत्र इत्यनुशुश्रुमा पुत्रपौत्रेश्च नियतं साधुलोकानुपाश्नुते॥
en: The son is called Putra because he frees his ancestor's debt. Through sons and grandsons one always enjoys the happiness of those regions which are reserved for the pious and the good.

sn: श्वशुर उवाच वातातपविशीर्णाङ्गी त्वां विवर्णो निरीक्ष्य वै। कर्षितां सुव्रताचारे क्षुधविह्वलचेतसम्॥ कथं सक्तून् ग्रहन्यामि भूत्वा धर्मोपघातकः। कल्याणवृत्ते कल्याणि नैवं त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: The Father-in-law said-O you of excellent vows and conduct, seeing you wasted by wind and sun, deprived of your very complexion, emaciated, and almost destitute of consciousness through hunger, how can I be such a transgressor against the rules of virtue as to take your share of the barley? O auspicious damsel, you should not say so, for the sake of those auspicious results for which every family must try.

sn: षष्ठे काले व्रतवती शौचशीलतपोऽन्विताम्। कृच्छ्रवृत्तिं निराहारां द्रक्ष्यामि त्वां कथं शुभे॥
en: O auspicious lady, how can I hold you at even this the sixth division of the day abstaining from food and observing vows? You are gifted with purity and good conduct and penances. Alas, even you have to pass your days in so much misery.

sn: बाला क्षुधार्ता नारी च रक्ष्या त्वं सततं मया। उपवासपरिश्रान्ता त्वं हि बान्धवनन्दिनी॥
en: You are a child, afflicted by hunger, and belong to the softer sex. You should be always protected by mc! Alas, I have to see you worn out with fasts, O you who are the delighter of all your kinsmen.

sn: स्नुषोवाच गुरोर्मम गुरुस्त्वं वै यतो दैवतदैवतम्। देवातिदेवस्तस्मात् त्वं सक्तूनादत्स्व मे प्रभो॥
en: The Daughter-in-law said You are the senior of my senior, since you are the deity of my deity. You are, indeed, the god of my god. Do you, therefore, O powerful one, take my share of the barley.

sn: देहः प्राणश्च धर्मश्च शुश्रूषार्थमिदं गुरोः। तव विप्र प्रसादेन लोकान् प्राप्स्यामहे शुभान्॥
en: My body, life-breaths, and religious rites, have all one objects viz., the service of iny elder. through your favour, O learned Brahmana, I shall obtain many regions of happiness hereafter.

sn: अवेक्ष्या इति कृत्वाहं दृढभक्तेति वा द्विजा चिन्त्या ममेयमिति वा सक्तूनादातुमर्हसि॥
en: I deserve to be looked after by you. Know, o twice-born one, that I am wholly devoted to you. Cherishing also this thought, viz., that my happiness is your concern, you should take this my share of the barley.

sn: श्वशुर उवाच अनेन नित्यं साध्वी त्वं शीलवृत्तेन शोभसे। या त्वं धर्मव्रतोपेता गुरुवृत्तिमवेक्षसे॥
en: O chaste lady, on account of such conduct of yours you will for ever shine in glory, for endued with vows and steadiness in rcligious rites, your eyes are directed to that conduct which should be observed towards elders.

sn: तस्मात् सक्तून् ग्रहीष्यामि वधु नार्हसि वञ्चनाम्। गणयित्वा महाभागे त्वां हि धर्मभृतां वरे॥
en: Therefore, O daughter-in-law, I shall take your share of the barley. You deserve not to be deceived by me, considering all your virtues. You are truly, O blessed damsel, the foremost of all persons observing the duties of righteousness.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा तानुपादाय सक्तून् प्रादाद् द्विजातये। ततस्तष्टोऽभवद् विप्रस्तस्य साधोर्महात्मनः॥८शा
en: Having said so to her, the Brahmana took her share of the barley and gave it to his guest. At this the guest became pleased with that great Brahmana gifted with great piety.

sn: प्रीतात्मा स तु तं वाक्यमिदमाह द्विजर्षभम्। वाग्मी तदा द्विजश्रेष्ठो धर्मः पुरुषविग्रहः॥ शुद्धेन तव दानेन न्यायोपात्तेन धर्मतः। यथाशक्ति विसृष्टेन प्रीतोऽस्मि द्विजसत्तम।
en: With gratified soul, that first of twice-bom persons, endued with great eloquence, who was none else than the deity of Virtue in a human form, then addressed that foremost of Brahmanas and said, 'O best of twice-born oncs, I am highly pleased with this pure gift of yours, this gift of what was acquired by fair mcans by you, and which you did freely part with, accordingly to the rules of virtue.

sn: अहो दानं घुष्यते ते स्वर्गे स्वर्गनिवासिभिः॥ गगनात् पुरुषवर्षं च पश्येदं पतितं भुवि।
en: Indeed, this gift of yours is being bruited about in Heaven by the dwellers of that happy region. Mark, flowers have been rained down from the sky on the Earth.

sn: सुरर्षिदेवगन्धर्वा ये च देवपुरःसराः॥ स्तुवन्तो देवदूताश्च स्थिता दानेन विस्मिताः।
en: The celestial Rishis, the deities, the Gandharvas, those who walk before the deities, and the celestial messengers, are all lauding you, struck with wonder at your gift.

sn: ब्रह्मर्षयो विमानस्था ब्रह्मलोकचराश्च ये॥ कासन्ते दर्शनं तुभ्यं दिवं व्रज द्विजर्षभ।
en: The twice-bom Rishis who live in the regions of Brahma, seated on their cars, are anxious to see you. O foremost of twice-born persons, go to Heaven.

sn: पितृलोकगताः सर्वे तारिताः पितरस्त्वया॥ अनागताश्च बहवः सुबहूनि युगान्युत।
en: The Pitris living in their own region, have all been rescued by them. Others, also, who have not attained to the position of Pitris, have equally been rescued by you for countless cycles.

sn: ब्रह्मचर्येण दानेन यज्ञेन तपसा तथा॥ असंकरेण धर्मेण तस्माद् गच्छ दिवं द्विज।
en: For your Brahmacharya, your gifts, your sacrifices, your penances, and your acts of piety done with a pure heart, go you to Heaven.

sn: श्रद्धया परया यस्त्वं तपश्चरसि सुव्रत॥ तस्माद् देवाश्च दानेन प्रीता ब्राह्मणसत्तम।
en: you of excellent vows, you practice penances with great devotion. Your gifts have, therefore, pleased the deities highly, O best of twice-borm ones.

sn: सर्वमेतद्धि यस्मात् ये दत्तं शुद्धेन चेतसा॥ कृच्छ्रकाले ततः स्वर्गो विजितः कर्मणा त्वया।
en: Since you have made this gift, in a season of great difficulty, with a pure heart, you have, by this act of yours, conquered the celestial region.

sn: क्षुधा निर्मुदति प्रज्ञां धर्मबुद्धिं व्यपोहति॥ क्षुधापरिगतज्ञानो धृतिं त्यजति चैव ह।
en: Hunger destroys one's wisdom and drives off one's righteous understanding. One whose intelligence is overwhelmed by hunger renounces all fortitude.

sn: बुभुक्षां जयते यस्तु स स्वर्ग जयते ध्रुवम्॥ यदा दानरुचिः स्याद् वै तदा धर्मो न सीदति।
en: He, therefore, who conquers hunger, conquers Heaven, forsooth. One's righteousness is never destroyed as long as he cherishes the inclination of making gifts.

sn: अनवेक्ष्य सुतस्नेहं कलत्रस्नेहमेव च॥ धर्ममेव गुरुं ज्ञात्वा तृष्णा न गणिता त्वया।
en: Disregarding filial affection, disregarding the affection one feels for his wife, and reckoning virtue as the foremost, you have paid no attention to the cravings of nature.

sn: द्रव्यागमो नृणां सूक्ष्मः पात्रे दानं ततः परम्॥ कालः परतरो दानाच्छ्रद्धा चैव ततः परा।
en: The acquisition of riches is an act of slight mcrit. Its gift to a worthy person is fraught with greater merit. Of still greater merit is the (proper) time. Lastly, devotion is fraught with the highest merit.

sn: स्वर्गद्वारं सुसूक्ष्मं हि नरैर्मोहान्न दृश्यते॥ स्वर्गार्गलं लोभबीजं रामगुप्तं दुरासदम्।
en: The door of Heaven is very difficult to see. Through carelessness men cannot see it. The bar of Heaven's door has cupidity for its seed. That bar is kept fastened by desire and affection. Indeed, Heaven's door is unapproachable.

sn: तं तु पश्यन्ति पुरुषा जितक्रोधा जितेन्द्रियाः॥ ब्राह्मणास्तपसा युक्ता यथाशक्ति प्रदायिनः।
en: Those men who have subdued anger and conquered their passions, those Brahmanas who are gifted with penances and who make gifts according to the extent of their ability, succeed in seeing it.

sn: सहस्रशक्तिश्च शतं शतशक्तिर्दशापि च॥ दद्यादपश्च यः शक्त्या सर्वे तुल्यफलाः स्मृताः।
en: It has been said that be who gives away a hundred, having a thousand, he who gives away ten, having a hundred, and he who gives a handful of water, having no moncy, are all equal as regards the merit they acquire.

sn: रन्तिदेवो हि नृपतिरपः प्रादादकिंचनः॥ शुद्धेन मनसा विप्र नाकपृष्ठं ततो गतः।
en: King Rantideva, when divested of all his riches, gave a small quantity of water with a pure a small quantity of water with a pure heart. Through this gift, O learned Brahmana, he went to the celestial region.

sn: न धर्मः प्रीयते तात दानैर्दत्तैर्महाफलैः॥ न्यायलब्धैर्यथा सूक्ष्मैः श्रद्धापूतैः स तुष्यति।
en: The deity of righteousness is never pleased so much with large gifts of costly things as with gifts of even worthless things, if acquired lawfully and given away with devotion and faith.

sn: गोप्रदानसहस्राणि द्विजेभ्योऽदान्नृगो नृपः॥ एकां दत्त्वा स पारक्यां नरकं समपद्यत।
en: King Nriga had made gifts of thousands of kine to the twice-born class. By giving away only one cow which did not belong to him, he fell into Hell.

sn: आत्ममांसप्रदानेन शिबिरौशीनरो नृपः।।१०० प्राप्य पुण्यकुताल्लोकान् मोदते दिवि सुव्रतः।
en: Ushinara's son Shibi of excellent vows, by giving away the flesh of his own body, is rejoicing in the celestial region, having attained to the regions of the pious.

sn: विभवो न नृणां पुण्यं स्वशक्त्या स्वर्जितं सताम्।। न यज्ञैर्विविधैर्विप्र यथान्यायेन संचितैः।
en: Mere wealth is not merit. Good men acquire merit by exerting to the best of their power and with the help of righteousness. One does not acquire such merit by means of even various sacrifices as with even a little wealth that has been acquired by fair means.

sn: क्रोधाद् दानफलं हन्ति लोभात् स्वर्ग न गच्छति।। न्यायवृत्तिर्हि तपसा दानवित् स्वर्गमश्नुते।
en: Through anger, the fruits of gifts are destroyed. Through cupidity one fails to go to the celestial region. One conversant with the merits of gifts, and leading a just course of conduct, succeeds, through penances, in enjoying the celestial region.

sn: न राजसूयैर्वहुभिरिष्ट्वा विपुलदक्षिणैः॥ न चाश्वमेधैर्बहुभिः फलं सममिदं तव।
en: The fruit, O Brahmana, of this gift made by you (of a prastha of powdered barley) is much greater than what one acquires by many Rajasuya-Sacrifices with profuse gifts or many Horse-Sacrifices.

sn: सक्तुप्रस्थेन विजितो ब्रह्मलोकस्त्वयाक्षयः॥ विरजो ब्रह्मसदनं गच्छ विप्र यथासुखम्।
en: With this prastha of powdered barley you have conquered the eternal region of Brahman. Go you in happiness, O learned Brahmana, to the house of Brahman who is without the stain of darkness.

sn: सर्वेषां वो द्विजश्रेष्ठ दिव्यं यानमुपस्थितम्॥ आरोहत यथाकामं धर्मोऽस्मि द्विज पश्य माम्।
en: O foremost of twice-born persons, a celestial car is here for all of you. Do you ascend it as you please! O Brahmana, I am the deity of Righteousness. Behold me!

sn: तारितो हि त्वया देहो लोके कीर्तिः स्थिरा च ते॥ सभार्यः सहपुत्रश्च सस्नुषश्च दिवं व्रजा
en: You have rescued your body. The fame of your achievement will least in the world. With your wife, your son, and your daughter-in-law, go now to the celestial region.

sn: इत्युक्तवाक्ये धर्मे तु यानमारुह्य स द्विजः॥ सदारः ससुतश्चैव सस्नुषश्च दिवं गतः।
en: After the deity of Righteousness had said these words, that Brahmana, with his wife, son, daughter-in-law, proceeded to the celestial region.

sn: तस्मिन् विप्रे गते स्वर्ग ससुते सस्नुषे तदा॥ भार्याचतुर्थे धर्मज्ञे ततोऽहं निःसृतो बिलात्।
en: After that learned Brahmana knowing all duties, had thus ascended to the celestial region with his son, daughter-in-law, and wife numbering the fourth, I came out of my hole.

sn: ततस्तु सक्तुगन्धेन क्लेदेन सलिलस्य च॥ दिव्यपुष्पविमर्दाच्च साधोनलवैश्च तैः। विप्रस्य तपसा तस्य शिरो मे काञ्चनीकृतम्॥ तस्य सत्याभिसंधस्य सक्तुदानेन चैव ह। शरीरार्धं च मे विप्राः शातकुम्भमयं कृतम्॥ पश्यतेमं सुविपुलं तपसा तस्य धीमतः।
en: There with the scent of that powdered barley, with the mire caused by the water (with the Brahmana had given or his guest), with the contact (of my body) with the cclestial flowers which had been rained down, with the particles of the barley powder which that good man had given away, and the penances of that Brahmana, my head became gold. See, on account of the gift of that Brahmana who was firm in truth, and his penances half of this my ample body has become golden.

sn: कथमेवंविधं स्याद् वै पार्श्वमन्यदिति द्विजाः॥ तपोवनानि यज्ञांश्च हृष्टोऽभ्येमि पुनः पुनः!
en: O twice-born ones, for converting the rest of my body into gold I repeatedly go, with a cheerful heart, to the hermitages of ascetics and sacrifices performed by kings.

sn: यज्ञं त्वहमिमं श्रुत्वा कुरुराजस्य धीमतः॥ आशया परया प्राप्तो न चाहं काञ्चनीकृतः।
en: Hearing of this sacrifice of the Kuru king, gifted with great wisdom, I came here with hopes. I have not, however, been made gold.

sn: ततो मयोक्तं तद् वाक्यं प्रहस्य ब्राह्मणर्षभाः॥ सक्तुप्रस्थेन यज्ञोऽयं सम्मितो नेति सर्वथा।
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, it was for this that I uttered those words, viz., that this sacrifice can by no means compare with (the gift of) that prastha of powdered barley.

sn: सक्तुप्रस्थलवैस्तैर्हि तदाहं काञ्चनीकृतः॥ नहि यज्ञो महानेष सदृशस्तैर्मतो मम।
en: With the grains of that prastha of powdered barley, I was made gold on that occasion. This great sacrifice, however, is not equal to those grains. This is my opinion.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा नकुलः सर्वान् यज्ञे द्विजवरांस्तदा॥ जगामादर्शनं तेषां विप्रास्ते च ययुर्ग्रहान्॥
en: Having said those words to all those foremost of Brahmanas, the mungoose disappeared from their view. Those Brahmanas then returned to their respective homes.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं मया परपुरंजय। यदाश्चर्यमभूत् तत्र वाजिमेधे महाक्रतौ॥
en: Vaishmpayana said O conquerer of hostile towns, I have now told you all about that wonderful incident which took place in that great Horse-Sacrifice.

sn: न विस्मयस्ते नृपते यज्ञे कार्यः कथंचन। ऋषिकोटिसहस्राणि तपोभिर्ये दिवं गताः॥
en: You should not, o king, think highly of sacrifice. Million of Rishis have ascended to the celestial region with the help of only their penances.

sn: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु संतोषः शीलमार्जवम्। तपो दमश्च सत्यं च प्रदानं चेति सम्मितम्॥
en: Abstention from injury to all creatures, contentment, conduct, sincerity, penances, selfcontrol, truthfulness, and gifts, are each equal in point of merit to sacrifice.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच यज्ञो सक्ता नृपतयस्तप:सक्ता महर्षयः शान्तिव्यवस्थिता विप्राः शमे दम इति प्रभो॥
en: Janamejaya said O powerful Rishi, kings are attached to sacrifices. The great Rishis are attached to penances. Learned Brahmanas observe tranquillity of mind, peacefulness of conduct and self-control.

sn: तस्माद् यज्ञफलैस्तुल्यं न किंचिदिह दृश्यते। इति मे वर्तते बुद्धिस्तथा चैतदसंशयम्॥
en: Hence it appears that nothing can be seen in this world which can compare with the fruits of sacrifices. This is my conviction. That conviction, again scems to be surely correct.

sn: यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा तु बहवो राजानो द्विजसत्तमाः। इह कीर्ति परां प्राप्य प्रेत्य स्वर्गमवाप्नुयुः॥
en: Numberless kings, O best of twice-born persons, having adored the celestials in sacrifices, acquired high fame here and obtained the celestial region hercafter.

sn: देवराजः सहस्राक्षः क्रतुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः। देवराज्यं महातेजाः प्राप्तवानखिलं विभुः॥
en: Gifted with great energy, the powerful king of the deities, viz., Indra of a thousand eyes, obtained the sovereignty over the deities through the many sacrifices he performed with gifts in profusion and attained to the fruition of all his desires.

sn: यदा युधिष्ठिरो राजा भीमार्जुन पुरःसरः। सदृशो देवराजेन समृद्ध्या विक्रमेण च॥ अथ कस्मात् स नकुलो गर्हयामास तं क्रतुम्। अश्वमेधं महायज्ञं राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: When king Yudhishthira, with Bhima and Arjuna by him, resembled the king of the deities himself in prosperity and prowess, why then did that mungoose depreciate that great Horse-Sacrifice of the great monarch.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच यज्ञस्य विधिमग्र्यं वै फलं चापि नराधिपा गदतः शृणु मे राजन् यथावदिह भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Do you listen to me, O king, as I describe to you duly, O Bharata, the excellent ordinances about sacrifice and the fruits also, O king, that sacrifice yields.

sn: पुरा शक्रस्य यजतः सर्व ऊचुर्महर्षयः। ऋत्विक्षु कर्मव्यग्रेषु वितते यज्ञकर्मणि॥
en: Formerly, occasion Shakra celebrated a particular sacrifice. While the limbs of the sacrifice were spread out, the Ritvijas became busy in performing the various rites ordained in the scriptures.

sn: हूयमाने तथा वह्नौ होने गुणसमन्विते। देवेष्वाहूयमानेषु स्थितेषु परमर्षिषु॥ सुप्रतीतैस्तथा विप्रैः स्वागमैः सुस्वरैर्नृप। अश्रान्तैश्चापि लघुभिरध्वर्युवृषभैस्तथा॥
en: The pourer of libations, possessed of every qualification, becaine engaged in pouring libations of clarified butter. The great Rishis were seated around. The celestials were summoned by one by contented Brahmanas of great learning uttering scriptural Mantras in sweet voices. Those foremost of Adhvaryyus, not fatigued with what they did, recited the Mantras of the Yajurveda in soft account. on one one

sn: आलम्भसमये तस्मिन् गृहीतेषु पशुष्वथा महर्पयो महाराज बभूवुः कृपयान्विताः॥
en: The time came for killing the animals. When the animals selected for sacrifice were seized, the great Rishis, O king, felt mercy for them.

sn: ततो दीनान् पशून् दृष्ट्वा ऋषयस्ते तपोधनाः। ऊचुः शक्रं समागम्य नायं यज्ञविधिः शुभः॥
en: Seeing that the animals had all become dispirited, those Rishis, gifted with wealth of penances, approached Shakra and said to him, “This method of sacrifice is not auspicious.'

sn: अपरिज्ञानमेतत् ते महान्तं धर्ममिच्छतः। न हि यज्ञे पशुगण विधिदृष्टाः पुरंदर॥
en: Desirous of winning great merit as you are, this is, indeed, a mark of your ignorance of the rites of sacrifice. O Purandara, animals have not been ordained to be killed in sacrifices,

sn: धर्मोपघातकस्त्वेष समारम्भस्तव प्रभो। नायं धर्मकृतो यज्ञो न हिंसा धर्म उच्यते॥
en: O powerful one, these preparations of yours are destructive of merit! This sacrifice is not consistent with virtue. The destruction of creatures can never be said to be an act of virtue!

sn: आगमेनैव ते यज्ञं कुर्वन्तु यदि चेच्छसि॥ विधिदृष्टेन यज्ञेन धर्मस्ते सुमहान् भवेत्।
en: If you wish it, let your priests perform your sacrifice according to the Agama. By performing a sacrifice according to the scriptural ordinance, great will be the merit acquired by you.

sn: यज बीजैः सहस्राक्ष त्रिवर्षपरमोषितैः॥ एष धर्मो महान् शक्र महागुणफलोदयः।
en: you of a hundred eyes do you perform the sacrifice with seeds of grain which have been kept for three years. This, O Shakra, would be fraught with great virtue and productive of fruits of high efficacy.

sn: शतक्रतुस्तु तद् वाक्यमृषिभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः॥ उक्तं न प्रतिजग्राह मानान्मोहवशं गतः।
en: were The deity of a hundred sacrifices, however, moved by pride and overwhelmed by stupefaction, did not accept these words uttered by the Rishis.

sn: तेषां विवादः सुमहाशक्रयज्ञे तपस्विनाम्॥ जङ्गमैः स्थावरैर्वापि यष्टव्यमिति भारत। ते तु खिन्ना विवादेन ऋषयस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥
en: Then, O Bharata, a great dispute arose in that sacrifice of Shakra between the ascetics as to how sacrifices should be performed, that is, should they be performed, with mobile creatures or with immobile objects.

sn: तदा संधाय शक्रेण पप्रच्छर्नृपतिं वसुम्। धर्मसंशयमापन्नान् सत्यं ब्रूहि महामते॥
en: All of them exhausted with disputation. The Rishis, then, those beholders of truth, having made a compact with Shakra, asked king Vasu.

sn: महाभाग कथं यज्ञेष्वागमो नृपसत्तम। यष्टव्यं पशुभिर्मुख्यैरथो बीजै रसैरिति॥
en: O highly blessed one, what is the Vedic declaration about sacrifices? Is it preferable to perform sacrifices with animals or with seeds and juices.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा तु वसुस्तेषामविचार्य बलाबलम्। यथोपनीतैर्यष्टव्यमिति प्रोवाच पार्थिवः॥
en: Hearing the question, king Vasu, without at all judging the merits of the arguments advanced on both sides, at once answered, saying, 'Sacrifices may be performed with any of the two kinds of objects ready.'

sn: एवमुक्त्वा स नृपतिः प्रविवेश रसातलम्। उक्त्वाथ वितथं प्रश्नं चेदीनामीश्वरः प्रभुः॥
en: Having answered the question thus, he had to enter the nether regions. Indeed, the powerful king of the Chedis had to undergo that misery for having answered falsely.

sn: तस्मान्न वाच्यं ह्येकेन बहुज्ञेनापि संशये। प्रजापतिमपाहाय स्वयम्भुवमृते प्रभुम्॥
en: Therefore, when a doubt arises, no person, however wise, should singly decide the matter, unless he be the powerful and self-born Lord himself of creatures,

sn: तेन दत्तानि दानानि पापेनाशुद्धबुद्धिना। तानि सर्वानादृत्य नश्यन्ति विपुलान्यपि।॥
en: Gifts made by a sinner with an impure heart, for this, when very large, become lost. Such gifts go for nothing.

sn: तस्याधर्मप्रवृत्तस्य हिंसकस्य दुरात्मनः। दानेन कीर्तिर्भवति न प्रेत्येह च दुर्मतेः॥
en: By the gifts made by a person of unrighteous conduct, one, that is, who is of sinful soul and who is a destroyer, just fame never acquired either in this world or in the next.

sn: अन्यायोपगतं द्रव्यमभीक्ष्णं यो हपण्डितः। धर्माभिशंकी यजते न स धर्मफलं लभेत्॥
en: That person of little intelligence, who, from desire of acquiring merit, celebrates sacrifices with wealth acquired by unfair means, never succeeds in acquiring merit.

sn: धर्मवैतंसिको यस्तु पापात्मा पुरुषाधमः। ददाति दानं विप्रेभ्यो लोकविश्वासकारणम्॥
en: That low wretch of sin who hypocritically assuming a garb of virtue makes gifts to Brahmanas, only created the conviction in men about his own virtue.

sn: पापेन कर्मणा विप्रो धनं प्राप्य निरङ्कुशः। रागमोहान्वितः सोऽन्ते कलुषां गतिमश्नुते॥
en: That Brahmana of uncontrolled conduct, who acquires wealth by sinful deeds, overwhelmed by passion and stupefaction, attains at last to the goal of the sinful.

sn: अपि संचयबुद्धिर्हि लोभमोहवशंगतः। उद्वेजयति भूतानि पापेनाशुद्धबुद्धिना॥
en: Some one, overwhelmed by cupidity and stupefaction, becomes bent on storing riches. He is seen to persecute all creatures, urged by a sinful and impure understanding.

sn: एवं लब्ध्वा धनं मोहाद् यो हि दद्याद् न तस्य स फलं प्रेत्य भुङ्क्ते पापधनागमात्॥ यजेत वा।
en: He who, having acquired riches by such means, makes gifts or performs sacrifices therewith, never enjoys the fruits of those gifts or sacrifices in the other world on account of the wealth having been acquired by unfair means.

sn: उञ्छं मूलं फलं शाकमुदपात्रं तपोधनाः। दानं विभवतो दत्त्वा नरा: स्वयन्ति धार्मिकाः॥
en: Men having wealth of penances, by giving away, to the best of their power, grains of corn picked up from the fields or roots or fruits or potherbs or water or leaves, acquire great merit and proceed to the celestial region.

sn: एष धर्मो महायोगो दानं भूतदया तथा! ब्रह्मचर्ये तथा सत्यमनुक्रोशो धृतिः क्षमा॥ सनातनस्य धर्मस्य मूलमेतत् सनातनम्। श्रूयन्ते हि पुरा वृत्ता विश्वामित्रादयो नृपाः॥
en: Such gifts are fraught with virtue and equal to high austerities. Such gifts, as also mercy to all creatures, and Brahmacharya, truthfulness of speech, and kindness, and fortitude, and forgiveness, form the eternal foundations of virtue which itself is eternal. We hear of Vishvamitra and other kings of ancient times.

sn: विश्वामित्रोऽसितश्चैव जनकश्च महीपति। कक्षसेनार्टिसेनौ च सिन्धुद्वीपश्च पार्थिवः॥ एते चान्ये च बहवः सिद्धि परमिकां गताः। नृपाः सत्यैश्च दानैश्च न्यायलब्धैस्तपोधनाः॥
en: Indeed, Vishmvamitra, and Asita, and king Janaka, and Kakshasena and Arshtisena and king Sindhudvipa, these and many other kings, gifted with wealth of penances, having made gifts of articles acquired by fairness, having attained to high success.

sn: ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्रा ये चाश्रितास्तपः। दानधर्माग्निना शुद्धास्ते स्वर्ग यान्ति भारत॥
en: Those amongst Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras, who perforin penances, O Bharata, and who purify themselves, by gifts and other deeds of righteousness, proceed to the celestial region.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: जनमेजय उवाच धर्मागतेन त्यागेन भगवन् स्वर्गमस्ति चेत्। एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व कुशलो ह्यसि भाषितुम्॥
en: Janamejaya said If, O illustrious one, celestial region is the fruit of riches acquired by fair means, do you fully describe it to me. You are wellconversant with the subject and, it is, therefore, proper for you to explain it.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: तस्योञ्छवृत्तेर्यद् वृत्तं सक्तुदाने फलं महत्। कथितं तु मम ब्रांस्तथ्यमेतदसंशयम्॥
en: O twice-born one, you have said to me what the high fruit was that accrued to that Brahmana, who lived according to the Unchcha mode, through his gift of powdered barley. Forsooth, all you have said is true.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: कथं हि सर्वयज्ञेषु निश्चयः परमोऽभवत्। एतदर्हसि मे वक्तुं निखिलेन द्विजर्षभा॥
en: In what way, however, was the attainment held certain of the highest end in all sacrifices? O foremost of twice-born persons, you should fully expound all this to me.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। अगस्त्यस्य महायज्ञे पुरावृत्तमरिंदम॥
en: Vaishampayana said Regarding it is cited this old narrative, O chastiser of enemies, of what took place formerly in the great sacrifice of Agastya.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: पुरागस्त्यो महातेजा दीक्षा द्वादशवार्षिकीम्। प्रविवेश महाराज सर्वभूतहिते रतः॥
en: Formerly, O king, Agastya of great energy, devoted to the well-being of all creatures, entered into a Diksha extending for twelve years.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: तत्राग्निकल्पा होतार आसन् सत्रे महात्मनः। मूलाहारा: फलाहारा: साश्मकुट्टा मरीचिपाः॥
en: In that sacrifice of the great Rishi many Hotris were engaged who resembled blazing fires in the splendour of their bodies. Among them were men who lived upon roots or fruits, or who used two pieces of stone only for husking their corn, or who were supported by only the rays (of the moon).

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: परिपृष्टिका वैघसिकाः प्रसंख्यानास्तथैव च। यतयो भिक्षवश्चात्र बभूवुः पर्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Among them were also men who never took any food unless it was placed before them by others desirous of feeding them, and those who never ate anything without having first served the celestials, the departed Manes, and guests, and those who never washed the food which they took. There were also Yatis and Vikshus among them, O king.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: सर्वे प्रत्यक्षधर्माणो जितक्रोधा जितेन्द्रियाः। दमे स्थिताश्च सर्वे ते हिंसादम्भविवर्जिताः॥
en: All of them were men who had obtained a sight of the deity of virtue in his embodied form. They had subjugated anger and acquired a complete mastery over all their senses. Living in the observance of self-control, they were freed from pride and the desire of injuring others.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: वृत्ते शुद्धे स्थिता नित्यमिन्द्रियैश्चाप्यबाधिताः। उपातिष्ठन्त तं यज्ञं यजन्तस्ते महर्षयः॥
en: They were always observant of a pure conduct and were never obstructed by their senses. Those great, Rishis attended that sacrifice and performed its various rites.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: यथाशक्त्या भगवता तदन्नं समुपार्जितम्। तस्मिन् सत्रे तु यद् वृत्तं यद् योग्यं च तदाभवत्।१०।
en: The illustrious Rishi (Agastya) acquired the food which was collected in that sacrifice and that came up to the required quantity, by lawful means according to the best of his power.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: एवं विधे त्वगर-त्यस्य क्रतवः कृताः। सहस्राक्षस्तदा वर्तमाने तथाध्वरे। न ववर्ष सहस्राक्षस्तदा भरतसत्तम॥ ततः कर्मान्तरे राजन्नगस्त्यस्य महात्मनः। कथेयमभिनिवृत्ता मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्॥ नववर्ष अगस्त्यो यजमानोऽसौ ददात्यन्नं विमत्सरः।
en: Numerous other ascetics at that times celebrated large sacrifices. As Agastya, however, was engaged in that sacrifice of his, the thousand-eyed Indra, O best of the Bharatas, ceased to pour rain (on the Earth. At the intervals, O king, of the sacrificial rites, this talk took place among those Rishis of purified souls about the great Agastya, viz., 'This Agastya, engaged in sacrifice, is making gifts of food with heart purged of pride and vanity.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: न च वर्षति पर्जन्यः कथमन्नं भविष्यति॥ सत्रं चेदहं महद् विप्रा मुनेादशवार्षिकम्।
en: The deity of the clouds, however, has ceased to pour rain. How, indeed will food grow? This sacrifices of the Rishi, you Brahmanas, is great and extends for twelve years.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: न वर्षिष्यति देवश्च वर्षाण्येतानि द्वादश॥ एतद् भवन्तः संचिन्त्य महर्षेरस्य धीमतः। अगस्त्यस्यातितपसः कर्तुमर्हन्त्यनुग्रहम्॥ इत्येवमुक्ते वचने ततोऽगस्त्यः प्रतापवान्॥ प्रोवाच वाक्यं स तदा प्रसाद्य शिरसा मुनीन्। यदि द्वादशवर्षाणि न वर्षिष्यति वासवः॥ चिन्तायज्ञं करिष्यामि विधिरेष सनातनः। यदि द्वादशवर्षाणि न वर्षिष्यति वासवः॥ स्पर्शयज्ञं करिष्यामि विधिरेष सनातनः। यदि द्वादशवर्षाणि न वर्षिष्यति वासवः॥ ध्येयात्मना हरिष्यामि यज्ञानेतान् यतव्रतः। बीजयज्ञो मयायं वै बहुवर्षसमाचितः॥
en: The deity will to pour rain for these twelve years. Thinking on this, you should do some favour to this Rishi of great intelligence, viz., Agastya of severe penances. When these words were said, Agastya of great prowess, pleasing all those ascetics by bending his head, said, 'If Vasava does not pour rain for these twelve years, I shall then perform the mental sacrifice. This is the eternal ordinance. If Vasava does not pour rain for these twelve years. I shall then perform the Touch-Sacrifice, This is the eternal sacrifice. If Vasava does not। pour rain for these twelve years, I shall, then, putting forth, all my exertions, make arrangements for other sacrifices characterised by the observance of the most difficult and serve vows. This present sacrifice of mine, with seeds, has been arranged for by me with labour of many years.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: बीजैर्हितं करिष्यामि नात्र विघ्नो भविष्यति। नेदं शक्यं वृथा कर्ते मम सत्रं कथंचन॥
en: I shall, with seeds, do much good. No obstacle will arise. This my sacrifice is incapable of being baffled.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: वर्षिष्यतीह वा देवो न वा वर्षं भविष्यति। अथावाभ्यर्थनामिन्द्रो न करिष्यति कामतः॥ स्वयमिन्द्रो भविष्यामि जीवयिष्यामि च प्रजाः। यो यदाहारजातश्च स तथैव भविष्यति॥
en: It matters little whether the deity pours rain or no downpours come. Indeed, if Indra does not, of his own will, show any regard for me, I shall, in that case, change myself into Indra and keep all creatures alive. Every creature, on whatever food he has been nourished, will continue to be nourished on it as before.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: विशेषं चैव कर्तास्मि पुनः पुनरतीव हि। अद्येह स्वर्णमभ्येतु यच्चान्यद् वसु किंचन॥
en: I can even repeatedly create a different order of things. Let gold and whatever else of riches there is, come to this place today.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: त्रिषु लोकेषु यच्चास्ति तदिहागम्यतां स्वयम्। दिव्याश्चाप्सरसा संघा गन्धर्वाश्च सकिन्नराः॥ विश्वावसुश्च ये चान्ये तेऽप्युपासन्तु मे मखम्। उत्तरेभ्यः कुरुभ्यश्च यत् किंचिद् वसु विद्यते॥ सर्वं तदिह यज्ञेषु स्वयमेवोपतिष्ठतु। स्वर्गः स्वर्गसदश्चैव धर्मश्च स्वयमेव तु॥
en: Let all the wealth which is in the three worlds come here today of its own accord! Let all the tribes of celestial Apsaras, all the Gandharvas along with the Kinnarvas, and Vishvavasu, and others there are (of that order) approach this sacrifice of mine! Let all the wealth which exists among the Northern Kurus, come of their own accord to these sacrifices. Let Heaven, and all those who have Heaven for their home, and Dharma himself, come here.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: इत्युक्ते सर्वमेवैतदभवत् तपसा मुनेः। तस्य दीप्ताग्निमह सस्त्वगस्त्यस्यातितेजसः॥
en: After the ascetic had uttered these words, everything took place as he desired, by virtue of his penances, for Agastya was gifted with a mind which resembled a burning fire and was possessed of extraordinary energy.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: ततस्ते मुनयो हृष्टा ददृशुस्तपसो बलम्। विस्मिता वचनं प्राहुरिदं सर्वे महार्थवत्॥
en: The Rishis who were there saw the power of penances with rejoicing hearts. Filled with wonder they then said these words of grave significance.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: ऋषि उवाच प्रीताः स्म तव वाक्येन न विच्छामस्तपोव्ययम्। तैरेव यज्ञैस्तुष्टाः स्म न्यायेनेच्छामहे वयम्॥
en: The Rishis said We have been highly pleased with words you have uttered. We do not, however, wish penances should diminution. Those sacrifices are approved by us which are performed by fair means. Indeed, we wish duly those sacrifices which rest on lawful means.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: यज्ञं दीक्षां तथा होमान् यच्चान्यन्मृगयामहे। न्यायेनोपार्जिताहारा: स्वकर्माभिरता वयम्॥
en: Acquiring our food by lawful incans and observant of our respective duties, we shall seek to go through sacrificial initiations and the pouring of libations on the sacred fire and the other religious rites.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: वेदांश्च ब्रह्मचर्येण न्यायतः प्रार्थयामहे। न्यायेनोत्तरकालं च गृहेभ्यो निःसृता वयम्॥ धर्मदृष्टैर्विधिद्वारैस्तपस्तप्स्यामहे वयम्। भवतः सम्यगिष्टा तु बुद्धिहिंसाविवर्जिता॥
en: We should worship the celestials, practicing Brahmacharya by lawful mean. Completing the period of Brahmacharya we have come out of our house, observing lawful methods. That that your suffer any understanding, which is freed from the desire of inflicting any kind of injury on others is approved by us.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: एतामहिंसां यज्ञेषु ब्रूयास्त्वं सततं प्रभो। प्रीतास्ततो भविष्यामो वयं तु द्विजसत्तम॥ विसर्जिताः समाप्तौ च सत्रादस्माद् व्रजामहे।
en: You should always, O powerful one, commend such abstention from injury in all sacrifices. We shall then be highly pleased, O foremost of twice-born ones. After the completion of your sacrifice, when dismissed by you, we shall then, leaving this place, go away.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: तथा कथयतां तेषां देवराजः पुरंदरः॥ ववर्ष सुमहातेजा दृष्ट्वा तस्य तपोबलम्।
en: As they were saving these words, Purandara, the king of the deities, gifted with great energy, seeing the power of Agastya's penances, poured rain.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: आसमाप्तेश्च यज्ञस्य तस्यामितपराक्रमः॥ निकामवर्षी पर्जन्यो बभूव जनमेजय।
en: Indeed, O Janamejaya, till the completion of the sacrifice of the Rishi of great prowess, the deity of rain poured rain which met the wishes of men both about quantity and time.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: प्रसादयामास च तमगस्त्यं त्रिदशेश्वरः। स्वयमभ्येत्य राजर्षे पुरस्कृत्य बृहस्पतिम्॥
en: Placing Brihaspati be one him, the king of the deities came there, O royal sage, and pleased the Rishi Agastya.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: ततो यज्ञ समाप्तौ तान् विससर्ज महामुनीन्। अगस्त्यः परमप्रीतः पूजयित्वा यथाविधि॥
en: On the termination of that sacrifice, Agastya, filled with joy, adored all those great Rishis duly and then sent them all away.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कोऽसौ नकुलरूपेण शिरसा काञ्चनेन वै। प्राह मानुषवद् वाचमेतत् पृष्टो वदस्व मे॥
en: Janamejaya said Who was that mungoose with a golden head, which said all those words in a human voice? Asked by me, do you tell me this.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतत् पूर्वं न पृष्टोऽहं न चास्माभिः प्रभाषितम्। श्रूयतां नकुलो योऽसौ यथा वाक् तस्य मानुषी॥
en: You did not ask me before and, therefore, I did not tell you, Hear as I tell you who that mungoose was and why he could assume a human voice.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: श्राद्धं संकल्पयामास जमदग्निः पुरा किला होमधेनुस्तमागाच्च स्वयमेव दुदोह ताम्॥
en: Formerly, the Rishi Jamadagni desired to perform a Shraddha. His Homa-Cow came to him and the Rishi milked her himself.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: तत्पय: स्थापयामास नवे भाण्डे दृढे शुचौ। तच्च क्रोधस्वरूपेण पिठरं धर्म आविशत्॥
en: He then placed the milk in a vessel which was new, durable, and pure. The deity Dharma, assuming the form of anger, entered that vessel of milk.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: जिज्ञासुस्तमृषिश्रेष्ठं किं कुर्याद् विप्रिये कृते। इति संचिन्त्य धर्मः स धर्मयामास तत् पयः॥
en: Indeed, Dharma desirous of determining what that foremost of Rishis would do when seeing some injury done to him. Having thought thus, Dharma spoiled that milk.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: तमाज्ञाय मुनिः क्रोधं नैवास्य स चुकोप ह। स तु क्रोधस्ततो राजन् ब्राह्मणी मूर्तिमास्थितः।
en: Knowing that the spoiler of his milk was Anger, the ascetic was not at all enraged with him. Anger, then, assuming the form of a Brahmana lady, showed him self to the Rishi.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: जिते तस्मिन् भृगुश्रेष्ठमभ्यभाषदमर्षणः॥ जितोऽस्मीति भृगुश्रेष्ठ भृगवो ह्यतिरोषणाः। लोके मिथ्याप्रवादोऽयं यत्त्वयास्मि विनिर्जितः॥
en: Indeed, Anger, finding that he had been vanquished by that foremost one of Bhrigu's race, addressed him, saying, 'O chief of Bhrigu's race, I have been conquered by you. There is a saying among men that the Bhrigus are very wrathful. I now find that that saying is false, since I have been subdued by you. was

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: वशे स्थितोऽहं त्वय्यद्य क्षमावति महात्मनि। बिभेमि तपसः साधो प्रसादं कुरु मे प्रभो॥
en: You are endued with a powerful soul. You are endued with forgiveness. I stand here today, acknowledging your sway. I fear your penances, O righteous one! Do you, O powerful Rishi, show me favour.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: जमदग्निरुवाच साक्षाद् दृष्टोऽसि मे क्रोध गच्छ त्वं विगतज्वरः। न त्वयापकृतं मेऽद्य न च मे पन्युरस्ति वै॥
en: I have seen you, O Anger, in your embodied form. Go you wherever you like, without any anxiety. You have not done me any injury today. I have no grudge against you.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: यान् समुद्दिश्य संकल्पः पयसोऽस्य कृतो मया। पितरस्ते महाभागास्तेभ्यो बुद्ध्यस्व गम्यताम्॥
en: Those for whom I had kept this milk are the highly blessed Pitris. Present yourself before them and ascertain their intentions.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: इत्युक्तो जातसंबासस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयता पितॄणामभिषङ्गाच्च नकुलत्वमुपागतः॥
en: Thus addressed, stricken with fear, Anger vanished from the sight of the Rishi. Through the curse of the Pitris he became a mungoose.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: स तान् प्रसादयामास शापस्यान्तो भवेदिति। तैश्चाप्युक्तः क्षिपन् धर्म शापस्यान्तमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: He then began to please the Pitris in order to bring about an end of his curse. By them he was told these words ;-By speaking disrespectfully of Dharma you shall attain to the end of your curse.'

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: तैश्चोक्तो यज्ञियान् देशान् धर्मारण्यं तथैव च। जुगुप्समानो धावन् स तं यज्ञं समुपासदत्॥
en: Thus addressed by them, he wandered over places where sacrifices were performed and over other sacred placed, employed in censuring great sacrifices. It was he who came to the great sacrifice of king Yudhishthira.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: धर्मपुत्रमथाक्षिप्य सक्तुप्रस्थेन तेन सः। मुक्तः शापात् ततः क्रोधो धर्मो ह्यासीद् युधिष्ठिरः।।
en: Dispraising the son of Dharma by a reference to the prastha of powdered barley, Anger became freed from his curse, for Yudhishthira (as Dharma's son) was Dharma's self.

description: Concluded The highest end of all sacrifices
sn: एवमेतत् तदा वृत्ते यज्ञे तस्य महात्मनः। पश्यतां चापि नस्तत्र नकुलोऽन्तर्हितस्तदा॥
en: This is what took place in the sacrifice of that great king. The mungoose disappeared there in out very presence.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्।।
en: Having saluted the Supreme Deity (Narayana) and the highest of all male beings (Nara) and also the Goddess of Learning (Sarasvati), let us cry success.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: जनमेजय उवाच प्राप्य राज्यं महात्मानः पाण्डवा मे पितामहाः। कथमासन् महाराज्ञि धृतराष्ट्र महात्मनि॥
en: After having gained their kingdom, how did my grandfathers, the great Pandavas, treat the high-souled king Dhritarashtra?

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: स तु राजा हतामात्यो हतपुत्रो निराश्रयः। कथमासीद्धतैश्वर्यो गान्धारी च यशस्विनी॥
en: How, indeed, did that king who had all his counselors and sons killed, who was with it a support, and whose wealth had vanise.., behave? How also did the illustrious Gandhari act?

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: कियन्तं चैव कालं ते मम पूर्वपितामहाः। स्थिता राज्ये महात्मानस्तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि।॥
en: For how many years did my noble grandfather rule the kingdom? You should tell me all this.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्राप्य राज्यं महात्मानः पाण्डवा हतशत्रवः। धृतराष्ट्र पुरस्कृत्य पृथिवीं पर्यपालयन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Having regained their kingdom, the great Pandavas, their enemies all killed, ruled the earth, placing Dhritarashtra at their head.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: धृतराष्ट्रमुपातिष्ठद् विदुरः संजयस्तथा। वैश्यपुत्रश्च मेधावी युयुत्सुः कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Vidura, Sanjaya and the highly intelligent Yuyutsu, who was Dhritarashtra's son by his Vaishya wife, used to wait upon Dhritarashtra.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: पाण्डवाः सर्वकार्याणि सम्पृच्छन्ति स्म तं नृपम्। चक्रुस्तेनाभ्यनुज्ञाता वर्षाणि दश पञ्च च॥
en: The Pandavas used to consult that king in all matters. Indeed, for fifteen years, they did all things under the advice of the old king.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: सदा हि गत्वा ते वीराः पर्युपासन्त तं नृपम्। पादाभिवादनं कृत्वा धर्मराजमते स्थिताः॥
en: Those heroes used very often to go to that king and sit beside him, after having adored his feet, according to the wishes of king Yudhishthira the just.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: ते मूर्ध्नि समुपाघ्राताः सर्वकार्याणि चक्रिरे। कुन्तिभोजसुता चैव गान्धारीमन्ववर्तत॥
en: They did all things under the command of Dhritarashtra who smelt their heads in love. The daughter of king Kuntibhoja also obeyed Gandhari in all matters.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: द्रौपदी च सुभद्रा च याश्चान्याः पाण्डवस्त्रियः। समां वृत्तिमवर्तन्त तयोः श्वश्वोर्यथाविधि॥
en: Draupadi and Subhadra and the other ladies of the Pandavas treated the old king and the queen as if they were their own father-in-law and mother-in-law.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: शयनानि महार्हाणि वासांस्याभरणानि च। राजार्हाणि च सर्वाणि भक्ष्यभोज्यान्यनेकशः॥ युधिष्ठिरो महाराज धृतराष्ट्रेऽभ्युपाहरत्। तथैव कुन्ती गान्धार्यो गुरुवृत्तिमवर्तत॥
en: Yudhishthira gave the king costly beds, dresses and ornaments, and food and drink and other enjoyable articles, in profusion and of such superior kinds as were worthy of royal use. Likewise Kunti behaved towards Gandhari as towards a senior.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: विदुरः संजयश्चैव ययुत्सुश्चैव कौरव। उपासते स्म तु वृद्धं हतपुत्रं जनाधिपम्॥
en: Vidura, Sanjaya, and Yuyutsu, O you of Kuru's race, used to always wait upon the old king whose sons had all been killed.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: श्यालो द्रोणस्य यश्चासीद् दयितो ब्राह्मणो महान्। स च तस्मिन् महेष्वासः कृपः समभवत् तदा॥
en: The dear brother-in-law of Drona, viz., the very superior Brahmana, Kripa, that powerful bowman, also attended upon the king.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: व्यासश्च भगवान् नित्यमासांचक्रे नृपेण ह। कथाः कुर्वन् पुराणर्षिर्देवर्षिपितृरक्षसाम्॥
en: The holy Vyasa also used to often meet with the old king and recite to him the histories of old Rishis and celestial ascetics and Pitris and Rakshasas.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: धर्मयुक्तानि कार्याणि व्यवहारन्वितानि च। धृतराष्ट्राभ्यनुज्ञातो विदुरस्तान्यकारयत्॥
en: Vidura, under the order of Dhritarashtra, superintended the performance of all religious acts and the adıninistration of the law.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: सामन्तेभ्यः प्रियाण्यस्य कार्याणि सुबहून्यपि। प्राप्यन्तेऽथैः सुलघुभिः सुनयाद् विदुरस्य वै॥
en: Through the excellent policy of Vidura, by the expenditure of very little money, the Pandavas got numerous agreeable services from their feudators and followers.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: अकरोद् बन्धमोक्षं च बध्यानां मोक्षणं तथा। न च धर्मसुतो राजा कदाचित् किंचिदब्रवीत्॥
en: King Dhritarashtra freed prisoners and pardoned those who were condemned to death. King Yudhishthria the just never said anything to this.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: विहारयात्रासु पुनः कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। सर्वान् कामान् महातेजाः प्रददावम्बिकासुते॥
en: On those occasions when the son of Ambika went on pleasure trips, the highly energetic. Kuru king Yudhishthira used to give him every article of enjoyment.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: आरालिका: सूपकारा रागखाण्डविकास्तथा। उपातिष्ठन्त राजानं धृतराष्ट्रं यथा पुरा॥
en: Aralikas, and juice-makers, and makers of Ragakhandavas waited on king Dhritarashtra as before.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: वासांसि च महार्हाणि माल्यानि विविधानि च। उपाजह्वर्यथान्यायं धृतराष्ट्रस्य पाण्डवाः॥
en: Pandu's son collected costly dresses and garlands of various kinds and duly offered them to Dhritarashtra.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: मैरेयकाणि मांसानि पानकानि मधूनि च। चित्रान् भक्ष्यविकारांश्च चक्रुस्तस्य यथा पुरा॥
en: Maireya wines, flesh of various kinds, and sherlets and honey, and various kinds of food agreeably prepared by the admixture, of many articles, were caused to be made for the old king as in his prosperous days.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: ये चापि पृथिवीपाला: समाजग्मुस्ततस्ततः। उपातिष्ठन्त ते सर्वे कौरवेन्द्रं यथा पुरा॥
en: Those kings who came there one after another, all used to wait upon the old Kuru king as before.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: कुन्ती च द्रौपदी चैव सात्वती च यशस्विनी। उलूपी नागकन्या च देवी चित्राङ्गदा तथा॥ धृष्टकेतोश्च भगिनी जरासंधसुता तथा। एताश्चान्याश्च बह्वयो वै योषितः पुरुषर्षभ।॥ किंकराः पर्युपातिष्ठन् सर्वाः सुबलजां तथा। यथा पुत्रवियुक्तोऽयं न किंचिद् दुःखमाप्नुयात्॥ इति तानन्वशाद् भ्रातॄन् नित्यमेव युधिष्ठिरः। एवं ते धर्मराजस्य श्रुत्वा वचनमर्थवत्॥
en: Kunti, Draupadi, and she of the Sattwata race possessed of great fame, and ulupi the daughter of the Naga king, and queen Chitrangada, and the sister of Dhrishtaketu, and the daughter of Jarasandha, these and many other ladies, O king, used to wait upon the daughter of Subala like maids of all work. Yuthishthira always enjoined upon his bothers that Dhritarashtra, who was deprived of all his children, might not feel himself unhappy in any way. They also, on their part, listening to these pregnant commands from king Yudhishthira, showed particular obedience to the old king.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: सविशेषमवर्तन्त भीममेकं तदा विना। न हि तत् तस्य वीरस्य हृदयादपसर्पति। धृतराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्ध्या यद् वृत्तं द्यूतकारितम्॥
en: There was one exception, however. It was Bhimasena. All that had followed from that match at dice which had been brought about by the wicked understanding of Dhritarashtra, did not go away from the heart of that hero. Yuthishthira always enjoined upon his bothers that Dhritarashtra, who was deprived of all his children, might not feel himself unhappy in any way. They also, on their part, listening to these pregnant commands from king Yudhishthira, showed particular obedience to the old king.

description: The conduct of the Pandavas after regaining their kingdom
sn: सविशेषमवर्तन्त भीममेकं तदा विना। न हि तत् तस्य वीरस्य हृदयादपसर्पति। धृतराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्ध्या यद् वृत्तं द्यूतकारितम्॥
en: There was one exception, however. It was Bhimasena. All that had followed from that match at dice which had been brought about by the wicked understanding of Dhritarashtra, did not go away from the heart of that hero.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं सम्पूजितो राजा पाण्डवैरम्बिकासुतः। विजहार यथापूर्वमृषिभिः पर्युपासितः॥
en: Thus adored by the Pandavas, the royal son of Ambika passed his time happily as before, waited upon and honoured by the Rishis.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: ब्रह्मदेयाग्रहारांश्च प्रददौ स कुरूद्वहः। तच्च कुन्तीसुतो राजा सर्वमेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: That perpetuator of Kuru's race used to make those foremost of offerings which should be given to the Brahmanas. The royal son of Kunti always placed those articles at Dhritarashtra's command.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: आनुशंस्यपरो राजा प्रीयमाणो युधिष्ठिरः। उवाच स तदा भ्रातृनमात्यांश्च महीपतिः॥ मया चैव भवद्भिश्च मान्य एष नराधिपः। निदेशे धृतराष्ट्रस्य यस्तिष्ठति स मे सुहृत्॥
en: Shorn of malice as king Yudhishthira was, he was always affectionate towards his uncle. Addressing his brothers and ministers, the king said, 'King Dhritarashtra should be honoured both by myself and you all. He, indeed, is a well-wisher of mine who obeys the commands of Dhritarasthra,

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: विपरीतश्च मे शत्रुर्नियम्यश्च भवेन्नरः। पितृवृत्तेषु चाहःसु पुत्राणां श्राद्धकर्मणि॥ सुहृदां चैव सर्वेषां यावदस्य चिकीर्षितम्। ततः स राजा कौरव्यो धृतराष्ट्रो महामनाः॥ ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यथार्हेभ्यो ददौ वित्तान्यनेकशः।
en: He, on the other hand, who treats him otherwise, is my enemy. Such a man should certainly be punished by me. On days of performing the rites ordained for the Pitris, as also in the Shraddhas performed for his sons and all well-wishers, the great Kuru king Dhritarashtra, gave away to Brahmanas, as each deserved immense quantity of wealth after his heart.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: धर्मराजश्च भीमश्च सव्यसाची यमावपि॥ तत् सर्वमन्ववर्तन्त तस्य प्रियचिकीर्षया।
en: King Yudhishthira the just, and Bhima, and Arjuna, and the twins, desirous of doing what was liked by the old king, used to execute all his cominands.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: कथं नु राजा वृद्धः स पुत्रपौत्रवधार्दितः॥ शोकमस्मत्कृतं प्राप्य न प्रियेतेति चिन्त्यते।
en: They always took care that the old king who was afflicted with the destruction of his sons and grandsons, with, that is, grief caused by the Pandavas themselves, might not die of his grief.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: यावद्धि कुरुवीरस्य जीवत्पुत्रस्य वै सुखम्॥ बभूव तदवाप्नोति भोगांश्चेति व्यवस्थिताः।
en: Indeed, the Pandavas treated him in such a way that that Kuru hero might not be deprived of that happiness and all those articles of enjoyment which he had during his sons lifetime.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: ततस्ते सहिताः पञ्च भ्रातरः पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥ तथाशीला: समातस्थुर्धृतराष्ट्रस्य शासने।
en: The five brothers, viz., the sons of Pandu, treated thus Dhritarashtra, living under his command.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: धृतराष्ट्रश्च तान् सर्वान् विनीतान् नियमे स्थित्तान्॥ शिष्यवृत्तिं समापन्नान् गुरुवत् प्रत्यपद्यत।
en: Dhritarashtra also, seeing them so humble and obedient to his commands and acting towards him as disciples towards preceptors, treated them also like a loving preceptor in return.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: गान्धारी चैव पुत्राणां विविधैः श्राद्धकर्मभिः॥ आनृण्यमगमत् कामान् विप्रेभ्यः प्रतिपाद्य सा।
en: Gandhari, by performing the various rites of the Sharaddha and making gifts to Brahmanas of various objects of enjoyment, became freed from the debt she owed to her slain children.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: एवं धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥ भ्रातृभिः सहितो धीमान् पूजयामास तं नृपम्।
en: Thus did that foremost of righteous men, viz., king Yudhishthira the just, endued with great intelligence, along with his brothers, adored king Dhritarashtra.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स राजा सुमहातेजा वृद्धः कुरुकुलोद्वहः॥ न ददर्श तदा किंचिदप्रियं पाण्डुनन्दने।
en: Vishampayana said Endued with great energy, that perpetuator of Kuru's race, viz., the old king Dhritarashtra, could not see any ill-will in Yudhishthira.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: वर्तमानेषु सवत्तिं पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु॥ प्रीतिमानभवद् राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः।
en: Seeing that the great Pandavas were in the observance of a wise and righteous conduct, king Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, became pleased with them.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: सौबलेयी च गान्धारी पुत्रशोकमपास्य तम्॥ सदैव प्रीतिमत्यासीत् तनयेषु निजेष्विव।
en: Subala's daughter, Gandhari, renouncing all sorrow for her (slain) children, began to show great love for the Pandavas as if they were her own children.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: प्रियाण्येव तु कौरव्यो नाप्रियाणि कुरूद्वहः॥ वैचित्रवीर्ये नृपतौ समाचरत वीर्यवान्।
en: Gifted with great energy, the Kuru king Yudhishthira never did anything that was disliked by the royal son of Vichitravirya. On the other hand, he always treated him in a highly agreeable way.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: यद् यद् ब्रूते च किंचित् स धृतराष्ट्रो जनाधिपः॥ गुरु वा लघु वा कार्यं गान्धारी च तपस्विनी। तं स राजा महाराज पाण्डवानां धुरंधरः॥ पूजयित्वा वचस्तत् तदकार्षीत् परवीरहा।
en: Whatever acts, grave or light, were directed by king Dhritarashtra or the helpless Gandhari to be done, were all done with respect, O monarch, by that destroyer of hostile heroes, viz., the Pandava king.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: तेन तस्याभवत् प्रीतो वृत्तेन स नराधिपः॥ अन्वतप्यत संस्मृत्य पुत्रं तं मन्दचेतसम्।
en: The old king became highly pleased with such conduct of Yudhishthira. Indeed, he was grieved at the remembrance of his own wicked son.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: सदा च प्रातरुत्थाय कृतजप्यः शुचिर्नृपः॥ आशास्ते पाण्डुपुत्राणां समरेष्वपराजयम्।
en: Rising every day at early dawn, he purified himself and went through his recitations, and then blessed the Pandavas by wishing them victory in battle.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: ब्राह्मणान् स्वस्ति वाच्याथ हुत्वा चैव हुताशनम्॥२२ आयूंषि पाण्डुपुत्राणामाशंसत नराधिपः।
en: Making the usual gifts to the Brahmanas and making them utter benedictions, and pouring libations on the sacred fire, the old king prayed for long life to the Pandavas.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: न तां प्रीतिं परामाप पुत्रेभ्यः स कुरूद्वहः॥ यां प्रीतिं पाण्डुपुत्रेभ्यः सदावाप नराधिपः।
en: Indeed, the king had never derived that great happiness from his own sons which he always did from the sons of Pandu.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: ब्राह्मणानां यथावृत्तः क्षत्रियाणां यथाविधः॥ तथा विट्शूद्रसंघानामभवत् स प्रियस्तदा।
en: King Yudhishthria at that time became as agreeable to the Brahmanas the Kshatriyas, and the various bands of Vaishyas and Shudras of his kingdom.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: यच्च किंचित् तदा पापं धृतराष्ट्रसुतैः कृतम्॥ अकृत्वा हृदि तत् पापं तं नृपं सोऽन्ववर्तत।
en: as to King Yudhishthira forgot whatever wrongs were done to him by the sons of Dhritarashtra, and saluted his uncle.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: यश्च कश्चिन्नरः किंचिदप्रियं वाम्बिकासुते॥ कुरुते द्वेष्यतामेति स कौन्तेयस्य धीमतः। न राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य न च दुर्योधनस्य वै॥ उवाच दुष्कृतं कश्चिद् युधिष्ठिरभयानरः।
en: If any man did nay thing that was not liked by the son of Ambika, he became thereby an object of hatred to the intelligent son of Kunti. Indeed, through fear of Yudhishthira nobody could talk of the evil deeds of either Duryodhana or Dhritarashtra.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: धृत्या तुष्टो नरेन्द्रः स गान्धारी विदुरस्तथा॥ शौचेन चाजातशत्रोर्न तु भीमस्य शत्रुहन्।
en: Both Gandhari and Vidura also were well pleased with the power which the king having no enemics showed for bearing wrongs. They were, however, not so pleased, O destroyer of foes, with Bhima.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: अन्ववर्तत भीमोऽपि निश्चितो धर्मजं नृपम्॥ धृतराष्ट्रं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य सदा भवति दुर्मनाः।
en: Dharma's son Yudhishthira, was truly obedient to his uncle. Bhima, however, on seeing Dhritarashtra, became very dispirited.

description: The respectful treatment of the Pandavas towards Dhritarashtra
sn: राजानमनुवर्तन्तं धर्मपुत्रममित्रहा। अन्ववर्तत कौरव्यो हृदयेन पराङ्मुखः॥
en: That destroyer of enemies, secing Dharma's son pay his respects to the old king, saluted him outwardly with a very reluctant heart.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरस्य नृपतेर्दुर्योधनपितुस्तदा। नान्तरं ददृशू राज्ये पुरुषाः प्रणयं प्रति॥
en: The people who lived in the Kuru kingdom could not mark any difference in the cordiality which existed between king Yudhishthira and the father of Duryodhana.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: यदा तु कौरवो राजा पुत्रं सस्मार दुर्मतिम्। तदा भीमं हृदा राजन्नपध्याति स पार्थिवः॥
en: When the Kuru king recollected his wicked son, he then could not but feel unfriendly, in his heart, towards Bhima.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: तथैव भीमसेनोऽपि धृतराष्ट्र जनाधिपम्। नामर्षयत राजेन्द्र सदैव दुष्टवद्धदा॥
en: Bhiimasena also, O king, moved by a wicked heart, was unable to put up with king Dhritarashtra.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: अप्रकाशान्यप्रियाणि चकारास्य वृकोदरः। आज्ञा प्रत्यहरच्चापि कृतज्ञैः पुरुषैः सदा॥
en: Vrikodara secretly did many deeds that were disagreeable to the old king. Through deceitful servants he caused the commands of his uncle to be disobeyed.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: स्मरन् दुर्मन्त्रितं तस्य वृत्तान्यप्यस्य कानिचित्। अथ भीमः सुहृन्मध्ये बाहुशब्दं तथाकरोत्॥ संश्रवे धृतराष्ट्रस्य गान्धार्याश्चाप्यमर्षणः। स्मृत्वा दुर्योधनं शत्रु कर्णदुःशासनावपि॥ प्रोवाचेदं सुरंब्धो भीमः स परुषं वचः।
en: Recollecting the evil advice of the old king and some deeds of his, Bhima, one days, in the midst of his friends, slapped his armpits, in the hearing of Dhritarashtra and of Gandhari. The angry Vrikodara, recollecting his enemies Duyrodhana and Karna and Dushasana, gave way to a fit of passion, and said these harsh words :-'The sons of the blind king, capable of fighting with various kinds of weapons, have all been dispatched by me to the other world with these arms of mine which resemble a pair of iron clubs.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: अन्धस्य नृपतेः पुत्रा मया परिघबाहुना॥ नीता लोकममुं सर्वे नानाशस्त्रास्त्रयोधिनः।
en: Indeed, these are those two arms of mine, loO king like maces of iron, and invincible by cnemies, coming within whose clasp the sons of Dhritarashtra have all been killed.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: इमौ तौ परिघप्रख्यौ भुजौ मम दुरासदौ॥ ययोरन्तरमासाद्य धार्तराष्ट्राः क्षयं गताः।
en: These are those two well-developed and round arms of mine, resembling a pair of elephantine trunks. Coming within their clasp, the foolish sons of Dhritarashtra have all been killed.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: ताविमौ चन्दनेनाक्तौ चन्दना) च मे भुजौ॥ याभ्यां दुर्योधनो नीतः क्षयं ससुतबान्धवः।
en: Smeared with sandal-paste and deserving of that adornment are those two arms of mine by which Duryodhana has been sent to the other world along with all his sons and kinsmen.'

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: एताश्चान्याश्च विविधाः शल्यभूता नराधिपः॥ वृकोदरस्य ता वाचः श्रुत्वा निर्वेदमागमत्।
en: Hearing these and many other words, O king, of Vrikodara, which were so many darts, king Dhritarashtra gave way to cheerlessness and sorrow.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: सा च बुद्धिमती देवी कालपर्यायवेदिनी॥ गान्धारी सर्वधर्मज्ञा तान्यलीकानि शुश्रुवे।
en: Queen Gandhari, however, who conversant with every duty and endued with great intelligence, and who knew what Time brings on its course, considered them as untrue.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः पञ्चदशे वर्षे समतीते नराधिपः॥ राजा निर्वेदमापेदे भीमवाग्बाणपीडितः।
en: Then, after fifteen years had passed away, o monarch, king Dhritarashtra, afflicted (constantly) by the wordy arrows of Bhima, became stricken with despair and sorrow.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: नान्वबुध्यत तद् राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ श्वेताश्वो वाथ कुन्ती वा द्रौपदी वा यशस्विनी। माद्रीपुत्रौ च धर्मज्ञौ चित्तं तस्यान्ववर्तताम्॥
en: King Yudhishthira thc son of Kunti, however, knew it not; nor Arjuna of white horses; nor Kunti; nor Draupadi possessed of great fame; nor the twin sons of Madri, knowing every duty and who were always engaged in acting after the wishes of Dhritarashtra. was to

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: राज्ञस्तु चित्तं रक्षन्तौ नोचतुः किञ्चिदप्रियम्। ततः समानयामास धृतराष्ट्रः सुहृज्जनम्॥ वाष्पसंदिग्धमन्यर्थमिदमाह च तान् भृशम्।
en: Employed in doing the behest's of the king, the twins never said anything that was disagreeable the old king. Then Dhritarashtra one day honoured his friends by his confidence. Addressing them with tearful eyes, he said these words.
