description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच विदितं भवतामेतद् यथा वृत्तः कुरुक्षयः॥ ममापराधात् तत् सर्वमनुज्ञातं च कौरवैः।
en: Dhritarashtra said You know how the destruction of Kurus has happened. All that was brought about by my fault, though the Kauravas approved of all my counsels.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: योऽहं दुष्टमतिं मन्दो ज्ञातीनां भयवर्धनम्॥ दुर्योधनं कौरवाणामाधिपत्यऽभ्यषेचयम्।
en: Fool that I was, I installed the wickedminded Duryodhana, that enhancer of the terrors of kinsmen, to rule over the Kurus.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: यच्चाहं वासुदेवस्य नाश्रौषं वाक्यमर्थवत्॥ वध्यतां साध्वयं पापः सामात्य इति दुर्मतिः। पुत्रस्नेहाभिभूतस्तु हितमुक्तो मनीषिभिः॥ विदुरेणाथ भीष्मेण द्रोणेन च कृपेण च। पदे पदे भगवता व्यासेन च महात्मना॥ संजयेनाथ गान्धार्या तदिदं तप्यते च माम्।
en: Vasudeva had said to me, 'Let this sinful wretch of wicked understanding be slain along with all his friends and counselors.' I did not listen to those words of great significance. All wise men gave me the same beneficial advice. Vidura, Bhishina, Drona, and Kripa said the same thing. The holy and great Vyasa repeatedly said the same, as also Sanjaya and Gandhari. Overwhelmed, however, by filial affection, I could not follow that advice. Bitter repentance is now my lot for my neglect.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: यच्चाहं पाण्डुपुत्रेषु गुणवत्सु महात्मसु॥ न दत्तवाश्रियं दीप्तां पितृपैतामहीमिमाम्।
en: I also repent for not having bestowed that blazing prosperity, derived from sires and grandsires on the great Pandavas possessed of every accomplishment.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: विनाशं पश्यमानो हि सर्वराज्ञां गदाग्रजः॥ एतच्छ्रेयस्तु परमममन्यत जनार्दनः।
en: The eldest brother of Gada foresaw the destruction of all the king; Janardana, however, considered that destruction as highly beneficial.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: सोऽहमेतान्यलीकानि निवृत्तान्यान्मनस्तदा।।२३। हृदये शल्यभूतानि धारयामि सहस्रशः।
en: So many battalions of troops belonging to me, have been destroyed! Alas, my heart is pierced with thousands of darts on account of all these results.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: विशेषतस्तु पश्यामि वर्षे पञ्चदरोऽद्य वै॥ अस्य पापस्य शुद्ध्यर्थं नियतोऽस्मि सुदुर्मतिः।
en: Of wicked understanding as I am, now, after the lapse of fifteen years, I am trying to expiate my sins.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: चतुर्थे नियते काले कदाचिदपि चाष्टमे॥ तृष्णाविनयनं भुजे गान्धारी वेद तन्मम।
en: Now at the fourth division of the day or sometimes at the eighth division, with the regularity of a vow, I eat a little food for simply satisfying my thirst. Gandhari knows this.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: करोत्याहारमिति मां सर्वः परिजनः सदा॥ युधिष्ठिरभयादेति भृशं तप्यति पाण्डवः।
en: All my attendants believe that I eat as usual. Through feat of Yudhishthira alone I concealed my deeds, for if the eldest son of Pandu came to know of my vow, he would feel great pain.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: भूमौ शये जप्यपरो दर्भेष्वजिनसंवृतः॥ नियमव्यपदेशेन गान्धारी च यशस्विनी।
en: Clad in deer-skin, I lie down on the Earth, spreading a small quantity of Kusha grass, and pass the time in silent recitations. The illustrious Gandhari, also, passes her time in the observance of similar vows.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: हतं शतं तु पुत्राणां ययोर्युद्धेऽपलायिनाम्॥ नानुतप्यामि तच्चाहं क्षत्रधर्म हि ते विदुः।
en: Thus do we both act, we who have lost a hundred sons none of whom ever retreated from battle. I do not, however, grieve for those children of mine. They have all died while performing Kshatriya duties.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: इत्युक्त्वा धर्मराजानमभ्यभाषत कौरवः॥ भद्रं ते यादवीमातर्वचश्चेदं निबोध मे।
en: Having said these words, the old king then addressed Yudhishthira in particular and said, 'Blessed by you, O son of the princess of Yudu's race! Listen now to what I say.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: सुखमसम्युषितः पुत्र त्वया सुपरिपालितः॥ महादानानि दत्तानि श्राद्धानि च पुनः पुनः।
en: Cherished by you, O son, I have lived these years very happily. I have (with your help) made large gifts and performed Sharaddhas repeatedly.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: प्रकृष्टं च यया पुत्र पुण्यं चीर्णं यथाबलम्॥ गान्धारी हतपुत्रेयं धैर्येणोदीक्षते च माम्।
en: I have, O son, to the best of my power, acquired merit largely. This Gandhari, though destitute of sons, has lived with great fortitude, loO king all the while at me.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: द्रौपद्या ह्यपकर्तारस्तव चैश्वर्यहारिणः॥ समतीता नृशंसास्ते स्वधर्मेण हता युधि।
en: They who inflicted great wrongs on Draupadi and robbed you of your affluence, those cruel men-have all left the world, killed in battle according to the practice of their order.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: न तेषु प्रतिकर्तव्यं पश्यामि कुरुनन्दन॥ सर्वे शस्त्रभृतां लोकान् गतास्तेऽभिमुखं हताः।
en: I have nothing to do for them, O delighter of the Kurus! Killed with their faces towards battle, they have attained to those regions which reserved for the wielders of weapons.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: आत्मनस्तु हितं पुण्यं प्रतिकर्तव्यमद्य वै॥ गान्धार्याश्चैव राजेन्द्र तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि।
en: I should now, do what is bencficial and meritorious for me as also for Gandhari. O great king, you should grant mc permission. are

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: त्वं तु शस्त्रभृतां श्रेष्ठः सततं धर्मवत्सलः॥ राजा गुरुः प्राणभृतां तस्मादेतद् ब्रवीम्यहम्।
en: You are the foremost of all righteous persons. You are always devoted to virtue. The king is the preceptor of all creatures. It is for this that I say so.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: अनुज्ञातस्त्वया वीर संश्रयेयं वनान्यहम्॥ चीरवल्कलभृद् राजन् गान्धार्या सहितोऽनया।
en: With your permission, O hero, I shall retire into the forest, clad in rags and darks, O king, along with this Gandhari.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: तवाशिषः प्रयुञ्जानो भविष्यामि वनेचरः॥ उचितं नः कुले तात सर्वेषां भरतर्षभ। पुत्रेष्वैश्वर्यमाधाय वयसोऽन्ते वनं नृप॥ तत्राहं वायुभक्षो वा निराहारोऽपि वा वसन्। पल्या सहानया वीर चरिष्यामि तपः परम्॥
en: I shall live in the forest, always blessing you. It is proper, O son, for the members of our family, to make over sovereignty, when old age comes, to children and lead the forest mode of life. Living there on air alone, or abstaining froin all food, I shall, with this wife of mine, O hero, practice severe austeities.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: त्वं चापि फलभाक् तात तपसः पार्थिवो ह्यसि। फलभाजो हि राजानः कल्याणस्येतरस्य वा॥
en: You shall be a sharer of those penances, o son, for you are the king. Kings are sharers of both auspicious and inauspicious acts done in their kingdom.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच न मां प्रीणयते राज्यं त्वय्येवं दुःखिते नृप। धिङ्नामस्तु सुदुर्बुद्धिं राज्यसक्तं प्रमादिनम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said When you, O king, are thus subject to grief, sovereignty does not please me at all. Fie on me who am of wicked understanding, devoted o the pleasures of own and absolutely negligent of my true concerns.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: योऽहं भवन्तं दुःखार्तमुपवासकृशं भृशम्। जिनाहारं क्षितिशयं न विन्दे भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: Alas, I, with all my brothers, was ignorant of yourself having so long been stricken with grief, emaciated with fasts, abstaining from food, and lying on the naked earth.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: अहोऽस्मि वञ्चितो मूढो भवता गूढबुद्धिना। विश्वासयित्वा पूर्वं मां यदिदं दुःखमश्नुथाः॥
en: Alas, foolish that I am, I have been deceived by you who have great intelligence, inasmuch as, having filled me with confidence at first you have latterly undergone such grief.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: किं मे राज्येन भोगैर्वा किं यज्ञैः किं सुखेन वा। यस्य मे त्वं महीपाल दुःखान्येतान्यवाप्तवान्॥
en: What need have I of kingdom or of articles of enjoyment, what need of sacrifices or of happiness, when you, O king, have undergone so much affliction.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: पीडितं चापि जानामि राज्यमान्मानमेव च। अनेन वचसा तुभ्यं दुःखितस्य जनेश्वर॥
en: I consider my kingdom as a disease, and myself also as afflicted. Plunged though I am in sorrow, what however, is the sue of these words that I am addressing you?

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: भवान् पिता भवान् माता भवान् नः परमो गुरुः। भवता विप्रहीणा वै क्व नु तिष्ठामहे वयम्॥
en: You are our father, you are our mother; you are our foremost of superiors. Deprived of your presence, how shall we live.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: औरसो भवतः पुत्रो युयुत्सुनृपसत्तम। अस्तु राजा महाराज यमन्यं मन्यते भवान्॥
en: O best of kings, let Yuyutsu, the son of your loins, be made king, or indeed, anybody else whom you may wish.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: अहं वनं गमिष्यामि प्रशासतु। न मामयशसा दग्धं भूयस्त्वं दग्धुमर्हसि॥
en: I shall go into the forest. Do you rule the kingdom You should not burn me who am already burned by infamy.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: नाहं राजा भवान् राजा भवतः परवानहम्। कथं गुरुं त्वां धर्मज्ञमनुज्ञातुमिहोत्सहे॥
en: I am not the king. You are the king. I am dependent on your will. How can I dare grant permission to you who are my preceptor?

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: भवान् राज्य न मन्युर्हदि नः कश्चित् सुयोधनकृतेऽनघ। भवितव्यं तथा तद्धि वयं चान्ये च मोहिताः॥
en: O sinless one, I cherish no resentment in my heart on account of the wrongs done to us by Suyodhana. It was ordained that it should be so. Both ourselves and others were stupefied (by fate).

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: वयं पुत्रा हि भवतो यथा दुर्योधनादयः। गान्धारी चैव कुन्ती च निर्विशेषे मते मम॥
en: We are your children as Duryodhana and others were. My conviction is that Gandhari is as much my mother as Kunti.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: स मां त्वं यदि राजेन्द्र परित्यज्य गमिष्यसि। पृष्ठतस्त्वनुयास्यामि सत्यमात्मानमालभे॥
en: If you, O king of kings, go to the forest leaving me, I shall then follow you. I swear by iny soul.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: इयं हि वसूसम्पूर्णा मही सागरमेखला। भवता विप्रहीणस्य न मे प्रीतिकरी भवेत्॥
en: This Earth, with her belt of seas, so full of riches, will not be a source of joy to me when I am deprived of your presence.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: भवदीयमिदं सर्वं शिरसा त्वां प्रसादये। त्वदधीनाः स्म राजेन्द्र व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: All this belongs to you. Bending my head low I make my obeisance. We are all dependent on you, O king of kings. Let the fever of your heart be removed.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: भवितव्यमनुप्राप्तो मन्ये त्वं वसुधाधिप। दिष्ट्या शुश्रूषमाणस्त्वां मोक्षिष्ये मनसो ज्वरम्।।५५
en: I think, O king, that all this that has come upon you is due to destiny. By good luck, I had thought, that waiting upon you and executing your commands obediently, I would rescue you from the fever of your heart.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तापस्ये मे मनस्तात वर्तते कुरुनन्दन। उचितं च कुलेऽस्माकमरण्यगमनं प्रभो॥
en: Dhritarashtra said-Odelighter of the Kurus, my mind is fixed, O son, on penances. O powerful one, it is proper for our family that I should retire into the forest.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: चिरमसम्युषितः पुत्र चिरं शुश्रूषितस्त्वया। वृद्धं मामप्यनुज्ञातुमर्हसि त्वं नराधिप॥
en: I have lived long under your protection, O son. I have for many years been served by you with respect. I am now old. You should, O king, grant me permission.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा धर्मराजानं वेपमानं कृताञ्जलिम्। उवाच वचनं राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः॥ संजयं च महात्मानं कृपं चापि महारथम्। अनुनेनुमिहेच्छामि भवद्भिर्वसुधाधिपम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said these words to king Yudhishthira the just, king Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, trembling all the while and with hands joined together, further said to the great Sanjaya and the great car-warrior Kripa, these words: I wish to solicit the king through you.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: म्लायते मे मनो हीदं मुखं च परिशुष्यति। वयसा च प्रकृष्टेन वाग्व्यायामेन चैव ह॥
en: My mind has become dispirited, my mouth has become dry, through the weakness of age and the exertion of speaking.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: इत्युक्त्वा स तु धर्मात्मा वृद्धो राजा कुरुद्वहः। गान्धारी शिश्रिये धीमान् सहसैव गतासुवत्॥
en: Having said so, that perpetuator of Kuru's race, viz., the pious old king, blessed with prosperity, leaned to Gandhari and suddenly looked like one dcad.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: तं तु दृष्ट्वा समासीनं विसंज्ञमिव कौरवम्। आर्ति राजागमत् तीव्रां कौन्तेयः परवीरहा॥
en: Seeing him thus seated like one shom of consciousness, that destroyer of hostile heroes, viz., the royal son of Kunti, became penetrated by a piercing grief.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यस्य नागसहस्रेण शतसंख्येन वै बलम्। सोऽयं नारी व्यपाश्रित्य शेते राजा गतासुवत्॥
en: on me am Yudhishthira said Alas, he whose strength was equal to that of a hundred thousand elephants, alas, that king sits today, learning on a woman.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: आयसी प्रतिमा येन भीमसेनस्य सा पुरा। चूर्णीकृता बलवता सोऽबलामाश्रितः स्त्रियम्॥
en: Alas, he by whom the iron image of Bhima on a former occasion was reduced to pieces, leans today on a weak woman.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: धिगस्तु मामधर्मज्ञं धिग् बुद्धिं धिक् च मे श्रुतम्। यत्कृते पृथिवीपाल: शेतेऽयमतथोचितः॥
en: Fic who exceedingly unrighteous. Fie on my understanding. Fie on my knowledge of the scriptures. Fie on me for whom this king lies today in a manner that is not worthy of him.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: अहमप्युपवत्स्यामि यथैवायं गुरुर्मम। यदि राजा न भुङ्क्तेऽयं गान्धारी च यशस्विनी॥
en: I also shall fast even as my preceptor. Indeed, I shall fast if this king and Gandhari of great fame abstain from food.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽस्य पाणिना राजन् जलशीतेन पाण्डवः। उरो मुखं च शनकैः पर्यमार्जत धर्मवित्॥
en: Vaishampayana said The Pandava king, knowing every duty, using his own hand, then softly rubbed with cold water the breast and the face of the old king.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: तेन रत्नौषधिमता पुण्येन च सुगन्धिना। पाणिस्पर्शन राज्ञः स राजा संज्ञामवाप ह॥
en: At the touch of the king's hand which was auspicious and fragrant, and on which were jewels and medicinal herb's, Dhritarashtra regained his consciousness.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच स्पृश मां पाणिना भूयः परिष्वज च पाण्डव। जीवामीवातिसंस्पर्शात् तव राजीवलोचन॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Do you, again, touch me, O son of Pandu, with your hand, and do you embrace me. O you having eyes like lotus petals, I am restored to my senses through the auspicious touch of your hand.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: मूर्धानं च तवाघ्रातुमिच्छामि मनुजाधिप। पाणिभ्यां हि परिस्प्रष्टुं प्रीणनं हि महन्मम॥
en: O king, I wish to smell your head. The clasp of your arms is highly gratifying to me.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: अष्टमो ह्यद्य कालोऽयमाहारस्य कृतस्य मे। येनाहं कुरुशार्दूल शक्नोमि न विचेष्टितुम्॥
en: This is the eighth division of the day and therefore, the hour for taking may food. For not having taken my food, O scion of Kuru's race, I am so weak that I cannot move.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: व्यायामश्चायमत्यर्थे कृतस्त्वामभियाचता। ततो ग्लानमनास्तात नष्टसंज्ञ इवाभवम्॥
en: Great has been my exertion while soliciting you. Rendered cheerless by it, O son, I had fainted.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: तवामृतरसप्रख्यं हस्तस्पर्शमिमं प्रभो। लब्धा संजीवितोऽस्मीति मन्ये कुरुकुलोद्वह॥
en: O perpetuator of Kuru's race, I think that receiving the touch of your hand, which is like nectar in its vivifying effects I have been restored to my senses.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु कौन्तेयः पित्रा ज्येष्ठेन भारत। पस्पर्श सर्वगात्रेषु सौहार्दात् तं शनैस्तदा॥
en: Thus addressed, O Bharata, by the eldest brother of his father, the son of Kunti, from affection, gently touched every part of his body.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: उपलभ्य ततः प्राणान् धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः। बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य मूर्ध्याजिघ्रत पाण्डवम्॥
en: Regaining his life, king Dhritarashtra embraced the son of Pandu with his arms and smelled his head.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: विदुरादयश्च ते सर्वे रुरुदुदुःखिता भृशम्। अतिदुःखात् तु राजानं नोचुः किंचन पाण्डवम्॥
en: Vidura and others wept aloud in great sorrow. On account, however, of thc poignancy of their sorrow, they said nothing to either the old king or the son of Pandu.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: गान्धारी त्वेव धर्मज्ञा मनसोद्वहती भृशम्। दुःखान्यधारयाद् राजन् मैवमित्येव चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Gandhari, knowing every duty, bore her sorrow with patience, and loaded as her heart was,, O king, said nothing.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: इतरास्तु स्त्रियः सर्वाः कुन्त्या सह सुदुःखिताः। नेत्रैरागतविक्लेदैः परिवार्य स्थिताऽभवन्॥
en: The other ladies, Kunti among them, became greatly afflicted. They wept, shedding profuse tears, and sat surrounding the old king.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: अथाब्रवीत् पुनर्वाक्यं धृतराष्ट्रो युधिष्ठिरम्। अनुजानीहि मां राजस्तापस्ये भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then Dhritarashtra, once more addressing Yudhishthira, said these words-Do you, O king, permit me to practice penance's.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: ग्लायते मे मनस्तात भूयो भूयः प्रजल्पतः। न मामतः परं पुत्र परिक्लेष्टुमिहार्हसि॥
en: By speaking repeatedly, O son, my mind becomes weakened. You should not, O son, afflict me after this.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: तस्मिंस्तु कौरवेन्द्रे तं तथा ब्रुवति पाण्डवम्। सर्वेषामेव योधानामार्तनादो महानभूत्॥
en: When that foremost one of Kuru's race was saying so to Yudhishthira, a loud sound of wailing arose from all the warriors there present.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: दृष्ट्वा कृशं विवर्णं च राजानमतथोचितम्। उपवासपरिश्रान्तं त्वगस्थिपरिवारणम्॥ धर्मपुत्रः स्वपितरं परिष्वज्य महाप्रभुम्। शोकजं बाष्पमुत्सृज्य पुनर्वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing his royal father of great splendour, emaciated and palc, reduced to unworthy of him worn out with fasts, and loO king like skeleton covered with skin, Dharma's son Yudhishthira shed tears of grief and once more said these words.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: न कामये नरश्रेष्ठ जीवितं पृथिवीं तथा। यथा तव प्रियं राजंश्चिकीर्षामि परंतप॥
en: a state O foremost of men, I do not wish for life and the Earth! O scorcher of enemies, I shall engage myself in doing what is pleasant to you.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: यदि चाहमनुग्राह्यो भवतो दयितोऽपि वा। क्रियतां तावदाहारस्ततो वेत्स्याम्यहं परम्॥
en: If I deserve your favour, if I am dear to you, do you eat something. I shall then know what to do.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा धृतराष्ट्रो युधिष्ठिरम्। अनुज्ञातस्त्वया पुत्र भुजीयामिति कामये॥
en: Gifted with great energy, Dhritarashtra then said to Yudhishthira, “I wish, O son, to take some food, with your permission.

description: Gruel act of Bhima, the grief of Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira
sn: इति ब्रुवति राजेन्द्र धृतराष्ट्रे युधिष्ठिरम्। ऋषिः सत्यवतीपुत्रो व्यासोऽभ्येत्य वचोऽब्रवीत्।।८७।
en: When Dhritarashtra said these words to Yudhishthira, Datyavati's son Vyasa came the and said as follows.

sn: व्यास उवाच युधिष्ठिरः महाबाहो यथाह कुरुनन्दनः। धृतराष्ट्रो महातेजास्तत् कुरुष्वाविचारयन्॥
en: Vyasa said O Inighty-armed Yudhishthira, do unhesitatingly what Dhritarashtra of Kuru's family has said.

sn: अयं हि वृद्धो नृपतिर्हतपुत्रो विशेषतः। नेदं कृच्छ्रे चिरतरं सहेदिति पतिर्मम॥
en: This king is old. He has again, been made sonlcss. I think he will not be able to bear his grief long.

sn: गान्धारी च महाभागा प्राज्ञा करुणवेदिनी। पुत्रशोकं महाराज धैर्येणोद्वहते भृशम्॥
en: The highly blessed Gandhari, cndued with great wisdom and kindly speech, bears with fortitude her excessive grief owing to the loss of her sons.

sn: अहमप्येतदेव त्वां ब्रवीमि कुरु मे वचः। अनुज्ञां लभतां राजा मा वृथेह मरिष्यति॥
en: I also tell you (what the old king says.) Do you obey my words. Let the old king have your permission. Let him not die an inglorious death at home.

sn: राजर्षीणां पुराणानामनुयातु गतिं नृपः। राजर्षीणां हि सर्वेषामन्ते वनमुपाश्रयः॥
en: Let this king follow the path of royal sages of old. Indeed, all royal sages retire into the woods at last.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः स तदा राजा व्यासेनाद्भुतकर्मणा। भगवानेव नो मान्यो भगवानेव नो गुरुः। भगवानस्य राज्यस्य कुलस्य च परायणम्॥ प्रत्युवाच महातेजा धर्मराजो महामुनिम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Thus addressed at that time by Vyasa of wonderful deeds, king Yudhishthira the just, gifted with mighty energy, said to the great ascetic these words, 'Your holy self is held by us in great reverence. You alone are our preceptor. You alone are the refuge of this our kingdom as also of our family.

sn: अहं तु पुत्रो भगवन् पिता राजा गुरुश्च मे। निदेशवर्ती च पितुः पुत्रो भवति धर्मतः॥
en: I am your son. You, O holy one, are my father! You are our king, and you are our preceptor! The son should as dictated by every duty, obey the commands of his father.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः स तु तं प्राह व्यासो वेदविदां वरः। युधिष्ठिरं महातेजाः पुनरेव महाकविः॥ एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि भारत। राजाऽयं वृद्धतां प्राप्तः प्रमाणे परमे स्थितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by the king, Vyasa, that foremost of all persons knowing the Vedas, that foremost of poets gifted with great energy, once more said to Yudhishthira these words, 'It is so, O mighty-armed one! It is as you say, O Bharata! This king has reached old age, He is now in the last stage of life.

sn: सोऽयं मयाभ्यनुज्ञातस्त्वया च पृथिवीपतिः। करोतु स्वमभिप्रायं मास्य विघ्नकरो भव॥
en: Permitted both by me and you, let this king do what he wishes. Do not stand as on obstacle in his way.

sn: एष एव परो धर्मो राजर्षीणां युधिष्ठिर। समरे वा भवेन्मृत्युर्वने वा विधिपूर्वकम्॥
en: This is the highest duty, O Yudhishthira, of royal sages. They should die either in battle or in the forest according to the scriptures.

sn: पित्रा तु तव राजेन्द्र पाण्डुना पृथिवीक्षिता। शिष्यवृत्तेन राजायं गुरुवत् पर्युपासितः॥
en: Your royal father, Pandu, O king of kings, respected this old king as a disciple reverses his preceptor.

sn: क्रतुभिर्दक्षिणावभी रत्नपर्वतशोभितैः। महमिरिष्टं गौर्भुक्ता प्रजाश्च परिपालिताः॥
en: (At that time) he worshipped the celestials in many great sacrifices with profuse gifts consisting of hills of wealth and jewels, and ruled the Earth and protected his subjects wisely and well.

sn: पुत्रसंस्थं च विपुलं राज्यं विप्रोषिते त्वयि। त्रयोदशसमा भुक्तं दत्तं च विविधं वसु॥
en: Having obtained a good number of children and a prosperous kingdom, he enjoyed great riches for thirteen years while you were in exile, and gave away much wealth.

sn: त्वया चायं नरव्याघ्र गुरुशुश्रूषयाऽनघा आराधितः सभृत्येन गान्धारी च यशस्विनी॥
en: Yourself also, O king, with your servants, O sinless one, have worshipped this king and the famous Gandhari with that ready obedience which a disciple pays to his preceptor.

sn: अनुजानीहि पितरं समयोऽस्य तपोविधौ। न मन्युर्विद्यते चास्य सुसूक्ष्मोऽपि युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Do you grant permission to your father. The time has come for his to attend to the practice of penances. He does He does not cherish, O Yudhishthira, even the slightest anger against any of you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतावदुक्त्वा वचनमनुमान्य च पार्थिवम्। तथास्त्विति च तेनोक्तः कौन्तेयेन ययौ वनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said these words, Vyasa, soothed the old king. Yudhishthira, then, answered him, saying, “So be it.' The great ascetic then left the palace for proceeding to the forest.

sn: गते भगवति व्यासे राजा पाण्डुसुतस्तदा। प्रोवाच पितरं वृद्धं मन्दं मन्दमिवानतः॥ यदाह भगवान् व्यासो यच्चापि भवतो मतम्। यथाऽऽह च महेष्वासः कृपो विदुर एव च॥ युयुत्सुः संजयश्चैव तत्कर्तास्म्यहमञ्जसा। सर्व एव हि मान्या मे कुलस्य हि हितैषिणः॥
en: After the holy Vyasa had departed, the royal son of Pandu softly said these words to his old father, bending himself in humility, 'What the holy Vyasa has said, what is your own purpose, what the great bowmen Kripa has said, what Vidura has said, and what has been asked for by Yuyutsu and Sanjaya, I shall quickly do. All these deserve my respect, for all of them are well-wishers of our family.

sn: इदं तु याचे नृपते त्वामहं शिरसा नतः। क्रियतां तावदाहारस्ततो गच्छाश्रमं प्रति॥
en: This, however, O king, I beg of you by bending my head. Do you first eat and afterwards go to your forest-retreat.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो राज्ञाभ्यनुज्ञातो धृतराष्ट्रः प्रतापवान्। ययौ स्वभवनं राजा गान्धार्यानुगतस्तदा।॥
en: Vaishampayana said son Having received the kings' permission, the highly energetic king Dhritarastra, then, went to his own palace, followed by Gandhari.

sn: मन्दप्राणगतिर्धीमान् कृच्छ्रादिव समुद्वहन्। पदातिः स महीपालो जीर्णो गजपतिर्यथा॥
en: With weakened strength and slow motion, that highly intelligent king walked with difficulty, like the leader, exhausted with age, of an elephantine herd.

sn: तमन्वगच्छद् विदुरो विद्वान् सूतश्च संजयः। स चापि परमेष्वासः कृपः शारद्वतस्तथा॥
en: He was followed by the highly learned Vidura, and his charioteer Sanjaya, as also that powerful bowman Kripa the of Sharadvata.

sn: स प्रविश्य गृहं राजन् कृतपूर्वाहिकक्रियः। तर्पयित्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठानाहारमकरोत् तदा॥
en: Entering his palace, O king, he performed the morning rites and, after pleasing many foremost of Brahmanas, he took some food.

sn: गान्धारी चैव धर्मज्ञा कुन्त्या सह मनस्विनी। वधूभिरुपचारेण पूजिताभुङ्क्त भारत॥
en: Gandhari knowing every duty, as also the highly intelligent Kunti, adored with offers of various articles by their daughters-in-law, then took some food, O Bharata.

sn: कृताहारं कृताहारा: सर्वे ते विदुरादयः। पाण्डवाश्च कुरुश्रेष्ठमुपातिष्ठन्त तं नृपम्॥
en: After Dhritarashtra had eaten, and Vidura also and others had done the same, the Pandavas, having finished their meals, approached and sat around the old king.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महाराज कुन्तीपुत्रमुपह्वरे। निषण्णं पाणिना पृष्ठे संस्पृशन्नम्बिकासुतः॥ अप्रमादस्त्वया कार्यः सर्वथा कुरुनन्दन। अष्टाङ्गे राजशार्दूल राज्ये धर्मपुरस्कृते॥
en: Then the son of Ambika, O monarch, addressing Kunti's son, who was seated near him, and touching his back with his hand, said, 'You should always, O delighter of the Kurus, act vigilantly about everything connected with your kingdom consisting of eight limbs, o foremost of kings, and in which the claims of virtue should ever be kept foremost.

sn: तत्त शक्यं महाराज रक्षितुं पाण्डुनन्दन। राज्यं धर्मेण कौन्तेय विद्वानसि निबोध तत्॥
en: You are, O son of Kunti, cndued with intelligence and learning. Listen to me, O king, I tell you what the means are by which, O son of Pandu, the kingdom is capable of being righteously protected.

sn: विद्यावृद्धान् सदैव त्वमुपासीथा युधिष्ठिर। शृणुयास्ते च यद् ब्रूयुः कुर्याश्चैवाविचारयन्॥
en: You should always, O Yudhishthria, honour those persons who are old in learning. You should listen to what they would say, and act accordingly without any scruple.

sn: प्रातरुत्थाय तान् राजन् पूजयित्वा यथाविधि। कृत्यकाले समुत्पन्ने पृच्छेथाः कार्यमात्मनः॥
en: Rising early in the morning, O king, adore them with due rites, and when the time comes for action, you should consult them about your (intended) acts.

sn: ते तु सम्मानिता राजंस्त्वया कार्यहितार्थिना। प्रवक्ष्यन्ति हितं तात सर्वथा तव भारत॥
en: When, led by the desire of knowing what would be beneficial to you about your measures, you honour them, they will, O son, always declare what is for your behoof, O Bharata!

sn: इन्द्रियाणि च सर्वाणि वाजिवत् परिपालय। हितायैव भविष्यन्ति रक्षित द्रविणं यथा॥
en: You should always keep your senses as you keep your horses. They will then prove beneficial to you, like riches that is not wasted.

sn: अमात्यानुपधातीतान् पितृपैतामहाशुचीन्। दान्तान् कर्मसु पुण्यांश्च पुण्यान् सर्वेषु योजयेः॥
en: You should employ only those ministers who have passed the tests of honesty, who are hereditary officers of state, possessed of pure conduct, self-controlled, expert in the discharge of business, and endued with righteous conduct.

sn: चारयेयाश्च सततं चारैरविदितः परैः। परीक्षितैर्बहुविधैः स्वराष्ट्रप्रतिवासिभिः॥
en: You should always gather information through spies in various disguises, whose faithfulness have been tested, who are natives of your kingdom, and who should not be known to your enemies.

sn: पुरं च ते सुगुप्तं स्याद् दृढप्राकारतोरणम्। अट्टाट्टालकसम्बाधं षट्पदं सर्वतोदिशम्॥
en: Your citadel should be properly protected with strong walls and arched gates. On every side such walls, with watch-towers on them standing close to one another, should be made as will admit six persons walking side by side on their top.

sn: तस्य द्वाराणि सर्वाणि पर्याप्तानि बृहन्ति च। सर्वतः सुविभक्तानि यन्त्रैरारक्षितानि च॥
en: The gates should all be large and sufficiently strong. Kept in proper places, those gates should be carefully guarded.

sn: पुरुषैरलमर्थस्ते विदितैः कुलशीलतः। आत्मा च रक्ष्यः सततं भोजनादिषु भारत॥ विहाराहारकालेषु माल्यशय्यासनेषु च। स्त्रियश्च ते सुगुप्ताः स्युर्वृद्धराप्तैरधिष्ठिताः॥ शीलवद्भिः कुलीनैश्च विद्वद्धिश्च युधिष्ठिर।
en: Let your purpose be accomplished through men whose families and conduct are wellknown. You should always protect your body also with care in matters connected with your food, O Bharata, as also in the hours of sport and eating and in matters connected with the garlands you wear and the beds you lie upon. The ladies of your household should be properly protected, looked over by aged and trusted servitors, of good conduct, well-born, and possessed of learning, O Yudhishthira.

sn: मन्त्रिणश्चैव कुर्वीथा द्विजान् विद्याविशारदान्॥ विनीतांश्च कुलीनांश्च धर्मार्थकुशलानृजून्।
en: You should made ministers of Brahmanas possessed of learning, endued with humility, well-born, knowing religion and profit, and adorned with simplicity of behaviour.

sn: तैः सार्धं मन्त्रयेथास्त्वं नात्यर्थं बहुभिः सह॥ समस्तैरपि च व्यस्तैर्व्यपदेशेन केनचित्।
en: You should hold consultations with them. You should not, however, admit many persons into your consultations. on particular occasions you may consult with the whole of your council or with a portion of it.

sn: सुसंवृतं मन्त्रगृहं स्थलं चारुह्य मन्त्रयेः॥ अरण्ये निःशलाके वा न च रात्रौ कथंचन।
en: Entering a chamber or spot that is wellprotected (from intruders) you should hold your consultations. You may hold your consultation in a forest hat is divested of grass. You should never consult at night time.

sn: वानराः पक्षिणश्चैव ये मनुष्यानुसारिणः॥ सर्वे मन्त्रगृहे वा ये चापि जडपङ्गवः।
en: Apes and birds and other animals which can imitatc human beings should all be excluded from the council chamber, as also idiots and lame and palsied individuals.

sn: मन्त्रभेदे हि ये दोषा भवन्ति पृथिवीक्षिताम्॥ न ते शक्या: समाधातुं कथंचिदिति मे मतिः।
en: I think that the evils which originate from the divulgence of the counsels of kings are such that they cannot be remedied.

sn: दोषांश्च मन्त्रभेदस्य ब्रूयास्त्वं मन्त्रिमण्डले॥ अभेदे च गुणा राजन् पुनः पुनररिंदम।
en: You should repeatedly refer, in the midst of your counselors, to the evils which arise from the divulgence of counsels, ochastiser of enemies, and to the merits which flow from counsels properly kept.

sn: पौरजानपदानां न शौचाशौचे युधिष्ठिर॥ यथा स्याद् विदितं राजंस्तथा कार्यं कुरूद्वह।
en: You should, O Yudhishthira, act in such a manner as to determine the merits and faults of the inhabitants of your city and the provinces.

sn: व्यवहरश्च ते राजन् नित्यमाप्तैरधिष्ठितः॥ योज्यस्तुष्टैर्हितै राजन् नित्यं चारैरनुष्ठितः।
en: Let your laws, O king, be always administered by trusted judges placed in charge thereof, who should also be contented and of good conduct. Their acts should also be ascertained by you through spies.

sn: परिमाणं विदित्वा च दण्डं दण्ड्येषु भारत॥ प्रणयेयुर्यथान्यायं पुरुषास्ते युधिष्ठिर।
en: Let your judicial officers, O Yudhishthira, mete out punishments, according to the law, on offenders after careful determining the gravity of the offenses.

sn: आदानरुचयश्चैव परदाराभिमर्शिनः॥ उग्रदण्डप्रधानाश्च मिथ्या व्याहारिणस्तथा। आक्रोष्टारश्च लुब्धश्च हर्तारः साहसप्रियाः।॥ समाविहारभेत्तारो वर्णानां च प्रदूषकाः।
en: They who take bribes, they who are the violators of the chastity of other peoples' wives, they who inflict heavy punishments, they who are liars, they who are revelers, they who are stained by cupidity, they who are murderers, they who are doers of rash deeds, they who are disturbers of assemblies and the sports of others, and they who brings about a confusion of castes, should, according to considerations of time and place, be punished with either fines or death.

sn: हिरण्यदण्ड्या वध्याश्च कर्तव्या देशकालतः॥ प्रातरेव हि पश्येथा ये कुर्युर्व्ययकर्म ते।
en: In the morning you should see those who are employed in making your disbursements. After that you should look to your toilet and then to your food.

sn: अलंकारमथो भोज्यमत ऊर्ध्वं समाचरेः॥ पश्येथाश्च ततो योधान् सदा त्वं प्रतिहर्षयन्।
en: You should next supervise your arms, pleasing them on every occasion. You should devote your evenings to envoys and spies.

sn: दूतानां च चराणां च प्रदोषस्ते सदा भवेत्॥ सदा चापररात्रान्ते भवेत् कार्यार्थनिर्णयः। मध्यरात्रे विहारस्ते मध्याह्ने च सदा भवेत्॥
en: The latter end of the night should be devoted by you to settle what acts should be done by you in the day. Midnight's and midday's should be devoted to amusements and sports. At all times, however, you should think of the means for the execution your projects.

sn: सर्वे त्वौपयिकाः कालाः कार्याणां भरतर्षभ। तथैवालंकृतः काले तिष्ठेथा भूरिदक्षिण॥
en: At the proper time, adorning your body, you should sit prepared to make gifts in profusion. The turns for different deeds, O son, ceaselessly revolve like wheels.

sn: चक्रवत् तात कार्याणां पर्यायो दृश्यते सदा। कोशस्य निचये यत्नं कुर्वीथा न्यायतः सदा॥
en: You should do your best to fill your treasuries of various kinds by fair means. You should avoid all unlawful means for that purpose.

sn: विपिधस्य महाराज विपरीतं विवर्जयेः। चारैर्विदित्वा शुज्रेश्च ये राज्ञामन्तरैषिणः॥
en: Learning through your spies who your enemies are, who are bent on finding out your shortcoming, you should, through trusted agents, cause them to be destroyed from a distance.

sn: तानाप्तैः पुरुषैर्दूराद् घातयेथा नराधिप। कर्म दृष्ट्वाथ भृत्यांस्त्वं वरयेथाः कुरूद्वह॥
en: Examining their conduct, you should, O perpetuator of Kuru's race, appoint your servants. You should cause all your deeds to be accomplished through your servitors whether they are appointed for those acts or not.

sn: कारयेयाश्च कर्माणि युक्तायुक्तैरधिष्ठितैः। सेनाप्रणेता च भवेत् तव तात दृढव्रतः॥
en: The commandant of your army should be of firm conduct, courageous, capable of bearing hardships, loyal, and devoted to your wellbeing.

sn: शूरः क्लेशसहश्चैव हितो भक्तश्च पूरुषः। सर्वे जनपदाश्चैव तव कर्माणि पाण्डव॥
en: Artisans and mechanics, O son of Pandu, living in your provinces, should always do your acts like kine and asses.

sn: गोवद्रासभवश्चैव कुर्युर्ये व्यवहारिणः। स्वरन्ध्र पररन्धं च स्वेषु चैव परेषु च॥ उपलक्षयितव्यं ते नित्यमेव युधिष्ठिर।
en: You should always, O Yudhishthira, be careful to ascertain your own shortcomings as also those of your enemies. The shortcomings also of your own men as also of the men of your enemies should equally be known.

sn: देशजाश्चैव पुरुषा विक्रान्ताः स्वेषु कर्मसु॥ यात्राभिरनुरूपाभिरनुग्राह्या हितास्त्वया।
en: Those men of your kingdom, who are wellskilled in their respective callings, and are devoted to your good, should be patronized by you with adequate means of support.

sn: गुणार्थिनां गुणः कार्यो विदुषां वै जनाधिप। अविचार्याश्च ते ते स्युरचला इव नित्यशः॥
en: A wise king, O chief of men, should always see that the accomplishments of his subjects might be kept up. They would then be firinly devoted to you, seeing that they did not fall away from their skill

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच मण्डलानि च बुध्येथाः परेषामात्मनस्तथा। उदासीनगणानां च मध्यस्थानां च भारत॥
en: Dhritarashtra said You should always ascertain the Mandalas which belong to you, to your enemies, to neutrals, and to those who are disposed equally towards you and your eneinies, O Bharata.

sn: चतुर्णां शत्रुजातानां सर्वेषामाततायिनाम्। मित्रं चामित्रमित्रं च बोद्धव्यं तेऽरिकर्शन॥
en: The Mandalas also of the four kinds of enemies, of those called Atatayins, and of allies, and the allies of enemies, should be distinguished by you, O crusher of enemies.

sn: तथामात्या जनपदा दुर्गाणि विविधानि च। बलानि च कुरुश्रेष्ठ भवत्येषां यथेच्छकम्॥
en: You should sec that the ministers of state, the pcople of the provinces, the garrisons of forts, and the forces, O foremost one of Kuru's race, are not tampered with.

sn: ते च द्वादश कौन्तेय राज्ञां वै विषयात्मकाः मन्त्रिप्रधानाश्च गुणाः षष्टिादश च प्रभो॥
en: The twelve (enumerated above), O son of Kunti, form the principal concerns of kings. These twelve, as also the sixty, having Ministers for their foremost, should be looked after by the king.

sn: एतन्मण्डलमित्याहुराचार्या नीतिकोविदाः। अत्र षाड्गुण्यमायत्तं युधिष्ठिर निबोध तत्॥
en: Politicians call these by the name of Mandala. Understand, O Yudhishthira, that the six incidents (of peace, war, march, halt, sowing dissension's, and conciliation) depend upon these.

sn: वृद्धिक्षयौ च विज्ञेयौ स्थानं च कुरुसत्तम। द्विसप्तत्यां महाबाहो ततः षाड्गुण्यजा गुणाः॥
en: Growth and diminution should also be understood, as also the condition of being stationary. The attributes of the six fold incidents, O you of mighty arms, as resting on the seventy-two (already enumerated), should also be, carefully understood.

sn: थदा स्वपक्षो बलवान् परपक्षस्तथाऽबलः। विगृह्य शत्रून् कौन्तेय जेयः क्षितिपतिस्तदा॥
en: When one's own side has vecome strong and the side of the enemy has become weak, it is them, O son of Kunti, that the king should fight against the enemy and try to acquire victory.

sn: यदा परे च बलिन: स्वपक्षश्चैव दुर्बलः। सार्धं विद्वांस्तदा क्षीणः परैः संधि समाश्रयेत्॥
en: When the enemy is strong and one's own side is weak, then the weak king, if he has intelligence, should try to make peace with the enemy.

sn: द्रव्याणां संचयश्चैव कर्तव्यः सुभहांस्तथा। यदा समर्थो यानाय नचिरेणैव भारत।॥
en: The king should collect a large quantity of articles (for his commissariat). When able to march out, he should on no account make a delay, O Bharata.

sn: तदा सर्वं विधेयं स्यात् स्थाने न स विचारयेत्। भूमिरल्पफला देया विपरीतस्य भारत॥
en: Besides, he should on that occasion set his men to work for which they are fit, without being moved by many other consideration. He should, (when obliged to part with a portion of his territories), give his enemy such land as are not productive of a plentiful harvest.

sn: हिरण्यं कुष्यभूयिष्ठं मित्रं क्षीणमथो बलम्। विपरीतान्निगृह्णीयात् स्वं हि संधिविशारदः॥
en: (When obliged to pay coins), he should give gold containing much base metal. (When obliged to surrender a portion of his army), he should give such men as are not noted for strength. One who is skilled in treatics should, when taking land or gold or men from the enemy, take what is possessed of attributes the reverse of this.

sn: संध्यर्थं राजपुत्रं वा लिप्सेथा भरतर्षभ। विपरीतं न तच्छ्रेयः पुत्र कस्यांचिदापदि॥ तस्याः प्रमोक्षे यत्नं च कुर्याः सोपायमन्त्रवित्। प्रकृतीनां च राजेन्द्र राजा दीनान् विभावयेत्॥
en: In making treaties of peace, the son of the king should be demanded as a hostage, O chief of the Bharatas. A contrary course of conduct would not be wholesome, O son. If a calamity come over the king, he should, with knowledge of means and counsels, try to liberate himself from it. The king, O foremost of kings, should maintain the cheerless and the destitute among his people.

sn: क्रमेण युगपत् सर्वं व्यवसायं महाबलः। पीडनं स्तम्भनं चैव कोशभङ्गस्तथैव च॥
en: Himself protecting his own kingdom, the king, endued with great might, should direct all his efforts, either one one after another or simultaneously. against his of enemies. He should afflict and obstruct them and seek to drain their treasury.

sn: कार्यं यत्नेन शत्रूणां स्वराज्यं रक्षता स्वयम्। न च हिंस्योऽभ्युपगतः सामन्तो वृद्धिमिच्छता॥
en: The king who desires his own advancement, should never injure the subordinate chiefs who are under his sway. O son of Kunti, you should never try your strength with that king who is desirous of conquering the whole Earth.

sn: कौन्तेय तं न हिंसेत् स यो महीं विजिगीषते। गणानां भेदने योगमीप्सेथाः सह मन्त्रिभिः॥ साधुसंग्रहणाच्चैव पापनिग्रहणात् तथा। दुर्वलाश्चैव सततं नान्वेष्टव्या बलीयसा॥
en: You should try to steal a march by producing, with the help your ministers, dissension's among his aristocracy and feudatory chiefs. A powerful king should never seek to root out weak kings, for these do good to the world by cherishing the good and punishing the wicked. O foremost of kings, you should live, conducting yourself like a cane.

sn: तिष्ठेथा राजशार्दूल वैतसी वृत्तिमास्थितः। यद्येनमभियायाच्च बलवान् दुर्बलं नृपः॥
en: If a strong king advances against a weak one, the latter should make him desist, by adopting conciliatory and other modes.

sn: सामादिभिरुपायैस्तं क्रमेण विनिवर्तयेः। अशक्नुवंश्च युद्धाय निष्पतेत् सह मन्त्रिभिः॥
en: If these measures fail, he should, then, with the help of those who are interested in his welfare fall upon the enemy for fighting him out. Indeed, with his ministers, treasury and citizens, he should thus adept force against the invader.

sn: कोशेन पौरैर्दण्डेन ये चास्य प्रियकारिणः। असम्भवे तु सर्वस्य यथा मुख्येन निष्पतेत्। क्रमेणानेन मुक्तिः स्याच्छरीरमिति केवलम्॥
en: If the issue of the battle turns against him, he should, then, fall, sacrificing all his resources one after another, renouncing his life in this way, he will acquire freedom from all sorrow.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच संधिविग्रहमप्यत्र पश्येथा राजसत्तम। द्वियोनि विविधोपायं बहुकल्पं युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O best of kings you should, also, reflect properly on war and peacc. Each is of war kinds. The means are various, and the circumstances also, under which war or peace may be made, are various, O Yudhishthira.

sn: कौरव्य पर्युपासीथाः स्थित्वा द्वैविध्यमात्मनः। तुष्टपुष्टबलः शत्रुरात्मवानिति च स्मरेत्॥
en: O you of Kuru's race, you should, with coolness, reflect on the two (viz., thy strength and weakness) with regard to yourself. You should not suddenly march against an enemy who has contented and healthy soldiers, and who is gifted with intelligence. On the other hand, you should think carefully of the means of defeating him.

sn: पर्युपासनकाले तु विपरीतं विधीयते। आमर्दकाले राजेन्द्र व्यपसर्पेत् ततः परम्॥
en: You should march against an enemy who is not provided with contented and healthy combatants. When everything's is favourable, the enemy may be beaten. After that however, the victor should retire.

sn: व्यसनं भेदनं चैव शत्रूणां कारयेत् ततः। कर्षणं भीषणं चैव युद्धे चैव बलक्षयम्॥
en: He should next cause the enemy to be plunged into various calamities, and show dissension's among his allies. He should afflict the enemy and inspire terror in his heart, and, attacking him, weaken his forces.

sn: प्रयास्यमानो नृपतिस्त्रिविधां परिचिन्तयेत्। आत्मनश्चैव शत्रोश्च शक्तिं शास्त्रविशारदः॥
en: The king, conversant with the scriptures, who marches against an enemy should think of the three kinds of strength, and, indeed, reflect on his own strength and the strength of his enemy.

sn: उत्साहप्रभुशक्तिभ्यां मन्त्रशक्त्या च भारत। उपपन्नो नृपो यायाद् विपरीतं च वर्जयेत्॥
en: Only that king, O Bharata, who is gifted with alacrity, discipline, and strength of counsels should march against an enemy. When his position is otherwise, he should avoid offensive works.

sn: आददीत बलं राजा मौलं मित्रबलं तथा। अटवीबलं भृतं चैव तथा श्रेणीबलं प्रभो॥
en: The king should provide himself with power of wealth, power of allies, power of foresters, power of paid soldiery, and the inechanical and trading classes, powerful power of one.

sn: तत्र मित्रबलं राजन् मौलं चैव विशिष्यते। श्रेणीबलं भृतं चैव तुल्ये एवेति मे मतिः॥
en: Among all these, power of allies and power of riches are superior to the rest. The power of classes and that of the standing army are equal.

sn: तथाऽचारबलं चैव परस्परसमं नृप। विज्ञेयं बहुकालेषु राज्ञा काल उपस्थिते॥
en: The power of spies is considered by the king as equal in efficacy to either of the above, on many occasions, when the tiine comes for applying each.

sn: आपदश्चापि बोद्वव्या बहुरूपा नराधिप। भवन्ति राज्ञा कौरव्य यास्ताः पृथगतः शृणु॥
en: Calamity, O king, with which rulers are overtaken, is of many forms. Listen, O you of Kuru's race, as to what those various forms are.

sn: विकल्पा बहुधा राजन्नापदां पाण्डुनन्दन। सामादिभिरुपन्यस्य गणयेत् तान् नृपः सदा॥
en: Indeed, calamities, O son of Pandu, are many. You should, always, count them, distinguishing their forms, o king, and try to meet them by applying the well-known ways of conciliation and the rest.

sn: यात्रां गच्छेद् बलैर्युक्तो राजा सद्भिः परंतप) युक्तश्च देशकालाभ्यां बलैरात्मगुणैस्तथा॥
en: The king should, when possessed of a good arıny, march (out against a foc), O scorcher of enemics. He should, also, mark the considerations of time and place, while preparing to march, as also the forces he has collected and his own merits.

sn: हृष्टपुष्टबलो गच्छेद् राजा वृद्ध्युदये रतः। अकृशश्चाप्यथो यायादनृतावपि पाण्डव॥
en: That king who seeks his own growth and advancement should not march unless he has cheerful and healthy warriors. When strong, O son of Pandu, he may march in even an unfavourable season.

sn: तूणाश्मानं वानिरथप्रवाहां ध्वजद्रुमैः संवृतकूलरोधसम्। पदातिनागैर्बहुकर्दमां नदी सपत्ननाशे नृपतिः प्रयोजयेत्॥
en: The king should make a river having quivers for its stones, horses and cars for its current, and standards for the trees which cover its banks, and which is miry with foot-soldiers and elephants. Such a river should the king apply for the destruction of his enemy.

sn: अथोपपत्त्या शकटं पद्मवज्रं च भारत। उशना वेद यच्छास्त्रं तत्रेतद् विहितं विभो॥
en: According to the science known to Ushanas, arrays called Shakata, Padma, and Vajra, should be formed, O Bharata, for fighting the enemy.

sn: चारयित्वा परबलं कृत्वा स्वबलदर्शनम्। स्वभूमौ योजयेद् युद्धं परभूमौ तथैव च॥
en: Knowing every thing about the enemy's sirength through spies, and examining his own strength himself, the king should begin war either within his own territories or within those of his cncmy.

sn: बलं प्रसादयेद् राजा निक्षिपेद् बलिनो नरान्। ज्ञात्वा स्वविषयं तत्र सामादिभिरुपक्रमेत्॥
en: The king should, always, please, his army, and hurl all his strongest warriors (against the cncmy). First determine the state of his kingdom, he should apply conciliation or the other well-known mean.

sn: सर्वथैव महाराज शरीरं धारयेदिह। प्रेत्य चेह च कर्तव्यमात्मनिःश्रेयसं परम्॥
en: By all means, O king, should the body be protected. One should do what is highly beneficial for one both in this world and in the next.

sn: एवमेतन्महाराज राजा सम्यक् समाचरन्। प्रेत्य स्वर्गमवाप्नोति प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन्॥
en: The king, O monarch, by acting properly according to these ways, attains to Heaven hereafter, after ruling his subjects piously in this world.

sn: एवं त्वया कुरुश्रेष्ठ वर्तितव्यं प्रजाहितम्। उभयोर्लोकयोस्तात प्राप्तये नित्यमेव हि॥
en: O foremost one of Kurus' race, it is thus that you should always seek the well-being of your subjects for attaining to both the worlds.

sn: भीष्मेण सर्वमुक्तोऽसि कृष्णेन विदुरेण च। मयाप्यवश्यं वक्तव्यं प्रीत्या ते नृपसत्तम॥
en: You have been instructed in all duties by Bhishma, by Krishna, and by Vidura, I should, also, O best of kings, from the affection I bear you, give you these instructions.

sn: एतत् सर्वं यथान्यायं कुर्वीथा भूरिदक्षिणा प्रियस्तथा प्रजानां त्वं स्वर्गे सुखमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: O giver of profuse presents in sacrifices, you should duly do all this. You shall, by acting thus, become dear to your subjects and acquire happiness in the celestial region.

sn: अश्वमेधसहस्रेण यो यजेत् पृथिवीपतिः। पालयेद् वापि धर्मेण प्रजास्तुल्यं फलं लभेत्॥
en: That king who worships the celestials in a hundred horse-sacrifices, and he who rules his subjects piously, acquire merit that is equal.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवमेतत् करिष्यामि यथाऽऽत्थ पृथिवीपते। भूयश्चैवानुशास्योऽहं भवता पार्थिवर्षभ॥
en: Yudhishthira said O king, I shall do as you order me. O foremost of kings, I should be be further instructed by you.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: भीष्मे स्वर्गमनुप्राप्ते गते च मधुसूदने। विदुरे संजये चैव कोऽन्यो मां वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Bhishma has ascended to Heaven. The destroyer of Madhu, has departed (for Dwraka). Vidura and Sanjaya, also (will accompany you to the forest). Who else, therefore, save you, will teach me.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: यत् तु मामनुशास्तीह भवानद्य हिते स्थितः कर्तास्मि तन्महीपाल निर्वृतो भव पार्थिव॥
en: I shall, certainly, follow those instructions which you have today given, desirous of doing good to me. O lord of Earth. Be you assured of this, O king.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः स राजर्षिर्धर्मराजेन धीमता। कौन्तेयं समनुज्ञातुमियेष भरतर्षभ॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by the highly intelligent and just king Yudhishthira, the royal sage, Dhritarashtra, O chief of the Bharatas, wished to obtain the king's permission.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: पुत्र संशाम्यतां तावन्ममापि बलवाश्रमः। इत्युक्त्वा प्राविशद् राजा गान्धार्या भवनं तदा॥
en: And he said, 'Cease, O son. I have been। tired greatly.' Having said these words, the old king entered the apartments of Gandhari.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: तमासनगतं देवी गान्धारी धर्मचारिणी। उवाच काले कालज्ञा प्रजापतिसमं पतिम्॥ अनुज्ञातः स्वयं तेन व्यासेन त्वं महर्षिणा। युधिष्ठिरस्यानुमते कदारण्यं गमिष्यसि॥
en: Pious Gandhari knowing the opportune moments, said these timely words to that husband of hers who resembled a second Lord of all creatures, while resting on a seat :—'You have got the permission of that great Rishis, viz., Vyasa himself. When, however, will you go to the forest, with the permission of Yudhishthira?

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच गान्धार्यहमनुज्ञातः स्वयं पित्रा महात्मना। युधिष्ठिरस्यानुमते गन्तास्मि नचिराद् वनम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Gandhari, I have received the permission of my great sire. With the permission of Yudhishthira (next obtained), I shall soon retire into the forest.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: अहं हि तावत् सर्वेषां तेषां दुर्दूतदेविनाम्। पुत्राणां दातुमिच्छामि प्रेतभावानुगं वसु॥ सर्वप्रकृतिसांनिध्यं कारयित्वा स्ववेश्मनि।
en: I wish, however, to give away some riches capable of following the status of Preta, for all those sons of mine who were addicted to calamitous dice. Indeed, I wish to make those gifts, inviting all the people to my palace.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा धर्मराजाय प्रेषयामास वै तदा।॥ स च तद्वचनात् सर्वे समानिन्ये महीपतिः।
en: Vaishampayana said Having said so (to Gandhari), Dhritarashtra sent for Yudhishthira. The latter, ordered by his uncle, brought all the articles necessary.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: ततः प्रतीतमनसो ब्राह्मणाः कुरुजाङ्गलाः॥ क्षत्रियाश्चैव वैश्याश्च शूद्राश्चैव समाययुः।
en: Many Brahmanas living in Kurujangala, many Kshatriyas, many Vaishyas, and many Shudras also, came to Dhritarashtra' place, with gratified hearts.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: ततो निष्कम्य नृपतिस्तस्मादन्तः पुरात् तदा॥ ददृशे तं जनं सर्वे सर्वाश्च प्रकृतीस्तथा।
en: The old king, coming out of the inner apartments saw them all as also his subjects collected together.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: समवेतांश्च तान् सर्वान् पौरान् जानपदांस्तथा॥ तानागतानभिप्रेक्ष्य समस्तं च सुहृज्जनम्। ब्राह्मणांश्र महीपाल नानादेशसमागतान्॥ उवाच मतिमान् राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। भवन्तः कुरवश्चैव चिरकालं सहोषिताः॥ परस्परस्य सुहृदः परस्परहिते रताः।
en: Seeing all those assembled and citizens and inhabitants of the provinces, and his wellwishers also thus collected together, and the large number of Brahmanas arrived from various kingdoms, king Dhritarashtra of great intelligence, O monarch, said these words :-'You all and the Kurus have lived together for many long years, well-wishers of each other, and each doing good to the other.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: यदिदानीमहं ब्रूयामस्मिन् काल उपस्थिते॥ तथा भवद्भिः कर्तव्यमविचार्य वचो मम।
en: What I shall now say in view of the opportunity that has come, should be done by you all even as disciples accomplish the orders of their preceptors.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: अरण्यगमने बुद्धिर्गान्धारीसहितस्य मे॥ व्यासस्यानुमते राज्ञस्तथा कुन्तीसुतस्य मे।
en: I have set my heart upon retiring into the forest, along with Gandhari as my companion. Vyasa has approved of this, also the son of Kunti.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: भवन्तोऽप्यनुजानन्त मा च वोऽभूद् विचारणा॥ अस्माकं भवतां चैव येयं प्रीतिर्हि शाश्वती। न च सान्येषु देशेषु राज्ञामिति मतिर्मम॥ शान्तोऽस्मि वयसानेन तथा पुत्रविनाकृतः।
en: Let me have your permission too. Do not hesitate in this. That good will, which has always existed between you and us, is not to be seen, I believe, in other kingdoms, between the rulers and the ruled. I am worn out with age on my head. I am destitute of children.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: उपवासकृशश्चास्मि गान्धारीसहितोऽनघाः॥ युधिष्ठिरगते राज्ये प्राप्तश्चास्मि सुखं महत्।
en: You sinless ones, I am emaciated with fasts, along with Gandhari. The kingdom having passed to Yudhishthira, I have enjoyed great happiness.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: मन्ये दुर्योधनैश्वर्याद् विशिष्टमिति सत्तमाः॥ मम चान्धस्य वृद्धस्य हतपुत्रस्य का गतिः। ऋते वनं महाभागास्तन्मानुज्ञातुमर्हथ॥
en: You foremost of men, I think that happiness has been greater than what I could expect from Duryodhana's sovereignty. What other refuge can I have, old as a I am and destitute of children, except the forest? You highly blessed ones, you should grant me the perinission 1 seek.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वे ते कुरुजाङ्गलाः। वाष्पसंदिग्धया वाचा रुरुदुर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: Hearing those words of his, all the residents of Kurujangala bewailed aloud, O best of the Bharatas, with voices choked by tears.

description: Dhritarashtra scttles about returning into forest
sn: तानविब्रुवतः किंचित् सर्वाशोकपरायणान्। पुनरेव महातेजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽव्रीदिदम्॥
en: Desirous of telling those grief stricken people something more, the highly energetic Dhritarashtra once more addressed them and said as follows.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच शान्तनुः पालयामास यथावद् वसुधामिमाम्। तथा विचित्रवीर्यश्च भीष्मेण परिपालितः॥ पालयामास नस्तातो विदितार्थो न संशयः।
en: Dhritarashtra said Shantanu duly ruled this Earth. Likewise, Vichitravirya also, protected by Bhishma, ruled you. Forsooth, you know all this.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: यथा च पाण्डुर्भ्राता मे दयितो भवतामभूत्॥ स चापि पालयामास यथावत् तच्च वेत्थ ह।
en: You know also how Pandu, my brother was dear to me as also to you. He also ruled you duly.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: मया च भवतां सम्यक् शुश्रूषा या कृतानघाः॥ असम्यग् वा महाभागास्तत् क्षन्तव्यमतन्द्रितैः।
en: You sinless ones, I have also served you. Whether those services have come up to the ideal or fallen short of it, you should forgive me, for I have attended to my duties carefully.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: यदा दुर्योधनेनेदं भुक्तं राज्यमकण्टकम्॥ अपि तत्र न वो मन्दो दुर्बुद्धिरपराद्धवान्।
en: Duryodhana also cnjoyed his kingdom without a thorn in his side. Foolish as he was and possessed of wicked understanding, he did not, however. do any wrong to you.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: तस्यापराधाद् दुर्बुद्धेरभिमानान्महीक्षिताम्॥ विमर्दः सुमहानासीदनयात् स्वकृतादथ।
en: Through the fault, however, of that prince of wicked understanding, and through his pride, as also through my own impolicy, a great destruction of the Kshatriyas has taken place.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: तन्मया साधु वाऽपीदं यदि वासाधु वै कृतम्॥ तद् वो हृदि न कर्तव्यं मया बद्धोऽयमञ्जलिः।
en: Whether I have, in that matter, acted rightly or wrongly, I pray you with joined hands to remove all recollections of it from your hearts.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: वृद्धोऽयं हतपुत्रोऽयं दुःखितोऽयं नराधिपः॥ पूर्वराज्ञां च पुत्रोऽयमिति कृत्वानुजानथ।
en: This one is old; this one has lost all his children; this one stricken with sorrow; this one was our king; this one is a descendant of former kings;-considerations like these should induce you to forgive me.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: इयं च कृपणा वृद्धा हतपुत्रा तपस्विनी॥ गान्धारी पुत्रशोकार्ता युष्मान् याचति वै मया।
en: This Gandhari, also is dispirited and old. She. too, has lost her children and is helpless. Stricken with grief or the loss of her hens, she solicits you with me.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: हतपुत्राविमौ वृद्धौ विदित्वा दुःखितौ तथा॥ अनुजानीत भद्रं वो व्रजाव शरणं च वः।
en: Knowing that both of us are old and afflicted and destitute of children, grant us the permission we seck. Blessed be you, we seek your protection.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: अयं च कौरवो राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ सर्वैर्भवद्भिर्द्रष्टव्यः समेपु विपमेषु च।
en: This Kuru king, Yudhishthira the son of Kunti, should be looked after by you all, in weal and woe.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: न जातु विषमं चैव गमिष्यति कदाचन॥ चत्वारः सचिवा यस्य भ्रातरो विपुलौजसः। लोकपालसमा ह्येते सर्वधर्मार्थदर्शिनः॥
en: He who has, four such brothers of abundant prowess, for his counselors will never fall into distress. All of them are conversant with both Virtue and Profit, and resemble the very guardians of the world.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: ब्रह्मेव भगवानेष सर्वभूतजगत्पतिः। युधिष्ठिरो महातेजा भवतः पालयिष्यति॥
en: Like the illustrious Brahman himself, the Lord of the universe with all its creatures, this Yudhishthira of great energy will rule you.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: अवश्यमेव वक्तव्यमिति कृत्वा ब्रवीमि वः। एष न्यासो मया दत्तः सर्वेषां वो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: That which should certainly be said is now said by me. I make over to you this Yudhishthira here as a charge. I entrust you, also to the hands of this hero.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: भवन्तोऽस्य च वीरस्य व्यासभूताः कृता मया। यदेव तैः कृतं किंचिद् व्यलीकं वः सुतैर्मम॥ यदन्येन मदीयेन तदनुज्ञातुमर्हथ।
en: You should all forget and forgive whatever injury has been done to you by those sons of mine who are no longer alive, or, indeed, by any one else belonging to me.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: भवद्भिर्न हि मे मन्युः कृतपूर्वः कथंचन॥ अत्यन्तगुरुभक्तानामेषोऽञ्जलिरिदं नमः।
en: You never cherished any anger again't me on any previous occasion. I join my hands before you who are famous for loyalty. Here, I bow to you all.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: तेषामस्थिरबुद्धीनां लुब्धानां कामचारिणाम्॥ कृते याचेऽद्य वः सर्वान् गान्धारीसहितोऽनघाः।
en: You sinless one, I, with Gandhari by my side, beg your pardon now for anything done to you by ihosc Sons of mine, of restless understanding, sullied by cupidity, and ever acting as their desires prompted.

description: Dhritarashtra announces his intention and apologizes to the citizens
sn: इत्युक्तास्तेन ते सर्वे पौरजानपदा जनाः। नोचुर्वाष्पकला: किंचिद् वीक्षांचक्रुः परस्परम्॥
en: Thus addressed by the old king, all those citizens and dwellers of the provinces, filled with icars, said nothing but only looked at one another.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तास्तु ते तेन पौरजानपदा जनाः। वृद्धेन राज्ञा कौरव्य नष्टसंज्ञा इवाभवन्॥
en: Thus addressed, O you of Kuru's race, by the old king, the citizens and the inhabitants of the provinces stood sometime like men shorn of consciousness.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: तूष्णीम्भूतांस्ततस्तांस्तु बाष्पकण्ठान् महीपतिः। धृतराष्ट्रो महीपालः पुनरेवाभ्यभाषत॥ वृद्धं च हतपुत्रं च धर्मपल्या सहानया। विलपन्तं बहुविधं कृपणं चैव सत्तमाः॥ पित्रा स्वयमनुज्ञातं कृष्णद्वैपायनेन वै। वनवासाय धर्मज्ञा धर्मज्ञेन नृपेण ह॥
en: King Dhritarashtra, finding thein silent, with their throats choked by grief, once more addressed them, saying, 'You best of men, old as I am, and sonless and through cheerlessness of heart, bewailing along with this my wedded wife, I have obtained the permission, in the matter of my retirement into the forest, of my sire, the Island-born Krishna himself, as also of king Yudhishthira, who knows every duty, you righteous dwellers of this kingdom.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: सोऽहं पुनः पुनश्चैव शिरसावनतोऽनघाः। गान्धार्या सहितं तन्मां समनुज्ञातुमर्हथ॥
en: You sinless ones, I with Gandhari, repeatedly solicit you with bent heads, You should all grant us permission.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा कुरुराजस्य वाक्यानि करुणानि ते। सर्वशो राजन् समेताः कुरुजाङ्गलाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these pitiable words of the Kuru king, O monarch, the assembled dwellers of Kurujangala all began to weep.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: उत्तरीयैः करैश्चापि संच्छाद्य वदनानि ते। रुरुदुः शोकसंतप्ता मुहूर्तं पितृमातृवत्॥
en: Covering their faces with their hands and upper garments, all those men, burning with grief, wept for a while as father sand mothers would weep.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: हृदयैः शून्यभूतैस्ते धृतराष्ट्रप्रवासजम्। दुःखं संधारयन्तो हि नष्टसंज्ञा इवाभवन्॥
en: Bearing in their hearts, from which every other thoughts had been removed, the sorrow born of Dhritarashtra's desire to leave the world, they looked like men shorn of consciousness.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: ते विनीय तमायासं धृतराष्ट्रवियोगजम्। शनैः शनैस्तदान्योन्यमब्रुवन् सम्मतान्युत॥
en: Checking that agitation of heart due to the announcement of Dhritarashtra's desire of going to the forest, they gradually were able to address one another, expressing their wishes.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: ततः संधाय ते सर्वे वाक्यान्यथ समासतः। एकस्मिन् ब्राह्मणे राजन् निवेश्योचुनराधिपम्॥
en: Setting their words briefly, O king, they charged a certain Brahmana therewith and thus replied to the old king.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: ततः स्वाचरणो विप्रः सम्मतोऽर्थविशारदः। साम्बाख्यो बढ्चो राजन् वक्तुं समुपचक्रमे॥
en: That learned Brahinana, of good conduct, chosen by unanimous consent, conversant with all subjects, master of all the Rics, and named Samba, tried to speak.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: अनुमान्य महाराजं तत् सदः सम्प्रसाद्य च। विप्रः प्रगल्भो मेधावी स राजानमुवाच ह॥
en: Taking the permission of the whole assembly and with its full approbation, that learned Brahmana of great intelligence, conscious of his own powers, said these words to the king.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: राजन् वाक्यं जनस्यास्य मयि सर्वं समर्पितम्। वक्ष्यामि तदहं वीर तज्जुषस्व नराधिप॥
en: O monarch, the answer of this assembly has been committed to my care. I shall speak it out, O hero! Do you receive it, O king.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: यथा वदसि राजेन्द्र सर्वमेतत् तथा विभो। नात्र मिथ्या वचः किंचित् सुहत्त्वं नः परस्परम्॥
en: What you say, O king of kings, is all true, O powerful one. There is nothing in it that is in even slightly tinctured with untruth, you are our well-wisher, as, indeed, we are yours.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: न जात्वस्य च वंशस्य राज्ञां कश्चित् कदाचन। राजाऽऽसीद् यः प्रजापाल: प्रजानामप्रियोऽभवत्।।१५।
en: Indeed, in this royal family, there never was a king who coming to rulc his subjects, became unpopular with them.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: पितृवद् भ्रातृवच्चैव भवन्तः पालयन्ति नः। न र दुर्योधन: किंचिदयुक्तं कृतवान् नृपः॥
en: You have ruled us like fathers or brothers. King Duryodhana never did us any wrong.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: यथा ब्रवीति धर्मात्मा मुनिः सत्यवतीसुतः। तथा कुरु महाराज स हि नः परमो गुरुः॥
en: Do that, O king, which that righteoussouled ascetic, the son of Satyavati, has said. He is, indeed out foremost of instructors.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: त्यक्ता वयं तु भवता दुःखशोकपरायणाः। भविष्यामश्चिरं राजन् भवद्गुणशतैर्युताः॥
en: Left by you, O king, we shall have to pass our days in grief and sorrow, remembering hundreds of virtues possessed by you.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: यथा शान्तनुना गुप्ता राज्ञा चित्राङ्गदेन च। भीष्मवीर्योपगूढेन पित्रा तव च पार्थिव॥ भवदुद्वीक्षणाच्चैव पाण्डुना पृथिवीक्षिता। तथा दुर्योधनेनापि राज्ञा सुपरिपालताः॥
en: We were well-protected and ruled by king Duryodhana even as we had been ruled by king Shantanu, or by Chitrangada, or by your father, O monarch, who was protected by the prowess of Bhishma, or by Pandu, that ruler of Earth, who was overlooked by you in all is deeds.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: न स्वल्पमपि पुत्रस्ते व्यलीकं कृतवान् नृद! पितरीव सुविश्वस्तास्तस्मिन्नपि नराधिपे॥
en: Your son, O monarch, never did us the slightest wrong. We lived, depending on that king as trustfully as on our own father.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: वयमास्म यथा सम्यग् भवतो विदितं तथा। तथा वर्षसहस्राणि कुन्तीपुत्रेण धीमता॥
en: It is known to you how we lived (under that ruler). Similarly we have enjoyed great happiness, O king, for thousands of years, under the rule of Kunti's son of great intelligence and wisdom.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: पाल्यमाना धृतिमता सुखं विन्दामहे नृप। राजर्षीणां पुराणानां भवतां पुण्यकर्मणाम्॥ कुरुसंवरणादीनां भरतस्य च धीमतः। वृत्तं समनुयात्येष धर्मात्मा भूरिदक्षिणः॥
en: This righteous-souled king who celebrates sacrifices with profuse gifts, follows the conduct of the royal sages of old, belonging to our race, of meritorious decds, having Kuru and Samavara and other sand the highly intelligent Bharata among them.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: नात्र वाच्यं महाराज सुसूक्ष्ममपि विद्यते। उषिताः स्म सुखं नित्यं भवता परिपालिताः॥
en: There is nothing, O monarch, that is even slightly censurable in the matter of this Yudhishthishta's rule. Protected and ruled by you, we have all lived in great happiness.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: सुसूक्ष्मं च व्यलीकं ते सपुत्रस्य न विद्यते। यत् तु ज्ञातिविमर्देऽस्मिन्नात्थ दुर्योधनं प्रति॥ भवन्तमनुनेष्यामि तत्रापि कुरुनन्दन।
en: The slightest omission cannot be laid at your doors and yours sons. Regarding what you have said about Duryodhana in the matter of this destruction of kinsmen, I beg you, O delighter of the Kurus, (to listen to me).

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: न तद् दुर्योधनकृतं न च तद् भवता कृतम्॥ न कर्णसौबलाभ्यां च कुरवो यत् क्षयं गताः।
en: The carnage that has overtaken the Kurus was not caused by Duryodhana. It was not brought about by you. Nor was it brought about by Karna and Subala's son.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: दैवं तत् तु विजानीमो यन्न शक्यं प्रवाधितुम्॥ दैवं पुरुषकारेण न शक्यमपि बाधितुम्।
en: We know that it was encompassed about by Destiny, and that it was incapable of being counteracted. Destiny is not capable of being resisied by human exertion.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: अक्षौहिण्यो महाराज दशाष्टौ च समागताः॥ अष्टादशाहेन हताः कुरुभिर्योधपुगवैः। भीष्मद्रोणकृपाद्यैश्च कर्णेन च महात्मना॥ युयुधानेन वीरेण धृष्टद्युम्नेन चैव ह। चतुर्भिः पाण्डुपुत्रैश्च भीमार्जुनयमैस्तथा॥ न च क्षयोऽयं नृपते ऋते दैवबलादभूत्।
en: Eighteen Akshauhinis of soldiers, O monarch, were collected. In eighteen days that army was destroyed by the foremost of Kuru warriors, viz., Bhishma and Drona and others, and the great Karna, and the heroic Yuyudhana and Dhritadyumna, and by the four sons of Pandu, that is, Bhima and Arjuna and the twins. This destruction, O kiing, could not happen without the influence of Destiny.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: अवश्यमेव संग्रामे क्षत्रियेण विशेषतः॥ कर्तव्यं निधनं काले मर्तव्यं क्षत्रबन्धुना। तैरियं पुरुषव्याप्रैर्विद्याबाहुबलान्वितैः॥ पृथिवी निहता सर्वा सहया सरथद्विपा।
en: Forsooth, by Kshatriyas in particular, should enemies be killed and death encountered in battle. By those foremost of men, gifted with science and might of arms, the Earth has been exterminaled with her horses and cars and elephants.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: न स राज्ञां वधे सूनुः कारणं ते महात्मनाम्॥ न भवान् न च ते भृत्या न कर्णो न स सौबलः।
en: Your son was not the cause of that destruction of great kings. You were not the cause, nor your servants, nor Karna, nor Subala's son.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: यद् विशस्ताः कुरुश्रेष्ठ राजानश्च सहस्रशः॥ सर्वं दैवकृतं विद्धि कोऽत्र किं वक्तुमर्हति।
en: The destruction of those for-most ones of Kuru's race and of kings by thousands know, was engendered by Destiny. Who can say anything else in this.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: गुरुर्मतो भवानस्य कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभुः॥ धर्मात्मानमतस्तुभ्यमनुजानीमहे सुतम्।
en: You are regarded as the preceptor and the master of the whole world. We, therefore, in you presence, absolve your righteous-souled son.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: लभतां वीरलोकं स ससहायो नराधिपः॥ द्विजाग्र्यैः समनुज्ञातस्त्रिदिवे मोदतां सुखम्।
en: Let that king, with all his associates, obtain the regions reserved for herocs Permitted by foremost of Brahmanas, let him sport blissfully in the celestial region.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: प्राप्स्यते च भवान् पुण्यं धर्मे च परमां स्थितिम्॥३८ वेद धर्मं च कृत्स्नेन सम्यक् त्वं भव सुव्रतः।
en: You, also shall attain to great merit, and unswerving steadiness in virtue. O you of excellent vows, follow fully the duties laid down in the Vedas.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: दृष्टिप्रदानमपि ते पाण्डवान् प्रति नो वृथा॥ समर्थास्त्रिदिवस्यापि पालने किं पुनः क्षितेः।
en: It is not necessary for either you or ourselves to look after the Pandavas. They are capable of ruling the very Heavens, what need then be said of the Earth?

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: अनुवय॑न्ति वा धीमन् समेषु विषमेषु च।॥ प्रजाः कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ पाण्डवाशीलभूषणान्।
en: O you of great intelligence, in weal as in woe, the subjects of this kingdom, O foremost one of Kuru's race, will obey the Pandavas who have conduct for their ornament.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: ब्रह्मदेयाग्रहारांश्च पारिवहश्चि पार्थिवः॥ पूर्वराजाभिपन्नांश्च पालयत्येव पाण्डवः।
en: The son of Pandu makes those valuable gifts which are always to be made to foremost of twice-born persons in sacrifices and in obscquial rites, after the manner of all the great kings of yore.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: दीर्घदर्शी मृदुर्दान्तः सदा वैश्रवणो यथा॥ अक्षुद्रसचिवश्चायं कुन्तीपुत्रो महामनाः।
en: The great son of Kunti is mild, and selfcontrolled, and is always disposed to spend as if he were a second Vaishravana. He has great ministers who attend on him.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: अप्यमित्रे दयावांश्च शुचिश्च भरतर्षभः॥ ऋजु पश्यति मेधावी पुत्रवत् पालितः सदा।
en: He is compassionate to even his enemies. Indeed, that foremnost one of Bharata's race is of pure conduct. Gifted with great intelligence, he is perfectly straightforward in his dealings and rules and protects us like a father his children.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: विप्रियं च जनस्यास्य संसर्गाद् धर्मजस्य वै॥ न करिष्यन्ति राजर्षे तथा भीमार्जुनादयः।
en: From association with him who is the son of Dharma, O royal sage, Bhima and Arjuna and others will never wrong us in the least.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: मन्दा मृदुषु कौरव्य तीक्ष्णेष्वाशीविषोपमाः॥ वीर्यवन्तो महात्मानः पौराणां च हिते रताः।
en: They are mild, O you of Kuru's race, to them that are inild, and fierce like snakes of dreadful poison to them who are fierce. Endured with great energy, those high-souled ones are always devoted to the well-being of the people.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: न कुन्ती न च पाञ्चाली न चोलूपी न सात्वती।।४६ अस्मिन् जने करिष्यन्ति प्रतिकूलानि कर्हिचित्।
en: Neither Kunti, nor your (daughter-in-law) Panchali, nor Ulupi, nor the princess of the Satvata race, will do the least wrong to these people.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: भवत्कृतमिमं स्नेहं युधिष्ठिरविवर्धितम्॥ न पृष्ठतः करिष्यन्ति पौरा जानपदा जनाः।
en: The affection which you have shown towards us and which in Yudhishthira is seen to exist in a still larger measurc, is incapable of being forgotten by the people of the city and the provinces.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: अधर्मिष्ठानपि सतः कुन्तीपुत्रा महारथाः॥ मानवान् पालयिष्यन्ति भूत्वा धर्मपरायणाः।
en: Those powerful car-warriors, viz., the sons of Kunti, themselves devoted to the duties of virtue, will protect and cherish the people even if these happen to be unrighteous.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: स राजन् मानसं दुःखमपनीय युधिष्ठिरात्॥ कुरु कार्याणि धाणि नमस्ते पुरुषर्षभ।
en: Do you, therefore, O king, reinoving all anxiety of heat on account of Yudhishthira, set yourself to the accomplishment of all meritorious deeds, O foremost of men.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं धर्म्यमनुमान्य गुणोत्तरम्॥ साधु साध्विति सर्वः स जनः प्रतिगृहीतवान्।
en: Hearing these words, fraught with virtue and merit, of that Brahmana and approving of them every person in that assembly said, 'Excellent, Excellent' and accepted them as his own.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: धृतराष्ट्रश्च तद्वाक्यमभिपूज्य पुनः पुनः॥ विसर्जयामास तदा प्रकृतीस्तु शनैः शनैः।
en: Dhritarashtra, also, repeatedly speaking highly of those words, slowly dismissed that assembly of his subjects.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: स तैः सम्पूजितो राजा शिवेनावेक्षितस्तथा॥ प्राञ्जलिः पूजयामास तं जनं भरतर्षभ।
en: Thus honoured by them and looked upon with auspicious looks, the old king, O chief of Bharata's race, joined his hands and honoured them all in returi.

description: The history of the war as described by a Brahmana
sn: ततो विवेश भवनं गान्धार्या सहितो निजम्।। व्युष्टायां चैव शर्वर्यां यच्चकार निबोध तत्॥
en: He, then, entered his own palace with Gandhari, Listen now to what he did after that night had passed away.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो रजन्यां व्युष्टायां धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। विदुरं प्रेषयामास युधिष्ठिर निवेशनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said After that night had passed away, Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, sent Vidura to Yudhishthira's place.

sn: स गत्वा राजवचनादुवाचाच्युतमीश्वरम्। युधिष्ठिरं महातेजाः सर्वबुद्धिमतां वरः॥ धृतराष्ट्रो महाराजो वनवासाय दीक्षितः। गमिष्यति वनं राजन्नागतां कार्तिकीमिमाम्॥
en: Gifted with great energy and the foremost of all persons endued with intelligence, Vidura. having arrived at at Yudhishthira's palace, addressed that foremost of men, that king of undecaying glory, in these words:—King Diritarashtra has perforined the preliminary rites for accomplishing his purpose of retiring into the forest. He will start for the woods, O king, on the coming day of full moon of the month of Kartika.
