sn: स त्वां कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ किंचिदर्थमभीप्सति। श्राद्धमिच्छति दातुं स गाङ्गेयस्य महात्मनः॥ द्रोणस्य सोमदत्तस्य बालीकस्य च धीमतः। पुत्राणां चैव सर्वेषां ये चान्ये सुहृदो हताः॥ यदि चाप्यनुजानीषे सैन्धवापसदस्य च।
en: He now solicits from you, O foremost of Kuru's race, some money. He wishes to perform the Shraddha of the great son of Ganga, as also of Drona and Somadatta and Vallika of great intelligence, and of all his sons as also of all other wishers of his who have been killed, and, if you permit it, of that wicked king of the Sindhus.

sn: नरर्षभम्। एतच्छुत्वा तु वचनं विदुरस्य युधिष्ठिरः॥ हृष्टः सम्पूजयामास गुडाकेशश्च पाण्डवः।
en: Hearing these words of Vidura, both Yudhishthira, and Pandus' son Arjuna of curly hair, became very glad and applauded them highly.

sn: न च भीमो दृढक्रोधस्तद्वचो जगृहे तदा॥ विदुरस्य महातेजा दुर्योधनकृतं स्मरन्। अभिप्रायं विदित्वा तु भीमसेनस्य फाल्गुनः॥ किरीटी किंचिदानम्य तमुवाच भीम राजा पिता वृद्धो वनवासाय दीक्षितः॥
en: Bhima, however, of great energy and an unappeasable anger, did not accept those words of Vidura in good spirits, recollecting the acts of Duryodhana. Understanding the thoughts of Bhimasena, the diadem-decked Phalguna, slightly bending bending his face downwards, addressed that foremost of men in these words: 'O Bhima, our royal lather who is old, has resolved to retire into the forest.

sn: दातुमिच्छति सर्वेषां सुहृदामौर्ध्वदेहिकम्। भवता निर्जितं वित्तं दातुमिच्छति कौरवः॥
en: He wishes to make gifts for advancing the happiness of his killed kinsmen and wellwishers now in the other world. O you of Kuru's race, he wishes to give away wealth that belongs to you by conquest.

sn: भीष्मादीनां महाबाहो तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि। दिष्ट्या त्वद्य महाबाहो धृतराष्ट्रः प्रयाचते॥ याचितो यः पुरास्माभिः पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्। योऽसौ पृथिव्याः कृत्स्नाया भर्ता भूत्वा नराधिपः॥१२ परैर्विनिहतामात्यो वनं गन्तुमभीप्सति। मा तेऽन्यत् पुरुषव्याघ्र दानाद् भवतु दर्शनम्॥
en: Indeed, O mighty-armed one, it is for Bhishma and others that the old king is desirous of making those gifts. You should grant your permission. By good luck it is, O you of mighty arms, that Dhritarashtra today begs wealth of us, he who was formerly begged by us. Mark the reverses brought about by time. That king who was before the lord and protector of the whole Earth, now wishes to go into the forest, his kinsmen and associates all killed by enemies. O king, let not your views deviate from granting the permission asked.

sn: अयशस्यमतोऽन्यत् स्यादधर्मश्च महाभुज। राजानमुपशिक्षस्व ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरमीश्वरम्॥
en: O mighty-armed one, refusal, besides bringing infamy, will yield demerit. Do you learn your duty in this matter from the king, your eldest brother, who is lord of all.

sn: अर्हस्त्वमपि दातुं वै नादातुं भरतर्षभ। एवं ब्रुवाणं वीभत्सुं धर्मराजोऽप्यपूजयत्॥
en: You should give instead of refusing, O chief of Bharata's race!' Bibhatsu who was saying so was applauded by king Yudhishthira the just.

sn: भीमसेनस्तु सक्रोधः प्रोवाचेदं वचस्तदा। वयं भीष्मस्य दास्यामः प्रेतकार्यं तु फाल्गुन॥ सोमदत्तस्य नृपते रिश्रवस एव च। बाह्रीकस्य च राजर्षेनॊणस्य च महात्मनः॥ अन्येषां चैव सर्वेषां कुन्ती कर्णाय दास्यति। श्राद्धानि पुरुषव्याघ्र मा प्रादात् कौरवो नृपः॥
en: Yielding to anger Bhimasena said these words :-O Phalguna, it is we that shall make gifts in the matter of Bhishma's obsequies, as also of king Somavatta and of Bhurishravas, of the royal sage Valhika, and of the great Drona, and of all others. Our mother Kunti shall make such obsequial offerings for Karna. O foremost of men, let not Dhritarashtra perform those Sharaddhas.

sn: इति मे वर्तते बुद्धिर्मा नो निन्दन्तु शत्रवः। कष्टात्कष्टतरं यान्तु सर्वे दुर्योधनादयः॥
en: This is what I think. Let not our enemies be gladdened. Let Duryodhana and others sink from a miserable to a more miserable position.

sn: यैरियं पृथिवी कृत्स्ना घातिता कुलपांसनैः। कुतस्त्वमसि विस्मृत्य वैरं द्वादशवार्षिकम्॥ अज्ञातवासं गहनं द्रौपदीशोकवर्धनम्। क्व तदा धृतराष्ट्रस्य स्नेहोऽस्मन्द्रोचरो गतः॥ सार्धं पाञ्चालपुत्र्या
en: Alas, it was those wretches of their family who caused the whole Earth to be exterininated? How have you been able to forget that anxiety of twelve long years and out living in deep forest in cognite that was so painful to Draupadi? Where was Dhritarashtra's affection for us then?

sn: कृष्णाजिनोपसंवीतो हृताभरणभूषणः। त्वं राजानमुपजग्मिवान्।॥
en: Clad in a black deer-skin and divested of all your ornaments, with the Princess of Panchala in your company, did you not follow this king?

sn: क्व तदा द्रोणभीष्मौ तौ सोमदत्तोऽपि वाऽभवत्। यत्र त्रयोदशसमा वने वन्येन जीवथ॥
en: Where were Bhishma and Drona then, and where was Somadatta? You had to live for thirteen years in the forest depending on the products of the wilderness.

sn: न तदां त्वां पिता ज्येष्ठः पितृत्वेनाभिवीक्षते। किं ते तद् विस्मृतं पार्थ यदेष कुलपांसनः॥ दुर्बुद्धिर्विदुरं प्राह द्यूते किं जितमित्युत। तमेवं वादिनं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। उवाच वचनं धीमान् जोषमास्वेति भर्त्सयन्॥
en: Your eldest father did not then look at you with eyes of parental affection. Have you forgotten, O Partha, that it was this wretch of our family, of wicked understanding, who enquired of Vidura, when the match at dice was going on, 'What has been won?' Hearing thus far, king Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, gifted with great intelligence, rebuked him and told him to be silent.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: अर्जुन उवाच भीम ज्येष्ठो गुरुर्मे त्वं नातोऽन्यद् वक्तुमुत्सहे। धृतराष्ट्रस्तु राजर्षिः सर्वथा मानमर्हति॥
en: Arjuna said O Bhima, you are my elder brother and, therefore, my senior and preceptor. I dare not say anything more than what I have already said. The royal sage Dhritarashtra deserves to be honoured by us in every way.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: न स्मरन्त्यपराद्धानि स्मरन्ति सुकृतान्यपि। असम्भिन्नार्यमर्यादाः साधवः पुरुषोत्तमाः॥
en: They who are good, they who are distinguished above the common level, they who break not the distinctions which characterise the good, remember which characterise the good, remember not the wrongs done to them but only the benefits they have got.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा फाल्गुनस्य महात्मनः। विदुरं प्राह धर्मात्मा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ इदं मद्वचनात् क्षत्तः कौरवं ब्रूहि पार्थिवम्। यावदिच्छति पुत्राणां श्राद्धं तावद् ददाम्यहम्॥ भीष्मादीनां च सर्वेषां सुहृदामुपकारिणाम्। मम कोशादिति विभो मा भूद् भीम: सुदुर्मनाः॥
en: Hearing these words of the great Phalguna, the righteous-souled Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, addressed Vidura and said these words, "Instructed by me, O Kshatri, do you say to the Kuru king that I shall give him as much wealth from my treasury as he wishes to give away for the obsequies of his sons, and of Bhishma and others among his well-wishers and benefactors, let not Bhima be dispirited at this.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा धर्मराजस्तमर्जुनं प्रत्यपूजयत्। भीमसेनः कटाक्षेण वीक्षां चक्रे धनंजयम्॥
en: Having said these words, king Yudhishthira the just highly applauded Arjuna. Meanwhile Bhimasena began to cast angry looks at Dhananjaya.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: ततः स विदुरं धीमान् वाक्यमाह युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेने न कोपं स नृपतिः कतुमर्हति॥
en: Then Yudhishthira, gifted with great intelligence, once more addressed Vidura said, King Dhritarashtra should not be angry with Bhimasena.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: परिक्लिष्टो हि भीमोऽपि हिमवृष्ट्यातपादिभिः। दुःखैर्बहुविधैर्धीमानरण्ये विदितं तव॥
en: This Bhima of great intelligence was greatly afflicted by cold and rain and heat and by a thousand others griefs while living in the forest. All this you know.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: किं तु मद्वचनाद् ब्रूहि राजानं भरतर्षभ। यद् यदिच्छसि यावच्च गृह्यतां मद्गृहादिति॥
en: Do you, however, instructed by me, say to the king, O foremost one of Bharata's family, that he may take from my house whatever articles he wishes and in whatever measure also he likes.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: यन्मात्सर्यमयं भीमः करोति भृशदुःखितः। न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यमिति वाच्यः स पार्थिवः॥
en: You shall also tell the king that he should not suffer his heart to remember this show of pride in which Bhima, deeply afflicted, has indulged.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: यन्ममास्ति धनं किंचिदर्जुनस्य च वेश्मनि। तस्य स्वामी महाराज इति वाच्यः स पार्थिवः॥
en: Whatever wealth I have and whatever Arjuna has in his house, the owner thereof is king Dhritarashtra. This you should tell him.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: ददातु राजा विप्रेभ्यो यथेष्टं क्रियतां व्ययः। पुत्राणां सुहृदां चैव गच्छत्वानृण्यमद्य सः॥
en: Let the king made gifts to Brahmanas! Let him spend as largely as he likes. Let him liberate himself from the debt he owes to his sons and well-wishers.

description: Arjuna advises Bhima, to give up his hostile feelings
sn: इदं चापि शरीरं मे तवायत्तं जनाधिप। धनानि चेति विद्धि त्वं न मे तत्रास्ति संशयः॥
en: Let him be told besides, 'O monarch this very body of mine is at your disposal, and all the riches I have! Know this and let there be no doubt in this.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु राज्ञा स विदुरो बुद्धिसत्तमः। धृतराष्ट्रमुपेत्यैवं वाक्यमाह महार्थवत्॥ उक्तो युधिष्ठिरो राजा भवद्वचनमादितः। स च संश्रुत्य वाक्यं ते प्रशशंस महाद्युतिः॥
en: Thus addressed by king Yudhishthira, Vidura, that foremost of intelligent persons, returned to Dhritarashtra and said to hin these words of great significance, 'I at first reported your message to king Yudhishthira, Reflecting on your words, Yudhishthira of great splendour spoke highly of them.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: बीभत्सुश्च महातेजा निवेदयति ते गृहान्। वसु तस्य गृहे यच्च प्राणानपि च केवलान्॥
en: The highly energetic Bibhatsu, also, places all his places with all the riches therein, as also his very lifc-breaths, at your disposal.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: धर्मराजश्च पुत्रस्ते राज्यं प्राणान् धनानि च। अनुजानाति राजर्षे यच्चान्यदपि किंचन॥
en: Your son, king Yudhishthira, too, offers you, O royal sage, his kingdom and life-breaths and riches and all else which belongs to him.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: भीमश्च सर्वदुःख नि संस्मृत्य बहुलान्युत। कृच्छ्रादिव महाबाहुरनुजज्ञे विनिःश्वसन्॥
en: Bhima, however, of mighty-arins, recollecting all his numberless sorrows has with difficulty given his consent, breathing many heavy sighs.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: स राजन् धर्मशीलेन राज्ञा बीभत्सुना तथा। अनुनीतो महाबाहुः सौहृदे स्थापितोऽपि च॥
en: That mighty-armed hero, O monarch, was solicited by the righteous king as also by Bibhatsu, and induced to treat you cordially.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: न च मन्युस्त्वया कार्य इति त्वां प्राह धर्मराट्। संस्मृत्य भीमस्तद्वैरं यदन्यायवदाचरत्॥ एवं प्रायो हि धर्मोऽयं क्षत्रियाणां नराधिप। युद्धे क्षत्रियधर्मे च निरतोऽयं वृकोदरः॥
en: King Yudhishthira the just has prayed you not to be displeased for the improper conduct which Bhima has shown at the recollection of foriner hostilities. This is generally the conduct of Kshatriyas in battle, O king, and this Vrikodara is devoted to battle and the practices of Kshatriyas.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: वृकोदरकृते चाहमर्जुनश्च पुनः पुनः। प्रसीद याचे नृपते भवान् प्रभुरिहास्ति यत्॥ तद् ददातु भवान् वित्तं यावदिच्छसि पार्थिव। त्वमीश्वरोऽस्य राज्यस्य प्राणानामपि भारत॥
en: Both myself and Arjuna, O king, repeatedly beg you for pardoning Vrikodara. Be gracious to us. You are our lord, O king, you can give away as you like whatever money we have. You, O Bharata, are the master of this kingdom and of all lives in it.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: ब्रह्मदेयाग्रहारांश्च पुत्राणामौर्ध्वदेहिकम्। इतो रत्नानि गाश्चैव दासीदासमजाविकम्॥ आनयित्वा कुरुश्रेष्ठो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयच्छतु। दीनान्धकृपणेभ्यश्च तत्र तत्र नृपाज्ञया॥
en: Let the foremost one of the Kuru race give away for the obsequial rites of his sons, all those foremost of gifts which should be given to the Brahmanas. Indeed, let him make those gifts to persons of the twice-born caste, taking away from our places jewels, gems, and kine, and slaves both male and female, and goats and sheep. Let gifts be made to also those who are poor or blind or in great distress, selecting the objects of his charity as he likes.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: बह्वन्नरसपानाढ्याः सभा विदुर कारय। गवां निपानान्यन्यच्च विविधं पुण्यकं कुरु॥
en: Let, O Vidura, large pavilions be made, rich with food and drink of various tastes collected in abundance. Let reservoirs of water be made for enabling kine to drink, and let other meritorious works be done.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: इति मामब्रवीद् राजा पार्थश्चैव धनंजयः। यदत्रानन्तरं कार्यं तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: These were the words said to me by the king as also by Pritha's son Dhananjaya. You should say what should be done next.

description: Vidura communicates to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira's apology for Bhima's conduct
sn: इत्युक्ते विदुरेणाथ धृतराष्ट्रोऽभिनन्द्य तान्। मनश्चक्रे महादाने कार्तिक्यां जनमेजय॥
en: After Vidura had said these words, O Janamejaya, Dhritarashtra expressed his satisfaction at them and made up his mind for making large presents on the day of full moon in the month of Kartika.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विदुरेणैवमुक्तस्तु धृतराष्ट्रो जनाधिपः। प्रीतिमानभवद् राजन् राज्ञो जिष्णोश्च कर्मणि॥
en: Thus accosted by Vidura, king, Dhritarashtra became highly please, O monarch, with the act of Yudhishthira and Jishnu.

sn: ततोऽभिरूपान् भीष्माय ब्राह्मणानृषिसत्तमान्। पुत्रार्थे सुहृदश्चैव स समीक्ष्य सहस्रशः॥ कारयित्वान्नपानानि यानान्याच्छादनानि च। सुवर्णमणिरत्नानि दासीदासमजाविकम्॥ कम्बलानि च रत्नानि ग्रामान् क्षेत्रं तथा धनम्। सालङ्कारान् गजानश्वान् कन्याश्चैव वरस्त्रियः॥ उद्दिश्योद्दिश्य सर्वेभ्यो ददौ स नृपसत्तमः। द्रोणं संकीर्त्य भीष्मं च सोमदत्तं च बाह्निकम्॥ दुर्योधनं च राजानं पुत्रांश्चैव पृथक् पृथक्। जयद्रथपुरोगांश्च सुहृदश्चापि सर्वशः॥
en: Inviting then, after proper examination, superior Rishis, for the sake of Bhishma, as also of his sons and friends, and causing a large quantity of food and drink to be prepared, and cars and other vehicles and clothes, and gold and jewels and gems, and slaves both male and female, and goals and sheep, and blankets and rich articles to be collected, and villages and fields, and other kinds of wealth to be kept ready, as also elephants and horses decked with ornaments, and many beautiful maidens who were the best of their sex, that foremost of kings gave them away for the behoof of the dead, naming each of them in due order as the gifts were made. Naming Drona, Bhishma, Somadatta, Valhika, and king Duryodhana, and each one of his other sons, and all his well wishers with Jayadratha as the first, those gifts were made in due order.

sn: स श्राद्धयज्ञो ववृते बहुशो धनदक्षिणः। अनेकधनरत्नौघो युधिष्ठिरमते तदा॥
en: With the approval of Yudhishthira, that, Shraddha-sacrifice became marked by large gifts of wealth and profuse presents of jewels and gems and other kinds of riches.

sn: अनिशं यत्र पुरुषा गणका लेखकास्तदा। युधिष्ठिरस्य वचनादपृच्छन्त स्म तं नृपम्॥ आज्ञापय किमेतेभ्यः प्रदायं दीयतामिति। तदुपस्थितमेवात्र वचनान्ते ददुस्तदा॥
en: Teller sand scribes on that occasion, under the orders of Yudhishthira, ceaselessiy asked the old king, Do you command, O king, what gifts should be made to these, All things are ready here-As soon as the king spoke, they gave away what he directed.

sn: शतदेये दशशतं सहस्र चायुतं तथा। दीयते वचनाद् राज्ञः कुन्तीपुत्रस्य धीमतः॥
en: A thousand was given to him that was to receive a hundred and ten thousand was given to him that was to receive a thousand, at the command of the royal son of Kunti.

sn: एवं स वसुधाराभिर्वर्षमाणो नृपाम्बुदः। तर्पयामास विप्रांस्तान् वर्षन् सस्यमिवाम्बुद॥
en: Like the clouds refreshing the crops with their downpours, that royal cloud pleased the Brahinanas by downpours of riches.

sn: ततोऽनन्तरमेवात्र सर्ववर्णान् महामते। अन्नपानरसौघेण प्लावयामास पार्थिवः॥
en: After all those gifts had been distributed, the king, O you of great intelligence, then deluged the assembled guests of all the four castes with repeated surges of food and drink of various tastes.

sn: स वस्त्रधनरत्नौधे मृदङ्गनिनदो महान्। गवाश्चमकरावर्तो नानारत्नमहाकरः॥ ग्रामाग्रहारद्वीपाढ्यो मणिहेमजलार्णवः। जगत् सम्प्लावयामास धृतराष्ट्रोडुपोद्धतः॥
en: Indeed, the Dhritarashtra-ocean, swelling high, with jewels and gems for its waters, rich with the villages and fields and other foremost of gifts making its verdant islands, heaps of various kinds of precious articles for its rich caves, elephants and horses for its alligators and whirlpools, the sound of Mridangas for its deep roars, and clothes and wealth and precious stones for its waves, deluged the Earth.

sn: एवं स पुत्रपौत्राणां पितृणामात्मनस्तथा। गान्धार्याश्च महाराज प्रददावौर्ध्व देहिकम्॥
en: It was thus, O king, that that monarch made gifts for the behoof, in the other world, of his sons and grandsons and departed manes as also of himself and Gandhari.

sn: परिश्रान्तो यदासीत् स ददद् दानान्यनेकशः। निवर्तयामास तदा दानयज्ञं नराधिपः॥
en: At last when he became tired with the work of making such profuse gifts, that great GiftSacrifice ended.

sn: एवं स राजा कौरव्य चक्रे दानमहाक्रतुम्। नटनर्तकलास्याढ्यां बह्वन्नरसदक्षिणम्॥
en: Thus did that king of Kuru's race celebrate his Gift-Sacrifice. Actors and mimes continually danced and sang on the occasion and contributed to the pleasure of all the guests. Food and drink of various tastes were given away in profusion.

sn: दशाहमेवं दानानि दत्त्वा राजाम्बिकासुतः। बभूव पुत्रपौत्राणामनृणो भरतर्षभ॥
en: Making gifts in this way for ten days, the royal son of Ambika, O chief of Bharatas' race, became liberated from the debts he owed to his sons and grandson. became liberated from the debts he owed to his sons and grandson.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः प्रभाते राजा स धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। आहूय पाण्डवान् वीरान् वनवासे कृतक्षणः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having settled the hour of his departure for the forest, the royal son of Ambika, viz., Dhritarashtra, summoned those heroes, the Pandavas.

sn: गान्धारीसहितो धीमानभ्यनन्दद् यथाविधि। कार्तिक्यां कारयित्वेष्टिं ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः॥ अग्निहोत्रं पुरस्कृत्य बल्कलाजिनसंवृतः। वधूजनवृतो राजा निर्ययौ भवनात् ततः॥
en: Endued with great intelligence, the old king, with Gandhari, duly accosted those princes. Having caused the minor rites to be performed, by Brahmanas knowing the Vedas, on that day which was the day of full moon in the month of Kartika, he caused the fire which he adored daily to be taken up. Casting off his proper dress he wore deer-skins and barks, and accompanied by his daughters-in-law, he left is palace.

sn: ततः स्त्रियः कौरवपाण्डवानां याश्चापराः कौरवराजवंश्याः। तासां नादः प्रादुरासीत् तदानीं वैचित्रवीर्ये नृपतौ प्रयाते॥
en: When the royal son of Vichitravirya thus started, the Pandava and the Kaurava ladies as also other women belonging to the Kaurava race, began to bewail aloud.

sn: ततो लाजैः सुमनोभिश्च राजा विचित्राभिस्तद् गृहं पूजयित्वा। सम्यूज्याथै त्यवर्गं च सर्वे ततः समुत्सृज्य ययौ नरेन्द्रः॥
en: The king adored the palace in which he had lived with fried paddy and excellent flowers of various kinds. He also honoured all his servants with gifts of wealth, and then leaving that house set out on his journey.

sn: ततो राजा प्राञ्जलिर्वेपमानो युधिष्ठिरः सस्वरं वाष्पकण्ठः। विमुच्योच्चैर्महानादं हि साधो क्व यास्यसीत्यपतत् तात भूमौ॥
en: Then, O son, king Yudhishthira, trembling all over, with words choked by tears, said these words in aloud voice, viz., 'O righteous king, where do you go?' and fell down in a swoon.

sn: तथार्जुनस्तीव्रदुःखाभितप्तो मुहुर्मुहुनिःश्वसन् भारताग्र्यः। युधिष्ठिरं मैवमित्येवमुक्त्वा निगृह्याथो दीनवत् सीदमानः॥
en: Arjuna, burning with great grief, sighed repeatedly. That foremost of Bharata princes, telling Yudhishthira that he should not behave thus, stood cheerlessly and with heart plunged into distress.

sn: वृकोदरः फाल्गुनश्चैव वीरौ माद्रीपुत्रौ विदुरः संजयश्चा वैश्यापुत्रः सहितो गौतमेन धौम्यो विप्राश्चान्वयुर्बाष्पकण्ठाः॥
en: Vrikodara, the heroic Phalguna, the two sons of Madri, Vidura, Sanjaya, Dhritarashtra's son by his Vaishya wife, and Kripa, and Dhaumya, and other Brahmanas, all followed the old king with voices choked in grief.

sn: कुन्ती गान्धारी बद्धनेत्रां व्रजन्ती स्कन्धासक्तं हस्तमथोद्वहन्ती। राजा गान्धार्याः स्कन्धदेशेऽवसज्य पाणिं ययौ धृतराष्ट्रः प्रतीतः॥
en: Kunti walked first, carrying on her shoulders the hand of Gandhari who walked with her bandaged eyes. King Dhritarashtra walked confidently behind Gandhari, placing his hand on her shoulder.

sn: तथा कृष्णा द्रौपदी सात्वती च बालापत्या चोत्तरा कौरवी च। चित्राङ्गदा याश्च काश्चिस्त्रियोऽन्याः सार्धं राज्ञा प्रस्थितास्ता वधूभिः॥
en: Drupada's daughter Krishna, she of the Salvata race, Uttara the daughter-in-law of the Kauravas, who had recently become a mother. . Chitrangada, and other ladies attached to the royal house, all followed the old king.

sn: तासां नादो रुदतीनां तदासीद् राजन् दुःखात् कुररीणामिवोच्चैः। ततो निष्पेतुर्ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियाणां विट्शूद्राणां चैव भार्याः समन्तात्॥
en: The wail they uttered at that time, O king, from sorrow, resembled the loud lainentations of a swarm of she-ospreys. Then the wives of the citizens-Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas and Shudras-also came out into the streets from all sides.

sn: तन्निर्याणे दुःखितः पौरवर्गो गजाह्वये चैव बभूव राजन्! यथा पूर्वं गच्छतां पाण्डवानां द्यूते राजन् कौरवाणां सभाया:॥
en: At Dhritarashtra's departure, O king, all the citizens of Hastinapur became as distressed as they had been, O monarch, when they had seen the departure of the Pandavas in former days after their defeat at the match at dice.

sn: या नापश्यंश्चन्द्रमसं न सूर्य रामाः कदाचिदपि तस्मिन् नरेन्द्र। महावनं गच्छति कौरवेन्द्रे शोकेनार्ता राजमार्ग प्रपेदुः॥
en: Ladies who had never seen the sun or the moon, came out into the streets on that occasion, in grcat sorrow, when king Dhritarashtra proceeded towards the great forest.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: तत: प्रासादहर्येषु वसुधायां च पार्थिव। नारीणां च नराणां च नि:स्वनः सुमहानभूत्॥
en: Great was the uproar, at that time, O king, of both men and women standing on the terraces of palaces or on the Earth.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: स राजा राजमार्गेण नृनारीसंकुलेन च। कथंचिनिर्ययौ धीमान् वेपमानः कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: Endued with great intelligence, the old king, with joined hands, and trembling with weakness, passed with difficulty along the principal street which was crowded with persons of both sexes.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: स वर्द्धमानद्वारेण निर्ययौ गजसाह्वयात्। विसर्जयामास च तं जनौघं स मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: He left the city of Hastinapur by the principal gate, and then repeatedly asked that crowd of people to return to their homes.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: वनं गन्तुं च विदुरो राज्ञा सह कृतवणः । संजयश्च महामात्रः सूतो गावल्गणिस्तथा॥
en: Vidura had made up his mind for going to the forest with the king. The Suta Sanjaya also, the son of Gavalgani, the chief minister of Dhritarashtra, was of the same heart.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: कृपं निवर्तयामास युयुत्सुं च महारथम्। धृतराष्ट्रो महीपाल परिदाप्य युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: King Dhritarashtra, however, caused Kripa and the powerful car-warrior Yuyutsu 10 refrain from following him. He made them over to Yudhishthira's hands.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: निवृत्ते पौरवर्गे च राजा सान्त:पुरस्तदा। धृतराष्ट्राभ्यनुज्ञातो निवर्तितुमियेष ह॥
en: After the citizens had ceased following the monarch, king Yudhishthira, with the ladies of his house, prepared to stop, at the command of Dhritarashtra you desist.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: सोऽब्रवीन्मातरं कुन्तीं वनं तमनुजग्मुषीम्। अहं राजानमन्विष्ये भवती विनिवर्तताम्॥
en: Seeing that his other Kunti was desirous of retiring into the forest, the king said to her, 'I shall follow the old king. Do

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: वधूपरिवृता राज्ञि नगरं गन्तुमर्हसि। राजा यात्वेष धर्मात्मा तापस्ये कृतनिश्चयः॥
en: You should, O queen, return to the city, accompanied by these your daughters-in-law! This king, goes to the forest, determined upon practicing penances.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: इत्युक्ता धर्मराजेन बाष्पव्याकुललोचना। जगामैव तदा कुन्ती गान्धारी परिगृह्य ह॥
en: Though king Yudhishthira said these words to her, with his eyes bathed in tears, Kunti, however, without answering him, continued to go, catching hold of Gandhari.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: कुन्ती उवाच सहदेवे महाराज माऽप्रसादं कृथाः क्वचित्। एष मामनुरक्तो हि राजंस्त्वां चैव सर्वदा॥
en: Kunti said O king, never neglect Sahadeva. He is very much attached to me, O monarch, and to you also always.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: कर्णं स्मरेथाः सततं संग्रामेष्वपलायिनम्। अवकीर्णो हि समरे वीरो दुष्प्रज्ञया तदा॥
en: You should always bear in mind Karna who never retreated from battle. Through my folly that hero has been killed in the field of battle.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: आयसं हृदयं नूनं मन्दाया मम पुत्रका यत् सूर्यजमपश्यन्त्याः शतधा न विदीर्यते॥
en: Surely, my son, this heart of mine is made of steel, since it does not break into a hundred pieces at not sceing that child born of the SunGod.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: एवं गते तु किं शक्यं मया कर्तुमरिंदम। मम दोषोऽयमत्यर्थं ख्यापितो यन्न सूर्यजः॥
en: When such has been the case, O chastise of enemies, what can I now do? I am very much to blame for 1101 having said the truth about the birth of Surya's child.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: तन्निमित्तं महाबाहो दानं दद्यास्त्वमुत्तमम्। सदैव भ्रातृभिः सार्धं सूर्यजस्यारिमर्दन॥
en: O crusher of enemies, I hope you will, with all your brothers, make excellent gifts for the sake of that son of the Sun-God.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: द्रौपद्याश्च प्रिये नित्यं स्थातव्यमरिकर्शन। भीमसेनोऽर्जुनश्चैव नकुलश्च कुरूद्वह॥
en: O mower of enemies, you should always do what is agreeable to Draupadi. You should look after Bhimasena and Arjuna and Nakula and Sahadeva. The charge of the Kuru race have now fallen on you, O king.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: समाधेयास्त्वया राजंस्त्वय्यद्य कुलधूर्गता। श्रश्रूश्वशुरयोः पादान् शुश्रूषन्ती वने त्वहम्॥
en: I shall live in the forest with Gandhari, besmearing my body with fifth, engaged in the practice of penances, and devoted to the service of my father-in-law and mother-in-law.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गान्धारीसहिता वत्स्ये तापसी मलपङ्किनी। एवमुक्तः स धर्मात्मा भ्रातृभिः सहितो वशी। विषादमगपद् धीमान् न च किंचिदुवाच ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by her, the virtuous Yudhishthira, with passions under complete restraint, became, with all his brothers, plunged into great sorrow. Gifted with grcat intelligence, the king said not a word.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: मुहूर्तमिव तु ध्यात्वा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। उवाच मातरं दीनश्चिन्ताशोकपरायणः॥
en: Having thought for a inoment, king Yudhishthira just, dispirited and plunged in anxiety and sorrow, said to his mother, saying,

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: किमिदं ते व्यवसितं नैव त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि। न त्वामभ्यनुजानामि प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: What, indeed, is your object? You should not do it. I can never grant you permission! you should show us mercy.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: पुरोद्यतान् पुरा ह्यस्मानुत्साह्य प्रियदर्शने। विदुलाया वचोभिस्त्वं नास्मान् संत्यक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Formerly, when we were about to leave Hastinapur for the forest, O you of agreeable features, It was you who, reciting to us the story of Vidula's instructions to her son, stimulated us to exertion. You should not leave us now.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: निहत्य पृथिवीपालान् राज्यं प्राप्तमिदं मया। तव प्रज्ञामुपश्रुत्य वासुदेवान्नरर्षभात्॥
en: Having killed the kings of Earth, I have acquired sovereignty, guided by your wise words communicated through Vasudeva.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: क्व सा बुद्धिरियं चाद्य भवत्या यच्छुतं मया। क्षत्रधर्मे स्थितिं चोक्त्वा तस्याश्च्यवितुमिच्छसि॥
en: Where now is that understanding of yours about which I had heard from Vasudeva? Do you wish now to deviate from those Kshatriya practices about which you had instructed us?

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: अस्मानुत्सृज्य राज्यं च स्नुषा हीमा यशस्विनि। कथं वत्स्यसि दुर्गेषु वनेष्वद्य प्रसीद मे॥
en: Leaving ourselves, this kingdom, and this illustrious daughter-in-law of yours, how will you live in the inaccessible forest? Do you relent.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: इति बाष्पकला वाचः कुन्ती पुत्रस्य शृण्वती। सा जगामाश्रुपूर्णाश्री भीमस्तामिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Kunti, with tears in her eyes, heard these words of her son, but continued to go her way. Then Bhima addressed her, saying,

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: यदा राज्यमिदं कुन्ति भोक्तव्यं पुत्रनिर्जितम्। प्राप्तव्या राजधर्माश्च तदेयं ते कुतो मतिः॥
en: When, O Kunti, sovereignty has been acquired, and when the time has coine for you to enjoy that sovereignty thus acquired by your children, when the duties of royalty await discharge by you, whence has this desire entered into your mind?

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: किं वयं कारिताः पूर्वे भवत्या पृथिवीक्षयम्। कस्य हेतोः परित्यज्य वनं गन्तुमभीप्ससि॥
en: Why then did you causc us to exterminate the Earth? Why would you leave all and wish to take up your residence in the forest?

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: वनाच्चापि किमानीता भवत्या बालका वयम्। दुःखशोकसमाविष्टौ माद्रीपुत्राविमौ तथा॥
en: We were born in the forest. Why then did you bring us from the forest while we were children? See, the two sons of Madri are overwhelmed with sorrow and grief.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: प्रसीद मातर्मा गास्त्वं वनमद्य यशस्विनि। श्रियं यौधिष्ठिरी मात(क्ष्व तावद् बलार्जिताम्॥
en: Relent, O mother! O you of great fame, do not go into the forest now! Do you enjoy that prosperity which, acquired by power, has become Yudhishthira's today.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: इति सा निश्चितैवाशु वनवासाय भाविनी। लालप्यतां बहुविधं पुत्राणां नाकरोद् वचः॥
en: Firmly resolved to retire into the forest, Kunti disregarded these lamentations of her sons.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: द्रौपदी चान्वयाच्छ्वधू विषण्णवदना तदा। वनवासाय गच्छन्ती रुदती भद्रया सह॥
en: Then Draupadi, with a cheerless face, accompanied by Subhadra, followed her weeping mother-in-law who was proceeding on from desire of going into the forest.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: सा पुत्रान् रुदतः सर्वान् मुहुर्मुहुरवेक्षती। जगामैव महाप्राज्ञा वनाय कृतनिश्चया॥
en: Highly wise and firmly resolved on retirement from the world, the blessed dame walked on, frequently loO king at her weeping children.

description: Kunti's determination to follow the blind king
sn: अन्वयुः पाण्डवास्तां तु सभृत्यान्तः पुरास्तथा। तत: प्रमृज्य साश्रूणि पुत्रान् वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The Pandavas, with all their wives and servitors, continued to follow her. Restraining then her tears, she addressed her children in these words.

sn: कुन्ती उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि पाण्डवा कृतमुद्धर्षणं पूर्वं मया वः सीदतां नृपाः॥
en: Kunti said-What you say, O mighty-armed son of Pandu, is indeed, true! O kings, formerly, when you were all dispirited, indeed, I cxcited you all.

sn: द्यूतापहृतराज्यानां पतितानां सुखादपि। ज्ञातिभिः परिभूतानां कृतमुद्धर्षणं मया।॥
en: Seeing that your kingdom was taken away from you by a match at dice, seeing that you all fell from happiness, seeing that you were governed over by kinsmen, I instilled courage and high thoughts into your minds.

sn: कथं पाण्डोर्न नश्येत संततिः पुरुषर्षभाः। यशश्च वो न नश्येत इति चोद्धर्षणं कृतम्॥
en: O foremost of men, I encouraged you so that the sons of Pandu might not be lost, so that their fame might not be lost.

sn: यूयमिन्द्रसमाः सर्वे देवतुल्यपराक्रमाः। मा परेषां मुखप्रेक्षाः स्थेत्येवं तत् कृतं मया॥
en: You are all equal to Indra. Your prowess resembles that of the very celestials. I acted thus so that you might not live, depending upon others.

sn: कथं धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठो राजा त्वं वासवोपमः। पुनर्वने न दुःखी स्या इति चोद्धर्षणं कृतम्॥
en: I instilled courage into your hearts so that you who are the foremost of all righteous persons, who are equal to Vasava, might not again go into the forest and live in misery.

sn: नागायुतसमप्राणः ख्यातविक्रमपौरुषः। नायं भीमोऽत्ययं गच्छेदिति चौद्धर्षणं कृतम्॥
en: I instilled courage into your hearts so that this Bhima who has the strength of ten thousand elephants and whose prowess and manliness are widely known, might not sink into insignificance and ruin.

sn: भीमसेनादवरजस्तथायं वासवोपमः। विजयो नावसीदेत इति चोद्धर्षणं कृतम्॥
en: I instilled courage into your hearts so that this Vijaya, who was born after Bhimasena, and who is equal to Vasava himself, might not be cheerless.

sn: नकुलः सहदेवश्च तथेमौ गुरुवर्तिनौ। क्षुधा कथं न सीदेतामिति चोद्धर्षणं कृतम्॥
en: I instilled courage into your hearts so that Nakula and Sahadeva, who are always devoted to their elders, may not be weakened and rendered cheerless by hunger.

sn: इयं च बृहती श्यामा तथात्यायतलोचना। वृथा सभातले क्लिष्टा मा भूदिति च तत् कृतम्॥
en: I acted thus in order that this lady of welldeveloped forms and of large eyes might not suffer the wrongs inflicted on her in the public hall without being avenged.

sn: प्रेक्षतामेव वो भीम वेपन्तीं कदलीमिव। स्त्रीधर्मिणीमरिष्टाङ्गी तथा द्यूतपराजिताम्॥ दुःशासनो यदा माद् दासीवत् पर्यकर्षत। तदैव विदितं मह्यं पराभूतमिदं कुलम्॥
en: Before you all, O Bhima, trembling all over like a plantain trce during her catamenial period, and after she had been won at dicc, Dushasana, through folly, dragged her as if she were a slave. I knew all this, Indeed, the family of Pandu had been subjugated (by focs).

sn: निषण्णाः कुरवश्चैव तदा मे श्वशुरादयः। सा दैवं नाथमिच्छन्ती व्यलपत् कुररी यथा॥
en: The Kurus, viz., my father-in-law and others, were cheerless when she, desirous of a protector, bewailed like a she-osprey.

sn: केशपक्षे परामृष्टा पापेन हतबुद्धिना। यदा दुःशासनेनैषा तदा मुह्याम्यहं नृपाः॥
en: When she was dragged by her fair locks by the sinful Dushasana without little intelligence, I lost my senses, O king.

sn: युष्मत्तेजोविवृद्ध्यर्थं मया हुद्धर्षणं कृतम्। तदानीं विदुलावाक्यैरिति तद् वित्त पुत्रकाः॥
en: Know, that for increasing your energy, I instilled that courage into your hearts by reciting the words of Vidula, O my sons.

sn: कथं न राजवंशोऽयं नश्येत् प्राप्य सुतान् मम्। पाण्डोरिति मया पुत्रास्तस्मादुद्धर्षणं कृतम्॥
en: I instilled courage into your hearts, O my sons, so that the family of Pandu, represented by my children, might not be lost.

sn: न तस्य पुत्राः पौत्रा वा क्षतवंशस्य पार्थिव।। लभन्ते सुकृताँल्लोकान् यस्माद् वंशः प्रणश्यति।।१६।
en: The sons and grandsons of that person who brings a family to infamy never succeed in acquiring the regions of the righteous. Indeed, the ancestors of the Kaurava race, were in danger of losing those happy regions which had become theirs.

sn: भुक्तं राज्यफलं पुत्रा भर्तुर्मे विपुलं पुरा। महादानानि दत्तानि पीतः सोमो यथाविधि॥
en: As for myself, O my sons, I have, before this, enjoyed the grcat fruits of that sovereignty which my husband had won. I have made large gifts. I have duly drunk the Soma-juice in sacrifice.

sn: नाहमात्मफलार्थं वै वासुदेवमचूचुदम्। विदुलायाः प्रलापैस्तैः पालनार्थं च तत् कृतम्॥
en: It was not for my own sake that I had urged Vasudeva with the stirring words of Vidula. It was for your sake that I had asked you to follow that advice.

sn: नाहं राज्यफलं पुत्राः कामये पुत्रनिर्जितम्। पतिलोकानहं पुण्यान् कामये तपसा विभो॥
en: O my sons, I do not wish for the fruits of that sovereignty which has been acquired by my children. O you of great power, I wish to attain, by my penances, to those happy regions which have been acquired by my husband.

sn: श्वश्रूश्वशुरयोः कुत्वा शुश्रूषां वनवासिनोः। तपसा शोषयिष्यामि युधिष्ठिर कलेवरम्॥
en: By rendering obedient service to my fatherin-law and mother-in-law both of whom with to take up their residence in the forest, and by penances, I wish, O Yudhishthira, to exhaust my body.

sn: निवर्तस्व कुरुश्रेष्ट भीमसेनादिभिः सह। धर्मे ते धीयतां बुद्धिर्मनस्तु महदस्तु च॥
en: Do you cease to follow me, O foremost one of Kuru's race, along with Bhima and others. Let your understanding be always devoted to virtue. Let your mind be always great.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कुन्त्यास्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा पाण्डवा राजसत्तम। वीडिताः संन्यवर्तन्त पाञ्चाल्या सहिताऽनघाः॥
en: Hearing these words of Kunti, the sinless Pandavas, O best of kings, became ashamed. They, therefore, desisted, along with the princess of Panchala, from following her.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: ततः शब्दो महानेव सर्वेषामभवत् तदा। अन्तःपुराणां रुदतां दृष्ट्वा कुन्ती तथागताम्॥
en: Seeing Kunti determined upon going into the forest, the ladies of the Pandava family uttered loud lamentations.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: प्रदक्षिणमथावृत्य राजानं पाण्डवास्तदा। अभिवाद्य न्यवर्तन्त पृथां तामनिवर्त्य वै॥
en: The Pandavas then went round the king and saluted him duly. They ccased to follow further, having failed to persuade Pritha to return.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। गान्धारी विदुरं चैव समाभाष्यावगृह्य च॥ युधिष्ठिरस्य जननी देवी साधु निवर्त्यताम्। यथा युधिष्ठिरः प्राह तत् सर्वं सत्यमेव हि॥
en: Then Ambika's energetic son, viz., Dhritarashtra, addressing Gandhari and Vidura and supporting himself on them, said, Let the royal mother of Yudhishthira cease to go with us! What Yudhishthira has said, is all very true.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: पुत्रैश्वर्यं महदिदमपास्य च महाफलम्। का नु गच्छेद् वनं दुर्गं पुत्रानुत्सृज्य मूढवत्॥
en: Renouncing this high prosperity of her sons, abandoning those high fruits that may be hers, why should she go into the inaccessible forest, leaving her children like a person of little intelligence?

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: राज्यस्थया तपस्तप्तुं कर्तुं दानव्रतं महत्। अनया शक्यमेवाद्य श्रूयतां च वचो मम॥
en: Living in the enjoyment of sovereignty, she is capable of practicing penances and observing the great vow of gifts. Let her, therefore, listen to my words.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: गान्धारि परितुष्टोऽस्मि वध्वाः शुश्रूषणेन वै तस्मात् त्वमेनां धर्मज्ञे समनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: O Gandhari, I have been much pleased with the services rendered to me by this daughter-inlaw of mine. Conversant as you are with all duties, you should command her to return.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: इत्युक्ता सौबलेयी तु राज्ञा कुन्ती मुवाच ह। तत् सर्वं राजवचनं स्वं च वाक्यं विशेषवत्॥
en: Thus addressed by her husband, the daughter of Subala repeated to Kunti all those words of the old king and added her own words of grave meaning.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: न च सा वनवासाय देवी कृतमति तदा। शक्नोत्युपावर्तयितुं कुन्ती धर्मपरां सतीम्॥
en: She, however, could not make Kunti to desist inasmuch as that chaste lady, devoted to virtue, had determined upon living in the forest.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: तस्यास्तां तु स्थिति ज्ञात्वा व्यवसायं कुरुस्त्रियः। निवृत्तांश्च कुरुश्रेष्ठान् दृष्ट्वा प्ररुरुदुस्तदा॥
en: The Kuru ladies, understanding how firm her resolution was about her retirement into the forest, and seeing that those foremost ones of Kuru's race (viz., their own lords), had ceased to follow her, began to bewail aloud.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: उपावृत्तेषु पार्थेषु सर्वास्वेव वधूषु च। ययौ राजा महाप्राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रो वनं तदा॥
en: After all the sons of Pritha and all the ladies had returned homewards, the highly wise king Yudhishthira his journey to the forest.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: पाण्डवाश्चातिदीनास्ते दुःखशोकपरायणाः। यानैः स्त्रीसहिताः सर्वे पुरं प्रविविशुस्तदा॥
en: The Pandavas, exceedingly cheerless and stricken with grief and sorrow accompanied by their wives, returned to the city, on their cars.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: तदहष्टमनानन्दं गतोत्सवमिवाभवत्। नगरं हास्तिनपुरं सस्त्रीवृद्धकुमारकम्॥
en: At that time the city of Hastinapur, with its entire population of men, both old and young, and women, became dispirited and plunged into grief. No festivals of rejoicing were observed.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: सर्वे चासन् निरुत्साहा: पाण्डवा जातमन्यवः। कुन्त्या हीनाः सुदुःखार्ता वत्सा इव विनाकृताः॥
en: Afflicted with grief, the Pandavas were shorn of energy. Abandoned by Kunti, they were deeply afflicted with grief, like calves destitute of their dais.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्तु तेनाला गत्वा सुमहदन्तरम्। ततो भागीरथीतीरे निवासमकरोत् प्रभुः॥
en: Dhritarashtra reached that day a place far distant from the city. The powerful king arrived at last on the banks of the Bhagirathi and took rest there for the night.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: प्रादुष्कृता यथान्यायमग्नयो वेदपारगैः। व्यराजन्त द्विजश्रेष्ठैस्तत्र तत्र तपोवने॥ प्रादुष्कृताग्निरभवत् स च वृद्धो नराधिपः।
en: Brahmanas knowing the Vedas duly ignited their sacred fires in that retreat of ascetics. Surrounded by those foremost of Brahmanas, those sacred fires shonc forth in beauty. The sacred fire of the old king was also lighted up.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: स राजाग्नीन् पर्युपास्य हुत्वा च विधिवत् तदा॥ संध्यागत सहस्रांशुमुपातिष्ठत भारत।
en: Sitting near his own fire, he poured libations on it according to due rites, and then adored the thousand-raycd sun as he was on the point of setting.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: विदुरः संजयश्चैव राज्ञः शय्यां कुशैस्ततः॥ चक्रतुः कुरुवीरस्य गान्धार्याश्चाविदूरतः।
en: Then Vidura and Sanjaya made a bed for the king by spreading some blades of Kusha grass. Near the bed of that Kuru hero they made another for Gandhari.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: गान्धार्याः संनिकर्षे तु निषसाद कुशे सुखम्॥ युधिष्ठिरस्य जननी कुन्ती साधुव्रते स्थिता।
en: Near to Gandhari, Yudhishthira's mother Kunti, observant of excellent vows, happily laid herself down.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: तेषां संश्रवणे चापि निषेदुर्विदुरादयः॥ याजकाश्च यथोद्देशं द्विजा ये चानुयायिनः।
en: Within bearing-distance of those three, slept Vidura and others. The Yajaka Brahmanas and other followers of the king laid slept on their respective beds.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: प्राधीतद्विजमुख्या सा सम्प्रज्वलितपावका॥ बभूव तेषां रजनी ब्राह्मीव प्रीतिवर्धिनी।
en: The foremost of Brahmanas, who were there, chanted aloud many sacred hymns. The sacrificial fires blazed forth all around. That night, therefore, seemed as delightful to them as a Brahmi night.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: ततो रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां कृतपुर्वाह्निकक्रियाः॥ हुत्वाग्निं विधिवत् सर्वे प्रययुस्ते यथाक्रमम्।
en: When the night passed away, thcy all arose from their beds and performed their morning acts. Pouring libations then on the sacred fire, they continued their journey.

description: The arrival of the party at the forest
sn: उदगमुखा निरीक्षन्त उपवासपरायणाः॥ स तेषामतिदुःखोऽभून्निवास: प्रथमेऽहनि। शोचतां शोचमानानां पौरजागदैर्जनैः॥
en: Their first days' expe:"ence of the forest proved very painful to them of grieving hearts, them who were grieved by the inhabitants of both the city and the provinces of the Kuru kingdom.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो भागीरथीतीरे मेध्ये पुण्यजनोचिते। निवासमकरोद् राजा विदुरस्य मते स्थितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Acting according to the advice of Vidura, the king took up his residence on the banks of the Bhagirathi which were sacred and deserved to be inhabited by the righteous.

sn: तत्रैनं पर्युपातिष्ठन् ब्राह्मणा वनवासिनः। क्षत्रविट्शूद्रसंघाश्च बहवो भरतर्षभ।॥
en: There many Brahmanas who had taken up their residence in the forest, as also many Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras, came to see the old king.

sn: स तैः परिवृतो राजा कथाभिः परिनन्ध तान्। अनुजज्ञे सशिष्यान् वै विधिवत् प्रतिपूज्य च॥
en: Silting in their midst, he plcased them all by his words. Having duly adored the Brahmanas with their disciples, he disinissed them all.

sn: सायाह्ने स महीपालस्ततो गङ्गामुपेत्य च। चकार विधिवच्छौचं गान्धारी च यशस्विनी॥
en: As evening camne, the king, and the illustrious Gandhari, both descended into the stream of the Bhagirathi and duly performed their ablutions for purifying themselves.

sn: ते चैवान्ये पृथक् सर्वे तीर्थेष्वाप्लुत्य भारत। चक्रुः सर्वाः क्रियास्तत्र पुरुषा विदुरादयः॥
en: The king and the queen, and Vidura and others, O Bharata, having bathed in the sacred river, performed the usual rites of religion.

sn: कृतशौचं ततो वृद्धं श्वशुरं कुन्तिभोजजा। गान्धारी च पृथा राजन् गङ्गातीरमुपानयत्॥
en: After the king had purified himself by a bath, the daughter of Kuntibhoja, gently conducted both him who was to her as her father-in-law, and Gandhari, from the water into the dry bank.

sn: राज्ञस्तु याजकस्तत्र कृतो वेदीपरिस्तरः। जुहाव तत्र वह्निं स नृपतिः सत्यसङ्गरः॥
en: The Yajakas had made a sacrificial alter there for the king. Devoted to truth, the latter poured libations then on the fire.

sn: ततो भागररथीतीरात् कुरुक्षेत्रं जगाम सः। सानुगो नृपतिर्वृद्धो नियतः संयतेन्द्रियः॥
en: From the banks of the Bhagirathi the old king, with his followers, observing vows and with senses controlled, then proceeded to Kurukshetra.

sn: तत्राश्रमपदं धीमानभिगम्य स पार्थिवः। आससादाथ राजर्षि शतयूपं मनीषिणम्॥
en: Endued with great intelligence, the king arrived at the hermitage of the royal sage Shatayupa of grcat wisdom and saw him.

sn: स हि राजा महानासीत् केकयेषु परंतपः। स्वपुत्रं मनुजैश्वर्ये निवेश्य वनमाविशत्॥
en: Shatayupa, O scorcher of enemies had been the great king of the Kaikeyas. Having made over the sovereignty of his kingdom to his son, he had come into the forest,

sn: तेनासौ सहितो राजा ययौ व्यासाश्रमं प्रति। तत्रैनं विधिवद् राजा प्रत्यगृह्णात् कुरूद्वहः॥
en: Shatayupa received king Dhritarashtra with due rites. Accompanied by him, the latter went to the hermitage of Vyasa.

sn: स दीक्षां तत्र सम्प्राप्य राजा कौरवनन्दनः। शतयूपाश्रमे तस्मिन् निवासमकरोत् तदा॥
en: Arrived at Vyasa's hermitage the delighter of the Kurus received his initiation into the forest mode of life. Returning he took up his residence in the hermitage of Shatayupa.

sn: तस्मै सर्वं विधिं राज्ञे राजाऽऽचख्यौ महामतिः। आरण्यक महाराज व्यासस्यानुमते तदा॥
en: The great Shatayupa instructed Dhritarashtra in all the rites of the forest mode, at the command of Vyasa.

sn: एवं स तपसा राजन् धृतराष्ट्रो महामनाः। योजयामास चात्मानं तांश्चाप्यनुचरांस्तदा॥
en: Thus the great Dhritarashtra set himself to the practice of penances, and all his followers also to the same course of conduct.

sn: तथैव देवी गान्धारी वल्कलाजिनधारिणी। कुन्त्या सह महाराज समानव्रतचारिणी॥
en: Queen Gandhari also, O monarch, along with Kunti, put on barks of trees and deerskins, and began to observe the same vows as her husband.

sn: कर्मणा मनसा वाचा चक्षुषा चैव ते नृप। संनियम्येन्द्रियग्राममास्थिते परमं तपः॥
en: Restraining their senses in thought, words, and deeds, as well as by cye, they began to perforin sever austerities.

sn: त्वगस्थिभूतः परिशुष्कमांसो जटाजिनी वल्कलसंवृताङ्गः। स पार्थिवस्तत्र तपश्चचार महर्षिवत्तीव्रमपेतमोहः॥
en: Shorn of all stupefaction of mind, king Dhritarashthra began to practice vows and penances like a great Rishi, reducing his body to skin and bones, for his flesh was all dried up, bearing inatted locks on heard, and his person clad in barks and skins.

sn: क्षत्ता च धर्मार्थविदग्र्यबुद्धिः ससंजयस्तं नृपति सदारम्। उपायरद् घोरतपो जितात्मा तदा कृशो वल्कलचीरवासाः॥
en: Vidura, conversant with the true interpretations of Virtue, and gifted with great intelligence, as also Sanjaya, waited upon the old king with his wife. Both of them with souls under control, Vidura and Sanjaya also reduced themselves, and wore barks and rags.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तत्र मुनिश्रेष्ठा राजानं द्रष्टुमभ्ययुः । नारदः पर्वतश्चैव देवलश्च महातपाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Those foremost of ascetics, viz., Narada, Parvata and Devala of Austere penances, came there to see king Dhritarashtra.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: द्वैपायन: सशिष्यश्च सिद्धाश्चान्ये मनीषिणः। शतयूपश्च राजर्षिर्वृद्धः परमधार्मिकः॥
en: The Island-born Vyasa with all his disciples, and other persons gifted success, and the royal sage Shatayupa of advanced years and possessed of greit merit, also came.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: तेषां कुन्ती महाराज पूजां चक्रे यथाविधि। ते चापि तुतुषुस्तस्यास्तापसाः परियर्चया॥
en: Kunti adored them with due rites, O king. All those ascetics were highly pleased with the adorations offered to them.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: तत्र धाः कथास्तात यक्रुस्ते परमर्षयः। रमयन्तो महात्मानं धृतराष्ट्रं जनाधिपम्॥
en: Those great Rishis pleased the high souled king Dhritarashtra with discourses on religion and virtue.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: कथान्तरे तु कस्मिंश्चिद् देवर्षि रदस्ततः। कथामिमामकथयत् सर्वप्रत्यक्षदर्शिवान्॥
en: At the conclusion of their converse, the celestial Rishi Narada, seeing all things as objects of direct perception, said the following words.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: नारद उवाच केकयाधिपतिः श्रीमान् राजाऽऽसीदकुतोभयः। सहस्रचित्य इत्युक्तः शतयूपपितामहः॥
en: Narada said There was king of the Kaikeyas, possessed of great prosperity and perfectly fearless. His name was Sahasrachitya and he was the grandfather of the Shatayupa.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: स पुत्रे राज्यमासज्य ज्येष्ठे परमधार्मिके। सहस्रचित्यो धर्मात्मा प्रविवेश वनं नृपः॥
en: Resigning his kingdoin to his highly virtuous eldest Soil, the virtuous king Sahasrachitya retired into the forest.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: स गत्वा तपसः पारं दीप्तस्य वसुधाधिपः। पुरंदरस्य संस्थानं प्रतिपेदे महाद्युतिः॥
en: Reaching the other end of blazing penances, that king, gifted with great splendour, attained to the region of Purandara where he continued to live in his company.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: दृष्टपूर्वः स बहुशो राजन् सम्पतता मया। महेन्द्रसदने राजा तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषः॥
en: On many occasions, while visiting the region of Indra, O king, I saw that monarch, whose sins had all been consumed by penances, living in Indra's palace.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: तथा शैलालयो राजा भगदत्तपितामहः। तपोबलेनैव नृपो महेन्द्रसदनं गतः॥
en: Similarly, king Shailya, the grandfather of Bhagadatta, attained to the region of Indra by the power alone of his penances.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: तथा पृषध्रोराजाऽऽसीद् राजन् वज्रधरोपमः। स चापि तपसा लेभे नाकपृष्ठमितो गतः॥
en: There was another king, O monarch, of the name of Prishadhra who resembled the holder of the thunder-bolt himself. That king also by his penances proceeded from the Earth to the celestial region.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: अस्मिन्नरण्ये नृपते मान्धातुरपि चात्मजः। पुरुकुत्सो नृपः सिद्धिं महतीं समवाप्तवान्॥
en: In this very forest, o king, that king, viz., Purukutsa, the son of Mandhatri, acquired great Success.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: भार्या समभवद् यस्य नर्मदा सरितां वरा। सोऽस्मिन्नरण्ये नृपतिस्तपस्तप्त्वा दिवं गतः॥
en: That foremost of rivers, viz., Narmada, became the consort of that king. Having practised penances in this very forest, that king procceded to the celestial region.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: शशलोमा च राजाऽऽसीद् राजन् परमधार्मिकः। सम्यगस्मिन् वने तप्त्वा ततो दिवमवाप्तवान्॥
en: There was another king, highly righteous, of the name of Shashaloman. He, too, performed severe austerities in this forest and then ascended to the celestial region.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: द्वैपायनप्रसादाच्च त्वमपीदं तपोवनम्। राजन्नवाप्य दुष्प्रापां गतिमय्यां गमिष्यसि॥
en: You also, O monarch, having arrived at this forest, shall, through the grace of the Islandborn, attain to a very high cnd and which is difficult of attainment.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: त्वं चापि राजशार्दूल तपसोऽन्ते श्रिया वृतः। गान्धारीसहितो गन्ता गतिं तेषां महात्मनाम्॥
en: You also. O foremost of kings, at the termination of your penances, shall become gifted with great prosperity and, accompanied by Gandhari, attain to the end reached by those great ones.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: पाण्डुः स्मरति ते नित्यं बलहन्तुः समीपगः। त्वां सदैव महाराज श्रेयसा स च योक्ष्यति॥
en: Living in the presence of the destroyer of Vala, Pandu thinks of you always. He will, O monarch, certainly assist you in the attainment of Prosperity.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: तव शुश्रूषया चैव गान्धार्याश्च यशस्विनी। भर्तुः सलोकतामेषा गमिष्यति वधूस्तव॥
en: Through serving you and Gandhari, this daughter-in-law of yours, possessed of great fame, will attain to residence with her husband in the other world.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: युधिष्ठिरस्य जननी स हि धर्मः सनातनः। वयमेतत् प्रपश्यामो नृपते दिव्यचक्षुषा॥
en: She is the mother of Yudhishthria who is the eternal Dharma. We see all this, O king, with out spiritual vision.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: प्रवेक्ष्यति महात्मानं विदुरश्च युधिष्ठिरम्। संजयस्तदनुध्यानादितः स्वर्गमवाप्स्यति॥
en: Vidura will enter into the high souled Yudhishthira. Sanjaya also, through meditation, will ascend from this world into the celestial region.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा कौरवेन्द्रो महात्मा सार्धं पल्या प्रीतिमान् सम्बभूव। विद्वान् वाक्यं नारदस्य प्रशस्य चक्रे पूजां चातुलां नारदाय।२१।।
en: Vaishampayana said That great chief of Kuru's race, endued with learning, having, with his wife, heard these words of Narada, praised them and adored Narada with unprecedented honors.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: ततः सर्वे नारदं विप्रसंघाः सम्पूजयामासुरतीव राजन्। राज्ञः प्रीत्या धृतराष्ट्रस्य ते वै पुनः पुनः सम्प्रहृष्टास्तदानीम्॥
en: The assembly of Brahmanas there present became filled with great joy, and desirous of pleasing king Dhritarashtra, o monarch, themselves worshipped Narada with great respect.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: नारदस्य तु तद् वाक्यं शशंसुर्द्विजसत्तमाः। शतयूपस्तु राजर्षिर्नारदं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ अहो भगवता श्रद्धा कुरुराजस्य वर्धिता। सर्वस्य च जनस्यास्य मम चैव महाद्युते॥
en: Those foremost of twice-born persons also lauded the words of Narada. Then the royal sage Shatayupa, addressing Narada, said, Your holy self has increased the devotion of the Kuru king, of all those people here, and of myself also, O you of great splendour.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: अस्ति काचिद् विवक्षा तु तां मे निगदतः शृणु। धृतराष्ट्र प्रति नृपं देवर्षे लोकपूजित॥
en: I wish to ask you something. Listen to me as I say it. It is about king, Dhritarashtra,O celestial Rishi, that are adored of all the worlds.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: सर्ववृत्तान्ततवत्ज्ञो भवान् दिव्येन चक्षुषा। युक्तः पश्यसि विप्रर्षे गतिर्या विविधा नृणाम्॥
en: You know the truth of every affair. Gifted with celestial vision, you behold, O twice-born Rishi, what the various ends are of human beings.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: उक्तवान् नृपतीनां त्वं महेन्द्रस्य सलोकताम्। न त्वस्य नृपतेर्लोकाः कथितास्ते महामुने॥
en: You have said what the end has been of the kings mentioned by you, viz., association with the king of the celestials. You have not, however, O great Rishi, decured what those regions are which will be acquired by this king.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: स्थानमप्यस्य नृपतेः श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं विभो। त्वत्तः कीदृक् कदा चेति तन्ममाख्याहि तत्त्वतः।।२८
en: O powerful one, I wish to hear from you what region will be acquired by the royal Dhritarashtra. You should tell me truly the kind of region that will be his and the time when he will attain to it.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: इत्युक्तो नारदस्तेन वाक्यं सर्वमनोऽनुगम्। व्याजहार सभामध्ये दिव्यदर्शी महातपाः॥
en: Thus addressed by him, Narada of celestial vision and endued with austere penances, said in the midst of the assembly these words highly agreeable to the minds of all.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: नारद उवाच यदृच्छया शक्रसदो गत्वा शक्रं शचीपतिम्। दृष्टवानस्मि राजर्षे तत्र पाण्डुं नराधिपम्॥
en: Going at my will to the palace of Shakra, I have seen Shakara the lord of Sachi; and there, O royal sage, I have seen king Pandu.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: तत्रेयं धृतराष्ट्रस्य कथा समभवन्नृप। तपसो दुष्करस्यास्य यदयं तपते नृपः॥
en: There is a talk arose, O monarch, about this Dhritarashtra and those highly austere penaces which he is performing.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: तत्राहमिदमश्रौषं शक्रस्य वदतः खयम्। वर्षाणि त्रीणि शिष्टानि राज्ञोऽस्य परमायुषः॥
en: There I heard from the lips of Shakra himself that there are three years yet of the period of life of this king.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: ततः कुबेरभवनं गान्धरीसहितो नृपः। प्रयाता धृतराष्ट्रोऽयं राजराजाभिसत्कृतः॥ कामगेन विमानेन दिव्याभरणभूषितः।
en: After that, king Dhritarashtra, accompanied by his wife Gandhari, will go to the regions of Kubera and be highly honored by that king of kings. He will go there on a car moving at his will, his his body adorned with celestial ornaments.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: ऋषिपुत्रो महाभागस्तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषः॥ संचरिष्यति लोकांश्च देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्। स्वच्छन्देनेति धर्मात्मा यन्मां त्वमनुपृच्छसि॥
en: He is the son of a Rishi; he is highly blessed; he has exhausted all his sins by his penances. Gifted with a righteous soul, he will roam at will through the regions of the celestials, the Gandharvas, and the Rakshasas. That about which you have enquired, is a mystery to the gods. Through my affection for you, I have said this high truth.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: देवगुह्यमिदं प्रीत्या मया वः कथितं महत्। भवन्तो हि श्रुतधनास्तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषाः॥
en: You all are possessed of the wealth of Shrutis and have burnt all your sins by your penances.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इति ते तस्य तच्छ्रुत्वा देवर्मधुरं वचः। सर्वे सुमनसः प्रीता बभूवुः स च पार्थिवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these sweet words of the celestial Rishi, all the persons there assembled, as also king Dhritarastra became greatly pleased.

description: The arrival of ascetics to see the king
sn: एवं कथाभिरन्वास्य धृतराष्ट्र मनीषिणः। विप्रजग्मुर्यथाकामं ते सिद्धगतिमास्थिताः॥
en: Having cheered Dhritarashtra of great wisdom with such talk, they left the place, going away by the path that belongs to those who are crowned with success.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वनं गते कौरवेन्द्रे दुःखशोकसमन्विताः। बभूवुः पाण्डवा राजन् मातृशोकेन चान्विताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Upon the retirement of the king of the Kurus into the forest, the Pandavas, O king, afflicted besides by grief on account of their mother, became very dispirited.

sn: तथा पौरजनः सर्वः शोचन्नास्ते जनाधिपम्। कुर्वाणाश्च कथास्तत्र ब्राह्मणा नृपतिं प्रति॥
en: The citizens also of Hastinapur were possessed by deep sorrow. The Brahmanas always talked of the old king.

sn: कथं नु राजा वृद्धः स वने वसति निर्जने। गान्धारी च महाभागा सा च कुन्ती पृथा कथम्॥
en: How, indeed, will the king, who has become old, live in the solitary forest? How will the highly blessed Gandhari, and Pritha, the daughter of Kuntibhoja, live there?

sn: सुखार्हः स हि राजर्षिरसुखी तद् वनं महत्। किमवस्थः समासाद्य प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्हतात्मजः॥
en: The royal sage has always lived in the enjoyment of every comfort. He will certainly be very miserable. Arrived in the deep forest, what is now the condition of that personage of royal descent, who is, again, bereft of vision?

sn: सुदुष्कृतं कृतवती कुन्ती पुत्रानपश्यती। राज्यश्रियं परित्यज्य वनं सा समरोचयत्॥
en: Difficult is the feat that Kunti has performed by separating herself from her sons. Alas, renouncing royal prosperity, she choose a life in the forest.

sn: विदुरः किमवस्थश्च भ्रातुः शुश्रूषुरात्मवान्। स च गावल्गणिर्थीमान् भर्तृपिण्डानुपालकः॥
en: What, again, is the condition of Vidura who is always devoted to the service of his elder brother? How also is the intelligent son of Gavalgani who is so faithful to the salt given him by his master?

sn: आकुमारं च पौरास्ते चिन्ताशोकसमाहताः। तत्र तत्र कथाश्चक्रुः समासाद्य परस्परम्॥
en: The citizens, including even the minors, meeting together, asked one another these questions.

sn: पाण्डवाश्चैव ते सर्वे भृशं शोकपरायणाः। शोचन्तो मातरं वृद्धामूर्नातिचिरं पुरे॥
en: The Pandavas also, greatly stricken with grief, bewailed for their old mother, and could not live in their city long.

sn: तथैव वृद्धं पितरं हतपुत्रं जनेश्वरम्। गान्धारी च महाभागां विदुरं च महामतिम्॥
en: Thinking also of their old sire, the king, who had lost all his children, and the highly blessed Gandhari, and Vidura of great intelligence, they could not enjoy peace of mind.

sn: नैषां बभूव सम्प्रीतिस्तान् विचिन्तयतां तदा। न राज्ये न च नारीषु न वेदाध्ययनेषु च॥
en: They had no pleasure in sovereignty, nor in women, nor in the study of the Vedas.

sn: परं निर्वेदमगमंश्चिन्तयन्तो नराधिपम्। तं च ज्ञातिवधं घोरं संस्मरन्तः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Despair entered their souls as they thought of the old king and as they repeated, of that terrible destruction of kinsinen.

sn: अभिमन्योश्च बालस्य विनाशं रणमूर्धनि। कर्णस्य च महाबाहो संग्रामेप्वपलायिनः॥ तथैव द्रौपदेयानामन्येषां सुहृदामपि। वधं संस्मृत्य ते वीरा नानिप्रमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: Indeed, thinking of the destruction of the youthful Abhimanyu on the field of battle, of the mighty-armed Karna who never retreated from fight, of the sons of Draupadi, and of other friends of theirs, those heroes became highly dispirited.

sn: हतप्रवीरां पृथिवी हृतरत्नां च भारत। सदैव चिन्तयन्तस्ते न शर्म चोपलेभिरे॥
en: They could not get peace of mind upon repeatedly thinking that the Earth had become divested of both her heroes and her riches.

sn: द्रौपदी हतपुत्रा च सुभद्रा चैव भाविनी। नातिप्रीतियुते देव्यो तदाऽऽस्तामप्रहृष्टवत्॥
en: Draupadi had lost all her children, and the beautiful Subhadra also had become childless. They, too, were of cheerless hearts and grieved greatly.

sn: वैराट्यास्तनयं दृष्ट्वा पितरं ते परिक्षितम्। धारयन्ति स्म ते प्राणांस्तव पूर्वपितामहाः॥
en: Seeing, however, the son of Virata's daughter, viz., your sire Parikshit, your grandsires somehow lived.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ते पुरुषव्याघ्राः पाण्डवा मातृनन्दनाः। स्मरन्तो मातरं वीरा वभूवुर्भृशदुःखिताः॥
en: Those foremost of men, the heroic Pandavas, those delighters of their mother-became greatly stricken with grief.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: राजकार्येषु पुरा व्यासक्ता नित्यशोऽभवन्। ते राजकार्याणि तदा नाकार्षुः सर्वतः पुरे।॥
en: They who had formerly been always engaged in royal offices, did not at that time attend to those deeds at all in their capital.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: प्रविष्टा इव शोकेन नाभ्यनन्दन्त किञ्चन। सम्भाष्यमाणा अपि ते न किञ्चित् प्रत्यपूजयन्॥
en: Stricken with deep sorrow, they could not find pleasure from anything. It any body asked them, they never honored him with an answer.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: ते स्म वीरा दुराधर्षा गाम्भीर्ये सागरोपमाः। शोकोपहतविज्ञाना नष्टसंज्ञा इवाभवन्॥
en: Although those irresistible heroes were grave like the ocean, yet they were now deprived of their knowledge and their very senses by the grief they left.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: अचिन्तयंश्च जननी ततस्ते पाण्डुनन्दनाः। कथं नु वृद्धमिथुनं वहत्यतिकृशा पृथा॥
en: Thinking of their mother, the sons of Pandu became anxious as to how their emaciated mother was serving the old pair.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: कथं च स महीपालो हतपुत्रो निराश्रयः। पल्या सह वसत्येको वने श्वापदसेविते॥
en: How, indeed, is that king; whose sons have all been killed and who is without refuge, living alone, with only his wife, in the forest haunted by beasts of prey?

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: सा च देवी महाभागा गान्धारी हतबान्धवा। पतिमन्धं कथं वृद्धमन्वेति विजने वने।॥
en: Alas, how does that highly blessed queen, Gandhari, whose dear ones have all been killed, follow her blind husband in the solitary forest.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: एवं तेषां कथयतामौत्सुक्यमभवत् तदा। गमने चाभवद् बुद्धिधृतराष्ट्रदिदृक्षया॥
en: Such was the anxiety shown by the Pandavas when they talked with one another. They then set their hearts upon beholding the king in his forest asylum.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: सहदेवस्तु राजानं प्रणिपत्येदमब्रवीत्। अहो मे भवतो दृष्टं हृदयं गमनं प्रति॥
en: Then bowing down to the king, Sahadeva said, “I think you wish to see our sire.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: न हि त्वां गौरवेणाहमशकं वक्तुमञ्जसा। गमनं प्रति राजेन्द्र तदिदं समुपस्थितम्॥
en: From my respect for you, however, I could not speedily speak on the subject of our journey to the forest. The time for that sojourn in now come.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: दिष्ट्या द्रक्ष्यामि तां कुन्ती वर्तयन्ती तपस्विनीम्। जटिलां तापसी वृद्धां कुशकाशपरिक्षताम्॥
en: By good luck I shall see Kunti performing penances, with matted locks on her head, practising severe austerities, and emaciated by sleeping on blades of Kusha and Kasha.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: प्रासादहर्म्यसंवृद्धामत्यन्तसुखभागिनीम्। कदा तु जननीं श्रान्तां द्रक्ष्यामि भृशदुःखिताम्॥
en: She was brought up in palaces, and nursed in every comfort and luxury. Alas, when shall I see my mother who is now toil-worn and plunged into great misery.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: अनित्याः खलु मर्त्यानां गतयो भरतर्षभ। कुन्ती राजसुता यत्र वसत्यसुखिता वने॥
en: Forsooth, O chief of Bharata's race, the ends of men are exceedingly uncertain, since Kunti, who is a princess by birth, is now living in misery in the forest.'

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: सहदेववचः श्रुत्वा द्रौपदी योषितां वरा। उवाच देवी राजानमभिपूज्याभिनन्द्य च॥
en: Hearing these words of Sahadeva, queen Draupadi, that foremost of all women duly honoring the king, said, with proper salutations,

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: कदा द्रक्ष्यामि नां देवीं यदि जीवति सा पृथा। जीवन्त्या ह्यद्य मे प्रीतिर्भविष्यति जनाधिप॥
en: Alas, when shall I see queen Pritha, if, indeed, she is alive! I shall consider my life as not passed in vain if I succeed in seeing her once more, O king.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: एषा तेऽस्तु मतिर्नित्यं धर्मे ते रमतां मनः। योऽद्यत्वमस्मान् राजेन्द्र श्रेयसा योजयिष्यसि॥
en: Let this sort of understanding be ever firm in you. Let your mind always take a pleasure in such virtue as is involved, O king of kings, in your desire of granting such a high boon on us.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: अग्रपादस्थितं चेमं विद्धि राजन् वधूजनम्। काङ्क्षन्तं दर्शनं कुन्त्या गान्धार्याः श्वशुरस्य च॥
en: Know, O king, that all these ladies of your house are staying with their feet raised for the journey, from desire of seeing Kunti and Gandhari, and my father-in-law.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: इत्युक्तः स नृपो देव्या द्रौपद्या भरतर्षभ। सेनाध्यक्षान् समानाय्या सर्वानिदमुवाच ह॥
en: Thus addressed by queen Draupadi, the king, O chief of Bharata's race, summoned all the leaders of his army to his presence and told them.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: निर्यातयत मे सेनां प्रभूतरथकुञ्जराम्। द्रक्ष्यामि वनसंस्थं च धृतराष्ट्रं महीपतिम्॥
en: 'Cause my army, full of cars and elephants, to march out. I shall see king Dhritarashtra who is now living in the forest.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: स्त्र्यध्यक्षांश्चाब्रवीद् राजा यानानि विविधानि मे। सज्जीक्रियन्तां सर्वाणि शिबिकाश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: To the officers in charge of the ladies word the king gave the order, 'Let various kinds of conveyances be properly equipt, as also all my closed litters counting by thousands.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: शकटापणवेशाश्च कोशः शिल्पिन एव च। निर्यान्तु कोषपालाश्च कुरुक्षेत्राश्रमं प्रति॥
en: Let carriages and granaries and wardrobes, and treasuries, be equipt and ordered out, and let mechanics have ihe command to march out. Let men in charge of treasuries go out on the way leading to the ascetic hermitage of Kurukshetra.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: यश्च पौरजनः कश्चिद् द्रष्टुमिच्छति पार्थिवम्। अनावृतः सुविहितः स च यातु सुरक्षितः॥
en: Whoever amongst the citizens wishes to see the king, is allowed to do so without any restriction. Let him properly protected.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: सूदाः पौरोगवाश्चैव सर्वं चैव महानसम्। विविधं भक्ष्यभोज्यं च शकटैरुह्यतां मम॥
en: Let cooks and superintendents of kitchens, and the whole culinary establishment, and various kinds of edibles and viands be ordered to be borne out on carts and conveyances. proceed,

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: प्रयाणं घुष्यतां चैव श्वोभूत इति मा चिरम्। क्रियतां पथि चाप्यद्य वेश्मानि विविधानि च॥
en: Let it be proclaimed that we march out tomorrow. Indeed, let no delay take place. Let pavilions and resting houses of various kinds be erected on the way.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: एवमाज्ञाप्य राजा स भ्रातृभिः सहपाण्डवः। श्वोभूते निर्ययौ राजन् सस्त्रीवृद्धपुरःसरः॥
en: These were the commands which the eldest son of Pandu gave, with his brothers. When morning came, O monarch, the king started with a large following of women and old men.

description: Yudhishthira goes with his party to see the king in the forest
sn: स बहिर्दिवसानेव जनौघं परिपालयन्। न्यवसन्नृपतिः पञ्च ततोऽगच्छद् वनं प्रति॥
en: Going out of his city, king Yudhishthira waited five days for such citizens as might accompany him and then went towards the forest.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच आज्ञापयामास ततः सेनां भरतसत्तमः। अर्जुनप्रमुखैर्गुप्ता लोकपालोपमैनरैः॥
en: That foremost one of Bharata's race, then ordered his troops, which were protected by heroes who were headed by Arjuna, and who resembled the very guardians of the universe, to march out.

sn: योगो योग इति प्रीत्या ततः शब्दो महानभूत्। क्रोशतां सादिनां तत्र युज्यतां युज्यतामिति॥
en: Immediately loud clamour consisting of the words, 'Equip, Equip'! of horse-men, O Bharata, engaged in equipping their horses.

sn: केचिद् यानैनरा जग्मुः केचिदश्वैर्महाजवैः। काञ्चनैश्च स्थैः केचिज्ज्वलितज्वलनोपमैः॥
en: Some proceeded on carriages and vehicles, some on quick-coursing horses, and some on a arose cars made of gold and effulgent like blazing fires.

sn: गजेन्द्रश्च तथैवान्ये केचिदुष्टैनराधिप। पदातिनस्तथैवान्ये नखरप्रासयोधिनः॥
en: Some proceeded on powerful elephants and some on camels, O king. Some proceeded on foot, which belonged to that class of combatants which is arined with tiger like claws.

sn: पौरजानपदाश्चैव यानैर्बहुविधैस्तथा। अन्वयुः कुरुराजानं धृतराष्ट्रं दिदृक्षवः॥
en: The citizens and inhabitants of the provinces, desirous of beholding Dhritarashtra, followed the king on various kinds of conveyances.

sn: स चापि राजवचनादाचार्यो गौतमः कृपः। सेनामादाय सेनानी प्रययावाश्रमं प्रति॥
en: The preceptor Kripa also, of Gautama's race, that great leader of army, taking all the forces with him, proceeded, at the command of the king, towards the old king's hermitage.

sn: ततो द्विजैः परिवृतः कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। संस्तूयमानो बहुभिः सूतमागधबन्दिभिः॥ पाण्डुरेणातपत्रेण ध्रियमाणेन मूर्धनि। रथानीकेन महता निर्जगाम कुरुद्वहः॥
en: The Kuru king Yudhishthira, that perpetuator of Kuru's race, surrounded on a large number of Brahmanas' his praises lauded by a large band of Sutas and Magadhas and bards, and with a white umbrella held over his head, and surrounded by a large number of cars, started on his journey.

sn: गजैश्चाचलसंकाशैर्भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः। सज्जयन्त्रायुधोपेतैः प्रययौ पवनात्मजः॥
en: Vrikodara, the son of the Wind-God, went on an elephant huge as a hill, equipt with strong bow and machines and weapons of attack and defense.

sn: माद्रीपुत्रावपि तथा हयारोहौ सुसंवृतौ। जग्मतुः शीघ्रगमनौ संनद्धकवचध्वजौ॥
en: The twin sons of Madri went on two quickcoursing horses, well cased in mail, wellprotected, and equip with banners.

sn: अर्जुनश्च महातेजा रथेनादित्यवर्चसा। वशी श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्तैर्दिव्येनान्वगमन्नृपम्॥
en: Arjuna of great energy, with senses under restraint, proceeded on an excellent car effulgent like the sun to which were yoked excellent white horses.

sn: द्रौपदीप्रमुखश्चापि स्त्रीसंघाः शिबिकायुताः। स्त्र्यध्यक्षगुप्ताः प्रययुर्विसृजन्तोऽमितं वसु॥
en: The royal ladies headed by Draupadi proceeded in closed litters protected by the superintendents of women. They scattered showers of wealth as they went on.

sn: समृद्धरथहस्त्यश्वं वेणुवीणानुनादितम्। शुशुभे पाण्डवं सैन्यं तत् तदा भरतर्षभ॥
en: Teeming with cars and elephants and horses, and echoing with the blare of trumpets and the music of Vinas, the Pandav army, O monarch, shone with great beauty.

sn: नदीतीरेषु रम्येषु सरःसु च विशाम्पते। वासान् कृत्वा क्रमेणाथ जग्मुस्ते कुरुपुङ्गवाः॥
en: Those chiefs of Kuru's race proceeded slowly, resting by delightful banks of rivers and lakes, O monarch.

sn: युयुत्सुश्च महातेजा धौम्यश्चैव पुरोहितः। युधिष्ठिरस्य वचनात् पुरगुप्ति प्रचक्रतुः॥
en: Yuyutsu of great energy, and Dhaumya, the priest, at the command of Yudhishthira, were engaged in protecting the city.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा कुरुक्षेत्रमवातरत्। क्रमेणोत्तीर्य यमुना नदी परमपावनीम्॥ स ददर्शाश्रमं दूराद् राजर्षेस्तस्य धीमतः। शतयूपस्य कौरव्य धृतराष्ट्रस्य चैव ह॥
en: By slow marches, king Yudhishthira, reached Kurukshetra, and then, crossing the Yamuna, that highly sacred river, he saw from a distance the hermitage, O you of Kuru's race, of the royal sage of great wisdom and of Dhritarashtra.

sn: ततः प्रमुदित: सर्वो जनस्तद् वनमञ्जसा। विवेश सुमहानादैरापूर्य भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then all the men became filled with joy and quickly entered the forest, filling it with loud sounds of joy, O chief of Bharata's race.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते पाण्डवा दूरादवतीर्य पदातयः। अभिजग्मुर्नरपतेराश्रमं विनयानताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said The Pandavas got down at a distance, from their cars and proceeded on foot to the hermitage of the king, bending themselves in humility.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: स च योधजनः सर्वो ये च राष्ट्रनिवासिनः। स्त्रियश्च कुरुमुख्यानां पद्भिरेवान्वयुस्तदा।॥
en: All the combatants also, and the citizens and the wives of the Kuru chiefs, followed them on foot.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: आश्रमं ते ततो जग्मुधृतराष्ट्रस्य पाण्डवाः। शून्यं मृगगणाकीर्णं कदलीवनशोभितम्॥
en: The Pandavas then reached the sacred hermitage of Dhritarashtra which abounded with herds of deer and which was adorned with plantain plants.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: ततस्तत्र समाजग्मुस्तापसा नियतव्रताः। पाण्डवानागतान् द्रष्टुं कौतूहलसमन्विताः॥
en: Many ascetics of rigid vows, filled with curiosity, came there for seeing the Pandavas who had arrived at the hermitage.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: तानपृच्छत् ततो राजा क्वासौ कौरववंशभृत्। पिता ज्येष्ठो गतोऽस्माकमिति बाष्पपरिप्लुतः॥
en: The king, with tears in his eyes, asked them, saying, 'Where has my eldest sire the perpetuator of Kuru's race, gone?

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: ते तमूचुस्ततो वाक्यं यमुनामवगाहितुम्। युष्याणामुदकुम्भस्य चार्थे गत इति प्रभो॥
en: They answered, O monarch, telling him that he had gone to the Yamuna, for his ablutions, as also for fetching flowers and waters.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: तैराख्यातेन मार्गेण ततस्ते जग्मुरञ्जसा। ददृशुश्चाविदूरे तान् सर्वानथ पदातयः॥
en: Proceeding quickly on foot along the path pointed out by them, the Pandavas saw all of them from a distance.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: ततस्ते सत्वरा जग्मुः पितुर्दर्शनकाक्षिणः। सहदेवस्तु वेगेन प्राधावद् यत्र सा पृथा।॥
en: Desirous of meeting with their sire they walked rapidly. Then Sahadeva ran quickly towards the spot where Pritha was.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: सुस्वरं रुरुदे धीमान् मातुः पादावुपस्पृशन्। सा च बाष्पाकुलमुखी ददर्श दयितं सुतम्॥
en: Touching the feet of his mother, he began to weep aloud. With tears running down her cheeks, she saw her darling child.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य समुन्नाम्य च पुत्रकम्। गान्धार्याः कथयामास सहदेवमुपस्थितम्॥
en: Raising her son up and embracing him with her arms she informed Gandhari of Sahadeva's arrival.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: अनन्तरं च राजानं भीमसेनमथार्जुनम्। नकुलं च पृथा दृष्ट्वा त्वरमाणोपचक्रमे॥
