en: Then seeing he king Bhimasena, Arjuna and Nakula, Pritha tried to advance quickly towards them.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: सा ह्यग्रे गच्छति तयोर्दम्पत्योर्हतपुत्रयोः। कर्यन्ती तौ ततस्ते तां दृष्ट्वा संन्यपतन भुवि॥
en: She was walking in advance of the childless old pair, and was dragging them forward. Seeing her, the Pandavas feel down on the earth.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: राजा तान् स्वरयोगेन स्पर्शेन च महामनाः। प्रत्यभिज्ञाय मेधावी समाश्वासयत प्रभुः॥
en: The powerful and the great monarch, gifted with great intelligence, recognising them by their voices ard also by touch, comforted them one after another.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: ततस्ते बाष्पमुत्सृज्य गान्धारीसहितं नृपम्। उपतस्थुर्महात्मानो मातरं च यथाविधि॥
en: Shedding tears, those great princes, with due formalities, approached the old king and Gandhari, as also their own mother.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: सर्वेषां तोयकलशाजगृहुस्ते स्वयं तदा। पाण्डवा लब्धसंज्ञास्ते मात्रा चाश्वासिताः पुनः॥
en: Indeed, regaining their senses, and once more consoled by their mother, the Pandavas took away from the king and their aunt and mother the jars full of water which they ha been carrying

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: तथा नार्यो नृसिंहानां सोऽवरोधजनस्तदा। पौरजानपदाश्चैव ददृशुस्तं जनाधिपम्॥
en: The ladies of those leading men, and all the women of the royal household, as also all the inhabitants of the city and the provinces, then saw the old king.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: निवेदयामास तदा जनं तन्नामगोत्रतः। युधिष्ठिरो नरपति: स चैनं प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: King Yudhishthira presented all those individuals one after another to the old king, repeating their names and families and then himself adored his eldest sire with respect.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: स तैः परिवृत्तो मेने हर्षबाष्पाविलेक्षणः। राजाऽऽत्मानं गृहगतं पुरेव गजसाह्वये॥
en: Surrounded by them all, the old monarch, with eyes bathed in tears of joy, considered himself as once more staying in the midst of the city of Hastinapur.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: अभिवादितो वधूभिश्च कृष्णाद्याभिः स पार्थिवः। गान्धार्या सहितो धीमान् कुन्त्या च प्रत्यनन्दत॥
en: Saluted with respect by all his daughters-inlaw headed by Krishna, king Dhritarashtra, gifted with great intelligence, with Gandhari and Kunti became filled with joy.

description: The meeting of the Pandavas with their mother and the blind king
sn: ततश्चाश्रममागच्छत् सिद्वयारणसेवितम्। दिदृक्षुभिः समाकीर्णं नमस्तारागणैरिव॥
en: He then reached his forest-retreat which was highly spoken of by Siddhas and Charanas, and that then was filled up with vast crowds of men all desirous of seeing him, like the sky teeming with my raids of stars.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स तैः सह नरव्याप्रैर्धातृभिर्भरतर्षभ। राजा रुचिरपद्माक्षरासांचक्रे तदाश्रमे॥
en: Vaishmpayana said The king, O chief of Bharatas' race, with those foremost of men, viz., his brothers who all had eyes resembling lotus petals, took his seat in the hermitage of his eldest sire.

sn: तापसैश्च महाभागैर्नानादेशसमागतैः। द्रष्टुं कुरुपतेः पुत्रान् पाण्डवान् पृथुवक्षसः॥
en: There sat around him many highly blessed ascetics, coming from various regions, from desire of seeing the sons of that lord of Kuru's race, viz., the Pandavas of wide chests.

sn: तेऽब्रुवज्ञातुमिच्छामः कतमोऽत्र युधिष्ठिरः। भीमार्जुनौ यमौ चैव द्रौपदी च यशस्विनी॥
en: They said, 'We wish to know who amongst these is Yudhishthira, who are Bhima and Arjuna, who the twins, and who is the illustrious Draupadi?'

sn: सर्वोस्तानभिनामतः। संजयो द्रौपदी चैव सर्वाश्चान्या कुरुस्त्रियः॥
en: Then the Suta, Sanjaya, in answer to their queries, pointed out to them the Pandavas, naming each, and Draupadi too as also the other ladies of the Kururace.

sn: संजय उवाच स्तनुर्महासिंह इव प्रवृद्धः। स्ताम्रायताक्षः कुरुराज एषः॥
en: Sanjaya said This one fair like pure gold, who is endued with a body which looks like that of a fullgrown lion, who is possessed of a large aquiline nose, and wide and expansive eyes of a coppery hue, is the Kuru king.

sn: तानाचख्यौ तदा सूत: अयं पुनर्मत्तगजेन्द्रगामी प्रतप्तचामीकरशुद्धगौरः। वृकोदरः पश्यत पश्यतेमम्॥
en: This one whose tread is like that of an infuriate elephant, whose complexion is as fair as that of heated gold, whose frame is of large and expansive proportions, and whose arms are long sand stout, is Vrikodara. See him well.

sn: यस्त्वेष पार्वेऽस्य महाधनुष्मान् श्यामो युवावारणयूथपाभः। सिंहोन्नतांसो गजखेलगामी पद्मायताक्षोऽर्जुन एष वीरः॥
en: The powerful bowmen who sits besides him, of darkish color and youthful frame, who resembles the leader of an elephantine herd, whose shoulders are as high as those of a lion, who walks like a sporting elephant, and whose eyes are as expansive as the petals of a lotus, is the hero called Arjuna.

sn: कुन्तीसमीपे पुरुषोत्तमौ तु यमाविमौ विष्णुमहेन्द्रकल्पौ। मनुष्यलोके सकले समोऽस्ति ययोर्न रूपे न बले न शीले॥
en: Those two foremost of men, who are sitting beside Kunti, are the twins resembling Vishnu and Mahendra. In the entire world, they have not their cquals in beauty and strength and excellence of conduct.

sn: इयं पुन: पद्मदलायताक्षी मध्यं वयः किञ्चिदिव स्पृशन्ती। नीलोत्पलाभा सुरदेवतेव कृष्णा स्थिता मूर्तिमतीव लक्ष्मीः॥
en: This lady having eyes expansive as lotuspetals, who seems to have touched the middle age of life, whose complexion resembles that of the blue lotus, and who looks like goddess, is Krishna, the embodied form of the goddess of prosperity.

sn: अस्थास्तु पार्वे कनकोत्तमाभा यैषा प्रभा मूर्तिमतीव सौमी। श्चक्रायुधस्याप्रतिमस्य तस्य।॥
en: She who sits besides her, possessed of the complexion of pure gold, who looks like the embodied rays of the moon, in the midst of other ladies, O foremost of twice-born oncs, is the sister that unrivaled hero who holds the discus.

sn: इयं च जाम्बूनदशुद्धगौरी पार्थस्य भार्या भुजगेन्द्रकन्या। चित्राङ्गदा चैव नरेन्द्रकन्या यैषा सवर्णामधूकपुष्पैः॥
en: This other, as fair as pure gold, is the daughter of the Naga king and wife of Arjuna. This other whose complexion is like of pure gold or like that of Madhuka flowers, is the princess Chitrangada.

sn: इयं स्वसा राजचमूपतेश्च प्रवृद्धनीलोत्पलदामवर्णा। पस्पर्ध कृष्णेन सदा नृपो यो वृकोदरस्यैष परिग्रहाय्यः॥
en: This one, whose complexion is like an assemblage of blue lotuses, is the sister of that monarch, that lord of hosts, who used to always challenge Krishna. She is the foremost wife of Vrikodara.

sn: इयं च राज्ञो मगधाधिपस्य सुता जरासन्ध इति श्रुतस्य। यवीयसो भाद्रवतीसुतस्य भार्या मता चम्पकदामगौरी॥
en: This is the daughter of the king of Magadha who was known by the name of Jarasandha. Possessed of the complexion of an assemblage of Champakas, she is the wife of the youngest son of Madravati.

sn: इन्दीवरश्यामतनुः स्थिता तु यैषा परासन्नमहीतले च। भार्या मता माद्रवतीसुतस्य ज्येष्ठस्य सेयं कमलायताक्षी॥
en: Possessed of complexion dark as the blue lotus, she who sits there on the earth, and whose eyes are as expansive as lotus-petals, she is the wife of the eldest son of Madravati,

sn: इयं तु निष्टप्तसुवर्णगौरी राज्ञो विराटस्य सुता सपुत्रा। भार्याभिमन्योर्निहतो रणे यो द्रोणादिभिस्तैर्विरथो रंथस्थैः॥
en: This lady whose complexion is as fair as that of heated gold and who sits with her child on her lap, is the daughter of king Virata. She is the wife of that Abhimanyu who while divested of his car, was killed by Drona and other fighting from their cars.

sn: एतास्तु सीमन्तशिरोरुहायाः शुल्कोत्तरीया नरराजपल्यः। राज्ञोऽस्य वृद्धस्य परं शताख्या: स्नुषा नृवीरा हतपुत्रनाथाः॥
en: These ladies, the hair on whose heads shows not the parted line, and who are clad in white, are the widows of the killed sons of Dhritarashtra. They are the daughters-in-law of this old king, the wives of his hundred sons, now deprived of both their husbands and children who have been killed by heroic enemies.

sn: एता यथामुख्यमुदाहता वो ब्राह्मण्यभावादृजुबुद्धिसत्त्वाः। सर्वा भवद्भिः परिपृच्छ्यमाना नरेन्द्रपल्यः सुविशुद्धसत्त्वाः॥
en: I have now pointed them out in the order of precedence. On account of their devotion to Brahmanas, their understanding and hearts are divested of every kind of crookedness. Possessed of pure souls, they have all been pointed out by men, these princesses of the Kaurava line, in answer to your queries.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं स राजा कुरुवृद्धवर्यः समागतस्तैर्नरदेवपुत्रैः पप्रच्छ सर्वं कुशलं तदानीं गतेषु सर्वेष्वथ तापसेषु॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus that aged king of Kuru's race, having met with those sons of him that was a celestial among men, enquired about their well-being after all the ascetics had departed.

sn: योधेषु वाप्याश्रममण्डलं तं मुक्त्वा निविष्टेषु विमुच्य पत्रम्। स्त्रीवृद्धबाले च सुसंनिविष्टे यथार्हतस्तान् कुशलान्यपृच्छत्॥
en: The warriors who had accompanied the Pandavas, leaving the retreat, sat themselves down at a little distance, getting down from their cars and the animals they rode. Indeed, after all the crowd, viz., the ladies the old men and the children, had been seated, the old king duly addressed thein after making the usual polite enquireis.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच युधिष्ठिर महाबाहो कच्चित् त्वं कुशली ह्यसि। सहितो भ्रातृभिः सर्वैः पौरजानपदैस्तथा॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Yudhishthira, are you in peace and happiness, with all your brothers and the dwellers of the city and the provinces?

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: ये च त्वामनुजीवन्ति कच्चित् तेऽपि निरामयाः। सचिवा भृत्यवर्गाश्च गुरवश्चैव ते नृप॥
en: Are they who depend on you also happy? Are your ministers, and servitors, and all your seniors and preceptors also, happy?

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: कच्चित् तेऽपि निरातङ्का वसन्ति विषये तव। कच्चिद् वर्तसि पौराणी वृत्तिं राजर्षिसेविताम्॥
en: Are those also who live in your kingdom frce from fear? Do you follow the old and traditional conduct of kings?

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: कच्चिन्यायाननुच्छिद्य कोशस्तेऽभिप्रपूर्यते। अरिमध्यस्थमित्रेषु वर्तसे चानुरूपतः॥
en: Is your treasury filled without disregarding the restraints imposed by justice and equity? Do you behave as you should towards foes, neutrals, and allies?

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: ब्राह्मणानग्रहारैर्वा यथावदनुपश्यसि। कच्चित् ते परितुष्यन्ति शीलेन भरतर्षभ।॥ शत्रवोऽपि कुतः पौरा भृत्या वा स्वजनोऽपि वा। कच्चिद् यजसि राजेन्द्र श्रद्धावान् पितृदेवताः॥
en: Do you duly look after the Brahmanas, always making them the first gifts? What need I say of the citizens, and your servants, and kinsmen, are your foes, O chief of Bharata's race pleased with your conduct? Do you, O king of kings, adore with devotion the Pitris and the deities?

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: अतिथीनन्नपानेन कच्चिदर्चसि भारत। कच्चिन्नयपथे विप्राः स्वकर्मनिरतास्तव।॥
en: Do you adore guests with food and drink, O Bharata? Do the Brahmanas in your kingdom perforin the duties of their order, walk along the path of virtue?

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: क्षत्रिया वैश्यवर्गा वा शूद्रा वापि कुटुम्बिनः। कच्चित् स्त्रीबालवृद्धं ते न शोचति न याचते॥ जामयः पूजिताः कच्चित् तव गेहे नरर्षभ।
en: Do the Kshatriyas and Vaishyas and Shudras also within your kingdom and all your relatives, perform their respective duties? I hope the women, the children, and the old, among your subjects, do not grieve (under distress) and not beg (the necessaries of life).

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: कच्चिद् राजर्षिवंशोऽयं त्वामासाद्य महीपतिम्॥ यथोचितं महाराज यशसा नावसीदति। इत्येवंवादिनं तं स न्यायवित् प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Are the ladies of your households duly honoured in your house, O best of men? I hope, O king. that this race of royal sages, having to you for their king, have not fallen away from fame and glory?

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कुशलप्रश्नसंयुक्तं कुशलो वाक्यकर्मणि। कच्चित् ते वर्धते राजस्तपो दमशमौ च ते॥
en: Vaishampayana said To the old king who said so, Yudhishthira, knowing morality and justice and well-skilled in acts and speech, spoke as follows, putting some questions about his well-being.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अपि मे जननी चेयं शुश्रूषुर्विगतक्लमा। अथास्याः सफलो राजन् वनवासो भविष्यति॥
en: Yudhishthira said Does your peace, O king, your self-control, your tranquility of heart, grow? Is this my mother able to serve you without fatigue and trouble.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: इयं च माता ज्येष्ठा मे शीतवातावकर्शिता। घोरेण तपसा युक्ता देवी कच्चिन्न शोचति॥ हतान् पुत्रान् महावीर्यान् क्षत्रधर्मपरायणान्। नापध्यापति वा कच्चिदस्मान् पापकृतः सदा॥
en: Will, O king, her residence in the forest yield fruit? I hope this queen, who is my eldest mother, who is emaciated with (exposure to cold and wind and the toil of walking, and who is now given to the practice of serve austerities, no longer yields to grief for her children of great energy, of all whoin performing the duties of the Kshatriyas, have been killed on the field of battle.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: क्व चासौ विदुरो राजन् नेमं पश्यामहे वयम्। सञ्जयः कुशली चायं कच्चिन्नु तपसि स्थिरः॥
en: Does she accuse us. sinful wretches, who are responsible for their destruction? Where is Vidura, O king? We do not see him here. I hope this Sanjaya, performing penances, is in peace and happiness.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचेदं धृतराष्ट्रो जनाधिपम्। कुशली विदुरः पुत्र तपो घोरं समाश्रितः॥ वायुभक्षो निराहारः कृशो धमनिसन्ततः। कदाचिद् दृश्यते विप्रैः शून्येऽस्मिन् कानने क्वचित्॥
en: Thus addressed, Dhritarashtra, answered king Yudhishthira, saying, O son, Vidura is well. He is practising austere penances living on air alone, for he abstains from all other food. He is emaciated and his arteries and nerves have become visible. Sometimes he is seen in this empty forest by Brahmanas.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: इत्येवं ब्रुवतस्तस्य जटी वीटामुखः कृशः। दिग्वासा मलदिग्धाङ्गो वनरेणुसमुक्षितः॥
en: While Dhritarashtra was saying this. Vidura was seen at a distance. He had matted locks on his head, and gravel's in his mouth, and was greatly emaciated. He was perfectly naked. his body was besmeared all over with fifth, and with the dust of various wild flowers,

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: दूरादालक्षितः क्षत्ता तत्राख्यातो महीपतेः। निवर्तमानः सहसा राजन् दृष्ट्वाऽऽश्रमं प्रति॥
en: When Kshatta, was seen from a distance, the fact was communicated to Yudhishthira. Vidura suddenly stopped, O king, loO king towards the retreat.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: तमन्वधावन्नृपतिरेक एव युधिष्ठिरः। प्रविशन्तं वनं घोरं लक्ष्यालक्ष्यं क्वचित् क्वचित् ।।
en: King Yudhishthira pursued him alone, as he ran and entered the deep forest, sometimes seen and sometimes not seen by the pursuer.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: भो भो विदुर राजाहं दयितस्ते युधिष्ठिरः। इति ब्रुवन्नरपतिस्तं यत्नादभ्यधावत॥
en: He said aloud, 'O Vidura, O Vidura, I am king Yudhishthira, your favourite-Exclaiming thus, Yudhishthira, with great exertion, followed Vidura.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: ततो विविक्त एकान्ते तस्थौ बुद्धिमतां वरः। विदुरो वृक्षमाश्रित्य कच्चितत्र वनान्तरे॥
en: Having reached a solitary spot in the forest that foremost of intelligent men, viz., Vidura, stood still, learning against a tree.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: तं राजा क्षीणभूयिष्ठमाकृतीमात्रसूचितम्। अभिजज्ञे महाबुद्धिं महाबुद्धियुधिष्ठिरः॥
en: He was greatly emaciated. He retained only the shape of a human being. Yudhishthira of great intelligence recognised him, however.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: युधिष्ठिरोऽहमस्मीति वाक्यमुक्त्वाग्रतः स्थितः। विदुरस्य श्रवे राजा तं च प्रत्यभ्यपूजयत्॥
en: Standing before him, Yudhishthira addressed him saying, 'I am Yudhishthira.' Indeed, adoring Vidura properly., Yudhishthira said these words in the hearing of Vidura.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: ततः सोऽनिमिषो भूत्वा राजानं तमुदैक्षत। संयोज्य विदुरस्तस्मिन् दृष्टिं दृष्ट्या समाहितः॥
en: Meanwhile Vidura looked at the king steadfastly. Casting his look thus on the king, he stood motionless in Yoga.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: विवेश विदुरो धीमान् गात्रैर्गात्राणि चैव ह। प्राणान् प्राणेषु च दधदिन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियेषु च॥
en: Endued with great intelligence, he then (by his Yoga-power) entered the body of Yudhishthira, limb by limb. He united his vital airs with those of the king, and his senses with the king's senses.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: स योगबलमास्थाय विवेश नृपतेस्तनुम्। विदुरो धर्मराजस्य तेजसा प्रज्वलन्निव॥
en: Indeed, with the help of Yoga-power, Vidura, burning with energy, thus entered the body of king Yudhishthira the just.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: विदुरस्य शरीरं तु तथैव स्तब्धलोचनम्। वृक्षाश्रितं तदा राजा ददर्श गतचेतनम्॥
en: Meanwhile the body of Vidura continued to lean against the tree with eyes fixed. The king soon saw that life had fled out of it.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: बलवन्तं तथाऽऽत्मानं मेने बहुगुणं तदा। धर्मराजो महातेजास्तच्च सस्मार पाण्डवः॥ पौराणामात्मनः सर्वं विद्यावान् स विशाम्पते। योगधर्मं महातेजा व्यासेन कथितं यथा॥
en: At the same time, he felt that he himself had become stronger than before and that he had gained many additional virtues and accomplishments. Gifted with great learning and energy, O monarch, Pandu's son, king Yudhishthira the just, then recollected his own state before his birth among men, Possessed of mighty energy, he had heard of Yoga practice from Vyasa.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: धर्मराजश्च तत्रैव संचस्कारयिषुस्तदा। दग्धुकामोऽभवद् विद्वानथ वागभ्यभाषत॥ भो भो राजन्न दग्धव्यमेतद् विदुरसंज्ञकम्। कलेवरमिहैवं ते धर्म एष सनातनः॥
en: King Yudhishthira the just, endued with great learning, became desirous of doing the last rites to the body of Vidura, and wished to cremate it duly. An invisible voice was then heard, saying, 'O king, this body which belonged to him called Vidura should not be cremated. In him is your body also. He is the eternal deity of Virtue.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: लोकाः सान्तानिका नाम भविष्यन्त्यस्य भारत। यतिधर्ममवाप्तोऽसौ नैष शोच्यः परंतप॥
en: Those happy regions which pass by the name of Santanika will be his, O Bharata. he performed the duties of Yatis. You should not, O scorcher of enemies, grieve for him at all.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: इत्युक्तो धर्मराज: स विनिवृत्य ततः पुनः। राज्ञो वैचित्रवीर्यस्य तत् सर्वं प्रत्यवेदयत्॥
en: Thus addressed, king Yudhishthira the just returned from the place, and represented everything to the royal son of Vichitravirya.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: ततः स राजा द्युतिमान् स च सर्वो जनस्तदा। भीमसेनादयश्चैव परं विस्मयमागताः॥
en: At this, that effulgent king, all those men, and Bhimasena and others, became filled with wonder.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा प्रीतिमान् राजा भूत्वा धर्मजमब्रवीत्। आपो मूलं फलं चैव ममेदं प्रतिगृह्यताम्॥ यदर्थो हि नरो राजस्तदर्थोऽस्यातिथिः स्मृतः।
en: Hearing what had taken place, king Dhritarashtra became pleased and then, addressing the son of Dharma, said, 'Do you accept from me these gifts of water and roots and fruits! It has been said, O king, that one's guest should take what one takes himself.'

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: इत्युक्तः स तथेत्येवं प्राह धर्मात्मजो नृपम्॥ फलं मूलं च बुभुजे राज्ञा दत्तं सहानुजः।
en: Thus addressed, Dharma's son answered armed king ate the fruits and roots which he gave.

description: Dhritarashtra enquires Yudhishthira of his well-being and the latter's reply
sn: ततस्ते वृक्षमूलेषु कृतवासपरिग्रहाः। तां रात्रिमवसन् सर्वे फलमूलजलाशनाः॥
en: Then they all spread their beds under a tree and passed that night thus having eaten fruits and roots and drunk the water that the old monarch had given them.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तु राजन्नेतेषामाश्रमे पुण्यकर्मणाम्। शिवा नक्षत्रसम्पन्ना सा व्यतीयाय शर्वरी॥
en: They passed that night which was marked out by auspicious constellations thus, o king, in that hermitage of pious ascetics.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: ततस्तत्र कथाश्चासंस्तेषां धर्मार्थलक्षणाः। विचित्रपदसंचारा नानाश्रुतिभिरन्विताः॥
en: The conversation that took place was marked by many reflections on morality and wealth. Consisting of delightful and sweet words, it was greed with various citations from the Shrutis.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: पाण्डवास्त्वभितो मातुर्धरण्यां सुषुपुस्तदा। उत्सृज्य तु महार्हाणि शयनानि नराधिप।॥
en: The Pandavas, O king, leaving costly beds, laid themselves down, near their in other, on the naked earth.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: यदाहारोऽभवद् राजा धृतराष्ट्रो महामनाः। तदाहार नृवीरास्ते न्यवसंस्तां निशां तदा॥
en: Indeed, those heroes passed that night, having eaten the food which was the food of the great king Dhritarashtra.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: व्यतीतायां तु शर्वर्यां कृतपौर्वाह्निकक्रियः। भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजा ददर्शाश्रममण्डलम्॥
en: After the night had passed away, king Yudhishthira, having performed his morning rites proceeded to survey that'hermitage in the company of his brothers.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: सान्तःपुरपरीवारः सभृत्यः सपुरोहितः। यथासुखं यथोद्देशं धृतराष्ट्राभ्यनुज्ञया।॥
en: With the royal ladies, the servants, and his priest, the king roved about the hermitage in all directions as he pleased, at the command of Dhritarashtra.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: ददर्श तत्र वेदीश्च संप्रज्वलितपावकाः। कृताभिषेकैर्मुनिभिर्हताग्निभिरुपस्थिताः॥
en: He saw many sacrificial alters with sacred firs burning on them and with many ascetics seated on them, who had performed their oblations and poured libations in honour of the celestials.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: वानेयपुष्पनिकरैराज्यधूमोद्गमैरपि। ब्राह्मणे वपुषा युक्ता युक्ता मुनिगणस्य ताः॥
en: Those alters were covered with fruits and roots of he forest, and with heaps of flowers. The smoke of clarified butter curled upwards from them. They were graced, besides, with many ascetics possessed of bodies which appeared like the embodied Vedas and with many laymen.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: मृगयूथैरनुद्विग्नस्तत्र तत्र समाश्रितैः। अशङ्कितैः पक्षिगणैः प्रगीतैरिव च प्रभो॥
en: Herds of deer were grazing or resting here and there, shorn of fear. Countless birds also were there, engaged in uttering their sweet notes, O king!

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: केकाभिर्नीलकण्ठानां दात्यूहानां च कूजितैः। कोकिलानां कुहुरवैः सुखैः श्रुतिमनोहरैः॥
en: The entire forest seemed to resound with the notes of peacocks and Datyuhas and Kokilas and the sweet songs of other warblers.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: प्राधीतद्विजघोषैश्च क्वचित् क्वचिदलंकृतम्। फलमूलसमाहारैर्महद्भिश्चोपशोभितम्॥
en: Some spots were echoed with the chaunt of Vedic hymns recited by learned Brahmanas. Some were adorned wit large heaps of fruits and roots gathered from the forest.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: ततः स राजा प्रददौ तापसार्थमुपाहृतान्। कलशान् काञ्चनान् राजंस्तथैवौदुम्बरानपि।॥ अजिनानि प्रवेणीश्च स्रुक् स्रुवं च महीपतिः। कमण्डलूंश्च स्थालीश्च पिठराणि च भारत॥
en: King Yudhishthira then distributed amongst those ascetics golden or copper jars which he had brought for them, and many deer-skins and blankets and wooden sacrificial ladies and Kamandalus and wooden Platters, and pots and pans, O Bharata.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: भाजनानि च लौहानि पात्रीश्च विविधा नृप। यद् यदिच्छति यावच्च यच्चान्यदपि भाजनम्॥
en: Various kinds of vessels, made of iron, and smaller vessels and cups of various sizes, were also given away by the king, the ascetics taking them away, each as many as he liked.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: एवं स राजा धर्मात्मा परीत्याश्रममण्डलम्। वसु विश्राण्य तत् सर्वं पुनरायान्महीपतिः॥
en: Pious king Yudhishthira, having thus roved through the forest and seen the various retreats of ascetics and made many gifts, returned to the place where his uncle was.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: कृताह्निकं च राजानं धृतराष्ट्रं महीपतिम्। ददर्शासीनमव्यग्रं गान्धारीसहितं तदा॥
en: He saw king Dhritarashtra, seated at ease, with Gandhari besides him, after having finished his morning rites.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: मातरं चाविदूरस्थां शिष्यवत् प्रणतां स्थिताम्। कुन्तीं ददर्श धर्मात्मा शिष्टाचारसमन्विताम्॥
en: The righteous souled monarch beheld also his mother, Kunti, seated not much remote from that place, like a disciple with bent head, gifted with humility.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: स तमभ्यर्च्य राजानं नाम संश्राव्य चात्मनः। निषीदेत्यभ्यनुज्ञातो बृस्यामुपविवेश ह॥
en: He saluted the old king giving his name. 'Sit down', were the words the old king said. With Dhritarashtra's permission, Yudhishthira sat himself down on a mat of Kusha grass.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: भीमसेनादश्यचैव पाण्डवा भरतर्षभ। अभिवाद्योपसंगृह्य निषेदुः पार्थिवाज्ञया॥
en: Then the other sons of Pandu with Bhima among them, O you of Bharata's race, saluted the king and touched his feet and sat themselves down, with his order.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: स तैः परिवृतो राजा शुशुभेऽतीव कौरवः। बिभ्रद् ब्राह्मीं श्रियं दीप्तां देवैरिव बृहस्पतिः॥
en: The old Kuru king, surrounded by them looked highly beautiful, indeed, he blazed with a Vedic splendour like Brihaspati in the midst of the celestials.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: तथा तेषूपविष्टेषु समाजग्मुर्महर्षयः। शतयूपप्रभृतयः कुरुक्षेत्रनिवासिनः॥
en: After they had sat themselves down, many great Rishis, viz., Shatayupa, and others, who were inhabitants of Kurukshetra came there.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: व्यासश्च भगवान् विप्रो देवर्षिगणसेवितः। वृतः शिष्यैर्महातेजा दर्शयामास पार्थिवम्॥
en: The illustrious and learned Vyasa, gifted with great energy and respected by even the celestial Rishis, showed himself at the head of his numerous disciples to Yudhishthira.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: ततः स राजा कौरव्यः कुन्तीपुत्रश्च वीर्यवान्। भीमसेनादयश्चैव प्रत्युत्थायाभ्यवादयन्॥
en: The Kuru king Dhritarashtra, Kunti's son Yudhishthira of great energy, and Bhimasena and others, stood up and going a few steps, saluted those guests.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: समागतस्ततो व्यासः शतयूपादिभिर्वृतः। धृतराष्ट्रं महीपालमास्यतामित्यभाषत।॥
en: Approaching near, Vyasa, surrounded by Shatayupa and others, addressed king Dhritarashtra, saying, 'Be seated.'

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: वरं तु विष्टरं कौश्यं कृष्णाजिनकुशोत्तरम्। प्रतिपदे तदा व्यासस्तदर्थमुपकल्पितम्॥
en: The illustrious Vyasa then took an excellent seat made of Kusha grass placed upon a black deer-skin and covered with a piece of silken cloth. They has reserved that seat for him.

description: The passing of a day in the forest by Yudhishthira
sn: ते च सर्वे द्विजश्रेष्ठा विष्टरेषु समन्ततः। द्वैपायनाभ्यनुज्ञाता निषेदुर्विपुलौजसः॥
en: After Vyasa had been seated, all those foremost of twice-born persons, gifted with profuse energy, sat themselves down, with the permission of Krishna-Dvaipayana.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः समुपविष्टेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। व्यासः सत्यवतीपुत्र इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ धृतराष्ट्र महाबाहो कच्चित् ते वर्तते तपः। कच्चिन्मनस्ते प्रीणाति वनवासे नराधिप॥
en: Vaishampayana said, After the noble Pandavas had all been seated, Satyavati's son Vyasa said, 'O Dhritarashtra of mighty-arms, have you been able to achieve penances? Is your mind, O king, pleased with your living in the forest?

sn: कच्चिद्धृदि न ते शोको राजन् पुत्रविनाशजः। कच्चिज्ज्ञानानि सर्वाणि सुप्रसन्नानि तेऽनघ॥
en: Has your grief begotten of the destruction of our sons in battle, disappeared from your heart? Are all your perceptions, O sinless one, now clear?

sn: कच्चिद् बुद्धिं दृढां कृत्वा चरस्यारण्यकं विधिम्। कच्चिद् वधूश्च गान्धारी न शोकेनाभिभूयते॥
en: Do you practise the ordinances of forest-life after having made your heart firin? Does my daughter-in-law, Gandhari, suffer herself to be overwhelmed by grief?

sn: महाप्रज्ञा बुद्धिमती देवी धर्मार्थदर्शिनी। आगमापायतत्त्वज्ञा कच्चिदेषा न शोचति॥
en: She is endued with great wisdom. Endued with intelligence, that queen understands both virtue and profit. She is well conversant with the truths which relate to both prosperity and adversity. Does not still grieve?

sn: कच्चित् कुन्ती च राजंस्त्वां शुश्रूषत्यनहंकृता। या परित्यज्य स्वं पुत्रं गुरुशुश्रूषणे रता॥
en: Does Kunti, o king, who for her devotion to the service of her seniors, left her children, attend to your wants and serve your with all humility?

sn: कच्चिद् धर्मसुतो राजा त्वया प्रत्यभिनन्दितः। भीमार्जुनयमाश्चैव कच्चिदेतेऽपि सान्त्विताः॥
en: Have the high-minded and great king Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, and Bhima and Arjuna, and the twins, been sufficiently comforted?

sn: कच्चिन्नन्दसि दृष्ट्वैतान् कच्चित् ते निर्मलं मनः। कच्चिच्च शुद्धभावोऽसि जातज्ञानो नराधिप॥
en: Do you feel delight at seeing them? Has your mind become freed from every strain? Has your disposition, O king, become pure on account of he increase of your knowledge?

sn: एतद्धि त्रितयं श्रेष्ठं सर्वभूतेषु भारत। निर्वैरता महाराज सत्यमक्रोध एव च॥
en: These three, O king, are the foremost of all concerns, O Bharata, viz., abstension from injury to any creation, truth, and freedom from anger.

sn: कच्चित् तेन च मोहोऽस्ति वनवासेन भारत। स्ववशे वन्यमन्नं वा उपवासोऽपि वा भवेत्॥
en: Does your forest-life any longer prove painful to you? Are you able to acquire with your own exertions the products of the forest for your food? Do fasts pain you now?

sn: विदितं चापि राजेन्द्र विदुरस्य महात्मनः। गमनं विधिनाऽनेन धर्मस्य सुमहात्मनः॥
en: Have you learnt 'o king, how the great Vidura, who was Dharma's self, left this world?

sn: माण्डव्यशापाद्धि स वै धर्मो विदुरतां गतः। महाबुद्धिर्महायोगी महात्मा सुमहामनाः॥
en: Through the curse of Mandavya, the deity of Virtue became born as Vidura. He was gifted with great intelligence. Endued with high penances, he was great and high-minded.

sn: बृहस्पतिर्वा देवेषु शुक्रो वाप्यसुरेषु च। न तथा बुद्धिसम्पन्नो यथा स पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Even Brihaspati among the celestials, and Shukra among the Asuras, had not intelligence like that foremost of persons.

sn: तपोबलव्ययं कृत्वा सुचिरात् सम्भृतं तदा। माण्डव्येनर्षिणा धर्मो ह्यभिभूतः सनातनः॥
en: The eternal deity of Virtue was stupefied by the Rishi Mandavya with an expenditure of his penances acquired for a long time with great care,

sn: नियोगाद् ब्रह्मणः पूर्वे मया स्वेन बलेन च। वैचित्रवीर्यके क्षेत्रे जातः स सुमहामतिः॥
en: At the command of the grandfather and through my own energy, the highly intelligent Vidura was procreated by me upon a soil owned by Vichitravirya.

sn: भ्राता तव महाराज देवदेवः सनातनः। धारणान्मनसा ध्यानाद् यं धर्मं कवयो विदुः॥
en: A deity of deities, and eternal, he was, O king, your brother. The learned know him to be Dharma on account of his practices of concentration and abstraction.

sn: सत्येन संवर्धयति यो दमेन शमेन च। अहिंसया च दानेन तप्यमानः सनातनः॥
en: He grows with truth, self-respect, tranquillity of heat, mercy, and gifts. He is always engaged in penances, and is eternal.

sn: येन योगबलाज्जातः कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। धर्म इत्येष नृपते प्राज्ञेनामितबुद्धिना॥
en: From that deity of Virtue, through YogaPower, the Kuru king Yudhishthria also took his birth. Yudhishthira, therefore, O king, is Dharma of great wisdom and immeasurable intelligence.

sn: यथा वह्निर्यथा वायुर्यथाऽऽपः पृथिवी यथा। यथाऽऽकाशं तथा धर्म इह चामुत्र च स्थितः॥
en: Dharma exists both in this world and in the next, and is like fire or wind or water or earth or space.

sn: सर्वगश्चैव राजेन्द्र सर्वं व्याप्य चराचरम्। दृश्यते देवदेवैः स सिद्धैर्निर्मुक्तकल्मषैः॥
en: He is, o king of kings, capable of going everywhere and exists, pervading the entire universe. He is capable of being seen by only those who are the foremost of the deities and those who are purged of every sin and crowned with ascetic success.

sn: यो हि धर्मः स विदुरो विदुरो यः स पाण्डवः। स एष राजन् दृश्यस्ते पाण्डवः प्रेष्यवत् स्थितः॥२१
en: He who is Dharma, is Vidura and he who is Vidura is the (eldest) son of Pandu. That son of Pandu, O king, is capable of being perceived by you. He is before you as your servitor.

sn: प्रविष्टः स महात्मानं भ्राता ते बुद्धिसत्तमः। दृष्ट्वा महात्मा कौन्तेयं महायोगबलान्वितः॥
en: Gifted with great Yoga-Power, your highsouled brother, that foremost of intelligent men, seeing the high-souled Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti has entered into his body.

sn: त्वां चापि श्रेयसा योक्ष्ये न चिराद् भरतर्षभ। संशयच्छेदनार्थाय प्राप्तं मां विद्धि पुत्रका॥
en: O chief of Bharata's race, I shall unite you also with great benefit. Know, O son, that I am come here for removing your doubts.

sn: न कृतं यैः पुरा कैश्चित् कर्म लोके महर्षिभिः। आश्चर्यभूतं तपसः फलं तद् दर्शयामि वः॥
en: I shall show you some feat which has never been accomplished before by any of the great Rishis-some wonderful effect of my penances.

sn: किमिच्छसि महीपाल मत्तः प्राप्तुमभीप्सितम्। द्रष्टुं स्प्रष्टुमथ श्रोतुं तत्कर्ताऽस्मि तवानघ।॥
en: What object is that, O king, whose accomplishment you wish from me? Tell me what is that which you wish to see or ask or hear? O sinless one, I shall accomplish it.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: जनमेजय उवाच वनवासं गते विप्र धृतराष्ट्र महीपतौ। सभार्ये नृपशार्दूले बध्वा कुन्त्या समन्विते॥ विदुरे चापि संसिद्धे धर्मराजं व्यपाश्रिते। वसत्सु पाण्डुपुत्रेषु सर्वेष्वाश्रममण्डले॥ यत् तदाश्चर्यमिति वै करिष्यामीत्युवाच ह। व्यासः परमतेजस्वी महर्षिस्तद् वदस्व मे॥
en: Janamejaya said Tell me, o learned Brahman, what that wonderful feat was, which the great Rishi Vyasa of great energy accomplished after he had his made promise to the old king, when Dhritarashtra, that foremost one of Kuru's race, had taken up his residence in the forest, with his wife, and with his daughter-in-law Kunti and after, indeed, Vidura had left his own body and entered into Yudhishthria, and at the time when all the sons of Pandu were living in the hermitage.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: वनवासे च कौरव्यः कियन्तं कालमच्युतः। युधिष्ठिरो नरपति→वसत् सजनस्तदा॥
en: For how many days did the Kuru king Yudhishthira of Undecaying glory, stay with his men in the forest.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: किमाहाराश्च ते तत्र ससैन्या न्यवसन् प्रभो। सान्त:पुरा महात्मान इति तद् ब्रूहि मेऽनघ॥
en: Of what food, O powerful one, did the great Pandavas support themselves with their men, and wives, while they lived in the forest? O sinless one, do you tell me this.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तेऽनुज्ञातास्तदा राजन् कुरुराजेन पाण्डवाः। विविधान्यन्नपानानि विश्राम्यानुभवन्ति ते॥ मासमेकं विजह्वस्ते ससैन्यान्तःपुरा वने। अथ तत्रागमद् व्यासो यथोक्तं ते मयाऽनघ॥
en: Vaishampayana said With the permission of the Kuru king, the Pandavas, O monarch, with their troops and the ladies of their household, lived on various kinds of food and drink and passed about a month in great happiness in that forest. Towards the close of that period, O sinless one, Vyasa came there.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: तथा च तेषां सर्वेषां कथाभिर्नृपसंनिधौ। व्यासमन्वास्यतां राजन्नाजग्मुर्मुनयो परे॥
en: While all those princes sat around Vyasa, engaged in conversation on various topics, other Rishis came there.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: नारदः पर्वतश्चैव देवलश्च महातपाः। विश्वावसुस्तुम्बुस्च चित्रसेनश्च भारत॥
en: They were Narada, Parvata, Devala of austere penances, Vishvavasu, Tunburu and Chitrasena, O Bharata.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: तेषामपि यथान्यायं पूजां चक्रे महातपाः। धृतराष्ट्राभ्यनुज्ञातः कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Gifted with severe penances, the Kuru king Yudhishthira, with the permission of Dhritarasthra, adored them according to due rites.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: निषेदुस्ते ततः सर्वे पूजां प्राप्य युधिष्ठिरात्। आसनेषु च पुण्येषु बर्हिणेषु वरेषु च॥
en: Having got that worship from Yudhishthira, all of them sat down on sacred seats (made of Kusha grass as also on excellent seats made of peacock feathers.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: तेषु तत्रोपविष्टेषु स तु राजा महामतिः। पाण्डुपुत्रैः परिवृतो निषसाद कुरूद्वह॥
en: After they had all been seated, the Kuru king of great intelligence took his seat there, surrounded by the sons of Pandu.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: गान्धारी चैव कुन्ती च द्रौपदी सात्वती तथा। स्त्रियश्चान्यास्तथान्याभिः सहोपविविशुस्ततः॥
en: Gandhari, Kunti and Draupadi, and she of the Satvata race, and other ladies of the royal household also sat down.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: तेषां तत्र कथा दिव्या धर्मिष्ठाश्चाभवन् नृप। ऋषीणां च पुराणानां देवासुरविमिश्रिताः॥
en: The conversation which then arose was excellent and had reference to subjects, connected with piety, and the Rishis of old, and the celestials and the Asuras.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: तत: कथान्ते व्यासस्तं प्रज्ञाचक्षुषमीश्वरम्। प्रोवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठः पुनरेव स तद् वचः॥ प्रीयमाणो महातेजाः सर्ववेदविदां वरः। विदितं मम राजेन्द्र यत् ते हृदि विवक्षितम्॥ दह्यमानस्य शोकेन तव पुत्रकृतेन वै। गान्धार्याश्चैव यद् दुःखं हृदि तिष्ठति नित्यदा॥ कुन्त्याश्च यन्महाराज द्रौपद्याश्च हृदि स्थितम्। यच्च धारयते तीव्र दुःखं पुत्रविनाशजम्॥ सुभद्रा कृष्णभगिनी तच्चापि विदितं मम। श्रुत्वा समागममिमं सर्वेषां वस्तुतो नृप॥ संशयच्छेदनार्थाय प्राप्तः कौरवनन्दन। इमे च देवगन्धर्वाः सर्वे चेमे महर्षयः॥ पश्यन्तु तपसो वीर्यमद्य मे चिरसम्भृतम्। तदुच्यतां महाप्राज्ञ कं कामं प्रददामि ते॥
en: At the close of the conversation the highly energetic Vyasa, that foremost of eloquent men, that first of all persons knowing the Vedas highly pleased, addressed the blind monarch and once more said, 'Burning as you are with grief on account of your children, I know, O king of kings, what object is cherished by you in your heart. I know the sorrow which always exists in the heart of Gandhari, that which exists in the heart of Kunti, and that also which is cherished by Draupadi in her heart, and that burning grief, on. account of the death of her son, which Krishna's sister Subhadra also cherishes. Hearing of this meeting, O king, of yours with all these princes and princesses of your house., I have come here, O delighter of the Kauravas, for removing your doubts. Let the celestials and Gandharvas and all these great Rishis, see today the energy of those penances which I have acquired for these long years. Therefore, O king, tell me what wish of yours I shall grant today.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: प्रवणोऽस्मि वरं दातुं पश्य मे तपसः फलम्। एवमुक्तः स राजेन्द्रो व्यासेनामितबुद्धिना॥ मुहूर्तमिव संचिन्त्य वचनायोपचक्रमे। धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतश्च सफलं जीवितं च मे॥ यन्मे समागमोऽोह भवद्भिः सह साधुभिः। अद्य चाप्यवगच्छामि गतिमिष्टामिहात्मनः॥ ब्रह्मकल्पैर्भवद्भिर्यत् समेतोऽहं तपोधनाः। दर्शनादेव भवतां पूतोऽहं नात्र संशयः॥
en: I am powerful enough to grant you a boon. See the fruit of my penances. Thus addressed by Vyasa of great understanding, king Dhritarashtra thought for a moment and then prepared to speak. He said, 'I ain greatly fortunate. Lucky am I in obtaining your favour. My life is crowned with success today, since this meeting has taken place between me and you all of great piety. To-day I shall attain to that highly happy end which is reserved for me, since, you ascetics who have penances for wealth, you who are equal to Brahma himself, I have succeeded in obtaining this meeting with you all. There is not the least doubt that this sight that I have obtained of you all has purged me of every sin. son

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: विद्यते न भयं चापि परलोकान्ममानधाः। किं तु तस्य सुदुर्बुद्धेर्मन्दस्यापनयैर्भृशम्॥ दूयते मे मनो नित्यं स्मरतः पृत्रगृद्धिनः। अपापाः पाण्डवा येन निकृताः पापबुद्धिना॥
en: O sinless ones, I have no longer any fear about my end in the next world. Full as I am of love for my children, I always remember them. My mind, however is always pained by the recollection of the various acts of wrong which my wicked of exceedingly evil understanding perpetrated. Having a sinful understanding, he always persecuted the innocent Pandavas.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: घातिता पृथिवी येन सहया सनरद्विपा। राजानश्च महात्मानो नानाजनपदेश्वराः॥ आगम्य मम पुत्रार्थे सर्वे मृत्युवशं गताः। ये ते पितूंश्च दारांश्च प्राणांश्च मनसः प्रियान्॥ परित्यज्य गताः शूराः प्रेतराजनिवेशनम्। का नु तेषां गतिर्ब्रह्मन् मित्रार्थे ये हता मृधे॥ तथैव पुत्रपौत्राणां मम ये निहता युधि। दूयते मे मनोऽभीक्ष्णं घातयित्वा महाबलम्॥ भीष्मं शान्तनवं वृद्धं द्रोणं च द्विजसत्तमम्। मम पुत्रेण मूढेन पापेनाकृतबुद्धिना॥
en: Alas, the whole Earth has been devastated by him, with her horses, elephants and men. Many great kings, rulers of various kingdoms, came for helping my son and succumbed to death. Alas, leaving their beloved father and wives and their very life-breaths, all those heroes have become guests of the king of the dead. What end, O twice-born one, has been attained by those men who have killed, for the sake of their friend, in battle? What end also has attained by my sons and grandsons who have fallen in the battle? My heart is always pained at the thought of my having brought about the destruction of the powerful Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, and of Drona, that foremost of Brahmanas, through my foolish and sinful son who was an injurer of his friends.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: क्षयं नीतं कुलं दीप्तं पृथिवीराज्यमिच्छता। एतत् सर्वमनुस्मृत्य दह्यमानो दिवानिशम्॥
en: Desirous of getting the sovereignty of the Earth, he caused the Kuru race, blazing with prosperity, to be annihilated. Thinking of all this, I burn day and night with grief.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: न शान्तिमधिगच्छापि दुःखशोकसमाहतः। इति मे चिन्तयानस्य पितः शान्तिन विद्यते॥
en: Deeply afflicted with pain and grief, I am unable to get peace of mind. Indeed, O sire, thinking of all this, I have no peace of man.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छुत्वा विविधं तस्य राजर्षेः परिदेवितम्। पुनर्नवीकृतः शोको गान्धार्या जनमेजय॥
en: Hearing these lamentation expressed in various ways, of that royal sage, the grief, O Janamejaya of Gandhari, became fresh.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: कुन्त्या दुपदपुत्र्याश्च सुभद्रायास्तथैव च। तासां च वरनारीणां वधूनां कौरवस्य हा॥
en: The grief, also, of Kunti, of the daughter of Drupada, of Subhadra, and of the other members male and female, and the daughterin-law of the royal house of Kuru became equally green.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: पुत्रशोकसमाविष्टा गान्धारी त्विदमब्रवीत्। श्वशुरं बद्धनयना देवी प्राञ्जलिरुत्थिता॥ षोडशेमानि वर्षाणि गतानि मुनिपुङ्गव। अस्य राज्ञो हतान् पुत्राशोचतो न शमो विभो॥
en: Queen Gandhari, with bandaged eyes, joining her hands, addressed her father-in-law. Deeply afflicted with grief on account of the destruction of her sons, she said-O foremost of ascetics, this king has passed sixteen years grieving for the death of his sons and shorn of peace of mind.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: पुत्रशोकसमाविष्टो निःश्वसन् ह्येष भूमिपः। न शेते वसतीः सर्वा धृतराष्ट्रो महामुने॥
en: Afflicted with grief on account of the destruction of his his children, this king Dhritarashtra, always breathes heavily, and never sleeps at night, O great Rishi.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: लोकानन्यान् समर्थोऽसि स्रष्टुं सर्वांस्तपोबलात्। किमु लोकान्तरगतान् राज्ञो दर्शयितुं सुतान्॥
en: Through the power of your penances you are competent to create new worlds. What need I say then about showing this king his children who are now in the other world?

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: इयं च द्रौपदी कृष्णा हतज्ञातिसुता भृशम्। शौचत्यतीव सर्वासां स्नुषाणां दयिता स्नुषा॥
en: This Krishna, the daughter of Drupada, has lost all her kinsmen and children. Therefore, she who is the dearest of my daughters-in-law grieves greatly.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: तथा कृष्णस्य भगिनी सुभद्रा भद्रभाषिणी। सौभद्रवधसंतप्ता भृशं शोचति भाविनी॥
en: The sister of Krishna, viz., Subhadra of sweet words, burning with the loss of her son, grieves as deeply.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: इयं च भूरिश्रवसो भार्या परमसम्मता। भर्तृव्यसनशोकार्ता भृशं शोचति भाविनी॥
en: This lady who is respected by all, who is the wife of Bhurishravas, stricken with grief on account of the fate of her husband, always indulges in heart-rending lamentations.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: यस्यास्तुश्वशुरो धीमान् बाह्निकः स कुरूद्वहः। निहतः सोमदत्तश्च पित्रा सह महारणे॥
en: Her father-in-law the intelligent Valhika of Kuru's race. Alas, Somadatta also was was killed, along with his father, in the great battle.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: श्रीमतोऽस्य महाबुद्धेः संग्रामेष्वपलायिनः। पुत्रस्य ते पुत्रशतं निहतं यद् रणाजिरे॥
en: Alas, a hundred sons, heroes who never retreated from battle, belonging to this son of yours, this king of great intelligence and great prosperity, has been killed in battle.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: तस्य भार्याशतमिदं दुःखशोकसमाहतम्। पुनः पुनर्वर्धयानं शोकं राज्ञो ममैव च॥ तेनारम्भेण महता मामुपास्ते महामुने।
en: The hundred wives of those sons are all grieving and repeatedly increasing the grief of both the king and myself. O great ascetic, stricken by that great onslaught, they have gathered round me.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: ये च शूरा महात्मानः श्वशुरा मे महारथाः॥ सोमदत्तप्रभृतयः का नु तेषां गतिः प्रभो।
en: Alas, those great heroes, those great carwarriors, my father-in-law, Somadatta and others, alas, what end has been theirs, O powerful one.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: तव प्रसादाद् भगवन् विशोकोऽयं महीपतिः॥ यथा स्याद् भविता चाहं कुन्ती चेयं वधूस्तव।
en: Through your favour, O holy one, that will take place for which this king, myself and this daughter-in-law of yours, viz., Kunti, shall all become freed from our grief.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: इत्युक्तवत्यां गान्धार्यो कुन्ती व्रतकृशानना॥ प्रच्छन्नजातं पुत्रं तं सस्मारादित्यसंनिधम्।
en: After Gandhari had said so, Kunti, whose face had become waste through observance of many hard vows, began to think of her secretborn son gifted with solar effulgence.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: तामृषिर्वरदो व्यासो दूरश्रवणदर्शनः॥ अपश्यद् दुःखितां देवीं मातरं सव्यसाचिनः।
en: The boon-giving Rishi Vyasa capable of both seeing and hearing what took place at a remote distance, saw that the royal mother of Arjuna was afflicted with grief.

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: तामुवाच ततो व्यासो यत् ते कार्यं विवक्षितम्॥ तद् ब्रूहि त्वं महाभागे यत् ते मनसि वर्तते।
en: To her Vyasa said, 'Tell me, O blessed one, what is in your mind. Tell me what you wish to say.'

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: श्वशुराय तत: कुन्ती प्रणम्य शिरसा तदा॥ उवाच वाक्यं सव्रीडा विवृण्वाना पुरातनम्॥
en: At this, Kunti, bending her head to herfather-in-law, and overcome with bashfulness, said these words to him, recounting the past incidents of her life. To her Vyasa said, 'Tell me, O blessed one, what is in your mind. Tell me what you wish to say.'

description: The conversation of Vyasa and other ascetics
sn: श्वशुराय तत: कुन्ती प्रणम्य शिरसा तदा॥ उवाच वाक्यं सव्रीडा विवृण्वाना पुरातनम्॥
en: At this, Kunti, bending her head to herfather-in-law, and overcome with bashfulness, said these words to him, recounting the past incidents of her life.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: कुन्त्युवाच भगवश्वशुरो मेऽसि दैवतस्यापि दैवतम्। स मे देवातिदेवस्त्वं शृणु सत्या गिरं मम॥
en: Kunti said O holy one, you are my father-in-law and, therefore, my deity of deities. You are my god of gods. Hear my words of truth.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: तपस्वी कोपनो विप्रो दुर्वासा नाम मे पितुः। भिक्षामुपातो भोक्तुं तमहं पर्यतोषयम्॥ शौचेन त्वागसस्त्यागैः शुद्धेन मनसा तथा। कोपस्थानेष्वपि महत्स्वकुष्यन्न कदाचन।॥
en: A twice-born ascetic named Durvasas, who is full of anger, came to my father's house for begging alms. I succeeded in pleasing him by the purity of my conduct and of my minds as also by refusing to notice the many wrongs he did. I did not yield to anger although there was much in his conduct quite capable of exciting that passion.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: स प्रीतो वरदो मेऽभूत् कृतकृत्यो महामुनिः। अवश्यं ते गृहीतव्यमिति मां सोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: Served with care, the great ascetic became highly pleased with me and disposed to grant me a boon. 'You must accept the boon I shall give,' were his words to me.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: ततः शापभयाद् विप्रमवोचं पुनरेव तम्। एवमस्त्विति च प्राह पुनरेव स मे द्विजः॥ धर्मस्य जननी भद्रे भवित्री त्वं शुभानने। वशे स्थास्यन्ति ते देवा यांस्त्वमावाहयिष्यसि॥
en: Fearing his curse, I answered him saying, 'So be it.' The Rishi once more said to me, '0 blessed damsel, O you of beautiful face, you will become the mother of Dharma. Those deities whom you will summon will obey you,

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: इत्युक्त्वान्तर्हितो विप्रस्ततोऽहं विस्मिताभवम्। न च सर्वास्ववस्थासु रमृतिर्मे विप्रणश्यति॥
en: Having said these words, the twice-born one vanished away from my sight. I becamefilled with wonder. The Mantra, however, which the Rishi gave has lived in my memory at all times.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: अथ हर्म्यतलस्थाहं रविमुद्यन्तमीक्षती। संस्मृत्य तदृषेर्वाक्यं स्पृहयन्ती दिवानिशम्॥
en: One day, sitting with my chamber I saw the sun rising. Desiring to bring the maker of day before me, I recollected the words of the Rishi.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: स्थिताऽहं बालभावेन तत्र दोषमबुद्ध्यती। अथ देवः सहस्रांशुमत्समीपगतोऽभवत्॥
en: Without any consciousness of the fault I committed, I called the deity from mere childishness. The deity, of a thousand rays, before me.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: द्विधा कृत्वाऽऽत्मनो देहं भूमौ च गगनेऽपि च। तताप लोकानेकेन द्वितीयेनागमत् स माम्॥
en: He divided himself in two parts. With one portion he was in the sky, and with the other he stood on the Earth before me. With one he hearted the worlds and with another he came to came me.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: स मामुवाच वेपन्तीं वरं मत्तो वृणीष्व ह। गम्यतामिति तं चाहं प्रणम्य शिरसाऽवदम्॥
en: He told me, while I was trembling at his sight, these words:-Do you ask a boon of me.' Bowing to him with my head I asked him to leave me.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: स मामुवाच तिग्मांशुवृथाऽऽह्वानं न मे क्षमम्। धक्ष्यामि त्वां च विप्रं च येन दत्तो वरस्तव॥
en: He replied to me, saying, 'I cannot bear the idea of coming to you fruitlessly, I shall consume you as also that Brahmana who gave you the Mantra as a boon.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: तमहं रक्षती विप्रं शापादनपकारिणम्। पुत्रो मे त्वत्समो देव भवेदिति ततोऽब्रवम्॥
en: I wished to protect, from Surya's curse, the Brahmana who had done no evil. I, therefore, said, 'Let me have a son like you, O god.'

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: ततो मां तेजसाऽऽविश्य मोहयित्वा च भानुमान् । उवाच भविता पुत्रस्तवेत्यभ्यगमद् दिवम्॥
en: The deity o. thousand rays then entered me with his energy and stupefied me completely. He then said to me, 'You will have a son, and then returned to the firmament.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: ततोऽहमन्तर्भवने पितुर्वृत्तान्तरक्षिणी। गूढोत्पन्नं सुतं बालं जले कर्णमवासृजम्॥
en: I continued to live in the inner apartments and desirous of saving the honour of my father, I cast into the waters my infant son named Karna who thus came into the world secretly.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: नूनं तस्येव देवस्य प्रसादात् पुनरेव तु। कन्याऽहमभवं विप्र यथा प्राह स मामृषिः॥
en: Forsooth, through the grace of that god, I once more became a virgin, Otwice-born one, even as the Rishi Durvasas he said to me.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: स मया मूढया पुत्रो ज्ञायमानोऽप्युपेक्षितः। तन्मां दहति विप्रर्षे यथा सुविदितं तव॥
en: Foolish that I am, although he knew me for his mother when he grew up, yet I did not try to acknowledge him. This burns me, O Rishi, as is well-known to you.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: यदि पापमपापं वा तवैतद् विवृतं मया। तन्मे दहन्तं भगवन् व्यपनेतुं त्वमर्हसि॥
en: Whether it is sinful or not so, I have told you the truth. You should. O holy one, satisfy the craving I feel for seeing that son of mine.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: यच्चास्य राज्ञो विदितं हृदिस्थं भवतोऽनघ। तं चायं लभतां काममद्यैव मुनिसत्तम॥
en: O foremost of ascetics, let this king also, O sinless one, obtain the fruition today of that desire of his which he cherishes in his bosom and which has become known to you.'

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचेदं व्यासो वेदविदां वरः। साधु सर्वमिदं भाव्यमेवमेतद् यथाऽऽत्य माम्॥
en: are Thus addressed by Kunti, Vyasa, that foremost of all persons, said to her in reply, "Blessed be you, all that you have said to me will happen.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: अपराधश्च ते नास्ति कन्याभावं गता ह्यसि। देवाश्चैश्चर्यवन्तो वै शरीराण्याविशन्ति वै॥
en: You are not a biame at all. You were restored to virginity. The deities are possessed of (Yoga) power. They are able enter human bodies.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: सन्ति देवनिकायाश्च संकल्पाज्जनयन्ति ये। वाचा दृष्ट्या तथा स्पर्शात् संघर्षेणेति पञ्चधा।॥
en: There many deities. They beget (offspring) by thought alone. By word, by sight, by touch, and by sexual union, also, they beget children. These are the five methods.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: मनुष्यधर्मो दैवेन धर्मेण हि न दुष्यति। इति कुन्ति विजानीहि व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: You belong to the order of humanity. You have no fault. Know this, O Kunti! Let the fever of your heart be removed.

description: The history of Karna described by Kunti
sn: सर्वं बलवतां पथ्यं सर्वं बलवतां शुचि। सर्वं बलवतां धर्मः सर्वं बलवतां स्वकम्॥
en: Everything is becoming for those who are mighty. Everything is pure for those that are mighty. Everything is meritorious for those that are mighty. Everything is their own for those who are mighty.

sn: व्यास उवाच भद्रे द्रक्ष्यसि गान्धारि पुत्रान् भ्रातॄन् सखींस्तथा। वधूश्च पतिभिः सार्धं निशि सुप्तोत्थिता इव॥
en: Vyasa said Blessed be you, O Gandhari, you shall see your sons and brothers and friends and kinsmen along with your sires this night like men risen from sleep.

sn: कर्णं द्रक्ष्यति कुन्ती च सौभद्रं चापि यादवी। द्रौपदी पञ्च पुत्रांश्च पितॄन् भ्रातूंस्तथैव च॥
en: Kunti also shall see Karna, and she of Yadu's race shall see her son Abhimanyu. Draupadi shall see her five sons, her fathers and her brothers also.

sn: पूर्वमेवैष हृदये व्यवसायोऽभवन्मम। यदास्मि चोदितो राज्ञा भवत्या पृथयैव च॥
en: Even before you had asked me, this was the thought in my mind. I entertained this purpose when I was urged to that effect by the king, by you, O Gandhari, and by Kunti:

sn: न ते शोच्या महात्मानः सर्व एव नरर्षभाः। क्षत्रधर्मपराः सन्तस्तथा हि निधनं गताः॥
en: You should not grieve for those foremost of men. They met with death on account of their devotion to the practices of Kshatriyas.

sn: भवितव्यमवश्यं तत् सुरकार्यमनिन्दिते। अवतेरुस्ततः सर्वे देवभागा महीतलम्॥
en: O faultless one, the work of the gods could not but be done. It was for accomplishing that object that those heroes came down on earth. They were all portions f the celestials.

sn: गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव पिशाचा गुह्मराक्षसाः। तथा पुण्यजनाश्चैव सिद्धा देवर्षयोऽपि च॥ देवाश्च दानवाश्चैव तथा देवर्षयोऽमलाः। त एते निधनं प्राप्ताः कुरुक्षेत्रे रणाजिरे॥
en: Gandharvas, Apsaras, Pishachas, Guhyakas and Rakshasas, many pure persons, many individuals crowned with (of penances), celestial Rishis, deities ad Danavas, and heavenly Rishis of spotless character, met with death on the battle field of Kurukshetra.

sn: गन्धर्वराजो यो धीमान् धृतराष्ट्र इति श्रुतः। स एव मानुषे लोके धृतराष्ट्र: पतिस्तव॥
en: It is heard that he who was the intelligent kings of the Gandharvas and named Dhritarashtra, took birth in the world of men as your lord Dhritarashtra,

sn: पाण्डुं मरुद्गणाद् विद्धि विशिष्टतममच्युतम्। धर्मस्यांशोऽभवत् क्षत्ता राजा चैव युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: success Know that Pandu of unfading glory and distinguished above all others, originated from the Maruts, Kshatta and Yudhishthira are both portions of the deity of Virtue.

sn: कलिं दुर्योधनं विद्धि शकुनि द्वापरं तथा। दुःशासनादीन् विद्धि त्वं राक्षसाशुभदर्शने॥
en: Know that Duryodhana was Kali, and Shakuni was Dvapara. O you of good features, know that Dushasana and others were all Rakshasas.

sn: मरुद्गणाद् भीमसेनं बलवन्तमरिंदमम्। विद्धि त्वं तु नरमृषिमिमं पार्थं धनञ्जयम्॥
en: Bhimasena of great power that chastiser of enemies, is from the Maruts. Know that this Dhananjaya, the son of Pritha, is the ancient Rishi Nara.

sn: नारायणं हृषीकेशमश्विनौ यमजौ तथा। यः स वैरार्थमुद्भूतः संघर्षजननस्तथा। तं कर्णं विद्धि कल्याणि भास्करं शुभदर्शने॥ यश्च पाण्डवदायादो हतः षड्भिर्महारथैः। स सोम इह सोभद्रो योगादेवाभवद् द्विधा॥ द्विधा कृत्वाऽऽत्मनो देहमादित्यं तपतां वरम्। लोकांश्च तापयानं वै विद्धि कर्णं च शोभने॥
en: Hrishikesha is Narayana, and the wins are the Ashvins. That foremost of heat-giving ones, viz., Surya, having divided his body in two parts continued with one portion to give heat to the worlds and with another to live as Karna. He who was born as the son of Arjuna, that gladdener of all, that heir of the properties of the Pandavas, who was killed by six carwarriors (fighting together) was Soma. He was of born Subhadra. Through Yoga power he had divided himself in two parts.

sn: द्रौपद्या सह सम्भूतं धृष्टद्युम्नं च पावकात्। अग्नेर्भागं शुभं विद्धि राक्षसं तु शिखण्डिनम्॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna who originated with Draupadi from the sacrificial fire, was an auspicious portion of the deity of fire, Shikhandin was a Rakshasa.

sn: द्रोणं बृहस्पतेर्भागं विद्धि द्रौणिं च रुद्रजम्। भीष्मं च विद्धि गाङ्गेयं वसुं मानुषतां गतम्॥
en: Know that Drona was a portion of Brihaspati, and that Drona's son is born of a portion of Rudra. Know that Ganga's son Bhishma was one of the Vasus who became born as a men.

sn: एवमेते महाप्रज्ञे देवा मानुष्यमेत्य हि। ततः पुनर्गताः स्वर्गं कृते कर्मणि शोभने।॥
en: Thus, O you of great wisdom, the deities had taken birth as human beings, and after having accomplished their purposes have returned to the celestial region.

sn: यच्च वै हृदि सर्वेषां दुःखमेतच्चिरं स्थितम्। तदद्य व्यपनेष्यामि परलोककृताद् भयात्॥
en: I shall today, dispel that sorrow which is in the hearts of you all, about the return of these to the other world.

sn: सर्वे भवन्तो गच्छन्तु नदीं भागीरथी प्रति। तत्र द्रक्ष्यथ तान् सर्वान् ये हतास्तत्र संयुगे॥
en: Do you all go towards the Bhagirathi. You will then see all those who have been killed on the field of battle.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इति व्यासस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वो जनस्तदा। महता सिंहनादेन गङ्गामभिमुखो ययौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said. All the persons there present having heard the words of Vyasa, raised a loud leonine shout and then went towards the Bhagirathi.

sn: धृतराष्ट्राश्च सामात्यः प्रययौ सह पाण्डवैः। सहितो मुनिशार्दूलैर्गन्धर्वैश्च समागतैः॥
en: Dhritarashtra with all is ministers and the Pandavas, as also with all those foremost of Rishis and Gandharvas who had come there, started as directed.

sn: ततो गङ्गां समासाद्य क्रमेण स जनार्णवः। निवासमकरोत् सर्वो यथाप्रीति यथासुखम्॥
en: Arrived at the banks of Ganga, that sea of men look up their abode as pleased them.

sn: राजा च पाण्डवैः सार्धमिष्टे देशे सहानुगः। निवासमकरोद् धीमान् सस्त्रीवृद्धपुरःसरः॥
en: The endued with great intelligence, with the Pandavas, took up his abode in desirable spot, along with the ladies and the aged ones of his household.

sn: जगाम तदहश्चापि तेषां वर्षशतं यथा। निशां प्रतीक्षमाणानां दिदृक्षूणां मृतान् नृपान्॥
en: They passed that day as if it were a whole year, waiting for the approach of the might when they would see the deceased princes.

sn: अथ पुण्यं गिरिवरमस्तमभ्यगमद् रविः। ततः कृताभिषेकास्ते नैशं कर्म समाचरन्॥
en: The Sun then reached the sacred mountain in the west and all those persons, having bathed in the sacred river finished their evening rites.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो निशायां प्राप्तायां कृतसायाह्निकक्रियाः। व्यासमभ्यगमन् सर्वे ये तत्रासन् समागताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said When night came, all those persons, having finished their evening rites, approached Vyasa.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्तु धर्मात्मा पाण्डवैः सहितस्तदा। शुचिरेकमना सार्धमृषिभिस्तैरुपाविशत्॥
en: Dhritarashtra, with purified body and with mind solely directed towards it, sat there with the Pandavas and the Rishis in his company.

sn: गान्धार्या सह नार्यस्तु सहिताः समुपाविशन्। पौरजानपदश्चापि जनः सर्वो यथावयः॥
en: The royal ladies sat with Gandhari in a secluded spot. All the citizens and the inhabitants of the provinces ranged themselves according to their years.

sn: ततो व्यास महातेजः पुण्यं भागीरथीजलम्। अवगाह्याजुहावाथ सर्वान् लोकान् महामुनिः॥ पाण्डवानां च ये योधाः कौरवाणां च सर्वशः। राजानश्च महाभागा नानादेशनिवासिनः॥
en: Then the great ascetic, Vyasa, of great energy, bathing in the sacred waters of the Bhagirathi, summoned all the deceased warriors, viz., those who had fought on the side of the Pandavas, those who had fought for the Kauravas, including highly blessed kings belonging to the various kingdoms.

sn: ततः सुतुमुल: शब्दो जलान्ते जनमेजय। प्रादुरासीद् यथापूर्वे कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः॥
en: At this, Janamejaya, a deafening uproar was heard to arise from within the waters, resembling that which had formerly been heard of the armies of the Kurus and the Pandavas.

sn: ततस्ते पार्थिवाः सर्वे भीष्मद्रोणपुरोगमाः। ससैन्याः सलिलात् तस्मात् समुत्तस्थुः सहस्रशः॥
en: Then those kings, headed by Bhishma and Drona, with all their armies, arose by thousands from the waters of the Bhagirathi.

sn: विराटद्रुपदौ चैव सहपुत्रौ ससैनिकौ। द्रौपदेयाश्च सौभद्रो राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः॥
en: There were Virata and Drupada, with their sons and forces. There were the sons of Draupadi and the son of Subhadra, and Rakshasa Ghatotkacha.

sn: कर्णदुर्योधनौ चैव शकुनिश्च महारथः। दुःशासनादयश्चैव धार्तराष्ट्रा महाबलाः॥
en: There were Karna, Duryodhana, and the powerful car-warrior Shakuni, and the other children, possessed of great strength, of Dhritarashtra, headed by Dushasana.

sn: जारासंधिभगदत्तो जलसंधश्च वीर्यवान्। भूरिश्रवाः शलः शल्यो वृषसेनश्च सानुजः॥
en: There the of Jarasandha, Bhagadatta, Jarasandha Jarasandha of great energy, Bhurishravas, Shala, Shalya and Vrishasena with his younger brother.

sn: लक्ष्मणो राजपुत्रश्च धृष्टद्युम्नस्य चात्मजाः। शिखण्डिपुत्राः सर्वे च धृष्टकेतुश्च सानुजः॥
en: There were prince Lakshamana, and the son of Dhristadyumna, and all the children of Sikhandin, and Dhrishtaketu with his younger brother. were son

sn: अचलो वृषकश्चैव राक्षसश्चाष्यलायुधः। बाह्निकः सोमदत्तश्च चेकितानश्च पार्थिवः॥
en: There were Achala, Vrishaka, the Rakshasa Alyudha, Valhika, Somadatta, and the king Chekitana.

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो बहुत्वाद् ये न कीर्तिताः। सर्वे भासुरदेहास्ते समुत्तस्थुर्जलात्ततः॥
en: These and innumerable others appeared on that occasion. All of the rose from the waters of the Bhagirathi with shining bodies.

sn: यस्य वीरस्य यो वेषो यो ध्वजो यच्च वाहनम्। तेन तेन व्यदृश्यन्त समुपेता नराधिपाः॥
en: Those kings appeared, each clad in that dress and equipped with that standard and that vehicle which he had while fighting on the field.

sn: दिव्याम्बरधराः सर्वे सर्वे भ्राजिष्णुकुण्डलाः। निर्वैरा निरहङ्कारा विगतक्रोधमत्सराः॥
en: All of them were dressed in celestial vestments and all had brilliant earning. They were free from all animosity and pride and divested of anger and jealousy.

sn: गन्धर्वैरुपगीयन्तः स्तूयमानाच वन्दिभिः। दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरा वृताश्चाप्सरसां गणैः॥
en: Gandharvas sang their praises, and bards waited on them, chanting then deeds, Robed with celestial raiment's and wearing celestial garlands, each of them was waited upon by bands of Apsaras.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्य च तदा दिव्यं चक्षुर्नराधिप। मुनिः सत्यवतीपुत्रः प्रीतः प्रादात् तपोबलात्॥
en: At that time, through the power of his penances, the great ascetic, the of Satyavati, gratified with Dhritarasthra, gave him celestial vision.

sn: दिव्यज्ञानबलोपेता गान्धारी च यशस्विनी। ददर्श पुत्रांस्तान् सर्वान् ये चान्येऽपि मृधे हताः॥
en: Gifted with celestial knowledge and strength, the illustrious Gandhari beheld all her children as also all those who had been killed in battle. son

sn: तदद्युतमचिन्त्यं च सुमहल्लोमहर्षणम्। विस्मितः स जन: सर्वो ददर्शानिमिषेक्षणः॥
en: All persons assembled there saw with steadfast gaze and hearts filled with wonder that amazing and inconceivable scene which made the hairs stand erect.

sn: तदुत्सवमहोदग्रं हृष्टनारीनराकुलम्। आश्चर्यभूतं ददृशे चित्रं पटगतं यथा।॥
en: It looked like a high carnival of pleased men and women. That wondrous scene looked like a picture painted on the canvass.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्तु तान् सर्वान् पश्यन् दिव्येन् चक्षुषा। मुमुदे भरतश्रेष्ठ प्रसादात् तस्य वै मुनेः॥
en: Dhritarashtra seeing all those heroes with their celestial vision obtained through the favour of that sage, became full of joy, O chief of Bharata's race.

sn: तदद्युतमचिन्त्यं च सुमहल्लोमहर्षणम्। विस्मितः स जन: सर्वो ददर्शानिमिषेक्षणः॥
en: All persons assembled there saw with steadfast gaze and hearts filled with wonder that amazing and inconceivable scene which made the hairs stand erect.

sn: तदुत्सवमहोदग्रं हृष्टनारीनराकुलम्। आश्चर्यभूतं ददृशे चित्रं पटगतं यथा।॥
en: It looked like a high carnival of pleased men and women. That wondrous scene looked like a picture painted on the canvass.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्तु तान् सर्वान् पश्यन् दिव्येन् चक्षुषा। मुमुदे भरतश्रेष्ठ प्रसादात् तस्य वै मुनेः॥
en: Dhritarashtra seeing all those heroes with their celestial vision obtained through the favour of that sage, became full of joy, O chief of Bharata's race.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते पुरुषश्रेष्ठाः समाजग्मुः परस्परम्। विगतक्रोधमात्सर्याः सर्वे विगतकल्मषाः॥ विधि परममास्थाय ब्रह्मर्षिविहितं शुभम्। संहृष्टमनसः सर्वे देवलोके इवामराः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then those foremost of men, shorn of anger and jealousy and purged of every sin, met with another, according to those high and auspicious ordinances which have been laid down by regenerate Rishis. All of them were happy of hearts and looked like celestials moving in celestial regions.

sn: पुत्रः पित्रा च मात्रा च भार्याश्च पतिभिः सह। भ्रात्रा भ्राता सखा चैव सख्या राजन् समागताः॥
en: Son met with father or mother, wives with husbands, brother with brother, and friend with friend, O king.

sn: पाण्डवास्तु महेष्वासं कर्णं सौभद्रमेव च। सम्प्रहर्षात् समाजग्मुर्दोपदेयांश्च सर्वशः॥
en: The Pandavas full of joy, inet with the powerful bowman Karna as also with the son of Subhadra, and the children of Draupadi.

sn: ततस्ते प्रीयमाणा वै कर्णेन सह पाण्डवाः। समेत्य पृथिवीपाल सौहृद्ये च स्थिता भवन॥
en: With pleased hearts the son of Pandu approached Karna, O king, and became reconciled with him.

sn: परस्परं समागम्य योधास्ते भरतर्षभ। मुनेः प्रसादात् ते ह्येवं क्षत्रिया नष्टमन्यवः॥
en: All those warriors, O chief of Bharata's race, meeting with one another through the favour of the great ascetic, became reconciled with one another.

sn: असौहृदं परित्यज्य सौहदे पर्यवस्थिताः एवं समागताः सर्वे गुरुभिर्बान्धवैः सह॥ पुत्रैश्च पुरुषव्याघ्राः कुरवोऽन्ये च पार्थिवाः। तां रात्रिमखिलामेवं विहत्य प्रीतमानसाः॥
en: Renouncing all unfriendliness, they became established on amity and peace. It was thus that all those foremost of men, viz., the Kauravas and other kinsmen of theirs as also with their children. They passed in great happiness the whole of that night.

sn: मेनिरे परितोषेण नृपाः स्वर्गसदो यथा। नात्र शोको भयं त्रासो नारति यशोऽभवत्।।९। परस्परं समागम्य योधानां भरतर्षभ। समागतास्ताः पितृभिर्भ्रातृभिः पतिभिः सुतैः॥ मुदं परमिकां प्राप्य नार्यो दुःखमथात्यजन्। एकां रात्रि विहृत्यैव ते वीरास्ताश्च योषितः॥ आमन्त्र्यान्योन्यमाश्लिष्य ततो जग्मुर्यथागतम्। ततो विसर्जयामास लोकांस्तान् मुनिपुङ्गवः॥
en: Indeed, the Kshatriya warriors, on account of the happiness they experienced, considered that place as Heaven itself. There was no grief, no fear, ne suspicion, no discontent, no reproach in that region, as those warriors, O king, met with one another on that night, Meeting with their sires and brothers and husbands and sars. the Indias ........ grief and felt great joy. Having sported with one another thus for one night, those heroes and those ladies, embracing one another taking one another's leave, came back to the places they had come from. Indeed, that foremost of ascetics dismissed that collection of warriors.

sn: क्षणेनान्तर्हिताश्चैव प्रेक्षतामेव तेऽभवन्। अवगाह्य महात्मानः पुण्यां भागीरथी नदीम्॥ सरथाः सध्वजाश्चैव स्वानि वेश्मानि भेजिरे। देवलोकं ययुः केचित् केचिद् ब्रह्मसदस्तथा॥ केचिच्च वारुणं लोकं केचित् कौबेरमाप्नुवन्। ततो वैवस्वतं लोकं केचिच्चैवाप्नुवन्नृपाः॥
en: Within the twinkling of an eye that large crowd disappeared in the very sight of all those persons. Those great persons, plunging into the sacred river Bhagirathi, proceeded, with their cars and standards, to their respective abodes. Some went to the regions of the gods, some to the region of Brahman, some to the region of Varuna, and some to the region of Kubera. Some among those kings went to the region of Surya.

sn: राक्षसानां पिशाचानां केचिच्चाप्युत्तरान् कुरून्। विचित्रगतयः सर्वे यानवाप्यामरैः सह॥
en: Amongst the Rakshasas and Pishachas, some proceeded to the country of the UttaraKurus. Others, moving delightfully, went in the company of the celestials.

sn: आजग्मुस्ते महात्मानः सवाहाः सपदानुगाः। गतेषु तेषु सर्वेषु सलिलस्थो महामुनिः॥ धर्मशीलो महातेजाः कुरूणां हितकृत् तथा। ततः प्रोवाच ताः सर्वाः क्षत्रिया निहतेश्वराः॥ या याः पतिकृतान् लोका निच्छन्ति परमस्त्रियः। ता जाह्नवीजलं क्षिप्रं मवगाहन्त्वतन्द्रिताः॥ ततस्तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा श्रदधाना वराङ्गनाः। श्वशुरं समनुज्ञाप्य विविशुर्जाह्नवीजलम्॥
en: Thus did all those great persons disappear with their vehicles and animals and with all their followers. After all of them had departed, the great sage, who was standing in the waters of the sacred rivers, viz., Vyasa of great virtue and energy, that benefactor of the Kurus, then addressed those Kshatriya ladies who had become windows, and said these words, 'Let those amongst these foremost of women who are desirous of attaining to the regions acquired by their husbands cast away all idleness and quickly plunge into the sacred Bhagirathi. Hearing these words of his, those foremost ladies, placing faith in them, took the permission of their father-in-law and then plunged into the waters of the Bhagirathi.

sn: विमुक्ता मानुषैर्देहैस्ततस्ता भर्तृभिः सह। समाजग्मुस्तदा साध्व्यः सर्वा एव विशाम्पते॥
en: Freed from human bodies, those chaste ladies then went, O king, with their husbands to the regions acquired by the latter.

sn: एवं क्रमेण सर्वास्ताः शीलवत्यः पतिव्रताः। प्रविश्य क्षत्रिया मुक्ता जग्मुर्भर्तृसलोकताम्॥
en: Thus, those ladies of various conduct, devoted to their husbands, entering the waters of the Bhagirathi, became freed from their mortal bodies and attained to the companionship of their husbands in the regions acquired by them.

sn: दिव्यरूपसमायुक्ता दिव्याभरणभूषिताः। दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरा यथाऽऽसां पतयस्तथा॥
en: Possessed of celestiai forms, and adorned with celestial ornaments, and wearing celestial garments and garlands hey proceeded to those regions where their husbands were living.

sn: ताः शीलगुणसम्पन्ना विमानस्था गतक्लमाः। सर्वाः सर्वगुणोपेताः स्वस्थानं प्रतिपेदिरे॥
en: Endued with excellent conduct and many virtues, their anxieties all removed, they were seen to ride on excellent cars, and gifted with every accomplishment, they found those regions of felicity which were theirs by right.

sn: यस्य यस्य तु यः कामस्तस्मिन् काले बभूव ह। तं तं विसृष्टवान् व्यासो वरदो धर्मवत्सलः॥
en: Devoted to the duties of piety, Vyasa, at that time, becoming a giver of boons, granted to all the men there collected the fruition of the desires they respectively cherished.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा नरदेवानां पुनरागमनं नराः। जहषुर्मुदिताश्चासन् नानादेशगता अपि॥
en: People of various kingdoms hearing of this meeting between the hallowed dead and living human beings, became highly pleased.

sn: प्रियैः समागमं तेषां यः सम्यक् शृणुयान्नरः। प्रियाणि लभते नित्यमिह च प्रेत्य चैव सः॥
en: That man who duly listens to this discourse meets with everything that is dear to him. Indeed, he obtains all agreeable objects both in this world and in the next.

sn: इष्टबान्धवसंयोगमनायासमनामयम्। यश्चैतच्छावयेद् विद्वान् विदुषो धर्मवित्तमः॥ स यशः प्राप्नुयाल्लोके परत्र च शुभां गतिम्। स्वाध्याययुक्ता मनुजास्तपोयुक्ताश्च भारत॥
en: That man of learning and science that foremost of pious persons, who recites this narrative for the hearing of others wins great fame here and an auspicious end hereafter, as also a union with kinsmen and all desirable objects. Such a man has not to work hard for his maintenance and meets with all sorts of auspicious objects in life. These are the rewards reaped by a person who gifted with devotion to Vedic studies and with penances, recites this narrative in the hearing of others.

sn: साध्वाचारा दमोपेता दाननिषूतकल्मषाः। ऋजवः शुचयः शान्ता हिंसानृतविवर्जिताः॥ आस्तिकाः श्रद्दधानाश्च धृतिमन्तश्च मानवाः। श्रुत्वाऽऽश्चर्यमिदं पर्व हवाप्स्यन्ति परां गतिम्॥
en: Those persons who endued with good conduct, devoted to self-control, purged of all sins by the gifts they make, endued with sincerity, having tranquil souls, freed from falsehood and the desire of injuring others, adorned with faith, belief in the scriptures, and intelligence, listen to this wonderful book, surely attain to the highest end hereafter.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: सौतिरुवाच एतच्छुत्वा नृपो विद्वान् हृष्टोऽभूज्जनमेजयः। पितामहानां सर्वेषां गमनागमनं तदा॥
en: Santi said Hearing this story of the reappearance and departure of his forefathers, the highly intelligent king Janamejaya became greatly pleased.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: अब्रवीच्च मुदा युक्तः पुनरागमनं प्रति। कथं नु त्यक्तदेहानां पुनस्तद्रूपदर्शनम्॥
en: Filled with joy, he once more asked Vaishampayana the subject of the reappearance of dead men, saying of the reappearance of dead men, saying-How is it possible for persons whose bodies have been destroyed to reappear in those very forms?

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: इत्युक्तः स द्विजश्रेष्ठो व्यासशिष्यः प्रतापवान्। प्रोवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठस्तं नृपं जनमेजयम्॥
en: Thus asked, that foremost of twice-born persons, viz., the disciple of Vyasa, that first of speakers, possessed of great energy, thus answered Janamejaya.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अविप्रणाशः सर्वेषां कर्मणामिति निश्चयः। कर्मजानि शरीराणि तथैवाकृतयो नृप॥
en: This is certain, viz., that acts are never destroyed. Bodies, o king, are born of acts; so also are features.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: महाभूतानि नित्यानि भूताधिपतिसंश्रयात्। तेषां च नित्यसंवासो न विनाशो वियुज्यताम्॥
en: The great primal elements are eternal on account of the union with them of the Lord of all beings. They exist with what is eternal. Accordingly, they have no destruction when the non-eternal are destroyed.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: अनायासकृतं कर्म सत्यः श्रेष्ठः फलागमः। आत्मा चैभिः समायुक्तः सुखदुःखमुपाश्नुते॥
en: Acts done without exertion are true, and foremost, and yield real fruit. The soul, united, however, with such acts as require exertion for their performance, enjoys pleasure and pain.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: अविनाश्यस्तथायुक्तः श्रेत्रज्ञ इति निश्चयः। भूतानामात्मको भावो यथासौ न वियुज्यते॥
en: Though united so, yet it is a certain internee that the soul is never modified by them, like the reflection of creatures in a mirror. It is never destroyed.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: यावन्न क्षीयते कर्म तावत् तस्य स्वरूपता। क्षीणकर्मा नरो लोके रूपान्यत्वं नियच्छति॥
en: As long as one's deeds are not exhausted (by enjoyment or endurance of their fruits good and bad), so long does he consider the body to be his ownself. The man, however, whose acts have been exhausted, without considering body to be self, takes the self to be something otherwise.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: नानाभावास्तथैकत्वं शरीरं प्राप्य संहताः। भवन्ति ते तथा नित्याः पृथग्भावं विजानताम्॥
en: Various existent objects, attaining to a body, become united as one. Those very objects become eternal to men of knowledge who understand the difference.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
