sn: अश्वमेधे श्रुतिश्चयमश्वसंज्ञपनं प्रति। लोकान्तरगता नित्यं प्राणा नित्यं शरीरिणाम्॥
en: In the Horse-Sacrifice, this Shruti is heard in the matter of the killing of the horse. The certain possessions of embodied creatures, viz., their vital airs (and the senses, etc.) exist eternally even when they are borne to the other world.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: अहं हितं वदाम्येतत् प्रियं चेत् तव पार्थिव। देवयाना हि पन्थानः श्रुतास्ते यज्ञसंस्तरे॥
en: I shall, you what is beneficial, if it be agreeable to you, O king. You have while employed in our sacrifices, heard of the celestial paths.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: आहृतो यत्र यज्ञस्ते तत्र देवा हितास्तव। यदा समन्विता देवाः पशूनां गमनेश्वराः॥
en: When preparations were made for any sacrifice of yours, the celestials became beneficially inclined to you. When, indeed, the celestials were thus disposed and came to your sacrifice, they were lords in the matter of the passage.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: गतिमन्तश्च तेनेष्टा नान्ये नित्या भवन्त्युत। नित्येऽस्मिन् पञ्चके वर्गे नित्ये चात्मनि पूरुषः॥
en: Therefore, the eternal ones (viz., Jivas), by adoring the deities in sacrifices, succeed in attaining to excellent ends. When the five primal elements are eternal, when he soul also is eternal, he called Purusha is equally so.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: अस्य नानासमायोगं यः पश्यति वृथामतिः। वियोगे शोचतेऽत्यर्थं स बाल इति मे मतिः॥
en: When such is the case he who sees a creature as disposed to take various forms, is considered as having an erroneous understanding. He who indulges in too much grief at separation, is, I think, a foolish person.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: वियोगे दोषदर्शी यः संयोगं स विसर्जयेत्। असङ्गे सङ्गमो नास्ति दुःखं भुवि वियोगजम्॥
en: He who sees evil in separation should give up union. By standing aloof, no unions are formed, and sorrow is renounced, for sorrow in the worlds is born of separation.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: परापरज्ञस्त्वपरो नाभिमानादुदीरितः। अपरज्ञः परां बुद्धिं ज्ञात्वा मोहाद् विमुच्यते॥
en: Only he who understands the distinction between body and self, and not another becomes freed from the erroneous belief. He who knows the other viz., self attains to the highest understanding and becomes freed from error.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: अदर्शनादापतितः पुनश्चादर्शनं गतः। नाहं तं वेद्मि नासौ मां न च मेऽस्ति विरागता॥
en: As regards creatures, they appear from an invisible state, and once more disappears into invisibleness. I do not know him. He also does not know me. As regards myself renunciation is not yet mine.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: येन येन शरीरेण करोत्ययमनीश्वरः।
en: He, who is not possessed of power, enjoys or endures the fruits of all his deeds in those bodies in which he does them.

description: How persons whose bodies have been destroyed re-appear
sn: तेन तेन शरीरेण तदवश्यमुपाश्नुते। मानसं मनसाऽऽप्नोति शरीरं च शरीरवान्॥
en: If the act be a mental one, its fruits are enjoyed or endured mentally; if it be done with the body, its results are to be enjoyed or endured in the body.

sn: अदृष्ट्वा तु नृपः पुत्रान् दर्शनं प्रतिलब्धवान्। ऋषेः प्रसादात् पुत्राणां स्वरूपाणां कुरूद्वह॥
en: King Dhritarashtra had never seen his own sons. Getting eye-sight through the favour of the Rishi, he saw for the first time, O perpetuator of Kuru's race, those children of his who were very like his own self.

sn: स राजा राजधर्माश्च ब्रह्मोपनिषदं तथा। अवाप्तवान्नरश्रेष्ठो बुद्धिनिश्चयमेव च॥
en: That foremost of men, viz., the Kuru king had learnt all the royal duties as also the Vedas and the Upanishads, and had acquired certitude of understanding.

sn: विदुरश्च महाप्राज्ञो ययौ सिद्धिं तपोबलात्। धृतराष्ट्रः समासाद्य व्यासं चैव तपस्विनम्॥
en: ighly wise Vidura acquired great success through the power of his penances. Dhritarashtra also acquired great success for having inet the ascetic Vyasa.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच ममापि वरदो व्यासो दर्शयेत् पितरं यदि। तद्रूपवेषवयसं श्रद्दध्यां सर्वमेव ते॥
en: Janamejaya said If Vyasa, disposed to grant me a boon, kindly show me my father in that form which he had clad as he used to be clad, and as old as he was when he left this world, I may then believe all that you have told me.

sn: प्रियं मे स्यात् कृतार्थश्च स्यामहं कृतनिश्चयः। प्रसादादृषिमुख्यस्य मम कामः समृध्यताम्॥
en: Such a sight will be most agreeable to me. Indeed, I shall consider myself crowned with success. I shall have gained a certainty of conclusion. O let my wish be satisfied through the favour of that foremost of Rishis!

sn: सौतिरुवाच इत्युक्तवचने तस्मिन् नृपे व्यासः प्रतापवान्। प्रसादमकरोद् धीमानानयच्च परीक्षितम्॥
en: Sauti said After king Janamejaya had said these words, the highly energetic and intelligent Vyasa, showed his favour and brought Parikshit.

sn: ततस्तद्रूपवयसमागतं नृपतिं दिवः। श्रीमन्तं पितरं राजा ददर्श जनमेजयः॥
en: King Janamejaya saw his royal father possessed of great beauty, brought down from the celestial region, in the same form that he had and of the same age as he was (at the time of leaving this world).

sn: शमीकं च महात्मानं पुत्रं तं चास्य शृङ्गिणम्। अमात्या ये बभूवश्च राजस्तानं ददर्श ह॥
en: The great Shamika also, and his son Shringin, were similarly brought there. All the counselors and ministers of the king saw them.

sn: ततः सोऽवभृथे राजा मुदितो जनमेजयः। पितरं स्नापयामास स्वयं सस्नौ च पार्थिवः॥
en: King Janamejaya performing the final both in his sacrifice, became highly pleased. He poured the sacred water on his father even as he caused it to be poured on himself.

sn: स्नात्वा स नृपतिर्विप्रमास्तीकमिदमब्रवीत्। यायावरकुलोत्पन्नं जरत्कारुसुतं तदा॥ आस्तीक विविधाश्चर्यो यज्ञोऽयमिति मे मतिः। यदद्यायं पिता प्राप्तो मम शोकप्रणाशनः॥
en: Having performed the final bath, the king addressed the twice-born Astika who had originated from the race of the Yayavaras and who was the son of Jaratkaru, and said these words — 'O Astika, this sacrifice of mine is fraught with many wonderful incidents, since this my sire has been seen by me, he who has removed all my sorrow.

sn: आस्तीक उवाच ऋषिद्वैपायनो यत्र पुराणस्तपो निधिः। यज्ञे कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ तस्य लोकावुभौ जितौ॥
en: Astika said The performer of that sacrifice in which the ancient Rishi, Dvaipayana Vyasa, that vast receptacle of penances is present, is sure O foremost one of Kuru's race, to conquer both the worlds.

sn: श्रुतं विचित्रमाख्यानं त्वया पाण्डवनन्दन। सर्पाश्च भस्मसान्नीता गताश्च पदवीं पितुः॥
en: O son of the Pandavas, you have heard a wonderful history. The snakes have been reduced into ashes and have followed the footsteps of your father.

sn: कथंचित् तक्षको मुक्तः सत्यत्वात् तव पार्थिव। ऋषयः पूजिताः सर्वे गतिर्दृष्टा महात्मनः॥
en: Through your truthfulness, o king, Takshaka has with difficulty escaped a painful fate. The Rishis have been all adored. You have seen also he end that has been acquired by your great father.

sn: प्राप्तः सुविपुलो धर्मः पापविनाशनम्। विमुक्तो हृदयग्रन्थिरुदारजनदर्शनात्॥
en: Having heard this sin-cleansing history you have acquired abundant merit. The knots of your heart have been united through seeing this foremost of persons.

sn: ये च पक्षधरा धर्मे सद्वृत्तरुचयश्च ये। यान् दृष्ट्वाहीयते पापं तेभ्यः कार्यानमस्क्रिया॥
en: They who are the supporters of the wings of Virtue, they who are of good conduct and excellent disposition, they on seeing whom sins disappear, we should all bow to them.

sn: सौति उवाच एतच्छुत्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठात् स राजा जनमेजयः। पूजयामास तमृषिमनुमान्य पुनः पुनः॥
en: Sauti said--Having heard this from that foremost of twice-born ones, king Janamejaya adored that Rishi, repeatedly honouring him in every way.

sn: पप्रच्छ तमृर्षि चापि वैशम्पायनमच्युतम्। कथावशेषं धर्मज्ञो वनवासस्य सत्तम॥
en: Knowing all duties, he then asked the Rishi Vaishampayana of undecaying glory about the sequel, O best of ascetics, of king Dhritarashtra's residence in the forest.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच दृष्ट्वा पुत्रांस्तथा पौत्रान् सानुबन्धान् जनाधिपः। धृतराष्ट्रः किमकरोद् राजा चैव युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Having seen his sons and grandsons with all their friends and followers, what, indeed, did that king, viz., Dhritarashtra, and king Yudhishthira also, do?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तद् दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्ये पुत्राणां दर्शनं नृप। वीतशोकः स राजर्षिः पुनराश्रममागमत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Seeing that highly wonderful spectacle, : viz., the re-appearance of his children, the royal sage, Dhritarashtra renounced his grief and returned to his hermitage.

sn: इतरस्तु जनः सर्वस्ते चैव परमर्षयः। प्रतिजग्मुर्यथाकामं धृतराष्ट्राभ्यनुज्ञया॥
en: The common people and all the great Rishis, sent away by Dhritarashtra, came back to the places they respectively wished.

sn: पाण्डवास्तु महात्मानो लघुभूयिष्ठसैनिकाः। पुनर्जग्मुर्महात्मानं सदारास्तं महीपतिम्॥
en: The great Pandavas accompanied by their wives, and with a small retinue, went to the hermitage of the great monarch.

sn: तत्राश्रमपदं धीमान् ब्रह्मर्षिर्लोकपूजितः। मुनिः सत्यवतीपुत्रो धृतराष्ट्रमभाषत॥ धृतराष्ट्र महाबाहो शृणु कौरवनन्दन। श्रुतं ते ज्ञानवृद्धानामृषीणां पुण्यकर्मणाम्॥ श्रद्धाभिजनवृद्धानां वेदवेदाङ्गवेदिनाम्। धर्मज्ञानां पुराणानां वदतां विविधाः कथाः॥
en: Then Satyavati's son, who was honoured by twice-born Rishis and all other person, arrived at the hermitage addressed Dhritarashtra, saying, 'O mighty-armed Dhritarashtra, O son of Kuru's race, listen to what I say! You have heard various discourses from Rishis of great knowledge and sacred deeds, having penances for wealth and excellence of blood, knowledge of the Vedas and their branches, of piety and years, and of great eloquence.

sn: मा स्म शोके मनः कार्षीर्दिष्टेन व्यथते बुधः। श्रुतं देवरहस्यं ते नारदाद् देवदर्शनात्॥
en: Do not set your mind again on sorrow. He who is wise is never moved at ill luck. You have also heard the mysteries of the deities from Narada of celestial form.

sn: गतास्ते क्षत्रधर्मेण शस्त्रपूतां गर्ति शुभाम्। यथा दृष्टास्त्वया पुत्रास्तथा कामविहारिणः॥
en: Your children have all attained, through performance of Kshatriya practices, to that auspicious end which is sanctified by weapons. You have seen how they moved about at will in great happiness.

sn: युधिष्ठिरः स्वयं धीमान् भवन्तमनुरुध्यते। सहितो भ्रातृभिः सर्वैः सदारः ससुहृज्जनः॥
en: This Yudhishthira of great intelligence is awaiting your permission with all his brothers and wives and kinsmen.

sn: विसर्जयैनं यात्वेष स्वराज्यमनुशासताम्। मास: समधिकस्तेषामतीतो वसतां वने॥
en: Do you send him away. Let him return to his kingdom and rule it! They have passed more then a month in thus living in the forest.

sn: एतद्धि नित्यं यत्नेन पदं रक्ष्यं नराधिप। बहुप्रत्यर्थिकं ह्येतद् राज्यं नाम कुरुद्वह॥
en: The station of sovereignty should always be well-guarded, o king! O you of Kuru's race, kingdom has many enemies.'

sn: इत्युक्तः कौरवो राजा व्यासेनातुलतेजसा। युधिष्ठिरमथाहूय वाग्मी वचनमब्रवीत्॥ अजातशत्रो भद्रं ते शृणु मे भ्रातृभिः सह। त्वत्प्रसादान्महीपाल शोको नास्मान् प्रबाधते॥
en: Thus addressed by Vyasa of incomparable energy, the Kuru king, well versed in words summoned Yudhishthira and said to him, 'O you having no enemies, blessing on you! Do you listen to me, with all your brothers! Through your grace, O king, grief no longer stands in my way.

sn: रमे चाहं त्वया पुत्र पुरेव गजसाह्वये। नाथेनानुगतो विद्वन् प्रियेषु परिवर्तिना॥
en: I am living as happily, O son, with you here as if I were in the city of Hastinapur. With you as my protector, O learned one, I am enjoying all agreeable objects.

sn: प्राप्तं पुत्रफलं त्वत्तः प्रीतिर्मे परमा त्वयि। न मे मन्युर्महाबाहो गम्यतां पुत्र मा चिरम्॥
en: I have obtained from you all those services which a son renders to his sire. I am highly pleased with you. I have not the least dissatisfaction with you. O mighty-armed one. Go now, O son, without waiting here any longer.

sn: भवन्तं चेह सम्प्रेक्ष्य तपो मे परिहीयते। तपोयुक्तं शरीरं च त्वां दृष्ट्वा धारितं पुनः॥
en: Meeting with you, my penances are being slackened. This my body, gifted with penances. I have been able to sustain only on account of my meeting with you.

sn: मातरौ ते तथैवेमे शीर्णपर्णकृताशने। मम तुल्यव्रते पुत्र न चिरं वर्तयिष्यतः॥
en: These two mothers of yours, living now upon fallen leaves of trees, and observing vows similar to mine, will not live long.

sn: दुर्योधनप्रभृतयो दृष्टा लोकान्तरं गताः। व्यासस्य तपसो वीर्याद् भवतश्च समागमात्॥
en: We have seen Duryodhana and others who have become dwellers of the other world, through the power of Vyasa's penances and through the merit of this my meeting with you.

sn: प्रयोजनं च निर्वृत्तं जीवितस्य ममानघ। उग्रं तपः समास्थास्ये त्वमनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: O sinless one, I have gained the object of my life. I now wish to practice the austerest of penances. You should grant me permission.

sn: त्वय्यद्य पिण्डः कीर्तिश्च कुलं चेदं प्रतिष्ठितम्। श्वो वाद्य वा महाबाहो गम्यतां पुत्र मा चिरम्॥
en: The obsequial cake, the fame and achievements, and the family of our ancestors, now depend upon you entirely. O mightyarmed one, do you then go either to-morrow or this very day. Do not tarry. O son.

sn: राजनीति: सुबहुशः श्रुता : सुबहुशः श्रुता ते भरतर्षभ। संदेष्टव्यं ने पश्यामि कृतं मे भवता विभो॥
en: O chief of Bharata's race, you have repeatedly heard what the duties are of kings. I do not see what more I can say to you. I have no longer any necessity with you, O you of great power.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तवचनं तं तु नृपो राजानमब्रवीत्। न मामर्हसि धर्मज्ञ परित्यक्तुमनागसम्॥
en: Vaishampayana continued : King Yudhishthira replied to the (old) king who said so, saying, 'O you who know every rules of virtue, you should not cast me off in this way. I am guilty of not fault.

sn: कामं गच्छन्तु मे सर्वे भ्रातरोऽनुचरास्तथा। भवन्तमहमन्विष्ये मातरौ च यतव्रतः॥
en: Let all my brothers and followers go as they like. With steadfast vows I shall wait upon you and upon these two mothers of mine.'

sn: तमुवाचाथ गान्धारी मैवं पुत्र शृणुष्व च। त्वय्यधीनं कुरुकुलं पिण्डश्च श्वशुरस्य मे॥
en: Gandhari then said to him. 'O son, let it not be so. Listen, the family of Kuru is now dependent on you. The obsequial cake also of my father-in-law depends on you Depart then, O son.

sn: गम्यतां पुत्र पर्याप्तमेतावत् पूजिता वयम्। राजा यदाह तत् कार्यं त्वया पुत्र पितुर्वचः॥
en: We have been sufficiently honoured and served by you. You should do what the king says. Indeed, O son, you should obey the command of your sire.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः स तु गान्धार्या कुन्तीमिदमभाषत। स्नेहबाष्पाकुले नेत्रे प्रमृज्य रुदतीं वचः॥
en: Vaishampayana continued : Thus addressed by Gandhari, king Yudhishthira, rubbing his eyes which were bathed in tears of affection, said these words bewailingly.

sn: विसर्जयति मां राजा गान्धारी च यशस्विनी। भवत्यां बद्धचित्तस्तु कथं यास्यामि दुःखितः॥
en: The king is renouncing me, a also the illustrious Gandhari. My heart, however, is bound to you. How shall I, stricken as I am with sorrow, leave you.

sn: न चोत्सहे तपोविघ्नं कर्तुं ते धर्मचारिणि। तपसो हि परं नास्ति तपसा विन्दते महत्॥
en: I do not, however, at the same time, venture to obstruct your penances, O rights our lady! There is nothing higher than penances. It is by penances that one act quires the Supreme.

sn: ममापि न तथा राज्ञि राज्ये बुद्धिर्यथा पुरा। तपस्येवानुरक्तं मे मनः सर्वात्मना तथा।॥
en: O queen, my heart not longer as of old towards kingdom. My mind is wholly set upon penances now.

sn: शून्येयं च मही कृत्स्ना न मे प्रीतिकरी शुभे। बान्धवा नः परिक्षीणा बलं नो न यथा पुरा।॥
en: The entire Earth is empty now. O auspicious lady, she does not please me any longer! Our kinsmen have been reduced in number. Our strength is no longer what it was before.

sn: पञ्चालाः सुभृशं क्षीणां: कथामात्रावशेषिताः। न तेषां कुलकर्तारं कंचित् पश्याम्यहं शुभे॥
en: The Panchalas have been wholly rooted out. Only nominally they exist. O auspicious lady, I do not see any one who may assist at their reestablishment and growth.

sn: सर्वे हि भस्मसान्नीतास्ते द्रोणेन रणाजिरे. अवशिष्टाश्च निहता द्रोणपुत्रेण वै निशि॥
en: All of them have been reduced to ashes by Drona on the field of battle. The remnant were killed by Drona's son at night.

sn: चेदयश्चैव मत्स्याश्च दृष्टपूर्वास्तथैव नः। केवलं वृष्णिचक्रं च वासुदेवपरिग्रहात्॥
en: The Chedis and the Matsyas, who were our friends, no longer exist. Only the tribes of the Vrishnis are all that remain, Vasudeva having kept them up.

sn: यद् दृष्ट्वा स्थातुमिच्छामि धर्मार्थं नार्थहेतुतः। शिवेन पश्य न: सर्वान् दुर्लभं तव दर्शनम्॥
en: Seeing only the Vrishnis I wish to live. My desire of life, however, is due to my wish of acquiring merit and not riches or enjoyment. Do you cast auspicious looks upon us all. It will be difficult for us to see you.

sn: अविषह्यं च राजा हि तीन चारप्स्यते तपः। एतच्छ्रुत्वा महाबाहुः सहदेवो युधां पतिः॥ युधिष्ठिरमुवाचेदं बाष्पव्याकुललोचनः। नोत्सहेऽहं परित्यक्तुं मातरं भरतर्षभ॥
en: The king will commence to practice the most austere and unbearable of penances!' Hearing these words, that king of battle, the mighty-armed Shadeva with eyes bathed in tears, addressed Yudhishthira, saying, 'O chief of Bharata race, I dare not leave my mother.

sn: प्रतियातु भवान् क्षिप्रं तपस्तप्स्याम्यहं विभो। इहैव शोषयिष्यामि तपसेदं कलेवरम्॥ पादशुश्रूषणे रक्तो राज्ञो मात्रोस्तथानयोः। तमुवाच ततः कुन्ती परिष्वज्य महाभुजम्॥
en: Do you return to the capital soon. I shall practice penances, O powerful one! Even here I shall reduce my body by penances, engaged in serving the feet of the king and of these my mothers!' To Kunti, after embracing that mighty armed here, addressed him thus, Depart, O son! Do not say so.

sn: गम्मतां पुत्र मैवं त्वं वोच: कुरुः वचो ममा आगमा वः शिवाः सन्तु स्वस्था भवत पुत्रकाः।।४०
en: Obey my behest! Do all of you go hence. Let peace by yours! You sons, let happiness be yours!

sn: उपरोधो भवेदेवमस्माकं तपसः कृते। त्वत्स्नेहपाशबद्धा च हीयेयं तपसः परात्॥
en: By your stay here, our penances will be impeded. Fettered by the ties of my affection for you. I shall fall off from my high penance's.

sn: तस्मात् पुत्रक गच्छ त्वं शिष्टमल्पं च नः प्रभो। एवं संस्तम्भितं वाक्यैः कुन्त्या बहुविधैर्मनः॥ सहदेवस्य राजेन्द्र राज्ञश्चैव विशेषतः। ते मात्रा समनुज्ञाता राज्ञा च कुरुपुङ्गवाः॥ अभिवाद्य कुरुश्रेष्ठमामन्त्रयितुमारभन्।
en: Therefore, O son, leave us. Short is the period of our existence, O you of great power. By these and various other speeches of Kunti, the minds of Sahadeva and king Yudhishthira were composed. Those foremost ones of Kuru's race, having received the permission of their mother as also of the (old) monarch, saluted the latter and began to take his leave.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच राज्यं प्रतिगमिष्यामः शिवेन प्रतिनन्दिताः॥ अनुज्ञातास्त्वया राजन् गमिष्यामो विकल्मषाः।
en: Yudhishthira said Delighted by auspicious blessings, we shall return to the capital. Indeed, O king having received your permission, we shall leave this hermitage freed from every sin.

sn: एवमुक्तः स राजर्षिर्धर्मराज्ञा महात्मना॥ अनुजज्ञे स कौरव्यमभिनन्द्य युधिष्ठिरम्।
en: Thus addressed by the great king Yudhishthira the just, that royal sage, viz., Dhritarashtra, blessed Yudhishthira and gave him permission.

sn: भीमं च बलिनां श्रेष्ठं सन्त्वयामास पार्थिवः॥ स चास्य सम्यङ् मेधावी प्रत्यपद्यत वीर्यवान्।
en: The king comforted Bhima, that foremost of all persons gifted with great strength. Gifted with great energy and great intelligence, Bhima showed his sub-missiveness to the king.

sn: अर्जुनं च समाश्लिष्य यमौ च पुरुषर्षभौ॥ अनुजज्ञे स कौरव्यः परिष्वज्याभिनन्द्य च।
en: Embracing Arjuna and clasping those foremost of men, viz., the twins also, and blessing them repeatedly, the Kuru king gave them permission to go.

sn: गान्धार्या चाभ्यनुज्ञाताः कृतपादाभिवादनाः॥ जनन्या समुमाघ्राता: परिष्वक्ताश्च ते नृपम्। चक्रुः प्रदक्षिणं सर्वे वत्सा इव निवारणे॥ पुनः पुनर्निरीक्षन्तः प्रचक्रुस्ते प्रदक्षिणम्।
en: They adored the feet of Gandhari and received her blessings also. Their mother Kunti then smelt their heads, and dismissed them. They then went round the king like calves, when prevented from sucking, their dams, Indeed, they repeatedly walked round him, loO king steadfastly at him.

sn: द्रौपदीप्रमुखाश्चैव सर्वाः कौरवयोषितः॥ न्यायतः श्वशुरे वृर्ति प्रयुज्य प्रययुस्ततः।
en: Then all the ladies of the Kaurava household, headed by Draupadi, adored their father-in-law according to the rites laid down in the scriptures, and departed.

sn: श्वश्रूभ्यां समनुज्ञाता: परिष्वज्याभिनन्दिताः॥ संदिष्टाश्चेति कर्तव्यं प्रययुभर्तृभिः सह।
en: Gandhari and Kunti embraced each of hem, and blessing them bade them go. Their mothers-in-law instructed them as to how they should behave themselves. Getting leave, they then departed, with their husband.

sn: ततः प्रजज्ञे निनदः सूतानां युज्यतामिति॥ उष्ट्राणां क्रोशतां चापि हयानां हेषतामपि।
en: Then loud sounds were heard, uttered by the charioteers that said, “Yoke, yoke,' as also of camels that granted aloud and of horses that neighed briskly.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा सदारः सहसैनिकः। नगरं हास्तिनपुरं पुनरायात् सबान्धवः॥
en: King Yudhishthira, with his wives and troops and all his kinsmen, started for Hastinapur.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच द्विवर्षोपनिवृत्तेषु पाण्डवेषु यदृच्छया। देवर्षिर्नारदो राजन्नाजगाम युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: After two years had passed from the date of the return of the Pandavas from the retreat of heir sire), the celestial Rishi, Narada, O king, came to Yudhishthria.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: तमभ्यर्च्य महाबाहुः कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। आसीनं परिविश्वस्तं प्रोवाचं वदतां वरः॥ चिरात्तु नानुपश्यामि भगवन्तमुपस्थितम्। कच्चित् ते कुशलं विप्र शुभं वा प्रत्युपस्थितम्॥
en: the mighty-armed Kuru king, that foremost of speakers, viz., Yudhishthira, having duly adored him, made him take a seat. After the Rishi had rested a while, the king asked him saying, 'It is after a long time that I see your holy self arrived at my court. Are you in peace and happiness, O learned Bhimasena?

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: के देशाः परिदृष्टास्ते किं च कार्यं करोमि ते। तद् ब्रूहि द्विजमुख्य त्वं त्वं ह्यस्माकं परा गतिः॥
en: What are toe countries which you have passed through? What can I do for you? Do you tell me. You are the foremost of twiceborn ones, and you are our highest refuge.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: नारद उवाच चिरदृष्टष्येऽसि मेत्येवमागतोऽहं तपोवनात्। परिदृष्टानि तीर्थानि गङ्गा चैव मया नृप॥
en: Narada said I have not seen you for a long time. Hence it is that I have come to you from my asylum. I have seen many sacred waters and the sacred rivers Ganga, also, O king.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच वदन्ति पुरुषा मेऽद्य गङ्गातीरनिवासिनः। धृतराष्ट्र महात्मानमास्थितं परमं तपः॥
en: People living on the banks of Ganga report that the great Dhritarashtra is practicing the austerest of penances.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: अपि दृष्टस्त्वया तत्र कुशली स कुरूद्वहः। गान्धारी च पृथा चैव सूतपुत्रश्च संजयः॥
en: Have you seen him there? Is that perpetuator o Kuru's race in peace? Are Gandhari and Pritha and the Suta's son Sanjaya also in peace?

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: कथं च वर्तते चाद्य पिता मम स पार्थिवः। श्रोतुमिच्छामि भगवन् यदि दृष्टस्त्वया नृपः॥
en: How, indeed, is that royal sire of mine doing? I wish to hear this, O holy one, if you have seen the king.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: नारद उवाच स्थिरीभूय महाराज शृणु वृत्तं यथातथम्। यथा श्रुतं च दृष्टं च मया तस्मिंस्तपोवने॥
en: Narada said Listen, O king, with calmness to me as I tell you what I have heard and seen in that asylum.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: वनवासनिवृत्तेषु भवत्सु कुरुनन्दन। कुरुक्षेत्रात् पिता तुभ्यं गङ्गाद्वारं ययौ नृप॥
en: After your return from Kurukshetra, O delighter of the Kurus, Your sire, O king, proceeded towards Gangadvara.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: गान्धार्या सहितो धीमान् वध्वा कुन्त्या समन्वितः। संजयेन च सूतेन साग्निहोज्ञः सयाजकः॥
en: That intelligent king took with him his (sacred) fire, Gandhari and his daughter-in-law Kunti, as also Sanjaya of the Suta caste, and all the Yajakas.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: आतस्थे स तास्तीव्र पिता तव तपोधनः। वीटां मुखे समाधाय वायुभक्षोऽभवन्मुनिः॥
en: Having penances for wealth, your sire set himself to the practice of severe austerities. He held pebbled of stone in his mouth and had air alone for his food, and abstained altogether from speech.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: वने स मुनिभिः सर्वैः पूज्यमानो महातपाः। त्वगस्थिमात्रशेषः स षण्मासानभवन्नृपः॥
en: Engaged in severe penances, he was adored by all the ascetics in the forest. In six months the king was reduced to only a skeleton.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: गान्धारी तु जलाहारी कुन्ती मासोपवासिनी। संजयः षष्ठभुक्तेन वर्तयामास भारत॥
en: Gandhari lived on water alone, while Kunti took a little food a intervals of month. Sanjaya, O Bharata, lived, eating a little every sixth day.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: अग्नींस्तु याजकास्तत्र जुहुवुर्विधिवत् प्रभो। दृश्यतोऽदृश्यतश्चैव बने तस्मिन् नृपस्य वै॥
en: The sacred fire, O monarch, (bclonging to the Kuru king) was duly adored by the sacrificing assistants who were with him, with libations of clarified butter poured on it. They did this whether the king saw the rite or not.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: अनिकेतोऽथ राजा स बभूव वनगोचरः। ते चापि सहिते देव्यौ संजयश्च तमन्वयुः॥
en: The king had no fixed dwelling. He became a wanderer through those forests. The two queens, as also Sanjaya, followed him.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: संजयो नृपतेर्नेता समेषु विषमेषु च। गान्धार्याश्च पृथा चैव चक्षुरासीदनिन्दिता॥
en: Sanjaya acted as the guide on even and uneven land. The faultless Pritha, O king, became the eye of Gandhari.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: ततः कदाचिद् गङ्गायाः कच्छे स नृपसत्तमः। गङ्गायामाप्लुतो धीमानाश्रमाभिमुखोऽभवत्॥
en: One day, that best of kings went to a spot on the margin of Ganga. He then bathed in the sacred river and finishing his ablutions turned his face toward his hermitage.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: अथ वायुः समुद्भूतो दावाग्निरभवन्महान्। ददाह तद् वनं सर्वे परिगृह्य समन्वतः॥
en: The wind rose high. A fierce wild fire set in. It began to burn that forest all around.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: दह्यत्सु मृगयूथेषु द्विजिह्वेषु समन्ततः। वराहाणां च यूथेषु संश्रयत्सु जलाशयान्॥
en: When the herds of animals were being burnt all around, as also the snakes which inhabited. that region, herds of wild board began to take themselves to the nearest marshes and waters.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: समाविद्धे वने तस्मिन् प्राप्ते व्यसन उत्तमे। निराहारतया राजन् मन्दप्राणविचेष्टितः॥
en: When that forest was thus afflicted on all sides and such distress came upon all the living creature living there, the king, who had taken no food, was incapable of moving or exerting himself at all.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: असमर्योऽपसरणे सुकृशे मातरौ च ते। ततः स नृपतिर्दृष्ट्वा वह्निमायान्तमन्तिकात्॥ इदमाह ततः सूतं संजयं जयतां वरः। गच्छ संजय यत्राग्निर्न त्वां दहति कर्हिचित्॥
en: Your two mothers also, exceedingly emaciated, could not move. The king, seeing the fire approach him from all sides, addressed the Suta Sanjaya, that foremost of skillful charioteers, saying, 'Go, O Sanjaya, to such a place where the fire may not burn you.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: वयमत्राग्निना युक्ता गमिष्यामः परां गतिम्। तमुवाच किलोद्विग्नः संजयो वदतां वरः॥ राजन् मृत्युरनिष्टोऽयं भविता ते वृथाग्निना। न चोपाय प्रपश्यामि मोक्षणे जातवेदसः॥
en: As regards ourselves, we shall allow our bodies to be destroyed by this fire and attain to the greatest end. To him, Sanjaya, that foremost of speakers, said-'O king, this death, brought on by a fire that is not sacred, will prove calamitous to you. I do not, however, see any means by which you can escape from this fire. our

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: यदत्रानन्तरं कार्य तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति। इत्युक्तः संजयेनेदं पुनराह स पार्थिवः॥ नैष मृत्युरनिष्टो नो निःसृतानां गृहात् स्वयम्। जलमग्निस्तथा वायुरथवाऽपि विकर्षणम्॥ तापसानां प्रशस्यन्ते गच्छ संजय मा चिरम्। इत्युक्त्वा संजयं राजा समाधाय मनस्तथा॥
en: That which should next be done should be marked by you. Thus addressed by Sanjaya the king once more said, “This death cannot be calamitous to us, for we have left our home of own accord. Water, fire, wind, and abstention from food, are laudable for ascetics. Do you, therefore, leave us, O Sanjaya, forthwith.' Having said these words to Sanjaya the king concentrated his mind.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: प्राङ्मुखः सह गान्धार्या कुन्त्या चोपाविशत् तदा। संजयस्तं तथा दृष्ट्वा प्रदक्षिणमथाकरोत्॥
en: Facing the east, he sat down, with Gandhari and Kunti. Seeing him in that attitude Sanjaya walked round him.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: उवाच चैनं मेधावी युड्क्ष्वात्मानमिति प्रभो। ऋषिपुत्रो मनीषी स राजा चक्रेऽस्य तद् वचः॥
en: Gifted with intelligence, Sanjaya said, 'Do you concentrate your mind. O powerful one!' The son of a Rishi, and himself endued with great wisdom, the king acted as he was told.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: सन्निमध्येन्द्रियग्राममासीत् काष्ठोपमस्तदा। गान्धारी च महाभागा जननी च पृथा तव॥
en: Governing all the senses, he remained like a post of wood. The highly blessed Gandhari, and your mother Pritha top, remained in the same attitude.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: दावाग्निना समायुक्ते स च राजा पिता तव। संजयस्तु महामात्रस्तस्माद् दावादमुच्यत॥
en: Then your royal sire was overtaken by the wild-fire, Sanjaya, his minister succeeded in escaping from that fire.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: गङ्गाकूले मया दृष्टस्तापसैः परिवारितः। स तानामन्त्र्य तेजस्वी निवेद्येतच्च सर्वशः॥ प्रययौ संजयो धीमान् हिमवन्तं महीधरम्।
en: I saw him on the banks of Ganga in the midst of ascetics. Gifted with great, energy and great intelligence's he bade them farewell and then started for the mountains of Himavat.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: एवं स निधनं प्राप्तः कुरुराजो महामनाः॥ गान्धारी च पृथा चैव जनन्यौ ते विशाम्पते।
en: Thus the great Kuru king met with his death, and it was thus that Gandhari and Kunti, your two others, also met with death, O monarch.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: यदृच्छयानुव्रजता मया राज्ञः कलेवरम्॥ तयोश्च देव्योरुभयोर्मया दृष्टानि भारत।
en: In course of my wanderings at will, I saw the bodies of that king and those two queens, O Bharata.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: ततस्तपोवने तस्मिन् समाजग्मुस्तपोधनाः॥ श्रुत्वा राज्ञस्तदा निष्ठां न त्वशोचन गतीश्च ते।
en: Many ascetics came to that asylum, having heard of the end of king Dhritarashtra. They did not at all grieve for that end of theirs.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: तत्राश्रौषमहं सर्वमेतत् पुरुषसत्तम॥ यथा च नृपतिर्दग्धो देव्यौ ते चेति पाण्डव
en: There, O best of men, I heard all the details of how the king and the two qucens, O son of Pandu, had been burnt.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: न शोचितव्यं राजेन्द्र स्वत: स पृथिवीपतिः॥ प्राप्तवानग्निसंयोगं गान्धारी जननी च ते।
en: O king of kings, you should not grieve for him. The monarch, of his own will, as also Gandhari and your mother, got that contact with fire,

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा च सर्वेषां पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्॥ निर्याणं धृतराष्ट्रस्य शोकः समभवन्महान्।
en: Vaishampayana said, Hearing of the departure of Dhritarashtra from his world, the great Pandavas all bewailed.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: अन्तःपुराणां च तदा महानार्तस्वरोऽभवत्।॥
en: Lord sounds of wailing were heard within the inner apartments of the palace. The citizens also, hearing of the end of the old king, bewailed aloud.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: अहो धिगिति राजा तु विक्रुश्य भृशदुःखितः॥ ऊर्ध्वबाहुः स्मरन् मातुः प्ररुरोद युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनपुरोगाश्च भ्रातरः सर्व एव ते॥
en: 'O Fie', cried king Yudhishthira in great agony, raising his arms a loft. Thinking of his mother, he wept like a child. All is brothers too, headed by Bhimasena, old the same.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: अन्तःपुरेषु च तदा सुमहान् रुदितस्वनः। प्रादुरासीन्महाराज पृथां श्रुत्वा तथागताम्॥
en: Hearing that Pritha had met with such a face, the royal ladies bewailed aloud in grief.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: तं च वृद्धं तथा दग्धं हतपुत्रं नराधिपम्। अन्वशोचन्त ते सर्वे गान्धारी च तपस्विनीम्॥
en: All the people grieved upon hearing that the old king, who had become childless, had been burnt to death and that the helpless Gandhari too had shared his fate.

description: Narada comes to Yudhishthira and describes the death of Dhritarashtra, Kunti, and others
sn: तस्मिन्नुपरते शब्दे मुहूर्तादिव भारत। निगृह्य बाष्पं धैर्येण धर्मराजोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: When those sounds of wailing ceased for a while, king Yudhishthira the just, shopping his tears by summoning all his patience, said these words.

sn: तथा महात्मनस्तस्य तपस्युग्रे च वर्ततः। अनाथस्येव निधनं तिष्ठत्स्वास्मासु बन्धुषु॥ दुर्विज्ञेया गतिर्ब्रह्मन् पुरुषाणां मतिर्मम। यत्र वैचित्रवीर्योऽसौ दग्ध एवं वनाग्निना॥
en: When such a fate overtook that great king who was engaged in austere penances, despite the fact of his having such kinsmen as ourselves all alive. It seems to me, O twice born one, that the end of human beings is difficult to guess. Alas, who would have thought that the son of Vichitravirya would thus be burns to death.

sn: यस्य पुत्रशतं श्रीमदभवद् बाहुशालिनः। नागायुतबलो राजा स दग्धो हि दवाग्निना॥
en: He had a hundred sons each gifted with mighty-arms and possessed of great prosperity! The king himself had the strength of ten thousand elephants, Alas, even he has been burnt to death in a wild fire.

sn: यं पुरा पर्यवीजन्त तालवृन्तैर्वरस्त्रियः। तं गृध्राः पर्यवीजन्त दावाग्निपरिकालितम्॥
en: Alas, he had formerly been fanned with palm leaves by the fair hands of beautiful women, was fanned by vultures with their wings after he had been burnt to death in a wild fire.

sn: सूतमागधसंघेश्च शयानो यः प्रबोध्यते। धरण्यां स नृपः शेते पापस्य मम कर्मभिः॥
en: He was formerly roused from sleep every morning by bands of Sutas and Magadhas had to sleep on the naked earth through the acts of my sinful self.

sn: न च शोचामि गान्धारी हतपुत्रां यशस्विनीम्। पतिलोकमनुप्राप्तां तथा भर्तृव्रते स्थिताम्॥
en: I do not grieve for the famous Gandhari who had been deprived of all her children. Observing the same vows as her husband. she has acquired those very regions which have become his.

sn: पृथामेव च शोचामि या पुत्रैश्वर्यमृद्धिमत्। उत्सृज्य सुमहद् दीप्तं वनवासमरोचयत्॥
en: I grieve, however, for Pritha who, renouncing the blazing prosperity of her sons, became desirous of living in the forest.

sn: धिग् राज्यमिदमस्माकं धिग् बलं धिक् पराक्रमम्। क्षत्रधर्मे च धिग् यस्मान्मृता जीवामहे वयम्॥
en: Fie on this sovereignty of ours, fie on our prowess, fie on the practices of Kshatriyas! Though alive, we are really dead.

sn: सुसूक्ष्मा किल कालस्य गतिर्द्विजवरोत्तम।
en: O foremost of superior Brahmanas, the course of Time is very subtle and difficult to understand inasmuch as Kunti, casting off sovereignty, became desirous so living in the forest.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्य जननी भीमस्य विजयस्य च। अनाथवत् कथं दग्ध इति मुह्यामि चिन्तयन्॥
en: How is it that she who was the mother of Yudhishthira, of Bhima, of Vijaya, was brunt to death like helpless creature! Thinking of this I become stupefied.

sn: वृथा संतर्पितो वह्निः खाण्डवे सव्यसाचिना। उपकारमजानन् स कृतघ्न इति मे मतिः॥
en: In vain was the god of fire pleased at Khandava by Arjuna! Ingrate that he is, forgetting that service, he has burnt to death the mother of his benefactor.

sn: यत्रादहत् स भगवान् मातरं सव्यसाचिनः। कृत्वा यो ब्राह्मणच्छद्मा भिक्षार्थी समुपागतः॥ धिगग्नि धिक् च पार्थस्य विश्रुतां सत्यसंधताम्।
en: Alas, how could that deity burn the mother of Arjuna! Putting, on the guise of Brahmana, he had formerly come to Arjuna, for begging a favour! Fie on the deity of fire! Fie on the celebrated success of Partha's arrows.

sn: इदं कष्टतरं चान्यद् भगवन् प्रतिभाति मे॥ वृथाग्निना समायोगो यदभूत् पृथिवीपतेः। तथा तपस्विनस्तस्य राजर्षेः कौरवस्य ह॥ कथमेवंविधो मृत्युः प्रशास्य पृथिवीमिमाम्। तिष्ठत्सु मन्त्रपूतेषू तस्याग्निषु महावने॥ वृथाग्निना समायुक्तो निष्ठां प्राप्तः पिता मम।
en: This is another incident, O holy one, which appears to me to be productive of greater misery, for that king, met with death by union with a fire that was not sacred! How could such a death overtake thai royal sage of Kuru's family who, after having governed the whole Earth, was engaged in the practice of penances! In that great forest there were fires that had been sanctified with Mantras. Alas, my father has made his departure from has world, coming

sn: मन्ये पृथा वेपमाना कृशा धमनिसंतता॥ हा तात! धर्मराजेति समाक्रन्दन्महाभये।
en: I suppose that Pritha, emaciated and reduced to a from in which all her nerves became visible, must have trembled in fear and cried aloud, saying, O son Yudhishthira! and awaited the terrible approach of the fire.

sn: भीम! पर्याप्नुहि भयादिति चैवाभिवाशती॥ समन्ततः परिक्षिप्ता माताभन्मे दवाग्निना।
en: She must have also said, O Bhima, save me from this danger! when she, my mother, was surrounded on all sides y that dreadful fire.

sn: सहदेवः प्रियस्तस्याः पुत्रेभ्योऽधिक एव तु॥ न चैनां मोक्षयामास वीरो माद्रवतीसुतः।
en: Among all her sons, Sahadeva was her darling. Alas, that heroic son of Madravati did not rescue her!'

sn: तच्छुत्वा रुरुदुः सर्वे समालिङ्य परस्परम्॥ पाण्डवाः पञ्च दुःखार्ता भूतानीव युगक्षये।
en: Hearing these bewailings of the king. all those person who were present there began to weep, embracing each other. In fact, the five sons of Pandu were so stricken with grief that they resembled living creatures at the time of the dissolution of the universe.

sn: तेषां तु पुरुषेन्द्राणां रुदतां रुदितस्वनः॥ प्रासादाभोगसंरुद्ध अन्वरौत्सीत् स रोदसी॥
en: The sound of lamentations uttered by those weeping heroes, filling the spacious chambers of the palace, escaped therefrom and penetrated the very sky.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: नारद उवाच नासौ वृथाग्निना दग्धो यथा तत्र श्रुतं मया। वैचित्रवीर्यो नृपतिस्तत् ते वक्ष्यामि सुव्रत॥
en: Narada said The king has not been burnt to death by an unsanctified fire. I have heard this there. I tell you, O Bharata, such has not been the fate of Vaichitravirya.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: वनं प्रविशतानेन वायुभक्षेण धीमता। अग्नयः कारयिन्वेष्टिमुत्सृष्टा इति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that when the old king gifted with great intelligence and living on air alone entered the forest (after his return from Gangadvara), he caused his sacrificial fires to be duly ignited. Having performed is sacred rites there with, be abandoned them all.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: याजकास्तु ततस्तस्य तानन्गीन्निर्जने वने। समुत्सृज्य यथाकामं जग्मुर्भरतसत्तम॥
en: Then the Yajaka Brahmanas he had with him cast off those fires in a solitary part of the forest and went away as they liked, O foremost one of Bharata's race.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: स विवृद्धस्तदा वह्निर्वने तस्मिन्नभूत् किल। तेन तद् वनमादीप्तमिति ते तापसाऽब्रुवन्॥
en: The fire that cast off grew in the forest. It then produced a general conflagration in the forest. This is what I have heard from the ascetics living on the banks of Ganga.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: स राजा जाह्नवीतीरे यथा ते कथितं मया। तेनाग्निना समायुक्तः स्वेनैव भरतर्षभ।॥
en: United with that (sacred) fire of his own, O chief of the Bharatas, the king, as I have already said to you, met with death on the banks of Ganga.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: एवमावेदयामासुर्मुनयस्ते ममानघ। ये ते भागीरथीतीरे मया दृष्टा युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O sinless one, this is what the ascetics have told me, those viz., whom I saw on the banks of sacred Bhagirathi, O Yudhishthira.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: एवं स्वेनाग्निना राजा समायुक्तो महीपते। मा शोचिथास्त्वं नृपतिं गतः स परमां गतिम्॥
en: Thus, O lord of Earth, king Dhritarashtra, coming into contact with his own sacred fire, departed from this world and attained to that high end that has been his.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: गुरुशुश्रूषया चैव जननी ते जनाधिप। प्राप्ता सुमहतीं सिद्धिमिति मे नात्र संशयः॥
en: Through service rendered by her to her seniors, your mother, O king, has acquired very great success. There is not the slightest doubt of this.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: कर्तुमर्हसि राजेन्द्र तेषां त्वमुदकक्रियाम्। भ्रातृभिः सहितः सर्वै रेतदत्र विधीयताम्॥
en: You should, O king of kings, now perform the rites of water to their honour with all your brothers. Let, therefore, the necessary steps be taken.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः स पृथिवीपालः पाण्डवानां धुरंधरः। निर्ययौ सहसोदर्यः सदारश्च नरर्षभः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then that lord of Earth, that foremost of men, that upholder of the burthens of the Pandavas, wen tout, accompanied by all his brother as well as the ladies of his household.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: पौरजानपदाश्चैव राजभक्तिपुरस्कृताः। गङ्गां प्रजग्मुरभितो वाससैकेन संवृताः॥
en: The inhabitants of the city as also those of the provinces, actuated by their loyalty, also went out. They all proceeded towards the banks of Ganga, every one clad on only a single piece of cloth.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: ततोऽवगाह्य सलिले सर्वे ते नरपुङ्गवाः। युयुत्सुमग्रतः कृत्वा ददुस्तोयं महात्मने॥ गान्धार्याश्च पृथायाश्च विधिवन्नामगोत्रतः।
en: Then all those foremost of men having plunged into the river, placed Yuyutsu at their head, and began to offer oblations of water to the grant king. And they also gave similar oblations to Gandhari and Pritha, naming each separately and mentioning their families.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: शौचं निवर्तयन्तस्ते तत्रोपुर्नगराद् बहिः॥ प्रेषयामास स नरान् विधिज्ञानाप्तकारिणः। गङ्गाद्वारं नरश्रेष्ठो यत्र दग्धोऽभवन्नृपः॥
en: Having finished those rites which purify the living, they returned but without entering their capital lived outside of it. They also sent a number of trusted people well conversant with the ordinances relating to the cremation of the dead, to Gangadvara where the old king had been burnt to death.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: तत्रैव तेषां कृत्यानि गङ्गाद्वारेऽन्वशात् तदा। कर्तव्यानीति पुरुषान् दत्तदेयान्महीपतिः॥
en: The king, having rewarded those men beforehand, commanded them to perform those rites of cremation which the bodies of Dhritarashtra and Gandhari and Kunti still awaited.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: द्वादशेऽहनि तेभ्यः स कृतशौचो नराधिपः। ददौ श्राद्धानि विधिवद् दक्षिणावन्ति पाण्डवः॥
en: On the twelfth day, the king, properly purified, duly performed the Shraddhas of his deceased relations, which were marked by profuse gifts.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: धृतराष्ट्रं समुद्दिश्य ददौ स पृथिवीपतिः। सुवर्णं रजतं गाश्च शय्याश्च सुमहाधनाः॥
en: Referring to Dhritarashtra, Yudhishthira made many gifts of gold and silver, of kine and costly beds.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: गान्धार्याश्चैव तेजस्वी पृथायाश्च पृथक् पृथक्। संकीर्त्य नामनी राजा ददौ दानमनुत्तमम्॥
en: Uttering the names of Gandhari and Pritha, the king, gifted with great energy, made many excellent gifts.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: यो यदिच्छति यावच्च तावत् स लभते नरः। शयनं भोजनं यानं मणिरत्नमथो धनम्॥
en: Every man received what thing he wished and as much of it as he wished, Beds and foods, and cars and conveyances, and jewels and gems, and other wealth were given away profusely.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: यानमाच्छादनं भोगान् दासीश्च समलंकृताः। ददौ राजा समुद्दिश्य तयोर्मात्रोर्महीपतिः॥
en: Indeed, the king, referring to his two mothers, gave away cars and conveyances, dresses and coverlets, various kind of food, and female slaves adorned with various ornaments.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: ततः स पृथिवीपालो दत्त्वा श्राद्धान्यनेकशः। प्रविवेश पुरं राजा नगरं वारणाह्वयम्॥
en: Having thus made many kinds of gift in profusion, that king then entered his capital named Histinapur.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: ते चापि राजवचनात् पुरुषा ये गताभवन्। संकल्प्य तेषां कुल्यानि पुनः प्रत्यागमंस्ततः॥
en: Those men, men who had gone to the banks of Ganga at the command of the king, having disposed of (by cremation) the remains of the king and the two queens, returned to the city.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: माल्यैर्गन्धैश्च विविधैरर्चयित्वा यथाविधि। कुल्यानि तेषां संयोज्य तदाचख्युर्महीपतेः॥
en: Having duly honoured those remains with garlands and scents of various kinds and disposed of them, they informed Yudhishthria of the accomplishment of their task.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: समाश्वास्य तु राजानं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। नारदोऽप्यगमद् राजन् परमर्षिर्यथेप्सितम्॥
en: FINISH AHSRAN The great Rishi Narada, having comforted king Yudhishthira of righteous soul, went away to where he liked.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: एवं वर्षाण्यतीतानि धृतराष्ट्रस्य धीमतः। वनवासे तथा त्रीणि नगरे दश पञ्च च॥
en: Thus did king Dhritarashtra make his departure from this world after having passed three years in the forest and fifteen years in the city.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: हतपुत्रस्य संग्रामे दानानि ददतः सदा। ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिमित्राणां भ्रातॄणां स्वजनस्य च॥
en: Having lost all his children in battle, he had made many gifts in honour of his kinsmen, relatives, and friends, his brothers and own people.

description: Narada describes the history of the death
sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु नृपतिर्नातिप्रीतमनास्तदा। धारयामास तद् राज्यं निहतज्ञातिबान्धवः॥
en: King Yudhishthira, after the death of his uncle, became very cheerless. Deprived of his kinsmen and relatives, he somehow bore the burthen of sovereignty. JAVASIKA PARVA

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरेयत्।।
en: Having saluted Narayana and Nara the best of male beings, as also Sarasvati the goddess of Learning let us cry success.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच षट्त्रिंशे त्वथ सम्प्राप्ते वर्षे कौरवनन्दनः। ददर्श विपरीतानि निमित्तानि युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said, When the thirty-sixth year (after the battle) arrived, the delighter of the Kurus, viz., Yudhishthira, saw many unusual portents.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: ववुर्ताताश्च निर्घाता रूक्षाः शर्करवर्षिणः। अपसव्यानि शकुना मण्डलानि प्रचक्रिरे॥
en: Winds, dry and strong, and showering gravel blew from all sides. Birds began to wheel, making circles from right to left.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: प्रत्यगूहुर्महानद्यो दिशो नीहारसंवृताः। उल्काश्चाङ्गारवर्षिण्यः प्रापतन् गगनाद् भुवि॥
en: The great rivers ran in opposite courses. The horizon on every side seemed to be always covered with fog. Meteors, showering coals, dropped on the Earth from the sky.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: आदित्यो रजसा राजन् समवच्छन्नमण्डलः। विरश्मिरुदये नित्यं कबन्धैः समदृश्यत॥
en: The Sun's disc, O king, seemed to be always covered with dust. At its rise, the Sun was shorn of splendour and seemed to be crossed by headless trunks.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: परिवेषाश्च दृश्यन्ते दारुणाश्चन्द्रसूर्ययोः। त्रिवर्णिः श्यामरुक्षान्तास्तथा भस्मारुणप्रभाः॥
en: Terrible circles of light were seen every day around both the Sun and the Moon. These circles showed three colours. Their edges seemed to be black and rough and ashy-red in color.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: एते चान्ये च बहव उत्पाता भयशंसिनः। दृश्यन्ते बहवो राजन् हृदयोद्वेगकारकाः॥
en: These and many other omens, fore shadowing fear and danger, were seen, o king and struck the hearts of men with anxiety.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। शुश्राव वृष्णिचक्रस्य मौसले कदनं कृतम्॥
en: A little while after the Kuru king Yudhishthira heard of the wholesale destruction of the Vrishnis on account of the iron bolt.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: विमुक्तं वासुदेवं च श्रुत्वा रामं च पाण्डवः। समानीयाब्रवीद् भ्रातृन् किं करिष्याम इत्युत॥
en: The son of Pandu, hearing that only Vasudeva and Rama had escaped alive, summoned his brothers and consulted with them as to what they should do.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: परस्परं समासाद्य ब्रह्मदण्डबलात् कृतान्। वृष्णीन् विनष्टांस्ते श्रुत्वा व्यथिताः पाण्डवाभवन्॥
en: Meeting with one another they became greatly stricken with surrow upon hearing that the Vrishnis had met with destruction through the Brahmana's rod of Punishment.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: निधनं वासुदेस्य समुद्रस्येव शोषणम्। वीरा न श्रद्दधुस्तस्य विनाशं शार्ङ्गधन्वनः॥
en: These heroes could not believe the death of Vasudeva, like the drying up of the ocean. In fact, they could not believe the destruction of the holder of Sharnga.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: मौसलं ते समाश्रित्य दुःखशोकसमन्विताः। विषण्णा हतसंकल्पाः पाण्डवाः समुपाविशन्॥
en: Inforined of the incident about the iron bolt, the Pandavas, became stricken with grief and sorrow. In fact, they sat down, utterly cheerless and stricken with blank despair.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं विनष्टा भगवन्नन्धका वृष्णिभिः सह। पश्यतो वासुदेवस्य भोजाश्चैव महारथाः॥
en: Indeed, O holy one, how was it that the Andhakas along with the Vrishnis, and those great car-warriors, viz., the Bhojas, met with destruction before the very eyes of Vasudeva?

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच घट्त्रिंशेऽथ ततो वर्षे वृष्णीनामनयो महान्। अन्योन्यं मुसलैस्ते तु निजघ्नुः कालचोदिताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said When the thirty-sixth year arrived (after the great battle) a great calamity overtook the Vrishnis. Moved by Time, they all met with destruction on account of the iron bolt.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: जनमेजय उवाच केनानुशप्तास्ते वीराः क्षयं वृष्ण्यन्धका गताः। भोजाश्च द्विजवर्य त्वं विस्तरेण वदस्व मे॥
en: Crused by whom did those heroes, viz., the Vrishnis, Andhakas and the Bhojas, met with destruction? O foremost of twice-born persons, do you fully explain all this to me.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विश्वामित्रं च कण्वं च नारदं च तपोधनम्। सारणप्रमुखा वीरा ददृशुभरकां गतान्॥
en: One day, the Vrishni heroes numbering Sarana amongst them; saw Vishvamitra and Kanwa and Narada arrived at Dwraka.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: ते तान् साम्बं पुरस्कृत्य भूषयित्वा स्त्रियं यथा। अब्रुवन्नुपसंगम्य दैवदण्डनिपीडिताः॥ इयं स्त्री पुत्रकामस्य बभ्रोरमिततेजसः। ऋषयः साधु जानीत किमियं जनयिष्यति॥
en: Afflicted by the rod of punishment held by the celestials, those heroes causing Shamba to be disguised like a woman, approached those ascetics and said, “This one is the wife of Vabhru of great energy who is desirous of having a son. You Rishis, do you know for certain what this one will produce?'

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: इत्युक्तास्ते तदा राजन् विप्रलम्भप्रधर्षिताः। प्रत्यब्रुवंस्तान् मुनयो यत् तच्छृणु नराधिप॥ वृष्ण्यन्धकविनाशाय मुसलं घोरमायसम्। वासुदेवस्य दायादः साम्बोऽयं जनयिष्यति॥
en: Hear now, O king, what those ascetics, attempted to be thus imposed on, said, “This heir of Vasudeva, by name Shamba, will produce a dreadful iron bolt for the destruction of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: येन यूयं सुदुर्वृत्ता नृशंसा जातमन्यवः। उच्छेत्तारः कुलं वृत्स्नमृते रामजनार्दनौ॥
en: O wicked and cruel ones, intoxicated with pride, through that iron bolt you will become the exterminators of your family with the exception of Rama an Janardana.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: समुद्रं यास्यति श्रीमांस्त्यक्त्वा देहं हलायुधः। जरा कृष्णं महात्मानं शयानं भुवि भेत्स्यति॥
en: The blessed hero armed with the plough will enter the ocean renouncing his body, while a hunter of the name of Jara will pierce the great Krishna while lying on the ground.'

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: इत्यब्रुवन्त ते राजन् प्रलब्धास्तैर्दुरात्मभिः। मुनयः क्रोधरक्ताक्षाः समीक्ष्याथ परस्परम्॥ तथोक्त्वा मुनयस्ते तु ततः केशवमभ्ययुः।
en: Attempted to be deceived by those wicked ones, those ascetics, with eyes red in anger, looked at each other and uttered those words. Having said so they then went to see Keshava.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: अथाब्रवीत् तदा वृष्णीश्रुत्वैवं मधुसूदनः॥ अन्तज्ञो मतिमांस्तस्य भवितव्यं तथेति तान्।
en: The destroyer of Madhu, informed of what had occurred, summoned all the Vrishnis and told them of it. Gifted with great intelligence and fully acquainted with what the end of his family would be he simply said that that which was destined would surely take place.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: एवमुक्त्वा ह्रषीकशः प्रविवेश पुरं तदा॥ कृतान्तमन्यथा नैच्छत् कर्तुं स जगतः प्रभुः।
en: Hrishikesha having said so, entered his palace. The Lord of the universe did not wish to ordain otherwise.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: श्वोभूतेऽथ ततः साम्बो मुसलं तदसूत वै॥ येन वृष्ण्यन्धककुले पुरुषा भस्मसात् कृताः।
en: When the next day came, Shamba actually produced an iron bolt through which all the individuals in the family of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas became reduced to ashes.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: वृष्ण्यन्धकविनाशाय किंकरप्रतिमं महत्॥ असूत शापजं घोरं तच्च राज्ञे न्यवेदयन्।
en: Indeed, for the destruction of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas, Shambas brought forth, through that curse, a dreadful iron bolt that looked like a huge messenger of death. The fact was duly reported to the king.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: विषण्णरूपस्तद् राजा सूक्ष्मं चूर्णमकारयत्॥ तच्चूर्णं सागरे चापि प्राक्षिपन् पुरुषा नृप।
en: In great distress of mind, the king (Ugrasena) caused that iron bolt to be reduced into fine powder. Men were engaged, O king, to cast that powder into the sea.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: अघोषयंश्च नगरे वचनादाहुकस्य ते॥ जनार्दनस्य रामस्य बभ्रोश्चैव महात्मनः। अद्यप्रभृति सर्वेषु वृष्ण्यन्धककुलेष्विह॥ सुरासवो न कर्तव्यः सर्वैर्नगरवासिभिः। यश्च नोऽविदितं कुर्यात् पेयं कश्चिन्नरः क्वचित्॥ जीवन् स शूलमारोहेत् स्वयं कृत्वा सबान्धवः।
en: At the command of Ahuka, of Janardana, of Rama, and of great Vabhru, it was, again, proclaimed throughout the city, that from that day, among all the Vrishnis and the Andhakas one should manufacture wines and intoxicating liquors of any kind, and that whoever would secretly manufacture wines no and spirits should be impaled alive with all his kinsmen.

description: MAUSALA PARVA Yudhishthira marks many unusual portents
sn: ततो राजभयात् सर्वे नियमं चक्रिरे तदा। नराः शासनमाज्ञाय रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥
en: Through fear of the king, and knowing that it the order of Rama also of unimpeachable deeds, all the citizen bound themselves by a rule and abstained from manufacturing wines and spirits. was

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं प्रयतमानानां वृष्णीनामन्धकैः सह। कालो गृहाणि सर्वेषां परिचक्राम नित्यशः॥
en: Vaishampayana said While the Vrishnis and the Andhakas were thus trying (to avoid the impending calamity), the embodied from of time (death) every day wandered about their houses.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: करालो विकटो मुण्डः पुरुषः कृष्णपिङ्गलः। गृहाण्यावेक्ष्य वृष्णीनां नादृश्यत क्वचित् क्वचित्।२।
en: He looked like a man of terrible and fierce aspect. Of bald head, he was black and of tawny color. Sometimes he was beheld by the Vrishnis as he peered into their houses.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: तमनन्त महेष्वासाः शरैः शतसहस्रशः। न चाशक्यत वेढुं स सर्वभूतात्ययस्तदा॥
en: The powerful bowmen among the Vrishnis shot hundreds and thousands of arrows at him, but none of these succeeded in piercing him, for he was none else than the Destroyer of all creatures.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: उत्पेदिरे महावाता दारुणाश्च दिने दिने। वृष्ण्यन्धकविनाशाय बहवो लोमहर्षणाः॥
en: Day by day strong winds blew, and many were the evil omens which arose, awful and foreboding the destruction of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: विवृद्धमूषिका रथ्या विभिन्नमणिकास्तथा। केशा नखाश्च सुप्तानामद्यन्ते मूषिकैर्निशि॥
en: The streets swarmed with rats and mice. Earthen pots showed cracks or broken from no visible cause. At night, the rats and mice ate away the hair and nails of sleeping men.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: चीचीकूचीति वाशन्ति सारिका वृष्णिवेश्मसु। नोपशाम्यति शब्दश्च स दिवारानमेव हि॥
en: Sharikas chirped, sitting within the houses of the Vrishnis. The noise made by those birds ceased not for even a short while by day or by night.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: अन्वकुर्वन्नुलूकानां सारसा विरुतं तथा। अजाः शिवानां विरुतमन्वकुर्वत भारत॥
en: The Sarashas were heard to imitate the hooting of the owl, and goats imitated the cries, O Bharata, of Jackals.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: पाण्डुरा रक्तपादाश्च विहगाः कालचोदिताः। वृष्ण्यन्धकानां गेहेषु कपोता व्यचरंस्तदा॥
en: Many birds appeared, moved by Death, which were pale of color, but that had legs red of hue. Pigeons were seen to always disport in the houses of the Vrishni.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: व्यजायन्त खरा गोषु करभा श्वतरीषु च। शुनीष्वपि बिडालाश्च मूषिका नकुलीषु च॥
en: Asses were born of kine, and elephants of mules. Cats were born of bitches, and mouse of the mungoose.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: नापत्रपन्त पापानि कुर्वन्तो वृष्णयस्तदा। प्राद्विषन् ब्राह्मणांश्चापि पितृन् देवांस्तथैव च॥
en: The Vrishnis, committing sinful deeds, were not seen to feel any shame. They showed disregard for Brahmanas and the departed manes and the departed manes and the celestials.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: गुरूंश्चाप्यवमन्यन्ते न तु रामजनार्दनौ। पल्य: पतीनुच्चरन्त पत्नीश्च पतयस्तथा॥
en: They insulted and humiliated their preceptors and elders. Only Rama and Janardana acted differently. Wives deceived their husbands, and husbands deceived wives.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: विभावसुः प्रज्वलितो वामं विपरिवर्तते। नीललोहितमञ्जिष्ठा विसृजन्नर्चिषः पृथक्॥
en: Fires, when ignited cast their flames towards the left. Sometimes they threw out flames whose colour was blue and red.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: उदयास्तमने नित्यं पुर्यां तस्यां दिवाकरः। व्यदृश्यतासकृत् पुम्भिः कबन्धैः परिवारितः॥
en: The Sun, whether when rising or setting over that city, seemed to be surrounded by headless trunks of human beings.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: महानसेषु सिद्धेषु संस्कृतेऽतीव भारत। आहार्यमाणे कृमयो व्यदृश्यन्त सहस्रशः॥
en: In cook-rooms, upon food that was clean and well-boiled, were soon, when it was served out for eating, innumerable worms of various kinds.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: पुण्याहे वाच्यमाने तु जपत्सु च महात्मसु। अभिधावन्तः श्रूयन्ते न चादृश्यत कश्चन॥
en: When Brahmanas, receiving gifts, blessed the day or the hour fixed for this or that undertaking or when great men were engaged in silent recitations, the heavy trend was heard of many men running about but no one could be seen to whom the sound of such sound could be ascribed.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: परस्परं च नक्षत्रं हन्यमानं पुनः पुनः। ग्रहैरपश्यन् सर्वे ते नात्मनस्तु कथंचन॥
en: The Constellations were repeatedly seen to be struck by the planets. None amongst the Yadavas could, however, see the constellation of his birth.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: नदन्तं पाञ्चजन्यं च वृष्ण्यन्धकनिवेशने। समन्तात् पर्यवाशन्त रासभा दारुणस्वराः॥
en: When the Panchajanya was blown in their houses, asses of dissonant and awful voice brayed aloud from all sides.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: एवं पश्यन् हृषीकेशः सम्प्राप्तं कालपर्ययम्। त्रयोदश्याममावास्यां तान् दृष्ट्वा प्राब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Seeing these sings which showed the perverse course of Time, and seeing that the day of the new moon coincided with the thirteenth (and the fourteenth) lunation's, Hrishkesha, summoning the Yadavas, said to them these words:

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: चतुर्दशी पञ्चदशी कृतेयं राहुणा पुनः। प्राप्ते वै भारते युद्धे प्राप्ता चाद्य क्षयाय नः॥
en: The fourteenth lunation has been made the fifteenth by Rahu once more. Such a day had appeared at the time of the great battle of the Bharatas. It has once more appeared, it seems, for our destruction.'

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: विमृशन्नेव कालं तं परिचिन्त्य जनार्दनः। मेने प्राप्तं स षट्त्रिंशं वर्षे वै केशिसूदनः॥ पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्ता गान्धारी हतबान्धवा। यदनुव्याजहारार्ता तदिदं समुपागमत्॥
en: The destroyer of Keshi, viz., Janardana, thinking upon the omens that Time showed, understood that the thirty-sixth year had come, and that what Gandhari, burning with grief on account of the death of her sons, and deprived of all her kinsmen, had said was about to take place.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: इदं च तदनुप्राप्तमब्रवीद् यद् युधिष्ठिरः। पुरा व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु दृष्ट्वोत्पातान् सुदारुणान्॥
en: The present is exactly similar to that time which Yudhishthira had marked at sight of those dreadful omens which appeared when the two armies were arranged in battle-order.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: इत्युक्त्वा वासुदेवस्तु चिकीर्षुः सत्यमेव तत्। आज्ञापयामास तदा तीर्थयात्रामरिंदमः॥
en: Vasudeva, having said so, tried to bring about those occurrences which would make Gandhari's words true. That chastiser of enemies commanded the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to some sacred water.

description: Vasudeva orders the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to the seacoast for bathing in the sacred water of the ocean
sn: अघोषयन्त पुरुषास्तत्र केशवशासनात्। तीर्थयात्रा समुद्रे वः कार्येति पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: The messengers immediately proclaimed at the command of Keshava that the Vrishnis should make a journey to the sea-coast for bathing in the sacred waters of the ocean.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच काली स्त्री पाण्डुरैर्दन्तैः प्रविश्य हसती निशि। स्त्रियः स्वप्नेषु मुष्णन्ती द्वारकां परिधावति॥
en: Vaishampayana said At that time the Vrishni ladics dreamt every night a woman of black color and white teeth, entering their abodes, laughed aloud and ran through Dwraka, snatching from them the auspicious threads in their wrists.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: अग्निहोत्रनिकेतेषु वास्तुमध्येषु वेश्मसु। वृष्ण्यन्धकानखादन्त स्वप्ने गृध्रा भयानकाः॥
en: The men dreamt that dreadful vultures, entering their houses and fire-chambers, gorged themselves on their bodies.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: अलंकाराच छत्रं च ध्वजाश्च कवचानि च। हियमाणान्यदृश्यन्त रक्षोभिः सुभयानकैः॥
en: Their ornaments and umbrellas and standards and armour were seen to be taken away by dreadful Rakshasas.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तच्चाग्निदत्तं कृष्णस्य वज्रनाभमयोमयम्। दिवमाचक्रमे चक्रं वृष्णीनां पश्यतां तदा॥
en: Before the very eyes of the Vrishnis, the discus of Krishna, given by Agni, made of iron and having its nave composed of hardest adamant, ascended into the sky.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: युक्तं रथं दिव्यमादित्यवर्णं हया हरन् पश्यतो दारुकस्य। ते सागरस्योपरिष्टादवर्तन् मनोजवाश्चतुरो वाजिमुख्याः॥
en: In the very sight of Daruka, the excellent car of Vasudeva, effulgent like the sun, and properly equipt was taken away by the horses yoked to it. Those foremost of horses, numbering four, and fleet like the mind, fled away, dragging the car after them along the surface of the ocean.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तालः सुपर्णश्च महाध्वजौ तौ सुपूजितौ रामजनार्दनाभ्याम्। उच्चैर्जह्वरप्सरो दिवानिशं वाचश्चोचुर्गम्यतां तीर्थयात्रा॥
en: The two great standards of Krishna's car and Baladeva's car, having the emblems of Garuda and palmyra, which were reverently adored those two heroes, were taken away by Apsaras who, day and night, called upon the Vrishnis and the Andhakas to start on a pilgrimage to some sacred water.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ततो जिगमिषन्तस्ते वृष्ण्यन्धकमहारथाः। सान्तःपुरास्तदा तीर्थयात्रामैच्छन् नरर्षभाः॥
en: When these omens were seen and heard, those foremost of men, viz., the powerful carwarriors of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas, became desirous of setting out, with their whole families, on a pilgrimage to some sacred water.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ततो भोज्यं च भक्ष्यं च पेयं चान्धकवृष्णयः। बहु नानाविधं चक्रुर्मा मांसमनेकशः॥
en: They prepared various kinds of viands and edibles and various kinds of wines and meat.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ततः सैनिकवर्गाश्च निर्ययुर्नगराद् बहिः। यानैरश्वैर्गजैश्चैव श्रीमन्तस्तिग्मतेजसः॥
en: The troops of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas, blazing with beauty and gifted with fierce energy, then set out from the city on cars and horses and elephants.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ततः प्रभासे न्यवसन् यथोद्दिष्टं यथागृहम्। प्रभूतभक्ष्यपेशस्ते सदारा यादवास्तदा॥
en: The Yadavas then, with their wives, proceeded to Prabhasa and took up their residence there, each in the (temporary) habitation which was assigned to him and all having profuse provisions consisting of edibles and drink.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: निविष्टांस्तान् निशम्याथ समुद्रान्ते स योगवित्। जगामामन्त्र्य तान् वीरानुद्धवोऽर्थविशारदः॥
en: Hearing that they had taken up their abode on the sea-coast, Uddhava, the wisest of men, who was, besides, well-versed in Yoga, went there and to their leave (for departing).

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तं प्रस्थितं महात्मानमभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिम्। जानन् विनाशं वृष्णीनां नैच्छद् वारयितुं हरिः॥
en: Krishna, with joined with joined hands, saluted Uddhava, and seeing him bent on departing (from the world) and knowing that the destruction of the Vrishnis was night, did not feel any disposition to prevent him.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ततः कालपरीतास्ते वृष्ण्यन्धकमहारथाः। अपश्यन्नुद्धवं यान्तं तेजसाऽऽवृत्य रोदसी॥
en: The powerful car-warriors among the Vrishnis and the Andhakas, whose hour hand come, then saw Uddhava proceed on his great journey, filling the entire sky with his effulgence.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ब्राह्मणार्थेषु यत् सिद्धमन्नं तेषां महात्मनाम्। तद् वरनरेभ्यः प्रददुः सुरागन्धसमन्वितम्॥
en: The Vrishnis, mixing with wine the food that had been cooked for great Brahmanas, gave it away to monkeys an apes.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ततस्तूर्यशताकीर्णं नदनर्तकसंकुलम्। अवर्तत महापानं प्रभासे तिग्मतेजसाम्॥
en: Those heroes of fierce energy then began to revel with drink, at Prabhasa. The entire field echoed with the blare of hundreds of trumpets and abounded with actors and dancers.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: कृष्णस्य संनिधौ रामः सहित: कृतवर्मणा। अपिबद् युयुधानश्च गदो बभ्रुस्तथैव च॥
en: In the very sight of Krishna, Rama began to drink, with Kritavarman, Yuyudhana and Gada and Vabhru also did the same.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ततः परिषदो मध्ये युयुधानो मदोत्कटः। अब्रवीत् कृतवर्माणमवहास्यावमन्य च॥ कःक्षत्रियोऽहन्यमानः सुप्तान् हन्यान्मृतानिव। तन्न मृष्यन्ति हार्दिक्य यादवा यत् त्वया कृतम्॥
en: Then Yuyudhana, inebriated with wine, derisively laughing at and insulting Kritavarman in the midst of that assembly, said, 'What Kshatriya is there who, armed with weapons, will kill men locked in the embraces of sleep and, therefore, already dead? Hence, O son of Hridika, the Yadavas will never tolerate what you have done.'

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: इत्युक्ते युयुधानेन पूजयामास तद्वचः। प्रद्युम्नो रथिनां श्रेष्ठो हार्दिक्यमवमन्य च॥
en: When Yuyudhana had said these words, Pradyumna, that foremost of car-warriors, applauded them, expressing his disregard for the son of Hridika.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ततः परमसंक्रुद्धः कृतवर्मा तमब्रवीत्। निर्दिशन्निव सावज्ञं तदा सव्येन पाणिना॥
en: Greatly enraged at this, Kritavarman, cmphasising his disregard for Satyaki by pointing to him with his left hand, said these words:

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: भूरिश्रवाश्छिन्नबाहुयुद्धे प्रायगतस्त्वया। वधेन सुनृशंसेन कथं वीरेण पातितः॥
en: Professing yourself to be a hero, how could you so cruelly kill the armless Bhurishravas who, on the field of battle, sat fasting.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: हति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा केशवः परवीरहा। तिर्यक्सरोषया दृष्ट्या वीक्षाचक्रे स मन्युमान्॥
en: Hearing these words of his, Keshava, that destroyer of hostile heroes, giving way to anger, cast an angry look at Kritavarman.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: मणिः स्यमन्तकश्चैव यः स सत्राजितोऽभवत्। तां कथां श्रावयामास सात्यकिर्मधुसूदनम्॥
en: Then Satyaki informed the destroyer of Madhu as to how Kritavarman had behaved towards Satrajit for taking away from him the celebrated gem Syamantaka.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तच्छुवा केशवस्याङ्कमगमद् रुदती तदा। सत्यभामा प्रकृपिता कोपयन्ती जनार्दनम्॥
en: Hearing the narrative, Satyabhama, giving way to anger and tears, approached Keshava, and sitting on his lap, increased his anger (for Kritavarman).

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तत उत्थाय सक्रोधः सात्यकिर्वाक्यपब्रवीत्। पञ्चानां द्रोपदेयानां धृष्टद्युन्नशिखण्डिनोः॥ एष गच्छामि पदवीं सत्येन च तथा शपे। सौप्तिके ये च निहताः सुप्ता येन दुरात्मना॥ द्रोणपुत्रसहायेन पापेन कृतवर्मणा। समाप्तमायुरस्याद्य यशश्चैव सुमध्यमे॥
en: Then rising up in anger, Satyaki said, 'I swear to your by Truth that I shall soon cause this one to follow the five sons of Draupadi, and of Dhrishtadyumna and Shikhandin, they, viz., who were killed by this sinful wretch, while they were asleep, with the help of Drona's son, O you of slender wish, Kritavarman's period of life and fame has come to an end.'

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा खड्ड्रेन केशवस्य समीपतः। अभिद्रुत्य शिरः क्रुद्धश्चिच्छेद कृतवर्मणः॥
en: Having said these words, Satyaki rushed at Kritavarman and cut off his head with a sword in the very sight of Keshava.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तथान्यानपि निघ्नन्तं युयुधानं समन्ततः। अभ्याधावद्धृषीकेशो विनिवारयितुं तदा॥
en: Yuyudhana, having performed this feat, began to strike down others there present. Hrishikesha ran to prevent him from doing further mischief.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: एकीभूतास्ततः सर्वे कालपर्यायचोदिताः। भोजान्धका महाराज शैनेयं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: At that time, however, O king, the Bhojas and Andhakas moved by the perverseness of the hour that had come upon them, all became as one man and surrounded the son of Shini.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा पततस्तूर्णमभिक्रुद्धाञ्जनार्दनः। न चुक्रोध महातेजा जानन् कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: Janardana of great energy, knowing the character of the hour stood unmoved without giving way to anger, seeing those heroes rushing in anger at Satyaki from every side.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ते तु पानमदाविष्टाश्चोदिताः कालधर्मणा। युयुधानमथाभ्यघ्ननुच्छिष्टै जनै स्तदा।॥
en: Urged by fate and inebriated with drink, they began to strike Yuyudhana with the pots from which they had been eating.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: हन्यमाने तु शैनेये क्रुद्धो रुक्मिणिनन्दनः। तदनन्तरमागच्छन्मोक्षयिष्यन् शिनेः सुतम्॥ स भोजैः सह संयुक्तः सात्यकिश्चान्धकैः सह।
en: When the son of Shini was being thus assaulted, Rukmini's son became greatly enraged. he rushed forward for rescuing Satyaki who was engaged with the Bhojas and the Andhaks.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: व्यायच्छमानौ तौ वीरौ बाहुद्रविणशालिनौ॥ बहुत्वात्रिहतौ तत्र उभौ कृष्णस्य पश्यतः।
en: Gifted with might of arms and w’alth of energy, those two heroes acted with great courage. But as the odds were overwhelming, both of them were killed before the very eyes of Krishna.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: हतं दृष्ट्वा च शैनेयं पुत्रं च यदुनन्दनः॥ एरकानां ततो मुष्टिं कोपाज्जग्राह केशवः।
en: Seeing his own son, and the son of Shini too, killed, the delighter of the Yadus took up, in anger, a handful of the Eraka grass which grew there.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तदभून्मुसलं घोरं वज्रकल्पमयोमयम्॥ जघान कृष्णस्तांस्तेन ये ये प्रमुखतोऽभवन्।
en: That handful of grass became a terrible bolt of iron gifted with the energy of the thunderbolt. With it Krishna destroyed all those who came before him.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: ततोऽन्धकाश्च भोजाश्च शैनेया वृष्णयस्तथा॥ जघ्नुरन्योन्यमाक्रन्दे मुसलैः कालचोदिताः।
en: Then the Andhakas and the Bhojas, the Shaineyas and the Vrishnis, urged by Time, struck one another in that dreadful right.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: यस्तेषामेरकां कश्चिज्जग्राह कुपितो नृप॥ वज्रभूतेव सा राजन्नदृश्यत तदा विभो।
