en: Indeed, O king, whoever amongst them took up in anger a few blades of the Eraka grass, these, in his hands, became soon converted into a thunder-bolt, O powerful one.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तृणं च मुसलीभूतमपि तत्र व्यदृश्यत॥ ब्रह्मदण्डकृतं सर्वमिति तद् विद्धि पार्थिव।
en: Every blade of grass there was seen to be converted into a terrible iron bolt. All this, know, O king, was due to the curse imprecated by Brahmanas.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: अविध्यान् विध्यते राजन् प्रक्षिपन्ति स्म यत् तृणम्॥ तद् वज्रभूतं मुसलं व्यदृश्यत तदा दृढम्।
en: He who hurled a blade of grass saw that it pierced through even such things as were utterly impenetrable. In fact, every blade was seen to become a dreadful bolt having the force of thunder.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: अवधीत् पितरं पुत्रः पिता पुत्रं च भारत॥ मत्ता परिपतन्ति स्म योधयन्तः परस्परम्।
en: Son killed father, and father killed son, O Bharata! Inebriated with wine, they rushed and fell upon one another.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: पतङ्गा इव चाग्नौ ते निपेतुः कुकुरान्धकाः॥ नासीत् पलायने बुद्धिर्वध्यमानस्य कस्यचित्।
en: The Kukuras and the Andhakas met with destruction like insects rushing at a burning fire. As they were thus being destroyed, no one among them thought of escaping by flight.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तत्रापश्यन्महाबाहुर्जानन् कालस्य पर्ययम्॥ मुसलं समवष्टभ्य तस्थौ स मधुसूदनः।
en: Knowing that the hour of destruction had come, the mighty-armed Keshava stood there, seeing everything. Indeed, the destroyer of Madhu stood, raising a bolt of Iron formed of a blade of grass.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: साम्बं च निहतं दृष्ट्वा चारुदेष्णं च माधवः॥ प्रद्युम्नं चानिरुद्धं च ततश्चुक्रोध भारत।
en: Seeing that Shamba was killed, as also Charudeshna and Pradyumna and Aniruddha, Madhava became filled with anger.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: गदं वीक्ष्य शयानं च भृशं कोपसमन्वित॥ स निःशेषं तदा चक्रे शार्ङ्गचक्रगदाधरः।
en: Seeing Gada lying dead on the ground, his anger became enhanced. The holder Sharnaga and the discus and the mace then rooted the Vrishnis and the Andhakas.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: तन्निघ्नन्तं महातेजा बभ्रुः परपुरंजयः॥ दारुकश्चैव दाशार्हमूचतुर्यन्निबोध तत्।
en: Hear, O king, what that conqueror of hostile towns, viz., Vabhru of great energy, and Daruka, then said to Krishna.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: भगवन् निहताः सर्वे त्वया भूयिष्ठशो नराः। रामस्य पदमन्विच्छ तत्र गच्छाम यत्र सः॥
en: O holy one, a very large number of men has been killed by you. Turn now to where Rama has gone! We wish to go there where he has gone.

description: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas start on a pilgrimage and meet with their doom
sn: भगवन् निहताः सर्वे त्वया भूयिष्ठशो नराः। रामस्य पदमन्विच्छ तत्र गच्छाम यत्र सः॥
en: O holy one, a very large number of men has been killed by you. Turn now to where Rama has gone! We wish to go there where he has gone.

sn: गत्वा कुरुन् वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो ययुर्दारुकः केशवश्च बभ्रुश्च रामस्य पदं पतन्तः। अथापश्यन् राममनतवीर्ये वृक्षे स्थितं चिन्तयानं विविक्ते॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Then Daruka, Keshava and Vabhru left that place following Rama. They saw that hero of great energy sitting thoughtfully, reclining his back against at tree, in a solitary place.

sn: ततः समासाद्य महानुभावं कृष्णस्तदा दारुकमन्वशासत्। सर्वमिमं महान्तं पार्थाय शंसस्व वधं यदूनाम्॥
en: Finding Rama of great soul, Krishna ordered Daruka, saying, 'Going to the Kurus, inform Partha of this great carnage of the Yadus.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनः क्षिप्रमिहापयातु श्रुत्वा मृतान् यादवान् ब्रह्मशापात्। इत्येवमुक्तः स ययौ रथेन कुरुस्तदा दारुको नष्टचेताः॥
en: Let Arjuna come here speedily hearing of the destruction of the Yadavas though the Brahmanas' course.' Thus addressed Daruka, deprived of his senses by sorrow, proceeded on a car to the capital of the Kurus.

sn: ततो गते दारुके केशवोऽथ दृष्ट्वान्तिके बभ्रुमुवाच वाक्यम्। स्त्रियो भवान् रक्षितुं यातु शीघ्र नैता हिंस्युर्दस्यवो वित्तलोभात्॥
en: After Daruka had departed, Keshava, seeing Vabhru waiting on him, told him these words 'Do you go speedily for protecting the ladies. Let not robbers do them any injury, tempted by the riches.

sn: स प्रस्थितः केशवेनानुशिष्टो मदातुरो ज्ञातिवधार्दितश्च। तं विश्रान्तं संनिधौ केशवस्य दुरन्तमेकं सहसैव बभ्रम्॥ ब्रह्मानुशप्तमवधीन्महद् वै कूटे युक्तं मुसलं लुब्धकस्य।
en: Thus orderded by Keshava, Vabhru still helpless with wine but cheerless at the destruction of his kinsmen, wen away. He had rested for a while by the side of Keshava, but as soon as he had gone to a distance the ironbolt, attached to a mallet in the hands of a hunter, suddenly sprang of itself upon that solitary survivor of the Yadava family and killed him who also had been included in the curs of the Brahmans.

sn: ततो दृष्ट्वा निहतं बभ्रुमाह कृष्णोऽग्रजं भ्रातरमुग्रतेजाः॥ इहैव त्वं मां प्रतीक्षस्व राम यावत् स्त्रियो ज्ञातिवशाः करोमि।
en: Seeing Vabhru killed, Keshava of great energy addressed his elder brother and said, 'Do you, O Rama, wait for me her till I put the ladies under the care of kinsmen.

sn: ततः पुरीं द्वारवतीं प्रविश्य जनार्दनः पितरं प्राह वाक्यम्॥ स्त्रियो भवान् रक्षतु नः समग्रा धनञ्जयस्यागमनं प्रतीक्षन्।
en: Entering the city of Dvaravati, Janardana said these words to his father, 'Do you protect all the ladies of our house till Dhananjaya comes.

sn: रामो वनान्ते प्रतिपालयन्मा मास्तेऽद्याहं तेन समागमिष्ये॥ दृष्टं मयेदं निधनं यदूनां राज्ञां च पूर्वं पुरुपुङ्गवानाम्।
en: At the skirts of the forest Rama is waiting for me. I shall meet him today. This great destruction of the Yadus has been seen by me even as I beheld before the carnage of those Kshatriyas who were the foremost ones of Kuru's race.

sn: नाहं विना यदुभिर्यादवानां पुरीमिमामशकं द्रष्टुमद्य॥ तपश्चरिष्यामि निबोध तन्मे रामेण सार्धं वनमभ्युपेत्य।
en: It is impossible for me to see this city of the Yadavs without the Yadus beside me. Know that going to the forest I shall practice penances with Rama in my company.

sn: इतीदमुक्त्वा शिरसा च पादौ संस्पृश्य कृष्णस्त्वरितो जगाम॥ ततो महान् निनदः प्रादुरासीत् सस्त्रीकुमारस्य पुरस्य तस्य।
en: Having said these words, Krishna touched the feet of his father with his head and quickly left him. Then a loud wail of sorrow arose from the ladies and children of his house,

sn: अथाब्रवीत् केशवः संनिवर्त्य शब्दं श्रुत्वा योषितां क्रोशतीनाम्॥ पुरीमिमामेष्यति सव्यसाची स वो दुःखान्मोचयिता नराग्र्यः।
en: Hearing that loud sound of wailing uttered by the weeping ladies, Keshava returned and said to them, Arjuna will come here. That foremost of men will relieve you of your sorrow.

sn: ततो गत्वा केशवस्तं ददर्श रामं वने स्थितमेकं विविक्ते॥ अथापश्यद् योगयुक्तस्य तस्य नागं मुखान्निश्चरन्तं महान्तम्।
en: Proceeding then to the forest, Keshava saw Rama sitting in a solitary place. He also saw that Rama had set himself to Yoga and that from out his mouth was issuing a powerful snake.

sn: श्वेतं ययौ स ततः प्रेक्ष्यमाणो महार्णवो येन महानुभावः॥ सहस्रशीर्षः पर्वताभोगवा रक्ताननः स्वां तनुं तां विमुच्य।।
en: The color of that snake was white. Leaving the human body, that great Naga, of a thousand heads and having a form as large as that of a mountain, endued besides with red eyes, proceeded along the way leading to the ocean.

sn: सम्यक् च तं सागरः प्रन्यगृह्णा नागा दिव्याः सरितश्चैव पुण्याः॥ कर्कोटको वासुकिस्तक्षकश्च पृथुश्रवा अरुणः कुञ्जरश्च। स्तथा नागो धृतराष्ट्रो महात्मा॥ नागश्रेष्ठो दुर्मुखश्चाम्बरीषः। स्वयं राजा वरुणश्चापि राजन्॥ प्रत्युद्गम्य स्वागतेनाभ्यनन्दं स्तेऽपूजयंश्चार्घ्यपाद्यक्रियाभिः।
en: Ocean himself, and many celestial snakes, and many sacred Rivers were there, for receiving him with honor. There Karkotaka, Vasuki, Takshaka, Prithushravas, and Varuna, Kunjara, Mishri, Shankha and Kumuda, and Pundarika, and the great Dhritarashtra, and Hrada and Kratha and Shitikantha of fierce energy, and chakramanda and Atishanda, and that foremost of Nagas called Durmukha, and Ambarisha, and king Varuna himself, O king. Advancing forward and offering him the Arghya and water to wash his feet, and with various other rites, they all adored the powerful Naga an saluted him by making the usual enquiries.

sn: ततो गते भ्रातरि वासुदेवो जानन् सर्वा गतयो दिव्यदृष्टिः॥ वने शून्ये विचरंश्चिन्तयानो भूमौ चाथ संविवेशाग्र्यतेजाः।
en: After his brother had thus gone from the (human) world, Vasudeva of celestial vision, who was fully acquainted with the end of all things, wandered for sometime in that solitary forest thoughtfully. Gifted with great energy he then sat down on the naked earth.

sn: सर्वं तेन प्राक्तदा वित्तमासीद् गान्धार्या यद् वाक्यमुक्तः स पूर्वम्॥ दुर्वाससा पायसोच्छिष्टलिप्ते यच्चाप्युक्तं तच सस्मार वाक्यम्।
en: He had thought before this of everything which had been foreshadowed by the words uttered by Gandhari in former days. He also recollected the words that Durvasas had spoken at the time his body was smeared by that Rishi with the residue of the Payasa he had eaten.

sn: स चिन्तयन्नन्धकवृष्णिनाशं कुरुक्षयं चैव महानुभावः॥ मेने ततः संक्रमणस्य कालं ततश्चकारेन्द्रियसंनिरोधम्।
en: The high-souled one, thinking of the destruction of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas, as also of the previous destruction of the Kurus, concluded that the hour (for his own departure from the world) had come. He then controlled his senses (in Yoga).

sn: मात्रेयवाक्यप्रतिपालनाय॥ निमित्तमैच्छत् सकलार्थतत्त्ववित्।
en: Knowing the truth of every topic, Vasudeva, though he was the Supreme Deity, wished to die for removing all doubts and establishing a certainty of results, simply for upholding the three worlds and for making the words of Atri's son true.

sn: स संनिरुद्धेन्द्रियवाङ्मनास्तु शिश्ये महायोगमुपेत्य कृष्णः॥ जराथ तं देशमुपाजगाम लुब्धस्तदानीं मृगलिप्सुरुग्रः।
en: Having controlled all his senses, speech, and mind Krishna laid himself down in high Yoga. A fierce hunter of the name of Jara then came there, for finding a deer.

sn: स केशवं योगयुक्तं शयानं मृगासक्तो लुब्धकः सायकेन॥ जराविध्यत् पादतले त्वरावां स्तं चाभितस्तज्जिघृक्षुर्जगाम।
en: The hunter mistaking Keshava, who was stretched on the earth in high Yoga, for a deer, pierced at him at the heel with an arrow and quickly came to that spot for capturing his prey.

sn: अथापश्यत् पुरुषं योगयुक्तं पीताम्बरं लुब्धकोऽनेकबाहुम्॥ मत्वाऽऽत्मानं त्वपराद्धं स तस्य पादौ जरा जगृहे शंकितात्मा।
en: Coming up, Jara saw a man dressed in yellow robes, rapt in Yoga, and gifted with many arms. considering himself an offender, and filled with fear, he touched the feet of Keshava.

sn: आश्वासयंस्तं महात्मा तदानीं गच्छन्नूचं रोदसी व्याप्य लक्ष्म्या॥
en: The high-souled one comforted him and then ascended upwards, filling the entire sky with splendour.

sn: दिवं प्राप्तं वासवोऽथाश्विनौ च रुद्रादित्या वसवश्चाथ विश्वे। प्रत्युद्ययुर्मुनयश्चापि सिद्धा गन्धर्वमुख्याश्च सहाप्सरोभिः॥
en: When he reached the celestial region, Vasava and the twin Ashvins and Rudra and the Adityas and and the Vasus and the Visuvedevas, and Munis and Siddhas and many foremost ones among the Gandharvas, with the Apsaras, advanced to receive him.

sn: ततो राजन् भगवानुग्रतेजा नारायणः प्रभवश्चाव्ययश्च। योगाचार्यो रोदसी व्याप्य लक्ष्म्या स्थान प्राप स्वं महात्माप्रमेयम्॥
en: Then, O king, the illustrious Narayana of dreadful energy, the Creator and Destroyer of all, that preceptor of Yoga-filling Heaven with his splendour, reached his own inconceivable region.

sn: ततो देवैर्ऋषिभिश्चापि कृष्णः समागतश्चारणैश्चैव राजन्। गन्धवौय्यैरप्सरोभिर्वराभिः सिद्धैः साध्यैश्चानतैः पूज्यमानः॥
en: Krishna then met the deities and (celestial) Rishis and Charanas, O king, and the foremost ones among the Gandharvas and many beautiful Apsaras and Siddhas and Saddhyas. All of them bending in humility, adored him.

sn: तं वै देवाः प्रत्यनन्दन्त राजन् मुनिश्रेष्ठा ऋम्भिरानचुरीशम्। तं गन्धर्वाश्चापि तस्थुः स्तुवन्तः प्रीत्या चैनं पुरुहूतोऽभ्यनन्दत्॥
en: The celestials all saluted him, O monarch, and many foremost of ascetics and Rishi adored him as the Lord of all. The Gandharvas waited on him, singing his praises, and Indra also joyfully praised him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच दारुकोऽपि कुरुन् गत्वा दृष्ट्वा पार्थान् महारथान्। आचष्ट मौसले वृष्णीनयोन्येनोपसंतान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Meanwhile Daruka, going to the Kurus and seeing those powerful car warriors, viz., the sons Pritha, informed them of how the Vrishnis had killed one another with iron bolts.

sn: श्रुत्वा विनष्टान् वार्ष्णेयान् सभोजान्धककौकुरान्। पाण्डवाः शोकसंतप्ता वित्रस्तमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: Hearing that the Vrishnis along with the Bhojas and Andhakas and Kukuras had all been killed, the Pandavas, burning with grief, became highly moved.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनस्तानामन्त्र्य केशवस्य प्रियः सखा। प्रययौ मातुलं द्रष्टुं नेदमस्तीनि चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the Arjuna, the dear friend of Keshava, bidding them farewell, started for seeing his maternal uncle. He said that destruction would soon overtake every thing.

sn: स वृष्णिनिलयं गत्वा दारुकेण सह प्रभो। ददर्श द्वारकां वीरो मृतनाथामिव स्त्रियम्॥
en: Proceeding to the city of the Vrishnis with Daruka in his company, O powerful king, that hero saw that the city of Dwraka looked liked a women left of her husband.

sn: याः स्म ता लोकनाथेन नाथवन्त्यः पुराभवन्। तास्त्वनाथास्तदा नाथं पार्थं दृष्ट्वा विचुक्रुशुः॥
en: Those ladies who had, before this, the very Lord of the universe for their protector, were now lordless. Seeing that Partha, had come for protecting them, they all bewailed aloud.

sn: षोडशस्त्रीसहस्राणि वासुदेवपरिग्रहः। तासमासीन्महान् नादो दृष्टैवार्जुनमागतम्॥
en: Sixteen thousand ladies had been wedded to Vasudeva. Indeed, as soon as they beheld Arjuna arrive, they uttered a loud cry of sorrow.

sn: तास्तु दृष्ट्वैव कौरव्यो बाष्पेणापिहितेक्षणः। हीनाः कृष्णेन पुत्रैश्च नाशकत् सोऽभिवीक्षितुम्॥
en: As soon as the Kuru prince met those beautiful ladies deprived of the protection of Krishna and of their sons as well he was unable to look at them, vision being obstructed by tears.

sn: स तां वृष्णयन्धकजलां हयमीनां रथोडुपाम्। वादित्ररथघोषौघां वेश्मतीर्थमहाह्रदाम्॥ रत्नशैवलसंघातां वज्रप्राकारमालिनीम्। रथ्यास्रोतोजलावर्तो चत्वरस्तिमिनहदाम्॥ रामकृष्णमहाग्राहां द्वारकां सहितं तदा। कालपाशग्रहां भीमा नदी वैतरणीमिव॥
en: The Dwraka-river had the Vrishnis and the Andhakas for its water, horses for its fishes, cars for its rafts, the sound of musical instruments and the rattle of cars for its wayes, houses and mansions and public squares for its lakes. Games and precious stones were its moss. The walls of adamant were the garlands of flowers that floated on it. The streets and roads were the strong currents running in eddies along its surface. The great open squares were the large lakes in its course. Rama and Krishna were its two mighty alligators. That agreeable river now seemed to Arjuna to be the dreadful Vaitarani bound up with Time's net.

sn: ददर्श वासविर्धीमान् विहीनां वृष्णिपुङ्गवैः। गतश्रियं निरानन्दा पद्मिनी शिशिरे यथा॥
en: Indeed, the son of Vasava, gifted with great intelligence, beheld the city to look even thus, reft as it was of the Vrishni heroes.

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा द्वारकां पार्थस्ताश्च कृष्णस्य योषितः। सस्वनं वाष्पमुत्सृज्य निपपात महीतले॥
en: Shorn of beauty, and perfectly cheerless, it presented the aspect of a lotus flower in the season of winter. Seeing the sight that Dwraka presented, and seeing the numerous wives of Krishna, Arjuna bewailed aloud with eyes bathed in tears and fell down on the earth.

sn: सात्राजिती ततः सत्या रुक्मिणी च विशाम्पते। अभिपत्य प्ररुरुदुः परिवार्य धनञ्जयम्॥
en: Then Satya the daughter of Satrajit, and Rukmini too, O king, fell down beside Dhananjaya and bewailed.

sn: ततस्तं काञ्चने पीठे समुत्थाप्योपवेश्य च। अब्रुवन्त्यो महात्मानं परिवार्योपतस्थिरे॥
en: Raising him then they caused him to be seated on a golden seat. The ladies sat around that great one, giving expression to their feelings.

sn: ततः संस्तूय गोविन्दं कथयित्वा च पाण्डवः। आश्वास्य ताः स्त्रियश्चापि मातुलं द्रष्टुमभ्यगात्॥
en: Praising Govinda and talking with the ladies, the son of Pandu comforted them and then proceeded to see his maternal uncle.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तं शयानं महात्मानं वीरमानकदुन्दुभिम्। पुत्रशोकेन संतप्तं ददर्श कुरुपुङ्गवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said, The Kuru prince saw the heroic and great Anakadundubhi lying on the ground, and burning with grief on account of his sons.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: तस्याश्रुपरिपूर्णाक्षो व्यूढोरस्को महाभुजः। आर्तस्यार्ततरः पार्थः पादौ जग्राह भारत॥
en: The broad-chested and mighty-armed son of Pritha, more afflicted than his uncle with his eyes bathed in tears, touched his uncle's feet, O Bharata.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: तस्य मूर्धानमाघ्रातुमियेषानकदुन्दुभिः। स्वस्रीयस्य महाबाहुर्न शशाक च शत्रुहन्॥
en: The mighty-armed Anakadundubhi wished to smell the head of his sister's son, but could not do it, O destroyer of enemies.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: समालिङ्गग्यार्जुनं वृद्धः स भुजाभ्यां महाभुजः। रुदन् पुत्रान् स्मरन् सर्वान् विललाप सुविह्वलः॥ भ्रातन पुत्रांश्च पौत्रांश्च दौहित्रान् ससखीनपि।
en: The old man of mighty-arms, deeply afflicted embraced Partha with his arms and wept aloud, remembering his sons, brothers grandsons, daughter's sons, and friends.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: वासुदेव उवाच यैर्जिता भूमिपालाश्च दैत्याश्च शतशोऽर्जुन॥ तान् दृष्ट्वा नेह पश्यामि जीवाम्यर्जुन दुर्मरः।
en: Vasudeva said Without seeing those heroes, O Arjuna who had subjugated all the kings of the Earth and the Daityas a hundred time, I am still alive! I see, that I cannot die!

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: यौ तावर्जुन शिष्यौ ते प्रियौ बहुमतौ सदा॥ तयोरपनयात् पार्थ वृष्णयो निधनं गताः।
en: Those two heroes who were the dear disciples of Arjuna, and who were much were course respected by him, alas, O Partha, through their fault, the Vrishnis have been destroyed.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: यौ तौ वृष्णिप्रवीराणां द्वावेवातिरथौ मतौ॥ प्रद्युस्रो युयुधानश्च कथयन् कत्थसे च यौ। तौ सदा कुरुशार्दूल कृष्णस्य प्रियभाजनौ॥ तावुभौ वृष्णिनाशस्य मुखमास्तां धनञ्जय।
en: Those two who considered as Atirathas amongst the foremost of the Vrishnis, and referring to whom in of conversation you were wont to indulge in pride, and who, O chief of Kuru's race, were ever dear to Krishna himself, alas, those tow, O Dhananjaya, have been the chief causes of the Destruction of the Vrishnis.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: तु गर्हामि शैनेयं हार्दिक्यं चाहमर्जुन॥ अक्रूरं रौक्मिणेयं च शापो ह्येवात्र कारणम्।
en: I do not censure the son of Shini or the son of Hridika, O Arjuna! I do not censure Akrura or the son of Rukmini. No doubt, the curse (of the Rishis) is the sole cause.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: केशिनं यस्तु कंसं च विक्रम्य जगतः प्रभुः॥ विदेहावकरोत् पार्थ चैद्यं च बलगर्वितम्। नैषादिमेकलव्यं च चक्रे कालिङ्गमागधान्॥ गान्धारान् काशिराजं च मरुभूमौ च पार्थिवान्। प्राच्यांश्च दाक्षिणात्यांश्च पर्वतीयांस्तथा नृपान्॥ सोऽभ्युपेक्षितवानेतमनयान्मधुसूदनः।
en: How is it what that lord of the universe, viz., the destroyer of Madhu, who had shown his prowess for killing Keshin, Kansa, and Chaidya swelling with pride, and Ekalavya the son of the king of the Nishadas, and the Kalingas and the Magadhas, and the Gandharas and the king of Kashi, and many rulers assembled together in the midst of the desert, many heroes belonging to the East and the South, and many kings of the mountainous regions, alas, how could he remain indifferent to such a calamity as the curse denounced by the Rishis?

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: त्वं हि तं नारदश्चैव मुनयश्च सनातनम्॥ गोविन्दमनघं देवमभिजानीध्वमच्युतम्।
en: Yourself, Narada, and the Munis, knew him to be the eternal and sinless Govinda, the Deity of unfading glory.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: प्रत्यपश्यच्च स विभुञ्जतिक्षयमधोक्षजः॥ समुपेक्षितवान् नित्यं स्वयं स मम पुत्रकः।
en: Alas, being powerful Vishnu himself, he saw without interfering, the destruction of his kinsmen! My son must have himself allowed all this to happen.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: गान्धार्या वचनं यत् तदृषीणां च परंतप॥ तन्नूनमन्यथा कर्तुं नैच्छत् स जगतः प्रभुः।
en: He was the Lord of the universe. He did not, however, wish to falsity the words of Gandhari and the Rishis, o destroyer of enemies.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: प्रत्यक्षं भवतश्चापि तव पौत्रः परंतप॥ अश्वत्थाम्ना हतश्चापि जीवितस्तस्य तेजसा।
en: Before the very eyes, O hero, your grandson, who had been killed by Ashvatthaman was revived through his energy.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: इमांस्तु नैच्छत् स्वाज्ञातीन् रक्षितुं च सखा तव।।१७। ततः पुत्रांश्च पौत्रांश्च भ्रातृनथ सखींस्तथा। शयानान् निहतान् दृष्ट्वा ततो मामब्रवीदिदम्॥ सम्प्राप्तोऽद्यायमस्यान्तः कुलस्य भरतर्षभ।
en: That friend, however, of yours did not wish to protect his kinsmen. Seeing his sons and grandson and brothers and friends lying dead, he said to me these words, O Bharata's race. The destruction of this our family has at last come.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: आगमिष्यति बीभत्सुरिमां द्वारवतीं पुरीम्॥ आख्येयं तस्य यद् वृत्तं वृष्णीनां वैशसं महत्।
en: Vibhatsa will come to this city, viz., Dvaravati. Tell him what has taken place viz., this great destruction of the Vrishnis.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: स तु श्रुत्वा महातेजा यदूनां निधनं प्रभो॥ आगन्ता क्षिप्रमेवेह न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा।
en: I have no doubt that as soon as he will hear of the destruction of the Yadus, that hero of mighty energy will come here forthwith.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: योऽहं तमर्जुनं विद्धि योऽर्जुनः सोऽहमेव तु॥ यद् ब्रूयात् तत् तथा कार्यमिति बुद्ध्यस्व भारत।
en: Know, O father, that I Arjuna and Arjuna is myself. That should be down by you which he would say.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: स स्त्रीषु प्राप्तकालासु पाण्डवो बालकेषु च॥ प्रतिपत्स्यति बीभत्सुर्भवतश्चौर्ध्वदेहिकम्।
en: Tile son of Pandu will do what is best for the women and the children. Even he will perform your funeral rites.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: इमां च नगरी सद्यः प्रतियाते धनञ्जये॥ प्राकाराट्टालकोपेतां समुद्रः प्लावयिष्यति।
en: This city of Dvaravati, after Arjuna's departure, will, with its walls and edifices, be speedily swallowed up by the ocean.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: अहं देशे तु कस्मिंश्चित् पुण्ये नियममास्थितः॥ कालं कर्ता सत्य एव रामेण सह धीमता।
en: As for myself retiring to some sacred place, I shall pass my time with the intelligent Rama in my company, observing strict vows all the while.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशो मामचिन्त्यपराक्रमः॥ हित्वा मां बालकैः सार्धं दिशं कामप्यगात् प्रभुः।
en: Having said these words to me, Hrishikesha of inconceivable prowess, leaving me with the children, has gone away some where which I do not know.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: सोऽहं तौ च महात्मानौ चिन्तयन् भ्रातरौ तव।॥ घोरं ज्ञातिवधं चैव न भुञ्जे शोककर्शितः।
en: Thinking of those two great brothers of yours as also of the dreadful destruction of my kinsmen, I have abstained from all food, and am emaciated with grief.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: न भोक्ष्ये न च जीविष्ये दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि पाण्डव।। यदुक्तं पार्थ कृष्णेन तत् सर्वमखिलं कुरु।
en: I shall neither eat, nor live. By good luck you meet me, O son of Pandu. Do you accomplish all, O Partha, that Krishna has said.

description: Arjuna starts to see his maternal uncle
sn: एतत् ते पार्थ राज्यं च स्त्रियो रत्नानि चैव हि।। इष्टान् प्राणानहं हीमांस्त्यक्ष्यामि रिपुसूदन॥
en: This kingdom, with all these women, and all the wealth here, is your now, O son of Pritha! As for myself, O destroyer of foes, I shall renounce my life however dear it may be.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः स बीभत्सुर्मातुलेन परंतप। दुर्मना दीनवदनो वसुदेवमुवाच ह॥ नाहं वृष्णिप्रवीरेण बन्धुभिश्चैव मातुल। विहीनां पुथिवीं द्रष्टुं शक्यामीह कथंचन।॥
en: Vaishampayana said, That scorcher of enemies, viz., Bibhatsu, thus addressed by his maternal uncle, replied, with great cheerlessness of heart, to Vasudeva who was equally cheerless, saying, 'O uncle, I ma unable to look at this Earth when she is reft of that hero of Vrishni' rare and those my other kinsmen.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: राजा च भीमसेनश्च सहदेवश्च पाण्डवः। नकुलो याज्ञसेनी च षडेकमनसो वयम्॥
en: The king and Bhimasena and Sahadeva and Nakula and Yajnaseni, are of the same mind with myself in this matter.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: राज्ञः संक्रमणे चापि कालोऽयं वर्तते ध्रुवम्। तमिमं विद्धि सम्प्राप्तं कालं कालविदां वर॥
en: The time has come for the departure of the king also. Know this that the hour of our departure too is near. You are the foremost of those who are well conversant with the course of time.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: सर्वथा वृष्णिदारास्तु बालं वृद्धं तथैव च। नयिष्ये परिगृह्याहमिन्द्रप्रस्थमरिंदम॥
en: I shall, however, O chastiser of enemies, first remove to Indraprastha the women of the Vrishni race as also the children and the aged.'

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: इत्युक्त्वा दारुकमिदं वाक्यमाह धनञ्जयः। अमात्यान् वृष्णिवीराणां द्रष्टुमिच्छामि मा चिरम्।।६।
en: Having said so to his uncle, Arjuna, next addressed Daruka, saying, I wish to see forthwith the chief officers of the Vrishni heroes.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: शक्रप्रस्थमहं नेष्ये इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं सुधर्मं यादवी सभाम्। प्रविवेशार्जुनः शूरः शोचमानो महारथान्॥
en: Having uttered these words, the heroic Arjuna, grieving for those great car-warriors, entered the great hall of the Yadavas, called Sudharma.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तमासनगतं तत्र सर्वाः प्रकृतयस्तथा। ब्राह्मणा नैगमास्तत्र परिवार्योपतस्थिरे।॥
en: When he had taken his seat here, all the citizens, including the Brahmanas, and all the ministers of state, came and stood surrounding him.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तान् दीनमनसः सर्वान् विमूढान् गतचेतसः। उवाचेदं वचः काले पार्थो दीनतरस्तथा॥
en: Then Partha, more grieved than they, addressed those grieving and cheerless citizens and officers who were more dead than alive, and said these words which were well suited to the occasion.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: वृष्ण्यन्धकजनं स्वयम्। इदं तु नगरं सर्वं समुद्रः प्लावयिष्यति॥
en: I shall take away with me the remnants of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas! The sea will soon engulf this city.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: सज्जीकुरुत यानानि रत्नानि विविधानि च। वज्रोऽयं भवतां राजा शक्रप्रस्थे भविष्यति॥
en: Equip all your cars and place on them all your riches. This Vajra will be your king at Shakraprastha.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: सप्तपे दिवसे चैव रवौ विमल उद्गते। बहिर्वत्स्यामहे सर्वे सज्जीभवत मा चिरम्॥
en: On the seventh day from this, at sunrise, we shall start. Make your preparations immediately.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: इत्युक्तास्तेन ते सर्वे पार्थेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। सज्जमाशु ततश्चक्रुः स्वसिद्ध्यर्थं समुत्सुकाः॥
en: Thus addressed by Pritha's son of Pure deeds, all of them hastened their preparations with eagerness for securing their safety.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तां रात्रिमवसत् पार्थः केशवस्य निवेशने। महता शोकमोहेन सहसाभिपरिप्लुतः॥
en: Arjuna passed that night in the palaces of Keshava. He was suddenly overwhelmed with great sorrow and stupefaction.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: श्वोभूतेऽथ ततः शौरिर्वसुदेवः प्रतापवान। युक्त्वाऽऽत्मानं महातेजा जगाम गतिमुत्तमाम्॥
en: When morning dawned, Vasudeva of great energy and prowess attained, through the help of Yoga, to the highest end.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततः शब्दो महानासीद् वसुदेवनिवेशने। दारुणः क्रोशतीनां च रुदतीनां च योषिताम्॥
en: A loud and heart-rendering sound of wailing was heard in Vasudeva's palace, uttered by the weeping ladies.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: प्रकीर्णमूर्धजाः सर्वा विमुक्ताभरणस्रजः। उरांसि पाणिभिर्जन्त्यो व्यलपन् करुणं स्त्रियः॥
en: They were seen with disheveled hair and divested of ornaments and garlands Beating their breasts with their hands, the indulged in heart-rendering lamentations.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तं देवकी च भद्रा च रोहिणी मदिरा तथा। अन्वारोहन्त च तदा भर्तारं योषितां वराः॥
en: Those foremost of women, viz., Devaki and Bhadra and Rohini and Madira threw themselves on the bodies of threw themselves on the bodies of their lord.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततः शौरि नृयुक्तेन बहुमूल्येन भारत। यानेन महता पार्थो बहिर्निष्क्रामयत् तदा॥
en: Then Partha caused the body of his uncle lo be carried out on a rich vehicle borne on the shoulders of men.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तमन्वयुस्तत्र तत्र दुःखशोकसमन्विताः। द्वारकावासिनः सर्वे पौरजानपदा हिताः॥
en: It was followed by all the citizens of Dwraka and the people of the provinces all of whom greatly stricken with grief, had been disposed towards the deceased hero.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तस्याश्वमेधिकं छत्रं दीप्यमानाश्च पावकाः। पुरस्तात् तस्य यानस्य याजकाश्च ततो ययुः॥
en: Before that vehicle were born the umbrella which had been held over his head at the conclusion of the horse-sacrifice he had performed while living and also the burning fires he had daily adored, with the priests who had used to attend to them.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: अनुजग्मुश्च तं वीरं देव्यस्ता वै स्वलंकृताः। स्त्रीसहस्रः परिवृता वधूभिश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: The body of the hero was followed by his wives decked in ornaments and surrounded by thousands of women and thousands of their daughter-in-law.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: यस्तु देशः प्रियस्तस्य जीवतोऽभून्महात्मनः। तत्रैनमुपसंकल्प्य पितृमेधं प्रचक्रिरे॥
en: The last rites were then performed at that spot which he liked while he was alive

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तं चिताग्निगतं वीरं शूरपुत्रं वराङ्गनाः। ततोऽन्वारुरुहुः पत्न्यश्चतस्रः पतिलोकगाः॥
en: The four wives of that heroic son of Shura ascended the funeral pyre and were consumed with the body of their husband. All of them attained to those happy regions which were his.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तं वै चतसृभिः स्त्रीभिरन्वितं पाण्डुनन्दनः। अदाहयच्चदनैश्च गन्धैरुच्चावचैरपि।॥
en: The son of Pandu burnt the body of his uncle together with those four wives of his, using various kinds of scents and perfumed wood.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततः प्रादुरभूच्छब्दः समिद्धस्य विभावसोः। सामगानां च निर्घोषो नराणां रुदतामपि॥
en: As the funeral pyre blazed up, a loud sound was heard of the burning wood and other combustible materials, along with the clear chant of Samans and the lamentation of the citizens and others who saw the rite.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततो वज्रप्रधानास्ते वृष्ण्यन्धककुमारकाः। सर्वे चैवोदकं चक्रुः स्त्रियश्चैव महात्मनः॥
en: After it was all over, the boys of the Vrishnis and Andhaka races, headed by Vajra, as also the ladies, offered oblations of water to the great hero.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: अलुप्तधर्मस्तं धर्मं कारयित्वा स फाल्गुनः। जगाम वृष्णयो यत्र विनष्टा भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Phalguna, who was careful in observing every duty having caused this duty to be performed, went. O chief of Bharata's race, next to the place where the Vrishnis were killed.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: स तान् दृष्ट्वा निपतितान् कदने भृशदुः :खितः। बभूवातीव कौरव्यः प्राप्तकालं चकार ह॥
en: The Kuru prince, seeing them lying killed all around, became exceedingly cheerless. He, however did what required to be done in view of that which had taken place.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: यथा प्रधानतश्चैव चक्रे सर्वास्तथा क्रियाः। ये हता ब्रह्मशापेन मुसलैरेरकोद्भवैः॥
en: The last rites were performed, according to the order of seniority, to the bodies of those heroes killed by the iron bolts born, by virtue of the curse denounced by the Brahmanas, of the blades of Eraka grass.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततः शरीरे रामस्य वासुदेवस्य चोभयोः। अन्विष्य दाहयामास पुरुषैराप्तकारिभिः॥
en: Searching out the bodies then of Rama and Vasudeva, Arjuna caused them to be burnt by expert persons.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: स तेषां विधिवत् कृत्वा प्रेतकार्याणि पाण्डवः। सप्तमे दिवसे प्रायाद् रथमारुह्य सत्वरः॥
en: The son of Pandu, having next perforined duly those rites that are done to the manes of the dead, quickly started on the seventh day, mounting on his car.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: अश्वयुक्तै रथैश्चापि गोखरोष्ट्रयुतैरपि। स्त्रियस्ता वृष्णिवीराणां रुदत्यः शोककर्शिताः॥
en: The windows of the Vrishni heroes wailing aloud, followed the great son of Pandu, viz., Dhananjaya, on cars drawn by bullocks and mules and camels.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं पाण्डुपुत्रं धनञ्जयम्। भृत्याश्चान्धकवृष्णीनां सादिनो रथिनश्च ये॥
en: All were in deep sorrow. The servants of the Vrishnis, their horsemen, and their carwarriors too, followed the procession.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: वीरहीनं वृद्धबालं पौरजानपदास्तथा। ययुस्ते परिवार्याथ कलत्रं पार्थशासनात्॥
en: The citizens and the inhabitants of the country, at the command of Pritha's son, started at the same time and proceeded, surrounding that cavalcade destitute of heroes and numbering only women and the aged and the children.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: कुञ्जरैश्च गजारोहा ययुः शैलनिभैस्तथा। सपादरक्षैः संयुक्ताः सान्तरायुधिका ययुः॥
en: The warriors who fought from the backs of elephants proceeded on elephants as huge as hills. The infanty also set out, together with the reserves.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: पुत्राश्चान्धकवृष्णीनां सर्वे पार्थमनुव्रताः। ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया: वैश्याः शूद्राश्चैव महाधनाः॥ दश षट् च सहस्राणि वासुदेवावरोधनम्। पुरस्कृत्य ययुर्वजं पौत्रं कृणस्य धीमतः॥
en: The children of the Andhaka, and the Vrishni races, all followed Arjuna. The Brahmanas and Kshatriyas and Vaishyas, and rich Shudras, started keeping before them the sixteen thousand women who had formed Vasudeva's harem and Vajra, the grandson of the intelligent Krishna.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: बहूनि च सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च। भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकस्त्रीणां हतनाथानि निर्ययुः॥
en: The widows of the other heroes of the Bhoja, the Vrishni and the Andhaka races, lordless now, that started with Arjuna, numbered many millions.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तत्सागरसमप्रख्यं वृष्णिचक्रं महर्धिमत्। उवाह रथिनां श्रेष्ठः पार्थः परपुरंजयः॥
en: That foremost of car-warriors, that conqueror of hostile towns viz., the son of Pritha, escorted this huge procession of Vrishnis, which still abounded with wealth, and which looked like a veritable ocean.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: निर्याते तु जने तस्मिन् सागरो मकरालयः। द्वारकां रत्नसम्पूर्णो जलेनाप्लावयत् तदा॥
en: After all the people had started, the ocean, the home of sharks, and alligators, flooded Dwraka, which still teemed with riches of every kind, with its waters.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: यद् यद्धि पुरुषव्याघ्रो भूमेस्तस्या व्यमुञ्चत। तत् तत् सम्लावयामास सलिलेन स सागरः॥
en: Whatever portion of the ground was passed over, ocean immediately flooded over with his waters.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तदद्भुतमभिप्रेक्ष्य द्वारकावासिनो जनाः। तूर्णात् तूर्णतरं जग्मुरहो दैवमिति ब्रुवन्॥
en: Seeing this wonderful spectacle, the inhabitants of Dwraka walked faster and faster, saying. Wonderful is the course of fate.'

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: काननेषु च रम्येषु पर्वतेषु नदीषु च। निवसन्नानयामास वृष्णिदारान् धनञ्जयः॥
en: Dhananjaya, after abandoning Dwraka, proceeded by slow marches, causing the Vrishni women to rest in charming forests and mountain and by the sides of delightful rivers.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: स पञ्चनदमासाद्य धीमानतिसमृद्धिमत्। देशे गोपशुधान्याढ्ये निवासमकरोत् प्रभुः॥
en: Arrived at the country of the five waters, the powerful Dhananjaya encamped in the midst of a land that abounded with corn and kine and other animals.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततो लोभः समभवद् दस्यूनां निहतेश्वराः। दृष्ट्वा स्त्रियो नीयमानाः पार्थेनैकेन भारत॥
en: Seeing those widows escorted by Pritha's son alone, O Bharata, the robbers felt a great temptation.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततस्ते पामकर्माणो लोभोपहतचेतसः। आभीरा मन्त्रयामासुः समेत्याशुभदर्शनाः॥
en: Then those sinful wretches, with hearts possessed by cupidity, viz., those Abhiras of ill omen, assembled together and held consultation.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: अयमेकोऽर्जुनो धन्वी वृद्धबालं हतेश्वरम्। नयत्यस्मानतिक्रम्य योधाश्चमे हतौजसः॥
en: They said, 'Here there is only one bowman, viz., Arjuna. The party consists of children and the old. He escorts them alone. The warriors (of the Vrishnis) are without energy.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततो यष्टिप्रहरणा दस्यवस्ते सहस्रशः। अभ्यधावान्त वृष्णीनां तं जनं लोप्पहारिणः॥
en: Then those robbers, numbering by thousands, and armed with clubs, rushed a towards the procession of the Vrishnis for looting them.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: महता सिंहनादेन त्रासयन्तः पृथग्जनम्। अभिपेतुर्वधार्थं ते कालपर्यायचोदिताः॥
en: Urged by the perverse course of time, they fell upon that party, frightening it will loud leonine shouts and desirous of slaughter.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततो निवृत्तः कौन्तेयः सहसा सपदानुगः। उवाच तान् महाबाहुरर्जुनः प्रहसन्निव॥ निवर्तध्वमधर्मज्ञा यदि जीवितुमिच्छथा इदानीं शरनिर्भिन्नाः शोचध्वं निहता मया॥
en: The son of Kunti, suddenly ceasing to advance along the path, turned, with his followers, towards the place where the robbers had attacked the party. Smiling the while, that mighty-armed warrior addressed the assailants, saying. “You sinful wretches, stop, if you love your lives! You will rue this when I cut your bodies with my arrows and take your lives.'

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: तथोक्तास्तेन वीरेण कद कृत्य तद्वचः। अभिपेतुर्जनं मूढा वार्यमाणाः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Though thus addressed by that hero, they disregarded his words, and though repeatedly dissuaded, they fell upon Arjuna.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततोऽर्जुनो धनुर्दिव्यं गाण्डीवमजरं महत्। आरोपयितुमारेभे यत्नादिव कथंचन॥
en: Then Arjuna tried to string his large, indestructible, celestial bow with some effort.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: चकार सज्जं कृछ्रेण सम्भ्रमे तुमुले सति। चिन्तयामास शस्त्राणि न च सस्मार तान्यपि॥
en: He succeeded with great difficulty in stringing it, when the battle had become furious. He then began to think of his celestial weapons but they would not come to his mind.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: वैकृतं तन्महद् दृष्ट्वा भुजवीर्यं तथा युधि। दिव्यानां च महास्त्राणां विनाशाद् व्रीडितोऽभवत्॥५६
en: Seeing that furious battle, the loss of the might of his arm, and the non appearance of his celestial weapons, Arjuna became greatly ashamed.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: वृष्णियोधाश्च ते सर्वे गजाश्वरथयोधिनः। न शेकुरावर्तयितुं ह्रियमाणं च तं जनम्॥
en: The Vrishni warriors including the infantry, the elephant-warriors, and the car-men, failed to rescue those Vrishni women who were being snatched away by the robbers.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: कलत्रस्य बहुत्वाद्धि सम्पतत्सु ततस्ततः। प्रयत्नमकरोत् पार्थो जनस्य परिरक्षणे॥
en: The concourse was very large. The robbers attacked it, at different points. Arjuna tried his best to protect it, but could not succeed.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: मिषतां सर्वयोधानां ततस्ताः प्रमदोत्तमाः। समन्ततोऽवकृष्यन्त कामाच्चान्याः प्रवव्रजुः॥
en: Before the eyes of all the warriors, many foremost of ladies were dragged away, while others went away with the robbers of their own accord.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततो गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तैः शरैः पार्थो धनञ्जयः। जघान दस्यून् सोद्वेगो वृष्णिभृत्यैः सहस्रशः॥
en: The powerful Arjuna, supported by the servants of the Vrishnis, struck the robbers with arrows shot off Gandiva.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: क्षणेन तस्य ते राजन् क्षयं जग्मुरजिह्मगाः। अक्षयाहि पुरा भूत्वा क्षीणा: क्षतजभोजनाः॥
en: Soon, however, O king, is arrows were exhausted. In former days his arrows had been inexhaustible. Now, however, they proved otherwise.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: स शरक्षयमासाद्य दुःखशोकसमाहतः। धनुष्कोट्या तदा दस्यूनवधीत् पाकशासनिः॥
en: Finding his arrows exhausted, he became deeply afflicted with grief. The son of Indra then began to strike the robbers with the horns of his bow.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: प्रेक्षतस्त्वेव पार्थस्य वृष्णयन्धकवरस्त्रियः। जग्मुरादाय ते म्लेच्छाः समन्ताज्जनमेजय॥
en: Those Mlechcchas, however, O Janamejaya, in the very sight of Partha, retreated, taking away with the many foremost ladies of the Vrishnis and Andhakas.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: धनञ्जयस्तु दैवं तन्मनसाऽचिन्तयत् प्रभुः। दुःखशोकसमाविष्टो निःश्वासपरमोऽभवत्॥ अस्त्राणां च प्रणाशेन बाहुवीर्यस्य संक्षयात्। धनुषश्चाविधेयत्वाच्छराणां संक्षयेण च॥
en: The powerful Dhananjaya considered it all as the work of destiny. Filled with sorrow he breathed heavy sights, at the thought of the non-appearance of his (celestial) weapons, the loss of the might of his arms, the refusal of his bow to obey him; and the exhaustion of his arrows.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: बभूव विमनाः पार्थो दैवमित्यनुचिन्तयन्। न्यवर्तत ततो राजन् नेदमस्तीति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Considering it all as the work of destiny, he became greatly cheerless. He then ceased, O king, to make further efforts, saying, he had not the power which he had before.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततः शेषं समादाय कलत्रस्य महामतिः। हतभूयिष्ठरत्नस्य कुरुक्षेत्रमवातरत्॥
en: The high-souled one, taking with him the residue of the Vrishni women, and the wealth that was still with them, reached Kurukshetra,

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: एवं कलत्रमानीय वृष्णीनां हतशेषितम्। न्यवेशयत कौरव्यस्तत्र तत्र धनञ्जयः॥
en: Thus bringing with him the remnant of the Vrishnis, Dhananjaya established them at different places.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: हार्दिक्यतनयं पार्थो नगरे मार्तिकावतम्। भोजराजकलत्रं च हृतशेषं नरोत्तमः॥
en: He established the son of Kritavarman at the city called Marttikavat, with the remnant of the women of the Bhoja king.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: ततो वृद्धांश्च बालांश्च स्त्रियश्चादाय पाण्डवः। वीरैर्विहीनान् सर्वांस्ताशक्रप्रस्थे न्यवेशयत्॥
en: Escorting the remainder, with children and old men, and women, the son of Pandu established them, who were reft of heroes, in the city of Indraprastha.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: यौयुधानि सरस्वत्यां पुत्रं सात्यकिन: प्रियम्। न्यवेशयत धर्मात्मा वृद्धबालपुरस्कृतम्॥
en: The dear son of Yuyudhana, with a number of old men and children and women, the righteous-souled Arjuna established on the banks of the Sarasvati.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: इन्द्रप्रस्थे ददौ राज्यं वज्राय परवीरहा। वज्रेणाङ्करदारास्तु वार्यमाणाः प्रवव्रजुः॥
en: The rule of Indraprastha was given to Vajra. The widows of Akrura then wished to retire into the forest. Vajra asked them repeatedly to desist, but they did not hear him.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: रुक्मिणी त्वथ गान्धारी शैव्या हैमवतीत्यपि। देवी जाम्बवती चैव विविशुर्जातवेदसम्॥
en: Rukmini, the princess of Gandhara, Shaivya. Haimavati, and queen Jambavati, ascended the funeral pyre.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: सत्यभामा तथैवान्या देव्यः कृष्णस्य सम्मताः। वनं प्रविविशू राजस्तापस्ये कृतनिश्चयाः॥
en: Satyabhama and the other dear wives of Krishna entered the forest, o king, resolved to practice penances.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: द्वारकावासिनो ये तु पुरुषाः पार्थमभ्ययुः। यथार्ह संविभज्यैनान् वजे पर्यददज्जयः॥
en: Those men who had followed Arjuna from Dvaravati, were divided into groups, and bestowed upon Vajra.

description: Arjuna's departure from Dvaravati and his adventures in the Land of the Five Rivers
sn: स तत् कृत्वा प्राप्तकालं बाष्येणापिहितोऽर्जुनः। कृष्णद्वैपायनं व्यासं ददर्शासीनमाश्रमे॥
en: Having done all these acts suited to the occasion. Arjuna, with eyes bathed in tears, then entered the hermitage of Vyasa. There he saw the Dvaipayana seated at his ease.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रविशन्नर्जुनो राजन्नाश्रमं सत्यवादिनः। ददर्शासीनमेकान्ते मुनि सत्यवतीसुतम्॥
en: As Arjuna entered the hermitage of the truthful Rishi, he saw the son of Satyavati seated in a solitary spot.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: स तमासाद्य धर्मज्ञमुपतस्थे महाव्रतम्। अर्जुनोऽस्मीति नामास्मै निवेद्याभ्यवदत् ततः॥
en: Approaching that Rishi of high vows and gifted with a knowledge of al duties, he said, 'I am Arjuna'-~and then awaited his pleasure.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: स्वागतं तेऽस्त्विति प्राह मुनिः सत्यवतीसुतः। आस्यतामिति होवाच प्रसन्नात्मा महामुनिः॥
en: Satyavati's son, endued with high penances, answered, saying, "Welcome!' Of tranquil soul the great ascetic further said, 'Take our seat.'

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: तमप्रतीतमनसं निःश्वसन्तं पुनः पुनः निर्विण्णमनसं दृष्ट्वा पार्थं व्यासोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ नखकेशदशाकुम्भवारिणा किं समुक्षितः। आवीरजानुगमनं ब्राह्मणो वा हतस्त्वया॥
en: Seeing that the son of Pritha was greatly cheerless and breathing heavy sighs repeatedly and filled with despair, Vyasa, addressed him, saying——Have you been sprinkled with water from anybody's nails or hair or the end of anybody's cloth, or from the mouth of a jar? Did you know any woman before the cessation of her menses? Have you killed a Brahmana?

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: युद्धे पराजितो वासि गतश्रीरिव लक्ष्यसे। न त्वां प्रभिन्नं जानामि किमिदं भरतर्षभ॥ श्रोतव्यं चेन्मया पार्थ क्षिप्रमाख्यातुमर्हसि।
en: Have you been defeated in battle? You look like one shorn of prosperity! I do not know that you have been defeated by any one. Why then, O chief Bharata's race, this exceedingly dejected look! You should O of Pritha, tell me all, if, indeed, there be no harm in telling it.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: अर्जुन उवाच यः स मेघवपुः श्रीमान् बृहत्पंकजलोचनः॥ स कृष्ण: सह रामेण त्यक्त्वा देहं दिवं गतः। (तद्वाक्यस्पर्शनालोकसुखं त्वमृतसंतिभम्। संस्मृत्य देवदेवस्य प्रमुह्याम्यमृतात्मनः॥) मौसले बृष्णिवीराणां विनाशो ब्रह्मशापजः॥
en: Arjuna said He whose complexion was like that of a cloud, he whose eyes were like pair of large lotus petals, viz., Krishna has, with Rama, renounced his body and ascended to heaven.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: बभूव वीरान्तकरः प्रभासे लोमहर्षणः। एते शूरा महात्मानः सिंहदर्पा महाबलाः॥
en: At Prabhasa, through iron bolts caused by the curse denounced by Brahmanas, the destruction has taken place of the Vrishni heroes. That destruction has been awful and not even a single hero has escaped,

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: भोजवृष्ण्यन्धका ब्रह्मन्नन्योन्यं तैर्हतं युधि। गदापरिघशक्तीनां सहाः परिघबाहवः॥ त एरकाभिर्निहताः पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्। हतं पञ्चशतं तेषां सहस्रं बाहुशालिनाम्॥ निधनं समनुप्राप्तं समासाद्येतरेतरम्।
en: The heroes of the Bhoja, the Andhaka, and the Vrishni races, O Brahmana, who were all gifted with high-souls, great might, and leonine pride, have killed one another in battle. Possessed of arms which looked like maces of iron, and capable of bearing the strokes of heavy clubs and darts, alas they have all been killed with blades of Eraka grass. See the perverse course of Time. Five hundred thousand mighty-armed warriors have thus been killed. Encountering one another, they have met with destruction.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: पुनः पुनर्न मृष्यामि विनाशममितौजसाम्॥ चिन्तयानो यदूनां च कृष्णस्य च यशस्विनः।
en: Thinking repeatedly of this destruction of the Yadava warriors of immeasurable energy and of the illustrious Krishna, I cannot get peace of mind.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: शोषणं सागरस्येव पर्वतस्येव चालनम्॥ नभसः पतनं चैव शैत्यमग्नेस्तथैव च। अश्रद्धेयमहं मन्ये विनाशं शार्ङ्गधन्वनः॥ न चेह स्थातुमिच्छामि लोके कृष्णविनाकृत्।
en: The death of the holder of Sharnga is as incredible as the drying up of the ocean, the displacement of a mountain, the falling down of the heaven, or the cooling property of fie. Deprived of the company of the Vrishni heroes, I wish not to live in this world.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: इतः कष्टतरं चान्यच्छृणु तद् वै तपोधन॥ मनो मे दीर्यते येन चिन्तयानस्य वै मुहुः।
en: Another event has taken place that is more painful than this, O you having penances for wealth. Repeatedly thinking of it, my heart is breaking.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: पश्यतो वृष्णिदाराश्च मम ब्रह्मन् सहस्रशः॥ आभीरैरनुसृत्याजौ हताः पञ्चनदालयैः।
en: In my very sight, O Brahmana, thousands of Vrishni ladies were carried away by the Abhiras of the country of the five waters, who attacked us.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: धनुरादाय तत्राहं नाशकं तस्य पूरणे॥ यथा पुरा च मे वीर्यं भुजयोर्न तथाऽभवत्।
en: Taking up my bow, I found myself unequal to even string it. The power that had existed in my arms seemed to have disappeared on that occasion.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: अस्त्राणि मे प्रनष्टानि विविधानि महामुने॥ शराश्च क्षयमापन्नाः क्षणेनैव समन्ततः।
en: O great ascetic, my weapons of various kinds failed to appear. Soon, again, my arrows became exhausted.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: पुरुषश्चाप्रमेयात्मा शंखचक्रगदाधरः॥ चतुर्भुजः पीतवासाः श्यामः पद्मदलेक्षणः। यश्च याति पुरस्तान्मे रथस्य सुमहाद्युतिः॥
en: That person of immeasurable soul, of four arms, holding the conch, the discus, and the mace, clad in yellow robes, dark of complexion, and possessing eyes resembling lotus-petals, is no longer seen by me! Alas, reft of Govinda, what have I to live for, dragging my life in sorrow?

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: प्रदहन रिपुसैन्यानि न पश्याम्यहमच्युतम्। येन पूर्वं प्रदग्धानि शत्रूसैन्यानि तेजसा॥
en: He who used to stalk in advance of my car, that divine form gifted with great splendour and unfading power, consuming as he proceeded all hostile warriors, can no longer be seen by me.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: शरैर्गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तैरहं पश्चाच्च नाशयम्। तमपश्यन् विषीदामि घूर्णामीव च सत्तम॥
en: No longer seeing him who by his energy first burnt all hostile troops whom I afterwards killed with arrows shot off Gandiva, I am filled with grief and my head swims, O best of men! Penetrated with cheerlessness and despair, I cannot get peace of mind.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: विना जनार्दनं वीरं नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥ श्रुत्वैव हि गतं विष्णुं ममापि मुमुहुर्दिशः।
en: I dare not live, reft of the heroic Janardana. As soon as I heard that Vishnu had left the earth, my eyes became dim and all things disappeared from my vision.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: प्रणष्टज्ञातिवीर्यस्य शून्यस्य परिधावतः॥ उपदेष्टुं मम श्रेयो भवानर्हति सत्तम।
en: O best of men, you should tell me what is good for me now, for I am now a wanderer with an empty heart, despoiled of my kinsmen and of my prowess.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: व्यास उवाच ब्रह्मशापविनिर्दग्धा वृष्ण्यन्धकमहारथाः॥ विनष्टाः कुरुशार्दूल न ताशोचितुमर्हसि।
en: Vyasa said The powerful car-warriors of the Vrishni and the Andhaka races have all been consumed by the Brahmanas' course. O chief of Kuru's race, you should not grieve for their destruction.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: भवितव्यं तथा तच्च दिष्टमेतन्महात्मनाम्॥ उपेक्षितं च कृष्णेन शक्तेनापि व्यपोहितुम्।
en: That which has taken place, had been ordained. It was the destiny of those great warriors. Krishna allowed it to take place although he was fully competent to befell it.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: त्रैलोक्यमपि गोविन्दः कृत्स्नं स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥ प्रसहेदन्यथाकर्तुं कुतः शापं महात्मनाम्।
en: Govinda was able to after the very course of the universe with all its mobile and immobile creatures. What need then be said of the curse of even great Brahmanas?

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: रथस्य पुरतो याति यः स चक्रगदाधरः॥ तव स्नेहात् पुराणर्षिर्वासुदेवश्चतुर्भुज।
en: for you He who used to proceed in front of your car, arined with discus and mace, through affection was the four-armed Vasudeva, that ancient Rishi.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: कृत्वा भरावतरणं पृथिव्याः पृथुलोचनः॥ मोक्षयित्वा तनुं प्राप्तः कृष्णः स्वस्थानमुत्तमम्।
en: That great one of expansive eyes, viz., Krishna, having lightened the burthen of the Earth and cast off his (human) body, has attained to his own high seat.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: त्वयापीह महत् कर्म देवानां पुरुषर्षभ॥ कृतं भीमसहायेन यमाभ्यां च महाभुज।
en: By you also, O foremost of men, with Bhima for your helpmate and the twins, O mighty-armed hero, has the great work of the gods been done.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: कृतकृत्यांश्च वो मन्ये संसिद्धान् कुरुपुङ्गव॥ गमनं प्राप्तकालं व इहं श्रेयस्कर विभो।
en: O foremost one of Kuru's race, I regard you and your brothers as crowned with success, for you have accomplished the great purpose of your lives! The Time has come for your departure from the world. Even this, O powerful one, is what is beneficial for you now.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: एवं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च प्रतिपत्तिश्च भारता॥ भवन्ति भवकालेषु विपद्यन्ते विपर्यये।
en: Even thus, understanding and prowess and foresight. O Bharata, arise when days of prosperity have gone. These very acquisitions disappear when the hour of adversity comes.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: कालमूलमिदं सर्वं जगद्बीजं धनञ्जय॥ काल एव समादत्ते पुनरेव यदृच्छया।
en: All this has Time for its root. Time is, indeed, the seed of the of the universe, O not FINISH MA Dhananjaya! It is Time, again, which withdraws everything at its pleasure.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: स एव बलवान् भूत्वा पुनर्भवति दुर्बलः॥ स एवेशश्च भूत्वेह परैराज्ञाप्यते पुनः।
en: One becomes powerful, and, again, losing that power, becomes weak. One becomes a master and rules others, and again, losing that position, becomes a servant for obeying the order of others.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: कृतकृत्यानि चास्त्राणि गतान्यद्य यथागतम्॥ पुनरेष्यन्ति ते हस्ते यदा कालो भविष्यति।
en: Your weapons, having achieved success, have gone away to the place they came from. They will, again, come into your hands when the Time for their coming approaches.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: कालो गन्तुं गतिं मुख्यां भवतामपि भारत॥ एतच्छ्रेयो हि वो मन्ये परमं भरतर्षभ।
en: The Time has come, O Bharata, for you all to attain to the highest end. This is what I consider to be highly beneficial for you all, O chief of Bharata's race.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतद् वचनमाज्ञाय व्यासस्यामिततेजसः॥ अनुज्ञातो ययौ पार्थो नगरं नागसाह्रयम्।
en: Having heard these words of Vyasa of great energy, the son of Pritha, receiving his permission, returned to the city of Hastinapur.

description: -Concluded Arjuna sees Vyasa at his hermitage and bemoans his loss. Vyasa's counsels to Arjuna
sn: प्रविश्य च पुरी वीरः समासाद्य युधिष्ठिरम्। आचष्ट तद् यथावृत्तं वृष्ण्यन्धककुलं प्रति॥
en: Entering it, the hero approached Yudhishthira and informed him of all that had taken place about the Vrishnis. JSALA PARVA

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वती व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्।।
en: Having saluted Narayana and Nara the best of mal beings, as also Sarasvati the Goddess of learning, let us cry success.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: जनमेजय उवाच एवं वृष्ण्यन्धककुले श्रुत्वा मौसलमाहवम्। पाण्डवाः किमकुर्वन्त तथा कृष्णे दिवं गते॥
en: Janamejaya said Having heard of that fighting with iron bolts between the heroes of the Vrishni and the Andhaka races, and having been informed also Krishna's departure from this world, what did the Pandavas do?

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वैवं कौरवो राजा वृष्णीनां कदनं महत्। प्रस्थाने मतिमाधाय वाक्यमर्जुनमब्रवीत्॥ काल: पचति भूतानि सर्वाण्येव महामते। कालपाशमहं मन्ये त्वमपि द्रष्टुमर्हसि॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Having heard the particulars of the great destruction of the Vrishnis, the Kaurava king was determined on leaving the world. He addressed Arjuna saying—'O you of great intelligence, it is time which cooks every creature (in is cauldron), I thing that what has taken place is due to the cords of Time (with which he binds us all). You should also see it.'

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: इत्युक्तः स तु कौन्तेयः कालः काल इति ब्रुवन्। अन्वपद्यत तद् वाक्यं भ्रातुर्येष्ठस्य धीमतः॥
en: Thus addressed by his brother, the son of Kunti only repeated the word, “Time, Time!' and fully endorsed the view of his eldest brother endured with great intelligence.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: अर्जुनस्य मतं ज्ञात्वा भीमसेनो यमौ तथा। अन्वपद्यन्त तद् वाक्यं यदुक्तं सव्यसाचिना॥
en: Knowing the resolution of Arjuna, Bhimasena and the twins fully endorsed the words which Arjuna had said.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: ततो युयुत्सुमानाय्य प्रव्रजन् धर्मकाम्यया। राज्यं परिददौ सर्वं वैश्यापुत्रे युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Determined upon retiring from the world for acquiring merit, they brought Yuyutsu before them. Yudhishthira made over the kingdom to the son of his uncle by his Vaishya wife.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: अभिषिच्य स्वराज्ये च राजानं च परिक्षितम्। दुःखार्तश्चाब्रवीद् राजा सुभद्रा पाण्डवाग्रजः॥ एष पुत्रस्य पुत्रस्ते कुरुराजो भविष्यति। यदूनां परिशेषश्च वज्रो राजा कृतश्च ह॥
en: Installing Parikshit also on their throne, as king, the eldest brother of the Pandavas, filled with sorrow, addressed Subhadra, saying, 'This son of your son will be the king of the Kurus. The survivor of the Yadus, viz., Vajra, has been made a king.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: परिक्षिद्धास्तिनपुरे शक्रप्रस्थे च यादवः। वज्रो राजा त्वया रक्ष्यो मा चाधर्मे मनः कृथाः॥
en: Parikshit will rule in Hastinapur, while the Yadava prince, Vajra, will rule in Shakraprastha. You should protect him, Never set you heart on sin,

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: इत्युक्त्वा धर्मराजः स वासुदेवस्य धीमतः। मातुलस्य च वृद्धस्य रामादीनां तथैव च॥ भ्रातृभिः सह धर्मात्मा कृत्वोदकमतन्द्रितः श्राद्धान्युद्दिश्य सर्वेषां चकार विधिवत् तदा॥
en: Having said these words, king Yudhishthira, the just, alone with his brothers, promptly offered oblations of water to Vasudevas of great intelligence, as also his old maternal uncle, and Rama add others. He then duly performed the Shraddhas of all those kinsmen.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: द्वैपायनं नारदं च मार्कण्डेयं तपोधनम्। भारद्वाजं याज्ञवल्क्यं हरिमुद्दिश्य यत्नवान्॥
en: The king, in honour of Hari, and naming him repeatedly, fed the Dvaipayana Vyasa, and Narada, and Markandeya having penances for wealth, and Yajnavalkya of Bharadvaja race, with many delicious food.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: अभोजयत् स्वादु भोज्यं कीर्तयित्वा च शाङ्गिणम्। ददौ रत्नानि वासांसि ग्रामानश्वान् रथांस्तथा॥ स्त्रियश्च द्विजमुख्येभ्यस्तदा शतसहस्रशः। कृपमभ्यर्च्य च गुरुमथ पौरपुरस्कृतम्॥ शिष्यं परिक्षितं तस्मै ददौ भरतसत्तमः। ततस्तु प्रकृतीः सर्वाः समानाय्य युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: In honour of Krishna, he also gave away many jewels and gems, and presses and clothes, and villages and horses and cars, and female salves by hundreds and thousands to foremost of Brahmanas. Calling the citizens, Kripa was installed as the preceptor and Parikshit was made over to him as his disciple, O chief of Bharata's race! Then Yudhishthira once more summoned all his subjects.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: सर्वमाचष्ट राजर्षिश्चिकीर्षितमथात्मनः। ते श्रुत्वैव वचस्तस्य पौरजानपदा जनाः॥ भृशमुद्विग्नमनमो नाभ्यनन्दन्त तद्वचः। नैवं कर्तव्यमिति ते तदोचुस्तं जनाधिपम्॥
en: The royal sage informed them of his desire. The citizens and the villagers hearing it kings' words became stricken with anxiety and disapproved of them. “This should never be done'—said they to the king.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: न च राजा तथाकार्षीत् कालपर्यायधर्मवित्। ततोऽनुमान्य धर्मात्मा पौरजानपदं जनम्॥
en: The king, knowing the changes brought about by time, did not listen to their advice. were Possessed of righteous soul, he persuaded the people to submit his views.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: गमनाय मतिं चक्रे भ्रातरशास्य ते तदा। ततः स राजा कौरव्यो धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ उत्सृज्याभरणान्यङ्गाज्जगृहे वल्कलान्युत। भीमार्जुनयमाश्चैव द्रौपदी च यशस्विनी॥ तथैव जगृहु: सर्वे वल्कलानि नराधिप। विधिवत् कारयित्वेष्टिं नैष्ठिकी भरतर्षभ॥ समुत्सृज्याप्सु सर्वेऽग्नीन् प्रतस्थुर्नरपुङ्गवाः। तत: प्ररुरुदुः सर्वाः स्त्रियो दृष्ट्वा नरोत्तमान्॥
en: He them made up his mind he leave the world. His brothers also formed the same resolution. Then Dharma's son Yudhishthira, the king of the Kurus, renouncing his ornaments, wore barks of trees Bhima and Arjuna and the twines, and the illustrious Draupadi similarly clad them salves in barks of trees, O sing. Having caused the preliminary rites of religion, O chief of Bharata's race which to bless them in the accomplishment of their design, those foremost of men renounced their sacred fires to the water. Seeing the preaches in that guise the ladies wept aloud.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: प्रस्थितान् द्रौपदीषष्ठान् पुरा द्यूतजितान् यथा। हर्षोऽभवच्च सर्वेषां भ्रातॄणां गमनं प्रति॥
en: They seemed to look as they had looked formerly when with Draupadi forming the sixth in number they had left the capital after their defect at dice. All the brothers, however, were infinitely delighted at the prospect of their retirement.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: युधिष्ठिरमतं ज्ञात्वा वृष्णिक्षयमवेक्ष्य च। भ्रातरः पञ्च कृष्णा च षष्ठी श्वा चैव सप्तमः॥ आत्मना सप्तमो राजा निर्ययौ गजसाह्वयात्। पौरेरनुगतो दूरं सर्वैरन्तःपुरैस्तथा।॥
en: Ascertaining the desire of Yudhishthira and seeing the destruction of the Vrishnis, no other course of action could satisfy them then. The five brothers, with Draupadi forming the sixth, and a dog forming the seventh, started on their Journey. Thus did king Yudhishthira depart, himself heading a party of seven, from the city of Hastinapur. The citizens and they royal ladies followed them for some distance.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: न चैनमशकत् कश्चिन्निवर्तस्वेति भाषितुम्। न्यवर्तन्त ततः सर्वे नरा नगरवासिनः॥
en: None of them, however, could venture to address the king for persuading him so give up his intention. The citizens then returned.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: कृपप्रभृतयश्चैव युयुत्सुं पर्यवारयन्। विवेश गङ्गां कौरव्य उलूपी भुजगात्मजा।॥
en: Kripa and, others stood around Yuyutsu as their centre, Ulupi the daughter of the Naga chief, O you of Kuru's race, entered the waters of Ganga.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: चित्राङ्गदा ययौ चापि मणिपूरपुरं प्रति। शिष्टाः परिक्षितं त्वन्या मातरः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: The princess Chitrangada started for the capital of Manipur. The other ladies who were the grandmothers of Parikshit gathered around him.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: पाण्डवाश्च महात्मानो द्रौपदी च यशस्विनी। कृतोपवासाः कौरव्य प्रययुः प्रामुखस्ततः॥
en: Meanwhile the great Pandavas, O you of Kuru's race, and the illustrious Draupadi, having observed the preminary fast, started with their faces towards he est.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: योगयुक्ता महात्मानस्त्यागधर्ममुपेयुषः। अभिजग्मुर्बहून् देशान् सरितः सागरांस्तथा॥
en: Seeing themselves on Yoga those great ones, resolved to observe the religion of Renunciation, passed through various countries and teached various rivers and seas.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: युधिष्ठिरो ययावग्रे भीमस्तु तदनन्तरम्। अर्जुनस्तस्य चान्वेव यमौ चापि यथाक्रमम्॥ पृष्ठतस्तु वरारोहा श्यामा पद्मदलेक्षणा। द्रौपदी योषितां श्रेष्ठा ययौ भरतसत्तम॥
en: Yudhishthira proceeded first Behind him was Bhima;. next walked Arjuna; after him were the twins in the order of their birth; behind them all, O foremost one of Bharata's race, went Draupadi, that first of women, endued with great beauty, of dark Complexion, and having eyes like lotus petals.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: श्वा चैवानुययावेकः प्रस्थितान् पाण्डवान् वनम्। क्रमेण ते ययुर्वीरा लौहित्यं सलिलार्णवम्॥
en: While the Pandavas started for the forest a dog followed them, Proceeding on, those heroes reached the sea of red waters.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: गाण्डीवं तु धनुर्दिव्यं न मुमोच धनञ्जयः। रत्नलोभान्महाराज ते चाक्षय्ये महेषुधी॥
en: Dhananjaya had not thrown off is celestial bow Gandiva nor his couple of inexhaustible quivers, actuated, O king by the cupidity for valuable things.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: अग्निं ते ददृशुस्तत्र स्थितं शैलमिवाग्रतः। मार्गमावृत्य तिष्ठन्तं साक्षात्पुरुषविग्रहम्॥
en: The Pandavas there saw the God of Fire standing before them like hill. Closing their way, the god stood there in his embodied form.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: ततो देवः स सप्तार्चिः पाण्डवानिदमब्रवीत्। भो भोः पाण्डुसुता वीराः पावकं मां निबोधत॥
en: The deity of seven flames then addressed the Pandavas, saving—'O heroic sons of Pandu, known me as the God of Fire.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: युधिष्ठिर महाबाहो भीमसेन परंतप। अर्जुनाश्विसुतौ वीरौ निबोधत वचो मम॥
en: O mighty-armed Yudhishthira, O Bhimasena who are a scorcher of enemies, O Arjuna, and O twines of great courage, listen to what I say!

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: अहमग्निः कुरुश्रेष्ठा मया दग्धं च खाण्डवम्। अर्जुनस्य प्रभावेण तथा नारायणस्य च॥
en: Oforemost ones of Kuru's race, I am the God of Fire. The forest of Khandava was burnt by me, through the power of Arjuna and of Narayana himself.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: अयं वः फाल्गुनो भ्राता गाण्डीवं परमायुधम्। परित्यज्य वने यातु नानेनार्थोऽस्ति कश्चन॥
en: Let your brother Phalguna proceed to the forest after casting off Gandiva, that great weapon. He has no longer any necessity for it.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: चक्ररत्नं तु यत् कृष्णे स्थितमासीन्महात्मनि। गतं तच्च पुनर्हस्ते कालेनैष्यति तस्य ह॥
en: That precious discus, which was with the great Krishna, has disappeared (from the world).. When the time again comes, it will return into and his hands.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: वरुणादाहृतं पूर्वं मयैतत् पार्थकारणात्। गाण्डीवं धनुषां श्रेष्ठं वरुणायैव दीयताम्॥
en: This foremost of hows viz., Gandiva, was procured by me from Varuna for the us of Partha. let it be made over to Varuna himself.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: ततस्ते भ्रातरः सर्वं धनञ्जयमचोदयन्। स जले प्राक्षिपच्चैतत्तथाक्षय्ये महेषुधी॥
en: At this, all the brothers requested Dhananjaya to do what the god said. He then threw into the waters (of the sea) both the bow and the couple of inexhaustible quivers.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: ततोऽग्निर्भरतश्रेष्ठ तत्रैवान्तरधीयत। ययुश्च पाण्डवा वीरास्ततस्ते दक्षिणामुखाः॥
en: After this, O chief of Bharata's race the God of Fire disappeared then and these the heroic sons of Pandu next went out with their faces turned towards the South.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: ततस्ते तूत्तरेणैव तीरेण लवणाम्भसः। जग्मुर्भरतशार्दूल दिशं दक्षिणपश्चिमाम्॥
en: Then, by the northern coast of the salt sea, those princes of Bharata's race, went to the south west.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: ततः पुनः समावृत्ता पश्चिमां दिशमेव ते। ददृशुभरकां चापि सागरेण परिप्लुताम्॥
en: Turning next towards the west, they saw the city of Dwraka covered by the ocean.

description: The king leaves the world after hearing Krishna's departui e
sn: उदीची पुनरावृत्य ययुर्भरतसत्तमाः। प्रादक्षिण्यं चिकीर्षन्तः पृथिव्या योगधर्मिणः॥
en: Turning next to the north, those foremost ones went on observant of Yoga, they were desirous of going round the whole earth.

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते नियतात्मान उदीची दिशमास्थिताः। ददृशुर्योगयुक्ताश्च हिमवन्तं महागिरिम्॥ तु
en: Those princes of controlled souls and devoted to Yoga, proceeding to the north, saw Himavat, that huge mountain,

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: तं चाप्यतिक्रमन्तस्ते ददृशुर्वालुकार्णवम्। अवैक्षन्त महाशैलं मेरुं शिखरिणां वरम्॥
en: Crossing the Himavat, they saw a vast desert of sand. They then saw the powerful mountain Meru. The foremost of all highpeaked mountains.

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: तेषां तु गच्छतां शीघ्रं सर्वेषां योगधर्मिणाम्। याज्ञसेनी भ्रष्टयोगा निपपात महीतले॥
en: As those powerful ones were proceeding quickly all rapt in Yoga, Yajnaseni, falling off from Yoga, dropped down on the Earth.

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: तां प्रपतितां दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनो महाबलः। उवाच धर्मराजानं याज्ञसेनीमवेक्ष्य ह॥ नाधर्मश्चरितः कश्चिद् राजपुत्र्या परंतप। कारणं किं नु तद् ब्रूहि यत् कृष्णा पतिता भुवि॥
en: Seeing her fallen down, Bhimasena of great strength addressed king Yudhishthira the just saying, 'O scorcher of enemies, this princess never did any sinful deed. Tell us what the cause is for which Krishna has fallen down on the Earth.'

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पक्षपातो महानस्या विशेषेण धनञ्जये। तस्यैतत् फलमद्यैषा भुङ्क्ते पुरुषसत्तम॥
en: Yudhishthira said, She had great partiality for Dhananjaya in particular. She obtains the fruit of that conduct today, O best of men.

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वानवेक्ष्यैनां ययौ भरतसत्तमः। समाधाय मनो धीमान् धर्मात्मा पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Vaishampayana said, Having said this, that foremost one of Bharata's race went on. Of righteous soul, that foremost of men, gifted with great intelligence, went on, with mind intent on itself.

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: सहदेवस्ततो विद्वान् निपपात महीतले। तं चापि पतितं दृष्ट्वा भीमो राजानमब्रवीत्॥ योऽयमस्मासु सर्वेषु शुश्रूषुरनहंकृतः। सोऽयं माद्रवतीपुत्रः कस्मान् निपतितो भुवि॥
en: Then the all wise Sahadeva dropped down on the Earth. Seeing him drop down. Bhima addressed the king. saying, 'He who with great humility used to serve us all, alas, why is that son of Madravati fallen down on the Earth?'

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आत्मनः सदृशं प्राज्ञं नैषोऽमन्यत कंचन। तेन दोषेण पतितस्तस्मादेव नृपात्मजः॥
en: Yudhishthira said He never thought anybody his equal in wisdom. It is for that sin that prince has dropped down.

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा तं समुत्सृज्य सहदेवं ययौ तदा। भ्रातृभिः सह कौन्तेयः शुना चैव युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Having said this, the king proceeded, leaving Sahadeva there. Indeed, Kunti's son Yudhishthria went on, with his brothers and with the dog.

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: कृष्णां निपतितां दृष्ट्वा सहदेवं च पाण्डवम्। आर्तो बन्धुप्रियः शूरो नकुलो निपपात ह॥
en: Seeing both Krishna and the Pandava Sahadeva fallen down, the brave Nakula, whose love for kinsmen was very great, fell down himself.

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
sn: तस्मिन् निपतिते वीरे नकुले चारुदर्शने। पुनरेव तदा भीमो राजानमिदमब्रवीत्॥ योऽयमक्षतधर्मात्मा भ्राता वचनकारकः। रूपेणाप्रतिमो लोके नकुलः पतितो भुवि॥
en: Upon the falling down of the heroic Nakula of great beauty, Bhima once more addressed the king, saying, 'This brother of ours who was gifted with full righteousness and who always obeyed our commands, this Nakula who was peerless for beauty, has fallen down!'

description: The departure of Pandava princes from the world
